Location is perfect for the inner harbor and candem yards. valet parking was a bit slow but very nice to have. Try the chocolate mouse cheesecake at the nearby Cheesecake factory.

title: “The secret paradise near Union Square”
text:
I love this place!! As well as the superbly-trained and HAPPY staff...
Been returning here for years....because it is retro-classy, close to 
everything and comfortable. Best-kept secret in San Francisco....

title: “Wonderful Hotel”
text:
This was a wonderful hotel, just a block or two from Fisherman's Wharf. 
The lobby and bar area were lovely, the staff friendly and accommodating. The conceierge was fantastic, with great tips on transportation and where to eat. The beds and pillows were the most comfortable I have ever slept on in a hotel anywhere. The food in the lounge and restuarant was a little pricey, but that isn't unexpected. 
The breakfast buffet was amazing, and only $6.95 for children 18 and under. The business centre wasn't busy in the evening, and my teens were able to check their email at no cost. I was also able to go online in the business center to get driving directions when our plans changed. I would heartily recommend this hotel to business travellers and families, and would definitely stay there again if I ever get back to San Francisco.

title: “Excellent!”
text: We booked two rooms for the weekend through priceline. After reading the reviews of this hotel, I was very scared about this place but I was way off. This was a great hotel. The hotel was being remodeled which was great. We received a remodeled room that was roomy and in excellent condition. Plasma tvs in each room and a great bed. The entire staff was great to us as well. They went out of their way to help us out. This is a great hotel. Do not trust the negative reviews on this hotel. We would highly recommend the Metroplitian Hotel.

title: “Cosy hotel, great location!”
text:
Spent a week in Boston in april just wanting to relax and see the city. The hotel is actually 3 Brown-stone houses, which we thought was great for getting the feel of traditional Boston. Got a standard room which was surprisinglig big through a deal on Hotels.com. The toilet got clogged easily, but wasn't a real problem. Nicely decorated rooms and friendly staff. Breakfast isn't much to speak of, I recommend going to a nearby cafe in stead.
Location is perfect! Everything is in walking distance. We walked to beacon hill, north end, aquarium, brookline and harvard and spent many hours under the sun in Boston Common. Newbury street is beautiful and fairly quiet, and packed with restaurant choices for dinner. And an extra plus for having Ben&jerry's right down the street:)
Would recommend to others, and is my first choice should I return.

title: “Unsafe !”
text:
We stayed here for 5 nights in July 2012. On our 4th night there,my husband's truck window was smashed and his tools were taken and his vehicle trashed. We had returned around midnight from moving our daughter from The University of Texas at Austin. We noticed that all three lights on the side of the hotel were not working. We went inside to report the lights not working but there was not any employee to be found.This was the place we were told to park since we have the moving trailer and we assumed the hotel had security. Well, guess what, I was told by the front desk the next morning that they do not have security. Where are the employees late at night? There was no employee to be found and we looked for a long long time.
 Around the back of the building we noticed a homeless camp on the Hilton Garden Inn's premises.This was in their parking lot. We advised the front desk the next morning. Guess what, they were back the next night. We insisted that they call the police as we suspect this is who was breaking in the cars. We were not the only vehicle broken into. We were told by the girl at the front desk that they come in to use their bathroom, eat their cookies and fruit left out for guests, etc. Why have they not done something about this before now .Please,Please what is going on here. After a long discussion with the police officer, he finally asked them to go elsewhere. My question is, when did Hilton Hotels start allowing homeless camps in their parking lot and why ? We did not feel safe here and will not return.
As far as the rooms go, they are nice Hilton Garden Inn rooms, the service in the breakfast area is excellent. The cook goes over and above, very nice.
I do believe there is a night problem going on at this hotel which management needs to look into. I am giving the low ratings because of the safety issue.

title: “rooms 541 & 542 - special, but especially so for families!”
text:
We're staying here as we speak & so enjoying this hotel. My husband & I are here for a few days getaway while the kids are at camp.
When I made our reservations, I chose the "automatic upgrade" options for a suite/higher floor/anything available, since it's our anniversary tomorrow & we wanted to treat ourselves. My initial reservation was for a king bed room at the AAA rate, tho I'm a Hyatt Platinum member so get wifi for free, plus late check-out if we needed it. And other cool stuff that's not important right now. ;) 
We were upgraded to a Junior Suite (or is it called a Parlor Suite? I'm not sure) - in any case, rooms 541 (the king bed) & 542 (the separate, connecting, "suite", w/ a pullout couch & bathroom). What is very special about this particular space is that room 542 extends into what is basically the size of another small room, an entertainment area w/ a tall dining table & six bar stools. Plus a full-size refrigerator in an alcove. And the hotel could add a roll-away bed.
So we are enjoying - greatly - three large windows overlooking North High Street, the space of three rooms, 2 flat-screen TVs, 2 bathrooms, 1 small frig (included in the king-bedded room), 1 full-size frig, eating space for 6, a living room w/ pull-out couch, and could add a rollaway bed if we needed it - there's plenty of room for it. Wow. It's a fabulous space for families. Though it's making us happy w/ the kids away at camp, too :). 
The hotel, of course, is not perfect. I understand another reviewer's complaints about the climate control in the room, which was confusing to me at first, but isn't an insurmountable problem. It's a very enthusiastic air conditioner. Set it high, turn it off if it's too cold, and oh, I wish other hotels had the same problem. I'd rather cuddle up w/ a blanket to sleep than be too hot. 
Our biggest bummer about this hotel is that there's no Club Floor or Concierge Club. We stay in Hyatt hotels all the time, and far prefer to have access to those quiet spaces, w/ their generous breakfasts & plentiful evening appetizers. I have no idea why a hotel like this - catering to business travelers, but also rowdy state-wide school competitions/adult gatherings (think hundreds of teenagers/partiers), in a state capitol like Columbus (where, frankly, there aren't any luxury hotels at all. even the Ritz in Cleveland is meh) - does not have an Executive Club/Concierge Club/whatever they want to call it. It is a huge failing in a hotel that wants to be of this caliber. And missing a niche in the whole freakin' state. 
Nit-picking, the pool has been closed during our stay, supposedly until tomorrow, which was not disclosed on the website or when I made our reservation. Room service tends to be slow at inexplicable times. The food is either Standard Hyatt Menu (which gets boring fast, and that's no reflection on the Columbus hotel) or a bit spotty. Fun Buffalo Chicken Sliders, interesting Blackened Chicken sandwich, gross cheesecake truffle dessert things. Ick. 
OTOH, almost every employee we've encountered has been amazing. Really, Hyatt employees across the board are exemplary. 5-star quality but family-friendly & not stuffy. Four Seasons-ish. Being in Ohio, this hotel has an especially high level of friendliness and helpfulness, while maintaining a professional demeanor. 
William, a bellman, has gone above-and-beyond several times and should be recognized for his excellent work (the construction downtown! his patient directions. the large party/parade this weekend! his helpful insights. and several other instances. He has been, for us, the prime representative of this hotel and has done an amazing job at it). Hyatt wants & needs people like him. Ashley at the front desk was sweet & bubbly & informative about local hot-spots. In the coffee shop, room service, housekeeping - almost every person we've encountered has been natural (very Midwest), friendly, but professional, highly competent, and employees Hyatt should be proud of. Very similar in quality to our favorite, the Hyatt at Coconut Point. 
Next year, if our kids are at camp the same week again, we would absolutely consider staying here (unlike the Ritz in Cleveland, where we stayed last year while the kids were at camp. not worth a second visit). We'd recommend it to anyone who needs a downtown location, and suggest rooms 541 & 542 to families or people who like space, in particular.

title: “Different part of town”
text: I have been wanting to stay at this hotel for some time. Have been following the Tripadvisor reviews and was disappointed to see it fell 20 places down the rankings. But still decided to try it to see what it was like. Tripadvisor reviewers were right to say it's not in the most pleasant areas of town. But in the daytime, it looks safe, and the walk from Andrew Station is relatively short. From Andrew, you are 2 stops from South Station, where you can take the Silver Line Bus to Logan Airport. I was disappointed when I checked in, that I only got a low floor, when I specified on my reservation that I preferred a high floor. This is not the 1st hotel where that has happened, but it makes you wonder if front desk has the same information in their computer that you have on your reservation. The room was huge, twice the size of rooms I'm used to. I was afraid I might be under a family of kids but it was relatively quiet during my 2-night stay. But I only had a view of one side of the carpark. I don't think front desk gave me the best room available at the time. And it is not cheap. $119 a night plus tax for this part of town, I paid less for being closer to downtown. The hotel is within walking distance to the South Bay Shopping Center, which has a lot of shops, including Target, Home Depot and Best Buy. The room has a fridge that is so cold you don't need ice for your drinks. Shower has the best shower pressure I'm experienced anywhere. Internet is free, which is a huge plus for me. There is a laundry room, which can come in handy. I think I would stay here again, if I got a cheaper rate. And I would request at check-in to be on a higher floor next time.

title: “Recently remodeled, friendliest staff, great breakfast”
text: This is the 2nd time I have stayed at the Baymeadows Residence Inn. It has been updated since my last stay -- new carpets, furniture, appliances, etc. The units are arranged in small buildings and has the feel of an apartment complex. I stayed in the 2-queen suite this time, and it is just slightly larger than the 1-king suite I had last time. For 1 or 2 people, I would choose the king, but for more than 2, choose the 2-queen (with sofabed.) Breakfasts are great -- waffles, eggs, egg muffin sandwiches, oatmeal and grits, cereals, etc. Mon-Tues-Weds nights there is food served from 6-7:30pm. Such a nice feature after a long day of travel. Food served during our stay included ziti, chili, and hot dogs. Not a ton of food, but sure beats having to go out and find a restaurant when you are tired! Rooms are currently hard-wired for internet but supposed to go wireless in April 2012. For now, they do have wireless routers you can borrow if you do not have an ethernet connection on your tablet or other device. I highly recommend this Residence Inn.

title: “I've had better stays here”
text:
The Hilton is my normal LAX airport hotel choice. I've had very good stays in the past but this one was lacking as far as rooms go. The first room I was given was on the Executive Floor. It was tucked in a corner, near the elevator(contrary to the what I always ask for) with a very small window on the side wall of the room. It seemed that this room was almost an "afterthought." I went down to the front desk and very politely asked for a different room. The woman who helped me was very nice. Due to the hotel being very full, she offerred and I accepted a slightly smaller room on the 4th floor. 
This room had another very limited view but this time it was of what appeared to be a courtyard between the towers. It was again very close to the elevators which I don't like and they were doing construction on the tower I was in. The floor was covered in plastic and they'd laid plywood over it. Everytime someone walked by it was noisy. I didn't hear any construction noise but this set-up was "low-rent."
The room looked ok on the surface but after being in it for awhile I noticed some deficiencies......it was very humid and the room never did cool down to my preferred comfortable sleeping temperature. The TV needed to be repaired or replaced - - the sound was awful. The shower in both the original room and my second and final room needed to be cleaned or have the caulk replaced. 
One suggestion I have for the hotel if their representatives read this is to reconsider the placement of the small table they have which holds the coffee pot and ice bucket. The placement of it is in the direct line you make from the bed or desk to the bathroom. I ran into at least twice. 
Finally, despite my displeasure with the room situation, the staff at that hotel is wonderful. The bartenders are great! One of them very kindly gave me a book he'd finished reading. The breakfast room service delivery gentleman was polite and kind as he'd been for my previous stays. The staff that work the front desks are alway pleasant and do their best to be accommodating. 
I will stay here again as I'm hopeful my room experience was just a "one-time" occurrence.

title: “terrible customer service”
text:
I was looking forward to my stay at this hotel and when we showed up the hotel overbooked us. It was about 6 pm at night and our credit card was already charged. We showed up, valeted our car (no self parking) to find out we had to go somewhere else. The hotel manager did not offer any future stay courtesy to us nor did they apologize. They just sent us to a Hilton across town. If we wanted to stay in a big corporate hotel, we would have booked with them. We chose this hotel because of its intimate atmosphere. 
What a disappointment since the hotel looked really nice and quaint. We are avid travelers and are constantly recommending hotels to our friends, family and co-workers. Too bad this hotel will be loosing a lot of our business.

title: “Traditional style”
text:
16-07-08
Just had four nights at the Lombardy, and this was our third time staying there. It's a relatively small hotel, but after a slightly nonchalant and rude check-in process, we had no complaints:
- our suite had two double beds (necessary for us and our two children)
- there was a mini-kitchen (with the usual over-priced foodstuffs)
- the beds were very comfortable
- the rooms were well serviced
- we could swim for free at the sister hotel (The Washington Plaza), and they had well-priced happy hours(!)
Why not five stars?
- old-fashioned lifts
- poor TVs (no channel guides, no premium channels)
- slightly dark
- location is okay, but not great

title: “Nice Stay”
text: We stayed at the Intercontinental based on the acceptance of a blind bid through Priceline. We received a price of $175 per night, which is a great price for a 4-star hotel in downtown Boston. The amenities were as you would expect for a hotel of this caliber. The rooms are great. The staff was helpful. Overall, the location isn't the best, but really isn't too bad if you are a walker. It was about a 10 minute walk to the North End and Quincy Market/Faniel Hall. In the other direction, it was about 15 minutes to Copley Square. We would have no hesitation about staying here again.

title: “Loved it!”
text: Hotel was clean, beautifully decorated, friendly staff and all! Visited Seattle for a Conference and this hotel is a short two block walk to the convention center. We used the Downtown Shuttle Service to and from the airport and was very pleased with them as well. I enjoyed my stay at the Olive 8!! Hotel was EXCELLENT!

title: “Courtyard is clean and reliable...a few problems...”
text:
My mom and I stayed at the Courtyard Marriott Worthington for a baby shower on 1/15/05. The hotel is clean. The bed was comfortable and clean. The bathroom was clean. What else do you want really? We were checked in with lightening fast speed. We arrived in our room and there were 2 water bottles on the desk with a price tag on them $2.75 each. We were joking around saying "hey, we could drink those and fill them up with the tap!" and then we noticed the seals were already broken! We had to go downstairs so that we didn't get charged for them.
The pool area was nice and clean. However, the towels are located in the fitness center next door. There were no towels by the pool? Seemed like an odd setup. 
If I would have known about the FREE high-speed internet, I would have brought my laptop. Nice feature for the business traveler.
The breakfast buffet was $8.99 a person. The selection was good, however, we had an early flight and were the first ones in the restaurant and the woman at the counter was not quite awake yet and a little cranky. We felt we were "bothering" her by eating in the restaurant. There was a waffle iron, but no waffle batter. When we asked where the batter was, the young girl ROLLED her eyes. Yep...you guessed it...nice service. :-(
Also one suggetion that needs to be made to all the hotels in this area: GET A SHUTTLE TO THE AIRPORT. The cab cost us $45!!!! 
The front desk young man was very nice and fast. The hotel is clean and I would probably stay there again.

title: “Dirty martini's & oyster bar, what's not to like?!”
text: Stayed here for business in NY for 2 days. Got a good deal on a site. Hotel is fun and the staff are lovely. This is a hotel for people who like action and a buzzy environment. I met friends in the oyster bar both nights and the food was yummy with a killer dirty martini cocktail and the staff were nice. We had a good time. My room was small but perfect and comfy and everything worked great. It is a little actually a lot noisy with pipes in rooms, neighbours, corridor door slamming and house keeping knocking and yelling 'housekeeping' on every door in the corridor also had no idea how to work heating out which blew out cold air but I think this is a fun hotel for people who want to visit somewhere super social. I really like the opening ceremony store and the staff were so sweet and nice. i would definitely stay here again and recommend it for those up for a bit of fun in a great central location.

title: “Perfect Stay - Highly Recommended”
text:
Perfect location for first time visitors to NY. The hotel is next to all major attractions (Top of the Rock, Empire, MACYs, Times Sq etc) as well as fantastic shops on 5th and 6th Ave. Furthermore, the hotel staff couldn't have been better. They were so friendly, helpful and professional. They made you feel welcome at all times. The bed in the room was the comfiest we have ever slept in. The shower was amazing and the room was kept immaculate. There was complimentary wireless connection and printer, which was ideal for booking tickets and events while in NY. The breakfast was tasty and plentyful. 
We loved our room, but other's might feel that the room is rather small (because the bed is so big). We had no problem with this as there was plently of drawers and a wardrobe to put our clothes away. 
To complete this perfect stay was the views of the Empire State Building from the Roof Top Bar. It's the most amazing view and worth staying in the hotel just for this! Perfect for a romantic getaway (feels like you can touch the Empire Building as it is so close). To be honest, don't look at any other hotels (this is the one!).

title: “Nice and Friendly!”
text: We stay at this location when visiting family in the area. It is always nice and clean and the staff is very friendly. The area has plenty of shopping and places to eat so it works out very well for us when visiting. I highly recommend it!

title: “Bed Bugs!!!!”
text: Room was nicer than expected, didn't personally deal with staff. Not far drive from downtown Charlotte. Came home and a week later I start getting these mysterious bites on my arms and feet. They itch like crazy and are swelling like mosquito bites. Never had this in my life. Did some research, BED BUGS!!! It says it can take up 14 days for the symptoms to show. My husband was not affected as all people aren't allergic to their bites. I will always check the rooms and bed before I stay!

title: “Easy access to both airport and city”
text:
Manners and service go a long long way in my book and I experienced superb levels of both during my stay at the Hilton Boston Logan Airport, the staff are super friendly and helpful! First things first, if you're going to stay here you have a choice of cool views, on the one side there's an amazing view of the Boston Skyline from across the harbour, and on the other, there's the airport and all it's interesting operations....I had the Boston skyline and I was almost sorry to leave!
If you're departing from Logan in the wee hours, which I was, then you can't really get more accessible to the airport than this. There's a shuttle departing every 15 mins, which incidentally will pick you up, and then there's the walkway connecting the hotel to terminals A&E. 
The shuttle also gives you easy access to transportation into the city, I wouldn't at all mind being based here for my entire trip to Boston next time as unlike many other cities the airport is actually close! 
Plenty of food options here! It was great seeing my friend off with a couple of drinks before his flight back to London, which allowed me to test out the walkway! 
Wouldn't hesitate to recommend this place to anyone!

title: “Newer and better”
text: I have stayed at this hotel several times before when a guest of the University of Pennsylvania (it is in the heart of campus), and it has always been pleasant. But this time, I noticed some definite upgrades in quality and comfort. The furnishings appear new, very attractive Art Deco lamps and opulent bed coverings, new feather bed tops. Other new luxury touches included a heavy white bathrobe and Godiva chocolate mints on the pillow. Nice bathroom amenities, comfortable bed - altogether I really enjoyed my stay. The location is great if you want to see the campus.

title: “Bell Training Beware”
text:
I knew things were gonna be bad when I was left at the airport for over an hour waiting for the shuttle. The rooms are alright but try to get a top floor. Not much soundproofing between floors. 
They advertise to bell training center attendees that they will have a shuttle available to and from the centre as well as within a five mile radius. Well here I am on Saturday with a day off and no shuttle to get me anywhere and a minimum two hour wait for a cab. Shuttle service has left me waiting for an hour twice and over a half hour numerous times with previous arrangements made. My colleagues who are staying at the best western have had zero problems with their shuttle. Go stay there. There are lots of restaurants near here but if you have a day off try to come up with some other way to see the sights.
Also try to get up earlier and skip the breakfast they serve here. Yuck. 
I would gladly stay at a lower grade hotel if it meant I wouldn't be sitting here on a beautiful day in a new country with nothing to do but write this review.

title: “Excellent Hotel!”
text: We completed our honeymoon in San Francisco and looked forever to find the perfect hotel! We couldn't ask for a better find! From the moment we arrived the doorman kindly greeted us and wouldn't let us carry a thing! The hotel is absolutely beautiful (the lobby and the rooms). The location is perfect...easy walk to many fun spots. We will definitely be staying here again!

title: “Great location! Cool staff and shuttle to seaworld!”
text: I always try to stay here cause everything is so convenient I dont need to rent a car and the view is killer. Front desk, shuttle drivers and house keeping are all super friendly.

title: “Fabulous hotel, great location, cute dog...what more could you ask for?”
text: Great hotel, in the perfect location for having a break in San Diego. Friendly staff, who were helpful and knowledgeable about restaurant recommendations. Beautiful decor, nice big rooms, great shower. Only slight niggle was no rest room in the gym that I could see so had to trek down seven floors in the middle of a workout to use the facilities....answer to that of course being dont work out!!!

title: “Not a 3 star by any stretch of the imagination”
text:
I booked in here for one night via Priceline. As I bid for the hotel, I did not know which hotel I would get until my bid was accepted. I would avoid this hotel and pay a bit more (or bid on a 3.5 star in another area). The lobby is nice and the desk staff, while not terribly knowledegable try to be helpful.
The hotel has a fair amount of trash in the parking lot (bottles, fast food wrappers, etc.). The rooms are in need of renovation. The paint is chipped and scarred and the wallpaper in the bathroom is peeling. The shower curtain was stained and needed a good cleaning and the shower bar was covered in rust. There was also a lot of rust on tge air conditioning vent and cold air return.
While there is complimentary WIFI and a microwave and mini fridge in each room, the rooms themselves llok old and tired. the TV was an old Zenith cathode ray tube model.
I wanted to use the gym but unfortunately of the 4 machines in the gym area, three were broken. The TV in the GYM area also had an 'out of order' sign plastered on it. The pool looked like it had not been skimmed in a while as there were a leaves floating on the surface. Additionally, there are no towels out at the pool area.
The location is pretty good, but there are other hotels in the area that I would choose first over visiting this hotel again.

title: “Nice pool on a hot summer day”
text: We stayed at this hotel for a couple of nights during a very hot and humid August weekend. We enjoyed the pool, however it was very busy and getting a chair was not easy. There were only limited chairs in the shade. The concierge was very helpful with directions and local restaurants. The room was clean and comfortable, but could be updated. The hotel is located at a major intersection along the interstate and light sleepers could be bothered by the traffic, but it wasn't really an issue for us. They are building some ramps and overpasses in the area, so getting into the hotel can be a bit confusing depending on the direction you are coming from (we didn't hear any construction noise). Our only complaint would be that we were out all day and came back to get ready for dinner and found housekeeping there around 5:00pm - the hotel needs to have some door knob hangers so that guests can indicate when the room is ready to be cleaned.

title: “Excellent Stay, from the service to the food to the location”
text:
I spent 3 nights here in February as a part of a group who was in town for a meeting. I had personally negotiated the rooms and while NYC is expensive and the W is no exception, this hotel has a great location in respect to our office and we didn't want to risk being farther away in winter.
I didn't get to the hotel until past 3am due to delayed flight, but there was still someone to bring in my bag, check me in, etc, immediately. They didn't mention they had upgraded me to a mega room, but it was a pleasant surprise. There was also a message from the GM on the phone welcoming me, as well as a few amenities and a note. Very nice touches.
The room was larger than I expected, thanks to the upgrade and was a solid size for the city. I'm never a huge fan of the W bathrooms as there's never much room to put your stuff, but this one was slightly better than normal. The soap tray in the shower never held anything though, anything i put there would immediately fall off. The shower was a bit awkward with just half of a door, but it worked out okay.
The bed was very comfortable and the TV has a guide on it which I love compared to just having to scroll through. There are plenty of plugs near the bed which is always a plus and all the normal amenities like a safe, etc were there. 
They seem to always be doing road work in NYC at night, so bring your ear plugs no matter how high up you think you'll be staying. The heater in my room sounded like it was taking off when it started, but it seemed like just the first time was bad and then it wasn't so loud.
The food from room service is always great at Ws and this was no exception. In fact, besides the room service I had once at The Hotel at Mandalay Bay, this is the best I've ever had for dinner. Miso Halibut with a side salad and a glass of wine, plus they give you bread and a chocolate. Don't get me wrong, $65 for this meal is beyond ridiculous and is it really necessary to have a delivery fee, processing fee, tax and 20%+ gratuity? There's no way I would have done it if I wasn't exhausted and at least had a per diem from my work.
The next night I went to the bar with some colleagues and the drinks were good, but expensive, and the bar was definitely a happening spot.
What I appreciate most about this stay is that everything was done exactly as quoted -- there were some rooms on our group that were supposed to be charged directly to the guest, internet was included, etc and everything came out exactly as it was agreed to (this seems simple but trust me, I've had horrible experiences elsewhere).
As long as I get a deal, I'll stay at this hotel again because of it's proximity to my office.

title: “Everything Hollywood Should Aspire to Be.....”
text:
I was gifted this reservation and traveled with friends to celebrate the culmination of my law school application process. Predicated upon a letter of interduction written on my behalf, we were graciously accorded a Marvelous Suite on the 2nd Floor. Suites, to my understanding, are located - by design - on floors 2-5. While the view was not "Hollywood", the space was amazing and very well lit. The front desk staff was most accommodating and gracious - as was the valet service. While we did not dine at the hotel, the public areas were both engaging and gorgeous. Since the pool was not yet operational, we were graciously offered privileges at the Roosevelt Hotel pool - both in very close proimity and an incredible property itself 
All room amenities were high-end and the bed was a dream. Very quiet when we eventually turned in. 
Since this property is so new, kudos are due to the General Manager in particular and the staff in general for extending the ultimate effort for a seamless opening. Can't wait to return!!

title: “What a disaster”
text:
The Westin La Canterra is a beautiful property perched on the hills outside of San Antonio with gorgeous views of the city and a fabulous golf course as well. We were booked here for one night on a return trip from the Hill Country to Houston We had stayed here on prior occasions and booked here based on positive experiences. On this stay, we decided to book one of the casitas located quietly from the main hotel tower. 
Our experience was terrible from the get go. We were fourth in line at check in and after 15 minutes, we were still fourth in line. There was only 1 check in attendant and if I hadn't complained, I might have waited 30 minutes before being able to check in.
Since I was staying in a casita, the hotel is suppose to meet you at your car with a golf cart for use to drive to and from the casita. However, we waited in the hotel parking lot for the promised golf cart to no avail.
The casita room was nice enough, but hadn't been properly cleaned. There were foodstuff, drinks and used q tips laying around. To compound our problems, our room lacked towels and coffee supplies. When our golf cart was finally made available to us, there was no key to turn it on or off; we were then instructed on a work around by literally monkeying around with a mechanical device under the seat. 
The next day when flushing the toilet , the water in the commode backed up and wouldn't stop running. There was no turn off valve, so our room became a complete mess.
The manager was nice enough to understand and wound up giving us the room for free and provided dinner (which was sub par, but free). 
Overall, the casitas are in serious need of updating.
Beautiful property, but the hotel needs some attention.

title: “Very Good Hotel”
text:
My wife and I recently stayed at the Intercontinental New York Times Square Hotel for a day of sightseeing and a Broadway play in the evening. After a few problems after checking in, the front desk staff was most accommodating and attentive to our needs. 
We were tight on time to make it to "Jersey Boys" curtain at 8:00 PM, so the Concierge came to our rescue with a dinner reservation very close to the theater so we could make the play on time. The restaurant was great (Thalia's), especially their specialty drinks!!!
I would highly recommend this hotel to business travelers or families interested in staying close to the Theater District. The rooms were very large and extremely comfortable, and the view from the higher floors is really incredible! We will definitely stay at the Intercontinental New York Times Square Hotel again during our next trip to NYC.
I

title: “Free Parking”
text: The location of this hotel was great for Times Sq or SS Intrepid/Harbour Cruises only a few hundred yards walk to either and therefore central enough you can reach anywhere. We were travelling coast to coast so the free parking was a bonus for us. We stayed 3 nights and for £87 per room per night incl parking was great value for NYC. I would definantely recommend to car users for value & location. Even if I was travelling without a car I would still consider this hotel.

title: “Great location and loved the view”
text: The Wyndham was a great location for our busy weekend in Jacksonville and everything was perfect, from our swift check-in to the clean room, extra fluffy pillows, quick response to more coffee and anything else we asked for, to the wait staff that was fun and friendly. Loved the bubble bath. You guys think of everything. Thank you!

title: “Good cost-benefit rate, very well localized, a few "buts"...”
text: A few steps from Times Square, average price for the area, but good cost-benefit relation. Well decorated lobby, good service, but in the room cleaning, beds and towels ok, but service not very good regarding bathroom floor. Internet wireless signal weak in the 9th floor where I stayed. Air conditioning could not be regulated - very cold, even setting the temparature to 80 F, for instance.

title: “Not your father's Holiday Inn”
text:
Pardon me, but I check the little things..air/heat filter, bed bugs, service, drains working, carpets, staff.
This is one of the best hotels I have enjoyed.
A bit out of the way but worth the effort if you wish a good rest and service.

title: “A very good hotel and excellent location”
text:
I started my trip staying at The Alex Hotel... Well, after 2 days staying in that TERRIBLE hotel, I gave up and start looking for other options. Finally I was between Jumeirah, The Pierre and The Palace. The Palace was much more expensive and was out of the contest. Finally although I liked Jumeirah moore, The Pierre was charging for a better room the same that Jumeirah was charging for a standard room. 
At The Pierre, I noticed that everyone there is very polite and they really do care about you. Great staff! The room is very good, not a Encore at Wynn room, but a 5 star room.
What I dislike was:
a) It´s a little bit confuse the hall of entrance... You´ve to take a few moments to "learn" where everything is.
b) It´s outrageous what they charge for using the internet. US$2.00 per minute!!! Plus 0.95 per page B&W you prited.
c) They charge for everything... And a lot! For example: I rented a limo in NY with a driver. With them, the cost per 2 hours was US$179.00 and I payid at CARmel Company US$99.00 for the same service.
Finally, what can I say? It´s a good hotel, but I would recommend ONLY if you can get a reasonable NY price (because NY is differente from everywhere else). If you can afford, stay at the Ritz at Central Park. If you can´t, try to stay in Trump (normally they have good prices). And if even that is expensive, stay at The Wellington Hotel. 
I already stayied in more than 10 differente hotels in NY and I can say The Pierre is a Top 5. The only one I would definitely recommend to avoid is The Alex Hotel.

title: “We had a wonderful stay at this hotel”
text:
We spent the night of May 22 and also May 29 at the Hilton Boston Logan Airport and had awonderful stay each night. We have stayed here a number of times in the past and enjoy being welcomed by DeeDee in the Dining Room. Our dinner meals were outstanding.
The beds and pillows were extremely comfortable and it was nice to have a night light in the bathroom.
This hotel was an excellent choice.
Hotel Guests from Bella Vista, California

title: “Worst hotel service I have ever had in 30 years!”
text:
Stayed at the Hilton LAX for three nights last weekend for a conference. Absolutely unbelievable less than two star service ! First they gave away the second two nights of our stay three night booking. The hotel had been booked in Canada over ten days previously. Fortunately we checked over something to do with the credit card billing and found out and had to rebook otherwise would have been out in the cold. Managed to salvage our booking. We were at this time being quite calm and freindly. Got up to the room and the sheets hadn't been changed or the room cleaned at all! Called to complain and then the next night came back to a uncleaned room again- bathtub full of dirty water, no towels, room hadn't been cleaned so there was tea left in cups- but the bed had been made.??Complained again and they sent someone up at midnight with towels who made excuses why they hadn't cleaned it fully? Are you serious? How do you make the bed and leave a clean bathmat and no towels and the rest of the room a mess???
Then I saw an enormous cockroach in the bathroom on the main floor while at the conference the second day.
After we checked out they had double charged the credit card they had expressly said they wouldn't charge and charged the other card as well.
Called the manager and he was playing hard ball with us after I mentioned that this was a hilton not a grade B hotel and they had some responsibility to at least keep their word with the credit card payments. All of this was double checked because the general feeling was that things were not in order.
Also you have to pay for internet and they block your access to your IPhone net usage while you are at the hotel. 
Need I say more? I would never, repeat never stay there again even if it was free.
After the service from the day manager I would not stay in another HIlton. He was rude and didn't show any accountability or concern over any of it.
This has never happened to me in all the years of staying in all kinds of Hotels worldwide. Ok, people make mistakes but the manager is responsible to be accountable and make up for them. I repeat do not stay here if you can find other lodging.

title: “When you don't care, it shows.”
text:
How unfortunate! The worst DoubleTree--actually, the worst Hilton product--I've experienced.
My check in was surly, and I didn't even get the trademark cookies DoubleTree is known for. I have a Hilton HHonors Gold card and a Platinum AMEX Hilton Card, and the agent just gave me the cold shoulder. I asked about the customary breakfast coupons, and he told me I was on a list.
The nastiness notwithstanding, he did upgrade my room to a junior suite. The decor of the hotel is quite tired, and very dated--circa 1987. Still the bed was nice, even though it was a double, not a queen. There was a sitting area, and if I leaned out of the hotel windor, I could see City Hall. Hallways were even more dated than the room.
Bathrooms have granite counters, and showers have a curved rod.
As for that list, the folks in the restaurant didn't know about that, but finally I did get coupons. Free breakfast can be worth what you pay for it. . .the omelettes and waffles, made to order, were good. . .all else less so. Coffee was thin. Service was spotty.
Fitness center is free to guests, and right off the indoor pool and outdoor sun deck. Five treadmills and three ellipticals. Nice, but not well maintained. The headsets, for example, were not replenished daily.
In fairness, some of the staff were nice, but on the balance, the hotel is just sleep walking through being open. Supposedly a renovation is planned, but for now, everything is just a mish-mash of decor, etc. . .
I paid $89 through Hotwire, and the hotel's going rate was twice that--more for the junior suite where I stayed. For $89, the very central, very convenient location was worth it, but at full price, I'd have been much more unhappy.
It is so unfortunate that the management of this hotel could run things so poorly. There is a sign in the elevator that says, "When you CARE, it shows". Well, when you don't care, it shows too. 
I'm not sure anyone cares here--from the surly person who checked me in, to the pleasant but brisk person who checked me out--and never asked how my stay was.
Unless you get a screaming deal here, stay elsewhere. Or wait for the renovation. The photos in the lobby of the product to come look nice.

title: “Many problems, rude staff, small rooms, whole hotel floor smelled of cigarette smoke”
text:
I'm a marathon runner in extreme shape and I was accused of smoking by the management. When I told them I don't smoke they basically called me a liar. The WHOLE floor I was on stank of smoke. They tried to bill me $350 cleaning fee. LOL. American Express had to take care of the false accusations. Their management team is awful, extremly condescending. OH AND JULIE -- SHOULD BE FIRED ASAP SHE IS THE EPITOME OF FAIL.
Here is my letter to the St Regis: 
The serious and shocking allegations leveled by management of the St. Regis hotel of wrong doing on my part involves smoking in a guest room.
As I have told all parties involved, I DO NOT SMOKE, I HAD A LOVED ONE JUST PASS AWAY FROM CANCER.... I expect prompt attention to this matter. I have never ever been wrongly accused of smoking before, especially by a supposed 5 star hotel. These accusations have cause myself and my wife plenty of anguish and ruined our honeymoon. I am mortified and sincerely hope this is taken care of before I escalate this to the next level. Attached find my response to front desk manager Julie --:
Hello Julie,
Thank you for removing the mini bar charge. As I had told you at check out, we did NOT use the minibar. 
As for the $350 charge for smoking I don't know what your talking about? Neither myself or my wife smoke. We are marathon runners and smoking is not one of the things we do to train. A close relative of mine recently passed away from cancer, WE DO NOT SMOKE. At this point proof from the St. Regis is necessary that in your words "you and your guest appeared to have smoked in a non-smoking room". I am completely shocked....The first room we were given the whole floor smelled strongly of smoke, also we had no cell service. We asked to be moved promptly, which we were NOT and the second room also smelled musty / smokey in addition to being dirty. Also the whole 12th floor smelled of smoke.
My wife and I had several problems staying at the St. Regis San Francisco .
First was asking to be moved and our "butler", or the front desk dropping the ball. We checked in at 1pm and were not moved until approximately 7pm. The bathroom and the window ledge were filthy and we had to let housekeeping know to come and clean it again. There was never ice or water in the room, after we made a point to let housekeeping know we wanted it there. Several times we ran out of toilet paper and had to call the front desk, half a roll was left in the room and not an extra anywhere to be found. We ordered room service once, the order was all wrong, they forgot my fries with the sandwich, and also the dressing for my wife's salad. We had to wait another 30 minutes to get the ordered items, by that time the food was cold. Never once were we greeted by the doorman when we walked in after a long day. Both floors we were given rooms on smelled of smoke. The final problem was when we were checking out and you Julie -- were helping and there were
bogus charges on my bill. This 
is extremely unprofessional and completely the opposite experience I've had at other St. Regis properties . I am a frequent traveler and I have never been treated so poorly by a supposed 5 star property.
As I told you when I was checking out yesterday I am in Napa Valley for few more days of vacation. Your email this morning pretty much ruined my day.
I would expect the St. Regis to solve this today amicably and issue a complete refund asap. I would like you to forward this email to the San Francisco hotel manager and St. Regis head office. I will be contacting them as soon as I return to Los Angeles .

title: “Nice Property & People---Great Deal!”
text:
This would not ordinarily stick out as a hotel I would choose, but after buying it sight unseen thru Priceline's Express Deals makes it a stellar performer. I took a chance on buying this 3 STAR hotel via Priceline for 2 nights and then kept on buying.
On a family visit with business attached I needed a center base that was convenient and inexpensive for a week. Holiday Inn San Jose-Airport was a great fit.
Found this one via Priceline for $61-70 a night (depending on how busy the the hotel is I guess).
You can book this hotel on Priceline Express Deals CHEAP. Here is the listing heading:
San Jose Area
$169 similar hotels+
$61 per night
This Hotel has: Indoor or Outdoor Pool | Free Parking | Restaurant | Business Center
Pros:
Updated on the 7th & 8th floors where I was located with lovely furnishings.
Whole hotel has nice public space, a bar, restaurant and outdoor patio area with fireplaces and pool.
Staff was pleasant but not overly friendly even after 7 days.
Convenient location to most things in the South Bay.
FREE WiFI on 7 & 8. Cable on other floors.
Free Parking.
Cons:
Breakfast buffet is free with full priced room but $15 without and NOT WORTH IT. Eggs, bacon, sausage etc was just not fresh. Order off the menu instead (fresh) or go to Denny's next door. Wait staff was nice but used to the free coupon crowd. You might ask for a 20% off coupon for breakfast as they seem to hand them out easily.
I had to change rooms 2 times during the week because of Wifi down in one section and then a Mold smell in another room. All the rooms were well kept, updated and clean. 
Parking can be tough in front late at night but there is more in the back.
BOTTOM LINE:
If you can buy it through Priceline----DO IT!

title: “Great Airport Hotel”
text: Often difficult to find a good hotel near a big city airport. But thia one deserves praise. Competent courteous staff. Nice size clean rooms (in fact, beautifully clean and comfortable throughout). And excellent shuttle bus service make this a real standou!

title: “No”
text:
The location is pretty good. Located on the eastern part of Boston, a few minutes walk away from the aquarium and from historical sites.
The actual hotel is a waste of money. The shower handle shot out and water came gushing everywhere. They fixed it but just the fact that it happened is ridiculous. The front desk guy was very nice and helpful, so that made it a bit better.
The whole floor smelt like pot the night we stayed. That same night, we were in the elevator with what seemed like homeless people, and they came off on our floor. Guess the Hilton lets anyone in!
Don't bother with this hotel. Location is good, but there are definitely better for the price. It's too pricey for what you get (which are just headaches)

title: “Good location and free parking.”
text:
The hotel is located in a good location for a visit to san francisco,CA as a tourist.
It's appears safe around the area and has free parking with limited parking on lobby level.Elevetor is centrally located on lobby/parking level with luggage carriers and room key access for the elevators at the lobby location making it safer access to the hotel.There is some sight seeing brochures and maps in the lobby with a small seating area.
The room was very nice and clean and well appointed with flat screen tv(approx. 42"),with round table with chairs and bay window view and climate(ac unit) underneath this area of the window.The climate control was on the wall near the bathroom.The window did open at this level making it precarious for children to be around with the window open though.A modern alarm/radio clock was on night stand besides bed.Plenty of pillows for the bed of which was king size and firm mattress made it very comfortable sleeping on.
The bathroom was roomy and had a heat lamp as opposed to exhaust fan and nice showerhead and plenty of soap dishes in tub with supplied shower cap and soap,shampoo,conditioner.A coffee maker with ice bucket and hot and cold cups provided along with coffee/tea I think also.A ice machine and drink machine only is on this level at elevator.
Furnishing were clean and modern and overall very nice!
I don't remember seeing a hotel directory though in the room of amenities,etc.A phone was availabe but didn't need one like most unless need to call the front desk which never had a reason to since the room was well appointed with everything.
I definitely will consider staying again at this property of their other properties.It's pricey for the area($98/nt weekday and $140/nt. weekend but hey this is san francisco,CA).

title: “too pricey for what you get”
text:
Stayed at hotel for 5 nights. the location is great. right next to Broadway, soho and tribeca. Good shopping and a lot of good restaurants.
the Room is very small. no brekfast included. have to pay 23$ for some fruit and coffee. please.
They don't have a gym, but they have agreement with NY Sports club on Broadway. Remeber to bring your own lock, or they charge 10 $.
Room either has hot or cold settings. so you have to wake up and turn off or on. Room seems kinda old, the hotel could stand a bit of renovation.
decent place in great location, but it's too pricey for what you get.

title: “Really not good”
text:
First I should start with I travel to NYC 12 to 20 times per year and am familiar with many of the hotels. I have stayed in over 10 hotels there this year alone and without a doubt the Bentley was the worst. Having said that let me share the good first. Their staff is very friendly and helpful. Unfortunately the hotel itself was not at all good. They suffer from some misbelief that they should turn off your electricity when you are out of the room and raise the blinds so even this week when it was cool outside it was hard to get the room cool (under 75). That was exacerbated by the lousy air conditioner as well. On top of that he hotel is very poorly located for most NYC travelers and it requires a lot just to get to the more popular areas for business or touring. To top it off they had my bill completely wrong (overcharged my by $46 plus taxes per night) which they did fix but it took a while. If I had not asked for a room under my door (that is not their ordinary practice) I would have been checking out before I found this and it took over 10 minutes to fix.
In summary I would recommend staying almost anywhere else in Manhattan until they get the HVAC and electricity fixed unless you just need to be under the 59th street bridge.

title: “Fantastic”
text: Wow what a great hotel. Great staff, great rooms and location. Will stay again for sure.

title: “Good hotel in Japantown”
text:
We stayed here during the 2012 SFIAAF. It was super centrally located for the festival and convenient to the the screenings at the Kabuki and New People. The hotel itself is very nice. Our room was lovely. It was in the Garden section of the hotel, but our room was on the 4th floor. It was a corner room that was quite large. Toilet, sink, and shower were in separate areas which was great if you are staying with a friend. Decor was beautiful. Sauna attached to the shower room was a nice suprise
Only negatives: wall was thin so we heard our neighbor, we had a corner room which made it super easy to hear the street traffic at the rear of the hotel, and the shower head was too low. I'm 5'8" and had to crouch to wash my hair. Also the ledge on the tub made it easy for water to roll onto the floor creating a mini pool. Wouldn't be an issue if I were a tub-soak type of person. 
However, I would stay here again.

title: “Great location”
text: On check in the lady changed our room from a 2 x double to a king with a roll away and we are very thankful to her for suggesting this change - our room was large and had a lovely view. Wifi is not free - great location, next to Grand central station, and easy walking distance to most attractions. We walked everywhere but it was prob a 30 min walk to central park and Tiffany's - easy to get taxi from hotel front. The only complaint I would have about the room was the toilet setting - it was near impossible to reach the toilet paper! We were traveling with 4 other couples and they also had difficulties with this, with some having to change rooms, as if you are large than average you can not physically twist yourself into the required position to find the loo paper! silly complaint yes but it seemed that many also thought the same!

title: “Great front desk & concierge service”
text: I was at the Grand Hyatt for a conference, and it was good, as conference accommodations go. Very clean, nice service. Don't bother with the in-hotel restaurants. Way over priced and the food isn't great.

title: “Cheaper than most hotels downtown!”
text: Compared to a lot of the hotels downtown this hotel was one of the cheapest! And taking that in consideration i really like this hotel! Service is ok. Parking is a bit pricy, $20

title: “Clean and Good Location”
text: I stayed here for a weekend by myself (single female) and was happy with the service and the rooms. It is a budget hotel but was clean and comfortable and would happily stay here again. It was close to trams and trains. Had a safe in the room which was good to keep valuables in.

title: “Great Location!”
text: Stayed there for our Spring Break trip to NYC. We have visited many times and try to find something that has good access to the subway but not sacrificing comfort. This was a great find for us. Very comfortable rooms, great beds, breakfast was plentiful - something for everyone. Just around the corner from the red line and a couple blocks from the yellow. A stones throw from many of the theaters. A nice walk to Central Park. Very good location for us. Staff was great - friendly and nice. Will go back! Probably ask for a room on the back side, though - 8th is busy and LOUD!

title: “Modern Hilton - decent rooms, well located, nicely appointed”
text: Rooms are nice, beds are great, no complaints. I sleep well, but did note the train engineer's attempt to alter my experience (multiple horn blasts at 2am, but hey, I am on East Coast time, so 2am here is coffee time in DC....). Bathroom is nice, but has a motion sensor on the lighting which actually shut off a couple of times while I was in the shower. I am as "green as the next guy", but the auto shut off light, combined with a closer on the bathroom door meant showering in the pitch dark. For the less adventurous soul it might have been dangerous. Combination of price, location, decor, great breakfast location makes this a great value and nice place to stay. Hilton is a superior brand. Don't take my comments as negative. I am not picky. This is a good value in a very modern room. A very comfortable stay. Staff was courteous and professional. Room is spotless. Hoping the hotel reads this: the fitness center could use some TLC (TV on elliptical is not functional, headsets not cleaned, stocked, no clock in fitness room, check overall cleanliness in fitness center). Again,small things. I like this hotel.

title: “Reasonable stay for business travelers”
text: On two recent stays, I found the rooms at the Fairfield Inn near the Philadelphia Airport to be clean, if slightly in need of updating. The complimentary airport shuttle was a nice amenity, and the front desk staff were friendly and helpful. While the regional train stops about a 10-minute walk from the hotel, the sidewalk is discontinuous. The shuttle driver was willing to drop me off at the station on his way to the airport, which I appreciated. I walked back from the station to the hotel when finished in center city - it was a feasible walk, but the discontinuous sidewalk and possibility of heavy traffic makes it a little less convenient than one might imagine. During my second stay, I had a rental car - it was a quick drive to the University of Pennsylvania from the hotel. If I visit Philadelphia again on business, I'll be pretty likely to stay here again.

title: “Only if you desperate”
text:
This is our first 2 hours dealing with this hotel:
Waiting 25 minutes for the shuttle that suppose to be there every 20 minutes (24/7)
Calling the hotel - no answer for 4 times and then finally when we got someone to answer we told that the shuttle will be there "shortly".
30 minutes later - we are on the shuttle for the 5 minutes drive!!!!
Checkin was smoothly - nice surprise!
Got in to the room: Stinks, stained carpets that I don't dare to walk barefoot, free bottle of mineral water (shame it was opened), broken handles, and I can continue....
maybe 20 years ago it was a nice place...
NOT today
Go somewhere else doesn't worth ANY money!

title: “A little disappointed with the second-tier room”
text:
Got stuck overnight and had a good stay before so picked this hotel with a airline discount voucher. The room was still pretty nice, but not nearly as nice as the Park and Fly room. I checked the website, but am not sure how to distinguish between the rooms--I'd like to know what I am getting when booking here.
Overall, the hotel is clean and is a really good hotel. The shuttle is frequent, it is near the subway, and has a parking garage (though not cheap to park with daily rates). 
Internet access is free in the lobby, but not in rooms, which is a negative. For late arrivals, it would be nice if food-service was available later. The bar has pretty good food but closes at 10 or 11 PM and there is not a lot close if you do not have a car.
The staff is friendly and efficient. For stranded travelers, they do offer toiletries. The lobby is large, and nicely decorated, but somehow sterile. Overall, this is a good place to stay near the airport, and a really good value. I do often recommend it for park and fly.

title: “Rooms and staff are great, hope the street changes its crowd”
text:
This is a big room for NYC standards, specially where they have the king beds. I know the rest of the USA has huge rooms, but this is as big as the (newer) budget hotels are going to get. It was comfortable, nice flatscreen, and bathroom was also bigger than expected. 
Yes the street is creepy, but just keep a brisk walk and you'll be fine. This complex is actually brand spanking new, and a similar hotel is about to open its doors next door in a couple of months time. Then there will be three hotel towers on the street. So when the scaffolding will be gone, and there will be a lot more foottraffic moving along, that should take away more of the creeps. Although I saw a lot of cops on the streets, so until then you'll be fine too.
Do yourself a favor and turn north on Ninth Ave, there are great restaurants a couple of short blocks up, and restaurant row isn't that good compared what they have going on upwards of 43rd and 9th! 
For the gay travelers, this is also a gayfriendly neighborhood. Jammed between 8th and 9th av (and 43rd and 57th street), try Therapy, nice place for drinks. And non-gays, it is not going to scare you away, its just guys and girls having fun, but not in a leather/non clothing, don't want to confront your kids and grandma kind of way, so at least enjoy the cuisine! I did see a lot of family's trying to get into the restaurants, but as they have a lot of 2 person tables, you might want to reserve so you don't miss your show. 
Ask for a high floor, and you'll have great view of the cityscape, nothing facy though, just tall buildings! Elevators are quite quick, as there are three. I've been in 30 floor 10 room a floor, buildings with 2 slower ones than these, so this is again as good as it gets. Just plan for the breakfast rush, then it might take 5 mins max. Staff are either trained well, or non-New Yorkers, they laugh, and look you in the eye while checking in!
So all in all, this is a great hotel, in a great location, 2 short blocks to 42nd, and a long block to times sq (7th), subway (huge 42nd street subway interconnect station) at the end of the street, across from port authority busterminal (take the bus from Newark airport, and it will drop you of at 42nd and 8th, 2 short blocks from the hotel, and pick up is at 41st, so only one short block!).

title: “Don't forget the ear plugs!!”
text: Even if there is a rare moment of quiet in downtown Manhattan, you won't get any sleep because the air conditioning is so noisy!! Rooms are mediocre, very small bathroom. Front desk could be a lot friendlier. The breakfast is very cheap - but dreadful!! Don't take it - go out to eat!! The only good thing is the location - and even this is not good at the moment as they are building right next door! You have to pay for internet.

title: “Amazing views, and great service.”
text: My boyfriend and I have stayed at this hotel on multiple occasions. The rooms facing the water have great views, and they have great room service. The restaurant also has great food, and pool area is great! Overall, I love staying here, it's a great hotel in San Diego and is also close to downtown and the beach.

title: “Outstanding Service”
text: The hotel was superb but the service made the stay outstanding. Everyone there seemed to take a personal stake in making the stay perfect.

title: “Clean & close to interstate”
text: The staff was helpful &, for the most part, friendly. Hotel was clean. There is not a whole lot around it, but it is a quick drive to other areas. Breakfast was above average for what it was. We could hear road noise (of course, it's right by the interstate), but that wasn't bothersome to us.

title: “Great location”
text: We stayed here over Chrismas and had a great time. The staff we helpful and when we had a problem with noisy pipes ,the repair man was there in minutes ! He was fantastic and went beyond the call of duty.The location is great,just a short walk to the MOMA ,Radio city,Central park etc.We didn't eat there as we thought it was too dear and the local delis are hard to beat.The room was a good size and the bed was very comfortable.My one complaint is that we had to ask every day for more tea and coffee bags.

title: “Convenient”
text: I came for my sons BMT graduation!! The hotel was close to the base. Front desk very helpful with directions. Stores and resturants very close(Still need car though). If anything I would complain about is I didnt get to utilize the spa or pool or the breakfast was out the hotel before served . Plenty of towels!! Definately will stay here anytime I visit.

title: “Fantastic Hotel and Great Location”
text: I spent 1 week at the Omni Parker house while attending function for work and the hotel was fantastic. The rooms were very nice and quite large for being downtown. Overall the hotel itself was quite immaculate as were the conference rooms. The staff was always very nice and would call me by my name as I walked through the lobby. Location was fantastic and there was lots to do within walking distance including a large shopping area with various stores.

title: “Great night's sleep in a great location.”
text: First trip to NYC and my next stay will also be at the Michelangelo. Great location. Loved the beds! Unobtrusive and helpful staff. Great start to every morning w/ wonderful coffees and croissants in the lobby. We were on the 7th floor w/out a view, but that was perfect, as I am a light sleeper and combined w/ the blackout curtains, I slept later than at home and only awoke once during the week to external noise! I loved the turn down service w/ chocolates.

title: “Radisson LAX: excellent”
text: We stayed at the Radisson LAX for a few days prior to a trip to our honeymoon in Hawaii, in order to be close to the airport, close to a storage unit where we stored our car, and to rack up some points in our Club Carlson account. We didn't expect the level of service we received; it was great. From Feliipe in the restaurant, to Norma in the bar and Ricky and Dwayne at the front, everyone was incredibly accommodating and went out of their way to make sure we got everything we needed, whether it was printing our boarding passes for us, making exceptions to menu items, or whatever. When we get back from Hawaii, we'll need a place to stay in L.A. for a few more days, and this Radisson will definitely get our business. I had stayed in the Radisson in Miraflores (Lima, Peru) for a couple of weeks earlier this year and was impressed; this facility is every bit as good. It definitely rates a 5-dot rating.

title: “A good choice”
text:
This Westin property is a pretty nice hotel. The staff is very friendly, the hotel is modern and the location is good. My room was very clean but did seem a little dated. 
My room had a couple of issues. The bathroom towel bar was coming off the wall and a light fixture was broken, actually exposing some wiring. I reported both to the front desk. A maintenance person tried to fix the light but it was still dangerous. The right response should have been to either properly fix the light or move me to another room, which they didn't do. I'll give them the benefit of the doubt because Westin is normally better than that. 
Valet parking is steep, $32 a day. Self parking is available for a little less but you lose in and out privileges. Do yourself a favor and go the valet parking route. The pool was a little small but nice.
Overall, I liked this Westin. It is suited for business or family travel.

title: “Nice hotel, nothing really special but good shuttle bus”
text: Not right in the centre of everything and because of this I think it is rather expensive for what it is. Nice comfy rooms though, very large and clean, but breakfast nothing to write home about. They do however offer a shuttle every half hour into downtown and to the space needle so that is really great.

title: “Such a Treat”
text: I was so excited about staying the Library Hotel and my expectations were exceeded. Our room was delightful. If you love books, reading, and libraries, this will be an experience you won't forget. The Reading Room, with delicious breakfast, treats, and of course the wine and cheese reception, is beautiful and cozy. I love the front desk staff encouraged us to have our local NYC friends meet us for the reception before we headed out for the night. I had my girlfriend meet us one night, and my husband had his friend meet us another night. This was so special to be able to welcome them and show them a hidden gem in their city. The bathroom in our room was fantastic. The entire hotel was beautifully decorated for Christmas. I must also mention the fabulous location right in the heart of Midtown. Steps from Bryant Park, NYPL, and minutes from Rockefeller Center. I absolutely hope to return to the Library Hotel!

title: “Good Budget Choice”
text: I've stayed here twice now. Overall, it's decent lodging for the price. Don't expect plush towels or other niceties. If you want clean, simple and cheap, this the place. Less than 15 minutes from downtown San Diego (depending on traffic).

title: “Disappointing”
text: My husband and I travelled to Washington, DC for the October 28, 2012, Marine Corps Marathon. Wanting to treat ourselves to a nice weekend, we selected L'Enfant Plaza Hotel over someplace like Best Western or Days Inn. For the price ($341 total for 2 nights), we expected some luxury. Not only was L'Enfant not luxurious, it wasn't even clean. There was trash in the hall way. The carpets and drapes in the room were stained. The wall paper was peeling. At the time of reservation (several months in advance), we requested a room with a king size bed. When we checked in, we were given a room with two double beds (not even queen size). When we requested to be changed to a king room, the desk clerk was rude and short tempered before complying. For the quality and service at L'Enfant, I would have expected to pay $75/night, not $149 + tax. We were disappointed with our stay.

title: “Excellent for those site seeing in Manhattan”
text:
We stayed in this hotel for 3 nights.
We found that the hotel was in a great and safe location. It's only 6 blocks away from the Empire State building, even closer to Penn station for access to the airports and has a police station very close by so no worries about security (not that you have to worry about this in Manhattan anyway). It is not, as someone mentioned close to the flat iron building (think they put the review against the wrong hotel).
The rooms are small but that's to be expected in one of the most expensive real estate places in the worlds. It wasn't to small that my sister and I couldn't fit to large bags in though. Also given that as tourists I think we just slept in the room and showered size wasn't that important.
The rooms are very clean and the beds are comfortable. The hotel staff couldn't be more helpful even though New Yorkers can appear a touch cold to begin with.
The breakfasts are basic. Cereal, coffee, muffins, doughnuts, waffles etc.. and are self service but if you don't like them then there are loads of cheap options to eat out close by.
All in all I would highly recommend this hotel as a cheap (for Manhattan anyway) option. As they say you get what you pay for.

title: “LOVED IT!!!”
text: To start with the location of this hotel was perfect for us. I went with a group of Premier Design Jewelers for the companies National Rally which was held at the Fort Worth Convention Center. The hotel was only a few blocks away. It was also within walking distance to many restaurants and shops. Not to mention the Starbucks in the lobby of the hotel...that was my favorite!!! The staff was very friendly and the hotel was gorgeous. I've stayed in several embassy suites and for the most part they've all been really nice but this location takes the cake. They are known for their gorgeous atrium in the center of the hotels and because of the location of this one, it doesn't have one...but it doesn't matter. Oh and not to forget the great breakfast bar they have. What's better than a made to order omelet bar with a chef there to make yours fresh each morning....YUMMY!!! This embassy suites is by far the best one I've ever stayed in. I will for sure be staying there next time I visit Fort Worth.

title: “Don't Stay Here Ever (no matter how cheap it is!)”
text:
If you check out my other reviews, you can see I'm not the most critical person. There are cheaper hotels/motels which are basic, but still clean and comfortable.
Hotel Whitcomb was a WHOLE other story. First off, the front desk is ridiculous with lines that may take you 20 minutes just to find out where the lobby bathroom is. They have 2 people working with no person dedicated to checked-in guests for simple questions. There is a gated line for all of us to wait which takes forever because of their inefficiency.
The person who helped me is this woman who had this "holier than thou" attitude who thought she was working at the Ritz-Carlton.
After finally getting my room card, I ventured to find this room. Now, the lobby and individual floors are lovely with old woodwork and such, but then you get to the really awful part. I followed the signs to my room, which I found out quickly, was BEYOND the fire door where there were 2 rooms in an unfinished fire escape looking hallway. The fire door was heavy enough that if I were screaming in there, no one would even hear me! (See pictures) The other room didn't even have a plaque on the door for the room number...it was written on the wall in PENCIL!
When I got into the room, it just got worse. The room was dark and dusty. My allergies immediately worsened. It was spacious, but everything was just old. There were 2 queen beds. When I lifted the coverlet, the underside was yellow and dingy. Moreover, hair (not the kind on your head) that was clearly not mine were laying in the coverlet. The bedding smelled like someone had already slept in it before and no one had changed the sheets.
As if it couldn't get any worse, the bathroom had hair (again, not from your head) on the walls and floors (at least 5 I could count, which is 5 too many).
I got my room changed to one that was not in the fire escape. The person at the front desk who helped me, I think his name was Burney, was very nice. The subsequent room was much nicer was clean crisp sheets and an almost clean bathroom (there was still a hair on the toilet).
I would never stay in this hotel ever again. Chains like Best Western, Holiday Inn, etc which are basic but comfortable (see my other reviews) are much more worth it than this dump. The only thing that was good about this place was that it was right on top of a MUNI/BART stop so it was easy to get to the airport and other places.

title: “Fantastic location”
text:
Well I have just come back from staying at the hotel and I have to say I have very little to complain about. The room was clean, the housekeeper was very quick, no sonner had we left the room and she was in there cleaning. The room was huge!! There were 4 ladies staying in 2 rooms, loads of space for clothes etc. The location of the hotel was great to get around and see all of NY. 
We didnt eat at the hotel, but we did at the diner next door, if I would recommend anything its DONT GO THERE!! The staff were rude, the food terrible and they expected a 15% service charge...for being rude?!! We found a fantastic little place just up the road on the right hand side, close to central park, that did the best breakfast, they were welcoming, the food was to die for and we couldn't have ate a nicer breakfast, plus it was the same place as next door!!
If you are new to the city the city bus tours were a good way in which to see all of new york and to hop on and off.
All in all we had a good stay, the only thing that ruined the holiday was the last hour. We requested a private car with the concierge and left our lugage with him to store, we tipped him and thanked him. Then when we collected our lugagge they got confused as to which was ours?!! Then I helped carry the luggage to the car, the concierge brought 2 of the eight bags, then he was really stroppy when we didnt tip him, when we had already tipped the earlier concierge and he only brought a few bags to the car?!!! We booked the car to take us to Newark airport and was quoted $55 plus tip, that was fine, when we got in he tried to take us to JFK?!! Then said that if we wanted to go to Newark it would be $70. plus tip. 
All in all the hotel was fantastic for what we wanted it for, just a place to sleep, it was a shame that the concierge ruined the end part of the stay.

title: “Best location in downtown Denver!”
text: My husband and I love to stay at this hotel when we go out in downtown Denver. The location is incredible. The rooms are VERY clean, and I love the newly renovated rooms. They have an "urban hip" feel, and they are very clean. A very special thanks to your friendly staff!

title: “Smaller than a sardine can, horrible service, but ok value for new york city”
text: The price and location is good considering it's in New York City, however, the room and bathroom were ridiculously small, barely any room for two suitcases, and one adult alone in the bathroom was very claustrophobic. Customer service was pretty horrible, they did not assist me with the beverage machine when it did not work, and they don't have a phone you can use to call for delivery, you have to go out a bit into the streets to use a pay phone. Overall if you're only staying for a couple nights, and need a place to just sleep and shower, than belnord hotel is doable. Otherwise, you need to pay more to stay in a larger hotel with better service in the city.

title: “Very friendly, clean and comfortable.”
text: I found the staff very nice. The rooms were large and the bed very comfortable. The decor is very bright and welcoming. I really liked the bathroom shower head which was very large and shower gel dispenser.

title: “Nice hotel”
text: We had a very nice three day stay at this Marriott! It was very comfortable and in a convenient location! We had breakfast included in our rate and it was very good! The bathroom was beautiful with a separate tub and shower!

title: “So So Experience”
text:
Visited Red Lion on 5th Avenue for a one night stay. Whilst the hotel is in a great location for visiting Pike Place and the shopping areas and the rooms are quite nice, I have to agree that for the price this hotel was really not worth it. We paid $199 US per night plus taxes.
The person we dealt with at check in ( Ryan ) was very miserable and impersonal. Really needs some customer service training.
This is the noisiest hotel I have ever stayed in. The walls must be made of paper as the people in the next room REALLY were enjoying themselves, if you know what I mean!!!!!!
The elevators were close by and were also going all night. The showers made a very loud vibrating sound when switched on not tonly in our room but all the rooms above and below us. Needless to say we would never stay at this property again.
I did not sleep at all that night which did not make for a very restful start to my Alaskan Cruise.

title: “Good hotel, excellent location”
text:
We were a family at 4, with two elder children. We had two double room, one at 9th floor and one at 15th floor. These rooms were similar. The rooms were clean and with enough space. The bathroom was good. The beds were very good. The hotel staff was very serviceoriented and helpful, The concierge (Larry) was very helpful with good suggestions how to utilize a short stay to see as much as possible.
We hadn't breakfast includeed, we bought breakfast one day, but we seemed the price was a bit high. The breakfast buffet was good with lots of choices but $20 + tip is maybe too high.
The hotel is very centrally loceted, only 5 min from Times Square, Broadway and the subway was at the corner. We really recommend this hotel and it was a good choice for us.

title: “Could not fault this hotel.”
