text: Besides the great location, the large room with huge bed and great amenities, we were mostly impressed with the fact that when we expressed our concern about being able to hear people on the treadmill, they immediatley changed our room with a smile. We were so grateful as the noise had kept us awake from about 5am that first morning. Fantastic place. The only down side was the cost of parking $48 plus tax per night, ridiculous. But we did find another parking spot around the corner for $20 per night.

title: “So So - not much else to say...”
text:
A typical, well used downtown hotel. Nice looking and pleasant interiors, but nothing too spectacular. Really didn't experience any problems while staying there. The beds were very comfortable - that was the best part of the stay there!
The only complaint I had while staying there was the amount of dust in the room. You can tell that the main surface areas that people use are wiped down - but the non traditional areas do not get dusted very often. Items such as the top of the in room coffee maker, tops of sink splashguards, picture frames, etc. were not dusted in a while. The Nintendo game controller sitting on the bureau looked like it hadn't been used or dusted in months. The headboard to the bed was loaded, too. I even wrote the word "dust" in the dust itself before my final night's stay there - and the word was still there after housekeeping cleaned the room! The room wasn't dirty - just very dusty.
Be aware of the downtown Houston area, too. Just about every restaurant closes there by 7:00 during the week - and the weekend, forget it. Most food spots downtown do not even open on the weekends! Made eating a meal under $20 a challenge most nights.
(I travel all over the country with my job, and I contribute on EVERY hotel I stay in. Trip Advisor has been a great tool for me, and I contribute fairly, for both good and bad facilities.)

title: “My favorite place to stay in New York!”
text:
Hi this is LONG ISLAND CHICK here with my new review on the Sheraton Tribeca.
If this is going to be your first trip to New York City then welcome. If you have been here before, then you will have some ideas on what to do and where to stay. The most important thing to ask yourself would be, what do I want to do?, where do I want to eat?, etc. I live on Long Island and come into NYC all the time. The Sheraton Tribeca is in an ideal location. if you are driving in, the hotel staff will park your car overnight for you. All you have to do is pull up in front of hotel. Yes they charge a fee, but what parking garage in New York doesn't? You will be so close to the subway (across the street) you can go anywhere. To top it off Little Italy and China Town are within a hop, skip and jump away. I love to eat at DaNico and DeGennaro and go shopping at Step Up Boutique on Mulberry Street. The hotel staff is great and the place is immaculate. They have a nice sit down area for free WiFi, bar, cafe and a small deli like stop for coffee and take out breakfast etc. And if your an AMERICAN EXPRESS STARWOOD member then check it out for cash & points. There is no better time to come to NYC then during the holiday season. Everything is in full swing with lights and decorations. Plan ahead and you will have a great time. There is also the Discount Ticket Booth at Times Square. Don't let the long lines fool you as they move quickly. 50% to 60% off some broadway show is not a bad deal. Yes. you have to see a show. How could you come to NYC and not see a BROADWAY OR OFF BROADWAY show? This is NYC after all. Have fun and most of all be safe and be aware of your surroundings at all times.

title: “Disappointing”
text: Let me start with a positive, the room was very clean and the bedding comfortable. However, the "standard room was very very small, a queen bed barely fit into the room. The staff was just okay...not very helpful or kind. The morning of checkout, I realized I had left something in the room. The hotel staff made no attempt to looking for it or returning our phone calls. Also, the pool has very strange hours...don't expect to relax and layout during the day. Lastly, Whats with the pill bottle decor on the nightstand??...weird! see pic.

title: “Atmosphere even if most on the property are too young to know a rock from a rolling stone.”
text: If you're celebrating - this is upscale and fun! Clearly attractive to youth and the giddiness of their inexperience, relaxed, very San Diego. The staff handles immature drama graciously. No tension. Nice. It's located perfectly to the convention center. The marina is close by, Nobu is fantastic, the Float is fabulous. Most importantly it's right on 5th at the gateway to the gas lamp district which reminds me exactly of M street in Georgetown DC. Incredibly fun and accessible. Friendly staff. Polite but to the point. There is no discomfort at all staying here and being of "age" but be mindful this is an upscale late night party district on the weekends. So go stay in Del Mar if you're looking for solitude and quiet. The staff is down to earth and doesn't have affect just lots of expeditious people skills, even if they're too young to know a rock from a rolling stone.

title: “Graceland + HeartBreak hotel”
text: Was a stop-over on our way to Orlando..Hotel is a little aged.. But clean.. Lobby is cool with the Retro chairs. Took our young girls in the Pink Cadillac to the BBQ restaurant for dinner was delicious and fun. Enjoyed the tour of Graceland and staying right there was handy. The package deal for the hotel that included tour tickets is well worth the money check out the Web sit for the Hotel. Certainly visiting Graceland is something you should get on the bucket list.. And staying at the Hotel added to the experience.

title: “Met our needs - travelling with child”
text:
My wife and I stayed here for a week at the end of July. We were travelling with our daughter so we wanted a suite. This was the only reasonably-priced suite we could find for our trip. 
It's location near the GWU-Foggy Bottom metro stop is excellent. It's also minutes from Watergate (CVS, Safeway, café, etc.) and a 7-11. 
The renovations were never an issue, although one elevator was covered in a protective covering. The hotel is definitely dated and worn, however, the renovations should take care of the that. That said, it did the job and provided what a family would need in a suite. 
The staff were friendly and helpful. However, whenever we really needed assistance (at check-in and check-out) there was only a single person on duty. 
I had to get into the safe-deposit box in the office before check out and no one was available to help. The bell hop even tried to open the box to no avail. I would've done it myself, but I didn't want to interfere. I waited for 10-15 minutes before some guy got off the phone in the back office. 
Our room had an adjoining door which, unfortunately, led to noisy neighbors in the next room. That door did not provide much sound insulation and they woke our daughter up a couple of times at night. 
The rooftop pool is small but adequate and provided much-needed relief from hot days walking around the Mall. You did get to see some close-up views of plans landing at National airport. 
Room service was decently-priced as far as hotels go and the breakfast food was fine and punctual.

title: “The door slamming hotel”
text: Brand new property where space is a commodity. There is not much common space. Rooms brand new but small. Shower is tiny. Water pressure is limited by water saver. Free breakfast every morning. Free wifi. The biggest negative of this hotel is that you can hear a lot of noise in the hallways and tons of door slamming, especially when house keeping starts about 9.

title: “Great hotel, great location, great city”
text:
Who could ask for a better location? Right over Grand Central Station, so you have access to the incredible New York City subway system that can take you virtually any place in the five boroughs. You're also a two minute walk to buses going uptown, downtown and crosstown.  
Grand Central also has two levels filled with food shops and restaurants, priced from very reasonable to not so reasonable, but very delicious. You're also close to literally hundreds of restaurants serving great food and walking distance from the great theaters and shows on Broadway and Lincoln Center.   Getting back to the hotel: It's recently been remodeled. The rooms are modern looking and extremely comfortable. And the staff will bend over backwards to accommodate you in every way they can. As for the price, it varies with the season, but the last time I stayed there I found it very reasonable and a real value for the money. You'll leave feeling rested, relaxed and glad you stayed there

title: “Unexpectedly bad with surly service”
text:
I booked this hotel based on the reviews here. When I arrived, it seemed fine - I arrived late at night (11PM). The lobby seemed pleasant, if a bit dated. The front desk staff couldn't find my reservation. Producing the confirmation code from my travel agency didn't help. Bottom line is, they didn't have my reservation. Granted, it was some communication snafu between my agency and the hotel, but it wasn't MY fault. I prepaid for a room with guaranteed late arrival. The front desk agent DID end up taking care of it, but not without a surly attitude. The tone of the transaction was that it was my fault, and that she was doing me a huge favor. I finally said "Look I'm not trying to argue. All I know is that I booked a room through my travel agency online and prepaid for 4 nights. I picked this place because the TripAdvisor reviews said that the staff was great." "Well, we are great, sir, and I am taking care of you," was the response, but I still felt that the transaction was unnecessarily laced with surliness and a condescending attitude. 
That said, the hotel really needs some work. It is older, and smells very musty and tired. The hallways carpets are badly stained, and many of the walls, doors, and corners are scuffed and chipped and worn. Furniture in the rooms is serviceable, but is old, with chips and scuffs. The room smells old and musty. The tub in the bathroom needs refinishing. There is no refrigerator, no microwave, and the WiFi is unbelievably slow. Elevators are old, slow, creaky, and a recent repair on the control panel made it confusing, as if there is no 3rd floor, since the 1 and 2 buttons are lighted, but the 3rd floor button is unmarked. This is simply an indicator of how old and in need of renovation this place is. 
I would rate this place as 1.5 or 2 stars, certainly not 3+. 
On the plus side, it is quiet, and is conveniently located. The breakfast bar is tiny but OK. Restaurant staff is friendly. Rooms are large.

title: “Great hotel in convenient location”
text: We really enjoyed staying at the Palomar during our trip the San Francisco. The room was modern, clean, and cozy. The hotel was located right on the main shopping street and close to many attractions. The best surprise is the happy hour each day that includes sangria and wine. Would definitely recommend this hotel to a friend.

title: “Best staff in LA”
text: The staff here is some of the best I have seen. Emily at the front desk is amazing and Angel in room service. They have been sold out a lot so that is why I rated it a value. Usually hotels go rate crazy at max occupancy. I have stayed here three times this month and wouldnt go elsewhere.

title: “Mixed Impressions”
text:
I stayed in this hotel because I was attending a meeting at the Convention Center down the block. Starting with the positives, this Embassy Suites appears to be very new, had a very nice sized room with a flat screen TV in the livingroom (and regular TV in bedroom), nice bathroom amentities, a very nice breakfast buffet and excellent sushi available for take out/eat in in the restaurant in the lobby.
On the negative staff, the front desk staff was brusk and seemed to lack the customer service standard that I have come to expect at Hilton, Marriott and Hyatt properties (this is a Hilton property). Also, unless one was attending the Convention Center (which is about two windy blocks away), the hotel seems a little out of the way of DC attractions. 
Given a choice between this hotel and the Homewood Suites property (also a Hilton Chain) in DC, I'll return to the Homewood Suites. Better room, amenities and staff.

title: “Good Value, Good Location, Mid Market Hotel”
text:
Just got back and felt this was a very good hotel for the money. Very clean and staff was helpful. We reserved a bay view room for $149 (floors 9-11) but unfortenatly the FOG blocked most of the views... the hotel is about 10 blocks from the bay so we could see the houses and businesses all the time!
We arrived way early (930 am) and our room was ready so we got to check in! Breakfast was ok.. cereal, boiled eggs, fruit, juices, bagels... nothing super.. but plenty.
We flew into SFO and took BART ($4.95) to Powell station, then bought a 3 day UNI bus/trolley car pass for $15.. took Powell-Hyde trolley (we packed light) to Lombard street and walked 3 blocks down to hotel. It is true, busses nearby.. I was a bit nervous about finding my way around but the front desk staff extremely friendly and had a map of a few major routes... found out 1 block away bus 30 goes by fishermans warf area, then china town, then financial district, then by Powell station. It comes about every 7 minutes! So we rode 30 about 20 times. So excellent location for using public transit.. and staff is helpful.
Only compliant is that the windows are not mirrored at all... so close the drapes for privacy... we discovered this later in the day when we went out for a walk.. a little too late.
Again, we would stay in a heartbeat again here... very clean and in good shape.. they also use newer keys than the old magentic cards. They even held our bags the last day all day long for no charge!

title: “NYC Trip”
text: Have stayed at the Hampton Inn on several occasions. Location is perfect if you are in the city for shopping or seeing a show. Kids love to go to FAO and visit central park when we are here. Breakfast is a wonderful, but if you want to go out i would recommend Fluffy's just up the street.

title: “Tiny!!”
text: We stayed at The Milford for four nights in early September. The hotel is in a perfect location for exploring Times Square / Hop on Hop off buses / Shopping. The down side is that the location is all this hotel has to offer, the rooms are tiny! no room for luggage, very cramped conditions and bathroom is no better. The renovations are cosmetic and of low quality, was paint on carpet of our room, cheap fixtures, air con very loud and kept turning off. The staff are rude and not in the least bit helpful, lobby is always packed with people and hectic, hallways are dark and damp smelling, and our room was not clean when we arrived, hair in tub and in bed, carpet dirty, and it was not cleaned much better while we were staying there.. We booked this hotel simply to rest our heads at nights but even for that I would not stay here again.

title: “A great stay all around”
text: Clean, attractive, a great location, and really excellent service. The room was small but nicely decorated. Good food nearby, easy transportation...I simply have no complaints. The best part of the experience were the other guests we met and the laid back, friendly staff here.

title: “One Of the Best”
text: Stayed here at the end of a long trip around the USA and have to say it was just wonderful. All the staff were very friendly and helpful, especially the doorman and front desk staff - even when I forgot my room number! The bed was so comfortable and the room very high quality. I can't recommend this hotel highly enough for comfort and service, can't wait to go back.

title: “Quaint small hotel in NYC”
text: We had never stayed in the downtown area of NYC before. One of the criteria we looked for was parking. The Best Western Plus Seaport on Peck Slip almost under the Brooklyn Bridge was one of those we managed to seek out. It is about one block away from the South Street Seaport as seen on many a movie and is a hot spot for tourists. Located in a very historic area of New york, this hotel is on the old side with plenty of character that grabs you from entering the lobby through the halls and into the room. Our room at five windows in a corner unit. it was like staying in a bed and breakfast. Very clean and functional, the hotel was a quick walk to many of the significant sites of downtown NYC, City Hall, Wall Street, Federal Hall, 911 Ground Zero, fun shopping and great restaurants and leisure spots. The Best Western was also one of the more affordable hotels in NYC. The staff were most helpful and welcoming. They ensured our comfort and cared about our stay with them. Do stay. Feel the hostory from the cobblestone streets to the beautiful architecture of the low rise buildings around the hotel. Explore the wonderful pubs and shops only steps away and of course see parts of downtown NYC that few people take the time to explore.

title: “Chicago Getaway for New Family”
text:
We were very pleased with the service that we received while staying at the Hyatt Regency Chicago. 
The hotel is in "ok" shape and generally clean for the shape that it is in. The hotel location is awesome! It is close to everything!
We didn't experience any delays with checking in and the front desk staff was very helpful. We purchased our room off of Priceline for $75 and we inquired about an upgrade to a suite when we checked in. The upgrade would have been an additional $150 so we opted not to do the upgrade. We had requested a refrigerator for our room and they waived the $25 fee for that since we had an infant with us.
The room that we got had an awesome view of Navy Pier and we enjoyed the fireworks from our window on Wednesday night. The bed was VERY comfortable. The only downfall was the paper-thin walls and the connecting doors between the rooms. On the first night, I could hear the guy next to us snoring throughout the night. Needless to say, our infant heard him too so mom and baby didn't sleep good the first night. Thank goodness he checked out and we had a better night's sleep the next night. 
After we checked out, we came back to the hotel to pick up our luggage (after shopping all day) and Angie at the Assistant Manager's desk was VERY helpful with giving us a temporary suite to use so that I could privately breastfeed our infant.
The service at this hotel was top notch! As a family, we probably won't stay here again only because of the noise issue. Other than that, it is a great hotel.

title: “A very average forgettable stay”
text:
room inside door handle fell off the first time we used it.
We paid $20 per day extra for two breakfast meals per day, to find out that we could of paid
less just ordering the same meal from the menu. Very loud parking lot.

title: “I'm glad I didn't listen to the bad reviews”
text: After reading about bed bugs and roaches, I was apprehensive about staying here, but booked my room nonetheless as it is, in fact, very close to EVERYTHING. It was close to the freeway entrance, as well. GREAT LOCATION! The front desk kept it very simple and easy for both check-in and check-out, which was a relief considering how tired we were. The room was clean and the beds were sufficiently comfortable - NO BUGS! The only thing that they could improve upon is their shower... It was all hard water and felt kind of slimy. Other than that, great stay at the Best Western Holywood Plaza!

title: “Pretty hotel, perfect location and excellent quality price ratio.”
text: We were very happy to stay there. The staff was always friendly and helpful. The location of the hotel could not be better, it is nearby all the cool places. The accommodations were always nice and clean and the decoration is lovely. The price quality ratio is excellent. Congratulations on a great service.

title: “Awesome location, clean room, helpful service”
text: I was suprised at some of the reviews posted on this website. I stayed there for a weekend in Chicago on July 2nd and was very pleased. The people at the front desk were very friendly, the room was very clean (although not huge), and the location was incredible (near the Water Tower and right across the street from the Four Seasons). Although it may not qualify as a luxury hotel, it is certainly a very affordable and great place for couples, business travelers, and families to stay during their trips to Chicago.

title: “Very average”
text:
Hotel is situated in a fantastic location with the Gaslamp Quarter strolling distance.
But there are a couple of things about the hotel that were very frustrating, Wifi is an additional $10 per day per device! My wife and I both have a notebook, and an iphone, so $40 per day is a joke. Walk out the main entrance, turn right, walk to the corner, then turn left. Walk 50 yards, and you will find a Starbucks with free wifi!
Next ripoff was the parking. $25 per day is over the top. If you walk out the main entrance, turn left and walk a block, you will find a carpark with reasonable rates.
No fridge in the room, and the carpet was old, damp and smelly. The old TV was discovered by accident, located behind a mirror above the fireplace.
We booked this via a website that mentioned a nice bar, but this was closed while we were there.
Not value for money.

title: “Terrific Staff”
text: My wife and I stayed for one night while I had an out-patient procedure done at Mass General. We wanted a nice quiet place to stay with restaurants and convenience stores nearby and Hotel Commonwealth was perfect. Our junior suite was large, well appointed and offered a beautiful view of Kenmore Square. And we were particularly impressed by the staff. Everyone we dealt with was personable, helpful and extremely professional.

title: “Great Staff”
text: We stayed at the Radisson LAX for a lengthy period during a process of relocating. We were looking for a hotel that allows dogs without charging daily fees and this one does. They do have a one-time fee for any length of stay. Sleep-number bed was decent, although it was a little dated and didn't seem to be working fully (I've slept on a newer one that was better). Room as well was good, again, a little dated but nothing that turned me off from the room. Would have enjoyed a microwave in the room, however, there is one hiding under the staircase that the front-desk staff directed me to! Food here was great quality, we especially enjoyed the chicken pot pie in the lounge area. The parking area was a challenge and expensive. Radisson has an unfinished parking ramp that seems to have been completely abandoned in terms of building it. Would love to see this complete. Otherwise, plan to walk across the block or pay for valet. Overall, though, this was a great place to stay. The staff was very attentive and friendly. Enjoyed chatting with several of them.

title: “Nice hotel in the heart of midtown”
text: Hotel is clean, quiet and in the heart of midtown manhattan if that is the location you are looking for. The service is nice and there are a lot of restaurants/attractions in the area. One negative is that their elevators were very slow and being taken out of service. I decided to use the stairs and found them cluttered with supplies which is extremely dangerous and a fire hazard. I will be making a formal complaint to the GM of the hotel regarding this dangerous condition - see pictures.

title: “Nice hotel but small rooms”
text: Stayed at this hotel for one night with my three children. This is a new hotel. It has a modern and clean decor. I stayed in a room with two double beds. Rooms are very small especially the king bed rooms. They have an area for breakfast which was nice. It is also next to Dunkin Doughnuts and a deli. We got bagels at the deli which were good. The subway is right across the street. We were doing things in SoHo which made this hotel convenient. Not the easiest place to get a taxi however. Employees were all very nice that I encountered.

title: “Awesome Experience and Excellent Customer Care”
text: Hotel Indigo was the meeting hotel for our annual conference at the end of January. The Hotel Indigo staff went out of their way to ensure that each meeting attendee had a pleasent stay and that every need of our attendees was meet above their expectations. The staff is to be commended. Overall the stay, breakfast options, and assistance provided by the Hotel Indigo team was exceptional. Looking to come back to Hotel Indigo in 2012.

title: “Gorgeous Art Deco Hotel, Central to everything”
text: My family and I stayed here for 11 days and absolutely loved it. The New Yorker is central to everything. Macys is only a block away, Madison Square Garden is across the road, the Empire State Building is close by... the subway station is directly next to the hotel. This hotel is perfect for any New York stay. Great diner 'Tick Tock Diner' downstairs that is open 24 hours - and cheap for New York. There are also plenty of great places to eat nearby and a great pizza place across the road - Famiglias. The hotel reflects Art Deco style and boasts a gorgeous big foyer. The hotel also offers complimentary wireless internet, a gym and much more. Rooms and bathrooms are a little small - but overall we didn't spend much time in our rooms. Staff were warm and friendly. This hotel is excellent value for money and a great place to stay. This hotel is a safe comfortable choice for New York and you can't go wrong! Loved it!!!

title: “Weekend Getaway”
text:
We stayed here in February for a weekend getaway. We had booked via Hotwire which was an amazing rate considering the tier of hotel this is. Silver Cloud Hotel has very nice staff as well as the shuttle driver who was very helpful in guiding us around the downtown area. 
Jimmy's wasn't very busy but it should be, the food was great and they had a wide variety of beers on tap. Not far from downtown at all and if you choose not to use the complimentary shuttle, cab rides are no more than $7.00-$8.00 to get to major attractions downtown. 
We will definitely stay again!

title: “Good experience”
text:
I just wanted to let you know that I stayed in this hotel on the evening of 8-6-12 and had a great experience. The staff was especially knowledgeable and friendly. After a bad experience a few weeks before at a Comfort Suites in Nashville, TN, I was happy to be treated with such respect and to be shown appreciation for staying there. The first room I was given, smelled like it had been smoked in but I was quickly given a clean room w/o any hassle.
Thank you!

title: “I will go back......”
text: The rooms were great, the kitchettes were very handy and the people were super. First trip to New York and when we go back would love to stay here again. Could walk to Time Square, Macey's just down the street and it was not a busy part of New York at all.....Great time with great friends.................

title: “GREAT SERVICE but needs some improvements”
text: the hotel service was excellent.....but the room needs some small improvements......more lighting(too dark)......cotton balls and q-tips.........a fan in the bathroom..........the upside to the room was a wall sound machine........very good for sleeping.........and a very easy safe to get in and out of...........we had a very nice stay and would consider going back again...:)

title: “Cool place on the Marina”
text:
Stayed here 3 nights for work. The hotel is very secluded and semi private. Right in the marina on the breakwater but still close enough to walk to Starbucks in the morning. There are several good restaurants close by as well. 
The hotel itself is landscaped like a tropical jungle and maintained very well. Although it is an older property it has been updated many times and is very comfortable without being worn. 
The room was large and the bed was comfy. The bathroom was decent sized as was the closet and coffee area. 
The heating and AC was a bit aged, either on or off with very little control but the weather is so temperate in SD that I only used it to heat the room for about 20 minutes when I got in it then turned it off completely the rest of the night. 
The restaurant was decent and the bar very lively. Many locals (those that live on the boats in the marina) party in the bar as there are bands nearly every night. A quiet drink and conversation is out of the question as the volume is fairly high. 
I could definitely stay here again for a quiet weekend away. Not the most glamorous but very comfortable and clean.

title: “Skip the 5-star hotels - stay at the Tabard Inn for its old world charm and excellent restaurant”
text:
We stayed here for three nights with two teenage children. We booked a suite which comprised a large twin room with lounge area and an interconnecting queen room. Both rooms shared a private bathroom. The decor is charming - it is not difficult to image Ernest Hemmingway or F. Scott Fitzgerald reposing here - with the added advantage of no TV. The hotel is well located just off Dupont Circle with easy access to public transport and taxis. 
Our accommodation was very clean and comfortable and the housekeeping staff provide the best laundry service ($10 for a large load washed and folded - other hotels should take note). 
The restaurant is a hidden gem - excellent complimentary breakfast and we had the most enjoyable dinner of our 3-week trip (weather permitting, enjoy the beautiful courtyard).
We would definitely recommend staying here.

title: “enjoy the city before entering this hotel...”
text: ...because, this hotel is so fun, we didn't even leave it all day or night. it had secure indoor parking for our harleys. shortly after arriving, it was kick back time. there were 3 free cocktails each, with hot dogs, good chicken, meatballs and lots of other free snacks. we were so full and happy, we couldn't leave to go eat dinner in columbus. we ended up in the pool and hot tub for the rest of the night. the pool is an indoor/outdoor type so you can swim under the windows and out under the stars. both the pool and hot tub were perfect temperatures. the free breakfast was enormous and delicious. the internet was free and there's little business center and a small store there with some grocercies, snacks and sundries. all the people that work there are fun and helpful. we will have to go back to see columbus sometime since we spent all our time in the hotel.

title: “Rip-off hotel”
text: Be sure to bring your wallet with enough cash to pay for all the sneeky extras this hotel will charge you. They don't tell you that parking is a fee per night and once you check out slap you with a hefty bill, after you just paid for an overpriced room. There is very limited parking in the area, and difficult to park several blocks away when carrying luggage. Can't say that the rooms are anything to write about. I would not stay at this hotel ever again.

title: “Best Value and Great location”
text: I love staying at this hotel when I am in downtown LA. It is a great location, staff is friendly and the rooms are clean and nicely decorated in a cool manner. It is the perfect style of hotel I like to stay in and it is also a great value. Thank you Robert and Adrian for such great service at check in.

title: “Thanks for raising your prices during the hurricane”
text:
I was staying at the Comfort Inn during hurricane sandy when my flight to Vegas got cancelled. The hotel is sparse, the rooms tiny and very, very noisy if you are overlooking the street. 
When I asked to extend my booking for another day, the price had suddenly gone up $150 dollars... And there was no power of hot water in the hotel because of the hurricane. I had no choice but to stay on but as soon as I could, I moved to the Hilton in Times Square at half the price of the comfort inn. 
Next time I'll go to the Hilton first.

title: “Great Staff!!”
text: My stay at Four Points in L.A. was awesome!! My room was immaculate and the staff was incredibly nice. In passing, I mentioned my recent graduation while checking in. After returning from a day in the city, I was met by a Congratulations card, signed by all the staff and a beautiful dessert tray! I was so blown away, I actually cried - tears of happiness of course! lol! My entire stay was that way. This is a winning hotel - you will definitely enjoy your stay at Four Points Sheraton - L.A.!

title: “Friendly, helpful staff, a convenient location”
text:
After spending several days in Yosemite, we drove into San Francisco and spent our last three days at the Donatello. The staff was helpful, friendly, and always willing to give directions or advice when asked. The man that helped us with our bags recommended a nearby restaurant, Fino, for dinner. We lucked into a last minute opening there. Good advice!
Overall, we thought the hotel was well located, reasonable priced for a city, with clean pleasant and good sized rooms.

title: “Great stay”
text: We paid $72/night for a Friday to Monday stay in May through Priceline. I can easily say I would have paid more for the room. We were in the Beach Building (where the Denny's restaurant is located) next door to the main building on the third floor and I didn't think there was any issue with being in the other building. We had an interior room, so we heard no street noise. The room and bathroom were both spacious and very clean. Beds were plenty comfortable. We had a desk and an arm chair in the room as well. The street cars that run along the wharf pick up right outisde the rear doors and two cable car line pick ups are within a very close walk. There is a Safeway grocery store about 3 blocks down the street (handy for cheap eats/drinks). There was also a much cheaper car parking lot (I want to say less than $20 a day) on North Point Street.

title: “Very nice hotel in a rough part of town”
text:
Our stay was enjoyable and the staff was very helpfull. 
Was surprized by the size of the room. The free breakfast was good however after 3 days I could have used some new choices.
The hotel provided a free shuttle to Union Station every hour which was quite nice however, I think they should schedule them more often, the demand is quite high in the morning. Reserve your seats when you reserve your room if you can. 
The neighborhood is a little rough however, we never felt threatened. There really aren't any places to eat, be sure to eat dinner before you return.
I would stay here again without a dought.

title: “Nice and clean and close to everything!”
text: We chose to stay here because it was so close to Rockerfeller Center and Radio City, not to mention a short walk to a great view for the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade. The room was awesome. Clean and very comfortable. The staff were pleasant when checking in and checking out. Nice lounge for drinks and wonderful buffet breakfast on Thanksgiving morning as they were closed the remainder of that day. Next door a great deli for breakfast, lunch and snacks! The price was right for us to stay in Manhatten for 2 nights!! There are other Hotels close by, but they were at a much higher price point. Double tree was great for us. We liked our warm chocolate cookies we received at check in. My only complaint: no coffee maker in the room, but as I said we got coffee next door at the Deli and brought it up to our room!!!!

title: “Great central place to stay!”
text: My sister and I just spent a week in New york and would highly reccommend the hotel Chandler as a central place to stay. Its 2 blocks from the Empire State building and right off 5th Ave. Very very central! Its not cheap but definatly not as expensive as some of the others. We had a small room with 2 double beds but it was fully functional. The shower in the bathroom is amazing and the complimentary Aveda products were a nice touch. The staff were always courtious and helpful. The bellboys are always there to grab a cab for you, should you need it. The staff hand out maps on arrival too, which is great if you have never been to the city before. The only negative thing I could say is the lack of tea/coffee making facilities in the room. The hotel offers complimentary tea/coffee in the lobby but most people would'nt want to go to the lobby in their PJ's of a morning to grab a cup! We stayed on a room only basis but there are plenty of deli's nearby, most open 24hrs. I would advise people to avoid eating out in the area as it is overpriced and obviously geared towards tourists. Take a taxi to Greenwich Village in the evening for more variety and better value for money. However, there is a nice Thai place across the street from the hotel which has lovely food and inexpensive. All in all, the Hotel Chandler is a great place to stay and check out the city as most tourist spots are within walking distance.Take a city bus tour, a must for all the relevent info on the first few days of your trip. There are agents on every corner in which to buy tickets.

title: “Outstanding hotel two minutes from Union Square”
text:
Swanky old-school Hilton just two minutes from Union Square and same distance from famous Powell trams that run to Fisherman's Wharf. The opulence of the public areas combined with the enormous size of the property makes you want to spend hours just hanging around the hotel! Breakfast is American buffet style - All You Can Eat and thera is also an excellent rooftop restaurant. Great atmosphere in the bar as well, refreshing change from the torrid fug that usually bedevills hotel watering holes.
The rooms are elegantly appointed with the most comfortable beds I've experienced. I've reviewed plenty of hotels on Tripadvisor and you will see that I don't hand out the 5 star rating easily: if there was a facility to give 6 stars, this hotel would get it

title: “Relaxing Spring Break”
text: This was our second year coming to La Cantera. It's always very relaxing sitting by the pool and hot tub overlooking hill country. This hotel is great if you have kids or if you want a couple's get away. They have an adults only area pool which is nice to get away from all the kids but the other large pool area is more kids oriented. Lots of great shopping, entertainment and food nearby. Find Chela's Taco Truck located just a couple miles away near UTSA. We booked on hotwire.com and it was a great value this year $115 per night. If you book on hotwire look for a 4 star hotel, in the six flags area with the following amenities- resort, smoke free rooms, fitness center, golf, tennis, etc.. I think it's the only 4 star resort in the six flags area. Also check out betterbidding.com. It's a must for all travelers looking for good deals on hotwire or priceline. Also know that they have a resort fee but it's worth it cause it includes free parking, internet, towel service, fitness center, etc.

title: “Above expectations”
text:
Just returned from a 3-day business trip to Philadelphia. I booked last minute for a very reasonable price. The hotel is in a restored historical building. The room was fine, good desk and chair, free internet (cable), excellent bed, morning paper, bath room small but OK, no safe in the room. 
I didn't try the breakfast as there are many coffee cafe's around. The location of the hotel is excellent, right down town, in front of city hall and only a five minutes walk from the convention centre. I walked everywhere and never used a cab, except for the ride from the airport ($ 26.50 fixed price).
Just coincidentally I booked here, but it was a nice surprise and I will return for sure.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: From the moment we checked in, we felt very welcomed by the staff. The location is great, especially if you dont mind the 15 min walk to the main shopping area. The public rooms are spacious and so are the rooms. The staff were more than helpful to assist in our desires.

title: “Excellent hotel. Competetive price on...”
text: Excellent hotel. Competetive price on weekends. The room was spacious and pleasant, spotless new bathroom. Location is great near dupont circle and many restaurants and bars.

title: “I really enjoyed staying in this hotel”
text: I have probably stayed in 30+ hotels in NYC over the years and this hotel was a very pleasant experience. I got a suite with 2 queen beds and 2 baths for $264.0, you can't beat that. The hotel is brand new and the location is A+. I would not hesitate to stay there again.

title: “AWFUL EMPLOYEES! RUDE and DISRESPECTFUL! I would NEVER stay again!”
text: The hotel is lovely however, the employees are extremely rude and very unprofessional. I have stayed at many 5 star resorts and hotels and this by far was the WORST experience than I have ever had! When I walked to the front desk, the girl behind the counter RUDELY informed me that I handed her my debit card instead of a credit card. I told her that was how I was paying. Is being wealthy in your bank account an issue these days??? So, she smirked and ran my card. When she gave me the amount I was unclear on the charges so I asked her where the additional $100 came into play? She RUDELY asked "Did you park valet?" I said "Yes" She said "Well it is $22 a day. If you don't want to park Valet you can always go get your car and park it yourself! This is DALLAS!" As if I was from some small town out in the middle of no where and as if I were some PEASANT. I think my jaw dropped! I said NO that is ok, I was just asking for you to clarify. She smirked again and handed me my key and she then asked me... "IS THAT EVERYTHING?" As if I WAS BOTHERING HER!!! I said no and took the keys and she just stood there! She didn't say "Enjoy your stay at the Magnolia....or... If there is anything else please let me know!" NOTHING. NOT EVEN A SMILE! The room was fine. Clean. HOWEVER, I was woken up at 6 in the morning by my smoke alarm BEEPING non stop. So I called down and they sent someone to look at it. The guy said... Well it is broken. I have to go get another one. And he removed it from the ceiling and DID NOT RETURN! I went to my event.... I was sitting at the table and 3 of my friends who were also staying at the hotel said the SAME THING happened to them with the front desk girl! So I wasn't imagining things! I stayed another night since I didn't feel like driving back tired.... ordered room service which was very good! Then did the express check out so I DID NOT have to meet up with Ms. Nasty Pants again! As I was leaving .... low and behold there she stood at the front desk in all her glory.... SMIRKING AT ME! I just walked to valet... I was entirely too tired to go to the front and speak with a manager. I just didn't have it in me. As I was standing at valet. I was approached by the Valet gentleman and I handed him another place's valet ticket... they were both blue so I could clearly see that happening. WELL he didn't think it was an obvious reason for a mistake. He handed it back and said "THIS is NOT the Magnolia's!" I said " Oh I'm sorry about that" and began looking through my purse for their ticket. He TURNED HIS BACK to me and said to another employee standing there. " I have NO IDEA what that WAS ABOUT!" I just HAD to respond! I was NOT HAPPY at this point! I said " Well clearly I must have Valet'd somewhere else!" He looked at me and just WALKED AWAY! I stood there .... jaw dropped on the ground! Another employee saw my reaction and walked over to me and said Ma'am do you have your ticket. I said I am looking for it. He said well what kind of car do you have? I said "I drive an Infiniti" He said "Oh I know which car that is" I looked at the board of keys and said "My key is on # blah blah blah" .... as he handed my key to another valet man... the other employee who so RUDELY turned his BACK earlier walked over and started to YELL at the gentleman helping me! He told him to go stand somewhere else.... and they began bickering right in front of ME!!! As if I were NOT A GUEST at their hotel! I again felt like saying IS THIS REALLY HAPPENING???? I will NEVER EVER EVER stay at this hotel again. I will not recommend it to any of my friends or family memebers. The room was decent. But I would stay at another DECENT hotel before I gave my business to this place!

title: “Might be excellent but didn't experience breakfast or evening reception.”
text:
We have always enjoyed the Staybridge brand, but this property was especially welcoming. The staff was attentive from the moment their front doors slid open. They greeted us and were very gracious, although under stress during a busy time made difficult because the computer system had just gone down. We were upgraded, and that was nice too.
The smells of places really affect me. I can smell smoke before most people, and my family tends to make fun of my "ability". This hotel reminded me of clean laundry. The bed was a little soft, but it felt great to my 1400+ mile back. 
Staff recommendations for dinner, a suggestion for our puppy, and Memphis barbecue enticed us to stay another night. The property is convenient to excellent eateries, Graceland, and Shelby Farms. Shopping is a half mile away, and Benihana is next door. If you are planning a trip to Memphis, stay at the Staybridge.

title: “We Love NYC”
text: My wife won a trip to see the black eyed peas at Madison square Gardens and this was the hotel we stayed at. I found the staff very friendly and the rooms very clean. I made the mistake of putting my own beer in the bar fridge in the room. I didnt realise it is automatically charged to your bill when you remove things from the fridge. The staff were very helpful and i was never charged for my mistake. When in NYC the hotel is really just a place to sleep so the size of the room doesnt really matter. The beds were very comfortable. The location was awesome every thing is walking distance. I wish I was there right now!!! I love New York!!!!! I would definitly stay at this hotel again!

title: “Expert guidance by concierge Peter Gill”
text: Expert guidance by the very professional concierge Peter Gill added tremendous value to our recent stay at this wonderful hotel. He recommended several nearby attractions, minimizing travel time but maximizing the enjoyment of our visit on a steamy humid weekend visit to the capital city. He also quickly supplied a recommendation and made reservations on short notice for dinner and a wonderful neighborhood restaurant. This hotel was recently refurbished and we enjoyed the makeover.

title: “Location great”
text: Our second stay at this city hotel we stayed with friends from the UK who were impressed with the location of this hotel we found the staff very helpful and friendly

title: “Location. Location. Location”
text:
Hard to beat for its location the Fairfax at Embassy Row still has the look and feel of a bygone era, which is not particularly appealing to me. However, I do recognize they do their job right catering to people who want to enjoy this experience.
Stayed one night with wife for an anniversary and we were not disappointed. Location is perfect right next to Dupont Circle and a metro station.

title: “Just Another Business Trip”
text:
Went with b/f to his Wells Fargo thing. Service was excellent, room was much better than my Upper Manhattan stays. The storage was great; 2 walk ins. View very good; Bay Bridge. Lots of room for business gatherings. The breakfast bennies were marvelous! There is a Starbucks right there in the lobby. Starbucks, in the convenience of the lobby's beauty and climate control, is a few feet from "Urban Tavern". So, if Starbucks' loading up doesn't cut it, you got this great restaurant a few feet away where the staff is unexpectedly cordial and attentive. Urban Tavern breakfast buffet is loaded with comparatively SUPER protein and VITAMINS. There is the regular menu of buttermilk and wholewheat pancakes with bananas or blueberries, Vitamin B shots called Carotene, C, and Greek Yogurt with Honey. They even have dim sum; the meat stuffed moist rolls and soft shrimp/cabbage pork rolls. And check out the cheese lover's corner: artisan cheeses with smoked trout, pickled herring and fresh mozarella.
On the entry wall there is a pastry shelf; danishes, chocolate croissants, muffins, Et al., On another wall there are wonderful breakfast lineups; grilled potatoes, eggs benedict, and a plentiful fruit bar.
Comparatively speaking, the gym is adequate for cardio, and just a step below marginal for free weights. Cables are allright.
Happy Hours at Urban Tavern were great too; nice environment, plenty of space.
p.s. This trip included wineries tours, Sausalito, and some walking around Union Square

title: “A virtually faultless stay.”
text:
I stayed here wirth a friend for five nights as a 21st birthday celebration, and, as my title states, I could barely find a single fault with the hotel. Service was of a very high standard, as was the food and bedroom facilities.
A weather forecast card being left on the bed after the turn-down service was a lovely touch :)
The only thing I will say is that DO MENTION IN YOUR RESERVATION IF YOU DON'T LIKE HEIGHTS because, as it happened, we were on the top floor (46) and it's pretty scary...thankfully, we didn't have a problem with it, but anyone with a fear of heights would do well to mention this!! A fantastic view though...
To conclude, we had an absolutely fantastic stay and I wouldn't hesitate for a second to go back there again...it truly was the most amazing experience. An absolute must for travellers who want to enhance their trip to New York!!

title: “great room ...that is it!”
text:
Just returned from SFO trip and the room was perfection, the city is great.historic and colorful.
however, the room was the only good thing about the trip.terrible dining, drinking and in general concern for the guests.

title: “World class resort and world class service”
text: I carefully chose a resort for a weekend to get engaged. The Westin La Cantera resort staff more than exceeded my expectations. Besides having top-notch facilities, the staff delivered world class service. Everyone should experience this resort and if you want to do anything "special" during your stay, look up Rhonda Hughes. She made our engagement event a weekend to remember. I highly recommend this resort!

title: “Great hotel and friendly, helpful staff”
text: We went to Ft. Worth by train and I was a bit worried about getting around town, so I choose this hotel because it offered a free shuttle. Ou experience was great from check in to check out. Comfortable room, friendly employees, great shuttle drivers, and excellent breakfast included with the stay. I would definitely recommend it and would stay again in a heartbeat. The location is a bit off the beaten path, but it was very quiet, and the shuttle will take you downtown, to the museums, and the stockyards etc.

title: “OVERPRICED & DISAPPOINTING”
text: I stayed in the standard King room for four nights. The room was VERY tiny and the bathroom exceptionally small (only one person could fit). There were also no drawers/dresser, only a closet. I have stayed at the Hyatt, Hilton and Doubletree in San Diego. The rooms were much larger and more comfortable for less money. Also, the exercise room is a closet. I found the $35 parking fee quite high, as it really works out to at least $40/day with tips. A boutique hotel should be MUCH nicer.

title: “Nice long weekend at the Barclay”
text:
My husband and I (in our late 20's) stayed at the Barclay two weeks ago in a basic room and loved it. I love older buildings and this one did not disappoint. The hotel was beautiful inside and out. I like the regal decor as opposed to a modern scheme, so this hotel met my expectations. The room and bathroom was very clean. The bathroom was tiny, but of course this is typical. Plenty of hot water and nice water pressure. Nice comfy bed and pillows. We heard no noise from the street or any other rooms (Room 1165).
The location is EXCELLENT! Convenient to everything. Close to subway too. The Concierge is very helpful and always polite. Each staff member we encountered was delightful.
We enjoyed a Yankees game while in NY. The hotel is only about 30 minutes by subway to the stadium. Again, nice location.
The hotel bar is VERY expensive. Skip the late night cocktail, or stop somewhere else before heading in for the night. Ex: Crown and Coke $30.00. 
Overall, I have no complaints and really enjoyed our 3 day stay at the Barclay. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “The cleaning staff was great... everything else was awful.”
text:
This hotel is an example of a company that doesn't even try anymore because they know people will just keep coming. They know that, being near an airport, weary travelers desperate for some shuteye will come stop in no matter what. Even their comments to people who have posted reviews here seem to simply have been copied and pasted by some drone. 
I used Hotwire (on my brother-in-law's recommendation) for the first and last time here. Firstly, it turns out the discount I received was actually far less than advertised, they seem to have just jacked up the price on Hotwire; and secondly, I felt like I was being treated as a second class citizen because I tried to be thrifty. I understand that you can't always expect the same level of glamour when trying to save a few bucks, but to be poorly treated by a major hotel chain? That's appalling to me.
I was traveling with 3 other people (myself, a friend, and a couple), and we were shocked by the size of the room. The beds were too small for the couple to sleep comfortably, let alone for two grown men to share. We asked for a rollaway bed, but they said they couldn't because it was a fire hazard which seemed odd to me. I'm not saying that they were lying about it, but I have never had a problem getting a rollaway bed in similar establishments in California. The front of desk's only recommendation to me was that I consider sleeping on the floor if I wasn't comfortable. I had to leave that conversation I was so upset at those childish remarks. I was polite and rational, and I was met with hostility and sarcasm. My friend, who is admittedly over emotional at times, almost cried at being treated like that.
What really irks me is that the room was clearly set up for two people. Two towels, two cloths, two individual shampoos. The desk staff said that they simply give rooms to Hotwire who then fills the rooms, but they could at least maintain some communication with Hotwire to ensure that they're ready to welcome your guests in a professional manner. But nope, they just passed the buck and kept telling me things that they "couldn't" do instead of finding a way to resolve a situation. 
Thanks alot though to the great members of the cleaning staff who were helpful and friendly. You guys deserve alot better.

title: “Great spot!”
text:
Great location, nice modern and clean... So close to times square it's the perfect spot. Little bistro beside entrance is perfect spot for breakfast or dinner. Will stay here again for sure.
Easy walk to Grand Central...

title: “Good location, small rooms, terrible AC, and great service = "just okay"”
text:
We chose this hotel for it's central location, for the "Old World feel" and for a change (we stay overnight in Boston about twice a year). We immediately experienced the good and bad of the "Old World" with the gorgeous lobby, pleasant service and tiny guest room with incredibly tiny bathroom. We looked on it as good training for our upcoming trip to Rome ;)
We were put on the 8th floor looking towards City Hall Plaza. Through a filthy window, looking down, we could see the roof of King's Chapel and the Old City Hall. Our room was next to the elevators, so we were concerned about noise, but it was never an issue. Our AC unit did not cycle, so the room was either very cold for long periods or uncomfortably warm for long periods. The beds were very comfortable, once we leapt up into them! They were very high off the floor, which was appealing in an Old World sort of way, but annoying to this 5' 1" gal, especially in a such a small room. The shower pressure and temperature were good. The room safe was big enough for laptop and cameras. The TV was new flat screen and the iron worked well.
The elevators, all of them, stopped working the evening we were there. We were lucky enough to be near a bellman who was bringing bags to someone's room and invited us to join them in the service elevator, which was working fine. That was very nice as we were in a rush to change before our show. The elevators were working by the time we got back.
We used valet service with no complaints other than the long wait for pickup (25 mins on Sunday morning ... it's much less in other hotels in the city).
Dinner was a disappointment, great dining room with attentive service but terrible food - all overcooked and bland tasting. Breakfast was better. The coffee was excellent.
All in all, it was "just okay". For all the options in Boston at this price, we'd choose a more modern hotel next time.

title: “Just my opinion, but I don't think I would stay here again.”
text: First, the good, got a great deal on two rooms, the rooms were clean, very nice tv. Now the medium, the first night we were there they came and cleaned the rooms, although, my son's bed was not made and a note was left saying his belongings (a pillow) were on the bed. I guess they only noticed because he had a covered pillow case because we all had our own pillows on the bed. No big deal, as long as I have clean towels I'm happy. Now, on to the worst of it. One outlet didn't work, one was sporadic, which I guess would not be a big deal to some. But, when charging 3 cells phones and a laptop it becomes a major inconvenience. Not all the lights worked. The rooms are tiny, so if your claustrophobic, go elsewhere. The a/c kicks on literally every 7-10 minutes, it is very loud. Unless you are in the bathroom it blows directly on you no matter where you are in the room. We had to stack our pillows just right on the bed so it wouldn't blow on our faces.We had two rooms, and the set ups were the complete opposite, but the situation was the same. When the a/c is not running every noise from the street echos thru the vent, just as loud as if you were actually standing on the street. No clue where the ice machine is, maybe you had to ask at the bar, Oh, and it costs an additional $24 a night to park!!! If you're lucky you can make a deal with the parking lot attendant across the street.

title: “Only if Verizon Center Event”
text:
This was my first stay at a Kimpton Hotel anywhere. 
It was a not a good first impression.
Reserved Monte Carlo upgrade and indicated higher floor in reservation. Got there and they wanted to put me in the dungeon. Said that wasn't acceptable.
Waited for over an hour for them to clean one on a higher floor.
Finally, just went with a standard closet....I mean room.
They are VERY SMALL. Not acceptable for DC.
At around $200 per night, you can get MUCH better accomodation in the city.
Only time I would ever consider going back is if I were there specifically for event at Verizon Center in the evening and didn't want to worry with cab or Metro.
Service was NOT GOOD.
Room was TOO SMALL
Food in Poste Brasserie was BAD
All in all, I would warn you away from this one.

title: “Lovely Hotel!”
text: Traveled to DC for a convention. We were all put up at different hotels....but I by far got the best as the Capital Hilton exceeded my expectations. I had a corner room. recently remodeled...very lovely,clean, comfy bed and pillows...nice views from three windows of the St Regis across the street. Cant comment on food or drink, we were fed like queens at the Washington Hilton, the hub of the convention. Upon check in I was informed that my roomie was to be a person named Kevin....funny since I am a woman! The staff did not seemed too concerned about this...LOL..neither was I !! But he never showed...so had a gigantic room to myself!! I will definitely stay again!

title: “A must see for Detroit”
text: I grew up in Detroit and have fond memories of the downtown area at it's height of prosperity. The JL Hudson Company and the Penobscott building. Thank you Westin for believing in the Book Cadillac to give her a new youth! Our stay was amazing! Great service. immaculate rooms and the vibe of Detroit!

title: “Great location for exploring Boston!”
text:
Stayed at the Omni from June 29 to July 5. Beautiful, historic hotel near Fanueil Hall, Freedom Trail, Boston Common/Public Garden and New England Aquarium. All sites within 5-10 minute walking distance, Beacon Hill maybe 15 minute walk. Red line T station is located at Boston Common about a 5 minute walk. Hotel check-in was quick and bellman promptly brought our bags up to our room. Elevators can be a little slow but consider that the building dates from 1855--take time to view the carving and wood work in the hotel.
We booked an executive size room with two double beds, sofa (w/foldout bed), chairs and coffee table, and small TV. Room was very clean and well kept. Beds *very* comfortable and room a good size for two adults and two teens. Tiny but efficient batthroom. Consider becoming an Omni Select Guest member--we had juice and newspaper brought to our room every morning and turn-down service in the evening. Housekeeping prompt everyday and straightened up beds and left clean towels. Wonderful room to come back to after walking all day around Boston! 
We enjoyed breakfast in the Parkers restaurant which offered a buffet (eggs, sausage, cereal, oatmeal, waffles, pastries, fruit) or you can order off the menu. We also had drinks and appetizers in Parkers bar which serves until late in the evening. Food at both restaurants very good, excellent service. Lots of Dunkin' Doughnuts nearby, Starbucks (right across the street), Ruth Chris' steakhouse, and other dining choices nearby. Try Legal Seafood (at Long Wharf near the New England Aquarium) and Bertucci's (Fanueil Hall) for terrific food and service. Take the time to enjoy a meal in the North End and stop at Mike's Pastries for dessert.
Neighborhood around the Omni is safe and we felt safe walking around Boston late at night. Some homeless people around Boston Common and Downtown so would avoid those areas late at night. Consider venturing out of Boston to MinuteMan Historical Park (Lexington and Concord) and the Adams Historical Site in Quincy. You can use the Red Line T/bus 62 or 76 to get to the National Heritage Museum and use the LibertyRide (operates seasonally) to see the MinuteMan historical sites in Lexington and Concord. You can take the Red Line T to Adams Historical Site (stop at Quincy Center). See the National Park Service website for more information: [--]
Highly recommend the Omni Parker House hotel if you are looking to stay in the heart of Boston near most attractions.

title: “They bill you for everything!!!”
text: I was disappointed that you had to pay daily for internet connection. Most hotels now have free wi-fi--so didn't understand that! Second, parking is $20 a day. The hotel doesn't have it's on parking and will not validate parking tickets. First time I have had that happen also. Rooms were nice and beds were comfy....the bathroom is huge!!! Very convenient to convention center, nighttime dining and mall...walkways connected to all!!!!

title: “Super Friendly”
text: From the doorman, to the reservation desk, lounge & cafe; everyone we met was cordial, helpful, and generous with hotel resources. Owners have obviously hired for pleasant personality and it works. Nice room, attractive and spotless pool, good food & handy location, with airport shuttle and directly opposite a stop on the new light rail system. Great value (off-season, anyway) and highly recommended.

title: “A great stay for a good price”
text: The room was very clean and roomy. The air conditioning worked great during the heat wave of 100+ degrees. Hotel is about 3 miles away from a mall with many eating option such as Olive Garden, Cheesecake Factory, etc.

title: “Surprise!”
text: This place looks like a nursing home converted into a motel. But don't let that fool you. The large rooms have king beds, sofa, fridge, electric broiler, and dishes. There's a wall desk big enough for spreading out blueprints or other documents, and wireless to do email. You could hold a meeting in your room, but they also have a conference room available. The staff hosts a central breakfast bar with toaster waffles, bagels, grits, boiled eggs and more. The lady overseeing the breakfast is very friendly and shared her secret for making really great grits even a Northerner would rave over. There's also a gas station right next door, with quick access to I-295. After reading all the reviews, we took a chance. We are glad we did.

title: “midget-beds!”
text:
The main reason to stay in the Handlery is, of course, the location. Couldn't be more perfect. But there are a lot of other hotels on the same block, so...
The rooms (we had three) were the smallest we 've had during our whole trip, but that's not that bad. Much worse were the beds.
Frankly, I'm at loss for words to describe these tiny little beds in these tiny little rooms. It is impssible for two adults to sleep in it. Don't even try, I did, it does not work. 
Service of the staff was ok, but nothing special. Have had cleaner rooms too. (hairs in the bathroom).
I was invited, so I don't know the price, but I suspect that it's barely worth the money, if at all....
Next time in San Fransisco, I'm certainly going to try to find another hotel.

title: “Paradise for the kids .... Hades for the adults!!!!!!!”
text: First, I will start off by saying that our kids, ages 8,6,4 and 8 mos, had an absolute BLAST. Highlights of the trip were: waverunners, bonfires, great pool service, and a fun dinner at the local Fillipis's Pizza in PB. We rented a bayside bungalow for 3 nights. The rooms were old. Customer service was terrible .... basically, expect none. There was not enough shade at the pool or the Barefoot Bar. It's basically Paradise for the kids and Hades for the adults!!!! Piece of advice, set your expectations low and you will not be disappointed. We paid $279 for the bayside bungalows and I think it's a fair price. However, NEVER pay $579 for the bungalows .... it's just not worth it!!!!!!

title: “Housekeeping needs to do some cleaning.”
text:
Service was terrible. We stood outside for quite some time before someone finally came to help us check in our car-- after going to guest check-in twice. It was 11pm, we had our 8 month old daughter, and she was tired, plus it was cold. 
When I initially made the reservation I requested a rollaway crib, nothing was in the room. I called downstairs and we had to wait another 30 minutes for that to arrive. We ended up just having her share our bed because the crib actually looked pretty dirty (rusty in spots) and old. 
Our room had trash in the trash can, and just overall appeared dingy. We weren't impressed, and they should reconsider their rates until they want to at least make it a bit cleaner. I've stayed at numerous boutique hotels, and never have they been this bad. 
The following night we got to enjoy the music from the street below because the windows are that thin.
The rooms were drafty and the heating worked poorly. Won't ever return.

title: “Good for Airport Overnight”
text: We stayed at the SeaTac Hilton in November during a travel layover and had a prepaid reservation. We have stayed here before, always in a prepaid room. We like the location and the hotel in general, although we are often in one of the smaller rooms on the first floor, probably because of our prepaid status. It is comfortable, clean and quiet. We usually have a meal in the bar. They have a good selection, and the prices are far lower than in the restaurant. The airport shuttle runs regularly.

title: “The staff let this hotel down”
text:
I stayed here for my 30th birthday and thanks to the staff it was the most stressful experience I have ever had in an hotel.
To cut a VERY LONG story short - the hotel took 3 payments off our credit card for our stay here! This left us with virtually NO money for the remainder of our 2 weeks in the States. We eventually got it back a couple of days later, but you can imagine how stressful and time consuming it was sorting this with several managers at the hotel.
And did we get an apology - NO!
The hotel is a lovely place to stay though, vert clean and spacious. Just a shame the staff are useless..............

title: “Better Service At Motel 6”
text:
I searched and searched for a nice hotel to stay in overnight in The Big Apple. I went to every search engine and finally found what I thought was a good deal and 3 1/2 stars to boot!!! The pictures alone sold the place. The rooms looked new and spacious with views of the city.
When I booked the room, I asked for non-smokingand a king-size bed, with a view of the city.
When we arrived we were told we couldn't check in until 4pm. We checked our luggage and went out for an hour. When we returned reservations said we had a Smoking, two double bed room. I had to argue to get a non smoking, king size bed.
When we got to our room down the very smelly hallway, I was appalled at the size of the room. We had a view of heating ducts and the carpet was nasty!
The HBO sound was broken, only the HBO! It took over 20 minutes to get anyone on the phone to assist us, and even then they didn't do anything. I couldn't make a call with my calling card unless I left my credit card # at the front desk! All calls cost the hotel, so we have to charge you. For a calling card call, billed to my house! What?!
The shower took over an hour to drain and the cafe prices were shocking for what the food was. Over $20 dollars for Eggs Benedict?!
I paid $ 300 for a nite in a hotel less worthy than The Bates Motel. I'd rather sleep in my car

title: “Great value”
text: Good location and breakfast makes this hotel a fantastic value for the business traveller. I hope to stay here again. You don't even have to leave to find a snack or light bite when you have arrived late. Coffee, sandwiches, etc.... It's all good.

title: “Wonderful overnight at the Westin!”
text: Stayed at this property in December 2011 for a family overnight. What a great time we had and we thouroughly enjoyed our room. Actually parked ourselves in the Copley Place parking garage and walked a small ways into the hotel. It was cheaper than paying for valet service. The hotel is very nice...the lobby welcoming and the staff very helpful. The room we had requested was not yet available (waterfront views) junior suite so we were assured that the room they did have ready was equally as nice with views of the city and they did reduce our nightly rate. The junior suite on the 31st floor was wonderful...very large and a corner suite....it had two queen beds, a sofa bed and a desk. The bathroom was adequate and the coat closet on entry was great. Room was very clean except for a stain on the sofa bed cushion. The windows were many and the view wonderful-quiet for the most part although the night we were there, the wind was howling and being on the 31st fl in a corner room, you were bound to hear it whip around the building. Most rooms nowadays have a fridge, not this one. We did request a fridge and they were very quick about bringing it up. Our kids wanted a snack later in the evening and so we were forced to take from the honor bar- two juice, and two pkgs of peanut M&M's was a staggering $19.00+ dollars. The location was great. We were able to jump fairly quickly onto the subway to ride to government center-T station basically right around the corner from the hotel. We loved the fact that the hotel was accessible and attached to the Copley Place shopping mall. No need to walk outside in the freezing cold. We did enjoy our overnight in Boston at this hotel and would come again-but would really love the views of the harbor that we were looking for.

title: “worst hotel, poorest service in new york city”
text:
The WORST hotel I've ever stayed in. A lifetime traveller, and someone who frequently stays in New York hotel, I ended up in this pit after my usual was booked.
1) The staff has an attitude. The front desk manager, a man named Chris who must have graduated from the Al Queda School of Personality Dynamics, is, without a doubt, the most hostile service employee I have ever encountered.
2) In 2007, a New York hotel where the heat, television and internet doesn't work??? I spent nearly two hours on the phone trying to get online, and complaints about heat and television resulted in NOTHING.
3) At nearly $500 a night, I would have done better sleeping in a cab for the night and it would have been a whole lot cheaper.
4) There should a college course entitled, "How Not to Treat Guests - a Case Study of the Beekman Tower Hotel."
In a word, DON'T.

title: “Tabatha Williams was a fantastic representative of the Hotel”
text: Our stay started out somewhat rocky. My reservation could not be found by the clerk, even with the confirmation number. Two days after check in, Tabatha Williams worked with my partner, obtaining a room with a balcony. At the time of check out, we realized that the 1st clerk had registered me under another name - apparrently the reason for not being able to find my reservation. Tabatha once again pleasantly and patiently corrected the information and the rate. When I received my credit card bill I had a charge I wasn't expecting. Tabatha very quickly was able to determine that I had been a charge for a "no show" and issued an immediate credit. Tabatha takes action is very pleasant, helpful, and an asset to the hotel. Our stay ended up being a fantastic one because of Tabatha.

title: “Great place if you don't plan on sleeping”
text:
The W Hollywood is gorgeous. The staff was attentive and helpful throughout our trip. Rooms are gorgeous (super cozy beds) - unfortunately, I didn't get the quality sleep I was hoping for. 
I was on the 4th floor and noise from the parking lot below (I don't believe it's owned by the hotel) was INSANE. It sounded like a parking lot party was going on. Screaming valets, bass, pounding music. As the lot isn't owned by the hotel, that is no reflection on the staff or their attentiveness - just an unfortunate neighborhood. 
To their credit, colleagues on 2 other floors had loud partiers in their hallways - and within a few minutes of calling the front desk to complain, those noise issues were corrected. 
The neighborhood definitely leaves something to be desired. It's pretty much a mix of stripper clothiers, tourist shops, tattoo parlors and a Trader Joes. The hotel itself is amazing, however. Morning and afternoons are lovely, quiet and mellow. In the evening it turns into a hot spot packed with hipsters looking to see and be seen. 
The Bliss Spa on the 4th floor is delightful. 
The restaurant on the roof has a great view, but beware the dresscode by the pool. 
This is definitely not a kid-friendly hotel, which was fine with us. Certainly not the place to bring the family if you're doing the California Disney circuit. Also, you will probably not feel comfortable schlepping around the W in shorts and a t-shirt. It's a hotspot, and the clientele dresses and acts accordingly. 
The cost of internet is $15 a day. For what they charge for a room, that seems a little ridiculous to me. Not to mention the $9 bottle of Fiji water in the bathroom...

title: “Great for accrss to trade shows”
text: Front desl staff are friendly, rooms are ok but getting old. Bar really rocks on Tuesday night kareoke night if that is your thing. No breakfast except a little sandwich place and don"y bother.

title: “Great location, good but some suggestions to make it even better”
text:
I stayed at the Grand Hyatt New York several times. The new Grand Club is very nice, the breakfast selection for the complimentary continental breakfast is good.
The gym on the top floor is nice if you're just wanted a hick work. It would be nicer to add a jacuzzi, steam room or perhaps a pool, but this s Manhattan.
I stayed t several different rooms before, but this time my room was not really designed for a business traveler. I would have loved to have a desk with a phone and convenient plugs for my computer. As with many other hotels, the Internet system does not allow to access our own server to send emails, so I had to call tech support every day to open up my IP. Tis is not a specific Hyatt problem, but a provider issue.
The staff was helpful. I would have loved to have a minibar or at least some bottled water at night, but again this is not Singapore, Dubai or London . It's New York and the substandard US hotels get away with these days compared to the rest of the world.
Overall I enjoyed my stay, can't complaint about this excellent location in the center of the Big Apple

title: “Excellent location (quiet riverwalk), stylish concept, exceptional service.”
text:
I held a meeting at this hotel and received nothing but compliments for my selection. It is in a good riverwalk location (quiet) with spacious and comfortable rooms. I loved having meals on my room's private balcony. I even received nightly turndown service with a chocolate!
The lighting throughout is very dim which seems odd -- like you are having a clandestine meeting and don't wish to be seen -- not at all the image for a business meeting. However, upon learning celebrities use this location for its privacy, it made perfect sense and intrigued the attendees although no one bumped into anyone famous during our stay.
I highly recommend this location for a business meeting and/or a business stay.

title: “Loved the Casablanca!”
text:
My husband and I stayed here for our first stop on honeymoon. We loved the hotel, had a romantic atomosphere and great location for Times Square.
We loved the cheese and wine in the evening and the breakfast was fab. We were even able to pop back for coffee during the day.
Rooms were clean,cosy andt comfortable. Staff were lovely.
We had a great time in NYC and would stay here when we visit NYC again.

title: “A nice splurge”
text: Beautiful hotel, great location ! Pricey but worth it as we have paid more in downtown Boston and gotten a lot less. Great Oyster Bar, all staff very courteous, will be back!

title: “Nice hotel smack dab in Times Square...”
text:
I brought my teenage daughters to NYC for a weekend trip, and chose this hotel based on its location and reviews. 
Upon arrival, we were treated wonderfully. The ground floor elevator room (actual lobby is on 7th floor) was beautiful, with water running down the walls and on the ceiling. The lobby itself is very chic and modern; it makes you just want to linger and lounge about. There is a busy bar, but the overall atmosphere is very zen-like. Although we were early, they stowed our luggage and said they would call my cell when the room was ready. While we were out sightseeing and shopping, my cell promptly rang around 3pm, with the hotel informing me that our room was ready.
We were on the 45th floor in a 'Spectacular' room with a view of the square. Although NYC hotel rooms are small by nature, I would consider this a good size; 2 queen beds that were insanely comfortable, a large modern bathroom (nix on the privacy with the shadow glass walls and door; my daughters got a kick out of it though) and room for 3 people to move about without freaking out. It was clean as a whistle, and was not very noisy at all.
