The hotel promptly sent our bags up when we arrived back, and they were always very kind and courteous to all of us. I cannot comment on the restaurant there, as we always ate elsewhere; looked nice though, so maybe next time. When we checked out, they once again stowed our luggage (late flight), and nicely arranged for it and our cab to be ready and waiting when we got back at the end of the day. 
I would stay at the hotel again without any thought. The location right on Times Square is unbeatable, our room was comfy and extremely clean, and the hotel itself is modern and hip. My teenagers loved it!

title: “Great Service and Rooms”
text:
Overall, this was truly a great place to stay. While there were a few lapses in our recent 5 day stay ( we had 2 rooms), the Affinia has one of the best staffs we have seen in a long time with people who go out of their way to provide quality and friendly service. It is also the only hotel we have stayed at where we took pictures with the doormen -- Victor and Joel knew us by name and made it a pleasure to stay there. At the front desk, there were a few wonderful people. Andre had checked us in and went out of his way throughout our stay to help us with dinner reservations and recommendations. The other great front desk person was Kristen who fixed an unresolved issue quickly and professionally after a different front desk person failed to follow up as promised. Even the maintenance person, Jeff, arrived quickly and fixed a low battery problem in the electronic safe and did it with the same high level of customer service. 
My biggest complaint about the Affinia was the lack of clarity about Internet access and Internet charges when we made our reservation. After reviewing the ambiguous wording from the website regarding charges, the reservation agent said that her interpretation was that the Internet was included in our room charge and that we would not be charged for Internet use. The reservation representative was very nice and said that she would make a note in our file so we would not have an issue at check-in. I do not like surprises about charges. Unfortunately, we were informed at check-in that there was a daily charge for the Internet. The Affinia needs to be clearer and to train its agents so that hidden charges don't happen. While I was unhappy about not receiving what I was promised, I would still give this hotel top marks because of the overall quality of the service and rooms. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Perfect hotel for a quick visit”
text: This is a great stay for someone visiting for a day or two. The hotel is very modern and clean. Our rooms were decent in size and came with a great bathroom. Staff was friendly and the location was nice. It was right near the harbor and by a few T stops so it made for a good visit. One downside was that this hotel is located next to a few bars, so when we came back from visiting the city, there were alot of loud, drunk college kids milling around outside. Could not hear them once inside the hotel though. Great price too! Would stay here again for sure.

title: “Good and Bad of Phoenix Park”
text: The motel is 80 years old but redone well. The original room I was in was soooo small that there was barely enough room to walk around the bed. On the flip side the bed was very comfortable, but overall too small to do anything in the room. I asked to change rooms and for a small fee, I was put in a room soooo nice!! that it was unbelievable. I could move here and live in this room. Upstairs bed, downstairs sofa, TV and desk. I ate in the Dubliner for lunch, good meal. I ate there for breakfast and the restaurant manager was soooo rude that I refused to eat there again. Overall the staff (other than the guy at breakfast) were very nice to deal with. The meeting room had pillars in it and was not an acceptable spot for our meeting.

title: “Hotel very good. location excellent.”
text: Booked this hotel after reading reviews on tripadvisor. Stayed for a week and enjoyed our stay. The room was very clean and quite large by New York standards. The first morning I discovered the shower door was not closing properly and then the shower control broke when i was having shower. Both problems were fixed later that day. The location was excellent though the street is a little run-down. My only small complaint would be the bar/restaurant. We did not use this for breakfast as there are loads of places nearby but the bar itself lacked atmosphere and seemed to be rarely used by guests.

title: “Perfect downtown NYC location”
text: We spent one evening in the city for a business dinner. The WallStreet Inn was ideal in various ways. You can walk very easily to local pubs and a few restaurants. The hotel was clean, quaint and quiet. A complimentary breakfast is included. The room was on the small side but the building is old, so that is to be expected. The bathroom was small but was nicely updated. We would stay there again without a second thought. A very convenient parking garage is located across the street. A small and personal place. The hotel made for an enjoyable visit in 'thee' city!

title: “Best kept Secret”
text:
This is the best hotel I have stayed at in years
It is clean and wonderful
The staff is great and the free breakfast is awesome
Friendly enviroment heated pool.
We need more hotels like this one

title: “A quiet spot in a noisy city”
text:
We have stayed in several hotels in this area and Raffaello is by far the quietest room we have ever stayed in. There were no sounds from the street, our room did face a parking area and the back of the Seneca so we did not face the street. Even better there were no sounds from the rooms on either side and no loud door slammings in the morning. And all the rooms on our floor were occupied. The bed was comfortable as we're the pillows. The best rest we have had in a hotel in Chicago.
The elevators are small so we checked out earlier than planned to avoid the rush.

title: “WOW.Just saying”
text: Hotel (great),Staff cant say enough (Darlene) and the rest of her staff went way out of there way to make us welcome.Being a manager for a major retail store,and a truck driver for 20 yrs iv stayed at a lot of places but this was one of them i will be going back too.Let me add,being clean and sober (3 yrs) and stayingin San Antoino was a blast.Thank you Red roof inn,and priceline.com.

title: “Enjoyable Stay and Great Value”
text:
My partner and I stayed at the Chandler Inn on 7/5-6. Overall the place was great and served our travel needs very well. 
Room - we like the upgrade! The new modern finishes are fun and overall the room was very functional despite being a bit compact. 
Location - the South End neighborhood is fantastic. It's a nice calm getaway from downtown, which is only a few stops away on the T (Back Bay station is a 5-minute walk from the hotel). A breakfast diner and a pretty good coffeehouse are also located right around the corner.
Nightlife - Fritz is a gay sports bar, located underneath the Chandler. We hung out there both nights - friendly crowd and nice bartenders. We liked how we could order a beer and take it up to our room if we wanted. They were also relaxed about ordering out for pizza delivery. Cool place.
Suggestions to get to five stars -- improve the coffee situation in the lobby (offer some good stuff, or install a keurig coffee maker and stock it with a variety of k-cups to permit guests to pick their own kind of brew). Also, it would be nice to hand out a neighborhood map, or list of restaurants within walking distance (we figured it out well enough, but it would be a nice service touch).
Overall it's a nice place and great value - We'll definitely return!

title: “A Fun Stay”
text:
I'm from the area, but wanted to have a "sleepover" to celebrate my birthday with my girlfriends. I chose the W...
Pros - 
Overall, it was a good stay. We had three rooms - two spectacular suites and one fabulous suites. We found them all to be clean, comfortable, and tastefully appointed. I found the valet person, bell-hop person, security, and room service person to be very nice. We were thinking of going out to Hollywood or Santa Monica to party, but ended at the hotel bar which was perfect. It was surprising spacious, had good music, and a dance floor. Also, because I am an SPG Gold Member I was able to check-in early and check-out early which was much appreciated. Rooms service was fast and we ordered something not on the menu ant they were able to make it happen. Also, the hotel knew it was my birthday and sent complimentary snacks and alcoholic beverages as well as birthday card. Finally, all the rooms were on the same floor which was quite convenient. 
Cons -
Not to many cons, just little things that prevented a score of "Excellent." First, we had some champagne we were planning to bring in and enjoy in the room. We were told that's not allowed because of city mandate and because the W is such a high profile hotel. Upon leaving, I was told by another employee that it was simply because the hotel wanted the income from the minibar. I didn't appreciated the inconsistencies. Second, the front desk staff/manager didn't exactly exude a warm demeanor. There is something to be said about being nice and welcoming. Third, the air was not working in the main room and had to be fixed which was done promptly. Also, I think that the bath tubs could have been upgraded at the suite level - they were ordinary. At the W in SD you get a soaking tub at the same room level.

title: “NYC wrapped in a single hotel!”
text: Overall i really enjoyed my stay at the Standard. I have stayed at the Standard in LA and other hotels in NYC and am extremely impreseed with the hotels aesthetics and feel. It simplifies big city wrapped up in its giant structure. I loved the tight room and amazing bathroom features. The hotel is a little pricey but you know the quality that comes with that. Great amenities downstairs with a packed bar scene.

title: “Still my favorite place to stay downtown”
text:
The Moore is quirky, clean, and an amazing value for staying in downtown Seattle. My husband and I rented a suite on the 7th floor with my MIL for Mother's Day, and we had a wonderful time wandering the market, visiting the Sci-Fi Museum and Experience Music Project, as well as taking in a Mariners game at Safeco field, which is about a fifteen to twenty minute walk away.
Comfortable queen and twin beds, great little kitchenette, dining room table, and our own bathroom for less than $150 in downtown Seattle on a Saturday night -- this is unheard of at any other property in the area.
Perfect place to stay if you need a safe place to crash for the night downtown. Noisy? You're in the middle of downtown Seattle -- what do you expect? We heard the usual assortment of vehicles and city sounds, but no problems with our neighbors in the hotel. The elevator is tiny and old, but I consider that to be part of the charm.
If you are high maintenance and need every detail to be spit and shine, stay someplace else. If you like staying in an offbeat hotel and want to be in the center of everything, this is the place to book.

title: “Few excellent things covered up other deficiencies”
text: I managed a hotel before, cleaniness was very good in the room. The sleep number did not work on bed, however the bed was VERY comfortable. Loved the view with the planes. Could not find HBO and there was no way to figure out the channels on the tv. No guide anywhere, no welcome book to explain amenities of hotel or close by things. Speaking of, there is nothing around this hotel to do. When originally booking room over phone, very nice lady was VERY helpful, and I was VERY pleased with price of room. The lounge/restaurant had good food and a good bartender/waiter, but it was not so welcoming because she was too busy working by herself, and the restaurant was not even open. Still I was fine to order at the bar - I just wanted it busier. I felt as if the food just could not be made good, but it actually was and the bartender made my evening enjoyable. In the morning, I went to PAY for my own breakfast which I wont complain as the room was so cheap....however I got up early to go eat and was told "Uh, the chef no called, no showed today, we have no breakfast open". Shuttle driver was nice, but in a hurry. Got impression he had another driver doing next shuttle run and that driver might not have been as dependable. Hotel seemed understaffed, never saw more than 4 employees whole stay.

title: “Very solid hotel for families”
text:
We stayed in the Embassy Suites at the Philadelphia airport for 5 nights. The room was the typical two room Embassy Suite suite, but seemed even larger. There really was a lot of room. There are two new flat screen HDTVs, one in each room, and they get HD channels. Parking was free and the breakfast was great. 
However, it must be noted that the hotel is very loud. You can hear almost everything going on in the atrium from the living room. It is better in the bedroom. Also, we didn't get housekeeping to clean our room once because we had the do not disturb sign up the first time they came through and we specifically asked housekeeping to come back later and they did not on several occasions. Also, make sure you know that this draws the typical Embassy clientele: families. 
Overall, I was pleased. Especially with the $99 rate.

title: “Great Stay”
text: ok so the rooms are small, i wasn't planning to spend any time there. The rest of the hotel and its amenities make up for it. Its exciting vibe and since i was there alone it worked out well that there were a couple bars in the hotel that i can hang out at... Great place.

title: “The amazing Oxford Hotel”
text: We stayed at the Oxford Hotel here in Denver for the night and it was amazing!! We live in Colorado and decided that we needed a night downtown. We arrived and the service was awesome from the time we pulled up to valet our car till the time we left. The food was wonderful!!! We had a couples message at the spa. The spa was fabulous and the message was just what we ordered. The room we stayed in was beautiful! We had such an amazing time that we are think about going back once a month. I would highly recommend this beautiful hotel!!!

title: “Don't think twice”
text:
Everything about our stay in this beautiful hotel was perfect. Our suite was enormous and absolutely wonderful. The hotel staff was warm, friendly, helpful in every department. The
food was delicious and beautifully presented. The location was perfect for us and we enjoyed much of the city by our own foot transportation. The Alexis Hotel is our new "home" when visiting family and friends in Seattle.

title: “Great Location and terrific Breakfast Bar”
text: Family of 4 - Parents and 2 teenage daughters stayed for 4 nights. First visit to NYC. Had a grand time. Hampton was very convenient to everything. 1 block away from the Blueline subway. Less than ten blocks from 42nd St and Broadway. Near dining and drugstore for those after hours items. Six blocks south of Columbus Circle where there is an indoor mall with Whole Foods Market which has a GREAT food bar and only $7.99 by the pound. Lots of food for little dollars. The Hampton itself was very clean and organized. The complementary Breakfast Bar was outstanding serving till 10am. Crowded sure, but that was because it was delicious. Staff very friendly and everyone smiled all the time. We were on 2nd floor and it was surprisingly quite for being closer to the street. No or little traffic noise at all. Would stay there again and recommend it.

title: “NO PROBLEMS”
text:
hi,
Just back from a stay in The Wellington Hotel and found it fine. NYC is very expensive to stay in and this Hotel is a three star basic but an ideal location, you really cant get more central. The room is small but spotless and a little bit dated but in saying that your never there only to sleep. The staff was lovely had no complaints at all, I left a bag in the cab going to the airport and the staff in the hotel posted it to me. If you are looking for value for money good location clean but basic accomodation you cant go wrong I would have no hestitation in staying there again.

title: “Friendly service, good location, good price”
text:
I stayed in the Ramada this year for my trip to the Boston Marathon. From the moment I was picked up by the hotel shuttle driver I knew I had chosen the best place for my needs. The driver had no sooner pulled away from the airport when he began handing out maps of the transit system to all the runners on board. He clearly explained which stops we neede to take in order to get to the Marathon expo and the race-day busses and informed us that there would be extra shuttles running to and from the transit station all weekend. Although breakfast normally begins at 6, they began service at 5am on race day to ensure the guests would have a chance eat before leaving for the race. There is also free coffee available 24 hours a day - a big perk for some. 
The hotel is an older building, but my room was clean, well lit, with a comfortable bed and cable TV. There was a problem with the hot water the first day I was there, but maintenance quickly dealt with this. (They actually arrived within 5 minutes of me reporting the problem) I had leftovers from my supper and, although there was no fridge in my room, the staff kept it overnight in the fridge behind the counter for me. The hotel was completly booked but I was in bed by 9pm each night and did not find things at all noisy. If you do not have a vehicle, the hotel is well situated as, there is a drug store, liquor store, and a wonderful deli / market directly across the street.The frequent shuttles to the subway station and the short duration of the subway ride into town make one feel like they are staying close to downtown without the burdens of a downtown price! I would recommend this hotel to someone who is looking for inexpensive, friendly accomodations. 
There is no fitness centre, but guests have the use of the one in the Comfort Inn a block away should they want to work out.

title: “Best stay ever”
text: This is the perfect place to stay in the Gold Coast area of Chicago. The service was excellent and the hotel is absolutely beautiful. The Waldorf Astoria has the most wonderful staff and amenities! The staff went beyond what is expected and made our trip to Chicago perfect.

title: “Oasis of tranquility.”
text:
Lovely, clean hotel with very kind & pleasant staff that went out of their way to be nice & accommodating. 
Rooms are well laid out & spacious and the beds are super comfy - we hated to leave them. 
Bathroom was nice & clean. 
Awesome breakfast buffet! Staff even gave us to-go cups of coffee & a bottle of water for the road. How nice! 
Highly recommend!

title: “small, friendly, convenient location”
text:
very friendly front door/ valet people. Nice to come back to hotel for that reason. 
Room was not that big but had two windows as corner room. 
very clean but could use more drawers at every furniture item. Would be nice if staying there more than one night. 
great shower/tub combo bathroom and robes.
Location is great, near restaurants, shops and sightseeing places.
And complimentary SVU service on first come basis to nearby locations, both drop off and pick up if available--nice extra perk. 
Will definitely stay there again.

title: “Fantastic hotel with spectacular service”
text: Gorgeous hotel - we stayed on the 38th floor and had an unbelievable view. Everyone who works there is incredibly friendly, nice and helpful. Loved it and can't wait to return.

title: “True Mid-West Friendliness”
text:
You know you're going to get high standards of service and good facilities when you make a reservation at a Sheraton, and this was definitely the case here in Chicago. I'd heard about the friendliness of the mid-West people and everyone I came in contact with in this hotel was cheerful, helpful and sincerely interested in making my stay in their hotel and their city as enjoyable as possible.
Location is great - right on the river and within walking distance of lots of major attractions including the excellent shopping on N Michigan Ave (the Magnificent Mile). Great restaurant, atmospheric bar and even though the hotel was full at the time I stayed with lots of guests in evidence, there were always quiet public areas to sit and watch the world go by or plan the next sightseeing venture.
The bedrooms were spacious and well-equipped, with marvellous views of the city. The executive lounge area was a welcome extra - worth the slightly higher room rate, in my opinion.
Full marks to all the staff here - they were the icing on the fabulous Sheraton cake!

title: “Trouble place”
text: I got the hotel thru hotwire usually when i reserve with them the rating was pretty good. This time they missed it. They give candlewood hotel 2.5 but it is a 1 star hotel. Dirty room, leaky air condition and restroom fan is not function. I asked to chage to another room they said i have to wait 4 hours. I paid the full amount and i do not have any choice to finish the remainder of my two days stay here. I alredy have staffy nose and headache. DO NOT STAY AT THIS HOTEL PERIOD.

title: “Lovely Hotel”
text:
I stayed in this Hotel overnight during Memorial Day and it was a lovely hotel! 
Very nice rooms and the staff was very helpful and it was convenient to downtown DC.
I highly recommend it.

title: “good location but dont expect to sleep!”
text: good location..true..good price off season, true..clean..true..however the walls are so think you can hear every bump, walk, or drawer close in all rooms near you..and door slam all night while people come in and out..had to purchase ear plugs to make it through and our family hardly slept..what a shame! and this was off-season! i cant imagine what it is like in summer or fall!!! i would have to say paying more to sleep would be my choice hereafter!

title: “It is what it is.”
text:
The staff at Hotel Bijou are the most helpful and friendliest people you will ever meet. 
If you’re relying on public transportation, then the hotel location is hard to beat. SF Bart system (Their subway system) is under 200 yards (or meters) away, making a very easy trip to and from the airport. Same goes with the cable car, the light rapid system (The F Train will take you to Fisherman Warth), and their bus service. The cable car will take you to Fisherman warth, but the cost is $5 per trip, and the line up is very long. The light rapid system is only $2, and you can get a transfer that is suppose to be only 90 minutes, but you should get a lot more (like 2 to 3 hours). 
Hotel Bijou offer free WiFi, the internet speed is pretty good. Download 128 KB/s, Upload 50KB/s. 
The continental breakfast is only good if it is free (included with your hotel stay) 3 type of breads, White, Whole wheat (Wonder bread), Beagle, and Eggo Waffles. Basic beverage, OJ, coffee, milk, hot water for tea. Only saw one type of cereal, Cheerio. They also have a basket containing hard boiled eggs. Considering that they serve hard boiled eggs everyday, only one would think that they would have perfected the timing, but yet the yoke is always green and rubbery. If breakfast is not included with your hotel stay, save your money and go somewhere else and eat. 
Noise, if you’re a light sleeper that can’t sleep with earplugs; then stay away from this hotel. In case you forget to bring your own earplugs, Hotel Bijou does offer free ear plugs.
Water pressure, this is an older hotel, so the plumbing pipes can only handle so much pressure. The water pressure is very low, the shower head is like the CLR commercial where the shower head is dribbling. Take about 15 minutes to fill the bath tube with water. 
Washroom is already small enough, but to put in a pedestal sink is crazy. No counter space. The shelf they put above the sink is a joke; enough to place 2 cups and your toothpaste; not much more after that.
Elevator, again being a older hotel, you can only install what you can. This elevator is small, can fit 6 adults, and the speed of the elevator is very slow. No need for a fitness room at this hotel, just run up and down the stairs, it’s a lot faster. One day, a couple was in front of me waiting for the elevator, I noticed that it was going up, and it’s on the second floor, I ran up the stairs to my room on the 5th floor, and when I left the room, the elevator door opened. I rode the elevator down to the lobby only to see the same couple waiting for the elevator, The look on their face was priceless when they saw me getting off the elevator.
Homeless people and prostitute outside the hotel, this is very subjective. If you live in a small town or city, and not used to handling this kind of environment; it can be intimidating. With that being said, I saw girls in their 20’s walking down the street by themselves (8PM), so while it might be intimidating, it’s not dangerous.
Travelocity rated this hotel as a 2.5 star; I beg to differ. I would be hard press to rate this as a 2 star hotel; I would give this hotel a solid 2 star only if they would replaced the pedestal sink with a countertop sink in their washroom.
Overall, this hotel is good for value minded travellers. The hotel location is hard to beat, and if you can handle the noise, and the pan handlers; then this might be the hotel for you.

title: “Cute but cramped”
text: Newly redone boutique hotel, The Hotel Lincoln has got a great location in the heart of the Lincoln park neighborhood of Chicago. However, while the rooms are attractively furnished they were very tiny (like "New York City tiny"!) and the walls between the rooms were paper thin. We were able to hear the cell phone ringing of the room next door. The staff was very friendly and eager to please. And there is a beautiful rooftop bar/lounge that we enjoyed even though it was raining and we could only look outside at the great view. If location is important I'd stay here again, but have found nicer hotels for the price closer to the Loop/Michigan Ave.

title: “Relaxing place! Next time we're bringing the kids.”
text:
This HI was a nice little surprise! Booked online for a spontaneous but cheap 4 day weekend with my husband. 
First night we had one of the older rooms but we didn't check in until 11PM so no surprise there. The next day we asked for a different room and got a poolside room. Wonderful space right on the putting green. 
The restaurant was good and the vouchers we received were an extra bonus. Restaurant staff is very friendly, as is the evening desk clerk. 
Pool is nice and wasn't that cold (even in March). Never went to the bar area but it looked clean and was rather busy. 
Had a wonderful stay and will be bringing the boys next time!

title: “Great location but poor sleep quality”
text:
The hotel lobby is nice and the atmosphere was very chilled as we expected and had been hoping. 
I was trying to find America’s equivalent of ‘The Dakota Hotel’ chain I’ve stayed in, in the UK. 
The décor is very modern and contemporary however the rooms are not great.
The carpet was pretty grubby in our room and the curtains seemed pretty dirty too.
The bed was good though, nice and comfortable and the bedding very fresh and clean.
You’re right in the heart of the city centre, so you hear everything at night, from the sirens of Fire Engines to the shouts from the down-and-outs as they squabble over the contents of the trash, down below on the street.
One of our windows could not be fully closed because there was some kind of air-conditioning unit, or extractor system, which basically prevented it from closing and so we were often unable to sleep at night because of the city noise.
Homeless people are very well treated in San Francisco and because of this, there are many of them. They seem to be fairly harmless on the main but you have to keep your wits about you, just like you do in any major city. 
The hotel staff point out, where not to go at night and where is safe. The ‘No Go Area’ is not too far away from the hotel but likewise, you’re just off Union Square, which is perfectly safe.
We loved San Francisco as a city and with it only being a three night stay, at the start of a two week trip from San Francisco down to LA and across to Las Vegas, we knew that we would make up for our lack of good sleep in San Francisco, later in the holiday. 
I’d definitely go back to San Francisco and I’d definitely chose to stay in the heart of the city as opposed to Fisherman’s Wharf but I’d chose a different hotel and hope for double glazing and windows which block out the city noises as much as possible. 
Our next stop was Carmel which was total peace and relaxation by comparison but in terms of fun and enjoyment, San Francisco as a place, is hard to beat.

title: “Overall a positive experience”
text: A good location for tourists. The room was spacious, clean, comfortable and had everything we needed. A couple of minor maintenance issues that when reported were fixed immediately. The sour notes were slow check in and slow service in the elegant Dome Bar. These were understaffed. The staff working flat out while managers stood around idly and offering no assistance.

title: “Decent hotel for the price”
text:
Room was ok. Hotel was quiet. Would stay here again.
Continental breakfast was good with the exception of the waffles. The batter was just pancake batter and wasnt sweet at all.

title: “My first choice in NYC”
text:
Very clean hotel in a great position, the rooms were a good size, I always book direct with the hotel, that way you always seem to get the upgrade, we had a corner room wich was as large as some suites.
The hotel has a great position, within walking distance of the hustle and bustle of Times square and Central park.
The bed was so comfortable,great to come back too after a day in the big apple, the bathroom was a bit small, but bathroom products were fantastic.
I would love to go back and stay here.

title: “Not Good. Not Bad. Just Average”
text:
Gosh, I hate that I am writing this review. I wanted to have a very strong like for this experience. 
The Good:
The location. It is within walking distance to all of our favorite sites - Michigan Avenue, Millenium Park, and State Street. CVS across the street is always helpful.
The staff. Very friendly. Helpful staff. The bellhops, the front desk clerks, and the concierge. Everyone was really nice.
The lobby was phenemonal. Very modern and clean. 
The room had chargers for different devices - I forgot my iPhone charger and definitely took advantage of this.
The room was overall very clean.
The Bad:
It took more than five minutes for the water to heat up.
The Ugly:
That shower stall. My goodness. There was soooo much mold. There was no way that we were getting in that shower stall. We brainstormed ideas to prevent our feet from touching the stall - plastic bags wrapped around our feet, running across the street to CVS for bleach and shower shoes.
We decided to ask for another room...at 11:35 pm. I was surprised at the response that I received from the front desk. I don't believe that a late-night maintenance call is the appropriate solution and insisted on a room change. My request was fulfilled, but I was a little disappointed that I had to ask three times.
This room was better, but there were still issues with the shower stall, but we remedied that with shower shoes. :) Bring your own!

title: “Just what I would expect from Renaissance in and out”
text: After spending one night at the drab Crown Plaza downtown with horrible service and tired rooms we checked out early and moved out to the Reniassance across from SouthPark Mall. It didn't dissappoint. The rooms were clean and quiet despite a full house of football fans. Any place we wanted to get to was within 20 minutes and SouthPark Mall was conveniently right across the street.

title: “Good Location”
text: After searching for hotels, reading reviews, etc. I decided to book a 2 night stay at the Pacific Shores Inn. I booked directly through the hotel website as some of the reviews I read had recommended this and I was able to get a better rate this way. Reviews I had read were mixed which made me a little skeptical, but my friend and I were wanting a place near the beach and the price was right. I must say, we were pleasantly surprised. It looks pretty much like any other smaller scale motel when you arrive, but the lobby has been recently updated and the staff was friendly. We had a first floor room which had recently been remodeled and quite nicely so. The room had two beds, a table and chairs, typical hotel furniture, a walk-in closet with microwave, refrigerator, iron/board, etc. and the bathroom featured ceramic tile, granite, and a glass shower (no tub). The room was clean and pleasant. We also had a table and chairs outside our room on the sidewalk. Location was great, 1/2 block to the beach. Some of the second floor rooms had an ocean view, but we found the ease of parking right outside our door nice. We were right across from the pool also which was nice. I believe they are still in the process of remodeling so you may want to request a room that has already been done. Overall, we had a fun time in Pacific Beach and were pleased with this lodging choice.

title: “Hotel Rex is a Gem”
text:
The Hotel Rex is a fantastic place to stay when visiting San Francisco. With a convenient Union Square location, you are really within walking distance of all the great points of the city. Besides being a few block from the BART station and Union Square shopping, it's really just an easy walk to the theater district, Chinatown, Jackson Square, Financial District, and a beautiful walk around Nobb Hill. To get to Fisherman's Wharf, it's just a $7 cab ride.
Now back to Hotel Rex itself...what a gem. The rooms are quiet (except on Saturday night...I think the college kids at the nearby Art Academy were partying at some club) and decorated with a comfy, funky flair. But the best part about staying here is the friendly, efficient, and extremely helpful staff at the front desk. And what a neat surprise to eat a lovely breakfast in the connecting restaurant, Cafe Andrea. With the jazz/french music and the library theme...it's a joyful way to start your day. Also most helpful is the computer room next door where you can print your boarding pass lickety split.

title: “long term? do not stay here!”
text: This LaQuinta Inn and Suites leaves a lot to be desired. The rooms have an odor, not overpowering, but a musty, dusty scent, and -after being vacuumed it smelled like cat litter for a while. (gross) Also, I question whether they put clean sheets on the bed after a week, or just make the bed. I have also had the maid leave a dirty, used washcloth on the bathroom counter. I requested my weekly room cleaning on Tuesday and they came in on a Monday, my only day off (when I had planned to sleep upon my return to my room). I have privacy issues and I was totally unprepared for maid service, so I found this quite distressing. These units have kitchenettes, but the supply of utensils is strange: 1 room had 4 teaspoons, 1 knife and 1 fork, the next room had 4 knives, 1 spoon and no fork. Some rooms have other cooking utensils and some have none at all. I brought my own pots to cook with and I would not want to see what they may offer in that area. The grouted tile floors in the rooms are disgusting, with the grout really showing the filth in the center of the room and very clean, almost white grout along the corners and under the bathroom counter. The front desk staff --most of them leave a lot to be desired, and only pretend that they care about my concerns. The hotel next door allows a truck driver to park a refrigerator truck where it runs loudly and disturbs guests in the LaQuinta, but no one seems to care about that. This was an awful experience over all and I would never consider staying here again.

title: “Fine for an overnight stay”
text:
The general standard of this hotel is very good and has all you need for a short stay. The room was clean and comfortable but don't expect anything really modern and contemporary. Service and food in the bar was good. Apart from having to pay for WiFi, there's not much to complain about, and despite being very close to the airport, we couldn't hear the planes.
If you can get a good price, you can't really go wrong if you stay here.

title: “Perfection!”
text:
This is the first review I have ever written but I believe the Sanctuary Hotel merits a review. I have to say I absolutely love the Sanctuary Hotel! My husband and I visited from October 29th until November 3rd. It was my first (long awaited) trip to NYC. I agonized over choice of hotel as my husband had a horrible experience with the city when he was younger and took much convincing to make the trip back. I had actually booked another hotel and then switched at the last minute to the Sanctuary. What a good decision!
 We arrived shortly before the snow storm hit. While it must have been an inconvenience for most people, it was magical for a southern girl like me! We arrived at the hotel in a private car (graciously arranged by Sanctuary staff) around 11am. Since the hotel is a short walk from Rockefeller Center, we made the trip down to the famous ice skating rink to check it out. Suddenly the snow began to fall….and wouldn’t stop! It was fantastic just being able to sit and watch the scene.
 Back to the hotel….We stayed in room 306, which is a queen superior. I must say it is quite a small room but I expected as much from NYC. I imagine the more expensive rooms are somewhat larger. However, despite the size it was extremely beautiful, luxurious, and carefully planned to maximize space. My only issue was that the opening into the closet was so narrow; my husband’s duffle bag wouldn’t fit. It spent the entirety of the vacation on the floor between the wall and bed. The shower however, was a generous size and as my husband and I are both quite tall, it was a joy to use. 
 The mini-bar was fully stocked with larger bottles of liquor, wine, beer, tonic, etc… There was also an array of snack foods and other useful items available at better than average mini-bar prices. The toiletries seemed to be of good quality and were replenished as needed. The bed was very comfortable and the room seemed extremely clean. I realize the hotel is only a few months old but I sincerely hope they can keep up with the superior level of cleanliness we experienced.
 We did not test the breakfast buffet but we did peak in to see what they had. It looked like basic continental type offerings but certainly adequate and well worth the price (free!). I do have to mention the diner across the street from the hotel. It is called Evergreen Diner and we thought it was fantastic. We ate there every morning. They had anything you could possibly want for breakfast and were very reasonably priced. I highly recommend the waffles and pancakes. 
 The Sanctuary Hotel is in a very good location that is close to many of the sites a person might want to see. It is situated between Rockefeller Center and Times Square, but is on a quiet street in the diamond district. There are many restaurants close by and for those so addicted….a Starbucks at the corner. Fifth Avenue is an easy walk two blocks away. There are two subway lines within a block of the hotel. Although I am a subway newbie, I was able to easily figure out how to get around the city using this efficient mode of transportation.
 We had nothing but good experiences with the hotel staff. They were friendly and plentiful. A member of the house-keeping staff stopped by each evening “just to make sure everything was OK”. My only issue I had with the management had to do with the billing for the room. I had booked the room online using my debit card. It was a non-refundable rate and the website indicated that once I booked, my card would be charged. When we checked in, I was asked for a credit card for “incidentals”, which I realize is standard procedure. I gave them a credit card (different from the card I thought had been charged). A hold was put on this card for the entire amount of the room, in effect, tying up my credit card to the point where I couldn’t use it. I don’t understand why this was done since the room was supposed to have been paid in full using my debit card. This caused some stress as for safety reasons, intentionally left all but one credit card and one debit card at home. I did get a quick response from the hotel Director of Front Office, Ms. Vashenko, who said she would expedite the request to release the hold on my card.
 Despite the one problem, I would absolutely return to this hotel and would highly recommend it to others. Thank you so much for making this dream trip to NYC so very special for me!

title: “ok with flaws”
text:
This is on the "hotel circle" which is a bunch of hotels set back from a freeway in mission valley. That sounds not so good but this Hotel has done a good job of isolating what is an extended complex from the freeway. Its a pretty quiet place with plants, palm trees and pools. 
Staff - they were very friendly, helpful and professional.
Room - I was in the first floor of the tower block. The room was kind of elegant and very roomy and had a balcony facing the pool. It had a kitchenette but very lacked essentials like knives and forks. An issue was that the room had a connecting door and you could easily hear people next door though thankfully they werent that noisy. I think my room was part of a two room suite and so my "bed" was a sofa bed which was ok but I could have done with a real one thanks.
Location - somewhat out of town but the good news is its right next to a trolley station which is very fast and takes you most places in town and is $5 for a day ticket. There is alot of parking but I came without a car. 
The main hassle during the stay was internet which was lousy - failed for 24 hours and was not free approximately $10 for 24 hours. There was free internet if you visited some cafe place which was pretty good for service and food.

title: “Good, but not a top ten in America...”
text:
We are both in our 30's and have stayed in very nice resorts both internationally and domestic (four seasons, etc)
My honest opinion being a native to Chicago is the hotel is of course beautiful but overall just OK.
This hotel is a "top ten" in every list, but no WOW factor at all.
The room is very nice and good bathroom (not much better than a deluxe hyatt)
The tea service was 'OK" You expect perfect service, food, attention and overall it was nothing better than a decent lunch.
The peninsula bar is a great place to enjoy a scotch, cigar, champagne !
We once had our privacy please on and were in the shower when housekeeping came in. I called down and asked why they did not look at the sign. They really had no response. Half the time you call concierge they forward you on somewhere else.
At four seasons you can ask any staff member for something and he will personally call the right people and call you back.
Nothing wrong with this place, but 600-800 a night let's get something clear - it might not be worth it.
The pool (3rd time there in 3 years) is not beatiful and again no wow factor. Small hot tub and the spa renovation makes no sense.

title: “Brilliant”
text:
This was our 1st leg stop of our brilliant honeymoon and the Sofitel Hotel gave us a brilliant start. 
Upon arrival the bell boys were on hand straight away to help us with our luggage and was extremely friendly. The person who checked us in was also very friendly and helpfull and provided us an upgrade on our room upon hearing we were on our honeymoon and also helped us with information on how to get to Universal Studios, as we only had 2 days in LA and had a city, movies and beach tour the next day.
The room that we had was located at the top of the hotel where all the special suites are located. It was very spacious had a king size bed that was out of this world comfort, (the best bed I have ever slept in), there was a seperate sofa to chill out on with an ipod dock system on hand. All the usual amenities kettle, coffee, glasses etc. Flat screen HD TV.
The bathroom was fantastic especially the shower as it was enormous and even had a seating area inside. There is a window from the shower looking into the room that can go from see-through to frosted if you wanted your privacy. Also there were dimmers on the lights so you could adhust according to the mood.
The Simon LA restaurant breakfast was amazing, the food tasted very nice and fresh and the staff made us feel at home.
I would definitely reccommend this hotel to anyone, the service we received was great and there are pick up services available if you are planning tours around LA from this hotel.

title: “Met expectations”
text:
Four of us from Alberta Canada arrived late on January 10. Our reserved room was ready and the night manager gave us his parking space because the underground lot was full - a nice touch. We booked here because it is close to Universal Studios Hollywood and easy to access from LAX.
The room was fine, everything worked and no troubles. Breakfast standard HIE fare, not much room for seating. As reported by other travellers, an awful smell in the elevator. Take the stairs - some exercise and the smell was much less. Thankfully the room didn't have the smell!
15 minute walk to Universal Studios where we spent the day. That evening the manager was helpful in suggesting a place to eat down Cahuenga Blvd. We caught BF the next day and then left. Would recommend for those going to Universal Studios.

title: “Great spot”
text:
We stayed at the Inn last month and were pleasantly surprised. It is clean and comfy, with lots of nice extra touches. Real plants in the rooms, robes, free bottled water and nice toiletries. Very clean bathrooms. The rooms are spacious, bright and cheerful. 
Continental breakfast was excellent! One of the best I've seen. The Inn is only a short two block walk to the Pier at Venice Beach and the Venice Canals are only a block away. There are restaurants nearby. The staff were all very helpful and friendly. 
The Inn is on a busy street and there is construction nearby so it might be a good idea to bring earplugs if you are a light sleeper. All things considered this is a great hotel for the money!

title: “An amazing quality hotel in the inner harbor of Baltimore.”
text: When we got to the hotel and walked into the hotel for the first time I couldn't believe the quality of this hotel. It was a little more expensive, but it was worth it all for once. The room was huge and I was amazed with the beds. The city is loud so I advise you to close all your windows. I didn't and we kept hearing cars going up the street all night. If you like the Yankees, but the tickets are too expensive, go to a Baltimore Orioles VS New York Yankees in Baltimore and make a vacation out of it. We got All You Can Eat Tickets for $40 per ticket.

title: “A terrific bargain!”
text:
Look...I've read so many bad reviews on The Latham here, but I just don't get it. Upon our Sunday afternoon arrival, the valet and doorman were both very attentive and friendly. Check in was very smooth and courteous. The desk clerk was a well-groomed young man who greeted us with a smile and identified us respectfully as "Mr." and "Ms." He was unable to locate our breakfast vouchers at that time, but said he would have them sent to our room ASAP. No sooner had we checked into our very pretty room, when the doorman arrived with our missing vouchers. 
The room was cozy and VERY comfortable, although I DO wish the doors were a little thicker and more soundproofed from chatter in the hallway. However, there was very little street noise, and the king bed was VERY comfortable! We both slept like logs, and woke up refreshed. Breakfast service was attentive and friendly, and the food quality was very good. Our car was retrieved promptly (within ten minutes of request), and was in the same shape as we left it.
I've stayed in motels and hotels of ALL prices and service ratings; from Day's Inns to suites at The Four Seasons. Sure, The Latham is NOT The Four Seasons, but for the price it's a fantastic bargain, unmatched by its terrific location in the City's center. 
If I have ONE major complaint, the one that keeps me from giving The Latham a five-star rating, it is the terrible telephone reservation service. I was transferred back and forth between the operator and the reservation desk twice. The phone rang until it forwarded back to the operator each time. He continued to put me through to the reservation line where no one was answering. This happened twice, after which I hung up in frustration. My fiance tried again in the evening, and was able to make our reservation, however, she said the clerk sounded "like he was on drugs" and was not particularly friendly or helpful. I was almost afraid of what to expect on our arrival. I had read the bad reviews on here and I was becoming very reluctant about staying at The Latham after the phone call hassle and negative reviews, but I figured that for one night's stay it wouldn't matter much, even if there were flaws. Besides, the other hotels were booked solid. I am so glad I kept my reservation, because everything after that was just great! We will go back to The Latham, but I would urge the powers that be there to look more carefully at their reservation process. It certainly was not of the same caliber as the hotel itself!

title: “Disappointed - Well below par”
text: Having Just flown from London to New York to spend a lovely weekend as a tourist (not the usual business trip), I booked a double deluxe room (basic room to you & I) being a gold Hilton Honors card holder I must admit I did expect a lot from this hotel and it let me down on almost every detail. the check-in took at least 15 minutes. the room was small even by London standards. We were obvisously near an extractor outlet because with the window open 1cm there was an awful smell of cooking food. This hotel is old, and it shows! whilst I agree that a lot of modern hotels feel cold & stark. This hotel is souless. As a frequent traveller around the world I have stayed in many top class hotels. The Waldorf=Astoria is not a top class hotel. My recomendation is to either stay at the Intercontinental next door or the Ritz Carlton overlooking Central Park. I know I will next time.

title: “modern, comfortable rooms in good location”
text: modern, comfortable - but don't book Atrium view-rooms - there is no real light, just windows to the inside of the hotel (gets dark in the rooms), but beside of this, the room and the service was very good - the location of the hotel is really good - subway is about 1min away (just outside the hotel is an entry to the subway), Quincy Market 3min and the Aquarium also about 4min walk

title: “Really cool place to stay if in N.Y.C”
text: This hotel was really funky and reminded me of Urban Outfitters/Starbucks. The staff were really nice and extremely helpful and the location for everything was great. The only downside was we booked a bunk-bed room so was extremely cramped with all the shopping bags :( But could not fault the hotel, top notch!

title: “Better every time”
text: We spent another wonderful time at the Chelsea Pines Inn just before Christmas. It has been our second time at the CPI and it was even better then the first time because they had added to the already very generous breakfast our favorite 'George Clooney' coffee. So we really felt at home. Service was as always excellent and the staff very helpful given tips not only for the neighborhood but for the whole city. We will be back for sure!

title: “Absolutely Magnificent”
text: My family and I stayed at this hotel July 1st - 5th. The hotel was very clean and family oriented. The breakfast was delicious with plenty of food choices. The staff was terrific and we truly felt like valued guests. One of the nice gestures the hotel staff did was after walking back from viewing fireworks on the 4th of July, we were greeted by staff with bottles of water. It is the little gestures that mean so very much. The location was terrific for my family.......short walks to two Metro Station. Like previous reviewers, the small pool and strong chlorine smell was the only complaint.I will definitely recommend this hotel to family and friends.

title: “Modern hotel for the modern traveller”
text: I stayed at the Yotel in august with a friend. Our trip was last minute and we were only on NYC for two days, one night so proximity to the actoion was important. We arrived at the Yotel at 7am and were very pleased and surprised that our room was ready?! It could have been because it was a weekday but regardless we were able to check in, freshen up and start our sight seeing. The hotel is about 4 blocks to Times square area and also a few blocks from the fashion district. Location was great! We did the double Decker bus tour because the city is so large we were able to get on and off where we wanted to walk easily. After a long day sight seeing you can spend the evening on the rooftop terrace at the yotel which becomes quite he hang out for locals as well as tourists. Their is a.bar, restaurant and lounge area to meet anyone's needs. The staff at the yotel is very friendly and checkin and checkout are a breeze on the computers but help is not far if u need it. Our rooms were compact but.the layout of the room gives you space and compartments to place your things which make it usable space. The one thing I would consider is be comfortable with the person you go with because he restroom is a bit more open with just a curtain for privacy. You can't really see the person but it could be uncomfortable for some. In he morning the yotel offers complimentary muffins, coffee and tea on level 4. Checkout is at 11 but you are able to leave your luggage in the yobot all day and then come back before your departure to pick it up. I would recommend the yotel for technology friendly people or those who are open minded and appreciate modern design. We got am amazing deal online for the hotel at almost 50% off. I'm not sure if I would pay full price though.

title: “Have to return to find the ghost!”
text: We traveled to Boston from Cape Cod and stayed at the Omni Parker House, a perennial favorite. The hotel is centrally located, just down from the capital, and within walking distance of the ports. Still haven't seen the ghost that haunts the hotel, but hope to one day!

title: “Would Recommend”
text:
This is a typical Hampton Inn property. Small but efficient rooms. Clean, friendly staff, and good location. Tons of options in the area for food, even a few within walking distance.
Not a drawback for me, but I know some travelers do not like rooms without closets. Instead the room has a piece of furniture to hang up clothes in. My room had a fridge and microwave, do not know if all rooms have this.
Overall great value, and would reecommend to anyone.

title: “Good stay”
text: I stayed here for a business trip. Nice entrance. Comfortable room. I had a courtyard view which was great in the morning. I was able to get to the Riverwalk in about 5 minutes walking slowly. Staff recommended good places for dinner.

title: “Great Hotel!”
text: Had a great stay at Taj Campton Place! Fantastic location, amazing service, great use of space in the guest rooms. Room service food was also very tasty! Would highly recommend!

title: “MOLDY MILFORD”
text:
We went back to this hotel as it was one of the less expensive hotels in the city with a great location. We had stayed here 2 years before and it was closed for renovations last year. It was reopened this year so we figured we would try it assuming it had been renovated. BIG MISTAKE! Not only were the halls dank, dark and smelly as it has been closed up for a year, the room was horrid. We tries to get another room we were even willing to pay an extra $50-100 per person but they were booked, if you can imagine! We called housekeeping to ask for 2 blankets, never saw or heard back from anyone, never received the blankets either. As to the bathroom, to say it was small was an understatement Small would have been bearable at least if it had been clean. The sink still had the 2 different taps for hot & cold, that dripped all night. The shower would have loved to meet some Clorox as the mold was all black around the faucet and tiles along the bottom of the wall where it meets the tub. The shower head periodically gave you hot and cold water with no rhyme or reason as to when you would get blasted with either one. The best was the wallpaper literally hanging off and then finally falling off the wall behind the toilet. Oh and last but not least were the rusted out bottoms of the door frame, which looked as though they would collapse at any time....
NASTY is a mild word in describing this snakepit! The room itself had 2 double beds, and I use the word beds loosely, they we more like sponges sitting on top of a box top. There were no covers on the bed except for the top sheet, which maybe that way as the "BED BUG" scare through out Manhattan, but not to worry, those bugs have moved on up and out of that neighborhood! We learned our lesson and will not be back at the MILFORD! I don't care if the "THE DONALD" takes that place and makes it over. I guess at $350.00 a night you get what you pay for....It will certainly be worth it to pay more to get halfway decent.

title: “Worst and most expensive Marriott I've ever experienced”
text: This is the worst Marriott experience I have ever had, which is inexcusable at $350 for one night! Arrived at 5 PM to a room that was heavily deodorized to conceal, unsuccessfully, the smoke odor in the room. Five minutes later some guy showed up with a refrigerator that I had supposedly ordered, except I had not!! Had no internet access and was referred to a help line for half an hour, after which call the help desk confirmed there was something wrong with the hotel routers. The call with the help desk was a challenge because the phone had a loud and constant static noise during the entire call. I had internet for about 5 minutes when the hotel emptied out for dinner, but again no internet when I came back from dinner or in the morning. Too many users during the peak hours, so the claim that there is wireless internet and that it is free is false, except if you check your email at 3 AM. There was no cold water in the room; the water went from hot to boiling hot, in the shower and in the sink!! The lining of the shower curtain was moldy. This hotel is old and tired, but priced like the top-of-the- line hotels in DC. If this is the only place you can stay in DC, I suggest changing your trip!

title: “no complaints from Adele Hamilton New Zealand.”
text: I had 2 nights here at the hotel. i was a bit concerned prior to staying here as had the reviews. I cant believe how negative people are. We found the hotel despite being old good value, central, comfortable and clean. Loved the deep bath. The staff could not have been more helpful and friendly. The location was awsome. Sure theres road noise and homeless people around but what do you expect in abif city like this. This is not something the hotel can do anything about. I have stayed in more expensive places than this and they have not always been as good. Come on give this place a try we were very happy. Thanks staff at Renior Hotel.

title: “A NYC "Value"”
text:
OK, so this being NYC, value takes on a strange definition. This is an expensive hotel by any normal measure, but reasonable in NYC. The location is great, being close to the theater district is a real plus and the staff are by in large super. 
The rooms are goodly sized, modern and clean. The gym facilities are great and well kept.
The hotel is Time Square busy, so keep that in mind, but this is a great NYC choice.

title: “Decent hotel”
text: Clean room, overpriced, good location. When you hear the name Wyndham, you thought at least it is 4 star hotel but this is not, so do not expect that. Next time, I will stay near the Hotel Circle, nicer hotel for the same price or less.

title: “Excellent Value”
text: There is nothing bad to say about this hotel. Great location - right at Times Square in the middle of everything. Friendly and helpful staff. Great breakfast every morning. Saved us lots of money. The room seemed to be recently re-done -- everything was clean and attractive - we even had a flat screen t.v. The room however was small - but typical for NYC. Bathroom also quite nice and clean. I can't complain about anything. Excellent value. You really don't need to stay in a big large and expensive hotel. They even have a little gym set up off the lobby, plus internet service in the lobby area. Totally an excellent hotel - just small. I would absolutely stay there again and again. Just be aware of one thing ... when we booked at the front desk our return transportation to Newark Airport .... they over-charged us about 6 dollars each on the shuttle. I guess that's how they make a couple of extra dollars for their service. We should have done it ourselves directly with Supershuttle. Supershuttle charges $19.00, and we paid the hotel $25.00 each. Oh well.. you live and learn.

title: “An uncharacteristic disappointment for us with this fine brand”
text: We stayed there for a few days before Christmas. The HVAC in our room was very loud and made noise even when it was off, keeping us up most of the first night. We left the room at 9 the next morning and mentioned the problem to the front desk. When we returned at 4 PM it had not been tended to - and neither had the room been made up. When I called down, they said that they don't make up rooms unless you specifically ask them to. The engineer who showed up shortly thereafter to fix the HVAC told us that this was nonsense, which we understood it had to be, and when the cleaning lady later showed up (at around 5) she was defensive and a bit aggressive about having been tattled on. The HVAC was not fixed, though it was somewhat less noisy. Also, the scent that permeated the room, meant to be reminiscent of a spa or something, reacted badly with my wife's allergies.

title: “Budget property - Decent location”
text:
First of all, there are FIVE Comfort Inns in Manhattan. I am certain some of the views on this page were written for the wrong hotel. Reviews dated Dec.27 and Aug. 28 for sure, this is NOT the Comfort Inn Manhattan, it is the Comfort Inn on 36th just adjacent to the Javits Center, it has only 56 rooms (only 5 per floor), obviously used to be some sort of housing project or budget apartment building.
It is extremely budget, no frills! See photos on Orbitz. I thought I was booking the CI Manhattan. Although we saw workers mopping the floors and doing some maintanence, the hotel was not clean. The baseboards in our room had 3 inches of dust and dirt. The bedspread had cigarette burns. It is just an old hotel, I thought I had read they had renovated it some years back, maybe it sees a lot of group traffic. The hotel is in a great location for the Javits Center, but is on a run-down street with mostly vacant buildings. I felt uneasy walking back to the hotel late at night. Madison Square Garden is 3-4 blocks, Macys and a Subway station. On a good note, the parking (1 1/2 blocks away) was reasonable at $25 per day for an SUV, and the Continential breakfast was Comfort Inn standard and fine. There is no real lobby, staff is friendly, security seems to be in place (we were called at 6am one morning to see if we were expecting a visitor). In addition, EASY in and out of the city, I-495 ends and starts right at the hotel. We had a great time in the city, but I would not stay here again.

title: “Great place to stay if you travel alot for work.”
text: I stay here every time I travel to San Antonio it has big rooms that have all been remodeled, the staff is always friendly and I always feel safe staying here. If you are looking for a nice place to stay this is it. I also like the fact it has guest laundry facilites.

title: “cockroaches all over”
text: This was the worst motel I have ever stayed in. Dirty. Food left behind bed was the cause of roaches in the bedroom. Dead roaches in kitchen area. The bed was dirty with hardened staines on the blanket and quilt. Save your money and find another place. I needed to use the laundy, but with live roaches all over the room, I couldn't.

title: “average hotel, good location”
text:
the location was good, the room was spacey, the bathroom was quite big.
my only complaint is that my room was very very dark and looking at backside of the buildings - not really the first thing i want to see in the morning, but then this was business trip.
apart from this there was nothing special about this hotel, but then many hotels in this area are rather generic and with not much personality.

title: “A lovely Sanctuary in New York City”
text: Located close enough to Times Square to be convenient to major attractions and transportation, but also set just far enough away to be isolated from the area’s noise and craziness, the Sanctuary is my new, go-to New York boutique hotel. After a visit earlier in the year where I made some casual suggestions for improving the hotel to management (mostly related to glitchy Internet and TV services), I was promptly invited back to see if my next experience would better meet my expectations the second time around. It did. The technology problems had been resolved, allowing me to fully enjoy the clean, cool, contemporary atmosphere and the services of one the most friendly and accommodating hotel staffs I’ve encountered during my travels. The rates are in the middle to upper range for this type of property, but I found the Sanctuary to be a level above other boutique hotels in its category and worth the additional investment. Highly recommended.

title: “Hotel great, area not so much!”
text:
Stayed here for 5 nights towards the end of August, as I was attending a conference at the Moscone Center. 
The hotel was excellent, and very comfortable. Rooms were clean and well equipped. I only had limited dealing with the reception staff but they were friendly and helpful each time. And it was only a 10 minute walk to the Moscone Center.
My only two grievences were that the windows are single pane and subsequently you hear everything outside (you will need ear plugs unless you are a heavy / deep sleeper!) - and that the area is pretty intimidating. I suppose I did just get used to it after a few days and did find that the best route back from Moscone was along Howard Street and then up 7th to the hotel. But a number of times in the evening I would glance down side streets and see gangs hanging out, or have to navigate around homeless folks in the street. In all fairness we had no incidents in the 5 days we were at the hotel - we never bothered the people in the street and they never bothered us, but as I say, it was pretty intimidating and I was quite relieved to checkout at the end of our stay. 
If this bothers you, factor in the costs of taking a cab back to the hotel every night in your holiday budget!

title: “Great location, but needs more work.”
text: We really thought the location was great. It was close to alot of things that we were interested in. BUT our room was just average. The bathroom and paint really needed some work. The bed was just ok. The noise level was pretty high in our room, as we faced the street. The front desk person was curteous.

title: “Fabulous facilities”
text: Stayed recently for a conference that was taking place at the hotel. The rooms are by far the best i've seen in Chicago. Spacious with exactly the right amenities for any traveller. Loved the running track, thought this was a great idea and the views surprised me as it was only on the 3rd floor. Attentive front desk staff made the check in process super speedy and the late check out was greatly appreciated. I've knocked a star off because the service at breakfast was very slow and we had to ask several times for condiments or extra milk. Despite this I would definitely stay again.

title: “patchy”
text: hmmmmm another Intercontinential disappointment .... some amazing staff contrasted the rude and unhelpful checkin in staff (well just one) .... the queen beds are NOT for 2 people .... maybe 2 very young children. The bed was on an angle so felt like I was sleeping on a hill .... Fantastic Location however if you have a question after hours you are out of luck ... very small rooms and bathrooms - I guess that is New York

title: “Fantastic for the right price!”
text: Got a super deal on Priceline and our room and stay exceeded my expectations! Staff was friendly, room was amazing, free shuttle to the Market and back and more made this a really fabulous stay. Highly recommend, especially if you're a sports fan as the hotel virtually looks into Safeco Field! Be sure to visit the rooftop pool and spa!

title: “Staff was friendly and rooms were clean”
text: I thought that the facility was good for the purpose of my travel. Room was clean. Bed was comfortable. Thought it would be noisey with the airport next door, but was suprisingly quiet. Great highway access to get to most places in the southern area of Phoenix. Don't stray to far from the property for it changes quickly, but found the ammediate area was safe and secure. The hotel dinning was suprisingly good.

title: “Inexpensive hotel on metro line”
text: This is a newer hotel right on the metro line. It is in a "questionable" neighborhood, but if you hop on the metro (literally 1/4 block away), you can access all of DC and norther VA. There is also a couple fast food restaurants, and a 5 guys right across the street. But, it is in the middle of nowhere, yet we used this hotel to go see the Nationals. Parking is pricey and by valet only.

title: “A great experience”
text: Met my son in Indy for the Final Four last week--So glad we stayed at the Crowne Plaza airport. Spent a lot of time in the bar, and what a fantastic crew they have working there. Holly, Nikki, Sally--the bartenders, and even Kelsey, the young bus girl, hostess, etc were all so professional and totally entertaining. They made our trip so much more enjoyable! If you happen to be in Indianapolis and either staying at the Crowne Plaza Airport, or close to there--Do yourself a favor and stop by.

title: “Overpriced”
text: I paid $135 for this Hampton Inn that was in excellent condition and very clean. However, they told me I could walk to the Colorado Convention Center when I made the reservation but it was 2 miles away and very difficult to navigate. You would think they would have a shuttle or van to the downtown area-----you need a car if you stay here. The hotel staff was helpful and the room was very clean.

title: “Excellent room with great fresh donuts, guava juice,coffee and free paper”
text: We stayed the night before our cruise and slept very well in a huge king size bed. Had sushi (all you can eat in one hour) next door. In the morning the manager, Kazi Ahmed had the best donuts that I have tasted...they are made by someone who has been in business for 40 years. Fresh juice, coffee and a free ride to the ship (which we could see from our room). Upon our return, we were able to check in at 9:00 a.m. We went to Universal and Disneyland and enjoyed our stay for two more nights. I liked sunning by the cute little pool. Will stay here every time we visit southern cal...very clean and reasonable...and I worked for Hyatt Hotels for 36 years...getting free rooms all over the world...thank's to the whole staff!

title: “Hairstyle and Dinner”
text:
This was my first visit to the Haim Salon my stylist was Katie. She gave me a cut and color. First of all Katie is the most adorable young lady. She was very professional and has the most wonderful personality. My hair has never looked this good!! I look like a new person, I wanted to dress up and go out with my husband!! He by the way loved my new look!! She is amazing!! 
My husband and I had dinner at Amaya and service there was spectacular! Ekrem came to our table and introduced himself making sure we were happy with our meal. The food was great but the service was what made our meal so good. 
My husband and I will deffinately return!! I will deffinately be returning to Katie! I don't want anyone else touching my hair!!
Bravo to you and your staff!!

title: “Decent location/Decent Hotel for the money”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for 2 nights in order to see the historical monuments in DC. The hotel is definitely within walking distance of the US Capitol which is why I chose this hotel. However, just keep in mind that it is still a hike if you plan on walking to and from the US Capitol to your hotel. Even though you are only a few blocks from the Capitol those are LONG blocks and is likely at least a third of a mile from the hotel.
And while I had absolutely no problems I think the location of the hotel was just a little bit shady. Since it isn't right in front of Capital you are located inside a neighborhood that isn't very active. I'm sure it is safe but I made sure I looked twice when I had to go to the ATM machine at night a block away.
For the money (don't spend more than $140 a night if possible) I would say it was worth it only because it is within walking distance of the capitol. The room was a decent size for me with plenty of closet space. However, if you listened you could probably here anyone's conversations outside their rooms (the walls seem kind of thin).
All in all I would recommend this hotel if you are young, in shape, and just want to save a few bucks when visiting the area.

title: “Great location, Great price, great value”
text: My daughters and I wanted to spend a couple of days in Chicago over Christmas break and do some shopping without spending a fortune on the room. This hotel met all our expections and then some. We were close to the Magnificant Mile for all the great shopping and within walking distance to great restaurants and the subway. The free trolley to Navy Pier was a great perk as well, but we could easily have walked there as well. The concierge desk was helpful with directions and everyone was helpful and friendly. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Makes business travel amazingly convenient”
text: I always avoided hotel airports thinking they were horrible places for those bumped off their flights. Well, my experience at the O'Hare Hilton changed all that. It is incredibly convenient to go from gate to hotel back to the gate. The staff was very friendly and concerned about providing good service. The public spaces were spacious, clean and welcoming. The food served was tasty & always with healthy choices. It was easy to make arrangements to leave the airport site to visit local restaurants. The room was large and quiet. Very nice..thanks for chaning my mind about airport hotel;s!

title: “Very good hotel although not exceptional”
text: I stayed here for a week for a mixed business trip/weekend away with my girlfriend. The room (1025) is a great size for a NYC hotel, with a large main area, large bed, kitchenette but quite small bathroom. The desk staff always seemed busy when I passed and maybe because of this they weren't that friendly on check-in. We did not eat at the hotel, although the Rare bar/grill does look nice. The locations is good for East Midtown and business; Grand Central a 10 minute walk; however, for general tourism, something more central would have been better as we like to walk. However, the rooms benefitted from this by being very peaceful. Rooftop bar has great views although cocktails are average.

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
From the time you enter the Fairmont Copley through your departure the service is excellent.
The Copley is situated at Copley Sq. with easy access to shopping on Newbury St., the Copley Sq. and Prudentiall Malls are right next store,and the subway is a block away.
The hotel is decorated with lovely historical pictures and is furnished with early American furniture. Rooms are comfortable and spacious.
When visiting the Copley be sure to have a bite to eat in the famous Oak room.
Our visit to Boston was much more enjoyable because we stayed at The Fairmont Copley Plaza.

title: “A hotel worth checking into”
text: I've stayed at the Ambassador and the hotel is in the process of complete renovation. Everything is new and the staff was very accomodating. The continential breakfast was beyond what I expected and they fed my child without me being there and he even brought my breakfast to my room. The price of the rooms are quite reasonable and if your a stockyard fan there is a weekend shuttle to and from Billy Bob's. You can't go wrong checking into this hotel.

title: “Great location but ...”
text: This hotel has a stunning location, right at the heart of the SF waterfront, by the cable car and public transport and close to both tourist sights and the business district. But it is not quite as good as one might have expected - the rooms are noisy (the walls are so thin that one hears both street noise and other guest noise), the bath is tiny (one cannot actually have a bath in it), the entrance is confusing. For one night, I did not mind too much, but I would not stay here for a longer stay, whether my visit to SF was on business or for pleasure.

title: “Location, location, location”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the Affinia Liaison for our 28th wedding anniversary. In general, we were satisfied with our stay. We booked the $109/night weekend rate. Based on the location, we felt that the price was fine.
The good:
You cannot beat the location. You are two blocks from the Capitol and two blocks from Union station. We parked the car and did not use it once during our stay. The neighborhood seemed safe. We experienced no issues walking in the area, even at night. There is a shelter a few blocks to the west, however, there are no tourst attractions in that direction. The rooftop pool is nice in the evening. It was nice to go up there for a few drinks to end the day. We found the staff to be very polite and accomodating. They responded quickly to anything we asked for. The Charlie Parker steak house is two blocks away for fine dining. Affinia also offers a selected number of pillow types. I tried the memory foam pillow. My wife was very happy with the standard down pillows.
The bad:
The hotel is still under renovations, so, there is no restaurant. It should be finished soon. We walked to Union Station for breakfast (full breakfast for about $5). The building is definitely dated, but, the alternative would have been to demolish and rebuild. Affinia made a business decision to renovate, so, they had some constraints. With that said, I think that Affinia did not get the best value from their contractors. Some of the renovation work in the rooms is shoddy. The room quality is acceptable at the reduced rate, but, if Affinia starts charging the same prices as their NYC hotels, I would question the value. Our room had a faint smell of cigarette smoke. We reported this (we did not want to get tagged with the $250 cleaning fee for smoking). The housekeeping staff sprayed some air freshener to hide the smoke smell. Again, the staff was very responsive; this is more an issue with the use of an old building. I believe tha Affinia needs to change their web site in order to reflect what is actually available at the hotel.
