They have not gotten around to putting flat screen televisions in the rooms and the bar/restaurant is not open, yet.
The ugly:
Get ready for sticker shock when you park your car. Valet parking will run you about $45/day. Self-parking cost us about $37/day. I hope my car enjoyed its accomodations!
At the price, my wife and I would stay here again. The beds are comfortable and we like the location. I expect Affinia to bring the hotel up to their NYC hotel standards.

title: “Great hotel, Great Rooms, Great Hotel Gym”
text:
Stayed here on business in January 2012 for 6 nights for a conference. I travel a lot for business and this hotel definitely exceeded my expectations.
Rooms are large for NYC-- clean, spacious, and comfortable. Elevators are quick and fast, even though there is a lot of traffic and many floors.
In-room internet worked great and the fitness center (although it cost $14.95 to use) was large, well-equipped, and open 24 hours.
Definitely reccomend for business.

title: “Great place to stay for a conference in Boston”
text: This hotel has a great location in Boston making it easy to escape for breaks from work to experience glimpses of the city. I had a gorgeous view of the prudential and the river (ask for a high floor). As a bonus it's attached to shopping malls, so I could get early Xmas shopping done too. Great restaurants and bars are all really close by. My room was spacious and on the corner, with plenty of space to work. The only downside is that the feel is very cookie-cutter corporate. Motivating for getting work done, but not cozy or interesting or anything like that. But I prefer small hotels and that's just my preference. There was nothing wrong with it per se-- very clean and friendly staff and all that-- I just prefer more interesting spaces.

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text: I stayed 3 nights in January for a business trip. It was truly a wonderful hotel as many reviewers described. The location was great, close to downtown business district; and restaurants in the Gaslamp District. The room was clean and the bed was comfortable. Friendly staff and great service. I will definitely recommend this hotel.

title: “Extremely convient to Mayo Clinic”
text: We stayed in the two bedroom suite seperated by a living room/kitchen area $249. Standard Residence Inn layout. Very Clean, staff very helpful and compassionate. Permitted us to use late checkout which was appreciated to rest between tests at the hospital. Free hot breakfast. You can park the car and not have to more again and use the free hotel shuttle to get to the Mayo hospital cllinics. Hotel is also connected by an inside walking tunnel that connects directly to the hospital. We will stay there again inspite of the cost because of the convenience when enduring multiple tests scheduled at different times during the day.

title: “Front Desk Service”
text: I was especially impressed by the front desk service of Gentlejoy. She went our of her way to help me with an email/fax transaction that was time critical. Gentejoy provided her own email address for me to use, as well as waiving any charges to my room. She was so courteous and friendly. Thank you for such great service!

title: “Better Than Expected”
text:
We stayed for 2 nights feb 11 & 12. Hotel was actually nicer than I expected inside and out. Everything looked really clean and well kept and the pool looked nice too. We arrived early Saturday about 10am and our room was not ready, but they gave us a parking pass. So we parked our truck and off we went. We spent the day walking and bar hopping along the board walk and did not make it back to the hotel till about 5pm. I had asked for an upstairs room and they gave me a large room upstairs, close to the office, the stairs and the street...Our room was updated and I thought quite nice. The bed was comfy and we had a fridge, microwave and a coffee maker. Location of the hotel was excellent. Once we parked our truck (in a covered parking spot) we walked everywhere and did not use the truck once. Lots of places close by to eat or stop in and have a drink. Lots more places closer to Belmont park (the roller coaster) if you enjoy walking-which we do.
Tips-Bring your own coffee, filters and coffee cups. You have a coffee maker in the room, but you need to bring everything else.
If you go to the office to get coffee and sweet rolls in the morning. Bring the tray from your room. They don't have plates or trays in the office if you are trying to carry more than one thing.
Dont stay in a room close to the road--even a Saturday night, off season was loud, loud, loud. Some of the cars sounded like they were driving through the room and the kids coming back from the bars sounded like they were also in the room at times. I went down Sunday to see about changing rooms and the girl at the front desk was great and said they could change me to the other end, but that Sunday night would be much quieter. She also offered to help us move our stuff which i thought was cool. We decided to just stay put and she was right Sunday was much quieter. This was not a deal breaker for us, but something you should be prepared for. Never felt unsafe and the hotel seemed pretty booked with a pretty good bunch of folks

title: “FANTASTIC DOWNTOWN CHICAGO HOTEL”
text:
First I would like to thank Hilton for the great upgrade to the executive floor -lakeside room! That was awesome! The room was very clean and updated nicely. We had two bathrooms and two double beds. The bathrooms were spotless and smelled fantastic. ( I think it was the soaps and shampoo that left such a good smell) The beds were doubles- so very, very small for two adults, but we managed as there were 3 of us. The beds were very comfortable and the bedding excellent quality. ( What you would expect from a Hilton!) 
The free access to the 8th floor health club was a very nice surprise and my son said it was the best work out room he has ever been to while traveling. He said it was huge and even had a running track- modern updated workout equipment and lots of them!
The 57.00 dollars was worth paying for valet service. We at least knew our vehicle was secure and would be safe for the overnight. The valet guys were very nice, efficient and when we called for our vehicle to be brought up in the morning it was waiting for us when we got there. Parking fees are ridiculous in big cities - so bite the bullet and pay the extra money and sleep peacefully knowing your car won't be stolen or stripped down. 
Front desk was very friendly and nice- their smiles were appreciated after our long trip in rain, fog and stand still traffic on the Chicago interstates. 
The only 2 negatives were the very thin walls - we heard the elevator every time it reached our floor ding and heard every inconsiderate group of guests that just had to talk while walking to their rooms at 11pm at night. I swear it wouldn't kill anyone to walk quietly to their rooms and shut the door without letting it bang - but I have yet to see it or should I say "not" hear it.So my advice would be take earplugs to get a good nights rest.
The air conditioning was slow to cool the room- when we checked in it was 73 so we turned the thermostat down to 70. It took almost 7 hours to cool it. So I would hate to see how it does on a sweltering hot day in the 90's - as the temps were only in the 50's when we got there.
We would stay there again - happily when going to the Chicago downtown area!!

title: “Trendy Hotel & Attentive Service Ruined By Loud Music!”
text:
We asked for a quiet room and booked three months in advance but nobody was listening!
The rooms are really nice and our 5th floor room seemed all that we asked for, until we went to bed! Extremely loud music from the bar below prevented any sleep and several complaints to the Bar and Hotel Manager eventually achieved elevation to the near silent upper floors - much better!
The Management were extremely apologetic.

title: “Beautiful property but lacking in key areas”
text:
In a fantastic location (near a number of other great hotels like the Lenox, Four Seasons, and Ritz Carlton), the Taj has tough competition.
The property has beautiful touches abound (chandeliers in the hallways, antique door fixtures in the main lobby, etc.) and is simply charming.
However I experienced a few things that were deal breakers for me:
1. The room (park view) was *extremely* loud. The street is busy and loud and I woke up about 5 times during the night as a result.
2. The service has mixed, but crucially flawed in dealing with complaints. I called down for my car, was told it would be up in 10-15 minutes, and waited 40 minutes (counted it on my clock). As a result, I was late to the meeting I flew out to Boston for. The valet management and hotel management was extremely unapologetic and quite frankly judgmental. Never apologized once, never offered to comp the valet. My company paid for the trip, but I don't care. I have worked in 4 diamond resorts and customer service is key. Really poor.
3. The food is really mixed. I love their breakfast, but their desserts in the bar with absolute garbage. I love desserts, my bar is really low, and I couldn't stomach either their Opera Cake or Boston Creme Pie. Their wine list was also blatantly wrong (Oh we forgot to update it... it's not an 07 napa cab, its an 08. BIG DIFFERENCE if you know wine. When asked how long the menu had been un-updated, the bartender told me about half a year). Nice guys!
So fantastic location, but potentially extremely noisy and clearly not focused on delivering magical customer experiences (which is what hospitality is all about).
Next time - Lenox, 4 Seasons, or Ritz.

title: “Great place to stay with kids!”
text: The food in the restaurant was delicious! I ordered the shrimp and grits both nights. The breakfast was good, too. We did have to wait about 10 minutes for a table of six, so plan your time accordingly. There is a "Five Guys" across the street and a sandwich shop almost next door. The hotel is very close to the train- great location. The rooms were clean. We had a wonderful visit, and I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Thanks for the view”
text:
This is a solid Marriott property and the staff was very friendly. We were upgraded to a corner view room with a spectacular vista down Penn. Ave. to the Capitol. The Washington Monument was front and center and the Lincoln Memorial glowed at night. We watched the Turkey Trot from our perch as runners and walkers poured up and down the street below.
The Club lounge was very crowded and seating was limited. The food, however, was very good. We all used the gym, pool and sauna and found the facilities to be fine. While the valet parking is expensive and the porte cochere was small and packed with vehicles, the location of the hotel is superb. I travel to the D.C. area often and I will stay here again.
I only gave this hotel 4 stars because I was charged for minibar items that we did not touch or consume. My sister had the same issue. Check your bill!

title: “Great hotel that acknowledged SPG platinum status.”
text: My fiancee and I were fortunate to have been on the receiving end of any of the many negative experienced shared by other reviewers. On the contrary, our stay over the busy 4th of July weekend could not have been any more enjoyable. They acknowledged my SPG Platinum status w an upgrade to a suite and fresh strawberries w 3 dips. She enjoyed her massage/manicure at the Bliss spa in the basement. Save yourself some money and visit Press Liquor for any alcohol you might want to consume instead of paying the outrageous minibar fees. Given the hotel's location and proximity to public transit, we'll definitely come back again.

title: “Airport quick”
text: Had to layover and glad I chose this hotel. Hot tub has very powerful jets and clean water. Room was very spacious and clean and QUIET. Down the street is a restaurant called The Village Inn that doesn't look like much and claimed "The Worlds Best Pies" (free slice on Wednesday) which I scoffed at until I had a slice.

title: “Outstand stay and service”
text: Hotel and staff went above the norm to make our stay exceptional. Great stay. Willstay always....

title: “We loved it and we will definitely be back!! Hopefully sooner rather than later!!”
text: Our stay at the Austin Four Seasons was perfect as always! We traveled with our two children, and they treated them like little princesses. As we were leaving the resort on Sunday, they wanted to know when we could come back! The food, staff and service were impeccable. Definitely our best hotel experience in Austin. Thank you FOUR SEASONS!!

title: “Location,location,location”
text: This Hotel was perfect for "bike New York " , close to the bike expo and the ferry landing at the finish. The hotel clerks were very accomadative , the rooms are larger than any hotel in the city for this price. My friends and I will be here next year.

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text:
Booked via Hotwire and received a fabulous rate. Front desk was very accommodating to my requests a check in, despite the hotel being full, and the hotwire rate. The room was oversized compared to a typical guest room, the bed was wonderful, and the housekeeping staff was superb. The location is great. Parking was not a problem - parked in the lot on 6th and K and spent $8 per night, although this would have been much higher if I kept my car parked there during the day. 
The only downside was the noise from the train - however a room on the other side of the hotel would solve the problem. Definitely the best SD hotel I've stayed at - will definitely stay again.

title: “Bad First experience”
text: I booked the Artisan Hotel because it was the closest Hotel from my conference at the Peabody and was 3 miles away for the best price. The logistics of getting back and forth was a hassle and cabs are expensive so i took the bus. When I checked in the first night my card for my door did not work 2 times. When i finally got in the toilet didn't work. Not a ggod start. It was fixed the next day and I really liked that they had a desktop computer to work for free since I didn't bring my laptop and had work to do. Everthing else was fine with my visit except for when I left my room for 45 min. came back and my room was cleaned and i left my wallet by the TV instead of on my body or hiding it and a $10 bill was gone. I could not prove it and at the front desk it says they are not held liable for lost or stolen items, so I did not bring it up. When i came back i emailed the corporate office and a Mr. Barrera emailed me back apologizing for the situation and refunded $10 back to me and offered another one night stay which was very generous of him. I would give it another chance, I will just keep my wallet with me this time.

title: “Perfect location”
text: Great location for any leisure stay in Washington DC. Near virtually any monument, the White House, Museum in the District. Not far from a few Metro locations. We paid $85 or so a night off of Priceline 3 days before our stay. Well worth the cost. DId not try any of the hotel restaurants but the Conceige was extremely knowledgeable as were the Bellmen. Also if you go down Pennsylvania towards the Capitial there are many restuarants, there are very few very near the hotel. Walking in the hotel area though seemed decent and mostly safe.

title: “Just a great place to stay”
text: We visit California twice a year and start and finish each trip in this motel. We stayed there now about 10 times over the past 5 years and we love the place. We don't know what the critics of this place are talking about! The staff is friendly and very helpful. The motel is rather old, the room could do some remodeling, but they are very clean and quiet. Good value for the money. The guests are friendly and social, for a friendly talk or more if you want. Much less attitude than usually in gay hotels. Parking is free and easy. If you are looking for a gay, cruizy, safe, clean and affordable place to stay in Hollywood, this is the place.

title: “Great Location Good Price”
text: Stayed here for 4 nights with my husband and three teenagers. Was good value for money. Greta location and the breakfast was good. Would stay there again.Friendly helpful staff - My husband accidentally left a shirt in the wardrobe and they found it and put it aside for us.

title: “Amazing view”
text:
My husband and I stayed here for a few days on vacation before his stay became a business trip. We used honors points for our portion of the stay, so I'm not sure how to rate the value, but overall we had a fantastic time. They upgraded us to the 24th floor with a view of Coit Tower and it's surroundings. Absolutely gorgeous sight with the fog rolling in every morning and night.
The hotel staff for the most part was fairly helpful. The man who checked us in was great. The valet was fast and polite. Concierge needs some work... We were consistently on our own trying to find good restaurants. Scala was superb, by the way.
Hotel is next to Chinatown. We walked to the Ferry Bldg...15min?? Cabs are easy to find. We had one driver who loves to play drumsticks and sing while he drives lol.
Overall, you'll be happy with the Hilton...one word of advice-if the elevator gets stuck, try the open door shut door buttons to unjam it. Yes we did get stuck. but only for about a minute :)

title: “Easy access to most of DC,s most popular sights”
text: Good value and very close to the White House, National Mall and the Smithsonin . Room was nice but a little small , very quiet and overall was a nice experience staying there. The staff was very nice and on 2 occasions the restaurant manager gave us great reccomendationd on local placed on interest. You are 3 blocks away from the White House.

title: “Great location and value for money”
text:
I stayed at the Hollywood Celebrity Hotel in connection with the 2011 Academy Awards in Hollywood. The hotel is in fact right behind the Kodak Theatre. Orchid Ave (where the hotel is located) is actually shut down on Oscar Night. Thus, the hotel is very close to all the action on Hollywood Blvd, with Graumann's, all the museums and other attractions in Hollywood right around the corner. It's also a 2-minute walk from The Magic Castle.
My room was huge! Apparently I was upgraded so I got a room with two queen beds even though I'm a solo traveller. Aside from the main room, there was a small room with a fridge and a dining table, as well as a medium-size bathroom and a room with plenty of closet space for your clothes. My room was bigger than some of the suites I've stayed in at fancy hotels in Las Vegas. 
That being said, the room looked very dated and worn out, with bland walls and not much attention paid to interior design or decoration. It's not a place you'd feel comfortable spending a lot of time in. But if you are not planning on spending much time at the hotel anyway, and instead explore the tourist attractions of the area, the Hollywood Celebrity is a good choice for a traveller on a budget.
Unlike the room, the halls and the lobby area look very nice. There's also a computer in the lobby for the guests to use. 
The free Wi-Fi was very slow and unstable. To be fair, the manager offered the use of a LAN connection with a network cable, if you have a laptop. I don't know if that connection was more stable or fast though.
A nice feature was a complimentary breakfast. You got some basic choices of toast, croissants, yoghurt and juice. Nothing fancy or delicate by any means, but it was okay considering you didn't pay extra for it (and the room rate is very reasonable to begin with).
There is no view to speak of from the room and across the hotel there is often noise from young folks partying and such. This can make it difficult to sleep if it happens while you are staying at the hotel.
In terms of amenities, there's all the basic stuff, including a fridge in the room that you can use as you wish, and a TV with all the major channels, including HBO. There was even a microwave oven which is a nice touch. 
In short, the hotel is great for the location and the price. For a two-star property it exceeded my expectations but it's not a Las Vegas resort by any means and it doesn't try to be.

title: “Great location but service is WAY off”
text: I generally love Westin hotels and the location was perfect in Copley Square, but this was NOT a good stay. When we pulled back the comforters, our sheets were stained (in a way I can't even convey in this review). The bathroom was cleaned only at what I consider to be an "average" level. This feels like a Westin that WAS nice but is not any longer - very poorly managed and no customer service. After our incident, we didn't receive even the slightest apology. The location is amazing but the experience was very dissatisfying.

title: “Comfortable and convenient, reasonably priced.”
text:
Hotel management team courteous efficient and friendly, only too pleased to move us to a quiet, better room due to noisy interior work being carried out above our original room. 
Linen changed daily, maid service very efficient.
A conveniently situated Hotel at most reasonable rates.
Can recommend room 210
Would certainly make a return visit.

title: “Old World Elegance - Modern Amenities”
text:
We chose the Churchill because it was close to where our daughter was starting college the next day. It was the perfect location, a block away from the historic Adams Morgan district. The very helpful and friendly front desk staff directed us to the perfect Brazilian restaurant only three blocks away. Since our daughter had just returned from a trip to Brazil, we couldn't have been more pleased.
We easily found free parking only a block away. We spent a quite, peaceful evening in a room that seemed like it should have cost twice the price we paid. It was a very elegant way for my daughter and I to spend her last night before she started college and the life of a poverty-stricken student. Our only regret was that we couldn't luxuriate in the morning as she had orientation the next morning.

title: “Everything went well”
text:
Everything on this business stay went well, no trouble with check-in, room was great and clean, valet parking was easy. Very easy access to this hotel from the airport. I have never been to San Antonio before and had no trouble finding the hotel.
The hotel is an easy but not short walk to the the convention center. I recommend walking through the Rivercenter mall.
There are a lot of restaurant choices. If you are health conscience there are very very food stores in the downtown area, so I relied on Starbucks and Walgreens. The hotel breakfast is great if you are on an anti-paleo high carb/sugar diet, plenty of donuts, waffles, muffins, bread etc. If you are looking for an upgrade, have breakfast at the Marriott.
I needed to leave early in the morning for my flight. I call the previous evening to have my car ready for 4:00 AM. To my delight, my car was ready and I was out the door with no hassle at all. I wish all hotels had such good coordination with staff.
The parking fee was high, other than that I was happy with the rate.

title: “Clean and comfortable. Great location”
text: Stayed one night as part of coach tour mid September. Room was excellent, really quite spacious with a large bathroom,comfortable and clean bedding. Very friendly staff and location was great. Lots of restaurants nearby as well as so many of the historical sights to visit within easy walking distance. Would stay longer next time.

title: “Well-Worn, Functional Suites • 10-Min. to PHL Airport • Free RI Airport Shuttle”
text:
Adequate for overnight stay if proximity to airport is your priority. Older, 2-story, townhouse-style buildings (no elevator); just over 100 suites. A sub-standard Residence Inn (RI), long overdue for refurbishing. 
Studio Suite, Queen Bed  (2nd-Story Near Gatehouse)
---------------------------------
• Spacious, quiet room, but furnishings, furniture, cabinetry, counters are worn.
• Older TV with poor reception; hopefully all TVs are updated to LCDs.
• Small bathroom: shower/ tub combo with peculiar on/off, hot/cold water dial -- an imaginative, overly complex plumbing fix that appears to be a workaround to installing the appropriate fixture. 
• Good having stove, kitchenette, dining counter (with stools) -- just run-down.
Free
------
• On-site self-parking. (Versus $45 parking in heart of Center City.)
• Modest breakfasts (each morning) & evening food (Tue., Wed., Thur.).
• Computer & printer in lobby to print documents & boarding passes. (Room Internet problematic, so used lobby computer.)
Approximate Drive Times (Depending on Traffic)
----------------------------------
• 10 min. (3 mi./ 5 km) to Philadelphia International Airport (PHL). (Call for free RI airport shuttle.)
• 20 min. (8 mi./ 13km) to downtown Philadelphia: Center City, city hall, museums, historic sites.
If you require modern style, comforts, & niceties, best look elsewhere. Functional for quick overnight stay, but wouldn't recommend for anything longer.
(Would only return if other hotels were unavailable or this RI were *completely/ thoroughly* redone. Unfortunate because it's extremely convenient to PHL -- just not worth the unpleasantness.)

title: “Great value compared to other hotels in this location.”
text: I recently visited SF for a work conference, then extended my trip a few days for pleasure. During the time of the conference my business partners and I stayed at the Marriott Marquis for $305 a night. After the conference was over my wife joined me and we moved to the Hilton on Union Square, which was more than half of the price of the Marriott. The price difference did not reflect the quality of the hotel, as I thought the Hilton was very much just as nice of a hotel as the Marriott. The location is great, very centralized to many of the "sights" San Francisco has to offer.

title: “Very disappointing”
text:
Well, it took me a long time to write this review. I never want to say anything bad if I don't have to and it sometimes takes me a while to gather my thoughts. The best thing about this hotel was the location. That and there was a travelzoo rate that couldn't be beat. 
My problem with the hotel was this: They ask you where you want to stay and what amenities your want. We got none of them. We ended up on the second floor near the elevator with a room overlooking the stairwell. Our room was the size of my closet. We were staying there for 5 days and I was hoping for something better. 
Our friends got in that night and, when we went to their room for a drink, we were shocked to see that they had a HUGE rom with a fantastic view. Not only that but they had a fridge, coffee station and all the amenities we were looking for. So, I call down to the front desk and ask if we can have a room like theirs - corner room with a view (what we asked for in our booking). The response? Sure, for a hundred bucks extra a night.
I explain to the front desk that they booked the same travelzoo deal we did and the response? Well, they're only staying one night and you're staying 5. Really? I'm spending MORE money so I get a crappier room? Add insult to injury and the hotel tells me the reason they got that room is that the hotel is sold out so they got upgraded! The hotel is not sold out the time we're staying so we'll have to give them another 400 bucks if we want a room like theirs. 
I bit my tongue, sucked it up and lived with it. This was in May. It's now August and I'm still fuming about it. It would have been no big deal for them to give me a better room and then they would have gotten a GREAT review from me. Bad customer service if you ask me.

title: “Very good”
text:
We are 4 English couples and stayed here for 3 nights for our sons wedding on 4th July.
I cannot praise this hotel too high, we were charged $89 a night including breakfast - the rooms were spacious, clean and very, very comfortable.
The prices for the drinks and food were good and the service was very friendly, the pizzas as a snack at lunchtime were very good.
The location is not ideal for the centre of Columbus (but it was for our family wedding) and it is right next to the Interstate highway with a very good shopping center within 2 minutes walk.
It is unlikely we will need to stay in this area again but if we did this hotel would be our first choice without doubt.

title: “Good Value, Nice Room”
text: A clean and comfortable room at a nice price. During one of the busiest tourist weekends in San Diego where average hotels charged rates nearing $400, our family of four stayed for $139/night. This included complimentary buffet breakfast (very good) and a $25 gift certificate at the restaurant's hotel--parking is also free. The pool and hot tub area are well maintained like the rooms. The only drawbacks are the 25 minute drive to downtown SD which can take longer b/c of traffic and no fridge in the room. We would certainly stay there again.

title: “Lovely Setting - Friendly Staff”
text:
I stayed at J.W. Marriott Spa & Resort for three nights for a business event. Staff were all very friendly and helpful. The facility is gorgeous! I could have spent most of my trip in the lobby or the huge arrival verandah. This impressive property blends very well with the natural surroundings and I was thrilled to see jack-rabbits eating grass on the lawn on my way to breakfast. Dining outside was a treat as well since all sorts of birds, including hummingbirds happily mingled with diners and staff and more aggressive species waited to snatch left overs from the buffets and clearing trays. The impressive labeled native plant collection on the walking paths and an adequate number of big comfy wooden benches and chairs made it easy to tolerate the high temperatures (102 - 106 during my stay). The distant mountain range was an impressive view from my balcony. A colleague said she'd seen a coyote on the path during an early morning jog. This facility is definitely for nature lovers and is a perfect backdrop for nature photography.
My king room was adequate, though the color scheme and decor made it a little too casual - might do well with an update. The room and the entire hotel were clean and tidy though. In my room was a large desk with ethernet (wi-fi is free in the lobby), big screen TV, large chest with in-room safe, large closet, loads of large mirrors, a seating area with loveseat and coffee table and a large bath with deep soaking tub and separate glass shower. When I reported the toilet handle was barely attached to the tank when I got to my room maintenance arrived promptly to make the repair and the front desk followed up via phone to ensure all was well. 
Meeting areas were great but our group was quite large so we utilized several salons. Because of the size of the room it was difficult to view either of the huge screens while presenting from the center of the stage. One thing everyone noted was the hotel catering staff for the meeting was reluctant to leave the buffets out for very long even though the meeting frequently ran past break time. Stragglers arrived to the foyer to find the serving trays had already been removed though there had still been plenty of food.
Food during the meeting and via room service was good, nothing extraordinary but certainly not inedible. The resort boasts several restaurants though I did not get a chance to try any of them. There is also a spa, golf course, swimming pool with 'rafting,' a Starbuck's and Kinko's as well as several upscale shops. Kiosks to print boarding passes are across from the front desk and are a welcome convenience. The conscierge desk staff was even there late evening to help facilitate day trips or outings and there was a multitude of brochures to peruse. Each morning, a variety of newspapers were available at reception. 
Despite the magnitude and elegance of the entry and reception, the main focus at Marriott Spa & Resort seems to be comfort and a down to earth friendly, cheerful approach. I suppose that would explain the sunny yellows and bright colors in the rooms rather than more somber and stuffy elegance. One point to keep in mind if heading here for a stay is the resort is very large. I was on one end of the building on the lobby level and my meeting was at the other end. It was easily a ten minute walk, albeit through the beautiful lobby and past a bank of windows through which I could watch the bunnies enjoying the lawn.
Marriott was advertising a deal, $99 a night for up to four nights for a future visit but it was necessary to prepay and I wasn't sure when I'd be in Phoenix again so I didn't get details but I would definitely recommend this property for leisure or business especially at those savings!

title: “Never again!”
text:
I am writing this review from the hotel. This is by far the worst hotel I have ever stayed at. The room is dirty and the air in the room as well as the hallway and lobby do not work. The sheets are so thin that you can see the mattress under neath them. We had no towels in our room when we arrived and it took about two hours for towels to be delivered. This am after our room was cleaned they did not leave us towels again.
We had ordered a roll away at 4 pm and it finally arrived At 11:50.
The water park is sick! The slides are rusted and the water is hot. Two areas do not even have water. There are not enough tubes and the guards walk around like they are watching but twice today I saw a guard walk right by people who needed help. It is hard to take the guards seriously when they have lifeguard or supervisor written with sharpie marker on their shirts. 
To make things even worse they closed the pool for well over an hour today for mandatory training.. Why wouldn't they do that during the week instead of in the middle of the a SAturday.
Yuck! Yuck! Yuck! Next time I will save my money and head to Holiday World!

title: “Awesome Hotel Great Staff”
text: I stay at this hotel a lot when I come to Austin for business or for pleasure. It's a great price and the staff is excellent especially their new front desk clerk named Austin. He's extremely nice and always helpful. Every time I've stayed at this hotel recently I've had an amazing experience. I'm sure there's little problems wrong with the hotel here and there like when there's a Gecko in the bathroom or something little like that but Gecko's are supposedly a sign of good luck and they're everywhere in the Austin area because they eat bugs, I know a lot of my friends that have homes and apartments in Austin have them in their homes so thats not something to complain about. All and all this a great hotel with a super nice staff, a great location, an excellent breakfast layout, and a great price. I would recommend this place to everyone who comes to stay in Austin.

title: “Ripped Off-Literally”
text: Stayed one night for business and paid $49 for parking my car to wind up with a medicore room with a dripping sink. The real annoyance came after checkout when I realized that although I locked up all my valuables in the glove compartment and only gave the valet key to the attendant, I neglected to remove the coin changer I keep completely stocked in the center console. Since I hadn't used any change since the day before when I stocked it and the only time the car was out of my control was when it was parked for $49 in the Westin garage, someone there helped themselves to a $1.30, figuring, I guess, that I wouldn't notice the small amount missing. Pretty sleazy for such an expensive place and a sad experience for one of Starwood's platinum guests.

title: “Great service, great location!”
text: Wanted to provide a review as I relied on tripadvisor in booking the Renaissance. Saw there were some less than stellar reviews, but booked anyway. Really glad I did. Front desk staff was amazing! Although I had apparently goofed up something when I tried to book online, the staff was able to get me the exact rooms (connecting) that I needed. There are 12 floors - the hotel is a square with an inner courtyard. We had inner rooms and could see down into the pool. The rooms are large & clean; the beds are very comfortable. Concierge lounge in on the 12th floor. Nice selection of food and is well-managed. We walked to the stadium for a ballgame, aquarium, ships at inner harbor. Everything was easy.

title: “Half the people are super helpful, half are rude and basically useless.”
text:
I recently stayed at this property with a wedding party. There were two major issues:
1st. The elevators smelled like a sewer. Every employee had the same line, " I dont smell anything" Although every guest of the hotel said it smelled like a sewer. 
 2nd. I had sent myself a package the day before I arrived at the hotel via overnight courrier. When I checked in to the hotel at 1:30pm I mentioned that I was expecting a package. the front desk staff told me that they would alert receiving and deliver the package to my room. I went to lunch and went to the front desk again at 3pm and asked if the package had arrived, I was told that it had not but that it would be delivered to my room when it did and that everyone knew about it. Okay I went to get dressed for the rehearsal dinner at 5 pm and was in my room until that time. At 5 pm I went back to the desk one more time before leaving for the evening and asked again. I returned to the property at 11 pm and went to the front desk to see if my package was there. They said that it was not and that the receiving office was closed and that I woudl have to check again at 7:30am. i went back to my room and tracked the package and found out that it was delivered at 1:50PM!!!!! 20 minutes after I had asked for it in the first place. I went back to the front desk and the lady there was completely rude to me said I could voice my complaint to the manager the next moring at 7:30am. I then went to the bar to meet the rest of the wedding party and told the story to the bartender. Amazingly, he picked up the phone and within 10 minutes my box was delivered to me at the bar. Matt, the bartender and Riley the manager that night earned major bonus points with me. The inept lady at the front desk shoud be fired as should the people who checked me in and everyone that I asked thereafter. Nothing like being blown off by the staff. Definately never stay at or recommend this place to anyone.

title: “A great place”
text: Seattle is expensive, so shop around on Hotels.com or Booking.com and definitely use Trip Advisor to review everything you’re looking at. After days of searching, I came across this place and I’m thrilled I did. First, it has free underground parking which is always a plus. It has great staff who are very friendly and happy to help point to great restaurants or things to do. It’s in a great location, right in the heart of the University area which means lots of different places to eat and public transit. The hotel has a pool but it isn’t located within the building, it’s about a block away. It has free wi-fi that is strong and that’s necessary for trip planning. The room we had was amazing…two big begs and a very cool separate space with a counter and bathroom. There was an extra sink outside the bathroom which is always helpful when you have three people in the room. Awesome Keurig coffee maker which makes fabu coffee and tea. We were on the sixth floor and the only noise you hear is sirens which are quite frequent. I slept through it but my partner didn’t. If you’re sensitive to noise, bring earplugs. The only negative we had with this hotel was that they didn’t tell us that the free shuttle to downtown should be pre-booked. So when we phoned down the next morning, they informed us that the next three hours of the shuttle bus was booked. Seriously? So they gave us bus directions which were wrong so we waited at a bus stop for 30 minutes before finding the actual bus that went downtown. So other than that, things were great. I’m sure the free shuttle would have been useful so book ahead. I would stay at this hotel again for sure.

title: “European style”
text:
Friendly front desk, clean room, comfy bed, nice towels and very close to the beach. I had a room with a Pacific Ocean view (if I looked out at an angle). The roof top for sunsets is a must and be prepared for the wind up there.
Ask for where the locals go to eat for more reasonable pricing -- you'll have to drive there or be prepared for a good walk.
I'll be going back and staying longer.

title: “Would Never Stay Here Again!”
text: I chose the Courtyard because I was intrigued by its listing on the National Registry of Historic Places. But apparently when the building was converted from a bank to a hotel, they didn't bother installing any additional sound proofing or insulation materials - which is completely insane considering that a House of Blues is located immediately next door! On a Saturday night (which is when I stayed), the noise and vibrations from whatever was going on in the venue was enough to wake the dead. The thumping went on until the wee hours of the night, and the next morning, a screaming toddler next door decided that nobody should sleep past 6:30am. On top of everything, the A/C unit in the room was loud, the plumbing was loud, the room was cramped, and the view out the window was pretty depressing (homeless people and tattoo parlors). The only good thing I can say about this place is that it is close to public transportation so you can get the hell out.

title: “Westin was wonderful!”
text: Just returned from a three day stay at the Westin Hotel in Charlotte. It was a wonderful experience! Our room was spacious, clean, and comfortable. All hotel personnel from the front desk to the bell captain were friendly and helpful. It was so convenient to the Convention Center and downtown restaurants. We can highly recommend this upscale hotel!

title: “Extended Stay Hotel - nice”
text:
I stood in Candlewood Hotel Polaris over a weekend in March - so just 2 nights. The hotel is very nicely located at the new Polaris Mall which is north of Columbus on the interstate to Cleveland. From the exit its less than one mile. Even though, the place way very quite - I at least did not hear the highway. The area is dominated of course by this wonderful nice new Mall with lots of restaurants and shops preaded around. 
Entering the hotel took me two rounds in my care around the hotel - because I was expecting a big entrance hall or such - but only a small door leads to the reception. Once there a friendly young lady checked me in, telling me that this is an extended stay place where you only receive service once a week. I didn't know that before, but it explains the small entrance hall. This was ok to me anyhow since I only stood there 2 nights. But you can obtain more fresh towls from the reception any time. And this explains to me why it is so cheep compared to other hotels in the area. 
The room itself has a small kitchenette but with a big fridge, a microwave and that was all I used - I also saw the stove, plates, mugs, galsses, the full story of a suite. So this is very nice if you really intend to stay there some what longer. I even saw signs taking of an indoor pool - which I didn't use but I saw the Gym which was at least not crowded. The rooms are nicely decorated and there is enough room. Everything looks modern well maintained and clean. No complains to this either. 
So the last statement - would I go there again: of course, its an inexpensive place with lots of annemities at a nice location.

title: “Would stay again”
text: Stayed one night December 16, 2012 for a quick holiday lights tour trip. Impressed with the hotel from the check in process, to check out. They held our bags in storage, even retrieved them when we needed more "layers" to sightsee, called the cellphone to advise when the room was ready and delivered the bags to the room. Room was clean, comfy and had a little kitchenette. 1 block off times square and convenient to everything, even the Gray busline tours! Perfect. Will definitely stay again!

title: “A little luxury for a long weekend”
text:
This was our first stay in a luxury hotel in the U.S. after staying in luxury hotels in Asia for a few years, so some expectations-adjustment on our part is probably in order. That being said, the St Regis Washington was a nice way to ease ourselves back into being Stateside, and we would certainly choose to stay at this hotel again.
We spent a long weekend at the property, with husband in town for meetings and wife and now-older kids for sightseeing. The hotel is well-located for the major sights and is housed in a stately historic property. Our room (which was ready for us) was beautifully decorated but not spacious, although city hotel rooms rarely are.
The excellent service makes this hotel a standout, as it always does at St Regis properties. The doormen were friendly, courteous and knowledgeable; the concierge efficient, professional and attentive with his follow-up calls to us regarding some arrangements. It was exceptional that the hotel managed to provide us with a peaceful stay with no lapses in service despite the numerous IMF receptions going on throughout the weekend (including one down the hall from us) and the requisite wedding.
The only disappointments were the absence of a bathtub (shower only), slippers, and day shades. Our room faced the street and our only lighting options were closing the heavy drapes to sunlight, or leaving them fully open to the building across the street. The typical white sheers behind the drapes would have been welcome.
Our visit was otherwise enjoyable and we certainly look forward to staying again.

title: “Design hotel very well located”
text: If you want to discover DC over a week end and dislikes standardized hotels lacking character then you can choose blindly the Helix. Close to Dupont circle and offering discounts outside of peak period, it is a safe bet.

title: “Never Stay Here”
text: PLEASE, DO NOT STAY HERE. The halls smell of Indian or Oriential food at all times. The staff is not helpfull at all. The Maintenance department is worthless. I stayed in this hotel for Buisness and regret it. The Wireless Web is non-exesistant and all of the rooms do not have wired web. If they do then it is as slow as dial up. In the first 2 days I was in 3 rooms. The first was size wise fine but the AC would not work. The Second was a Handicap room but no Web Access. The Third was room 1002. I dont know of a smaller room that I have ever stayed at in my entire life. You could barely walk around the bed. The Desk"table" was in a corner alcove opposite the dresser with the TV on top with enough room for a chair. You just couldnt sit in the chair. Glad I had a long ethernet cable to sit on the bed with my laptop. The shower had a nozzle that only sprayed you in the face. If you wanted to really rinse, you had better let it drip. The staff only had the "Authority" to give me a "10% Discount" on the first night. The manager whom I called later(2 weeks) offered another 20% on the first night only. This is not the first time I have stayed there, but it is certainly the last. My travel agent,who is a manager with STA Travel will spread the word within her organization to never book anyone there at all.

title: “Amazing pool, spa and workout facility”
text: This is a great hotel. It's not going to be some cool, trendy place to party at, but it is going to deliver on customer service and relaxation. The staff are super friendly and helpful. I wanted to go for a bike ride and they put me in touch with a shop that found me a bike, picked me up at the hotel and took me to the shop. The hotel kept my bike overnight and the shop picked it up the next day. Again, great service. I also found the workout facility to be top notch as I watched cheesy girl movies while doing the treadmill. Then, I took a warm dip in their heated pool while watching the lights of Austin twinkle from the rooftop. I also ordered a lot of room service, and the food was all quite tasty.

title: “Great value for your money”
text:
We chose this hotel as a result of other trip advisor ratings and were just thrilled!
Back Bay is the best location - close to everything.
Subway 10 mts from the door.
Close to Newbury Street with all the restaurants and shops.
Hotel is clean, staff are so friendly, rooms small with excellent double beds, and have everything you need. Exc bathrooms with hair dryers. Good air-conditioning in each room. Free tea/coffee served in reception every morning. Highly recommend.

title: “Great Value, Superb Location & history all around”
text:
Recently stayed at the Boston Park Plaza after finding a great deal on Bookit.com. I was very thrilled with the great rate I got but was nervous... Would this be too good to be true? When I arrived it was fantastic! Lobby is beautiful and busy. Check in was a breeze. Rooms are small but the hotel was built in the 1920's and I didn't need much room. I wasn't there to stay in the room all day anyway.
The location cannot be beat! Close to public garden, Newbury Street shops, the T train stop, tons of restaurants and the State house.
Also the upgrade to the tower level is worth the extra $$$,
Plus, I found great parking much cheaper than valet on Tremont next to PF Changs. $20 per night vs $44 from the hotel. 2 minute walk away.

title: “nice room, bad coffee”
text: Returning from Australia to Michigan, arrived at hotel mid-morning, a room was available and we were able to check in immediately. Bedding was comfortable, noise level was low, and the curtains blocked nearly all sunlight, perfect for recovery from trans-Pacific flight. Overall clean and tidy; could be improved with a microwave and a better coffee-maker (probably the worst in-room coffee ever). Shuttle was available when needed, though friends had longer-than-expected wait a few days earlier.

title: “By far my worst stay in NYC... or anywhere”
text:
I always spend a week in New york in early December and have had the pleasure of spending far too much money for decent hotels due to the holiday season. I expect to be "ripped-off" to a certain degree. However, my stay at the Hampton Inn Times Square was by far the worst hotel experience that I have ever had, and I travel often for work.
I'll start with the good:
- Location if you are interested in staying in the Theater district/Times Square area. Not ideal for shopping, but close to tourist attractions.
- Room size isn't typical NY tiny. It is average Hampton Inn sized.
That is it for the good.
The bad:
- The room was tired and of poor quality. Carpet itchy, bathroom icky, and bed not comfortable.
- Snooty front desk. Seriously, at the Hampton Inn? I love the typical, slightly gruff, get down to business NYC attitude, but at checkin the service was distracted, unorganized AND had an elitist attitude. They lost my reservation information. I had to re-pay for the room and wait a month for reimbursement for a pre-pay. And, no one was apologetic. They were also too busy to answer the two questions via phone when called. Why have a front desk?
- The breakfast was not even worth mentioning. A deal if you like cornflakes and bad coffee, but that is about it.
- Speaking of coffee. The supposed everlasting help-yourself coffee, was always out even during regular breakfast hours. The coffee is horrible if you are lucky enough to get a cup and the little counter was a serious mess of trash and spills all week long.
So, I maintained a positive attitude through the whole thing. Was always cordial to the service desk. I have worked in service and know it can be hard and customers can be demanding. I know that patience usually pays off. But the straw that broke the camel's back was:
I attempted to fed-ex some paperwork back home and asked whom I should leave it with upon check out. Again, the extremely rude staff acted like I was an idiot and told me to leave it at the bellman's table. Since no one was there and I was a little nervous about the important documents that I was next-daying, I tried to reconfirm that it was ok to leave there. Again shunned and told rudely, "it will be taken care of." Long story short - My package did not arrive for more than a month. I finally became irate with the hotel. No help was really offered although the concierge (who had been m.i.a. my whole week's stay) at least treated me with a little courtesy on the phone. The hotel had removed my shipping label and relabeled it with what they guessed was the correct airbill from another guest at the hotel. My label was brand new on a brand new never been shipped box? I don't know who could be idiot enough to make that error, and not even attempt to call the number on the package to verify if they thought it was a mistake? My package ended up with some very sweet mailroom clerks at a factory in the middle of nowhere that I had to personally track down. The hotel was zero help in getting my package back, even though they were 100% responsible for the error.
I would have given this hotel a 1.5 star maybe 2, until the fed ex issue. I wish I could give it zero now.
I would expect more for a hotel that I spent $65/night to stay in! I spent far more than that to stay at this unorganized, rude, uncomfortable and tired motel. 
Nightmare. Save yourself the headache and discomfort.

title: “Elegant but musty”
text: The staff was friendly and helpful. The afternoon wine and cookies at bedtime were a nice touch. I couldn't help but think I was staying at my grandmother's house. The musty odor (we were on the top floor) was reminescent of "ancient but clean". All in all, we thought the location was great. Our friends that traveled with us were disappointed that a king size bed was not available. Our friends are a little on the heavy side, so this was an issue. We found it within comfortable walking distance to many places. They offer a complimentary taxi voucher for early mornings. We used ours to take us to the wharf to begin an early day. We enjoyed the stay.

title: “Good convention hotel”
text:
Stayed at Hilton Garden Inn for 4 nights in July 2007 and have a somewhat mixed review. Was in Philadelphia for a Convention and the location was very convenient for that as it is located directly across from the Convention Center. 
Had no problems with check-in and every staff member that I encountered was friendly and helpful. We were in an ADA accessible room and it was very large. Bed was not very comfortable until I discovered the 2nd night that it was an adjustable firmness (a piece of information that would have been nice to have!) All rooms at the hotel have free wireless internet and a microwave and refrigerator (always nice when staying several nights). Nice toiletries and plenty of towels and hot water. Room was very clean (thanks to Quanda, our great housekeeping staff member). There is also a guest coin laundry, very nice so you don't have to pay hotel prices to have some clean underwear. Hotel is also convenient to historic sites about 6 blocks away. (take the Duck tour...lots of fun!)
Had breakfast at the upstairs restaurant one morning and it's nothing to write home about. Overpriced for what you get. A better option for food is the Reading Terminal market next door. It has tons of food stalls of every kind. I had a huge breakfast at the diner there for less than $7 including tip. Also great for lunch...has food of every ethnicity you can imagine...from Southern to Jewish deli to Asian to French crepes. The hotel is on the edge of Chinatown, so lots of options there. Maggliano's Little Italy by the Marriott is delicious. There's also Hard Rock Cafe around the corner.
The other downside is that the area around the hotel is somewhat seedy at night with lots of panhandlers and homeless wandering the street. Was awakened each night by sirens and street noise; not all night but was still there.
Would probably not stay here again if the Marriott across the street was available, but was okay for our convention purposes

title: “Perfect”
text:
We attended a wedding in Charlotte and stayed for one night. The check-in staff (Kate) were friendly and efficient. Daren, the shuttle driver, was quick to add that he would be glad to take us anywhere within a two mile radius--which includes all of the downtown area. Because of the excessive heat, we ate dinner at the hotel and the food was really good. John, the "proprietor" of the restaurant was friendly and came over to chat with us about the Redskins. The room was comfortable, good water pressure in the shower and the kitchen had everything we would have needed if we had cooked in. But the best part was the breakfast! No "powdered" eggs on their buffet--unbelievable selection of food and the staff all wore smiles on their faces.
GREAT place to stay.

title: “Large Convention Hotel in Need of Upgrade”
text:
The Hyatt Regency is a large, convention style hotel, that is located just off of Michigan Avenue in the midst of downtown Chicago.
The hotel is huge and there a multiple towers within the hotel complex. The first floor of the hotel has an open, casual restaurant and some sitting areas while the lobby is on the second floor. A bar called Big is on the second floor and had a neat vibe.
The room was decent. The bathroom was not grand or large but efficient. The bed was comfortable and was in the middle of the room with a large desk area behind it. The TV is HD. Large windows showed a nice view of the lake from my room. There was slight problem with the air conditioning and it did not keep the room cool enough most of the stay. 
The staff was great all around. 
Did not eat at the restaurants as there are amazing choices in downtown Chicago (a great meal at Shaw’s Crab House).
The workout facility was efficient and the machines seemed to be fairly new and in working order.
Overall, the hotel is getting old and is need of some upgrading. There are some better choices in the area (like the Fairmont around the corner) but if you can get a good price (we paid an average of about $150 per night) or have a convention in the hotel, it is fine.

title: “Loved the hotel”
text: We stayed there for 3 nights. Beautiful lobby and the people at the front desk were great. We paid for twin beds but got full size beds. The rooms were big enough and very clean. I enjoyed the restaurant and the bar. The location was wonderful. The only thing I had a complaint was the noise. We were on the street side and I could hear music and horns but most of the time too tried to care. I enjoyed the Gift shop, travel services and they booked your transporation to the airport. Great for the price and location is to die for. I also got to see Kevin Spacey when he was in the play just down from the hotel. He signed his autograph and got some good pictures. Will be back next year

title: “Charming gem at the airport...”
text:
When I booked this hotel using points, inwas not expecting much for one night before heading to Sedona. I knew hey had a pool, but not much else. 
When I arrived, it was midnight, so darkness covered the outdoor area, but I immediately noted the pleasant and modern lobby, and cool bar area. When we were walking to our room though, I did notice some nice seating where people were chilling by a fire pit which seemed very cool. Upon entering my room, I was even more surprised by the lovely suite, which was huge with living area and 2 doubles in the other room. 
In the morning, I was even more happy by the serene pool and outdoor patios, an the tasty room service at a great price.
After spending a few hours at this hotel, I was happy to say I would go back. My expectations were very well exceeded. 
4 on service because the fitness center was closed, but the staff had no idea. The shuttle was not totally convenient, with limited runs to and from the airport when I needed it. Also the room service menu was not updated with breakfast. Still, had a pleasant stay at this hotel.

title: “Nice, clean place. Great for those driving.”
text: Nice, clean and comfortable rooms. Free parking is good for those who drive. Location not exactly the most convenient.

title: “This Hotel is a Kip!”
text: Just back from a staying in the Pennsylania Hotel, and what a Kip (Dump) this is. We booked a "Superior Room" and had to move rooms after 5 mins. We got a somewhat better room, but it was still a Kip. Dark and dingy rooms, and the smell of damp was strong. So we just made the most of a bad thing. The staff never batted an eyelid at our complaint as I'm sure they heard it all before, it way like water of a duck's back to them. Never again will I stay in that kip and I'd strongly recommend you to stay away from it. On checking out, the staff never asked if we enjoyed our stay, or asked if we'd return to their "Hotel", because they know it's a Kip too.

title: “Solid Chelsea area hotel in NY”
text: Stayed at this Sheraton Four Points hotel recently on a trip to NYC for the US Open tennis. This is a 3.5 star solid, clean and comfortable hotel. We wanted to be close to Penn station (7 block walk) for easy trips out to the tennis center. It's a 20 min ride on the LIRR from Penn. The rooms were the usual small NYC size, but clean, great bed. Staff are very helpful and friendly. The area directly around the hotel is slightly sketchy at night. Great coffee/tea shop around the corner on 7th by 26th - Argo. Great spot for breakfast. The restaurant/bar at the hotel seems to be a separate business. They add a tip to the check for you so pay attention. After drinks with friends one evening I ended up paying 2 lots of 18%!! I did manage to get it changed when I checked out, but I'm sure not everyone notices, and the bar staff do not mention that they have added a tip/service charge for you.

title: “Stayed at this hotel to attend training at the worst Software Co. on Earth!”
text:
This is the corporate hotel for the worst Software company in the whole world. I stayed for training this year in February from Sunday through Friday. The hotel was pretty nice. I'm no longer with the Software company--thank you LORDY.
I was totally blown away as I came up the escalator from the street level and entered into the grand lobby. There are a million lights suspended from the top of the atrium; and it looked heavenly to me! One of the other victims (I mean trainees) told me that he spent his honey moon in this hotel back in the 70s and that it hadn't changed at all since then. He didn't realize it until he saw the suspended lights. Totally impressive?
I think the bed I slept in in my room, was also from the 70s! I have really never had a bad bed experience up until then--the bed was actually lop-sided. I didn't think it was that big of a deal at first, until after I went to sleep and realized I kept waking up because I was bracing myself in my sleep for the sensation of slipping out of bed.
As if the lobby was not stunning enough, my room offered views of the Bay Bridge, and the clock tower in terminal. Views were outstanding. Room as a little dated, but ok, except for the bed. Everything was withing walking distance, restaurants, offices, trains, trolley, bus, etc. Very outstanding location--the center of the action. Lobby bar made very good drinks--I had a few as I comtemplated the mistake I made signing up with this Software company.

title: “Maybe my expectations were a little high....”
text: Having read many accounts on this website and also the usual travel journals, i decided the W would be the ideal choice for a UK newbie tourist to NYC. As this is a $500 a night hotel, i was expecting a lot for my money, but I dont think we really got it. This hotel seemed more aimed towards the US business market and we couldnt help feeling fairly out of place. The bed was extremely comfortable, but in general the fittings were below par, already looking a little worn. Service was pretty ordinary, food and drink is overpriced even for New York, but I guess the demand to be seen here is quite high. The location was ok but I wouldn't choose to go back to this W hotel in the future.

title: “Trip to San Antonio March 25”
text: I enjoyed a nice stay at Drury Plaza Hotel Riverwalk. Upon check-in, the front desk clerk gave me an upgrade to a suite. I was on the 10th floor of the San Fernando Tower. The room must have been right in the middle, because the Cathedral was right in front. I could see a little of the riverwalk, and could see the boats when they went by. The room was very clean and comfortable. I attended a meeting on-site, and the room was a good size. Afternoon drinks and snacks were great, just had to wait alittle in line for drinks, but no problem. I only ate one breakfast, but there was plenty available. The access to the Riverwalk through the basement was nice. I would go back and stay again.

title: “Super clean and comfortable”
text: This is a moderately priced (for NYC) hotel that is spacious (again, for NYC), modern, and very clean. Our room featured high ceilings (14' or so), a full size bed, a desk, refrigerator and closet area. The room appeared recently renovated and the bathroom was big enough that we didn't feel cramped. There is free bottle-it-yourself water on each floor and a closet with extra soaps/shampoos/pillows/etc on each floor. Just a couple of blocks to the World Trade Center and close to the subway.

title: “Very good Courtyard property for business travel”
text:
I stayed here for about a week on business. The hotel is large and appeared to be recently renovated. The hotel staff was great on check in.
The rooms are large and comfy and had a fridge and microwave in room. 
The hotel is about 10-15 minutes from downtown and just a few minutes from the fancy Cherry Creek shopping area. The hotel has a good onsite restaurant and bar. I had dinner one night at the restuarant and it was great. There are multiple restaurants within walking distance of the hotel.
Overall this was a good hotel. If you are looking for something in downtown than this isn't the hotel for you. The hotel is located very close to the freeway for easy access.

title: “Not bad at all”
text: I spent 8 nights at the Omni when attending a conference in San Francisco. The hotel's location is fantastic, bang in the middle of town without some of the grime associated with Union Square. The public areas and reception are clean and smart. The room was comfortable and quiet (courtyard rooms are quiet but with a view of the neighbouring office block), but very plain - nothing in there to denote it as special in any way. The service, however, was very good indeed - bright and attentive staff at every level from housekeeping to management. Room service food was fantastic, although for the most part I got take-aways from neighbouring Chinatown. I'll certainly use the Omni again.

title: “Interesting hotel”
text:
When we went into our first room it was left uncleaned. The bed wasn't made and towels were on the floor. The staff was very friendly and quick to repond to this oversight on their part. Sometimes these things happen so I never sweat it.
 I was disappointed as a Priority Club Platinum member that I was not offered a room upgrade before or after the room incident. I did get a free drink voucher for the room not being done which helped to make up for the mistake.
 The hotel is awesome if like trains. It sits right next to the Amtrak Train Station. The entire hotel shakes when the trains pass by. You can spend all day looking around the hotels train related decorations.
 We had one of the most uncomfortable beds for a Crowne Plaza that we ever had. Not sure what the deal was, but for 2 nights we did not sleep very comfortable. 
 The attached restaurant was well worth the stop. I had no complaints with the food or with the service.
 We would stay here again if we were to visit Indianapolis again.

title: “Tiffany, a breath of fresh air!!!!”
text:
Once in a while you run across an employee so wonderful that you just have to share it.
We were working from 6am and got back to the hotel at 7pm Needless to say we were dragging tired and sleepy. We came to check in, we were Greeted by Tiffany's smiling face! She was cheerful, funny and so very sweet. She had our tired, worn out, beat up bodies Laughing and joking and gave us a second wind. We stay at a lot of hotels, it's not often we run into an employee like your Tiffany! What a breath of fresh air!!! Thank You Tiffany and Thank You Crowne Plaza for hiring such a delightful person! We will be back!!!!

title: “Lovely hotel in a GREAT location”
text:
We stayed at the Michelangelo to celebrate our 25th wedding anniversary. The hotel is in a great location, right in midtown, just a few minutes walk from everything you want in New York. Our room was upgraded for us on arrival, presumably because they knew it was a special occasion, and we had a 6th floor room overlooking 51st St.
We had no problems at all with facilities or room. The air-con is a bit noisy but you get used too it.
The concierge, James, was very helpful with ticket advise and flowers for the room.
Of the 7 hotels we have stayed at in the US this year , the Michelangelo was far and away the best.
I have no problem in recommending this hotel.

title: “Great Location”
text: We loved our stay here. The service and breakfast were good. We were pleased with our room, although not large it was very clean and comfortable. The location is so convenient to the sub way and has so many great restaurants and shops close by. It is close to the Hudson River and you can take a long walk along the River which is very pleasant.

title: “Perfect Chic New York Hotel”
text: This hotel is a great New York hotel. Enjoy the bar on the lobby floor and be sure to enjoy breakfast on the beautiful patio.

title: “You can easily do better”
text:
This hotel at first glance from it's website and ground floor appears to be a very good choice. However, once you get onto 3rd floors and higher, it's very apparent that the upkeep of hotel has been very poor. The first room I stayed at had the following problems:
-AC unit was blowing out cigarette odor despite being a non-smoking room
-Tile in bathroom was cracked and degrading
-Carpet in room was stained in several areas
-Free wi-fi was extremely slow
-TV was an CRT unit that had very poor picture quality and limited channel selection.
-Considerable street noise.
After being requested to be relocated to a second room, the following problems were noticed:
-AC unit was not blowing out cigarette odor BUT it was not able to cool the room either.
-Tile in bathroom floor was stilling broken in several areas.
-Carpet in the room was still stained in several areas with about six 6" black stains.
-Free wi-fi was again very slow...wasn't sure if Google would even load.
-TV was again an old CRT unit with same issues.
-Considerable street noise.
In addition to this, the gym offered on the 11th floor was practically falling apart and was not opened at its posted time. The 5-7PM happy hour selection (both free food and half price menu selection) was very limited. It is right next to a metro stop but being located in LA, there are plenty of metro rail and bus stops all over the city and most only being 5-10 minutes walk away.
Had they offered other incentives, such as 3 pieces of free laundry, complementary dinners and/or drinks, or other incentives...this would have made them more competitive against other hotels and motels.
So the take-away from this is: Only use this hotel when you can't find any other hotels or even motels to stay at, which should be very tough situation to get into. If I had a chance to do this again, I would have chosen a hotel with loyalty programs like Hilton or Holiday Inn chains.

title: “What a dump !!!!”
text: What ever you do DON'T stay here, unless you like roaches and hookers. Dont belive the picture on the net, they show a total different place. I stayed there one night and I had to sleep with the lights on because I thought I would be attacked by the roaches. The toilet stopped up the very first time I used it, it took me about 30 mins to check in. My room was on the fourth floor which means I had to take the elelavator. I did that once. This place is a dump avoid it at all cost unless your a pimp with W*****.

title: “Excellent location,easy to get to many sight seeing places and restaurants.”
text: We stayed at the Holiday Inn Select for one week in May 2010 including Memorial weekend. We had a most enjoyable stay, although at first reception had our dates mixed up but soon sorted everything out. The rooms were very comfortable and the pool on the fourth floor was a pleasant enterlude from our sightseeing. We did not have a car so used public transport, taxi cabs and organised tours which we arranged on arrival. The staff were very friendly and helpful, the breakfast,is excellent value for money. Internet is free. Lcation is second to none. The Hotel itself is old fashioned but having stayed at many a modern Hotel this one had character and would not hesitate to stop here again.

title: “Dated But Enjoyable”
text: Was a little hesitant in staying at this hotel due to some reviews I read prior to our trip. However, I found it to be as others had said. Definitely dated (Elvis' Rock Era) but in a nice way ! There could be some updates in the bathrooms for sure ~ they have seen better days. As I'm very fussy about clean rooms, I was a little worried.... no need. I felt very comfortable here. The staff was super ! Would definitely return.

title: “Very Nice Hotel”
text: This hotel rises up and stands out from all the other hotels in downtown Indy, with its blue glass and curving design. And from the moment we pulled up til the time we drove off all the staff were all very nice and helpful. The room my wife and I stayed in (for our wedding anniversary) was on the 32nd floor with a view of downtown Indy. It was the best view of downtown that I had ever experienced. She said the the view and room was very romantic. The room was just what we wanted... clean, quiet and very useable! We enjoyed our first stay at this beautiful hotel and we will be going back again!

title: “Excellent service at a steal of deal”
text:
We stayed there for three days and we loved the entire staff. They were very responsive to all of our requests. 
We did the breakfast package and I would highly recommend this package. The food from the National was outstanding.

title: “Hidden jewel in the Emerald City!”
text:
Happened upon this hotel while doing a last minute search online, and got a great rate on hotels.com. My husband and I were traveling with our 3 year old daughter and this place was great for her and us. The staff is very friendly, the food is amazing, the grounds are immaculate, the rooms are big and the decor is best described as modern chic. The included continental breakfast is truly continental with a Northwestern accent, not your typical disappointing American "Continental breakfast".
We loved this place and will return.

title: “BEST HOTEL!!! Incredible Service!”
text: I stayed at the Hilton Times Square over "Hurricane Irene" weekend. Although I was hesitant about the planned vacation, given the poor weather forecasting, the weekend turned out to be one of the best we have had. Our stay at the Hilton Times Square was truly amazing. The staff treated us like family, setting up movies for us to watch, and making sure any single need was met or worry was settled. In particular, Yaniv Packin, "Rooms Division Executive" was oustanding. He greeted us with such enthusiasm and made my family feel so safe, secure, and worry-free. There was truly a sense of control that I noticed here at the hotel - the staff were extremely attentive and supportive even though there was a natural disaster occurring right outside the doors. It is so nice to see a staff so dedicated to the guests during somewhat difficult times. I will definitely be coming back here to stay soon, hurricane or not!

title: “Very Nice, close to Splashtown”
text: My husband and I went to Splashtown and stayed at this hotel, it is located at the next exit past Splashtown so it was very conveniently located. The room was good sized, it was clean, and the bed was very comfortable, it had the ammenities you would want in a room: microwave, fridge, iron and ironing board, coffee maker and hair dryer. The dining area was nice, the hotel offered bacon and make your own waffles, cereals, breads, sweet rolls, fruits,etc. It would be nice if they offered eggs also. We had a good stay and i would recommend this hotel. They also have room safes which we ended up not using and the front desk lady (Barbara) kindly removed the charge when asked to without hesitation.

title: “Served Its Purpose Well”
text: We stayed here on a "Park, Sleep, Fly" deal where you can spend the night, take the hotel shuttle to the airport, and leave your car at the hotel. We flew out of Indianapolis to escape the high airfares in Cincinnati, and it was cheaper to stay at this hotel than to pay for the long term parking at the airport. This makes it a tremendous value. The hotel was nice, too! It is a basic hotel with large, clean rooms. We had two queen beds, but the room was not cramped. The shuttle service was very efficient. Someone called the day after I made the reservations to arrange a time for the shuttle to the airport, and on our return, the shuttle was at the airport within 15 minutes of our call. Although we left before the scheduled start of the breakfast, the staff had set out some muffins and such for us, which was appreciated. The only flaw was the air conditioner. It had been set so the fan would not run continuously to drown out the inevitable hotel noise. Therefore, the A/C would cycle on and off, quite loudly, all night long. I read that this Amana model of A/C can be controlled by the hotel, and it would be nice to allow the guests to run the fan if desired. Otherwise, this is a great place to stay if flying out of Indianapolis.

title: “Ft Worth hotel trhat takes care of cutting horse folks”
text:
This hotel treats us horsemen real well. The rate they give us with all the goodies that come with it . . . from the big breakfast to the program they've got of donating to our cutting horse foundation, it all swert for us. The breakfast lady always helops us out and the fornt desk team always seems to get it done.
So thanks from Bernie to you all. I'll be back for the stock show.

title: “Excellent hotel, good location & incredibly reasonably priced”
text: The hotel is gorgeous, the main lounge area was fabulous for a drink and the rooms were perfect. Took a wonderful trip with my siblings and we booked 2 rooms each with 2 beds AND 2 bathrooms. The extra bath in the room was priceless and I was extremely happy with the room rate, surprised actually. You're not right on the Mile, but you are literally down the street from Millennium Park and the Art Institute (great museum). You are actually situated in the middle of the Mile and all the museums. We had a fantastic time and I can't say enough about the hotel, wouldn't consider looking elsewhere for the next trip.

title: “Spacious room, close to Magnificent Mile”
text: Spent one night in transit in a spacious, air-conditioned room with about one hundred channels to choose between on the TV! The bathroom was clean and the beds allright. The staff was very helpful with printing of boardingcards and storing luggage before departure. And the location is fantastic, very close to the centre of town.
