The walk along Grand to the nearest station on the Blue Line for O'Hare airport is quite long, however. All in all, an affordable and recommended motel alternative in the centre of Chicago.

title: “Satisfied guests”
text: My mom and I stayed here last week in a room on the 10th floor facing Powell Street. We chose this hotel because my husband and I had stayed here about 7 years ago. The location is great. The rooms are very clean and comfortable. When we arrived, there was a box of chocolates and a bottle of wine waiting for us in the room (the wine in celebration of my mother's birthday). We ate breakfast in the hotel restaurant every morning. All of the staff were friendly and helpful. The rooms do not have A/C, but there is a ceiling fan and we found it more than adequate for the current temperatures. In fact, we turned it off at night because it was too cold. I highly recommend this hotel for people who want a clean, comfortable hotel in a great location.

title: “Outstanding Stay in Radisson Phoenix Hotel”
text:
My stay in this particular hotel was outstanding - they treated us well and greeted as as friends.
I did have a problem with my particulare Number bed and, bless the maintainence man's heart, but he couldn't get it fixed. So, he contacted the front desk and suggested we be assigned another room. No problem to us! We switched - but before the maintainence man left her checked both of the beds - worked just fine. Then he handed us each a coupon for a free breakfast the next day - UNBELEIVEABLE and not needed, honestly. The entire staf was FANTASTIC and yes, we would stay there again.
Billie Snell

title: “Not Worth the $$”
text:
I have to agree with all the reviews here. Not being familiar with the layout of Seattle, I assumed this hotel was close to Downtown. Its about 5 blocks or so. Not a problem, as the curtious front desk woman called us a taxi. 
 The rooms needed to be renovated, as they just didn't seem modern and fresh. I didn't like the bathroom either but it wasn't bad.
 The breakfast bar was wonderful, no complaints. I agree with the elevator comments, I was pretty sure we were going to get stuck in there, but we didn't.
 There are no close restaurants so we ordered in, which was fun and not a problem. 
 I didn't have any problems with this hotel, its just not as classy as the others in the area. I didn't book this one for my second trip.
 By the way, the rate is too pricey for this hotel but that's Seattle.

title: “ok for the price”
text: The room was spacious and nice view of the neighborhood. No in room coffee is a drag and poor water pressure in the shower. Upon check in they failed to let me know that the carpet was being replaced on the entire floor I was on. I had to dodge the floor layers, glue and debris which would not affected my stay had they just notified me prior or given me the option to stay on another floor.

title: “If your company isn't paying, go elsewhere”
text: Stayed at the Marriott Waterfront while in Baltimore on business. Good location relative to waterfront activities. Unremarkable room. Botched room service. Attitude from the front desk. For the $375/night I expected much more. No comparison to the Marriotts I've stayed in in NY, DC and other big cities.

title: “our new go-to hotel in Manhattan!”
text: Absolutely great experience.. our suite had the view that everyone coming to the city wants! across to the East River, down to the Statue of LIberty. NIcely furnished, (flat screens in both the living room and the bedroom!) and very accommodating staff (asked for a Keurig and they put one in the suite before I got there.. nice service.) The Tick Tock diner was great for a fast breakfast; they even had Irish bacon ! Tried the "finer" dining restaurant in the hotel and that wasn't half bad either... the mussels, in fact, were some of the best I ever had and they were unlimited. This is our new hotel for NYC stays.

title: “Poor value for the money”
text: The location is great, but the hotel is old and uncomfortable. The service can be a bit rude or a bit sleazy - typical for New York, but something you don't expect in expensive hotels. The restaurant in the hotel is pretentious and has a nice view of the Central Park, but the food and the chef are quite average. There are a lot of hidden charges - expect to pay a lot more than what you see on the websites or what the reservation people tell you. The place is definitely NOT one of those warm places where one wants to return.

title: “Much better choices out there!”
text:
My husband and I tried this hotel for 1 night, as a staycation. Location is ok. Staff are friendly but not very intelligent and move slowly.
Our in room safe did not work and no one in the hotel could fix it.
Our breakfast was served with plastic silverware and no napkins, because they ran out (and restaurant was not nearly even full!). Kind of strange.
Beds are ok, pillows small. Loud toilet made noise all night. Didn't sleep well at all.
I wouldn't stay here again, it wasn't repulsive but there are better choices!!

title: “Boutique Hotel within view of the Capital”
text:
We chose this hotel because we wanted to see the National Art Gallery and sculpture garden, among other museums on the mall. This is as close as you can get--but nothing can be reached without walking at least a few blocks so pack good walking shoes. When you exit the hotel and look left you see the capital building about two (long)blocks away, and the mall begins to the right of that. Hotel is a few blocks from union station and metro, half a mile walk to heart of chinatown and several blocks to several nice upscale restaurants. There is a very extensive cafe and take out catty corner to hotel was cheap easy alternative for breakfast, lunch or snack. Got a great deal for a 4 star hotel on name your own price, but beware as the parking is VERY EXPENSIVE. 
This is a modern, european style hotel popular with foreign travelers. Very busy when we were there for cherry blossoms, but staff were friendly and efficient. Lobby rolled into comfortable seating and modern bar and restaurant with outdoor seating and lovely tables and glassware. Would have sat there and had a cocktail but there was a private party and hostess told us we might have to move inside in a short time so we went elsewhere. Great pillow menu--choose from 6 different types of pillow (including metallic, memory foam, and an herbal one!!!). Sabrina in guest services was a hoot, with a sweet southern accent and great banter, and sent me up two kinds to try. The king bed was great--wonderful mattress, bedding, and lots of pillows. Coffee pods in room were european blends and full-bodied--a nice touch. Decor was eclectic mix of modern stark with grey walls, patterned artwork and a zebra pillow on the lounge/sofa. The light in the bathroom had a motion sensor and turned on when you walked in, but required pushing a button to turn it off (a good thing, preventing turning off on you at an inopportune moment). Just wish the light was brighter in the bathroom and vanity (a pet peeve of ours--you need more when putting in contacts, shaving or--for my wife--applying makeup).
Concierge was as sweet and helpful as could be, and recommended several good restaurants in area and had menus for most of them. Was honest about hearsay vs. firsthand knowledge. We chose a not fancy but authentic thai restaurant on 6th street near chinatown that we enjoyed. However, parts of that area were run down and my wife wouldn't have felt safe walking alone at night. 
Overall was great location for sight seeing--especially this end of the mall (there were bus tours that stopped near hotel for further points), but if you're looking for easy wallking for night life stay in georgetown and use the metro or buses for sightseeing during the day. This was a great deal when booked through name your own price. If you want to save money, find somewhere else to park ($48 a day) and eat at cafe catty corner to hotel for breakfast and snacks.

title: “Good stay at the Parc 55”
text:
This was our second visit to the hotel in 2+ years and on arrival Michael was as attentive and helpful as ever and importantly, knowledgeable of what is going on in the city.
Check in was quick and as before, we stayed in a Club level room on 33rd floor which was clean and tidy. Shortly after arrival Housekeeping knocked the door to ensure we had everything we required, which was considerate and a nice touch.
The two Queen sized beds were comfortable but note are similar to UK double bed size, not King. View out over the city was excellent with Giants stadium to our right, Alcatraz island just visible to our left, Union Square is 5-10 mins walk and Powell Street turnaround is just round the corner. 
However, even though we were high up in the building you can still hear police sirens during the night as street noise funnels up between the high rise buildings. Also, as the hotel is in the financial quarter/slightly downtown of the city there are a number of homeless/down and outs wandering around. These did not cause us any problems but may be unsettling to those who are less well travelled or of a nervous disposition.
Club breakfast is continental style/reasonable, with cereals, cold meats etc. and the three staff present could not have been more attentive in finding English tea for us!
The hotel reception area is spacious and has several pieces of nice, decorative artwork around. Overall, we enoyed our stay at the Parc 55 which was comparable to our previous visit there.

title: “Wonderful view, wonderful place, wonderful people!”
text:
I live in upstate NY and decided to get away for a couple of days over the Labor Day weekend. We wanted to stay someplace on the ocean and we have two dogs, and found it's really hard to find someplace right on the beach that pets are allowed. So we decided to look at Boston because it's on the ocean and we though we might take a ferry ride (we learned that the Harbor Cruises do allow pets on the sightseeing tours). I was going to stay at the Residence Inn Tudor Wharf, which as a Marriott rewards member I knew would be consistent and good as usual. But it appeared to be a bit more on the river, and since we usually order take-out because of the dogs, we really wanted a room with the view.
I had been searching hotels in Boston and kept coming back to the Boston Harbor Hotel, but wasn't sure I wanted to spend the money for it. When I looked at their web site, I couldn't help but call the hotel to see what they might have available. The night before we were going, I was fortunate enough to speak to Debbie, one of the managers, who was extremely helpful and was able to give me a great rate in a Harborview room. I decided then that I would pamper myself and my husband, because we had been working really hard lately! Was I ever glad I did!!!
From the moment we arrived at the hotel, I would say SERVICE is the first word I could say about the hotel, and that word continued throughout our stay. I'm amazed at hotels like this where the people get to know your names, and even the names of our dogs as we took them in and out. When we got into our room though, I heard my husband say "Wow!" as he looked at the view. We were on the 8th floor which had an amazing view of the harbor and we could see the ocean beyond. I felt as though I could just sit there looking! But there was one glitch - the room we were in didn't have windows that opened, and I knew that some did, even if every so slightly, and I wanted to be able to hear the sounds of the harbor! Never fear - I called the front desk and they said there was an identical room right next door, and they moved us immediately. 
That night we ordered dinner from their more casual restaurant and my husband said it was the best clam chowder he ever had. I had also inquired about staying a third night with Debbie, and she sent me a nice note back saying she would extend the rate. She was working at night so I never did get to meet her, but based on our phone conversations and notes, I felt like I knew her, or at least I knew that she was taking care of us as a guest.
The decor was beautiful, and the housekeeping staff was great as well as the bellhops, just everyone! We also both were able to use the pool, which is huge, and the whirlpool which was the best I was ever in (really hot and big). My husband also sprung for the deep tissue massage that was really something. It's so easy to get to the spa, you just take the elevator straight down without having to walk around the hotel in your swimsuit - that was a little plus I really liked. 
Finally, the location is really nice.....very central to everything, including the wonderful new greenway that was marvelous for walking the dogs, but not as busy and crazy as the scene down by the Marriott LongWharf where we took the cruise. On the cruise I was able to see the location of the Residence Inn, and it looked very nice, but not like the view from the Boston Harbor Hotel. 
Now I'm spoiled - if I ever go to Boston again, I'm going to want to splurge for this hotel!!! I can't recommend it enough.

title: “A special treat and moving experience”
text: When I enter this establishment, I feel like I am stepping into hallowed ground. The first obvious difference from any other hotel in this area are the displays commemorating the proud history of the US Marine Corps; if you are lucky, you may be greeted by two bulldogs wearing Marine uniforms, or the pup who has already outgrown his first uniform. The third floor hallways have extensive bios displayed for every commandant since the Revolutionary War. The 11th floor has a memorial to all Marines who have given their lives defending the country. On every floor there are tributes to the sacrifices and accomplishments of the Marine Corps throughout their history. On this trip, a small plaque caught my attention; it had the names of six 15-16 year old Marines killed in action in several different wars. I increase my knowledge of and appreciation for the Marine Corps on every visit. There is a superb gym with every conceivable piece of workout equipment in the basement, including a serious three lane lap pool. The top floor houses the superb Leatherneck Grill with breathtaking views of San Francisco, great breakfast buffet, delicious dinners (had the rack of lamb this time), and outstanding service(!). I am not a Marine but I believe everyone should spend some time perusing the displays and increasing their awareness and appreciation for this great branch of the military. The arrangement of the rooms make you feel more like you are staying in someone's very comfortable home than in some kind of commercial property. I suspect that all of this great hospitality and service is attributable to a staff truly dedicated to the mission of maintaining this tribute to the Marine Corps and their members; it starts with the "landlord", Major General Myatt, USMC (ret.) who served in two wars. I highly recommend this hotel experience!

title: “Never again!”
text: I decided to unwind and get away for one day at a really nice place. This is not the place! We were told we could check in an hour early and got in an hour and 30 minutes late. TV wouldn't work and told "working on it". We had to check with desk 3 times to get it fixed. I wanted a cold soda but no machine except for gift shop. I found a note on the door that said "gone to lunch back at 6:40 (25 min later). Really? They can't staff a gift shop? The room is hot and smell of Clorox is so pungent that my eyes are watering. I'll take a Marriott or something where you get a small fridge, etc. This is sadly disappointing.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: This was my first time in Chicago staying for 4 nights. This is a lovely "boutique" type hotel with friendly and courteous staff. The bed was huge and very comfortable but I am glad that I had a room at the rear of the building as the train is really close! The location is great it was easy to walk to many of the main attractions. As a solo traveller staying on business it was perfect. I fell in love with Chicago and would be happy to stay at the Silversmith again.

title: “A great experience - will go back for sure!”
text:
Location, location - this hotel is a mere couple blocks from the harbour National Aquarium, down Pratt Street from the Ravens' and Orioles' home parks. Beautiful building, supremely friendly staff (front desk, valet and security) made for a great first impression. The room itself was a decent size, the bathroom was pristine - I didn't like the rainfall showerhead much but my wife absolutely loved it... and for those who dislike hotel bath tubs, they did away with it - replacing it with a modern walk-in shower. Very cool. Large LCD television and a more than comfortable bed iced it for us.
We didn't get much of a view because we were on the first floor, but there was zero noise from the outside or the hallway. We weren't there to gaze out the window and the convenience of being down the hall and around the corner from the front desk and valet service was great.
Valet service is second to none - $30/day isn't all that bad and as others point out, if you want it, in/out service is possible with 15 minutes' advance notice. I saved a HUGE amount by booking through name your price on Priceline.com but wouldn't have been disappointed paying full-pop to stay here. The convenience of location, availability and friendliness from the staff and all in all, a perfect stay.
We will be back in the area sooner than later as we were only in town for two days, and we'll be going back to this hotel without a doubt. In fact, we'd consider staying here while visiting nearby Washington DC in the future - it's only 40 minutes away and a very nice drive.

title: “Great hotel in not-so-great area”
text:
Once you get inside this hotel, you "feel" safe regarding the surrounding area! The staff makes you feel welcome and the rooms have a new feel to them. The only problems we encountered was that one of the rooms had a toilet that wouldn't stop running water once you flushed it and the shower had no shower curtain! We called the front desk and they sent someone to fix the problems within a decent amount of time.
If you have to stay near the airport, then this hotel will probably do the job just fine. If you need to eat at nearby restaurants - there aren't any. There is a hotel restaurant, but we didn't try it.

title: “I don't know if I would stay again...”
text:
We stayed for 3 nights, and while it's not the most glamorous spot, we had the priveledge of staying while Julie, the desk clerk worked. I work for an expensive, 4 star, luxury hotel in Seattle, and to be honest, thats where Julie should be. She was super friendly, great with directions, places to go, she even helped me fix my jeans! ( And believe me, I needed my jeans!)
The room was mostly clean, but housekeeping missed some "gentlemans personal items" which my mother and I disposed of. Not cool. Also there was still a bud light in the mini fridge when we arrived.
Blood stain on the sheet, also not cool.
Hot breakfast was alright, we liked the Texas shaped waffles.
If management sees this, I hope they will give Julie a raise, as she's the reason we didn't leave.

title: “Well located April 2007”
text: We visited this hotel in 2007. Its just off of Times Square so its not as noisey. We was in a part of the hotel which was in the hotel! We got upgraded and not sure why or how, but the premier room we had was lovely. We had continental breakfast in our exclusive lounge and afternoon snacks n drinks eveyday thru to the early part of the evening which was great. We only got a cab once as we walked eveywhere. As long as you have a decent map then walking is easy. The only time i felt uneasy was on saturday night in times square there seemed to be alot of young men in groups but never ever saw any trouble. Central park is lovely and had a fun carriage ride around with a lovely irish man. Did not do a show on broadway but did a few bars instead! Done all the tourist attractions but would recommend going up empire state of an evening as the view is fab. Found a diner that done a foot long hotdog Heaven haha! A great place and will go again in next few years.

title: “Great location, lovely lobby with old world charm”
text: The Roosevelt is a lovely hotel in what I think is a perfect location. It is close to the theater district and midtown, yet it is quieter than most hotels in the area. A well-equipped fitness center is important to me and the Roosevelt has it- machines, free weights, water and even fresh fruit. The room was small but had everything I needed and in NYC, you don't really spend a lot of time in the room.

title: “Great location, facilities, attentive staff, Really 5 star”
text: We had a great experience from the polite and pleasant car valet service to the efficient reception, the good value restaurant and excellent housekeeping. Really clean suite with little touches like fresh ice each day . The views from the roof are spectacular. I was impressed by the staff everyone asked if we were ok or needed anything. We really felt the staff cared and it was reflected in the overall high standard

title: “Hampton Inn on Beale did not disappoint”
text:
My husband and I traveled to Memphis August 15 - 19, and decided to stay at the Hampton Inn, based on all the great reviews. The hotel did not disappoint. The location was a block from Beale and was close to the free shuttle to Graceland, Sun Studio and Main Street. We stayed in a suite, which was great, because it had the living room/kitchen, along with the separate bedroom area. 
Breakfast in the morning was great. There are enough selections that everyone should be able to find something to eat that they like. There was also coffee and tea available in the lobby anytime, day or night, plus a little store, where you can purchase drinks, snacks, etc. Although, like any hotel, they are pricey, but you pay for convenience.
The rooms are very clean and are cleaned promptly. We have experienced terrible maid service at other hotels, but this was top notch. One of my biggest complaints, is you typically are not provided with enough towels. This was not the case at the Hampton Inn.
We did not use the pool or jacuzzi, so I can't speak to this, but it looked nice. It is a bit small. I did use the gym, which is also a bit small, but has adequate equipment.
The staff were very accommodating. If we needed directions, suggestions on where to eat, or assistance in scheduling a taxi, they were very quick to assist, and always did it professionally.
In numerous reviews, I did read that the noise from downtown is loud in the evening. This is true. The music starts mid-afternoon and goes until the early morning, so if you're a light sleeper, this is probably not the place for you. My husband and I actually took a sleeping aid every night, so we could fall asleep. The hotel itself was very quiet. We did not experience noise in the hallways or adjoining rooms at any time during our stay.
In the future, if we decide to return to Memphis, we will definitely be staying at the Hampton Inn.

title: “"Bachelorette Bash 2008 6/25-6/29"”
text:
We had an awesome time. The hotel is beautiful, very clean and welcoming. Rooms are spacious (dbl/dbl suite) and I loved the decor. It is only a 15 minute ride from DCA airport ($20 taxi ride). The food in the restaurant was delicious and the happy hour over the top with the jazz and drink specials (loved the pomegranate mimosas) . 
Staff: Robert, Abhi & Mamadu at the desk were very cordial and great ambassadors for DC. Very helpful with places to go and how to get there. The doormen Zack & Efrim were always polite and willing to get us a taxi. Tiffani & Dan helped me coordinate a bachelorette luncheon in the dining room. It went very well. Last but not least Marcello was great-he made us feel so special and obliged to make just about any drink we could think of.
The hotel is wonderful and close to Georgetown shopping just up M ST about 3 miles. There are restaurants, CVS's, cigar shops, palm reading and jazz clubs within walking distance. We had a an awesome stay.
I would definitely recommend the St. Gregory and will stay here again and again.

title: “Beautiful hotel with lots of glitches”
text:
Started off on a VERY BAD note. I travel frequently and am a light sleeper, so have learned to ask for a room on a high floor away from the elevators. Made the request when booked on the hotel web site. Called the morning of check-in and repeated the request. Arrived tired from a day of traveling and was given a pre-assigned room on the lowest possible floor, street side, directly across from the elevator. After much discussion and being told there were no other rooms available, I was given one on the 7th floor away from the elevators. Bit confusing as it appeared there was only one other person staying on the same floor.
Wet used washcloth still hanging in the shower when I walked in - made me question the cleanliness of the room. Room was beautiful. Shower was spacious, but sink and counter felt cramped for one person - don't know how two would share. Due to negotiations for location, I guess I was in a "non-standard" room - but word to the wise, this king size room did NOT have a sleeper sofa as was advertised on the web site. Also, hotels.com advertised that the rooms had bathrobes and minifridges - wrong. Bed very comfortable.
AC is VERY LOUD. I liked the white noise - helped me sleep - but I can see how it would be annoying to some. AC went out one of the nights throughout the hotel, but was fixed when I returned from work the next afternoon.
Package rate included breakfast. Went down the first day - about 30 mins after scheduled opening. Cook came out and apologized as the wait staff had yet to show up. He didn't know where the menus were, but offered to make me whatever I wanted. By the last morning, the restaurant manager was visibly present and making people happy, so it looks like they're making an effort.
Tried using the fitness center. Lowceilings - felt like a dungeon. The cardio machines don't have individual TVs - three TVs are mounted on the walls. Tried to change the channel on the TV in front of me, and the other two turn on and change channels. Luckily no one else was working out. Didn't use it again.
Had a newspaper delivered to my door 2 of the 5 days I was there. They're at the front desk, so I'd pick one up there if the delivery failed.
Housekeeping restocked the single use coffee 3 of the 5 days I was there. Called the front desk when I returned in the evening and they promptly brought up coffee.
Shampoos/lotions only restocked once during the stay - they did have mouthwash which was a nice touch (had it been restocked more often).
Wi-Fi was flawless and free. Location is great.
Overall, beautiful hotel with so much potential, but management has a lot of work ahead of them before I'll stay again.

title: “Great attitude from all staff”
text:
I appreciated the friendly, accomodating attitude from all of the staff....front desk, restaurant and house keeping. I requested a quiet room on the 4th floor and my request was honored. I also had a late flight on departure day so they extended my check out time. I sat in the front desk area waiting for the rest of my family one day and observed that the staff was supportive of every guest who made a request. So nice to see the consistency of service. My room was clean. The bed was very comfortable with a nice
pillow top mattress and best of all, the bedding was double sheeted so I did not have to
have any considerations about how recently the "bedspread" had been laundered.
I had a nice conversation with one of the staff about how well the company takes care
of their employees. It definitely translates to good customer service.

title: “Excellent hotel with superior service.”
text: Fix the drapes in room 1120 so they are all attaached. It was still functional just looked off. Add mouthwash to room supplies.

title: “Best Hotel and would love to stay there again!”
text: The hotel was wonderful. The staff was very helpful and friendly. They made our stay stress free. When I was checking in a young boy came into the lobby and had gotten too hot outside. The front desk staff immediately got him water and cold towels and took great care of him. The hotel was very clean and modern with a beautiful pool and patio with a fireplace. We stayed in a king suite that was the perfect size with 2 t.v.s. and more than enough space. I would highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Fabulous Hotel and Location in Chicago”
text: What a wonderful surprise we got when we booked this hotel from a quick look online! Our stay here was fantastic. While not for the faint of pocketbook, if you are seeking elegance. quiet and a great location, you should be quite happy here. This is a new Waldorf (used to be the Elysian) and the brand new renovation throughout has been gorgeously done. The lobby and room decor were beautiful. Service rivaled the best we've experienced anywhere. This is a "no tipping" hotel, which was hard for us to get used to, but the friendly, helpful staff lived up to the promise and tips were always refused (with a thank you and a smile). Upon arrival, we were offered an upgrade for a slight upcharge to an apartment-style suite on the 18th floor with two exposures, a large living room with gas fireplace, balcony, and 1 and 1/2 baths. The upgrade was well worth the additional cost. The one-bedroom suite was massive, very nicely furnished, with ample closets (3) and drawer space. There was a wet bar complete with its own refrigerated bin full of ice cubes, a nice touch. The master bathroom was fantastic too, with an enormous frosted glass-enclosed shower, double sinks and soaking tub. When I phoned the hotel staff to inquire about printing out boarding passes for our flight home, all I had to do was supply some flight details and, within minutes, the board passes were slipped under our door. We found the Waldorf to be perfectly located for shopping and restaurants. The hotel's entrance is tucked away with its own private courtyard driveway entrance, making dropoff easy and cabs were always at the ready. Just steps away there is also a Starbucks and a Walgreens, a nice convenience. This hotel really sparkled during our stay. We hope it continues to do so. Five stars and two thumbs up.

title: “Location the only good”
text: Last week my wife and i visited NYC and our expirince in this hotel was not the best .with 4 nigth you have a breakfast coupon .but the only that they serving were coffee and muffing that not a breakfast .also the security personals were too rough .the check in /out line always has many people .To be honest the hotel has very good location to me that the only good.

title: “Friendly and very Helpful!”
text: As soon i arrived at this locationFirst thing i noticed that staff is "Friendly and very Helpful". i was very pleased to see that facility is newly renovated and soooooo clean. i would recommed everybody to stay here and enjoy it.

title: “great location, use AAA discount, near streetcar transportion,small bathrrom”
text:
over great location for all the tourist. Few blocks from Fisherman's Wharf, a 7-eleven (to pick up water for the hotel), a convenient "F streetcar" station (I could see the stop from my room) where for $2/person will drop you off right in front of pier 33 for alcatraz tour, Ferry Building, Union Square, to name just a few of the most common places. Staff very helpful. free to print boarding pass in "business center", I used AAA discount and got rooms for about $30/night cheaper. I'm 5'6, 140# and found the bathroom kinda of small. Also, because the street car stop was right outside my window, I could hear it at night, I think it runs till like 1AM. If you are a light sleeper, you might consider requesting room not facing the streetcar stop. 
Transportation: I took taxi from the SFO (san francisco airport), $50 before tips. supershuttle was around $17/person. When leaving hotel for airport, I found several shuttles advertisements in tourist books (including the one given at hotel) for only $11/person to the airport. Much cheaper, I used it and it was fine. Found 3 companies advertised in tourist pamphlets:
I would give it a try because these are smaller companies vs supershuttle so you are unlikely I would think to have a full shuttle leaving the airport. 1)415-822-2648 “SF City Shuttle Service” ($11 with coupon, $14 without), was the one I used and had no problems. 415-255-4899 ($11 w/o coupon was what I saw advertised), 415-202-0733 (advertised $11 with the coupon so I don't know how much they charge without it)

title: “Surviving Sandy”
text:
We arrived in NYC on Sunday 28th Oct, just before Sandy. I had booked this hotel after reading the reviews on Trip Advisor. It turned out to be a great decision as not only was it an excellent hotel, it had power throughout the storm. I cannot fault anything with our stay and found the staff to be very helpful, cheerful and professional. As the cruise we were joining was unable to get to NYC and we were unable to leave, the hotel let us stay an extra night at the same rate when they were turning people away who needed accommodation due to the storm.
The breakfast was excellent as was the wine and nibbles in the comfortable lounge.
This is a superb hotel and will recommend it to all our friends. I just need to go back to NYC to do all the things I was unable to do because of Sandy!

title: “Old World Charm”
text:
As other reviews state, this is an older hotel; however, I like the fact someone thought to save as much of the original flavor as possible. Our room was on the 17th floor--a two-room suite. There were many amenities: in-room coffee, many toiletries, the Sleep Number bed. Our room was very clean, the towels were clean and smelled fresh. Yes, the wallpaper is outdated but this is not a $300+ per night hotel, either. The staff was friendly and the breakfast was good. The scrambled eggs were hot, fresh fruit, cereal, bagels, toast, danish, good coffee and juice. No meat--but I don't eat meat anyhow. 
To those who complain about noise--you are in a big city. Ambulances run, fire trucks run--they are meant to be loud so people get out of the way. And being in a big city--they get a lot of calls. I heard emergency vehicles and some hall noise but nothing that kept me awake or woke me up in the middle of the night. 
The location was very convenient to Camden Yards and the Inner Harbor. If you're looking for a good hotel based on price--this one is good. I was not disappointed.

title: “Good value, Good location”
text:
We chose this hotel for its price and location and certainly were not disappointed. If anything it exceeded our expectations given what we paid and the price of hotels in New York.
Our room was clean and functional with quite a small bathroom but fine for our needs.
There was also a safe free of charge.
Location - this would be hard to beat for the Times Square/theatre area. It takes less than five minutes to walk there and also very good for 5th avenue shopping. There is a subway station directly opposite.
Breakfast - this was typical for a hotel of this sort and perfectly nice. Quite busy at peak times.
The staff were all very friendly and helpful and after three weeks touring we came back and spent our last night there.

title: “Such high hopes, such a big letdown”
text: This was to be the highlight of a quick tour of the South. However, it was a big disappointment as I found the hotel dark, worn and uninviting. With the reputation on the line you would think that this hotel would be snappy, bright, cheery and alot of fun. Breakfast was acceptable but disposable dishes were a bit cheap. If you're desperate to be near Graceland it will have to do. I was going back with a group of friends in April but have since moved into downtown Memphis (15 minutes from HH) to be near decent restaurants and alot more nightlife and activities.

title: “Cheerful Service”
text: My family and I stayed 4 nights at this hotel while attending a conference in Dallas. I was greeted cheerfully at reception when we arrived, and when they noticed we were travelling with young children, they gave us a unit away from the main expressway. The rooms were clean when we arrived, and were kept clean throughout our stay. The cleaning lady left a personal greeting for when we arrived, and left additional personal notes during our stay. She also cleaned dirty dishes that we left in the sink. The front staff provided us with a couple of services for free, when they very well could have charged us. We would definitely stay here again if we were to travel to Dallas in the future.

title: “Great Anniversary Memories”
text: We stayed at the Drake to celebrate our 20th anniversary December 27 - 29. Having stayed for our honeymoon, and on many occasions since, there was no doubt about where to stay this year. A junior suite with executive floor privileges was the start of a great stay. The hotel is as beautiful as ever, with some recent renovations obvious. Our only disappointment was that the room was somewhat worn looking, and the bathroom very small for a suite. Also, lack of wi-fi in rooms was inconvenient. Otherwise, another great visit to a truly "Grand " Hotel!

title: “Great Hotel”
text: We had a wonderful stay. My children loved the beautiful pool and the staff could not have been nicer. It was a great family trip and we loved the Four Seasons! Stay Here!

title: “Just keeps getting better”
text: I continue to use HGI Phoenix Airport over all the other places in the Phoenix area, for so many reasons but the most important from day one they treat you as faimly and that is not one person its a awesome staff. As many times I have stayed here I witnessed first hand this. It can be a one time stay or many your treatment is always outstanding. The morning staff in the dining room starts your day off and always willing to help you get your breakfast to start the day of bright. I would specifically acknowledge Mike in the front office, Richard and Domica at the registration desk, Cassandra in the dining room. All of them (and the entire team) do a great job providing professional and courteous service. Thanks for making me feel like part of your family.

title: “New York Charm”
text: We stayed at The Barclay for one night. The room was gorgeous, the hotel is very nice in general. Our bathroom was too small, though, more appropriate for a 2-3 star hotel, and worst of all, gunk was up into the sink, making it utterly disgusting. When I complained to the management about it, they apologized and offered us free buffet breakfast. The location of the hotel is spectacular.

title: “Great Stay”
text:
This hotel was very clean, most convenient to both bus and subway stops. A full breakfast is included. The employees were helpful. Would have given it five stars, but due to one of our two rooms not being ready until more than two hours after check in time I gave it only four.
Management did adjust our first night's bill for that room for one night.
Believe you will find this hotel will meet most all of your needs.

title: “Not impressed for a Sheraton property. OLD property in need of updating”
text: For the price and the Sheraton name, i was not impressed. It's an older converted property that needs more updating. Convienient to the airport. Shuttle was slow. Beds were OK, good pillows. OK work area with good chair, but NO plugs nearby. Moderate road noise. bathroom was updated and was decent, had flat screen TV. Noisey AC unit. Overall an OK property, but the Sheraton name calls for higher standards than this and the nightly rate was no bargin.

title: “Good quality for our money”
text: We had read the reviews and decided to try the hotel. We ended up with $ 129 pr night for a regular king and free parking, as an AAA special for 3 day weekend. (They accepted my Euopean AAA sister org.) Arriving they asked it a double bed with a balcony was ok, and we accepted that and got a room on the 9th floor. Not much street noise that high. The the bathroom was relatively bigger than the bed room, but the room was ok for a big city and had a fridge to keep our water cold. We enjoyed the cheap martinis one afternoon and had the 17.95 brunch on Sunday with a basket of sweet muffins, an entree + dessert and all you want of either bloody marys, champagne or mimosas. Our Slovenian waiter was not the most experienced, but provided us with 2x2 free esspressos when we had him agree with us that most American coffee isn't strong enough. (Sorry, European tastebud here). The food was good, but I guess one needs to have a few glasses of the booze before the price is really good..

title: “Nice room, good rate, central location, helpful staff”
text:
I stayed here with my wife for two nights over 4th of July weekend. Our room was on the 12th floor facing south. It was right across from the elevator, which initially gave me pause, but the sound insulation was good enough and the bed was on the far side of the room so we weren't disturbed.
The room was a good size with king size bed, large flat panel tv, big windows to let in the light, and dark curtains to keep it out. There was also a small frig with typically overpriced mini-bar plus an iron/ironing board in the closet. The marble bathroom was spacious and clean with plenty of towels, soap, shampoos, etc. as well as a small coffee maker with a few varieties of coffee and tea. Shower was roomy and strong.
The location is VERY central, only 1 short block from Independence Hall and 2 blocks from the Liberty Bell. There are numerous restaurants of a wide variety of prices and flavors within easy walking distance. The concierge/front desk staff were particularly helpful recommending excellent places for brunch and dinner.
The hotel doesn't have on-site parking, but there is a garage right around the corner which charged us $27/night (it was $34/night through the hotel's valet parking service). The subway is only two blocks away if you want to venture further afield, and taxis seemed pretty available although we walked everywhere. They do prominently feature their spa, but we didn't try it out.
All in all this is hotel is pretty much what you should expect from a 4-star city-center hotel. It's an older building, though not without it's charms, and didn't seem to have a lot of common space, but we never intended to spend a lot of time at the hotel anyway. For under $200/night it's pretty competitive.

title: “Should be a 2 star hotel”
text:
I arrived with my partner after a long journey from London, tired and tattered, looking forward to relaxing and settling into NY.
Checking in was speedy and efficient. When I entered our room I was shocked, the room was very, very small (I know space is at a premium in NY but this was $520 per night), dark and dirty looking, no views whatsoever, tiny bathroom with no work/ storage surfaces, no mini bar, no tea & coffee facilities, 3 coathangers and a large ugly box tv that took up most of the space in the room. 
Within a minute of being in the room and seeing the state of the place, I rang down and requested a room change. I was given another room,. Agan unsatisfactory, same as before, shocking!. Again I requested another room change. I was shown two more, and settled for the one that had the better bathroom, a decent sized workspace for putting toiletries on. Still this room was inadequate for a 4 star hotel. The air vents very thick with grime, the towels worn, tired and dirty. 
I have stayed in Hyatt hotels before in London and Belgium and found them to be first class. The grand Hyatt NY is a blot on their portfolio and I would never stay there again. I wish I had read the reviews on this website before checking in.

title: “Worth every penny!”
text:
Stayed 2 nghts on the 4th of July wknd. Checked in late and thought we were gonna get the leftover rooms but they upgraded us to a premier rm on the 16th floor. Breathtaking views of downtown SD and only occasional sounds of sirens. Rooms were very clean and very ornate old world charm. Loved the lil room separating the shower/toilet area from the bdrm. Great quiet area to get ready while kids are still sleeping.;) 
Great location! Will definitely stay again! $32 for valet parking and $15 for facilities fee per day but ok if you go in knowing.

title: “Omni Austin Southpark enjoyable”
text:
Our weekend visit in Austin at the Omni Austin Southlake has been really relaxed and enjoyable. We were greeted at the front door by artfully arranged flowers and low sitting couches arranged for comfortable conversation and visiting with friends or colleagues. While this is one of the older properties for the Omni, it was impeccably maintained and tastefully decorated.
The valet was pleasant, helpful and prompt and the front desk staff while harried checking in a streaming abundance of guests, remained composed and kind, answering several questions and guests with a smile and useful info. 
We had requested a quiet room in the back of the property and they placed us in a lovely corner room on the 9th floor with a small balcony, perfect for enjoying morning coffee. We were well away from the road noise and the room itself was roomy and pleasant, and really quiet.
We are Select Guest Members and had coffee in the room (do sign up for membership before you come to any of the Omni properties since it is a free membership and there are privileges that go with it, such as coffee in the room and complimentary water on arrival - though they did forget our waters - we came prepared for the extreme Texas temps).
The hotel itsel is well situated for traveling about Austin, though we both recommend using the service road as often as possible since it really does make for the easy off/on exits and avoidance of heavy travel during rush hour, like most cities.
The restaurant here unfortunately had poor reviews, negating its onsite convenience, so we hopped on the service road traveling south and found a large number of restaurants conveniently located within 2 miles such as McDonalds, Taco Canbana, WhataBurger, Macaroni Grill, and an unexpected Indian delight off of the William Cannon exit to the right, Asiana Indian cuisine, in a little strip mall with fantastic chicken tikka Marsala for me and amazing butter chicken for the hubby.
For the shoppers, treasures await in this delightful southern capital, and if you enjoy bargains be sure to hit Round Rock premier outlet mall, always popular.
For sightseers, Austin is filled with music, art and a plethora of choices for exploration, check with the concierge or front desk staff for options during your stay - there are fantastic bike trails and athletic pursuits for the more athletically inclined.
We look forward to a peaceful, relaxing and fun filled weekend in one of our favorite Texan cities, despite the crazy August heat (if you are here during the hottest month of the year as we are, just plan ahead, lots and lots of water, sunscreen and cute hats we purchased during our last trip here, and you are set). 
There is also a lovely pool downstairs, speaking of crazy heat here in August, if you enjoy the water and want a cooling swim or enjoying reclining poolside. At 5 pm on a Friday afternoon, there were relaxed and quiet sun worshippers with room for additional guests.

title: “Perfect Location; awesome accommodations”
text: We stayed at the Holiday Inn Riverwalk for two nights over the New Years Eve weekend. Upon arrival, check-in was a breeze. After parking our car in the on-site parking garage, we were a little confused as to which elevator to take to our rooms. A hotel employee, James, saw us and immediately helped us to the correct elevator. Sales & Marketing Director Andy Hearon could not have been more gracious or accommodating.

title: “We won't stay here again”
text:
If you’re looking for a comfortable bed and a hot shower, then this might be okay for you. There were pros and cons, the price was great, but overall, we’ll look for a different hotel next time.
Problems: We reserved a suite with one queen and 1 sofa bed, for 2 adults, 2 children. We confirmed when checking in that our 2 children would be sleeping on the sofa bed. It was late, we were tired and wanting to get to sleep. In the room, we discovered there were no linens or pillows for the sofa bed and only two towels in the bathroom. It took a lot of time and multiple trips for the night manager to find sheets, pillows, pillow cases, and two more towels. The room was set for 1-2 people, and it seemed to require a lot of effort for them to dig up what they needed for the sofa bed, and they were not prepared, even though we had told them when we reserved, and again when we checked in.
Wifi – we arrived on Wednesday, with a work laptop, intending to do some work that night, Thursday and Friday. We called and confirmed on Tuesday that they had wifi in the rooms, as it says on their website. When we couldn’t get it to work Wed night and called, they told us that the wifi was not working, and they hoped it would be fixed on Friday. Not acceptable. If they had told us when we checked in it was not working, we would have found a different hotel, but by that time, we had just spent a lot of time finally getting everything for the sofa bed, and unpacking. No sense of urgency regarding wifi from the management, and they seemed to think that because they had a computer in the lobby, we should be fine. We didn’t need to google a restaurant - we needed to get on a vpn with our own laptop. The mgmt needs to be more diligent on this, and should have had a technician out there as soon as the problem was discovered. It was finally working on Friday.
The room and the linens did appear clean, but the linens were in seriously bad shape. Literally holes and otherwise worn and threadbare, stained including what looked like blood on the white comforter. Towels were very worn on the edges. They are not spending money to replace items when they should. The toilet paper was so cheap, it disintegrated when you tried to use it. The alarm clock in the room didn’t work, but they did replace it when asked – they had to search other hotel rooms to find one. The exercise room – the two pieces of equipment were both broken. You could use the elliptical with no resistance only. Treadmill had an out of order sign. The hot tub next to the pool was hot but the jets did not work. We did not request a handicapped room, but were given one. That was fine, but it was next to the office where the manager goes in and out using a heavy door, all night long, waking us up constantly. There were no counters in the bathroom – it’s one big room with toilet, sink, tub/shower. We had to put toiletries on the floor. There isn’t even really a ledge to set items on around the tub. There is no soft lighting or lamps anywhere in the room – all bright fluorescent light fixtures. The sofa bed slanted up, but at least the up part was at the head, and the kids didn’t seem to mind.
Good: Free breakfast was actually better than expected. No protein, but the waffle maker was nice, fruit, muffins, bagels, cream cheese, cereal, milk, OJ. The “kitchen” area in the suite – small fridge, microwave, cabinets – was very nice and helpful. Air conditioner worked fine, the queen bed was comfortable. The location is very convenient to the freeway and restaurants. Recent release family movies shown in the evenings, easy parking.

title: “Good for the money”
text:
We had a good stay at the Lucerne. The staff was very attentive, but I knew more than they did about Metro passes and the airport check-in than they did by studying on the internet.
The room was quite large and nicely decorated. There was a problem with towels/ashtray/coffee replenishment. 
The in-room coffee maker was a lifesaver although there are coffee shops available on every corner in NYC. The computer in the conference room was free for 1/2 hour per day. The in-room web TV is $10/day. The rooftop deck was closed for renovation, and it would have been nice if it had been open as that was one reason I picked the Lucerne.
Plenty of reasonably priced restaurants within waking distance. I would stay there again.

title: “enjoyed our stay”
text: I stayed at this hotel for 3 nights in mid Oct. I got $209 per night weekend rate which I think it was a pretty good deal by its location. The hotel seems got remodeled recently. I like the new room décor, much better than the one I saw two years ago. I gave it 8 out of 10 score.

title: “Great spot and lovely staff!”
text:
The Brentwood is a great little Inn in a residential area. This is not a fancy place but it has a certain chicness with good attention to detail. The person who booked us in was very helpful printing off maps and recommendations for meals. The breakfast was a simple affair but very good quality-loved the charming little courtyard with a water feature to pacify the weary soul!
We found the area safe and pleasant to walk around in (restaurants are a good 15 min walk away but down a nice plant lined neighbourhood)
This area is good for Hollywood and the beaches and we travelled and parked ok everywhere (albeit at a cost at Venice beach).
We loved the place and will definately stay on our next visit!

title: “The Price was exceptional for the size of the room, and the view i received was Spectacular!!”
text: My boyfriend and I were EXTREMLEY satisfied with our recent stay at the Wyndham Hotel located in San Jose. The Staff was entirely helpful in answering all of my questions and concerns. The minute I arrived they didn’t hesitate to make me feel very welcome and I was just blown away by their outstanding customer service! Virginia, The women at the front desk set me up with a Beautiful room on the 7th floor overlooking downtown San Jose. I honestly couldn't have asked for a better room, the view I received was spectacular!! I was very pleased with her professionalism and warm-friendly attitude. At other hotels I've stayed at cleanliness has always been an issue for me but I was shocked with how well the hotel presented itself. I liked how I was given the option to have my sheets and towels changed daily instead of at the end of my visit. The Best part was how reasonable the price of my stay cost. Some might be fooled into thinking its very pricey because the atmosphere was very upscale compared to other hotels ive stayed at. Another GREAT aspect to The Wyndham Hotel is the restaurant located in the lobby area. After a wonderful night of rest my boyfriend and I requested to receive a wake up call around 9 a.m. The Call came on time as they promised but we didn’t have a lot of time to drive around looking for a Denny’s so we decided to eat at the breakfast buffet downstairs. We LOVED it!! As we entered the Host made sure to well inform us with every bit of information we needed to know. I was also very fascinated with how on top of it the waiters were. Besides the delicious food the location was extremely convenient for us. And let me also add that there was no long lines or confusing menus to deal with so it was very time consuming. I was very pleased with my overall stay at the wyndham hotel and I would suggest it to anyone interested in an upscale hotel at an affordable price. I do plan on returning very soon!!

title: “Another Wonderful Experience at Elan, LA”
text:
Six months after my initial visit to Cedars-Sinai, I returned for a week of follow-up tests and stayed again at Elan. I was welcomed by very professional, friendly and caring staff. My room was lovely: very clean, king size bed, flat screen TV, free WiFi computer access, room safe, mini bar, beautiful patio view, etc. 
During my stay I frequented the daily continental breakfast bar and the nightly wine and cheese reception. I had so much fun meeting guests from far and near also attending these activities. After receiving medical "good news", I celebrated that evening during the wine and cheese reception with guests who were now new friends.
This time I explored the Beverly Center, Melrose Ave and other interesting areas. If I needed a cab and knew ahead of time, the staff had one waiting for me. The area is delightful and safe for walks and I took many. There are also a variety of eateries nearby.
I plan to return in a year and have already made reservations to stay at Elan. It is a lovely boutique hotel and I recommend it highly.

title: “Beware...What a dissappointment”
text: We had reservations for 4 nights and we checked out at 6:15 am following the first night’s stay. If you require more than 2 hours sleep per night this hotel is not for you. Beds were extremely uncomfortable, a brick platform would have been a improvement. The room’s windows are not insulated and the street noise was constant. I now realize why the Hotel web photos only show the bathroom sink. The sink takes up a fourth of the total bathroom sq. footage. Hotel does not have a ice machine and charges for internet connection. Upon check-out and after I had expressed my discontent, the clerk informed me that there would be a $50.00 early departure fee. After a brief discussion the fee was waived. The location of the hotel is accommodating. Strongly recommend staying elsewhere.

title: “Great Value”
text:
We stayed here one night on our way home from gc. 
Very clean room, plenty of space - pull out couch in separate room. The bed was very comfortable. The room had 2 flat screen tvs.
Many pools to choose from - it was very hot, so we used the pool at night, it was perfect. - separate adult pool w/bar.
The staff was very nice. When I called to confirm my reservation, the operator noticed that there was a special and reduced our rate to $99 - very good deal for this very comfortable room.

title: “As expected.”
text:
If this hotel were anything but excellent, I would be disgusted considering the price. But I was very pleased with the hotel. Staff was exceptional. Everyone was pleasant and helpful. Was there for a business meeting, so didn't get to do much within the hotel. (no spa or fitness center) 
Location is very nice. Right near the mall. Not convenient to restaurants or nightlife.

title: “So So experience”
text:
I booked to stay here for family vacation in June. The hotel was located in a fairly good location within 10-15 minute walk to the subway near Dupont Circle. The area felt clean and quite safe but there were not much restaurants or shops around.
The lobby has lots of character and as the name implied had a 1920s feel. Although because of the red color, felt a bit dark in the hallway.
I felt the room was OK, it lacked a microwave or fridge despite what the lady over the phone said. It was available for a fee of some $25/night. I mean, for that price over the 4 days, you can buy a cheapo at Walmart and throw it out after your stay. My room had a funny door that was locked with a big mirror propped up against it to hide it. Rather weird. The staff was so-so, not terribly friendly or helpful when we tried to get directions though. The bed was comfy but I felt the big pillow needed a good cleaning. The hotel also needs to provide more soap/shampoo/body wash. Of the few days I was there, they never replenished anything.
Overall it was average.

title: “A beautiful, historic hotel right in the heart of Austin”
text: You feel like you're stepping back in time at this lovely, history-filled hotel. Top notch service from the moment you enter until you check out. The on-site restaurant serves delicious cuisine for every appetite! This hotel has many ammenities not found in other hotels we've stayed.

title: “It's Fine”
text:
I stayed here for one night on business, checked in late form the airport, but checkin was polite and efficient. The room was spacious, clean and well appointed. Overall, a little bit tired, but not dirty. There was ample space with a king sized bed, desk and chair and a separate soft chair. The hotel had complimentary wifi which I always appreciate. There's a pub adjoining the hotel which I had no opportunity to use, but they use this for breakfast in the mornings. That said, it didn't open until 9:00am the morning I was there so I walked forty yards down the street to a very nice little coffe shop called Macarons and had my coffee and muffin there.
I've read mixed reviews about this hotel, but it was well placed for where I needed to be on business, it was clean and had everything I needed so I would use it again if back in the same area of New York on business. Price wise, it wasn't off the scale either.
I believe it's not the most convenient location if you are holidaying in NY and doing touristy stuff and I'm not sure I'd want to stay a week here if I was on holiday, but if you are coming to New York on holiday and are on a budget, then this hotel is fine. My three stars is a little on the harsh side, but without a pool, you can't really give it four can you?

title: “Attentive, friendly staff-great service!”
text: We brought our women's basketball team to a tournament in San Diego and were given Collin Kallman's name for the host hotel. He was terrific in setting up our accomodations, even rooms for family and friends. When we arrived, check-in was smooth and the staff very helpful and friendly. Anything we needed was provided quickly and with a smile. The team had a great time, and we plan to return again next year!

title: “One night stay in a corner room”
text:
Overnight on a business stay. Got a room on the 33rd floor. Got in early and was hopeful for a room...alas it was not ready. The desk clerk was most apologetic and gracious, as was was the bell captain who held my bag till 530 when I returned. Room was a corner, and was very spacious by NY standards. It was clean, as was the bathroom, which had plenty of towels (a bit rough). Nice looking TV but the resolution of the picture was terrible. 
Bed was a bit too hard for my taste, and the pillows didn't have much fluff in them. But the shower was great, and there was plenty of counter space on the sink. Closet was adequate. Great if you are looking for a moderate hotel close to times square. I would return!!

title: “Premium Service is the Standard”
text: Although this trip was for business, staying here was a pure pleasure. The staff was incredibly friendly and helpful, even after I checked out, they helped me with my needs to see the sites downtown. The room was over-the-top clean, food excellent, staff superior; what more do I need to say?

title: “Better than I expected”
text:
I stayed at this motel from 7/11 - 7/16 2012 for Comic-Con. I was wary of it based on some negative reviews, but I was pleasantly surprised. Check in was easy, and they let us add a day to the end of our stay at a discounted rate. 
The room was clean and included a mini fridge and coffee maker. We had the queen suite, which includes a bedroom and a separate living area with a pull out sofa. It included two full bathrooms, both with showers. I showered at different times each morning and always had plenty of hot water. 
I was apprehensive about using the pullout sofa so I brought a blowup twin mattress, and there was plenty of space for it. The only kind of gross thing was that there were a couple of hairs in the obviously otherwise clean pillowcases - I attributed these to belonging to the housekeeping staff. We asked for more linens and got them within 20 minutes.
The room entrances are all outside off the parking lot, but I never felt unsafe as others have mentioned. The door had two secure locks which I used, but I never saw anyone hanging around during my stay that made me feel nervous about security. I did not hear excessive noise, but then again I sleep with ear plugs, so who knows. Nothing noticeable while I was awake. 
The washers and dryers were nice to have - you will need quarters and there is no change machine. The pool looked nice although I did not use it. The on-site diner-type restaurant was a little pricey, but the food was good. Room service is available until 10PM.
All in all it was a pleasant stay. I would not stay there again for Comic-Con, as I realized it would be more convenient to stay downtown, but in general it's a fine motel in a good location.

title: “Dirty and not up to Westin standards”
text:
Apart from the views, this is a very disappointing hotel. My room was dirty (see attached photo of someone else's hair all over the toilet tank and towels) - I checked in at around 11pm, so was in no mood to have housekeeping come at that hour to take care of it. Reception seemed indifferent when I told them about the situation the next morning upon checkout. 
There is only one option for breakfast, which is really surprising in a hotel of this size and in this location. It's a fast service cafeteria. As far as I could tell, there was no table service. Not a venue where you'd want to hold a breakfast business meeting.
As a Starwood Platiunum Preferred Guest member, I have come to expect reasonably high standard from the Westin properties I've stayed at. This one just doesn't cut the mustard.

title: “Great location, great customer service”
text: Excellent stay. They were able to accomodate a VERY early check in. There was some construction going on outside the room, but it was a trade off as we were happy to get in after a long redeye from the west coast. Concierge was great - restaurant recommendation was excellent (Giacomo's Boston). Hotel location is superb.

title: “Wonderful hotel, but there were "buts"”
text:
A great hotel, but…
My wife and I travelled with our baby to this hotel, and I specifically called twice before our arrival to ensure the staff placed a crib and made room in the mini refrigerator for the storage of formula. It didn't happen, we had to wait a while to get the crib, and no one ever came to our room to make room in the refrigerator.
Also, through no fault of the hotel, someone had smoked in the original room that we occupied. To my dismay, they tried to move us to a smaller room, and eventually they made arrangements for a room the same size as the original room. This process took almost two hours, not good after a 7 hour drive from DC, and a cranky baby on our hands.
With all that said, and besides these initial glitches in service, I still have to say this is a great hotel. The staff was very warm and friendly, the room was large and beautiful, and the location superb. It is located on the upper east side of Manhattan, away from the hustle and bustle of the busiest locations there. In a sense, it was an oasis of sorts. It is only a half block from Central Park, with great access to Madison and 5th Avenues, the Metropolitan Museum of Art and the American Museum of Natural History. 
I would stay at this hotel again and recommend it to others.

title: “Nice resort, close to great shopping”
text:
The Ballantyne Hotel & Lodge Charlotte, North Carolina
http://www.theballantynehotel.com/ 
The Ballantyne Hotel & Lodge (one of Starwood Luxury Collection) is located just 20 minutes from Charlotte-Douglas Airport and downtown Charlotte. This place is an ideal venue for meetings, weddings and social occasions. 
The hotel includes an 18-hole golf course, Gallery Restaurant and Spa, complete with a fitness facility with personal training classes and indoor and outdoor pools. The hotel also offers wine tastings of the finest wines bi-monthly on Saturdays at 6pm throughout the summer in Gallery Bar.
The hotel is within 18 miles of downtown Charlotte and the SouthPark Mall (my favourite shopping place) featuring Neiman Marcus, Tiffany, Nordstrom, etc.

title: “Top notch service”
text: This upscale Hyatt property strikes me as a cross between an Andaz and a Park Hyatt. Indeed, with some more upscale atrwork and finishes it would fit right in with other Park Hyatts. Ultra friendly staff. Beautifully appointed with an excellent restaurant Urbane and servers like Jen (& a kick butt happy hour) A block from the light rail from the airport. They've got it all.

title: “Not LIke it Once Was - A Disappointment”
text:
What a difference a year or so makes. I thought this was one fabulous hotel in the past. I could not believe how it has changed for the worse. This leads me to believe that the management staff has changed.
My room had a wire hanger on the floor along with some paper itmes - housekeeping had neglected to look anywhere but the obvious places as this was near the lamp table and a bit hidden. Having stuff that wasn't mine on the floor did not make me happy. The unit itself appeared well taken care of otherwise. The room was well equipped and the bathroom was well supplied and clean.
Check-in wasn't all that pleasant as the man checking us in appeared annoyed but I did get him to smile at the end. We received a card for breakfast (which we did not need) but the hours of breakfast were not mentioned.
Our room was quiet which we appreciated. Unfortunately neither of us could sleep -- not quite sure why that happened. I did not find the bed all that comfortable so that could be part of the problem.
The evening reception was weak. Last time we stayed they had an elaborate spread of food and this time popcorn, pretzel and chex mix and some crackers and ?tuna dip. There was a wonderful gentleman who came around and asked us if we wanted a drink and then brought them - don't know his name but he was previously the banquet manager. The bartender seemed to be having an off evening, too, as he didn't engage much with the guests and surely did not smile.
Breakfast had lots of items as usual. Food quality itself was terrible compared to last visit. I ate nary a bite. We also had dinner in the restaurant and it wasn't very good either. Last year the food was exceptional. Don't know if they changed cooks or what.
Not sure that I would stay here again as there are so many hotels in the area and I'm sure one of them exceeds this one.

title: “Salima D”
text: I have stayed at this location several times, the W is my favorite place to stay. Mainly because the staff make the stay memorable, they could not have been more attentive. Derron the doorman went above and beyond during my last stay in December. My family that joined me during the trip could not of been more impressed with the service. The moment we arrived Derron welcomed all of us and made us feel special and this continued during our entire stay. Great location - would definitely book again as always.... great service!!!

title: “Disappointed”
text: This hotel has such great reviews that I was sure it was going to be fantastic. To my disappointment, it was average at best. I made reservations months in advance for a room with a kitchen for my husband and I and our 2 dogs. When I called to confirm, they told me there were no rooms with kitchens available. OK... so we had a smaller room. The parking IS free, but the cars are so crammed in that it's next to impossible to get in and out. But my biggest complaint is the NOISE! There were noisy cars in the courtyard, paper thin walls, and a noisy staircases with people going up and down all night. Needless to say, none of us got much sleep. It is difficult to find a hotel that accepts pets, and they were very accommodating. But I just don't think this hotel deserves the raves that others' have given it.

title: “Great deal for the $$”
text:
Stayed mid week for about 120$/night. Staff was helpful. Great location and decent bar.
Rooms are small but clean. I had one (?queen/double) bed and that was enough for 1 person. Would definitely come back if the $$ is right.

title: “Amazing time”
text: I was there for nine days and it felt like home because of how warm and friendly the staff was. They were always helpful and made the experience incredible. Two members of the staff that really stood out were Amanda and Kim. They were consistently doing best job they could to help in any way and it was really refreshing.

title: “Comfortable, excellent location, great staff”
text: Excellent place to stay for Bass Hall events. Staff is wonderful. Valet--only parking is an significant (surprise!) expense until you figure out how to get into the public parking garage around the corner.

title: “Terrible hotel”
text:
I would strongly suggest finding another hotel. As soon as we got there we stood at the front desk and the lady in the lobby stood there looking at us until i finally greeted her. Then they had no communication with hotels.com, where i booked the room. The woman had no idea we had a reservation even after i provided her with the confirmation numbers and papers that i had printed out.
 They finally gave us a room. We took the scary and ancient elevator to the sixth floor. This elevator is the slowest elevator i have ever seen. The halls are narrow and dirty looking. The room was smaller than any hotel room i have ever been in. I could barely get out of bed on the side of the bed because the walls are right there. You had better be small for this room. The shower had problems too. The hot water handle became scalding hot while in use and burned my wife's hand when she turned it off. She warned me so that i uses a rag to turn it off. There was also scalding hot water leaking out of the handle so if you do choose this hotel, please watch your kids in the bathroom.
 There is absolutely no view of anything other than a brick wall. I would expect to pay about $39/night for this type of hotel. I know it is new york and everything but it was horrible. At least my wife and i have something to joke about now.

title: “Customer Service came through”
text: I posted the review, "Nice staff, but this hotel is simply not clean." After several attempts to get a response beyond a form letter from corporate, the general manager's office at this location has agreed to refund me the cost of my stay which is absolutely wonderful and deeply appreciated. The money is important, but it's the willingness to take responsibility that really changes my attitude. Thank you, Westin Times Square.

title: “This is great large hotel in one of the finest cities in the world.”
text: The staff bend over backwards to help the guests at this world-class hotel.

title: “Fantastic Stay!”
text: My wife and I just returned from 6 days and 5 nights at the San Diego Marriott Marquis. What a tremendous stay! The property has an excellent location near Seaport Village and the Gaslamp District. We had a balcony room in the north tower with a fantastic view of the bay and the Coronado Bay Bridge. The property is well maintained in all regards and the personnel were quite friendly. It was a bit chilly at night, so the many fire pits came in quite handy. Tequila's, the outside bar, was a wonderful venue with excellent customer service. There was live entertainment on Friday and Saturday night. We can't wait to stay here again.

title: “A bit of the strip in Motor City”
text: Designed much like a higher end LasVegas hotel, this hotel has some glamour going for it. It's a nice hotel, beautiful rooms.... but extremely pricey. We stayed here 3 years ago for a weekend getaway and it was beautiful. We noticed with this trip that the furnishings are beginning to show their wear, and though the rooms are still beautiful $300+/night doesn't quite fit.

title: “Physical hotel good. Staff clueless”
text:
Hotel has had a 6 million dollar renovation. It is quite nice. Sheraton sleep sweet beds very good.
Cinnamon Restaurant. Good quality food, friendly service. very reasoanle prices.
Ok to the clueless Front Desk Staff...............
I arrived at noon. I realise check in is at 3pm. Most hotels will at least look to see if a room is available early and if not offer to store your Luggage for you. The lady at the Front Desk did not even look and told me to return at 3pm.
I return at 3pm. First set of keys I am given. I enter the room there is a poor guy sleeping in the bed. I apoligize to the guy and return to the Front Desk.
Front Desk Clerk informs me there are no more King Beds even though I am Guaranteed a King non smoking with my reservation. I cannot be bothered to argue. I go to room number 2 and the room is not cleaned and someones Luggage is in the room still.
I go to room number 3 and discover it is 2 double beds. I am not happy at all but cannot be bothered to argue as I am tired.
I then try to retrieve my bags. I hand the Front Desk Clerk my 2 Luggage claim tickets and ask her to please page the Bellman. She informs me that the Bellman has left for the day. I find this strange as in Sheratons there is usually Luggage assitance from 8am -11pm at least. I inform her I do not need assitance but I need to retrieve my bags. She walks me into a storage closet and makes me retrieve my own bags. Not good. This is supposed to be a secure area.
Cannot believe this hotel has no Concierge. The Front Desk staff do not know any restaurants, ditto the Bellman. I asked the Front Desk manager for directions to the St Regis Hotel the next day. This is another Starwood property. He did not know and had to ask someone else. Surely the hotel should have a Concierge who is knowledgeable of the area.
Next day maintenance knocks on my door at 9am to paint the door even though I have a do not disturb sign on my door.

title: “HORRIBLE DO NOT GO HERE!!”
text: I went to NYC with my older sister for a fun weekend away. We did not expect to stay somewhere nice but this was just terrible! The line for check in was out the door-i felt like I was in an airport! No free wifi and the basement looks like a scene of a horror movie!! When we went upstairs to our room the place felt like a prison. Our room number was kicked in. When we got inside our room we were disgusted. There was dust everywhere-the place must have NEVER been cleaned. I was scared to even sit on the beds because they looked filthy. The carpet had stains everywhere. As soon as we looked around the room we knew we needed to get out of there. We left immediately and found another hotel that was clean. Don't stay here!

title: “Bringing the House Down”
text:
The Farmer's Daughter has much to commend it. The location is the best, right across from the Farmer's Market and The Grove. Decorations are whimsical, the cookies and drinks in the lobby each evening are a nice touch available in most hotels. The "high speed" internet was free but faster service cost extra. Did not try it to see if it was worth the price. The free internet was generally draggy. Beds were comfortable and towels changed daily when put in the tub.
What brings the place down is the housekeeping. The most egregious incident was the maid going into clean the room while we were at breakfast although we had a Do Not Disturb sign on the door. We had not picked up. Cameras and laptops and phone chargers were lying around. When we came back in the room, the maid, who was still in the room, had cleaned up and tossed a suitcase onto a chair. Maybe it is too much to expect that the Do Not Disturb sign provides a modicum of privacy but that was my expectation and I felt my privacy was violated. To add insult to injury, it turned out the maid did not speak English and evidently did not know what the sign meant. When I went down to complain to the staff, I got a tepid "sorry". If you hire staff who do not speak the language of the hotel, management has a responsibility to assure that they know what things mean. This was a miserable failure.
