Whether or not it is connected to the untrained maid, we had one bar of Ivory soap, in the room when we arrived. This bar of soap had to serve for bath/shower and sink handwashing. In spite of my request, a second bar was not forthcoming. A dirty coffee cup was never replaced. It took three days before a dirty glass was replaced. 
Several front desk staff members were friendly but others simply ignored us as we came and went with no friendly hello, a behavior even the largest hotels today have trained their staff. This was our second stay at this hotel but it will be our last.

title: “Fantastic value for the location”
text: My partner and myself stayed at the Red Roof for a long weekend in April. Although being in NYC you don't spend much time in your room, I would recommend this hotel to anyone needing reasonable, comfortable accommodation in a really central area. The subway is really close and you are practially on Broadway and 5th. The staff help as much as they can - we were impressed when we changed rooms (DO NOT settle for a room ending in 10, 11 or 12 as they are small with a rubbish view - just check the fire escape floor plan near the lifts) and we were moved to a much larger room, high up, litererally face to face with the Empire State Building. Our flights home were early evening and the hotel let us keep the room for as long as we needed it for a very reasonable fee. If you need internet access don't use the room facility - it is not good and quite expensive. About 2-3 doors down turning right out of the hotel (I think number 2 W 32nd St) there is a cheap internet cafe on the 2nd floor of that building. I could go on about how fabulous NYC is but this is a hotel rating website.....

title: “Nice Airport Hotel”
text:
Thanks to my flight being canceled at the last minute and a $370 one way car rental price, I decided to stay near the Philadelphia airport and take my chances to get home the next day.
I've stayed at this property several times before, so it was a no-brainer for me to select it again on this trip.
I called the hotel directly to ask if it could accommodate me around 11:00 at night. Knowing that they could, I waited a short time for the shuttle. The driver was absolutely hysterical with me and the other couple who was on the shuttle. The 4 of us cracked jokes the entire way to the hotel.
As always, I was given a Tastycake at checkin and instead of going to my room, I went to the bar for a cocktail and to get a sandwich to take to my room. I was in my room, having my sandwich by 11:45.
The room was comfortable, as always.
Thankfully, the airline was able to get me home, albeit 14 hours later than scheduled, but my stay at the Hilton Philadelphia Airport was a pleasant respite in my travels.

title: “1st NYC Hotel.Good,clean but nothing spectacular”
text: We stayed there during Christams period for 4 nights and got upgraded to Executive King as part of Great Escapes Deal.There's not really anything bad I can say about it really.The good points were the location, however I think from our experience it really is a bit TOO central but thats a matter of opinion.The room was small even for an executive king havong stayed anight previously at The Palomar in Philadelphia the night before in a 1 bed suite for the same price the value was downgraded as indicated.Thsk staff were polite and we were welcomed by the manager as it was our honeymoon.Our bed was poor though and we both ended up having bad backs by the end of the 4 nights.

title: “Great location!”
text: It was my first time in NYC and The Wellington was an ideal hotel to stay in. The foyer to the hotel was lovely, decorated for christmas and we were greeted with very friendly American bellboys. My room was rather spacious with a wonderful view of Time Square and the city. It was very clean and a maid cleaned the room daily. The ensuite was very basic but clean. The only problem if you are staying on the 16th floor or lower...you will be waiting a long time for the lift. The lifts get full with the people from the higher floors so by the time it reaches the lower floors it is full. A huge advantage is the location. Times Square is a 5 minute walk away and Central Park is a 5 minute walk in the other directon. To be honest New York is a brilliant city, with so much to see and to do we only spent our time in the hotel sleeping. A couple who we travelled with however were unhappy with their hotel room. They were on level 6 and the room was very small, the bathroom in particular was very small and the view was awful. I think The Wellington Hotel could therefore be a hit or a miss depending on the floor level you are placed on...but again the hotel is not an important part of a holiday in New York City. When i visit New Yorks again in the future I would definately consider staying at The Wellington again.

title: “Night and Day”
text:
We checked into this hotel on a Saturday, after being unable to get to Europe due to the unrest in France. The hotel was full of families with young children. We were initially put into an interior room with a view of only the alley behind the hotel, and with very little light. As a Hilton Diamond, I immediately went downstairs and explained that the room we were given was unacceptable. The clerk agreed, and we were put into a room that faced the street (albeit on the 4th floor). The room was fine. On Sunday morning, we were unable to get anywhere near the free breakfast (Embassy Suites standard), due to the multitudinous children milling about unsupervised. Granted, this is the fault of the parents more than the hotel, but it should have been incumbent upon management to insist that parents monitor their children. 
Monday morning was somewhat less chaotic, but by noontime the families had cleared out, and the clientele was all businessmen (note: the rate increased by $100 from Sunday night to Monday night). There is great dining nearby in as you head a few blocks to the east (near Chinatown), including a Ruth's Chris and a Fuddrucker's (whatever your tastes). A couple of blocks to the SOUTH is a Brazilian restaurant (Fogo de Chao) which is absolutely over the top. 
In in-house restaurant, however, was overpriced, with poor service and minuscule portions - absolutely NOT recommended. Avoid at all costs!
The Metro Center and Chinatown Metro stops are both only a few blocks away, thus making the entire city accessible. The White House is a pleasant six block stroll.
Ultimately a good choice, but I would be reluctant to stay again on a weekend.

title: “Great Pet friendly stay”
text: We arrived late in the evening and the front desk was very kind & willing to help. Our request for top floor was fulfilled. Had our room keys and check in ready when we arrived The room was new & fresh & very roomy Very comfortable bed. Older TV but worked fine. The one "not so positive" we noticed was the area. The only thing close by was a very busy small gas station and a Waffle House (with TERRIBLE staff). Cops were dealing with some issue at the gas station when we stopped for a soda,,, then later, cops were at the Waffle House when we walked over for take out. It did not affect our stay. Comfortable and quiet and just what we needed to continue our trip refreshed.

title: “Incompetent service, malfunctioning TV”
text:
This hotel is a mediocre hotel just off Union Square. Cheap and not terrible finish. 
The service is terrible though -- I waited 20 minutes to check in, though there was no line when I arrived! Apparently the spanish speaking biker who walked in after me needed to be attended to first, complete with laughs and stories about old time. 
And then when I checked out and needed help with a billing problem through Expedia...3 calls later, the night manager and company still haven't resolved it. Infuriating! "yes I can confirm to you that you checked out but I am not comfortable telling that to expedia". Wha??? 
And finally, about every 90 minutes all night -- the TV would randomly turn on. Finally, around 4am I realized it wasn't my fault and figured out how to unplug the TV. A poor night's sleep.

title: “Great hotel !!!”
text: We stayed at this hotel for a AABC World Series at Baseball USA. Was a little worried that it would be old and dingy. Much to our surprise the hotel was immaculate and friendly. What we look for in a hotel is cleanliness and let me tell you it was spotless. We also was looking for a pool because all our games were in the evening and this pool was nice as well. Could of been cooler but with the temps in the 100's everyday and down in the 90's at night that wasnt going to happen. The rooms in older hotels usually are worn but I can honestly say everything looked very nice. But the cleanliness is what stood out, the bathroom and everyting was great. Now to the staff !! Paulette, Denise, Abraham, and Daniel were the few that we came in contact on a daily basis over the 6 days we stayed there and they absolutly went above and beyond to make us comfortable and happy. From Paulette making sure there was fresh decaf coffee every morning for me, Denise giving us the best recomendation for dinner, to Daniel's smile as we left the hotel and returned every evening, and Abrahams efforts to keeping the pool clean, enough could never be said about this staff!!! Housekeeping also has to be mentioned because they kept our room stocked with clean towels and did not miss a thing cleaning everyday while we were at the pool. I sure hope each and everyone of them is being paid what they are worth making this property a busy one. It all comes down to the staff putting you on the map as a property worth staying at...and this staff goes the extra mile for its patrons each and every day. They sure made our stay at this Best Western a pleasant experience...Thanks Paulette, Denise, Daniel, and Abraham !!!! And the whole staff !!! We would without a doubt stay here many more times.....

title: “PARKING IS TERRIBLE”
text:
This hotel is FABULOUS for proximity to the many medical buildings/hospitals in the area. 
BUT (wish I could bold that word,) there should be SOME sort of information or disclaimer about the parking situation. Upon making a reservation someone should inform you of the situation. I know it is downtown Boston and parking is a commodity but SERIOUSLY. It is a parking garage (with a 6'3" clearance so hope you drive a small car) which is $18 a day. The parking was not well marked (as small Best Western symbol so we passed it,) the spots were TINY, the garage was SCARY and there was NO ELEVATOR! So if you parked up three or four levels you had to go back down the same way the cars are zooming up?! I was traveling with several others including a baby so we had a large SUV and I don't know how we fit that sucker in there. Our antenna scraped on all the concrete supports. The parking attendants were nearly impossible to understand and rude beyond belief. There is NO PLACE TO STOP AND UNLOAD YOUR CAR. You can get help inside with a luggage cart but seriously! The room was OK. We had two refrigerators, two microwaves (I'm assuming one of each didn't work) and there were missing handles on the drawers and dresser. The TV was such poor quality that when we ordered a movie you had a hard time telling what color things were b/c of the distortion. There was a black curly hair in our shower. Ew. The price was CRAZY for what we got.
However, it is truly the closest place to the hospitals and medical buildings. Just know what you are getting yourself into with parking, cleanliness, service and cost of rooms.

title: “Very Loud weekend nights.”
text: I stayed here with my 3 children in April on a Friday and Saturday night. The courtyard is great and the kids loved the pool. The staff was very helpful. The rooms could use some work, but were not terrible for the price which included parking & continental breakfast. The only downside was the on premises nightclub plays EXTREMELY loud music until 2:30am. It is so loud in the rooms that even with the windows shut I could understand clearly everything the DJ said. My kids slept through it thankfully. The brochure says there may be noise until 11:00pm, which I was prepared for. It wasn't until 3:30am until all the partiers quieted down. There were some other guests yelling for them to be quiet. Maybe weekday stays are better.

title: “Fabulous!”
text:
We picked the Hotel Boheme for the location while on our Honeymoon. 
When we got there the location was great and the Boheme and staff were even better. The staff went to great lengths to make sure we were happy. They offered suggestions for restaurants. We enjoyed our room overlooking the street and the noise, sounds, and smells. We will definitely stay here again.

title: “Great Deal”
text: I stayed here for 4 nights. Upon check-in, the owner gave me a cold bottled water which was greatly appreciated after the 4 block walk from the light rail on a 113 degree day. I requested a king room but got 1 queen, I didn't complain. I'm sure they would have switched rooms but I was too tired and hot to move. The room was very clean with a newly updated bathroom. It was very quiet too. The morning continental breakfast was a great treat on the way out the door to the Convention Center. I grabbed a fruit and some Tang. ( My daughter was staying at the Hyatt and was not provided with any type breakfast )Also, FREE WIFI-gotta love it! (Again, the Hyatt didn't have this.) I had a great rate with AAA. The money I saved I spent at restaurants. One thing that bothered me was the area. I felt like I should be back in my room by dark. The church across the street had a sign that said something like this: "Please don't sell or use drugs outside this holy place.") I'll be back next year though.

title: “A sigh of relief!”
text:
Looking at some of the reviews on trip advisor sometimes convinces me that there are some complete miseries out there.
The Intercontinental is considered a pretty damn good hotel in New York and was booked by a friend of mine, on my behalf. I was certainly not disappointed. The arrival is impressive as one of the other reviewers mentioned the Lobby is fantastic, with plenty of comfortable seating areas and large freshly cut flower displays. 
The hotel restaraunt and bar was good, really nice buffet breakfast which I didn't try until the last day, I probably would have eaten breakfast there every day if given the choice again. The staff were friendly, approachable and knew their stuff, which is exactly what I want when in an unfamiliar place.
The room was not the most recently updated (and neither was the hotel actually) but was tastefully presented with quality fittings. Nice big bed (really comfortable), nice bathroom, with a good shower (how many decent hotels have you been in and the shower is rubbish). The mini bar and coffee making facilities were a little steep, but hey.
The location, possibly the most important factor to me, was great. Just round the corner from Grand Central Station (making it easy and cheap to get to downtown manhattan and ground zero, liberty etc) , two blocks from 5th Avenue and the shops.
We paid about £800 for 4 nights, not bad I thought, I would definately want to stay there again. As for New York, coming from someone who doesn't do city breaks, great and safe city that you have to see,

title: “Excellent”
text:
Another great choice based on TA reviews.
The location--Union Square--is ideal. Walk to Chinatown, BART, cable car (if you must), shopping, SOMA, restaurants. The area just to the west is a bit seedy at nite, but in perspective downtown SF is the safest-seeming big city I've been to in the US. Hotel also has a complimentary town car--they took me to the CalTran station--have no idea how much further you can push it.
From the outside nothing special but the upper lobby (base of the atrium) has some sort of impressive modernist sculpture and a nice (but pricey) bar. Plenty of Irish pubs in the area too. Notice one reviewer panned the restaurant. Served him right. Within a few blocks is a great Indonesian place, a Morton's, a wonderful taqueria, and the best Chinese outside China. Anyone who travels a bit can attest: ONLY LOSERS EAT IN THEIR HOTEL! 
The room was clean, bright, large enough, with a large immaculate marble bathroom with separate shower and bath. Service was efficient, though they were mysteriously stingy replenishing the soap. 
PP is really a first-rate business hotel that works great for vacations, though nothing particularly charming, romantic or historic about it. If you're in SF on business you can probably find something closer to the financial district/Embarcadero but at the cost of things to do at nite. 
Highly recommended.

title: “You pay for the location”
text:
Plusses: easy access from the international terminal when your connecting flight is early the next morning. Pleasant staff.
Minuses: not the best cleaned room; as I was reorganizing my suitcase I stepped on something crunchy: it was multiple nuts etc that were swept to the edge of the bed skirt so obviously no vacuuming was done near the edge of the bed. there were some pieces of paper on the bathroom sink area that should have been cleaned up as well; at over $300 per night this is unaccepable.

title: “Comfortable Stay in San Fran”
text: This hotel was a great fit for location and comfort. The hotel is beautifully decorated, with a welcoming lobby. My room was clean and spacious. The mini bar also offered a fun array of food and drinks. The Triton staff were extremely friendly and knowledgeable, offering great recommendations for food and shopping. I would recommend this hotel for travel and leisure.

title: “Stay elsewhere if you want to sleep!”
text:
What can I say, I wish I had seen previous reviews. We stayed at the weekend and were at the far end of the hotel, furthest from the noisey bar across the street! Yet, Friday night the music was on till midnight and Saturday till 12:40am, although the reception staff did file a complaint with police! 
Although the hotel was basically ok, it is not in the most convenient location for walking to the downtown/riverwalk area! Breakfast and parking were difficult due to large school/youth groups with the parking lot filled with various busses! 
Breakfast not great, limited items and pancake machine out of action. For the rates charged, the hotel didn't live up to the rate. Staff although polite, did not seem interested in assisting guests. If you want a great location and value your sleep stay elsewhere. There are hotels charging similar rates without the drawbacks!

title: “Rooms are a little dated. Small bed (queen) for such a large room. Small bathroom.”
text: Good value, but not a fancy hotel. Rooms have a dated decor. Small bathrooms. Friendly service.

title: “Thank you trip advisor reviewers”
text: My fiance and I wanted to take a trip to New York but with us both being in school we were on a tight budget. The only places I looked at were placing that were within budget but that had good reviews. This place did not dissapoint. It was perfect for the traveler who does not want to spend the whole trip in their rooms. The staff were very freindly, let us have an early check in. We were in a great location, room was a good size, nice TV and pretty confortable beds. It you are looking for 5 star this is not, but it is a great place to stay and we will for sure go back and have recommended it to several of our friends.

title: “Wouldn't stay here again”
text: I came here for a professional conference, which was held in the hotel. The lobby of the hotel is opulent, but the rooms leave much to be desired. The rooms are very small and the walls are thin -- I could hear the people talking in the next room at night. The bathroom is the smallest I've ever seen, without even a counter on which to set toiletries. While the hotel is old and quaint, the rooms and bathroom are so small that they are not comfortable. The hotel makes a poor choice for a conference venue. The meeting rooms are split between the Mezzanine level and the 4th floor. This was an awkward set-up to try to get between these floors. The elevators were extremely slow and crowded, to the point of being clostrophobic! My company is paying the bill my stay here, and it's a good thing, because I wouldn't waste my money on this hotel.

title: “Nice Place to stay”
text:
This hotel was very nice. I wasn't sure if my husband would like all of the bright colored walls and different type decor in the room, but he thought it was great. The staff at the hotel were very friendly. The gave us snacks upon check in, which consisted of a candy bar, an apple, trail mix and bottled water. The staff also help us with directions to many places around the downtown area. Our room was clean and pleasant. Loved the nice tranquil music that was being played when we entered the room. The beds were high off the ground and very comfortable. The only regret I have is that I forgot my pillow at home. Their pillow was ok, but it wasn't like the one I have at home. The windows did show a lot of light, but there were blackout shades to help if you needed it to be darker. The air conditioner was a bit loud when it turned on. It did wake me up in the middle of the night. Not sure if this is in all of the rooms or just the one I stayed in. The bathroom was very nice and large. I loved the shower. The cable tv could have been a bit better. The guide to the tv, did not work, so you didn't know what you were watching on tv. Also, you couldn't buy a movie, because that feature did work either.They also do not have a free breakfast, but we were able to drive a little way down the road to grab us a bite that morning. The hotel is within walking distance to the Galleria. The staff at the hotel gave us a map to the Galleria and told us the best way to get there by foot. Overall I really did like this hotel. My husband and I would stay here again.
DeeAnna

title: “Great staff, great Location”
text:
Stayyed at the Hollywood Orchid Suites for a couple of nights.
From the outside it just looks like a normal building once you got in it was nice.
The room was huge with a seperate Kitchen and dining area didnt really use the kitchen much apart from putting some beer in the fridge but it looked like it all worked ok.
The pool looked nice but again I didnt use it as was a short stay.
Bit of noise acouple of nights as the walls seem thick but the noise ssems to travel through the doors but it soon went away.
The best thing about this plae is the Location right at the side of the Hollywood and Highland centre which leads on the walk of fame where there is plenty to see and and places to eat.
The staff were helpful when had a couple of questions and handed out leaflets with nearst places to eat, cinema times ect. when I had quesions of how to get to Universal Studios the guy worked there told me how to get there and back. noc harge for leaving luggage eithier.
All in all good place to stay

title: “I attended the LifeLine Food Bank Dinner and Fund Raiser”
text:
My four day experience at CedarBrook was exceptioal. From the front desk checkin to the Copper Leaf restaurant I had a great experiences. The grounds are imaculately groomed and the guest rooms & public spaces are spotlessly clean and well maintained. The public living rooms with bottled water and complimentary snacks is a very nice touch. This is truly one of the best kept secretes in the greater Seattle area. 
Try it, you will not be disappointed. Bill Moton

title: “Solid 4 Star Property booked thru Hotwire”
text:
I travel to Seattle regularly; I'm familiar with the downtown hotels.
At $85.00 is a great deal! Thier rack rate varies crazy from $141 to $400+ for a standard room???
Property is large and recently updated. Public areas are classic/modern and spotless; but not very interesting...
Vales, bellman and front desk were allways professional and welcoming.
Rooms are larger than the norm with simple wooden furniture and a blan, beige color pallet. Again not very interesting, boring...
Everything worked in the room. Bathroom was roomy with good lighting and lots of hot water.
Maid service could of been better. Carpet vacuuming or wiping down the tub/bathroom floor was never done and it really needed it...
Amazing Core Fitness center and pool on top floor and it's free to use!
Room service was expensive, not tasty and late being delivered.
Sundry/gift shop is the most expensive I've ever seen! Person staffing it was creepy and not helpful...
I would totally recommend the Sheraton as a good, solid business class hotel. Families and vacationers would find it boring; they'er better options...

title: “Great home base in Chicago”
text: I stayed at the Best Western River North in Chicago for 2 nights and it was a great hotel for price, convenience and location. We were on the third floor in a double room in the annex building (not much of a veiw out the window thought). Rooms are fine, not overly spacious, but adequate for the amount of time spent in the room. Everything was clean and well maintained. The three best things about the hotel are the free parking, the location - near Michigan avenue, the river, Millenium Park and the rooftop terrace. We really enjoyed a nice summer evening up there, eating Chicago style pizza from the restaurant next door, enjoying a cocktail, and watching the lights of the city come on. I would definitely stay here again. Only downside - is I wish I would have brought my own pillow - theirs were way too puffy!

title: “terrible service”
text: The service was terrible in the restaraunt and lounge. If you wanted silverware you had to get up find a waiter and ask them. If you wanted something to drink other than coffee or the juice provided once again we had to get up and find someone. If you wanted a beverage in the lounge you had to get up and go to the bar, eventhough there was a waitress there. We even had to wave at her to take our order and was not very pleasant about it. The front desk staff were friendly enough but not a real pleasant friendly. They either seemed under staffed or the staff just messed around enough to seem overly busy. The bathroom was quite small.

title: “Great rooms, great location, great pool, great service”
text:
With our family, we had booked three double rooms in Jan 2009 and were fully satisfied with the Grand Hyatt. A highlight was the well-heated pool and the outdoor spa.
Location: As others had said, excellent location, close to everything.
Rooms: Spacious, beautifully furnished and decorated. Beautiful bathrooms with massage shower.
Public areas: Everybody enjoyed the gas fireplace in the lobby after coming out of the freezing coldness outside.
Breakfast: We had a rate with buffet breakfast included which was very good with a good selection of cooked items and cooked-to-order omelettes.
Pool and gym: High-tech gym with Life Fitness machines, a large and well-heated indoor pool and a steaming outdoor pool which was especially enjoyable since it was freezing cold. Breathtaking views of the mountains from the spa.
Service: Bellstaff and recipionists were extremely helpful and friendly.
We did not eat in the hotel's restaurant but walked a few steps to the Ship Tavern in Brown's Palace Hotel and had a most enjoyable, reasonably priced dinner there.

title: “Good for lodging, sleep and shower!!”
text:
For San Francisco prices, it's cheap, so don't expect anything. 
Stayed there 3 nights and even if "Raj" (our host) had a hard indian accent and didn't smile a lot and was prompting us for the money, he wasn't rude, he was helpful and funny in a way. The hotel is very old and so it "looks" old, but despite the age it's very quaint, it's clean and very quiet and very well located, close to very nice places and to public transportation, next door to a big parking structure, which was nice when parking is hard to find and expensive, we payed only $25 dlls for 24 hrs and took the bus, so it worked nicely.
Though not a gourmet breakfast buffet, it sure helps when u go out in a run, and can take little cakes to go.
We stayed in a room with no bathroom, but didn't mind at all, facilities were real close and clean, no bad smells of any kind, no noises either. 
We went there only to sleep and shower, and it worked for us.
Didn't want to pay for anything else but a clean bed and shower, and that's what u get. We wanted to get to know the city, not the hotel, and we did.
Don't be discouraged by the other reviews, this hotel "works" for the money.

title: “7th Stay Just as Good as the First”
text:
From June 5th to the 10th, I visited The Michelangelo for the 7th time since first discovering it back in December of 2007. It has, and will remain, my home whenever I visit New York.
As always, the location cannot be beat. Broadway theaters, great restaurants, stores, and subway access are all minutes or sometimes steps away from the hotel. Another plus for the location - You're pretty much right in the middle of midtown New York, without having to be in the middle of all the chaos. The hotel remains a quiet sanctuary for sleep and winding down after a long day of walking around the city, and dealing with the crowds.
The hotel is tastefully decorated, and brings a sense of calm and elegance as soon as you walk through the doors. The rooms are also larger than normal for this part of town. I usually get upgraded to a Junior Suite when I check in, but I did not this time. Still, the room was plenty large, with a gorgeous marble bathroom, and a luxurious bed. The staff is also highly attentive, and always friendly. They refer to you by name, and whenever a problem in the room arises, they send someone up to fix it promptly.
Speaking of the staff, I must single out one individual who always goes above and beyond whenever I say here - His name is Henry, and whenever he carries my bags to my room, he talks to me as if he has been my friend for years. He also goes out of his way for his guests. On this particular visit, I was downstairs in the lobby one morning, using the free Internet to check e-mail. Henry walked up to me, and asked me if he could get me a juice or coffee. I assumed he meant from the hotel bar, so I asked him how much a juice would cost. He shook his head, and said he would get me one from the store down the street. Before I could say anything, he ran out of the lobby. 5 minutes later, he came running back, with a small container of orange juice. I reached for my wallet to pay him, and once again, he shook his head. He said that I was a VIP, and that everyone there appreciates how often I stay at the hotel. 
So, even if I did not get my usual room upgrade, the staff still went out of their way, and regarded my return visit as something special.
I think that's what sets The Michelangelo apart. As a regular returning guest, I always feel special and welcome there. They acknowledge my loyalty, and seem genuinely honored that I have chosen their hotel as my "home" in New York. There are other perks here, such as how the elevators are also the fastest I have experienced in a hotel. I have never had to wait more than 5 seconds for an elevator to arrive, even during the busy dinner/theater hour, when everyone's going out for the evening. The free breakfast is also small, but pretty good. Some reviews have said that the free breakfast was moved to a small basement room. But, the week I was there, it was being held in the Mezzanine area just above the lobby. So, maybe they are trying it in different areas.
I guess if I must find fault, the front door staff could be more attentive. I think I held the door open for guests more than they did. Still, this is a minor flaw considering how excellent everything else is here. Thanks to the staff of the Michelangelo for another fantastic stay, and I look forward to my return in the Spring.

title: “Great Hotel - Fab location cant ask for more”
text: We stayed for 3 nights at The Crowne Plaza Times Square, then 1 night (our last night at The Barclay Hotel) The Barclay cost a lot more and we were staying there for a last night as a special treat, we wished we had stayed at the Crowne Plaza the whole time The Barclay was so expensive and tired in comparrison and miles away from anywhere, staff were rude, very dissapointing, we changed rooms it was no better, the bathrooms are old things in the room were broken such as the ironing board. Stop at The Crowne Plaza for a modern stay with friendly staff and great location. The Barclay Hotel isnt recomended unless you want a nice reception area as thats all thats nice about it.

title: “Great Hotel - Huge Rooms - Great Value”
text: Just back from a 5 night trip and I will definitely stay in this hotel again. Staff were extremely friendly, the rooms were far bigger than most New York hotel rooms, location was great (5 mins walk to Times Square) and the free internet definitely came in handy.

title: “Back Bay Hotel”
text: Very nice hotel. Centrally located and close to the Copley Square subway station. Close enough to walk to Newbury, Beacon Hill, Boston Common, Chinatown, theater district, etc. Rooms are a little small, but nice. Staff is very friendly. A quality hotel!!

title: “Would stay there again for sure!”
text: I booked this hotel via Hotels and got a very good rate. I was looking for a nice hotel in Midtown and found it very good value for the price. The room was very spacious with two large beds, nice bathroom, a walk-in closet and had a great view of the Empire State building. It also has a gym and swimming pool with a great view! The place was clean, the staff were polite and very accommodating. You can't beat the location for being near Grand Central, which makes it easy to get anywhere. There are also always taxis in front of the hotel. I would definitely recommend this hotel!

title: “Better than anticipated”
text: Based on the half and half mixed reviews, I was nervous to stay here but we were pleasantly surprised how great everything was here. Some of the negative reviews about blood on the sheets, bed bugs, rude staff etc were not anything we experienced during our stay. We were here for a 6 day September vacation to see the city. Jackie, the front desk attendant checked us in and was really friendly and welcoming. The few issues we had while there were immediately addressed. We used the vending machines on the second floor to try and buy water. The machine was out of water, and took the money we had put in. When we informed the front desk attendant, he went in the back room and pulled out two bottles of water for us. We received a courtesy call when we opted to not have housekeeping straighten the room one morning, letting us know that if we needed anything, just let someone at the front desk know. There is usually someone at the door as you exit to hail a cab for you if you need one. The breakfast was ok, mostly sugary pastries, cereals, pancakes and other carbs. The walls seem thin, but we were staying during a relatively quiet week so noise wasn't much of an issue. On our last night during our stay, the neighboring room sounded like it was full of small children yelling but it was quiet by the time we were ready to sleep. I wish there were fans in the bathroom. Also, the sink does not drain fast if you keep the water running. Other than that, our stay was enjoyable.

title: “Excellent hotel, great location”
“Very nice, great location!”
text: You cant beat this location...close to highways, great restaurants (all within walking distance!) Nice pool area & work out area, clean rooms. Winking Lizard across street great family place to eat! Close to columbus zoo (another must see!)

title: “Another wonderful review”
text:
I'll just add my kudos as other before me have done. The Talbott is a small, european feeling hotel just off the hustle of Michagan Avenue. 
The charming street is a beautiful backdrop to the outdoor restaurant where food is very good. The hotel staff is exceptionally helpful and friendly (Gene the conceirge is fantastic!) Our room was huge, clean and comfortable -- extra nice Aveda toiletries!
A wonderful property in a wonderful location and a good value for $179/night.

title: “Stay AWAY from this DIRTY Place”
text: Wow! Very disappointing. Room was so dirty, even a a spider web with baby spiders inside the front door. We were there for 3 nights and our room was NEVER cleaned. When we went to the front desk (they don't answer the phone) for towels we were told they would give us towels "this time" but we needed to "bring the dirty ones down". The sofa sleeper sagged to the middle. The bathtub bottom is filthy, guess they've never heard of Mr Clean Magic Erasers-thank goodness Marriott has, which is where I'll be staying on my next visit to Columbus. I have stayed at a Hawthorn before and was pleased. NOT this time. The neighborhood is sketchy, the hotel fits right in and the staff doesn't seem to care. Save your money, keep going past this place!

title: “Great place for a short stay”
text:
Spent two nights here as part of a wedding party in early Sept 2006. We benefited from a preferential rate as it's a bit expensive otherwise in my view.
The hotel has a great location right in the heart of downtown Boston - pretty much everywhere of note is within walking distance - this will save you $$ on cabs.
Parking is OK albeit the staff could be friendlier and the check-in process is prompt (tip - join the frequent guest scheme and you will get express check in and out and complimentary drinks and newspaper).
The lobby is grand and the downstairs bars are good - although they are not open very late.
Lifts are old and small and can take a time to reach your floor.
Rooms are clean and light but not big and could probably do with an update.
Concierge service is great - we used it to get our laundry done and it was delivered in room on time.
Breakfast is not cheap but is very good.
The ballroom has great views but very dated decor (we were there for a wedding) and really needs an update.

title: “Disappointing Hotel - Not what you would expect from a 4* Hotel”
text:
We wanted to end our California trip with something special, we thought.
So we decided to book two nights at the Sheraton...
The pictures on their homepage are very deceiving, considering that part of the hotel is covered with scaffolding.
OK, The location is good, however, you have about a dozen hotels to chose from in that area (within 2 min. walking distance, one hotel is basically next to the other) which maybe a better choice.
The room was on the 3rd floor. It was noisy and overlooking the hotels air-conditioning. The bathroom was really tiny and we had mold. They offer internet at $11 (without tax!) for what they call 24 hours, the only problem is that their 24 hours end at 12:00 noon (regardless of which time you decide to take it). I asked the concierge about this and received a snotty answer. 
Staff were not very friendly and customer oriented. The overall taste this so-called 4* Hotel left was very disappointing throughout.

title: “Antonio is the best!!”
text: My friends and I stayed at this hotel last weekend for 2 nights. Beautiful hotel and super location right on the river walk. I had never been to San Antonio and was very pleased. We were cared for by Antonio in the breakfast restaurant and he was wonderful! I visited twice in one morning and he remembered me the second time and looked happy to see me. He was very kind and offered us to go cups for our drinks. ANTONIO is a keeper of an employee!!!

title: “DON'T BE LURED BY THE HYATT NAME OR THE 4 STAR RATING”
text:
Avoid this hotel. The room was quiet and clean. That's the only positive. 
The concierge was horribly uninformed in every way. The front desk was unresponsive. The lobby is sterile and noisy. The bed was way too soft. There are no safes in the rooms. The sauna was out of order and the locker room needs an immediate overhaul. The food in the restaurant is below average. The place gives a general impression that no one is in charge. We were charged for items in the minibar that we never consumed. Extra cost for wifi. And apparently they treat their employees badly. There were pickets outside. 4 Star? No way.

title: “Fabulous place to stay”
text: Such a nice airy clean tall room. Everyone was pleasant, the food for breakfast was amazing and the pool area was well kept clean. Highly recommend a stay here. If it is a few dollars more, it is well worth it. They usually have coupons for discounts on their website too!

title: “A great place to stay in New York!”
text: We just got back from over a week in New York, staying at the Hotel Metro. The room was small but comfortable and very clean. The bed was super comfy and the staff was efficient. Jeff, the concierge was especiially helpful They are urenovating so you want to get a room up high and on the quiet side. The rooftop terrace is an added bonus - a great place at the end of a buy day. Watching the Empire State Building at night from the terrace was a highlight for me.

title: “Great hotel for the price”
text:
This hotel is an unexpected find. It is quiet, the rooms are immaculate, and the staff is friendly. I was in San Jose on business, so I was especially pleased that there was a large desk and free internet access. There is also a small outdoor pool and a small workout room, which were not fancy but were decent enough. Two small details that never seem to get mentioned but that I always appreciate knowing- the rooms are heated/cooled by the standard under-the-window noisy blowers found in most hotels of this price range (not great) but the windows do open so you can get a fresh breeze if you wish.
The only downside to the hotel is that it is located in a vacant feeling neighborhood. Don’t expect to walk out of the hotel for a bite to eat or to grab a coffee, you will need to drive somewhere or take the light-rail. The hotel is within a very short (5-10 minute) walk to the VTA light-rail station to downtown and the convention center. When I stayed here I didn’t have a car and got around by the VTA just fine.
Overall, for the price this hotel is a great choice and I recommend it.

title: “The best hotel to stay at in San Jose, CA!”
text:
My husband and I have stayed at the Sainte Claire in San Jose, CA numerous times. Lisa, the General Manager, was nothing but wonderful to us, making our stay each time, perfect! Clean, spacious rooms, feather king sized beds, wonderful staff and a beautiful restaurant, IL fornia. The front staff members, Rona and Ramona, were btoh friendly and accomadating. We had champagne delivered to our room for our anniversary. Thank you to Lisa, Rona and Ramona for a wonderful stay, every time. We look forward to our next vsit to the hotel and would highly recommend this hotel to anyone! 
- Justin and Christy da Cunha

title: “Good hotel in great location”
text:
We stayed here for one night as part of a Southern State tour. The hotel was quite centrally located in Memphis and a short 15 min walk up the main street to Beale St. Trolley buses run up the road for those who don't want to walk - Having sat on a coach for hours makes you appreciate a nice walk.
Our room was very large with a kingsize bed, flat screen TV, coffee maker. The bathroom was massive and I think the room was probably for disabled/wheelchair users. Breakfast wasn't included but the hotel opposite had a coffee shop.
I had a great stay at this hotel, but probably partly due to the great experience from the day spent at Graceland, SunCity, The Civil rights museum and the highlight Beale St. I would definitely love to return to Memphis to spend more time in the city and would not hesitate to choose this hotel.

title: “Perfect location, perfect service”
text:
Our daughter's wedding was held nearby and we utilized a block of 10 rooms for the weekend. The location looks out over lower New York Harbor with the Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island outside the windows. The rooms even come equipped with a telescope. The bed was very comfortable and a luxury bath with two robes, two sinks and separate shower and bathtub. Even better than the luxury accommodations was the service we received from each and every staff member. Laura at the front desk remembered that we had visited 2 months before. One couple in our party is deaf and they set up the room with special facilities to help them (vibrating alarm clock, door bell which turned the lights on and off, TTY to speak to front desk) and then Jason, a member of the guest relations staff, came to the room when they checked in to explain the special features. A week before we arrived, I received a 3 page survey to inquiring about special needs, who was paying and for what. 
The housekeeping staff anticipated the needs in the bridal suite and staff arranged for photos of the bride and groom to be taken from a closed-off outdoor roof location. If I didn't know any better, I think they may have actually arranged for the perfect weather as well. In summary, while it is expensive, the Ritz is a beautiful luxury facility located at the tip of Manhattan with exquisite service. My wife and I will come back to stay for special weekends in New York CIty.

title: “2 star ???”
text: Stayed Saturday night 10/1/05. The entry door lock was broken. The bathroom door did not close. The room had mold on the walls, and the paint was falling off. The shower had the flow of a garden hose. The bed frame was too big for the mattress and was sticking out of the bed enough to scrape your legs. The table lamp switch was broken and it could not be used.

title: “great staff”
text: stayed there for work this week. staff competent and nice. rooms were clean and nicely set up. good deal for breakfast. great location. good room rates. as usual though in DC parking rates are high only bad thing about the rate

title: “been guest since opened”
text: Have traveled for 50 years and this has to be the most efficient and friendly motel i have been in. clean convenient to airport and restaurants. only happy hour with beer wine and nearly a full meal. service beyond compare .

title: “Suited our needs perfectly”
text: Sometimes reviews just blow my mind. No room service, no hair dryer, no pool...did you not do ample research among a thousand hotels in Los Angeles? The Wilshire is perfectly fine. Very friendly staff, great continental breakfast, a peaceful environment, sizeable and comfortable rooms, free parking in a quiet and safe neighborhood. It was absolutely perfect for those visiting Los Angeles who are on the go and hotel amenities is not the purpose of the visit. Each morning I would take my laptop to the breakfast area and research what it was we wanted to do that day. There is a computer in the lobby but often times folks had the same idea I had so I found it more convenient to take my own laptop. The seating areas outside were great in that I could just relax as the remainder of my party was almost ready to go. The bathroom in our room was huge with a vanity just ourside of it so that a couple of us could be getting ready. We utilized the large closet and the refrigerator came in handy as we stocked it with water from the nearby 99 cents store...that's a place to see. The farmer's market was close, a great venture, and the beaches and other tourist attractions were all within 30-40 minutes of this hotel, including a drive up to Malibu. Beverly Hills is just a half mile away to the west and Sunset and Hollywood Blvds are just a couple miles directly north. The Wilshire was far better in terms of nearby attractions and necessary amenities than I could have hoped for.

title: “Great location and service outweighs small room size”
text: I stayed here with my 9 year old daughter for two nights in July. We are frequent visitors to Boston and have stayed at many different hotels throughout the city. The location of the Parker House is second to none. It is a SHORT walking distance to so many great venues - Quincy Market, the North End, the Commons and Newbury Street shopping, plus Downtown Crossing and many key Freedom Trail sites, plus the T. Beyond the location, the hotel is very child-friendly, with a welcoming kit for kids with goodies and trinkets, plus milk and cookies delivered to your room! The concierge desk was helpful and knowledgeable as would be expected in a hotel of this caliber, and the business center offered internet access and online flight check-in. In short, everything we needed for a comfortable stay. The rooms are small and the walls thin, but it is a historic hotel in a historic city after all - besides, they are well-appointed. And, we found a great deal on the nights we stayed - under $150. Highly recommend this hotel for a comfortable stay and easy access to almost anything you need.

title: “Great Value in SF”
text:
In 2010 paid only $74+tax for the AAA rate. This was a fraction of the price of any of the major chains anywhere in the northern part of SF. The place wasn't special or super lux, but very clean and comfortable and FREE PARKING.
You can see more about my trip to Cali and my stay here: http://freetravelgenius.com/california/#chelsea

title: “Noisy Freight Train at Night”
text:
I recently stayed at this hotel while attending a convention in San Diego. My time over the weekend was fine, light traffic noise from the street, but nothing too unexpected. However, from Monday through Thursday, a freight train runs outside the hotel several times a night, blasting it's horn. The first night the train woke me at 1:30am and continued with the horn for 30 minutes. I asked for ear plugs, but was told they had none.
The hotel bed was very comfortable and the staff were pleasant, but a good night's sleep is tremendously important when traveling. I will not stay at that hotel and would not recommend it to any but the heaviest sleepers.

title: “For an expensive hotel could be much bette”
text: It is supposed to be a luxury hotel, but the attention to detail in a true luxury hotel is lacking. First evening, the bar lost our order and it took 45 minutes to get an order of fries. They made up by complimenting our drinks, but it would have been good if they had got our order right. Room is OK, bed is a lot less comfortable than at the Sheraton. All TV channels do not work (channel 33 - USA for example), and our toilet flush needed to be adjusted each time to make sure it did not run. Not what you expect from a high end hotel. Service was acceptable, not exceptional. The lobby is a night club at night and loud, which means that it is not possible to relax in the lobby after hours. The location is awkward for cabs, it takes a lot of maneuvering to get taxis in the midst of all the traffic. Would certainly not stay here again.

title: “Are you all kidding me”
text:
I read reviews on this and other sites before booking this hotel. They all made this place sound Ok, so we went for it. Let me say, I knew that it wasn't Ok as soon as we pulled into the parking lot. The building is old and in need of major renovations. We checked in, and the lobby was the only nice thing about the place. Our room was small, in dire need of updating, and just down right bad. The bathroom wasn't big enough for me to turn around in. The bed was hard, like sleeping (or not sleeping) on a box spring. I would understand all of this if this was a room for $49.99, but it was $120 a night. We could have staying in LoDo in a top of the line hotel for the same price. Shame on this company for trying to pass itself off as anything but a cheap, dirty hotel. I felt like I should have been paying by the hour. Spend your money wisely and stay downtown for a few extra bucks. 
Oh, and we left a personal blanket there, called the next day to go and pick up and they claimed to have not found anything in the room. Its a king size blanket for goodness sake, and we certainly didn't have it.

title: “Harrington a definite bargain”
text: The Hotel Harrington is a great bargain. It is close to everything in DC that one would like to see. If you're not spending a lot of time in your room, this is the perfect hotel. The rooms are small. The showers go from hot to cold and then back again without any warning. And, there is standing water in the tub when you shower because it drains very slowly. That being said, you are within a few blocks of a pharmacy, metro stop, several Starbucks, Ford's Theatre, FBI Buiding, etc. The staff are fine and they give you a list of recommended local eateries that is very accurate. For the price, which was at least $70 per night below anything else close to its location, this hotel is perfect for the traveling family.

title: “Even Better Than Anticipated”
text: Reviews of this property were consistently outstanding; so much so that I was prepared to be a bit disappointed. Well based on our recent stay, I can't say enough good things about this hotel and especially the staff. They were consistently friendly and went out of their way to provide the services we needed. From check-in to breakfast to help with transportation, they were exceptional. The room was as promised - very clean, contemporary, and serviced properly everyday. The breakfast was well prepared, PC service on the mark, and the elevators worked flawlessly. But the most surprising was the help we received when leaving NY. I asked the doorman to get us a taxi to go to the airport. I had already priced car service and because it was mid morning decided it would be less expensive to take a taxi. Well the hotel has an arrangement with a car service and after a brief discussion with an amazingly upbeat and courteous doorman, we took the car service offered (two cars waiting). When we arrived at the airport the driver advised us that Delta now flew from serveral terminals and waited while I checked. We were at the wrong termianl for our flight so he took us to the correct one before leaving. Although the hotel was conveniently located and the rooms better than average, the staff made a good trip to NYC truly great.

title: “Try to get as far as you can from a window!!!”
text: Great location, didn't like the restaurant and try not to get a room facing either 8th Av or the 48th. You won't be able to sleep. If you get an upper room or one of the suites, then you are lucky and you will get a great return for what you pay. For some reason, at the time of doing the renovation they forgot to renew all the windows!!!!

title: “Hotel is better than Graceland”
text: This was a funny place. Filled with Elvis pictures, things and guests that all had arrived because of Graceland. Situated across the street from Graceland and being rather cheap. Funny thing to sit and talk to people from around the world about music and rock'n'roll. Actually much more fun than visiting Graceland itself. Good american breakfast is included

title: “perfect!”
text: we recently just stayed at this hotel for one night. everything about our stay was great! the rooms are very spacious, the hotel staff were all very friendly and the location can't be beat! next time we are in chicago we will definitely stay here again.

title: “Decent hotel for business stay”
text:
I stayed in this hotel for a couple of nights in early October. The stay was quite pleasant, with staff generally friendly and helpful.
The location of this hotel is really good, with shopping and good food within walking distance.

title: “Dated, but clean”
text: Stayed here because of its proximity to Carnegie Hall, which is right across the street. Got a HUGE room considering the price. The furnishings are dated, but the room is very clean. The beds were newish and very comfortable. Even though my room was at the front of the buidling, it was very quiet. The building is owned by a church group; all the employees of the hotel were extremely friendly and helpful. Nothing fancy here, but a very good value. Located only a block or two from Central Park.

title: “Magnificent Setting”
text: Beautiful property, Desert Oasis. Expansive lobby with several restaurant options. Happy hour specials daily. Multiple swimming pools, so plenty of room. Was here for a conference which was well run. Rooms were spacious & full of ammenities

title: “At last – an affordable AND good NY hotel”
text: Each time I visit New York I have vowed never to return to the hotel I've chosen - until now. The Mansfield is quietly stylish and the 'senior' room I had was spacious with a living room and bedroom - two TVs etc. Other reviewers on this site seem to have had tiny rooms, so maybe the secret is to ask for a 'senior' room. For three nights, including a Saturday, I paid an average of $166 per night - including tax and continental breakfast. Staff were pleasantly attitude-free.

title: “Great location, great stylish rooms”
text: The hotal was perfectly placed in midtown for all major tourist attractions, close to subway and Penn Station to access Newark Airport. The rooms were lovely, comfortable and amazingly spacious for a new york city centre hotel. We went for a king room on the 26th floor, which was great as you got a view out to the west river and even a sneek preview of the Empire State building. The staff were very friendly and helpful. We did not opt for breakfast as there were so many cheaper deli providers near by. Time square is a five minute walk away. For the location the price was excellent. We will definitely be coming back.

title: “Not as expected”
text:
From the hotels website you would think this was the best hotel in Denver. I was excited to check in and stay here. Once I was here, I found the service to be less that adequate, some of the staff was rude and I could not figure out why there is nothing to show you where things are. No map of the hotel, no book in the room, no signs. After 2 days I found the breakfast area, still have not found the fitness area and when I asked, I was told to "roam around" there is lots to see......
I also found the housekeeping staff to be less than acceptable. For 2 days they have not emptied the trash container, never refilled the in room coffee and as for dusting, I am not sure if that is a monthly event here or not at all. For the price and the hype, I was not impressed. Too many other choices downtown, I will not return.

title: “Perfect location”
text: Located right next door to the John Hancock Observatory and the expensive shops, this is in the perfect location. All the staff were extremely helpful, and our room was great. Bed very comfortable and good size, HD cable, really good shower. I was a bit cautious after reading reviews of guests' belongings going missing, but I locked my suitcase up just in case, and was fine! Reception smells really good too!

title: “DON'T SWIM IN THE POOL!!!”
text:
We stayed at this hotel just for 1 night, but that was 1 night too many! 
 We checked in very late, around 10 p.m. The front desk clerk, Michael, could have cared less. He didn't seem to know anything about the hotel when we asked him questions, like when the breakfast was the next morning. or if the sofa sleeper had linens in the room. We had our 13 year old son with us. He had just turned 13, and this was a surprise birthday trip for him, so we wanted everything to be nice for him. 
 I chose this hotel because it was fairly new, and they sounded nice on the phone, and the rates were good. Ha! My son and I went in to look at the pool, and to our DISGUST and HORROR, there was a young couple MAKING OUT in the pool!! We were both VERY embarrassed, and so were they! Obviously, they weren't about to leave, so we did! What kind of hotel is this? Definitely NOT something I wanted my son to witness! And after that experience, we definitely were NOT interested in swimming in the pool!!!
When we got up to our room, there was just 1 blanket for the sofa bed, no linens! This is WHY we asked Michael downstairs about them. My husband called the front desk, and spoke to Michael and told him the problem. 30 minutes later, still no linens! We were just about to call back, when Michael called us and asked what we needed! Didn't he hear us the first time? Another 15 minutes went by, and FINALLY, the linens arrived! So, our son had to wait 45 minutes before he could go to bed because of the hotel's incompetence!! Nice to feel so welcome! HA!!
The breakfast the next morning was so-so. Nothing great, but I guess for free you can't complain much. There was a big group of kids, so it was fairly crowded and not a big selection of items. It was hard to get to the items, because these kids were all crowded around the waffle machine, so it was hard to get by them.
When we checked out, I complained to the girl at the front desk and asked for a business card for the manager. I emailed him when I got home about our unsatisfactory stay and STILL have not had a reply back. Guess he doesn't care either!
I have since called the Marriott 800 number, and told them of our experience. The customer service rep told me that the manager DOES need to respond to me, and took some notes down as I re-iterated everything again to her, but so far, nobody has called back, and still no email from the manager. Nice, eh? I guess he only wants to hear positive comments.
Marriott, you may want to take a closer look at this new hotel and their incompetent staff! It's too bad that such a new hotel is ruining the Marriott reputation! I always thought very highly of the Marriott chain until this happened.
We will NEVER stay here again, and will think twice about staying in any other Marriott properties too, since NOBODY seems to care about replying back. I have told all my friends and family to stay away!
We stayed at a WONDERFUL EMBASSY SUITES in Houston, Texas for 8 nights before this hotel. Maybe Marriott should take a lesson from the HILTON properties! We will be staying at Hilton hotels from now on.
AVOID this place by all means!!

title: “Don't Stay Here if You Want to Sleep!”
text: Let me start off by mentioning the good things: Hotel has a good location close to Union Square; our special occasion was recognized by a box of malt chocolate balls waiting for us in our room; we received a nice Deluxe King on the 19th floor overlooking the city; the pool was nice; the housekeeper was very nice. We were so excited to be staying at this hotel until we tried to sleep. One word of advice- stay away if you like to get a peaceful sleep! You can hear every single word, footstep, and toilet flush from other guests. This hotel does not have any kind of noise proofing or sound installation. When complaints were made to the hotel about this, they were not proactive in the least bit. Because we did not get much sleep at this hotel, we will likely return to the Palace on our next business trip.

title: “amazing hotel! the best place we've ever stayed by far!”
text:
We loved this hotel so much! My boyfriend and I booked a room last minute on www.orbitz.com so we got a special discount. The hotel we had been booked into previously (The Red Vic) was an utter disappointment on arrival so we decided not to stay there. We got a taxi to this hotel...and we couldn't believe our luck!
The staff were so friendly and efficient - we were booked into our room in no time. The room was immaculate - and the bed was incredible! completely covered with luxurious white pillows. The ensuite bathroom was so spacious - having a bath or shower was an absolute pleasure. The key cards made us feel very secure and safe during our stay.
We got to use the beautiful pool and sauna facilities during our stay for minimal cost. The downstairs bar was lovely - they were always giving us free drinks! The starbucks downstairs was a nice touch too! coffee and buns for breakfast! yay!
Staff kindly helped us with our bags - they even let us store them in the hotel when we went off on a bus trip for a few days! They called us taxis and always gave us information on where to go and what to see.
We stayed here for far longer than we had first anticipated! It was such a romantic, clean, spacious, bright hotel in the best possible location (walking distance to Union Square!) I'll never forget it :)

title: “Astor on the Park represents good value for money and forms the ideal base for sightseeing in New York”
text:
First let's get the negative points out of the way. Yes, the lift is slow and sometimes it is easier to use the stairs. Some of the rooms are small, but all are clean and each bathroom is decorated to a high standard, the hotel having been refurbished in 2005. The individual air conditioning units fitted in each room are effective but a little noisy. There are no other facilities at the hotel apart from the bedrooms, a reception area and a drinks machine and Internet station (expensive) in the basement. 
Now the positive points about this friendly small hotel. It is well placed on Central Park West and is very reasonably priced. The staff all tended to be friendly and helpful and were happy to engage in conversation and offer advice on places to go and things to see. The hotel is frequented mainly by European guests making it feel comfortable for other visitors from the UK/Europe. Being able to walk out of the hotel and straight into the park is a real bonus. Even at the north end, the park is really well used, with many joggers and people exercising during daylight hours. It is a relatively short walk across the park to the Guggenheim Museum (at 90th Street on the east side). The hotel is very well placed for the subway (B and C lines) being located between the stops at 103rd and 110th Street (110th Street is slightly closer). A trip to downtown takes around 10-15 minutes, and with a weekly ticket for the subway and buses ($27) makes getting around NewYork cheap and easy. There is a very modern and well-stocked Supermarket on 110th Street (Cathedral View) and a small American dinner one block back on 107th Street (La Exquisite) that is convenient for breakfast with a typical meal of omelettes and coffee costing around $10/head. A short walk away from Central Park down Louis Armstrong Avenue (and across Manhattan, Columbus, and Amsterdam Avenues) brings you to Broadway which has a good range of reasonable restaurants at sensible prices. The area between Central Park West and Broadway is a little rundown, although it seemed safe enough to us. Two other places worth mentioning that are within easy reach of the hotel are The Hungarian Pastry Shop (near the junction of 110th and Amsterdam Avenue) for cakes and coffee and Miss Mimmis Café (on the corner of 110th and Columbus Avenue) for a really good taste of a Southern kitchen.
Overall, we had a really good stay at the Astor on the Park Hotel and would certainly stay there again in future.

title: “Basic 1950s motor court in great location”
text: With short notice I needed a place to stay near UCLA and based on other reviews tried the Wilshire Motel, which is very easy to get to from UCLA on the #2 Blue Bus. I had passed it many times in the past and been curious. It is a set of small cabins set in from Wilshire Blvd. I got a back cabin which was clean, small, basic, but at a basic price. AC with compressor on very noisy, but on "Low Cool" fairly quiet. From other reviews there are some real dives in the Santa Monica area, this is a big step up. Not for those who like fancy hotels though, but the location can't be beat.

title: “Nice Hotel, but noisy.”
text:
This is a nice hotel, but it's more suited to families. As a business traveller I wanted to be close to the airport for an early morning departure and I expected a typical airport business hotel. The hotel is more of a resort and teaming with young kids. I changed rooms a few times as the road noise (not the airport) was very noisy. In the end I just put up with it.
The front desk manager was impatient & arrogant - next time I'll stay at the Hilton,Marina.

title: “Great Trip”
text:
This was a last second booking, It was an unexpected leg to my trip so I was not in a happy mood. I have to say the staff escepically Vicki at the front desk was very helpful and really made my trip, she was caring and cherful person.
Raafeal at the door was also exceptional and rec few places I should see and some local places I should go to.
The hotel is in a great location, it's clean and service is great. 
The staff do go out of there way to make you comfortable.
The downside I found is there was no coffee machine in the room.
Will book again.
Parveen

title: “Upper-Mid-Class Hotel a little bit far from downtown”
text:
I visited the Hotel end of September 2012.
At our arrival we were greeted very friendly and everything was prepared for a fast and uncomplicated check-in.
The rooms are very big, modern and clean.
Parking was with 16 Dollars per night for this location a bit too expensive, but we could find a cheap alternative close by.
For shopping you can reach the fashion mall in just a few minutes. And you can find affordable but good restaurants close by.
With the San Diego trolley, which stops in front of the Hotel you can go to San Diego Downtown easily and don't have to bother drinking a good glass of wine in one of the very nice places in San Diego Glaslamp Quater.

title: “3 Day Stay”
text: I just spent 3 days in Dallas for training. I found this hotel to be a great place to stay. From the front desk clerk (Steve) at check in until I checked out with the General Manager (Sam) my stay was perfect. I found this hotel to be clean and quite contemporary in it's decor. I particullary found the beds to be really comfortable. Better than being at home.

title: “Not *really* a four-star, more like a 3.5”
text:
I gave this hotel a 4 because there isn't a 3.5 and I don't want to be overly critical. I received the room complimentary due to a horrible stay in a Holiday Inn in the Bahamas last year (this hotel is actually no longer a Holiday Inn because of so many problems apparently). The listed room rate was $259 and I honestly think it was very over-priced, even if it was in Times Square. 
The biggest complaint? The drain in our shower was broken/the tub stopper was sticking up and under it was a huge hairball (not ours). I didn't bother to call down because we were planning on taking a shower anyways, but I'm sure if housekeeping had adequately cleaned the shower/tub after the previous guest, they would have noticed it. Also, the lighting in the shower/tub/toilet area was very dark (the sink area did have adequate lighting however).
The room's decor was fairly basic, white linens which gave it a bit of an elegant touch, but none of the sleeping "helpers" that others have listed (mask, spray, etc.) The bed/comforter and pillows were nice and soft, however not as incredible as the ones that we had just stayed in a few days earlier in Niagara Falls (different review/hotel).
"High speed" internet (wireless) was $10.95 a night, which isn't too bad, but there was a very low signal strength (1 bar). 
The front-desk, bellmen and concierge were friendly enough and it is nice that after check-out, they will store your luggage for the rest of your stay. The parking was terribly expensive - $54 for 25 hours - and that was "valet" on-site hotel - and I think it was a $10 surcharge for having a mini-van (takes up more space or whatever). I had heard it was $40, so I was a bit shocked. 
Overall, it wasn't a bad visit, but if I had to pay the $259, I would have expected a lot more.

title: “excellent hotel”
text: I was impressed! The lobby is spacious, the staff is friendly and very accomodating, the room is large and clean. We stayed on a Saturday night to see the Oriole's play the Yankees. The neighborhood was well policed and safe. Easy walking distance to Inner Harbor and Camden Yards. Explore further: go to Fells Point and Federal Hill! There is a new night club area on Market Place close by, but I did not see any problems walking at night with my family. It is a city!

title: “Worst Experience”
text: My son and I have stayed at the four seasons in Dublin, Bev. Hills, Westlake, and others and I must say, our experience in San Francisco (May 25, 2012 - May 28, 2012) has been the worst! As usual, I arrived and ordered a drink. The bartender looked at me with a blank expression and was rude (never experienced this before at any four seasons). Second, they placed my son's bed under the air vent, and I awoke to my son being congested. Third, when I asked to upgrade because the room they selected for us was too small, they hiked the price of the junior suites by 20% (more than the advertised price on the net). Again, I stay at the four seasons a lot and was shocked at the rude and essentially poor standards of this hotel. I will never stay here again and in fact will be checking out and staying at the Ritz while we end our short vacation in San Francisco. I am truly dissapointed with this hotel.

title: “Exceeded expectations”
text: Best in San Antonio! Fabulous rooms, lobby, restaurant and service. Will be my new home base in San Antonio.

title: “Small but nice...”
text:
Our family of four recently traveled to Chicago for a long weekend of sightseeing. We booked our trip on Priceline, but were concerned about the small room dimensions. Upon check in we requested that our room be changed to a room from one bed to a room with two beds. The front desk staff was very accommodating, and they were able to switch our room without issue.
Even the two bed room was small, but it was adequate. The beds were exceptionally comfortable, and the bathroom was a good size and well apportioned with amenities.
The lobby and bar area was very cozy, and a nice place to spend some time before retiring. The staff was very friendly, and we enjoyed our stay there.

title: “First impression disappointing but hotel won us over”
text: Although my family was disappointed when they first entered the small, worn rooms, by the end of our stay even my 15 year old daughter commented that she liked the hotel. We stayed 4 nights in a two room suite with the bathroom between the two rooms. By choosing this hotel, I was able to get individual twin beds for my two teenage children and a queen bed in a separate room for my husband and me- all at a budget price. The hotel staff was very nice and the quiet lamp-lit sitting room off the lobby usually had 3 or 4 people working on laptops. There was nothing sleek or modern about this place but the staff was very nice and helpful. The two elevators were quite small but not busy. I was worried about staying so far from Times Square but found pleasure in strolling the streets on the Upper West Side- something I wouldn't have experienced otherwise. The trip to Times Square was about 10 minutes and didn't seem that far after all.

title: “Excellent Times Square Family Hotel”
text: We stayed here for a week in July 2011, and it was fantastic. Our King Suite was a decent size and had a totally separate living room (with good sized sofabed) and bedroom.....so great for a family of 4. Staff were excellent - always responded quickly to the (minor) issues we had......and they give you a cookie for reporting a maintenance problem! Pretty much the same price as a regular hotel. Really quiet (on the 43rd floor) despite the buzz below. Excellent breakfast buffet (go for the inclusive rate though, as it would be $17 per person or something to purchase separately. This hotel is right on Times Square, so you do have to wade through thousands of people to get to the door......but it is a great location for travel up or down town.

title: “A Hidden Gem”
text: Stellar service & excellent location. We enjoyed the peaceful and beautiful grounds. The rooms were quiet and very comfortable. The walking trail & fitness were better than any hotel we have visited. Best hotel in Houston & we'll be back.

title: “All Perfect!”
text: Stayed only 1 night with my hysband and two kids but it felt like a week! The service and staff are amazing, kind, polite, helpful, always offering Fuji water, so nice! We were allowed to check in a little ealry so we could go over to a Bruins game, the concierge gentlman was great, as was the bell hop, and valet service... we settled into a spacious room with amazing views, the room was perfect! Dinner at the hotel was amazing, the pool and large hot tub area was a ton of family fun and room service breakfast the next morning was delicious, after my massage! Will definitely go back and highly recommend this hotel, well worth the money spent!

title: “Loved the Midtown”
text: Just back from Boston, stayed at the Midtown for 9 nights I could not fault it. The rooms are clean, the beds are very comfortable,plenty space in the room, asked for a room at the back and it was very quiet. The staff were helpful at all times. Its in a great location, there are three T stations nearby.The nearest for breakfast is Thorntons. Its ok , got sick of all the eggs on the menu.Plenty restaurants within 10 mins walk on Newbury Street and visit Uno on Boylston Street for dinner.

title: “Quiet location”
text: Had a large, clean room with two queen bed and a pull out sofa. Newly renovated bathroom. Nicely located close to subway system. Stayed earlier this year in midtown and this location was alot quieter. Great soda shop downstairs. Mudville bar across street in now closed. Great deli on church street. Nice neighbourhood. All very helpful and friendly staff. Walking distance to china town, WTC and wall street.

title: “Lassandra is awesome”
text: Every year we stay at this hotel and one of the deciding factors when it comes time to decide is Lassandra. We know we could stay at a less expensive hotel but feel the service and food prepared by Lassandra well make up the difference. She always remembers us and always knows what we want to eat and how we like it prepares. No matter how long her line is she always keeps it moving while still taking time to make her guests feel welcomed and important. She is a gem.

title: “Good hotel location okay”
text: Hotel is nice, modern, some rooms are smaller....modern decor. The train is loud in some of the rooms. The location is not that close to shops, etc on Michigan Ave. You either have to like to walk or take a cab. The Concierge Service and Front Desk service is great though. The Concierge, Dillon, set us up at a great local restaurant, Nia. Food was great and LOTS of it! If you don't mind being slightly out of the way, and want great service, this is a good choice. Also, the bed was very, very comfortable. Slept great!

title: “Excellent place to stay”
text: The rooms were spacious, the beds were absolutely terrific, the shower was powerful and the rate for the room for what we got was a tremendous value. The staff was attentive and nice. The lobby and the common area was beautiful. The property was located next to a very nice shopping area. I would definitely stay there again.

title: “Unremarkable & Odd”
text: I travel quite a bit and have stayed in a lot of hotels over the years (mostly for business). I took a chance on Aloft because of the great reputation of the "W" hotel brand. While not a bad hotel, it was an odd stay. It's clean and the staff was great. But the hotel itself was very strange. It was impossible to find and parking was horrible. Don't expect to get in and out quick. The rooms are starkly decorated. If felt like a jail cell. There was almost an inch of room under the door, so the noise in the hallways was crazy loud. There's no closet in the room, just a small curtained-off area. The shower has one wall that is frosted glass which faces the rest of your room. What?
