I understand that Aloft is not a traditional-type of hotel. It's "chic." But they missed the mark. It feels more like a cheap imitation of IKEA. It's also quite worn already. Lastly, there's no free breakfast - just a little store where you have to buy your breakfast items a la carte. I'd never stay here again. Very noisy, dark, and just plain odd. I suppose the only good thing about it is that it's located in the center of downtown. So everything is walking-distance. And again, no complaints about the staff or cleanliness. Oh the bed was comfortable.

title: “A nice Birthday stay”
text: My wife and I stayed there on 9-1 and 9-2 for my birthday. We had a very nice room with a view of the little lake. The front desk folks were very kind and the maids were very friendly. In wanted to take the pillows, they were so comfortable. They had a small but nice exercise room and pool which we enjoyed. I would definitely stay there again.

title: “Great hotel!!”
text:
Well located off the magic mile, the decor and room appointment superb, staff of the highest calibre, services that boggle the mind--what a stay i had early march 2005, truly memorable!!
The hotel is just simply one of the best i have stayed in from location to decor to staff to everything...i would highly recommend this hotel to anyone that wanted the best in surroundings and comfort.Well worth the price and very few hotels i have stayed in around the world could compare with all the peninsula has to offer....it is hard to describe absolute perfection!!

title: “Stay Away From This Filthy Place”
text: dishonest Management, dirty rooms, unfriendly staff - thats all I can say about this terrible place. I cannot understand, how some people find the rooms clean. You put your health in jeopardy if you stay there. When we complained about the discrepancy between the internet photos and the reality , the staff told us that everybody is lying on the internet and we have to pay for the room even if we don't stay.

title: “Great place to stay in Nob Hill”
text:
We spent two nights at this hotel and we are satisfied with our stay.
Pro: 1. good location, about 10 minutes walk from the union square.
 2. The staffs were courteous and helpful.
 3. Our room was spotless and well maintained. 
 4. We ordered late-night room service once, the food was pretty good and delivered promptly.
Con: 1. Small bathroom.
If you have to bring your car, you may park on the nearby street if you can find a spot. Or you may park across the street at Grace Cathedral which only charges $27 per day. A tip I got from TA.
http://www.gracecathedral.org/visit/getting-to-grace-cathedral/

title: “You could stay somewhere excellent for this price, but not in NYC!”
text:
In the perpetually up-and-coming-but-never-quite-arriving Chinatown/SoHo/Bowery area, this hotel is, for the money one pays, the best of a pretty bad lot. We spent two lots of one night at each end of the holiday here, averaging$160 per night, for which in the UK (and most of the rest of the world, if we're honest) you could stay somewhere really good with more than just a passing acquaintance with the traveller's comfort.
The rooms are incredibly small - on the last night we were in a windowless room [Grandpa used to tell me about those, I didn't think they still existed...]. The bathrooms were tiny and for the mobility impaired beware, there is no lift, only steep stairs and narrow coridoors. Trouble is, there's no point in moaning, because in dear old NYC you really have to pay over $250 per night to stay anywhere even half decent (as we did for other bits of the holiday). The alternative is to stay at an anonymous chain near one of the airports, so in this city, the adage "location, location, location" is truer than anywhere. As you don't come to NYC to sleep, it's a small, albeit expensive, sacrifice to make.
So in short, stay here if you must, but don't think too hard about the cost because for the location, I promise that you won't find anything better for the exhorbitant price. Welcome to NY!

title: “good hotel and good location”
text: We got a great Priceline rateof 75.00 a night. The room was very nice and the hotel was great too. You just have to be a little careful as the hotel is located on the edge of a rough area. But it is still in a very central location and i would recommend the hotel alot.

title: “Hidden Jewel”
text: Although I had read good reviews on this site I was still taken aback by the excellent location of this hotel - it really was on Times Square.We had a bit of a search to find the entrance but it was worth hunting for. The next surprise was the lack of noise from the street as we had a wonderful view of Times Square. By New York standards the room was spacious and well equipped. The bed was very comfy and the shower was super. Would certainly stay at this hotel again.

title: “A room with a view”
text: We treated ourselves to a long weekend at the Soho Grand over the Thanksgiving holiday. We flew all the way from CPH to my hometown and arrived at the hotel tired and jetlagged. Check-in was warm and friendly (remember this is NYC). Upon arrival, they noticed it was our birthdays (my man and I have birthdays 3 days apart) and delivered a deliciious chocolate cake to our room. How thoughtful. The service throughout our stay was extremely high. Room service was fast, delicious and expensive but worth it. The rooms are small. Again, this is New York where space is a commodity. But the small thoughtful amenities such as not only a cd player in the room, but also a varied selection of music, puts the Soho Grand a step above your traditional hotel. On Thanksgiving Day, we were treated to free-flowing hot pumpkin cider. Best of all was the view we woke up to every morning and went to sleep to every night. My hometown never looked better. The Soho Grand is what a downtown NYC hotel should be, plus a whole lot more.

title: “Solid, but not the chain's best”
text: Well furnished executive suite with a rather small bathroom given the size of the suite... especially for a woman with hair products and cosmetics. Service was wonderful and attentive as expected. The structure, however is a bit dated and in a so-so area that is not especially well located for strolling or shopping. Both the restaurant and bar were excellent.

title: “Small rooms but great location”
text:
I've stayed at this hotel a couple of times. It has a good location, being just off the main street in downtown area and only about 10 minutes walk along a well-lit, pedestrianised street to Beale Street area. It is a nice location, as one side of the hotel is the parking lot, and the other side opens out onto the main street where the trolley cars pass, and you can sit outside and watch the world go by.
Rooms are acceptable but not that big - a bit small if you're staying for more than a night I'd think. Staff were mixed - the person who checked me in was very 'cold' and unwelcoming, but another member of staff later on was very welcoming and addressed me by name each time we passed in the hotel.
Continental breakfast was OK - bagels, toast, yoghurts, pastries and a do-it-yourself waffle maker, but the lady on breakfast service was quite grumpy and unhelpful. If the breakfast was meant to run until 9am, at 8.30am when things were starting to run out, she refused to replenish anything - even when it was obvious that there was plenty more. I felt sorry for the people who came down after me as they would have gone hungry!!
Overall, 8/10. At least it was clean!

title: “Brilliant stay, great location, fantastic time.”
text: Well, what can I say, what a fantastic, brilliant little hotel, excellent value for money, me and the wife stayed here for a week in Jan 2012 and had a excellent stay, couldn't ask for anything more, great location not far from the underground, just a 2min walk, friendly staff, clean room, what more can I say.... the only problem was internet connection was rubbish, but that shouldn't put u off..... I would defo recommend and most defo stay there again... 5 stars.*****. Thx you Best Western....

title: “Homeless People in an Upscale Hotel”
text:
Nice hotel, great location, decent service, terrible security. I was staying on the 15th floor and went to walk down the stairs to use the vending machines on the 15th floor. I ran into several homeless people sleeping in the stair well. Where was security?
This is a first tier hotel, with equivalent rates. This lack of security is frightening.

title: “Why not try for perfection ?”
text:
The Park Central is our home away from home in New York. We come regularly from France to visits NY's rich cultural life, restaurant scene and we're known to do "some" shopping. For us the central location and the price/quality relation of Park Central are deciding factors.
True, it's a large place but staff really try and give individual service. On a longer stay (ours was six nights) you can have a room according to your wishes (we always receive a quiet room, at the back). We heard that the hotel is getting completely renovated next year. Let's hope they do not "renovate" the rates. i'm curious to see the result.
What can they (definetly) do better? The departure scene is nearly always messy, disorganised, with pushy taximen and the hotel doorman, who should be there to help you but participates in the general mix-up. This is the only hotel in the whole world that i know of where you are charged exorbitantly for holding your luggage. From the morning checkout to our afternoon/evening departure, we paid 30$ plus tips. Yes thirty dollars, for safekeeping of our bags betweem 11am and 3 pm. After having been thus ripped off, we were introduced on the (ice cold) pavement) to a collection of drivers (taxi and hotel limo) all hustling for business plus bellman and doorman joining in this large cacophony. I swore: "never again". How can such a nice hotel where we've been coming for four yeras repeatedely, give you a showoff that is unworthy of it's name and the quality of service it stands for. I gave the hotel management three weeks to answer my email with a request for an explanantion on their departure policy. In the absence of any reaction my adivice is YES stay at Park Central BUT BEWARE and make your own exit arrangements. Need a good ripoff? Give them your bags to hold !!!

title: “I decided to ignore reviews and BIG MISTAKE !!!!!”
text:
Where do I start ! Well how about every floor flooded including stairways. Wet stairways. Broken elevator so you have to climb 4 floors to your room. Dirty sheets, and bathroom, dressing table wallpaper and bathroom cabinet in ill repair doors falling off. Trying to grab coffee and it is instant with a spoon in it for multiple users. What about trying to get a donut at the front desk and have the carpenters and elevator repair people go before you. Breakfast is as other reviewers said on a small counter in office. Bananas were green, there is no place to sit and eat you have to bring back to your room. 
We had to leave unexpectedly because of a family death and they would not refund our last day. We stayed two of our three days thinking we would make the most of it. We reserved superior king rooms, but were given double bed and when asked them why they offered no reason. Just said well you got two beds......we wanted the King Room we reserved. 
We left so fast because of our family members death that we forgot our car and house keys in the room. We called the hotel to try and recover them and were told that the maids have a separate office that is only open 8am to 4 pm. The manager and front desk people have no idea what is lost or put in lost and found only the maid. So no one else is aware of things lost or able to recover them for you. 
Noisy street, no restaurants that are affordable within 7 blocks. This hotel is a 7 block up and down hike to the wharf and other activities. Office staff are not at all helpful or friendly. There are other afordable hotels nearby. Holiday Inn , Holiday Inn Express, Sheraton, and Radisson pay a little more and be closer to the activities. San Francisco weather can be cloudy cold and windy walking can be unpleasant. 
I have stayed all over the world including Europe, Mexico, and Middle East this is the worse ever. We would have stayed our three days had not the death occurred. They absolutely refused to refund our last day stay, so if you book be prepared to stay or loose. Very rude and bad business practices.

title: “YUMMY BREAKFAST included!”
text: My family and I very much enjoyed our stay here. I think the best part was the breakfast! It was delicous! My family of 5 got to eat in the restaurant located inside the hotel for FREE! It was a buffet style breakfast with bacon, eggs, grits, potatoes, biscuits and gravy, waffles, toast, danishes, cereals, assortments of fruit, yogurts, and juices. It was delicious

title: “great location, great lobby, nice room”
text:
Stayed just one night at the barclay, got a great price comparably speaking to the other hotels in new york, and that made the decision. The reception was very nice, even though we came in quite late...the room was comfortable, bathroom absolutely needs redoing, so small and around 35 years old. Very convenient for those of us who do not want to spend a million dollars on a cup of coffee in the morning, cafes, convenience stores right across the street. 
Did not use any other amenities there except to sleep. The bed was very comfortable, the only downside I encountered was that I had a triple and the sofa bed had not been set up, so at 1 in the morning, housekeeping had to come to bring linens, and together we set the bed to expediate. - I could not understand why the third bed was not set up in our 1 bedroom room, since that is how it was booked and guaranteed. otherwise, quite pleasant stay and absolutely a great location.

title: “Perfect base camp to explore San Diego”
text:
What attracted us to this hotel was the availability of "kids suites". this seems to be a fairly new marketing thing, but a good one. What this place does is include a nice bunk bed (twin on top, full below) in the room with a std queen. My two teenage daughters absolutely will not sleep in the same bed anymore. Our option has been large (and expensive) suites to this point, so, this option seemed like a good alternative. The kids suite worked out perfectly. No fights... The room is average size, nothing special. Very clean... Well maintained, older fixtures, plenty of hot water. Appeared to have new wall unit AC. big mini fridge, DVD player, 32" TV, Microwave, room safe, Nicely kept landscaping etc. Attentive staff in the office. Clean heated (8 ft !) pools and hot tub... 
Make no mistake, this is after all, a motor hotel... doors on outside facing parking lot etc. However, if you are there to sleep and see the sights, it is just fine. Metros and other trendy folk will not be happy with this hotel. Look towards Balboa Park for the hip neighborhoods... However, if you have kids and you plan to be spending all your time at Sea World, the Zoos, Legoland etc. its tough to do better.

title: “Great choice for visiting NYC”
text:
Really happy with our stay at the Distrikt. It is very clean, modern and comfortable. It’s a small boutique hotel, with only 5 rooms per floor, generally quiet. We booked a view room and ended up on the top floor, with a great view of the west side, Hudson river and lights near Times Square a few blocks away.
The room itself is adequately sized, not spacious but not cramped, with an extremely comfortable bed and good lighting. Amenities include an iron and board, Keurig coffee maker with two coffee and two tea pods complimentary per day, and free wifi. The bathroom was nicely appointed and a decent size, with lots of counter space for your stuff, great water pressure in the shower and a good hairdryer. On arrival we found two (packaged) brownies as a welcome, and each evening the turndown service includes a couple chocolate squares and a card indicating the next day’s weather, a nice touch. 
The property doesn’t have a lot of facilities, other than a bar/restaurant on the main floor. We only had one breakfast there, it was good and not overpriced for a city hotel – you can get the continental for $10 which includes fruit, cereal, yogurt, pastries, and hard boiled eggs, or they also have other items to order off the menu. They offer free coffee in the lobby in the morning, and two flavors of iced tea in the afternoons. There are also three computers available along the front of the lobby.
Service was friendly and helpful; we got a great dinner recommendation one night. We didn’t ask a lot but they were great about helping with the questions we did have. And they regularly offer some extra fun surprises for their guests, such as having a food truck out front giving out free food at “happy hour” – the day we arrived, they were doing made-to-order ice cream sandwiches from 4 to 6. Yum! On the other hand, they lack a few of the basics one generally can count on in larger hotels – no postage stamps for sale at the front desk, and it was hit or miss whether we could get change for a $20 bill. 
The midtown location is very convenient for tourist activities. A few blocks from Times Square and the theater district, and very near the starting point for the hop-on, hop-off busses. Being right across the street from the Port Authority bus terminal, it’s very easy to use the subway. That also means you have all the crowds of people going in & out, but they’re around the corner, not on the side facing the hotel. And yes, there is a parole office on this block, which sometimes had a line of people outside, but it never felt uncomfortable or unsafe walking back to our hotel at any time of day or night. There are three other hotels immediately adjacent to the Distrikt, all tall skinny properties lined up in a row. And just up 9th Avenue begins the Hells Kitchen restaurant row, several blocks with a variety of good restaurants.
All in all, I highly recommend the Distrikt – it’s a great base for exploring the city, appropriately priced and very comfortable, with a fun and welcoming atmosphere.

title: “On the Fence”
text:
My room was on the function room floor, it was strange to walk out of my guestroom to see a buffet station set near my door. 
Bathroom was beautiful, the bath tub was a nice size and at first the water pouring from the ceiling was fun but it splashed all over the glass wall. It's more of a conversation piece but impractical. The Molten Brown shampoos were mounted on the wall in the shower instead of those environmentally unfriendly miniature bottles. Somehow the germaphobe side of me was grossed out by the thought of someone else using products from the same bottle.
For a dark rainy city the decor was a little too gloomy. It's a chic colour scheme but walking in at night after dinner I was left with a lonely feeling.
Staff were unimpressionable, neither great nor bad. The gym didn't have windows, I prefer to see natural light when I workout.

title: “NOT WORTH”
text:
Prices Are Very High We Pay $277.00 For Two Nights When You pay same money to stay in Holiday inn or even one of the Marriot hotels chain , I been on those before.
restroom is dirty you actually see mold in shower and toilet, and that bad smell from the carpet was bad.
I will definitely not going back to this hotel. the only good thing about this is the location not around the corner but no more than 10 minutes drive..
Unfortunately we dis online reservation too late and this was the only hotel available, no wonder why.
I will not recomenr this particular location of la quinta.

title: “A gem near Central Park!”
text:
The well-situated Le Parker Meridien is a good choice for both business and leisure travelers. It has easy access to the Subway and is within walking distance of Central Park, Broadway, major museums, and other tourist attractions. 
Other than the burger joint, the hotel restaurant and the bar are a bit pricey, but there is a very good Thai restaurant right next door--not to mention plenty of other eateries nearby. I didn't try the room service so can't comment.
I've stayed in both a deluxe king room and a double room. The deluxe king had a fabulous view of Central Park, and by New York standards, it's quite spacious. I find the firm bed very comfortable, and I like the simple, modern decor. The bathroom was clean and nice. As for the double room, it comes with two twin beds, not double beds, making it unsuitable for more than two people. The room also seemed smaller. As much as I like the hotel, I wouldn't book a room here if I needed two beds. 
The service was friendly and efficient. There are plenty of bell staff around to help you, and housekeeping responded swiftly to my request. 
There is a small but lovely swimming pool near the rooftop and a huge gym, neither of which I was able to check out on my first two visits. But I hope to during my next stay!

title: “Wish we could have stayed another night”
text:
We chose this hotel due to the free parking and closeness to the airport. Upon arrival we were immediately greeted by the friendly hotel staff. Easy check in, clean, spacious room, comfortable bed. We arrived late but needed to eat dinner and we walked next door and had dinner. There were 4 restaurants to chose from that you did not have to get in your car and drive to. We took the food back to the hotel ate and went to bed for our early 5am wake up call for the airport. 
They say on their web site that breakfast is not served until 6am but they have everything out shortly after 5am for all of the early travelers. Quick easy shuttle service to the airport and, easy pick up service from the airport to the hotel. Great place to stay.

title: “On the Riverwalk”
text:
I'm always a little biased at a convention hotel when I only have to pay the bulk negotiated rate but here goes anyway. The hotel itself was what you would expect from a Hyatt. The staff was helpful and I never had to wait. The room had everything you could ask for except free wi fi. The hotel is at least a four star and reflects it.
Now let's discuss location. The hotel is on the Riverwalk. An escalator in the lobby takes you directly to the river level and you will find yourself on a relatively quiet beautfilly landscaped section of the riverwalk. Walking about a block along the riverwalk you can turn into a little inlet that includes an upscale mall and the landing for the guided tour riverboats with a handful of decent restaurants as well the usual mall fare. The mall also is an airconditioned shortcut to the Alamo. If the mall doesn't appeal, continue a block or so along the river through a nicely landscaped walkway along the riverbank and enter the original Riverwalk where you will find wall to wall restaurants , bars and gift/souvenir shops and large crowds and another Hyatt which you should not confuse with our Grand Hyatt a few blocks away. You could stay for a week, never eat the same place and not be disappointed. This heavily commercialized section lasts about four or five blocks before reaching the main river channel which has been recently landscaped and the walkway continues which you can walk along if you want a little exercise and thinning crowds. 
Note: My favorite restaurant meal in the whole world is the Shrimp Paisano at Paisano's located in the middle of the restaurant section. We go there every time we come to San Antonio and often when coming through from Austin on the way home. If you decide to try it, don't take the tables between the walkway and the river as I may be waiting for one.

title: “Worst Chain Hotel in Chicago”
text:
Where to start?
The rooms are shabby. The beds are undersized. The bedding smelled of bleach. The elevator is impossible. Valet parking took 1/2 hour with nobody ahead of us. Staff is pleasant enough but has no knowledge of the city.
We booked this due to its contingency to DePaul University, but that (relative) convenience did not make up for everything else.
Extremely disappointing.

title: “Wow what a location...”
text: Great location - I did not stay at this hotel but I did get a tour and WOW! This is a beautiful property. Great location on the river like it's partners Westin & Sheraton Hotels. Wonderful work out area and again, wonderful bedding. Views are killer & staff is great.

title: “Had a great experiance from strat to finish!”
text: Lots of fun on this staycation! We are manhatanites and want to do it again...

title: “Handy to everything”
text: Arrived in New York after a red-eye from LA, expecting the worst with 7 hours to check-in. To my surprise we were offered a choice of 3 rooms immediately. Stayed in the newer block which houses the pool on the tenth floor. The view of MANHATTAN at night from the rooms and pool are worth the money. The subway is one block away, buses pass straight by, and a taxi to Times Square was $5. The rooms were quite spacious and live up to the photographs. McDonalds and Starbucks close handy. No problems moving in Manhattan, and the subway was handy for lower Manhattan journeys. All in all, a great stay!!

title: “Good location”
text: Stayed two nights this past week. I would have given this property an excellent were it not for the soft, back breaking beds. Rooms were comfortable, although the heat was a bit uneven. Living room fine, bedroom cold. As with most other Staybridge properties, breakfast was above average. Great location, as The Fishers, Carmel area is more upscale than other Indy suburbs in the best part of Indy area. One exit south on I-69 is 82nd St with tons of shopping, including Mall at Keystone Crossing, with Saks and even a Cheesecake Factory. Ask if front desk can call ahead to put you on a waiting list to save time. One exit north to 116th St is downtown Fishers where there is an Original Pancake House. Skip the hotel breakfast one time and treat yourself! Hotel is 25 minutes from Indy airport, and 20 minutes to downtown. I recommend this property!

title: “Family fun in New York”
text: Stayed at the Waldorf for seven nights at the beginning of April 2012. We are a family with teenagers. The hotel was fabulous,location was great my only advice would be book for at least four nights when visiting New York there is just so much to fit in. we stayed for a full week and still didn't do everything.

title: “Great hHotel with a fun atmosphere”
text: The hotel was awsome, the guestrooms were just renovated and they will blow your mind. The staff is awsome and you really can't beat the location. Next time you visit Seattle you have to stay at this hotel.

title: “Better than expected”
text: Reviews of this hotel varied from very good to poor, so we didn't really know what to expect, and were pleasantly surprised by a good sized room, very comfortable king sized bed, very clean. When we complained about the toilet running on and on, it was fixed the next day. We were on the 2nd floor, by the parking lot (very sparsely used) and so had a view of Alcatraz and Fisherman's Wharf, which we enjoyed. We found it very convenient for shopping as we could pop down one floor and be on Jefferson Street, right in the middle of shopping and restaurants. I wouldn't recommend the IHOP - too busy and not great food. Johnny Rockets makes a good breakfast, and try Boudin's for Clam Chowder in a sourdough bread bowl. Close to the tour buses, Pier 39 and the Alcatraz ferry (which I recommend).

title: “Great place to stay..”
text: We enjoyed our stay at this new hotel. Staff was very friendly and helpful. Julie at the front desk is perfect for this job! It was cute in the morning because two very nice college-age guys were in charge of breakfast. They kept everything well stocked and fresh. We spent the day at the U.S Whitewater complex which was just 15 minutes away and had a great time with our 11, 13, and 17 year old children. Don't miss this attraction. We will definitely stay at this hotel again if we are in the area. A+ for a great hotel. BTW, there is a Walmart, McDonalds, Panera Bread, Applebee's and several other restaurants just up the road.

title: “This a gem of a hotel in a perfect location.”
text: We liked everything about this hotel: Location, staff, amenities, restaurant, bar, etc. It is a small comfortable hotel on Union Square. The rooms are small, but that really didn't bother us at all. They are very well arranged and worked just fine. The decor is nice, the beds comfortable, the hotel is well maintained, the wireless access works, the restaurant serves a good breakfast (the only meal we actually had there), the staff is pleasant and helpful. Also, we got a great deal--look at the specials on-line! Our absolutely only problem was that the room was overly warm the first night we were there, even thoughwe turned the thermostat way down and ran the ceiling fan. We discovered the second night we could open the window because it had a safety stop on it. We will return.

title: “Good Place To Stay!”
text:
We had a very nice stay on 9/17-19/12. The rooms,staff,breakfast were very nice and clean. We were able to walk to the doctors office and Methodist Hospital.
We had only two small complaints, the indoor pool was cold and the hotel really needs
better parking or atleast a way to come in instead of walking around to the front.
Will be staying again when we come to the Medical Center area.

title: “Great hotel for the business or convention traveler!”
text:
I have stayed at this hotel a few times on business. Terrific location near energy buildings, reliable wifi, terrific food and service at breakfast. The beds are comfy and the rooms are nicely laid out.The location is an easy walk to many businesses and the hotel is connected to the tunnel system for those scorching Houston summer days! Drawbacks are the restaurants are on the pricey side and parking was $28 a day. Don't rent a car if you don't need one. Shuttle service from IAH airport to hotel is $23 each way. There is a free bus system in the downtown area Mon - Fri and a rail system to take you to museums.
More light in the rooms would be welcome. Tough to put on make up with the dim lights in room and bathroom.

title: “Super Place -- One of my favorite hotels”
text: Have stayed here on business many times and just love this hotel. Location is awesome + super cool terrace and bar at the top overlooking ballpark. My only complaint, I suppose, would be the $38/night for parking. Seems high, but other than that, you cannot go wrong here!

title: “Adequate but not for the business traveler”
text:
I stayed one night at the Hard Rock in a standard double room. I chose the hotel because a block of rooms had been reserved for the rate of $219. I have stayed in the Hard Rock Las Vegas at least six times and liked it very much. This hotel was barely adequate. I like good contemporary decor but this room was dark and rather depressing. Everything was some shade of gray (including bedcovers), which would have been fine if there had been decent lighting. The lighting was terrible. Do not expect to get any work done in your room unless you bring your own lamp. I called down to the front desk twice because I could not figure out how to turn one light on and no one ever came. 
The bed was comfortable and the bathroom was nice (cool vanity) but don't expect to take a bath because there was no tub. The prompt room service was the high point. They brought me a nice fruit plate with my continental breakfast for no extra charge (I had not asked for it), the juice was fresh squeezed, and the coffee hot.

title: “Staffs are very helpful. Shuttle driver is very nice”
text: overall it is good. I did not give 5 stars because of one night stay in smoking room. The smells made us sick.

title: “Affordable and Good Quality in Great Downtown Location”
text: Friendly staff, clean & good size room. On Grand and Bowery in Chinatown. Loved it!

title: “Perfect Stay Except for One Thing That's Easy To Fix”
text:
We travel to Chicago once a quarter and plan to stay at the Trump Tower from now on. the location is perfect and the view from my room, which I am looking out of now is sublime. The service has been super friendly and my room is decked out with well-thought out amenities. My bathtub is the nicest ever. It is modern with very luxurious spa products but has a homey touch with the shelf you can rest your juicy novel one while you soak. The pillow menu is fun and the choices of snacks and drinks in the mini-bar is eclectic in a good way. in short, the room is as nice as it gets.
I love to exercise and was very impressed to see the Technogym weights and the yoga DVD included in the room. We have a spa room and there actually is room if you were inclined to workout in the room. I decided to take advantage of the excellent workout facilities and attend the spin classes that were offered. 
Sonya, the spin instructor, is as good as any instructor I have ever had. She is very motivating and her winning personality along with the super friendly people who regularly attend made me come back the next day. 
So here's my complaint: the temperature in the spin studio is almost unbearably hot to work out in. There is an extra charge of $30 to take the class so I am hoping that the management will use my $60 to buy some ceiling fans or even standing fans to help circulate the air in that stuffy space. I am hoping to see them when I come back in the fall!

title: “Everything on a budget”
text: Stayed in Sept for 3 days .Great location ,great rooms ,great staff, best hotel we stayed in during 3 week stay in the States and Canada. What more can you say. Ladies and gent on the front desk were really helpful , room was great for the price (we were at the front and noise from St was not a problem). Good breakfast in the morning included. Easy walk to the space needle and other things there ,easy walk to the water front and centre of town. Would stay again ,Seattle was great and really nice city .

title: “Major Renovation Necessary”
text:
Im a Starwood Preferred member who has stayed at many of the Starwood hotels. I made a reservation to stay at the Westin Grand in DC to celebrate a birthday. I booked directly through the hotel website.
 Entering my room on the 7th floor, I was horrified to see the condition of the room. The walls looked as is someone had thrown food on them. The wall over the window clearly had water damage. Two outlet faceplates were hanging and the evacuation notice of the back of the door has been ripped off. The carpet also had stains over 90%. 
I called and asked to be switched to a different room, which the hotel accommodated. That room, also on the 7th floor, was no better. There were stains on the walls, baseboards and again, the carpet was badly stained. I asked for the manager come to my room to see my issues. He informed me the hotel was in need of a makeover and would try and find me a cleaner room but that the carpets all over the hotel were basically going to be the same. 
I informed the manager that I was not going to stay in the hotel and wanted a refund. The only good experience was how willing the manager was to refund my money. 
I completely understand that hotels need renovations but to not inform travelers of the current state of the hotel or have the room rate reflect that is completely misleading.

title: “Great for what it is”
text:
This is a great motel for a great price. Where i think they go wrong is by calling it a hotel. It is not, so if you arrive expecting concierge services, luggage assistance etc you will be disappointed. Where they excel is being a fantastic motel; so please arrive with expectations with the price you pay.
A somewhat disappointing experience was arriving at 9:30am (well before checkin time I know) and walking into the front office to see the general manager having a personal conversation with a friend and having to ask for assistance with checking in. Whilst this was then provided very quickly and my bags stored, i did however feel a bit of an annoyance as he was clearly mid conversation. Neither the less I stored my bags and was told they would try and have my room by midday (before checkin). When I returned at around 1pm the room was ready and I was offered either a first floor or ground floor room. No luggage assistance was offered ( but this is a motel remember, so was perfectly acceptable to me.) 
The room was a perfectly acceptable motel room. Clean and comfortable ( but window looked onto corridor as per motel room). The toilet seat was broken and tv not operative when I entered but within 15 (without calling) an engineer was there to fix it.
The location was perfectly suitable and whilst an easy walk I chose to take the subway to take time to get into the thick of Hollywood and was very easy to use. As far as noise complaints go, I never heard a peep. One night I had my tv turned on and was called fro front desk saying a neighbor had called and the tv was disturbing their sleep. I need to thank front office for being so forthright with me. I never wanted to disturb anyone and turned it down immediately. That shows to me that if there is ever a noise issue that front desk will deal with it straight away.
One other thing I must mention that absolutely blew me away for this level of hotel/motel was the housekeeping staff and the general manager of the hotel each went round all the rooms before going home to ask how they were enjoying their stay and if they needed anymore towels/ soaps etc. This simple little touch truly made me feel at home and that the staff cared. After 4 nights of check ups from the general manager before he left I felt like he truly cared about his guests (checkin experience more than forgiven). Not even at a Four Seasons has the general manager of the property accompanied housekeeping staff during their final duties before leaving for home. What a difference that made to this reviewer! Well done!
Was this a great hotel? No. Was this a fantastic motel? YES

title: “Worst hotel of its kind in 57th Manhattan. a disgrace to Holiday Inn”
text:
This hotel is a nothing short of disgrace. We stayed for two days. first Hotel appear to be Ok from outside. dont be fooled by pictures you see on internet. Room was with torn wall papers and king size bed that looked like so worn that middle of beds mid section was sunked in. The worst of all regarding this hotel is that the toilet. I had to hold down the pressure switch for more then a min. to flush even then it was poorest of most basic preparedness for any guest. 10th floor hall way was worn and requires a extensive renovation. Add to this, breakfast is nothing short of "slob on the plate" with over charged bill. NO I am not a hotel spy or other hotel owner or employee. I was just shocked to see What they call "HOTEL" exist in place like manhattan 57th street near most upscale area.
Its nothing short of disgrace for holiday Inn chain. Parking fee was 25 flat but attendant is rude that when asked to inspect the car before they take the car to garage, they get easily offended ( which all should do) handled car very roughly flooring the car infront of guest. This hotel needs to be SHUT DOWN. I AM NOT KIDDING DO NOT GO THERE even they ay price is 94 dollars a night. NOT WORTH A PENNY.

title: “Wonderful Stay”
text: I stayed at Park Hyatt for one free night and it was the most wonderful stay! In the past year I have stayed at so many different hotel chains and I must admit this was by far the best. One would expect that because the room was free you would not receive such good service but not at Park Hyatt, the staff was great. This includes a young lady coming to our door asking if we needed any ice! Never has that happened. The restaurant/bar offers great service and light fare if that is what you need. Hilton, you have some work to do! Oh let me not forget I asked for a late check-out fully expecting I would pay a fee but was told "no problem" and no fee!!

title: “So glad I found this place!”
text: I stayed at Hotel des Arts only one night, but I arrived early in the morning and met a friendly woman at the front desk who offered to keep my luggage secure while I attended my conference, etc. The hotel was a quick walk from BART and in a great spot for me to get around to the places I wanted to see. When I was able to check in in the late afternoon I was given an old fashioned key (fun!) and sent up to a comfy, clean, and quiet room. Claw foot bath tub, beautifully hand-painted walls, plenty of towels, pillows, soaps/lotion, and big windows. If you like being surrounded by art, and dealing with laid back but professional and helpful hotel staff, Hotel des Arts is the place.

title: “Arrogant staff, "Business Class" not worth it.”
text:
I stayed for 3 days with Business Class upgrade promotion.
1. There was virtually no wireless reception in my room. When I pointed that out to the front desk, all they did was to give me a 1-800 number that I was supposed to call. When I said what is "Business Class" worth if I don't have internet, she said I have to call the 1-800 number.
2. When I had my breakfast at "Raffles" on Friday, I asked the staff there how long they will serve breakfast on Saturday. Answer: "All Day". When I went for breakfast on Saturday at 12noon, the waitress told me that my "Business Class" breakfast voucher was only valid until 11am. But neither was that stated on the voucher nor was I told at check in or by the waitress on Friday. I went to the front desk again. Answer: "In every hotel in the world breakfast is only in the morning." When I said that then it should either be told me on arrival or stated on the voucher, the answer was: "These vouchers are printed centrally for all US. It would be too much effort to change them individually". 
3. As mentioned, I had a late day on that Saturday and went for breakfast around 12noon. As a result, nobody ever came back to make my room, neither were my amenities in the bathroom replenished. 
4. When checking out any paying a bill of almost $900, I do not expect from a hotel of your class to have to pay $2 for storage of my suitcase until departure.
All in all: Wonderful room, excellent location. But the service really made it difficult to like the stay. And that is supposed to be business class?

title: “Clean, great location”
text: Can't beat the location for the price. Central location and yet quiet. Room was teeny tiny but if you are expecting big and posh at this price, you are in the wrong city. Staff was generally friendly. However, before our stay we called to verify we could use Travelers Checks and cash them and were assured we could. When were stayed there suddenly the story changed and they would not take them. This caused a bad inconvenience. But, in the scheme of things, that is not a big thing. Breakfast was decent. At times it seemed like a youth hostel as a lot of young people would congregate in the small lobby and made it difficult to navigate. Again, at the price I paid, I was easily able to overlook this. Would definitely stay there again.

title: “Comfy great experience!!!”
text: I cant say enough about this hotel stay- Pros: Price and great for the rooms we got, clean and spacious! We were on the very top floor and there was a beautiful view- Please see pictures attaches. the room was clean and spotless. bathroom had a small both jaccuzzi and was roomy as well-AC/heater worked great, beds were sofft and fresh feeling! it was like sleeping on a cloud. balcony was nice and lot of tables to sit on outise to enjoy view, desk area to sit and write if needed. Guy in the front desk was friendly and continetial breakt fast was good. Easy to get taxis.Cons: the breakfast area was cramped and the location seems to be a bit far from attractions- other than that great stay!

title: “Perfect”
text: We stayed at the Westin for the Women's Big Ten Tournament. Every staff member went out of their way to make sure we had everything we needed and that our stay was a good one. The room was spacious and clean. The location downtown is within walking distance to many restaurants and shops and the mall.

title: “Rude staff”
text:
The hotel in itself was fine. We had 2 rooms and the rooms were nice by New York standards- spacious enough, well-lit etc... The location was decent too.
I had made the reservation over the phone which they apparently spelled wrong, so when I called to confirm my reservation- they had a hard time finding it. Then when they did, I figured that they would correct it... but apparently they didn't. The front desk staff was rude and asked me several times if I had booked HIS hotel. It got resolved but he was rude.

title: “what a great hotel with a great location!!!”
text: I originally booked this hotel, because it was about a block from Lucas Oil Stadium not expecting too much from it. But when we arrived we were greeted by the front desk by Kisha and Wanda. They were very nice and had a great attitude towards us even though there were a bunch of football fans coming and going. The breakfast was really good along with the food that they served after the game late at night. The customer service was excellent and I should know. I am an overnight hotel manager in Chicago. The staff was the best.

title: “Harmless but unispiring”
text: Relatively well located in Foggy Bottom and not too far from Georgetown, the Marriott is a straightorward business hotel, which does little wrong but little to inspire. The bedrooms are well sized and standard Marriott fair, but the pool and gym are small. Breakfast buffet is fine, though service is less than wholly attentive.

title: “Excellent Austin Stay”
text: We had a wonderful time at the Four Seasons Austin. We actually live in town and were looking for a get away sans kids. We had a very nice room facing the river with a balcony. The hotel is older, but has been well maintained/updated. The bed was super comfortable and the room was nicely decorated. The bar is a perfect place to hang out and have a drink. It was a romantic setting and a great place for us to relax after dinner. The lobby and bar area were decorated for the Christmas season which added to the magic of our stay. The gym is well appointed and had everything I needed to get a great workout. Being right on the lake also allowed us to pull away for a morning run which is a must while visiting. The spa is small, but our service was excellent as you would expect at Four Seasons. This hotel is probably one of the best luxury hotels in Austin because of the location being right on the lake and close enough to downtown activities to walk.

title: “Reminded me of an abandoned, haunted house”
text:
At check in, the receptionist was new and, after concluding a personal phone call, admitted she was having trouble processing my reservation. Next day, the manager had to do it all over again.
My room smelled extremely musty and moldy (dust and active mold) and the window faced a dirty, empty lot next door -- with the sun streaming in all evening, closing all the curtains tightly was the only option (although the hotel was not full and other rooms were available on the other side, reception was empty and I was just too tired to care). 
Sleep was difficult because a live band was playing music until near midnight...next door or down stairs, I don't know where it was coming from, but it was loud, annoying, and guaranteed I wouldn't be back.
Room service was good, though - fast and delicious food. :)

title: “Wonderful...Perfect Location”
text: This was me and my husband's first time visiting New York. We were unsure of where to stay. We just knew we wanted to be close to restaurants and shopping. EVERYONE walks in New York. So put your walking shoes on. When we arrived at 60 Thompson I was extremely impressed. This boutique hotel is super sheek and elegant. The service was magnificent. The location is PERFECT. Its close to everything. When you a walk out of the hotel there are boutiques everywhere and a ton of eating places. The hotel is only a couple of blocks away from Broadway where a lot of the major clothing and shoe stores are located. We could not have a picked a more perfect hotel. There is also a roof top bar that is ultra hip and has a beautiful view of the city. When we return to New York we will certainly stay here again. Also the rooms are pretty pricey but we got a good deal by booking it on Quickbook. It cut the price of the room in half.

title: “Will not return”
text:
My husband and I were in town for a wedding. We arrived just before the 3pm check-in and the lobby was a mess; there were so many people waiting to get checked in. We were told we could have a smoking room if we wanted to check in right away. We decided to wait for a non smoking room and checked in at 3:15 (there were still TONS of people standing around because their rooms weren't ready). 
The hallways were so tiny- you couldn't walk 2 wide in this hallway! The room was very tiny as well. The bathroom had no counter- just a ledge that was maybe 4" wide. Absolutely ridiculous. To sit on the toilet, you had to keep your arms tucked tight and your left knee went under the sink. Unreal. And we booked a queen but when we got to our room, it was a full. I called the desk and they confirmed that yep- it was a full. They apologized and said they didn't note my reservation with a queen and the queens were all taken. The desk receptionist then said there were people waiting and she couldn't discuss this.
We will NOT stay at this hotel again!

title: “Great Hotel - but very very noisy”
text:
The hotel is in a good location just 10mins walk from Penn Station.
We checked in early and asked for a high room so they gave us one on the top floor (32nd). The view is not perfect because of a building opposite but it is good nonetheless.
The room was very good and had everything we needed in it.
Problems with the room were the water pressure on the shower kept cutting out in the morning. Probably due to the number of people using it. Not sure if this is an issue for all hotels in the area or not?
Second issue was the thin walls. On the first night we could hear some muffled chat next door. On the second night we had some Spanish speakers who seemed to be shouting at one another for an hour or so.
Third issue was the hotel only has 3 lifts for 32 floors, each with 10 rooms on them. As a result you can be waiting for 5-15mins for a lift depending on how busy things are. 
If I did it again I would have got a room on a lower floor and used the stairs.
Breakfast was a little basic with just a burger & scrambled eggs available as the hot option. Also a queue for the toasters. Was not that impressed so we missed breakfast for our subsequent 2 mornings?
Having said that the hotel is in prime location for sightseeing and the Times Square/Rockefeller/Empire State area is all in walking distance. 
The corner of 40th/8th Ave has the port authority and a Porn DVD shop. As with any commuter terminal there are people hanging about and some of the look dogey but we never felt threatened or anything. Cabs seem pretty cheap so you can always get one back if you feel worried.
All in all a good place to stay but bring some earplugs and stay on one of the lower floors.

title: “totally remodeled”
text: If you are needing some place to stay overnight at the airport this is a great property. The hotel staff was friendly, curteous and helpful all at the same time, the rooms were completely renevated and have a new contemporary look with plasma tv's, apple ipod decks etc. Overall my stay at the hotel was excellent oh i forgot about the beds they were comfy as well. This would be a good choice and the rates arent that bad either.

title: “GREAT FAMILY SPOT OR ROMANTIC GETAWAY”
text: My entire family stayed at the Hotel Lincoln for a St. Patrick's Day renunion. Some of us in family suites, with kids others in king bedded rooms. Each room was decorated with its own special flare,beautiful colors, lots of texture and interesting artwork, and truly comfortable beds and sofa beds, We also rented a hospitality suite with large table (seated 20) plus TV's and recliners so that we could all hang out together and the kids had some room to play. It just could not have ben better for our group. The staff was very helpful and friendly. We had food delivered some nights and we ate delicious breakfasts in Elaine's cafe downstairs and a special Sunday bruch in the restaurant Perennial Vivant also on premises. Definitely our hotel of choice for all upcoming family get togethers and romantic getaways. Highly recommend it.

title: “Carpet should be replaced”
text: Hotel has undergone a beautiful renovation; however, the cleanliness is lacking. The floor in my bathroom was not clean, and the carpet was terribly stained in several areas. One lamp bulb was out and the tv's are old. The bedding was clean though.

title: “Best hotel in Detroit”
text:
I work in Detroit during the week and have stayed at many hotels in and around the metroplex. I stayed here one night so I could have a good jump-off point for an early morning flight, and discovered this great hotel. 
Rooms are very modern, comfortable, and clean. The hotel definitely has more class than your run-of-the-mill Hilton or Marriott. Room service is great (try the Sante Fe pizza for something spicey, but be very hungry). 
Only downsides.... Everything is expensive (room rates, room service, and in-room bar). Also, the last night I was here, there was a large convention that made it almost impossible to move through the lobby.

title: “Great location, decent hotel”
text: One of the best located hotels - directly across the street from MoMA, a block or so from Central Park, close to Metro stations, shopping and dining. Two night stay was pleasant. The interior is a little dated but room and bathroom were larger than expected for this part of NYC. Front desk staff were just okay - no major problem but could have been a touch more courteous. Concierge was a real loud mouth. Elevators are being renovated and take forever to arrive. All in all, for the location in Manhattan, probably worth staying at if you can get a good deal on the price (I paid $479 for two nights).

title: “Great Stay with Kids!”
text:
I stayed at the Omni June 28 and 29 with my two boys, ages 11 and 13. I had earned a travel voucher through my sales job and selected the Omni from a very limited number of DC hotels listed in their brochure. I chose it because it looked nice and it was close to a Metro stop. The cost was free to me. I looked into staying an additional night, but: 1) They had no rooms available for the third night, and 2) If they had, the going rate was between $300 and $400. OUCH!
Upon arriving, we were very impressed by the gorgeous lobby. Beautiful marble floors, crystal chandeliers and floral arrangements. Doormen were welcoming and friendly. Check in was very smooth. Our room was ready, even though we were a little early (2pm). The room was pretty standard. Not as opulant as the lobby, but very nice. The biggest plus-factor was the size...a good 4-5 feet longer than a basic room you might be used to. There was a walk-in closet at one end and a makeup/dressing room outside the bathroom. The two Queen size beds were very comfy.
The bathroom was done in marble with a pedistal sink. Glass shelves over the sink and toilet made up for not having vanity space. There was a window in the shower, covered by faux wood blinds. Very clean...no mold or icky grout.
The room also featured a balcony (4th floor) accessed by a door (not a sliding glass door, just a single French door). Judging from the exterior, there are not a lot of balcony rooms.
The carpet was in pretty good shape, bedspreads a little worse for wear and the upholstered chair was faded and a little stained. They appear to be renovating little by little...our balcony overlooked several large dumpsters holding rolled up carpet and chairs that looked like our stained one! 
The location could not be beat.... we had easy access to the Metro (Adams-Morgan/Zoo stop) and it was a short walk to the Zoo. There are lots of restaurants around, including a 24-hour McDonald's and a WONDERFUL cafe/diner called Open City. We ate breakfast there both mornings.
We did not eat in the hotel, due to the price, but the restaurant looked pretty. We wanted to order pizza delivered to the room one night, and the concierge happily provided the names of local places that would deliver.
We also used the pool and hot tub, which were well-maintainted and attractively landscaped.
The staff was very pleasant and friendly. Overall, we enjoyed our stay and would stay here again, but it is not worth the standard rates. I would highly recommend this hotel if you can get it for around $150 per night.

title: “Wonderful Repeat Stays!”
text:
I have stayed at this hotel several times on business and each time I come back it gets better! They have recently remodeled the rooms and they have implemented the Crowne Plaza "Sleep Advantage". There are quiet floors (all the floors are pretty quiet, however) and in each room they have amenities to help you get a better night's sleep! There are eye shades and a clip to keep the curtains drawn together to prevent morning sunlight from getting in. They also have lavender linen spray and a sleep cd that takes you through guided muscle relaxations to help you fall asleep faster! 
All of the beds are BRAND NEW and they are very comfy - plus there are seven pillows on each bed! The linens are clean and the pillows are fluffy. The room and bathrooms are also very clean.
The Elephant and Castle pub downstairs has a very wide menu selection and the food is great! 
There is no shuttle from the airport, but a cab is $20 + tip to anyplace from the airport to downtown! There are also shuttles operated by 3rd parites that are cheaper but they make a whole bunch of stops and take quite a bit longer to get to the airport.

title: “Wonderful Beachfront Hotel”
text: OB Hotel made my trip a wonderful experience it has a beautiful court yard and when you side in the court yard you could see the ocean and it was fantastic and you could walk to shop places to eat. Just wish I could of stay longer the rooms were simple and very clean. I went with my daughter and we enjoy it every much. We also met the owner who was very friendly. I can't wait to go back! We had a courtside room downstairs so when you walk out of the room you would see the ocean. I think it is a really great place to stay. Can't wait to go back!!!!!! Can" say enough about the place good price a nice small hotel staff friendly ...........

title: “Can't find better staff anywhere!!”
text:
I was a little nervous when booking this hotel, because it is fairly new and not many reviews. However, I cannot adequately express how wonderful all of the hotel clerks and staff were. Rooms are small but have great ammenities for their size. Prices absolutely fantastic. What was missing in elaborate decor was certainly made up for by the treatment we received. Wouldn't hesitate to recommend and will go back. 
Can't say enough good about it!!!!

title: “Perfect for a relaxing, scenic vacation”
text: The rooms are beautiful! The bed are very comfortable. They even have steps, stored in the closet, if you are short like me and need a boost into the bed due to the hig side frame. Glass shower doors, don't seem to be the best - end up with water on the floor sometimes. Refrig is great to store some beverages, fruit etc. Our first room was the junior suite, but we really wanted 2 queens so they moved us after the first night. Even found us a toaster to use in the room. Free coffee, ice water, iced tea and lemonade. Breakfast for purchase. Free newspaper M-F. Twice a day maid service, with turn down and chocolate in the evening. Right on the boardwalk. Beautiful sunsets every night. Great heated pool and hot tub. Beautiful lounge chair towels provided at the pool. Pool towels provided in the room, but bring them back with you from the pool. parking is usually $20 a day and internet usually is a charge, but because of them having to move us, we were not charged. Stayed here back in 1999 also, and they have beautifully upgraded the rooms. You can walk to restaurants, groery store, pharmacy, cold stone or yogurt land. Great place to just relax and enjoy life!

title: “75th Reunion”
text: Our group of "old" gals held a reunion with the Four Points Sherator as our base. It was convenient for even our age group to walk to points of interest in San Antonio. The staff went out of their way to be friendly, cheerful, and enjoy the times with us. They printed out maps, gave directions, found nearby gas stations, looked up locations and then told us how to get there, changed out fluffy duvet for regular blanket, actually walked us to one location as it was nighttime and dark on our walk. Checked on our progress daily by Manager to where we were feeling like home-folk. All of us agreed when and if we ever go back to San Antonio we would stay there and recommend it to everyone who is planning a trip there.

title: “Overpriced and watch the”
text:
The Arizona Grand is a sprawling "suites" hotel in which all the rooms are suites, much like an Embassy. The problem with this property is that it is heavily spread out. You need a golf cart to get from the lobby to the room, and getting a golf cart for the return is not easy. The rooms are nice, but not luxurious. They are very similar to an Embassy Suites, There are no frills. The TV's are old with no connections for DVD or computer. There are no bottles of water in the room.
There are no restaurants in the resort. No place to eat breakfast. No bar. There are however, several restaurants on the "edge" of the resort, most of which are a significant walk or require a shuttle. The only breakfast place is a Denny's about 8 minutes walk down a very busy 6 lane street and across a major intersection.
The biggest disappointment was the "resort fee." I was forced to pay a $25 per day resort fee above and beyond the advertised price when I booked the room. This fee supposedly covered my access to the water park, a daily newspaper, and internet access. The water park was closed, I got no paper, and the internet crawled a a snail's pace. I used my 3G card the entire stay. None-the-less, the manager refused to waive the fee for me or any of my colleagues.
I'd avoid this resort and the 5 other people I was there with all felt the same.

title: “Just average hotel”
text: The hotel is very close to Union Square and a number of restaurants and shops. The room was OK, but the bathroom was extremely small for the size of the room. The hotel was average, we didn't really have very many complaints other than the noise. The doors/walls are very thin, so it's easy to hear when others enter/exit their rooms or are walking in the hallway.

title: “Riverwalk Plaza Hotel”
text:
We vacationed in San Antonio four times. The last three times we went to see the Xmas lights on the Riverwalk. We have returned to the Riverwalk Plaza Hotel all three times. The hotel is close to all the major attractions that San Antonio has to offer. An entrance to the Riverwalk is just across the street.
The price, location, cleanliness, and service are all to be recommended at this hotel. As we really enjoy the lights on the Riverwalk at Xmas, I am sure we will be going back again. When we do, we will be staying at the Riverwalk Plaza. The complimentary cookies at the front desk are good too.

author.location: Somers Point, New Jersey, United States

title: “Great location”
text:
Stayed here on New Year's Eve. The wait to check in was horrible - over an hour. The line snaked around the whole lobby. I understand that it was a holiday and the hotel is in a prime location, but they were not even fully staffed at the front desk. A small sour note to begin our stay.
We got a corner room on the 28th floor with a great view. The room was spacious and well appointed. We had no ice machine on our floor and had to ask THREE different housekeeping employees where the closest one was (no ice on the floor above or below either. Wierd!)
We visited the lobby bar after enjoying First Night festivities and also ordered room service. Both were very good. 
You can't beat the location. Copley square and Prudential mall are great. It's a short walk to Newbury Street where we had dinner reservations at Stephanie's on Newbury. Check it out!

title: “Poor Service”
text:
I went to the Omni after I read all of the great reviews posted on this site. Personally, the hotel was nice but I thought the service was very poor and rude.
The restaurant / bar was nice but again the service was terrible. We waited for 20 mins to get service - and that is only because we went to the Bar 3 times to remind them we were waiting. Each time they kept saying someone was coming...We finally left and ordered room service.
Service is everything to me...I will not be going back to the Omni next time I'm in Los Angeles.

title: “Excelente ;)”
text:
We stayed with my family for 3 nights, first time visiting San Francisco. This hotel is located close to everything you want to see and you will need. There is an iHop and a 7/11 right next door (very important if you have little ones). We were able to see lots of attractions AND take a rest in between.. in 2 days! 
The hotel employees are very friendly and willing to help. The pool area and lobby is nice and clean. 
Totally recommend!

title: “Helpful staff/good location”
text: Booked this hotel after seeing many satisfied posts on Tripadvisor and was not disappointed. Staff were friendly and helpful, location in a safe area, clean although small room, great choice of restaurants nearby on Polk. I hired a mini van and although tight, parked OK (maximum height available is 6ft 8ins). My only regret was that many of the restaurants on Polk were booked up and I would recommend booking a table in advance. Great visit - I'll be back.

title: “Outstanding! We will Definitely stay here again.”
text: My family stayed at the Hampton Inn Times Square North in July for 5 nights and it was a wonderful stay. The staff is very professional and friendly. The hotel was clean and up to date. As many have stated, the hotel rooms are large by NYC standards. It was four of us and we stayed in a room with 2 queen beds. This was more than enough room for us since we were hardly in the room anyway. We didn’t take a trip to NYC to stay in the room. The breakfast was good with a variety of items to choose from(hot and cold). Red Apples were available in the lobby 24/7 and cookies were served in the afternoon. Coffee, Tea, and hot chocolate was also available 24/7. The location of the hotel was wonderful. It was within walking distance of Times Square, and Central Park. We even walked to 34th street to Macy’s. The only minor compliant I have is the A/C in our room didn’t seem to cool properly. This wasn’t a big deal because it was cool, but not cold. We were there in July so we would have liked to room to be cold when we returned from outside. Oh, and we also requested a mini refrigerator and it was bought to up promptly. I can’t say enough good things about this hotel and we will definitely return on our 2012 visit to NYC. Keep up the good work Hampton Inn Times Square North.

title: “Off the beaten path from PHX”
text:
I stayed here for a horrible trip: going to see a client and get my a** kicked. So my mood was already glum. I arrived with two colleagues from FL at 9:06 am on a weekday. I'd called ahead and was told we'd probably be able to get rooms around 10am even though check-in is usually in the afternoon. 
My directions from the car rental center were wrong, so I went out of the way. But even without that snafu, this hotel seems a little far from the airport--well, specifically, from the rental car center. It doesn't feel like an airport hotel, as it's situated in a little office park and you drive by some really grim areas filled with stripper shacks to get there. So location merits a D.
That said, the front desk clerk very helpfully got us three rooms even though it was only about 10am. (Note the huge, electric blue asparagus stalks in the lobby--weird.) My room was a good five-minute walk from the elevator, which is ridiculously far, so be careful when reserving. The room itself was generic Hilton, albeit with a southwestern flair. I was pleased that the a/c blew very cold, and surprised to find a little balcony off the room that overlooked the pool. 
I was gone all afternoon and had a 7am flight out the next day, so I didn't check out the gym or the pool or any other amenities. We did have dinner in the hotel restaurant and it was surprisingly good and, as I recall, not overly expensive.
Parking, as you'd expect, is free. Another colleague joined us and took the free shuttle, which he said was fine and timely.
All in all, it's a perfectly acceptable property, but it doesn't feel all that close to the airport, and I can't imagine why anyone would stay in this part of Phoenix unless s/he had an early morning flight.

title: “Perfect location... Perfect view”
text:
This was by far the best hotel I have ever stayed in. View, service and clean. 
People say to much noise but it didn't bother us at all. We had a times square view but I'm sure all views are amazing. 
Our room was on the. 22nd floor

title: “not happy”
text: I know we were in downtown but at $205 a night (walk-in rate) this place was waaaay overpriced. The employees were nice as was the bed but the room itself was dirty and beat up with scrapes, scratches, and stains on the walls and dirty, stained carpet. Will never go back.

title: “One night stay at the park south”
text: The room was very simple, but a pleasant complimentary breakfast and the fantastic staff on the desk who helped me with a hire car that failed to turn up made it a wonderful place to stay

title: “A nice place to stay in the Inner Harbor”
text:
Brookshire Suites was a nice place to stay. The staff was very friendly, although check-in and check-out were very slow. We had two suites - one was the regular suite and one was an executive suite. The regular suite was smaller than your average suite, but the executive suite was large and had plenty of room. The rooms were clean, but needed some minor repairs - scuffs on the walls, frayed carpeting, etc. We parked across the street because the woman at the front desk said it would be cheaper, but we paid over $30 to self park for less than a day and valet would have been $25. The breakfast was very nice - something for everyone - pancakes, eggs, meat, muffins, cereal, fruit, yogurt. 
 We booked the "Discover Down Under" Aquarium package through Orbitz, which includes two VIP (immediate entry) tickets to the aquarium. VIP tickets were great, because we didn't have to get to the aquarium at any special time, and when we got there, we just walked right in. Also be aware, other hotels offer express entry, but that is not the same thing as immediate entry. 
I would definitely recommend that you check around for rates. Our room rate through Orbitz was $159, whereas it would have been $239 if we had booked directly with the hotel. Just use the "check rates" button on tripadvisor.com, and you might get lucky like we did. 
I also have to mention the great customer service that we received via email before our trip. I sent email to harbormagic.com and all of my questions were answered, even after they knew that I had made my reservation through Orbitz. I can't say enough about how nice they were.

title: “Excellent service, position and value for money”
text: Stayed here for 3 nights with my husband, 2 kids (9, 11) and my parents. All of us were very impressed with the location, right on union square better location than the high priced hotels. We arrived at 10 am exhausted from a flight from Australia and for the first time in my many travels they had both rooms ready and available for immediate occupation, WOW. The service the whole time was wonderful, breakfast in the morning and wine with nibbles every evening. It was like staying in a home away from home. Would definitely stay there again.

title: “Love It!”
text: Always a great experience at the Curtis. Fun and quirky. Great customer service and rooms are super clean and updated. I came to a conference here and the Curtis helped make it a great time. How can you not enjoy your meeting when your water is served from the Kool-aid Man pitcher? Location is perfect to enjoy downtown Denver.

title: “Noisey”
text: Hotel noisey. We complained & the front desk offered an upgrade for additional $50 a night. Room was suppose to be a queen, but was actually a full. We booked directly thru hotel, not priceline or hotels.com. Great location. Clean, but don't expect a good nights rest!

title: “Lovely hotel in historic building”
text:
I spent three nights in mid-October at the Omni Severin while traveling on business. The location is good...right in downtown and literally across the street from the old Union train station. This is my second business stay in Indianapolis (my first was at the Hilton Garden Inn off Monument Circle). The rooms are a good size and the bed was comfortable. A goodly supply of towels in the bathroom, although the towels were stacked onto a low table beneath the sink which jutted out (due to the u-pipe beneath the sink) and I ran my shin into it more than once.
Good water pressure in the shower, although the tub is very low, so didn't really lend itself to a luxurious soak after a long day, I'm afraid. If you're an Omni Loyalty member, you get free WiFi during your stay + free bottled water. You also can get a free pot of coffee (w/cream & sugar) delivered to your room in the morning. The entire staff was incredibly friendly & dedicated to making sure my stay was comfortable. There was not a single time that I asked for something where I wasn't taken care of immediately. As an aside, part of the hotel is still in an historic hotel building from the early 1900s. In fact, the original lobby is still there, located behind the new, modern one. It's gorgeous and is now used for private functions.
The ONLY downside to my stay was that I specifically requested a "quiet room, away from the elevator" in my reservation. This is also specified in my Omni Loyalty preferences and I reiterated the request upon check-in. When I got to my room, I couldn't have been booked in a room closer to the elevator without being in the actual elevator! The room's door literally faced the elevators!! I called down to the desk immediately and they moved me promptly to a different room (actually 2 doors away from my travelling companion) which fit the bill. I also received several communications from the hotel manager during my stay apologizing for the mix-up. I truly appreciate that they handled the issue so quickly, but I guess I still don't 100% understand how it happened in the first place. It's the only reason I knocked this review down 1 star.
I would definitely stay here, again and, despite the mix-up with my room, think the Omni Severin is a great hotel in Indianapolis.

title: “Convenient for a one-night lay-over in LA.”
text: We stayed for one night at this airport hotel on our way back from Southeast Asia, in transit waiting for our next flight back home in Texas. It's a decent and inexpensive lay-over, one notch better than it's sister, The Courtyard Marriott, one block away. We paid $119 for the night, compared to $99 otherwise at The Courtyard. Breakfast was not complimentary. The room is small, as expected, but the reception area is unexpectedly large, as large and good looking as several other 5-star hotels. The staff at the reception desk is professional and courteous, though not as warm or welcoming as they should be. The transfer shuttle to the airport is efficient, on time, and our driver was pretty nice and helpful. Other than that, nothing else is extraordinary, except for the really convenience of the location. We will definitely stay at this hotel on our next needed lay-over.

title: “A suite for the price of a room....”
text:
Always difficult to find a good price in a great town as San Antonio so we decide to drive to Austin by the Highway I35.
Along the Hwy, lot of motels indicate their prices on great lighting signs and we decide to stop at the Howard Johnson at $42 ... but it was not the good price( about the double...) Just on the side Travelodge indicated $39 and, at the desk ,it was not too the good price and finally it was $65... not really happy of that, one more time but the surprise was when we entry in the room (N°160), it was a SUITE.... What a space, a saloon, the comfort, clean, coffee etc...
What a surprise, a good surprise and a good deal for the price.
Good breakfast and wifi.

title: “FIRST CLASS”
text: Surpirsed my husband for a birthday-Easter~Yankess/White Sox opener weekend getaway in April. There is no finer hotel in New York City. The Ritz Carlton~Central Park has superior service, amenities and ambiance. Our Park View Room on the 19th floor overlooking Central Park was magical. From the concerige services, room decor, frette linens, club level amenities, Central Park location/view and overall luxury melted our hearts with pleasure. What a way to rekindle any marriage, at the Ritz, first class!

title: “Love this hotel!”
text: Stayed at this hotel for the NEA convention. The staff was very helpful, changing their breakfast serving time to accommodate our Texas caucus. The only thing that was even a little disturbing was the price of parking (which did not agree with what they had posted in their in-room information) and was very high in comparison to parking around the corner.

title: “Amazing Hotel!!!!”
text: Totally wonderful historic hotel. I booked this hotel on Hotwire for $106 to surprise my husband for his birthday. He thought I must have paid a fortune. It was a beautiful hotel and the staff could not have been more friendly. The hotel was completely modern but retained that historic feel. I agree with previous reviews that the bathroom is a bit small compared to other luxury hotels, but no big deal. The bed was one of the most comfortable I've ever slept in and besides the occasional sound of the El, was very quiet. The breakfast buffet was amazing, but a bit pricey. It was a bit of a walk to other restaurants, but the area was very safe and cabs or train was readily available. There was a free shuttle all day to the Magnificenat Mile shopping area. I would recommend this hotel to anyone!

title: “Great hotel, loved it and would recommend it to others!”
text: Me and my girl friend went and had a blast. I love San Antonio and to stay at the Holiday Inn made my stay even better. The staff was great, friendly and presentable. Bartender was nice too. It was clean and quiet and had no problems. Loved how they played music during the day, it got us in a fun spirit mood. The furniture and the interior was beautiful and wouldnt change anything about it. Our view was great looking out on our balcony you could see the pool with a movie playing and the nightlife. The lights music and the pretty buildings. Definitely when i decide to go back i'll go there again.

title: “Fantastic boutique hotel - ultra modern!”
text: Stayed at the Hotel Indigo when my son graduated from law school this May. Hotel was incredibly clean, modern, spacious and comfortable. Our suite was amazing. Wish we could have stayed for a week!

title: “pretentions to hipness and grandeur that fall short”
text:
