i stayed with colleagues for two nights at the zaza last week on business. it's totally over-rated. local colleagues, upon hearing that we were staying there, looked vaguely piteously at us. the worst thing is that the hotel thinks it's a sexy boutique, but it's not. witness the random taxidermy peacock in reception, the ugly paintings, the bar with bright over head lighting and poor acoustics.
pluses:
* molten brown toiletries.
* comfy beds.
* quiet rooms.
* clean and modern.
* tasty room service.
* kobe beef carpaccio in the hotel restaurant.
minuses:
* unknowledgable concierge - he rattled out a recommendation for a restaurant for us before we even told him what kind of place we were looking for.
* tacky decor - helmut newton cheapie prints abound, fake hand-written post it notes stuck on your bathroom mirror schilling the sister hotel in houston. the executive chair at the desk in your room is - vinyl? 
* terrible service in "happening" restaurant (dragonfly) - we had to negotiate for a table for 10 mins in a half-empty restaurant. the hostess tried to seat us in the "cocktail area" - a corner table behind the hostess stand with a plastic bench. how insulting.
* no baths - not on our floor anyway, just a shower stall. why? there's lots of room.
* eco lip service - you can re-use your towels to be green. but no recycling bins and no sign to re-use sheets.
* no daily newpaper upon waking - there's a pile in reception.
* business center - a JOKE! two terminals, one broken, painfully slow.
we won't be back. it's not bad, just pretentious and a little bit sad.

title: “Great place and good service”
text:
I'm not used to staying at higher end hotels, but I still have to say this was a very enjoyable stay.
First, I'll tell you this was a free stay as part of my Hilton Honors program, so I don't really want to judge it for "value". If purchased through a bargain web site, it probably would have been a $200+/night room. They allowed us an early check-in - possibly because of my gold membership or possibly because they had light bookings for the weekend, or possibly just to be nice.
The hotel begins on the 15th floor of a building. The Hilton signage gets lost in all of the other signs in the area, so you might want to get the "house" number before going there. You enter a building hallway that runs from 42nd Street to 41st Street. It's real close to the Port Authority Bus Terminal and is an extremely convenient location if arriving by bus. Inside is a marble floor. You enter elevators that express you to the lobby on ~15th floor. 
The desk clerks (especially Julita (sp?)) and concierge personnel were very polite and helpful. I'm always a little skeptical in metropolitan areas of people being rude and pushy, but we experienced the exact opposite here. 
 There is a bar/resaurant area in the lobby. You enter different elevators to go to your room floor.
The room was clean and very nice with a panoramic view towards the East River. We could see the Statue of Liberty way off in the distance. The furnishings were in good condition and the bath was clean with a nice selection of complimentary personal items and linens.
We ate in the city except for a free breakfast at the hotel (again, complimentary due to my gold membership). I expected a rather basic breakfast. Boy was I wrong. It was a buffet, but not the usual. There were a variety of good pastries, a couple of types of eggs, smoked salmon, bacon, sausage, fresh OJ and other jucies, waffles, pancakes, etc - what a buffet!!!! Needless to say, I overate. I guessed it was a $25/person value. it turns out the normal price is $26.
We checked out before we were ready to leave the city and the hotel has a luggage storage room on the ground floor operated by bellhops, so we didn't have to lug our bags around the rest of the day. Again, all personnel were very polite and helpful without being pushy.

title: “Comfort and convenience in Westwood, CA”
text: We always stay in Royal Palace when we're in LA. It's clean and convenient if you want to stay near UCLA. Good rests nearby and free parking for guests. The breakfast is good and if you want more then go to Denny's.

title: “Somethings growing in the bathtub”
text:
I was profoundly disappointed in this hotel. I booked four different hotels for my most recent stay in Los Angeles. All hotels were booked through hotwire, but this was the only 4 star. All others were 2 or 3 star. Naturally, I assumed this would be the nicest. Unfortunately, I could not have been more wrong. 
Although I wasn't terribly impressed with the amenities of the hotel (there was only one restaurant opened when we got there and it was the most up-scale, when we just wanted an evening snack, the gift shop was not opened at 10PM) the main problem was with the bathtub. It was completely covered in small black spots. At first I thought it was paint spattered on the bottom of the tub, but I rubbed it, and it smeared! It was the consistency of charcoal. Of course, I called the front desk and the immediate response was, "I'm sorry, we don't have any other rooms available." I insisted that housekeeping come up and clean the tub. A nice gentleman came very quickly and cleaned, then asked me to come look and approve the work. The tub was spotless. I thanked him and asked what the stuff was. His only response was, "It's nasty, isn't it?" I agreed that it was, but at least the tub was clean so I didn't say anything else.
Imagine my surprise when the next morning the tub was in exactly the same condition as it had been when we arrived the night before!! The photos that accompany this review were taken in the morning, AFTER the tub had been cleaned and appeared spotless 8 hours earlier. I wish now that I would have called the Health Department and waited until they got there, but I wanted to get started on my vacation. I put a towel down and took my shower.
This hotel was by far the worst of all four; the others were quite a pleasant surprise after this fiasco. The photos were taken with my cell phone.

title: “Good location for family trip”
text: This property is a good choice if you are traveling with children. We were able to walk to the subway, the bus, shopping, dining, sightseeing. The staff was very helpful (especially Roberto who helped us with our luggage) and the suites were well appointed, with plenty of room and privacy for parents and kids. The bathroom was a bit narrow, as is often the case in Embassy Suites, but the extra sink in the bedroom helps with the traffic flow when your whole family is trying to get ready at the same time! There is no view to speak of, and it sometimes got a bit noisy, but overall this did not bother me. One surprise is that the complementary manager's reception serves a full bar, not just beer and wine. The breakfast got ridiculously crowded, though, and the location of the breakfast buffet in relation to the elevators makes it worse. Another complaint is that the parking is very very expensive, but I am sure that is competitive with other properties in the area. Overall, not perfect, but a good deal.

title: “Great place, Great Location”
text:
Love San Francisco,
My wife and I stayed part of our honeymoon here at the Sheraton, 23 years ago. We often come back to reminisce, walk the wharf and have great sea food, eat in China Town, and smell the ocean air. The Sheraton is a great base for staying in San Francisco. You can take the Rice a Roni trolley cars all over town, losts of fun, very romatic!

title: “Great hotel stay”
text:
What a wonderful quiet hotel, close to evertything in the center of Seattle! The hotel staff was wonderful, friendly and best of all helpful. The lobby bar is a great place to cap off a wonderful day of seeing the sights of Seattle. 
This is a newer hotel with LEEDS silver certification. Great "green" touches through out the hotel. The rooms and common areas were very clean. Great spa area with whirlpool, swimming pool and mens and women's locker rooms each with a wet and dry sauna.
Very comfortable bed! Great breakfast included if you are a AAA member.

title: “Great stay”
text: We spent three nights at Le Meridien in San Francisco. It was a great location to several of the sights - the Ferry Building and Embarcadero was esp. close. Chinatown was a walk away. We did walk to Fisherman's wharf but had to bike back. The hotel itself is very elegant. As a rewards member, I was able to get a higher room, we did have to pay a minimal for a bay view, but it was worth it. The room had windows on both corners. The bathroom was nice a roomy. The bedroom itself was a little small, but sufficient. Excellent breatkfast in the hotel restaurant. The lobby had free Starbucks in the morning and a happy hour in the evening. I would definitely recommend this hotel.

title: “small and smelly”
text: we went to this hotel for new years eve. the room was tiny (about 15 x 15) and the bathroom smelled of sewage. the staff were rude and check in took forever. furthermore, the nye party sponsored by the hotel was EXTREMELY DISAPPOINTING! don't stay here. take your money down the street to the sheraton where you'll find a nice hotel with the same great location.

title: “Great place”
text: Good business hotel. Excellent concierge facilities with helpful and knowledgeable staff. Real plus is the free shuttle service to local restaurants. The take you to the place of your choice and collect you when the restaurant calls!!! Free of charge (apart from a tip of course). Hotel is close to a fantastic shopping mall too.

title: “Dirty, bad customer service, yet expensive - in a word: Horrible”
text:
I've read some of the recent reviews giving this hotel an "Excellent" rating, and I wonder if those people stayed at the same place I did. I'm a Hilton Hhonors VIP, so I have a minimal standard expectation of a Hilton property. This one missed the mark by miles, even when accounting for the generally substandard level of customer service one finds in Memphis as a whole.
After arriving, I spent the first 35-40 minutes of my stay trying to get the hotel staff to give me a room that had been properly serviced by housekeeping. The first room had been smoked in, despite the hotel's non-smoking policy. The second room had beds that weren't made at all. The third room's bathroom had obviously not been cleaned - there were icky remnants of the previous guest in and on the toilet, and there was also a large, very noticeable buttprint in the bedspread of one of the beds. The fourth room didn't have anything horribly wrong with it at first glance (although I was to find out later that my first impression was incorrect), so I stuck with that one. During this entire ordeal, I never received a single apology from the front desk staff; nor did they do anything about the fact that I was carting my luggage back and forth and up and down during all the room-changing fun.
The rooms weren't the only thing that needed cleaning - the hallways and elevator lobbies were strewn with trash, and looked like they hadn't been vacuumed in a month at least. This, despite my stay being in the middle of a work week.
The "high-speed" wireless internet service was $10/night, but it was actually low-speed, and dropped several times during the evening.
Room cleanliness was marginal, and I found that housekeeping had taken several shortcuts, forgotten or overlooked things, and had done things that I found disgusting:
- Ony one of the beds had been recently serviced - the other had dust and crumbs on it. It had obviously been untouched in quite a while.
- Numerous items were overlooked - there was no shampoo, only one washcloth, and only one large towel. This was in a 2-double-bed room! 
- There was a partially-consumed bottle of water on the TV stand, with the "you will be billed $4 if you drink it" tag still attached.
- The coffee cups for the in-room coffee maker smelled exactly like the room's complimentary bar soap. It was clear that the coffee cups had been "cleaned" in the room with bar soap, probably used soap left by a previous guest.
I called Guest Services to ask them to address these issues, but the person who answered the phone spoke with an accent or speech impediment that made him impossible to understand. I have lived in many parts of the world, and have spent numerous years living in the Southeastern US, but I could not understand a word this man said. I can't imagine what would cause Hilton to choose this staffer to answer phones. I tried to explain to him what the issues were, but I could not understand his responses. We ended the call with me unsure whether he was going to do anything to resolve the problems. No one ever showed up to fix anything, so my question was ultimately answered.
The only thing positive I can say about this hotel is that it is right off I-240, which makes it easy to get to.
I will not ever stay there again, and I strongly recommend that this place be avoided. Again - I wonder if the people posting recent positive reviews stayed someplace else, and confused it with this hotel.

title: “Great H/I Location!”
text: This particular Holiday Inn Express is the very best value for the money anywhere in the U.S. I have stayed in Holiday Inn facilities for over 25 years, and I found this one to be among the very best. I have been a Platinum Level Member for a very long time, and I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone planning to stay in the area.

title: “Excellent Staff and Service”
text: We recently spent a week at the Affinia for my wife's birthday and as most holidays go, a few things went wrong. I found the Affinia staff extremely helpful and not only solved our concerns immediately but went out of their way on many occasions. I would highly recommend the Affinia and would definitely stay again when I am in New York.

title: “Wonderful, wonderful stay!”
text:
The Hotel Valencia provided the perfect retreat for the second stage of our Texas holiday.
The doormen were a model of efficiency and the delightful water feature that greets you is a nice architectural touch! The reception is on the 2nd floor with a lovely open feel that leads into the curved bar (with nice views over the river). The room was nicely arranged (the mink throws an elegant touch). The hotel's location (slightly away from the bustle) was a huge plus. Close enough to stroll along the riverwalk though. And moments from the Alamo. Do check out the quiet courtyard with flames and more falling water! Take a good book and relax in a soft chair as the sun sets...

title: “Excellent Service”
text: We stayed three nights in a suite with a special package rate currently being offered and it was a good value. We were on the fourth floor facing Madison and never heard anything through the double glazed windows. The suite was spacious (albeit a little too louis XIV for my tastes) and well appointed. The bed was unbelievably comfortable. There were 2 baths which was convenient for entertaining. The service was impeccable. Gym was small but equipment was good. Robert, the concierge, was well informed and took care of our needs. We were pleasantly surprised by this hotel. The only disappointment was our venture into Bemelman's one evening. We stopped by for a cocktail before heading back to the room and the bill was $65.00. If we had been there for more than 20 minutes it might have not bothered, but it bugged me that we weren't made aware of a $20 per person cover when we were first seated. It was a minor annoyance for an otherwise great experience.

title: “Nice hotel, great location, not worth the price.”
text:
This is a great central location in downtown DC - walking distance to the Capital, stores & restaurants. We appreciated that the room was very clean and the bed extremely comfortable. Everything else was just so-so. 
When we checked in, there was nobody staffing the (non-automatic) door and no offer of help with our bags. This was indicative of the level of service we encountered during our stay. There was no automated checkout, and we had to wait for staff to resolve the problems of several other guests before we could check out. Housekeeping came at 8:30 in the morning, knocking & knocking until they woke me out of a dead sleep. When I go to the live music capital of the world, I like to stay out late & sleep in a bit. If the hotel wants to start housekeeping that early, they should warn guests so they can use the "do not disturb" sign. 
The decor is traditional and gilt-y. If you're looking for stylish and hip, this is not the hotel for you. The bathroom is spacious, but without the attention to detail that I would expect from a 4-star hotel. Weak water pressure, no bathroom fan, skimpy towels. Some days we got a bathmat, some days we didn't. Sometimes we got 4 towels for 2 people, sometimes we got 3. Although the room had a king-sized bed, there was only 1 bathrobe. I had to call twice before a second was brought up, then the staff who brought it stood there silently, clearly expecting a tip for bringing what should have been in the room in the first place. 
My husband got locked out of our room and they wouldn't let him into the room because we have different last names. This is good security - but good service would have been to call me (they asked for my cell phone number at checkin) and ask me if he was authorized access. He was standing right next to me when we checked in and they gave us two keys, but they didn't ask for the name of the other guest. To me, this reflected poor attention to the details expected of a hotel of this price. I was very glad I'd gotten the room on Priceline, and paid far less than the rack rate.

title: “Great location for exploring downtown Chicago , comfortable room that might be noisy.”
text:
We stayed here for two nights after a business trip brought us to Chicago. We got a good internet rate. If you ride the Metra line and get off at the Madison station you are just steps from the front door. That is a very good thing for getting around but it is noisy. We requested a quiet room away from the Metra line and were put in the side area behind a building. The noise from the El echoes through the empty space and is noticeable but the train stopped running at 1 pm and started up again at 4 am so I got some sleep. The room is clean, comfortable, and has a coffee maker and refrig.. The lobby is very large and comfortable and they have two computers available for use. The elevator is card run so I felt safe. The hallways and doors are noisy and we did hear several loud guest during the night going to their rooms. We ate at Ada's one night and it was good.
I found it strange that the hotel has a policy against bringing alcohol into the hotel or it will charge a corkage fee on it. Not sure how they enforce this as it did not affect us but made us wonder if they go through your luggage or drawers to enforce? We always purchase diet coke and save on this cost .

title: “It Sucks!”
text: The Good Nite Inn on Greenwood is good only if you want an inexpensive place to sleep. Otherwise, the patrons in adjoining rooms are noisey! People park their cars in TWO spaces an complaining to the office gets you NADA! And going to the Denny's across the street to eat is a good one hour wait...just to get seated in summer days!

title: “We were very pleased with the comfortable beds and resonable prices.”
text: I traveled to Indy with a group of 8 women, we were in town for a show and shopping and were pleasantly surprised with the wonderful location next to wonderful shopping and great resturants. The staff was very helpful with directions and provided a list of the local resturants. Would be happy to return again for the same kind of weekend.

title: “Beautiful Property”
text: I have stayed here four times now! Not only does this hotel have a great location in the Baltimore harbor, its up to date and the staff is out of this world!!! Everyone is always so nice and smiling! No matter the time of day the entire hotel is always spic-n-span!!! The rooms are always clean and the beds are so comfortable! Thank you so much guys and I will see you soon!!! :-)

title: “Fine for business”
text: If you're in Denver for a meeting, and aren't planning to tour around or eat at fine restaurants, this hotel should meet your needs. Located in the Stapleton area, they offer free shuttle service to/from DIA, and also to the nearby malls. Rooms are fairly large, and the interior of the hotel has an atrium, which gives it a light, airy feel. Ask for a room on the south side - there are train tracks and a grade crossing on the north side, and the 4AM train whistles by on a daily basis. Loud, even on the 9th floor. But the hotel does provide earplugs. Conference food was decent; I didn't try the regular restaurant. Internet was s-l-o-w. Glad I didn't have to pay for it (included in conference pkg. - otherwise, there is a charge). The staff were all very pleasant, helpful and eager to please. Overall, a positive experience.

title: “Fantastic hotel and location”
text:
We recently stayed at the JW Marriott at LA Live during our stay for the 2012 Rose Bowl. It was a fantastic hotel choice. There is a lot going on in the area, Staples Center, Nokia Theatre, Grammy Museum to name a few. There are also some very good restaurant choices that are a short walk from the hotel. 
The hotel itself has a fabulous lobby which is great for people watching and relaxing. It has above average food and a great staff to serve you. The lounge was very upscale and enjoyable. 
The rooms are bigger than most hotel rooms and were very clean. The views from the rooms were awesome as well. 
Overall, the hotel exceeded my expectations. I would definitely stay there again in fact, we didn't want to leave.

title: “Restful Sleep”
text: I stayed at the Palomar for a night when my workday turned into an evening. I arrived close to 1 am and the front desk staff was very accommodating. My room was very comfortable. The beds are a little too soft but the pillows were great (personal preference on mattress style). The tv is flat screen around 42 inches. The bathroom are a decent size with marble countertops. There is not a separate shower. I found the light switches complicated but that might just have been my sleep deficit. When I checked out in the morning, the hotel staff at he front desk again was very pleasant again. Will likely be using this option in the future.

title: “Making a reservation more than painful”
text: On hold for a very long time to try and make a reservation. Every 4 seconds (I timed it) an automated voice comes on that says "thank you for continuing to hold. Please stay on the line and your call will be answered by the next available agent." Try listening to this for more than 5 minutes and I guarantee you will want to hang up and stay at a Best Western. After all that I finally get a live person who asks me for everything including my first born only to tell me there are no rooms available. You couldn't check this first? It's a big city - there are much friendlier places to stay.

title: “Brilliant trip”
text:
We stayed at the Alex for the 4 days immediately before Christmas. The two bedroom suite provided perfect accommodation for myself, husband and 17 year old daughter - not an easy combination! 
The hotel staff were really friendly and helpful - especially Ed and Nick. No problem with showers or lifts which others seem to have moaned about. We had a very good meal in the restaurant - do try the red apple cocktail! The view of the Chrysler building was breathtaking - a wonderful intro to NYC for husband and daughter on first time visit, and very convenient for shops and theatres. Schedules permitting we will certainly be back.

title: “Great location, nice room, impersonal staff”
text:
Our first impression of the JW Marriott was not good. The bellman that met our cab wasn’t friendly and passed us along to another bellman that took our bags as far as the front desk and left us there without waiting to either take them to our room or store them until our room was ready. Then he simply stared at us in an unpleasant manner waiting for a tip.
We arrived about two hours before the 4 p.m. check in time and were offered an early check in if we took our pre-assigned with double beds rather than the king that we had requested. We were told that we could get a king bedded room if we waited until 4 p.m. I asked about a view and was told the double room was on the second floor overlooking Pennsylvania Avenue or if we waited for the king bedded room it would not have any view. We were staying on a corporate rate so we didn’t expect anything other than the lowest price/class room location.
We opted to wait for the king bed and were basically told to deal with the luggage ourselves by going to the bell desk. A well-run hotel would have called the bellman over to us, not the other way around. Again we had to deal with another unfriendly bellman to store our luggage until the room was ready.
Our room was ready at the promised hour and this time we had a very nice bellman who took our bags up.
Our king room was on the 10th floor, room 1087, and actually did have a bit of a view to the right over the rooftops towards the Old Post Office Pavilion and the Reagan International Building. The view to the left was the side of an office building; the view down was of the rooftop AC units. It had an oddly configured window area set into a corner with two windows. The window corner made the room a bit larger than other rooms in the basic room category. I agree with another review that said the rooms facing the interior courtyard had a “minimum security prison yard view”, we were able to see that view and were pleased that at least we had an outside facing room. We also visited a friend in a room with the Pennsylvania/14th Street corner view and it was fabulous but much noisier than where our room was located due to the street noise.
The room wasn’t large but it was normal for a big city hotel. The only complaint we had with the size of the room was that the desk was too close to the bed and when one of us was on the computer we had to pull in the chair to let the other walk past.
Furnishings were nice and the bed was comfortable with lots of pillows. The down quilt was too hot, even when we cranked down the temperature at night we melted under the down quilt. The windows in our room could not be opened.
The bathroom was small but had plenty of counter space. It was lacking towel racks; only one rack was in the tub/shower area. No towel ring for the hand towels so we had to just leave them on the counter. The rain-type showerhead was nice but the water pressure was not strong. The bath products provided had a nice aroma and were replenished daily. Maid service was good and at least they were friendly.
When we arrived I noticed we didn’t have robes or a hair dryer so I phoned for them. It took two hours and two phone calls to get them. Every time I phoned for any request or question the person taking the call was less than friendly or professional. I recently stayed at a Loews resort where the operator always thanked me by name and asked if there was anything else they could do for me. At the JW Marriott the operator just said “okay” whenever I made a request, not even a thank you.
There was enough closet space and a few drawers in the room. The mini bar fridge was full but not locked so we could use it for storage and we never saw a mini bar attendant or price list. There is a small bar area in the alcove of the room with extra glassware and a coffee maker with free coffee.
We were able to get a couple of wireless signals in the room so we never had to pay for internet usage. The set up of the desk and the plugs for the computer and other equipment was very good. The desk and the TV swiveled so it was easy to use the TV as a monitor for the computer.
We only ate breakfast at the hotel and it was fine. There are many good restaurants and quick food shops near the hotel. We liked the pastries from the Firehook Bakery that was a couple of blocks away. For a quick sandwich the Corner Bakery is literally around the corner. There is also a very tiny wine shop just outside the front door of the hotel that had good prices. The best bar in the area is across the street at the Willard Hotel.
We had no complaints about the elevators. Once or twice we waited a few minutes (nothing like the 10 minutes or more that previous reviews mention). Usually we had little or no wait. The hotel was filled with convention goers so the elevators were in constant use; in fact one was shut down completely for repair.
The location is just about the best in town for sightseeing of the Mall, the White House and the monuments. Overall our final impression of the hotel improved greatly from our first impression. We were able to get a one-hour late check out and the bellman storing our luggage for the rest of the day was much friendlier than the staff that greeted us upon arrival. The hotel overall is very nice but the staff could use better training in customer service. If I were staying in town for vacation rather than business I would probably select another hotel nearby unless I was able to get a great rate at the JW Marriott.

title: “Wonderful moderate hotel with the friendliest staff I have ever encountered”
text: Minutes from Chicago's Midway airport, this motel is conveniently located to downtown Chicago either by car or the El train. The hotel is located in a large hispanic neigborhood. We were uncomfortable at first, but realized it was safe at all times. The rooms were clean, the beds comfortable, the staff the friendliest and most helpful I have ever encountered in the US or Europe. The free shuttle wil take you to the airport or to the nearest El train. The modest breakfast was excellent (they served Dunkin Donuts breakfast sandwiches - egg, sausage and cheese between a bagel) as well as donuts. There is free parking (other downtown hotels charge for parking).The only negative was they put us in a handicap room to begin with. We checked out for a day (travel to another city)and came back to a regular room which was much more spacious.

title: “Impressive hotel in a good location”
text:
We stayed here for 5 nights in October and found it to be a clean, comfortable hotel.
The Hotel
This is an impressive hotel. The lobby area is beautiful and certainly has the wow factor. There are some small shops and a Starbucks located on the ground-level, with the Reception and Concierge on the upper ground level. As a result of the size of the hotel, some of the rooms can be a few minutes walk from the elevator - absolutely no issue for us, but if you have mobility problems it might be worth requesting a room close to the elevator.
The Rooms
We stayed in a room with 2 double beds. The room was very spacious with modern decor and was a very nice place to rest. The room had a TV, desk / dressing table & chair, 2 telephones, an easy chair with foot stool, 2 double beds each with bedside tables, 2 wardrobes, bathroom with bath and shower, and a hairdryer. We found the room to be very clean (with the exception of a used tissue in the sink on arrival!) and it was maintained well throughout our stay. Our only gripe is that there was no mini-bar and no tea / coffee making facilities and, for the price of the room, I would expect both of these things. I assume that the lack of these facilities was to encourage guests to use the (quite expensive) bar in the lobby and the (similarly expensive) Starbucks franchise on the ground-level. The beds were very conformable and we certainly had lots of space in the room.
Staff
We found the staff, without exception, to be helpful and friendly. The Concierge staff were very accommodating and were more than happy to make all reservations for us. Door staff similarly were very helpful and had taxis waiting within seconds.
Location
The hotel is located just inside the Loop on East Monroe about a ten minute walk to Millennium Park and the Harbour and about a 5 minute walk to Macy's and other shops. We walked almost everywhere from here and found the majority of places to be easily accessible. A walk to the Shedd Aquarium / Soldier Park took us about 50 minutes, but this was a gentle stroll along the harbour, and could be done in less if you walked with purpose! There are El stations just outside the hotel, and a couple of nice bars / eateries just next door to the hotel (The Exchequer Pub & Restaurant offers a discount to Palmer House Hotel guests).
Overall
We had a very comfortable and enjoyable stay in this hotel, and we would definitely stay here again if we were to return to Chicago.

title: “Perfect!”
text: Great customer service, awesome pet lovers suite, convenient location!

title: “Thanksgiving in Chicago”
text:
The entire stay was excellent, in large part due to the help of the concierge, TK Karadzovski who helped us figure out where to eat, what to see, and where to go, with particularly notable assistance in getting us to the front of the lines in places when it was WAY too cold to stand outside!
She is an ASSET to the hotel!
Thanks, Zade & Amna.

title: “Grand, alright!”
text: Impeccable service! Make sure you ask for the pet goldfish when you check in.

title: “Best Hotel for the Money”
text:
If you refuse to share a common bathroom on the floor, then this place is not for you. But the showers and toilet areas are all private, immaculately clean and well located. "Common" does not mean there are people showering in the next stall. The individual shower rooms are locked and seldom do you even see anyone on your way back to your room.
For $90/night I had a small room facing the front. I could see W. 11th St. from my window! A/C, ceiling fan, writing desk and chair, vanity/sink and single bed. Clean sheets, clean pillows and clean rug. The staff is helpful and non-intrusive. There is continental breakfast but it was served in the basement area and I didn't like the ambience (or lack of it). But this is included for free. Also, a hair-dryer and super clean robe is in each room. I find these things handy since I travel very light. Oh an WiFi too!
All in all, when I can walk to Union Sq., SoHo, Washington Sq. Park and Chelsea from ANY location in NYC for $90/night, I would almost sleep on a park bench.
Great Hotel and very interesting clientele. Quiet, and nicely decorated. But don't expect the Ritz.

title: “Nice suite hotel in the heart of Chicago”
text: We just got back from a stay at the Comfort Suites in Chicago. We were on a budget, but still wanted a good location in the city, and this place fit the bill. Our suite was roomy, with a living area, small kitchen area and separate bedroom. The living area had a pull out sofa bed which was perfect for our teenager. The king size bed in the bedroom was very comfortable. The bathroom was tiny but functional. The staff were incredibly helpful, and actually seemed to enjoy their jobs.

title: “Very average, better choices out there.”
text:
During a recent trip to San Francisco and Napa Valley, we stayed here after my wife booked this hotel through Priceline. This was our least favorite place we stayed on the entire trip, staying at five different hotels on the trip of various types. First problem, when we checked in we were actually sent to the annex a block over. The annex is older and it shows. Wifi connections were poor, the computer provided on the floor we were on was so slow it was unusable and the card activated elevator was only working sporadically.
The second issue is that if you pay for parking when you check in, it's for the main hotel, meaning your walking a block over to your room. The ridiculous part of that is that there is private parking right next to the annex that is much closer and cheaper. Fortunately I knew there had to be some other parking options, so when I checked in, I asked the clerk if there was private parking near. He smiled sheepishly and stated quietly that there was cheaper private parking right behind the hotel. To his credit, when asked he was truthful, but I watched two people check in before me who paid for the parking at the hotel and were told nothing. Don't ask don't tell I guess.
Anyway, if you book through priceline like we did, the options are kind of out of your control. But if you are picking your own, I would suggest trying other options. FYI, it's not walking distance to Fisherman's Wharf, but the Hilton at Union Square was priced similarly and was much better. Also enjoyed the Union Square area much more than the Wharf. You can always take cheap public transportation from Union Square to Fisherman's Wharf anyway, so I suggest staying around the Union Square area.

title: “A good hotel”
text: My brother and I stayed at this Hotel in September. although it is basic the rooms are comfortable and the staff friendly. We found it to be very reasonableand in an excellent location . We encountered no problems and were happy with our choice of accomodation.

title: “I Concur: No Problems”
text:
Spacious even if youre comparing with non-NYC Hotels: compared with standard NYC Hotel rooms these rooms are airplane hangars. 
Clean. The colour scheme may lend itself a little to dingyness: beige and dark brown, but it's clean nonetheless and well-maintained daily.
Views are great. We were actually on the back side of the Hotel looking south to the old city and East across to Brooklyn. Lots of blue sky. 
If driving, park in the lot across the street. It's 30 bucks a day instead of the 55(!) dollars the Hotel charges for Valet parking. There are lots that are even cheaper within a short walk if you check nyc.bestparking.com before arriving. 
To clarify an earlier post, the nearest Subway is at Park Avenue, about 100 meters away, and it's one stop south of Grand Central. 
The neighbourhood is quiet, and the food at the Barking Dog Pub in the hotel is both good and reasonable. A few more good restaurants on Third Ave, just east of the Hotel.
The gym is excellent appointed and complimentary. Big plus.
The only con I can think of is the 15 bucks a day for internet. That's too much, especially when internet is now commonly free and wireless in similar hotels.
The theatre district is very accessable by Subway (one stop up, and one stop over is Broadway and 42nd), or an 8 dollar cab ride to your show if youre pressed for time and need to make an 8 PM curtain on time.
We liked the neighbourhood. Murray Hill is safe, and a nice break from Times Square now that the Square has become an even larger loitering station from 50th down to 34th streets as Broadway is partially blocked for "pedestrians." 
Things to do in avoiding Times Square since your in Murray Hill? Take the #6 Subway on Park Avenue a few stops south and you end up at the foot of the Brooklyn Bridge. Walk it. 
Walk around the corner on Park Ave to the Morgan Library, always cheap (12 dollars or less), and free on Friday nights. Great architecturally and for it's varied treasures. 
Walk two blocks over to the Empire State building, then further up to the Library and Bryant Park.
Take the Same #6 one stop North to Grand Central, and walk up Park Avenue, or simply walk up from the hotel. Tour the Waldorf (a really remarkable landmark.)
This is not a luxury hotel; it's probably something better. It's clean, quiet, functional (you could cook a turkey in the kitchen if you'd like, though that may be a little much) in a good neighbourhood away from the madness of Times Square.

title: “Great Location!”
text: Rooms are very small, but clean. Housekeeping staff was very accommodating. The whole experience was fine even though the hotel is under construction.

title: “Best stay in San Diego!”
text: I recently stayed at the Inn at Sunset Cliffs in San Diego and had an amazing time! I was with my husband and our twin 2 years old girls and I couldnt have asked for a better experience. All of the staff were friendly, curtious, welcoming etc. We enjoyed one of their 2 bedroom suites with the kitchen unit. How convienent was that!! We were able to get some snacks and drinks for the girls, they had a huge fridge, dishes and everything we needed! Overall I would say this place was a one of a kind experience and having traveled to other places in San Diego we will definately be staying here again!!

title: “Acceptable but not quite a Luxury Collection”
text:
Very trendy design at this one year old boutique near Neiman Marcus in downtown. There is not a club lounge as there is at some Lux Collection properties. The rooms are well appointed as would be expected at a hotel that wants to charge $250/night. We had a package that included a bottle of champagne (Charlie Palmer sparkling) and also included breakfast for two with complimentary parking. 
There is a very nice work out room on the 9th floor, and pool on the 10th floor. The pool area is quite small and has a hopping bar. Minors are prohibited from the pool area after 6 pm because it's a scene, especially on the weekends. If you are into clubbing, this is a good place to have a drink. They also have a night club downstairs called PM that is also very popular. The elevators are not locked off or monitored in the evenings, so anyone can jump on and ride up to a floor of their choosing whether they are staying in the property or not. The rooms on the 10th floor can be inconvenienced by the noise of people in the hallways going to the pool bar on 10. I would not recommend anyone stay on this floor. The lobby is very nice and we had a couple glasses of wine while getting hit on by two older women who had flown in from Anchorage to attend an Eric Clapton concert. Not exactly what you would normally find in the lobby of a Luxury Collection hotel, but kind of fun none the less. The hotel restaurant is Charlie Palmer and while we didn't care to eat a steak, it has received excellent reviews in the Dallas press and I'm sure is top notch.
We thought the staffing was a little untrained. They tried hard, but it's definitely not a 5 star experience. I had a problem at the desk when reviewing my bill and while the gal helping me got everything taken care of, some buttinskee from the restaurant was interjecting his comments about why I had a tax and gratuity added to my bill for a "complimentary" breakfast. He was a little over the top, but I'm sure he'll not be there long with his demeanor.
Furthermore, the room service breakfast was not acceptable we didn't say anything but it really wasn't that good. So so at best. Had we paid for it and it wasn't included in the inflated package price we paid, I would have quickly called and asked that the food be re-cooked and brought up. The presentation was plain, very plain and it took way to long to set it up once they got it to the room.
All in all, it's a modern trendy boutique hotel, well appointed as you would expect at a Luxury Collection property, but it is definitely geared to a younger party crowd that would enjoy the hip modern vibe of the rooms and wouldn't care about so-so service, especially when they are getting loaded at the poolside bar.
We normally stay at another property in downtown Dallas with impeccable service and always on the Gold floor where there are complimentary food presentations throughout the day, private check-in and an honor bar. We pay $139 at that hotel which is far less than the Joule and with incredible rooms that were just redone last year even though it's of a more traditional design, so we won't stay again at the Joule, but it was an interesting experience and our only real observation was the service level and quality just wasn't quite up to snuff with the staff.
If you get an absolutely ROCK bottom price for the Joule it might be worth a stay, but otherwise there are other alternatives close by with impeccable standards and service.
I'm a Platinum SPG member so I'm in and out of a lot of Starwood Properties and while this was entertaining for a night, I would not have wanted to stay here longer than I did.

title: “Had a nice time”
text:
We stayed here on July 3, 2006 with our 2 kids. The location is close to everything. We were able to walk to Rock N Roll McDonalds, Rainforest, Hardrock, and Ed Devebicks (sp?). We also caught the sightseeing bus by the Mcdonalds. We walked and shopped on Michigan Avenue. The subway station is also nearby and we took it to Millenium Park and Grant Park for Taste of Chicago.
The staff was very friendly. There was a 2 hour cocktail reception and breakfast included. There was plenty of seating for both. 
We loved having the extra space in the room. 
We parked in the parking garage and didn't have any problems.
The lobby area was really pretty with a cascading waterfall.
The only complaint we have is the kids said the pool was too small.

title: “Good value in Dallas”
text: We stayed two nights at the Magnolia Hotel in downtown Dallas in early January. We found the staff very friendly and accomodating. Good value for the money. The only downside was no formal restaurant on the premises, but there were several good restaurants in the area.

title: “Gets worse every stay.”
text:
Unfortunately, I stay at this hotel a lot. I can't say I've ever been entirely thrilled with it (like the time there was no hot water, and I had to go to my meeting without a shower), but every time I go there it seems to get worse. At a minimum, they never get it entirely right. 
I'll focus on my most recent trip. In the bathroom I had not used, there was a towel hanging on the back of the door. I get that hotels are trying to be more environmentally friendly, but I don't want to use another guest's towel. Also, my own towels had not been restocked, which of course, I didn't realize until I was climbing into the shower. Fortunately, there was one clean towel. 
I had lunch in their restaurant, because the hotel is quite isolated and it's the hotel or Benihana. I ordered a salad. Hard to believe but they messed up my salad, even though I was very clear on how I wanted it. I had to send it back, and when it came out the second time? Messed up in a new way. Who messes up a salad twice? The Westin Park Central. It all worked out OK though, because the flank steak in the salad was pure rubber and completely inedible. 
The manager dropped by to apologize and give me his business card, but didn't offer to comp my meal. An inedible salad and a diet Pepsi was $23.00. 
When I wanted to print my boarding pass for my return flight I stopped by the business center where they charge $5.95 for 15 minutes of internet access, plus a per page charge for printing. I dropped by the front desk and asked if there was some place I could print my boarding pass, and they told me the business center. I stay at a lot of hotels, and never pay to print a boarding pass. When I told this to the front desk clerk, he just looked down at his computer screen and shrugged.
The sad thing is, I have status with Starwood. I was on the Starwood perferred floor with my unclean towels, and unstocked room. I can only pray my sheets were clean. I can't imagine what must happen if you don't have status. 
As a side note to Westin: 
Your bath products are terrible. Way too perfumey. Men don't want to smell like women, and women don't want ot smell like Westin.

title: “Great stay at the Thompson LES”
text: Great hotel with some of the most pleasant and friendly staff I have seen in quite some time. We asked for a high floor and were booked into a room on the 17th floor with a wrap around balcony with amazing views of the city. The design of the rooms are very cool with black wooden floors, a concrete ceiling and amazing linen. They have a pool on the third floor which was perfect for some cocktails, the bar on the 7th floor was closed during my stay. Thank you Thompson LES I had a fabulous stay and will return!!

title: “Beautiful Downtown Hotel”
text: Large, beautiful rooms. Service was excellent. The location is within walking distance of so much in Seattle. Only negative was that the bar staff was overwhelmed when our group of 10 came in for drinks.

title: “Our 2nd Stay not as good as Our First”
text:
We have stayed here twice. The last time the weekend of April 30th, the food was so good at the Birch Restaurant that we hardly left the place. Our server was very charming that I knew if we ordered what he recommended - it would be a great dining experience and it was. However the room had some problems and it was a very busy weekend and the management could not be reached. For one, there was some chlorine or chemical substance near the pool that destroyed my partners jeans. And as our bad luck would have it, when we had breakfast in the morning at Birch and the table hadn't been wiped and my shirt was covered with maple syrup. It certainly wasn't the fault of the server and i don't know how someone must have taken a bath in the syrup.. but after the weekend we had 2 garments spoiled.
Our room phones and a few other things during this stay like the knob on the AC control were broken. So we are debating if we should stay here again. The first stay was absolutely perfect and I know if we were able to get a chance to talk to the management that they would have remedied the problems.

title: “My room was infested with cockroaches.”
text:
The location of the Sohotel is great, the room was a decent size for the price with a nice window and view and the shared bathrooms were clean. At first everything seemed great. 
However, after returning to the room after my first night out and turning on the lights, I discovered that the room was infested with cockroaches. There were many cockroaches on the floor and walls and even cockroaches crawling on the bed and the pillow. The desk clerk would not give me a different room and would not do anything to get rid of the cockroaches. I wanted to pay for just that one night and check out in the morning. I was told that my credit card had already been charged for my complete stay and the hotel would not give me a refund. I was on a very limited budget and could not afford to lose the money, so I slept with the lights on to keep the cockroaches away.
I have stayed in other inexpensive hotels in NYC and this place was awful!

title: “Excellent Hotel & Location”
text: Eldon Luxury Suites is located near the Metro and Washington DC Convention Center and offers upscale suites. We found a great deal on the Washington DC travel and tourism website and couldn't pass it up. We got luxury accommodations with the Freedom Suite (1-comfortable King bed w/ a very uncomfortable sofabed and fully equipped kitchen). The Metro is about two blocks away. CVS is just around the corner. There are two grocery stores nearby. We walked to the Whole Foods Market about a mile away and had dinner on an outside patio. They offer free continental breakfast before 10AM with pastries from a local bakery, coffee, tea and juices. We stopped at the Cozy Corner right around the corner, a ma and pa operation with very cheap breakfasts. The taxis average $10 each way. For the value, quality and location, I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Resort HAHA! Spa doesn't exist!”
text: This is an over priced hotel on a lake. the view is very nice if you get a lakeside room. The bacony is dirty and rusty, the bathroom is moldy, they could hire a cleaning staff that actually took the time to clean. We were there for two days, housekeeping had to be asked to clean the room. When they did, they threw personal possessions around the room. The coffee/wine bar was never staffed. When we arrived the second night, there was a drunk man urinating in the flower bed in front of the main entrance. Try explaining that to your children. The only meal charged to my room was a buffet breakfast for three people that cost $56.00. Somehow that ended being $80.00 at check out. The front desk person was unable to account for the difference. The room was a double queen room, this room at any other hotel would have been $120.00. This place is soooo over priced and I can only guess they rate themselves, because this is not a resort and not a spa and not worth the prices they charge for anything. This is a chalk it up to experience and I'll never stay there again deal.

title: “Great hotel near LAX”
text: This was my first stay at this property. It's so close to LAX, you can almost walk there, if there were sidewalks. Solidly good property, personable and welcoming staff, free Internet access in the lobby with a good number of pcs, free airport shuttle service and good breakfast buffet at a reasonable price. Comfortable rooms with the typical great Sheraton beds. At least during my stay, this is a very busy property. Great soundproofing because I heard no airplane noise during my stay on the 3rd floor. Public transportation is close by but it's slow which is the southern California way. Santa Monica is close by for shopping and dining and you can take one public bus there. Mustafa at the Front Desk is great!

title: “Clean, Noisy, Mediocre Front Office Workers”
text:
We have stayed in this hotel for two days. Overall the hotel is clean and that is very important in New York City. Although you are paying the ususal overpriced fee per night. There is constant noise even at higher floors.
The front office people are indifferent and sometimes even annoying. Finding a flat for rent or a boutique hotel would be a better alternative.

title: “Typical Expensive San Francisco Hotel”
text:
My husband and I stayed here, even though we only live 30 minutes away since it was our anniversary and we had to be in the city early the next morning anyway. We looked at quite a few hotels, as never had stayed in a hotel in SF since we live so close and decided to splurge on this one.
The W chain is well known and caters to the younger affluent business/party goers, which is evident when you walk into any of their hotels. Rude and arrogant, but decorated in a funky way. We arrived 2 hours ahead of check in (3pm) and called to let them know that we were going to be there early. When we got there they told us our room was not cleaned and we would have to wait in the lobby. Where they had free internet which is nice (but they don't provide wireless in the rooms, interesting isn't it. It is like 15-20 to actually get internet in your room). They want you to hang out downstairs to give that trendy vibe so people come out and hang out in their bar. 
Anyway the front desk guy was rude. Took our cell phone number to let us know when it was ready. There were maybe 30 people waiting for their rooms, and at 3 pm magically they were all cleaned. Basically they didn't want anyone to check in ahead of time, even though everyone knew they were done being cleaned. We had a Fabulous room on the 24th floor, which had a king corner view. The view was AMAZING. But we were paying a lot for that view so it was expected. They had a cute sitting corner and it was nicely decorated. However all the decorations were covered in dust (the frames, fake tree branch, games, books). The TV was oddly small and in a weird position that hurt your neck when trying to watch. The bed was comfy, however the sheets (which are supposed to be one of their trademarks) were not Wonderful. They had obviously been bleached and it doesn't matter what your threadcount is if you bleach it ever wash, it is no longer soft and luxurious. 
Also the room was not "clean" feeling as I would expect for the price that we were paying. THe bathroom was very nice but you could tell that it had been used A LOT. 
Overall the hotel is just okay. I am sure when it opened it was great, but it seems a bit worn around the edges for the amount of money you are paying. If you like the W hotels by all means stay here, but I feel that in a city like SF you can probably find something a little bit different and definitely cheaper. It was a disappointment to us.
(oh value parking is $50, but it has in and out privileges and our car was always ready to go when we got down there)

title: “Disappointed”
text: This hotel is well located but not well kept. We were initially shown a room with unwashed sheets, enough said! When we requested housekeeping, the front desk told us it would be easier to change our room. We were moved much smaller room ( you would think they would have made a small attempt to make us happy). Unfortunately this room had peelin wallpaper, moldy bathroom and generally unvacuumed feel to the carpet( needless to say we kept shoes on) as I was too tired to tussle with the front desk again. We were there for a pleasurable memorial day getaway, so I didn't let this experience put a damper on our trip...but, I would not recommend this hotel until they get a handle on their housekeeping and spruce up the rooms

title: “Good intentions but they get lost in the details”
text: We stayed here this last weekend and I have mixed feelings about the hotel. I booked it through an Internet operator because they were offering a good price and I was looking for a nice place downtown. As positive I would mention the friendliness of the employees and the nice decoration. Location is wonderful, 10 minutes from Beale street. Also, the room was comfortable and roomy, with a wet bar and complimentary coffee. Negative, the valet parking service. The employees were doing what they could, but cars were piling up in a one way street, often blocking the traffic and we had to pay $23 + tax/day. Nobody informed us in advance about the fee, we had the surprise when we were checking out. The AC/heating unit in the room was awfully noisy, we had to turn it on when we were leaving the room, to achieve the temperature we wanted. The bathroom was roomy but very dark, I had trouble applying the make up and the hair dryer only had one speed, it was insufficient for my hair. They had high speed Internet, but not wireless, which surprised me, you had to plug the laptop, at least in our room. No cable available, you had to pay extra, the TV only had like 9 channels available. They offered a wide selection of movies, but the price was between $12 and $13 dollars. The breakfast was continental, a very simple selection; I would have liked some eggs and bacon available. As I said, it is a very nice hotel but they need to work the details a little bit more.

title: “Good location.”
text: We stayed at Crowne Plaza Philadelphia for 2 nights. The hotel has a great location. Only one block from Rittenhouse Square and the main commercial street, and of course very near good restaurants. The room was nice. The only problem is that the hotel is crowdy, lots of people everywhere. THEY GAVE US THE ROOM AT 6 PM. Too late for people who is coming from another city and tired. They told us to visit the museum and return in 1 hour but the room was not ready for us although other people were given one. The price was really good, but not the attention. They tried to avoid our complaints for the late room by giving us a complimentary continental breakfast. But when we tried to have it before leaving the hotel the case was that the bar was closed al 7 o'clock.

title: “Grand Canyon and San Diego Vacation”
text: We stayed 4 nights at this hotel and it was pretty much as expected from reading other reviews.Checkin was effortless as I had booked through Travelodge and as I had requested ,received a room on the upper floor and away from highway. The room itself was average, looked nice but carpet was stained and looked a little dirty, the room had the mini fridge as I had requested, one of the windows would't close properly. The biggest problem I had with the room was that there was no venting in the bathroom,so when you took a shower you either had to open the window(which my wife and daughter were not comfortable with, no curtain) or when done showereing, open the door which let the steam and heat into the room. We were very pleased with laundry facilities used them twice. maid service was excellent, they gave us pool towels to take to the beach with us and even folded our blankets that we had brought with us. Overall a pleasant stay,good location, very economical, was charged exactly what was quoted. Sidenote WIFI worked well and was free but to use computer in laundry area $2.49 per minute.

title: “unfinished room”
text: I did a priceline and got a room for $50 which is a good deal however the room I was given was unfinished. The walls were not completely painted. The staff was indifferent. The hotel is also not well situated for walking around Philadelphia. Finally the parking is expensive, $18 a day. Overall, I would not stay at this hotel.

title: “We got married here, and we return frequently!”
text:
This is without question the "Grand Dame" of Seattle Hotels.
The exterior is classic, and upon entering the "Lobby", a grand mult-floor height marble hall, one feels like this is one of the grand European hotels.
We were married here several years ago, in a small family-only ceremony in the Cascade Suite, a marvelous one-bedrom 3,400 sqft suite with a private dining room (where we had a private dinner served).
Unfortunately, there is no way to make that into a suite with several bedrooms, despite the grand living area; the most that can be enclosed in privacy - and safety for young children - is with one other executive suite.
Therefore, we've also stayed in the only 3BR suite in the Hotel (still not quite large enough for the family). As far as we know, the other corner suites are 2BR at most.
Usually, when it is just the two of us, we stay in a large executive suite, and occasionally in the larger bedroom (part of the corner parlor suite that goes with the 2-bedroom suite... and with the one 3-bedroom suite).
As wonderful as this hotel is, there are some problems with the heating system, such that it is tricky to get a room that isn't too warm.
We now know which rooms to request, and we call ahead and remind the Front Desk staff that we'd like the thermostat turned "as cool as possible".
The service here is absolutely the best. With special requests for a large extended family, the hotel staff came through with everything from tiny bathrobes for children (which we of course purchased for the grandchildren!) to getting a prescription refilled on short notice.
And we've arranged special meals in the Georgian Room (the first time, when we could still hand-carry a special bottle of wine on board a commercial flight), and it was just perfect.
We tried another hotel, and we walked out of the new Four Seasons (The Olympic *used to be* a Four Seasons), which was in one of the few seamy areas left in downtown. 
We then tried one of the new high-rise hotels, but it was like walking into the (small) lobby of an office building, simply to be spirited upstairs on the elevator right by the front door.
(To due justice to this other Hotel, it did have a wonderfully huge and deep bathtub, with water that came out of the ceiling; if only our grandchldren could have seen THIS!)
But the suite was just "another modern hotel suite", albeit one with very soothing displays on the walls, a very "zen" sensation to be sure, one lasting the full stay.
The Fairmont Olympic has become "our home away from home" during our frequent and occasionally extended trips to Seattle and the surrounding area.
Sign up for the FREE "PRESIDENT'S CLUB", which allows you free Internet Service.

title: “Nice room, but nothing else spectacular”
text: I was there for my 30th H.S. reunion. The food at the reunion was terrible. Everything else was boring, bland and inexpensive to serve. A lot of pasta, beans, rice, fajitas. That was it. They had a carving station with just turkey. I've never been to a restaurant, hotels included where they didn't serve at least roast beef, ham, pork or something other than turkey at a carving station, and quite honestly, the turkey was the only thing worth eating. All of the food in the serving containers was cold, they had only one dressing (Caesar) for the salad, not even oil and vinegar, and they started clearing the tables of all the candles only 2 hours into the reunion, which I thought was really rude, since it was only 9:30 p.m. at the time. I was really disappointed. I thought they would serve better food considering this was a large event with a lot of people. To top it all off, they overcharged my credit card $36.00, which I had to call my bank and deal with that issue. Our room was nice but VERY small. Hardly any room to move around in. Next time I stay in the valley, I'll definitely pick someplace else. I was reading the room service menu, and apparently it wasn't just the reunion. They hardly had anything to choose from for dinner. Literally, they had like 3 or 4 items. No steak, no prime rib, just salmon and pork chops. This isn't a poor part of town. They have the worse room service menu I've ever seen. Needless to say, I won't be back there ever again. Oh and for those of you that don't bring your own computer but need to get online, they charge you $12.00 for 15 min. Every hotel I've ever stayed in gives you access for free, whether in your room or in the lobby.

title: “Nice for a quick stay”
text: Our one-night stay was a pleasant one. The staff was friendly and accommodating. Check-in and check-out were quick and easy, despite my boyfriend leaving his photo ID at home. Our room was huge, the L-shaped couch was comfortable, and the king-sized bed was a dream to sleep on. The major downfall of the room was that we were on the second floor and therefore didn't have much a view so it was somewhat dark. We ordered room service from the pub next-door (Mackeys), and despite it being a Saturday night, the menu was quite limited, but tasty. Some of the appliances in the room (iron, TV remote) didn't work very well. The bathroom was small with little counter space, but Q-tips and cotton balls were provided which was a nice touch you don't often see in hotels. We also lucked out with easy street parking, a good thing b/c nearby parking garages were closed when we got there. Overall, a good experience.

title: “Great hotel for a girls trip to DC”
text:
We loved this hotel! The location was fine. We used the DuPont Metro station to get around which was only about 5 blocks away. The Old Town Trolley tours pick up from the Marriott across the street. So we never felt like we were too far out of town. Cabs to and from downtown were about $10-12 depending on traffic (and there were 2 extras in the car, so there were surcharges).
It's always great to have a suite. This was no exception. The bathroom was clean and had a lot of space for three girls' toiletries (along with two sinks outside of the bathroom). The beds were fine. The staff were great, always helpful. The breakfast was great too. We were there for Memorial Day weekend and it was packed, but they had extra seating out and everything worked out well. We were on the floor with a lot of Rolling Thunder participants and families, but never heard a thing at night. The free internet stations are a great help to those of us without smartphones and who don't want to bring laptops on vacation, but do want to be able to check on reservations, print maps and check in at the airlines.
The only complaint I had was about room service. They were a bit slow and the only staff who I didn't find entirely polite. 
Shockingly, we even got good deals in the gift shop (similar items on the street or airport were more than they were here). Also this is about 2 blocks from a Walgreens, so we were able to pick up some items and keep them in our room fridge.

title: “Dirty room”
text: In general the rooms have been clean, but this last time it could have used a little more. There was a red stain on the light switch that I did not want to identify.

title: “A Midtown Treat”
text: A wonderful location at an outstanding price (Expeedia gets you one night free). W. 44th right off of 5th is a great place to be, close to everything, but quiet even in midday. The two blocks to Times Square are full of interesting things (the whimisical facade of the landlocked home of the NY Yacht Club is worth a trip down 44th alone) and first rate restaurants. Be sure to get a suite. The rooms are small (as is the whole building) but the suite is a great value and exceptionally comfortable. The M Bar is terrific and the service friendly and welcoming... their Manhattan is as good as any you will ever get in its namesake city. The 24 hour espresso machine doesn't sound like that much of an amenity, but is a real treat when you get in late from a night on the town. Only downsides... airshaft views from the suites and no in-room movies... but if you'd wanted the Sheraton you'd have gone their anyway. A special place for people who enjoy and understand Manhattan.

title: “Nice Hotel”
text: This hotel is very modern and posh. I stayed there with 13 other girls for a Bachelorette party on a Friday. The area is abuzz on weekends and there are lots of beautiful people hanging around the lobby, bar, and waiting in line to get into Ghostbar. The hotel is right next to the AA center and there was a Stars game going on so the area was VERY busy and crowded. Traffic was not the greatest. Overnight valet parking was $24. Service was great but got the feeling that if we weren't cute young girls we would have been ignored. Although none of the staff yelled at us, I was told several times by my friends that when they booked the room they were reminded over and over again to keep the noise down. So, if you are going there to party in the room, think of going somewhere else. Overall, room was nice and clean. Staff was very helpful and mean it when they say "Whatever, whenever". We needed a limo ASAP and they called and booked it and had it there in 30 minutes. I would stay here again with the girls.

title: “Great and Friendly Service!”
text: I stayed here after having a difficult time catching a missed flight due to some bad weather at my destination. First off I'm thankful they have shuttle service to and from the airport so I didnt have to worry about a cab. The hotel was nice. Knowing that Sleep Inn is a budget brand I didnt expect it to be like the Ritz Carolton when I walked in. The staff was amazing! Super helpful in helping me get situated and helping me get around the city that night. The room is fine. I see on here that people have complained about cigarette smoke but that was not my experience. My room smelt fine and I didnt have any issues. They arent soundproof. You can hear people opening and closing doors, but it was a Saturday night and this hotel seemed almost completely full. The hotel is very close to the city. I ventured to downtown to check out how Charlotte is. All in all I would say my stay was great. Great service, which means a lot to me, rooms were fine, close to the city, airport shuttle service, free wifi, and a great breakfast. If Im ever in Charlotte again then I would probably stay at this location again.

title: “Great Place to stay!”
text: This hotel is close in proximity to Beale Street and most attractions. Rooms are very large, spacious and well kept. Management is very nice and accommodating. This isn’t the Peabody but for us it works perfectly! We have stayed here two out of three times and will continue to stay at this property!

title: “Nice, new, friendly, convenient”
text: I had to book a trip to Indianapolis last minute and booked through Priceline: $50/night. Am an Elite member and treated as such. The staff was exceptional - they were extremely busy with a Colts game and conventions, but made sure they were very friendly and poised. Also very informed about surrounding eating and shopping choices. The lobby and rooms have just been renovated and everything is very nice. All rooms had a coffee maker and a mini fridge. The pool/whirlpool was the exception. The whirlpool has some sort of weird plastic liner on in and a ring of dirt in it. The location is fantastic and a skybridge connects you to the convention center and the Circle Center Mall. It is a great choice for business and family travel.

title: “Not up to web Site”
text: Period of stay 4 - 7th November 2004. Having read the review of the hotel my wife and I were a little apprehensive. However, we were assured by the hotels web site that all refurbisment would be completed by the autumn. What a pity the hotel doesn't read its own publicity. The bar was still under construction. Our room had the new TV etc but also a plug in heater because the radiator did not work. This restricted the space a little. The windows were dirty although they could be opened to look at the traffic etc below. The warddrobe was very small and very old fashioned. When having a shower the water half filled the bath and took about 20 minutes to go down the plug. On the plus side the staff were extremeley helpful, including the bell hop. Howevevr, on the day we were checking out Reception did not know it was the day of the NYC Marathon, depite there being a team of Italian runners staying the hotel. Don't bother with the breakfast - to dear. Instead go to the NY Luncheon Diner on E49th Street. Excellent service and they refused a tip.

title: “Spacious & Gracious NYC rooms! What a find!”
text:
We spent a great family weekend at the Blakely Hotel on a January trip to NYC. The weather outside was cold, snowy, rainy and wet and while the sights of the city beckoned, we were anxious to return to our very spacious, beautifully decorated suite at the Blakely. The front desk was accommodating and welcoming; the continental breakfast ample, with yogurts, cereals, juices, breads and fresh fruit replenished throughout the serving hours. Our suite had a microwave and mini-fridge with a sink and counter, and we could have prepared a light meal, however the Italian restaurant off the hotel lobby was too tempting to pass up. 
 The beds and pillows were comfy and we basked in all the space--it is such a luxury to find in the City. We thought the location was perfect: a couple short blocks off Broadway, yet within walking distance of Times Square and Central Park---even in the snow! An H&M store was a couple blocks away, so the teens were thrilled. 
 We loved the Blakely blue umbrellas which were provided in inclement weather and look forward to our next return visit. The Blakely provides a lot of bang for the buck and is a wonderful family hotel. You'll be hard-pressed to find so much square footage for the dollar!

title: “short walk to white house”
text:
My daughter(15) and me stayed at the end of our trip for 3 nights. Staff is very helpful and friendly, room was big, clean, beds ok. Slept well although room was located at the street. Park service very expensive, breakfast at the fireflies, too.We went to Starbucks just 5 minutes away. Subway just 2 minutes, but if you want to walk to White House, go by foot, it will only take 20 minutes. Restaurants nearby.Hop on hop off bus stops directly at Dupont Circle which is a nice place in the evening, music and artists.
We enjoyed our stay, neigbourhood was ok, felt save. Would stay there again.

title: “Great service”
text:
Having read other reviews on trip advisor I decided to book a couple of nights at the Four Points. Unfortunately on arrival I was told that the hotel was still fully booked and that I would have to be transferred to another hotel. Normally this would not be good news but I was transferred to the Roosevelt at no extra cost (cab fares paid both ways) and also given a full refund for the night I missed at the four points.
On arrival the next day I was especially looked after by Melissa on reception who put me in a great room on the 18th floor (room 1805). The high speed internet connection was free (first time ever for me in a NY hotel) and you even got a complementary bottle of water!
Although the location is not the best in NY it's very central location and a quick cab ride to time square or a short walk to Broadway, Greenwich Village etc.
I'll definitely book it again.

title: “decent”
text: The hotel has its pros and cons. The staff was very nice and knowledgeable. The biggest con was that there was no free coffee in the room or the hotel itself. The price of a small coffee was 2.29 and it was cheaper to go across the street to dunkin donuts to get coffee. The rooms are small but nice. The tiny bathroom has one mirror and that is difficult for 2 females to put on makeup, to do hair, etc. There is another mirror but it is covered in some sort of antique substance that is attractive but you can barely see yourself . There is also only one space for outlets besides the one in the bathroom. The location is decent and in walking distance to a lot of areas. The wine tasting is great and the decor is very nice. The beds are the best I have slept on in a hotel room before.

title: “Friendly Staff, Good Location, Lots of Resturants close by”
text: Not bad for a Hampton Inn,,, The room was clean and comfortable. The Staff was helpful with directions to subway and restaurants. The hotel looked a little old, but was clean and easy to navigate. My only negative was the noise from the fire station located across the street. Sirens all night, as they turn them on right when they exit the station. Also, noise when the bars close. I was not certain what is close by, the the clubs were packed on Friday pm till closing. This is not the hotel's fault, perhaps you should ask for a room with a view of the back side, or lake side of this property. ( I am not certain if this is even an option ). Close to Frontera Resturant and other Chicago dining experiences

title: “Very Rude Desk Managers”
text: We stayed here because The Willard is "the place to stay in DC". The hotel is lovely but any granduer of the lobby is lost due in part to rude staff and management. We arrived late on the first night and were checked in by a very rude agent. When I asked to speak to a manager he informed me that he was the manager and that if I needed to speak to someone else I would need to wait until Monday morning. Our room was lovely but when your first impression is clouded by poor service it's hard to enjoy the stay. I will not be staying at the Willard anytime soon. Perhaps they should just call it a glorified Holiday Inn and be done with it.

title: “Reasonably Priced for NYC”
text: My husband and I have stayed at the Affinia Dumont two years in a row over the 4th of July weekend. The hotel is within walking distance to Macy's and the other stores on 34th Street. A subway station is a short walk from the hotel. The beds are very comfortable and the rooms are quiet because there is very little hallway noise (there are fewer than a dozen rooms on each floor). We stay at the Affinia because there are fireworks at the foot of 34th Street every year on the 4th. A non-smoking room on a high floor with a view of the river was requested well in advance, and although we checked in at 4:00 pm on the day we arrived, they were unable to accommodate either request. We were disappointed. The toilet in our room was making noise constantly when we arrived. We were not as happy with our stay this year and we will probably stay elsewhere the next time we visit New York City.

title: “Great value for New york and excellent staff”
text:
Ended up here as a volcano refugee. Chose not to go back to our original hotel and booked in here instead. 
As we were stuck the staff were great at letting us re-book our rooms daily at an agreed rate and not taking advantage of our predicament. 
Rooms are small but perfectly formed. I had some of the best nights sleep I've had in ages there. Shower lovely and the free wi-fi appreciated.
