The bed would have been tight for a couple but great for a single. 
If I return on business I will be looking to stay here again.

title: “Large Comfortable Room near the airport”
text: We were only passing through Charlotte while driving to VA. We were pleased with the size of the room. Large for a suite. We were worried about the airplane noise but it was nonexistent after about 10:30. Breakfast was average to below. ooms were clean but will need some updating in a while. Neighboorhood is isolated but right off Billy Graham Pkwy.Staff was only average. We did ask for assistance setting the alarm clock which was tricky.

title: “Don't take the Kids!!!”
text:
First, I paid higher than the price quoted on Orbitz which according to the local cab driver was triple the normal cost of the rooms. The rooms were right out of a bad 70's pimp flick and looked like they might be rented by the hour. We were lucky enough to stay in the mirrored suite. The walk-in shower covered in mirrors and included a table had red and blue light in the ceiling. The two shower heads didn't have enough water pressure to equal one good one. The bed with mirrors over it and on the walls was covered with cheap rose petals and a funky heart shaped pillow and came complete with a red light over the bed. When we looked in the cabinet where the microwave was kept there were about 5 or 6 porn magazines. The newest equipment was a stereo in the room. We were on the second floor of the Inn and when it rained the carpet in front of the door got soaked.
After hailing a cab from an evening sports event when we told the driver were we were going he reponded "oh man, just my luck!" and refused to turn in to the hotel parking lot and dropped us off at the lot adjacent to the hotel. We asked a local about safety in walking to some the the events and she responded that normally it wouldn't be safe but because of the games police presence was heightened in that area and the normal criminals knew to stay away! Upon return to our room there was a man a few doors down and was scratching like he was coming down off of drugs and asked us if we "had anything".
I had to put something over a spot on the sheet the first night and the next day pulled them off completed and pour water on them to ensure they would be changed. I also bought spray bleach and lysol for the walk in shower and some of what I though was just tile marks rinsed down the drain! The pictures on the web site must be at least 20 years old or the rooms have seen a lot of use.
It was in walking distance to the Uptown Cabaret which I found out was a strip club so there was local entertainment. Getting food however was another issue as there were no restaurants locally that stayed open late and no local shopping. Overall it served its purpose and we had some good laughs about it; hey maybe if there is a next time I will try one of the heart shaped jacuzzi rooms; but I'd rather think that I won't make the mistake of booking my hotel late when I need to come to the area next time.

title: “Ugh.”
text:
The rooms are TINY even by NYC standards, and the wifi is really weak. The glass bathrooms are a travesty, but to be fair they do warn you about that. The worst thing, though, was having to share the lift with the pretentious wankers going up and down to/from the rooftop bar. (We had to wait up to 10 minutes just to get a lift to the lobby.) The bar's view is nice, except you won't be able to get a) a table and b) service because of the aforementioned crowd of pretentious wankers - who get pretty drunk and rowdy later in the evening, so not recommended if you have kids or if you hate drunken idiots. 
On the plus side, the staff are pretty nice.
It's pretty expensive for what you get. If you're on a budget you'd get better value from a hostel - if not, stay somewhere else!.

title: “Nice hotel with large rooms”
text: We have stayed here twice and have had great experiences both times. Rooms are large, clean, nicely decorated and updated and the beds are comfortable. This past stay we got a large top floor room with two walls of windows overlooking Kenmore Square. It is not the most central location if you are sight seeing in Boston, but the T stop is conveniently located right in front of the hotel and Newbury Street is a nice walk (4 or 5 blocks away). Great place to stay if you want to be close to Fenway. We enjoyed returning from dinner elsewhere in the city and having a night cap at the Eastern Standard connected to the hotel.

title: “Great Location”
text: A good rate for this area of Chicago. Clean and very polite and helpful staff. The best part of this hotel is the location. Right on Rush St. so tons of great restaurants. Walking distance to a great deal of the best attractions and really close to the Mag Mile.

title: “Best of Dallas”
text: This was my second stay at the wonderful Melrose. A former frequent guest of the Crescent Court, the Melrose has it all over them for service, warmth, and the true definition of hospitality. From the moment you enter, you feel as though you are home. The Bar is fabulous, the food excellent, and the Front Desk staff is second to none, especially Michael. And..for the business traveler, the location is fantastic and you can actually walk places. Thanks again to all and see you soon!

title: “Beautiful convenient hotel”
text: Very comfortable and clean room. Beautiful lobby and surroundings. Stayed here for a visit to Michigan State as we had an early flight out in the morning. Extremely convenient shuttle. Very friendly staff. Great room service.

title: “Old and fatigued”
text: Stayed for a convention so the room rate was reduced. The rooms are depressing and the mattress was soft soft soft. The pillows were tiny like a bento box. Bathroom dismally small and not attractive. No minibar. Front desk people were indifferent. Valet lost my car keys.

author.location: Cape May Court House, New Jersey

title: “A good place to stay”
text: My family of 5 stayed there for 1 week. The rooms were good. They were clean and comfortable. The beds were not as comfortable as I had read. They were average, not great, but not poor. The rooms air conditioning never seemed to get the room super cool. But it was comfortable. The breakfast buffet was fair to good. It depended on when you arrived. Sometimes the food was warm, sometimes not. The pancakes were never hot, just barely warm. The only problem we found was that large groups of kids came to stay there. It would get very loud in the atrium and you could forget breakfast if you didn't arrive before them. The lines would get so long and there were never enough tables available. The ones that were available had dirty food trays on them. One thing I will say is that the staff did keep the kids quiet at night. We didn't have any problems with them keeping us awake, and we were surrounded by them. The location of the hotel was pretty convient. It was about a 10 to 15 minute walk to the metro. We would stay there again if we had our kids with us, because of the extra sleeper sofa.

title: “Great Value, Nice Room”
text: We were flying out of DIA to go on the Alaskan Cruise. Trying to decide whether or not to leave our car in the long term parking, take a shuttle, get a ride from family and leave the car at their house,... what to do? Hubs found out Microtel allows parking in their lot, and provides a shuttle to the airport. No extra charge. For the price of a room, free parking and free shuttle? Done deal! The best part is, its a NICE ROOM! Large, clean and with a decent continental breakfast! Only drawback was the parking lot was FULL and we had to wait a bit for a parking spot in the lot, not on the street, to leave the car for the full week. Small inconvenience for a LOT of convenience! The desk clerks were friendly and accomodating, the shuttle drivers friendly and considerate. We have stayed twice now, both good experiences.

title: “Wonderful team”
text: Amazing front desk team anchored by Lisa Kaiser and Crystal Hughes and Aaron Gonzalez. Go the extra mile in every visit and care personally for each guest. Best concierge team of any hotel I've visited worldwide most especially Casey Duggan and Fredo but each of them is totally generous and able to make everything you dream of happen from little to huge favors and requests. Bazaar restaurant is superb but the little known jewel if the hotel is Tres with its amazing breakfasts and wonderful host Autumn. The pool is also hugely restorative and the entire waitstaff up there are attentive and kind. I only vacation now at the SLS. It's my home away from home in Pratt because the hotel is so beautiful but mostly because the hotel team is simply the best in the business. I couldn't be more thankful to each of them. I recommend the hotel with my whole heart. Bravo and than you

title: “Ask for Lillian at the Spa Di La Fronza”
text: This is in a prime spot in the middle of the city, with nice views of the river and close access to a river walk. Plenty of restaurants and nightlife within walking distance of the hotel. I stayed in king bed room and it was set up nicely, with an area to work, comfortable bed, flatscreen, etc. Hotel decor has a boutique feel to it. The hotel overall is pretty massive and a bit of a maze to find your way around, particularly if you are attending a conference here. There's a coffee kiosk set up on the 1st floor to grab a quick Starbucks and muffin in the AM. The gym is set up well, with newer machines. Across from the fitness center is the Spa Di La Fronza, where I wandered in and asked to schedule a massage. Lillian took care of me and did a great job working out the kinks from a long sales conference. Its a full service spa, including barber services as well.

title: “Without question, THE BEST hotel we've stayed in”
text: We have stayed twice in this hotel. We absolutely LOVE it. The staff is amazing, helpful and friendly. The hotel is so close to everything you need. If ever we return to Indy, this is our hotel, no question! It doesn't get better than the Embassy :)

title: “Not what I expected from a Doubletree”
text:
I stayed here for a conference and found the hotel to be lacking. The hotel refused to allow anyone an early check-in and told everyone to come back at 3. At 2 I found that many others had already received their room even after requesting an early check-in so I could make it to the conference opening on time. When we did get our room we were surprised to find someone already in the room. The hotel apologized with free breakfasts for our stay. My HHonors account has the request to be away from the elevator and instead we were given the room that backs up to the elevators for sound effects for our stay. 
I agree with other reviews that the breakfast would not have been worth it if we had paid, but the restaurant staff was the best staff in the hotel. The front desk staff was slow, unresponsive to requests and flat out rude. What appeared to be the manager had many awkward conversations with hotel staff in the lobby area which is quite small. The only restroom on the main lobby level was out of the way, small and not very clean. 
To top it off we had booked 2 rooms for business. Originally these were 2 double rooms but we had asked to change one to a king room due to change in attendance. The hotel staff would only put this down as a request on our reservation. When my boss checked in he was given a double room and told no kings were available. When I checked in I had to wait because only kings were available. So they refused to honor the request but yet tried to get me and my business associate to take a single bed room after they gave out a double? The hotel front desk staff seems to be understaffed as well as not empowered to handle most problems.

title: “Location & Value = 10 out of 10”
text:
Ok, I'll keep this short and simple. Location is fantastic. 1 block from Cable Car and 2 blocks off Fisherman's Wharf main area.
Room was average, they are renovating hallways on 4th floor but we experienced no inconvenience with workers or noise. No view, others picture of rooms with no view are accurate. Safe in room with key. Bathroom clean and average. Don't let some pics on trip advisor for this hotel fool you - the HI Express is more modern than the HI beside it but seems that the "older" looking pics on here are of the HI not the Express.
Breakfast was ok, eggs left something to be desired. Wireless in lobby only, rooms are wired. Staff said they'll be getting wireless on the floors eventually. Parking is retarded at $40+/day.

title: “Do Not Stay Here....”
text: if you require valet parking, onsite garage or bellman. But my hubby and I knew that before we booked the reservation and this Sheraton turned out to be a gem of a hotel! We usually stay Midtown/Uptown at the larger Starwoods, but our business brought us down to the Chelsa area. We pulled right up front, I got a luggage trolly from the lobby, we unloaded and my husband parked at the recommended garage a convenient 1 and 1/2 blocks away. Parking rates were $25 a day, below NYC price standards. Check in was a breeze with Paul doing a FAB job. In fact we found all the staff to be friendly, smiling and helpful during our 2 night stay. We stayed on the 12th floor facing the back and it was the quietest room we ever had in NYC. The hotel is on 25th St which is quiet in itself so I don't think staying street side would be a problem (just don't get a room next to he ice machine, it was literally by the door of one of the rooms). Room was smaller than we were used to but more than acceptable in size. Bathroom also on the small side, did not have a tub, but a large walk in shower which we preferred. Room and bath were pristine with not a speck of dust or dirt. Sheets were crisp, towels were large and soft and both smelled like they were hung outside on a summer day. Bed was incredibly comfortable. No problem controlling room temps. Room lighting was more than ample. We are big readers while in bed and usually have to change hotel bulbs to make them brighter or move lamps closer to the bed. Not here. Two reading lights over the bed and lights bedside were perfect! We did not eat in the restaurant or go to the bar, but when we popped our heads in to look around every staff person smiled or said hi. Two elevators were super fast and we never waited more than 30 seconds for one. Convenience of close subways both Uptown and Downtown. Free (plug-in) internet in the room with 2 computers and a printer downstairs. Coffee machine in room but we preferred the free coffee station set up each morning in the lobby. Electronic safe in armoire. We had a lovely experience at this hotel and we would not hesitate to stay there again.

title: “A special location for a wonderful mini vacation!”
text: I was surprised to find a small hotel in a very central location in SF at such a reasonable rate in a world class city! The service was great and dinner at Kuleto's next door was superb. If you don't want the sounds of the city (sirens, street musicians playing saxophones and garbage trucks in the morning) don't stay here. But if you want a wonderful SF vacation spot near the cable cars, Union Square, Foley's Irish Pub, and Kuletos for dinners, give this place a try. The service was superb, the rooms are renovated to include a killer shower, and all the electronic amenities you need are provided in the room including an IPOD docking station and wireless internet. We would definitely return.

title: “Never again”
text: A real rip off. We paid 370.00, I guess because it was St pats weekend, but it was no better than a days inn room. I had stayed there before because the location is great, but for 190.00 you can handle the small, older rooms, not that well kept. We had a leak in the celing in the bathroom, which got progressively worse by the time we checked out. This stay really ruined it for me. I will never stay in another Marriot. The staff was friendly while we were there, but when I called to complain after we had left, I was treated with sarcasm on the phone the first time. I finally reached someone who cared and I wound up getting one free night next time I am in san diego. As if I will ever return to that hotel. There are many others which are newer and better in that same area. I would suggest the hyatt or embassy suites.

title: “Tiny or Cozy?”
text:
Everything is tiny. Tiny lobby, tiny rooms and even on a seemingly tiny street. Yet the decor and the staff manged to turn this all into a plus. Decor had a very hip feel to it yet was very comfortable and soothing. Staff was incredible and the complimentary wine hour and cont'l bkst added to the welcoming atmosphere. 
Really enjoyed the atmosphere in the Ruby Room and the menu and food was great. Even though it comes across as "light fare", the quality, service and portion size made us turn it into dinner.
Only drawback would be some tourists may be put off by its unusual location. The neigborhood is a bit gritty but you're within walking distance to Fanueil Hall, Fleet Ctr events and the North end.
Have also stayed at its sister Hotel - the Marlowe and found it equally as enjoyable.

title: “Great value for the price...”
text:
I only travel to New york on business once a year or so, and when I do I need to be on somewhat of a room rate budget. I asked a reliable business friend where he was staying for the conference he was also attending, and he recommended the Park central, which was only two blocks from where I needed to be for two days.
I booked a non-refundable King for about $300 about a month in advance. By middle-of-the-road Manhattan standards, this hotel delivered. Check-in was seamless (except for one little glitch I'll mention in a minute), service was friendly (front desk, lobby coffee bar, bellman), and the room was reasonably large, clean and with enough amenities to feel I got my money's worth. My wife was with me and she agreed that there was plenty of value and comfort in this hotel experience. Located on 7th at 55th, the hotel is central to everything and everywhere in Midtown.
The only little issue was a call I received from the front desk at 10pm the night after I checked out. Apparently they failed to secure my credit card number when I checked in and needed to get the card number again so that they could close out the folio. It wasn't any sort of scam, but I insisted when I called them back the next day that they needed to improve their front desk manners in that no guest should be called on a personal cell phone after check out at 10pm at night. That was a fluke; I still recommend this hotel.

title: “great location, very poor hotel”
text: perfect location in NY, but the hotel in itself is very poor. Dated decor, unfriendly personnel, useless and grumpy concierge, VERY noisy air con, broken telly, no room service, broken down lift, the list goes on. Again, the location is perfect,but I would not recommend this hotel.

title: “Perfect Stay - Our Dog Loved It Too!”
text:
As the proud parents of a fuzzy four-legged canine "son", we are constantly looking for good dog-friendly hotel options while on road trips from Toronto. The Onyx did not disappoint!
We love a good 8-10 hour road trip but few hotels welcome dogs. A handful of chains do, but don't truly make for a dog-friendly experience. In such establishments, owners need to be present in the room with the dogs or have to crate them while out for dinner. Anyone reading this who has a dog will know that crating a dog for a couple of hours isn't ideal in an "outside of the home" environment.
ALONG COMES KIMPTON! YAY!
We learned about Kimpton's dog-friendly services online and researched them here on TripAdvisor and are so glad we did! Our experience at the hotel was amazing!
We checked in with our dog and were welcomed with open arms. Based on Kimpton's email blitzes and website blurbs about dogs, I almost expected staff to make a bigger deal out of how cute our pooch was, but since there were apparently several other dogs in residence, ours was just another guest. Fair enough. LOL! 
The nice part of staying at a Kimpton hotel with a dog is that you're put on a floor with other dog owners and you can leave your dog in the room - uncrated - to go out for dinner/shop/etc. On top of that, if you plan on being out for more than a couple of hours, you can hire staff for a very fair rate to stay in the room/entertain Fido/walk the dog/Etc. 
Guests without dogs: Have no fear! As mentioned, the rooms for dog owners are confined to specific blocks/levels. Plus, they only allow a certain number of dogs on site per night.
On to the room! We loved the decor and leopard robes. :) The room was not especially spacious for the price but it was chic and comfortable. We had plenty of space for our two suitcases and our dog bed so all was fine. I have paid more for less at other places. The room had all of the right amenities compactly tucked into space saving shelving. Again, the room's design was lots of fun and felt cozy and comfortable.
The wine "happy hour" in the lobby was a nice perk. The lobby itself was quite small so we felt a little crowded. It wasn't like we could kick back and sip on a leisurely glass of vino. But it was fun anyway. I mean, really, there should be no complaining about free wine! :) The wine reception is a very smart concept because it gives Kimpton staff the opportunity to answer a bunch of guests' questions all at once. It probably takes pressure off the front desk/concierge later in the evening as they won't have to deal with constant calls asking about restaurant recommendations, directions, etc. As a guest, it's simply refreshing to speak with staff in person rather than on the phone. It felt more personal.
Valet parking was efficient and the usual pricing applied. (I can't remember what we paid but it was at par with any US/Canadian metropolitan city.)
The location makes for an excellent base exploring the city and is especially close to the Boston Garden, Quincy Market and North End. We started our evening off with some authentic clam chowder at a pub in the market followed by the best pizza I've ever had at the famous Regina Pizzeria in the North End. After a wee walk we were able to justify indulging in the outstanding dessert cannoli from Modern Pasty. We bought extra cannoli to enjoy on our drive the next day, but our dog found them when we weren't looking and gobbled them up! Lucky dog! LOL! Needless to say, you will find much to do in the area and the subway is nearby as well. You really won't need to drive in Beantown. Nor would you want to. I've driven all over North America but always get confused with all of the little one way streets in Boston! :) 
The only downfall was that we only had time on this particular trip to stay just one night! We would have loved to stay longer! We will definitely be back. I have always liked Boston and can't wait to return to The Onyx with our pooch and explore the city again. I need more time so I can go shopping and enjoy more of the amazing restaurants that have popped up over the past few years. I looked at their website today (November 12, 2011 and it looks like they have some good specials on 3 night stays in January! The travel bug is biting! Don't hesitate to book this deal if you can! Boston is beautiful in the winter!)
Thank you Onyx for a wonderful stay!

title: “It,s OK for the price.”
text: Ended up here during Pride Weekend with a last minute reservation. The room was clean and not unpleasant. Oddly the bath was nearly larger than the room. The service was not rude or pleasant, just there. Had no trouble but many others were very dissatisfied. If you want to be in the center of the city, the location is wonderful.

title: “poor customer service”
text: One of the reasons I wanted to stay in this hotel was because it advertised a fridge in the room. Our refrigerator was broken. I asked FOUR times for it to be fixed and it never was. Wouldn't go back.

title: “Perfect Uptown Hotel”
text:
Uptown Charlotte is the city center. Buzzing with high rises, businesses, restaurants and a vibrant social scene, Charlotte is getting the attention of some pretty influential party planners. The 2012 Democratic National Convention confirmed and headed to Charlotte. The CIAA Basketball Tournament has made Charlotte home for quite a few years. And when you have a NFL stadium (Charlotte Panthers) sitting right there in the middle of the city, looks like Charlotte has the secret sauce in quickly becoming a southern city powerhouse.
Now that you have a few good reasons to visit Charlotte, North Carolina, top it off with a great hotel. Make your reservations at the Westin Charlotte. This Starwood property is centrally located to everything and place for your ideal Charlotte experience.
The guestrooms are spacious and the beds are divine. One of my favorite features are the huge windows that seem to outline room. I am one of those travelers who open the curtains as soon as I check-in. I need to see where I am...scope out the view. And the Westin Charlotte does not disappoint. A large window accessorizes the bed's headboard and makes it easy to watch that quiet sunset; oh so city chic!!
Before you checkout, start at least one morning with an amazing breakfast, at the Westin's Ember Grill. Breakfast, by far, is my favorite meal of the day and I do not believe in rushing through a well laid out buffet. Sit down, slowly sip your coffee and/or juice and savor each bite. The grill staff will take great care of you.

title: “"Great Hotel, Excellent Services"”
text: I came in from Connecticut to the Hilton Hotel on July 22, 2011. The Young lady at the front desk was very proffesional and polite and exceptionally helpful. The room service was excellent, the valets and bellman was very helpful and courteous. I had my meal at the dining room and the staff there was veryprofessional. Our overall experience was wonderful. Keep up the good job and continue doing what you do best. My Husband and i had no complaints it was a very great experience.

title: “Love D.C.! The Courtyard is another story.”
text:
If you look at my other reviews, you will find that I am a pretty satisfied traveller and usually give really good reviews so that shows what I thought about this hotel. 
First of all the good:
1) Location is excellent. An easy walk to the Chinatown metro station. There are lots of things to do in the general vicinity of the hotel. Ford's theater is about a block or two away. 
2) The bar/restaurant downstairs has pretty good food and is the restaurant serving the room service. All in all, the room service was excellent however a little pricey. 
And now the bad:
1) The hotel is located directly across the street from a place called the UltraBar. The a) ultrabar has incredibly loud music, b) our hotel had incredibly thin walls, or c) a combination of the two. All in all, the music was very loud even in our room and made it moderately difficult to sleep at night. As a side note, I am 29 years old, and quite enjoy bars and clubs so this is not an old man rant. Its just that after an incredibly long day of site seeing I do not like being kept up by a club blasting bass all night long. I can only imagine that for most people, this would be an incredibly annoying distraction to an otherwise peaceful trip to D.C.
2) The hotel staff was just not really all that helpful or inviting. 
3) The pillows are absolutely awful. I'm not sure if you can find a cheaper pillow somewhere, but I challenge you to try.
4) The room itself was incredibly tiny, with what felt like furniture just shoved into whatever corner and opening could be found. Making it quite cramped and not all that useful. Do I really need a chair and ottoman next to my tv, facing the opposite wall, crammed in a corner? Who finds that useful and comfortable? 
In summary, the only thing I liked about this hotel was the location.

title: “Fantastic Hotel, bad location for tourists”
text:
The Marriott is a fantastic hotel with great amenities.
It is clean friendly and very accommodating. The only 
problem is the location. This hotel is ideal for business 
travellers, but for tourists there is very little you can do in
Downtown LA. The underground and taxis are very convenient,
but we would suggest stay North Hollywood if your on holiday
otherwise you will spend a great deal of time and money in
cabs or on the tube.
This is definately the best Marriott we have stayed in in 
any country. Thanks

title: “Pleasant and spacious with friendly staff”
text: I recently stayed at the Hyatt Summerfield for two nights while attending a friend's wedding. I was pleased with this hotel, the studio suite I reserved was large and easily fit myself and three other travelers with room to move around. The room was very clean. The kitchen had everything we needed and we were pleased that the room included an extra vanity area with sink and electrical sockets (perfect for a group of women!). Lots of closet space, extra storage areas, and comfortable beds were also appreciated. We also had a large tv and a dvd player. The color scheme in the room and the rest of the hotel was very nice and the resulting atmosphere was relaxing. The breakfast was good each morning with plenty of selections, and the other travelers were pleasant (I had heard some other extended stay style places in Austin had questionable characters living in the hotel - some other guests experienced that at their hotels but it was definately not the case here). Parking was convenient and the buildings were accessible through a few entrances which made getting in and out easy. Friendly staff rounded out the whole experience. I will stay here again.

title: “Quietly elegant”
text:
We were worried about this hotel being overly trendy. We should not have worried. The staff were young, friendly and efficient. Any noise on Saturday night did not permeate our 2nd floor room.
We appreciated the ice machine and coffee-making facilities on each floor, the quality toiletries and the efficiency of the room cleaning. Plus the very comfortable bed.
We only ate in the hotel once. The food was fresh but a little on the expensive side.
The hotel is very close to subway stations so even as novice NYC subway users we managed the transfer from JFK by public transport very easily and used the subway a lot during our stay.
Soho restaurants are a short walk away.
Square diner is 5 mins away and great for breakfast.

title: “Classic - Pure DC”
text: We hosted a business meeting here. Fantastic meeting room, and great service from the staff, they were flexible and fast with last minute changes. The hotel oozes history and elegance. My room was much larger than expected for such an old hotel, especially the bathroom. The location is prime for anyone wanting to explore the city. Expect to pay a lot for food and drink.

title: “Ah-mazing desert oasis!”
text: My family recently stayed in Villas but they provide access to the JW's pool and resturants. The Pool area was amazing. Resembled a desert oasis. The hotel was gorgeous and everything was set up so nicely. The waitresses were very attentive and kept coming around to bring more drinks or food. Pitchers of free water were everywhere which is much needed in 100+ degree weather! Tons of room and chairs so we never felt crammed next to anyone. Phoenix was a pleasant surprise!

title: “Why did I do this?”
text:
I read the reviews and gambled-- I should have trusted the reviews. I am a Hilton Diamond member that means I spend about 40 stays at Hilton each year.
Upon check in, I was not welcomed as a diamond member and did not receive a room upgrade. I was given passes for breakfast but based on reviews here, I wasn't paying 8.95 for each child and 13.00 for each other adult.
Pros: Hotel is near other hotels such as motel 6, comfort inn, ramada inn. They had a fire pit and small seating outside. Hotel is located 10 mins from zoo.
Cons: 16.00 charge per night for parking. The parking garage is very narrow-here's a tip-drive to rear of garage and park.
The onsite food pantry had beer, cokes, ice cream, juices, wine, but no milk. We had to buy that for 3.00 per glass in the restaurant. Rip off. We found a target down the street for the next night. The pool was heated but small.

title: “Good Hotel”
text:
Stayed in hotel for 5 nights in February. Check in was good, quick and the staff were friendly and helpful. 
Other reviews suggested breakfast was busy and you had to be up early. As we were site seeing most days we were down for breakfast at 8am and never had to wait for a table. The breakfast area was a bit small but a good selection was available. 
Our room had plenty of room and was bigger then expected. The staff were all friendly and always acknowledged you!
The location of the hotel was very good on 39th St, close to Times Square, Broadway, Maddison Square Garden and the subway but not too close to make the hotel noisy.
We got a car from the hotel to Newark Airport, at a cost of $82 including tolls and tip, we didnt think this was too bad considering it cost $80 for taxi from Newark to the hotel.

title: “We had stepped into a time machine”
text:
Very basic accomodation - no refigerator in rooms only a small icebucket.
In house meal greasy and unattractive.
Low cost in comparison to other Sil Valley hotels.
Light rail at doorstep and so we could avoid expensive taxis to town.
We dined at Denny's - two blocks North or across the road - pizza, mexican & Starbucks.
Apparently newspapers are only delivered for some guests - don't bother asking at the desk!

title: “Fantastic Stay at the Crown Plaza Beverly Hills”
text:
I have recently returned from a holiday in the United States and chose to stay at the Crown Plaza Hotel in Beverly Hills for an initial period of five nights from the 23rd to 28th September 2007.
Due to some accommodation problems in New York I had to leave a few days earlier than I anticipated. I contacted the Crown Plaza Hotel and arranged two nights accommodation for the 16th & 17th September so that I had somewhere to stay once I arrived in Los Angeles. It also gave me time to try and organize for the five nights that I booked to be moved forward, subject to availability.
From the moment I arrived at the hotel I was impressed with the level of service. I arrived at approximately 11pm on the 16th September, 2007 after flying from New York to Los Angeles. I had not been able to access the internet at all while I was in New York (as I use broadband not wireless internet services) and realized when I got to my room that it looked as though only wireless internet was offered. 
I made a general enquiry with one of the staff, who organized to send someone up to my room within 5 minutes. I was advised that the hotel could still accommodate broadband Internet access and would just need to hook up a cable. Given how late it was I advised the gentleman that I was happy enough to wait until the next morning to get things sorted out. To my surprise he offered again to connect up the cabling, which only took another few minutes, stating that after arriving late that I might like to sleep in the next morning and the internet would be ready to access whenever I needed it the next day. I was so grateful for this level of service, particularly late at night.
I then noticed the Sleep Advantage pack on the bed … after unpacking a few things I had a shower … put the cd on … a few drops of lavender on my pillow and got into what can only be described as the most comfortable bed that I have slept in while staying in a hotel. I quite honestly thought I was in heaven. What a fantastic idea, especially for people either arriving at the hotel late and/or after a long flight. 
Despite a lot of problems being caused through the company that I originally booked my accomodation through, I did manage to stay the 5 additonal nights, mostly due to efforts of two of the Managers at the Hotel, Mr Cruz and Mr Page. I cannot express my gratitude enough to them for their professionalism and genuine desire to ensure that I was able to stay the five nights that I had paid for and be able to continue my stay at the hotel.
The level of service offered by the staff at the Crown Plaza Hotel continued to impress me the entire seven nights of my stay. All the staff were friendly, professional and couldn’t do enough to ensure that my stay at the hotel was the best that could possibly be offered.
I would not hesitate to stay at the Crown Plaza Hotel again ... I really had a fantastic stay here!

title: “Decent Enough....”
text: The amenities were not what I expected for the ratings and price of the room, but it was definitely more than sufficient. The location sort of made up for it. Very close to shopping and the riverwalk.

title: “On a scale of 1-10 this hotel and staff is 100.”
text: A repeat stay can often be disappointing in a hotel - not with the Park Hyatt. Every single detail is thought out to please the guest. It is absolutely the BEST example of running an excellent hotel - worth every penny spent.

title: “Priceline room not so great”
text:
On a Priceline stay, we got the dreaded double-bedded room. The bed is not uncomfortable, but it is very noisy in the roms that face Lexington Avenue, even up on the 13th floor
Our bags took over one hour to get delivered from the lobby to our room, and we had to call down for severaql items that the housekeeper had forgotten to include in our room (washcloths, coffee cups).
I'll hope for other properties in this Priceline zone in future.

title: “Average Hotel; Great Staff”
text:
Recent 2-night stay with family. Staff does a great job with a dated property. Rooms were decent size; comfortable; functional. Great shower pressure. Institutional feel throughout -- could be the color scheme or the lighting, but everything felt odl and tired. Staff, however, was superb, especially in the restaurant where everyone was eager to offer great service. Indoor pool is a nice plus (kids enjoyed it); when it got too warm in the pool area, the staff was very repsonsive. Computer availability (free) in the lobby was a nice convenience. Plenty of free parking.
TGI Friday's across the parking lot is atrocious. Just skip it. Too many better options nearby.

title: “Great!”
text:
Would highly recommend this hotel. The location outstanding as it is in walking distance to shopping and attractions. Just blocks to Pike Market.
The room was large, extremely clean, and well appointed.

title: “Great location, great price”
text:
Our 3-night stay was surprisingly nice--I thought Union Square would be overpriced and touristy-lame. As retired military we joined the club to get a price break and reciprocity for other military hotels--the hotel staff tells you the break-even point for yr stay. Our 2-double bed room was not especially roomy but we were able to fit in a cot for our 3rd child at no charge. Housekeeping was quite cheery about our requests for extra towels, etc., and the room was tidied nicely. The breakfast buffet was everything other reviewers have mentioned, and a super way to start the day. The kids discovered the delights of strawberry cheese blintzes one morning.
 The room didn't seem tired, though it was a bit dusty. I thought the bathroom was fine. Other good things: the large soap/shampoo/condit. dispensers in the shower, good thermostat control, free wi-fi in room, nice views, comfy reading chair, convenient location, 6am coffee & scones in business center. We walked 5 blocks to Market & Powell where we found the SF visitor center (very helpful), and SF Shopping Centre (big mall w/ pretty good food court). It's an easy place to catch the cable car, BART & Muni (bus) around town. We took the Muni to Golden Gate park very easily (the CA Academy of Science rocked!). 
 I can't think of a reason NOT to stay at the hotel again. Beautiful, historic, convenient, great price, and a friendly staff. When we checked in I mentioned that our hospitality card only noted 4 and I would need to purchase a buffet ticket for my 3rd child. She waved that off, changed the ticket to 2 adults and 3 kids, and off we went to our room. So great.
p.s. There's a dress code for dinner, not unreasonable. Street noise was a problem for the light sleepers.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: I had a wonderful suite that separated into two rooms with TWO bathrooms. The location was in the heart of the Union Square dist. The staff was extremely helpful and always cheerful. I felt like they truly cared about my comforts. I will definitely stay here again.

title: “Good location in San Francisco for sightseeing”
text:
Good basic hotel in perfect sightseeing location in San Francisco. Spent 7 days there in a standard, but spacious double room on the front looking towards the Hyatt Hotel. Used the hopon-hopoff city sightseeing buses recommended by the Virgin rep (one block away and around the corner) so handy for doing the many sights of San Francisco. Highlights of our trip were definitely the night tour of Alcatraz (book online in advance with the official site for the inside tour otherwise you will just sail around it), walking the Golden Gate Bridge, exploring Golden Gate Park, lunching in Scomas in Sausalito outside in the sun (where Otis Redding apparently wrote 'Sitting on the Dock of the Bay' on a houseboat), exploring the tall ship/boats/submarine at Fishermans's Wharf, riding the cable cars and seeing crooked Lombard Street, exploring Chinatown, eating Clam Chowder in the Blue Mermaid, drinks in Jacks Bar, Irish coffee in Buena Vista and dining in the many restaurants in Little Italy - about 15 mins walk up Columbus. For us, we preferred to dine in Little Italy as we found the Wharf too big, brash, touristy and tacky (with a sprinkling of homeless and drunks wandering around) restaurant-wise it's probably great with kids, but as we were a couple we preferred the smaller more intimate restaurants up on Columbus. However, we did eat dinner in Knuckles (The Hyatt's restaurant opposite) and Pompei's Grotto on the Wharf (where we had the cheapest bottle of house wine in all the restaurants we visited) when we were tired and didn't want to walk far after sightseeing. We did find house wine very expensive with our meals, much more expensive than at home, and don't really understand why when all the Californian vineyards are only an hour or so away up the coast. Another night, when we were too tired, we just got a take-away pizza (recommended by reception) and a bottle of wine from the local supermarket and stayed in our spacious and comfortable room watching TV. 
The Holiday Inn Express itself was busy with friendly helpful reception staff but no bar or restaurant in-house. The breakfasts, just off the lobby, were hectic and plentiful, but not the healthiest - mainly consisting of burgers, burnt bacon, rubbery eggs, bread, pancakes, scones, very sweet pastries, tea, coffee, juice and some cereals including one rainbow coloured cereal (dread to think how many colourings and sugar in that one!!). The only healthy thing on the buffet was a banana and even the yoghurts were like the little kiddie ones once again full of colouring and sugar. Needlesstosay, I wasn't overly impressed with breakfast and even worse it's all on paper plates with plastic, knives and forks. But then, you could argue that breakfast was included in the room rate so it was cheaper than eating out every morning. 
There are two internet terminals, to the right as you come into reception, which were handy if they weren't busy and also useful for printing out info and our boarding passes. 
Overall, we were glad we booked the Holiday Inn Express and on our last day we enjoyed sitting by the pool of its sister hotel, the Holiday Inn, nextdoor so we could savour a little bit of Californian sunshine even in November. A nice suntrap, but disappointing you couldn't order a drink or food by the pool during the day (maybe it's different in the summer).

title: “Excellent hotel near Inner Harbour”
text: We stayed here a few months ago in the King Premier room and everything was absolutely fantastic. The hotel has a terrific architectual design as it used to be an old railraod building (much more exciting than it sounds). There are these gorgeous marble stairways which provide a terrific picture op in the lobby area. The staff was wonderful and of typical Kimpton quality. We didn't get a chance to dine at the restaurant but the Kimpton Wine Hour was great, albeit crowded. Our room was very spacious and had a two person soaking tub which made the stay more memorable. Location wise, the hotel is essentially right between the Mt. Vernon area and the Inner Harbour so you can't go wrong either way. We got a little confused with some of the service elevators as they're right next to the regular ones so we would've appreaciated better signage but this was pretty minor. Love to return again and would recommend to anyone visiting Baltimore.

title: “GREAT SPOT ESP FOR SPORTS FANS!”
text: this place is great. the staff is really nice, the rooms are clean and newer, they all have a sink and refridgerator. the bathroom is huge, and if you're in town for a game this hotel is directly across the street from both stadiums (for seahawks and mariners games). it will literaly take you 30 seconds to walk to the gate of the stadium!

title: “Good Location & Nice Room”
text: We booked with a group and the rate was high but the hotel had great beds and sheets. It was also a block or two from Little Toyko and withing walking distance to other sites. Comfortable stay with refrigerator and desk in room. Stayed a week and staff was helpful. The hotel is lacking a pool but the Japanese garden is very pretty. Also, it was undergoing renovations into a Doubletree at the end of our stay which created quite a bit of noise.

title: “Best Motel Stay Ever”
text: This motel 6 is just wonderful. It is new, very clean and the appointments in the room go way beyond what I would have expected in a motel. Many hotels I have stayed in are not as roomy and as well appointed. The room even has a ceiling fan and a selection of pillows for sleeping. Breakfast buffet in the morning was great and had just about anything anyone would have wanted for breakfast. Owners and employees are very nice. Plan to stay there whenever I go back to Austin, TX regardless of where I have business in the city. The traffic to get there is more than worth the wonderful stay..

title: “Nice Place if You Are Going to a Concert at Cricket Wireless”
text:
My husband made the reservation for this hotel and as I drove to this place I grew concerned as it is practically on the border with Mexico. In addition, it was hard to find as it is in the back of an industrial area. However, once I settled in, I relaxed and found it to be a nice hotel. The service was good, the room was clean and spacious and the beds were comfortable. That was perfect for one night's sleep after a concert. 
It was very convenient to Cricket Wireless where we were going to the concert. The major downside was the lack of good food within walking distance. We ended up at Wendy's for dinner because that was the only option we could find. 
I recommend this hotel if you are going to a concert or need to be in that specific area. Otherwise, it is off the beaten path!

title: “Would stay again”
text:
The hotel was farther from attractions at Union Square but it's close to lots of restaurants and waling distance from the cable cars.
We walked some of the way but if we had to do it over, we would ahve booked something a little closer. 
The service at the hotel was very good, they catered to everything we needed. There was no airconditioning! We didn't really need it because it was the spring but , if you needed it, you wouldn't be able to stay here. Overall the beds were okay, and the room was a good size for Frisco. There was a very busy wine tasting every evening and the everything worked well. We had a hard time getting a hold of the front desk sometimes though.

title: “Enjoyment & Comfort”
text: The Chancellor is a wonderful place to stay. We enjoy the rooms and the location of the hotel. We have been coming here for ten years.

title: “First rate location...”
text:
Sometimes a hotel can ruin the first impression of a newly-visited city, especially after a long Transatlantic flight. Well, the Chancellor didn't. 
A comfortable hotel, excellent location and helpful staff created a good feel immediately and it formed the bedrock of a great first time visit to San Francisco. 
Hotels in downtown San Francisco can be very pricey but, with the breakfast and parking package (we rented a car), the Chancellor was very good value. (You must have a car to experience driving down Lombard Street! )
Unless you arrive very early in the day, suggest you buy a bus/trolley ticket on the day of arrival and use it the following day. This ticket is not valid for 24 hours from the time of activation - it is valid for a calendar day only. But it is good value for money and great for the essential trolley (and old-fashioned trams) rides.

title: “excellent”
text: Was booked at the Red Lion Hotel for a conference after the original hotel I had reserved had construction delays. Stayed for two nights, and had a spacious corner room on the tenth floor with two queen beds and a wet bar area with refrigerator. Free wireless internet access in the room and the hotel, which worked fine. Room was clean, good beds, no HBO but an above average cable channel selection. Wasn't bothered by noise from other rooms (I think the noise problem is worse if you have a door to an adjoining room). Parking $25 a night, but with in/out privileges--occasionally crowded and needing valet assistance. Staff was friendly. Great location an easy walk to PIke Place Market, two blocks from the convention center. Would stay there again.

title: “Good Boutique Hotel in Upper West Side”
text: Spent three nights at OTA just after Thanksgiving. Great location - near subway, Central Park, and all that Upper West Side has to offer. Property is well kept, clean, and beds very comfortable. Prices are reasonable for NYC though rooms are pretty small - you get a bed, a dresser, a chair (that had to be used for luggage storage since the room was so small), and a good sized bathroom. Not very quiet as building construction was going on across the street and that may last for some time. Staff friendly enough. No bar or restaurant on property, though you have many options all around the hotel.

title: “Wellington Was Beyond Expecations”
text: We stayed at the Wellington from July 2-6. I was a bit nervous given all of the negative reviews of the hotel, but it exceeded my expecations. The hotel is in a great location and a easy walk to Central Park, the theaters, shopping and Times Square. The room was small, but clean and quiet. We had a corner room with a view of Times Square. Given the price and location of the Wellington, it would be hard to find a better deal. We would definitely stay at the Wellington again.

title: “Wow!!!”
text: I have stayed in hotels all over the world and this is by far the most original, most hip hotel I have seen. Every corner of the public area is captivating, like walking through a modern art museum.

title: “A wonderful experience”
text: We loved this hotel. We are Omni members and enjoyed all the treats like coffee delivered in the morning (and it's GOOD coffee) and cookies for the kids. The apple cider and gingerbread men in the foyer were a lovely touch. The reception and valet parking staff were friendly and efficient. We had the kids fantasy suite and our room adjoined theirs - highly recommend this, our kids loved it and so did we.

title: “Quality rooms (aside from paper thin walls) but many glaring problems”
text: The hotel overall was ok but we struck quite a few problems, firstly we were surprised when we arrived that the porter did not offer to take our bags to our room, he just dumped them at the elevator, on the second night I was quite ill after eating seafood at the hotel and also that night I found out the walls are very thin and I could hear the guest next door snoring most of the night. The quality of the furnishings in the room is quite good and the staff are generally friendly, I would rate the hotel as just average overall.

title: “Great for Families, central location to metro”
text: This was the 3rd time we have stayed here in 3 years. 2X while we looked at local colleges. On our first night as we came back from dinner I requested extra towels at the front desk, there were 5 of us, the towels were in the room before we even got upstairs. My daughters have very long hair which gets everywhere when they brush it, each day the bathroom and rooms were spotless, they even left extra soap and shampoo once they knew there were 5 of us in the room. Staff always said Good Morning & Good Evening. The breakfast is one of the reasons we stayed here each time. Each person was able to find something to eat each day, whether it was the pancakes, omlettes, waffles, bagels or oatmeal we never went hungry. There is plenty of other stuff to eat too! Garage is spotless and you can fit a minivan in the space. You need a code to get in and out of the garage so we knew our car was safe. Use the metro instead of driving around the city. Metro is very easy and fast and Dupont Circle is only 4-5 blocks from the hotel. There are many restaurants in Dupont Circle so we ate there 2 nights after our travels around the city. If you are not from a metropolitan area like New York, Boston, Chicago be prepared for the food prices all over even pizza places. Dinner for the 5 of us at nice restaurants averaged $110 including tip, no alcohol, only sodas. Good prices since we are from the NY Metro area where dinner for the 5 of us averages $150 but others have found the DC prices high.

title: “Challenged Layout”
text:
The property is located near downtown Austin and located on Congress avenue. Still a cab ride to sixth street. The property is not layed out very well. Anytime you need to go to the parking garage you have walk around the building and take the elevator up to your car. 
The rooms have been remodeled and look very well. The hotel did run out of towels. The hotel staff is great and the "free" shuttle was very fast and took us where we needed to go.

title: “Nice, but be aware.”
text:
Be aware that Houston City does not allow roller beds inside 2 bed rooms. We didn´t know that, but we were told at the reception that one bed would be sent to the room. Two hours later the bed hadn´t come yet (11pm be the time). After 2 calls to reception, we first learned about this Fire Marshall regulation. So, to solve the problem, they sent us an inflatable mattress. My point is, if we had been told about this regulation before, we might have paid for 2 rooms, or look for another alternative. The WiFi is simply terrible also. If you want high speed, you will be forced to pay an extra amount, which I consider a Stone Age practice. Charging extra for WiFi is like charging extra for tap water, simple as that. 
Great breakfast in the second floor (included), and check out the rooftop pool and spa; really nice. Also, be aware that parking is valet only, and costs about $28 per day.

title: “Best value in San Diego Area.”
text: The rooms are not luxurious but they are clean and somewhat spacious. We even had a small refridgerator, which was very helpful for our 4 night stay. The location is awesome--it is close to beaches, Seaworld, downtown, old town, etc. (10-15 minute drive). The price was definitely lower than the majority of San Diego hotels. There is a Denny's about 100 yards across the street & plenty of other places to eat close by.

title: “Horrible place to stay”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for one night on Dec 25. The hotel was running some Christmas buffet for non-guests that day so all the guest parking spots were taken and we had to park quite a distance away and lug three suitcases through the rain. 
Our first room seemed ok. That is until we flushed the toilet. Next thing we see is water flooding the entire bathroom, seeping out into the room and under the adjoining room door and into the next room. By the time maintenance came, the entire room and part of the hallway was covered in water. We got a new room on another floor, and the toilet broke again. We couldn't flush for the entire trip. Horrible plumbing in this hotel. 
Hot water takes quite some time to come in and the pool area is not stocked with towels. I guess you have to bring bath towels from your room in order to go swimming. The pool is nice, but we didn't even get to enjoy it. The staff is friendly, but the hotel has an out of date feel. Very old fashioned.
Bottom line: if you don't flush the toilet and don't require hot water or towels by the pool, this is the place for you.

title: “Not quite five stars”
text: A beautiful hotel in a great location, but the rooms do not have minibars. Seriously, a top notch hotel needs a minibar in the room. Four Seasons, minibar? check. Intercontinental? Check. Even the hideous Hyatt in the theater district? Yep, has a minibar. Hotels without minibars thus include: the Red Roof Inn in Fenway; the Howard Johnson's downtown; and, at least according to websites, several local Holiday Inns along the 128 corridor. Oh, and, apparently, the Boston Harbor Hotel.

title: “Nice hotel near the harbor”
text:
I stayed with my daughter for two nights over the July 4 holiday. We were close by the harbor area, aquarium and Independence Day fireworks display. The hotel is not right on the harbor, but is an easy block walk to the central part. There is a small upscale shopping gallery attached to it.
I had originally selected a king bed non harbor view, which was available at a good price. When I went to lock up my valuables in the in room safe (there were some comments on this site about security problems), the safe wouldn't lock. They immediately sent up a security officer, who performed diagnostics but could not get it to work. He called up someone from engineering, but the only solution was to either swap safes from another room or have me move. To their credit, they worked with the front desk to try to get me an upgrade for my trouble. I wound up getting two queen beds with a (very) partial harbor view and a working safe for the same price.
The room was nice, with a small refrigerator, comfy beds, decent sized bathroom and very clean. The AC was able to cool the room properly despite the 100 deg F. heat wave. There was a nice pillow selection, although the foam pillow had an odd shape that caused a neck ache the following morning. Some of the extras, like the coffee machine, were in odd places in the backs of cabinets - I actually had to ask where the ice bucket was after 10 minutes of looking, but it was there.
The staff was mostly helpful and accomodating. We did not eat in the hotel or use the internet access (breakfast and internet are extra, but I think that is a Marriot policy for this grade of hotel). The only time there was an issue with elevator service was during the very crowded period of July 4 afternoon and evening.
We did use the indoor pool, which was a bit cooler than expected but otherwise fine. I would not hesitate to stay here again.

title: “Absolutely wonderful...looking forward to a return visit.”
text:
My wife and I stayed one night at the Hotel Giraffe on a last minute little romantic getaway and we were very pleased and impressed.
We had made reservations, but arrived 6 hours before check-in at 9AM and the staff was very accomodating in arranging a room for us right away. Upon departure, we need a couple of extra hours given our late flight and again they were very accomodating.
The rooms themselves are very comfortable, beautifully decorated with a clear impression that all guest amenities and room details were throughly planned out - from the quality of hotel towels to the various lighting options with the well placed switches for total convenience to the real plant in our room giving it a nice little touch of home. Our room also had a really lovely balcony and although we did not use it, it gave the room a very delightful touch.
In the mornings the hotel offers a complinentary breakfast of pastries, fruit, hard boiled eggs, coffee, tea, and juice - definetly nothing elaborated, but perfect for starting your day in New York, all enjoyed in the very comfortable hotel lobby. In the evenings there is a complimentary wine and cheese that served as the perfect break for us after a day on the town before we went up to our rooms to rest for our night on the town.
As for location, it was perfect for us as we explored both uptown and downtown and being right in the middle had great access to everything - especially with a subway station right across the street (which would recommend any visitor to embrace and use - it defintely is the best and most efficient way to get around, especially with the all you can ride $7 a day 'fun pass'.
Would definetly go back to the Hotel Giraffe - staff was very nice, room was very comfortable, and the location gave us access to all of Manhatten in a convenient manner. And as for New York hotels are concerned, felt the total experience we got was good value relative to what we would pay at a compriable hotel.

title: “Nice hotel but with some noise problem.”
text: This hotel was nice. It didn't wow me, but functional. The front desk was well managed with helpful staff. Seemed clean in all areas. Priced at $100 a night was a little more than I thought it was worth. My room location probably caused the lower rating. 1st floor as requested, but it was located next to a side exit. The side door would slam. I felt as if someone was slaming my room door. It was annoying!

title: “great for us”
text: we needed a place to stay one night before a cruise....we wanted near the airport as we were travelling with 3 young children (3.5 yrs and below).....their van got us at the airport and all our bags (11 of us travelling together)....rooms were huge....everything was very nice....quiet for by the airport....we can't speak for the neighborhood as we didn't leave the property (van-ned the next a.m. to cruise pier)....my only criticism was restaurant was way expensive....if your travelling with kids like we were or on a budget, the restaurant was mucho bucks...not family friendly at all (seemed like good food, but....)

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
Good things:
Perfect Location. Very trendy and modern rooms with microwave and refrigerator. Free internet was nice because we constantly were looking things up about NYC (restaurants, sights, etc) before we went out for the day or the night. The TV was really nice. Very close to a subway stop which makes things so much easier. Also surrounded by good restaurants and shopping.
Bad things: The room we had was on the 26th floor and the elevator was such a pain to wait for. The service was not that spectacular. I found the women we checked in with was not very professional. The rooms are small, and both my boyfriend and I did not get the best sleep. Bed was not as comfortable as some other Hilton hotel's I have stayed in.

title: “Enjoyed our stay there”
text:
Stayed here in the first week of Dec 05 for four nights. Must agree both with my colleague from Ireland and with the reviewer from LA on both counts of shopping and slight problems. More so than using the seperate lifts I thought the stairs on the entrance were a problem with heavy luggage caring them down them. However to be fair also to the hotel, I think in hindsight our cab driver should have pulled around to the side entrance within the car park which would have made things a bit easier. We did have a room on the 15th floor so that does afford great views of Boston. Didnt think there was anything particularly wrong with the neighbourhood more than the usual things you see late at night, though a bit more street lighting would make one feel more secure.
The hotel staff were very helpful as was our housekeeping. We didnt spend much time in our room as the Macys and Filenes were way too near for my girlfriend not to get tempted to visit, some days several times. The pool and fitness centre were great too and the hotel always seemed to be buzzing, in the evening at least, with people who had been attending conferences there. That did add to the atmosphere a little
All in all I would stay there again, it was value for the rate I felt, plus having stayed in the Boston Harbor for the preceeding four nights, I was a little worried that it would be a major let down. My fears were unfounded as although the hotel isnt a world beater it more than lives up to its billing. It does exactly what it says on the tin.

title: “GREAT HOTEL”
text: This is my new favorite hotel in New York! Rooms were great, love the location and the staff is fantastic. Went to Gilt for drinks, worked out and got a massage. Could not ask for a better stay!

title: “This hotel is the WORST of the LAX hotels”
text: I foolishly believed some of the Tripadvisor reviews and booked here for an overnight before an early morning flight. The trainee at the reception desk checked me into a "quiet" room that I requested. It turned out to be overlooking the LAX runway and you could hear every plane thundering by. When I called to ask if all rooms where this noisy, she sarcastically asked if I would like a room overlooking the dog kennels (where the dogs apparently bark all night). Finally, I had to appeal to a manager to get their quietest rooms, overlooking a busy, noisy street, which was the best of the three bad options between runway, kennel and street noise. Do NOT stay here if you want to sleep. The sound insulation is the WORST of any airport hotel I have stayed in. The rude and indifferent service by the front desk staff ranks equally at the bottom of any hotel in any city around the world. Shame on Westin!

title: “stay over”
text:
Run of the mill hotel but in a good location near to Fisherman's Wharf. Had no restaurant only small coffee area and pastries bar for breakfasts. But there are plenty of places nearby to eat.
Only stayed here 2 nights on way back to UK from Hawaii. We had room 2090 and if I had stayed another night would have insisted of room change.1st night we were to tired to complain and 2nd night couldn't be bothered!That room is right next door to the vending machine/ice machine room and made a very loud hum all night long. It is also facing the multi storey car park so no view.
Staff were o.k but house keeping kept knocking on the door early in the morning to check on us!!!!!!!!

title: “Great hotel to base your Boston stay.”
text: This hotel is convienient to the Airport and train station and has a shuttle bus that runs every half hour 24 hours a day. This hotel is not one of the newer ones in the chain but is very well maintained and has a very friendly and helpful staff. The free continental breakfast was good and they had plenty of room for every one to sit and enjoy it. I would highly reccomend this hotel to anyone.

title: “Absolutely superb accommodation - stunning views of NYC”
text:
This was my first time to New York and we were not disappointed with our choice of accommodation having researched considerably on Trip Advisor, so I hope that these few words help somebody else with their choice.
The Millennium UN Plaza is quite simply excellent; from the moment we arrived to the moment we left our stay was wonderful. We arrived a little early from JFK however the front desk were extremely friendly, informative and most accommodating and allowed us to check in at that time, so we didn’t need to wait around.
Rooms within other hotels in NYC are usually on the small side so I am told however our room here was most spacious, king size bed (at least), flat screen TV and room safe etc & extremely clean. Reasonably sized bathroom, with bath/shower, sink, toilet & hairdryer etc – what more would anyone want. Our room was simply superb, views were stunning night and day, and we could not fault it at all. We had a view over the east river looking south towards lower Manhattan/Wall St etc and it was stunning any time of day, also great views of both the Empire State Building and the beautiful Chrysler building, stunning. It was a pleasure to wake up in the morning, and always a pleasure to return.
27th Floor – the pool and the fitness centre are wonderful. And there is also a sauna although we did not use it. FYI you need to use the 2 right hand side lifts in order to access the 27th floor. Well worth the effort and a great way to relax after a hectic day around the sights.
The Millennium Plaza is a wonderful hotel, we did not want to leave and we will certainly return next time we visit NYC, thank you to all the staff for making it a great stay.
If you have not visited before this may help too:
To and from JFK – we used an official yellow cab. There is a flat rate fare of $45 + $5.30 tolls + tip (15-20% expected – we paid $60 and the drivers seemed very happy with that). At the taxi rank tell the attendant you want the flat rate fare to your destination before you depart (if that is what you want) else you will get the standard metered fare. You will then be given an official piece of paper with the driver’s number on etc, which I thought was most re-assuring. The journey took about 25 minutes but I think we were very lucky, expect anywhere up to an hour in traffic, which is what it took when we returned to JFK. Again on the return leg don’t forget to ask for the flat rate fare. We also got charged the $5.30 toll upon the return to JFK, not sure why as I think it is a one way toll but I could be wrong, still it wasn’t worth the debate during or at the end of the journey. There are some cheaper alternatives into Manhattan but for the few extra $s I have to say door to door this is far the easiest and best use of your precious time.
There is so much to see but here are a few we did and would recommend:
Rockerfeller Centre for great panoramic views, you can get a 2 visit ticket to see night and day. Well worth it.
Staten Island Ferry – its free, and stunning views of Skyline, and of Statue of Liberty.
Central Park – with a good pair of walking shoes.
Grand Central Station – what a wonderful building & only a 5/10 mins walk, couple of blocks straight down 44th.
The underground - is a must just to say you have done it, very safe in the day We used it a couple of times to return from Lower Manhattan which is worth a walk through the different areas but takes time ($2.50 per single ride, pay at machine). We found Grand Central station to be the closest to the Millennium Plaza hotel, plus there was something special about disembarking at the iconic station that appears in so many movies.
Also there is a great Deli at the corner of 44th and 2nd, turn right out of hotel lobby and 2 minutes if that, on the corner. It has every thing you want and very reasonable, coffee, donuts, fresh sandwiches, you name it has it. Great place. 
Trip Advisor has been a great resource to me so I hope these few words are of use to someone else especially if you are new to NYC as I was, and the few places mentioned are just a sample of the many places to see and visit. Enjoy.

title: “Unforgetable vacation!”
text:
My family and I spent our Easter vacation this year at the St. Regis in Washington, D.C. 
The facilities were exceptional and first class all the way. 
The front desk manager, Ertug Ersoy, and Concierge, Leslie Valtin, and Leila, could not have been more accommodating and gracious during our stay, they all went above and beyond to make sure my family and I had a wonderful time.
As a family, we enjoy dining out and have been to many first class restaurants - their recommendations of restaurants were terrific and we were not dissapointed!
Thank you again for making our trip a memorable one and we cannot wait to go back!
Hank & Annie Rovillard

title: “Great Hotel!”
text: We enjoyed our stay at Adante Hotel & would stay there again. We were greeted Tony at checkin who was always friendly & helpful at the front desk. Our room was clean & tidy with a huge ensuite, big TV, iron, safe & ceiling fan. The area can feel a bit dodgy at night, but we felt safe going to & from the hotel. The only negative is that the complimentary breakfast isn't very exciting, so we went to 'Dottie's True Blue Cafe' nearby & enjoyed delicious breakfasts there.

title: “Everything we were promised and more.”
text:
Travelled with my wife and teenage daughter from the UK to NYC on March 20th. Read the reviews on T/A and got a bit of a mixed bag of opinions which is good. Was attracted by the location and the fact that there was a 24 hr diner witthin the hotel. Booked with letsgo2.com who were very efficient. Flew with Continental from Manchester, who were every bit as good.
We took the train from Newark airport to Penn Station, which is a 5 min walk to the hotel. On our arrival we were met at the front desk by the very helpful Muhammed. We asked to extend room use until 18:00 on check out day to co-incide with our flight home. Not only did we get a free upgrade to a suite, but he sorted this for us for $75+tax. The hotel was probably built in the 1950's and has recently had a full refit. Our room was nothing short of perfect. On the 23rd floor, overlooking 8th Ave, The Empire State building and Madison Square Garden, complete with TWO large flat screen tv's.
With about 7 elevators, getting to our room from the lobby never took more than 5 mins. Times Square was a ten min walk up 8th Ave. Rooms were serviced daily, and cleaning staff were great. We did all the usual visits, but the best was the helicopter trip around Manhatten and up the river. It's not cheap but at $160 inc tax and fuel supp it was worth every penny. Suprizingy, we used the 24 hr MacDonalds outside the hotel for breakfast every day. Without question it represented great value for money, with a very varied menu too. The hotel diner we found to be a little pricey altho the food was good. Do take your laptop as the hotel provides free WiFi which was very useful. Shopping for clothes, shoes, electronics is great if you look around. The stores near the hotel are very competative. The nearer you get to Times Square however, the dearer it gets. Avoid those trendy eateries in Greenwich and Soho, we paid $100 for diner for 3 of us, which wasn't much tastier than MacDonalds!!
For the return journey to the airport, we opted to use the hotel's transportation service. They confirm your flight, and provided us with a limo for $85. This is considerably more money than the train ($15 each) but is much quicker. All in all we will use the hotel again, and look forward to going back soon. You wont be disappoined, there are some less than pretty hotels in the city. We are glad we chose this one (thanx to TripAdvisor xx

title: “First time in New York - I'll definitely be back!”
text: 3 Friends stayed here for one night, all first timers to New York! We were staying with friends in Jersey, and wanted to at least stay one night in the city (that's all we could afford!). Great location, Penn Station so close by! I think we over payed - booked at the last minute for $500/night. Staff very friendly, corrected booking error made by last minute internet travel site. Staff called to our room twice just to make sure everything was ok. Had pillow menu, and also mini stuffed "king kong" on bed (of course you had to pay to take it home with you, New York isn't a cheap town!) Great space for 3, room had 2 full baths and full kitchen. Felt like we were staying in an apartment. Nice lobby- had a rich perfume smell purposely wafting in to create atmosphere.

title: “Large room but mixed service”
text:
After a fantastic stay at the Queenstown (NZ) Sofitel, I had high hopes for the DC branch. Have to say it didn't quite meet the mark.
Good: wonderfully spacious room; plenty of space in the bathroom; large comfy bed; impressive selection of toiletries; very close to the metro; circulator and the tourist attractions, reception and concierge were pleasant and helpful.
Not so good: checking in, the bed only had a really thick cover and no thin blanket so it was sweltering hot till we asked for one the following day (and got two since they remade the bed properly); the aircon didn't function correctly so the room was very hot one night; aircon was really really loud even on low; no kettle or tea or cups in the room; room service took forever (when calling again after 30mins, was told they were very busy); poor service at breakfast (but attentive service at dinner); area can be a bit desolate at night and there's construction next door.
Wouldn't stay in the DC hotel again.

title: “Adjust.Sleep System Beds!!!!”
text:
There were many hotels to choose from, so I chose this one because of the low price, the proximity to family and to try the Adjust.Sleep System Bed. 
All in all the hotel was fine.
PLUSES: free Wi-Fi, easy parking, gym, pool, business center
MINUSES: poor lighting and not able to keep bathroom door ajar 
(as a night light).
The Adjust.Sleep System Bed is purely a gimic (so not a plus).
All things being the same, I would come back again.

title: “Great Space Needle view, did an early check-in & late check out!”
text:
These people took awesome care of me. Getting there a few hours early, they had the room for me at noon. I was able to stay in it till 1pm the next day -- over twenty-four hours of room use. 
Friendly, competent, and accommodating -- I highly recommend this place.

title: “Good value, GREAT location, but NOT a five-star hotel due to snooty check-in staff and pretty standard room”
text:
What we LOVED: central location if you're hanging out in downtown or Loop area. Walk to Millenium park, Chicago River architectural tours, deep dish pizza. SO convenient. I also liked our room on the 21st floor, with lake views. 
We DIDN'T appreciate: our snooty check-in clerk.

title: “Really friendly and helpful staff conseirge very useful overall pretty nice place to stay”
text:
After reading some of the reviews of this place I felt very apprehensive after booking to stay for four nights. However upon arrival the security staff at the door took our bags to the bellman who took them to our room while we checked in. A good start we thought. Checking in was nice and simple although they wanted to take a $100 a night deposit and a credit card, tell them you have neither if you don't want to pay this as we did, they weren't too bothered, just means you can't charge anything to the room but don't reccomend this as hotel service is normally well overpriced anyway. 
The room on the first night was as expected enough room to fit a double bed and an en-suite and not all lot else, the room was however clean the heating worked the bathroom was newish and the tv had all the channels you could want there was free wifi but don't expect to stream a film only get limited bandwidth. Having said this didn't go to New York to stay in watching tv or a film on my laptop was good to be able to find places and to book things to do (recommend to beat the crowds). 
On the second day we were happily upgraded to a suite which was double in size had a bigger bathroom with a bath and again room was very clean and tidy.
As mentioned earlier the conseirge desk was very helpful and we were able to print out pre booked tickets using iPads they had at the desk they also told us where good places to go were whilst we were looking around.
