Can't review the food at the hotel as we never ate at it. There is a bar which on Friday and Saturday nights gets quite busy and if you are on the lower floors can be heard but this wasn't that much of a problem as we were on the 11th floor.
Checking out is at 12 on the day you depart and was easy but as our flight wasn't until 6 the hotel was able to keep our bags in safe storage until we were ready to go to the airport they security guy hailed a cab and loaded our bags.
All in all brilliant hotel undergoing a bit of a makeover hence probably some bad reviews before but seem to have got it together now definitely recommend for a weekend break

title: “Fantastic stay!”
text:
We chose Fisherman's Wharf to get out of the hustle and bustle of Union Square. It was definitely the right choice and the Hyatt made it worthwhile. 
We were greeted by Leslie who was lovely and helpful, especially when we wanted to have a mini fridge brought up to the room. This was done promptly and at no cost. 
The room was large with a comfortable bed and contemporary decor. The WiFi is not free except in the lounge which is a real shame.
We had a view of the pool which was ... interesting. I think a few people lounging at the pool had no idea or didn't care that others could see them. One woman was sitting with her legs apart which was so disgusting! Another guy was happily picking his nose - getting nice and deep. Tip for those guests - you're not at your house! People watching, indeed!
The location of the hotel is fantastic. Not far from Pier 39 and also where the sightseeing bus begins their route. We used this to get to Union Square, then hopped back on when we were ready. Lots of places to eat. There is also a SafeWay super close which is great for picking up lunch etc. It was also close to our departure point for our day trips. 
The service at this hotel was fantastic. Everyone was very courteous and welcoming. House keeping went above and beyond (especially with coffee requests). Check out was speedy. 
Would definitely stay here again! I was very wary about staying in Fisherman's Wharf overall, but now I wouldn't stay anywhere else.

title: “Clean and friendly”
text: we were impressed with the friendliness of the staff, especially Scott and Gabriella.. We really enjoyed the hot breakfast and the cleanliness of the eating area. We will be staying here again. housekeeping staff was very professional.

title: “Great Hotel for the price”
text: We stayed here last weekend, it has been recently renovated and still looks a little rough from the outside, but TOTALLY worth it. It is located near the Hard Rock Cafe, Rainforest Cafe and within walking distance to so much more. FREE Parking is an added bonus. I can't wait to go back to Chicago and will stay here again!

title: “Great Location, Nice Hotel”
text: Nothing spectacular but nice enough and great location......The room was exactly as tripadvisors stated...room was small, but the view was great, water pressure really stinks, room seems damp, but I guess it was the humidity.... We heard train whistles all night but I kind of liked it.... We requested a high floor and got the top floor which was really nice and the elevators are very fast. The restaurant decor was really nice, food was okay, waitstaff is very attentive and very friendly - We got the rate that included self parking - and if you don't get lost in the parking garage it was very convenient. The location is super - right on the riverwalk and mall and walking to the Alamo and Alamo plaza which has lots to do....RipleysBON, Haunted adventure, Guiness, restaurants, shops...etc... Don't miss the mirror maze - we loved it! on our last trip to SA we took the hop on/off bus tour to the missions and Market square...the visitor center is next to the Alamo...so, technically you would never have to drive anywhere else once you got to the hotel. I don't like the pillow tops on the beds - they move around and get kind of lumpy...We requested a rollaway for one of our kids so they would not have to sleep together - but I ended up pushing it up next to the floor - to ceiling window and sleeping on it myself the second night- It was extremely relaxing - like sleeping on a cloud looking down at the world. There is a Denny's right across the street - good for breakfast if you don't want to pay the big bucks at the hotel restaurant. They also have a little Starbucks style coffee/brkfst/salad stand - but I think the hours are weird. One thing I really disliked was that there was a channel on the TV that showed full male and female nudity - just a regular channel - not one that you specifically seek out - or pay for...so if my kids were channel surfing......!!....Luckily I saw it first so I knew to supervise their tv watching and we didn't watch that much tv anyway - they supposedly have a parental lock - but I tried to use it and the channel still came up ...HELLOOOOOO!!!

title: “Great deal! Greater location”
text: Terrific location ! Enormous, clean room, Large bathroom. Bought on hotwire for 151 per nt...great deal!

title: “Wonderful Stay”
text: This was our first visit to Chicago and we got an incredible deal for four nights using a third party website. With that in mind we were fully expecting a more basic room. However on arrival we were given a wonderful room on the 16th floor overlooking the river and to describe the view as stunning is an understatement! The room itself was spacious and very clean, as was the bathroom. Credit to all the staff working in the hotel as everyone was friendly and helpful, from the concierge who assisted us with Ryder Cup journey planning to the team at the Cityscape Bar. Do try and visit the bar if you can as the views here are also outstanding. Location wise we were close to many attractions, but with taxis also outside the hotel it was easy to get around the city. We hope to be back!

title: “BED BUGS!”
text:
I stayed April 16th 2011, without looking at reviews. We left this morning with bed bug bites everywhere. Location and service is fine but I obviously would not return because they are most definitely infested. Also, the shower was scorching hot and the only way to fix it was to shut the hot water off completely but that may have been an issue only in the room I 
stayed in.

title: “Sorry, but can´t recommend it. You have to search again.”
text:
Before you arrive to Off Soho Suites, you are expecting a nice apartment in a nice neighbourhood, close to everything.
Before you arrive, you are thinking, I made the right choice, this is not a bad price compare to other hotels in New York, specially if you are a group of 4 people.
Well, we were a group of 4 people and all of us expected the same, but sorry, dreams don't come true.
2 people will sleep ok, the other 2 won´t sleep at all. Sofa bed is quite uncomfortable and the worst part is the noise coming from the Air Conditioning devices just outside your window. I tried with diferent ear-plugs, but non of them worked.
Yes this is true, New York is the city that never sleeps, specially if you stay here.
If you are hard sleeper, then this is the place for you.

title:
“The worst hotel in the world
at $127.00 i'd opt for a motel!! It'll be bettet trust me”
text:
They reserved me a two bedroom condo for me but when i got there all the condos were under renovation!!!! ?????? WTF? I couldnt get another room anywhere else due to it being a saturday. They wanted full price for two rooms instead. Which turned out to be more than the cost of the condo!!! More by $47.00!!! They took my reservation and did a "bait and switch" on us. This was on my wedding day and it was for my in-laws who flew in from overseas. I was embarresed to say the least. I 
Will NEVER use this hotel ever again. Did i mention the blankets had holes in it from cigarettes in a non smoking room??? Rooms smell bad an odor of musk, and after you sleep there once your body feels icky, sucks here get better rooms for the same price everywhere else!!!

title: “Best Hotel in Boston”
text: By far this hotel outranks every hotel in Boston. Every aspect of my stay was perfect. I will be back! From the moment I arrived at the Fairmont Battery Wharf I was blown away at the hotel, the location, and the staff. Everything was wonderful. We will see this hotel listed among the top tier in the country. Can't wait to go back!

title: “Mixed Feelings”
text:
My husband & I stayed for 2 nights and found it to be one of the most well-decorated hotels we've stayed in. We loved the contemporary linens, decorations. leopard-print robes and Aveda bath products. However, beware! There is no toothpaste provided. Rather, you would be expected to pay $3.95 for a mini-tube found in the mini-bar, which we thought was lame.
We did feel the room was small, but right around what one should expect in the city anyway. There is no coffee maker in the room, but that is made up for by the hotel's provision of organic coffee & high-quality tea in their lobby/communal living room area, along with free wine & beer in the evening and milk & cookies in the later part of the evening.
We thought the front desk staff was dispassionate--not warm, but not rude. The housekeeping staff on the other hand is very friendly. Parking is a pain as it generally is in the city, so I would suggest either parking down Howard Street in the open-lot parking which is roughly $16 from 8am - 5pm.
Overall, it was not a bad deal, considering that we paid $70 on priceline. I found out that we could have upgraded to a bay view room for $50 per night, but decided to pass on it since we were planning to spend more time outdoors.

title: “Deceptive”
text:
We are still doing time at this hotel, unfortunately.
On check in we specifically asked for a quiet room, as we are here for an important meeting at City Hall, which we were still in the process of preparing for. We were instantly assured that we were "lakeside," then the clerk "appeared" to doublecheck and confirm that we were assigned a "quiet room."
After taking the elevator to the 9th floor, we opened the door to our room to discover it overlooked the expressway -- no quiet and no lakeside, and the room is Handicapped Accessible! Oversized bathroom, no closet, and low level facilities!
On a return trip to the front desk clerk to insist on a quiet room, we were told there were absolutely no other rooms available, period. Zero satisfaction and zero effort to make good on their statements or honor our request.
Yesterday we were disgusted by the deception and misleading comments made by the clerk on check in, and today we're overtired due to lack of sleep and excessive noise thanks to the location of the room. Our recommendation to our governmental funding unit will be "NEVER book this Holiday Inn again."

title: “Better choice then I expected”
text: I was looking for a cheap hotel in a walking distance from McCormick Centre and this one was a better choice then I expected according to the website. I appreciated the kids-friendly staff, free coffee and tea, possibility to use the fridge and microwave. The rooms were big, clean, although furniture seems old and used. But wifi ran quickly, TV at the room, many restaurants around. Unfortunately no elevator, bit noisy. But right on the red line of train. If you don't expect luxury, I would recommend that.

title: “Great Stay At The Millenium”
text: I stayed here 2 nights with my wife and could not have had a better time we stayed on the 33rd floor. We had a view right out at ground zero which I did not see since 9-11 so it was a learning experience as far as accesing the damage. The room service was great and the mini bar is a tease but for those prices I could not touch it. So I advise anyone who stays to not look in there because it 's gonna get you. I would recommend this to all peole for all different reasons.

title: “Would not return”
text: We usually stay at the Sheraton, but wanted to try the Marriott because it was a slightly more convenient location and about $40 less per night, but I will be returning to the Sheraton on my next visit. The lobby of the Marriott is nice with a wall-sized big screen TV in the sports bar. Location is also excellent for Prudential Center, Back Bay and parents visiting their students at Berklee or Northeastern. The decor in the rooms definitely needs an upgrade and hallways and rooms were not super clean. Staff was helpful and friendly. Because it's a non-smoking hotel (good thing) everyone hangs out around the front entrance smoking, which I thought was pretty disgusting. I also don't like when hotels charge you to use the computers in their business centers.

title: “had higher hopes for this place”
text:
Wish I could pick a rating between average and very good. 
Pros: Large room, nice bar and outdoor fire pit area, great breakfast buffett (although expensive), friendly staff, convenient location
Cons: Reservation got messed up, housekeeping didn't come, keys didn't work, parking deck is a zoo, sink kept backing up

title: “a great hotel”
text:
this is one of the best run hotels i have ever been in from the moment we checked in to check out everything was great i have stayed at more expensive hotels and this beats them all 
there was nothing to complain about

title: “Never Again”
text:
Ours was a comedy of errors, but safe to say that most of it was due to inefficiently trained staff.
To begin with, the directions given be their staff were wrong.
Our booking was wrong, we had to change rooms due to my friend needing universal handicapped room(shower stall). At first they tried to give us a room with ONE King, we needed 2 queens. The manager finally comped the second room. 
My tub was dirty(I don't think it should have had black grout around the tub....it looked a lot closer to mold/mildew than decoration), my friend's sink plugged and we couldn't pay the way we wanted to pay, even after we ask them at least 3 times if they could split the bill or how else can we pay--Red Roof Inn needs to train their staff.

title: “nice remodel!”
text: We stay last weekend at this newly remodeled location. It is very nice! The staff are very friendly and the shuttle service to the airport is great. We did the park and fly and the price is the best we could find. Even though it is very close to the airport, it is super quiet.

title: “very nice indeed”
text: found the hotel to be excellent. the staff were very friendly and helpfull. the room we stayed in was very clean and cosy. the food in the resturant was lovely and found it to be good value for money. it was a bit of a long way out of town with no resturants nearby but we used the bus and cab to get to and from the city which was very affordable. thumbs up from me.

title: “Not bad for the price”
text: After reading the many terrible reviews this hotel has gotten I was very nervous about staying there. But I was surprised by what I found suring my stay. The staff was friendly, not indifferent, as I expected. Yes the lobby sets you up to expect big things from the room and that expectation will not be met. However, we found the room to be big enough (I've seen smaller) and it wa clean although a bit dingy with marks on the walls and an old fashioned bathroom. But we got this room by using Priceline for the first time. And for $70 a night it was just fine. The restaurants in the hotel are great (especially Schmicks for wonderful fresh fish) and it met all of our expectations for such a small price. If I had paid the full price I would have not been happy, but for $70, the location could not be better and I can live with walss that need a paint job.

title: “A bit dated but Great service.”
text: This hotel is In a good location. If you don't mind walking, you can just walk around Washington from the hotel, also walking distance to Georgetown. The hotel itself felt a bit dated compared to what Im used to but still quite nice. The service was fantastic, we and the same staff on the same shift, by the 2nd or 3 rd day you feel like a local. The batman always remembered what my drink was etc. Great little bar downstairs which doubles up as a breakfast venue. Rooms were quite ok with a tv sitting area and. Ice big bathroom. Bed quite comfortable. I can't say whether it was value for money as I didn't pay, work did.

title: “beautiful but unsafe”
text:
Our first days at this hotel was bliss, the staff & management were so welcoming & kind. The rooms are fantastic, facilities is everything you need, hotwater, aircon, clean, well serviced, TV, free wireless internet, laundry services, a little shop that sells snacks & microwavable food, free breakfast which was well organized & free coffee in the reception. Another bonus which was really awesome for our situation which was my husband going to work during the day & i was alone at the hotel, the staff offer to drive you to malls, restaurants or anywhwere else within a 5mile radius. 
Our stay at this hotel would have been outstanding if not for the fact that we were robbed at gunpoint in the hotel parking lot. Now I know that being Texas and all its expected that people do carry guns but being a tourist it completely ruined our 2 week stay in Houston. Although the hotel staff did everything they could to help with the investigation I believe the situation could have been easily avoided. Firstly the hotel premises should have been fenced off or there should have been security guards in the parking lot after dark. Even the staff that worked night were scared that they would lock the door after a certain time. Therefore I gave location no rating & since the thiefs took my handbag with everthing in it I rated value as 2.
We were followed from the ATM machine not far away which we used on the way back from dinner. So people do not use ATM machines at night as we were told by the officers that it was becoming a common occurence.
If it wasnt for this incident I would probably have rated the hotel as 4 or probably 5. 
I would recommend this hotel to a friend however only after there is more security in the front or parking lot.

title: “Turn the bathroom fan on”
text:
First tip on staying here. Close the bathroom door and turn the fan on. Hopefully that will prevent the smoke alarm from going off. I wouldn't know - I didn't do either and ended up dripping wet, naked, and frantically trying to turn off a horrendously loud smoke alarm. I suggest detaching it from the wall and throwing it under the mattress. When I called the front desk to let them know it seemed like they were well acquinted with this problem - probably happens daily there. 
Beyond that, hotel was ok at best. My non-smoking room smelled of smoke. I know modern design is a cool thing at hotels and tend to enjoy it, even if I wouldn't decorate like that at home. I've become a big fan of W hotels. This is not that. This is the least practical hotel room that I have ever stayed in. I didn't watch TV, but the fact it was on the floor off to the side didn't really make me want to deal with it. The bed platform is quite a toe-stubber, it seems to be everywhere. I personally don't mind the glass bathroom but I could see it bothering many others.
Should I have to stay in DTLA again it will not be at The Standard.

title: “Not fancy but really nice”
text: The hotel looks small (small lobby for instance), but it is also modern and clean. The staff is very nice and helpful. The swimming pool on the rooftop is a bit disappointing: quite small and the air (yes, the air, not the water) is totally overheated (in summer !). The hotel is also very well located. The rooms are small but quite nice.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: We just got back from a four night stay at the Belvedere, it was great. When I booked the hotel I was unsure from some of the other reviews, but we were really pleased. First of all, the location was excellent, It's on W. 48th street between 8th and 9th ave, on the edge of the theater district. It was perfect because we could walk almost everywhere and weren't far from the subway stop. Restaurant Row is on 9th ave. and so there were great food options, I recommend Joe Allen for pre-theater dinning. You can walk to everyshow and timesquare. The hotel itself was very nice too. The lobby is very nice, and we were always greeted friendly. We were lucky and got a great room, make sure to ask for the highest corner room possible that way it'll be bigger and you'll have a better chance for a good view (and less noise). The room was very comfortable, and a great deal for the price. I would definately recommend the Belvedere Hotel to anyone. It made our vacation really pleasent and fun.

title: “Horrible Customer Service”
text: I prebooked and prepaid my stay at the Hyatt Regency but when the day to stay came we had whiteout blizzard conditions at home and were not able to travel. I tried calling the hotel and explaining the conditions and asked to move the reservation forward a day. I was treated very rudely by the agent and they refused the request. I am a VIP card holder for Hyatt hotels brands I have never had this type of service at any of the other hotels. I didn't want a refund or to cancel the reservation, I was simply asking to move it forward a day because the weather conditions made it dangerous to travel and the region I live in was under an emergency alert. Horrible place.

title: “Beautiful location, Stylish rooms, Attentive, Friendly staff, Regular price too high”
text: I got a super priceline rate on this room. Obviously it wasn't in the tower with a view, but it was very stylish and comfortable. The grounds are spectacular and right on the marina. I'm sure the restaurant was great although I was too cheap to dine there. The fitness center is surprizingly well equipped with a great view of the marina (you will need help finding it though). This is where my frugality comes in. I always thought that the higher the price, the fewer extra charges there would be. I couldn't understand the $35 valet or $25/night self park when the hotel seemed to own their own lots. It was a nice location, but I don't think it was in an area where parking is usually not free. Maybe since they were so close to Sea World they figured they could pull it off since Sea World charges for parking. I could understand the internet not being included in my room since I got it at less than half price. Best Western, MicroTel, Holiday Inn and almost every place I've ever stayed offer it for free BTW. The breakfast wasn't free either. I still got a great deal for the level of property it was but I might not have been as happy if I paid full price.

title: “It's a dump. If you're going to bother going to NY,pay the extra for something better”
text:
The place is a tip. The hotel itself is absolutely huge, and facing Madison Square Garden, so when you roll up to the place, you think you 're in for a treat. You could not wish for a better location. 
Inside, it looks like a scene from "The Shining". The huge lobby is authentic 1930's (last time it was decorated or cleaned). The rooms are frankly a disgrace. We went back to the lobby and demanded to be moved , but the one we were moved to was no better. The rooms are dirty, dusty and smell. If I went again , I would not stay there. With the subway system as good and as widespread as it is, there's no need to stay absolutely slap bang in the middle of NY. Even if you did want to stay in the middle, and like me you have travelled halfway around the world to get there, pay the extra, get something better. Don't let this dump cast a shadow on your trip. I have to add that New York is my favourite city I have ever been to. I was a cynic before I went, but found the people the most genuine I have come across anywhere in the world. Just don't stay here. Please.

title: “Great location and good value”
text: We stayed 4 nights at this hotel. Apart from two of the reception staff who we nicknamed Miss Sunshine and Miss Congeniality for their less than friendly approach, we found this apartment good value and very handy to all the main sights. With a kitchenette you could prepare a basic meal but there are a number of reasonable restaurants nearby. The breakfast was sufficient. There are a couple of small supermarkets close. The guest laundry is handy. The rooms were spacious, clean and comfortable. We would stay there again.

title: “Who needs sleep?”
text:
We stayed at the Stockyards Hotel on a Saturday night. The noise from the drunken revelers on the street just below our window kept us up until nearly 3 a.m. 
So, if you plan on visiting on the weekend, be prepared -- or ask for one of the interior courtyard rooms.

title: “Great rooms and Excellent location”
text:
I recently completed a one night stay at the Doubletree Suites Times Square, and it was a very memorable stay. I was debating back and forth whether to stay at this hotel or at the newer, recently renovated Conrad in Battery Park City. Ultimately, this one won out because of the extremely convenient location.
I checked in on a Saturday afternoon around 330pm, and had no wait or trouble getting my room. We had a room on the 25th floor with a partial view of Times Square. The room itself was very large by any standard (any especially by NYC standards, where you'll be lucky to have any walking room in most hotel rooms). This room had a very large living room with sofabed, chairs, flat screen TV, sink, and fridge. The main bedroom had 2 double beds, another flat screen, and there was access to the very large bathroom via both the bedroom and living room.
The room was very comfortable; everything from the water pressure in the shower to the central air conditioning worked great. As I mentioned above, the location is second to none, as you are right in the heart of Times Square. 
The only possible knock is the price; the nightly rate for the night I was there was in excess of $600, which is very high even by NYC standards. Luckily, as a Hilton Honors Gold member, I had accumulated enough points for a free night. The best part is a free night here costs as many points as many smaller Hilton properties in the area.
I would definitely come back here in the future for any special events, especially birthdays or New Years.

title: “Perfect location and economical hotel”
text: Have stayed here many times and each time was satisfying. The room prices have always been very competative for NYC. Central location is perfect for business and leisure. On the lucky occasion of getting a park view room the stay becomes very special.

title: “Nice place to stay”
text: We stayed three nights. The location is in a good location to get around Jax.

title: “Inn New York City - The chilled out side of the city!”
text:
My wife and I stayed at Inn New York City for a week in late May (20th to the 27th May). When first entering the Vermont Suite, you feel like you are transported into your own little world. The duplex style suite has everything you need and is furnitured so elegantly. With this suite having it's own separate entrance it feels like you are experiencing New York from your own place in the Upper West Side.
After spending the days in a variety of places around New York, it was always great to get back to the peace and tranquility of our place, before freshening up for the evening.
I can not recommend this place more highly. The owners are there as much or as little as you need, the pantry is refreshed everyday and the facilities are first rate.
What makes The Inn even better is that it is just a couple of blocks away from Central Park and there is a metro stop at the end of the tree lined street (so you can get around the city so easily). I would highly recommend the $24 seven day ticket (or other metrocard options) as it is an excellent way to navigate the whole area.
With this being our first trip to New York, we will definitely be back. We would definitely stay at Inn New York City!

title: “Great hotel, friendly staff, and upgraded for free”
text: Went to Boston for a weekend getaway, booked a suite directly on the hotel's website and when arrived was informed we had been upgraded to the presidential suite! Front desk and hotel staff were very friendly and helpful. Room service slightly overpriced but food was good.

title: “this is a budget hotel”
text: it is meant to be a budget hotel, and with that in mind it is good. it is however in an exellent location and whilst the rooms are very small and simple (a bit stuffy and airless) and breakfast (from a cupboard) is more than basic! the staff are incredibly helpfull and friendly.

title: “Great value”
text:
Stayed for two nights during spring break. The hotel is kinds hard to get to if you are coming from I-10. Has a parking garage. Pool and hot tub were crowded as was evening food. We decided to eat breakfast early to avoid the crowd. We ate breakfast between 6 and 6:30 am and there was only about 5-6 other people eating. I would suggest getting to breakfast early. I used the business center--free internet, free printing. I had a king bed suite. The kids slept on the pull out sofa. Room had a fridge and microwave. I was on the 11th floor and I could hear kids running down the halls and slamming doors when I was on the sofa but once I closed the door to the bedroom I didnt have a problem. The breakfast and supper all-you-can-eat buffet is a great value. You can make your plate and take your food up to your room. Buffet saves a lot of money and has lots of choices.
Breakfast: apple juice, orange juice, milk, cereal, oatmeal, biscuits and gravy, french toast, scrambled eggs, sausage, bagels, muffins, make-it-yourself-waffles.
Evening: sodas, alcoholic drinks (for adults), soup, baked potatoes, chicken strips, nachos, salad, hotdogs
Cons: The elevators are very slow. The blankets are a little then, so I went down to the front desk and got another one.

title: “Nice size room for NYC”
text: The room is a good size and clean. Our view was okay but we were not on the top floors. That was not important for my stay but if it is for you, then definitely request the highest floors in the hotel. I really like the location, right near the empire state bldg, but off the busy tourist path. Staff was friendly and helpful. Rooms were nice and quiet.

title: “Awful, not very friendly to Newlyweds”
text:
My wife and I stayed here for two nights after our wedding before heading out to our honeymoon. We requested a King Premier room but when we got to the room we saw it had two tiny little beds. Called the front desk and they said they didn't have a King room and we'd have to wait. The parking lot seemed empty and the hotel didn't seem all that busy so I wonder why they didn't have the proper room we had paid for. After a few hours we had to check back, the desk didn't call us and then they had a king bed available.
The room was not very nice. Sheets and pillows were cheap materials and very worn. Definitely NOT what I would expect from an alleged 4 star hotel. 
The start of our stay actually ruined the mood for the rest of it. Screwing up our room followed by uninterested service from the front desk made us feel like we weren't wanted.
Here's a tip to the hotel staff and management: When a married couple checks in, give them the King Bed Rooms, not your pathetic tiny bed rooms!!!!! And no Wifi in 2011??? That's stupid! Gosh! You'd think they'd have that much common sense! The room was also noisy -- elevators, construction, thin walls.
We ordered room service several times. The food was decent and delivery was as expected. But sadly, that's the only positive comment I can make on this hotel.
WAY TO RUIN THE MOOD INTERCONTINENTAL!!!!

title: “First Visit at Algonquin Hotel”
text:
I had recently read a story about the renovation at The Algonquin Hotel and decided to stay there while visiting New York again. It turned out to be an excellent choice. Everyone was helpful and very friendly and made you feel very welcome. The rooms are small but beautiful, very comfortable bed, great bathroom, very clean. The hotel has a lot of history connected to it. And of course, there is that wonderful cat "Matilda" who lives in the lobby, and if she isn't taking one of her cat naps, will greet you with her wonderful personality and send you on your way to explore her exciting city. The hotel is close to the theatre district and 5th Ave. Who could ask for anything more.
Fan of New York from St. Louis, MO

title: “Helpful Staff”
text: Very helpful staff for planning your trip around Boston and the New England states. Very clean and near some great eating. Close to the Red line...very handy.

title: “Out of the ordinary”
text:
I spent a weekend at the Inn and it was my first time in Baltimore. I must say this place contributed to make my stay memorable.
This is not your ordinary hotel room, as it could well be bigger than your own apartment. The rooms are absolutely huge, with full living/dining room, large bathroom with full double jaccuzzi and shower, and a large room with a great closet. If you are in for a long stay in Baltimore, there can be no better place.
I loved the fact that the structure is actual concrete walls (i.e., little outside noise), and the decor is raw mediterranean: painted walls in warm colors, concrete floors, rugs instead of carpet. Free wine and water in the fridge (if only all hotels were like this!), a super comfy bed and breakfast cooked to order delivered to your room (or at the Agora Cafe downstairs, except Sundays). Last but not least, a non invasive, super friendly assistance from the young staff.
The only odd thing that gets time to get used to are the sensor lights, which I quickly learned how to manage, but still had to get up one time to switch it off as a brisk move to snooze my alarm triggered the lights on. Minor damages thought.
The hotel itself was great, but location turned out to be perfect. You are right in between the nice restaurants and shops at the Inner Harbor, and the bars and nightlife of Fells Point, without having to endure noise or any sort of traffic that you may find in either of these (especially the noise). I was on a lower floor facing the street and had no problem with noise.
You can easily walk to many of the attractions in Baltimore from here, park your car nearby or take one of the free city circulators that stop right by the hotel. There was plenty to see here and whenerver I decide to come back this wll certainly be my first choice.

title: “Location, location, location!”
text:
We stayed at the JW Marriott over the holiday weekend with our two kids and the location was the best!!! If you want to be close to all the monuments, museums and the White House, this is the place to be! The hotel is very nice and everyone we experienced was very friendly. The valet is quite pricey at $40/nt (plus tax) but that is what we saw around town and the convenience of having the car at the property is worth the few extra bucks. We got the breakfast package which I highly recommend if you are with a family. It saved us time and money getting a hot meal before we began touring for the day. 
Finally, the room. The room was very clean but a bit on the small side. This did not matter as we were gone most of the day. But the best part was the view!!! If you choose this hotel and you are visiting DC for pleasure and the sites, splurge and pay for a room on the 12th floor with a view. The view is worth the splurge!!! There is a huge balcony shared by about twenty rooms. We looked directly at the Washington Monument. To our left, the capital. To the right, the Lincoln Memorial. Giant American flags whipping in the wind to add to the amazing feeling you get while snapping pictures view out your door! 
Overall, a fantastic stay and I highly recommend this hotel if you are visiting DC!

title: “What's not to like”
text:
I walked by the Intercontinental back in 2008 and looked at the location and the Starbucks right next to the lobby and decided: Next time I'll stay here! So I did, and really have nothing to complain about. Great room, perfect location and friendly service. Unfortunately, the pool was closed at the time. We were free to go to the pool at the Marriott across the street if we'd like. Had a decent burger at MJ Steakhouse and my morning coffee at Starbucks. 
I however do agree that any hotel these days should have free internet, but many just used Starbucks. My plan was not to stay in my room too long anyway.

title: “True to it's name”
text: I just got back from a weeklong trip to New York City where I had the pleasure of staying at the Pod 39 Hotel. Upon arrival, I must say that my first thoughts were of shock and surprise at how small the rooms truly were! I had already read all the reviews that talked about exactly how small these rooms were but I had not been expecting this. However, after the intial entry into the room I had discovered that it actually started to grow on me, going from small to "cozy". This was because I only really spent about 9 hours a day in the hotel sleeping. This brings me to my next point; location. The hotel is located conveniently near Grand Central Station, making all my daily ventures into the city seem extremely easy. I could catch the S shuttle to times square or take the 4-6 subs to reach all the major districts of manhattan. In the end, the proximity of the hotel to the subway terminal made my stay in new york extremely convenient, especially on those nights when I would stay out till 3am. The hotel staff were always courteous and helpful, as every time I arrived I was greeted by a friendly hello. The room service was also exceptionally fast, as all of my requests were brought up in record speed - literally a minute or two after I shut the phone. My one complaint was that out of my 5 night stay, my room was not serviced on the final night. All in all, my stay at the pod hotel just seemed to get better and better as the nights went by as it really started to feel like home.

title: “A lot of bang for cheap price.”
text: I stayed here for a night with couples. We went to the inner harbor and came back to just sleep. Beds were comfty, clean, and quiet. I have to say the man up front Kal was so helpful with every request I had. If you need to get things done ask for him! He made personal calls all night for my late transportation needs! Complimentary breakfast was good for being free. The Waffle machine was a hit =)

title: “Hotel needs a good renovation but good value. Very helpful staff.”
text: If you are interested in the Chicago Public Library, the Chicago Art Institute, the Field Museum and the Shedd Aquarium, this hotel is superbly located. Otherwise, you'd probably prefer a hotel further North. The staff is very helpful but the hotel needs a good renovation.

title: “Great location, easy walk to Times Square”
text: The location is very close to Times Square yet not too close for comfort, i.e. noise. Just a 5 to 10 minutes walk and you'll be in the middle of everything, the subway, shops, Broadway, etc. The bed was very comfortable, the room was clean and spacious by Manhattan standards. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Older Motel”
text: This hotel was clean. It is older and very noisy. You could not set the fan to run all the time to block the noise, The fan kicked on & off the entire time. Don't know which was worse the noise or the fan.

title: “Great airport hotel”
text: Great airport hotel and value for price. I commonly stay here and at another Starwood property. They were updating the lounge area during my last stay and looking forward to the addition. Hot tub was not quite hot enough but hopefully easy to rectify.

title: “As Bad as it Gets”
text: I stayed here awhile ago and I have to say that it appears to be the worst value in NY City. It is definitely the worst hotel I stayed in NYC. Not only was the room extremely small, it was in a very seedy portion of the Big Apple. The only plus is that it is a short walk to Times Square. Other than that, I say, stay away from this place! It needs to be torn down and replaced with something that is better suited for the nae NY Inn

title: “Worst Hotel In America”
text: We Needed a hotel for the night, and this was one of the only ones available. We pulled up, and the parking lot was full, so we figured it would be ok.. WRONG! The beds were so hard you could feel the springs, all hours of the night you could hear people running back and forth in front of our room screaming at the top of their lungs. Traffic noise was loud, and you could even hear your neighbor flush their toilet. In the early morning, the room above us was still having an active party, complete with jumping up and down, and who knows what else.. The fridge in the room was so loud, and it kicked on constantly to the point we un plugged it. The hotel seems to attract the pay by the hour crowd, and was really shady once the sun went down.. I would not stay here with kids, etc..

title: “Good place to stay for Chicago business trip”
text: Spent 2 nights there - Room was much better than average. Clean, quite (19th floor). Check in / Check out was smooth as can be. Good internet connection. $10 cab ride to Sears Tower. $50 ride to Airport. Lots of places to eat and shop within walking distance including groceries and pharmacies.

title: “Centrally Located Freindly Staff”
text:
I booked thru Hotwire.com and was a bit leary at not knowing where I was going to stay. I went to Chicago for the Bears Fan Convention March 31 to April 1, 2007. After I booked on Hotwire, Club Quarters came up. I had never heard of the hotel and was dismayed to see they want a credit card deposit for incidentals. I do not have a credit card. Once you book on Hotwire, you can not change your booking. I called the hotel and was told, no problem, just leave $50 cash. (On arrival, the front desk lady told me it was $50 a day. I told her that's not what the guy on the phone said. I had no problem paying, as I had the cash on me. I was about to give her the $100 when I asked about a Bank of America ATM. She gave me the location and then said it was for telephone use and movie purchases. I laughed and said I was in town for the Bears Fest and I have a mobile. She said to give her $60.)
I arrived quite early for check in, 9am to be precise and check in is at 3pm. The staff was able to find me a room and check me in any way. I was told it was a smoking room, but could NOT smell any smoke. I even sniffed the curtains and no smoke smell. The room is VERY spacious. I estimate it to be 17 ft by 8 ft. 
The bed was quite comfortable and the temperature of the room excellent. The shower is also quite large and I had hot water on demand. The bathroom and room itself were really clean. 
There is free internet access in the business center. The business center on floor 3 next to the ice machine and vending area is small. There is one computer and one printer. I only needed to use it twice and did not have to queue up. 
The only downside to my stay: the rooms are not sound proof and I could hear what seemed like every door opening and closing nearby. But I did NOT hear any of the traffic on Adams St.
The staff were freindly and courteous. My deposit was refunded to me in full when I checked out (I didn't use the phone or the TV - I was busy with daBEARS!!!! ) 
The hotel is centrally located, plenty of bus and el routes nearby. It is within walking distance to all major sites in the loop area. There is a Starbucks next to the hotel and a 7-11 across the street that is open 24 hours a day. There is a Bank of America with an ATM a block away.

title: “Nice Location, Old Rooms”
text: The location is great. The public areas of the hotel are stunning. The rooms are another story. They are old and dark and not well kept. When we asked to change rooms they told us they were all the same rather than trying to accomodate us. Also, at the end of our stay we found some outrageous fee on the bill that was associated with the "free" breakfast. Of course, we were told we had to pay this.

title: “awful service”
text:
The infrastructure is a little past its sell-by-date at best. This could be rescued by great service, but sadly it isn't.
Two minor faults in the room -- a non-functioning light and a closet door which wouldn't stay closed -- became jaw-clenching frustrations when they weren't fixed even on the third time of asking. The third time, by the way, was to the duty manager, who has also not delivered on her promise to let me know the cause of the non-responsiveness.
All hotels have little glitches from time to time -- the good ones fix the problems first time round and apologise. In bad ones, they don't and they look you in the eye and lie to you.
This is a bad hotel.

title: “Excellent in every way!”
text:
Wonderful hotel that has everything anyone could want. It is obvious that lot of attention went into the design of this hotel. It is very clean & new. The rooms are lovely & comfortable. Has a great pool, a nice large hot tub/spa, and a well set-up work-out room.
Our room charge included breakfast for two and the assortment was awesome. Felt like I was on a cruise ship with the spread!
The best part of all though is that it has a day spa right in the hotel (also accessible from an outside entrance if not staying at the hotel). The spa is lovely & all of the staff were pleasant, warm & welcoming. The services there were reasonably priced & very professional. Will definitely go back.

title: “Very Pleased”
text:
We spent five nights at this hotel, and were very pleased! The staff were all very accomodating, and the facility was within walking distance to DC subway stops. There is a grocery store (Whole Foods) a very short distance away. The hotel is near embassy row, and the neighborhood was quiet, and seemed quite safe for evening walking excursions. 
We will stay here againg when we return to DC in the future!

title: “A luxurious, welcoming retreat in the heart of Midtown Manhattan.”
text:
My teen and I stayed at Sanctuary Hotel for a week long trip this past month. I was being an indulgent mother as she chose the hotel based on the photos of the decor she saw online. I am a bit particular about where I stay and was leaning towards a big name hotel vs. a boutique hotel. Wow. What can I say? Sanctuary Hotel provided a first rate stay. And the primary reason I feel this way is because of the staff. A phenomenal bunch of young men and women who really go out of their way to take care of you. But overall, it is really a fabulous place in Midtown Manhattan.
Decor~ Check out the photos online. It is really a beautifully decorated place. I liked the darker decor, I thought it was peaceful but very, very hip. I have to admit that I was a bit cautious initially, thinking that it was going to be some sort of cool urban place with an attitude to match, but I couldn't have been more wrong. It is chic and it is very, very welcoming.
Location~ Times Square is truly steps away and around the corner from Sanctuary. Broadway is just a few steps further and Top of the Rock is about the same distance in the other direction. The subway (which we became quite proficient at) is on the corner. There is a small shop across the street for sodas or snacks and tons of restaurants, shops, etc. within walking distance. NYC is a very walkable city, so once you have the basics sorted out, it is very easy to get to Central Park and several other locations from Sanctuary. Also Grey Line bus tours is barely a block away. And the staff is always on hand to help with directions, maps...and encouragement!
Room~ The queen room was fine for two. We had plenty of room to move about, the "closet" was sufficiently large enough to hold our things for a week, the bathroom is gorgeous....overall it is a well planned out space for a city hotel. We were offered a choice of the 9th or 2nd floor upon check in and were told that we would have more natural light on the 9th floor. We were also advised that Haven, the rooftop bar, was just above us and that we "probably wouldn't be disturbed" by the noise. Hmmm. It did get loud in room 907. They woke us up two nights in a row dragging furniture across the floor at nearly 2 am. I finally, grumpily, stomped upstairs to complain. They were mortified and apologized profusely (I probably scared the hell out of them). They were very sweet and one of the guys even had me point out where our room was so they would be quieter! After this we were able to sleep fairly soundly in the room after about 11pm. I think it just is what it is. They have a fabulous rooftop bar. If you think the noise will be too much, ask for a lower floor. I don't think there's much they can do about it.
Cleanliness~ Absolutely pristine. I will say the only staff we had issues with was housekeeping (one of the maids snapped at my daughter when we asked for clean towels...she was very fortunate I didn't get her name or else I would have been downstairs at the front desk in an instant) but they still do an excellent job. 
Haven Bar~ Fun. Beautiful. Friendly. Make sure you make a trip up to the rooftop to enjoy the music, the view, and a drink. Absolutely worth it. A wonderful place to slip up to after dinner in the city. I liked the bar inside the hotel as well. There they would show old, romantic movies like "An Affair to Remember" on a huge screen. And Dean Martin and Frank Sinatra are mixed in with more contemporary easy jazz singers all day long....Sigh. Such wonderful touches.
Breakfast~ The girls who serve at breakfast are amazing! They never falter at bringing you what you need or request with a smile. They dash around in these cute little black dresses as unobtrusively as possible. Never was a coffee urn empty or the pastry tray not filled...fabulous. They have bagels, bread, hard boiled eggs, pastries, a little cereal...and apples, oranges, bananas....I would suggest that maybe some Greek yogurt and granola or other kinds of fruit would be a nice change sometimes. But then again we were there for a full week. At any rate the breakfast was always plentiful and the coffee was always fresh and strong...great way to start the day.
Service~ I saved the best for last. Where to start? Let's see. There is, of course, Jacob the concierge, who would toil and hustle to get Broadway tickets or restaurant reservations or bus passes....I swear, the man is a walking encyclopedia of New York City. He has contacts all over the place and is so easy to talk to about different options for entertainment (and an occassional burst of a Gershwin tune). Also Jimmy, his sidekick at the front desk, whose droll English humor (wicked man) always made me laugh. I loved interacting with the staff....And there's Julio and the other doormen who made the place feel as safe as Fort Knox....Freddie, Brandon, Lauren....everyone was so sweet and helpful. Marta gave me written directions for the subway to Greenpoint, a Polish neighborhood in Brooklyn and we found it with no troubles. They really made our stay special. 
When we were on the plane home I mentioned to my daughter that we might want to stay closer to Greenwich Village on our next stay in NYC but she firmly said "No". It's the Sanctuary Hotel or nowhere for her. This coming from a teen that I thought was happy just having her daily glass of milk and cinnamon roll for breakfast and free wi-fi. But then just yesterday she said wistfully, "Do you remember Jacob at the hotel? Wasn't he nice? Wasn't everyone nice? It was so pretty. Don't you miss it there?" Yeah. I really do.

title: “The beds are the best!”
text: We stayed at this hotel for the White Rock Marathon in December of 2008. There were a lot of people, but we did not hear a lot of noise from our room. The room was huge, and the bathroom was nice. However, adjusting the temperature of the water for the shower was very tricky; the handle was very sensitive. Room service was pricey, but what do you expect? It's room service! The best thing about this hotel was the bed. It has to be the move comfortable one I've ever slept on!

title: “A "Downtown Delight" in D-Town”
text: The Hotel was in a good location downtown not far from "Greektown".We had a good view over the city.The rooms are beautifully decorated and spacious with huge beds and huge T.V.'s.The breakfast is buffet style and very fresh and well laid out.The staff are helpfull and friendly.The valet parking guys were great.We ate out in Greektown at the "Grapevine" restaurant which was busy and the food was good.We also ate at Fishbone's Rhythm Kitchen Cafe.The food was excellent.Both restaurants are within short walking distance of the Hotel and were safe to walk from even at night.We also ate outside at the stylish Rhino Bar next door where there was live music and the patio was lit up with lanterns and torches, wonderful as we were yards to the hotel!We also met some great people in Detroit on our travels and can't wait to go back.Give it a try!(tip....book online with hotel for great rates)

title: “Cheap, Clean, Nice, Good location, FREE parking”
text: This is a nice place for the budget. Friendly staff, close to cable car, right on Lombard street. I would stay there again.

title: “Disappointed”
text: I've stayed in other Omni Hotels across the country and have had good experiences. But this hotel is really not up to the standard I've experienced at other Omni Hotels. The rooms need to be upgraded. The furniture is very worn. The hot tubs (both indoors and outdoors) were not hot at all. They were lukewarm. The pool was incredibly crowded and not anything special. Every website I looked at has this hotel as a four star hotel. It is not that at all.

title: “huge factory”
text: we stayed there from 31st october to 8th november (2 adults with 2 children ) to run the NY marathon. Great city will certainly visit again. NY is definitly a city to visit with your children (ours are aged 8 and 10) but be prepared to walk a lot - don't miss out on walking all along broadway - you'll see the city through all its different areas and oh so many cultures - just lovely. We never felt unsecure. The hotel is huge - does its thing but nothing more. Re the elevators : still long wait but fortunatly we only stayed on the 14th floor (room 1425) room was ok (changed from 1411 no problem to change) but friends who stayed on 45th floor had a much longer wait - use the escalators (but during our stay 2 of them broke down for 3 days ) to avoid the hassle from 8th to groundfloor; Perfectly located but we will never again stay in a hotel with so many rooms - hotel is not cosy it's a factory - convention hotel - but ok - staff did its job well.

title: “Great stay”
text: Stayed for a week, good location. Clean tidy room, not the biggest room ever but what I would expect in New York. Not situated directly on Times Square but just a short walk. Staff helpful and happy. Would stay again and would recommend.

title: “First trip to Seattle!”
text:
Stayed two nights at the Sheraton while up in Seattle from LA for a friends wedding. Let me just start by saying this, I'm no usually a big fan of major chain hotel companies; the Marriott's, Sheraton's, and IHG's, but it was a tremendous hotel. 
Pros: Service & Great Concierge team, Great Chef Concierge. High floor swimming pool, jacuzzi, and huge fitness center overlooking the city. Very clean rooms and public area's. Location. In-Room Coffee!
Cons: None that I can think of...

title: “Great short stay”
text:
On this trip I was only staying one night as a sort of stop over on my way to East Hampton. I picked it for the price (I got a good rate, about $240, including tax), and the location. There are a ton of different subway lines all within two blocks, which makes it easy to get to any part of the city. There's also a Hampton Jitney stop about 3 blocks over at 3rd Ave, which was easy to walk to. 
Check-in: Was quite efficient. The room they allocated me didn't have a soaking tub (one of the deciding factors in staying here), but the clerk said he would see what he could do and they held my bags for me (I got into the city at about 1pm, so I wasn't expecting my room to be ready right away). When I got back to the hotel around 5 my room was ready-with a tub!- and they had someone bring my bags up within ten minutes. 
My Queen (805) room didn't have a view, but I wasn't really expecting one, and certainly didn't need one when I was only staying one night. It did have a little non-functioning terrace and high wall, which still let in light yet provided some privacy and seemed to block the noise quite well. The room was clean and cool, with a nice desk and flat screen. The bathroom rivaled those of some five-star hotels in the city that are nearly twice what I paid here (I'm thinking of the Mark on the UES and Trump Soho). Gorgeous tub, large separate shower, two fluffy robes and lovely Molton Brown amenities. And this is in their lowest room category!
I didn't end up going to the Happy hour provided in the Cellar Bar so I can't comment on that. There were two lovely chocolates waiting for me in my room, and when a maid came for turn-down service (I said no, I was already in my pjs, though next time I travel somewhere I need to arrange a turn-down time in advance!), she gave me another two! 
Check-out the next morning was quick and efficient, they offered to get me a taxi or hold my bags again, even though I didn't need to, and let me go with a bottle of water. 
The only nit-picky thing I could say was that I had to open the front doors myself. Now I'm not some delicate princess, but with a small suitcase and overnight bag plus purse, it certainly would have made my life a little easier. That is literally the only downside to my stay. I would definitely stay here again, even for a longer visit.

title: “Lovely old world charm”
text: Loved this old hotel. Huge rooms ! Great price and warm and friendly staff. Would stay again and the location is fantastic. Grab the $4 breakfast, wow !

title: “Welcomed back with a plate of truffles...”
text: Welcomed back with a plate of truffles and choc. covered strawberries. Awesome! Left my jewelery in our room before moving to the club level. Got a phone call as we were moving in, security brought all my jewelery to our room. I'm amazed and relieved that I even saw it again. I didn't know I had even left it and they had already called us.Best service, friendly and great food and wine. Will only stay here if I go to San Francisco again!

title: “Better then expected.”
text: We were very worried about this place, because of all the negative reviews, bugs, etc. We really had no problems here. It is a budget hotel, so do not expect more than that. The room was small, but the bed was comfotable enough. There was a November blizzard raging outside, but we were plenty cozy. Staff were helpful with restaurant picks. It is a decent location for lower manhatten. We walked to the World trade center location, ran to Battery Park, etc. Good subway connections within a few hundred yards of the hotel.

title: “Not clean”
text: I stayed at this hotel because it was the closest to my relatives home. I read good reviews about this hotel from this website. The horrific part about this stay was I found a bug on my bed. When I contacted the front desk she explained its because they had military people and Japanese businessmen that stayed there. I informed her that every time I've stayed at hotels, and I do travel quite a bit, I have never discovered a bug in my room. I didn't think that excused them from not properly cleaning up their hotel especially at the amount I paid each night. I will not stay here again.

title: “Excellent Stay- Hotel shuttle made it easy to get around”
text:
While this hotel may be located a distance from the convention center area- the shuttle service made it so easy to go back and forth to the convention center multiple times a day. Our favorite shuttle driver was Johnny... He really knew a lot about Phoenix and recommended some great things to do.
The hotel itself was very pretty. The glass elevators make the mundane activity of riding an elevator a breathtaking adventure. There were so many pretty plants in the hotel and they were real plants. The koi pond was very calming to look at. 
Hotel gym was pretty small, but they had passes to a larger gym if you were interested. I didn't go because I was happy with the cardio machines located on-site. 
The rooms were very comfortable. Having all of that space made the stay very relaxing for two colleagues to share the room while attending the convention. 
Everyone at the front desk was really helpful and kind. They recommended some great restaurants within the shuttle range too.
I would definitely stay here again. This was a great experience and home away from home for the five nights I was there.

title: “Got used to it”
text:
Let me start by saying that my wife and I weren't expecting the Waldorf. This is a discount inn in the middle of Manhattan and there are bound to be a few issues to deal with. We found the staff to be helpful and pleasant, but were disappointed when we were assigned a basement room that afforded a view similar to that found from the front window of the "Cheers" television show. The room was small and the bed considerably smaller than the queen we thought we had reserved. A queen wouldn't have fit into that room. Being the basement, the room also would have beern interesting had we been plumbers since the drop ceiling couldn't hide all of the pipes. On the positive side, the room had a great bathroom--huge shower, nicely tiled. We found the room to be clean. Being from a small town, New York street noise took a little getting used to, as did the FIRM bed. But we were there five days and grew accustomed to the place. Another positive about the inn, is the location. Being near the intersection of Lexington and 30th St., it's midway between downtown and midtown. We walked to many of the sights and the subway is close by. Breakfast comes in the form of a voucher to the corner deli/grocery.
We agreed that we'd stay there again, although we'd probably like to move up a couple of floors.

title: “smokey Residence Inn Dupont Circle”
text:
We stayed at the Dupont Circle Residence Inn in Feb. 2007. Stayed for 4 nights. This hotel is supposed to be ALL NON- SMOKING, but it apparantly does not enforce the rule. At times when the hotel was busy - early morning and in the evening we could clearly smell cigarette smoke, mostly in the bathroom. The management did offer to move us to another room. Well, we were hopeful that the offender would check out. We should have moved to another room. There was no smell of smoke in the hallways and I guess the hotel could not figure it out. There is a resturant below the rooms, so maybe it came from there.
 I have a breathing condition so it was unpleasent. Otherwise the room was very good. Quite clean. It was kind of noisy cause it is on a main street. Free parking - though we did not have a car. The cost was reasonable for the room. The breakfast and afternoon snacks were pretty good. Easy access to the public transportation/ subways. Stores and restrurants in area were good. Interesting sight seeing just on the way to the subway! There was a very good Thia place a couple of doors down. It was tucked into a basement so easy to walk by, but not to be missed. Wish I could remember the name.

title: “Another Kimpton gem”
text:
I'm a big fan of Kimpton Hotels, and so I am inclined to give positive reviews of their properties, but the Serrano really shines with friendly, helpful front desk staff and a very cozy atmosphere. The big, decorated Christmas in the middle of the lobby creates a great first impression. As other guests have said, the lobby is beautiful, full of comfortable couches and seats and perfect for relaxing during their daily hosted wine receptions or reading the free New York Times over coffee during the daily free coffee service. Jasper's restaurant also is a comfortable, casual bar-restaurant with very good food. There was a great, boisterous, and joyful crowd in Jasper's during a Monday night football game, and even eating alone I was having a good time. I have no doubt that some rooms in this typical-for-Kimpton converted older hotel are small, but my corner room was huge and light-filled. My only complaint was that the selection of basic cable did not include HBO. I had a small sad over that.
I have to comment on the Serrano's location on the edge of the Tenderloin. As a 6 foot tall guy, I never felt at all insecure walking near the hotel, and if you only head to the east or north of the hotel, there should be no problem. Unlike other reviewers, I never saw anyone actually smoking crack near the hotel. In addition, there was a doorman at the front door every time I was there. Undoubtedly, a single woman would not want to head west from the hotel into the Tenderloin, but Union Square, with thousands of tourists, excellent restaurants, and world-class shopping, is only two blocks east of the hotel. For me, the bottom line is that this is a very nice Kimpton hotel, with excellent service, and hopefully people won't pass it over because it is on the edge of, but not in, a rough neighborhood.

title: “Great experience”
text:
I stayed at this hotel last month. I didn't want to pay a lot for a downtown hotel and parking. I had to do some training near Petco park. The hotel is conveniently located next to the the 163 freeway and getting to downtown in the morning and evening was easy.
From check-in to check-out everything went well at this hotel. The receptionists were friendly and efficient. The room was nice and clean. The beds are wobbly but comfortable. The area surrounding the hotel is safe and kind of commercial (lots of other hotels/restaurants/etc)
Probably the best part of my stay was the breakfast. They had a full hot breakfast with do-it-yourself waffles, eggs, sausage, fruit, cereal, drinks. If you get down to the breakfast area when it opens at 6, there are not many other people. Breakfast is open from 6-10am.
I hate writing reviews but I feel that this hotel and staff did a great job and I will stay there again in the future.
Thanks

title: “”
text: Annmara did an great job.she know how to give the best service. The old fashion way. The hotel needs more people like her.

title: “Terrific location”
text: Not only is this hotel lovely, with super-friendly and helpful staff, but it's also in a prime location if you're visiting some of the best tourist spots in D.C. I walked to the mall from here and visited two of the Smithsonian museums on the mall and my feet survived! This is a great hotel for tourists and in addition to being walking distance from the mall, it's also close to a metro station. And it's in a very historic building. Wonderful!

title: “Top floor and Hilton VIP lounge is nice”
text:
The top floors have a good view and the Hilton Honors lounge in the evenings is a great place to have a snack, or a drink and see the city as the sun sets. Good quality rooms and furniture and a very good location is that only 3 or 4 blocks away from the Westlake shopping center.
The only odd complaint is that union workers were very bothersome outside when we checked in. I think this problem will go away, but they kept pestering us to check out and boycott the hotel. They were very agressive and troublesome.

title: “Perfect for our trip, nice upgrades”
text: Loved our room, the amenities, the hospitality hour and even the breakfast got approval from our group. The yellow line bus/trolley comes every 15 minutes and takes you to all the attractions in San Antonio. Catch the bus right across the street. We will be back here!

title: “Sleeping in Seattle......”
text: This hotel was our top pick to stay when we visited Seattle. We liked everything, from the service, cleanliness, convenience to the space needle, and especially to the bakery (Nielsens Bakery for the Snitters). The beds were comfy and we had an excellent night's sleep before our flight back to the east coast. This place was almost perfect except for the internet service. I just gave up trying to connect from my laptop since the signal was very weak from our room. I wound up using my Droid instead.

title: “Excellent! simple, good value, clean, great location”
text: I usually stay at this hotel when I come to Seattle. It is in a great shopping area and close to the airport. I have stayed here maybe a dozen or more times over the last 5 years. I first started using this hotel because my dog was welcome. It also offer a great breakfast. The service is great and the staff is friendly and helpful. It is very clean.

title: “Excellent choice!!! - Will stay there again!!!”
text:
The Elan Hotel is a nice hotel with a very friendly and helpful staff. The room was comfortable and had a save, iron + board, minibar (very important and you can lock it), big TV Flat Screen, iPod docking station with alarm and radio, a lot of space where you can store your clothes and luggage, the best hairdryer ever, a balcony door, enough towels (big, middle and small) and it was perfectly clean.
Great bonus is the breakfast: great coffee, tea, orange juice, bagels, muffins, croissants, etc (from Wolfgang Puck) just delicious!
As it's a business hotel you can meet in the lobby with your business partners or use the conference room. 
If you need a taxi or any other kind of transportation (limousine, sedan, etc.): The front desk staff is always helpful and organize a driver and if you go to a place like venice you get a special price.
At 5pm-7pm they have a wine & cheese reception to meet people and relax yourself - it's free!
The area around is good and there are a lot stores and restaurants in the Beverly Center, also Subway Sandwich, Starbucks, Coffee & Beans and Taco Bell as CVS are in walking distance. 
To get to the Farmes Market & The Grove or Whole Food (supermarket) take the bus line 14 or 16 (14 comes more often and it's the fastest way) there are also shopping possibilities (Zara, Nordstrom, lots of eating, etc)
We were very happy and had a great stay and will definitely stay there again!!!

title: “Very disappointed”
text: We booked this hotel through Hotwire for a great rate. Had we not received suc a great rate I would have been even more disappointed with our stay. The pool was being renovated, but we were not informed of this thru Hotwire or the direct website. We did not find that out until we checked in. The TV was constantly freezing, which made it impossible to watch. The water was extremely loud...we knew when the people in the room next to us washed their hands or went to the bathroom because the pipes were so loud. The staff were not very helpful regarding the quickest way to get most places. For example, they did not inform us of the free trolley we could take to navy pier. The restaurants on site were very over priced. We also saw tons of dirty trays left outside of rooms for days. The view wasn't great, the parking was shady, and the empty, ugly lot in front of the hotel was a turn off. I wont stay here again. It is not family friendly and much more of a business hotel.

title: “A wonderful surprise”
text:
After reading the reviews I was very nervous that the hotel would be an old noisey uncomfortable place. When we arrived we were wonderfully surprised! The hotel had an elegant feel, with a nice lobby. We requested 2 rms with 2dbl beds each away from expressway. When we arrived they only had one room w/ 2dbl beds and a corner room near expressway. The corner room was great! It was like a mini suite with separate sitting room and sleeping area. There was some noise from street but nothing like I was expecting, just a little background noise. The 2nd room was smaller in comparison but very comfortable with nice ammenities. Pool on 28th floor with hot tub was small but had a great view especially at night. Staff were all very accomodating and nice.
Location was okay, walking distance to most but hills were very steep so more strenuous of a walk for distance.
Would definitley stay again and would reccomend it.

title: “Excellent Location and Primo Staff”
text: This Candlewood Suites hotel was nicer than any that I have ever stayed in! It is like a palace as it sits on top of a limestone hill. I did a job in Bulverde and this hotel was the nicest and best value for the area! The outdoor pool was sparkling and enjoyed every day after work. The entire staff was accommodating and worked around my schedule to see to it my room was cleaned weekly. I worked odd and inconsistent hours, but I was always looked after and treated perfectly by all the staff. I stayed at the hotel with another business partner for over a month. It was a great stay and I recommend this hotel for any long stay. Kudos to the team on nice people that keep the hotel clean and comfortable.

title: “My Favorite Hotel in DC! 5 Star Service from the Front Desk”
text: My experience at this hotel was fantastic! The hotel is beautiful and the staff are great most especially CJ at the front desk. He is very knowledgeable and went above and beyond our expectations. Upon mentioning that we came from CA. He graciously suggested some good restaurants, museums and shopping centers in the area. For somebody who does not have a clue in the area, the information provided by CJ is very helpful especially with my kids around. He even called the next day and ask how everything went. The whole family enjoyed the stay and we are definitely coming back in DC before the year ends! Kudos to the wonderful staff of Embassy Suites!

title: “Great location, nice hotel”
text:
Great location for a family. Very short walk to Fishermans wharf and Ghiradelli Square. Rooms were very clean, bathroom sink area a little small.
Staff very helpful and pleasant

title: “Very nice”
text: We stayed 3 nights over presidents day weekend. Hotel is very clean, rooms nicely decorated. The room was typical in size although we were told it was an upgraded room and larger than most, king bed and sleep sofa. I do recommend requesting a higher floor as the noise from the street can be a bit loud, In fact when we checked in the desk clerk made the suggestion. Location was great, easy access to the metro just 1 block up. My only complaint was the breakfast set up. Very small area for the amount of people in the hotel. Imagine aprox50 people in a 12x12 room trying to get breakfast, then try to find a place to sit. Just doesn't work never mind the people picking food up with there hands then putting it back, coughing and sneezing on the food too.....well you get the picture. All and all the hotel is great just skip the breakfast

title: “A cool unique hotel, but not completely comfortable”
text:
I stayed here for 4 nights. The hotel occupies half of an old train station. The other half is still a working train station. Because of this you will hear the train running and noise could be a problem if you are sensitive to it. it did not bother me much, and I thought it was actually kind of cool. I stayed in one of the train car rooms and that is a unique experience. An old train car is divided into two rooms. It is obviously a little smaller than the other rooms and is long and narrow. I had a king bed in my room, and there was about a foot or two of space from the foot of the bed and the wall. I like trains and enjoyed my stay there. 
Although not uncomfortable, you do give up some comforts at this hotel. There are no external facing windows in any of the rooms. Every room has a window, but they all face the lobby or the hall way. That was my main complaint with this hotel, but being that it is located in a train station, it is to be expected. 
The pool is OK, about what you would expect from a Crowne Plaza hotel. Service is good, as is the restaurant. I had breakfast there every morning. 
All in all, I would recommend this hotel as it is very unique. However, I would not recommend staying there for an extended amount of time.

title: “Find another hotel”
text: This was the 4th W hotel I have stayed in over the last 4 weeks and by far was not up to standard. Checked in and the room which was an upgraded room was small, musty and extremely hot (air would not cool down). Checked out within an hour and went to the Westin on 42nd street.... Much better choice. The manger for this W has moved and is now at the Westin. If you want a W in NYC stay in Times Square.

title: “perfect location”
text: the best thing about this hotel was its location near alot of activities and metro thought the lobby needed alot more natural light, even though it was large, it felt like a cave the room was large for nyc but the bathroom could've been alot better the door was a sliding barn type door with glass which threw alot of light into the bedroom if you were trying to sleep also, there was no area around the sink to put toiletries and their case the toilet was an airline type flush which could wake the dead while it might look stylish it was not practical

title: “renaissance marriott downtown”
text:
My husband and I stayed here for 5 nights - he attended a conference (great location for that) and I was on my own. First impressions weren't great. Receiptionist at booking wasn't friendly whatsoever - bad day or something and that set the tone. She was very distant. THEN there was Floyd - a porter. He made up for everything. Couldn't have had more personality.
Room was satisfactory - nothing more. TV sucked - needed to have someone come in to fix it. Getting rooms cleaned was a big 'production' at times and always someone knocking and checking up on cleaning staff. 
Gym and pool were alright. We stayed on 5th floor so that was convenient. As well, they checked us in early without making a big issue - that was great, and let us stay 2 hours later - that was great as well. Very accomodating
Best secret was restaurant - Steve's across the street - down one block. Awesome in every way. American cooking - relaxed.
 ..Sad part is - there is nothing going on downtown. Very little shopping to be had. Wednesdays (4 - 8 pm) Saturday mornings 8 - 12) there was a fun market. Enjoyed that. Lots of homeless meandering around so I didn't always feel safe. Merchants hired people in orange shirts (forget name) community hosts were everywhere to offer assistance in any way - info - a walk somewhere, etc. Great strategy. Some day the downtown will be totally wonderful again. For now - they are trying to make downtown come alive again.

title: “Loved restaurant and service!”
text: Stayed next door but ate at restaurant. Loved Moises our waiter. Service was impeccable and sandwich was tastey!

title: “PLENTY TO SEE AND DO IN THE HEART OF THE FINANCIAL DISTRICT”
text: The Hilton hotel in the heart of San Francisco's Financial District is a wonderful place to stay. Whether you are on vacation or travelling for business the accomodations are well above average and extremely comfortable. The staff throughout the hotel are very courteous and always willing to assist you with all of your needs. All of the sights and sounds of San Francisco are easily accessed from the financial district. If you prefer to stay in the hotel the food and beverage service available is excellent. The business center is always clean and available 24/7 as well as the exercise facility. There is also a list of spa services available though I have never tried any. The financial district is a great area with San Francisco and the Hitlton is an outstanding value for the price.

title: “Good, but...”
text:
