Based on reviews here and elsewhere online, I stayed at the Enclave for three nights last week. Con - My room was somewhat small, and did not have a loft ceiling or a jacuzzi tub. When I inquired about this, I was told that these are only found in one of the six suites, not in most of the other Enclave rooms. I believe there are 30 total. Other than a bath robe, the amenities were standard-issue, not luxury. The only mirror was in the bathroom. 
Pro - The bed was comfortable and the room was quiet. Good location.

title: “Thanks Westin Galleria - for nothing”
text:
We were staying Saturday 1/16/10 to Monday 1/18/10 because I was running in the Houston Marathon on 1/17/10. At 12:15 AM the morning of the race, we were awakened in our room by extremely loud music coming from somewhere in the hotel. At 12:45 we were finally moved to a room 14 stories down from our original room where we could still feel the base from the music vibrating through the walls. I finally got back to sleep around 2:30 AM but had to wake up at 5:00 AM for the marathon. The race was much harder than it should have been after months of training due to my complete lack of sleep the night before. My wife and I had planned on staying through Monday, but we left on Sunday to go home because we were both so exhausted from lack of sleep. We spoke with the manager before leaving and he apologized and said the music was coming from a party that was supposed to end at midnight but didn't end until after 2:00 AM. Why would anyone ever okay a party that loud at a business where people are literally paying money to sleep? And then how would they be surprised when it got out of hand? 
Our weekend away was completely ruined by the Westin's complete disregard for our comfort. I would never recommend this hotel, or any Westin, even to my worst enemy after this experience.

title: “Great place to go with friends”
text:
Came here for stag do, and there was about 12 of us, and this place was AWESOME lovely rooms better then what i thought, if your tourist this is perfect too and if your looking for posh side then go towards Beverly Hill 
The only let down for me was the breakfast which was not all that more of coffeee/tea and cornflakes and toast simple as that, but there is cafe outside the hotel on right who does full breakfast
But overall this is perfect location to get everwhere....and in budget

title: “Warwick, Exceptional”
text: The Warwick, New York was beautiful top to bottom. Beautiful suite, remodeled dining room, attentive friendly staff, great mid-town location. A great experience.

title: “Outstanding Hotel!”
text: The Hotel Helix is just great! The staff and service are wonderful, the beds are very comfortable, and the rooms are quiet. Our five year old daughter really enjoyed staying there, too; the woman at the front desk was very friendly and made us all feel welcome. My husband and I appreciated the staff's help and courtesy. We highly recommend this hotel and look forward to staying there again in the future.

title: “I see why they're renovating.”
text:
Just got back from a night at this hotel, and I can see why they are in the midst of a renovation. Clearly, we stayed in one of the older rooms. The beds were just OK, but the pillows need replacing. The bath was split, with the vanity being perfectly acceptable and the bath being perfectly in need of repair. Old grout had been given a top coat, and that top coat was falling off, exposing mildew-laced grout in much more than one spot. The bathroom floor had stains, and the push-style drain plug was found to be broken off and not accommodating to a quick repair. 
The rest of the room was pretty standard with some almost character-giving quirks to the layout. Surprisingly low ceilings and a CRT-style television round out the notable features. 
Outside the room, amenities appear to abound through the lobby, with multiple dining locations and a nice-looking pool and patio. Front desk staff was courteous, if informal (which I don't personally mind). 
The east tower underground parking garage does not seem to have been planned for the purpose of parking cars in an efficient manner. There are support columns in every other space, and drivers of larger vehicles will find the task challenging, to put it mildly.
It has potential. I might be willing to give it another go after the renovations have been completed. But currently, I am certain that better deals are to be had.

title: “Great time at hyatt Penn”
text: Having traveled innumerable times and being a hyatt gold member I had to write a review as it seemed that so many people bad mouthed this place. First of all hyatt has repeatedly gotten my business as they truly value me as customer. Every time I have asked for A certain request they have granted it. Regarding this hyatt it is I would say it is a solid 4 star. Had a corner room with nice view of delaware river. The hotel itself is next to society hill area where a great deal of nice chic restaurants. The pool has a nice turquoise shimmer and nice view of Delaware and despite other grips by other trip advisor peeps the pool is great (not best pool I have ever seen but good pool) overall nice stay and best part got priceline rate of 100/night

title: “A really bad start....improved along the way.”
text:
We had a very bad start to our stay. We arrived at 2:30pm, but rooms weren't ready for an early check-pin; no problem, check-in wasn't until 3pm anyway. By 3pm, however, rooms still were not ready for us and several other customers. Most of us waited in the lobby for about an hour for the staff to finish cleaning rooms from the night before. This was especially tough with a baby in tow. To make matters worse, the front desk associate, Michael (Mike), showed little concern as everyone waited. He became even less helpful later, when my wife inquired about the crib that we had requested in advance. He said that the hotel had no cribs, and when my wife pressed him on this, he insisted that he was positive they don't have cribs. Finally, he asked someone in the back if they did, and they said, "Of course we have cribs!" Our interaction with Mike scarred our experience, even though the rest of the staff were helpful and friendly through the remainder of the stay. I never saw him greet or smile at anyone.
Regarding the delayed check-in, the staff were just unprepared for the arrival of a convention the week of July 15. Shannon was polite and offered an apology when we checked out, but no compensation or concession was provided for the late check-in.
The room was fine, with only a couple of annoyances (no mirror besides the bathroom mirror, and no tub....just a shower). The bed was good. The room seemed clean. We had a persistent problem with our room keys (cards) losing their programming and having the front desk reprogram them.
Parking was $12/day self-park, but I had found a Comfort Inn a block over that was $5/day in-and-out.
Breakfast was great, and the staff very helpful: eggs, sausage, yogurt, bagels, muffins, belgian waffles, etc.
Great location right with a small park in front of and also behind the hotel.

title: “Clean, well maintained, and amazing location”
text:
We stayed here for two nights, and we were really pleases with the cleanliness and location of the hotel when we arrived there after 8 hours drive. The hotel was out of our budget but we decided to book it since we were gonna be in NYC for only to days and we wanted to be in the middle of the action, we were not disappointed.
Having the complimentary breakfast was a bonus and it helped us getting through the day, although the variety is basic but we were satisfied. As some others mentioned the elevators are really slow but i guess that comes with a tall and busy hotel. we stayed on the 28th floor and the room was quiet and we could almost here no sound from the street below.
TIP: if you are gonna drive park in the ICON parking lot about two blocks east and when you are checking out ask the front desk to stamp your parking receipt, you will get a big discount from the parking facility.

title: “No complaints at all”
text: I stayed at La Quinta for 7 nights with my girlfriend last month and have no complaints about the hotel. Location is perfect, room was small but very clean, bathroom too, staff was friendly and helpful, nice rooftop bar, great complimentary breakfest, free wireless internet access. Would definately stay again and recommend to my friends.

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text:
My husband and I stayed here from the 23rd of August until the 30th. I was a bit worried about what to expect after reading mixed reviews. Check in time was 3pm but our room was ready at 1.30pm when we arrived. The hotel lobby is stunning. Our room was a petite room but it was actually very big, it was spotless and the bed was very comfortable. Workmen needed to fix a pipe in our bathroom so the Manager gave us a free breakfast which was great. The maid also broke our phone charger by accident but the hotel offerred us free late check out time which suited us great as check out was 12 and we did not leave for the airport until 4pm.
The staff were very nice and the maids were lovely. The lifts were a bit busy in the morning but fine any other time. The hotel is very central to everything. The food court around the corner for the hotel is good for breakfast. There are lots of eating places nearby and lots of Irish bars/restraunts.
I would highly reccommend drinks in the revoloving lounge in the Mariot at Times Square. China Town is definitely an experience.
Overall I would highly reccomment this hotel and would not listen to any of the bad reviews. I would go back to the Roosevelt in a flash.

title: “Best New York Stay Ever”
text:
My partner and I travelled to New York on the 19th of November. We arrived to the affinia hotel after 6pm staff at the reception were so nice and porters were most helpful. I was amazed to see how spacious our room was it was fab for 5 nights. We were so near times square and macys it was great. we walked everywhere great exercise!! The male conceirge was most helpful he booked tickets to go see the lion king for us and helped us make a reservation at the marriott revolving restaurant in times square, which to me was a total surprise as what i didn't know at the time it would be to celebrate our engagement.
i would definatly recommend this hotel for business/ shopping/ romantic get aways. lovely hotel. only thing is food expensive i.e. breakfast best eating at the euro cafe about 500 m from the hotel.

title: “Nice clean hotel”
text:
My son and I were visiting colleges in San Diego and this is where we stayed. It's located conveniently close to I-5 on the north end of San Diego which was nice since we were driving south from the Bay area and didn't have to drive through downtown at night.
The room was clean and the toiletries were basic. The beds were acceptable. Free wi-fi was helpful. The complementary breakfast was very nice which included both hot and cold choices.
There is a Chili's Restaurant located across the parking lot which was nice for one evening of not wanting to drive anywhere.

title: “Great Location--Recommend for Hip Leisure Travelers in young 20s-30s”
text:
First time at the W--heard about the beach bar (seems like a favorite of locals). Didn't find service there (at the bar) to be great and they needed some umbrellas for shade, but thought hotel staff in general were very friendly and knowledgeable. 
Everything was a bit smallish--pool area, bar, fitness center and rooms, but very creative feel to it.
My favorite 2 things--free coffee in the morning and sitting on the comfy cushions along the window sill in my room reading a magazine and looking out into the city.

title: “Made Great Pals with the Palomar”
text: They really take care of you here. From Darren, the friendly face at the front door, to the concierge staff who can get you in anywhere you can really get spoiled here. Like all the Kimpton Hotels, there's lots of extra touches, like the manager's wine party every night. And jars of jelly beans in the afternoons. Take advantage of the upgrade offer when you book- for a few bucks more, if available when you show up, you can get a suite. Ours was enormous, and it came in handy. Even though my husband and I were on a short vacay, we both had to do a few conference calls. With two rooms, we almost did not get on each other's nerves. My only issue with this hotel is the slightly noisy heat/ac. Not a huge deal, though. And don't bother with the bar downstairs, there's an excellent dive bar across the street called Snickers. Don't let the homeless drunks peppered in with football fans fool you- Snickers is stocked with high end tequillas and vodkas. And all sorts of microbrews.

title: “Don't go there”
text:
The place consist of two parts: hotel and hostel. I stayed for 2 nights in hostel in 2-beded dorm. At first sight the hostel looked good. It had an attractive and nice decoration. The stuff is nice and helpful. The room was tiny and beside the bunk bed there was some kind of closet and a TV. The bathrooms were clean and generally ok, however there was only the one shower per storey - it was definitely not too much!
If you expect any kitchen - forget it. There are no kitchen facilities except of a single microwave oven.
And at the end, the worst thing - I saw several times the mices running in my room!
IMO - The place is not worth staying there. It is expensive (I paid 60$/night) and doesn't offer anything more then overnight. If you would like to stay in Chelsea, better go to "Chelsea International Hostel", just few blocks away. You will get there better service and pay less.

title: “Not A Great Hotel”
text: We've stayed at Loews Hotels on several occasions and this Loews doesn't match up. I understand they just took over the property several months ago, but based on the room, it shouldn't be given 4 stars. The bathroom does not have an exhaust, the bathroom door was broken and we were not given enough towels and cups for 4 people in the room (left with 3 towels and 2 cups). Maintenance came up, put a tissue on the vent fan and stated the exhaust was working and all the rooms were like this. I complained to the Manager and nothing was done. We lived with wiping down the bathroom mirror after each shower and propping the door open with a sneaker. I was quite surprised the manager didn't do anything; offer another room, a credit, a breakfast, something. I did request additional towels and coffee be placed in the room daily to make our stay comfortable. I told her that 2 cups and 3 towels were not acceptable for 4 people reserved in the room. They should renovate this hotel if they want to continue to use the name Loews. I won't be recommending this Loews location!!

title: “Incredibly disappointing”
text:
I was booked at the Mosser for the Fancy Food Convention. I was there for 5 nights. The location was excellent to the Moscone Convention Center, but I quickly began looking longingly at the Marriott Marquis across the street!
The building is a lovely old Victorian furnished with shabby furniture in the lobby with no real style. The desk staff were friendly but not terribly helpful. My employer was checking in later and had made the reservations, but had not paid for them yet. They allowed me to check in, but put the first night on my credit card, plus $25??? Bizarre. No one seemed to be able to explain why and that was after I complained when they wanted to add $75 to the first night's rate.
The room was dingy, due to poor lighting. The walls had black scuff marks on them, the tub had pubic hair in it. The corner sink was impossible to use without getting water everywhere. The bath amenities were environmentally "green" and smelled like vomit. The towels were threadbare and cheap. The bedsheets did not even cover the mattress on the bottom. The windows were sealed, no air conditioning and the room was not only very noisy, but hot. Wood blinds at the windows did little to keep the room darkened and were dusty. The more modern looking platform bed was okay comfort wise, but the platform was scuffed and dirty--clearly not an area that housekeeping was interested in maintaining.
There was no clock in the room, unless I turned on the wall mounted tv (with cords falling out from behind) to see what time it was. The phone was mounted on the wall and impossible to hang up without using the cord to wrap around the entire unit to keep the receiver from falling out. It was hung too high on the wall to reach for a wake up call from the bed. The wall mounted light over the bed, was also hung in a very inconvenient area which required standing up to turn off. Both choices were poor design choices and a cheap way to avoid night stands. The night stand that was attached to the platform bed was on one side only and was broken and tilting so that items slid off when placed there.
Housekeeping was loosey goosey. The bed was never completely made up with the decorative pillows that were on the bed at check in, and the towels, as bad as they were, were never replaced in the same spot. The glasses in the bathroom, once used, were never replaced, so I had to rinse them out and use the same ones repeatedly, despite my leaving notes for housekeeping, along with a tip!
A morning breakfast of a cup of coffee and mediocre muffin was offered in the lobby with little place to sit. While the coffee seemed decent, the only offering with it was sugar or equal, and half and half. No skim or low fat milk, no honey for tea--things one can expect to find even at a cheap hotel!
Concierge service was non existent. When I requested a call to the shuttle for pickup I was told that they did not use that company and so they didn't have their number--REALLY? No computer there at the desk to look it up?! I asked for some affordable local restaurants and kept getting referred to Annabelles next door, which was pricier than I wanted. That was the only restaurant they could tell me about. I went across the street to the Marriott Marquis where their concierge not only told me about some great places close by but she provided me with a list of many options ---and I told her I wasn't even staying there!!
My overall impression of this place is that someone had a few bucks and desire to turn a beautiful old VIctorian into a trendy boutique hotel and then they went off to travel or do something else leaving no one in charge or accountable. Clearly the only employees who were schooled in the fine art of hospitality were Joe the bellman/doorman and his counterpart. These two gentlemen were sharp, friendly, take charge and helpful every day. 
I wouldn't go back if it was free.

title: “A Sweet Suite Hotel”
text: We loved this hotel! Recently renovated, we were pleasantly surprised by the room size-all rooms are suites and have mini kitchens, sofa beds and the bed/linens were very comfy. The staff was helpful and friendly-it was our first visit to Baltimore and they gave us a room on one of the top floors overlooking the city. Extremely clean-nice big bathroom as well. Overall I thought the Tremont was great. You can park next door at a City lot for $15/day vs. valet at $25. The hotel is about 6 blocks from Inner Harbor, but the walk was fine. Staff even provides a shuttle service to area restaraunts at no charge. I loved staying at a smaller hotel and this one was fantastic-highly reccommend!

title: “Best hotel ever”
text: Just spent 5 days at this hotel at a convention. It is quite possibly my best hotel experience ever. The staff were awesome at every level, food was excellent, and the service was impeccable. I will certainly return here, congratulations on running a great hotel, I would highly recommended this place

title: “Loved it!”
text:
Had a great stay here, and was glad to have taken the recommendations of Trip Advisor. Staff is great, from dealing with Tim in reservations, to the young curly-ish haired girl at the front desk, I felt the service was wonderful. 
Loved the decor in the rooms, and the area where breakfast, and the happy hour are held was a lovely space. They ordered a car service for us and really just made it an enjoyable trip. It really did have a calm feel to the place. Can't wait to return.

title: “A good, affordable hotel in a great location. No complaints.”
text:
The Chancellor Hotel is in a prime location at the North West corner of Union Square. It is relatively close to all transportation including the BART from the airport. Although you will have to walk several blocks with your luggage from the Powell St. Station. The cable car stops right out front. The people at the front desk are very helpful with directions and bus lines.
The hotel is very affordable compared to the others in the same neighborhood. The staff was nice and helpful. The lobby had seating, a bar and a small restaurant as well as a tour desk. I suppose the tour desk (where you could also buy public transportation passes, get airport shuttles, even water and cigarettes) was a good idea, but somehow, I thought it brought the lobby down a notch. There seemed to be free cookies and fruit in the lobby. I was too shy to ask if they were free. And there was free coffee and tea at all times. I was disappointed in the restaurant. They were out of sourdough toast for my breakfast. What’s the point of being in San Francisco if you don’t have sourdough toast?
The rooms were clean and renovated. They weren’t huge, but they weren’t ridiculously small either. The bathrooms were large enough. The hotel was fairly quiet, although I could hear my neighbor’s alarm every morning. 
The neighborhood is great, of course. There are great restaurants, a Starbucks, and a very very convenient Walgreens very close by. You will be going there a lot! Of course Union Square is known for it’s shopping. I may stay there again if I need an affordable hotel. I have no complaints.

title: “We'll be back!”
text:
My husband and I flew up from South Florida to meet my two best friends from NJ there to celebrate my 31st birthday in Chicago. The weather was suprisingly gorgeous, (high 40's low 50's) which made the short walk to Magnificent Mile from the W very pleasurable. 
The hotel seemed like the place to be. We arrived at midnight on Friday and the lobby was live w/ what looked like an afterwork crowd at the bar. Everytime you stepped out of the elevator you felt like you were at a party, or in the least a lounge. The music was not loud or overbearing as many have posted on this site. It is not a hotel I would recommend bringing your children to, and it is best suitable for anyone ranging from 23-40 who enjoys the party scene. The rooms were nice, beds and linens were very comfortable, and the bathroom was adequate (and yes the Bliss products were a total plus). The lighting was dim ( the type of lighting that makes you look flawless) which after a while can get on your nerves, but not enough to make me not want to stay here again. Back to the lobby- perfect for casual lounging while taking full advantage of their free wifi and sipping on a cocktail. The barmaids were extremely friendly and come by any part of the lobby you are in to take your order, so you don't even have to get up to go to the bar. 
 We found a great restaurant on Rush St called Heaven on Seven (Hi Mike!!) which served the best GUMBO we've yet to taste. They have an endless collection of hot sauces w/ all sorts of crazy names. They also have a great breakfast menu. 
Sears Tower was totally disappointing and was just a check on our list of things to do in Chicago. However, the corner of the Sears Tower was like a ride at Universal Studios. The wind on that corner was something fierce- we couldn't even get the cab door open, which was really strange since it wasn't windy anywhere else. 
The mall at the Water Tower Place was great. Best boot collection I've ever seen at the Lord & Taylor's there. Best deep dish pizza is hands down , Giordano's. (Pizzeria Uno- the original- doesn't carry the same menu as the franchised Uno's do, and they don't have the happy hour menu's either- in my opinion- not worth the visit). 
We found a cool Irish Sports Bar w/ great drink specials called O'tooles. 
There is a place called West Egg that seemed like a great breakfast spot- but the wait was 25 mins so we didn't eat there. The menu looked great tho, and the prices were just right. 
You have to tip the copper cowboy on Magnificent Mile to take his pic, but definitely one for the memoir books. 
We took a 10 min cab ride to the Funky Buddha Lounge, and had a blast. Great place to meet locals who can tell you about other places to check out. 
Navy Pier was nice. You feel obligated to go since the W is directly across from it, but other than the Forest Gump impersonator in front of the Bubba Gump restaurant, it wasn't no where near the highlight of my trip--although the ferry ride around Lake Michigan made for great pics. 
There is a free trolley that travels all around. Ask the concierge for the schedule and it will save you alot of time and cab money. My friends took the train from Midway and said it was really easy to figure out. We took a cab from O'hare and that ran us approx $40 w/ tip. 
Depending on what time of year you go (weather permitting) there's lots to see and do within walking distance of the W. 
On our last night there we checked out the Whiskey Bar on the 33rd floor, but it was EXTREMELY dark and SMALL. Smoking is permitted, so if you don't smoke, it's not the place for you since it's so small the cigarette smell will linger all over you. 
Last, but definitely not least for me, we visitied the Chicago Public Library. 10 Floors!!! A library enthusiasts heaven!! 
Overall, I loved Chicago. It was exactly how I pictured, full of culture and diversity and proud of their locals who flourish in the arts. I can't wait to go back and check out Bucktown and Old Town.

title: “Nothing Rosy About Roosevelt Hotel”
text: Check-in was at 3 pm and we arrived at 6pm but our room was not ready and was still being cleaned. We were given complimentary drinks at the bar and served great martinis! But our room was not ready until two and a half hours later! The luggage was never delivered to our room and we had to call to follow-up and at 11:30 pm it was finally delivered!! When we asked the porter what happened, he had no idea because he just came on the night shift. The bathroom and bedroom were small and no better than a budget hotel. The bathroom door was warped and did not close, the cold and hot water in the bathtub must have been switched because it did not work properly, the glass shelf on the mirror was broken, and there was mold along the rim of the tub and sink, and the fan was broken. At times the pressure in the toilet was low and did not flush. The only update in the bedroom was the flat screen tv and the energy saving light bulbs. The dresser drawer was broken, the bedside lamp looked like a cigarette had burned through the lamp shade, the air conditioner unit was very loud, the down comforter had no duvet cover, and there was no painting hung as advertised in the website photo but two screws were exposed. There was nothing "luxurious" about this hotel whatsoever and it was very disappointing.

title: “A Very Nice Stay”
text: We had a suite since we had six family members. The room was quite, clean and well taken care of. The room didn't smell like your typical "hotel room" it was much better. The down side was that you were charged extra to use the internet and it didn't work well. We had two laptops, a Dell and Apple so it wasn't our computers. They had to give us several codes before it worked properly. The pool was very nice and clean. The breakfast was really good,and we found the gift shop with better deals than some of the local stores. We stayed there primarily because they were on a list for Starline tours which provided shuttles to and fro. After checking out we stored our luggage in our van during the tour with no extra charge for parking. Our van and articles were safe in their secured parking garage. If I ever return to LA., I would definately stay again. It is a little pricey but again, you get what you pay for. We were very pleased.

title: “Affordable, convenient, great service”
text:
When I first began researching hotels in Chicago, I was shocked at the expensive prices of rooms downtown, and the additional expense for parking a car (sometimes $30 a day). Because of the moderate room prices and good reviews, we decided on Carlton Inn Midway and were not disappointed. It is not a new facility, but neither is it in disrepair. It is clean and with all modern conveniences, and parking is free. It has a parking lot with entrances to the rooms from the lot, but with someone in the lobby 24 hours a day it feels secure. The neighborhood is one of mixed ethnicities, with a high school right across the street and a good Greek restaurant next door. We felt safe walking around in the area. The only inconvenience is that it's a 20 to 30-minute ride on the train to downtown Chicago. You just have to plan accordingly. 
 After experiencing Chicago traffic, we decided to park our car at the inn, get a CTA 3-day pass, and take the elevated train into the city for sight-seeing. The Orange line Pulaski Station is very close by, within easy walking distance. The folks at Carlton Inn offered to take us to and pick us up from the station in their van if we didn't want to walk. They also furnished maps and information about restaurants, tours, and driving directions when we left. Everyone in the office was very friendly and helpful. 
Someone in a previous review mentioned the dog in the office. The owner's dog spends the day lying around in the office pretending to be an area rug. He's some sort of large terrier, very cute and completely passive. 
For breakfast, the sausage/egg/cheese bagels are substantial, but there are lighter offerings as well--a good selection. 
Our next trip to Chicago, even if we fly (it's one stop from Midway Airport on the train), we'll plan to stay at the Carlton Inn Midway. It's affordable, convenient, and the service is great.

title: “Service is Terrible”
text:
My review is primarily for the bar and lounge. I went with a couple of friends to the W. We were there for drinks this weekend. The menu and decor looked great. The bellhop was very well dressed and had good manners.
However, I am writing this complaint because the bartender and cocktail waitresses were horrible. First of all, the bartender gave us attitude. She was completely polite to the gentlemen next to us, who were part of the gentlemen's club yet made faces when she thought we couldn't see. The cocktail waitress was friendly, but ridiculously slow in getting back to us. We waited at least 20 minutes before getting service. On top of this, the cashier totally stole from me and my friend. 
I bought an extensive amount of alcohol beverage for my friends to drink. I normally do not drink myself but since I was staying in the W hotel, I thought I ought to enjoy my time here. 
At the end of the night, I wrote down and kept my receipts. When I got home today and was looking through my bank statement, I noticed something was amiss. ALL of my receipts from the W hotel bar and lounge were more than I wrote down for in tip. I looked again. The cashier apparently padded their tip with extra.
I had even marked down that I had left tip in CASH. I normally tip in cash to do the waitress a favor. But this is unacceptable. As far as I'm concerned skimming a little more from the top, like this, even if I can afford it, is still stealing.
I plan on telling all of my friends and coworkers not to go to the W. I am also going to file a complaint on ripoff report - As well as call the managers. I just hate it when people do stuff like this and people let them slide.
It was just a little too much. I mean if it had just been the attitude, I would say everyone has a bad day. But the fact that these girls were pretty much obnoxious and selective about who they'd help, I think they really need to be put in their place.

title: “Not entirely a Grand Hyatt...maybe a moderately OK one.”
text:
One of the most amazing things about a regal NYC hotel is its lobby - and admittedly the Grand Hyatt has a beautiful and ornate lobby. However, all of the polish and glamour soon wore off when we experienced the front lobby staff.
As we were unable to use the kiosks, we had to make way to the front desk to be assisted by a human being. What we received was a flash of hatred only experienced as an American youth traveling to Communist USSR in the early 1980s. Instead of assisting us, the front desk agent went back to her keyboard, clacking away while her knitted eyebrows told us that we were almost to the point of death should we bother her with our measly request of checking in to our hotel room.
About five minutes later, a second front desk staff member arrived, reassuring us that this was indeed the front desk, and this is where we check in. We were given our room assignment, confirmed my Hyatt Gold Passport Platinum status, and directed to the elevators. Soon, we were on our way to room 1971.
As part of Hyatt Gold Passport Platinum status, I'm supposed to get the best room available within the category booked. To all my fellow travelers, I sincerely apologize. Based on the state of my room, I would surely suggest that your rooms were scarier. 
Room 1971 featured a lovely cracked closet door, mold (not crown mold) around the door of the bathroom, and a toilet wedged between the shower and sink that required the strength and acrobatic skills of Cirque Du Soleil to use. Additionally, for all of those that dislike adjoining rooms - you had not one, but TWO adjoining rooms - one on each side of the room. Nonetheless, the King-sized bed was comfortable, and the desk area along side the TV was useful to complete work on my partner's laptop. The room also had a functional A/C and Heater, and the noise levels (as you faced 42nd Street) were almost inaudible once the window was closed.
Our further interactions with the hotel staff were just as cordial as our knitted brow friend, showing us that customer service is indeed on life support at this hotel. When we called to inquire about the correct method to use to obtain free internet, the response was "If you're Platinum, you should know." Yes, because all hotels are the same. As a FYI, When you access the T-Mobile hotspot, and enter your room number, it apparently is automatically removed from your room charges. 
Bell staff were courteous, and unlike many other NYC hotels, did not tout their friend's town cars or expect tips for helping with bags or hailing cabs. While tips were appreciated, there genuinely seemed to be some helpful staff outside of the hotel. Directions and help with getting our navigation straight was truly appreciated. This, honestly, was the saving grace of service at the hotel - otherwise it would have been a terrible experience.
With hotels fighting each other to keep in business in this economy, abusive service and rooms with cleanliness issues do not win repeat customers. Would it cost that much more to have someone fix a crack, kill some mold, and coach your front desk people to smile? The Hyatt Grand Central NYC has not won a repeat customer here.

title: “Stay elsewhere- it's still an SRO”
text:
The Jane is very cheap- no doubt about that. Location is good, lobby and bar are cute. That's where the positive aspects end. 
Stayed in a room with bunk beds and tiny doesn't even begin to describe the space. It was about 4x9 and my friend and I could hardly be in the room at the same time except to sleep. What little room there is happens to be very well designed. Don't ask me how they got the bunk beds in there.
There are shared bathrooms, which is fine if you don't mind that kind of thing. However, there are still semi-homeless people living there and the conversion from a single occupancy hotel (SRO) is still underway. 
For the price, there really are other options. Got a room for $99 at the Ace Hotel (nice beds, private bath and 6x the size) after one night at this place.

title: “Hotel Allegro is great for location and price.”
text:
The Hotel Allegro is a great deal if you can get a low rate (under $ 100) and if you are not spending a lot of time in the room. The location is great. It is in the heart of the theater district. Do not expect a good view. If you want a view, look at pricier hotels on the Mag Mile. You will most likely pay at least $200 for a view. There are several modes of transportation available, including the EL. The rooms are quite small. I would strongly suggest only two per room. The bathrooms are also very small. The room is decorated in a very funky, modern style with a music motif. The room service is fairly efficient and the honor bar is pricey but has a good selection. One word of warning: the walls are VERY thin...my husband and I woke up around 3 a.m. to the sounds of the next room's headboard slamming into the wall...no need to say more. If you have kids with you, be prepared to explain the birds and the bees! Ha! In the evenings, there is complimentary wine in the lobby. The staff is really nice and the atmosphere is great. The hotel is actually attached to the Palace theater, so you are only a few steps from a great show. If you are a couple, students, or budget-minded and you want a great hotel at a great price with a great location, then the Hotel Allegro is for you. 
Another bit of advice, if you find cheaper rates than the hotel offers, the hotel will match that other rate and upgrade you to a better room, such as a suite, just for booking directly with them.

title: “Great view - not great room”
text: Had a great view from my room, but when you are a Marriott hotel I would not expect there to have the wall paper pealing from the walls. Lobby is wonderful and the staff is very nice.

title: “Good place, good location”
text: No real bells and whistles with this hotel, but the best thing about it is the convenient location and decent price. The service is WONDERFUL here, it really is a model of what service should be. The room was clean and comfortable. There is a lot of "Hollywood" themed stuff around the hotel, which is cute. We didn't have the chance to use the pool, but they have a mini Hollywood sign out there, which is a great photo op if you're a tourist like we were. The hotel has free wifi, which is always a great plus.

title: “Friendly Staff! Nice Quaint Hotel!”
text: I have to start by saying friendly staff make a hotel very enjoyable to stay in! We arrived early in the morning by bus and got to the hotel no later then 10:00 am. Obviously we could not check in by this time however we were greeted by a very friendly staff who kindly stored our luggage for us behind the desk until our room was ready. They even went out of there way to get us some breakfast even though they had stopped serving. The Hotel is in a great location; a 2 minute walk away from Madison Square Garden and only about a 15 minute walking distance to Time Square. The hotel room is a bit on the smaller side however it did not bother me because it was a clean, cozy and comfortable room. For the price we payed we certainly found a gem at the Hampton Inn Madison Square Garden. When we return to New York we will certainly stay here again and I would recommend this hotel to anyone visitng!

title: “Where has this hotel been all my life?”
text: My husband and I just got back from a lovely 4-day stay at this hotel in San Francisco. I must admit, I'd never heard of Club Quarters but I booked it through Hotwire for a great rate for San Francisco. Well, this one's a keeper - will definitely go back to this place again and again. The location was ideal - we were able to pretty much walk most everywhere. The hotel itself is in a nice, safe, clean location in the Financial District, close to several colorful pubs and a mall across the street that had a Landmark movie theater showing some interesting indie/art films. You can also almost see Chinatown, it's that close. And since that's one of our favorite places, we were delighted. The hotel is also very close to the Embarcadero, which you can follow all the way around to Fisherman's Wharf. We thought it might be a bit of a walk, but were pleasantly surprised at how close we actually were. The only thing we took a cab ride to and from (less than $20 each way) as the walk was about an hour each way and we had some time constraints, was for Haight-Ashbury. The room itself was small, but clean, comfortable, and efficient. Nice sheets and pillows. You can also help yourself to extra pillows, among other amenities, from this guest closet they have on most of the floors. Room actually had a nice little peek-a-boo view of the ocean. Pretty roof terrace w/ great views of the city. An unlimited supply of chilled, filtered water. Friendly staff, coffee, tea, and hot chocolate 24/7 in the large, comfy lounge downstairs - comes complete with free wi-fi, complementary use of computers/Internet, HD TV, fireplace, board games, etc., Has a modest but convenient workout room and laundry room. And best of all - attached to an inviting pub called the Elephant and Castle. Yup - definitely coming back. Thank You Club Quarters!

title: “Don't go for the private car”
text: This hotel was nice enough. Our only problem was being locked out of our room when we had requested (and received) a late check out....so be sure to check at the desk that your key card still works before heading back up to your room. Also, we were advised by the "bell man" that renting the hotel's private car to take us back to LGA was cheaper (at $51.00) than taking a cab...."due to the extra fees involved". We waited for the "private car" long enough and ended up taking a taxi anyway. The fare? $30.20 add to that a generous tip!

title: “The Cookies are Great Internet is a Service Charge”
text: I reserved this room through an affiliate travel booking platform and got a great room rate. Aprox. 75.00 (not including taxes) for a full day stay. Late check in was effortless and was greeted with a warmed cookie. I think it is fair to mention it costs to use internet in your room but for business travlers I suppose that is an expected cost. Great friendly staff took the edge off our long day of intercontinental travel. I would choose this hotel again as our stop over.

title: “Great Value, Great Location, Other Than That...”
text:
We spent four days sans kids in NYC for our 17th anniversary. We chose On The Ave despite the mixed reviews because of the great price and great location. We were more interested in a place to collapse after a long day of sightseeing (this was my wife's first trip to New York) than a deluxe experience and were willing to take the gamble. 
I am happy to report that our hunch was correct. The room was a good size (upgraded to Deluxe), it was clean (no bed bugs, which had been mentioned in an earlier review!) and it was only 2 blocks from the subway. We could easily walk to the Museum of Natural History and across the park to the Met and Guggenheim. Great neighbourhood - we got a kick out of seeing the locals in their native environment - with lots of restaurant choices, including a Sarabeth's a few blocks away for breakfast. We didn't use a cab other than to get to and from La Guardia; walking and subway were perfect for us.
To be so close to Central Park (a plus for us), shopping and the subway was what sold us on this hotel. Would we go back? Variety is the spice of life - we are curious to try the Excelsior, also in the 'hood, a bit pricier but probably a bit nicer. Note that staff were friendly and courteous, prompt at addressing the couple of concerns we had (got locked IN our room one morning) and the hotel was also very quiet, despite being across from a fire station (I don't think they use their sirens at night, only during the day when we generally weren't around). For the price, very, very hard to beat but you won't be getting The Plaza for $250/night so don't expect it.

title: “The Dream is really posh!”
text: Friendly staff, from doorman to management! Definitely recommend it. Great location, subway is at the corner. Walking distance to great restaurants too! Will definitely go back and stay there whenever in NYC!

title: “Magnificent location”
text: This is a new hotel for the Club Quarters group and it is right next to the World Trade Centre rebuilding site, no noise despite the location. The restaurant on the top floor has a fantastic view of the building site and surrounding areas, also the bar staff kept me entertained for hours.....no it was not the alcohol. The rooms are quite small however you are right there in downtown NY so what do you expect. Being a new hotel all the amenities are great and the guest lounge downstairs is a great chill out place for reading, there free tea and coffee. Its a short walk to the subway to get you uptown and this being my first trip to NY, things were easy to find. The staff were all wonderful, very helpful in every aspect, just wish I could remember their names to give them acknowledgement publicly. Taxi apparently cannot part in the area so you either need to book a car, smart choice for going to the airport, or walk around the corner to the Marriott and wait there. Good sports bar in the back of the Marriott however does not compare to the view from the balcony at QC.

title: “Best deal around Michigan Avenue”
text: Based on traveling to Chicago on business for the last 10 years, this is the best deal in the Michigan Ave area. The rooms are spacious, clean, quiet, and the staff is very accomodating. Simply put, this is the best deal around. Everything is in walking distance if you perfer, and convenience to the train and cabs is also easy. The breakfast & fitness room make mornings a snap, and the convenience of nearby restaurants make dinner/lunch very easy. The true suite rooms (there is a door that closes & truly separates the bedroom from the living area) make traveling with others/children very easy. The kitchen is stocked with utensils and dinnerware. This has become our preferred location & doubtless will remain so.

title: “Letter To Hotel Management...Ugh!”
text:
I just returned home from California. Thankfully, once I checked out of the Westin Bonaventure Hotel, my vacation took an upward turn and became very enjoyable.
The Bonaventure hotel caused me nothing but grief! At check in I was told that there was no room available. Then a king-sized bed became available. After much insistence, my reserved 2-bedded room miraculously appeared. A few hours later, I found out that my roommate had been placed in a separate room. Please note, that upon my arrival, I was told she had not yet checked in! Now, I was told to move my belongings to her room on a lower floor; no assistance was offered. 
Later, I discovered that my camera was missing. I called the front desk and was told to come down and get a new key to my old room, so I could search for my camera. Upon entering the room, I noticed that the toilet paper had been "re-pointed", soap replaced, and that the bathroom trash (my tissues and soap wrapper) removed but the room had remained unoccupied. Only the housekeeper had entered the room and my camera was nowhere to be found.
Lost camera, I sadly returned to my room and notified security. Just as my roommate and I were about to fall asleep (2 AM), the phone rang. Scared to death, fearing bad news from home, I quickly answered the call. Thankfully, it was only hotel security, informing me that my camera had NOT been found...Could this not wait until sunrise?
Next morning, securing my belongings, I called for the housekeeper. We had been told to phone, when we were leaving the room, or the room might not get made-up, as on the previous day.
Around 6 o'clock the following evening (7/15/08), the fire alarm went off in our room. We called the front desk and were told that security would come up to check our alarm. Ten minutes later, when security did not arrive, I heard noises in the hallway. Upon peeking out of my door, I smelled strong smoke and saw many security men. One said to me, "Ma'am, you'll have to evacuate the building." Strangely, nobody had bothered to knock on our door nor did the front desk advise us of the emergency. My roommate and I, plus a few others on our floor, were ushered by police into a hallway for evacuation. Unfortunately, the uninformed officer had placed us in a circular hallway without an escape route. Luckily, an officer was standing near the fire door and heard us banging. We were then escorted through the smokey building to an actual stairwell. We walked down the 14 flights and attended our formal banquet in our street clothes.
Next morning, the alarms sounded once again. Again, we phoned the front desk for information/assistance...The phone rang and rang, never to be answered. In a few minutes, an announcement came over an in-room loud-speaker (where was it the previous night?). We were told that the situation was being investigated, to remain calm, and that we would be updated, shortly. Since we did not smell smoke, we tried to remain calm. The message repeated itself, numerous times, as we dressed and went to our Hadassah Brunch. We never received an "all clear" but the lobby seemed calm and quiet.
This was truly the vacation from hell...And I have not even mentioned the food service; yikes...4 bagels for every 10 guests! Although I did not pay for my room (front desk comped for my troubles), the lost camera, which cost over $300, more than made up the difference. I could go on with this horrific tale but my blood pressure is going up...I will, however, mention that a microwave, as was promised, was not available during my entire stay. The good news is...NutriSystem meals are not bad at all, when eaten cold!
Upon returning home, I found my camera battery charger, in my suitcase. Please inquire if the housekeeper would like to have it or has she already "found" a replacement charger for MY camera?!

title: “A surprise in DC....”
text:
I have just returned from 5 weeks travelling around the States and consider myself fortunate to have commenced my tour in Washington staying at the River Inn for 3 nights. A well-situated hotel, within easy walking distance of Georgetown and the Kennedy Centre, the River Inn was pretty good value for money.
Am surprised by some of the more negative reviews - my room was spacious, spotlessly clean and well-equipped. Front desk staff were helpful, and the restaurant, "Dish" was a good option one evening.
Would stay here again if I am lucky to return to Washington.

title: “A pleasant surprise”
text: The hotel looked disappointingly ordinary from the outside, but once you get into the small lobby area, the atmosphere is stylish and cheerful. The room was extremely spacious, with a good desk area if you needed to do some work, and a great marble surface for making hot drinks. The bed was very comfortable, and the plasma TV screen and furnishings were modern and stylish. The staff were courteous and helpful at all times. My only criticism was the room service from the Lola restaurant. Not only did they deliver the wrong order, but it was over-salted and over-priced. They did however give me a full refund without quibbling when I complained. The hotel is in a very central location, and I would definitel recommend it to anyone who wants to stay in downtown Seattle.

title: “Excellent hotel and The French Room is dining at its very best.”
text: My wife and i have stayed at the Adolphus several times and it is a great hotel in downtown Big D. Rooms are big and very clean, staff is courteous and helpful. The French Room is without equal in dining pleasure. Food is unequaled, waitstaff is highly trained and knowlegeable. Wine list is extensive. When we are in Dallas going to the Adolphus and The French Room is a must.

title: “Stylish and well run”
text:
My husband and I stayed for three nights in June after a busy time at our jobs in Los Angeles. The trip was purely pleasure--museums, restaurants etc.-- and we had heard about this new hotel in the Hyatt chain. It's location is fabulous--across from the NY public library--and the hotel staff was wonderful. The rooms were very stylish and modern. It is true that there is not a lot of storage space and the lighting system--touch tone rather than swtches--was erratic, but all in all this was a wonderful hotel. I particularly appreciated the complimentary non alcoholic beverages, free internet, and free local telephone calls. No feeling of stinginess, which one often finds at hotels--particularly chains.
Suggestions: provide better bedside reading lights; keep the bar open after 11:30 PM (this is supposed to be a city that never sleeps!); and provide a later check out time for Hyatt Gold and Platinum card members.
The restaurant Cafe Boulud near the Met is fabulous, as is the south Indian restaurant, based in India, Saravana Bhavan.

title: “Great place to stay for a father and daughters getaway”
text:
Stayed at the Doubletree from July 05 - Jul 09, 2005. I enjoyed my stay. I was with my two daughters ages (19 - 16 ). Location was great just walk out of your room and u were right there. This was my first time in NY. I had requested one of the newer rooms and we were given one.
Housekeeping was great and the staff was friendly. I would stay at this location again if the price was right again. 
GREAT STAY IN NYC WILL DO IT AGAIN. CANT GO WRONG WITH THIS HOTEL AND LOCATION.
BRING LOTS OF CASH FOR NYC FOOD. PRICES ARE HIGH

title: “JW Indy”
text: JW offers great room product, spacious rooms, wonderful updated amenities, beautiful appointed bathrooms. Service is EXCEPTIONAL from the moment you pull up. Concierge was helpful, suggested many options and so friendly. The only thing we were not as happy with was the breakfast room service. Our jam selection arrived and was opened and partially used already. Not centrally located in town a few blocks out of everything but small enough city it isn't a problem.

title: “Excellent Hotel and location”
text:
Just returned from San Francisco after a 3 night stay at the Orchard Hotel. We picked the Orchard because of the price, the location and the positive reviews. We arrived at SFO and walked over to the BART station, A 30 minute ride into the City for $5.50 one way is a great way to transfer. Arrived at the BART Powell Station and walked up the stairs and caught the Powell/Mason Cable car which dropped us about 100 feet from our hotel. Our check in was painless and the staff was very accommodating. They gave us a choice of a couple of rooms, we opted to take a room on the 6th floor facing Bush street (front of hotel), the front desk staff said that if was quieter because the back side of the hotel has trash pick up noise in the early hours of the morning. We found our room to be very clean, with adequate amenities.
The king size bed was very comfortable and shampoo, conditioner, body lotion, hair dryer were provided. The room was exceptionally quiet, with no adjacent room sounds and very little street noise. Each morning a buffet continental breakfast was provided with several choices of ham, cheese, hard boiled eggs, toast, jam/jellies, spice cake, cereal, fresh fruit, coffee, juices, etc. The rooms also include DVD players and the front desk has a variety of DVD movies to choose from at no cost.
We ate at several places during our stay, but absolutely loved Harris Steak House for the best filet I ever tasted, also ate at Tadisch Grill, the seafood was excellent, and for a quick inexpensive great Chinese lunch, try the House of Nanking. 
I would definately stay at the Orchard Hotel on our next visit to San Francisco.

title: “Dated and Disappointed”
text:
We used Priceline and ended up here. It was a BIG disappointment! The hotel is non-smoking however it smells as if that was not always the case. The room was very cramped and there was trash in the waste basket in the bathroom. The TV set is an old floor model and there were limited Cable channels. We asked for a double and the beds were so small my husband's feet hung off the bottom!
The comforters were worn, the pillows were worthless. The blinds were not blackout shades and didn't even pull closed. Heating and cooling weren't a problem. There is no in-room fridge or microwave (you have to go to the first floor "concession stand area" around the corner from the checkout desk. We didn't bother to visit the pool or sauna (it was December). The door slams loudly every time you enter or leave the room which is disturbing at any hour.
My husband said the room service was good. The location was very convenient but aside from that I hope we never have to stay here again.
Our usual hotel is the Sheraton Inn and Suites and thie Crowne Plaza Columbus North is NO comparison.

title: “A Blue Gem in Downtown Dallas”
text: Stay here instead of the big names - for smaller rooms and a bit off the track you will find a great price, friendly staff, excellent affiliated fitness center, and decent, fair priced food in the restaurant.

title: “A Great Stay”
text: What puts this hotel over the top is the staff. This included the front desk (very helpful) and the shuttle service providers, who were sweating they were working so hard to get everyone where they needed to be! This hotel serves a lot of people going back and forth to the medical center and it was comfortable, clean and provided a great breakfast with lots of choices and "to go" bags. The rooms aren't huge but there's plenty of storage space and two TV's. Even though the shuttle will take you anywhere you need to go, i'd leave an hour's time to get anywhere in the morning (7-9AM) -- eat breakfast in the meantime. There are a few restaurants in walking distance, but not many (the shuttle will drive to Rice Village, apparently). Overall the hotel was nicely renovated, clean and the staff was memorable. I highly recommend it over the much more expensive hotels right on-site at the medical center.

title: “Friendly Staff, Unfriendly Accommodations, Overpriced Parking”
text:
I expected a lot better accommodations than I received at the Radisson. I stayed here because Radisson is known for it's semi-luxurious hotels and accommodations. This hotel however, was a disappointment. 
The sleep number bed was extremely comfortable as I slept on one of the lowest settings possible and just sunk right into the bed. The room itself was large however the bathroom was as small as a coat closet with no room to move. The carpet was old and had rust stains or some other stains all over (mostly by the windows). The TV was from 1995. And when I attempted to call guest services or the operator I never got an answer. Room wise--I've had nicer and more updated rooms at Motel 6 for a quarter of the price. 
The staff was friendly and willing to help out wherever they could (or whenever I got them by phone). The free wifi in the room was extremely slow and the free print from your own computer service to guest services printer was not working. So I had to go down to the business center and pay $7 for 15 minutes of internet time. Tried to print my boarding pass from the same computer and could not do it because it blocked pop ups and these computers would not allow you to change that setting. 
The valet parking attendants were extremely nice although I was very upset that parking was $20 per night here and there were no other options available. 
Overall this was an average hotel experience but a subpar Radisson experience.

title: “Amazing service, nice rooms for the price”
text: The rooms were very neat and clean. The bathrooms could have been a bit bigger. The service was excellent. The people at the front desk were very friendly and extremely helpful. Well definitely stay there again when in San Diego.

title: “Horrible service, attempted to increase rates”
text: The staff lost my reservation, attempted to give me a room at a rate higher than what I had been promised, attempted to charge me more for a room larger than what I wanted, continually ignored my military rate, and when we refused to pay the increased rate inferred I didn't have enough money to cover the full stay, and insulted my wife when we left.

title: “Go ahead and book this one, you won't be sorry”
text: We had planned to spend three nights in San Antonio in August and after reading many reviews on this site decided on this hotel. I am so glad we did because we loved it. Our room was in the San Fernando tower and had a spectacular view of the cathedral from our balcony. The building itself is charming and retains many of the features of the former bank building that it once was. Although it is a bit of a hike to get to the tower rooms, the rooms more than make up for it. Our room was huge and consisted of a living area with lovely furniture, a huge bathroom and separate bedroom with king size bed. There was plenty of wardrobe space, an iron an ironing board, kitchenette and coffee maker and mini refrigerator. We loved being able to sit on our balcony taking in the view. Each day that we went out it was so nice to come back to a beautifully cleaned, cool room. The building has an indoor an outdoor pool and we made use of both. There was also a great terrace on our level of the building but it was just a bit to hot while we were there to take advantage of it. All the staff were courteous and helpful. The breakfast buffet provided more than enough choice of the usual fruits, yoghurt, cereals, pancakes etc. The evening reception was ok if you were looking to save money but the food offerred didn't change from one night to the next and was predominantly fried, fast food type fare. There was a basic salad though. Each guest was entitled to three free alcoholic drinks which seemed quite generous. I suspect it could get very busy at peak times of the year but while we were there it wasn't too bad. The riverwalk area was much smaller than I had imagined and this hotel had direct access to it. We liked that security of the hotel in that you had to use your room key to operate the lift. When we travel we don't feel the need for valet service, hotel restaurants, room service or a stocked bar fridge as these all add to the cost and we would rather spend our money on other things.So if thats what you are looking for another hotel might suit you better, but for us the Drury Plaza was perfect.

title: “'Excellent' is the word!”
text:
My husband booked this hotel for our wedding night (This was last year's (2010) summer, but I never got a chance to come back and write a review)
Our stay was very very nice, we were upgraded to a suite (complimentary). In short, everyone at the hotel went out of their way to make our stay very pleasant and memorable.
I highly recommend this hotel and would go back to stay in a heartbeat!!
Thank you Hotel 1000!!

title: “Lock was Broke”
text:
Imagine just pulling your top over your head and having some strange man walk in to your room. I stayed here for 2 nights so that I could take my husband to watch his beloved Dolphins play football for his birthday. My husband went down to grab us a muffin & coffee, I jumped in to the shower. I was pulling my shirt on over my head when our door opened and some other man with coffee for his wife came walking in. It seems that his key also opened our door. He was just as embarrassed as we were upset. My husband and this stranger both went to the front desk to get the keys reprogrammed. The staff were friendly but unable to fix the problem. The stranger's key still opened our door. Now how would you feel? We asked for a new room - all booked. We waited half an hour for a maintenance man to come up when he said he was going to follow us right up. Was the door fixed? We have no idea, all we could do is sleep with the deadbolt on the door and one eye open. Our tv remote was broken which at first was just an annoyance but after the lock it was just the icing. We will never go back.
Now if the manager replies to this with the standard statement as below, you will know it is computer generated crap.

title: “Wow - are these rooms small!”
text: This may be a classic and filled with history but stick to the lobby and bar. Can't believe how small the room was. Almost didn't need a remote control because I could stick my toe out of the bed and change the channel. The bathroom door can't open all the way because it hits the bed. Can't imagine more than one person in this room. And even the hotel acknowledges that it's noisy since they have a pre-printed card and earplugs on the nightstand. Not all bad though. Service was friendly and responsive. Location is good. And small notwithstanding, the room was clean. I'm glad I stayed here once, but doubt I will return.

title: “Fabulous service and a touch of luxury in a great location.”
text: What a respite from the hustle of Times Square. We received wonderful service from the moment we stepped up to the registration desk, where Daniel expertly handled our check-in with wit and flair. When we walked into the room, I was delighted by the cleanliness and amenities like the coffee pod brewer and the microwave and fridge. When we turned in for the night, the luxurious bedding really caught my eye, especially the soft, high thread count sheets and downy pillows. I slept great because the room was quiet and we could draw the black-out curtains against the near daylight of the goings on down below. I highly recommend the Doubletree Suites, the responsive staff will make sure you have a delightful, comfortable stay.

title: “Enjoyed my stay and looking forward to come back”
text:
I have just came back from a six day stay in this hotel and as usual, i will write some reviews about it.
1. Location
Location is a bid off the main attraction. However, the zoo is nearby and there is a huge park nearby should you want to jog or have an evening or morning walk.
2. Facilities
If you are on a business trip. This hotel facilities is one of a good choice. It fits the business purpose plus you can also spend time at the park when you are already tired and wanna rest. And oh ya... there is a nice garden behind the hotel as well and if you happen to be there in spring. It is even better!!!
If you are with kids... since not much is there in the hotel... you can either opt for an evening or morning walk at the park. Or take them to the zoo... or to the pool. There are also playgrounds around that area.
3. Conclusion
Compared to other hotel right in the city area... this is sort of a retreat location. There are rows of shops nearby for your convenience. A convenient store..restaurant, bank... laundry and even access to underground. . 
For me, I have made a good choice. Oh ya... did i mention that there is even a starbuck inside the hotel!!

title: “Great customer service”
text:
I travel to NY 9-10 times a year, this hotel is truly a home away from home for me. Each time I return, I am acknowledged as a returning guest and treated as though I am the most important guest there that day.
Guest services manager, Ryan Shafi, always has a pleasant smile and a great attitude. The one time he was not able to make a change I had requested( it was an oversight on my part), I walked away feeling he had truly done everything within his power to make it happen.
Great place to stay!

title: “great hotel”
text:
very clean.
staff very professional.
decor is very nice.
wish i had more time to spend there.

title: “Helpful staff at Hyatt”
text: We stayed at the Hotel for 2 days to attend a Conference. The staff was cheerful and extremely helpful and went out of the way to help us. The Conference Area is enormous and one can get really lost in the maze. Cleanliness is impeccable. Kudos to the Housekeeping and the Maintenance departments for such a great show.

title: “Decent hotel at a good rate for Chicago”
text:
Stayed at the Doubletree for an overnight. It was a recently remodelled hotel. Lobby was nice. Rooms were generally nice and clean. It had onsite parking which was great even though it was $43 a night to park which is similar rate to other downtown hotels. The hotel was a few block off of Michigan Ave so within general walking distance or a short cab ride from a lot of downtown Chicago hot spots.
Only concern I had was the elevators and the common areas. They didn't have air conditioning or at least it wasn't working which made for a hot trek to and from your room especially in the heat of summer. Also, the elevators seemed to be constantly backed up. I had to wait a couple of difffernt times for an elevator which I would unusual because they were always full or there was a line to get on in the lobby. Maybe they weren't all functioning. Regardless it wasn't enough to disrupt our stay.
Overall the hotel was just that, a hotel. It was a decent place, but I wouldn't go out of my way to stay there again unless I was able to get a great rate again.

title: “Great Place, Great Location, Great Service! Thanks for a great trip, Topaz.”
text: The hotel, location and staff were great. Communication was great before, during and after our stay. The front desk staff was professional, genuinely friendly and on top of their game. Our room was clean, fresh and very large for D.C. The decor was funky following the Kimpton theme, and the beds, pillows and other amenities were top notch. The Family Fun Package offering Cookies, Milk and a Movie every night was something the kids looked forward to every single night. Their attention to detail, making every part of our stay enjoyable was refreshing. We were able to walk to great restaurants and were only 5 minutes from the Dupont Circle Metro station, making it very easy to get around. Keep up the good work. If you are looking for a great DC Hotel...stop looking and book the Topaz. You will not be disappointed.

title: “Loved it”
text:
I stayed with my 15 year old son at the Comfort Inn Manhattan. I was a little sceptical as I got out of my yellow cab from the airport, mainly because the hotel entrance was small, no doorman and different to the larger hotels that I have previously stayed in in New York.
All that was to change. From checking in, the staff were really helpful. The lifts were a little slow but the hotel is older so I expected this and it didnt cause a problem at all. On getting to our room I couldnt believe how lovely it was. Really clean, comfy beds, large TV which my son couldnt wait to switch on, and plenty of room to put clothes, suitcases etc in a walk in closet. I liked the fact that the room had its own safe deposit box. 
The room was quite dark, it did have several lamps but admittedly the light wasnt great, but then I didnt come to New York just for a well lit room. On opening the curtains I was rewarded with a fantastic view of the Empire State Building - what more could you ask for.
The hotel is central for everything, everything right on your doorstep, underground station more or less right outside the door. Brendans cafe is lovely, right next door. Macys literally over the road. Just a brilliant base to get around everywhere. Times Square is literally a 10 minute walk away and probably about a 20 minute walk to the stores on 5th Avenue - just brilliant.
Breakfast consisted of waffles and donuts, toast and cereal and an abundance of coffee and juice. It was enough for first thing in the morning. Theres a great selection on the room service menu too. 
Will definitely book this hotel next year rather than the flashier bigger hotels who seem to spend more time doing up the lobby than refurbing the actual rooms. This was a comfy, small, friendly, hotel right in the heart of New York City.

title: “Not so happy this time around”
text:
We were delighted with this hotel when we visited it in 2010.
However, maybe due to the high occupancy or who knows why, the service this year was much worse.
We came back to our room everyday to find some unpleasant surprise, like something had not been done by the maids. We let it go when it wasn't really disrruptive. However, the last day, we found that the beds had been only half-made.
We went to the front desk to complain, and had to show the pictures we had taken from the room so as to prove our point.
The person in the frontdesk wasn't impressed either, but there was nothing they could/would do about it.
He tried to convince us that we might have left the "do not disturb" sign at the door, which wasn't the case. Something had been done around the room like rearranging the towels, and so on, but the beds weren't completely made and the pillows were lying on the floor to our disgust.
We were told that the manager would contact us back, but I'm still waiting (since the beginning of July, so I do not think this will even happen).
I said last year that we couldn't wait to book with them for the years to come, but unfortunately, I think this was the last time we will have ever stayed at this hotel, as we found that the quality level has dropped dramatically and there are better options around for about the same price.
It's a real shame.

title: “Great Food, Great Atmosphere & Terrific Service!”
text: A wonderful repreive from the summer heat, craft beer, Mediterranean cuisine and the delightful cast of personalities there to assist you make this a most refreshing refuge... and all with the beauty of the Riverwalk at your feet.

title: “Fantastic trip to Beale”
text: Had an awesome time staying at the Westin this weekend. Our suite faced The FedEx Forum and the Gibson Guitar Factory. Literally around the corner from Beale St. Great restaurant downstairs called Bleu(Chargrilled Oysters and Mac & Cheese) and a Starbucks next door. Beyond the location the suite itself was amazing, the bathroom had a huge whirlpool bath and a shower sauna that I will not soon forget. Can't wait to come back here, so fun!!!!

title: “Very nice hotel, with good location and service.”
text:
I stayed two times in the hotel during business trips. 
It have all the services, a very good breakfast and the personnel is very nice.
It is located a few blocks to the Gaslamp District with lot of restaurants.

title: “Good for business”
text:
My husband was staying at the Omni for business, and I joined him on part of the trip. I have to say that I'm used to the Four Seasons, so I'll try to judge the Omni NOT based on that standard, as the Omni is a 4-star.
 I think this is a great hotel for business travellers. We had a suite and it was very large. Great location, perfect for shopping! For a 4-star, the hotel seemed very nice. There were a few glitches-a dirty glass, amenities not replaced by housekeeping, etc. And the lighting was so dim it was difficult to put on my makeup in the bathroom. But other than those things, very clean and an excellent location.

title: “Time warp decor...don't. Marriott Plaza”
text:
This hotel is old and tired. The rooms are VERY outdated and small. Decorated in a drab green and beige, old wallpaper and stained popcorn ceilings. If you are looking for a hotel that makes you feel pampered and on vacation look elsewhere. Usually Marriott's provide a quality product but this was lost in the shuffle.
B & T (Houston, TX)

title: “Depressing views - slowest service ever...”
text:
The views for the majority of the rooms are depressing as you stare at pale brick walls of other guest rooms. NOT at all as pictured on the hotels website.
Room service took over an hour the first morning (just coffee!) and 45 minutes the second morning. The staff were unapologetic but said the manager would be notified. (not sure what that means or why)
Obviously, I won't be back...

title: “Excellent spot in San Francisco”
text: Had a perfect stay here during a recent conference I attended. I always love Marriott for the comfort of their beds and pillows, and this place was no exception. Staff were very attentive, friendly and helpful. Location is excellent only a couple of blocks from the wharf and accessible by streetcar. Numerous places to eat within walking distance.

title: “Very good hotel”
text:
I love love Hampton Inn hotels! I've never been disappointed.
This one is in a great location, close enough to Times Square so you have plenty of restaurants and entertainment nearby but away enough so it's not noisy.
The room was small (but it's New York!) but clean and comfortable.
The hot breakfast is included and you have a lot of different items to choose. It can be a bit crowded so come as early as possible!
Our room was very quiet, the only issue was the very noisy a/c but if you don't use it at night you should be fine.
Be careful to ask for a room on a low floor if you don't want to wait 10 minutes for the elevator (only 2 of them so it can be crazy during the rush hour).
We left our luggages at the front desk on our last day and one of our suitcases was missing when we came back 5 hours later.
The front desk manager did a great job and we finally found it but it was a very stressful situation (we almost missed our flight!).
I will be back at this hotel on my next trip to new York!

title: “excellent”
text:
Read reviews was very worried, but unfounded, checked in early was given a room on 5th floor so I asked if there was anything higher as I had read the best view were there, moved to 25th floor. Lovely room never had to wait long for a lift and the staff were lovely and friendly. My friend was trying to contact her aunt but the phones in the lobby were not working so one of the staff left her use her mobile and would not accept payment for it. 
Breakfast I would not recommend very expensive there was a lot to choose from but who can eat $39.00 of food this early, you could not get a decent cup of tea.
You can check in to your airline in line in the hotel which was great.
The only fly in the ointment was a lady called Janice who work on the ticket counter, I was trying to book to go to the shopping outlet and she took a personal call and was trying to arrange a party, she was then arranging her social life for the next week while I waited, not at all professional and was the only let down, my friend tried a little later to book on the same trip and she said her computer was not working and to come back, when we went back the desk had closed and at no time was we told to come back as they were leaving, lucky for us there was someone very helpful the next morning.
Ate a fantasic Italian restaurant just 1 block from the hotel come out and turn left, it was near a luggage shop i think it was called prezza norte, the food was out of this world the portions are huge the starters are for 3 people not one.
In all would recommend this hotel everytime, I have learnt that if you want to be treated with respect you need to treat the person you are speaking to with respect, no-one wants to help a moanie awkward customer at any time. I have to say there were some moanie americans there.

title: “OK Hotel, the rooms are extremely loud....”
text:
Stayed for a night in late June. Had an amzing rate through hotwire so booked it. The lobby and bar and lounge are really warm and cozy. The best part of the hotel. The service was fine, most of the employees were young and it seemed that they were new hires trying hard but learning the ropes. The rooms were plain white, the lighting was fair at best, walls paper thin. We could hear our next door neighbors convo at they were not speaking loudly.
