The bathrooms were tiny, toiletries were missing and one towel in the bathroom. The beds were very comfy and the sheets were of high thread count. Hard to believe this hotel was charging plus $350 a year or 2 ago. 
The hotel was next to empty and I would imagine the economy played a huge factor in that. The place just felt a little off and had this cold and dark feeling. Not what I expected.

title: “Perfect stay!”
text:
We arrived at the Affinia Dumont on 1st April after an uneventful flight with Virgin.
We were slightly early for check in, but were given access to our room straight away, which was a nice touch. The room itself was lovely. On the 37th floor with views of the Chrysler Building. 
Must admit before we went I was a little nervous about being a little out of the action, but found that I relished the (relative) peace and quiet the hotel offered. 
Found everyone who worked at the hotel to be lovely and helpful. Even when asking random questions about locations of different shops etc. We got them to organise us a car to the airport at the end of our stay and this was $75, which I didn't think was bad. 
Only dissapointment was they tried to charge us for two movies which we didn't watch in the room. We didn't actually touch the pay for view part of the TV. This was resolved quickly and easily though. 
All in all a wonderful stay and if we were going back we would book it again without question.

title: “Right on the River Walk”
text:
The hotel is in a great location right on the river walk, with easy access to the Alamo, shops, restaurants etc. There is a multi-storey car park (self-parking) on site.
The reception staff were very friendly and helpful. We arrived early, but they were happy to store bags and called my mobile as soon as a room was available. 
Initially we were given a room by the elevator. We were not happy with this and reception changed it for us immediately.
Our room was comfortable and well equipped.
There is a buffet breakfast and a cocktail hour "kick back" with food, which are included in the rate. Service very friendly and efficient. Not keen on the polystyrene plates and plastic cutlery.
There is a swimming pool on the roof, with a few sunbeds, tables and chairs. A real bonus for some late afternoon relaxation.

title: “"Hollywood Steal"”
text:
Now, this hotel is situtated right next to Yamashiro - (Mountain Castle) a sushi restuarant with a breathtaking view of Los Angeles. The property has been part of Hollywood History for almost 100 years. The property consists of lower hotel (Magic Castle , up the hill is Hollywood Hills Hotel then turn to the peak is Yamashiro - all walking distance)
The Hollywood Hlls Hotel is adjacent to The Magc Castle Club where check in, unlimited snacks and complimentary breakfast are available. The hotel is not modern or chic. It doesn't have any flat screen televisions or Ipod docks. However it's pool is next to Yamashiro garden and has a great view of Hollywood since the whole property is situated up in the hills.
It's walking distance to Hollywood Boulevard and Highland. SO the location is a Gem. I had a good experience with my stay. We tried the 1 bedroom suite and the kitchen and restroom were clean stocked with towels and all. It was also quiet and a nice walk down the hill to Hollywood Blvd. (A free shuttle is also available to and from Magic Castle entrance) Parking is $11 a night.
I'll definitely come back- however if you're looking for a luxurious hotel with automatic draperies this isn't it... The Hollywood Hills Hotel is more rustic, simple and tranquil.

title: “Love this Hyatt”
text:
I have to recommend this hotel as a choice for accommodations when visiting or simply getting away in Chicago. The rooms; while not extremely fancy are most comfortable and some of the room views, especially of the lake are gorgeous!
The staff is very pleasant, and the service overall was exceptional. The rates are also reasonable for a hotel in Chicago, very close to downtown.
Because I am a regular; once for my birthday, I had a card, cake and fruit basket waiting for me at check-in... it made my day!
Try this hotel, I guarantee you'll like it!

title: “OK”
text: This is an older hotel with exterior entrances, which isn't necessarily a bad thing. It looks like they are trying to keep up the rooms. The bed is comfortable and the chair with ottoman was nice. The bathroom however was not so clean. There were hairs in the sink, toilet and shower. It appeared that it had not been cleaned in a while. The carpet was worn and spotted as well. The wireless internet was unreliable as well. The office area is nice. The two computers are nice to print boarding passes and check your email. The staff is very friendly and the free breakfast is adequate, a little small though. They do offer a free shuttle to the airport, but allow extra time. The driver was 25 minutes late, making it a rush to get through security in time. Overall it is an ok hotel.

title: “Excellent!”
text:
Excellent Hotel. I was in town for a wedding reception here. Rooms are 
nicely furnished and for NYC seemed large. Beds have a featherbed. I 
did some work while here and found the desk chair very comfortable. 
Free high speed internet access was easy to use and fast. My bathroom 
had a large walk in shower but no tub--lots of soaps and stuff provided 
as well as a copy of the New York Times. The health club is big for a 
hotel and was not busy on either Sat. or Sun morning when I attended. 
There was no whirlpool--something I would have enjoyed after a long 
flight. I know there were people staying in the adjacent rooms, but I 
never heard anything from my room. 
 The wedding reception was one of the best orchestrated I've seen--excellent food and a terrace on the top floor with a view of central park.

title: “Wonderful Hotel”
text:
Spent 15 nights in this fab hotel in April with Hubby and two teenage daughters. We got an upgrade on arrival to a lovely large room with two bathrooms. I was very worried about this hotel having read the reports on trip advisor. Having stayed there I really don't know what these people were talking about. 
Everything about this hotel was wonderful from the very comfortable beds to the food and the lovely staff. The staff couldn't do enough for us especially Georgina in housekeeping who looked after us like we were her own. The hotel is old ( part of the historic hotels of America ) also very elegant which added to its charm for me. 
Ate in Bonfire a steakhouse attached to the hotel very nice indeed though a little on the expensive side. Mc Cormacks and Schmicks also very nice especially the sea food more reasonably priced and there is an irish pub also in the hotel where my husband enjoyed a few pints of Guinness. Hotel very centrally located to all amenities. Could not say enough about this hotel and would definately stay there again.

title: “Very good for this price”
text: We've stayed in Jerry's motel for 3 nights, rooms were a little bit shabby, but very clean, and we've had all necessary things: iron, shampoos, free wifi and parking. It's not far from centre and very close to chinatown. And we've got free snacks when we arrived, that was very nice. The only disadvantage I can imagine - walls are thin, you can hear people talking in next room.

title: “Disappointing.”
text:
I stayed here with my boyfriend for two nights on vacation during the week and was pretty excited about staying here. The only reason that this place is getting anything more than the worst rating is because the gentleman who checked us in was so courteous and helpful. For the price that one pays to stay here, you will find more value in the closest Holiday Inn. At least there is a standard that one can expect from a stay here. 
We stayed in a Standard room on the second floor. I'll start with the good. The location from the hotel is nice as it is around the corner from Union Square and centrally located. The lobby is impressive and tastefully decorated. There was a comfortable king sized bed in the room. That's where the good ends. It seems like the Morgans Hotel Group spent all their money renovating the lobby and the elevators. Our floor just seemed painted over with an awful pastel purple color. The room, the closet, and the bathroom were small. The bathroom grout was orange from rust seeping from the metal pieces. Our bathtub drain was clogged. After calling to have it fixed the next day, we gave up as we had to spend the whelse weekend taking quick showers to avoid standing in ankle deep water. Sleep was not an option as the walls were paper thin and you could hear everything from the music thumping from the bar downstairs to the conversations outside the door to the street noise outside.
We opted for $36 all day parking with in and our privileges next door to the hotel on the first day. We should've stuck with those guys because we paid $57 (includes parking tax) to wait outside for more than the 15 minutes promised to bring the car around. We also had to chase down the valet as he left the car without the keys without acknowledging us before heading inside to the computer. 
We had a wonderful stay in San Francisco but could not count on this hotel to be a comfortable place in which to return. No thanks.

title: “Excellent hotel, location and service.”
text: The location was great close to Grand Central, Bryant Park and Times Square. Friendly service from all the staff and especially from Bill. The room was quite comfortable, very quiet and kept clean. I would recommend a king bed as the queens size appeared to be smaller than usual queens. The toiletries were quality Molten Brown. There is free WiFi and the complimentary coffee in the morning. The complimentary overnight shoe shine was greatly appreciated. We had a perfect stay and would go back in a flash.

title: “Memphis Trip”
text:
I'm frequent traveler to Memphis, TN and have stayed at several hotels in the area. In fact I have stayed here when it was Plaza Hotel under old management........but I'm impressed how this hotel has turned around under new management.
This completely renovated hotel with amazing indoor pool is out outstanding at the rates offered.......I'm definitely coming back.

title: “Really incredible 'hotel'”
text:
Very very cheap hotel, but very very durty and......
We booked a room for three people and when we been there they gave us a room withg a spacious for max 1 person. As well the photos that they show in the web site are different comparte to the really room. they gave us another room, just after the main entrance, wich was not bud as a spacious but it was raining inside the room.

title: “Nice family location”
text:
Booked for family of 5, through hotwire. Brought extra matress.
Very convinient hotel, nice pool good location.
make sure to join starwood for free breakfast.

title: “Choose a different hotel”
text: I have stayed at this hotel in the past, so I thought I knew what to expect. I was wrong! I woke up in the morning to a lukewarm shower that turned ice cold after about one minute. I called the front desk and was told that yes, there was a problem with the boiler, but they were working on it. As the morning went on, no water would come out of my sink. I realized brushing my teeth would be an issue, so I went out to the vending machine to buy a bottle of water. The vending machine was empty. I went to the front desk to buy water, and they gave me two bottles at no charge. I left for the day to return around 4:00 p.m. Still no hot water, although there was a small stream coming out of the sink faucet now. The room had not yet been cleaned. I called the front desk, who told me they were working on getting the hot water fixed. I asked to be moved to a different room, as I found out that it was only my floor and wing of the hotel that was without hot water. They refused, saying they were booked. I pressed, and they relented and gave me a room on a different floor. Upon opening the door to the new room, I was blown away by the smell of bleach. I am very disappointed in this hotel and will not be returning. The staff, especially those at the desk this afternoon, were indifferent to my lack of hot water, any water, or a clean room. There are many hotels to choose from in this area and my colleague and I have decided we will be finding a different one for our next trip.

title: “Comfortable, clean and great location.”
text:
We were aware that the rooms in most New York Hotels were small and were prepared for the worst. The room was small but with adequate space. The beds are small for doubles but very comfortable. Room was clean and towels and bedding changed daily. Our room was quite noisy as was at front of hotel and could hear the bin lorries, sirens and carpark across the road from about 5am. We found the staff to be very helpful and loved the coffee shop next door for take out breakfast.
The foyer area is extremely dark but we ended up quite liking it!
Had read about the bed bug situation on here before went and we were horrified to be greeted by a big billboard outside the hotel about them. However we found out that this was being carried out by former employees with a grievance and the hotel can't stop it. We certainly had NO problems with bedbugs!
The Paramount Bar built on to hotel is extremely expensive and the staff in there were quite rude, the Library Bar staff were lovely but again incredibly expensive.
The location is absolutely fantastic and the only things to say about the hotel are the room could have done with a mirror near to a plug, bed could have been bigger. Wi-Fi costs and cahsrged $2 to look after bags before departure. None of these things were a big issue for us and they looked after our bags free when we arrived as not supposed to get into room till 4 and we were there at 1.
When we first arrived we were very apprehensive because of the signs outside and did take a sheen off of the excitement but was all for nothing so please don't panic if you see it!!
If was going back to NY would probably stay here again.

title: “Short Stay At The Sheraton”
text: Super nice staff. Check in & out was easy. Van serviced to and from airport was prompt. The room was spacious and well appointed. Nice amenities in the bath. And the view of the harbor was beautiful.

title: “Location, Location, Location!”
text:
We travel in to NYC quite often. We enjoy Broadway shows and Great restaurants. We usually stay in the Theater District or on Central Park South. This time we picked The Radisson Martinique. We were Extremely Satisfied with our choice. Herald Square just outside your front door. Subway outside your front door. Very easy to get a Taxi.
Walking distance to Theater, if you like. Five minute walk to Union Square Area. We will be sure to stay here again!

title: “Lost image”
text:
Very disappointed by my stay (4 nights),poor service,room done in the evening.
i think the objective of this hotel is to have private meetings and celebration which occupy the Mezzanine and lobby room on the first floor.
10 years ago,it was a different hotel.

title: “Great Location, I would stay again!”
text: Blue Sea Lodge is as close as you can get to the beautiful beach, located literally out the back gate of the pool area. Every night we left the windows open and fell asleep to the sound of crashing waves. The rooms are simple but comfy, with a fridge and a balcony, which are great. One night guests came into the courtyard at about 2:30 a.m., loud and playing in the pool. I called the front desk to let them know. In about 5 seconds the manager was there and in no uncertain terms told them to get out of the pool and go to bed. Fabulous. One thing I would skip is the breakfast area....it's stuff you'd find in a free continental buffet, but not free. Take advantage of the big grocery store down the street and the fridge in your room. I also wish there was more chairs in the pool area, but no biggie. Good choice for beachside San Diego.

title: “Great location, disappointing rooms”
text: After reading reviews regarding this hotel we were looking forward to splurging and staying in one of the celebrity suites. However, what we didn't know when reserving, the suites are first come first serve. That means that when we got there, we were very disappointed to find out that all the suites were gone except for the Kathy Griffin suite. This was the worst, over priced, disappointment possible suite. Nothing special except for a box on the wall with a shoe in it. The couch and furnishings clashed and nothing actually looked good! One in our party was an interior designer and struggled with the ill fitting design. Don't bother to upgrade to a suite- if you get stuck in this one it isn't worth it!

title: “Great for the Family”
text:
This is the perfect place for any family--if you don't mind driving to get to downtown attractions. Rooms are very nice, beds are really comfortable, and each room comes equipped with a small refrigorator. 
The resort also has three restaurants that are excellent although very pricey. The grounds are just beautiful. You won't be disappointed with this stay. It is very quiet and relaxing, and I would think, better than staying on the Riverwalk which seems so busy and noisy.

title: “city dwelling for business AND leisure”
text: Very Good service from this hotel. There are employed individuals who will give you the time of day and who are so polite and respectful in their etiquette. Room service was timely and professional and respected your privacy. Food was always at its expected temperature, and the service was polite to stand outside my door to wait for the bill, therefore respecting my privacy. The front desk was very helpful. Since my arrival was at midnight, i took a taxi which cost about $12. But for my return to the airport I took public transportation. It was easy and convenient. From this hotel, ALL public transportation is easy and convenient. And, the office for public transportation is practically next door. You can get any kind of pass and schedule. Bristol was nice to hold my luggage on the last day after I checked out but still had time to explore San D. before having to go to the airport. As for the on site restaurant Dixie's, that is convenient. I had the lavosh pizza. It's served on a cracker, not cracker-like crust. All the ingrediants were prepared well, and they all went well together. This I had in the bar area. Very wonderful bar tender!!! For breakfast, which was what i had for room service, I liked best to just get the basic breakfast with eggs to order, toast, bacon, and fruit instead of potatoes. The San Diego omelet would have been good if they would stick to the ingrediants listed on the menu, but instead they also add green bells and red onion and a lot of both that of course steal the show. They are both raw and strong. "The Currant" is a great place to eat out for breakfast and just across the street. There is a light in the shower! The air system was a bit on the cooler side. The vent was always blowing, so when the unit did not sense to turn on the vents would just blow cool air until the the sensor sensed that it needed to kick on the heat. I got used to it and planned accordingly. There were two little windows that opened to the outdoors. I like being able to open a window. There are few TV channels and nothing ever on. I basically did not use the TV and did not pay for any movies. I used the dry cleaning service which was timely and fine, but my slacks were not as smooth and freshly cleaned as i'm used to...The hotel really has all the great ammenities and charm and style that one would want out of an urban stay, but not quite plush. It's nice and the bed is VERY comfortable. And the robe and towels are nice. But it's not luxurious. I would stay at this hotel again. Mind all though, I only stayed here because I found an $85/night deal online. $150 a night, i don't know about that. But that's MY budget. With the convenience of public transportation, one could save on renting a car, etc. that maybe it all balances out.

title: “Overpriced”
text: I stayed here with my spouse when he was traveling for business. His room was paid for at this hotel so this is where we stayed. The hotel was nice and the location is good but it's not worth the price. We've stayed at several hotels over the years and this was the smallest room we have stayed in - an odd triangle shaped room. I also missed the amenities that are included in the price at other hotels, such as internet, free local calls, frig, etc. (I will NOT pay for amenities that should be included, regardless of how much I miss them.) When I arrive in a city I always look through the phone book for ideas of places to visit, unique shops, etc. The room did not have a phone book and when I asked for one at the front desk I was told they did not have any because they prefer guests to use the concierge. How am I supposed to know what I want to see if I don't know what there is to see? The hotel does have a good location. Near several buses to take you to various tourist locations (the zoo, Old San Diego, Coranado Hotel, etc.) Also near the Midway museum and a cruise ship dock. Again a nice hotel but other hotels are just as nice/clean, include amenties and are half the price.

title: “Comfortable, friendly property”
text:
Location: Downtown, pretty close to Union Square. We didn't enjoy downtown nearly as much as the Mission, and will stay there next time. For where it is, location is great.
Staff: We had no problems with the staff at all - they were friendly and attentive. The person who checked in in front of us had some reservation issues but we must have only caught the end of it, so no judgement from us.
Room: We had room 718 on the top level, a "junior" suite. Good view, no noise at all. The two beds layout actually worked really well as we both felt unwell the last day or so. Fairly basic layout, but everything was new and comfortable. Floorboards are always a bonus too. Lots of great selections on the TV. Only negative was that we really would have appreciated a mini bar. The bathroom was fine enough - the toiletries were pretty low grade but we had soap from other hotels, and got shampoo/conditioner from Walgreen's. 
Miscellaneous: In some ways it is a tarted up hostel, in a "vibe" way. No problem at all, just putting it out there.
Overall - really great value hotel. We paid about $115 + tax for the "top" style room, which is about right. Probably wouldn't be so keen to fork out too much more, but it was great value.

title: “Okay but nothing special”
text:
Hyatt Regency is okay for a stay in Washington. Capitol is close but this is not an area where there would be lots of restaurants or services. Also, there is some kind of social services building close to the hotel, which means that there are some people loitering in the area and some tried to approach me for money. I didn't find the area the best in town. 
Starbucks is next door if you want to skip the expensive hotel breakfast. Union station is a few blocks' walk from the hotel (incl. car rental and a large food court).
Room is okay, as is the bathroom. Both were clean.
The hotel has a good small store for convenience items and little snacks.

title: “Wonderful location, clean, friendly!”
text: This hotel is right on the canal and is pet friendly. The rooms are very clean and has a lot to offer, like excellent hot complimentary breakfasts, a grill on the balcony for guest use, a game room and dinner and drinks some nights! Cheri and Brittany were wonderful and extremely helpful! We stayed for 3 nights with our dog and it was very quiet! Every nght we took a walk along the canal. The hotel is close to monumental circle, we walked there, and other memorials. We also walked down and rented a kyak and paddle boat on the canal!! The pool was a little on the small side, but it was very nice!

title: “Great Experience”
text: Great experience, The staff was excellant, awesome breakfast waiting for us every morning. The housekeeping staff kept our room nice and cozy for us. Great location, perfect to walk to river from as well as the pier. Perfect for the Mag mile for shopping and dining. Will definately staff again.

title: “Nice break, beautiful grounds”
text: We spent a day here before heading to SeaWorld. Checkin was fine. Paying a high price so you expect good service. Pool areas and lazy river were clean, lots of tubes to be had. The only down side was that the water was FREEZING. IT was in the low 80s and breezy, but you could not stay in the water longer than a few minutes. Kids included. The hot tub was a welcome retreat. Bikes were available, although we saw several sitting outside peoples rooms and not being used throughout the day while we waited for some to be returned to ride. Drinks were of course outrageous, but yummy and we were on vacation so did not mind splurging. The burgers at the Country Store by the pool were fine and convenient. Would return in the heat of the summer for a better pool experience.

title: “Very friendly, honest and helpful”
text: I recently stayed here for two nights while doing business in Encino. Although my room could have used updating (worn carpet), it was in reasonably good shape and clean. The front desk staff and breakfast room staff were very friendly. I accidentally left my watch in the room (an anniversary gift from my husband). I called soon after checking out of the hotel and they went immediately to the room to find it. They held if there for me in safe keeping for three days until Fedex could pick it up and return it to me. During the process I spoke to several people who were pleasant and reassuring. They were very trustworthy and honest.

title: “1st Class!”
text: Our family of 7 was extremely fortunate to spend last weekend in the luxurious MacArthur Suite, which included 3 bedrooms, 3 baths, kitchen, dining room and family room. The decor was equisite, and that was probably the most comfortable mattress of my life. Certainly the lap of luxury. Plus, the staff was amazingly accommodating and gracious. Excellent, excellent experience!

title: “Loved the roof top pool”
text:
We booked direct and were able to use a special AAA code for three of the nights and paid $265 with tax for the other two nights for 5 nights in early June. The staff were very helpful booking tour bus rides and the door man Larry was great with helpful travel tips and always a friendly greeting. 
 We had breakfast all 5 days in the hotel and the staff were quick and friendly. We had the breakfast buffet three mornings and oatmeal the other two. Dinner buffet with your friendly host was a special treat. He came around and made sure everything was top notch. He even taught my granddaughter and fun coin trick. 
 The room layout was OK but the bathroom needed some shelving to place your personal items on. The shower was small(narrow) but room was clean and smelled smoke free. Overall room and bed OK. The AC worked well and it was hot outside so we appreciated it.
 The roof top pool is busy in the afternoons and the life guard was very attentive ... never once reading or talking on the cell phone while people were out by the pool. I counted 36 people on night in and around the pool. It was very clean and refreshing after a hot day of sightseeing. We took my grand daughter there nightly and she loved it too. Fresh towels are provided poolside.
 I felt the rooms were overpriced but the best deal I could find in the down town DC area. We walked to the White House and back one morning. The subway is about 18 minutes away. This was a very long walk for me with a bad back. We did take three taxis there and found out the hard way one must ask "How much to ...congress or Union Station or Air Space Museum?" When we did not ask we were charged $15 and when we did we were charged $9 and $10. So they expect you to ask for a price as there are NO Fair Meters.
 Five days was not enough to see this wonderful town... our nation's capital. Be ready to ignore people asking for handouts at night. This was hard for me. Have a great trip.

title: “Great Hotel and Close to Downtown”
text:
We stayed two nights at this hotel and while it isn't fancy it was more than sufficient. It's a little older but the rooms are comfortable and the price is great. It has a terrific pool and the front desk was extremely helpful. The breakfast was plentiful and the restaurant attached to the hotel has perfectly adequate food. The music is rather loud but it is very convenient for the dinner hour.
All in all I would highly recommend this Clarion Hotel.

title: “Nice hotel”
text: Had not stayed here in 10 years. Still beautifully maintained. Rooms updated nicely. No breakfast spot in Towers. Parking was problematic. No late dining options other than room service. Overall, a nice hotel.

title: “Not upto "Westin" standard”
text: When you book a room at a Westin, generally you're assured that you're in for a good experience, but sadly, this Westin doesn't live up to those expectations. The customer service is poor- I'm a SPG Platinum member, and I had to wait a good amount of time as there was nobody at the check-in counter. Also, there's no Club-Room, the continental breakfast option they give as Welcome Amenity is absolutely crappy. The room is OK, but bathrooms are very small. Also, their sound-proofing is bad- you wake up in the morning hearing doors being open and shut. It's like staying at Four Points Sheraton, and paying for Westin. I will not recommend staying here, there are many better hotels in Chicago.

title: “Regulars”
text: We stay at the City Center HIE for every Seahawks home game. We are always greeted by the Friendly Staff, who are also very helpful in answering all our questions. Parking is safe and secure. Shuttle service to games is reasonable and convenient. Hotel is neat and clean. Rooms and service are Excellent. Prices are little bit on the high side unless you book through Hotels.com....watch site for sales. We will continue to book this hotel everytime we travel to Seattle.

title: “Clean, new, great location, reasonable”
text: Stayed for one Saturday night. $134 AAA rate. Room was a nice size, extremely comfy king bed w/LOTS of pillows, small living area w/loveseat, chair and table, nice kitchen area w/full-size frig, microwave, two burners, and a nice island counter w/two chairs. Fake hardwood in kitchen and carpet in rest of unit. Bathroom sink/counter is outside of bathroom which is nice. Everything was spotless, brand new. Enough towels, toiletries, and kitchenware for 4 people. Continental breakfast in nice large area on 2nd floor was egg soufle, scrambled eggs, sausage, bacon, bagels, toast, muffins, yogurt, assorted cereals and fruit, coffee, fruit drinks. Did not use spa/pools or bar. Best thing about this hotel was the staff--so friendly and warm and helpful, always smiling--they are a pleasure to deal with. The front desk staff, maintenance workers and breakfast were especially impressive. No valet parking, lot across the street, you can walk everywhere in the innerharbor area, many great restaurants nearby. No bellman, you take your luggage to your room yourself using a cart from the front desk. The front desk gives you written directions to the parking garage and even back to 95 which is a nice touch. This hotel is a great value and would be perfect for a family w/children considering the size and ammenities of the rooms. We definitely plan on a longer visit w/friends next time!

title: “Great Location”
text: Great Location. Nice clean hotel close to Cable car terminus. Very reasonably priced Thai restaurant on property.

title: “Great hotel with great service, but expensive parking”
text: This hotel is in a great area, only a few blocks from Michigan ave and the Red Line Train. It is a very safe neighborhood...only Con: the fire station is down the block and although we heard 2 or 3 fire trucks a day, it never bothered our sleep. The rooms are pretty in muted greens and the beds are soft and clean. The hotel is very nice, with a great breakfast in the morning. The staff is just the best! Super friendly! Always ready to help. We even called down and had them bring up a fan for our room, which got there 10 minutes after we asked, at 11pm at night. One problem was the a/c in our room. We had it turned down as low as it would go, and the room never got very cool, however, with the fan, it was fine and not worth complaining about. THe room met my expectations in terms of being clean, although you can see some wear and tear. The elevators are pretty slow, but the other amentities made up for these small things. The parking was pricey: 42$ for hotel valet. Instead, I parked right up the street on the left accross from the Snickers bar. That parking lot is $25 for over night parking. If you get there after the night person has left, you can park and pay at Snickers. The pool area is also nice, and we used the hot tub on several occations after sight-seeing all day. WE would go down around 4pm for an hour, and be the only people in there. If we return to Chicago, and could get a good deal on the room like we did this time, I would totally stay here again!!! Its a great place at a good price!

title: “DO NOT STAY HERE IF YOU WANT AMENITIES...”
text: My husband and I were down at Greektown casino and decided to stay at the hotel, the lobby is awesome but once you get on the elevator you have to put your key card in a slot to get the elevator to move and you can only go to the floor you are staying on. We opened the door to our room and it wasn't a bad room just that it didn't have a coffee maker and there is a sign saying that you can get coffee in the casino but if you are there before 6am you can't find anybody and if you step outside of the casino bums are peeing on the walls of the casino it was disgusting, no stores are open and the hotel offers breakfast but it was expensive. The bed was comfy but the room was extremely warm no matter what temperature you put on the thermostat. I would never stay here again.

title: “Great Location”
text: The Sheraton Suites is the perfect place to stay to play, relax, and enjoy. The club level room had a wonderful view and was exceptionally appointed. We were able to walk to the PETCO stadium, and the Gaslamp district. Symphony Hall is right next door. The reception and valet staff were terrific.

title: “Perfect find!”
text:
We stayed at this Holiday Inn for five nights in the beginning of December at the start of a mini tour of the States. 
We stayed in this hotel to explore LA and can honestly say we were not dissapointed. 
I had emailed the hotel prior to our stay to advise that it was a surprise for my partner (this was his 40th birthday present!!) and when we checked in the receptionist wished Steve a happy birthday and advised that they had upgraded our room to a larger corner room with a fridge - fantastic!! 
We checked in to our room on the fifth floor and it was spacious and extremely clean. You can tell this isnt a brand new hotel but everything was in good working order and kept extremely clean and tidy. We had lots of storage space, a very comfy king size bed and a nice balcony overlooking the Hollywood hills and tennis courts. 
There was a function room below and we did experience some noise, but this finished reasonably early and I cannot say it bothered us. 
There are tennis courts, a gym, swimming pool and a small shop at the hotel. 
There is also a restaurant and bar, we only used the restaurant once for breakfast on the day we left. It was very nice but seemed very quiet in the evenings. 
Ironing board & Iron, TV (not flat screen), Hairdryer all in room. NO Safes. 
Parking was not a problem - charged $12 per night. Easily accessible to get to all the sights. Right off the interstate, so you could hear the traffic but nothing major. 
It was nice staying at this hotel, as you felt safe and it was in a nice residential area but close to all the attractions - would definately reccomend!

title: “Hilton hits the spot”
text: I stayed here for 5 nights back in August. Had a room on the 33rd floor reserved for HHonors members. This hotel is huge but the view was fantastic down Avenue of the Americas. Good facilities and great location in mid town, very easy to get around Manhattan. Beds were comfortable. Great value as I had a special rate but not sure it's worth the $300+ rack rate.

title: “no air conditioning”
text: Quaint hotel, but uncomfortable because of no air conditioning. Seattle was in the 80's when visiting. Some rooms have "air" but not all. It was filled so we could not be moved. No privacy when you open windows and curtains to try to get some outside air. We finally had to move to another hotel at 11pm. Good location and price.Pay for parking.

title: “Top 4 Star Hotel”
text: Beautiful hotel. Centrally located to all the attractions that entice you in a big city. Got a great deal on Travelocity which surprised the upscale guests that were greeted alongside plain ole me! We had a blast pulling up in our Toyota next to Mercedes and Lexus's. Please try the grapefruit martini - put me to sleep comfortably each night!

title: “Comfortable and inexpensive”
text: The room i stayed in had a beautiful view, it was also very quiet. Upon checking in i was told of all the things to do in the area that night, as i was there on business i did not have the time but certainly make me think about coming back! A very nice place to stay if visiting the city on business or pleasure

title: “The only Baltimore hotel for discerning travelers!”
text:
As a frequent guest at the Harbor Court, I was stunned to read any negative views on the property. Clearly, anyone who would expect a coffeemaker in a 5-star hotel room is not the type of traveler who frequents properties similar to Harbor Court in other cities--namely Ritz-Carlton, Four Seasons, and other members of Preferred Hotels. Guests staying at Harbor Court receive top-notch servcie, but should coem prepared to pay for that service!
You will pay extra for high-speed Internet service, overnight parking, and coffee or tea (delivered via In-Room Dining 24 hours a day). But you will be pampered in ways simply not possible at the city's generic Marriott, Renaissance, Hyatt, and Sheraton hotels. From the incredible Hampton's 5-star restaurant overlooking the Inner Harbor to a huge Fitness Center that includes a tennis court with an unmatched view of the city skyline, this hotel has it all!
Insider's tips:
1. Take advantage of the afternoon tea at the casual Brighton's restaurant. During the holiday season, the Teddy Bear teas for children featuring Santa Claus are a sight to behold!
2. Sit in the alcove at upscale Explorer's Lounge to enjoy the city's finest martini while lsitening to jazz and gazing at all the celebrities enjoying the relative peace and quiet.
3. Take advantage of the hotel sedan (with tuxedoed chauffeur) to get around town. It's much easier than driving your own car through the crowded streets!
4. For recreation, play an hour of racquetball on the hotel's court while the kids relax in the spacious new indoor swimming pool. What a terrific way to work out while having fun!

title: “Clean, Quiet and Quick!”
text: Arrived at 9:30 a.m. to a very friendly reception staff who had a room ready for us. Had booked over the Internet and had requested a quiet room on a higher floor, and the staff accomodated both requests without having to be asked again. Booked a studio room with two beds. Room was at the end of the hallway, with 3 windows and a view of the top of the Chrysler building. Kitchenette was well stocked with amenities (although we never used it except for using the fridge). Very clean. Ultra-comfortable beds. Would highly recommend!

title: “Trendy, Safe & Very Fun”
text:
We stayed at Ace Hotel NYC ("The Ace"). It is on W 29th Street between 5th & Broadway. It is a super trendy hotel in midtown Manhattan. Rooms are small but on par with sizes of other hotel rooms in NYC. Nothing to be disappointed about. The room and the hotel were very quirky with fun sayings on the keycards, exits, walls, etc. It was very well done. The staff was excellent and courteous. If you want a quiet hotel, this isn't it! Energy and fun is what this place is all about. We will definitely stay again. We appreciated this hotel very much for our very first NYC trip.
-Subway is immediately around the corner
-Few blocks from Macy's Herald Square
-Several blocks from Times Square but is safe and manageable to walk
-Few blocks from Flatiron building and Flatiron district
-Stumptown coffee in the building is excellent
-Entertainment every night in the lobby
-Photo booth in the lobby

title: “Great little hotel - a gem!”
text: I've never stayed at a hotel before that ASKED you to review them on Trip Advisor. You know they must be confident! This place seemed out of the way on our GPS but we wanted a hotel close to downtown San Diego but not too pricey as we were traveling with my elderly mother who is handicapped and on a budget. Turns out the motorway is just down the street with easy 15 minute access to downtown San Diego. The handicapped acessible room for my Mother was wonderful with a huge bathroom. My husband and I had a two room suite on the second floor - nice cold a/c, cute little kitchen and two queen beds in the bedroom and a sofa bed in the main room. The pool is small but heated, no jacuzzi. Lovely flowering bouganvillae all around the complex. The breakfast room is quite small, but the choices good. However, if you are bringing someone in a wheelchair, there is not much room in the breakfast room - we had to help someone in a wheelchair who was travelling soho and it was tricky although management is super helpful to all who visit. You can get free DVD rentals at reception too! There is always coffee and free highspeed internet access in reception and the staff is very helpful at all times. Highly recommended!

title: “Loved the Ritz, Not the Location”
text: The Ritz Carlton Washington DC is a great hotel. The service is incredible. In fact, the valet knew our names as soon as we got out of the car. I am still not sure how he figured this out. We stayed here for our first wedding anniversary and it was excellent. The hotel even made special accomondations for us. The room was nice, the bed comfy, and the bathroom amazing! Although the restaurant was closed for renovations, the breakfast buffet was served with lots of choices. The only downside was the location. Its a significant walk to the National Mall and Capitol. So, if you are planning a trip to DC during a hot season, as we did, the walking will become quite a burden. Taxies are not cheap- it cost around $10 no matter where we went. The trolley system is expensive as well ($28 per person per day). I wouldn't have minded the location had the weather been nice. I'm not sure why they picked next to the Exon gas station for a location, but we never felt unsafe. However, it didn't make for a very pretty location. So if you don't mind getting a bit of exercise, this hotel was very enjoyable. Otherwise, the Willard or the Hay-Adams would be a better choice for location.

title: “Disappointed”
text:
We booked a junior suite with lake view, and expected what was shown on the web site -- a big, open large suite. What we got was a small bedroom and a small sitting room. We were on the 3rd floor, and our lake view was marred by a view of the roof of the portico and the HVAC pipes.
There was a burned out light bulb in the bathroom, and the hair dryer died during the first use. We had a man from maintenance in the room for about an hour. Who wants that? They took out the dead hair dryer, leaving us with a dinky little piece of junk hair dryer. There is very little counter space in the bathroom.
There was a leak from the toilet pipe through the wall in the bathroom onto the floor, obviously of long standing. All of this was reported to management on the form they requested us to fill out. Yet not a word from them apologizing for the problems.
The guys at the front door were first rate. People you talked to in housekeeping were just as nice as can be. But the room itself was a disappointment, and I've already steered two people away from the hotel for a visit nest month.

title: “Great location, charming hotel”
text: Hotel was wonderful to deal with. Email inquiries were answered within minutes. Check-in quick and friendly. We had asked for deluxe queen--got two doubles--minor glitch. Charming public areas. Wine and snacks at 5. Only two complaints: waitstaff at breakfast not exceptional; windows were grime covered on the outside. I have never seen filtthier windows---pretty much eliminated any view. Location is excellent--a block or two to all public transportation, a few minutes to Chinatown, one block over from cable car to the wharf. Rooms are small, as in a European hotel.

title: “Great Location and Employees”
text: One block from Capitol South Metro stop and many restaurants. Clean room with mini-fridge, microwave, and dishes. Very helpful and friendly employees. Small bathroom, but nicely appointed. OK breakfast. Great neighborhood: quiet, shady, pleasant. Comfortable bed. We would definitely stay here again.

title: “Worn out wonder”
text: This hotel is a conundrum. It is not glamouress but for a big rude city like L.A. the staff are absolutely wonderful. However the hotel is right off the 405 which for a Irish country girl was rather exciting but very very noisy. The hotel does provide earplugs but like Karl Pilkington I can hear my heart beat so I don't like them. It is convenient if you are a contestant on "Wheel of Fortune" or "Jeopardy" as there were several at the bar hoopin and hollerin like they'd won the rodeo but that's more funny than annoying. The annoying thing is the bathrooms are so outdated. They are worn and rather sad. The rooms are nice and the telly is HUGE for the room. The breakfast was absolutely FANTASTIC and the restaurant staff were wonderful. I love Hilton most of the time and I liked this hotel but one thing....IT IS NOT CLOSE TO THE AIRPORT. Do not let the reservation agent fool you. It is very very far so let the shuttle take you or it will cost you about 40 bucks.

title: “Very Pleased!!”
text: My family and I stayed here for four days due to a family member graduating from the Air Force Academy. All family members that stayed at this hotel were very pleased with the rooms, breakfast and all staffs. They let us take a wheelchair off the premises doing our stay. If I go back to Denver; I'm going to select this hotel. Thank you.

title: “New adventures with Good Friends”
text: The stay at the Westin was excellent from making reservations with a very professional and pleasant agent, Jessie. She made everything easy. Things continued to be great from arrival to departure. The staff couldn't have been more helpful and did it with a smile! There were eight of us and all enjoyed New York City!!! A Broadway show, Ellis Island, Central Park and Art Museum, dipped our feet in the ocean at Coney Island and can say we had a good time and a hot dog on Coney Island. Walked, met interesting Taxi Drivers and nice people on the Subway. Had wonderful meals and lots of laughs, only to return to our warm and comfortable rooms for an excellent nights sleep. Good Friends, Fun adventures in the Big City, at the best hotel!!!

title: “Good location. Friendly staff”
text: We stayed 4 nights in May. The hotel is in a good location and within walking distance to many of the sites including the White House, mall etc. metro line is fairly close by also to get to other places quickly. From this location, we walked to Library of Congress, White House, Smithsonians, embassy row and other places. I liked the staff. They would always smile and say hi. Everyone from the front desk staff to the bell men to the housekeeping staff were friendly. Rooms were not overly large but adequate and beds were comfortable. I would stay here again.

title: “Noisy, as in no soundproofing”
text: Ahhh, what can we say about this hotel. We were staying here on a deal from a timeshare company, so I guess we shouldn't complain too loudly BUT since when did we want to subscribe to 24 hour broadcasting of other guests' lives? We could hear everything from the rooms on either side of us and could understand their conversations. We had a mother and kids on one side, laughing up a storm and music videos followed by business telephone conversations on the other. we're sure they could hear us too, which leaves something to be desired, we're sure. They have a great location, but need to invest in some soundproofing before we would stay there again. The restaurant had good food, but was understaffed. Other than the soundproofing issue, we found them clean and comfortable. We would however, not stay here again unless it was free or close to it! Definitely not up to Best Westerns' standards.

title: “Brill Location”
text: This was our first trip to Boston, the location was ideal,room was very good, you are mins to excellent food places and shops.The hotel was within walking distance to the T(Trains) which take you to all key places.Staff were friendly and helpful.If you intend to go at this time of year make sure you take warm jackets etc,I have never felt cold like it, although you soon forget once you are walking,plenty of coffe shops to have a break. The trolley tour gives you a good view of the overall area and I would recommend this to get your bearings.

title: “For this hotel "total" price means something else!?”
text:
I booked this hotel on the hotel’s website, (I book hotels and flights always on-line so I'm quite used to it) 
At the end of the booking process, I was given a TOTAL PRICE for the stay and asked if I authorize them to charge my credit card for that amount, to which I selected YES.
3 weeks later I see in my statement a charge from this hotel for 220 USD more than the total amount which I was originally given, when I contacted the hotel, I’m told that that charge is for taxes. 
The problem is, there is nowhere in their website or in the confirmation email that I received, telling me that I’m going to be charged this extra 220 USD, there's a breakdown of the "type" of daily tax but not sign or clarification about the total amount I was due to be charged for (without my consent!) or if the tax are, or are not included in the total price. 
I felt cheated and I expressed my unhappiness and frustration for the fact that this hotel has charged me this amount without my consent, the only solution they gave me was to cancel the booking and refund me the total amount.
After this incident I’d be more than happy to do so, but unfortunately, it’s now too late to book any other of the hotels we liked, they are fully booked or prices have increased over our budget.
Conclusion: if this is happening before arriving...what can we expect once we get there? Well, I’ll let you know!

title: “Great stay, awesome location”
text: This place is awesome, elegance all the way, great value as well. Service was great, especially free nightly snacks until 9pm. Breakfast was continental and that means bacon, eggs, and Starbucks coffee!! My only con is no FREE WIFI! In the room, you can get it in the VIP LOUNGE.

title: “Great place! Very convenient.”
text: Staff was friendly and helpful. Check-in and checkout went smoothly. Room was very clean, bed very comfortable. Had a great stay and would highly recommend. Easy access to subway.

title: “Great LODO Hotel”
text: I read many reviews of this place and was a little scared to stay here but I'm glad I chose to stay here anyway. I was in town on business in the Denver Tech Center area but chose to stay downtown to be nearer to better nightlife. There were awesome restaurants, the 16th street mall, and plenty to do near this hotel. And the hotel itself was great too. My room was new and renovated and very functional. The staff was all very friendly. There was a really cool bar/restaurant connected to the building and the gym was great. The valet parking was really pricey but parking is normally expensive downtown, so you live w/ it. I stayed in the same building where the lobby was so I can't comment on the rooms in the other buildings but I was really pleased overall with my stay and would recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: “Living Nightmare”
text: This Place Is Terrible everything was good until i had rude awakening. Sometime around 4 in the morning i heard sounds of sexual intercouse. Also my toilet pipe blew and fecal matter was all over half of my room. The manager was nice enough to send a plumber to my room, and we soon found out the problem was there was a dead rat along with a few used condums That was Cloging the toilet. There was bullet holes in my wall, and in the middle of the night a african man threw a cinder block at my window. Walked into my room and asked for his XXX DVD's. I had know idea what he was talkin about??? He then kicked a hole through the wall and pulled out his XXX and then walked out. Police did show up looking for this man, and said we is wanted. I also belive he may have been smoking weed. I will never come within 50 miles of this place ever again. WORST NIGHT OF MY LIFE!!!

title: “Grand old hotel”
text: If you are looking for a modern hip hotel this is not the place for you. But, if you want stately elegance and an old fashioned decor with excellent service, this is the place for you. Location is very convenient. Rooms are a bit small and even the "suite" that I stayed in was not particularly large. But, service was excellent (including valets, check in and concierge). Even though it is a bit pricey in general, I found the package that included breakfast and parking to be a good value.

title: “If in Columbus, you must stay here!”
text: Exceptional, excellent, extraordinary! This hotel is outstanding. The area is easily accessible to the expressway. Several wonderful restaurants including their own on site. When in Columbus we ate at the Columbus Brewery Company. Yum! A must see in Columbus. The Columbus Zoo is top notch! And the Polaris Fashion Mall is a shopper's dream! Back to Weston, the staff is friendly, classy and professional. It was our anniversary! The staff made sure to make it memorable. We needed directions and the staff actually walked outside with us to point out streets. The rooms were cleaned and spacious. Some may be "put off" by the parking fee. Don't be! It is worth it to stay downtown. The gentlemen who park your cars are gentlemen who by the third day knew us by name! That is impressive. We spoke with both day and very late night staff and not one time did we have anything less than kind assistance. I can't emphasize enough that this is best hotel we have ever stayed at! Thank you Westin!

title: “Great hotel”
text:
I booked the hotel well in advance to spend a special weekend getaway. The rates were high, but extremely competetive with what else was offered in the city and much lower than comparable hotels, like the Ritz around the corner.
From the moment we arrived the attention to detail and friendliness of the staff was outstanding. My partner had a birthday and I casually mentioned that at time of booking and on the evening of the birthday we had to our surprise a lovely cake waiting for us. Our requests for ice, extra glasses etc. were taken care of in minutes and the lady giving the wake up call in the morning even mentioned the weather (it's snowing outside). Very impressive. The Lobby is grand and the rooms are stunning. I especially loved the extra comfy beds and large mirrors in the room. Having Central Park right outside just adds to the fantastic value. We had a romantic dinner once in their restaurant (which is quite hidden). Food and service was great, couldn't have asked for more. Will definitely stay there again when in New York.

title: “They gave me the shirt off their back! (Ok - their jacket!)”
text: I recently attended a 2-day planning retreat with my team at the Sheraton. Not only was the facility beautiful, parking easy, every employee prompt and courteous - but when I was freezing in the conference room (even after they adjusted the air conditioner) - the general manager gave me her personal jacket to warm up! Now that's service! She even let me keep it over night. The food was top rate too. I believe the environment and service really added to the productivity and tone of our meeting. We'll be back next year!

title: “The Service Could (and Should) Be Better”
text: Our April 2012 five day stay did not get off to a good start. We arrived at 3 p.m. and were told by a less than friendly room clerk that our room was not ready and that she did not know when it would be ready. We cooled our heels in the lobby for an hour. A curt parking valet demanded the keys to our car while we waited for our room, and he wasn't very nice about it. Meanwhile, we tried to locate three other groups of family members arriving separately. We tried to reach our daughter and her family, who were said to have checked in, but could not get them on the house phone and the less than friendly clerk refused to tell us her room number. Our daughter-in-law and one grandchild arrived in her car but were not allowed to check in because the reservation was made by her husband, who was arriving later with another grandchild. So another wait in the lobby deal. By this time we were all sorry we'd chosen this resort, which seems to be oriented to convention business while individual family guests get short shrift. Once we were all in and settled things did improve. Most of us stayed in the Casitas. Its furnishings were worn but serviceable while the carpeting was badly in need of cleaning. However, at almost $500 a night (including all the various taxes and fees) we were a bit disappointed. The grounds were immaculate, as was the golf course. The bellmen were friendly and the room service was excellent. The food was excellent and the service fairly good at Francesca's Restaurant, but the service in Brannon's Cafe and at poolside was terrible. You cannot expect little kids to wait an hour and fifteen minutes for their food to arrive. This is particularly inexcusable when the the restaurant was never more than one-third full of patrons. Formerly in the food service business myself, I recognize gross understaffing when I see it. Unfortunately I never met Food and Beverage Manager Philippe Wilhelm, about whom other reviewers have kind words; my words to him would have been less than kind. Our last family reunion vacation in Texas was at the Hyatt Lost Pines Resort near Austin. I recommend it over Westin's La Cantera.

title: “Great service, average stay.”
text:
Stayed here while visiting a friend in Houston for a weekend. It is tucked away somewhat, and the entrance is a little hard to find (thankfully my friend was familiar with the area). It's in very close proximity to the Galleria mall, and although it's tucked away from the main road this is actually a good thing as the roads around the mall can be quite hectic throughout the day.
Room: Standard fare for this type of property, but bed and linens were clean, room was tidy upon entry and bathroom was quite spacious. Water pressure in the shower was also just fine. I was unfortunate enough to have an adjoining room and there were people in the room that connected to mine. Normally this would be fine except these people smoked weed regularly (to which I did report to the front desk), and well, had some 'fun' at night which when you're in an adjoining room there is NO sound barrier and any noise comes unfiltered right through the door!!
Staff: Very friendly, courteous and gave good information. No complaints here. I had to get my remote changed for my TV as the batteries had died, and a member of the staff brought a replacement right up to my room - very appreciated.
Overall: Like I said, this is a basic property and the quality is what you would expect for a Courtyard location. Just request no adjoining rooms (unless you know the people you're adjoining with!). 
Source: I'm a Travel Agent.

title: “Great Engagement weekend”
text: My girlfriend and I stayed at the hotel and did the Tribeca Tryst-a package for engaged couples. The hotel, tribeca tryst package, and all the staff were AMAZING. No complaints at all. Breakfast in bed was delicious and all the great shopping afterwards was worth the price of the hotel. The bed was the most comfortable we have ever experienced in a hotel.

title: “Small but convenient”
text: The Club Quarters is an extremely clean hotel with great service. The location in the financial section is convenient to transportation -- the T is a block or so away. It is very quiet and nearly deserted at night but the main streets are never that far away in Boston. Smallish rooms but overall not a bad deal.

title: “Lovely hotel with just a few drawbacks”
text:
Overall we had a very enjoyable 4-day stay at this hotel. It is a beautiful facility with a rich and interesting history, which to me was a particularly relevant thing to consider when visiting DC. The down side - our room was pretty small and not quite what I was expecting. I book hotel stays through a popular discount service, and in the past I've been blown away by the quality of the rooms I get. I think most hotels recognize that these services are used by frequent travelers, so they might spoil you a bit. This time, I felt like I got what I paid for. Can't complain, but certainly not super-impressed. 
Other considerations - the air conditioning in this older building is very loud. Might disturb some sleepers, but i didn't mind the sound. It's just a "whrrrr" ... not jarring. And, yes, the parking is atrociously expensive! Look for off-site long term parking if you have a car. The Metro stop is just steps away, so you shouldn't need a car during your stay anyway.
Staff was great, attentive and professional. Food was also very good and the atmosphere was enjoyable. A good choice for a DC visitor.

title: “A Grand Stay at a Grand Hotel”
text:
We just returned from a 4 night stay at the Fairmont Hotel . The primary reason was business, and since we had a one day conference, we were eligible for the conference rate for our entire stay. We were not leaving San Francisco until Friday, but could not get the last night at the Fairmont, so we booked the last night at the Mark Hopkins which is directly across the street (the bellman at the Fairmont wheeled our luggage across for us).
The Fairmont's lobby is a precursor of things to come. The spectacular restoration of Julia Morgan's 1907 design is magnificent, and the Laurel Room (main hotel restaurant and bar) has also been restored. We found check in to be helpful even though our room wasn't ready when we arrived, we opted for the room specially selected for us by the conference manager, Sarah Zisman, with whom I had several pre trip emails trying to seccure our last night's stay. The room was large, and well appointed with a good view overlooking the landscaped courtyard. It was in the main building, which we really enjoyed, and although there are probably better views in the tower, I was really glad that we were in the original building. The bed was absolute heaven and the shower was really strong. The windows even opened which we love!
Our concierge, Nelson was always very helpful, and all of his suggestions were great. The only negative comments are about the housekeeping which was erratic in terms of towels, bath rugs, and toiletries. It seemed that the more we tipped housekeeping, the worse the service.
Overall, we loved this hotel. Location was great between three trolley lines, and we would try to stay here again.

title: “Comfortable stay in a convenient location with great service”
text:
Have stayed here a few times for business and always had a positive experience. The location is great (though the loop does close down at night), walking distance to millenium park and a block from the Willis tower.
SPG amenities make it an even better experience, with free water and Internet. Further, the personalized service adds a nice touch (TK was very responsive and helpful!).
Overall, very happy with W city center, looking forward to the next stay.

title: “Good hotel, would stay again”
text:
Stayed at the San Carlos for four nights in mid-May for $269+tax via QuikBook.com.
The hotel did not disappoint. It did all that was expected, albeit I wanted a clean, safe hotel in a good location. It's difficult to say more. Service was friendly and efficient, but our needs were probably modest.
Room also came with microwave, fridge, coffee machine, and cuttlery so could eat in the room.
Best feature of the hotel was the three free PCs for web access. It also had a wireless zone, but I didn't try this.
Breakfast - buffet with juice/tea/coffee and rolls/donuts/etc. Included in the price so makes it a better deal.
Location - one block from the subway, and plany of restaurants within walking distance - either on 50th Street, or between 2nd and 3rd Avenues and one to two blocks away.

title: “A fresh hotel with a fantastic rooftop bar”
text:
We chose to stay at the Ink48 for the last two nights of our week-long trip to New York. The hotel is situated close to the Hudson River, about a 20-minute-walk from the Times Square. Our room was more than big enough, clean and tidy, and had a comfortable bed and a magnificent city view. The staff was very friendly.
The breakfast in the hotel's restaurant was very good, but a bit expensive. If you go for it, make sure to try the homemade granola! If you prefer something simpler, there is a diner on the 11th Avenue.
Located on the roof is the hotel's most spectacular feature: The Press Lounge. This is Ink48's rooftop bar, probably one of the most spectacular ones on Manhattan. The skyline view is nothing less than fantastic, and the atmosphere is great. Definitely worth a visit!

title: “It is always a great experience staying at The Palomar”
text:
This is the place we usually stay at in San Francisco. It is a block from The Metreon and a few blocks from our favorite gallery, The Catharine Clark Gallery. We often fly up from LA for the weekend to attend openings at The Catharine Clark Gallery. The hotel seems small when you enter the lobby but it is actually HUGE. The only reason I gave it a four for location is the number of pan-handlers on the streets near the hotel. From Oakland Airport take the BART Bus to the BART Station and take the BART into the city, get off at Montgomery Station and it's less than a block to the Hotel. From SFO you can take BART directly to Montgomery Station. 
If you want a dead-quiet sleep experience ask for an inside room, no amazing view of the San Francisco skyline but, zero noise from the street.

title: “Overall decent choice”
text:
We stayed here for two days over a weekend. Booked on Priceline for $125 per night. The reception, situated in a grand lobby, nicely booked us into a King executive on a higher floor. Even though there was no view, the room was nicely sized and had an extra entrance foyer and extra door, which greatly attenuated noise from the next room. The facilities were fine. The location is great, right next to the Waldorf, Roger Smith, and Benjamin. The subway is 2 blocks away. 
On the plus side, the hotel has great architecture, much more pleasing than the minimalist look of many a newer hotel. On the negative side, the bed was much too soft, and the bedding was much too thick for the summer. The shower was somehow badly designed so that it is very easy to have water leak out onto the floor. 
Over all, a decent choice if booked at a reasonable rate.

title: “Lipstick on a Pig”
text:
This place is a 50-60s style hotel. It's extremely outdated, smells of mold, and has been brightly painted. If your thing is to stay in outdated properties, you will be in heaven. How does a room smell of mold in the desert? I don't know but the Clarendon's rooms do. Old style single pane windows mean that the wind causes them to blow against each other all night meaning you get to listen to it. I was charged a resort fee of $15 per night. This I'm used to but one of the perks to have free munchies from the in room mini bar. Problem....my mini bar never had anything in it! I left early. Not my style.
On a bright note. The staff is young and eager to please. Unfortunately, this hotel is like lipstick on a pig. It's still a pig.

title: “Best Bar in New York”
text:
Hotel is modern, the rooms are pretty much right out of "dwell" magazine very cool. Staff are great and the rooms are very clean. In New York we did not know what to tip housekeeping so we just put most of our change under the pillow each day (around 4-5 bucks) When we got back every day our room was spotless. I have to say that I have trouble sleeping if the room is dirty, not here. The cleanest hotel I have been to-period.
The location is great, you are within 3 blocks of the east west and north south subway lines (8th and 14th st) Also 1 block away from the Chelsea food market (a must see visit but only takes about 30 min to go through) as for walking if you walk fast you can count for about 45 seconds per block, but the general rule is about 1 minute. so from here to the start of central park (8th and 60th) will take you about 45 min to walk. You are within a 1 hour walk of all the museums but the subway is very safe and will take you about 5-10 min to get to where you want to go. We walked for the first 2 days and then started running out of time, so started taking the subway every where. Don't go by some 80's b horror movie, the New York system is fine very safe, very fast and very easy to understand.
Well as for the title the roof top bar seems to be the new "it" place in NYC, but as a guest you get in for free and get to dodge the couple hundred investment bakers, lawyers and stock brokers in line. The views from the roof are awesome, tunes are great and the drinks aren't that bad (about 9 bucks for a pint of stella and 12 bucks for a glass of red).
The bar is a must see I went there three out of the five nights I was there, even if it was just for a night cap.
Maurice from Kamloops

title: “Loved the W chicago”
text: My boyfriend and I stayed at the W hotel lake shore last summer. I found this hotel to be very nice. The service is great when you first walk in. There was a women who walked up to me and asked me if she could take my coat and bags and help me check in. I thought was over the top nice. We had been in the car all day so the service was a pleasant surprise. The room is not very big, but for Chicago, you can't beat it. The hotel is very modern and very cool to look at. The bathroom was very unique, it had little wooden windows you could open or close - made the room feel very cozy. The location was great - the hotel over looks Navy Pier. Nice views of the city.

title: “A bit shabby”
text:
The hotel needs a makeover. The room was clean enough but the little things like the elevators and some of the fixtures just need upgrading. Great location, though, especially if Dealey Plaza is your main destination. It's only two blocks down.
Service was very good.

title: “Yet another great stay at the Silver Cloud”
text:
Stayed at this hotel in mid June. This was our fourth stay here and found it as good as the first time we stayed, 6 years ago. The rooms are a good size, with comfy beds and very clean. Breakfast is very good for a hotel of this class with plenty of choice. The hotel is about a 5 min walk to the trolley, which takes you into the centre of Seattle...I think the hotel still has it's own shuttle too, which has a drop off service into the city. We have always found the staff to be friendly and helpful. 
I would certainly stay here again when we visit Seattle, and would recommend others to stay here when visiting the city.

title: “Great Hotel in Central Location”
text: I stayed for a week over New Year and could not fault the hotel. The location is just great for walking around the north Boton area or getting a train out to the City Art Galleries and Airport. Had an excellent meal in the restaurant and would highly recommend the Sirloin Tips and a glass of Malbec.

title: “Beautiful, pet friendly hotel.”
text: I loved everything about this hotel. The staff was friendly and very helpful. The decor was nice. Rooms were clean. Beds were comfortable. We stayed on the 11th floor. It was quiet and the view was breathtaking. Skyline, PETCO park, and harbor were visible. The 9th floor has a nice bar with fire pits and a water feature. Very beautiful at night. Walking distance to the Gaslamp. One block from ball park. My favorite thing about the hotel is that it is pet friendly. No extra charge for pets. No size limit or limit on number of pets. 9th floor has a grassy area for dogs and PETCO park is one block away. Would definitely stay at Hotel Indigo again. Valet parking is a bit expensive, but there is some public parking a few blocks away.

title: “Best way to stay in Washington DC”
text:
We moved to the River Inn for the vacation part of a trip that started in a downtown conference hotel. Have stayed there before, and this time found the hotel even better than our good memories of the earlier trip. 
• Rooms: Every room at River Inn has a small but complete kitchen, supplied with coffee make + beans and grinder, and minimal but adequate dishes and implements. With supermarket and stores a short walk away at the Watergate Complex, this makes breakfast and simple meals an economical and pleasant alternative to restaurant dependence. Our room was attractive, clean and comfortable in every respect. Flat screen tv with decent cable package. The bathroom immaculate with interesting rain-style showerhead. Climate control worked adequately, and room darkening curtains worked.
• Location: Foggy Bottom area with good metro stop closeby (Washington's subway is excellent and easy to use); hotel is on a mostly residential street, pretty and very quiet at night. The Kennedy Center is about a 15 min. walk away. I think this attractive and convenient area is a much nicer choice than downtown. 
River Inn has become our favorite hotel for Washington, will certainly return.

title: “Great stay would definitely stay here again.”
text: Brian at the Hilton honors desk was amazing! Very helpful and kind. Pool was closed but we got to swim at hotel Nikko. The front doormen were not that great. They never once opened doors for us but that is my only complaint. Cleanliness I gave a 4 just because prior tenant or maid left a washcloth wrapped around the bathroom light. I assume to dim the light but I am glad my 7 year old pointed it out to me a day into our trip. The washcloth was burned by then and could have started a fire if we didn't find it. However the stay was exceptional. I have never been disappointed with the Hilton family hotels!

title: “Consistently Great”
text: I have stayed in the Hilton Seattle Airport several times on business (most recently, January 2009) and have always had a great experience. The rooms are large and comfortable, with a great work area and lots of light. There are extra amenities in the room (body wash, robe, umbrella) that are appreciated. The hotel's breakfast buffet is very good, with a lot of healthy options. The fitness center is well-equipped and clean. The hotel's staff is particularly excellent -- in the one instance where I had a problem, it was quickly resolved. The shuttle drivers to the airport are really nice and the shuttle service is reliable and fast. The hotel has a great location, both for convenience to the airport and for using the bus to get to downtown Seattle. Highly recommended!

title: “queen of the mile”
text:
spent one night during christmas holiday. check-in was seamless, however upgraded room
not worth the extra money. hotel lobby arguably the best holiday decorations of all chicago
hotels,
room on lower floor functional w/ michigan ave view. hallways large and well lit.
all in all, for a dated hotel, very well run and a good value and location.

title: “The Omni, although classy and beautiful makes you feel at home”
text: Read the reviews, joined the select club and arrived at the Omni on New Years Eve 2009. Walked in the front lobby and admired all of the wonderful holiday decorations. Our stay was even more than we could have hoped for. We had a beautiful, spacious corner room on the 7th floor. Booked the zoo package and had breakfast and valet parking included. We have stayed in many hotels in the DC/Arlington area and none compare to the value we recieved at the Omni. Ate at both restaurants, had a minor issue with food cooked less than desired in the lounge but it was remedied promptly and the hotel manager took the time to check in with us on our stay, very impressive. The free internet and morning beverages for select members was a really nice touch. We will recommend the Omni Shoreham to friends and family and plan on returning in the not too distant future.

title: “very good option among so many offers”
text: I've been to many san francisco hotels to attend medical meeting but this isw by far the best quality-money. very well located, very good rooms and staff perfect. one day they forget to clean the room and as soon as we call, a girl came (unfortunately she did his job in one minute). we also have a complimentary breakfast (we didn´t expect so).

title: “Central and Comfortable”
text: Spent two nights here and thoroughly enjoyed the comfort and amenities provided. Very modest tariffs, very affordable. All mod cons provided in the rooms and sleeping arrangements quiet and cozy. Extremely close to shopping and food places. Woould highly recommend both for couples and family.

title: “Quaint and comfortable”
text:
I stayed here on business and was pleasantly surprised by the character of the hotel - my room was full of antiques but had a flat-screen TV and free wireless internet (which I couldn't use on my iPhone but there was a computer set up in the lobby). There is afternoon tea/cookies, and the breakfast is basic but good. There is a Starbucks about a half-block away.
The staff were very helpful and brought me a new bedside clock when mine wasn't working. The bathroom was clean, the bed was comfortable, and the shower worked well. The towels were nice. 
I was here in the winter, but there is a nice courtyard that I was told guests can sit out in during the warmer months.
The location is safe and excellent for Society Hill, Thomas Jefferson/Wills, Pennsylvania Hospital, Washington Square, and Old City. It is only a short walk to Broad St and then a short walk from there to Rittenhouse.

title: “Great hotel & location!”
text: This was a great hotel. We purchased an upgrade to get a tower room and the views were fantastic! This hotel is convenient to public transport; metro, buses, trolley and cablecar. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Tour trip in May 2012”
text: The hotel was very nice. There was a problem with the hot water so showers were quick and dreaded(cold). The restaurant next door was a 5* in food and service. This was our first trip to New York and we enjoyed all very much.

title: “Hub of Activity, Great Convienience”
text: The Hyatt Regency DFW is one of the easiest hotels to reach in DFW and can be reached on foot by walking through the garages. While the location is great, so too is the service and level of amenities available. The hotel was recently refurbished and the rooms are very nice.
