Additionally, the hotel bar and food is very good and open late to meet your travel needs. The bar tends to have a very social scene, so much so that the hotel has an annual New Years Eve party that is well attended. Many rooms have balcony's and the hotel recaptures some of the glamour of travel in the days past.

title: “Location, Location, Location.”
text: The heading says it all the Belleclaire Hotel is in a great spot on the Upper West Side in a primarily upmarket residential area, giving you wider tree-lined streets, clean and respectable neighbourhood. Our room on the 9th Floor No. 923 deluxe queen, had a view to the river and very little noise, was clean and a comfortable bed, slightly squeaky but we got used to it. Quality restaurants abound, and the fresh fruit market/supermarket on the corner is very handy. The Manhatten Diner on the opposite corner is good for breakfast and coffee is reasonable, they will deliver right to your room if required. We chose to walk all over the city but the subway was close by and taxis always at the ready. Central Park is a couple of blocks one way and the river is about the same in the opposite direction. Staying in a highly residential area gives the tourist a chance to take a step back from the busy end of town times square etc but still be close enough to enjoy it all. New York City is everything you would expect and more.

title: “Excellent value in an expensive city.”
text:
I've only got two issues with this hotel, it's a three block walk from the nearest El and the air con is noisy but apart from that it's terrific value. It's in an interesting and safe neighbourhood with good bars and restaurants within easy walking distance. The staff are amazingly helpful and the rooms are clean, the bed comfortable. What more do you want?
There are buses nearby which go into downtown and when i go back to Chicago, this is where I'll stay.

title: “Great stay over Labor Day Weekend!”
text:
I stayed at the JW Marriott for two nights over Labor Day weekend with my boyfriend. The grounds are beautiful, the room itself was not remarkable (average) but the bathrooms w/glass door shower and marble floors was nice, food at Roy's great (def go with the price fixe menu and they make great dirty martini's), Blue Sage breakfast buffet is a must (blue corn pancakes and tons of fresh fruit), the pools were large and nice (but lazy river was pretty crowded in light of the holiday - but tons of chairs everywhere), pool drinks a bit weak and overpriced and pool food not so great at all, the Revive spa was excellent (and i've spa'd at tons of places...def worth it to use the facilities. to escape the crowd that sunday we got a couples massage, i got a facial and we used their private pool and facilities, way less crowded), a quick walk across the street (10 mins) gets you to a great mall and outdoor food/shopping area (hit up Albertsons for drinks and snacks to save you from the pool side menu) - some say too far to walk but i disagree, the gym is nice and not crowded when we were there, have a drink on the lower level lobby at dusk, the in room lotion is from the spa so its great stuff (got the boyfriend to ask for extra!), take a walk at night around the grounds and lay on a lounge to look at the stars, and have the Transtyle sedan pick you up at the airport ($50 - and they make no other stops unlike the other shuttle services) and for the trip back to the airport do the same but ask for the "shuttle" that gets you on the hour ($15 and we got the same exact car .. wondering what "shuttle" means)...oh, and late checkout is pretty late so stretch it if you have a later flight like we did!
a few odd things - house keeping came pretty late in the day and forgot turndown service both nights despite personal requests (not sure if she was just too busy), heard the pool ran out of towels for a little while during the day (we got there by around 11am so not a problem for us), the room is so-so for a 5 star hotel...
finally, go to expedia for air and hotel - we got a good deal (spent more on food and spa services!)

title: “Looks can be deceiving.”
text:
Under the glowing night lights that changes colors, I entered the Clarendon hotel. The lobby is decorated with jewelry artfully displayed in cases, while a tiny price tag is also visible. The wait at the front desk was a bit long, since there was only one hotel staff checking people in and providing free night time snacks for other guests. When it was finally my turn, I commented on how smart the display was, but didn't receive much of a response from the front desk. The cost, even with a Groupon was high. (I spent $49 per night for the Groupon, then $20+ per night is required up front when I check into the hotel. That means, about $70 per night, with a discount.)
I took the elevator upstairs. I found a beautiful view of the pool area and made a mental note of swimming in this pool the next day. As I approach the glass door handle, I noticed that the handle does not seem very clean or new, even under the dim and limited night light. When I entered my room, I also noticed that the lamp was not completely clear of debris. This was the same with the hair dryer. I found an extremely unreliable wireless internet that is difficult to connect to and was supposed to be "free." 
I tried out the pool the following evening. The water was really shallow, the water was not clear, and there are no lights under the pool. It was simply not suitable for swimming in, maybe a good place to "relax." (In my mind, pools that are not used for swimming are a waste of space and result in a waste of my time.) While I was swimming, the lady at the front desk went around the pool area and rearranged towels. Since I require a high prescription to see, I had place my eye glasses and room key inside my towel. I trusted that the lady would not move a towel that had contents inside. I was so wrong. I could not see, but the lady in the front desk denied seeing glasses, did not try to find my glasses, and acted as if this was unimportant matter. Finally, upon multiple attempts and tears (I was extremely insecure being by myself, not able to see, not owning contacts, being amongst ignorance.), the lady at the front desk finally asked another staff who was doing laundry to look into the laundry. 
After what seemed like at least 30 towels he looked through, there it was, my glasses and room key are in the wash. Glasses were all fogged up, although there's a tiny scratch and the shape is not in the best condition they are still functioning. 
The lady at the front desk was, again, by herself. I don't know if that contributed to her "seeming ignorance," or if that's just the type of service this hotel provides. Regardless, this hotel is not worth even the $70. I have stayed at much nicer hotels in the area for cheaper prices.

title: “Love The Dana When I visit San Diego”
text: Great spot, nice clean rooms. beautiful pool. great service. I have stayed there 3 times and will definitely go back! The Location is awesome, close to the beaches; rooms are nice, well appointed. Paying for parking is a downside.

title: “Great Value!”
text:
After reading many great reviews on this hotel, we booked it for one night (a Sunday) during a quick day and night in San Diego. It did not disappoint! The hotel was very clean and had a nice feel and friendly staff when we walked in. Parking was $10 a day with a gated garage which was a plus and less expensive than other hotels. We arrived early so our room wasn't ready but they took my cell phone and called when we could get in. They also upgraded us from a partial view to a full view of the ocean. We loved the location of this hotel. Since we were there such a short time we wanted to be close to restaurants and the beach so we could easily walk. There are a bunch of restaurants along the boardwalk (where the hotel sits). We dealt with 3 different staff members while we were there and they were all very friendly and helpful. They even had a corkscrew available for us to use to open a bottle of wine we bought to sip on our balcony.
Only issues we could see were that while the accommodations are very clean and spacious they are pretty basic and the bathroom a little dated, with very little water pressure in the shower. However our bed was very comfortable and we slept great with the balcony door open listening to the sounds of the ocean! The free continental breakfast is what you would expect for a free continental breakfast, not bad but nothing fancy. It was enough for us to grab something quick on the way to the airport.
Overall it was a great (too quick) stay and we would definitely recommend to anyone staying in the area and we would stay there again!

title: “Suited our needs”
text: The staff was pleasant and courteous. The rooms were clean and well-appointed. Comfortable beds, large rooms, decent breakfast. Being only a three story hotel, the elevator was painfully slow. Although close to Mission Bay and the beach, the traffic in the area makes for a slow jaunt to these places. But price was right.

title: “Excellent!”
text:
We were traveling to Colorado for a family wedding in Estes Park and were attending the Rockies game the following evening. With advice to see the 16th Street Mall and wanting to stay in the heart of Downtown Denver as well as wanting close proximity to Coors Field, I decided to book with the Sheraton in Downtown Denver. I could not have picked a better hotel and location if I had traveled to Colorado just to book our reservations alone. We recieved a great rate and was more than pleased with the hotel and service we recieved upon our arrival. Our rooms were clean and had excellent views of Denver! I would HIGHLY recommend this hotel to anyone traveling to the Denver area, as well as any other Sheraton hotels.
Thank you for a great stay with Sheraton Downtown Denver!

title: “Location, Location, Location! And a good price, too!!”
text: This older but well maintained hotel is in a fabulous location, at the entrance to Point Loma off North Harbor Drive 5 minutes from the San Diego airport, directly across from a marina and seawall, and just off the very tip of Shelter Island. For walkers, it's perfect. But it is also a good jumping off point, close to the Convention Center, Coronado, the Downtown area, Sea World, and the San Diego Zoo. There is bus service steps away or easy access to major routes for cars. My room was clean and adequately furnished. The bathroom is small and would be impossible to share at the same time for two but all fixtures were in good working order. A breakfast with suitable variety is supplied accompanied by a complimentary paper. For dinner, there are several quality restaurants within walking distance and many more a short drive away. There is a lovely patio overlooking the harbour with ample chairs and loungers to use. There is an unheated pool that was a bit too cool to try on this stay but one I plan to use when I return. I can unreservedly recommend this hotel to anyone travelling on a budget who does not want to sacrifice location when visiting San Diego.

title: “Great”
text: We stayed at this hotel for over a week. There was a kind of European feel to the place.There was only one (very small) working elevator, but we were on the third floor so used the stairs. The staff was friendly, the location was great, and the bed was one of the most comfortable hotel beds I've slept on. Our view was of an adjacent office building, but I've had worse in NYC at twice the price. We booked through an online travel service (Orbitz) and got a great package. The restaurant was nice the one night we ate there. GWU is across the street, and there are many other restaurants in walking distance - including the Georgetown area. Sometimes the housekeeper left free bottled water in the room - sometimes they did not. Ditto for a newspaper. Some days yes, some no. The free high-speed Internet service was great. Overall, I'd stay there again.

title: “Location not the best if you like midtown activities”
text:
I stayed at the Marriott Courtyard Upper East Side September 8th - 10th 2006. This hotel is new ( open only about a month at the time of our stay ) and I found a great rate. I stayed with my girlfriend and we wanted to give this hotel a visit. Our regular hotel of choice is the Marriott Marquis.
The hotel is on 93rd street, upper east side, down by the East River ( hint-hint ). The cab fare, if there are no traffic problems ( NYC - lol ) to Times Square will cost about $12, so about $24 or so round trip if you dont plan on taking a cab to other parts of the city before returning to this hotel. The most we paid was $15 to Times Square due to traffic and detours. The hotel doesnt have a taxi stand but the staff will get a cab for you. The bellman actually walk down the street to bring a cab to the hotel entrance. The staff were friendly and helpful.
The king room we stayed in was clean but VERY small. The bathroom is VERY SMALL. The bed was comfortable, nothing fancy about it but it's not the worst. The pool can be viewed from a huge glass window in the main lobby. There are no restaurants , bars, or lounges at this hotel. They do have a small snack stand in the lobby by the check in area.
I give this hotel 3 stars because of the room size, bathroom size and very BASIC room ammenities. Nothing fancy, nothing shabby..

title: “Wonderful!!!!!”
text: This hotel was absolutely wonderful. I don't have any complaints .We were always busy. The lazy river was a blast, the man made beach was cool, and the bike rentals were great as well. I could go on and on about the activities but the list would be too long. My kids were very disappointed when it was time to leave. We will be back next year!!!

title: “fantastic location”
text: This hotel was very good - the location is excellent. 3 mins walk from 5th avenue shopping, 5 mins walk from Broadway & Central Park. Inside the hotel was very clean and tidy - the rooms are clean, comfortable and well stocked. The only bad thing were that you sometimes had to wait a while for the lifts. Would certainly stay there again. Fantastic time, fantastic city.

title: “A park bench might be better!”
text: Terrible service, gangs roaming the hallways, dirty room, no tissues, toilet paper or towels. We left the room for the day and when we came back they had given our room away! Thank goodness we didn't leave our stuff there too scared to!) Internet is spotty at best. If the whole town is booked except this place, you may want to consider sleeping in your car or on a park bench.

title: “Great Value”
text: I just returned from a two-night stay at this hotel and have only positive things to day. Location is great. Steps away from subway and within walking distance to Rockefeller Center and all the great diners. Room was superb, very clean and yes on the smaller side, but that’s New York for you. Hotel staff was excellent and helped us with all of our requests, even checked our luggage the day we were leaving so that we can go out for lunch. This was the New Year’s weekend and they were extremely busy, yet very courteous and professional. I have stayed at other higher level hotels in New York and they do not compare to room clealiness or staff here. I have had an excellent stay here and will definitely return in future.

title: “good location, average rooms”
text:
At the Boston Marriott Copley Place, you are paying for a big-city hotel with an downtown, upscale location. It is in the Back Bay area, and is part of the high-end Copley Place mall. The views of Boston and the Charles River from the upper floors are nice. This is what you are paying for.
My room was nice -- slightly above average but not that much different from some of the other Marriotts I frequently stay at, including the Courtyard and other lesser lines within the Marriott chain. The bed was very comfortable, and I slept very well. A nice flat-panel TV and coffee maker were in room. The bathroom was standard size, but nice and clean, and everything worked.
Besides the location in the Back Bay area, the hotel is also close to the Back Bay rail and subway station. I did not have a car, but I doubt that parking is anywhere close to free. Internet cost about $13 a day; expensive, but typical for a hotel like this.
The front desk staff was a bit confused with my room assignment, but after patiently explaining my situation several times, they overcame their reluctance to listen and finally realized that I did indeed have a problem that needed to be straightened out. However, every night when I would walk through the lobby, I'd see a line waiting to check in. On my last night there, there were at least a half-dozen people waiting in line. This should not happen at any hotel, especially one as upscale as this Marriott. For a hotel this size (there were well over 30 floors), they clearly need to put the customer first and hire more front-desk staff.
The fitness center, which is on the 5th floor, was very good, and was one of the best I have seen. There seemed to be plenty of treadmills and ellipticals, some strength machines, and even a small pool.
I was on the 28th floor, and would often have to wait a while for an elevator. Not too big of a deal. They did provide me with the WSJ at my door each morning, which was very nice. Each day my room was made up without any problem.

title: “A well priced business hotel in a great location”
text: This is a good choice for a no frills, low budget hotel in Manhattan. Rooms are good, although the rest of the hotel feels dated. Great location. If you are not too fussed about the wow factor (lack of), this is not a bad choice.

title: “Above Average Hotel for NYC”
text: Terrific location and helpful staff. Decor is very pleasant in the public spaces with a huge lobby. Room is well decorated but the bath room is tiny & needs exhaust fans. The Grand Hyatt uses T Mobile Hotspot for internet service which was GREAT. Room service prices were outrageous. But great shopping and food near by. We got a great price through Priceline so I was overall pleased considering what I have often paid for hotel rooms in NYC.

title: “We would stay here again”
text:
Location, ambience, character, WiFi, breakfast, did I mention location?
We met friends from Houston and stayed here the w/e of 9/24-9/25/2011. Both my wife and I and our friends would not hesitate to stay here again or to recommend it. We had a room on the 6th floor facing the lobby and they were in a 7th floor suite. You are literally across the street from the Alamo and only a block from the Riverwalk in a historical district in the heart of the city. Parking at $20 per day is a good deal. Free breakfast and internet were very nice. The hotel was clean, nice decor, friendly staff, and there is so much to experience within walking distance that we enjoyed it very much.

title: “The Hard Rock Rocks!”
text: I had to attend a 2 day group business meeting and the group booked into the Hard Rock Hotel San Diego. I found this to be a very comfortable, clean and modern hotel. The staff was very freidnly and helpful. It ma seem a little pricey, but it is at the foot of the Gas Lampo District and I think, resonable for it's location and quality. They could put a little more thought and monsy into their fitness room (a couple of the machines needed minor repairs) but that would be my only constructive complaint. Overall, a great hotel!

title: “Near Perfect”
text: Stayed there Aug 17 - 20. Greeted by warm and friendly staff. Every time we would go out and return, someone was there to say "welcome back." Location was perfect. We used this as a base of operation for a three-day pleasure trip and it completely met our needs. Even though it is close to the airport, no noise at all. Beautiful views of the harbor. Great walkway along the harbor and a beautiful park area nearby. Got some of the best sleep I had gotten in months. Even though it was quite hot and ridiculously humid (by San Diego standards), the room was comfy and cool. Bathrooms are a tad small, but manageable. There was a half-marathon on Sunday and the access to the hotel was blocked for a couple of hours, but the staff gave us plenty of notice and there were no issues at all. My only complaint was the parking fee. I thought $19/night was a bit steep. All in all, I fully recommend this place to everyone who wants the beauty of San Diego, but not the noise of the city.

title: “Great Stay”
text:
We had a great stay at the Doubletree. The hotel shuttle was fast and easy, just call when you land and they will be there within minutes. The rooms were nicely decorated and the beds were comfortable. If you stay on the side by the freeway the noise could be a problem. We could hear both the sounds of the freeway and the planes landing. At night with the AC on the noise didn't bother us at all and it was fun to watch the planes landing during the day.
The hotel is a 15 minute walk from the Gasslamp and about 5 minutes from Little Italy and the Center City trolley station.

title: “Just ok”
text: We also stayed over the July 4th weekend. The interior of the hotel has a modern look. Despite being Hilton Honors members we never received any free water as we normally do. Breakfast was typical Embassy Suites. Had the bacon behind the counter so we had to ask for it. Managers reception was ok. Chips and salsa with a cold nacho cheese sauce were the only things to eat. Have had better at other Embassy Suites. We did hear alot of kids running around, but if you sleep in the interior bedroom it's not a problem. On the other hand if you sleep in the outside room you could hear people walking/running around and music from the lobby.

title: “Nice Boutique hotel near Union Square”
text:
The Serrano is located a few blocks from Union Square where there are a lot of restaurants and shops. Unfortunately, a few blocks south of this hotel is near the Tenderloin, so we stayed away from that area. This hotel was also in walking distance to Chinatown and the North Beach, about a mile or so. They offer a free wine reception from 5-6 every night and coffee every morning from 5-10. We didn't order room service, but the menu looked good. The staff was extremely helpful, recommending various restaurants and offering us directions and to hold our baggage. 
I would recommend this hotel and would stay there again.

title: “Basic room on the side of the road.”
text: Conveniently located right off Exit 117 on I-71. The hotel is a bit difficult to get too as the route is convoluted. I had a basic king room. Used a coupon for a $75/night rate. Typical country Inn furnishings though the table and chairs were looking a bit worn and stained. The bed was comfortable. Pillows were ok but not great. Bathroom was basic. Limited toiletries available. Free wireless internet. Basic cable TV.Breakfast limited to cereal, boiled egg, pastries, biscuit and gravy, coffee, juice. I've stayed in nicer Country Inns with better food for less. My lower opinion of this hotel may be due to the hotels age and it looks like it gets a lot of business. There was a nice sportsbar down the street with a good steak.

title: “Very nice and comfortable hotel”
text: I like to stay here when traveling to DC. The location is good, rooms are well appointed with a luxurious bathroom. I stayed in one of the standard king rooms and was very comfortable. The staff is friendly and helpful but the poor desk clerk could have used some assistance in handling the busy morning checkout. I will stay at this hotel again.

title: “Couldn't be better!”
text: I was only there one night for a convention, but the Omni hospitality and room was top notch. Great quiet room, lots of counter space in the bathroom, and beautifully appointed. The food that was catered from there was delicious at our meeting, and healthy.

title: “A Wonderful Stay!”
text:
I stayed at the Grand Hyatt Washington DC October 16 -- 20, 2009. The hotel is in a great location with easy access to everything Washington DC has to offer! Plus it has underground access to the Metro which is nice, especially when it is raining. I had a king bedded room, Atrium view on the second floor. The room was spacious and clean. Parking a car and internet service is expensive and we did not use either service. The Grand Slam is very good and so is the deli (we at there each morning). The staff was more than accommodating. They answered all my questions and gave some good advice. 
There have been many complaints about the noise level when you are in your room. Yep, it's there but honestly, it's no worse than other hotels that I have stayed at before (and I do travel alot). That would be the only fault. Other than that, it's fine. 
If you are looking for a good, solid hotel with easy access to DC, stay at the Grand Hyatt!!!

title: “Great hotel for airport stopovers”
text:
We stayed at this hotel as we got in late to the airport one night and we were driving 6 hours to our next stop the day after. The room was large and it was great for us to have a bedroom door so that our 23 month old could go to sleep easier than if we sitting right next to him. We returned to this hotel a week later before another early morning flight and the room we had again was also roomy and the free wireless internet worked well on all of our phones and laptops.
We weren't there at the times to experience much service/breakfast/swim but the feeling of the hotel was that nothing would be too much trouble if we had to ask for something.

title: “2.5 Star for 4 Star Price”
text:
Hmm, what to say about this Marriott? It's in a good location if you want to be near touristy sights--Fisherman's Wharf, Giradelli Square, Pier 39--but it is far away from the city center.
Also, the hotel is badly in need of an upgrade. The rooms were decorated with wallpaper border and acoustic ceilings from the 70s. Walls were paper thin--we even heard our next door neighbors zipping their suitcases in the morning. Management was happy to move us after we complained about barking dogs at 8 a.m. Staff was friendly, but hotel is a bit shabby for the $200/nt price. Perhaps that's what it costs to stay in SF!
We had a great dinner at One Market in the Embarcadero area. Food was very good, service was a bit suffocating, but overall, a 5 star experience.

title: “nasty rooms”
text: The first room we were checked in was dirty, greasy face smudges on the windows, chocolate stains on the pillow cases. We switched rooms to find out that it was worse than the first one. Again, oily faces on the windows and door, hair everywhere in the bathroom, an old rusty toilet. I dried off after a shower and there was hair hanging from my body (that obviously didn't belong to me) from the towel!! We complained the next morning, they checked the first room but refused to look at the room we actually stayed in. The staff was rude and extremely lazy. They are definitely on motel standards, not Hilton. They expected a 7 month pregnant woman to walk up their hallways to find a working ice machine at 1am, rather than getting it for me themselves after me requesting it, just so the night audit can finish her conversation with an equally lazy security guard. Customer service is completely out the window with this hotel. When I tried to follow up with the hotel's manager the following days, I got hung up on!

title: “Better than expected”
text:
I read a lot of reviews before we stayed there so we were expecting it to be horrible. When we got our room key we went to the assigned room, used the key and opened to door to find the lights on, the tv on and someone's open suitcase! It had obviously been assigned to someone else! So we were nice, explained what happened and they upgraded us to their 'executive floor", floor 14. Our room did seem nicer: large flatscreen tv, balcony and ipod alarm clock. The bathroom was not redone. We didn't have any problems after that. We walked back and forth between the "uptown" strip and the Blake a few times, which was about a mile. They did have a van that would go "uptown" at the top of the hour. A lot of people we spoke to had a lot of complaints about the place. I tried to confirm our reservation before we came and had to call three or four times without any luck. I hope things get better management wise. I guess expecting the worst can really leave you to pleasantly surprised.
Note: Our other friends stayed at the highly recommended Dunhill Hotel, which they got the price of $180 for a wedding and they said that their rooms were very tiny, they were very disappointed. If that is your price range, book at the Omni down the street instead.

title: “Enjoyed our Stay: Great Value”
text: Just returned from a girlfriend reunion/get-away weekend. The Hotel Andra was a great spot for our reunion. Loved the decor in both the lobby and rooms. We shared two rooms, both with two queen beds. The rooms were clean and, while not huge, were a good size. The beds were extremely comfortable. Our view was pretty poor (the roof top of the neighboring building) but the price was right and we were on the go, anyway. The location is outstanding. We were able to walk everywhere but still feel like we were not in the heart of the "skyscrapers." The staff also were friendly and helpful. I would return to the Hotel Andra anytime!

title: “Good with a few quirks”
text:
This Homewood Suites is like the typical. The upside of cookie-cutter properties is that you know what to expect. The downside is tedium. If you've ever stayed at a Homewood Suites then you already know what to expect. Here is how this one is different and a few observations.
It is right off 1604 (divided highway). There are a couple of places to eat nearby (walking distance) but not many. However, one exit down the highway are a series of strip centers (Target, Lowe's, grocery stores, fast food etc). I found the signage a little lacking. I could see the hotel - but there are a number of businesses with different entrances and the hotel's sign was hard to locate initially.
The room has no doors except for the bathroom door - which is unusually large. It's as though the design was for an accessible room but then they changed their minds. The problem is that the door blocks the closet and sink area. If you are alone it's not a proble. If you have a couple of folks trying to get ready in the morning it would be a bigger annoyance.
The bathroom is shower only (no tub). That was fine for me, and the website may actually tell you that and I just missed it, but if I were travelling with kids and needed a tub that would have been a surprise for me.
I thought the breakfast was a little unusual in that there were no eggs. There was bacon one day and suusage the next, there were carb options (bread, oatmeal, pancakes etc) but no eggs. I was there for 2 days and it was the same both days - I thought that was strange.
The room is quite large. The kitchen is stocked with plates and utensils etc so it is quite functional. The bed and linens are good quality. The bath towels could stand to be updated - reminded me of the gym towels issued at the YMCA. 
Overall it was quite fnctional - not luxurious - but functional with a few quirks.

title: “Clean and reasonable!”
text:
We were in S.D. for Legoland and SeaWorld, and my criteria was for low rates but clean. After searching T.A. many times I kept coming back to Lamplighter. As for the hotel, the reviews are accurate. Very clean, comfortable and updated rooms.
The price really couldn't be beat. The pool was pleasant - we swam and ate dinner out there twice. Very importantly we felt safe here and weren't worried about who might be lurking in the middle of the night. 
So there is food to be found in the surrounding neighborhood, but w/ a seven yr old, grandma, Mom and Dad we really wish there was a coffee shop to sit and be served something. So, you just need to plan on stopping off the highway on your way home.
As for the extra time spent driving to theme parks and beach, it's really not too bad. I just kept reminding myself that we would be safe and comfortable upon arrival and we definately saved money. (Used a AAA discount before summer break.)

title: “Great location and great hotel”
text: The location is very good (at about the center of the 16th street mall). There are numerous restaurants and lots of activity nearby. The hotel was clean. Elevators were fast. Service was fast, friendly, and not at all intrusive. Our room was absolutely silent. The bed was comfortable. The in-room coffee was very good and convenient (no carafe). The televisions were HD and actually carried HD programming. The price we paid was good. The pool area was large and had nice views of mountains, but the water was cold. One thing that was strange was that the indoor part of the indoor/outdoor pool was air conditioned, which probably contributed to the coldness of the water. Parking was 23-26$ per night (we parked elsewhere for 1 dollar per night). Internet was free in the lobby, but not in rooms. It is because of this that the hotel gets 4 stars and not 5. Overall this hotel was a very good experience, and I was on the fence between 4 and 5 stars. Please, Westin, stop charging for internet access.

title: “Great Location”
text: Travelled to NYC for long weekend to celebrate big birthday with my friend. Fantastic location, rooms are a good size, rooftop bar atmosphere & views amazing. Great base in lively area. Would definitely return

title: “BEST HOTEL FOR THE PRICE”
text: The service was great Mr. Zapata the manager, and his staff were very nice and very courteous allways going above and beyond to make sure everything was ok. the room was very clean and confortable we enjoyded the swimming pool very much. the hotel was within 15 to 20 minutes from any point of interest or family attractions.we look foward to coming back and staying there next year.

title: “Start Spreading the News”
text: Could not fault except my trip wasn't long enough!! Check-in was swift & welcoming as were all staff! We had 2xdbl bed room which was spacious & not special request! Linen crisp & changed daily! Hotel situated for easy walking distance to Macys dept store, Times Sq, 5th Ave & Empire State building! Tik Tok Diner excellent & U can get take away too after a long sightseeing day if you want to eat then collapse ontop of your bed! I'll def use New Yorker Hotel again if I ever return to the fabulous city New York City is.

title: “Great location, no complementary internet”
text: I was here for a conference, and typical of most large hotels hosting conferences, you had to pay an additional fee for internet. I understand why, but it seems odd that if I stayed at a lower end hotel down the road, it would have been free. Housekeeping was fine, but they were always very late in the day, usually when I was coming back from sessions (around 4pm) and they were just getting to my room then. Extremely inconvenient. The staff were great however, so I really can't complain. The concierge lounge staff were AWESOME! Even if you have to pay extra, it's worth it.

title: “Might be okay under some circumstances, but not a top choice...”
text:
This hotel might be better suited for a family visit, given that they do offer apartment-style suites with full kitchens. However, I think there are better choices, especially for business travelers.
Pros: 1) Free breakfast every morning. Each day, they usually had scrambled eggs, omelots, bacon, sausage, various types of bagels or muffins, fruits, cereal, waffles (make yourself), etc. This was very popular and seems to be a big reason for staying here - particularly if traveling with a bunch of kids. 2) Free wireless internet. You had to sign in each day to reestablish your connection, but this was a good deal relative to some of the more upscale members of the Marriott "family" that are typically still charging for internet access. 3) Free dinner each night -- sort of! This might be a plus for cheapskates, but I didn't find "Chili Night" or "Soup and Sandwich Night" very appealing. 4) CVS Pharmacy, open 24 hours a day, is right next door. This is very convenient.
Cons: 1) Not as upscale as the other choices in terms of ambience and amenities. 2) Location isn't as convenient in terms of quality restaurants...you have to do some walking or take a cab (the offerings right around the hotel, meaning within a 5 minute walk, are extremely limited). 3) On checkout, they tried to stick me with a $13 movie charge when I had barely even watched TV at all during my stay. I found this curious because when I pointed the error out, they immediately removed the charge without the slightest argument or question. This made me wonder if they are in the habit of sticking extra charges on your bill, especially for those staying for five or six days as I did...they may very well figure that you won't even notice when you check out. It was a little suspicious. 4) No real lobby to speak of...this probably doesn't matter much unless you are in a group and like having a place to meet up with a sitting area, etc.
Overall, this place was is okay, but I would be very unlikely to stay there again. About the only compelling thing is that the free breakfast might save you a little money if you've got a gaggle of kids with you and want to eat cheap...the "residence" aspects, such as full kitchens, would also be useful for those on extended stays with family.

title: “Beautiful Resort - pool is amazing”
text:
My husband had a conference at the JW Marriot and I tagged along to relax by the pool! I'm sure glad I decided to attend. We had a king room with a Juliette balcony. It was a nice room - comfortable bed, couch and chair and mini fridge. The highlight of the hotel is definitely the pool area. More chairs than you can count, servers that are very attentive, a lazy river and water slides. I really liked the adult infinity pool for some peace and quiet. 
The resort is in the middle of a residential area, about 25 minutes from downtown San Antonio - rent a car if you're interested in seeing the river walk. I think they designed the resort so that you never have to leave - Starbucks, Fedex and small dry-goods store onsite. There are many dining and drinking choices on-site. The gym was nice and big for a hotel gym. I didn't use the spa, as the prices were very high. Parking is kind of a pain - either valet for $24/day, or self-park. There aren't a ton of parking spaces and it's kind of a hike to the parking. 
Very friendly staff! The resort was beautifully decorated. I would go back again!

title: “More Good than Bad”
text: We originally picked this hotel because they allowed us to bring our dog. After reading some of the reviews (very recent ones) I was a bit nervous about what we would find. Soon I discovered my worries were unnecessary. Here's the good: convenient parking across the street, GREAT location one block from Times Square.. everything is here, a clean room, an awesome shower which is so warm it's hard to leave, a comfortable king bed, and an inviting place for our puppy. If you are looking for something swank or spacious, this is not the place for you. However, if you are looking for a good deal in a fabulous location (and if you happen to have a dog) I would definitely recommend the Time.

title: “Close to everything!”
text: A friend and I stayed at the Affinia Manhattan recently. We booked the hotel as part of a special -- so we got a one room suite at a really good price. The location is perfect -- just a short walk to Times Square, 5th Avenue, Empire State Building, and Chelsea District. If you like to walk (like we do) you can walk just about any place else from here, or take the subway. The hotel is older but has recently been updated. The rooms were very modern and clean. The suite was very roomy and had great amenities. And we even got a free bottle of wine by allowing them to post on my Linkedin account. I'd stay here again.

title: “Overnight for the Denver Marathon”
text: The hotel staff was very friendly and the room clean. It had a full kitchen and a balcony overlooking downtown. It was a very close walk to downtown and near the civic center. They have a fantastic shuttle service that will take you to where you want to go in a 3 mile radius and will pick you up too.

title: “The best catering staff, food,hotel and bay views for a surprise 40th”
text:
Hello Hillary, Dbriana and the catering staff of the Mission Bay Hyatt,
Just wanted to send a quick thank you to you all for making my
husband's surprise party a wonderful success. It was such a relief to
enter the suite and see everyone smiling and yelling 'surprise'! The
room was beautifully decorated, well laid out and the food was
amaizing. The timing and taste was perfect; from the champagne toast,
passed h'ordourves, and the best large-group meal I've had since our
wedding in MN! There were countless compliments that night and in the
days to come regarding how delicious the food was. Your staff and
chefs pulled off a delicious event for 25 folks brilliantly!
Having been to quite a few large goup meals in the past, this one by
far exceeded expectations. The salmon I had was moist and full of
flavor, the steak my husband had melted in his mouth. Well done- even
with the distance traveled from the kitchen to the penthouse,
everything was still warm and fresh from the grill. I can't say enough
good things about that night. Thank you again for all your help and
energy in pulling off a very successful surprise party! Happy New
Year!
P.S. watching the Christmas boat parade from the penthouse was a wonderful treat, didn't even miss the fireworks. The room was very relaxing, the views unbelievable, well worth the splurge for one night!! I would highly recommend this hotel in San Diego, the location is not within walking distance of downtown, but is a lush hideaway from the bustle of the city and has lovely views of the harbor and ocean, almost boutique-like in style.

title: “Good value and location for business travel”
text:
Read the reviews of this hotel and worried about the room and noise. Fortunately I got a great room (1104) quiet and relatively spacious for a hotel that is more like contemporary European minimalist hotels. Not a room to lounge about but comfortable for business purposes. Breakfast at The Market was tasty with lots of healthy choices. Staff is accommodating. Hotel is located close to the subway, Suffolk Law School and New England Law 
School. Would return.

title: “Excellent Stay”
text: Great place to stay and the staff was so very friendly..Our room was located on the side of the building at night you did not hear a peep of noise..so very surprised due to the fact that we where just steps away from times square. I have already recommended this hotel to my family and friends..again i say....EXCELLENT STAY!

title: “Fantastic Stay At the Marriott Marquis”
text: My third trip to New York and the first time to the Marriott Marquis and what a delight it was, despite a few reservations about the size, it a very large hotel, everything was spot on. The rooms were an excellent size and very comfortatable, the staff all very pleasant and helpful, and it had nice touches, like a Starbuck on the ground level, a decent giftshop, plenty of restaurants, and a theatre. Whilst it does host conventions and can be quite busy, this had no effect on our stay, as the conference rooms were on seperate floors. The lift system was excellent although some found it a bit confusing, but in reality it was pretty simple. On the top two floors they have a rotating resaurant and lounge, and this is spectacular if a bit pricey, but worth a look all the same. Also a great location right in the heart of Broadway & Times Square. An impressive hotel all round.

title: “Friendly staff and perfect room for the occasion”
text: The service at the hotel was unbelievable. When I explained the special occasion my fiance I were celebrating the upgraded our bedsize and also gave us a high room with river views. It was absolutely wonderful. While I agree with many reviewers that the rooom is quite small, I found it to be a very cozy small. I did not find it anxiety provoking and it was nicely set up. The lighting in the halls was perfect. The only weird thing was the window between the room and the bathroom, although a curtain could be closed. It may not be ideal for extended stays in New York, but for short stays I think it would be perfect.

title: “Ridiculous Management”
text: We recently stayed at this hotel with our sports team. The hotel management acted like they had never had a sports group stay there before. They seemed like they were not aware there would be 100 8-12 year old kids at the hotel. They had hired 3 security guards that were searching peoples ice chests, taking away their pizza by the pool, and just outright harrasing our families. In 1 word it was RIDICULOUS. I would never reccomend this hotel to anyone let alone a sports team or group activity. This is probably a very nice hotel for the business traveler who goes to bed at 9:00 pm. But I will NEVER spend another dime at any Hilton hotel because of the poor treatment my friends and I received.

title: “CLEAN, COMFORTABLE and COZY”
text: I attended a conference there in December. My daughter attended with me and we stayed for four nights. The room was clean and the bathroom was especially nice and clean. The housekeeping staff was helpful and friendly. The room was cozy and very comfortable. There was a turn down service that put chocolates on your pillow. There is a mini bar and snacks in the room that you have to be careful not to open or even remove to look at or a sensor will go off and you could be charged. The hotel provides a small refridgerator for your room upon request. They offer very large and soft towels and robes. They offer complimentary slippers. Also it is convienantly located to lots of places to eat. In the evenng there was a piano player in the lobby and if your there for a conference, it gives it a nice atmosphere to hang out in the fancy lobby and meet people and visit. NICE! The elevators are old and a little scary and small. Not real convienant for handicap or wheelchairs but they can fit, its just a tight squeeze. The only downfall is that it is so noisy that you can hear every word and yell on the street. The windows are old and thin. We bought earplugs at CVS across the street at the mall and that took care of the rest of the week! Love the art gallery and luxurious furnishings of the hotel. The food for the banquet was great!! We had a great time the conference and enjoyed our stay. Thanks to the owners! Plus they treated us with alot of respect as minorities. =)

title: “A peaceful luxury hotel in the heart of Manhattan”
text:
Arrived in NYC after a few days in Boston and Rhode Island - lousy long drive down because of road accident on Interstate - arrived late afternoon in 100 degree heat - Omni was a joy to arrive at - bell staff were incredibly customer friendly. Very easy and quick check in. Very welcoming bedroom. Maitre D' in Firesides Restaurant and Bar was very customer friendly (hope he enjoyed his holiday in the Andes the following week). Concierge staff very helpful and friendly. Liked the free beverages in the room on wakeup and the free wifi (part of the Omni frequent guest membership), Enjoyed breakfast in Firesides.
Hotel is very central for shopping and for theatre.
Minor downsides - toilet blocked twice - but maintenance staff arrived very quickly to resolve the issue. One (European?) member of staff at Reception was a bit curt. Barman in Firesides was very abrupt on a couple of occasions. Business Centre available but cost to use PC and to print / fax.
Don't go to the cafe across the road - tried breakfast there - very average food, and very very hot inside (no air conditioning?)
But defintely a great hotel for our visit and would absolutely be prepared to stay there again.

title: “How do you feel when staff treat you like a pig”
text:
We have stayed at the standard, lovely location, nice concept.
But... my wife went to the bar at 21.46. this is important because the 18th floor bar closes at 10. She is told that last order was 15 min before closing at which stage she looks at her watch and notice 9.46
meanwhile i went to drop something in our room and after waiting for 1 of the 4 elevators for the 350 rooms + outside guest flocking, i arrive at the bar trying to find her.
then it becomes really great. Security comes to me and put a hand on my shoulder - which is already unacceptable - and say excuse me sir (politely) you have to come out of the bar; when asked why he adds that i am dressed in a pijama and they have a strict dress code policy. 
I have problems beeing treated like this. My pijama is a cool pair of pant i bought a few month ago in tokyo.
I am not expecting security to be "au fait" of what guest buy where, nor do i expect to like my clothes.
But i cannot accept security to physically intrude on my shoulder and make value judgement of the way hotel guests are dressed.
This for me is fascism and it has no place in the service industry.
We are leaving tomorrow and will spend another week at the crosby, a fantastic hotel in soho where service is top.

title: “Cramped Noisy Rooms, Never Again!”
text: Very uncomfortable stay. Double beds which are way too small for two people have been squeezed in a very small room with just a few inches left around them. Almost no sound proofing in walls or the window which is literally 6 inches from your sleeping head. You hear every inconsiderate person walking by, and every car starting or parking only 4 feet from the window. AC is loud and doesn't work right so you have to leave the window open which makes it even noisier and more unsafe. The toilet flush sounds like an F16 preparing to take off and you can here same noise from every neighboring room. Otherwise, it was okay.

title: “Excellent hotel with excellent service”
text: We stayed at the George several years ago and happily returned to it on this trip to Washington. Partly, we returned to the George because the hotel is SO CLOSE to everything we want to see and do and the hotel itself is so nice. Parking our car (valet) was $40 a day but it was worth it because we didn't need the car and wanted it in a nice safe place. Taxis are easily obtained to find a restaurant but Bistro Bis, attached to the hotel is delicious and they went out of their way to make sure everything was attended to. Dinner was especially good and easy to get to, since we didn't need to go outside.

title: “Great location, good service, a few deficiencies”
text: Hampton Inn is a reliable brand. This location is great for access to the convention center or to "uptown" which is really "downtown" as most of us would know it. The service was great and very welcoming. While the basics of the room were fine, the aroma left much to be desired, especially for those with delicate respiratory systems. Not sure if the artificial aroma was there to mask something or just a freshener, but it was very unnatural and unpleasant. Because I like Hampton Inns and because the staff was most accomodative, I hate to give a bad rating, but I feel I must be honest. Attention to room air quality should improve client satisfaction.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: We have just returned from a wonderful five night stay at the Fairmont Copley Plaza Boston. From the moment we stepped in to the Hotel we were met with smiling friendly faces. The Hotel was very nicely furnished and will be even better with the renovations that are going on at the moment. We had no noise from these at any time during our stay. Our room was very large with two queen sized beds and a large walk in wardrobe and the bathroom was huge. Our room was clean and tidy and much better than what we were expecting due to some of the negative reviews of the Hotel on this site. We had breakfast in the Hotel every morning and the waiters were extremely friendly and efficient. We also had free wifi in our room after signing up for the Presidents club online. They have a resident dog called Catie Copley who was able wander around the Hotel and even had her own bed in the Reception area and guests were able to take her for a walk. The Hotel is in a great location and we walked everywhere We would not hesitate to stay at this Hotel again if we ever returned to Boston.

title: “Great hotel; great location; great price”
text: Stayed here for two nights on a first time to Seattle. Alternatives were expensive downtown hotels with outrageous parking, or this hotel that was a short distance from downtown, with cheap underground <secured> parking, for half the price. Glad we chose this hotel. Rooms aren't big, which is fine because we were only there for the nights to sleep. The beds were extremely comfortable. Staff were great, very friendly, helpful, and inviting. The rooftop was a bonus. Great views of downtown Seattle and the harbor/bay. If I was to go back to Seattle, I would def stay here again. Hidden gem.

title: “Great hotel, great staff, great food!”
text:
Just returned from 3 days in Seattle where we stayed at the Hotel Vintage Park. Exceptionally friendly and knowledgeable staff who went out of their way to assist with any need. Trulio, the attached restaurant is outstanding and has a comfortable clubby atmosphere. The rooms are comfortable and well appointed.
A wonderful small hotel in downtown Seattle.

title: “Scam alert - all rooms non-refundable, charging you extra & deceptive practices”
text:
Room types are listed as: "Traditional King - Non-refundable" and for $25 more, "Traditional King."
Now, a rational person would assume that one of those room types is refundable and one is not. That you are risking saving $25 if you are 100% sure plans will not change. Sadly, this is not the case. both room types are non-refundable, and they are happily ripping you off if you choose to pay $25 extra in case plans change, because if they do, you will still be billed in full.
Shame on you, Sheraton Tribeca.

title: “BHT best hotel ever”
text: Best hotel ever kind staff huge rooms like St. Regis and four seasons hotels new York but cheaper just scary it was robbed in 1973

title: “Nice Hotel in the Financial District”
text: I just stayed at the Gild Hall it was a nice hotel well placed for our purpose but I was very surprised there was no free WiFi you would think in today's world it would be just there no questions.

title: “A Perfect New York Experience”
text: Spent five nights at On The Ave and couldn't recommend it enough. Perfect location as it is two blocks from the subway at 79th Street and five blocks from the 72nd Street station where you can take the #2 and be in the middle of the Theatre District (42nd Street) in one stop! Had a room on the 16th floor with a spacious terrace looking toward the Hudson River. The room was generous by any standard with the most comfortable bed in the world. Also had a comfortable sofa and chair. The Front Desk staff and Bell Staff greeted us every time we arrived or departed for the day. You're in a great walking neighborshood close to Central Park and too many restaurants to count. Plan to return in December.

title: “Funky and different”
text: We stayed in a painted room. The one that looks like the Unibomber's hideout. We liked it. We had a private bathroom and it was narrow, but the water pressure was fantastic. It was cheap for the city and in a great location. Right at the gate to Chinatown but within a few blocks of Union Square. Traveling in their old-timey elevator was cool too. If you're looking for something unusual, stay here, if your looking for luxuary, this is not your place.

title: “Great Hotel for Families”
text:
Great Hotel HUGE by NYC standards good beds clean nice and well taken care of !
all in all a very good hotel
A word of Warning aboutr "black cars" vs taxis taxis are usually WAY cheaper and metered please please if you have any questions ask your bellman.

title: “Overall was ok”
text: Compared to other Residence, room were very small and I had a Jr Suite (two rooms). Rooms seem to be crammed with furniture. Their staff was excellent and very helpful. The first few days the train was a nouisance but after the third day I got used to it. Not enough parking available and $12 per day.... Recommended for business travel only.

title: “Excellent Night”
text:
Only staying one night in SF so we thought we would give Parc 55 another go (last time was excellent, but we like to change up hotels for fun). I called and made reservations direct with them. It was an extremely great rate, but was for two double beds when we would have liked a queen or king. Got to the hotel and CHRISTINA at the front desk checked us in. I asked if they had the possibility of changing our room to a queen or king. She did it for no charge and on top of that got us a corner room which was perfect with full wall length windows all around. 
The location is great because it is slightly off all the busy streets but is central to Union Square, Market St., Trolley Cars and BART. Had drinks at the bar which is very nice and went out that evening. 
Hotel is clean, modern and great service. Only downside would be that parking there is very expensive, but you could always park in a public garage not far away. Would definitely stay again!

title: “Allergy to cigarette smoke”
text:
I have been looking forward to my stay at the W hotel since Feb. when I booked my "fabulous suite". I arrived at the hotel today only to find that the hotel staff ran out of non-smoking rooms and stuck us in a smoking suite. Given that I have had bronchial infections in the past, I was insistent that they accommodate us to what was available until a non-smoking suite opened up. The only option we were offered was to downgrade our room so that the 3 of us would share 1 bed, OR upgrade it even further for a significant fee. It felt like they were looking to crank out couple of more bucks from us. Ultimately we were given no choice but to stay in our room and open all the windows to air out the second hand smoke and this has only soured the experience even further. I understand circumstances occur but in the case where the hotel gave away our room, they should have made reparations for mishandling our reservations. Extremely disappointed, travelers beware!
Ourcheck-in staff did not seem to care and made no effort to help us find another room that is non-smoking.

title: “A great find!”
text: We stayed at this hotel during Fleet Week Oct 8th. 2005 and it was a last minute booking via an online website. The rate was excellent considering it was 3 days before our arrival. I loved the location steps from Union Square, the quality of the furnishings, the helpful staff. Our room was on the 2nd. floor facing the hotel's air conditioning vents which meant we had to close the blinds all the time. No matter, the room itself was tastefully furnished, clean and the in-room fridge, iron & coffee-maker very convenient. Ate breakfast at Lefty O'Douls twice. Also ate their great hand-carved roast beef sandwiches for lunch. Would not hesistate to stay there again.

title: “Take your ear plugs!”
text:
The hotel is undergoing major renovations and we got a great room with plasma TV and lovely clean beds. However, with renovations comes
....noise! Noise from 7am drilling and banging not to mention all through the night police sirens. The hotel is not far from the hospital so if you stay here ask for a room as high as you can and away from the street. The staff were very helpful and gave us ear plugs!!.The hotel is situated between 2 metro stations and is a 10-15 minute walk to either. Bear this in mind when you have walked your
feet off in washington all day. The hotel gave us a map of places to eat in the area and gave us the impression that the nearest and best place to eat was the hotel. So each mealtime we waited up to 20 mins for a table and breakfast was an unpleasant and expensive free for all. However there are many eateries on M street just alongside the hotel! If you do go sightseeing in Washington and the Smithsonians, I advise you to take sandwiches as the area is devoid if places to eat. Toilets are the portable stinky potties too! Still, I'm sure this hotel will be great when finished!

title: “Overbooked Again! "Walked" to Sofitel”
text:
Booked through Hotwire and confirmed reservation directly with the Westin. We arrived at the front desk to be told they "overbooked again", apparently this is a common occurance. They initially said they would get us a room at the Sheraton. I expressed dissatisfaction with that option and was told they try not to, but they could get us in at the Sofitel. I had seen the Sofitel on here and knew it would be better, so I was happy with that! The gentleman was fairly nice about the whole thing and thanked me for not chewing him out "like people normally do when this happens"
So long story short if you book the Westin be prepared to possibly walk to another hotel. It wasn't too far to the Sofitel, but in 20 degree weather, a couple blocks didn't feel great
I also reviewed the Sofitel

title: “Can't imagine it being much better than this”
text: Location, location, location. Cleanliness and attentive service. The only knock--and this may have been just a one-time thing--we didn't find the concierge as eager to help as we might have wanted. Still, superb hotel in a most excellent spot in NYC.

title: “highly overrated, stay away”
text: I booked Hotel 17 following the brillant reviews it got on TripAdv. I was highly disappointed as I found a rundown hotel with a miniscule room (just big enough to fit a queen size bed, an outdated small bathroom, a noisy malfunctioning aircon and a window facing a wall. I had booked for 4 nights but decided (wisely) to change hotel after the first since upon enquiring with the desk they told me that all double rooms are alike. Certainly not worth the price, stay away from it, with just a few bucks more you can stay at a much more decent hotel in manhattan.

title: “Best NYC Hotel experience in a LONG time”
text:
I travel to NYC 5-6 times a year on business. I usually stay towards midtown in the Royalton, Algonquin or the Iroquois to be close tot the office. This time I was looking for a change, and a good deal. 
I had heard some good things about the Standard, and though I had a poor experience in the Los Angeles Standard I decided to check the new NYC location our none-the-less. 
The room was perfectly appointed. Great bathroom complete with a shower featuring a natuaral rain style shower head - nice! The floor to ceiling window along one entire wall was amazing, provided great views, and made the room feel a little more spacious. The bed was top notch comfort - great linens and pillows. My room featured a small couch and table that were perfect for working. 
Its rare to stay in a hotel room that feels like home. I loved this room - to the point that I was actually a little sad to check out. 
I love the little diner in the front of the hotel - perfect place to grab a great breakfast before starting your day. Try the steel cut oatmeal with raisins - awesome on a cold NY morning. 
The only tricky part is the locations, while its quite beautiful with the highline and the river right there, it is a ways from the subway, meaning more cabs than I usually like. But in the end the hotel was so perfect Iplan to stay ythre every chance i get...

title: “Our Go-To Hotel Anytime We Travel to NYC”
text: This is the second time we have stayed at the Casablanca Hotel and it won't be our last. Perfect location (amazing to be conveniently located in Times Square and not know it -- the hotel is incredibly quiet and peaceful inside); amazing, friendly staff; charming, clean, and spacious rooms; and a wonderful daily continental breakfast and wine and cheese evening reception (not to mention free snacks and beverages available 24/7). This trip, my birthday happened to coincide with our travel dates -- the hotel upgraded our room for free and gave us a lovely bottle of wine to celebrate. Quality hotel, quality experience!

title: “A Relazing Stay”
text:
Just returned from a 2 night stay at the Plaza. From the moment we checked in until departure every member of the staff we came in contact with was fantastic, great customer service. We arrived early so our room wasn’t ready. She checked with housekeeping and said it would be about 10 min. She was correct and 10 mins later were in our room. 
As mentioned on other reviews we asked for a room facing town vice the interstate. We were on the 8th floor (818) and extremely happy with the room which had a king size bed. Water pressure for the shower was great along with an endless supply of hot water. The shower head didn’t seem to be attached to anything in the wall. Not a big deal since it worked great.
There is free WiFi and our room did have a mini frig.
Ate breakfast twice. Off season so no buffet so ordered off the menu. The omelet was large and very filling. My wife enjoyed the fruit platter. Service was fast and friendly and food good. At first thought the prices were a little expensive but after checking other hotels they were in line.
Self parking is $15 per day and valet is $18 per day. Parking is in a controlled area. Parking lots cost $5 per day across the street but not secured as is most parking around Beale St. We used the hotels shuttle service once (very satisfied) but decided after to use the trolley with access across the street through the Marriott lobby next door for the experience. After check out the staff let us keep the car in the lot until we returned later in the day.

title: “Basic But No Complaints”
text:
Yet again another great Tripadvisor recommendation! 
The most important thing was the room was clean and functional. Only slightly disconcerting that there was a mouse trap on the floor but I hope this was there as a precaution! The room did seem clean and everything was functional including a nice TV and fridge which was handy to keep drinks in. Nice clean sheets and comfy bed. The room was also surprisingly quiet given we were in the "city that never sleeps"
Also great location, lots of restaurants on 8th - 10th Avenue and only 10mins from Times Square!
Staff friendly and helpful and a free left luggage room which was very handy.
All in all a fairly basic hotel but no complaints and exactly as expected. Great value for New York and great location.

title: “Excellent New Years Eve Location and Price”
text:
Our friends and we come to Philadelphia each New Years to meet some other friends who live in the area. The out-of-towners usually stay in another hotel, but I felt their rate had gotten out of hand this year. I checked TA and we decided to try the HI Express.
We were not disappointed at all. The location was great, the staff courteous, the room clean, and the price right. The system for checking guests on this very busy night made us feel very secure coming in and out of the hotel. When we checked out on New Years Day, there was a delay in getting out of the parking garage, so we were literally one minute too late when we reached the parking gate, which would not open. The front desk employee came out, explained to the parking attendant what happened, and we left without any hassle or unfair charge. The whole experience was excellent, especially for the price. 
If you want a pool, this hotel's isn't available in the winter because it's outside. Other than that, this hotel was perfect for our needs.

title: “Very Nice Stay!!”
text: Hotel is very clean and comfortable! Would stay again. Only complaint is that I was a little annoyed that the front desk knew we were parking vehicles, told me where to park and how to get there but did not explain that we would have to pay the front desk to get the discounted price. My brother-in-law had to run all the way back to the hotel from the garage to pay and run all the way back as we were already running behind schedule.

title: “Nice Hotel in a great location”
text: We recently returned from a long weekend trip to NYC and stayed at this property for 2 nights. It is right in the middle of Times Square, convieniently located to everything you desire. We were on the 24th floor facing 7th Ave, so it would get a bit noisy. We requested a great view so we were prepared to live with the sirens and noise for the great view. The beds were very comfortable with plenty of pillows. The bathroom, while a little on the small size was fine for the two of us. I would definetly stay here again on our next trip to NYC.

title: “Probably worst quality hotel I've stayed in”
text: We were travelling with a 5 month old. Despite assurances on the telephone when we booked that the room had basic facilities such as access to a kettle, this was not the case when we arrived. I had to order a kettle of boiling water everytime I needed to make a bottle. The bathtub was filthy, the shower head fell off and banged me on the head, the plug didn't seal properly so we couldn't have a bath. After complaining, we were moved to another room. We required a room with 2 beds, and the 'equivalent' room we were moved to had a king and a sofa bed, the latter of which was not fit to be slept on and had apparently already triggered 'quite a few complaints' - why not replace it then? The fittings were shoddy - the shower door handle fell off when I tried to close it. despite making it very clear that we were deeply unimpressed with the room and how our complaints were handled, we were only given a room rebate of 1.5 nights, despite staying the for 4. For the price being charged per room, we would not book here again. Oh, and charging guests $15 per day for wifi is criminal.

title: “Wonderful Lobby”
text: Visited with two children and had very large interconnecting rooms - ideal. Lobby is amazing. Swimming pool a great asset and very quiet early in morning. Lots of restaurants nearby.

title: “Great service”
text:
We stayed here in January while in town for a wedding. We were very near Dupont Circle so couldn't have asked for a better location.
The hotel was very clean and designed in a modern style. We did have an issue with our first room --- noise from something mechanical --- but the staff were attentive and accommodating. They moved ustina different room on a higher floor and it was perfect -- very clean and very comfortable. 
We had dinner in the restaurant and the food was quite good. My husband had a very good lamb shank and I had crab cakes. We were actually surprised how good the food was!
I will definitely stay here again. For the price, this place was a steal!

title: “Make sure Miriam writes your group rate down”
text: I called and spoke to Miriam to inquire on a group rate that I qualified for. She gave me the rate which was good. Later, when I spoke to her again - she advised me that she didn't give me that rate because she didn't have it written down???? She raised the rate tremendously and didn't apologize for the inconvenience or anything. I was so furious that I cancelled and ended up booking elsewhere.

title: “Excellent”
text: The Concierge--Ariel, helped find my roommates aunt and uncle, whom she hadn't seen in almost 18 years. They had a glorious reunion. She got us a discount on our trip to the beautiful San Diego Zoo, and had information for everything we asked her about--which was a lot! We also had a woman help us with our luggage, and many more questions, her name was Beth. They made our stay be the best time we could have possibly had! I have to say, this was one of the trips of my life! The entire staff at TOWN AND COUNTRY was gracious, helpful, and accommodating!!!! I have a brace on my knee, and they had someone pick us up and take us wherever we needed to go, in a short time they would arrive, even though there were several of us who needed a ride. THANK YOU SO MUCH!!

title: “Nice hotel, very conveniently located”
text: Visited the Renaissance for 1 night in mid-April with 2 friends. We had a nice 2 queen room, plenty of space for the 3 of us for the night. The hotel is undergoing a lot of renovation, so looks a little construction-y, but should be great when its all done. This hotel is very convenient to everything in the harbor area. We were able to walk to Fells Point, Little Italy, and the Power Plant area. Cabs were also easily obtained in the overhang of the valet area. Our car was valeted & very quickly brought back to us when we turned in our ticket. Overall, it was a nice stay!

title: “worst trip to Austin Texas ever”
text:
I was referred t the Crowne Plaza by a Friend and was excited with my accomodations,but wait the next day disaster hit all week.I was in the Bar checking my email ,I finished and told the Mgr himself I was taking my laptop to my room and I would be right back to eat dinner.
by the time i got to my room my phone was ringing and the MGR said I left and dint pay my tab,i told him I was comin right back and was going to eat,what a jerk this person was.Then some customer namedafter Grover Cleveland was whispering sweet nothings in the pregnant Bar Maids ear and He looked at me and toldme to mind my own business,I wasnt doing anything just waitin on a drink soda with my meal ,this guy got all irrate ??OK,i'm ready to leave this property,,but not before I was refused Breakfast when I had a Platinum PC card that entitles me to free breakfast,Malcolm the F&B MGR fixed that,Thank You Malcolm.Then at check out there was only 1 person athe the front desk and she informed me she was the best and she was a Manager (Pat Vaughan)she was trying to check out 3 people at a time and messed up all of our folio's,got my PC number wrong and handed me the guy besie me his receipt,its sad cause this is a nice place and could be a grea stay,but not with the Employees workin there now,Malcolm Leslie is the only Good Manager at this Hotel.

title: “I'd Stay Again”
text: I wasn't looking for luxury or 1st class service. I wanted A/C, a double bed and a shower/bathroom. Was there something left to be desired? Of course. But I didn't get bitten by beg bugs, I felt safe during the night, nothing was stolen from room/vehicle and everyone was friendly. We never used the pool but we saw other people enjoying it. Don't go there if you want everything to be perfect and spotless. Stay there if you are rarely going to be in the room and all you want is a place to sleep, shower, and stash your things. I'll stay there again. It's about a 10-ish minute drive to downtown and the neighborhood is decent. We never saw shady characters and even though it's right next to I-35, we slept soundly. Watch out-the hot water gets hot real quick. We got the room on the Saturday of the Memorial Day weekend.

title: “Mostly good”
text: If there was a way to rate 3.5 I would. The hotel has a nicely renovated lobby with the lounge theme found elsewhere, nice cafe area, self service computers and free coffee (breakfast is not included). It does not appear that the renovations have continued upstairs to the rooms. My room was nice, but had a dated appearance. The hallways have that DC Federalist style with wallpapers, carpets, generally nice but a bit worn. Staff was doing touch-ups while I was there - like repainting the trim around the elevator doors. The room was very small and had good furniture but the mattress was very old and soft, it hurt my back. The bathroom is tiny and with a pedestal sink so there is no counter space. The closet was tiny and there was really no place for me to place my rolling suitcase in a flat position to pack/unpack. The door to my room did not close tightly, wide enough gap to allow bright light to shine in all night - it also meant I could hear all the commotion in the hallway, screaming child running around until midnight everyday (I think my parents always had me in bed hours earlier, even when on Holiday...) An update on the wifi - it appears to be complete throughout the hotel and works well in rooms and common areas. The staff is very friendly and seemed eager to please. I think they are trying to make the best of their situation. Overall this hotel is mostly good, I just hope the guest rooms get an update like you find in newer Courtyards, this place could be real gem in the Courtyard family. There is parking on site for $29/night, which is typical of DC prices. On-street parking is available in the neighborhood but the regulations are tough - 2 hour limits until 8:30pm and then starting again at 6:30am.

title: “Only worth staying if you find discounted accomodation online...”
text:
I've stayed here twice now, both times I found discounted rooms online. I would never pay full price for this hotel, it's a fantastic hotel but you only really stay there because it's the "Ace Hotel".
Sleep quality is average....29th street is quite busy and always congested with honking taxis. Try request a higher hotel room if you can. 
Front desk staff need more training....I've come across the same front desk lady twice now and she's as cold as ever. Check-in was for 3pm but our rooms weren't ready until 4:30pm. She apologised and gave my friend and I a drink token to use at the bar. We sat there for at least an hour and you would think she would've come got us to tell us our room was ready? No she did not, I had to go back to the front desk and ask her what was going on and she gave me this doe eyed look like she'd never seen me before! Only after did I ask if our room was ready again she kind of shrugged it off and said "Ohhh....yeah it's ready now"......weird.

title: “Very satisfying”
text:
I have to my stay was very satisfying. The beds were super comfortable, I slept like a baby for the two nights I was there. I thought New York hotel rooms would be small, but the this hotel, the rooms were fairly decent. The hotel was maintained very well, clean, and friendly staff. I couldn't do much or use the facilities or ventured around a lot, however, from what i saw, there was no pool, not sure if there was a gym. 
The bathroom products were bath and body works products, and it was very nice.
I would definitely stay here again next year when we go to New York!

title: “Gives Comfort a new meaning”
text:
A very nice place to stay in a city that we love! We slept great every night on the comfortable beds. The staff members were quick to respond to our every need, from the front desk team to Vivian, our favorite housekeeper, who gave us a warm welcome and cared for us like family. 
The coffee, cookies and ice water in the lobby were nice touches and the breakfast started our days off right. It's not a fancy looking hotel from the outside, but its cleanliness and friendliness inside more than makes up for it - like a hidden gem.

title: “Perfecto”
text: My friend and I just stayed there for two nights. I was surprised at the cleanliness of the room and the up to date paint, wood moldings, windows & bath fixtures. Small but a great value. Linens were fresh and ironed. The staff were more than friendly and courteous. I would definitely return and recommend to others. The location is great for shopping both small shops and the large dept. store, "Century 21". One must go there for the experience. The coffee caffe and the restaurant are each separate and both were so lovely. Parisian influence. The wait staff were so accommodating.

title: “The Hotel George is a conveniently located hotel with high quality service and fun, free extras!”
