text: The hotel is very clean and inviting. The staff are very friendly and always give great recommendations. I was able to check in early without a problem, and had no problems during my four night stay. Be sure to take advantage of the free happy hour!

title: “Excellent but old-fashioned”
text:
Looking at its website before arriving, I was worried about not liking the St Regis. In general, I do not like classical-style hotels in the US, but the excellent service and very comfortable rooms won me over. The St Regis is an exceptionally well-run hotel with fantastic staff in a perfect New York location. For this style of hotel in NY, I still prefer the Peninsula but it is a very close race.
Right from the moment I arrived, everyone was unfailingly friendly and polite: nothing was too much trouble, and every single person who met me greeted me with a cheerful smile. The butler service was much more practical and useful than other hotels I have stayed at: the butler was very friendly and seemed to take a great personal pride in sorting out whatever you requested. Room service breakfast was excellent, and good value compared to other NY five star places.
The rooms themselves do the very best they can around the old bones of the hotel. They are decorated in a clean, classical style--my Astor Suite was in a muted yellow with silk wall panels, while my colleague's Grand Luxe room was in a light duck egg blue. Both were good sizes and well laid out, with classical marble bathrooms that are a good size and well-equipped. 
The Astor Suite suffered from the very small windows you get on the top floors of the building, but in return for that the views were good. For me, given the hotel's short height and location, none of the views are spectacular: just nice views up and down the grand streets. The Grand Luxe room was much brighter, but you only really saw the fronts of other buildings from the windows.
All the facilities worked excellently, as expected at this level. Good high-speed internet and excellent climate control in both rooms. Given this and the fact that all services are 24h, it makes a great hotel for business travellers as well as a luxurious place for a holiday. 
Value-wise it's very expensive but on a par with the other five star places in NY.
I only stayed for one night but I definitely want to go back and try the place again.

title: “A MOST pleasant surprise!”
text:
My wife and I checked in after a 4 day drive up the coast enroute from San Francisco to Vancouver. Everything from our check in to departure exceeded our expectations. The room was very nice and the staff was personable, pleasant, helpful and efficient. It is a medium size hotel with great charm and excellently maintained.
We recommend it to everyone including family and friends...

title: “Really Needs Service Improvement”
text:
I stay at a Marriott property in Denver every couple of months and thought I'd try the Marriott City Center again, even though our last experience wasn't fantastic.
This hotel definitely needs some work on its service. It seems everytime we stay there the front desk staff are inefficient and rather disintereted in their guests. As a gold member, I asked for an upgrade to a corner room, which I was told would be no problem. We got to the room and not only wasn't it a corner room, it was one of the smaller rooms. When we called the front desk, they just remarked "don't know why they told you that, we have no corner rooms."
There is still no open restaurant in the hotel, except for the open bar area.
The rooms were clean and had good bedding.
On the positive side, the breakfast in the club level was very good with excellent service. It was the best part of our stay at the hotel.

title: “Great Stay at New York Marriott Financial”
text:
Stayed at the New York Marriott Financial right before the Christmas holidays. The other Marriott properties in New York would do well to follow the example of the Financial Marriott. Rooms are larger and you definitely have the feeling of spaciousness. The staff is very accomodating and how bad can it be when there is a Roy's Restaurant on property. The restaurant serves breakfast (which is wonderful), lunch and dinner and of course dinner being their forte. It is very easy to catch the subway to get anyplace in the city. Also, easier to get to any of the airports from this property.
Enjoy

title: “Great find!”
text: I recently visited LA for the first time, primarily for business. I spent my first three nights at the Elan, based on reviews on TripAdvisor and the recommendation of an associate. It was a pleasant experience from the start, with no problem checking in just after 8am - even having breakfast (love those bagels). That was a godsend, having left Australia 24 hours before. The staff were friendly and helpful and my room was immaculate each day, with replacement toiletries, shower hat etc. I make that point because at the trendy Beverly Hills hotel I moved to afterwards - not once did the toiletries get replenished in four nights. And that hotel was more expensive and had no breakfast or free internet. The shower curtain which is plastic on one side and towelling on the other is a brilliant idea - one of the rare times I've not had water leak everywhere in a hotel bathroom! I was travelling alone and found the Elan to be well located for dining and shopping. Even though I was told some places were too far to walk - if you have comfy shoes, it's not that far to places like the famed restaurant The Ivy on N. Robertson Blvd. Check out the hotel's website for special deals. The walls did seem a little thin but thankfully the vocal chap in the adjoining room went to sleep early. Would definitely return.

title: “Lovely small hotel with superb service”
text: My wife and I staying at the Lighterlighter for 8 nights, combination of business and pleasure. This is upmarket "motel" type accommoadation of the very highest order. Most impressive is the level of service, friendliness and welcome provided by the General Manager, David, and the rest of his team. We have travelled worldwide and stayed in hotels of all levels, but the Lamplighter provides service of the highest order at a very reasonable rate. The pool was excellent, and the breakfast provided us all that we needed. Thoiugh we were not travelling with our family, it would also be an excellent choice for a family stop. But make sure you have a car, as the hotel is some miles out to the east of San Diego (which actually suited us fine). I recommend the Lamplighter to you most highly.

title: “Dowdy, yes but very charming..”
text:
My family and I spent 6 nights at the Hotel Wales between Xmas and New Years Day 2006. The rooms are spacious (by NYC standards), furnished in a simple yet comfortable style and the beds are comfortable. Our suite had a large walk-in closet, living area (with TV, sofa and chairs), large bedroom with TV, city views and a perfectly adequate bathroom. There is room service provided from Sarabeth's kitchen downstairs...including wine and cocktails (much needed after travelling 8 hours with a two year-old).
The second-floor dining room/tea parlor is a wonderful and quiet place to have breakfast (continental) or tea in the afternoon...Definitely old-world and charming.
This is our second stay at the Wales and would definitely go back. In no way are the accomodations at all comparable to the Four Seasons or the Carlyle but, then again, neither is the price (around $300 for the suite). The location, although pretty far uptown from 5th avenue shopping, is close to all of the city's cultural highlights. Finally, in a city where one is bound to be out of their hotel room by 9 am, I would rather save my money on a splurge lunch at Le Bernardin or dinner at La Grenouille than on $1000 a night (for similar sized room) hotel accomodations. It really depends on what you want out of your visit.

title: “Not as nice as Residence Inns or Embassy Suites”
text:
We were persuaded to try this hotel after reading so many positive reviews. While there were some positive attributes, the hotel doesn't compare favorably with Residence Inns or Embassy Suites. Perhaps it's under new management, but it certainly doesn't deserve all the raves on this site. We will stick to Marriotts or Embassy Suites from now on.
First the positives: the pool and basketball courts were nice and welcomed by my family; the free laundry facilities were nice to have after a week on the road (and surprisingly available); the location is convenient to attractions in La Jolla, Del Mar and north San Diego and not too inconvenient to downtown (although lacking in any real San Diego "flavor").
The negatives, which we feel outweighed the positives:
The one-bedroom King Suite was very small. There was barely room to lay out suitcases for our family of four and have room to walk. The pull-out couch in the living room extended completely to the television cabinet so that it was impossible to make up (the bed was not made up and we had to request mattress pad, sheets, blanket and pillows to do it ourselves). Furthermore, the mattress was so uncomfortable that we had to pull it off the bed frame and lay it on the floor. The sleeper sofa was an obviously cheap piece of furniture and has not worn well. The bed linens for the king bed were so worn out and scratchy that it felt like sand in the bed. When will hotel chains realize that customers won't tolerate uncomfortable beds and linens?
The lay-out of the bedroom was also most inconvenient. The bathroom door opened into the closet so that trying to get into the closet and maneuver around the bathroom was awkward. The doors to the outside hallway are so thin, you can hear every word spoken and every TV.
The hotel was nearly full, yet management had only assigned one poor woman to manage the breakfast "buffet". The food was of poor quality, there was not enough of the hot (microwaved) food and no employee was assigned to clear tables or empty overflowing trashcans. We opted to purchase our own cold cereal and poptarts so as not to have to deal with the mess! I felt sorry for the woman who had to handle nuking the food and refilling everything by herself each morning!
Overall, I'd say the property is poorly managed and understaffed for the size of the hotel. However, even improved management and new bed and bath linens cannot compensate for the lack of size and cheap furniture in the "suites." Skip this one and head to the Residence Inn across the road.

title: “Good service from housekeeping”
text:
Haydee was very helpful and polilte. She brought fresh towels and straightened the room on request.
Tay at the front desk in the afternoons was also a pleasure to work with.
I agree with some of the other comments about shady characters hanging around this hotel. That is its only drawback really. it wouldnt surprise me if prostitutes are working out of this hotel.

title: “It is ok, you are paying for locatin”
text: After reading many reviews of Stay; I was a bit hestitant. Here is my summary. The lobby is fantastically decorated which sets your expecations high for the room.....which is adequate but not to the design level of the lobby. If their lobby was more basic maybe the rooms would exceed expectations? As far as size and price.....it is in line with the general area - it is NYC so hotel room in this area are SMALL, and price fluctuates with demand; so one week you could pay $200 for the room the next $400 - so how much "value" you get from Stay is proporinate to what you paid.

title: “You could hear a pin drop!”
text: What a wonderful hotel ! Check in staff was super friendly and quick to check us in.We had people staying in all rooms around us but we never heard a sound. Thank you Hyatt for doors that close slowly and do not slam shut.Bedding was top notch,large flat screen with a fridge!This property was pre paid with 3rd party booking at a great rate but we were treated like stars.Wonderful

title: “Great stay!”
text: I highly recommend this hotel. Very dog friendly and the service was impeccable. Rooms are clean and beds are comfortable. Coffee/tea service in the morning in the lobby was so great!

title: “Ideal boutique hotel location for Denver Perfiorming Arts Center events”
text: We love this hotel because it is a five-minute walk to the Denver Performing Arts complex. Most people in the audience are still trying to get their cars out of the tall circular parking garage when we are back at the hotel bar enjoying ourselves. Breakfast is wonderful and the service in the little restuarant is both warm and professional. They got our reservations all wrong, but their email alert let us know and they fixed everything right away. One major complaint because we are enthusiastic readers: The lighting in the room is not at all adequate. We always return to this hotel each time we go to an event at the Performing Arts complex. Valet parking takes your car away and then you can walk everywhere in LoDo.

title: “An Excellent Bargain for the Windy City!”
text: This hotel is steps away from the world-famous Magnificent Mile! While it is in an establishment built decades ago, the staff was incredibly accommodating, especially Michael! While my stay was not one of pleasure, they sure made my stay quite hospitable! Kudos to Red Roof Downtown Chicago!

title: “Good, Not Great”
text:
The Prescott is a very nice hotel. In many ways it is right on point, yet in other ways if falls short.
Things they do well...
--excellent lobby staff. Very friendly, helpful and outgoing especially Jill and Emily. The doormen are excellent in providing services including directions and an excellent price on a town car return to the airport. Check this out. It's almost the same price as a taxi and much more enjoyable.
--wonderful maid service. She kept our room perfect. I would have liked a bit more attention to the bathroom but I think the staff is instructed not to touch visitor's personal items. 
--Very quiet--even though the hotel was full, there was no sound of slamming doors or people running in the halls. It seems a very well behaved crowd is attracted to this property.
--Nice bed linens and robes in the room
--perfect location. You can walk anywhere
Things they need to work on...
--Building mechanicals. The building is old and the air conditioning has a difficult time keeping up. It was 85* when we arrived and it took over 12 hours for the room temperature to go down 6*.
---Matresses. With all the emphasis on heavenly beds, grande beds and super beds in the chain hotels, it would be important for Klimptons to keep up. Our mattress was horrible. Very thin and uncomfortable. Considering we were in a suite, it was very disappointing to have such a horrible mattress. This area really needs improvement if they plan to remain competitive.
--Whirlpool tub needs to be upgraded. The jets were brown and looked moldy. The shower curtain was dirty on the bottom inside the tub.
--The wine hour is nice but couldn't they spring for a couple of bowls of nuts or chips? Kind of cheap!!!!!!!!!!!! 
This hotel is good, not great. It has a tremendous amount of potential and a willing staff. Emphasis should be put on upgrading. Boutique hotel visitors really notice the little things.

title: “Over-rated”
text: It was a big deal for me to say I was staying at the Waldorf, but beside the grand lobby, I was not impressed. I stayed for five nights on a business trip, and won't do it again. I'm going back to NYC in two weeks, and I'm going to try somewhere else. The Waldorf is just old. The rooms are old. It was burning up hot in my room and no way to cool it down. Someone had to come open a window for me, and the there was a constant whooshing sound of air being sucked out of the window. I was on the 8th floor and had absolutely no view of anything. I get to say I stayed there, and I never will again.

title: “great location, quiet and clean”
text: small rooms, but comfortable, quiet, clean with all the amenities. The location is great to walk to everything in lower Manhattan and close to the subway. Can't beat that on a short trip.

title: “A great boutique hotel”
text: The hotel is very upscale and the service is excellent. Overall, a great value.

title: “Dissapointed”
text:
The Manhattan Club: I stayed with my friend-owner for the US Open and was greatly dassapointed. The room is big but furnished poorly, old spotted sofa, leaking aircondition from the ceiling, the toilet is not for a 'big' person. Staff is half-friendly. Elevators are just terrible, over slow, wait up to 15 min. There are additonal elevators offered to guests: trashed, dirty, and smell... due to no airconditioning at that area.
The only positive is location and roomy space. But for the same price of ~$400-500 Hilton is much better.

title: “Nice room”
text: Stayed here a night when my flight got delayed, based on TA reviews. The reviews are accurate; the rooms are really nice and spacious. My king room was really a suite, with a couch area, desk, wet bar, and TV on one side. The bed and bathroom are on the other. Front desk help was very helpful, they can direct you to cabs and the light rail into the downtown area. Also there is free breakfast and wifi, plus a nice little food display at the front desk, where I bought and immediately wolfed down a chef salad and slice of cheesecake on my arrival. Across the parking lot is a mini-mall with several fast-food restaurants, including a soul food place that has excellent BBQ ... and it's cheap! A FedEx Office there too. About the only drawback I can report is the room smelled musty when I first went in, but I think it was because the A/C wasn't on. Once the room cooled down the smell went away.

title: “Nice experience with only a few minor glitches”
text: We stayed at the Omni Shoreham with our two teen grandsons for four nights. We chose the Zoo package which was well worth the extra considering the appetites of two teens and the WONDERFUL breakfast buffet that was included in the deal as well as free valet parking. We used the metro, one block away, for our transportation so the car sat snugly in the lot until our departure. The metro ride to the monuments was about 20-- 30 minutes including a transfer at Metro City stop. We also rode the double decker tour bus which stopped one block from the hotel. Sitting on top was fun for all of us and the bus stopped at all of the popular sights including Arlington. The boys (as well as my husband and I) were very impressed with the elegance of the hotel, the pool, exercise room and the little amenities such as milk and cookies in room and plenty of linens, pillows, etc. It is a beautiful old hotel and the room was certainly clean and adequate though we noticed a couple of minor needed repairs (leaky tub faucet, wall trim end cap missing). The small refrigerator in our room was barely cool so our water bottles were not kept as cold as we would have liked. The service was great except when we were leaving and waited almost a half hour for our car to be brought up. Other than the "free" breakfast we found the prices in the restaurant to be prohibitive. However there were several reasonable neighborhood restaurants close by that offered a variety of decent ethnic as well as traditonal American food. There is even a Baskin-Robbins nearby!

title: “Wonderful service and location”
text:
I brought my daughter to NYC to celebrate her 13th Birthday and I decided to stay at The Muse because it seemed like a fun and "cool" place for her to stay. Never once did the staff and ambiance of The Muse dissapoint. When making the reservation online I had mentioned it was my daughter's Birthday; she was greeted with a plate of cupcakes and a sweet note upon entering the room ~ what a wonderful little surprise for her! Also during our stay, she was wished Happy Birthday from the desk staff several times which she thought was nice. The entire staff alway had a smile and a kind word to say, everyone alway took the time to say hello when passing by. 
We were both pleasantly surprised at the size and decor of the room and she loved relaxing in the leopard print robe during some of our down time. I loved the wine reception each evening; what a wonderful way to relax at the end of a long day pounding the pavement and before leaving for dinner. Take a moment to visit the restrooms off the lobby, each has it's own unique and fun personality!
Overall we both loved our stay. This was my first visit to a Kimpton Hotel and if The Muse is any indication of what the hotel chain presents to it's customers, I will definitely stay again.

title: “Lovely lobby, garden and decor...”
text:
I stayed at this hotel when it was called the Monarch and liked it and now as a Fairmont I am in love with it. I like bright, classy decor and attention to details in hotels and the Fairmont has it all. The lobby is light and airy and is half situated in a glass atrium. The inner courtyard of the hotel has a beautiful fountain, glass lanterns, flowers, and trees that are strung with tiny white lights at night. The lobby also has inviting overstuffed sofas and chairs that invite its guests to sit and have a glass of wine or read a book.
Our sixth-floor large king room had a sofa and chair and lots of space to spread out. The bed, pillows, and linens were first rate and very comfortable. The spacious bathroom comes with lovely rose-infused bath products that made me feel as if I was in a high-end spa. 
All the public spaces are decorated with the latest in upscale furniture, fixtures, rugs, and lights. Even the hallways are bright, inviting, and very clean. Each day when we came back we felt as if we were home--especially since the elevator talked to us--yes, Siri (the I-phone girl), has a part-time job.
The hotel is about seven blocks from Georgetown and numerous restaurants, but for breakfast and a quick light lunch or dinner try Bread and Chocolate on 23rd Street. We ate there four times and each meal was very good. 
The doormen at this hotel also deserve a special mention as they are all extremely nice and change the large hotel doormat--yes, the doormat--three times a day to say "Good morning," "Good afternoon," and "Good evening." I also like the fresh lemon water that is always available in the lobby--particularly nice when Washington DC hits the high 90s. It's in the details...
I would highly recommend this hotel and will return on my next trip. The only minor negative is the TV reception--station choices are limited and the reception (at least in our room) was fuzzy.
Still and all, my favorite hotel in DC.

title: “Great location, poor service...”
text:
Hard Rock Chicago was just ok. The location (right on Michigan) is steps away from Wacker Drive, river tours, the loop, etc. We really enjoyed the proximity to everything. However, the concierge was not all that helpul. We had to request a refrigerator three times before they finally delivered it. Also, when I asked about an I-Pod docking station, they said they'd "call me back." The next day, after not hearing, anything, I called again. The concierge told me one was not available for my room since I wasn't in a suite but "there's a Radio Shack down the street." Not quite the "can-do" attitude the hotel tries to boast about.
The room was decently sized and we had no problems. The view of Michigan Ave. was nice from the 22nd floor.
Overall, if you get a good deal (like we did on Hotwire), go for it. Otherwise, look elsewhere.

title: “good price”
text: Is a good hotel, very clean and is good located.. The service is excelent

title: “Charming and elegant”
text: We enjoyed 5 nights at this hotel whilst in New York for a wedding. We have previously stayed at The New York Palace (one of my favourite hotels) but thought we would try here this time. The room was had reserved was large and comfortably furnished with plenty of room for our baby's cost, pushchair etc. Large rooms like this can be difficult to find at city hotels. The location is great and the best shopping is all within walking distance as is Central Park and many other attractions. The reception and public areas are elegant and you could easily spend time there just watching the world go by!

title: “Wonderful Staff and Accomodations”
text: My husband and I stopped in Charlotte after dropping our children at camp. We enjoyed 2 nights at the Marriott Southpark and walked to shopping and restaurants. The pool was beautiful and the fitness room was outstanding. We highly recommend and would even bring our boys back. Only thing we thought was silly is no free wifi.

title: “bad service--guarantee doesn't mean what it's supposed to”
text:
I had a prepaid guaranteed late arrival reservation but was bumped when I arrived at 5 p.m. Other guests were allowed to check in after I arrived. To make matters worse, I had a sprained ankle but had to stand at the counter for 15 minutes while the clerk wasted my time insisting that she go through all the possible restaurants in town even though I told her I just wanted to get to my room.
I was moved to a low rate hotel that was two miles away from my colleagues. The Hilton didn't even offer any compensation for failing to honor my guarantee.

title: “comfortable rooms in a great location”
text: From this hotel, you can easily walk to Water Tower Place, Miracle Mile shopping, Navy Pier and a bunch of local pubs, restaurants and breakfast places. Of course, you needn't go out for breakfast as it is provided, along with many healthy options. The staff here couldn't do enough for us and always with a smile. I have visited Chicago often over the past 20 years and stayed in other Marriott properties. They were fine, but when I return, I'm going back here because of the overall feeling of caring service. Nice job by the management and staff!

title: “Great place City Suites Hotel”
text: While in Chicago we picked our hotel so it was within walking distance to Wrigley Field. City Suites Hotel is an older building on W. Belmont Ave. We enjoyed the surroundings and the coziness of the hotel. The rooms have an older charm about them and are clean and comfortable. Russell, at the front desk, was a tremedous help with recommending places to eat and places to take two teenage boys while visiting. He helped make our trip easy to enjoy.

title: “Nice, Pleasant, Unremarkable...”
text:
Picked this hotel for a day stayover in Denver because it looked more "interesting" than the other chain hotels in the airport area. Booked through CheapHotels.Com about a month in advance.
Nice, clean, pleasant and totally unremarkable... The room was spacious and had high ceilings, bed was comfortable, small fridge and micro in the room. Small private patio opened into a courtyard. NO BATHTUB, but a nice, oversized shower.
I was a little dissappointed cause I thought it would a notch above a boring Embassy Suites room, but it was roughly equal without the included breakfast or cocktails...
The neighborhood is NOT upscale and nothing worth walking to in the vicinity.

title: “Helpful, considerate staff, great location”
text:
Our family stayed at the Hampton inn, downtown, over the recent April break. From the minute we pulled up and had to park almost to the end of the block, we were greeted by staff who bent over backwards to help us a welcome us. The first indication that we would be cared for was the doorman/parking attendant who walked all the way down to meet our car and welcome us. Front desk staff was knowledgeable and always helpful, breakfast staff was friendly and accommodating. We were most impressed by the kindness of our housekeeper, Leslie. Unfortunately, on the 2nd day of our vacation, our daughter hurt her ankle and had a cast put on at Philadelphia Children's Hospital. When Leslie heard about what happened she offered her help if it was needed. The next day, slipped under our door, was a handwritten note from Leslie along with a DunkinDonuts gift card, for our daughter. We were so moved by her thoughtfulness and generosity! 
We found the people in Philly, and in particular, our hotel staff, to be welcoming and considerate. We would most definitely return to this hotel, no question. A room that is clean and comfortable is only part of what we loved about this Hampton Inn. The staff really make the hotel great.
Only one small suggestion though. The hotel is hard to identify when you are driving down the street looking for it. How about a Hampton Inn sign nearer to street level?

title: “Disappointed”
text:
It's ours first and probably will be the last stay with any Radisson. They charge extra for any standard services in other hotels. Double beds cost $20 extra everyday. A rollaway bed costs $20 extra everyday. Plus they reserve $30 "deposits" everyday for the course of your stay. We were told that the "deposits" will be refunded to us 5-7 days after we check out. We have stayed with 5 different hotels in Baltimore and this is the first time we ever heard such a policy. 
Our door lock wouldn't work properly on the fourth day because the battery was out. The door can be opened without a key. The hotel shuttle service is not reliable at all. On one occasion it was late for 15 minutes. One employee (probably a manager) in the hotel was using that shuttle for some business so it didn't return to the hotel on time. When we finally got on the shuttle, the driver had an attitude, refusing to talk nor help with the bags.
Some front desk attendants, the door men and the guy who fixed the lock are nice. The location of the hotel is very good, about 10 minutes walk to the harbor.

title: “one of my fave hotels”
text:
This is one of my favorite hotels to stay at.
It's right on the lake. The rooms are great - great layout, decor, amount of space.
Cool bar.

title: “Great Hotel in Seattle”
text:
The hotel is very good, perhaps not as huber cool as some of the newer W hotels.
It is nonetheless very nice, the room is large, with a nice bathroom.
Service is good and I found it exceptional good value for money. However I booked it though an expedia package.
I would stay again!

title: “Everything you need for a comfortable stay in Memphis”
text:
Our purpose in Memphis was to explore a new city. This location was convenient. It backs up to Main Street which is closed to traffic but has a $1.00 trolley ride which will take you to Beale Street. However it is only a 10 minute walk there. The hotel was spic and span. Every employee was personable and helpful. The beds were comfortable. The shower was great. 
The free breakfast was not really my cup of tea, so to speak, but what can we expect for free. It was hard boiled eggs, canned fruit cocktail, cereal, not-too-fresh breakfast pastries and make it yourself waffles. 
Other than the breakfast no complaints. I would stay there again.

title: “great little hotel for cheap price”
text:
I looked at several hotels while booking my trip to the San Francisco area, and for the price and the location you can't beat the Adante, formerly the known as Hotel Nuvo. I had read other reviews of this hotel about complaints with homeless people, but like any other city, the homeless are there and did not bother me. be kind and at least say hello to them. They won't bite, but rather appreciate the camaraderie.
The room I had requested was to be away from street noise and away from the elevator. While I did get a room on the 4th floor away from street noise, I was only a few steps away from the elevator. The rooms were quiet, comfy, clean, and spacious. It is equipped with a couch that doubles as a fold away, 2 night stands, desk, and complimentary in room tea and coffee. TV and phone are obviously included as well, along with extra pillows if needed.
The bathroom is equally spacious, with an abundance of towels and amenities including hair dryer, and a closet with a security safe, iron and ironing board. The bed was comfy enough, although I did wake up a few times the first night due to my boisterous neighbors, which was no fault of the hotels.
Altthough the entire hotel is non smoking, there is a slight lingering smell of smoke in the hallways. The staff could manage to also check the blankets for wear and tear as there was a patch and hole in the one I had. 
The continental breakfast was a bit dissapointing as there was none before 7a.m. The juice machine is shut off before this time as well. Another reason why I had booked here was for the continental breakfast. On the second day I did manage to catch a glimpse of their breakfast which was store bought pastries and white toast. On the third day I did not even bother with breakfast as it was already gone, but the juice machine was shut off and it was only around 10am. You are better off wandering the SF area on your own to find a place to eat which there are more than plenty and better than stick around for breakfast here. Besides, you get to experience the city this was as well. Overall I would come book here again.

title: “Stay Away”
text:
I had the unpleasant surprise of checking in at Club Quarters Philadelphia. Starting with the check in process. If you pump you own gas and self check out at the supermarket this is the Hotel for you! The Staff were unhelpful and unpleasant. 
One elevator was out of service for a planned overhaul yet this info was not divulged until I had already checked in. This cause long waits to get to my room and a long climb back down to get to the lobby (the Down elevator never arrived).
The Room Key worked for one swipe only and continually had to be reprogrammed to gain entry into the microscopic sized room. The frustration was only enhanced by the desk clerk reprimanding me for not knowing how to store the key. Even with my multiple trips to the front desk the same clerk always seemed surprised that I was a guest.
Finally the counter in the bathroom extended too far over the toilet and impeded the toilet seat lid from fully opening. Therefore, if you attempted to pee standing up the lid would crash down on your knees. Nor could you sit down due to odd this arrangement (got the picture?)
I requested to speak with a manager and was told NO Manager is on duty until Sunday afternoon (this was on Friday afternoon). I decided to check out without spending the evening and was told I would still be charged for the room.
Monday, I attempted to contact Club Quarters General Manager Zvi Cohen and was first connected to the wrong voice mail. When I called back I was finally connected to Mr. Cohen's Voice mail yet never received response to my concerns.

title: “good bargain for the price”
text: The location was very convenient and quiet compared to all the motels nearby. There was not much light in the room and it was quite small but we just stayed there for the night so it was fine. Breakfast was ridicolous. The parking was small but we left the car in the street.

title: “Clean and served its purpose”
text:
We stayed in the marrakech earlier this year. Before we left we emailed to ask to be in a room near our friends who we were going with. On arrival we checked in only to find out we were as far away as we could possibily be. Also we had both paid for the same size rooms however our room was considerably bigger than our friends and we were told this could not be rectified. Although this was a pain the rooms were clean and comfortable the only pain being the noise from outside but hey its New York not a desert Island so we expected this. The bar to the hotel was not open at all which was a shame as we were expecting this to be open and would have been nice after a long day walking around but there are places very near that you could go to chill out for a bit so it wasn't to much of a pain.
Our stay there was good however the hotel is well situated for the tube station so getting around is very easy (the hotel is a long way away from any of the central attractions so tube or taxi is essential). Also the staff at the hotel were very helpful and gave a lot of good advice where to go when we asked. The atmosphere is very relaxed in the hotel and although there is no lift the door steward at the front did help my girlfriend with her case so it was not a problem at all. The staff also saved us money by helping us book cheaper transport back to the airport at the end of our stay.
I would say that if you want to see New York at a reasonable price and not spend to much time in the hotel this is the ideal place however if you are looking for a nice hotel where you can spend lots of time I would look for somewhere else.

title: “Interesting location, friendly staff, better than the plastic HInn but don't epxpdect luxury”
text: Good location ... Helpful staff ... Great place to eat across the street .... Interesting early morning stroll

title: “Good Value, close to Galleria”
text: Two elderly aunts and I stayed 2 nights for a family event. We all had our own rooms and were perfectly happy with the cleanliness and the comfy beds. I slept very well both nights. Nothing fancy, nothing negative, good AAA rate of $63. Easy access from/to I-635. Enjoyed the easy walk to Galleria. Hotel offers "Candlewood Value" room that has internet/printer (free), plus washers/dryers, work-out equip and an honor system panry for all sorts of things like pop tarts, bananas, apples, juice, sode, milk, canned soup/tuna, gum, candy bars, toiletries, etc.

title: “Comfortable hotel - Friendly staff”
text:
We just got back from our four day stay at the Alex. The studio suite we had was very nice with little extras like robes, slippers, comfy bed linens and nice quality TV. We did not have much use for the kitchen area (except the fridge), but it was nice to have nonetheless. 
Kudos to the concierge for figuring out the restaurant we wanted from just a description of the food and general location because we forgot the name/address. And, double kudos to the IT guy who figured out how to get the internet working on my husband's lap top. Sorry I can't remember your names but if you were working on May 27th (IT guy) and 29th (concierge), you know who you are. Staff was all very friendly. Door men always greeted us with a smile and got us cabs very quickly. The gals who cleaned our room (we were on the 30th floor), were very friendly and did a great job. We'd come back to the room in the afternoon and it would be clean. We'd come back late at night and the bed was turned down and slippers and robes ready to go. Avoid the mini bar and room service unless you enjoy outrageous prices. (industry standard, but I just can't stand it getting ripped off with the so-called "convenience fee") There are some markets in the area, so grab some soda, water, etc and stick it in the fridge if you have one in the room you choose.
We were concerned about a few of the reviews about problems with hot water. The water was hot in the morning and evening at the times we used it, so I guess they worked that problem out. One issue that was a bit annoying was the elevator. I am sure the staff/management is aware of the problem. Lets just say we consistently ended up waiting a long time for an elevator with bell hops, etc. running back and forth in front of us. Somewhat chaotic at times. For this reason, I cannot give the hotel an excellent rating. I have experienced this at other NYC hotels, but it is an inconvenience just the same.
Oh yeah, check out the deli around the corner called Pinnacle, they have great lox & bagels and the guys behind the counter were friendly. Not a common thing in the city.

title: “Highly recommended”
text: This is the second time I have stayed there. There are a lot of options in Seattle and I believe this one stands out among them. The price is excellent, the staff are professional, yet not stuffy. I felt I could ask them anything yet not feel stupid. The rooms were clean and downright cute! I ate in the restaurant and the food was good and quite reasonably priced, including the wine. My co-worker was able to order her food a special way that she needed and received it exactly like she wanted and enjoyed the flavor as well. I highly recommend the Hotel Deca and would stay there again in a heartbeat.

title: “Outstanding location and service”
text: The Parker House has the perfect location for touring Boston. It is directly across the street from the red Freedom Trail, and just around the corner from Boston Common and the Old State House. It is a historic hotel, which means that the rooms have most likely been reconfigured multiple times, and the hallways meander and in some places, are different widths. The result is the rooms are all different, unlike the "cookie cutter" rooms in modern built hotels. I was disappointed that the rooms have window units and not central air. For the first few days of our visit, it was quite warm so the A/C ran continually, which was a bit loud at night. Also--and this is a pet peeve of mine-- I would expect a hotel that averages over $225 a night would have better towels. Ours were like sandpaper. I've stayed at $69 a night chain hotels that had better quality towels! Another result of reconfiguration is that some bathrooms are almost microscopic. Our deluxe category room was very spacious and comfortable, but the bathroom was so small it could only house a pedestal sink, and had no counter space at all. A curved shower curtain rod had been installed, which caused the shower curtain to extend out into the middle of the room. We didn't spend too much time in the room except to sleep, so these shortcomings didn't affect our overall delight with this property. The staff is excellent and the property is spotless and well maintained. Even if you don't stay here, you should definitely do a walk-through of the beautiful lobby.

title: “Nightmare in New York”
text:
We stayed at this hotel on Black Friday night. We could not check into the hotel until 4:00 pm so we had to store our bags and come back. On their web site it showed beautiful remodeled rooms. This was not the case. Our room did not have heat and we had to call 3 times to get a response to this. Our telephone did not work in our room. They never did fix it. The bathroom was dirty and there were black curly hairs on the floors and walls. We are blond and redheaded. I could not take a bath because the fiberglass tub was broken in the back and would not hold water. 
There was almost no seating in the lobby to even wait for anyone or to meet friends. My nephew and mother came into to town to see a show, and they would not let them into our hotel, not even the lobby, to visit us after the show becasue they did not have a room key. They tried to call us but(see above) the phone was broken and they could not get a call through. 
When we checked out we had to pay $3 per bag to leave them at the hotel. This included our shopping bags from the day before. It was an all over bad experience and we would never stay here again. There was no down escalator so we had to carry our bags down the steps to street level. All this for $300 per night.

title: “Disappointed”
text:
I am originally from NY and love the upper west side... great hotel location. Currently, I live in Austin and not a high maintenance 40 year old. I had a beautiful corner room for $325 per evening. The room was wonderful, the construction... not so much! I woke up every morning with a jack hammer in my ear at 7 a.m. I asked to change rooms which would require me to pick up all of my items and change rooms. The staff offered me a breakfast voucher as the hotel was fully booked. 
As mentioned, I was staying in a room full of beautiful windows and shockingly noticed a scaffold w a few men slowly cleaning the windows. The staff said they called the engineer and they would be finished by days end. NOT! They were back the next day. 
The lobby is a construction zone and the staff simply replies that the hotel is going through major renovations. Maybe they should warn guests and not place them in a room with loud construction. I am not much of a compaliner and love NYC. Although, a breakfast voucher and a smirk for $325 a night for three days doesn't set well with me. 
I also called to see if I left my home keys were left in the room and never received a call back. I would think twice or ask if you have a non-construction zone room and men polling down your window. A warning would have been nice.
I will never stay at the Belleclaire again. 
Best with your travels!

title: “Grat Choise in San Jose”
text:
I just can't believe I never wrote a review about this Hotel. After reading some of the reviews about the Marriott San Jose, I asked myself, Are these people for real????
I stay at this Hotel one or two time per week, YES, you heard right.
I defenetely love this Hotel. I have never had the Valet experience but everything else is just great. 
When you come in the Lobby is beautiful, always playing some groovy music at the same time very relaxing. Very large lobby with very funky furniture. The front desk staf is soooo friendy and always very helpful. I feel like Im back home when I stay here. Did I mention is right Down town San Jose, close to everything. 
The room are just beautiful with great views of the mountains (some rooms) or down town San Jose. Also very clean and confortably large. So many restaurants around, but the Restaurant at the Hotel is also delicious. The bartender downstairs from Spain is very sweetand also very good. 
I work for Jetblue and I this is one of my favorites hotels. If you have a chance to got to the Concierge , OH MY GOD!!! The food is wonderful and the staff there is one of the best. She will treat you like a movie star. 
The pool is wonderful and they have the best Gym ever. 
I also stayed at the Hilton next door once and it was not that good. I defenetely recomend the Marriott San Jose for your next visit or vacation. You will love this Hotel.

title: “I like this hotel. A lot.”
text:
This is my second time staying at this hotel - both times for couples weekend in Charlotte. It is very easy to get to and next to the epicenter (use the pedestrian bridge on 2nd floor to get there without having to worry about traffic lights). The room was spacious (we upgraded to a suite) and on the 9th floor. The only weird thing was the couple joining us got a standard room and ended up on the 14th floor. I would have totally gone for the standard room higher up. Word to the wise: bigger may not always be higher. 
The staff was great. Because of several events downtown we received a couple of emails warning us of changes in the traffic patterns. (We didn't get that kind of attention at the Ritz where we stayed the next night). 
Overall, I was very pleased. Note that prices may drop after you reserve your room. At the ten day prior to arrival ark, there was a $20 price change. (enough to cover the paking).

title: “Location Location Location”
text: Spent two nights here for business meetings and found the place great. Directly across the street from Camden Yards and easy walking distance to everything. My room was very clean and comfortable, the staff is friendly and the morning breakfast is nice, not great but nice. The business meetings themselves went very well as the staff made sure every whim was handled quickly.

title: “Typical style-over-substance hotel”
text: This is a typical hotel designed for people who talk about the vibe of a hotel rather than its comfort or pleasantness. The staff is right in line with this philosophy: nice, friendly people who don't really know how to work in a hotel. The bartender forgot about my order then got it wrong. When you walk into the room your first challenge is to find the lights because there aren't any switches near the doors. You have to go to each individual fixture and figure out how to turn it on. The bathroom doors require constant movement to gain access to the toilet or the sink. The drapes don't close all the way. I would at least expect a place that caters to undiscriminating hipsters to facilitate the charging of electronic devices but this place is no better than your usual hotel in that regard. The plugs are inconveniently placed behind the bed or by the sink. On the plus side it is clean.

title: “This place is great!”
text:
We stayed here on our Anniversary and had a great time. Our terrace room was spacious and clean. Service was outstanding. A great value and a great location.
The only negative was a loud,noisy nightclub across the street. But you are staying downtown in a big city so some noise should be expected.

title: “Very Impressed”
text:
After staying in some dubious accomodation last time we visited New York, I was a bit worried.
We stayed here for two weeks and was able to book a 'long term stay' which meant we got the best room in the hotel at very reasonable rates. 
We had the King Suite which was huge. It had three built in wardrobes, seperated living area, massive king bedroom, microwave, two tvs and of course a great view.
I wouldnt bother with the breakfast on offer, go to 'essa bagel' across the street theyre an institution in NY.
Not sure if hes still there but Terry at the front desk was one of the nicest staff weve ever encountered.
Its true the courtyard hotels arent as fancy as your normal Marriott but I was still really impressed.
The only thing I would say is if its your first time to New York consider staying on the West Side. We did find this location not quite as dynamic as other areas weve stayed in.

title: “Huge SURPRISE!”
text: We booked this hotel because we were traveling on a budget. We actually booked the room for $125 a night. We were really nervous when we were pulling up, the area seemed a little shady. However, to our surprise we were staying in the most beautiful hotel. Everything on the interior has been remodeled. Its a very very modern hotel. We had flat screen tvs and the most comfortable bed. we had a delicious breakfast on the roof in the morning. We were about a mile from all the major shops and then we took the bus to fisherman's wharf. I think it was like $4 bucks round trip and it took about 15 minutes. We walked at night time from the mall and it was a okay but if I did not have my husband I would have felt unsafe. But you cannot beat this hotel. Its spectacular. I was shocked. We only booked one night because we were unsure and we ended up staying g 3 nights. It was well worth it. I would recommend this for hotel for anyone. Its clean, beautiful and the staff was outstanding. They helped us to get reservations and gave us directions anywhere we needed to go.

title: “We love this hotel”
text: We got a room on a higher floor with a very beautiful harbor view ^^ We both love it and the room was clean. The staffs were nice and helpful. However, the parking fee is very expensive. If you want to take the free shuttle from the station back to the hotel, then you have to make sure you have enough time to wait for that. We waited for more than 30 mins after we called the front desk >< So we took the airport shuttle (one of them will go to the water taxi stop which is just next to the hotel) on the next day.

title: “Polite but ineffective front desk”
text:
After a valet parking miscommunication by the front desk, the valet person told me he would take the charge off my bill. Very nice. I started using the public lot across the street. ($8 instead of $28-, OK no in/out, but still.....) I check the bill and its still there. Front desk staff assures me its taken care of.
 At check out the bill still reflected a parking charge. So the front desk lady assured me it would be taken off. I come home and the bill reflects the charge again. Called the front desk - hopefully this is it. Could it be that difficult????
 Otherwise, nice location to walk to 4th street restaurants, Congress St Bridge and 6th street.
 Mattress was soft and lumpy. Otherwise, room was nice. Breakfast buffet was varied and overall pretty good. Just wake up the front desk, being polite is nice, but being effective would be better.

title: “Great place, better location”
text: I looked all over the city for a good hotel on a tight budget. I felt very lucky to have found Hotel Fusion. The location is great; safe neighborhood, 2 blocks from union square, 1 block from trolley turn/loading location, good shopping, good food and desserts. The staff was very nice and answered every question I had about San Fran with a smile. If we come back to San Fran again, we would love to stay here.

title: “Service with an attitude”
text:
The rooms were nice, the location is good, and the property is well kept, but the service is lacking. Room service (breakfast) was almost an hour late and arrived cold with several items missing. When I called to complain, they didn't seem to care. I was told that they were really busy and that it would be another 45 minutes before they could send anything else up. Later that morning, we needed a cab. With no bellman outside, we went inside and asked the concierge to call a taxi. His first response was to ask us to wait outside for a bellman to show up. 
When I refused, he reluctantly agreed to call a taxi for us, but he made sure that we knew it was "beneath him". After checking out, I realized I had left something in the room and called the hotel. I was unable to speak with anyone and was told I would have to leave a message on the "lost and found" machine. Unfortunately no one ever called back. Although a nice property and the on-site restaurant (Panzano is great, you can do a lot better in downtown Denver.

title: “Satisfied!”
text:
We paid $134. for 3 adults on a Saturday night. We were there for an NFL football game the next day. The outside is deceiving, plain and a little dingy (a tornado of flies was circling the outside entrance)looking but the inside is very nice! We got there at noon planning to ask to park and walk around until room was ready but no need as room was ready and front desk gentleman (very very nice guy) let us check in early. We secured a spot in one of the 8 available in parking lot. We did not use or see the parking garage.
The room (405) was clean and though small, well appointed. Small table with chairs for laptop, amazingly comfy beds, double shower head was great! We asked for a balcony room as suggested by previous posters and it was a GREAT tip! There was some noisy foot traffic when the bars let out around 2-3 am but we didn't mind as it was quite entertaining. 
Front desk staff on day and evening shifts were great. NOC shift was a little lame but nothing to file a complaint about just lackluster. Breakfast area is large and accommodates the guests very well. There are two computers for use (Apples) I had to wait only once when I needed them to print out something. Walk to Pikes Market was easy and convenient. Very satisfied overall with stay, accommodations and value.

title: “Good Situation”
text:
Stayed at this hotel for 7 nights. We found it adequate, clean bedrooms, good bathrooms; but room was a little on small size.
Very well placed for central San Francisco.
The staff very friendly and helpful
We enjoyed our stay both the hotel and the city!!

title: “great central and clean”
text: quite reasonable cost for new york $85 for a double room.great location just of union square but on a quiet street.lovely atmosphere not fancy but great decor.shared bathrooms but spotlessly clean and never had to wait to use.beds very comfy with tv/dvd player in room.would definately go there again

title: “A meeting planners dream!!”
text:
This hotel is beautiful, but as a planner the needs of my clients go so much deeper. The service that is offered at this hotel surpass even 5 star hotels we have utilized. The staff doesn't know the word "no" ensuring that every detail is checked and double checked! The client was exceedingly satisfied and looking for other meetings to hold here!
Book now before they are over capacity!
Thanks to everyone at the hotel for helping provide an amazing experience!!

title: “great hotel”
text:
We were there over Easter-family trip of 4 in conected rooms. Service is excellent-white gloved bellmen everywhere- they'll bring refrigerators, Ice, appliances to rooms on a moment's notice. Efficient check in, checkout, and garage. Large recently decorated rooms with most up to date electronics. Modern bathrooms. Large closets with rtequisite robes/slippers.
Location perfect for shoppers, sightseers, people watchers.
The only negative we encountered is outrageous (even by New York standards) prices in lobby restaurant-$8.00 cup coffee, $10.00 muffin, $25.00 "continental breakfast" for 1 comprised of muffin and croissant. 
Cocktails similarly high.

title: “Great location on Mission Bay!”
text: We live in Orange County and travel to San Diego several times a year. I have Always wanted to stay at this hotel. We finally had a chance the week of July 4th. We got upgraded to a partial bay view (the view was mostly of the neighboring park). The rooms were average and were not anything special. The pool was also just ok. However, you are literally right on the bay. All the sporting activities are just outside your door! It is great! Plus in the evening you can talke a stroll and watch the fireworks at Sea World. Location of this hotel is great! It is close to all the major attractions and Old Town. Great place to stay! We will be back!

title: “Great place to stay in NY Time Square with a few faults”
text:
I have stayed in many Residence Inn and lately have been disappointed with large variation in quality. It would be sad if Marriott became the equivalent of Best Western with poor quality control. However, the Marriott Residence Inn Time Square is among their best (Chicago is their best).
First off, this hotel is not in Time Square but about 6 small blocks away. Is this important? We were surprised how often we walked from the hotel to Time Square to eat or see a musical and at times wish it was closer. On the other hand, the hotel is very well isolated from street noise on our 16th floor room. Oddly enough, sounds from the hallway were very loud because of the large front door bottom gap. The hotel is mid way between two MTA stations so a small walk is needed to get a ride. A 10 block walk will get you to Penn Station if you need to catch a train out of Manhattan. 
The room has two sections. The bedroom part is about 15 feet x 15 feet with queen bed, sofa bed, and closet. The other part has the kitchen, bathroom and hallway and is about 8 x 15. The kitchen had a microwave and slow cooker but no range or other heating device. There is a dishwasher and refrigerator. This is fine. Just don’t plan on cooking anything – just reheating restaurant leftovers or making a sandwich. There is no dining table but there is a nice eating area with bar chairs for 2. The bathroom is small, has basin, toilet, and bath/shower, and enclosed with door. The ventilation was adequate. The room was very nicely decorated and felt comfortable.
There is WIFI everywhere but often with marginal signal strength. I lost my connection on both my iPad and iPhone frequently and had to login again every time. The whole thing was a nuisance. You might want to bring your own router and generate your own signal from the wired access.
We didn’t need any help from the front desk staff so I can’t comment on the service level. There is a nice convenience store with lots of handy stuff in the lobby. The included breakfast was excellent. There were 6 hot items and everything else you would expect in a paid buffet breakfast. Some of the hot items changed day to day. The whole 3rd floor is used for breakfast, lounge, and bar. It looks like a library and not a diner. This is a good retreat if you need to read or use a computer at night while your partner sleeps. The lobby is tiny and not usable for anything except waiting for transportation. Also on the 3rd floor are three full internet stations with printer. These days, you need to be able to surf anywhere and print your own tickets for most venues, including the 9/11 Memorial.
All in all, we had a great stay here at the Marriott Residence Inn Time Square while exploring NY.

title: “Cant expect more for that price”
text: I recently booked a room at Liberty Hotel, at LA. The room was not that great, they stated two queen beds but the room had only two double beds. The flooring in the toilet was horrible, the tiles were cracked and even the toilet was tilted slightly. The good thing about this hotel is it location, less than 5 minutes walk to the hollywood area. The parking is behind the hotel in a narrow ally and the space is not sufficient enough for all the cars. I had to leave the keys at the front desk, so that they could park my car at some other location.

title: “I would be happy to stay here again.”
text:
This hotel was very comfortable. We stayed in the 19th floor & i Loved the view. 
The staff were friendly & welcoming. 
Bed was good.
Even on the 19th floor I found my room to be very noisy with the single glazed windows. 
The position was great for being right in the centre of everywhere. 
The blue hop on hop off bus stops right outside the hotel, which worked well for us.
Overall a good spot

title: “Location is Everything”
text: We chose at this motel while visiting Los Angeles because it was close to the sights of Hollywood. We did not realize at the time that the actual neighborhood was a little seedy but we always felt safe. The motel was clean, offered a nice free breakfast (although the breakfast area was quite small) and the rooms were adequate size with flat screen TV. It had a pool that looked clean but we did not use it. There is parking on site although the spaces are small. The people who ran the motel were very nice and extremely accommodating to our requests - they even allowed us to keep our car parked there after check-out so we could go back to see some sights we missed. I would recommend this motel if you are looking for a clean place to spend a few days while in the Hollywood area. It is basic but the cost was very reasonable.

title: “loved the plaza”
text: yes on aug 28,2006 we arrived into la and drove to another hotel that wanted outrageous fee, they refered us to you and are we glad. the manager a dark man even knew how to pronounce our last name, said he had a serbian friend, and we were so glad we stayed it was clean and fun, thanks carmen and milan djokic

title: “Wonderful, accommodating, and historic”
text:
We stayed at the Sofia Hotel in San Diego for a conference I was attending. It was quite convenient to the Conference Center, Gaslamp District, Shopping District, and taxis were very reasonable to Old Town, the San Diego Zoo, and the airport.
The 'boutique hotel' feel made the historic nature of it charming if not a bit small and compact.
The staff was very helpful and got us everything we needed easily and hospitably.
Great place to stay.

title: “Great Theatre Hotel”
text: It's a great hotel if you are seeing a show at the Paramount, which is directly across the street. The hotel is great and the staff is wonderful. They are helpful with everything. I've stayed there on more than one occasion and love it each and everytime.

title: “Awesome hotel with a great staff! And it's affordable!”
text:
My daughter and I stayed her for a few nights in mid-March and had a wonderful stay. From the moment we walked in the staff was very welcoming and helpful, especially Nick and David. They made us feel right at home and were a great source of information when we had questions. The room was awesome! Super comfortable bed and a very well planned space. The kitchen was a very nice extra to have! The breakfast selection offered a nice variety and the evening reception was also a great bonus! 
We will definitely be returning on our next visit to New York City!

title: “Clean,... Though Mega Noisy!!!!!!”
text:
I stayed with a friend in this hotel for 5 nights and whilst our room was bright, clean and comfortable unfortunately construction work and road works were on going the whole time. They drilled into the ground til 2:30am outside my window and back up at crack of dawn with more banging, drilling and trucks pulling up. Understandably this was out of the hotels control however they did not do much to ease the situation after I queried if they knew when late night banging would stop. Minor set backs included the lift service and air con.
The hotel has it's advantages, it's very central for the financial district and subway was a quick stroll from the hotel so made it handy to navigate the city. The staff overall were helpful and for the price was a reasonable stay, I am sure this would be an idea stay when the contruction and roadworks finish!!!

title: “Excellent Location - Lovely hotel”
text: Stayed at the Pearl Hotel for 5 nights at the beginning of June with 6 friends. Lovely hotel with fantastic location. Bedroom, bathroom and walk in wardroom spacious and clean. Breakfast included in our deal which was a bonus! Food was fine although the dining area was quite casual - sat on sofa/chair instead of dining table/chair. Bed was very comfortable and the there was a bit of noise from the a/c unit although it didn't bother me.

title: “Convenient and comfortable”
text:
We had a very pleasant stay overnight for a weekend of museum visits. The hotel was clean, the staff efficient and the food through room service plentiful and tasty. The room was large and comfortable.
The fitness room was very well-equipped and the pool was clean and a good temperature.
Checking in and out were efficient. We were mostly interested in a convenient location and this was walking distance to all of the museums and sites that we wanted to see. We also found good reasonable places to eat near-by.
Our only complaints are that the parking is expensive ($30 for the day - there are cheaper options near by but we only had 24 hours so did not want to spend time looking around for it), and also that there was some loud noise from other guests who were partying late at night. The hotel is large and there was at least one big function going on. However the noise issue was quickly addressed.
We found a good price through the hotel website and would certainly stay here again.

title: “Terrible”
text: This place was the worst. Hair all over the bathroom, mold on the walls, rugs were dirty, curtains falling off the walls, stains all over the bedstread. As soon as we walked in the room we call management for them to see these disgusting rooms. They sent up a newly hired 17 year old male staff with keys to different rooms. One floor up and they were slightly better. The staff are rude and not helpful. We travel to NYC once a month and have stayed in several different hotels this was the worst place I have ever stayed and the price unacceptable. We paid over $250 for three rooms each and our stay was wasn't worth $25. Do Not stay here.

title: “highlight of our trip”
text: I cant believe all the bad reviews this hotel has received! I stayed there for 3 days in september and it was one of the highlights of our vacation, all of these people writing complaining are so focused on the small rooms, but all the hotels in Manhatten are small unless you want to spend a fortune, and who goes to NYC to sit in your room. The whole point of NYC is to be out and about enjoying the enormous anount of activities then you go back to your hotel to change or sleep, and it was in the perfect location for that. I woke up and took a jog in central park, its right near the subway and its just uptown enough to be out of the real crazy busy area just downtown, which is fun of course but its nice to go back to your hotel and be just outside the madness yet still in a great location near the upper east side. Now to the hotel itself, its facade is so understated which is refreshing, it knows its good so it doestn have to boast by putting up a huge fake front, but when you go in and take the unassuming escalator up you are warmly greeted by such a nice foyer area, nice wood floors, cool lighting, chic, im so sick of these oversized marble pompous entryways of other hotels. The staff was so friendly, we were able to check in early, and why call the room small like ive read here, cozy would suit me better, my girlfriend and i were so excited to know that when we came back after a loud bright night in the city we would return to this charming, wood floored, wood walled(cozy)room, we slept so well in this space. The library room was very charming, nobody mentioned relaxing on a nice leather couch in front of the fireplace, we played a few games of pool on the billiards table, very relaxing, they had table with chess boards set up, books to read, come on people loosen up a bit and enjoy. The whole property is very modern and interesting, and yes a bit dark which is perfect for how the atmosphere of the place is, plenty of candles lit and many seating area to relax. Did anyone mention the bar of this place, the elevators open and the music hits you, wow this place is alive at night, classy but still fun, dancefloor always full and a generaly nice goodlooking crowd. I have to be truthfull and admit that the only downside of this hotel is some of the extra prices, if you want to get a good laugh look at the prices of roomservice, breakfast is a joke, i could not even imagine dinner prices, great comedy, but hey your in NYC so go eat out thats the whole point of going there, and let the someone else get ripped off at their food prices, but other than that it is truly a unique place.

title: “Good Location,Small rooms”
text:
Well, I didn't had great expactions regarding the Hotel, but it was nice surprise. The concierge was very helpfull and after a quick check inn, I've move to my room. I've asked a room on a top floor and they gave me one.
The room was small, but I didin't had to share it now so it was enough.
The bath room was big enough.
Very clean and wityh high speed internet free. You have to ask for the password.
It was only one nigh, but a good sleep night.
The breakfast room is so tiny that if you bring 10 friends, it will full, so the better is to take the breakfast to the room. I did it and it was much better.
I recommend for short trips.

title: “Cool Setting, Upscale Design, Affordable Prices”
text:
Very cool mid-town setting with an upscale design at affordable prices. We recently stayed at the Night Hotel and we thoroughly enjoyed the experience. The room prices are very reasonable considering the product: on the small side but nicely appointed with very comfortable beds. The service is always friendly, efficient and helpful. As for location, proximity to Times Square can be interesting. The only downside: industrial strength heating/cooling systems in the rooms can be very noisy. Otherwise it's a perfect spot for a short business trip in the center of the city, or for a long weekend near the theater district.
Stayed October 2011

title: “Better to Sleep With Homeless in Central Park Than Use This Hotel”
text:
I Meant to write this a lot earlier to warn people about this hotel, but have had to deal with damage from Hurricanes
Ramada Inn Eastside- New York, New York
161 Lexington Avenue
New York City, NY 10016
We have traveled extensively all over the world for over 30 years and stayed in a range of lodging ranging from super luxurious six stars to rooms with dirt floors that you had to lock the doors to keep the goats out. When you go to Manhattan and pay those prices you expect a certain level of accommodation. Not a hotel better suited for some third world country. My apology for any third world county who has such a hotel.
Ramada Inn - New York, New York is dirty, small and had an odor problem. As soon as you entered the hotel you are hit by wall of smell somewhere between musty and old gym locker. Our family stayed in this hotel for six days. We would have moved out within 30 minutes if could have found another room. For some reason most of surrounding hotels were booked. The lobby was small and dirty with furnishing showing their age. There were two small elevators so we had to split into two groups. My daughter got stuck between floors for almost an hour. This elevator continued to do this the entire time we were there so we avoid it. The other elevator was soooo slow. It was much faster to walk. Not sure they ever fixed it. Even now there may be some poor guest trapped. The hallway to our room had musty smell of mold. Although we had requested a non-smoking room our room had the odor of stale cigarettes and half cleaned ashtrays littered the room. I won’t tell you how the bathroom smelled. The seat to the toilet was broken and if you did not sit just right you would slide right off the toilet onto the floor. Despite numerous requests over six days nothing was done. Bath tub was filthy (could tell by the pubic hair the previous occupant was a red head) and the drain control had a jagged piece of metal sticking out is side. The grout between the tiles had a nice coating of slimy blackish mildew. This is the only time I can remember on vacation going out to corner market and buying a bottle of bleach and scrubbing pad to clean the bathroom so we could use it. Very low water pressure and at best it was luke-warm. Tried to adjust the temperature and the faucet knob literally came off in my hand. Found major dust bunnies and debris of previous occupants in the space between the bed and the wall.
There was no tv remote in the room. Called the front desk and got nothing but promises. Had to wait until the occupants of a nearby room checked out and why the made cleaned that room got their TV remote. When we checked into the room the lightbulb to the reading lamp was burned out, called down to request it be replace. Said it would be. After several days and several requests and no action we went out and bought our own lightbulb. The bedspreads on the beds were in terrible condition with a number of holes you could one or more fingers through.
Then we get to the really fun part- meeting the room’s wildlife. On our first night after checking in going out to dinner and getting ready for bed, we pull back the bedspread and blanket and watch a number of black dots scurry across the sheets- LARGE fat bedbugs. I even managed to capture one in an empty pill bottle. Took a picture of it for proof and I will post in the picture. I immediately called the front desk and they said they would take care of it. How they took care of it was to ignore the problem and continue to use the same sheets. The reason I know this is there was a stain on one of the sheets and it was the same sheet night after night. It not a very pleasant thing to have to strip off the sheets from your bed, take them out into the hallway and shake them vigorously to get rid of any wildlife. Were talking doing this for five nights in a row. Despite this the sheets felt itchy. Then we had the world famous game called “Chase the cockroaches up the walls as you take a shower” Don’t get too close or they might jump on you. New York Roaches are well known for being aggressive and nasty. See a race in progress in my pictures I have posted about this hotel
Meeting the hotel’s wildlife continued at it Complimentary Continental Breakfast. Bagels were stale, juice had an off taste, fresh fruit had some pieces beginning to rot, flies and nats buzzing around food. Got a great picture of one when he landed on our table. I think he is smiling. What do you think? See picture I have posted. The bananas were in such bad condition they should have been buried rather then served to human beings. All it took was one exposure and a resulting queasy stomach and during the rest of our stay we ate breakfast elsewhere.
Among the Amenities offered were Computers with Internet access. Which was very true if you can find one that works or you can try and use a keyboard with most of the letters and number worn off. What the hotel does not tell you is that they do not provide printers. I found this out when I was in the process of trying to check in for my flight and wanted to print my boarding pass. I was informed at the front desk I would have to use the next door cybercafe. 
This meant you would have to pay by the minute to use the internet. I found out later from front desk that this was owned by the hotel. Nice way to earn a few extra buck from something that was suppose to be a free Amenities.
Then we come to the management and staff of the hotel. By their actions and response to questions asked and various requests by guests, they seemed to look at us guests as some sort of ill smelling bottom feeding scum sucking creatures and they were deities who like Job in the bible was cursed with the affliction of having to put up with them. Not only were they not responsive or helpful, they were ant-responsive and anti-helpful going out of their way to make the guest feel small when they dared disturbed important activities of reading a newspaper, talking to their girlfriends on the phone or just staring out the window.
While the price may seem right, the experience is not worth it. There are a lot better hotels than this in the area for about the same money. NYC is a fantastic place. Why ruin your visit by staying here. 
Good Luck, See The World and Stay Safe

title: “Surprisingly low-cost for the location and nice room.”
text:
If you go to San Francisco and you want to stay in a 4 star+ hotel in a good location, you have to pay a minimum $300. We were pleasantly surprised with the Hyatt Regency San Francisco. I went to the Hyatt website and with my AAA discount, paid less than $250 per night for a weekend in Oct. I booked 2 King Rooms - one for myself & husband, the other for my sister & brother-in-law. Her room was just as nice as ours.
The hotel is in the financial district, but within walking distance of Union Square and only 2 blocks from Pier 1. We went to the 49ers/Bucs game - to get to Candlestick, we walked a few blocks to the bus stop and took The 72 bus for $12 roundtrip. On Saturday, we walked to North Beach for dinner. The hotel is centrally located.
Rooms -- they must have been renovated recently. We had a beautiful view of the bridge, all of the furniture had been updated since our last visit 2 years ago and they even had a TV in the bathroom mirror. My husband loved the very large shower. Extremely clean and when I called for a shower cap, the nice gentleman at the door brought me 2. I then received a follow-up call to make sure my request had been taken care of -- that is wonderful service.
Great hotel bar and we were lucky enough to get access to the regency club because of my hgp status. Fantastic views, the continental breakfast was more than just pastries, juice & coffee -- they served a delicious oatmeal, smoked salmon, a variety of fruits and juices as well. The coffee machine made a very nice latte. The evening spread was just as nice. Keep in mind however that they have an honor bar, so you make your own drinks, but you are supposed to pay for them.
All in all we had a fantastic weekend and will definitely stay here again. I'm in SF for business in next week and have already booked another stay.

title: “Unforgettable romantic rendezvous!”
text: My husband and I have stayed here before and enjoyed it so much that we decided to go back again. Both times, we used a Travelzoo promotion, which includes a very large discount and free valet. We really just wanted a one night getaway to ourselves. From the moment we set foot on the property, everything was wonderful! Everyone was so friendly and welcoming!
