We were given a $10 coupon to the minibar for being part of their Kimpton In-Touch program (which is free- register online). Our room was huge and very modern. We booked the King Spa, but I believe we were upgraded to a suite because our room had an additional living room area. The bathroom was very large and had a 2 person shower and a huge soaking tub that you had to climb into via a marble step. We went to their free 5pm wine tasting. We had free appetizers, along with sangria, and enjoyed talking with other guests. When we got back to our room, the concierge had sent us a bottle of champagne and strawberries because he had heard us saying it was our anniversary. We were floored by this kind of customer service and attention!! We knew they had a DVD player in the room, so we brought our favorite movie to watch that evening. Overall, staying at the Hotel Palomar made all the difference in the world for our celebration, and we will be using it again in the future!!

title: “You get what you pay for!”
text: Going to make this a short review: This hotel is not a pleasant place to stay in at all - my mum nearly killed me for booking it!! HOWEVER, we decided last minute to stay in NY, so we wanted something cheap! You really do get what you pay for and although i would not stay here again, we had a great time and the location is very good!! Also, we were up and out early as we did not really want to be in the room! So probably got to see more of NY than we would have otherwise!!! That's about the only good thing i can say!!

title: “Outstanding-Loved Hotel Palomar”
text: Stayed at the Palomar from May 21-May 25, 2008. Everything was wonderful. Hotel staff goes out of their way to make you feel comfortable. Our room was an executive king on the 9th floor; which was a comfortable size. The property was always quiet, thus making it ideal for uninterupted slumber. Every evening we returned to find our bed turned down and soft jazz playing on the radio. This made for a great prelude to winding down from a busy day sightseeing. As a previous guest stated...the hotel left nothing to be desired. Would most definately stay at the Palomar again. Kimpton Hotels are just FABULOUS!

title: “very good hotel in central location”
text:
Stayed for three nights during a weekend paying a very good rate through priceline. Got a room on the lower floors which was of good size compared to NYC standards.
Very clean & modern, everything was in perfect order. I was especially amazed that the room was very quiet, heard hardly any noise neither from outside or from other rooms or the hallway.
Coffee maker with starbucks provided, mini-bar is pricey.
Location is perfect, almost on Times Square. Subways, eating options etc within walking distance. Check-inn staff & concierge very efficient. There is a small business center. Internet fee is 9,95$. Housekeeping did also a good job. The hotel is connected to a cinema with a mexican restaurant and a starbucks. Small grocery next door. 
Overall, I really enjoyed the stay at the Westin Times Square, nothing to complain about. Would definetely return if I got a good rate.
Small hint: If you need a cab to travel outside manhattan, do not let the hotelboys know. They call a cab already waiting and the cab driver needs to pay some sort of commission for the ride which will be eventually paid by yourself. I did that mistake and it ended in a 10 minutes argument regarding the price for a 5 miles ride to Jersey city. So just tell the guys you want to a destination somewhere in Manhattan and negiotate the fare with the cab driver afterwards (but this is a problem certainly not limited to the Westin).

title: “Escapist”
text: Conventions can be stressful. Its great to be enveloped by the ambiance of elegance & leisure when the day's business is over. My room was smaller than the usual, the food merely so-so, but that lobby is unforgettable.

title: “Check in nightmare”
text: Our dental team was kept waiting in the lobby while the front desk emailed forms to be completed and faxed back. This is for a room that was reserved, confirmed and paid for prior to their arrival.

title: “Satisfied Customer!”
text: We booked through Hotwire to get a good rate. Upon arrival, it didn't appear to be in a great area but we weren't walking so it was fine. It's in a corporate area and headquarters such as Ford are very close. Fairlane Mall is only a mile away. I was greeted by the very friendly desk clerk and welcomed to the property. After checking me in, she provided warm chocolate chip cookies. I had a friend with me who was not staying at the hotel but she gave them a cookie as well. We found our room to be a corner king. It was roomy and decorated quite nicely. Everything we encountered was clean. The pool and 2 jacuzzi's were a joy to use after a long day. It was nice that after 10pm it was adults only. I'd have to say that the fitness center is one of the best I've seen in a hotel. They had Precor equipment and it was top notch. My husband and I became ill during the night and were feeling awful come morning. A request for late check out was not a problem. All communication with the staff was friendly and helpful. I did not use the restaurant so I can't comment on that. Chili's is basically in the parking lot and Red Robin is next door. I felt completely safe at this property as well. All outside doors require key cards to enter. Key cards are also needed to operate the elevators. A security car circled the property. It was a nice experience and I'd definitely recommend this propety.

title: “Charged in Excess”
text:
Worst place I have ever stayed at!! Okay, my boyfriend and I have stayed here a few times prior and didn't have a terrible experience (definitely not the greatest though), but this past time ensures that we will NEVER stay here again.
First of all, the king bed we slept on was the most uncomfortable bed. It had stiff sheets, a scratchy blanket, and tiny pillows which were unsatisfying. Secondly, the room was arranged so awkwardly. Everything seemed to open the wrong way (the refrigerator door, the bathroom door, etc) so you couldn't even maneuver in the room properly.
Last, and most importantly.... PLEASE CHECK THE BACK OF YOUR DOOR!!
California State law requires all hotels/motels/inns to post a card on a "conspicuous" place which lists the rate or range of rates by the day for lodging. (Check out CA Civil Code Section 1863 for the info.) Well, the rates listed were anywhere from $65-$105. I was charged $140 per night. According to the law, for any violation they shall pay $100 or three times the amount of the sum charged in excess, whichever is greater. When it came time to check out, I mentioned this to the front desk agent. Mind you, I was being polite and not looking for an argument just looking for my refund that I was due. However, the front desk guy was very argumentative and kept mentioning that I was incorrect; it was based on "supply and demand". Look, I know what supply and demand is, and I know I was staying on Labor Day weekend. However, the issue is that I was charged in excess of what the maximum amount was listed, regardless of the fact that it was Labor Day weekend. We argued back and forth for a while, which ended up with us leaving without our refund.
I have continuously called the hotel requesting to speak to the manager. Every time, the manager is not there, even though I have called back when the front desk agent has said the manager would be there. I have also sent an email with no reply.
I'm sure the management is too lazy to update the cards that are on the backs of the room doors, so perhaps you too are being charged in excess. Good luck in getting your entitled refund though.

title: “More than adequate, but nothing special”
text: My college roommate and I try to meet up once or twice a year for a trip and decided to hit Chicago over the July 4th weekend. I found a $99 rate at the Swissotel through Travelzoo so that made booking accomodations an easy choice. The location was super convenient for us...a quick walk to Grant Park for Taste of Chicago and the fireworks, the Art Institute, and nearby L stations to get us everywhere else as we were without a car (for which I was grateful based on the hotel's parking fees). Our room had two full beds which were very comfortable and we liked that we had a shower stall separate from the bath. Everything was very clean in our room...housekeeping took good care of us. The hotel was packed and we did hear quite a bit of noise from other guests but only when they were passing through the hallways...no big deal. What was a problem was the crazy wait time for the elevators. People were lined up halfway through the lobby a few times when we were passing through...luckily we were always on our way out when the lines were that bad so we didn't have to wait too long. Overall, I think the Swissotel is a perfectly nice facility and I feel like we got a good deal but I would never consider paying full price to stay there as you can get the same amenities and service at lower rates elsewhere.

title: “Just ok..”
text:
Eh. 
Only reason we booked this hotel is because many of the other hotels in the area were booked or uber expensive due to the 10K race that weekend. Rate for a double room was going at $168/night. Was able to use my points because I'd never pay that for a room at the Radisson. 
The Good:
Check in was smooth, employees were friendly, lobby decor had that "Texas" charm. Nice fish tank and seating area. The Radisson has an onsite Starbucks along with a TGIFriday's restaurant. There's also a happy hour in the lobby that we should have taken advantage of but didn't. Location is good as it is walking distance to many of the good bars and restaurants or a short cab ride away depending on what you're in the mood for. Pool area was just okay. Not enough chairs around the pool if you wanted to lay out, but there was a deck area above the pool with more seating. They have a "business center" with just one computer, printer, and I think a fax machiene. You can use it for a minimum or $10.83 (I just needed to print something so the cost was a bit annoying). They have a gym but I didn't use it. We had a paper in the morning and there was a complementary bottle of water in in the room. Room was also equipped with a flat screen tv and a desk. You have the option to valet or self park. We chose the self parking at $16/night which is average for most hotels in the area.
The not so good:
Hotel rooms feel more like a motel. Definitely dated and it seemed like they wallpapered over old outlets because walls weren't smooth. It said we had sleep number beds, but couldn't find the remote to use them. Linens looked old and tattered. We were on the 4th floor facing Cesar Chavez and Congress, was able to watch the 10K run in the morning but really not much of a view. Bathrooms were very small and in need of a facelift. They did have a coffee maker and a small vanity outside of the bathroom which allowed for a little extra space. 
Overall I'd say the Radisson is just average, but don't go in with high expectations. It's an ok place to stay the night if you can get it at a cheaper rate.

title: “Would definitely stay there again”
text: My wife and I took another couple to New York City recently. The other couple was visiting us from Brazil and this was their first visit to the United States. Imagine our surprise when we discovered the street on which the hotel is located (46th) is nicknamed Little Brazil. The street had several Brazilian restaurants on it and many Brazilians stay in the hotel. Needless to say, we felt right at home. First off, the name is a misnomer. The hotel isn't at Times Square, which is two blocks away. They don't normally allow you to let check in before 3 p.m., but they already had several rooms cleaned and allowed us to check in at 1:30. Our room was on the top floor, which meant a long, slow elevator ride up. There are two elevators, but only one that goes all the way up. The room was very nice and really clean. It was a little small, but very comfortable. It had a huge walk-in closet with a programmable safe for our valuables. There was also an extra pillow. The TV was a flat screen that telescoped out from the wall. The bed was extremely comfortable. The climate controls on the air conditioner kept our room the perfect temperature. The bathroom was a little cramped, but clean and adequate. Only one person at a time can really use it to get ready, so plan accordingly if you're on a schedule. One really nice feature is that the maid service doesn't come banging on the door at 9 a.m. like most places. We never saw them on our floor, but our room was always cleaned and the towels replaced. They left more than enough towels each day, so that was never a concern. There were two cordless phones in the room, with clear instructions on which numbers to dial for specific services. Now, when we wanted to go out, we had to wait for the elevator to come up to the 14th floor from the lobby, which was very time-consuming, especially if you're in a hurry. You could take the stairs if you don't mind descending 14 flights of stairs. One nice little unexpected bonus was the second-floor bar. Dubbed "the biggest little bar in NYC" by the management, it stays open late and offers just about any libation you could desire. The sign out front promised $3 drafts, $3 shots and $5 cocktails. We went two different nights. The first night they were out of draft beer. The shots were the smallest I've ever seen, but what do you expect for $3? The bartender was a friendly young American girl who kept our glasses filled. The place is tiny, with only enough room for six two-seat tables and three chairs at the bar, but has all of the high-dollar liquors. The second night couldn't have been more different than the first. A different bartender, who sounded like she might have come from Eastern Europe, never did get the prices right. She tried to charge me $6 for a shot and had no idea what the actual prices were when I questioned the prices. She was playing this Euro techno-pop music very loudly, so much so that it made it difficult for my wife and I to talk. She also had her boyfriend sitting at the bar, and between drinking shots with him she went downstairs and out front with him to smoke, leaving the bar completely unattended and several people's glasses empty for an extended period of time. The next day, even though we'd checked out, the hotel alowed us to leave our bags there while we explored New York City some more. They locked the bags in a secure room until we returned to pick them up up. It was extremely cordial of them to do that even though they were under no obligation to do so. I recommend this hotel and would stay there again.

title: “Great value for a $200 room”
text:
This is my seventh stay at this hyatt, which has recently gone through a fairly extensive renovation. Having said that, if looking for a true five star hotel, you will be sorely dissappointed. 
PROS
almost always available, even when booking day of, and at a very reasonable price.
Every room has a balcony which is particularly beneficial for smokers.
Great video oh demand, which is a staple at most hyatts, but if you plan to use, expect to pay approx $16 per movie.
Room service provides a fairly comprehensive selection of dishes that most people can find something that they enjoy. (the fries are phenomenal)
There is a Starbucks in the lobby that provides convenient access to a standardized and renowned coffee maker with minimal hassle. (can be charged to room)
The Hyatt Cenbtrury Plaza also offers an amazing convention center for throwing events and charity functions.
CONS
Expect to pay an additional $20 a day in valet fees if you have a car, not to mention a ten minute wait to receive your car, longer if there's an event
Rooms are below average size compared to most hyatt regency's in the US.
The AC is extremely outdated, which isn't a problem unless your in the heat of summer.
the hyatt has many events, which will probably disappoint the family who comes here for a quite vacation.
The bathroom is probably the biggest weakness of the whole hotel, being extremely small with a toilet that only a little boy would be comfortable on.
The bar in the lobby always closes early, with bartenders that are more focussed on the women than the customer service 
OVERALL
again this is a great hotel for either a hyatt patron, or someone who has come for an event at the haytt, but it could be equated to an older woman who has just gotten a face lift to attract its prey, many things are outdated, or poorly thought out in room layout

title: “Just OK for a convention”
text:
Apparently this hotel is located in a high crime area. There were police cars parked in front of the restaurants that were within walking distance of the hotel every night. When walking back to the hotel after dinner the police advised us to be careful.
There is Starbucks located right in the hotel lobby which is a real plus except that it is closed on Saturday and Sunday. I guess they cater to the people in offices and not to hotel guests.
The water lines were being replaced and the water from the faucet was very dirty looking. We were compensated for that with the receipt of one bottle of water in our room which I guess was supposed to last two people for five days. The ice from the ice machine was also dirty.
Our room was a King mini-suite but did not contained a refrigerator or microwave. There was a coffee maker and some days the coffee supplies were replaced. Other days, they weren't.
The hotel charges $10.95 per day for EACH wi-fi connection so for our two computers the charge was $21.90 per day - ridiculous!
The meals that we had along with our convention [lunch and dinner] were really excellent e.g. a large grilled salmon salad for lunch.
It's not just this hotel but lately every hotel room we have been in has been really dark making it very difficult to read.

title: “Not in the best area, but OK for what we were looking for”
text:
I'm really late in writing this review, so I wont say too much. My friend and I were looking for a cheap place to stay in San Diego...and that's exactly what we got. The hotel was nothing to write home about (except if you want to tell people about the strip club across the street). But in a way that was OK because we were just there to shower and sleep. However, the area the hotel is in doesnt look like it would be the safest, and we would have to admit when coming back to the hotel late at night we were sometimes a little scared. Totally unfounded though. 
All in all we got what we paid for. I wouldn't go back mostly because it wasn't in an area that had anything going on except fast food restaurants and strip clubs. It's nice being able to walk around the area near your hotel...but not here! Not a "touristy" area by any means.

title: “Excellent for children”
text: Stayed in November 2003. VERY nice Residence Inn. If you have children pick the bunk bed option; my daughters LOVED them. The breakfast might not have been as all encompassing as other RI we have stayed at - but very good. Only minor problem is that you are unable to walk to any good restaurants nearby. But highly recommend this RI.

title: “In the Middle of Garment District”
text:
My Husband and I were very satisfied with the service and the room. We arrived early, but that was just fine because we left our luggage with the Hotel Receptionist and went shopping right outside the hotel. By the time we walked 1 block, we purchased cologne, purses, walking suits and a leather wallet.
We were even satisfied with the food off the street cart (chicken and gyro on pita bread). 
It was great that the hotel managed to keep an upscale look among all of the action right outside of its doors. Keep up the great service Broadway Plaza. We will return!

title: “Great staff and above average food. Rooms an issue”
text:
Okay full disclosure. I am a Marriott point addict. Not so much for vacations or leisure but as someone who travels 130 days a year I tend to go out of my way to stay at Marriotts. Thus when coming to Seattle for a conference I chose the Renaissance as it was the nearest Marriott property to the convention center ...a short 6 blocks downhill and a very long 6 blocks back up 
Rooms. 
Sadly the one thing that is an issue Rooms are okay but on the smaller side. Too much furniture jammed into them and bathrooms are small and not very well appointed. It's clean and it's okay but it needs a bit of a rethink in terms of layout. Secondly and worse is lack of sound proofing. I had a a connecting room door and could literally here everything going on next door. Literally my neighbors calls to his wife and I didn't need to turn on my tv since I could hear his as if we were sharing a room. He wasn't particularly loud talker it's just clear that no sound proofing was evident. Luckily he checked out after one day but it really would make me think twice about staying here again. Which is too bad because the public areas are lovely, modern comfortable and well designed. The service was great friendly compotent and knowledgeable. 
I ate a few lunches in the restaurant and the food was very good with lots of local ingredient s and very fresh...but still the small rooms, tiny bathrooms and complete lack of sound proofing make me think you should try the Marriott Seattle waterfront instead. Or there is always the four seasons !

title: “Excellent little hotel”
text: It was sparkling clean, the rooms were well appointed and very quiet. Since the building used to be the Chemists Club, it was a cute touch to use laboratory beakers as drinking glasses in the bathroom. The location was very convenient and the staff was extremely friendly and helpful

title: “Great hotel for good price”
text: Great hotel for the discounted price on [--]. You can walk to Georgetown! We stayed here for a quick girls weekend and thought it was perfect. The concierge was very helpful too! He booked us restaurant reservations and advised a good tour. Highly recommended!

title: “Great stop over”
text:
My wife and I spent an overnight layover at the Sheraton Gateway.
We found the hotel to be great for what we needed before continuing on to San Francisco the following day. 
The staff members at the front counter were friendly enough although I didn't agree with having to pay for short term parking. If we needed it overnight then fair enough but we only needed parking for 4hrs before having to return our rental car. 
The room was big and very spacious. 
We used the gym on the ground floor. There were various weight machines and cardio machines. The pool was closed due to maintenance.
The main restaurant was closed due to it being a Sunday so we ate at the bar. The food was good and reasonably priced. There was also an endless supply of non alcoholic drinks.
In regards to the internet we used the internet on the ground floor which was located next to the bar. It was complementary so I'm not sure why the other review writers were charged. 
There is a complementary shuttle service to the airport which runs approximately every 20minutes. Because the Sheraton is the last pickup its a direct trip to LAX which takes about 5-10minutes. 
Overall the Sheraton is a great stopover/layover and I highly recommend it. 
The only negative I have which doesn't involve the Sheraton is the poor service provided by United Airlines. All I can say is their service in general sux!! I don't recommend as a preferred airline.

title: “Nothing special”
text:
Ask for a renovated room! I was staying in a renovated room, while my friend was not, so I got to compare them both. 
They have great beds and I got a good night's sleep. That is always the priority to me! Some of the hotel is a bit dated and unstylish, but if you are travelling on business and a good night's sleep is your priority, you will be happy. Towels and toiletries are nice too. 
The hotel is on the Riverwalk, which can be convenient, but can be loud at night. If this is a concern, request a higher floor. The balconies are large and a nice touch. 
The breakfast buffet and parking are ridiculously expensive. I pay less for both when I travel to New York City!
The fitness center has great weights and some nice machines, but half of the cardio machines were broken during my visit.
The best benefit of this hotel is they have a free washer and dryer for guest use! It's in the workout room, so you can babysit your laundry and workout at the same time. They sell laundry soap for only 50 cents. The pool stays open late, but is small and plain. 
If I were travelling for leisure and had time to enjoy the hotel, I prefer the Marriott Plaza. This is fine for business though, if you are on someone else's dime!

title: “Great Location for UNF Activities”
text: We stayed here for our first UNF visit... and it has always been our best stay for the last four and a half years! We had everyone stay here for graduation... with a party by the pool before heading to the beaches! Easy walk to great places to eat, and and easy drive to even more. The staff was nice and the room was clean. We have always felt comfortable here and this stay was no exception.

title: “Good Value and Good Location”
text:
Good Value for the money. Tribeca is less expensive than other neighborhoods in NYC and Hilton Garden Inn is a good choice:
- free internet (that works! Sometimes you have a free access but no work)
- fair prices in the pantry pavilion in site
- good staff
- subway in the same block
- well located btw Tribeca and Soho

title: “Clean, Comfortable, Good Price and Free Parking!”
text:
Cow Hollow Inn isn't fancy or upscale but it's very reasonably priced and most important to me, it was very clean and comfortable. It might be a ways away from Fisherman's Wharf but we did walk there one day so it's doable if you like to walk. It's right on the bus line so it's a convenient place to stay once you learn the transportation system of the city buses or the double-deckers. The staff were very friendly and helpful with maps and giving us info. about how to ride their public transportation. We wished our room had a small refrigerator but that was no big deal.
 The FREE parking in their garage was a big plus as many other hotels charge you to park there. Also, another big bonus was the excellent restaurant they have, just take the elevator down or walk outside. We ate breakfast there twice and it was excellent with delicious homemade pancakes and crepes! We would definitely stay here on our next trip to San Francisco.

title: “They made it right and went beyond”
text:
We stayed happily on an upper floor front room for our niece's wedding 18 months ago and loved this hotwl.
Being in Boston to care for very sick relative, we needed peace and quiet as well as a fabulous location. I read another review that challenged the "quiet" promised by the staff, and asked the staff about room 101 being quiet. I was assured that it was very quiet.
When we checked in on a Saturday, we talked to the reception desk staff about our need for quiet and he reassured us that it was very quiet. We checked in and unpacked. The room faces the alley at the allet level and had numerous trash bins (the large rectangular metal ones). I went to the front desk again to ask about trash pickup day. The woman did not know when yhe trash pickup day was, but assured us that 101 was a very quiet room.
No trash pickup on Sunday morning...gloriously quiet, comfortable, more space than we needed. Then, Monday morning, 2am...until 4:30am, the various sanitation companies drove their trucks through the alleys and pickep up, dumped and slammed down the now empty metal bins. This was followed by a delivery truck idling outside those lovely windows, so we left early to catch breakfast near the hospital facility. We asked about the trash pickup and complained about the noise...this gentleman said the pickip was every day.
After following up our cimplaint through managers, we were offered room 103, which has no exterior walls, but is on a short hallway to rooms 101 and 102.
THIS is the room you want for quiet. They not only changed our room, but gave us a 50% refund for the noisy night's stay. Then I left prescription glasses in the nightstand when my husband checked out (I was at the hosp already). Figured it out 2 days later at home and called the hotel. They found it and fedex'd it back to me. 
Thanks to Kurt and Scott and the front desk folks for easing the strain of this kind of family visit. We will stay there again because of the excellent response to our needs.

title: “Pleasant Stay”
text: We arrived on Easter Sunday, 3/23 and stayed for 4 nights leaving on Thursday, 3/27. Our request for early check-in, queen bed, and corner room were accommodated. Check-in easy and no problem. The room was on the small side but in a large older city, this is to be expected. The windows are single pained with no screens so you can literally hear everything outside from people talking, glass bottle throwers, and sirens. If that will bother you, bring plugs because I don't see that problem changing no matter what room you stay in. We bought a bottle of wine for our room and we called down to the front desk and within 5 mintues, we had wine glasses and a bottle opener sent up to our room. There is only 1 elevator so either be patient or take the sprial staircase. People who do not have luggage complain about taking the stairs but hello, you are in SF!!! Walking on an angle kinda comes with the territory!!!!! The hotel provides a cold continental breakfast but we did not take part so I can not comment. Bar area open for night until about 930ish. Nice, they even have "hh" prices. Drew is a nice guy! Check-out was as easy as check-in.

title: “Hidden gem”
text: Our stay at Casablanca was great. The front desk staff were very helpful, the rooms were cleaned and turned down promptly each day, and we were provided with complimentary robes and slippers for our entire stay. The hotel had complimentary snacks and beverages throughout the day (cookies, fruit, water, coffee, etc.) and the wine reception each night was fabulous. The hotel had an overall European feel which was a nice change from the standard chain hotels in the area. The room rate was very competitive, especially considering it's proximity to Times Square, Broadway Theaters, and 2 large subway stations within one block. We would definitely not think twice to stay here again.

title: “Great rooms, great value!!!”
text:
The Omni Colonnade was a good stay, especially for the price we paid. We booked a package through Travelocity and got a good deal. We also signed up for the Omni's free Membership program for added free bonuses- free newspaper every morning, free WiFi and a turn down service that we never got. The hotel in itself is nice. The lobby and recpetion areas are not that great, especially compared to other Omni hotels, but it was not bad either. For Xmas, they had a huge Alamo made of ginger bread and it was very nice and impressive. their Xmas tree was lovely and they had professional photographers if you wanted a pic taken of you next to it or the Alamo. The only thing i did not like at all in the lobby area was the really loud and obnixious music. I hope they turn the volume down. However, we got back late at night a couple of nights, and they had a guy playing the piano at their piano bar, whish is right next to the lobby...that was very lovely. 
The Rooms were the best part of our stay at the Omni. They are spacious, and VERY clean and comfortable. THeir bed was a little piece of heaven. Lots of down comforters, lots of plush pillows, VERY cozy indeed. The room is the reason why i would stay here again. The bathroom was run of the mill. Nothing extravagant, but also not as bad as other comments made it sound. Regular bathrooms that you get at any hotel. The view was breathtaking, we had view to the whole city from floor 15, it was really spectacular, and the sunrise from there was aboslutely stunning. 
The service was very mediocre. The front desk staff made it feel like it was a nuisance to approach their desk. From the room i had to call three times to get extra towels, and our wake up calls were up to 20 minutes late each time. THe bell bloys and bell captain were super nice and friendly, especially Jose, and they were the only ones that made it seem like they wanted to make our stay memorable. But again, the front desk staff was rude and stand-offish, which for a supposedly four star hotel, was very disappointing. 
The pools, saunas, hot tubs and work out room were fabulous. I did not use them because we were visiting family and spending as much time with them as possible, but the area looked so very nice. 
The Bolo's restaurant was great, the breakfast buffette was delightful and for a very good price. On Xmas day we paid the 50 bucks for the Xmas buffette, for which they used the ballroom areas, and brought chefs, piano player, and lots of wait staff, and it was really truly wonderful and elegant. 
Overall it was a good stay, but my disappointment was in the type of attention and service from the front desk. But the most important things, that is the room, the bed, and the cleanliness of the hotel, were spectacular. I would stay there again, but would love to see the front desk staff give better service.

title: “noisy heaters, not clean, very no frills hotel”
text:
i suppose if you are only interested in saving money, this place is adequate, and probably a step above some of the really sleazy hotels in NY. 
It did the job and the bed was comfortable, the furnishings and fixtures in the room and bathroom were in good shape, and i always enjoy free wifi, but the pipes clanked in the heater all night, and the place wasn't all that clean, especially in the hallways and elevators.
The building feels dingy, feels like it's in an old warehouse, cramped corridors, no lobby to speak of, not much service of any kind. The "fitness center" is 3 pieces of old cardio equipment crammed into a basement closet with no windows and poor ventilation. I asked at the front desk if there was a nearby full service gym that guests had access to, and they didn't have a clue (and referred me to two other people at the hotel who also had no idea... didn't seem like that obscure a question).

title: “Overpriced and lack of interest from the staff to address problems”
text:
Would not return to this hotel .
Old shower design required you to get in the shower to turn it on and no hot water available for 10 minutes. Staff said that we would just have to wait for the water to heat up . No apologies were given. Just that "it was an older building" . We have never had to wait for hot water.
Went to Happy Hour and the house wine was $17.00 dollars A GLASS!!
A dog across the hall started barking at 7:00 am when the owners went to breakfast. Finally enough people complained to the 
front desk that they took the dog downstairs.
We will not be returning to this over rated Dallas landmark...
.

title: “Wonderful stay at NYC's hidden gem”
text:
I am a frequent visitor to New York City and this was, without question, the best visit I have had in years and I owe a lot of this wonderful experience to the folks at this fine establishment and the marketing department of the parent company. The city director of marketing, who assisted me with my visit, was brilliant. Amazing staff, timeliness to my requests, assistance for various reasons, etc ... everything was wonderful. I am staying at this property or another in this company every time I visit the city from this point forward.
The biggest bonuses were the free upgrade from a corner King deluxe room to an unreal suite with a perfect view of the NYC skyline and the surprise New York Yankees birthday gift package I received upon arrival. Little things that are unexpected go a long way and for someone who worked for the world's No. 1 resort at one time and currently is in public relations, these were just two of the many things that made this visit unbelievably wonderful.

title: “Beautiful Family Resort on PB”
text: This is a beautiful resort with amazing grounds and beachfront location, convenient to attractions. Great food and service. Tired rooms need updating, but livable for now. Splurge for beachfront, it's worth it.

title: “I liked the price and clean bed!”
text: I used the pool often and it was generally good to swim in. When something was broken the staff expressed concern and took action. There was no question about the cleanliness of the bath area. Comfy bed, heater and air-conditioning. It was pretty close to Seaworld and the downtown area.

title: “Great stay”
text:
Hotel itself is in good location, right above the subway station. Room I stayed was big and bed was comfy. The staffs were very knowledgable.
The bad is the maid just doesn't seem to care much about cleaning. The very top of the blinds are really dirty. Other than that, my two night stays were great.

title: “Good room no sleep”
text:
ZaZa is outwardly beautiful and if you are into partying and people watching it is a great place to stay. We stayed in the ZaZa suite, supposedly the nicest in the hotel, and it was fabulous. Opulent, well furnished and extremely neat. The rest of the hotel is a bit cramped including the lobby, restaurant and bar. 
The people watching is great but if you want to go to bed before 3:00 Am on the weekend and you are facing the front of the hotel you can forget it. Loud techno music blasts from the bar and can be heard and felt four floors up. 
Overall a nice hotel but it can't decide if it is a night spot or a luxury hotel. It only succeeded on the former.

title: “Can't believe they put us up here!”
text: Came with a colleague to do a project in Austin. We were shocked that they put us up in this dive. What a way to treat out of town guests. It is literally underneath the freeway, which you can hear all night long. The hotel was dirty and gross inside. There were all sorts of drunk guys (fellow hotel residents) hanging around at night on the balconies. I didn't feel safe going to the pop machine outdoors. We were so happy it was only one night. Next time we will pay for our own hotel and stay somewhere decent.

title: “Bad hotel for business travel, perhaps for a cheap shopping vacation”
text: I came to NYC for 2 nights for business, and based on the reviews on TripAdvisor, I chose Hotel Stanford for the location near my client as well as the price (within my per diem budget). This was NOT what I expected from the reviews. The carpet had stains on it, the bed was extremely wobbly, the furniture had dust and hair on it and the TV was extremely outdated as was the decor. Paint was peeling and it looked like the chain lock on the door had been replaced at least three times. I must not have gotten one of the "updated" rooms; I was in room #1014 and the musty smell gave me a headache. I was nervous to take my socks off or get under the covers (which the room did not even have a comforter)... and I am a traveller who is comfortable staying in hostels and budget hotels! I would MAYBE consider this for someone looking for a cheap hotel in a good location... because the location was great... but I moved on my second night to the nearby DoubleTree for just $100 more a night. To me it was worth it. Cannot comment on the breakfast because I didn't stay long enough. You get what you pay for and even though $200 a night seems like a lot to some people, apparently it doesn't pay for much in NYC. Not according to my experience at this hotel. A pro was that it was fairly quiet.

title: “Wonderful hotel!”
text: We spent 4 nights at the Allegro over Memorial Day Weekend and loved it! We got a free upgrade to a suite, the rooms were fun, the service was great. The all-you-can-drink wine hour was very nice; the lounge is cool and everyone was there mixing it up. The walls were not too thin, but if you have rude loud people next door (as we did one night), you may hear it. Otherwise, very quiet. The rooms were very comfortable, everyone was friendly and helpful and it was a fun hotel all in all. Way better than those boring old basic hotels like the Hilton and Hyatt! Very close to an L station and an easy walk to everything = Good Locale.

title: “Great Location and price but poor service”
text:
Great location and excellent price but most of the staff couldn't have cared less. 
When we checked in we noticed a strong odor - like baby powder. We assumed someone had gotten over zealous with air freshener and turned on air-handling system to clear out the smell. When we came back to room at around 6 pm it still smelled so we called to front desk. They said they were all booked up and to call housekeeping which we did. But no one responded by 10 pm. Next morning we called housekeeping again. They said they'd be up within 10 minutes. We waited half hour then went to breakfast. We requested new room and did get moved - to a room with a very loud air-handling system. Housekeeping did show up eventually - they were in the room when we came back from breakfast.
Rooms were clean but common areas were not. Good continental breakfast.

title: “not impressed”
text: when the lobby doubles as a bar and the "heated" but in fact unheated pool area is designed to be a drinking lounge you have need to be concerned. especially as a biz traveller who might need some sleep. the staff were not overly concerned with anything, if we had this experience at a 3 star hotel i'd be as unimpressed as i am with this stupid ipad2. the room overlooked one of the loudest service plant setups ever but the alternate was the pool/bar area. parking is a nightmare so the hotel charges you $36 usd /day to make up for this. its tad too far to walk with kids to anything worth walking to. we were booked for what was intended to be a relaxing week but when the soft beds did in one back and threatened to do in another we shifted after 3. must try harder.

title: “Attention to detail, execution and commitment.”
text: I stay in 75-100 properties a year. The difference between a professional and an amateur is attention to detail. This trip was for a conference involving 4000. The hotel even thought to put out complimentary bottles of water at the registration desk for those waiting in line. Lines, by the way, that never materialized because of sufficient front desk staff and preparedness. Without exception every staff person I had contact with was professional, courteous and helpful. The multi-towered property is laid out so long elevator lines don't develop at lunch or the end of the day. Connected to food places that are per diem friendly without braving the elements. Property is well maintained and comfortable after a long day.The Sheraton Dallas was committed to playing a role in the success of this conference. In my opinion, they hit a home run.

title: “We Agree ....we loved it!”
text: We (family of four) stayed here on a spur of the moment weekend getaway. The decor of this hotel is great - beautiful and out of the ordinary. From the moment we stepped into the place we had good time. (especially because of the friendly, welcoming and fun loving staff!) Our room, though not large, was fine for the four of us. It was comfortable and modern. We had a great view from our 16th floor room and we also wandered up to the terrace patio for an even better spot for pictures. Drinks at Opia were delicious and the singer on Saturday night was very good. Breakfast the next morning at Opia was also good. Overall a wonderful stay- would highly recommend.

title: “Great Chicago Location”
text: Incredible view out our 23rd floor room. We left the curtains open the entire stay, both night and day views were spectacular. Lunch at the hotel was excellent but on the pricy side. Nice breakfast spot two doors down. Took city tour in the double decker bus. Must see the show millionaire quartet! Everything is close, would stay at hotel again, very friendly staff.

title: “Hidden Gem”
text:
We stayed in one of their suites and it was perfect for a bachelorette party. Close to everything - galleria (shopping), midtown, rice village (night life). The colors were really fun and fresh, not overwhelming or tacky.
Liked the shower, although no curtain (not designed to have one), loved the counter space in the "kitchen" area (mini fridge & sink) and adorable/fun ice bucket, you just wanted to take it home.
Liked that there were two AC thermostats, but didn't like that the bedroom AC didn't ever kick on. The bedroom was uncomfortable for sleeping, but the outer room was perfect.
We asked for extra shampoo and conditioner (sunday morning) and they were quick to bring it up.
Not too many people I know have heard of it, so all in all, great place, great location and the parking is free.

title: “Great location, good hotel.”
text: The location of the hotel in Manhattan is outstanding - walking distance to Times Square, Central Park. Couldn't have asked for a better spot for a hotel. All the staff with whom I interacted were quite friendly and helpful. One concierge I approached a couple of times to help with directions and advice was excellent. The room was a decent size, pretty much what I would expect for Manhattan. It wasn't big but not small either. It was clean, comfortable and quiet, so I couldn't ask for much more. I stayed on the Club Lounge level so I had access to that lounge. It was helpful for using the internet and grabbing a bottle of water. The snack selections were okay but I have seen better at other Sheraton hotels. Nevertheless, it was convenient to have access to this lounge. I didn't use any facilities within the hotel. However, my one complaint about the hotel - $15/day for wireless internet and $10/day to use the gym? When you're paying $300/night, it seemed excessive. Despite those drawbacks, I would stay here again. You can't beat the location and I found the room very comfortable.

title: “This was a nightmare!”
text: The pictures are truly deceptive. The hotel staff was rude and inconsiderate. This is one of the dirtiest hotels I have seen in my life! I booked this place through hotels.com, after a verbal confirmation that I would have a private bath! After seeing the hotel, and the shared bath; we were out in 10 minutes. We waited on the road, while I worked out the refund with the staff at hotels.com. The only positive side to the place, is it's location. And, by the way, it is NOT a cheap stay! One may rather stay on the streets! Thankfully we got our money back...from hotel.com; the hotel manager refused to even listen to our woes!

title: “Absolutely lovely, clean and great situated. Friendly staff.”
text:
For a short or longer stay, you will like this hotel. To expensive for me as I travelled alone but as they had a discount I had to try it. Had such a wonderful stay!
It was my second time in New York. I actually wanted the same hotel as last time but the Milburn had an interesting discount. Breakfast is included and really basic, but available. Staff is always friendly and ready to help you, advice you. New York is known for small rooms but I was surprised of the great size. Nice bathroom, big flatscreen tv, I-pod alarm, kitchenette, microwave, fridge, iron and ironing board. There was also a lounge sofa. Gave the room a luxureous feeling.
Situated in a nice safe area, subway at 72 and 79 St nearby, several supermarkets and a lot to see and shop on Broadway if you want to walk to 42nd Street. It is not down town but down town is just around the corner.

title: “A classic - Iconic - In the 80's I'd have been delighted - Now dated.”
text:
It's the name that you grew up with, the communal areas lobby, bars are faultless, I booked on a BA Flight and Hotel package at a very attractive rate, maybe some rooms are being modernised... mine was clean, but dated.. Okay, so the room was a little passe, in style, non of the fittings stood out,and maybe waiting to be refurbished - however I'd expect the little things to be better - the towels and toiletries not of the quality I'd expect, En Suite was just old marble and fittings / shower curtain and shower - just dated - with a light buzzing in the wardrobe, which I couldn't switch off, Air con a little difficult to control, a mini bar with no pricing, no coffee facility - I could have asked and didn't !, the TV channel list under glass next the bed, was out of date - maybe this was a deliberate theme !! 
I didn't have breakfast as was on business and getting up early, but room service seems inline with other mainstream Hiltons.
For business - fine, for my money I'd spend the extra and go W.

title: “Another "Great" Stay”
text: We love New York City in December and have been there many times. This is our second stay at the Grand and we will be back. The location is perfect as it is in walking distance of Times Square, great shopping and theatres. We ride the subways for other areas of town and with absolutely no problems as you don't even have to go outside to get to Grand Central Station, just down a hall. The contemporary rooms are clean and very comfortable, they just need a full size mirror and it would be perfect. We had a small problem the first day and needed clean towels and they were there in 5 minutes. All the staff was very friendly and helpful.

title: “Very nice hotel”
text: This hotel was very nice. The decor is very good, the roof top bar is good at night pritty expensive but its new york city and your in a roof top bar so you dont expect it to be cheap. Very clean hotel, beds changed every day, the cleaner even folding up all my clothes i left out.. All the staff are very friendly. The bed is possible the best hotel bed i've slept in. Its in a very good location, metro stop 5 minutes walk away. If you Going to new york i'd stay here.

title: “Good hotel, bad area”
text:
I stayed at the Cova hotel with my boyfriend. I had read the reviews on here prior to our trip so was prepered for the dodgy area. The receptionist was very helpful as soon as we arrived and gave us a map outlining places to avoid so that is exactly what we did and we were fine. We walked to union square a couple of times during the day and once in the evening (avoiding walking straight through tenderloin district) but i would not advise this after dark .Nobody bothered us but it was quite intimidating with all the drunks and druggies although my boyfriend thought i was making a fuss about nothing!
We used the shuttle a couple of times which worked quite well. Once you get to union square, the public transport is so good that it's so easy to get around.
In general we found the Cova hotel very nice. Friendly staff, lovely breakfast and clean rooms. To be honest we were rarely in our room so the lack of facilities didn't really bother us. The only thing i would say is that the rooms are boiling. We roasted over night and although we were provided with a fan, our room was still like a sauna, and that is no over exageration!

title: “Inexpensive, convenient and friendly”
text: We have stayed here frequently on our visits to Austin. The rooms are generally OK and well-equipped. Twice, I have had issues with noise coming from an adjoining or overhead room, and when I took my concern to the front desk, the staff and management have been very accommodating in moving us to a quieter location. In fact, they have been downright friendly about it. Given the price, no one should be expecting luxury or a swanky location. But the location is convenient, the price is right, and the service is well above average.

title: “good value”
text: Next door was a major construction site, but regardless, the Hampton Inn Madison SG offers a good location, clean rooms and bathrooms and friendly service. Nothing exceptional, but equally nothing worth complaining about. Would gladly stay there again.

title: “Great hotel for business or alternative to the usual tourist hotels”
text:
My 4 night vacation stay at the Harbor Court Hotel was quite good. I booked using Hotwire and as expected I got a very average room with a view looking out to the hotels AC unit. Not a problem for me as I prefer white noise anyway.
All the advertised amenities were present, but some things were slightly odd. I knew the room was going to be small ahead of time. However there were 2 support beams (or pillars if you will) that made the wall jut out about 10 inches and was 12 inches wide. This made walking around the bed a toe-stubbing nuisance and the desk chair could not freely pull away from the desk. Tight manuevering to get seated. There was some paint chipping in the closet and doorway. On my second day there was a guy painting the hall outside my room. Luckily the fumes were faint. Also there was a bit of an electrical short in bathroom light switch. Had to flip switch a few times to get it to work properly. LCD TV was mounted above closet(!?), not centered in relation to the bed and/or desk chair. Lobby staff was just average. Any friendliness from them was not genuine.
Beyond those minor concerns, the hotel was very nice. This location is fantastic if you want to avoid the Union Square and Fishermans Wharf touristy areas. Some friends that are native San Franciscans commended my choice. Easy access to MUNI bus, rail, and cable car (California St.) as well as BART (Embarcadero station). I was not around enough to partake in the coffee, wine, and cookies very much. The lobby computer with printer is a nice touch for making maps and directions so you can explore SF. 
My bed was very comfortable! Good sized bathroom. Shower was more than adequate. Housekeeping did a nice job. Expensive minibar but there is a Walgreens and 7-11 a block away for food and supplies. Ice machines on 3 floors. Nice modern AC unit in the room which is kind of rare for boutique hotels in SF. I liked the decor very much.
When I return to the Bay Area I will definite shop for a good rate on the Harbor Court Hotel. I recommend it to anyone visiting on business or any tourist that prefers to stay away from busy the Union Sq. or Fishermans Wharf hotels and still enjoy a waterfront location will great transportation options.

title: “will stay here again!”
text:
my mum and i just returned from a 4 night trip to the big apple and were very happy with our experience at the tudor hotel. check in was very efficient and our room was modern, clean and although small, more than adequate for our stay. the lifts are excellent and very quick. breakfast is expensive - $16 each - we didn't eat there as a result and found the nations cafe at the corner of 1st and 49th street perfect for our needs and only a short walk away. the area around the hotel is nicely maintained and quiet and while it's 5 blocks of a walk to 5th avenue, we founf we encountered plenty of shops along the way to occupy our daily walk!!!!
i would definitely recommend the tudor hotel and will be returning again.

title: “Staybridge Suites - Not on times Square”
text: I enjoyed my stay at the Staybridge but felt a little bit cheated as its not actually on Times square but only 5 mins away. The complimentary breakfast did the job but was very basic. But then most hotels I looked at didn't offer it at all. It was great having a kitchenette within our room and the Fridge/Freezer was much appreciated as it had an ice maker. Rooms are nicely done as are the bathroom. They also arranged to get us back to the airport at a whopping $88

title: “Very nice except for the concierge”
text: I visited Seattle with two friends and stayed at the westin hearing good things about it. We enjoyed our stay the beds were extremely comfortable and most of the service was great. The only issue we had we the concierge, it seemed that most of the time they were unaware of the area they were able to tell us how to get to pikes but other than that they were pretty useless. Overall we definately enjoyed our stay and would stay again!

title: “Where to Begin...”
text:
I am not a picky person. But this place...oh, where to begin. 
We booked the place despite some negative reviews on this site. Heck, there are negative reviews about our favourite hotel on this site, so we take it all with a shaker of salt. A mistake on my part. 
First of all, the positives. The family restaurant, though most portions of the food served was inviting Coronary Artery Disease (however I find this a US phenomenon not limited to this restaurant), was open late, had good service, and reasonably priced. The Liquor store next door was fabulous, perfect for late-night munchies and of course, the liquor, which we needed substantial amounts to get us through our reservation period at this hotel. The pool - nice, clean, beautiful surroundings with giant rose bushes and floral gardens. 
The fun stuff ends there folks. The room was dank, dark, the lights worked at varying intervals that could only be attributed to the lunar cycle, the carpet was dirty. It started out as an "OK" on the cleanliness factor, and deteriorated to "Disgusting" on the day we checked out. The bathtub did not drain - AT ALL. We left a comment about this on the "housekeeping comment card" which then proceeded to sit in the exact same table location we had left it on the first day. Of course, travelling with my mom and step-father - who is a hairy guy, if I may be so blunt - the tub and bathroom was filled with disgusting hair by the end of our trip. I hated taking a shower and didn't touch ANYTHING while I was in there. Oh yes, the supersonic toilet. I suppose this is a California water-saving thing, but the toilet had a button on top that you had to push to flush, and you had to pound on it to elicit any effect at all. When you pounded hard enough, the toilet flushed with such ferocity that I started hanging on to loose jewellry/hair/clothing lest I be sucked into the vortex never to be heard from again. 
Service was adequate, but I felt sorry for the folks who worked there - it has to be damaging to the self-esteem to be forced to wear a neon hawaiian shirt to work every single day. 
They also advertise the Trolley stops outside the front door. If the front door is Old Town State Park, which is a two mile drive away, they are correct. 
Trust me, I am not a whiner. I have stayed in some grotty hotels. This is the second grottiest. The only reason the other hotel in my grotty category wins first prize is that it had bullet holes in the door and no towels. But you would expect that in Detroit :)

title: “Not as bad as I thought it would be”
text:
Yes the room was TINY. It was NOT big enough for more than 2 people. With that being said it was clean and modern. I did use Priceline and booked two rooms....one for my husband and I and one for our two kids. We were having our house painted and didn't want to take any chances with our asthmatic daughter.
Check in was VERY quick and easy. The staff was nice and attentive. There was a little bar in lobby that was nice and quaint. We watched a bit of the NBA finals there.
The lobby is very modern and sleek. It looked very trendy.
The room was the same as the lobby...dark and trendy looking. It was just God awful small but since we checked in then left for dinner and returned at bedtime it wasn't a problem.
All in all, downtown Chicago isn't a place where you'll sit in the room so it's OK that it's small. I'm more concerned with cleanliness and the room was clean. The location is across from a food pantry but since I live in Chicago (about a mile from Hotel FelixI can tell you that Catholic Charities soup kitchen isn't a place where "bad" people hang out. Hungry people line up, eat, and leave so don't be deterred by this fact. 
Chicago is a big city with a crime problem. If you don't go into high crime areas you'll be ok and downtown is safe for a city the size of Chicago.

title: “Worst Hotel Ever”
text:
Walked in at 11pm after long flight from South America for early meeting. After getting registered (more than 20 minutes - and in my time schedule this is eternity) they assigned me my first room. 
As soon as I walked into the elevator, first thing I noticed was a very Dirty & Stained carpet. Odd humidity smell mixed up with sewer water. 
Opened the door of the assigned room and the smell was even worse. Again went down to FD, to request a new room for which I had to wait at least 10 more minutes - and was told they had already given me their "best room for the night"
Next room did not smell as much, tired as I was I decided not to do anything else but rest. 
Fell asleep wondering how they fit this bed into the room, that being a Full Size bed, clattered up the whole room without almos any walking space. 
Central AC is fixed to a certain temperature which is not the confort level for anyone. Its only a $$ saver for the owners!
DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS HOTEL AT ALL. EXPENSIVE, SMELLY, TERRIBLE SERVICE!.

title: “No surprise”
text:
This Hilton has a very good central location. You can reach by foot the main points of interest of Boston.
For the rest, nothing particular to declare. The Hilton quality : professional staff, functional great rooms (one bedroom suite), ... Of course, no breakfast included. For free internet, you need to go in the lobby (it’s better than nothing). 
In few words : quite good value for money, no surprise.
Breakfast tip : at 0,6 mile, the North Street Grill (229 North Street).

title: “Trendy Hotel”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Hotel Palomar over Memorial Day weekend. We were planning on sightseeing during the day, and enjoying the restaurants and nightlife after. At first, I was a little hesistant because I had found other hotels that were closer to the museums and momuments. But we had heard good things about the Palomar from a friend, and the price was alot better than some of the other hotels, so we gave it a shot. 
We were so happy with this hotel! We found street parking easily, so we were glad we didnt have to shell out money for the valet parking...i think its $35 a night. The doormen and the reception staff were very friendly, and we got an automatic upgrade to a king size room. The room was very clean, spacious, although there is no view, even on the high floor. The bed is sooo comfortable, and there is a ipod dock as an alarm clock. The bathroom was a little small, and the was no flat screen TV, as was stated on their website.
The area around the hotel was also very good...alot of places to get something to eat. The hotel is close to the Metro, about 2 blocks, and the short cab ride from the momuments, georgetown, and the waterfront area of DC. There is a Starbucks, Subway and a CVS that is walking distance. The street around the hotel seems safe, just be smart, as you would in any metro city.
Overall, we had a great stay at the Hotel Palomar! We appreciated the friendly service from the reception staff and the doormen. We will definitely recommend this hotel to friends that will be visiting DC.

title: “A little spooky with good beds”
text: In the depth of Chinatown and its smells. Rooms are spacious but expect stained carpet and barren walls. Four women travelling together with no secondary mirror in room. Adequate bathroom with comfy beds. Bed linen appeared clean. Noticed no sprinkler system in room. OK if you spend absolutely no time in the room other than sleeping.

title: “I stayed here because of a meeting at the...”
text:
I stayed here because of a meeting at the hotel. I am not a fan of historic hotels for several reasons and the Menger is no exception.
1. The room smelled
2. The bathtub and shower looked like the run down tubs I've had in "OMG we have to pull off the road motels" with paintings of Elvis and velveteen bedspreads.
3. The air conditioning in the room did not function properly .
4. The walls were thin.
5. It was spendy.
6. The fitness center had 2 ellipticals, 1 treadmill and a bike and is not open 24 hrs. 
There were positives:
 It is a beautiful hotel with a beautiful courtyard.
It's right next to the Alamo and a shopping mall.
Free Internet in your room.

title: “Not too Bad !”
text: We were very concerned almost sick about coming here with all the poor reviews and we booked through Priceline therefore there was no looking back... We were also pleasantly surprised at what we found. The lobby is beautiful, Excellent location and tons to do in the area (ww walked everywhere or the T is at the door step). the rooms are very average, but clean... YOU WANT TO TRY AND GET A RENOVATED ROOM ~ I think this is the trick at this hotel based on the reviews I've been reading. Also, the price was right for what we got! Boston is a great city and I would reco this hotel for it's location, value and overal average quality....

title: “Quirky but cool”
text: I stayed at this hotel for one night while in DC for a business trip this week. The rooms are comfortable but quirky. Very high ceilings, funky decor and leopard print hotel robes. The room was quiet though and very comfortable. The staff was great as were the amenities. Cocktail hour at 5:00 pm and free coffee at 6:00 am. The fitness center was small but the equipment was fine. The location is great. Very near the Verizon Center and the International Sky Museum.

title: “Underwhelming”
text: This place trys to be a hip, unique boutique NYC hotel, but it's pretty rough around the edges...i.e. not that clean and a bit tattered. The decor reminded me of Ikea-cheap. The service was indifferent, not even a smile when you walk in the entrance. And don't expect anything beyond "no frills" ameneties. The room was what I called "The Cave". It was TINY and the only window was down this small hallway that served no purpose and faced another hotel room window in the back of the hotel which meant a depressing, dark and dreary room, not to mention the fear that your neighbor could be looking into the room if your shade was up. My husband arrived a few days before I did and had I been the first to arrive I would have asked for a different room considering he was staying for 9 nights, but he was tired and isn't as picky as I am. The bathroom was nice and clean but your arm hit the toliet paper dispenser everytime you sat on the loo because it was such a small bathroom. We had the A/C on HIGH the entire time just to keep the temp comfortable, even though it was not that hot outside. The location of the hotel is fine and pretty centrally located. But, for the same range price, you can find better places in New York.

title: “Did not enjoy”
text: I stayed on the top floor of this property (beneath the night club) and did not sleep due to the excessive noise above. As you walk into the property, I felt as if I was entering a nightclub and not a hotel. In addition, there is not much to do around the property. Will not be going back.

title: “Average Hampton Inn”
text:
The Hampton Inn brand continues to offer the same amenities across the USA. I did not see cookies at check-in, and rooms were large but very modest. The rooms did not have some of the amenities that I've come to expect: microwave, refrigerator etc... 
Very close to La Jolla for going out in the evening and very easy drive into downtown San Diego. 
It is very close to the Marriott, a very simple minute walkover from the Hampton. I was attending a conference at the Marriott but did not want to pay the price for the rooms. Hampton was much more affordable. So, if you are looking to save on the room fee this is a good alternative. 
Breakfast typical Hampton Inn and was fine. 
Rooms are clean. 
Free wi-fi
Views are not available really... highway on one side, other hotel on the other. 
Next to a Taco Bell and there is a Mexican restaurant w/in walking distance. 
If you have a car, there are many options for food about 2-10 miles away.

title: “Perfect place for a cheap comfortable stay”
text: The hotel was warm, very comfortable and in a good location. You did have to get the subway to go to the main shopping areas but it was nice anyhow where we were as there were lots of good restaurants and shops nearby and central park was really close too. We had a shared bathroom, but no-one else shared it so it was just ours, it was so clean and the maid came everyday with fresh towels and cleaned the room. We even got a TV with loads of channels free of charge which was great to watch after a busy day seeing the sights. I cannot say anything bad about this place, it was not luxury but was just right for the very affordable price. Try the French Roast for breakfast or Dinner which is about 6 blocks away, the oatmeal is amazing and the City Diner is awesome for their Salmon Steaks!

title: “Courtyard was excellent!”
text: My husband, teenage daughter and I stayed at the Courtyard Convention Center in DC and loved it. The beds were comfortable, the room was clean and the service was excellent. The location was unbeatable, next door to the International Spy Museum (which we recommend to all visitors) and the National Portrait Gallery (also a must see for art lovers). The hotel is also near many restaurants and the Metro (subway). The Gordon Biersch restaurant downstairs had good food and service (don't miss the garlic fries!), and although the bar was always crowded in the evening, we did not have to wait for a table for dinner. Chinatown and souvenir shops are within walking distance, as are many of the sites. We walked a block to the Old Town Historic Tours ticket office and caught the city tour, which was informative and affordable. We could not have beat the rate we got through AAA for anything comparable. I would definitely stay at at a Courtyard again.

title: “Good hotel, with a few negatives”
text: Typical Embassy Suites, in a good way. We really enjoyed our stay there, and would definitely stay again. The rooms and staff were nice, the hotel was nice with a big, beautiful koi pond in the lobby that the kids liked, the free internet in the business center was helpful, the breakfast was good with an excellent selection (hint: don't be late, they close it down right on time), and the location was great - 20 min or less to all major attractions, including the beach. Lots of restaurants and a nice mall close by with a playground for small children. The few negatives are: the sofa bed was awful - it was ridiculously uncomfortable. The mattress felt like springs with a sheet on top. Every spring was sticking out. They really need to replace them. I had a relative staying in another room, and her sofa bed was the same way, so it wasn't just our room. Also, other Embassy Suites I've stayed in had a nice kitchenette. This just had a very small area behind the door - the fridge didn't get very cold, and there was no freezer, which was disappointing. Still, it was nice to have the sink, fridge and microwave, however, small. The pool is nice for adults (even has a sauna) but definitely not a place for kids to play, so if your family expects to hang out in the pool, this is not the place. It's indoors, and is just a small rectangle pool with no shallow area for kids to play, not even large steps to hang out on. Also, the hotel rooms could really use a shelf or two in the bathroom. If you have more than one person, there's nowhere to put toiletries, etc. other than on the sink. If they just stuck a shelf on the wall, it would really help create more storage space. Lastly, they could really use a little noise buffer from the lobby, like more plants. All the rooms surround the lobby, and even though we were high up on the Honors floor, the noise still drifted up when there was happy hour or a band playing. We were prepared for the parking cost, we just considered it part of the overall cost of the hotel, however, it's very inconvenient - three stories with no elevator and only one lane in the garage - two cars can't pass eachother, one needs to back out for the other to get by. The front desk had conveniently printed directions to every surrounding location, which was very helpful. The hotel was comfortable overall and relatively quiet, with helpful staff and was in a good location, so we enjoyed ourselves very much, and would stay there again.

title: “New Hotel”
text:
This is a new hotel. Stayed on the 28th floor faceing the Empire State Building and Macys. Great view. New Hotel. Well kept. There are still some things to correct from construction but the staff is trying. The rooms are small but in NY thats OK.
Stall showers are great.
Breakfast not worth the $18. The rolls were frozen and not fresh. Made omlets were good. Wait staff are a waste. Tip the cook instead.

title: “Great hotel”
text: Warwick is my regular choice whenever I come to NYC. Even though it’s not as glamorous as the one in Paris (Champs d’Elysee), it has great location and very nice rooms. Warwick proved to be heaven last time I was there. For some reason, my travel agent was not able to find me a room. We tried everything booking on their website, expedia, booking, etc It was sold out. I ended up in a different hotel which proved to be a dump. I called Warwick and literally begged them to find me a room. Talked to the most efficient person on earth. In less than 5 minutes, she was able to find me a premier room and secure me an early check in (that was awesome because I still had to spend a nite in that dump). I might have paid a bit more but it was worth every single penny. Warwick is the best choice if you are looking for comfort, cleanness and feel like home time (cozy rooms, spotless bathrooms, sleek sheets and fluffy pillows).

title: “Okay, but not great”
text:
My recent stay at the Grand Hyatt in NYC left some things to be desired. Probably the biggest complaint is that the hotel's high speed internet access is wireless only and they have few working adapter kits - so I was unable to connect my laptop during my stay. I hope for better from a business-class hotel.
There were also a couple of issues with the room itself. The airconditioning was somewhat inadequate. Despite cranking the temp down fairly low, I was never really able to get the room properly cooled off. Also, the sink drain didn't work properly and the door stuck on closing so you always had to remember to close it behind you by hand. Somewhat minor quibbles perhaps, but for $350/night, I expect better.
The upshot is that if you have a conference in the hotel, the convenience probably makes it worth staying there, but otherwise I think there are better choices for your dollar in midtown.

title: “Very Helpful”
text: As evacuees from Houston during the Rita Hurricane, we were fortunately blessed with being given a room by the hotel since most hotels in the area were already booked. After being on the road for 10 hrs from Houston, we were exhausted and hot. There were 8 people in our group, and since we could not get the room for more than 2 nights or even another room since they were so full, they happily agreed to let all 8 of us stay in a double bed room. The room was surprisingly not too small, a little uncomfortable, since we did have 8 people, but overall very accomodating. The room was clean, the breakfast bar was good. I loved the waffle maker. High speed int was included and the staff was EXTREMELY helpful and attuned to our needs. I would definatley stay there again if I ever make a trip to the area, but hopefully not to avoid another hurricane!

title: “Excellent Boutique Hotel”
text: When my travel agent called this a "boutique hotel", I wasn't sure what she meant - but evidently that is code for small and elegant. The restaurant/bar downstairs is the place to see and be seen in DC. Many movers and shakers were in and out of the hotel on a daily basis. The hotel is quiet and clean and so awesome. The staff was amazing and very attentive, always remembering your name and what your plans were for the day and asking how things went upon your return. There were other fabulous restuarants within walking distance, or if you need a car or taxi, it will magically arrive.

title: “Good experience. Nice views.”
text: This was my first trip to Seattle. I loved the views from the room and the bed was SO comfortable, heavenly. There were a couple times we had to call for things like bad creamer needed to be replaced, room service was there in a flash. We had a suite and the rooms needed a bit of updating (furniture a bit worn and one of the light fixtures was broken), but overall good size, spectacular views and very clean. I would return to this hotel again.

title: “We liked it and will likely visit again....”
text:
The receptionist (Ms. Tabatha) was very professional/friendly. She greeted us and made us feel welcome.
Hamie, our waiter, was very attentive and a pleasure. He made my other half, feel like she was the only one in the restaurant. 
These two aspects were the highlight of our stay.
The internet was great! I was able to complete some homework for a course I'm taking...
The room was not that great. No vent in the bathroom...not to mention that it was small and cramp...

title: “Don't stay here...”
text:
Don't be fooled by the name - it does not share the typical quality of an Embassy Suites
The rooms are good size with decent furniture but they smell and the carpets are old. The management and front desk service personnel are incompetent and really don't care about their guests.
As others have stated - the location is questionable - as were some of the guests. One of the nights we stayed there - the police (3 uniformed officers) were outside a room on the 2nd floor - with a guy sitting down outside the door. Not sure what was going on - and too afraid to ask.

title: “Tuscan Inn at the Wharf”
text: Very quiet, comfortable hotel. We wanted to visit our favorite restaraunt at the wharf and visit an art exhibt. We found that both were within 2 blocks or so of the hotel. We did take a stroll further away, but caught one of the 2 person bike rides back to the hotel at a very fair price. Thanks.

title: “Beautiful Hotel, Great Location, Great Service, but no bar”
text:
We stayed in the Ritz Carlton for 5 nights for my son's wedding in Central Park. The staff were excellent and could not have done anymore for us. The room overlooking Central Park was fantastic and as someone else commented, the shower was fantastic. Extremely comfortable, clean and very spacious. I would recommend this hotel to anyone and we would definitely stay there next time we are in NYC.
On the downside, we booked the hotel through Virgin Holidays, who neglected to advise us that the bar and restaurant were undergoing refurbishment and were closed. Therefore, if you wanted a drink or breakfast outside your room, they were only available in the foyer lounge area, which whilst it was lovely for sitting and watching the world go by, was not the same as sitting in the bar after a long days sightseeing or having a quite breakfast. 
Don't get me wrong though, this was not the fault of the Ritz Carlton, but Virgin who should notify customers of renovations in the properties they offer.

title: “Nyma is a good hotel to stay in”
text: The Nyma hotel is central to all the Tourist sites, it i also wallking distance to all the fashion outlets including Macy's The rooms are very clean and well maintanined the service is good,. I would recommend Nyma Hotel to anyone planning a trip to NYC.

title: “Affordable, comfortable and a good location for downtown”
text:
We were looking for a place near the Phoenix Convention center that was not as expensive as the main hotels. It was nice and comfortable. Staff was very pleasant and helpful.
