Within walking distance to most major downtown areas plus only a couple blocks to the new transit system.

title: “Best in the area”
text:
I have to say, I've stayed more than 500+ hotels in the world because of my business.
Always, staff is the most important thing that made a hotel or a company different than others as far as I know. Porto Vista is not the best hotel in the world, but their staff is amazing. They're even better than my assistants in job :) 
They always take care about all my needs, all you need to do is, ask!
A big thanks from the vales to the manager. This hotel will be my best in San Diego always.

title: “Decent stay for the price”
text: My fiance and I stayed here in May 2010. The hotel was ok. Nothing spectacular but it was clean and decent. The bed could have been better as with the carpet. The bathroom was really big. I think if you are going to be on the go and need a place to stay, then this would be ok. The econo lodge would be better.

title: “Mediocre service”
text:
Nice Lobby, rooms and baths but very dissapointing service. Had to retrieve my car twice on the first day and it took 15 to 30 minutes MORE than the 1/2 hr notice that they request. I spent almost 2 hrs total standing in front of the hotel waiting for the lone garage guy to finally bring it out.
We stay in DC often and have found better service for less money in smaller hotels around Wasahington Circle.

title: “Okay, but better choices.”
text: My usual Chicago hotels were all sold out during a recent business trip, so I decided to give Amalfi a try. The location in River North is excellent, particularly if you're interested in nightlife. The staff was all business when I checked in - no mention of the free breakfast on every floor, I found out about that the next morning (nice surprise). Room size was good, generally clean and comfortable bed. I had a room in the back of the hotel which literally faced a wall, so the view was awful and there was little natural light. In fact, the whole hotel feels...dark and cavernous? Nothing wrong here, per se, but I think there are better options in the area, my favorite being the Dana Hotel .

title: “Not what it was”
text:
We have stayed at the Benjamin before but hadn't been there in the last two years. The Benjamin was always the hotel I recommended to others when they inquired about mid-town hotels. It was a wonderful alternative to the Waldorf and W.
The location can't be beat. At the right price point (under $450), the suites are still a better deal than a room across the street at the Waldorf. The closets are larger than some bathrooms in NYC hotels (the Hudson comes to mind). The hotel's smaller size makes the lobby area less frantic (see the check-out line at the Waldorf on any weekday morning). The small kitchen (microwave, regular sized fridge, sink, cutlery, dishes) is very handy, especially when traveling with small children. The full sized desk with a printer/fax and free internet service was much appreciated.
However, I have to say that I was very disappointed on this trip. The service was erratic. Some of the front staff were falling over themselves to be helpful and friendly but others were abrupt. New York is packed with tourists and so was the Benjamin, so perhaps they were all overwhelmed. The doormen, however, were outstanding (always a smile and greeting, hailed cabs from blocks away, etc.).
On arrival, one of our suites was not ready and although we were given a key card, the cleaning staff were still working in the suite. The previous guests had been granted a late check out due to problems with their outgoing flight. We had had to wait until after 5pm before we could enter. When we requested the same courtesy on our check out date, we were told that we should check our luggage. I was also not overly impressed with the concierge.
The rooms were in need of refurbishing. The carpets in both suites had issues, ranging from very frayed edges coming away from the walls to needing to be retightened (ridges were visible and somewhat of a hazard). The sofas were getting worn and one had buttons coming off. The cushions sagged. The TV's in one suite experienced intermittent static which made it unwatchable. The tile laminate in one bathroom was worn through in spots and the green waterproof wall board was visible.
Noise was a serious issue. The hotel had repeated false fire alarms, both at night and during the day. Having a busy fire station one block away was not conducive to restful nights. 
Will I continue to recommend the Benjamin? Probably.However, I'll also be suggesting alternatives.
BTW, I do not recommend the regular rooms, only the suites. The regular rooms are small and not a good deal given the price. Better can be found elsewhere.

title: “Comfort amidst Times Sq.”
text: We've stayed at this Renaissance hotel three times in the last three years. The staff has always been professional, friendly (for NY), and very responsive. Our room on one of the concierge floors was comfortable , well arranged and surprisingly roomy(again, for NY). The clientele was primarily traveling professionals. Bathtub, always a key element for the reviewer, just perfect. The concierge breakfast is among the best; minor complaint is that the table and chairs are weirdly matched and not very comfortable and the breakfast room was too cool all three mornings of our visit. We are quite likely to stay here again, even though we enjoy trying new places.

title: “Disappointing”
text:
Went to NYC for Birthday.
The hotel is in a great location....and the free muffins and coffee was much appreciated!
But apart from that, it was pretty poor.
I agree with other reviewers, the reception desk service was poor.
Our room was big, but cold, which in January is a problem! The bathroom was tiny, and impractical.
I went with a group of 5 and none of us liked it, and would never stay there again.

title: “Nice Place and Great Location”
text: We liked this hotel a lot. Good service. Nice decor. Very clean. The location is so good, 2 blocks from Empire State building. The beds are soooo comfortable! The only complain we have is the shower water pressure was low sometimes. Room is small, but i understand that's what you get in NYC.

title: “Great place to stay”
text: Our stay at this hotel was very comfortable. The staff was always polite and helpful and more than willing to help with any arrangements you may need. Our room was above average and the bed was fantastic. The whole hotel was very clean. If you stay during the week they offer a free limo service into the business district in the morning. We missed out on this opportunity because we slept in, but it was a nice bonus if you are up in time. We did manage to take advantage of the free internet in the business center to confirm our return flight. That was a nice addition to the stay. The location of the hotel is only two blocks to fisherman's wharf and not too far from north beach. My one and only complaint was that we had a very close view of the tree outside and that was about it. So I recommend that you ask for a room on the fourth or fifth level. Other than that one complaint our stay was smooth and uneventfull, just how we like it:).

title: “Perfectly Acceptable Hotel”
text:
Due to the negative comments I had read I was more than a little nervous about our stay.
This is just an example of why User ratings on Internet sites need to be taken with a grain (or tablespoon) of salt.
It is probably more of a 2.5 Star than a 3 Star Hotel but for a price of under $150 for a King in central San Francisco it is hard to beat.
As for our overall experience rating I would lean towards giving it a 3.5 dot rating not a 4 dot rating.
ROOM:
The room we stayed in was probably the largest room we have had in San Francisco. It wasn't huge or anything but probably bigger than our rooms at Harbor Court or the Juliana.
Besides this is San Francisco who plans on staying in the room for very long?
The room was clean although the wall paper was a little old. The bathroom is a bit small and Spartan but still clean and functional.
It is an old building and there is a slight musty smell. It's just old building smell really. Hardly noticed it after awhile.
The biggest disappointment was the hot water in the shower in the morning. There wasn't a lot.
LOCATION:
The location is great. Easy walking distance through Chinatown to Washington Square and Fisherman's Wharf. Short walk to the Powell Street Muni Station just past Union Square.
STAFF:
The Hotel staff was very friendly and efficient. Extra towels were provided promptly. I must have mentioned, at some point in the booking process, that this was an anniversary trip. When we got to the room there was a complimentary bottle of wine and a card. 
I am fairly familiar with the city and had ideas on what to see and where to eat. What few city questions I posed to the concierge were answered very informatively.
NOISE:
Very EARLY on Monday Morning I remembered the garbage collection on Bush Street. It is loud and seems to start VERY early in the morning. You can't blame the hotel for this and I have had the same problem in other nearby hotels.
DINING:
We didn't eat at Masas but it looks wonderful and also amazingly expensive. 
EXTRAS:
The complimentary newspaper was the Chronicle and not USA Today -- a definite plus. The wine at the tasting was fine and easy to quaff. The breakfast seemed sparse but we were on our way to Mamas on Washington Square anyway.
PARKING: 
San Francisco is such a great town for walking we never get a car. Walking on Lombard in the Marina district, towards the Presidio, we noticed a lot of Motels....
WHAT IT IS NOT:
If I was in town on business I would probably choose a different Hotel. We were on vacation and didn't bring our laptops so I cannot speak about the wireless connection. It did not have a business center nor an exercise room. The computer in the lobby was 15 cents a minute so it could get costly. It was fine for on-line airline check-in.
Also it is not a hotel to plan on spending a lot of time in the room. There is no room service and the desk is small.
WHAT IT IS:
A perfectly acceptable and affordable hotel for a nice weekend vacation in San Francisco.

title: “Excellent stop room brand new”
text:
I got this near the airport and it was so close to my thrifty rental car as well. THe room was huge with 2 heater control units - full kitchen with a dishwasher and large bathroom. I got this on priceline and they gave me the handicap room. It looked brand new. Im not sure if the whole place is this new but the hallways looked it. There was even a continental breakfast with great coffee and a bagel. They told me they had shuttle service to the airport every half hour. THe location was less than one mile from the airport. With the esa it says the desk hours close at 10 am. I got in at 12 :15 am and luckily there was someone there. Not sure why. Also no shampoo in these esa places so bring your own and the vender machine only takes quarters- no dollars.
Fantastic place would rate it a 3 star.

title: “Great Idea, Somebody”
text: A movie theater in the hotel lobby--it sounds like a gimmick. But you know what? It works! My guests and I enjoyed a day of sightseeing, including Alcatraz, and when we got to the hotel in the evening, one of the movies was "Birdman of Alcatraz." It was the perfect ending to a great day. The theater is just one of the nice touches at Bijou. Some of the others are good towels, very nice soaps and shampoos, and a good value for lodging in the city. After checkin I noticed a gym-socks smell in the elevator, but one of the staff neutralized it with freshener before I even had a chance to mention it to them--good job! Otherwise the place was very clean. Breakfast is tasty but minimal--bagels and muffins. We did not experience noise problems mentioned in other reviews. Noise level is normal for the city, and less than at other hotels. Occassional sound of elevator, which I first thought was a distant vacuum cleaner, but it too was minimal, and we were right next to the shaft. Housekeeping kept knocking in the morning, but it wasn't their fault. Someone (another guest?) kept turning our "do not disturb" card around. Housekeepers were friendly and helpful. I am a member of the hotel company's "Joy of Life" club, and was supposed to get extra goodies in the rooms, which we received in one room, but not in the other. Desk staff didn't know what to do about that. Otherwise, desk staff was very friendly and very helpful--their dining suggestion helped us find a reasonable and uncrowded diner for lunch. Yes, the neighborhood had some homeless, but they weren't threatening, and didn't even approach us; they were actually more agressive at Fisherman's Wharf. I would enjoy staying at Bijou again, except that I want to try other hotels in the Joie de Vivre group.

title: “New, modern, and well managed hotel.”
text:
I stayed here on a priority club reward night a few days before Thanksgiving. Great place, very new and modern. I have started using IHG's Crown Plaza brand over their Holiday Inn brand whenever possible and have been much happier. I'm becoming more and more disappointed with Holiday Inn hotels each passing year as they seem to be slowly but surely slipping into the budget bracket.
 Not so with this property, you see the fresh upscale quality of this facility the second you enter the bright and elegant lobby area, and it just continues on from there. The check in process is smooth and painless and the desk staff is friendly, efficiant, and well trained.
The rooms are well appointed and very comfortable with fast internet and top rate ammenities. I used the resteraunt and bar for dinner and evening cocktails and was very satisfied with both. I literally wanted for nothing at this hotel, this is a proven sure bet. You can't go wrong here...

title: “An exceptional experience from check-in to check-out”
text: The service, environment and restaurant/room-service food was exceptional. From check-in to check-out, I was treated like a VIP and found the experience to be exceptional. Although I was traveling on business, I would certainly return with my family and recommend this establishment to others.

title: “You get what you pay for.. rude front desk staff included!”
text:
Let me first say I am writing this review as I am being harassed by a prank caller- that itself just cost them a star.
Anyway, we made this reservation on travelocity in front of the hotel staff because the price they were offering was a $20 dollar difference and if we wanted to pay that much we could have gone across the street to the comfort inn (which we probably should have). We tried to check in early since we were all tired and on the road with an infant but they said we would have to wait til 4pm to check in and because it was 90 degrees outside and only 9am we asked if we could atleast have someone sit in the air conditioned lobby with the baby and the woman with the bad attitude and 80s hairstyle said "we can't have you sitting here all day" .. this place is cheap and you get what you pay for.. rude front desk staff included!

title: “Would definitely stay here again -- priceline made it a great bargain”
text: Hotel dates to the 1930s and has a lot of history (political events including Clinton's Inaug. Ball, movies filmed there, etc.) -- very large hotel with large lobby. You can tell the by the rooms that it's an older hotel in that our king room was very large, bathroom somewhat small, but had a huge walk-in closet and a large flat screen tv. We were there during 4th of July weekend, used price line and got this regularly $249 a night room for $105 a night and the front desk didn't treat us any differently as we have experienced in other places where we have used priceline -- very friendly, gave us a nice view on a higher floor, etc. Elevators are small for such a large hotel, but they come quickly. The neighborhood is GREAT -- walking distance to the Zoo, 1 block from the Metro station and LOTS of very nice little restaurants within 1-2 blocks -- very safe feeling area too. For those that don't like chinese or Thai food, there is also a McDonalds and Chipotle Grill. Great breakfast restaurants nearby as well -- never had a bad meal anywhere.

title: “Good experience on business trip”
text: I stayed a week at this hotel during first week of May 2012 business trip. I knew nothing about it before this trip, except what I read on TripAdvisor (which turned out to be right on target, as usual). Chose this hotel based primarily on location, but also price and availability - a convention was in town and taking up most reasonably-priced and decently-located hotels. I was not disappointed. The staff was terrific - greeted me by name every time I came and went; always ready to help me get around the city to the many different locations on my agenda. Comfortable bed; cean and quiet room. Great experience overall.

title: “Great hotel....slow elevators!”
text: This hotel was incredible. My husband and I stayed for 3 nights in a 1 bedroom suite. They room was very spacious and had 2 tvs! 2 downsides to the hotel is the SLOW elevators....not a surprise as it is an older hotel and the curtains in the bedroom. I like the curtains that blackout the light and they only had sheers.

title: “WHERE ELSE DOES A CONCIERGE CALL YOU BEFORE YOU ARRIVE?”
text:
I guess that was my first tip-off that the Omni in Chicago was not going to be an ordinary hotel experience.
It lived up to its reputation from the moment that I was greeted by the doorman upon my arrival till my departure 3 days later. Make sure you sign up for their Loyalty Program to get immediate upgrades like Clothes Pressing, Morning Coffee/Juice Service and free WIFI. 
I will now always ask if there is an Omni where ever I'm staying

title: “Wonderful historic hotel”
text: If you are going to DC over the weekend when hotel prices are very low, you must stay here. It is a great experience at a bargain price. The decor is gorgeous, the rooms are very spacious and the service is friendly and attentive. Central location so you can walk to all the museums and the metro.

title: “Decent location”
text: This property is located right off I-465 on the east side of Indy. Rooms are decent and clean but could use some updating. Be aware, too, that there are not a lot of restaurant choices in the area. But, for a good stay while on business on the east side, this property will suit your needs.

title: “cheap in all senses”
text: Location - 3 blocks from union square. Thats what you pay for. Room is ok if you dont mind the mice and the homeless people arguing outside. Service however is beyond bad. Indian guy at front desk is rude and uninterested in the guests. No aplogy för the mice, simply an "ok". We changed rooms because of the furry little friends, only to find his family in the next room. Pay extra and stay somewhere else. B & L, Sweden

title: “Ideal location for all attractions”
text:
We stayed for 5 days Nov '05 and found ourselves within 5-10 minutes walk of Times Square, from which there are many transport links to any part of the city. We walked from the hotel to Lower manhattan in around an hour (the best way to take in more of the city). 
The rooms are pretty basic, but all have cable TV and internet access and are clean and tidy. Anyone with a criticism of the hotel is spending too much time in their room and needs to get out and see the city!
The hotel doesn,t have a restaraunt but being on 42nd street there are deli's, restaraunts, bars and everything else you could need within 5 minutes walk.
Oh yes, its got an outdoor pool but not for me in November thankyou!

title: “Sleep Inn has no SLEEP”
text:
On our second night of our stay, this is what happened: 
At around 12:00am, people outside started partying. We called the front desk. They said they would take care of it. 15 minutes later, they still hadn't shut up. We called the front desk again, and they said once again they would take care of it. Yet a few minutes later, we had to send someone down to the front desk. They said that he had let a bunch of ladies stay in the neighboring room. They shut up this time and we were awoken AGAIN at around 2:00am because they had started again. We called for the third time and they said they would call the police, which they didn't do until fifteen minutes later, when we called for the FOURTH time. When the police still didn't show up, one of us went down again, they just sat there until they did something. They finally shut up and checked out next night. We considered checking out a day early.
The help desk there is the most unhelpful help desk ever. What's the point of a help desk when they don't help you?

title: “Okay, but still better than others”
text:
I booked this hotel for the night before my interview at UCLA. It's convenient to the UCLA Medical Center (just up the hill). I did not have a car, but from seeing the parking situation, only bring a compact car if you want to park.
I was "upgraded" to a suite. The kitchenette had a fridge but no dishes or utensils. The living area had a TV and couch. The internet access is not wireless, but they provided a cord if you did not bring one.
The bed was comfortable and clean (please see my other reviews for much worse places than this). The bathroom was clean. There was also a TV in the bedroom.
The front desk staff was helpful, especially when looking for local areas to eat within a walking distance. Check-in and check-out was quick.
The included continental breakfast was basic, but decent.
I would stay here again for business or the budget minded traveler.

title: “Fabulous river view convenient to Georgetown, Foggy Bottom, GWU”
text:
I was delighted when I walked into the room and looked out at the view: the sun setting over the Potomac River, with Georgetown and Rosslyn in silhouette. (Rosslyn's not that pretty by day.) The location is really good, five-to-ten minutes walk to the Foggy Bottom/GWU Metro station, GWU Hospital; Georgetown shopping about 15 minutes in the other direction.
Really good price for this location and for the amenities. The one bedroom suite with kitchenette (stove top, microwave, sink, full sized refrigerator) is plenty of room for a couple, or maybe a couple with a child (or two) small enough to sleep on the sofas. The desk staff was pleasant, but a bit passive--their first response to a problem was to suggest how I might fix it myself, when prompted they'd agree to help. 
The building is dated, though, and the bathroom is tiny. With washroom through-put of only one person at a time, a family would have to stagger washing up. Don't rely on the restaurant being open for meals. During my stay they were frequently tied up for private parties, and they don't post in advance when they do that.

title: “Good for Business Travel”
text:
I stayed here for business travel. The hotel is easy to find and near the office I used to work in. The staff were very courteous and the warm cookie when you check in is a nice touch. 
I booked through my company and not sure if that contributed to my being upgraded but I ended up with a king sized bed suite. 
The room was very nice and clean with plenty of room to walk around even with the large bed. There was a desk to work and closet space. Also a chair to watch TV. The TV was a nice flat screen hung on the wall which didn't distract too much. Also had a small pod machine to make either coffee or tea. The bathroom was modern and well stocked. 
I ate in the restaurant one evening and it was passable. Not the best meal I've had in NY but it was good for when I didn't feel like going outside the hotel to eat after a long day. 
My only complaint is that you have to get up EARLY to make sure you get water for a hot shower. The first night I slept until 7am and even after running the water for 20min it was still ice cold so I had to suck it up. This hotel seems popular with the business travel crowd so I guess mornings during the week tax the hot water supply. 
Overall, I would stay here again the next time I have overnights in NYC.

title: “not worth the price”
text:
Booked a room at the Warwick Hotel in Denver for NYE 07. Checkin was fine. When we got to the room, it overlooked the parking lot and Cap Hill. Called down to the desk and were told since the hotel was full, we could not move to a west facing room. My daughter wanted to go swimming and as she was going out the door, she noticed some hair on the floor---not ours,but human or dog. I called housekeeping and showed the staff the hair on the floor. She vacuumed where the hair was and then said is there anything else i can do? I requested that the whole room be vacuumed and it was done. No apology was offered by housekeeping. Since it was NYE, we ate at Randolph's, the hotel restaurant for the prix fixe menu. It was wonderful with fantastic service both for the dinner and for room service breakfast the following morning. After we ate dinner, my daughter wanted to go back to the rooftop pool. Although there were signs and also special rules for NYE, the pool should have been open until 10PM. When we got to the pool door, it was locked with a chain. When I called down to the front desk, they said that they had decided to close at 8PM--I guess so people would not be tempted to see the city fireworks from the roof. The front desk did apologize and also apologized for the hair on the floor. No comps were offered however--not even a glass of champagne. Halls were very noisy which was understandable. 
Dogs were numerous but not really obnoxious. The rooms are big with two chairs. The minibar was adequate. No soda machines--have to buy from minibar. The shower did not have a lot of pressure and the furniture was a little beat up. Certainly not antiques--just old furniture. the bed was hard but adequate. All in all, it was an okay hotel. definitely, not worth the price of the lodging.

title: “Fun & funky but service could be improved”
text:
While the decor in the Helix was fun & funky, the service leaved a little to be desired. My 2 teenagers and I stayed there on a quick trip to DC. The teenagers loved the decor, not to mention the leopard and zebra robes. 
 The metro stop is a little bit of a walk, but we felt completely safe even walking back at night. 
 There was no way to turn up/down the A/C and the 2nd day the maid forgot to leave one of the original leopard blankets/throws on the bed. It took 2 calls to the front desk to get another blanket. 
 The bathroom is tiny for 3 people to share. I thought the beds were extremely comfortable but I could have been too tired to care.
 I had also rented a car, not knowing really whether to or not since we were coming in from Baltimore, and the only option they offered for parking was the $27/day valet. We didn't use the car at all and when we left, I literally got my own car out of the space where they had parked it right in front of the hotel.
 I'm glad we stayed there because the kids really liked it, but I don't know that I'd stay there again.

title: “Loved the J.W. Marriott Desert Ridge”
text: We were there during the first week of August for four nights. When we got there it was 3:30 and we were able to check in. They gave us a room in the fourth floor (where the complimentary washer and driers(2) are) with a great view into the patio and the pools. It was great. The hotel has activities schedule daily some are free others at a cost. The concierge desk was a great help. They have suggestions on places to visit and most important direct directions. What they say in the other reviews is true. This is certainly another type of heat. We were able to go to different places(Old Town Scottsdale, Slide Rock, Sedona, Heard Museum) because it really doesn't feel that bad. Well the hotel is spectacular. They told us that the hotel wasn't that busy that week but we still saw that the lazy river was pretty full. The pools are really nice and we were able to find chairs and there were plenty of towels available. The lazy river has a slide and plenty of adults were enjoying it. The kids menu is a steal for $4 you really get a huge serving. Most of our dining was away from the hotel since we did visit other sites away from the hotel during the early mornings. We would come back to the hotel around 3:00 and would hit the pools till after dark. Pools close around 11:00 p.m. Something that was not mentioned in this site is that during the summer months it's monsoon season in AZ. This means that late in the evenings lightning could strike and then it could rain which means you can't be in the outdoor patios enjoying the music being played or in the water. For one of the nights we were there we had one of these storms. We went to our room to change out of our swimming attire and just when we were on our way downstairs the entire hotel lost power for about a half hour but the power did restore pretty quick. The weather changed rather quickly. It's true that across from the hotel is a mall with restaurants and even an arcade called Jillians. We really enjoyed our stay there. The lazy river was super fun for the kids and the pools are all very nice and not that deep at most four feet. All in all I recommend this hotel... we definetely plan to go back soon!

title: “BED BUGS!”
text:
Traveling on business for several weeks to Charlotte. Stayed in this hotel on Monday night and didn't notice anything. Last night (Tuesday), I was in bed, flipped my pillow over and saw bed bugs crawling everywhere! So, in the middle of the night I packed up my belongings and went down to the lobby. The hotel staff didn't seem concerned or even apologetic. They gave me another room and sent me on my way. When I asked what was normal Marriott protocol for such events, they said they'd talk with management. Still haven't heard a response back and I'm stuck at this hotel for the rest of the week for business. 
Disappointed by Marriott's lack of professionalism. In the very least, they should offer to have all of my garments and luggage professionally cleaned. This is disgusting.

title: “Disappointing...”
text:
ALL of the towels provided were paper thin and an off white, like what you'd get at an old gym to use. The bed sheets were thin as well, like an undershirt 15 years old or that they've been on the bed for a few days prior to our arrival. Halfway through our stay, I mentioned this to the staff but still received the same level of quality with the towels (the sheets were slightly better). If it were one or the other, I may not have even written this review, but the fact that it was both and they're the 2 personal items a hotel can provide that, in my opinion, can really make or break a stay so I had to write this!
I'd give it a really bad rating, but the other things that make Residence Inn the experience I've learned to enjoy were spot on: Nice breakfast with good variety throughout our week long stay, wonderful and cheerful staff, clean and modern amenities, and of course free parking and WiFi.

title: “wonderful hotel”
text: I stayed here for 5 days in december 2010 with my wife and 4 year old son. Its a small hotel tucked away in a corner on the side street leading away from union square which is steps away. We were booked in to a smaller room.Ann at the front desk asked us if we would want to upgrade for a slightly higher price- though reluctant at first we happily agreed when we saw the room.The room itself was cosy and warm though it overlooked a brick wall. the bed was comfortable and internet worked well.The staff are very helpful. in the evenings there are cookies, nuts and wine in the same area where breakfast is set up. The area is a little small for more than 2-3 people at a time, but the whole experience was very nice. We enjoyed our time in the city though it was very cold and rainy all the time. Ann and Omar at the front desk deserve mention and are very helpful with requests and information regarding the city or bus routes etc. The hotel is just a few steps from all the action in Union square but still retains a serene mood. Though a little small in areas but we thoroughly enjoyed our stay.

title: “Worth staying at”
text: We thought this hotel was beautiful, really unique to turn an old jail into a high end luxury hotel. We were there before check in and our room wasn't ready, so they took our bag and gave us a bag tag so that we could go out sight seeing without it. We parked at the hotel and the total for the stay (one day-24hrs) was $42. When we checked in late afternoon, we were offered complimentary champagne, which we took up to our room to enjoy. Someone brought our bag up within minutes. We stayed in the old part of the building, facing Charles St. The room was beautiful, spacious, and clean. I had asked for the down to be removed prior (husband is allergic to feathers) and when we got to our room, that had all been done. The only negative was that there is an outside bar that was hopping until 2 am, right below our window. UGH. There is also a central bar in the lobby area, which is also very popular til late. Not as noisy as the outside one, but could be problematic for light sleepers. We ended up going to bed around 12:30, so we didn't have the energy to switch rooms at that time. If you're going to be out late, then the room was cool and worth it, but if you want to go to bed early, you might want a room in the new part of the hotel. The beds were comfy- not to hard, not to soft. The concierge was really helpful in recommending a restaurant within walking distance and a quick breakfast place for the next morning- both were great. All in all- will go back for sure (and stay in quieter room).

title: “Great place to stay, excellent staff.”
text:
Found this Hampton Inn on-line. Typical of the Hampton Inn family room was functional, neat and clean. Took in a great play thanks to therecommendation and help of the on-site Concierge. Front desk staff were very polite and extremely helpful with every request we had. Walked to the attractions we had selected and even found a tour to WTC Memorial and Statue of Liberty starting within blocks of the Hampton Inn.
Love the great fre breakfast which is more extensive than other Hamptons I've stayed at. Will definitely stay there on my next New York City trip.

title: “Pleasantly Surprised”
text: This was a fantastic hotel centrally located to some great sites. Just a few blocks from Times Square, Rockefeller Center, 5th Ave., Central Park and about 100 yards from a subway stop. The staff were very friendly and helpful. The room was actually quite a bit larger than I expected. It had hardwood in the hall and the bathroom was done in wall to wall granite tile. The linens were extremely clean and the bed was very comfortable. Another very nice touch was the free wireless internet access we enjoyed. We were able to use our laptop to fine tune our vacation as we went along. Really only two minor complaints....the lighting in the bathroom was a bit dim and the two elevators were slow and small. Overall, those two minor inconveniences were nothing compared to the positives of our stay. Will definitely go back to the Blakley again.

title: “I loved this hotel”
text: I would tell anyone to stay here. It is so nice and so quite for a New York hotel. The staff is great. The food is great. We loved our stay here. This type of hotel should be the standard not the exception.

title: “Dated, but service makes up for it...”
text: Spent 11 nights at this location and it was not bad. The facility is a bit dated but the service and attention received by all staff members mitigated the aged facility. The large clunky old TV’s were changed out for flat screens during my stay so that was a step in the right direction. One weird thing was the indoor pool… really in El Paso, TX it’s sunny over 360 days out of the year. The front desk staff did coordinate with the Courtyard down the road to use their outdoor pool, so all was well on the sunbathing front. The nightly light dinner and early morning breakfast was much appreciated and very tasty. Make sure you ask for a room in the rear as the constant din of I-10 is very annoying. Ample, secure, free parking is a plus as well. All in all for the price paid it is one heck of a deal.

title: “Nice business stay”
text: Nice business stay. I stayed in room 403 which was handicap accesible, which I did not need. My complaint with this was that the light in the restroom automatically turned on a fan and it was VERY loud. Also seemed like I could hear WAT TOO MUCH of what was going on next door :) The breakfast buffet at TGI Fridays was awesome! And the fitness center was fine.

title: “Over priced, not worth it”
text: I stayed at the Inn at Penn for three weeks whilst doing some work in Philadelphia. The location was excellent as it was close to the university and HUPs. I was surprised at the lack of service I experienced from the reception staff. I had prerequested for my room to be on the top floor, when i mentioned this , the reception staff just told me my room was on a high floor and they would not be changing this. There was free wireless internet in the foyer and library but it was very expensive to pay per night to have it available in the room. The gym was a reasonable size and as i was staying for so long, i had complimentary breakfast included. The buffet was fine, however, when occupancy decreased, they stoopped providing hot food for the breakfast. In general the staff that served at the breakfast room were lovely and friendly. The rooms were average, and a bit noisy as overlooking a main street. Compared to a much cheaper hotel I had just stayed in, I would say that this is a very over priced hotel, that lacked the good service (apart from the staff at breakfast) and I am sure there are other cheaper hotels nearby that would be much better

title: “Super Clean!!”
text: I do agree that the decorations are a bit bla. However, the location and cleanliness of the hotel more than make up for what it is lacking in interior design. The bed is also extremely comfortable and the L'Occitane amenities are a magnificent touch. I have been known as a very picky traveler and I would recommend the Commonwealth to anyone. This hotel is spotless!!

title: “In Desperate Need of an Updating”
text:
First the Good: 
 The staff was excellent. Everyone was pleasant and accommodating. The hotel was clean in the sense of day-to-day cleaning.
The Mediocre:
 The breakfast was not bad, not excellent, just middle of the road for an ES. The evening reception was not as good. Besides the drinks, just pretzels or tortilla chips and dip and/or salsa.
The Bad:
 The rooms, including the furniture, are very tired and need to be renewed. I saw two rooms and both had the smell of 'old carpet' no amount of cleaning can get that out. The furniture and carpet had very old stains. The cushioning/stuffing on the furniture is shot- I could feel the wooden frame by just softly pressing on the upholstery. The wooden chairs at the table wobbled so much I expected to crash to the floor. The color scheme- coral and dark green- went out of style 10 years ago. 
The pool area was very nice and clean but the chemicals were too strong- the following morning our eyes were still bloodshot. This might have been an anomaly and hopefully it's no like that all the time. 
I have been a loyal Hilton Diamond member for over 10 years, but unfortunately I have to say there are better options in the Jacksonville area than this hotel, although a good remodeling might change my mind.

title: “$11 for self park”
text: dated wierd hotel with rude staff far from eveything except the airport

title: “Good Value, Lousy Neighborhood”
text:
We recently returned from 4 nights at the Hampton Inn-Crosstown. There is no question that you get great value at this hotel compared to the much higher rates at most other moderate hotels in Boston. The usual complementary hot breakfast that Hampton Inn offers was great, the suite was roomy for our family of five, and the pool offered welcome relief from the heat and humidity. 
The hotel's shuttle is a great idea in theory but while we were there they only had one mini-bus running and it only held 13 people. We noticed many guests complaining that they had to wait a long time and many gave up and took the bus or called cabs. We took it downtown one morning after having to wait an hour and then we took a cab back to the hotel at night rather than fight the crowds.
By far our biggest concern was the neighborhood of the hotel. Numerous panhandlers surrounded the front of the hotel and in one direction was a very run-down part of the city. We did not feel safe at all and there was no restaurant within walking distance of the hotel. We, along with many other guests, had to take a cab just to get to a restaurant. There is also a hospital right next to the hotel so you hear sirens and a hospital helicopter off and on all night. Finally, our linen was not clean upon check-in and our toilet malfunctioned a few times.
My family will not stay in this hotel again and I do not recommend it to others for now. Perhaps in the future the neighborhood will be built up to be more tourist-friendly.

title: “Great Location”
text: Great Location and Great Hotel.... The staff was perfect and the location could not have been better.. The rooms were a little warm, the temp controls did not work that well... ( Opened the window and we were fine) Otherwise, perfect.......

title: “A BEYOND BELIEF DIVE!”
text:
My daughter and I went to NY in July/04. We initially booked 6 nights in another hotel, but when we decided to add a 7th night the hotel we were staying at was booked, so the 7th was at the Pennsylvania. We paid $155.00 Cdn for the 1 night that I booked online at one of the discount websites. I am not complaining about the cost if it was half decent....The 1st room was dingy, but we were willing to tolerate it for 1 night. We were tired from a long day and we just wanted to relax & watch TV but it turned out the TV was obviously broken- there was a 6"X2" hole in the front of the TV where the remote sensor electronics were suppose to be. How could housekeeping miss that???? I called the front desk about it, waited at least 1/2 hour, nothing happened so I went down to the front desk & asked for a 2nd room. We got up to the 2nd room (dragging our luggage everytime, I was not paying a bell boy for all that travelling in this dump) and the key would not work. I called downstairs and we had to wait at least another 20 minutes for someone to bring another coded key for the room. The room stunk of dampness and mildew and the all carpet in the area outside of the bathroom door was wet, so I guess it was a good thing the one window in the room was jammed open approx 6-8 inches to air it out. I stood on a chair to use my body weight to close it- it would not budge. The fact that we were on the 13th floor was some comfort, but not much. It certainly was not energy efficient because it was very hot that night and we had the A/C on full blast to help with the smell and the humidity. Then there was the bathroom-not a single towel, face cloth or anything in there. Again I ask-what did housekeeping do in there? I had to call down to housekeeping 2x, in 1/2 hour intervals for towels- we got 2 bath towels & 2 facecloths...no bath mat, which explains why the carpet was so wet. Then the next morning it cost $12. to hold our luggage for 2 hours so we could do more sightseeing before our flight. (The other hotel did not charge for this service) Even the hallways leading up to the rooms were ugly. The doors to the room looked like 100 yr old deteriorated wooden bank vault doors. 
Fortunately the 1st 6 days of our trip was great, I would recommend NYC to anyone. We loved it there, we took in all the sights, shopped, walked, took the subway, taxies etc. The people there were very friendly and helpful. We hope to go back next year but I will never be back at this hotel again!

title: “Cynical in the extreme”
text:
Two issues that tell you all you need to know about this hotel
1. Daily internet access 16.95
2. Mini bar empty - small bottle of mineral water 12.95. Told room service I would complain. "Do what you need to do".
Possibly one of the worst hotels I have ever stayed in.

title: “Lovely, Well Appointed Suites & Service”
text: As a Johns Hopkins patient my husband and i have stayed at the Tremont Plaza many times. The suites are comfortably appointed with airy rooms and a well set up kitchen area. Having a special rate for Johns Hopkins patients, as well as shuttle service to the hospital was a big plus: we could leave our car at the hotel. The restaurant food was very good, and many times we were with casts of televisin and movie crews and celebrities. A surprise little extra. The staff was very good about making certain that I was kept comfortable, (I was per-surgical) and accommodated us in an efficient and gracious manner. The hotel is very centrally located and the staff always had lovely recommendations as to what we could do to enjoy ourselves. You really can't ask for much more than that.

title: “Good Location; Good Value”
text:
I like to stay at Best Western's because of the variety of lodgings available and their overall good quality and value.
Good location across from the San Diego Harbor; just west of the airport in the Point Loma neighborhood; an easy 10 minute drive to airport rental cars and 15 minutes to downtown. A variety of restaurants nearby with Denny's and fast food drive-thrus on Rosecrans St. and more upscale mid-price places on Harbor Island.
Had reserved a room with king size bed but was assigned a room for the disabled with a double on the 4th floor; went back downstairs for a new room and got what we wanted on the 7th floor. Desk clerk on duty at the time (mid afternoon) was professional but not cordial.
Room was very comfortable; all rooms have a large balcony but no outdoor furniture for one to enjoy being out on it. Free unsecured wifi but the download speed is verrrry slow.
Very Quiet at night, but in the morning you can hear the rumble of moderate traffic on the old concrete pavement of Harbor Drive; There was also construction going on next door that started at 7 AM but that is probably completed by now.

title: “Great relaxation!”
text: We just spent 4 nights at the Hayes Mansion and have once again been spoiled! This was our third year of March get together with friends from NoCal and Central Cal. Service is 1st class, grounds are beautiful, restaurant is great and the Spa facilities are included. Our room included a full breakfast buffet including omelette station. Spa facilities include locker, robe, steam room, exercise facility, indoor spa and out door spa and pool. We will be back next year.

title: “Green is great but stains, dirty linens, peeling wallpaper and general dirty feeling is not.”
text: Grounds are beautiful and the breakfast/happy hour are nice, but I can't get past unsealed grout and peeling wallpaper in the bathroom and finding someone else's hair in the bed linens. Sofa has large greasy stains. It is also hard to find and not in the best location. I greatly appreciate efforts toward sustainability but hotels must present a feeling of cleanliness and this one does not.

title: “Keep Your Items Under Lock And Key”
text: My stay at the courtyard in downtown Ohio (west spring street) was not that bad.....first off, they gave us a room with a broken toilet but they were quick to assign us another room. It was pretty much uneventful until my day of checkout when I realized that my favorite heels were missing. The staff said they would call me with an update but nobody ever did....I had to call them Lord knows how many times!!! Finally one of the staff tells me he would look into it...he calls me back and says that no shoes were ever found and that they are not responsible for "misplaced" or "items left behind"....I explain to him that nothing was "left behind" or "misplaced"....and that the word he must be looking to use is STOLEN....must have flown past him because he told me the same thing over and over again....In the end I gave up....they were not apologetic and tried to make it seem that it was my fault that my items were missing....I would therefore warn you to LOCK UP your valuables or favorite items because they will not be responsible for your "misplaced" items.......It's not even about the shoes...they were just regular shoes...I was not claiming that I had an expensive pair of Manolo Blahnik......It was just their whole attitude about it!!!

title: “incredible luxury-- peace and quiet”
text: wonderful stay! I have enjoyed many trips to nyc, and the surrey is the most luxurious stay yet! 3 other lady friends and I caught a special end of summer promo. upper east side near the park- doesnt have the quick conveniences--- think 4 or 5 blocks to a coffee shop or convenience store--- it sure makes up for that in nyc classic money style. the hotel was a true 5 star, with LARGE upper deck overlooking the park. Lovely onsite restaurant and lounge-- you could live like a trust fund new yorker here! half a block to the carlyle-- bemmelmans bar was delightful--- could just imagine carey grant and ingrid bergman here listening to the piano bar and enjoying the hand painted murals. Great if you want peace and quiet.....but if you want a more "neighborhood" feel but still upscale- go farther east or rather to the upper west side ( think "you've got mail" with meg ryan ). HIghlight was sarafinas fabulous pizza a few blocks away, and La Maison du Chocolate macarons--yum........lovely trip, but uws or the village still calls for spur of the moment satisfaction.............

title: “Very pleased”
text:
My husband happened upon the Argonaut Hotel while on a business trip so booked it for our March Break vacation. I was a little nervous about it as my husband has different standards then I do. I think my poor husband was a little unsure as well because he knows my standards are higher than his. The good news is that I was very pleased with the hotel. Everyone was very friendly and helpful. The rooms were clean and comfortable and nicely decorated...so much more character than your standard Holiday Inn style. Rooms were well maintained every day. All staff were professional and attentive. I particularly found the concierge, Olivia, very good at her job. She helped us map out our day trip with our rental car up highway 1 along the north coast (well worth a visit by the way, absolutely beautiful scenery) and visits into the various neighborhoods of San Fransisco. Be sure to venture out from Fisherman's Wharf. We thoroughly enjoyed our visits to North Beach, Haight Ashbury, China Town, Union Square and renting bikes from Blazing Saddles to the right of the hotel was a hightlight. We cycled across the Golden Gate Bridge to Sausolito with our teenage son...lots of fun. 
We thought the wine hour was a nice touch and the Mermaid Restaurant was great for breakfast and a casual bite to eat. The waiters were very friendly and accomodating...more so in fact than in a couple of the classier restaurants we went to.
Overall a great vacation, partly due to our stay at the Argonaut Hotel. We would highly recommend it to our friends.

title: “Family Vacation in Seattle”
text:
We had such a wonderful at the Silver Cloud Hotel on Broadway. Everything was excellent, we were treated like Kings and Queens. 
Would would recommend the Hotel to anyone staying in the area.
Thanks Silver Cloud Team!!!

title: “A very nice stay”
text:
I was attending a conference in the Convention Center in April, which is attached to the Sheraton on the 2nd floor.
Sheraton Check in was rapid, efficient, and the customer service at a high standard. I was directed to my elevator and tower directly and made my way to the room.
As is usual for Texas, everything is bigger, and this hotel is no exception. While the overall property is huge and common areas the same, the room floors design was laid out in an easy to navigate square pattern. I have stayed in much more sprawling properties. While the walk from front desk to the North Tower elevators is a 5 minute hike, from floor elevator to your room is a quick walk, regardless of where the room is in the square.
The room was very clean, non smoking, well lit, had a nice large screen flat panel TV, and a wall to wall window with a view of downtown. The bathroom was surprisingly spacious, nicely designed, and stocked with toiletries and linens.
The bed was very comfortable, and the room quiet. I had no problems sleeping for my whole stay.
The eateries around the hotel were sparse. Being on the edge of town, a short walk (10 minutes max) to Main street was the fastest access to a restaurant area. I visited two places downtown, both of which had very nice cuisine, one Mexican establishment known as Iron Cactus and another Italian establishment known as Ravenna. I also observed several other interesting places on the same street. The West End was known to be near and worth exploring, which I did not have time to walk further into. Word of advice: The last night I ate at the Sports Bar in the hotel to save time. The food was very fried and awful compared to the external establishments on Main street. I would NOT eat there again. Also, the only coffee shop nearby is in the hotel, Pete's, which closes promptly at 5pm. You have to be joking. 5pm in a convention hotel? I recommend the SHeraton kick them out and invite a Starbucks onboard with a later opening time. The nearest Starbucks, by the way, is only open until 6pm and is also on Main Street.
The Hotel gym is awesome. I have never said that in any property I have reviewed, but this one merits the praise. It was more like a LA Fitness or Bally's than a hotel based micro-gym. I never had a problem finding a treadmill, since there were about 20+, and that carried over to the life cycles, rowing machines, etc. All the equipment was new, functional, had TV screens, or you could look out at the roof top pool, which was surrounded by lounge chairs and outdoor beds. Yes, Beds, which sounded like fun for falling asleep after a quick swim or just enjoying the outdoor air. Blast not bringing my swim suit along!
Checkout was efficient and in short order I was ready to leave from the underground parking area.
Which leads me to the one issue I had with the stay. My room key was coded to allow egress from the parking garage. Naturally it chose to quit working when I used it in the underground lot that last day. The HELP button on the exit post worked, whereupon I had to explain who I was, why I was calling, and wait for them to check that I was valid to exit, a 5 to 8 minute delay. 
Not a tragic issue, but given all the good things that occurred at this property, one I can live with.
I would come to this property again at any time and wholeheartedly recommend it to others staying in this area.

title: “Perfect on all counts”
text: I took my daughters on an American Girl Weekend to Chicago. The Intercontinental had a package giving us a discount, doll beds (one free to take home), and cookies and milk at night. The room was impeccably clean. The staff was very helpful. Room service was excellent, fast and hot. The hotel dining room had good food and warm service. The pool is amazing! You feel transported to another time in the pool area and is very magical. The location is good and although other hotels may be closer to American Girl Place at its new site in Water Tower Place, this one is across from Nordstrom and is just a lovely place to stay.

title: “Great rooms in a great location”
text:
This is a great hotel in a brilliant location. The rooms are pretty big by New York standards with great comfy beds. The bathrooms weren't massive but perfectly adequate and nice toiletries etc! 
The lobby is very old fashioned and grand and the staff were helpful. Not the best service by American standards but they did change our room after acknowledging that we wanted a king room rather than twins. 
The hotel is located in midtown, very close to 5th Avenue and a nice stroll up to central park. Great location for shopping and exploring the area. 
We did not eat at the hotel as there are so many other places to try but the bar was quite nice for a quick drink on the way out to somewhere with a bit more atmosphere!
Overall a great place to stay to explore the city - who wants to spend a lot of time at their hotel anyway during a short trip to NYC?!

title: “Very nice hotel.”
text: Enjoyed the relaxing attitude. Property was very well decorated and maintained. Would definitely stay here again.

title: “that was frightfull but good and cheap anyway”
text: frankly, that was my 2nd visit in NY. we had little money, tickets to Moscow in 3 days and nowhere to spend night at. at the first sight that place was awfull, stinky and frightening. buti dont regret about our choise. i liked that atmosphere of some kind of adventure there. the staff was very friendly and polite. they helped us with their good different advise and im thankful to them. if im in NY again,ill chose ELK.

title: “One of the nicest Best Western hotels I've used.”
text: When I made my reservations I was not thinking much about the hotel but I was impressed when I walked in and saw the cleanliness of this property. I was greeted promply by the desk staff who also gave me information on the many restaurants located within walking distance. My room was nice and had triple sheeting and free internet access. I didn't get to use the pool although it looked so inviting in the almost 100-degree weather. I was told this hotel just won the Best Western Housekeeping Award and I can see why. Totally recommend it to anyone looking to stay in this part of town.

title: “Good for business and pleasure”
text:
I stayed here for a week last year and thought it was quite an excellent hotel for business.
I would recommend a room on the top floor if possible as the views over this flat city are incredibly good. You will find good views of the Rockies. 
My room was a bit tired, the TV aged and the bathroom in need of a refresh but the wifi worked well as did the laundry service and room service were courteous!
I would try a hotel down town next time to be in the more fun areas of the city but for getting around this was a good place to stay.

title: “Great location”
text: We traveled to Indy to visit Butler University with our three kids. We loved our room, we loved the food, and we loved the location. Walking distance from everything. Room service was fast and the food was hot and great! The kids had a great time in the pool. We also ate at the Colts Grill across the street. That was a fun experience.

title: “A small hotel with a huge surprise”
text: My spouse and I were leaving to The Bahamas and so needed a hotel close to the IAH airport. We picked the Hyatt Place and didn't go in with any expectations being a hotel close to the airport. Wow were we totally surprised!!!! The hotel was fantastic and the staff was very friendly and attentive. The room we had was absolutely huge and from what we were told the rooms are identical in every Hyatt Place, not just this one. We never expected anything great, just a hotel for the evening. What we found though was a hotel that we would travel anywhere and stay at!!!

title: “Teenagers beware for technolgoy fails you here.”
text:
I being a 18 year old highschool guy came to Denver for a family reunion and stayed at the Hyatt. I brought my Xbox for as any other teenage guy, are eager to play some of the new games. But.... Even though the tv has all the input plug-ins needed, the hotel still locked the tv inputs which forbidden me to play Xbox. I thought, oh well I just get my laptop out. Wrong again. Wi-fi doesn't come free here and it's not cheap. ($10/per night) crap.
Although the service is good, staff is friendly, and rooms are nice, if you don't have a teenager who wants to escape his family reunion to playing video games, then come here. Otherwise go to a lower grade place that doesn't have the technology to block tv inputs and charge for wi-fi.

title: “Loved Chicago and the Swissotel is GREAT!”
text:
Fantastic Spring Break thanks to the Swissotel, our cousins the fabulous local hosts and all the amazing activities in Chicago! 
Our top recomendations for families:
-Book through priceline and then ask the nice people at the front desk for a good view. We got a beautiful and huge room on the 24th floor for less than $80 a night.(!!!)
- Park at the Millenium garage (if you have a car) to save yourself the $45 daily charge at the hotel. My husband dropped us off at the lobby with the lugagge, went to park and walked back all in 25 minutes. It's also an easy walk from the Swiss to Navy Pier (blech...
 we didn't care for it) and to the Miracle Mile (wow...cool area). 
--Get the CTA visitors pass and catch the bus right across the street
to get unlimited rides to almost anywhere else you'd want to go. We found the buses to be clean, quick and full of interesting people to meet and learn from. The pass is also good for the L which the kids loved.
-The CityPass is a good deal for all the museums. Shedd Aquarium, Adler Planetarium and Field were the best for our 7 and 8 year-olds.
-The Lincoln Park Zoo is free and very nice. Take the 151 bus all the way north and get a great tour on the way!
- Hit Trader Joes grocery store on State St. for gourmet snacks, fruit, muffins and boxed milk to keep in the room. If you use the fridge, have the auto-charges from the minibar taken off your bill (ouch!)
-Our favorite restaurants that were both entertaining and inexpensive:
Ginos East (near the watertower) has a great ambience for kids--bring pens for grafitti--and huge Chicag style pizza. Yummy, and cool
kids meals for $5 too!
Ed Debevics is fun--sassy servers, diner food, total check about $30 for all four of us. 
Signature Room on top of the Hancock Tower--OK, this place is expensive but we only went for desert and LOVED the view from 96th floor. It's higher than the observatory and we got to sit in a lovely
room and look out the windows for the price of chocolate cake!
Reva's Persian and Mediteranian (on Ontario)---very exotic and tasty. Beware the giant portions. We ordered 2 meals for the 4 of us to share and still had more left then we ate. They vary the specials (duck, lamb, filet mignon, game hens) with 2 or 3 choices every day for around $12-$15 each.
Brain Food Cafe in the museum of Science and Industry--sounds crazy I know but it was the best museum food ever. Skip the grill and sandwich choices in front and go straight back to the 'home cooking' station. No line, a plate full of REAL food with drink included for $7 each.
Murphy's across from Wriggly's (#6 bus to red line) for a true Chicago Pub experience complete with locals, baseball, hot dogs and root beer
Most of all, have fun and walk around a lot to check out this great city! If you are lucky enough to get a sitter (thank you Lisa!!!) then a night at the House of Blues is a MUST.

title: “Disappointed :(”
text: Hotel was standard. Parking very inconvenient. Stayed in top level to get view of bay; parking at top very limited and tight spots. As guests, you're paying $12 day for parking, would have liked better parking availability for guests. Rooms were standard. However, room was not cleaned as we returned after 3:30 in the afternoon to get ready for dinner. Called housekeeping to clean room which they promptely did. We left room so they could clean and decided to go to dinner to avoid the crowds. For our visit, the only thing we liked was having the hotel within walking distance to the shops, restaurants, and trolley tours. Next time, will plan to stay somewhere else.

title: “What a great location”
text: This place is so well located that it allows you to easily get to all the main attractions. The rooms were clean. The view from our room was great and we loved the bedding! Because we had some bad weather we especially liked that we could walk indoors to the Top of the Hub and to several nice restaurants. They charge an outrageous price for the parking and a fee for internet hookup which annoyed us, but overall we were very happy with our stay.

title: “The best hotel stay I have had in 50 years.”
text: From the moment we arrived the service was excellent, the food was excellent and the staff went out of their way to ensure we lacked for nothing. Some of the most beautiful landscaping I have ever seen as a backdrop to the golf courses. The Frank LLoyd Wright architectural style building nestled under the palm trees is extremely unique.

title: “The best hotel in El Paso hands down!”
text: Our family stayed in el paso for two months, we tried 4-5 hotels and this s the best one. It's new, elegant (granite counters, dark wood furnitures, etc), clean, very nice pool and courtyard, and staff are really nice. They provide free breakfast AND dinner! Plus FREE laundry, you just have to buy detergent. I can't say enough good things about this place.

title: “OK but a little out of the way.”
text:
My husband I stayed for 3 nights last week. He had business in Brookline so we made a long weekend out of it. It was kind of last minute so I didn't research as much as usual. 
I went with the Constitution Inn because it looked decent, the price was right and several other hotels I tried were completely booked.
As far as hotels go it was fine for the little time we spent in it. It was definately no frills, but the water was hot, things worked properly and the bed was quite comfortable. Everything but the rug was very clean. The elevator was slow and the parking was several blocks away. Those things didn't really bother me.
The only problem for me was that the address on their website read boston and they were actually in Charlestown, a ferry ride or trip over the bridge away. There was transportation by ferry, bus or taxi but the T doesn't go to Charlestown directly. 
We enjoy walking and actually walked back to the hotel from long warf but it took 45mins at a brisk pace and isn't for everyone.
The staff were courteous and helpful and overall I would recommend the hotel, but advise that it is out of the way from "Boston". I'm downloading pics.

title: “Awesome location, great hotel”
text:
This was my second trip to NYC in less than 14months, the hotel was easy to book and had good communications prior to me staying. On arrival the staff were courteous, friendly, funny and helpful. They informed us that they had upgraded our room for free to a suite, living room and twin bedroom, also has a "kitchen" area (sink, microwave and fridge). We had no view, but seen as we were in NYC all day and all night until bedtime this was not a problem and infact was a benefit as there was no traffic or light intrusion. The location of the hotel is brilliant, 2 blocks from Central Park, 5th Avenue, just up from Times Square, all very easy walking distance. There are subways located in 55th and just on the corner near to the hotel heading to Times Square - these get you to the rest of Manhattan easily. The hotel was warm and very comfortable. Concierge and bellman were very helpful. My advice would be not to eat at the Cafe adjoining the hotel esp for breakfast, this is quite costly, I would recommend going on the 55th street (the side of the hotel) and walking about halfway down the block to Au Bon Pain, can get really good breakfasts (muffins, bagels, yoghurt, fruit, juice, tea, coffee) for about $20 for 2 people whereas the Cafe at the hotel is about $40 for 2 people.
Overall really good hotel, would recommend and would and will stay there again.

title: “So welcoming”
text: It was altogether a great experience staying at The Chelsea Pines. It was a very personal service with real care in helping us with ideas of where to go and what to do. It was our 10th wedding anniversary and a lovely bunch of white roses was delivered to our room from the owners. If we return to New York we have no doubt we would stay there again.

title: “Excellent location”
text: This is a big, busy, hotel, but you can't beat the location. Great views from some rooms, very convenient breakfast on the executive level. Rooms are very comfortable and very clean. The only problem is the busy elevators - just allow extra time in the mornings. One of our best stays in NYC.

title: “Disappointing”
text:
Hotel was expensive (US$250 including tax) for what you got. 
There are no black out blinds and the gingham curtains, whilst cute, let all the light into the room. 
My room was really noisy, we could hear flushing water all night from other rooms and lots of traffic. The hotel is situated near a fire station so be prepared for sirens going through the night.

title: “Fabulous Staff”
text: I travel often, and I must say that the staff at the W Hotel Chicago, City Center, is as good as any I've ever seen. From the front desk to the banquet staff, to the planning team to the team at the W Insider desk, every W team member goes out of their way to be helpful and make you feel welcome.

title: “No wonder they are #1 in Denver!”
text:
We chose Embassy Suites at the Convention Center for a 4-day conference stay, because it was rated so highly by TripAdvisor. Our visit was perfect from beginning to end! Spacious and quiet room, comfiest bed + multiple pillow types made for great sleep. The free, large hot breakfast buffet with made-to-order omelets (and the friendliest of cooks, Brian was a standout!) started each day of meetings just right. 
The free evening "manager's reception" had a variety of snacks and drinks. We were busy most nights but tried it once and found a nice selection of beverages, fresh vegetables & dip, pretzels, and seasoned popcorn. 
Be sure to try the restaurant. We came back for lunch one day to watch a Big Ten basketball game, I had their 3-cheese grilled cheese on jalapeno cheddar bread & a bowl of tomato basil bisque soup. Not your momma's grilled cheese!
The fitness center, which consisted of 3 treadmills and 3 elliptical trainers + the standard weight benches and bike, was busy every morning, so get there early. 
Add to this the ideal location (steps from a fabulous selection of eateries and fun on 16th Street) and an exceptionally courteous staff, and our stay at Embassy Suites was easily the best surprise of our time in Denver. 5 stars all the way around!

title: “Cool and comfortable in a great location!”
text:
I recently stayed at this little gem for a long weekend vacation with a friend. This place has many great features:
1. The location is fantastic - Nolita is one of my favorite neighborhoods in New York, filled with great little restaurants and bars (try Cafe Habana, Bread, & Epistrophy, and a hundred others!) and unique boutiques. (See Erica Weiner, Love Adorned and Metal Pointu's if you like jewelry). It is a short walk to Soho, Lower East Side, Little Italy, China Town, etc. It's right in the middle of it all, if you want the gritty, lower New York experience.
2. The hotel lobby is modern and warm. Every evening they turn on an animated art light that looks like flowering vines blowing in the breeze. 
3.The front desk is helpful, and the doorman is super friendly and welcoming (hi Felix!). He remembers everyone and makes you feel like a VIP.
4.The rooms are small and simple, but well-planned and bright. The bathroom was great, and there IS a curtain you can use for privacy in those infamous glass showers. Not a problem at all. My room had a balcony which was a nice touch.
5. Wi Fi and The New York Times are included.
My only complaints are:
1. There is no operating restaurant or bar.
2. The included continental breakfast is pretty minimal (and no real protein avail) Coffee was great, tho!
3. Hallways are very dark.
4. There was a lot of street noise in the room I was in (5th floor, Kenmare side). I'm not sure there's anything they can do about it, so I just turned on the fan and slept fine.
Overall, a great stay and would definitely return!

title: “Spacious Rooms, pretty bad service”
text: The hotel suited our needs just fine...the room was very spacious and clean. However the service and housekeeping crew was not top notch. Every morning we had knocks on our door by housekeeping, in about 30 minute intervals...they need to get their scheduling right. They never once replenished our amenities, and they supplied no lotion. Also, the people at the front desk are very kind, but not too sharp. We asked for the closest car rental place so we could get a ride in the courtesy shuttle (3 mile radius), a girl connected us to a rental place that she said was the closest. We rent a car, then go down to the lobby for our ride, and we are informed the place we were given is outside of the radius and they couldn't give us a ride. However, there is another place closer, and if we change our reservation, they could drive us. Something they clearly should have taken care of for us, as it was their mistake. We asked for some water to the room, and they said "sure you can come down and get it". If you want a nice room at a good rate, the place is great, just don't expect great service.

title: “Worst hotel experience I've ever had!”
text: I have never had such an awful experience at a hotel in my life! The staff at this hotel, from the snooty concierge, to the managers that don't know the first thing about customer service to even the maid rolling her eyes at me....this place is awful!!!!! Their "fully stocked suite" is anything but, out dated, not stocked and the manager actually prevented us from bringing our alcohol to our room before we ever had a chance to cause trouble. Mind you, I was with 3 other women in their 40s and 50s, clearly a party crowd! A friend in another room woke up to being bitten by bed bugs and was treated rudely when she complained. Then they pre-charged the room without consent after reminding them we'd be splitting the charges at check-out. I will NEVER stay at another Omni again.

title: “no complaints, great stay”
text: we booked thru "hotwire" and after paying were informed we had a "petite room". Called hotwire to tell them this was not satisfactory and they told us to call hotel directly to see about upgrade. We called and told them we were coming to Chicago to celebrate our anniversary and they upgraded us for no extra cost. The hotel staff were very friendly, helpful and the housekeeping was excellent. The location is great for everything. We will definitely be back.

title: “Excellent location and spacious room.”
text:
Stayed for 2 nights on a weekend break and got a great rate by paying in advance on the hotels own website accorhotels.
The location is ideal for Rittenhouse Square and shopping and the sights. Room well maintained with very comfy bed, nice sitting are, flatscreen tv and spacious bathroom with seperate bath and shower.

title: “Stayed for Business”
text: Chose this hotel over more expensive options for a business trip. Check in was easy and hotel employees were friendly. When I arrived in my room, there was a chewed up wad of gum on the dresser in my room - directly across from the sign on the bed stating "Fresh and clean for each customer". Ha! Hotel staff was responsive when I called the front desk. Other than that, it was a good stay. The hotel was quiet and bed was comfortable.

title: “Great alternative to downtown”
text:
Nice quiet place to stay. A lot cheaper then hotel downtown. By car, the downtown is a 10 minutes ride.
Nice continental breakfast included.
Shopping center nearby.
the only downside of this hotel is that you will need a car to get around.

title: “Great stay except that breakfast was chaotic”
text:
Let it be known that I am a big fan of Embassy Suites hotels. When I traveled to Seattle for business, I decided to try out this property because my experience across at a hotel across the street had not been so good two weeks prior. It happened to be the Sunday night of Labor Day Weekend when I checked in so the hotel was extra crowded. The front desk staff were well trained and went above and beyond the call of duty for two guests in front of me and also for me. Because I did my homework and read the Trip Advisor review by another guest, I brought earplugs so that when the train rumbled in the "backyard", I couldn't hear it. The building vibrated every time a train went by but it was like having a free magic fingers bed. Speaking of the bed, it was incredibly comfortable; the room had all the accoutrements that you'd expect at an Embassy Suites property. 
 The only two areas in which the hotel could improve are listed below: 
 1. More luggage carts. I had to print off several pages of legal documents so I took my printer with me on this trip. It was convenient to have the luggage cart on Sunday night. On Monday morning at 9:30, there were none to be found. I was told there were only five. I had to make three trips to my car. While I didn't mind the exercise, it made me late for my next appointment even though I allowed plenty of time.
2. Have extra staff work breakfast on a holiday morning. I went down for breakfast at 8:00 a.m. and there was still two hours of breakfast service remaining--until 10 a.m. There were no plates, no utensils, no trays, no coffee--regular or decaf, no juice (but the Coke dispenser was working). They had run out of food in the regular tray line. There were so many people looking for all of the above that one could hardly move. I don't think I've ever been to any hotel where there were more people in the breakfast area. I was really disappointed and it took me an hour to get my food. The line was 30 minutes long to get a made-to-order breakfast. One guest asked the kitchen employee if there was any more coffee and she yelled at her and said that she was too busy this morning. Apparently, she was stressed out and needed some help in the kitchen. My guess is that when the vacancy rate is higher, this would be a calmer environment on a normal morning. I would stay here again despite those two concerns because I had one of the best sleeps ever and that's the reason, after all, that one stays in a motel: to get a good night's rest.

title: “Great service close to Galleria”
text: Really helpful staff! Great stay. they really have a great pool it's really pretty and when it's hot outside, its amazing

title: “Great place to stay”
text:
My wife and I have been travelling the whole california coast by car using highway one, 2 weeks into the holiday so far this motel has been the best we have stayed in.
Big room, very clean, good staff, quite of a night so our 3 night stay was great for getting a 
good nights sleep unlike many other places, fridge, microwave, iron, coffee machine, great
location, the nearby 7/11 shop was a godsend. My wife felt very safe here which was a great
bonus would retun without thinking twice

title: “Love this Hotel!”
text:
Hotel 140 is a basic hotel. Very clean rooms and staff so friendly. I have stayed here twice and enjoyed each visit and had no problems at all. Beds very comfortable and rooms were quiet.
Great location in Boston and rates are affordable. Will stay here again and again!
Love the in the wall ironing boards!!

title: “Great Value”
text:
Rooms were updated and clean, very nice but beds are very uncomfortable (wasnt a big deal for us). Location is good, not the best part of hollywood, but considering price and the fact that you are still close to everything you cant complain.
