For the price we paid I was very impressed, especially since parking was included. We didnt experience any of the parking issues others noted and they were fully booked during our stay. This hotel is mostly occupied by a younger crowd (not a surprise given location) so it can get noisy at night, was not an issue for me and my family but if you are a light sleeper this may not be the place for you.
Overall we were very impressed and happy with our room. It is a motel, therefore if you are looking for the ammenities of a hotel you will not find it here.

title: “Stylish experience, but not relevant for a stay in Manhattan”
text:
The W Hotel at the Times Square is directly located on Broadway and 47th Street at the heart of the Times Square. As described already in other reviews, the hotel is very stylish, with the reception and lobby on the 7th floor. The regular rooms are going to the 33rd floor, above you have the upgraded rooms with very stylish names. The hotels interior is mainly styled in black, with the exception of the entry on the ground floor (water fall above your head) and the lobby on the 7th floor. I got an upgrade and styed for two nights on the 35th floor. The rooms are spacious with a king size bed, a large office desk and toilette/bath room. Thw room had two huge mirrors, a FlatTV and a nice shower behind a glas front. The rooms pretend to be very stylish, but made on relatively cheap materials from my judgement. Internet is not for free, breakfast I have not tried. The hotel owned restaurant 'Blue Fin' serves good fish food and was over-booked. Overall, a good hotel, but with 330 Dollar for a night not necessary cheap.
For a more typical hotel experience, better try the Crowne Plaza, one block away and proper hotel feeling.

title: “Frighteningly dirty”
text: Peeling paint, stained, torn carpeting, broken rusted and cracked bathroom fixtures. I looked at three rooms, and all were the same. I booked a non-smoking room, and confirmed, but the front desk initially put me in a smoking room when I started to check in. Desk clerk said he had no idea what the condition of the rooms were. While I was waiting in the lobby, another guest came down to say that his window had fallen into the room!

title: “So-so Embassy Suites. Could be better.”
text: We stayed at this Embassy Suites quite a few years ago, probably before this helpful website existed. Judging by the reviews here, it seems as if nothing has changed since we stayed there. I personally prefer to stay at an Embassy Suites whenever possible but this particular one did not impress me. Unlike other Embassy Suites hotels that I have stayed at (Cary, NC and the one near the Pittsburgh Airport), I did not find the hotel to be very well maintained. The indoor pool was very cold and the water was not clean. It looked like someone had taken several handfuls of the "foam" that collects on top of the hot tub when the jets are on and dumped the foam into the pool water. Overall, we were very disappointed with this Embassy Suites. The managers reception was about worthless and there was not much variety of foods offered at the breakfast buffet (usually Embassy Suites has a cooked-to-order breakfast). The room wasn't too bad although it was a bit noisy while we were trying to sleep. The atrium of this hotel really carries the sound, making the waterfalls loud enough to hear in the rooms. Also, depending on the location of the room, there is some noise due to the proximity of the hotel to the airport, but it wasn't too bad. What really disappoints me is that this Embassy Suites isn't one of their older properties, where one can expect some wear and tear. It was built in 1990 and the very first Embassy Suites was built in Overland Park, Kansas in 1984. Maybe the manager should read the reviews of his or her hotel on this website and fix some of the maintainance problems, but unfortunately most of the staff here don't seem to care about the condition of the hotel or the needs of their guests, which is very sad. I would probably not stay here again.

title: “Great location!”
text: This was a very nice hotel. It was right on the Freedom Trail, so location was wonderful. I will also say that it was the most comfortable bed I ever slept in. My gripe is that it took us 2 hours to find the hotel. If you are depending on your car navigation system, their address on School St. does not work. There are several School Streets in Boston and we were at them all! Other than that if was a very good place to stay in Boston.

title: “great location”
text:
Stayed here with the family for one night in August. There is no hotel more centrally located than this one. Rooms were clean. Staff was fine. A bit lacking in amenities. The hotel is 42 stories high. They have a small breakfast buffet and a small windowless lobby. But the reality is, you probably will not be hanging out at the hotel anyway so it does not matter. Just expected a bit more from a Hilton as far as amenitites.
Good for families. Clean. central location. Easy to get in/out of due to small lobby.

title: “Lovely Hotel”
text: We found the hotel to be exactly as it says in terms of standards and space. The room was very spacious and the level of service was impressive. It is expensive however it is a great hotel to launch your New York experience. It is close to the subway, cross town buses to the ferry, but also to delicatessens and some lovely eateries. (buy a weekly for the subway, it is money well spent) Only a 15 minute walk to Times Square and Broadway yet far enough away to be able to escape the noise and bussle of the square. Easy to get to all you need to do in New York.

title: “excellent service and location”
text: We stay at the Gergetown Suites located in 30th. I dont have any complain with this hotel, everything was perfect, location (close to the main street M in georgetown) (if you want to go to the monument and museum, close to the hotel is a bus stop that take you everywhere), services, cleaning, decoration, the room was huge, well equipped. This hotel include the breakfast that for my family was great, included: cereal, bread, pastry, juices, coffee, fruits, eggs and sandwiches. I have a great time with my family.

title: “Unique, sophisticated, and always welcoming”
text:
I stayed at The Time this week for business. The Time Hotel is the place I used to stay a few years ago when other models and I worked the NY Auto Show. It's a great location, and we loved their lounge. It's one of the best martini lounges in Times Square. In fact, it's almost too good because it's the kind of place you just stop in on the way to your room and then realize 3 hours later you're still there and have made 5 new friends...including the bartender!
With similar atmosphere and unique qualities as the nearby W Hotel, the Time is a better choice. Yes, it's a bit smaller because it's a boutique hotel, but this also gives it a more personal touch. Oh, and it's about 40% less per night than the W.
Oh, and the gym is just what you need. The stylish yet affordable restaurant, Serafina, on the first level is open for breakfast through dinner.

title: “Best staff, best location, best offerings and best atmosphere!”
text: Don't forget to download their App so you can stay connected to the hotel no matter where you are. Get concierge assistance, learn about the hotel amenities and what to do and see in San Diego!

title: “Natasha made the stay wonderful. She was a joy!”
text: The bed was "heavenly". We were treated like royalty. Natasha was very attentive and was eager to assist in any way.

title: “It's the BEST in the WESTin....”
text: Our company recently had a live event hosted by the Westin San Diego. The whole staff was great (we needed water refilled to the ballroom every hour, they let us use the loading doc, and worked with us on pricing for valet, employee hotel rates, etc). The valet workers (esp Benji and concierge Berlon) were so accommodating, friendly, and helpful. Everyone I came in contact with had a pleasant attitude and just wanted to help. I loved this hotel!

title: “I recently stayed at this Hilton hotel...”
text: I recently stayed at this Hilton hotel, the staff was very helpful and courteous. I would definetly recommend this hotel to anyone traveling to Houston, Texas.

title: “Cheap, great location, 3 mins walk to time square”
text:
We stayed in this 1 star hotel in august 2011. We stayed 3 nights, bed linen clean, changed on the second night. Its a old hotel, so interior is very poor, but if this did not bother you and your are on a budget, I would recommend this hotel. Reception was very helpful, there was
a information centre opened for taking booking to the sites from 9 in the morning, till 10 at night thuis was great use.

title: “An Ok Hotel, but ...”
text:
The Martinique on Broadway is a well located midtown hotel, one block away from the Empire State and Macys. It is within walking distance of Times Square. 
We tried to check in at 2.00pm, but were told the room was not ready and to come back at 4.00pm. When we returned the receptionist still had a struggle to find us a room. Overall the reception desk was not a welcoming experience. 
The room we had was a triple. It was small, containing two narrow double beds. Decor was a little tired and the bathroom had seen better days. The good news was that it was at the rear of the hotel away from the traffic noise.
Avoid the mini-bar - $3.25 for a can of soda! There is a Duane Reade drugstore virtually next door charging the proper prices.
Breakfast in the hotel restaurant was adequate, but expensive. Better to find a diner for better value.
Overall an OK experience, but could have been better. The Virgin Atlantic cabin crew that flew us over stayed there so it can't be all bad.

title: “Glad I stayed here!”
text:
I am still at the Renaissance after being here for almost a week. The staff are phenomenol!
The pool is just the right temperature and has some shade. There is still a huge deck so you can find lots of sunshine. From previous reports I was afraid there was no sun...that's how you can be easily misled by reviews! Could maybe use more lounge chairs although because of the heat people didn't stay too long. 
The rooms are very nice. If you have a king room it is a little more roomier than the one with 2 queens. The bathroom is laid out nicely with a comfortable bath tub (important to me). 
The rooms were quiet.
The lobby is beautiful...they are constantly changing the look with candles at night and different pillows in the daytime....very decorative.
You won't be disappointed if you stay here!!!

title: “NEVER AGAIN, THEY WOULD NEED TO PAY ME TO DO SO!”
text: This place is horrible, I came here with my family after a long drive from Kansas City, which consists of 6 people, and I along with my family expected a good night of sleep. The price of this hotel seemed like a great deal...WRONG! When I checked in there was a security guard, he was the hotel clerk. The "high" speed wi-fi gave me two bars on my phone and laptop and ranked only 2 MBS for download and .4 MBS upload. The "kitchen" was horribly place next to the bathroom, so you couldn't even stand there, and it was also unusable since the stove was broken, the fridge was hotter than outside, and the microwave was also broken. The beds, think about it this way I've camped in Kansas during rain and a visible tornado outside on the cold ground, I would rather camp again. Oh did I mention the "AC" had smoke coming out of it once we turned it on while we were sleeping. Did I mention about the front desk warning us there was a PEDOPHILE next door, and we would wake up to back pain occasionally with sounds of people talking. There wasn't even free breakfast which I look forward to every time I go to a hotel. There were stains all over the place and it smelled like weed.

title: “Great location and great value”
text:
We stayed 2 nights in San Francisco and I have to say I was very suprised by how good value this hotel was.
Ok - there isn't any parking facilities and you better off arriving between 9am and 5.30pm if you don't want to use your mobile to call the nightwatch.
The room were spacious and clean and ours even had a minikitchen which helped with the food.
View on the inside court was bad but not what we came for any way. 
On the upside, we even had ESPN for the NBA finals...
I recommend for budget travellers.

title: “Bed Bugs”
text: We were hoping that this hotel would meet our expectations since it is so close to where our son lives in the city. We were very disappointed when we found bed bugs in the bed on our final day of stay. We reported to the staff on check-out and they seemed to be surprised but from reading other reviews on this site they were having problems with bed bugs in May. We have filed a complaint regarding the situation and waiting for responses from corp.office.

title: “Absolutely Loved The Dana on Mission Bay!”
text: We arrived at The Dana on July 5th and stayed through the 7th. We stayed in the "new" part of the hotel and the rooms were absolutely immaculate, we had 2 queen beds and a sofa sleeper. The arcadia door opens onto a patio overlooking Mission Bay and a great park. If you have children I would recommend the ground floor as your children can play in the grassy area of the park as you sit on your patio watching them. Make sure to bring frisbees, kites etc. It was absolutely wonderful! There are also concrete fire pits located on the actual beach for evening hot dog roasts etc. We are already making plans to come bcak next year with 4 other couples. The pools are great with a pool bar located at the Tropical pool. The ONLY negative thing I can say is DO NOT EAT at the Blue Pearl. The wait staff is inexperienced, and EXTREMELY slow! There were only 3 other couples eating when we were there but our serving time was crazily slow-food cold when served- and a dirty table remained dirty the entire time we were there.

title: “Balmoral hotel, Bournemouth, England”
text: All round excellence. Food, staff, sea view, lots of space in the car park, all excellent.

title: “Good Deal”
text: I booked this room based on Trip Advisor reviews having never heard of this place before. The staff was friendly, the room was clean and large, mine had a bedroom and a sitting / lounge area. Not super fancy but they don't bill it as a luxury place either. I think the representations were accurate. Internet access was included and worked well the entire stay. Overall I would stay here again and the hotel is in a good location. I got the room for $119 a night through Expedia and stayed for four nights during a business trip, it may not be as swanky as some other hotels, but being a seasoned traveler my experience left me feeling as though it was a fair deal.

title: “Treading in the footsteps of the intelligentsia”
text: I was going into NYC for a quick trip to visit a friend from England. The city was very crowded and most of my usual "quick overnight" spots were booked. Everything was terribly expensive. I kept looking and finally found an inexpensive corporate rate under the auspices of my company at the Algonquin. I was quite excited since I had gone into their bar for cocktails earlier in the year and I thought it was a fabulous place to have a drink. I arrived early, and while they could not accomodate me, they were very gracious about taking and checking my bag. The person at the desk was Ann and I noticed another writer commented how professional and pleasant she was - I agree. I came back a few hours later and checked in to a VERY tiny room - but honestly, I expected no better with an inexpensive rate and a very busy hotel. The room had every amenity and the only complaint I had (which the hotel could resolve) is that the bathroom was teeny tiny and yet had the world's weirdest tub/shower arrangement. It was the size of a shower, but was a tub that was extremely deep and I could not even get into it. Better they should rip out that tub and just put in a stall shower. Also, (and the hotel cannot fix this!) I was facing 44th street and so it was quite noisy. I had ear plugs so I could drown out the noise, but I suggest you ask NOT to face 44th if possible. The location is absolutely fabulous. RIght by Times' Square and 5th Avenue, next to the Harvard Club, across from the Penn Club and walking distance of Grand Central. As I am Marriott Gold, I received coupons for a free continental breakfast which was lovely, fruit, juice, tea, pastries - just perfect. I would definitely go back to the Algonquin, but I would probably pay a little extra to get a larger room (I don't think any are huge though) - and also ask not to face the busy street. Oh, and bring your credit card for the cocktails - the bar is absolutely fabulous and they serve the most elegant, old style cocktails you can possibly imagine - but you really pay for the treat - our cocktails were more expensive than our dinner!

title: “Good Choice, Nice Place...”
text:
We were on a family road trip in the SF area and had just left a terrible Motel 6 in Fairfield. We didn't pre-plan or reserve anything in SF so we were actually just looking for a reasonably priced, comfortable hotel with a good location and found the Sheraton.
We were happy with the rate ($150 plus $40 parking) and the room was much nicer that what we had just stayed in so we were thrilled. 
The hotel itself was very nice and we had great service but I think its biggest asset is the location. 
Very close to the wharf and walking distance to the pier, restaurants, trolley, etc....
Had a very nice stay and would recommend it.

title: “Great location, service and accomodations”
text:
We just returned from vacation where we spent 4 nights at the Mayflower Park. It was excellent. The service from the concierge to the bellmen was great. Our room was on the small side but it was fine for us. It is an old historic hotel so one has to expect that. The room was very clean and nicely decorated with a great view of the city (9th floor). The location of the hotel was very convenient. We walked to Pike Place in minutes (every morning!), we walked to the Space Needle through Belltown, to Pioneer Square and Capitol Hill. The restaurant in the hotel, Andaluca, had a great breakfast menu (never made it there for dinner). We went to Oliver's, the cocktail lounge, several time and recieved great service, expertly poured cocktails, and even free appetizers one night. 
I highly recommend this hotel for a visit to Seattle.

title: “Strongly recommend”
text:
Have stayed here twice in the last two months for long weekends and strongly recommend this hotel for business/ tourist travelors looking for low-frills professional service with excellent value. 
If you a comfortable, spacious environment without the in-your-face glamour of some bigger name hotels this is a very good choice. Each room has a full kitchen which is very nice and the rooms are certainly large by NYC standards. On my most recent trip, I was travelling with my fiancee's parents and we each booked our own rooms but upon arrival the desk upgraded us to a very comfortable two-bedroom suite. They are much less travel savvy than my fiancee or I and felt very comfortable at this hotel.

title: “Nice Hotel, Great Location”
text:
After searching the internet for a room in Chicago for a short two night visit, I was a bit discouraged because they were all either too expensive or too far away from the sights we wanted to see. Then I found the Silversmith! 
It is only a block away from Michigan Avenue and Millennium Park, and the underground public parking garage is very convenient for self parking once you have checked into the hotel.
The doorman was extremely helpful, as were the front desk clerks. Our room was nicer than we had expected, considering we paid about two-thirds to one half of what other hotels in the area were charging. It wasn't the biggest room, and maybe the furniture was a little bit large for the space, but it was very pleasantly appointed. The train is next to the hotel, so it may be bothersome for some people, but the windows were very good at blocking outside noise.
I would definitely stay here the next time we visit Chicago, and would recommend it to anyone who wants to be in that area.

title: “Good value for money”
text:
We weren't expecting much from this place as it was so cheap. However, it was clean, quiet and comfortable. Of particular note was the motel's close proximity not only to the Old Town, but also the tram/Amtrak/bus station, taking you pretty much anywhere you need to go. 
We stayed at a few places on our west coast road trip and this place was one of the best in terms of value for money. It was also one of the few places where there was a dining room where you could sit and eat breakfast. There was also a good choice of food - pastries, muffins, fruit, cereal, boiled eggs. There was also a pool but we didn't use it. 
Would recommend.

title: “Too bad there is not a better hotel in town”
text:
I stayed here for 4 nights on the recomendation of a client. 
This hotel is really a 2.5 star hotel and should not be considered a poor hotel. Full service HIltons, etc. are 3 star, Hampton Inn's 2 star, The Crowne Plaza is positioned as a full service high rise version of a Hampton Inn. The restaurant, room service, etc. gets this hotel the extra half point over a Hampton Inn, Marriott Courtyard, etc.
Normallly, I would flunk this hotel, because the hotel internet did not work, and unlike, a Hilton or Marriott chain hotel, there is no central IT support. Call during the day when the IT manager might be around. There is intermittnet wi-fi available from the Port of Los Angeles. However, through out the hotel, the staff is very friendly and that makes up for the lousy internet. Room was a tad larger than a Hampton Inn with Hilton Garden Inn level furniture and the room was clean and not worn. The bathroom was fine but the sink drain did not work and the tub was clogged up. Normal problems.
The 10th floor breakfast had very good coffee and a very friendly hostess, but otherwise no hot foods and very low end pastries, blah fruit, etc. - far worse than a Hampton Inn or simllar hotel.
I ate at the hotel restuarant once and had a burger. The staff was very friendly, and the burger was rather good. The menu otherwise looked very overpriced. For better options stray a block or less for the Green Onion, a Mexican joint, or Papadakis.
This was a one shot trip and my client was in Rolling Hills. Next time I will try something on Redondo beach. I suspect there are better hotels in Long Beach as well, but for me, that was too far from my client. If you have to stay in San Pedro, you might as well stay here.

title: “Good place for the price”
text:
My wife and I stayed here for a few days in March 2004. While it is certianly not the ritziest hotel I have stayed in, it was good, especially for the price. We stayed in one of the moderately-priced "suites" for the extra $30 over a standard room, and I think it was worth it (we looked at the standard room for kicks). Much bigger, has a little kitchenette and a jacuzzi tub. Since we ate out, we could bring home doggy-bags for midnight snacking, out of the fridge and warmed up in the microwave....The location is fine for safety, but make sure you read up a little bit on the area. Most importantly, don't walk south on Jones all the way to Market - after several blocks, it takes you into the Tenderloin district which is not nice. That said, you have to walk a ways to find a seedy area....For touring, the location is fabulous. 
Every morning, my wife and I walked down to Union Square for a coffee, and you can go anywhere from there. Since we'd bought a MUNI pass, we could even hop a bus to the square if we were REALLY lazy, and you can go anywhere in the city from Union Square....We looked around at some of the other hotels in the area while walking around, and didn't think there was anywhere else we'd rather be staying....The daily wine&cheese was a nice touch, and we were more than satisfied with the complementarty breakfast fare.

title: “Great value, comfort, style. No fuss, no muss.”
text:
Even with all the available new choices of hotels in this area, I return again and again to the Maritime because I know I can expect a reasonably high level of service and comfort at a great price. I also don't worry about what the room will be like because all of them are exactly the same in size and layout except for the suites, and they all face west with porthole windows toward the Hudson River.
The rooms are small in terms of square footage, but they are so elegantly and efficiently designed that I've never felt cramped in them. The huge porthole window helps alot, but they also let in alot of noise from the outdoor area of the restaurant and the street below, so make sure to get a high floor room if you want to sleep.
The food in the Italian restaurant as well as the Japanese one in the basement level of the building is very good and available for room service delivery. The wifi access is free and available throughout the hotel. The staff is helpful and responsive.
The neighborhood is great for shopping and entertainment, bordering as it does on the Meatpacking District and Chelsea. Access to other parts of the city, especially downtown is fairly quick by taxi or subway.
The hotel is no longer new but it's obviously well maintained because it does not show its age at all. Couldn't really ask for more from a hotel in NYC at this price range. Excellent overall.

title: “Well, This is how it should be done.”
text:
I have wanted to stay in downtown Baltimore for a long time after working here several months ago so i could try some downtown restaurants and see the city at night.
Last night the 17th, I checked in here as I am big on Choice Hotels. Now I won't kid you and tell you that everything was great, it was not. To most, my complaints would seem pretty minor but I felt like the personnel at the front desk mostly just didn't care and didn't take care of my needs. In the morning I complained and left feeling like I had been taken advantage of.
I did call back and asked for the General Manager, left her a message.
Well, I got a call back and she was actually concerned about my experience. Of course refunds were offered, extra points, etc. I am not that guy, what I wanted was simply for someone to understand that my time away from home was interrupted and not as enjoyable as it could have been and just make sure it doesn't happen again. Just acknowledge me. I believe that the GM actually did care and really wanted to make this a better place to stay.
So while not in the top ten, possibly yet, I do believe they mean it when they tell you they care about your stay.

title: “great hotel and location!”
text: I stayed at the Wellington in Feb 2011 and it was great, brilliant location as it was just a short walk down the road and your in Times Square, or a short walk the other direction and your in central park. It was freezing when we went but the room was always nice and warm! We didn't ever eat in the hotel so can't comment on that but we always went to Fluffies for breakfast which was just across the road and was great!

title: “Whenver Whatever; Not so much........”
text: This was my Birthday weekend and Valentines Day so it was a combined celebration. Not so....... During he booking process I selected the Mega Room; not so Mega. Although, for NYC I guess it was OK. I spent almost 800.00 dollars for a 2 nite stay. With that being said I had some expectations. During the booking process, I requested alternative bedding/pillows do to both myself and partner being highly allergic to feathers. This request was acknowledged by the receptionist at check in. I was told that she would ensure that it would be taken care of that evening. After a few spa treatments I returned to the room with crooked eye brows from the waxing tech Jackie at the Bliss Spa and the manicure pedicure from Lucy was actually a pleasant surprise. On my way out that evening I stopped by the front desk to inform the receptionist to let her know that my request had not been taken care of. The receptionist was rude and ignorant; she stated sarcasticaly that she did not know if it had been taking care of. I politely informed her that if it had been taken care of that I would not . After an evening out, I returned to the room only to be disappointed that the request was denied. A phone call was made to the desk and after waiting for 2 hours we opted to sleep on towels so that we could get some sleep. Housekeeping on the 16th Floor was pathetic. Room was very dusty to add insult to the allergens. However, when on the second night the crumbs from the inital day were still on the floor it confirmed that the assigned housekeeper was not only miserable that she actually had to work but incompetent. She appearantly did not use the vacuum cleaner. Bliss Spa was also a BIG Disappointment; when using the Facilities the products to cleanse your face and body did not come out of the dispensers freely it was a chore to get a squirt of soap. Also, the gym was not that clean. There were no paper towels and or disenfectant to sanitize the equipment before or after use.

title: “Great stay”
text: We stayed here over labor day weekend for one night. Wish it was more. Service was great, room was clean and spacious and the view was spectacular. I felt like we were staying in a $300 a night room but paid much less. Very easy to get to from airport.

title: “Very comfortable stay”
text: Our stay at the Hilton was very comfortable and easy. The staff were pleasant and extremely helpful, and despite the huge numbers of people coming and going at the hotel, we felt that we were well taken care of and not anonymous. The convenience to the airport was also a plus. I would definitely feel comfortable recommending this hotel to anyone.

title: “This was a great place”
text:
We stayed here last week and thought it was wonderful. The staff were incredibly friendly and helpful. And they seem to love having kids here. But it's not a 'kids hotel' at all. The 5pm wine hour was more suited to the grown-ups while the kids got to have cider and play Wii. The area (Fisherman's Wharf) is pretty touristy but it's a good location to get everywhere else. Cable cars, bike rentals etc. We ate one meal at one of the touristy restaurants but quickly learned to expand out perimeter and go to less $$ places. 
Argonaut is not cheap but it's totally worth it for a fun, relaxed, well situated vacation hotel.

title: “Fun Hotel!”
text: Everything was great! We arrived very early on check in day, and they managed to arrange a room for us earlier than check in time. The rooms are small and the washroom is separated from the rest of the room by a curtain, which was at times difficult, but we managed. The rooms were very clean. The location is great, short walking distance to metro and times square. The complimentary muffins and coffee in the morning was great. If you didn't get enough coffee in the morning, you can always get free coffee/latte/mocha/tea on your floor in galley room. The galley also has a small fridge and microwave for everyone on the floor to share. The concierge is very helpful, and guided us in the right direction. On check out day, we used the Yobot to store our luggage, and came back later to pick it up. The Yotel Hotel is a fun hotel to stay at, I would highly recommend the YOTEL hotel!

title: “Overpriced-Horrible Food”
text: The hotel is very expensive, but the room comfortable. My biggest complaint is the horrible quality of food. This hotel needs Chef Ramsey! I had the maple glazed salmon and I must say, expensive and tastless. The salmon was dry and overcooked and the presentation looked like it must have fell on the floor on the way to my table. We unfortunatly tried breakfast the next morning and I should have learned my lesson from the night before. The Chef must be on vacation or should be replaced!

title: “Average accomodations but great location.”
text: We stayed here as part of a reserved room block (wedding). Check-in was a breeze despite the large line. I don't know the category of room but we had a basic room with a king bed (15th floor with no real view). The room is on the smaller side and it is dated. The bed was comfortable and the linens were clean. The bathroom doesn't have much counter space and needs updating. Good water pressure in the shower. Location is great with Grand Central station right across the way.

title: “Have to disagree with the bad reviews - Love This Place”
text: I live in the Baltimore area and we love this hotel - especially for weekend getaways. Now I wouldn't stay anywhere for $300 a night so we stay here when they run their special packages on harbormagic -- a true bargain - -- every time we have been here, the staff has been extremely nice, helpful and most inviting. Rooms were fantastic!!! I highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Fabulous Location, Great Value for NYC”
text:
The Hotel Belleclaire is situated in a fabulous location on the Upper West Side of NYC. It's conveniently located two blocks from the subway and is right down the street from a great grocery store, fantastic restaurants, a bakery, etc. Also, Central Park is only a five minute walk from the hotel. Who could ask for more in terms of location?
Our room was newly-remodeled and included a mini-fridge. The lobby is undergoing some construction, which was a bit of a pain, but the hotel management was apologetic, so in the scheme of things, it was no big deal.

title: “Happily stayed several times.”
text:
I have stayed at this hotel several times and it's pretty reliable. Sunil the gentleman at the front desk is very nice and accomodating. He always sets me up in the room that I want which is very clean and super accessible. The breakfast is basic and well stocked. It's a great location within driving distance to several restaurants and right off of 290. There is a lot going on in the area. 
I'll be back!!!

title: “Trendy and different, wonderful staff”
text:
If you want to stay somewhere different the Sanctuary is for you. It's trendy, fun and the location right by Times Square is great. All the staff were amazing, welcoming, helpful and charming. Nothing was too much trouble. We were even emailed before we arrived to see if they could help us with anything.
Arrived late and were given an upgraded room on the 3rd floor facing the street. It was really noisy and next day we changed rooms to a room on the 7th floor, also facing the street,
which was much quieter. If you are a light sleeper request a high up room or one not facing the front. The room was lovely (not much storage space), very comfortable and bright with a great bed. The shower and basin area were open plan in the room (not the loo!) which was unusual but a great way of utilising space. There was a large flat screen TV, room safe, in fact everything you could possibly need.
The only thing we thought let the hotel down was the very disappointing breakfast. It was adequate but very basic with hardly any choice of anything and no healthy options. Coffee was weak and awful. Not like the usual New York breakfasts we've had before. Better to add a few dollars to the room rate and improve the breakfast. Otherwise we loved our stay at the Sanctuary.

title: “Enjoyed our stay and will definitely be back next Summer!”
text:
Just wanted to say thank you for an enjoyable stay at Hotel Beacon. My girlfriends and I travelled to the US last month and spent 10 days in New York. We had a comfortable 2 bedroom suite and we were welcomed with some goodies on arrival. The location was very convenient, very central to nearby shops, cafes and the subway. The staff were also very friendly and helpful at reception!
My parents and relatives have also stayed at the Hotel Beacon several times so I would definitely recommend it to my friends and family! 
We will be visiting again hopefully same time next year :)

title: “Stay here”
text: Whether you're in the Detroit area for business or you live in the area and are just looking for a weekend getaway, the Book Cadillac is the place to go. The first thing that strikes you upon entering the hotel is the amazing sense of peace that you get from the decor: the designers have created a visual sense of quietness with the color palette, use of natural materials, and outstanding modern art that seems to blend into the walls through the choice of paint technique or wallpaper behind each art display. Wall and ceiling coffers and curves as well as art and sculpture that draw your attention through lighting create interest everywhere you look. The public spaces on the 4th floor recreate an original 19th century ambiance. On a lower level are a pool, a spa, and a range of weight training machines, bikes, treadmills, and free weights. The restaurant where we had breakfast builds a menu around superfoods, with an emphasis on fruits, nuts and vegetables that are actually good for you: what a concept. The premier king room is huge, with a sitting area, a large-screen TV, and an extra large bathroom. The walls are so thick that you hear absolutely nothing, even as between the bathroom and the main room. Natural materials -- stone and wood -- but with a completely modern aesthetic make the room something you will not want to leave. The pillow-top mattress, bountiful pillows of all different sizes and extra luxurious bedding add to the feeling of intense relaxation. As counterintuitive as this sounds, come to downtown Detroit for the weekend: go wander through the Detroit Institute of Arts, have dinner at the Whitney, and then stay at the Book Cadillac. You will feel refreshed, relaxed, and as though you have entered a different world, albeit only temporarily. The vision of that world will stay with you though, once the Monday workday rolls around.

title: “Perfect place to rest your head for the night!”
text:
My wife and I were in the city to celebrate a friends birthday and saw the reviews on Trip Advisor and decided to stay here. We arrived early (11 am) and had no trouble checking in early. Our room was on the fourth floor facing Ludlow St. and unlike other reviewers, we had no trouble with the noise from the street.
Overall, the room and bathroom were spotless, the bed was comfortable, and the service was extraordinary. Keep in mind, it is a Comfort Inn. If your looking for a Kimpton hotel experience, at Comfort Inn prices, you'll be disappointed. 
Tips: 1) If you're staying a week I would find a hotel with more amenities and larger rooms. If you're staying the night, there's not a better place on the East Side. 2) The parking garage the hotel uses is much further than the municipal lot which is only 1 block away. The municipal lot is only $10.00 more for 24 hours... USE IT! 3) Get down to the breakfast area early (before 9 am). It gets pretty busy the later it gets and things get pretty picked over.

title: “Not a great Hilton”
text:
We stayed at the Hilton Philadelphia Airport for one night in April of 2007. I am a Hilton Diamond level member and I would not stay here again. They've tried to update the rooms with granite bathrooms and updated bedding but this is still an old dreary hotel. The restaurant and lounge areas are so dark. They look and feel as if every surface is coated with years of grime. 
The breakfast buffet was the worst I've ever experienced and that is saying a lot! Black bottomed coffee cups make it difficult to tell if your cup is dirty or clean. My cup was dirty...I'm glad I didn't assume it was clean!
I like Hiltons in general but this property is one to pass on.

title: “Stay Away From This Hotel!”
text: No amount of heavenly bedding or Westin propaganda will convince you that you are staying at a Westin hotel. I hope Westin management reads these reviews. This place is a travesty. The service is appalling, from housekeepers literally screaming at each other down the hallways to the 15 minute wait it took for someone to attend the front desk at 11:45PM so I could check in.

title: “Loved everything but the bed”
text: Honestly, we live here in Colorado on the Eastern Plains and received this hotel on a Priceline bid. I had read the reviews of the outdated motif and carpet issues so we were prepared. We found the staff charming and helpful. We noticed the issues with the carpet and decor but we found the rock waterfall quirky and fun and didn't mind the aesthetic issues. However, we did draw the line at the bed. When we laid down, it felt like falling into a deep, dark hole. The poor thing was so worn out and by the time we woke up in the morning our backs were hurting. Both my husband and I have had issues with back injuries so a good mattress is essential. So while I love the workout center, pool, and staff, the mattresses definitely need updating.

title: “Service beyond compare!”
text:
My first stay at Loews Denver, but it won't be my last. From the first step into the hotel, the service was amazing.....kind of like being at "Cheers"..... where everyone knew your name! As I was traveling alone, it made me feel very welcome.
From the friendly front desk staff to the very knowledgeable concierge to the very accommodating bell persons and restaurant/bar staff. I can't say enough about the service at this hotel. As a person who travels worldwide for my business, I stay at luxury hotels often and the service at this hotel rated up there with the best. I had a fabulous view of the mountains from my large well appointed room. Yes, this hotel is a short distance from downtown, but it was so nice having a complementary driving service to take me there and to restaurants when I wanted to go. Drivers were very friendly and knowledgeable about the city. A great hotel in a great city!

title: “Beautiful Location”
text: Location is superb, walking distance to major attractions. Front desk staff is friendly and helpful, and the food in the restaurant is pretty good. However, if you sit out on the terrace, be prepared to wait for service. I waited 1/2 hour before I gve up and went inside to ask for my check. That service is belw the standard for what this hotel aims to be, and is what keeps me from giving it a 4 star rating.

title: “Very pleasant stay”
text: The room was more than adequate for our two night stay and the complimentary breakfast was very nice. The staff was helpful, even calling up to the room to make sure everything was in order. We appreciated complimentary internet access on the hotel's computer - and the fresh baked cookies at the front desk.

title: “Just lovely”
text: We went to washington for the Inauguration, and we could not have picked a better place. The location was just fabulous, and we were within walking distance of most of the events and parties we went to. The condo was clean and very well maintained. We liked the cocktail lounge on the main floor which was well used on Sunday as liquor stores are closed. The staff was very attentive and just plain nice. I am happy to have had such a nice place to stay at during the inaugural activities. It was most excellent!

title: “Excellent hotel for Single Traveler!!!”
text: I was very impressed with this hotel. The location on W46th at Broadway was an amazing location to everything in midtown. The beds were clean and comfortable, with an Ipod docking station and flat screen TV. The room, however, is small and may cause challenges for two people in the room. But for one person, I loved the compactness of the room. No tub in the bathroom, only a shower. Nice size closet, but had to pull the curtains out of the way to open the door. Like I said, compact, but sufficient. Good breakfast room with cereal, fruit and yogurt, bagels which is great with me. The staff was friendly and helpful and seemed really concerned about my needs. I would definitely stay here again if traveling alone to NYC again.

title: “Lovely hotel, great location in an historic city”
text:
I booked this hotel after minimal research due to a good deal coming up on hotels.com. We were originally booked in for 3 nights, but were delayed by last-minute transport problems. We contacted the hotel directly, as well as hotels.com, and they were both very helpful and accommodating in refunding our first night's stay at very short notice.
The hotel itself was in a great location, very close to shops and restaurants, and within walking distance of the historic district. There was valet parking available, or alternatively there was a "self-park" lot which led to the back of the lobby - this was not really self parking as there were still attendants who would move your car upstairs, but at least it provided the opportunity to do some rearranging and organising of bags (we're on an extended roadtrip) without having the valet breathing down our necks. The lobby is beautifully decorated, very open and spacious with a lovely high ceiling. The hallways are wide and perhaps a little tired looking - they give the impression that it is an older building. The room with 2 double beds was very spacious and tastefully decorated. The only issue with the room was that there was paint peeling from the surface of the bathtub. Laundry facilities are available.
The staff were generally helpful and friendly, though the doorman who brought my bags to the room delivered a rapid-fire spiel about the hotel's facilities without once making eye contact - I got the feeling that he felt like he had better things to do.

title: “Loved the location”
text: My husband and I and our two young sons stayed here in December and loved it. Very safe and excellent location. Literally situated between Fifth Avenue and Times Square and just down from Rockefeller Center. Was able to walk to everything we did. Even walked from Museum of Natural History, through Central Park, and back down Fifth Avenue to hotel. Would definitely stay here again and would highly recommend it to anyone, especially if travelling with children. Only negative was the small rooms and slow elevators but these were very minor cons compared to the great advantages of staying here.

title: “Good Location”
text: We have stayed at the Charlotte Matthews location for the past two years. It is a great location if you are attending the Southern Christmas Show in Charlotte. It is just a couple of miles from the conference center. There are numerous restaurants located near the hotel -- some within walking distance. The hotel is very clean and quiet and the staff is very accommodating. We would definitely stay here again when in the Charlotte area.

title: “A Nice Change of Pace”
text:
I recently stayed at the Adolphus while visiting Dallas for a cheerleading competition. However, this stay at the Adolphus was definitely a departure from the normal, hum drum accommodations we’re used to. For this type of event we normally stay at a Holiday Inn, Fairfield Inn and those types of hotels, which are fine. We’ve been confortable and have had no complaints. However I was very pleased when I stepped into the lobby of the Adolphus. Now I’m a very modern girl. Like things to be new and modern. Wouldn’t normally go for anything old fashioned. But surprisingly I enjoyed the historical décor of the Adolphus very much. I read a plaque on the building that said the hotel was built in 1911 by Adolphus Busch, co founder of Anheuser- Busch. Much of the original décor and architecture remains, from the lobby to the rooms. The rooms vary as well. They are not all the same in layout and size. Because we were with a group I got to see a couple of different rooms. My room was on the smaller side, having a long hallway leading to the sleeping area. The desk was in this hallway. The sleeping area had two double beds with posters, but the bedding was very comfortable. We slept like a dream. The bathroom was huge. Large wardrobe housed the flat screen tv and some drawers. There was a mini bar as well as a small coffee maker in the room as well. Also the closet was HUGE. Like a walk in closet.
However there were a couple of small negatives. Nothing major. First, as I said the bathroom was huge and was consistent with the historical décor. The floor had a piece of some sort of sticky gum or something on it. It kind of blended in with the floor and was off to the side so may not have been seen by housekeeping. But they should mop the ENTIRE floor. Also, the shower wasn’t my favorite. It had an old fashioned shower head where the water only went straight down. You had to stand right underneath it. Not a lot of pressure either. The appearance of the shower was very nice with slate wall tiles, however. The other negative is that after our first night there, we got up early and went to the competition and didn’t return until about 3. When we walked in we saw that the room hadn’t been cleaned yet. I was quite annoyed about this because I wanted to come to the room to rest because we had a busy morning. They didn’t come until 3:30. I left the room so they could clean and came back to get my jacket to go outside about 15 mins later and she was already done. I don’t think they vacuum daily. The room seemed clean, though. Also, the walls must be paper thin. I think the first night the room next door may have been empty, but the 2nd morning we could hear a VERY loud, unpleasant conversation, complete with profanity, going on next door. I think it was a phone conversation because I could only hear one voice. When I walked to the adjoining door I could hear the conversation clear as day. The Rodeo Bar & Grill had great burgers and is only open for lunch and dinner. There is another, much more expensive restaurant on the premises as well that serves breakfast.
Overall, it was a good experience and I really enjoyed the different atmosphere from the usual hotel we stay in. It was like going back in time. Also, we got a very group rate of $99 per night which I was very surprised about. I would have thought they would charge much more, so it seems the rates are pretty reasonable. I wouldn’t mind staying there again if I ever come to Dallas again.

title: “Embassy Suites ruined our vacation!! ”
text: We have stayed at the Embassy Suites, Scottsdale-Phoenix, every year for spring training, but our last visit will be our final visit!! When we first arrived, we were promised a "Perfect 10" visit - what a joke!!! The first day, we received no housekeeping - not a big deal!! But, the second day, when we received no housekeeping it was a problem. So, we had to beg the staff for towels. Still, no big deal. (Hey, we're paying $300 a night, what do you expect!!) Then, we were double charged for internet service - oh well. Now, here's the kicker - the third day, we went out to the parking lot and all the passenger windows on our Expedition were smashed in, and my son's school books, dvd/cd player were gone. The staff admitted that the parking lot had no security and that this had happened before. They offered absolultely no assistance!!! The alleged "managers Paul and John" were pathetic. The purported real "manager Carol" could not be contacted, but we were promised a call from Carol immediately when she returned - it's been two weeks - no contact from Carol, yet!! We had to spend the entire day dealing with police, rental car companies, insurance companies, and glass companies. This was susposed to be a vacation - it turned into the biggest headache and hassle. The hotel "managers'" attitude was "To bad for you; you trusted us!" When we reminded them that they promised us a "Perfect 10" visit, they just looked at us like we were crazy. They offered no transportation to the rental car place, no assistance dealing with the police... Their lack of concern, help, etc... was shocking and appalling!!!! We will never stay at Embassy Suites again!!! And recommend that if you do stay at this hotel, don't expect anything, but hassles, poor service, and no security!!

title: “You'd have to be desperate”
text:
We accidentally booked this Day Inn, thinking we were getting the one closer to the Galleria. The website we booked through was nonrefundable, so we figured we would check it out. 
This hotel claims to be near the Galleria. We drove past the Galleria, then another 15 minutes without traffic to get to this Days Inn. Not really near the Galleria. The neighborhood around it was nice though.
The hotel looks rundown from the outside even. Finding our second floor room was a challenge, and not something I would enjoy late at night. We booked what was called a Queen room, but oddly enough came with a double bed. The room was tiny, and I don't need a lot of room. The bathroom had an odd half tub, and one couldn't close the door to the bathroom without squishing behind the toilet. The mattress looked like it was just as old as the exterior of the building. It was droopy and hard, and you could feel the springs every few inches.
On the plus side the room was clean. The sheets looked clean even. It's hard for old carpet to look clean, but it wasn't bad.
We decided to cut our loss (which wasn't much) and stay elsewhere. We never regretted it.

title: “Gorgeous and expansive grounds, pricey food”
text: Visited in August with several colleagues for a conference. Positives: huge resort with many rooms which are located away from the lobby and are quiet. Several pools, which are very nice, including the lazy river. Cons: everything other than room rates, which were reasonable for August in AZ, is costly. Spa services 25-30% more expensive than on the West Coast. Food is also expensive: five restaurants on site, including a stakehouse, Italian, and Hawaiian fusion. Food was almost too fancy, and it was hard to get some reasonably priced "regular" options. Local pizzeria (California Pizza Kitchen) less than a mile away (which you would not want to walk in 100+degree heat) does not deliver after 3pm, so the food bill runs up pretty quickly. Probably not too big a deal for vacation, but a problem if you are on a tight travel budget. Tip: If you want to see anything except the resort itself, consider renting a car (there is a Hertz branch right at the resort).

title: “There are better hotels”
text: Walking into the lobby of this hotel we thought we must be in the wrong place. It is extremely small and seemingly unorganized. They were unable to check us in due to computers being down so we went into the bar, which was substandard as well. The only thing that saved us was the fact that the room was clean and decently decorated and equipped. Luckily we were only staying two nights and the location is the reason we chose the hotel in the first place. We were using Starwood points - if we had been "paying" I definitely would changed hotels once I saw what we were in for. My husband, who usually doesn't pay too much attention to hotels, said "Honey, I thought we usually stay a nice hotels". That says it all.

title: “Staying here was a pleasure!!!”
text:
We are a middle aged couple with a son in his 20's who wanted to see many, many sites in Washington D.C. This hotel location was exactly what we were looking for. We walked to all the sites from the hotel, also including Arlington, Cemetery. Although the Metro was nearby (3 blocks) we never found the need to get on.
It took minutes to check in the hotel and EVERYONE was absolutely friendly.
Chinatown and the Verizon Center was a block away. Restaurants and sites are all around this hotel. The Washington Mall is blocks away. The hotel was a bit pricey (more for business) but for the location you can't beat it. We would stay here again!!

title: “Excellent value and location for short trip.”
text:
4 of us ( two couples) stayed at the Staybridge Suites in March 2012 for 5 nights. It was our first trip to New York.
The location is excellent, only a short walk to the Subway, or on street level to TImes Square. 
The hotel is very clean and the rooms well appointed. Great modern amenities and large bathroom.
Although we didn't use the kitchen, it had a good basic range of utensils, cooktop, and huge full size fridge.
We got a great deal for this hotel which made it even better ( approx $179 / night).
The only downfall was the breakfast buffet. The choices were very limited and it was always crowded. Most mornings we just grabbed a juice and ran.
If you stay at this hotel, I can highly recommend it for cleanliness, location and value for money.
PLEASE, if you stay here - grab yourself a slice of the 99c pizza, from 2 bros pizza on the corner!

title: “Great view”
text:
The room was nice, it had a murphy bed. The view from #2450 was spectacular.
Express checkout was simple, and boarding passes were printed in the hotel lobby free of charge.
The room was clean, but the wine glass kept disappearing. I had to call once for a replacement, the next time I did not bother.
Self parking is $36 per day.
Stores and restaurants are close by.

title: “Quality Plus”
text: My girlfriend and I stayed for 4 nights at The Iroquois New York Hotel in May and we were delighted with the accomodations and friendly, helpful front desk staff. The location is ideal; close proximity to Theatre District and Central Station. There is a very good and inexpensive restaurant next door for breakfast. It is very clean, exceptionally comfortable beds and all amenities are included . Daily newspaper, bottled water. We had a room with two double beds, down comforter, Egyptian cotton sheets. It is a small boutique hotel so expect the room and closet to be on the smaller scale. Highly recommend.

title: “Saha saves this place”
text: This hotel is located within a few blocks of Chinatown, but if you walk one block the opposite direction, you will find yourself in the ghetto. Though the room was nice with a comfy bed, the front desk people were very unhelpful. Honestly, one of the best parts about this hotel is Saha, the restaurant downstairs.

title: “Great Place to Stay”
text: This is a nice small hotel. Everything was clean and breakfast was great. The staff is very helpful and knowledgable of the area, and the beds are really comfortable. My room was close to the freeway and I couldn't hear the traffic at all (and I'm a somewhat light sleeper). I would definately stay here again.

title: “Great value”
text: One of the best hotels for the price. Clean and interesting decor. Well done!

title: “Wedding Weekend”
text: Stayed at this hotel because it was the recommended hotel for a wedding that I was attending. Overall nice rooms, spacious, clean. The bed was pretty bouncy, I felt my partners every turn in the bed. Overall great stay.

title: “Hot water (lack of) saves me money”
text:
I'm going to start by saying that this hotel is great. Modern, stylish, hip. Not the classic hotel you can expect to be in NY. Staff is relaxed but professional.
Rooms are really comfortable for NY. Mine had huge bathroom with tube and separated shower and a double sink. TV service, on demand, minibar, snacks (overpriced as always), some other articles that you may want in an emergency (anti acids, condoms). Free internet service, safe, bathrobes, iron, board. A comfortable desk and extra seating.
The AC worked great. Temperature always was perfect.
The second day there was no hot water in the entire building. In my case I was lucky enough to take a shower when I came back early in the morning (or late night if you prefer). But when I woke up around 11 am, the water was running cold. It was fixed late the same day when I came back to my room.
The hotel has a great rooftop bar. High energy, nice people, gorgeous bartenders (if you see Natalie you will know what I mean), great music and a nice view of the Empire State. Has a swimming pool (heated) but I never used.
There is a restaurant and I believe that there is another bar downstairs but I never went there. Hear some music one day when I came back and there was some people taking pictures in some kind of red carpet. There is also a Lacoste store in the corner of Park and 29th with access from the lobby.
When I made my checkout, I got 50% off for when the hot water wasn't running. A win win to me since I did not have any issue or complication with that.
One complaint: I got back one day at 2:30 am and asked for ice. After 4 calls in a period of 45 minutes I got the ice for my drinks. A lot of time.
Really nice hotel. Close to every place in NY. I will come back very soon.

title: “Now a Hilton Garden Inn”
text:
If your number one concern in a hotel is a good nights sleep, this hotel is for you. The bed was great. The staff was also friendly, the meal prices (including room service) reasonable and the location is great. 
Yes, the hotel is right by the highway but road noise was not an issue in our room. Yes, the place is also tired. However a staff member told me that, along with now flying the Hilton flag, the new management team is going to spend 10 million dollars on the place. So I suspect that once the construction pains are over this hotel is well placed to compete for convention business and for visitors who want to be where the action is.
 In other words all the previous reviews (and this one) will shortly mean squat.
Other notes; valet parking is $15 a day (but friendly and efficient). This is the only hotel I have ever been in where there are NO local newspapers available (I noticed a lack of newspaper boxes in Austin in general). There is no gift shop. The roof top bar closes at twelve, but given the hotels proximity to Austins late night scene I can see how they can't compete.

title: “Second stay...just as good as the first”
text:
When returning to the Baltimore area we immediately booked this hotel again.
Rooms are fairly large and nicely decorated. There is a large flat screen tv, desk area, good sized bathroom and the beds are COMFY. Hotel is in a renovated warehouse, lovely lobby area with huge ceilings and a nice sitting area. There is a computer and printer for guest use. I didn't use the fitness room but the machines looked quite new, looked really nice. The breakfast area has tables and a breakfast bar all along the windows. It gets busy, but people come and go quickly. Good selection of items, hot and cold. 
Location isn't where people would think of when they think 'inner harbor', but it's only about a 10 minute walk to the Aquarium, historic ships, and shops. There is a water taxi stop just down the street. 2 blocks from the restaurants at Power Plant Live, 15 minute walk to the pubs/shops in Fell's Point, 10 minute walk to Little Italy. The one downfall is that there is a church just down the street with a large park where a good amount of 'underprivledged' people were 'living'. I can see how that could make some people uneasy. We never had an issue walking by, but it didn't have the nicest smell when you pass. On our first stay at the hotel the desk clerk suggested was cab back from Little Italy if it was after dark. No concerns during the day though. 
My only complaint about the hotel is how heavy the room doors are. Our friends heard doors closing (slamming) quite often thoughout the night. Also, the bathroom door in our room wedged into the frame and made it impossible to quietly shut the door during the night. We did report that to the hotel when we checked out though. Isolated issue. 
Great stay overall

title: “Great starting point for first time NYC visit”
text:
We were very pleased with the location and facilities and value at Hilton 
Garden Inn, Times Square. The price was good compared to other properties yet we were blocks from the theater district, directly across the street from the Grey Line sightseeing bus line, and several blocks from Times Square. Parking in a lot right next to the hotel could not have been easier, and the $30 a night reduced rate was a good deal. We had checked out of our room and left the baggage in the holding room for our last day of sightseeing, and we miraculously get Letterman tickets! The desk staff worked hard to get us checked back into another room so we could spend another night even though they had to clean a room after a cancellation. The bellhops were all so helpful and fun. I would recommend this highly. Oh, one word of advice. This was a last-minute trip. I found an excellent rate 8 days before our departure date but waited until the following night to book, and the price had gone up (on all sites) by $50 a night. Even with Tripadvisor discount, that was a blow. Book early!
Still, perfect for us.

title: “New Years Fun”
text:
My husband and I stayed in a one bedroom suite for two nights over the New Years Eve weekend. Our friends also stayed in a one bedroom suite on the same floor. We all really enjoyed the rooms-from the spaciousness of the livingroom to the nice size bedroom. The bathroom was very nice with separate vanities for him and her, a water closet, separate soaking tub and shower. The doormen and baggage valet were very friendly and helpful. It's always nice to talk to locals like them to see where to eat and play!
The bar was nice and we enjoyed a few drinks there. I told the bartender how to make a drink for me and he made it perfectly. Breakfast (which was included in our package) at Bice Ristorante was good, not great. The waffles were a little bland. I would have liked to had dinner or lunch there because reviews of the restuarant from several sources were mostly very good. Oh well, next time, because all of us plan to be repeat customers at this hotel!

title: “Don't do it!!!”
text:
This place is the worst hotel I have ever stayed at in San Antonio! We decided to stay there after learning of the historical significance of this hotel. Upon entering the room we were overwhelmed with a stench of what I think was urine. Backed right out and the staff gave us another room. It was much smaller and had a queen instead of a king bed. We were going to complain but were afraid of what they would give us next. I told my wife let's just get through this. The walls were so thin I could literally hear a fork scraping a plate as someone was eating next-door! Now here's the kicker. It's 10.00 PM on a Saturday night and we are watching tv and the wife is on the phone. There's a knock on the door and were told there is a noise complaint and to please quiet down. WTF!!! Never again! 
And as for the historical value you can just wander in off the street and roam through the whole hotel and their exhibits all day and night for free as many people were doing.
Be warned.

title: “Fun little hotel”
text:
I stayed at the Chancellor with my grown daughter because we had just 2 days and wanted to shop and sightsee. I picked it because the reviews were so great, and I really loved it. You can't beat the location, and the parking set-up worked well for us, since we had a car with us. We left it in the garage most of the time and used the cable car in front of the hotel. Mostly we walked.
The room was very small, as was the bathroom, but it was so clean, cute, and neat that we were fine with it. We had been warned through Tripadvisor reviews that the rooms were small. 
Best of all was the service! Everyone was just real friendly and very helpful. We had a blast!
Highly recommend "Beach Blanket Babylon" if you can get tickets.

title: “Not that Great”
text:
Trendiness of the hotel is decent, they have blacklights in the elevators. However, for all the hype around the hotel, just didn't like it that much- here's why:
- The pool has 4 chairs, and is the size of a large bathtub. Get there early, because it's also in a recessed cave that blocks out the sun at certain times of the day.
- The rooftop beach is not at the top of the hotel on the 20th floor, it's on the 2nd floor. Rooftop sounds way cooler than "outdoor 2nd floor pool", but might be considered a little misleading.
- There was black hair in my sink.
- The ipod dock didn't work- I could hear music when I had my ear pressed to the speakers, but cranking the volume all the way up didn't get the volume to reach the other side of my room.
- Windows in my room were filthy.
- There was a waterfall when you walked up the stairs to the beach- at first I thought this was really cool. The I realized it was from the crew washing soot off the building from a fire they had last year. The W didn't cover the area where the water came streaming down.... the did put towels on the floor so people didn't track water into the ulta-hip lobby. Hopefully they don't reuse those towels...
- The Acura free ride anywhere you want is not usually available anytime you really want to use it.
- The treadmill that I used in the morning to work out was already warmed up. There was sweat everywhere on it. You might find this appealing... I did not.
- I checked in for a meeting and they remembered to tell me that I had a welcome packet waiting for me, but forgot to give it to me. I assumed they meant it was waiting in my room, but they actually meant it was waiting with them. When I called and asked, they did bring it up to my room.
So that's pretty overwhelmingly "Not that Great" in my book. 
The bartender at the beach bar was really friendly, as were the people at the desk. And the decor is really cool. They also have good music, but I've stayed at Holiday Inn Expresses that were cleaner, had bigger pools, and decent amentities.

title: “Fantastic new property for us when the NYC Athletic Club was booked.”
text: The Location is excellent for any activity midtown NYC. Cabs at your fingertips due to excellent staff at the front: Latoya/Krys. Hope to return soon. Also, it was a lovely neighborhood with more to explore next time.

title: “Old-fashioned SF charm”
text: Old-fashioned SF charm, with modern comforts and good price! A true delight! In easy walking distance of Powell Street Cable Car, Union Square, Metreon, Yerba Buena gardens, SFMOMA, UC Berkeley Extension South of Market Center, BART stations. Hotel staff very professional, friendly, knowledgeable of the city. Staffers anticipate your needs. Rooms retain original Victorian architecture: sink, large window, small room, high ceilings, no AC, ceiling fan. Narrow stair cases lead to the floors -- but also an elevator. Rooms are updated in smart way: window that opens for fresh air, dual-pane to block street noise, comfortable bed, multi-line phone, internet access, tv. The less-expensive rooms have a common toilet & shower/tub on the hall, shared between guests. Rooms with private bath are available. Everything is exceptionally clean. (And always the case - I'm a repeat customer.) Robes are supplied because of common toilet/bath. Secure -- after midnight your key is required to enter the building, a desk clerk is present day and night. Safe area -- surrounded by other hotels, restaurants, stores. Probably best for singles or couples, since rooms are small (in a Victorian way) and stair cases are narrow and turn. No need for car, since in the heart of the city. Doorman can whistle a cab for you, if you don't want to walk.

title: “Best deal in town!”
text: Stayed for one night before flying out the next morning. Location is great, 10 min drive to the rental car return station. Booked a king suite through Expedia. Awesome rate and great hotel. Flat screen TV's were big and they have an actual sleep number bed. Best night's rest of our entire vacation! Highly recommend this hotel. Friendly staff, clean spacious room, and comfortable bed.

title: “Enjoyed the Country Inn”
text: We had a family weekend in Ft Worth and reserved the 2 room suite. It was clean, the staff was very friendly and everyone enjoyed the continental breakfast, especially my grandson. I would recommend this hotel.

title: “Fantastic hotel - great location”
text:
We thoroughly enjoyed our stay at the Broadway Plaza hotel. We stayed for 6 nights and it was a perfect location for exploring New York City. The staff were fantastic, the room was very spacious and the room was spotless. 
Breakfast consisted of a couple of pastries and fruit if you were lucky enough to get there before it ran out. The kitchen is small where you eat breakfast and often we found all the seats were full, however they do provide trays so you can take the food back to your room. On the plus side they are one of very few hotels in New York that include breakfast in the price. 
The wireless internet signal was extremely weak in our room which meant that the internet was intermittent. After spending a considerable amount of time on the phone to the engineering company sadly the quality did not improve. 
Overall the hotel was superb and we would definitely stay there again!

title: “Room for improvement - Definite potential”
text:
I booked at this hotel for my birthday weekend with my husband. Being that my bday is so close to the holidays i thought i would never find an affordable hotel to stay. I booked our trip through travelocity and read the great reviews about this hotel. Im usually not hard to impress so I figured I would not let the negative reviews get in my way. I can NOW see why the most common statement about this hotel is that it is "dated" . Dated it is! I can understand that they want to keep the old new york charm and all but there is some room for improvement. You can have that old vintage look using a modern touch. For one, they definitely need to update their prehistoric TVs. and the bathrooms need some new tiling. There was hair in the tub draining that truly grossed me out, they need to definitely work on that. I also saw som mildew on the grout of the bahroom tiles. The rooms are spacious and the kitchenette is adorable and very useful. The hotel itself is in the CENTER of it all. Definitely a very good location. the hotel is literally right across from MSG and Penn Station. Its 10 minutes (walking) away from the heart of Time Square, no need to take a cab or subway. We went walking to Bryant Park, Radio City, and Time Square, on foot. The staff of the hotel were very friendly and helpful, no complains there! If youre looking for something fancy and top notch, dont stay here. But looking for an average room to be close to everything, this is the place. This hotel has lots of potential if they invested in some painting and tiling and new TVs. Would I stay here again? Probably. 
Some useful info:
Cab fare to and from LGA = 45.00 dont take the Super Shuttle -will take you forever!
Walking distance to Time Square, Radio City, Rockefeller Ctr, Bryant Park
Concierge can get you in at any sold out event (but it will cost you)
Tickets can be purchased at the concierge - I used this advantage and saved me time

title: “Great Family Hotel...thin walls.”
text:
Love the location, 5 mins from Sea World and about 10 mins from San Diego Zoo and 10 mins from the airport. Staff was helpful, we had an issue with our room upon checking in and but was immediately replaced. Breakfast was perfect for the us and kids. 24hour Starbucks coffee and bananas was EXCELLENT. 
I have two issues...THIN WALLS/Ceiling and difficult to park at night. I can hear people walking on the floor above us and our room next to us which was annoying at 7am if you want an extra hour of sleep. Parking was difficult if you come in at around 10pm. However, the 2 queen bed room was huge and clean.
Overall, we had a great time in San Diego and there were more pros than cons in this Hampton Inn. I would consider coming back again.

title: “Great location, good property, nice staff”
text:
Let's get one thing straight off the bat: this is a BIG hotel that often has meetings and conventions. I think a guest's experience will vary largely based on the type of convention that is there (bankers vs. cheerleaders) and whether or not there is one going on. I have stayed at the Grand Hyatt three times this past year for a total of five days (twice with my wife and five-year-old son, and once with just my wife). We've always been very pleased with both our rooms and the service received. I'm surprised by other comments that talk about unfriendly service: we've never experienced that. Even the housekeepers would greet us in the morning as we walked to breakfast with a smile and a friendly "good morning." I've stayed in many D.C. hotels over the years on both business and pleasure, and think the Hyatt compares well to many of the other hotels in the city.
Pros: Very good location, walkable to Mall sights and with a major Metro interchange under the hotel (Metro Center) in case you don't want to walk; easy to get to from Union Station or D.C. suburbs due to the Metro stop underneath (some of the low-cost bus services like BoltBus also stop right across the street from the hotel); nice, large rooms with comfortable bedding and other amenities; excellent off-season rates (including in the summer when Congress isn't in session); good breakfast buffet (but expensive if not included in your room rate); friendly and accommodating staff; attached parking garage ($26 for 24 hours) is convenient; convenient to Chinatown area and other night-time spots (movie theater, restaurants, etc.)
Cons: Like I said, it's a big hotel. Elevator waits can be annoying when the hotel is fully booked; may be a wait for breakfast if you go late; breakfast buffet is pricey a la carte when not included in room rate (~$20 person, and ~$10 for kids) and lines can be long (not the best-designed buffet for large volumes of people); street parking is limited during the week, but opens up on the weekends (try to find a street spot if you are there on the weekend before paying the garage rate); Starbucks coffee shop closes early during the week.

title: “Very pleasant stay”
text:
I had the pleasure of spending an entire week at this hotel. I am so pleased at the service I received while there. From the time I checked in, I was greeted by two very pleasant attendants who were racing to serve me. They were very friendly, and greeted me with a smile. They gave me directions to my room, and ensured I had everything I needed. The room attendants were very quick. As soon as I left the room each morning for breakfast, I came back to a clean room....every time. What phenomenal service. The breakfast was very good each morning. The hotel was close to many places, and finding something to eat was very easy. I decided to order room service one night because I didn't feel like stopping anywhere else. It was EXCELLENT. My compliments to the chef. I didn't get a chance to partake in the manager's reception, but I'm sure the food was gtreat. 
This hotel made it very easy for metro enjoy my stay. I really felt as if I was a home away from home. I thoroughly enjoyed my stay,and will definitely choose this hotel again for any future stays in Dallas. My many thanks to the entire staff of the Embassy Suites Love Field.

title: “Disappointed”
text:
This is one of the most horrible hotel i've been. The only good point is that it's very close to the space neadle. If you still want to go. Make sure your room is not on the street side. The fan in the bathroom was very noisy. Our room was right in front of the elevator. What else can i say... Don't go there.
+ Lobby look very good
+ Pool
+ Breakfast
- Room is small and old
- We could hear the other rooms
- Very noisy. The road right in front of the hotel.

title: “YIKES!!”
text: We stayed at the Warwick for four nights in July. We were in a Jr. Suite. Positives first. The employees we encountered we're all polite, friendly and helpful. The location was great. Although there are a lot of homeless people around, we never felt threatened. Easy access to pretty much everything. Now the negatives. Even with the jr.
