Suite, the room was small (although we did have two bathrooms which was convenient). The rooms need a TOTAL overhaul. The carpeting is filthy, the bedspread was completely torn in many places, the snacks on the desk were covered in dust, etc. there is NO excuse for this. C'mon guys, when a room is empty, shampoo the carpet (or better yet replace it!!). Bedspread torn? Go to Target and buy another one. Dust on candy and snacks you want people to buy? Are you kidding? Disgusting!! And, you should know better because I have read that complaint in other reviews. All in all I think this could be a nice place to stay, but not until management gets their act together!

title: “Great Customer Service but no safe in room”
text:
The staff at the Hilton Garden Inn did an outstanding job from check-in to check-out and were very friendly, professional and accommodating. Although the hotel is located at the intersection of some major roads, the rooms were quiet, even the even numbered rooms which face a road.
The breakfast staff did a great job ensuring that everyone was served their made-to-order breakfasts in a timely manner and topped-up on coffee. The quality and selection of food was great. The workout facility was completely adequate and the indoor pool has some excellent "aquatic entertainment".
Rooms were clean and comfortable, and provide a variety pillows from soft to not-quite-firm. The large HDTV had an excellent picture and a large variety of channels. Internet speed was good. My only complaint is that in-room safes are not provided, so I had to leave my laptop at the front-desk.
Overall, an excellent experience. I would stay there again.

title: “Great hotel, excellent location”
text: My boyfriend and I really enjoyed our stay. We were here for 4 nights (8th - 12th) and the hotel is in a great location for exploring Chicago. We walked to the museums and Navy Pier. Grant Park was wonderful. The hotel staff were really friendly from the housekeeping staff, the front desk staff and the bellhops - particularly helpful. The view from the pool area across Grant Park to Lake Michigan were fabulous. The rooms were clean, comfortable and serviced every day. The Savoy Grill attached to the hotel was good for breakfast and the bar staff really friendly.

title: “Watch for extra charges!”
text: Although the accommodations are fine and there are no complaints there, I felt ripped off by their extra charges and fees I booked through Expedia and with the added taxes and "fees" that totaled $42.68 per room, I thought that unless we purchased something from the mini bar, I would not have any additional fees to pay. At check out on two rooms I was charged another $21.78 per room for the convenience of wifi. When I received my credit card bill I also had a fee of $5.44 for a toothbrush according to the hotel. No one in my party remembers using the toothbrush in the room, but none the less it doesn't appear I have any recourse. I just want to warn others that book at this hotel through Expedia take this into consideration and try to get costs up front to avoid this. Expedia could not resolve with the hotel and was unable to get a breakdown of the fees that were added at the time of booking from the hotel. In my opinion the hotel charged their internet fee twice but I can't prove that since the hotel is vague and Expedia can't provide the breakdown either.

title: “Absolutely fantastic”
text:
I've stayed 2 nights at this hotel: we had a pretty good deal because of the season I guess. Our room was on one of the highest floor with view on the Empire State Building: absolutely amazing!
The room is big enough for 2 and is well furnished and decorated. The room and the bathroom were perfectly clean and you have plenty of products and towels in the bathroom. Staff is very nice. The wifi is working well and is free.
The hotel is not very far from everything but you have to walk at least 10 to 15min to go to Times Square for example. But if you don't like to walk you can catch a cab very easily in this area or there is the subway.
The only 2 negativ things are the following: 1) Next to the hotel there are construction so you can be scared at first impression but finally we haven't felt unsafe at any time even by night 2) There is no complimentary breakfast

title: “Don't Do it to Yourself”
text:
My husband and I decided to stay here for a week long vacation in NYC due to its convenient location and rooftop pool. BIG MISTAKE. The room was not that clean, the marble top tables have stains and drink rings, the carpet damp and the entire room smelled of stale cigarettes. YUCK.
We checked in on Friday morning and by that evening, the hotel turned into a zoo. Much to our dismay, the hotel roof deck is a weekend long party, with non stop drunk party goers up and down the elevators all night, making it impossible to get an elevator if you are on your floor trying to go anywhere. I had to call the front desk for them to route an elevator to my floor!
I do NOT recommend AT ALL.

title: “Great location, value”
text: I attended a conference at this hotel, staying for 5 nights. The hotel was clean and nice. I appreciated the great downtown location. I would definitely recommend this hotel. I had a special club room that had better decor than the regular rooms. The workout facility is really nice and overlooks city streets. The only complaint I really have is that some of the food that was served by the hotel for our conference was underwhelming. I ate nearly all of my meals as buffets provided by the hotel for our company. It was certainly serviceable but many of the dishes lacked flavor. It is a fun hotel.

title: “Great Property”
text: Stayed three nights (Sept 16-19th). Located in an upscale neighborhood and a very beautiful location. Was impressed from the moment we saw the hotel and golf course. We were greeted by the bell staff and informed that we could valet or self park. Rooms were not quite ready at 2:30 so they stored our luggage and took it to the room as soon as they were notified. We had a marvelous lunch in the wine bar overlooking the tennis courts. Great food and service. Rooms were ready afterwards and luggage had arrived. They were large and very nice. Beds and linens were awesome and comfortable. Nice flat screen tv but was disappointed that it was not HD. Room was called a resort room, so no balcony and lower floor but still very nice. All staff were great but don't ask bell staff for directions. We got lost trying to get to a wedding at the House on the hill which was only 2 miles away but were sent in the wrong direction. Pool area is very nice, the food was good and they would make whatever you wanted. Visited the spa for a massage, pricey but worth it and the facilities were nice as well. We also enjoyed the breakfast buffet and had great service there.

title: “Great place to stay”
text:
This was my first time staying at this hotel, and I was very positively suprised. 
I stayed for business 2 nights, and very professional and helpfull staff. 
Nice large walk in shower, which was a perfect way to start the morning, after a cup of coffee from the coffemaker in the room.
I will be back for sure.

title: “Fantastic location for the price!”
text:
Our room was of a good size, comfortable & very clean. We had 2 queen beds & it fit our family of 4 perfectly. Parking's rather limited but we managed to get a park every night. The complimentary continental breakfast was more than adequate - bagels, croissants, bread/rolls, tea, coffee, hot chocolate, juices. You can help yourself to free coffee & tea available throughout the day. A PC with free internet access (in the lobby) is a wonderful service for guests.
Staff are very friendly & helpful. Kudos to Alben in paticular! Lots have been said about him already & we throroughly agree.
Love the location as it's in the heart of Hollywood & very easy to get to the different attractions. Universal Studios is only 1 train station away. Leave the car in the carpark & take the train!
Would definitely stay here again.

title: “Overly Average”
text:
A very ho hum property. Front Desk was impressed with themselves and trying to welcome me 10 different way while trying to get my keys to print.
I could not get a Standard Room and had to book a Tai Pan Room with access to the Tai Pan Lounge on 8th floor. Skip it. For an extra $100 night you get Cheerios, Special K, and coffee and a little fruit and the rest of the day was the same or less. The staff did nothing but walk around the lounge or sit at their desk in the lounge. There was very little attempts to please or provide service.
Go to Starbucks on the corner.
The hotel is close to nothing but the Washington Monument.
There are so many better properties in Georgetown or Capitol Hill.
This property is more impressed with themselves than the customers staying there.

title: “Over excited security guards!”
text:
My cousin and I booked into room 28 on the 29th floor on Sunday 18/9/11, having looked forward to our first visit to New York for months. Having had a long day travelling (and finding the shuttle bus from Newark airport to the hotel- which proved a challenge and took over an hour) we decided to have an early night before enjoying the sights of the city the next day...and were asleep early.
Imagine our horror at being woken up at 10.00 p.m. by a man's voice yelling from the corridor that 'Security would break down the door if we didn't open up immediately, and the fine for smoking marijuana was $250, and $500 if we denied the offence'....It took a moment for us to wake up and listen to this tirade from outside our door..so we phoned down to the hotel lobby to report this intrustion on our privacy...who confirmed it was indeed a security guard banging on our door trying to gain access to our room. It seemed best to open the door before he did indeed break down the door and frame and cause himself an injury. Imagine his surprise to be confronted by two 60 ish English ladies in their Marks & Spencer dressing gowns, looking more than a little bemused at the allegations being made that it was a federal offence for marijuana to be smoked in the room!!!!!- we were beyond words, not sure what was worse, being accused of smoking illegal substances or being woken up from a deep sleep-however, he was not to be daunted....he was determined to see his excitement of a possible 'drug bust' through. It seemed that the 'marijuana alarm' (whatever and wherever that is in the hotel) had gone off showing our room to be a den of pot smoke...and he claimed 'the whole of the 29th floor had complained of the smell of marijuana coming from our room'..at this point I tentatively peered over the shoulder of the second security guard to see if there were hoards of irate residents waiting to see us dragged out of the room....but no-one in sight....now at this point, someone should have put on the brakes, calmed down and assessed the situation, but no, it was obvious we were not be be afforded any courtesy, he insisted on looking in our toilet!!!- now why would we try to stop him....obviously the hotel was not going to give us any privacy and there was to be no thought for our feelings of bewilderment and almost fear at the hands of this overwraught security man....and at this second point in time, having inspected the toilet (!) it would have allayed our fears of being at the mercy of this excitable man if he had apologised for waking us up, apologised for putting the fear of god into us, confirmed that maybe his 'marijuana alarm' was wrong and needed repair...but no......he stormed out of the room and left us wondering what sort of hotel we were staying in. Next morning we waited for some sort of explanation....maybe a phone call to apologise, maybe flowers in our room, maybe complementary meal vouchers in the TickTock diner...but no....absolutely nothing, just an icy stare from the security guard as we walked passed him to the lift.....luckily we found the city of New York friendly and ameniable when we were out and about, but we lived with the fear of another raid before our departure the following day....so I do hope you are not booked into room 28 on the 29th floor....!

title: “Wonderful Stay!”
text: We just returned from a one night stay at this property. The location is good. Very close to shopping and walking up and down Michigan Ave. The room was modern and decent sized as was the bathroom. Everything was clean except for the decorative pillows on the bed. I noticed some stains on those so we threw them to the floor. The service was exceptional. Everyone was very nice and we even received a complimentary box of toffee that was sent to our room from the hotel. We would defintely stay again! I also noticed no noise, which is very rare in downtown Chicago hotels.

title: “simply the best”
text: We chose the hotel for its location, which was close to our meeting place, and for the cost. You could have blown us away when we saw the rooms, which were beautifully appointed--bathrooms were very upscale with vessel sinks and great lighting, bedding was terrific, wonderful single coffee makers,--but we really weren't prepared for the staff and service that we received. Paul, the General Manager, takes customer service to a new level, and the rest of the staff clearly follow his example. Where did they come from??? I don't think I've ever--and I have traveled extensively--experienced such personal excellence from staff in a hotel. We needed to have the feather pillows replaced for health reasons and when they couldn't find any (it's a small hotel), they sent out for them. They were delivered by the time we came in from dinner! One small oversight--we did not get our wake up call as requested. Had we been there another night, we would have made sure we asked for it during day hours. Breakfast was good--excellent coffee/cappucino, pastries, fruit, yogurt. If you like small, boutique hotels that don't cost an arm and a leg, this place is for you. Don't let the lobby fool you.

title: “Not as good as the website says”
text: We stayed at the Grant Plaza twice in July, and were fairly disappointed. We had seen the pics on the website of the 'newly decorated' rooms, and they remained a mystery! Our room was quite poky, old, and the bathroom looked like it was from the 70s! It was clean though, and a good location for the city - right in the middle of Chinatown. When I needed to use the loo after we checked out, I had to go to one in a cupboard in a basement full of old tvs and beds - bizarre! All in all, its ok, but don't expect it to be as good as the website pictures.

title: “Outstanding”
text: OMMGGGGG this hotel is wondeful me and my mom stay4ed there 3-6 to 3-7 and it was wonderfullllllll we wanted an early check in but we waited for 2 hrs after we checked off an early check in a 9 am while we were waiting me and my mom went had breakfast thereeere outstandinnng then saw WTC by the time 12 pm came around they finally had a oom and upgraded us to a harbor room caz we watied for awhile for a room and the pppl there have the most nicest manners evver.There rooms ar beatuifl and there bathroomms.Telecscope in the harbor roomm nd all there facilited conceirge everything never complained it iss a great price,,but one thing is the mini bar hadd high priced food $5 for a soda ad 3.50$ for a bag of m&ms but everything was great

title: “Outstanding Hotel with Five Star Service”
text: This is a truly outstanding Hilton Garden Inn. Our room looked exactly like what is shown in the photo. It was nicely updated with very nice furnishings. The room was also very clean and comfortable. The television had over 50 cable channels, which is rare for many hotels these days. Although the location is very close to the airport, noise from the airport is not an issue. The hotel is beside a lovely canal where folks can walk or bike. This is about the only water we saw in Arizona. Where this hotel truly stands out is with its staff. They are most helpful and friendly. The airport shuttle driver picked us up with 10 minutes of our call to the hotel advising of our arrival. He gave us bottled water when he picked us up at the airport -- a nice touch in the Phoenix heat. HHonors vouchers for water were also provided by the front desk at check in. The front desk staff were friendly and helpful. Jolene (Lura), in particular, stood out and was most outstanding. She went out of her way to help and to make us feel comfortable. We noticed her interactions with other quests were very also warm, calming, and professional. In all of our travels, we have never encountered a nicer, more helpful front desk representative than Lura. Because of her and the overall condition and comfort of the hotel, we will continue to stay here during future trips even if the hotel charges more than what we paid on this trip. You won't find a more comfortable or better quality hotel for the money, and you certainly won't find a more helpful or friendly hotel staff. Lura and all of the staff that we interacted with really know how to treat travelers right. The extra touches and five star service really make this hotel stand out.

title: “Perfect for fun in NYC”
text:
Like the other folks have said, this is the *perfect* place to stay for a midtown family vacation ... or self or second honeymoon or whatever. 
The parking is just down the block on 46th between 6th & 7th, and (with hotel validation) is much cheaper than usual for NYC. The hotel is in the middle of all the Manhattan fun; but when you're in your room all you see is the lights, no noise or disturbance.
Ideal!!!!
Small extra thing: a few months ago I booked a trip here, but we had to cancel due to illness (everyone in the family was laid up) at the last minute. The manager was very accommodating, I really appreciated his help.

title: “Can't wait to come back”
text: This was our second stay at a kimpton hotel. What a wonderful experience. The room was beautiful and the view was incredible. Staff was very friendly and helpful. I would recomend this hotel to anyone. Extremely pleased.

title: “Too Stark”
text:
The are of Le Parker Meridien make up for what it lacks in warmth. We booked a room for three adults and they had told us it would be two queen size beds. But when we arrived the beds were what they called 'double' Really only one person could occupy the bed.
So at an extra charge, we upgraded to a junior suite and there was going to be an extra charge if we wanted a view of Central Park. The front desk person we had made us feel that she was the customer and we were imposing to ask for more comfortable accomodations.
The rooms are too modern. Not cozy enough for the price they ask. The only redeeming quality was the convenient location of the Hotel.
One recommendation for management is to train the staff to make us the customer feel welcome. Don't treat us like we are a bother for such an expensive stay!

title: “Great stay in a great location”
text: We just stayed at The Dolphin Motel for 2 nights and just loved it ! Cute room, super clean and had a nice balcony in front of room for sitting and watching boats go by in the harbor. It is located on the corner of Harbor drive which was great as we took a beautiful and easy drive all the way around past parks and marinas and the naval ships. We did a lot of sightseeing around Coronado, La Jolla and San diego and this was a perfect "home base". Will definitely go back.

title: “The hotel staff couldn't do enough for my wedding guests. They went over the top in service!”
text: This is the perfect hotel to choose if you are arranging a hotel for guests attending a family wedding. Customer service is first rate at the "Drake". The hotel did everything possible to make my guests in 29 rooms happy, comfortable and content. The staff was informative, helpful, friendly, always positive and wanting to please. It's a great atmosphere, warm cozy and the lobby lounge area an ideal location for a "meet and greet". Lauren, in group sales, was refreshing and made every accomodation to make our special occasion perfect. I highly recommend the Sir Francis Drake. I wouldn't hesitate to come back to the hotel on my next visit to San Francisco. Kudos to all!

title: “Great hotel with wonderful service”
text: I was in Baltimore for business that included a conference that was held at the Tremont Grand (attached to the hotel). The staff greeted us at the door and the check in process was smooth. The hotel is a former apartment building so the rooms are very large. I had an end unit that included a large room with queen beds, kitchenette, and a large walk in closet. The room (bathroom included) was very clean. The hotel has 37 floors so there are 4 elevators to accomodate. I did not turn on my tv and I was traveling alone so I was able to hear some elevator noise but I think most people would not even notice. The only strange thing was that the room was missing a clock. I use my phone for this purpose so I was ok. I did request wake up calls which occurred without mishap. The hair dryer did not work and when I called the front desk they were very quick to respond with a replacement hair dryer. I definately enjoyed my stay and it was a quick walk to the Inner Harbor.

title: “Lovely for an Anniversary Weekend”
text:
My husband and I found this gem of a hotel after tiring of the ordinary selections in downtown LA located by our son's apartment in the heart of the business area, and one which would offer more charm for a special celebratory stay. We had read a short review in the NY Times travel section shortly after booking our stay here earlier this year which confirmed that our choice was going to be a good one, as it was from check-in to departure. The staff was accommodating and courteous, the rooms clean and spacious. We took advantage of the complementary car service (which is provided within a certain radius of the hotel) to take us to LACMA one morning. We only had one meal at Mr. C's - breakfast on Sunday, which our children had thoughtfully pre-arranged for us as they had called ahead with the menu that had been printed out in an invitation slipped under our door upon arrival. However, our waiter had to be reminded to bring us some of the items on the pre-set menu but to his full credit would not accept a tip as he assured this it had all been taken care of at the time the arrangements had been made.
There are quite a few restaurants and stores within easy walking distance from the hotel which made for some pleasant early morning and evening strolls. 
The advice to book a room facing toward the neighborhood as opposed to the street was definitely a good recommendation and worth the additional charge as I can see how it affords for greater peace and quiet, not to mention nicer views. 
My review is delayed in posting but not at all because of any dissatisfaction with our stay; in fact, we will likely be return guests as we found this to be among the more comfortable properties within an easy drive to downtown LA.

title: “Not as good as last time”
text: We stayed at this hotel in September and had a great 8th floor room. This time we stayed on the 4th floor and it wasn't as nice. The ceiling was very dirty where the air ducts blew on them. There was only one chair at the eating counter in the suite. The bed and linens weren't as nice as those we had last time in the 8th floor room. The large air vents in the walls in the hallways had missing and damaged slats. The exercise bike was broken. Maintenance and room quality there seems to be spotty. It was OK, but nothing special.

title: “Great Family Get-away”
text: Our family of five stayed the first week of January and had a wonderful time. The room was standard Embassy Suites fare ... roomy, clean but perhaps a little tired. The lobby was beautiful and the ducks, fish were fun for the kids. The pool, however, was what made the trip for the kids - they loved it! Very clean, plenty of towels, nice hot tub, too. Breakfast and cocktail hour were great - everyone was very, very helpful. The restaurant looked too fancy for our three little ones so we didn't try it.

title: “Great Location and hotel”
text: The Warwick is in a great location. Close to Central Park, 5th Avenue etc and has everything you could need. I stayed here on two occasions in Dec/Jan, 5 days in Dec and 5 days in Jan, staying on the 16th and 23 floors. Absolutely no noise, which was great and the service was good!. A special mention to the doormen, who were lovely and always helpful. Their knowledge on directions and local eateries etc was fantastic. The decor may be deemed a little dated in terms of 5 star but the overall feel of the hotel is a great one. Definitely a great place to stay. I look forward to going back!

title: “Absolutely the worst”
text:
Cons: Our first room had water damage that was completely unimaginable. It looked like a monster growing out of the wall. Our second room was just as bad. Don't let the website pictures fool you. There was brown wall paper peeling off, furniture with the paint worn off. The bedding doesn't match. It is like a Amityville Horror. Absolutely not a hotel I recommend using until they update the place. It is way past unacceptable. I can't believe it's a member of the Starwood Hotels program. It gives the brand a bad name. 
Pros: The staff was nice.

title: “Update please?”
text: The "Spot" was definately the highlight of the trip. The worker put me in a handicap room and when I requested to be changed to a room with a closet, he proceeded to inform me that it is company policy to "give away" those rooms. The second room was better. It was quite and had a closet and a shower curtain, however, it smelt of moth balls. All in all, it was a place to shower and sleep while I stayed in LA for work. I would definately not recommend this location. Although conveniently located, the last update was probably the early 1990's. All week long there was a sign signafying a wet carpet. Really lacking in the welcoming atmosphere. I have paid much less for a way better experience. The lobby is beautiful but the rest is lacking.

title: “Great hotel, poor location”
text: This hotel was very clean with a beautiful lobby and helpful staff. My complaints are three: was close to shopping but only a block away from a bad part of town littered with homeless and "special" massage parlors. The hotel did not have free wi-fi. The hotel also charges 45 dollars a night to park in their garage.

title: “dated but decent”
text: We made a reservation for a room with a queen bed and a full kitchen. Our room had no kitchen. The room was a good size, staff was friendly, and the restaurant was nice. However, the bed was uncomfortable and the mattress cover was in shreds. The TV remote control did not work properly and we couldn't get all the channels.

title: “Thanksgiving in Chicago”
text: Checked in on Thanksgiving day. Arrived before noon, we were quickly met as we got out of our car and treated like we were the only people in Chicago. Room was not ready but we were early so it was not an issue. The staff checked our luggage and we sat in the lobby bar and had a drink. Staff was extremely friendly. We had a great corner room, they are small but very well appointed. The bathroom was nice and a huge shower, big enough for two (or three). Parking is expensive ($55 for valet in/out service per night). Nice location, close to al the great shops and the John Handcock building. Will stay here again

title: “Probably very nice for those who are NOT in any way disabled...”
text:
I decided to book this hotel based on reviews I read here along with the price and availability. Before booking I called to make sure that it was going to be good for a handicapped person. I was travelling with my mother who had a knee replacement in October and is still healing. I made it very clear on the phone that we could not share a bed and there would need to be a bit of room to maneuver in the room. I was assured that even if I booked via Hotwire it would be fine, as the person on the phone took down my name (unfortunately I did not catch theirs).
We get to our room, very excited as it would be my mum's first time staying over in NYC and we're in this gorgeous hotel that I've shown her the website/photos for. We open our door to find one twin/full bed, a desk, and a TV. There wasn't even enough room for 2 people to SIT on that bed, let alone sleep. The bathroom was small but very nice, and there was a large closet...space that could have been better utilized in my opinion. On top of this, the room stunk of what I thought was men's cologne - however it's one of the products the cleaning staff uses.
I could tell instantly that my mother was extremely disappointed, as I had ASSURED her that everything would be fine and now it wasn't. We ended up completing all of our plans in NYC except for staying over and eating a traditional breakfast the next morning (which we were both quite excited for, I used to live in the city and sometimes miss it quite a bit).
On the survey you get upon checkin, I explained to them exactly why we left early and why I was disappointed. I left my phone number and email address and honestly expected to at least hear from customer service. Not a peep. I'm actually going to be forwarding them this review as well, because that is *NOT* how you handle a situation. If your hotel isn't going to be suitable for someone, tell them when they call in and ask. Don't lie to them to make the sale and then screw them over when they get there.
It's a shame because the hotel itself is lovely, despite ongoing renovations.

title: “Chaotic stay - four rooms in three days!!! A shame.”
text:
I so wanted to love this hotel. Big plus point is the location - overlooking the river, and within walking distance of shops, attractions, lots of restaurants, metro stations and so on.
The biggest negative was that we ended up using FOUR rooms in three nights. We'd originally booked a prepaid river view twin through Expedia.
Room 1 - given a river view twin, but a smoking room - not mentioned at check-in, which I was surprised at - only found out when we got into the room which stank of smoke - you could also see nicotine stains on the net curtains - unusable to non-smokers
Room 2 - receptionists very friendly initially, but after much searching on their computers (we were stood at reception for about 10 minutes with no chat) we were told there were no suitable rooms, so we ended up with an upgraded King room with an extra bed promised. No river view this time though, although these rooms have obviously been refurbished - a bit glossier. Extra bed was promised that evening and on return to the room it was found to be against the wall - WE had to clear furniture out the way so we could put it down - farcical! 
Room 3 - After one night in the King room a river view twin non-smoking was made available - given an upgraded one so given that we'd only booked a standard it was eventually a good result. Water pressure in the shower very poor though, despite it looking like a great rainfall type shower. Wi-fi was very hit and miss - had to sit on the floor near the door for a signal.
Room 4 - on our last night we were told the water was being switched off the next morning, so we had to shower either before 9am, or use another room. Getting up before 9am wasn't convenient, so we had use of another room on another floor to shower in. Tellingly the water was being switched off to solve the shower pressure problem.
Overall then not the smoothest stay, but it was very cheap (£270 for three nights). Had we not swapped rooms and been allocated what we'd booked on the first night then this would have got 4/5 easily, especially given the location. Didn't try the restaurant as we just used the Corner Bakery for breakfast. 
Staff are friendly but they really need to communicate more - we were stood like lemons at the front desk whilst they were finding rooms for us, just tapping on the computer. They really need to let the guest know what they're doing.

title: “Not a hotel for four in a room”
text: We had originally booked this hotel to stay for five nights, but only stayed one. The room we were allocated was very small, dark and not as described. We asked shortly after arrival if there were any other rooms available, and was told by the female receptionist that the hotel was full, however this was not the case. We returned to the room to check on the Internet and we could have booked a room that evening. We were not prepared to stay so looked for another hotel, which we found. On checking out in the morning and advising the male receptionist that we were leaving, we were asked if we would like to see another room! We advised him of the events of the previous night and said no it was too late as we had booked elsewhere.

title: “Excellent location for the centre of D.C.”
text:
We stayed here for two nights. The check-in was very fast and efficient, the reception staff were friendly and helpful.
The rooms were spacious and tastefully decorated, and the bed was very comfortable. Everything we wanted to see was well within walking distance, the museums, national archives, white house and national mall were 10 minutes at steady walking pace. Also really easy access to the underground system that takes you straight to the airport.
The breakfast was priced so that you will end up buying the "all you can eat" option, this seemed a bit pricey to us at $20 each, unless you are going to eat tonnes of food for breakfast, but i suppose it is a 4* hyatt. 
We also found the resturant inside quite expensive, and the waiter didn't recommend any sides of vegetables with the mains, so we unexpectedly ended up with a piece of chicken and a shallot as a meal! Save your money and go out for something to eat, or spend your money and go out for something really good to eat!
We got a good rate on priceline for this hotel - it comes as a 4* in the capitol hill area, and paid £99 per night, which I feel was about right for the hotel and service.
Wifi is availlable, but like most chain hotels you have to pay over the odds, this is bettered by most independent hotels who offer it for free.

title: “Doesn't get better for an airport Residence Inn”
text: This place was entirely satisfactory for being an airport Residence Inn. The front desk service, especialy Lindsay, was super nice and efficient. The room was updated and clean, and quiet to boot. I have been to many Residence Inns and this one is near the top, in my opinion. There's also a ton of food options nearby if you can naviate the spaghetti bowl of highways that is that area of San Antonio.

title: “great value and location”
text:
The hotel is a great value for Union Square. I booked well in advance, and later checked rates and noted they had dropped. I emailed the hotel and they honoured the lower rate with no hassles at all.
Due to flight delays I arrived exhausted at 2am. Check in could not have been better and more friendly. I had a very slow and somewhat rude guest ahead of me in line, but the check in clerk managed to acknowledge me, make me feel welcome and get to me as quickly as he could while still paying attention to the person ahead of me. My check in was quick and easy.
My room was small compared to a modern chain hotel but it really wasn’t an issue for me. I enjoyed attention to detail with the bedding, modern furnishings, safe, flat screen TV, huge closet, lots of big fluffy towels and quality bathroom amenities. All things I didn’t expect at a hotel of this rating. The bed was very comfy. The room was spotless. The in-room wifi worked well every time I logged on.
They have a variety of pillow types to try out. Some in-room, some you just order (free). I bring my own pillow when I travel, but it was a fun addition to the room experience.
Coffee, tea and cookies in the lobby were a nice touch.
Potential guests should remember this is not a fancy hotel, but it did exceed all my expectations of a 3* hotel. I would not hesitate to stay here again, or recommend it to a friend.

title: “Recommend staying elsewhere”
text:
I stayed here for 2 nights while in route to my next destination. Having stayed at 3 hotels in Philly in the past 2 months, I was pretty disappointed in this place. Yes, they are all expensive, but for the price of what you are paying to stay near the city center of Philly, spring about $20-30 more a night to stay at a nicer place in a better location. The Hampton Inn is near the convention center, but its on the backside of the convention center on the "not so nice" side. 
I was in the middle of a 2 week trip, so used the laundry facilities downstairs. There is 1 washer and 1 dryer. There was a note that if laundry detergent was needed, to go to the front desk. I went up, and they didn't have any. They sent an employee across the street to a small convenience store to get some, and then he forgot to get quarters as I had requested. So, I went over to the convenience store myself. The front desk staff wasn't the most pleasant (ok, slightly lazy) and when I checked in, the employee at the front was just in her socks and no shoes. What!?! 
I stayed here the same time as the other poster with the fire alarm incident. The hotel staff told us to go back in after about 20 minutes before the fire department even showed up. yeah,...not sure I want to stay in a large hotel that takes the fire department over 20 minutes to show up... 
Also, the guests that stay here seems to be a little more in "party mode" than some of the other local hotels. There was vomit in the elevator, and a lot of young adults/teenagers around. If you are older, and are looking for quiet, this isn't the place for you. I could even hear my neighbor blasting their alarm radio (before the fire alarm went off) at 11pm at night. 
Honestly, spring a bit more to stay at the Loews, Marriott or another hotel on the other side of the convention center. Its easier to get a cab, safer neighborhood and a higher caliber of hotel staff.

title: “A Very Nice Hotel Experience”
text:
From the moment I arrived I was greeted by a very polite gentleman that took my luggage and escoted me to the front desk. The check in was quick and courteous. When I arrived at my studio suite and noticed that I did not have a shower curtain, I made a trip back to the front desk to ask for one and to get a city map and suggestions for dinner. By the time I returned to my suite the shower curtain was already put up. The restaurant recommendations were excellent. I went to the small store in the front of the hotel and the gentlemen in the store were also very friendly.
I attended the conference at another hotel during my stay and was driven to and from the conference by the nice gentlemen at the Magnolia Hotel. Every night for dinner we were driven in very clean luxury SUV's to our destination and picked up. The hotel staff went out of their way to make us feel special every time we saw someone.
The happy hour is nice and comfortable with very courteous service. I was pleased that I could get a late light snack of cookies and milk from the lounge when I had some late night work to do.
I will only stay at this Hotel when I visit Houston.

title: “Fabulous Weekend Getaway”
text:
My husband and I went to Barton Creek for a long weekend to celebrate our first anniversary. I can not say enough wonderful things about this resort! 
The staff was friendly, outgoing, and more than accomodating! The hotel has undergone recent renovation and it shows! There is a new lobby bar that was lots of fun, beautiful pool area, and FANTASTIC views! 
The rooms were spacious, clean, and nicely appointed. The bathroom had a sink with beautiful granite countertops right outside of the bathroom, across from the closet. The main bathroom with the shower/tub had another sink as well. The room had a huge flat panel tv and wonderful sheets!
I will say that housekeeping was a little slow and most days our room was not made up until 3:00. This really didn't bother us at all though. I am certain that if we had called the front desk and requested earlier housekeeping, they probably would have accomodated that request.
The spa facilities have just been completely redone and it was fabulous! 
We never ate any of the food on the property. We prefered to eat at some of our favorite Austin spots. It is true that there are not a lot of restuarants right near the hotel, but a 10-15 minute drive is really not that bad. There was a great restaurant VERY close to the hotel called "The Grove". It was a fun wine/pizza/Italian spot. 
My husband played golf and said the course was beautiful and very well maintained. There were coolers of bottled water spread out all over the course.
Overall, it was a fabulous stay! As we drove away this morning we said that we will definitely be staying there again!

title: “Great Restored Hotel”
text: Although the lobby has kept its beautiful older marble, the rooms are pure Marriott. The hotel is in a beautiful older part of the city close to Union Station, which is currently being restored. The views from the rooms overlook this historic city and is very close to the Link station which I took from the airport. I have to say that it is the staff that makes this hotel stand out. They were so welcoming and friendly to a very tired traveler who had obviously had a bad day.

title: “The Most Convenient Business Travel Lodging (ever)”
text: I recently stayed at the Westin Detroit Metropolitan Airport Hotel on a business trip to Michigan. The Westin had all of its regular great service and facilities but I have not ever stayed at a hotel that was located INSIDE an airport terminal before. What a terrific convenience especially with a tight and early flight schedule. The security access point right in the lobby was especially practical with short lines and expeditious access. The convenience of the terminal access combined with the great Westin service I am accustomed to was simply wonderful. I'm not sure if there are other hotels located within airports around the country but I will definitely be looking for them on future travel.

title: “Shabby, worn out rooms”
text: Yes, the hotel is very convenient for quick access to LAX with a frequent shuttle, but the rooms themselves have stained carpets, torn draperies, nicked furniture, etc. The beds, though, ARE comfortable. If I stayed again I would pay the higher price for a refurbished room. I am a Priority Club Platinum member and I was put on the concierge level floor which is the top (16th) floor. Nonetheless, these rooms have NOT been refurbished and were very disappointing. The hotel has not responded at all to my complaint made with Priority Club, though I was told I could expect to hear from them and it has now been six weeks.

title: “Great value for families, clean and convenient”
text: Very clean hotel with great staff in a convenient location. You can walk to everything, but it is a good walk. Close to China Town. Helpful staff all around. Great hotel for families. Good price, safe area, good location. Good breakfast. Not far from metro station, but we were there while there was a game going on so the trains were terribly crowded. During the day it was fine when we went to Arlington.

title: “Outstanding hotel!”
text: We frequently use Tripadvisor to find places to stay, especially in locations at which we have not visited previously; so when we say the high ranking for this Country Inn and Suites, we decided to give it a try. We were not disappointed; it was outstanding in every way! The location was very convenient to DIA, where we were leaving the next day, and they even offer a free shuttle service there. The rooms were spotlessly clean, the bed was extremely comfortable, the grounds were well maintained, the staff was friendly and helpful, and the free breakfast was one of the best we have ever experienced, both in quality and quantity of choices (and we are very picky about breakfast buffets, since my husband is a diabetic and needs to have options other than just high-carb foods). The Country Inn and Suites chain is one we have used frequently, and this one will be our new favorite in the Denver area. Highest recommendation!

title: “Beautiful place, service was in need of improvement”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the mansion for our one year wedding anniversary. I had tried to contact the staff before arriving to get something special in our room on the first night to no avail. I spoke with several different people everytime I called and couldn't get a straight answer. 
Upon arriving, the mansion was just as beautiful as the pictures. The staff was very friendly and helpful. Each morning we had breakfast in the Silver Creek Dining Room. The first day the food and service was spectacular, the following two days both the food and service continued to decline. On our last night there, we decided to try the restaurant at the hotel, Orlo's. We had reservations for 7:30pm...we arrived and sat at our table for 20 minutes and never even got water. We then decided to leave and go downtown for dinner. I called the front desk and they stated that they could "try and find someone to deal with this problem." Unfortunately, this last night left a bad taste with us about the mansion. It seemed that there was either a lot of new staff or high turnover that the communication was sub par.

title: “Rude Supervisor”
text: On Thursday February 11, 2010 around 3:15 As I sit at the bar inside of Doubletree Hotel I heard a big commotion like a fight was about to abrupt when I overheard an Employee from the hotel screaming and using profanity to a lady I believe to be a customer at the front desk of the hotel. It worried me because I noticed that the lady wasn't even yelling she was trying to ask a question. Soon I found out the employee was a House keeping supervisor. He was tall black and slim. This type of attitude provoked me and my clients to never come back to such foul mouth environment especially from employees. "If you would like supervisors to talk down disrespectful and curse at you then this is the place".

title: “Great Location”
text:
I have stayed in New York before and have paid between $120-$300 a night with in Times Square so I was a little worried as to what the hotel would be like for the price we paid and I have to say it was better than the other two hotels. The room was clean (evey day ,and with fresh towels) very quiet.
Great location for what we needed.
There are a few minor things that need to be looked at,the shower water supply runs hot one second and cold the next, no where to hang towels.
We stayed 4 nights and hope to go back again.

title: “my stay”
text: Nice room, do wish it was a bit lower even though I know it was in Downtown area of Chicago. I didn't see a tv listing & should have the BTN channel since we are in the conference. Maybe have a listing of local resterant joints and attractions that might be around.

title: “Good Location, Okay Hotel”
text:
There is nothing wrong with the Sheraton. It is right on the 16th Street Mall, and in easy walking distance of the main downtown attractions (museums, sports arenas, state buildings, LoDo). The rooms are secure, and reasonably comfortable and quiet.
That being said, this hotel is not special. There are no robes or slippers for the average guest (The desk staff said there are some available, but they never did bring us any, despite our many requests). The pool is outside and heated, but there is not hot tub. There is a sauna and a decent exercise room with bikes and treadmills. It is in the tower building and a very long walk from the plaza building.
The food prices are very high, and you have to pay $10/day for a fridge. You also have to pay to use the ethernet in your room (about $20 for high speed daily, 11 for low speed daily). There is free wireless in the lobby.
In our room the showerhead was very poor and sprayed everywhere. The bathroom sink did not drain properly and "chugged" all the time (very annoying).
There was no ventilation in the room apart from the fan under the windows. 
The bedcovers are the old-fashioned polyester kind that probably have never been washed. Expect to feel a bit germaphobic while here.
Bottom line: this is an okay hotel to be based out of, in a reasonable location. HOWEVER, it is not a good hotel for spending much time in. The average guest room does not offer robes, slippers, fresh air, a good shower, or clean-feeling linens.

title: “Nice hotel but there might be something better?”
text: Hotel Diva is a nice hotel with a great location near union square. The service was great and the staff was very friendly and helpful. Our room was spacious and clean. I could hear some outside noise in our hotel room but in all fairness it was Gay Pride Week and there seemed to be some serious partying going on around town. In it's quest to be edgy the elevators and hallways were very dark. Mood lighting I guess you could say. The Mexican restaurant next door is delicious and there is a Starbucks conveniently connected to the lobby. All in all I liked the hotel and enjoyed my stay but would probably give Hotel Monaco or The Clift a try next time if the rates were comparable.

title: “Would stay again”
text: This was the second Hilton that we stayed in over the course of 30 days, and of the two this one was much more professional and in general we walked away from this hotel much happier than the last. We received excellent pricing thanks to Priceline. The hotel had a very elegant look and feel to it. We were greeted warmly at the front desk and were pleasantly surprised by the accommodations. It was strange that they had a rather old TV in the room, but we weren't really there to watch television. Beds were very comfortable. The pool was nice, although not great mainly due to how shallow it was in most areas. The fitness room had good quality equipment. We only had breakfast at the restaurant and it was rather good. I recommend the Spanish migas. The aesthetics of hotel were top notch. We had an enjoyable time walking the diameter of the small lake next to the hotel. The ducks that also enjoy the lake took a walk with us. The internet and parking was not free. If we had not gotten such a good deal on the hotel the parking rate would have bothered me, but I understand the need to charge being that the place was in Lincoln Centre. The hotel was basically across the street from the Galleria mall. We did not actually visit the mall on this particular trip, but it is an excellent place to shop and the hotel offers an hourly shuttle to and from the location. I would stay there again if we could lock in on the same great rate.

title: “Great boutique hotel, ask for balcony room”
text:
Great little boutique hotel on Kenmare Street in NYC. Very close to all the key areas of lower Manhattan. The rooms are small, as many are in NYC, but very clean, modern, and well appointed. I had a balcony room on the 9th floor with a great view of the city. 
I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Great Location!”
text: The Roosevelt is a wonderful hotel! I have stayed her twice and was very pleased both times. The rooms are clean and comfortable, the beds were comfortable and the location is great. We take the train in and are able to walk to the hotel from Grand Central there are plenty of subway stations nearby. We also walk from the hotel to 5th Ave and Times Square! Any time I travel to NY I will stay at the Roosevelt!

title: “New, stylish, comfy and clean!!”
text: My family stayed at the JW Marriott on the way to a big family reunion. We found a great deal for this hotel on Priceline! Anyway, the hotel was easy to find, parking was cheap ($6/ day) for a major city and the hotel is right across the street from a museum and a big park. The hotel itself is modern in style and guest services (touch screen lobby directory and free wifi). The rooms were very clean, the towels and linens were soft. What I did not like is that the ice machine was on the 2nd floor, and staying on the 14th floor, we found that inconvenient. Also, in order to use the internet service IN the business center I had to pay. 40 cents/min. Other than those things, I would recommend this hotel to anyone visiting Indianapolis.

title: “Good service and location, but small & noisy room”
text:
Spent one night at the Hotel Mela on business; location is next to Times Square (and near our NY office). I found the room to be clean and nicely appointed, but the room and bathroom are very small (by U.S. standards, anyway). Also, there's no place but the bed to put a laptop, or eat breakfast. For details, read on...
Room - it's pretty small. There's literally room for the bed, the entertainment center/armoire, and a night stand on each side of the bed. No chair. The bed is a full and is very comfortable. The appointments have a understated, modern look, and a smallish flat screen HDTV is included, (but understand there's no HD programming). The mini-bar has a couple of, shall we say, interesting items to purchase for close encounters... Room was very clean. One problem - even though I was eight floors up the soundproofing is non-existent, and I could hear everything on the street.
Bathroom - also very small, and very clean. Limited space for vanity (glass shelf above the sink). The shower is awkward - the door is all glass, and has a weird inward angle, and it is hard to close the door. I managed to get it closed, but water still got all over the floor.
Food - room service was prompt; I got a bagel, so no comment on the quality of the rest of the food.
Location - right next to Times Square, so if this is your destination, the location is great. I was here because it is so close to our NY offices. However, the surrounding area is loud, so be prepared for noise.
Other - staff was friendly, and the lobby has complimentary had hot chocolate with marshmallows. 
Overall - not an optimal business hotel. I could see my wife and I staying here, but the ambient noise would likely lead me to pick somewhere else. Plus, being the boorish American that I am, I like at least a standard US sized hotel room. :-)

title: “Don't let the mediocre reviews deter you, I would recommend this hotel...”
text: I was a little nervous about what we would arrive to after reading several mediocre and negative reviews for this hotel. Fortunately, we were very pleased with our stay. If you're expecting the Hilton, don't stay here. I think some previous reviewers may have higher expectations than what this hotel class typically provides. Our 2 double bed room was clean, the bed linens weren't the old polyester style (very glad to see this), and the continental breakfast in the morning was great. They had a good variety - coffee, waffles, bagels, sausage biscuits, breakfast hot pockets, cereal, milk, and OJ. Not anything fancy, but hey, it's FREE and certainly sufficient. There is also free wireless internet for guests and this was nice to have since both my friend and I had our laptops. If you don't have a computer with you, guests are able to use the business center in the lobby for free as well. The location is very convenient to downtown since it's right along I-35 and parking is free. The rooms included a refridgerator, microwave, and coffee maker. We slept great in the beds, too. I paid $100 a night, and for that price so close to downtown, it was perfect for us. I would stay here again and recommend it to anyone who is looking for a convenient budget-friendly hotel.

title: “View of Lady Liberty on the 4th of July!”
text:
Stayed here overnight on July 4th to be in a convenient place to walk to the fireworks. This is a great hotel! I am a big Marriott fan and am so for a reason. I have yet to stay at a Marriott that has disappointed me. 
Location: I live in CT and have been to NYC many times. 
If you have never been, you may find the Marriott Marquis in a better "touristy" location, as it is smack dab in the middle of Times Square, but I wanted to be able to walk over to South Street Seaport to watch the fireworks. This hotel is a 5 minute walk to Battery Park where you catch the ferries to Ellis Island and the Statue of Liberty. Its about a 10-15 minute walk to South Street Seaport, and around the corner from The Twin towers site (I get chocked up just writing those words). If you do drive in from CT (or anywhere in New England) follow the hotel directions and do the FDR, not the West Side Highway, much less traffic and easy. 
Hotel: I had read the reviews here before booking (I always do!) and knew that the elevators were slow, so I was prepared to wait. And as a matter of fact, it wasnt that bad and they are in the process of replaing them with high speed elevators! From the moment we pulled up to the hotel, we were greeted by one of the nicest Bellman that I have every met! (ps its $50 to valet your car for 24hours). He set the stage for all the staff that followed. Tennile was a sweetheart at the front desk. We asked for a room with a view of the Statue of liberty , she checked and was able to accomodate us! we stayed in room 3604-- awesome view!!! The room was clean, bright, flat screen TV, nice marble bathroom. Bed was definatley not the "marriott bed" but it was fine. We had a package that included breakfast for 2 in Roys Rest. off the lobby. It was a very nice buffet with all you could want! and the staff there just couldnt have been nicer!! there is also a real Starbucks attached to the hotel, so you can enter right thru the lobby. 
if you stay here, you cant go wrong!

title: “Great Business Trip”
text: The hotel is beautiful, the rooms are well manicured, and the VIBE is amazing. In particular the service I received from Megan at the front desk upon check-in and the service from Patti at the lounge bar were fantastic. In addition after my checkout the service continued with a follow-up from Patrick Armano (Talent Coach) and Jim McPartlin (General Manager). I look forward to my next W experience!

title: “Excellent Stay”
text: My husband I I stayed at the Petite Auberge about 3 weeks ago for 5 days. We had an excellent stay. We had one of the basic homes and it was more than adequate. We spent most of our time sightseeing, therefore we had no need for a large room. The staff was so helpful and accomodating. They went out of their way to give directions and recommend restaurants. The breakfast was good every morning, with plenty of healthy choices. We especially enjoyed the cookies that were put out every day as well as the fruit and drinks provided. Another thing that was not mentioned on this page was that the guests at the Petite Auberge could use the fitness room at the White Swan. This was especially nice for my husband who wanted to use the treadmill. Overall it was a great stay!

title: “A real find.”
text: The Galleria Park is an older hotel that has been very nicely rehabbed and updated. Because of their age, the rooms are a little smaller than in modern hotels; however, they are very attractive and comfortable, with up to date bathrooms. If you arrive by BART, the hotel is only a five-minute walk from the station. I was in town to see a couple of museum exhibits, and was very pleased to discover that SFMOMA and the Contemporary Jewish Museum, not to mention the Yerba Buena Center, also were only a five-minute walk away, just south of Market. There is a nice little bakery and cafe next door where I got a good casual lunch and breakfast. The hotel has an outdoor "park" on one of its roofs, and that provided a nice place to relax after a busy day in the City. As an added bonus, I found a promotional code at www.retailmenot.com that saved me about $38 per night. I definitely will stay there again.

title: “Very nice.”
text: Really enjoyed my stay here. Great customer service and location. Easily walked to Chinatown and Japantown. Great location. Check-in was a breeze and the person who brought our luggage got us ice, told us where things were, and was very helpful and friendly.

title: “Great Spot”
text:
We stayed here for a couple nights over the weekend, and found it to be a great spot. The location is perfect, the price was good. The parking was a decent price ($15/night). The hotel staff were very helpful - they suggested places to eat. Our hair dryer did not work - a new one was brought up within 10 minutes.
The room was clean. The bathtub is a little dated, but that's about it. The water pressure was amazing! The bed was pretty comfy.
There is a restaurant there, but we didn't try it. The prices seemed a bit much. 
We walked to the market and to the Space needle in minutes.
We had a room on the 6th avenue side, and it was a little noisy on the street around midnight, but it wasn't that bad.
We would stay here again. A great experience.

title: “Close to Attractions”
text:
Having read mixed reviews on this site, we didn't know what to expect. Overall, we were pleased with the stay. 
The hotel is close (within walking distance) of the White House and the Mall, as well as the Metro, restaurants/shops and other sights to see. The daytime staff are welcoming and accomodating. The evening and early morning staff are rude and abrasive. 
We were able to check in nearly three hours early without having to pay extra, which allowed us to begin our vacation immediately. 
While it is true that you can hear doors slamming and water running (from toilets/showers) at night, it is no different than living in an apartment complex or college dorm. It is also much less expensive than other hotels even a few blocks away. 
To that end, the neighborhood is exciting and bustling: it is known as an 'upscale' district with nice homes, but also close to the University, which brings the bustle and vitality of college life. It was never very noisy, and we did not feel unsafe at all, even walking at night. 
If you are looking for a five-star, posh hotel with a day spa and the like, this is not the place for you. But if you just need a safe, warm and (relatively) quiet place to rest after a long day of sight-seeing, it is a good choice.

title: “Convenient Location”
text:
We were not surprised or disappointed. This motel has been accurately advertised and reviewed. The location was incredibly convenient less than a five minute walk to the Los Angeles Metro station which gave ready access to the sites of Hollywood and to downtown LA. An all day metro pass is currently $6. Also the ice cream shop one block away was a total treat after a hot day of sightseeing. 
If you want a typical 2-star motel for a decent price and a very convenient Hollywood USA location the Coral Sands Motel is worth a try.

title: “Lovely stay - perfect location for visiting philly”
text:
Visiting with my wife and 2 young children, all of our needs were met. Room was nice, staff were friendly and location perfect. (I loved Reading Terminal Market next door). 
I have no reason to moan or complain
Wished it could of been a little cheaper as I would have liked to have stayed longer, but I guess that option doesnt exisit in downtown Philadelphia!

title: “Great hotel”
text: What a fabulous hotel in the Union Square district of San Francisco. After travelling for nearly 27 hours we arrived at the hotel to be greeted by friendly staff who made our check in as quick as possible. The room was clean and I can honestly say we did not have one complaint during our whole stay! The location is great as it is only 2 blocks from union square and the cable car turn around (beware this does get very busy from mid morning on!) I have read on other reviews about the number of homeless people on neighbouring blocks however I found there to be homeless people throughout the city and not just in this neighbourhood. Hotel Nikko added to the wonderful experience we had in San Francisco, and I hope to be able to return at some point!

title: “3 day stay at NY Hilton”
text:
Conviniently located on the Avenue at the Americas in central Manhattan, the Hilton New York, whilst retentive of beautiful high ceilings and retro features, is in need of rejuvenating, as the wallpaper is peeling in most areas, and the skirting boards are falling apart. Upon our arrival, ther did seem to be the slightest misunderstanding over rooms, but once overcome, we were welcomed up to our 42nd floor room, with an excellent view of central park. The room itself is very mediocre, looking very 70's without being stylish. From what I have picked up on from reading other reviews, most rooms seem to be small and dingy, however we were designated a spacious suite with a large living/dining area, two bathrooms and a double bedroom. Although large, I feel that the space coul have been used more productively as the rooms were all minimally furnished, and a little surpulus; does anybody really need two bathrooms? 
Whether or not within our three day stay at this hotel, housekeeping did come, was hard to tell, as the rooms looked pretty much the same in the morning as it did in the evening; I'm certain necessities such as made beds were not attended to. 
Dining at the hotel was of poor quality, the executive lounges delicacies consist of processed dumplings and dry spring rolls, although the question begs that in a city such as New York that is rich in Michelin starred rester aunts, does the food really need to be all that amazing? 
Although the food is not one to be remembered, the staff is; as by and large the the employees were all very willing to help and were very welcoming, especially as we were a little clueless as to were everything was.
Despite being such a busy hotel, the atmosphere as surprisingly jovial, especially as our visit was close to Christmas, you could really tell they'd made a huge effort to make it all look nice.
Overall, a pretty mediocre hotel in desperate need of a re-design of it's dated features, with an 
excellent location and welcoming staff, however does nit compare to other city Hiltons I have 
visited.

title: “Excellent and "Teckie"”
text: 2 day stay, Sun/Mon and could not have been better. Wife took both room keys when she went shopping and I wanted to share in the evening libations. Called front desk and asked if just my DL would suffice for ID to get another key and reply was "Not Necessary, I know who you are." OUTSTANDING CUSTOMER SERVICE. GREAT WI-FI, plenty power outlets on lamp bases to charge all the "Toys". 5 STAR! Very modern and CLEAN!!

title: “Nice stay, we'll be back!”
text: We have stayed at other Thompson properties and this was equally nice. Nice decor, great location, clean rooms. Really friendly and helpful staff. Reasonable rate.

title: “So many amenities!”
text:
I was so thankful that my boyfriend booked this place for our short last minute vacation in California. 
The location was great, next to a major highway, and was a midpoint between all of our travel destinations north and south.
For the amount of standard/free amenities given, the value for the suite was awesome!
1) Free breakfast everyday - 
Cereal, oatmeal station, waffle maker & batter, pancakes, hashbrowns, potatoes, canadian bacon, bacon, sausage, eggs (cooked in different ways), bagels, muffins, coffee, tea, juice, milk, yogurt, and white rice & miso soup ingredients! Enough variety to make breakfast different everyday!
2) Free dinner everyday - 
We did not partake in this because we were normally out for dinner, but there was a schedule on the refrigerator letting us know what "theme" they had for dinner for which day.
3) Free wi-fi is always good.
4) Don't have to pay for parking (unlike the downtown San Diego hotels).
5) Fitness Center (24 hrs), pool, basketball court, and patio outside.
6) Nearby restaurants walking distance from the hotel.
7) Suite included a full kitchen! (Fridge & freezer, microwave, stove top, dishwasher, sink, cabinet, cutlery, dishes, dish washiing soap, etc.) The only thing NOT there was an oven haha
8) There were many more amenities listed on the fridge we did not use, but were surprised that these services were available: Coin-op laundry facilities, dry cleaning pick-up/drop off, & grocery shopping.
There was a variety of people here. Tourists, families, and business people were eating free breakfast every morning in the large lounge area. This is a great place for anyone.
If we decide to vacation in the San Diego area again, we are definitely coming back here = ) !

title: “wonderful getaway”
text: My husband and I decided to stay at Henderson's for our first anniversary. We wanted to visit the aquarium and other Inner Harbor attractions and had debated about staying here vs staying at a cheaper location and driving in. We decided based on the reviews and the hassle and cost of driving/parking to go ahead and stay. We are so very glad we made that choice and will come back without reservation. It was very restful. Very quiet. We called ahead to ask about an evening activity we were looking into, and the front desk offered to make the calls for us and let us know! The rooms are very comfortable and breakfast was fantastic, and generous. The aquarium was a bit of a walk, but we could have opted for the water taxi. There is plenty of dining nearby. It was a great choice for our anniversary and we hope to return sometime.

title: “Beautiful pools, average rooms”
text:
Overall the property was pretty nice. Great location right on mission bay close to the beach, good sized standard rooms with clean and comfortable beds. Washrooms nice and of good quality. Large plasma screen tvs and good coffee in the makers in each room.
The really nice part were the pools. One very secluded feeling pool w hot tub (shallow) and another near the main area that was very pretty right beside the bay. Both pool areas have very large hot tubs. The Firefly restaurant was really nice and we enjoyed being out at night with the lights. 
would stay there again if we get another good deal!

title: “Clean hotel!”
text: My fiance and I stayed here one night, looking for a clean, resonably priced hotel, close to down town. The room was very clean. The front desk clerk was very friendly, and even recommended a place to eat and gave us directions. The beds were comfortable, and had no problems sleeping!

title: “Detriot Stay Over”
text: This hotel is quite the complex. It feels like the Blade Runner towers as you approach it as it very Modern and the tallest buildings in the area. The staff here is incredibly friendly... from the valet, to the bar staff to room service... we have no complaints. The hotel is on the waterfront and we were lucky enough to be there when there was a festival going on. For the summer months it has rows of patios looking over the river. Great experience! ` the only negative thing is there wasn't a fridge in the room.

title: “Elegant historic hotel in the heart of Chicago”
text:
This hotel is a beautiful restored 1920's club hotel on the corner of Michigan Avenue and Huron, on the "Mag Mile" just two blocks from the Water Tower and the Chicago tourist office. Michigan Avenue buses stop just down the block. At the tourist office we were able to buy transit passes, theatre tickets, and get helpful advice. Good restaurants nearby. Boat tours on the Chicago River were an easy walk away. 
Excellent breakfast buffet and good bar food available in the hotel, which has a business center with Internet connection and a fitness center on the 25th floor. People over 70 may recall that this is where the radio broadcast of Don McNeill's Breakfast Club once originated. For folks from a small town, this felt like our idea of a big city hotel. We loved it.

title: “Great hotel. Easy walk to everything.”
text: We stayed in May for 3 nights and had a great time. The staff were very friendly and helpful. The room was massive with separate bedroom, really great when you have 2 small children. Kitchen was also great, heating bottles and for the quick breakfast before heading out. The biggest plus was the laundry in the basement. I was able to the laundry late at night with no problems. When travelling with kids you need a kitchen and laundry this is why we always stay with the Affinia group. We will be back again next time we come to New York.

title: “Classic elegance and friendly service in the heart of downtown.”
text: My family and I have stayed at this hotel on numerous occasions and love it! The hotel is beautifully appointed and the service has always been friendly and courteous. The only minor issue that we have experienced is the sometimes long wait at the front desk counter. The hotel is located right in the middle of downtown El Paso, within easy walking distance to numerous restaurants, museums, the city's Convention Center and downtown nightlife. The rooms are spacious and well-appointed. The main lobby area is gorgeous, as is the Dome Restaurant. This is always our first choice hotel when we travel to El Paso.

title: “GREAT place to stay!”
text: Stayed here for a convention. Everyone on the hotel staff bent over backwards to ensure that our stay was fabulous! The breakfast and happy hours are wonderful money saving perks. The trolley stops right in front of the hotel which makes traveling around town very easy! Joe, the manager, was outstanding! Will definitely stay there again. :-)

title: “So, I really wanted to love this place...”
text: So, I really wanted to love this place and my initial impression was fantastic. The lobby is beautiful & luxurious and I couldn't wait to check-in and relax in our room. And here's where it all went downhill. The front desk clerk was a little on the snippy side. We were given our keys and sent on our way only to find that she had given us a room with ONE double bed which is not what we had reserved. You would think the front desk clerk would have thought something was amiss when she checked us in. My husband was standing right there and at 6'6 would barely fit in that bed by himself, let alone the both of us. I immediately called down only to be placed on hold for an eternity so the manager could be consulted. The manager never even bothered to speak to us to apologize and had the clerk handle it. I had to tell them that I had the printed documentation/receipts that proved we were guaranteed more than that. At this point, the only room available was a handicapped room with 2 double beds. At least one of us wouldn't have to sleep on the floor. By the way, the first room we were given was quite shabby and on par with a "Days Inn" level. The wallpaper was peeling. The furniture looked old & worn. The second room looked like it was more recently updated but still lacked the oomph that nice hotels should have. It was a failed attempt at replicating the look of Kimpton Hotel properties. The TV was extremely dated. No wifi!!!!!! In this day & age???? And, of course, they charge for it. And they charge for the use of the gym!!!!!! Seriously? How can you give your customer subpar accommodations & claim to be a luxury hotel? The only reason they get 2 stars is because of the lobby, friendly bellmen and location.

title: “Avoid lower floors... especially room 202”
text:
As the most important thing about a Hotel room is how well you sleep; I must give this hotel a low rating. When checking in as a HHonors guest I was informed that I had received a corner room (room 202) due to my status (now only Blue but use to be Gold). Come to find out a subway train will shake this room every 15-30 min (movie plug: see Triplets of Belville minus the dog). When I tried to hook my iPod up to the clock radio to drown out the noise I came to find out that this nor the radio function was working. Thank God their was a free internet connection (even though it was quiet slow) as I was able to download a white noise sleep app for my iPhone that helped a little.
Other than the issue related to the sleeping the hotel was very nicely located in Times Square and had a very nice doorman crew. This may be a really nice hotel experience on the higher floors. Note: the street noise was not the problem; just the subway.
The one other disappointment was when we tried to request a late-check-out I was informed that anything over an hour would cost +$50 and you could not use points to extend your stay, again I guess status is important here as I am a Platinum with SPG and they always let me stay till at least 3PM, even in NYC (Sheraton Manhattan & Four Points Times Square).

title: “Outstanding Hotel”
text: This past stay at the Hotel Commonwealth was once again an outstanding experience. I spent about 2 weeks there and enjoyed every moment. The staff remembered my name from the moment I exited the car, and I felt like I was coming home after a long while away. Everyone was so kind and gracious. My Family had joined me this year and spent a few nights at the establishment, and they too were absolutely impressed with the impeccable service, the friendliness and warmth of the entire staff, and cleanliness of the Hotel. I wanted to note that my parents had just returned from 3 weeks in France staying at some extremely nice properties there, and they had to comment to me that you can spend 5 times more staying at a hotel, but you cannot get the kind of genuine kindness and earnestness to make your stay a perfect one as they experienced at the Hotel Commonwealth. They were very impressed. My brother and his family too enjoyed the stay and wish to return. This is my 9th trip to Boston, and my 9th stay at this Hotel and I am already planning my visit again next year. I want to thank the Hotel Commonwealth for helping to make my family’s and my vacation such an enjoyable, comfortable, and memorable one. This is truly an outstanding hotel!

title: “Terrific, Trendy historic Hotel”
text:
Just returned from a quick trip down the coast to Seattle, we stayed right downtown at Hotel Max as an alternate to our usual Pan Pacific, and were very pleased with a great stay there. The rooms are very well decorated with art by local Seattle artists, a fantastic idea! The beds and rooms were very comfortable and sleep quality was terrific. 
The building is a renovated historic building, they kept a lot of the great original (I believe) features of the building in both exterior and interior. That being said the floor plans didn't leave for much space in the bathroom, but neither of us minded, it had a nice soaker tub though. :)
The desk and bell staff were great hosts, and it was really impressive that the GM emails you post stay to check up.
Would definately return and recommend this hotel to others looking for something trendy in the downtown core.

title: “Great location, pretty balconies, dirty rooms!”
text: We stayed at The Lexington on November 21st for a night in the city to see the Macys' Thanksgiving Day Balloon Inflation and then for the parade. We booked two suites at a very reasonable price of 289. Upon entering the first suite it was obvious that housekeeping does not do a thorough job. The ice bucket was filled with old popcorn kernels from a previous guest. The pullout couch should have been replaced years ago. The cushions sagged into the bed and upon pulling the bed out it was obvious the sheets were not replaced since the previous guest. The room temperature was hard to control and we had to use the air conditioner to offset the heat. The bathroom, for one particular suite was the size of a closet. Where the second one was enormous and completely redone. The second suite was nice and roomy. When we called house keeping they came up when we had left the room and wiped out the ice bucket which upon returning still smelled of popcorn...really!!!
