Manager did the right thing and adjusted the price on the room with all the problems. The view and balcony from both suites was absolutely beautiful though!

title: “Outstanding hotel”
text:
This is by no means a small hotel, yet it has everything you would expect from a small boutique hotel. I must admit I was lucky enough to get one of the premium rooms (there are four of those per floor on the corners of the building), which is actually a spacious suite with separate bedroom, living room and two bathrooms. The huge shower cabins are stunning. Equipment is great with coffee machine, large flat screen TVs, iPod docking station... And bathrobes and slippers are provided, which is so rare in US hotels. Rooms are bright with large windows. Furniture is modern and clean, even if it may be lacking character and style...
Numerous elevators guarantee you never have to wait long despite this being a 12-story building. The lobby and restaurant/bar area are one single open area, but a again a pleasant and bright one. 
Location is central, still quite a few blocks away from Times Square, 5th avenue and other iconic locations but just two blocks away from Madisson Square Garden and Penn Station which is very convenient. While this part of 35th St doesn't look overly attractive it's certainly very safe as the hotel is next to a major police station...
Staff has been very courteous and welcoming. I wish I could have stayed longer.

title: “Beautiful Hotel”
text: Stayed here on business but also was able to enjoy some downtime. Very nice hotel and staff. Close to the Riverwalk, Alamo and other attractions. The hotel restaraunt was above and beyond my expectations; food and service were excellent and nice atmosphere. Lobby bar very young and fun. The staff is very courteous and attentive to guest's needs. The infiniti pool was spectacular and I loved slipping into their super comfy robes after a refreshing shower. Would absolutely stay here again!

title: “Great Value”
text: Clean and comfortable. Courteous service. Great value. Nothing to complain about.

title: “Really Great Location!”
text: This hotel is just one street away from Michigan Ave...The Magnificient Mile and a great location for getting on tours and seeing the city on foot. The morning breakfast on the 6th floor and evening light suppers days Mon-Thur are very convenient as well. It was served in a beautiful room with view of the city. We would difinately used this hotel again!! There are a number of good restaurants in the area as well and it felt safe to be out in the evening.

title: “Great hotel, Great location!!”
text:
We stayed at this hotel twice. Before and after a cruise on the eastern coast. I am a Starwood Prefered Guest and used points, so the room did not cost me anything.
We only stayed one night before boarding our cruise ship. We arrived at the hotel at around 5:00pm and were given a roon quickly. We were placed on the 29th floor. Excellant view in a spacious room. The only thing we did not like was the sink. It is a stainless steel sink which doesn't provide much room for your toiletries. However, they do provide a shelf to put things on. 
The flat screen tv's, heavenly bed and shower were the rooms biggest assests. 
We did eat breakfast at Sula's the next morning, it is located inside the hotel. Very expensive, but you do get a lot of food. I would suggest splitting a meal or go somewhere else. There are several other resturaunts close by that are much cheaper.
After our cruise we returned for a three night stay. This time we were given an upgrade to a 43rd fl corner view room. However, since we arrived early (9:30 am) from the ship, the room was not ready. 
We left our bags with the bellman and decided to go for a walk. However, it was raining. No problem! The hotel offered us use of their umbrellas without even asking. Now that's great service!
When we returned about 1:30 our room was ready. What a fantastic room and view. We did not want to leave. This hotel is in a perfect location. A block from Times Square. A short walk and you are in the middle of everything. Actually the sidewalks are packed, but that's what Times Square is all about, right?
Within the hotel is Chevy's mexican food. Very reasonably priced and good food. There are also theaters in the hotel. 
We did go to Shula's (famous for their steaks) for dinner. The prices are outrageous! It was about $150 for the two of us and that only included one glass of wine, but did include a couple of sides and desert. The sides are huge and should be shared. The desert was fantastic. Just watch out for the prices.
The hotel's location is key. Right across from the port authority and next to the subway. We took the subway down to battery park to catch the ferry to the Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island. If you want to go into the base of the statue, go early as the tickets sell out by 9:00. We then walked to ground zero, to take a moment. We returned to the subway and made our way home. 
Oh, I forgot to mention John's pizza. It is world famous and right around the corner from the hotel. It is so good we ate there twice. 
I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone. If I ever return, I will be staying there again!

title: “Enjoyable stay”
text: Just got back from an enjoyable stay at the Intercontinental. The location was great only one block from the heart of Times Square. Th service was great as when we checked in our room was not ready and they called us when it was (we arrived very early). The room was small (corner room) but the view was fantastic. Very clean and comfortable. The bathroom was very nice. Families note there was no tub. The shower was great and the bath amenities top shelf. The robes were also very comfortable. Very good choice for a romantic weekend.

title: “Good for business trips”
text: I have stayed at this hotel for several business meetings. The hotel has a nice atrium court with a cafe, bar and small market. The cable cars are right out outside of the lobby entrance and most rooms have unobstructed views of the San Francisco bay. This hotel is great for conferences, but I wouldn't stay here for a romantic weekend. The rooms are somewhat bland and there are better hotels in SF with more character (Mark Hopkins, Ritz, Orchard).

title: “Way better than what people may say...!”
text:
Honestly, I almost cancelled my trip to NYC when I read the reviews about the hotel. That would have been a big mistake since me and 4 of my friends spent a very nice - not to mentioned relatively cheap (!) - 3-day weekend in NYC in early March 2011, thanks to Riverside Studios Hotel.
The room is very faded, the paint is old, the carpet is teared up in the corner and the place is a bit noisy, BUT the room is large, clean, includes a fridg and a TV. You share the bathroom, but water pressure is very good and hot water is not a problem. 
Seriously, I think it's hard to ask for more at that price... It cost us 20 $ each per nights (5 adults), all included! All this at a very walkable distance from Times Square and only a few blocks away from a subway station.
I surely recommend this hotel to anyone on a budget who's willing to cut-off a bit of comfort... Couples who are looking for a place to stay for a romantic weekend in NYC should look somewhere else though...!

title: “Good hotel, a little expensive at times”
text: Located in midtown, so for business its perfect. Otherwise the trendy parts of Manhattan are a taxi/subway ride away. The hotel has 3 restaurants, the main one is too expensive, the middle one isn't good, but the bar is pretty decent. The gym has every you would need for a weary business travelers and the rooms are bigger then most New York hotels. If you can attain some status in Hilton Honors you will usually be upgraded.

title: “great location, cheap but i have wifi problem”
text: it is 2 blocks away from Union Square. The price is cheap compare to the great location, and the clean room.

title: “The worst hotel, at this price range.”
text: I don't understand the other reviews. This was a bad hotel. The rooms were not clean, the pool area was a mess with no open seats, the service was below average, even the food in the restaurant was bad. Frankly, of all the hotels I have stayed in the past year (that means about 20), this was the worst!

title: “Awesome value”
text: This hotel was a great value in an excellent location. Walkable to everything. Rooms were nice, beds comfortable, staff really friendly. The only thing I would say could really improve is the water pressure in the shower. Other than that, loved it! But the bathroom was spacious and very clean. I will be back.

title: “Great hotel and location in Chicago”
text: We were pleased with our stay at the Amalfi in Chicago. We booked through Expedia and took a chance based on reviews and all went well. Large room, view of the city, comfortable beds, clean and nice large bathroom. Extras included buffet breakfast on each floor, which was well stocked with cereals, fruit, juice, sticky buns etc. Also, cocktail party each evening at 5:30 pm until 7 ish. Cocktails and appetizers. Staff was great, friendly and helpful. Highly recommend this hotel.

title: “basic and cheap”
text:
I stayed here this past weekend. The location is very convenient. It is walking distance to lots of restaurants, public transit and shopping. 
It is situated at a very busy intersection, so it gets very noisy. I had to use my earplugs to get a good night sleep. It attracts a lot of young guests, so there is a lot of activity and loud music. 
All this to say that this place is not ideal for a family with young children. If you're single and don't mind the noise, then it is a suitable place to stay at. It is cheaper than most places in that neighbourhood. The rooms are very basic. The staff is very friendly and accomodating. The housekeeping staff was also very good. But don't expect any frills. It is as basic as it gets. But it is good for the price.

title: “So-So Hotel w/Great Location”
text:
There are a few good things about this hotel.... location, location, & location. It is close to shopping, the river walk, water taxis, etc. However, the room was only so-so. Great view of the river, but needed some TLC. The bathtub had apparently been painted (used to be blue!) and was peeling. The shower head had a loose part, shower curtain rings broken, and the carpet had a burn mark.
If you decide to stay here, the first thing you want to ask at the desk is, "Is this room near the elevator?" We spent 2 nights in Room 3801 next to the elevator. I'm assuming the elevator is old because it clunked and bonged all night long. I am one of those people who unpack everything and didn't want to move all my stuff for only one additional night's stay, so tolerated it the 2nd night. When I was checking out I found it very interesting that the clerk did not ask how my stay was, while the person checking out next to me was asked by the other clerk. I'm sure they don't bother to ask those who got stuck in an "elevator room."

title: “Trump Soho Awesome”
text: Just stayed at Trump Soho this past weekend for two nights. Every detail was accounted for and all the staff were attentive and kind. Great Soho neighborhood and hotel is clean and beautiful. We had a great time at the pool as well. You can't go wrong here.

title: “A Chicago landmark worth a visit”
text:
This hotel is for you if:
You want to be near Michigan Ave Shopping district
You like old school grand hotels. The original Fairmont in SF comes to mind as a good comparison. 
You are not on a budget - though the price isn't bad for a downtown hotel in a major city.
This hotel is not for you if:
You need to be a short walking distance to the central business district - The Loop/Wacker Drive is a 10 minute, $10 cab ride - it would be at least a 20 minute walk for most people. In a Chicago winter that can be a long walk.
If you have a fear of elevators. They are old and make noises. I have no such phobia, but man, if I did, I would need to be sedated. Seriously, if this is even sort of an issue for you, get a lower floor room. About half the elevators have a couch in them, which is pretty awesome. 
I enjoyed my stay here a great deal. So some of this is a little nit-picky. If you are a light sleeper - try and get a non- connecting room. I could hear my neighbor on the phone and watching TV. My room looked out over Lake Shore Drive, which gives you a great view, but you could also hear the traffic on Lake Shore Drive. 
This property actually has a mini-bar! Many properties have done away with the mini-bar, so its like spotting a rare bird.
Three full service restaurants on property, and a cafe. Plus the Palm Court for afternoon tea. With live harp music. The Coq D'Or is a classic old school cocktail lounge with dark wood and leather chairs. They have a smaller menu, but the food is good. Drinks are not cheap - about 8 for a beer, 11 for a cocktail, but again, not out of line with a downtown hotel bar. 
My bathroom was huge. I appreciate this. The room itself was spacious - often older properties have really small rooms. Like the aforementioned Fairmont in SF and the Mayflower in DC. 
The coffee bar on the lower level had good food and a good latte, but dear lord, it was super slow. And I visited three times, at different times of day. 
This property is a block away from American Girl Place - if you have a little girl you wish to spoil, this is a great place to stay. Make sure to make reservations for tea.

title: “The best of the best”
text: We spent 11 nites at the Pacific Terrace, it is difficult to find 1 thing lacking at this hotel, beyond excellent staff with knowledge in all areas, a great breakfast buffet, very clean, and so close to the beach. This is where I would stay again and again. The personal attention paid to each and every guest was excellent. Thanks for the wonderful time.

title: “Great staff and excellent location!”
text: Great location that is within walking distance to Times Square, Fifth Ave shopping & Central Park. Staff is outstanding! Room decor is a bit outdated but very spacious rooms for New York City.

title: “Brillant”
text: I stayed in this hotel from the 20th to the 27th november this year 2012 which was only last week. It was me and my girlfriends first time to new york and america. As soon as we arrived at the hotel we were greated and made welcome. We were checked in and out by a lovely and polite woman called Ellen who put us up on the 25th floor in a very spacious room, with an excellent view. This room was ready for us straight away and she rang a few moments after to make sure everything was ok. The room was always cleaned when we left in the morning and when we came back it was spotless. After we settled in we went down to the concierge desk to book our week with shows, sports and everything else new york has to offer. The receptionist called Hector and the woman who works with him (forget her name) were unbelievably helpfull and step by step helped us book everything and plan our stay which was the best week ive ever had and also my girlfriends. Massive thank you to them and all the staff who work there. We would recommend this hotel to anybody and we will definitely be going back to new york and staying here again.

title: “Every time we stay Magnolia exceeds our expectations!”
text: Every year my husbands company has a party downtown. I enjoy the ambiance and service that comes from Magnolia so much more than that of major hotel chains. Even with all the commotion from the events that were occurring the staff is still willing to provide excellent service. We were craving hot chocolate at 1230am and needed milk...even though the room service was closed they still helped us out. Awesome staff and beautiful hotel!!!

title: “Wlecome To New York”
text: I had some reservations about booking this hotel. I thought the photo's they have posted looked a little shabby. But there was nothing to worry about. Having visited New York several times this was the best hotel I've visited. Everything worked here. The impressive lobby, the relaxing piano bar, friendly accomodating staff and excellent rooms. It also hosted the fastest checkin/out in the whole city. Dont forget your in New York so request a high floor room and breath in the view of the Big Apple.

title: “Good value for DC”
text:
This is the only place that seems to charge less than $200/night on most nights - a major plus in seriously-overpriced DC. If you manage your expectations & remember this is a Days Inn, not the Four Seasons, you'll be fine. The location is very good: a quick 5-10 min walk to the Van Ness metro station, which zips you into the heart of DC in just 15-20 minutes. (And contrary to a previous reviewer, Van Ness is a relatively safe DC neighborhood - I should know, I used to live there & I'm picky about such things). There's a grocery store (Giant) and CVS pharmacy about 1 block away, and a few average restaurants (Potbelly, Subway, Epicurean, a pizza place across the street). 
Other pros: The rooms are decently-sized, lots of linen, free WiFi in every room (major plus if I'm working), good blackout curtains. I've also stayed here multiple times in the past year, and don't recall ever seeing one of those paper-thin, between-room-doors that allow you to hear your neighbor's every snore and sigh.
Some cons: The front desk tries to be helpful, but most of the time the staff seem a bit stressed and clueless. They also once had an issue with the card key machine and it took more than 10 minutes to page someone to let me into my room (when the guy finally showed up, he just joked in Spanish with the rest of the staff and didn't even apologize) - not that pleasant at 10pm after a long day of work/traveling. But these are minor cons in the large scheme of things - I still prefer staying here to most other DC hotels because of the good value and location.

title: “A great long weekend at the Conrad!”
text: Great stay at the Conrad Chicago for our 1 year anniversary. Lovely accomodations with an excellent location for all the city of Chicago has to offer!

title: “A true San Francisco experience!”
text: The Sir Fancis Drake was a true San Francisco experience, glamerous yet warm and hospitable. I was there on business but brought along my Mother and girls (age 7 & 8) The staff was very helpful while I was unable to assist my family. The location is perfect, we school clothes shopped on the square, road the trolly to peir 39 and it was an easy travel to the zoo for my mother and the girls. The room was very clean and a stylish design. Also, I was pleased in the staff''s ability to multi-task and provide excellent service to a packed house. I highly reccomend this hotel!

title: “The Pennsylvania ?”
text: Ok so heres the thing. You have travelled to New York, you're excited, buzzing with sensory overload , the buildings are tall, no HUGE, the traffic crazy, the people "colorful". You pull up outside what appears to be a serious contender of a hotel, you walk into the lobby, WOW. This could be it, you might have just found the bargain of a lifetime right here in New York City !!! You check in, sooo excited and cant wait to see the room, open the door and .............. Aww its not what you expected. .. Ok so the rooms, or at least the one I stayed in was very big. However it was sooo basic and tired looking. I'd say it wasn't too clean either. Would I say I was let down?? maybe not.... its all started to come back to me. I got an excellent rate for a hotel that covers your basic needs, its in a seriously good location, walking distance to Times Square, right around the corner from the Empire state building. And you know what its in NEW YORK CITY the Grrreatest City in the world!!. Honestly when you travel to NY you should forget what the hotel is like, you will be only minimal time there and after a day or night in the big apple you would sleep on a bed of nails if that all that was available. If you want to see NY and are easy about the hotel then the penn is for you.

title: “Not your typical Radisson”
text:
I stayed at this hotel recently and it was a big mistake. The hotel is dated and most (not all) of the staff at the front desk really lack sense of customer service. Especially this front desk person who worked the evening of Dec 2nd. I had left my luggage with them as I had checked out that morning but the flight was not until 7PM. We both went to a room where all the luggage was held and it was dark in there, so he turned the light on. I am guessing the bulbs are the new ones where they take some time to warm up and glow. This man not realizing that it was the bulbs, asked me very rudely, to move away and not block his view. He grunted at me and acted like a child...did he forget that I am not a family member but a customer!!!
The room was nothing to write home about either. Each part of the shower, was different. They must have replaced each part as they went bad.
It appears that Southwest staff stays here when in San Jose, unless they have a special floor, I think the SW employees are also getting a raw deal. 
The only good thing was t he number bed and t he quality of the towels. So I gave them 2 out of 5. Stay somewhere else!!!!!!!!

title: “Convenient location, wonderful staff!”
text:
This hotel is very conveniently situated in walking distance to Millenium Park, the Magnificent Mile and the riverfront walk. Other than going south to the museums, no cab was needed. Our room was quiet, roomy, and nicely appointed. Very clean. We dined at the lobby bar which has a lovely view of both the city and atrium lobby. The food was very decent, and the staff very friendly.
We were there for a large group convention and the staff managed the large crowds with ease. Very happy with our stay and would definitely at this Hyatt location again!

title: “One of the best hotels in NY”
text:
The service was amazing, the rooms had good veiws over the city, with many lifts in the hotel, it took no time to get up to the rooms. It had a good posh feel, but not too pricey. Although the cost of the meals in hotel are something to look out for.
All round though and enjoyable expirence and would definetly go bakc again

title: “FANTASTIC Location, AWESOME Service, ADORABLE Style”
text: My husband and I (late 20's, early 30's) totally enjoyed our stay at The Farmer's Daughter! This hotel is not your normal high rise, it only has 3 stories and it's definitely far away from the hotel chain standard. It's quaint decor is shabby chic and if you're looking for luxury, you won't find it here, however if you're looking for a FANTASTIC location, AWESOME service, and ADORABLE style then The Farmer's Daughter will be just as perfect for you as it was for us! The staff is super helpful with printing maps, making reservations...etc and will be more than able to answer any of your traveling questions! The rooms were fairly quiet and we enjoyed the renovated motel to hotel. I will most certainly stay here again and recommend this to anyone who is a Price Is Right hopeful or looking to lots of shopping/eating at The Grove! My husband and I were able to do everything on our list from this great location and we look forward to our next stay here!

title: “Cost-effective and brilliant hotel with some little minuses”
text:
We had a Superior Queen room and it was in our opinion roomy and cosy. The condition of room was very good and we liked room's modern decoration. I'm always a little bid mad of cleaning. That's why I have to say once again the room was pretty clean but anyhow especially the floor could have shined more. We saw one cockroach in our room during the week we spent there but it wasn't a big deal.
Bahtroom was also roomy and nice. 
The only minus comes from AC, it was pretty loud.
Some one could also think it is a minus that only 2 of 3 elevators has been working past couple of years even there is a label on wallet that one elevator is out of order just temporarely. Anyway two elevators is enough for this hotel.
The hotel staff was very friendly and helpfull. We have just positive memories of them.
The location at upper West Side is perfect. The nearest subway is almost at next door. There are lot of good restaurants and breakfast places nearby.

title: “Perfect for what it is.”
text: I arrived early to start my work day and asked to check my bag. The desk already had rooms available and promptly checked me in! Very impressed. Was given a room on a high floor that had everything I needed: nothing more, nothing less. Service was warm and friendly always and nights were quiet. All of this at a terrific rate. I will definitely be back - when it's not sold out!

title: “Not in the Best Part of Town”
text:
This Marriott is rather dated and could use some remodeling. The bed was extremely comfortable but the wallpaper was falling off and the carpet is old and worn. Front desk staff very friendsly and helpful. 
Not in the best part of town. I ventured out looking for some stores/restaurants using my GPS and very quickly drove into some scary/questionable areas. Not close to downtown or the major malls. I'll probably choose another area of Indy next time.

title: “Great for Fenway!”
text:
We picked this hotel since we had tickets to three games at Fenway. Our last experience in Boston was that it can be difficult to get a cab back to the main hotel area. This location was perfect - a six minute walk to the game. You can see Fenway from some of the hotel windows. 
Hotel is top notch - lovely rooms, great service. Very clean, all the amenities. 
My only negative comment is that room service (provided by Eastern Standard - a very good restaurant in the hotel) and the menu is a bit limited after 11 pm. We also liked the oyster bar restaurant. 
Overall a very good stay although I'm not quite sure why it's the top rated hotel in Boston - if we weren't going to baseball, we would have thought it was a bit out of the way! However, it is only a five or ten minute walk to Newbury Street. 
We would stay again - especially if we were going to multiple baseball games.

title: “Upscale place, Great Location”
text:
This place offers a wonderful location on 57 between Park and Lexington. 2 Blocks to the subway on 59th. Very clean and easy access. A little on the Modern/Euro side. There is also a roof top bar. 
This is a Marriott, so your points can apply. 
.

title: “Not your average boutique hotel”
text: It's not a boutique hotel at all, and it's not a Marriott or chain-like in any way. This will satisfy all of your hipster yearnings, from the modernist furnishings to the lack of elevators and boxed water. Good beds, sheets, pillows, towels, and a very happening neighborhood if you want to party with the twenty to thirty-somethings. Breakfast is in the basement and is self serve, including make your own waffle. The coffee is not strong enough, but it's all you can drink. We would stay here again.

title: “Favorite Hotel in DC!”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Hotel Lombardy when we were in town for a concert at the Kennedy Center. The hotel staff is polished, professional, friendly and attentive. They were always ready to hold the door, hail a cab, or give directions.
This boutique hotel was immaculate, like something right out of a movie! Our room was somewhat small, but stunning. And I have never seen a hotel bathroom so clean! The plush king bed was extremely comfortable, and we could not hear a sound from the city outside the entire night. Thick curtains blocked out almost all light -- what a great night's sleep!
The Hotel Lombardy is convenient to just about anything -- a 10 minute walk to the Kennedy Center, 2 blocks from the Foggy Bottom metro, 4 blocks from the White House... With tons of great, reasonably-priced places to eat, due to the nearby universities.
One word of warning -- Be patient with the elevators. They are hand-operated by the hotel staff, so it may take a minute for them to get to you. Definitely a unique feature of this hotel, I have never seen something like this before! My husband and I found this a treat, despite the brief wait.
Overall, I would strongly recommend this hotel to anyone wishing to stay in the Georgetown area of DC. We booked our room on Expedia, and it was only about $100 / night, plus $30 / night valet parking. Especially at such a low price, this was one of the best hotels we have ever stayed at.

title: “Small but efficient”
text:
Our family of 4 just stayed at "Your Stay Broadway Apartments" December 25th through the 29th. It was alot better than I expected after reading alot of the reviews. We had 2 adults and 2 teenagers, boy and girl. The check-in was very fast and effecient and they let us check in before 3:00. We rented a one bedroom studio apt, so it was alittle small for 4 grown people. It did have a queen size bed with not very good pillows and a couch that made into a double or queensize bed also. Since we had teenagers who did not want to sleep with anyone we had an air mattress which took up alot of room. We were unable to get a rollaway bed. The kitchen area was small but clean with great appliances. The TV was great and it did have internet access which we used quite a bit to look up places to eat. The only real complaint I had was the heater in the room. It did not have a thermostat so the room was either too cold or too hot. It was pretty quiet considering it was right in the busy part of Manhattan. The location was great, right by a subway station! I also did requesat another blanket for the air mattress and we got it right away. It is a great place for 2 people or 4 people with small children. Feel free to e-mail me if you have anymore questions. 
Burkefan06@cox.net

title: “Disappointing”
text:
This hotel was such a disappointment, given that it is in such a great location. Leaving aside the fact that it really is now quite dated in its decor ( I think we have all moved on from the "groovy" OO's style), the reception staff were rude and disinterested, as were the Wet area staff. One got the impression that they were only there to service those who were of interest to them and worthy of their attention. The concierge on the other hand was terrific- very knowledgable and keen to assist, as were the door men, all of whom were very helpful. 
Better attention needs to be paid to the cleanliness of the place - a vaccuum of the corridors would be a nice touch!
It is in a great location, away from the craziness of Hollywood etc and close to shops and restaurants, but serious attention needs to be given to a number of key areas ( staff in particular) before I would recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: “Best kept secret in S.F.”
text: Stayed at The Orchard Hotel the end of August. A real hidden jewel! Friendly staff, great room decor & immaculate; would definitely stay again & recommend it. Also, in a great area.

title: “Wasn't Impressed”
text:
My Husband and I stayed for 1 night in between travel on our way home (We stayed at the Marriott Marina Del Ray on the way out, which was great). We arrived early after taking a 9hr red eye flight, so needless to say we were exhausted. The gentleman who checked us in was gruff, short and unfriendly. We knew we were very early but were hoping we could check in so we could sleep for a few hours. We did end up getting a room, but he wasn't pleasant about it at all. 
On the plus side the shuttle from LAX was nice, we never had to wait more than 10- 15 minutes. The hotel isn't really near much but we took a cab to Manhattan Beach, which was nice. Had a lot of great restaurants and shops. We had lunch in the hotel restaurant (Champions was only open at 4pm for dinner) and it wasn't that bad. Next time we'll prob check out the Courtyard or Renaissance.

title: “"But we don't have any suites" be warned! Inadequate laundry, too”
text: Booked an executive suite over the phone, at higher cost than standard room, when arrived were given key to a grim, ghastly, rundown two double-bedded room, not the two room suite we had expected. Went back to reception to be told "but we don't have any suites in this hotel"(with a straight face). Stood my ground, reminding them what their website claims, and was eventually given... surprise, surprise, a two room "executive suite" as booked. The standard rooms look nothing like the pictures on the website, and the sofabed in the suite was the saggiest and squeakiest we encountered on our holiday. Breakfast was as bad as other reviewers have said (toast and bagels only), but diner next door is okay breakfast option. Laundry totally inadequate - a single washing machine and drier, for perhaps eighty to a hundred rooms.

title: “Reasonable, personable”
text: At top of hill at Dupont Circle area, this small hotel is warm and friendly. The entrance for cars is a little confusing, but the valets and bellmen are excellent. About five blocks from the subway, it is in a good neighborhood with restaurants about two blocks away that are interesting and ethnic. Prices for DC are good, and the rooms are clean and comfortable. My room was not made up when I arrived back at 3:30PM, but two super-efficient housekeepers arrived and made everything neat in short order. Elevators are quick, and service is too. I would stay there again.

title: “Great View”
text: We had a room on the 29th floor and loved the view. You could see the Space Needle, the Pike Place Market sign and the sound. Our suite had plenty of room and the service was great.

title: “Brilliant holiday, poor hotel”
text:
After discovering tripadvisor a week before a friend and I were due to fly out to New York I was very worried, but I thought as long as we felt safe (as we are not even in our twenties) and our room was clean it would be OK. I suppose the one good thing was that when we got there I was expecting the worst - and that was what we got. Having checked in we went in the lift to our room on the third floor. As soon as the lift doors opened the smell hit us - it was terrible - like it hadn't been cleaned for years. However as we knew we were only going to be in the corridors for a short amount of time each day, we tried to over look it and proceeded to our room. Walking down the corridors, the carpets were stained, as were the walls, in addition to which the doors of the rooms were mouldy and broken - I can now also see what other tripadvisors meant when they said the doors looked like coffins. When we found our room it was dark and dingy, the beds hadn't been made and there was used towels all over the bathroom. I felt quite sure this would happen - it would seem it happens to most people. We then went back to reception where we were allocated a new room, but recieved no appolgy for the state of the original room. When we got to the new room on floor seven, the room was notabley better, which seems unfair on those who are on lower (worse) floors and have paid the same price. However, this is not to say that our room was nice, although the lighting was better, the main lamp did not work. I notice some people have commented that they had stained curtains - we didn't even have curtains. The bathroom was by far the WORST part of the hotel, there was a hole in the ceiling, the bath was literally flaking away, and it was hit or miss as to whether or not our water was BROWN. In terms of the staff, some were very friendly and helpful, others weren't - either way do not always trust what they tell you as we were informed that the shuttle bus back to the airport would take about a hour/hour and a half tops - it took over two. I would also recommend to avoid the rip off prices in the shop, a few stamps, a drink and a chocolate bar cost me $14.
If like us you are booked into The Pennsylvania Hotel and are now very concerned about what you have read, try not to worry too much, despite everything that I have told you above, we still had a GREAT holiday, aided by the hotel's brillant location (it's best feature). At the end of the day, we just laughed about it and got on with enjoying our holiday.

title: “Nice hotel. I would stay here again.”
text: Nice hotel, good location, and very clean. I would definitely stay here again when I'm here in San Diego.

title: “One word can sum my experience up - AMAZING!”
text: When I stumbled in awkwardly with quite a few shopping bags, I was immediately greeted by the assistant general manager, Carlton. He was very friendly, professional in manners, and helpful (he even offered to bring my bags up for me). I didn't have reservations because it was a last minute overnight stay in the city. He set me up with a nice king size bed - in a quiet corner room. The bathroom was clean (stocked with bath and body products - one of my favorite brands), bed was extremely plush and comfortable, temperature was perfect (didn't need to adjust at all) and a 32 inch flat panel HD TV kept me entertained. I slept like a baby and checkout went smoothly in the morning. Before leaving, I had asked his staff for suggestions on great eats around the area (supplied me with quite a few options). This hotel even had a Starbucks, literally, a few feet from the elevators (perfect for my morning coffee addiction)!! Rates was reasonable for this stay, especially for a king size bed!

title: “great spot lovely people super clean.”
text: we stayed several nights and really enjoyed this location. the staff was helpful an friendly. you can even check your luggage in early a huge plus for travellers from afar. The rooms and baths were extremely clean. therooms are tiny but really all you need for this super location. complete with a fan and hbo they offered more privacy than expected.

title: “Cant go wrong here !! worth every penny !!”
text:
Just spent 3 nights at the Courtyard Marriott . All I can say is it was worth every penny . I thought the rooms were a decent size , very very clean , very nice in general . Solid walls , so you didnt hear anything else going on next store , or in the hall. The bathroom was very large for a hotel , not to mention the shower was very soothing . The Bed ???? geeeeeeeesh was it every comfortable . The only other time I have stayed in a bed this comfortable was in the Hyatt Regency in Maui ( but that cost me 325.00 a night ) I fell asleep every night before 10 which is unreal for me , but the bed was so comfortable I couldnt help it . 
They have a great buffet in the morning for breaksfast . Quite a spread they put on . I am talking waffles , eggs , omeletes , ham , sausage , bacon , fruts , yogurts , toasts , bagels , everything you can think of . I cant possibly think of a single bad thing to say about my stay at the Courtyard . From the minute I walked in , until the minute I left it was truly a pleasure being there . If you are caught in between a list of hotels to stay in while visiting San Diego , take my word on it that the Courtyard Marriott is a no brainer !!! for about 100 a night good luck trying to find something better . Absolute slam dunk !!!! And believe me I travel a lot , and I dont give good reviews to just any hotel.......

title: “Convenient downtown location”
text: Stayed here during American Society Clinical Oncology Annual Convention June 2012. Came in by Chicago Transit train from O'Hare - $2.25 includes one transfer. In spite of doing my homework, I couldn't find the hotel from the Clark/Lake CTA station! Walked round in a circle, asked a couple of people and then found it. It's not actually on the Miracle Mile, just a couple of blocks away. Reception staff very pleasant. Room key system was new to me and they should have explained it to first-timers. You have to "flash" your key in front of elevator call button to get it to respond, and similar arrangement for hotel room access, except door opens as soon as you flash your card. I was looking for the receptacle to insert the card. Quite frustrating standing there trying to gain room access! I probably seemed stupid to those familiar with the system, but it IS different from standard door entries! Room comfortable ++. WiFi included in room rate, which was "rack rate" for Convention - a hefty $259 + tax. SBux didn't open until 7 am which was after my departure time for the Convention Centre. That was the only breakfast option. My room-mate took advantage of the Gym facilities and gave them a good report. Main plus is walking distance to Miracle Mile and the Loop. Free shuttle bus to Navy Pier 100 yards from front door. It’s well worth a visit. Took a harbor boat trip to get a great view of Chicago skyscrapers from Lake Michigan. Safe walk back to the hotel. Lots of eating options close by. Top-line steak house on main floor was always busy, which suggests it’s good. Cowboy statue at restaurant entrance was like John Wayne. Redline subway literally on the street corner by the hotel. Altogether convenient, but nothing spectacular for the $$$$.

title: “Best hotel stayed in!”
text: I have to say this hotel exceeded my expectations. I was a little apprehensive due to getting such a good deal online for a basic double. 380 pounds for three nights in a five star hotel was great! The location was v good only a five min walk to the metro and many restaurants just outside the hotel. We went to the Mexican across the road which was lovely!! The hotel itself was very clean modern and luxurious. The room was massive for a basic double. Aveda toiletries very nice touch. The free wine hour was a fantastic little extra. Bar and restaurant area beautifully decorated although we didn't actually eat at the restaurant. The staff were friendly and helpful. This hotel is by far the nicest hotel I have ever stayed in and I would definately reccommend this hotel. Thanks for a wonderful stay!!

title: “Really Nice but busy”
text: We stayed at the JW Marriott in July. The resort is very tastefully decorated. It is a very large resort, which is both a pro and a con. there is everything available to do there, but I was surprised at how many of the activities were at an additional fee. We couldn't believe how busy the pool was. Call well in advance if you want to reserve a cabana by the pool. The pool area is enormous. My biggest disappointment was how dirty the pool area was. Went down in the early morning and they had not cleaned around the pool from the day before. There was food and empty cups everywhere. the ground was sticky from people spilling drinks. We were there on a holiday weekend, I am assuming they do a better job when it is not so busy. I would recommend going there off season, I have a feeling it would be much more enjoyable.

title: “Everyone is a VIP”
text: In traveling for business and simultaneously apartment-hunting, I was on one of the most hectic trips of my life and could not have been more thankful that I was staying at the Tribeca Grand. After having to extend my stay at the absolute LAST minute multiple days in a row, I was never left in a position of having to change rooms and the front desk even honored the initial rate I had secured, even though I had booked it on a travel site and their actual rate was increasing. I'm sure had I been staying at any other hotel, I would have encountered countless issues with the rate, the room availability and the check-out times. The only "problem" during my entire stay was that there wasn't an upgraded room when I checked in, but I was immediately moved the next day into the room I had requested and comped drinks at the lounge (which happens to be one of the best spots in the city to mingle) for the inconvenience. By the second day, everyone on staff already knew my name and were some of the friendliest and most helpful hotel employees I've ever encountered on all of my travels. The Sunday brunch at Church lounge is already famous locally, and lived-up to it's reputation. To top it all off, the hotel actually gifted me the pet goldfish from my room as a companion for my new apartment! Even though I'll be living in the city, I'm sure I'll be visiting the hotel regularly just for the great atmosphere and people.

title: “Amazing Level of Service”
text:
I can't say enough great things about our stay here. We had a block of rooms for our wedding weekend and everyone received exceptional service. From the moment of check in, to the room service, housekeeping, bellman, bar staff, event managers, etc, everything was handled impeccably and with a wonderful welcoming atmosphere. No request we made was too big or too small--and we made a lot! Absolutely exceptional service by people who seemed to enjoy their work!
The standard rooms seemed very nice, but small as would be expected in a hotel of this age. We had a suite, which was very reasonably priced and absolutely huge, so that may be a good option for those looking for more space.

title: “great location; worth the parking spot alone”
text: We stayed here over Memorial Day weekend. Location is right on the beach. The location is perfect if you're going with a group of friends for the weekend. I was surprised that it was fairly quiet considering our room was right above the pool. Room was spacious and clean. May be more appropriate for a younger couple/group. Parking was $17/night which is very reasonable considering finding parking in PB is nearly impossible. The only negative thing about the hotel is that the jacuzzi seemed very unsanitary - we all needed showers afterwards because there was a stench that the water left us with.

title: “Nice little hotel”
text:
We selected this Hotel based on the Tripadvisor reviews (comparing price and quality). The Hotel is very reasonable. It is clean (but could be a bit cleaner/fresher) and the rooms are nicely decorated (Asian). The location is good. At walking distance from the Union Square (approx. 10 minutes) and not too far from the Bay. 
There is a Parking next door. The restaurant serves very good breakfast.

title: “Lower your expectations and you'll love it”
text:
This is a funny one.
The hotel really is cheesy but you know to expect that really. What I didn't expect was the tiredenss and somewhat crummyness of the rooms, and more so, the food and beverage service which was pretty dreadful. It seemed like a hotel with a glorious past, that has fallen on hard times. This contrasted heavily with the warmth of the staff, who were to a person, exceptional. 
The rooms - suites - were certainly enormous - but you felt that cringe feeling that while superficially clean, it really was a bit dingy and the sheets and blankets were ancient. The least appealing fact was that the corridors smelt dank - as if they'd had years old alcohol spillages - and the elevator was creaky and slow to the point of thanking your lucky stars you made it out of it! The shop is great. Didn't use the pool but have to admit its a smile winner.
Breakfast is all in and eat as much as you like, though what's on offer isn't that appetising. Donuts, grits, and cold stuff. The fact that your cups plates and cuttelry is plastic is a bit offputting however - same for the burger the night before (which was very unimpressive). This dining [------]area feels more than a bit crummy - though I have to admit the continual big screen video loops of elvis concerts do get you in the mood. 
However again - the warmth and friendliness of the staff made up for a lot. Two told me it is due for major rennovations and there is rumour that there is to be a new hotel built so watch this space.
Having said all of this, I would recommend a stay - just important to have moderate expectations. In fairness the prices are good - we booked online for the all-in graceland package and suite. The piece de resistance is the proximity to Graceland and staying at heartbreak links in beautifully to that experience. The five minute walk over to the Graceland welcome area through the car lot seems strange, but the sight of the Lisa Maria Jet soon has you i intrigued. I canot praise the Graceland facility enough - the staff are fantastic (and getting the graceland package at the heartbreak is a good idea as its great to be able to go to the special and much shorter line to pick up your pass). You are then welcomed and bused across the road to Graceland, and the tour, taken at your own pace with the use of all-in audio guide headphones - is truely warm, intimate and informative. You are free to linger and appreciate the space, and even as a not-particulalry strong Elivs fan, I found it a brilliant expereince. I can't recommend it enough.
One last big thumbs up to the Heartbreak - the courtesy van to the airport is a fantastic touch and was very much appreciated. It came the minute we asked for it, and our driver was a sweetheart and without any cheese, gave us a sense that he was proud of the Graceland expereince and Elvis legacy for his town - and why wouldn't he be.

title: “MORE LIKE A YOUTH HOSTEL THAN A HOTEL”
text:
Where do I start...........this place is a joke
Booked this supposedly hotel for me and my partner due to the reviews, what a BIG mistake. As soon as we got there we looked at each other and regretted it, we are in our 30's so we are not old, stuck up or prudish. We walked in and was greeted by very loud music and loads of young adults (18-21) everywhere. Anyway regretably we checked in and within 30 mins checked back out. Our room was tiny with no privacy in the bathroom not even a door, just a curtain. The bed is sat up so when you have laid it out you are crawling over each other to get round the room. The walls are paper thin that we could hear people in the next room and EVERYTHING they were doing (if you catch my drift). 
When we checked out was told by a the reception staff that I would receive a refund due to it not living up to the reviews and we left and checked in to alot nicer place. It wasn't until driving away that you notice it is in a very dingy part of town where i would not feel comfortable walking out in the dark, alot of shops are boarded up people hanging on the corners of streets and would take approx 20 mins or more to get to time square at least. The hotel have refused to refund me so am now taking it further due to the reviews of it being a stylish hotel near times square that is a complete and utter joke!!!!!! I would not recommend this to families or anyone that would want to enjoy there stay but only suitable for a very tight budget, between the ages of 17-21 and you are really not fussy at all as we would of rather stayed in a tent as there would of been more space... we are just glad that we were able to find somewhere much more suitable and right near macys for the same kind of price that this hostel had charged us

title: “Still Our Favourite SF Hotel!”
text:
Over the past five years, my husband and I have stayed at this inn whenever possible (ie are able to snag a good deal!). It is our hotel of choice because:
- all staff, from desk manager to housekeeping ladies, are friendly and helpful
- perfect location: right at Union Square. Saks and flagship Williams Sonoma in the next block
- complementary continental breakfast is fresh and delicious (hard-boiled eggs, assorted breads and pastries, yogurt, cereals)
- atmosphere is calm, intimate and elegant, without being toffee-nosed!
- clean, relaxing rooms, decorated in golds and reds -- while downtown SF hotels are usually on the small size, have never felt cramped in this hotel's rooms
- nice business room with one internet station & printer
To the management and staff: we really appreciate staying at your lovely hotel, thanks and look forward to seeing you again!

title: “Great value”
text:
Clean, comfortable and spacious room.
Staff friendly and helpful.Good sports bar.
In a quiet area, but only 20 minutes by bus to the very centre of town.
Thoroughly enjoyed my stay and would recommend this hotel.

title: “What a sincere little hotel!”
text: The concierge and reservations staff greeted us upon our arrival with sincerity and warmth. They provided outstanding advice and service throughout our stay. The rooms in the King George reminded me of rooms I have had in Rome and Paris -- small, but charming. Despite the fact that neither room had a view, I very much enjoyed this hotel and would stay there again.

title: “Exorbitant Luxury”
text:
I was very excited to be staying at the Fairmont, until I got there. After having dealt with Fairmont Royal York in Toronto for years, I was sure I wouldn't regret my choice.
The room was very luxurious with a king size bed, and wonderful sheets and pillows. Exactly as described in the website. The temperature in the room was just right, and the view of the city was great! But that's all you got for your money. None of the standard items were included. If you wanted your morning coffee, you had to call in-room dining, and be charged $6USD a person for the delivery plus the cost of the coffee. The water in the room was $6USD as well, so if you're thirsty, it's the tap water from the bathroom. YUCK!
I had pre-arranged for a crib for my 10 week old son, and was advised upon checking in the crib was already in the room. Except when we got there, it wasn't there. When called, a hospitality staff brought an assembled Graco Pack N Play, and dropped it unceromoniously in the room. If I had known that was what my son would be sleeping in, I would've brought my own from home!
I do have to complement the chef on the dinner we had the first night. We had in-room dining, and it was fantastic. The couscous was perfectly spiced, and the steak was just right! If only the proper steak knife had been provided! It was an adventure trying to cut the steak with what I could only call a pointy butter knife!
Overall I was very disappointed with my stay at the Fairmont. Instead of feeling pumpered as I expected, I felt gouged. I wouldn't be staying at the Fairmont again.

title: “Average hotel in a bad location”
text:
To be clear, this is the Holiday Inn Express at Silverlake, not Hotel 250 at silverlake, not sure why the confusion on the name. Even the shuttle service from the airport also had a hard time figuring out what hotel I was seeking transportation to, even though the hotel referred me to their service. They had to go by the street address.
Girl at check-in was very friendly and helpful as were all the other staff I encountered. Rooms were clean. Parking was sufficient. Hotel was quiet during my stay. The room was very simple with no frills. You get the basic amenities but nothing more. I think the rooms could use a bit of remodeling to feel a bit more accomodating. I was on the fifth floor, and the outside walkway faced right into the hillside and wasn't well lit at night...but at least it was quiet and not facing a noisy road. My other view was a portion of roof then Rt101. When the haze lifted enough, I was just able to make out the Hollywood sign on the distant hills. 
The biggest con: Location location location. At first I did not rent a car thinking I could just take the metro to the LA Convention Center since it was only two blocks away. One look at the neighborhood and I opted for the rental car. There were some homeless hanging out near the hotel and it wasn't the kind of neighborhood I would feel safe walking in well after dark. The good news in all of this is that the hotel is set up upon a hill so there is a buffer zone between the neighborhood and the hotel property. But if staying here, plan on renting a car or taking a taxi. 
Overall, generally pretty average. Other than the location I had no major complaints. At the same time, the services offered were just the bare bones, and the only real compliment I could give is that their front desk service was friendly. Bottom line: stay here if on a budget or having trouble finding room elsewhere. But look somewhere a bit nicer first if you can afford it.

title: “Never again.”
text: This is the first time I have stayed at Comfort Suites and I will not stay there again. One of the reasons I chose the hotel was for the swimming pool. I had my 4 children with me and the heater to the pool was currently broke. The breakfast was poor. It was the same thing all 4 days I was there. The microwave in the room didnt work and had to be replaced. I had to call for housekeeping to come take dirty linens and trash. The refrigerator in the room was at room temp and did not keep our food cold. The ONLY thing I complained about was the pool and the fact that my children were looking forward to it and the manager said, "oh, sorry." She did nothing to try and make it up. It was a looong 4days with 4 children and no pool. I will not go back to that hotel.

title: “Didn't expect much”
text: This is an average Motel 6 which we stayed at at the last minute because we arrived late and it seemed to be conveniently located for relatively quick access to downtown Fort Worth and to the stockyards. The room was small but clean and recently renovated. The bathroom was nice. We encountered three issues: 1. You had to pay for wifi which is ridiculous in this day and age and included at other hotels in this price range; 2. There was no breakfast, only coffee. Again, other hotels in this price range provide breakfast; and 3. We were awakened by a lady knocking on our door early in the morning looking for her husband/boyfriend who must have been staying there with someone else given the yelling that took place later on. That was a definite reminder of the type of motel we were staying in and the class of people one might encounter there...

title: “Exactly what I had in mind...”
text: We stayed at the Affinia the Friday night before Christmas. The hotel was exactly what I was looking for: great location, trendy/stylish yet comfortable room, helpful staff, and a great view. And the Affinia delivered. I would highly recommend this hotel, plus its a great value.

title: “Wow! Experience Texas Hospitality First-Hand!”
text: La Mansion was, without a doubt, the best hotel I have ever experienced. The service was unparalleled--every employee went out of their way to make our stay wonderful. From front desk person to concierge, we were waited on hand and foot. From the moment we arrived, we were treated to the kind of service I've always wished for but never received. We arrived at 11:30 p.m. and were immediately upgraded to a poolside room and then brought via hotel car out to dinner. Rudy, our wonderful driver, brought us in to the restaurant, waited until we were done, and took us for a late-night tour of the area. We were offered rides to shopping and local attractions. Our room was gorgeous and so comfortable. I am amazed at all the complaints I read here--it's like they're talking about a different hotel. I HIGHLY recommend this hotel, but go through AAA to find better rates.

title: “Nice oasis on fringes of chelsea”
text: We usually stay in the 50's but decided to do something different and stay in chelsea. From arrival to departure the hotel was excellent. We had a quick lunch which was great but never got the chance to have dinner. Staff is friendly and there are plenty of them to go around. A very young staff but handled with maturity. The only problem we had was we were on a corner room on the 9th floor and you could here every noise, even the subway. Our friends stayed towards the back and said it was very quiet. The surrounding streets are not the best the city has to offer. A lot of wholesale perfume and junk. Would not recommend a nighttime walk around. You are right around the corner from Eatly and the flea markets so just a short walk and you are out of the grunge. All in all a very cool hotel, hopefully the neighborhood will catch up soon.

title: “Great Hotel for Family Trip”
text: The suite was perfect so that the 2-year old could sleep in the bedroom and we could do things in the living room. PROS: Full-size crib that seemed quite comfortable for the 2-year old, lots of room, lots of kid-friendly restaurant options nearby (including Shake Shack, Blue Smoke and others), Whole Foods also a few blocks away. CONS: The sliding doors between the bedroom and the living room didn't insulate much noise, the lights and TV automatically turn on when someone enters the room (even if one of us was in the room), which had the potential to wake up the sleeping 2-year old.

title: “Very Nice Sheraton”
text: Great hotel to stay at in Indianapolis. Several nice restaurants around the hotel.

title: “Decent place with some garish upgrades in a nice neighborhood.”
text: I don't know what the Renaissance looked like before renovations but now it is completely over the top. The rooms are also a bit noisy, with hall chatter leaking in at Midnight, and somewhat humid as there is no exhaust fan in the bathroom. That said, the bed was comfy as anything and the hotel does have a good location across from the mall.

title: “Loved this hotel!”
text: It was updated, clean, and had a great view of the bay. It was also ideally located in the Gaslamp Quarter to several shops and restaurants and Petco Park. It was also a short taxi ride to the various tourist attractions like Seaworld, San Diego Zoo, and Seaport Village. You don't need a rental car if you stay here while in San Diego.

title: “Nice stay at the Taj”
text:
Spent two nice evenings at this hotel in the heart of Boston. Convenient to shopping, dining and sightseeing.
The staff was helpful, the hotel clean, the amenities first rate. We enjoyed the lounge in the evening and noted that there were a good number of business travelers staying at the Taj.
The only negative was our "city view" was a construction site across from our room. We didn't obsess about this since the construction work didn't start until we were up and around.
All in all, we were satisfied.

title: “Fantastic hotel but niggling minor problems”
text:
Took our honeymoon at this hotel, booked through British Airways. We signed up in advance for Select Guest, and received free drinks and newspapers every morning. The hotel itself was very welcoming, commodious and clean, with the restaurant staff very helpful and food of good quality. The location is excellent - less than 5 minutes from a Metro station and in a safe, lively neighbourhood. The concierge service is the best we've ever come across - extremely knowledgeable and extremely helpful.
However, a host of minor problems during our stay has knocked the hotel down from 5 blobs to 4: our key-cards failed twice during our stay, because the wrong departure dates had been programmed onto them - each necessitating a trip back down to the lobby to sort out. The towels disappeared twice without being replaced. The bath mat would appear for one day, disappear for two days, then return mysteriously. There was a large air-con unit several floors down underneath the window which ran intermittently throughout the night. Used room service trays were left in the corridors for hours before being cleared away.
Having said that, these were only minor problems and we would both cheerfully stay at this hotel again, for location, helpful staff and good presentation.

title: “I loved my Kimpton Experience.”
text: From the doorman who always said "welcome back" to the friendly and generous staff, my experience was fabulous. Great location near Union Square - we could walk everywhere. Smallish rooms, but so well appointed it did not matter. Besides, we were out and about at our conference. It was warm, so we left the window open at night; BIG mistake, as Union Square can be noisy 24/7. After we closed the window and put on the air conditioning, we slept like babies in their ultra comfy beds. The wine reception really added to our enjoyment, as well as free internet.

title: “Great place to stay while in Chicago!”
text:
We picked the Courtyard because of a $99 special on Travelzoo. The hotel was very nice, clean, and the staff were friendly and helpful. Starbucks in the lobby, which was nice. We checked in 3 hours early with no problem. I had requested a room on a high floor and got room 2008, on the 20th floor. King size bed, sofa with pull out bed, desk & chair. Nice and comfortable, and the window size was the length of the outside wall with a pretty good city view. We ordered room service once, it was ok, but overpriced in my opinion. Ice & soda machines on each floor are nice. Shower was perfect, good water flow, and plenty of hot water. Toilet and tub in seperate area from sink. 
Location was great, one block off Michigan and a bus stop we used a lot. Lots of restaurants, very expensive stores, and a Dunkin Donuts and White Hen store around the corner. Concierge staff were SO helpful with advice on buses to take and where to get off, as well as offering us free tickets to a play. 
The only negative was that they advertise on the Marriott site there is free internet on the tv. They have limited access that is free, mostly weather, stocks and news sites. We went ahead and paid the 9.99 access fee, but none of the sites we wanted would load for us. (Sites like google, yahoo, etc.) Not even Trip Advisor would load! Not a big deal, but thought I would mention it, cause we were looking forward to the internet access to check email, and we couldn't. All in all, I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Stay elsewhere”
text: Put up here as a conference I am speaking at is nearby. Street noise, free but too slow Internet, movie that stopped half way through, hallways not air conditioned. Just isn't up to business travel standards.

title: “Part Good, Part Bad, Part Ugly”
text:
This is a very busy, fast change of customers, loud, party atmosphere hotel. This is mostly due to the location of being near the stadiums for the Eagles, Flyers, Phillies, 76'ers which also host rock concerts and other types of entertainment.
I was working at one of the stadiums and stayed at this hotel for six months so I saw most of the good, bad, ugly.
Starting on the outside- Apparently the hotel does not manage it's own parking area- It is rented out to some company and during some of the events it is blocked off and parking is sold for $40 per space. Yes, it is still free for guests but during football games it gets quite crowded with the tail-gaters and parking can be difficult. Also, just before a game the streets around the hotel become grid-locked with cars waiting for stadium parking to open. Not much the hotel can do about the grid-lock, just a fact that I once got stuck for 45 minutes trying to get in. Remember to get a pass from the front desk if you need to go out when it is being "rented" out.
Another annoying thing about the parking is they often put a chain across the west entrance to help control traffic during a event- And then leave it up for weeks afterward- I put up with this until one night I saw a fire engine come to this entrance and found it blocked when responding to a emergency call for the restaurant. Once I complained to management they did take it down right away but this was after it had been up for many weeks.
After a "event" the parking lot can be full of beer cans and bottles, some broken. I informed the front desk of a broken gallon wine bottle near my car at 7am and it was not cleaned up until 10:30 am.
Coming into the hotel the little square smoking ashtray at the front entrance is a joke. It is often "stuffed" full and will start smoking on it's own. The front entrance could use with a weekly power wash.
I don't believe the luggage racks have ever been cleaned. They are filthy and in very poor condition with metal strips broken and the carpet on the bottom is pretty much black instead of the intended red color.
At check-in some of the staff is quite friendly and helpful- Others can be machine like with almost no interest in being helpful or interested in your needs.
The rooms are pretty much standard Holiday Inn but with the crowds they get it can get extremely noisy with groups coming in and having parties and when moving between these rooms they set the door hasp lock to keep it open so you get the constant "banging" of the doors until they leave for whatever event they are there for.
Then after the event and after the bar closes comes the real noise of the shouting and yelling with more banging on doors and on three different occasions fights in the hallway on my floor.
The worst is when there is a rock concert- After the recent VanHalen concert I had to call security twice on the room next door- And the absolute worst is when the recent "chicken-wing" eating contest was held (this party starts at something like midnight and goes on into the morning). The noise kept me up from 1am to 4am with me again calling security twice. Perhaps the hotel was a bit overwhelmed by the size of the crowd and the amount of liquor that was drunk. If extra security was on hand, more was needed.
In the guest laundry they have two washers and two dryers. One washer was "out of service" from the middle of October to the end of November. Then one dryer was "out of service from the middle of January to the middle of February.
On the good side the room cleaning service people were fantastic in helping us with our every need and request. Always with a friendly smile and a big hello every time we crossed ways. (thank Klemintina)
And then there was Nik- He must be a manager of some sort and got involved when I had no hot water in the room and the only answer maintenance could say was to change rooms- I had already changed rooms twice due to cleaning and maintenance and was not about to do so again. When Nik heard of my situation he personally took charge and had the hot water working withing 24 hours. (thank you Nik)
Even though I rated this hotel as average I don't suppose it is fair to blame the hotel for the large groups of intoxicated people it has to deal with. It does have a good location.
It can be a good place to stay, just be aware of the events happening and be ready to deal with it.

title: “We wrote our own chapter at the library”
text:
We returned to Australia yesterday having spent 8 nights at the Library Hotel. After having spent three weeks apart, my wife and I were reunited at this exceptionally comfortable and romantic New York hotel. The reception was warm and the concierge service was expert and delightful. Their recommendations of restaurants and activities left the guide books well behind.
Our room (the Fashion Section - 700.006) was terrific, facing Maddison Avenue, it was larger and sunnier than the other rooms we snuck a peek at. The decorations and finishes were a lovely touch. Ours was designed and appointed by Vera Wang, and filled with beautiful books about clothes, style and fashion.
Afternoons in the Reading Room are a must - where one can meet fellow travellers (and readers) over a glass of wine and nibbles. (Just a shame that the mood music is on constant loop.)
The location in Midtown Manhattan is ideal for explorers of all sorts - right around the corner from Grand Central, it is so easy to get anywhere by foot or subway.
We were very sad to leave, and we hope to return someday.

title: “Great Find!”
text: The Quincy is a great hotel in an excellent DC location. The rooms are comfortable with a modern feel and very clean. Although we did not have a view - unfortunately, our room looked out on the heating/cooling equipment on the roof - we did not stay at the hotel for a view. Instead, we stayed there for its location. It is only one block from the Farragut North Metro stop and one block from both the bus and Circulator stops. It is also just a short walk to the White House and then on to the Mall. We couldn't have asked for a better hotel and all of us were very pleased with our stay. We would definitely stay again.

title: “It was a great older hotel.”
text:
I could just imagine this hotel that was built in the early 1900's. It must have been quit the place. It is a wonderful place to stay in San Francisco. I liked that is wasn't large and is in a nice location. Chancellor is across the street from Union Square and close to the Hop on Hop Off shuttle buses that take you all over the city. The hotel has been tastefully updated keeping the integrity of the old building and would recommend the hotel to my friends..
 The staff is very professional and will go out of their way to help you enjoy your stay in San Francisco.. I would stay there again.

title: “Coolest hotel!”
text: This was the coolest hotel that I've ever been in! Rock n' Roll decor, hip furniture, creative details. This is not your average hotel. Great location, close to restaurants, bars, shopping, Magnificent Mile. The bed was super comfy and I didn't hear any noise during the night. You can even have them deliver a thermos of coffee in the morning to your door for free! If you want a fancy schmancy hotel, don't stay here. If you want something cool and different, give Acme hotel a try!

title: “Nobody's perfect; even at top dollar”
text: It's a crying shame that this resort hasn't got its whole act together given the peerless architecture and setting. Some elements of their customer service put others into stark relief with their crass ineptitude e.g. we arrived and sat down for afternoon tea and were told "you'll be waiting a long time before THAT table gets cleared". No "hello", no "how may I help you?". Tactless; not what you want to hear after a 300 mile drive. I thought it might have been a one off, sadly however, only half the employees were putting their customers first. On the upside, the main restaurant delivered memorable quality food, wine and service. Likewise the spa staff were attentive and courteous. Excellent for a day/evening visit, maybe for an overnight but you'll feel short changed with a longer stay.

title: “Good hotel, location is ok”
text: I stayed at the Omni Shoreham hotel a few days back. While the hotel is good and we got decent spacious rooms, i somehow felt the woodley park area where the hotel is located is quite dead compared to say a dupont circle. That is the only reason why i would not highly recommend this hotel. If you get a good rate, go for it. Dont pay too much though!

title: “Terrible location”
text: We booked this hotel based on reviews from this website only to realize that the location is terrible. There is nothing nearby and hardly any restaurants within a short walking distance. Rodeo drive is only a few blocks away but the distance between each block is quite far, it took us around 25 minutes to walk to rodeo drive. I would recommend that you stay in Hollywood if you have free time at night and want to walk around, the shops open until around 9pm and there is plenty to do. Taxis cost us $30 from our hotel to Hollywood!

title: “Nice room, great staff, bad area”
text:
We booked 5 nights at this hotel. The rooms are small, but nice with comfortable beds. The cleaning was poor, dirty under the beds and along the edges around the room. We arrived during daytime, and when the evening came we discovered that there was a lot of homeless and people doing drugs. They didn´t approach us unless you were smoking, but it felt very unsafe. We were afraid to go anywhere else but to the restaurang across the street! Our first night in the hotel, we felt marijuana smoke in the hallway.. 
Nothing to do during the evening, only two or three restaurants close to the hotel. A few more close to Rose Avenue about 5 min walk from the hotel.

title: “This hotel offers apartment-like accommodation on the upper east side with few of the usual hotel services such as a café.”
text: Our one-bedroom suite was spacious and had a full kitchen - larger than we had expected. While comfortable, the suite needed updating, eg, the broadloom had seen better days. The staff were very friendly and helpful. The free wi-fi was great. Don't bother using the room safe; it's not bolted to the wall or floor. One downside about the location - it's on the corner of 2nd Avenue where subway construction has been ongoing for years, so not pleasant to walk along, as well as noisy.

title: “great service and ammenities, small room with thin walls”
text:
I travel pretty much every week for work, and it's been a very long time since I stayed in a room where the walls were so thin that I could literally hear the people talking next door. And, unfortunately, that was the problem with my room at the Hilton San Francisco.
Of all the hotels that I've stayed in the Union Square area, the Hilton has the most up-to-date rooms, although the room I was given was small and tight with an equally small bathroom. I thought I was back in NY!
It's a shame, too, because the hotel has lots to offer - extremely friendly and efficient staff, a few good restaurant choices and a Starbucks in the lobby, good (but not great) location 5 minutes walk from the Powell Street BART station. 
Just make sure you watch where you walk - this hotel's location right on the edge of Union Square also places it in the SF "Tenderloin" district. If you walk out the wrong door you'll find yourself in a pretty "colorful" (read that: seedy) street.

title: “great location for great price”
text: we chose this hotel after reviews from trip advisor and we were not disappointed. Rooms were basic and clean, very safe at night, its walking distance to all spots. We had 2 kids (4 & 1) and we walked to fishermans wharf (about 20 mins) and even back from Union Square (about 30 mins) so we found it was a great location. Only gripe to mention is that it does not have a bar fridge so we had to use the ice bucket to keep the milk cold and you do get a bit of street traffic noise if you are on the road side.

title: “Great Location-Attentive Staff”
text: Hotel is very well located to see the highlights of Seattle. Monorail to Space Needle/Experience Music Project/ Sci-Fi Museum is a few blocks away, easy walking distance. Same for Pikes Place Market and great local restaurants. Hotel seems to cater to business travellers which explains the coffee stains on the the carpet next to the desk. No joke. Stayed in 3 different rooms in same hotel. Coffee stains in 2 out of 3. BUT have to say after checking in very late (1am) and the next morning mildly complaining about the cleanliness of the room, we were upgraded (without asking) to a room on the top floor with a perfect view of the Space Needle. (Thank you Marissa!). Many fine local restaurants within walking distance nearby.(Top Pot for doughnuts, Serious Pie for pizza). There is also a drugstore one block over for any forgotten items. Check out the "Local Vine" for some great Washington wines! Staff very friendly and helpful Happy to make reservations for dinner etc..). BTW Taxi service in Seattle is awful. Waited 45 minutes for taxi to cruise pier that never arrived. Can recommened Daniel at Liberty Transport [--] who helped us out while he was there picking up another fare. Overall would definitely stay here again and would rec'd to anyone. Try out the "Washington Red Apple Martini" with free wi-fi in the lobby at hotel.

title: “A Grande Dame, Who is Just a Little Tired”
text:
The St. Anthony Riverwalk Hotel is a beautiful and fascinating lady of-a-certain-age in a terrific downtown San Antonio location. She’s a little worn around the edges, but still has all the glamour and style gained by living well since 1909. Wonderfully decorated in authentic French antiques with sculptures and paintings galore the St. Anthony is a place of lovely niches. From the comfortable bar in the beautifully appointed Peacock Room with its windowed streetside patio, to an elegant restaurant with sweeping staircase, the hotel offers lovely sitting areas where one can enjoy a cocktail, read a book, or engage in lively conversation.
