Be sure to look at the framed lobby photographs of former guest luminaries John Wayne, Princess Grace and Prince Rainier, Audie Murphy, and Arnold Schwarzenegger.
Rooms are only OK with comfortable beds, operational air conditioning, and high ceilings, but dated appointments. Oh yeah, there’s also a ghost who inhabits the tenth floor, specifically Room 1080. We stayed on the 10th floor, but were not visited by the ghost. He may have been on vacation.
The St. Anthony is about three blocks from the Alamo; Shrine to the Texas War of Independence. With free admission and fascinating history, plan to spend an easy two hours on the Alamo grounds. Also close (two short blocks) is the famous San Antonio Riverwalk, a classic entertainment venue with bars, restaurants, historic markers, and boat tours. Visitors can walk for miles through beautiful near-tropic flowering plants along the river. 
We are told there is an extensive remodeling scheduled to begin in 2013, which will “keep the good and fix the bad”. We hope it will be successful. There’s a lot to like about this dear old Grande Dame that we would love to enjoy again.

title: “Excellent Park & Fly Package”
text: My husband & I stayed for one night at this hotel. Although a bit pricier than most of the other park & fly hotels, we thought it might be worth it for the covered & secure parking and the close proximity to the airport. We made the right choice & would go back again. The room was clean and had a separate bedroom & living room area. The bathroom was fairly spacious. The wakeup call came on time and I was pleasantly surprised to see the breakfast buffet all set up at 5am for early travelers. They do cook to order omelets starting at 5:30 - which we couldn't stay for - but there were eggs, waffles, home fries, bagels, fruit, cereal, etc. The shuttle comes every 15 minutes - at least between 5 & 6 am. But you are so close to the airport it takes only a few minutes to get to the terminal. Upon return, we called the number they gave us as soon as our airplane touched down. A van was waiting for us after we obtained our luggage and the car was ready & waiting at the hotel - all warmed up. It was effortless - and this was at 11pm! We will definitely use this hotel again when flying out of Logan.

title: “Great location. Clean rooms. Friendly staff.”
text: I've stayed at this hotel several times and I love the location. It's a short drive to just about everywhere and very convenient to Hobby Airport. There are great restaurants all around the hotel and even a nearby park across the parking lot for the kiddos. The staff is always friendly and the rooms are pretty spacious and comfortable. I will stay here again. The cost is always very reasonable.

title: “More you could not wish for”
text: This was, quite frankly, one of the best hotel experiences we have had anywhere (and we stay in a lot of hotels!) Our reception was warm and friendly...quite the opposite to what we are accustomed to in big cities. Our luggage was toted up to our room for us and there was real interest shown in our well-being. Our room was outstanding....no other word for it.....large, homely, scrupulously clean, welcoming and sumptuous....and that doesn't include the tv incorporated in the bathroom mirror. The kitchen facilities were great...microwave, coffee machine etc...all clean and well looked after. Turndown service with chocolates was offered every afternoon. The bed was not only the best we have been given in ANY hotel....it was far better than our own back home! We could easily have stayed here forever. We did try out the restaurant and were just as impressed by that. we cannot praise this hotel enough. We did have a very good deal for this by booking well in advance and by paying at time of booking....a good tip for anyone on a budget who feels that this outstanding hotel may be beyond their means! Oh,by the way, the location could not be better if you want to explore San Francisco...Union Square a two minute walk away, with all the big shops and cable car stop. another great feature of this hotel was the 'club' on the top floor, available to all guests...rooftop views, free coffee and tea at any hour, fitness centre, and comfy seating....together with very friendly, helpful concierges. if we go back to San Francisco, there is no doubt where we'll be staying!

title: “Great Location”
text:
First and foremost it should be noted that the Milford is a very old Hotel dating back to the 20's and therefore the small closet like rooms. Hotels rooms just weren't that big back then.With that said all I can say in defense of this Hotel is the outstanding location. One block to Times Square
about 4 blocks to Radio City and so on. I understand that they are going through a major renovation project but that started 2 years ago this month, how long does it take? My guess they started at the top and they are working their way down. I stayed on the 5th floor and the room albeit tiny was barely passable. The bathroom floor looked like it had not seen a mop in weeks or months and there was a black hair in the bathroom sink ( I have dirty blonde hair). There was no temperature control so you were at the mercy of the heat coming on once in a while. Fortunately it was a very mild weekend and not much heat was needed. The sheer curtains at the window were dirty with black stains. Perhaps the renovated rooms are very nice, so if you choose to stay here request one of the rooms that has been redone. Even with this bad review I would probably stay there again because of the fabulous location. Expect the worst and be pleasantly surprised if things have changed next year when I go back for my annual NYC Christmas trip.

title: “Convenient location and friendly staff”
text: This Embassy Suite proved to be in a very convenient location - close to the AZ 51 freeway and Paradise Valley Mall area [Wal-Mart, In & Out etc.] at Cactus & Tatum. I recently stayed here for 5 nights and found their staff very friendly and helpful. Ada, Tiffany, Daniel, Adam and Evan at the front desk were always ready to assist. The large suite-room was clean and comfortable. The walkway around the golf course was terrific for my early morning treks. Good choice for my stay in the Valley of the Sun!

title: “Over-priced & over-rated!”
text:
I hate to be so negative, but I really did find this hotel totally over-rated. When we were checked in, our room was fine but with a tiny bathroom. There was NO complementary water in the room, despite being a 4 star hotel and paying hefty room rates. When I asked the staff about water in the room, they scoffed at the idea of complementary water, and in general were snooty and unhelpful in all my dealings with the hotel staff.
Regarding location, the Fairfax is located close to Dupont Circle, which we found to be quite quiet, and missing the buzz, shops and restaurants that are all present at Georgetown. If it's your first trip to DC, as this was for us, I would definitely stay in Georgetown and experience great atmosphere and have shops and restaurants on your doorstep.

title: “Cheap...okay for 1 night”
text: Stayed in a 2 bedroom suite for 1 night with our kids for a volleyball tournament. This hotel appears from the outside to be newer than it is. My husband wanted to call it that "70s hotel", but I talked him into that "80s hotel". It smelled like the room might have previously been a smoking room although now it is designated non-smoking. The floor was completely dirty. It needs updating and repairs (broken lamps, damaged doors, chipping paint, etc.) BUT for $79 for one night, it was okay. The area is convenient, but noisy! Do not plan on sleeping except between the hours of 11 pm and 5 am. The area is odd. Kind of business park, but sort of deserted. Max & Irma's and Wendy's close by are shut down.

title: “Satisfied”
text: If you want a place with friendly service, spacey rooms, and overall cleanliness I would recommend this hotel. Granted, we might have gotten lucky looking at some of the reviews, however I had very few problems with this hotel. I enjoyed the overhead lights by the bed and desk area and the shower was very roomy. The only complaint I could really have is that one of the sheets was tore up a little bit on the corner but only noticeable if you really look at everything. Fantastic internet speed as well.

title: “Good Value For Price”
text:
Having not been to San Antonio for 20 years, I researched budget hotels near the airport extensively on Tripadvisor. Red Roof was running a promotion for redicard members and I chose this property both for the decent reviews and the promotion. 
For the price and proximity to the airport, this was a very good deal. My Superior King room was clean and the staff was very accommodating and friendly. The internet access was free and worked without problems. My only problem all weekend was not enough towels the first night. A request to the front desk for more was handled speedily and without question.
Highly recommend this property for the budget vacation traveler.

title: “What a GEM!!”
text:
I had the pleasure of staying at the Palomar while I was in D.C. on a business trip from Cambridge recently. Since we have a Kimpton Hotel, the Hotel Marlowe in Cambridge, MA, I knew that I loved the hotel chain and their always fresh and different concepts in other cities. The Palomar did not disappoint!!
From the time I walked into the lobby, everyone from the bellman to the front desk was smiling, friendly and accommodating. My room was HUGE and beautifully furnished with sleek, modern (but not TOO modern) furnishings, and I later learned that the hotel had undergone a recent renovation from top to bottom.
Although my business trip kept me occupied from morning until well into the evening each day, I did have time to run back to the hotel for a quick refresh each day between 5-7p. The first day that I walked in at 5-ish, I was shocked to see the lobby filled with hotel guests enjoying the complimentary wine reception--something that I don't usually participate in because of the somber, poorly-attended "wine receptions" I have encountered in other hotels in the past. That was far from the party going on in the Palomar lobby! Everyone seemed to be old friends, and considering there were businessmen/women, families, couples and even a couple of Bassett hounds (very pet-friendly hotels, Kimptons are!), this was no easy feat! I must admit that I stopped by to pick up a sparkling Sangria and ended up staying for 20 minutes chatting with other hotel guests. I was sorry to leave the party and already anticipating the next afternoon for this energy boost at the hotel.
In short, everything was wonderful. I look forward to returning to this hotel with my husband to enjoy its convenient proximity to Georgetown and all the local sites that I didn't have time to visit on this trip.
One side note for travelers to D.C.: I have never encountered a more informative, friendly and welcoming group of taxi drivers in my life! Always a challenge in other large cities, the Washington cab drivers were more than helpful and EXCELLENT tour guides for the city!

title: “Last Minute choice best was best”
text: Booked this hotel 1 day before arrival for Friday thru Sunday June 11 - 13. Can't say enough about the staff, the cleanliness and the room. This place is an Oasis from the craziness going on right outside the door. The absolute best location for the New York experience. Go with the Johns Pizza trip they recommended but avoid the El Centro mexican place. Great stay.

title: “Very Good Location, Decent Hotel”
text: The hotel itself is not really worth the price you pay, but the location is probably the best in the city. This hotel is connected to Grand Central Station, so it's very convenient to jump on the subway and get to anywhere in the city. It's only one stop away from Times Square(with a subway shuttle running until midnight) and from there you can get to all the tourist sights in the city. If you don't want to take the train, no problem, you can get to quite a few places within 20 minutes. The Empire State Building, Times Square, and Rockefeller Center is about 10 minutes. A walk to the east harbour and the United Nations building is also 10 minutes. A walk to Central Park is about 20 minutes, but you can walk down either 5th Avenue of Madison Avenue and take in the shopping on the way there. And if you want to go to a Yankees game, there a shuttle from Grand Central Station right to the stadium. As for the actual hotel, the lobby is nice and clean, the rooms are actually fairly large for New York, but nothing luxurious, just your basic hotel room. But you don't pay for the room, you pay for the location.

title: “Disgusting Dump-Don't Be Fooled!”
text: Dreadful experience that nearly ruined our NY vacation. From dirty bedding to scary showers this pitiful excuse for a "hotel" is nothing more than a run down dormitory possibly from 1910 and never having been updated with the exception of decades of "dust cover" paint. The occasionally tolerant staff and semi-convenient two block walk to the subway certainly doesn't negate or outweigh the putrid smelling tiny shoebox room, noisy plumbing and ventilation systems that keep you up all night, grungy stained red carpets, questionable bath accommodations, barely there door locks, college-sized twin fit for (1) anorexic girl, a large toddler or possible two infants lying end to end, the fact that the "luxury" suite offers you and your spouse the romantic amenity of sleeping in miniature separate beds in miniature separate rooms, a "vanity" area represented by a medicine cabinet affixed to the wall and a tiny little wash bin, one smoky towel per person irregardless of your stay duration and most importantly the convenient shower while you pee option the bathroom area affords as the shower stall and commode are a mere 10 inches apart. All-in-all the great "value" other reviewers speak of would only exist if you're trip objective was to spend your entire getaway apart from your co-traveler, searching for a medley bugs in your microscopic separate rooms, while looking over your shoulder at the paper thin door, held secure possibly by a toothpick lock, that could be knocked in at any moment and all 1 of your towels taken and used to finish off the smoke signals they started before folded and offered to you!

title: “Very Personalized!”
text: I have to say that after staying at some of the best five star accommodations in the US as well as in Europe and Asia I have a warm place in my heart for 15 Beacon. This hotel, while being one of the priciest in this area, does not disappoint. I felt right at home, and being a young single woman who travels quite often for business this is saying a lot. The concierge and Front Desk seemed to pick up on my attitude as well as taylored their advice about Boston directly for me. The staff was friendly but was certainly not intrusive and the room was immaculately clean. I love the amenities and even though I am Very picky about the products I use on my hair, etc I still love the products they offer in all of the rooms! Overall, I will never hesitate to stay at 15 Beacon and will always highly recommend it!

title: “Awesome Union Square location!”
text:
Fantastic Location
I don’t think we could have asked for a better hotel location in San Francisco. The Taj is located right in Union Square which is close to plenty of restaurants and shops. It is very easy to catch the trolley cars and buses from this location.
The hotel is not big, so it has a boutique feel.
Room: we stayed in a deluxe room. We felt our room had plenty of space and was well appointed. Our room did not have a view, which was not an issue for us, since it meant we encountered no noise.
The bathrooms were fantastic and the towels and linens were some of the best I have experienced in all my travels. 
Dining: we did not eat in the restaurant; however, we did go to the bar on several nights and enjoyed drinks and dessert there. My only compliant was that the bar did not have enough bar snacks that you could just order to snack on – like wings, spring rolls, satays, etc. 
The only other issue we had was on a couple of nights there were some large groups in the bar, which really was a little small to cater for a large group all ordering meals. Don’t get me wrong the staff looked after us well so it was not due to a lack of attention; it was just that these groups seem to take over the entire bar.
Overall I would recommend this hotel to everyone: for the location and for the wonderful services and amenities. 
The hotel is pretty expensive, but I think that is expected in San Francisco, plus you really do get the services and amenities of a luxury hotel.

title: “The ultimate in UNprofessionalism”
text: I attended a wedding here and spent the night afterward. There is a complete lack of respect and attention to detail from the staff. The place was dirty, the food was sub-par, the toilets didn't flush. The staff simply did not seem to care. I would not recommend this place to anyone, especially for a wedding. If you intend to stay the night here, think twice. You might want to find a hotel that is clean and has appropriate staffing.

title: “Very nice change from cookie cutter hotels”
text: Neat place, had a sole, VERY nice staff, great parking, BIG rooms, big effort placed by staff to do a good job.

title: “Great Value and Place!”
text: My husband and I went on our 2nd wedding anniversary trip to NY. We wanted to see all of the sites in 3 days and we did see a TON! This hotel was centrally located only blocks from Times Square, and was the best value! We requested a room high enough and facing the Empire State (only one block over) the view was fantastic! The room was BIG (especially for NYC) and had everything we needed. We felt safe as well. I would go to this hotel again for the bargain!

title: “Great hotel and fantastic position”
text: I've just come back from the hotel 373 on the 5th avenue. The hotel is in a great position, almost in front of the Empire State Building and few steps from Times Square and Madison Square Garden. It is also very close to Macy's and to a lot f souvenir stores. The staff is friendly and helpful. As written in other reviews,the rooms aren't too big but the bed is huge and the bathroom is comfortable and neat. You have a well working wifi connection all throughout the hotel. The rooms are clean and I could see the Empire State from my window. I would definitely recommend this hotel!!

title: “Nice hotel, good location”
text: The Strand Hotel has some great features. The front desk staff and bellmen were excellent. The concierge was ok. The housekeeping staff is their weakest link. The room we had in this hotel was rather small, but fine. The shower had "issues" because of a half-wall only, and it leaked onto the floor every time we took a shower, despite our best efforts to keep it dry. Breakfast was ridiculously expensive, and just ok. We also had dinner here and the food was very good. The only suggestion I would have is that they get rid of the "steak sauce" that was served with a very nice steak. The steak sauce was A1 from a bottle. After all that effort to make a nice steak, why not make a little sauce instead of pouring from a bottle. Or, serve it on the side for those that like it.

title: “Supremely horrible service”
text:
All I can say is the front desk staff - (Thomasina or something) - she was the worst I have seen in awhile. You can give some leeway to age, etc., but outside of that - she was so rude. Ugh. The hotel was OK , it really only has the location going for it.
 Also, as I was looking around the hotel there was a sales person and a manager arguing in the gift shop. Classy.

title: “Assets and liabilities”
text:
My husband and I purchased an auction package that included the Driscoll hotel so we came taking our chances. This is a boutique hotel with some limitations. The building itself is older so no air conditioning, no on-sight resturant or bar, and no outdoor seating or patio. The most difficult was finding on-street parking and when located it was on a steep hill!
 But the assets Far outweigh any difficulty. This is a place where the service is consistent and sure to spoil you for anywhere else. In advance of our visit we asked for resturant recommendations and Marty arranged for some of the best dining experiences ever. We highly recommend this if you don't already have your favorites. The continental breakfast is superb. For a cold breakfast the offerings are so bountiful you don't miss anything hot. You eat in elegant room with fresh flowers throughout the room and several choices of national and international newspapers to choose from. Added fun were bottles of water in the room personalized for the hotel with picture of the Driscoll on the inside. Our grandchildren loved them! 
If you want to be pampered, this is the place to go.

title: “Fabulous!”
text:
We cannot say enought great things about this hotel. When booking, we advised the hotel we were staying there for my daughter's birthday. When we checked in, there was a birthday gift for her - a really nice Waldorf Astoria chef teddy bear. They also gave my son a nice toy taxi so he would not be jealous. Wanting to impress everybody, they also had a welcome gift for my husband and me - a free buffet brunch for 4!
Our room was large for a NYC hotel and had a separate dressing room with makeup table. Alana, who checked us in. told us she chose this room for our daughter and it was perfect. The room was nice and beds were very comfry. Each and every staff member could not be nicer - each one took time to joke with our children. The rate was extremely reasonable - even if this was not a top hotel. 
We all decided we want to stay at a Waldorf on every trip.

title: “Great Location for Convention Center”
text: Close enough to convention center to walk (weather was fine - wouldn't want to do it on a very rainy day...). Didn't really do anything but sleep there. It was clean and the staff was nice. I had to call because the message about my allergies to feathers wasn't relayed from conference to hotel or missed (I bet it would have been ready if I had called the hotel directly.) Wall Street Journal was supposed to be delivered in the mornings but they missed me the first two days.

title: “Hotel Mela Is Great!!!”
text: My husband and I were in New York for a couple of days before cruising and we had the pleasure of staying at Hotel Mela. From the moment we walked into the lobby we knew our stay would be pleasant. Very professional and friendly employees. We were upgraded to a suite and did not even ask for an upgrade. The room was spotlessly clean, comfortable and plenty roomy. The location is great. Right in the middle of Times Square. No noise from the street when you are in your room. We will certainly stay here again when we return to New York. Thanks to Mela employees for such a pleasurable trip.

title: “Great new property!”
text: This particular Hampton is simply outstanding. It's new and has a great ambience. I've never seen a Hampton this nice. And the service is truly outstanding...as in I made my reservation for the night before I meant to and when I showed up late the next night I didn't have a reservation. They took immediate care of me and credited my no show reservation and gave me the same rate. Be sure to note that this on on I 30 at NORTH Cockerell Hill and not on I 20 at South Cockerell Hill. Also, this is located in a new shopping area that has a great selection of stores and restaurants.

title: “Business Travel, Sheraton Chicago Towers”
text: Excellent customer service, both as guest and for corporate meeting work. We present the best of cosmetic dental implant professionals in the Chicago 1-7 ballrooms at the Sheraton and as our 13th production was just completed, it truly is a very good team effort by all. Local labor, our traveling team, the venue staff, it really is a pleasure to produce events here.

title: “Great Stay- Deserves a 5”
text:
I've been staying at many hotels in the DC area always shopping price but have not been at less than a 3 star hotel property in months. I have also been giving out a couple of 5 stars based on the hotels exceeding my expectations, more than a 5 star stay.
Staying at the Hotel Palomar a few weeks ago in November brought back why a hotel really deserves 5 stars as they not only exceeded my expectations, the hotel stay was just great in all aspects. 
Check-in- they desk people could not have been more helpful. It was also rainy out and as I checked in I sat by the couch near the fireplace and could not have been more warmed in a gloomy outdoor environment and while I sat there a few of the employees asked if I needed anything w/o being intrusive. Good experience.
Room was in the back so while I did not have as much early morning light, it was a gracious and contemporary room, bed and linens were soft and inviting, bathrobes hung in closet (big closet), bathroom was very graceful and modern, it was ultra clean and I ended up joining the Kimpton Club and got my w-fi for free. This was key as I usually am out 6am-10pm when I am in DC but had tons of work to do in the hotel so I was able to move back and forth between room luxury and lobby luxury w/ my mobile devices.
Coffee in the morn was delicious and did not have to spend on Strabucks. Doormen could not have been nicer or more helpful for the 2 rainy days I spent there. This was in spite of taking metro which to Dupont Circle is only a 3 block walk (You can exit Dupont North or South and it's about the same walking distance) Did not get to the wine happy hour but wish I had. Left feeling very pampered, well rested, caught up on my work in a luxury hotel desrving to be #1 or #2 in DC.

title: “Great place to stay”
text:
This hotel has just been completely remodeled. There was still some drywall dust in the hallway where light fixtures were installed. The only way to tell it is not a new building is the elevator was not new. There still must be some remodeling going on because during the day, Saturday included, they were using a jackhammer in the basement. We were six floors up right above the work and it was annoying. 
The rooms were great. The only thing missing from the full kitchen was an oven, it had everything else, including a dishwasher. They have both one and two bedrooms suites. The two bedroom suites were the size of an apartment and everything is new. 
Each bedroom had a TV along with the "living area". The beds were very comfortable. I will stay at this hotel the next time I am in Indy.

title: “Does not meet expectations”
text: Looked at other reviews and was really surprised at the poor quality, the room air was hard to work, beds uncomfortable, breakfast awful. Not sure what others see with their rave reviews, makes me wonder if they are real.

title: “Lovely decor, great location, a few service issues”
text: Having stayed at the Argonaut in San Francisco I had high hopes for this hotel. I ended up feeling a little let down. It's a nice hotel and in a great location, but it was a bit lacking in the service department. Room wasn't ready when we arrived (early) and we were asked to come back at 3pm, which was fine. Still not ready when we returned at 3.30 which wasn't fine. As I inked down on seating in front of reception to wait, was soon noticed by manager (?) and within 20 mins had room on 10th floor and vouchers for complimentary drinks. This would have swayed things back in their favour except the safe didn't work and despite two phone calls no one ever arrived to look at it! Also had to call housekeeping as they left us without towels and it was the only hotel bar I've ever visited as a guest and been asked for my credit card before they'd serve me! Oh, and just arrived home and they've added an extra charge to my credit card. Not part of the bill they showed me on checkout...

title: “Great price and great location!!!”
text: The Rodeway inn is located in a nice area and close of culture center of the Baltimore. The room is comfortable and the price is good. I recommend this hotel.

title: “Nice Hotel but not Much Character”
text: I stayed at this hotel for two nights in August on a business-related trip. The hotel was clean and comfortable. It is modern so it lacks the character and charm of some of the other hotels in Denver but it is a very nice hotel. Its location is a moderate walk to the Rockies baseball stadium and the historic district in Denver. It is a short walk to the pedestrian mall. I would recommend this hotel but not for hosting a meeting or seminar. I felt the accommodations for a seminar I attended were very poor. The room was so cramped that some attendees did not even have a table at which to sit.

title: “Lovely hotel great location”
text: Very modern hotel with all the amenities you would expect from a Hilton. It is right across the road from the new wtc site, so there is a lot of construction going on there at the moment, but this didn't bother us, in fact our room overlooked the work site and we found it quite interesting watching them. The subway station is virtually right outside the door and it easily walkable to the hudson river. You can get cheaper hotels than this, but I felt we had value for money for what we paid, although the drinks in the bar were a litte pricey!

title: “Absolutely Loved It”
text:
We stayed 2 nights at the San Carlos Hotel - 3 adults & 2 children. We all cannot rave enough about this hotel. The hotel staff are extremely friendly & very helpful. The room we had was a 1 bedroom suite & it was quite large, very clean & elegant. Loved the Aveda products. 
The hotel is in a great location. We would not hesitate to book here again especially when you consider the price of such a large room - it seems like a bargain.

title: “Cannot be faulted.”
text: Wonderful location, clean, helpful staff. My second stay and I look forward to my third next year.

title: “Amazing central NY hotel!”
text:
I just returned from a 4 night stay at the Staybridge & have nothing but good things to say about the hotel!
The rooms were awesome, comfy beds, air con & fully stocked with toiletries. 
Breakfast was great, served as a buffet do you could eat as much as you wanted! Or could take it to your room! Coffee served throughout the day was a nice touch too in the lounge area! Very handy pantry section located on 1st floor stocked with sweets, drinks and ice creams, pay cash or charge your room. 
The bar in the hotel (bar forty) was a really cute hideout from the busy bars in times sq, drinks are well worth the money as the barmaid was not shy with her measures ;)
I would recommend this hotel to anyone! 
Thanks Staybridge!

title: “Good Value for the Location”
text:
Location, location, location. That's what the Midtown has going for it. Definitely worth checking out for parents with students at the schools along Huntington Ave. Right across the street from Symphony Hall and a block from Jordan Hall and BU/Huntington Theater. 2 blocks from the Pru. When we stayed, it wasn't cheap... but it was significantly cheapER than the other hotels in the immediate vicinity.
It's very basic... kind of like a 1960's motel transplanted into the city. Skim the reviews and you'll find some complaints about cleanliness... our room and the corridors were clean, though dated and a bit institutional. AAA's two-diamond rating is quite accurate. 
The staff we met were extremely friendly and helpful. The parking was convenient.
This hotel is not a destination. It's a place to sleep, for a few bucks less, while you do other things in the area. Worth your consideration if that's what you're looking for. We would certainly consider going back. But if you want an exercise room, places to hang out, lots of cable channels, luxury, onsite restaurant, or a view, check out the fancier places.

title: “Would happily stay there again!”
text: I Loved staying at this Hampton Inn. The staff was lovely, complimentary breakfast was plentiful and hot, room was very clean and comfortable. This Hampton inn is only a few miles away from the the airport and the downtown center (it was literally in between the airport and downtown). This place was another nice memory to an already memorable trip.

title: “Good location, easy on/off freeway”
text:
The hotel was easy to find and in a great location. Even in rush hour, it only took us 10 minutes to get to the Downtown area.
Room was clean and well-maintained. They have a nice (if pricey) little snack shop just off the front desk with sodas, chips, candy, ice cream, etc. Staff was friendly/helpful.
Got a great price on Hotwire at $76/night for a Fri/Sat/Sun stay. The one drawback was parking. There is a parking garage, but it wasn't noticeable from the front entrance. Parking in the outside lot is very difficult to find after 3pm or so.
I would definitely stay again. No opportunity to sample their food, but maybe next time.

title: “Good location-excellent service”
text: We stayed over the July 4th weekend and found the Holiday Inn Express to be a great value for Manhatten. We arrived a bit early for check-in and our bags were stored safely and were easy to retrieve when we returned to the hotel. As it has been said-the location is very convenient. Breakfast time is BUSY-but always lots to choose from-we enjoyed eating outside every morning. Yes the rooms are small-I totally expected this in NYC--it was not unbearable, even with two teenagers!! The room was clean, we did have to request more towels a couple of times, but my daughter left a note for housekeeping one morning and from then on we had plenty of towels! On our last day, we had a late flight out and once again our bags were stored safely for the day. I would definitely stay here again--NYC was fantastic as always!!!!!!!!

title: “Very Nice”
text: The employees of this hotel are incredible friendly and helpful! Traveled a lot but seldom experienced something like this... The room was just what we needed and the view was very nice. The only thing reason why I don't give 5 points is that the wall/ ceiling could be freshly painted (paint was peeling)...

title: “Never again!”
text: Nastiest & grossest hotel we have ever stayed in! In Austin for F1. Problems from the minute we stepped through the door. They pre-charged my card for the entire 5 day stay & at check-in, they couldn't find an available room. WTF? Mold in bathtub. Broken glass door held by tape. Asked for another room. Still mold in tub. Moldy smell throughout hotel. We hung our towels to use again but they were always taken away! Eco friendly? yeah, right. Ice makers didn't work. We were so disgusted, we left a day early. We will NEVER stay ay ANY Howard Johnson's. EVER.

title: “Four Seasons San Francisco”
text: If you are looking to have a sublime hotel experience in San Francisco, nothing beats staying at the Four Seasons. Every inch of the hotel is gorgeous with incredible art, decor and furnishings. The staff is welcoming and warm.. The rooms are luxurious, especially the all marble bath rooms, with double doors that make the space feel open and bright. HIghly recommend the Four Seasons San Francisco when you want to experience the best! Location is suberb!

title: “Perfect in every respect”
text:
I returned to the Chelsea Pines Inn after having stayed there fiteen years earlier and having visited New York City many times in between. I dont know why I stayed anywhere else.
I travel extensively for business and pleasure, staying in all types of accommodation around the world, from the very basic to the very opulent and am comfortable saying that my stay at the Chelsea Pines Inn was one of the most memorable of all. The team at the Inn know their market, they know what people are looking for in a hotel such as theirs and they deliver it with a great combination of friendliness and efficiency. The location can’t be beaten, being right at the junction of the Village, Meat Packing District and Chelsea. Yet despite W 14th St being a busy thoroughfare and the footpaths busy with people at most hours, the hotel is quiet. I slept with the window facing onto the rear courtyard open at night and woke to the sounds of birds in the trees – not what one would expect in Manhattan. The immediate area on 14th St had everything that I needed in terms of some great delis, a laundry, drug store etc while the range of restaurants and bars in the neighbourhood really offers something for every taste and budget. A number of subway lines are on the same block and there are plenty of attractions within walking distance so transport was never an issue. My room ticked all the boxes – comfortable bed and bed linen, great bathroom with strong water pressure in the shower, bathroom amenities that I actually wanted to use, a decent sized wardrobe with plenty of coat hangers. Breakfast downstairs was the perfect way to start the day – the quality of produce was outstanding.
However all of the above only counts for so much without the great team at the hotel – everybody who I met (and I imagine that I met pretty much the entire team during my stay) showed a pride in their work and in their place of work and were genuinely interested in offering advice, guidance, a helping hand with luggage, a map printed out and marked up with directions – I cannot rate the team highly enough. 
Staying at the Chelsea Pines Inn is like staying at the very comfortable home of a very good friend – I will definitely be back.

title: “Massive hotel in central location with very poor service”
text:
My husband and I stayed there earlier on this month. The check in experience was dreadful, we had to ask to speak to the manager as they were offering corner rooms looking into a brick wall or close to the street where you can not sleep. After speaking to the manager we managed to get a decent room but for a +1000 room hotel is not good enough. 
The room was not cleaned until after 5pm, they charged for use of the fitness centre which looks like a dungeon. 
This is definitely a hotel I would recommend

title: “excellent location and value”
text:
We loved our weekend stay at the Excelsior. It's right next to the Museum of Natural History and Central Park, which made it a great location. There's a subway stop at the end of the block, super easy. They upgraded us to a junior suite for free, which was a great way to start our day. Awesome showerhead in the bathroom!!!
My only complaint was that you had to pay for wi-fi. I get free wi-fi at crappy beach hotels in FL, but have to pay for it in a nice hotel on the Upper West Side? What's that about?

title: “I feel like I got more than I paid for.”
text: I was looking to stay somewhere for the night. This hotel was located right off the Interstate. There is a Village Inn located right next door but unfortunately it was closed on Sunday. The bed was comfortable enough. I was on the 5th floor and had a great view of the city. My favorite part of the stay was the breakfast. Scrambled eggs, ham, cereals, soft bisquits & gravy, waffles, pastries and other stuff I can't remember. I ate till i was stuffed. No complaints about the food. It all tasted really good. I paid under $100 for my one night stay. I think I got more than what I paid for.

title: “Breathtaking luxury ... great location.”
text:
Stayed at the St. Regis while on business. The rooms were huge! Room had a spacious shower as well as a bath. Wish I had more time to spend in the hotel proper and take advantage of all the amenities. Free shoe shine ... a plus.
Highlight: I needed to rent a car, and the hotel's concierge took care of me in 10 minutes ... awesome!

title: “Fantastic Hotel”
text:
Just got back from this hotel today and we loved our stay there. 
It's in a great location, just one block from McPherson subway station, bus stops right outside and about 3-4 blocks walk away from the White House. There weren't a great deal of places near by to eat though so be prepared to travel a little further afield for food in the evening. That said, the DC restaurant that is over the road from the hotel was good, and the hotel food itself was also good. We ate in the bar one evening (happy hour 4-7 includes bar food half price) and in the restaurant one evening - free wine when you order a main course... they know how to incentivise!! The Sunday breakfast buffet also offered really good value and there was a good selection.
Our room was lovely. We were upgraded to a junior suite which had tons of room. The hotel itself is very nicely decorated, very clean and modern, but classically styled. This goes through to the rooms too.
The staff were really friendly and very helpful. They couldn't do enough for you. 
I wouldn't hesitate to stay here again if I was in DC.
My one 'must do' DC tip is the Segway tour. Right over the other side of Franklin Square (right outside the hotel) is the segway tour office. This was so much fun and the best way to see the sights. You go round the capital building, the mall, the washington monument, the whitehouse and tons more. I now want a Segway!!

title: “great location, outdated rooms- cleaner pays flying visit”
text: very slow to check us in upon arrival, the hotel though is constantly busy in reception as it really is a popular hotel for Europeans due to its location. Very basic breakfast with their not being a lot of space , breakfast was always busy and chaotic no matter which time we ate . The rooms were not large but were quite adequate ,we heard the cleaner go in to our room from our friends room next door ,and timed it at 3 minutes ...to make bed and wipe around .The windows were filthy unable to see out of the main one in our 10th floor room.All in all a good experience but at 279 US dollars a night for 6 nights we thought it overpriced,but to give it a low rating would be unfair ,had we been spending more time in hotel we may not have been so happy as it is just a basic no frills hotel

title: “PA Traveler”
text: The hotel fit the bill for parking the car at the Philadelphia Airport while on our two week vacation. The rooms were clean and well maintained. The shuttle to and from the airport was very convenient. The lot was not gated, but it was well lit and had numerous security cameras available.

title: “Amazing experience!!!”
text:
We have just returned from a week in San Fransisco at the Renaissance Stanford Court Hotel. What an amazing week! I have never been treated so much like royalty. From the moment we arrived, until we checked out we had a great experience. 
We could never describe how amazing our "personal concierge" was at assisting us in every little detail. He pointed us in the right direction, made arrangements for us to get there, and made sure we had a good time afterwards. That was a personal touch I have never had at any other hotel.
We also miss the beds so much!! They were super comfy!! Such a positive sleeping experience, it did not seem like a hotel, it seemed like HOME!
The breakfast buffet was the greatest, as were the waiters and restaurant staff. And the morning "smoothie" shot was something special! (our favorite was the strawberry one!)
The rooms were spacious and very clean. The windows were such a plus...not only great views of a beautiful city, but they opened so you could get the fresh air. They were beautifully furnished as well. The housekeeping staff was the best. They were on top of things the whole stay. We left our valuables out in plain view, and never had a thought that they would not be there when we returned. Our beds were made as soon as we left, and turned down as soon as we returned at night.
I could go on about this place, but you really need to see for yourself how wonderful this place really is.

title: “Hurricane Sandy life savers”
text:
A big thank you to everyone at the Hilton Times Square for your time, friendliness and comfort during this time. We were previously staying in a Best Western and Comfort Inn in Downtown (both of which lost power), and if we had known that the Hilton was cheaper and more spacious we could have stayed here from the beginning. 
Everything has been top notch.

title: “chicago's desperado destination”
text:
I recently arrived to the BOLD new michigan avenue hotel destination (namely hard rock hotel); and found the experience immediately hip, atmospherically relaxing with simple undertones of elegance, a mindful valet & baggage handler, desk staff aimed to pleased, a vastly knowledgable concierge, rooms that environmentally shifted your mindset from work to pleasure, and a bar/restaurant with healthy and edging cuisine choices ... all in all ... your stay will play as a favorite song! I highly recommend this hotel and experience.
Respectfully,
MJS

title: “Great city, not so great hotel”
text: My children (ages 4 & 6) and I stayed one night at Club Quarters before moving to another hotel. The staff was nice and at first put us up in a suite. The suite looked good and was spacious, but we quickly noticed that the elevator was behind the wall and we would not be able to sleep with the noise of the elevator. We went to get our room changed, but they didn't have any other suites available so we got a standard room. The standard rooms are tiny and definitely not as nice. We decided to make the change so that at least we could sleep at night. The bathroom was tiny and the walls around the shower were cracking and crumbling. I was suprised to discover the hotel was only built 8 years ago. Apparently it was an old bank that Club Quarters converted into a hotel. It also suprised me that given they could have done anything they wanted, they chose to make the rooms so small and cramped. Club Quarters definitely needs to maintain their room better. My recommendation is that if you are going to stay here, get a suite, but not the one located directly next to the elevator.

title: “Awesome stay!!!”
text: After reading some of the reviews placed on here before staying I was absolutely dreading going on holiday!! Even to the point of cancelling and losing our money and trying to find somewhere else, well the worry was wasted!! The hotel and it's staff are amazing, the lobby is spotless with a friendly atmosphere. Hotel staff are eager to help and nothing is too much. Never had to wait for the lift, many other reviews claimed they were useless, well they weren't, they do the job. You press the floor you want on the keypad, it tells you what lift to use and you wait for it, plain and simple!! Room brill, was expecting a little box, but very spacious and clean. Bed and pillows so comfy you don't want to get up and after the busy day running around New York it's something to look forward too! Location again amazing, outside main hotel entrance, turn left and you are less than 5 mins walk from central park and turn right and you are 10 mins away from times square! Cannot fault the hotel at all on anything it's staff, appearance and location are spot on! Would recommend this hotel to all I know, we already planning another visit to New York in the future with friends and am going to stay here again.

title: “Does the job for those on a budget”
text:
The interior grounds look like a typical 70's-style motel with pink door, thick metal railings and a follow-the-maze path to our room. We actually like kitsch and it didn't bother us at all, actually it should stay right this way. The style extended to our room which was unfortunately a little tired (and smelly) but it did the job and we slept well. We didn't try the breakfast as we were leaving at 4am. However, the free shuttle provided a swift ride to LAX which is less than 5 minutes away. It was supposed to leave in 15 minutes but we and other travelers were ready so the driver left right away.
One thing I liked with this property, and the reason I chose it, is its close proximity to many rental car companies. Fox, Thrifty and Payless are right across the street. I just had to check in, gaz up next door, drop the car, and walk back for two minutes to the hotel. That's quite a convenience.
All in around, at that price point it is fine and I would go again. Recommended for any traveler on a budget. Remember it's a Travelodge so people who expect luxury should go to a more upscale chain.

title: “Good Service, Nice Rooms”
text:
I stayed at the Garden Inn with a friend for 3 nights. We were in town to run the marathon and had requested a quiet room away from the elevator. After a smooth check in, we rode the elevator up to our room, took one step out and one step to the right and were at our room. I called down to ask about getting another room (after explaining that I had requested one away from the elevator). The attendant told me she had no record of me asking for this (even though I had the request printed out in my confirmation) and she said all of the rooms were full. So this started off on a bit of a sour note. However, the elevator was in fact quiet so it became a non-issue. The next issue arose on the day of the marathon. We left the room at 4:30 in the morning and came back at 3:30 in the afternoon to find that our room had yet to be cleaned. This was a bit disappointing since we both just wanted to shower and sit down. The housekeeper was apologetic and offered to have another cleaner come back in the evening. So we left for dinner and came back to a semi-clean room- trash was not emptied, supplies were not restocked and it was questionable whether or not our sheets had been changed (we had requested this since we didn't do it the day before). Finally, we called down the next morning to have coffee delivered to our room and it never showed up.
We went down to check out the next morning and the attendant asked us about our stay. We told her about some of the hiccups and she seemed genuinely concerned about what happened and offered to buy us breakfast. 
All in all we were impressed with the staff (they had been very helpful with directions and giving us tape and other supplies) and the rooms and would recommend this hotel for other travelers.

title: “Great Boutique Hotel!”
text: The location of this hotel is super - less than a block from Times Square!  The decor is gorgeous, but it's the staff that makes this property really special.  Everyone was so friendly, and super-helpful.  Genuinely interested in making sure you have a great stay.  The room was beautifully decorated, although small (even by NY standards).  Breakfast was great!  All in all, I would definitely recommend this hotel.

title: “Exceeded Expectations”
text: Spent overnight on a "staycation" with my partner. Everything was terrific. Lots of effort goes into the little things that make you say "wow," which I almost never say about a hotel. Sunday brunch in the restaurant was included and terrific. They aim to please in all respects.

title: “Loved the location and the guitar shaped pool”
text: We walked in and used a Roomsaver coupon. Spent 2 nights there. If you are looking for a location close to Graceland, this is ideal. You can see the pink walls from the Hotel. The guitar shaped pool is a nice idea as are the two 24 hour Elvis movie channels. However, the room itself has an outside corridor. The room was clean but the towels were so thin that you could spit through them. The breakfast buffet was limited and very busy. The seemed to serve only brown spotted bananas. It was also very hot in the breakfast area. However, it was value for money but if I had to offer some advice, bring your own towels. The staff were a real joy. Friendly and helpful at all times.

title: “Loved This Hotel”
text:
What a hotel! The whole team that works there are wonderful. Traveling there for a meeting, upon arrival we met Patricia who took good care of my parents, my brother, sister in law, their two kids and myself. She was absolutely wonderful and so sweet to the kids. I ended up sick with the flue while we were there and the kitchen team wished me to feel better as did the gentleman who brought my hot tea up. He said he heard I was sick and that to just let them know when I needed more hot tea. The pillows were so comfy, the rooms were small but incredibly comfortable as well. The showers were magnificent, especially with being sick. They have so many amenities they offer it just makes for the greatest boutique hotel to stay in. 
It was wonderful and I would tell anyone who is looking to be taken care of beautifully, be close to all of the neat things to see or do in mid-town Manhatten.

title: “a haven with a very high standard of facilities and service”
text: New York is awesome and we have had a wonderful time. The hotel gave us the sanctuary we needed from the hustle and bustle outside. The staff were so gracious and we much appreciate their professionalism. The location was perfect for getting both downtown and uptown, the subway station very nearby. The internet facility enabled us to check places to go and make bookings for meals, exhibtions and the Empire State Building. Rooms were stylish and well-equipped. Our sons loved their huge room with two double beds. The roof top garden was peaceful with its water feature and allowed us to catch our breath, with the very welcome complimentary wine and cheese, before stepping out for an evening on Broadway. We thought the hotel was very well thought out and professionally run. It suited our taste for boutique hotels completely and we thought it was a good sign that there were plenty of Americans there too.

title: “Good Value for money - Excellant location”
text:
Myself and my boyfriend stayed in this hotel in January 2005- apologies as haven't got around to writing until now.
We stayed for 9 nights in january and despite the rain had a fantastic time!
We read the terrible reviews and approached the hotel with a great deal of trepidation, however i can safely say that previous reviews were somewhat exaggerated and the hotel more than met our needs.
We arrived and yes, did have to be moved from the first room we were placed in. As other reviewers have mentioned it was almost as though reception were testing us- with a small room that stank of smoke and looked out onto a brick wall. Once we complained about the first room we were moved to a perfectly adequate room that looked out onto Macy's! I am certain that if we had asked to be moved again we would have been given a better room but at the end of the day we were exhausted from travelling and settled on the 9th floor.
Things to note- the location is fantastic. Madison Sq gardens just over the road- beware of the touts selling tickets outside the hotel- they are more or less the same price in the ground and guarenteed genuine. Macy's is literally two mins walk away- great for stocking up on shopping- tip for any brits visiting- if you visit the customer services desk they'll give you an overseas discount card (when you show your passport) allowing a further 15% discount off all purchses- well worth it!
Hote is also just over the road from subway- saver for feet after you've been walking for hours.
The empire state building is approx 5 mins walk from the hotel and times square 10 mins. This really was a great location as we found that we could walk down broadway to little italy and china town but could also walk uptown to MOMA, central park etc.
Yes the room s aren't great but we had large TV, clean bathroom (free toiletries replaced every day) maid service was excellant- cleared up our shopping bags and misc rubbish every day. Bed was very small but hey, we were happy to cuddle!
Tips for NYC- Zagat guide is great for searching out good restaurants, national history museam free in evenings- bargain! Bloomingdales v expensive compared to saks and macy's. You must take the free staten island ferry to statue of liberty- just as good as the trips. Be prepared for tipping everywhere. Don't take shampoo, shower gel etc,- it's riduculously cheap and comes in huge bottles over in states. Century 21 is a massive discount store next to ground zero- my boyfriend bought DKNY ties for $10 each.

title: “Great Location”
text:
Stayed here 9th Feb thru 13th Feb 2005. This hotel is in a great location for first time visitors who want to see all the attractions in a few days. The rooms were clean and average sized. The only downside to it was the size of the windows, they were tiny and this meant the rooms were very warm.
Staff were exceptional! Helpful and courteous at all times. If I was on the same budget (£80 per night) I'd stay here again.

title: “nice trip”
text: We stayed at the James in early Dec. for our annual girls shopping trip and the location was great for shopping on Mich. Ave.Check in was great as we had an early arrival and were able to go ahead and check in.We had a double room with queen beds,that were wonderfully comfortable.The bath was spotless and the amenities were nice.The evening turndown was wonderful!It was a little awkward for the TV to be behind the sofa, as you couldn't set on it and view the TV,but from the beds the viewing was fine.If I could make a suggestion, it would be better lighting and another chair in the room would be extremely helpful for viewing the television.We hope to stay again this year and look forward to staying here again.

title: “Great Location”
text: Great place to stay while visiting Chicago. Walking distance to shopping and theaters. Lots of places to eat close by. The staff was helpful and friendly. Nice breakfast and comfy beds.

title: “Run-down and noisy - Beward the "Club Floor"”
text:
Expect smallish rooms that are badly in need of remodeling. Shower is just a trickle, carpet is worn, TV is ten years old, etc.
I paid extra for the club floor, on the top two floors of the hotel. However, my room overlooked the service area for the tent they had erected for a conference. There was noise of forklifts and trucks all day. I went to sleep to the sound of backup alarms every night.
The club itself is physically attractive, but quite a rip-off. Don't expect free self-service drinks as in most such places. Everything is brought by a waiter. Alcoholic drinks are at regular hotel bar prices. Non-alcoholic drinks are free, but then they make a big show of presenting a zero bill on which you are supposed to include a tip, so unless you want to be a jerk you end up paying a high price for your free drinks. Breakfast and evening snacks are sparse and tired-looking. 
The location of this hotel is great. There's nothing here that a little demolition wouldn't fix.

title: “Good experiences in the past - but concerned about recent review”
text: I have stayed at this hotel about twice per year since 2002, when it was the Bradford, and then Summerfield, and I intended to book a room for this June. But, now I am concerned about the previous review about the giant cockroach. I am even more concerned about the response from the General Manager. She did not address the bug problem at all - just asked the guest to contact her directly. I previously lived in Texas for 10 years, and understand that Texas has giant cockroaches, but I need to know there is not a cockroach problem in the hotel. I would not be able to sleep there if I saw one. I'm sure others would like reassurance also.

title: “We loved the view!”
text:
We stayed in a king suite. Lovely room with a spectacular view! The corner living room was comfortable and again, that fab view! Tinsy, tiny bathroom, but it functioned well.
The downside? Foam rubber pillows. We asked about down pillows and were told by the bellboy that he would check, but he didn't check. We also asked for a wake-up call on our last morning for 4:20 a.m. to catch an early morning plane. Fortunately I had set the alarm because the wake-up call never happened.

title: “Drink the wine then dine!”
text:
I was here with my significant other for three nights. The deluxe king room was cozy and the bathroom was adequate. Internet service worked throughout our stay. The showers were nice and hot and the room was cleaned everyday. The decor in the rooms may not be the fanciest or newest but the overall service, helpfulness, and great location made our stay enjoyable.
Dave the bartender was very friendly, funny, and helpful. He helped us navigate the city for great places to eat and suggested places we should check out. The receptionist was friendly and accomodating. The free wine was a great way to kick off the evening. Walgreens down the street sells transport passes and the stops on the busses/trolley are right down the street. There is also a great diner down the street that serves breakfast.
All in all we had a great time and would recommend this hotel. It may not be a luxurious hotel but for the price, location, and the helpfulness of the staff, it was well worth it.

title: “The most friendly, cleanest, accommodating, hotel I 've ever stayed in.”
text: Once we (3 best friends) hit the door . We knew this hotel was the best choice we made. All the employees and the maneger ansered questions, gave directions, very freindly. They treated us like family. Breakfast was wonderful, many choices to choose from. At night ( tues. - thur.) a managers beer, wine and appetizers , get together. On oue trips we've never had this where we've stayed. But this was a Great way to meet ,talk, exchange info. with emp. and fellow travelers. We feel your people are like friends and would come back to visit. Also recommend others to stay here. And a special Thank you to Your Outstanding Maneger Ray Velazquez. and Georgia Rios. P.S. The coffee pot is always on. And travlers could use dinning room for card,games, ect. We were there every night. Thank You.

title: “Comfy hotel, great location to explore the city!”
text: We were visiting friends on the nearby Air Force base and decided to spend our last night in the city by ourselves. We chose this hotel because of its close proximity to Chinatown, that it had a cable car stop right outside the hotel, and that it was so highly rated on TripAdvisor. We took the cable car down to the pier and back, were able to take a nice stroll through Chinatown, access the Mission district via BART, and get to the airport via BART. I couldn't recommend this hotel more, just based on its location, but it was also cozy and sweet and perfectly comfortable. It kind of reminded me of a hotel we stayed at in Florence, Italy, a few years ago--just the right amount of space to put your things down, take a nice shower, and get a good night's rest.

title: “Very comfortable hotel with a location that works.”
text:
Ample bedroom with twin double beds. Very comfortable and crisp linen giving a marvellous sleep. Very clean bedroom with a quiet and effective air conditioning unit.
Sign up free of charge to the select guest programme on the hotel website and complimentary juices and hot drinks, as well as newspaper, will be brought up to the room when you wake.
No problems at all about the standards of this hotel.
In my opinion the Downtown location has far more plus points than negative ones. The attractions of the beaches and Hollywood are certainly some way away but buses and metro are both within 5 minutes walk and will deposit you onto Hollywood Boulevard inside 25-30 minutes. The Downtown district is full of architectural interest and highly impressive. Views from the top of the City Hall are splendid, a free treat that is often overlooked by visitors. Also nearby is the fantastic Union Station, with trains out to the valley towns.
True that nearby Pershing Square and Skid Row are filled with transients after dark and are a bit challenging, but trains to Civic Centre metro stop bypass all of that and provide a more comfortable 5 minute walk to the hotel.
The facilities nearby, particularly the cafes of California Plaza, make it pleasant simply to be around the hotel neighbourhood.
Highly recommended.

title: “Nice views, absurd prices”
text: Unfortunately, as it develops its brand, Mandarin Oriental doesn't seem able to produce hotels that come anywhere near the charm of the original Oriental in Bangkok. Their New York hotel is a case in point. Arriving, no one bothered to accompany us to the lifts that go to reception on the 35th floor and we weren't escorted to our room either. Worst of all, this place is very, very noisy, with awful vibrating sounds coming from the lifts and party noise from other rooms and reception areas. Staff have a nose-in-the-air attitude and prices for all services are too high even by New York standards. With hotels like the Caryle and the Four Seasons to chose from, this place had better pull up its socks.

title: “Historic Hotel in beautiful location”
text:
Stayed over Easter weekend to attend the Cherry Blossom Festival. The grounds are beautiful and back up to a national park area. Great location, about a block away from numerous restaurants (restaurants in the Omni are very pricey) and 2 blocks from the metro-line. The room I stayed in was at the end of the hallway, so it was very quiet, the beds are awesome (slept like a rock, which it not normal for me), My room had a small room attached, that had a closet and bathroom which was great for us since one person could shower and dress in privacy, while the other person could sleep undisturbed (the extra door between the bathroom and bedroom, kept bathroom noises out of the bedroom). Staff was very friendly and helpful. 
Some minor problems: I did notice that a small area of ceiling had a different color the rest of the room and I had told the bellman about a foot stool in the room that had a broken leg when he brought my bags up but it was never replaced or repair during my 3 day visit. Also I was told by a Police Officer that the biggest issues they have at the Omni location is stolen luggage from out front of the entryway, where the bellmen leave it. So I would advise you to stay with your luggage until it is in the hotel (don’t get the wrong idea, Hotel is in a nice area and I never felt unsafe walking in the area)

title: “Perfect location to explore Chicago”
text:
This Sheraton was one of the best Sheratons in which I have stayed. It had a few issues (room not ready at check-in time, dresser door broken) but everything was remedied quickly and with a pleasant smile. We just returned from a 5 night stay there'd and were very pleased with our choice of hotel. We had a nice view of the Chicago River and a portion of Lake Michigan and did not even request an upgraded view room. We had requested a slightly larger room because we had my son's wheelchair to store in the room and we were provided with a larger room which was certainly helpful and welcome since there were four of us staying five nights.
The best part of the Sheraton was the location. We were walking distance to practically everything in the city - navy pier, Mag mile (Michigan ave), the loop, grant park, millennium park and even the museum area ( about 1.7 miles to them but totally walkable). We even walked to Sears (Willis tower) and John Hancock Building.
The breakfast buffet at LB Bistro was probably the best I've ever had too!

title: “Very close to convention center”
text: I stayed in this hotel for five nights while attending a conference at the Austin Convention Center. This hotel is very conveniently located to the convention center. The rooms were typical Hampton Inn. They were clean and reasonably large. The had only wired internet in the rooms (wifi in public areas only, but it was free. They provided a typical Hampton Inn free breakfast. The pool was outside, and it was too cold to be used. There were many restaurants within walking distance, and a couple delivered "room service." There was also a coffee shop on the first floor.

title: “You won't be disappointed”
text:
Just came back from a four day stay and have only good things to say about the hotel. Location couldn't be better. Great rate on Choice hotels website. 1/2 block from Michigan Ave. and right on all the bus lines. We came into Millenium station and the bus(157) dropped us right in front of the hotel. Easy walk to tons of restaurants, shopping and Navy Pier. Transportation is so easy in Chicago. Leave your car outside the city (so you don't have to pay to park) and buy a CTA pass (at CVS) that will take you anywhere. Bus drivers are very helpful. We requested a larger room and had no problem with the request. Bathrooms are small, would of liked a vanity instead of pedestal sink. Beds average.
 The West Egg Cafe is excellent for breakfast and right around the corner. 7/11 and Dunkin Donuts right across the street.
 We have stayed in a lot of hotels in downtown Chicago and will definitely be back. Best place we have stayed for the price and location!

title: “quiet, comfortable bed, nice room”
text: Business trip to speak at a lunch meeting at this hotel, so I stayed here the night before. Upgraded to suite. I have a select comfort bed at home so its nice to have one when I travel. This property has select comfort beds in some rooms. Pillow was very nice - firm unlike some cheap pillows that require stacking 2-3 to get enough support. Front desk called a nice cab company to drive me to dinner and picked me up to bring me back to hotel. Front desk allowed later checkout. My flight was not until 5:00pm so was able to checkout at 2:30pm. Complimentary shuttle to and from airport. Called for shuttle from airport when I arrived and they were there in 5-10mins. Even though hotel is near airport, I never heard any air traffic.

title: “A good hotel, but by no means perfect!”
text:
I recently spent three nights at the Fairmont San Jose, attending a conference held in the hotel. My room was comfortable and large enough to accommodate a king-size bed, small sofa, and plenty of space in which to work. Nothing extraordinary, but large, elegant and clean. Three things spoiled the room. Three lamps didn't work. There was a large crack in the basin in the bathroom and there was a horrible smell from the drains. All of these should be easy to identify and fix, and this suggests to me that routine checks and maintenance are overlooked. 
I was given complimentary internet access because I was attending the conference. I used room service one evening. The food was good (though not exceptional), but service was slow (nearly an hour) and supplementary charges made the overall price high.
When so many hotels these days offer broadly the same experience and facilities, it's the attention to details that makes the difference. The Fairmont needs to remember that and improve its overall service.

title: “A horrible, horrible dump!”
text: Room was fillty, broken door knob, trash was strewn around when check in.Complained to the front desk person and was given a key for a different room. Same story again! Given 4 more keys to check out other room, 11th, 12th floor. None was good and 2 huge bags of trash was right by the elevator for 3 days straight! Viny tiles in bathroom was ripped and very dirty. Black stuffs was on the wall and the floor. Old yucky carpet was put on top another old, yucky one underneath. Lints and dirt was visible around edges of carpet. Things need to be fixed everywhere you look! Old window air conditioner didn't work and the temp. outside was 104 degrees, so we were quite miserable. Everything was awful, horrible! Had to put towels on the bathroom floor and the bed and everywhere so we can walk and sit on the bed. There were 4 tiny soap pieces (made in India) on the broken sink and the scent of the soap was bad also. It must be old and cheap soap! I wanted to take pictures to show my family after the trip but decided not to. didn't want to ruin my camera with all the yucky, yucky things in the room. Carter place needs to be demolish. Please call the health department!!!

title: “Excellent Extended Stay Hotel”
text:
We have stayed at this Hotel numerous times and we have always been satisfied. During this trip we are traveling with two disabled family members and booked a two bed room suite. The suite has two queen beds in one bed room and a king bed in the other. The living room and kitchen/dining areas are spacious and comfortable. The Hotel is very clean and well maintained. The staff is professional, courteous and very customer service oriented. Another good sign is that the employee turn over is low. We see the same staff at the front desk, the breakfast area and during the dinner we met during our previous visits. Some still remember our name. The free breakfast every morning is good and the dinner served four evenings a week is actually much better than you would expect for a fee meal, Along with free beer and wine, this is a very good value.
I visit this Hotel three to four times a year and will continue to do so.

title: “1 night for free.”
text: I stayed there for a night for free after finding that Marriott marquis have canceled my booking and they booked me this hotel for free for one night. The hotel is well known, I cant say much more, but the rooms are a bit small and nothing special in decoration, good bathrooms and excellent T.V offers and services such as DVDs and tv channels. Room services are brilliant and very fast. I would recommend this hotel for sure, for who likes to live a luxury life, but, I will not really pay 700 dollars a night to stay here. Nothing special in the rooms.

title: “Japanese Elegance at the Miyako”
text: What an incredible find. Located in LA's Little Tokyo, the Miyako is an oasis with elegantly appointed rooms done in simple Japanese decor. The rooms were good sized and the bathrooms were large with high-tech toilets that do everything but...... Just think toilet/bidet and massage in one. Even though it's downtown, the neighborhood seemed very nice and friendly, even at midnight. There's a dozen Japanese restaurants right across the street and a small inner city mall nearby. The staff was at the least, prompt and efficient and at best, very friendly. My only caveat would be the plasma screen TVs. You say plasma screen and you think high end. But I've noticed at many hotels with plasma TVs that the screens just aren't very good: blurry, poor resolution and pixelation. But it certainly makes a good impression when you walk in the room. I usually stay in West Hollywood, but on a budget. The price, $115, with free broadband and convenience of the Miyako will be hard to beat.

title: “wonderful getaway”
text:
My husband and I spent one night at the NYC Sofitel. We chose the Sofitel based on the Tripadvisor reviews. The check in staff was very attentive. The were actually able to give me a lower rate then I had previously booked. The room was extremley clean. However it was a bit on the smaller side. Rooms are standard with a queen size bed... you need to request a king.Of course we expect that in the city. NIce Plasma TV and very well equipped bathroom. Bed was comfortable and Linens impeccable.
The Hotel Bar was on the smaller side...difficult to find a seat at times even though it was a Sunday evening. Nice bar menu and good staff. The atmosphere in the hotel was quiet and relaxing. You felt removed from the hustle and bustle of the city.
We will definetly return to the Sofitel in NYC.

title: “My 8 year old daughter and myself had the best end of summer trip ever.”
text: We had so much fun that we were sleeping by 9:00 at the latest every evening. Then we were up early each morning waiting for the Oasis to open. My wife was very jealous that she couldn't make the trip. Our photos and how our daughter won't stop talking about it has "mom" very upset that she couldn't get off work. Next time. Thank you AGR.

title: “The smallest most cramped room i have ever stayed in”
text: i was bundled off to 2 of the smallest rooms i have ever been in within the space of 12 hours before being finally given the queen sized room tht i had actually booked... but i soon realised the promised land was no good either... the queen room is only enough to somehow fit in one small bed... one basically needs to walk over the bed to go from the door to the loo... such great design and so badly planned... the corridors are dingy and smelly.. there is no housekeeping service at all .. staying here was the most claustrophobic and cramped i have ever felt in all my travels..

title: “Wonderful staff, with one exception”
text:
I was delighted for the opportunity of a return stay at the Hotel Indigo. Despite others' experience with third-party booking, I was actually treated very well. 
Due to travel delays, I arrived in Chicago near midnight (several hours later than scheduled). I was concerned about the room status since this was a Hotwire booking. But the front desk clerk, Lissa, could not have been more helpful. I phoned ahead and she said, "Yes, I see your Hotwire booking" -- [so she knew this was 3rd party] -- and I have noted your delayed arrival for a reservation of one night." I replied it was actually two nights -- we had added on a second night after the initial reservation. 
Lissa quickly found this information, and remembered it when I finally arrived very late that night at the hotel. Her greeting was friendly and professional -- as soon as I identified myself, she let me know she was the person to whom I had spoken on the phone, and she expressed empathy for the long day of travel delays. (A small thing, perhaps, but it really makes a difference to a tired traveler.) She also told me just to come down to the desk in the morning and they would work out having the "second" reservation applied to my room without necessitating a move.
When I came down the next morning, the only downside was a non-uniformed woman working at the front desk computer. I explained about the reservation consolidation and she *rolled her eyes*(!), made some sort of snorting noise and said "I don't think so," and went back to what she was doing. It was appallingly rude. Luckily a woman standing next to her (who was in the "uniform" of other clerks) quickly said, "Yes, Miss ____, I took care of the reservation this morning and you are all set!" I said the other woman had been very rude; the competent clerk apologized and asked if she could take care of breakfast. I had already eaten, but I appreciated the offer to make things right. Note to management, though: the older woman who works the computer and is not dressed like the clerks should not have contact with guests.
Kudos on the excellent night clerk and morning clerk. I typically book directly through the hotel, although in this instance I used Hotwire on a whim -- and I am pleased to say that I have been treated cordially no matter the booking source (as should be the case in a competently managed hotel.)
P.S. -- The only oddity: since the elevator is near the front door, I realized many guests do not realize there is a small restaurant in the back of the lobby. Rooms have a large menu for a restaurant nextdoor, but no info on in-house dining, which is too bad because it is in a very cute space!

title: “Best stay and service that I have had with a hotel”
text:
We arrived at the hotel at check in time (3PM) and was greeted at the door by the bell man. He was very polite and helped us with our bags to our room. 
Our room was great.. We had 2 rooms side by side.. The beds were to die for, nothing but comfortable.. 
We had room service in the morning, which was great, nothing beats waking up to coffee, muffins, danishes, and crossiants by your bed..
I have stayed at many hotels, but The Hilton Back Bay is by far the best hotel. Location is great close to many restaurants and shops..

title: “Great anniversary destination”
