text: We love the sheraton and return there whenever given the opportunity. It always exceeds our expectations from luxury and ammenaties, to service that goes beyond. This trip was no different. We were celebrating our 19th anniversary and the staff (Mark H) found out the reason for our stay at the time we checked in. He was friendly and kind as we shared the details and then went on our way. Later that night, after returning from an evening out, we were surprised by a beautiful, and delicious, anniversary cake in our room! What a treat and a wonderful surprise. Although my husband tried to take credit (haha), we knew it was Mark's kind efforts that made our evening even more special. We'll be back for sure!

title: “Competitive rates-5 Diamond Resort-Lazy River”
text: Luxury Resort in Phoenix, AZ. The best of everything. 'Nuff said.

title: “Convient”
text: Spent five nights at this hotel, nice location near river, very easy to get about. Only about a 10 minute walk to Michigan Ave and shopping, many places for dining right in the neighborhood. Bar in hotel was pretty expensive, big city prices.

title: “You must avoid the "Bay 2" Rooms”
text:
I was given a room in the Bay 2 building on check in, told that my rate (Corporate) was only for rooms in that building, not in the tower. The building was motel style with open-to-the-outside doors.... Kind of creeped me out. The room looked ok, decor-wise, but was dark and very musty. My co-worker was spot-on when she said that the smell of my room was like a basement. ew. I requested another room (less musty please) and finally given a room at the very bottom of the tower. It smelled far better and did not have the damp-dark feel of the Bay building. Be sure to AVOID the Bay buildings. I am pretty sure those are the rooms that are generating all of the bad reviews on here.
Other items:
Swim bar was great place to hang out, casual, great for football watching, cool bartenders (this is a bar BY the pool, not a cheesy swim up bar)
Red Marlin food and service was great! Enjoyed a nice breakfast and dinner there, very enjoyable, significantly betterr than most hotel restaurants.
If you like to run, ask the concierge for a map. They have little cards to take at guide you on 3 and 6 mile routes.

title: “Really, Off the Avenue”
text: OTA is really off the avenue, as it is about 100 feet west of Broadway on 77th St. This older hotel is undergoing extensive renovations, and the rooms are quite nice and elegantly furnished. Staff are supportive and very helpful. Excellent location on the Upper West Side, close to the Museum of Natural History.

title: “Nice people and location”
text: Location is good, MUNI bus system very easy to use from this hotel. Front desk people were always helpful and nice, hotel is not a Hilton Price for a night is about $100 pretty good considering how much the others places charge. Hotel is clean and safe, breakfast isn't something to write home about but again for the price this place fit our needs for three nights. Bagel place around the block and a Starbucks very close by, up the street on Polk is very good hamburger/family place the served nice food and good service.

title: “First Class !!!”
text: I lived in Chicago for 15 years, but moved away 2 years ago. I decided to return for a long 4 day weekend to visit friends. I knew I wanted to stay near the Water Tower for its shopping and restaurants. Thus, I picked the Sofitel Water Tower for my stay. I was able to find the best rate on the hotel’s website (www.sofitel.com) .The location of this hotel cannot be beat. The hotel sits on a quiet block but is only about 2 blocks to Water Tower. I was impressed the moment I pulled into the entrance for valet parking. I was greeted and offered assistance with my luggage immediately. During check-in I was also greeted with a warm and friendly smile. I was fortunate enough to have a Prestige Suite on the 29th floor. The suite is 700 square feet and is definitely worth the extra money. The view on the 29th floor was amazing. You could view the Hancock Building and Lake Michigan. Then there was the bed. You will feel like you are floating on a cloud. This was the softest bed I have ever experienced. If you don't like soft beds, then you may want to request a firmer bed type before arrival. Next was the living space which feels like a cozy and comfortable apartment. There were 2 hd tv's and a great working area for 2 people. I really feel in love with the bath products----Hermes. This hotel has everything going for it: location, great service, outstanding rooms. I could not ask for anything more. I have stayed at other hotels in the area, but this is now my favorite place in Chicago. I highly recommend the Sofitel Water Tower. I will definitely be staying again.

title: “Horrendous Service - Not in Chelsea”
text:
The hotel is much more in the sketchy shopping/flower district than it is in Chelsea. I paid over $800 for a room and had worse service than $80 hotels. First, it is not in the best neighborhood. 
Second, the Bells just sat there while I unloaded luggage followed by simply pointing to where I can check in... I was in Business Casual attire, so it is not as if there was any reason to be snubbed. They do give you a nice cookie at check in. And lastly, after literally paying a total one night bill of something right near $870, they have the audacity to then charge you almost $10 for wireless service. Are you kidding me??? I have stayed at the Belnord Hotel on the upper west side for a couple hundred dollars and had better service. I highly recommend staying somewhere else....

title: “Home away from Home”
text: We were visiting long time freinds who we haven't seen in years. and wanted to be near in a convienantly located area. We got that and more. The bed was very comfortable and clean. The service was outstanding. We had an issue withh our bill at the end but Mr. Villamar was understanding, patient and resolved it for us. we give the intercontinental two thumbs up and will recommend to family friends and most like come back for a future stay.

title: “Great value”
text: Well located, big rooms, kitchen, helpful staff (Ms.Negesti is one of them). It was not the first time I stayed at the Eastgate Towerand certainly not the last. Great value!

title: “Nice hotel close to San Diego Airport”
text: My wife and I, a retired couple recently had the pleasure of staying one night at the Ramada Limited San Diego Airport. We were very pleased with the location, cleanliness and proximity to the airport. The room was small, adequately furnished and very clean. The mattress was very comfortable. Desk service was very friendly and helpful. Free WiFi is available. The motel is literally across the street from a bunch of nice, non-fast food restaurants located on the marina and a nice place for a leisurely stroll. It is a very short distance form the airport; less than 10 minutes and an easy drive.

title: “Over-rated”
text:
I am business traveler and stay in quite a lot of hotels. Cleanliness and service are what is important to me. On both scales I would rate the Hard Rock as quite poor. When checking in there was only one person at the registration desk and we was overwhelmed because not only did he have people registering but he repeatedly had to answer the phone to deal with guests. There was a sign at the desk highlighting the hotel's remodeled rooms, I asked the person registering if it was possible to get one on the remodeled rooms. The registrar said he would see what he could do. Needless to say the registration process was interrupted by several phone calls. ( I had booked the room because I colleague had selected the hotel so I wanted to be in the same hotel as him. I was booked for an upgraded room. ) The room I received was not remodeled. I understand that he may not have been able to accommodate my request, but it would have been nice if he had told me rather than ignoring my requests. When I stepped off the elevator, the floors are painted in dark colors giving a dank and dungeon like feel which is amplified by very little lighting. The darkness, however, could not hide the carpet mottled with stains. Entering my room things were little different than the hallway. The Carpet is dotted with stains throughout the room and fraying in several places. The walls and furniture are marked up and chipped. There is a small standing wardrobe tucked in an alcove instead of a closet which barely fits two suits and an overcoat. There are two small drawers for clothes. Overall the room is average size but is in very poor condition. Given the state of the carpet, I was happy to have my own slippers because of the filthy carpet but also because no slopers were provided. No robe was provided so I had to call to get a robe sent up. For people use to nice down comforters, there is a comforter on the bed but it is pile filled and quite dated looking. the rooms look and feel dirty which makes any stay feel unpleasant. 
 I used the fitness center. It also is tired and dated. Some equipment seemed to not function properly. They had plenty of towels but oddly the had earphone cover pads but no headsets. Itis in the basement and the motif is dark with a dungeon like feel. 
 As to the service this confirmed my belief that financially the hotel is having difficulty. The service quality is terrible and the hotel is operating with minimal staff. I had a hint of this when I checked in and my assumption was confirmed throughout the stay. When I called room service no one picked up the phone. I tried again allowing it to ring for many minutes. No one picked up. I called the front desk and was told someone from room service would call me back. After waiting, I called room service again finally someone answered. Another example of poor service was that I had to request twice to have a package that was sent to me delivered to my room. The next day after a day of meetings I returned to my room at 4:00 and discovered that my room was still not cleaned. A minute after I entered the room, I hear a knock. I expected the maid, but rather I was greeted by the person checking the minibar. Clearly filling the minibar is more important than cleaning the rooms. I asked if he could send someone to clean the room. He assured me they would, but of course after waiting I had to call housekeeping to get a maid sent up. The service quality of the hotel is poor and indicative of a hotel that is understaffed.
 My guess is that the Hard Rock is having financial difficulties. It may be confined to this property but the condition of the hotel and the poor service indicate to me that they are cutting corners. I would not recommend staying here.

title: “Would go back to San Fran just to stay at the Argonaut”
text: My family and I stayed here on the recomendation of Trip Advisor and I will never travel again without checking here first. We had taken a long driving vacation thru the southwest and ended up in San Fran. Never having been before we were looking forward to our last stop. It could not have been better. The staff was extremely helpful and friendly. And the rooms were great. I had a hard time getting to sleep when I got home because my bed cant compare to the comfort of the beds at the Argonaut. Rooms were large and warm which was needed as it was cold and wet outside. I will not go to San Fran again unless I can stay here.

title: “Great Hotel in SF”
text: My Husband and I stayed two night in this past weekend (July 6&7) to celebrate my 10th wedding anniversary. We had stayed in this hotel three times in the past three years. I debated if we should stay somewhere else for this special visit before I booked my hotel. I am so glad I stuck with Omni SF. The staff was extremely friendly, totally up to par for solid 4 star hotel. It was easy in and out to drive to the Hotel. Valet guys were very helpful. By the way, $27/day valet parking w/in&out privilege in Fri&Sat is a good deal. Walking in the hotel, we were greeted with two glasses of Champagne upon arrival. Omni Royal Ambassador Debora Tjandra surprised us with a bottle of Champagne and Strawberry coated classic Chocolate in our room for our special 10th Wedding Anniversary! Thank you so much Debora! Thank you Omni SF! The room was very clean and comfortable. Watching quite a bit of Hotel Impossible lately, I did the thorough check of the bed and bath room like the way Anthony Melchiorri does his inspection. Absolutely NO complain! Bed and Pillow were all very good. Bath room was spotless. I am happy with every single aspect. Location is really good, walking distance to everywhere. Walking distance to have anthony bourdain's SF visit experience (R&G Lounge, Tonga room, north beach, farmer's market etc). Cable car is right outside of door. As Omni select guest for the past several year, I am thrill to see Omni SF always keep to the level it should be. I will go back for sure!

title: “Needs sound proofing bad!”
text: Ok for one night clean and inexpensive. But the room next door sounded like they were in my room. Paper thin walls

title: “Best place to stay!”
text: I loved staying at Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers. It is a beautiful place and one of my favorites was the river walk right next to the hotel. The room was excellent and clean and I was so comfortable in the bed. I got a great nights rest, wonderfull food and the staff at the hotel was the best I have ever experienced!! I highly recommend Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers!

title: “Wow what a place to start your trip”
text:
We have just returned from a holiday to New England and decided to start our trip with three nights in New York, so we thought where else than the Waldorf. We booked directly with the hotel, but then after visiting the Trip Advisor reviews we were more than a little worried by what we read. No need, we arrived at the Waldorf to be greeted by a delightful bell boy, who introduced himself and said if there was anything he could do, we only needed to ask. Check in was swift, and within 10 minutes we were in our room, which was delightful, lovely furnishings and bathroom everything we had hoped for. During our stay the concierge station was always helpful with theatre tickets and restaurants for dinner. They recommended a really nice Italian and the food was excellent. 
I can't praise this hotel enough, no wonder a lot of the staff are long standing. You can tell.

title: “Elegancy of another age”
text:
This hotel is very elegant and historic with rooms who get the view of Lake Michigan. Some of the rooms can be very romantic, other kind can be small and dark, all depends of the budget! Now as an old fashioned thing, there won't be wifi but they do have a hard wired internet connection. The hotel lobby court is wonderful for drinks and a snack with nice music. The Drake does housekeeping very well, excellent soaps, shampoo, conditioner & body creams as well. The food is also quite good, the Palm Court is a true delight. Service is as it should be... quick, seamless...
What I don't like : papers on the walls and some cheesy stuff that make the decor overdated. The hotel needs renovation to enter 21th century.
Cherry on the cake : Drake is extraordinarily convenient to shopping inner or outside with Rush Street about a 5 minute walk away...

title: “Long stay for business travel”
text:
The hotel location is pretty near to the airport but you won't be hearing any airplanes noises though. There's a list of eateries nearby or within the shuttle route at the front desk. They have free shuttle van to airport 24 hours a day as well as some other location. It is also near to the train station that goes to town. Free WIFI available in the rooms. No laundry during the weekend. Self laundry is available in one of the building. Breakfast spread are OK. They have social nights where there are food and drinks available to the guests. Pool and gym are located nearby the lobby area. The staffs are friendly and helpful.
A few things for me to comment was, no one was around to help me with the luggage when I arrived (8 pm on a Sunday night) though I did saw some baggage trolley there. I was located on first floor where the AC unit was located beside the building and it got pretty loud during the night which was not helpful when you are fighting to beat the jet lag. Lastly, did received 1 question from 1 of the staff which was rather sensitive (religion related). Others might have not taken it as lightly as I have. Just a thought to share.

title: “Definately worth the price”
text: Great location - easy walk to 6th street. Room was as expected, some obvious wear and tear but overall good condition. Nice TV, comfortable bed, decent size room w/micro & fridge. Breakfast also as expected - simple but adequate. Only complaints were the Internet was very slow at times and the water was not quite hot enough. Staff was very nice. Great value for the price!

title: “Really nice staff but lots of thing went wrong.”
text: This hotel has a swell location, it's a very pretty place, and the staff are super nice. But there was construction going on; the escalator was out of service and one elevator bank was broken - so for my four-day stay, there was just one set of elevators for the whole hotel, and that meant at least a 3-5 minute wait for each trip. They shut the water off most of one day but didn't warn me about it; and each time I left my room, I'd have to make a double trip back to registration because my card key wouldn't work. Every time. The complementary breakfast and bar is really nice, but room service food is inedible. All in all - a handful of nice things, but quite a few irritations.

title: “Cool and Modern”
text: Native New Yorker that now lives on the west coast. Went back home for a wedding. Was pleasantly surprised by how beautiful the hotel was. The staff was friendly didn't bother you at all. It would be a great business hotel. It is all the way on the west side so it is a bit out of the way if you are walking in the winter to the train. but, the weather was beautiful and took $6-15 dollar cabs almost everywhere we wanted to go. Stayed in the Hudson room. It had a separate living room area with its own flat screen. Very cool to entertain friends after a night out. Bed was comfortable and the bathroom pretty big. The shower had the multi heads and the rain shower head. Loved my showers. The view of the river and the Intrepid were priceless. Rooftop bar is super cool. Restaurant had good breakfast but a bit pricy ($15-20).

title: “Poor Living Conditions”
text: The room I had was unsanitary are roach infested. I reported it to the front desk the very next day they told me I had to call a 1-800 number I did and was told I would hear from someone soon. I'm still waiting to talk to them and I'm still living in these unclean conditions because I can't get my money back.Every morning when I get up there are roaches in the sink. The bathroom was horrible and filthy I had to clean it myself. Thank God my apartment will be ready soon and this only temporary for me but God help the ones who have to stay in such poor living conditions.

title: “Perfect Stay, Excellent Location, More For Your Money ...”
text: I was surprised to find that the hotel outdid any review I had read. The staff is MORE than helpful & nicer than ever. Accommodations where wonderful. For those who are looking to stay in the union square area, it is Safe, Pleasant, Comfortable, Helpful, Real SAN FRANCISCO Charm ... I could go on & on & on. Feb. 2005 was when I stayed & I will certainly be returning to stay here again & again & again. I will also be telling all my friends & family about my wonderful experience there. ENJOY!!!

title: “Don't stay here!!”
text: The entrance is grand but don't be fooled. The rooms are very small and very (very) old! Service sucks. We arrived one morning at 10am and we're told we couldn't check in before 3pm to our room as no rooms were available and had to sit in the bar. When we spoke to the manager suddenly a room became available. The doormen are only interested in looking at your hands to see how much tip they will get. None of them helped us take our luggage up the stairs. One night all the corridors stunk of smoke. The door to our room stops about 3 inches off the ground so the smell enters the room. There is also no room service between 11pm and 8am. A hotel in NYC with no room service. Absurd. You also have to pay for wireless internet access. You can use it for free at the coffee shop opposite. But the hotel makes you pay to use your laptop. The linen on the bed is also really cheap. So much so that you get static on your clothes and shocks when you turn on the light after being in bed. Cheap and nasty

title: “Home away from Home...”
text:
Have stayed at the Hilton in San Jose and always enjoy returning.
Great staff and the newly renovated property is fantastic!

title: “Excellent Stay”
text: I took my husband to New York for his 40th Birthday. I had contemplated cancelling the booking after reading so many negative comments about the lifts. I'm so pleased we didn't - they let us check in early, we had a lovely room with a bed so comfy we wanted to take it home with us. The lifts weren't a problem the only time it took more than 30 seconds was on Friday and Saturday evening when the hotel was full and then the staff helped out. The location is amazing and so convenient. Room service was excellent - bit pricey but what do you expect? I really can't fault the hotel and will recommend it to anyone who will listen!

title: “Great hotel, location & price”
text: I was looking for an affordable hotel over Columbus Day weekend. This hotel had an awesome location. It's right on the edge of North Beach, Chinatown and the financial district. We could walk everywhere we wanted to go, Peir 39 and the Wharf, all the restaurants in North Beach, the Embarcadero, we even walked to AT&T Park only to watch the Giants loose game 2 of the NLCS! The bus stops are close to get to BART, Union Square or the Wharf if you prefer not to walk. The service at the hotel was excellent. The continental breakfast was good. My only complaint is that the walls are thin and if your neighbors are the slightest bit noisy, you will know. I am planning on going back next year and will most likely stay there again. You can't beat the location.

title: “Great location!”
text:
Used for a 3 day stay in DC. 
Check-in hassle, friendly professional reception staff. 
Clean, well appointed rooms. Spotlessly clean bathroom.
Breakfast room, buffet on offer, good breakfast options, attentive staff, a great plus!
Location? Easily found by taxi drivers, a 10 (?) minute walk to nearest DC metro stop. 
Neighborhood? Safe, not too noisy, despite constant front door traffic. 
Positives? Professional staff, clean rooms
Negatives? Infuriatingly annoying hotel wifi. Patchy. Inconsistent (but complimentary!), no mini-bar-fridge.

title: “Worst hotel experience of my life!”
text: I have stayed at hundreds of hotels (including many 1-star) and have never wrote a bad review or even felt compelled to do so until this experience. There was a drug deal going on as we checked in and there were drug baggies all over the parking lot and grass of the hotel. We had to leave in the middle of the night after the people in the next room were trying to forcefully enter our room. There is a club in the hotel which resulted in alot of people all over the place making a lot of noise. Before we fled we were not able to sleep at all and we were exhausted. We had to drive back home and then drive back to Baltimore again the next morning. The staff are like robots and could care less. When we left, there were police on site at the hotel as it was completely out of control. There were also prostitutes entering a room. I still cannot believe this hotel is a Best Western and I would never have expected this as the reviews were relatively good and the photos (the lobby and pool) were nice and are realistic. Do not stay here!

title: “Only mom loves me more”
text:
We stayed at the Omni for my birthday weekend. Not only did they accommodate us with an early check-in, they gave us an upgraded room! That evening, we returned to the hotel to find a piece of incredibly good chocolate birthday cake big enough to share, along with chocolate chip cookies milk on a personalized plate for our 11-y/o. I don't think anybody has made such a big fuss over my birthday since I was 11. The following morning - my actual birthday - when we walked into the lobby the front-desk manager sang out, "Happy Birthday!"
The location of the hotel is great - within easy walking distance to Chinatown and the Ferry Building. We got excellent advice on restaurants and things to do, and all the staff was very friendly and helpful. This is definitely at the top of my list of places to stay while in SF.

title: “Poor value”
text:
We just returned from 3 night at this hotel and were disappointed. 
The front valet staff speak poor English and can't provide basic directions even around the city. The belman who took our luggage to the room spoke indiscernable English as well. He seemed perfectly friendly as he listed the amenities of the hotel, though we understood very little.
The hotel is near the Capitol and surrounding attractions which adds the prime attribute to the place. The room was fine and beds moderately comfortable. Food is reasonably good.
Front desk phones aren't answered promplty when calling from the room, so be prepared to wait. Further, bring your own umbrella if rain is forecasted because they might run out of them as we discovered.
They don't guarantee King size beds even though they told us on the phone that we had a King size bed reserved. 
I wouldn't spend over $300 per night on this hotel if others are available.

title: “Just okay”
text: The Wingate is one of my favorate fallback hotels that cater to the business traveller. This particular Wingate is adequate but it is absolutely ready to be remodeled. The newer Wingates are far superior to this one.

title: “Best Hotel on the West Coast”
text: This hotel is one of a kind - the staff treats you like family and the accomdations are movie star-esq....GM Bob Lacasse is doing a wonderful job.

title: “Omni even better on second trip this year”
text: The front door staff, especially the supervisor, were extremely helpful during our 4 night stay this month. We love the location next to MOCA and near downtown restaurants and the Metro. The hotel is very comfortable and handsome. I just wish they would clean the exterior windows. Although the Grand Cafe is a little pricey for breakfast and lunch, the food, service and ambience are all very good. The courtesy car for trips within 3 miles is definitely a strong bonus at this hotel.

title: “Nice Hotel in a great location”
text: I stayed six nights at the New Yorker for a business trip. The hotel is conveniently located on 8th and 34th. The walk to the Jacob Javitts Convention Center was an enjoyable 10-15 minutes walk. My room was clean and roomy, with a small walk in closet. I enjoyed having a view of the river from my room and not looking at another building 10 feet away. Conveniently, Starbucks & Penn Station is located just across the street. Each night we walked to Times Square and the restaurant row area on 46th between 8th & 9th street. This NYC hotel was reasonable at $189.00/night. The Tick Toc Diner in the hotel is open 24 hours a day. The bathroom was small, with a pedestal sink and a tub buy lacked ample shelving to place all of a womens H&B items. I would stay at this hotel again.

title: “Beautiful stay in a lovely setting”
text: We needed a comfortable and friendly hotel as we were staying for 6 nights and Hotel Teatro filled our needs in a most gracious manner. The room was small but we have stayed in smaller rooms in Europe so that wasn't a bother as we were visiting our daughter and her husband so we were out most of the time. The bed was extremely comfortable with delicious linens. I phoned the hotel upon our return to find out if they were Frette and what the thread count was. I received a long distance phone call answering my questions. The staff is young and very courteous. The sink was sluggish in the bathroom but it was fixed very quickly when we reported it. The only tiny negative thing was the t.v. reception but that hardly seems important as everything else lived up to and beyond our expectations. The french doors leading to a small balcony overlooking the clock tower was most welcome. We will definitly stay at the hotel again when we visit Denver.

title: “Not as bad as expected!”
text:
We booked our break to New York in March 2010, my husband and I were very excited until we checked the most recent reviews of the Hotel Radisson Lexington. When we arrived we were given an ample room although the bathroom could have benefitted from a refit.
The staff were very friendly and not pushy or wanting tipped all the time!!
Starbucks was in the foyer which was a major plus. The hotel also had a good gym which my husband used everyday. 
Staff were very helpful at the guest services and booked our transport back to the airport and also very knowledge.
Radisson Lexington is in a great central position.

title: “AIDA Plaza is a nice homebase to stay in the vivid centre of SFO”
text: I enjoyed the old fashioned style of this hotel. My room was nice and clean. I you don't mind staying in a vivid area of the city, you will enjoy finding everything around the corner. AIDA is a pleasant alternative to hostels. The crew of the hotel was always nice and friendly. The lobby is very often filled with guests checking their mails. There's always coffee and tea available. I will be back here next time in SFO.

title: “Wonderful Beds”
text:
I went to visit my daughter who is going to college in Arizona. It was spring break. We stayed two nights and enjoyed our stay.
I went there thinking it would be quiet. It was probably the wrong time to go for that. Many of the guests had small kids. The rooms were not as quiet as I remember Drury Inns being. The breakfast and evening drinks and food were pretty crazy, but tolerable. They ran out of things like coffee cups and hot appetizers, but they were very responsive and did their best to keep up.
The main thing that my daughter and I enjoyed were the beds. I should have looked at the mattress maker. They were extremely comfortable. My daughter, who sleeps on dorm room beds thought it was the the best part of the stay. It was hard to get up in the morning.
The staff was very friendly and helpful. I recommend this hotel, but don't expect a sound proof room.

title: “Wonderful bed!”
text:
This is the first hotel we have stayed in where the maid service actually honored our "do not disturb" sign on the door! We slept til 2pm without a single knock on the door. Also, when they clean the rooms, I noticed they go in the room and close the door - that way the noise from the vacumn cleaner doesn't bother anyone. 
My one and only complaint was that there was no hot water, only very luke warm for the bathtub when I ran a bath at 9:00am on our first day and again at 2:00pm the next day. I was hoping for a nice hot soak. We were on the 9th floor....which may or may not have anything to do with anything.
The front desk staff was very friendly and helpful. We had asked them to call us a cab to take us to the clubs on 6th street, and instead they offered their van shuttle and we only had to tip the driver. We will definitely stay at this hotel again.

title: “Loved it!”
text: I had never stayed at a Kimpton property before so I was a little leery. I am in love. I have found my new hotel chain. As soon as my husband and I entered the facility we were greeted by an amazing staff. Everyone was very friendly and went out of their way to ensure that we enjoyed our trip. For a hotel that also allows pets I was very impressed with how clean our room was. It was cleaner than some establishments that do not allow pets. The hotel is also in a great location and probably a 30 second walk to Starbucks. Probably a 5 minute walk to the train station. I can't wait to go back!

title: “This hotel has lost whatever positives it once had.”
text: Friday check in 6:30PM Hilton Diamond Member--meant nothing--check in very impersonal , care less attitude. No consideration of membership status at all when given a room with 20 year old TV and paper thin walls. Friday and Saturday night--no sleep due to loud and out of control party next door. Called security on numerous occasions and all they did was ask the multiple people in the room to "please keep it down" . Parties on both nights went until after 2AM and this hotel could care less. Checking out of this "hotel or club" in one (1) hour to go home and get some sleep. I have stayed here in the past but will be sure to find alternatives in my 4-5 visits to Chicago per year.

title: “Clean and smelling like roses”
text: Friendly staff and the DVD library was a nice surprise. First time I've experienced an Eco theme which made it more boutique-ey. Location is central in Bush St and only down the road to Union Square. Also pretty much on the route to the Piers via Chinatown and Little Italy for either the cable car or buses. Great location for the price(winter time).

title: “Great location”
text: We stayed four nights, the king suites are beautiful, spacious, nice large closet and bathroom. When we were ready to go to the San Jose airport they picked us up at the door, wonderful service. We will go back there, the hotel is in the heart of Silicon Valley.

title: “Great Location, Nice Facility, NY PRICES”
text: This is a very nice hotel. The rooms are large by NYC standards. The location is right on Times Square so is excellent if you like being in the middle of all that. You can walk to the theaters, shops restaurants etc. It is a few blocks to the nearest subway if you are traveling about town. There is no frig in the room, the bed was quite comfortable, breakfast was $30 for nothing that special, everything here is pricey but if you are paying $400-$500 for a room I guess you should expect that.

title: “Hotel Carlton Sutter Street”
text:
Great location, great service, great rooms. Amazing value for your money and right in the middle of down town SFO. The Hotel Carlton is a smaller boutique hotel ideal for anyone who loves to travel, loves great style and service but doesn't have the duckets to throw away. Must mention, Theo at the front desk is great, always warm and always attentive to the guest's needs. 
Cool surprise is the SAHA restaurant, which serves Morroccan/Yehmeni food. It is by far the best Moroccan I've tasted so far (sorry to all the others), we blew a $100.00 on dinner which was reasonable given what we got. 
The only negative is if you have noisy neighbors, but that's a complete variable. Otherwise, we woke up and showered to city views, and looked forward to coming back each night. 
I'd stay again in a heartbeat. In fact, I'm probably booking this month :)

title: “Great Hotel for Family Vacations to D.C.”
text:
This summer my family and I travelled to D.C., for vacation. We were not sure where to stay, safety was our top priority. After researching the area hotels we booked with L'Enfant Plaza Hotel. It is a great location to the Mall area. It was safe, and it has a Metro Station located in the lower level of the hotel. The hotel resturant was great and there were other resturants located in the lower level of the hotel plaza. The interaction with the hotel staff was great, they were always trying to please us. It is a very safe location with good security and surrounded by Federal Offices and Law Enforcement. There was an excellent view of the Mall area from out room. We will be staying there next time we are in D,C.. I would strongly recommend it to families or 
business travellers in the DC area.
David Call, North Carolina

title: “Great hotel and location”
text: My husband and I spent five nights at this hotel during our first trip to New York. It is conveniently located to explore the Soho, Tribeca and Greenwich Village areas, as well as having two subway stops nearby (Spring Street and Canal Street). The rooms are a good size by European standards and were spotlessly clean. The bed was comfortable, the shower was excellent and there was plenty of closet space, which is not always the case in hotels. Free wifi was included in the room price. All staff members we dealt with were friendly and courteous. It was one of the few hotels in Manhattan which offered complimentary breakfast. There was plenty of choice, including a waffle machine to make your own fresh waffles. Guests can help themselves to tea and coffee 24/7 in the breakfast room and complimentary cookies are ordered in each day from the bakery which is a nice touch. There is a small bar in the lobby and an ATM. Despite the hotel being quite full while we were there, away from the lobby area, the hotel remained quiet. There are a plethora of restaurants, bars and shops in Soho and Greenwich Village which can be reached on foot or a short subway ride and we enjoyed spending our evenings there. We bought the 7 day metrocard and were able to explore Manhattan easily, day or night. If you are looking to stay away from the more “touristy” areas while still being in an excellent Manhattan location, I would definitely recommend this hotel. I would certainly stay there again if I return to New York.

title: “Not the "Best" that Boston has to offer - Detailed Review”
text:
Truly I would like to give this hotel a 2.5/5 stars. Let's just say that Best Western isn't exactly the best. However, you definitely get what you paid for...
I booked this hotel because of the number of amenities for the low cost, plus a decently close proximity to downtown. It is one of the very few hotels in the Boston area that offers free Wi-Fi, breakfast, parking, and even a shuttle service for an affordable price. Needless to say, I was sold. Though, not so much after arrival...
The Roundhouse is a neat building, as it is completely round and pretty old. It's located in a sort of industrial/commercial area and just down the road from a pretty busy hospital (very noisy). It is not the nicest area of Boston, but I can't say that I felt as if I would be mugged or in immediate danger. I would just recommend being very street-smart at night and to use your common sense. 
Though because of the location, the free parking was a bit of a problem. There is a main lot, but it is on the main street. The area surrounding, like I said, is not the best. While I didn't feel totally unsafe, I certainly did not like leaving my car in that location. There is additional parking behind the hotel, which I used mostly, due to the fact that I could see my car from my room in those spots. However, all of the parking is poorly laid out. The lots are just oddly located. The spots behind the building are hard to maneuver. They are very, very poorly lit. As far as I could see, there were no security cameras. All of that was a little unsettling. 
Inside, the hotel looks pretty standard for a Best Western. The lobby was always pretty clean, so was the breakfast area. Both were small, though. Check-in was quick and easy. The front desk staff were decently nice. However, the smell of the inside of the hotel's lobby and floors was absolutely wretched. It smelled incredibly musty and old. Given the age of the building, it is understandable to encounter a bit of odor, but this was practically unbearable. It made entering and exiting the hotel uncomfortable.
Our room was decent and was odor-free. It was spacious, hosting a small living area, bedroom with a king size, and bathroom. Closet space was standard. There were two TVs. The furnishings were standard, but slightly worn. The bed was moderately comfortable. The cable for the TVs was always messing up. One day, one of the TVs didn't even work. The light switches by the bed stuck a lot and were hard to turn on and off. However, there was ample lighting. Overall, the room itself gets a 3.5/5. 
The bedroom and living space were reasonably clean. The bed was clean and made nicely, but if you examined around the room, there was a lot of dust behind and around things. The bathroom upon our arrival had not been cleaned well. There were a few hairs in the tub. I didn't make a stink, though. I took some Kleenex and wiped them away. However, when I went to unroll the tub mat to shower, I was disgusted. It smelled pretty rank and had dirt and debris particles on it. It was also wet. My boyfriend called the front desk for a replacement and they brought up one promptly. However, the maid never removed the old one from our room and it remained under the sink area for the remainder of our stay. That ticked me off a bit. There were a few bugs in our room. Not bed bugs, but still not pleasant. For a nearly week long stay, our sheets and bedding were changed once. The towels were not exceptionally clean and had a weird smell. Cleanliness and maid service was poor, overall. It could have been worse, but it could have been a whole lot better. 2/5
The room was VERY noisy at night. That does not bother me, as I am not a light sleeper. However, I can see how it would bother some. Trucks, cars, and plenty of other vehicles were driving past at all hours. The hotel is even next to a Sunoco, so tons of traffic expected. The hospital nearby provides plenty of sirens at all hours and a lot of the traffic. So, if you sleep lightly, rethink your stay.
Breakfast was a madhouse. This is not entirely the hotel's fault. Because of the affordability, this hotel is busy with lots of travelers and families. The breakfast area is very small and simply cannot accommodate the number of guests the hotel hosts. This wouldn't be so bad if the guests were not so rude. People cut in front of you, push, shove, and are just downright terrible. If idiots and their idiot children with no manners get on your nerves, I caution you to rethink your stay on that fact alone. That is not Best Western's fault, though. Needless to say, we brought our breakfast to our room! The complimentary breakfast, however, was not that awesome, but it was not horrible. It hosted a better variety than some hotels: bacon, eggs (still frozen and not good, though), waffles, yogurt, fruit (not the freshest), cereal, bagels, toast, etc. But the menu never changed and often the items were prepared all that well. Like the eggs, we tried them one morning and actually took them into our room, put them in the microwave for 1 minute, and they were still frozen! Yuck! Overall, this complimentary breakfast receives a 3/5.
The Wi-Fi was speedy and awesome. Nice freebie. 5/5
The shuttle was always busy and a bit confusing. We had a car, so we didn't use it. Can't review it.
Traveling from the hotel into downtown is quick and simple if you have a vehicle. I thought the geographical location was a decent value for the price. We were just five to twenty minutes away from all of the attractions. Usually only about ten. That was nice. However, this is not a good location if you lack transportation, as the walks required to most things are a bit far. 
We only got free cookies one night. They were good, but there never seemed to be very many available. That made me sad. :(
Also, there was construction going on around our building, which rendered us without hot water for half of our stay. We were notified very late at night by a note under the door of the issue, after we had already went to shower and noticed on our own. They offered no compensation, except a sorry. The next day the water was fine, but the night after it was ice cold again. We called the front desk to let them know. They offered to change our room, but since it was an issue for the building, we didn't see how that would exactly solve the issue. The next morning, there was still no hot water. They still did not offer us any compensation and were not very apologetic when I mentioned it at check-out. That ticked me off. 
Overall, I was a bit disappointed and unimpressed. For the price, it isn't horrible, but there is better available. This hotel needs to mostly improve its parking by installing a few outside lights and its overall smell and cleanliness.

title: “Great Place To Stay”
text: Great Hotel! I come to New York City often for both business and personal reasons and always stay at the Affinia Manhattan. It is business friendly and the pleasant staff is customer-focused, well trained and very perceptive and responsive to your personalized needs. The Affinia’s up-to-date conference rooms support business meetings very well. The Niles restaurant located within the hotel lends itself very well to team group dining. I might add that the food is delicious, too! The rooms are clean and stylish. Located in midtown across from Penn Station, it is the perfect home base for all your professional or personal needs. You can get anywhere you want in NYC very conveniently. I highly recommend this hotel for business or personal trips - the perfect home base!

title: “Perfect Location”
text:
Hotel is just north of Times Square, and perfectly located for exploring the city - especially if this is your first time visit. Rooms are beautifully appointed with great deep soaking tubs. 
Only drawback to the hotel is that the bar with the view of of TS closes super early, which is tragic. It can also be a bit noisy because of location -- but if you want a totally quiet room don't stay in TS.

title: “dated rooms, great amenities”
text:
Checkin at 2300hrs was pretty weak: 1 person in line ahead of me, 2 people behind me, one agent, took 20 minutes til she could be freed up and see us. Our check in took 30 seconds. Didn't get a SPG Plat upgrade. Room was nice, but getting a bit dated. Clean. Loud AC. Internet had avg speed.
The pool was awesome, really nice for a 4pts. Woulda expected this from a Sheraton or something. There was a bar, too, but from what I recall, it was a bit pricy.
There was a parking charge as well. Like most parking charges, this can be avoided by looking around for free parking. 
Location was meh. It's an airport hotel, whadda expect.
The amenities here are top notch for a 4 points, I'll come back if I ever get stranded.

title: “Warm and Friendly Staff”
text: My wife and I were in New York City for a funeral with our grown sons and other relatives, including an infant. All in all, we had 5 rooms at the Hilton Garden Inn - Chelsea. The hotel is on a rather unattractive street in Manhattan, but within easy walking distance from Penn Station and many mid-town locations. As soon as we arrived we were struck by the staff. They were very friendly and accommodating, and everyone made our two-night stay enjoyable. The hotel is attractive inside, and the rooms are large (for New York City) and well designed. I especially like the Herman Miller desk chairs, which I now understand are a feature of many Hilton Garden Inns. Breakfast was very good. It is not "free" as in some other hotels, but the fact that guests pay for breakfast means the food is better than most "free" breakfasts and the dining room is less crowded. The breakfast staff were as accommodating to our group of 10 as were all the other staff, putting together a large table for us each morning. Overall, a great experience. And, it has made this formerly Marriott-centered traveler look for more Hilton Garden Inns, such as the one where we are right now. (Review to follow after we leave.)

title: “Excellent location, friendly helpfull staff, Gay neighbourhood..”
text:
I stayed for a week tru St Patricks day. The location was great, cheep diner next door, food market at the end of the block and subway 2 blocks away, easy to get around.
The room was a fine size, for NY !, King bed, comfy, heating a bit noisey, was on the 12th floor, not much of a view, builders across the road making noise at 8am so not very helpful for a lyin.
The room was cleaned each day, free Internet access in the room, or 2 pc's in the lobby to use for guests, free. Free small btl of water in the room each day, and free starbuks coffee in the lobby up to 11am, bathroom was an ok size, walk in shower, nice. the usual shower gels there too, and a hairdryer. The walls are a bit on the thin side, can hear the tv in the nxt room, and the doors are always left slam shut, so quite noisey when this happens.
The food and drink was a bit pricey in the hotel, cheep diner 2 doors away, shops and food market at the end of the block.
The staff were very friendly, I brought the wrong adapter for my phone charger and the lady in reception gave me a loan of one for the week, no charge !
Gay bar right behind the hotel so happy days lol.
I enjoyed my stay.

title: “Wonderful rooms, great decor, reasonable rates & decent breakfast”
text: This hotel was a great value for the price. Very clean and high end decor both in the lobby and the rooms. Generous space in the room and comfortable beds. The bathroom also was fairly large. We had a cot brought in and still felt spacious. Large flat screen TV, mini fridge & microwave. Service was great. The free breakfast was good, we missed the free evening snack but will try next time I stay at a Drury hotel. I would recommend any Drury hotel after this experience. Free wifi was easy no password needed, snacks in lobby at all times, great service.

title: “Employee Customer Service goes above & Beyond”
text: Having trained customer service in a service environment (casino), having an employee go above & beyond is rare. Audrea S. bartender at V's lounge did just that. A couple came in wanting to have 10 guests come in for a surprise bday party in the lounge. The lounge had already been booked for a private party. Audrea could have just told the couple that and had them leave, but instead, she went to find her supervisor to see about other arrangements. Other arrangements were made and the couple could have their surprise party. Just wanted to pass this along. Good Job.

title: “Good for the money”
text: The location is fairly good, but a little rough around the edges. Its a good base to see San Francisco from though and is walking distance to Union Square, with some decent restaurants near by too.

title: “Not that great- especially for the price”
text: I stay almost exclusively at Marriott hotels, and found this one to be very underwhelming, especially at $300 a night. My room overlooked construction, my bathtub drain-stop was lying in the middele of the tub, the staff was minimally pleasant. Won't be back.

title: “Great sized room in a superb loaction”
text:
As 5 of us were travelling we booked a two room suite which are quite rare in New York. A couple of weeks before travel we were advised that this room was no longer available a t this time. Instead we were offered a one bed suite and a studio suite in adjoining rooms which turned out to be fine.
Reading the reviews we were concerned by some of the comments on the quality of the hotel. Whiilst the carpet was a bit threadbare and the sofa bed was a bit tatty, this was more than compensated for by the size of the accomodation and the high standard of cleanliness. The beds were super comfy and the kitchen was a real bonus. Also we travelled during a heatwave and were impressed that the AC performed realy well.
In terms of location, we found it to be a very quite and safe part of the city. The closest subway was about 10 minutes walk away but we used the M50 bus which stops just on the other side of 1st Aveneue . This provides a frequent service cross town to 5th Avenue and Time Square/Broadway. Also there are plenty of good restaurants and bars in the local area.
We were also impressed with the friendliness of the staff. If you are staying for any length of time use the weekly internet rate.
All in all a great first stay in New York and we would certainly recommend friends to stay at this hotel.

title: “Excellent service but room is noisy”
text:
The hotel is in a very good location and the room are large and very comfortable . The staff,  
is Very attentive and provide first class service
Two. Major flows. The room is noisy it is not well insulated f.rom the outside.
 noise and the air condition is old noisy and start and stop frequently.

title: “Stay Away”
text:
This was the absolute WORSE hotel stay of my life. The pool was closed (guests were not notified until you were on the premise) the staff would lie (when I asked to be moved to another room) they said there were none available, within 30 seconds one of the managers said there were rooms (he did not know that a staff members had told me they did not have any rooms. The breakfast orders were handled incorrectly for two days. The valet misplaced my request to bring my car around. One of the mangers solution to my problem was to moved to a different hotel (I am a single parent traveling along with my 10 year old daughter during spring break).
Not only do I not want to EVER stay at the Mewnger again, I don't even want to go to San Antonio.
Really left a bad taste in my mouth!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

title: “ABSOLUTLEY FABULOUS”
text:
I have the pleasure of staying here for an extended stay. I am so thrilled with the service and staff here I couldn't wait until check out to post a review!
I have stayed at MANY Marriott properties due to business travel-- many of which are full service hotels, and high priced. I also have stayed at many Hilton properties.
The Residence Inn by the Galleria is HANDS DOWN the best experience I have had thus far. The staff couldn't be more helpful and always have a GENUINE smile. They have gone over and beyond my expectations-- and I have very high standards.
The location is perfectly in the middle of a very upscale and happening area-- but at the same time when I enter the property-- I feel more "at home" than I have felt at any other hotel.
Cheers to the staff at Residence Inn by the Galleria-- I would recommend the property to families or business travelers-- anyone who wants a wonderful experience-- and the reasonable price is just a bonus. :)

title: “Decent Hotel, TERRIBLE SERVICE!”
text:
If location is what you are looking for, then this may be the hotel for you, but the service was TERRIBLE from start to finish! We travel a lot for our jobs so we are both very familiar with service, and the hotel industry. Therefore we can handle more than the average business traveler when it comes to knowing things can happen with hotel reservations.
My friend from college was getting married, and my husband was one of the groomsmen. When we arrived at the hotel to check in they pulled up our reservation and went through the standard process asking us for a credit card. We asked the girl at the front desk what would be held on the card as the rooms for the groomsmen were to be paid for by the mother of the groom. All of a sudden it was like we had offended her and she snapped back “well, I don’t have that”. I was a little taken back by her reaction, and I told her it was all to be taken care of before we arrived. She replied “well, IF that’s true, the mother of the groom has NOT put down her credit card for this reservation and nothing has been charged, therefore I need your credit card for payment or you won’t have a room HERE”! At this point, my husband politely excused us, and he called the mother of the groom. She was just about to get on her plane and would be there in a couple hours, but she was sure she had already given her credit card to the person in charge of blocking the rooms for the wedding. When we let the agent know this, she said we would need to wait for her to come with the FOP before we were allowed in the room.
As our friends (other groomsmen) started to arrive at the hotel, naturally, none of the rooms had been paid for and we all had to wait in the very small lobby of the hotel. It became very crowded as there were more than 30 of us in the lobby with our luggage. No one offered to store our luggage or offer us drinks at the bar, so there we all sat/stood waiting on the mother of the groom to arrive at the hotel. After she finally arrived and it still took over an hour to get us all checked in because they had to route all the charges to her room to charge her credit card. Still, no compensation for our inconvenience was offered. Not even an apology.
On top of everything, when we finally DID get into our rooms, we had a friend (also in the wedding) and his wife sharing our room with us. They were not there for the payment fiasco but had the pleasure of experiencing similar “customer service”. As her husband was parking the car, she tried to check in with her last name. Since their name never did make it onto our reservation, and the FD didn’t bother to ask if she was sharing the room. She thought her husband might know more about their reservation and decided to wait until he returned. As she was standing in the lobby, a security guard told her if she did not have a reservation, she would NEED TO LEAVE THE PROPERTY!
The whole wedding party experienced this kind of service the entire weekend. We will NEVER return to this property even if our rooms ARE being paid for!

title: “Simply Wonderful”
text: Location of the hotel is awsome. Everything downtown is walkable, and if it's raining they have umbrellas you may borrow from your room. No need for a car really if you are there for only a few days. Staff is wonderful! I was in a corner room on a lower floor but my view was still wonderful. The bathrooms are spacious, with a stand alone shower and a soaking tub. This hotel is quite the oasis in a very busy part of the city.

title: “Great Value”
text: No fluffy towels. Only 12 TV channels. No room service. A wimpy "continental" breakfast. Kinda dowdy. BUT: a clean, spacious room. Plenty 'nuff amenties for a place to "hang your hat in." Friendly, helpful, albeit inexperienced staff. Not close to Inner Harbor, Orioles, Ravens. BUT worth every single cent of 89 bucks a night. If you want the Hyatt, get your checkbook out. For half (reallly, less) the price, this is a no-brainer.

title: “Nice weekend getaway”
text: My mother and I were in town this past weekend for a rally and for some sightseeing and stayed at the Washington Court Hotel. I was pleased with the overall service. The view we had from our room wasn't great, but we were only there to sleep so it didn't really matter. The rooms were spacious and the beds really comfortable. The hotel seemed really crowded when we got there but check in was quick and easy and the staff was really friendly. The location was perfect for us....within walking distance of Union Station and the Smithsonian museums.

title: “Cool Hotel”
text: Cool hotel. Great location. Nice roof top bar with great cocktails.

title: “Great hotel and fantastic location”
text:
We stayed at the Hyatt Regency during a trip to Chicago with friends and had no complaints at all. We got a good deal on it by booking through the unnamed hotel offered by expedia and we couldn't be happier with the result. The rooms were quite large and modern, bathrooms were renovated, and everything was very clean.
The hotel is huge and busy! Some people may not like this - if you prefer to be personally greeted everytime you enter the hotel, this place is not for you - but we had no issues with it and we were able to assistance from the information desk when we needed it. It also offers a bar and several restaurants if you want to stay close to the hotel one night.
The location is perfect for visiting Chicago. It was very close to the Magnificient Mile, boat cruises, and Millenium Park. Walking distance to Navy Pier as well, and even the Shedd Aquarium and Field Museum if you're interested in a longer walk. 
Stops for most of the train lines are also only a 5-7 minute walk away. If you find that it is too long of a walk with your suitcases, you can always just grab a cab for a few dollars to take you to close train/subway stop.
Overall, we would definitely recommend this hotel!

title: “Not so "comfort"able”
text:
My husband and I recently took our 3 kids (ages 7, 5, and 2) and stayed in a Kids' Suite for 8 nights. The overall experience was so-so. It did serve it's purpose to provide us with somewhere to sleep and store our stuff while we were out all day, but I know the next time I go to San Diego, I will book another place.
The location was OK - close to the airport, Sea World, SD Zoo, and the beach. There's also a shopping mall reallly close by, along with several restaurants. But here are the problems that I had with this place:
1. They advertise waffles for breakfast, but they didn't tell you it's only on Saturday morning. I originally picked this place over other comparable facilities is becaues of their advertised waffle bar breakfast. Their normal breakfast consist of toast, bagels, pastries, cereal, milk, OJ, cranberry juice, coffee/tea. On Sunday they add eggs and sausage patties.
2. The pillows and mattress were REALLY uncomfortable. My husband descrived the pillows as bags of giant cotton balls. For the king size bed, instead of the normal 2 king-sized pillows,they give you 5 square throw pillows.
3. The TV cable to the kids' room cuts in and out. We had to fiddle around with the cable to get a somewhat clear reception.
4. The front desk clerk was RUDE. She didn't even know their own Sea World fun pass promotion when I asked her and told us to call Sea World ourselves...umm, it's a special that's advertise on your website, hello!!!
5. The toilet did not flush properly. We had to hold the lever down for the toilet to do a complete enough flush.
6. The shower head was really sub-par. The water pressure was horrible, though the water stayed hot while all 5 of us showered or bathed.
7. The water in the pool was somewhat cloudy. My husband attributed this to the fact that everyone was probably wearing sunscreen, but I think it's just gross.
8. They charged for parking.
9. The wall/door did not cut the noise out. Late at night we could hear the noisy pool people in our room while we tried to go to sleep.

title: “Not as bad as you`d think - but almost!”
text:
We stayed here for 5 nights in September, and having read previous TA reviews was not expecting much. However it was my girlfriends first visit to NYC, so we weren`t planning on spending alot of time in the room.
Firstly, the check-in and out queues are as bad as previously suggested. And to store luggage in the lobby before a late flight home was a painful experience. Unlike every other hotel I`ve stayed in I had to PAY for the privilage($4 / bag), queue up AGAIN at check-in to get a luggage tag, then locate the lugage room via an elevator and a creepy walk down in the bowels of the hotel. Also there are no restrooms in the lobby.
The staff were generally typical New York, direct and too the point, which is fine, but at least a please and thankyou would have been nice once in a while. 
The rooms were actually OK. I`d requested a `renovated` room, only to be told they had no such thing - honest at least! However the room was very clean, the TV worked fine, and the bathroom was acceptable for this price. Also, I found the hotel corridors to be perfectly well lit and not at all creep as previous reviewers have suggested.
The only negatives to the rooms were the maid service. Towels got less and less each day, bed not properly made and attempting to walk in the room at 8am despite the `Do not disturb` sign!
Overall, the location and price means that its a bit of a bargain really. It has a motel feel to it, and its clear the staff do not care. This maybe due to the fact the place is looking likely to be knocked down shortly for redevelopment.. Personally I would pay another $60 a night and stay at the Doubletree Met or Novotel uptown.

title: “Great experience”
text: This hotel is located at the beginning of the Gas Lamp District. It was in the perfect spot and the room was clean and very comfortable. The view was of the parking garage and the stadium, so not the best. Had a great bar in the room with snacks and other things to make your stay, but they were ridiculously over priced. $4.00 for a snickers. Lol. And you could get one downstairs for 99 cents. Was disappointed that we couldn't use the pool or even see it because they use it as a club. But overall enjoyed our stay and would stay there again.

title: “Basic functional hotel popular with tourists”
text: I stayed two nights mid week with a colleague on a trip to attend a conference. This hotel is pretty unremarkable. It looks modern from the outside, but the rooms are a bit dated, and on the small side. Mine was pretty dark and there was definitely no view to speak of. Reception was pretty efficient, although I was glad we arrived before the coach load of tourists who were then queuing behind us at check in. WiFi was free although the password they give you at checking changes each day which means you need to call reception, which is a pain. It was fast once I got it going, but the sign-in screen where you put the username and password were very difficult to use on my iPad and iPhone and froze a few times. Breakfast is basic self service but absolutely fine, although it was extremely busy. Think cinnamon rolls, preprepared omelets, plastic cutlery.

title: “Excellent Stay”
text:
The hotel is conveniently located among all the sights to see in the DC area. It is convenient to the L'Efflant Plaza Metro station where four metro lines intersect. 
The facility is clean and very comfortable. The staff is accommodating and went out of their way to be helpful. 
On the downside, the only minor inconvenience was the lack of food facilities in the area. To get a really good meal, a car was needed. Even with that said, we will be back to enjoy this great facility again! Thanks.

title: “Impressive common areas, rooms are okay”
text:
This is a great hotel for a company offsite. The lobby area is very spacious and great to chat with a group of co-workers or 1:1 chats. Fairmont is very central yet located just a couple of minutes from the airport.
The room was not bad but unimpressive. Several hotels that cost less can provide more comfort.

title: “No bedbugs!”
text:
I searched high and low for a place in NYC that was nice, in a good location and with NO bedbugs. I found it.
Pros: 
It was clean!
Loved the bathroom mirrors -- a girl's dream. Huge and well lit...perfect for putting on your makeup for a night on the town.
Pretty good food from the restaurant downstairs (Rare Bar & Grill) and great service.
Quiet! Sometimes it was so quiet you'd forget you were in NYC (until we opened the window!).
Plenty of cable channels. More than I'm used to in a hotel.
Cons:
The bed was pretty firm. My BF and I both have bad backs so we were pretty stiff by the time we left.
Parking sucks...because there is none. The hotel charges $55/night. The garage across the street charges $36. I know it's NY but geeeez!

title: “Good hotel and location, but not perfect”
text:
You probably should not book this hotel without understanding the location: the Lower East Side is a bit more gritty and perfect for a good night out. It is also 10 minutes walk from Soho. But is not the ideal location for tourist hotspots, if this is a priority. For me, the location was perfect, but it is worth noting.
Key positives: the hotel was slick, the room smart and minimal, light with very comfortable bed and decent bathroom. Upgraded to a 10th floor corner room with a great S Manhattan view. The bar was pleasant enough for an early evening drink and the inclusive breakfast offered fruit, bagels, toast, jam and tea and coffee, which was enough (though for something more imaginative google 88 Orchard, a decent cafe within 5 minutes walk). The LES location is great for evenings out (also close to Soho and East Village) and there is a Subway within 2 minutes walk that gives you quick access to Manhattan/Brooklyn. Free wifi also gets a ++.
Key negatives: the hotel designates all rooms as non smoking, but does not enforce it. Hence my room smelt like a smoking room on arrival. The best the hotel could do was offer an air machine during the day, which took two days to have an effect. In addition, the exterior primarily being metal framed glass, the room got cold in the evening without pumping in enormous amounts of hot air through the AC.
Summary:
A great location, great views and no complaints about the size or contents of the room. However, it's not perfect: anybody who is a non-smoker probably doesn't appreciate a night in a smoking room and it can get chilly in winter without blasting the AC. I would stay here again but would probably try other alternatives in the neighbourhood first.
BTW - the light switchers have dimmers - for those who complained the rooms were too dark.

title: “Very Good Hotel”
text: We spent New Year's weekend 2011/2012 here, and our stay was very pleasant. The location is excellent, being adjacent to Time Warner Arena and only steps to all Center City has to offer. The hotel is a contemporary style, very attractive. Our king-suite was spacious, clean, and comfortable (especially the bed). Once our room door was closed, we never once heard any hallway noise, not even on New Year's Eve. The staff - Front Desk, valet, housekeeping, breakfast staff - were all friendly, welcoming, helpful, and efficient. I wouldn't hesitate to stay here again.

title: “Lovely hotel and location”
text: Came for a weekend trip to the city. The hotel was great and in a very convenient location. Most attractions were about 15 minutes away. Breakfast was decent - buffet style. The only thing was that when I called for an amenity to be brought to the room there was no runner on shift and I was politely asked to pick up the items at the desk. Overall I enjoyed my stay very much.

title: “Don't believe the Description”
text:
The literature, the web site, the photographs lead you to believe that this hotel is on the edge of a hip, desirable, art deco area - it is not. Its location is seedy, the walk from Canal street subway is past pretty dodgy stores and characters - the internal prices for breakfast and drinks high, and not good value for the $189 deal.
Counter Staff very helpful.

title: “Wonderful Experience”
text: Stayed for one night with my senior mother to celebrate her birthday. Great location near Times Square. We walked from Penn Station to the hotel (about 9 blocks), from hotel to Radio City (about 7 blocks), to restaurant row. Our room was not available at early check-in so we stored our luggage and enjoyed the fresh coffee. tea, latte, etc. and fruit/pastries available all day on second floor lounge before heading out into the city for awhile. Everyone was extremely polite, helpful and accommodating. Rooms and bathrooms appeared updated and very tasteful. Hotel very clean. Didn't make it to evening wine and cheese, but there was a bottle of champagne in our room when we returned at night . Loved everything would return in a heartbeat.

title: “THE spot if your shopping downtown”
text:
Myself and 3 girlfriends stayed here for a weekend of shopping on Michigan Avenue. None of us had stayed here before. We were thrilled that we were a half a block off of Michigan. When we visited it was a wonderfully warm weekend. We were able to walk to Navy Pier which was about a mile away.
The room was a nice size. We had a room with 2 double beds. The beds were comfortable and nice. The only real issue with room was that the hotel is 2 blocks from Northwestern Hospital and we heard the sirens all night both nights. This was a little distracting and did make hard for a few of us to sleep.
We all loved the bathroom. It had a huge walk-in shower and was very clean. With 4 woman we had tons of makeup etc so it was nice for all of us to be able to spread out our stuff on the counter. The amenities were very nice.
We didn't eat in the restaurant nor did we go to the bar so I can't say if those are any good.
The only parking available was the in the ramp accross the street. We opted to leave our vehicle there all weekend and walk or take a taxi everywhere we went. 
The lobby was nice and we didn't really notice the elevator issues that some of the previous posters commented about.
If I ever return to downtown Chicago, this will be my first choice for accomadations.

title: “A Hybrid Hotel/Motel”
text: I was quite surpised to walk through the doors of the lobby, check-in, then walk outside to the front door of my room. Half of the establishment is indoors like a hotel, and the rest are outdoors like a motel. The room was old and the insulation was poor...I heard every car door close and people walking by the door. It really needs a renovation. I stayed here because it was less than 2 miles from the place I needed to work out of. In retrospect, I should have found a place a little further and a little nicer, even if it's 20 minutes away. I do have to say that the price was right, though.

title: “Very Nice Hotel, Great RIverfront Location”
text: This hotel is in a great location on the riverfront. Great front desk staff. Rooms are clean, large and quiet.

title: “Excellent value and location”
text:
BW Bowery was a great hotel. The desk staff were very helpful and friendly, especially as I had arrived at 9.30am after an overnight flight from South America. They managed to get me a room very quickly despite checkout being 11am. Offered me to help myself to the breakfast which was still being served while they did it. Breakfast was fairly simple, coffee, juice, bagels, muffins etc but all fresh and restocked throughout the breakfast period 7-10.
Room was large, clean and comfortable beds. I had a room facing over Grand St and it was very very quiet by NY standards. Only the very occasional truck horn cut through the peace. Bathroom floor had under floor heating which was a nice touch.
At first you may think you are a long way from anywhere however the subway is one block away and its on the B&D lines both of which was express lines, 3 stops you are at Macy's, 4 stops times square.
Would definately stay here again

title: “Lovely stay”
text: We stayed in room 630, which was quite nice. The bathroom was extremely modern and incredibly clean, with lots of hot water (thank you for the great water pressure!) and fluffy towels, and plenty of space to place our toiletries. The tub comes complete with lovely soap and loofah and was so clean that I had to indulge. The butler met us upon check-in and oriented us to the room, informed us that the butler service was available 24 hours/day, that they would press 2 garments at no charge and that coffee/tea would be delivered with a wake-up call. Although we did not utilize the Butler service at all, the service throughout the hotel was amazing. The concierge staff is incredible, friendly, knowledgeable and very accessible. I asked for ideas for my 18 year old and was given such great ideas like jazz clubs, comedy clubs, and the garment district (i.e. not the traditional, boring tourist items). The beds so very soft and clean and comfy, the sitting area very roomy...fresh fruit in our room daily...bottled water to drink...the maid even folded my daughter's pile of clothing one day and left me a beautiful white rose our last night. Funny thing as I was planning to stay at the Mandarin Oriental, but was having a problem getting my reservation, so I was at the St. Regis "by accident." And, boy was I pleased!! I also want to comment on the "dated" comment I saw in an earlier review. OK, so the room decor might remind you of a more traditional and older Parisian hotel....but, make no mistake, these rooms are NOT musty, old, or dusty. This place is really clean & fresh, with modern stunning linens, great pillows, good windows, bathrooms, etc. and is a great place to stay. For those needing more modernity in their decor, the comfy beds, great bathrooms, and incredible (yes, incredible) service will more than make up for it. And, before I sign off, the breakfast in the restaurant was incredible, creative and tasty. And they were so nice to me, even though most people were quite well dressed and I was in my jeans! (although it was not necessarily set up for people in a rush as I seem to always be....). We ate there 2 days and I can vouch that both the buckwheat pancakes and the yogurt/granola are exceptional....And, I may have had one of the best massages ever in their spa.

title: “Amazing hotel with great service!”
text:
I travel quite often for work and have stayed at a ton of starwood hotels. By far this one was my fave. I wish I was able to stay in there longer. The hotel rooms are amazing and we were upgraded to a suite.
The staff and location of the hotel is great. It is right across from the Gas Lamp and a mall.

title: “Nice hotel”
text: Stayed in this hotel for one night. Booked the Bridal Package - came with free breakfast and champagne - the best package on the Westin internet site. The hotel is modern and interesting looking - and on one of the hotest days of the summer, a cool relief. Check in was quick and efficient - although the "we charge for all calls" lecture seemed harsh - maybe some would fine the admonition helpful. The room was nice - in a modern style, clean, bed was as you would expect in a Westin. Bathroom was small and not particularly luxurious. Ordered a snack at midnight - burger, fries and chicken tenders were barely edible, although delivered within a half hour. Delivered one glass of water for two people. Breakfast in the restaurant - included in the package - was good.

title: “Excellent Value for Money”
text:
This hotel is great... for what we paid, we expected a very ordinary hotel. Our 3rd Floor Lomard St view room had a partial view of the Golden Gate Bridge... imagine what you would have to pay in London for a partial view of Tower Bridge for example.
The hotel is clean and the breakfast is great.. lovely coffee and muffins, croissants etc.
Close to bus routes and centrally located to walk to many major attractions.... loved it!

title: “We will return!”
text: The room was huge and nicely appointed. The location was perfect next to shopping and restaurants and within easy walking distance to all the downtown hot spots. A welcomed change from the big hotel chains. We would stay there again on our next visit to the area.

title: “Great Harbour View in Boston”
text: The Seaport Boston Hotel is a great hotel right on the water and near the convention center. It provides easy access to events at the convention center as well as quick access to the North End and Logan Airport. It is a very busy hotel if there is a show in town, so be sure to bring some patience with you. Lines are long, but staff are friendly and helpful. A short walk to Morton's Steakhouse makes for a great dining experience. Rooms are small but well appointed with comfortable beds, plus linens and toiletries by Gilchrist. Also a pretty good value for a prime Boston location.

title: “Three Generation Girl Trip”
text: My daughter, one year old granddaughter and I spent three nights at the Oxford Hotel for a little getaway the week before Christmas. We were welcomed by two very jovial, helpful gents.....assisted us with all the "stuff" necessary when traveling with a young one, parking the car, and so on. They continued to help throughout our stay - carrying our bags upon returning from shopping, walking and driving suggestions, etc. Check in was super, the room was beautiful, as is the rest of the hotel.
