The only concern was that our room was near the ballroom where a holiday party was held one night. Some louder (but happy) foot traffic much later in the evening. We found that we could walk to nearly all the places we wanted to go. All staff was friendly and helpful, and we got a really great rate which included valet parking. We look forward to returning to the Oxford during our next visit to Denver. AND the Christmas decorations were gorgeous!

title: “For the $ Best a value for the location.”
text:
For those with a limited budget this is THE best value for lodging in Downtown Chicago, when you can book in the $80/nite range.
We've have stayed in some dives and we have stayed in some 5 Star places like Shutters on the Beach in Santa Monica, The San Maria Isabel in Mexico City, Penninsulas, etc. The Tremont is a 5 Star dive. It is a little rough on the edges but for the value and location it can't be beat.
The lobby has a very nice sitting area with nice leather chairs and couches.
Right next door is Ditka's which has a decent menu (on the spendy side though).
We stayed in room 1503 which was small but adequate. As we were out and about the town most the time, the room size mattered little. The windows were small but the room got good light in the day and has a nice view of Michigan Avenue. Cable channels were limited but the carried FOX (Rare for Chicago) a plus for us NRA members.
Room could have used a place to hang up stuff but overall a really suitable place. We've rated service average because we had really no interaction with the staff, though the limited interaction we did have was very nice.
For the value and location and condition of rooms our room at least was thumbs-up.

title: “relax before you go on a trip”
text: I stayed there because I didn't want to drive and it was cheaper than other hotels for a couple of hours stay and they have a free suttle to the airport every 30 minutes it is an average hotel the only bad thing is that the people at the front desk are not there I waited like 15 minutes for someone to come and I was the first one on the line the breakfast is no good but the uy of the shuttle was really nice you need to be there 10 minutes or 15 ahead of time if not they will leave you and you will have to wait like 25 minutes (it happened to me) for the price is a good choice if you are going to travel early morning find a parking it's not easy!!

title: “been here before, and ill definitely come agian!”
text: we had stayed here lastyear too. we keep choosing hotel 140 because its cozy and has a nice homey feel. its convienent location was perfect because it was near the wilbur theatre and thats where we were heading that evening. the staff at the front desk were wonderful and very welcoming! we will definitely be back next year! the one downfall was the maid service..if you have a do not disturb sign on the door sometimes they dont see it and knock anyway and the toilets are so loud when theyre being flushed! you can hear ones down the hall from your room., but other than that it was wonderful! and when we arrived we had gotten a complimentary upgrade!

title: “Do Not Be Fooled by the Pictures!!!”
text: Absolutely not what you expect...did not expect to share bathroom. Also, rooms not very clean besides the sheets. Walls in our room were filthy( there was some kind of drink all over the wall). Space is Extremly small!!!! You can barely turn around. Ac worked good. No other amenities in the room...no fridge, no iron...nothing..Hotel " restaurant" offered just snacks...Fake advertisement for free wi-fi. My I-Pad did not connect to the weak network. The only good thing was location...nothing else!! Would not recommend it unless you have no other choice..

title: “Location, Location, Location”
text: The Warwick is an average hotel in a great location. The service is always very good; the rooms are very average - nothing terrible, just an "old" feel to everything. Like the hotel could use a great makeover someday soon! But it's located directly across the street from my offices (I live in Denver but my company is based here in Seattle). You've got the view of the Space Needle, a "smoking" floor, and very good service. The downstairs restaurant, Margaux, is very good, too. I could stay at other hotels when I'm in town, but they're all more expensive and further away from "work." So I usually opt for the Warwick. Most times I have a cheese and fruit tray waiting on me upon arrival. So it's a comfortable business alternative. Not sure I'd recommend it for vacationing families, though.

title: “Great location and friendly staff”
text: We stayed 3 nights in Oct. Nice rooms in an old hotel near 5th Ave & 31st St. Great service, friendly and attentive staff. Hotel beds, showers were great. Bathrobes in the rooms. Free coffee. Continental breakfast for a fee. Hotel had a bar in the lobby which we didn't use. Wifi only in lobby, intermittent service in rooms. Would stay again.

title: “Excellent stay”
text:
Excellent stay, great location.
Front desk agents were friendly and helpful. Incredible Staff.

title: “Good hotel, great location”
text: Stayed for 2 nights while attending a conference. Room was small and furnishings a bit worn (but a new flat screen TV), but everything was clean and in good working order. Unlike some others, I was able to manage the climate controls, though it took some time. The staff was efficient, if somewhat diffident. The location is excellent for anything in Midtown. I would definitely stay there again for business travel.

title: “Japanese simplicity in SF”
text: the first hotel on our two week driving tour of california. the nikko met all of our expectations although we had requested a high floor previously by email and this wasn't honoured. room nice and comfortable. public areas very nice including a nice relaxing bar. breakfast very good with several japanese options. only complaint is the charge to use the pool/health club.

title: “One of the best!”
text:
The proprieters go overboard with many thoughtful extras to make our stay comfortable.
I loved the healthy fresh fruitt in the lobby. Breakfast was quite good. 
The whole place was very clean and tidy.
This was at the high end of Super 8s we have stayed at.
We definitely plan to stay there again.

title: “Highly recommended”
text:
Great choice for all of central Boston and Back Bay. Very smooth check in with pleasant staff and a great buffet breakfast. The rooms are great. Large enough for two adults and two teens. Shower a little counter intuitive for Europeans but hardly a big issue.
Location as has been pointed out is superb with short walks to Boylston and Newbury St shopping. Easy stroll to Boston Common and if you want even through to Cambridgeshire Mall and Fanueil Hall. Subway is close if you prefer although stations being rebuilt this year and public AC not very effective/non existent. 
Would like to return. Costs very very reasonable for centre of a US city and much better than anything in NYC.

title: “good value”
text: For Boston, this was a good value. reasonable close to downtown. Helpful staff. Would use again.

title: “Comfortable and accommodating”
text:
My married, adult daughter and I spent two nights in the Inn at Venice Beach. Check-in time is 3 pm , but we surprised them around noon and there were no rooms ready. The nice gentleman behind the desk said he would have something ready before 2 o'clock, if we could wait. We had flown in from Memphis and were tired after our flight, so he offered to lock our luggage inside a utility closet for safe keeping while we went to eat lunch and stroll down the beach. When we returned close to 2 o'clock, he checked us in without a problem. Our room was right beside the lovely outdoor patio area where breakfast is served and we were concerned it might be noisy. But we had no problem with noise whatsoever.
Later in the evening, I asked the man behind the desk (sorry but don't know his name) about the Gray Line Tours, and he recommended the VIP Tours. Obviously, the hotel gets a percentage if they book a tour, which is fine with me. My daughter would be busy with friends the next day, so I took the tour alone and had a grand time chatting with other tourists. I was not disappointed. The six-hour tour of the entire Los Angeles area was well worth the $60.
The desk clerk arranged for a taxi to the airport on the morning of our departure, which arrived about five to ten minutes early. I appreciate promptness so that wasn't a problem. This particular taxi driver owned his own cab and was extremely helpful and polite. Not at all like the rude driver from somewhere in the Middle East who gave us a ride to the motel upon our arrival. It was obvious that the Inn had a working relationship with this driver, so that was appreciated, too.
Oh, I almost forgot about the breakfast. It's simply continental but fresh with plenty of choices. It kept me full until lunch time.
All in all, my stay at the Inn was delightful. The desk clerk(s) were all very helpful and eager to hand out advice about the local attractions. The location is top notch, just far enough away from the beach to avoid the noise and the crowds. There are many good choices of restaurants within a one to two block walk and if you want to rent a bicycle, that can be arranged, too.
Give this Inn a whirl. You will like the clean, comfortable beds and the helpful attitude of the staff.

title: “DON'T STAY HERE UNLESS YOU'RE IN DIRE NEED OF A HOTEL!!!”
text: This motel was absolutely disgusting. It looks exactly like where cops set up drug and prostitute stings. The ice bucket was stolen from the radisson hotel, it smells like a mix between dirty air conditioning and cigarettes. The bed is ridiculously uncomfortable, and the towels, let's just say I'm lucky I brought my own. The point is, don't stay here...EVER!

title: “very pretty hotel , but one problem: rooms too tiny, difficult to move inside rooms”
text: the hotel is very pretty, modern design, very close to main attractions, very clean, it'd be perfect if rooms were not so tiny.. there was not space for 2 luggages, and to move thru the room you had to give priority to each other.

title: “Fabulous kitchen, with lots of options.”
text:
This little Inn on the corner of a highly busy intersection, was quite quaint. The manager Denise, was fabulous, so helpful, and personable. She went out of her way to help us do anything we asked and even those things we didn't even ask for. 
The kitchen in the main area was wonderful for breakfast, lots of choices and things that were easy to make. We left each day feeling like we had a good breakfast that saved us money at a regular breakfast place. 
The shuttle service was a godsend for us, saved on parking and gasoline costs and the general hassle of traffic.
The one thing that I would have liked to see was the actual rooms be upgraded a bit nicer, they looked cheesy. The curtains did not block out the light, so we had to put up a blanket that we had in our vehicle. Also, the actual parking spots next to the rooms, were so small that unless you had a small economy car, you would have to take up two parking spots, or park in the back of the hotel. Unsafe because of vandals, and having to walk in the dark area is unsafe as well..
Overall, I would rate Carefree Inn as very good, and I would stay there again. Many thanks to the manager, Denise who was so nice, like dealing with a family member.

title: “Moved in the same day as a lot of the Motorcylists with the ROT Rally”
text:
The hotel was busy, some guests kept the luggage carts in their rooms for hours, but the staff helped me carry all of my belongings up to my room. They were great. Nicki at the front desk was very kind and helpful too.
Hotel room was beautiful. Hotel in general was tastefully decorated. Prices for a beer were a little outrageous (especially for a Courtyard). I would return for another visit without giving a second thought.

title: “Perfect Wall Street Location”
text: Obvious great location for financial district business travel but we went for the weekend. Walk to World Trade Center, Brooklyn Bridge, South Street Seaport, All the ferries: East River, Governors Island etc. In real estate terms it has location, location, location. Here is a very clean and reasonable hotel from which to base your visit to lower Manhattan. New York small size room, queen bed not king. On the corner of Wall and Williams means you have quiet neighborhood at night. Helpful staff gets the job done.

title: “great room”
text: Our room was clean and quiet, a super value for our stay. We got a great rate as return clients. It is close to downtown Charlotte without costing what the downtown hotels charge. Our king room was comfortable and spacious.

title: “Classy Queen Anne”
text: The Queen Anne Hotel is a delightful place to stay for a San Francisco vacation. The price is a bargain in a boutique hotel. It is in a quiet neighborhood but close to a variety of tourist attractions. Japan Town and the Fillmore district are a short, nearly level walk away as is the Bush Street neighborhood of historic homes. For those with a car it has very easy access to Van Ness, the 80 Fwy to the East Bay, Golden Gate Park, and downtown. Also the parking fee at $14 per day is half of the price of comparable Union Square hotels. The hotel decor is a San Francisco treat, but the real treat is the staff and service. You really can sit in the lobby/lounge area, have a cup of tea or an afternoon sherry, meet fellow travelers and unwind. The staff is genuinely friendly and helpful. We go to San Francisco two or three times a year and will definately return to the Queen Anne.

title: “Henry Robinson is the man!”
text:
A very nice hotel made better by staff people such as HENRY ROBINSON who was friendly and helpful and went out of his way to make our stay enjoyable.
As for the restaurant, the chefs apparently have a very different concept of what "well done" means, but if you like your burgers with a pulse, go for it. The waitress (Michelle) commiserated with us and comped me with a free dessert (which was excellent).

title: “Historic and Beautiful!”
text: Old, Historic and still beautiful - great staff, verry responsive. And - what a location!

title: “Very nice and historic hotel but DIRTY”
text:
Last weekend I attended a wedding at the St. Anthony, I made my reservation on October the 30th, almost a month and a half before my stay. 
At my arrival the valet parking staff were very nice, they spoke both English and Spanish but at the front desk they said that they did not speak Spanish which I do not thing is good at a very touristic destination, specially in a city with a lot of Latin visitors, at least that is my point of view.
The guy at the front desk was very fast to assign my room but he was like a machine, when he saw me he just said "credit card and photo ID", I handed him the documents and he gave me the keys to room 737. The bellboy, a nice guy who happened to speak English and Spanish took us to the room, he had to use his card to open the room because our keys where not working, anyway the bellboy placed our luggage in the closet and described the hotel services and facilities, after that he offered to take our cards to the front desk and reprogram them.
Our room was at the end of the corridor which makes it different from the others because of its location, it is smaller than the others. The space between the beds and the TV is very narrow, it is hard to open the closet door because there is a chair that cannot be placed anywhere else because of the limited space. 
When we left the room to go for a dinner we picked up the keys and asked about a different room because of the lack of space, the same front desk guy from the beginning told us that they only had that room left and that he was not able to do anything because the hotel was full, I thought he had really nothing to do, I said nothing further and left to have sit at the lobby to wait for the rest of my relatives to go for dinner. While in the lobby I saw several people arriving to the hotel and getting rooms, but there where not a better room for me regardless of my advanced reservation and earlier arrival. I felt I was being discriminated.
I found out water stains behind bathroom's door and lots of dust behind the beds and on the night table. The edge of the air conditioning grille was black and a little misplaced.
The first night the housekeeper made our beds around 4 PM. The second night I found half of a death EARWIG in my bed, I took it to the front desk when leaving the hotel, they offered to make an inspection of the room to make sure that the next customer is not going to find such thing. They gave me free parking due to the inconvenience and the girl at the front desk was very understanding. 
I think that this is a nice hotel that needs to improve cleanliness and customer service (bilingual and more friendly staff).

title: “Great boutique hotel”
text: We were very lucky to stay at this European-style boutique hotel near Union Square. We even met the owner and listened to her fascinating history. This is an extremely friendly place, with good sized, well appointed rooms, a lovely restaurant, etc. Do stay there!

title: “Cold service”
text:
Chose this lodge for the location and price - these 2 factors combined can't be beat. However I would consider paying more in return for better standards of service. The front desk was too cool and didn't offer any information or assistance. It seemed like they were more interested in office work on the computer than taking care of guests.
This place was like staying at grandma's house, with a sagging bed mattress that needs replacing and old bed linen. The housekeepers were also quite noisy in the mornings, talking loudly to each other across the hallway.

title: “Best time ever in N.Y. thanks to the staff at the Carlton!!”
text:
Made us feel like Kings and Queens as soon as we stepped out of the cab in front of the hotel. Did not have a single complaint, price was very reasonable, room service was great and they even helped us get into a show that I did'nt even know about.
We will be back next time we are in N.Y..
Thanks Keep up the good work.

title: “Location, Location, Location (and did I mention location?).”
text:
I stayed at the Residence Inn Austin for 4 nights during SXSW 2012. 
Check in was a breeze. Even though the hotel was at capacity during my stay, I was able to get my room even though I was several hours early for check in.
Room was spacious, clean and well appointed. Staff was super helpful and always friendly.
The location is what puts everything over the top. Only 2 blocks from the 6th street action. Also, 2 blocks makes a world of difference regarding noise (it is still noisy in the area but not as bad as being right on 6th).
I am not sure I could be any more satisfied with this place. I will attempt to get it for SXSW next year.

title: “Less than Average”
text: Stayed for 3 nights in mid February. the hotel is very tired and in need of a refurb. Suite was ok but carpet and furniture needed replacing. Complimentary brakfast was cafeteria stlye at best and the single cook on the omelet station simply could not cope and unfortunately the product was not great. It piches for a family on a strict budget and i guess it partially achieves a fair outcome; very little service apart from the pleasant doorman

title: “Great location, fun hotel - LOVE the Corner Office restaurant too!”
text:
This hotel is wonderfully located right, smack-dab in downtown Denver and within walking distance to performing arts center, convention center and the 16th street mall. We got a top, corner room with a large king bed. It was wonderful and clean. I personally love the kitchy, pop culture decor - it reminds me of being a kid - remember playin connect four and twister? 
We purchased a breakfast package online since we were celebrating our anniversary. We got the coupons for the breakfast with our room and the next morning we were really sad to read that we could only get food off the buffet. We love the Corner Office's Breakfast burrito so we BEGGED the manager of the restaurant to allow us a subsitition for a burrito. I didn't notice on their website that you only got the buffet with the deal (so read the fine print if you plan on getting a pre-packaged deal).
Also, note that even with a reservation, it still costs you about $20 to park your car (even if you do it yourself). Also, I have stayed at the Curtis about 5 times and I have never gotten a room with a bathtub...they all have just showers. It would have been nice to soak in a big tub - so that was a bit disappointing.

title: “Beware the beds.......”
text:
We frequent Columbus about once a month for shopping and use discount sites. I know that every hotel on polaris parkway is upper middle class And for $38 a night I knew it would be an effeciency suit of some sort which is a bargain. If you are not familiar with the area THIS WILL BE HARD TO SPOT since the signage on building is small. It is located off 71 which for us is in between my preferred shopping. It also is located across the street (eight lanes) from Polaris fashion place (very large enclosed mall with lifestyle center and it us also within walking distance (like yards so same side of street) to Wendy's Quaker steak carrabas and go cart game center. And just walk up the street and there is a target and a beginning of a long and large upscale strip mall that has old navy ulta tjmaxx world market beat buy big lots lane Bryant hallmark and thats just a few. This is one of the best exits within Columbus because there is so much and it stretches left and right with choices. Safe surroundings too. Polaris parkway is surrounded by upscale neighborhoods. 
NOW ABOUT THE BEDS
YOU WILL WANT TO READ
We got a studio with a queen bed and it was so hard I couldn't sleep until 6 am! And there will be an oversized chair and guess what it is a pull out twin bed! No one told us about this! I discovered it after trying to use cushions as pillows because there are not extras in the room. But I will add that I'm 5'6 170 pounds and anyone bigger or taller will not fit on the pullout. It is a mini twin. And our carpet needed more cleaning as it was stained. The room did have a full size fridge and cabinets but had few pans and had two small burners.

title: “Stay here a lot!”
text: Have now stayed at this hotel 9 times and have always had a good experience. From Betty at the front desk to the morning breakfast staff, they know me by name and treat me great. Good value for the money and close to UTSW where I go a lot. I agree with a couple of reviewers, a fridge and microwave in the room would be great (I sometimes get one). I feel safe at the hotel and love the dark curtains so i can sleep in if needed. Easy on/off I-35. If you need a hotel close to downtown/medical area then this is a great deal for the money. I will keep staying here for sure on visits to Dallas.

title: “No local paper? More corporate mediocrity.”
text:
I'm currently a guest, the location and staff are great and the room is decent. But, I doubt I'd stay here or another Holiday Inn again. Corporate vendors have ruined the personal experience 
As they say the devil is in the details and despite global warming (fact, not opinion) they still don't open the pool until Memorial day. My g/f likes to swim and what is labeled as the pool looks more like a large kidney shaped wading pool. As for me, they only deliver USA Today and no local paper. Bizarre. If you're coming from out of town one would expect they would want you to have access to what's going on locally. Never mind the fact USA Today is written in eighth grade english. 
I haven't gone to the the restaurant because the menu looks overpriced and unimaginative.
As for the gym, I guess if you think one brand of equipment works for everything, it's for you. Me, personally I like equipment that is selected for functionality, the Starttrac treadmills are great but the other Startrac equipment is useless, the elliptical is especially poorly designed. 
In conclusion, if you are a fan of MacDonald's, Appleby's, and the rest of corporate mediocrity this is the hotel for you! After this stay I doubt I will ever stay at another Holiday Inn or Intercontinental. But, hey I guess this is what happens when you emphasize shareholder value over product.

title: “Superb staff & location”
text:
Well this hotel was at the start of a trip I had with my wife to California and Vegas where we spent 3 nights at that hotel. From a shopping perspective the location is superb but I would downgrade to 4 stars as goin west is towards a bit of a dodgy area (Tenderloin) but thats towards midnight. 
The remaining of the experience was superb the room was well furnished but a bit small. The staff were extremely polite, helpful and would provide continuos tips on things to do. The fifth floor cofee was outstanding and so was the breakfast.
In general I would love to go back to this place to get a real flavour of San Francisco only avoid Tenderloin late at night but rather than that you have everything you could imagine around you,

title: “Great hotel, Affordable prices, big rooms, good location!”
text: A great hotel for the price in NYC - especially if coming with kids b/ the double rooms are huge and all rooms have a kitchen. Staff is extremely helpful as well.

title: “Great location and service but mattresses need changing”
text: Checked in on July 11th for a night after fights to La Guardia were cancelled. Very smooth check-in, great looking hotel with well laid out rooms except the mattress in room 228 sagged to the point of giving the sensation of being pitched downwards. Mentioned it to the front desk on check-out to but the woman merely giggled! All else was very good - excellent room service, convenience to the terminal building including one-time access for emergency shopping for stranded passengers.

title: “Awesome location - reasonable price”
text: The front desk clerk was friendly and helpful, as well as most of the Concierge staff with the exception of one rude one. The lobby is beautiful and the room was quite nice with the exception of the bathroom - extremely small. If you are a large person you will most likely touch the walls while trying to shower. The carpet is dated but clean. The bed had great linens and was very comfortable. The kitchenette was a convenient added bonus. It is a bit noisy at night but we did not expect it to be quiet in downtown Manhatten. Overall, we would stay here again if for no other reason than the great location.

title: “Everything about this hotel feels like a nightclub!”
text:
The Hotel on Rivington can be a fun place to stay, but it's not for everyone. First, understand that everything about the hotel has a nightclub feeling to it. The first floor is actually a restaurant/bar (with an adjacent hair salon). You take an elevator to the second floor to check in, and there is a lobby on the second floor for hotel guests. There is also a modern conference room, that was being used for a modeling photo shot when we arrived.
Upstairs the halls are painted black with a dark red accent pattern. The rooms have floor-to-ceiling windows and two great wraparound curtains, one sheer and one room-darkening. The beds are very comfortable, with TempurPedic memory foam mattresses and down comforters and pillows. The room also has a nightclub-like decor. Strangely the wall-mounted TV is small, not much bigger than my computer monitor, although it does swivel to face the bed or the seating area. The shower has a large window with no shade, but in our room it appeared that there was line of sight into the shower from other buildings. Or was there?! The balcony is unpleasant and small, and if you have any fear of heights or vertigo don't even go out there. You stand on a steel grating that is literally bolted on to the side of the building. I kept looking at the two steel bars (with two bolts on each) that were all that connected the balcony to the building. Was that rust on the bolts? Also, strangely, the balcony doors do not lock. Luckily no one lowered themselves on a rope ladder, ninja-style, from the balcony above us, and walked into our room, but the thought did cross my mind.
On the top floor there is a great 3-level penthouse space that can be rented for events, including a rooftop lounge with large wooden hot tub. Unfortunately on our first night they had a huge party up there, and we could hear the music and the dancing and the partying until 4 a.m. In general the rooms do not have very good exterior soundproofing, and even if there is not a rooftop party on the night you stay, you will hear the traffic & horns from Delancey Street and the Williamsburg Bridge well into the night.
Also be aware that the Lower East Side neighborhood is not for everyone. Unlike the bohemian shops and restaurants of the VIllage and the trendy boutiques of Soho, the East Side definitely has a rougher edge that recalls its role as a tenement slum in the early last century, and a pit of crime and drugs in previous decades. It is still more "Taxi Driver" than "Sex and the City," despite the many nightclubs, immigrants, and artists. It didn't feel particularly unsafe, but like this hotel you need to understand what you are getting into before you go.

title: “Appreciation for your Hard Work”
text:
To Whom it May Concern,
We recently held a wedding in one of your wonderful ballrooms, the Panahi & Cohen-Gadol Wedding, and it was very successful thanks to your wonderful, hard working crew and management. I deeply appreciate all the effort your crew put into this wedding which made it even more special. Thank you Billy, Elias, Estella, and Moses and the rest of the crew for being so pleasant and on time with your help, your work truly made a difference that night. title: “Superb Hotel. Great location depending on what you are there to do.”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for 4 nights and just loved it. Our room was extremely spacious. The bathroom was huge. Hotel amenities were outstanding. The lobby bar was always a great starting or ending point of our day.
The hotel is a bit isolated from retail and dining, but, very close to the National Mall and all of the Smithsonians. There are really minimal shopping and dining areas around the National Mall anyway. We always went to Dupont Circle for bars and restaurants. There is a Potbelly Sandwich shop next to the hotel which was great. Around the corner is the Cafe Twelve, great casual sandwiches for breakfast and lunch to go. Starbucks across from the hotel was nice. CVS is across from the hotel as well. That is ALL that is close to the hotel. I'm not kidding. Also, just a short walk to the waterfront. Be prepared to walk ALOT.

title: “Great little boutique hotel smack dab in the center of the business district!”
text: Hip little hotel right in the middle of the business district. Rooms were clean and well appointed. The staff was young and friendly. Don't remember if they had room service or a restaurant on site. After all who wants to eat in their room in San Francisco.

title: “Wonderful service, wonderful value”
text:
This hotel is very new, and the rooms are super clean and well-appointed for the price. A king suite at this hotel was 50% less than a 2 queen room at a nearby hotel. We stayed here with a 10 month old and a 4 year old, and the staff was super helpful. A crib was waiting for us in our room, the desk staff helped us get a ride to local shopping venues to get things we needed, and anything we requested was provided with a smile.
One night, we needed to do laundry, but the dryer was out of service. The housekeepers volunteered to let us use the hotel dryers after the load we were washing in the guest washer was finished. They took our wet clothing, dried it for us, and delivered it to our room (folded!) free of charge. They clearly go above and beyond at this hotel, and I couldn't recommend it strongly enough. 
And yes, it's a great looking hotel -- not your grandma's Holiday Inn, and it's very close to the airport, has its own restaurant (though it's more like a restaurant-ette with a limited menu and limited hours) with surprisingly decent food, a bar, and a pool. I have traveled for business and pleasure to luxury hotels that this inexpensive, family-friendly, airport hotel could rival.

title: “Good hotel, nice rooms”
text:
We stayed at the Essex Inn on 20th July for two nights having just arrived from the UK. The hotel is on Michigan Avenue on the opposite corner to the Hilton. Hotel pool was nice but extremely cold. We didn't eat in the hotel but had breakfast at Yolk ... a great place for breakfast and highly recommend it. Hackney's is a restaurant a couple of blocks away and was excellent american/mexican food...family friendly.
The hotel has a courtesy bus which will run you down town to the shopping district. You wait for it in the lobby. We were first there waiting with some friends and gradually the lobby filled up. Some people, unbeknown to us, had gone outside the hotel so when the bus arrived... they all filled it up with no space left for others who had waited for about 45 mins! Hotel should be clearer about where the bus picks up from and what the queuing set up is or first come first served basis.
We had prepaid for this hotel through Trailfinders in the UK but they still put a $75 7-day hold on our credit card which is now on it's 8th day and it is still on there. Had to email them to remove it.
Be sure when you check out of American hotels that you get a hard copy of your bill. Three times now on this trip across America, hotels have overcharged our card and I have had to chase them to re-credit our card. One of the hotels was the Hilton!
We walked from the Essex to downtown Chicago having missed the bus and actually it was a delight with beautiful architecture, parks... etc., Millenium Park is great and has a water fountain where the kids can put on their swimming gear and run about in the water jets which come out of animated towers. American Girl Store is a must for any young girl and Hersheys Chocolate was good too.

title: “This is a great place to stay!”
text: We stayed here for a week in August-September 2004. We weren't expecting such a great experience. First, the service in this hotel is just excellent -- a very big surprise. Second, the restaurant in the hotel is an award-winning, highly-acclaimed destination in and of itself. This is not a typical Marriott by any stretch and if you are visiting San Diego, I'd highly recommend it. It is very close to Del Mar and all of its restaurants and shopping. We had a delightful stay and we'll go back.

title: “Customer service was non Existent!! Don't do it people!!!”
text: Where do I begin!! I checked in mid afternoon July 14th with my two siblings, two from desk agents were at the front. A woman and a man the woman seemed to be pre occupied on the computer paying her phone bill and kindly asked the man to check us in. We were given all our stuff quickly and sent off with no information about the hotel features and minutes after arriving to our intensly small room had to call down about how to access the wifi. Then the NIGHTMEAR began...my brother used the washroom and the toilet stopped working we called down someone came to fix it but the room had an intense suage smell.. So we decided to open the balcony door and head out for our night activitys.. Upon arrival around 3am after a show we entered the room to find a horrible smell of suage!! Right away I went down stairs to ask for some airfreshiner or any kind of help really.. So I went down and explained the situation to the obviously grumpy night auditor.. He looked at me like I had interrupted his paper work and told me that house keeping opens in the morning (when I check out). He askers me what type of smell I answer him then he asks with attitude if I thought about closing the bathroom door. Of Course that was our first instinct I said. So he asked me what I would like him to do, I asked for some ferbreeze maybe. He started angrily going through the drawers(slamming them) as if I had I convienced him or I was a homeless person begging to sleep in a hotel I pay OVER 200 dollars a night for! I felt very unconfortable so I told him that's fine we will figure it out and went and went back to the room. To avoid confrontation and to address his behavior with someone else in the morning when I got upstairs I called down to ask for his name long story short the phone conversation was dumbfounding, he told me I didn't need his name because I refused assistance and that he basically wasn't going to tell me his name he ended the conversation by telling me to talk to a manager in the morning and hung up!!! I could not believe it I was being so polite to him and he treated me so rudely! I told the managaer on the morning and thats was about it i got an apology and no sleep. I will NEVER stay at a BEST WESTERN again, first and last time

title: “Great Staff”
text: This hotel is a little older, but it is very nice. Anat at the front desk is great!!! All of the staff does a nice job and I am very happy I picked this hotel.

title: “Good and Comfortable”
text: There are so many things to enjoy offered by the hotel. The pool, free full breakfast, fitness center and comfortable pillows with the bed. The hotel is surrounded by other hotels so they need to be alittle bit better than the rest. Check in is easy, but I ran into several problems during my last stay and there was one one person to assist and I waited a LONG time. The hotel offers DISH TV so if its windy the reception is terrible. My room door entry lock quit working and I was forced to get teh front desk to open my door everytime I needed to get in. No maintenance guy on duty or a reason they couldn't fix it for some reason. Small problems that they can help with faster. Overall a decent place to stay and I will again.

title: “Speak as you find”
text:
We were at the Roosevelt for five nights over the UK October half term. Myself, wife and two boys (10&15) had reserved a superior room but the very cheerful receptionist upgraded us to a Deluxe- which was nice! The room was on the seventh floor with a great view of Madison Ave. It had two very comfortable King-size beds, good TV and plenty of room for.......stuff.
Now, as I say in the intro, one has to "speak as you find" and we found: friendly staff- Mike the concierge was very helpful and booked a great helicopter trip for us; a quiet, clean well presented room and bathroom; the bar straight out of cheers- with good beer-BASS! and great atmosphere.
Super location near to everything. We had breakfast over the road at "Cosi" most mornings- good value and friendly-made us a lovely cup of tea! We were able to walk everywhere in midtown easily from the hotel. We found a lovely Italian restaurant off Times Square called Bella Vita and ate there a couple of times.
All in all, a fantastic holiday and at such a good price!

title: “Great Hotel”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Westin on our wedding night in order for our early-morning honeymoon flight to be a little bit easier to make. We were only looking for convenience, but we got a fantastic, classy hotel that I would recommend to anyone staying in the Detroit area, not only those who need a hotel convenient to the airport. Our room was huge, with a king bed, desk, large dresser, big bathroom, flat-screen tv, and sofa. We ordered room service, which arrived very quickly. The reception and lobby area are very pretty and modernly decorated.

title: “Closer than Close...”
text: I stayed at the BW after reading previous reviews. I loved everything about this hotel. The room service was excellent, there were not bugs, the continental breakfast was awesome considering the large variety (hot/cold cereal, waffles, sausage biscuits, variety of juices etc. My daughter, husband and I enjoyed the stay. The computer room was nice i was allowed to charge my iPod for free.The pool was refreshing and somehow guests bar-b-qued. There was no noise at night. This hotel is right next to the expressway and close to all my new kin folks...............also take extra pjs the AC is extremely COLD.......

title: “Great Price and Location”
text:
I stayed at the Comfort Inn Theatre District for 1 week in August. This was my second time staying at the hotel and I was happy with it again. Location is everything with this hotel. 2 blocks from times square, most theatres are only a few blocks away. Lion King and Rock of Ages are on same street. Restaurant row and many other restaurants are close by. We walked everywhere from here: Central Park, Rockefeller Center, Madison Square Garden, Empire State, 5th ave shopping... For anything farther away you can catch the subway at times square that is just a few short blocks away. Grayline Tours is a few blocks away (they do the open top tour buses). 
The rooms are a little small but I think that is common of any hotel in NY. We managed fine with three of us in a room. Room was clean other than the comforter on one bed was dirty when we got there and not cleaned for the entire week. We took it off the bed and left it off. Sheets were good. Also our room wasn't vacuumed the entire week we were there. Although I did see them vacuum other rooms when guests changed. 
Breakfast is your standard continental breakfast. The eating area is small so can get crammed if you go at the busy time. We took our food to our room to eat most days. 
Only one elevator and is a little slow so you can wait for a while if lots of people leaving at same time. We took the stairs a lot. 
I would stay here again because I love the location although I was a little bothered by the dirty comforter. I hear it is common for hotels to not wash comforters very often and just wash the sheets.

title: “nice room at a great rate!”
text: We stayed at the Hotel George for one night. The room was clean and well decorated. It was not as spacious as other Kimpton hotel rooms we have stayed in, but fine for a night. We ordered room service once: the portions were small and the price on the high side, but the quality was nice and service was prompt. The service throughout the hotel was great- the staff seemed very friendly and happy to help. The location was convenient- it was within walking distance to the museums and close to Union Station. I would stay again for a short visit.

title: “loved it!”
text:
I can't say enough good things about the Mosser. I'd be very, very surprised if there was anywhere else in SF that offered such good value for money, such an amazing location and such consistently good customer service. 
Like others have pointed out, the rooms are small but they're spotless and very well designed. The location is superb - very safe compared to just a few blocks further down the road (I had friends staying on 7th St off Market and the difference was marked) and also within walking distance of just about everything you'll need. The service was exceptional (I also stayed at the Whitcomb - avoid! - and the Hilton - so, so) and the little touches, like the free muffins and coffee for breakfast, very welcome. 
I can't fault it and I'll definitely be staying there the next time I'm in SF. It's a no-brainer, people - book it!

title: “Great Customer Service”
text:
I am really impressed with this hotel. The location is within 2 miles from the airport. The decor is contemporary. Both the bar and dining area was comfortable. But most importantly, the customer service was excellent. Huy, at the front desk, bent over backwards to be accommodating. He helped me get the best price for my room. He answered all my questions about the local sites, and he was just plain nice. Renato in dining was great, too.
The next time I visit San Jose, I'll definitely stay at the Crowne Plaza.

title: “Everything about our stay in this hotel...”
text: Everything about our stay in this hotel was fabulous. First impressive thing is they answer the phone directly there is no automated service. When I called from Miami to ask directions someone answered. Within two rings and was very helpful. Then I got an early checkin and late checkout. The room was spacious and clean. The tvs were awesome flat screen with hdmi input, they make it very easy to hookup your video game. The breakfast and dinners are decent and the staff is the best I have ever seen the location is close to everything. If you're coming to Chicago with your family there is no better choice. Thanks

title: “Great location - great hotel - great staff- WOW!!”
text:
I am a Hilton Diamond member who often travels to Charlotte....probably 4 times a month.
 I have tried the local Hiltons, Doubletrees, Homewood Suites, Hilton Garden Inns, etc in the Charlotte area. And all were pretty good. BUT THIS PLACE IS THE BEST!! It has a great location near the upscale Southpark mall. The hotel is on a pedestrian friendly mall of it's own. A short walk to Dean & Delucca for a sandwich, snacks, etc. The hotel itself is VERY attractive both inside and out. I was thrilled to be there!!. The staff was top notch and very helpful with suggestions on local restaurants. I CAN NOT SAY ENOUGH GOOD ABOUT THIS PLACE. IT IS THE BEST. I will make this my only Hilton stay in Charlotte from now on.

title: “Great service”
text:
The staff at the Red Roof Inn when above and beyond service, I booked my room on the wrong date and was actually a no show and they just set me up with a room.
They gave me so much help with my day in Seattle!
Not the prettiest hotel in the world but the service is 5 star. Thanks for all the help.

title: “A Nice Place”
text: A very nice place, but . We had a problem getting the television to work, but a call to the front desk summoned a maintence man who quickly fixed it. It was very noisy on the 17th street side of the hotel with lots of partying and kids running around but I guess that was to be expected on a Parade of Lights evening. Fortunately our suite was far enough from the noise that it did not bother us.

title: “Sufficient”
text: Rooms are very small for the price, but location is great. We had a one double bed and private bathroom but overall felt like you were in a closet. There was also no view from the window but it's very clean hotel.

title: “would recommend!”
text: Excellent location, few steps to Chinatown, a few blocks to Union Square, BART and cable cars. Clean room and bathroom, bearable noise (came to room so tired, didn't even pay attention to that))), friendly staff, cheap rate. Would stay there again without doubt, were very pleased.

title: “A real find...”
text:
To be able to actually open your window and get fresh air is no small feat in NY... Stayed on a room facing the street on the 8th floor. The room was spacious, the bathroom spot clean with lots of fresh towels when we needed. Thanks to a tip provided on this forum, we draw a straight line when presented with the "tip voucher" at b'fast, whch was included in the room rate, as not to be surprised with "additions" at the end of our stay..... All the staff were more than helpful, but outstanding were the bell boys/concierge. And, finally, the location!!! Subway station right at the hotel's front door can't be beaten.
The only complaint is the mattress - it sunk in the middle and I had to sleep on the edge... careful not to fall on the floor......
Otherwise - highly recommended !

title: “Nice hotel, hectic location, need some touch ups”
text: My husband & I travel to NYC several times a year for fun. Each time we have stayed somewhere different. We stayed at the W Times Square over Thanksgiving in 2003 since we wanted to be near the parade route. We booked a wonderful room and thought it was extremely spacious for a NY hotel. The Blue Fin bar was nice but the drinks were expensive. We went there once just for the atmosphere. It was nice not to have the lobby on the ground floor since the Times Square is so hectic. It is a great location if you plan to see some broadway shows. I loved the hotel but would not stay there again just b/c of the location. It is way too chaotic.

title: “Great find in Philly!”
text:
My boyfriend and stayed in this hotel for three nights in January, and we were very very impressed. The hotel is older but has been completely redesigned in a modern and chic way. 
Our room was great, with hard wood floors and a brick washroom, which made it very comfortable and stylish. 
The location was ideal as we were right between new and old philly. 
The reception staff was also very helpful. 
The breakfast was good for continental- but no one should expect bacon and eggs...
I would definitely recommend the hotel, especially if you can get a great deal as we did.

title: “A more than decent hotel for the price”
text:
I recently stayed at this hotel for 2 nights (July 8 & 9) during a combined holiday/business trip to Colorado. Although I inadvertently booked a smoking room, the hotel immediately, at my request, were able to switch it to a non-smoking on the second floor (if I understood correctly, the rooms on the lower floors are newer). 
My room was clean, beds and bedding were comfortable, wi-fi was fine. The hotel was not noisy and I slept well. Breakfast was excellent -- among the best I've had in the Choice family of hotels -- with a wide variety of cold and hot choices, including porridge, cottage cheese and fresh cut fruit!
The hotel was for me a wee bit difficult to find, in the dark with the GPS -- but I think Lily, my GPS guide may have been a bit confused :). The hotel does offer a free shuttle which worked well for me the two times I used it, both for pick-up and drop-off in Denver. 
Front desk staff were reasonable, with just a couple of minor things:
- lack of clarity regarding the shuttle pick-up location. I was initially told it would pick me up where I needed, but when I later called for an actual pick-up I was told that I needed to go to a specific location. The woman on the phone was at first very unhelpful in explaining where I could find the pick-up location, frustrating since I was tired and not at all familiar with Denver. However it eventually got figured out.
- just prior to check-out I was unfortunately delayed because the last minute items from the bathroom and dressing area that I needed to pack in my bags were all wet. I needed to empty out water, dry everything off, and pack damp items. Grossness of grossness, I realized the water came from leakage in the ceiling in both those rooms. Very yucky and very annoying and also because I had timed my morning in order to return a car rental by the required time. I advised the desk clerk at check-out who assured me I would hear from the desk manager via email (he/she was not on site at that time) but, 8 days later I have yet to hear something.

title: “Perfect, Relaxing Luxury”
text: I frequently travel to Denver for work and always stay at the same big name hotel chain. This time they were sold out so I chose the Brown Palace which I walk by on my way to the office. I knew about its history and heard from others that it was really nice, so I decided to stay. From the moment I walked inside I could tell that this hotel was luxury all the way. I walked into my room and was literally taken back. It was huge and it wasn't a suite or anything. I had a king bed, flat screen tv, coffee table, couch, and 6 lamps. How big does a room need to be for 6 lamps? Pretty big, and the bathroom...wow. The shower was about 7ft in length, all marble, and had shower heads on both sides that sprayed you from everywhere. Who needs the spa in the hotel when you have a shower like that. Everyone was very nice, and the food in the 5 hotel restaurants was great. You'd be crazy not to stay here!

title: “Many stays at this property”
text: Our grandkids live a few miles away so this is our place to stay to see them. The rooms are clean and spacious, bed was good, check in easy, breakfast is good and varied, pool clean. We also attended a convention in Oak Hill last weekend and spread the news at the meeting that it was only a short drive from this IH express and that people should stay at this property next year. So, I guess we are the new advertising committee! :)

title: “As Mentioned”
text: Don't bother staying here if you don't care about going online (internet). Fitness center needs major work, as well as housekeeping dropping the ball a couple of times. Good luck.

title: “Nicest HGI I've Stayed At”
text:
This hotel is 10 stories high, and the classiest Garden Inn I've ever stayed in (and I've stayed in a lot). Typically, you'd expect the white tile entry with the chandelier and the Golden Girls furniture. Not here. This place is like walking into swank W or the like, with a great bar stocked with flat screens, and very courteous staff. The room was great with all of the latest amenities, and here's (sadly) one of the best parts- outlets everywhere! No struggle to plug in my iPod, Blackberry, laptop, Bluetooth- plenty of electrical current to spare!
The only dig on this place is its location- although in good proximity to the airport, Van Buren is known to be one of the raunchiest parts of Phoenix, and this hotel sticks out like a 10 story sore thumb. Great hotel, just stay indoors after the sun goes down (unless crack and prostitutes are a part of your business trip).

title: “Fantastic”
text: Third stay at this resort was the best ever. Newly renovated rooms are great, water park a blast as usual, and food excellent with lots of choices. The staff was very friendly. Highly recommend if you have kids that like water parks. Mine are 10 and 13 and loved it.

title: “Great Hotel, Great Location”
text:
I recently stayed at the Casablanca and was wonderfully surprised at this little hotel. We had no trouble finding the hotel, the location is fantastic! The hotel staff was very helpful and our rooms were such a nice change from the typical hotel rooms that I have stayed in for years. My only negative was the warmth of the room, we like cooler rooms and the rooms were too warm for comfort and when we adjusted the thermostat down it didn't make a lot of difference. The heat is radiator heat versus central air which is why it is harder to manage. The internet connection was great for me and being free always factors into the cost of a hotel.
I would recommend this hotel to anyone wanting to visit the city.

title: “Location, not too expensive and nice people”
text: That s the Grant Hotel for me.. room was clean.. it s very close to Union Square (so close to the Bart, from the airport) and cable car stop in Bush Street (30 seconds walking from Hotel).. just a bit noisy if you get room facing the main street.. overall was good for us!

title: “This is THE HOTEL”
text: Words are not enough to describe this hotel, not only the rooms are perfect but everything else is just like a dream. We enjoyed a stay in The Waldorf in a long weekend pre-christmas, if you have the occasion (and the money) do not hesitate! Love it!

title: “Kind of like a Residence Inn but downtown in a high rise...”
text:
The Magnolia is a unique hotel - it's in a good location if you want to stay downtown, and the rooms are enormous - at least mine was. I had a one bedroom "apartment" basically, with a full kitchen. A little overkill for a one night stay but I wish I had a room like this when I was here for a week! 
The breakfast is really average, what you might get from a Residence Inn or something like that. Buffet and after a few days it would get old fast. Fortuntely if you want to spend a few dollars there are many breakfast places really close by.
I wasn't impressed by the fitness room, I don't understand why these places think that a having aerobic machines constitutes a gym. They have the room but I'd like to see more varied equipment.
The bed was comfy and my only regret is that it was an overnight stay and I didn't get more time to spend here.
One pet peeve - on the way out I asked for a Taxi to the airport and they pulled up with a Limo. I asked the price and it was quite a bit more expensive than a Taxi. My problem is I asked for a Taxi, not a limo, and I don't need to be part of some payback scheme between the bellman and the limo driver. Be honest, and maybe you would have got a tip from me instead of sending me looking for my own cab on the street. I might try this place again because I really did like the room.

title: “Great hotel, bad timing”
text:
I got a fantastic deal for this hotel on Priceline for a one-night stay en route to Louisville. Hotel was fantastic, room was great, nice and quiet, staff couldn't have been friendlier.
The only problem was that it was Indiana Black Expo Summer Celebration weekend in Indy. Cops were everywhere. Streets were blocked off. It took me 60 minutes of wandering through downtown Indy to be able to get into the parking garage.
When I got to the hotel's doors, I was stopped by security and asked whether I had a bracelet to get in. I didn't and then had to get one as I check in. Seemed prison-like, but I don't blame them. The event has been spiraling out-of-control. I think about 10 people were shot a year earlier.
Again, I'd recommend the hotel to anyone. It's a fantastic stay. Just make sure you know what's going on downtown when you're planning to stay.

title: “Perfect for our short stay city break”
text: We didn't require plush accommodation as we were out of the room from early until late. Just needed decent service with clean rooms and good bathroom. The Comfort Inn had all these things. Towels and bedding changed every day if you wanted plus a clean around. Breakfast was just the ticket with hot and cool food and drink choices. Free wifi was great, we took the laptop so we could stay on top of city events and plan our days out. Also were able to leave our bags in a lock up on check out day so still able to max out our final day without lugging bags around. I would recommend it.

title: “Met High Hopes for quality!”
text:
After having a priceline bid for a four star in downtown SA accepted (on second try, with short notice), we stayed at the Hyatt for one Saturday night, for $100, plus priceline fees and taxes that brought the total to $125. 
After receiving the notice of acceptance, I called the hotel directly to request specifics. I had heard that guests receiving "bid" rates were given the less than desirable rooms, but Hyatt really took care of us.
I asked for a non-smoking, upper-level room in a corner with a King bed, and we got a beautiful room on the top floor (1118 - highly recommended), in the corner! The redecoration was really nice - contemporary, with quality materials. The room was in perfect condition and the bed was extremely comfortable - lots of pillows! 
Staff was all very friendly...if you want to be on the river walk, this location is perfect. Expect to pay about $10 for a night of parking in the garage across the street...I think there is a $16 charge for hotel guests staying up to a week.

title: “Twentieth Wedding Anniversary heaven !”
text:
To celebrate our twentieth wedding anniversary my wife and I spent a long weekend in New York. We had heard much about Fitzpatrick's and were eager to check it out. I travel extensively with my work and can compare this hotel against many others around the globe. I don't post reviews as a rule but feel on this occasion that the quality of this hotel and its staff warrants a post.
The location is perfect. We walked everywhere from Central Park to Times Square.
The staff are terrific.They are professional, helpful but not overly intrusive.
The hotel is spotless. We had a suite on the 11th floor. It felt like home from home.
It has an Irish feel....... but new Ireland, not OTT Blarney !
I might be swayed a little by the spice of rekindled romance and a large 'brownie' balance but it wouldn't have happened without the perfect venue and the most gracious of hosts. 
Fitzpatick's take a bow.........

title: “Comfy, Clean, Wonderful Location....”
text:
My husband and I just returned from a trip to San Antonio (5/16 - 5/23) and had the wonderful pleasure of staying at the O'Brien. I made the reservations solely on recommendations from this site, and the cost was very reasonable. When you walk in the door you know immediately this is the place for you. Staff very friendly...Geoffrey at check-in, and Sherri in the mornings... Sherri did a great job of keeping the morning breakfast items supplied and fresh. We enjoyed grabbing a bottle of water supplied at the front desk everytime we left for the riverwalk...(just a few brief steps away)... and being able to get coffee, mocha's ,hot chocolate any time of day was great. For $90.00 (plus tax) we had a very nice balcony room. We got our morning coffee, food and took it back up to our room and read the paper out on ther balcony. It is a long balcony shared by other rooms, we met some nice folks on our stay there. Our room was 211, with a king size bed. The bathroom had an old fashioned claw-footed tub with gold fixtures. Plenty of water pressure in the shower. There is turn-down service at nite, with chocolates left on your pillow !!!
I am a bit of a hotel snob...as my husbnd says...I search high and low when we travel to make sure we have a clean, comfortable room. The O'Brien definitely fits that bill. We will definitely stay there again, without hesitation, one of the best stays I've had while traveling. When I stay again I will request a room on the second floor with the balcony...room 211 if available !!!

title: “Fantastic Little Spot in Union Sq”
text: My husband and I had mutual business trips and he had selected this hotel. While I usually book at a larger chain as I am a member of their loyalty program, I was pleasantly surpirsed upon arrival at how nice the rooms were (we upgraded to the back building by the pool). Although no one offered to assist me with my luggage so I had to lug up a large bag by myself up the stairs to othe other building, after that the service improved and everyone was very friendly and helpful. It was a great place to get some work done then relax by the quiet courtyard poolside, and a fantastic location right in the middle of Union Square. Top amenities in room but they could some in room movies (perhaps ours did not work) would be nice. Aside from that, the only areas that could use improvement is incorporating an onsite fitness center (you currently get a discounted rate at a gym very close by) and some free hi speed or wireless at least in the restaurant. Charming place overall and would definitely stay there again.

title: “Oasis in Boston”
text: Great city hotel in a fabulous downtown location, you can walk or take the subway anywhere from this hotel. The warm friendly staff is helpful in every way. The rooms are clean and comfortable. The restaurant is excellent,"The Woodward" go for drinks,eat and enjoy the fun lively crowd. Tip: Ask for Trish, she is the best waitress and the most fun and adorable.

title: “What's not to love ?”
text:
We stay here off and on when coming up from Orange County to see a play at the Pantages or several other smaller theaters close by. Often we will come up by train and then Metro it to this hotel, a very easy trip. We do not get the suites with kitchens but even the "smaller" rooms have eating areas with a small refrigerator.
This hotel is clean, cute and cheap. It is also friendly. Free continental breakfast, free internet, free parking. free exercise/steam room on top of a great room at a great price- what's not to love ?
It is very close to the Hollywood/Highland Metro station where you can easil;y get to: downtown, Chinatown, Little Tokyo, Pasadena, Universal Studios, Union Station, The Music Center, as well as many other places of interest. We always make sure we have dinner at Musso and Franks when staying here.

title: “You will not feel at the White House, but you will experience 4S Service Quality”
text:
This is absolutely not the New York or Istanbul 4S. Its kind of old, brick and mortar building, right in Georgetown. There is no lounge to have a drink, just a steakhouse with an inside bar. BTW, the steaks there are lightly boiled in butter first, then grilled, good but not worth the cholesterol damage! But the seared Foie Gras is remarkable and worth the unhealthy chemicals! The fitness and spa are surprisingly large and well equipped, at the end of a long way to get there. The pool is a lap pool, nothing fancy, rather small and inside only. The rooms are somewhat contemporary, but somewhat traditional as well.
As a location is is just outside of the downtown buzz, but very close also. There are nice cafés and shopping around the hotel, and the service is 4S quality. We visited other properties while we were there, like the W, the Jefferson's and a couple others, and that confirmed our first choice on the 4S. We did not see the Park Hyatt inside but it seemed well located and it may be a good option to try as well.
So overall a good choice if you value the 4S exceptional service. But do not expect the typical expansive lobby and lounge, contemporary design that other 4S offer.

title: “Luxurious getaway with the family”
text:
I've stayed at the Four Seasons Seattle several times, both on business and for family getaways. The service is always excellent, discreet yet friendly, and the rooms are beautiful and luxurious. 
When traveling with my family, we upgrade to a slightly larger room which is very generously sized to accommodate 2 queens + a rollaway without feeling cramped. The bathrooms are gorgeous with a separate toilet area, shower and soaker tub and my favourite L'Occitane bath products. If you let them know you're traveling with children, they send them up a lovely welcome snack (locally made chips, soft drink, cookie) and, for younger children, a darling stuffed animal!
The outdoor pool area is beautiful but less appealing in the cooler months - not that that stops my daughter from insisting on swimming. The infinity pool is beautiful - pics taken from the right angle make it look like you're swimming in the ocean! The hot tub is nice as is the fire pit. 
There's self-serve coffee and espresso drinks tucked away in a hidden area of the lobby (near the elevators) and a small amount of pastries in the morning but you have to get there early! The pastries are gone in a flash and the coffee/tea service disappears quite early; can't remember the exact time but it's very limited. However you're right by Pike Place Market so excellent coffee and breakfast options are within a 1-2 minute walk.

title: “Stunning!”
text: This hotel is fabulous! The location is great, staff are friendly and we love the modern decor. We've stayed there many times and always recommend it to friends or family that are visiting Chicago. It is within walking distance to many attractions and nice restaurants!

title: “Worst Hotel Ever”
text: My husband, myself and a group of people stayed at the Blake Hotel May 20th and 21st. This is by far the worst hotel I have ever stayed in and do not recommend it to anyone. I dont even know where to begin... At check in we found out that they like to nickel and dime you with parking. Normally when making a resevation you would think that would be brought up. The front desk staff was great when it came to taking it off for us. One couple in our group was charged for parking and they didnt even have a car. That was also taken off the bill at the end of the stay. Next the $10 breakfast...WHAT A JOKE!!!!!! If you like to pay $10 for dried cereal then this is the place for you. Also they charge $3 for a cup of coffee with no refills. The was NO hot water in the rooms and the shower is terrible. It is a half glass door and water gets all over the floor. You use all the towels in your room just to clean up the water. The maid decided that since we ask them 10 minutes before they were leaving to clean our friends room they werent doing it, so they had a dirty room for 2 days. Like we know you are off at a certain time. We were also there with a group of people and had a "block" of rooms. Yeah right everyone was spread out everywhere on different floors. The shuttle service was pretty much non existant. There was no room service so if you were hungry you had to travel to get food. Real nice for people who dont live in the area. Thermastats did not work in some of the rooms and they were so hot. The pool is really small and by a busy road. WIFI was not included. There was no mini friidge. We will not even concider this place on our next trip down to Charlotte. I would rather pay the extra money and get the ammenities then stay at the place again.

title: “Excellent stay”
text: First of all I have to express surprise at the reviews that don't give this property its just reward. Our stay there was nothing short fantastic. The room was great, the service even better and the location is enviable. Perhaps some of the other reviews don't take into consideration that every big city has big city realities. Manhattan, Los Angeles, London, it doesn't matter, you will find traffic, people (yes some of them vagrants), and all the challenges of big city life. Maybe some of the reviewers are safe in their sleepy suburban utopias but that is not the reason why you visit San Francisco in the first place! You are on Market street! That's like Times Square or Hollywood Boulevard! Location, Location, Location, and the price makes this place a great bargain. I love San Francisco and have stayed at numerous hotels all over the city (most of them much more expensive) but this one hits the spot. In prior trips I ended up spending my money on expensive cab transportation to the area where this hotel is located. Now I just walk out the door and enjoy the best the city has to offer. Absolutely recommend it.

title: “Nice place good location”
text: Clean and friendly good safe location easy to access just about any area of Jax. The breakfast had a lot to choose from and the place was clean and for the most part quiet. Love the fact that my dog is always welcome..

title: “The beds are a vacation in themselves!”
text: Super comfy beds and pillows! The rooms are funky and cool. Definitely great for those who want a little sass in their stay. The staff were attentive and helpful, even calling after we got settled to make sure we were happy. Yes, the rooms aren't palatial- but you're in downtown Seattle, what do you expect?

title: “Beautiful property, great service!”
text: Designed in a French style the rooms are beautifully appointed and much larger than average. The service is fantastic and the location is very convenient.

title: “Nice hotel in excellent location”
text: he hotel was very nice but the unfriendliness of the staff should deserve a prize: The most unfriendly bunch in the world! Would I recommend it? Only if you are sure you don't neet anything from the reception or anyone else working in this hotel.

title: “think twice before staying here”
text:
Let me start by saying I generally love La Quinta hotels and have stayed in many all around the country. I was very surprised to find this hotel to be so poorly cared for. Pretty much everything was dirty. The rug in our room was the worst, but not as bad as the breakfast room. The counters had a smear of sticky and goo across them. There didn't seem to be anyone working in the room as there has been at all of our other La Quinta stays.
The parking is inside a gated area that you need a # to enter because of the neighborhood. I noticed that the back parking lot door was unlocked at all times. When I asked about the non-locking doors they told me it wasn't needed because of the security gate. This seemed fine until while walking my dog, I noticed a gaping hole in the corner of the gate. It was large enough for a large male to easily get through. 
If you are looking for a place close to Graceland that is cheap to stay at and you are not overly concerned with sanitary conditions or safety, this might be a perfect place for you.

title: “Great location. Lots of space. Pleasant staff. Good breakfast.”
text: We stayed at this hotel for two nights, at the end of October. We usually stay at one of the Embassy Suites downtown, but we got a good deal on this Homewood Suites and we will definitely stay there again. It's just down the street from our favorite restaurant, Joe's Steak and Seafood, which was definitely a plus. Also, just across the street from the Nordstrom's entrance to the Mall on Michigan Ave. We walk everywhere, when we are in Chicago, so this hotel was great. We were there on a weekend, so didn't get to try the Manager's Reception. I'd give it 5 stars, but the bathroom door would hit the toilet, if the seat was down and it could use a little updating. That being said, we're looking forward to our next visit. Also, I went looking for some hair things, so I could put up my daughter's hair and couldn't find any in their shop, so asked at the front desk and they gave me a handful of rubberbands. Just what we needed! :-)

title: “In Desperate Need of an Update!”
text:
While the location of and the view from the hotel is lovely, I cannot find anything else positive about our one night stay. Because we were attending an event at the hotel, we thought it would be just to stay on site. Terrible mistake! Even though we were supposed to stay for 4 nights, we checked out after just one and were fortunate to get a room at The Grand Del Mar. 
I fully admit to being somewhat of a hotel snob, but I can suck it up and deal with less than a perfect accommodation if I have to; however, the level of inferiority at the Hilton San Diego Resort & Spa was just too much to take. From the dingy room, to the terrible, teeny-tiny bathroom to the subpar breakfast during which I was served tea with curdled milk after a half-hour search for black tea bags, my list of dissatisfactions could go on and on.

title: “Great location and Value”
text: This is obviously and older hotel and shabby in some aspects, but we just returned from a two nite stay in a 1 bed suite with our two kids. The hotel is in a great location, near times square, subway, theatres, etc. The suite was much bigger than I thought. The kids slept on the pull out and we had the bedroom to ourselves. Both rooms had TVs. Very comfy and clean. Elevator was very small and some areas a bit musty. But, again, a great value.

title: “Average at best”
text:
There are better choices for the money.
Room just average. Clean and comfortable enough. No mini-fridge as I've come to expect from a Marriott. No chairs on the tiny balcony. 
Pool and courtyard areas situated where they are shaded until at least late morning or early afternoon (no warm, sunny areas to sit in the morning hours.)
Nice bar area, but extraordinarily rude bartender on duty when we visited (arrived near closing time. He left no room for doubt that he was ready to go home!) Otherwise, staff was courteous, though the doormen were overly aggressive. Declined assistance with bags, they grabbed them anyway (so of course I was obligated to tip.)
Not a great selection in the restaurant: nothing offered for an inexpensive, casual bite to eat. Only dined there once, at breakfast - food OK, but extremely slow service. Even heard a server tell another guest - "if you don't order the [overpriced, unless you're starving] buffet, you will be here a while." Very true.
Unlikely I will stay here again. Chose hotel due to proximity to Qualcomm stadium, but there are others within a few miles. Best rate I could find was $125. Not worth it.

title: “Great location, but service needs improving.”
text: We stayed for 3 nights over Easter. The hotel is really well located and in very close walking distance to many amenities. The room was large with a great view of the city and an amazingly comfortable bed. On the down side, the rooms was not ready when we arrived (2pm) and we waited in the lobby for someone to tell us when we could go to our room, but nobody came. The maid service was adequate, but they overlooked clearing away used glasses and emptying bins. The most aggravating feature is that the hotel WiFi will not connect in the guest rooms and is only intermittent in the lobby. The staff did eventually sort it out, but hardly service with a smile!

title: “Best quality/price in NYC”
text: I booked two rooms last February. My wife, my daughter and I stayed in one room and my sister and her friend who were visiting from Europe stayed in the other room. The hotel location is great. The lobby is deceiving compared to the rooms which are nicely appointed, large for NY standard and comfortable. The bathroom is nothing different than your typical hotel bathroom but with more amenities. The room was large enough to have a king size bed, a pull out couch and a table without feeling tight. And they do not charge more if you use the pull out couch. The bed was comfortable and pillows smelled fresh. The staff was very friendly. This is the best quality/price hotel I have ever found in NYC. Two nice French restaurants nearby - Le Bateau Ivre - www.lebateauivrenyc.com/ - and Le Montparnasse - montparnasseny.com. They serve brunch too.

title: “Great hotel, great location, awesome staff.”
text:
For a weekend trip to San Francisco, after researching all the hotels around Fisherman's Wharf, my wife and I chose the Best Western Plus Tuscan Inn on North Point Street. The two main reasons; 1) The location is in walking distance (two short blocks) of some of the best restaurants at the Wharf and 2) They had a special that included valet parking at no additional cost. This alone saved us approximately $44 per day. The cost of the room, at $300+ per night, was high but pretty much every hotel in the area was the same or higher. So any savings you can find is awesome. When you add the mostly above average reviews on Tripadvisor and other sites we were sold. 
Upon arrival we were greeted by the valet and were ushered in to the front desk, right inside the front door. The staff here is wonderfully friendly and very patient no matter what the need. As with most hotels in the area the room is rather small but not tiny. Our room was tucked away in a corner so we had no issues with noise from other rooms or from the hall. It was also very neat and clean. The only issue we had with the room is the sink area is outside the bathroom (which is normally very good) but is very small and the bathroom door opens into the area making it hard to maneuver if one person is using the sink area and another is in the bathroom. But as long as you "plan ahead" it's a non-issue.
One nice thing is the hotel hosts a complimentary wine reception every afternoon starting at 5PM, allowing guests to mingle while they try out California wines. There is also a restaurant on site, Café Pescatore. Unfortunately we did not get the chance to try it but the menu looks awesome and appears to be priced reasonably.
Overall a great hotel in the heart of the Fisherman's Wharf area. A great and friendly staff made for a highly enjoyable stay. I would highly recommend staying here and will do so again on our next trip to the area.

title: “Great Hotel for the price”
text:
I stayed at Hotel 31 recently and also stayed last year. I think for the money you pay here the hotel is great. I have stayed in lots of hostels and budget hotels in NYC and this is by far my favourite.
