The rooms are clean and I was lucky this time with a great view of the Empire State Building. The shared bathrooms are always clean and I have never had to wait to use one. The location is fantastic, right in the heart of Manhattan. The staff were all really helpful and friendly.
I would recommend this hotel to any budget traveller who just wants somewhere to rest their head between embarking on the sightseeing, shopping and nightlife of NYC and think that for $69 a night it is a good deal.

title: “Downtown Sheraton in Baltimore”
text:
I recently stayed at the Sheraton at 101 West Fayette Street, Baltimore, MD. 
#1) Don't deviate from the area (especially alone). Baltimore's finest are just about on every corner when night falls, but they can't see everything.
#2) Approximately 6 blocks walking distance from the Harbor (not too bad)
#3) Kudos to the staff for the daily, refreshing, complimentary water in the lobby. It truly hit the spot on those 90+ degree days.
 #4) Hotel offers a daily Happy Hour from 5pm-7pm which tap beers are $3, most specialty and mixed drinks are $5, and a selection of appetizers are $5. This may be the most economical time to dine at the hotel. The restaurant's regular menu is way over priced. C'mon...who is willing to pay $10 for a burger and an additional $2.95 for fries? Hello? The hotel is one block walking distance from Burger King, McDonald's, and Subway.
#5) Other than the expensive restaurant, housekeeping was wonderful and the staff was friendly. My housekeeper, Ms. Yolanda on the 14th floor, was very professional and did an excellent job keeping my room clean and fresh.

title: “Great location, nice hotel.”
text:
I've made several week-long stays at this hotel. It has a great location, close to Times Square but out of the general hubbub. It's also within easy walking distance to a lot of ethnic restaurants, plus it's across the street from a Food Emporium, a grocery store that also stocks prepared foods. There's also a very nice French bistro attached to the hotel. I only tried it for breakfast, but it was very good, and the atmosphere was relaxing, early in the morning at any rate. 
My rooms have been fairly large large by NYC standards and clean, although some of the upholstered furniture (and sometimes the curtains) have been stained and in need of professional cleaning or replacement. The beds are comfortable, and the microwave and refrigerator in good working order. There is also coffee/tea available in the lobby in the morning. 
The staff is polite, especially the maintenance people. A small pet peeve of mine: a man at the front desk told me we were bing "upgraded" when I knew the rates were identical between the room I booked and the one they gave me. Guest services staff is helpful though.
All in all, this hotel is in my top 2 for stays in NYC.

title: “Sophisticated yet down to earth”
text: A wonderful hotel, very close to Union Square and all the main San Francisco attractions. This was our first time in San Fran - we were there for New Years Eve so we picked a room that allowed us some space to relax - a suite complete with designer furniture, decorated in pastel shades. Our room wasn't ready when we arrived, so we were offered a glass of wine in the lounge area while we waited. Mood lighting, a roaring fire and a HUGE rocking chair adorned the lobby area. Certainly not like any hotel I've stayed in before. Given the location and the bars and restaurants within the hotel, if you're not comfortable around 'beautiful people' then this isn't the place for you. The staff were great - very friendly and accommodating and the doormen were excellent - the front doors are super heavy and they were always there to open them for you! Overall a lovely hotel - and well worth the money for the experience!

title: “Good Hotel”
text:
We stayed for 4 nights at the Mayflower in an upgraded suite well worth the extra few pounds following a bit of haggling at the check in.
The suite was excellent, loads of room, nice lighting and a most excellent bed plus 2 wide screen TVs.Yes the mini bar is expensive but isnt every mini bar.
The staff were helpful and polite and we did enjoy breakfast but do try for a breakfast included deal as its not cheap.
The restaurant was okay very average food but again good polite service.The bar closed on our first night and was moved to a lovely area upstairs with once again great service.
There are plenty of restaurants within easy walking distance the streets seem fairly safe so dont be afraid to venture out although it is a good idea to book in advance.It is an attractive hotel historic and very ornate we were told it was Bill Clintons favourite Washington hotel !!
My only complaint would be room service which was rather slow.We ordered tea on each morning and they never managed to get it right,one tea bag for two no milk etc but to be fair I mentioned it on checking out and the room service was removed from our bill. 
The hotel is in a very central area which makes most of the tourist sites within easy walking distance however when required we found the cabs to be fairly reasonable.
We do not generally like large hotels but we found the Mayflower very acceptable

title: “Great rooms-close the everything!”
text: Rooms were clean and spacious. The employees are nice, helpful and efficient. The breakfast was ok, for free. It's a converted bank so the rooms are not what you normally get with a suite, there is no way to close off the living area from the sleeping area. The old vault in the basement is neat to see. The wifi connection was bad.

title: “Clean room but hotel missed the mark”
text: I have to preface this with saying I come to New York twice a month for work. I usually stay in non-chain hotels like the Marcel and all in and around the area of this hotel. I would not choose to stay at thie hotel again. A lot of people complained about the size of the rooms and they are small but that didn't bother me because I am used to small NYC hotels and I am by myself and only use the room to sleep. That being said, I could not sleep at all at this hotel. I expect to hear street noise in NYC bit I also expect a hotel that charges $300+ a night to have double panerd windows that block out the noise. It was so loud that I woke up no less than 10 times the two nights I was there. This is a BIG issue. Also, the second night I came back to my room it was frigid. The AC was on full blast but it was fall time, not summer. I called to ask how to turn the heat on and was told it was regulated by the building and therefore th best they could do was bring me a space heater. I man, what $300 hotel needs to bring in a space heater? The noise was by far the number one issue but the room is also a little odd as it doesn't have a spare electrical outlet for your laptop and phone. You have to unplug something. The room is modern and very clean and the staff is ice but I would not stay here again. There is no fitness center but there is a cool rooftop deck

title: “Fabulous hotel experience”
text: I just returned from a long weekend in New York with my mother, aunt and two sisters. Our stay at the Casablanca Hotel made the entire trip worthwhile. Before the trip, I had a long conversation with the concierge who helped me select rooms and book a car service. Upon arrival, we were welcomed in, had our luggage immediately stored (as we were there early to get our vacation started) and directed to their 2nd floor lounge for water, coffee, tea and light snacks. The location is perfect - just off Times Square but not in the middle of the hustle and bustle. After a visit to Rockefeller Center, St. Patrick's and MoMA, we returned to the hotel for the 5:00 wine and cheese reception - again incredible. My family was so happy to have this place to rest and relax and the food and drink was very generous. Our rooms were beautiful and immaculate. We had 2 - a 2 bed room and a suite with 2 beds and a pull-out couch. Very generously sized with great amenities. The breakfast the next morning was delicious - especially the wonderful bagels. We were always greeted professionally by the staff and felt completely safe. And, if you are in to the movie "Casablanca," you will love the decor of this place. They pulled it off in numerous touches throughout the hotel in a very tasteful way. I have stayed in the chains in New York but from now on I will be staying at Casablanca Hotel.

title: “Disappointed”
text:
Upon arrival, the hotel seems compressed and small. Room was small, no bathtub, hardly any room for luggage. We were put into a terrible room with scaffolding outside our window on the second floor. We were moved to a higher floor. We had to order ice, it took almost an hour. Second time we ordered ice, it didnt come at all. Bed/pillows were average.
Poor service.

title: “Will definately stay here again”
text: We had a blast staying at the Redbury. The staff was helpful. The room was awesome and huge. Very clean. Very comfortable bed and the atmosphere was great. It also had a kitchen(but no pots and pans). We stayed on a Mon. and Tues, there was no noise at all. Excellent location too. I highly recommend staying here.

title: “Not A Fan of the Baltimore Grill”
text: My wife and I arrived at the lord Baltimore on August 22nd, 2003. We fortunately reserved the Plaza Suite Plan, where you get drinks and food for breakfast and pre-dinner with the "deal". Well, after the accomodations were fine; the Club Plaza was a great idea; I figured this place was special! So, we tried the Lord Baltimore Grill on August 22nd for dinner at 7 P.M. To make an upseting story short, The staff was so under-staffed and the management so incompetent that we and eventually another ten customers left the Grill without ever received our entrees! You probably wouldn't mind if I said that we were there for 30 minutes, but we were not served even after one hour! I filed a claim with the grill management; was promised two "Comps." ; and received a personal call from the Lord Baltimore Hotel. 6 weeks later (Today) Pat and I are still waiting for the complimentary dinners, not so much for the free-bies but simply for the satisfaction of knowing that Radisson Hotels really do care and don't claim a solution to their staff problems without really satisfying their guests! Are they a classy chain of hotels or a want-a-be chain. Tom and Patricia

title: “Great location and service.”
text: The hotel itself is very nice. The bathrooms are c and the plumbing seems to always be in working order. The Climate control systems did not have any issues during my stay, and I have not had any issues with these systems in past stays. The bed is comfortable, especially with the comfort adjuster for firmness of the mattress. Parking is a little steep for the area (valet) but the proximity of your vehicle to the hotel is worth it (the parking garage and hotel are the same building. The service people were extremely helpful. Had a file that needed to be printed for a presentation and the public printer was not working at that time. The service desk person helped me get my document printed, above and beyond what was called for in my situation. I do greatly appreciate them for this effort.

title: “Wonderful place to stay”
text: Would definitely recommend this hotel. Everything was clean and well taken care of. Breakast was plentiful. No probs with noise or parking and was in an excellent location to head on down to Old Town, which was awesome, as well. My single complaint was that the shower heads weren't high enough on the walls. They were fine for me, but my 6 ft boyfriend had a hard time ducking under them to get wet.

title: “Great hotel, but poor for business travelers”
text: Stayed here while on a business trip during the middle of February. While the hotel was excellent, for the price of the room, I expected services one commonly finds at an average hotel these days - namely, complimentary wireless internet and a reasonably priced business center. What I found was wireless internet for $14 a day and a business center that cost $7 for 10 minutes of usage. Certainly people that stay at the Ritz can afford these prices, however in my opinion these basic features should be included complimentary. I recommend this hotel for all but business travelers.

title: “A Great Stay, As Always”
text: This is a beautiful hotel in a very central location to several areas of Boston. The staff are friendly, the rooms well appointed and the adjacent eateries are excellent. I have stayed here several times while on business and always look forward to return visits. I highly recommended this hotel!

title: “FABULOUS”
text: After being picked up at the airport by the shuttle, we arrived 4 hours prior to check in. We did not think we would be able to check in to our room so early, but we gave it a shot. The front desk staff was more than accommodating and got us to our room right away. After about five minutes of getting settles the phone rang, and it was the front desk asking how our room was. We were blown away by how nice everyone was! The room was large, and spotless! I can not say enough good things about the caring, kind, and helpful staff, but I do know if we return to Denver, we will be staying here!

title: “Don't be put off by the lobby”
text:
We booked our 3 night stay on the strength of all the favourable reviews appearing on TA. Our first impression of the lobby was rather depressing. I suppose this was caused by the choice of decor (generally dark grey) and its miniature proportions (a very tall hotel built on a small footprint). But when we got up to our room it was as splendid as predicted.
I think there are 34 floors with 6 rooms per floor serviced by 5 fast guest lifts. We were in a corner suite on the 24th floor at a discounted cost of $625 for 3 nights (Sun, Mon & Tues).
We had fine views of the Chrysler building and the East River. With a big desk, dimming lights and a grand sofa, it felt like home. The bed and pillows were perfect. The bathroom was very well fitted and well maintained. One can sit on the throne and enjoy the view! (But we didn't get any of the free toothpaste promised on their booking confirmation.)
The kitchen had everything we wanted in order to prepare simple breakfasts. But with cooker, microwave, fridge and freezer one could comfortably cook quite elaborate meals. And for the less ambitious there are delis in both directions providing a wide selection of pre-prepared dishes.
On two evenings we ate in the Barking Dog restaurant next door to the hotel costing about $80 (2 persons) for starter, steak and a large glass of wine. The NY sirloin steaks were so large that we asked for the barking doggy box, and we found we had the basis for the third evening meal.
The Empire State Building is four blocks away along 34 Street, but cannot be seen from the hotel. Macy's is one block further.
The purpose of our visit was sightseeing, and our application to the Big Apple Greeter organisation was successful. We were met in the hotel reception and taken by subway to Lower Manhattan. We walked through Greenwich Village, Soho, Little Italy and Chinatown, past the World Trade Centre site, and ended up at the Staten Island Ferry Terminal. Our Greeter, Bill, was retired like ourselves and he loves these parts of Manhattan, having lived nearby since a boy. This walk took about 3 hours. We left him and took the free ferry to and from Staten Island passing Liberty Island on the way. In the afternoon we had an appointment at the Federal Reserve Bank to inspect all their gold! On the next day we walked to the Rockafeller Centre (about 20 mins) and went to the top of the Rock. We then went by subway to the top end of Central Park, and walked back through the park, via Times Square and back to the hotel (about 3 hours walk ignoring shopping stops). On the third morning we took the subway down to City Hall and walked over Brooklyn Bridge.
I mention all these activities simply to illustrate how conveniently situated the hotel is. The closest subway station is in 33 Street, one block away.
We travelled from and to JFK by Skytrain, E Train, and 6 Train, costing $7 single. It was quite an easy journey and took less than an hour. I am glad we didn't give in and take a cab!

title: “Good, but not my favorite...”
text:
I stayed at the St. Regis for three nights following a trip to Asia. I checked in fairly late (9 pm) so there was no problem getting a room. The hotel is quite modern but beautiful. My only other previous St. Regis experience had been at one in New York City; it is far more traditional in appearance and frankly, I found it much warmer with better service.
The room was beautiful, with a nice view and great bath. The layout in the bedroom, with the hidden closet arrangement is different but nice, with ample space and lighting. The fitness area, shared apparently with the residences, was well equipped and very clean. The concierge was helpful and gave me a great recommendation for an Italian restaurant in the neighborhood.
Overall a very nice hotel, but after the NYC St. Regis I was expecting just a bit more.

title: “Convenient stay”
text: We arrived to LAX almost at midnight. We quickly found our way to the hotel transportation area. About 10 min later we saw the Crowne Plaza and Renaissance shuttle. About 15 minutes later we were checking in with no problem. The room was clean and comfortable. Next morning we had a breakfast voucher and had the breakfast buffet. It was good, but wouldn't have taken it if we didn't had the vouchers, since I felt it was a bit overpriced. But there's a small cafe/deli in the lobby too, if you want something cheaper. I find this hotel perfect for a night stay before or after a flight.

title: “Short walk to Space Needle”
text:
My wife and I stayed one night here in January 2011. We were attending a winter party and wanted a decent, modern place to stay that was a short walk from the Space Needle. The Hyatt is a relatively new, small hotel towards the western edge of the downtown area. Overall we found our experience to be a good one. Because of its small size, the hotel is somewhat limited in its offerings. There is a small restaurant area in the modern, clean lobby. One can check in at a kiosk located near the front door. We found check in to be quick and efficient.
Our room was comfortable and located on one of the upper floors (the hotel is only a few stories high). The shape of the room was a bit odd, but there was a nice couch, lounging area situated apart from the bed/bedroom area. The bed and furnishings were modern, nice and new. The bathroom was nice. The windows are sound proofed and we had a restful sleep.
Seattle has a lot of downtown choices, but if I had business or an event in this western part of the downtown, I wouldn't hesitate to stay here again.

title: “A treasure in the heart of San Francisco”
text: While traveling to Napa and Sonoma Valley we stayed on either end of our trip here. What a great little boutique hotel at Union Square. From the minute we arrived, the front desk was nothing but cordial and helpful. The rooms were nicely decorated, clean, quiet, and comfortable. The evening wine and cheese was fun because we had such great conversation with other guests including a couple from New Zealand. The late evening cookies and tea were a nice touch before we went to bed after dinner on the town. The morning breakfast of pastries, croissants, yogurts and various breads to toast was filling. The coffee was outstanding and kept us going for the morning. We highly recommend this little gem to all who are traveling to San Francisco.

title: “Loved the Beacon”
text: Loved the location, the staff and the room! We will come back! Always stay on the Upper West when we visit NYC, and The Beacon is now our new favourite hotel :-)

title: “Good points and bad”
text: It was easy to find. The hotel seems to have old and new sections. I was in the old. I loved the pool with a deep end 8 1/2 feet deep. There is a large hot tub hidden in what I believe is a newer section. A security/maintenace guy arrived to turn the lights on at the tub one evening, noticed we had no towels and went and got us some. Hope he gets some credit for it via this review. Nice touch. Now for the room. It seemed old with a newer bed and tv in it. It was ok. The second of my 2 nights there, I went to have a shower before supper after returning from a day at Magic Mountain and there was no hot water. Not even luke warm. Freezing cold. Unacceptable for what they charge for the room, period.

title: “Worst Hotel Ever”
text: The hotel and its management are quite deceitful. When I phoned in our reservations I was told it was not pet friendly and could be made allergy friendly ; ie removing feather pillows etc. Not the case. The staff is rude and gievs a deer in headlights look to every question. Our room smeleld of mold and must, the door did nto properly close, the bathroom facuet leaked and flooded the floor and the towels were full of long , black hairs. Never mind the gym is a closet with no lights and to get to get you walk across an unsafe parking lot. We were so disgusted we refused to pay, demanded our car from valet, and checked out after 1 1/2 hours. Did I mention the large human fingernail on the lobby floor that didn't seem to faze staff? Horrible Horrible. Never stay here unless you want feel dirty all day and all over. I'm sure had I stayed I would have left with bedbugs or some kind of disease. HORRIBLE.

title: “Great location, pleasant staff, nice experience”
text: As the previous reviews say, I have to agree. Great location, wine and cheese in the evening was fantastic touch, nice start to evening. Breakfast was simple but good start to day. Room was quite small and no bath but I think that was to be expected in a Manhatten Hotel. really clean room and bed was so comfortable. If anyone is reading this review I have one bit of advice....Please go to Tony's restaurant next door, amazing food!

title: “wonderful”
text: i recently spent a week at this hotel and being a former hotel employee its nice to know a hotel has such professionals working for them. And liking a clean room i was glad i had Gisella who took great care in making sure my room was clean and stocked with everything that i needed. she was very professional and courtious and always had a smile on her face, which is good for a person traveling far from home. she is one of many who work in the hotel with the same feeling for their work and they all should be commended for all they did in assisting me in anything that i needed during my stay.

title: “Great Time at 70 PA”
text:
We have just got back from a long weekend at 70 PA and we had a fantastic time. The weather was not so great (resulting from Tropical Storm Kyle) so we were so glad that we had chosen a good 4* hotel that is geared up to making their guests' time as comfortable and as luxurious as possible.
I personally feel that the hotel is in a quieter part of NY (38th East) but still pretty central (2 or 3 blocks from Grand Central Station and the same for 5th Avenue) so we had the best of both worlds. 
TIP: If you are a light sleeper get a room as high up as you can to try and get away from as much as the street noise as possible. Also request a room away from the lift.)
The hotel itself doesn’t look as 'boutique' as you might expect from the outside - and the lobby is not as intimately opulent as one might expect if familiar with other boutique style hotels BUT the staff were all welcoming and helpful. The concierge (I didn’t get his name) was a star and got us a table at the Marriott Hotel The View Restaurant at the very last minute (This restaurant was great for city views but ask for a table by the window in advance and DO get the tasting menu – gorgeous and great value when you compare to London tasting menus!!). 
TIP: There is wine tasting in the lobby every night from 5 - 6pm (approx) which looked great fun and a real bonus after a hard day shopping.
The rooms are what makes the hotel in my book. It feels like walking into a cocoon after the chaos of the city - all warm lighting, soft fabrics and soothing green tones. It takes about 10 seconds to take in the peace and then you notice the… 42" plasma, the amazingly well stocked mini bar, the L'occitane toiletries and the exemplary 24 hour room service menu. Oh and did I mention the spa menu if you fancy some relief for those tired feet from all the walking? (because you will walk!) 
In summary, this hotel really does try to please everyone and doesn't fail. We loved it and would go back, if not there, then definitely to another Kimpton Hotel.

title: “Very Upscale”
text:
I have very mixed feelings on how much I actually liked my room, however the hotel overall was nice. Here is a list that may make it easier:
Pros
Beds & Pillows were amazing
Location was great
The view was great
The lobby was huge and nice
Extreamly upscale hallways & Elevators
Many restaurants in the bottom of the hotel
Cons
The bathroom was very old and a little dirty (the tile)
The windows open & have no screens (careful with kids)
Furnature had chips and dents
Roomservice has a fee of $3.50 + 15% Tip + $$$$ Food
Hallway noise is loud (request a room at the end of a hall)
No refrigerator in room
Closet door needs updating and barely closes
Entire room EXTREAMLY small
Parking is $40 a day with NO discount for hotel guests
What I really think with this one is you are paying for the location. The regular rooms are nothing special although you can't beat those beds, they were great. You will be very impressed by the lobby and hallways but don't be tricked. The interior of the rooms can't measure up looks wise and it is mainly because of the bathroom and how small the room is. Overall, I would say the feeling here is old world ritzy. The parking is horrible at $40 daily and I think they should give a discount to hotel guests.
Overall, I did enjoy my stay but if this hotel was very expensive in comparison to something that looked nice and was a little cheaper, I would say go with the cheaper hotel.

title: “Nice for Price”
text:
Stayed at the bedford hotel for 5 nights at the beginning of October. Rooms were of a resonable size with two 4ft beds, although me and my wife only used one, it had all the facilites you would expect and need with a handy self continaned kitchenette.
Location was handy 5mins from Grand central station and only a 15min walk to Times Square, very worth the money.

title: “Lousy hotel”
text: The Wellington hotel is very old and a run down property. The room we stayed in was very small and uncomfortable. The smoke detector was missing and wires were hanging down from the ceiling. The air conditioner wasn't working properly and would start smoking if you tried to use it. You see why the smoke detector was missing. The staff has no concept of the word service. They were unattentive, and in some cases down right rude. If you go to New York it is a great city full of things to do. However, don't ruin your trip by staying at this hotel.

title: “Good Hotel”
text: I had a nice stay. Service was very good. Rooms very clean and well appointed. Some signs of age here and there, but nothing shabby. Very nice outdoor area.

title: “Try another hotel”
text:
We arrived here on Sunday 18th July, exhausted because we were on our final city of our three week road trip. San Francisco was our favourite city but the Holiday Inn, Fisherman's Wharf was our worst hotel!. The address we were given was spelt incorrectly, not a lot of good when you are relying on a sat nav, but when we arrived we were surprised to find that though we had found the correct place to park the car our actual room was located about a block away and as there was no parking facilities in that part of the hotel we would have to walk carrying all our luggage as there were no luggage trolleys. 
This was bad enough but we were then told via our in-room welcome pack that the pool and laundry room were in the other part of the hotel where we had to initially register. We had passed people in swim gear carrying what looked like laundry bags but never dreamed that this was the only way to achieve this.
We also found out that the rooms have no closeable curtains, only voile, so we woke very early and due to no double glazing we could hear the kitchen staff emptying bins at 4am. Beatiful city.....................shame about the hotel

title: “Wonderful location”
text: The location makes this a great place to stay. It is close to the monuments and the Lincoln Center. For walkers and joggers, it is very close to the Potomac, C&O Canal and Rock Creek pathways. The hotel is older, but my room and the common areas were clean and neat. The continental breakfast was an added bonus.

title: “Big Clean room, fun bar, good food and a Starbucks, perfect for business traveler”
text:
I just returned from El Paso after a 3 day trip for meetings at Fort Bliss. I have used TripAdvisor for years to check out hotels that I am considering staying at. This is the first review I have written. I was surprised when I got home and read so many negative reviews. I was wondering if I was at the same hotel. Now I believe some of the grips are valid and that the hotel was in need of some renovations, many of those concerns have been address with the on going improvements. However, some of the other complaints might be coming from someone that just has a vendetta against the hotel based on the number of first time reviewers. "Beer Bottles being broken in the parking lot and music until 4am?" Really??
My room (224) had a nice view of the courtyard with trees and grass. It was quiet although there was some workers replacing carpets and I could hear the power equipment during the day. I also noticed that they were enclosing some of the hallways on the first floor which would make it quieter. I had the breakfast buffet ($8.95) which is cheap and was very good. 
One night I walked around the corner to a nearby restaurant/brewery. (Jaxon's I think) They have great micro beer and food. It was nice not having having to drive. After diner I enjoyed a few drinks at Teddy's bar in the hotel which is a popular local bar with music and dancing. It sure beats sitting in some lobby bar with 3 other guys watching Sports Center and while the bartender reads the newspaper. There is also a full Starbucks in the parking lot. 
On my last night, there was large local event going on in the lobby and pool areas. It was an 80's party. When I got back from dinner, people were already arriving for the party. Security was out directing traffic to nearby lots for the party goers. I mentioned I was a hotel guests and they allowed me in the main lot so I could park right next to the building as I had been doing all week. At no point did I see any "Hells Angels" or urine as one "reviewer" claims. I am not saying this hotel is perfect, there are some flaws but don't be misinformed by some of these wild stories. I am a member of Marriott and Hilton Honors as well as Priority Club. My review is my recent actual experience at the Holiday Inn Airport, El Paso. The only other thing I would add would be how nice the staff was. Every person I spoke to was smiling and very helpful. The free bottle water in the room is also a nice amenity.

title: “Wonderful!”
text: During my one week stay, the personnel was extremely friendly and supportive. The rooms are beautifully and tastefully decorated and the food is very, very good. Will come back often!

title: “Amazing Staff and Location”
text: We were going to a Si Fi Convention at the Hotel . The Con was only 6 miles from our house so we didn't need to but since it was our Anniversary I booked it as a treat for my Hubby ( and I ) , We had to get there early for a early morning TV Show that was doing some promos for the Concarolinas convention and the Hotel let us check in Early , I had previously been in e mail contact with John Noonan and he was great in answering all my questions . He even came out and spoke to us when we were in Costume the next day , The Hotel is beautiful but the Staff is AMAZING . Any thing we wanted or needed any questions we had they had the answer. Our first morning we met Iboc in the Executive Lounge and we chatted and had fun with her for a while (she is an ICE expert ) she even remembered me (on the Phone ) when we were checking out . From the housekeeping to Management they were all great ,John even sent Champagne and Chocolate covered Strawberries to our room for our Anniversary. What makes this even more special a few weeks prior my Husband and I had returned from an 8 day trip to Mexico at an All Inclusive 5 star Resort and we weren't treated as special as we were at the Hilton . It was a Great stay and the perfect location as our favorite Mexican Restaurant Zapata's is right across the Lake . The location of the Hotel is perfect for dining and shopping and the great Lake that has a path all around to walk and even paddle boats.The Hotel did a great job not just for us but i had a lot of friends staying there and they agreed that the Hilton Hotel was Top Notch . We are so glad we decided to stay there . Usually we wouldn't as it is so close to our house but we already bought our tickets for next years Convention so we will probably book again for our Anniversary and have a great weekend . Thank You John, Iboc and all the staff that made our Anniversary and weekend getaway a special one to remember .

title: “12 year old adults”
text: Beware when you book your rooms here. We had 2 rooms for 8 people 3 over age 18, 5 kids under 18 (ages 15, 14, 11, 10 and 1) and were charged an additional $17.25 per room after we left and told we misrepresented the number of adults we had. They consider 12 and over as adults. Hotel is fine other than the bait and switch.

title: “Feel like royalty”
text:
I had not stayed at this hotel since it was the Ritz Carlton. It was so nice to be back in a nice neighborhood with exceptional service. 
From the minute you get out of the car to the front desk to the consierge - they are all wiling to help you. I was traveling on business and needed reservations and recommendations. The consierge was excellent. He hit every restaurant on the head in price, quality, atmosphere including a great Italian within walking distance.
The rooms are spacious with all amenities including the robe and slippers. I did have a problem with housekeeping one night and not only got apologies from housekeeping but from the front desk when checking out. Things do happen but it is a good hotel that attends to their mistake quickly.
My package included high tea. As I was traveling on business I don't always have time for that but as I came in at the end, the hostess held everything for me. What an end to a day. 
The gym is small but I never had a problem despite the size of the hotel. The pool is beautiful. It is expensive but you get what you pay for.

title: “excellent location”
text: Hotel was in an excellent location just of Times Square. Room was small but had everything that was needed. Maid service every day. Some days chocolate and next day weather forecast left in room. Fridge in bedroom. Our room was at the back and had a view of the wall and rubbish that had been thrown on to roof, but at least in was quiet at night. I think if you were at the front of the hotel it would be quiet noisy. Only used the bar once as it was very expensive $22 for one Gin and Tonic and a bottle of beer. Plenty of pubs nearby if you want a cheaper priced drink. Turn left when you leave hotel and the local cafe the Evergreen does an excellent breakfast. We got a good deal as we booked early but may be quite expensive. Staff all very helpful. You can even borrow umbrellas when it rains, but make sure you return it as it would cost you $25 if you dont. Would definitely stay here again if I was to return to New York.

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
The hotel was very nice. We arrived very early and had no problem checking in. The bags did take a while to be brought to the room, but overall not a problem. The bed was very comfortable and the room was very quiet. The water pressure in the shower could have been better. The staff was very pleasant.
The hotel is very close to a Metro stop and the White House. The walk to the Mall was very easy.
The only issue that we had was the large number of homeless people in the surrounding areas, especially north of the hotel. We were begged for money every time we left the hotel but were not bothered much.
Also, during the evening and on weekends, many of the local restaurants are not open. We were looking for lighter and less expensive meal options than the hotel offered and there was not much choice near the hotel on Saturday and almost none on Sunday.

title: “Fantastic Services...It's the only place to stay when visiting Charlotte. Can't wait to get back, again!!!”
text: A warm and welcoming atmosphere from the time you enter the hotel. Service with a smile. Staff goes out their way to make you feel special. Spacious room, quiet setting, everything strategically spaced to accomodate a family vacation or business trip. Food prepared to you exact liking. Can't wait to get back to Charlotte. I'll only stay at the Hilton Charlotte University. Many thanks to Monique Stubbs-Hall and the staff!!!!!!!

title: “Such a relaxing and nice hotel.”
text: The staff were friendly, the rooms were very nice and clean and we slept great! We will be visiting again!

title: “Another great stay ...”
text:
This was our second stay this year at the Century Plaza. We stayed for the Academy Awards, and then now for Memorial Day weekend.
The hotel is gorgeous and a real gem. The staff were friendly and helpful.
We booked on Priceline with a rate of $105 per night. Parking costs an additional $35 and the valet was always efficient. We always called down to have the car brought up and it was always waiting for us by the time we got downstairs.
If you are a Hyatt card holder, you also get free coffee at Starbucks!
The room was comfortable, and in the Summer its great to be able to open the balcony door for fresh air, a breeze and to sit outside.
There is free internet access in the lobby/bar area. I found also that as we were on a lower floor than before, I also had free internet access from the CAA building across the street in our room!
Another great stay, and we will certainly return.

title: “Great location, clean and impressive hotel”
text: Excellent location. Staff were friendly and helpful. Room was clean and modern if not slightly dark, but this was due to the direction of our room. Recommended highly for those wanting to shop- just off 5th.

title: “Great location, clean rooms and exceptional staff”
text:
We stayed here back in Sept. 2011 during the power outage. We stayed for 7 nights and couldn't have been happier. Despite being without power for about 12 hours, the experience was great. The staff went out of their way to make sure everyone was as comfortable as possible. People were given light sticks in an attempt to provide some light. They staff even opened the keg to allow people to make the best of the situation.
We found the room, the location and the staff to be top notch. The rooms were a bit dated but they were exceptionally clean. The pool is on the small side but certainly clean and well kept.
The breakfast was good and plentiful as were the evening receptions during the week. The light meals during the week included an entree, lasagna one night, soup and salad another night and hamburger and hot dogs another night as well as rolls, beer and wine. The staff does a great job handling the crowds and replenishing the food.
If you are looking for a nice, friendly place to stay, this hotel is worth a stay. We will definitely stay here again. We were very happy with everything!

title: “Stay somewhere else.”
text:
Where to begin?? This hotel had horrible service. The manager "Nicole" was non-existent during our 5 day stay. We were shuffled around rooms, and called liars when we pointed out the things that weren't working. The windows are taped shut with duct tape. The walls had mould and blood, it was horribly creepy. We stayed in winter and the radiator in the room was very noisy, clicking and hissing. Bring earplugs. The hallways were so small my bag kept hitting the walls as I walked. 
The only good point is that it's not TOO expensive if you shop around for a deal. also, it's near a subway station which is on the express route so getting downtown is quick and easy.
I would not recommend this hotel and I would not go back. All we wanted was a place to sleep and shower while traveling on a budget, but this 2 star hotel couldn't even give us the bare minimum. Do yourself a favor and stay somewhere else!!

title: “Comfy room in good location”
text:
We arrived by train and after a short walk we were quickly checked in to our room. The staff were really helpful and offered some great advice on what to see and how to get around.
The room was comfortable and a good size but our view was just the windows of other rooms. This meant we had to keep the blinds down for privacy.
The afternoon wine tasting was a great way to meet other travelers and pick up tips for the rest of our holiday.
The restaurant served good breakfasts and dinners.
The interesting bath robes are a nice touch and made for some great photos.

title: “Staff deserves lots of credit”
text:
Thought the construction would be finished and it would be decorated for Christmas. Wrong.
Yellow tape, check in underground , and even the reflecting pools were bone dry. But every staff member went above and beyond in service and politeness to overcome the construction set-up. 
There are top of the line restaurants outside the hotel within walking distance. But if you stay inside the hotel you will be taken care just fine. We lucked out with a suite in the green tower, renovated, 26th floor with a living room and 1.5 bathrooms . View of the Hollywood sign and the mountains. 30 plus feet of floor to ceiling windows and the bedding was marvelous. Yes , you pay for parking and internet service but this a major city where all the downtown better hotels nail you for that. Easy access to freeways, zoom off to Santa Monica, Pasadena or drive down the street to Wilshire Blvd. and go to Beverly Hills. We came from North Carolina for the Rose Bowl and stayed until Jan 4th.
The Westin served us well.

title: “Repulsive road trip”
text: Last minute we wanted to hop in the car and do a New Years Eve get away at a water park. We usually drive only an hour to Kalahari, which is fabulous! This time, we wanted to do something different. The staff was CRABBY as soon as we walked in. We did not feel welcomed. Then we had to stand in line just to wait for an elevator just to get to our GROSS room. My kids had fun at the water park, that was smaller than any indoor water park we have been too. The other new year activities were for younger children. We had dinner at the bar because the free buffet included in our package did not start until 9:30, when we went to check it out there was a line out the door just to get the DISGUSTING food. Then the highlight was the guests across from our room yelling screaming, banging into our door ALL NIGHT I am NOT exagerating. I called the front desk 4 times. Had a message into a manager from day one, and I finally reached her 4 days after we got home, she basically said Oh well it was New Years!! My advice DON"T go, this place is GROSS!!!!!

title: “Deceiving advertising”
text: I reserved and paid for a king 2 bedroom suite. I called ahead of time and asked about the shuttle and was advised we could take the shuttle back and forth throughout the day to Sea World, the Zoo and to Old Town. When we arrived I checked in and went to the "suite". It had 2 queens and a sofa bed. One room was separated by 2 very large doors--which I suppose made it 2 rooms. I went to desk and they advised they had no king suites. The "view" from the sliding glass doors and balcony would have been beautiful but it overlooked the I-5 freeway! Very noisy day and night. Oh, and the shuttle...it only went to the zoo at 9:30am and picked us up at 4:30p--the zoo was open until 9pm. Same thing with Sea World--when we arrived we wanted to go about 12:30p and they advised they only went once in the morning. Big disappointment. I selected this hotel for the shuttle, the view and the king bed and didnot get any of that. The management was very sarcastic in saying, "I apologize". Actually, they could have cared less. They did re-imburse the $15.00 parking fee at Sea World when we pressed it after deciding to take a rental car there. I would strongly suggest staying somewhere else. OH, by the way, I am a platnium member with this chain.

title: “Awesome, excellent staff, old but clean hotel and very comfortable - yummy breakfast pastries!”
text:
We got upgraded (i think), but the our room is old style but beautifully restored to like new. It is basic but spacious, the most spacious so far. 
Unlike every other hotel i have stayed in my two month trip on both USA coasts breakfast is served until 11am (most were 9.30) and was fantastic for a continental breakfast. 
The laundromat has four washing machines and four dryers so you can wash at any time up until 9pm for 1.25USD per load. Most only had 1 machine and dryer. 
Our room is huge and fully self contained with a real fridge, stove etc 
The complimentary bikes are popular, i saw 10 this morning and now there are 2 left!
Thanks to others that previously reviewed this hotel, the staff and amenities are second to none for value for money.

title: “Great Place to Stay”
text:
Comfort Suites, was a great place to stay , Its on my favorites list..
I travel to Chicago Often this hotel was clean, great service and a great location.. everthing Chicago has to offer is right here at your finger tips, from Dinning , Shopping, Sports and Business..
This Hotel offers it all..

title: “LOVED IT”
text: Hot Spot, I will be there for Taste of Chicago 2010

title: “wonderful stay”
text: We come to Denver a couple times a year to visit our son and this hotel was the best place we've stayed. Clean rooms, comfortable beds and very friendly and courteous staff! We have chosen this hotel to be our "come to" place when we are in Denver!

title: “Just ok - not typical Westin”
text:
The hotel was fine, but nothing impressive and definitely the most outdated Westin I have seen. The location was perfect for several of the touristy spots in the area and the price was reasonable. The best experience we had at the hotel was a nice breakfast with excellent service.
The dark and cramped room left much to be desired. I expect better at a Westin. The night we checked in I went to get ice, and found that someone had left a catering box with a tuna sandwich rotting in the ice room on our floor. Two days later when we checked out that trash had still not been cleaned up even though the smell could be detected throughout the entire hallway. Disgusting!!

title: “Belvedere..service "just ok", location "10+"”
text: Arrived early, 10am, asked for early check-in, total indifference by staff, finally checked in almost by 4pm, a number of disgruntled people in the lobby waiting for rooms, overheard lots of complaining. When I left, I was allowed late checkout at 1pm (usually noon). I was less upset about their inability to check us in early as I was how unfriendly the staff were. And I found this consistent over the 5 days I was there. I've been to NYC numerous times, usually stay at Hotel Penn which was cheap, cheap, cheap, dirty, dirty, dirty, but very friendly and great service for such a huge hotel. I had a mouse in my room last visit so I decided to change hotels and try something new. Belvedere is very convenient to Broadway. I was able to walk to every play (and I saw 6) and never had to take a cab except when I went to the village. The breakfast was good. Three young women working the breakfast buffet stood talking to each other, unfriendly like we were intruding (10:45am and the buffet closed at 11:00am but still, there were only 2 other customers and we weren't able to check in....). The rooms were clean, nothing special, one chair in my room, no desk. It was very humid and hot while I was there, even in October. The window a/c worked very well. Toilet very small, hot water not consistent. My rates were not great. I would stay there again but none in my party of 4 had anything glowing to say about it except how conventient to the theaters. Oh, and cabs were very easy to grab here, more so that other hotels I've stayed at. TIP! for Broadway lovers, check out "Jim Caruso's Cast Party" at Birdland Monday Nights, I've been twice and it's the best. It's on 44th, just 4 blocks away.

title: “Sleepless in Manhattan”
text:
The room's size, furniture and amenities were all great. Lots of space, a small kitchenette, convenient location to NYC attractions. Tiny bathroom but everything worked.
Still, the main reason for a hotel room in NYC is to have a comfortable place to sleep, a home base that is a respite from the hustle-bustle of the city. We stayed for several nights, and there was never a quiet night where our sleep wasn't continually interrupted by commotion on 31st Street. 
We were in an inside corner of the hotel on the 10th floor, an inner corner furthest from the corner of 7th Ave and 31st Street, so we weren't directly over the street. We were told it would be a 'quiet room.' A commercial building across the street is being renovated, but there were never workers there during the day; they arrived at 11 pm and constantly dragged debris from the building to the street where it was broken up, scraped along the pavement and compacted by garbage trucks til 4 in the morning. Crash boom bang crackle, plus yelling all night. We were told nothing could be done to stop the ruckus, until finally one night the front desk sent out a security detail to ask for some relief. The next night, however, the noise was back. 
There is also a firehouse next to the hotel on 31st street, and there are sirens and truck horns many times a night as the fire trucks leave the station. 31st Street east of 7th Ave, across from the side of the hotel, is also a haven for the homeless to move in after nightfall with their shopping carts, trash bags and blankets to bed down on the sidewalk. Trash that was put out by the neighborhood buildings for early morning pickup was being rifled by the homeless and dropped noisily on the pavement, possibly to hear if there were any bottles or cans that might be retrieved for their deposits. 
A minor irritation within the room is that the TV's sound didn't work, and the maintenance person insisted that it was the cable TV company's fault and he couldn't fix it for the many nights we were there. He said that all the TV's in the hotel had poor sound. We eventually set the remote to see closed captioning to watch the news and weather with text under the picture. 
The day staff is cheerful and really wants to help if they can, but the night staff appears to offer excuses but no action on any concerns we raised. 
In summary, a pretty room that you can't sleep in or even watch TV to find out the weather is no bargain. The hotel can't get rid of the noisy louts who work construction all night across the street, nor can they relocate the homeless on the sidewalk, or silence the very loud sirens. Unless you need no sleep, and don't mind these irritations, look elsewhere.

title: “Absolutely LOVELY!”
text: I'm not sure where to begin with this review, because I have so many nice things to say. I stayed at this hotel for business travel, and I was a little apprehensive initially because I had never heard of the Seaport Hotel. But my office in Cambridge moved to Boston...right next door to the Seaport, so it made sense to stay here. I was pleasantly surprised at how lovely this hotel was. It is located right near the water (in clear view), and you can also see the airplanes landing and taking off from Boston Logan. The room provided a nice plush robe that kept me very warm. The room service was so fast, I couldn't believe it. Let me also say that the food I had with room service as very good, and I used room service for both dinner and breakfast. I can't wait for my job to send me back to the Boston office so I can stay at the Seaport again!

title: “great inn within walking distance to everything”
text: Stayed at the White swan Inn 2 nights the first week of August. The Inn is very cozy. The parking is right out front for valet and we got the parking package so it was at a discounted rate. They do ask for a 30 minute window to bring the car around. So no problems just plan ahead. The inn could use a bell hop but we only had one bag so its wasn't a huge deal to us. We had a 5th floor room. No view but still a great room. The decor was very floral and there is no AC but it really isn't needed. A ceiling fan would be a nice touch. The room even came complete with its own teddy bear available for purchase as a momento. The mornign breakfast was very good-usually a quice as well as cereal and toast. The evening wine reception is a nice touch complete with cheese and crackers. The study area where breakfast and the wine reception are is very dark but it is very quiet and has nice decor. I would recommend this inn to all.

title: “Awesome experience! Great staff! Exceptional value!!!!”
text:
Everything was wonderful, from check in to check out! Staff was very courteous, and very knowledgeable of the attractions in the area and even the new light rail system! The pool was brilliantly lit, even had tiny lights at the bottom!!! The suite we stayed in was spacious and had a HUGE TV in the bedroom.
When I'm back in Phoenix I will come again for sure! I can't wait!!!!
The attached "Mexico City" style Mexican restaurant was without a doubt the best food I had during my stay! Absolute first-class meal at unbelievably reasonable prices!

title: “Kudos to the four seasons staff chicago”
text: Kudos to the staff at the Four Seasons Chicago they made our stay exceptional!! We stayed Dec 16th and 17th. From the moment of entry the staff were welcoming and one step ahead of our every need. Our suite was great tx to megan at checkin. Our dining experience was outstanding tx to our server Russell and the dining room host megan. The followup and attentiveness by mgrs Nick and Steve only added to our recognition of a world class operation.

title: “did the job perfectly”
text: Just back from NY, having stayed here for 4 nights. It was everything we expected, nothing more and nothing less. 10 minute walk to time square, 3 minute walk to central park. Rooms were small, but nice. Had own bathroom, which was nice sized and clean. Had a window, but no view. For anyone going on a budget, would definitely recommend it. No complaints from me.

title: “Convenient location and good value”
text: My wife and I brought our kids for their first NYC trip a few weeks ago, and chose the Salisbury for the location and value. We booked a suite (two rooms), and had plenty of space (including more closet space than anyone could ever dream of using). It was convenient to the subway, so just about all of Manhattan was within our reach. It was also 2 blocks south of Central Park ,and the kids loved that. My only complaint has to do with the slow elevators...in the morning when they were having their breakfast buffet on the third floor, it wasn't unusual to wait for several minutes for one of the two elevators. Although not soundproof, the rooms were very quiet. I'd stay here again and also recommend it to my friends.

title: “Not bad at all!”
text:
At first I was concern about the place since it had some really bad but some good reviews. I made my reservation thru a travel agency that booked on line for me. Since I wasn`t so sure about the hotel I made a call before to confirm my reservation and ask for a non-smoking room. The frond desk people were nice but the reservation sounded very angry and said to me to keep calling cause at that moment she couldn`t do anything about it (p.s. I was calling from Brasil).
But well... I arrived at the place and what a surprise, it wasn`t bad at all! The people at the front desk were very nice and outgoing, I asked for a non-smoking room and they didn`t mind at all. Of course with this price you cannot expect much, but we got a really comfortable bed and clean private bathroom. Enough for our purpose, that was enjoy NY and not waste time in a hotel room. 
Nearby there is a great Greek restaurant, the one that has a pizzaria together! also it has a Subway, Donkin Donuds, a mini-market and a Delicatessen that we used to have breakfast there. The Subway station is only 2 stops to Times Square, center of downtown Manhattan.
I was very well treated by everyone in front desk and some other people that stays in front of the hotel(I`m not sure if they were from security, or doorman, or maintenance... but they were really nice!
P.S. The wi-fi internet is kind of slow, but even that, I guess, I was luck, cause I was able to connect most of the time that I needed to. 
P.S. When in the elevator press 1 for front desk and main door, cause if you press B you will be on the basement and it is very scare and messy there!

title: “Has Potential but not there yet - dissapointed - DON'T TAKE THE PAID UPGRADE”
text:
We were excited to stay at the Nolitan because of all the great reviews. When we arrived we were dissapointed to find that the rooftop and restaurant are essentially non-existent..on top of that when we got to our city view balcony room it was TINY. I understand NYC hotels are small, especially in the boutique group, but this was really small. For the price tag the hotel just did not deliver. Even the rooms looked sort of tired for a newer hotel. 
The biggest warning and turn off was that they tried to get us to pay for an upgrade at check in. I actually almost took them up on the offer as it was only $35/night and we could get a king room. On second thought however I decided to stick with our original booking. I am glad I did - when I looked online to see what the difference in the upgrade offer room was and our booked room it was actually CHEAPER!!! They tried to get us to pay for a downgrade! I feel so uncomfortable about this. I also heard them trying to upgrade the people who came in after us. 
On checkout I asked the gentelman who checked us in about his offer and asked him why he was trying to get us to pay more for a downgraded room - he said he was offering a better room on a higher floor but we were already staying in a city view. When i told him that he said he was offering a corner room - it would have made sense but I specifically asked when trying to decide if we should take the offer if it was a corner room he was offering - he said No - just a king room and the only difference would be the size of the bed.
Maybe it was a mis-understanding but it just isn't settling well with me. BEWARE of this tactic - it's a trick.
I will say the people were friendly and service was good too - unfortunately not enough to make up for the other short comings.

title: “Amazing spacious suite in great location!”
text: Location of this hotel was excellent, couldn't believe the location. Given that in NY hotel rooms are usually quite cramped, this one was huge with a kitchenette at the entry, large seating area, balcony, good sized bedroom and tons of closets. The bathroom, however, was quite tiny. I was definitely impressed and after seeing the rooms that my friends had in other hotels, was extremely pleased with the Kimberly and would recommend this to travelers to NY.

title: “Quality Hotel at a Reasonable Price”
text:
Downtown LA needs more hotels like this--good hotels at a good price. Though it's a few blocks outside the Downtown core, it is in one of the livelier areas of Downtown LA. The Miyako caters to Japanese travelers and tour groups, but works fine for Americans. It's an even better location now that the Gold Line light rail to Union Station, Pasadena, and East LA stops one block from the hotel (the Red Line subway is about a 10 minute walk away). 
They need to do some cosmetic repairs, like repainting the buttons in their elevator.

title: “Awful”
text:
I stayed at the Inn at Longwood in for one night this June for a conference. The front desk staff were unhelpful, unfriendly and very slow (Terrance I believe was his name - but the woman who checked me out was equally unfriendly and surly. 
When I got to my room, the desk chair had the seat cushion detached with the screws taken out of it and was sitting on top on the desk. The bathroom had a used soap bar in it. The rooms are also noisy, but that's to be expected given the location. The bed was very firm, so if you like a rock hard bet, you'll be happy.
I would NOT recommend this hotel.

title: “If you would like to stay in a stinky closet with no air, Mosser is the right choice for you”
text: I would recommend this hotel to my friend only if I wished slow and excrutiating death on them. I'm not a spoiled person, I come from Russia, I've stayed in multiple hotels and hostels, and believe me the size of the rooms cannot be described as "European". My husband, myself and our little son have just got back from our Nevada-Arizona-California road trip, and Mosser has totally spoiled our SF experience. Imagine a closet, no air (even though the hallways are air-conditioned), and horrible stink. I'm a bit claustrophobic and I had to get drunk to fall asleep. We woke up at 5:45 in the morning (it was my husband's birthday and he joked that it is very nice to wake up in a closet in San Francisco :) and ran. I always read Tripadvisor reviews, and I find them very helpful. But I believe that a lot of positive reviews about The Mosser definitely don't reflect the real picture. The service was actually quite good. Our bellman was extremely nice and helpful. Beware of The Mosser!

title: “Non smoking room was smoking and close to nothing”
text: We booked through expedia and therefore did not receive a non smoking room since expedia requests are only honored after everyone else who booked through Doubletree is accomodated. The manager was a jerk and refused to accomodate us until we demanded to smell every room to choose one that would be less offensive. then he came up with a non smoking room. In addition, there is nothing even remotely close to the hotel such as a sandwich shop or conveneince store so you are forced to order from hotel

title: “Nice Place”
text:
The staff goes out of its way to make your stay pleasant. Rooms are always clean and fresh.
I enjoy staying at this hotel. Dana and the people make one feel welcome. I stay at this hotel up to 8 times a month and I am never disappointed in the hotel.

title: “I will recommend whole heartedly !”
text: People are so nice and helpful.. Really appreciated Mark, the concierge. Room was quiet as requested and Ioved the extra touches- the free daily paper ,morning coffee, wine+ hour and the location is unbeatable- right across from the Metro and 3 short blocks from Michigan Ave. close to all the shopping. Price was not cheap , but still fairly priced especially because they 'do it well'.

title: “Great vacation!”
text: We just returned from a fabulous vacation\cruise from San Diego. We spent a few days in San Diego before we left on our Mexican cruise. We had no idea what hotel to book, and because of the great reviews Embassy Suites had on tripadvisor.com, we decided to stay there. We couldn't of asked for a better hotel. They picked us up from the airport the minute we arrived, helped us with all of our luggage, and checked us in to a suite with a breath-taking view of the bay. The rooms were very spacious and clean, and very quiet. The best feature of the suite was that there were two vaniety mirrors, one in the bathroom, and one on the outside of the bathroom. This is important when you have four people trying to get ready every morning. The hotel was in walking distance of Sea Port Village, Horton Plaza, and the Gas Lamp District, all great places to visit with many restaurants and shopping to choose from. The hotel provided a cooked to order\express buffet breakfast every morning, which was included in the overnight stay. It was very convenient to wake up, get ready, have breakfast right there, and be on our way. The best suprise we had was the fireworks over the bay that we had a full view of from our suite at night, apparantly they are on display a couple times during the week. Checkout was very easy, and they even stored our luggage until it was time for them to transfer us over to the cruise terminal, again at no charge. We had a pleasant experience with Embassy Suites and would not even hesitate to stay there again. We highly reccomend a stay with them on any of your future vacations to San Diego.

title: “The Staff- Six Stars, hotel...3”
text:
It was.fun for a night. Service was outstanding, over the top great. We were celebrating our anniversary, and they had chocolates, champagne, and a signed card from all the hotel staff.
My wife forgot her contacts solution, they brought her a complimentary bottle.
Hotel is fun, but rooms are small, and bathroom sink area is small (my wife likes a large sink area). 
My only complaint would.be it kind.of.has the stereo typical San Francisco Gay vibe they always show in.movies. I don't know quite how to describe it. There is no coffee in the room but Starbucks is across the street, and a cafe next door. 
Over all great stay for a night, very close to Union Square (2 1/2 blocks) and right next to China town and the financial district. But I don't think I.d stay here again if I'd chosen mu hotel by name instead of through hotwire.
Also, it was nice that they had a wine happy hour, where they served wine and other beverages, and had a Taro Card reader-(that's the kind of stuff I didn't like) 
It just kind of had a weird vibe to the place. But again, staff was outrageously nice, they held all our bags for us the whole day after we checked out so we could shop in Union Square. If I got this hotel again as a surprise through hotwire or Priceline I'd still go, but wouldn't choose it by choice.
Also, we were upgraded because of our special occasion, so again, Bravo to the staff. Its just a little too "Fabulous" for me. :)

title: “Fantastic hotel!”
text: What can I say? This hotel exceeded all expectations of mine in comparison to other hotels that I've stayed in the states. The room was clean even though small, it's not the size that matters but the quality of the room. Our floor was relatively quiet but you could definitely sometimes hear the stairway door shutting, but that wasn't too much of a big deal for me. The staff are tremendously warm and friendly given they are more than welcome to have assisted us with any queries we had and whenever we left and returned to the hotel, they always greeted us with a smile. The Collage bistro provided great breakfasts for us, I especially enjoyed the french toast and at night, the bartender was easy going to even have a chat to after a long day walking the city. The location is great given that we could walk to time square in 5 mins and there was a subway station just 2 minutes away from the hotel making it relatively easy to travel all around Manhattan. If I was to return to New York for another holiday, I would definitely stay at Distrikt again, it was a great experience!

title: “Partly Disappointed”
text: The grounds of the hotel are spectacular. When you first arrive, you honestly feel as though you're arriving at an upscale, 4 star resort. However, the workers at the front desk quickly dispel those thoughts. They are rude and very unhelpful They behaved as though they were doing me a favor to let me spend my $125 per night there. Then, they informed me that the room I booked was not available, and that it was a "first come, first served" basis on the rooms. Believe me, that was not stated up front. Anyhow, the room I checked in to was dated with 1970's Queen Anne style furnishings, complete with a little 25" square TV. The carpet is royal blue, and there were enough stains on it to make me believe it had once served as an oil change shop. I will say, though, that the rooms were clean. I promptly asked to be moved to a balcony room, which became available the second day of our stay (2 of 5 nights). My teenage son loved the heated pool, and the meeting rooms were very nice. So, overall...the grounds and the meeting space was great. The rooms are terribly outdated, and the customer service sucked. The location of the hotel is very good, and very convenient to the mall, restaurants, and the Trolley.

title: “Clerk abandons front desk”
text: We chose this hotel due to its proximity to the airport. We received a room closest to the lobby and across from the ice machine. When we opened the door, we were surprised to find another travelers belongings in the room. They quickly showed up and indicated that they were in the process of moving since the air conditioning was broken. It had been 105 degrees in Denver that day, so we returned to the front desk to request another room ourselves. That's when the drama began. The clerk indicated that the hotel was completely booked and there were no more rooms. Just then, another patron showed up demanding that the clerk get creative about finding him the promised 5-person bed space he had reserved. The patron insisted that the clerk solve the problem and encouraged him to contact the manager. Apparently, the manager also could not think of a solution to satisfy the client, who grew more insistent. The beleaguered clerk could not think out of the box and all the while, a build up of customers trying to check in huddled in the very warm lobby. Finally, the customer asked whether the clerk could give him 6 blankets such to create a mattress. The clerk left the front desk presumably to fetch the requested items. He walked to the back door and wasn't seen again. The phones were ringing off the hook, and with the clerk was no where in sight, the impatient crowd ventured into the back office in an attempt to find blankets for the one patron, and contact phone numbers for the owners and manager. It was nearly an hour before the manager showed up. To the manager's credit, he gave us the room complimentary due to the A/C problem. It was a warm, sleepless night. But at least it was free.

title: “Great beds, beautiful grounds”
text: Stayed here a few days ago and have stayed several times in the past. Have never had a problem whatsoever. The beds are some of the most comfortable I've ever slept in. Just wished they had queens instead of doubles. Nicely decorated rooms. Indoor and outdoor pools are not large, but well maintained. Large grounds with some lovely walks. Staff is very friendly and efficient. Location is a ways from downtown, but very convenient to the Arboretum shops and restaurants. Self parking is easy and there is valet, too. The restaurant is excellent, but the snack bar in the atrium is very expensive. Great place to stay!

title: “My great, quiet, well-located, go-to hotel in Manhattan”
text: Great upper west side hotel. Nicely done, quiet, with great staff and location. For the price, one can't do better in NY, so this is my go-to hotel there. Easy walk to Natural History Museum, Joe, the Art of Coffee, Jacques Torres, Peacefood, Land, Cafe Lalo, Central Park, and dozens of other great places, not to mention the subway to the rest of the city. One could easily spend days just in the area around the hotel!

title: “Doubletree Metropolitan in NYC is awful.”
text:
Having a pretty rough experience at the Doubletree in NYC. It was the only open hotel around my office so I decided to give it a shot and I wish I decided on a place farther away. I showed up and the front desk was fine but upon entering my room found that the fire alarm cover was sitting on the bed, the bathtub contained some form of matter and there was CANDLE WAX covering the insides of my room drinking glasses.
I called down to the front desk requesting a room change but they said they were overbooked as it was, so I just asked for some new glasses. The gentleman showed up 10 or 15 minutes later with a blanket in hand and I had to explain to him I just wanted some new drinking glasses and not a blanket. The gentleman brings back clean glasses and I head to bed around 10:30 PM, after receiving a call from the front desk regarding my glasses, due to a 7AM meeting on Park Ave.
The last straw happened when at 11:30, I wake up to a shrill ring and it's my bedside phone. I pick it up not knowing what to expect and it's someone from the "CareLine" asking if I received my remote control. I'm never rude to hotel staff but was about to lose it at this point. I say it's the wrong room, I never ordered a remote control and the woman says, "Ok...Well do you need anything else?" I just need a clean place to sleep for under $500 a night and this will never again be the place.
The only redeeming quality here is the bedding and the location.

title: “Couldn't have been better!!”
text:
Great price,
Great free parking,
Very accomodating staff - They allowed us check in early and jumped through hoops to see if a room was available to us!,
Great room - We had a jacuzzi room and it was super!,
Fantastic breakfast. - The breakfast area is the nicest "continental" breakfast area we have ever seen. It has many nooks and crannies- a library-like setting in one part, large solarium type in another, and even an outside area. The food selection was great, complete with eggs and sausage!

title: “Great value”
text:
I stayed at the Baldwin for two nights while I attended a seminar at the Grand Hyatt a block away. The hotel is right at the gate to Chinatown on Grant Avenue. My flight happened to get in very early and after a BART trip to the Montgomery station and the short walk to the hotel, I asked if it was possible to check in and was graciously accommodated.
I had a single room on the second floor just above the lobby. Although I had requested "the quietest room possible," the room was right on the street. It was noisy but not unbearably so; the windows are really good, and I always travel with earplugs. Had I not been there on a weekend, it might have quieted down much earlier than it did on Friday and Saturday nights. I was really tired so I wasn't disturbed by the city noise (only thing that woke me up was the 2:00 a.m. garbage truck) . The room was super clean. There is a digital safe in the roomy closet. Wireless internet is available for $9/day. Water pressure was excellent and all in all, I had no complaints.
This is a ten-story property and I'm really glad my room was only on the second floor--the elevator is slower than anything I've ever seen, so after getting my bag to the room I used the stairs for the duration of my stay. 
The staff was friendly, helpful, and efficient, and at the AAA rate of only $104 per night, I could not have asked for a better experience!

title: “Loved it - just like nearly everyone else”
text:
I had stayed at the hilton for a conference and then changed hotels to hang around NY for an extra day. was on my own and did expect the room to be a signficant "drop down" after the Hilton but it pleasantly wasn't a big adjustment ! Only stayed for a night but the staff still treated me very well, they were very efficient with the booking etc. 
It's been nicely renovated and my room was small but perfect for 1 person (fine for one night !). Lots of hot water, etc. It was definately a very affordable NY option for 1 person travelling alone. 
I have stayed in other guest houses in NY and this one is far superior to other experiences thus far. 
Will be back !

title: “Excellent Hotel with Great Location”
text:
Location: Great downtown location. Hotel is located around the corner from Beale Street
Occasion for Stay: Stayed here for a vacation/B-day trip with my wife.
Room: Because of my Hilton Honors Diamond status, I requested an upgrade to a suite. Could not get it for the first night, had a regular room on the Honors Floor, which was fine. Was upgraded to a 2 room suite with double balcony the next night. The room was well appointed, bed extremely comfortable, and noise-free (ask for a room away from Beale Street).
Cleanliness: Room was spotless.
Service: Friendly front desk crew. Also good security after hours.
Food: Breakfast was fine.
Parking: Hotel has parking garage located adjacent to the hotel
Shuttle Service: Didn’t use.
I highly recommend this property.

title: “Two stays at HOJO”
text:
I stayed at Howard Johnsons twice on my layovers in Phoenix. I must say that the first stay I was not impressed. The room was just so so, however it was clean although it was pretty bare bones. The bed was comfortable and that was all I cared about. 
On my return trip, I was impressed by the room. Upon entering I was pleasantly surprised at the appearance of the room, it was nicely appointed. The bed was the best! The sheets were soft and cuddly and there were plenty of covers. I slept like a baby and awoke refreshed.
All in all Howard Johnson is a good value for travelersThe location of the hotel was not in a very good part of town, but it was very convenient to the airport.

title: “really nice downtown hotel close to points of interest”
text:
3 of us stayed here for 6 days and loved every minute. Location is great for walking to Navy Pier, Millenium park, Magnificent Mile shopping and Riverside.
Used the "loop" to get to Sear's Tower.Used the Trolley Bus tour to see city highlights and then Wrigley's Park Stadium- excellent value.
Found that reasonably priced restaurant choice was a bit limited however breakfast at the West Egg opposite the hotel was very good.
Rooms at the hotel are well appointed and well managed.
Contrary to other reports we read we found use of the roof pool is free to guests.
All staff were very helpful however a special mention must be of Ron at reception who seemed to find that nothing was too much bother- a really nice guy.

title: “Great San Francisco experience,”
text: We recently stayed at the Donatello over Thanksgiving with some friends from Oregon. Contributing to our wonderful time in San Francisco were the comfortable accommodations we enjoyed at the Donatello. Our rooms (which were the same) were large, clean, and contained all of the amenities one would expect from this caliber of hotel including a refrigerator, microwave, coffee maker, and a small sink. The staff was very congenial and ready to meet our every request with eagerness. The morning continental breakfast consisting of many food choices was delightful and more than sufficient to prepare us for our day's excursion. We have stayed at the Donatello before so we felt comfortable inviting guests to join us this time, and they enjoyed their experience as much as we did. We look forward to returning in the near future.

title: “Great weekend!”
text: We flew to Charlotte on 11/10/12 for the sole purpose of going to see the Denver Broncos play the Carolina Panthers and stayed in this hotel for two nights. We had a king bed and the room had a little sitting area with a couch and another chair. Mini kitchen had everything you could need for a few night stay, including utensils, a dishwasher, full fridge, and a wine bottle opener.
