Hotel was great- bed was comfortable (on the firm side, which I love, but not everyone does), bathroom was nice, room was clean, etc. Front desk staff were great and helpful. The business center was right in front of the elevators and we had no trouble printing off our boarding passes for our flights. The hot breakfast was good and the omelet station was fantastic! Staff during breakfast was extremely nice, funny, and friendly. Actually, everyone we made contact with during our stay was friendly- from housekeeping to the maintenance man we talked to in the elevator! We did walk onto the outside patio area that had the very small outdoor pool - it was off of the 7th floor. Good area to take a glass of wine or a cocktail and sit outside and look at the city. For our purposes, the hotel was about a mile from the NFL stadium (Bank of America Stadium). It was an enjoyable walk through the downtown (or uptown as they call it) area. Yes, the hotel is near the bus terminal station but we did not feel unsafe as some of the other reviewers mentioned. There were police/security outside whenever we walked by, no matter the time of day/night. The hotel is within walking distance to most of the restaurants/bars in the uptown area. The hotel is right next to Time Warner if you are traveling for a basketball game or concert. We were able to go to a bar at the Epicenter (about two blocks away) called Howling at the Moon. It was a dueling piano bar and we highly recommend! We didn't use any bus or train services while there. We did take a taxi from the aiport to the hotel and it was $25.00 each way (not including tip). The hotel was less than 10 miles from the airport. This was our first trip to Charlotte and we enjoyed every second!

title: “Friendly, great for families & well priced”
text:
I stayed here for a night with a large travelling party and it's a perfectly good, well sited hotel at Fisherman's wharf. Check in was very pleasant with a wonderfully friendly and chatty receptionist. The rooms are ok - this hotel probably needs a bit of a refresh in 2012 as things are starting to look a bit out of date and worn but that said, everything was clean and the bed was comfortable.
This is a really great hotel for families as it has a great buffet breakfast and good amenities. Fisherman's wharf itself in November isn't the best place to be in San Francisco and I noticed far more homeless and begging going on around the streets than my last visit here 4 years ago - sign of the times I guess. Ultimately the very thing I love about San Fran is it's "realness" in relation to other cities but I can understand why some reviewers would comment on that.
We visited Alcatraz for the evening tour which was just brilliant and the walk from hotel to Alcatraz pier is about 15 mins or so.
Ultimately for a good price this is a great place to stay - one thing I would thing about if I was IHG was investing a bit of money in this hotel in 2012 if you want to keep people coming...

title: “Best hotel ever!”
text:
We have traveled all over the world, and stayed at everything from 5-star palaces to dives for $2 a night--and this blew them all out of the water. First of all, the hotel is decorated beautifully. What could have been an otherwise mundane 3 star hotel is uplifted by thoughtful touches in every room--moroccan stools, beautiful paint on the walls, and inexpensive but cute furniture. Very boho/ethnic chic. Secondly, the staff is great. They were very courteous and with one exception, helpful with getting around San Francisco, and even the unhelpful person was nice. Third, the lobby is a great place to hang out. Don't expect much from the wine cocktail hour--the wine is not the greatest--but visually the lobby is quite inviting with beautiful fabrics on the walls, two fireplaces, and unusual and carefully selected furniture. Finally, the restaurant--we didn't get to eat dinner there, but the breakfast was good. I highly recommed the Yemeni Fouel, a soupy bean paste with poached eggs. They also have more American breakfast options like waffles. 
If you are looking for 5 star luxury with down comforters and persian carpets as doormats, this isn't it. But all things considered, I would call this the best hotel I ever stayed at. It's perfect for the former backpacker who has moved up in life, but I don't think others would be disappointed either. We got a good deal from the hotel website.

title: “Great location!”
text:
Stayed one night for a conference at the Convention Center, which happens to be right across the street. The hotel is also only 6 blocks from the great Larimar Square and walking distance to the Pepsi Center and Coors Field.
Staff was friendly and the room was clean, but few things made this hotel standout amongst some of the other great downtown hotels that offer more creative little touches (free milk and cookie hour or cocktail hour at some other downtown hotels...). The view though was nice since it is neighbors with the Convention Center which happens to be shorter than the sky scrapers offering a view of the snow capped Rockies.
Vallet will hold your car even past check out, which given expensive downtown parking, saves you from having to double pay for parking.

title: “Very nice hotel”
text: My girlfriends and I stayed at Jurys for 3 nights and we were not disappointed. The service was friendly, efficient and respectful at all times. Our room was spacious, the washroom was large (we enjoyed the heated towel rack and Aveda products)and the beds were very comfortable although we would have been happier with two queens rather than two doubles. As first time visitors to Boston we found the location excellent - we were able to walk almost everywhere and felt very safe going to and from the hotel after dark. I would definitely return to Jurys!

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
No negatives, (can't blame them for the fog spoiling the Bay view !). 
Friendly helpful staff, excellent location, get your timings right (i.e. miss the tour buses) and the queue for the cable car disapears, loads of good restaurants (especially Bubbagumps on Pier 39 for the kids and Mcormick and Kuletos at Ghirardelli Square for the grown ups), Consierge can also recommend a good Chinese restaurant who will delivery to your room.
Our room faced the bay (fourth floor), no problems with noise, very comfortable beds, bathroom was adequate (why do they need to be big ?) decor is bold but makes a nice change for corporate blandness. Didn't leave my heart but will go back and stay there again !

title: “Great location and a good experience overall!”
text:
The good: Comfortable bed, great location to Nob Hill and Chinatown; easy transport to everything else. Breakfast was good, but doesn't start until 7am. Friendly staff and front door locked in the evening (maybe a minus to some, but left me feeling more secure). Airport Transport arranged easily and a multilingual staff.
The not- so- good (not bad enough to be called bad): Room was small, but as-advertised. The decor is a little less than 'family friendly' on some of the floors (lots of nudes, but I didn't care). It is an older hotel but I feel like it adds character. I did hear other guests sometimes (mostly water pipes from other rooms), but not really any traffic noise.

title: “wont stay anywhere else”
text: i went with my husband and mother in law july 4th weekend.. the staff was for the king bed suite so nice . we got there at 12pm and they let us check in three hours earlyl. great location. ten minute walk to the harbor five to little italy. i missed breakfast (slept late) the staff made up a plate for me despite my polite protests. valet service is pricey but vey hospitable- asked us if we needed any directions every time we got in the car. rooms clean. nothing fancy. we got the suite since mom in law with us. the only drawback was that i wish there was more of a seperation between the rooms. But will go again without her. cant beat the price. paid 150 on priceline fairfield 800 number wanted ten dollars more than priceline. overall a great place to stay for the money.

title: “Just as Expected for Radisson”
text: Beds are very comfortable with sleep number remote. Didn't know how to use it though. Room devices functioned well. Elevators are slow and sometimes unreliable. Also, noise from outside is very easily heard. Staff very friendly, particularly our chambermaid. I would stay here again if in Baltimore.

title: “If You're Going to San Francisco...”
text:
...be sure to check out this hotel!
I break my reviews down in point form when I can because it helps give traveller's a clearer picture and also when I have loads to say about a hotel (in this case, all good stuff).
I stayed at this hotel on a recommendation from a friend and it was the best decision! There are, however, two things I must point out: 
1) I got this through a Travelzoo promotion so it DID include continental breakfast and free Wifi.
2) I am long past the budget hotels but I never choose the 5* Luxury hotels. I'm usually somewhere around 3-4 * 
So, the review.
Service: Excellent. From check in to check out I had nothing but polite, courteous, friendly service from everyone - desk staff, breakfast staff, maid - everyone. Always ready to help or answer questions and offer information at check in without being prompted. It made an excellent impression on me right away.
Room: perfect for me. Clean, spacious enough, quiet enough and dark enough (though on holidays I'm an early riser when I have sightseeing to do). Well stocked for toiletries etc and a full minibar (which I never use but I know is a plus for some guests), a flat screen telly (same as minibar) and no surrounding noise.
Location: excellent for sightseeing - very close to Union Square and I walked to Fisherman's Wharf (though if you aren't a walker, the cable car is two blocks away). MUNI is right on the corner across the street and there's a Walgreen's right across as well. The hotel is very close to a seedy part of town but if you practice caution and are aware, you should be ok. Also, SF is full of street beggars etc so it's hard to be central and escape that. 
Price: Travelzoo promotion at $99 a night including breakfast and Wifi in May. As my friend who lives in CA said, "You don't get places in SF for $99 a night that are any good" 
Except this one!
In short, I recommend this hotel - if you're like me amd use hotels as a place to keep your luggage and sleep at the end of a busy day sightseeing - then this is the place for you.

title: “Would stay again”
text: We were "homeless" after giving birth to our first child since we were moving from San Diego to Seattle. We had to stay the weekend in San Diego and choose the Marriott. They were able to give us a room towards the very end of the hallway so our newborn's cries wouldn't disturb very many people Very accommodating and friendly staff. Centrally located in San Diego where all our friends could meet us. We would definitely stay there again.

title: “Amazing Customer Service”
text: The location - picturesque with easy access to Riverwalk. Room - very comfortable. Customer service - the highlight. Hotel staff was prompt, friendly and provided exceptional service. Elissa especially went out of her way to make our stay enjoyable.

title: “Great Place to Stay”
text:
We have no complaints about this hotel. The room was perfect, the staff was very friendly, and the breakfast was great too. I still can't believe how cheap this hotel is. It's by far the best Comfort Suites we've stayed at and it's also the cheapest. You can't go wrong with this place. 
I did overhear a woman complaining that the airport shuttle didn't start running until 6:00 AM. Apparently their website says that it runs 24/7. I don't know that for sure though.

title: “Wedding In Paradise”
text:
I had both my wedding and wedding reception at the Bay Club Hotel and Marina this past weekend (Oct 7-9) and could not have been more pleased with how the entire affair turned out. Most of my guests came in from out of town so we had them all stay at the hotel. It was a great decision because they all enjoyed themselves and had wonderful things to say about the hotel. Everyone loved being so close to everything (downtown San Diego, the San Diego Zoo, Sea World) and they loved their rooms. They had incredible views from both sides of the hotel and received great service from the hotel staff. We had wonderful weather that weekend so many of them got a chance to relax by the beautiful pool and patio in the back of the hotel. They all raved about the food and the wonderful (complimentary) breakfast buffet each morning. 
As for my wedding and reception I worked with Tammy Garbini, Director of Sales and Marketing and she took care of everything right down to the last detail. We decided to have the ceremony outside on the back patio which was absolutely gorgeous against the incredible views of the marina. As luck would have it the weather was spectacular so we truly got married in paradise! After the wedding Tammy arranged for a nice cocktail hour so our guests could mingle and enjoy drinks and hor d'oeuvres. It was the perfect touch to lead into the reception. The food at our wedding reception was delicious and the service from the hotel staff was fantastic. They took great care of not just our bridal party but every single one of our guests. Absolutely everyone felt attended to and it gave such a warm and personal feeling to the entire affair. I didn't have to worry about a thing - Tammy and her incredible staff handled everything for me so I could enjoy my day and spend every minute with my guests. We absolutely loved it and had a wonderful time!
The next time I have a big party to do I won't hestitate to have it at the Bay Club and Marina. Or even a nice weekend with friends … We had a great experience and are looking forward to going back there soon!

title: “Location, location, location”
text: This hotel is situated downtown and within a short walk or monorail ride from most attractions in Seattle--access to light rail is also on the same block so getting most places in Seattle including the airport is very easy. The hotel is very nice and was clean--we had a double queen with two bathrooms which was really great!! The bar in the lobby was also a perfect spot to wind down the evening. Would definately stay here again

title: “Great place to stay in Boston!”
text: My wife and I stayed here for 4 nights in July 2011 in a spacious, clean, self contained room with it's own kitchenette, a living room, bedroom and bathroom. The room had very nice decor and furnishings. The location in a lovely old neighborhood was excellent, being a stones throw from the Prudential Centre and Copely Plaza shopping malls, as well as the restaurants and shops in nearby Newbury Street. It's also only a short walk to the historic part of Boston. This is a real gem. Chris and Kim Tatam

title: “Horrible Night!”
text: My boyfriend and I booked a room here last minute to attend a wedding in Scottsdale. I was really excited because i had heard that this was a really nice place. WE were really excited when they assigned us a condo type room with a covered parking space. WEll, when we drove back to our room, which was a duplex, with one more larger room below us, we were upset because all of the four parking spots were taken, by who , I don't know. SO we parked on the street. This was fine. So let me get to the horrible part. When we were ready for bed, at about 10pm, we heard very very loud rap music apparently coming from the room below us. I called the front desk once and they called the other room and the music stopped. OKAY fine, right ? NO WAY. At about 12am we were awoken to very very loud music and a bunch of kids screeming "HAPPY BIRTHDAY". I called front desk, they sent out security and the music stopped. ABout 20 min later, the music started again. AND SERIOUSLy, it seemed like our walls were paper thin. We could hear these kids cussing and yelling and we even smelled pot. I was SO furious by this point, its 2am now, I called front desk and asked for another room. THEY REFUSED and said they would call security again. Security did nothing but made all the kids leave the room. SO now the kids are standing outside our window cursing and breaking bottles. WAS this the HILTON OR WHAT?? I called the front desk yet again and demand a new room or to call the police. They still did NOTHING. Let me tell you I was even afraid to go outside to check on my car. Well, I called and got the managers name, obviously an inexperienced kid, and in the morning when I spoke to the manager, he again did nothing. OH wait, he took $20 off our BILL> I WAS SO FURIOUS!! I will absolutely never ever stay here again. I cannot believe a hilton would allow this. ANd I didn't even mention that these kids came back in the morning about 6:30 am and began slamming doors. PLEASE, don't stay here if you want peace and quiet.

title: “Lovely hotel”
text: Good boutique hotel in a quiet clean location yet very near to Grand Central station, Empire State building, NYC Public library. Friendly helpful staff who care about customer service, free wine reception at 5pm every day, tea and coffee in reception in the morning and cold drinks in the afternoon. Nice bedrooms and a very safe clean location. We stayed for 7 nights and thoroughly enjoyed it.

title: “beware of the hotel's reccomendation of americanaticketsny as a company to obtain broadway tickets for you(30-150%upchar”
text:
Beware fo americannaticketny's temendous upcharge on broadway tickets
I called the hotel's concierge and asked if they could help in obtaining tickets for Wicked the said they would help and they patched me thru to ammericannatickets I spoke with katlin "the manager of the hotel site for americannaticketsny" she said she could find me tickets she never told me of the tremendous upcharge for a non sold out performance the cost of the tickets were $200 dollars apiece ($156.25 and their fee 0f 43.75)
 I was not informed by either the hotel or katlin that there would be a 30% upcharge for the tickets Katlin said she is trained to say "they are a service company and that the consumer has to figure it out for themselves"
I spoke with the manager on duty for the hotel sunday morning 15jul12
she informed me that they are aware of the up charge and that the concierge was supposed to inform guests of the up charge and that she would speak to them to be sure they inform future guest of the 30-150% up charge as this did not happen with me.
I then returned to my room and called the concierge desk and was informed from a different person that there is a 30-150% up charge and that as a guest you wouild do better going to the box office and/or ticketmasters(as they only charge about 10 dollars as their fee) he also said not all the members of the concierge staff do this but he try's to do this
HOPE THIS WILL HELP FUTURE GUESTS ! GO TO THE BOX OFFICE OR TICKETMASTERS
I HAVE NO FINANCIAL INTEREST IN THESE AGENCIES AND WANT EVERYONE TO GET A FAIR SHAKE AND HOPE THE HOTEL'S STAFF WILL BE HONEST WITH THEIR GUESTS

title: “Great accommadation for Denver Area Travelers”
text: The desk service was outstanding. The receptionist understood my needs for space and made the appropiate accommadations. The room was spacious and provided great comfort for the entire family. We also felt very safe and secure within the hotel complex. Evryrthing a traveling family needed was available.

title: “Okay, but can do better for the price”
text:
I stayhed here for only 1 night, mostly because the hotel were my conference was being held was full that night. The location is good for tourist activities, within easy walking distance of the White House. The staff were all extremely pleasant. The lobby in this historic hotel is beautiful. The room was pretty quiet, and the bed (with way too many pillows) was very comfortable.
On the downside, my room was quite small and very dark and cramped feeling. The window looked across at another wing of the hotel. When I arrived in the evening, the light switch nearest the door didn't turn on any lights, so I had to make my way in the dark to find another switch. No WiFi, but there is wired internet (for $12.95/day). The dining options in the hotel are pretty limited. I ordered room service, which arrived promptly. There were a lot of mirrors in the room, which is nice, but there was a full-length mirror directly opposite the toilet, which annoys me. And finally, the room had no hotel directory or guide--just a room service menu--so I really had no clue what services the hotel has or where anything was.
Overall, it was okay. The employees are to be commended for their great attitudes. But for the same price ($170 government rate), I could have done better.

title: “Great location and value for money”
text:
My friends and I stayed here for 5 nights. We arrived late on Saturday and the check in was smooth and swift, staff on the reception were very helpfull even printing out information for us from their computer.
We had a room for three, twin in one room with a little room off this with a single bed in it. The room was clean and made up every day, bathroom small but sufficient with as much hot water as we needed, clean towels every day.
The hotel was built in 1904, so yes if you look close enough it has a cracks here and there but it is full character, coffee and muffins in the morning are a great bonus.
It is well placed in the city for everything shops, subway,Empire state building etc.
Could not fault this hotel, ideal and fit for purpose as a base in New York.

title: “Scene from a horror film”
text:
I visited with some friends on a 6th form college trip, our total number being 29, so we had alot of rooms, but the group were spread out over all floors.
When we first arrived our eyes were immediatly drawn to the 'danger' tape in the corner of the lobby where the plaster was falling off the ceiling. I hoped that things would get better, unfortunatly they did not. One of the lifts was out of order, so rather then wait around i choose to use the main stairs. These were fine till we reached 5th floor where there was all kinds of rubbish and cigarette ash along with flammable liquids with lids of ect.
My room was shared with 3 others yet only 3 keys were provided and only 3 sets f towels ect. The bed was not terrible but when i first arrived we had to remove the top cover and shake the dust off. The shower was also a cause for concern, it would not keep a stable temperature and when my friend had finished, the hot water tap would not turn off and the bath was filling up as the plug stuck. it took 3 people to turn the tap off. None of the showers in friends rooms kept a temperature either.
We were the lucky ones, we had a kitchenette part in our room, but many people had small cramped rooms which with 2 double beds can cause problems in moving about and storage of suitcases ect. In one bedroom a mousetrap was found set under the bed, and in another cockroches were living.
The staff on a whole were not friendly or helpful. When my friends and I ordered Chinease takeaway, and had it in our room, we did not wish to keep the left overs in the room, given findings elsewhere we did not want to encourage insects in our room. When we took down the rubbish they glared at us for daring to disturb them and snapped that there was a bin in the lobby. 
The back stairway was even worse then the front. It had doors and curtain poles on the stairs. These did not seem a very health and safety way about things.
Overall my stay in New York was good, but i spent as little time as possible in the hotel. We hope to return there again sometime, but will not be staying in the same hotel. If you are considering a stay in this hotel, i urge you to reconsider immediatly!

title: “OK”
text: Not bad. Nice pool area with hot tub. Small gym and free parking and internet. Booked two nights on travel supermarket for about £55 per night but when we stayed an extra night it cost double that through the hotel. That's how they get you!!. Friendly staff and ok location right on the freeway. San Diego is about 20 minutes drive.

title: “Thumbs up for the Skyline Hotel”
text: We've just returned from a 4-night break in New York staying at the Skyline Hotel. We found it to be very clean, the staff were helpful & it's only a 10 - 15 minute walk from the Rockefeller Center, 5th Ave & Broadway. We'll be back soon.

title: “Crowded, busy hotel”
text:
We got a great deal on a room at the Palmer House so decided to stay there. It was clear, upon check-in, that you get what you pay for. Our room, a Studio, was tiny. I'm not kidding -- I know people with walk-in closets bigger than the room we had. It was long and narrow, with one full-size bed located right inside the door. Past the bed, they had crammed in all of the furniture that they put in regular sized rooms. One dresser would have been fine -- we really didn't need the desk and chair across from it, because you had to move the chair away from the desk to open the bureau drawers. 
The only other issue was the feeling of a constant crowd in the hotel. The only time I have ever had to stand in a long queue, literally snaking between velvet ropes to register, was when we went to Las Vegas. The Palmer House Hilton had the same feel as a busy Vegas hotel --- all hustle/bustle and no elegance or personalized service. We were awakened both nights, once at 2AM and the next night at 4AM, by screaming teenagers coming back from partying. Since the bed was right by the door, we could hear everything in the hallway, which didn't exactly make for a pleasant night's rest. 
My advice -- stay there for the location, and the price if you can get a good deal on the web, but beware!

title: “Great Location, Family Friendly”
text: Stayed here for a Dental Convention at the Moscone Center. Location was great, within walking distance to EVERYTHING ( china town, the convention center, union square, the trolley, ect. ) Room was very clean, and quiet. I could hear some noise from the street, but that's to be expected when staying in a city. The staff was very friendly and accommodating. My 2 yr old daughter joined me on the end of my business trip, and a crib was immediately brought up to the room with sheets and a blanket. There was plenty of room for the crib with the 2 queen beds. The Breakfast is overpriced for what you get, but that seems to be pretty standard in hotels. I would definitely stay at the Hotel Nikko again.

title: “Fabulous!”
text: My husband and I stayed at The Inn At Henderson's Wharf, Fells Point for our anniversary. It was perfect! The room was beautiful and spotless with a gorgeous view of the waterfront and wharf. Check in was smooth and quick and the person working even wished us a happy anniversary. We arrived at the hotel at 12:30 p.m. and our room was ready! The complimentary bottle of wine was wonderful (Chilean). We also received a snack tray of cheeses, crackers, chocolates and fruit. I believe this was due to our anniversary. Nice touch! The bed was so comfortable and the linens were very high quality. Loved the bathrobes too. I usually don't use the toiletries provided by the hotel but these smelled so good, I couldn't resist. There were also fresh flowers in the huge bathroom and a live potted plant in the bed area. The person who handled our check in was very friendly and helpful and made us feel welcome immediately. He also arranged our dinner reservations. Another plus..... parking was free, easy and secure. The deluxe continental breakfast was lovely - fresh berries, melons and other fruits, bagels, cereal, pastries, hard-boiled eggs, juices, coffee, tea, etc. We had our breakfast in the beautiful courtyard. We will definitely stay at this inn again. It was very convenient.... just a short walk to the water taxi stop. We were also offered a complimentary limo service to our dinner destination but decided to walk. Can't say enough about this gorgeous, clean, friendly inn and I am very particular! I even liked the fact that there was no "hotel smell" at Henderson's. Highly recommended.

title: “Good downtown hotel”
text:
Spent one night on business in early April. This is right in the heart of downtown near offices and good restaurants. $25 cab ride from airport. Clean and quiet room with closet, desk, table and chair, alarm clock, phone, and coffee in room. Curb service was good, checkin was hospitable if a bit slow. Checkout was efficient and prompt. Bed was comfortable, shower above average. On-site sports bar and cigar bar were each separate from lobby and quite enjoyable, there are several other nightspots a very short walk away. Starbucks in lobby. Overall nothing extraordinary, but everything well done.
One neat thing about this hotel is a historical marker in the sidewalk outside pointing out that this same location was an inn over 200 years ago and George Washington actually spent a night here. There are other similar markers around town if you have a few minutes to walk around.

title: “Couldn't fault this trip”
text: We stayed here for the first 3 days of our honeymoon. On arrival we were greeted at check-in by very friendly staff. Our room was upgraded from an internal room to a tower room with beautiful views of the bay, Alctaraz and Coit Tower. They couldn't have made us feel any more special. The room itself was excellent, clean and large. The bathroom was fantastic with a separate shower cubicle which is always better. The check-in staff also made us aware of the Tonga Bar downstairs in the hotel which has a rain storm with thunder and lightning. This made a good evenings entertainment. The concierge was very helpful when we had any questions. Room service was great and there was a vast choice to order in. The setting is perfect with the trolley not far away. Beware of the hills they're steeper even than they look!!

title: “Pleasantly surprised”
text: at the room in the Edison. I was very apprehensive after reading the negative comments but I couldn't fault our room. It was clean and spacious and perfect for our requirements.

title: “A three star hotel at five star prices!”
text:
The JW Marriott Desert Ridge fell short in every respect not only as a JW but as any Marriott branded hotel. The hotel was very expensive and unless you are on an non-scrutinized business expense account, I would not recommend this property for leisure. It is overcrowded, underwhelming and not what you would expect of a Marriott or any luxury property for that matter. The rooms are three star at best and we were charged $500+ a night! The service was not there. The check in process was impersonal. The lobby was cold and uninviting. The housekeeping service was average, no turn down service! Maintenance was lousy, we had a broken air conditioner and toilet. Dishes and trash were in the hallways and public areas. It was as if they expect you to pay extra for an average room and lousy service because it has the JW brand name. We certainly did not get good value or have a good experience. 
About us: I am a Marriott rewards elite member. We were a group of several families with adults and children ranging from 9 to 18 yrs. We were in Phoenix for spring break. We have stayed at other Phoenix properties including Squaw Peak, Paradise Valley, the Buttes, etc.
About the hotel: As a Marriott Vacation Club property, this consists of a main hotel building and canyon vacation villas (timeshares). There is a golf course and several pools on site. The resort's grounds are nice but not easily accessible since most of the green space is reserved for the golf course. There is a road that you can walk down. There is a elite concierge lounge, but this was not available due to a group being at the hotel. The breakfast buffet is good but costs $25 a person, ouch that's steep for a large group with teens for a breakfast that should be included. The food at the pools was lousy and is expensive, certainly not what you would expect at a JW. The drinks are also expensive expect to pay dearly for every drink for you and your kids. The only bright spots were a Roy's restaurant on property which has an excellent happy hour and a Starbucks Coffee. Other than that expect crowds and to spend lot's of money: crowded pools, crowded lounges, crowded lobbies and nowhere to relax. The pool area is like a zoo cage where you need to go through a single point of entry either with key card or a daily wrist band. The pools are OK but very crowded. The water was too warm for our tastes. It is hard to get chairs by the pools so get there early to reserve. There are 3 pools and a lazy river. There is also a large hot tub but it was too hot for me. There was a mix of families their with young children, teens and business people with spouses. As a side note, the signs to the left of the lobby that direct you to the pool were wrong and lead you to a gate that you cannot enter.
Our room was a connecting room. The room was loud from the noise of the air conditioner and we could not sleep. When we requested to be moved, the front desk refused saying there was nothing available. We were also given an accessible room which was specifically not our request. The toilet was also broken. When I mentioned this to the front desk, they did nothing. This is poor customer service. 
We asked for a restaurant recommendation & reservation from the concierge and they sent us to one of the most expensive restaurants in town (Sassi) it ended up costing us over $50 pp for pizza and pasta including the kids meals! Not very considerate. We then found Kierland Mall area which has Maggianos, PF Changs, etc. There is also a mall across Deer Valley that has an Albertsons and other stores.
In short, my experience was that the JW Desert Ridge was overpriced, overcrowded, my room was poor, the service was not there and did not deliver on any of my expectations. I will definitely not recommend this property to anyone for leisure.

title: “Fantastic Hotel we would stay again”
text:
This hotel is very central to most sights in the City. Most of the buildings in New York are Art Deco and this one was no exception, it truly was lovely, a hugh chandlier in the lobby, marble flooring, staff were very helpful, it has a feel of the 1930's, decorated to a very high standard. Dress was casual, nothing formal. 
As this was a surprise present for my 50th my husband had booked a room on the 39th floor, which meant we had a sitting room next to the bedroom, which was lovely and roomy, the photo at the top shows the room we had. The best sight of all was looking out of my bedroom window and seeing the Empire State Building, The Crysler Building, Madison Square Gardens, truly a fantastic sight night and day, especially at night, New York by night is breath taking. The breakfast room was next door to our room and had panaramic views all round, right down to lower Manhatten the Business District, the Statue of Liberty etc. 
The Subway Penn Station is next to the hotel which makes travelling much easier if you don't want to walk everywhere. Macy's is just round the corner, the biggest photographer shop B & H, biggest post office I have ever seen are both just round the block. Round the back of the hotel if you ask the bellboy, there is a lovely beautifully decorated restaurant, with excellent food at a place called Uncle Jack's, look for their offers at lunch time and especially on Sundays you will not be dissappointed.
I cannot fault this hotel in anyway, we would certainly stay there again no hesitation. Attached to the hotel is an American Diner called Tick Tock, lovely food, if you like rissottos, try the shrimp one, the flavour was outstanding, you get lots for you money, food is cheap and plentiful, better than eating out in the uk!!! For two lovely meals it cost us £9!!!
We ate here a few times as it was 24 hours, just like the city, you don't check time in New York as you can get what you want anytime!
Also attached to the hotel is another restaurant with a bar, I realised towards the end of our stay that the Tick Tock is also licensed. We didn't try this one, as we had such a full programme could not fit it in but all looked lovely and reasonably priced. Maybe we will try it when we come back next time, as we would like to do New York at Christmas time one year.
All in all you would not be disappointed if you were to book this hotel, to be fair we did have a posh room not sure what the other rooms are like, without the sitting room, I still feel there would have been enough room, besides you have come to see the City not stay in your room!!! But looking at the quality of the hotel I feel the other rooms would still be of good size. It's main attraction is location, can't beat it for that alone. Very central and if you like walking it is within reach of most sights, the further ones use the Subyway, very easy to use and if you get a 7 day Metro Card - $30 you can use it as many times as you like on the Subway, well worth the money. 
I could talk all day about New York but it wouldn't be fair, you have to find out for yourself, I found it enchanting, the smells, the sounds, busy, vibrant, noisy. The New Yorkers are the friendliest people, they love to help you, customer service is impeccable, you do have to tip for everything, they are part of their wages, to be honest tipping is pennies, but we felt every penny was worth it.
I will go now, enjoy the hotel and enjoy New York!!!! I defy you not to.

title: “10 points !”
text: I give 10 points to this Hotel. A lot of people should go there and learn a little bit what's hotel hospitality. All the information that we needed was provided by the frond desk. A lot of great facilities ( Bar, Internet studio, Art Gallery ). They were doing renovation in one of the elevators, but the letter appologising was signed by the GM, which seemed to me as he Know all the time what's going on in his hotel. Personal Minibar and wine reception at the Bar for free, where u can find a lot of travellers and have nice conversations with them.

title: “BEST LOCATION BEST STAFF BEST SIZE ROOMS!”
text: This hotel is literally my second home. I would not think of staying anywhere else while im in NYC(business or pleasure). The location is perfect. Its not in the center of Time Square where all the traffic lights and noise are but a block away providing quieter nights and no crazy billboard flashing lights. Convenient to everything subway, port authority, penn station, central park, broadway, and hells kitchen(best restaurants...more affordable 9th ave) are walking distance. The staff always is eager to help and make wonderful recommendations. The rooms are LARGE compared to many hotels in NYC. Did i mention the staff? Martyn, Sondra, Nancy, Marilyn, Jose, Albert, Sam, Ugene, Joella, and the rest ROCK! Catch them at their BEST and let them know!

title: “Bad bed, old bath, very friendly reception”
text:
The location is very central - 200 m to the city hall, right next to Chinatown (although the streets are quite dark and I suppose many would not like walking to Chinatown) and close to Independence Hall and all.
My room - 903 - had an old bed that gave me a very bad sleep :-(. The plumbing in the bathroom was loose, and I definitely hadn't the feeling that I was at a Hilton.
Breakfast was ok for an American hotel, but nothing special with just few options and very little and quite standard fresh fruit.
What made the hotel gain the third point was the receptionist, and I am ashamed for having forgetter her name. She asked kindly about my sleep and when I said that I had actually slept badly, she looked very concerned, asked for details about the bed, made notes and gave me a 10K Honors-point compensation. Not that it can replace a night's sleep, but she made me feel a lot better. Credit to her!

title: “Very good stay”
text: Rented a two bed suite for a girls weekend. The room was nice and hotel staff was very helpful - brought in rollaway, provided a complimentary key to the business center, allowed late check-out, complimentary breakfast bar was extensive if not a meal that you might pay for, and staff was friendly. Overall, they left a very good impression.

title: “Disrepair - Will not return - Would not recommend”
text:
There's a lot of disrepair: rusty fixtures, wet carpet in closet and on main walkway near bathroom, nonworking bathtub drain. Room was basic, bare and cramped. TV received about 12 channels. We had ants in the room around the bathroom sink. The fitness center was a joke. The equipment was filthy. The elliptical and bike were unusable. The two treadmills might have worked. The weight machine was broken with the stack of weights stuck at the top.
Breakfast was a plate of eggs, sausage, and two pieces of white toast ... no choice of other items and not continental as their site claims.
Please note that if you want a microwave or fridge in your room, you have to rent it; although, there is a microwave available near the lobby. Also note that they provided only enough for one cup of coffee in the room.
There were a few positives: The staff was friendly and helpful. They could only do so much though in this tired, worn out facility. The bed was clean and comfy, and the pool and hot tub were enjoyable as well.
Overall though, we will not return to this location, and we will not recommend it to friends.

title: “Great Hotel and brilliant location near Fishermans Wharf”
text:
Stayed at the Best Western Fishermans Wharf Hotel in June 2005 and really loved everything about it. A warm welcome on arrival and a nice suite although the rooms were quite compact, however I understand this is common in Fishermans Wharf . Our suite was located on the inner courtyard of the Hotel and lovely and quiet away from any possible traffic noise. Can highly recommend the Restaurant attached to the Hotel for both breakfast and dinner. All in all a great Hotel to stay in at a reasonable cost close to all the action on Fishermans Wharf.
Free internet use in the reception area was a great touch.

title: “Millenium Hilton New York”
text: Really nice hotel, we had a room in 25th floor, great view on top of 9/11 memorial and the new constructions and Hudson River on the back. Friendly staff, and a nice pool-sauna-gym. Only downside is the area, cause the financial district is not the best place to be at nightfall, but of course we knew that prior to our booking. Really nice connection with the subway though. Recommended.

title: “Sr. Manager, Software Company”
text:
One of the best experiences. A great place to stay!!!
Pam Tarini

title: “Old Hotel”
text:
Small, room (even for NY!), with old furniture -the drawers wouldn't close-, and the bathroom was really small and uncomfortable.
The attention was ok.
Location isn't what I'd reccomend, but if you wan't to be in the middle of the torist world, then it's an ideal location.

title: “Cockroaches in the rooms!”
text: Terrible hotel in terms of cleanliness. Very old hotel, going through multiple renovations. Our first day we were given a room without a doorknob & still getting fixed. We then complained to be moved to the 3rd floor where we were waken up every morning by 7AM by workers outside on the scaffolding. We then found cochroaches in our room from there forward and even a used condom on our outside window. Otherwise, 1 block from Times Square and super close to Hell's Kitchen--otherwise very very dirty. Showers & bed not that great.

title: “Average to Very Good, except for the astronomical parking fee!”
text: Considering the issue with parking, I should rate this hotel as poor or terrible. I had originally booked at the other Sheraton -- the Four Points -- but poor reviews caused me to switch to this hotel, and it was less expensive than either the highly rated Radisson or the Hilton. I don't remember anything particularly special about this hotel or my stay -- check-in went quickly, the staff was efficient but not overly friendly thus "professioinal" and my room was attractive and clean. And very close to the airport! So for a place to sleep it was fine. The Starbuck's in the lobby was closed when I checked out, but my friend ordered really expenisve room service which came quickly and was (according to him) okay tasting. My big complaint was parking. I had rented a car, and when I pulled up to ask the valet where the parking lot was, he said there wasn't one and only valet parking was available. I think I was scammed. Later I saw a pay lot behind the hotel. What gives with that? At least the valet in the morning was quick to retrieve my car and was good with my parking it in front for a while. I guess people at an airport hotel don't drive? He should have at least given me the options.

title: “Very pleasant experience”
text: We just returned from a weekend in Philly and our dtayvatvthe holiday inn was excellent! We just returned from a week vacation at a very upscale resort in Jamaica and aside from the view(can't beat the Caribbean) our stay here was very comparable! Great job to everyone who takes pride in this fine establishment. We already booked another night next month.

title: “WOW: I am here right now and this place is gross!”
text: Okay, so I am here at the Crowne Plaza right now. We got into our room about 2 hours ago. The Staff: VERY Friendly. The decor, old. But this is fine, we expected it. What we didn't expect is the MANY hairs all over the tub (It is like they didn't even clean this place) and the NASTY bed spread with stains all over it. I mean seriously, I have 3 kids and 127 employees... I have been to 10 Countries and just about every state in the nation. I booked this on priceline because they said it was a 3 1/2 start joint. I am telling you, AT BEST it is a 2. I am so bothered, I am not even going to call down stairs to tell them because frankly, I don't have the time or the patients to be moved around. Shame on Crowne Plaza. Time to go and clean my own bathroom and lysol the joint (Yes, I went to Walgreens and bought Lysol... had no choice.)

title: “Perfect Location, Great Rooms, Super Clean, Not A Big Property...What's Not To Love!”
text: This hotel was perfect! Not a screaming busy typical 800+ room convention hotel. If you haven't figured it out yet, small properties like the Chicago Conrad, treat individual liesure travelers better than the big places who care more about large busienss and convention travel groups. I like that the reception is 5 floors above the street giving it a nice quiet exclusive vibe. The rooms are extremely well layed out so that you feel tucked away from the hallway. Immaculately clean. Friendly helpfull staff. Free coffee in the morning. Free bottled water in the room, which you need after a walk on Mich Ave. Big bathrooms with classy touches like high quality towels & wash clothes. The beds and pillows are almost the equal of our highend stuff at home. Loved the little dimmer lights in the ceiling above each pillow so one spouse can read while the other sleeps. Nicely furnished room with comphy sitting chair and foot stool. This place is quiet and a relaxing retreat when Michigan ave sidewalk crowd is getting to you just duck upstairs to the Conrad. I'd recommend a room that doesn't front Michigan ave as those rooms might be a little less peaceful because of the busy street below. Our room faced north toward the Hancock building and had no street below it. Not a single negative. Great!

title: “Thanks again to the Arizona Biltmore and to Frank & Albert's”
text: Although it has been a few weeks since my family and I spent almost 10 days at the Arizona Biltmore (this was my 14th year in a row staying at the Arizona Biltmore) and although I have neglected to get this written until today, I made commitment to myself that I would make the time today to send my thanks to the entire Staff at the Biltmore and especially to James and Inez who waited on us most nights when we enjoyed dinner at Frank & Albert's. The Menu and wine selection are great at F&A but the service we received from James and Ines was truly extraordinary: each nite James and/or Ines welcomed us truly like Family; special needs for granddaughters Olivia and Ruby (6 and 4+) cheerfully were accomodated; the dining experiences were great in every way and genuinely "spoiled" us in a way that makes me hope we can all gather as a Family next year for my 15th year in a row to the Biltmore and meals at Frank & Albert's. Thanks again all of you at Frank & Albert's and especially James and Ines.

title: “Nice staff, dull room.”
text: I've stayed in much nicer Doubletree Hotels. The chair was threadbare with stuffing coming out of the arms. The room and the hallways have an industrial feel to them and one long wall or our room had no artwork where it clearly needed something to break the monotony. This Doubletree is clean and the bed, as in all Hilton properties, is very comfortable. The hotel staff was friendly and helpfulm and it's a great location, next to Chinatown. But, the room was disappointing. It felt drab and dull. Wish we'd stayed at the Hilton instead.

title: “Teeny, Tiny Rooms and Grump Staff”
text:
Stayed at the Roosevelt over Thanksgiving 2002. Our room was extremely small. Not a room for resting and relaxing in, simply a spot to sleep. 
We upgraded to a "spa suite" that had a whirlpool tub and it thankfully, included a sitting area. Overall, the accomodations were just average. The only thing this hotel has going for it is location - we were able to watch fireworks and a parade all from the window of our room. Will stay somewhere else next time.

title: “Never stay any place else!”
text: I first discovered On The Ave a few years ago when friends came back from a trip and mentioned this great place they stayed at on the upper west side. They lavished nothing but praise for this hotel. They loved everything from the staff to the room to the bathroom amenities. I was skeptical at first...then I saw the web site. It appeared to be everything they said so for my next trip I booked a room. I was not disappointed! On The Ave was everything they said it would be and more. I would encourage anyone to give it a try. You will not be sorry. I have been back many times and have never had anything but great stays.

title: “Great location, reasonably priced, good value”
text:
Very good location, reasonably priced.
This hotel had a very good location right on Lombard Street which was close to restaurants and attractions. The room was adequate and had the convenience of a microwave and mini-fridge. The desk clerks were nice and accomodating. The continental breakfast consisted of hot beverages and orange juice plus prepackaged Danishes and also a few bananas. We usually ate breakfast at the IHOP which was a block away. There was alot of traffic noise as Lombard is a very busy main street. When you turned on the heat, there was a funky odour. My husband found the bed hard but I liked it. It would have been nice to have a dresser in the room as we kept our clothes in the suitcase for the entire 7 days. It was good hotel at a reasonable price. Public transportation was very efficient and close by.
From what we heard from others, summers tend to be cold here so we went in mid October and the weather was nice from 67-80. We went to alot of attractions and especially enjoyed the Alcatraz at night tour, the Wax museum, Fisherman’s wharf, Chinatown and the bay cruise. The seals at Pier 39 are also something to see and hear.The traffic is very crazy here and parking is expensive. Don't bother to rent a car - buy the City Pass for $59 which includes admission to museums and aquariums as well as unlimited public transportation. We even took the bus to Haight-Ashbury where the hippie movement is alive and well. There are so many restaurants here especially on Chestnut Street and this hotel was close to Plutos - a great salad and sandwich place with good food and good prices. Chinatown has good authentic Chinese food very reasonably priced too. Check out Union Square with all the high end shopping and beautiful buildings. We walked across the Golden Gate Bridge- it was windy but a great experience.
We loved our week in San Francisco. The people here were very friendly and the city is safe.

title: “Lovely stay”
text: We recently had 2 weeks here and it was a great place to stay. The room was comfortable especially the bed and bathroom. And it was spotless. However the breakfast service left a disappointing edge. Still not something that would prevent me from recommending this lovely hotel. The staff were very helpful and accommodating. And the Blue Duck Tavern is a great restaurant. Stay here!

title: “Excellent!”
text: Perfect spot in times square, intimate and cozy. Nice cont. breakfast, yummy treats during the day and wine n cheese in eve. Here's lookin at you kid!

title: “Godd Hotel Great Location”
text:
Stayed in the Millenium for 3 nights on our second trip to New York.
Hotel is in a great location in Midtown to see the city from. Most of the major subway lines are close and it is on top of times square. I had requested a high room with a view to give an extra edge to our stay and on our arrival we had a room on the 38th fllor with a view of the crysler building, Paramount buiilding and The empire state building from our huge window. The room was not a suite or in the Premier section but was a great size and very clean. You cant really ask for more in Midtown.
The room was expensive as it was Marathon weekend but the hotel although full never seemed crowded and each time we had to peak to staff they were polite, friendly and helpful.
Great place for restaurants and bars in and around times square and a good starting point for the whole city.
No traffic noise even at the most busy times and the only down point we had with the hotel were the astronomical prices at the hotel bar. Go accross the steet and you will get better drinks and better value for money.

title: “Great place to stay, clean and comfortable”
text:
This hotel is a great place to stay on business or pleasure. The rooms are clean and comfortable. The staff goes out of its way to please their guests. I would stay here again. It is in the heart of everything and is safe and secure.
If you are a runner like me, all you have to do for a great running route is to turn right out of the main entrance of the hotel, go up Eighth Avenue about 1/2 mile to Columbus Circle and then go straight into Central Park which is just behind Columbus Circle. Nothing better than a run through Central Park and you have very quick and easy access to it from this hotel. 
I will stay here again when back in NYC.

title: “Pleasant... until check out.”
text:
I recently stayed at the Tribeca Grand for a business trip. Because there was a bit of a savings and a few extra things my business partner and I booked the "Tryst in Tribeca" package which included a "full american breakfast delivered to your room" along with champagne on arrival (which we never got, maybe you had to ask for it). We ordered the breakfast from the room service menu the first night - when it was delivered the next morning the guy gave us the bill with the full amount charged to it. I told him that we had the "tryst" package and the breakfast was included. I gave him our card that listed all of the items that came in our package and he seemed satisfied with that and said he would correct it. Next day we had arrived too late the night before to order from the room service menu. The next morning we called down to the front desk to see if it was too late to order breakfast that was included in our package - the person that answered said it wasn't and to get "whatever you like". So we got a hold of room service and got two breakfasts (salmon and whitefish platters - not cheap at $25 each), one fruit salad, two oj's and coffee and tea. They brought it up to us and again gave us the bill ($108), we told them that we had the "tryst" package and that it was included. They acted like they knew nothing so we told them to call the front desk and have them explain that it was included.... getting frustrated at this point since our room cost about $400 per night you would think that room service and the front desk could communicate with each other. 
So.... that morning I go to check out and, of course, the bill has both of our breakfasts on it. Then after I explain about our "full american breakfasts delivered to our room" package the desk person brings it back to the manager. Apparently we had a $60 limit for each breakfast. We were supposed to have received a voucher when we checked in that explained that information (never received it). I explain to them that I never received it and didn't know there was a spending limit (which you would think they would explain to you when you check in or even when you book the reservation... in case your voucher isn't in the packet that they give you.) After 15 minutes of waiting around (and the next customer behind me checking out and having their breakfasts on the bill as well) I had to leave. The manager wasn't able to speak right then so he called me while I was in the cab - I explained myself that we never received a voucher. He said he couldn't do anything about it and that we would have to pay the difference in the amount - he was really not nice about it and basically made me feel like crap. I was really disappointed in their customer service which is why I'm writing this review. If he had been a little more flexible and understanding and offered to not charge for that extra $60 or so bucks (which there is about the cost of 2 oj's, coffee tea and a bagel) then I would be writing a much nicer review. The room was pretty - although the tv sound kept getting softer then really loud. The bed was comfy. The food was yummy. I just wish the people had been more accommodating and understanding. Beware if you book a package from them to get all the info ahead of time and know there is a limit on a "full" breakfast. Oh yeah, and get ready to spend some serious dollars.

title: “BED BUGS”
text:
I was staying in room 2221 and was bitten by bed bugs and also found them on my body. The Management did not really care and have made no effort in contacting me following my report. 
The previous night I could smell a strong toxic smell in my room and in the hallway, I am wondering whether they were already aware of the infestation and were spraying the rooms in advance. 
AVOID THIS HOTEL !!!

title: “The Crowne Plaza in Jacksonville is No. 1”
text: Our military reunion was held there in 2008...All attendees has a wonderful time. The front office staff, Director of Sales, and the rest of the staffers were great . The detail to service was outstanding. I highly recommend this hotel for reunions & leisure time.

title: “Great hotel with all the amenities, European feel and reasonable pricing.”
text: I have been staying at the Tuscan Inn for the last ten years, always in June in connection with an annual event in San Francisco that I participate in. The location of Fisherman's Wharf area made me suspicious, as the area is very "touristy". However, the Tuscan Inn has the best of all worlds- great location, all the amenities, excellent staff, nice restaurant adjoining, and very reasonable prices. They have guests from all over the world, and the tradition of wine tasting each evening makes for some great new acquaintances and friendships.

title: “Manager on Duty - Super attentive!”
text:
Great hotel with lots of amenities! While in Dallas for the State Fair of Texas, me and my co-workers stayed at this hotel and it was very accomodating to us. 
The manager on duty, Beth Pacheco, was absolutely amazing. She checked on us at dinner and even brough us chocolate when asked if they had anything sweet. I would definitely refer this hotel and hope to stay here again in the future.

title: “Don't even have to leave the building!”
text:
We booked Hotel Commonwealth through the Rue La La deal for a special night out. (We live just a few blocks away.) We have had visiting friends stay here so we were fairly familiar with what we were getting into, but we had even more fun than anticipated! 
We hopped from The Hawthorne to Eastern Standard and then back up to our room. The room was clean and good size. I LOVE the Fresh products in the bathroom. Definitely a great hotel and a great location.

title: “Perfect Location Nice Traditional Hotel”
text:
Our trip was for my hubbys 40th birthday, we wanted something central but also a bit special. After reading many reviews we settled for the Hotel Roosevelt on Madison Avenue in midtown Manhattan. 
We usually prefer modern comtemporary hotels however this one has a traditional grand feel with a very impressive lobby and foyer.
Firstly and most importantly is the location of this hotel, situated in midtown, very close to Times Square and Grand Central Terminal. We walked everywhere and did not require the subway/taxi at all. Walking distances to many great restaurants and all the hot spots.
On arrival we were given an upgrade to a fab very generously sized room on the 16th floor with a great view. The room itself was very very clean and our super queen bed was extremely comfy. Room cleaned and maintained to a high standard. The room was always very warm which suited us, however may be uncomfortable for others, there is air con. 
A couple of small gripes - the bath is very shallow and you cant have a soak, which after a long day sight seeing and walking is much needed!
No coffee/tea making facility however we requested a coffee maker and it was delivered promptly. Albeit we had to use paper cups !
Also we expected there to be an adaptor for our chargers etc, ended up buying one.
Lastly there is no fridge in the room for water etc, however we had an ice machine close by. 
The staff are super friendly and efficient and the hotel is a very good choice for a first time visitor to NY. We would definitely go back. Perfect for our requirements.

title: “Don't eat at the Red Rim if you stay here”
text: The Marriott Phoenix Airport itself was decent. The rooms were nice and the beds comfortable. We ate dinner at the Red Rim. It is supposed to be fine dining and the prices support that notion. The service was slow and inconsistent, however very polite. The food was not nearly at the same level as the price. I had the chicken stir fry that was supposed to come with brown rice. The chicken was tough and they gave me white rice. My wife's steak that was supposed to be medium rare, was medium, our daughter's cheese quesadia had chicken and other things it wasn't supposed to and overall the food quality was sub par. The manager did however take 25% off of our bill for all the mess ups and our complaints about the food.

title: “Great location and room”
text:
Great location, just a few doors down from Macy's and around the corner from Madison Square Gardens.
The room was spotless and had good facilities. The highlight was the king bed with adjustable firmness. 
Free wi-fi and gym facilities are also massive bonuses. 
Staff were friendly and attentive.

title: “Excellent”
text: Stayed for one night on a recent business trip. Great location. Good staff. Room enormous with a well appointed bathroom. Breakfast was very good too. Couldn't fault it. My new first choice for Boston FD.

title: “Staff aimed to please!”
text:
The hotel itself is a nice place to set up camp, but the staff was the best part of the whole experience. They desired to please the guest, and were very friendly. The front desk staff actually ordered my room service dinner when we returned from the football game, the girl who brought room service was really nice, and the bar staff was excellent. J W "Bill" Marriott himself would be pleased with the service here. 
The hotel itself is well kept, with a great and comfortable bar, good rooms, nice beds, and free parking, not to mention it's not very expensive. It may be tricky to find, (it's south of the Omni) but it's worth it.

title: “Las Vegas in Detroit”
text: Booked a room for my wife's birthday. We had previously stayed at the Greektown hotel/casino as well as the Motorcity hotel/casino, and were excited to finally get a chance to stay at the MGM, it didn't disappoint. Although compared to the other two Detroit hotel/casino's it was a little pricey. Everything you could imagine that you would want in a upscale hotel the MGM delivers. As other reviewers have stated the bathroom is almost worth the price alone.

title: “an excellent and less expensive option to a city centre hotel, yet only 3 blocks away”
text: I normally stay at either the Sheraton or Hilton on 6th Avenue in the heart of the city. This trip I tried this new property and was very pleasantly surprised. It is only a 3 block walk up Pike St from the Sheraton. The price is much lower, as is the parking charge. The full hot breakfast was great and not offered at either the Sheraton or Hilton. Fully equipped kitchens where helpful as well. I've found a new favourite place to stay in Seattle

title: “Excellent & Feinstein's To Boot”
text: Went there for the first time and was very pleasantly surprised. For NYC the price was reasonable. The service was excellent. We had booked an event at the Feinstein's night club which was amazing. What a great atmosphere. The only complaint is that they could use a face lift.

title: “amazing! already planning our trip back”
text: we recently stayed here for my birthday in november. with it being my birthday they upgraded us to a skyliner view room, with a free film to watch and I also received a lovely piece of cake that said happy birthday on, this was a lovely add to the stay. before we left for new york i was worried on what to think about the hotel because I had read bad things on this website, but we had nothing to worry about at all! it was an amazing hotel, with very friendly staff, the rooms were very clean and they made out beds everyday. we had four of us staying in one room and there was plenty of space. the shower was amazing..so big! the beds were also extremely comfy and I had no trouble getting to sleep. we had a lovely lady called paulina help book our stay and we couldn't thank her enough for how lovely they all made it. the day we left we needed a taxi back to the airport and the doorman arranged for the hotels car to take us! this was an amazing hotel and I can't wait to go back..also, brilliant location right next to times square x

title: “Classic NY elegance but not true luxury any longer”
text: This was my 10th time at The Waldorf Astoria and while one will still be seduced by its grand lobby and lovely shops I am truly convinced that the hotel needs some serious updating/refurbishment. My room was upgraded one level slightly larger (for which I was appreciative) as I had been the one who booked 15 other rooms for a group function. While the check-in process was very pleasant and my room size spacious, the rooms for our entire group were run down looking---carpets in need of cleaning and worst of all-- almost none of our heaters/air conditioners worked causing us to not sleep well due to the high temperature in our rooms. When I called for assistance the only option was to go from a very hot room to having the windows open and being very cold---to their credit they responded immediately to my request. On the plus side: Room service was delicious, courteous, prompt, in large servings and actually worth the typical hotel price for it. The housekeeping was friendly and efficient. The toiletries were plentiful (Ferragamo) and rooms were furnished with excellent linens and lots of towels. If you can get a very good price on the hotel it's worth it.

title: “Awesome hotel all around!”
text:
Beautiful Hotel at Seaport that is close to a lot of new fancy resturants such as Legal Seafoods, LTK, and Temazcal with great views of the water. 
Rooms are comfortable with added details such as Keurig coffee machine, heated mirrors in the bathroom, Bose alarm clock, and free WiFi. Beds are comfortable and rooms have great views of the port. Room service food is very good and delivery is very on point. 
A well equiped gym and a decent sized pool. The hotel also has bikes to rent so you can explore the neighborhood. Make sure to walk down seaport to Yankee Lobster and get their lobster plate or NE lobster roll. It's delicious.
Tip: The hotel charges for bottled water inside the room, however, there is a free beverage area in the gym with lemon or strawberry water, orange juice, and milk in the refrigerator that are free of charge.

title: “Great Value in Midtown New York”
text:
We stayed at the Affinia Dumont in January 2008 and had a very nice room on an upper floor which gave us views of the Chrysler Building and the East River. The rooms were large and comfortable - and even had a full kitchen. The pillow menu is a nice touch. For the price and location you cannot beat this hotel and we would stay there again. 
 Be aware that the Affinia Dumont is not really a luxury hotel (3 star max). There is no restaurant in the hotel - a real pain if the weather is bad and there was no concierge to assist us with dinner plans. The front desk did give us a list of the restaurants in the vicnity...but could not give any specific guidance.

title: “Worst hotel experience in 20 years.”
text: Police officers in lobby upon check in (should have taken this as a sign) and some bad event was just wrapping up. Not recognized as a Gold Points member. Wake up call the next morning not placed (or so I thought). In actuality, my phone in the room was not working at all. Breakfast bar was empty of most items at 7:30a.m. as I was leaving property for a meeting and no attendant was to be found. No newspapers for guests on any morning. Upon return that evening, I found a pile of some brown substance in the corner of my room and went down to the front desk to ask for housekeeper. I was informed that housekeeping staff was gone for the day. On way back to room, I found a housekeeper in the lobby and she went to my room to inspect and remove brown pile which turned out to be rotting meat. Hotel doors slammed all night on my floor and noise level left me with zero sleep for both nights I stayed at this property. Repeated requests to speak with a manager were ignored and I left my card for management to contact me and they still have not as of yet. Please do not stay at this property.

title: “Clean and comfortable room”
text:
We stayed here just one night, as we were having dinner in SF and didn't want to drive home (about an hour drive). The motel is on Lombard, right off Van Ness Avenue. We know what a busy area this is, so I requested a quiet room in the back, which they gave us.
It was very quiet. The bed was comfortable. The room was clean and it looked like the bathroom had been recently remodeled. The rate was very good, so it was perfect for our needs. Free parking too, which is a big plus in S.F.
I would stay there again.

title: “Take your chances”
text: Stay on fourth floor. Faulty electic, faulty AC, no hot water. Dorian, Sandy and Steve are great. Avoid others. Don't use the catering hall. Very unprofessional. Medeocre food at best. Untrained servers. Worst bar tender ever. Non accomodating. Stayed for a week and your stay will be good or bad depending on what room you get and what staff is working. Not consistent.

title: “Don't valet your car.”
text: I've stayed here several times for conventions and a couple times when visiting family in town. Most of my stays have been great. The hotel complex, rooms, restaurants, etc are top-notch. However, my last experience was soured tremendously when my bags were stolen out of my car in while it was parked int he garage (valet). There was no damage to my car - so the valet attendant must have either left it unlocked or one of the attendants participated in the theft. The hotel took no responsibility because they subcontract valet parking. The valet parking operation never returned my calls and gave me the runaround every time I called. They even accused me of making the whole thing up.

title: “Great value!”
text: There are a boatload of hotels on this strip of the Sam Houston tollway, and I've tried several of them, but this property is a gem! The rooms are large, the staff couldn't be friendlier, and the breakfast is huge & runs until 10 weekdays & 11 on weekends. I'm always in Houston the 1st weekend in February, and I plan to make this hotel a regular visit.

title: “Great location”
text:
The hotel is in central location.Very close to the shops and cafes.
The rooms are a bit noisy,you can hear everything , specialy slamming doors as they are made from very heavy metal and people come back at different time as NYC never sleeps.If you are not very light sleeper you would be fine.

title: “At the heart of Americas' number One city”
text:
Nice welcome, small basic room though - receptionist arranged an upgrade to a slightly larger one for $10 a day for our 7 day stay. They cater for transitory business travellers rather than vacationers. However, the position is close to city sights, restaurants, amenities, Chinatown and transportation. Breakfast in restaurant very nice although buffet at weekends not so good. Omelettes excellent! Pity the 3rd floor restaurant not open in evenings
Concierge service superb, reservations made in sought-after restaurants on our behalf. Would probably stay again next year.

title: “A Haven in the Bustling City”
text: The Intercontinental Brand is world renowned for luxury, service and taste. The Times Square location does not disappoint. It is unusual to find a luxury hotel this close to the Times Square area although several higher end properties are cropping up here and there (i.e., the Chatwal). The hotel is in an unusual location: a block west of the the main theater district. Yet, although it is a bit off the beaten path, this location is excellent for a pre or post theater stay. The staff is attentive and professional. Upon entering the lobby, your first greeting is by way of the lovely scent that wafts through the air. We were quickly greeted and thanked for our loyalty to the brand and enjoyed a sky view room on one of the upper floors. Although there were some families perhaps on holiday who may have needed to speak to their children about their "inside" voices versus their "outside" voices, we found the rooms to be quiet, clean, good size and welcoming. Don't remove anything from the minibar or the countertop--all are weighted and you will be charged once they are removed. The bathroom is spacious with an awesome shower, a large square sink--lovely towels and amenities. (there is no separate commode area). Beds are super comfy. Bedding is soft, lightweight and serene. Decided on breakfast at Cava: carrot juice, coffee, tea, great Belgium Waffles with pecan butter and berries, eggs, potatoes, meats---the usual fare, but generous portions impeccably prepared. Service outstanding. Prices are in keeping with the hotel star rating and NYC. The "self" parking is using the lot directly across from the hotel. The website and hotel says that this is $30 for 24 hours. (you get your ticket vouchered/marked at the front desk as you leave) We stayed 24 hours plus 4.5 hours and the total was $50. Not sure how this worked, but when you park in NYC, you pay--unless you arrive very early the morning, the pricing is usually very high. (FYI: valet is $60 with no in/out privileges per 24 hours) Highly recommend this property for the adult theater goers who are looking for a less frenetic property than those directly around Times Square. The Intercontinental is a gem!

title: “Beautiful hotel, great room, snooty front-desk service”
text:
We actually live in Chicago just a few blocks away from the Elysian but had the opportunity to spend a night at the hotel. Although our room was on a low floor with a view of a brick wall, the room itself was spacious, beautifully furnished, with a very comfortable bed and superb bedding. The pool and workout area are also very nice; we didn't check out the spa. 
I thought the front-desk staff was a little snooty. When we got there, right around our check-in time, we were told our room wasn't yet ready and that they would come find us in the waiting area when it was. After waiting about a half hour and 10 minutes past the designated check in time, I went back to the desk to see if our room was ready, and alas, it was. So, no one ever came back to tell us that our room was ready, and I think a 5 star hotel should offer better service. The hotel itself is beautiful, however, and in a great location for exploring the city.

title: “Basic Motel Accommodations”
text:
I'm not sure what other reviewers expected, but when you book a room in San Francisco that's under $200, you're going to get a basic motel. These accommodations are exactly that - motel-type accommodations.
Check in was slow - their clerks are not personable and seem to take forever to process a check in from a booked reservation. That said, there were no problems and I got a key that worked for my entire four night stay, with the bed type promised (king) and the location requested (main building).
The room was clearly updated within the last year or so, with a contemporary style - neutral, single color bedspread & curtains, modern wood furniture, etc. That said, the room could have been more clean - they need to clean the bathroom grout, the walls and the carpet. But the stains were not dirt - so I didn't feel as if I couldn't go barefooted. Bed linens were clean.
Continental breakfast was actually better than I expected - cereal, muffins, coffee and toast available. My alternative for this booking was the Travelodge Central, where they offer a single kind of danish for breakfast.
The location is excellent - I don't understand other reviews complaining of safety of the area. All I can think is that they've never stayed in downtown SF before. The street traffic / street scene is exactly what you find outside the Hilton and the Marriott . . . and SOMA is a very eclectic and vibrant area, with excellent restaurants within walking distance, some of the hottest clubs and bars (for both straight and gay clientel) and a five minute walk to the Civic Center BART station. Who could ask for more? There are homeless people EVERYWHERE in SF - so don't rate this motel down because they were outside the lobby. I actually didn't see any undesirables in the immediate vicinity - just local residents (people live all throughout this area) and workers (the Federal Building is two blocks away). Enjoy the eclectic nature of San Francisco and embrace the diversity!
All in all, a decent place - I booked for around $100 a night, so how could I complain? I got a decent motel accommodation in a great, vibrant location.

title: “nice property”
text:
Last weekend my husband and our 2 adult sons had adjoining rooms on the 11th floor across from the elevators. Quiet, clean, comfortable beds. I was puzzled when I found ear plugs and an eye mask on the bed. Then I found out why - sleep package. ok
The only noise came from the doorwall that did not seal. Nice balcony. We were there for our nieces wedding.

title: “Awesome service”
text: I stayed at this inn with my family for 3 nights. The location is good. Right at the pacific coast hwy, very close to shopping centers and car rental companies. we were given a very clean room with a flat tv and reasonable furniture.
