There was also free parking ;) the thing that i was so satisfied about was the service and the nice, awesome receptionist. He warmly welcomed us and thoroughly guided us with the questions about the city. He was always available for help and questions. Most importantly, i had a bus ticket to san diego the day after, and i could not find any place to print out my tickets. The receptionist printed out the tickets and he was so nice not to charge us! I was so satisfied with this place especially the room cleanness and the service. Oh yeah! I forgot the coffee in the morning! Free coffee was available 7-10 AM. Long story short, dont miss this awesome place.

title: “Great location”
text: The argonaut hotel is in a wonderful location. Staff are extremely helpful and very friendly. I stayed here for 2 nights before heading to Seattle. Although I was out all day and rarely at the hotel, the room was very cosy and I slept well in the comfortable bed. Afterr 2 cold nights the bath was a welcome addition. Also there was a lovely fire burning in the lobby when I got in both evenings and I would have enjoyed spending some time there sampling wine. I was in walking distance to the cable car and f line which made getting around town very easy. I would definitely stay here again. Join Kimptons to enjoy free wifi and a discount on the in room bar.

title: “Would definitely stay again.”
text:
I love the location of this hotel. Its right next to public transportation which we found wonderful since we didn't have a car. You do hear the trains when awake but we never heard them when we slept. We didn't have to use the earplugs that were supplied. 
Nandu was very friendly and helpful. 
The shuttle runs 6 AM to 10 PM. 
Maria (shuttle driver) was very helpful with information. She recommended Filiipis for the best pizza. It was the best pizza and located in Little Italy within walking distance. 
The shuttle has a daily schedule to the zoo for guests. It leaves at 10 am and picks up at 4 pm. 
Hotel was clean and housekeeping did a great job. 
Breakfast was good. Biscuits and gravy. Scrambled eggs with ham and cheese. Waffles. Muffins. Toast. Bagels. Etc. The dining area was clean and spacious. Plenty of tables. 
Jack in the Box is one block over. 
If you aren't overly sensitive to noise from the trains I would highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Relatively New & Very Good City Center Residence Inn”
text:
Flying to DIA, I made online reservation with Big Sky Shuttle for both my trip into downtown Denver and my return trip to DIA.
No problems, so I can recommend this shuttle company.
My check in was early, so my one bedroom suite was not ready so they offered me a studio on the top floor. Check in was friendly and welcoming. Sometimes the studio appear to be roomier because there is not that wall separating the bedroom from rest of the suite. This property is relatively new so everything looks good. The room was very clean and cleaned well each day I was there. Good size studio room was small kitchen, with breakfast nook. Small loveseat and lounge chair but in a fun positon. There was plenty of natural light in this room. Overlooking the courtyard. Bathroom was clean and water pressure was good and temperature was good.
My room was quiet and the bed was comfortable. The A.C worked well but was a bit noisy. The Residence Inn breakfast was better than most Residence Inns and there was plenty of room to sit and eat as well plenty of friendly staff helping around for the breakfast.
In the large lobby there are also two complimentary computer/internet stations. There is small gym with Precor machines and outside of the gym is a patio which features a hotub. Lots of smoking folks hang out there.
This property is just a few blocks from the 16th street mall. If you're reasonably good shape you can also walk to Coor's Field from this property.
The 16th Street mall, like some of the other reviewers have stated is nothing unique. Though there are plenty of souvenirs vendors located there and there are you're typical shops and restaurants you find in most cities. There are a fair number of street people around the open mall and some do ask for some change.
There is a free bus that goes in both directions of the mall.
At one end is the local and state govenment facilities and just a few streets from there down is the famous and historic Brown hotel (Where Obama and Clinton are staying for the DCC. 
 At the other end of the mall is Union Station and there are some good resturants down. Like the Wynkomp Brewing Company, towards Coors Field. Also further down from Union Station, a little bit of a walk of Convergence Park. A nice water park with a massive REI store there. 
I found the small but more unique Larimer Square more interesting than the 16th Street Mall. There is great coffee house there called the Market.
The convention center is walkable from the City Center Residence Inn. On the 16th street mall are several convenience stores nearby: 7-11, Rite Aid and Walgreens.
I took the Grayline City tour. My morning tour was cancelled because according to Grayline the bus driver called in sick.
So I took the afternoon tour. The tour bus can pick you up at your hotel if you call in advance. The bus then goes to the Cherry Creek Shop center (typical suburban upscale mall). 
The tour is not too interesting other than it gives you a good point of reference of how close many of the Denver offerings are from each other and accessible by light rain or bus. With Denver's very good public transportation system you get easily get to it's many sporting venues: Invesco Field at Mile High, the Pepsi Center and Coor's Field. 
There is huge condo buidling boom in downtown Denver, kinda of like downtown Seattle.
The weather in Denver was not too hot and plesant for August.
Many of the downtown eating establishment like Zeidy's Deli close during the weekend and primary cater to the downtown working commuters. 
My stay at the Residence Inn City Center was pleasant and Icannot think of any problems. I highly recommend this property if you need a base of operations and/or your business is downtown. A clean and modern facility with great staff and great location.

title: “Great Hotel near Indy!”
text:
I stayed at this Wingate for two nights on a business trip. It is very conveniently located close to the airport and just a 10 minute drive to local shopping and dining areas. My room was clean and spacious, and included a desk with a lamp and internet access, a comfy plus chair with an ottoman, a microwave and a mini-fridge.
I only have two minor complaints: the cable channels were somewhat limited, and two pieces of equipment in the exercise room weren't functioning properly: the stationary bike and the step machine. The treadmill and the weight machine were fine. (The fitness center, overall, was more than I would have expected, so I was quite happy about that!)
I didn't get the chance to try the pool or hot tub, but they looked inviting.
The breakfast area was large and well organized. I have to compliment the staff on their efficiency. When I stayed, the hotel was at capacity --- there was a convention going on that brought a TON of teenagers into the city, and many of them were staying at the Wingate. They were all well behaved, and the single staff member working the breakfast area really kept up with the high demand in the morning.
I would definitely stay here again, and in fact will request that my travel agent book a room for me here when I next come to Indianapolis.

title: “Business Trip”
text: This Marriott is a traditional corporate hotel and even to the extent that the weekend rates were very expensive.The only complaint I had was that the Concerige lounge was being renovated and the elevators were very slow. Be aware of parking a car, as it was very expensive as well.

title: “good place, good location”
text: Booked this room on hot-wire.com. It does have a great location and the place is in overall good condition considering its age. The only issue i had with the place was the size of the bed. but thats wasn't that big of deal. Check in was smooth and fast. People working at the hotel were freindly

title: “Great Time”
text: Recently stayed at the Wit and it was wonderful. Great service, great rooms and great location. Wonderful rooms with a great view in the corner suites, stayed on the 19th floor awesome view !! Near everyhing, the shopping, restaurants and bars. The Roof bar was a blast. Thanks for the great service, i will be back !! One thing, how about free internet??

title: “2nd time is even better...”
text:
This was my second visit to the Resort and it was just as good as the first, everyone is friendly including the other quests who visit with you as you were family. I had trouble deciding what dates to go and Katrina in reservations was very patient with me and always was so accomodating. I attended a Fung Shei lecture and loved the speaker, I tried the Tarot cards just for kicks and the guy was very professional and focused. The only not so 5 star experience on the property was the spa, I had a problem with my massage and Chris the manager promptly handled it but when I went back to the spa, Chris was gone and a female manager was in charge and she did not honor what Chris had said. I had just dropped 500.00 at the spa and she was un accomodating. All in all, Lake Austin Spa Resort is the Bomb, it is a must do for every women who needs to rejuvinate!
I cannot wait to go back next June!

title: “Stunning hotel in the perfect location”
text: We have just returned from a six-night stay at the Sofitel and were incredibly impressed. Everything - from the helpful and friendly staff, to the beautiful and spacious rooms, to the amazing location - was perfect. We could not have asked for more. The breakfast was delicious (although a little expensive), and every day we returned to our room to find our bed made, complimentary bottled water and chocolates and soft music playing on the Bose stereo. After spending our days taking in all the sights of New York, it was a real luxury to come back to the soundproof, relaxing room and get a good night's sleep in quite possibly the most comfortable bed I have ever slept in. The bathroom was stunning as well, and the L'Occitane toiletries were lovely. The entire hotel is also delicately scented with amazing smelling candles, and there is also free internet which was very useful. No complaints whatsoever. If you're looking for a luxury hotel in the heart of Manhattan, this is the one to choose.

title: “The Old Gray Mare”
text: We are 25 year customers. I'm sad. Our hotel has became very average. The walls and tub were dirty. Everthing seems so expensive, parking, $25. Average is $100 a couple with no drinks. Very rude bartender...we were scared not to tip her over our $4 coffee and a $4 coke. Room sevice is a joke....below average food has a $4 delivery charge and 19% tip included. Then the guy stands and waits for a cash tip. This hotel is not in the middle of the action. The greenery is so thick that a balcony room has lost its appeal. I'm looking for a new home away from home. I must mention that the people, other than the female bartender, try very hard and are extremely nice, but you can get that at most hotels. Good bye old friend, i must let you go.

title: “Very Kind People - Great Plaza Club Level Stay”
text: The Radisson Lord Baltimore was a short and safe walk away from the convention center. I stayed one week for a business trip combined with a couple of days of leisure. I was very impressed with the value of this hotel for the price. I stayed on the plaza level so that I wouldn't have to worry about breakfast. The breakfast was great and their evening appetizers and wine were filling and generous. I loved the downstairs bar food too. Everyone was so kind and helpful. The doormen and receptionist were great with providing directions to local flair as well as arranging transportation to the train station and airport. The building is old and rooms small but well kept. By the 2nd night I had found my right sleep number on their beds and rested well. It was easy to make the hotel home for the week.

title: “The staff were very helpful and polite”
text: The hotel was fine so we decided to stay the first night for our dinner. We had a steak for 2 with veg and 2 bottles of local beer. I was amazed at the cost. They charged $115. Some other members of the party had breakfast and was charged $48 for coffee and toast for 2.

title: “Not what I remember....”
text:
Since I have traveled a great deal, I always notice the details and service where I stay. It took almost an hour to check in at the hotel and then find a bellman to accommodate our luggage since our room wasn't ready. No one really cared that we were tired and frustrated...
This was a special trip to celebrate my sister's recovery from breast cancer. The "special" view I requested was "already given away" when we finally checked in. We were in the older section of the hotel which we liked but it didn't have any of the "special" products in the bath or a bathrobe which I always look forward too. The coffee maker had only papercups and no tea bags ( my sister likes tea). It just wasn't the luxury hotel we remembered. For the price we could do better in San Francisco around the Square.

title: “Great Location, Odd Hotel”
text:
I love a boutique hotel - as a matter of fact i prefer them. But this one was just odd. The decor is reminiscent of a hip hotel designed in the 90's - but I hear that this one is actually rather new, so I'm a little confused. 
The beds are quite comfy, so I'll give credit where credit is due. That said, the remainder of the room is eclectic to the point of annoying. The green dresser, the obnoxious book shelf stereo, the oversize lamps hanging over the bed, it was all just, well.... odd. And possibly trying too hard. 
But, to Kimpton's credit, I did just stay at their Eventi in NYC, which was awesome, so I wouldn't rule out Kimpton Properties, just maybe not this one...

title: “OUR HOME AWAY FROM HOME!!!”
text: Have stayed at this hotel 3 times now. I LUV NYC and Regency is our Home Away from home. Our last visit was Sept 2009 for our 10 yr wedding anniversary. Hotel team was Incredible. Attentive and a BOttle of Champayne waiting for us in our room to celebrate. This hotel is away from the hustle and bustle of Times Square and 7th Avenue (BUT a short walk away) BUT it is in a glorious location - Park Avenue!!! 2 mins walk to Central Park. We are travelling to NYC again this year and The Regency is already booked. Room sizes are Fabulous, one of the biggest in New York. Dont go past this hotel.

title: “Could not have been nicer”
text: Did online checkin and upon arrival went to the kiosk and showed the printout, swiped credit card and voila...the key was in my hand. No standing in the long line formed at checkin. Security is great with key access needed for the elevators. Beautiful room with comfortable bedding....Very nice buffet breakfast was available on site at Keatings.

title: “Old style charm at reasonable prices”
text:
After walking a few blocks from the metro and arriving at the 1920 art deco Hotel Lombardy building, we were welcomed by the smiling doorman and led us to the teeny weeny front desk area for check-in process. Check-in was swift since I used the advance pay option when reserving online (this saves quite a bit off the week day rates; AAA card offers tremendous savings off the weekend rate; sometimes same day rates seem deeply discounted too). However, during check in, we were not told the one very important feature every business traveler needs to know: Hotel Lombardy does not have a business center. Although there is a full service Kinkos behind the hotel with several kiosks, unfortunately you don't receive any discounts as a hotel guest. 
Now, back to the hotel: The guest rooms have two entrance doors -- the first is brown louvered wood that looks like a door that belongs on an old quaint ocean cottage and the second is the more traditional hotel door with magnetic access lock. 
I was pleasantly surprised at the size of the guest room. It was large enough for me to entertain a handful of classmates I invited over. My guest room had two double beds with plush bedding, a work desk, a dressing room with vanity (and two robes), gorgeous steel and chrome bathroom fixtures against a white tile backdrop, and a separate wet bar/dining room (with curtain door closure) the length of the guest room. I travel with ear plugs so the noise was no problem at all for me. Oh, by the way, there is no complimentary breakfast. But who cares? The location is surrounded by eateries and a two level Whole Foods. 
Oh, and the smiling doorman that led us to the teeny weeny front desk area for check-in process was there when we left. He was still smiling and working. But when he saw we were leaving, he placed the guest bags down, and the old style charming way, shook our hand and bid us a warm farewell.

title: “Awesomeness!”
text: Everyone was just very friendly and warm. We lost our documents in other Renaissance htl in NYC and one guy at the front desk was just very helpful and coordinated to solve the problem. The room was nice and spotless. Very convinience spot to go everywhere, even in the cold days...

title: “The "W" Stands for Worst in San Francisco”
text:
Where to begin? Maybe I should tell you that the W hotel San Francisco used to be one of my favorite hotels in the city. The rooms were stylish, sexy, comfortable and the public areas were lively, clean and attractive. Not anymore. It’s a design disaster! 
The second thing you should know is that the hotel is undergoing major renovation – major. A fact that we were never informed of at any part of our reservation process. There is no lobby and the makeshift check in area is truly deplorable. There are work lights, tarps, paint and pathetic “oops” signs everywhere – letting you know that acknowledged that problem. Maybe they could tell you about the problem before you book the hotel.
If the lobby wasn’t enough reason not to stay here – the remodeled guest rooms definitely are. The rooms are now a disaster of crappy furniture, white walls, tan carpet and broken plastic Buddha’s. As a designer myself, I have fallen in love with many W Hotels’ designs in the past—I understand and appreciate good design. This is not good design. The room looks like someone made a last minute dash to a Japanese version of IKEA and slapped crap on the walls, put together cheap furniture and left before it was finished. The room décor is a disaster. It is also pathetic to see remnants of the old décor still pathetically left behind: a dark wood headboard, a sink, a mirror, drapery tracks on the ceiling without drapes. None of it works. It’s hard to choose the worst element in the room. The freeform mirror glued onto the old headboard? The plastic Japanese “art” pathetically installed on the wall? Or maybe the random lamp balancing on the edge of the desk that obviously didn’t fit into its nook?
The new disastrous design also makes its way into the W restaurant Trace. Before I tell you about the restaurant, let me say the staff at the restaurant was excellent and the cuisine was very good. The restaurant is also a design disaster. If the challenge was to take a great space and break it into 17 cramped and uncomfortable areas—mission accomplished! The cheap looking décor looks like it came from the same Japanese IKEA and someone has the novel idea of making black wood cages in which to place the tables. Even the waiters complain about navigating the maze of cramped tables and black wood crates. There is also a “dot” pattern on the wall and windows, a theme that permeates the new areas, and it is annoying, tedious and already dated. Whew! 
In short, I would never stay here again and I felt truly ripped off. Something I usually have not felt at any other W hotel before.

title: “Absoluteley superb”
text:
We spent 8 days at the Castle Inn during June as part of our 6 weeks honeymoon of Hawaii and the west coast.
This motel/hotel has very little to argue against it. In fact we could think of nothing! Location is superb, bus stop just out on Van Ness, and the Powell Hyde cable car route two blocks along Broadway. We were staying for a week, so we purchased a $20 transport pass from the fishermans wharf cable car turntable, and with the bus and cable car options close by, the hotel is extremely well located, and in a safe area. The Thai restaurant on the corner was great and cheap, get the takeaway and bring back to your room. 
The Star of India around the corner has a buffet for $8 which was the best Indian we've had in a while.
Use the microwave to heat your left overs.
Versa and the other staff are a wealth of information. If we ever come back to SFC, the Castle Inn will be our place to stay without question.
David & Maria Burt, Wingan Way, Morwell Australia

title: “Your basic budget hotel at a good price”
text:
My wife and I stayed at this Red Roof in late March for 3 nights. The room was cleaned each and every day, with no complaints to be made on any of the days. We had a room w/ a king size bed, and working desk. The hotel had free wi-fi, which my wife took advantage of almost every day of our stay, and never had an issue with it. We paid a little under $50 a night.
 The location is decent. We went to a few different areas of Memphis, ( to be specific, we went to the memphis zoo, Beale St., Graceland, and the casinos in MS. during our 3 day stay) and this hotel was pretty convenient for all of our destinations. We stayed on the east side of Memphis due to the fact that we went to Nashville after our stay in Memphis and this location was convenient to our plans. Easy on and off the interstate. Their are plenty of places to eat nearby, from Ruby Tuesdays, and Shoneys, to fast food like Taco Bell, Churches Chicken, etc; all within a mile or two. We found a bar nearby called Good TIme Charlies, which was a fun place to hang and have a couple beers as well.

title: “Lovely Hotel, friendly staff and great location, I would stay there again!”
text: I really enjoyed the hotel. The staff was outstanding and parking attendants were great! The place was clean. This is a great location as I visited the Museum of Tolerance and this hotel was only about a mile away. I will be back.

title: “The Argent has gone downhill-watch out!”
text:
I have stayed at the Argent a few times before this visit and, while not a great hotel it does have a good location and have grown use to it, faults and all. However this last visit was just after an ownership change and it has gone downhill considerably. 
We changed rooms a couple of times and each had their own problem from elevator noise to clogged sinks. The thrid room we finally ended up in was a very small corner room that barely allowed us space to get around our luggage. I figured since we booked through expedia they didn't give us a choice of nicer rooms.
The usually terrific staff has been cut to the bone. There was never a bellman visable at the desk the entire weekend and the concierge was the worst I've ever come across. When asked to reccomend a restaurant they handed us an outdated list of so-so places and told us we had to call them ourselves! The only service they were eager to provide was a city tour. They must've asked us a half a dozen times to book one, even after we told them we'd been to the city numerous times. This is not "an award winning concierge team" as advertised. 
The room service food was late and cold. Our dirty tray sat outside our door until the late evening, along with numerous others. What's going on here? This hotel use to be nice but, no more for me. I come to SF a few times a year and will go to another hotel in the future. I would advise everyone to do the same.

title: “Would definitely recommend this hotel!”
text:
I was feeling some angst as the person who was doing the booking for our sister weekend. There would be 7 of us and some coming from other parts of the country. I needn't have worried! This hotel was in a very good location, within walking distance to everything we had wanted to see. 
The staff was very friendly and helpful. We had asked for rooms close together and not only did we get that but had adjoining rooms - plus a bonus of one being a suite with refrigerator, microwave & stove!

title: “Clean and Close”
text: We were in town for the Oriole's - Yankee game over the weekend and had a very nice, clean room on the third floor. The room was smaller than other Marriott's we've stayed at, but clean is what counts. The hotel is a 10 minute walk to the water - perfect considering how crowded and noisy the harbor area can be. The staff were very nice and the housekeeping checked in on us the first day to ensure that we had everything we needed. If you go for a baseball game this is also a perfect spot - Camden Yards is literally across the street. Overall a great time - the only bummer was that the service in nearly every restaurant was poor. The Wharf Rat was the best of them all. La Tasca the worst.

title: “fine hotel but desolate location”
text: Stayed at this hotel because it was within walking distance of a tradeshow I attended but, that was the only thing that was within walking distance in this sterile area of town. The lobby is big, nice, modern and airy. The rooms are nice and comfortable. Staff somewhat aloof and cool but I've read in other reviews that this is typical of Boston. You are on your own if you want a taxi.

title: “Great location!”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for 4 nights in total. The hotel is in a great location, with the magnificent mile less than 5 minutes away!
There is builiding work being done on the hotel, but it didn't bother us, the bar and breakfast area were closed because of this but 'West Egg' a few blocks away was fantastic for breakfast. We ate there every morning of our stay. 24 hour store across the road from the hotel does rather nice snacks, such as sandwiches and pizza, and of course sells alcohol! 
The room was of a decent size, and was clean. The bathroom was small, but again, clean. 
I would stay here again, as the location is fantastic. 
We had no bother in Chicago, we felt very safe.

title: “Swank and class”
text: There are some hotels that are just too hip for their own good. Dream is elegant and modern, but not too over the top hipster. It's not cheap, but it is lush and comfortable. The whole place has a feeling of decadent romance due to the materials used...fabrics, wood, steel. All very well executed.

title: “brilliant location”
text: just got back from newyork this week i was very worried about this hotel after reading some reviews before i went but found nearly nothing wrong with the place it is well positioned 10 minutes walk to times square which is ideal and subways were very close to. the rooms were very clean and the bed made everyday and the towels changed everyday what more could you want we also had a bonus of having a great view of the empire state building out of our window. I must admit i did find that (some) of the staff weren not to friendly but most of the others were helpfull enough. i would stay there again because at the end of the day your in newyork to visit places and enjoy yourself and not to sit and find faults with places maybe i was out to much and didnt pick them up but i was satisfied with the place so i wouldnt read to much into the other comments go and enjoy yourself NEWYORK IS FAB and the skyline isnt to bad either

title: “Returning to our Chicago Home :)”
text:
The Staff
This was our second stay in this hotel and we chose it because we loved it so much last year. From the moment you walk in you are treated very well by the valets. We pulled up to the curb in front of the hotel and the valets immediately took care of our bags and car. Since we arrived earlier than check-in they had no problem storing the bags for us until our room was ready. When we checked in the front desk staff was extremely friendly and talkative like they've known you forever. Throughout our stay we were greeted with smiles from everyone. I was there for business so when I left the hotel every morning the valets asked how I was doing and told me "It is so nice to see you!" My husband and daughters left the hotel everyday to visit the museums and the valets treated them like family, instructing them on which direction to go or which buses to take. We finally saw the server in the breakfast room, Connie, who we fell in love with last year. She actually remembered us and asked my husband how his job was going. Her daughter is working there now and is just as sweet as she is, she looks just like her too! Overall the staff cannot be beat. Every evening the manager stood out in the lobby and talked to guests as they came in and out to get coffee. I love being treated like I am not only welcome there, but wanted there.
The Room
The room was perfect and large with a living room, kitchen and a king bedroom with a bathroom. The kitchen had a stove, microwave, full size refrigerator, sink, and dishwasher as well as dishes for four and pots and pans. Both the living room and the bedroom had large flat screen televisions with quite a few cable channels, we settled on the Food Network and HGTV for most of our stay. The bed had many different blankets to suit your needs. The main comforter was like a big pocket with a down comforter in the middle of it. Underneath that was a large fleece blanket and then a regular sheet. There were 6 pillows provided on the bed as well as an extra one in the closet. The pullout sleeper sofa came with a fitted sheet and flat sheet as well. At night it was like having two bedrooms with us in the king bedroom and the kids on the sleeper sofa in the living room. The provided toiletries were high class instead of generic hotel soaps. The shampoo, conditioner and body lotion were all Bath & Body Works Rain-kissed leaves, and the soap was a Neutrogena bar. There was also a USA Today newspaper left at our doorstep every morning.
Amenities
In addition to the wonderful staff and the modern and spacious rooms, this hotel comes with many great amenities. The indoor pool and fitness room are on the 19th floor surrounded by windows on three sides- you can imagine the downtown Chicago view! The pool goes from 3 feet to 4-1/2 feet deep and is surrounded by lounge chairs and tables and an unlimited supply of towels. Free coffee, hot chocolate, tea, and water is provided in the lobby at all times (24/7) and is great for raising your energy level to explore the city. The extra touch of providing flavored creamers in addition to regular creamer for the coffee is wonderful, I love my coffee with french vanilla creamer. The free breakfast is worlds above any "continental" breakfast served by other hotels. The menu changes slightly daily, but usually includes cook-yourself waffles, vanilla yogurt, granola, fruit, oatmeal with various toppings, toast, bagels, and then various hot items such as steak and eggs, bacon, sausage, or fried potatoes. There is also a free dinner Monday-Thursday with different themes each night. During our stay we had an Italian night, a French Quarter night, a mexican night, and a barbecue burgers night. Free wine and beer as well as lemonade, tea, and water is served with these meals. In addition to the main entrees they also include soups, sides, salad, and yummy desserts. There is free wifi which is pretty reliable, I only had trouble a couple of times. If you don't have your own laptop they also have a business center with desktop computers set up where you can work, check your email, or print your documents. The front desk also has a little 24 hour convenience store where you can pick up a coke, toiletries, or other miscellaneous items. If you forget any of your toiletries from home they will provide them for you at no cost. We had forgotten our toothpaste and my husband went down to buy some but was offered some Colgate packets for free instead.
Location
The location of this hotel is fabulous. It is just a block from Michigan Ave and is surrounded by many restaurants. Within a 1 block radius were restaurants like Buca di Beppo, PF Changs, Chipotle, Jimmy Johns, Weber Grill and more. The grocery store is a Jewel-Osco located a block and a half west of the hotel on State Street. It's an easy walk to Oak Street Beach on the north side of Michigan Ave and Millenium and Grant Parks on the south side of Michigan Ave. You are also just three blocks from the river that runs through the city and the River Walk. There is a free trolley stop for Navy Pier right in front of the hotel and a plethora of bus stops right on Michigan Ave to get wherever you need to go. Bus 10 takes you to the Museum of Science and Industry, 146 takes you to and from the Museum campus with Field Museum, Shedd Aquarium, and Adler Planetarium. Bus 151 takes you to the free Lincoln Park Zoo.
Issues
One of the two elevators went out of service while we were there. It took a little longer when waiting for an elevator to arrive. However, the staff went out of their way to offer the service elevator in the back to guests from the lobby on the 6th floor or the entrance on the 1st floor. During the weekend they also extended breakfast hours so that no one would miss out due to the elevator issue. They made it very clear that they were doing everything they could to ease the inconvenience of the non-working elevator. We had a corner room on the 7th floor (room 716) which was right next to the stairwell. You could hear people walking up and down the stairs and it got really loud if kids or multiple people were using them at the same time. It didn't bother us but some people are more sensitive to noise. I'm sure the stairs aren't used often when the elevators are working.
Overall this hotel has everything you could ever need and you can't find a better staff anywhere. It's nice to be treated like family when you are on vacation. You get the true feeling of being home away from home. We look forward to our next stay!

title: “spacious, clean room, good location”
text:
Stayed here for 5 nights. Room was very clean, staff courteous. The amenities are great - it's spacious, almost like a studio suite. The microwave, sink, plates and mini fridge (not minibar!) let you do a bit of in-room cuisine, which saves on cost and lets you control more of what you eat (for the health-conscious). 
TV gets a ton of movie channels, wireless internet is free and there's a little desk for your laptop.
Room gets street noise - especially thursday and friday night - people on the streets below were partying pretty loud.
Didn't try the continental breakfast, but it's part of the amenities.
This is a great deal. I'd stay here again if I traveled back to San Francisco.

title: “Heartily Recommend”
text:
We stayed at the Salisbury for 5 nights, and were very pleased. We had requested a room on an upper floor and at the back, and we received a great one - at the end, so no shared wall by our bed. The
weather was hot during our trip, so we needed to run the window air conditioner in the room, which worked well and also drowned out any noise. The mattress was firm and comfortable, and we slept great. 
Our room had a little alcove with a microwave and fridge, which we had requested, and made good use of. The closet space was great, there was an in-room safe, and we had lots of floor space. The photos
posted here accurately reflect the decor and overall style of our room. We were on the 17th floor, and yes, twice we had to wait for the eleveator for maybe 3 or 4 minutes, but most other times, it was there in under 2. 
The room was clean, water pressure good, and the staff very friendly and responsive. We ate breakfast only once at the hotel, and agree that $4 is a very reasonable price for it. Apparently this fall they
started charging (?). The rest of the time we bought food at a good sized grocery store one block to the west. Others have commented on the convenient location, and we concur.
The only drawback we had was that they had redone our bathroom and had made it what I call a European style, with a drain but no lip or ledge, so the water went all over the floor, as they had not sloped the tiles at all toward the drain. We were able to solve that by asking for extra bathmats or towels, and we built a dike with them which worked fine. The maintenance guy we talked with the first morning said "they did it wrong" so who knows how many rooms are like
that and what the hotel will do to solve it. To some people, this might sound like a major issue, but to us, since we were happy with the room otherwise, and we had already unpacked, we were content to deal with it. 
There's a subway stop at either end of the block. We bought an unlimited 7 day pass and definitely got our money's worth - we went all over, in addition to walking a lot. We took a taxi only from the
airport and back, and we got two very nice drivers.

title: “A hidden gem in San Fran”
text: I found out about this hotel through the Trip Advisor website. We got a great deal for the Memorial weekend and paid significantly less than other hotels. If you are looking for posh, this hotel isn't it, but what it is is clean, well managed, convenient and perfect for anyone wanting to be close to everything. There were tons of actvities within walking distance and easy access to most sites. The free parking was great and it was nice to know we always had a spot. The free treats for breakfast were appreciated and the management was always available with a friendly smile. Varsa did a great job arranging a tour and the management really went to bat for us when the tour group did not pick us up. They were on the phone immediately and made sure all of our needs we met. I highly recommend this spot as an affordable and convenient place to spend the night when in San Fran.

title: “Excellent!”
text:
Stayed there just to attend the first playoff game of the AL Series and thought the hotel was terrific. We had a large suite (two queens and a fold out couch) which was spacious and comfortable. Check-in was easy and it was nice to be able to have a valet park the car overnight ($32 but worth it).
The hotel was comfortable walking distance to Camden Yards (even in the rain), and was close by to a number of bars and restaurants. The complimentary breakfast was the usual Hampton Inn style, and just what we needed. What to come back and try this for a longer visit.

title: “Small but good”
text: On a fun street with funky bars and clothing boutiques, the Comfort Lower East Side is a great pied-a-terre in Manhattan. Close to Little Italy and China Town, but also close to the Metro, it is a relatively good value for NYC. The staff were also friendly and helpful. The free continental breakfast, however, is not worth it. Grab a sandwich at Starbucks on Delancey instead.

title: “Top notch everything!”
text: We stayed 2 nights and were very pleased with the size of the room(king executive) the bed was extremely comfortable, we had a sitting area and being a "Select member" their rewards program got us free morning beverage room service. We ate at Juliette's the onsite restaurant and had a glass of wine at JBar,staff was friendly and very helpful! Located right downtown Jacksonville it offers easy access to the beaches and lots of shopping near by.

title: “Lovely setting for a vacation!!”
text: The layout of the room was wonderful. We stayed in a bayside bungalow and were able to take advantage of the refrigerator and microwave. We liked the two dressing areas on either side of the bathroom. The room was comfortable and felt just like home. Can't wait to come back.

title: “Did not disappoint”
text: I stayed at this hotel a few months ago on a business trip, usually I have little say in where i stay, but I was given the choice on this trip, and after consulting trip advisor, I went with The Lenox Hotel. I have to agree with the high rating, the hotel is in a perfect location, right next to the T, and allowed me to feel at home while i was in a city I rarely visit. The free wifi was a plus as I had work to do, and the concierge was great in his dinner recommendation, and helpful with directions as well. Would love to stay in this hotel when I'm in Boston again!

title: “Our Vacation in Austin, TX”
text: My Boyfriend and I decided to take a vacation to Austin, TX this year. Thanks to the friendly staff @ Howard Johnson we were able to find many things to see and do. The breakfast was great in the mornings and the rates are reasonable. I would absolutly Recomend this hotel!!

title: “Clean, Great Location, Fantastic View”
text: My husband and I just had an overnight get-away in Chicago. We found the Holiday Inn Mart Plaza to be an ideal central location for walking about the city. We did a lot of walking. Especially nice was its close proximity to night life and restaurants. The hotel was clean and spacious. The concierge and bell hops were very helpful. We would definitely stay there again.

title: “Perfect!”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Omni for 4 nights and we didn't have any complaints. The hotel is a little on the pricey side, but worth the money! (sometimes it is nice to splurge!). The location is in the financial district but within walking distance to a lot of places - and public transportation will get you to a lot of places, as well. The staff was helpful, when we asked questions, and the rooms were very clean. I would definitely stay here again!

title: “Stay was decent, but dealing w/ staff was AWFUL”
text:
This hotel booked my reservation wrong
Double charged me for my room
Said they refunded the amount (they didn't)
They accused me of calling their AGM a FAG after they were the ones who were extremely rude to me and my banker.
Even their head of operations in Detroit was rude and said his employees dont lie and they have recordings of the conversations (that's a lie because I said no such thing and if they could listen to the conversation they would know that!)
Everyone there with the EXCEPTION of George Monahan was extremely rude. They were not apologetic for what they did wrong and kept hanging up on me. I already have anxiety/depression and the way they treated me left me in tears.
I will be speaking with my lawyer... in fact I already have.
Don't stay there. It is not worth it.

title: “Walk sideways entering your room...”
text: and stay that way because the room is absolutely tiny! Bathroom, too, retrofitted into a high-ceilinged ex-post office upstairs room. If you can deal with that, then prepare for outlandishly-priced breakfasts which ran something like $25 for pancakes and a glass of OJ, and nouveau-cuisine dinners that leave you starving and headed for Rosa Mexicana down the block for chips, guac, and an affordable drink. The hotel's location is however excellent, and rates aren't over-the-top, with the bar, restaurant and lobby nicely appointed and well-staffed, offset however by the three or four bellmen or car attendents who are constantly hanging-out directly at the bottom of the hotel's narrow front stairway. Overall OK for a night if you're alone or have to be in that locale, otherwise rob a bank and fold yourself in half.

title: “Staff is amazing..”
text:
This is a nice place to stay if you are in the area. The staff is great and very accomodating. Denise mentioned Ivory, and she is very kind and helpful. She will go out of her way to make sure you are satisfied. I was impressed with her hospitality. 
The king room I had was huge. Everything was functional and comfortable. There are several good restaurants surrounding this property including Salt Grass, Pappasito's (Unbelievable. Try the Mexico City chicken soup. It comes with white meat shredded chicken, rice, diced avocadoes and cilantro. It rocks. They also have a warm salsa with a bit of a kick.), and Chilis. Sorry, I digress. I get caught up when talking about food. 
I was pleased with my stay here. I really don't have any complaints, but maybe a suggestion. The lighting in the room is all fluorescent and it's just a little stark for my taste. It feels like being in the office. I know that the pressure is on to convert to energy saving mercury-laden bulbs, but I'm still having a problem with it. Maybe it's just me. It doesn't feel homey. Maybe others like it...I don't know. Personally, I still enjoy the warm, cozy glow of an incandescent bulb. To each his own. I just turn the lights out and open the window.
I would recommend this property without hesitation.

title: “Great find!”
text: We stayed at the Morgans in May for a weekend. We come to NYC at least once per year. We always look for bargains, and so we found the Morgans. It's a very nice hotel, apparently with a lot of European guests. Rooms are a bit funky/artsy and have a very comfortable feel. We got a superior room and had a view of the Empire State Building. The staff was very friendly. Unusual for NYC: the hotel offered a good complementary breakfast. Our main complaint was the construction on Madison Ave, with steel plates on the street; although we were on an upper floor, we could hear trucks and buses rumbling over them. But maybe that was the reason for the bargain, in a city that never sleeps...

title: “a perfect hotel,even via hotels.com”
text:
Based on other travellers reviews I was expecting this hotel to be a hit or miss. Since I've booked with hotels.com i was expecting,as usual,an old,worn out room with no view. When asked to have a better view the lady at the front desk gave us a city view wich was really fantastic. Ok no fireworks,but the view was stunning anyway. The hotel has still that '80 feelings that does not bother when clean and rightly updated. You can actually notice this place has gone tru renovation more than once in the public areas. The staff was very attentive,especially in the grill restaurant/cafeteria.
The rooms are in a word HUGE,very clean and well kept. A little bit on the darkish side maybe. Bed was just ok,I was expecting a bit more from a Westin Heavenly bed. It turned out that it's the same mattress I have at home ( Sealy) just way bigger...
I'm not fancy about Seattle,but If it will happen to go back there this will be my place to stay.

title: “Nice hotel”
text:
We stayed in this hotel last week for two days and enjoy it very much. It's really close to the airport and you can call for their free shuttle from the airport.
The breakfast was good and not that basic, It included eggs, bacon, pancakes, fresh fruits and bread.

title: “Exceptional in every way”
text:
We recently chose to stay at The Allegro for 8 nights to celebrate our 1st Wedding Anniversary (and attend Lollapalooza). From the grandeur of the foyer and lobby, to the friendly welcome and complimentary upgrade, we were treated, upon arrival, exceptionally well. 
The suite was gorgeous - tastefully decorated and the size of an apartment - perfect for a long stay. The decor was both visually interesting and of a high-quality; and let's not even mention how comfortable the bed was - we are intent on finding out the brand to buy one for home! 
During our stay the housekeeping service was of a very high standard and our every request (such as requiring a make-up mirror and coffee maker, to the complimentary shoe shine service) was seen to with efficiency and professionalism.
The 'Wine Hour' was a real point of difference to other hotels - and a wonderful way to sample different wines and beers, while socialising with other guests.
While The Allegro is a social hotel - for those that choose to enjoy the services and amenities - it is also very private - a welcome retreat in the busy entertainment district of downtown Chicago.
Overall we highly recommend the hotel and can't wait to visit again on our next trip to Chicago.

title: “great hotel, location, watch for erroneous charges”
text:
I dont normally write such reviews but I felt I should paint a picture of this one
great location right next to Union Square and shopping, Starbucks in the lobby open late.
friendly relaxed helpful staff on the desk
great pool/gym area especially for kids
their only restaurant was a bit expensive and didnt really cater for kids (except for the buffets)- room service we were told was sandwiches only after 11pm
watch out for the automatically charging mini bar - touch anything and its charged to your room (not good when you have kids)
room was a good size because I asked for 2 beds but we could see from the floor plan that most of the others on our floor were really small.
be sure to check for erroneous charges even after you have left...we arrived unexpectantly late in the early morning as our original flight was cancelled and even though we had paid in full in advance we were charged a "no show fee " of $225 some 10 days afterwards and unbeknown to me.....then had some difficulty contacting accounts to sort it out (11 international phone calls UK to US + various emails over 4 days costing me alot of money) - dont bother leaving voicemail or emailing them as no one ever returns them....I was then told that there had been an error on their web site charges and I hadnt been charged enough for the room!!

title: “Not a hotel chain--quaint, beautiful, friendly!”
text:
This resort is outstanding for any conference needs. The grounds are beautifully maintained, the food is excellent and everything is spread out so you never feel cramped. Rooms are nicely furnished, no saggy beds. Numerous outdoor pools. Trellises restaurant is wonderful with a fabulous staff but ask for Pati for the best service!
Not a place to bring young children since not much for them to do on site except pool. Resort has shuttles and nearby trolley that takes you to local attractions and into other parts of San Diego. Hotel is connected via walkway to a large outdoor mall with lots of large chain stores, restaurants and movie theatre.

title: “awesome weekend!!”
text:
went with my daughter had a really good time got the 48 hour hop on hop off tickets for the bus tour a must for new York very informative guides we even had a lady who sang songs on the way round! 
when you book into this hotel they ask for your credit card and take out $100 straight away failing that you have to give them a deposit in case you have any extras, we didn't as out in room mini bar was locked!! 
the radiator was hot all night this was a bit disturbing as the radiator was unplugged! 
every thing else was grand we had breakfast at a restaurant across the road called moonstruck it was very reasonable and rather large portions! 
my advice to any one going to new York who wants to see the sights pre book on-line before you go especially for the empire state building saves nearly two hour wait in queues

title: “Basic Nothing-Fancy Hotel”
text: Great location! Four Points by Sheraton LAX is right next to LAX. The room is clean and spacious, but nothing fancy. Service was not bad, but nothing special, either. If you are looking for a basic hotel room with a flat screen TV, clean bathroom and comfortable bed, then this hotel is a good choice. But, beware of the parking fees: you have to park at the parking structure across the small street from the hotel. It seems that the parking service is run by a separate company. Their space is tiny and crowded most of the time.

title: “Rude woman on front desk.”
text: We booked a room with two beds for myself, husband and child for three nights. When we arrived we were very rudely told that we had two separate rooms with one bed in each for the first night (as the carpet had been cleaned) and would be expected to change for the second night. This resulted in my husband being in a one room and myself and child in another. I was not happy about this as we had booked months in advance. The woman at front desk continued to be rude each time I spoke to her. Besides this very rude woman, I really enjoyed the rest of the hotel, which was clean with an excellent breakfast choice.

title: “Thank You Habitat!”
text: This hotel is a GREAT value! If you are traveling with kids it can't be beat. Our room was huge! There were two comfortable king size beds in seperate bedrooms, two full baths, and a pull out sofa in the "family room". Our family of 5 was quite comfy there. The kitchenette is a bit dated but who cares? I was delighted that is was all clean and working! But by far my favorite thing about Habitat is the price. Our room including taxes but minus our Go Austin card discount was only 146.05 per night. If you take into account what the incredible hot breakfast would have set us back (50.00 easily) this is an amazing bargin. Thank you Habitat. We had a wonderful stay!

title: “LOVE this place ! so much !”
text:
I cannot overstate how great this hotel is. Ignore all those bad reviews - I think those people either had a bad day or were a little rude themselves. If you go in here, smile and have fun with the staff, it will be youru best hotel experience ever !!! (Some of those other reviews are old, too, and I can say from personal experience that new managers have made this place SHINE !! It just keeps getting better ...) 
The rooms are so beautiful, with the most sumptuous king sized beds and fabulous sheets. Something like a million thread count ! You will get into that huge comfy bed and not want to get back out. So order room service - the food is awesome (a little pricey, like ALL room service, but so worth it ! Live it up a little !) and stay IN ! 
The last time I was here with my girlfriend, it rained all day and we didn't even care. We went to a great little Thai place right across the street and ate in and watched movies and just enjoyed the wonderful room !!!
Super clean, a great location, beautiful lobby and restaurant - this one of the best hotels I have ever stayed at, and the only one I even think about in SF.

title: “Overall a wonderful experience”
text:
As I sit at the B.C. pool....full tummy post breakfast, I feel compelled to write this. 1. To share my great experience and 2. To quiet the prejudice regarding staff.
Overall, my experience is great...beautiful resort (would be perfect if bathrooms were upgraded). Great proximity to downtown Austin and Lake Travis (yesterday's excursion). Beautiful golf course (inspired to learn...booking lessons today). Just a peaceful place.
For all the disappointed folks...I am a foodie and the menu is reasonably tasty....fresh with generous proportions. The comment regarding foreign staff is just a reflection of a poorly traveled guest who can't appreciate Texas's multicultural make-up. Please keep this in mind when you read the skewed reviews.
My score is 4/5 only because of my bathroom.

title: “Nice hotel; helpful staff”
text:
This hotel is attached to the new convention center in Boston which was convenient for us since we were attending a meeting. The hotel itself is lovely; very modern. Room was quite nice. We found the staff to be very friendly and helpful throughout.
It is not located in the most exciting area in Boston, but there are some interesting places along the South waterfront and the jogging map provided takes you by and on the fishing piers. It is not far to Back Bay and restaurants. There is an Irish bar type restaurant in the lobby which was good.
Would recommend

title: “Excellent Stay in Boston”
text:
Just got back from a mini trip to Boston. We booked this hotel based on the location, as we wanted to be close to the food and shops. We were not disappointed. The hotel is in the best spot in the North End; you can't beat that for the money! Steps away from Quincy Market, the water, and the subway. Our room was big, modern and comfortable, and had all the amenities we needed. The staff were friendly and extremely helpful.
We appreciated the convenience of the valet parking, but it seemed expensive at $45 a day. It was also great that the hotel let us check in early, but they also charged a $12 early check in fee to park. Our only other complaint was that there didn't seem to be any soda machine or ice machine anywhere in the hotel. 
Those small things aside, we will definitely return to this hotel and are already planning our next trip to Boston!

title: “Hotel/concierge service par excellence”
text: We planned a day trip to Seattle from Vancouver BC but since the weather and road was getting icy getting back we decided to stay overnight.Decided on this hotel since I have stayed at sixth avenue inn years back. We inquired at the front desk for availability and price. The professional and friendly staff really provided us more than what I would expect in terms of how we were given a good drop in rate for two rooms.The room was very comfortable , well maintained and quite. Overall I am impressed with the hotel with a very competitive price/comfort than staying in an exorbitant priced hotel in downtown area.

title: “Excellent place to stay with young children”
text: The hotel staff was extremely attentive. Our luggage came up to our room about 30 seconds after we arrived at the room. Anytime we asked for something, it would take literally minutes for someone to wisk it up to the room. We were also upgraded to a suite (used starwood points for booking) and had a roll-a-way bed which turned out to be a full size bed. This was perferct for our 4 and 6 yr old to share. We had a beautiful view of the bay bridge. The hotel was also extremely convenient. It was about a 4-5 block walk to North Beach. Great Italian restaurants, however they are also very close to all the strip bars. Also a short walk to the Ferry Building which has a lot of wonderful little gourmet restaurants and food shops. The fitness center was also well equipped with earphones and TVs hooked up to the treadmills (which is convenient to work off all the food you will consume during your stay in S.F.) Overall, a wonderful weekend family getaway. We look forward to coming back again. Only drawback is the price of parking, but that's par for the course in San Francisco.

title: “Great Place for Business or Pleasure”
text: I have stayed at the Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers for several years for business and have enjoyed each of my stays with them. They are a pleasure to work it and have made me feel welcomed each and every time I have been a guest there. It is so refreshing to be greeted by doorman and the front desk staff because they know you and make you feel like family. Working with the professional staff in planning a major conference is refreshing; they are open to new ideas and have great suggestions to make your event a success. I was there for five nights and enjoyed each one of them. It is also a nice place to unwind after a long day. You will love the beds, you will sleep like a baby! The location is amazing and close to many restaurants and great places to shop. The hotel is well maintained and very clean; you can tell the staff takes proud in there work.

title: “YOU COULD NOT PAY ME ENOUGH TO STAY HERE!!!!!!”
text: I warn you condition of this hotel is nothing like it appears in the promo photos on this site. Believe me the photos need to be updated to reflect the actual condition of this deplorable establishment! It is dirty and very, very run down and is located in a bad part of town! The elevator is one step above a dumb waiter with a manual door and it is so small it is over crowded with one passenger and one suitcase. We made our reservations in advance through choisehotels.com using my VISA to confirm and hold our reservation. When we arrived we were treated like we were low lives renting the room by the hour by the hotel management who demanded we fork over a $20 CASH key deposit. After refusing to pay the $20 cash key deposit and using the antique elevator to get to the third floor and then seeing the deplorable condition of the room we decided not to stay and immediately checked out NEVER TO RETURN!

title: “Phew!!!!!”
text:
lbertsons are a 3min drive away. Can't think of anything the supermarket didn't sell, apart from proper baked beans, but then you can never get them in the states!
We ate at The Keg, both the steak & the salmon was delicious. We also tried The Bamboo Club - a wide variety of asian dishes on offer. Did not eat at the JW but Roy's looked superb.
Very,very hot the entire week but you know before you go so be prepared. Will not be returning - there are too many places out there still to visit, but would recommend both the MCV & Arizona.

title: “Very nice hotel but a few small problems”
text:
Our family (two girls 10 and 13) went on a quick trip to Chicago and spent one night at the Park Hyatt. I booked a Park View room with the AAA discount which includes breakfast. There are plenty of workers to help you as you pull up and get your luggage. They ask your name and escort you to the front desk where they tell that worker who you are. 
 I was thinking that we might want to upgrade to a suite since I wasn't too happy about sleeping in double beds so I inquired at the front desk if one was available. I would have booked this earlier but how many people could occupy each suite was very unclear on the website and I even called to ask but that person was not any more helpful about whether we could all fit (or if rollaways are allowed). I was told that no suites were available at the front desk but was given a complimentary second room that connected to the other room! The only little problem with this arrangement was that we had no view. But having two king size beds and two bathrooms was great!
As mentioned by other reviewers, the rooms are very nice. My husband LOVED the chair in the room it was so comfortable! The baths were big enough for two so my crazy two daughters put on their swim suits and had fun with the bubble bath that was kindly given to us along with an American Girl doll bed when a worker saw my younger daughter carrying an AG doll in the lobby!
Other perks were complimentary movies (although they are quite old) and free apples and water. However, there were a bunch of other munchies near the water with no note to suggest whether these were also complimentary or not. I think anything that has a cost should be listed on a sheet. Anyway, I found out that all those snacks are not free. The housekeeper ended up putting the waters next to the bed during turndown but I would have preferred some chocolates. Oh well!
Another problem is the firehouse station being so close. Yes, I don't enjoy hearing loud sirens at all hours of the night, and I am a sound sleeper. However, the hotel is located near all the best shopping so can't complain about that at all. The AG place is right across the street.
The other perks of the hotel such as the butler service and use of a car are mentioned in their website but not freely offered once you arrive at the hotel. Maybe the info is burried away in some book in a desk but I think the front desk should inform guests directly of these perks. 
Another slight annoyance is that it is unclear how breakfast is included in your rate. What I mean is that we were supposed to have breakfast as part of our package but we didnt receive any vouchers or info on how to make sure you aren't charged for the food. In such a nice place, it feels awkward to have to ask when you receive your bill for the full amount. However I did ask and was told it would be deducted later. It hasn't shown up on our bill yet but I would think at least our tip would...I would prefer that the front desk would explain when you check in how the package works so you don't have to feel foolish asking. And I did call down to the front desk right before going to eat and was told I would just have to give them my room number. That wasn't quite how it worked.
Lastly, the pool bottom looks very dirty. My two daughters decided they would rather not swim in it. 
They provide free water in your car as we discovered after leaving in our cup holders with a note to drive safely. That was nice!
Hope this info helps someone.

title: “Hidden Gem within San Antonio...ONLY HOTEL I WILL STAY AT WITH SAN ANTONIO”
text: This hotel is simply amazing!!! From Ray the manager to Linda the Housekeeper, and Georgia the cook this hotel will blow you away!!! Cocktail parties during weekdays, beautiful suites, HDTVs, spacious rooms....very first class very professional. Just a few block from the Alamo, the Riverwalk, the Rivercenter Mall, and many MANY other historical places. Free hotel shuttle and extremely friendly staff will ensure your stay is the best it can be. Comfort Suites, Riverwalk, 505 Live Oak, San Antonio, TX.

title: “Best location , Times Square.”
text: They have a big diversity in room. Some are very nice, but most of them (I have been many times there), are old , small and not updated. The cleanness is an average one, and you can find many airlines crews in the lobby. The hotel is very big, so don't expect to a personal servise.

title: “Good value”
text: Room was very clean, people at the front desk were nice, breakfast was fine (a waffle-maker made it somewhat above average, but the quality of the fresh fruit was low for SoCal), there's a pool, and parking is free. Very convenient for driving anywhere in San Diego, but not itself walkable to anywhere in particular. The reasonable price, friendly service and cleanliness mean I'd happily recommend it to other travelers.

title: “Nachos and Chips found between sheets in bed.”
text:
I have stayed at this location often due to business travel and have finally had it. Aside from the snack in my bed that I didn't order...The hotel restaurant took a little over an hour to bring my order. I was the only one in the place..
Old hotel that needs a makeover.

title: “A very pleasant midtown boutique”
text: I've stayed in a lot of midtown hotels very close to the City Club, such as Morgan's, the Royalton, the Algonquin and the Millennium. From now on , this is going to be my first choice. The rooms are light and airy, the beds superb, the staff extremely helpful and the rates very reasonable for NY. Excellent.

title: “Quite Decent, but Not Distinguished Enough for a Top-Ten Rating”
text:
This was my first stay at any Jameson Inn (2 nights, business, late October 2011). Although the place is certainly adequate and probably above average, I'm unsure that it deserved the #4 TripAdvisor ranking among all Jacksonville hotels that influenced my decision to book a room. The rating is #7 as I write this.
This hotel is located a little off I-95 exit #344, about 8 miles from downtown. The area seems safe and relatively quiet, with 8 to 10 other hotels, sit-down and fast-food restaurants, and small office complexes nearby. An Applebee's and a Waffle House are within very short walking distance; in case your GPS goes nuts like mine did, the Jameson is the first hotel after the Applebee's entrance.
My web reservation (Jameson site) was in order; the lobby is very clean and inviting. I was greeted cordially by Thomasa, the desk clerk. In response to my web request for the highest & quietest room possible, she said that their first floor was their "quiet" floor. I was doubtful, but she reassured me. I got room #111, at the end of the hall right next to ice & vending, which made me even more doubtful. However, Thomasa said that no one was booked above me, which was true on both nights (therefore, I can't comment on how sound-resistant the floors are).
The room was quite clean and nicely appointed, with decent lighting, double beds, and less free floor space than usual (for example, it was hard to do sit-ups). The luggage rack was built onto the floor and wooden, not like the flimsy metal/strap racks in many mid-range hotels. The room had a nightstand between the beds, a small desk in the corner, a recliner chair, a closeable wardrobe, an iron with board, a hair-dryer, and a flat-screen TV that swiveled. One major plus was the abundance of electrical outlets; another was the outstanding water pressure (plumbing). There was NOT a microfridge or a microwave oven in this room (normally a big minus for me); if I recall, some rooms are supposed to have them.
The bath sink was outside the bathroom proper (a plus), with plenty of counter space on which to spread out. Soap & shampoo were provided, but no conditioner. The bath linens were typical for mid-range hotels: some pieces were adequate for use, others (more than half) were at end of life. As a major minus, the water seemed to be very hard, because showering, shampooing, & shaving took longer than they should have: it was too hard to work up lathers.
When I sat on the end of the bed, it groaned, and I got the sense that the mattress would tip (however, it didn't). The bed & pillows were comfortable enough, and I slept well except on the second night, when other guests exited their rooms at 6 a.m. and slammed their doors. I heard no other noise (including ice & vending) and didn't know whether anyone was booked next door, so I venture to say without full commitment that the thickness of the walls may be pretty good.
My key card worked every time in my room door and at the outside entrance nearest my room. Happily, when the maids serviced my room, their master key cards didn't cancel out my ability to enter with my card, as happens too often elsewhere.
My 6:45 a.m. wake-up call came at 6:37, and my 8 a.m. call came at 7:52. This is a little off.
A breakfast buffet included pastries, some fruit, and the opportunity to make hot waffles. However, I saw no milk, which meant fighting those tiny plastic containers of MooMoo coffee-creamer. There also appeared to be no cereal, for those (or those with kids) who consider cereal rather normal to find at breakfast.
The hotel has a small, square pool, more for cool dips than for swimming. The garbage can & ashtray by the side exit to the pool weren't overflowing, but they obviously hadn't been emptied for some time.
I never encountered this "Ryan" employee whom earlier reviewers have raved about. Thomasa was quite friendly but wasn't from Jacksonville, so she couldn't really answer specific questions about the area. On the first morning (Friday), an unsmiling desk clerk with permed blonde hair, perhaps in her 40s, couldn't really be bothered, and I really had to persist in order to get some answers. Checkout on Saturday at around 9:30 a.m. was swift and uneventful; a young clerkette asked me how everything was. Somewhat grumpily from having been awakened by slammed doors at 6 a.m., I muttered, "OK, I guess." The clerkette said (not in unfriendly fashion), "Just 'OK'?" I muttered about guests' having slammed their doors, to no response.
In summary, I COULD and MIGHT stay here again, but I'd look further before committing. There's a Microtel and a Red Roof Inn among the other choices, and I'd consider them upon reviewing their TripAdvisor ratings. The Jameson's rates were pretty good, and it's a decent place; however, given the above non-optimal observations (none of which was fatal to my stay), I don't believe that this hotel deserves as distinguished a TripAdvisor ranking as #4 (at booking) or #7 (at this writing) in a city of Jacksonville's size.

title: “A bargain for the money! very clean and quiet!”
text: We wanted something away from the hustle and bustle of Baltimore, yet close enough so we could go sightseeing. This was an ideal, quiet, yet refreshing location. The place was immaculate, and the staff very helpful and friendly.

title: “Great location and service”
text:
I discovered this Marriott very recently when I wanted a hotel location in downtown San Diego which was within walking distance of the convention center and all the Gaslamp restaurants. The staff were very welcoming and helpful. I requested an upper floor with a "view" and was given one. Of course, there are other hotels blocking the bay view but I was happy with a partial view. For those who want a view of Petco Park, home of the SD Padres, it is right next door. 
I enjoyed the fact that I could walk all over the Gaslamp area at night and return from an event near the convention center feeling very safe. The room was small but well appointed with all the nice touches that the Marriott brand is associated with (e.g., good quality toileteries, a very comfortable bed). The staff were happy to answer any questions about the local area and also provide good directions.

title: “Luxus pure, but expensive”
text: We had a great time in New York and the hotel was great too. I really can't say something negative with the exception of the pricing of everythink. Yeah, i know, it is a five star restaurant, but 38 USD per person for breakfast on top of the price for the room is not acceptable. So i had to go to Starbucks every morning to get our coffee and somethink else. 10 USD for both! I looked also at the room service, but i would never eat a sandwich for 30 USD. i can't taste sooooo good. Finally we only used the hotel for sleeping and to enjoy the view on the harbour and the statue of liberty.

title: “Great Staff and Location; in need of facelift though”
text: Just stayed four nights with our family in a deluxe corner suite. It was huge! Two baths, a dining room and a gym...who could ask for more? Well, guess we could. While we were upgraded to the Tower side from American Express Centurion, the rooms were still in dire need of a facelift. The property is in the best location, has a festive and wonderful lobby, and most importantly, a willing, able, kind and friendly staff; yet, its old. if you want a four seasons room experience, this is not the place. however, if you want a huge room with a great staff, look no further. Our family will definitely be coming back....

title: “WB: Westin, not Warner Brothers”
text:
The Westin Bonaventure was convention headquarters for an organization of musicians in early July. 
In downtown LA, the location was fine for bus trips to the Cathedral and the new Disney Concert Center. We could have walked there.
Inside, the hotel is a maze of colors and shapes throughout the building. The elevators seem to work either very quickly or very slowly.
It took several days to become accustomed to the locations of the various conference rooms, restaurants, lobbies aand elevators.
The rooms were OK, but on the small side for two full sized beds. Airconditioning worked well and was easy to operate. 
There was no refrigerator in the room; when I requested one, I was put on a waiting list.
The coffee pot's lid kept coming off, but the machine did produce coffee. I did not have time to check out the TV, nor to try the fitness center or the various items of physical training in small areas along the center. Nor did I 
have the opportunity to visit the restaurant on the 35th floor, atop the tall tower. 
Energy conservation policy is in effect; if you want the sheets washed, leave the official note on the bed. If you want the towels washed, leave them on the floor of the bathroom. Otherwise, they would not be changed during your stay.
Unfortunately, our convention occurred over the 4th of July weekend. Most restaurants were closed on the 4th and 5th. That meant only two workers on duty Monday morning for 2,000+ hungry people
who had to catch a bus by 7:30 AM.
Breakfast of low-fat granola cereal, a 2 oz container of milk, one glass jar of juice and 1 medium coffee cost $14.24. 
The banquet, for the most part, was well done; 
at my table one person collected the tickets reflecting choice of entree; two other waiters seemed terribly confused as to the number of chicken and beef dinners desired.
The outdoor reception (for which convention guests paid $15 each) left something to be desired. The champagne flowed freely; reaching the hors d'oeuvres required standing in a long line.
Price for convention goers was $155 per night for 1 or 2 per room, plus 14% tax and 0.8% surcharge. 
If you want downtown location, you have the choice of the WB or the Wilshire Grand.

title: “Great hotel and location but very noisy”
text:
The location of this hotel was perfect!!! Literally on Times Squares doorstep!!!! The staff were friendly enough and the concierge Walter was great. He was so helpful. The lobby was very unusual, very modern and contemporary. The room was small but it was fine for us. The only problem with this hotel is the noise. The walls are so thin you can hear everything. The doors slamming, people talking at 4:00am and the cleaning staff shouting to each other from 7am. Not really good for sleeping! We were lucky we were on the 4th floor as the music from the bar is loud enough and when we were walking up the stairs to our room the music only started to die out on the 3rd floor.
I would recommend this hotel for the location but if you like your sleep I would stay somewhere else.

title: “Perfect in all the ways”
text: Price was excellent for what they offered. Spacious room with big window and a nice view. Shower and toilet separate from the basin create more space. Comfortable big queen bed. New furniture. Very clean. Service was excellent, courteous, but not exaggerated. Relaxed bar downstairs.Free internet, complimentary bottled water everyday, ice brought to the room, newspaper. Walking distance to museums. I was expecting less and was pleasantly surprised.

title: “Pros & Cons”
text:
First the positive.
Fantastic location. On the harbour front. 15 mins drive to anywhere. Fantastic supply of accurate hand drawn maps available from reception. They made sure we didn't get lost once. Friendliest service you will get. Nothing is too much trouble for the staff. The maid even offered to dry our beach towels for us. Price. Very cheap for the location. Cleanliness. Absolutely spotless.
Now the negative.
Very very small rooms. Paper thin walls.Just hope you don't have noisy neighbours. The TV;s have a volum limit on them to try and ensure you don't annoy your neighbours. Noisy AC. Don't keep it on all night or you won't sleep. Rooms have all had a recent lick of paint, but need a bit of a refurb as some of the fittings (shower etc) look a bit tired.
For the price, it's fantastic. Don't be fooled into thinking it's a 5 star hotel. Its a budget motel

title: “Wonderful experience”
text: We stayed at the JW Marriott Washington DC for two nights in December 2011 and had a wonderful experience. The hotel is very conveniently located within walking distance of the White House, Capitol, Mall, Newseum, Smithsonian, etc. The staff was VERY friendly and accommodating. The room was very clean, comfortable (beautiful white white Egyptian cotton bedding) , and quiet. We requested a room near the pool so we were on the inside (away from street noises) and just down the hall from the really nice indoor pool and hot tub. There is also a full fitness center. We ate dinner at the Avenue Grill (on the premises), which was reasonable and very good. The lobby and hallways of the hotel were beautifully decorated with fresh flower arrangements. This hotel has parking (valet) which is very convenient too although it is not inexpensive. This stay was a little anniversary getaway for us. We mentioned our anniversary in passing to the staff at check-in and were totally surprised when we returned to our room that evening to find champagne, fruit, cheese, crackers, chocolate covered strawberries and a lovely card signed by many of the staff. They went all out! What a wonderful surprise! This hotel really knows how to make their visitors feel pampered. When visiting Washington DC again, we will definitely stay at the JW Marriott!

title: “Good Value, Great Service!”
