text: Stayed here for three nights 5/17-5/20/2012 with 3 kids, mother-in-law, and husband, who was reporting to Ft. Sam Houston. Service was amazing! The man helped use with our many bags, and got the air and TV on in both our rooms upon arrival. Very friendly, kind, and courteous. The pool was small, but clean, and after our stay at another hotel the two nights before, my kids were very happy to have some pool time! The hotel was undergoing renovations (specifically, exterior painting was being done while we were there), but the inconvenience of that was minimal (couldn't open windows, they were covered with plastic for one day)...plus the painters were also very helpful holding doors for us going in and out when they were nearby. The laundry room only housed 2 washers and 2 dryers, which were enough for me to stay caught up and not have to haul home a bunch of dirty clothes. Though it was obviously an older hotel, our rooms were very clean and comfortable, and huge! The value was good. If I get to go visit my husband again while he's at Ft. Sam, I will most likely stay at this hotel again. :-)

title: “Great Location”
text:
Good - location, cleanliness (no bedbugs here), location, location, location, service, great shower.
Bad - lack of storage space in the bedrooms, sparse toiletries and barely any coathangers.
If you want to be downtown then this is a great place to be. Easily within walking distance of SOHO, Financial District, Tribeca and even the East Village if you're in shape and it's not too hot.

title: “One of my favorite hotels”
text: Very large guest rooms, some with beautiful views of Stonecreek GC and Camelback mountain.Great staff at front desk and the mgrs reception and breakfast. The cook was especially friendly. No dining in short walking distance but shuttle will take you to several options.Also close to shopping mall. Pool is average.

title: “Perfect!”
text: Clean, neat, classy. Perfect rooms, reasonable price, highly recommended. Not to mention the history behind the hotel! Oldest running hotel in New York City! Very cool. Amazing location. 1/2 block from Penn Station, very close to Times Square, across the street from Macy's. Stay here!

title: “central location and good price”
text:
I recently stayed here for 5 nights while attending a conference at the Moscone center. The first thing to note is how central and convenient the hotel is. Having caught the BART train from the airport to powell street($8.10) I had only a simple 5 min walk to the hotel, which is one small block up from union square. I was also only a 10min walk from the convention centre. Despite a number of homeless generally wandering around the central region(they seem harmless) it is generally very safe, and there was always plenty of people on the surrounding streets. With the surrounding transportation links, the whole of SF is pretty much accessible from this central area.
The hotel itself doesn't look much from the outside, but once you get inside it is much nicer. My hotel room however didn't quite match up to the advertised pictures in that there was none of the exposed brick wall, and as such lacked a little character. It was small, but ample enough as a single traveller, but 2 persons with luggage may have found my room a little tight. it was however clean, and the bed was extremely comfortable, which is the usually the most important point of a hotel room. 
A number of comments have been made about the noise. All the noise I experienced was extrenal and not within the hotel itself(stayed on 6th floor). It must be remembered however that this is not a modern purpose built hotel with double glazing etc, and as such there is little protection from the external noises. I can certainly report that the binmen do indeed arrive early(6am) several times a week and are extremely loud, although luckily I was genereally awake anyway from jet lag, and thus wasn't a major problem for me. 
I didn't have breakfast as it wasn't included in my rate, but there are plenty of options available for breakfast within the surrounding streets to suit all budgets and taste. the bar on level 2 was always busy in the evenings, with many non-residents coming in. There was always a good atmosphere here, and usually a live band in the early evenings. Not the cheapest bar in SF though. 
the staff were all very friendly and helpful throughout my stay
In summary this is not a perfect hotel, but its central position, relative cost, and comfy bed make up for this. If however an early morning wakeup is an issue for you then you may wish to consider another hotel, although I suspect you will get the same elsewhere unless you're in a more expensive modern hotel.

title: “Loved it!”
text: Friendly, warm, and welcoming hotel! Beautiful room, great sauna, attentive staff, and terrific location. We were able to easily walk to MoMA, Union Square, and Ferry Building. We will definitely stay here again!

title: “2 wonderful stays - review long overdue”
text: I have now stayed at Ink48 twice on business travel, once in February 2011 and once in August 2011. February was my first trip to NYC, and I picked based on prior experience staying in a Kimpton hotel and proximity to the Javits Center (nice for walking). I was welcomed warmly, was assisted with business needs, and was greeted by the staff by name each evening when I returned to the hotel and they were kind enough to check in with how my trip was going knowing that it was my first time in the city. I thoroughly enjoyed soaking in the tub each evening with the Aveda bath salts (I was on my feet alll day!) and the beds are always soo comfortable. I became ill after eating one evening and the staff was very attentive... someone came to my room to check on me and also had bottled water, ice, and crackers sent to the room. A manager was kind enough to call me the next day to make sure I was feeling better. I happened to fill out a generic survey about my stay that was emailed to me when I returned home, and was impressed to have the Director of the Front Office personally respond, thanking me for my feedback and requesting I contact them when I would be returning. (which I did) When I arrived on my return stay, I had been upgraded to a cityview studio, and upon walking into the room, there was a bottle of wine, a big bowl of some beautiful fresh fruit, and a hand written card waiting for me. When returning to my room the second day, there was a box of truffles. (the way to my heart MIGHT be through my stomach haha) I was delighted to see many of the same faces and was of course treated to the same great service- many small, but appreciated gestures. I ate in the restaurant and found the server to be informative and friendly, and the food was delicious! I certainly plan to keep returning to this hotel when I travel to the city twice a year on business, and hope to make time to check out the lounge on my next visit.

title: “excellent location; great place to stay”
text:
We booked this hotel due to its proximity to Boston Logan airport, and its complimentary shuttle service, to and from it (although, to be honest, there is a very good shuttle service close by, leaving from the Airport metro station).
The hotel was everything we needed it to be: nicely furnished, clean, spacious rooms - that included a small fridge, a microwave, two tv's, and a kettle (as we were travelling with our infant son, this was very good to have; and, as we stayed here on two separate occasions, we got to stay in two different rooms); excellent location, with a handy metro (subway) station close by, and the downtown area twenty minutes away (we were pushing a baby stroller); close to the airport, and with friendly staff.
The breakfast buffet was not bad, even though it was not too "creative", if you know what I mean.. Just standard stuff: toast, cereals, etc.. For us, however, this did the trick..
Some other reviewers have complained about the Manager's complimentary reception, but we happened to arrive just as it was taking place... It's just a bit of crackers, cheese, etc., with soft drinks.. It helped us fill in a hole in our stomachs, so we could make it downtown for dinner.. We can't complain about it, especially as there was no charge for it.. Of course, we wouldn't go out of our way for it!
We also tried the pool, with our child.. It was fine.. The only thing we didn't like is that the floor coming into the pool area can get too wet and slippery; tricky to navigate when you're carrying a child (maybe some draining racks / duck boards would help here)..
The staff were very good, and they were lovely to our little boy, who had a blast learning to walk in the spacious lobby (this, by the way, gave us a nice first impression of the place; we hate closed in, stuffy lobbies)..
On a down note, the pints of Samuel Adams were expensive, but that's just to be expected in the big cities in the States...
The food in the restaurant was fine - nothing too impressive, but did the trick!
We would definitely go back, and we certainly recommend this hotel!

title: “OK, sort of dirty, and bugged by handling of crib charge.”
text:
Not a big deal, but first hotel I've ever stayed in that charged us for a crib--$20 a night. 
What did annoy me is that I had called in advance to confirm that they would have a crib for us. Told the agent we could easily bring our own (driving in from nearby), but they said not to worry. Which was weird, because when we got there they said cribs were first come, first serve, and they weren't sure they had one, and, that they charge $20 a night. They did find one eventually (causing some unnecessary stress in the process because we'd have to find another place otherwise), but did charge us $20 a night for a crappy pack-n-play--which they didn't set up, or even bring to our room. Would almost have been cheaper just to buy a portable crib and then throw it out afterwards.

title: “Very solid choice for business travel”
text: Was there for stressful overnight business trip. Very clean room. Very quiet. Excellent lobby with cafe/bar. Staff were helpful and extremely courteous..

title: “Perfect start to our US trip”
text: Arriving extremely jet lagged into San Francisco, we were so happy we had picked this hotel! Loved the flavoured iced water in the lobby (especially the strawberry), this was definitely appreciated over the 3 nights we stayed. Was never really up early enough for brekky, so can't comment! Loved the location, it was so easy to get everywhere we needed to go. Everyone was so helpful and friendly including Maverick the dog :-) Great pick for anyone staying in San Fran.

title: “Not in Business to Please their Guests”
text:
My husband and I made a reservation for the week of June 5th at the Chelsea Savoy Hotel back in April, 2011. I requested an email confirmation at that time so that we would have something in writing. When I did not receive the email by the next day, I called the hotel the day after and gave the front desk clerk my email address again. When I still received no confirmation, I called again three days later, and finally a week later was my same request for the third time. Note: The front desk employees find the English language somewhat challenging. I had to repeat the spelling of my name and email address, and also the phone number every time I called. Still, after a week, I had not received an email confirmation. 
My husband decided to contact the hotel and Googled “Chelsea Hotel”. Unfortunately, he did not realize that there is another “Chelsea Hotel” – the famous older hotel - right down the street. They advised that they had no reservation for us. So, we were under the impression that we needed to start over with making a reservation, not realizing that my husband had called another hotel. Needless to say, we ended up with two reservations for the same days at two different hotels. I received an email confirmation from the “Chelsea Hotel” five minutes after calling. The Chelsea Savoy never sent a confirmation after 4 phone calls.
When we did not check in on June 5th we were charged with a “No Show” from the Chelsea Savoy – even though they never confirmed our reservation in writing, nor did they try and use the contact phone number we left them.
When we returned from our vacation and saw the “No Show” charge the next month on our credit card bill, it took several phone calls before we realized what happened with the reservation duplication. My husband and I do realize that part of this was our fault for having contacted the other Chelsea Hotel, but we had called Chelsea Savoy and requested an email confirmation on several different occasions. We felt that the hotel should assume some of the responsibility for the miscommunication. 
I contacted the manager – Debbie Pappas to explain what occurred while trying to make a reservation with her front desk and asked for her assistance in forgiving the “No Show” charge. She never returned our calls and I was always informed by the front desk that she was either “not there” or “in a meeting”. In reading the reviews for this hotel online, I can see where this is an old worn out phrase that the front desk has used repeatedly to keep from having to handle any kind of complaint. Debbie – the manager finally answered her phone on Friday, September 9 so that I could discuss this charge with her. 
Debbie was polite and seemed to understand how this problem occurred and proceeded to tell me that she would check into it and get back to me the “beginning of the next week” (week of 9/18/11) after questioning her front desk employees that no email was ever sent to us to confirm the June 5th reservation. I never received this follow up phone call from Debbie Pappas. She lied about getting back in touch with me. There still has been no credit back to my credit card and I have left numerous messages this past week for Debbie to return my call. 
I will continue to dispute this charge on our credit card. It simply is not good business practice to charge someone for goods or services and then give the customer nothing in return. 
It seems that the “Chelsea Savoy” has similar poor reviews from guests that feel that they have overpaid for rooms after being quoted one price, did not received part of what they paid for (breakfast), incurred FRADULENT credit card charges, etc. There are also complaints by other customers complaining about being dodged by “the manager” for almost any given problem. The Chelsea Savoy Hotel is not in business to give their customers a nice enjoyable stay. They are totally in the business to charge high prices for rooms and do not care how you have to go about “booking up” for the week as Debbie referenced during my one chance to speak with her.
I tried to email the Chelsea Savoy hoping that someone else would contact me regarding this issue, but my email was returned immediately due to a bad email address posted at the website. 
Thank you for allowing me to post at your site.

title: “Nice but old and spooky”
text:
FIRSTLY - dont go to Downtown LA for any kind of holiday / Vacation. Just dont. 
Right then... The hotel nice-ish the reveiws are right - good public rooms, great sports bar (if a little down market) good fitness center although there is a charge...
The rooms are a bit hick. I am sure they are clean but they just give the impresion that they are dirty - 
The furniture is dated. The TV was cerca 1980 surly and the bathroom small. I really didnt fancy the shower at all and waited until I got to beverly Hills where we moved to on realising there was NOTHING to do in Downtown.
The black and white pictures in the hallways downstairs of happy days of yester-year from the hotel are very creepy and add to the spookyness which this hotel holds - the cocktail bar look like it is from "the shining" 
its ok - it was quite cheap i suppose - Im a 4/5 star Hilton guy so this was not my bag really - it may be yours.

title: “Nice Place, Outrageous Price”
text: This was a very nice, fancy hotel in DC. I would never have dreamt of staying in such a fancy place but did so for a wedding. For the price, the rooms were nothing special, but the service was very nice. No real extras that could justify the cost. Guess it is the location and just a different way of living.

title: “Great for leisure and business travelers”
text: Great to stay at a hotel that really seems to focus on providing good service. Everyone from the valet that parked my car, the bellman who helped me with my bags, the friendly front desk agent to the bar staff all were very nice and helpful. The rooms were very nice and cozy, I had a great view from the 17th floor. The fitness center and business center are both free and are 24hrs. Very nice pool and whirlpool area. Great location, it is on the Riverwalk but on the quieter end so its about a 5 minute walk along the Riverwalk or a short river taxi ride down the river to get to all the restaurants and bar areas. Which was great for me when I wanted to go have a nice meal it was not far away and I also did not hear any of the loud crowds leaving the bar at 2am when I was trying to sleep. Overall a great deal for the area and quality of service at the hotel.

title: “A gem in NY”
text: I admit that when I first saw the hotel, I kinda went: OMG, what did I do! But honestly, great friendly staff, clean and pleasant rooms, quiet at night. Spent more time out of room than in - but that's the point right? A few blocks from Broadway and close to the subway. Parking was $10 a night and that's a steal for NY!

title: “The place to stay in San Diego!”
text: If I were to tell you that the Hotel Indigo was one of the most hip, chic, swanky and dog-firendly hotels I have ever had the pleasure to stay in, it would be an understatement. From the airy and roomy lobby with the Phi bar, to the beautifully adorned rooms, it has it all. When we checked in, we were greeted by very warm, friendly and knowledgable staff who were happy to assist us. The rooms are amazing! Hardwood floors (I mean have you ever heard of such a thing?), huge beds with luxurious bedding, spa-like shower, and a mini-Keurig coffee maker in the room (if you own a Keurig, you know why I was happy)! Bottom line, a great place to stay and convenient to everything!

title: “Just Fine for a Short Stay”
text: Satisfactory accommodations. Clean & quiet with nothing distinguished about it. A large building with rooms. For an overnight stay waiting for a flight the next day, what else do you wish? Recommended but only at a hotwire price. If you'd like a "Sheraton upgrade", another Sheraton (on Century Boulevard) a block away nearby offers much more including many on-the-premises food choices.

title: “Ramada Colfax Rd Denver”
text: Very nice staff, quick to respond to my needs. My room had a toilet that did not flush after 2 uses, and a hair dryer that was faulty. Both times I called down to the desk and within 5 minutes we had someone up to repair successfully our issues.

title: “Very nice hotel”
text:
I have stayed here many times. I have always found the staff to be helpfull in every respect. The rooms are typical for this type of hotel. 
As other people have stated the location for this hotel is second to none. Close to shopping, the theater district as well as many of the major tourist attractions. 
Do your best to search for better prices as booking directly can sometimes be pricy.

title: “Exemplary service at the Westin Riverwalk”
text: This was the best experience I have had at a Westin property anywhere and I have stayed at quite a few. The staff was gracious, hospitable and knowledgeable. The decor was elegant and the room was very comfortable. I happened to be in San Antonio on business but plan on returning to stay with my family for a leisure trip. The food at Zocca, on-site restaurant was fantastic as well. Great experience at clearly the guests come first at the Westin Riverwalk.

title: “Highly Recommend”
text: This is a great hotel! All of the staff I interacted with was extremely friendly and accommodating. The nautical theme is carried out in a fun and inviting way, which makes this a truly unique and fun place to stay. There are also two great restaurants in the hotel to choose from - Japanese and Italian. Both were wonderful. I highly recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: “As Nice As They Say”
text:
We stayed mid-week after getting a reasonable price with Orbitz. Considering how nice the hotel is, it can be a better value than staying at a Holiday Inn if the extra cost is bearable for you. It is probably too expensive for an extended stay or a business trip, but it is certainly worth the money for a special occasion.
The delightful included breakfast alone almost made up for the difference in cost between this hotel and a mid-range hotel. It was incredibly nice, and the server was efficient and friendly. The pancakes (the name doesn't do them justice) were the best I have ever tasted. 
Other than the waiter at breakfast, we only had contact with hotel staff when we arrived and left. They were friendly and offered to help with our bags upon arrival and departure.
The hotel is in a good location along the river, but is a little hard to find at first. Auction Avenue, which leads over a bridge near the hotel was recently re-named A.V. Willis Avenue. The hotel address didn't show up in our older GPS, but the entrance is located in the 600 block of Island Drive.

title: “Extremely convenient but very busy”
text: Stayed at hotel with wife and 7 year old daughter while in NYC for 5 days on holiday. Have stayed in many hotels in NYC but this was first time at Roosevelt. Arrived a little early and room with two double beds not ready so they gave us a room with a king bed and free roll out for our daughter. Room was on the small side with a small bathroom. We didn't plan on staying in room much so not so concerned about size of room. yes hotel was extremely busy therefore staff also very busy but we were not there to be appreciated by the staff we stayed for location which was extremely convenient to most major attractions. We got a great rate of $160 a night on expedia so at that rate were happy with hotel. Would not pay full rack rate however. Many cheap breakfast and dinner places with good food very close by. relatively good gym free of charge which had no one else in it when i went. Very happy with stay at discount rate

title: “Nice tourist hotel in good location”
text: Stayed at the Herald Square back in August. Booked on-line directly with hotel. Hotel lobby has glass partition at check in desk. First impression was "here we go" but dont let it fool you. Room was newly renovated with pergo flooring and new bedding. Large and extremely clean bathroom. Very quiet location at night which is good. 3 minute walk to the 34 street subway station which has many lines. Staff very friendly and helpfull. Great value here...will be back !!!

title: “Wonderful hotel”
text: Wonderful hotel, nicely located, well-apportioned rooms and easy check-in, etc. Absolutely would stay here again. The only negative is the onsite restaurant isn't very good, but that's not a major problem when there are so many places to eat within easy walking distance

title: “Overall a good stay”
text:
I stayed at Hotel Derek for 2 nights. Staff was helpful. The room's heater was not working but I was moved to another room. 
Parking is chsllenging and valet service is super slow. 
Self parking is not an option only valet. 
Overall satisfied.

title: “Westin Times Square”
text: Had fantastic time in New York and this hotel was right in the midddle of all the action in Times Square. (one block away) Did not have breakfast as it was very expensive but plenty of local cafes nearby. Beds were like a dream and had 2 quilts each plus luxury mattress toppers and wonderful pillows. Bathroom had strange metal basin but good hot shower and bath, no shower gel which was weird as there was body lotion. Only one bath robe but it was heavenly soft to wear (my daughter nicked that!!!) Coffee machine supplied but nothing for tea drinkers like myself. Found cafe on opposite block which actually served HOT tea. The Americans seem to mainly drink coffee or warm tea.

title: “You go for business”
text:
We stayed here for 4 nights for a conference which was taking place in the hotel. The service (as to be expected with the Marriott) was excellent. Friendly everyone from check in to bell stand to concierge. We had a city view room which was nothing overly special but big enough. The bed was wonderful but maybe a touch too soft. 
The location was great - right next to market street and close enough to the water - walking distance from a lot of attractions.
They have a fabulous sky view bar which opens at 4pm. Great cocktails and a good scene around 6pm.
Not the most romantic hotel in SF but... you go for business.

title: “Very good and could be great”
text:
I have just returned from a four-night stay at The James. The hotel's location made it ideal for exploring Chicago's main attractions and it was easy to pop in and out to escape the heat and to get showered and changed. When I wanted to stray further, it was easy to grab a cab outside the hotel. 
The staff were very helpful in arranging an early check-in, which was greatly appreciated after a transatlantic flight.
After some issues with the air-con on my second and third days, I was moved to another room. This was annoying but the 100 degree heat meant fully-functioning air-con was most definitely required and the girl at reception organised the switch very quickly.
The loft suite was very spacious with lots of nice little touches like the media room, an Ipod dock and two televisions. I did have repeated problems with some of the in-room equipment (such as the projector in the media room overheating and switching itself off) and, although issues were resolved quickly, it became tiresome having staff wander in and out to fix things that should have been in working order before guests were checked in. The filtered water and the ice left in the evenings made life easier. Having free wi-fi was great. The bed was incredibly comfortable and made for a great night's sleep.
The air-con in the hotel rooms does seem to be very noisy on the whole, which became mildly irritating after a while. 
I had breakfast in the hotel and have to say I was under-awed by it and the room service meal, given the great reputation that David Burke's Primehouse has. The one meal other than breakfast that I had in the Primehouse was excellent, however. 
This is a good hotel that could be great if a little more attention was paid to resolving the issues with the air-con and the gadgetry in the rooms.

title: “Nice Hotel, Staff could be friendlier.”
text: This was our first trip to US and NY, we had heard stories about NY room sizes so was pleasantly surprised, the size of the room was fine Location is a bit far away from Times Square and shopping- macy's, bloomingdales etc. you need to taxi it or subway. There is a subway just up the road so no problems with transport around the city. Front desk staff not very friendly, there was a problem with our booking (they couldn't find it), eventually we got our room, after travelling for nearly 24 hrs from Australia we really needed to crash. Overall hotel was fine, but staff need to be a bit friendlier.

title: “Amazing stay.... very central. beds amazing!”
text:
After a 19 hour trip from Australia, our bus drops off outside this hotel! Talk about being in the midst of things.. Broadway, Time square. 
Amazing location! Very central to everything you could want. Central Park not far, Taxis everywhere and cheap. Conceirge was helpful when needed, very quick to respond with any request. 
We had Corner King room, view down hudson river on the 27th floor, beautiful view of city lights and room was quite large compared to what i had read. 
BEDS! Well , when you lay down, dont expect to wake up for awhile, they will make you sleep.. Truely fantastic after such a long trip.. Close blinds and noise is almost not there.. 
Check in and check out is good, no hassle. 
Hard rock cafe nearby, Planet hollywood also, across road from MM and Hurleys. If you dont like crowds, dont stay in Time square.. 
Although we didnt eat in the restaurant, the view is amazing.. The bar also has some good cocktails and reasonable prices. Very relaxing atmosphere and view to Time square. 
This was our first visit and why we picked such a central location. 
NOTE : No fridge in our room, not sure of other rooms. A let down for me. 
Very well done Crowne Plaza.

title: “Clean, Professional and safe place for Motorcycles”
text: Really enjoyed my stay at the Drury Inn, not sure where to start, so many good things to say. Great locked and videoed parking garage (have to pay) which we liked considering our Harleys were going to be parked over night. Free wifi was awesome and lightning fast while using my iPhone. front desk lady was super friendly and helpful. I know this sounds odd but I think made a difference, the manager was wearing a dress shirt and tie and was very busy working with kitchen staff at breakfast time to make sure all was clean and organized. One thing that stands out was, cleaning staff and maintenance persons were all happy and pleasant, good sign of good working conditions. I would stay here again 100%. Oh, not like it really matters but our room overlooked a solarium? and not outside, not a big deal, just would be nice to get up in the morning and see how the weather is outside...once again, not a big deal. thank you, hope this helps.

title: “Terrible”
text:
Don't stay in this hotel! I had the worse experience ever!! I saw people drunk walking out of that hotel, hochie mamas throwing up outside and people moving in with all their funiture, and walking in with no luggage but clothes with hangers! Come on People no luggage! Wait thats not it a Cat drinking water from the pool. My son woke me up at around 2 am that he was scared cuz people were screeming outside. I looked out and people were fighting outside! SCAREY!!
The gas stove was not working. My husband had to turn off the gas! Don't Stay in this HOTEL!

title: “Awesome views”
text: This hotel had some awesome views of Chicago! The staff was great as well. We had a large group staying at the hotel for a family reunion, Rick Ueno was very nice to get us all rooms on the same floor near each other so that we could spend more time together. Our large group took advantage of the Club Level Lounge throughout the days/evenings that we were there. This provided us a large space to gather and talk as a group. The learly evenings were made even more fun because of Rene. He made us feel welcome and felt like he was part of the family. The hotel was in a great location so we were able to park our cars for the weekend and either walk everywhere or take public transportation. Overall our experience was fantastic.

title: “Trendy little hot spot”
text:
We recently spent one night at this hotel and were quite satisfied with the rooms and the service, however found the $53 parking outlandish and it was the sole reason we stayed only 1 night. The lobby was both trendy and clean. Our waitress, Angela, in "The Livingroom" was outstanding, probobly the friendliest person we met in all of Chicago. 
We loved the rooms, they were gorgeous and the Bliss products in bathroom were to die for, I actually regret not going down to the spa to purchase some of that face wash! The location was good, walking distance to everything. I'd recommend it, if you fly into Chicago...but if you have to park a car....save your pennies before you stay here!

title: “Excellent service all around!”
text: The hotel staff were wonderful, wireless access was great and seamlessly available, cleanliness was beyound expectations, great location, convenient to restuarants and transportation, staff responded to any and all questions/concerns. I would give this hotel my highest recommendation.

title: “Nice, but needs more lighting”
text: So, what's with the yellow wallpaper and crema marfil floor and counter? Bathroom casts a sickly yellow glow everywhere, which isn't so great for putting on makeup. Or shaving. Overall, a lovely place to stay. Clean, quiet, perfect location, but pricey.

title: “It was OK. Good location.”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for about 10 days last July. It’s nicely located if you are going to a hospital in the Medical Center.
The rooms were outdated, but clean. Nice and spacious lobby area in case you have nothing to do. Their shuttle and concierge service was courteous and knowledgeable. I had a horrible time trying to use their “business center”. They only had 2 computers with internet available, so there always was a line to use the computers. I didn’t eat at their restaurant but there are many options within walking distance.
I booked through Priceline and paid about 1/3 of the regular rate.

title: “bad restaurant, no room window, no wifi”
text:
The restaurant was bad. Stay away unless you're starving or just want a beer.
 It seems that some rooms look into a hole between the neighboring building and the hotel. The roof at the bottom of this hole is slanted so if you're unlucky you could get a room with a window that's blocked. And at the very least all of the rooms that look into this hole don't get any sunlight. 
They don't ave wifi. I've never stayed in the 4 star hotel that didn't have wifi - and they try to charge $10 a day for wired internet access - rip offffff.

title: “Hotel Palomar exceeded our expectations”
text: I initially booked the hotel since the reviews were good and the location was across the street from where other family members were staying. We were pleasantly surprised with the size of the room. The queen size beds were very comfortable. When my son forgot his toothbrush, they actually brought one up for him. The person checking us in was extremely helpful informing me of stores around the area as well as offering us a small refrigerator in case I needed it for extra water, etc for my marathon the next day. The hotel also accommodated the runners for the Marine Corps Marathon by starting coffee at 4am vs the usual 6am. Since I was running, I didn't partake in the wine they offered, but next time. The gym was also a decent size with everything you need for a good workout. Being pet friendly even made this a definite choice for next visit to DC.

title: “We always choose this hotel when ever we fly out of Chicago!!!”
text:
I was very impressed with the fine service provided to us by Alketa at the front desk!! What a delight!! She is energetic and displays a winning attitude!! Her enthusiasm for her career choice is infectious and we will always remember our outstanding stay because of her!!
Alketa fills a very important role for the Renaissance Chicago O'Hare Suites Hotel!
Please make certain that you share this information with her!!
Maxine Snyder

title: “Great Location... Great Service and Value for Money”
text: We selected this hotel for our 9 day visit because of its location and the pool... The location was so central to Times Square, Broadway Theatres, Central Park, 5th Ave Shopping, The Subway, Hop on Hop off bus, Hells Kitchen for a selection of restaurants with good food. There was a convenience store behind the hotel for a cheaper feed, Starbucks and McDonalds also if required. The hotel is an older style hotel with great service and friendly staff. The room was clean and well presented, The bathroom was an older style however clean and functional. The bed and pillows were super comfortable. If we were to say anything negative we would have to say that the noise from the housekeeping room next door was an issue, however this may have been due to our room location. There was no refrigerator, iPod dock or WIFI in room... However WIFI was free and available in the lobby with a number of computers also available for guest use. Overall stay was great with awesome service and would stay again.

title: “Beware! Bed bug reviews are accurate! Heed advice and stay elsewhere”
text: I arrived in the evening to a somewhat pleasant staff who barely spoke english. I was given a tiny room - which was fine as I wasn't planning on spending much time in it. Although I must say I was a bit surprised that the room didn't even have a telephone! While I was trying to sleep, I noticed something out of the corner of my eye moving. I turned on the light to find a small reddish bug. The hotel is old and a few bugs is to be expected. I got some kleenex and picked it up. Before jumping back into bed however, I pulled the covers back to make sure there wasn't any more. What I discovered was horrifying!! There were a couple dozen bugs crawing under the covers and along the rim of the bed/mattress. I panicked and immediately packed my stuff and went down to the front desk and told the staff who looked absolutely shocked and surprised at my discovery. After the other reviews on this board, it is clear they were putting on a "good show" of disbelief! They moved me to another room that I picked apart from top to bottom. While I didn't find any bugs, I didn't sleep either. I kept the light on because I researched bed bugs on my laptop and it said they don't come out when its light. Not immediately, but two days later, red bumps appeared on my arms, hands, neck and feet - the areas that were exposed during the night. They itched like crazy and stayed on me for well over two weeks. I advise anyone who is "sitting on the fence" on this hotel to really heed the reviews of this board as they are indeed accurate and truthful. I understand that the price of this hotel is appealing when it is so hard to find any others in Manhattan that come close. But there is a resaon for their "low price" - its a bug infested dirty place! Is it worth your HEALTH just to save a buck? The choice I made to stay really put a damper on the rest of my vacation, dont' let it hamper yours.

title: “Nice hotel, close to main attractions if you don't mind a walk”
text:
This hotel is clean and well-maintained, with a friendly staff. All parts of the hotel I saw were up-to-date. Though it is not as fancy as some Hilton properties, it works well for families. 
As for the location--the hotel is one mile to the Mall. The walk is pleasant along clean, safe streets. If you have young kids, as we do, consider bringing a stroller or be prepared to carry them. Bus stops and the Metro are also options, though we chose taxis for convenience as we were there for a short visit. A taxi ride to the Mall area is less than $10 for 2 adults, 2 kids and about $10 to the National Zoo. We saved more by staying in this hotel and taking taxis than if we'd stayed in a hotel closer to the sights. 
There are nice cafes and coffee shops along the way to the White House, so I recommend planning your meals around your walks to/from hotel. If you are fit and don't mind walking, this is a nice place to stay and see part a regular part of the city. 
We stayed on a busy weekend, so breakfast was crowded. The food was plentiful, but seating was not so we took breakfast back to our suite.

title: “Nice for pre-departure at the end of travel”
text: Had a pleasant two night stay ending travel in SouthWest and having a glimpse on San Diego. Fulfilled my expectations in cleanliness, room/bathroom size for taller man. Everything functioned well and breakfast was very good. Frienliness of staff welcomes one here once again!

title: “We will be back! This is a winner!”
text: Indeed, this is a great location-a block from Times Square, close to good restaurants and the theater district. The rooms are small, but some more expensive hotels have much smaller rooms. Don't expect many frills or great views, but the staff was friendly and helpful, the beds were comfortable (pillowtop), and room was very clean. We weren't asked to write a review, but we decided this will be our hotel of choice for future trips. It is an unbeatable value for the location.

title: “Decent 3.5 star hotel, in a great location”
text: The Sheraton is located walking distance to Central Park, Radio City, Carnegie Hall, many broadway theaters, and Times Square. The hotel itself is clean, busy, and roomy. There is a good fitness center, for an extra change. I avoided the fees and ran in Central Park instead. The restaurants and bars in the hotel are not worth mentioning, but the hotel is steps from several execellent restaurants and pubs. So, I didn't bother eating at the hotel. For breakfast, walk out side exit and walk to several Starbuck or the West 53rd deli which has excellent breakfast offerings. The rooms are large, except for the bathrooms which is cramped. The bed and linens are equal to most luxury hotels. And free coffee and tea in the room. On peeve, was that the hotel charges 3.25 per luggage item if you want them to hold your bags for the day if you have a late flight.

title: “They get it!”
text:
Service, impeccable but not arrogant.
Rooms-older but well maintained and nicely appointed.
The featherbed! 
Great hotel-it's continental, classy and well run. A pleasant experience overall!

title: “Good location, small room, boutique feel”
text: Having stayed a few nights at a large chain hotel, I booked a room at Villa Florence to experience something different. Location was great, within 5 minutes of the cable car and streetcar stops. The hotel is well maintained for a building its age and rooms are clean. Upon check-in, we were upgraded to a King room. We were told that it was street facing on the second floor, and if it were too noisy we could change rooms - appreciated the honesty of the check-in staff! The room was small, but it had its charm, and L'occitane toiletries :) One night, there was a guy playing a saxophone on the corner - very clearly audible, as were the cable car bells! But it didn't bother me - I quite liked listening to the sounds of the city and the noises died down later at night. Overall, I enjoyed my stay here.

title: “At the top of a very steep hill, but great hotel”
text:
We stayed at the Fairmont as part of a wedding party otherwise we probably wouldn't have picked it. Try and get a room high up - preferably in a corner - we were in 614 and had three huge windows with the most incredible views south over the city. We didn't draw the curtains at night so we could wake up and see the view.
Everyone else talks about service and the lobby so I'll keep my review to this - don't stay here if you can't manage walking up hills. The Fairmont website claims to be close to the BART station, which isn't exactly a lie, but the map doesn't show hills. The Fairmont is at the top of one. A steep one. 
Luckily, we braved the streets and traffic and drove our bags to the hotel before dropping the car off at the airport after having been to Napa. Frankly we wouldn't have made the hills, up or down, with our luggage. Even without heavy bags, the hills do put you off coming and going more than once a day, unless you are either driving or are prepared to pay for taxis everywhere.
If nothing else, to say you stayed at the Fairmont San Francisco is a real buzz so you forgive the hills and the fraying decor (as did John McCain who stayed there 2 days before us), and you're guaranteed to always find you hotel in SF/USA guide books - it's a city landmark.

title: “wonderful experience”
text: We stayed at the Elvis Presley Heartbreak Hotel in Memphis, TN during Spring Break this year (2009) and we LOVED every minute of it. We stayed on the first floor. It was a room that had one king size bed in one room and a queen size sofa bed in the other room along with two TV's-one in each room. This is called the King Suite. I admit that the hotel could use some renovating, however, it was a good value still. It wasn't like the roof was falling over our heads or anything like that. The room was actually quite nice. It was spotless, roomy, and had a mini kitchen complete with a small fridge, microwave, and coffee maker (along with delicious complimentary coffee). The beds were as comfortable as could be. The complimentary continental breakfast was the best. They had fresh fruit, a variety of juices and cereal, yogurt, sausage and gravy, biscuits, muffins, bagels just to name a few of the yummy items. The Bar also is where you can buy your food and eat it in the dining area, where you can see Elvis concerts on a big screen, so nice and relaxing. The drinks area phenomenal as well. they have a shuttle that takes you from the hotel down to Beale Street and back for free, which is so awesome. There is alot to see and do in the downtown Beale Street area. Marlowes Restaurant down the street also sends a beautiful pink cadillac limo to pick you up and take you back. their food is quite delicious as well. And of course we couldn't leave without visiting Graceland across the street. It was an experience we will carry with us for the rest of our lives. It was amazing. The entire staff both at the hotel and Graceland was professional and friendly. It was a very great experience overall for all of us. There is a Walmart not too far from the hotel as well where you can buy food items (inexpensive) and take advantage of the mini fridge and microwave in the room. As long as this hotel is still standing, we will go back over and over.

title: “Beautiful Decor and pleasant staff!”
text: The hotel and rooms are beautifully decorated. I found the staff at the front desk helpful and while having a night cap the bartender was very friendly. It was a pleasant surprise to find such a wonderful place to stay on our way to Disney World.

title: “GREAT BOUTIQUE HOTEL NEAR DOWNTOWN”
text:
We found the Clarendon during a New Years stay 2011-12. The pool was terrific, friendly guests & lots of lounging options. Was it beat up or worn? Let me say this: YOU try staying out in the Phoenix sun for more than one season and not look a little worse for it!! 
Re: wifi, I had no trouble. There were always 3 or 4 WLANs open, not a problem. 
I'm w/ Colleen on the LACK of light in the rooms, but having lived 8 yrs in Phx, I chocked that up to the massive sunlight available most months, and avoiding unnecessary heat production. There's little, if any, overhead lighting.
About the snacks -- my husband checked us in, so I wasn't paying much attention, hence I missed out on free candy BUT it was made clear to me that rather than clutter up their world w/vending machines, I could simply ask for what I'd like. I had a COLD diet Coke every day. That made me smile.
The food at Gallo Blanco is simply outstanding AND inexpensive. 3 to 7 pm happy hour EVEN ON WKENDS!? We love food adventures, but why go anywhere else when it's so close and cheap? We ate there 6 times - breakfast, lunch and dinner. 
Re coffee - Tastes great and it is pretty easy to use the system. I usually travel w/a real coffee mug. Do that, unless you want to drink out of styrofoam.
Bedding and mattress? LOVED THEM. 
The price was affordable for a terrific place in a neighborhood that was comfortable and very close to public transit -- buses and the cool new light rail. I used to live nearby, so I was a little reluctant, but I felt comfortable.
Our room did have a smoke smell, but an open window solved that, and I am picky! I found a fewburns in the carpet, so - mystery solved. Not an ongoing issue for me.
I'd definitely stay again.

title: “Wonderful, excellent, best of any Hampton Inn”
text: I've been a Hilton Honors member for over 10 years, and am currently a Diamond member (i.e. I travel lots for work and leisure, and have stayed in many Hampton Inns and other Hilton brand properties over the years). This is THE NICEST Hampton Inn I have had the true pleasure of staying in (and only because of a flight cancellation!). The staff are great and the decor, design and furnishings in the rooms make it look/feel almost like a boutique hotel. The headboards were faux leather, and and bathroom looked like it could have been from Restoration Hardware. I certainly will stay here again when in Charlotte!

title: “Commodore - Don't Stay In This Stink Hole!!!”
text: We went to Seattle for Labor Day Weekend 2002. As soon as we arrived at the Commodore, the tattooed and pierced heavy metal guy at the front desk did not have any record of our internet reservation, nor could he honor our confirmation number. The pictures and advertisements Commodore has in their website is a total lie! Please do not think of coming here unless you were so, so low in cash that you are in the throes of desperation. Unless you enjoy staying in a smelly, tiny room with dirty sheets, cigarette burned bed covers, please do not come here. We ran into a lot of strange characters in this motel (it's almost a welfare motel). I tell you I'm not a picky person since I've frequented hostels before, but this place is beyond hostels. I would have rather stayed in hostels. It's totally dirty. My friend got bed bugs after one night and I could not wait to leave it. We even had to change the light bulbs ourselves since there was no light in the room and the guy at the front desk would not do it. Talk about lousy service. Trust me, I'm writing this because I don't want anyone else to experience this. Even if you're a backpacker, don't even think of coming here.

title: “Excellent, comfortable hotel”
text:
Midtown location, near the Waldorgf Astoria, and a couple of blocks to the nearest subway. It is also possible to walk to 5th Avenue and the Rockafellor Center.
We had a 2 bedroom apartment on the 9th floor. Very clean and comfortable. One room with a kingsize (or perhaps larger bed), other with twin beds (which my 20 and 18 year old appreciated). Aircon and TV in both rooms and in the living room. Powerful shower.
We received a good welcome from the staff with a small basket of goodies in the room. The complementary breakfast was just the job, but perhaps the only criticism I can think of is that it did get busy in the dining area. There was a tray in the room so that you could take your breakfast back to your room, or don't go for breakfast at 9am. This is a minor criticism.
Overall the staff were very helpful when we needed anything.

title: “Aging gracefully, but with a few wrinkles.”
text:
My family and I stayed at the RC SF for 3 nights, October 20-23, 2007. It had been several years since my last stay, so I was curious to see how the hotel had aged. My review of the property follows.
The RC SF is located on Stockton St. between California and Pine mid way up Nob Hill. It is an impressive looking structure with the entrance and handsome lobby area located on the fourth (street) level of the hotel. There is construction ongoing at the corner of California and Stockton, but it appeared to be unconnected to the hotel and was not (other than being an eyesore) a bother. 
We arrived around 1 p.m. and check in at the front desk was painless. We had 2 rooms reserved, a Club floor executive suite with a nearby club king room. The suite was ready for occupancy, but the king was not. Both rooms were located on the 8th floor which is the actual location of the club lounge, though I think the RC classifies the 7th and 9th as club floors as well. The elevator for the 8th floor is via keyed access and opens directly into the lounge area where we were greeted warmly by the club concierge. 
Those of you who have stayed on the club floor of an RC know the drill. There is a light breakfast, lunch, tea, dinner and after dinner serving served at appropriate times with coffee, tea, soft drinks, beer, wine and cocktails available all day. The rate runs about $150 a night more than a standard room, but I generally find it worth the money. While there was always a good variety of sandwiches, crudités, cheeses and desserts at the RC SF, the menu selection never seemed to change much during our stay. Still, it is a pleasant space and a popular gathering spot. The lounge is "child friendly" which made it a bit active during parts of our stay. Not bothersome really, but active. 
Our suite was in the typical RC “executive” configuration. The door opened into a small foyer with a closet and half bath. The foyer opened up into a living room with a desk, a love seat and 2 arm chairs. The window provided a view of…well, not much. (I have stayed at the RC SF several times on several different floors and have never had a view of much of anything except buildings.) No balcony, but the windows did open about 3 inches to allow a breeze. A glass paneled door with sheer curtains separated the living room from the bedroom, which was nice sized with what I found to be a very comfortable king bed. The dressing area and bath (with separate tub and shower) was behind the bed. 
The suite was clean and fairly well maintained. A few pulls in the carpet and a bit of torn fabric, but nothing too bad. Other than the bed, the furniture was not extremely comfortable and needed updating, I felt. New flat panel TV’s were present in both the living area and bedroom. Wireless internet at $12.95 a day was available, but somewhat slow. The bathroom was a bit cramped and poorly laid out, I thought, but serviceable. Good water pressure during our stay.
The RC SF has a nice spa with the usual services available. It also has a very good fine dining restaurant on par with other RC properties. There is a talented harpist in the lobby bar during the afternoon and an excellent sushi chef there during the evening. There is a house car available for trips within a mile or so of the hotel. 
The biggest substantive complaint I had during our stay was the noise level in the room. I know that others on this site have made the same remark. The windows appear to be orginal equipment (If I recall the property opened in 1996) and do not have a great deal of insulation. There was a great deal of bleed through street noise at all hours of the day and night, which was annoying. 
Now on to being picky. Service at the hotel started off great and then went downhill. I was quite impressed with Valentine, the club concierge, and the front desk and bell staff...Jason and Joel at the front door were especially nice and helpful. However, the staff members at the lobby lounge and outdoor patio off the terrace bar (on the second floor in the courtyard) were weak. Several servers at the lobby bar were standing around chatting with one another, but not doing a good job watching the floor. Still, the service at the lobby lounge was stellar compared to the patio outside the terrace bar. I attempted to enjoy a spectacular afternoon there with a cocktail but could not get anyone to wait on me. When I finally asked for a drink from a passing staff member (who apparently did not work the patio) I was told to “go upstairs to the lobby bar to get a drink” and bring it back. Odd, I thought, as there were people eating (inside and out) at the terrace restaurant. Certainly not the level of service I expect from the RC. 
I was also disappointed in the servicing of the room. We left early one morning and did not return until 4 p.m. only to find that neither room had been cleaned. When I called the front desk to inquire when the rooms would be cleaned, I was told that I should have asked for an “early” service. Huh?
Again, these are picky comments. As I am sure Mr. Roa (whom I respect for responding to the posts on this site) will admit, however, it is the fine details that separate a 4 star from a 5 star property. 
In the interest of full disclosure, I admit to being a fan of the RC chain and have stayed at dozen or so of their properties around the country. (Pentagon City and Cancun being 2 of my favorites.) To be frank, though, I prefer the Huntington Hotel in San Francisco. It is up the street at the top of Nob Hill on California. Smaller, independently owned, with a wonderful view from the rooms that front California (Grace Cathedrial and the park, with the bay visible in the distance from rooms on the higher floors) and well kept (although, in fairness, somewhat dated) rooms. Impeccable service. While there is no club floor, the Big 4 bar and restaurant compensate by being clubby and wonderful. Plus, even though my favorite rooms there front busy California St., they are much quieter due to heavy, insulated windows. I would have stayed there this trip, but booked late and the property was full.
So, how has the RC SF aged since it opened in the mid 90’s? Fairly well, I think, with the exceptions noted above. I give it a solid 4 rating. If they take care of the noise problem and work a bit on service issues, it will be a 5. All in all it was a pleasant stay. 
I hope this has been helpful and informative. Safe travels everyone.

title: “Fabulous boutique hotel!! Great for the luxury traveler....”
text:
This hotel is located right off Times Square, but it's not a bad thing in this case. Walk out the front door and turn left... Times Square. Turn right....... Access to NYC. The service is great. They have a nice lounge area and great food. Hotel offers hot chocolate throughout the day. The restrooms on the main level are a site to see so please do!
The rooms are NYC-small, but that is to be expected. They are modern with a luxury, traditional foundation. This hotel can handle business or pleasure for your travels. There is a great market right next door to get breakfast sandwiches, wine, snacks etc so you can feel like a true New Yorker. 
The staff are welcoming and accommodating without being overbearing. 
You will definitely want to go back!!

title: “Very Happy & Will Return”
text:
We spent a delightful night at the Hilton...yes the lobby is large and bustling, but this is NYC! Very quick service by a delightful customer service lady at check in. She placed us on the 27th floor, a renovated floor, which even had a slice of Central Park in our view. The room was lovely -- high ceilings, tastefully decorated, fabulous linens, very comfortable bed, fine bath, lots of towels. Our robes were missing and once we called for them, they were brought up to our room pronto. Fast elevators, tons of very hot water. The temperature in our room and the hallways was just fine, not too hot at all. And you can't beat the location. We plan on returning this fall. And check out was a breeze!
We got a wonderful rate through Priceline, $125. We usually prefer older hotels with lots of grand detail, but I have to say that I was thoroughly satisfied with the feel of our room -- with the high ceilings and lovely appointments, plus great view, I don't see how we could have done better without paying much, much more.
Also we parked our car further west where the parking garages are cheaper ($25 for 24 hours) and walked to the Hilton. No big deal.

title: “In 30 years of travel to NYC this is the worst hotel I have encountered.”
text: I booked a room with a queen bed, the first two rooms they offered upon check in were twins, I refused them and was given a so-called superior room that was dated, tiny, dirty, and had can aged walls. The front desk and manager did nothing to resolve my complaints. My last stay at the Jolly. Too bad because the Murray Hill location is convenient to my business meetings and grand central station.

title: “great”
text:
I must admit I nearly changed hotels after reading some of the reviews on this hotel but I'm glad I didn't. 
Very friendly staff, beautiful grounds and a stone's throw from a huge shopping mall and tram at the rear, what more could you ask for ! 
Yes, the room did smell a bit but only because it hadn't been aired for a while, after the first day it had gone and yes, there are some rooms that look onto a brick wall (why they built them like that who knows ! ) but if you don't want a view and just enjoy the resort, these rooms go for peanuts !
I know you can't please everyone but it seems easier to write a review if you've had a bad experience then a good one..........

title: “Location, location...”
text: We loved the location of the hotel and when we chose not to walk, the metro was accessed without going outside. In our experience, the staff was very accomodating. This was a good thing as we had two rooms and 12th floor lounge privileges and during our 9 day stay we were continually having our card keys reactivated accurately. Our regular sleeping room was on the small side and the small vanity was inside the bathroom. I ate one lunch in the waterside cafe and it had a very limited menu. There are too many options in the area so I advise skipping meals there. I believe we would consider staying here again.

title: “One of the better Courtyards!”
text: I always stay here when visiting family. Clean, pleasant, convenient, pretty new. Has the Bistro, walkable to WalMart to pick up stuff you forget to bring. Close to Ruby Tuesdays, Ale House, Cracker Barrell, etc. Many stays there and never a problem!

title: “Couldn't love it more!”
text:
Absolutely loved this place - loved the modern decor, the flat screen tv, the morning coffee, the short walk from the metro and the great restaurants and cafes in the neighhbourhood. I got an amazing $99 hotwire rate for two nights, but by the end of my stay I was desperately trying to rearrange my schedule so I could stay a few more nights, and I would've paid $300 a night happily if I couldve done (the hotel, it turned out, was booked out, and my plans weren't flexible enough). 
I especially loved the soaps in the bathroom, the furry bedspread, and the yoga workouts on the in room entertainment (and the helpful chap who delivered a yoga mat to my room). The pool too is a good size. 
When can I come back?

title: “Clean hotel with some small issues”
text:
Clean hotel in nice area. Day staff were quite courteous and wonderful; night staff was a bit harried and abrupt. Breakfast buffet was quite good for this type--buffet with hot,fresh waffles and sausage rollups you reheat, as well as muffins, danish, cereals (hot/cold), juices, and coffee. 
Outside of hotel could use a coat of paint and a little other renovation. Double beds were tiny, if you had 2 guests using a double bed apiece, or 2 adults with very small children, they are adequate. Otherwise, I would steer clear of these unless you like very tight quarters or are fond of "spooning."
I had a little bit of a problem with the high speed internet connection, but my laptop is somewhat dated (Pentium 2--I know, but it still works!!) The internet support was knowledgeable and got me up and running in no time. 
I would give it a 1.5 star rating now, with a strong 2 star if they clean it up a bit with the beds and exterior.

title: “Absolute worst!”
text:
We stayed here several years ago and I still have the scar on my leg from climbing over the bed and radiator to get to the bathroom. As far as we saw, there was one elevator that only seemed to move when it felt like it. The room was dirty, small and seedy. With the exception of the bellman, the staff was rude and didn't seem to give a hoot if you were there or not. NO parking to speak of. We parked in a parking garage about 3 blocks away. 
Would rather sleep in the park than stay here again!

title: “Good Hotel”
text: The hotel was perfect for us. The location is great, lots of restaurants in the area and only a few blocks from the Belmont redline subway station. The room, while somewhat small, was newly decorated with a decent flatscreen TV and a clean, modern bathroom. The entire stay was good. They have free complementary breakfast until 10:00AM and decent complimentary coffee served all day.

title: “Another great stay at The George”
text: It was five hours later than I expected due to flight delays but the staff made up for it. Reminded me why I stay here for business and pleasure during my frequent trips to DC. Great staff, terrific restaurant and convenient location.

title: “oh dear!!!!”
text:
pre booked in december 2007.requested standard room with king bed and high floor.stayed hotel june 2008
on arrival given 2x double bedded room on floor 2 which was one floor above outside bar. requested change of room but offered room with no exterior view -only view of atrium so offer declined --big mistake!!
the noise from the outside bar was super decibels and floor two (room 242 was ours) should be avoided at all costs when booking.make clear to the hotel that outside bar noise rooms are not acceptable.
plus points:-
location excellent
food ok
staff generally friendly

title: “Clean, friendly and a good price!”
text:
We stayed here both before our cruise and on our return. To make our reservation I called the hotel directly, the reservations agent/receptionist was very helpful and when i told her we were going on a cruise she offered us a great deal on a cruise package. We arrived from the UK, jumped on the shuttle bus (shared with the holiday Inn), stayed one night and was then driven to the new Smith Street Port. Our transfer arrived dead on 11am just as we had been told and was a breeze in a clean and comfortable bus.
We were made to feel welcome by the friendly reception staff on our arrival and given clear directions to our room. We were on the 2nd floor towards the back, considering the hotel is so close to the airport there was no noise whatsoever. Our room was spacious, was well equiped and very clean.
Our second stay was for 2 nights and we arrived very late, again the reception was just as friendly and helpful and we had the room next door our previous one. Again it was spotlessly clean and comfortable.
The hotel is just a 2 block walk from the light rail into Seattle ($2.50). We found this to be very convenient and obviously cheaper than staying downtown. There is also a Denny's a block away, if you want a meal.
For the price I don't think you could find a better place to stay in the area, clean, comfortable, convenient and very friendly/helpful staff.
We will be staying here again.

title: “ok once finally in room”
text: i got to the murray early room was not available yet. i waited 30 min after check in time . room still wasnt ready. 20 min later front desk gave me a key and said go and check if room is ready it was not ready! i finally asked for an upgrade. luckly this room was ready. once i got in my room which was a jr. suit i was very happy with the room. It was very very large compared to the rooms ive stayed in at the raddison lex. very clean. now check out day was not that great. im from orlando so im not use to whistling at cabs. and when i come to new york usualy someone who works at the hotel helps me catch a cab. the door man told me where I could catch a cab. after 5 cabs passesd me i went back to the hotel to complain. the doorman was asked to catch me a cab. and I made it to airport by a hair.

title: “Seriously amazing...”
text:
We stayed here for about a week in February 2011 and it exceeded our expectations! We got this hotel in a flight+hotel package deal, so we ended up paying about $100,- a night for 3 people. Fantastic value!
We had requested a room with a view of the Empire State Building and we were very happy to find out we got a room with an amazing view on the 29th floor. The room was spacious enough, even with the sofa bed in the middle of the room. The bed was very comfortable, however the sofa bed was rather uncomfortable and very bad for your back. But hey, it's a sofa bed, and at least it wasn't the worst sofa bed I've slept on. Also, the kitchen was huge, which is especially great for longer stays.
The free internet was also great, very fast, we never had any problems with the connection...
Best thing about the room though... no bedbugs!
The breakfast buffet was amazing, bread, cereal, yoghurt, muffins, scones, pancakes, waffles, hash browns, turkey bacon, sausages, breakfast burritos, fresh fruit, juice, milk, coffee, thee, hot chocolate.... And best of all... it was free! Also, everyone was so friendly
The people at the front desk were very friendly and happy to help with directions and shopping/broadway/other excusion ideas. We were also very happy with the free luggage storage on our final day in New York. Also, there's a computer/printer in the lobby, which is great for printing out boarding passes, bus tickets, directions and so on, all free of charge.
The location was also perfect, about a 5 minute walk from the centre of Times Square, away from all the noise. Across the street from Bryant Park, which was still covered in snow, which was beautiful. Plenty of lunch/dining options around and within easy walking distance of Macy's and lots of other shopping opportunities. 
Also close to the Port Authority Bus Terminal, about a 10 minute walk with luggage, which is great for bus transfers to/from the Airport. We got an airport taxi from Newark to the hotel, which, including toll and a tip was around $70,-. Since there was only 3 of us the bus turned out to be a lot cheaper and just as fast, one way is $15,- per person. I think a round trip is $25,- p/p. Next time we'll definately take the bus.
The only negative points during our stay...
* We had to make our own sofa bed.
* Since it was was very cold during our stay we asked for extra blankets or a duvet for the sofa bed, we were told this wasn't a problem, however when housekeeping showed up we were told there were no extra blankets or duvets. Instead we were given 2 extra sheets, which didn't help much with the cold.
These were only minor disappointments though, which didn't bother us all that much, and certainly didn't ruin our trip or anything like that.
Thanks Residence Inn, for a great week! We'll definately be staying with you again for our next trip!

title: “Great Hampton Inn Opened in 2005”
text: This is a great Hampton Inn where we have stayed on family visits several times. The property opened in 2005. Rooms are very clean, the continental breakfast has a number of options -- not just pastries and coffee -- and the staff has always been friendly. The hotel is convenient to I-10 and I-295 on the west side and a short drive from Orange Park, downtown and the airport. We will keep returning.

title: “great rooms with excellent views and staff”
text:
arrived 5th feb for a 4 nights break,room was excellent sorry no this was not a room it was an apartment with lounge and kitchenette with microwave ,oven ,fridge freezer etc ,etc and separate bedroom with excellent views from 19 th floor .clean bathroom and linen.
 staff were very friendly and accommodating stored our luggage and arranged taxi ride back to airport with very friendly driver.
 well placed for all major sights , good range of restaurants in area , and was surprisingly quiet after dark
 try restaurant at top of tower good views of manhattan. 
 this was booked on internet and would use again.

title: “Great location and excellent service”
text: We stayed at the Club Quarters for 3 days in November 2011, the week-end of the Philadelphia Marathon. We booked a standard room and the size was perfect. The bed and pillow were quite confortable as well. The location is unbeatable, you can walk to all main attractions very easily. It's really close to the city hall, and there are a lot of stores and restaurants in the area. We were extremely pleased with the client service. It was impeccable. All employees we met were very nice, helpful and smilling all the time. The hotel restaurant is excellent, as well as the service. Again, very friendly and helpful staff. On Friday nights, you can bring your own wine at the hotel. We would definately go back to this hotel without hesitation!!!

title: “I wouldn't stay again!”
text: The hotel is in a good location it's right beside a shopping centre and near the cable cars. the room we had small for 3 people though and the shower took us ages to work as it was complicated. what i didn't like with this hotel and why i wouldn't recommend it to anyone is because of the way the staff treated us upon arrival, they were no way polite or helpful, as we had a problem with our credit card, we came from Ireland and they told us if the card wasn't sorted then we had nowhere to stay as they couldn't book us in without one, it was shocking as this had never happened to me before, even though we had the room paid for before we came they just needed the card for security reasons! the woman who booked us in seemed like she didn't want us there at all and this was a first time to America for 2 of us and it put us in a downer as we thought we were going to be treated like this for the next 3 weeks we got it sorted our eventually but i'd never go through that treatment again!

title: “Great location for Park Avenue and Modern Art Museum”
text:
We stayed for 4 nights
Hotel well located for Subways, Central Park and the Modern Art Museum as well as the high end shops of Park Avenue. Not much in the evening as this is a business district but some great breakfast cafes! Room was a reasonable size but a little bit of a squeeze for 2 adults and 2 teenage girls. Bathroom was very small and the overall lighting could have been better as it was a little dark. We had an inside facing room and the view from the window was awfull. Staff helpful when needed which was not often. Rooms clean, TV, DVD player, toiletries etc. Free tea/coffee/hot chocolate available in the lobby and the bar had a good happy hour. Some bars close by on the same street and a fantastic deli on the corner. free wifi which worked very well and a workstation with printer in the lobby

title: “The worst hotel I've ever seen”
text: This was the worst hotel I've ever seen. It's so bad, in a very bad and unsafe location in downtown San Francisco. Tens of rooms share one and only ONE shower!!!! You also have to share toilets!!!! There is no service. You need to ask and change your SINGLE towel every day. No service to clean the room or do the bed. The breakfast was nothing: muffins and fruit. Honestly, my stay there was a nightmare.

title: “Good location, but better options are available!”
text:
This is an old hotel in a good location, but the rooms are very small and the hotel is very run down! We stayed on points for six nights recently and were very disappointed. You will hear noise from the bars across the street. If you make a reservation, please ask what year they last renovated? Breakfast was marginal.
As an FYI, we didn't have a car since the North subway station was very close and convenient, but parking is $40/night.

title: “A wonderful hotel and fantastic staff”
text: From the moment you pull up in front of the Prescott on Post Street, the staff goes out of their way to be helpful and make sure you feel special. The facilities are fantastic and the amenities relaxing.

title: “Excellent Value; Stunning Architecture”
text: This was the second visit to the Millennium Biltmore by my wife and me. The public areas in this hotel are breathtaking and invoke a far more elegant period of travel history. Our room was quite nice. We booked a "Club Room," which included access to the Club Room Lounge and afternoon tea overlooking Pershing Square. The room was adequately sized, very comfortable, well-appointed, and also had view of Pershing Square. Our dinner at Smeraldis was excellently prepared and the service there, and for that matter, everywhere at the Biltmore, was professional and attentive at all times. For an expertly prepared cocktail in the most elegant of settings, you must visit the Gallery Bar. Again, I cannot say enough about the courtesy, helpfulness, and professionalism of the staff we encountered at this fine hotel. You can spend more at other establishments, but from our experience, when taking into account the caliber of the facility and the level of service, you will be hard pressed to find a better value. We will definitely return.

title: “Best Location Ever!”
text: I stayed here for four nights with a friend - we asked for a twin room, which was two queen size beds. We had a view overlooking Broadway and Times Square and could not have had a better location. 2 minute walk to subway, a very safe area to stay, even for two women to walk back to their hotel late at night. I would most definitely recommend this hotel to anyone, and will be staying again!

title: “Comfortable, welcoming hotel”
text:
Stayed for 2 nights at end of a road trip. Convenient for Fisherman's Wharf and the Muni network of public transport. Comfortable good sized room, surprisingly little traffic noise at night (and we were on the outside of the building), though was noticable during day. 
Would use again for business or pleasure if needed accomodation in this part of SF.

title: “Clean, Fresh, and a great location!”
text:
We stay at the Orchard Garden Hotel whenever we go to San Francisco for the weekend. The rooms are a little small but very comfortable. You can always rely on the staff being friendly and helpful and the rooms being clean, fresh with very comfortable beds. It is located right outside the entrance to China town on Bush street, just a few blocks from Union Square.
The price is a great value for the location and quality that you receive.

title: “One of the best hotels in NYC”
text:
Room was a tad small, but very clean and overall excellent. Location is great, and staff were very helpful. The breakfast (included) and free "snack bar" day-round were outstanding. 
Staff communication did have some problems, though, as requests made to one staffer were unknown to others, resulting in several missed connections I regretted. In spite of those minor problems, however, I would happily stay there again. And intend to.

title: “Great experience in San Diego”
text:
We stayed at the Dana on our recent trip to San Diego with our daughter and her husband and 10 year old twin girls. All of us loved our experience at the Dana - we stayed in the rooms that view Mission Bay. The kids loved the swimming pool and the table tennis. Breakfast at the hotel restaurant was good and the location was ideal.
There is a higher end restaurant at the hotel and although we didn't dine there it looked like a nice place to eat. We would definitely recommend this hotel and we plan on going back again.

title: “Nice change for Spring break”
text:
We decided to do something different then our typical beach Spring break trip this year. The Wild Oak Ranch was a nice surprise. The weather was cool in the morning so very nice for my morning run on the nature trail at the nearby Hyatt Hill Country resort. By 11am it was sunny and in the 80's so perfect for the pool. It was wonderful to go somewhere for Spring break that wasn't crowded or outrageously expensive. Our one bedroom condo was roomy, beautiful and I thought the bed was very comfortable. 
 The pool area with water slides and separate lazy river were extremely nice, clean and beautifully landscaped. You didn't have to rush out to reserve a pool chair in the early morning because they were plentiful all day. I loved having our own isolated area on the lazy river to sit and read or jump on a tube and float around with a drink from the bar. 
 I was there with two teenage boys who enjoyed the water slides, some water volleyball, soccer, basketball and lazy river. The machine for tokens for the arcade was broken so they were able to do the air hockey. They enjoyed smores one night and checked out free DVD movies from the front desk in the evenings. 
 The staff especially at the bar/restaurant JB's were friendly. We ate some meals in the condo, some at JBs and went out for Barbecue at Rudy's and Mexican at Soluna. We had a great day at Sea World which is open weekends at that time of year. There were virtually no lines for the water rides or roller coasters. Sure beats standing in line at Disney World.
