We did not make it to Fiesta Texas since it is only open weekends that time of year. The Texas schools have Spring break earlier in March so that is most likely why things weren't so crowded.

title: “Great Place to Stay in New York”
text: The Strand is a lovely hotel and really well positioned. Close to the subway and anything else you want. The decor is stylish and the staff very friendly & helpful. The rooftop bar is nice if you can get a space as it is very trendy and much of the 'comfortable seating area' was reserved - even a no go for guests which we thought a little less than friendly.. Needless to say we did not go back despite what jcould have been a great view. The room offers plenty of information about hotel facilities but the one thing that we wanted A KETTLE (Being British we do like our tea - and at present there is no restaurant or coffee shop within the hotel) was omitted from the list. We mentioned the absence of a kettle to make drinks apart from breakfast when we were leaving as we thought it a down point and were told this was available on request - no one told us this!!! A small omission but it would have made a great diffference to us. The breakfast - included in room rate was excellent and offered a great choice. Think this is a fairly new hotel so there will be teething problems but overall the hotel is really good. We would stay there again (and would request a kettle!!)..

title: “Felt like Paris,Very clean comfortable and closeWe loved our 2 day theatre and french resturant getaway”
text: Very clean comfortable and close. We loved our 2 day theatre and french resturant getaway. Great staff!!

title: “AWESOME”
text: Worth every penny. I knew when we arrived and the Valet escorted us to the front desk we were in for a wonderful stay. The staff was professional, polite and attentive. This was our 20th Anniversary weekend. The Hotel and staff took what I had hoped would be a good weekend and made it great. The only negative comment I could make is to the traffic noise at night. But with the awesome downtown location I don't know how you could resolve that problem. I very much look forward to the next opportunity we would have to return to this hotel.

title: “Needs help”
text:
i can forgive the reufbishement - even if the work starts at 7am. I can forgive the fact that the top 3 floors of the hotel are open to the elements during the refurb. I can forgive the fact that the room might have done with a deeper clean- it was okay, But the staff are so sullen its unbelieveable. The management really needs to sort this out.
Free shuttle to the airport - very handy. Dont use the concierge for anything. they will rip you off. We priced various trips - they wanted 100 dollars for Universal Studios (50 dollars for the bus???? or 45 dollars for the Getty - when its free. Figure out other ways to get there.

title: “Terrible Service”
text: Their customer service is awful. I spent a week trying to resolve a cancellation issue and they were almost totally unresponsive. I gave up and paid the bill and found out that they overcharged me. I spent two weeks trying to get them to fix the bill without success. I finally had to get my credit card company involved and the threat of non-payment got them to correct the bill. I have never received any kind of apoolgy for the overbilling.

title: “Clean, but not so convenient”
text: Nice stay, clean room. Wish they allowed pets. The location is a bit inconvenient, you have to make a u-turn on the service road to get to the hotel coming from the north and the traffic is heavy-but that is Austin.

title: “A perfect fit for me”
text: I've stayed at the Phoenix on two trips, been very happy both times, and will stay there again the next time San Francisco calls. Yes, it isn't for everyone, but I think it's pretty easy to figure out which camp you fall into. I found the location central and convenient to mass transit, the room comfortable, and the slightly-edgy retro atmosphere charming, attractive and pleasantly unstuffy. The hipster folks at the front desk were friendly and welcoming. If the noise from the bar (which I'll admit I didn't particularly care for) is an issue for you, request a room at the back of the courtyard, sheltered a bit behind trees and gardens from the scene out front.

title: “Excellent Hotel and great vacation !!!!”
text:
We stayed in The New Yorker Hotel with my wife at the dates between 19-25 October 2012 during our annual vacation.Beginning from the check-in period, the hotel front desk ( many thanks to ANA...)personnel has showed us a very positive and helpfull attitude towards us.Our room was on the 33th floor.We had a magnificient view of Empire State Building and Rockefeller building.The hotel has a great location , the subway stations (red and blue lines) are very close.In addition there is MACYs store in the 34th street which is very close to this excellent hotel.The rooms are also very clean.We do advice this great hotel.
Ugur B. (İstanbul-Türkiye)

title: “great stay and great location.”
text: Our apartment was being painted and the fumes were so bad we needed a hotel. The Days Inn was great. Room was very clean and employees very nice. It felt like a little vacation for one night. Thank you Days Inn Chicago, did not even know you where in my neighborhood. We will send our family and friends there when visiting.

title: “If you can get a deal, this is a nice place.”
text:
I decided to catch a couple of baseball games and, being familiar with Seattle from previous visits, knew that any downtown hotel would not be far from either Safeco Field, the Space Needle or Pike Place Market. It just became a matter of which place offered the best price for a nice room. It had to be 3 stars or better. The Renaissance came in at $90 a night, through Hotwire.
This hotel is conveniently located off of Interstate 5. the downside, of course, is noise. My room was on the 16th floor and, while it was ok, I could still hear muffled traffic noise. Check in was friendly and fast. As noted in previous reviews, the parking cost is expensive. $36 per day with taxes. Yes...most of the nicer hotels, downtown, charge like this, but I'd jump at the chance to stay somewhere that offered reasonable parking rates and nice accommodation.
The downstairs lounge is quite comfortable with reading/business rooms. Elevators were fast and quiet. The room, while getting a little worn, was still nice. Mine faced east, giving me a view of the expressway and some of downtown Seattle. The king-size bed was comfortable. Slept well. Flat screen tv worked good. Found that it would get a little fuzzy if it was pointed in the "wrong" direction. Bathroom was nice. Large enough.
The rooms have those single serving coffee makers. I don't drink decaf so, if you're sharing the room with another coffee drinker, you'll need to ask for a 2nd regular coffee.
I never made it up the 26th or 28th floors. I understand that they have lounges and pools and stuff up there, but I was in town, with friends, for a couple of games. Mostly, we were out and about. If you enjoy walking, both Safeco field and Pike Place Market are fairly close. About 20 - 25 minutes to either, going - mostly - downhill. If you're heading downtown and still have the energy to walk back, after, head up to 6th Avenue. You'll avoid the steep hills. Much more gradual. Coming back from Safeco...take a taxi! It's about $7. (Same for downtown.)
There is a $13 daily charge for room wifi. I was told, however, that the wifi is complimentary in the lobby lounge. I set up my iPad, there, and to my surprise, it worked for my entire 3 day stay...no matter where in the hotel I was! My room, included. No charge. Try it and see if it works...

title: “Awesome, Nuff said”
text: Absolutely wonderful hotel, clean, nice rooms, super friendly and accommodating staff. One of the best views in dallas, I can't say enough good things. I would recommend this hotel any time. I will be back!!!

title: “Great location, top notch service and a sound sleep.”
text: I had a great stay here on my last trip to Chicago. Great location with an outdoor cocktail bar on the 5th floor (lobby level.) Easy to get around the city and Joe's is right out the back door for the best seafood in Chicago.

title: “Not worth it-Stay in the city”
text:
When we got there we were a little disappointed because it looks like a motel not a hotel. We walked in and the rooms were ok, but the problem was we could hear the the family next door. EVERYTHING they said and all the noises they made! It was horrible. They might as well have been in the room with us. There was also a moldy/musty smell from the bathroom. The bathroom looked nice, but that was about it. We asked to switch rooms so they sent my husband to another room with two double beds. The room had not been serviced, the bed sheets had pen marks on them and so we waited 20 minutes for them to service it. When we walked into the room my husband took off the bedspread and saw that they never serviced the room, they just made the beds with the same sheets as the family before us! GROSS! My husband then proceeded to go to the front desk and tell them what happened; they immediately checked us out and never apologized for what happened. The woman at the front desk said the family that was in there before us was only in there for 10 minutes. That is why they didn't change the sheets.
We ended up going to the Marriott which was great!

title: “Westin on 3rd St. was adequate”
text:
We stayed at Westin on 3rd St. and Market for one night on Aug. 11. The room was rather small, but adequate and clean. The lighting in the room was not bright enough if you intend to read a book, as I did. The layout of the room was different than what I am used to, with the TV at 45 degree angle from the bed. After sitting on the bed to watch TV for 15 minutes, my neck was very sore. I used Priceline and paid $175 plus tax for one night. So maybe I got what I paid for, a standard room with no view and nothing extra. 
There is a parking garage directly across street from the hotel so it's convenient for those who want to save a few bucks on parking. We used the hotel valet parking ($42 + tax + tips) and was happy with it. We did have a good time shopping and dining nearby as the hotel is in easy walking distance to Union Square. All and all it was a nice stay but nothing spectacular.

title: “Pretty Good for the Money”
text: The rooms were very clean but kind of small. Reminded me of my dorm days in college. It works though. My husband, 1 year old daughter and I were there for 6 weeks until we could move into our new home. They were nothing but helpful. They let us look at 3 different rooms so we could choose one that would fit our family and needs. You don't pay taxes over a month of staying there which makes it extremely affordable. It kind of sucks that you have to supply some of your own things but for the value it is worth it.

title: “Excellence in the heart of Manhattan”
text:
Our 4 night stay at "The Hilton - Times Square" was wonderful. To be fair we did arrive early to find our room was NOT ready. But that was no problem for the staff. We simply left out cases with the consiege and set off exploring New York. There wasn't alot spent in the Hilton because the nature of New York the city that realy does NOT sleep, but the staff were always friendly, helpfull and curtious. 
Located on the 28th floor with a fantastic view over the hudson to New Jersey, the room was plenty big enough and the king sized bed made for restfull evenings. Returning in the evening, the bar was always welcoming with a lovely mellow atmosphere, (if only the barman would smile a little more).
In short I would recommend this hotel for all the right reasons, if you want to explore New York with a convenient location and comfortable surroundings.

title: “Great location, nice service, a little pricey”
text:
The location for this holiday inn express is what you pay for. The hotel was full 
when we checked in. The parking space is a little tight, but the hotel staff helps you
park.
The staff was courteous, and the breakfast in the morning was decent and contained
bagels, cereals but no toast. We had booked a smoking room by mistake, and as the hotel 
was full, the front desk couldn't help us. As expected, the room smelled of strong smoke. 
They had a basket of goodies (chocolates, cookies) + 2 bottles of water, which was 
nice.
We would stay here again, but would certainly search for a better price

title: “Worth the splurge”
text: The Peabody has a great location in downtown Memphis 10 ft off of Beale. We loved the lobby, fountain, duck hype and entire property. While the duck thing is for a lack of a better term, silly, it adds levity. I want levity on my vacation and if the little lady I am traveling with gets a kick out of it, then it's worth the price of admission (which is free by the way - you don't have to stay here to see the show and everyone is welcome). We however did make our accommodation at the Peabody staying 3 nights utilizing the B&B package. The service and attentiveness of staff was beyond reproach, A+, 10 out of 10. While I can point out several instances of exemplary service and grand dame character, I was disappointed to find a large cockroach in my room. I guess it can happen anywhere, you just don't want to see it in your $275 per night hotel. With the ability to overlook that situation, I think of the lovely cloistered pool and hot tub, well appointed lobby and above average service to give this 5 stars.

title: “Good location for visiting The Mall”
text:
Location is very good and Metro station and supermarket are close. Not many restaurants near.
Good service, standard breakfast.

title: “Excellent hotel, friendly and good services provided from all staff.”
text:
I had a very pleasant 7 nights stay at the London NYC hotel. Whether cleaners, porters, concierge or front desks staff. Every one is very helpful, friendly and the services at the hotel are world class!
Particularly, I would like to mention Sam Lee, Tony (not sure his surname) as well as Ying Yu (although she works on 9th floor). They have left me with extremely pleasant memories, they are extremely helpful and had spent a lots of time and patience to guide us where to go, how to get there and even for something very small. We are so grateful to them.
We will stay in the London NYC hotel again whenever we are in the New York in the future and would not hesitate to recommend it to everyone. It really is a world class hotel!!!
I wish the London NYC hotel continue with it's success and see you soon.
Best wishes
Dr Xiao-Ping Zhai

title: “A FAIL!!!”
text: Went to Houston this past weekend with a husband and friend for his birthday and needless to say not impressed with the Homewood Suites. The Homewoods that I have previously stayed when much better for some reason. First off, the location of the hotel is behind the Fairfield Marriot, which if i were not looking we would have passed up. Second, the rooms were extremely small for the 3 of us, even though there was a sleeper sofa in the living room. Breakfast in the morning consisted of egg patties (never have I seen these), bisquits with sausage gravy, a waffle iron to make your own waffles, cereal and juice...very disappointing. Now the upside was that the night staff were very nice and tried to be as accomodating as possible, and there were a lot of stores in the area for shopping, etc..but the best time I think we had was at Pappadeux on Westheimer. Other than that, I will probably not stay here again. It was not close enough to the nightlife, plus there was some construction going on that made it seem like you were going around in a circle just to get back to our room.

title: “reasonable motel with free parking”
text:
clean en comfortable motel with a large bathroom
the beds are small.
good internet
friendly staff.
no breakfast or coffee but there are enough coffee corners near.
1.5 mijl from downtown or harbors

title: “Great Place to Stay Near Sea World”
text: We've stayed here at least four times in the past few years and we keep coming back. The hotel is clean and in great shape. The staff is friendly and professional. The hotel is in a beautiful location, with ocean or harbor views from every room. It's a 5 minute drive to Sea World, or you can take a 10 minute boat ride from the hotel to Sea World. The zoo is only 15 minutes by car. There are several pools and three water slides -- one for younger kids, and two for the older ones. During the height of the season, the pool area gets very crowded, so be prepared. There's an outdoor fire pit near the pool where you can make s'mores (hotel will provide the ingredients and tools). The hotel restaurant, Red Marlin, not only has great harbor views, but is very family friendly. However, it is on the pricey side for adult meals. It has a good breakfast buffet, but as an alternative, there's an Einstein's Bagels a short walk along the waterfront from the hotel, near the hotel fitness center. You can also pick up wine and food at the provisions store connected to Einstein's. Kayaks and other small boats can be rented next to the fitness center as well. All in all, it's one of the best places to stay in San Diego, especially with kids.

title: “modern luxury in a great location”
text:
Modern, streamlined look in the rooms. Great bed (very firm). TV in the bathroom mirror. Spacious bathroom. Beautiful infinitiy pool and very nice fitness center, both with view of the harbor. Quiet hotel--every room's door is in an alcove off the main hall. We did have noise from outside because of some kind of carnival in Fells Point on Saturday, but it stopped at 10:30
Good security--room key needed to take elevator above public floors.
Two very minor issues: no ice available for self service, must call hotel to bring; balcony off of a king room had only one chair (I'm sure I could have gotten a second chair if I'd asked, but wish they'd just have 2 available. Here at a conference rate, so value was extremely good.
Service--front desk and concierge--was outstanding

title: “Location, Cleanliness and Heavenly Beds!”
text: Spent one night prior to cruising and got a great rate on Priceline. Perfect location, super comfortable beds, spacious rooms, great views! Easy walking distance to almost everything - Von's (for Seattle's Best Martinis and Manhattans), monorail (to get to the Space Needle), and Lola's (for a delicious breakfast!). Also very close to the cruise terminals. Bathroom was a little small, but adequate and very clean.

title: “Loaded with History and Charm”
text: The room was nice size and as old as the hotel is, it was amazing how well the plumbing and air conditioning worked! Upon check in I learned this is where JFK proposed to Jackie AND where he had his bachelor party. Tried a Boston Cream Pie which was good and the service was friendly at both the Last Hurrah (Joe at the bar) and the Parker House Lounge. This is a very nice hotel, they do turndown service and include water in the rooms. The workout facility was nice and clean too. The only drawback for me was the room was somewhat dark, the view from the window was terrible and the bathroom was very small with no counterspace. I would stay again though because those are not high priorities. The location of the hotel is very prime, a minute away from Boston Commons and more.

title: “Worst place I've stayed by far!”
text:
Has "do not enter building is perilous to human life" notice on the front door. Notice placed there by a building inspector, the best thing you can do is heed the warning! Our room had bed bugs, mice and rats. The window leaked cold air into the room. The shower was shockingly small and the toilet worked only sometimes. We changed rooms twice and they never got any better. DO NOT STAY IN THIS DUMP!!! 
On the only plus, it is two blocks from Times Square but this does not make up for how badly this place is lacking in EVERYTHING else.
DO NO STAY AT THIS PLACE.

title: “Great Location, great views &/or sightings from the rooftop? You got that right!”
text:
Fun, conveniently located, close to all my favorite UWS restaurants, Lincoln Theatre, Hudson River bike path, Central park, train stations, splurge & enjoy at this trendy and chic boutique hotel. 
I didn't experience any noise of any sort, housekeeping was fantastic with cleaning & turndown services, no complaints, just kudos all the way.
Bathroom was small, but very modern and shower had no door, but I just figured that was the way of the future... Oh, amazing shower head, beds were nice & comfortable, great size flat screen TV, needless to say we got a dream room. B-)
Bell staff greeted me "Every Time" sounding warm and sincere, "Did I mention Every Time"? ...so did the housekeepers and bartender at the rooftop bar. Reception could learn a bit from them, my only concern (not really issue). Us tourists need lots of love to shop & spend with confidence while in town... kidding, just a warm smile, tone and look in the eyes will do!
Other than that, hallways/rooms are clean, great decor & vibes... as seen on Gossip Girls, I definitely recommend it!

title: “Good hotel for the area”
text: This is a great hotel to stay at when in the Galleria area of Houston. It is not as pricey as some and is even fairly close to the medical district.

title: “Not the Westin Service You would expect”
text:
1. Rude front desk
2. Breakfast buffet has very few choices
3. Valet Parking takes forever
4. Rooms are ok, but lack of attention: i.e. no cotton balls, not q tips, no shoe shine, no in room slippers

title: “Funky hotel in a great location”
text: Stayed here for 3 days in April with my spouse and two kids. The decor at the Topaz is really funky and fun. The rooms aren't the biggest, but they are more than adequate if you are out doing touristy things all day and just need to sleep at night. There was a fairly large dressing area outside the bathroom which was nice. The lobby/check-in area is really small, as are the elevators. The location of the hotel is really great. DuPont Circle has lots of great restaurants nearby and it's easy to hop on the metro. It's also possible to walk to the sites -- the Mall, the White House, etc, but it is a hike. Plan to take a cab or the metro back. All in all, we enjoyed our stay at the Topaz and would come back. My kids "tween" aged kids still talk about what a great hotel it is. They really appreciated the sense of style. Also, the Topaz's AAA rates make staying here a fairly good buy (although not cheap) for the location.

title: “Highly Recommended for Family Trips to NYC”
text: We stayed at this property for 3 nights during our first family trip to New York. This turned out to be the perfect place for us. Just a block away from a couple of subway lines, plus the bus lines on 23rd Street, we found the location to be nearly ideal, since we were trying to avoid the crush of Times Square. The room (2 queens) seemed very generous by NYC hotel standards, and both the room and bathroom appeared to have been renovated within the last year or so. Breakfast was standard Hampton Inn fare- we usually avoid the egg choice from the chafing dish, but oatmeal, make-your-own waffles, mini-muffins, danishes and yogurt will fill you just fine for your morning out (if your staying multiple days, though, you should walk over to Murray's Bagels on Eight Ave once). Staff was attentive and professional. We will definitely stay here again.

title: “Unique and Amazing”
text:
We stayed at the Hotel Whitcomb in late March. I picked the hotel because it appeared unique and had history. We booked our room directly with the hotel via phone and only paid about $80 a night for a king size bed. This was our first trip to SF and I wanted it to be perfect and memorable since I would be proposing to my partner on this trip. It was amazing. The hotel staff was courteous and helpful. The hotel decor is amazing from the lobby all the way to the rooms. I can't say enough about how nice the hotel was. There were a few things about the hotel that could be improved however it is around 100 years old and some of age is what makes it so memorable and different than all the other hotel chains. When we booked our room I did it over the phone because I wanted to find a smoking room. They advised they had two out of there over 400 rooms and told me on 3 occasions that I could get a smoking room. When I arrived that was not the case and I was told they did not have any. Not a big deal but was slightly disappointed in the mis information. But after I checked in and was able to take in the beauty of the hotel I forgot about the whole smoking issue and enjoyed it just the same. (Actually we smoked less because of it). If I had to list the worst thing about the hotel I would have to say the water saving shower heads. If I had only one suggestion to make to the hotel it would be to reconsider the shower heads as there are many other water saver heads out there. Just a thought! We drove to SF and used the valet parking where we left our car without worry for 4 days. I don't suggest trying to drive in this city unless you know it well and at $28 a day to park and the public tranportation right out the front door of the hotel there is no need to drive. The public transportation is affordable at a $1.50 for most. If you go make sure to try the Hotel resturant. It is top notch and I had a perfect experience. You should also look up Incredible Adventures for a tour of the Muir Woods and Wine Country. Affordable and completely enjoyable. 
In conclusion, this hotel is a +4star hotel at a -3star price. You will not be disappointed and since my partner said "yes" we will either be going back for our honeymoon or maybe even plan our wedding there. Either way, I will definately stay at this hotel again and after my experience there I think any other hotel would be a let down.

title: “Clean, comfortable and safe”
text: The room was clean, comfortable and very adequate for a budget rate. The shared bathroom was always available and very clean, and the building had an old style charm to it. The east midtown location is ideal for traveling to the other Manhattan spots and the #6 subway is but a few blocks away. Only negatives might be the poor indirect lighting in the room.

title: “Tenth floor is OK”
text: In march we stayed in a beautiful room on the tenth floor. The room was rather warm and small but the furnishing and the bathroom were new and everything was clean and neat, including the corridors. Nevertheless I understand the poor reviews. One time the lift stopped at the fifth floor. On that floor we saw carpet with holes in it and dirty walls.

title: “They are still working out the kinks”
text:
We paid the extra $ for a "club room", which was suppose to include additional amenities (padded hangers, scale, makeup mirror) and located on one of the top 2 floors. When we arrived, they tried to put us on the 14th floor. I explained that I paid to be put on the club room floor and would wait for one to be cleaned. A few hours later, my room was ready. It was on the 20th floor. When I arrived at my room, I was sorely disappointed. It faced water towers on the roof of the adjacent building, and I had no view. There were no amenities. Worse of all, it was right next to the stairwell, so the room was a weird shape and very small for 4 people. I checked the website and read that the "club rooms" were located on the 21st and 22nd floors. I called and spoke to a manager. She said she could have someone bring me the amenities. I told her I wanted the club room I paid for. She then moved me up two floors to the exact same room but on the 22nd floor. I called them again and asked if this was really the size of the rooms with 2 double beds. She didn't seem to know. After some checking, she determined that all the large rooms that have a view of the Empire State Building were king bed only rooms. Therefore, if you have 4 people in your room, you get the small room with no view, but if you have two people in your party, you get a larger room with a view. That seems backwards to me. 
Another problem was the construction on the roof top bar, which was directly above us. Starting at 7 a.m., construction workers were using the stairwell sharing a wall with us. Bang, bang, bang went the door every 5 minutes. Sawing, drilling going on above us. At night, the security people were constantly using our stairwell to secure the construction site. Bang, bang, bang went the door. 
Yet another problem was the television feed for the rooms. We were all set to watch the NBA championship game in our room. As soon as the game started, the television feed would pause and pixelate. We missed every basket made or attempted. Called downstairs. They said when too many guests were using the televisions in their rooms, the "feed" could not handle it. My minor son and husband had to go to the bar to watch the game (not a great place for a child), and the bartender refused to turn down the music so the crowd that was watching the game could hear the television.
Needless to say, this hotel opened before it was ready. Their website falsely advertises these "club rooms" and that needs to be corrected. Won't stay here again.

title: “Great Place”
text: My wife and I again visited Baltimore and stayed at our favorite Hotel, The Waterfront. The staff is outstanding(especially Frank the bell man) and very informative. All of our requests were granted and the corner room was great even though it is starting to show a little wear. The view is fantastic, the food is great you can't ask for more.

title: “This hotel is very nice, but their crowning glory is Amy English..”
text: Amy was involved in our stay from start to finish... & made us feel special & important...if all the staff at this hotel had her attitude & follow through...there would be no reservations available...the room was quite nice & not as small as expected after reading info on tripadvisor reviews...very clean, & comfortable...has nice restaurant & bar...good food...not as Irishy as I thought...very modern...very beautiful hotel & centrally located...had a wonderful time....

title: “Nob Hill exceeds expectations!”
text: My wife, two children, and I stayed at the Nob Hill Motor Inn for three nights in early November. For under $100 a night, we received a spacious room with 2 very comfortable queen beds, continental breakfast, and free parking. From the outside, it looks like a typical 1950s motor inn with a U-shape and parking underneath the rooms. But the rooms themselves have obviously been renovated. They are as nice or better than most chain hotels. The location is on Pacific Ave, one-half block east of Van Ness and 2 1/2 blocks west of Hyde, where you can pick up the cable car. Pacific is amost level so the walk to the cable cars is easy. We purchased 3-day Muni transit passes and rode cable cars, streetcars, and the subway all over the city. Within 2-3 blocks there is a wide variety of restaurants. The continental breakfast (muffins, doughnuts, apples, bananas, and packaged pastries) is quite satisfying. We enjoyed breakfast, but if you want something more gourmet or more substantial, you will need to eat out. The husband and wife owners appear to work all the time and are quite friendly. We highly recommend Nob Hill.

title: “dated but clean”
text: Reasonable rates, clean rooms and friendly staff. Conveniently located near center of city. Airport shuttle comes by every 35 minutes.Starbucks located off lobby. Full service bar. Free Hop on Hop off bus at corner

title: “Just avoid that heater noise”
text:
Be careful with booking via booking.com. They are giving the small rooms which have window to a little hole full with all of the heaters. That sound is incredibly terrible. I had a long journey from Honduras to NY but couldn't find a luxury to sleep. My solution was listening high volume music.
Room was clean, small but efficient. i stayed alone and its quite enough. If you select your room away from that heater yard, hotels location is perfect!
Also the bar in the entrance was cool. You are just a minutes walk away from everything in NY.
(-) 
noise pollution
free wifi is not working regularly
small rooms
(+)
location
bar
ipad docks in the rooms
price per location

title: “Great deal, good location, new hotel”
text:
Stayed there for five days. Brand new Hilton hotel and good location. Really nice to stay in brand new surroundings, rooms etc. 
Right next to subway, financial district, battery park and shopping. Nice to have the opportunity to get away from All the fuzz at midtown. 
Good service from staff in All matters. However problems with the tv several times. They fixed it but could be better. Fairly small room and bathroom but that might be the case because we booked cheapest alternative - about 850$ for 4 nights incl.tax. 
No free wifi in rooms. Should be standard in such a hotelbrand. 
Free coffee/tea in rooms. Refill everyday. 
Excellent cleaning and maintenance of rooms by staff.
Breakfast really basic and below average. 15$ per person. However good service in restaurant. Starbucks just next door.
Would stay there again if deal still on.

title: “Great Location!”
text:
We visited Chicago for a friend's wedding. A block of rooms were saved for out of town guests for a special rate. We were able to find a cheaper price on the hotel's website. My husband and I loved the location. We could walk anywhere we needed to go. Close to downtown shopping, beach, and beautiful Lincoln Park and the zoo. 
We did not spend a lot of time and money at the hotel itself because of the higher prices for food and drinks. We did take advantage of the bike rentals, gym and public computers in the lobby. We really enjoyed our stay and would come again if in Chicago.

title: “Very cool!”
text: This is an old 1914 hotel that has been refurbished. Very interesting and simple art-deco theme. Sort of Bohemian/Hostel type feel. It is nothing fancy, but we thought it was super-cool and fun to be right on the boardwalk. The rooms are very clean -- the bathrooms were especially squeaky-clean, and when we had a problem with the bathroom sink draining slow, they got someone up there in minutes to fix the problem. The rooftop patio was fun in the evening we met some great people up there every night -- from Australia, Ireland, and all over the U.S. If you are looking for a chain hotel atmosphere like Hampton Inn or Fairfield Inn, this is definitely not for you. This is much more hip and fun.

title: “Very impressed ”
text:
The location of this hotel is amazing. From our room we could see the reflections of time square on the adjacent building. You are literally in it! The hotel reception staff were helpful and the art deco feel was great. We took the elevator to our room and whilst the corridor looked a little shabby, on entry to our room we were pleasantly surprised! 
We did upgrade to a deluxe room when booking and I'm glad we did. Big king bed, huge new tv, sofa, leather chair and desk. The room is immaculate and the smell of 'new' still lingers. This room had definitely JUST been refurbished and was everything we needed and more. Expresso machine, air con, fridge, brand new linen and towels. Spotless bathroom!
We had a good black out blind and only a little road noise for saying where we are location wise and only on the 8th floor. This was NO problem.
Couldn't be happier with our choice!

title: “Family vacation”
text:
Great time, great hotel in a great part of DC. Stayed 10 days and they really treated us like family.
Haile (doorman) gave great advice anytime we needed anything.

title: “The location is good”
text:
I was visiting New York from Seattle to attend the Buildings New York Show at Javits. I got a decent deal (for New York) at the Waldorf, so I took it instead of one of the show hotels. the show hotels were southwest of times square, so I opted for a better location and it was a correct choice. I like staying somewhere in the vicinity of Rockefeller Center.
First, I was very impressed with the staff at the Waldorf. they had a number of staff just standing in the lobby who would offer to help without asking if you had the slightest concerned look on your face. The concierge was great and was spot on with the choices. The business center was nice, but fumbled the ball on a package delivery that was guaranteed by 8 AM, but not delivered to me. The Bull and Bear restaurant was closed for renovation, so I could not comment on it and there weren't a lot of other choices in the hotel. 
The room itself was on the small side, typical of New York, I guess. But it had a nice work desk, an arm chair, and a largish flat panel TV. If you want to watch TV, however, it pretty much has to be from bed. luckily the beds was extremely comfortable with many pillows.
The bathroom was a little dated, but everything worked. 
An oddity was that the shower head was at the back opf the tub, on the opposite end from the valve, so adjusting the temperature was time intensive, as the flow restricter made you wait for a while for the temperature to change. Flow was pretty anemic. the room seemed to be very quiet, other than a thin door hardly blocking hall noise.
The fitness center was OK, but pretty standard. Not what I would expect for the price. In some packages you have to pay for it and it is definitely not worth paying for.
All in all, not a bad stay. I have stayed at the Palace and think that the Palace is a little better, but is probably more expensive. I wish the hotel had a tower lounge.

title: “CK Sayers Visit”
text: Great place to stay. Room was clean and breakfast was available at 5:00 a.m. The hotel was very affordable!

title: “Stunning quiet elegance - so perfect in every way.”
text:
Generally we stay at the Palmer house (and we love the place). We decided on a change of place, it was just the two of us in the city celebrating our 16th anniversary.
We checked in late after a wonderful dinner. The staff was expecting us, knew it was our anniversary and quickly had us checked in and up to our room.
The view was stunning, the room magnificent. Nothing small about it, a full two room suite - both rooms were very large and spacious, well appointed.
'
The bed was perfect, the view lovely and the room divine. 
Breakfast was a large buffett with a full assortment of items (nicer than average for a weekday buffet) - eggs to order, fresh fruit everywhere, smoked salmon - a very nice meal.
I lost my valet ticket....no problem...within moments I had my truck and we were off and on our way.
The hotel, it's management and staff are to be congradulated.

title: “Excellent Location and Clean Rooms!”
text:
This hotel is in an ideal location (Corner of H/14). I could walk to all of the sites I was interested in: Holocaust Museum, Smithsonian Museums, White House, etc etc. It was also very close to a Starbucks, Cosi and CVS Pharmacy (was cheaper to buy snacks/water here then in the lobby store).
The rooms are small but this was fine since the location was great. The maids were great. The room was always neat and clean when I came back. There was a few stains in the bathroom that were there when I got there and there when I left that were a bit gross (blood on mirror for example). I am in hotels too often that I often bring a little thing of Clorox wipes and wipe what I know I will be touching in the room (yes you can call me anal but that's okay). 
When I first checked in I was put in a room behind the elevators. I returned to the front desk and was promptly put in another room. 
The bell hops/concierge was very helpful and knowledgeable. 
There was free WIFI everywhere in the hotel... huge incentive to book here again! 
So with all good things come some bad...
1. The female bartender (I cannot recall her name) was good at service. However, I heard her talking loudly about patrons of the hotel in a negative manner (for one example, a guest had come down to the lobby in an unflattering outfit. The bartender went on and on about how people need to look in a mirror once in a while and just because they sell tube tops doesn't mean you should wear them.) I also heard her disparaging fellow employees. (I guess she use to be the manager/boss of a co-worker. She regretted giving this woman/co-worker such a good recommendation because now she is stuck working with her again.) 
As a guest/patron of the hotel, I was wondering what was being said about me when I walked away from the bar. It was just unpleasant and unprofessional.
2. The Grist Mill's menu is very limited and cannot handle special requests. I just wanted a bowl of pasta and was told that was not available. I asked if the pasta dish on the menu that had shrimp in it could be served minus the shrimp... well we could switch it out for chicken but it has to have on of those in it... um ok.

title: “Good enough”
text:
The Travelodge is a functional hotel, perfect for a single night stop.
The desk staff were efficient.
The room was clean and comfortable.
The neighbourhood was not the nicest, but after an 11 hour flight, we weren't planning to venture further than Dennys, which is at the front of the property.
The breakfast was very chaotic. There is no seating in the breakfast room, and little seating outside. We ended up sitting by the pool. The breakfast room was very untidy, with cereal spilt all over the counters and trash not put in the bin. Breakfast offered 1 bagel per person, but unlimited cereal, coffee and juice.
The free shuttle will pick up and drop all over the airport. There are the usual phones in the terminal building. We were dropped at our car rental instead of the terminals.

title: “Absolutely LOVED it!”
text: Hotel Giraffe completely exceeded my expectations. Located in the Flat Iron district/Grammercy Park- in a very quiet neighborhood (for New York), yet a short cab ride, or walk, away from NY hot spots, including SOHO, and Penn Station. Small boutique, with only 50 something rooms, so not really busy. Staff is extremely helpful, always with a smile. As soon as you walk in the door (opened for you, of course), your bags are wisked away. Beautiful rooms- modern, art deco-y. Gorgeous. Breakfast in the lobby (free) with the best bagels ever, and in the afternoon, free champagne, tea, and cookies. Everybody should come to this hotel.

title: “Close to Where I Needed to Be”
text: This being my second time staying there I can say that the service and staff are great. The room had everything I needed and comfortable. The location was perfect for where I needed to be and while I didn't use the pool it looked clean and well maintained. I will always make my reservations there whenever I come back to the area.

title: “Great Staff”
text:
My wife and myself stayed at The James for just under a week earlier this month. I'd read a lot of the reviews here and was sceptical as to whether the staff could be as helpful as everyone said they were. Having experienced them first hand ....the are really great, very helpful and made us feel at home.
Other than that, really enjoyed The James. Fantastic location, near some great restaurants and the subway. Room was nice and quiet so both of us slept very well. Would definitely stay there again.

title: “Very good hotel in very good location”
text:
We stayed here for 5 nights, after staying in New York for 2. Took the Amtrak train from Penn Street Station, New York to Union Street in Washington. Train was very comfortable.
On arrival at the hotel, we were met by friendly staff. Our room was lovely, spacious and clean.
Ideally situated for the Air and Space Museum - 2 minute walk. 
When we travelled the 'Circulator' bus wasn't operating in the area of our hotel, so we opted for the underground, which was only $9 dollars each for the day. Great way to get around the sights, and it went as far as the Arlington Cemetary and the Pentagon.

title: “Great location”
text:
I was in town for a convention from June 7-11.
Great location: This was an awesome location for shopping, dining, and walking distance to Pike Place. The convention center was literally a block away but not connected to the hotel.
Hotel dining: I did not utilize room service but for being a Westin, I expected a little bit more. There is only a Ruth Chris and a Starbucks at this location.
Room: Very nice room that can fit two people comfortably.

title: “Unless you like to stay in filth, do NOT stay here!”
text: I will begin at the very beginning. When we pulled up I ran in to get checked in. I asked where to park and the attendant said "It's safer up front, park under a light." That should have been my first clue! The smell in the lobby was not appealing. What I didn't realize is that the floor we were on would smell much much worse. It was a mixture of bug spay and stale cigarette smoke. We arrived in our room and it smelled like I just walked into a bar, a mixture of stale cigarettes and B.O. It was so bad we opened the patio door. Immediately I noticed a roach next to my best friend that had just locked the front door. Within seconds of entering I had to kill a roach!!!! Then I saw the bathroom. The mirrors, tub, sink, and floors were filthy, nothing was clean! I posted pictures of the horrible conditions. I immediately called the front desk and received a refund. Needless to say we found a much better place to stay that night for the same price. This place should be condemned.

title: “Great location with terrific security”
text: Well located for travel with either a car, or for public transport. The undercover parking is extremely safe because of the security gate (swipecard operated), and there are security cameras monitering the hallways. We also felt perfectly safe walking in the area, even at night. The hotel has an inner courtyard. The rooms overlooking this wee courtyard are extremely quiet. The outer ones on the road sides are also fairly quiet because of the double-glazing, and also have good views. The only problem we encountered was that our swipe cards didn't work on the parking garage door, but it's probably been fixed by now. Apart from that, it's a fantastic hotel and we look forward to returning again.

title: “Great Convenience meets great value”
text: On a budget but need a good hotel close to the Capitol Mall and congressional offices? This hotel is for you. A room price of under $200 within walking distance of so many sites, in a hotel with nice rooms and continental breakfast is great value. The Capitol Hill district, with its three story brick late 1800s town house, corner churches, and a vibrant restaurant area is a big plus -- great eats (including the Obamas favorie burger place) are only three blocks away. And the Capitol South metro stop is less than two block -- I was in the China Town shopping area less than 15 minutes after leaving my room. Ask for a room overlooking C Street if you'd like a view of the neighborhood. Another good thing about the CHS, was that the streets are quiet. It feels like a less precious Georgetown.

title: “Great location and value”
text: Really like the Wolcott. Great location and excellent value for money. The rooms are clean and comfortable and the muffins are a nice touch in the morning.

title: “Do yourself a favor give Hard Rock San Diego a try”
text:
The Hard Rock Hotel is a great place to stay in San Diego. It is excellently located in the downtown Gaslamp district. There are tons of restaurants, boutiques and entertainment venues all within walking distance.
The staff treated my wife and me like Rock N Roll stars…. Had a blast

title: “Nice enough...”
text: We booked this motel based on all the glowing reviews here on Trip Advisor. I expected a Day's Inn masquerading as a Hilton...but got a Day's Inn masquerading as a Day's Inn. It wasn't bad, just not up to the levels of some of the glowing reviews here. Check in was easy, the lobby staff was nice. The lobby and breakfast area was clean, but there was a strong odor of some sort of incense. Sadly, the room was the same way. The wife didn't mind, but it drove me nuts. That said, the room and beds were clean, as was the pool area. Since this is a motel, there's no interior corridor. We humped our luggage up the stairs to our second floor room (didn't see the elevator). That's fine. The door stopper on our door was broke so we used a chair. No biggie. The laundry is on the second floor, and shares a room with the exercise equipment. Word of warning for those planning to use the exercise room: the air conditioner was NOT on when we went to wash clothes. It was HOT in there! I would check an hour or so before you plan your workout. We didn't try the free breakfast (Denny's was calling), but the wifi worked great. Location seems good for air travellers, and the price was right for our family of four.

title: “Great Stay!”
text: This hotel is awesome! The location is great and the staff is really friendly and they go out of their way to make you feel at home. There are lots of restaurants and shops within easy walking distance and the hotel restaurant is top notch, too. If you're a Priority Club member, they have a weekly Manager's happy hour offering drinks and appetizers. They also raffle off Priority Club points to get you closer to that free stay or other goodies!

title: “Staff very friendly.”
text:
Booked on the internet through findnewyorkrooms, after booking I came accross this site and read all the reviews and was a little worried given some of the bad reviews.
When we arrived Edward at the desk informed us that the hotel was full of police officers from all over the world staying as guests, so we felt pretty safe knowing that.
This hotel for the price is very good, yes it is a pretty old building, and yes it does have a hand operated elevator(which is staffed), but why some guest see this as a problem I do not know, if anything it gives the hotel character.
The rooms were basic but very clean and the location of the hotel is ideal for sightseeing NY. (5min to Empire State)
This was me and my partners first visit to the states so we were going to Washington DC for a few days and then going back to NY the day before our flight home, we did not book any Hotels for our last night, but on our first day in NY we decided to stay that night in the Deauville, what more of a recommendation do you need than that.
A big thank you to Edward and Emily at the desk who could not have been more friendly :)

title: “Good price and good area.”
text: The staff were very accommodating and nice for handicapped traveler. Excellent continental breakfast and nice pool. Too bad there was a railroad close by, but overall very nice Hotel.

title: “Perfect stay!”
text: Our stay here was great! We had a nice room with a view of the beginning of the riverwalk, it was always cleaned well when we came back everyday. The hotel is off the main part of the riverwalk just by a half of block which made it quieter and more pleasant. The restaurant downstairs-Signature Tapas was excellent with good prices, we ate two dinners and a breakfast there, all good meals. We did not use the pool area, but did see it, small but seemed clean and pleasant with tables with umbrellas and deck chairs.

title: “THIS IS A DEFINITE PLACE TO STAY.”
text: Beautiful hotel, beautiful grounds. Friendly staff. Awesome happy hour/snack buffet! Great pool and hot tub. Rooms were spacious and we got two rooms across from one another. Both had amazing views! This hotel is also within walking distance to several restaurants and Paradise Hills Mall as well as a Target. Will definitely stay here again if I'm in this part of the city.

title: “Great price and the great staff makes this place a best buy!”
text: The five of us certainly enjoyed our stay at the Days Hotel Circle. We were there for seven nights and were treated wonderfully. The front desk people were polite and extremely helpful. This hotel provides free shuttles to and from the airport, Sea World, and the Zoo. Who can argue with comfortable, convenient, free transportation to the biggest attractions the city has to offer? The shuttle drivers were also courteous and helpful to us 'tourists.' The ladies that cleaned the room deserve an award. Imagine how much "stuff" five people had with them for an 8 day/7 night trip! Yet, they persevered, and performed miracles every day. The hotel also has free Wi-Fi, a public computer in their lobby, and a beautiful, sparkling pool area. Negatives? The front desk could use extra personnel on duty, especially during the busy check-out times. And the Hotel Circle area needs restaurant choices outside the hotel's restaurants.

title: “Good price, great location, great staff”
text:
Our stay there was really good!
The staff was very kind and helpfull. They convinced us to stay there and we do not regreet about the decisión.
The price was very good.
It is located just 600 meters of girardeli square and fisherman warf, so we walked there. Even at night, the way to the hotel was quite, lighty and safe!
On the other hand, we could find bus stops for where ever place we wanted to go!
The rooms were nice, clean and they had a fridge. I think other people got rooms with microwave!
The combination of price, location and kindness of the staff definitely make our vacations in SFO a great time to remember!

title: “Non Disclosed charges”
text:
My wife and I stayed one night at this hotel and was charged $45.00 for parking in their parking structure. Not only is this obviously and extremely exorbitant, there was no disclosure of this charge ahead of time for the traveler. Unethical business practice.
What we saved in a attractive room rate, the hotel more than makes up for in undisclosed charges. Shame on them!

title: “Good Location”
text: Parc 55 is a nice, clean hotel. Great location, 2 blocks from cable cars and BART. We had a room on a higher floor with some good views.

title: “Good Service, Great Location”
text:
We stayed at the Affinia for 5 nights at the beginning of Aug 2009.
We were meeting 2 groups of family members from different towns and requested to have rooms next to each other, which they were able to accommodate.
We checked in, went to dinner and when we came back we realized the air conditioner was not working. We called the front desk (around 11:30pm) and someone came up right away and moved us one room down, which was a complete upgrade from the room we had before, no questions asked and we didn't have to switch back for the rest of the trip!
The hotel is located in central Chicago, right off the magnificent mile. In walking distance to every sight seeing spot you can think of (some walks longer than others).
It is also immediately next door to Traditional Chicago Deep Dish Pizza --- go early, no reservations on weekends.
For the things not in walking distance (wrigley field, various restaurants) The Train was about 3 blocks walking distance. 
The staff was nice and even gave us recommendations to local bars (that were not expensive)
The skytop bar is cool, but way over priced.
Also the main elevator that goes to the higher floors is very slow. 
Housekeeping was great.
Before you go, you can go online and request the type of pillow you want (down, ipod speaker, buckwheat, memory foam, firm)
They also allow you to borrow (complimentary) and IPOD walking tour of Chicago
We used the fitness center a couple days, very small but adequate...a couple elipticals (with TV attached), bikes, weight machines, water cooler... about the size of one hotel room.
There is Duane Reed around the corner for snacks and beverages as well.
All in all great deal (we booked through a different hotel website, not directly through the hotel and got a great deal.

title: “Great!”
text: I tried this Hyatt Place because it was a bit cheaper than the Hyatt Place located near the OSU campus. I have stayed at that Hyatt Place several times and you couldn't ask for a better room so I was anxious to compare the two. The looks of this Hyatt Place could have you wondering what kind of room is on the inside. The outside is very plain and not modern at all. The concrete coming in to the lobby could use some power washing to give a more welcoming and clean entrance to the hotel. Inside though, the hotel is wonderful. Very modern and decorated nicely. The lobby area is smaller than the one on campus but every bit as nice and clean.The rooms are exactly the same only with a smaller bathroom. Wonderful beds and pillows, a huge flat screen tv, granite countertops, and very clean! I went down to the breakfast area the next morning and the continental breakfast was very nice and had a various array of breakfast foods. I was very satisfied with this hotel!

title: “Renoir”
text: We stayed at the Renoir hotel in September next time we will be finding another hotel. It was clean and the hotel staff were quite friendly, but the surrounding streets were a little bit scary, we looked outside of our window and saw people using drugs and our tour driver told us not to leave the hotel at night as it was not safe. It was only 2 streets away from the nice part of the city and there is a little club in the hotel which gets busy. we did have a good time, beautiful city.

title: “Thanks to all the TA reviews”
text: Thanks to all the TA reviews, there were no surprises. Queen room small, but I was expecting smaller. We had a total of 8 pieces of luggage and shopping bags and with care managed not to trip over anything. Doormen very friendly and helpful. Desk staff not so, but not rude. Just bland. Coffee service in lobby until 10 AM, unless it runs out at 9:45 AM, which it did and the not so friendly desk staff said they would not be making any more. Plan on returning to Chicago this summer and unless Priceline changes its rating, will probably get stuck here again. Would never pick this hotel, but for $60 or less a night, you are getting good price to value.

title: “Not blown away”
text: I happened to stay here as a result of Hurricane Irene. We took refuge in Boston, rather than sit if our in Cape Cod. It was pouring with rain when we arrived, one take an escalator from the entrance to the lobby/reception/bar. The noise was horrendous, once we reached the check in desk (10 minutes), it transpired that there were 2 weddings going on simultaneously and guests from both seemed to be everywhere, as were dogs, one the size of a horse. So firstly if you are looking for a very loud cacophony and a menagerie, this is the place for you. I had 2 rooms, was upgraded for one of them to a corner grand deluxe, nice enough, though only one bedside light for a twin set up, a little odd and when I mentioned this to the duty manager, his response was perhaps the hotel wasn't for me! That aside he was friendly enough, though needed some serious training when it came to customer care. The second room was a little cramped; basically it was nothing special, though nothing bad. The gym is located at the end of the lobby/reception/bar beyond the lifts, it’s a windowless cupboard and looks like an afterthought. We had one meal in the evening at the hotel and thereafter ate out, very uninspiring. How this hotel can be part of any "Luxury collection" I have no idea. The problem with it is that is doesn't quite know what it is and who it’s catering for. Once they sort that out, then perhaps it would improve. Finally, though I hope this was a one off occurrence, the hotel parking team lost our car they had parked and it ended up after 45 minutes for me to have to go and find it in the 7 storey car park, strangely it was park right by the entrance! Yes the location is good, but the hotel is well...................it’s just ordinary, feels like any airport hotel chain, nothing special.

title: “Handy”
text:
Good Place to stay for early flight the next day.
Have a shuttle bus that takes you to the various terminals. 
Rooms are clean, seems fairly new. Well decorated. Quiet
Computer access in lobby is free. also have a business center you can use for a charge.

title: “Room review”
text:
General area outside was dirty. Pictures advertising this hotel are not a true reflection of what it is actually like. 
Room was not clean found hairs all over bathroom floor the room itself was shabby and in serious need of makeover. Staff we met were pleasant and welcoming however would not stay in this hotel again.

title: “Great Location, but . . .”
text:
Great location in the northern end of Michigan Avenue. We chose the Allerton because of a previous good experience. This time, very disappointing:
Entrance is small but cozy. This is a classic older "vintage" hotel so there are some things that deserve grace. Here are specifics:
Reception - good, attentive, quick
Elevators: VERY inefficient, bring a book or a scarf to knit, you will need something to do as you wait. They are extremely small so if your group is larger than 5 or more than a carry-on luggage you will need two. 
Hallways: carpets need replacing - old, stained, dingy. Understand the vintage decor, but the carpeting still needs updating.
Room: We were given the guest room of a suite. Way to small for our foursome. We shimmied our way around the luggage and packages all weekend. No closet, no coffee-maker, no iron or board - very annoying to be so cramped. Beds were comfortable, room temp good. The view of the alley was disappointing and the dumpster noice and talking in the alley all night long was terrible. The windows are so thing it seemed like they were open. The sirens from emergency vehicles drowned out the dumpter sounds. 
Bathroom: Amazing how a architect could accurately design the door to be about 1/16 of an inch from the basin countertop! I've never seen such precision! SMALL. An overweight person would have trouble getting in that bathroom - seriously. The shower was roomy, clean, immediate hot water, nice big shower head and good pressure. Towels were old/used. 
Restaurant: They only serve breakfast and lunch - plan ahead to make reservations somewhere else. Breakfast menu was good. We had the buffet - eggs, bacon/sausage, potatoes, oatmeal, variety of cereals, nice variety of fresh fruit medley, bananas, apples, oranges. JUice, coffee and feshly made toast included. Cost ~ $15. Servers were excellent - very attentive.
Overall impression: a 2 out of a 1-5 scale with 5 being best. Some things a 1. I would stay somewhere else. Stay one or two blocks off Michigan in a better hotel and for less. 
Value - 1 out of 5. For $300 we should have requested another room.

title: “Good Stay! Perfect for family travelers”
text: Found this hotel in room-saver coupon magazine. Very good price. Friendly staff. Room was in great condition. The bathroom is very spacious. They have basic cable which was okay. What I liked about it the most it was that it had a gated parking lot.

title: “Family Vacation”
text:
The stay was a great experience. The staff was very helpful with all our needs including with directions around the city. The rooms were very clean and they would shop for your groceries if needed. Their breakfast was different daily and had a large assortment from full or continental what ever you like. They also had dinner daily but we never made it back to the hotel in time. There was so much to see.
Not knowing anything about the area when we made reservations we were surprised how easy it was to get around. The subway{and buses) was a few long blocks away and was easy and fast to go anywhere in the city including Arlington. We felt safe walking in the area and could walk to White House. There is not any other attractions close and you will need to use transportation. You could stay anywhere in the city because of transportation but we could not have picked a better location or hotel for us.

title: “Strictly a convention hotel.”
text:
I accompanied my husband who attended a conference at the adjacent convention center. I agree completely with previous reviewers; the Grand Hyatt may be okay for a business traveler, but I do not recommend it for the leisure traveler. We requested one king bed, we got two doubles. The sheets did not fit (too small) and the mattress pads were ripped. The room had no make-up mirror and toiletries were not replenished until requested. The bar was overrun with convention attendees. The room alternated between being too hot or too cold. The pool is a outdoor pool designed for fitness, not fun.
There are MANY other nearby hotels that must be better that this charmless "Grand" Hyatt.

title: “Slept like a baby...”
text: Excellent airport hotel. It's clean and inviting, with great beds and linens and a relaxing hot tub. A shoutout to the front desk attendant who coordinated my husband's return shuttle from the airport rental agency--thank you, you are excellent and efficient. Another shoutout to the earlybird who drove the airport shuttle, you are fabulous. The staff at this hotel take their jobs very seriously. Too bad we couldn't extend our visit through breakfast. Many, many thanks. Stay here.

title: “Excellent staff in an excellent hotel”
text:
We loved this hotel. The location is brilliant and because we were on the 20th floor we were not disturbed by the noise of Times Square at all. The room was clean and well decorated. There was not that much room to walk around but I think that's normal for New York hotels. The bathroom was large and the shower worked well. The only criticism is that there were no hooks for the bathrobes which sounds trivial but actually was quite annoying! The hairdryer provided didn't work but when I phoned reception for a replacement a very cheerful porter turned up with one within 3 minutes.
The staff in this hotel are incredibly nice - the bar staff especially go out of their way to be pleasant. The view from the bar is amazing and the food is lovely and reasonably priced for New York.
The decor in the lobby and bar is cool contemporary. The music is a bit loud but it's quite groovy.
We would definitely stay in this hotel again.

title: “Beware!”
text: If your a frequent travler like I am, this is one to avoid. This sure isn't the LaQuinta on the TV commercial. Toilet would not stop flushing all night. Front desk didn't have anyone to fix it or another room. Needless to say I had two more bags to carry out the next day under my eyes. TV stoped working in the middle of the night to cover the sound of the toilet flushing. This place is just dirty in one of the least attractive places in Seattle. If you like Denny's, Jack in the Crack or The Greasy Spoon across the street for your dinner choices then your in luck. They are all in the same parking lot. This is the kind of experience that makes me want to find another job.

title: “Friendly, under construction, promising”
text:
Stayed here on my way home from a family trip, time away for my wife and I. It had a wonderful location in downtown Indy. The hotel itself was quite old, undergoing refurbishing, probably why we got the nice deal that we did, including valet parking. Everyone was pleasant, had a club level room and access to the club w/ the rate. Was surprised at how little was offered in the club in the evenings . . . diet coke, coke, sprite and coffee/tea and some fruit. It was quite sparse compared to other clubs that I have been in. I was surprised, but another review had mentioned it, so I was not completely shocked. However considering that this was a Westin, I was still surprised. If I had paid a premium rate for the club access, I would have been extremely disappointed. Breakfast was nice, I was late getting there (after posted hours), but they still had enough that I was satisfied and it was well prepared. The gentleman that staffed the breakfast was very helpful.
The room was nice, plenty of room for two and the bed was comfortable, but the refrigerator situation was weird, never used it but never really figured out what it was all about. The bathroom was very small, adequate for the two of us, but smaller than in any of the last 20 hotels that I have stayed at, again I was warned in a prior review, so not surprised. Finally, another funny point, there was only one bathrobe available (even though the reservation was for two adults), luckily my wife desired one and I did not, could have been problematic if we both wanted it.
Overall, nice, clean and we had a good deal, would stay there again under the same circumstances, but would not want to pay more than we did.

title: “Great Breakfast”
text: Great Managers Reception in evening and cooked to order free breakfast in morning. Traveling by yourself or family it's a great deal.

title: “Decent Accomodations”
text:
Hotel overall was OK. Rooms recently remodeled and all feature nice 42" LG LCD TV's. Not sure if they all have microwave/fridge but mine did. The front desk staff were very nice and also the morning breakfast staff. I asked for my favorite Hampton bkfst (biscuit & gravy) and the next day they served it! Housecleaning staff was a bit off this week. First night, I had no hairdryer in the room. Second night, no wash cloths! 
Room was comfortable. AC/Heat is a through-wall unit with attached controls. No wall mounted thermostat. Price ($189) was on the upper end for this hotel. Hallway carpets need updating/replacing. Lobby being renovated now. I would prob stay here again if I had to, but may seek something better for the $$.

title: “30th birthday”
text: Beautiful hotel the decor is fabulous. The customer service it awesome...for the second you step foot here...from valet to the front desk bellhop to door service...bring dress clothes free happy hour on the bar next to lobby...great location to everything the loop and the mile..first time in Chicago and I'm so glad I came here....and thanks again for my special gift upon entry. Every visit to chi town I will stay here they have my heart.

title: “Good location”
text: We have just got back from staying in this hotel and to be honest after reading some of the reviews on here i was a bit worried if it was going to be OK - but - our room was clean, had hot water all the time and clean towels everyday, the reception staff were friendly and helpful and the location couldn't have been much better. The only negatives i could say were that we needed a new mattress in our room, the lift was slow and the walls were thin. The reception staff will sort out a taxi for you to the airport, they have free safety deposit boxes in the office and a safe room to put your bags if you aren't flying til late that day. The Captains Cafe next door was great for breakfast and was cheap too. The Empire State Building is only 2 blocks away, we really enjoyed the downtown bus tour, the tkts boxes have theatre tickets on sale everyday, to see the Statue of Liberty - the Staten Island Ferry - is a good idea as its free and you go right past the Statue.

title: “Excellent service and accommodations!”
text: Without notice or reservation on our part, Mr. Pete Ikonen was excellent with his attention and recommendation of a vacated "honeymoon suite" for my husband and I to stay in for the night. We will recommend this hotel!

title: “great location with wonderful bay view”
text: This hotel is located at a great location - Harbor Island. We had a room with a wonderful bay view. It is very pleasant to wake up and see the bay, all the sail boats, and people walking on the board walk. The room is not big , but is clean and service is nice. The front desk is courteous and helpful. I had an issue with wireless connection and the manager was kind enough to let me use the connection in the room without charging me. The hotel was remodeled 4 years ago. The bathroom has a tub and shower which is nice, except it is hard to control the water temperature. It it either too hot or too cold. The bed is a little too soft. Other than this, it has been a very positive experience.

title: “Spectacular views and location from the Westin NY”
text:
We stayed at the Westin New York at Times Square in August 2005 for our Honeymoon in New York. The hotel is one block away from Times Sqaure and in the other direction one block away from the Broadway shows, all in all a fantastic location. Upon arrival we were greeted from the Taxi by Westin Staff with a smile, they collected our bags from the car and took our name to get them sent to the room, we were then able to check in without the hassle of luggage. The bags arrived in our room a couple of minutes after us. 
When we went to check in we were again greeted by friendly staff who upon finding out it was our honeymoon promised to move us to a corner room the next day for the remainder of our holiday - which was done. I have to say both rooms were spacious, clean and had spectacular views and I would have been happy staying in either room, although the corner room gave you a better landscape of New York and was overlooking the Hudson and the Statue of Liberty.
The bed was extremely comfortable and the shower nice and powerful, although the bath is not as comfortable as you would hope for with the description given on the web - minor problems though. 
We were also able to get tickets to see "The Producers" from the Hotel ticket desk 2 days after arriving in New York - which saved queuing for hours in Times Square. As with any hotel the bar is outrageously expensive, but with New York on your doorstep who needs it. I thoroughly enjoyed my stay at the Westin and New York and would recommend it to others.

title: “An experience rather than just a hotel, and a great one at that”
text:
Stayed here for two nights and loved it. Location was excellent, good and close to Beale (although there are a few beggars who clearly hang about outside the gates later in the evening). Room was very nice, building was very impressive, self-parking was easy. Worth a visit to the memorabilia room to acquaint yourself with the hotel's great history, but also visit Lansky's in the lobby (still run by the extremely friendly Hal Lansky, who's father sold Elvis his coolest clothes, and its walls are adorned with signed memorabilia from Carl Perkins to ACDC). Obviously, the march of the Peabody Ducks is a sight not to be missed, as is the sign for "Duck Palace" on the roof (which also offers some great views of the river and the city).
Staff were very friendly and made everything extremely easy (except for one of the staff on the lobby bar was a bit rude in my opinion, but hey its his tip to lose). And no one can be friendlier than the excellent "Duckmaster"! 
Overall, our stay here was one of the best things about our time in Memphis.

title: “It was Great!”
text:
The hotel lobby was nice and the brekfast was cheap to buy even if you hadnt pre-booked it. The rooms were great and the beds were super comfy. was in a great ocation with a short walk to pretty much anywhere in the centre and a macy's just 10 minutes away. 
went as a massive group and the hotel staff were great about helping us out and all the conference rooms were nice.

title: “Misleading advertising”
text: Several items were misleading in adversing: The one BR is not really a one BR as there is no door between the BR and the living room; so privacy is compromised if more than 2 persons use the room. The apartments are in 4 different locations; so it was a drag to arrive at 239 West Newton office, only to shlep your bags 6 blocks to your final assigned room. The building is definitely over a century old, so there are no elevators. The bathroom lacks robe hook to hang your clothes while you are taking a shower. One single advantge of 171 Botolph location is proximity to Orange and Green subway lines and Shaw's Market in the Prudential Center. While a coffee maker was provided; there were no coffee or tea bags; some basic condiments (salt and pepper packets, creamer) need to be provided in the kitchen, so guests who stay only a few days don't have to buy full sizes from the market.

title: “Pretty decent stay...”
text: Clean hotel with good access to the south end of Denver's financial district. We got a great deal through Hotwire for a baseball game and definitely enjoyed the roof top pool. It's small but has great views and is a unique addition. Not the fanciest but great for the price.

title: “Romantic”
text:
We go to Pacific Beach once a year and stay at least 2 days. We payed a bit more and and got an ocean front room on the 3rd floor.This was our first time at this hotel. I did alot of reserch and there was some really bad reviews on line. We went any way.We got in late afternoon and watched the sunset from our bed. Add to that the sound of the waves from the ocean. WOW, it was so nice! We spent a lot of time just enjoying the sounds. Then there are some nice places to eat and lots of places to go that are close.We had a great time and will be back for sure!!!
Go on the off season or week day if you hate the crowds.
Jerry & Lonni

title: “Minor theft followed by unsatisfactory management response”
text: I suffered the theft of an iPod from a car I valet parked overnight while staying at the Marriott Courtyard at 866 3rd Ave New York NY in early July 2011. A full report was filled and I followed up with the general manager and corporate customer relations in Maryland. The subcontractor MPS Parking eventually sent a letter denying responsibility. I am dissatisfied with the outcome and how Marriott has handled this. I have been a loyal Marriott customer for many years and am just so disappointed. No one disputes the loss. No one seemed particularly concerned by a theft associated with Marriott operations. While everyone was very polite and professional from my vantage point they demonstrated little interest in keeping a good customer. Such terrible customer service is unusual for Marriott. Perhaps this particular Marriott is no longer interested in being a safe, secure and satisfactory place to stay.

title: “Drop off but no pick up at ship”
text:
This hotel was recommended to me since I could leave my car in their lot while taking a cruise out of LA. The cost was less than another hotel stay plus parking at the pier but it was hardly worth it. 
The room was clean but dark and not at all attractive. I could not get help bringing my bags to the room. When I got to the room my key card didn't work and because I was alone I had to drag all my bags back down to the lobby with me to get another key.
The room faced the street and was pretty noisy.
Next day I took their shuttle to the cruise pier which went pretty smoothly. They did help me get my bags in and out of their van.
When the cruise returned I called for a pick up and only then did they inform me that they don't pick up. 
I had to take a cab back to the hotel which pissed off the cab driver because he had been waiting in line for an hour and a half and all he got was a short fare to San Pedro. Since I didn't want to be dumped in front of the hotel with my heavy bags I told him if he took me right to my car and put the bags in the trunk for me I would make it worth his while so the 5-minute taxi ride ended up costing me $20.

title: “Clean and Spacious”
text:
I admit it's a bit odd to check into a hotel on the twelth floor but my room was large, clean and very comfortable. The sleeping area is separate from the living area and the bathroom is very large. The hotel is convenient to the airport, interstate, and the downtown area. Parking like most other hotels in this area of SD is outrageous. Even though this hotel is in the downtown area it is not actually in the Gas Lamp section which is about a 10-15 minute walk away.
