The pool is indoors and on the twelth floor and pretty basic as is the fitness center. I had breakfast at the restaurant twice and it was very good but overpriced as are most hotel restaurants. The staff were extemely friendly and helpful.
I used Priceline and was able to get the room for $85 /night and while I wouldn't mind staying here again I would prefer to stay closer to the bay or in the Gas Lamp District.

title: “Nice but underwhelming”
text: We stayed at the Deca for one night following a long drive through heavy Seattle traffic. Since I was exhausted I decided to take a short nap---and short it was indeed, because a teenaged girl began shrieking and running through the hallway outside of our room. To the hotel's credit, a security staffer came up and instructed the girls to stay in their room, but shortly after he left, the aforementioned girl was out giggling and running in the hallway. When I went down for dinner, I commented to the desk clerk about our noisy neighbors, and she said, "Sometimes things like that happen." I was speechless, but took that as a cue to seek dinner outside of the building. (The Deca has a small bistro in its basement, where we had lunch: the service was friendly, but the food was an overpriced disappointment. A small piece of grilled salmon was served over a large bed of lightly sauteed sliced onions and peppers. With 2 drinks, the total tab for the two of us came to over $30, and we left hungry. I also might add this hotel has no room service, so forget about breakfast in bed or late-night munchies in front of the flatscreen plasma TV that was in our premium room.) This is too bad, as the room we stayed in was pleasantly decorated and had plenty of space. We had a view of the city from our window, and the hotel is located very close to the University of Washington, where I was visiting. There is also free off-street parking, which is a lot to recommend in a town where parking averages $7 an hour. However, we were disappointed by the noise we could hear in our room. On one side we could hear our neighbors' television, while on the other, shrieking and giggling. Maybe a less noise-phobic guest would like this place: but I really need quiet to sleep well, so I didn't. Beware too, that the free continental breakfast is cleared away at 9 a.m. sharp---something that wasn't mentioned anywhere in the room---so you will miss out if you like sleeping in. I have to say I have visited Seattle many times and have stayed at several different hotels; I don't think I want to go back to this one. There are quieter places with far more amenities in that city.

title: “pretty good location, but awful service.”
text: My boyfriend and I travel a lot, and have stayed in many, many hotels, including several in the DC area. This hotel was not dirty, but the service was truly awful. The hotel clerk was rude and cut me off on two different occasions when I called him from my room asking questions whose answers should have been explained upon check-in. In order to log in to WIFI, you need a username and password, and when I called to request it, he was downright rude. Also, they took a 50 dollar deposit on my credit card, which would have been fine and not abnormal, but they did it without informing me about it first. To top things off, upon checking out, we were told that the clerk who checked us in had set us up for 2 rooms, when we only had one. Just incompetent clerks who weren't very helpful or kind. Also, the breakfast was really expensive, and there was no coffeemaker in the room which was a let-down. There was meter parking across the street, and that was nice to avoid paying the exorbitant charge the hotel was asking for overnight garage parking. Basically, if at all possible, avoid this hotel. There are much better ones in the DC area with amazing service.

title: “Great location and friendly staff”
text:
I stayed there for a week and was given a fabulous corner room for an extra $10. Superb location and very friendly staff. 
I've noticed that some of the other reviews thought the area was a little unsafe, and if you go down some of the side streets, it's not as nice as the hotel location, but the hotel itself was great.

title: “Great location - but tired and in need of help”
text:
we normally stay at radisson for a night or two on our holidays to the USA as the ol' stop over and recover from our long journey (from Australia) and this time hotel was noticeably tired. Our room was in need of repair - torn curtains and hinges on cabinets broken. The carpet also could do with a upgrade.. The service within the hotel was friendly but the Valet car service also needs some attention.. ourselves and watched other guests having to remove own luggage or load own luggage while the staff (who are their for this task) watched but were very keen to put the hand out for the tip..
Overall a disappointing stay and on our return prior departing USA we stayed down the road at the Sheraton Gateway (a little more) but finished holiday on a good note..

title: “Very nice”
text:
We stayed there for 5 days. Excellente location and friendliness of staff. Our room was big and comfortable.
Breakfast is poor.
I will recommend it.

title: “Great hotel, great location”
text: I recently stayed at Dream and was very impressed. The staff was courteous, the room was very clean, and I loved the location. I had a conference at the NY Athletic Club on 58th & 7th so the walk was just 3 short blocks up from Dream. I had meetings in the upper east side, upper west side, times square, and in lower midtown, and because of the great location I was able to walk everywhere. It's the first time I have been to NY without ever having to take a cab. The weather was perfect and the hotel's location to Central Park was very convenient. The price was great, the room was clean and confortable, and I would definitely stay at Dream again.

title: “Adolphus during a conference”
text:
Over the years since 1972 I have stayed at the Adolphus a number of times. I like it very much but this time the experience was a bit different.
While it was during a conference the things I will not were unusual for the property.
Housekeeping was a hit an miss propositon. One day the glasses would not be clean, the next day there would be no bath mat left. And so it went.
Several hotel venues are on a more restricted schedule. We could not host a small gathering for cocktails because the lobby bar is closed on Sundays and Mondays. The tea service in the lobby is on a restricted schedule as well.
I inquired at the concierge desk about a local restaurant and got directions. When I asked if the restaurant was open on Monday for lunch the concierge without calling assured me it was. After a twenty minute drive we arrived to a restaurant that was closed on Mondays. 
I will continue to stay at the hotel as I have for many years, but visitors should be aware of current conditions.
Also there is a great alternative for parking at Dalpark, just up Commerce street.

title: “It's ok...”
text: I stay in NY very frequently. Tried the Belleclaire because of the description I found on hotels. Parisian neighborhood? Look, I know the upper west side can be charming but PLEASE - this is far from a Parisian neighborhood! It's classic NY. Nothing special about this place at all. The mirrors in the lobby give the illusion of actual size, and I suppose to the numerous drunk adolescents and college-aged people staying there, mainly trendy foreignors looking for a cheap deal, it may actually provide that illusion. I was not fooled though.The first night there the bed was wonderful! It's true, very nice. BUT, the second night - sorry, the futon like mattress was enough to make my cranky back scream for anything else.The shower was the loudest I'd ever been in - it screamed like a victim in a Hitchcock film.Cheap hotel overpriced. Don't bother. You can find much classier places for the same money. Just look.

title: “Excellent Boutique Hotel”
text:
Stayed here for the weekend of 12/17/2011. Booked 2 full size rooms with two beds and requested high floors due to some earlier reviews on this site which mentioned subway noise. Upon arrival, they said they only had side by side rooms on the lower floors. When I pointed out that I had requested rooms on the higher floors, they gave us rooms on floor 9 and 10. The 10th floor appears to be the highest. They then upgraded us to corner rooms - very nice.
The rooms were very nice, spacious, and had lots of bells and whistles. The jacuzzi tub was wonderful to use. The electronic operated curtains were also a nice touch. Check in was effortless and they were very accommodating when we asked to store our luggage for the afternoon after we checked out.
I wouldn't worry about the subway noise. The subway does run underneath the hotel and you can hear it. However, you can drown out the intermittent subway noise with white noise generated by the heating/ac unit. Set the fan for continuous operation. It is fairly loud and it effectively drowns out the subway noise. Works like a charm.
This is a small boutique hotel and I think it has a great location and a great pricing. The pricing was attractive because of the soft opening of the hotel. I would definitely stay there again if I can obtain a similar rate.

title: “Totally satisfied”
text: I stayed here for four nights and has no complaints at all! I celebrated my birthday here and had champagne and gifts from the hotel. Nice and clean rooms, good locatation, perfect service and tasty breakfast. Overall I highly recommend it!

title: “Nice Hotel and Staff - Noisy Air Conditioner!”
text: We stayed for two nights for a relatives wedding in Fort Worth. Our room was nice, beds comfortable and above average and clean bathroom. Valet and desk staff very friendly. Quick service from valet as well, although it is expensive at $18/day! Main complaint is the 2nd night of our stay I got very little sleep due to a very obnoxious noise from our air conditioner, which we alerted staff to earlier in the day, but apparently was never resolved even though they said they would send a technician up to fix it. It was so late and I was so tired after the wedding when we got back to our room I didn't have the energy to complain about it..but ended up getting so fed up with the noise, I just shut it off and dealt with a warm room. I would probably look at other options, such as the Omni if I stay in FW again, but I can't say it was "bad".

title: “Another great stay”
text: Unfortunately my mother's cancer is back, fortunately we had the Inn at Longwood to stay at again. The staff is so helpful and nice and the room was quite comfortable. I am very sad to have to use the hotel again, but I am so grateful that the hotel exists where it is.

title: “Great Location and Value”
text:
We did research on Hotels for our trip to San Diego, and found that the Handlery fit our every need. The service was great and knowledgable, especially Michael in Concierge and Jeff our tourguide, van driver! Both were always willing to assist and find info we needed via internet if they didn't know. The one thing that could help is if the pool was heated better! Was a bit cold to enjoy.
Thanks everyone for a great trip to San Diego!

title: “Incredible Resort, Setting the standard with a HUGE water park & Starbucks!!”
text:
Overall, this is an excellent hotel with with an incredible swimming area; a mini-schlitterbahn. The pool area offers a large pool with lounge chair areas on water decks within the pool, beach entry, and lots of shade. There is a large lazy river with many entry/exit points. There is one entrance that offers a down hill rapid ride into the lazy river. There are two additional tube rides, a kids area with three water slides, and an adults only pool. We were at the hotel over a weekend until Wed. and there was never over crowding or lines. Another great point is that the pool has life guards to ensure there is no out of control behavior. This sure beats the pool monitors at the Hyatt resorts that literally watch people endanger others with annoying pool side behavior. 
The hotel itself is very impressive, it is built within the rolling hills of the Hill Country. The interior of the entire hotel is very inviting. The outdoors offers fire pits, outdoor fire places, rocking chairs, tables/chairs, etc. There are numerous areas to sit and have bottle of wine and look at the beautiful scenery or have a meal. The golf course looked very nice and appeared well maintained. 
The rooms were nice and clean. I do feel they should offer two Queen bed rooms vs. the two double beds. The beds were a little too firm but the linens were very nice and the pillows fluffy. 
We ate at the restaurants and enjoyed the food. There is a FULL SERVICE STARBUCKS!! This is a HUGE perk!!! 
I would recommend this hotel over the Hyatt Hill Country. 
The only issue that needs to be addressed is the BEEs...I know they are part of nature but they were swarming around parts of the pool where people had left their fruit garnish in the cup. They were also around the trash containers. If you have a bee allergy, this would not be the hotel for you. I did see a pool attendant spraying trash cans but faster clean up after guests or getting rid of all fruit garnish would be a more effective option. Overall, this is an incredible hotel...the new standard for what to expect from a resort pool.

title: “Comfy and Clean”
text:
My second time in N.Y. I returned to N.Y. to bring my daughter to college. In Texas, hotel rooms are large. However, in N.Y. you will definitely pay a whole lot more for what you get and that includes a hotel room, especially in Manhattan. In Texas, I can book a comfortable two room suite at the LaQuinta (nice chain hotel) for about $120 per night. In N.Y. for $120. don't even think about a two room suite. I was out a lot moving my daughter into her dorm. so I didn't spend a lot of time at the Newton. The time I was there, it was comfortable and served its purpose. There are really good restaurants in the area. My biggest adjustment was having one (very..very slow) elevator - you can take the stairs a lot quicker; there was no assistance with the baggage, which wasn't a too big of a problem because usually when they help, they expect a tip, and of course on this particular trip every cents was needed for my daughter's college expenses, so we were okay in carrying our own luggage. If you're in N.Y. for the social scene and will only use the room for sleeping, I recommend the Newton. If you're in N.Y. 
with your spouse or significant other and there's romance in the air, I would not recommend the Newton.

title: “Good location”
text: The lobby / interiors was great and nice, but the amenties within the room were not so good. We travelled with a baby and wanted to use the mini fridge in the room, but it was filled with snacks which were on a pay per snack bases. We had no space to keep baby milk/bottles in there. The staff in the conceirges were not very friendly either.

title: “A bit disappointing”
text:
In the 'pros' category, this hotel has great location. I guess the reason(s) I was disappointed were that (a) the room I got had very little to do with the ones depicted in photos on the web, in particular mine was not getting much light, and (b) almost inexisting sound insulation; my room was right in front of the elevator and I felt like I was in the corridor and in the street at the same time.
There might be much better rooms of course. I liked the free Internet access too. The other things were OK, not that I use much service anyway.

title: “A little too expensive for what you get”
text: I really have no complaints about this hotel, the staff was courteous, the room was clean (although very small). The sheets on the bed were sub-par, which I wouldnt complain about except for the fact that we were paying $180 a night. Overall, my stay was plesant but I would only stay here again if I got a significantly discounted rate. My advice is to check out the Chancellor Hotel...its closer to union square, has the same size rooms and service, but is half the price. The only difference between the two is that the Chancellor's lobby isnt as nice, and the carpet is older at the Chancellor as well.

title: “Excellent Deal”
text: I would definitely recommend this hotel but feel that it's a bit over-rated on Trip Advisor. We stayed for Thanksgiving weekend and got an incredible rate. The bed was very comfortable and the room big by SF standards. However, there were a few blemishes (cracked ceiling, tear in the sheets) and no real service to speak of. The front desk made check-out a big annoyance. There is no lounge/lobby area so you aren't going to hang out at this hotel--and many others have little perks like a wine hour--but due to the great location just off Union Square, I will absolutely return if they still have great rates next time I'm in the city.

title: “GREAT PRICE FOR WHAT YOU GET”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the Sheraton for two nights upon visiting our Freshman daughter at Texas Christian U for parent's weekend. We had previously stayed at the Omni, which was wonderful. This time my wife secured a very good rate and I happily agreed to give the Sheraton a chance. We were not disappointed. Not only was it comfortable and friendly, the location is very nice. Shula's restaurant is on the premises if you want a nice steak or a glass of wine (or two!). And, Bob's Steakhouse is right across the street at the Omni if you want an elegant steakhouse experience. It is near the convention center, but not near the happening portion of downtown Fort Worth.
Still, I enjoyed the hotel and appreciated the free water, apples, popcorn, etc. as a nice gesture. Would stay again for a rate under $150 per night

title: “Night Hotel NYC - WOW!”
text: Beautiful boutique hotel near Times Square. Sexy as hell! We didn't want to leave. Perfect accommodation for a romantic getaway. Contemporary, chic decor. Hip service.

title: “Excellent Property”
text: Conrad hotels always exceed my expectations and this property was no exception - beautiful hotel, great location, great staff. Rooms are modern, luxurious and clean. Valet was surprisingly quick also, but I guess it should be for $50 a night (really!).

title: “Very Average Hotel - Get what you pay for I guess”
text: We stayed here the last night of a 35 day holiday in the USA. We decided that as it was our last night and we were only staying one night so we would not spend much on the room. Well you certainly get what you pay for. Rooms were very tired, lifts were very slow and the location is at the very edge of Beverly Hills. Staff were friendly and helpful. We did not use any of the facilities as we checked in and out within 24 hours. The room booked was a standard king bed room. We were traveling with our two children (8 year old and 1 year old). Cot supplied at not added cost and as the bed was a king bed we let the 8 year old sleep with us because it was just one night. If you are looking for quality rooms and good location don't book here.

title: “Great choice for New York stay in the Upper West Side”
text:
We loved this hotel. The location is FANTASTIC, just across the road from a market, close to subway, walking distance from Central Park. 
The room itself can only be classified as a "suite", we had 3 closets (one fit all 5 of our suitcases) a bedroom, small lounge and kitchen. Kitchen could have had more utensils and crockery but that is a common complaint amongst all hotels.
All halls and elevators were clean and lovely. We didn't experience too much noise from traffic or other guests.
There was one lady, who cleaned the rooms, who had been at the Beacon for 30 years - she was an absolute delight to speak to. Everyone was very friendly.
This hotel greatly contributed to our delightful New York stay.

title: “Great Price and Service”
text:
The shuttle bus from the airport was prompt and took me to the hotel in less than 15 min. I just had to wait outside under the red sign labeled hotel pick up until the bus came by. The shuttle comes in continuous cycle every 15 min according to the hotel. Upon arriving at hotel, the desk was prompt and I was able to check in to the hotel in less than 10 min. The concierge was helpful and still open at 9 pm and helped me set up a taxi to Hollywood. The helped me to obtain a flat rate for the taxi into the city. I felt safe in the hotel and comfortable.
Overall the room was spacious and clean. The bed was comfortable with fluffy pillows. Only problem was outside lights were too bright shining into window but that's easily fixed with drapes. There were not so many towels provided but that was not a problem for me since it was just me in the room. There is free wifi, which is how I am currently writing this review!

title: “Pretends to be posh”
text: Although we had a good holiday , there was a problem with this hotel which pretends to be luxury and the charges and adverts would make you think it was. We arrived on Wed 24th Oct after flying from Heathrow to JFK and catching air train /subway to 51st/Lexington. Greeted by receptionist immediately and she knew we were staying with them. Given card and told room was on top floor via lift. Didn't need help but help was there. To get to lift had to avoid persons in bar and time share desk and a luxury shop. Got to our room . Well set out with living area and bedroom area. But bathroom was tiny and a wardrobe next to it was almost the same size poor design. One dressing gown only in wardrobe. No wireless present unless you pay 15 dollars a day. (We were paying more than 280 dollars a night for this room). We went out for a meal, restaurant didn't meet our needs. Came back god nights sleep in an King plus comfortable bed. Left room in the morning at about 9am. Came back at 3pm. Discovered that the room had not been made. They refunded 100 dollars off room charge. Room was a bit cold and the air conditioning units were uncontrollable despite my trying. They supplied an electric oil filled radiator. Power went off so not lights and no heating. Air continuing units continued to cool the room. Went for breakfast in the hotel next day. What a rip off. 60 dollars for bacon and egg which was also serve yourselves. Redeeming but not 280 dollars worth was the bed and two televisions. On last day had to store bags charged 9 dollars. Suggest this room only worth 170 dollars a night because it was only 3.5 stars.

title: “The Perfect Solution”
text: The Dunhill Hotel is the perfect change of pace from the large chain hotels where service, attention and comfort are often inconsistent or lacking. Being an historic hotel in the heart of uptown charlotte just adds to the benefits of the warmth and charm of this hotel. I stayed 18 nights over 4 weeks during March and the experience was not only a welcome change but convinced me that there isn't another place in Charlotte I would want to stay. The rooms are updated, comfortable and quiet. Hotel and restaurant staff were exceptionally attentive, courteous, and helpful. The restaurant consistently prepared very good entrees and I found myself eating in more than going out For those who are looking for a needed change of pace and want to have an exceptional experience, check out The Dunhill.

title: “Excellent quality and location”
text:
This was our fourth stay at the Michelangelo (4 nights this time) and the quality has never wavered. The rooms (executive king) are very spacious, well appointed and very clean. The beds are extremely comfortable. One small quibble: the air conditioning/heating units can be set to your individual preference but the fan is set to just one speed and may be a bit noisy for some.
While very convenient to Times Square, the theatres, Rockefeller Center and Central Park, the hotel is tucked away out of the bustle, in a quieter and less frenetic location. Safety and security at night were NEVER a concern in the surrounding neighborhood. Subway stations to several different lines are within two blocks of the hotel and virtually all the lines connect at nearby Times Square.

title: “The Perfect Experience”
text: This traveler has spent many a night in some great hotels. I would rate the Waldorf as among the best of an elite class. Key to a hotel is always the staff. In this regard they get high marks. Our initial room, while satisfactory, was on a lower floor. After spending one night of our 4 night stay, Guest Services Manager, Martin Benster, was able to relocate us to a higher floor with a fantastic view. He understood our needs and made sure we were happy. Service! This being our first visit to Chicago, we relied on the hotel concierge to help us organize our stay. Without a doubt, Edward Tobin is the best concierge we have had the good fortune to know. He was knowledgeable, resourceful, and fully understood what our desires were for our time in Chicago. Service! The hotel and rooms are all contemporary with nice clean lines and quality finish. The rooms are all well maintained with no signs of excessive wear. The beds were comfortable. We had a great night sleep from the first day. The hotel is large enough to provide amenities like a quality spa and yet small enough to give personal attention without a crowd of people to contend with. The spa is really very nice. Again, service was excellent. Staff was present but not intrusive. The location of the property turned out to be great. All of the best shopping in Chicago was very close to our hotel. What surprised me most was the value proposition this property offered. We were ready to stay at a competing hotel rated as one of the best in Chicago for a third more. After visiting the competing property, there’s no doubt we made the right decision. While a nice hotel, it was too large and had far too active of a lobby for our tastes. In the final analysis, The Waldorf Astoria was the perfect hotel experience.

title: “Excellent Service”
text:
We stayed three nights here, getting a bargain weekend rate. I was struck by how service-oriented the staff was (from the various concierges to the valets and bellmen). With the Fairmont name, I had been concerned that the overall feel would be formal and snooty. But it was totally the opposite, such that on the last night I made a special effort to express our gratitude to the night manager. Everybody was very friendly and engaging, and every question or issue that we had was dealt with expediently. Even a woman from the accounting department helped out when we were going to be late for a dinner reservation because our streetcar broke down. 
Our 17th floor room was fine, although in a few spots showed some aging. The elevator system works very well---even as far up as we were, we never had to wait long. The lobby area is elegant. The location is in the Arts District just a block or two from several major art museums, and within a 10 minute walk of the West End entertainment district and the downtown hub. There are many good restaurants nearby, or you can take the free streetcar a mile or so up to the trendy Uptown district. Another plus is that the hotel is easy to find and access if you're driving. Getting out of town is easy---just one block over and you're on an expressway. Parking is valet only, and we never had to wait for our car.
The hotel's fitness room was just OK, but the outdoor pool area is very nice, a large area with lots of foliage. As expected, given the hotel's weekday corporate crowd, the prices in the hotel's restaurant were very high, but we never planned to eat there anyway. We ordered a glass of port one night in the bar, and all they had was one for $20 a glass---ridiculous! We passed. In addition to the restaurant, there is a Starbucks in the hotel, so you can get some muffins, coffee and juice (but no orange juice) there for breakfast. 
In summary, this hotel proves how important a positive, friendly attitude by the staff can be to the overall guest experience. Our experience with the Fairmont was great, and the special weekend rate we got was an incredible value..

title: “A haven in the city”
text: Just home from a 5-night trip to the Big Apple staying at the Omni Berkshire Place. This is a fantastic, calming space in the city that never sleeps! The recent renovation makes for modern and comfortable rooms with superb beds - we never failed to get a good night's sleep. The location is very handy too - only a couple of blocks from the Rockefeller Center, Central Park and the 5th Ave department stores. It's also only a short walk from a couple of subway stations to get you out and about in Manhattan. It's worth signing up to the Omni Select Guest loyalty programme (free to do so) as you benefit from free wi-fi in your room and a cup of tea, coffee or juice delivered to the room each morning for each guest. We ate dinner once at the in-house Fireside restaurant and it was fantastic - try the Philly Cheese Steak dumplings and deliciously entertaining S'mores dessert which stole the show! We didn't have breakfast in the hotel, instead trying Isadora's (across the road) and Dishes (399 Park Ave - this was our favourite). All in all this is another great Omni hotel which I would not hesitate to re-visit!

title: “What a Great Hotel stay”
text:
Figured Hyatt was going to be nice since its a reputable chain, but WOW! We flew in on the red-eye and they let us check in at 6am, which I've NEVER been able to do anywhere. The hotel was beautiful and modern, with great triphop/ambient music piped through out. The room was clean and decorated well The bathroom was huge, the bed was so comfortable. Our housekeeper put things back exactly where she'd found them. 
By far the most helpful was the concierge who we kept making random requests of, but everytime he delivered! Highly reccomend.

title: “Worst La Quinta Ever”
text: This is the worst La Quinta I have ever stayed at. The rooms were dirty, and bathroom was disgusting. We would have gone elsewhere if there had been another option. There were gaps around the door, loud drunken shouting in the morning that no one seemed to care about. When we went to breakfast there was nothing out and when we aksed to have more they brought it out in a trash bag (clean I am sure). Then when we complained we got no reponse from Manager. We checked out and they messed up the billing on their end and i got charged multiple times for the room, even though it was meant to be a split payment. After spending all day on the phone and finally annoying customer service enough we got a response. No one offered to comp a room or anything. I am so dissapointed with La Quinta that I will be telling all of my friends and family to never stay at another La Quinta ever.

title: “Ok but...non-smokers beware”
text:
We stayed here for a week and experienced the big snow storm in February (26 inches!). It's close to Times Square and the convention centre so it was very convenient for us. It's in a pretty safe location. We never had any concerns walking back late at night. We had breakfast in the deli downstairs and at the Theatre Diner one block away. Starbucks is at the end of the block and a grocery story is at the other end of the block. 
The room was spacious but the bathrooms are very small. I'd go as far as to say that the bathrooms are very cramped with very little counter space. The shower provides enough pressure. There wasn't enough light in the shower/tub area though...once the shower curtain as pulled, it was a bit on the dark side.
Wireless access was easy to get for a fee of about $6 per 24 hour period. You have to get an access password every 24 hours from the front desk.
The rooms were clean enough BUT we had specifically requested a non-smoking room. When we arrived on a Saturday at 2pm, we were told there were no more non-smoking rooms and we were given a smoking room. It reeked of smoke...everything did. They sent up an ozone air purifier for us and delivered fresh pillows to us but for the first 2 days, it was still pretty bad. By the end of the 2nd day, the room smell was ok (a combination of the air purifier and us leaving the doors and windows open when we could).
So...would we stay there again? Yes...because after the room stopped stinking, it was a pretty nice hotel and you can't beat the price for that location. Just be wary of the fact that you may not get a non-smoking room if that's important to you.

title: “Fun place to stay”
text: We enjoyed the view overlooking Times Square and found the hotel to be located within walking distance of many great restaurants and shops. The elevator ride is a must. Our room was comfortable, clean and well appointed.

title: “Great place to stay”
text: We stayed her last week for three nights. Great room quiet and spacious. Our shower was great and so nice after a long day of work and sightseeing. We had a room on the 7th floor with a window to the atrium. Good recommendations from the staff on places to eat and how to get around on the public transportation.

title: “Hell Hath a Name - Carter Hotel”
text:
Carlsberg don't do hotels but if they did ... this would be the farthest thing from it.
OK, before I begin what is most definitely going to become a "rant" I should mention the one good thing about the Hotel Carter. That would be its location; it’s in a fantastic place close to Times Square, the bus terminal and a short stroll to 5th Avenue. Ok, now for the "rant".
I read a mixed bunch of reviews before I went on my trip about haunted rooms, thefts and it not being the best of hotels. But I thought "hey, I’ve stayed in some pretty cr*ppy places, how bad can it be?” Well let me tell you, it can be BAD!!!!
We (my girlfriend and I) arrived at the Carter late on Thursday 14th December 2006. We were greeted as we opened the door by the delightful whiff of the greasy cafe that is, for reasons unknown, adjoined to the hotel entrance. As we climbed the hotels steps, tastefully decorated in Technicolor patterns, set off by the various tones of dirt, grime and trodden in chewing gum I took the opportunity to admire the strange dolls that are displayed in glass cabinets around the entrance. As I admired them, and the 3 working Christmas lights that surrounded them, I enjoyed the tasteful out-of-tune music that played in the background. I can only compare it to a musical Christmas card that was low on batteries. Not put off, my girlfriend and I made our way to the reception.
The first thing that struck me about the reception area was the fact that it had clearly been designed to stop people leaping the counter and attacking the hotel staff. This being New York, I thought perhaps these sort of things happen. When I met our "Friendly" night receptionist, I soon learnt that all this security was in fact to keep her in. 
To say this woman was rude is an understatement. She had clearly attended the Adolf Hitler School of charm and passed with honours. After we received what I can only assume was the standard level of abuse and rudeness (and were charged for the pleasure) we made our way up to our room.
We were on the 19th floor, and let me tell you a ride in the lift (which I believe was last serviced upon the buildings contraction) is an experience in itself. Will you make it? Won’t you make it? It’s all very exciting.
When we got to the 19th floor hallway, the first thing that strikes you is the lighting or rather, lack there of. There is a 40 watt bulb once every 40ft, so its kind of like staying in a poorly lit multi-storey car park (but dirtier). We made our way to our room and arrived at our door that was tastefully decorated a nice shade of green/dirt with a few dents and smashes for good effect. 
On entering our room we saw that it was last cleaned some time in the mid thirties. The linen looked relatively fresh, except for a very suspicious stain, and the bathroom … well, lets just say if the room was cleaned in the mid thirties it was by a lazy cleaner who forgot to do the bathroom. But still, as I’ve said, I’ve stayed in some bad places and was not about to let a few decades of dirt, an abusive receptionist and dodgy lift put me off. I was in NEW YORK BABY … 
Having emptied our stuff into the spacious wardrobe (ooh another good point, sorry there was two) my girlfriend decided to have a quick wash before bed. As she did this I lay on the bed and decided to check out the wonder of American television. No sooner had I turned on the TV then came a yelp from the bathroom followed by the door opening and my girlfriend in fits of hysterical laughter. I walked over to see what was going on, when I noticed what was coming out of the taps. Now, I’m not too sure how to describe this but it was kind of like lumpy gravy with flecks of grey. Thankfully, we did have both hot a cold running versions of it. I was going to phone reception to complain when I remembered that this may mean I would anger the receptionist and god forbid, they set her free to come find me. So, we left the taps to run for 10 minutes or so and they did eventually run clear.
So, I went back to my laying on the bed and watching TV when something caught my eye on the wall. I looked, and with the reviews of this being a “haunted hotel” ringing in my head, I saw a pentagram had been etched into the wall. Fan-bloody-tatstic! Immediately wanting to get this out of my mind I thought I go to the window, pull the curtains back, and have a look at New York by night. I was quite impressed with the 5 square foot of Times square I could make out from our window and watched the bits of HUGE advertising boards I could see light up and change. As I stood there, I became aware of my right leg starting to get cold. Assuming the ghost of the Carter had come to get me I slowly glimpsed down to take a look at it. But instead of a gruesome spectre I instead saw that there was a hole, about the size of my fist, in the wall leading directly to the outside world. I was all set to complain, when I realised there was actually a better view of Time Square from the hole than there was from my window.
So that was my initial experience of the Carter, and frankly in the 2 nights that followed, it didn’t get any better. No doubt you are now reading this thinking “well if it was so bad why the hell didn’t you change hotels?” And the reason for that simply was we were there with another couple and the chances of getting 2 rooms on the weekend before Xmas were not good. Plus, I wouldn’t have been able to have such a good rant had I stayed somewhere different.
So, in summary … would I stay at the Carter again? NO. Yes it is cheap, but not cheap enough to warrant the state the place is in or the rudeness of the staff. I would highly recommend more spending a bit extra and staying somewhere where you don’t need several inoculations before visiting.

title: “Excellent service and location!”
text: We stayed here in late July and found this hotel a tremendous value. The hotel was clean and friendly. The staff extremely helpful. people were whining about elevators at this place but we felt they were fine? Not sure why people complained. Hint: Use the service elevator! Easy to do and OK to use! Breakfast was plentiful. Delicious hot food and fruit! Nice. We asked for a Lake view on a top floor. Georgeous!! Why would you gamble with another hotel when this one meets all your needs and is on the Magnificent Mile.

title: “Location Location Location”
text:
I booked my 3 night trip to NY in November staying at the Amsterdam Court Hotel and after reading some of the reviews I was wondering what to expect.
Don't worry!! I'm sure there are much nicer hotels in NY, with bigger rooms, more facilities, etc but if you are looking at only using your room as somewhere to sleep, it is ideal. The room we had, although small, was clean, the bed was made every day and we were supplied with fresh towels daily. 
The location however couldn't be better. Right on Broadway, 5 minute walk to the heart of Times Square and if you want to venture further afield there is an entrance to the underground network close by.
I would not hesitate in recommending this hotel and if you are intent on spending a lot of time stuck in your hotel !

title: “My wife had a work function so I am glad...”
text: My wife had a work function so I am glad I did not pay $1,375 for 6 days. Also the parking was over priced. I can't belivev that parking was not inclded. Wifi wasn't even included. They wanted to charge $10.00 per day to use it. But Maddogs Pub right next store had free wifi and you can have a beer. The hotel was in a great location that is all I can say that was nice.

title: “we loved ths hotel and we are going back.”
text: the hotel had everything we needed. kitchen,pool ,laundry facalities. it was 2 blocks away from the hospital my dad is in. all kinds of diffrent food places around the hotel.

title: “Big city, big promise, small rooms”
text:
Can't go wrong with nyc, but this hotel was a bit disappointing. The lobby and building are very impressive but we were bit surprised that the rooms didn't meet the expectations set on their web site.
For most the tourist hot spots the excelsior is a bit too much of a walk but sub way nice and close and this area has a few places to eat and drink.

title: “They have bedbugs!!!!!!”
text: They have bedbugs and wanted to charge us for our stay based on that we did not let them know the first night we got there... Seriously?!! We will be reporting them to the health department. They said they would call pest control the next day and continue to rent rooms and are not taking the issue seriously. Upon inspection both head boards were infested with live crawling bugs... They do not care about their customers!

title: “Excellent Hotel Best Service”
text: We stayed at this hotel for three nights. I was looking at various hotels for weeks on TripAdvisor before I finally decided to stay at this hotel and certainly don't regret it. We stayed in a two bedroom- one King, one Queen bed suite. Traveling with two elderly parents this has been the ideal room layout. This Homewood also serves a nice complementary breakfast every morning every day of the week, with a manager's reception at night Monday through Thursday evening. I must say that the service and staff are second to none. I am not usually a high maintenance guest, but for this trip I felt like I had made a number of requests, which the staff happily helped me with. The staff are very friendly and the front desk extremely helpful as well as patient. The rooms are very clean and well kept, although the bedrooms were slightly smaller than I thought looking at the pictures online, it still had plenty of room to walk around. I'm all about clean rooms and friendly helpful staff. I give his place 5 stars, and will be staying here again on my next trip to San Diego. In terms of distance, it's about a 15-20 minute drive to Sea World and 15-20 minute drive to the San Diego zoo. You could definitely go back to your room for lunch after spending time in the parks in the morning, take a nap and go back in the evening.

title: “Small but clean”
text: The hotel staff were very friendly and helpful. The rooms were small but clean. Breakfast was included. The food was only average and very crowded even when we went in early. The hotel is very close to Seaworld.

title: “Great value week in very good hotel”
text: Stayed for a week whilst visiting our daughter and son who are both working in Chicago. Not our first visit to this increadible city nor our first stay at the Affinia: We would willingly return to both. We had a mini-suite on the 21st floor with its great view south down St Clair. The room is spacious with a spacious sitting area with a pull out double bed - in addition to the very firm queen bed. Small but very functional bathroom, a good flat screen TV and some nice touches - including use of a couple of guide books, a book of city walks, a pedometer and even a rubber duck for the bath! The 29th floor bar with its open-air section is a very pleasant, if expensive, watering hole, though it was closed for private functions for at least part of the evening on at least three days during our stay. We did not use the hotel restaurant or room service so cannot comment on these. The odd request we made of house-keeping was satisfied, but not as promptly as we would have liked. Otherwise service was goood with very helpful front desk staff and doormen. One minor issue is that during busy periods the wait for the elevator (there are two serving 7th to 29th floors) can be frustratingly long. There is a host of restaurants within easy walking distance and the location, one block from the Magnificent Mile shops, cannot be faulted. Chicago's main attractions are close by - either a short taxi or bus ride.

title: “Great Business Conference Experience”
text: I stayed at this hotel in March 2011 for a two day business conference. It was a great experience, and I was very impressed with the conversion of this historic building into a hotel. My check in experience was fantastic-I was on an early flight and arrived before noon. The hotel staff took care of me immediately, and I caught a cab to the Philadelphia Museum of Art to see the impressive art, silver, & furniture collections for a couple of hours until my room was ready. I had a corner room, which seemed to be a little larger than some of the photos posted by guests on this site. The guest room was beautiful, and beds were very comfortable. My only caution is that most rooms only have large showers in the bathrooms and no bathtub, but that was not an issue for me. My business conference started at 3:00 and ended the following day at 4:00. All of the ballrooms, dining rooms, and breakout rooms were elegant and comfortable. The food was delicious compared to other conferences I've attended at other hotel brands. The service standard at this property is excellent. I would highly recommend this property for corporate events.

title: “Great Location, Bad Housekeeping”
text: I hate to give a bad review on this hotel but I hope it encourages the staff to do a better job. I usually stay in Mission Valley when I come to San Diego on business so I was excited when I found Sommerset Suites on Trip Advisor, the location and price was outstanding. I booked a room for 2 days, when I arrived around 2 PM I was told check in isn’t until 3:00, as is most hotels practice, but I have always found that there is usually a room ready for early arrival, this wasn’t the case. I was told to come back after 3:00. I came back a bit after 3:00 and was told my room was still not ready so I decided to wait in the lobby. After 45 minutes (and watching several other people check in) the manager asked if I had been helped, I told him no and how long I had been waiting. I also let him know this was my first time at his hotel and it wasn’t starting off too well. He told me he would take care of me immediately and returned with a key to an upgraded room, which was a nice gesture. I went to the room and it appeared nice, was a bit dated and the bathroom tile grout was cracking and sections had been replaced before since there were two colors. In the bedroom there were two double beds, made up with the additional oversized “frew-frew” pillows that covered extra space. I unpacked and then left for dinner. When I got back I pulled the extra pillows off and was getting ready to get into bed when I saw a long black hair on the pillow case of the sleeping pillows....GROSS. I took the pillow off and checked the others and the rest of the bed which appeared OK, so I went to bed. The next morning I brought the pillow with the hair to the front desk to show them that they really need to speak with housekeeping; they said they would and also bring it to the manager’s attention. When I got back to the hotel later in the afternoon, the manager apologized for the issue and assured me that his housekeeping manager had inspected my room to be sure there were no issues. I thanked him and then changed and went out. When I got back I tossed the extra pillows on the other bed then went to sleep. The next morning what I found on the other bed when I moved the pillows was appalling....a huge brown stain and long black hair on the cover. Luckily I didn’t sleep in that bed! I was told the housekeeping manager had personally inspected the room, how was this missed!! I called the manager and he came up, I showed him the extra bed. I knew he was embarrassed and I told him he had to see it for himself and I hoped that he would re train his staff. When I checked out, he did give me a free night which was very generous as I didn’t ask for it and, although appreciated, I told him I really can’t say if I would stay at his hotel again because of the cleanliness issues. From the time I arrived till the time I left it was a comedy of errors, I really wanted to like this hotel as it was such a great location. I may give the Sommerset Suites one more try next trip only to see if they took these issues to heart and that their house keeping standards have been improved. I really hope they do!

title: “Great stay!”
text: We've just returned from a great stay in New York. The only disappointing thing in the hotel was the view from our room. Disappointment was short lived - we left the net curtains closed, laughed about it and enjoyed the great views from the penthouse swimming pool. Found the staff helpful and polite. Loved both Norma's and the Burger Joint. Location is great. It was a very comfortable room to return to after busy days in the city. Very good value.

title: “Nice location and beautiful hotel.”
text: Check in was easy, very helpful front desk. Nice, clean rooms with beautiful views of the city. Good size and nice bathroom with all the essentials. Check out was easy via telephone. I'm looking forward to staying here, again.

title: “A charming little hotel with great service.”
text: Had the pleasure of spending three days at the White Swan Inn in San Francisco in early June. What a great place!! It's a small, quaint hotel tucked into one of the side streets in the downtown area. Easily within walking distance to the trolley lines and hundreds of shops and restaurants. All of the staff were very pleasant and very helpful in getting directions or making recommendations for things to see or do. This hotel more closely resembles a bed and breakfast than it does a hotel, and it has the charm of a place from an earlier era. If you're not into the take a number, large hotel scene, this is the place for you.

title: “Good value; good location; what more do you want ?”
text:
We stayed at the hotel as a family of four on a short break. The room was big enough for 2 adults and 2 teenage girls. Clean, well equipped and cleaned to high standard.
The staff are friendly and always eager to help and deal with queries giving tips on places to visit. The bar has a Happy Hour between 4-7pm and the staff are very accommodating quickly remembering your favourite tipple.
There is a well equipped gym which will meet most fitness requirements.
The hotel is well located for all the tourist sites being close to the Metro and on the 'jump on- jump off' bus route and the Circular bus which accesses most places at a $1 fare regardless of where you go. 
Local restaurants are more difficult to find and so I suggest you plan eating while you are out. The hotel give you a list of recommended restaurants. If you feel extravagant the hotel will arrange a taxi both ways to the Chart House which is a stunning experience.
We ate breakfast out of the hotel the first day but I strongly recommend the hotel all you can eat buffet for $16 - fantastic value

title: “loft room”
text: The location of the hotel is excellent we stayed here several times. However the loft room is a very big disappointment . I would not recommend this room. The clearance above the bed was very low on the dangerous side.The stairs very steep.Also the air condition was very loud. This time i did not enjoy my stay.

title: “This is a fine boutique hotel in Times Square”
text:
I don't know what more to say after the title...its a fine hotel in Times Square. Rooms are plush but small unless you upgrade. This is a solid 3.5-4 ''forks'' and as long as you get a good rate, you're in business. You don't want to overpay for this place as its not in the highest tier of boutique hotels in NYC..but you can have confidence that its trusty. I have stayed here several times but only when the rates come down. 
Hope this helps.

title: “fantastic service!”
text:
downtown san jose may not be as glamorous as its other bay area city-type counterparts (read: san francisco), but the fairmont san jose can surely make you forget that! 
its location is central in the downtown area, which is fantastic - walking distance to lots of restaurants, bars, entertainment, and even the light rail, if you are so inclined to try it. 
to start, the lobby is incredibly charming - but only second to the staff, who proved to be very helpful in addressing questions regarding my bill and providing suggestions on things to do in the area. my room was very neat and spacious, and the bed was remarkably comfortable. i was not bothered during my entire stay, and everyone who worked at the fairmont was incredibly friendly and accommodating - from the front desk agents to the housekeeping staff, all who were sure to greet me as I walked by.
all in all, a fantastic stay - would definitely stay here again!

title: “Can I live here? WOW!”
text:
We bid for this room and thought that even if it was a dump, it would suffice for a single night. We were pleasantly surprised! When I first checked in, the front desk clerk (Ashleigh) was sunshine and professionalism. I asked for two beds, which weren't available (it's becoming a pattern with "bid" rooms). I let her know that we were there for the marathon and one of us *cough* snores. She said they weren't completely full, and that she could upgrade me to a suite with a pull-out couch. Worth whatever upcharge there was going to be. None? Did I hear that right? She said that since they weren't full, she wanted to make sure I enjoyed my stay.
I got to the room and it was huge. Small living room, decent sized kitchen, large bathroom, and.... wait for it... a separate full bedroom that felt about the same as the Seattle Renaissance. It was decorated in a tastefully minimalist style, with upscale bedding, flat screens (yes, 2), granite counters, and plush carpeting.
We had a view of the water from our window, and it was a gorgeous sunset.
Breakfast the next morning was a typical breakfast bar, but hooray for some protein! (scrambled eggs). They have weeknight manager's receptions M-Th.
The business center is a single computer and printer, but it's in a nice, secluded room complete with a small library of books. Free Internet throughout the hotel that was pretty quick to load. There's a small store in the lobby with reasonably priced snacks (that, too, was a shock - the reasonable part.)
Parking in Seattle SUCKS. There's no way around it -- except that the one block around the hotel has 24 hour free parking. We were lucky enough to find a spot.
It was 5 blocks up and 6 blocks over to the start of the Seattle Marathon (the stadium at Seattle Center). Enough of us were there that a shuttle would have been good thinking. 
I'm really impressed with this hotel. The service was amazing, and every employee we passed acknowledged and/or greeted us. The hotel was spotless and looks new inside. Even at full price, this would be a bargain.

title: “Comfy Beds!”
text: First time in Romulus and the Marriott was great! Positives: Friendly staff, comfortable beds, quiet and safe hotel. Negatives - hair left on a couple of pillows and the carpet wasn't super clean. Otherwise - everything was great!

title: “A great place to stay in Dallas”
text: At first the location (intersection of 2 freeways)was a little disconcerting, but soon discovered that the location to the train station etc and the quality of this hotel and its staff were all far more important. The hotel car took us to the local shopping mall, the concierge arranged basketball tickets for us on New Years Eve at a moments notice and the gym and pool were fantastic. No hesitation about recommending this hotel to anyone coming to Dallas

title: “A great budget find in Boston”
text: This hotel was perfect, the room was fairly spacious and quite clean. The staff was friendly and had no problem with our arrival before check in time. The breakfast wasn't great, but it was free and better than just donuts. The rates are much lower than downtown. Their is absolutely nothing wrong with the neighborhood, it's not rich, but it's perfectly safe and reasonable. The walk to the subway is quick and easy. I cannot imagine staying anywhere else in Boston unless I wanted a luxury hotel or made some amazing find. There is also a little italian deli nearby for cheap eats as well as a shopping center where you can get most anything you need.

title: “My New Favorite Seattle Hotel”
text: I've stayed at quite a few Seattle hotels - mostly downtown. I don't know how I missed staying at the Mayflower Park all these years, but it will never happen again! It is absolutely the most charming, elegant, gracious, delightful and affordable hotel I have ever stayed at. It doesn't hurt that I had a corner room with a gorgeous view of downtown. My friends stayed next door in a non-corner room and it wasn't nearly as magical as having that view, but the staff was wonderful, the rooms were spotless and well-appointed (great bed, great pillows and bedding, spacious beautiful bathroom), room service was excellent and the hotel bar / restaurant, Oliver's, is worth a visit or three even if you're staying someplace else. Dee-lightful. I may never stay at any other Seattle hotel again.

title: “Not good”
text:
1. So much noise from inside the hotel
2. Need for restoration
3.Old towels
4. Not so clean
5. Good location

title: “Great Stay”
text:
Have seen this Microtel location many times, but never utilized it. Was plesantly surprised with everything. Great location next to the airport. Walked from my terminal gate to the hotel in about 10 minutes.
Rooms were small, but for what you need for a short term stay, it was excellent value for the $$.

title: “Great People, Great Room, Great Experience!”
text: The Magnolia Denver was great. The rooms are clean, spacious, and comfortable. The service was great and the food was wonderful. I would definitely stay there again if in Denver.

title: “Horrible Value!”
text: We were put in this hotel when the conference hotel filled up and couldn't accommodate us. We stayed on one additional night and were shocked to learn that the charge for that night was $486! What did we get for that charge? Not much! Parking was an additional $29/day. Wi-fi was an additional $10/day. Local calls were $1 each. Rooms were comparable to our later stay at Ayres Hotel (at less than 1/3 the price!) in terms of room size and furniture. There was no turn-down service; only one robe in the room; towels were well worn and there was only one towel per person. I had to use the same towel to dry my long hair and my body. The toiletries were "Ritz Carlton" and not special. The shower was very weak and we had to call for service since the tub faucet shot water sideways, causing a wet floor. The carpet was very dirty. The dining room prices were outrageous! Finally, the hotel puts blankets on top of the mattress (under the bottom sheet) which get bunched up during sleep resulting in a lumpy bed. Both my husband and I woke up with sinus reactions leading me to believe that dust mites are a big problem. Frankly, I wouldn't pay $150 a night to stay in this hotel. There are simply too many other, good options in the immediate area.

title: “Noisy but spacious”
text:
We stayed for 4 nights at the Drury Inn. We are regulars to San Antonio and this was our first stay in this hotel. We were on the third floor and the windows were overlooking the street (not the riverwalk) and the noise from the buses running all night was nearly unbearable. There was also a number of homeless people right across the street from the hotel entrance (also not on the riverwalk).
Breakfast, though free, was scarce if you didn't get down there early, as was the Manager's reception snacks. The lobby was extremely crowded during those times. The restaurant was also packed all the time and had long waits, but that was mostly due to it being on the riverwalk.
The room was average on amenities and large. A welcome space for us and 2 kids. Housekeeping was adequate and friendly. Staff at the hotel was helpful when we had questions and could get to them. This was a very busy hotel at all times.

title: “Nice Hotel, a Bit Pricey”
text: Nice hotel, pretty standard with the Residence Inn Brand. The parking was very expensice and the additional tax shot the bill up. The staff was helpful and friendly.

title: “Wonderful place”
text: I and 4 friends spent 4 nights at the BW Hospitality House. We weren't sure if it would be as good as the other reviews promised, but it was. It is very near the Waldorf Astoria, about one block away, at 49th and Lexington. We had the penthouse level. It was clean, freshly painted, remodeled. There were 2 separate bedrooms, two full baths, a living room, dining area, separate kitchen with full sized appliances. The penthouse had a walkout roof top patio that wrapped the room. We didn't spend much time out there as it was January, but it was a neat view - up to other high rises. The beds were very comfortable, firm matresses withpillowtops for comfort. Continental breakfast was nothing fancy, Lenders bagels, oj, milk, coffee, cereal, fresh fruit but they kept it replenished. They changed the towels daily, and gave maid service. It was definitely spacious. The elevator was prompt and the front desk people were helpful. The lobby is really just a desk area. It seems more like apartments than hotel. I was very pleased and would recommend it to anyone who needs a bit of space. It cost us about $80/person/night after you add in all the taxes, which I thought was pretty good for the space we got and the quality of the accomodations. We could walk to Rockefeller Center in less than 5 minutes, and shopping on 5th Ave in about the same. The subway was about 4-5 blocks up and another subway for cross town was another 4 blocks.

title: “Ghetto Nightmare”
text: My first sign of trouble at the Passport Inn and Suites was the bullet-proof "bankteller" baracade the family who runs the motel hides behind. The prostitute sauntering across the parking lot was kind enough to get the proprietor's attention so that I could check-in, otherwise I expect I would have had better luck waiting for the rapture than being noticed in the shadows that envelope this part of Houston. After paying for my intended four night stay upfront, I made my way to my assigned room. Having spent time in third world countries, I think it is fair for me to judge the accomidations as poor; the furniture consisted of a black faux-leather "love seat", a lumpy king-sized bed, a barely functioning television, a boombox, a brass and ebony dresser of drawers and a tragiclly neglected shower curtain. A colony fruit-flys had already been occupying the room for some time apparently, judged by thier particularly agressive nature. I spent one night of the four I paid for, the motels no refunds policy determined that the other three nights the fruit-flys had the room to themselves.

title: “Pleasant in the heart of NYC”
text:
A nice place to spend a few days in the NYC. Hotel is very close to Time square. Rooms are really nice, and breakfast was more than enough. :) 
I will come to this hotel again one day I hope.
Clean rooms. And very good service in lobby. Very friendly guys at the door too.

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text: This is my first stay here and I am very impressed with this hotel. The staff is so nice (especially Mandy and AnnaMaria) and the hotel is very clean. One of the best aspects is Wednesdays during happy hour. They have a managers special with free appetizers and drinks.

title: “nightmare on geary”
text: I will admit that the Hotel Diva is very appealing to the eye though the rooms are extraordinaily small, but the service is absolutely appaling. The staff is rude and pompus and not helpful in the least. I would never stay here again. If you want to check out the aesethics- be my guest. But beware of the staff and especially the service- IT BITES!!!

title: “Would stay again.”
text: I stayed here for 4 days this past July and loved it. It was a ways out of town but that was okay for us. With 2 small kids (3 and 6) we enjoyed the park right across the street. They enjoyed the pool as well. the drive to Great America and into town is not that long (20 minutes or so). We chose to eat out and did not get to try the on site restaurant. the room was clean and comfortable and had a small fridge for us to use. It's a beautiful building, on the older side, but it's been kept up pretty well. Looks like many have their weddings and other function there a lot so there was one day which the hotel looked really busy. We stayed mostly on weekdays so it was quite quiet. I'd stay here again.

title: “Great Location but needs renovation”
text: Great location but some of the rooms have strange configurations. My bathroom was a big as my room. Elevators are tricky for the first couple times as there are no buttons on the inside. You baiscially choose your floor outside and get in. They seem to run faster though.

title: “elegant hotel - world class”
text:
we upgraded to the newer Tower Rooms and I must say we were not disappointed with the views. The room was clean and well apponted although it alawys amazes me when hotel charges nearly 300 bucks a night and doesn't have a cofee maker in the room. Nonetheless, the Fairmont is elegant and compares well with world class hotels anywhere in the world. As someone else mentioned, the bars are quite excellent and especially the Tonga room where there is an interior rainfall, good music and lots of space to dance. 
We only found 2 negatives: first, was the cost of parking which was 50 bucks for overnight. The second was the concierge desk. We found them to be surly and not helpful. 
san francisco has so many wonderful hotels, we'll try some others next time.

title: “Very comfortable hotel, but rooms need darkening blinds!”
text:
I enjoyed my stay in the hotel. It has two rooms, a living area/tv/desk/minibar and the bedroom. The bathroom is quite large and comfortable. The staff was very friendly. The mini-bar wasn't any pricier than any other mini-bar and had a decent selection. The indoor restaurant/bar was really quite nice for both breakfast and late night drinks. I had only a few issues. The bedroom needs room darkening blinds! They had very nice shutters that did nothing to block out the light. I ALWAYS wake with the light, so this sort of sucked. The bathroom needed *more* light. Although there was a lighted make-up mirror and additional lights- none of the bathroom lights seemed strong enough. I DETEST overhead lights outside of a bathroom, but I actually welcome the option of good overhead lighting in the bath. It was simply a bit dark.
The neighborhood was fairly low-key, right near UCLA and some neighborhood restaurants, residential areas etc. If I was in the area, I would stay again.

title: “Kabuki Hotel in JapanTown”
text: Wonderful comfortable rooms, great views and surrounded by a Japanese food/shops mall...close to everything....super comfortable thick like goosedown mattresses and pillows, comfort robes and slippers, great service; beautiful Japanese gardens, just a beautiful hotel

title: “Nice hotel, horrible area!”
text: Hotel is nice, clean and all staff are very friendly. I have no complaints about the hotel itself however the area which it is situated in is not the nicest, to say the least. The hotel corner is full of tramps. I noticed a few comments on here saying that they did not bother you but I had a very different experience to this. Myself and my friend are both young girls in our early twenties staying in San Francisco for a few days, we were approached everytime we left the hotel and we did not feel safe in this area at all, we were scared to walk about during the day let alone at night. We cut our evenings short every night to make sure we were back in the hotel before dark, this meant we even missed the celebrations for 4th July. I would not recommend this area to anyone especially if you have children or are young like myself.

title: “Avoid it until the construction is done”
text: It is recently under construction (2012 summer). Location is not really good compare to other high end hotels in NYC. Keep checking the rate, and you could get a REALLY good deal. By the way, both Waldorf Astoria and Waldorf Tower are not for fashionista.

title: “Great Hotel - Great Location!”
text:
This hotel is located in walking distance to Michigan Ave., tons of shopping and restaurants. Location is prime!
The room itself was lovely. I stayed in the West Tower and had a great view of the River, Michigan Ave./Wrigley Building and a partial lake view.
It is a very busy "big city" hotel. If you don't like busy, then I would suggest a Hampton Inn or equivelant. 
They are professional and very accomodating to say the least. I have stayed here many times and you cannot beat the price if you shop around.
The lobby is very beautiful and great for people watching.

title: “Great stay”
text: We had very early flights out of Logan so we decided to stay close to the airport and hopefully have some time to explore the city. They offer a free shuttle to the airport or to the T station and there is also a water taxi that allows you easy access to the city. Staff was friendly, rooms were clean and modern. Restaurant was just so, so. I would stay again.

title: “LOCATION, LOCATION, LOCATION”
text: I just returned from 4 nights and it was fantastic!! I brought my in-laws whom are visiting from England and they could not believe the quality of this hotel!! You can walk just about anywhere!! We had a bayview room on the cable car turn around side, it was a bit noisy at night, but we were out late anyway. The wine reception is a terrific touch and the beds & pillows the most comfortable I have ever experienced in a hotel.

title: “A unique, trendy, tiny hotel in a GREAT location--just don't use valet”
text: We stayed at the nearby Westin Hotel for the first half of our trip to Seattle and finished the week at Hotel Max. The Westin was only mildly more expensive for the extra 1/2-star, and worth the upgrade to us in terms of space and staffing. Check-in at the Max was FOREVER with only 2 staffers and a firm check-in time (4pm). Might have been quicker if early-travelers had been given rooms first-come, first-serve. Valet Parking had the same problem. Truly, I recommend not driving in Seattle anyway since public transport is so great and the city is very walkable if you are in reasonable shape. Need another reason? How about valet-only parking at $30/nt? This was the most expensive and worst service we found in the area. Only 1 or 2 valets working the garage, so give yourself at least 15-20 mintues to get the car (in fairness, we noticed valets going on break with 2-3 couples still waiting for their cars--this was brought to the attention of management and very promptly corrected). Hotel Max was well-decorated and interesting, but the rooms had a dorm-room quality. We are small people and still had a tough time maneuvering around the room together. On the positive, the adjacent restaurant had amazing sushi rolls and martinis, we had a great view of the Space Needle from the room, the elevators were really cool (but don't forget your room key: you need it to use the lift), and the entire hotel was certainly designed well to maximize the space (or lack thereof). If you just need a place to sleep in the best shopping area near City Centre, within a brisk walk to Pike's Place Market, you're not driving around the city, and you'd rather take a shower than bathe, this hotel is unique enough to stay near the top of the list. Would we be back? A conditional yes. Only if check-in speeds up and only for a couple nights (before claustrophobia sets in).

title: “Great stay at the Orchard Hotel”
text: Good staff, clean and quiet hotel just a couple of blocks from Union Square and the theaters, easy walking distance to Ferry Building, etc. Rooms are well appointed and (at least on this occasion) a very good value - recommend the Orchard Hotel very highly.

title: “Great Hotel with great amenities”
text: This hotel was very impressive. The room was very large and so was the bathroom. I am actually typing this review in the room right now. I stayed on the 21st floor and in a corner room and the Internet connection the speedtest shows a 8.5mbps download speed meaning very quick for hotel internet access. I was able to watch youtube videos on it with no hiccups. The meeting rooms were great and well appointed. I liked the breakfast buffet as well as the two drink frees during their happy hour at the hotel.

title: “Good Service and Beautiful Hotel”
text: Very good service and nice hotel. We had a nice room facing the fountain. We watched the firework from our window. Really enjoyed the trip!

title: “Forget about Sleep in, Noisy Housekeeping Staff!”
text: This was our getway weekend. Booked in advance on line. A Little disappointment for it being a Marriott, but the price was for room was good , free parking, close to market square. This not a place for you if u want to sleep in. Maids are up and down the wall yelling "housekeeping" and knocking on doors. Doors and walls are very thin, even with our AC being on. we could still hear the noise. Vanity was very small. Honesty I would think twice about staying here again. Several other hotels around this one, I would check those out first.

title: “Perfect for business or family visits”
text:
Don't be fooled by the rather staid mustard/brown/brick color pallet of the appointments--this hotel is very comfortable and the furnishings new. Service was unfailingly friendly and helpful. The rooms were perfect little business pods with a small sitting area, sink, fridge and coffee maker, desk, and then the sleeping/bathroom area slightly separated. It also works, as in our case, as a good base for a family visiting the area/relatives/friends. Everything is just very efficient while still being cozy. 
Continental breakfast is included and it's on the generous end of continental (I've had it where it was literally just a plain, untoasted piece of white bread and a cup of tea). There's coffee, a generous Starbucks range of teas, cereals, fruit salad, pastries, toast and bagels. You can toast but anything you want cooked or any fancy espresso drinks will cost extra.
There are two computers with free internet and printing. The pool area is great with lots of loungers; it's big enough for a real swim and also shallow enough for kids. Less impressive is the fitness room, with exactly two treadmills, one elliptical machine, and one cycling machine. No weights, but there are complimentary towels and water.
Things go south a little in the bathrooms, where some serious grout scrubbing is needed as well as more light and more places to hang wet towels. Still, the wall paper is ingenious--a lovely shade of blue with thousands of tiny watermarks. It's pretty, and also hides a multitude of sins in a much more eye-pleasing way than all that brown and mustard.
My quibbles are minor however--my family really enjoyed our stay here and after having tried several area Austin hotels when visiting the relations, I think we've finally found our home away from home.

title: “I enjoyed the stay”
text: Though I like the towers better, The main WA was clean, the service excellent and the AAA price outstanding. We ordered room service which was delivered quickly, presentation splendid and the staff professional. Though pricy, it was worth being able to sit back and be served in our room in comfort ! Parking in the hotel is expensive, there are many parking opportunities close by. We enjoyed our whole stay at the Waldorf !!! We come in often.

title: “Westin....great hotel!”
text:
We stayed in one of the of Deluxe rooms and what can i say? It was huge!! It was a corner room so we had to walk down corridors (yes corridors) until we reached the main part of the room. 
The view was amazing. We could see the ESB, Hudson River and below us we could see Madame Tussards. We stayed on the 36th floor which we were happy with as we requested for a high floor. 
The bathroom was nice, the double headed shower came in handy and it was clean which was the main thing. Bad thing about the bathroom was that the bathroom robe were ripped and very creased but that didn't bother me!
The bed was kind of 'heavenly' but the pillows were too soft, i had to sleep on 3 pillows for me to feel some sort of comfort! But the beds were enormous and comfy.
The staff were ok, helpful at times. Shula's (restuarant in the hotel) was nice, waiters were very courteous and nice. Food was nice, my husband really enjoyed the steak, he said that it's the nicest steak he's ever had! 
The hotel itself is not as welcoming as the other hotel we stayed in. It was dark and looked more like an art gallery rather than a hotel. 
But all in all, it was very nice and i would stay here again.

title: “Great location, beautiful hotel but..”
text:
I researched hotels and cities for a year, and chose Boston for our honeymoon. The Boston Harbor Hotel seemed like it had everything we wanted; Great location for sightseeing, beautiful views of the harbor and luxurious accommodations. The hotel ended up having all of these great amenities, but...
I am in my late 20's and my husband in his early 30's, both very relaxed people who enjoy a quiet evening in, we aren't partiers by any means. We were hoping to have a romantic week in a beautiful hotel, and were disappointed to find that this hotel was very stale as far as a romantic atmosphere goes. It was filled with business people; we didn't see any other couples staying in this hotel. All of the guests were bustling around with their brief cases and on their cell phones. We wouldn't recommend this hotel to anyone who is looking for what we were looking for- A warm and romantic atmosphere.
It's a perfect hotel for people on business or maybe even for a ladies weekend. Couples stick out like a sore thumb, and very obviously not the hotel's main concern. 
P.S. Do not stay here if you have a pet allergy, as they allow pets to stay in the rooms, and do NOT do a good job of cleaning the pet hair, even if you request a deep cleaning (Clumps of cat hair on the chair)

title: “Great location with a nice view of the 2012 15 seconds of fireworks on the bay”
text: We had a nice stay over the 4th of July, good size room with a king size bed and flat screen TV. Restaurant had a great breakfast, dinner was not so great, only so so.

title: “Outstanding Customer Service”
text: My colleague and I arrived on 11 June after a delayed train. We were greeted by a smiling kind staff. My colleague travels to DC quite often; but this was our first stay at this property. She is a Marriott rewards member and was upgraded upon asking.
