We experienced an unfortunate incident and the staff IMMEDIATELY not only reacted; but went above and beyond by treating us to drinks/dinner and breakfast as well as providing us with complimentary wireless access. The hotel management team were compassionate and caring in their way of dealing with our issue. My colleague and I felt we were truly treated like royalty. Additionally, the food was exceptional. We both would stay at this property again when in DC. The managers Pio and Geary as well as the restaurant staff are extremely customer-focused. What could have been a very unpleasant stay turned out to be exceptional! The room to which we were moved was meticulously clean and incredibly comfortable. As someone who has traveled the world, I can honestly recommend this property while in the Dupont Circle/Georgetown area of DC.

title: “Good location, clean rooms, and helpful staff.”
text: We stayed here in the beginning of January and had a very nice stay. The hotel is conveniently located on the F bus line and two blocks from the trolley. Within walking distance of the Alcatraz boat and all of Fisherman's Wharf. Also within walking distance of restaurant Gary Danko (which is worth the money). Great stay for us!

title: “Nice, moderatly priced, boutique hotel.”
text: Took the family here for a Memorial Day overnight in the NYC. We all really liked this hotel, despite a few glitches. First the glitches: I came here with a comped room from a credit-card deal. Upon arrival, I was upgraded to a junior suite (great!), but one with only a king-sized bed (for 4 people, not so great!). We were certain we had requested for a room with 2 beds (we always do), but did not check the reservation before we came (our mistake). They offered air mattresses for our 2 teens, but did not come here to go camping. So we ended up purchasing a second room, although at a discounted price. Also, we lost the junior suite since we all wanted to be on the same floor. Not real happy about that. Minor room problems included a missing TV remote, slightly noisy air conditioner, broken bar drawer, and a wardrobe tilting at an odd angle (a bit like the tower in Pisa). All that aside, the hotel is new, the staff IS extremely helpful and friendly (as highlighted in other reviews), and the location is great! Like all Manhattan hotels, the rooms are small, but these were not cramped. Our beds were VERY comfortable with no spill-over noise from other rooms. The second floor lounge is nice (great seating), with complimentary snacks (great afternoon cupcakes!) and coffees. Also, there are only 5 or 6 rooms to a floor, so it feels more like a residential apartment building than a hotel. The restaurant that shares the ground floor (Lexington Brass) has a great breakfast, and I would imagine, great food all around (Whatever you do, do NOT eat at the place directly across the street at the south corner of 48th and Lex, its terrible). I would definitly come back here again.

title: “Smart, stylish hotel in a great central location”
text: The Nine Zero is a very smart joint, slap bang in the middle of Boston. There are several T stations nearby, Boston Common is a stone's throw away, Macy's is just around the corner, and the rest of the city centre is easily walkable. The hotel staff are friendly and efficient, the breakfast room is nice, and the room we had was large, stylish, well fitted-out, quiet, and had very comfortable beds. Highly recommended for a stay in this lovely city.

title: “Solid Pick”
text: Stayed for one night on business. Solid business hotel in a great location. Took the BART in from SFO and walked less than half a mile from the Market Street station. Rooms were very clean and comfortable though minimilist. Easy walk to the Embarcadero, Union Square or wherever. The only negatives is the speed of the elevator service. At one point I waited over 10 minutes for a car - others had the same problem. Also, because you are in the middle of the city, there will be some noise from the outside. Would definitely stay here again, even tough my meeting was at the Hyatt -where my last stay was only so-so.

title: “Try Better Options”
text:
We recently returned from this hotel after shopping and sightseeing in New York.
Due to availability, we transferred from The Sofitel. For more or less the same price, these hotels could not be more different. Central Park had poor service, very tired rooms with peeling wall paper and serious need of refurbishment. The Sofitel was very good quality by comparison.
Unfortunately the price does not reflect the value you will get, but busy time of year I guess so even Central Park can charge high-end prices.

title: “Above and Beyond”
text: There aren't enough words to descibe my wife and I's stay here at the Westin Galleria Dallas. We've been coming to this hotel for 5 years now and our recent stay was by far the best. This trip was for a celebration of my wife's birthday. From the time we pulled in for check-in to the time we had to say good bye, every single employee at the hotel, valet, front desk, concierge, housekeeping, went "above and beyond" their jobs to make sure our stay was the best one yet! I recommend this hotel to anyone considering visiting the DFW area. Guys, this is a great place to take your girl! It's connected to the Galleria Mall, therefore you can take her shopping and when the guys get bored, you can simply go back up to your room or go to the "Second Floor Bistro Bar" for a cold beverage!

title: “OK value, good location, short on sleep”
text: We stayed at the Melrose Hotel on our first trip to DC. We arrived earlier than expected, but the front desk let us check in early and drop off our bags so we didn't have to cart them around with us. The room was worn, but clean and much more spacious than I expected. Beds were comfortable and the view wasn't awful. The worst part of our stay was the New Year's Eve all-night party going on across the hall. The front desk sent someone to quiet them down after we called around 2 am. Not the hotel's fault, just unfortunate circumstances. We understood the cause for partying, but we were paying to sleep and wanted to do so in quiet. Location was decent. I mistakenly thought we would be able to walk to the Mall and other attractions. It would have been a several-mile walk to do so. We might have if the weather had been warmer, but the DC Circulator stops just down the street from the hotel and we used that means of transportation for most of our stay. We didn't park our car at the hotel due to the $34 + tax nightly fee...the Union Station deck was a better value at $20/night, as long as you don't mind leaving your car on the other side of the city. The staff that we encountered was helpful, we didn't see much of the hotel staff other than at the front desk. Overall, I think we got a great value, but we secured our reservation through a TravelZoo deal, saving probably between 50%-60% off the nightly rate. I can't imagine paying full price, as I didn't think the hotel was really all that different from a 3-4 star hotel chain.

title: “Recommended!”
text: For only $100 a night, we enjoyed clean, roomy accomodations in a nice, low-key part of town at the juncture of SoHo and Little Italy. Definitely recommended for budget travellers, and I hope to stay here next time around! We also lucked out getting a spacious corner room, Room 303---highly recommended.

title: “Hotel Nice, Restaurant Poor Service”
text:
We have just returned from our Spring Break holiday visiting family in Pennsylvannia and spending a few days in Philidelphia. We travelled as a family of four with a 10 month old and a 4 year old. We chose Penn's View based on many of the reviews that we fohund here at Tripadvisor, and you all did not disappoint. It was a lovely small hotel, with a polite staff. We changed our reservations at the last minute and were given a different room than initially agreed to, the replacement room had a long steep staircase to reach the room, and we were travelling with a crawling 10 month old. This was less then ideal but we worked around it and the staff was very apologetic and the room was very large, clean, and inviting. We were aware that this was not an ideal hotel for small children, yet the staff made many offers and accomodations to make us comfortable. We enjoyed our stay. 
A few notes on items we were not pleased with, there appeared to be a very small staff - in two days we only saw maybe five employees including the maids and breakfast servers. Also the hotel claims to have a remarkable first rate restaurant attached, the Ristorante Panorama. We found the food wonderful, but the service horrible. 
A few examples were... we were told reservations were not needed, then we're dismissed by the hostess and they 'made arrangements' for us, we expressed that we had a nut allergy at the table then they offered to bring pesto and recommended a desert that had nuts (they did not even tell us it had nuts, it was a poached pear filled with hazlenut cream) then they never apologized or offered a replacement. The one incident that really ruined the meal was that we were seated at a very small four top with a child that reaches everywhere, we were moving items so they were not thrown, we asked if a larger table was possible or assistance the waitress said, 'when you figure out what will solve your problem, let me know'. We dine out frequently with our children and they do behave in restaurants, but this experience did not fit the description of a first class wine award winning restaurant, with children or not. The food was good, but the service ruined the experience. We found the service as inattentive, rude, and unhelpful. 
Overall we would recommend the hotel for couples travelling or business, but would suggest somewhere else for dinner.

title: “Most value for money?”
text:
The Jane is probably one of the most valuable hotel right now, at least from my experience in NY. The service is excellent, all staff friendy and always ready to assist. Even if the rooms are SMALL (buy who will be in NY to sleep) and there is shared showers, the value of the hotel is in the service and the staff. 
One simple example: instead of standing waiting for your taxi, take a drink in the neighbor bar and the staff comes and get you when the taxi has arrived. Another example is that the baggage storage, including Alia me stuff get stored at the office.

title: “Great hotel!”
text:
Recently stayed at this hotel for a business conference. Hotel staff was excellent. Logistics of the conference were great and the food was pretty good. Nice rooms with comfy beds. 
Removed one star due to no fridge in the room, iron was inconsistent with steam and front desk was not staffed too well in the evening. Otherwise, pretty decent experience.

title: “Excellent”
text: Thank you to the entire staff, who made our trip to the city a pleasant one. From the check in to the check out, every staff member we encountered were polite. A true example of service.Thank you once again - Willie Mae Williams

title: “A Mini New York”
text: The Westin is located on the perfect corner of retails shops both high end and moderate walking distance from your room. Ditkas (great food and fun) is a few blocks away and the hotel is a affordable cab ride to some of the best sporting venues and the Navy Pier. The hotel itself offers a great bar and nice accomediations. We look forward to returning next year!

title: “Disappointing for a Hilton”
text: My husband and I stay at Hilton hotels all over the country because we appreciate the consistency of comfortable, clean hotels. But, this one is an anlomaly. This hotel is old and shows it. My husband is only a hHonors Silver member so maybe the Gold members, with the good reviews, got the good rooms? The staff seems nice enough, especially housekeeping. Room service is quick but the food is lackluster. $65 for a basic, plain breakfast for two. The bed is hard. The Kleenex has the consistency of Quick Trip T.P. The carpet and couch are sticky. There is a musty smell upon entering the room. I discovered the source was the overflow drain in the sink. You could actually see the mold. I had to hold my breath to brush my teeth. And after 3 attempts from housekeeping and engineering, there was no improvement. In the end, I just stuck a washcloth in it. There's no lobby to speak of. The restaurant is on the riverwalk and is kind of dirty and depressing. Don't try to work here. The desk is an ergonomic nightmare with a short chair and tall desk. And they charge $10 per computer per day. That's $100 for our 5 day stay. We just finished an excellent breakfast at Ostra at the Mokara hotel. Next time, for a few more dollars, we'll stay there. Or possibly the Drury, which looks beautiful, gets great reviews and is cheaper!

title: “Great stay for a great deal”
text: Great contemporary look and close to great outdoor mall outlets. Minutes awa from many local attractions. Only about two and a half hours away from Los Angeles :). Be sure to visit: Fashion Valley outdoor mall, Coronado Island, Coronado Beach, San Diego Zoo--Best Zoo ever!! For great fast food,visit El Pollo Loco andIn & Out Burger. For great seafood in a casual environment, go to King's Fish Restaurant. Buon Appetito (in Little Italy) is some of the best Italian Food you'll ever eat. Be sure to also visit Old Seaport Village. Have a superb lunch at the Edgewater Grill (as you overlook the harbor of the Pacific Ocean). You'll want t visit San Diego over and over again! What go to the Carribean when we have American treasures like San Diego (which has its own Coronado Island and other beautiful treasures)!

title: “Good hotel with good location”
text: I've stayed here a few years ago and enjoyed the stay. I have to say that now I'm seeing some accents could use a little "sprucing up", for example, the bathroom fixtures and the room desk are showing the wear and tear. However, we had a clean room and had a fine sleep. Didn't stay long, room might get cramped if you're planning a stay of more than a few days. Not particularly spacious. Convenient location. Our quick stay was quite satisfactory.

title: “Changed my opinion of Hampton Inn”
text: I've stayed in a few older Hampton Inn's in the past, and have always been disappointed. However, with this Hampton Inn being newer and right by the airport, I gave it a shot. It was a awesome hotel. The room was very nice and comfortable. The staff was very helpful. The shuttle to the airport was a very nice feature. Parking is free for up to 7 days. If I have to fly out of Charlotte again for an early flight, I will book this hotel without hesitating.

title: “Home away from home”
text: We sold our house and needed somewhere to stay untill we found a house. When i cane to check in the lady at the front BiBian was so nice and helpful. We got a mini suite, very nice fits the family. All the staff are nice. They Alow animals (hard to find a place that does) the pool and spa are clean and heated. Brakfast is good, hotel is very clean. I would come back anytime and recommend it to everyone, Had a great experience

title: “Enjoyed our stay very much”
text:
We have traveled extensively and have stayed in all types of places--dumpy to luxurious all over the world. I refuse to pay more than $300 a night for TWO rooms. Our stay at the Hotel Nikko was delightful. We had two double deluxe rooms for our family of four on the 15th floor. They managed to get our rooms very close together which was a special request. The rooms were spacious and very clean. I am picky about beds but found the beds to be comfortable. The Hotel is no longer brand new but our rooms had lovely wallpaper and beautiful marble in the bathrooms. For the price we paid, we could not have done better in downtown San Francisco. We liked it better than the Fishermen's Wharf Hyatt where we stayed two years ago. (Being from Seattle, I require a coffee pot in the room and this bugged me about the Hyatt--no coffee pots in the room but Nikko had little coffee makers. And we received a newspaper everyday--I love that.)
There are street people but I am from Seattle so we are used to this and it did not affect our enjoyment of the city and we walked everywhere. The location is perfect.
I am also picky about noise. I could not stand a night we spent in the fancy Fairmont Olympic in downtown Seattle because of traffic noise. But the Hotel Nikko is very quiet.
My only complaint is the windows were really dirty on the outside so the lovely view of the city was like looking through mud. They need to get the window cleaners up there.

title: “Over rated, but tried to make up for it”
text: dont get me wrong, the location is amazing, the room was ok-ish, but the staff were well below par given the price....and having a public roof top bar operating the hotel lifts is a big big mistake. We had to wait far to long for the lifts when the roof top bar was busy and we had to live with drunk roof top bar patrons when in the lift. The concierge was very un-helpful. We did send an email noting our issues and disappointment, which after a number of weeks was answered and the response was good enough......but no chance we will stay in this hotel again and would not (have not) recommended it to others.

title: “Good deal, we'll be back”
text:
I spent 4 days and nights visiting NYC with my fiance and 2 kids from 06/29 to 07/03. The hotel is very clean and well appointed. We stayed in a room with 2 double beds. The rooms are small and space is tight, especially for 4 people but we didn't spend much time in the hotel so that really didn't matter. The staff was pleasant and responded well to all of our requests. On the last day the staff allowed us to store our luggage after checking out as we did some last minute shopping. 
The hotel is just minutes walking distance from Times Square, Rockefeller Plaza and other popular attractions in mid town. For the location you can't beat the price. If you're looking for a hotel with a view this is not for you, we were on the 8th floor and our room was on the back side. All we could see was the alley below and the office building 30 feet away.
The continental breakfast was typical but well stocked and helped us get on our way each day. There are a number of restaurants near the hotel and plenty more just a few minutes away in Times Square. 
I hadn't been to NYC in nearly 20 years and I was very impressed with the overall cleanliness of the city. Everyone was polite to us and we had a great time. I'm already planning my next visit! I highly recommend the Holiday Inn Express!

title: “Wonderful Getaway!”
text: I resently stayed at the Ballantyne Resort and I had a wonderful experience. My family and purchaced the "Girl's Night Out" package and it was wonderful! From the moment we walked in the door we were greeted by smiling faces that were eager to meet any needs that we my have had. The rooms and the spa were wonderful. However, the only thing that I did not enjoy was the food that was included in the dinner portion of our package. I did not enjoy any of it from the appetizer thru the main course. However, the breakfast buffet was good and there was alot of variety. I will definitely be returning back to the resort in the near future.

title: “It was simply amazing as it always is!”
text: I love this hotel and will remain a customer no complaints and I love the extra's. I love that you are able to order room service without paying an arm and a leg. The staff is amazing, the room are beautiful the valet service is one of a kind. I could keep going on an on but just stay and you will see for youself. Amazing

title: “Adequate”
text: I was pretty worried staying here after I started reading all the reviews of bedbugs! So when we got there, we carefully searched our room & there was no evidence of bed bugs! In fact, the mattresses still had their tags on them! This hotel has a lot more rooms that I expected. It is old & the rooms are small & a deep cleaning is about due. The carpet could stand to be replaced & the windows do not block out much sound or airflow (I think the windows at Alcatraz are more airtight!)... But you are staying in a prime location at a fraction of the cost of other nearby hotels, so what can you expect? The BART station & the cable car turn around and shopping galore are directly outside the hotel. The staff was helpful enough. I would stay here again.

title: “Everything at Greektown was better than expected”
text: never thought when I booked a room at Greektown for a weekend getaway that it would be so nice. We stayed in a King corner room. The view was beautiful. the room was very clean and nice. Loved the bathroom and walk-in shower - No messy shower curtains to deal with. Very friendly staff. would definitely stay here again.

title: “Comfortable and warm experience”
text:
Upon my arrival at midnight from a long tedious day of travel, I was greeted by registration staff who honored my request by giving me a fantastic corner room with a city/lake view. From that initial experience I felt welcomed, respected and valued as a customer.
I then had the pleasure of becoming acquainted with a housekeeping person who was responsible for maintaining my room for two days over the weekend by providing the best housekeeping services (along with those service providers who followed her). However, she stood out because she paid attention to some of the room details that most travelers take for granted. There were remnants of grout on my and some of the other 20th floor bathroom floors - apparently not cleaned up by workers as a result of recent tub/shower work. This person took the time to clean and remove the residue from the floors - an act that made me regard her highly and appreciate her attention to care.
Quality service and personable staff interactions really matter to me. In addition to the outstanding service of these two exceptional women, LB's Cafe's friendly staff, and other pleasant and professional hotel personnel who I encountered during conference dining and receptions, I can honestly report that I had a great time, in spite of the weather, and will continue to support and recommend Sheraton Hotels.

title: “Generous room, but not really a suite”
text: I was somewhat disappointed as the Inn is listed as a suite, but it is only one large room with a kitchenette, a small sofa bed & a queen bed. My husband & I sometimes get up in the night and it is nice to be able to read without bothering the other. When this came about, I had to sit in the bathroom because it was the only part that had a door that shut off the rest of the suite. Otherwise everthing else was quite up to snuff and it has lower prices right now because they are remodelling one floor at a time. We did hear anything. Breakfast buffet was extensive.

title: “Wedding wonders nice garden and reception areas”
text: Where to start check-in pleasant and quick always a plus. Got our paking pass for the car (parking is not free). Most people say location is verything and this hotel fits the saying... great location walking distance to Starbucks, Ralphs, and tons of other places to eat drink and be merry. Hotel has a fireplace and seating in the lobby and a bar. As you walk past the pool area there is the cafe and another bar at the pool area. I did not get a chance to check out the pool sigh... but everyone else there seemed to be enjoying it the pool was supose to be heated. It is a nice size pool and one day there was a DJ there jamming some music a nice variety. Our room was a double on the first floor I kinda figure we has a senior woom because the toliet had an extender that raised it up although I didn't think it was really low. The beds were alright I slept well in min and so did my cousin. The guys at the front desk were nice I got to talk to one guy sorry didn't get his name very pleasant. The wedding was across th eparking lot held in the garden area, which was very lovely bubbling brooks and waterfalls are all over and nice bridges that you walk ove to get to the wedding area. The decorations were pretty green apples and flowers aranges all around. They had passed appetizers very good and drinks setup for aftr the wedding and the reception was held inside which ws beautifully setup with the wedding colors. The food at the reception was delious as well. Overall the hotel is very nice I thought may time to clean the carpet in our room or replace it there was free internet in our room and I believe maybe in other areas of the hotel we had a patio but no pation furniture maybe becasue we were so close to the pool they figure we didn't need or wan to sit and look at the parking lot.

title: “Service was excellent... but”
text:
The room was pretty poorly maintained. The toilet did not flush properly, the sink did not drain properly, the remote for the sitting room TV did not turn it on or off, the shower curtain rod was coming off the wall and there was some mold on the ceiling above the toilet. In addition, the furniture in the room was in fair to poor condition (the desk was badly banged up and the sofa cushions did not fit the sofa. Only one thing kept me from giving this hotel a poor rating, the service was very good. The parking attendant was upbeat and friendly and the woman at the main desk was also friendly and helpful. But the biggest reason for the great service was the concierge David. He was extremely friendly and helpful. He knew of great places to eat and was a joy to interact with. Honestly, David (the concierge) made us feel so at home, that we would consider coming back to this hotel despite the very poorly maintained room and bathroom.
If the hotel could get it's maintenance together, it would have gotten an excellent rating from me. The hotel is in a great location (one block from the Inner Harbor), they serve a nice breakfast and a happy hour drink (free). And the service (especially from the concierge) was top notch.

title: “Pretty nice hotel but had problems with the bathroom”
text: This overall was a nice hotel but the bathrooms had mold on the ceiling which should have been taken care of right away. Otherwise the pool was pretty nice espcially when they open the roof and you can hear the sounds of the city. The bedrooms were pretty nice overall.

title: “Very nice trendy hotel near Times Square”
text:
This hotel represents an excellent value in NYC, great location, everything feels fresh and new!
Rooms aren't as small as you might think there is however a pricacy issue as the bathroom is only separated from the room by curtains... 
My only gripe would be the wifi connexion which notconly proved to be slow but required reauthentifying everytime we came back to the room!

title: “Fantastic - the staff in the Monaco helped make it a trip of a lifetime!!”
text:
We had a fantastic time staying in the Monaco. The staff could not have been friendlier and more helpful. The wine reception every evening and the complimentary continental breakfast every morning added to enjoyment of our 1st visit to San Francisco. It was a joint celebration; our 40th Wedding Anniversary and my sister's partner 50th Birthday and the meal we had in the hotel to celebrate the joint occasion was second to none as was the attention to detail from the staff.
Thank you to all the staff and I hope you enjoyed the book about Edinburgh as much as we enjoyed all the interesting reading materials in the lounge. We will definately be back to this hotel and will certainly use the Kimpton chain if visiting anywhere else in America.

title: “Ok but not great”
text:
Stayed here for 3 nights. The rooms are okay without being luxurious. The things that let them down were breakfast - very average and we had to ask twice for our orange juice, plus we had to ask where our laundry was more than 24 hours after they had taken it. Given the price of the laundry this should not have needed follow up.
Finally, there seemed to be a high number of people who had room service breakfast on our floor, and their trays were left in the corridor for hours and hours, which resulted in a nasty smell. 
The staff on reception, concierge, housekeeping and valet were all extremely friendly and helpful.
Probably wouldn't stay here again, but it was okay.

title: “Customer Service is tops.”
text: My family and I have been regular guests at this hotel for years (15+). We've always been pleased with the staff and rooms (especially when upgraded to a suite--which is frequent at this property for SPG platinums). But, the service this past week has risen to new heights. The staff was awesome from Erica who checked us in last night, to our hostess in the Club Lounge Connie Aley--who took special care to prepare a delicious chicken kabob and made sure we were taken care of even when we slipped in 5 minutes after the evening Happy Hour ended. We highly recommend this hotel--the views, location are perfect. But, the staff--they make the stay really worth it!

title: “Irish hospitality !”
text: Great location, wonderful service, comfortable rooms, large bathrooms ... I could go on. Irish hospitality in a trendsetting hotel with a happening scene at the bar (Cuffs). If you appreciate good design and friendly service(not always found together in hip hotels) Jurys is for you. My only criticism - the gym could be larger, although it was functional. We'll be back.

title: “Nice, but NOT 5-Star”
text:
Front Desk staff was rather unfriendly. Doormen and bellmen were very welcoming and helpful Reservations agent told me that our room had 2 beds that were "queen width but full length" but this was not true; the beds were full beds. It's true that the bathroom is teeny tiny, but this seems to be standard for New York. Drawer and closet space is very good. 
Our worst experience at the hotel was trying to get a cab there on Friday night to make it for our dinner reservations in the Village. We waited 25 minutes with only two parties ahead of us. It was pretty odd. 
I don't think this hotel is at all a five star property; it's a four, at best. No wireless? Come on! Concierge service was spotty. On the one hand, we were given a great dinner recommendation and got reservations on virtually no notice, but another day, the person on duty seemed addled and unable to find something really simple.
The lobby is absolutely beautiful. Enjoy it! 
This is a good hotel, but isn't as luxurious as it bills itself being.

title: “Comfortable Hotel”
text:
The hotel is located near the Biltmore Shopping Centre - not in downtown Phoenix. They offer a shuttle service to the airport, although we didn’t use it – we had a hire car and there was ample free parking adjacent to the hotel.
Reception staff were helpful and check-in/out was quick and efficient. Our room was large with a microwave and fridge in the room. Our room was missing pillows, but this was quickly resolved by staff. Complimentary breakfast was provided, with a range of hot and cold food available. Free WiFi was available in rooms. 
We stayed for one night and did not use the pool or other facilities. If visiting the area again we would happily stay in Hotel Highland again – and would recommend if visiting the Biltmore area.

title: “Not bad for an overnight stop”
text: We only stayed one night. Layout of the room is really nice, loved the sitting area and desk and bar, beds were comfy. But when I walked into the room I immediately noticed that the carpet had stains all over throughout the sitting area, and by the beds. Also there were greasy fingerprint marks all over the bathroom door, countertop and the door to the hallway. I cleaned it myself. Cleanliness is #1 priority for me. No shower cap in room. Plenty of towels. A/C was either cold or hot - difficult to get to correct comfort temp. In the morning I went downstairs to get a decaf americano. The front desk girl didn't listen to me explain how to make it, even though the other gal at the front desk explained it to her several times. She finally had to come do it for her.

title: “Loved Crowne Plaza”
text: Brilliant hotel, had a wonderful stay on our first trip to the States. The location was good for walking to China Town, the shops and getting the cable car. Our room was big, airy and very clean. Would definitely return and recommend.

title: “Great Location”
text:
If you can handle the noise and crowds in this section of town, the hotel is a welcome retreat. Great location. Upscale and chic. Hotel staff was very attentive, friendly and available. There seems to be a tremendous amount of staff for the size of the property which probably leads to the relatively high price tag. Concierge (Bonita) was extremely pleasant and helpful with suggestions for restaurants and booking us a great table at Chaya was a really nice touch.
The rooftop terraces were ok but could have been so much nicer without the network of steel railings and astro turf everywhere.The views from the roof are otherwise fantastic. For a hotel that is supposed to be so eco friendly they could have invested a little more in roof top furnishings and plantings. The guestroom corridors were freezing. Room was decently appointed but a little worn already ( time to start replacing carpet). Breakfast at the Americano off the lobby was very good. Service there is also consistent with that of the hotel staff.

title: “What a pleasant surprise.”
text:
As I write this review, I am sitting in the lobby of the Warwick Melrose. We came to Dallas on business, but also wanted to stay in a hotel that was also luxurious and romantic, at a reasonable price. We found all that at the WM. From the warm greeting extended to us by Leon, to the courtesy car driven by the super-friendly Chad, we were treated royally. Excellent room service and a great restaurant. The chef came to our table and talked recipes with my lady friend. Our suite on the sixth floor (601) was just remodeled, and was exquisite, with great views from our corner bedroom. Two 42 inch flat screen TVs, tasteful furnishings, and a spacious bathroom with great shower amenities, thick bathrobes--we loved it all. 
A previous review mentioned the sirens. This is accurate, but perhaps because we were on an upper floor, we did not find it disturbing--rather more of the big city coda of urban sounds. Only major complaint is that wi-fi in rooms is not complimentary, but at least it is in the lobby. 
I have mourned the long demise of good service in America. My experience at the WM has given me hope that there still exist at least a few places where it is still valued and practiced. You will find it here.

title: “BEDBUGS”
text: BEWARE!!!! i stayed in room 6402 and for only two night and got bitten repeatedly by bedbugs. i thought the quality for a Marriot was sub-standard, and i have never had this experience at a Marriott before, but i warn you if you are staying - be sure to do a thorough inspection before you sleep there!!!

title: “Clean and friendly”
text:
I'm in my room right now getting ready to check out and just wanted to say what a great place it is to stay. People have commented that it's old, well duh, it's old, which gives it most of it's charm. My room is very nicely updated and clean and doesn't feel "old" at all. It's very small, but I don't mind at all, it's just me here. If there were two of us it might be a tight fit.
Check in was smooth and friendly as was the parking. There's a desk to work at and good (and free) internet connection. There's a wall radio, but also one of those docks with speakers. Comfortable bed, quiet air conditioning (not one of those thick clunky box things that wakes you when it goes on and off), thick walls (haven't heard anyone) and very clean, nice bathroom. 
Here visiting my son and we had a wonderful dinner at Caper's Loft. Highly recommend, very good food. This hotel is very centrally located and there are tons of places to eat within walking distance, also a small Safeway if you want to pick up snacks. There's a comedy club next to Caper's Loft but it's probably hit and miss. Last night's show really stunk except for one guy who did 15 minutes.
I was picking between this hotel and the Fairmont, which was more expensive, and I'm very glad I made the choice to stay here. Overall a great place to stay.

title: “Great stay. Friendly staff. Reasonable price for NYC.”
text: I just came back from NYC and I have to say that I'm very happy with the Hilton Garden Inn Times Square. I was offered a corner room and it was spacious, clean and to my surprise, even with a room in the second floor, contrary to what I read on previous posts, I couldn't hear any noise from the street (my room was facing the 8th av. which I liked) it was very quiet, although, you could hear the subway passing by, but actually it did not represent a trouble while sleeping as it wasn't loud. That was good because I have a very light sleep. Usually have to take pills to sleep but I did not need any over there. Perhaps I was so exhausted by the end of the day that I just felt asleep immediately; I was not even once woke up by the subway or any other noise. The location of the hotel is great, is just two blocks from Times Square and the subway, the price is also good, I paid average of 200 per night. But you have to make your reservation with time, otherwise the price will increase like crazy! The bed was very comfortable. The bathroom doesn't have evaporator, that's a bit inconvenient but it wasn't an issue, I barely noticed it. But it was very clean and that's one of the most important things you are looking at an hotel bathroom. I felt really good staying at this hotel. They have luggage storage for free, that's super convenient! we checked out at noon and grab our cases at 10pm to catch our midnight flight without any trouble. The doorman was very friendly and helpful, he got us a cab in less than 5 minutes to go to the airport. He certainly earned his tip. I'm a satisfied client. I guess when you go to NYC you actually spend little to barely no time in the hotel room, so what you are looking is a reasonable price, a nice bed, good location and quiet place to sleep and I feel like this hotel has it.

title: “Soul traveller”
text: Stayed at CQ over a weekend and found it to be a very good base. Location in the city was good and a convenient base to start exploring. Room was clean, spacious and very comfortable. Staff very helpful & polite. Would recommend this hotel to anyone coming to Philadelphia.

title: “Awesome”
text: It's truer, you get what you pay for, and this is no upscale hotel for sure, but it is by far the cleanest and most courteous hotel I have stayed in for the price. The rooms are kept in nice shape, and the customer service was phenomenal. I will definitely use this hotel any time I am in Charlotte. Thanks for an awesome stay!!!

title: “Great location, nice hotel”
text:
Stayed here for NYE 2010. Typical city hotel - nice lobby, clean and large room. The only complaint would be that they need more and/or faster elevators (not a very realistic request, I know!). However, crowds are to be expected on a holiday so it was understandable that the wait was a bit long. Overall a nice stay and I would not hesitate to stay again.
I should also note the PERFECT location for tourist attractions, local bars/restaurants, train/subway, etc.

title: “enjoyable stay in this hotel”
text: Have just returned from a 3 night stay at the Carlton. First impressions on the drive from the airport were not too good as the taxi did go through some dodgy looking areas. The hotel itself though was thankfully vey nice, It was clean and the staff were very friendly and helpful. The evening wine reception was well received and this was a good opportunity to meet other travellers and compare the days events. You could have as much wine as you wanted as well, The receptionist also plays the keyboard during this time. San Francisco has a lot of homeless people on the streets and although some of them approched us for money we never felt threatened at any time. The hotel that has a restaurant that seemed very popular although we did not try it. We did enjoy Fly the bar next door to the hotel though. I would recommed this hotel to other couples looking to enjoy the city without paying too much money. Value for money was excellent.

title: “Clean, modern and in a good location”
text:
We stayed here for 6 nights in July having booked the introductory offer. 
As commented, the rooms are quite compact. However, we spent the majority of our time exploring, so this wasn't really an issue. The view from the room was fantastic. The large LG TV and ipod adapter were a nice touch. I really liked the soft purple lighting in the room, but my boyfriend wasn't a big fan! I was apprehensive about the quality of the bed, as many reviewers had complained of the matress hardness, but having stayed here for almost a week I felt fine. 
The hotel is located within close proximity to Port Authority and Times Square. We were able to try some of the restaurants in the Hell's Kitchen area which were great! We also found the Yotel terrace a nice area to end the evening. 
My main concern is that some of the rooms are already showing signs of wear and tear, and therefore the hotel rooms may not be as appealing in a years time.
Overall, I found Yotel to be clean and located within a good area with accessible links to the rest of Manhattan.

title: “Wonderful hotel”
text:
We stayed at the Hotel Monaco Chicago for five nights and loved it. We had stayed at a Kimpton Hotel in San Diego previously and this one was even better.
The room was great, with an extremely comfortable King size bed and antique style furniture. We asked for a quiet room on a pet-free floor and that was exactly what we got.
The hotel is in an ideal location, being walking distance from many tourist destinations and from a choice of restaurants. Chicago is both an interesting and amazing city to visit.
The staff were both welcoming and very helpful. I would not hesitate to recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: “Nice hotel on the Riverwalk with exceptional service.”
text: My husband and I recently stayed at the Hyatt Regency on the Riverwalk to celebrate our anniversary. I thought the service and the courtesy of the staff was exceptional. I thought Steven and Jose went out of their way to be helpful and make sure that we were happy. We had a room facing the Riverwalk and it was very quiet. I have stayed on the Riverwalk before and it was noisey, so this was a welcoming surprise. The hotel also has a nice roof top pool and a nice gym.

title: “Very Modern....”
text:
Location, Location, Location..... this hotel was in a perfect spot. So close to Times Square, 5th Ave. and just about everything I needed to do/see on my (too short) visit. Room was very clean and modern. I loved the shower, and the bed was crazy comfortable. The room even came with it's own iPad for ordering room service, check out, etc....
This would be the perfect hotel for a romantic getaway, and room even came stocked for just such an occasion, but since I was there for business, I didn't get to take advantage! 
The lobby was very dark and at first I didn't even see the registration desk, but once I figured it out, no problems. And the staff was sooo nice, even suggesting places for me to take my clients for a photoshoot. 
Would I stay there again, absolutely.

title: “NOT a 4 star hotel! Stay somewhere else.”
text:
We booked this hotel through a last minute deal with bestfares.com and travelocity. We went with friends who booked the last "deluxe" (standard) room, thus we paid more for the upgrade to the "superior" room. When we were shown into the deluxe room, I told them there was an error and that we had upgraded. The front desk told me there were no such rooms called "superior" rooms only the deluxe (standard) and the suite. They did move us to a "nicer" deluxe room. I was quite irritated. And after 45 min on the phone with the company that sold us the room, and then walking down to the lobby on my cell (because they front desk would not answer the phone when the online company called), I found out they had lied to me and there were superior rooms. The front desk guy showed me an unupdated superior room that was quite dated. He told me that I was better off in the current room, even though I had paid for the upgraded room and it did not have the perks of the "superior" room on the website. 
Basically, I was manipulated to stay at the cheap room because they had sold out of the superior rooms and because I had booked online, I had no recourse. I was very irritated. 
The "nicer" room had major issues including a MOLD PROBLEM in the bathroom. And this room was nicer than the superior room? Stay somewhere else! This is NOT a 4 star hotel! And not 4 star staff!
We also had the joy of the fire alarm in the middle of the night. And our friends were woken several different nights from a very loud party in the room above them.
STAY SOMEWHERE ELSE!

title: “Perfect downtown Luxury hotel for people with little Kids”
text:
I travel to NYC often and have tried almost every high end hotel option out there. I usually stay uptown because with small children room size and cleanliness are of the upmost importance.
Those things aren't always so easy to find downtown. I have finally found my downtown home away from home. 
I just got back from a 15 day stay at the Trump Soho and I loved every second of it. I had a deluxe one bedroom suite and the views were BREATHTAKING!! My room number ended in 09 and was a corner suite that looked at the hudson from one side and up sixth ave with a beautiful view of the empire state building from the other. 
It was luxurious, super clean, child friendly and glamorous. The staff were always really helpful too. The bellmen and the doormen were always smiling and welcoming. They even lent me a stroller for the rest of my stay after I left mine in a taxi. 
 The suite was spacious and plenty of room for 2 adults and 1 child. Putting 2 kids in the living room area would be pushing it space wise but could be done. The sofa in my suites living room did not pull out but could be made up like a twin bed. Perfect for my 4 year old but might be tight for a teenager. The room controls (lights, temp and curtains) could be operated from your nightstand or through the remote on your TV. That was a cool and surprisingly useful feature.
The location was great, at the west edge of Soho between the west village and tribeca. You can walk anywhere downtown from here. I don't usually take the subway but there's a subway stop one block away that will take you straight uptown in a quarter of the time it will take you in a taxi during traffic. I used it more than I ever have before.
They have an outdoor pool area that serves lunch and drinks. It was mostly pretty, young, tan people but there were a few kids there and the atmosphere seemed kid friendlyish. The room service menu also had a bunch of kids selections. 
Also, This place is star studded. There were constantly paparazzi outside waiting for the multiple celebrities that were staying in the hotel. If celebrity sightings are your thing, you'll love it. Lily in the attaché department was super helpful before and during my stay as was Brandon the bellman. Every employee I encountered was nothing but great!!
This hotel is the perfect choice if you are looking for a luxurious, child friendly option downtown. Even if you've never though about trying downtown with kids this place will change your mind. I can't wait to go back!!

title: “Nice Hotel with Good location”
text: stayed at the US Grant Hotel for a week. The staff was friendly and very attentive. My one issue was noise from outside. The odd # rooms face the street, and it can get noisy. In the future I would request a room not facing the street. The matress and and quilts made the bed one of the most comfortable that I ever slept in.

title: “you get what you pay for”
text:
We decided to take a spur of the moment trip to San Diego and since we spend most of our time at the beach the hotel we stay at isn't that much of a concern. We were right to feel that way.Days hotel is just a place to sleep.Absolutely average in every way.It's an older hotel and it shows it's age.The one most notable feature of the room was the smell.It had an overpowering smell of "pine sol cleaning liquid".It was so strong our clothes reeked of it for days after we left. 
 There was also a greasy spoon diner on the grounds.Don't go there to eat if you value your stomach. All in all,you get what you pay for .Don't expect any more than that.

title: “Grand Hyatt- Location, Location, Location, and Comfort Too”
text: Close friend treated us to a night here for a girls weekend in NYC. Near lots of what we travel to NYC for, especially the shopping. Short cab ride to the theater district, Metropolitan Museum of Art and Madison Ave. shopping, a huge plus for four women wanting to do a lot in two days. Nice lobby. Check- in was automatic with a kiosk type stand like those used in airports. Room was small but very clean, with two double beds. Beds comfortable. Housekeeping was efficient; on a busy Saturday we called for extra pillows and towels and got them about ten minutes later. Did not use restaurants or room service.

title: “A Great Choice for our 20th Anniversary Celebration”
text: We stayed at the Magnolia in a standard king room with the "Romance" package. The experience from the moment we dropped the car with Daniel out front to time he said goodbye to us on the way out was top notch. The hotel is appointed in a very sophisticated way. The rooms are very nice and VERY quiet. The exercise room is fully equipped and the pool/hot tub area on the roof is great. The romance package was delivered as requested with roses, champagne and chocolate covered strawberries. The hotel does a great job offering ways to upgrade or enhance your stay as your check in date approaches so when you check in, all your decisions are made and you can relax and enjoy. The shuttle service to dinner in a GL class Mercedes was a great touch as well. We will be making the Magnolia an anniversary tradition.

title: “Spectacular”
text: This is a great hotel. One of the best stays I have ever had in a hotel.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: Loved this place! Was worried about the mixed reviews but took a chance and boy am I glad. The room was great - felt like my own apartment. Yes, the decorations are a little like grandma's house - but everything was spotless and clean. Room was in great shape - staff was nice - loved the kitchen, and the cleaning staff did our dishes every day. The restaurant wasn't very good - very pricey for what it offered. If looking for a restaurant go to the Hash House. Hotel has wireless internet -an added bonus - and you can't beat the location. Great place for gay couples - the neighborhood is very gay and accomadating. The price is great - I've paid the same for motels - I even found a special on their website that got me a $40 gift certificate to the restaurant (again pricey even with the gc) and a in room bottle of champagne. Park is right across the street, great restaurants and shops on University a few blocks away. Great place!

title: “Great Hotel!”
text: My boyfriend and I stayed at the Onyx Hotel over Memorial Day Weekend. The hotel is in a great location, within walking distance of the North End, Quincy Market, Fleet Center and the T. The staff was very friendly and we loved how the rooms were decorated. I would recommend this hotel to anyone and would definitely stay there again.

title: “my selected base in NYC”
text:
As i am heavy traveler within Europe Latin America and the USA i am trying to stay at the local Intercontinental hotel of which in NYC i feel at home having the priority desk stuff were i will mention in spacial the perfect service provided by
Annmara Gayle who gives you the assurance that you in person are been taking care off.
Perfect location and the best service.

title: “Very nice hotel, great room, right on campus”
text: Stayed here for three nights on a trip to Ohio State. My room was very large and beautiful. I loved the Keurig in the room, also had a fridge. The bathroom was very nice, and there was a ton of desk space with several outlets and an Ethernet cord provided for internet. They also had free Wifi. My king bed was incredibly comfortable as well. I ordered room service twice (breakfast and dinner). Both were delivered quickly and by very friendly staff. This was a great experience, and I will definitely go back next time I'm at OSU.

title: “The Magnolia is a beautiful hotel with excellent service in the heart of the theatre district in downtown Houston.”
text: We loved the amenities, including cookies at night and an excellent breakfast. We were never able to take advantage of the evening reception, but others in our party did and reported it to be lovely. Our room was spotless and very comfortable. We particularly enjoyed the rooftop pool with incredible views. Would we stay here again? Absolutely!

title: “Obama Day”
text: WOW! This hotel was amazing. If you live/love music, this is where you should stay! The rooms are stylish but very comfortable. You can't beat being on Michigan Avenue. You can walk to everything! We were there for the Obama Rally on Nov. 4th and to see a show. I would stay here every night if I could!

title: “Run........”
text:
We saw the ad for this in local paper...We walked in we were traveling with another couple...We wanted to see the room first. Four adults could hardly fit in elevator. 
The "suite" was so small, old furniture, nasty shower and a roach motel in the corner....I was speechless and embarrassed because I had picked this place and had friends with me...The room was dirty, no mattress covers. Hadn't been painted in years..I wouldn't of stayed there if it was free....
Travelers from Akron, OH

title: “Horrible experience”
text: We had the worst experience at this hotel recently. There was a glitch with the reservation on the part of the hotel. We walked in with our printed confirmation of the reservation and encountered "Elizabeth" at the front desk. She was extremely rude and unaccommodating. We asked to speak to the manager whose name was Yoki. We unfortunately encountered the same rude attitude. They were not willing to resolve the small problem with a pleasant attitude. We were so uncomfortable with their poor customer service, that we walked out and intruded on a friend and stayed at their apartment. Do not go there. There are far too many hotels to choose from to have to deal with poorly trained and power hungry service people.

title: “good locatoin with questionable staff”
text: Stayed 2 nights week of June 7th. Stayed in 2314 in the north tower. Check in went fine as it turns out because i arrived late in the evening. The rooms are on the small side and the bathroom is the size of a coat closet. The concierge lounge on the 22nd floor is spacious however the espresso machine has been broken for several months according to the staff. Well it look nice sitting in the middle of beverage area. While the hotel is not on the water its a 5 minute walk to the harbour downhill. The hotel is also close to camden yard and the blue line train which runs from BWI. Tried twice to eat at Shula's 2 in the lobby, seating wasn't a problem but the service or lack there of was. The first time after 10 minutes of not being greeted i packed it up and hit one of the local establishments for dinner. On the 2nd try i was actually acknowledged but it was still terribly slow. Time to check out and the bill is wrong, charged for the internet ( free if your platinum), quick call to the desk and they apologized and said to stop by for an updated copy. Stopped by at 7:30 and the charge was removed however now there is a mysterious $50 charge under the "other" column. Front desk clerk couldn't figure it out so they said to stop by before i headed to the airport. Get back at 10:30 and the line is 8 deep at the desk with 2 people actually handling the guest and 3 other managers/desk staff roaming the lobby not to concerned about the wait. Of course the Platinum/Gold desk was empty as well. Based on the comments of other guest in line it seems several people had issues with the random billing. After 15 minutes and no progress in the line I headed to the airport and just plan on desputing the "other" charge with Visa. If your looking for a full service priced property with a K-Mart service vibe to it, this is your place.

title: “clean friendly hotel in the middle of the city =)”
text: Check in and out was very easy and quick. staff are very friendly. Though some people had mentioned that this hotel was next to the parole office. I was traveling alone and felt very safe coming and going during any time of the day or night. Hotel was small and cozy.

title: “Amazing, Convenient & Friendly Place to Stay!!”
text:
Our group enjoyed the convenient location of Hotel Union Square. It was nestled in between major shopping, tourist attractions, restaurants and public transit all within walking distance! 
The hotel staff was knowledgeable, accommodating, and always willing to make our stay as comfortable as possible. A special shout out goes to Tony, who was always there to greet us with a friendly smile, no matter what time we got in! All hotels need a Tony!
As for the rooms, the decor was modern and unique. Rooms were cleaned thoroughly each day. The room was very comfortable, however, the noise level was a bit loud considering the fact that it was located on a major route where the trolley/streetcars pass through. So if you are a light sleeper, bring ear plugs! It was not a major concern for us, since we were truly exhausted each night from our daytime and night time adventures! 
This is definitely a hotel to consider when you want to truly experience San Francisco! So much to do, so much to see and a good place to stay in order to make your visit a memorable one!
Thanks again to all staff members who made our six day visit in SF an amazing experience! We would love to come and stay at your hotel next time we are in town!
Yours truly, 
Friendly Canadians, from Windsor, ON, Canada

title: “Very Nice. Very hospitable.”
text: Great room for $69 via Priceline. Excellent room with a view! Would definitely stay here again. Close to everything downtown. However, parking was OUTRAGEOUSLY expensive-$36/day.

title: “Excellent Rooms Hospitality Service The Whole Package At A Great Price!”
text: Hotel Indigo San Antonio Riverwalk made our stay a wonderful experience. We went to San Antonio for a wedding. There were numerous families who stayed at the hotel and we did not hear one of our parties complain. Will definitely stay there again. I highly recommend this hotel!

title: “Tired and shabby. A tourist spot perhaps, but don't stay here.”
text:
HORRIBLE.
Was first put into room 21-156. Reception said this was "upgrade, special large room". Room was large (huge actually), but totally bare except for bed, one arm-chair, small desk, and old small TV on a little dresser at distant far end of room. Room was barren, depressing, and dimly lit. Dirty carpet. Room had an strange wet bar alcove with an ugly partially dismantled sink. Wallpaper peeling, paint dirty, dim lighting. No amenities whatsoever- just two water glasses and an ice bucket. Small windows with view onto an air-shaft. Bathroom tiny, shabby, old, 1950s style, could barely get in the door. Nothing charming about this room - all just old and shabby. Last straw - sound proofing was so bad that I was woken at 6am by people talking in normal quiet voices next door - I could have easily joined their conversation.
Complained the next morning and reception then moved me to 'modern' room 20-209 for second night. This room was tiny, old style TV, barely room for a bed, small dresser, and desk. I suppose it had been renovated, since style was 1970 instead of 1950. Dirty carpet, peeling wallpaper in bathroom. Single small window with 'view' of a hotel wall 50 feet away. At least it was quiet.
By way of apology, reception gave me a $25 certificate usable only in hotel restaurant. Big deal - at least it paid for breakfast.
Valet parking was $100 for two days! Rates not posted outside when I checked in, so this was total surprise and shock.
Internet was wired and slow, for $19 a day.
Elevators were incredibly slow - sometimes had to wait 5 minutes for one.
My business associate was visiting from China and I'd hoped to show him a good Chicago experience. Palmer House was a big mistake. He had the same problem as I did with his room - he was first booked into a 'large' room, also found it barren and shabby, immediately asked to be moved to a 'better' room, which was small and shabby.
As a Hilton Honors member, I've often been upgraded to the Executive Floor. Not possible this time since hotel was full. No great loss though - I peeked into the Exec "Breakfast Lounge" on the 23rd floor, and as far as I could see all they'd done was crowd some tables and chairs into the elevator lobby on that floor.
Finally at checkout, they confused my associate's booking with someone else and only after some prompting did the front desk search their database to find and print the correct invoice for his expense report. Everyone at reception was nice and polite, but they were far from efficient.
Yes, the lobby is impressive, so maybe nice to stop in and see this place as a tourist attraction. But as a hotel to stay in, forget it. Rooms are Motel 6 quality at a premium price. 
Yes, it's a 'good location' near Millenneum Park, Mag Mile, etc, but there are a dozen other hotels in the same area.
PS. I provided exactly this same information in an online Hilton survey. Next week I did get a call from someone in the Palmer House Maintenance Department (maintenance? this place needs a major remodeling). He offered my a free one-night stay, which I declined (why would I want to repeat this miserable experience) and then offered 50,000 points, worth one free night at another Hilton property. At least they listened and made a small attempt at rectification.

title: “Awesome location, great price”
text:
This hotel is smack dab in Union Square, which is a perfect location for a tourist to San Fran. Although the room is very small, it is cozy and well decorated in soothing greens and browns. The room overall is very functional, with a very large closet so your bags don't overwhelm the room. The bathroom is also tiny, but well decorated in small tiles and a deep soaking tub. The place overall was extremely clean, and so relaxing and charming (it is a very old/historic hotel). It was so fun to roll out of bed and be in the middle of it all, and the staff was accomodating and very friendly. The cleaning crew cleaned in the afternoon unless you put a sign up requesting early cleaning, which was very nice.
Although the place was wonderful overall, it was slightly noisy since you are right in Union Square, and during our stay there was some construction right across the street. We were never bothered by the noise, though, unless the windows were open. The walls are slightly thin, and although not generally a problem because it attracts a pretty quiet clientele, we did have to ask the person on his cell phone next to us to keep it down at 4 a.m. The bathroom is not well-ventilated, so they ask that you keep the window open while you shower, which is slightly awkward to get to and has no curtain. The window is small, however, and tucked back over the toilet. There is also no heat in the hotel, so you must use a stand alone radiator, which works okay, but not great. This was only a problem a couple nights since we had unusually cold weather. The lobby also smells slightly moldy, which several people noted during our stay. These were the only cons about the place and were honestly very minor in comparison to how great the place was.
For the price, this place was fantastic and I would recommend it again in a heartbeat!

title: “Our best stay at any hotel, ever!”
text: This hotel was simply fantastic and lived up to its rating and price. We were celebrating our anniversary and had our Deluxe Spa King room upgraded to a Riverview Suite. We were surprised with complimentary champagne and strawberries! The Trump Attache' servive was wonderful and very attentive. The room service menu was very extensive for breakfast; lunch & dinner could have had a few more choices, but the food itself was very good. The room was clean and incredibly quiet. The staff was really helpful and professional and helped make our experience 200% better than we could have imagined. Trump Chicago is now our #1 hotel when we go to Chicago.

title: “Not bad for the Tenderloin District”
text: Great value for the hotel for being so close to Union Square. Sketchy neighborhood on the street west of the building, but the east side was fine. The street noise does not bother me since I have come to expect older building to have thin walls and major thoroughfares busy with traffic. No bedbugs, the heater worked fine, bathroom was small but once again it's an older building.

title: “Location saved the day”
text: I recently stayed at the roosevelt hotel in new york and for anyone considering staying here i would tell them to look elsewhere. This hotel is old fashioned, small and living in the past and the staff are not much better. On arrival we got checked in the girl at the desk was rude and not very informative, she also looked in shock when i asked if there was free wifi. Wifi in this hotel costs $15 a day per device don't bother with this there is a Starbucks down the road where you can access wifi for free. When we got to the room it was small and run down, we had booked the room for 3 but it barely could fit 2 of us. The only good thing about this hotel is location, it is right in the heart of NYC and you can get to most places by walking and if you do want to venture a little further central station is just a few blocks away. But for anyone who has stayed in NY before you will know that it is one of the easiest places to get around so for a better standard of hotel i would stay in a different location.

title: “Good location - Close to Seaworld and Old Town”
text: We stayed here while visiting San Diego area to tour San Diego State University, but while there for the tour, we also visited Seaworld. This hotel fit our budget and it was a decent place to stay. Walking distance to Old Town, which was fun for us to go to on our first day/night there. The next day, we went on our tour to SDSU, which was about 20 minutes away on the freeway. After SDSU we grabbed lunch at In-n-Out (took it back to the hotel and ate it in the pool area.) and headed to Seaworld for the evening shows. Seaworld was offering a 2-day for the price of 1-day admission, so we went back the next day for all of the daytime shows. It was nice to split the Seaworld visit into two days. We reserved two rooms, right next to each other, but not connecting. (We wanted internet and the connected rooms did not have wireless.) Problems: Sinks/Tubs backed up the first day and were fixed the next morning and one of my kids found a long, lock of hair (ewww) in the room. Positives: The staff was nice and the local police seemed to enjoy the attached coffee shop, so we felt very safe. We did not try the coffee shop.

title: “Very New Courtyard”
text: This hotel just started taking reservations in May 2008, so it's only about 2 months old. It is in pristine condition and very clean. It's too soon yet to tell if it will be well maintained but as of right now it's very clean and pretty. It is situated in Liberty Station which is newly remodeled and very well designed and landscaped. The hotel has a view of part of the bay and you can see the airport, but not hear the planes, thankfully. The rooms are small but space efficient. The beds are springless and very comfortable. The TV's are flat screen and high definition. There is a nice workspace and a fold out couch. The bathroom is roomy with nice fixtures. The halls are under-airconditioned and fairly small. There is a lounge with well appointed chairs and tables with lots of plasmas and even a fireplace. The fireplace is two sided with the other side in a partially outdoors terrace. There is a nice pool with a decent sized jacuzzi. I really liked the firepits they had for sitting around outside at night. Overall the hotel is very well designed and pleasant to look at. Enjoy!!

title: “La Cantera is terrific property”
text: WE came to La Cantera for a long weekend to celebrate my birthday. Great choice - highest level of service, great golf and no detail missed by hotel employees. Will definitely be back.

title: “Just OK”
text: Stayed there because of their "Park & Fly" privilege, where we could leave our car after staying one night. Only cost us about $20, figured would cost a lot more at the airport for the week we were going to be in Florida. Breakfast in the morning before we flew out was good, and the shuttle both ways was on time and very helpful. Rooms were just OK. Not the cleanest place.

title: “Great hotel in a great location.”
text: We spent a week here in late July and could not have been more pleased. The room was very clean and well appointed with a great view of the Chicago River and downtown. The staff was courteous and helpful throughout our stay and the location couldn't be better. I would definitely recommend this hotel!

title: “Decent upper west-side option”
text:
Stayed a week in October. Excellent location if you want to stay in this part of town. The pluses are that "Seinfeld" neighborhood feel and the fact that you are away from the chaos of midtown. The minuses are mostly mediocre restaurants (although plenty of them), and very little nightlife. The hotel was comfortable and modern, and the staff friendly. The staff was, however, extremely young and it seemed as if they were students trying to make extra money rather than folks seriously looking to get ahead in the hotel industry. The two (not a day over 19) doormen spent most of their time trying to pick up the even younger looking girls at the front desk. I thought this comical, but if you are looking for a polished staff, be prepared to be disappointed. I should also note that there was no bar in the lobby, so it was not the type of place that would lend itself to meeting other travelers.
I have stayed at both the Lucerne and the Excelsior in the past. On The Ave. is just as comfortable as those two, but lacks their charm. The Excelsior has the best rooms overall, but some disagreeable staff people. The Lucerne has a great staff and lots of charm (and one of the few good restaurants in the area), but a number of rooms with odd configurations, i.e. the door to your suite might open into the bedroom). Like the restaurants and other hotels in the area, On The Avenue is good...but not great.

title: “Nice Hotel, but poor Managemnet in a Crisis”
text:
Bear in mind that there are few cheap NY Hotels and the ones that are cheap are normally substandard. The New Yorker is mid-priced by NY standards. It’s a very nice Art Deco Hotel is an excellent central location – within walking distance of the Empire State Building, the Post office, Penn station and Madison Square Garden. Our room was not enormous but perfectly adequate and clean. The décor and furniture was ‘sound’ and not 'well worn' like many NY Hotels. The Hotels 24 hour ‘Tick Tock’ café was nice but overpriced like most hotels cafes are.
I have two gripes: the business centre only has two Internet PC’s (chargeable). I stayed in NY as an ‘Ash refugee’ (flight delays due to the Icelandic volcano) and there were queues to use theses PC’s all hours of the day. 
I initially booked two nights accommodation. I quickly realised that I would be stuck in NY for nine nights. I tried to book more nights on day one of my stay and was refused. I was told to return to the reception on day two. I was then refused on day two and told to return on the morning of day three (my check-out morning). This was obviously frustrating for me because I wanted to know if I could stay all week or would need to seek alternative accommodation, before I had to pack. 
Therefore on day two I used the Internet/Expedia UK to book more nights. I presented the confirmation paperwork to the reception desk. The guy said “fine, but if you booked through them I may have got a cheaper rate!” I explained that I had asked twice and not been allowed to. He said “that was odd, they were not fully booked”.
So I give the Hotel management one star but the hotel four stars. (If the Manager is reading this, I would love them to explain this strange policy to me)

title: “Memorable Stay at Hotel Angeleno”
text:
For our first ever visit to Los Angeles I stayed with family (wife and teenage daughter) at the Hotel Angeleno for 3 nights from Sept 8 to Sept 11. The hotel was booked through Thomas Cook and as the overall reviews of this hotel were favourable we were not
unduly put off by the location right next to Freeway 405 which is currently undergoing construction and will be for some time. We had decided not to hire a car and had little knowledge of public transport in LA and therefore were a bit concerned as to how we were going to get around and make the most of our short visit.
We arrived on Sept 8th mid afternoon after a long flight and already $45 down after the drive from LAX in a cramped taxi cab.
We were met at a reasonably cool and spacious reception by Cortney who made us feel welcome immediately and after checking in and a quick nap in our room, I returned to the reception area, grabbed a glass of complimentary white wine (served between 5:30 and 6:30pm) and started to plan some activities.
Cortney was very helpful and patient as we went through a few leaflets and booked a couple of ‘Starline Tours’; we tried to work out how we could get to Grauman's Theatre in Holywood to catch our first tour using the Metro, the nearest Metro Station to the hotel being Culver City. Eventually we decided it was best to book Hector (very jovial guy from Peru) who provides a Town Car service as an alternative to cabs and we could negotiate our rates, drop off and pick up times. At this stage I was feeling more confident as we had some sort of a plan and we could begin to relax, explore the hotel and look forward to the next few days.
Our room was on the 9th floor and had a tiny balcony overlooking the freeway; the traffic noise was considerable all night and it did disrupt our sleep a little so more effective double glazing could be installed. The room itself was spotlessly clean and beds very comfortable, shower was fine once we had worked out how to operate it! There is a restuarant on the 17th floor with a great view but it was a bit pricey for us so we restricted our visits to a couple of drinks and breakfasts which were excellent and served by courteous staff. There is also a pleasant pool area next to reception with heating provided in the evenings.
If you have a car then the hotel location is quite good with relatively short drives to the main LA attractions such as Beverly Hills, Hollywood, Universal Studios, Warner Bros, the beaches at Santa Monica and Venice. The suburbs of Brentwood, Westfield and the attractive UCLA campus are very close. Without a car you do feel a bit isolated (may apply to most hotels in LA), as there is nowhere to walk to in the evenings or early mornings but there is a shuttle bus service and we were dropped off at Westfield by a very enthusiastic Lonny and picked up again right on time after our evening meal. We also used the bus for a trip to the UCLA campus. We hired Hector again for our return trip to LAX on our last day to catch our connecting flight to Las Vegas. Hector is a mine of information and his car is far more comfortable than a cab.
Overall despite some drawbacks due to its isolated location and freeway noise (suggest a room higher up or facing away from the freeway); I would highly recommend Hotel Angeleno as the rooms are clean and comfortable, the overall facilities are good and I would especially commend the staff, Cortney, Joseph, Lonny and the others who were friendly, always helpful with useful information and ready to answer our questions on LA or Vegas and they made our stay in LA a truly memorable one.

title: “Watch your credit card billing!”
text: We stayed here for our son's recent wedding, incuring 12 nights of lodging between 3 rooms. The evening before check out, I made a point of having our credit card run on all rooms so that other family and the celebrant, a beloved priest were not charged. The next evening, his room was charged to his credit card, incurring stress and embarrassment on our part. After calling, I was told he was mistaken and nothing was charged to his account. The next day, noting that the error had not been corrected, I emailed an urgent message asking for the expense to be taken off his card and charged to our account. We received NO return phone calls, no emails, and NOTHING was corrected. 8 days later, my husband called and was told they "couldn't find" the charge, but they would keep looking and get back with us. (It was still on his credit card!) Finally, 11 days after check out, my husband called again (the 4th call) and they managed to find the charge and correct the error. NO apologies, no discount, nothing. This unprofessionalism was NOT worth the thousands of dollars we paid to stay there. Next time, we'll choose the 4 Seasons.

title: “Classic but needs to sharpen service”
text: I stayed at the Millennium Biltmore on a recent business trip. It's an old place, but overall well kept; appeals to a snooty crowd. You can only valet park at $40 per day. My room was very small but comfortable, with very limited t.v. channels. I found several hairs in the bathroom that were not my own. I hate that. I attended a luncheon banquet where the food was very good - no rubber chicken! Upon checkout, I had to wait a verrrry long time for my car to be brought up. No apologies; no personal attention. Still a great location, in the heart of LA.

title: “Excellent Location.”
text:
Very elegant hotel in the middle of San Diego. Just a walk away from shops and every type of bar and restaurant you could want. Helpful concierge if you need to find anything. Large comfortable rooms although our bathroom was very small with not much space to put anything. And important for us it was near the ship terminal as we were picking up a cruise from there.
Would recommend the hotel and definitely stay there again.

title: “Fine stay”
text: This is a newer property and it shows. Everything is quite clean and well serviced. We stayed as a visiting business guest. Our itinerary was 'club level', but this was not in the booking system. Upon discussing this with the front desk, we were given full access to the club level amenities, but not physically roomed on the club level. That was fine with us. Bed was comfortable. Pillows too soft for me (i realize i am finicky in this department). There was a reasonable amount of room noise from our neighbor (sounded like a late night drinking group), and I did call the front desk who had security put out the flames. Much appreciated. Check in and out was fast and stress free. You are right on the Easton shopping complex. My wife loved this as she could walk to any store she wanted and the movie theater while I was out on business.
