I would stay here again and would recommend this to everyone from families to business travelers.

title: “Average not great hotel”
text:
Pros: Relatively short drive to Universal Studios / Kodak Theatre from hotel. Cheaper rate than most hotels near the area ($72/nite).
A short 5 minute walk to the metro station.
Cons: Shady area during the night. Police said there are transients and prostitutes that stand in front of the hotel starting at 11pm. Do not walk around by yourself in the evening. 
Hotel staff were not knowledgeable about surrounding area and terrible at giving directions. Do not rely on staff giving advice. Staff were not polite or pleasant when checking in. They overcharged me and expected me to pay the higher rate even though I was quoted less. I found only one staff member at the front desk helpful.
The rooms were nice, clean, and comfortable but our toilet kept clogging.
At least there was a hot breakfast included.
Overall I would not stay here again. The negatives outweigh the positives. I would stay at The Hollywood Orchid Suites or somewhere else closer to Hollywood.

title: “Excellent location and great hotel”
text:
Aloft is a cool, trendy hotel with an excellent location. My room was fairly large, with new and modern textiles, a large flatscreen TV, safe, coffee maker, fridge and AC. I had a great view of the centre of Charlotte. 
Aloft is a prt of the Epicentre, which is the hot spot in town, with restaurants, bars, movie theatre and live bands playing outdorrs on weekends. It located about 200 meters from Time Warner Cable Arena. 
It has a hip bar, computers for guests in the lobby, food and drinks available all day and night (bagels, sandwiches, salads, soft drinks) and a small swimming pool with a great view.
If you're going to Charlotte, this is the place to stay!

title: “3rd stay - Staff are a credit to the hotel”
text:
This was our 3rd stay at the Intercontenental hotel in Times Square, booking again after 2 excellent previous stays in June 2010 and Sept 2011. This time we booked a delux room rather than a standard room.
Unfortunatly it all went a little off plan when we arrived on the Saturday night at midnight (5 am UK time). We arrived to find that they had no room for us, as they had overbooked the hotel, staff on reception were very apologetic and said that they had booked us a room for the night at the SOHO Grand (11-15 minute taxi ride towards the downtown area). We were very upset at this, as we were told to get in a taxi and pay ourselves upfront and claim money back when we checked in the following day. Not having a clue where the SOHO Grand was, was worrying especially as we by this point were very tired. 
We returned the following day, and our delux room was upgraded to a skyview room on the 29th floor, we had internet acess, wine, chocolates, water, nuts and fruit given to us. The accompaning note from the manager was very apologetic, but it was addressed to Mr and Mrs not Mrs and Miss!
The rest of our stay was brillent, the room was clean, tidy, bright and fresh, i wanted to bring home, my bed, the rain shower and the mirror from the bathroom. Was also feeling very jealous that the touch screen computer was better than the one i have here at home. The staff are very friendly, smart and well presented and full of advice, they all had time for a chat and never seemed in a hurry, Alll the staff are a credit to the hotel. The concierge helped us work the subways out, and the door man advised us on the weather, very helpfull to know that there was a cold wind and chance of rain before we left in short sleeved T-Shirts. When it rained we were offered umbrellas. The doorman even helped us to sort out a car back to the airport.
We will stay here again as it is one of the best hotels that we have stayed in, though next time we hopefully will spend all our time here rather than in another hotel.

title: “Great place to stay - spacious rooms!”
text:
I stood here Sept. 3. This place is great! Nicely decorated, spacious room. I had a deluxe king suite for only $119, a bargain for NYC. Before booking this place I checked out other hotels in Manhattan and Skyline was by far the best. All other rooms I viewed in other hotels were tiny ex. Clarion Park South, Broadway Plaza, Milford Plaza, etc. 
Skyline is comfortable had a very comfortable mattress with down bedding. The heated indoor pool is a plus and the vicinity of the hotel is great - close to all but yet far enough to avoid the city bustle. I've stayed at many hotels and this one is by far the best. I will definitly be back.

title: “Great place to stay!”
text: We stayed here July 4-7, 2006. Staff was very friendly and helpful. Rooms were clean and we had the room type we reserved waiting for us when we arrived. The pool and spa were nice - great that they are indoors. The shuttle bus personnel were prompt and informative. All staff was extremely courteous. We would stay there again and would recommend it to all.

title: “Liked everything about it!”
text: Booked through hotel's site directly and signed up to be " friends" of the Sofia" to receive announcements of offers, etc. At that time I read all of the reviews so I knew what to expect. Almost every review grades lower because of small room size, so this was not a surprise. I selected the smallest,least expensive room for 5 nights. When I checked in (4hrs early) I requested a room with a lot of natural light. Mary Ann was very friendly and she found me a front facing corner room so I had windows on two walls and was upgraded from a double bed room to a queen for bit less than I would have paid for the double. The room was clean. Yes water sprays out of the shower but it isn't much of a problem if you use your bathmat. The shower was roomy and had good spray. The bed and bedding were very comfortable. Closet was adequate. Large flat screened tv. The lobby was very comfortable and tastefully decorated. I had no trouble printing my boarding passes in the business center near the lobby. I peaked into the yoga place and people were using it. I received great directions and advice from desk staff and concierge. The mini fridge was great to keep the complimentary water bottles cold and i ended up heating up some delicious leftovers in the little microwave. I am a woman who stayed alone while attending a conference at the San Diego convention center. It was a pretty easy 15-20 min walk each way. Even as a single woman after dArk I felt safe walking the downtown and gas lamp areas because there were so many people around and many businesses still open. Some other reviewers said there were a lot of homeless--yes you'll see some, but my last conference was in San Francisco, and there are a lot more there--and sf's homeless approach you a lot more. Good shopping and eating very close by. The hotels own restaurant, Currant, (see separate review) definitely deserves your visit--ate here three times during my stay which is not something I usually do. The only very minor complaint was that after the first night, my in-room coffee was replaced as all decaf coffee. When I saw a maid later and asked for some regular, I was told the entire hotel was out of regular--and this remained true for the rest of my stay. A lovely coffee shop is just a few steps out of the lobby, but as someone who normally drinks a lot of coffee, it would have been nice to have some type of coupon or voucher for those of us who counted on in-room coffee as an amenity. However, I loved the cozy room (might have been less comfy if traveling with another person). Loved the lobby, the historical features of the building, the bed, location, and pretty much everything! Would definitely stay again. PS: I heard several people complaining about the cost to valet your car. There are cheaper public lots around for self valet. Also, I think it would have been a hassle to drive in the city. The city is very walkable and there are busses and cabs everywhere.

title: “Great night's sleep”
text: After reading a lot of the reviews for this hotel, I was a bit tentative to book our volleyball team there.....It ended up being GREAT!!! The beds were VERY comfortable. As a matter of fact, it was the best 3 night's sleep I've ever had at a hotel. The hotel staff was very friendly and courteous.

title: “Wonderful place to stay; loved it”
text: We stayed for one week, with four children and two adults, in a harbor facing suite with two bedrooms and kitchen. The front desk service was great- I had packages sent to the hotel and they were prompt about calling to pick them up or dropping them by the room. I also used the hotel safe; desk service was good. The suite was awesome. Beds were very comfortable; well stocked with towels; the kitchen was well stocked with cutlery, plates, glasses and cooking pans. We cooked lunch and dinner there each night. Breakfast was great; buffet with many options- eggs, cereal, toast, waffles, sausage. Very good. The eating area is large and so we didn't have trouble finding a table for all of us. We used the laundry three times; the washers were good; the dryers sometimes took two cycles (all were $1 each go). We used the pool (indoor) and hot tub everyday; in good condition; a good size. We enjoyed it. There is a park in front of the hotel and the harbor has a nice walkway so we spent about an hour taking a walk around just close to the hotel. We rented a car for the week and parked on the street next to the hotel the entire stay. Hotel parking is $20/day and is a needless expense. You have to pay for parking on the street but it is very low and you can park for up to 10/hrs at a time. You have to pay for parking from 8AM to 6PM and is free all other times. It rocked. Overall this is one of my most happy stays at a hotel. I have been around the world in all sorts of 5 star places- and this place hit the sweet spot for me. In fact, my husband was booked in at the Silver Cloud Inn- Lake Union down the street, and he left his hotel one night early to hang out with us instead!

title: “Piece of crap”
text: I went through Priceline and thought I was being hooked up by getting upgraded to a 4 star hotel when I had bid on a 3 star. I was excited when I got there but things went downhill after that. There was no fans in the bathroom so my bathroom steamed up within 1 minute of having a shower, the people working at the front desk were pretty rude, the hotel was way too big for its own good. It took us like 15 minutes to find the pool area because of the size of the hotel and nobody would help us find it. Valet parking was an absolute JOKE!!! The point of valet is to bring the car out front but we were told to pick it up from downstairs where we originally parked it. When we complained at the Valet desk buddy got a little bit testy. $40.00 to park our car and pick it up ourselves, absolutely ridiculous. I will never stay at this hotel ever again.

title: “Great Location, but won't be back, outdated rooms.”
text: The location is good, close to beach, airport and town. Most of the staff is helpful. When I booked this vacation through Vacation to Go, I was not advised about the pink bunkers, also there was no pictures of them on the Bahia website. These bunker I found out were builded in 1953. Little has been done to update them. The tub was staring to chip, there was a hole in the wall, the bathroom sink was outside of the bathroom, you can tell it was an add on, also there is rust in the sink. The beds and pillows were very uncomfortable. The restaurant took a long time to serve us and got the orders wrong.

title: “Long Day on Train... Nice night"s sleep...Priceless”
text: Spent a very long day on the train, I was delayed at making my connection. Didn't get in until almost midnight and I was checked in and in my room in less than 15minutes. Room was nice and cold and the bed was clean, crisp and very comfy! One there for one night didn't get to experiance any of the other amenities but my stay was excellent1 I will be staying here again, just a short walk from the train station and the location for enjoying all Chicago has to offer was perfect. Thanks from a weary traveler!

title: “Nice hotel, good location, would stay again.”
text:
We have been to several omni hotels, this was our 1st stay @ Shoreham. Hotel is nice- beautiful lobby, room (suite) very spacious, good outdoor pool.
When you join omni's club (do online & is free) you get free wifi & free coffee or tea delivered to your room in the morning. The first night we were here the kids got milk & cookies with turndown service. The second night we were here we were greeting ready to go out, housekeeping left note saying they would return for turndown service but didn't. Tonight, our last night, just got back to room, housekeeping left fresh towels but didn't do anything else in room. Have to say was little disappointed in the housekeeping- the bathtub does not seem to have been cleaned while we were using it (was clean @ check in).
Room furnishings are nice, but lacks a place to put make up on- if you are a family of 4 sharing a suite with 1 bathroom, it would be nice to have a place to sit by a mirror. All they would have to do is place mirror by desk in sitting room area. Anyway, those are small points. Would return to this hotel.

title: “Great place at reasonable price”
text: If you have work in the North area of the city, this is a great place to stay. Very efficient and helpful staff. Although the property is locted next to the highway, its very quiet. Several eating places close by too.

title: “One of the best run Marriott's I've stayed at”
text: The front desk staff walk out from behind the counter to greet you when you check in, the restaurant manager makes sure you have great meal, and the Concierge staff get to know you and are always pleasant and helpful. These are just some of the reasons this hotel is a very plesant place to stay.

title: “Best Hotel "Room" in the World”
text:
I stayed at a London Suite:
Highlights:
-All the rooms in the hotel are suites, so they are incredibly spacious: the bed room, the living room, and a petite changing area
-Automated curtains… awesome
-Consistently clean
-Pleasant staff (even though I had limited interaction with them)
-Rihanna, Will I am, and some famous Brazilian soccer player were there as well (a bunch of paparazzi were always at the entrance)
Cons:
-Internet did not work (I didn't ask for assistance)
-The use of the business center is not free
-No complementary water

title: “Pay for the pool?”
text: I researched this hotel, and those findings along with a previous experience at a Kimpton in Alexandria encouraged me to book this hotel in San Diego for an anniversary trip. Supposedly steps away from the Gaslamp District, it seemed wonderful. I booked a suite and upgraded to overlook the pool with a balcony. At check in we were informed that the pool for the next day would be closed for a private event from 10-4. Disappointing, since sitting at the pool was our main goal. The check-in attendant informed us that it was a private event...however they could get us in if we wanted to pay, $20 a piece. Really? With the room being approximately 288 dollars per night, they were not even going to comp us the price to go to the pool, which normally would be free. We were slightly shocked, but thought we would check out the room. The front desk called and told us that there was room on the guest list for us at only $10 per person. At that point we were too late to not be charged cancellation charges so we requested to be moved to the other Kimpton Hotel in San Diego. At that point the hotel staff was very polite and accommodating and made reservations for us. Overall be forewarned, there is a statement on the reservation site that states the pool might be closed for private events, heed the warning and call because there is no schedule listed on-line to inform a potential guest. In addition this hotel is very far out of the Gaslamp area, and walking back to this hotel at 2 am could be scary. Pool area is very tiny with limited seating.

title: “2nd Visit - Still Nice Place to Stay in San Antonio”
text: Just returned for my second stay at the Grand Hyatt San Antonio. Rooms are very comfortable, easy to get in and out of the hotel, especially down to the Riverwalk, and the front desk staff was extremely friendly. I especially like the 24 hour coffee shop in the lobby with lots of healthy snack choices. And I even used the pool this time to escape the 107 degree Texas heat.

title: “very good spot and noble hotel in NY”
text:
It was a really good experience at this hotel. We were located at the 37th floor with an amazing view over the Hudson river and the sunset. Very friendly and professional staff. The room was large. The pool is located on the 7th floor and it's very cool to sit at the pool having a drink and enjoying the NY-feeling. A very good location for strolling around in a very nice neighborhood with little shops and restaurants.
The only thing was, that the restaurant is under re-construction, the breakfast area was very small. They told us that the re-construction will be over in September.

title: “Looking very dated now”
text:
We all know hotel rooms in New York are small and W excel in having the smallest in all of New York. They do 'comfortable' well though and our room had the usual soft sheets and great in room dining service. It has been a few years since I stayed at a W and this has not aged well. In the post-downturn world all the 'quirky', 'funny' touches that they have now seem tired, cliched and out of tune with the zeitgeist.
Way too expensive for what it is, so glad I was not paying.

title: “It was okay.”
text:
i went with hundreds of people to Boston for a volleyball tournament end first long weekend of September, 2010. Not everyone stayed at this hotel though. 
Overall, the hotel was nice, spacious lobby, and it's a big hotel. We had four people in our room, and we had TWO washrooms, but each washroom was as small as your aparemtn closet. It felt it was made for children. I'm petite, 5'4, and I couldn't even comfortably move around in the shower, let alone majority of the people that are even silghtly bigger than I am.
I'm sure these were not most of the rooms format, as the hotel picutres on the webiste looked totally different, and other team mates' bathrooms were a bit more spacious. Don't get me wrong either, the rooms were HUGE.
There were no mini fridges either, so that was a downer.
We didn't get a chance to use any of the amenities in the hotel, so I can't comment on it, but if you are considering this hotel, I would recommend it, just make sure if you are travelling with family members or a group, remember to ask the conceige to not put you in the rooms with the tiny washrooms.

title: “A New High-end Mid-town Hotel Choice”
text: The hotel was completely refurbished last year to re-open as The London. Rooms are stylish and well-designed. For example, the in room safe is large enough for laptops plus valuables. The bed is perfect. Staff is highly professional and friendly - comparable to Four Seasons type service. We ate at both the Main Gordon Ramsey restaurant and the bistro adjacent to the bar. The main restaurant is only 44 seats which makes for a very special setting - staff was absolutely outstanding - food was world-class and you can have a blow-out meal for under $250 per person (wine, cocktails, tip and tax included). For a special birthday or aniversary, this is a well-priced experience -especially in NY. We tried the bistro after theatre and were equally impressed - highly creative small plates menu with very creative superb cusine. Even if you don't stay at the London, keep in mind the bistro for food and drinks. A great English-style tea (tea sandwiches, scones, pastries) is served in the bar/bistro after 3:30 for $35 per person - pricey but if you want to relive one of those great teas from your last London trip -this will do.

title: “Great but it had a couple of flaws...”
text:
We stayed at the Hyatt Regency Chicago from August 9-11 with family. This was our first time in Chicago, and definitely won't be our last. Let me quickly start off by saying Chicago is an incredible city with architecture that is out of this world.
Anyways, about the hotel. 
Service- Check-in was a breeze, and the receptionist, Maria, was fantastic. We then were happily greeted by a bellman, who gave us information on the hotel and city. The only restaurant we visited at the resort was the Bistro at 151, where we had fantastic service both times, once by a waitress named Lucy, who said good-bye to us the day we were leaving. All in all, the service was just amazing.
Room- The newly renovated rooms were very spacious, and our lakeview room in the west tower had a great view of both the city and Lake Michigan. The beds were pretty comfortable, and the bathroom was great. The only problem was that the windows weren't cleaned, so spiders were just hanging around outside the window but they caused no harm to us so it was fine. Overall, the rooms were good.
Restaurants- As I said before, the only restaurant we ate at was the Bistro at 151, where the food was fantastic, service was great, but the prices were a little too much. It was manageable, but still was slightly expensive. The breakfast buffet was also impressive, and not to mention delicious. 
Location- The location of the resort is, to me, unparalleled by any other in Chicago. It is right on the river, so if you want to do a river or lake cruise (which i recommend), this is the hotel to be in. Also, it is only about a mile walk along the river to Navy pier (which i also highly recommend), and is right across the bridge from the infamous Magnificent Mile. And Lastly, the resort is only a few blocks away from Millenium park, which has interesting sculptures, bridges, fountains, and gardens. I give the location an A+++.
Recommendations- BUG SPRAY!!! My whole family got seemingly attacked by bugs, and now i have over 25 bug bites. So bring bug spray to avoid lots of itching.

title: “Bad Service but Big Rooms”
text: Whoever so liked this hotel probably never stayed at an Embassy Suites before. Because when Hilton dropped this unit they knew what they were doing. Not only is this hotel old and Gray, but also has bad service. You really get the feeling that they are not even trying anymore. From the reception (still is not quite sure how to allocate the number of days the guest is staying) to the breakfast (meager and sparse). However, the rooms are nice and big. Unless this hotel drops their price by 50%, I would give it maybe six months to survive.

title: “Nice Convenient Hotel”
text: I stayed in the Junior Suite (Small living room & separate bedroom) on September 11, 2008. This was a convenient hotel right in the middle to Times Square. The bathrooms are very small. You can sit on the toilet & stand up straight and wash your hands at the same time or step your foot into the tub on your right side. This is to show you how small the bathrooms are at this hotel. The room was a decent size based on some of the other hotels in the area. I guess you had to downsize somewhere in the room to allow for the at least a half decent size, so the decrease was done in the bathroom. The customer service needs to be upgraded. The front desk clerks are very blunt when speaking to you. They give you the impression of "If I didn't ask, don't offer. Only do what your told!!". I thought it was just my opinion until I asked someone else staying at the hotel and received the same reply. I didn't like the fact you couldn't call or ask the front desk for a wake up call. You had to call an operator, which you can only do from your room in order to get this service. There is a employee who stands near the elevators in the evening (I guess to ward off unwanted guest). I don't see what good this does if he never asks anybody walking by to see their room key. In order to catch a cab you have to walk across the street to another hotel with the cabs lined up. This location is about a 10-15 minute ride from Penn Station.

title: “Manhattan here we come”
text: The location of this gem is perfect for a visit to Manhattan. Minutes from Broadway and Times Square. Minutes from Central Park. A chic urban decor with granite touches and comfy bed make this a favorite place to stay in NYC. Love the microwave, wet-bar area for quick comfort. Bathrooms are spacious enough for comfort.

title: “Better than OK”
text:
When we booked this hotel we were worried because we saw more negative reviews than good at that time. I have no complainst...the staff was very helpful, the in house restaurant was excellent, the rooms were very clean. Very close to Macy's, TJ Maxx and Marshall's. . .walking distance to all other sites that we wanted to see. . .
The only thing I can say negatively is paying for WIFI but that is a problem with all hotels.

title: “Keep your expectations low”
text:
I stayed here one night while in town to attend my nephew's graduation from Marine boot camp. This hotel was near the MCRD (but so are a lot of other hotels, so you do not need to settle for this one). I booked one of the "king suites" that had a living room with a sleeper sofa and a king bed. To use the term "suite" is quite an overstatement. The room was a little smaller, and more narrow, than a standard hotel room with 2 queen beds. Adding a "pocket" door to separate the living area from the "bedroom" does not constitute a suite. 
The free breakfast buffet was okay - but the only meat to be found was some diced ham in the scrambled eggs.
At least the price of the room is in line with what you actually get - a narrow hotel room.

title: “Comfortable and Great Location”
text:
The Arctic Club was a nice cozy hotel in the middle of Seattle's downtown. The rooms were nice and comfortable, the lobby always had a fire going and was cozy. The staff was efficient and cordial, very professional. It had a cozy, men's club, 30's atmosphere. 
Our room was not on a busy street, but you could definitely hear the city come alive around 7:30 in the morning. It was not loud, but there if you are a light sleeper. It didn't bother me, but I noticed it. The room service was fast and delicious. My only complaint would be the yellowish lighting in the rooms. The hotel bar had excellent food and was 1/2 off during happy hour. The clam chowder was to die for.
The hotel is situated in a convient spot, close walking distance to everything but the Space Needle. We walked to the shopping district, Pikes Market Place, Pioneer Square and the The Giant Wheel on the waterfront.

title: “Tried it for convenience but will return because we loved it”
text:
Needed a hotel in the area for several events throughout the weekend and needed it with short notice. The Ace fit the location need perfectly and they had availability so I booked it not expecting much more than a place to stay when not out and about. Turns out we couldn't have picked a better place to stay. The building has some historic soul and it's not the typical cookie cutter place, it feels old school NYC and in our book that's a very good thing. The room was very comfortable and we liked the layout, the bathroom was huge and it made getting ready very easy. Everyone in the hotel, from the bell staff, to the front desk, to the cleaning staff, to room service was pleasant and helpful. The Breslin was fantastic for an early Sunday breakfast/brunch (I hear it can get packed later on in the day) with awesome food. 
We are in NYC for overnight/weekend stays often and the Ace Hotel just made the choice of where to stay one less thing I have to worry about.

title: “An excellent choice at a great location”
text: I agree totally with willowsong. This hotel was so convenient and was so clean and fresh and very reasonably priced for NYC! We had the largest room which they call a suite. It has either a Q or K bed. There is very little wasted space and the bathroom is tiny, but we didn't need any more room than provided. Having the breakfast and late afternoon wine and cheese was wonderful. The staff was very responsive if we needed anything.It is 1 block from the subway, only a couple blocks from Central Park and near many of the museums along Museum Mile. I am going back in August to move my daughter after her internship ends and have already booked my room at the Franklin.

title: “Beautiful hotel, perfectly located for visting UPenn”
text: While expensive, the hotel is beautiful and very tasteful, especially if you are in of the newly renovated rooms. Located literally feet from the UPenn campus and surrounded by good restaurant choices, both upscale and casual. Only one criticism: being charged $12.50 to use Wifi in the room. When you are paying over $200 a night, this just feels like the hotel is gauging you. And in the business center, complimentary at most hotels, they charged $5 per 10 minutes of internet use. Overnight valet parking very pricey -- $35 -- but I can live with that a little better considering the lack of street parking in the area. A special and convenient hotel; just stop charging for Wifi.

title: “great place to stay!”
text:
The Roosevelt is in a great location, definitely walking distance to anything you want to do. 
While the front desk staff was very curt and often times seemed annoyed to help you, the managerial staff was excellent and very accommodating and wanted to make the best of our stay. We ran into a little situation, but the manager on duty took full responsibility and definitely made up for the mistake. 
The rooms are a good size for a New York hotel, and the bathrooms are a good size too. The housekeeping staff is quick and efficient. 
I would definitely recommend this hotel!!

title: “First time in Boston”
text: I had a recommendation to stay at The Lenox and I cannot speak highly enough. From the truly friendly and informative welcome at the front desk when I checked in, to the help from the concierge when I needed recommendations for shopping, to the advice from staff in the City Cafe restaurant on the best places to go in Boston. This hotel is 5 star all the way. They are genuinely interested in you having the best experience in Boston as they are obviously very proud of the city. The facilties are first class, the location is a short walk to everything and the overall atmosphere was one of "how can we help?" I will certainly be back!

title: “Good service”
text: I have stayed here 4 times in the past year for work. Desk clerks are some of the friendliest hotel staff I have seen. Bartender was also friendly. Room was clean.

title: “Simple and rather quiet”
text: The hotel is simple but clean. The reception was friendly. I can recommend this place.

title: “Elegant with an edge”
text: Stayed the weekend for a wedding and found it clean, fashionable and relaxing. The front desk was responsive and polite. I understand from others in my party that the poolside service was terrible, someone waited two hours for a sandwich but I enjoyed my stay immensely.

title: “great deal for a quick trip”
text:
i had an interview, and i got an amazing deal staying here, something in the ballpark of $100 a night, i got it because i paid upfront ahead of time (no refund if you cancel) with my credit card. Keep this place in mind if you ever need a quick place, it's right off the T, I mean RIGHT off the T, so basically your plane lands, you jump on a free shuttle to the subway and get on 1 train, ride a few stops and you're there.
You really can't beat the price or location, the rooms are spacious, my bed had something like 9 pillows on it, and there is a pretty long hallway from your entryway/bathroom to the bedroom area (it really is a pretty large room). The beds and pillows are very comfortable and the bathroom was very nice, the iron and ironing board were in good working condition as well.
I also went downstairs and got the free internet code for the lobby...turns out it can reach into your room as well if you're not up too high! Not my fault it still connected for free...
The hotel is connected to the local YMCA, so that is the gym facilities should you so choose to use them.
I recommend trying legal seafoods if you're into that type of cuisine.
Right across the street from Tufts dental and medical (right in china town), just a short ride to harvard/cambridge area.

title: “Poor handling of reservation”
text:
We booked on line about 5 days in advance and received a confirmation for 3 nights complete with confirmation number. When we arrived at the hotel, they had no record of our reservation and were full. When I showed them the reservation, they said they were sorry but did not know what happened. The manager tried to put us in a room with one King bed. I was traveling with my wife and 15 year old daughter and of course declined. To his credit, he did start calling around to try and find us a place to stay and got us confirmed at the Harrington Hotel, which was about $120.00 more expensive for the 3 nights than we had booked at the Windsor. I felt due to the error, that they should have paid the difference but he would not consider it. Then they claimed that our confirmation was only a confirmation that we had made a request, not that we had a confirmed reservation. But that is all we received. When you get an email with a confirmation number, room rate, type of room, dates of your stay and notice that you must cancel 48 hours in advance or you will be billed, then I think that indicates you have a reserved room. If they fail to provide the room, they should provide a substitute without any additional cost.
We were pleased with the Harrington and it was a better location for viewing the tourist sites but were unhappy The Windsor Inn would not stand by their reservation.

title: “The Service made this stay”
text:
I stayed for a conference and over four days was treated professionally and warmly. Yes the bathrooms are small, and as the restuarants seemed to be served from a central kitchen, food was not as hot as it could be. BUT the staff is what makes this hotel worth it. And to those reading this, this is not just a "gushy, sentimental" review. I have worked hospitality and know what true value is. It's not always the size of the room but whether the staff is there for you when you need them.
Thank you to:
Anika @ check in who patiently helped me find a suitable room.
Shane (shuttle driver) whose warmth has added to this hotel even in his first month there.
Hayley and Brett whose kindess cannot be compared (you know what you did).
Max (security) whose compassion and professionalism in a diffcult situation spoke volumes.
and John (waiter at Harbour's Edge breakfast on the 21st) whose sunny disposition did alot to offset the cloudy weather.
You all made my stay.
Simone Brown (Toronto)

title: “AMAZING!”
text:
I stayed at the Mondiran SoHo for 4night from March 4th.
On arriving my check-in was smooth and very quick.
I stayed on the 5th floor which still had pretty decent views of the city.
My room was big enough and the bathroom was very large too, the room was amazing in the quality of the fittings and the bed was way too comfy!
I had no problems with thin walls or noise from anyone else.
The best bit about the hotel for me was Imperial No. Nine.
Breakfast everyday was lovely!
The staff at the bar were 1st class and so friendly, by the end of my stay the all the bar staff and security knew me by first name and would always stop to have a chat with me.
It felt like chatting to friends, the hotel ahs a very personal touch and this shows in all the staff!
I have been a Morgan's hotel junkie for a few years and i have to say this is the best hotel i have stayed in.
I can't wait to stay again!

title: “great value!”
text: Had a conference across the street where they wanted twice as much for a room. La quinta not only has free parking but also free internet access as well as a nice breakfast included. The room was spacious, with an ample desk, comfortable bed, and a great a/c.

title: “Very good value in New York.”
text: We recently stayed in the Affinia Dumont. The rooms are excellent. The staff is exceptionally friendly and helpful. The location is fine. It lives up to the reviews in Trip Advisor.

title: “Great experience”
text: Had an enjoyable week stay in New York at this hotel. Very friendly service from all staff. Particular thanks to the hotel concierge, Erick who was very welcoming, helpful and gave great tips and advice on attractions, restaurants and he even me a lesson on how to use the tube. Would recommend highly and return.

title: “One night in Houston”
text: Our stay at this facility has been satisfactory except for the disappointment we had with the airport shuttle service indicated to be provided by the hotel at the hotel's website. We were arriving from Europe after a long flight (about 19+ hours) and called the hotel ahead to inform about our arrival details and requested pick up. We were told that the shuttle operated only between certain hours and no driver was available to pick us up on our arrival (about 10:45 p.m. on Saturday). Then, we suggested perhaps we take a taxi and get reimbursed. That suggestion was also refused and told to take up the reimbursement of the cost of taxi with the site we reserved the room to start with. We think the website should clearly state the airport shuttle operating hours to avoid surprises and disappointments.

title: “AWESOME”
text: Everything was great. The staff made us feel welcome our entire stay. The breakfast was very good, and its a plus since it was included!!! The girls at the front desk..Maria and Marialena were awesome, helping us with options to eat and shop, very friendly. The location is the best, it is close to everything. Will deff return on our next trip to NYC!

title: “Got the job done!”
text: My boyfriend and I arrived late (11 their time, but it felt like 2 am to us!) It was in a pretty good location and it was fairly cheap. One of the reasons we chose this was because it said that they offered a complimentary breakfast. To them, a complimentary breakfast consists of slices of bread, butter, and store bought pastries (we later saw the same ones for sale at a gas station). The shower was incredibly small. Other than that, it was an okay place to stay considering we just needed somewhere to sleep!

title: “Great overnight stay!”
text:
A 5 minute walk from the Walk of Fame and all the other things you expect from Hollywood, this was the perfect location as we only had one night in Hollywood. The room was clean and full of the things you need... towels, pillows..beds! 
The staff were very nice. Letting us check in early and check out late at no extra charge. We didnt have time to stop for breakfast but we saw a few people enjoying it. 
They did offer to book us on a sightseeing tour of Hollywood but we got one on the walk of fame as it was half the price of the one the hotel could offer. 
Perfect location for sighseeing, very clean and great value for money.

title: “Excellent Service by Stella”
text:
Just to inform you that your employee, Stella Estrada, provided us, Class of '71 Reunion on 8-6-11, Saturday night, with excellent, kind and friendly service. She was very attentive to our group's every need. I usually don't write letters but this time I just want you to know I, we, were very pleased by her actions.
Thank you very much .

title: “Best concierges ever (but reception not the warmest)”
text: We arrived for a six-night stay after booking directly with the hotel. Bit of a palaver with reception looking for credit guarantees which meant we had to phone the card admin and get things sorted with them before getting the room. This frosty start was quickly forgotten thanks to hospitable and charming service particularly from Luis. Even brought up a fridge into the room without being asked! Room for four of us was huge, perfect for early teens or younger children and parents. Concierges were the personification of helpfulness. Location is fabulous and try to get a room as high up as you can. Added costs of park views probably not worth as much as they're asking. Brilliant people work there and even the drivers and courtesy cars were made available to us (very useful for nipping down to Broadway show or dinner). Loved it and would go back tomorrow.

title: “Great hotel”
text: The price we paid for the room was a great value for a hotel in Manhattan. And the size of the room was big compared to other trendy hotels in NYC. Great location, friendly staff, clean room. The only issue we had was we couldn't get the room any colder then 74 degrees. It wasn't hot, but it wasn't very comfortable for us. We did not complain about this to the staff since it was a short stay only.

title: “New Years Eve Trip”
text:
Hubby and I stayed here 4 nights- departing on New Year's Day.
The doormen are extremely friendly and were helpful in arranging for a town car to transport us to the airport on New Year's Day morning.
Check-in was easy and the front desk staff always greeted us coming in from the street or coming out of the elevator. When asking them about local attractions, they were helpful as well.
The room was ok- but I expected a bit more from the reviews. Our bed was awfully hard- and I rarely sleep in one that is. Hubby and I did not address this with the staff, figuring all the beds were this way, that of course may not be the case. The bathroom was fine- but not spectacular.
Breakfast- such a big issue witht his hotel. I will admit- when Hubby and I went down the first day and saw the selection- I thought it would be the one and only time we ate the breakfast- then I tasted the croissants. They were great! The key is to hit breakfast when they are not packed- a much better selection. Also tried several of the coffee cakes and breads, which were above average. 
For the location and price (with breakfast included) it was a pretty good deal. By booking early- the 4 nights averaged out to $140 a night. 
I would stay again if I could guarantee the bed would not be as hard. And I will recommend it to others. If you are looking for a reasonable priced hotel in a good location, The Orchard is a great option.

title: “OVERPRICED PLUS PARKING CHARGE”
text: This is an overpriced Motel 6 as compared to the hundreds of Motel 6 locations I've stayed at in various cities in the US. It is NOT newly renovated but cost $40 more than NEWLY renovated motel 6 locations and parking is an additional $10 even though the parking garage is part of their property. The staff was rude and unavailable. Their is NO notification that parking will be charged on the website OR anywhere in or around the hotel lobby.

title: “Location, Location, Location!”
text: The Midtown is an inexpensive way to spend a few days in Boston -- the key word here is "few." Two nights (Feb. 2003) at the hotel during the city's biggest snow storm in recorded history was "the best place to be in Boston" given the hotel's proximity to the Prudential Center, Copley Square, the T, and the busline. Free parking in the hotel's partially covered garage added greatly to this favorable experience. The decor is "'60s utilitarian", the rooms could use more lighting, and the smell of cigarette smoke throughout the corridors leaves a lot to be desired. For under $100 per night in a very active part (Back Bay) of Boston, the cons are outweighed by the value. A longer stay in the city would require a different venue for us, however, -- two nights in this type of accommodation were all we deemed equivalent to the unbelievable price in a city the size of Boston. One night, when some inconsiderate guests decided to run up and down the hallways, play loud music and laugh and talk loudly as if they were in the privacy of their own homes, after 2 calls to the front desk, security handled the situation quickly and efficiently -- it's ashame some travelers have no regard for others when sharing overnight accommodations. Security responded to both calls, but only the second time did the guests finally decide to respect the right of other guests to quiet, especially after 2 a.m.!

title: “Excellent hotel”
text:
Stayed here one night in September and really enjoyed this hotel. Classy, with great service, and lovely restaurants.
Do try the wine tasting bar, it was great to have a chance to sample a lot of wines! 
Compared to Conrad Chicago, this hotel is IMO actually better. Very attentive staff, nice breakfast area. Pricey, but worth it. I must admit I didnt find Indianapolis all that interesting, but locationwise this hotel is hard to beat.

title: “A definite for party goers or singles, not a place for families!!!”
text: The place is different to all the other hotels that i have been too, i was there for 5 nights on a business trip and think that i went to the rooftop bar every night for a drink, definitely the best part of the hotel, if you are out to have a good time then it is cool. I only ate once in the restuarant and would have to say that the food was also good, it just happened to be that friends i knew in LA took me out for dinner. The staff were very helpful and polite. All in all a good hotel with a difference!!!!

title: “Great place to stay”
text: We loved this place, the staff were great, the beds were soooo comfortable and the location was perfect, Rochelle in reception was smashing, so helpful with great tips for getting the best out of your time in san francisco, forget the car as you can get anywhere by trolley bus or tramcar even golden gate bridge with just one change 30 from stockton street and change to 28 at laguna street which stops at the bridge car park with an $18 3 day pass you cannot go wrong, loved the time spent there.

title: “Wow! Oustanding Hotel & Staff! Five Star Stay!”
text:
What a delight to find a hotel that caters to their clientele. We were greeted upon check in with a SMILE and GOODY BAG filled with bottled water, candy and snacks. The hotel was very clean and absolutely beautiful! We could not get over how nice and luxurious the rooms were... we kept saying... Is this really a Super8? The rooms are well decorated and have great beds and linens. My sons bed had a teddy bear on it, an extra nice touch. The rooms come with waffle spa robes and slippers. 
The rooms were quiet and we got good rest before our early morning flight. The breakfast bar opened early just for us, as we had to catch an early flight. Our shuttle driver took us to the airport and assisted with loading and unloading bags. Shuttle pick up was nice and right on time. Overall, you can see that the owners (an family from India) take great pride in their hotel and really want to strive to be the best. Parking is included in the cost of the room, and was much cheaper than airport parking.
Great room and TOP NOTCH service all the way around. This is customer service as its BEST folks.

title: “Fantastic position and nice, good value hotel!”
text:
This hotel is only a couple of minutes walk from the Kodak theatre, Hollywood and Highland Centre and the walk of fame. The position was fantastic and the rooms comfortable and spacious. The complimentary breakfast was really nice with a lot of variety, cereals, toast, bacon, eggs, pancakes, cinnamon buns, bagels, juice, coffee and more. We really appreciated that there was a laundry room as we had not had that at the previous 3 hotels and were getting smelly, ha ha.
The only downside was the room service which is available but not made by the hotel onsite but an independant company and this was edible but not particularly nice. There were cafes and restuarants close by though so I would recommend going for food.
The staff at the front desk and breakfast room were all lovely, helpful and polite and we very much enjoyed our stay and would definately recommend to family and friends.

title: “Great value, great location, great experience”
text: My husband and I stayed here on our honeymoon in 2008. The rooms were large and spacious, but quite basic. Good sized bathroom, and spotless. Towels were changed every day. Any time we left we came back to the room looking like it had never been slept in. The decor was a little tired in the bedrooms, but the lobby was beautiful. The Edison Cafe served really nice coffee (especially first thing in the morning after a 7 hour flight) and the portions at breakfast were huge. The hotel bar "The Rum House" is a great place to chill out for the night. Can get very crowded very quickly, but the lady who sings there from Tuesday to Saturday (Karen Brown) is fantastic (and will even invite some of the patrons up to sing). Very pleasent experience, wasn't overpriced, and would happily stay here again.

title: “Simply Elegant”
text: I only had one night here, and want to return. The room was beautiful and spacious. And what a magical Christmas atmosphere! There were carolers singing when I checked in. The towels were so plush. Our business dinner was in a beautiful room. The service was great and the staff were friendly and helpful.

title: “great location and service”
text: Essex House has two advantages over hotels in the same price bracket, in my view: outstanding location and decent size rooms (something that can't be said for other hotels in the area). Service is very attentive.

title: “Ground Control to Major Tom!”
text: Great feeling to the hotel, nice smell, decent sized rooms considering it is uptown Manhattan. Clean, good bar area for a relaxed night and all so modern. The hotels has a space ship theme going on that is really refreshing from the standard hotel style. The only drawback is that it is about 10-15 min walk to Times Square - but them again all the ones in the centre are the like of the Hilton and the Sheridan plus it is away enough from the centre to offer a good night's sleep without any noise.

title: “you get what you paid for”
text:
affordable, good location. good service. 
has a smell. thin walls. i could hear snoring from the next room.

title: “My Experience”
text: I was very scared to stay here after reading the other reviews. My experience was nothing like the others. I had a clean pool-side room and had no problems while staying there. The room was nice and has a built in jacuzzi which we really enjoyed and was only walking distance from most of the attractions. The staff was nice and helpful.

title: “Clean, safe, small, but central”
text:
We stayed here at the beginning of September for five nights. The fiitst thing we noticed was the location - right near the Empire State building, grand central and a host of shops and eateries. The subway was only a few blocks away.
The room was fairly small and dark, but it was furnished well and very clean. We had maid service every day. We had a shared bathroom which wasn't a problem as we never had to wait to use the bathroom. The room had it's own sink and mirror with a hairdryer which was very handy. We had a queen size bed which was firm and spacious. We arrived in the middle of a heatwave, it was terribly humid, but the room had air conditioning that was almost a little too cold! The air con is very noisy, but eventually we figured out how to turn the fan down whilst still having the cool air blowing in.
The hotel didn't provide breakfast, which was a bit of an inconvenience, but we found several delis nearby that did a good breakfast.
The front desk staff are not the most sociable people you will ever meet, but they were efficent. The hotel was rather quiet at times, we didn't see many guests,I'm not sure why. A few people have mentioned the hotel lift being a bit on the old side, but I found it quite charming, we never had a problem with it.
Overall this hotel is basic, but great if you are just looking for somewhere to rest after sightseeing in New York.

title: “Great location - but issues”
text:
Stayed for 4 nights in June with my wife and son. Overall, I have to disagree with the exceptionally high ratings this hotel has been receiving on Trip Advisor. 
I'll list out the Cons and then the Pros to give an idea.
Cons:
Hideabed was badly broken when we pulled it out on our first night. Totally unusable, as all the springs that held the support for the mattress had been broken on one end. Called the front desk and they quickly sent up a roll away bed which was satisfactory for my son. We kept it for the duration of the stay.
An alarm woke us up in the middle of the first night. Called front desk and they said it was a false alarm. 
Tub didn't drain well on second night (first usage). Quite backed up. Next day's use it was cleared, so it looks like houeskeeping caught the issue.
Fawcet on tub got stuck in the "on" position on the 3rd night. Maintenance responded quickly to fix the issue. Good thing the drain issue had been dealt with or there would have been a flood.
Business centre in the a.m. of our departure was a mess. Someone had unplugged everything, and I had to re-connect the p.c.'s just so I could print my boarding pass. Couldn't get the mouse or keyboard to work on initial machine I tried, no matter how I fiddled around with the connections. Tech support line did not offer any help.
Error made on my final bill (overcharged) This was quickly dealt with by front desk staff when I produced a copy of my email confirming the rate I had been given.
See the theme here? Issues kept coming up which were mostly dealt with quickly and well by staff. 
Which leads me to ask - Perhaps taking some proactive rather than reactive measures would be appropriate?
How about regular checks of the hideabeds? Regular maintenance of plumbing fixtures? Verify rates before issuing the final checkout invoice? Check the business centre each morning to see if everything is working OK, rather than leaving it to your guests to clean up the mess?
Now for the PRO's:
Great location. RIght in the middle of the chaos, but very safe, secure and remarkably quiet.Good views from upper floors.
Good security. Love that you have to show your pass to get the elevator to the lobby in the evening.
Generally friendly and knowledgable staff. Great concierge, - very helpful. Most staff were quite friendly.
In summary, I can see why families stay here, although I may see if I have any other choices when I next travel to NYC with my family. This could be a really exceptional hotel if they move from reacting like champs to every new issues that comes up, to working to prevent them from happening in the first place.

title: “Terrific! We will go back."”
text:
Booked through Expedia, and that was fine - no hassles, not a problem at all. Parking was in a very secure location - a gated courtyard that had access by room key card. The room was very nice - 2 queen size beds, decent and clean bathroom with a deep tub. Our room had a small fridge which was a nice surprise. The room was clean, the sheets were clean, there were no unpleasant odors and the air conditioning cranked out the cold! The carpet was a little worn/stained in spots, but we don't sleep on the floor....
The location right on the corner of 26th and State - there is a bus (29) that stops RIGHT next to the hotel. Otherwise, Michigan Avenue is about 2-3 blocks north.
The neighborhood seemed safe and clean. We had no issues and look forward to returning! Special thanks to the receptionists who offered us great advice as we were learning our way around Chicago!

title: “Good Business Hotel”
text:
I stayed in the one bedroom deluxe suite with a colleague in the hotel. It is located near grand central metro station (just 4 blocks away). The biggest advantage is the location in mid town Manhattan. Room was large with street view but very comfortable for 2 people. Rooms have a good kitchen too. Overall I found the stay to be comfortable. 
Rooms were cleaned properly everyday and we never had to worry about our stuff. 
Did not try the restaurant as I am pure vegetarian and got food my aunts in NY. 
Hotel has a small gym which I used couple of times. 
I found the wi-fi charges to be very high compared to the same in 5 star hotels in India. 
Overall a good business hotel.

title: “Expected More.”
text: Great location (really close to the metro station), nice spacious rooms but I had lots of problems with the service. I checked in and was assigned a room that had not been cleaned. I called down to the front desk and they told me to come back down so I could be assigned another room. I asked if someone could just bring me the key to the new room so that I wouldn't have to lug my luggage back down since it took me a full 15 minutes to even get on the elevator because of the volume of people using the two small elevators. They said they would get someone up to me asap. I was able to relax for about five minutes in a chair in the room before housekeeping showed up and asked me to wait in the hall because they had to clean the room. I stood in the hall for another twenty minutes waiting for the key. I called back down again, and noone seemed to know anything about me being assigned a new room. They finally worked it out but it was very frustrating! The new room had a burned out bulb in the closet. I called down twice (once a day for two days) to have it replaced...it never was. It was very inconvenient because it is a deep closet and hard to see in the back without light. I had multiple problems with the wifi access ($10/day) when I asked for help at the front desk, I was referred to someone offsite who couldn't solve the problem. I got bounced around for about a half hour before they were able to get me online. Maybe it was just my bad luck to get such bad service? At a rate of $200+/night, I just expected more.

title: “Average hotel with maintenance issues”
text: Good size rooms, complementary shuttle to Stockyards and great breakfast, but the pool could have been cleaned better, and there was painting of decor going on in the hallways which had them covering up the smoke/fire detectors, without guests being warned. Also, the wi-fi kept falling out in our room, and staying outside by the pool was quite noisy because of the freeway next to the hotel.

title: “One of the best deals in the area”
text:
This is one of the best managed hotels that I have stayed in. The rooms are clean and comfortable. The pool and grounds were very 
clean. The front desk staff is very good under the management of Tammy. All the employee's were professional. 
Their rates vary by time of year and events nearby. I have stayed at the motel many times and have not had any problems there. 
I would recommend this motel to my friends as a clean, comfortable
and good value for San Francisco. Parking is free and for San Francisco that makes a even better value.

title: “Great hotel”
text: This was one of the nicest hotels we've stayed in. Very clean, close to everything San Antonio has to offer, and one of the most comfortable beds I have ever slept in. Just make sure you don't leave anything behind. The outfit I accidentally left in the closet must have found it's way into someone from housekeeping's closet.

title: “Nice for business travel”
text: Stayed March 2012. On travel for business in the city. The week we were there, week of the 11th, there was a flower/plant convention if you will but we did not see it as it was over but rooms still booked so could not find a room in town that would honor the special rate for work. The hotel connects to the train that takes you to the city. Front desk can help with schedules and times. Never been on a city train before. There are signs that tell you to pretty much sit down and shut up! Does make for a peaceful ride for sure. Business days were long so did not use pool or other facilities. Did use restaurant. It was very good, little expensive. Good filet mignon, $38 I believe. Nice bar, good breakfast. Just a few rates include breakfast. Nice, helpful staff, no problems there what so ever. Rooms have sound proof windows so you can watch the planes and not hear them. Beds were comfortable, cannot remember much else as has been a few months. We would stay again for sure when returning for business. Many hotels in town, Philly is a real nice city, we were impressed with how clean and maintained it was and many historical things to see. Thanks for reading, author, female, 50 years young!

title: “Best hotel ever stayed in”
text: We got a special on stay 2 nights get 1 free on the Club Lounge floor. We stayed 4 nights. The service in the lounge was excellent. Could have eaten all 3 meals there, but had booked 4 of the top 6 Trip Advisor restaurants for dinner each evening. Breakfast included smoked salmon. Coffee machine that's like making your own Starbucks. Lunch of sandwiches, soup & mini salads. Evening cocktails were included along with heavy snacks & 1 hot item and light desserts. I'll never stay in a regular room again. Staff was knowledgable in recommendations. Spa treatment was an additional highlight. Con~wish they had an outdoor pool. The pool was in the fitness area & roped off for swimming laps.

title: “It's all about what The Drake used to be, but it's still Grand!”
text:
Gorgeous entrance that's currently under construction, so yes, you triple park just to unload right now, but hey, that will be fixed soon! Great location - Hancock Tower is next door (hello late night cheesecake runs!) Then normal Hilton in room dining is available, but there are also several great restaurants on site. Lovely helpful staff, quick to respond, our only issue was when we tried to leave and the two bellmen couldn't find our keys and couldn't remember who had them or where they put (check your pockets buddy!) It was 4am, not like there were lots of people coming and going, LOL. 
We had a King bed room, decent sized. Fixtures are old school and lovely, bathroom could use a good scrub as the grout is quite aged, but that's being picky. New modern tv and furniture, lovely pillows and fluffy bed. Great view out on Mag Mile provided tons of entertainment. Definitely be prepared to hear your neighbors and the hustle and bustle of Chicago though. Agree with other posters, I wasn't able to regulate the temperature with the thermostat, but I called down and got a fan brought up quickly. The last night when we wanted to finish some leftovers, they even brought up a microwave and silverware for us! Also agree, our shampoo and coffee/tea were not replenished either. But the chargeable food and drink definitely was... Overall, nice place, a bit overpriced, but if you like the gold embossed mirrors, chandeliers, and history, why not!?

title: “cut the attitude”
text: Pretty hip, hot and happening place with stunning public areas and extremely tiny rooms. Great location just off Central Park. Arrogant staff mediocre service for price level.

title: “Seattle's First LEED Certified Hotel”
text: Apparently LEED means small rooms, low water pressure and a 30 second wait for hot water. Way overpriced for what you got. Breakfast at the restaurant was good. Walls were thin, as I could hear a conservation in the next room. Next time it is the Grand Hyatt.

title: “Great view, central location!”
text: Great experience!, the location is great, jus two blocks fron union square, and the cable car stop is around the corner. For shoppers, there is a big shoppping center one block away. The view fron the upper rooms is beautiful!!!!!!!!!!!!

title: “Beautiful, clean, great location!”
text: Stayed here for three nights and loved the hotel. As beautiful as you'd expect a Four Seasons to be. The service was outstanding. The location was great. Close walk to shops, restaurants. Right near the bat bridge. Head's up: The room didn't have a coffee machine and 2 regular coffees brought to our room from the lobby cost $16. Aside from that little surprise, everything was great!

title: “Very nice stay”
text: This is my first stay at a St. Regis. I would put it on par with the top hotels that I have stayed in. The location was perfect, close to two metros, the White House, lots of shops and restaurants, walking distance to Dupont Circle and the Mall. I found the service to be exceptional. I asked for assistance several times a day during my 3 day stay and each time was met with an extremely helpful staff person, at the front desk, from housekeeping, at the front door, in the lobby. I found the food service during meetings to also be very good, which is not always true at hotels that host meetings. My room had very nice amenities, including robes, high end wine glasses, extremely comfortable bed, high pressure shower, etc. Turn down service was very nice, with ice bucket filled, bottled water left out, etc. I would definitely stay at a St. Regis in the future.

title: “Can't wait to return to Hotel Giraffe”
text:
I stayed with my 9-year old daughter and her friend at Hotel for Giraffe for a week at the end of June. While there are many good hotels and lots of choice in NYC, what makes Hotel Giraffe a standout is the unparalleled level of service and warm welcome we received not only on check in but every day, from the front office staff, to the doorman, to the lady who set out breakfast in the morning right through to the housekeeping team. Nothing was too much trouble whether we needed extra towels, help with directions or advice on what to do with our day. Front office manager, Asim Burondker, deserves special recognition for his exceptional service.
We stayed in a Terrace One Bedroom Suite, and it was lovely. The rooms aren't enormous, but are well-appointed and very comfortable, and we appreciated having lots of cupboard space. The king-sized bed was incredibly comfortable, the bathroom lovely, and there was a well-stocked mini bar with everything we needed. There was a very nice turn down service every evening with staff noticing our needs and providing extra chocolates every night on the children's pillows. I also appreciated the speedy support and assistance with operating the controls for the television. Every one was amazing friendly and helpful and did everything they could to ensure a wonderful stay.
One final note - the continental breakfast in the morning was great and especially good for jet-lagged Australian travellers who can't help but get up at 5 am in the morning.

title: “Mission Valley Resort is Pet Friendly”
text:
Ideally located in hotel circle, this hotel has really mastered what great customer satisfaction is all about. The last several times that my family has been there the cleanliness, the service, and the homey feeling has kept us returning to Mission Valley Resort.
Pet friendly, but super clean and no odors leading guests to know this. There is one resident who makes this resort his home, it is easy to see why. If my son is accepted to the UCSD graduate program we would like to make this hotel his residence as well. A nice 24 hour coffee shop and a gas station and a liquort store are on the premises. Very convenient, and secure. A must stay.

title: “What a nice surprise”
text: We were so happy with our choice to stay here. From the minute we walked in and were seated with wine for check-in, things just went smoothly! The skyline room was nice and the balcony was a perfect way to end each evening. The staff was great and very helpful.

title: “This is a great hotel for the price. The rooms were very clean and comfortable (for Manhattan room size standards).”
text: The hotel was very clean and comfortable. The staff went out of its way to make sure that our stay was enjoyable and that we had everything that we needed. They even provided a mini fridge and daily bottles of water and fresh cookies each afternoon. They provided a large breakfast buffet each morning with different items each day for variety. The location is very convenient to Canal Street shopping and to several subway stations. The only con is that it can get noisy at night since it is near the Holland Tunnel entrance. Other than that, it is a great place to stay.

title: “Exclusive Affordable luxe hotel”
text: Just returned from a Hollywood themed spring break vacation with our two teens. Every person on staff was courteous and friendly. Our joined rooms were spacious and comfortable. I found a feat deal for this hotel on hotels.com. Nearby westwood and ucla was a great location for our kids to hang out and have dinner.

title: “Won't stay there again”
text:
This hotel is not up to the recommendations. Stayed in two different rooms, before and after going on a cruise. The room photos posted on their site are very favorable, as if they had photographed a recently remodeled room. The two rooms we stayed in were very dated, and badly in need of a remodel. It's apparent they are into collecting the money and not investing into repairing and keeping the rooms up. The bathrooms were especially lacking. Walls and floors are VERY thin.....I could hear every footstep of people in the room above on the vreaky floors. I heard that their better rooms are on the top floor. This is a hotel that was built a long time ago and has not been updated. All the great reviews are very puzzling to me. Yes, the staff was nice. But for me, the room is what I am paying for, and I thought it was bordering on grunge. Peeling wallpaper, stained carpet, etc. 
 I would not stay there again. It was ok for a couple nights, and the location is excellent.....near the transit system and the waterfront area/downtown. But if I stay in Seattle again, this is one case where I feel a little more $ spent would have yielded a much better value.

title: “Great family hotel, a bit inconvenient if you don't have a car”
text: This hotel was quite an interesting experience, since we had never stayed in a "family hotel" like that one (we were travelling with two kids). Generally speaking it was OK, with nothing exceptional, not anything out of place. Its main defect was that was the distance from the subway station (about 15 min walking), and in general we found that the public transportation system in Washington, DC is rather awful.

title: “Beautifully Restored Hotel in NY”
text: Hotel is beautiful and the owners treat you like mom and dad. There was a problem though with the reservation; I reserved and confirmed two rooms on-line using the Hotel's web site, but their system only booked one room. The Hotel was full and there was panic for a brief time. But the owners worked quickly to arrange a room for my associate in a beautiful Euro hotel two blocks away and even walked us over to book the other room. My room at the Blue Moon was big and expertly restored to match the rest of the hotel. This place is as much a work of art as it is a hotel and I'm sure it gets a lot of repeat business. All in all a pleasant experience. The glass of wine at check in is a very nice touch.

title: “The Best Hotel in New York City!”
text: I’ve been traveling to Manhattan for business for about 5-10 hotel nights/year for 25 years and over the years have stayed at many of the big hotels…Grand Hyatt on 42nd St, Marriott at Times Square, The Plaza, The Waldorf Astoria, The Essex House and many others. I discovered the Lombardy 15 hears ago and have stayed there exclusively since then. It is a small boutique hotel on 56th St between Park and Lex. The rooms are enormous by any standard but especially for NYC. Since the building is a co-op, every room is either a studio or one bedroom apt with a kitchen. Since each room is individually owned they are all decorated differently but the décor is controlled centrally by the hotel management. An earlier post complained of the décor looking dated. I disagree…I’ve stayed in probably 15 different rooms and every one of them is professionally decorated, each with different themes. They are all updated on a regular basis. All of the decorating is high-end, custom or semi-custom design and freshly done. In fact, it’s always fun to see what theme you are going to get in any given room. It is absolutely the quietest hotel that I have ever visited. The staff are true professionals and the service level is high. Everything you need to live is within a city block…restaurants, diners, delis, bars, drug store, etc. The subway is 2 blocks away at 54th and Lex. Staying at the Lombardy is like having your own high-end apartment in Manhattan.

title: “Beautiful hotel - can't wait to return!”
text:
I have just returned from a 3 night stay at the New York Palace and I thoroughly enjoyed my stay there. The hotel itself is beautifully decorated inside and even looks grand on the outside with its welcoming large black gates. I stayed in a room on the 23rd floor and the room itself was a wonderful size and more than big enough to fulfill anyone's requirements. The huge king size bed was definitely the most comfortable bed I have ever slept in! I was impressed with the large flat screen tv and the general facilities within the room. The bathroom was nice and generally clean (apart from finding a toe nail and a couple of darks hairs on the bathmat on the night I arrived - not very impressed!) however it could have been a little bigger! The turndown service with the slippers put out next to your bed and a chocolate on the pillow was a nice touch.
I didn't eat in any of the restaurants so I can't comment on the food however I was impressed with the efficiency of the room service and the lovely presentation. Overall, I really enjoyed staying at the Palace and the location was simply fantastic! If I had to report on anything negative, it would probably be the fact that I didn't find the front desk staff overly friendly. The doormen however were extremely friendly and couldn't do enough to help!
I would definitely reccommend this hotel and I certainly hope to be returning soon!

title: “Fine stay in NYC”
text:
We have stayed at the Best Western Bowery Hanbee Hotel in New York City two times, and found that this hotel gave us a good start of our stay in the city.
The room was satis'factory and the staf was very helpful.
Jahmel was always very kind and took good care of us, when we needed help.

title: “A mixed bag”
text: Stayed two nights for a wedding in the family. Atmosphere, nostalgic train station, downtown location - wonderful. Staff and service what one would expect from a good hotel (excellent). I didn't stay in a railroad car room, but the concept was intriguing. However, despite being warned, I was awakened several times by the train noise, and other visiting family members whose rooms were closer to the back of the hotel, got no sleep and asked that their rooms be moved. If you are a light sleeper, be sure to get a front room. The breakfast was less than I expect even at a chain motel and as a diabetic, I would have appreciated a selection that was not all carbs, even a hard cooked egg would have been welcome. It was jarring to learn that none of the downtown hotels maintain an airport shuttle and I had to take a taxi. Airport transportation should be de rigeur at any big city first class hotel, unless there is good public transportation. My relatives who drove in were equally surprised to learn that parking was not included in the price.

title: “i luved it!”
text: we stayed in this hotel on a skool trip frm northern ireland and ok it is a little bit old and needs 2 b cleaned bt the people are soooo nice and the receptionist wen and bought us stuff frm the shops!!! its a bed and some fod so i cant complain. it ws aawsome!!!!!!!!!!!!

title: “loved the facilities..but beware of theft, we were ripped off”
text:
The hotel is lovely, the location is GREAT. Good shopping, good restaurants and easy access to Jax beach, downtown and any other place you might like. The facilities are new. Nice pool, BBall court and the room was very clean and comfortable. 
HOWEVER, our portable GPS was stolen from our room from our suitcase. We arrived at 1:00 AM one night and were very clear headed about not leaving the GPS in our car overnight. We contemplated stashing it under a seat but decided that our room was the safest place. On our way out of car we wrapped the cord around the unit and put it in the suitcase, checked in and went up to bed. The next day we left to the zoo. We followed a family member, so we didn't need the GPS. We are certain that we closed the door tightly behind us. Old habit. That evening when we wanted to go to dinner on the beach, the GPS was nowhere to be found. No one had keys to the room except my husband and I. Housekeeping had come and gone. The $1000. GPS was now gone. we turned over the room. We took turns searching the car and the room to no avail. When we reported the occurance to the front desk, they were very nice but no help at all. No incident report, no help at all. They finally put an entry in the hotel log book. They suggest we look again in the light of day. Once the sun was shining the next day, we opened the curtains and searched and searched in case it had fallen somewhere. Keep in mind it's larger than would fit in a pant pocket. No luck. It's gone. The hotel claims the GM will call us. But, we are out our GPS. Insurance deductible is 1K. It's unfortunate as it permanently left a bad taste on what should have been a good experience. The hotel room had no safe. Anyone can walk in the front during regular hours and take the elevators up. No key card is needed for the elevators. In the evening we noticed the unit missing, 6pm, the staff was unable to contact anyone in housekeeping to question the occurence. So, great building...but watch your valuables. Perhaps hidden in the car is a better bet. We've stayed all over the state and country in all levels of hotels. this is the first time we'be been ripped off.

title: “I wouldn't recommend”
text: 8 people from our company stayed at this hotel for two weeks and checked out last Saturday. I would not recommend this hotel. The rooms were very small but the cleaning staff kept everything clean and there aren't any complaints there. However, we had the most terrible service from the front desk staff.. there was poor communication between the front desk and "guest services" offices. A manager was only available 8-5 (the hours we were out of the hotel working). It was impossible to see a manager. The hotel lost our credit card information multiple times after it was faxed, emailed, and a paper copy was given to them and charged all of the rooms onto our personal cards we only placed for incidentals. I would NOT recommend using this hotel unless you triple and quadruple check your reservations, nightly rates, and billing info daily because they will do whatever they can (including refusing to let you in your hotel room for hours) until they get your money days before check out. I am still watching pending transaction placed on my personal card days after I left and am spending hours a day to work out the balances placed on my personal card that have yet to be removed. OH, and we didn't have hot water for over two days and there was no refund, discount, etc.

title: “A positive surprise”
text:
After my company booked me into the Paramount I looked up the reviews. I was startled at the number of recent negative reviews. I prepared myself for a less than average experience.
I was delightfully surprised. The staff what friendly and helpful, check-in was smooth, the room was in great condition, it was a queen bed and the room was bigger than many 'boutique' hotels I've stayed at in the Times Square/Midtown area.
From the reviews I expected a less than average experience and, frankly, everything was great!
The a/c was a bit loud but that was fine, it helped filter out any street noise.
The only things I would have liked would have been free wifi and a mini-fridge.

title: “Enjoyable stay”
