text: We've stayed here several times and each time from check- in to when we checked out, we've had not one complaint. This Best Western offers an excellent an Park & Cruise Package with complimentary Airport/Cruise-Terminal Shuttle service. The location is perfect. There are plenty of restrurants nearby if you don't want to eat at the one attached to the hotel. The hot complimentary breakfast is more than adequate. Service is friendly and accomadating. The rooms are clean, with a microwave, small refrigerator and a coffee maker in each. We'll stay here again for sure.

title: “Great location, great room!”
text: My family of four (two youngish kids included) loved this hotel. It is in a prime location and the room was pretty great too (though the bathroom lacked a fan which meant it smelled pretty musty from never really drying out). We were up pretty high, but it was amazingly quiet... you would never know what a busy neighborhood you were sleeping in. We enjoyed our stay and would stay there again!

title: “An outstanding upgrade”
text: We booked this hotel for two nights in July for a few reasons: location, price and it was an lhw. When we arrived, we are lhw members, we were upgraded to a luxury suite that was stunning and cannot be faulted. The hotel did what was expected and is in an excellent location and compared to the prices of nearby hotels gives very good value for money. Just ensure you pay for the view over central park, it is worth it. Very pleased with our choice and over the moon with our upgrade.

title: “Big rooms”
text: Nice size rooms, clean, updated rooms. Good breakfast small room. Okay part of town. Close to Sea World.

title: “Amazing”
text:
I loved this Hotel. It was about 2 Blocks from the Metro. The Rooms where comfortable and clean. The had the best smelling Soap and Shampoo I've ever had in a Hotel. 
You could walk everywhere it was so close to all the Sightseeing Stuff. Navy Pier is about 5 or 6 Blocks. Milenium Park, we didnt walk longer then maybe 20min. I just loved it. The Concierge was extremely helpfull and the Lobby is just a pure Eyecatcher. Modern and Comfortable with a big Fireplace to sit. The one point that sucked was that the Free Wifi didn't seem to work in the Rooms so you had to take your Laptop to the Lobby to use it, but its not that big of a Deal. Its free after all and not $9.99 for 24 hours. 
I would recommend this Hotel to everyone.

title: “Two Major Problems”
text:
Our trip was for pleasure and after reviewing the comments on tripadvisor we choose the Drury Inn.
First of all let me say the staff was excellent, very friendly and knowlegeable. When we arrived they gave us a non-smoking room on the 7th floor, when we opened the door there was a distinct odor of smoke. We called the front desk and they immediately gave us another non-smoking room on the 6th floor. This room also had a odor of cigarette smoke but we contibuted it to a poor ventilation system and decided it wouldn't be any better regardless of which non-smoking room we had. The other problem we had was that the walls in this hotel are paper thin and one can hear everything that's said in the next room. Not a muffle like sound but just like they are in same room as you. We had a young child in the room next to us who cried until 2AM the next morning, we finally resorted to leaving the TV on to drown out the noise. The location is excellent and the hotel is beautifully restored but these two problems will keep us from recommending this hotel to others.

title: “Outstanding staff”
text: Great location, free parking and staff goes out of their way to be friendly. Great bartender during happy hour. Clean and up to date rooms and great food.

title: “A perfect Boutique hotel to stay in Boston”
text:
My family of 4 have very much enjoyed our stay at the Lenox. They're not only at a great location where we could walk to all the nice shopping places e.g. Newbury street and Copley Place, their service level are also excellent -from the doormen, bell, receptions, everyone. We felt very welcomed. There are a number of nice restaurants nearby as well, Shaw Supermarket about 5 min walk. The valet parking service also made our stay very convenient, didn't take too long for the car to arrive with the staffs all smiling and eager to help with directions, etc. 
We've stayed in a corner room with two queen beds, the room was large enough to accommodate four of us, each with large luggage. The bathroom was relatively small, but we don't find it a problem, it was very clean with nice toiletries daily replenished. Though the hotel is a little old, we, however, found it a charm of Boston and the decor goes well with the feel of the city. I must say that the rooms, the corridors and the facilities we saw are all very clean and one can see they've been well looked after. My husband ran into the GM early one morning and complained that the fruit bowl (bananas) were not yet there at the reception when he came down for complimentary coffee at the lobby, soon enough he had the fruit arranged. 
My boy would like to thank Sid, one of the reception or bell staff, for his daily warm welcome and that cute lobster toy! In all, a pleasant stay and we plan to come back. The price is reasonable given that they offer a large room for a family of four, if such a room was not available and we had to reserve two standard rooms, the stay would be rather expensive.

title: “Great location, good price, clean and good service”
text:
Ive spent 3 days in the city. The hotel has a great location, and also less than 20 steps from the nearest subway station as well as macys and 5th avenue shops.
Service, check in and check out were all great, room was very clean and the bad was comfortable, with this great system that allows you to set your own metress density.
The room itself is a litle crowded, i couldnt really find a space to open my suitcase comfortably other then on one side of the bed. 
The room was quite though the AC was a little noisy thoug worked well in the nyc heat.
My only small complaint would be the slow elevators, 35 floor with 3 small and small elevators is not s perfect fit.
Will stay here again for sure!

title: “Get away from it all without leaving civilization”
text: Very helpful staff, despite a snafu with a cancelled corporate credit card. Good food and a great waitress at the on-site steakhouse (ask for Melody and be prepared to be sassed, in the friendliest way possible). Spacious grounds with an Old World vibe and beautiful greenery, plus swimming pools to take full advantage of the San Diego weather. I wish I'd had a couple of extra days for leisure stay, but this trip was all about a technical conference.

title: “quiet and comfortable”
text: enjoyed our stay of two nights at this clean, comfortable and quiet Staybridge. The only suggestion I have would be for the hotel management to find a different location outside away from the front entrance for smokers to use. As a nonsmoker it is very unpleasant to have to walk through groups of smokers to get in and out of the hotel.

title: “Great location, decent room, nice front desk staff”
text:
As everyone has mentioned, this hotel has a fabulous location. One block from Broadway, the subway, two blocks from great food on 8th avenue, and 2 blocks from a great little grocery/deli on 6th. If you are like us, and you go all day long and will enjoy a meal back in your condo/room, try the Ernst Klein Fine foods. Among other things they had the best chowder I tasted while in NYC.
The rooms are nice sized by NYC standards with two very nice baths in each 1 BR condo. The bedroom is about the size of a normal NYC hotel room, and then you have a living room with a small, yet functional, 4 seat dinette. The partial kitchen has a fridge and a microwave. If you will need one, bring your own bottle opener.
I find that the unit needs some major updating, but when you are in NYC you leave in the morning and go home in the evening. My family probably spends more time in the unit than most, and we enjoyed it.
Several of the people have posted about rude front desk employees. I found the front desk to be great. The concierge was rude, as was the bellman named Jason who actually questioned the amount of the tip I gave him. I should have taken it back, but I didn't. I did speak with the office in Pennsylvania prior to going to NYC. I will say that the people on the phone from the main office were among the rudest people I have ever dealt with at any hotel. They were not onsite, so once you get there you do't have to ask them anything.
Elevators -- not bad at all -- not even once during the week did we have an unacceptable wait time.
On a scale of 1-10 I would have given the Manhattan Club a 9 based primarily on location.. For TA it is a solid 4 out of 5.

title: “Great location”
text: Well you can't beat the location, right at Market and Powell St. So if your looking for downtown shopping you can't beat this hotel. It is a little dated and could us an update. But the rooms are a good size, very clean and comfortable.

title: “Fantastic Location”
text:
Great location on 34th st, just next to Penn Station, the subway and two minutes from Macy's. Welcoming friendly staff and a nice atmosphere. Coopers bar is a nice place for a drink and something to eat, food was very tasty and reasonably priced. Rooms like most in New York are showing their age and could do with freshening up however were larger than expected. Beds were comfortable and bathrooms functional rather than boutique. I would recommend this hotel for location alone.
If staying here make sure you visit B&H photo for any electronic goods just along the street as well as the Skylight diner for breakfast which is excellent value.

title: “Wonderful location - wonderful hotel”
text: I had a great room with a view of the Needle. This hotel is located near to everything important in Seattle. Clean room and great service.

title: “amazing”
text: This is an amazing place to stay!!!!! Well worth the price!!!

title: “Don't stay here if they can only put you in the "M" units.”
text: This is my third consecutive year staying at this hotel for an area Girls Basketball Tournament. Thank god I won't have to attend next year, or anytime ever again. As part of the $52 million dollar renovation, units were built right up against the freeway. Why on earth they did this is beyond me. All other buildings look out over pools, the golf course, mountains, etc., but this building looks out at the freeway, and is so close that I can visually identify the type of cars driving by. AND, while sitting in the living room of my unit, with the blinds/door closed, I can tell the difference between a truck, motorcylce, car, etc. driving by, just by the sound which is ever so clear ALL NIGHT LONG. I cannot believe they have the audacity to place paying guests in these units. Of course, when I requested a room change, that was impossible because the "hotel is completely sold out due to the tournament." Which takes me back to my original point.......Why even build these units this close to the freeway in the first place? If you have to stay at the Arizona Grand Resort, don't let them place you all the way out in a "M" unit.......you will never, ever sleep.

title: “Near great sights”
text: I was so close to places we wanted to go. They even helped us choose places to go and places to eat. The price of the room were good priced for how close we were to big attractions.

title: “Whatever your needs, they shall be met!!”
text: It was everything I had hoped for and needed. The place to be in Houston!

title: “Residence Inn Rocks!”
text:
I attended a meeting in the Foggy Bottom/GWU area of Washington on May 18-20, 2006 and needed a place to stay. Unfortunately, every hotel within walking distance of George Washington University was already booked because of the scheduled student graduation that weekend.
An Internet search led me to the Residence Inn on Vermont Avenue. What a find!
The hotel was only 9/10 of a mile from my meeting location, but it was in the perfect location for everything else. Just a few blocks from the White House, the hotel was very central to the Mall and Capitol as well. As an added bonus, there is a CVS pharmacy located on the first floor of the hotel which carries everything you would need -- including snacks and pre-packaged meals like fresh salads, sandwiches, etc.
I had read earlier reviews on this site about the small rooms at this hotel, but my room on the 8th floor was very spacious. The room was well furnished and clean. The room included a refrigerator, stove, microwave, dishwasher, etc. and a small dining room table. 
Although the hotel advertised that it had high-speed Internet service available, the hotel is literally bathed in free wi-fi from at least a dozen surrounding routers, so it didn't cost me a penny!
The complimentary breakfast was great each morning. The hotel also provides complimentary dinner Monday-Wednesday and a dessert buffet on Thursday evenings. We weren't there for the free meals, but the dessert buffet was great!
The only issue we had during our stay was a TV remote that didn't work properly. A quick visit from a hotel engineer identified the problem - a wire had come loose on the TV itself. 60 seconds later it was fixed and he was on his way.
I'll definitely stay here in the future!

title: “Classy, Elegant Hotel”
text: My daughter and I stayed overnight at the hotel. I was greeted by a very friendly check-in gal, who just happened to be a UNLV Graduate (Go REBELS) like myself. We got there 3 hours before check-in time and I thought we would only be able to leave our luggage, but we were able to get right into room, drop off our luggage and go sight-seeing. The room was large, very comfortable king-size bed, large bathroom (even a robe for you if you need one), large LED flatscreen, loaded bar and snacks, and even a radio that you could attach an Ipod too. The hotel is in a great location: A less then 5-minute walk from the Park St. T; the Boston Common, the wharf, Quincy Market, etc. We had breakfast at the hotel, and although a little pricey, the portions were very generous, and the service impeccable. The entire hotel has this very hip-classy vibe to it, and the staff were all very friendly and helpful. I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone visiting the Boston area.

title: “Very good stay”
text: Nice clean hotel, room is larger than most rooms you get in hotels for this price in or near time square, staff are very friendly and helpful, slightly dodgy neighbourhood but that cant be helped and only a couple of blocks from portauthority and subway systems

title: “Not up to par”
text:
After staying at other Sofitel hotels, this hotel was a disappointment. The rooms are extremely small (even compared to European hotel rooms). The decor looks dated, especially the red carpets. But, most importantly, the rooms were noisy. As soon as I arrived I heard the people next door, which means the walls were extra thin. Then I was woken at 6 AM by loud water pipe noises in my room. I am not sure if it was a water heater, bad pipes, or just someone taking a shower, but it was loud enough to wake me and keep me awake. This was terrible, since I was on Pacific time, so it was like being woken at 4 AM. When I spoke to someone at the front desk, he was extremely rude and said that no one had ever complained about noise in the hotel. This is the most ridiculous and unsympathetic response. I was given a quieter room after speaking to the manager, who was very nice. However, the next morning at 8 AM, housekeeping banged on my door wanting to clean my room. This was extremely odd. It seems that they don't want their hotel guests to sleep in or relax, at least I never was able to. Also, although Sofitels are famous for their comfortable beds, the mattress in the first room felt old and worn. They just add a pillow top to it, which actually didn't even fit well. Not to mention that the bedding had a strange cologne like odor. 
The only aspect of the hotel that I liked was the restaurant. The food was wonderful and the service was great.

title: “Another gem from the Four Seasons”
text:
We stayed here for a weekend stay in early August 2012. This hotel is new, about 9 months since it opened. Typical Four Seasons experience - but a couple things really stood out here.
1. The bathrooms have TV there in. Built into the mirrors. Have seen this at a couple other hotels - nice touch.
2. The rooms have a remote built into the wall on either side of the bed that allows you to kill the lights by reaching over, and - this was big - turn on and off the Do Not Disturb from the bed, in canse you forgot. Do Not Disturb is electronic here, a little red light in the hallway confirms it.
3. The restaurant Wit and Wisdom was specatactular - for dinner one of the best meals I have ever eaten.
4. The inifinty pool outdoors was beautiful, and what a view of Baltimore from there.
5. Hotel is in a quiet area, so easy to walk to the rest of the Inner Harbor.
This was a wonderful stay. Our room (City view) still had a view of the marina and was clean and fresh. Hotel seemd to have an odd almost bacon smell when youi first arrived, but after a couple days did not notice it. Faint - but distinctive. Maybe it was a odor trick, but we were not the only guests that mentioned it. However, not strong enough to worry about.
The Spa was fully booked so we did not get a chance to use it - next time will do so and review.
A beautiful clean gem in Baltimore. We will be back!!!

title: “Embassy suites is THE hotel to stay anywhere!”
text: This place made me feel as if I was living in a Hacienda, friendly staff made it just wonderful to stay here. The food and drinks were excellent and delicious. I will continue to stay at the Embassy where ever my travels take me.

title: “Service made the difference.”
text:
Great new clean energy efficent rooms. Location is perfect for downtown restaurants, space needle, EMP Museum, etc.
The real difference here were the people, the service was excellent. From check-in, to concierge services, to the restaurant - the people were excellent.

title: “Perfect if you cruise from San Diego”
text:
I've stayed here in January for one night only, before my cruise.
The cruise terminal is literally across the street. No need to take any shuttle or taxi getting to the dock. Just cross the street! And if you want a wonderful surprise in the morning... ask for a room facing the bay. When you wake up you'll find the bow of the ship waiting for you. It was wonderful!
I've really enjoyed my stay here. From the airport I took their free shuttle, but since the airport is very close, even a taxi would have been unexpensive. 10 minutes ride and I was in the lobby. Got there early but the room was ready.
Now, my room was nice, clean and spotless. Nothing to complain about, I had as well a little balcony. Maybe is not the same as a 5 stars hotel, but it was a good one and I would certainly go back. 
They have a computer available by the concierge that you can use for free to check emails or flight, for about 5 minutes. Otherwise there is a regular computer where you pay. Walking to the heart of downtown takes about 10-15 minutes. I went out that night and enjoyed San Diego nightlife. In the morning I had a walk by the oceanfront, watched people getting off by the ship, then checked out and headed to the cruise terminal.
Didn't use any hotel restaurant or other service. The pool looked nice too.
Overall I had a very pleasant stay.

title: “Great hotel for all trendy NYC lovers”
text:
As a birthday treat for my GF I booked us in for a 4 days at the Hudson.
Great hotel for all style conscious 20/30 somethings
Yes the rooms may be a little small but hey its NYC you spend most of your time out of your room
Hotel bar was cool and the bar staff very knowledgable and friendly
Great location also for Central Park and very near the subway which is a great link for getting around
Sad to leave at the end and definately recommended

title: “The Best Hotel I'Ve Ever Stayed In!”
text:
What an amazing hotel! We were able to stay in one of the suites and it was just beautiful! 
The staff were so friendly and really helpful. I would stay in this hotel again and again. In fact if we visit New York again - this is the only hotel I'd stay in.
Ignore the negative comments - this hotel really is worthy of its hype!

title: “Nice and relaxing stay”
text:
We stayed for three nights at Humphrey's. We had a King Suite with a partial view of the water and the SD skyline. Even though the partial view included an overview of the parking lot, it was still a nice view nonetheless. 
When you drive in, it feels like a secluded resort. The grounds are well maintained and the rooms are extremely clean. 
The room was nice. It had nice wooden blinds on the window, a big comfy bed, plenty of towels, a coffee maker, and microwave/refrigerator combo.
We would definitely stay here again.
Make sure to eat at Brigantine's down the way. Best. Food. Ever.

title: “Park Central review”
text: Spent one night at the Park Central. We were glad it was for only a night. The alarm clock went off at 6a.m. in the room next to ours and continued until we called the front desk. The room also looked nothing like the picture that was posted on the web site. Bathroom was very clean. Can't say so much for the room. There was a big stain on the carpet along with a few huge stains on the window treatment. That really disgusted us. I guess you really do get what you pay for!

title: “Phoenix Stay”
text: This is a great hotel with a good location and the staff is so friendly. Close to food and dining and located right down the street from the ocnvention center. The view of the mountains from my room was beautiful and the sunrise in the morning was breath taking. The hotel amenities are wonderful including the workout area and the pool and most importantly all the latest safety features such as fire alarm and fire sprinklers. Overall great place for the money!!

title: “Nice stay, great breakfast staff, not perfect”
text: Stayed for a couple days for the ACC championship game and was generally pleased with the room and service. Very friendly breakfast cooking staff but the food was mediocre. Room and common areas were generally clean and well kept. Front desk staff was very pleasant. They did have long line at manager's reception and could have put in another bartender to speed things up. I did request extra towels at the front desk but I don't think they ever came. The location is okay and there always seed to be a cab ready at the front. The wi-fi at $10/day is annoying but there is wired access in the breakfast area.

title: “Good location, average hotel”
text:
We stayed at the Boston Park Plaza for a Memorial Day getaway to see the Red Sox. The hotel is in a wonderful location...right in the middle of everything, with a T stop right down the block. It was easy to walk to most locations, and when we didn't feel like walking, it was a quick jump on the T. 
When you arrive, the hotel looks really nice and the lobby is wonderful. We took the elevator up to our room on the 9th floor, and when we walked in, we were surprised at how small it was. While we didn't plan on spending much time in the room, it was tiny (if you've ever been to Europe, you'll know what I'm talking about). The bed was okay, but a little hard. Everything seemed clean. The bathroom was crazy...the shower was a tiny rectangle...maybe 12 inches wide. Neither my husband nor I could stand in it and shower without turning sideways, and we're not big people. There is no exhaust fan in the bathroom, so the little room gets steamed up pretty fast. Service was good though, and it was clean. The only thing was since we were near the elevators, you could hear them coming up and down. May bother some people, but we were tired at night, so we slept through it. 
Overall, it did what we wanted it to...provided a clean place to sleep that was near everything. If you don't want to spend a ton of money and aren't looking for luxury, then this hotel will be fine.

title: “Beware the pricing before you go”
text: This hotel is ideal for business travelers, as it is located in soulless Midtown Manhattan. The best part about the location is the proximity to Ess-a-Bagel, which serves up excellent bagels. The rooms are a little worn, which makes sense, considering this hotel offers mostly long term stays. Still, what miffed me about this location was that while the room we booked could accommodate six people, they insisted on charging exorbitant fees for extra guests--I'm not talking about a seventh person, but rather a third and fourth person. This is clearly exploitative, since there were no included breakfasts or other additional costs the hotel would incur by hosting more than two guests, especially in a room that could accommodate six people. Still, shame on me for not having read the fine print carefully when I booked the room. Since I wasn't paying with a corporate credit card, I was not happy. Don't make the same mistake I made. This place is worth neither your time nor your dime.

title: “Not bad at all...”
text: Spent one night at the Onyx in mid-October, room was small but very clean and well appointed. I liked the bed. The bathroom was functional, but a little cold. For the most part a typical Kimpton Hotel. There is no HBO on the TV. There is free wine in the evening (for exactly 1 hour) but no cheese, etc. Front desk staff was OK but not overly friendly. The doorman was helpful with suggestions for places to eat and drink. One thing I will mention, when I booked the room I asked for a higher floor,away from the elevator -- I got just the opposite, lower floor right next to the elevator -- maybe it was because I was there only one night, but then again, I am a member of the Kimpton quest loyalty program??? I'm usually in Boston once a month for business and this is the first time I stayed at the Onyx. I may try it again -- not sure, it's hard to tell from just one night.

title: “Excellent hotel near Galleria area”
text:
This hotel is quite nice. The service is excellent. They immediately gave us razors and shaving cream when we asked for them. 
Environment is nice and the large atrium and Southwest/Northern Mexico decor makes for a comfortable place.
The breakfast is nice and ample for American style breakfasts, including a full array of hot foods, fruits, yogurts and an expresso machine.
The exercise room is average, has all the nautical machines and treadmills, but kind of small for the size of the hotel.
The only potential drawback is location, which is convenient if you can drive there, but not if you're hoping to take public transportation or walk.

title: “Sweet Spot”
text: Complements the essence of what San Antonio truly can be: intimate, non-corporate, beautifully artistic, simply elegant. If you need walk-in closets and conventioneers, then, this is not your place. Liz + team (a la the swell Hotel San José and St. Cecilia in Austin) have given HH more of the hand-crafted, personalized, caring service that hoteliery should be -- feels like a old-fashioned club with lodging, etc. Hidden, dark cellar bar that is the city's most intimate. Great staff. Ocho, all-day cafe + bar on the river. Also, it's very near the superb San Antonio Museum of Art and the newly finished Museum Reach extension of the Riverwalk (very different than the center of town parts) which takes you to the Pearl Brewery Complex that includes the city's (a regional/national) touchstone standard restaurant, il sogno, with Chef Andrew Weissman and Co. HH is within sight/walk of significant San Antonio Public Library, the only public buidling by late, great Mexican architect, Ricardo Legorreta -- wonderful, big red edifice, likes of which Texas and the Southwest need much more of. Staying at HH is like staying in a whole different San Antonio than what you've experienced if one of the high-rise, convention hotels and chain restaurants is all you know. Try to stay an extra day. For other, small, tucked-away San Antonio finds, try a mid-week brew outdoors at La Tuna (cab ride from here) but finish the evening at HH and the basement bar.

title: “Great location but personnel that cannot help nor cares”
text:
I stayed at a suite at the Sofitel Hotel in New York city for 4 nights during December 2009. Great location; great room, but the personnel cannot help you with any issue you may have. They are not reliable. They just do not care. 
I have multiple examples.
The radio in my room was broken. After signaling to three different people (including the front desk) on three different occasions, it never got changed or repaired or provided with an excuse.
The room price on my final bill was differerent from my original reservation (confirmed, printed and signed). It changed during my stay without a notice... Nobody warned me nor provided an excuse.
I had asked to be moved to a higher floor on my last day in order to have a great view of the Chrysler building. After agreeing and confirming with me 3 times -- and after I had packed -- the hotel decided to give the rooms to other people. No warning, nor excuse. 
Very junior personnel. Clearly not well trained. Clearly not the type of service you need and expect from a large hotel.

title: “$150 for a <1hr. domestic phone call!!! Read the fine print”
text:
Would anyone nowadays think that a call within the U.S. would cost that much? Most landlines now consider any call in the U.S. to be local, so when I had to spend a lot of time setting up an iphone with our IS Dept., I didn't think anything of it. I'd love to know the hotel's cost for connecting that call.
In addition, I was charged for two internet connections ($15) to use my laptop and ipad, another $9 for a dropped domestic call (<1min.), and it took several weeks just to get copies of my bill sent to me by email. 
Sure, downtown hotels are expensive, but charges like this are unconscionable.
Otherwise, the location is OK- several blocks walk to Market Street, not a tremendous amount very close to the hotel. The room was decent, but I'm not partial to the setup with an electronic shade that separates the bathroom from the main room- I find it's much louder than an actual wall when there's more than one person staying in the room.

title: “Overbooked & thin walls”
text: Reserved non-smoking room with two beds well in advance. The only available rooms were smoking with one king. The front desk manager was no help. We could hear every conversation in the next room. The floors were sticky. Yes I could say it stunk. I have had a better nights sleep in a 30$ motel.

title: “Service needs Improvement”
text:
We stayed for one night on our way up to Napa with 2 other couples. We have stayed here before and really enjoyed the hotel. The hotel is still a great location with the best amenities, however, the service has fallen since last year. We had a late afternoon snack in the bar and the wait staff was stumbling with trying to get our drinks to us and serve the food simutaneously. The same thing happened later in the evening for cocktails. Other than that, this hotel is a great place to stay in the heart of San Francisco. We worked out in the fitness center and it was great. 
We ate dinner at Boulevard, a hot place in the city and the food was great!

title: “Great Location.”
text: We stayed in this hotel at the end of August/ beginning of September 2012 on the 36th floor with part city/park view. The room was very comfortable with a King size bed. Only complaint was lack of tea making facility which would have been very appreciated on returning to the room after walking around NYC. The air conditioning was quiet and worked well at keeping the room at a comfortable temperature, Housekeeping was excellent and the sheets, bed and en suite were kept impeccably. Our room rate included continental breakfast which consisted of buffet style self service of fruit salad,bagels, soft cheese, and fruit juice. The waiters came around with coffee or tea. The coffee could have been hotter on occasion. The dining room is really nice overlooking Central Park with huge windows, however I did note that there were very few tables for 2, resulting in a slow down and build up of a queue for breakfast. Given the amount of couples dining, more tables for two instead of for four would have helped. Staff were helpful and concierges were very knowledgeable about how to get around and where to go. Check in was smooth and hassle free. One of the best things about this hotel is its location. It is within 10min walking distance of Times Square, Empire State, Maceys, Museum of Modern Art, etc. Central Park is directly across the street, 5th Ave and the Museum Mile just around the corner. Sarabeths Restaurant is next door and is very good value. All in all we were very happy with this hotel.

title: “Great Airport Hotel”
text:
After a long flight from Portland, OR (via Newark) we were picked up promptly after
our phone call to the hotel by their shuttle. The driver was very helpful and the hotel
is only about 5 minutes from the terminal.
In the morning, there is an excellent breakfast and is served in a very nice area in
the lobby (not in some small breakfast room),
We needed to pick up a rental car the next morning at the airport. The shuttle driver
took us directly to the car rental lot rather than taking us back to the airport where
we would have had to ride another shuttle to the rental lot.
A very nice place to stay. Staff very cooperative.

title: “Great Stay! Very nice remodel”
text:
Great Stay! Very nice remodel 
Landed this with a great rate from Priceline and am very happy with the stay. The hotel was clean and the staff was overly friendly. 
I will agree with another reviewer that if the staff had hounded me like used car salespeople as soon as I walked in I would have been put off, but this wasn't the case for me. The staff was friendly and very helpful even though I got a really low rate through Priceline.
The room was nice and comfortable. A/C was great and actually got too cold. The fan is a little noisy, but what hotel doesn't have a loud A/C unit these days?
While outside later in the evening I was worried that the hotel is in the flight path for the airport, but upon returning to my room for the night I didn't hear any planes so I was happy with how the room sounded (or didn't sound if you will).
Did not appear to be an over abundant places to eat around the hotel so had to drive a ways to find a nice upscale place. 
Very close to I-77 and I-485 (by-pass) so easy to get to I-85 too. Rush hour in this area can probably cause some traffic issues, but not too bad for when I was there.
Would stay here again without having to think twice!

title: “great location and accomodations”
text:
We stayed in the 2 bedroom King/Queen suite, which also has 2 bathrooms. This was ideal traveling with persons who prefer not to share bathroom (sister, father-in-law, etc.) We could not be happier, the room included free parking & free wine. And full size kitchen and family room, plus 3 cavernous closets, made it a truly roomy place to stay. Only drawback for business travelers might be you have to walk to a restaurant, but with 60+ dining places in a few blocks, this was great excuse to go out. Also the furniture is a bit dated, seems to be from the 1980s. The maid staff are very good at cleaning, they spent about 45 mins doing our 2 bedroom suite. Also the TVs are not big flatscreens. This place is in the Marina district, the hip center of San francisco. Lombard and Chestnut streets are very convenient to go downtown, Union Sq, bay bridges & ferries. Like other reviewers, I hesitate to mention Cow Hollow as it may get too popular! 
Air conditioning: I dont think our bedrooms were setup for A/C; I only saw heating controls on the walls. There was an A/C on the family room floor, but this would rarely be needed since S.F. is chilly most of the year.

title: “Not suitable for business travelers”
text:
I've stayed in a number of San Fran's boutique hotels. If you follow my reviews, you know there have been some mixed results -- typically having to do with location and especially room noise. The Mark Twain was a new one for me, as all my favorites were booked due to the AUA conference in town.
This hotel is about a 15 minute brisk walk to the convention center. The walk is on streets that should be comfortable for most anyone to walk in terms of feelings of safety. There is a halfway house and church next door to the hotel, but there were fewer street folks near this hotel than some others closer to Union Square.
The good news is the hotel offered me perhaps the quietest stay in San Fran ever. They front desk honored my Expedia-communicated request for a rear-facing room. That helped, but the rooms and locations are unusually quiet for the downtown core.
The rooms are basic. Closet with no door. Minifridge in the dresser, decent TV. Clean bathroom. Paint and decor was dated and some wear marks on the walls, but nothing I'd think of as exceptional. Maid service was prompt and thorough and the hotel overall was clean.
The bad news is the internet connection. The wireless never worked while I was there. The wired (CAT-V) connection in the room was broken so I had to jack directly into the modem, which meant moving the heavy dresser. They advertise, and you pay extra for, "High Speed Internet". Using multiple speet test sites at very different times of morning, noon, and night, the speed never went above 0.38 up and 0.34 down. That's simply unacceptable. Ping times were always >50ms, which is abysmal. If you are a business traveler who needs to do something more on the internet than you can do with your smart phone, this means you simply cannot afford to stay at this hotel.
If you don't care about the low-speed connection, there is really nothing to warn you off this hotel. If you like or need a decent net connection, you'll have to look somewhere else.

title: “Good base to explore LA”
text:
We spent 6 nights at the W Westwood, cashing in a boatload of starwood points. The positives: they upgraded us to a suite, so we had plenty of room, and the hotel is in a good location, letting us get downtown and out to surrounding areas like Pasadena and The Valley pretty easily. The negatives: it was cool at night Thanksgiving week, and the heat didn't work very well; this was mostly remedied our second day when we were provided a space heater. 
We had a couple meals at the hotel, the first room service dinner was simple but good. Our second meal, at the outdoor area near the pool, seemed fine, but my wife got serious food poisoning, and ended up in bed for two days, and the only thing she ate that day that I didn't share was a soup with shrimp she had at the W restaurant.

title: “great stay - nonprofessional service”
text:
i was there for one week and it was great. outstanding design, capacious rooms and you always feel safe and comfortable. 
what i didn't like was the service. as we arrived there was a problem with my credit card. so the receptionist was absolutely overextended and had no idea to solve this problem. but new hotel - new service - i could understand that. then she called the manager. i travelled to a lot of countries and i have to say i never experienced a manager which was that unfriendly! only reason for her was to pay cash. so i had to suggest a solution. finally we got this small problem, but i was shocked how ARROGANT and unfriendly she was. she didn't wish us a pleasant stay. and when i saw her the last day she even didn't say hello! i think she should memorize the slogan: client is king! and a manager should always be an example for the others! this behavior was absolutely nonprofessional! 
nevertheless i like the hotel and would always recommend it. if you search a cool, new hotel where you can relax after a long exhausting day in NY, this is the one!

title: “Great Location!!”
text: I am so glad a co-worker told me about this place. I found it clean and quiet. The location absolutely rocks! Definitely staying there again.

title: “Home away from home....”
text: it was very nice stay, especially with the front desk staff... they where very helpful and always ready to anything that i would need during my stay... I would absolutely recommend to my friends and family and will of course come back soon ...

title: “Very Nice”
text:
This is a very nice business class hotel. The rooms were nice sized and I liked being able to open my window to get fresh air. 
The grounds were beautiful and well kept. This hotel looked to me to be very well managed. I even saw a bell hop polishing the luggage cart with Brasso! I returned about 45 mintues later and he was still at it. 
One thing I do not understand about the Doubletrees is why they charge for Internet access. The Hampton Inn's, which are part of the Hilton family and a step down usually always have free hi-speed internet. Why not Doubletree??
If I am in the north San Diego area in the future I would most definately stay here again.

title: “Not too happy”
text:
I stayed there recently and wasn't happy. I had a pretty depressing room, very dark although the weather outside was sunny. The bathroom was small and cramped, service was polite but not friendly and there was a mess with my reservation that took a few days to sort out. I was glad to leave and will not try again.
Furthermore, and this is no fault of the hotel, I wouldn't really advise anyone to stay in that area unless there is a special need to stay there (eg. work in the financial district) - it is pretty dead at night and very difficult to find a cab after 6pm.
Finally, I would have probably rated average instead of poor but took off a point for the $15 per day wifi - that is unacceptable as far as I am concerned.

title: “Very Nice Huge Rooms”
text:
This Hilton is located right downtown in a great location and overall it was a very pleasant stay. 
Parking was easy and convenient in the Hilton's underground garage. I believe the parking fee was $18 for overnight which isn't great but not outragious considering the location. 
Check-in was handled quickly and professionally and i was sent on my way. The hallways and public areas are attractive and well cared for. 
The room was incredibly huge especially for a downtown location. There was a huge area that contained the bed, desk, couch and end tables. There was a short hallway leading to the equally huge bathroom area. I wouldn't call the room's decor totally up to date. The carpet was older but clean as was the couch, desk and tables. The bed was extremely comfortable and a nice but undersized flat screen tv was also featured. The bathroom also hadn't been updated recently but was very clean and that fact really didn't bother me at all. I didn't hear any noise at all from the outside and i had a great night of sleep. 
The location is ideal with all the downtown nightlife, restaurants and tourist attractions literally within three blocks. 
This Hilton is a winner.

title: “Do not stay here !”
text:
Neg : Horrible breakfast , service , rooms and overall quality.
Pos : free parking space
WHY ? READ BELOW.
In april we made an extensive trip by rental car from Las Vegas to San Francisco. We made no reservations up front and wanted it to play by ear. But during our stay along the route, the hotelmanager warned us that not booking in advance could be dangerous in SF. So we looked up a place to sleep for 3 nights. We came across the Francisco Bay Inn and booked it via the internet. The price was an avarage of $89 a day. Parking and "breakfast" was included so that was another bonus, knowing that parking prices can go up as high as $30 a day in SF. 
ABOUT THE SERVICE :
When we arrived at 11.00 am , we couldn't check in before 03.00 pm.
The woman at the reception was not hospitable.
When asking for information she advised us to read the available leaflets. But when it came to making money , we were good enough ! she did sold us immediatly a tour of SF. We did had to wait before getting into our rooms. Price was $44 a person ( we were 4 ) and we had to pay $76 upfront to her. ( money in her pocket ! ). She said that we would stop at noumerous places, were we couldn't stop with our car. What a lie ! There were only a few stops and those could easily be made with our car too. The tour was no good ! Because we returned our car the next day, we needed a shuttle to SF airport a few days later. Price : $15 a person. We had to pay the woman at the reception $32 upfront ( money in her pocket ! ). So $28 had to be payed to the driver . But when we got to the airport, the driver asked $44. He was not to happy with the fact that I only was willing to pay $32 ( before tip ) for the trip. I was lucky to have asked for a receipt at the reception ! I wondered why the reception was not to keen to give me one. 
To the people of the Francisco Bay Inn, we were just walking ATM machines.
ABOUT THE LODGING :
Parking space was available, so, no problem.
We had to ask where our rooms were ( no explanation upfront ) and got directed to an elevator in a corner, that seemed to be the only survivor of the great fire of 1906. We were glad that it only had to take our luggage up 1 floor ( but it took almost 2 minutes ! ).
The room ( they called Superior ) was bigg enough for a family of undersized midgets. Openening our luggage and still wanting to get around was a smal problem. The room was smelly. Opening the window was impossible. It was blocked ( just like New York sky scrapers ). I guess they lost a lot of clients who jumped out the window after seeing/smelling al this horror. But the worst had still to come. Watching TV apeared to be a social event. The neighbours set the volume so high that even Al Capone would get awakened ( if he'd still stay at The Rock ). At night ( at around 10.00 pm ), EVERY NIGHT we got a private performance of the " Blue Man Group" ! A lot of loud banging and running around in the rooms. It seemed us , the people were in our room, jumping around on pogosticks on the wooden floor. One night we were even (ear)witness to a latino marital fight. The nextdoor neighbours were reinacting a scene from Saw3, the Bloody One. We were afraid to get stabed by a fork, knowing that the paperthick walls could not even stop Steven Hawkins without his wheelchair.
Breakfast was a disaster !!!
Powdered coffee, cakes is wrapping and 2 muffie chaires to sit in at the very very small reception area. No more comment !
In Conclusion :
Neg : Horrible breakfast , service , rooms and overall quality.
Pos : free parking space
But hey , we only payed $89 a night and got 24hr live entertainment. So why complain.
A perfect getaway for the Munsters !

title: “Four stars but only just!”
text:
We stayed at the Boston Back Bay Hotel for five days at the beginning of August in a standard room on the fourth floor. Wifi connectivity has been a bone of contention in recent reviews. It was largely available in our room and in half of the lobby but not in the attached Irish bar. Access was mostly slow and was not available on a couple of occasions.
Public rooms were well maintained and furnished though they did not seem that well used, perhaps because, in the evening at least, there was no bar or food service in them. The Irish bar has a pleasant, external basement patio but inside is dark, strangely furnished and rather dreary. We did not make use of the restaurant located there as prices seemed rather high. They were also high in the bar though service there, as elsewhere in the hotel, was efficient and friendly. Housekeeping did not service our room quite fully on one occasion. On the other hand the concierge was particularly helpful and cheerful. Check in was quickly conducted.
Our room was large with a king bed. There seemed to be plenty of drawer space though one of the drawers was broken. In general terms I felt that the room was in need of a make over. Furniture, fittings and decoration had a tired appearance: scuffs in the wall paper and furniture for example. The was a rather old fashioned mini hi fi and a largish flat screen TV. The choice of channels was limited for a hotel of this size and rating I thought. A refrigerator was provided (and ice making facilities were nearby) but no coffee making facilities, on the other hand, free bottles of water were put in the fridge on a daily basis. A safe was availabe, for the storage of valuables. Desk space and power points were ample for those who like me needed to work while staying.
Bedding was fine, though the original feather duvet felt unpleasant to the touch. Bedding was much improved when replaced by synthetic equivalents. The bed was a little on the firm side for me but this is a matter of personal preference of course.
The bathroom was large and reasonably well appointed with a shallow bath/shower, sink shelf and mirrors. The sink had a slight crack however. A comprehensive set of toiletries were present.
There are a number of not outrageously priced restaurants in walking distance and a 7 11 within easy walking distance is a resource for those who don't wish to pay $7 for a coffee in the hotel!
Overall, I liked the quality of service, room size, fridge and bathroom. On the other hand, the erratic wi fi, dreary and expensive bar area, shabbiness of the room and the cracked sink would put off some. Four stars, but maybe 3.5 would be more accurate.

title: “you must stay here”
text:
Once again I booked this hotel based on trip adviser and was not disappointed , it was perfect and I am very critical of hotels! 
The rooms were a very generous size for NY rooms and spotlessly clean (which is my main issue with hotels)
The only problem we had was we were originally in room 303 and although I'm not bothered about views the air vents and tubes that we looked onto were terribly noisey to the point that even with jet lag I couldn't sleep. The staff were brilliant they offered to move us there and then but suggested that if we waited until the morning we could move to a much higher floor.. I went to bed with ear plugs, they worked a treat. The next day we we're moved to a suite which was huge and made our stay very comfortable.
I wouldn't hesitate to reccommend this hotel, the surrounding area is lovely, there's a great mix of restaurants and cheap eateries nearby, in addition the staff were some of the most helpful I've ever come accross.

title: “Geat Hotel”
text:
It is a lovely hotel in Manhttan. It has clean small rooms which are cleaned everyday. There is a very good complementary breakfast. You could get tea coffee or hot water 24hs a day complimentary. 
The rooms and toilets are great and very clean with Television, A/C and Heater, Hair dryer, Iron/Ironing board etc .
Location is great. Working distance to Time Square, Empire state building, Macy's, JC Penny, 5th Avenue, Madame Tussades, all broadway theatres, Subway station etc to name a few.
Easy to get taxis.
We would deffinitely visit this hotel/NYC very Soon.

title: “Very good location and good bang for the buck...”
text: Very easy check in. Good location. Parking was very convienent as well. Just not really much to complain about. Had a nice pool with plenty of towels. Would stay there again.

title: “Nice hotel, avoid the jacuzzi room”
text: This is a very nice Hampton, very clean, good staff. When we arrived we noted the lobby was ice cold, nice. We went to our king jacuzzi room and it was quite warm. Fiddled with the A/C (which is quite difficult to read having such small letters), could not feel any cold air coming out of the A/C unit. Called the desk, and someone came up, and set the A/C to override the 'green' feature to get the room cool. When we returned from dinner it seemed a tiny bit cooler. We then used the jacuzzi. The room still seemed very warm by bed time (about 10:30) so I called down. The guy at the desk said there was no maintenance in house, but he could move us to a room down the hall, we could just leave our stuff in the jacuzzi room. He brought us the cards, and we did that. The room we were moved to was huge, I guess it was their 2 queen studio suite, it was nice and cold, and we both slept pretty well. I believe the problem with the A/C in the jacuzzi room was caused by long term issues with high humidity from the jacuzzi collecting on the A/C and freezing up. The desk guy who brought up the keys said the same thing and noted that their was cold water dripping out of the bottom of the A/C, but no noticeable air blowing thru it. Wish we had just selected the 2 Queen studio suite in the first place. In addition to excellent A/C it was huge and beautiful. The staff here was very helpful. Unlike other Hamptons this one did not offer cookies at the desk (or cookies and soft pretzels as we had in Philly). Not a big deal, but when you come to expect certain standard amenities.....we found out that the cookies are not actually standard for Hamptons, its something the individual Hampton has to choose to participate in. We didn't get a chance to use the pool or gym, but they both looked extremely clean. The breakfast was pretty good, some bagels baked with egg cheese and bacon on top. Oatmeal and coffee were fine. Coffee is at an opposing wall from the breakfast, which is probably a very good idea for people who are in a hurry and only want coffee, and don't want to have to deal with people milling around the breakfast area. I wanted to give the place a five, but the issue with the A/C kind of blew that. I'd definitely go back, but I'd avoid the hot tub room!

title: “Thursday Night Vibe”
text: I called and was told Thursday Night Vibe had started again every Thursday. I booked a room at the Kyoto Grand Hotel specifically to attend the Thursday Night Vibe event with friends and was informed of a blackout day. Is there a schedule in place so that vistors to your hotel will not be dissappointed if they want to book a hotel and be close to an event of their choosing, and not be forced to venture out in scary downtown for entertainment. The desk told me to contact the entertainment company, something I thought was odd since its held at your hotel. Maybe. there should be information at the front desk and website to direct the guests. I've stayed here numerous times for the Vibe event and never had a black out day. Anyway, I called my friends who planned on booking a room tonight, to warn them not to come this week because the vibe is blacked out. Since, I'm here, I have no choice.

title: “Horrible Customer Service”
text: The lady at the reception desk speaks at 10 miles an hour and gets frustrated at you for not understanding her. She gave us vocal directions to a nearby shopping center without giving us an maps and expects us to be as familiar to the place as she is. We had to tell her twice to remind cleaners to unclog our toilet. A few things that gave the Days Inn a 'Poor' rating as opposed to a 'Terrible' was because of the friendly cleaning staff who are always smiling and the free wifi which is password free and easy and fast to use which accounts for their lack of Disney Channel. Overall the hotel room itself is alright not wonderful however I shall not be enjoying my 3 and a half days at the Days Hotel Circle. Would not recommend this hotel, I'm sure there are plenty better ones.

title: “Tops in service and location!”
text: The staff were always very helpful, knowledgeable, and responsive. Great location. Our room was comfortable, but very tight on space. We didn't have a full supply of towels, but the staff was quick to respond when I called about this. The help at the front desk was always very accommodating, informative, and polite. I was surprised that we didn't experience nighttime noise from other guests. We didn't try the restaurant. The location is excellent. Parking costs $24 a night, and we could not access our car without valet service, but this was acceptable, given the circumstances.

title: “Not That Bad”
text:
My husband and I spent two nights in Chicago for St. Pat's; we stayed at the Tremont. We were very apprehensive about this hotel based on all of the bad reviews, but booked anyway because it was the best price we could find for the location we wanted. When we arrived we were pleasantly suprise. 
First Impression:
The hotel is in a great location, less than a block off of Michigan Ave. It appears nice from the street and has doormen and valet parking just like any other higher priced hotel. Upon entering the lobby we were greated with a wonderful scent, it was a great smelling place (there were candles burning.) Also, the lobby was very comfortable, with leather sofas and a grand piano.
Check In:
We were nervous about check-in b/c we had read so many reviews that said the customer service was horrible. We experienced the exact opposite. The front desk attendants were all very friendly and helpful. Check-in is at 3pm and we arrived at noon and were given our room with no problems.
The room:
A little dated, but clean and comfortable. I did see some of the things others complained about, such as peeling wall paper and chipped paint; but, neither were were that bad or noticeable. I am a clean freak and brought my own blanket and sheets but found the one's provided to be clean and fresh. The only real problems we had with the room was that the heating system was very old and hard to use, we were constantly hot and had no way to turn any air on; and the windows were very thin and you could hear a lot of street noise.
Overall, we would recommend this hotel. It has a very reasonable price tag compared to others in the same location, and was clean and comfortable. 
If you want a great breakfast spot walk about 4 blocks North and you will find a little restaurant called "The Pancake House", it was wonderful. 
Pros: Price, Location
Cons: Outdated

title: “Palace by the Bay”
text:
Would I be returning to this hotel in Jan. if it were terrible? No, this hotel is one of the most charming hotels I have ever stayed in. My husband and myself booked this also as another prior guest said off the SPG web site. Now as far as getting to the hotel. We simply took the Bart from SFO airport for around $5 per person. It took around 30 minutes and was easy to connect with. The bart stops just outside the hotel and how easy is that>
We enjoyed the very very pricey holiday brunch but it was Christmas and the price hurt less knowing we were doing something special for each other. Our room overlooked the blvd. and it was very nice. Very tiny bathroom but we did not plan on living in the bathroom the entire time. Great space in the Deluxe rooms. We asked nicely for an upgrade at check in and they were able to accomodate us.
One thing we should have done, we should have asked the closest way to Powell street. In fact we walked down Market for 6 blocks only to see we could have turned down a side street and been at Union Sq in a short hop vs the 6 plus blocks we walked. Use the map the hotel gives you We will in Jan. Palace hotel is conventient, clean, great staff, great food, weak bar for chocolate martinies though. Don't order one of those. but beautiful to look at. I will never go to the city by the bay and not stay at the Palace ever again. Why would anyone want to miss the chance of staying in a palace.

title: “A really cozy place - Enjoyed my stay !”
text:
I just came back from a short stay at the Library Hotel. I had picked the hotel, because I remembered that we spent a lovely evening on their roof terrace a year ago. Reading the reviews made me curious about the rest of the hotel.
Everybody at the front desk was very helpful and friendly and we did a swift check-in. The lobby is very understated and minimalist, but the book shelves made it look ‘cosy’.
I had booked a junior suit for a special discount price (499 $) and since this is even for New York a substantial amount of money, I expected a lot.
I was not disappointed. The room looked exactly like the picture on their website. While a lot of room was wasted on a front room/hallway, it was still spacious and airy, due to a lot of windows. All of them had nice wooden blinds, which gave the room a warm feeling, as did the room colours, mostly in beige and dark wood. There was a small sofa in one corner with two armchairs and a large flat screen TV. The bathroom was spacious and nicely decorated, with all the amenities one needs.
Having lived in New York, I knew that this was not going to be the quietest of all streets in Mid-Town. It was definitely noisy, but the windows are very sound-proof.
I did not see the reading room, but we spent some time upstairs in the winter garden and of course on the roof terrace. It would be nice, if the rooftop terrace had more comfortable furniture. The benches and little stools are quite uncomfortable and it is impossible to spent a leisure afternoon in the sun, without a major backache. Their free hotspot was available on the terrace and I was able to do my emails while sitting in the sun – not too many hotels in NY offer that !
As travellers before me have said: this is a great place and worth the money - I will return !

title: “Great location, great hotel, and not bland!”
text:
I have stayed here several times on business - usually on a gov't rate. For the money, there is not a better place I've found. 
The good:
Great location, near Dupont Circle metro, and lots of great places to eat. 
The bar has light food and a great bartender. 
The wine reception is a blessing after dealing with bureaucrats all day. 
The room is big
The WiFi free if you're a member of their guest program (which you can join for free)
If you hit it right you can get a free continental breakfast in the restaurant. 
Nice desk with 3 plugs!
Flat screen TV and DVD player
Very friendly staff
Gripes (all minor)
Sometimes the decor feels a bit too hip, if you want classic then don't come here
The lighting in the room is a bit dim. 
I think the dinner menu for room service is a bit spendy, although the sandwiches aren't bad. 
Nearby:
Pizza Paradiso for a good dinner!

title: “Good location, nice rooms”
text: I was very pleased with the location of the hotel and the quality of the hotel rooms. The building is beautiful and the staff is very friendly. The business center isn't actually a business center, just a couple of computers without any programs except for Internet Explorer. I needed to print a Power Point presentation and a lady at the front desk gladly offered to print it for me from the manager's office. The staff definitely goes above and beyond to make their customers happy. At night, it was a little bit hard to control the heating in the rooms, but it wasn't too bad. For the most part, the rooms were quite. There was one morning that I was woken up by a car alarm parked outside of the building (I was on the fourth floor), but I don't think that's the hotel's fault. Beware that the hotel does not have free internet service (it costs $9.99 per day) and there is also no free breakfast (there’s a restaurant but it’s pretty pricey). Overall a good experience. I would stay here again.

title: “Good stay & great location!”
text: Spent one night here on August 21, 2004. We had 3 rooms booked. Since we had booked on Priceline we were only guaranteed sleeping for 2 people each room. We had 7 people. Asked at check-in if they had rollaways available and they did. Cost $13.00 for the extra person in the room. Clerk at check-in was quick and friendly. Rooms were clean with one queen bed, desk & chair and one of our rooms even had a small couch. Rooms are a little on the small side but since they mostly cater to business travelers this seems adequate. Location to Quincy Market is fantastic. No more than a 5 minute walk. Next door is the Elephant & Castle Pub which was good. Overall I would definitely stay at Club Quarters again for it's clean rooms and great location. Especially for the great price I paid.

title: “Great location, Big room, All the amenities”
text: I recently stayed at the Hilton NY during a conference. I was expecting the normal big city conference room (drab, not freshened up style-wise, and small). None of those were the case here. The room had all the space I could want (std room) and several nice state of the art electronic touches and the housecleaning staff were excellent too. The bathroom had an updated walk in shower with frameless glass and nice lighting. This hotel is located near the Theatre District and Times Sq amongst other things.The restaurant within the hotel is great as well as the lobby bar.

title: “Great for Air Force BMT graduation!”
text: My son graduated from BMT at Lackland AFB in August. I would strongly suggest avoiding the hotels in the base area. It is not a nice neighborhood and the hotels there are all pretty run down. The Candlewood Suites near Sea World is awesome! Great location only about 15 minutes from Lackland, complete kitchen, nice pool area, everything you will need for an enjoyable stay! We were very pleased with our choice. We saved money by cooking a couple of meals at the room. The staff was very helpful as well. Nice place.

title: “Good facilities for convention center business”
text: The hotel is fresh and new(ish) with clean carpets, good linens, efficient work area, compact bath, refreshing artwork on the walls. Check-in staff seemed a little overwhelmed when faced with a large number of arrivals (be aware of the local convention and sporting schedule) - but as I was there for a convention, I can't complain. Bell staff was efficient at storing and retrieving luggage. A request for early check-in due to flight schedule was not met (a big day for turnover had housekeeping hopping). Some rooms offer nice mountain vistas. All seem to offer a window that opens for fresh air - a nice perk in a city high-rise. Also, the entire interior of the hotel is non-smoking so air is always fresh. Elevators feature video screens showing not the expected news or weather but varied scenes of Americana with sound effects (a swamp scene with frogs, a late night diner, and, creepily, an abandoned house). TV channel options were average (expanded basic cable). WIFi an added expense in- room. Of note: No minibar or in-room fridge forcing a trip to the 24-hour lobby shop for soda or juice and the bar or a call to roomservice for a beer. There is a coffee/tea maker with supplies. Doormen were good with basic directions. Concierge offers boarding pass printing and help with other basic needs (didn't test him with dinner reservations, event tickets, etc...). I thought the cost a bit steep for a small city and a hotel with limited services ($195 plus taxes) but didn't check against the Westin, etc... as this was THE convention hotel choice. Finally, breakfast buffet at the restaurant was ok: Choices were good but execution was poorand some food handling seemed almost unsafe (chafing dish eggs/sausage at room temp). Still - waitstaff was pleasant and efficient with coffee, clearing, and check. Overall - a fine stay.

title: “$11 for wifi?!”
text: This Sheraton is nice but really nothing special. It was lacking in a few basic things in the room (like an extra blanket, pillow and there were no robes) you’d expect a “4 star” hotel to have. Also we utilized the wifi in the hotel and they unknowingly charged us $11 to use it. I called downstairs and explained that there was nothing that indicated we would be charged (also I have a data plan on my phone too!). Eventually they begrudgingly took the charge off. The clerk who answered the phone said they would “just this one time,” and acted as if they were doing me a HUGE favor. Next time I want to stay in downtown Seattle I’ll stay at somewhere with better service like the Pan Pacific.

title: “Ok, good location, nothing special”
text: the hotel was ok, clean and felt safe enough at least. pretty good location, just off hollywood blvd. felt safe enought to walk back to at night. short walk to all the action. not much else to say, pretty bare and basic but BIG room compared to everything else we stayed in in USA, but bathroom. only had a couple of nights here but would stay here again.

title: “What more do you need?”
text:
Extremely clean, comfy, with free parking and breakfast. A good value in a pricey city. Yes, it is in an industrial area which has a few bars and not much else you would want in the way of night life.
Tony was a big help as we needed to check out and did not get the shuttle for a couple of hours after check out. He secured our luggage until we returned. The staff, including the maid, was very pleasant and friendly. We highly recommend it for budget travelers who need a clean, nice, but reasonable place to stay. Also got a good snack at the Thai restaurant across the street.

title: “Great for new york”
text:
We have just returned from a week at the Marriott. The hotel is above average and the service is alright. 
The A/C didn't work very well, so it was either always on or off. 
The rooms were OK but smelled musty. 
The bathroom needed some paint.
Great location and good staff. 
A very quite part of town. right next to the 9/11 sight.
Very close to Battery Park. The R, W and 1 subway are a block away.

title: “Good staff, needs attention from management”
text:
The staff at this hotel is excellent. But the systems need attention from management. The internet connection is sooooo sloooooow as well as expensive it wasn't really possible to use it for work (i had to switch to my own mobile broadband which, of course, costs me)
I spent 20 minutes following the directions in the in-room notebook to print a file. When i went downstairs to pick it up, I was told "oh that's outdated - you need to use this different process now" ... The "new" process didn't work either. However, the person at the desk very graciously printed my file for me.
I tried to order something from the menu in the in-room hotel guide and was told they didn't have THAT but they had something else (which arrived luke warm). In the notebook it listed the service charge as $2.50 but when i got the order it said the service charge was $5.00 ... When i asked about it they said the book "must be out of date." AND, they graciously took the charge off my bill. However, the staff said they didn't know what was in the in-room information and that it was probably all now out of date.
The clock in my room had not been changed from daylight savings time and I couldn't figure out how to change it myself so asked if they could do it for me. Never happened.
AND, the soda machine on this floor is broken.

author.location: Washington, District of Columbia, United States

title: “Nice Hotel Bad Neighborhood”
text: The hotel is nice, but be aware that the neighborhood is sketchy, especially along Ellis Street. The rooms are awesome. However, if you are traveling alone, I would not recommend this hotel. If you choose to stay here, remember to ask the hotel receptionist of an alternative route to the city center. There's a shuttle, but remember to reserve it early because if they're full, they won't make another trip out for another hour. Breakfast is provided but without any frills. During my stay, it consists of Ramen noodles, hard-boiled eggs, toast, croissant, waffles, cereal, juice, fruit, ham/turkey slices, milk.

title: “Cute but full of tourists”
text:
Nicely decorated hotel and the cinema is very cute. The location is very convenient for shopping/BART. Nothing wrong wiht breakfast- a decent range of bagels and muffins. I thikn every single guest there was a tourist (in the bad way) and they were a bit loud, moved a bit slowly, had annoying requests at the front desk... 
The area was fine- there were a few hmeless people-but you get that everywhere in SF and I didn't find it any scarier than any where we'd stayed before.

title: “Very Disappointing”
text:
I arranged this stay because of an overnight delay in my return trip from England. I had great expectations, becase I had never had a bad experience in a Best Western. There's a first time for everything. 
My room turned out to be a smoking room, despite my request for non-smoking. The room was unclean. In the morning when I went to the desk to ask for the complimentary shuttle back to the airport, I was told that "You didn't ask for it the night before." I had to take a taxi. 
I was very disappointed in this hotel, and won't be staying there again.

title: “Great location and very hip”
text: This is a very friendly hotel and right in the Lower East side.You can walk to Katz's deli and the not to be missed The Meatball Shop restaurant around the cornwer.It is open till the wee hours and the food is delicious and cheapThe hotel restaurant ia faboulous too.

title: “Great Location!”
text:
Can't beat the location of this Wyndham hotel: close to Eataly, the subway, Tappo pizza, and Madison Square Park. Kudos for the attentive staff, and friendly service.
We traveled with my elderly parents, so requested an accessible room for them, which had a king bed. My parents were unimpressed with the appointed space, so staff kindly relocated us to Room 1404 with double beds. Sadly, none of the beds were that comfortable although piled high with pillows (a choice of soft to firm would be appreciated); many in our party had trouble sleeping. 
While there is a deal for breakfast at the adjoining San Rocco, we found the space dark and cramped with questionable decor for our family of 6; however, a friend and I did enjoy colorful al fresco Negroni cocktails. 
P.S. Don't count on the contracted concierge to provide transportation - we had specifically requested (and prepaid) for a minivan as my Dad has trouble stepping up to a regular van. Sunday morning, 7 AM, a regular van arrived. To their credit, the Wyndham management kindly apologized, escalated the matter to the Apple Commuter owner, and generously offered to compensate, exhibiting the top-notch professional service noted above.

title: “Hyatt La Jolla is a winner”
text:
There were many positives for our two night stay at this property. We were on the Regency floor which is a plus for continental breakfast and I am sure evening snacks even though we did not take advantage (alcohol is at a charge)--it is not the biggest area so it tends to get crowded.
Rooms were quite nice and the bedding and bathroom were pleasant.
All of the staff we dealt with, especially at the front desk were excellent.
Like many Hyatt's, parking comes at a price--$16/day to self park in a connected garage next door or $20 + for valet.
There is a health club next door which is huge and I understand there is a fee to use it.
The pool is nice but they reserve 3 lanes for swimming laps which takes up about 75% of the total space leaving a small amount of 3 foot depths for others to wade in-something for families to be aware of.
If you do have a car, this hotel is a very nice base to travel to San Diego, Torrey Pines, or the beautiful views of La Jolla and the town itself.

title: “Great, new hotel near airport”
text: This is a great hotel! I have stayed here a couple of times now over the last year. It is the only SPG property that has free airprt tranportation at the Jacksnville airort. The hotel is new, so it is very clean. The staff is very friendly and helpful. The rooms are nice and the gym is also very nice with 2 treadmills, 2 bikes, 2 elipticals and some free weights. There is also a small pool that looks nice. The shuttle to and from the airport is very prompt and will also take you to nearby restaurants and stores. There is a huge shopping center across the sreet with multiple restaurants, shopping and a movie theater. I personally suggest you try Seafood Express and More. It is not in the shopping center acrosss the street but only a couple of minutes away and the shuttle will take you for free. It is a great, locally owned seafood restaurant that has wonderfully fresh seafood!

title: “Traditional Marriott experience”
text:
Rooms were clean, front desk service was excellent, bar was upscale with a starbucks above it. Overall a better than average Marriott.
Front desk decor, especially the wall behind the front desk was sub-par. Looked like a 2nd grader had done the construction. This was minor though and didn't detract from the stay.

title: “Nice location, Nice beds, lousy housekeeping”
text:
Just returned from a 7-night stay at this hotel. Our room #302 was a suite with 2 beds, living room with dining area and a kitchen.
As stated by everyone else, it is very close to the Foggy Bottom Metro Stop -- we highly recommend taking the very efficient DC subway and leaving the driving to the the locals! On a quiet mostly residential street. The beds and pillows were really comfortable so sleep was good. walls seem fairly thin but our neighbors tended to go to bed early or were very quiet.
The place itself needs some work. Floors seem to slant, carpeting is old and fairly dirty (hard to tell due to weird carpet pattern). In our room the cabinet doors on the TV stand and armoir in the bedroom were literally falling off. The bathroom was tiny and not very well kept. The kitchen had a new fridge and a stove, oven and microwave and dishwasher but there were hardly any utensils/plates and no bowls or "extras" to make it easy to cook anything if you wanted to. TV Remote controls did not work well, one did not work at all.
When we got to our room, the dishwasher had been run sometime in the week or so before and the water did not drain out and the kitchen smelled. They came to fix it the next day while we were gone but when the dishwasher was run again, the same thing happened. They did get it fixed by the 3rd day of our stay.
Housekeeping was inconsistent. I am sure they came to our room each day because the beds were made and trash emptied but some days that seemed to be all they did. On three different occasions, they took dirty towels but did not leave any clean ones and I had to call and ask for some.
All in all we mostly used our room for breakfast and sleeping as we were gone all day playing tourist. We did rent an in-room movie one night when we were tired.
A few other details:
There is a 7-eleven 1/2 block away, a Safeway nearby in the Watergate complex and a Starbucks at the Foggy Bottom Metro Stop. We mostly ate at Union Station, Downtown and in Chinatown.
We tried to check out the rooftop pool. That area was closed as it is seasonal. Pool is very small but we had hoped to catch a view from up there.
We took Super Shuttle from and to the DCA airport but it would have been very easy to take the subway as it picks up right at the airport. If you are staying more than a few days, the week long subway pass is an easy to use deal -- $32 for 7 days of unlimited use.

title: “Wonderful! Full of little extras!”
text: Everything was done excellently. The staff are friendly and professional. My favourite was the room, with little extras such as extra shelves, accessories, environmental, etc. You can't beat it for the location as well.

title: “Spectacular Service in a beautiful setting”
text: The US Grant is a tremendous hotel. By far the most luxurious downtown option I have stayed in. The US Grant's service rivals any hotel I've stayed in, any where in the world. The rooms were terrific and main areas of the hotel are beautiful. The food at the Grant Grill was spectacular. I can't say enough good things about this place. All of this at a tremendous value for the quality of the stay and the service.

title: “Excellent chain - ideal location but one disappointment”
text:
