Short leisure trip from London to NYC. Decided to stay at Eventi as we have used Kimpton hotels before (great service and one of very few to have a LGBT policy). Very smart city hotel and perfect location for exploring Manhattan. Room was excellent, comfortable and without fault. What I love about Kimpton hotels (as well as the excellent service and zero attitude) are the simple yet thoughtful things, like having a iron/board and an umbrella in your room (sadly it rained for most of the time we were there). The wine hour and morning coffee at reception were also welcomed. 
The one thing that let us down is the bar. This hotel features an uber-modern bar/restaurant rather than a traditional hotel bar and it's not IMHO particularly 'accessible' for the hotels guests. The first evening we arrived, we sat down to relax at the bar and ordered a glass of wine but were told that the seating was reserved after 10pm , so we only had about 30 minutes before we would have to 'move on'. I felt a bit disappointed, particularly as we'd only just arrived from London, being tired, we didn't want to venture out of the hotel but had to retreat to our room instead. Not particularly welcoming and no mention of this was made by reception. On another occasion, we headed to the bar only to find it closed for a private function. On our last day, we had an evening flight back to London so we had to vacate our room at midday. Whilst reception were happy to look after our bags (they weren't able to provide a late check out) we had to walk the streets of Manhattan for a couple of hours, but we kept ourselves entertained. Mid afternoon it was raining heavily so we thought we'd head back to the hotel to have a drink in the bar for a hour or two before heading off to JFK. Problem: the bar doesn't open until 4pm - great! So we had to make use of the FoodParc where we at least managed to get a beer (eventually. Good luck trying to use FoodParc, a very modern but odd concept. we eventually worked out what we were supposed to do * see below *). Then we found a couple of chairs on the third floor to sit on until it was time to go to the airport. 
The good thing about Kimpton is that they serve you well when you want help, otherwise they generally leave you alone. There's no pretentiousness, just quality service however whilst I understand that some people prefer a more utilitarian approach, I wouldn't mind a little more warmth and feeling that my hotel was more than just 'a base'. (note for all Europeans, there aren't many bars in the area so don't expect any kind of cafe culture that we are used to, it kinda makes you feel like you're an alcoholic "where can I get a drink around here?")
PS. FoodParc - to save you looking like a complete idiot (like we did) here's what its about. FoodParc is an eat/drink zone with a few different eateries/kitchens/counters/zones whatever you wanna call them (3Bs, Fornetti, Red Farm Stand, The Press and BeerParc) all with different menus. It's confusing because it's not clear quite what you do or where you order. You'll see banks of computer touch screens but no instructions on what to do. So:
Go up to a touch screen - they have the menus for all the eateries. 
Browse the menus and choose what you want to eat/drink (a bit like shopping online). 
Your order can include items from ANY of the eateries (as I found out after I had ordered! At first it looks like you only have the option to get items from one menu, but if you continue, you will get the opportunity to add items from the other menus)
You swipe your credit card
Computer gives you a printed receipt with an order number
Check TV screens above your head for order progress
When it's ready, go and collect your order from the appropriate 'vendor' 
Take a seat and eat (there's a load of raked seating out of sight at the rear)
(For those of you in the UK, think Argos!)

title: “Rude, incompetent staff made it a horrible experience”
text:
If you like being treated like you are an inconvenience and a nuisance, then you will like this hotel. I bought a Southwest Vacations package and it was fully paid in advance a month before arriving. The desk clerk, a man named Ram, kept saying in broken English that it was not paid for and he needed to charge my credit card. This went back and forth for several minutes and the supervisor (manager?) came out from the back and looked at the screen and talked to Ram and finally Ram admitted it was paid for. Did he apologize? No.
This hotel is divided into two parts on opposite sides of the street. The part across from the main check-in has NO ELEVATORS but three floors. Even the first floor is up a flight of stairs. Since I knew I would have a lot of luggage I called the day before and requested a room in the main part of the hotel and the woman who I spoke to siad that would be fine and I heard her typing it. When Ram assigned me to a room, it was not in the main part, but across the street. I told him about my phone call, and he said there were no rooms in the main part available. When I objected, the same man from the back came out and said "She didn't know. If you spoke to me, I would have told you. You booked a double bed, and all those rooms are across the street" and walked back to his office. I asked Ram what kind of beds were in the main part, and he said "Full." Did that mean "double" or was he ignoring my question? All this was taking so long a line was forming behind me. Then Ram said "Your room is across the street. If you don't like it, you can go somewhere else." I have never been treated so rudely by hotel staff. I would like to have gone somewhere else, but the events I was attending were just a couple of blocks away, so I didn't need a rental car. The events were very popular, so I knew all the hotels in the area would have no available rooms. So I had to stay. While all this was going on, I was looking at the signs in the lobby. One said "If you are suspected of bringing bed bugs into the hotel you will be surrendered to the Health Authorities and fines will be imposed." Another one said, "Breakfast consists of ONE cup of coffee, ONE pastry, and ONE glass of juice. God forbid you get a refill on your coffee - would they surrender you to the police? The next day I noticed a sign in the room saying room cleaning ended at 2pm. So I rushed to get ready and left at 1:30. I saw the maid and asked her if she would do my room. She frowned and said "I thought you didn't want service." I said "I do want service." She said, "Come in late, leave late," and shook her head. Apparently the maids think you need to schedule your life around their schedule, rather than the other way around. Obviously the manager does not train the staff. The room was TINY and the bed was hard as a rock. What a nighmare!

title: “Right in airport”
text: Flight canceled at 10 pm, called hotel from red carpet club and had room waiting for me - asleep by 10:15!

title: “Travel Inn Hotel - great with a pool in the city!”
text: Great with pool, fridge, microwave. Very convenient just 2 blocks to Port authority. Food store close by. Perfect when in transit a few days. We'll definitely go again, if the price is right (which it was now since we booked a couple of months ahead).

title: “Older Hotel, Awesome Staff”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for my first trip to NYC. In the business district, it's within walking distance to some of NY's best sights! Rockerfeller Center, Times Square, 5th Avenue. Being close to all the offices has one huge advantage, amazing food! 
We asked the concierge for food recommendations twice, and were not disappointed either time. Ruby Foo's near Times Square was a great Asian fusion joint (get the dumplings, they're to die for). Excellent atmosphere, good cocktail selection, and just the right amount of atmosphere for dinner (no loud music, but plenty to look at). The next suggestion was Bobby Van's Grill. As soon as we walked in, we knew the steaks would be amazing (everyone was in a business suit. Those men know their steaks!). The service here was above and beyond. Food to die for. Try it out! Oh, and there's a deli across from the backside of the hotel where the locals go, if you have had a NY bagel, get one there.
The hotel itself is older. Some of the wallpaper in the rooms is coming undone, and there are scratches on the walls. BUT, it is clean, well lit, and the beds are comfortable. The staff was friendly, professional, and very helpful. It's safe (they check your room key before letting you in after 11pm). It's in an excellent location. For the price, you absolutely cannot beat it.

title: “Great location for Downtown Denver”
text: Being close to the convention center it is no surprise that the lay out of the hotel has a definite business traveler feel to it. With that said, if I was going to the area for a long weekend with family I would still stay there without hesitation. Easy walking distance to the LoDo area and one block from the 16th street mall and across the street from the convention center. Rooms were roomy and very clean. Reception and staff in general were very service oriented that definitely kicked the experience up a notch. The location also looked like it is easy walking distance to Coor's Field and musuem areas. I'd go back without hesitation

title: “Get proof of your reservation!”
text:
I reserved a standard twin room on September 19th for three nights to begin September 23rd. Gave them my credit card number and received an oral confirmation #114304. Arrived there at 6:30 PM on the 23rd and guess what? No room for me and my wife!
Worse than that, the young aryan behind the counter lied and told me my reservation was for the Baroness across the street. My long distance records show that I have never in my life heard of the Baroness, much less telephoned them.
There seems to be some connection between the Inn at VM and the Baroness which I have not quite figured out, because the young lady at the Baroness was all apology and discounted our room without my even asking. Our stay there was terrible, but that's another story.
My closing advice to you all is that you get the Inn at VM reservation person to email you a confirmation. Apparently giving them your credit card number is not enough. Good luck.

title: “Xmas Xtra Special”
text:
I stayed here at the beginning of December 2004 and after reading some of the reports was very worried before I arrived but the stay was great.
My double double room was exactly as pictured. There was morning coffee available in the foyer every morning.
The reception staff were very friendly and the bellman helpful. Two lightbulbs blew when I was staying and they were changed within minutes of my call to reception.
Clean, comfortable and very convenient. Recommended.

title: “great hotel”
text: overall great stay. great spg platinum upgrade, great service, nice pool and gym.

title: “Amazing”
text: Stayed 6 nights with the muse celebrating our honeymood, had a few problems in the run up with our booking company but the muse were excellent in helping us sorting everything out, we also had a few special requests as it was our honeymoon and the staff couldnt have been more helpfull. The hotel is in the heart of everything and if its not within walking distance there are plenty of subway stations that are. Had a meal in the Nios and it too was lovely. Cant say enough good things about this place, Clean tidy and a great nights sleep all in the heart of times square and more importantly although there were probably loads of couples here on a special occasion they did their best to make us feel special. Will be staying here again if we ever return to NYC.

title: “A Bloody Rip Off”
text:
This was the first hotel we stayed at coming out of San Francisco and we arrived at about 1 am to a deserted downtown San Jose that looked like a ghost town. The evidence of the construction (daytime) occuring at the intersection was quite disturbing as there was nowhere to drive the car, nor to park in front of the hotel. I asked the valet where we park and if we could park ourselves and he looked at me and said, "I park it." Oh well, $10 down the drain as a tip for him doing nothing and another $35 just to park the car in some far away bunker lot that looked unsafe. I wondered how we would unload our luggage with the situation and the lone valet said nothing. I grabbed about 8 suitcases and bags, which was disorganized and sloppy, I probably dropped all my clean socks on the greasy pavement but there was no other way. Finally, after putting all our stuff on some wobbly cart, we entered the hotel. 
The hotel itself was built in the 1920's and it was said that it was remodeled, because in the 70's it had hit rock bottom as a "welfare hotel". The rude clerk at the desk did not express any sympathy or warmth and we took the elevator up to our room. It was a badly decorated room and very cold too. We went to sleep with a bad heating unit that clunked all night long. When I awoke, I took a shower and was nearly burnt because of the changes in the temp and then after touring the building, there were hardly any people there, we decided to eat at the Il Furgonrio restaurant but were disappointed that it had been closed due to the fact that no one was eating there. Where was everyone? The fitness room looked like a Stalag 13 exercise room, located in the basement. Everything was creepy in the building, namely the emptiness and lack of people. We only stayed there one night but it was a complete rip off as there were no extra amenties for the excessive and absurd price of $165!!! plus parking!!! If you are in the area, stay at a Motel 6, because its just the same, a night in the sack.

title: “Decent upclass Motel”
text:
Stayed here two nights in September. Actually, this is a pretty decent place for the money. I would classify this somewhere between a motel and a 3 star holiday inn express. The place itself is located on the main highway, plenty of places nearby to eat, shop, etc. But you do need a car.
The front desk staff are nice and professional. They don't coddle you, but treat you like an adult. The hotel is laid out on two floors with an inner courtyard where there is a pool. It is in a "motel style" layout, as your door opens onto the parking lot (if you're facing the parking lot on the first floor). Pretty standard, no frills place.
The rooms are nice. Yes, the furnishings are kind of dated (despite being renovated in 2006). There is flat-screen TV, but not many hd channels. There is a living area, but no table??!! The bed is decent, but the pillows horrible. The bathroom was tiny, and the tub/shower combo didn't drain properly. The room had a stale odor, and despite turning the a/c on full, it took a few hours to cool the room down. There was a free continental breakfast, but I never visited it.
Regardless, the price was very low. So all in all, a decent stay. If I was in the area again, I would stay.

title: “Beautiful Hotel in Perfect Location”
text: Extremely clean, friendly staff, large rooms, lots of restaurants outside the door, beautiful pool area, centrally located....would definitely stay here again! My only complaint is that parking is pricey.

title: “Pretty Good, pretty expensive”
text: My trip was in march 2007. My first time in NY. It was a little expensive for the rooms that they offered but it was ok if you are just going to be there at night. It´s nearby a metro station and a little walk from Empire State and Midtown. It wasn´t as clean as it could be, but enough! Great views from my window to the Empire State!!!

title: “Wild Oak ranch”
text: We stayed here for a family Vacation. We really enjoyed the place. I thought the rooms were fantastic, we stayed in a two bedroom. The pool was nice, two water slides and the lazy river was really nice as well. There are hammocks around the lazy river to just relax in and there are waiters and waitresses that will bring food/drinks to you poolside. We rented a car and did not limit ourselves to the hotel alone. The kitchen in the hotel room is well equipped and the staff was helpful with finding close grocery stores. There are grills on the property not too far away from the room. We enjoyed exploring San Antonio from this beautiful property with pleanty to do, it far exceeded our expectations.

title: “Small but elegant and very central”
text:
Spent one night, November 26 2011, at this legendary hotel. The room on the 7th floor was small (perhaps not by NYC, especially Empire State area, standards), but extremely clean and contained everything one needed, including a very charming, if a little tiny, bathtub. Both my female friend and I slept quite well that night, hardly hearing any noise whatsoever. The bed wasn't that large, so if you are 6 ft or above, it may be a little uncomfortable. Not much of a view but we didn't expect it in that area.
Staff were friendly and very helpful, but I only remember one name, a gentleman by the name of Terrin, who checked us out very efficiently on Sunday morning. Please forgive me for not remembering the names of the rest of the wonderful staff who went out of their way to assure us of a comfortable stay.
One strange, little funny incidence: the phone was missing in the room. Since we had several cell phones with us, we didn't discover that until we were trying to call to set up a wake up call. We decided we were too tired to run downstairs to ask the staff (it probably would have taken at least 30 minutes for them to bring o phone in and to connect it). We did report it when we checked out in the morning, and the staff assured us that they would look into it.
Sadly, Matilda the great cat was off that evening. A few colossal sighs of regret from us, but it was no one's fault that the iconic cat decided to hide.

title: “For the price, this place could use some work.”
text: I stayed here with a date and we did the Van Gogh package. Overall this was a very good value and we had a nice time. The hotel has very stifling and dry air and you could not open a window. Woke up feeling like I had slept in a sauna.

title: “Nice hotel in the Van Nuys Area”
text: The room I had was very large and accommodating. Everything was clean except for the top of the toilet-- a hair. Internet worked great. Signal for TV was sketchy for about 2 hours one night. While carpets in hallway were showing a little wear, the carpet in the room was nice and fresh, The bed was very comfortable. The breakfast was super--not sure of the cost; it was free as a gold member, Everything you need or want with regard to shopping is within walking distance. Recommened in Van Nuys area.

title: “Nice Hotel in a Great Location”
text: Stayed here for four days while in NYC-paid $208/night and thought for the money the hotel was an excellent value. The rooms I thought for NY standards were large-two queen beds and a sofa bed and plenty of space to move around. My one complaint would be the bathroom area-small sink and mirror outside the bathroom and then a separate room w/shower and toilet-somewhat crowded when everyone was trying to get ready at same time. The hotel had a restaurant-overpriced at least for breakfast and offered free internet use although the service was extremely slow...The entire staff was friendly and helpful and always with a smile. The lobby is small and not much to look at but the entire building was clean and well kept. We had a room on the 26th floor and could see the Hudson riiver in the distance....Would definitely stay here again...within walking distance to Times Square, Rockefeller center, Broadway etc....subway station access across the street and on the corner.

title: “First time at Country Inn and Suites”
text: I travel to San Diego frequently and have an office near this property. I have not been satisfied with other hotels near my office so I tried Country Inn and Suites on Lusk Blvd last week. Wow, what a pleasant surprise. I ahd a very nice spacious room, free wifi, nice bar in which to have a conversation after the work day and a great place to meet colleagues for breakfast in the morning. I dont know what I was expecting from a Country Inn but I was impressed. The staff is first class, the property appears new and looks upscale. This is my new home away from home when I'm in San Diego!

title: “Great Location. Great service”
text: I normally stay at the Gansevoort in the MeatPacking District but decided to try out the new property on Park Avenue as it was closer to a conference I was attending. The rooms are a great size for New York hotels with a nice modern/funky touch. The doormen and front desk staff were always extremely helpful and knowledgeable which was great considering some of the people in our group were first timers in NYC. Oh, and the rooftop bar is really cool. Will definitely be back in the future!

title: “Good deal - great location”
text:
Great location and room was very nice. We had two rooms booked (1157 & 1151) 1157 was much larger and was perfect 1151 was fine but small, I think this is there normal room. This place is a 5 minute walk from Central Park, the 2 deck "red" bus stops here which was a great surprise, and right next door to Carnigie Deli. Walk to Times Square. Parking was $39.00, and the hotel when booked directly on there WEB site $143.00 was cheaper than the Expedia/Hotels etc.
Based on pricing I would stay here on all future visits. Only one mishap was there checkin system went down when we arrived and they had no idea how to check people in, there front desk could use a larger staff - some people waiting 1 hour in line to check in.

title: “Perfect!”
text: We stayed at the Westin for 3 nights Through New Years Eve. I had read all the comments and had some concerns. Well I have to say We had a fantastic stay. The Bellman as we drove up could not have been more helpful or friendly . When we went up to check in we were told it would be an hour befor the room was ready. No problem we had lunch at Shulas it was very good and the room was ready when we returned. A corner room (not requested) on the 29th floor with Panaramic views with windows all the way around the room including the bathroom. We could see the river, times square and the empire states bldg. Also the wonderful Paramount Bldg.The beds were very comfortable and the room clean. Everyone we encountered at the hotel during our stay were very helpful and pleasant. We found the hotel to be a good choice. Keep in mind a smile goes a long way!

title: “Great room, great location”
text:
Fantastic location just a few blocks from times square, penn plaza, etc.
Nice studio room with modern furniture, full kitchen, and comfy bed.
Comp. breakfast buffet was delicious- standard fare, but well done.
Would def stay here again!

title: “Sexiest hotel in NYC”
text:
My fiance and I went to NYC for a weekend trip and stayed at the Night hotel, upon check in this cute girl named Christine at the front desk was so welcoming and professional, they checked in our luggage, carried it up and amazing we got an upgrade to their penthouse suite. The staff was very friendly and helpful. The location of the hotel was perfect, right in Times Square. Also, the black and white decor is extremely NY chic. 
LOVE IT, definitely staying here EVERY time we go back!

title: “what it claims to be, plus great location”
text: I've always wanted to stay here. My husband's business had some events here, which allowed for the perfect oppertunity to visit. We had a beautiful room!! From the other reviews, this must have been one of the redone rooms, because it was wonderful: historical flare with modern conveneices. Although, we were on the 6th floor, and our view was directly onto the roof with the heating units. We overlooked this fact and figured the time in our room we weren't looking outside anyway. For the price though, you'd hope for a better view. The banquet rooms, especailly the Starlight Roof, were gorgeous! There was good service, and I liked that there was a person outside helping to flag down taxis. It was quite cold, and waiting outside was not something we wanted to do that night. It also had a great location for us. It was two blocks from St. Patricks Cathedral, two blocks from Radio City Music Hall, and a short walk to Times Square.

title: “A great nights sleep and eats.”
text: I found absolutely no problems with this hotel. Easy to find, very clean, quiet and friendly and with a free hot breakfast. There was also an extra room if the dining area was full. There were many restaurants and shopping areas at this exit and downtown Indy is about 15-20 minutes. Nice residential area of town with quiet upscale neighborhood.

title: “Bland, hard to get to, nice guest rooms, common areas need help.”
text:
Kind of standard fare for Sheratons, this one is newer.
I had to loop around three times to figure out how to get to this thing, frustrating. Valet parking is STEEP! But then most of Galleria area is that way. The guest room was nice, fairly large but your typical bland Sheraton package. The corridors were nasty with stains and trash all over them, even though the guest room seemed clean, makes you really wonder.
Rates are ridiculous these days in Houston so I guess it was a reasonable value but I wouldn't spend that kind of money personally!

title: “A stunning hotel”
text:
A friend and I spent 3 nights here from 9-12 June. 
It's an excellent hotel with stunning lobby, rooms and great staff. 
If you're an IC ambassador check in is not separated from reception like Amsterdam, Madrid or Paris. That would have been a nice touch.
The concierge were very helpful and managed to sort out changes to my travel arrangements, restaurant bookings and onward delivery of a parcel. 
Jim in the round robin bar was a joy to talk to. 
The location is fantastic - we even manage to see the president cavalcade drive by. 
The only thing wrong, and I say this about many top hotels , are the charges fit wifi. Although the Willard was cheaper than most @ $10.95 a day. I still think its expensive for what many "cheap" hotels provide for free. 
If I come to DC again, I'd be sure to stay at the Willard.

title: “Clean, Comfortable & Caring”
text: We had a job in El Paso on the north side of town and this hotel was the perfect location for us. The hotel is new and very well managed. We needed in our room early and a late checkout as well. The staff were courteous and helpful. The room was large with a kitchenette and a table. The lighting was bright which isn't normal at some hotels so working at the table was possible. The hotel is close to anything you might need - even a theater!

title: “Nice time”
text: We always stay at the double tree when visiting my brother in philly because his college is right in the same area as the hotel. We vistied during easter weekend, it was busy then. When we checked in it was late but the front desk was welcoming and we got our free warm cookies as usual. We had gone up to our room on the 21st floor and it was a nice room. It was one of the rooms they renvoated, there in the process of redoing the rooms not all are done yet. It was a small room but it was nice and clean and have very comfortable but no room for a cot because there was 5 people staying in the room. Which when we made the reservacation they knew 5 people where going to be staying in the room and they had it in the computer that we needed a cot. So we called the front desk and told them, thankfully we were able to move to another room, they had told us they where ajoing rooms but it turned out it wasn't one room was near the elevator and our room was on the other side. The night manager didnt read the map right of the hotel. So we stayed in the room the one night and then the next day after breakfest we moved to another room that was an ajoing room which was nice. We luckly didnt get charged for the two extra rooms because the manager during the day said it was there mistake. Which was nice of them to do. We enjoyed the rest of our stay at the hotel, the staff was great with helping with anything we needed. The restraunt standing o is really good place to eat, there food is good. They also have another restraunt called acadmey cafe which is open for breakfest lunch and dinner but standing o is open till 1am. They also have an indoor pool, jucuzzi, raquetball courts, tanning bed and work out facility. If you want to play raquetball you can ask the front desk to rent rackets and they are free of charge to you. They have so many ameanties to help you with your stay even if u forogot something they have a list of what they can provide for you. This hotel is worth staying at and i will be staying her for time to come. I would come back here again.

title: “For the price, pretty good”
text:
The wildly varying reviews are quite interesting. I suspect it depends on your expectations and how much you paid. I think if I'd paid $219 per night I would be upset as well. However, I paid about $100 per night and was reasonably happy. 
The room was very small with just enough room for the double bed and there was no storage space, but the hanging pole had enough room for my clothes for a few days. The bathroom was also small, but the facilities fine.
In general, the hotel seemed a little shabby and in need of some refurbishment, but this seemed typical of the area and for the price was not a problem (if you're expecting the Hilton, then you should expect Hilton prices). The location of the hotel is great - a few minutes walk to the major downtown shopping area and metro station. It is true that the seedier tenderloin is equally close, but you can avoid that and it seemed very safe despite being run down.
The only real gripe I have is the breakfast. They really need to work on this. The dining area in the basement is cramped and the food is basic. They provide some chopped up fruit and various breads and preserves, with coffee and fruit juice. It is really basic and needs better quality foodstuffs and presentation.
All in all, I'd happily stay there again at a reasonable price.

title: “A room for $400 + per night should not have a rotted bathroom door”
text:
Although I think it's great that the manager, Mr. Schwartz, comes onto TripAdvisor and responds personally to many of the reviews, I'm beginning to think that maybe he is feigning surprise at the condition of the rooms in the hotel... more specifically that he is somehow unaware of the problem that many of the rooms have with rotted bathroom doors. 
My husband and I stayed 3 nights recently at this hotel. It was a short business trip that we pre-extended to spend a weekend in NYC. I was reluctant to stay here because of the mixed reviews on TripAdvisor, but we did not want to have to stay in two different hotels in NYC for a 3 night trip and we were able to get a "special" rate of $395 + per night.
When we got to our room and opened the door I immediately noticed that there was a very large splash mark of a white substance on the full length mirror next to the bathroom. I honestly think it was some type of air freshener that the maid sprayed into the room, but it made me a bit leery. Went into the bathroom and saw the bottom of the bathroom door was very rotted and moldy. I guess I was somewhat prepared for it having read about others on TA having a similar experience. I wouldn't expect to have a rotted bathroom door if I were paying $100/night. When I pulled back the shower curtain and looked into the tub there was a very long, black hair across the bottom of the tub. So needless to say, my overall first impression of the room was not the greatest. I called housekeeping and let them know my issues about the mirror and the tub. Didn't mention the rotted door as that would not be an issue for housekeeping to solve. They really wanted to send someone up right away to clean the bathtub and mirror, but I told them it was OK to just clean them the next day during their regular cleaning rounds. I'm sure that the room wasn't "dirty" per se, it was just the maid being slack and not inspecting the room before she/he left after cleaning. The furnishings in the room looked a bit tired and worn. It's such a bummer to pay $400 + a night when you know that you absolutely could get another hotel room at the same price in NYC where they would pay attention to detail.
There are some pluses to this hotel such as location. Everyone that worked there seemed very pleasant. Although, I kind of got a laugh out of the concierge on Friday night. I called down to ask a quick question. He said, "please hold for a brief moment" and I swear he had me on hold for 4 minutes. I hung up and called again and he said the same thing about holding for a "brief moment". Another 4 minutes goes by. At this point I actually was laughing. I went downstairs to talk to him directly and ask my question. I explained that I was the one who had called twice and that I was confused by his concept of a "brief moment". He told me that he is an optimist. Clearly the concept of under promising and over delivering was completely lost on him. Whatever... don't sweat the small stuff right?
There were a lot of people traveling with their pets on the weekend since this is a pet friendly hotel. I love animals so I had no problem with this. Lots of really cute dogs. If you have a dog allergy be forewarned though.
Breakfast at the restaurant was super expensive. We spent over $100 each day for 2 people. Again, just be forewarned. The service was very good though especially from a server whose name is George I believe. What a wonderful gentleman.
The beds are very comfortable and the hotel is relatively quiet for NYC.

title: “Amazing!!”
text:
My boyfriend and I stayed here for 5 nights for only 116 dollar plus tax.
The room was very very very big with a smal kitchen, an extra room with make up table and a bathroom. Everything was very clean, fresh towels everyday (even bed sheets if you want to), good cleaning crew and very good airconditioning.
Breakfast is included but is not very good (just some muffins, butter, bread, an apple and some coffee or tea), but some people may find this enough.
The location is great (close to george town) and the foggy bottom subway. For this price and this space, the best hotel in Washington DC!

title: “July 2003 visit”
text: Typical small out-door pool. The carpet in our room needed cleaning and the standard room was cramped for 2 adults and 2 kids. Free breakfast was outstanding with many different choices (although a new toaster would be nice). Located in a separate room it was big, but it was packed every morning. A microwave in the lobby area would be nice; the microwave in the breakfast room is unavailable after breakfast. Front desk was very helpful, but housekeeping was disappointing, perhaps it was the language barrier. Convenient parking will be gone if you stay out too late, you will have to use the underground parking. Locate beside Hotel Circle, it was convenient to jump onto the freeway and be on you r way to local attractions quickly.

title: “It was the right place for our family”
text:
We stayed at Pacific Terrace 2 years ago and it was a great memory so we went back this July and stayed 5 nights. We were so thankful that we even got the same exact room we had 2 years ago,,,a King Jr Suite. We are a family of 4 that includes twin 9 year olds.
I felt that the room was clean and well maintained. We loved that we had access to beach toys, chairs and an umbrella. The umbrella was a huge benefit to me as we are all extremely fair skinned and burn easily as a result.
The room had a breakfast bar area with refrigerator and microwave (plus a mini bar which we never used). There was a sofa sleeper that was a little larger than twin bed size which was great for the kids. The room was a great size and arrangement for us where we could have access to our own snacks and make a lunch or dinner for the times we wanted to save a little money,,,or too tired to go out. The "kitchen" area was stocked with plates, glasses and utensils. It was on the first floor with a patio that opened out to the pool area. It is the only room I've stayed in that had enough trash cans!
I thought the hotel was fairly quiet. We are not picky about things like that. My kids are usually the ones making the noise. There was a workout room that I meant to visit but never did and also a computer available. There are even books available to read which was great for me because I forgot to bring one.
The hotel is right off the beach. It is exactly what my daughters loved,,,,alternating between the pool and the beach. It was so easy for us with it being on the first floor. Access to the hotel and pool is secure. We always felt safe and it was not over-run with people at the pool or the breakfast buffet.
Surf lessons are offered up and down the beach. The boardwalk was great for exercise. We meant to rent bikes but never got around to it. 
It was a great and lazy vacation,,,,just what we were looking for. We didn't need the big resorts with the fancy pools. My daughters (age 9) were perfectly happy with the pool and beach. We met another family that had been coming there for 25 years and staying in the same room. Everyone we met was really nice. I feel like they kept up the clientele so we were never concerned with the other guests. Everyone was quiet and respectful of privacy.
The breakfast buffet was simple but just what we wanted. There was a great breakfast place down the beach a short walk,,,,Konos,,,the portions were huge. Yes, hotel parking is $20 per day,,,as it is for most nice hotels on the beach. 
There was a lot of kelp on the beach and I did read up on that situation about the kelp washing ashore and that it is best for the environment for it to be left there. It was interesting and I recommend reading up on the subject. It certainly didn't slow us down or impact us one way or the other.
The staff was friendly and helpful. We all pledged that we want to repeat it again next year,,,exactly the same as this trip.

title: “Good value, comfortable, fun pool”
text:
Stayed a Friday and Saturday night in January. Room was spacious, especially by NYC standards, and the bathroom & shower were enormous.
Bed was on a slightly raised platform, plenty of storage space beneath. The room had an iPod dock, and there is free WiFi throughout the hotel.
The pool (located just off lobby - photo attached) is a terrific feature, nicely heated in January, open 24 hours, with the swim-up bar open at 5pm. Free breakfast the next morning - the food is fine but the room is rather small; you may have to wait for a table.
Convenient location on a side street off Times Square. I prefer this to some hotels located directly on the square, where you get swept along by the flow of the tourist crowd as soon as you step out the front door.
Room Mate is a chain and I was on their mailing list after a previous stay in another city - email promotional rate of 150/night (177 w/taxes) was a great value.

title: “Horrible!!!Is too nice of a word to use...”
text: The first thing I notices was the hotel was not secure looking. The office is far from the property so if something happens and you scream for help you are on your own. The first room smelled like an old rug that someone let their cats & dogs spray on contstantly. The receptionist apologized & told me they were undergoing construction. I did not see a sign of this whatsoever. He gave me a second room which looked like a crime scence with a bloody hand print on the door and the door had been kicked in. The room had signs of mold, dirt, it was just plain ol nasty. I am a hardcore traveler & when I travel outside the country I like to live like the natives so I don't have to be in the lap of luxury. After I finished having my anxiety attack, I called a cab and got away as soon as possible. This should be converted to a prison or detention center of some sort. This is the worst hotel I have ever seen in my life. It gave true meaning to hole in the wall.

title: “Hidden Treasure”
text: I had to be in NY for a big conference and picked this out from earlier reviews, although I was puzzled why the last one was 2005. However, I suspect that Tripadvisor reviewers have been keeping quiet about this hotel in order not to swamp it with other customers.The Blakely is quite small - 100 rooms or so - with a limited lobby and range of services, but this means all your cash goes where you can feel it. Large rooms by NY standards, very comfortable beds, well-provided bathrooms and a very friendly and efficient staff team. Even the maids spoke reasonable English! The location is brilliant - Midtown and convenient for Times Square and Fifth Avenue, with good subway connections at each end of the street. 55th is not a busy through street, though so relatively little nighttime noise from traffic, etc. If I tried hard, I might complain about the noisy airconditioner and the jet of freezing air that it spewed out on the auto setting - but I have stayed in places that were far worse in this respect.

title: “Not a 5* Hotel !!!”
text:
As a treat I booked myself and my daughter into the walfdorf for our first trip to NY.
The room was very tired, all discoloured paintwork and everything was old.
The exterior windows were filthy you could hardly see out and I injured my back trying to open them they were so stiff. I got charged $17 for a miniature whiskey from the minibar and $59 for coffee and toast from room service. I complained and asked the manager what planet he was on, and he took it off the bill. Radio didn't work. TV remote didn't work. Bedside telephone didn't work. A complete rip-off, living off past glories. There's a lot better places to stay for the same money.

title: “Nice hotel in uptown”
text:
We were there for our family vacation this year and really loved it. Everyone there was really nice and helpful. The lobby was being renovated when were there but it looked like they were almost done. It didn't cause us any problems. 
The breakfast was great and they rotated the hot offerings daily so there was variety each day we were there. The only complaint here was the breakfast servers had gospel music blaring out of their kitchen every day we were there. I'm fine with them having their music playing but they could have toned it down so maybe only they could hear it while they are in the kitchen.
The rooms were nice but seemed a little small. That is not unusual for a downtown hotel as space seems to be at a premium. We were close to an elevator but didn't hear it at night. I usually put the fan on the A/C unit so it runs all the time. This always helps to drown out noises. I did notice that I was able to hear the water running from rooms around us a pretty good bit but it wasn't anything that kept me awake.
I wasn't aware that they had a shuttle that would take you around a 3 mile radius. We took advantage of it one time for dinner and it was a nice touch.
One last note. My son left his iPod nano and earbuds somewhere in the room. He realized he didn't have it after we were about halfway home. We called the hotel and they checked with housekeeping but it hadn't turned up. After we got home and unpacked, it still didn't turn up so we wrote it off as having been caught up in the bedding and probably washed or something like that. The next day, I got a call from the hotel that it had turned up. They offered to mail it to us but my brother lives there so he went by and picked it up.

title: “Beware!”
text: This hotel allows dogs that bark so loud that you will NOT get sleep at night! I was thoroughly pissed that for 2 nights I couldn't sleep. The general manager FINALLY showed up when I went out into the hall screaming that the freaking dog shut up. Ridiculous that they would allow this to go beyond the first complaint. My room was just big enoug for me to turn around in. The shower floor was so dirty that even bleach didn't clean it - be sure to have your shower shoes. Most of the staff was friendly enough though, except for the jerk that checked me out. I called (from my room phone) to have my bill ready at about 3:30 am and the clown at the desk told me he didn't print it because he had to verify that I was who I said I was. WHAT?!?!?!? I CALLED FROM THE ROOM'S PHONE!!!! Other staff I encountered were very friendly.

title: “Great price, rude staff”
text: We booked on Priceline, and felt like the front desk staff had an attitude about it. They were the only rude people we encountered during our visit to NYC. On the other hand, the valet staff was very nice. I think this is the first time in my life I've ever been treated the way the front desk treated our party. But...we weren't in the hotel long, so we didn't let it bother us. The location was very convenient, short walk to Grand Central or Times Square, and the neighborhood was safe and comfortable. Room was small, but bathroom was roomy. Bed was comfy, nice and quiet. We seemed to be the only American's on the property, the other guests were Italian and friendly. Nice place to crash after a long day of sightseeing, and with priceline, the price was great!

title: “Met all expectations & then some.”
text:
Stayed 5 nights in this stylish hotel just off Union Sq. Service and facilities were mostly excellent from the moment we pulled up at the curb until the morning we left. We got the "stay & park" package so we could not worry about the car. Staff were consistently friendly and helpful. I mentioned to the doorman that the bed was a little soft for me and that night found that they had put a panel under the mattress to firm it up - without being asked. We took full advantage of the morning room with coffee and newspapers (some juice too would have been appreciated).
The restaurant (French bistro) and bar (jazz at night) were both comfortable and served excellent and varied food.
Only desire would be for queen beds instead of doubles - but we made do.
Not a cheap place (but what is in San Fran) but it was well worth it.

title: “Okay, nothing special, wouldn't recommend”
text:
We arrived on Thursday night around 8. We were upgraded to a room on the 44th floor so we had a great view. As we went to our room, I noticed a room service tray on the floor a few doors down from our room. I thinking, oh, hasn't been picked up yet, no big deal. No complaints about our room and we were excited to see a small refrigerator available for our use. The bathroom was a great size. However there were no handtowels and the bathtub didn't drain well, filling up with water when we showered. Friday morning I informed the front desk of the drainage problem and it was taken care of right away. Because the bathtub problem was resolved so quicky, I was surprised that the room service tray from Thursday night was still in the hall. We left the hotel about 9, returning at 5, Friday afternoon and the tray was still there. Saturday morning around 9, I told the front desk about the tray. It is hard to believe that housekeeping hadn't picked it up yet. We stopped by the hotel about 3 and the tray was still there! At this point, I am making a mission out of getting the tray removed. Who wants to look at dirty dishes as they walk to their room? I called Service Express and told them about the tray. When we returned to our room about 7 the tray had been moved from the hall way to the table next to the elevator. I don't know if a guest moved it or if housekeeping did. At this point, I took the tray with its dirty dishes and half full pitcher of tea, down 44 floors to the front desk. I don't know what the issue is with housekeeping. There must be some kind of problem if a tray is left in a hallway from Thursday to Saturday night. Who knows how long it had been there before we checked in? If a tray can't be picked up, wonder how much cleaning really goes on in the rooms?
If you want a hotel near Times Square, then this is the place for you. Personally, I would not stay in this area again. It is way too crowded.

title: “Love this place”
text: Sometimes you can get a great rate, in part because it's not in the center of the usual business/tourist action around Embaradero, Union Square and the wharf. On the other hand, it's closer than the expensive hotels to the SF zoo and Golden Gate Park and the Haight. The rooms are very nice, the underground parking is $2/hr and $16 for 24 hours (but no in/out, not that it mattered to us, and valet is $40). If you don't have a car, it's about a $7 cab ride down to the BART. Restaurant's a bit overpriced ($3 coffee to go), but with the room deal, it's a small price to pay. Nice spa around the corner. Beds very comfortable, accommodating front desk, attentive management. My second stay, and I'll go back. The one thing that was a nuisance was the fitness center, which had only one treadmill and one bike -- it renders the morning schedule uncertain if you have to wait for a machine.

title: “Great hotel!!!! Clean, very nice staff, reasonable rates.”
text: My husband and I were in town for a trade show at the Greater Columbus Convention Center. This hotel was only a few minutes away and saved us a lot of money. We stayed for 2 nights in the standard king room and have no complaints. The rooms were nicely decorated and clean. The continental breakfast was good (eggs, sausage, waffles, fruit, cereal, juice, coffee, tea, donuts, etc). We did not use the pool or hot tub but they looked clean. The staff was very nice and helpful. We will definitely stay here again the next time we are in town.

title: “What a pleasant suprise!”
text: I usually stay at far more expensive hotels figuring you get what you pay for. Recently I attended a seminar in Leander, Texas and found there weren't any of my usual hotels in the area. I took a chance and booked at La Quinta Inn which was very close to seminar. WOW...what a surprise! The location was terrific, the rooms immaculately clean, the staff were all super helpful and friendly, and they even included a nice breakfast each morning! I would definitely return to this hotel, and I will look for La Quinta Inns now when I travel. It takes a lot to impress me, but this hotel truly went above and beyond my expectations!

title: “Wonderful stay at the UN Plaza”
text:
We stayed on the 29th floor and has a fantastic view of Manhattan (Chrysler building v nearby, lovely view of the Empire state etc) and the East River / Queens etc. Friendly staff, lovely breakfasts and clean, comfortable rooms with a huge bed! We booked via hotels.com and chose the option with breakfast, however we weren't told on arrival that we needed a voucher for breakfast every morning, but this was sorted out for us fairly promptly. We were close enough to everything without being right on Times square (which was a bit of a mad house to be honest! We were glad to be away from all that). 
I searched for ages trying to find the 'right' hotel for us - I'm happy to say that we were very pleased with this hotel. We're in our late 20s and it was just right for us, though some may feel the hotel is a little bit 'corporate' for their tastes and may want something with more character. But this is NYC and we wanted the whole sky scraper, fab room thing so it was perfect for us.

title: “Nickel and Dimed”
text: Reasonably priced hotel close to LAX. Generally clean and well appointed although there were some ominous yellow stains on the base of the toilet which were still there when I checked out 3 days later. What really wound me up was the outrageous overcharging for basic services I would expect to be included as standard. $12.95 per day for in room internet? $1.50 for a 5 second local call? No breakfast, not even continental? $4 delivery charge for the already overpriced room service? What a total rip off. To add insult to injury, in addition to the compulsory 18% gratuity (in the small print) added to my room service bill, the guy who delivered it went out of his way to point out how I could add a tip when signing the bill! I asked if the 18% had already been added which he confirmed and again pointed out where an additional tip could be added. This intimidating bahaviour is unacceptable and I'm sure some people would feel embarrassed into tipping again. On the face of it the hotel is reasonably priced but the shameless nickel and diming would deter me from recommending it or staying there again.

title: “Terrific Large Room!”
text: I stayed at this hotel with my wife, mother-in-law, and two children - ages 1 & 3. The rooms have been renovated within the last year, and ours was fantastic!...very large for a New York hotel. All of the furnishings and surfaces seemed practically new. The beds were great, and the fold-out sofa bed was even okay. It's the perfect size for a family of 4 or more. The bedroom is a separate room that can be closed off from the rest of the room, and the best part is the bathroom - which had a large double sink, and 2 doors - one connected to the bedroom, and one connected to the living room. Plus there is a 3rd sink in the wetbar! It's a great setup! The staff and service was great. The business center still needs updating. The location is great for tourist activities - there's a subway access point almost directly outside the front door. The TKTS booth is directly across the street. My only complaint about the location is that it's on a very crowded corner in Times Square. So coming and going often involves navigating through a dense crowd of people. If you need a large room in New York, this is a great choice!

title: “The perfect hotel to explore downtown!! We loved it!!”
text: The Omni Parker House is in the most perfect location! Only about a block from the train station, which conveniently you can get to from the aiirport. And it's within walking distance of the wharf shops/restaurant area, tons of historic buildings and only a couple of blocks from many of the trolley stops. The hotel is one of the oldest in the country and they say it's haunted! The room was small, but very practical and had everything we needed. The beds were SO comfotable and the concierge desk was wonderful! We will definitely go back to Boston and will choose the Omni Parker House!

title: “Infested!!”
text: Not to mention the management quoted a price and charged us double!! Yes, I mean infested! The bed we chose to put our children in turns out was infested with bedbugs. They feasted on our little ones all night! While on the road we called ahead for the cost ans was told we would receive the "managers special". When I reviewed my bank statement I noticed no "managers special" as quoted. This is the Quality Inn on Sycamore. Look for the collapsing gutters and falling roof tile. Stay away!

title: “Great Hotel If You Get Food Poisoning”
text:
The Omni San Francisco is the best hotel to recover in if you ever catch food poisoning! Let me explain, the Omni definitely didn't give me food poisoning, a grocery store hot bar in San Fran did. By the time I checked into the Omni, I was feeling the full effects of nausea and stabbing stomach pains. The wonderful woman who checked us in pretended that I was fine even though I'm sure she could see the pain etched across my face.
Even through the stabbing haze and the chills, I was able to appreciate one of the most comfortable beds I had ever slept in as far as hotel beds. The appropriate number of covers/duvets cradled me to sleep and more than enough luxurious fluffy pillows to lulled me to sleep. Throughout the night, I was awakened several times from knife like pains in my abdomen from the poisoning and was more annoyed at not being able to lay in that bed and sleep than the actual pain itself.
The room was very quiet even though we had checked in during the Chinese New Year celebration. The hotel was very busy with celebration participants checking in who were still feeling the effects of a lively celebration that was still happening just a few blocks away. Of course you get some sound, but it was more of a sporadic far away conversation than a blaring and lively debate right outside of your door. I also attribute the levels to the fact that a celebration was happening. 
I didn't get a chance to venture out into San Fran as I was recovering, however, the room was clean, comfortable and an oasis away from home. I didn’t get to see much of the hotel, but when I was feeling better, I did make it a point to order room service (which I got free as part of my hotel deal). The room service was fast (special note since the hotel was so full that day), the food was pleasant enough and the staff was very friendly and professional.
I would definitely stay here again!

title: “3.5 stars on Priceline-zero stars from me.”
text:
No parking, no parking, no parking-5 story parking structure is CLOSED, and you have to walk nearly 2 blocks down Sepulveda, past a dark, empty, abandoned office complex from the one parking lot that's closest (or you have to valet at $20 a day plus tips plus wait time). 
Don't accept a 3.5 star hotel from Priceline at LAX. This is it, and you don't want to be here.

title: “Awesome motel......even better staff!!!”
text: We stayed here back in November and couldn't have wished for a better base to our holiday. The welcome and check in was quick and easy and we were helped to our room with our bags. Room was immaculate and had everything's we needed. We asked to borrow the lap top hair dryer and mobile and nothing was a problem at all. Breakfast was brill....thank you hector for our apple and cherry pies every morning....perfect with the coffee and the read of the paper. The staff were really knowledgeable and really friendly, advising of places to go see, and paces to eat. On check out we were weighed and added to the book.....and said a goodbye, hopefully see you soon cash permitting. Awesome value for money, was like being looked after by family .....will return...thanks sooooo much.

title: “Good Location, Clean Hotel”
text: We stayed at Paramount for 1 night during a 6 day, 7 night trip to the Pacific Northwest. The hotel was very clean, the beds were comfortable. The hotel is located less than 2 blocks from the Light Rail Westlake stop (which was very convenient when we went to the airport the next day) and the same distance from Westlake monorail stop (to the Space Needle). The walk to Pike Place Market is about 10 minutes and is a straight shot down Pine Street.

title: “Very Nice NYC Midtown Hotel”
text: This was a pleasant surprise just East off of 6th Avenue on 35th Street. It is a clean, well kept up hotel for a personal visit with very good breakfast buffet choices. It is not for a spa or business meetings, but for a very good place to stay with nice staff attitudes that is $325 all in including NYC taxes a night vs. $450-$600 for the high end hotels, this is a good choice. We have relatives in the city whom we visit often, and we intend to return to this hotel. One can easily walk from Penn Station if you fly into Newark or JFK and take the train to Penn Station. Glad we found it.

title: “The Bloom is off this Rose - Sad to Say, I wish it were like the First Year”
text: This hotel is two years old and slipping. It is expensive with few discounts available. The hotel is busy with college crews that party all weekend nights and wake everyone up at 2 to 4 am on Friday and Sat. Nights. I had two bad nights of sleep. They do not make an attempt to wall off the party groups from the rest of the guests so everyone will suffer. The bed was uncomfortable. The mattresses are very soft, and cave in the center, most likely because of use and age. The bed linens are thin and rough. The pillows are small and uncomfortable. There is never an upgrade for Sr. Members of the Holiday Inn frequent guest stay program. However, you most likely would decline a one bedroom "suite", since the hotel has all one and two bedroom "suites" outfitted only with double beds. Only the studio "suites" have one small queen bed. There is no option for a king size bed here. I think that there is too much furniture in each room leaving no room for guest luggage. The breakfasts are overrun with hung over college kids on weekends and mis behaving rug rats during the week. The is too little room in the breakfast area for everyone to sit. The food is the standard Holiday Inn carbs and pre-cooked processed egg product, or for the afternoon, think Sams club frozen dinner carbs. The staff is changing, and new staff are clueless about the area. Fyi, the adress is RESEARCH BLVD. not the freeway, as you will not find a GPS or map with the location listed as written on all the hotel documents and web listings. This is a Franchise owned location. The Holiday Inn Mgmt. Group does a Very Bad job of requiring Owners to follow all requirements! When was the last time they pulled the name off a location, no matter how bad the facility or service? HELLO SR. MGMT. Are you listening? This may not the worst location, but not like it used to be and not improving as they are still busy since most of the other hotels in the area are Horrible.

title: “Much Better Than Expected Based On Reviews”
text:
I must admit I was more than a little nervous about checking into this hotel after reading some of the reviews on this site. But, my co-worker had made the arrangements and I had little choice but to go along.
I expected to find an old hotel with a great lobby that hid horror stories in the rooms. This simply was not the case. What I found was a very solid four-star property that was well maintained, clean and more than acceptable.
True the rooms have older furniture and lack flat screen televisions. True the plumbing fixtures are probably at least 30 years old. However the rooms and bathrooms were meticulously clean and nearly spotless.
Overall, I have no qualms about recommending this hotel to business travelers like myself.
When I return to El Paso, I will be returning to this property.

title: “Can't Believe it is a Starwood”
text:
Great location, helpful staff, but can't believe it is a Starwood. Is the hotel about to be upgraded?
Rooms were old. A/C did not work. I had them change my room three time. Maintenance guy hit the A/C with a wrench. I finally switch hotels to ALoft at 10pm at night.

title: “Older Hotel doing the job”
text:
The Embassy Suites Center City is an older "circular" hotel that was the style in the 70s. It is confusing getting off the elevators to orient yourself, but since there was only about 12 suites per floor, it wasn't a problem.
I was travelling for business, but brought the family along to tour Philly while I was in meetings. They enjoyed the location's close proximity to the Franklin Institute and the Art Museum, and the walk to Independence Mall was not too bad. 
Our view from the 19th floor balcony could see the Franklin Institute and the Art Museum. There are safety locks on the sliding doors. There is no furniture on the balcony.
The meeting rooms are on the top floor,(28th), with a great view of the city. There are no large rooms for meeting, though, due to the circular shape of the building and the elevators in the center. 
The bed in the bedroom was comfortable, double sheeted and plenty of pillows. The sofa bed in the living room was uncomfortable, my daughter had me lay on it to feel all the springs. Having just been in Disney 2 weeks prior with their wonderful sofa-beds, this was really bad.
Bathroom was well stocked with towels. Shower had good pressure. All standard supplies were there and replenished daily.
There was no supplies in the kitchen area if you wanted to use the microwave or fridge for anything, there was a sign to call if you needed any kitchen supplies, but we did not. There was water in the fridge. WIth a note that if you took it, it would be charged to your room.
The staff was wonderfully nice - (something you don't always expect in Philadelphia). The woman who checked me in the first day always remembered to ask me how the family was enjoying their sightseeing and teasing me about attending meetings.
I did not have any problems with service, quality, or seating for the breakfast or the evening reception. It seemed that they varied the snacks each night.
The TGI Fridays attached to the hotel allows you to charge to the room - which can be easier on the expense account. The prices were fair TGI Fridays prices, they did not seem inflated for being in center city or being in a hotel. There was a limited selection of the TGI Fridays menu for room service. Those prices were inflated.
Parking was by valet only, and it was $42 per day. Work that into the budget!

title: “Pleased”
text: When you first approach the hotel, you wonder if you made the right decision. After checking in and getting to our room (jr suite) we knew we had chosen correctly. The room was clean and confortable. The breakfast is light as advertised - bagels, muffins, doughnuts, fruit, juices. The only problems we had were: getting a cab, but we walked a block and usually could secure one fairly quick and maintenance turning our air off during the day. If travelling to NYC again, I would definitely keep this one at the top of our list. Anthony, the concierge/door man was most helpful too!

title: “#1 ranking for a reason”
text: Just spent 11 nights with my 2 daughters at the Casablanca. Great location, rooms were spotlessly clean each day, and complimentary breakfast together with wine and cheese each evening were a great addition. The staff were helpful and efficient, with any request taken care of with a minimum of fuss. Wouldn't bother trying anywhere else, this is the place to stay.

title: “Id rather have gonorrhea than stay here again”
text: Dirty and always smelled like pot. Employee was rude and dishonest.

title: “wonderful hotel, great location, excellent service”
text: We were very pleasantly surprised by just how good this hotel is. Close to Seattle Center, within walking distance of the monorail, good breakfasts, very accomodating staff and the most comfortable beds we have enjoyed in any hotel. The only drawback is paying $15 per day for parking. but in seattle, parking costs a lot of money. we will definitely be back in Seattle and when we do return, this is where we are staying.

title: “Good gym, bad food service.”
text: Stayed here for a conference. Location was good if you need to be close to convention center. The gym was excellent -- new machines in a clean, bright room -- I recommend that highly. However, the restaurant offered only generic food in a generic setting, and the service was slow. Also, I tried to get room service on a Sunday night and there was an hour and a half wait --I don't use room service that often, so perhaps that's normal. The lounge/bar was not a good place to hang out/unwind after a long day, and the lobby did not offer much seating, at least if it did, I could not find it. The room was decent and clean. The parking garage was very expensive, but there's probably not much one can do about that.

title: “Friendly staff, good value”
text:
I've stayed at this hotel on several occasions and have found it to be an affordable option with a convenient location to Hollywood. In fact, you're just a 2-minute walk from the Hollywood & Highland/Kodak Theater complex on Hollywood Blvd.
The beds here are comfortable and the rooms are large, especially for the price you're paying. They have a computer in the lobby for guests to use at no additional charge, free parking on the north side of the building, and they serve muffins and croissants with juice in the morning which is also complementary.
The front desk staff are very friendly and aim to please. The building is somewhat older but is nicely maintained and very clean. I would definitely recommend this hotel, particularly if you plan to see and do things in the Hollywood area.

title: “Decent Hotel, good value”
text: We stayted at the Serrano for 3 nights around Christmas. The hotel is old/a bit dated, but the rooms were nice and clean. The staff was friendly for the most part. We used their valet parking option for $30/night, and they took good care of our car. Overall, good location, decent hotel.

title: “Great Location, Very Affordable!”
text:
I took my husband to NYC for four days as a grad school gift. We stayed in early May (great time to go, weather is perfect) and we stayed at the Wellington at the suggestion of a close friend who has stayed there many times before. It was a great suggestion!
The hotel has a GREAT location! You are just six blocks from Rockefeller Plaza, three-four blocks from Times Square and the Theater district, and just three blocks from Central Park. The location could not have been better. There are two subway stations to access - one outside the hotel on the corner and one two blocks down - so which ever way you need to go, it's easy.
Service was good - quick check in (and it was busy when we arrived), room was small but clean, and the hotel was quiet (we were on the 16th floor). The concierge was VERY knowledgeable about directions and how to get to different places. He even gave us some suggestions for places to eat.
Great restaurants right near by - Ben 'Ash (a great Jewish deli) is across the street and Pick-a-Bagel is a block down and has great bagels and breakfast/lunch.
I would stay here again.

title: “Great hotel”
text: I've stayed at Hotel Vertigo for a weekend in San Francisco with my girlfriend. As soon as I got there I've got upgraded to a better room than the one reserved, great. The room was big, clean, well furnished and cozy. Bathroom was a bit small but still ok. For what I paid I believe it couldn't be a better stay.

title: “Customer Service works so hard to make your stay a great one!”
text: Its tough to be a big hotel in NYC - people from all over, different languages, different needs. Doubletree Metropolitan staff worked so hard to make our stay a great one (Oct 7-10). They have a customercare phone line that takes care of your every need. We had a few issues with our room, but not only were they resolved, the Manager (Matthew) totally took care of us and made me and my 2 sons feel like we were the only guests there. They took care of last minute requests and did so in a professional and helpful way. Kudos to the whole staff (and I mean housekeeping, concierges, desk staff and manager Matthew)! Would definitely recommend!

title: “Quiet..Quiet..Quiet”
text: I like this hotel because of it's location right off the I-10 and ample paved truck parking beside the hotel. I am a long haul driver and appreciate the clean quiet rooms and very helpful staff. There are also 3 restaurants within feet of the front door so it is very convienant to find food without having to get into my truck and drive around looking for something to eat.

title: “Top of the line all the way!”
text: We have been to Philly many times and stayed at other hotels -- the Alexander Inn, the Doubletree, etc. Those places are fine, but we wanted something different so we booked the Sofitel. It was top of the line all the way. Check-in was fast and smooth, the room was immaculate, no hidden charges or hassles at check-out. The valet parking is a little steep for one night ($41). We printed a coupon for a Central Parking System garage that's literally half a block from the Sofitel (1616 Sansom St.) and it was $28 a day for self-park. You can't beat the location of this hotel -- right in the middle of Chestnut & Walnut shopping, right by Shops at Liberty Place, Rittenhouse Square. I'd stay here again in a minute, without hesitation.

title: “Nice for the price”
text: Our family of four stayed at this hotel in March. As most of the other reviewers have said, the outside is new and the inside is dated. We booked a one bedroom suite. The bedroom was roomy but pillows were lacking. We requested and were given a rollaway bed which made the sleeping arrangements simple. My one complaint is that the website states that there is a light evening meal provided. This consisted of a small basket of crackers, a dish of salsa, some cheese cubes and a dish of fruit (this was for the entire hotel, not one person.) When I asked, the desk clerk stated that the website was misleading. When I booked, I planned on feeding the family a big lunch and enjoying their light dinner. No such luck. I ended up having to buy dinner for four each night as well. The breakfast was abundant although they did run out of items quickly and did not refill the trays. The location was good, there is a coffee house across the street and several restaurants within walking distance.

title: “OK if you don't expect much”
text:
Location of this hotel is the best thing about it - it is located on Wilshire blvd, the main street in LA, a rather safe location. Bus stop across the street, as well as metro station. When we asked the taxi driver that drove us to the hotel is this place safe, he said: This street good, one street up and down not good (it's good to know):-) 
Lobby of the hotel is big and nice (Starbucks coffee) but everything else is desperate for renovation. Carpet looks dirty. Rooms don't look clean at all, everything is worn out and old, especially the blankets. Internet is free of charge but very slow!
Good for one or two nights if you can't afford more and if not very picky.

title: “2nd time is a charm :)”
text:
I have to admit that my 1st experience with the W Hollywood was less than steller , but in their defense it was in the 1st few days of opening and as a club venue property i am sure it is easy to have things go haywire at the beginning....after voicing my frustration to a degree i spoke to Jim the GM at depth about my concerns and thoughts...I was suprised at how open minded he was about the criticism and his eagerness to change my views on the property and staff.
 I did revisit the property under my fiancee's name and SPG acct so that we wouldnt get any special consideration due to speaking with Jim....happy to say that we had a great time...were given a great upgraded room (my Fiancee is also a platinum SPG so upgrade was available)...staff was very friendly and room service was quik "and' good....now remember this is a Niteclub venue as well...and you should know that when booking your resv...the hotel tries its best to accomodate its guests in regards to the venue and the pool but as in LV, the venue also has a greater degree of control on access etc so make nice to the venue mgrs via the hotel staff or the WW staff...
 Pool is a bit small but has a goood vibe and yes lots n lots of beautiful people....even some that were never invited to the party,,lol
yes the curb and valet staff do need some work and some lessons on manners but remember most of them its their first job and with a property like the W they probably wont last long or wil be trained appropriately as time goes on...remember staff reflects mgmt and the Mgmt there definately wants to put its best foot forward so suffice to say that nothing is perfect but sometiems a willingness to be perfect is just as good...
i will definately recommend W Hollywood to my friends....my only regret is that i didnt get to meet Jim McPartlin (GM) sooner as he is a great guy who has had to practically re learn his job to deal with all of the new age way of running a Niteclub Venue Hotel and i must say he has done a wonderful job...The good thing is that he will be going to the W NYC soon so since we are there often i am sure that we will still be able to enjoy another venue run by a Top Notch W Veteran such as Jim....
Thx Guys and see you again soon...

title: “NOT A 3 STAR”
text:
My husband and I have stayed at the Residence Inn before, several years ago and we couldn't have been more satisfied. This past Christmas we spent a week there and was very disappointed. We were there three days and on Sat.(Christmas Eve day) the plumbing in
the bathroom was completely plugged. I went to the frontdesk and was told that it would be two hours beforeanyone could check it. They offered another room across the hall or in another building. At 6:30AM we were moving our things to another building. A staff
member told us that it wasn't the first time they have had problems. Also on Christmas Day we were given a sack on the door with extra coffee, a set of towels and soap since the manager give the staff the day off. We missed the notice due to the move. I also
noticed a desk clerk sleeping at 7AM and a staff member was feeding his family at the evening reception. I notified Marriott and the hotel manager e-mailed to say she was sorry for our displeasure in our stay. I told her we would not be staying there again. The place needs to definately improve in upkeep and maintenance.

title: “Excellent Hotel and Location”
text:
Stayed at the hotel with my partner for 4 nights in Feb. Our room was perfect modern tv and two double beds. The rooms was small but no problem at all. As it was just me and partner we didnt mind however a family of 4 may find it to small as there wudnt be alot room to get ready. The beds were very comfy! breakfast was great we also had a voucher for money off! The girls at the desk (to book shows etc) were fab, they helped us out on directions all the time. The cafe next door to the hotel was good open everday, as this is where we got our tea from in the mornings,also reasonably priced. The pizza place next door was also another good place to stop for a slice, very friendly. The hotel was in the best location, times square. Literally less than a min walk in to the heart of times square, so plenty to do in the surrounding area. 
Would definatly go back to this hotel in the future and would recommend. Gym Facility brilliant

title: “Very friendly hotel staff & a great place to stay”
text: This the best hotel I have stayed in a long time. The staff is great, the rooms are clean and the breakfast is yummy. Also the pool is very relaxing.

title: “great place to stay in Chicago. Absolutely love this place'”
text: great place to stay. you get what you pay for. The Blackstone is worth it.

title: “Good location”
text:
Great location and friendly staff. 
Only drawback: noisy area (I sleept well, but my girlfriend had to use "ear plugs").
We would definitly stay there again.

title: “Beautiful space for a wedding!”
text: I recently got married at Maple Manor and it was such a wonderful venue! Monique was very helpful and ran everything, I didn't stress about anything the day of which was important to me. We had so many compliments on the food and the beautiful space. I would recommend Maple Manor to anyone. It was a really wonderful experience.

title: “dirty (bathroom hadn't been cleaned) and unfriendly staff”
text:
I'd not recommend this place to anyone who doesn't feel like cleaning up the toilet upon arrival is a fun thing to do.
The staff was unfriendly and unresponsive. Breakfast was included but some stale bagels couldn't improve my impression in any way.

title: “Just OK hotel”
text: We stayed here for one night and the hotel was OK but nothing great. It was clean and the people at the front desk were friendly. The room was very small and since our room was facing the street, it was quite loud until the wee hours of the morning with street noises plus there is a bar right next door that played loud music until very late. Then early in the morning we heard the trash being picked up. Also, the neighborhood is not the greatest. If you need to get a good night's sleep, I would not recommend this hotel!

title: “Great stay!”
text: Got a great deal on priceline for 2 night stay on St Patrick's Day weekend.
