My wife's sister from Brazil was visiting with us for the month and we decided to go to Baltimore for a fun weekend out. The staff members were very friendly and helpful. When we checked in, they had us set up for a King bed. As tempting as that was, I asked if they had a room available with 2 beds. The guy at the front desk (I forget his name, sorry) upgraded us to a corner deluxe room, which was very spacious with two beds and lots of windows. The only reason I didn't give this hotel 5 out of 5 is because of the steep parking fee ($22 a day), which is normal for downtown in any city, and also you could hear a lot of noise coming from the street at night. Not located in the nicest part of town either, but still close to the harbor and power plant live, which is what we came for. All things considered, it was a great stay and I would hope to get this hotel again if bidding the Baltimore Inner Harbor area.

title: “Very comfortable and welcoming, but needs a few amenities for business travelers”
text:
Stayed for the second time at the Sofitel in Philadelphia. Both times, stayed in the junior suite, which is comfortable and "homey" - separate living room w/desk, both a tub and a shower, VERY comfortable bed - makes you want to stay in the room and just get room service. In-room safe, robes, plus a welcome basket that has slippers, tie rack, and many other amenities. Two large-screen TVs, Bose stereos (2), playing soft jazz when you first arrive.
The one thing I learned is that you need to request a coffeemaker for your room if you want it. You can do that when you make your reservation and it'll be waiting for you when you check in. Everyone is very accommodating, and the lounge area is relaxing. After a busy day in Philadelphia, going back to the hotel was like going home. I even had a room next to the ice maker and didn't hear a thing all night.
One negative for the business traveler: there is no free internet access in the room. Access is available for a sign-up fee. I don't know whether there's a Business Center where you can access the Internet or print documents, but the people at the front desk are top-notch on service, so it'd just be a quick stop there to find out.
The hotel is located just around the corner from Walnut Street, which has plenty of restaurants and designer stores and is near Rittenhouse Square.

title: “Perfect choice for taking in all that San Francisco has to offer”
text:
My wife and I recently had the pleasure of staying three nights at Hotel Vitale and given our needs, style of travel and itinerary we couldn't have chosen a better hotel.
We don't get to travel as often as we'd like being in the hospitality industry ourselves, but we know the difference between those who are just "doing their job" and those committed to excellence. At every staff level we encountered, the service was friendly, efficient and most of all helpful.
Our flight into SF put us there several hours before check in would begin, so we inquired before leaving home about the possibility to drop off our bags and go have fun until we were ready to check in. From that initial one on one contact to the moment we left the property for the last time after checking out, we were treated with the utmost of respect, congeniality and an obvious desire by all staff to fully serve our needs. When we arrived assuming just to drop off our bags, we were offered multiple room options, the opportunity to check in and a confident assurance that the process would take but a few moments and our worries for the next three days would be left behind.
That is exactly what happened and our entire trip was one of relaxed, leisurely paced fun and everyone at Hotel Vitale helped us achieve that.
Our suite, #330 was nicely decorated in comfortable tones and high quality features. We live in a rural area where one can hear a pin drop and despite our suite being just a few floors above a busy intersection, we slept soundly each night and suffered from no inside or outside distractions. We experienced no noise above what one should expect while the heart of an urban area. In fact, far less.
The beds and linens were very high quality and on the days we didn't want service our privacy was fully respected. The suite was amply sized for our needs and a comfortable respite to return to each night after long days and evenings mostly walking everywhere we enjoyed. 
The few instances of assistance we asked for were given enthusiastically, efficiently and with a sincerity that was a real comfort.
The quality of all the hardware and plumbing fixtures was outstanding and the only observation I have to make is the lack of true, high efficiency in terms of water conservation. We choose lodging partly based on their stated commitment to providing an eco-friendly experience and are both personally and professionally aware of what is available in this regard. Noticing the lack of a "lathering" valve or water volume adjustment on the shower head may be this treehugger being a bit harsh, but the shower head is the most used water device in a hotel. I fully understand and can appreciate that in the effort to meet some traveler's expectation of luxury it can be a difficult tradeoff and Hotel Vitale's other "green' efforts were more than obvious, so no harm, no foul.
While not an imposition to us or a major impact, the lack of separation and noise mitigation of the bar/lounge from the main reception area could be improved upon. The contradiction between the serene, muted understatement of the hotel itself and the loud din of the bar/lounge area was noticeable nearly every time we entered or exited between 4pm and midnight. While no guest rooms are on the ground floor, one must pass the noise source in order to go up to one's room. 
We had no idea business groups could enjoy themselves to such an extent and for so long each evening, but it did inhibit our efforts to patronize what appears to be a very nice restaurant and lounge more often than we did. 
Our days were filled with easy, convenient jaunts from the hotel and its proximity to the Ferry Building, a San Francisco gem is not to be understated. Every mode of public transportation available is within minutes of Hotel Vitale and we took full advantage of that fact. 
All in all, quite the enjoyable and memorable experience.

title: “good hotel, insanely great food, but out of towners might want better location”
text:
This is a beautiful hotel. We stayed in the tower. Concierge floor has WONDERFUL food, as does room service. You would not need to eat out...the food here is as good if not better. Yummy guacamole, steak sandwich, spring rolls, seafood alfredo pasta. 
Rooms are nice, flat screen, attentive maids.
If your room key stops working be prepared for a long walk (if late at night) or a very long wait for another one. The tower front desk not open late so you have to go to atrium. It's a HUGE hotel.
Decent location but not the best. During rush hour traffic is the pits to go even 15 minutes away.

title: “perfect for meetings and great location for business trips”
text: my company held a week long meeting here and I could not have been more impressed. Everything went so smoothly - the food was particularly excellent, not your average "hotel food." The rooms were great and I never had any problems. And don't even get me started on the cookies - they are just wonderful! Staff was overaccomodating to our needs and we never had to ask twice for anything, even when we made last-minute changes in the meeting. I could not say enough positive things about this hotel. We will definitely be back!

title: “Great location”
text: We were in Chicago for our annual Christmas weekend. Had not stayed at this particular hotel before, but couldn't pass up the special on Travel Zoo of $89/night (parking in attached deck for $26/day). One block off of Michigan Avenue. Just a great location for shopping and restaurants. Staff at the front desk was very friendly and helpful. Room was large, very clean, and very adequate for our stay, especially considering the rate we got. Would definitely stay here again, especially if we can ever get the special rate.

title: “No complaints”
text:
Great location - 2 minute walk to Fishermans Wharf.
Good value breakfast and foc internet.
Large rooms...no complaints

title: “Great location - Not a great room”
text: We stayed at this hotel for a long weekend. The location is great as it is just a few blocks from Beale Street. When we first walked in we were impressed by the lobby as well as the friendly staff. Unfortunately our feelings changed once we saw the room. The carpets were heavily stained and the furniture was old and worn. The climate controls in our two bedroom suite did not work properly. One bedroom was hot and the other was cold. We also found one of the bathrooms to not be very clean (grimy shower floor and hair on a towel). The fitness room was also cramped and extremely warm. The treadmills were old and outdated. Considering what we paid per night, we felt the amenities were not in line.

title: “2 Peas in a pod during hurricane Sandy!”
text:
We arrived at Pod 39 just before hurricane Sandy hit. :(
We stayed in a Queen Room facing the street. Yes rooms are tiny but we went to nyc to explore, so the room was not a big upset b/c we expected it! Although, the beds were very comfy. Also, definitely make sure you are comfortable with the person you're staying with b/c the bathroom is seperated only by a snowy glass door. 
During Sandy, the electricity went out and we were faced with many challenges - climbing the 16th floor :/ ...no hot water(only for 1 day) thank goodness for back up generators!! The staff were excellent during this time..Charlton was a big help going up and down everytime with us and Scott also and many others! A big thank you to all the staff they were very helpful always! It made our stay much easier and welcomed!
We were lucky enough to get our stay extended to actually explore once Sandy left! We made the best of the time we had left! The staff accommodated us very well!
Pod 39 is a great location. Just a walk away from Grand Central(beautiful inside), Empire state Building, Times Square, 5th Ave...lots of restaurants, coffee shops! Our fave bkfst place was bagel express..quick, easy and cheap compared to other places!
Be prepared to do alot of walking...you get to see more things rather then taking a taxi everywhere! 
We would def come back to Pod 39.

title: “Ripped off”
text:
Beware.
We went to a lovely reception here, but afterward, the parking valet tried to shortchange me by $10.00. When I asked for the rest of my change, he didn't even apologize. The hotel manager was almost as bad as the dishonest valet. It was really distressing to have this happen at such a beautiful Seattle landmark. I'm thinking that they don't do random drug testing with their employees.

title: “Good stay, friendly staff.”
text: The hotel was in a convenient location, the staff was very helpful with directions and went above and beyond to get us a cab when needed. Definitely will stay again while in NYC

title: “Good value in the $$$ city....”
text:
I was worried about staying here because the location is not great, other than being close to Madison Square Garden and Macy's, the neighborhood is safe enough, but has nothing else to recommend it. Having said that, the hotel itself, and especially the rooms are very, very nice. My room had 2 double beds that were very comfortable
and each had 3 pillows, (3 firm and 3 soft), to satisfy all sleepers!
My room had a flat screen TV, small chest of drawers, desk and an adequate closet. The breakfast is included in the room price and it is actually pretty good, as long as you don't need eggs and bacon everyday. They have fruit, yogurt, cereal, bagels, toast, english muffins, muffins and biscuits. In addition, they have 2 hot selections that they change each day. Newspaper, (USA Today) is also complimentary.
The breakfast room is pretty basic, but if you don't need something fancy, it's fine. The only thing I didn't like is that all the cups,
plates, bowls and cutlery were plastic, which is pretty environmentally irresponsible!
The bathroom in my room was a bit small, but everything was very clean and worked very well. Great water pressure in the shower. The location is convenient for 3 subway lines and there are good cheap internet cafes only 2 blks away, which is important since I don't have a laptop. I would stay here again. I found it much better than some of the 4 and 5 star hotels I have stayed in in Manhattan!

title: “BIG disappointment”
text:
My wife attended a conference in Chicago and the W Chicago Center was one of the recommended hotels. Because we had stayed at W in San Francisco last year and loved it, she was anxious to stay at the W again. A week or so before we went to Chicago, we received our credit card bill to find that the W had already charged over $600 to our credit card. When we arrived at the W, my wife pointed out that we had already been charged for $600 for our room. The desk clerk argued that we had not been charged but maybe only had "a hold placed". It was only after we presented a copy of the credit card statement and she disappeared into a back room did she agree that we had already paid $600. One of the first things the desk clerk said to us was to ask if we wanted to upgrade to a larger room. We declined thinking that a $300 a night room should be adequate. This turned out to be the smallest hotel room I have ever stayed in. Everyone knows how small the bathrooms are on cruise ships. The bathroom we had on our last cruise which happened to be an interior room not one of the top of the ship rooms, was bigger than the W 's bathroom. I counted the floor tiles. The sink was smaller than my bar sink at home. There was about an inch or two on each side of the sink to try to balance anything you tried to put down. You had to close the lid of the toilet to reach the flush lever. The only drawer space in the room were three small drawers in the night stand. The carpet was dirty. Of course it is very hard to see anything because it was so dark in the room. One lamp had a fairly decent light but the other lamp--the one on the desk--if it was a 40 watt bulb, I would be surprised. I tried to use the DVD player provided in the room but it was so dark in that corner that I could not see the controls. On Sunday, I asked the concierge for recommendations for dinner. He suggested we eat at the restaurant in the hotel. Later when we were ready for dinner, we found that the restaurant is not open on Sundays. 
On the positive, the lobby area is very nice, very hip with projections on the walls above the two giant archways. W always has a nice smell. The concierge desk was very helpful in printing out our boarding passes for our trip home.

title: “A real New York feeling”
text:
I spent three nights at the Chelsea Inn during my last trip to New York City and was very pleased by my stay.
Since I live in Montreal, I like going to spend a long week-end in NY here and there, and I've been to different kinds of hotels.
This was my best experience.
Since New York is very pricey, we were happily pleased by the very reasonable prices for such a great neighbourhood (right between Chelsea and Greenwich Village).
Our lovely and large room with queen size bed was perfectly clean and neat and very confortable. Since we agreed on sharing a bathroom with only one room next door (which caused no problem at all), we were charged 109$/night, breakfast included. For NY, this is quite amazing.
Of course, you have to be ok with the bathroom sharing thing. 
What I liked to most, aside from the cheap rates, the service and the lovely staff, was the feeling to that place.
Kind of vintage without actually trying to be. The feeling you get is that the place has not been redecorated since the 70's.
The bed seemed new, we had Air Con and all those facilities (fridge, flat tv, etc.) but the looks were very dated, which we found charming. 
The stairs crack a lot and by the windows, you see habitations and backstreets in bricks and that kind of stuff. You know, the New York feeling.
I strongly recommand it.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: We stayed overnight at this hotel on our way to Dayton. It was beautiful! Check-in was a breeze; all employees we had contact with were helpful and polite. We were disappointed we weren't staying longer. A relative in the area told us the restaurant is very good, but we did not eat there. BE AWARE that parking is $23 and internet access is not free. We got a fantastic rate off Priceline ($55 + taxes). Otherwise I might not have been so thrilled with the parking and internet charge.

title: “Beware the 8th Floor!!”
text:
We have a phrase in the UK - 'Fur coat and no knickers'. For those who dont understand it means flash on the outside with nothing to back it up on the inside.
The foyer is very spacious and attractive, the rooms an absolute disgrace.
 The 8th Floor was our unlucky abode. The room smelt of damp and NOTHING yes NOTHING! worked in the bathroom. The toilet didnt flush, the plug in the sink didnt stay in until I wedged a paper cup in the system and there was no shower head or mechanism.Oh and the latch on the window was broken making it impossible to close (The man on reception claimed this was OK as it provided air conditioning!!!!!).
We then failed to follow instructions and complained to reception who eventually agreed to move us. Our new room wasnt made up and closer inspection of the last occupants trash led us to believe it hadnt been cleaned for at least 4 days. The beds were unmade and wet towels littered the room. The staines on 2 of the chairs were not reassuring either.
We chose this hotel because of its location and price. The Hotels summary advised that this hotel was ideal for those who wanted to spend their money on the delights of New York and not on accomodation. This phrase is an absolute 'cop out'. I do not expect much from a hotel, as in my opinion you dont spend enough time in it to warrant a classy service , but this place is a shambles. To anyone thinking that my comments and others are overly harsh - trust me they are not - avoid this one like the plague!

title: “WiFi and Cell Signal issues EVERYWHERE”
text:
The only reason I stay at this hotel is for the conference center and so that I don't have to walk from a neighboring hotel to get to my conferences. If the WiFi and cell service worked, it'd be a win! Overall, it's a nice hotel. A few things just knocked it down. It may sound like I'm nitpicking. But I feel in letting you know about everything I've seen that might make a difference to you.
The staff have always been friendly every time I've been here. But the service and amenities seem to be going downhill.
What good is WiFi access in a business catered hotel if you can't access it? Simply put: the WiFi signal is only good near the front door of the suite. So if you want to use WiFi near the bedroom, forget it. I was assured that routers are placed every 15 feet in the hallway, but that's of little comfort since across the hall from me is nothing but an empty ceiling space that looks down onto the main lobby five floors down. I really don't understand, as well, why I have to purchase WiFi that is included FREE with my package only to be reimbursed at check out.... that makes absolutely no sense whatsoever. I suppose it wouldn't be nearly such an issue if my companions and I could actually get on with one of our five devices.
Speaking of signal strength... there's no cell phone reception either. if you're lucky enough to get a signal anywhere other than the main lobby, you'll have to be quick to avoid 'breaking up.'
There's hardly any WiFi or phone signal in the downstairs conference center, either. Again, for a hotel that caters to the business customer, these things should be no brainers. I brought my entire company here with the expectation that we can manage our business via either phones or WiFi. So far, we've been stuck with no way to contact our customers unless we go to the main lobby, find a computer in the business center, or go outside to make a phone call. Ridiculous!
Overall, we've always been pleased with the rooms. This particular room, 514, has almost no air flow to the bedroom and absolutely no airflow into the bathroom. So keep the shower temperature down low unless you want to be in a steam room. There's so much moisture in that bathroom that the satin nickel door hinges and other hardware look like some rusted piece of maritime history pulled from the bottom of the ocean. 
Did I mention that the air conditioning has been set to 60 since we got here three days ago but that the temperature has only gotten down to 74? I guess it's broken.
Something's wrong with the TV in the living room area. It's really dark. I enjoy the crayon all over the corner table, too. Looks like a daycare was held here for a while.
Power plugs are hard to find in the bedroom, but plentiful elsewhere.
I'm not too thrilled that office workers in the building just outside our window get to peek inside our room. We'd like to let natural light inside, but it just feels weird with them watching us.
Housekeeping was very regular and acceptable. A number of minor items got missed, however, such as clean cups and fresh towels to replace the soggy ones on the floor. They did take the throw from one of the beds and never replaced it...... 
Bruno has always managed to check us in each time we have stayed here. He is by far one of the most pleasant and enjoyable people I have ever met.
The pull out sofa is VERY comfortable... and I dare say almost more comfortable than the beds. The pillows go VERY flat VERY quickly... so bring your own if you don't want any neck pain.
The chairs are very comfy.
The morning breakfast is awesome and is certainly worthy of a $10 price tag. Many packages get this breakfast free. The staff working the breakfast line kind of hover around you to take your plates and trays away, so it sometimes feels like there are a bunch of buzzards flying overhead. There was one staff member that just acted a little 'weird' to us, all the way down to his shirt always being tucked in the front and completely untucked in the back. Everyone is certainly nice and pleasant.
The Finn and Porter restaurant is something that should likely be avoided altogether. A number of review sites place it only so so. I've eaten there a few times now, but it's not worth the hefty price tag. The service is poor and the food is often mediocre at best. Something always just tastes a little 'off.' The baked mac and cheese dish wasn't even warm and the cheese not even melted. Be cautious at the refill fee on the soft drinks. You get great quality soft drinks... none of that watered down stuff.... but you're also paying about $3 each. It's much easier to go down to McDonald's.
Be warned that a lot of stores, such as CVS, close early around here and many are not open on the weekend. Bring some 2 liters, even if you have to go to CVS. The soda machines run $2 for a 20oz coke product, which is often sold out.
We've found that a great alternative to the nearly $50 per day parking (outrageous, isn't it?) is to drive in from nearby and park at one of the Metro stations with Park and Ride and then take the metro for about $3. Metro parking is only $4 per day and they only collect during the day. So nights and weekends you just drive out. On this trip, however, there was noone there all week to give tickets or take tickets, so we didn't pay a thing to park and took the train. Instead of paying nearly $150 for valet parking for three days... we each paid $3 each way for a train ticket, costing us $18 total. That's a huge savings for anyone on a budget!
If you DO valet park a car, I recommend taking a photo or video of your car before you hand off your keys. On a previous visit, I needed an item from my car and a valet walked me down to the garage. I saw valets speeding through the tight confined deck with almost no care or concern. Nothing ever happened to my car, but there's always that possibility. It'd be hard for them to fight a picture or video of your car in front of the hotel at check in with no damage followed by a comparison with damage when you pick it up. If there is damage, don't pull away because they put out in the fine print that they are not liable if you move the car once it's been brought up.

title: “Hotel with a Heart”
text:
Recently a friend needed a little lift after releasing her senior dog due to failing kidneys. I contaced the hotel concierge, explainded the reason for the jaunt to the city and requested a special touch to be added to the room. As a loyal diamond Hilton Honors member, Lauren extended her persoal concern and empathy for being a part of a healing journey for a friend. She extended her work email address and invited my confirmation of arrival time.
Upon arrival, I was greeted by Lauren warmly at the front desk. She was able to extended an upgraded corner room with a great view of the Magnificent Mile and there was a welcome note giving directions to look in the refrigerator. Sure enough, the fresh berry assortment and real cream were available for a healthy treat. 
Many hotels have the finest amenities, but a hotel with fine people who care from the heart is priceless.
If you are looking for a great location, in a fabulous part of the city...Conrad Chicago must be a consideration.
If you are looking for a hotel staff who want to do their best to help you pull off a special treat...look nowhere else. The Conrad Hotel is your hotel.

title: “Amazing Value and top-drawer service. Very classy”
text: My wife and I, and a good friend of ours stayed for a night based on previous reviews I'd read. I think the hotel was a bit under capacity, so the very friendly and helpful front desk staff bumped us into some sort of suite; my wife and I in one, and our friend in a second. The service was fantastic and the room was just beautiful. The rehab of this old bank is really topnotch; the bathroom alone was good enough for us! comfortable jacuzzi tub, great lighting, interesting and innovative color scheme, and of course a heavenly-comfortable bed. One of the top 3 rooms i've ever stayed in... and the price was unbeatable. GREAT value.

title: “Queen for the Day”
text:
I visited the Barclay International Hotel to celebrate my 60th birthday. The visit started out with some complications that being the room accomadations were not correct. There were suppose to be 2 queen size beds in a suite but instead the room had a king bed and pull out couch.. When my son heard this he was extremely upset so he called up and was told they would make the necessary changes.. When I got to my room Lee from quest services called me explaning there was no more room accomadations for 2 queen beds. So, I very politely told her she must either change the room or rectify the situation.. When she hear it was my 60th birthday celebration and my son had made these reservations for me she told me she would make this all happen. Within minutes I was headed up to the Presidential suite where dreams I never thought could happen just happened... 
The Barclay went above and beyond what I could have ever expected. My weekend turn out to be one of the most fabulous weekends of my entire life... Thanks to everyone at the Barclay who made my 60th birthday a dream come true... I will be back again!!!!

title: “Great place to stay in Houston.”
text: The BEST valets anywhere! This is the best hotel at which I've stayed in Houston. It is private, quiet, well appointed and usually the staff are EXTREMELY nice and accommodating. I've never made the evening reception the several times I've stayed here, but I assume it's a nice treat. The cookies and milk at bedtime are great. The biggest complaint is you have to go to the lounge for wi-fi. A bit pricey, but it hasn't kept me from staying there on several occasions.

title: “Great for business travel!”
text: Lake outside with restaurants is perfect and quick after a long day at the office! Rooms are clean and staff is friendly! Great work out facility. Nice bar to grab a quick beer or a glass of wine. I'd recommend this to everyone!

title: “Great location, not bad for the price”
text:
The Hotel Salisbury is right beside Carnegie Hall, and a 2 minute walk to 2 different subway stations. We stayed in a 1 bedroom suite- the sofa bed is terrible, but we ended up just moving a mattress from one of the two double beds in the bedroom. Note that the double bed isn't really big enough for two people, so you'd be better off with a single king size instead! The bathroom is a bit cramped and doesn't have any ventilation, which can quickly lead to sauna conditions if you're having a shower!! 
Generally very clean and well equipped rooms- the fridge and microwave come in very handy if you don't fancy paying Manhattan prices for eating out. Difficult to find nearby locations for breakfast- restaurants in this area are VERY pricy. 15 minute walk to Times Square and Theater District.

title: “Huge Rooms with EVERYTHING”
text:
We dont usually stay downtown but this was quite a surprise! Loved the huge rooms with everything included that you could imagine. Wireless internet access was easy to use. Bed was very comfortable. Separate living area and kitchen and bedroom was very large. 
Breakfast buffet had everything you could imagine. 
Staf was very helpful and courteous.
Within walking distance of Convention center and the inner harbor!
The Dunkin Donuts walkup window next door was VERY inviting!

title: “Immaculate, Peaceful Cave”
text: I stayed at this hotel for 3 days and 2 nights in October 2010. The room was immaculate, very large, and very quiet. All of the staff members I encountered during the three days were genuine, kind, helpful, and professional. The complimentary breakfast was the best I have ever seen offered at any hotel in the world.

title: “Great location at a good rate”
text: The Holiday Inn Express 5th Avenue offers small but clean rooms at a reasonable rate in a great location--two blocks from Times Square and the theatre district. The front desk staff were cheerful and helpful, the room rate includes a buffet breakfast at a deli up the street. In all, it was easy and convenient and I will check for a room here first the next time I am heading up to NYC for the weekend.

title: “Worst stay ever anywhere”
text:
We arrived at the hotel at 4pm, and there were no towels in the room. I was told they would send some up. An hour later I was told they would send some up. I was told this until 8pm, when I was told they were out of towels in the hotel until 9pm.
I had also reserved a room with 2 queen beds and got a room with 2 large twin beds, not even full sized where my wife and I could not sleep in one bed (we are not that large either).
I had read a prior review complaning about the fact the hotel had run out of the "free" morning biscotti's as promised to quests. That did not happen to us. They sliced the biscotti's into 1/4 inch slices so all quests were assured to get a crumb, if they wanted (no one was taking them)
I asked to speak to a manager the night we aRRIVED TO DISCUSS THE TOWELS. i WAS TOLD NONE WERE AVAILABLE. i asked again the next morning, and was once again told none were available that day. I called again the next day upon returning home (long distance at my expense) and kept getting looped to the 800 central reservations numver. When I asked one of those people if I could speak to a manager or supervisor I was told none were available to talk to customers.
I left home at 5am the night of my stay and paid extra to get what we thought was going to be a nice room in the central warf area of the city the night before taking our son to Stanford for summer school and have a night on the town. After driving all day, and not only not being able to take a shower until after 9pm (arriving at 4pm) but being lied to every hour and forced to wait for towels based upon these lies, our "night on the town" was reduced to waiting in a very small, dingy hotel room with beds we could not all even sleep on. My wife and son rotated trying to sleep on a small chair.
I have never in my life stayed at a hotel, especially one this expensive that did not even have towels for their guests, lied about that and the bed sizes, and were so un-helpful witrh anything we needed.
There are plenty of other hotelsd in this area, any of them have to be better than this was.

title: “Stay here!”
text:
From the moment you walk into the Westin Times Square, you are greeted in a friendly manner that makes you feel like you are more than just a guest at the hotel. Everyone i came in contact with was friendly and helpful. 
The room was wonderful! one side overlooked the street and the other side i could see the Hudson. It was nice. The room was comfy and cozy. One night i was worn out from all of the walking that i had done that i just stayed in and order room service. i sat and ate and looked out at the view. Very nice.

title: “OK Stay”
text: The motel is right on Lombard, within walking distance of the Palace of Fine Arts; Lombard is the main artery for commuters coming across the Golden Gate bridge into SF so commuter noise is loud (try to get a room in the back of the motel). Room size is very good, but storage is sparce. Beds were very good. No privacy curtains with the sun darkening curtains so the room was either pitch dark or open to view by the common walkway. Breakfast was toast, muffins, juice, coffee/tea. WIFI and kiosk are at additional $$. Adequate parking; many spots are covered. Staff very courteous/helpful. Original Buffalo Wing (OBW) resturant very close; serves breakfast/lunch/dinner - great salads and burgers. Two-queen bed room was about $125/night with taxes.

title: “Great Location, Great Hotwire Price, Great Service, many 'little' charges added up.”
text:
We lucked out and got a $49.00 room on Labor Day weekend in the heart of downtown San Diego's Gaslamp. We live in the area, but decided it would be fun to have a 'stayvacation' and show the kids some of the sites. Had a beautiful room, they checked us in 3 hours early. Location was awesome, in the heart of the gaslamp. They honored our request to stay on the 'quiet' side - away from the noise of the trolley tracks. The breakfast buffet was delicious, fully stocked, and well serviced. Within steps of the Convention Center, Petco Park, and the Old Spaghetti Factory.
The few downsides - $28.00 a night parking, very small (yet classy) pool area, and pricey breakfast - cost almost $60.00 for three meals. (Though children 3 and under eat free.) Great trip overall!

title: “Nice for a night or two”
text:
We needed a hotel close to Lincoln Financial Field and weren't concerned with amenities that we'd have no time to use, so we chose this hotel. The location was a good one, a short drive from the stadium. The room was clean, the mattress was clean and comfortable, although the pillows were a little too soft. It took a lot of maneuvering to get the curtains to close all the way without having a gap where someone could peek in (we had a first floor room) and I noticed that the sheers were extremely wrinkled (I noticed the sheers in the breakfast room were wrinkled as well). The hotel was almost at capacity but was not noisy.
The free breakfast was nice, typical continental breakfast fare as well as a waffle-maker. The breakfast room was very clean and everything was well stocked. 
Every staff member we encountered was very friendly and helpful. There's a Ruby Tuesday's restaurant directly across the way, very easy to walk to. Room service is available from an outside delivery company.
The price was great, the room was clean and comfortable, and the staff was excellent.

title: “desk clerk indifference”
text: I stayed at the hotel on 10/31/12. The next day I realized that I had left a shirt behind. I turned around and told two hotel clerks about the situation. It was 1 pm. The clerk had called housekeeping. She had to ask them several times, as though they did not understand her. The clerk stated that the maid said that she did not see a shirt. I described the shirt and asked if she could keep check lost and found, she would not, she only repearted what the maid had said. What the clerk could have done, but did not was to send the maid back to the room or let me go up with her to check, but she did not. That was disappointing, so I left.

title: “Gracious staff, nice amenities, great value - personal, relaxed and friendly”
text: Stayed for two nights in July. When my single room wasn't ready, Vinnie got quite embarrassed (needlessly) and quickly upgraded me (free) to a king, which was comfortable with a spacious bathroom. Nice complimentary breakfast buffet and wine and cheese in comfy second-floor lounge and good deal on parking right next door. The staff was unfailingly gracious and accommodating, and employees I had never met were addressing me personally by the second day. The service staff was friendly and cheerful. Despite being just steps from Times Square, it's very quiet as soon as you step inside the hotel. Great value in NYC; I'd stay there again in a heartbeat.

title: “Perfect for business travel”
text: This was the second time staying at this property. Friendly staff, great breakfast and manager's reception. The only place I'll stay when in Houston on business.

title: “What a Ripoff”
text:
We stayed at the Radisson Hill Country Resort for two nights in February 2006. Got a hotwire "deal" for 85$ per night. At first we did have some problems finding the hotel because it is in a very isolated location. Yes, it is close to Sea World, but what good is that when the park is closed for the season. Shopping and dining is a 15 minute drive away. 
At had a very bad experience at check in. As hotwire "third party" clients we were treated like third class customers. The first clerk told us our requested two double beedrom was unavailable. He then checked with his manager and she told us that we would have to pay 50$ on top of our rate to get our two double beds. This is indeed a ripoff because in this case we would have paid more than their regular roomrate. So we just sticked with our king room on their third floor overlooking the parking lot.
The room was okay. It was nothing special though and comporable to Holiday Inn at the best. Marble bathroom was quite nice and the bed was comfortable. We did not get any amenities like soap and shampoo on our second night. I wonder if that's part of their hotwire customers policy as well ???
The pool area is quite nice as well with comfortable chairs and such. It was wintertime though and there was virtually nobody in the pool. Can imagine that it will be quite crowded during high season.
After all I would not stay there again because of the bad experiences I have made. You may like it if you pay their full rate and book through Radisson's homepage. But let me tell you it may not be worth that much money.

title: “Mouse”
text: We had a mouse in our room. My girlfriend called the front desk to see what they could do about it and they told us they could give us free WiFi and breakfast. I thought she was kidding when she said this, unfortunately she was not. We asked for a new room and they said no. I called back and said we were leaving and they magically had a room open up, also I got a nice dose of attitude from the woman on the phone from the front desk as if I did something wrong. We left and will not be back. Its unfortunate that they ended what was a great night at my friends wedding. I guess we were lucky that we lived so close as opposed to if it happened to family members that traveled for hours to get to there.

title: “Perfect in most every way”
text: We just returned from a 6 day stay at the Orchard and found it to be the perfect hotel for our needs, which didn't include a lot of the ameneties larger hotes might have to offer, but did include what we needed most including; a helpful friendly staff, a great location close enough to walk to most everything we wanted including Chinatown, Union Square, Northbeach, and if you didn't mind walking, Fisherman's Wharf was only a couple of steep hills away. Also, Steven the manager (owner?) was very friendly and accomodating to all the guest. The breakfast buffet was another great thing, and best of all the rooms had great beds and were very well insulated from outside noise which was much appreciated after a lot of long tiring days. One tip I would offer is if you can, get a room facing Bush St. which is a little quieter than those on the other side of the hotel (but Steven assured us he was working with the city to correct the noise problem on the "back side" of the hotel).

title: “Close to Cathedral and Chinese Visa Office”
text:
Only recommended if:
 you want to walk to the Washington National Cathedral 
 if you need to get a visa from the Chinese embassy
 otherwise, not recommended
 indifferent service, dreary rooms
 avoid the downstairs restaurant

title: “Caution:”
text:
Horrible service, strange smells, and absolutely NO assistance offered.
I needed cash to buy a coke... asked the guy at the front desk, who already had an attitude. He He didn't even suggest that they have an ATM in the lobby, which I didn't notice until the next morning. Pretty disappointing. 
The room smelled really bad, I literally brewed coffee in the little coffee maker, just to get the smell, at 2:00 in the morning.

title: “Really Surprised”
text: We booked the Flatotel for 5 nights, and only read the reviews on Tripadvisor after we booked so we were a bit worried about what lay ahead in this hotel. I emailed the hotel and asked for a refurbished room. All i can say is we were really surprised, the room was large, modern and clean,the bathroom was on the small side, but it was lovely, and that too was modern and spotless. The Lifts are a bit on the slow side, but we used the service lift a few times as did a lot of people. The breakfast consists of fruit and pastries tea or coffee, its ok and fills a gap before you head out. As regards the staff the restaurant staff are friendly and as is the bell boy and door man, although one or two of the reception staff could do with a week or two in a charm school.Overall we enjoyed our stay at the Flatotel and would stay there again. The Location of this hotel is excellent.

title: “A family with two kids : We enjoyed our stay”
text: \my wife and I with our two kids ages 3 and 9 just returned from a weekend stay for a night there. We took a weekend package with an executive room that includes breakfast. We liked the room that is big enough for all the family . The pool is very small but ok for the kids. The service was very good . The bar area is welcoming. Location is very central and convenient. Breakfast rate was added to our bill although it was included in the rate. That I did not like . Make sure you carefully check your bill during check out.

title: “Stay Away!”
text:
Here are the top 8 reasons we will not stay at this property again:
1) All common areas reeked of cigarette smoke.
2) The room was over 80 degrees when we entered.
3) No stopper in the sink - s small problem for those with contact lenses.
4) Clock radio found on the floor behind the night stand - with the time set one hour ahead. I'm guessing the room had not been used since the time changed.
5)The light fixture on the wall between the beds didn't work. The reson was that the cord had been cut and the plug was missing.
6) Property in general is old and has not been renovated for years.
7) When an attempt was made to discuss these problems, the front desk clerk walked away without any response.
8) The room we were given could only be reasonably accessed by a flight of stairs since the elevator was at the far end of the building. There couldn't have been more than 10 rooms in use and we could have easily had a room very near the elevator.
This property is rated 3 diamonds by AAA and is by the far the worst property we have ever experienced. Do not even think about staying there!

title: “Location is not all they have, but they sure do have that!”
text: This is a huge (50 stories plus) magestic old style luxury hotel. If is not up to the highest fliers these days, it is still a great place to stay in New York City. We requested and received a Times Square View. Our room was only 30 stories up, but we had a spacious, corner king room with windows on two sides that aforded a view (not totally unobstructed, but still very exciting and definitely worthwhile) of Times Square and all its action and crowds. The room had good lighting, plenty of comfortable and solid furniture, big TV, great large and clean bath rooms, and our room was very quiet. It did smell like someone had been smoking in our supposedly non-smoking room, but we only noticed that when the AC had been off awhile, so it was not overpowering and quickly dissipated away once we turned that up a bit. The maid skipped cleaning our room the day the Do not Disturb sign was out past noon, (although we were out all afternoon after that) but at least she/he did not wake my sleeping daughter. The front desk was pleasant and efficient, bell service stored our bags without a hitch, concierge was not overly friendly but did help us out when asked, and the room was clean, functional and very comfortable...actually the bed, blankets and pillows could be improved, but they were usable. Very nice stay I would do it again.

title: “Luxury Luxury Luxury!”
text: My 14 year old daughter and I stayed at Sofitel just before Christmas on the "I love Chocolate" special. Full breakfast came with the room as well as a fancy chocolate experience, which I will describe in a bit. The hotel is fabulous and pristine. The rooms are unparalleled. The beds with their thick feather duvets are fantastic. There is a marble bathroom with soaking tub and shower. The staff was so helpful and pleasant! Breakfast was delicious and gorgeous and we could order whatever we wished from the breakfast menu. And there is French Press coffee! The chocolate experience was a tray of mini desserts of different types which was brought to our room upon our request. I almost half expected to see some type of extra charge upon departure, but no, I was pleasantly surprised by a zero balance on the bill. I can't say enough good things about the Sofitel. If I had anything bad to say or any improvement to suggest, it is that there is no coffee maker in room. Therefore you must get dressed and ready and leave the room for coffee or get room service (either way you sort of have to face the world before coffee). Certainly not a major complaint though. Also, the location of this hotel is just by water tower and rush street. Plenty of fabulous restaurants and shopping just steps away.

title: “Great location, nice stay”
text:
We stayed in room 208. A large room that was very clean and well maintained.
Pros: Free parking garage, hair dryer, coffee maker, BEAUTIFUL furniture, safe, iron & ironing board, free WiFi, 47 in. LG LCD TV, quiet air conditioner, large sofa with a table & chairs. Great location to shopping & Fisherman's Wharf.
Cons: No breakfast or dining, no refrigerator or microwave, no laundry facilities on site
The location and price make this a very good value. We paid $175 for the first nights, and $100 each of the next two nights. Be aware - there is NO smoking allowed in the rooms, and they are serious. My wife smokes, but I can't stand it. On arrival, we asked if smoking was allowed in the garage area, and it was. She only smoked in the garage area, but on our final bill, we had an additional $75 charge for smoking in the room. Apparently, the smell on her clothes was enough for them to assume there was smoking in the room. To the hotel's credit, when I contested the charge, they dropped it from the bill without much argument.
We were within walking distance of Pier 39, Fisherman's Wharf, Chinatown, Alcatraz Tours and Russian Hill.

title: “Service....? Never heard of it here !”
text:
Yes the Standard hotel is on the fabulous High line, yes it has a really cool bar and it's restaurants are always full of cool people or wannabe cool people. But try being a hotel guest and you have little chance of service. Not strangers to luxury hotels around the world, we were flabbergasted at how badly we were treated by staff who seem to be caught up in the be- cool thing. I must say the young guys helping with taxis and luggage were polite and helpful, check in staff too were polite, but after that it was downhill. I managed to be well ignored as I waited to get breakfast, there was always confusion, and not much attention. I ate there only twice out of seven days. Try getting into the upstairs bars, and there is little hope. Guest? Are you on a list? No effort to provide service . In fact we tried twice and were virtually abused by the caricatures guarding the doors. Clearly wrong age demographic, over fifty, and not cool enough. 
The hotel rooms have amazing views but you don't find anywhere to hang your bath towel and the shower sprays onto the carpet in the corridor. Enjoy the highline but if you want to feel like a guest in a real hotel and to find some decent service, avoid this one.

title: “Good atmosphere but shabby and noisy!”
text: We were a group of 5 family members staying at the Fairmont in 3 rooms. The lobby is impressively large and ornate. Having said that we were also approached by a panhandler while sitting in the lobby. Our room was fine but the carpet was shabby and needed to be replaced. One of our group was placed in a room with a Murphy bed! My main complaint was the noise in our room from traffic. It was hard to sleep. The Fairmont is a grand old lady but badly needs some renovations. The location is very central but be ready to pay for parking. We did not eat breakfast there as it was too expensive but there are reasonable places nearby. We did enjoy appetizers and drinks at Shuckers.

title: “Like Home Only better”
text: The lobby is magnificent. The rooms are great. The club floor lounge is open many more hours than most. The breakfast and evening snacks were more than adequate and the best part was the staff. They new our name.They inquired about our visit and then remembered and checked the swim meet results when we came back in the evening. We enjoyed southern hospitality at it's finest.

title: “Enjoyed my stay”
text:
Excellant location only surpassed the service.
Everyone was solicitous and unfailingly polite.
Great view from the 32nd floor!
Clean-spacious-I would stay again and recommend it to anyone.

title: “Great Staff, Great Hotel, Great service adds up to Great holiday”
text: Stayed here for 8 nights (based on a friend's recommendation) from 20 September for our first visit to NY. Couldn't have been more impressed or satisfied right from check-in to check-out, Quick registration at which we were upgraded to a one bedroom deluxe suite (huge rooms including two bathrooms and kitchenette and large lounge room). As we were celebrating a special anniversary the hotel provided champagne and chocolate strawberries which were so much appreciated. Great lady at information / bookings counter who got us great tickets for Jersey Boys and also War Horse. Unfortunately can't remember her name but suffice to say " she was picking up what we were putting down", (a great saying she left us with). Niles is great bar for after show drinks or two or three. Also many thanks for the guys at the front door for their great work. When we come back, and we will come back, would not stop anywhere else. Congratulations to management and staff.

title: “Loved the mansfield great location ******”
text:
We have just returned from a fantastic stay in New York City. The mansfield was perfect for a city break, it couldn't have been more central, times square and 5th Av are less than 5mins walk. 
Check in was quick and friendly. Rooms are small but for this location its not really that surprising. "small" but perfectly formed in my opinion. Rooms were very clean and nicely designed bit of old meets new. 
I notice some reviews call the rooms tired, which in my opinion is harsh, if you are used to staying in Holiday inns with clinical beech cupboards and plastic flooring then yes it is more rustic than that but certainly not tired, more classic with dark wood flooring and nice neutral furnishings giving it a warm comfortable feeling, which was certainly welcomed by us when escaping the cutting december winds outside.
The air con didn't bother us, but our days were so packed we were asleep before our heads hit the pillow every night.
Breakfast was basic, but more than adequate. However, if you are looking for a big fry up every day then you may need to look elsewhere.
Staff were great and couldn't have been any more polite and helpful.
I thought the mansfield was great and would definately recommend to all.

title: “Happy to find The Time”
text: Great location in times square. Everyone who worked there was friendly with big smiles, from doormen to front desk staff. It was a very welcoming place to stay. I found this hotel on priceline- i needed a room in NYC last minute, put in a bid for a 3.5 star hotel in Times Square and this was the place that took it. Stayed on ninth floor, room 901, the room wasn't large, but there was a comfortable king size bed in a nicely decorated room. Other than no dial tone on the phones and a toilet that ran for awhile after flushing, everything was great. Location was outstanding. I would stay again no problem. Wish I had time to eat dinner in the restaurant. It looked really nice!

title: “quirky hotel with everything you could want”
text:
Del Sol is a great little motel near the harbour and within a 30 minute walk of Ghiradellis ice cream parlour. Easy access to every where using the bus system. If you want to be in the centre then this is a lttle way out but we travelled with 2 boys 11 and 8 and it was perfect for us. Swimmig pool was great and breakfast things to help yourself before heading out for the day. 
Very helpful staff and adequate rooms.
Would stay there again!

title: “Perfect:-)”
text: During our recent stay we were very pleased with the service and quality of your hotel and staff. We were treated exceptionally well and our meals was served with total professionalism and care. I must say that my meal was one of the best meal we have ever had. Our meals were served without delay and the timing of the food being brought to our table was spot on. very comfy and spacious room with two flat screen tvs. Large bathroom with no tub but double shower. Separate sitting room next to bedroom. Everything very clean, housekeeping very good. Free wi-fi in the room. Great gym on the 4th floor. Great location .

title: “miss it, would go back”
text: my sister and close friend stayed there for nine wonderful nights. the room we stayed in had plenty of room for the three of us. i believe we were in the deluxe double. the room was very clean as was the entire hotel. the staff was very professional and polite. i had a chance to check out the spa which i loved, could have spent more time in there. if you would like a little frig for continous drinks and to put a few snacks/food in they will provide you with one. there is everything you need in this area, the night-life, liqour stores, comedy shows across the street, drug store, endless food, a movie theater, we took in SITC, great movie.. easy excess to everything.. oh yes the beds were heavenly.. i would recommend this to anyone as i haved been to nyc 3 times and this was my best stay. it was a little more cost wise but truely worth the little more that i paid. i miss the westin and can't wait to get back to enjoy fabulous new york city..

title: “Clean, good service.”
text: I booked this hotel for friends who were visiting from the midwest. A slight mixup in the reservation but management resolved with better than expected outcome. The rooms are small but clean. The staff is friendly, helpful and were willing to go out of their way. The bell service is very good, kept our belongings locked up until we were able to check in. Good location. I would recommend again.

title: “Best locations in Manhattan”
text:
I was on a business trip to NY and had to select this hotel due to the proximity of my workplace.
This hotel is very conveniently located to a lot of eating joints, wall street, subways. About 10 minutes cab drive to Times Square, Broadway. Me being from India we are used to big hotel rooms however i found this place very cramped. The bathrooms were nice and clean but small.
Internet costs are $12 a day and believe me its not worth it, the quality was just too bad and the worse part is if you use two devices its $12 a device (which is very strange). 
There is Chipotle/Subway/Pharmacy about 50 mts distance from the hotel so you wouldnt sleep hungry for sure. There are couple of nice pizza joints located bang opposite to the hotel if you like Italian.
Niket

title: “Basic but spotlessly clean, friendly & right beside a subway stop”
text: I would recommend this hotel if all you want is somewhere to wash yourself, lay your head at night and maybe watch some tv. The rooms are extremely clean and comfortable.

title: “Not for Everyone, though a Nice Stay at the Pearl”
text:
Like those of you reading this review, we did our research prior to booking the Pearl. So, we knew that it had a funky vibe, could get loud in the evenings, and wasn't a 'in the middle of everything' type of place. 
If you want to be in the heart of the action in San Diego, this probably isn't your place. Nor is it a good choice if you want a totally quiet and traditional type of hotel experience.
However, if you want a unique experience, I'd suggest the Pearl. It's not for everyone, but after our stay we decided we did like the experience and the property.
When we called, we asked for a room that was away from the noise and action. We booked the smallest room, and yes - it's definitely small. However, we were heading out on a cruise and this helped prepare us for the next week on the ship.
The Gem room was small, but nice. Large flat panel TV, couch/bed combo, and Sza Sza on the wall (Beta fish) greeted us upon entry. Simple, but it worked. The bathroom was cruise ship size, and the only real negative was the shower curtain (mold!) and what looked like a few shortcuts in refinishing the bathroom... paint was peeling and in one area some rust was starting to show through the paint. Those were the only two con's, which were more than made up for by comfy bed (very nice)! We had the fan on for some air movement, and that hummed us to sleep... didn't even hear the activity outside the door in the bar/pool area. 
We took advantage of what the property had to offer. We grabbed the bus across the street for the $2 and 8 minute trip to Old Town and had a nice meal. We utilized the mini-mart next door for some ice cream treats and some liquor drinks, and grabbed some bottled water as well. The next morning, we borrowed the beach cruiser bikes and headed to Shelter Island for some breakfast at the muffin place and a nice ride along the waterfront as we watched the activity in the harbor. We could even see our cruise ship beckoning us for our coming trip to Mexico.
Staff weren't always at the front desk, though were extremely helpful. Directions, advice, and friendly conversation was the norm.
If you are rewards member of a Holiday Inn Express or Marriott, this won't be your typical stay and might not be the hotel for you. However, if you want a unique experience at a unique property, then consider the Pearl. We are glad we did.

title: “GREAT Service Comfortable Rooms Good Location”
text: As a coast to coast traveler for over 20 years, I found this location to be among the best in its class. Friendly staff, renovated rooms, clean, quite, comfortable. A GREAT value and a favorable location make this property a TOP PICK for me when staying in the Long Beach, CA. area.

title: “Friendly Service- Always clean room”
text: I enjoyed this hotel, it had friendly staff, a fun location, lots of neat little shops and restaurants nearby, and it was pretty easy access from the I-95 without being next to the freeway. The parking killed me though.- They did not tell me that they would bill me $24 a day for parking. OUCH!!!!

author.location: Salt Lake City, Utah, United States

title: “Very good hotel”
text:
The location of the hotel is great. It is close to ballpark and harbor.
The room and bathroom are very clean and spacious enough, and the bed is comfortable.
The hotel has a beautiful lobby.
Staffs were extremely nice and helpful.
This is a very nice hotel.

title: “Nice Lobby, rooms are average & need updating”
text: The hotel is average. The customer service is good. Arrived a couple hours later than check in time and front desk still had to double check with cleaning staff to see if room was ready. I requested a crib/playpen for my son when reserving the room and it wasn't in the room when I arrived, but they got it to me right away. Upon arriving I could see some aspects of the room needed updating. The carpet looked old, room had AC blasting (so cold, brrr!) and had a smell to it (best description-it was old carpet smell), bathroom had no blower and the towel rack had some rust on it. There is a safe to secure items, but that even looked old and was not operating properly. Part of our visit was to attend a friend's son's birthday at Chuck E Cheese and the front desk was kind enough to give me a print out with directions.

title: “Nice Hotel - Pleasant stay for a business trip”
text:
Stayed here on gov't business. My meetings were at this hotel. 
Room: Very nice. Clean. Large King Room. Nice work area.
Technology: Great wirless reception.
Staff: Very helpful and friendly.
Rate: I got the gov't rate.
Restaurant: Good.
Area: Nothing cheap foodwise very close. Only went out in the evening. The stockyards area is a short cab ride away. Many restaurants and entertainment venues. I recommend Risky's BBQ. Very good. Good portions and prices. There are restaurants in walking distance.
Fitness facility: Very Good. Good equipment. Plenty of maintained cardio equipment, free weights, and universal.
Indoor Pool: Did not use, but is looked very nice and clean. Hot tub also.
Meeting facilities: Very good.

title: “Very nice hotel”
text: This was a very nice hotel. The rooms were a good size and very nicely decorated as well as very clean. One the lower floors there is street noise so if you are sensitive to that I would request a higher floor. It is near the financial district so we took cabs to most places we went but it was also quieter and away from the hussle and bussle on some busier streets. Overall I feel it was a good value. Breakfast in the morning is very overpriced. Go elsewhere if you can.

title: “more of a business hotel than for family”
text: in the last leg of US trip our family stayed here from 22 - 24July. the hotel is massive and located in the downtown. more suited for business and a lot of hidden charges are there from the one advertised online. they will charge extra for even a refrigerator and the parking fees is massive even though Hertz is located in the hotel itself. Staff at the front desk are more of business like than smiling/friendly. breakfast is good, but expensive. the area is crowded and need to wait atleast 20-25 minutes in the line to get seated. if your group is more than 4 it is advised to take a cab whcih will cost you $40 to the O'hare airport rather than the transport from the hotel which charges you around $15 per head. for less luggage you can use the metro which is a couple of blocks away costs $2.25/head. the cab from hotel to the station will cost around $8 for the trip.

title: “Excellent Facilities”
text: A colleague of mine was staying at this hotel recently and invited me to use the second floor lounge. It was extremely comfortable and well appointed with beverages, snacks, and computer facilities. The staff was very accommodating - even loaning my friend a necktie for his business meeting and me a charger for my cell phone.

title: “Perfect Locale for a Weekend Getaway”
text:
The Palacio Del Rio is right on the Riverwalk,conveniently located across from the boat tour depot. 
Some recommendations while staying at this hotel:
1)The breakfast buffet is wonderful! Dine Al fresco if you can in the morning, before the heat. The shuffle of tourists aren't normally out before 8 am and the river is a tranquil spot for a cup of coffee in the morning.
2) Take the boat tour.. you will learn that the water is actually Clear! You can use the tour boats as water taxi's as well... great way to get around.
3) Visit some of the local sites. My husband and I had 3 days to really see San Antonio. We chose our destinations carefully... Here are a few I recommend highly:
a) The McNab Art Museum! It is FREE! The grounds alone are worth visiting.
b) The Natural Bridge Caverns - These are a bit of a drive, but if you have young adventurers, they will love this place. It is a bit of a hike through the caverns though, make sure to wear sturdy shoes! Also, this can be a nice break from the heat of summer.. the caverns are nice and cool!
c)Finally, Visit not only the Alamo but also one of the other Missions to get a feel for the area. I personally loved Mission Conception! But go Early to the Alamo.. this place gets crowded fast. 
And, if you are into food... A trip to Mi Tierra Cafe is a must! Not only is it the most decorated Mexican Restaurant I have ever been to.. but the desserts are Amazing. They have a bakery case at the front of the restaurant. My husband and I picked up a few tibits on the way out to have the next morning! We surely didn't regret it!

title: “Great location but a little tired”
text: Rooms need updating; feels like I was back in the 90's when I walked into the room. Great sized suites and complimentary upgrade due to my status. Good gym, but no outside windows so felt a little "basement-y" but well-equipped. Helpful staff and super fast check in. Gold floor was well-managed and Gold Floor concierge Ryan hooked us up with a great Thai restaurant in the Bloomingdale's building on Michigan Ave. Good location for the lakefront and Millenium park but too far from the "El" Blue Line to walk. Complimentary overnight shoe shine didn't work out so well for me: shoes were a half hour late (I had to call and remind them to bring them to me) and they didn't look like they had actually been shined.

title: “Great location and good hotel”
text: This old hotel has obviously been updated, and although our room was clean and comfortable, it was fairly sparsely decorated. Fortunately, we didn't spend a lot of time inside because we were busy seeing the sights that were just at our doorstep. The Alamo, of course, is the main event in this area, as is the River Walk and the mall right across the street. The bed was comfortable enough, although the room was hot-and-cold all night (no thermostat control in the room). Service was good, but we wished we didn't have to depend on valet parking (it seems there's always something left in the car and almost impossible to get it after it's been parked). All-in-all, it was a good value and we'd stay there again.

title: “The best week in New York”
text:
Two of us stayed at the hotel for nearly a week. From check in to departure, it was a great experience. The hotel is extremely well run and manages to obtain a boutique feeling despite its size of 140 rooms. Unlike other boutique hotels I have stayed in in NY all of the staff - and I mean all - were extremely helpful and friendly. In particular the girls on the front desk were wonderful. Their restaurant recommendations were always spot - on, and nothing we asked for was too much trouble.
The rooms are of a very high standard- with views which is unusual for New York. The bed was very comfortable and the bedding and pillows first class. The bathroom was well thought through with high quality toiletries and a great shower. 
Off the lobby is the attractive lounge area where you can while away time next to the fire or sit out on the terrace. The hotel restaurant is first class too.
This hotel will be my first choice next time in NY.

title: “Nice hotel with great location & good service”
text:
Upon arrival, Pablo @ the front desk was extemely nice & professional.
The hotel is situated very close to the Navy Pier & Michigan Ave/Magnficent Mile both within a walkable distance of about 10 mins. There is a great supermarket/pharmacy/liqour store "Dominick's" located 2 blocks away, which came in handy. Also, the hop on/hop off bus stop is about 1 block and half away in front of the Sheraton. 
The hotel itself feels a bit aged but, well maintained. The rooms are nice & clean. The pool was closed as we visited after labor day.
Overall, it was a good stay for the price we paid in the middle of the convention season!

title: “Beware - not 4 STAR”
text:
Here are the only reasons you should stay at Swissotel in Chicago, if you like:
1 - Hard Beds
2 - Small rooms
3 - Bugs and hairs (not yours) on your bed
4 - Someone else's mascara stain on your blanket
5 - $6.00 bottled water
7 - Construction sights next to your hotel
8 - Going to another floor for ice
9 - Mold/limescale pn the shower (? not sure what it was - I didn't bring my chemistry set). 
Absolutely disappointed in this place. I over paid and was overly displeased!!
On the good side - the bellmen were nice and there is a good view from the pool/fitness center area. But we won't stay there for that.

title: “No surprises”
text:
I'd booked this hotel based on the largely positive reviews on Tripadvisor. 
Having stayed at this hotel, I'd say that the positive reviews from earlier reviews reflected my own experience at this hotel, which was overall very satisfactory. 
The only thing I would have liked to see, which wasn't there, is a security latch on the room door. The lack of a security latch made me a little wary on the first night, in light of an earlier review in which it was reported that the hotel staff had entered the room while the reviewer was sleeping. As it turned out, I had no issues with room security nor hotel staff during my stay. However, the hotel could consider adding a door latch in future, to give its guests greater peace of mind.

title: “You won't regret trying this hotel”
text:
This was a great experience staying at Hotel Fusion.
Customer service was excellent. These guys are focused on making your stay right!
Being a block from Powell St. station was sooooo convenient.
Since our flight was delayed twice the day of arrival, we didn't get in till after midnight SF time. They were very helpful in getting us directed to them and then were waiting for us as we got to the door. 
We wanted a room with two double beds, but they offered us two separate rooms at the same price as one. Worked great. No sharing a bathroom.
Don't worry about no AC you won't need it. There was no street noise from our rooms.
Staff was helpful with everything we asked. Even printed our boarding passes for us before we left. No Charge.
Great concierge too!

title: “Great Place”
text:
We (spouse and two kids) had a very positive stay at this Upper West Side hotel! The rooms (the one-bedroom suite) were relatively spacious and clean, though not luxurious. The sofabed was already made up, which was nice, and there was even an extra cot in the room, which allowed our kids the luxury of not having to share a bed. The kitchenette was nice to have; I walked to Zabar's or H&H Bagel each morning for bagels and croissants (and coffee) for breakfast in our room. I'd agree that the sofabed didn't seem too comfortable (though I got to sleep in the regular bed), but I've never seen a sofabed that is as nice as a regular bed.
The staff was no-nonsense, but very helpful each time I asked for help with directions. They also helped us to arrange for a car service to the airport. They had books and playstation and all sorts of other kid-friendly items, but we were so busy enjoying NYC that we didn't have time to enjoy those activities at the Milburn.
The location was ideal for us - I usually have to stay in midtown when I'm in NYC for business, so it was nice to stay somewhere else; the theater district/midtown would have been way too noisy for my noise-sensitive child. We walked to the Museum of Natural History and to Central Park, and our kids loved taking the subway everywhere else (and the ocassional cab).

title: “Recommended”
text:
Spent a long weekend here. Room was large with a small kitchenette. Very close to everything. Farmers market and the grove are 1/2 mile away. Beverly center is 15 minute walk. Close to freeway access. Swingers diner downstairs is great. Ate both breakfest and dinner there and its good food. 
Beds were comfortable. Room clean. Can't ask for much more

title: “Fair hotel for the price.”
text: The hotel was really nice and the staff was extremely friendly and helpful. We were able to stay on a discounted rated so it was wonderful. I am not sure if I would pay the full price to stay there. We had a corner room which was really neat with the huge glass windows to look at the city. Watch out for the $25 valet fee that is extra and the only parking available.

title: “Great location downtown!”
text:
The Sheraton Downtown is the perfect location if you will be visiting Denver without a car. It is right at the corner of 16th Street where all of the action is. You can walk to many restaurants and bars. There is a shuttle that runs up and down the street all day. We didn't use it but it there are tons of them. 
The hotel layout is very strange. They have two sections. One on either side of the street. We were in the tower so we left the lobby, went under the street and into the tower building. It was confusing at times. 
The rooms are on the small side but clean and well maintained. 
We ordered room service breakfast the last day of our stay. It qualified as a hate crime. Toast, oatmeal, coffee and juice for two was over $50. Everything was cold and inedible.

title: “GOOD LOCATION IN DOWNTOWN PHILLY”
text: This was a last minute priceline reservation. Good - the location was excellent for walking around the historic area. The staff - though in other reviews were considered rude, was very accomodating. Deliah, who checked us in, was very friendly and helpful. The rooms were fine -clean, comfortable, quiet. I was rather surprised that there was no frig or microwave - this is the 5th weekend we have had to travel for sporting events and it is the first time there was no refigerator. Other than that, I paid $105 plus tax which was good, parking was $40 for the weekend,bu that is comparable to other ciites.

title: “Oh. Dear. (Not in a good way.)”
text:
I've traveled in developing countries. I'm down with staying in not-top-notch places; I'm still under 30. It's cool; sometimes that's what available, sometimes that's what the budget is. But this. Dear me. Some things are unacceptable as matters of health, safety, and security.
In that category:
1) No deadbolt on our door. None. Not ok. And keys only... easy to copy keys. Not safe.
2) No safe in our room.
3) Electrical outlets jerry-rigged and looking extremely unsafe - two prong only! The one behind the bed was impossible to reach, but that was probably good, because it might have set me on fire.
4) Air conditioner, which needed some firm whacks to get it going and seemed circa 1984, had enough dust accumulated in it that we seriously debated turning it on. That kind of stuff is gross. And easy to keep clean; no excuse.
5) Security of your personal information: this place is run on a typewriter-and-carbon-paper system. At the front desk, not only can they not do anything quickly, they also risk the security of guest (and credit card!) information. Upgrade this stuff; no excuse.
In the not-security/health risk but still bad:
1) The towels. C'mon. As small as could be, awkward if you're sharing a room with a colleague, but also thin and worn. 
2) Toiletry amenities were kind of vintage-y cute, but insufficient. Thus, not ironically cute. More like you were still in the early 1980s and sort of regretting it.
3) "Breakfast." It belongs in quotation marks, trust me. 
On the plus-ish sides:
1) It was clean enough. The beds were old and dorm-like, mattresses bad, and sheets were not nice, but it seemed clean.
2) Someone has clearly tried hard to decorate with care. It is sort of endearing, because they obviously tried, but you can't make an old YMCA into a Moroccan boutique hotel. It still smells like my college dorm - maybe the grout from the tiles or something? Industrial cleaners? It makes me think "no way will I ever go for 'Moroccan,' because it means 'this stuff is old so we'll make it dark and maybe no one will notice.'"
3) The pool area is nice for a drink - the kitsch works there.
The building is old - own it. Don't try to make it into some weird Moroccan theme. Go with the vintage-YMCA/college dorm feeling. That could bring up a lot of interesting memories for people. But to go Moroccan-esque, it only enhances the impression that one is traveling in a developing country. Upgrade the electrical outlets, door locks, and your reservation/payment system, at a bare minimum. Please.

title: “We'd stay there again”
text:
The Silver Cloud was chosen "blind" from the Internet. It turned out to be a good choice.
Despite not being exactly downtown (it's near the university and major hospitals), the hotel was convenient because ... ta-daaa ... it has a complimentary shuttle service which runs you virtually anywhere within a 5-mile radius -- and that includes all the good tourist bits like Pike Market, waterfront, Pioneer Square, downtown shopping and so on.
The hotel is unpretentious from the outside, but very clean and well maintained inside. It's only a couple of years old and it shows. The rooms still have an almost "new" feel to them. Furniture and fittings are good, solid pieces and the rooms are larger rather than smaller. Air-conditioning was easy to use and effective. There was a complimentary Continental-plus breakfast each morning, which included fresh fruit salad, cereals, yoghurt, waffles, toast and preserves, juice, coffee, hardboiled eggs and a personal favourite -- cream cheese and fresh bagels.
Despite being on a relatively busy intersection, we were never bothered by the traffic, apart from one or two ambulances, but hey ...
'Cayenne', the attached bar/restaurant was a nice place for an evening drink and meal, though some would find it a little "sterile" in its furnishings and once or twice, the noise was a bit much as it reflected off the hard surfaces. That said, the food was freshly cooked, plentiful and reasonably priced.
We enjoyed our stay and, with one slight exception, found the staff to be ultra-helpful and pleasant. There is a very comprehensive spa and exercise room available for guests to use, complimentary and open until late at night.
My wife and I would both stay there again in a flash.

title: “great hosts and lovely location”
text: this hotel is ideally situated on the San Antonio riverside which provides a pleasant antidote to the bustling activity right on the doorstep.
