It was lovely to start the day with a beautifully cooked breakfast and then in the afternoon to enjoy a glass of complementary wine before venturing out for dinner in one of the many good quality local restaurants. The bed was comfortable and clean, and the huge stone shower was ideal. We can strongly recommend this very personal hotel, which was very welcome after a long flight from the UK. It is central yet quiet, and full of creature comforts, such as an in-room goldfish, a teddy bear on the bed, and a rubber duck in the shower room!

title: “Service needs improvement”
text:
We recently stayed at the Clift Hotel for 6 nights. Everything was quite plesant with the exception of a couple of receptionists (We had problems with them from check in till check out) and the door man on Saturday evening. Seems like the female staff were much more professional and helpful compared to the male staff.
Everything seems like such an effort with a few (male) receptionists. When we requested for a queen size bed, he made us fell like he was doing us a huge favor. Even if he really did, perhaps it is not necessary to make it known to the customers. 
The receptionist (male again) was also very unhelpful with my requests for transfer to the airport upon checking out. I ended up making my own arrangements. From my experience, a hotel of this calibre should have more professional and helpful staff to assist customers. 
Returning to the hotel around midnight on Saturday was rather unplesant too. The doorman was impolite; behaving more like a typical door -----; which is what I do not appreciate from a hotel.
Overall, the hard ware is great but the soft ware needs much fine tuning!

title: “Basic Needs, but No Service”
text:
My friend, my 7 year-old son, and I decided to stayed one night here. We are HUGE Big Brother and Survivor Fans and rushed back to the hotel from a day trip to watch our shows. T.V. had terrible reception and called the front desk. She said that we could be moved to a handicap room with one bed but how in the world would three people fit in a bed? I asked if she could send someone to fix-no. I asked if she had "rabbit ears" for the T.V.-no. We had to sit at an angle to see color and watch as the screen skipped for two hours. Disappointed.
Breakfast was chaos with baseball teams. We had to eat in our rooms as did other guests. Mold in places and next to very urban neighborhood. Kept checking on my car...just in case.

title: “Descent Hotel”
text:
This is a decent hotel, reasonably priced in an area that can be extremely expensive to stay.
1 block from Union Square, modern decor, clean, good bed, good breakfast, free wifi - a bit of a funky vibe. 
Negatives would be its a city hotel - its not a warm meet and greet, its perfunctory in all things. Noisy but its on a busy street so to be expected - I had no view and the room was very small - bathroom a terrific size. So no problem on my own it would have been quite cramped for two. But having said that it was easily $100 cheaper than the next decent hotel in a convenient location. If I needed a 1 night stay in a safe, convenient location in SF I would stay here again.

title: “Great Bartender”
text: We stayed here the night before checking into the W Hotel downtown. The bartender (and hotel overall) beat the W by leaps and bounds. The bartender gave us excellent service and he even stayed open later on a Friday night to bring us beer while we relaxed in the hot tub. As a treat for the Bachelorette party we were celebrating he brought us complimentary shots. This is NOT what we expected from a basic hotel on the Interstate. Also, the breakfast was the best we had all weekend. I ordered 2 eggs over hard and it came with steamed fresh asparagus with cherry tomato garnish. Who would have thought?

title: “You might be the victim of an oversell”
text:
I had a reservation at Adante from aug. 14 -19, 2004. Being a single traveler I am not that picky when it comes to the service in a hotel. But I can't just "keep my mouth shut" after being oversold by Adante for my first night of my 5 night stay. They claimed their internet reservations were "hard to control". My only "crime" was being from the East and showing up for check-in at about 8 PM PST (if memory serves).... Well they were nice enough to pay my cab fare to the nearby hotel (for one night) that they transfered me to in a seedy area of Chinatown. I think this illustrates the merits of staying at a "recognized" hotel chain (Marriott, Best Western, Radisson... heck even Days Inn) which Adante is not... And while I do not fly across the continent in order to watch 500 (exagerating of course) TV channels in my hotel room, the ones I do get I expect to have decent cable reception (about 5 of them didn't).
Now for the positives. 
Other than that the staff is friendly, room was comfortable, practical coded in-room safe, accessible internet cafe. Hotel is conveniently located from a variety of restaurants and BART/Cable Car spots.

title: “Wonderful stay!”
text:
Treated my mother to a trip to NYC to celebrate her 60th birthday. I had originally booked another hotel but (thankfully) cancelled that reservation after reading reviews & having discovered this hotel on trip advisor. Although we only stayed one night during the first week in January, the hotel surpassed my expectations! The hotel was beautiful & decorated for the holidays. Everyone from the doormen, concierge (particularly Ruggero - thank you!), and Towers Club staff were helpful & always very courteous! The concierge was aware that we were celebrating my mother's birthday. She was greeted upon our arrival & a thoughtful, small treat & birthday card was sent to our room that night from the hotel.
The room was large & the bed was comfortable. There were Molten Brown toiletries & the best water pressure from the shower from any hotel I've stayed at. The gym had excellent equipment & great view. Towers Club offered a great selection. Hotel location was great & Rockefeller was a short walk.
I had pre-booked another hotel in Times Square to be close to our Broadway show & Macy's, but after our first night we both wished we could have cancelled the reservations at the other hotel. Thank you for making our stay special & memorable! I will return to The Towers at The New York Palace.

title: “Stay away from Parc 55! Valet caused my car windshield to be bashed in! i've uploaded photos to substantiate this”
text:
rooms (good): clean, exactly as pictured in photos from hotel site,
bathroom nice as well. walls were not super thin, so noise wasn't an issue.
price (good): one of the better bang for your buck hotels. our stay was
about $130 per night.
location (great): cant beat the location. a couple minutes walk to union
square and right across the street from bart station.
service (bad): not a single, genuine smile from check in to check out.
parking (horrible): $40/night. no self park, valet only. and this is
where the trip went horribly wrong. after checking out, we waited for valet
to bring our car (from what we later found out is a remote parking lot about
2-3 blocks away). we see our car finally, and the *WINDSHIELD HAS BEEN
BASHED IN!* the valet driver rushes past us without saying a single word
and talks to the valet manager, who says, "are you [--] me?" this is where
it gets good... the driver claimed that 2 pedestrians were arguing near our
car when one of the guys turned around, hit our car with his FIST, cracked
the windshield, and then ran off. SERIOUSLY??? that's the best story you
could come up within 3 blocks worth of time? my take is that the valet
driver probably almost ran someone over and didnt want to tell the truth in
fear of the consequences... and come on, no windshield could be smashed the
way ours was with someone's hand without flesh bits and blood smeared all
over our car. the police came and filed a report, and even they did not
believe the guy. "why didnt you call us at the time of the incident?" they
asked him. he gave no real response. these valet drivers have been trained
to have a police report done ANY TIME there's an incident, so this driver's
failure to abide company policy was quite suspicious to me. but i thot,
"whatever. as long as they can fix this situation and reimburse us, i'll
let bygones be bygones." boy was i wrong...
management (atrocious): i informed the valet manager that we expected to be
reimbursed for the costs of windshield reparation and that i wanted a refund
for my night's stay as compensation for the inconvenience of this whole
ordeal. he said that he would have to talk to the hotel manager about this.
 fine. 45 minutes later, the hotel manager came up to me and said, "so i
hear you expect a refund." WOW no introductions, no apology, no
explanation.. nothing. she claims that the hotel should not be responsible
for the actions of its valet department... ooo-kayy. and the timeline for
reimbursement for the windshield supposedly is indefinite as such claims are
in yet another department that is third party. allllrighty then.
conclusion: so it's been about 4 months and about 20 phone calls had been
made harassing management for reimbursement since the incident. the check
for windshield reimbursement finally arrived and cleared a couple days ago.
 so the last thing i must do to FULLY right this wrong is to write a
horrible review of the hotel. PARC 55 IS HORRIBLE AND HAS NO SENSE OF HOW
TO DO BUSINESS AT ALL. if you do decide to stay here, god help you. pray
every night that nothing bad happens, because if it does they will do close
to nothing to justify the wrong.

title: “Close to the Convention Center”
text:
Spent time in Indianapolis for convention. The best thing about the Westin is it's location to the convention center. You could be on a 15 minute break and make it up to your room and back to conference room in the convention center. The lobby is nice, has comfortable feel with good lighting and nice spots to read a book. The workout area and pool area are great, plenty of space and equipment. 
Down sides of my stay. The front desk staff was somewhere between rude and acknowledging I was there. You need a room key to go up the elevators, I lost my room key in the gym, had to go down to the front desk for a new key. This was a challenge and wasted a good portion of my morning. The room itself is not very well lit, the bathroom is small and lacks a fan. Since the bathroom does not have a fan, mold is on the ceiling. 
For down time leave the hotel, left on Washington st. will take you down to the river walk.

title: “convenient to javits center”
text:
yotel is a very good place to stay so that you can walk to javits center- the rooms are small, but contain everything you need. the rooms are well thought out and have windows that open which are important to me.
the weekend i was there was very rainy so I assume there were more people dining in the hotel than usual- i write this because the service at the restaurant ( for dinner ) was poor.
i think they also need a little more front desk help

title: “What were these people thinking?”
text: Yeah i read all the other reviews before going, not a good idea since it was not even close to what some reviewer said about this place, I waited for something to go wrong but everything was just perfect, sure the rooms are small but what do you really do in the room anyway but *&%^*^ and sleep, The staff was great answering any questions and the hotel atmosphere and decor was outstanding, dont read all the crap that others say, go for yourself and experience the excitement that this hotel offers.

title: “Great Hotel, just off the main "U" of the Riverwalk”
text:
Wonderfully clean, neat hotel. All remodeled. Spacious rooms with living room area. Good view of the river. Safe. Free parking. Hotel personnel was always kind and helpful. The food was good too! Quick service food via touch panel in the guest kitchen. Went to the complimentary computers to check my e-mail while the food was being prepared. An employee came to get me to tell me it was ready. She didn't know I was there - she searched for me! Morning breakfast with Starbucks coffee very good way to start off the day. Staff helpful when asked where to find certain places in the city. In fact, they came running out to my car to give me better directions when they realized it. All staff greeted me as if I was coming home when walking in the lobby. Great pool. Warm and clean. Within walking distance to almost everything. We even walked two blocks to pick up our Enterprise Rental. The street out front was busy, but manageable when we when touring in our vehicle. Actually quite an amazing area. The Riverwalk in back of the hotel was well lit so we could come back from the main area of the Riverwalk at night. It actually felt more safe than the street level. The street level had quite a few people waiting for buses. Never felt unsafe, just out of my element. Was only approached by two pan handlers, but never near my hotel, only on the riverwalk.
I would stay there again definitely.

title: “Disappointed with wait time”
text: It looks an hour was 20 minutes to checking in after long driving. on the reservation including complementary parking, but after I come back from dinner the staff wanted to park on the street. Bathroom fan noise is so loud from the next level.

title: “Great Service”
text: Everything was clean and comfortable, but the best part were the people. The front desk workers were so helpful about any of our needs. Sometimes helpful people make the stay just right.

title: “Nice but small rooms”
text: Rooms were clean and nice but kind of dated and on the small side. Getting ready in the morning was hot and steamy as there was no exhaust fan in the bathroom. They served a continental breakfast which was nice in the morning. When we booked the room they didn't mention that it was valet only parking for $32.00 so that was an extra charge we hadn't planned on. Probably would not stay here again in the future.

title: “Great location and they upgraded our room too”
text: Right there at the El Paso Airport the location couldn't be better, and when we gor there (after a whole day of travel) they upgraded our room.... so nice

title: “understated elegance”
text:
We have stayed at the Andaz twice within the past six months. We had such an enjoyable experience our first time around that we decided to return when I celebrated by birthday this past March.
The hotel is trendy with an understated modern elegance. The staff is extremely efficient and personable. The hotel is a converted prewar building and therefore the rooms are large with high ceilings (especially the lofts) and the bathrooms are large and very well appointed. I also like the fact that there was no additional charge for wifi internet and non-alcoholic mini bar items.
It's fifth avenue location is very convenient to Central Park, shopping and the theater district.
My wife and I have been traveling to NYC frequently for years and this is by far the best place we have stayed.

title: “You can't exist on name alone.”
text:
I found a place on Earth where the laws of physics cease to exist: room 3322 at the Fairmont Chicago. Let me explain. Upon check in my room was hot. I hate being hot. I cannot sleep when I'm hot. I'm irritable when I'm hot. The outside temps while I was in Chicago were upper 40s to lower 50s during the day and upper 30s to lower 40s at night. Why was the room so hot??? I found the thermostat on the wall. You can adjust the temp down or up and the fan speed down or up. I turn the temp down to 60 (lowest it will go) and the fan speed to high. This resulted in a tiny little trickle of air dribbling out of a tiny vent in the wall that looked like it was about to fall out. This was clearly not going to cool the room off. Suprisingly, the room had two windows that cracked open at the bottom around 5 inches. I opened both of them. It's cold outside. The wind is blowing fiercely. Surely my room will be cold in no time. Nope, it barely made a dent. What in the world is going on? I felt like I was the victim of a practical joke. 
Moving on... 
Hotel managers need to understand that people care more about being able to control their room temp than whether or not the soap came from some boutique where rich people would shop. 
Hotel managers also need to understand that putting a gross, scratchy coverlet and boudoir pillows upholstered in gross, scratchy material on the bed is a waste of time. They get thrown on the floor, and they never get washed. People want a nice, CLEAN bed. 
Overall, the room was nicely designed in modern, low key decor. The bathroom was nice, appointed in marble. Seperate shower and tub. Although, i did find a clump of hair in the bath tub that was not mine because I didn't take a bath, and I don't have any hair on my body that was that long or that color. If I'm dropping $300 on a room, I better not find anyone else's hair in the room. I know the cleaning staff has to be very thorough to accomplish this, but what the hell? It's the Fairmont right? It's $300 a night right? That's a freakin car payment. Clean the rooms!
You ever notice how the higher the room rate, the more you have to pay out of pocket for simple stuff. I'm paying several hundred dollars a night and you can't float me a cup of coffee and a stale doughnut??? Hell, $60-100 a night hotels give you a damn buffet in the morning or at least a cup of coffee and some breads. It's not the highest quality, but it's hot and contains caffeine. I've stayed in a $700 a night hotel, and they had a very nice, free breakfast including fresh yogurt and berries. Maybe the middle ground is where you get screwed, or maybe it's stingy ownership? 
Hotel feel: They're attempting to be as hip as possible while still being low key. The result is one of the darkest hotels I've ever been in. The lobby was lit like a club, and they even played some sort of ambient yet upbeat techno in the mornings I guess to get people pumped for the day. I don't know. The rooms were also very dark. You could turn on every light in your room, and it would still look someone turned on a couple of weak lamps. I don't like pooping in the dark.
Location: boring. There is a CVS across the street, which is nice if you can't afford a $5 mini bar Coke. It is one block north of Millennium Park, one block east of Michigan and one block south of the Chicago River and Whacker, but it felt so removed from the action. I'd much rather be on Michigan or around the corner from Michigan or on the river. I guess I'm being picky, but there are tons of hotels in Chicago that have much better locations and are probably much less expensive.
My view was nice, The room faced east so you could see Lake Michigan and a nice little park that bordered the University of Chicago. I would have preferred a south facing room to see the museum campus and Michigan Ave. I've never really considered Lake Michigan around Chicago very pretty.
Overall, you can spend this much and do much better IMHO. Do you research. Don't swoon over the Fairmont name. At least not at this location.

title: “Another Great Stay at the Sheraton Suites”
text: The last time I stayed at this property was in 2005 and it was a wonderful then as much as it is now. The staff is friendly and very accomodating, we were upgraded to the club level which provided appitizers at 5pm and breakfast in the morning. The room was comfortable and love the suite sleeper bed. Close to everything downtown and the parking is only $23 for the night. The Sheraton Suites provides the bang for your buck!

title: “Excellent location, great hotel!”
text:
We were debating between Santa Monica, Malibu, Beverly Hills and Hollywood, and after seeing all these on our trip, we couldn't have been happier that we ended up choosing this hotel. It was an excellent location for what we were interested in seeing. It is literally across the street from the Kodak Theater, Graumans Chinese Theatre, Starline Tours, and Madame Tusauds. It is on the walk of fame as well. 
We booked a cabana room with patio. I asked for an upgrade, which they easily obliged. We got a cabana room with balcony. The room was modern rustic with hardwood floors, dim lighting and a very comfy platform bed. It overlooked the nice pool area and Tropicana bar. 
My gripes: We checked in at 2:15 and they said they would call me when the room was ready. I never got a call, even by 6:30p, so we went back after seeing some sites. They apologized, but this was unprofessional. $30 for valet was not fun, especially when certain valets acted like they were more like club bouncers. Tips on our end were minimal to say the least. We tried to avoid it by pulling into the parking lot next to the hotel, but the signs indicated it was not entirely public parking, so you are kinda stuck with valet if you have a car at this hotel. Although retro and cool, the lighting in the room was not the best for seeing yourself, packing etc. I need some area with a bright light. Apparently, there is a club there called Teddys that is frequented by celebs and such. We thought about going, but were too tired and heard or overheard how hard it would be to get into.. I overheard the valet saying this to some Australian guys and the guys commented that there should be some sort of courtesy given to guests. I agree. 
This hotel is perfect for active, partying early 20s and possibly up to hip 40 year olds. I am 33 and would take my husband or girlfriends here, but not my parents or child. There were no kids in sight, and you can expect some noise if you are by the pool and some possible disruptions of the drunk partiers in the wee hours. However, it was not extreme or anything. Also, the hall wreaked of Mary Jane on one of the nights....must of been CA's medical MJ users. We were out and about most of the day and part of the night. Even with my gripes, the compliments outweigh them and I'd certainly consider staying here again.

title: “Excellent Hotel, Great Location”
text:
We stayed here in July 2010 for a week, the hotel is in an excellent location with Times Square and the Empire State Building within walking distance.
The hotel had a diner onsite called the Tick Tock Diner which was open 24 hours the food was brilliant and it was really well priced.
The rooms were lovely and clean and a great size, they were cleaned daily.
All the staff were very friendly and couldnt do enough to help.
Would stay here again in a heartbeat...

title: “Just what the Doctor ordered ....”
text: We needed a couple of days to just relax and de-stress. Beautiful hotel and rooms, good breakfast, coffee 24/7.Friendly and Knowledgeable staff .Wonderful stay, will stay there again. Well done, Thanks

title: “Unbelievable”
text:
I went Greenwich Hotel for 3 nights and was amazing !!! The neighborhood its the best with great options of restaurants, design stores and spas.
The service was a real boutique hotel, very personal but informal !!! I love !!! All the doors men are very polite and helpful. The front desk people was unbelievable helpful too !!! Everything was so perfect... the room was enormeous and very cute! My only complain was the bed floor, was made with wood and very noise when walk through - and its ok if you will be alone in the room... but a problem if you share. 
I definitely recomend the Greenwich Hotel for everyone !!!

title: “Absolutely horrible! Run don't walk from registering here!”
text: I am writing - at nealy midnight - because I can not sleep at Crescent Hotel SF. There is an incredibly loud band playing which at registration was booked as playing for a "hotel anniversary from 5-9pm". It is now 11:45pm. The room is too hot, If the window is opened the noise is even louder although that seems nearly impossible. And the pitch for "free wireless" should not be mistaken to mean "highspeed". The front desk person with whom I spoke can not and will not do anything but "pass on the information to management." He informed me the band will play until 1:30 am and that the heat can not be turned down due to the type radiator system they have, Although the room appears clean, I would not recommend this hotel,

title: “New York Home”
text:
Loved this hotel ! The staff were amazing, especially Omar.
The bar Basque with Tatum Greenblatt on Wed night playing trumpet was such a New York experience. We were there for the New York wine and food festival and stayed for 6 nights.
I have stayed at other New York hotels that were more money, but not as quiet and friendly.
The beds and bedding were sooooo comfy. Highly recommend this hotel!

title: “Unless you're just going to pass out after a game-shop around before booking (Full Review- Long)”
text:
An actual review, hope it is helpful to some of you. A few weeks ago we took a road trip to Indy for a weekend getaway. When we go on weekend getaways we often book the first night in a room with a whirlpool tub, because after driving for 3+ hrs, few things feel as good as relaxing in a whirlpool tub to soothe your aching back. So, we were pleased to find this holiday inn express has whirlpool rooms and there was one available for a rate comparable to other downtown hotels (I believe it was $179 online before taxes/fees, etc.) 
We made the drive, and GPS had no problem finding the hotel, but we did go through some interesting areas, including dark alleys, to get to the parking lot. The parking lot was attached to the hotel, was reasonably well lit, and half-empty when we arrived at 9:00pm. We were also excited to see that the hotel is directly across the street from Lucas Stadium. Unfortunately, it appears that Lucas Stadium is the only non-industrial building within a considerable distance of the hotel. There is some sort of a pub around the corner, but it was closed, even though it was a weekend night and there were only large, nondescript industrial buildings and warehouses around, which didn't bode well for us as we were tired, hungry, and looking forward to checking in, having dinner and relaxing in the tub.
When we checked in we found out we would be charged an additional $12 to park in the hotel lot. I thought this was odd considering we were staying as paying guests overnight, and there was no event taking place at the stadium across the street, but I decided that $12 was reasonable to have our car stay in the adjoining lot, rather than having to drive around in the dark looking for someplace else to put it. (It should be noted however, that with the additional charge for parking, this hotel is priced within the range of nearby, nicer 4* hotels with free parking.) 
When we asked the clerk about getting dinner nearby, he referred us to a number of menus on the counter for places that delivered. Unfortunately, he explained, most of them had already closed because it was 9 PM, and there isn’t any place within walking, or a short driving distance to eat. This was a serious problem. I grabbed the list of restaurants and the menus, thanked the clerk, and went upstairs to the room. 
Our room was clean and nicely decorated in typical midrange hotel furnishings, had no odors, and plenty of seating. The whirlpool tub was large enough for two people, was clean, and in a separate nook. Out the window we could see the large, dark, brick behemoth that is Lucas Stadium, and soon found that from our room we were perfectly within earshot of a number of Harley motorcycles with open pipes, and several economy cars with bass bins in their trunks. By 2 AM, this began to really get old, however I eventually realized the reason why these gentlemen were driving in front of the hotel over and over and loudly revving their engines, and booming their subwoofers. In a manner similar to the activity of adolescent males attempting to break wind louder than each other, these people were conducting a sort of physics experiment in acoustics. You see, the hotel, is directly across the street from Lucas Stadium and forms an enormous corridor within which loud noises are contained, and sounds reverberate off of the two large buildings. And since the only things separating these two buildings are a narrow street and parking areas (one of which will cost you 12 bucks) there is nothing to obstruct, or reduce this noise. Since few things entertain a young male with an IQ on the far left side of the bell curve as much as making ridiculous amounts of noise yes, noise is a big problem. But not as big of a problem as finding something to eat…
After we got settled, we fired up the laptop, connected to wireless (which worked flawlessly) and began attempting to find a place that would feed us. In short, I will advise you that if you intend to stay at this hotel overnight, you MUST eat before you arrive (which will require you to be in Indianapolis before 8:30 PM) or bring a sack lunch, some granola bars, beef jerky, something... Marcos, Bazbeauxs, Donatos, and nearly everyplace else, stops delivery and closes by 9pm (How do these guys stay in business, really? If the owners of any of these places are ever heard complaining about sales/numbers being down, someone, please slap them in the head for me.) The remaining establishments: Hotbox, Indy all-night, and others have reviews on review sites can only nicely be described as "mixed." By the time we located a place that was open, and could deliver, whose drivers weren’t serial killers, it was after 10 and we were starving. We ordered from a large chain. Our thinking was that by ordering from a large, established, corporate chain, we would get a standard, unexciting, but nonthreatening, established, corporate food in a reasonable amount of time. We were wrong. The dominoes guy on the phone said our pizza would arrive in “26 to 36 minutes.” Not 25 to 37, but 26 to 36 minutes. The Dominoes delivery promptly arrived an hour and a half later. The "pizza" was cold, limp and gelatinous, and missing toppings we paid for, and the “boneless wings” were cold chicken nuggets with a plastic cup of orange, sour smelling liquid to dip them in. And what a deal for $25!
After choking down this "food," we filled and fired up the whirlpool. The whirlpool was deep enough to submerge fully, and made plenty of noise, but the only jet that appeared to be displacing water was the one near my right foot. This was frustrating. Thankfully, my partner in crime figured out that the jets could be opened and closed individually. (Here's a hint, 10 counterclockwise turns of the whirlpool jet will open it.)
After a long soak, we headed to bed. The bed was firm, and the sheets were scratchy like unwashed and new, and like many hotels have decided to do these days, there were both firm and soft pillows provided, but all of them were smaller than standard pillows. I don't know who is responsible for placing these stupid little pillows in hotels, but I wish they would stop. If I wanted to sleep on toss pillows, I would stay home and sleep on the couch. (Actually, the pillows on the couch in the room were larger than the pillows on the bed.) I finally shoved three of the Chicklet pillows together, and tried to get some rest, because the Harley guys finally found something else to do, or someone else to annoy around 2:15 AM.
At 3:30 AM, after tossing and turning and removing each layer of bed linen one at a time, I realized I was uncomfortably warm. I had set the air conditioner on high cool earlier, but half-asleep, and now covered in sweat, I stumbled over to the air conditioner and realized that the air blowing into the room was warm. Despite of the complaints from the other side of the bed, I turned on the light and began fiddling with the AC. No matter what I did compressor would not kick on. Someone else previously had a problem with this air conditioner too, because the knob to adjust the temperature was stripped and came off in my hand, and the metal ac cover was loose. I hadn't noticed any problem with the air conditioner earlier, but now the heat in the room was unbearable. The thermometer on our portable ice chest read 82°. 
So, 3:45 in the morning, I pulled on my clothes and made my way to the front desk. I explained to the clerk that the air conditioner wasn't working, and that it was unbearably warm in the room. He explained that he had no other whirlpool rooms available, and offered me a fan. I explained that I didn't care what kind of room he had available, I just needed a room with a working air conditioner in order to get some sleep. Thankfully, he found us another room on the same floor. So, we packed up our stuff and dragged it to the other room, where the air conditioner was working and the room was cool. It dawned on me as I climbed into the new scratchy bed that we needed to find out what time check-out was, because we probably weren't going to get much sleep. I was extremely disappointed to find out that check out is 11 AM!
Four or Five hours later, I awoke to the sound of someone furiously pounding a fist on a door. “HOUSEKEEPING!!!” had arrived to clean a room across the hall. I covered my head with a Chicklet pillow, and tried to get more sleep, but it was no use. We slowly drank hotel room coffee, showered, got dressed and made our way downstairs. During our brief sleeping period, we had missed the “complimentary” breakfast, so we would need to go and seek out food yet again. This time however, we had a wonderful meal not too far from the hotel at a place called Patachou downtown. We had to pay to park in a garage, and walk three blocks in the rain, but our meals were excellent, and the service was even better.
So, recommendations in case you intend to stay at this hotel to see a game at Lucas Stadium (because there is absolutely no other reason to stay in this hotel, ever) include: eat someplace before you get here and/or bring some MRE’s or something that can be reconstituted with tap water from the sink or something, bring an adult sized pillow, bring earplugs, bring a fan, and try not to stay up too late because breakfast ends early and check out is at the crack of 11…

title: “Perfect Location / Perfect Price”
text:
OK, so this isn't the Waldorf Astoria...it's not supposed to be. But the location is PERFECT for anyone heading out on one of the vessels at the Landings right there practically in the parking lot!
The rooms were clean, roomy and just perfect for the night! If you're heading out do do some deep sea fishing from H&M Landing...this is the place to be! 
I had called after making my reservation to change it to a handicapped room, as I had to bring my daughter at the last minute, and they were very accomodating. The hadicapp room was perfect for us!

title: “Convention comfort”
text:
Of course I picked the only rainy week in Austin in forever... but running across the street to the convention center in the rain made me wish for a tunnel/ skywalk or something. 
Nice location, very convenient to 6th street area, decent breakfast restaurants. 
Now the bad part: The hotel nickel and dimes you but that's what I have come to expect in high end hotels. The internet in the rooms cost $12/day which is why the lobbey is filled with people on laptops. I wonder if their service was better. Parking is $18/day and if you dare to self park, be prepared to haul your luggage because all parking near the elevator is for the valeted cars. No you cannot park in the front during check in unless you valet. Another word of caution. If you are checking out on a football Saturday, have nerves of steel when you attempt to exit the garage... and then don't expect to go anywhere. People drive like maniacs.

title: “$7 Weekend Rate Parking 3 blocks away”
text:
You can't miss this hotel when you drive around the City Hall, but when we arrived, we quickly get a porter and unload all the luggage and after checked in, get all luggage into room, then back to the car and do self parking, why? valet will cost you $32, and it may take forever, so crowd and so small the entrance.
Dahammer told me the fantacy of this JFK Plaza Parking, 3 blocks away under the Love Park, $7 weekend rate that you can park from after 5pm Friday all the way to 9am Monday!!!
Not to many cars there but we chat with the security guards their to make sure everything is fine, and it did!! Then we had a nice tour walking around the stores, checking around Marriott next door (wow! $35 valet parking!) and of course pick up some tour info at next door Residence Inn and bought Dunkin Donut next to it... Hey! we seems to follow all TripAdvisors' tips!!!
Except when we got in our room, we set up our wireless router to get wonderful wireless Internet so that we can have our multiple portable all online ... Our room at 15th floor got wonderful view ...
The room is a big surprise that is the same as other Courtyard, except the ceiling is 10 to 12 foot high.
Got up the first thing is go get the car and came back to pick up the rest of family and lugguages. I am glad that I did self parking, so many people in the lobby, waiting for their cars ...
Then we went to Kimmel Center to join their 1pm free tour and park free at Lombard and Juniper, no meter need on Sundays. The theater is great! Then we went to Franklin's Court on 2nd St area, that is "undergrand"!!! Amazing! never found it till now ...
By the way, the pool is not at 5th floor as someone said, it is 1st floor. Also, that there is a very nice Tour Book in room, may be they read TripAdvisor's comment before and changed ...
I read all the reviews of TripAdvisor about this hotel before I went, and I have found this most important info that I can share is Dahammer's parking tip. By the way, along city hall and court house, the street need goverment people to be able to park. On the way walking back to hotel, I asked each and everyone I saw parking there ...
Dahammer's even best parking tip is $5 weekend rate at 1540 Vine St near 16th St and Spring, but it would be 6 blocks from this hotel, so I just use JFK Plaza one off Arch and 15th.
Comparing to the parking deck behind Courtyard that valet parking used for $23 vs valet parking $32. This $7 and $5 whole weekend parking is a great deal!!! Yes, they are very safe, they are parking deck with security guard and all doors are Exit ONLY, except the ones in front ...

title: “THIS WAS A GREAT PLACE TO STAY”
text: I would stay here again breakfast was good lots of variety breakfast area was clean as well A.Room was verry clean WAS A PLEASURE TO BE THERE AT A BUDGET PRICE VERRY EASY TO FIND

title: “Wonderful!”
text: From the doorman to the concierge and the front desk staff, this hotel was lovely. Room service was wonderful, even at 3 a.m. Albert at the front desk was so helpful and nice as was Rene the concierge. The food at the restaurant was delicious, the service very good. Our room was impecably clean, as was the bathroom. We have stayed there a few times, and would not even consider staying anywhere else. The location is fabulous, as well.

title: “Interesting Taste of Old New York Living”
text:
This hotel is bursting with charm and personality. It was a "Gentlemen's Rooming House" in it's hayday, a century ago. It is a rare treat to be able to stay in a building like this, with it's interesting staircase and hardwood floors. The beautiful library and 24 hour coffee service is a delight. 
It was a nice touch, and much appreciated, to be handed a bottle of water upon check-in.
The bedding was of a nice quality and it was changed everyday (many hotels are now cutting corners on this service).
The room was clean and adequate, but there is no place for coats or dresses, as the closet is only half length due to the (un-needed) minibar. A couple of hooks on the wall would be a very welcome and inexpensive addition.
My only other complaint is that the lighting in the room was extremely inadequate. Again, this would seem to be an easy and inexpensive fix. There are lamps, which provide direct lighting, but there is no indirect lighting, which gives the room a depressing and "cheap" feel. It appears that they probably paid big bucks for a professional designer to pull everything together. I always think it would be a great idea for a designer of a space to actually live in it for a night or two, to get a perspective. If that were the case, there would probably be much better lighting in the room.
The staff seem professional, but unlike most NY Hotels I have stayed, they do not acknowledge guests with the niceties of "Good Mornings" or "Welcome Back". As I write this, it seems a bit petty on my part, but it was something I noticed at the time. I think "detached" is the word I would use.
 Be prepared to hoist your baggage up the 4 or 5 steps at the front entrace, as the doorman is not always there (to be fair, they are hard-working and are usually helping other guests to their rooms). I think it may just be a shortage of help.
Overall, for the location and the price, this is a winner!

title: “Great start to a perfect honeymoon”
text:
We stayed at The Handlery for 4 nights from 1st September, our first port of call on our 3 week honeymoon in the U.S. My parents had emailed the hotel to let them know that we were arriving and were on our honeymoon. When we arrived the man behind the desk was so welcoming and polite and congratulated us before we went off to our room, to find that they had upgraded our 'regular historic room' up to what can only be explained as a 'Suite'! Huge for a city hotel! We were welcomed to a bottle of sparkling wine on ice and a bag of snacks and water...perfect after our 11 hour flight! Later on, getting back to our room after a day out, we found a message on the answerphone from the owner of the hotel, welcoming and congratulating us, and apologising that he wasn't available to welcome us when we arrived! Little things like this - that we really didn't expect, or need - made us really feel special and set our honeymoon apart from any other holiday.
The room, staff & The Daily Grill - All perfect, a brilliant start to our honeymoon! We hope to visit San Francisco again in the future, and would definitely consider staying at the Handlery again. The location of this hotel is great!

title: “Hotel ZaZa ..... AWESOME!!!!”
text:
I organized our company retreat this last week at ZaZa. WOW! Everything turned out so great. We had excellent service from the front desk staff, banquet staff, and everyone we came in contact with. The meeting room was such a nice setting for our retreat. We also utilized the spa onsite for everyone's massages. 
My entire staff thanked me for making all the arrangements at the hotel. I will definitely be back for personal getaways! 
Thanks to Marla in the sales office who did an amazing job taking care of my group!!!

title: “One of our BEST hotel experiences ever . . . can't wait to return!”
text:
More than any hotel I've ever seen, the San Carlos seems to inspire a "love it" or "hate it" type response; no one seems to be neutral. Well, put me down in the "LOVE it" category!
My wife and I spent 4 nights there back in June while we were in Phoenix for a convention and would gladly have made it 4 WEEKS if we could have! We loved everything about the hotel!
Having read the reviews on here, we were braced for the worst--but were pleasantly surprised in every regard! 
From the moment we arrived, the staff could not have been any more helpful or accommodating! After one minor mix-up, they more than compensated for that by giving us complimentary breakfast vouchers for the duration of our stay. When we expressed interest one night in trying a particular restaurant elsewhere in Phoenix (several miles away), the staff printed out directions for us & were eagerly awaiting our return later that night to hear our impressions of the restaurant; on another occasion, they took care of arranging a cab for us, etc. Extremely helpful and accommodating in every regard!
Our room was far more spacious than the reviews here had led me to expect--and beautifully decorated and appointed! The central air (which you almost never find in newer hotels) was an especially nice surprise. There was a brief period one night when my wife complained of hearing noise from the neighbors (I myself was out at the time) but that was it; neither of us ever noticed any disturbance whatsoever the entire rest of the time. In fact, everything about our stay at the San Carlos was about as restful, tranquil, and peaceful as could be imagined!
As others have mentioned, the location of the hotel is ideal: not only is there a light rail stop right outside the doors, we were within easy walking distance (5 min. or so) of the convention center and MANY fine restaurants! We didn't have a bad meal the entire week! Also walked to an AZ Diamondbacks game one night.
If you enjoy getting away from the cookie-cutter sameness of modern chains and are up for a place with a real history, vintage feel, distinctive character, and loads of charm--then the Hotel San Carlos is just the ticket! We have nothing but warm and wonderful memories of our week there and would gladly have stayed far longer if we could have!
Our convention will be meeting in Phoenix once again in about 5 years and we have every intention of staying at the San Carlos next time around also if there's any way possible; we're already looking forward to a return visit!

title: “Your Best Choice on Shelter Island”
text:
Stayed at the hotel many times. It is by far the best Best Western I've ever encountered. The staff is fantastic, the restaurant is great, and the prices are reasonable. You can't beat the location and they have their own Marina. I do not like the fact that the hotel and marina do not package rooms and boat slips together. The marina prices for transient slips are very high. $60.00 a day for a 26 foot boat. 
They even have a pool bar.....when's the last time you saw that at a Best Western? 
My only complaint for this trip is the low quality pool towels. They are only big enough for a small child. Island Palms, if you're reading this, spring for some decent pool towels! 
Rooms are very clean and the new side of the hotel can compete with the local Marriot for quality and decor. 
This is the place you want to stay if you are planning on going to a concert at Humphrey's. You don't have to worry about parking, and you can walk to the concert in just a couple of minutes.

title: “Pleasently Suprised”
text:
I used Sidestep the reservation came through worldres.
I have stayed in about 40 different hotels in San Francisco, but never anything outside of Downtown. I didn't stay downtown due to a convention at the Moscone center. I thank the convention for helping me find this hotel.
The Great Highway Inn came as a nice suprise. 
The G.H Inn is 1 & 1/2 blocks off of the "N" Judah tram line, and is a very easy walk, to access anything in the city. I took the walk both evenings after sunset and felt at ease due to lighting and the numbers of other people useing the same walkng areas.
With exception to early evening traffic the Hotel is in a very quiet area. Quiet is something unheard of in downtown SF. Parking is free at G.H.Inn. There is a free shuttle to UCSF Medical Center. There is an on site restaurant.
The room amenities are not what those demanding special treatment, or being treated like king will expect, but the are what you need. If you want snacks you will have to go to a nearby store and get them. That takes a bit of thinking ahead while riding the "N" line where there are many choices. Ice is available in the office.
The room was clean, quiet and comfortable. I heard NO noise from adjoining rooms and had two very good nights of sleep. I am easily awakened and had no problems at the Great Highway Inn.
I mentioned in my reservation that I had some health problems and would be using the shuttle and would like a ground floor room. What I got was what I asked for.
Cudos to the Great Highway Inn.

title: “Everything I expected”
text: Worth the visit. Beds were comfortable - Star Bucks in the lobby. Great place to stay

title: “Fine Line”
text:
There is a fine line between hip and cheesy and the line is drawn right down the middle of this hotel. 
I felt like I was staying in a Saturday Night Live skit...Night at the Roxbury meets Deiter the uber hip German. They try so hard to be hip but if you have to try, it just isn't hip.

title: “Quirky, friendly and a great place to stay”
text:
We have stayed in hundreds of hotels but were bowled over by this place. We got lucky and were upgraded to room 439 and what a lovely room.
The staff are all friendly, the free wine is actually pretty good and the fact they don't really have a restaurant ( Aruga the adjacent restaurant is not worth the bother with so many fine eateries nearby) is a plus as you are incentivised to go look elsewhere and explore.

title: “Southern Hospitality at its Finest!”
text: Last month I had the opportunity to travel to Austin Texas for a conference, and I am pleased to say that the Barton Creek Resort and Spa made it a memorable first trip to the great state of Texas! From the moment we arrived, we felt like we were staying in a southern manor house. The wood floors and decor have a warm, comfortable feel to them, and the employees with their "yes ma'am" manners made us feel like we were valued guests. The manor house theme extended to our large guest room, and everything was such charming southern style, it was hard to believe that we were in a hotel and not in someones home! Barton Creek is so proud of their state, and it was great to see that pride in their old photos of Texas that were hung throughout the hotel, the amazing Remington bronze sculptures, and even the lone star carpeting that they had! I would not hesitate to return to this wonderful resort and how they so proudly represent Texas is to be commended!

title: “Best service experience ever”
text:
As long as you like your bed a little on the hard side, this is an excellent choice for visiting LA tourist destinations. We stayed here for our first trip to the city and it is a great starting out point to drive to all things to do. 
The manager and all desk staff are very professional and helpful. They truly care if you are enjoying your stay which can hardly be said at most hotels these days. The breakfast and nightly reception made it an even more pleasant stay.

title: “Just average”
text: Stayed here in November with a friend. Got a good deal considering it was the week of the Formula 1 race in Austin (which for some reason spills over into San Antonio) and every hotel was WAY overpriced. Even though the hotel is close to the riverwalk, the area of the hotel seems somewhat questionable...its definitely not in the main touristy area. My friend and I had a car, so we did not have to walk to and from the riverwalk. I would definitely not do the walk at night! Ironically, there is a Ruths Chris Steak House (a higher end restaurant) very nearby, so maybe it is a neighborhood in tranasition. There is also free parking on site. The buidling is very well kept and appears to have been renovated (or at least painted) recently. The hotel is clean, quiet and the rooms are spacious. The rooms have a very nice contemporary rustic decor. One concern with the room was the temperature...it would get up to 81 degrees at night for no apparent reason (weather outside was mild) so we found it necessary to sleep with the very loud airconditioning unit on. The hotel is run by an Indian or Pakistani family. Unfortunately they were not very warm. And sometimes their children are left to tend the front desk, which can result in not being able to get your questions answered. And on the day we checked out, we asked to leave our luggage so we could go do more sightseeing. They agreed to allow to do so, but upon our return to pick up our luggage around 12:30pm, we realized that no one was tending the front desk (and maybe even the hotel!)...The owners had left to a party, so we could not get our luggage. Luckily they had left a phone number on the desk, so I called it and had to wait for about 20 minutes for them to return. In the mean time, another family arrived to check in and had to wait as well. When the owners did arrive, they didnt even apologize or offer an explanation. In terms of food, they offer a small continental breakfast with prepackaged pastries, bananas, apples, and coffee. They also sell water, softdrinks and snacks. Coffee maker is available in room as well.

title: “Great Off Season Surprise”
text:
The room had obviously been updated. It was clean and modern looking. It had a granite counter at the sink, which was in the room. The separate toilet & shower had a window. We looked directly out to the ocean, over the pool, and watched surfers in our spare time.
In season, summers and breaks, it's probably crowded and noisy. But it was quiet and half empty in April.
I always have a problem with hard beds and this was no different, it was too hard for comfort. Other than that, we were happy with our stay there.

title: “Great Hotel, Great Staff and Great Location”
text:
This hotel is very nice as well as spotlessly clean. The location is perfect as it is near the Wharf with all its great attractions plus fresh seafood. Also, public transportation is nearby.
We walked to Alkatraz Landing for our tour, to Union Square, up Lombard Street and down by the waterfront in both directions as there is lots to see. There is a Maritime Museum well worth a stop nearby and a nice park a bit further on. We walked to all these, but one would not need to as there is a variety of transport options and maps everywhere. 
The staff couldn't have been nicer, starting with the concierge. He was most helpful, booking our Monterrey tour and airport shuttle for us. He also told us that we could get a transportation pass at the camera counter at Safeway across the street, which we did. He gave us lots of pointers about the area and maps. A very nice and gentle man, indeed. 
For our city tour, we took the Hop on Hop Off Bus and road in the top, so we could have the nice views of the city and its charms, including Golden Gate Bridge. We thought it was a good choice and the ticket is good for 24 hours.
Our room was spacious, but even more importantly, quiet. It had a very comfortable bed and a little bar fridge where we kept a few groceries and snacks which we picked up from Trader Joe's and Safeway, both of which are nearby. 
The wine reception at 5:00 was a nice touch, for sure. 
We found the hotel restaurant too noisy for our tastes, so only ate there once. We, however, did not find one restaurant on the Wharf that we didn't like. The food was excellent and the service as was great. The prices are what one would expect at an nice resort; plan on about $60 for a meal for two, if you order wine. For good service we were told to tip 20%.
One thing that we did NOT care for was the loud music that seemed ubiquitous; but we must be in a minority, or they wouldn't persist on playing it. 
I would recommend this hotel to all travellers, although we did not see any children there which may mean there are better options for families. Plus, the Tuscan is expensive.

title: “Central Hotel”
text: We stayed here for 4 nights, very central for everything, good sized clean room. Free internet. The only bad point was the time we waited for the lifts, so sometimes we would go down by the stairs. The breakfast at Dennys always looked crowded so we found a little place at 540 Northpoint Street called Sunrise Cafe, very friendly couple with freshly cooked omlettes/scambled eggs/toast, etc.at a good price. A good location to stay at.

title: “Excellent value for your money”
text:
I stayed for a weekend in Yourstay Broadway Apartments with my wife. We booked a studio apartment. We really enjoied from the service there since our arrival. The check-in was quick, we got enough towels and linens for our stay, and we had free Cable TV. There was a problem with the air-condition system but it was fixed quickly by Yourstay team.
I stayed in hotels before but this serviced apartment was much better.
The price was fair enough, and I'm sure i'll book with Yourstay again.

title: “Great”
text: Great rasbarry martini made by Mark D was amazing he knew exactly what to make when i was unsure of what drink i wanted and was ever attentive

title: “Great Location/probably overpriced”
text: We won a trip to Memphis and stayed at the Marriott and found it to be a great hotal with great and friendly service staff. It was right on the trolley line which was VERY convienent. They food was good. It has a Pool and Hot Tub on the third floor with a large outdoor patio overlooking the city. If I had to pay $200 to $300 per night, it would have been overpriced in my mind. If you can get it for less, it's a good deal and the hotel and grounds are very clean.

title: “good location, comfortable bed”
text: Good beds here. Other than that nothing spectacular about this hotel. The room layout is a bit odd and the bathroom could be nicer.

title: “Beautiful Hotel”
text: I was able to stay at this beautiful place for 2 nights. My brother was having his wedding at the Tavern on the Green and so this was the hotel my family stayed at for the wedding weekend. The first night I stayed in the suite with all of the bridesmades, and my sister in law. She payed a bundle for this suite, and they were a bit unaccomodating that night. we needed cots brought in since there were about 13 of us, and the hotel had said they would be able to do this before check in. Once we got into the suite and got settled, we called for extra bedding and they said we were above the number of people allowed in the room and would have to pay full price for another room for the over flow of people. I feel they should have been a bit more accomodating or at least let us know this before booking. However, the concierge was very attentive and there was a constant flow of champaigne and fruit. The club access was amazing!!!!!! We also ate dinner at the BLT restaurant that is inside the Ritz and the food was amazing!! I would love to go back for a special occassion bc the prices are extremely expensive. In a way, I am spoiled bc now every hotel I am in I am wishing I was in a Ritz. The bathrooms to me are the BEST part. There is no comparison!!! Everything from floor to ceiling is marble and granite and pure luxury. The jetted tubs are amazing, and the glass showers are so nice. I do not think I would ever want to leave the room again if I was able to stay at the Ritz. I am hoping to book it at another location since I think NYC, especially the one in central park I believe is one of the most expensive.

title: “Great experience! Great Value!”
text: This hotel is centrally located in a great part of Downtown Detroit. Detroit's RiverWalk is a great outdoor attraction and is steps away from this hotel. The rooms at the hotel were very clean, spacious, and offered amazing views of the river and Canadian coastline. I live in the neighborhood and recommend this hotel to everyone who comes to visit me.

title: “Fantastic location and comfortable stay”
text:
I enjoyed my 6-night stay at the Hotel Abri. The location is fantastic - very close to the Powell Street BART station (handy getting to and from the airport) and Westfield shopping centre (many brand-name stores and a huge food court). It is also within easy walking distance to Union Square and the Moscone centre (where I was attending a conference).
The room (Deluxe Queen): quite spacious for a solo traveller. There was a wardrobe with plenty of hangers and bathrobes. Very nice furnishings and lots of drawers for storage. The mini-fridge was empty (perfect for storing your own drinks). There was a room heater/cooler unit but the temperature was fine for me during my entire stay so I never used it. The bed was very comfortable and the room was always very clean. I didn't use the coffee machine in the room. I had an inside-facing room as requested and so I didn't get any noise from the street... only I did get a lot of hoots from pigeons! The free wifi was fantastic and I had no connectivity issues.
The bathroom: wonderful toiletries and plenty of towels including large bathtowels. The shower was a very good size with a wide-brimmed showerhead. There was no real place to hang a handtowel (especially once the rail was used for bathtowels - no hook on the door to put it elsewhere). The only storage area for toiletries was next to the toilet which was a little strange.
The staff: I found the front desk and concierge staff very helpful. The computers in the 'business centre' (actually just two computers in the lobby near the lifts) had free internet access for 15 mins but you still had to enter a credit card number (presumably for when the time limit exceeded 15 mins) and there were 3 free B&W printing pages per day.
The negatives: there was no writing desk/chair in the room (despite the website stating that each room had a writing desk) - very awkward as I was attending a conference and had nowhere to put my laptop or books. I could hear people stomping up and down the corridor outside as well as doors banging shut, so the room wasn't very well soundproofed. Note that there are no breakfast facilities. I found the boppy music in the lobby and lifts a little bit irritating but it wasn't a big deal. Although the room was spacious there was an odd configuration so that there wasn't a great place to put the suitcase... I ended up putting mine in front of the coffee machine bureau.
However overall I had a very comfortable and enjoyable stay.

title: “Lovely hotel, wonderful location - steps away to Union Square!”
text: My husband and I recently stayed here for a kid free weekend. We don't live far from SF, but it was nice to be able to get away for a night and enjoy playing "tourist" and taking in the sights of SF. This hotel is literally a hop, skip, and a jump away from Union Square. We were able to check in early (which was awesome!), drop our bags off and start our adventures through the city. The lobby is dark, but cozy, and their are some interesting chairs and decor features all around. A little eclectic for my tastes, but it gave the place a fun vibe. Our room was okay - it felt a little small (probably because the bed was so huge), and it felt like there were mirrors everywhere - might be a turn on for some...I just found it strange. We did enjoy a drink in their hotel bar (this place was super cool), and all of the staff and valets were very nice and accommodating. I would probably stay here again.

title: “substandard service”
text:
nice hotel, but service at the restaurant and bars were slow and unprofessional.
the staff were unorganized and seemed new to the business.
the house keeping they just made the beds, did not clean room or bathroom.
won't go back.

title: “Another great stay”
text: This is not a flashy hotel with bells and whistles but it is a great base for a short break in New York. This is our second stay here and I am glad we returned to this hotel. The rooms are a reasonable size and both the bedroom and bathroom were very clean. I could nit pick by saying that the toilet roll holder was in an odd place and difficult to reach and that the view from our bedroom window at the back was awful but overall this is a great place to stay. The reception staff are helpful, one of them helped my son to get tickets for a Mets baseball game. The location is brilliant half a block from Times Square. I would certainly recommend it to anyone on a budget and the deli next door does a great breakfast!

title: “Great Value”
text:
Hotel was clean, staff was courteous & the rooms are very good size. 
I would stay here again.

title: “Compact and well positioned”
text:
This hotel is perfectly located within 10 seconds of Times Square, and of two subway stations within eye shot. The rooms are very small, 12 ft x 12 ft but very well thought out and clean, The aircon was not the quietest but was very efficient, The room has a huge widescreen tv and the bed was superb if only 4ft wide. As you look at the front of the hotel, to the right is a superb Delli, which does a great breakfast roll and sells everything you would wish to eat.
To sum it up, the room reminded me of sleeping in a well thought out Camper van.

title: “FANTASTIC - Lived up to all the previous reviews!”
text:
I found and booked this hotel based solely on the loads of fabulous reviews on this website. I've always found Tripadvisor.com to be very reliable and this was certainly no exception!
We stayed at Hotel Rex on the last night of our honeymoon after a week in Carmel. The room was great - despite some mention in other reviews that they were small we found there to be ample space and even had a sleeper sofa in our king room! The decor had character without being cheesy and it reminded me of the Chelsea hotel in New York with a splash more class. 
The wine hour was great and we stayed in the bar and listened to the jazz guitarist who was there that Friday evening. The bar was as pleasant and we found the drinks and bar food to be less expensive than anywhere else we'd been on the whole trip. 
I highly recommend this hotel. The location can't be beaten and it's great from top to bottom.

title: “Great location”
text: Had a great stay, my husband was on business and I came along (as he would say I was on vacation.) We were within walking distance to everything we even has a Starbucks a block or so away. Are room was very large and clean. It was very nice to have a full breakfast or a lite one every morning. I rarely give excellent and the reason I gave and average on sleep quality is because I'm use to a soft bed and this was a little hard. We would stay here again.

title: “Not as great as expected”
text:
I spent a Saturday night at this property and as a Gold HHonors member I was somewhat disappointed. This downtown hotel should be the top of the line property for the Hilton chain in Austin, but it sure didn't seem that way.
The executive level room I stayed in was small, with a very very small bathroom and a lovely view of highway traffic. All around us, the rooms were being painted so it didn't smell too great either. The executive lounge had pretty lame offerings for snacks and the breakfast in the lounge was at the same level as a Hampton Inn. The worst feature of the hotel is the elevators - they are very slow and always crowded. But, perhaps this is not unexpected for a convention center hotel.
The health club was ok but frankly I have seen better (and certainly more) cardio equipment in Hampton Inns and Embassy Suites...again, nothing in particular wrong with it, just not deluxe. The pool was lovely but so crowded during the day we elected to skip it on Saturday and instead had a lovely private swim on Sunday morning. During our visit, the spa did not have any capabilities for manicures or pedicures so I had to walk two blocks to a salon on 6th street for this service. That may not sound like a major problem, but imagine walking back at 102 degrees and in salon flip flops to protect your pedicure...hmm.
The parking garage seemed perilous as several cars were racing by at 35 miles an hour thru dark, blind turns. Needs more supervision or something.
On a positive note--very comfortable beds, friendly staff, good location. If you can stay here for $150 or under, you'll probably be satisfied. However if you get into more premium rates, consider another more deluxe downtown property.

title: “Awesome Location!”
text:
Stayed here in February 2012 and it was great! We had 4 adults in one room, which was a bit squishy but manageable. It was very clean though and an AWESOME LOCATION!!! Only a five minute walk to Times Square and Central Park!
Front Desk staff we're quite unfriendly both before arriving and during our stay but that wouldn't stop me from returning. Breakfast was good too, not a huge selection but what they did have on offer was great!

title: “great deal, excellent location”
text:
This place was perfect for me. I found the best rates using Kayak . com ($55 a night including all taxes and fees). Of all the other hotels in similar price ranges (meaning real cheap for me) this place was probably the best one and a safe area of town. You get a room with your own tub or shower (others in the same price range only provided shared bath or room). 
The hotel is in an ideal location, close to union square and the heart of downtown san francisco. There were many eateries in walking distance, taco bell and quiznos a few steps away. Various thai, indian and american restaurants are all a block or two away. The theater is right across the street. A walgreens is on the next block and the hotel is on the geary bus line. The bart line is only a few blocks walk away. 
There are no real amenities to speak of. Because the hotel is old the rooms are smaller than you might find in other cities, walls are thinner and the hallways look drab and the floors creak. The elevator works okay, is large enough for a couple of people and their suitcases. They lock the front door at night and you have to show your room key to get in but I like the security it provides as there is someone there at all times of the day or night. The front desk people were great, they allowed me to keep my bags there after I checked out, The guy even placed netting over my suitcases to prevent someone from walking off with it. 
As usual, you get what you pay for. There are many better and newer hotels in the area with large rooms and amenities provided but then they would probably cost a lot more for them also. 
If you are on a budget and just looking for a safe secure place to stay then this place might fit the bill for you.

title: “Disappointingly overpriced--but great location.”
text: I got this hotel blindly off of Priceline and knew instantly I had vastly overpaid for a 3 star upscale hotel, and my fears were validated on subsequently reading reviews. You walk in the front door and don't even know how to get to the lobby, which is on the second floor. The two elevators were slow and tiny. We walked into our first room in this "non-smoking" hotel and were greeted with the most smoke we had ever experienced. In addition, I was told the rooms were "deluxe". It was the size of a closet with barely enough room to move in front of the bed. We instantly returned to the front desk to get a better room. The desk clerk, without any apology, put us in a new room, and explained all the rooms were the same size. The new room, although smoke-free, did not have a functioning air conditioner. For expediency we didn't want to switch again. The bathroom was decent, but the room also lacked artwork. We both agreed that the bed/pillows were comfortable. The plasma t.v had poor reception (isn't it all cable?) I hate the feeling of getting ripped off, but I definitely had that feeling here.

title: “Arlington is cool”
text: I like this hotel! Good bargain, great location (near three subway lines) and very comfortable. Room was a decent size, very clean and there were plenty of hangers for your clothes (small detail but means lots to me). If you're looking for a good economy hotel, nothing fancy in a great location, book this hotel.

title: “Just ok”
text: Rooms are clean but smell of damp dog. Asked for pet free floor but did hear dogs barking in the middle of the night. Woke up with small bites on legs. Def NOT bed bugs but rather looked like flea bites. very disappointed.

title: “If you want service in the European tradition, stay here”
text:
The Barclay is one of only two hotels I choose when staying in New York since I moved to California. If you want trandy, this is not the place for you. If you want comfort and old fashioned service, stay here. I am fussy about hotels and find the Barclay reminiscent of good hotels in Europe. As a native New Yorker, I know good neighborhoods and the Barclay sits in one of the finest and most convenient.. 
Although all the staff are attentive, the restaurant and bar staff are truly delightful, especially Jose, one of ther bartenders, and I found the bell staff very accommodating. Since I tend to stay close to my base when I travel since I do most of my activities during the day, I ate most meals in the hotel and the food was terrific. 
The only drawback I noticed was that the hotel does need some freshening up and to my delight I found that it is planning a major renovation very soon. I look forward to staying at the Barclay again after that. It should be terrific.

title: “WE SO LOOK FORWARD TO OUR RETURN.”
text: This winter, December..we return to our 'home away from home'. Visiting New York, friends, theater, museums, etc. are definitely a motivaitng factors to endure the airline industry of today..staying at the Warwick, however, is truly the 'cherry' on top of the cake! This will be our fifth visit....every visit we keep on asking ourselves how can one improve on perfection. Angela..thank you for your personal continued assistance. We look forward to meeting your not so new GM, Mr. Sam Kapadia......and experiencing the renovated premium accomodations!

title: “lots of fun!!!”
text: had a great time. a little wild, but alot of fun!! felt very good about being there. nice rooms. xxx a plus.

title: “Never again hotel Carter”
text:
I went to Hotel Carter on a study-trip, and it was absolutely horrible. In our first room, there was a stank, there were hairs in the bed which was also broken, the tv and the bed lights did not work, and the door to the bathroom couldn't even be closed. After complaining we got a new room, which was dirty on the floor, but better, we thought... But no, when we went back after being out all day, we discovered that we had had a visit from rats. They had been in our bags and suitcases, they had eaten our food, peed and [--] in our luggage. My friends who were the ones cleaning after the rats also got flea-bits all over their bodies including their faces.
The employees of the hotel thought this was normal, and claimed that we also had that in Denmark. They even laughed of us. But fortunately (or what to call it...) they offered us a new room, but after lookng at it, we would rather switch with our teacher. Cause the new room had a big hole in the wall, with bits of food. It felt like an invitation to the rats.
Our 4. room was rat-free (so we think, at least...), but was still dirty and with cockroachs.
Two nights after, others from our group experienced rats in their rooms, and our teachers decided to move us all to another hotel.
Other visitors saw a rat in the hallway, and haunted it down with a shoe.
The only good thing about this hotel is the location, but is not worth it at all. I would not live their for free, and will not recommand it for anyone, it is health damaging and so disgusting.

title: “clean, funky and friendly!”
text: My sister-in-law, my husband and I stayed at the chambers in NYC in April 2010. It is a great hotel, a little funky with nice sized rooms. The beds were comfortable, the rooms clean and the rain forest shower head meant a great shower. The front desk staff was very friendly and they were able to give us a late check out because of some sports activities we had going on in the city. It's a great location, very close to Central Park. The only thing I didn't like was the lighting in the hall and the rooms was a bit dim, especially after coming in from a sunny day outside. We are planning on staying there the next time we go to the city and would highly recommend this place to friends and family.

title: “Experience it once, not twice - better value to be found”
text:
Having lived in Denver many years, the Brown Palace has definite allure and mystique. We wanted a weekend away, so I booked an advance room online. A few comments: Upon arrival, late evening, we were informed the "Top of Brown King" room we reserved was not available, and were asked to take a similarly appointed room with two queens. Not exactly what we were looking for in our weekend away. After expressing my disappointment in the switch, some ackward silences, and a few minutes, the desk clerk found a way to make one available. It turns out the room I booked weeks in advance was being help for someone else, I do feel bad for the disappointment they felt when they arrived for checkin.
Although the online reservation process was efficient, I found the description misleading. The room description includes the phrase "Complimentary beverages in refrigerator." After reading this, what would you expect? Something more than two luke-warm bottles of water in a fridge that wasn't turned on. After a day in Denver, returning to our room, the two waters were not restocked by housekeeping. A call to the front desk told us we were out of luck. For a $250+/night room, the whole experience failed to wow us. Room was nicely finished, toiletry items were great, linens and bed comfort were average.
Also, for the three days we were there, only one of the two guest elevators was in operation.
Also, for a bite to eat, Ship's Tavern is nice, but a little pricey. I would suggest a bison burger. For more affordable eats, head one block south to the 16th St mall which offers dozens of choices.

title: “WOW, What a Gem”
text:
My friend was ill and the front desk sent us pita crackers and ginger ale with ice! We were so taken care of., we had to request a later check out and No Problem
The room was comfy and super cheap with such a great staff!
So close to Magnificent Mile and State Street shopping that we really enjoyed the walks!
I will so stay here again!

title: “There's no place like home!”
text:
I have stayed in this hotel dozens of times since it opened in the summer of 1982. You might think a hotel about to celebrate its 30th birthday is past its prime, but this property has been renovated several times during the last three decades and has stayed in excellent shape. This is a solid structure--not like the cheap, imitation construction that we've become accustomed to in recent times. Walls are thick enough to prevent room-to-room noise, and yet the hotel is not so large as to ever become overcrowded. 
This was, when it opened, the finest hotel in the Galleria area of Houston, and I still consider it so. With a friendly and helpful staff, it is a great example of what the word "accommodation" really means.

title: “Amazing Hotel”
text: Just stayed at the Omni in Dallas next to the convention center. The Hotel is absolutely beautiful. Great restaurants and fantastic service. The staff went above and beyond for us. Could not have asked for a better stay. Keep up the amazing service!

title: “great staff”
text:
an excellent hotel very well situated for most attractions.
the staff were extremely helpful especially the concierge who provided great local knowledge about attractions and ball games etc.
the room unfortunately overlooked the air conditioning system but you can't have everything.
would reccommend hotel to friends

title: “Large beautiful room, excellent location, WONDERFUL staff”
text:
Our first time to San Francisco, so we chose this hotel based on Internet information only. But it turned out to be a hit. It is close to everything. The room was larger than expected, very clean, very nicely designed. It was very quiet. The bed was very comfortable. And there was nice desk space to work. So, the room was beautiful. But the hit of this hotel was its front-desk staff and a tall smiling gentleman who literally walked into the middle of the street, down a block or so, just to hail a cab for us.
