It was raining, the traffic was light but steady, and right out there was this guy going all out for me and my kids, who he didn't know from Adam. My kids were amazed at how dedicated he was. And when we needed a driver during rush hour to take us to another city, right at cabbie-shift-change time - which makes finding a cabbie impossible - this guy dialed a reliable driver he knew and in minutes we had a private livery (limo) driver taking us to Oakland. Unbelievable.
The female front desk staff was just the same. Very friendly, super helpful, never in your way but always there to help. My kids and I travel often - Chicago, DC, NYC - and I have never previously run into a consistently-wonderful front desk group. They were ALL nice, and all pleasant, but not in a smarmy, overbearing way. Just like...family welcoming you back, genuinely. Since the lobby is narrow, you must walk by them as you go to the elevator, so passing by them was always a nice warm welcome back. A stab in the dark for us in finding a hotel, but it was fantastic. A great hotel.

title: “We loved Hotel Fusion!”
text: We stayed at the Hotel Fusion for 2 weeks during August and September 2007. The Hotel was ideally located for exploring the city on foot. It is right in the middle of so many restaurants and shops, especially a wonderful icecream shop across the road called Coldstone Creamery. The Hotel itself was very clean and tidy with wonderful friendly staff who were happy to answer any questions we had and gave us lots of helpful advice about how to travel round the city. The free breakfast was scrumptious, offering toast, muffins, crossiants, juices, fruit, tea and coffee. Also free internet access was provided as well as access to a small gym! The Hotel was a two minute walk away from one of the main shopping centres as well as it being a one minute walk from the BART station which we used as transport from the airport instead of paying lots for a taxi! Pier 39 was a 45minute walk which was good offering lots of shops, attractions and you catch the boat here to Alcatraz. We also went on an amazing helicopter ride which was brilliant and i would advise everyone visiting the city to go on! The BART station was also linked to the MUNI which was ideal for visiting San Francisco Zoo where you can see the famous Gary the grizzly gulch and Wilbert the wonderful Warthog! The Hotel Fusion made our holiday perfect and is an ideal place to start exploring the fascinating city of San Francisco from.

title: “Great Service”
text: Customer service was very good. Clean rooms (Bedding was changed every morning). Handy to downtown and Bay. Overall really good.

title: “Great hotel and location”
text: We stayed for 4 days for my 50th birthday and were not disappointed, we were upgraded to a room with a huge bed and a bath which my partner loves. Breakfast was absolutely fine, with my only gripe being that all the cereals were sweetened up, ie honey flavoured, all 4 varieties supplied, nice plain old corn flakes or rice krispies would have been good, however it is only a small point. Other than that, no complaints, would i stay there again, definitely

title: “Excellent Hotel & Friendly Staff”
text: We stayed here two nights over the Labor Day holiday. The room was clean and with a family of four (12 and 16 year olds) the room was a nice size. Very convenient to area attractions. The tour bus even has a stop at the back of the hotel. We felt very safe in the area. The only bad thing about the hotel is the price for parking ($45 a night) but it seems like the going rate in that area. Would 100% stay here again.

title: “Impressed”
text: Spent 10 days in NYC and would definately stay at Southgate again. The room was large and clean. It was nice to have the kitchen. Everyone was friendly and helpful. Convenient location - across the street from Madison Square Garden and Penn Station.

title: “Not What I Hoped It Would Be”
text:
This hotel is in a great location in San Diego. The rooms are fairly large. There is a "free" breakfast every morning that is quite good, but it is usually very crowded. The room had a small refrigerator and a microwave (good when traveling with kids). The room had two TVs (but both were a little out-dated). The furnishings were not hideous, but they were a little worn. The staff was very friendly. The elevators were slow. 
The mandatory valet parking (at $22/day) was a mess! We typically had to wait between 15 and 30 minutes for our car each morning.
We did not get the room selected in our reservation (we were told no such room was available...King bed with balcony and no smoking). The room we got had no balcony (but did have the King bed with no smoking).

title: “This is the Place to Stay”
text:
My hubby must come for business to San A. often. He has stayed at the Watermark and the Omni. I chose the Hotel Contessa because just wanted to see how it was, looked neat in pictures. San Antonio is a wonderful place; I had no idea it has all the stuff it does. Wow! Thank goodness they didn't pave over the River! Tip: Go to the Alamo and pay the extra for the audio tour. I spent 2.5 hours here. 
I really loved it; the setting is wonderful. Rooms larger than most , nice bathroom. It's located in the best area overall to me. Just a little walk to Boudros. Right next door to the Villita shops, which were disappointing shop-wise but I enjoyed the preserving the architecture. 
I have to say after seeing where the Omni & Watermark is; think it's too loud over there. The Omni's exterior is nice but interior just so so. Watermark's exterior wasn't anything special but hubby said he liked their fitness center. (Which is very important to him, less so to me). Another option that looked nice was the hotel next door to the Hotel Contessa; Wyndham or Westin? not sure.

title: “Attention to EVERY detail. Perfection!”
text: I recently had a business working lunch for 20 in the Waterloo Room at The Four Seasons Austin. First, I want to thank Megan, Alyssa, Ruben, and Sami for all their outstanding service. They are a wonderful example of Four Seasons service and attention to every detail. I do an event like this once a month and the service and food at the Four Seasons was superior compared to other hotels and restaurants I have used in the past. The room was perfect and the setup was perfect. Attention is given to every detail. From the second I arrived at the hotel, I was greeted with a smile and excellent service. The hotel is in a great location for everything. The hotel is beautiful and the design is very comfortable. Everything from the lobby, restaurant and bar to the rooms are fun and aesthetically pleasing. This is the type of hotel that you don’t want to leave. This hotel is a destination spot for people in the Austin. Many of my guests commented that this was the perfect place to hold the meeting. I highly recommend the Four Seasons for any business event, small or large!

title: “Bad experience leaves bad taste...”
text:
I've stayed here a couple of times with no complaints. Overall, the staff is polite and helpful, the rooms are clean and, generally, quiet. This last stay, however, was unusual. I'd left my hotel room to have dinner with friends and upon my return, my bathroom was smoky and smelled STRONGLY of marijuana. Right away, I called the front desk who sent up security to verify my claims. I was told by security that I wasn't the only one to complain (the smoke had been coming through the shared vent in the bathrooms) and that I could have my room changed. When I called to change rooms, it took nearly 15 minutes to get through to the front desk, and another 10 before someone showed up to give me a new room key. The gentleman who gave me the new room key was extremely kind, very friendly and apologetic, but admitted that this was not the first incident (say what now?!)
Although I anticipated the airplane noise, being in such close proximity to the airport, what actually kept me awake was the noise from the street that I could hear from my room. Also, if you're staying for longer periods of time, there isn't a lot within walking distance to eat/do. Overall, slightly disappointed in this particular stay although I don't hold it against this hotel, or the chain... but perhaps improvements to be made?

title: “Missing Amenities”
text:
We stayed on a group rate for a conference. The reservation confirmation quoted one rate but we were charged a higher rate. Parking cost a rather stiff $14/night. By the time taxes and parking were added up, the $149 quoted rate got up to $200 per night. We declined paying $10 per night for high speed internet. There was no hotel airport shuttle for the nearby airport.
Several amenities, when compared to the average motel, were not available. The water would not get hot for showers although it was usually usable. There was no microwave or refrigerator. The Flat panel TV was mismatched to the TV shows, with the low-res image stretched. There was no way to correct the aspect ratio. The reception quality was poor (banding on stations). There was plastic bottle water available in the room for $5. A continental breakfast of coffee, some kind of unappetizing eggs and croissants was provided for four mornings of the conference. Cereal was available on at least one occasion. The coffee was good.

title: “Great if you have "low standards"”
text: plese don't fall for the good reviews, they were prob. written by staff, this hotel is truely DIRTY!!! please believe all reviews that warn you not to stay here ,carpets,tub,chairs,floors, everything dirty EXCEPT front lobby very misleading. Run don't walk away. NOT WORTH MORE THAN $45.00 A NIGHT

title: “Lobby Bar is worth the stay!”
text:
Love love loved the lobby bar/estaurant! Morgan was so cool, genuine and offered perfect advice on choices. She exemplifies authentic san franciscans!
Hotel a bit old once you get to the room. Typical san fr

title: “Wow negative reviews wrong”
text: I had booked this hotel through my american express fine hotels and resorts program and was a bit concerned with some of the reviews I had read on trip advisor. I even tried to change my reservation when I read the bit about the beds. I can promise you a fabulous experinece, the staff was amazing, the rooms were lovely and the location truley unbeatable. I am so glad that I didn't miss this experience because of that one negative reviewer.... Really lovely, I promise!

title: “great vibe and beautiful rooms”
text:
My stay at the W was perfect, with a very friendly staff and a warm welcome upon arrival. 
the room was just great , spacious and very modern design and equipments.
the food was very good and not too pricy for this hotel category.
the view on the roof is amazing. Clearly an adult playground.
also, the W is well located on the up and coming Hollywood bld area within LA - very close from several highways and the griffith park. This district has started a major rehabilitation phase and some great restaurants and shops are opening on a regular basis.
Will be back at the W Hollywood for sure!
Sébastien.

title: “front desk person was great.”
text: We arrived early , about 10am. Was given a better & bigger room than we had booked , as there were three of us it worked out great. We put our luggage in left luggage down stairs, bought tickets at another desk for the hop on bus, had breakfast from Tim Hortons adjoining the hotel out front & was on the bus by 11am.Very efficient. Did the lower Manhatan loop, went back to the hotel to get our keys , put our luggage in the room, had lunch & back on the bus for the upper Manhattan loop, all in one day, but at least we saw everything & wrote down the places we wanted to get off & investigate the next day.We were in New York 4 days 3 nights & packed a lot into it. We all said we would go back to the Hotel Pennsylvania, it's not new , but we found it comfortable & handy to most things.

title: “Not the best out there”
text:
The rooms are extremely small (I could not have stayed a week). There was some mold on the tile around the tub faucet. I felt that I needed to put towels down on the bathroom floor to walk through it. You have to pay for internet access. TV viewing is very limited, although, you could pay $12.99 to watch a new release or $3.99 to watch a sea lion program on the Discovery channel. We did watch a program on National Geographic channel for free. Breakfast buffett is $9.95 for one buffet. I made one local phone call for 50 cents. 
 They have advertised on the website that a sony playstation is included with room and I called to find out what games/movies they have available and was told they no longer have playstations in the room. I asked if we could bring ours and hook it up and they told me that we could, but when we arrived there was no way to hook a playstation the way they have the TV hooked up. 
I do have to say that all the employees are extremely friendly. I forgot my shampoo and the shampoo that they provided was really good shampoo. I normally use pantene and was afraid my hair would feel icky, but it did not. 
I would not recommend this hotel to a friend.

title: “Best place to stay for MD Anderson convenience”
text: Rotary House is a walkway across from the MD Anderson clinics and hospital. If you are a patient at MD, this is the most convenient place to stay, especially if you are having a series of tests run and can go back to your room inbetween tests. Parking is free with hotel stay, and the restaurants and shops within the "campus" make it a great place for caregivers and patients to park and not have to travel to get to appointments, etc. Within the hotel: Starbucks, Ice Cream service, market with pizza, salad bar, deli, and a full service restaurant. A volunteer gift shop carries necessities and cancer patient items, as well as a clothing selection. Lobby area is relaxing, with wonderful sitting areas and a musician playing soft evening music on alot of the days we have been there.

title: “For an airport hotel, better than expected”
text: Stayed here to catch an early flight out of Philadelphia. For a one night stay, it was good (and for the $60 I paid for it on Priceline, it was great). I remember the bed being really comfortable. Ordered room service as there were no hotels nearby -- was a little expensive (I mean, it's room service) but was surprisingly good. Hallways needed a good cleaning. Free airport shuttle in the morning was on time -- there were too many people to fit on one, so they immediately brought a second behind it with no delays. Good overall for an airport hotel.

title: “Art Takes Times Square”
text: We stayed at the FABULOUS Sanctuary Hotel on Sunday, July 15th as my art is being shown on 13 major electronic billboards in Times Square for the month of July: http://www.artistswanted.org/site/news/times-square-moment-a-digital-gallery-featuring-vicki-dasilva-surabhi-saraf-and-elly-cho/ nightly at 11:57pm, so we needed a place to crash. From the entry to the exit our experience was met by courteous, attentive staff, a luxury design, a hip, modern NYC hotel that goes above and beyond to satisfy their guests. Can't wait to return!!! Thanks AWESOME SANCTUARY with cool art!

title: “Clean, reasonably priced, plain rooms, exceptional views from corner room”
text:
Recently stayed in a corner suite on floor 14. Bed linens and towels were of high quality and bed was comfortable. The tv was some sort of flat tube with a shaky cable connection that we had to keep moving around to get any picture at all and there were few plugs to plug in anything like a computer or phone charger. An extension cord ran under the bed to plug in the bedside light. Most of the room was clean; except for mold on the bottom of the shower door and a lot of dust behind the curtains when we closed and opened them.
At check-in, we weren't told about complimentary coffee in the mornings (happened upon it on our final day there) or any other amenities that the hotel may have offerred. There are no ice machine so expect to tip whenever you need fresh ice. The sink near the bar and frig in the room drained so slowly that we couldn't empty much into it without it overflowing. 
The concierge didn't seem to enjoy his job and he was a little patronizing when explaining that one train station was only 1/2 block closer than the other. Parking valets and bell men were awesome, though, so they made up for him.
We may stay again if the price is right because of the close proximity to restaurants, outdoor dining, the train, and shopping. We would never, however, pay full price for a room in this hotel.

title: “Great Deal - Very Nice hotel, Great Location”
text:
The staff is very polite. Rooms are clean. Breakfast very good. A great option for you if you want a great time in NYC without spending unnecessary money with hotels. Very close to the NYC Metro and Times Square.
My next stay in NYC will be at the very same hotel.

title: “fantastic stay”
text: My husband and I went to NYC to visit and celebrate a birthday. From the moment you pull up to this hotel you are made welcome. Check in was seamless. While waiting to check in you are offered champagne, chocolate covered strawberries and chocolates. The rooms are wonderful!. Comfortable beds and huge bathrooms that are like a spa. The gigantic soaking tube is situated underneath a large window. You can soak and take in a lovely skyline. Lots of special little touches. We especially liked the expresso machine in the room! We can't wait to go back/

title: “The PERFECT hotel for a family vacation”
text:
My husband and I took our 14 and 16-year old daughters to NYC for 10 days, and I CAN'T RECOMMEND THIS HOTEL HIGHLY ENOUGH!
I used to travel to NYC on business every few weeks, and finding a spacious hotel room at ANY price can be a challenge. I really wanted the girls to see New York, but I was dreading sharing a cramped space with all of their stuff...I thought we would be climbing all over each other and their 30 pairs of shoes. But we stayed in the Executive One Bedroom Suite at the Kimberly for $420/night, and it was HUGE...king bedroom and nice masterbath, second 1/2 bath (godsend!), large living room/dining room combination with pull-out sofa bed (queen size, I think), fully-equipped kitchen (nice way to save a little money in an expensive city!), dining room that seats 6, balcony with a view of the Chrysler building, and 5 closets. Compare that to any accomodations for 4 in Times Square -- or even an apartment rental -- and you'll see what an incredible deal that is. (Book early...I think they only have one with a second half bath). They also have luxury suites with upgraded bathrooms, but this was very nice and perfect for our family.
Great location in mid-town so you can get anywhere you want to go easily. I highly recommend this hotel, especially for families with teenagers (btw: I didn't think it was possible, but we spent 10 days on vacation with our daughters and never heard "I'm SO BORED" once!....Worth every penny!)

title: “Fun and Friendly Place”
text: We have stayed here a couple of times, even though we are local, to gather with friends for a night in the City. It's always friendly, unpretentious, and a pleasure to stay at. We especially love that the hotel is dog friendly and that there is a nightly wine reception.

title: “More cons than pros”
text:
We just returned from this hotel. Lots of pros and cons... for the most part I think the cons outweigh the pros unless you have no other choice available.
Pros: good location, friendly staff, nice looking decor, somewhat reasonably priced, pretty good morning breakfast, internet downstairs.
Cons: (And these are big ones to me) The fold out bed in our suite ( I talked to others in suites also)was virtually unusable- worn out, flat and so uncomfortable our kids could not sleep on it. There are no other options as they do not have roll away beds. To top it off, we were given one sheet and a worn blanket that looked like it came from the county jail for bedding for the fold out -- not a second sheet, no mattress pad, etc.The pool was open but not heated so unusable, also very very small. Hot water was running out in the morning shower, inconsistent internet access in our room, first day we had 2 bath towels, one hand towel and one washcloth for our family of 4. But the staff was friendly... you decide.

title: “Good location with many complimentary amenities.”
text: Good location with many complimentary amenities including high speed internet access, breakfast buffet, and cookies in the evening.

title: “Great property”
text:
This is a great property. Newly renovated Courtyard and right near SAT Airport. The hotel does have some access issues, but that is to be expected around major highways and busy airport roads. The hotel is behind some other restaurant, but the hotel again is great along with the staff.
Highly recommend this hotel!

title: “Exceeds your expectations! for a GREAT price!”
text: Location is perfect, customer service is unmatchable, and the rooms were SO luxurious and the room was so affordable! For the price you are getting much more than any other hotel offers. Room service food was DELICIOUS! THey were so accommodating to our requests. I have traveled all over the world and stayed in many, many nice hotels around the world...in the nicest of destinations. I would HIGHLY recommend this hotel and its reasonable prices make it the icing on the cake!

title: “Highly recommended”
text: Booked this online after researching reviews on Tripadvisor. Was not disappointed. Had a King Study which was spacious and clean. Overlooked 8h Ave on 4th floor, but noise was not a problem. Despite being more of a budget hotel, we couldn't have had better service. The catering manager bought gluten free bagels and muffins for my son who was unable to eat much of the standard breakfast. There was no additional charge for this. We have stayed in superior graded hotels and this hotel certainly equals those in terms of service. The constant supply of coffee and fruit in the lobby is a nice touch too. We'd certainly go back if we visited NY again.

title: “Check MSG from your window”
text: If you want to be near Madison Square Garden or Penn Station, this is the place for you. I loved the old world charm and the rooms were well appointed and comfortable. If you can get one of the top-floor suites with a balcony, it will be life changing -- it was for me. Expensive but totally fun.

title: “Not Bad/Not Good...”
text: My family and I usually stay in Marriott hotels,we are rewards members,but this one I would probably skip next time.The dust ruffle was ripped,the privacy curtain had old food stains stuck to it,one of the pillows had a dark brown stain on it(I bring my own pillowcases though),and the room had an old smell to it. There were also a few beetles in the bathroom area.I blame some of this on the climate ,in general it is hot,muggy and buggy in Houston.Overall the hotel was OK generally clean minus statements above and the staff was courteous as well.The room served its purpose,but I will choose somewhere else next trip.

title: “Not a good choice for a weekend stay”
text: We stayed here over the 4th of July hoping to have a nice, relaxing hotel experience. The hotel was empty, but the clerk put us in a room next to some teenagers who were there to party! We moved rooms 4 times in the 2 nights we were there. The second room, the people next to us were smoking in a non-smoking room and up 1/2 the night partying. The next room had an ant infestation and the next room the A/C was not working properly and the carpets and bedding were damp from humidity. This is definitely a "hit or miss" hotel, with some nice rooms and some awful rooms. The breakfast is $11.95 per person and equivalent to the free continental breakfast you get at a Quality Inn off the Interstate! We paid $75.00 a night for this experience. I guess you get what you pay for. The guests were mostly younger people there to party. If you stay one night as a business traveler, I guess you could tolerate it. I would never stay there again.

title: “Peaceful”
text: This hotel is a quiet, pleasant, clean place to stay after the exercise of seeing Washington DC. The room we had was nicely arranged and large enough. It is a few blocks from Metro, has nice restaurants close by, and is within walking distance of the Potomac. The mall area and other tourist attractions can be quickly reached by bus and Metro. If possible, don't take a car because parking is $25.00 a night. The management were friendly and helpful.

title: “Westin Name, but not Westin quality or experience”
text: This hotel was not a Westin propertyoriginally and was only branded Westin a few years back. It has a dark interior with the typical multi-story atrium design that was popular in the 80's. the majority of the rooms look into the atrium so you really don't have natural sunlight in your room. My room on the 10th floor was in a corner which abutted a glass walled corridor so people walking by could look directly into my room - so the shades were always drawn. The bed was great, but no slippers or bathrobe. The fitness center is adequate, not great, as it only had two eliptical machines and three treadmills and one set of free weights. The wait staff at the bar acted as if they were doing you a favor getting a drink for you. My room was not properly cleaned before my arrival as the previous guest had left his underclothes in the dresser. I brought the clothes down to the front desk and they did not even apologize for the oversight. I only stayed here because I booked the hotel at time the rate was low compared to other hotels in the area. It is in a very convienent location.

title: “Great for the Price I Paid”
text: I got a deal for this hotel on Sunday for $135. Close to Times Square, near the 8th Ave/50th St station served by the C E and D lines. Great room for the price. However, only average for their rest of the week rate. I didn't want to pay $200+ for a room I only saw to sleep and shower so I moved on to a cheaper place.

title: “You won't believe you're in SA”
text:
We have stayed at this wonderful boutique hotel on several occasions. 
This place is awesome from hello to goodbye. The valets are always cheerful which always makes for a great start. The front desk and the rest of the staff are all just as pleasant. The VBar is rocking. We happy hour there often. We've dined at the Citrus several times and loved our meals and attentive servers. The rooms are so fine and pristeen. They are filled with all kinds of fun appealing things. Even live plants! The bed is so dreamy you won't want to get out of it. This is really one TOP NOTCH hotel. I only wish I could grab those specials a little more often! Fun & Funky & Upscale.

title: “Made my Stay enjoyable.”
text: I had an extended stay at this hotel and all of the people at this Hotel were the best. From the front desk who always were ready to help, to the girl who did my room. They make it feel more like being home than in a Hotel. Thanks to everyone.

title: “Uncomfortable.”
text: My company booked a room for me for a business trip and when I found out where I would be staying I promptly went to the hotel's website to see what it was going to be like. I was impressed with how luxurious the website made it out to be. However, upon arriving I felt the lobby area and front desk attendants to be a bit stuffy. Exhausted from a long day at work, I made it to my room looking forward to a nice plush bed. To my dismay, I was greeted by a bed that felt more like I was sleeping on the floor with a mat, flashbacks of kindergarten came to mind! That is my main complaint, but is a personal preference, if you like a "hard as a rock" bed, you will love this hotel!

title: “Awesome place for business and pleasure ...”
text: Travelled with wife and 2 kids, 2 years old. I had written to the manager requesting an upgrade - I was given a room with one bedroom and 2 (yes, 2) living areas. We were provided with champagne and the strawberries and even bath toys for the boys – very thoughtful !!! The concierge is great and the location superb. Not far from anywhere ... the parking attendants very helpful as well. One minus is the food - could have been better for the price.

title: “Classy”
text: I was attending a conference at GWU, and all the regular rooms were booked in the area, so I stayed in a junior suite at the State Plaza for one week. It was wonderful, I had a full multi-room apartment, with beautiful wooden furnishings, and it was fantastic to have my own full working kitchen: Stove, refrigerator, microwave, toaster, etc. There were no pots and pans when I arrived, but I asked for some and a bag was delivered that had everything I needed. They were a bit dented, but worked fine. The housekeeping did the dishes each morning, too. A convenience store next door had many basic groceries, and there was a Whole Foods market a few blocks away, though that then also meant carrying groceries a few blocks back! The main thing I didn't like about the hotel was that it was several blocks from the nearest Metro station. There are bus stops nearby, but the buses don't run as frequently as tourists really need -- they're more for the local commuters who know the schedules. Taxis were easy to come by though, and plenty of attractions along the mall were in easy walking distance.

title: “Great for Universal”
text:
Stayed one night in August based on website reviews as going to Universal
As previous reviews have said it is very handy for Universal, not walking distance but only 5 mins drive. The hotel and rooms where clean and despite being close to the freeway didn't suffer to much from traffic noise. Had a suite which was plenty big enough with mircowave and fridge, yet still a reasonable price. Breakfast good but needs more seating to accomodate all guests.
I would recommend the hotel for people going to Universal as it is good value for money. Don't book it for the pool because it is very small.
The only downside we found was that there are no bars and eating places close. Had to drive to find somewhere - not good if you want to drink!

title: “Great Location and Wonderful Staff”
text: My wife and I have stayed at the Georgetown Inn several times and have always had a wonderful experience. The staff is very professional, curtious and accommodating. We were once aided by the general manager (Robert Clark) who was amazingingly helpful, friendly and treated us like VIPs. The hotel is in the heart of Georgetown, attached to a great restaurant (Daily Grill) and is walking distance to a wide variety of shops, restaurants, bars and the waterfront. If you're going to visit Washington DC or just having a romantic night away from the kids -- this is the place to be.

title: “Good hotel, but bring earplugs”
text:
We stayed here for one night, a Saturday. The hotel was full with convention-goers but seemed to be run efficiently. Check-in was easy, the staff was great and the concierge was able to get us a great last minute dinner reservation.
The location can't be beat - right by the Powell Street BART station and lots of shopping (Bloomingdales, Nordstrom, etc.). I'd recommend taking the BART into the city and leaving your car at the station. Otherwise, parking is about $50/day at the Marriott.
The room was very nice, clean and the bathroom is large for San Francisco standards. The main problem with our room was that the walls were so thin that we could hear people talking in the room next door. And in the morning a child was blowing a whistle or something, and we REALLY heard that.
Also, the breakfast is very expensive, so go across the street to the Mel's or Denny's.
We got a great deal on Priceline - half price. So all in all, we were very satisfied with our stay.

title: “Good Hotel with Great bartender and chef”
text:
The hotel worked great for a recent business trip - my Team was there for 4 days and while the hotel has a few rough the upsides were easily offset.
The Bartender did a great job keeping us happy and even though Austin has plenty of establishments to choose from we were content staying at the hotel a couple of nights and had great food as well. 
I look forward to our next trip to Dr. Chen's Zen palace.....

title: “Fastest room service ever. Good business hotel.”
text:
Stayed here the night before last on business. Check in was a breeze. On the 29th floor, I could definitely hear sirens from the street that woke me up at night, so next time I'll request a higher floor. Ordered room service right when I arrived and it took 10 minutes. The next morning I called to order room service (there didn't seem to be one of those card on the door things) and it also arrived literally 10 minutes later. Very impressive. Of course it was insanely expensive. I appreciated the healthy options. For breakfast I had an egg white frittata with fennel and mushrooms and a pot of coffee. Total including service charge was $37, but that's the big city. Gym was ok, nothing special. The pool looked small but nice- no one was using it. Had an amazing view from my room-- took a couple photos to email to my husband. 
Agree with the comments about a small bathroom-- the bathroom was slightly larger than an average powder room with the addition of a shower/tub. But it was completely fine. Bed was comfortable, with a down comforter (of course) but definitely not as comfortable as a Westin Heavenly Bed, my gold standard.

title: “Good stay - Convenient location”
text: The hotel is in a very convenient location, close to airport, shopping and restaurants. The room was clean and quiet. My flight arrived early morning and I was able to check in right away. The staff was very professional. The beds were very comfortable and the food was good. Everything I expect from a Homewood Suites.

title: “Stay away - no value”
text:
We stayed at St.Mark's because a friend recommended the place to us. After a brief research of hotels online we thought that we would be getting a good value at St.Marks: for 135 USD a night we were promised a queen size bed and a private bathroom. In comparison, other hotels only offered a double or twin bed and a shared bathroom at this price. When we checked-in our first words were - WTF???!!!
The room was tiny. The bed was squized into a corner so that one of us had to climb in it over the other person. The bed was sooooo hard and uncomfortable. The rest of the furniture included an old dresser without doors and a wooden chair. Nothing else, not even an alarm-clock. Stand-up shower in a tiny bathroom. One old towel per person, no shampoos or soap. The door didn't have an extra lock or a peephole. There was a 1-inch gap between a window A/C unit and a wall. All the sounds of the street were in the room. I had an impression that I slept on the street. I also could hear the neighbors as if they were in the room. Also, they have no elevators and accept only cash. The pub downstairs is a major nightmare.
We stayed for two nights and moved out. We booked a room through priceline.com for the rest of the trip and ended up paying 120 USD per night in a 4 start hotel uptown. Of course, the neighborhood didn't have the "hip feel" but the room was spacious, clean with all the amenities worth 4 stars and CHEAPER! This review is not a commercial for priceline but since now we're using only priceline and no more "historic hotels"!!!!!

title: “For location,charm,a friendly and professional staff,and security the Edison can't be beat.”
text: This was our second visit to the Edison Hotel and we were very satisfied. We were in NYC to see some shows and having all of the theaters within easy walking distance is a great benefit. Being in the heart of Times Square with easy access to the TKTS Booth ,restaurants, and coffee shops makes it really fun.The staff is friendly and professional and we liked the security of having to show a room key to access the elevators. The Edison is not the most modern of hotels in the area, but that is a big part of its' charm. The room was comfortable and clean.The only small complaints: The bathroom is tiny and there is some street noise at night. We will definitely stay at the Edison on our next trip.

title: “Cool”
text: Small rooms, but the whole environment is excellent. Great decoration, staff (concierge) and guests.

title: “Good place, nice tavern”
text: An older Westin but very nice. Super customer service. Good restaurant with good service also.

title: “Beautiful decor marred by design flaws”
text:
We booked this hotel as part of an overall package for a 3-night stay in Boston. While we got a good deal, it was not a cheap stay. Upon arriving, we were impressed with the lovely, modern lobby and fast elevators. Our room was big, with new furniture and a flat screen TV. Beautiful, huge bathroom. Convenient desk and plugs for electronics. We had no problems with service - everyone was very friendly and willing to help. The bar was convenient - they let us take a glass of wine up to the room without any hesitation. 
There were two main problems. The sliding window between the bedroom and the bathroom is a total design disaster for couples. First, it does not completely close at the bottom, so all sounds (and smells) waft right into the bedroom, directly over the bed. Second, it has only a frosted glass panel, so, if anyone goes into the bathroom in the middle of the night, the light shines through into the bedroom, waking up the other party. (The bathroom was pitch dark at night -- and, since it was all marble, you really needed light to ensure you didn't kill yourself.) Anyway, the bathroom quickly became the joke of the trip, and if nothing else, will be one of the memories of our trip to Boston.
The other problem perhaps is not unique to Intercontinental. Since everything now seems to be digital, it is nearly impossible to have a room completely dark at night. The flat screen TV had a red glowing light. The phone had a green glowing light. The clock had a blue glowing light. The sprinkler system had a white flashing light. The curtains would not close completely. It struck me as ironic that there was so much light in the room where it needed to be dark and positively no light in the bathroom, where just a little of that glow would have been helpful.
There were a few other minor things. There was no coffeemaker. Also, no lotion in the bathroom to start, but they brought some the next day without me asking. The light on the make-up mirror did not work - until they cleaned the room - and then it did. Until the next day - and then it didn't again. One of the light bulbs had burnt out on a lamp - we did not mention it and I don't think it ever got replaced. WiFi service was a bit pricey at $14.95 /day or $6.95 hour. 
The location was okay for us - it was easy to find places to eat breakfast and to get on the T. But the Marriott and Boston Harbor Hotels probably would have been better locations for our touristy purposes.
Had I been alone and on business, this place would have been fine. As it was, I felt like we could have made a better choice although we had a pleasant stay anyway.

title: “Excellent palce to stay +++++”
text:
Just come back from a girls trip to NY - my first visit. We stayed at the Casablanca. On arrival its seems small and nothing to write home about. Even going to the room it was OK but nothing special. I could not have been more wrong. What a lovely hotel, warm, friendly and almost felt like staying with friends. The location is great. The staff cold not do more for you(thanks to you all). The rooms are comfortable and clean. A complimentary breakfast is laid on and also evening drinks and nibbles. The lounge is 24/7 with coffee, hot chocolate and snacks available. I woke one night and did not feel out of place going down in my PJ's and sitting in the lounge with a book and hot choc. The hotel was full but the right size so,did not feel cramped or overwhelming. 
I would recommend this hotel to anyone, old, young, families. I will be returning to NY as I loved it.......the Casablance is where I will be staying.

title: “Exellent hotel for price and location”
text:
Stayed here from March 9th - 13th and had a brilliant time in New York. This is in a great location with Times Square 2 minutes away and with a lot of stuff within walking distance. 
There's a couple of decent bars on the opposite side of the road if you fancy a couple of beers in the evening
The beds were so comfortable but the pillows are just too big! All the staff were really friendly and helpful, our stay was amazing and i really wont to go back to New York as its a really great city. 
If your looking for some good food i would recommend the Spring Street Natural Resturaunt in SoHo, they only have a small memu but all the food is natual and free range. I had the chicken and it was beautiful. 
So presuming that the prices stay roughley the same (we paid around $1000 for 4 people in a 2 bed room for 4 nights) i would definatley recommend this hotel.

title: “great value”
text: Stayed for a week for business...price is right. Located where I had to be. Older hotel but kept very clean. Parking can be an issue. Also was not happy that side doors were not kept locked at all times. Located on busy expressway can be noisy I bet when air is not running. Good Value.

title: “New York Classic”
text:
Whether you like the Carlyle really depends on your taste. If you liked hotels with an old-world charm, this may well be your favorite hotel.
The lobby is very tasteful, with a style that appeals to all generations. The "classical influence" really begins at the elevators, which are still manned by elevator operators. Frankly, I find that a bit pretentious and unneccessary. Why demand extra labor when there's no need for it? There's a difference between excellent service and excessive service. And in the context of the Carlyle's elevator operators, this is debatable.
With my lowly corporate rate, I had a standard room on the 19th floor. I understand that the hotel prides itself on history, so I won't be overly critical about the wear-and-tear of the furnishings and finishes. My overall impression of the room was warm, tasteful and intimate. It felt like a private residence rather than a hotel. However, rooms are on the small side compared to Four Seasons and Ritz Central Park.
You should have realized by now that I'm not a big fan of classical hotels. I didn't like the Plaza (back in the good old days) or Waldorf. But I enjoyed the Carlyle because of its service. I don't know whether it is the fact that 80% of the staff speaks with a French accent or the general professionalism, but I felt that the Carlyle's service is very personal. And that, may I add, is very different from the service you get at chains like Four Seasons and Ritz-Carlton. It makes the hotel a home for its guests.
If I were to pay $600 for a standard room, where would I stay? I have to admit that Carlyle would not be on the top of my list. But we all have different tastes.
Is it worth a try? Oh, yes.

title: “To my surprise”
text: My overall experience with Four Points Sheraton is between Above Average and Excellent. I booked a room online for a Sat. night to spend a pre-valentine's day with my boyfriend. I have to say I expected the room to be small being that it is in the city. But the size of the room was fine for one night, it was I have to say cozy. The room was clean, no smells, quiet, and no bed bugs. The bed was incredibly comfortable and my boyfriend and I didn't want to get out of bed. I will definitely stay at the hotel again. Unfortunately, I would have taken pictures of the room but I forgot my camera, duh me.

title: “Paradise”
text: Friendly staff, beautiful ocean views, clean rooms, close to restaurants. The list goes on and on. I definitely will be going back.

title: “Great Deal for the Money!”
text: Our stay at Embassy Suites was very enjoyable! The staff was courteous, the hotel is lovely and our room was comfortable. We traveled with our two children and this was perfect. The indoor pool was a huge plus since it was cold and rainy outside. The price was reasonable considering that the room was spacious enough to allow my husband and I to watch TV in one area while the kids watched TV in the bedroom area. We ordered in some pizza and made an evening of it. The following morning, the complimentary buffet was hot and fresh and best of all allowed me to sleep in a little while the hubby and kids had breakfast! The only drawback is the location of the hotel, but I would definitely stay here again and recommend it to others.

title: “Classy hotel ~ only one issue......”
text:
Room 232
Highlights:
I was impressed with this hotel as a whole. The hotel was beautiful and loved the decorating and design. Husband & I enjoyed a drink at the bar, a swim in the pool & relaxing in the hot tub. The beds are quite comfortable in my opinion and hubby and I had a great nights sleep. Loved the design of the room also. Modern design and electronics in the room.
Low Points:
Breakfast is NOT complimentary but it was adequate. I think if I were to stay there again, I would probably grab a nice breakfast at another restaurant. Most of the staff was quite nice, however, there was a female at the front desk that was QUITE PRETENTIOUS!! We experienced her attitude both upon check in and check out!!

title: “K-bocker pretty good”
text:
i got 2 nights at Knickerbocker Chicago on hotwire. last week
I got a newly renovated room on 10th floor - very nice & quiet & compact.
I could see the beach front from my window
I thought the staff were excellent and enjoyed my stay. 
Providing you get a new room, it's one of the best locations in the city.
Would definately return here
but
Why do 4* hotels charge $10 daily for internet ??
Also no tea / coffee or fridge in room

title: “Right in the heart of Chinatown”
text:
We almost always stay at Hilton properties, what can we say, we love their beds!! We stayed here for 1 night, just for a place to stay on our "date night". The hotel was pretty busy, but all employees were nice, and happy to help. The rooms were clean, moderately sized, and had a large desk that went from one wall to the next, even a cordless phone. 
The showers, IMO, suck. I like hot showers, this was barely warm enough for me to tolerate. However, my bf thought it was perfect. So if you do not mind not having a really hot shower, this shouldn't be an issue.
The only other thing about the rooms, is I could still hear everything outside, even though we were on the 12th floor. I could hear buses all night. Annoying.
Since we were running hours late for everything, we decided to order room service. It came quickly, and was very good, especially the tempura chicken skewers (wish I had ordered two plates!!) However, I ordered my burger well done, it was barely medium-well. I am not one to send food back, so I forced myself to eat about half of it. Upon check out the next morning, I brought it to the attention of the desk clerk, who apologized, and corrected the problem for us. More than he needed to do. 
The location is right Chinatown, which is about a 30 min walk to AT&T Park (can't come and miss a Giants game!).

title: “Road trip stop no 4”
text:
Stayed in the Clift for 3 nights during a road trip! The hotel is boutique styled and centrally located close to Union Square.
Our room was large, very clean and comfortable. Our bed was huge and so comfortable you couldn't help but have a good nights sleep!
A couple of things to note are the high price of parking (over $50 per 24 hours!!) we found a parking lot round the corner which offered valet parking for our whole stay at $75!
Also the hotel does not offer free wifi access, for the price you pay to stay here I felt this should be included.

title: “Stayed 3 nights at beginning of August - wish we could have stayed longer!”
text: Lovely room, very large with modern facilities - flat screen TV, iron & board, tea & coffee making, modern shower cubicle with really nice toiletries - super-large bed which had the most comfortable mattress ever and soft fluffy towels. The location was excellent, just a short walk to the centre of Union Square. We did not eat in the hotel because there are lots of places nearby. The best breakfast was at Lori's just around the corner. The best evening out was at an Irish bar/restaurant just down the road and around the corner where there was a great band playing 60s, 70s, 80s music (NOT O'Douls which we went to for breakfast one morning and found the staff to be rather rude). Great hotel!

title: “Wonderful service, great with kids”
text: My husband and I stayed here with our two boys (10 & 7) for a week and had a great experience. The room was lovely and the beds were comfortable, even for my husband who has chronic back pain. Service is definitely the hotel's forte. Everyone was friendly and helpful and super responsive without being overbearing and our boys loved the nightly milk and cookies. We ate in the Rowes Wharf Sea Grille twice and were pleased that the kids' menu had real food that was delicious. And with kids, the location was excellent - we walked everywhere. Wonderful place to stay!

title: “Great Location”
text:
Stayed for one night, it was okay.
Room was spacious enough, 4th floor no elevator, though not a problem for me.
Boris at the front desk either needs a personality or a career change. Kind of cold and indifferent.
Hotels.com charges way above what is posted on the rate card in the room.
Can't beat the location, though.

title: “Had to come back again!”
text: After a one night stay we had to come again and so glad we were here for 2 nights this time. Paid the extra fee for the Griffin Club, not cheap, but definitely got our money's worth! It basically includes breakfast, lunch and dinner (heavy appetizers--plenty for dinner) AND snacks and beverages all day plus full bar after 4 pm and desserts each evening. What makes it so special is the staff in the Griffin Club--they made us feel so welcome and really wanted to be as helpful as possible--serving food, preparing drinks, acting as a concierge--they did it all especially graciously. All the staff was great and special kudos to Alison. We also like this resort because of the great pools and the lazy river. Lots of kids but not as overrun as some other resorts with water parks. Evening entertainment in the lounge also fun (tho I wish some parents had better control of their small children).

title: “Budget GEM”
text:
Clean and tidy compact room with single queensize bed, with very helpful staff.
We satyed here for two days the experience was pleasant with free parking next to the hotel. It is located a few minutes walk from the gas lamps or italian districts and I could not have found a better location.
When we arrived it was fully booked so booking is probably wise.

title: “Cash Payment”
text:
As I am from Myanmar (Burma) and we do not have internationally accepted credit card system. It would be great, if you could let us book and pay by cash. It is inconvenient to ask US residence friends to assist.
But I need more stay to make my comment on your property more accurate.

title: “Great place the price is fair!”
text:
Stayed there four night this month. Staff was great. Room was nice, new, clean, and the air conditioner was the best! It was 95 degrees the week I was there. Microwave and fridge in the room was clean! 
And for once, the towels were really soft! Most NY hotel towels are like sandpaper. 
I will stay there again. 
Great location to walk around the streets of SOHO. So many shops and places to eat your head will spin. 
You are right next to the A C E subway and the 1 line is 2 blocks away and the 6 line is a few blocks in the other direction. 
BONUS on my week was getting to see Will Smith film Men in Black 3 right down the street.

title: “Fantastic Hotel!! Smyth Hotel in Tribeca”
text:
I recently enjoyed a great stay with my wife and my youngest child (4 months) at the Smyth Hotel in Tribeca. I was very impressed at the level of service and care we received from the general manager Alistair MacLean and his team. The rooms are awesome with a very cool decor. We stayed for a week and every day we received some great recommendations for places to eat from all the team members.
I will highly recommend the Smyth Hotel in Tribeca if you are looking for a great place to stay while exploring the city of NY.
We will for sure be back.
Cheers,

title: “Not worth it”
text: Staff was unhelpful and rude. I will never stay here again. I am a single female traveler and wanted some assistance getting to my business meetings. They did not give me any assistance or directions. I was frustrated and checked out. Don't bother coming here. Stayed at another hotel and was MUCH happier!!

title: “Kids love Embassy Suite”
text:
Rooms are comfortable. Everyone in the family loves the breakfasts, esp the kids. They can make their own waffles, order omelettes, get cereal and fruit, etc. The Manager's happy hour is also a nice way to relax after a day of sight-seeing; free appetizer and drinks (soda, beer, wine and some mixed drinks).
Parking is expensive per day.

title: “Elegant and comfortable”
text:
As you enter through the scaffolding, you immediately sense an old world elegant feel to the hotel. We had booked a double queen room and were pleasantly surprised by the spacious room. (I think it was twice the size of the room at the nearby W which I will not visit again). The beds were very comfortable and the room decorations were luxurious. I enjoyed the Aveda bathroom products. There were comfortable robes for 2.
Booking online got us complimentary buffet breakfast for 2. The buffet was very nice and we sat outside on a beautiful morning. It will be nicer when the construction next door is finished.
The concierge was very helpful for dinner and recommended a local hotspot where he booked us a table that same night. That restaurant was packed with a long wait (over an hour), but we weren't that hungry so we waited at the bar. I didn't expect much since we had only just made the reservations. We were pleasantly surprised when not more than 10 minutes had passed and we were seated. the host said that they like the concierge at the Talbott and were accommodating us since we were staying there. 
Free internet for 24 hours came with the room too. We also took advantage of the passes for the local Equinox. No hotel gym can compare to a full service gym like Equinox. We had great workouts!

title: “Fantastic Weekend!”
text:
We had a fantastic weekend at the Embassy Suites near the Galleria! Check-in was a breeze (even though we were early), and someone called from the front desk a few minutes later to make sure we had everything we needed in our room. The hotel is pleasant, well-maintained and quiet, just a short walk across a parking lot (as others have mentioned) from the Galleria. We loved the hot breakfast (especially the potatoes with Italian seasoning!), and our four-year-old fell in love with the swans in the lobby pool. On Sunday morning, a sweet clown delighted the children by making balloon animals for them. What a nice, thoughtful touch!
I have only one complaint: the pool is indoors and not heated. It was a disappointment for our little boy. The cold water didn't seem to bother him that much--but because he can't swim, Mommy needed to go in the pool with him... and Mommy doesn't like cold water.
Everything else was so pleasant, however, that I just can't lower the score for that. I highly recommend the Embassy Suites... especially if you're visiting the Galleria area with children.

title: “Great location - very reasonable”
text: This is a really good base.. it is a 5 min walk from the train station, the fabulous tram system runs in the streets surrounding this block and there is a car rental just across the street too,also it is very near to all the usual places to visit in San Francisco if you choose to walk.

title: “Terribly managed hotel - poor service at understaffed reception - stay at the Sheraton or Westin, instead!”
text: For convenience, I stayed at this hotel the night before my flight. As an Hilton Diamond member, I'm accustomed to better service than I received at the hotel. It took me 20 minutes to check-in (and that was in the Honors queue!). I told the person at reception I wanted a quiet room. While noting the comments in my profile (high floor; away from elevator), he assigned a room that was near the power-up end of one of the runways, and all evening, all night, and all the next morning I heard jet engines revving to capacity every 1- to 2-minutes. I tried several times to get guest services or an operator, but the phones just "rang and rang." Every time I attempted to obtain any service, it was an interminable delay. I was told by multiple people who work there that this is a common occurrence. This is not an employee problem; it is a greedy management problem. It also took me 20 minutes to check out (again, the Honors line), and not all of my charges (room service lunch) had been posted to the account. Some guests were in line for over an hour to check in (the "regular line"). Everyone was friendly - but overwhelmed and only marginally competent. The manager of this hotel should be fired at once. I do NOT recommend staying here. Instead, stay at the Westin or Sheraton - or anywhere else! This is a poorly-staffed and poor service hotel masquerading as a fine property. Ha!

title: “Great hotel...great location...on a budget”
text: Wanted to thank the hotel for the great service...loved the breakfast included...total location! Just where we wanted to be...handy to subway. Great neighbourhood to walk in...great shopping and eating. This was our first time in Boston, and we'll be back.

title: “New York New York what a wonderful town!!!!!”
text:
Stayed at the Westin Times Square In September 2004 and booked to stay at the Le Parker Meridien in Sept 2005. The Westin was fabulous.
What a great vacation it was in 2004 so good that we are returning for a second time.
What could we find wrong with the trip........nothing.
We danced at the Cotton Club Harlem, dined at Sardis, saw Chicago (the musical), travelled on the underground, visited ground zero, walked Brooklyn Bridge and felt completely safe at all times. What a vacation. Nothing compares with our visit.

title: “Disappointing”
text:
Stayed at the Belvedere with my wife just over a week ago- our third time in about four years. Before, apart from the real and obvious advantage of location, we found the hotel comfortable, safe, welcoming and cosy for such a central location. But now? To say the least we were disappointed.
First, I was coming joining my wife there from a business trip in Boston while my wife was arriving after a seven and plus hour flight from Ireland. So she arrived early pm to check in but they would not allow her check in because the booking was in my name. Even though she had details of our joint names and address, and even though she offered to pay the full room price for our stay in advance on her credit card, they refused her entry. So she had to hang around for four hours and amazingly, when she went back and asked a different manager they relented! Not a good start.
That night a full room of college kids in the room beside us partied all night until 6.30am -despite several calls to the front desk nothing happened. Bring some serious ear plugs for these rooms!
The hotel generally is frayed at the edges - we asked for late check out which they offered us for an additional 100 bucks- no thanks!
All in all we decided we would not be staying there again.

title: “Sad excuse for a fitness room, and other disappointments”
text: We spent the week of Thanksgiving 2003 at the Metro Center, mostly because we belong to the Starwood Group and wanted to earn points, not pay as much as the Sheraton Hotels, and because the description of the fitness room seemed good. However, the stay was awful. We had to switch rooms THREE times because each one had a problem. The rooms themselves are almost acceptable for the cheap rate we paid, but the fitness room was...completely unacceptable. It should have been closed altogether because the equipment looked to be over 15 years old and there were no barbells at all on the racks. The outdoor pool and jacuzzi appeared to be nice, but we didn't use them. The hallways were filled with loud childen and the pool hours were long, which made sleeping at 10pm impossible. Might be good for a family who wants to save money and enjoy a pool, but for a couple who wants to use a gym or have nicer accomodations do yourself a favor and pay more at a nicer place. There are multiple restaurants in the area which are low-cost, which might be another attraction for families.

title: “Best Hotel in Baltimore / Fells Point”
text: Compared to the other hotels I've stayed at in Baltimore, there is nothing that comes close to Henderson's. Nothing else compares. Superior service, staff, amenities, rooms are so comfortable you almost don't want to leave. Watch the boats come into the harbor with the Dominos sugar plant in the background. Parking is easy with a lot adjacent to the property. The only word for this hotel is 'perfect'.

title: “An undiscovered gem. Perfect value. Good balance of elegance and style.”
text:
New york hotels are always cryptic. You can spend $1000 dollars a night, and still receive the worst service and a minimal room or you can find a fantastic boutique hotel for under $300.
This time, I decided to do some research on boutique hotels and my investigations lead to the Carlton. I was a bit suspicious at first, when I asked my trustworthy team of locals about the hotel and no-one, literally, out of the 5 well-connected individuals that I asked, had even heard about the hotel.
However, upon arriving and checking-in, I knew that this hotel was special. 
No, the Carlton does not boast the best service in New York (in fact, I don't think ANY hotel in New York has premium service -Hong Kong Style)
No, the Carlton's restaurant is not the best in town.
But yes, the Carlton's rooms are certainly among one of the best I have tried for under $600 Dollars in New York City. In fact, I have spent over $800 for lesser quality rooms.
The decor is a nice mix of modern and classic french, which seems very inspired in the Lé Meridien hotels (before Starwood acquired the brand)
The hotels amenities are basic. The gym is good, well equiped and decently sized. The wi-fi is excellent, it's free and its lightning fast.
The hotel's location is a little bit off the beaten path, but that can be a good thing. If you don't mind walking 4 to 5 blocks, you're really in the middle of the action.
I can sincerely say that this hotel is an undiscovered gem, which truly delivers. If you are ever in New York and can get to stay at the Carlton for under $350 Dollars (which is possible), I would definetly recommend that you stay here.
I am sure that I will be back.

title: “Great Convention Hotel”
text: We visited Boston for the first time During the International Boston Seafood Show in March of 2011 . Originally we chose The Omni Parker House Hotel but after entering the rooms, decided to look for a better option . Let's just say the Omni had too many negatives (tiny rooms, dingy looking and haunted!) After calling around for vacancies during one of the busiest conventions of the year ,we found a room at IC Boston (thank God). The front desk staff saw how tired and frustrated we were and decided to make our transition easy by upgrading our rooms to the club floor . Club is the way to go , if you have the cash to spare and are coming in for business / convention because of all the freebies you'll receive with club access, such as unlimited food and drinks and use of wifi in their lounge. Speaking of wifi, that would be my greatest complaint if any. Wifi in my opinion should be complimentary at every hotel, however at IC's worldwide it's often very pricey . The rooms are very spacious ,well appointed and CLEAN. The shower is separated from the bath and you even get a scale and loads of fresh fluffy towels. However ,their beds were a litIe too firm for my liking. Loved the gym and pool area. Concierge is wonderful This hotel is beautiful and may considering coming back to IC for next Year's Seafood Processing show- if I get a good deal .

title: “Okay ,but has problems.”
text:
Just finishing a 9 night stay in a one bedroom suite.
Pros : 
One of the nicest staff I have come across in New York .
Very clean rooms with a great kitchen. subzero fridge and freezer .
Housekeeping is wonderful.Everything worked in the suite .
Great location,good gym with a trainer.Internet was good at $9 a day.
Cons:
No coffeemaker in the room.
The smallest bathroom I have ever come across. 
Sharing the elevator with all the staff is a problem .I stooped 5 times on 1 ride to let staff on or off .Everything form room service ,mini bar ,luggage .Maids etc....Is very bad in the morning .Long lines when they are busy as the staff hold the elevator in the basement.
No problem with the shower or hot water.
Ringos there restaurant was very hit or miss .Slow drink service and they would not allow you to buy at the bar and take it to your seat.My first morning Breakfast was strange.I took my cup of Starbucks coffee in with me to the bar which they use for breakfast and the next thing I know one of the waiters is garbing my coffee and trying to pour it into a water glass .I stoped him and the manager then tells me that I need to pour it in as they are not a Starbucks but a Restaurant.There was only one person in 
there apart from me .I left and never ate there again.There is a great diner across the road.
I had a little trouble with Reception but nothing major.
Overall ,I would not stay here again for a long trip.Good for a couple of nights only.

title: “i'll sleep in the car next time.”
text: I've traveled a lot and have never stayed in a place this horrible. I'd stay just about anywhere else. Brown stains on the walls next to the bed. Unexplainable stains all over the sheets. The power in our room went out at about 10 pm and didn't turn back on until after 11. The staff didn't seem to care at all. Everything smelled like vomit. No air and 90+ degrees outside. You would be better off, and probably safer, sleeping in the alley behind the hotel.

title: “Beautiful Hotel, Expensive Extras”
text: This is a beautiful hotel with beautiful rooms. It sits right on the harbor near the original site of the Boston Tea Party. The bathrooms are exceptional. The location is not as great as some of the other upscale hotels in Boston. I only paid $100 through Priceline for the room but the extras added up to almost another $100. Parking is $39, breakfast $24 (one person), cocktail $14. The staff was okay except the gift shop attendant who was hard to understand. Go through Priceline for this one!

title: “Times Square Trendy and Pricey”
text: If you want Times Square with a trendy vibe, this is a very good option. It is a bit pricey. If you're willing to be 5 -7 blocks away the price drops significantly by $100 - 150/nt. The staff is courteous and helpful. It is very well insulated against the bustling street noise...I heard no sirens or honking horns from my room. They have a roof top bar that's good for after dinner cocktails.

title: “Almost excellent..”
text:
A lot of reviews you read about here will talk about room size. Yes, it was small but there was enough room to stash our two large cases well out of the way.
The fron desk staff were excellent, very helpful indeed and offered to give us directions to anywhere we wanted to go. This was our fourth trip to NY so we were fine but it was a nice touch. There is no gym but they do give three day complimentary passes to a gym that is less than ten blocks away. Prepare however to hand over $25 for each night of your stay as a security deposit. They did try to sting us at the end for minibar items even though we had never opened it so be aware.
We stayed here in a heatwave and on quite a few days, housekeeping put the same sheets back on the bed which was not cool.
Check out the 10th floor roof deck, it gives amazing views of Empire State, quite probably the best part of the hotel.
Location is excellent, close for midtown, downtown and home to many fine bars and restaurants. There is a restaurant attached to the hotel which was busy every night, clearly a good sign!
I would recommend but perhaps not in summer when air-conditioning was either too loud or non existent, there was never a happy medium.

title: “UBELIEVABLY NASTY!”
text:
This was by far the worst hotel experience I have had in all my years of business travel. I read some of the reviews and was hesitant to have my assistant make my reservation at the Blake, better known as the "Fake", based on numerous horrible reviews of this dump. They are ALL true. For less money I could have stayed at the Hilton or Omni right down the street, and more convenient to downtown activities...what a HUGE mistake that I actually stayed at the Fake Hotel.
This place is in such disrepair it needs to be torn down to fix all the issues, I could go on and on about the ridiculously slow elevators, the dark dingy hallways, the shredded carpet as you exit the elevators, the water damaged ceiling tiles that made me wonder if one would come crashing down on me, etc., etc., etc.
This is one time you should trust your fellow traveler reviews and avoid this place at all cost. Your better off getting a room at a motel six.
AVOID THE "FAKE HOTEL" AT ALL COSTS! CONSIDER YOURSELF WARNED!

title: “Right Next to Hobby Airport Houston”
text:
I could see planes taking off from my room window...hear it too! Finding food nearby is a chore, and being near an airport, this surprised me. Hotels everywhere, but no familiar food restaurants, and I am not that adventurous when eating out of town...especially unknown mexican restaurants. The Hertz rental car place is right behind, so you can return in a jiffy. Other than a place to drop your head before an early flight, useless hotel and not for any form of comfort or rest.
Shower bar in my room was falling off.
Bath amenities did smell nice.
Breakfast area is tiny, so if a group is in there, forget it.

title: “Awesome Service”
text: I travel to LA frequently for business and always stay at the Sheraton Gateway because of their close proximity to the airport. The hotel staff is very accommadating, especially the Front Desk Staff. On my most recent visit I had a minor issue with my room. I called down to the Front Desk and Diane took care of it within seconds. That's the type of friendly service you expect when you visit various hotels. I definitely recommend this hotel to others.

title: “note to new owners”
text:
4 days and i'm in love. the hotel has been for sale for some time as reported in all the local newspapers. i think the most productive review would be a highlight of the things the buyers shouldn't touch.
1. the big four restaurant - don't touch the chef or the decor. the grand era of the union pacific railroad is alive in there, the bar is filled with local eccentrics, local gentry, business travelers and tourists, a fabulous place. the food is very very good and the service is experienced, friendly and efficient. DON'T TOUCH IT
2. the lobby, it's pure heaven.
3. those vines covering the exterior, a little bit of London
We look forward to a thoughtful renovation of the rooms (they're in various states of uninspired remodel).
THIS HOTEL IS A GEM, FOR HEAVENS SAKE I HOPE THE BUYERS SEE THIS AND HAVE THE TALENT TO DELIVER THE POSSIBILITIES IT HAS TO OFFER.

title: “nice location, good value”
text: 70 Park is a nice hotel. The rooms are small, but this is NYC. I would decrib the decor as grandma chic. Our room had a 42 in flat screen, ipod docking station, wine glasses and a comfy bed. The staff was very accomdating, from the doorman helping with parking to security helping return my wife's wallet which she left in the safe. The hotel offers a wine hour at 5pm in lobby for free, which is a nice touch. There was also free coffee and tea in the morning. Location is about two block from Grand Central Station, which is cool place to check out. Went to the Oyster Bar very old school, worth the walk.

title: “Good price”
text:
Stayed at the Knickerbocker on 11-20-05 and 11-21-05. I read the reviews about the small rooms. They are accurate. The room was tiny, but clean and comforatble. I stayed on 12th floor and noise was not a problem. I got a great price ( $76/ night)- Well worth the price. 
 I parked at self parking directly across the street for $21/day- but if you need your car, you should park valet.
Location was fine, staff friendly and helpful. Great place for the price, although with 2 people in a room it may be to small- I had a king room.

title: “A converted Hampton Inn with some problems”
text:
This Hampton Inn was converted from another hotel. Actually, there is a similar, attached building which is a Days Inn and the property has the feel of a Days Inn more than a higher caliber Hampton Inn. From the outside you can see the old sliding glass doors and inside the rooms you'll realize not everything was renovated to make the hotel look like a Hampton Inn. Still, in the rooms you will definitely find all of the Hampton style furniture and decorations you would expect.
When I checked in I wondered if I had made a mistake booking this hotel. A couple was changing rooms because their room smelled bad. Everything seemed as good as they could have been in my converted Hampton Inn hotel room until I saw a cockroach running across the floor. I looked under the bed skirt and found a nasty old sock that wasn't removed by housekeeping. Unfortunately I was already settled into my room so I didn't bother asking to be moved plus I didn't want to get into a worse situation. I did not sleep well with the thought of a cockroach running around the beds.
If you don't mind cockroaches, the beds were comfortable and the furniture is nice in the room. The bathroom was attractive with marble although I'm guessing the bathtub was old because it didn't drain well.
If you stay at Hampton Inns and expect a certain level of quality this hotel is definitely not for you. The other Hampton in the area is the real thing although it will likely be more expensive.

title: “Wonderful visit to DC”
text: My family and I stayed at this Embassy Suites hotel for 2 nights 12/ 21 /06 - 12/23/06 based on the tripadvisor reviews. I have been to DC many times for business, but this was the first pleasure only visit, and we had a wonderful time, including our experience at the Embassy. This hotel is very clean; and the rooms are quite spacious with numerous amenities. The lobby is simply lovely, and creates a relaxing ambiance. Complimentary breakfast and evening reception were very nice touches. Every member of my family enjoyed being here, especially the children. This hotel also sells tickets for various tours, and it is very close to the major attractions. Their restaurant, however is not very appealing, and they need more bell captain help. We had to use the cart to take our luggage to our room even though we arrived early in the evening. Despite these few negatives this will be my hotel of choice on my next vist to DC.

title: “Don't read their website”
text:
This is a nice hotel, but sadly we started out on the wrong foot. Wee had booked this hotel because their website said they had a separate shower and bath. When we checked in the room did not have this feature, the room is fine, could use some minor work, but overall above average. The common areas are very nice, clean, modern, etc. The help was very pleasant and accommodating. The breakfast (not included) was mediocre.
The location is great, convenient to most major attractions in Baltimore.
The concierge didn't know much, she tried but was not well trained.

title: “So comfortable”
text: Just returned from a weeks stay in this hotel, we booked a bay view room, the view was stunning, over the city to Alcatraz. The bed was ultra comfortable, best one we've ever had in a hotel. Location and staff were fantastic. Only thig we can grumble about is the ten dollar per day charge for wifi which when we all rely on it these days seems very expensive

title: “Worth a stay.”
text:
We spent a week in this hotel, and found no fault worth mentioning. we where here for a vacation. The neighborhood is Greek Town, which I found to be a plus. Always like to try something new. We are walkers, so we did a lot of walking, but there a watertaxis(within a couple blocks of the Hotel) or buses if you don't care to walk, but you miss a lot of the flavor of Chicago by just riding through it.
Getting back to the neighborhood, there are many restaurants within a couple of blocks of the hotel that offer excellent food. For Breakfast we walked to Meli's, about two blocks away, for the BEST Breakfast you'll run across in the whole of Chicago, very reasonable.
Would definitely stay at this property again,when in Chicago

title: “Crowne Plaza Times Square New York”
text:
We just got back from our stay in New York. We stayed at the Crowne Plaza Times Square and this hotel is absoutely amazing. The rooms are clean and large. The bathroom was great and always had fresh towels. We asked for extra blankets and they brought them to our room within that hour. The staff in the hotel are friendly and attentive, and always on their toes. After 10:30 PM there is security at the elevators making sure that everyone that was going to their room had rooms keys. They never let anyone on the elevators without a room key after 10:30 PM. The rooms had flat screen TV's with plenty of channels to see. One disappointment is that you have to pay 20.00 a day if you want to use the internet whether if it is in your room or in the lobby. 
The location of this hotel is in the heart of Times Square, perfect location. Ask for a room facing Times Square, we were on the 32nd floor and we did not hear any traffic. I would recommend this hotel to anyone, and we will stay there again when we return.

title: “Nice, cozy hotel, friendly staff, great location”
text: We enjoyed our stay. All of the staff were very helpful. Our room was clean, nicely furnished. Enjoyed the gas fireplace and stone-tiled shower. Happy hour is a good value and the views from the lounge are great. Some reviewers said thd hotel was too far, but we found it very convienient to Pike Place, shopping etc.

title: “Not worth the trade off”
text:
This hotel does have a good location, pleasant enough staff and nice decor. The trade off is apparently made in room size (micro) and basic amenities which are missing or for which one must pay extra. Call me crazy, but I do expect to be able to get coffee... even bad coffee... somewhere in a hotel. Either the crappy brew-it-yourself or in the lobby. Nope.
Towels and oddly, bathmats, were in short supply considering the shower is wide open to the bathroom and puts water all over the floor.
The pool is hip, but waaaay smaller than pictures make it seem. Unheated as well, but it was in the 90s so we didn't care.

title: “Great Location”
text: We were in room 814 West Tower. Two queen beds with a nice view of the river. The bathroom is small with very little space to set anything down, like a curling iron or make-up bag.
