We got a AAA rate of $143.10 per night which was the best price I could find for similar hotels in downtown Chicago. We met another couple who got a priceline rate the same weekend for $79. Guess I better try priceline next time. The hotel is well cared for and I love the hustle and bustle of a large full service hotel in a big city, so this hotel is great. You can't beat the location, easily walked up and down State Street and Michigan Ave for shopping. Easily walked to Navy Pier and the shops at Oak Street. We even walked to Greek Town although that was a little longer walk than most people might like. Check is was a breeze and we used the express check out. The only hot tip I can think of is, park around the corner for $38 per night vs. the $52 at the hotel.

title: “Great location with good value for money”
text:
Incidentally, I hadn't read reviews prior to staying here and decided solely based on price. However, I must say that I enjoyed my stay. The location was very ideal. All local attractions are within a 15 minute walk (White House, Smithsonian). Now, that is close! It's also very close to the metro underground subway system. The staff were also very professional. In fact, they were quite nice - almost friendly, even. Also, they were very informative.
The rooms itself were well maintained. It was simple and clean. Also, in my honest opinion, I think the hotel is good value for money. Compared to other hotels around, I think I got a great deal, considering it's prime location. So, I would definitely recommend the District to anyone traveling to the D.C. area. Check it out.

title: “Great location and value!”
text: Location just off Times Square is great. Cost is VERY reasonable for NYC. Were there during a cold spell, but nothing we did cooled the room low enough for our preference - even with the thremostat set to 60 and the fan on high the room never cooled. Restaurant has decent food but is over-priced. Rooms were very clean and hotel staff were very helpful. Paid $150/night for a weekend. Would not hesitate to stay here again as long as I could get the room for $225 or less.

title: “Very nice and quiet...”
text: Everything was very clean and my stay was very pleasant. I've stayed at "5 star" hotels whose rooms and ammenties were not as nice as Extended Stay Deluxe. I defintely recommend this hotel.

title: “Midtown Magnificence”
text: We have stayed at several hotels in NYC and Le Parker Meridien is now our favorite. The staff is very friendly, helpful, and engaging. The junior suite provides modern styling and spaciousness rarely found in a Manhattan hotel room. We are used to jam-packed rooms when staying in the city and couldn't believe a Midtown room with separate sleeping, sitting, and work areas. All the furniture and decor were modern and the room and overall hotel were very clean. The bathroom was large and had a tiled, walk-in shower. We didn't use any of the restaurant facilities because we like to explore the plethora of restaurant offerings that are within easy walking distance of this centrally-located hotel. I would highly recommend this property to anyone staying in Midtown Manhattan, and I would not hesitate to make reservations at this location again on a future trip.

title: “Sleeping was impossible!”
text: We stayed at this hotel for several days in October. The room was clean and spacious, and the location seemed perfect. It is across the street from North Station and a trolley tour spot. The problem is that the hotel is surrounded by bars, and the windows do not block any noise whatsoever! Friday night - bar fights right outside, screaming, cursing, garbage trucks, etc all night long. Saturday night - a repeat of Friday night with the added adventure of a man's bloodcurdling scream followed by sirens and firetrucks outside. Although the hotel slightly discounted our room because of the noise, I would not recommend this hotel to anyone on a weekend night.

title: “Filthy Rooms, Rude Staff, and cockroaches”
text: This may be a NYC landmark having hosted several celebrities from the 60's and 70's. However, that was also the last time they cleaned, painted and repaired this insanely filthy property. There were tiles missing in the 'kitchenette' with encrusted food filling in the space. Stains of who knows what dripping down the walls, window air conditioner was hanging half out the window ready to fall. And the topping on this cake is cockroaches. The incredibly rude staff refused to refund my credit card imprint, stating we had to speak to the 'accountant'. I had to file a complaint with Visa since there no 'accountant' seems to exist and they won't refund the nights stay. Do yourself a favor and stay next door at the Chelsea Savoy or up the street at the Affinia.

title: “Lovely hotel, pefect location, friendly staff & fab city!”
text:
We were greeted by extremely friendly staff upon arrival. We asked for a large room and we were given just that! Spacious & very clean.
Hotel had great amenities but unfortunately we weren't able to make the most of them as we were on a road trip to Virginia, New Jersey, Atlantic City & New York.
Ritten Square in Philly is just gorgeous!
Thanks for a wonderful stay! x

title: “Location and cozy! Great”
text: We had never been to San Fran so wanted something within walking distance to all the main waterfront attractions. Our travel agent, Terri, suggested this place and said it had a great location and cozier feel than some other hotels. She was right. It was our honeymoon and they made sure to congratulate us and sent champagne to our room. The room is not the most modern room but there was tons of space especially in the bathroom. Our view was the interior garden but we loved it because it was SO quiet. The front desk helped us with places to get batteries, food and some tours. Also there is a major grocery store right next door for all the little things you need. The complimentary cocktails in the evening were great...I love Italian beer and they don't skimp. It is a good way to relax after the day of sight seeing. My only gripe was the breakfast...or lack there of. Coffee, tea, hot chocolate and biscotti is nice but some fruit and breakfast bars would be a great touch. Other than that...I would stay here again in a second.--Chloe

title: “Classy Hotel in Downtown”
text: The hotel is obviously renovated from better times in the city. The rooms are enormous and the hotel has a nice classic feeling to it. The only downfall is that it's in downtown Detroit, which still hasn't really had any comeback. The staff was friendly and the hotel prices were not too terrible for the quality of the service/food. I do recall a $10 cereal in the hotel restaurant in the morning, which was a little ridiculous. But overall, I'd return.

title: “So Spacious!”
text:
What a wonderful hotel/deal for Manhattan.
This hotel is a hidden gem it seems in the sea of cruddy budget hotels in the city. It is labeled as a three star and you can truly find it for about the same price as the one and two stars in the area. The rooms were spacious and the view was great, right by the empire state building and the Chrysler building. 
The staff was friendly. The only complaint I would have would be that our bed was so firm, rock firm. But truly fantastic otherwise.

title: “Excellence for a week stay to explore downtown, but no longer than tha”
text:
Free breakfast and light-foods (monday to Wednesday). Other Residence in have M-Th
Valet parking $38, you can park 1 block away for $8-$15 a day (average is $1/hr). Watch out for game nights, then its a bit of a hassle ($12) 
Gym have a funky smell 
Extremely inconvenient having to insert your key to use the elevator every time you press the button, so inconvenient and a hassle. I know this is a security thing, but there got to be a better and less inconvenient way to do this. 
Food looks fancy. 
You cannot open the window (not good for long stay - its not healthy)
No door to separate your bed from the kitchen. So you get marinate in foods (hard to sleep)
This place is more like a hotel (a convenient hotel). Excellence for a week while you visiting downtown. Its worth it. However if you look for a place to cook at often and stay longer, this is not a good place due to the kitchen/room layout, no fresh air, and parking hassles. 
They have a great housekeeping team.
Room/kitchen looks fancy
Stove (no oven) and there are kitchenwares. However their non-stick pans are all damaged.

title: “Above the rest”
text:
I am always super worried when I find a seemingly great hotel, at a great rate, in a great location but this Hotel truly surprised us..in a good way!
We always try to book directly through hotels as they will most often match booking site rates, and will also suggest options you may not have considered. Hotel Andra had a great "Northern Neighbours" deal that chopped 15% off the listed price, discounted valet parking 50% and came with discount cards to Macy's. Of course you had to be from B.C. or Alberta to qualify but there were many specials which carried similar options as well.
We snagged a SPACIOUS king room that by many other chains, would be considered a junior suite. There was a massive king bed, separate sitting area, lots of work space, wet bar, makeup counter, and very "scandinavian" bathroom that I absolutely loved the shower!
Needless to say, you are in an absolutely fantastic location. We parked our car the day we arrived and didn't go back to it, until we were leaving seattle. Everything is within walking distance, no need to take transit either. There is an excellent greek restaurant on the main lobby floor that we ate at a few times, even just for a quick beer/snack between our ventures around the city.
Even though the hotel was quite busy, it never reflected poorly in the service. We were well taken care of from check-in to check out. Make sure you also take some time to check out the library in the lobby, kick back by the fireplace and enjoy a glass of wine served straight to you from Lola..
I would absolutely recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a comfortable, well managed hotel in a wicked location. I've never slept better away from home.

title: “Bell Desk to Front Desk”
text:
This hotel is dripping with Customer Service. They aren't lacking in any area when it comes to the needs of the guest. Everyone is so polite, friendly and above all extremely helpful. Andrew Franks who manages the reservations desk is a great front man for this hotel who only wants to make sure that you are completely satisfied with your acomodations, to Mark the Food and Beverage manager who is all over the Sports Bar being a hands on manager attending to any and all patrons making sure they are set, to Dan and Rita in concierge who are so helpful no matter what it is. Just call Rita and she can help get you a reservation in some of the best eateries in Dallas, and finally Amanda and Josiah at the bell desk who are happy to engage you in conversation or assist in any needs you have above and beyond luggage.
I am not related to any of these people. I have stayed there now 3 times in the last year and i would never consider staying anywhere else in Dallas because these guys treat you like an old friend and i'm a very tough critic when it comes to customer service.

title: “Not what I was expecting...”
text: I stayed at this hotel during my first work trip to Los Angeles. The staff was very nice and the bistro in the hotel lobby was great, but the rooms were less than desirable. Everything is outdated, the carpet is stained and overall, I was not impressed at all. For my first trip to LA, I was very disappointed.

title: “Great location...horrible bartender”
text: I recently stayed here and loved the location!! The subway is extremely close as is 5th ave and of course Central Park. There was a great deli around the corner (Amanda's Deli) where you can get a cheap but great breakfast sandwich. However, the bartender was awful!! A couple of days I had extra time on my schedule and wanted a drink but the bartender took forever and when I did get A drink...I never got another one. That's was definitely the worst part of my stay and I would recommend the hotel to anyone...just get your drinks anywhere else.

title: “Nothing special”
text: We were a bit disappointed with the Hilton ... not quite 4* in our opinion. It was functional, but nothing special. If you need a bed for the night it does the job, but be prepared to pay extra for any incidentals such as baggage check.

title: “Nice but overpriced”
text:
My husband and I spent labor day weekend at Hotel Contessa. 
Pros: The hotel and restaurant/bar area was very nice. The hotel has a great location on the riverwalk. The hotel is a little further away from the restuarants on the riverwalk but I thought that was better to be away from the noise. I thought the bell service was outstanding.
Cons: The bed was a little hard. We did have some problems with our bathroom though. The outlet in the bathroom did not work and the faucet in the shower was falling off.( This was a little disappointing for the price we paid for the room) We also paid to have a view of the riverwalk and the view was not worth the upgrade. Also we could hear cars passing on the street below all night. I also thought the price of the valet parking was a little expensive too. In the previous review, they had to wait a half an hour to get their car but we never had this problem. We would call and go downstairs and our car would be waiting for us. I also agree with previous review too that the pool is small and not enough lounge chairs.
Overall I think the hotel is nice but it is not worth the price. I don't think I would return to this hotel

title: “Awesome”
text: Great place! nicest hotel in Colorado. The hotel staff are friendly and fun. The room was fantastic, clean and comfy.

title: “The best hotel in NYC!”
text:
How could anyone not love the Andaz! On Friday, June 25, we were coming from Boston which is usually a 3 1/2 hour trip by car; our trip took almost 7 hours. (accidents and storms) When we finally arrived at the Andaz, Chad welcomed us with open arms and a glass of wine! 
Our check-in took about two minutes. Chad escorted us to our beautiful room on the 17th floor, a large king. Chad was never in a hurry; he answered all our questions and wanted to know if we were satisfied and if there was anything else he could do for us! 
Customer Service at the Andaz is a model for all! It's all about you! Non-alcoholic beverages and snacks are free! Sometimes, you just need a bottle of water or a coke, it's right there!
Our room included breakfast. When we went to the restaurant, we met Hasan, #107. He is young, energetic and such an asset to the Andaz. Our food was ordered immediately and delivered, just the way we wanted. He shared his wonderful story with us because we asked. Our breakfast was a wonderful experience.
At times the Andaz is out of our price range. My husband and I are both teachers, so we are very conscious about finances. So, at times we have had to choose other hotels. They have never lived up to the standards of the Andaz. 
Since both of our children live in NYC, we want to see them. 
The Andaz is and always will be our first choice. Unfortunately, we know at times we'll have to settle for less.
This is the best hotel in NYC!
Sincerely,
Jane and Mike

title: “Enjoyable stay”
text: The service was excellent and the hotel was great. Enjoyed my short stay there and wished I had stayed longer.

title: “Really enjoyed our stay!!”
text: We were very pleased with our stay at the Radisson Suite Hotel Rancho Bernardo. We recently stayed for three nights. The location was nice as it was away from the city but close enough to be able to be anywhere in about 20 minutes or less. The bed was very comfortable and we enjoyed having a separate seating area and TV that spun to face the bed or the seating area. The hotel offered a free breakfast at the restaurant on property.. which was a nice feature but.. the food wasn't very good. Overall.. we really enjoyed our stay and would stay here again.

title: “Good location - another US large hotel”
text:
I stayed for some nights at the Hyatt, i have been there before I think, many years ago.
It was ok, and probably deserves the very good characteristic, even if my room was at the far end of a looong corridor. It is not a cozy hotel, though, very businesslike, and the food was very so-so.
All in all, I was there because it was chosen for me, probably would have chosen soewhere else if I was on my own

title: “It's all here”
text:
We loved our stay at this resort! Not too big, not too small with beautiful views, amazing pools clean, comfortable rooms and efficient, friendly service. 
Be sure to look for discounted rates- we used our AAA membership & got a room for $143/night on a weekend, including $20 credit for breakfast buffet each day, which was delicious & offered a lot of variety. Front desk staff generously upgraded us to a lake view room, which was lovely and had plenty of space for our family of five. We were close to everything, yet this has a true resort feel and the service is great.

title: “A nice hotel at downtown”
text:
Overall, I like the hotel. It has a great location at downtown. It also has a good value for money, in my opinion (I used a corporate rate), compared to other hotels in LA.
The downside is, as others said, the facilities are old and need an upgrade. When I was there, the room thermostat broke down and a mechanic needed almost an hour and 2 persons to do fix it. Also, the card room key is very sensitive to iPad and handphones, according to the security. Many times, my keys did not work and had to be reset because I place them near my iPad. It was very annoying

title: “Very good location ok room”
text: Stayed here for a few nights, and the hotel is very good located. Very big hotel with a lot of rooms. It is a bit old but ok. The price was a bit expensive for the fact that it is a medium hotel. Staff was friendly and helpful

title: “New Culture”
text: I used to regard the Hotel Bel-Air as a wonderful escape. Unfortunately, a lot of the magic of this idyllic property has gone. Whilst the renovations to the hotel rooms were necessary, the whole culture of the hotel has changed. I had an unpleasant experience at the restaurant one night that became indicative of the change that has taken place and which was enough to alienate me from the hotel and instead to go to the comfort of the restaurant at the Peninsula Hotel. The restaurant clearly now brings considerably more people to the hotel and this is great for hotel revenue and exposure, but can be very stressful for guests. To what extent hotel guests receive preference now is debatable. The Bel-Air is no longer a 'hideaway' and the new restaurant may have produced a situation whereby the carrying capacity of the resort is exceeded to the detriment of hotel guests and those seeking a quiet place to exhale and enjoy the privacy of the Bel-Air culture that once was.

title: “Lots of history but that's in the past”
text:
The hotel is gorgeous and rooms royally appointed with comfy beds, 6 pillows, a very nice large HD flat screen TV, great toiletries, two airline check-in kiosks and numerous fast elevators etc. Overall if was a fairly good stay BUT there are some drawbacks. I got a room with two bathrooms which was great EXCEPT that when the neighbors on either side took their showers at 6 a.m. the bathroom in my room acted like an echo chamber and made it feel like I was actually in the shower with them. When the folks next door came home one night overly inebriated screaming in the halls and bouncing against the walls (not the hotel's fault) and THEN ran their shower at 4 a.m. for 30 minutes I was NOT a happy camper.
The biggest issue was Internet access charges that are about as non-business friendly as it gets. Paying $7.50 for up to an hour for net use is highway robbery to begin with but that's PER DEVICE. Have a pc and an iPad? Ca-ching times two, Even if you just use the Internet for 5 minutes you are charged $7.50. Log on again? Another $7.50 You can opt to pay $14./95/day for unlimited access but again that's per device. If you are staying for 4 or 5 days pay the $39.95 flat rate for up to 5 days, but better yet, if you are like most who just read and respond to 1-2 e-mails at best accessing the net for 10-15 minutes a day, throw yourself at the mercy of the front desk clerk and they may give you a promo code that lets you access the Internet for free. Most of the charges in the gift shops, bars, restaurants etc, are dramatically overpriced but opulence has its price for sure.
A couple of gems- Tamarind around the corner on Wabash had incredible food at incredibly low prices. The same can be said for Uncle Henry's Chicken (dont laugh- they have killer fried chicken). Eleven about 4 blocks south had great breakfasts too.The concierge desk was very helpful as were the bell clerks. They could have used more people at he Hilton Honors desk- I am an Honors member but it was faster in the non-Honors line. There is construction going on here too so if you sleep past 8 a.m. you may be outta luck cuz the jackhammers start early...
I would stay at the Hilton again for sure BUT they need to get real with Internet charges and I need to make sure I close my bathrooms door. One shower is usually more than enough...

title: “Would definitely stay again!!!”
text: Beautiful property, great location, friendly staff... very pleased with our stay. Valet parking is a bit pricey though. otherwise, NO issues.

title: “I will never stay there again.”
text:
How The Drake has a good reputation is a wonder to me. My first bad experience was being placed adjacent to the elevator lobby. I went out for the day, then dinner, and arrived late in my room. Looking forward to a good rest, I pulled the covers back and smelled a musty scent. I got in bed and sunk into a mattress that was probably never flipped- it smelled like dirty people. The pillows were stinky like filthy hair. It was so late I decided to wait until the morning to complain and covered my pillows and bed with towels. In the morning I went to the front desk and complained and they let me move down the hall- I moved myself. They offered me 2 free breakfasts.
There was a constant wait at the front desk. One friend had to wait until 5:00pm for her room. The room she was supposed to get was never available. On top of all of that, my room never cooled properly, the furniture was old and outdated, the elevators are slow, there was a rotting cucumber in the refrigerator, sheets were not turned down at night, and wi-fi cost $12 plus a day- ridiculous.
I will never stay at The Drake in Chicago again.

title: “Great Location and Friendly Staff”
text: Very Nice and clean rooms, good breakfast and very good staff. Location was the key. If I go back to NYC, I wouldnt stay anywhere else except this hotel.

title: “Pleasantly surprised”
text: Spent one weekend night. Great location. Courteous staff. Early chek in. Basic rooms but clean. Nconvenient to everything. Nice weekend Buffett breakfast. Expensive but fast valet. Starbucks on sight needs more staff. Accidentlt left shirt in closet. Called security who kept it for me when I returned.

title: “Good, not great”
text: Service was quite good, except for the fact that they were not able to fix the a/c properly for 4 days. Rooms & lobby look great, but very little storage space in the room (no drawers, one small closet) or in the bathroom for toiletries, which was pretty uncomfortable. Pretty good value for NYC.

title: “Top Notch Hotel”
text:
My wife and I took our annual trip to NYC on July 13th and returned on July 17th, so we got to spend 3 fabulous nights at the Sofitel. Once I laid on the bed for the first time, I wished I was staying there for a month. The room itself is a perfect size with plenty of storage for clothes and anything else you may want to store. We were also extremely happy with the bathroom and the oversized towels that were provided. The bathroom was tastefully decorated, had great lighting and there was tons of room for a NYC bathroom. We stayed in room 1720 and had a nice view of the Chrysler building at night. During the day, you were looking down into an alley and on rooftops. Not very appealing, but the night time made up for it.
The location can not be beat, as it is right on 44th street between 5th and 6th avenue. Extremely close to all the great midtown attractions, yet in its own little quiet world. In fact, you would never know that you are only a block and a half from the ever bustling Times Square. We ate at the Red Flame diner next door one evening and had a very nice meal for a reasonable price. We sat by the window, so we got to watch NY walk by as we ate. 
Also.....I wanted to extend thanks to the Sofitel for the following reason. The day before we were set to leave, my wife got food poisoning from the Rock Center Cafe in Rockefeller Center. She was sick all day and night to the point she couldnt even stand up. Our flight did not leave until 8:30pm on that day, so we had originally planned to store our luggage and do some more sightseeing. Well, that obviously wasnt going to happen. I asked the front desk if we could have late check out (only expecting a couple hours at most). She gave us until 8pm for no extra charge because of the circumstances. Normally, they would charge half the daily rate which would have been an extra $175. Needless to say, we were very grateful for their cooperation. Also, in past cases where we have been granted late checkout, the housekeepers bother you every 15 minutes until you leave. We stayed until 6pm without a peep out of anyone. That was very appreciated since my wife was asleep. 
I thoroughly enjoyed this hotel. I didnt have one complaint.

title: “Best hotel sleep ever”
text:
We got a deal thru Priceline, which made it even better. Great location. Close to everything and on the T-lines. PLUS...the bed was PERFECT. And the rooms were quiet. We were very near to the elevator which made me, a seasoned hotel traveller, nervous. But...not to worry. Quiet as can be. Pet friendly. Great place. I plan to go back on my next Boston visit. AND....its almost on TOP of the TD Garden for all bball and hockey games. SCORE!
 Stay here. You'll be happy.

title: “Excellent for Business Travel”
text:
I needed a hotel for a single night at the beginning of December. I tried the Hotel Mela for mys ingle night needs. It was an excellent choice for me.
 The street frontage of the hotel is very small and hard to find, but it is worth the search. It is located on 44th Street between Broadway and 6th Avenue. There is a parking garage directly next to the hotel and its restaurant. (Parking was $50 for the night which was not unreasonable for the area.)
 Check-in was very easy, and there were no problems with the elevators (as some prior reviews had mentioned). My room was on the 14th floor, and was small, but manageable for my one night stay. My room had a bed, armoire, and mini-bar cabinet. There were built-in lights on the bed's headboard. There was a single floor lamp. Notably, there was no chair and no desk. For my work, I was able to work on my laptop while sitting on the bed -- but if a desk is important for you may want to make sure you ask the reservationist when you make your booking. 
 The bathroom was exceptionally clean and well-appointed. I could not have asked for more. 
 I think my room was known as "superior". But, if you are staying for a prolonged vacation, I think you might want to opt for one of the hotel's larger rooms. 
 I ordered room service from the hotel's restaurant, and I was pleasantly surprised by the quality of the food and the speed of its delivery. 
 Overall, my experience at Hotel Mela was very good, and I would recommend this Hotel to anyone staying in the Times Square area in New York CIty.

title: “Sleepless in DC”
text:
Omni Shoreham is a lovely old hotel only a few metro stops from central DC. The lobby looks fabulous with all the crystal chandelier and fancy leather sofas. However the room I, my wife and our two children had for a week was more standard: two queen size beds, one chair, small table and a drawer, small walk in wardrobe. There was a small balcony but for some reason the door was removed and it was therefore inaccessible. We had a view to the Calvert Street but there was some humidity between the glasses of the window so we could barely see through it. The pool area was great, especially for the kids. It was not too deep and there’s also a small Jacuzzi.
We joined the loyalty program, mostly because of the free Internet, which eventually was most of the time unusable. We were able to connect the Wi-Fi but obviously the capacity of the service provider was so poor, the connection jammed all the time. Early in the morning or very late night we could check our emails etc. 
There is air conditioning in the rooms but it’s VERY loud. Don’t forget to bring your own earplugs with you or ask them at the reception!
If you’re member of the loyalty program you get also TWO free morning beverages delivered to your door or room, despite of the number of guests in the room. This was nice extra and most of the days worked fine but it’s hard to understand the limit of two drinks. Most of the mornings this worked fine. A morning after a nightly fire alarm we found the order left in the door but were later called back and asked if we wanted our tea and juice delivered later that day.
Finally a few words about the fire alarms: during our stay of seven nights we heard several fire alarms and there were two full evacuations. First one around 6am and the second one 1am. After the first one we got a written apology but no explanation from the hotel management and we understand accidents and errors happen. However the second event was handled very poorly. First the evacuation in the middle of the night, then only a few minutes after we were back in our beds several new alarms every two – three minutes! Eventually we went back down to the lobby to speak with the staff, just to find only one poor lady trying to handle a queue of families checking out.
Later that night I spoke with the Fire Chief on site who explained the situation: There was a contractor doing something with the elevators and because of them there was some leakage in the pipes that activated the fire alarm. I consider it to be on the hotels responsibility to make sure their contractors do their job properly and without causing unnecessary trouble for the hotel guests. 
Our two children were very scared to sleep rest of the week and as the first thing after our arrival at our next hotel in NYC, they asked if there will be any fire alarms at that hotel. Anyway the day after “the sleepless night of alarms” was completely ruined. 
What would we have expected then? An apology at least! Also, as it was clearly the hotels mistake, I think a one night refund, would have been a fair compensation. We arrived with great expectations but left with soar taste in mouth.

title: “Happy Anniversary to us :)”
text: My husband and I stayed here for our 28th wedding anniversary. It was a great 3 night stay. We have already booked our room for 4 days for our summer vacation next year. While the rooms are not the most beautiful, they are very clean, beds are comfortable and the staff is amazing. The grounds are gorgeous. Who wouldn't love to have a beach island to vacation on? We will be back.

title: “Great Location”
text: I am a little disappointed the how 'old' the room is and feels. The furniture and decorations leave a little to be desired, especially in a $300 a night room. The location is just about perfect though (walking distance to the beach) and the staff is very nice.

title: “A very late check in, made up for.”
text: My family and i arrived on Friday June 14th just after three pm. Upon check in I was informed that our room was not quite ready. So we waited and waited and waited. Appx 4:40 pm our room was finally ready. I inquired after appx one hour and asked for and received a comp on valet. Later i was given comp drink coupons. The staff was very nice.

title: “Large rooms”
text: We stayed four nights in a room with a king-size bed. Reviewers are spot on that the rooms are large by any standard and the location was perfect for our needs. We found our room to be quiet but don't expect a view. The only knock for us was when we went downstairs to print our boarding passes (flew Southwest Airlines) and paid $16 to print out 4 pages. Ugh! Also had to pay for wi-fi in our room since my husband was working while on vacation. Wi-fi downstairs in the lobby is free. Our room had a large desk area running the width of the room and two closets which was perfect for us. Friendly staff and a nice bar area!

title: “Great Location but DEFINITELY not a 4 Star Hotel!”
text:
We were very disappointed with what we got from this supposed 4 star hotel. The room was miniscule - smaller than an office cubicle. We had no room to maneuver around on another in the little floor space and there wasn't even a closet! No mini fridge, very small bathroom, extremely shallow sink, scratchy robe. Wireless Internet is included for free, which is a nice bonus. Lobby is swanky, beds are clean and comfy, but the 4 star rating is very misleading. We used Priceline and ended up still feeling like we'd been deceived.
That being said, it was an easy walk to Michigan Ave and just around the corner from several wonderful eat spots. Check out Orange on Clark St. for wonderful breakfast! 
For the price we paid via Priceline, it was a decent value. Still, no way this was a 4 star level. Seek elsewhere!

title: “Great stay”
text:
Perfect for sightseeing in Philly, right in the middle of Old City. It was easy walk to everything.
The room is nice and super clean, the best part about this hotel is the staff. They were friendly and helpful. Will recommend this hotel to every one i know.

title: “Great location but a little noisy”
text:
Visited NY with my boyfriend during Valentine's Day weekend and stayed at the Marrakech Hotel. If driving into NY, the Marrakech is ideally located since it is in the Upper West Side area (so you don't have to deal with driving downtown). Plus, there is a parking garage close by (located at 101st - between Broadway and Amsterdam) that is reasonably priced. Another bonus is that the number 1 subway stop is just a couple of steps from the hotel. 
As for the hotel: we stayed in a room with a 'queen' size bed. I have to warn you that their 'queen' is actually a double-sized bed. The room was small but clean. Don't expect anything too fancy - and bring hair conditioner if you use it because the hotel only provides shampoo. The walls are thin and so you can hear everything. The first night, we slept horribly because we were woken up by slamming doors and people in the hallway. Also, we were unlucky to have a room where the was a water pipe right by the bed so we had to deal with water draining/dripping throughout the night. Secone night we slept with earplugs and that solved the problem.
People at the front desk were friendly and helpful but they didn't seem to be able to give many suggestions with regards to good restaurants or things to do. The hotel does provide several useful maps upon arrival which is nice. (I highly recommond trying the Sook - thai restaurant - that is a couple of doors away from the hotel).
When checking out - know that the hotel charges $2 per piece of luggage (for large luggage - carry-ons are free) if you need to leave them with the front desk.

title: “Really good location”
text: This is the hotel that I always stay in NY, the location is really good, really close to the Mancy's Dept. Store, subway station, and walking to time square isnt that far. If you can book the hotel in advance, you can get really good price!

title: “Great architecture. Great food. Great stay.”
text: We've stayed at the AZ Biltmore many times, but the new management is stepping up their game. The Ocatilla Club in the former Arizona Wing offers a club lounge, continental breakfast, snacks, appetizers, cocktails and dessert as part of their package. Also, the deal included lunch and dinner at either Wright's or Frank and Albert's. Frank and Alberts occupies a beautiful new Frank Lloyd Wright inspired dining room that is New York hip and more casual than Wright's. Exec chef Todd Sicolo has done wonders. Everything from the food to the menu text to the plating has an architectural bent. The wait staff was unbelievably gracious and the new restaurant had only been open a handful of days. But it ran like a well oiled machine. Be sure to try: the duck fat poached French Fries (insanely good), Fallingwater cocktail (refreshing and sophisticated), the four flights of mini sundaes (a child's delight built for adults), the vanilla ice box cake, the fried chicken (amazingly moist), the Waldorf Salad (a great reinterpretation of the classic) and FAB pizza with a crispy semolina flour crust that brings to mind Nancy Silverton's pizza here in LA a Pizzeria Mozza. A great stay and wonderful service in an architectural masterwork. Pools for kids, cocktails for adults, golf and tennis nearby, privacy if you want it. The management now needs to work on the spa and gym to bring them up to the level of the restaurants, lobby and rehabbed rooms in the Ocatilla Club. We took a group of historians and architects here two years ago for a conference and they are still talking about their stay at the AZ Biltmore. Keep up the good work.

title: “A great bargain on the UWC”
text:
It's always wonderful when one's expectations are completely exceeded. We booked this room expecting a mediocre, hostel-style room. Instead we got a pleasant, simple room with a nice tv, comfortable bed, well-appointed bathroom and a fairly loud but effective air-conditioning unit. We also got to interact with some of the nicest and most helpful staff I've ever run into...in a Manhattan hotel or anywhere. The decor in the lobby and hallways was beautiful, as well.
I am a well-experienced traveler and I am acutely aware of the trade-offs one should expect when one pays half of the going rate for a hotel room. There was no elevator, no in-room wifi, not much art on the walls and as above, a simple, no-frills room. On the other hand, the location is superb with a Starbuck's next door and a dozen good restaurants within a few blocks. We found on-street parking for the weekend and saved ourselves $100. I also am a stickler for cleanliness in hotel rooms and there wasn't a dirty surface in our room.
Every single staff person with whom we interacted had a smile on their face, a helpful attitude and an extensive knowledge of the greater NY area. Our son and daughter-in-law live just a few blocks from this hotel and this is our new top choice for when we visit them. 
As long as you go to the Marrakech with appropriate expectations, I expect you to be as pleasantly surprised as we were.

title: “Friendly Hotel”
text: Whenever my husband and I are down in San Diego, we would always stay at the Hyatt or Hilton. This time we decided to book through Hotwire, and we got a room at the Sheraton Hotel & Marina. Our first time booking through Hotwire and first time ever staying at a Sheraton. We were nervous and didn't know what to expect, but when we got to the hotel grounds everything changed. Our check-in was fast and friendly. Our room was on the 4th floor and was nice and super clean. The hotel had everything we needed; close by the airport, easy access to parking lot and out to the main street, close by Little Italy and downtown San Diego, and other little shops. We loved our stay and would definitely stay at this friendly hotel again.

title: “People always have something to complain about”
text:
This hotel is very child friendly and one of the reasons I chose this establishment. Hotel was very clean and well appointed for anybody's needs. My family and I stayed in the two double bed room which worked quite well. In one area you have bathroom and bedroom and the other is sitting room or den. This worked perfectly because I had to work on some research while my son watched TV. 
As for the local area you have quite a bit of restaurants to choose from for most any needs. Within walking distance is Five Guys, P.F. Chang's and other restaurants of your choosing. About a 10 minute drive away is the Germantown Commissary (see my review for extra information). And if you need to find basic need items Target is a 10 min walk over train tracks or 10 min drive (it's easier to walk but not for the faint of heart). 
The free breakfast in the morning is basic but they have menu items a patron can easily order for your needs. As for other food on the menu I cannot review because I did not order any food items from their small cafe. However I did order a couple of coffee based drinks that were of Starbucks quality and price. With this being said this is the one part that brought the review down from 5 to 4 stars. The free breakfast was at times narrow in scope where only bread based items were the only thing on offer at that time. When passing later they had more items to choose from. 
As I've read reviews of this hotel too many people have particular tastes and interests that only a 5 star hotel would be able to suffice. If you don't want to be around other people then stay at a secluded cabin in the hills. As for people making noise the hospital is across the street and if families are in dire need this is one of the hotels they stay at so of course they are going to be making noise that may or may not be enjoyable. I found the staff to be friendly, the hotel well designed for my needs as well as others. Give it a try I don't think you will be disappointed.

title: “I left my heart in Hyatt Fishermans Wharf”
text:
Arrived after a 11 hour flight to be greeted by lovely welcoming staff. We had booked two rooms and requested for them to be close by.
One room was ready so they said to us to all go and wait in the one room and they will bring the keys down to the room. They were at the room with the keys within 15 minutes and the room was next door with a connecting door perfect.
The rooms were very spacious, the beds were amazing so comfy. I didnt want to get up in a morning because it was so comfy! 
The staff in the hotel were very friendly and helpful with directions and local information.
The location is great right in Fishermans Wharf and just around the corner is a cable car stop.
Had a great time in San Francisco and will definatley be returning to the Hyatt!

title: “Great Location, Great Value”
text: Pretty good deal for the money & great location near subways, short walks to main attractions - Times Square, Rockefeller Center... A little noisy, some hummming now and then but overall a nice experience. Take some PM meds with you just in case the taxi horns keep you up! Stayed in Room 518 - wasn't smelly, didn't face brick wall, had opening windows, radiator worked really well, has a/c, tv worked - and the elevator worked on our trip as well :)

title: “Fabulous location and old world elegance”
text:
The location was great for us because we didn't have a car. We were able to go one direction and hop on the monorail to Seattle Center and across the street we could catch the trolley to Lake Union. Our last day we decided to rent a car to go the wine area and the car rental was less than a block away. We were able to walk easily to Pikes Market also. There were several restaurants within easy walking distance.
The hotel lobby was very elegant and had a nice bar with a very friendly and informative bartender. The concierge and front dest clerks were all very accommodating and friendly.
We found the room to be very inviting, clean,thick towels, nice linens, comfortable bed and pillows, good water pressure and wine glasses with the ice bucket. The bathroom had a pedestal sink but also had a glass shelf large enough to store the toiletry bags. OUr view over looked a corner with Macy's on one corner. The room was typical size of an historical hotel or boutique hotel - not overly large but had everything needed. Overall if in Seattle again, we would definitely stay here.
OUr stay was the first week in June for 2 nights.

title: “Perfect Location !”
text:
Quiet hotel. Great location on 28th.
Loved waking up each morning and walking out our front door to be in the middle of the flower market! (plus the close proximity to our favourite new york urban development The HighLine)
Great way to start the day.
Aveda bathroom products. Free wifi.
The room design was very simple. But really when in NYC who stays in their room???
Front office staff were excellent and friendly.
Only complaint was bed pillows were too small and a little uncomfortable.

title: “Avoid it - no matter how good the price is.”
text:
My boyfriend and I stayed here while traveling to San Antonio. It was a huge mistake! The bed sheets were stained and when we asked for new ones, they gave us more that were stained. The pillows were also gross - so gross that I put a t-shirt around the pillow so there was another layer between me and that nasty pillow. 
The remote in our room didn't work so we called the front desk from the room. It rang and rang and rang. They not only couldn't give us a working remote but also neglected to tell us (when we walked to the front office since the didn't answer) that their phones were broken. 
This is not the kind of Ramada you'd expect with the name brand associated. It's more like a Howard Johnson. 
In the morning we wanted to speak to the manager but the person on staff said for us to wait about 3 hours until the actual manager showed up for work. We didn't bother waiting. They didn't care how our stay was. Such a disappointing experience for such a fun city like San Antonio.

title: “Great Hotel, Good Location”
text:
We were a little worried about the size of the hotel before we arrived, but when we arrived we were greeted by very friendly staff who knew theirs jobs and worked quickly, the reception aarea was spotless and had a great feeling.
We went to our room and upon viewing we can say yes it was small but had everything we needed, it was also very comfortable, we had a bunk room with two beds also a sink in the room. the bathrooms were on the same floor (4 of them) and you have lights above your door telling you when they are vacant or in use.
we would and will stay here again and again it's location is great infact from the hotel we walked to times square on about 4 days of our stay and it took about 30-45 mins
this hotel is great and i recomend it to everybody.

title: “Best beds and friendliest staff!”
text:
And did you know that they made it to Condé Nast Traveler Hot list 2007 – easy!
When I stay in hotels I look for uniqueness and details – an experience I’d like to bring back home and share with others. All hotels have great everything - beds, lighting, bathtubs etc. only thing that differentiates hotel properties is their choice of quality products and level of delivering the service. Congratulations on Exceptional job Pan Pacific! (Yes, I meant it with capital E, this is not a typo).
When I walked in hotel few things came in mind – good taste, class and hospitable atmosphere. From luxurious flower arrangements to first class beautiful art. 
Room:
I’ve attached a picture - bedside clock that raised memories. My grandparents have similar clock. How can a clock bring back so many memories? I called my grandma next morning to say how much I miss her and my family.
I get about 6-7 hours of sleep a night. That’s plenty for me. Do you ever feel like you need a vacation where you can just get away and shut all surroundings off? Get rest, comfort and peace - You have arrived. Sheets are so soft and mattress is like sleeping on a cloud. I slept 12 hours. 
Ladies – leave your magnifying mirrors home…they have what we need…a magnifying/adjustable mirror! No extending across the counter anymore. It’s an absolute must to have in bathroom. My lashes looked extra luscious that night.
Service is the second part of my evaluations – I asked for slippers and ice for my beverage – it was all delivered to my guestroom with enthusiastic smile and greeting. IN timely manner.
Stage three. Individuals who deliver the service. Any associate I came in contact with – you get welcoming and warm feel from them. And that’s all that mattered – having the right heart and mannerism to make me feel like home.
Thank you

title: “I'll be back...”
text: Stayed at the Sofitel for 2 nights in early December. Although the rates were up for the Christmas season($305/night) the value for this room was much higher than other boutique hotels in the area.(i.e. Whitehall Hotel). The room was on the 32nd floor facing the lake, with full plate-glass making up the exterior wall--Beautiful at night! Block-out window treatments made it dark for sleeping in. The room was somewhat small, with tiny cabinet-type closet space. Definitely missed not having an in-room coffee maker to start my day. The bed was oh-so comfy with feather mattress pad and duvet. Fabulous linens, as well. The bathroom was huge with both a wonderful tub and a walk-in shower. (Water pressure a bit low.) Bath done in marble with high-end fixtures. French bath products provided, as well as terry robe and slippers. Very, very quiet. Accurate thermostat. Four high-speed elevators deliver you quickly. Very capable concierge; acquired show tickets for us with no trouble. WONDERFUL location: 1/2 block from Mag Mile across from Water Tower Place. Several restaurants w/in 50 feet, including one on-site. Room service was wonderful and fast! Will definitely return, as the stay was so pleasant.

title: “Solid hotel near the airport - enjoyed our night stay”
text: We stayed one night before flying home. Their shuttle picked us up from the car rental place and returned us to the airport the next day. We really liked their dinner in the restaurant. We had an adjoining room for our two teens which worked out great. Only complaint was the party-crowd coming in at 2 am and slamming doors but that happens a lot. Our flight got cancelled the next day and we could not stay a second night at the same rate - so we booked over at the Renaissance (which was more luxurious in my opinion) and used one of the name-your-price sites.

title: “More Disappointment”
text: This was one of the worst hotel experiences I have had. I have stayed here before and had friends stay her and had a pleasant stay but the hotel has really gone downhill. There are several night clubs in the area with valet parking - people honk to try to park, well we heard honking and whistles of the valets until 5am, it was terrible. Either get sound proof windows or work with the local police department to stop this illegal noise, no excuse. On top of that the fire alarm went off at 4am and stopped a few minutes later, no word from anyone at the hotel what we should actually do. Turns out all of the elevators shut down so when we tried to leave at 8 am we had to wait 20 minutes for an elevator. I called the front desk and said "Do you realize the elevators are broken?" She said "All of them?" She did not apologize or explain what happened. It was like talking to a rude cashier at a fast food restaurant. When we returned to the hotel at 4pm the elevators were still broken and no one from the hotel was there to assist the mass of people waiting for 1 elevator. This is what you expect in the ghetto projects not a hotel. The hotel is in a good location and does have nice rooms and facilities but I will not stay here again.

title: “Loved, loved, loved it!”
text: We just returned from a weekend at the Bryant Park and we didn't want to leave! From the perfect room (which Darren and Robert were most kind to upgrade) to the fabulous bathroom, (best shower ever, great products, towels, bathrobes) to the best location, Bryant Park staff provides service par excellence. They are friendly, curteous, knowledgeable and accomodating. You have the question? They have the answer. We'll return as soon as possible.

title: “Great Location, Great Pool!”
text:
If you haven't stayed at the Hard rock San Diego and you like to have a good time then your missing out. The hotel is located in the Gas Lamp district and is a short walk or pedi-cab to 100's of restaurants and bars. The hotel itself has a great rooftop poolside bar/lounge as well a nightclub downstairs within the hotel. There is also a great sushi restaurant and breakfast restaurant located within the building. 
The location is right next to the surfliner(Amtrack) and metro station as well as a short walk to the convention center. 
There is always something going on in this hotel and you will never be dissapointed.
The rooms are ultra modern and are very well kept. I have never had a dirty room in this hotel.

title: “One of the best ... at LAX”
text:
We stayed here for one night on our way to Hawaii.
The hotel offered a park/fly package which was excellent value - one night's stay, and seven nights parking. By shopping around we found this for a bargain $135 plus tax. 
The room had a great view across the airport and was perfectly adequate for our needs. It had Westin's Heavenly beds (very comfortable) and the Westin Heavenly Shower.
The shuttle to LAX runs every 20 minutes, and takes under 10 minutes into the airport. If you miss it though, get the Thrifty car rental shuttle - it's right next door to the hotel!

title: “Good Value for New York City”
text: My husband and I stayed there from August 4-6 and were pleasantly surprised. Although the hotel doesn't look that great from the outside, the room was well equipped with kingsize bed and larger than we expected. It was very clean and the bed quite comfortable with ample pillows. It was an extremely hot weekend so the aircon was an absolute necessity. It worked like a charm and was reasonably quiet. Internet was included and worked flawlessly. The flat screen TV had a good selection of channels including HBO lineup. Bathroom was clean; amenities were plentiful. Shower pressure decent. Soundproofing was also very good. Two elevators helped transport us up to our 10th floor rooom. Staff was helpful especially the "doorman" who helped us navigate into a tight parking spot right across the street, saving us the expense of a private parking lot. The morning complementary breakfast was a big hit with a nice variety of hot and cold options. Newspapers also complementary. In addition, the location is great if you like Chelsea. Fun shopping and restaurants galore. Macy's is also within walking distance and subways nearby. All in all a very good experience at the Comfort Inn. It exceeded my expectations for a 2 star property. Would certainly consider staying there in the future.

title: “Still a grande dame, but should put on a spiffier dress?”
text:
I hadn't stayed in the Huntington since the mid-1980's, when it was the go-to place in 
San Francisco. It has always been old school, and remains so to this day. It is understated, 
and has the best situation of any San Francisco hotel on top of Nob Hill. It has spectacular 
views from the top floor of the whole harbor. The staff are very solicitous and fawning.
On the other hand, there are some quirks you just don't expect. For example, the toilet paper 
holder--most hotels do with a simple bar on which the TP rolls. Not the Huntington. Remember junior high school, where the roll was on a spring-loaded roller that gave resistance to any pull? That was because they didn't want you wasting paper or "decorating" the gym with festoons for paper. But in a hotel? It makes for a very frustrating experience. Likewise, the (many times refurbished) room interiors are not what you would expect at $375 a night--a bit like Ethan Allen on sale. The most annoying thing was the speed of the internet and the laborious procedure to log on. Most hotels these days just ask your last name and room number and you are off and going. Most luxury hotels include the internet. Not the Huntington. Room service is slow, but at least accurate and the food is still warm when it arrives.
Still, compared to the Ritz and other first rate San Francisco hotels, it is up there. I don't think it is quite the go-to place it used to be, and with a little greater attention to detail it could be back, but it needs that kind of attention. Living a bit on its laurels, I would say.

title: “the room was better than expected after reading the reviews”
text: the room was very nice and clean and renovated. (maybe it helps to be a starwood guest) obviously the rooms are going to be a bit smaller being in a city. we had a fabulous view of downtown looking towards dodger stadium. the rooms also had the great beds and good sheets. the staff was very nice, informative and helpful. the parking was $32/night but you are going to pay at least that anywhere else for an overnight in the city. the lobby is a bit cold and in need of updating.

title: “Lovely hotel, great location!!!”
text: We stayed at the Grand hyatt from 22nd -27th August, it was fabulous right from the start! Check in was quick and easy, we had a fabulous room on the 23rd floor, overlooking the city. Our room was recently refurbished, the room was very spacious with lovely matching bedding and curtains. We had an electronic blind which was super. Everywhere was lovely and clean. The bathroom was maybe a little small but that didnt really bother us. Plenty of hanging space for our clothes. The hotel itself was very clean, the lobby was very pleasant. All of the staff were very polite and helpful especially Elaine the conciege, who was very helpful to us. The location of the hotel was perfect, just a block away from Macys, saks, tiffanys and lots of great resturants nearby. China town was very close, we had an easy walk through Chinatown and on to Northbeach from there we found Lombard street, which we walked up and got some wonderful views of the city. I would definetly recommend the sightseeing hop on hop off bus, this was a great way of seeing the city highlights.Recommended restuarants: Lories diner, Maxs, Bubba Gumps and the Hard rock cafe. With such a fabulous city to explore it was great to know we had a lovely comfy bed to fall into at the end of a very busy and fun day. We would definetly stay at this hotel again it was brilliant!

title: “High end brand, very disappointed”
text: The Ritz Carlton is in desperate need of a renovation. The rooms are nice, but nothing spectacular. I will give them partial credit for the walk in shower. My only issue with the shower is that the pipes vibrate through thr walls. Heaven forbid you're sleeping because you will be awoken by the noise. It's horrible. The bed was mediocre in terms of comfort. I just wasn't impressed....I expect more from thr ritz Carlton brand.

title: “Great stay here, perfect Location! Will be back!”
text: Just back from a 6 night stay here with my partner. This was our first trip to NYC so we wanted to make sure we were in the perfect Location to do all our sight seeing. The Location could not of been better, a walk to everywhere, We walked to Times Square, less than minute walk. Central Park, Rockfeller Centre, Empire State Buiding, Macys ect. We got a taxi one day and that was to Chinatown. The hotel has late check in, not till 3, but we got there about half 2 and was not a problem to check in. We were on the 6th floor, there are 10 floors. I had read reviews about how small the rooms were so I booked the large room, The large room was a standard size room here in Ireland but I new what to expect booking a room in NYC. It def wasnt as small as some people had said but maybe that was the standard size room, they must be tiny! Bathroom is quite small. Wardrobe also very small, not enough room for both our clothes! However, the rooms were kept cleaned everyday. Large tv too. It is quite noisy on the street but what do you expect its NYC!! As there is so much to do in NYC, We were gone from morning to night, We slept and showered here, so did not mind what the rooms were like as long as they were comfy. Which they were, The size of the bed!! HUGE!! We had breakfast a few mornings here as food was great. We didnt have dinner here as so many places to choose from in Times Square. Yes the lifts are small, and slow, but I wouldn't not go back because of it. Staff were all very helpfull and friendly. Free Wifi, and they have 2 computers that are free to use also. Great stay , would def recommend to anyone and hopefully will be back again in the Future. Really enjoyed our stay here. Perfect Location, and great value for money. Cant wait to come back already!! Hope you enjoy ur stay!!... Maria

title: “Huge room for NYC”
text:
Caveat - we stayed on points so I can't comment on price/value, particularly since it was a December weekend visit. We were on the 15th floor, overlooking Times Square. While I much prefer staying closer to the Park, the views were amazing for our 4 year old son! He loved watching the screens. The room was up to date, very clean, and really large by NYC standards. I recently stayed at the Doubletree in Chelsea, and the room at the Suites in Times Square was easily 3 times the size. The living room had a queen-sized pull out sofa bed, plus a mini bar area with a small fridge and microwave. The bathroom was big with lots of vanity space, which was nice. Main bedroom had plenty of space. Note that the mattress was quite soft, which didn't bother me, but might be an issue for some. 
Even overlooking Times Square, the noise wasn't too bad. You could hear the occasional siren, but it wasn't loud enough to wake you up. 
Only two negatives: everyone was exhausted after a great, but long day so we opted to eat at the hotel restaurant on evening. The food was fine (about what you'd expect), but the service was lacking. They just weren't staffed nearly well enough for a weekend evening. Our server was very nice and apologetic, but the management should review the staffing needs at peak times. Also, probably like most places in NYC, check-out time was a zoo. Do not plan to check your bags with the front desk unless you have to, and then I'd recommend checking them as early as possible in the day. Fortunately, we were heading to the train station by noon so it wasn't an issue for us, but the line in the lobby to check bags was insane!
All in all, a great room for a family who relished having the extra space in Manhattan. Would recommend!

title: “Strongly recommend”
text: As Australians visiting the US for the first time for some years and needing to spend a night near LAX on both our outward and return journeys we spent a lot of time reading the reviews of various hotels located near the airport. This hotel had rated highly among other reviewers so we booked it. We were not disappointed in any aspect of our experience at this hotel. We were able to get very good but different internet prices for both nights spent in the hotel. It is very convenient to the airport with a regular shuttle bus and the service was top class. The room was comforable and clean with no noise. The bathroom was small but no smaller than others we have come to expect in US hotels. Staff were pleasant and accommodating. The restaurant downstairs was reasonably priced and the food good. I would strongly recommend this hotel.

title: “Superb Concierge experience !!”
text:
Concierge - Eden and TK were very extremely friendly - excellent restaurant recommendations. Eden especially remembered our names - took the time to make family specific suggestions and took a genuine interest in ensuring we enjoyed our stay. Brian was great at check-in, Juan from room service was a superstar - his service passion certainly shines - he deserves a raise!!
Air conditioning unit in # 2010 needs to be addressed - very noisy. Engineering recommended keeping fan on high to alleviate noise - hopefully they have recognized that is only a temporary fix.

title: “Very cool hotel!”
text: Hotel Max is a great place to stay! Very modern, very cool... great central location.. Easy walk to Pikes Market.. not too far from The Space Needle. Great restaurant, bar and sushi bar too. Everyone is very friendly and helpful.. For music and art lovers, there are great modern paintings by local artists and the guest room doors of one floor is blown up black and white photos of Seattle bands in concert. Highly recommend! Will stay again if I return to Seattle.

title: “Excellent service and accomodations”
text: Hotel service and level of quality, from the entire staff in every single functional area, to the facilities were outstanding. Made you feel special during your entire stay, as much as one could possibly enjoy that level of attention within a smaller luxury hotel setting. Rooms were spacious, clean, modern and have attention paid to the smaller details. Our family stayed in both suites and regular rooms, and everyone enjoyed their stay, which helped make this a more enjoyable weekend for all of us.

title: “Small but Nice”
text: We stayed at the Marcel's for 3 nights. The rooms are very small but the beds are incredibly comfortable.The staff were very nice and helpful. The hotel is close to the subways so getting around Manhatten was quite easy. The bathrooms are stocked full of nice toiletries and you can get free coffee and capucino in the lobby. I'd recommend using the stairs when getting around the hotel. The elevator is slow and has a funky smell. Ice was always available. I would stay at the Marcel's again but only if we were 2 people sharing the room. We had my husband's teenage daughter with us so it got real crowded.

title: “DO NOT STAY HERE”
text: First impression of hotel...was not good when we went to check in at the front desk at 6 pm; we were told that our room was not ready and would have to wait. After agreeing to wait for 30 min we were finally ready to check in. As my family and I were going to our room; the landscape appeared to be well maintained; but unfortunately the exterior of the hotel was not so lucky. The stairs were concrete; and they appeared to be unsafe...cracks on the back of these steps were so big and cracking that you could see thru every step at least 1/2 inch; the paint on the rails and deck where peeling horribly; and then as we go to enter the door we notice a dirty spite pop can sitting right outside our door; we then look up and above the entrance to our room was a wasp nest. We entered the room only to find the theme from the outside continued throughout the interior of the hotel; most of kitchen rooms are supplied with kitchen utensils and basic kitchen needs. Not this one; we had one sharp knife that was bent at the blade; 3 plates; 3 drinking glasses; a few utensils; and very little if anything was clean in the kitchen. The bathroom was very similar; dirty and old not well maintained at all. When we called the front desk to them about the bee nest; they said ok; they would send someone over; that didn't happen until the following afternoon and this was due to continous calls made to the front desk. The second day they didn't even clean the room....nor did they call and ask; when a call was made to the front desk for us to get clean towels brought to our room; the lady at the front desk said nobody would bring them to us but we could come get them; my husband explained we did not recieve room servie and were never given the option of having someone clean the room; the lady again replied...sir housekeeping has left for the day and if you want towels you will have to come down and get them. The next morning my son wanted to go swimming; we go down their only to find out the pool is closed because the pool man didn't start on time...and needed to finish....45 minutes later it was raining and could no longer go swimming. We did finally make it to the pool; only to find the hot tub out of order; no towels by the pool; the pool area was not clean....this was a trip for fathers day weekend; I would never stay at this hotel again; especially since they had the nerve to charge $119 per night; and this was supposedly a discounted rate.......not worth $1 a night.

title: “Perfect location”
text: Stayed here with friends as part of a 40th birthday celebration. We had 2 double doubles for 6 of us which were quite small but this didn't matter as we were out spending and celebrating most of the time. The location is fabulous if you want to shop - within 2 blocks of Bloomingdales, with Victoria Secret, Banana Republic etc all on the doorstep. It is also within walking distance of Central Park. The sports bar is buzzy (full of French businessmen watching rugby when we arrived). Joseph the doorman was especially helpful - managing to get taxis for 6 girls with luggage and shopping at short notice.

title: “The Worst Hotel Experience Ever!!”
text: I invite anyone planning to stay at this place to e-mail me for the full story of 3 extremely depressing days at the shabby Ocean Park Inn. I am preparing to write to the Better Business Bureau, Chamber of Commerce & anyone else I can think of. My husband & I and my brother & wife were treated in a most shameful manner. Never in 30 years of traveling have we had hotel management yell at us over the phone while we were trying to discuss problems with our room!! The "homeless", i.e. bums & transients, are allowed to completely take over the property. We watched drug dealing & alcohol use in broad daylight. Beware: If you are making reservations online & think the price for a full ocean view is too good to be true, you're right!

title: “Highest Marks”
text: Nothing but positive to say about this boutique Hotel and its staff. Front desk got us in our room early having just got off a cruise ship. The room was excellent and the location of the hotel in relation to the market and great restaurants is superb.

title: “Made us feel at home”
text: My wife had to be at the hospital next door for brain surgery. We check in and although the hotel room was very nice, I was going to be there for over two weeks and wanted something a little bigger. I went back down to the front desk to ask for a bigger room, maybe one with a small kitchen. I met Mr. Davies at the front desk. Bill took me around to look at three or four other rooms in the hotel. Bill then asked me why I was in town and what was my concerns. I told him what was going on and that after the surgery we were going to have to stay close to hospital in case of complications for a while. Bill then said not to worry anymore and found me a much larger place to stay in the hotel apartment next door with the kitchen as well as two bedrooms. He made our stay at a hotel feel more like a stay at a second home. He may not be aware of the impact he made on my wife and I. If you need a place to stay while in this part of Boston I can not urge you enough to call Bill Davies and schedule a visit. The Longwood Grill as well as the Food Court is just downstairs so no real need for anything else.

title: “COULDN'T BE MORE PERFECT!”
text: Last month my friends and I booked a stay here. I can't say enough about how great this hotel is! Absolutely everyone from the employees at the front desk, to the bartenders to the bellhops was incredibly accommodating and kind. They all went that extra mile to ensure my friends and I had as perfect a stay as possible and I will be booking my stays in New York at Gild Hall from here on out!

title: “good location”
text: nice place, close to convention center and gaslamp

title: “Great Location”
text:
The hotel is located just across from central park and is easy walking distance to Times Square - 5th Avenue. Bed was extremely comfortable and we received excellent service. Sadly we did not have a view of the park but this did not deter our enjoyment.
Recommend the Gray Line Downtown Bus Tour.

title: “Great Hotel!”
text:
The Hotel Allegro is a beautifully decorated art deco hotel in the Chicago Theatre District. It is walkable to the the Magnificent Mile and the shoreline (including Navy Pier) but it will probably take about 20-30 minutes to get to Navy Pier - very pleasant if the weather is nice.
We have stayed at Kimpton Hotels in 3 different cities now (Vancouver, Portland, Chicago) and the experience has always been pleasant. The staff are very friendly and professional, the rooms are clean with comfortable beds, and the cocktail hour in the lobby every day is a great touch.
Kimpton hotels are quickly becoming my first choice in accomodation when I travel!

title: “Great location and we loved the room”
text: We stayed in a corner room on the 20th floor with a balcony and a great view of Manhattan. The king-size bed was so comfy, we had our own little kitchen and the room was really spacious. The bathroom was stocked with Aveda products each day (always a good sign) and although the bath wasn't big enough to really stretch out in, the bathroom was clean and the shower was nice and powerful. The hotel itself is in a great location - just a short walk from Times Square and the Theatre District and a short subway or taxi ride from almost anywhere in Manhattan. Don't be put off by the psychedelic carpet in the lobby - this is a great hotel and we'd definitely go back.

title: “bad service”
text: Our mornings at this hotel would start off very badly with extremely rude service and attitude that we received from the servers in the restaurant. We would wait for long periods to be approached and offered coffee or juice. Breakfast was included in our booking however the waiters seemed to really resent our "free" breakfasts despite leaving a tip. The coffee was consistently horrible- not fresh. It got to the point where we dreaded going downstairs in the morning for breakfast. The concierge(s) was not very helpful and didn't really matter which one was working. No-one informed us that most Manhattan Stores would be closed on Easter Sunday despite making a big point about how excited we were to shop. There was a general laziness about all of the staff working there.

title: “Definitely not brand new, but DOES have some old world charm++”
text:
I read the reviews, but still took a chance for a group of my friends by booking at the Lord Baltimore. My guess is you get what you pay for. If you pay for the cheapest room, it might not be the best in the house! I was impressed and pleased with our choice.
LOCATION. It was convenient to the Inner Harbor and its attractions. We were in a group walking around late at night and had no trouble. About 4 blocks away, though, there seemed to be the local red light district.
BUILDING. I am not sure what the history of the building is, but it has some elegance, albeit from 60+ years ago. The lobby ceiling is quite stunning. Old elevator door "sills" are problematic - make sure to watch your step, and your bag going in and out of the elevator - the flloor is NOT level.
ROOM. I was in a business class room, and as an Carlson Club elite member was granted club privileges, which I only used once for breakfast. Breakfast was in a small area on an upper floor (17, I think) and only had places for maybe 12 people to sit.
The room was very adequate, with lots of room to work, a free bottle of water, free internet access, and great amenities in the bathroom. I love the nubby shaped bath body bar soap. I saw one of my friend's non-business class corner room, and it had lots of light. My room actually looked out into next door brick buildings and was quite dark, with ZERO view.
STAFF. Front desk was VERY friendly and warming. Concierge helped get us taxis, and give directions. Breakfast attendant on Club floor was very polite, and always cleaning.
Suggestion to hotel: In countries where tea is of great importance, they always have milk available for the tea. As a coffee drinker, I appreciate having milk in my coffee. There are small packets of milk which do not require refrigeration. Same as the half&half packets, but taste much better: UHT milk packets. (One brand is Parmalat)

title: “great value very clean”
text: Very nice and extremely clean, for the money it is a great value.

title: “Excellent value for money”
text:
The location is superb...literally a 2 minute walk from Macy's, 5 minutes from the Empire State Building and around 10 minutes from Times Square.
The room we got was on the top floor facing the front street and was bigger than we expected. It was clean as was the shower. The shower itself wasn't very powerful but you've got to remember you get what you paid for and it was satisfactory. 
The breakfast in the morning was basic but as everyone mentions the plastic cutlery was annoying. You have a choice of cereals, toast, bagels, fruit juices, tea and coffee as well as donuts (!)
The hotel was undergoing some renovations so in the evening the reception area was unsightly. You have access to the internet and a computer which has a printer attached to it. The wifi connection is fast and most of the staff are very helpful and friendly. 
The reason for 4 stars is the location....you literally are within walking distance of all the major sites as well as tube and Penn street train station. If I ever visit NYC again I would definitely consider this hotel again-it is value for money!

title: “Good location,average stay”
text:
Having stayed at a few hotels in central New York,I can stay that my latest stay was average.I was there on a business trip,so I had to use the business centre of the hotel (19€ to use the internet and make 8 copies).Plus the room was of medium size (i know New York hotels don't offer spacious accommodation).still for a price of 400€ I expected a more updated decoration.The bed was fine,good sleeping quality.The cleaning staff very helpful,the check in process smooth too.I didn't have any breakfast at the hotel.what is particularly annoying with this hotel is the number of people staying there.You constantly need to wait for the lift.
The location is convenient for strolling the 5th avenue or nearby streets.
I guess next time I will also explore other options in the city that never sleeps.

title: “Nice hotel, great location”
text:
The location in Belltown is excellent. Great restaurants and bars nearby, while it's within a couple of minutes of walking from Downtown. Given the very central location, the sounds of the city are audible - especially sirens and traffic, so keep this in mind if you're a bad sleeper.
I was there a couple of times during a period of two weeks. The first time the room was quite nice and fairly modern, while the room during the latter stay was a bit more dated. Anyway, the rooms are clean and housekeeping does a good job, although the time when they clean your room can be a bit arbitrary - anywhere from 9 AM to 5 PM, which makes it a bit tricky if you plan to be working in your room, for instance. Then again, there's always the "do not disturb" doorknob hanger. There's no minibar in the room, but there is a fridge. There's also a pool and a small exercise room in the basement. The breakfast at the restaurant was poor considering the prices. (E.g. a continental breakfast consisted of a tiny cup of fruit and a piece of toast with butter.)

title: “Nothing but the BEST in San Fran”
text: We travelled from Tampa for our first family trip to CA. Stayed here for two nights.
