From the bellhop to the concierge to the doorman,everyone here went out of their way to ensure that we had a pleasant and comfortable experience. The beds were sooo comfy! The shower and bath in our suite and the aromatherapy products were awesome! They made getting ready a spa like experience. The club suite was like a home away from home. Our family enjoyed the breakfast, drinks and snacks there each day of our stay. They had free Internet access there, which helped us plan the rest of our trip. I must say that Juan Carlos stood out as the best rooms manager we've ever encountered. He is doing a spectacular job with this hotel!

title: “Have to get in”
text: Even though you are not going to stay where as a luxury and expansive, this place is good to visit because of traditional Duck's Parade in the high level decorated lobby.

title: “My Favorite Hotel has just gotten better”
text:
I'm in Dallas monthly on business and have been staying at this hotel for over 3 years. They recently renovated the main areas and restaurant/bar for the Super bowl last year and they did a great job, (although you will see an increase in the rates you used to pay in the past). Previously, I avoided their restaurant and opted for the taxi to dinner option. But since their renovation, their new menu is great. They stick with as much organic and local farmers as possible. Even though I get breakfast free in the Concierge club, I opted for paying for the wild boar breakfast tacos (YUM) and the oatmeal waffle. 
 If you have access, the concierge club has also certainly stepped up their food offerings in the evening, sticking with a "theme" and offering heavier options if you wanted to skip dinner. Kristen is so friendly and helpful, that I feel like I'm "home with friends" when I'm in town. Also, I enjoy this club room most because you have the option of ordering "room service" delivered to the club room to enjoy (as opposed to eating alone in your room). More Marriott's should consider this. 
 The rooms have a modern feel to them and like others have commented, a higher room offers a nice view. The thread count on the sheets is heavenly and the curtains are great at keeping the room as dark as you need. The one challenge is that your cell phone may not work for long in certain rooms before you lose the call. If you are patient, you will sometimes find the exact spot you need to stand/sit in to not lose the call, or it may not be an issue. Also, although I'm not a gym person, I do like to take walks. Outside, next to the hotel is a HUGE parking lot that stretches multiple city blocks if you wanted to get out (and enjoy the 100+ degrees).
 Also, if you are an elite member, they have the express check in when you arrive so I do not have to go to the front desk. My key is waiting for me at the door.

title: “Very Close to TD Gardens”
text: As the title says it is very close to TD Gardens, one block. Our room was comfortable and clean. I did not think it looked "tired" nor did the lobby. Most of the service was very good, especially the front desk, they were helpful and expedient. We had breakfast in the Ruby Room one morning , it is a buffet that they set up on the bar. It was plentiful and good but the service was not. To add insult to injury she added 18 % gratuity to it so it came out to $20 a person, if it is not included, skip it. The other thing that I would skip is the valet parking. It is $42 a day. Should have parked in the Goverment Parking Garage a block away. While my husband and I were having a bite at a pub down the street before the game we attended I saw the valet park the car on the street, hit another car, looked and left. Parking on the street is free on Sunday, so you get charged $42 and the valet simply parks it free 50 feet up the street. It was a good location, the room was comfortable, the price was reasonable. I would return.

title: “The staff was very hospitable and welcoming, the rooms extremely clean”
text: I want to thank Shirly and Indira from the housekeeping staff. My husband has been missing his flip flops since we got back from our trip and I spoke with both of them on the phone and they were more than happy to help us out. They are mailing them to us tomorrow. I can't thank you enough Shirley & Indira!!

title: “Great location, nice extras”
text:
Stayed here over Thanksgiving weekend. Great location and the rooms were very nice. Definitely not cookie-cutter like chains. We have stayed at a number of Kimpton hotels and this one definitely did not disappoint. We stayed in a king room with a view of Park Ave. The room is small (BUT this is completely expected if you stay in NYC) but very nicely appointed. 5 gigantic mirrors, IHOME for our Ipod, nightly turndown service, yoga mats and equipment available upon request. The room had a very cozy feeling, just what you need after dealing with the throngs of people on 5th ave. Bathroom was completely fine. Again, small, but well appointed and exactly what we expected. The lobby is swanky and the nightly happy hour is fun. It's nice to meet other hotel guests! 
Another tid bit, Fagolini on Lexington (1 block off from Park) on 39th is a very reasonable cozy italian place. Quite cozy with good service and pretty romantic for my book!

title: “Good hotel in the financial district”
text:
Arrived for a 2 day stay from the UK, at the start of a longer trip to the US, at 1pm and even though check in is not until 3pm my room was ready and allowed to check in. As a Priority Platinum was given an upgrade to a large room which for NY standards was of a good size. No problems with housekeeping or any of the staff and was made very welcome.
This is not a hotel if you are looking for the bright lights close by on your first stay to NYC - but if you have stayed before, want to be in the fiancial district or dont mind travelling on the subway then this is a good choice with a variety of subway lines which will get you to nearly anywhere in the midtown area in anout 20mins. Also good for shopping as near to Century 21

title: “Great location”
text: This hotel is located 2 blocks from the convention center. It is also very near shops and eateries on the 16th street mall. It is clean and the staff is friendly. The only negative is no fitness center.

title: “Nice hotel, very kitsh”
text:
The hotel (or is it a large B&B?) is locateed in a couple of old houses in a beautiful residential area along Balboa Park. The decor is resolutely kitsh, it is a matter of taste of course. Upon entering the room, one is struck first by the decor, and at the same time by the excessive smell of air freshener. That, too, is a matter of taste, but breathing these chemicals all night long cannot be very healthy. I did not like the envelope requesting a tip for the maid, to be handed at the desk on check-out. Don't they pay their staff?
The bed was good, wifi was clear, there were a fridge, coffee machine, microwave, and everything was very clean. Continental breakfast is brought to the room, which is nice. Parking is on the street, easy to find.

title: “Decent business hotel on 183 N”
text: Stayed here for a few nights in February. Convenient if you need to be in the NW part of the city, shopping close by. Overall the hotel is OK, pretty average, the restaurant is quite average also. Seemed kind of expensive given the location.

title: “Beautiful grounds, the rooms are a bit rough around the edges”
text: The property is very nice, on an island in Mission bay. The rooms must have been built a very long time ago and show some signs of wear, we did have mold on the ceiling in the bathroom and the patio roof had wood rot. The decor in the room was nice. They do charge you $25 a night for parking. Over all I liked our stay at Paradise Point, the location is perfect you could almost walk to Sea World and it was fun exploring the beautifuly tropic property.

title: “Perfect SF motel”
text:
The rooms are clean, comfortable and spacious, and, above all, Varsa is everything you would hope for in a hotel manager. In fact, you feel more like a guest than a customer with the numerous ways in which she takes the trouble to help you. 
Breakfasts may be uncooked, but you can actually have a totally healthy breakfast (fresh orange juice with pulp, fresh fruit and healthy granola bars with coffee/tea), and since the rates are low with free parking and wireless internet, if you want more food, you can try the many excellent cafes on Polk Street. Unbeatable value, and in an extremely convenient location for driving, and walking to Fisherman's wharf, and public transport everywhere else. Maybe I should have kept this a secret treasure!! :-)

title: “Great location but so-so rooms”
text: The strength of this hotel is its excellent location--right next to Grand Central station. But our room was a disappointment. It was tiny but we thought that was standard for NY. Turns out we had paid for an upgrade that we never got. The temperature in the roomy was terribly cold even after we turned up the thermostat to 76. The problem was a very drafty window. The water pressure in the shower was not much more than a trickle but worst of all, Internet access was $16/day per device! Overall, the location makes it good if you don't need to spend much time in the room.

title: “We loved it and we'll be back!”
text: First, let me say that the location is perfect. My sister and I stayed on the 42nd floor. Our room was a corner suite that looked over Time Square and had a view of the Hudson River. The room was very clean. Bed was extremely comfortable. From check in, to bell boy, to concierge, to crabcake chef in the lobby - everything was above expectations! Loved the Doubletree Suites on Time Square!!!

title: “One of the worst i have stayed at”
text: The service at this hotel has to be the worst i have ever encountered. I arrived on the 1st August in the mid morning after a 14 hour flight. When i got to the counter the 2 people behind the counter just looked and kept talking in a language other then English and just made me wait. They were chatting and laughing. I was then served by the female on duty who was just incredibly rude and snooty. The pool area is the only thing this hotel has going for it. The rooms are average with terrible air conditioning. The food was always cool when it arrived from room service. I expected much better. The males behind the counter were always very friendly but the women were just not suited to service roles and they always looked messy. Don't let the name Hilton in the title fool you, this is nowhere near the standard that most Hiltons are. Would never stay here again.

title: “Perfect locatin for exploring the city”
text:
Stayed at the Tuscan Inn over the Fourth of July weekend after using Priceline before Christmas to book a room (although I didn't actually think I would get one for only $75/nt over a holiday weekend!).
Check in was quick and my boyfriend and I were given a queen room on the fourth floor facing the street. My boyfriend's first response was "wow, this is a tiny room", but it was what I was expecting considering the location and that this is only a 3-star property. It was in fact a small room (a King size bed would not have fit) with a tiny closet and 2 drawers for storing clothes. Good thing we only packed carry on luggage and didn't have much to put away!
The room was always clean and the maid staff was friendly, saying "hello" and "have a nice day" as you passed. We were frequently in and out of the room to change clothes or take a nap and never walked in on a maid (or were walked in on ourselves). One day we had the do not disturb sign on the door before the maid had come so we could rest, and when we finally stepped out for about an hour, we changed the sign for maid service and everything was perfect when we returned!
One bad part about the room was that some street noise traveled up, although we were only really disturbed one night when there was a car parked on the street playing loud music with people around it laughing and talking loudly.
Pros at the hotel:
Staff - Very friendly and helpful. We had to send and receive several faxes during our stay and they were always happy to help. We used the concierge to book theater tickets, which worked flawlessly, and we also called the front desk around midnight our last evening and asked them to arrange an airport shuttle the next day, which they did the following morning when the shuttle company opened.
Amenities - While this hotel isn't a luxury property, they have some nice touches like marble bathrooms, mini bar, room service and an evening wine reception every day (which many people attended). The restaurant attached to the hotel is nice, with a great little bar area and friendly bartenders. The restaurant breakfast menu is pretty minimal, but it does the trick.
Location - This is the best part of the hotel. Two blocks from Pier 41, one block to the F line street car two blocks to the cable car. This was an awesome area to gain access to many different parts of the city without trying too hard.
Overall, I would say this room was not worth the rack rate of $250+ per night, but it was far beyond my expectations at the Priceline bargain rate!

title: “THIS is a Marriott?”
text:
Let's just say that I am shocked that this property is a Marriott. I stay in hotels about 150 nights a year and my wife and I were in Houston for a family event that only required a one night stay and after checking in to this place, I'm glad it was only for one night! I am a Platinum Marriott Rewards member and there was no recognition of my status at checkin and the agent didn't even know what I was talking about when I asked about my Platinum amenity. After about 20 minutes of trying to describe what I was referring to, I finally gave up. 
The room was basic, but the padding on the bed was lumpy and the bathroom was poorly caulked and ad lots of mold. Had it not been so late, we would have checked out and gone to another hotel, but we were tired and just wanted to get a good nights sleep and get the heck out. Unfortunately, before we were able to do so, my wife and I had to strip the bed of the sheets and move the lumpy mattress pad around and remake the bed before we could rest comfortably. We still didn't sleep well, and we were up and out by 9AM because we just couldn't take it anymore.
Fortunately, Angelina at the front desk was a blessing in disguise when we told her about our checkin experience and the miserable night, comping breakfast and refunding $100 of the room rate and apologizing profusely for not being recognized as a top level Elite member at checkin. So, although the property needs some work, the Marriott Spirit prevailed in its staff.

title: “Great hotel, but a few disappointments”
text: I loved everything about this hotel and the service was amazing. The only issue was the expectations I had from reading some of the previous reviews. Many people talked about the complimentary upgrades if you belonged to preferred hotels (which I do). When I asked about this, they said all they could do was certain upgrades for a fee. I maybe had my expectations to high for that extra service & other little things from what I've read. I found the overall service great, especially the concierge & service staff. So take this review with a grain of salt, but I can say I will stay here again.

title: “Loved This Place”
text: Just returned from seattle. First time visiting and this hotel made it just the best experience. We loved the room, sooo clean and lovely to sleep in. The tv and movie service just topped off our evenings. The pool/hottub area are just awesome and overlook the pier area and the safeco field. It has a nice restaurant in the hotel as well right across the street. It is a little far to walk some days to the pike market or pioneer square but the shuttle offered could not of been any better. When we called for pickup it seemed like we waited no time at all and the drivers were fantastic with all sorts of suggestions. We used the shuttle extensively and it never let us down. Will definitely be staying here again. Nothing but good to say

title: “Firmly Average (C+) : Good Points and Bad”
text:
My fiancee and I live in Chicago, but occasionally head to a downtown hotel for a night away.
For fun and to get a vastly better price, we use one of the main discount services - Priceline or Hotwire.
This time around, I was fooling around with Priceline, attempting to see if I could get anything for the following day for a very cheap price. Saturday checkins with Priceline in downtown Chicago are usually a problem....
...but not this time. I gave Priceline a shot for $66 for a 4 star and it came back with the Sheraton. $66 is not only a vast savings over the hotel's regular rate, but it's substancially cheaper than the worst hotels in downtown Chicago.
The Sheraton is in a wonderful area, just a few blocks from Navy Pier, a few blocks from Michigan Ave and not that far of a walk from downtown. Fox and Obel, a wonderful grocery store, is also a block or two away.
Despite the low prices that I've gotten for hotels, I go in asking things like, "how would I feel had I paid full price?" 
Things started off fine enough. Check-in was going slowly (I've visited different chain hotels in the city and I've seen check-in go faster and the staff was still welcoming.), but thankfully, there weren't many people in line and there were plenty of staff checking in.
The person who checked us in was very nice and, unlike some other hotels, not only was priceline not mentioned (at some hotels, those who make cheap Priceline reservations are made to feel second class), the staff member told us about how they want every guest to be treated well and if there were any problems, to call them.
I was going to try to see if I could pay for an upgrade, but didn't really have an "in" in the conversation. When I saw that we had a room on the 25th floor, I didn't really make an issue of it, as I figured we were far up anyway.
We walked through the lobby, which was quite lovely, and went up to the floor. When we arrived, the door had been unlocked by the maid staff, who looked as if they'd just finished cleaning it (the cart was in front of the room). So, that wasn't too pleasing, and there were still also what appeared to be some breakfast room service plates (in one case, while I admittedly didn't see what the dish looked like before it was eaten, the remains didn't look too good) in the hall.
The room itself, however, was pretty nice. It appeared clean, with no noticable dents in furniture or other concerns. There appeared to be some light wear (not dirt, but just wear/tear) to the bottom part of the bedspread(by the floor), but aside from that, it was fine. The room was fairly plain - not all-white plain, but certainly nothing too fancy. Size-wise, however, it was definitely pretty roomy, with a couch and a nice view.
I took some great pictures out the window, which would have been nicer had the window not been dirty. The windows, while not terrible, were certainly in need of a wash. 
We got snacks at the Walgreens across the street, as well as at the previously mentioned Fox and Obel. We were pondering ordering room service, until we looked at the prices. Had I just ordered a burger, with gratuity (18%) and service charge ($3.25), it would have cost just under $20. Breakfast was similarly ridiculous - $19.75 (plus gratuity, plus charge, so we're talking in the neighborhood of $27 for what you can get for a fraction of the price at several different and very nice places within a half mile) for 2 eggs, meat, bread and coffee/ beverage. A pizza plate was $17 and change (and that's before gratuity), when one could easily walk to some absolutely terrific Chicago pizza places.
 I don't know what the Sheraton is thinking with these prices, given that there are definitely other options in the area, including PJ Clarkes across the street if you want a burger or something similar. Also food-related - there are no vending machines. They obviously want you to order one via room service or go to the gift shop. Walgreens is across the street, and both Fox and Obel and another grocery store are down the street. Get your snacks there. There's a Corner Bakery less than 1/2 a mile away, just off Michigan and across from the Wyndham hotel. Great place for a quality, fast meal if you're on the go.
Air conditioning was fine, although there is the odd feature that you have to lock the door before the air conditioning can go on. Obviously, a money-saving feature so that people can't just go out and leave the AC on all day while they're gone. Definitely the first time I've ever seen anything like it at a hotel, though.
We stayed at the W City Center last Summer and, interestingly enough, the room service was cheaper there - if not by a whole lot. However, the service was excellent and so was the food. Somehow I didn't think I'd have the same experience with the Sheraton, and despite the fact that the menu noted that if the food wasn't there in 30 minutes or it'd be free, given how they seemed to charge for everything in this hotel, I felt like if I did make an order and it came in 31 minutes, I'd have a debate on my hands.
The bathtub did have a massaging showerhead, which seemed to work wonderfully most of the time, but sprayed all over the place on a couple of settings. The bathtub was fairly nice but - didn't drain. We were only there for one night, settled in and didn't want to sit there while someone came up and fixed it, so we just left it. When we woke up the next morning, the water was still there.
The bed was one of Sheraton's relatively new Sweet Sleeper beds and, while it was not up to the W's Signature Bed (still, by far the best bed I've experienced), it was around the same quality was the Westin Heavenly Bed.
Continuing the feeling like nothing was complimentary was the fact that there is a charge of one full night if you change your dates of stay after check-in (in other words, no leaving early.) and a $75 charge if you check out after noon. Internet was pretty standard at $9.95 a day, although there are a few chains now offering complimentary internet. If you emailed something at the business center with an attached document, it was $1.50 per page. The bottle water in the room was definitely not free. The list goes on.
Fitness room/pool? Couldn't get a chance to check those out, because you had to sign-in at the fitness room and while apparently they didn't charge you for pool use, they do charge (I believe it's $9.95 a day?) for the fitness room and I didn't want to have to sign-in at the fitness room just to go through there to take a peek at the pool.
There are a few restaurants on the premises (including the famed Shula's Steak House) and, while I would have loved to have tried room service or the restaurants just to discuss them in this review, there's a point where things are just too overpriced to "try". I'd have liked to have given room service a try, just to be able to discuss the service and food, but the prices were just way too high to "try" anything.
Believe it or not, during the night, we began to hear noise from the pipes behind the bathroom. Not enough to keep us from sleeping (and I did get a good night's sleep in the Sheraton bed), but *definitely* very noticable, and it seemed like whenever the person (I'm guessing it was the room above, although it could have been next door) turned on the sink or shower, it was definitely heard. This is the first hotel we've stayed at (including some older ones) where this has been an issue. We also heard a lot of hall noise.
The TV offered a pretty decent lineup of cable channels. I've seen better, I've seen worse. I've read reviews of this hotel noting that they only offered a handful of channels, but there were definitely a bit more than that.
It's too bad that this hotel charges for just about everything (moreso than any other hotel I've stayed at), as it really produces a feeling in the consumer that they can't just sit back and enjoy - it's a "don't touch anything, they might charge us" feeling.
Staff was okay. We got a good morning or two, but nothing too overly friendly, and most staff we encountered just went about their business.
The final issue was check-out. The in-room system was not working (the menu would not come up, so express check-out was not possible), so we had to check out the old-fashioned way. I actually wanted to go though check-out at the desk, just to see what the service would be like. Thankfully, there wasn't much of a line. When I informed the desk clerk of the bathtub issue, he didn't seem to care a whole lot. I certainly wasn't trying to get any sort of discount or anything, I was just trying to tell him the issue. I didn't even get a "thank you for telling us." 
In an episode of "The Apprentice" a couple of seasons ago, when teams had to furnish hotel rooms, Trump noted how important the last impression was. I've really felt that way when I've stayed at hotels, as well. The Sheraton didn't do that well in this regard.
So, overall, for what I paid, this was a fine hotel. We got a clean, fairly spacious (if no-frills) room with a pretty good view. Given that there are definitely great views to be had from this hotel, I was really hoping for that, and certainly succeeded in that regard.
Would I pay full price? No. There are other hotels in this area (including a very nice Holiday Inn a couple of blocks North - the Holiday Inn City Centre) that are cheaper and there are other hotels for the same price that are a better value. After liking the W City Center so much, I'd also consider trying the W Lakeshore, which was also in viewing distance of the Sheraton, a good 4-5 blocks N.
Rating? I've seen the Sheraton rated 4 stars, and it's rated 3 1/2 by some services. Personally, I'd consider it to be a good 3-star hotel. The public areas are very nice, but the rooms were pretty comparable to the Courtyard Marriott over on Hubbard and State, which is a very nice 3 star. The Marriott service (see also the Marriott Residence Inn over by Water Tower downtown) was consistently better, as well. 
Would I come back? If the price was right - and by right, I mean in the range that I paid this time - I would probably consider another stay here. It's a lovely area, and very nice to stroll around. However, there were definite issues here that made me wonder how this could be considered a 4-star.

title: “Ryan and HGC rock!”
text:
I am a very discriminate business travel due to previous roles traveling the world. NYC is one of my favorite cities and I have found my home away from home at the HGC. I have stayed at this property several times over the past year and the experience is always great and consistent. If you do have any issues/problems (which you probably won't) the team there is attentive and on point! No stereotypically rudeness!
I have to particulary mention Ryan - the Guest Services manager. He has always been great to me every stay and pays close attention to detail. I recently took my son for a trip for his HS graduation and the room had a special note to him welcoming him to the city. Details count and keep me coming back and telling everyone I know to do the same. I wish I could keep this location a secret, but the team here deserves the accolades you see. Thanks Ryan and the HGC!!! - M. Perry

title: “Hilton Hospitality”
text: I always prefer to stay at Hilton family of hotels being a platinum hhonors member and I was not dissapointed. Room was compact but furnished very contemporarily. The balcony with the bay view in the tower was awesome too esp during sunsets. Service was ok but I have stayed at better hilton properties in orlando. I had requested for a cab one evening..waited 30 min and no show. I recommend this for families with kids. They have a huge pool and also play movies on a big screen by the pool after dark. $20 a day parking is ridiculous and includes valet parking. The fitness center is very outdated and crampy. The breakfast buffet is good but very pricey $20/person.

title: “Perfect, Clean & Modern - Great value”
text: All was excellent, especially decor and location. Only tiny complaint is that shower could be a bit more updated and clean.

title: “Very Good Hotel”
text: The Fairfield Inn at SeaWorld is a very good hotel. It is clean, bright, and well kept. The complementary breakfast has a wide variety of food and is constantly being stocked during eating hours. The hotel has a complementary shuttle to SeaWorld so you can leave your car at the hotel during the day. The staff is very courteous and knowledgeable of all the San Antonio attractions. There are several restaurants and shopping close to the hotel. Downtown San Antonio is about 16 - 18 miles, but it is an easy highway drive. Fiesta Texas is also a short drive on highway 1604. This facility is a good spot for getting to the Hill Country including Kerrville, Bandera, etc. All in all, a good headquarters location for a vacation in San Antonio.

title: “Great stay!!!”
text:
I still can't believe that I paid less than $100 per night for a room at the St. Anthony!!! Great hotel, location and service. I was just a bit surprised on how small the bedroom was but have no complains. Or maybe a little one (the carpet in my room smelled a bit) however this would not prevent me from staying there again.
Oh, they charge for wi-fi. Really?!

title: “Great Stay & no elevator problems !”
text:
My DD (8) and I stayed at the Marriott Marquis from the 12th-14th of April and we had a great time! I was very nervous about staying there because of some of the reviews but was driven to do so by the location! I am so glad I did because it was great! I used points to stay...65,000 but worth every one. We arrived at about 10:30 on the 12th and were able to get into our room right away, rm 2341. We had a great view of Time SQ, Toys R US & Good Morning America as well as the ESB! We ate at Breakfest at the Atrium, which was good and dinner at the View Lounge which was awesome...the view was fabulous!
As for the elevators we had no siginificant delays...we heard a few grumbles from other guests but nothing major. When we checked in, the front desk manager helped us and I mentioned what I read on the boards, evidently some of the hotel staff read the boards as well, and he said it is definitely getting better. I was very pleased with our elevator experience!
On the 14th we had a evening flight back to Germany and we were able to extend check out to 3pm with out any difficulty!

title: “The stay was too short for such a beautiful room!”
text: We stole away from our own B&B in Ogunquit for an overnight in Boston (my home town)...We love the Nine Zero...stayed there two nights back in December of 2007. When returning this time we wanted to treat ourselves again. From the moment we left the car at the valet parking, we were given first class treatment and then met Scott at the desk with check in. He was extremely friendly and yet very professional. He gave us lots of info while we chatted. Our room was perfect....seventh floor, corner room with a beautiful view and a sumptuous king bed....the bathroom was luxurious with Aveda products and terry robes. When we returned from dinner we found a welcome back gift of a box of chocolates from the Hotel Manager. That was a touch that we did not expect.....the next morning we chose to splurge and have breakfast in the dining room on the second floor. Oscar showed us to a table by the window and we enjoyed the French Toast, Fresh Fruit and juice and coffee. Oscar served us with a quiet reverance and attention to every detail refilling our coffee, etc without our notice. After breakfast we chatted and felt like we made a new friend. We are already looking to our next visit and mentioned on the way home that we should have stayed two nights! What a treat!

title: “Great place to stay!”
text: As always the Hyatt hotels are a exceptional place to stay. Staff was great-clean rooms-clean bathrooms. We didn't want to leave!! Loved the rooftop pool! Great location. It had a walkover bridge to get to the harbor so we didn't worry about crossing traffic. We will stay there again and again!

title: “Best Deal Around”
text: This is an excellent value and location. The staff handled chaos with ease.

title: “Exquisite environment, top level staff and support!”
text: This room was everything we hoped for .........spacious, quiet, elegant, comfortable and quite honestly a "can do" staff with the best attitude ever. A real bargain for the price!!

title: “Flawless”
text: Westin does it perfectly. Stress free. Stay and fly. Excellent service and food. We arrived easy check it, immaculate rooms,great service and food at lounge. Similar experience for breakfast. Relaxing atmosphere. Easy departure to airport.

title: “Very friendly staff!!”
text:
Before we decided on booking a room at the Andrews I contacted the hotel a couple of times since I made bad experiences with other hotels. This place is soooo helpful and very friendly, they reponded right away and gave me all the info I needed.
The room we had was rather small but clean! It had been cleaned every day! The parking lot was right behind the hotel and very friendly staff there too!
Breakfast was inclusive and served in the hallway so you could take it inside and eat in bed. It was very yummy and there has always been enough food except for the last few minutes of serving. The rates were great and the location too!A 5 minute walk to Union Square! Really a great choice!

title: “Excellent hotel with only a few minor flaws”
text:
We are a family of 5 and stayed for 3 nights in April in interconnecting rooms. 
Overall the hotel was great. The staff were friendly and attentive, the rooms were good and the beds comfortable. There were a number of things that could have been done better, which I have described below but, if you don't have time to read the rest, our overall summary is that this is a good hotel in a great location.
Having booked online a month in advance, with a confirmed reservation for rooms on the 20th floor or above, we didn't get off to a very good start on arrival. We were told that the only interconnecting rooms were on the 4th floor. In the rooms we found ourselves staring at the windows of the building opposite and decided to complain. The staff then 'discovered' they had interconnecting rooms on the 19th floor, not quite what we had booked, but a great view of Union Square. There are extensive overnight roadworks going on in Union Square at present, and the thin glazing on the windows allowed this work, and the traffic noise, to become quite intrusive, although we soon adjusted.
The rooms are newly refurbished, and although the furniture and decorations are not lavish, they are smart, neat and largely functional. Little things could be improved, like the fact that the room is provided with an ice bucket, ice tongs, a bottle opener, but no glasses! The kids were upset that their tastes were not catered for in the choice of TV channels delievered free to the room but again, these are minor complaints.
If you have a car, use the assisted parking at the garage across the street to save yourself valet charges. The restaurant on the 36th floor has fantastic views, the food is very good, and the waiting staff are friendly and helpful. We had a small problem with an undercooked dish, but were given a complimentary desert, which was very generous.
We would stay at this hotel again and thoroughly enjoyed our visit.

title: “Excellent service”
text:
Domingo Martinez Jr. did the difference every morning during breakfast. He was always smiling and ready to help.
The hotel is well located and frontdesk employees are very well trained to deal with foreign people.

title: “A solid hotel in Washington DC”
text:
I stayed here on business for 3 nights. 
I had a King room on the 6th floor and found the room comfortable with the usual facilites (see photos):
- Large HD flat screen TV
- Coffee / tea making facility
- Desk, phone, internet access ($19.98 for 2 days at time of writing this review)
- Complimentary toiletries
- Hairdryer
- Iron & board in-room
I made use of the hotel's gym which provided a decent amount of equipment and a pool; towels provided in the gym area, which is located on the 2nd floor.
The hotel has it's own bar (see photo) and restaurant, both of which are good, but relatively expensive compared to restaurants around the local area.
Capitol Hill is literally a 5 minute walk from the hotel (see photo) so location is great for the tourist (although I stayed in a B&B when visiting here last year, and found it to be more 'personal' for a holiday).
The staff throughout the hotel are great - all friendly and very helpful, so 10 out of 10 for the entire team at the hotel!
Overall, a good quality hotel providing a robust service - especially ideal for business use.

title: “Wonderful stay 3 years in a row!!”
text: We have stayed at this location in January for the last 3 years. Wonderful people, from the check in to the housekeeping staff, to the breakfast and then the check out. We have NEVER been disappointed with anything. We have a dog and they always make ALL of us feel welcome. The grounds are very nice and we always feel safe here. We would recommend this location to friends and family.

title: “Disappointing and overpriced”
text:
I recently spent 4 nights at the Doubletree Metropolitan, having high expectations from a 4 star, highly recommended and very pricey hotel in Midtown. 
Overall I was quite disappointed. A warning to all potential customers - the hotel rooms are NOTHING like what you see on the Doubletree website!! 
I stayed in an ordinary room (which still cost $300 per night not including breakfast) - the room was clean but the decor was very shabby - paint peeling off the walls, a completely bare, stark room, bad lighting and absolutely no space. Admittedly, it was my first experience of Manhattan hotels, but I refuse to believe that this is the best that 300 dollars can buy. 
The staff were civil, but not in any way warm, welcoming or helpful. Staying here, you're very aware of staying in a large hotel chain - the general feeling is totally impersonal.
As for facilities, the restaurant is ok - but again very expensive and the food ok but nowhere near 4-star standard.
My conclusion - this is a hotel that thinks it can charge 4-star prices for a 2-star service just because it's in Midtown Manhattan. Shop around before you stay here.

title: “Great stay!!”
text:
Stayed at the Sofitel for business. Excellent location, very central. Staff were great. Always pleasant and accomodating. Room was a nice size and had great mirrors. (I find few hotels have full length mirrors)!!
Would highly recommend and definitely would go back.

title: “Yotel is like living in an iPod”
text: It's like living inside an iPod...seriously. If you're looking for something different at a super affordable price this is it. Some people say it's small...but all times square near hotels are tiny...Yotel is smart about it though because they made the shower part of the room without a door; hence it makes the room seem more spacious. Pretty slick.

title: “Woul definately stay again”
text:
I couldn't believe just how large the rooms were! We didn't use the kitchen much, but there was everything you would need to make a meal if the NY cuisine was getting you down. I went with my family and we had 2 rooms. The A/C in my room worked extremely well and was quiet, however the one in my parent's room was a little noisier, but it by no means stopped them from sleeping. 
The bed was very comfortable and unlike a lot f hotels, the linen was of a good quality allowing you to ust sink into sleep after your flight, which was handy as ours had taken 28 hours rather than 7 with Delta but that's a different story.
The concierge was very helpful and very friendly. He told us where to go to find the best cheesecake, pretzels and diner in the city when we wanted to sample some typical american food. He also arranged a private car to take us back to the airport which only cost around $60 with tip and tolls. This was a lot cheaper than a metered taxi would have been especially as we were leaving in rush hour.
I would highly recommend this hotel for being safe, well located and quiet. It also comes attached to a very good italian restuarant that outdid an italian we went to in little italy!

title: “USC ucla game”
text: We have 30 people here wanting to watch game and eat . No guarantee to watch game says staff ok will eat and drink elsewhere. Not smart service.

title: “Good location, yet too pretentious”
text:
Location was great. Close to UCLA and Santa Monica.
That all said, the hotel staff strives to be a little too pretentious. 
The hotel was nice and clean. However the bathrooms need an update.
Construction was ongoing during our stay. The construction crew was using a glue that let off some very powerful, unpleasant fumes. Made me choke and gave me a headache as I walked by the construction zone. I advised to hotel crew of this and also notified them in a subsequent survey. The only response was "I will let them know". 
Also, there should also be self parking at this hotel. It is valet only a $25 a day. The garage is under the hotel and easily accessible to the hotel lobby. This would be easy for guests to self park in. I pulled up in my rental Hyundai... the valet guys at first were helpful until the guy in a Jaguar pulled up behind me... then they forgot I even existed.
Finally, the restaurant is overpriced.... this presumably is so to attract the local BelAir and Beverly Hills crowds. $50 Sunday brunch!

title: “Elysee = Perfection”
text:
New York City is the epicenter for so many of the world's finest things: food, fashion, business and finance, etc. So it always stuns me when I see chain restaurants and hotels packed with tourists when so many unbelieveable options exist to truly have that quintessential "New York Experience."
My wife and I came here for a week long vacation and to visit family. We chose the Elysee for its close proxmity to shopping, restaurants, and entertainment. It came through in every way imaginable. The rooms were clean, elegant, and comfortable. The staff was incredibly accomodating and offered world class service. When you stay at the Elysee, you really feel like a guest in a someone's home instead of some drone in some 40 story monolith with a fanny pack and an I heart NY t-shirt on. John the general manager personally went out of his way to make sure we had the best vacation possible. It was that small attention to detail that truly made our vacation as relaxing and memorable as it could be.
PROS: Close to subway, world class restaurants, shopping, Central Park, excellent service without being overbearing, clean and comfortable rooms, free breakfast, free happy hour with wine and snacks, SERVICE, SERVICE, SERVICE
CONS: The hotel could not do anything about it raining our last day there.
Rest assured, the Hotel Elysee will meet your expectatios and more. If you have never been to NYC, do NOT eat at TGI Friday or Crapplebee's, do NOT stay at some chain hotel. Stay at the Hotel Elysee and revel in the outstanding service, quality rooms, and perfect location.

title: “If you are a funky old Hippie, this is your Mecca!!!”
text: The hotel itself is clean & OK...but for what they are charging you are expecting the Marriott...but you are getting the Holiday Inn express!!!! The setup & motif is an old barn country feeling....hardwood floors & a jean denim blanket....One good thing is they don't allow pets! You are really just paying for the location! This hotel is really weird, in some of the rooms there are mirrors on the ceiling; Swinger Hotel? The staff isn't very friendly or professional...Way too many young kids work here who answer to a weak manager instead of a professional corporate structure. Stay at the Renaissance Airport Hotel...To hell with the Farmer's Daughter....

title: “LOVED IT!!!!!!”
text: Stayed at the Drury Plaza Hotel Riverwalk with my husband & Husky Mix! The entire staff was very friendly, especially to our dog! The room was clean & nice. The hotel is not even a block away from the Riverwalk & is 15mins from the airport. The hotel & Riverwalk is pet friendly! I would recommend taking pets during the day if they're people shy. Our Husky Mix loved the attention he got during the night life lol We really enjoyed this stay & will def stay again!

title: “Family owned and old fashioned customer service!”
text: This was our second stay at this small old style hotel. You park your car in front of your room here, and as other reviewers have said, the rooms and bathrooms are small compared so some other chain hotels. Just a few miles from UCLA, this family owned hotel has the nicest staff and they go out of their way to make your stay perfect. As we had an very large truck to bring my mother in law's scooter, they gave us a small stepping stool with a "reserved" sign to hold one of the larger parking spaces in front of our room while we were gone. This was so helpful in terms of getting a space we fit in as well as one that allowed an easy loading of an elderly lady! The rooms are very clean, comfortable and the breakfast is just perfect for us. You can get coffee and tazo teas in the lobby any time and you will always be greeted with a friendly smile. Don't miss the breakfast patio with the lovely fountain just off the lobby, a nice relaxing spot on a sunny morning. There is a bit of traffic on Sunset Blvd. it was not a problem for us, and quieter than other hotels we have stayed in that are closer to the freeways in this area. I felt the rates were very reasonable for Brentwood and the great location of this charming motel!

title: “Refreshing Take on the Motorcity”
text:
Originally from the Detroit area, I had grown up knowing Detroit to be a dilapidated version of a once proud city. Too young to have actually seen any of its original splendor, I was only aware that it ever existed because stories my grandparents told. Visiting Detroit after I had moved away, I especially longed for any semblance of the beautiful hotels I had heard once populated the city. Until fairly recently, all accommodations available in Detroit weren't even options to those travelers who required basic qualities such as safety and cleanliness. Stays in the suburbs were a necessity.
For 25 years of my existence, the Book Cadillac was nothing more than another abandoned ruin in the city of Detroit. Now, I am overjoyed to report that this hotel has been restored to a glorious place of beauty and glamour! Just as in my grandma's stories, it comes complete with movie stars and all (really)!
I would consider myself particular when it comes to hotels -and yet, would highly recommend the Westin Book Cadillac to all. It's location is ideal, and this is extremely important when visiting Detroit. The hotel's staff is very friendly and very helpful, albeit a little slow at times. The building's public areas, including the lobby, hallways, restaurants, and pool room, etc. are tastefully decorated with contemporary styling and very well-kept. The rooms offer the same aesthetic appeal and cleanliness, as well as extremely comfortable and luxe accommodations. 
I applaud the Westin for their successful efforts in renovating and revitalizing this property. If you have not visited the "D" in sometime, do yourself a favor and see it again from the perspective this hotel provides!

title: “NOT GOOD”
text: We were at your Hotel for 6 days for a Family Reunion in July. When we checked in my room smelled (mold, carpet dirty). I could not breathe. I had runny nose and kept sneezing. There were crickets everywhere and mosquitos. I do not expect crickets in my hotel room and when I complained to the front dest, they told me "that's the way it is in TX" I told her I am sorry but I don't accept that. We checked out after one night to a nearyby hotel who did not have crickets (still in TX). Sorry but I am from SC and we do not treat our visitors like that. This was our first visit to a Double Tree Hotel and the last one also. I was not the only family member that complained, about 6-8 were very unhappy with the rooms but did not check out because they had kids and older ones with them and that would have been a lot to pack up and move them. Oh by the way, the cookies were "Awesome." Thank You, Gloria from SC

title: “Mid week stay”
text: I stayed overnight when I went for a show at the Avalon club on Vine at Hollywood. I had a Cozy corner room which was lovely except for the billboard that stayed illuminated all night long. The desk said they had a blackout curtain on that window but I couldn't see how it worked in the middle of the night. Drai's on the rooftop for late lunch was marvelous especially in gorgeous, sunny & clear weathr.

title: “AWESOME NEW HOTEL IN CHICAGO”
text: My family and I stayed 4 nights at the Radison Blu during a recent visit to Chicago for the Lollapalooza Music Festival. The location was perfect and only a few blocks from the festival. The incredibly friendly and accommodating staff made our stay very enjoyable.The Filini restaurant/bar is so convenient and serves outstanding meals and appetizers all hours of the day. The workout facility was the best I have seen at a hotel and it included a lap pool and outdoor running track on the third floor. The hotel has 5star amenities, a very friendly staff and a perfect location one block from Michigan Avenue. It was the best hotel experience I have had in years

title: “Ideal location”
text:
Just returned from a 4 night break in New York but feel like I need another holiday to get over this 1! The hotel is the ideal location for anyone wanting to explore all the tourist attractions. It is less than a minutes walk away from Macey's, 5 minutes from the Empire State Building and about 10 minutes walk away from Time Square. Central Park is about a 20 minute walk but theres so much to see along the way it goes really quick. I was actually surprised how near everything was to each other.We bought a Metro card and caught the bus to Ground Zero and the ferry to go to the Statue of Liberty. We didn't actually go onto Ellis Island but caught the free ferry to Staten Island and jumped straight back on to come back. It was a good way to get some great photos. We also caught the ferry in the evening to get some photos of New York by night. It was far from a relaxing break and by the 3RD day my feet were screaming for me to stop walking on them! The free breakfast was a great way to start the day. There was bagels, cereals, fresh fruit, toast, coffee(24 hours a day),tea, juices and muffins on offer. The only downside of the hotel was there wasn't a bath in the room although I'm told that most hotels only have showers so it seems that its not unusual but after all that walking all I wanted to do was have a relaxing soak in the bath. The roof top terrace was closed when we were there, apparently its closed for the season. The rooms are clean, comfortable and of a decent size but to be honest, you spend so little time in the room anyway!
If you want to know anything else, just email me and I will try to be of some help!

title: “A Grand Old Hotel in the Classic Sense”
text: We cannot praise the Palace Hotel in San Francisco enough. From their glassed domed Garden Court retaining the century old elegance to the large suite with classic crown mouldings, baseboard, door casings and deep, and deep windowsills that allow you to sit in the sun and take in all the beauty of the surrounding city, every experience and amenity here is of the best quality. Our next visit and stay there can't come soon enough.

title: “Great hotel at a superb location between 5th and Broadway!”
text: We (Swedish couple 20-25) stayed at this HGI for three nights and couldn't be happier. Excellent location, equally close to most of NYC's landmarks - and VERY close to the ESB. Service is fantastic, the staff is always nice and friendly and seems to work by "rather saying hello once too often, than once too seldom". We also had a few somewhat strange (?) requests, but everything we asked for was instantly taken care of without so much as a raised eyebrow. We can't praise the servicemindedness and friendliness enough, especially that of Nikki's, one of the evening front desk staff members (?) who always seemed to have an answer to every question. We deeply and sincerely appreciate this hotel and most of all its staff. We will both return and recommend.

title: “Reasonably Nice Place”
text: I'm not a casino guy --- was here for 3 days for a conference. Mixing with the "casino crowd" coursing through the lobby constantly was not so great. Nevertheless, the rooms are quite nice, the view across the river to Canada quite nice, the FREE INTERNET the way every hotel should do it. The restaurant / bar choices downstairs weren't so great, as of course they want you to drink in the casino. The restaurant at the top floor is pricey but really a treat.

title: “Amazing Service!”
text: The staff at the Courtyard by Marriott San Diego Downtown provided us with amazing service, clean and comfortable rooms, and a vacation we will never forget. If you have a chance, take the time to explore the hotel or ask Nicholas, the wonderful concierge, for a tour! =)

title: “Really good value motel in San Francisco”
text:
I stayed at the Nob Hill Motor Inn with my husband for 10 days in March/April of this year and felt it lived up the reviews on tripadvisor which we used as our guide.
Good points:
Excellent Location, you can walk to all the main sights and to downtown. or you can walk a couple of blocks to the cable car. Polk street is nearby and there are great restaurants within walking distance and a really useful supermarket in case you want to use the fridge and microwave in your room and save even more money! Also good cafes for breakfast to supplement the free pastries. 
Very clean. Immaculate rooms and bathrooms. Fresh towels and toiletries every day. The standard of the decor is very good and we felt very comfortable and relaxed. Great large TV. Fridge, microwave and coffee machine.
Quiet location (better than downtown) and very comfortable beds. 
Helpful owners, can go to them with questions but they are not intrusive and you can come and go as you please.
We felt it was a home from home!

title: “Perfect Business Stay”
text: Kudos to General Manager, Dan Williams and his super friendly & helpful team! Was in Philadelphia for a conference (first visit) and was really pleased with the central location - right across the street from the convention center and close to many other sights, the comfortable and clean room, & very nice on-site dining. Look forward to returning for both business and pleasure!

title: “At the Waldorf.... March 24-26”
text:
I really wanted to love the Waldorf. I had set my expectations accordingly i.e. low, changed in a few large bills for smaller bills to tip everyone we came across and I had even made sure not to wear blue jeans at the Waldorf=Astoria so I could take in the historic hotel and feel one with my environment.
Unfortunately after the front desk, service pretty much went down hill. I remember Lauren checked us in and she was quite nice giving us the option of two rooms to choose from and even supplied us with a map of NYC, complimentary water and a verbal overview of the hotels restaurants. The room (1727) was nice enough, pretty clean and I could find almost no fault with the room, loads of hot water, working quiet heater, no inside or outside noise. The lotion that the staff leaves from FRESH is top-notch.
Unfortunately at the Waldorf apparently the doormen are too busy doing other things (standing around looking Waldorf=Astoriaish) to hold open doors.
At the Waldorf bell hops are too busy (talking about other guests broken luggage) to take your bags and just leave you standing around feeling foolish in front of the hellhop desk.
At the Waldorf cleaning staff never fully make your bed, but instead leave the bedspread and shams folded in the room on the luggage rack for your entire two night stay. 
At the Waldorf's Bull and Bear Restaurant where one soda, one drink and dessert run $50 the staff is far too busy to provide your table with a table cloth or service of any kind.
At the Waldorf you will be left to fight off black town cars sent over by the staff to take you to the airport. The WA even has a sign inside suggesting you only take yellow checker cabs, so why an employee would send a black town car over to it's guests is beyond me.
If you want to stay here, you are going to do it no matter what you read. It's not horrible, but I just say make sure you know why you want to stay here and that it's not because you think you're going to have some super four star treatment by the staff of the Waldorf=Astoria.

title: “Quiet in the City”
text: Very classy hotel with friendly and efficient staff. Just a block away from all the midtown highlights but extremely quiet. John the concierge arranged tickets for Jersey Boys and offered great suggestions for restaurants. We didnt get an opportunity to eat at the hotel's restaurant because there's an excellent corner deli and so many restaurants all around. Large room, comfy beds and we needed the cold A/C during an unseasonal warm spell.

title: “Not Bad”
text:
A group of eight of us stayed in the Wellington for 5 nights at the end of February. The first impression is that it looks quite nice in a dated sort of way. When we arrived it was total chaos. The queue for reception numbered about 20 and the staff did not seem to know what they were doing. When i finally got to the front 2 out of the 4 rooms were not ready and and the ones that were seemed to be the smallest they had.
On a plus side was the location only a 10 minute walk to Times Square and 2 minutes to Central Park.

title: “A Sea World Must!”
text: We stayed two nights for a Sea World get away. The hotel staff is the friendliest I've ever had. Everyone seemed to have time to say hello and talk. Were interested in our stay and what we're doing. The cleaning folks were nice enough to even find my sons toys in the drawer and arrange them on the bed. It was such a heart warming touch we did not expect. The walls are a little thin, but I've had worse. Other than that the place is new, clean and comfortable. Everyone was friendly, including guests. They also offered a happy-hour of beer and wine and that was a nice surprise too. OH, and do not over-look the shuttle to/from Sea World !!! --- My only suggestion for Microtel ... plastic business cards for the shuttle. -- a great stay, and we'll be back.

title: “Excellent Everything”
text:
We stayed here on 12/19/09 to celebrate a 35th wedding anniversary, it also happened to be the eve of a huge Nor'easter. The hotel is in prime location, right in the center of everything, but still seems to be a relatively quiet street. The hotel rooms all have there own fire places and jacuzzi tubs. Speakers are piped into the ceiling throughout the extra large rooms. We saw two other rooms that our extended family were staying in and they were just as nice. The entire staff was extremely nice and helpful and the next morning after the "blizzard" they brought our car to us from Valet within minutes. WE enjoyed brunch at the restaurant downstairs and it was outstanding. A little pricey but well worth it for the quality and freshness. 
I would highly recommend this hotel....I live in the city of Boston and I have stayed at the Westin Copley; The Sheraton in Fanieul Hall and although they were both nice this Hotel is off the hook! 
The bed was extremely comfortable also and everything was extremely clean.

title: “Loved this hotel! Great Location, Clean Modern and Best Beds Ever!!!”
text: This hotel was great. It was one block from fabulous shopping and great eateries. It was also walking distance (20 minutes) to the convention center and to the historic parks (30 minutes). The hotel lobby was very modern and the bell service and car valet staff were excellent upon our arrival and check-out. the room had the best bed we've ever had at a US hotel and the crib was great for our toddler, not a flimsy fold away that buckle under the tossing and turning. The bathroom seemed to be recently renovated with solid surface counters, all glass shower enclosure and separate tub. Room service was yummy and reasonably priced as big city hotels go. The hotel isn't bargain priced, but you get what you pay for and this was well worth our money. This will be the only place we stay when visiting Philly!

title: “Basic, no frills accomodations in the Theater District”
text:
I got a great AAA rate at this property of $117/night by booking a few months in advance before the hotel had even opened for business. Given that the UN General Assembly was in session at the time of my stay, this was an unheard of bargain for that week in NYC. However, even at that price and the fact that the hotel was less than a month old, I was less than thrilled with property and with my stay there.
Rooms are of decent size for accomodations of this class/price in Manhattan, with the sleeping area probably 200-225 sq ft. I had a room with 2 double beds (other rooms have only 1 queen bed). The bathroom was very small (the door barely cleared the toilet) but the vanity was spacious compared to other comparable properties I've stayed at in Manhattan. Upon walking into my room, my partner immediately noticed trash left behind (an empty carton of cigarettes and a soft drink cup were sitting on top of the closet unit). Otherwise, the room was clean--but I found this oversight by the cleaning staff unacceptable.
Beds were new and comfortable. I didn't like that the hotel uses bedspreads instead of the more popular double sheet/duvet covers in vogue these days at better properties. Bedspreads are not very sanitary (hotels rarely wash them), but since the hotel was less than a month old, I wasn't too grossed out (there weren't any visible stains). Sheets were a bit rough and scratchy. Pillows were ample (and feather-free). Towels were absorbent and soft and of decent quality for a hotel of this class.
HVAC worked well in the room. I was on the 6th floor facing 44th St and had few issues with noise but I'm used to living in NYC. The fridge and microwave ovens originally advertised by the hotel apparently are not going to be included in the rooms, or at least weren't at this time. My room lacked a desk and instead had a small square table that substituted for one. It had two arm chairs when it would have been better equipped with one desk chair and one arm chair. Oh, well. TV worked well overall and had reasonable channel selections. Wireless internet was free and worked well when I used it. Coffee machine and ice bucket in room were a plus (ice free in basement). There is only one elevator for this 7 story building.
Free breakfast was very basic and nothing to get excited over--cheap carbs to get you moving in the morning. Hours were rather limited as was the seating area. Breakfast consisted of coffee, juices, sugary cereals, some breads/bagels/pastries of mediocre quality and make your own waffles. The breakfast area was kept stocked the three mornings I was at the hotel.
Considering the hotel was less than a month old, it didn't seem like it was new, although it was generally clean and modern in appointments. I question whether over time this property will hold up. Hallways and rooms didn't appear to be vacuumed daily, and some of the dirt/mess from construction was never cleaned up. Housekeeping was a bit rude and not the best in the industry. This appears to be a family run property.
Would I stay here again? Well, likely not. I think there are better managed properties, and cleaner, more pleasing properties, at comparable pricepoints in Manhattan if you do your research. Perhaps I've been spoiled by some great deals at better properties in Manhattan during this recession. But now that the economy is turning around, the days of decent hotel rooms in NYC under $200/night might be coming to an end.

title: “Top of the Heap”
text:
This is the 4th or 5th time Hotwire has placed me at this property and I've come to rejoice every time it's revealed to me after I've made my up-front payment. This hotel is not only one of the best Four Points properties there is, I think it's one of the best Sheratons. Heck, it's one of the best hotels I've ever stayed at - period! This two-story edifice was the first hotel built near BWI. It's closest to the terminals and overshadowed by the more recently built behemoth Daily Parking Garage sited next door. There's free parking in front of the hotel (often right at the door if the parking gods are smiling down on you) and there's at-call shuttle service 24/7. By some historical dispensation, theirs are the only hotel shuttles that pull up at the closest curb to baggage claim exit doors.
Check-in is always friendly and efficient. The rooms are nicely outfitted with all the usual amenities. Even the art work is aeronautically themed. Housekeeping is flawless and Michener's, the hotel's restaurant, is first-rate in terms of food and service. By all means, try the Maryland Velvet Crab soup and crab cakes for some local flavor. I had my pancake epiphany here. "So THIS is how pancakes are supposed to look and taste" I thought the first time I tried them. Take the extra step and get the banana-nut pancakes. You can add on two eggs and bacon or sausage for only $3.
There are lots of nice little touches here. One I noticed were the large urns with flowers on the exterior sills of the floor-to-ceiling windows. One definitely gets the feeling that there's a real "We're all in this together" spirit on the part of the staff. Everyone is eager to please. Obviously, this "can do" attitude is inspired by savvy management. There's a real sense of pride here. Another advantage here is easy access to the light rail station at the terminal which affords an easy and cheap ride to downtown Baltimore for sight-seeing.

title: “hotel from hell”
text: booked this hotel three months ahead,to ensure we had a none smoking room.when we arrived yes youve got it, sorry sir only smoking available.when i explained that my wife was asthmatic the not to friendly receptionist asked" well do you want to book out" not an anwer when you have been traveling for several days.we reluctantly had to take the room only to be kept awake with the constant noise from the heavy road and rail traffic.at 4a.m the smoke detector began to sound,on phoning reception we were told maintenance would attend,when we left at 9.30a.m it was still bleeping.we had stayed in 10 seperate hotels on a fantastic tour all being of a very good standard except for this one which we would rate as very poor.

title: “Wonderful Stay, Wonderful Price”
text: My boyfriend and I stayed here for one night as a little mid-week getaway, and we couldn't have been happier with our experience. From the lobby to the cocktail lounge to our room, everything was clean and comfortable. The free appetizers/drinks at 5:30 every day were a great touch and a nice way to get our evening started. The room was bigger than we thought it would be and the amenities were lovely. The decor was modern and chic, and even the bathroom exceeded our expectations. Plus we got a great deal through the hotel's website. I'd highly recommend this hotel for anyone coming to visit Chicago and even for locals looking for a little break from the norm.

title: “excellent service”
text: Excellent service, I had a concern with my room and Avi and his manager were both extremely helpful and moved me to another very nice room.l

title: “Hyatt was Grand”
text: Spent three nights in July at the Grand Hyatt Seattle. The hotel was beautiful. The bathroom was magnificent. Had two rooms with 2 double beds in each. The hotel is within walking distance to many stores and restaurants (Cheese Cake Factory 1 block away). It is close enough to walk to Pike's Market and to the monorail to take you to the Space Needle. Don't eat breakfast at Ruth's Chris that is in the hotel. It is too expensive. Can't say enough good things about this hotel. Will definitely stay here again if I return to Seattle.

title: “value; comfort”
text:
We normally stay in Hiltons, H Gardens. or the like. we stayed here on basis of location and TA recommendation. We were not disappointed. Rooms very clean and well appointed. Cleaned to within an inch of their lives every day. Excellent efficient service from front desk. Parking free and easy to enter from Lombard Street -here heavy traffic on route 101. Access to Fisherman's Wharf and cable cars via r30 trolley bus. 
We used the passport -$20 for 3 days and we must have used $20 per day.
Breakfast is a couple of pastries and in room coffee, with a smile.
Couldn't really fault it

title: “Great Value !!!!”
text:
Stayed here as our origonal choice was fully booked and this hotel was recommended by a local friend. Great size rooms, well equiped and extremely good value. The rooms could sleep four people with free breakfast and free drinks at happy hr FOR AROUND £80 PER ROOM PER NIGHT!!!.
You can also get free minibus throughout the week. 
Only problem i could really mention is it isnt too close to the action of sunset boulevard or the theme parks but if you have a car then i doubt you will find better.

title: “Nice Hotel!! Good Location.”
text: I stayed at the Roosevelt Hotel in NYC with my 11 year old daughter and we really liked it. The rooms were clean and the staff was very helpful. We enjoyed sitting in the lobby for our last few hours and waiting for our train. Very close to the train station for a late night snack and a there is a little deli on the corner for inexpensive quick breakfast food in the morning. Very close to the American Girl Doll Store and Build a Bear if you have small children. Will be staying there again in a month. Highly recommend.

title: “Tried and true Marriott - used to be better”
text: When we first arrived, doorman service was lackluster-left on bags on the trolley outside and then in the hallway w/o telling bell staff where to take it; rooms are tiny here; concierge lounge used to have better variety and quality but has diminished; water in the room w/not stay hot-you had to constantly turn it up or down to get temperature right! Very annoying - and sink/tub did not drain. Overall location is great and Kenny on the bell staff was awesome but nothing else to set this hotel apart!

title: “Good Location, but Terrible Customer Service”
text:
I stayed here for one weeknight a few weeks ago. The location is very close to Times Square and easy walking distance to everything. It was also easy to grab a cab from here, going uptown or downtown. The rooms are very small, but clean, and it is perfectly fine for a couple of nights, especially if you are not planning to stay in the room very long. 
However, I was not impressed with the customer service - doing the easy checkout, I did not receive a bill. Realizing I needed a bill for an expense report, I have called the front desk and the Accounting department for the past week requesting one. I still have not received an email or phone call back. Very disappointing, considering it would take all of five minutes to email me a bill. Don't expect this hotel to go out of their way for you.
Also, the room service and bar do not open until 5 pm, and don't expect them to serve you at 4:59 p.m. either.

title: “Pleasant hotel”
text:
We enjoyed this hotel.
Quite homely. Nice pool, not enormous but big enough.
Quiet in the day when everyone diss appears to universal and other places, but busy from about 4 pm onwards, even through the evening.
Suited us as our daughter was recording in LA so we sat round in the day when it was quiet.
Restaurat serves good food and room was peaceful . Do ask for a quiet room if required, as it worked for us.
Overall very nice and would return

title: “Great service, nice room”
text:
Everybody who worked at the hotel was kind and courteous. The lobby is not big and opulent, but it is very nice. We received a free upgrade to our room because a regular room with a roll-in shower wasn't available, and that is what I had booked three weeks prior to our stay. The view out the window was bad, a concrete wall, but we didn't stay in the room long anyway. 
This hotel may be popular with celebrities. William H Macy was staying there whiled we were.

title: “Over 25 stays per year... & I love the place!”
text:
As a frequent business traveler I have made the Galleria Park Hotel my #1 lodging choice in San Francisco for over 5 years. 
I'm a clinically diagnosed high maintenance guest so it gives me pleasure to give Galleria Park my rare & unconditional praise. 
I don't think you'll find a more professional and friendly staff in SF. Sure you may hear street noise but that's typical in any major city.

title: “Nice hotel... great location.”
text: Been staying here regularly for the past 4 years. Terrific location, very convenient to many good restaurants and attractions. Staff are nice; never any problems. Highly recommend.

title: “Good But Not Grand”
text: I stayed here at the beginning of April. I was given a room on the 25th floor. It was spacious for two people but no more than that. I noticed there was a bit of mold on the shower curtain in the bathroom. Secondly, the elevators seemed to run a bit slow. The best thing about this hotel is the LOCATION!!! It is connected to Grand Central and is only blocks away from Times Square and the Empire State Building. When I made my reservation I had requested an early check-in, which was granted by the staff. I highly recommend this hotel to first time visitors to the city. I have stayed in numerous Hyatt properties throughout the country,this is was not my favorite. For being the only Hyatt property in the city, I feel they need to improve the cleanliness of the rooms and modernize the furniture. Do not stay here for more than $300 a night!

title: “Perfect Location & Affordable...”
text:
I stayed with a friend for 6 nights in the New Yorker. For us it was all about location & affordablity, New York is one of the most expensive cities when it comes to accommodation & value for money. This hotel has a perfect location, its hop skip & jump from from Macy's & Penn Station/Madison Square Gardens & 3 or for blocks from Times Square/Broadway Shows. We stayed in a double room it was little tight for floor space but it was clean & rooms were seen to everyday. The staff were helpful & friendly we had problem with hairdryer in the bathroom, rang down to receiption & they sent up someone up to fix straight away. The hotel its self has an old feel to it, when you get out of lift to its dated but i kinda liked that, it was step back in time a little, art deco feel to it... I know some people might want modern & new & bright but lets be realistic when you go to NYC its for Tourist Attactions & Shopping, you're not going to be spending all time in your hotel or hotel room..
I would stay in the New Yorker & i would recommend it to friends.

title: “Good value, but many problems”
text:
Plus points - decent sized rooms, good location, good value for money.
Minus points - very unhelpful staff, terrible plumbing (noise and effectiveness), old furnishings, poor check-in (got room at 11pm!)
In conclusion, if you can put up with the negatives, the location and value for money make the Bedford a reasonable choice.

title: “One of the best Marriott properties!”
text: Phenomenal views, outstanding customer service, perfectly located. What more can I say? It was a sheer delight to stay here. I absolutely recommend it. One tiny criticism: lack of seating in main lobby. Would be nice when you're waiting for someone. Otherwise, absolutely NO complaints here!

title: “Pretty Good with some Rought Spots”
text:
I completed a 1 night stay here on Friday. Upon check-in, we were given a choice of the $15 wine card or a cheese plate and a bottle of wine for our Diamond amenity. Since we were a party of two, I asked if we could have some extra funds on the wine card, to which the answer was no. In retrospect, I think I should have gotten the cheese plate and bottle of wine, since the wine bar is expensive and $15 is really only good for about 1 glass.
Check-in was fine. Parking is expensive at $35/night. We used a Diamond Suite upgrade and at first was put in a "Large King." I refused this room and told the front desk this was not a suite. We were then moved to an Andaz Loft. This isn't really a suite. But since I was only there for 1 night, we took this room. We were proactively warned about the, noise from the club above which was appreciated. 
Even though the Andaz Loft is definitely not a suite, I liked the room. I liked the decor, layout and the bed was comfortable. I don't know what this hotel was like before the conversion to Andaz, but i think Hyatt did a good job at renovating this property.
I checked out the rooftop bar/pool and the gym. Both were nice, but nothing memorable.
In the evening, we went to the wine bar. There wasn't a soul there, so we had the bartender to ourselves and got some good service. In addition to trying out the wines, we got some appetizers and the pizza and cheese plate we got were very good. One word of note: make sure to only put money on the card that you are prepared to use. Any leftover money on the wine card cannot be refunded, which I was a bit upset about because I saw no reason why they couldn't provide a refund.
In terms of the noise, yes it was loud. On the night we were there, it ended at about 1AM. For one or two nights, it would be ok for me and my sig other, since we are both heavy sleepers, but i definitely would not be able to take that noise every night.
The next morning we had breakfast and got the best service that we ever received throughout our stay from our waitress that morning. She was very courteous and gave us carte blanche to order whatever we wanted. We gave her a nice tip.
Unfortunately, at checkout, the front desk erroneously charged us for minibar charges which we did not take, and also erroneously charged us for breakfast. For some reason, it took a long time for this to be settled, and I left the hotel a bit annoyed with the staff.
In summary, I'd probably come back for another short stay, but I wouldn't be able to take a weekend here because of the noise. And I definitely wouldn't waste a suite upgrade here.

title: “An Elvis lovers dream”
text: Clean rooms, so close to Graceland, awesome looking pool...so much Elvis stuff which was perfect for a fan like me..great tv selections which include 3 Elvis movie channels..only complaints were even though our room was non smoking you could smell smoke from other rooms or from outside and the breakfast couldve had more selections...other than that a wonderful place to stay and we enjoyed it!!

title: “Going Back for a Third Time!”
text: This was our second visit, having also stayed at the Shelburne in April 2005 and we intend to make this an annual event. I agree with other reviews in that the hotel is a little 'tired' but it doesn't detract from the excellent service, enormous rooms (1 bedroom with 2 queen beds - the beds are so comfortable and there is also a pillow menu) which easily allows for family of 3 or 4, plus guest(s) on living room sofa bed.
