The living room is also massive and very comfortable and as well as comfortable sofas and armchairs, has extendable dining table and chairs. There are many wardrobes/cupboards so all the clothes, cases and shopping can be hidden away (together with the iron and ironing board provided). The kitchen facilities are fantastic - where else would you get dishwasher/large oven/hob/enormous fridge-freezer/coffee machine/microwave, etc? Cutlery, crockery, glassware are also provided and ample coffee/tea provisions are topped up daily as are dishwasher tablets and tea towels. The bathrooms are small but very clean and adequate and there are plenty of complimentary toiletries. The two bed rooms are extremely spacious, consisting of 2 double rooms, 2 bathrooms, extra large living/dining area and kitchen. Try to get a room with view of Empire State which adds to the NY buzz and the Chrysler Building is a few minutes walk up road, opposite Grand Central Station. Fantastic views of both from roof. (The roof bar is closed in April) A recent addition to the Shelburne is The Den - a relaxing, modern lounge area and our two younger members loved the gym. Best place for stocking up provisions is from D'Agostini's deli which is around the corner on E37th/3rd Ave. - great quality food and open late - they also deliver. The Rare Bar downstairs has great food at reasonable prices (try the basket of assorted fries and chocolate bread pudding - not necessarily together). Another handy place to eat is Hudson Place on corner of 36th/3rd - large menu and good prices. The area is a residential oasis just minutes from most tourist attractions and feels safe any time of day or night and is more than adequately provided for by delis, restaurants, bagel bars, etc. We feel 'at home' at the Shelburne and can't wait to return next year.

title: “Nice location with friendly but incompetent staff.”
text:
I stayed for 20 nights for business in downtown Houston. The location is convenient with several downtown buses passing regularly. Galleria and the stores nearby are a mecca for shopping, which I did much of too. The front desk is friendly and always answers the phone, even at late hours and holidays. Kudos for that!
There is a (slow) elevator available if your room is not on the ground floor. There are no meal amenities at the hotel but there are restaurants and a CVS pharmacy nearby. The laundry cost $2.00 to wash and the same to dry (look out; there is one washer for $1.00 which seemed out of place but who's complaining?) My room and also the rooms of my two colleagues looked and smelled clean but there was a 2 inch crusty stain on one side of my queen sized bed linen, which I avoided by sleeping on the other side. They claim to change bed linen every 7 days but after my first housekeeping visit - lo and behold! My stain remains! Is it possible they could have two bed linens with stains in exactly the same spot or is someone not doing their job? 
The worst experience was the toilet which clogged not once, not twice, but three times! After having the first malfeasance dealt with, maintenance was unable to effect a solution a second time leaving me to suffer with the stench for the rest of Sunday and Memorial day because 'maintenance doesn't work on that holiday'. At every stage I had to pester and prod the front desk to have the decency to offer me another room to perform my most basic of functions. I got much in the way of sorries but little follow-up - for example I was promised the card for a nearby empty room as soon as it was cleaned to avoid an embarassing pilgramage to the end of the hall. After waiting forever, I had to call the front desk who had obviously forgotten about me. 
This customer was made to understand what was more important to the staff when front desk had the gall to enquire on a minor payment detail while still neglecting to follow-up on my requests. When the toilet was finally cleared, I was left to clean up 'the mess' which seemed unfair since it was caused by their malfunctioning equipment. 
My other two colleagues had no complaints whatsoever about this hotel, so my conclusion is that you should be fine as long as everything works in your room but don't count on timely assistance in case of an emergency.

title: “Great Weekend Vacation!”
text: Stayed at the J.W. Marriott Hill Country for a girls weekend and had an amazing time! The hotel is absolutely beautiful. We spent the majority of our time by the pool, cabanas, and in the lazy river. The pool and surrounding areas are extremely well maintained, despite a record-breaking drought. The hotel room was well appointed with a huge “spa like” bathroom and very comfortable beds. If you want easy access to downtown San Antonio, this is not the hotel for you. It’s located north of San Antonio, many miles away from shopping/restaurants/nightlife. Great place if you’re looking to get away from it all! My only complaint was that the service was extremely slow at the pool and in restaurants. Staff members were always friendly and accommodating; however, we usually waited an extended period of time to place and receive orders. I’d say that was more of an issue of not having enough staff versus incompetent/rude staff. I would most certainly stay here again.

title: “Enjoyed my stay”
text:
We just came back from our 4day trip to S.D. Our stay at the Sheraton was good. I checked in early to get a good view, but since we requested two adjoining rooms they could'nt accomodate us with a better view unless we separated (understandable). We stayed at the east tower. All the restaurants and the main pool are at the east tower, just nice. The pool side food is typical of hotel food pricey and not that great. The hotel has updated its look in some areas and some are desperatly asking for help like the arcade. 
My sister stayed in the west tower. Rooms are renovated and seem larger. If your not traveling with family, stay there its more quiet. Overall we enjoyed our stay, Im not a big winer.

title: “Nice Hotel”
text: This was a nice upscale hotel in the Symphony Hall area of downtown San Diego. The bus and trolley system were maybe 3 blocks away. I was in San Diego with my daughter who was there for a business meeting pertaining to her job. The hotel is in a quiet like area. The only problem I found was there seems to be a lot of homeless people in the area, but they weren't loitering in the hotel area. They have the best breakfast buffet in town. Everything you can imagine was on the buffet. The staff was very friendly especially the blonde guy who works the bar. (can't remember his name) They offer light horsdvrs at happy hour. The drinks are pretty reasonable. It's was pretty chilly here I think in the middle 60's with the high of about 70. So after a cool day of walking and feeling that chill off of the harbor the hotel has a really nice heated pool and hot tub you want to try out. We had a double suite with a separate sitting area. The beds were really comfortable. Take along some flip flops because the carpet wasn't the best. The room smelled a bit from it. The water in the tub dripped all day and night. It was annoying. They maid service came to make the beds and bring clean towels, but they left any dishes or food on that you may have had from the day before. I ate some cereal in the room and the bowl and juice glasses stayed in the room for 2 days. Can use some upgrading.But other than that it was a pleasant stay.

title: “disappointing restaurant”
text:
The Carlyle retaurant is hailed as one of the last bastions of traditional haute cuisine.Whilst there were small glimpses of good food the overall experience is mediocre at best.The beef wellington was excellent but my daughters lamb was overcooked and indeed dried out.The creme brulee was not caramalised but burnt.The vegetables were soggy.
A dining experience is not just the food and this is were The Carlyle restaurant really fails-the staff were mostly snooty and reserved and we felt unwelcome from the moment we arrived starting with an unobserved/unacknowledged wait at the Maitre`d s plinth.
Save your money-there are far better restaurants in New York City.

title: “Clean but very dated”
text: Upon arrival we were disappointed that the hotel looked and felt very dated. Arrived via the monorail at about 8pm. Neighborhood did not seem very safe, streets were not well lit. In the morning it seemed better. Staff was very nice, breakfast room did not have enough seating. Food quality was ok.

title: “Best Weekend Ever”
text: I just had the best weekend ever at the Harbor Court. It wasn't huge but the room had everything we needed. We went with the room with the view and loved it. Who knew the bridge could look so good? (I'll post a pic if I can get it off my phone). We slept with the windows and blinds open all night. I even caught a glimpse of the sunrise. We will definitely be back again.

title: “A bit tired”
text:
This hotel has great staff in the lobby - very helpful, friendly so let me say that first. The restaurant too - great service there, well priced.
The rooms are the issue here - tiny room with bad storage for clothing - had a wardrobe only with no dresser - no drawers for other stuff, desk was crammed in corner and couldn't have desk chair pulled out without running into bed. Am not picky about room size as understand city hotel rooms are small but maybe if functional choices were made in how the room was set up - wouldn't have had issue. 
Now the bad part, the bathroom had a used body lotion in it and when I threw it out, it was put back the next day - the same one?! that's a bit unsavory to say the least. Bedding was clean but towels in the bathroom were stained and while I don't need them replaced daily, got a new towel with a new stain instead of just leaving the one I was using? which was weird and a bit creepy. 
If they could freshen up the rooms and get a better housekeeping staff, the hotel would shine as they have such nice folks downstairs and it's a pretty good value for the money.

title: “The most amazing service - a fabulous little hotel!”
text:
We were blown away by the superb check-in service, complete with a lovely glass of wine, and all conducted while we were seated on a comfortable settee in the lobby -- no standing at a front desk! The hotel staff came to us, with an iPad in hand, and took care of everything, from check-in to making a dinner reservation for us. Unbelievable! The room was incredible, too, though we could have used more outlets for all our device chargers. The check-out service was just as easy and prompt and efficient. Again, we did not go to a desk, they walked up to us with an iPad in hand. Wow!
The neighborhood is filled with very nice restaurants, bars, etc, all within walking distance, but if you don't want to walk, they will take you and/or pick you up in their private luxury SUV.
We will make a point of staying here again, for sure. We travel extensively and this hotel was a wonderful surprise - extraordinary service and an all-round delight.

title: “Great location, great service”
text: We just enjoyed three nights at Hotel 71. Great location and service. My only complaint is that room doors tend to slam shut. At night one hears other people entering/leaving their rooms and the doors are loud. Ben and Mike, concierge service, were very helpful.

title: “Perfect location and accommodation”
text:
We are a family of 4 from West Midlands England. Just returned from 6 days in NYC. The trip was to celebrate our eldest son's 21st and we were joined by our 17 year old son. The Beekman more than matched our expectations. We had stayed in NYC on a previous visit in Times Square vicinity. Much preferred Beekman location. Quieter but with good restaurants within a few blocks. Yes there is no subway station close but it is only a 15 minute walk to Grand Central Terminal. Room very large, kitchen very welcome, particularly the fridge in height of summer. The UN diner opposite very good for breakfasts. Check in very prompt, good service and bellman so helpful on last day with luggage and transportation to airport etc.
Would definitely recommend the Beekman after this experience.

title: “Great budget stay.”
text:
Don't stay here if you are looking for a luxury stay in NYC, but if you are willing to cut some corners to save money, this place is wonderful. It seems like they took an apartment building and transformed it into an inn. The only issue we had was that the toilet broke the first night, but they had it fixed by the time we woke up the next morning. Sharing a bathroom with another room is not a big deal. When my mom and I stayed there, we never even saw the guy who shared it with us.
Rooms are smaller, but the beds are very comfortable. There is a sink in the room, so you only have to go out to use the bathroom and shower. You get a free breakfast by way of a coupon for a bagel or pastry and coffee or tea for the cafe right next door. You can either get up and showered early, or (like we did) just throw on a coat and go get your breakfast before getting ready for the day. We took our breakfast back up to the room and then got ready as we ate it.
The location is great. A very short walk to Union Square and two different subway stations that access most of, if not all, the major subways in Manhattan.
Very safe and fun to stay at. Highly recommend it!

title: “Quiet hotel on the edge of the Riverwalk”
text:
This small, boutique hotel is on the edge of the Riverwalk within walking distance of just about everything. We stayed two nights, using the Groupon for one of the nights. Our room was on the 4th floor, the same level as the pool. (The first two floors are the Parking Garage and the 3rd Floor is the Lobby and Restaurant.) The room was small, but well appointed. And we liked the private patio that opened up to the pool area. The King sized bed was very comfortable, and the lighting in the vanity area was good. We had a refrigerator, ironing board, hair dryer, makeup mirror and safe in the room. Free Wi-Fi was a nice surprise. My only disappointment about the room was the very old, grainy television set that only offered a handful of channels. That was not what I expected in a hotel like this. The walls are very thin and unfortunately, the ice machine was right outside our room. Each morning, I can only assume that other guests were filling up their ice chests. :-/ 
The service level provided was hit or miss. The front desk was completely professional, but lacked that "friendly, I'm so glad you're here, what can I do to make your stay enjoyable" quality. The first night we were there, we asked for a couple of wine glasses in our room to help us celebrate our wedding anniversary. Unfortunately, we were told that this was not allowed and were offered plastic champagne flutes with the removable bottoms. (We ended up using the glass tumblers in our room.) This was not a big deal, but it's the little things that set a hotel apart and make you look for reasons to come back. 
On a more positive note, the housekeeping staff is incredibly responsive. When we arrived back at our room at 4:30pm after being gone all day, our room had not been freshened up. I let one of the housekeeping staff know and within minutes, two of the staff were in our room while we were relaxing on our patio, and had our room completely done in 15 minutes. 
We had breakfast at the hotel restaurant on the last day. It was a special breakfast menu for Groupon coupon holders, and it was delicious. Service was polite, but distracted. 
Overall, my impression of this hotel is that they are trying very hard from the top down to become a 4 star boutique hotel. The biggest thing I see lacking is that the employees of the hotel have not bought in. They feel overworked and underpaid (remember, this is just my opinion). Employees need to be empowered and they also need to be recognized for exceptional customer service. The sweet young lady at the front desk should have been able to go to the restaurant and come back with two wine glasses, or better yet, sent them up to our room, no questions asked. 
At the end of the day, it was a quaint hotel, and I would go back, but I would make sure that I see my room before I sign for it.

title: “Great hotel”
text: very friendly staff, great located and clean rooms.

title: “Sheraton Los Angeles Harbor Hotel”
text: My husband and I stayed there for our wedding night 10/24/04, just a standard room since we were leaving the next morning to Catalina, we thought that since it had the Sheraton name it would be a nice place to stay, although the room was clean, it really needs updating, the bathroom was awful, it had missing hooks and above the sink you could see up through the ceiling, and it was dusty and dirty. I was asked how everything was at checkout and I told them I was sorely disappointed. I would not recommend this hotel or stay there again.

title: “Great location, clean well done rooms are awesome”
text: Clean, modern rooms are just the right size - the location is amazing for shopping and walks to the lake. The restaurant off the lobby is fantastic, expensive but nice. Bar off lobby is a great hotel bar.

title: “Nice Hotel with small deficits”
text: Ok price value for SF, spacious rooms with complimentary breakfast. Minus in location. Area around Hotel is not very nice. We got stopped by police and had been asked to use a different street. For walking to Union Square you need first to walk one block up before crossing over. Breakfast room was very crowded - not enough space. Only go there if you don't mind bus groups.

title: “Furniture looking a little worn”
text: I always love my stay at the Hotel Elysee, and have stayed there on my NY vacation for the past 5 years. I do have have to say the staff is always very pleasant and accomodating, but the furniture, in the lounge especially could use an update, it's looking a bit dingy and worn. Other that that, it's the absolute perfect location, and the breakfast is great. Only wish the champagne and snacks in the evening were on the weekend too!

title: “Great stay”
text: Excellent room service. Front desk was a little up tight but great rooms a bit on the higher end. But over all great stay.

title: “Nice Hotel... if you wanna stay awake all night”
text:
I just returned from a one night trip to Columbus. I opted to stay close to the airport because I had to catch an early flight. I was given room 121 upon check in. I noticed when entering my room that it was right next to the outside entrance and the stairwell. I didn't realize how much of an issue this was until I tried to fall asleep at 10pm. It literally sounded like a herd of elephants were about to crash through my wall ALL NIGHT. I called the front desk and was told the hotel was completely booked so there was not an option to change rooms. If I said I slept a full 3 hours- that would be a stretch. 
Upon checking out at 6:00 am I explained my frustration over lack of sleep. The front desk person said that they never get complaints (SHOCKING!) from anyone in that room over the stair noise and because I had pre paid for my reservation online, there was nothing she could do. She also stated that they had gotten numerous complaints the night before because there was a basketball team staying on that side of the hotel so that was probably the cause of a lot of noise. I don't think I ever heard an apology.
It's unfortunate because the hotel did seem very clean and probably would be a nice place to stay if I were perhaps on another floor. I am frustrated that I spent over $100 to stay here and probably could have had the same kind of sleep in my car.
Maybe Hilton needs to work on teaching their employees how to handle situations like this a little more satisfactorily.

title: “Good location, good staff and clean room.”
text: I stayed this hotel for two weeks on business and in great comfort. The hotel staff are very nice and always smiling. The room I stayed was very clean, spacious and has a great bed. Every morning I could get a free coffee so I drank it before I went to work everyday. That was nice. Also housekeepers were courtesy. The location was good, near a station and you can go to a supermarket which is opened 24 hours a day and 2 minute walk away. I would like to stay this hotel again when I come back to Boston.

title: “A great hotel with a very welcoming staff.”
text: We hadn't stayed here for a while, preferring other Starwood properties in NY. But we're so glad we picked the W on Lexington this time. The entire staff was so welcoming and responsive to all of our requests. Room service was quick, and reasonably priced too! The location was convenient to Broadway and Lincoln Center, as well as very nice East Side restaurants. Also, easy subway trip from Penn Station. My only suggestion would be that if you're going to stay there, request a high floor. We were on 6, and the traffic from Lexington Avenue was a bit much at 6:30 AM. Otherwise, a great hotel in NYC.

title: “Good”
text:
I really quite liked this hotel. It had a certain charm but don't ask me why. This hotel is ideally located in Union Square and is close to the main tram stop at the bottom of Powell Street. The bay area will take around 30 minutes to walk but trust me the queue for the trams are usually much longer.
I found the room very spacious and cleanliness of this hotel very good. For the price, I found it good value and had a pleasant stay.

title: “Checking out DC from a great Hotel”
text: Great hotel, great location and a great price equals a great trip. The staff were friendly and accomidating. The location was 200 yards from Metro. Area seemed really safe for families. I will be bringing my daughter back in the spring to visit DC for a week and this is where will stay. Rooms had space and all the stuff you need for a home base.

title: “Amazingly Awesome!”
text: This was by far the very best hotel I have stayed in! The service was outstanding....extremely accommodating and helpful in every way. The guys at the front desk were professional and adorable in every way! The location is so convenient and accessible to great restaurants and attractions! 5 stars!

title: “perfectly fine”
text: Maybe things vary from room to room but our room was fine, no there wasn't an extra area for a couch or a big screen tv, but how much time do you spend in the hotel? The bathroom was twice as big as the one in my apt. The room was cleaned everyday. The only complaint really is that you have to recharge your keycard about everyday. Near the T and park. If you're planning on walking the city and not spending hours in the room this is a great hotel for the price, you want pools and fold out couches go across the street.

title: “Convenient location, nicely appointed, friendly staff”
text:
We would definitely stay at the Abri again. Great location near the end of the Cable Car route, close to shopping and the BART station. 
Rooms were comfortable and the bathrooms were very nice. A proper roomy stand-up shower rather than standing in a tub!
Friendly staff, from the front desk to the maintenance personnel.

title: “Beautifully designed hotel”
text: This hotel has great location with beautifully designed rooms. Quiet considering downtown location. The Klimpton renovations in downtown Seattle are done with excellence. Our only regret is that we didn't stay longer!

title: “business trip”
text:
I stayed here for week. The rooms are great, the location is decent. However, ask for room that do not have windows to highway 270. Noise from there is really irritating, mainly during nights. 
Quality of breakfast is medium, European hotels do have much more lavish breakfasts.

title: “Six days in Boston!”
text: My husband and I recently stayed at the Harborside Inn and loved it! We had an interior room on the 6th floor that was spacious and very quiet. The bed was very comfortable,the water in the shower was always hot and all the extras worked as they should. The housekeeping staff was very friendly and helpful and kept the room spotlessly clean.The front desk staff was knowledgable about everything Boston and greeted us with smiles and a hello every time we passed by. The location was perfect and the entrance to the T was right outside the front door. Quincy Market,where you could spend hours having fun, was just a block away. An Irish pub,called The Black Rose,was directly across the street and served some of the best food we've ever had plus they had live entertainment...a really fun place to eat. We thoroughly enjoyed our visit and would recommend this hotel to everyone!

title: “4 nights at the Dolphin”
text:
We have visited SD twice before, staying at the Homewood Suites in Del Mar and Motel 6 respectively. This time we wanted to try a location in Point Loma for a number of good reasons. After considering several options (most of the Pt. Loma properties are clustered close together) we opted to try the Dolphin based mainly on price and TripAdvisor reviews. 
We drove in after dark on I-8 and turned onto Nimitz Ave. at the end of the freeway which brought us right to the Dolphin. Our reservation was accepted and we checked in without problem. Our room was on the second floor which was fine. On first impression we were a bit surprised at the compactness of the room which reminded me of some I had stayed in throughout the UK. Apart from that the room was clean to an acceptable standard and everything that was in it worked accordingly. The place has a kind of '70's feel to it which we have experienced at other SoCal accomodations!
We found that the Dolphin was a combination of several pluses and a couple of minuses. The pluses included being situated in Pt. Loma which is a self contained community with most amenities within easy walking distance of the Dolphin. There is a great selection of restaurants, C stores, laundromat, gas stations etc. nearby and the streets are safe to walk after dark. In many ways it resembles most large towns that you would find on the Great Plains with that same "Howdy neighbour" friendliness. Pt. Loma is also strategically located in SD to provide quick access to all of the local attractions. We found that having wi-fi was a great convenience as we packed the laptop along. Morning coffee,OJ, and muffins are served in the outdoor courtyard which is very nice on warm sunny mornings. As many other commenters have mentioned the staff and management are very nice folks.
The minuses were few and rather petty. The hotel doesn't have a pool (one is located beside the office but belongs to the neighbouring Comfort Inn.) The hotel advertises itself as being on a quiet street (Garrison) which is technically correct, however it is sandwiched between two very busy streets (Rosecrans and Scott). My wife likes to sleep with the windows open and the early morning traffic was very noticeable. The street traffic can be overcome by closing the windows and turning on the circulating fan. Another irritant was the vibrating roar of fighter jets taking off from North Island late in the evening. The snug rooms are fine for sleeping but don't expect to entertain guests.
Overall we were quite satisfied with our stay at the Dolphin and would recommend it to anyone planning a trip to San Diego.

title: “Great location to all”
text: Hotel has a great location near all the main attractions and only 15 minutes from the airport. Seems to be a big host of conventions so not for someone looking for a quite getaway. Rooms are in really nice shape and beds are comfortable. They charge for WiFi which is unfortunate.

title: “Not bad but watch out for the "cityview" promise”
text:
My main problem with this hotel was that although the Hilton site advertises "cityview" rooms there are NO CITYVIEW rooms at this hotel. I know because when I mentioned this to the front desk they were surprised.
Also, although I had booked my room months in advance, when I arrived my basic requirements for the room (only 2!) were both ignored which makes me think that those "notes" you're required to add to your booking are never read by the hotel staff when they allocate the room. 
I had asked for no vending machines / icecube makers outside my door (they make a lot of noise) but the room had one of these exactly outside my door. Also, although I had booked for a "cityview" room I was given one on the 8th floor; it was only when I complained that I got moved to the 18th floor...
Location wise this is nearly perfect as it's next to Penn Station (not many people know this for some reason but you can get an overland train from JFK to Penn Station in the middle of Manhattan: cheap, fast and enjoyable!). Y ou get the best of both worlds by staying at this hotel: proximity to downtown and theatre-land / uptown are both in walking distance. You save a lot on cabs as you can go out in Chelsea and the numerous bars on 8th and 9th avenues without needing to get a cab on return. Also, the whole area feels very safe at night. Only problem I found with going out is there's nowhere to eat nearby late at night!! :)
The rooms are very small, yes.
I can't comment on the free breakfast as it's served way too early for me and there's no service to reserve anything.
Overall I had a fine time at the hotel and I would recommend it to budget travellers but if you're being charged more than $200 per room per night this isn't worth it.

title: “Great value”
text:
My cousin and I stayed here on a 3-night weekend trip to San Diego whilst holidaying in Los Angeles. 
We found the hotel to beclean, well-appointed and only a 10-15 minute drive to all attractions (we came mostly to visit the zoo).
Staff well-mannered and helpful.
The hotel had pleasant grounds - plenty of greenery, which is nice for a hotel on the outskirts of a city. 
Close to plenty of restaurants - always found somewhere good to eat.
Overall good value for money and adequate for a weekend stay/stopover to see San Diego. Would stay again in future.

title: “Really Good Experience”
text: The Fairfield Inn in Gallery Place/Chinatown is conveniently located near the metro, the Verizon center, and many great restaraunts. My wife and I stayed there recently for a concert at the Verizon center and were very pleased with the hotel and the staff. The rooms are comfortable and nicely appointed with name brand ammenities. The staff was accomodating and cheerful. The breakfast, although crowded, had a good selection of food items. The lobby always had cold water and snacks (We were there on a 104 degree weekend). The free wifi worked well and the attached restaraunt "The Irish Channel" seemed to have good daily drink specials and was popular in it's own right even with the local crowd. The gym was small but the equipment was all brand new and clean and suited my needs. All in all a very good experience. I would certainly recommend to anyone visiting the area.

title: “Good Hotel for the Price”
text:
I've always liked Doubletree Hotels because of the free cookies (and they are good cookies), but freebies aside, I was quite satisfied with my two-night stay in San Diego. The room was bigger than average and clean, the bed was a giant King with a pillowtop and 6 good pillows, and the bathroom (also clean) had the nice advantage of two sinks - one inside (a pedestal, no less) with the toilet and shower, and one outside. The decor was fairly contemporary (no hideous prints) and the art on the wall was actually okay. The whole look is more IKEA than Sears, for the most part. 
The downsides, which didn't bother me particularly, but need to be noted: the rooms are set up condo-style with 4 or so units to one building, and when the room next to ours had the shower on, we could hear the water rushing through the pipes pretty loudly. The small balcony overlooking a lawn was nice, but hadn't been swept in a while and had not a single chair. The sliding screen door was off its hinges. Also, a few bugs seemed to be able to find their way into the room, which I chalked up to the hotel being on a golf course and the fact that it was unbelievably hot the weekend we were there. Not a problem for me, but if you're not a bug person...
So that was our stay. Mostly pretty good. Friendly staff, no problems checking in or out. For the price, I think it's a pretty good deal. And --, those cookies were good.
note: We didn't eat at any of the restaurants on site, but there is a Starbucks just down the street in the Albertsons supermarket to get your morning coffee.

title: “Very Good Hotel, Excellent Location”
text: The Moore is not fancy, but is very functional. The location is great, the rooms clean, the staff very helpful, and the rooms are large. We had no problem with the location and the homeless--no worse than the rest of Seattle. It is within easy walking distance of almost all tourist attractions. And--it has 100 year old character. It's not some sterile, cookie cutter hotel.

title: “Maitland Mom”
text: We took our kids here for a family vacation. It is conveniently located and nicely landscaped. Loved being on the Bay and having access to jet skis, boats, kayaks and paddle boards. The food was good and the pools were nice. The only problem we had was our room was not ready at check in. We finally got into our room after 6:00 p.m. My son also left his sweatshirt on the bed and it was not turned in.

title: “Convenient location”
text: Easy access to lots of dining and shopping, easy checkout service.

title: “Awesome experience!”
text: This was the perfect hotel for our family trip to DC. Subway access in building. Convenient shopping. Breakfast buffet was great, and the free managers reception in the evening--complete with board games for the kids--was an added bonus. Pool was great for kids. Rooms clean and comfortable. Would definitely stay again.

title: “Amazing service”
text: Wonderful service from the staff at the W. Their approach to every request was impeccably polite and friendly.The hotel itself was absolutely fine - clean and smart. The beds are exceptionally comfortable and for those who like to sing in the showers the acoustics are of opera house standard. The free morning coffee in the lobby was of a strength to suit European palates and was the best I had in the four days I was in the city. Because of its location there are a lot of security people floating around, but they are not too obtrusive. WiFi is pretty expensive in the room, but there is a free service in the lobby. This is the only hotel I'll be using in DC in future.

title: “Great location, sophisticated and great breakfast diner”
text:
I thought this hotel was great. 
Its a big art deco style hotel with impressive reception hall and express lifts to floors 20 and beyond. We were on the 20th floor and while we didn't have much of a view it was a very good price for New York and we had 2 rooms (single rooms) I went with my Mother.
These rooms had a fairly large queen size bed I would say and nice touches like the art deco lights, furniture and bathroom fixtures. Also had nice HD plasma tv's and alarm clocks and nice sheets and duvet.
Location was great - I could see the 34th St Penn Station subway from my room, directly under us and this station served the A, C and E line train (all of which take you right out to near the airport and the airtrain for JFK airport)
A block away is another Penn St station subway which serves the 1,2 and 3 lines - taking you to the Staten Island Ferry, Times Square and West side of Central Park.
But you don't need a subway to walk to Times Square from here... its only a 10 minute walk and the Empire State building is only a 10 minute walk also. If you were going to Madison Square gardens for an event this would probably be the best hotel for you as it is just across the road. 
New York is quite noisy with sirens and hooting but the air con was great and the windows were closed and by later in the evening the traffic had died down and I didn't get disturbed by the noise while sleeping.
The hotel has a diner attached called the Tick Tock diner which is 24 hours and serve the greatest breakfasts! massive portions and although I have seen people complaining that they were expensive I didn't really think that was the case - compared to other places in New York.. New York is just expensive to eat I think. 
Hotel staff were okay - nothing special, they checked us in and checked us out with minmal effort but they were busy and the security staff by the lifts were friendly. 
All in all for the price I paid for 2 rooms I wouldn't have got the price of 1 room in some hotels so I was satisfied with what I paid and the standard of this hotel and location. 
I plan on going back to NY with my husband and would have no hesitation in going back to the New Yorker Hotel.

title: “Restaurant not open for dinner”
text:
Yes, that's what I said, so for dinner it is eat out or room service. The restaurant is open for breakfast. Not lunch either when I was there Feb 15-19 2012
The location is great, near Times Square, Empire State Building, good central location for 
shopping and site seeing. Room was clean and good size for NY. 
Just hard to give it more than three stars when after a 18 hour flight, just don't want to start
searching for a place to eat just want to sit and relax. Concierge was helpful when asked for information. I would recommend the hotel in spite of three stars.

title: “One block from 16th street”
text: This hotel is a very nice hotel with attention to detail. I stayed on the 30th floor and had to take a special elevator (second set of elevators) to get to my room. The lobby is huge, with lots of seating. The room is spacious with a flat screen tv, work station, and chair. Granite counter tops in the bathroom with plenty of room to spread out. You have to pay for internet even in the business center. Which was very expensive. When you are on business travel, internet is a must. You can print your boarding pass. The gym was available 24 hours and has the nicest gym that I have seen. You can walk to plenty of places to eat from this hotel.

title: “Very nice Hotel for the Money with Superb STAFF”
text:
I never write Reviews; this is my first. The Hotel represents excellent Value For Money and is a short walk to SOHO, Little Italy and Chinatown.
Room was not huge but clean, quiet and plenty comfortable.
The STAFF were superb, both at Check-in and in Housekeeping. I forgot an article in my room and checked out. Housekeeping retrieved it and returned it to me. GREAT JOB!

title: “Excellent hotel and superb staff!!!”
text:
The hotel is beautiful but the staff is really what makes this hotel so special. They are all so wonderful and really truly there to make your stay memorable. 
We came to celebrate our anniversary and we got an upgrade of a lifetime :) thank you for making our stay so special - we are truly grateful.

title: “A perfect choice for the right traveller”
text:
Pros:
1. Literally the front door is 30 feet from a BART and Muni station. Very convenient for getting around the city. 
2. While the room and bathroom are smaller than average, there were high ceilings, the decor was classy and the room was very clean.
3. Very possibly the most comfortable hotel bed I have ever slept in. My companion agreed.
4. Friendly front desk staff.
5. Surprisingly good water flow in shower--hot long showers are possible!
Cons:
1. Sketchy neighborhood at night. I can handle myself but one block off Market around 10pm on a Saturday night and I was regretting that choice. But hop on the muni and for 2 bucks you'll be fine.
2. Sometimes a bit loud. Partly due to loud people on my floor, but even on the 7th floor some of the street noise was a bother. But hey, you're in a big city--to be expected.

title: “Nice hotel, great price!”
text: We stayed at the Carl while we visited a friend just a short walk away. We had the largest room available but it was very reasonable at $115. We started out in a smaller room and asked to be moved. The staff was very accommodating and even moved our luggage to the new room while we were out. The room was spacious and clean and the refrigerator and microwave were very handy. The train was noisy but we got used to it. The location is terrific with shops and restaurants nearby and we (two women) felt completely comfortable walking around the neighborhood. I would definitely stay again, you can't beat the price for a nice, clean room in a big city.

title: “THE BEST HOLIDAY EVER IN THE WORLD!!!!!!”
text:
the best western hotel is a good hotel cause when i was away me and my family were just a couple of minutes from a good place for macys parade.
the hotel is good the staff are nice and the staff at reception are very helpful and it would be good if they had a food bit were u got food. 
the room i was in u could see a little of time square and u dont get a good sleep but apart from that thats it.
AND A BIG THANKS TO THE BAG PERSON HE WAS SO HELPFUL TO LOAD OF PEOPLE THANKS YOUR THE BEST...

title: “stay”
text: Lobby, hallways, elevator very dirty. Mattress was poor quality, along with the bedding. TV remore did not work, heating unit very loud

title: “Great stay!”
text: I arrived on an early morning flight many hours before check in. The staff was pleasant and allowed me to check in early with no problems, which I greatly appreciated. The room was small but clean, quiet and really well appointed. The bed was super comfortable. The hotel is centrally located with a lot of good places to eat nearby. I will certainly return soon.

title: “Overall very nice hotel”
text: Stayed at the Hyatt Regency Denver Convention Center for 2 days on business. Overall I have to say I was very impressed with almost everything about this hotel. All of the staff were professional and helpful. Room service was very prompt and food was great. Room was clean and I had a beautiful view of the mountains (snow covered from recent storm). This hotel is directly across the street from the Convention Center which was my destination each day and was extremely convenient. The only negative was that I could hear the people in the next room talking and coughing so that wasn't desirable. I'm thankful that's all I heard! I would certainly stay here again. They have a wonderful lounge on the 27th floor where you can watch the sunset over the mountains.

title: “A gem in downtown DC”
text: I stayed at the Morrison-Clark while attending a conference held at the convention center and nearby large hotels. The Morrison-Clark was a delight: quaint public areas but thoroughly modern amenities, and perfect location (4 short blocks to the metro, 2 blocks to convention center, an easy walk to White House and other tourist destinations). The staff were uniformly warm, helpful and courteous. My room was the smallest in the place, according to the emergency exit floor plan, but just fine for one person and very comfortably appointed for both getting some work done and relaxing afterward. Bedding was luxurious; room service was prompt and not outrageously priced (by room service standards, anyhow). Some initial connecctivity problems were resolved quickly and very courteously. One small "minus" is the neighborhood: some extensive rehabbing/construction going on, some weekend party noise ouside my window, and things gets a little dicey as you head north. But did not feel unsafe, and a small price to pay for a delightly stay. I highly recommend the Morrison Clark, and will return there.

title: “Beautiful hotel, but ridiculously loud!”
text: This hotel is gorgeous, no doubt about it. Very nice staff, very clean hotel. However, it is so loud. I am a deep sleeper and I was up half the night - you can hear the elevator, people walking, talking, etc. It wasn't just my room - friends on other floors shared the same experience.

title: “Exceptional Service!”
text: After two delayed flights and an exhausting day, I arrived late to check-in at the Westin, Detroit Airport. I'm guessing because of my tardiness, and that most other reservations had already checked in, however, the young lady at the desk, CALLED ME BY NAME as she welcomed me to the hotel. Wow! It's amazing what that small gesture can do to turn around what was previously a horrible day! She checked me in, upgraded me to a room on their "keyed" 8th floor where it would be less noisy, informed me about their 24 hour room service and quickly directed me to my room. I ordered soup (which was delicious and was delivered very quickly) and sunk into the incredible bed for a wonderful night's sleep. This was my first stay at this Westin, but I guarantee it will not be my last. AMAZING - FIVE STARS *****!!!!! Thank you for making my stay the BEST!

title: “Great value for a great suite hotel”
text:
I checked with Residence Inn, Springwood Suites and Homewood Suites before deciding on Bradford Homesuites, based on a (much-) cheaper rate as well as the TripAdvisor recommendations.
We stayed at the Austin location from Aug. 19-27 at US$99/nt, with practically no complaints (on prior visits we generally stayed at the 4* downtown Hilton, but a new child is changing our lives in that and many other ways). The facilities were fine, not old as other reviewers have mentioned. Our one-bedroom deluxe suite was very clean and well-equipped, and the service we received from the staff was excellent. 
I liked that most guest services were fairly priced (free local calls and wired Internet access, cheap snacks and items from the Bradford Market ministore), although we found the breakfast rather sparse (basically we had instant oatmeal and hard-boiled eggs two days, and then decided to go up the street to the Whole Foods for a quick breakfast). The crib supplied by the hotel was small and made of metal, and our baby kept getting his leg caught between the bars, but it worked out ok. Curtains were awesome, allowing us to sleep in as they kept out all of the light. Although the hotel says that cleaning only takes place once or twice a week, we found our room tidied and the bed made every day of our stay, which was a nice surprise.
The hotel is well located, practically on the corner of Capital of Texas Highway and MOPAC, allowing easy access to US183 as well. There are many stores located in the vicinity, as well as the Whole Foods mentioned above. The Arboretum mall is a couple of blocks away.
We will definitely stay there again, as this was a very pleasant and economical surprise.

title: “Great little find for the solo traveler on a budget”
text:
I'm on my 4th night staying in NY on business as I write this, in a double room with private bath. 
All in all the Pod is terrific for my needs and a fairly pleasant, especially given the low price. 
Positives: 
* Great midtown location. 
* Intelligent, functional room design in a small space. 
* Stylish in an "IKEA meets Amtrak sleeper cabin" sort of way
* Very clean.
* Nice rooftop for hanging around.
* Good Internet connectivity (free in-room wifi!) 
* Friendly and efficient staff
* Little street noise (at least in my room) 
Minuses: (all minor) 
* Smaller than usual rooms: "double room" probably only works for two people if they're REALLY into each other.
* wifi a little pokey at times
* low-price comes with a few missing amenities such as an in-room refrigerator and an ice-machine in the hotel
* flatscreen TV doesn't swivel, and doesn't directly face bed
* The noisy neighbors who checked in yesterday

title: “holliday”
text: I was stayed in this hotel for the second time. It's in a good location, to visit the city. The staff were so friendly and helpfull. The parking was near and cheap. Breakfast in the morning was so good . The room was very clean. Excellent.

title: “Nice hotel with a great location”
text: My friend and I were there for an event at Civic Center Park, so the location of this hotel was awesome. The room was nice, and I appreciated that I could open the windows. The fireplace was a nice touch. The bed was comfortable enough. We were surprised that breakfast was over so early on a weekday, consequently, we didn't get to partake. Also the evening reception was a little lacking. But the cookies between 8p-10p were a wonderful and tasty treat. All in all, I'd stay there again - if only for the location 1/2 block off 16th Street Mall.

title: “It worked for us!”
text: Stayed in the Mayfair room recently. The rooms were very clean and it was like having our own small apt. A short walk to the zoo. Food is close by. The whole place is really not a true hotel but rather like your grandmothers well-kept, but old apartment with all it's quirky furniture and decor collected over a lifetime. Everything is old but well maintained and perfectly functional. The breakfasts are cut up fresh fruit along with generic grocery store danish/pastries warmed up in a microwave. But it does the trick and saves the hastle of going out for breakfast. If you can get over the fact that this is not a cookie cutter hotel you will enjoy the uniqueness (and value) of the experience.

title: “Second Time and Still Very Good”
text: The bathrooms and rooms in this hotel are much larger than one would expect. Very Clean and good bathroom amenities. This is comparable to a large hotel in terms of room/mattress quality. Its a bit of a walk to the financial district, but close to SF City Center and Union Square. At the rates I've seen, I would stay here every time for business and hop on Powell BART back to Montgomery or Embarcadero. Its a great location for a night out in the City without breaking the bank.

title: “Cool, causal, and comfortable”
text: My wife and I celebrated her 70 birthday spending a week at the James and at no point did either of us regret it. Close to all the major subways, terrific SOHO restaurants and neighborhood buzz. The James' staff are the friendly, personable type we've come to expect from a boutique hotel. They really do seem to have genuine smiles and offers to help. Morning coffee in the lobby, evening wine and cheese, and bedtime cookies give this modern high design hotel a home-like quality. Last but not least: one of the most comfortable hotel beds ever and definitely the best pillows! Wow!

title: “Classy hotel for it's location”
text: I normally don't expect great hotels by airports, but I found that the Westin is convenient, nicely appointed and has friendly and helpful staff. When you need accessibility to the airport, it's close enough but not right on top of it so there's no noise. I would recommend it highly. On my last stay, I was in the lobby at the computer terminals, printing out my boarding pass. I didn't think anyone was around, but I sneezed; within 2 seconds, a staff member handed me a kleenex. Happenstance, probably. But impressive just the same.

title: “Wonderful facility for meetings!”
text: We just had our Board meetings at La Quinta. We had 16 rooms and we had a wonderful experience there. It was a very good price for the quality of the rooms. The food at the breakfast buffet and the catering for lunch and the snacks for breaks was good and very well presented. Luis and Angel were very helpful and took good care of us. The friendly staff at the front desk (Frankie, Alex and Elizabeth) were a great help to each of our Board members. This is a great hotel. Great option for meetings and for travelers who want an affordable good hotel close to the airport.

title: “Loved this Hotel!”
text: We stayed at this hotel for three nights to see the sights of Boston for the first time before heading up to Maine for a family vacation. Everything at this hotel was great and the service was top notch. As soon as we were shown to our room, a staff member knocked on our door ten minutes later and delivered milk and chocolate chip cookies for my two children. They received this treat everyday of our stay. Our room was immaculate with plush towels, bathrobes and slippers. At turndown we received bottles of Fiji water on the nightstand. We also had a great view of the Wharf. The location of the hotel was perfect for us. Since it is located right on Rowes Wharf, it's within walking distance to Quincy Market, Feneuil Hall and the North End. After a long day of touring Boston in the rain, we were too tired to venture out again for dinner, so we decided to eat in the hotel at the Rowes Wharf Sea Grill restaurant. I'm always skeptical of hotel food, however we had one of the best meals of our entire trip at this restaurant. Our initial plans were to stay at the Four Seasons Boston, however after unsuccessfully trying to book a room online for the four of us (they only allow three to a room) we decided to stay here and am very happy we did! We will definitely be back to stay here next time we are in Boston.

title: “Very Nice Hotel - spacious, clean, free breakfast, free fast internet”
text:
I stayed at this hotel June 27th and 28th of 2008 with family and had a very pleasant experience. I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone going to San Diego including my extended family and friends and look forward to returning to it in a few months. The staff was friendly, accomodating, and very helpful. This hotel is in a very nice newer area of San Diego off of Mira Mar and 15 min from Seaworld and 20 min from the gas lamp district. Nice location. The building itself is new with a beautiful entry way (stone faced fireplace) and complimentary drinks.
The rooms were spacious, very clean, with fully stocked kitchens (except an oven but that is ok) The beds are really comfortable, it reminded me of the Hyatt, Westin or Doubletree beds. The sofa bed was pretty uncomfortable as the mattress is extremely thin and small - without much cushion...however I informed the front desk and they brought up 2 mattress pads right away....I was impressed as I didn't even have to ask for it. When I made the reservation I informed the front desk staff and reservation that I intended on using the sofa bed for my niece and nephew and the sofa bed was pulled out and ready to be slept on when I went to the room...it was very nice.
The pool is clean and the hotel is in a great neighborhood. The breakfast was amazing...I travel alot and have been to many Staybridge Suites and other very nice hotels however this one in particular had the largest selection of breakfast items I've seen.....it was better than the Residence Inn Marriotts.
For breakfast they served scrambled eggs, pancakes, waffles, hardboiled eggs, fresh fruit including peaches, strawberries, cottage cheese, sausage, bacon, ham slices, cereals, oatmeals, biscuits and gravy and apple strudels, muffins, all different kids of juices and more. The staff were very attentive and would always refill food quickly.
Overall, the staff and hotel itself exceeded my expectation by far.
I would recommend it - Absolsolutely.

title: “Great hotel, NYC”
text:
A lovely hotel, excellent location for central park, natural history museum. midtown was within walking distance (1 mile). Gave a more natural impression of NY being near to residential district, saw SJP out for a stroll one evening!
Only faults were a chip in the enamel of the bath, hairline crack in sink, dusty ipod docking station. Thats being picky, 2 double beds in room, excellent furnishings and decor, friendly staff, shower was excellent!
Can't wait to go there again.

title: “Boutique Hotel in a Great Location”
text: So me and hubby enjoyed 3 nights here with my brother and sister-in-law. We booked the reservations online, and never having been there, we were curious and hopeful that we made the right decision for our needs. First of all, when we got off at Grand Central Station, the hotel was close enough to walk! A nice perk that started the weekend off on the right foot. The rooms were clean, comfortable and the smallish space (compared to other hotels we've stayed at), was extremely functional and well thought out. We were disappointed there wasn't a refrigerator, and the maid brought back some towels that were stained. The hotel offered car service, which we took advantage of. We ate breakfast there one morning, that was very good. And after a long day of sightseeing/dining, when we returned to the hotel, we enjoyed drinks in their bar. The staff couldn't have been nicer or accomodating. The lobby was always lively! All in all, I would definitely recommend staying here. Reasonably priced for the location, too - short walk to Times Square and Rockefeller Plaza.

title: “Plaza - Don't think so!”
text:
We booked to stay in the Boston Park "Plaza" hotel for a short trip thru expedia. Expedia rates it as a 4 **** hotel and says it is one of the best hotels in the back bay area!
We arrived Friday evening to be told that the double room we requested could not be given to us as they had run out of rooms! Instead myself and my Father had to share a king room, and they promised they would send up a rollaway bed (which never arrived). We got into the room, and although it had obviously had some money spent on it, still needed work. The paint was coming off the walls and the bathroom was awful. We stayed in there for the night and the following morning requested to be moved.
At 3pm we moved into a double room on the 7th floor which had a good view and was generally a better room. We were watching TV that evening when we observed something run across the floor - it was a mouse in the room! Needless to say we got moved immediatley and got our money back for that nights stay!
We moved into another room on the same floor and the room was OK but after all the things that had gone wrong we just wanted out of there! We checked our bill thru the TV system to see that we had been charged $40 for a breakfast we never had! We told the front desk and they argued with us, saying if it was on the bill we had it and would have to pay for it! After speaking to the Duty Manager we got it refunded!
Genreally, the foyer is nice but the hotel needs complete overhaul, in fact it needs to be ripped down and a new building put in its place! The bathrooms are awful and the staff unhelpful and do not apologise when things go wrong.
Stay somewhere else!

title: “Very Nice and Contemporary”
text: The Hotel was very new and the people who work there are extremely nice! It is out of all the chaos of time square and in my opinion the best food in new york was Greenwich Village/SoHo. The Hotel was perfectly nestled in a quiet part of SoHo. The hotel was very small only about 6 rooms per floor. It did not have a pool but did have a small fitness center that has everything to keep up with your workout routine. There was no resturant just a bar with over priced snacks but not even the a block away has bleecher street which has the best pizza in new york. So food should not be an issue. The last thing is that the hotel is one of the cleanest I have ever been in and each room comes with a large TV , and free wifi as well a desktop computers in the lobby. This hotel was by far worth the money and stay i highly recomend it.

title: “Great name, good enough hotel”
text:
This is a good hotel in a good location (15-minute walk from Union Square, and about 20-25 from Grace Cathedral). The Hitchcock connections are everywhere, from the loops of "Vertigo" and "Rear Window" to the thank-you note from Kim Novak in the lobby. The front desk staff can tell you where the main landmarks, buildings, and streets in "Vertigo" are.
Since I was only going to be in the city for a few days and wasn't planning to spend much time in the room, I reserved one that hadn't been refurbished. There was no fridge or microwave (which might matter if you like to bring food back from restaurants), and the fan in the bathroom was really loud--loud enough to drown out the television or radio in the bedroom. If I had been sharing the room, this would have been very annoying. I ended up not turning on the bathroom light if at all possible. The bathroom fixtures had seen better days (I couldn't get the faucet in the tub to stop dripping, but the housekeeper could), and there were old stains on the rug, but in an old hotel these things are to be expected. The linens and towels were spotless, the bed was firm and comfortable, and I don't have any complaints about the housekeeping service or the front desk staff; there wasn't a question about the hotel or the city that they couldn't answer. In the morning, tea and coffee were available in the lobby. The restaurant that is advertised on the hotel web site isn't open yet, but there are plenty of restaurants, internet coffee shops, convenience stores and bars up and down Sutter Street, so there is no reason to go hungry. I didn't use the hotel wi-fi; I had mobile broadband, but the connection could be iffy. If I had planned to spend hours online, or wanted to stream video or download large files, this could have been a problem, but for checking email once a day, it was okay. I will be interested in seeing how the rooms in the Vertigo looks once the renovations are complete.

title: “Time for upgrades & renovations”
text: Light was out in the bathroom upon arrival. Bathroom was SO small you practically had to climb on the toilet to get the door closed Bed was softer than anything I've EVER slept on. STRONG fragrance throughout hotel. TINY pool. No hot tub. Lobby was impressive and included pool and foosball tables. It seems that all the 2007 renovations were put into the lobby only. Good thing I got a phenomenal room rate!

title: “Great location, great views”
text: We stayed in a nice very large room with fabulous views of Central Park (for those with a room on the other side or lower down the view is also to be had from the top floor where the pool is, as well as a great 360° terrace). The location is obviously terrific - a couple of blocks from the Park, close to shopping and theaters, lots of public transportation nearby. Service was very attentive (and had to be because a number of things you would normally expect were missing from our room when we checked in). The breakfast place on the ground floor ("Norma's") is great; very crowded on weekends (make a reservation!). Minor criticisms: the furniture could do with an upgrade and the airconditioning controls were not working properly (we wound up putting newspapers over the vents to keep from freezing).

title: “Interstate Traveler's Ideal”
text:
Chic decor, all new, spotless. Good wi-fi in room. Super comfy bed and pillows. All utilities work well. Microwave and fridge in room. Only suggested improvement: bathroom lighting was a little dim in my room. Water was off for two hours mid-day for some plumbing service. Warning was posted. Breakfast bar was loaded with fresh healthy stuff to sticky, yummy fattening stuff. I liked the long window of 6 to 10 a.m.
Location is south of downtown, just off I65. I paid around $90.

title: “Nice suites, well-kept grounds”
text:
I helped run a seminar here and stayed for two nights. I enjoyed having a suite and found the room to be very comfortable. The decor was definitely a southwest theme which is only charming in Phoenix! The grounds were very lovely and it felt like a nice resort. I appreciated the feeling of relaxation even though I was working for much of my time there. 
The main issue we had is that my coworker and I were literally on other sides of the hotel because she was upgraded to some kind of deluxe suite. Her room was incredible, and it had a nice conference table, but I had to lug a bunch of boxes, a laptop, and other items back and forth. They were bustling because of another conference, but I feel like they could have gotten us two rooms slightly closer together. The catering and event staff on the other hand were extremely attentive. The manager was easily accessible, checked in with us often, and made sure everything was perfect. 
I'd happily recommend for a short family or couple getaway or business event.

title: “pretty bad”
text:
Only good thing about this hotel is the metro station across the street. The rooms desperately need updating, the wifi is TERRIBLE as is the tv. The bathroom was a decent size but the shower barely produced any water, with the water spraying everywhere in different directions.
There is next to nothing in this area and most of the people around seem dodgy, we only went out once at night and did not feel safe.
If you're coming to LA thinking its a glamorous place this area/hotel will definitely set you straight!
Pretty sure you could get somewhere better for the same price as it wasnt exactly cheap.
The staff were friendly and helpful, but i wouldn't stay here again.

title: “Great Hotel, Despite all the Negative Reviews”
text: I first have to say this is my second time staying at this hotel. The first time, they were going through renovations and making updates, so I was looking forward to seeing what they had done. Checking in was a breeze, and unloading was easy, with staff ready to greet you and help in anyway. We got to our rooms, great, a nice view of the Quaker Meeting house. Everything was close by, considering we were there for a dance convention, close by, we could have walked but with all our costumes, etc. that was out of the question. One thing that really stood out with our stay was one of our team members got a "bit" lost, to say the least. I found a staff member, and asked him for a city street map, he got me 1 better, James, the head of the security at the hotel. He gave me directions from where my friends were, the missed the exit, and was lost again. James said, if I needed him again, to request him and he would be happy to assist. He came out again, and stayed with me, patiently I may add, and we got my friends there. I joked with him, saying she would probably greet him with a hug, and well, when she got there, he found me and asked did your friends get here, they did, and I was right he was graciously thanked and hugged. That to me went above and beyond customer service. They could have given me a street map, walked away, and that was it. They really went out of their way, and it was GREATLY appreciated

title: “Outstanding value”
text: This place was extremely clean and the staff was very friendly and well-informed. The room was immaculate and internet access was free in my room. Enjoyed relaxing by the beautiful pool and jacuzzi. Plenty of parking (though it does cost $14 per night) and superb location with easy freeway access. Ask for a high floor so you can enjoy the view of Mission Valley. Rate was a little over $100 pe night which is outstanding for a hotel of this quality in San Diego.

title: “Great location but not perfect hotel”
text:
Stayed here for a week after Xmas on Marriott points. Atrium style hotel with rooms circling lobby/bar/reception area. Slightly disappointed with room - felt a bit dowdy and a lot of noise from neighbouring room - could hear full conversations. Great bathroom - very big and well equipped and well stocked with towels and toiletries. View into neighbouring office and quite dark. Also expected small tv in bathroom - thought I read this in a review but not there. Entrance to lifts weren't in view of reception staff and lifts weren't manned so anyone could walk in off street and get into lifts and potentially up to rooms. I thought there should be a keycard system to get lifts up to room floors.
Fab location so can walk to loads of shops/restaurants. We also walked to Fishermans Wharf - abour 30 mins. Handy for cable car. Easy walk to Market St for tram. A few doors from a great little theatre -Post St where we were able to see Dame Edna.
Only had happy hour cocktail in bar as quite expensive. Concierge very helpful. Ice delivered very quickly to room. 
Our safe didn't work on arrival and we reported this but when we came back from a walk it was still unfixed - this was a pain as we were having to carry all our credit cards and passports. Phoned again and were told that we had to be in the room for it to be fixed - this was not specified the first time. By this time we were due to go to 49ers game and had worked out how and when to get bus from Union Square. Really didn't want to carry our valuables so asked if we could use a safe at reception. When we got there the receptionists were dead slow and stop -only one person with each but we waited 45 minutes during which time a huge queue built up behind us to check in. Eventually we got sorted - very slowly. I ended up waiting behind reception while someone tried to find safe keys and worked out how to work it. We were missing valuable time at the game and I was fuming...wrote a note to the head receptionist as she served someone else saying how disappointed I was with this debacle. On return from game expected an apology or something in the room but nothing. On check out got an apology then very strangely about a week later got an e-mail apologising profusely and offering the refund of the Marriott points for one night of our stay. Better than nothing but a quicker apology would have left a better taste!
Not the best Marriott I have stayed in and if I had paid full rate I would have been somewhat disappointed.

title: “Very good value”
text: First trip to NYC in years. This hotel made the trip. Very good value. Excellent location with good transport links. Free wifi. Will def stay here again.

title: “Wonderful Stay at the Magic Castle”
text:
My boyfriend and I stayed two nights at the Magic Castle. Upon meeting the staff we knew we had a winner... they were very friendly. We were delighted to find out that we were upgraded to a suite at no extra charge. The pool was gorgeous, and we were offered help with our luggage but turned it down. We got up to our room and were amazed to find an entire kitchen and more than enough space for two early 20-year olds. We felt like we really were being treated to Hollywood glamour! 
The staff continued to be helpful for our whole stay. We even got a ride up to Yamashiro for dinner our second night. The free mini bar items were awesome, the breakfasts were good, and we were never bothered by any housekeepers.
The bathroom was a little dodgy, though. The only shelf was on a slant and couldn't be used, and there was mold around the tub. That wasn't enough to spoil our stay, though. And the price was definitely worth it!
Besides the beautiful pool and great staff, the best thing about this hotel is the great location. Steps away from Grauman's Chinese Theatre and Kodak Theatre. 
We will definitely be back!

title: “Convenient location and attractive rooms, but uncomfortable surrounding area”
text: This was a funny hotel. Very pretentious and "beautiful people" in the lobby bar...we felt underdressed and uncomfortable. The rooms were very nice, although they were unable to give us a room with two beds for our teenagers. We only ate at the restaurant for breakfast and service was so-so. One server took our orders without writing them down and I smiled and asked if she got all that...she said yes, then messed up my order! The Wheels car service provided by Acura was very helpful, and the valet staff was pleasant and welcoming. The desk staff seemed cold and not very welcoming. The location was convenient when driving, but not for walking. The courthouse was not far and the hotel is surrounded by the Sheriff's intake location and bail bondsmen. My daughter and I walked back to the hotel from the Gaslamp District and did not feel very comfortable. I would try somewhere else the next time we go to San Diego.

title: “Good location and hotel but not a 4 star hotel...”
text:
I booked a grand club room at he Manchester.
We were given first a king room with a very stuffy/smelly carpet and far from the club (level 22) where you have to o back to ground level, change lift and go back o level 32! After complaining on the smell, they easily changed us room but give us only a disable access one because they had nothing else...despite me reserving 5 months ! This room was fine anyway, so we stayed in this one. However we booked grand club and you have to know that the room is nothing special: just a standard room giving access to a club. Generally the club was "okay". We booked club following our experience at the hyatt grand cypress in Orlando... In San Diego the grand club standard was lower than in Orlando (no hot food served neither on breakfast nor evening). 
The soaps provided don't have a pleasant smell...so bring yours! The bed sheet didn't fit the king size bed, so we kept waking up on the mattress!
Generally disappointing standard.

title: “Cockroaches, Toenails, & Dirty Rooms”
text:
We stayed at this Hotel (glorified motel) for 3 nights July 9th,10,11, 2009. this was the dirtiest hotel I have ever stayed. The pictures on the website are decieving. They lobby is very nice, as is the Bar / Patio & restaurant area. ...but the rooms are not vaccumed, there was toenails & dental floss found on the floor when we checked in. Their are tags still on furniture that was bought at collections etc. Paint was spattered on the door jams from a lack of masking. Furniture was dinged up and dirty. AND....to top it all of i had a COCKROACH run across my floor & into the bathroom, where I had to squash it. I called down to the lobby only for them to say it was most likely a water bug. I had to request twice for it to be cleaned up, then was told it was a COCKROACH. I asked for some money off of my room for all this trouble & being so dirty. I was told they could not do that since I booked & pre paid with expedia. All in all I give this room 1 out of 5. 
My sister and brother in law stayed the same nights in a different room, the room was just as dirty (no cockroach) but they had the extra bonus of not having the A/C work in the room. DO NOT STAY HERE!!!! Look for some place else that is nicer for the same price!

title: “Very nice place”
text: I'm a travel agent. My wife and I stayed here in July, 2002. It's a great hotel. We would stay there again. We found a decent rate - $129 - shopping around and considered it a bargain. We asked for a nice view, but because there are so many tall buildings around this hotel, that's difficult. You have to be on a really high floor or faced a certain direction. In our case, we faced the Space Needle, which was fine. The hotel is beautiful and it offers a great location. It's near shopping, fine restaurants and more. Of course, since it's Seattle, there are coffee shops everywhere. We enjoyed the hotel pool, which is indoors on one of the top floors. From the pool, you have a nice view of the entire downtown area. There's also a workout area that's pretty decent.

title: “Nicely updated small hotel close to convention center”
text:
i chose to stay here rather than one of the mega-hotels at the convention center, which is just around the corner. This was much smaller, without the crowds in the lobby. It's an older hotel but has been updated in stylish fashion. My room was spacious, with comfortable bed and some nice amenities. There's a small bar/restaurant on the ground floor - I only had breakfast there, which was just fine. 
My only glitch was that I had booked a package deal for the hotel through travelocity that the front desk didn't recognize. They hemmed and hawed but eventually honored the deal (I had the printout with me.) I did think it strange that the hotel and travelocity wouldn't be in sync. However, it worked out in the end.

title: “Wonderful Hotel”
text: Myself and partner went with my best friend and her partner to celebrate our 40th birthday. Stayed for 5 nights, and our room on the 15th floor was wonderful. Was very surprised at the size of room, and the bathroom was superb..sparkly clean. Kitchen well equiped and the tea and coffee replenished daily as were the towels. Maid rewashed the crockery even when I had done it. Don't get a room above the 23rd floor as they have not been revamped yet (so my friend found, but was rehoused on a lower level, which was again, a very high standard). We asked if we could extend our check out after midday as we weren't being collected until 3pm, and although they were v busy, they let us extend 1 room, which was a great help (and at no extra charge). Hotel located just across the road from Penn Station which is really handy for the subway. Macys a short stroll and times square about 10 minutes walk away. Could see the Empire State from our window, and everything a tourist from England wanted to see was easily reachable. Would highly recommend this hotel, and will stay there again next time we visit.

title: “Check your reservation: they booked me into wrong hotel”
text: From the reviews this looked like a great place so I picked up the phone to make a reservation. Got through to the central reservations for the company (the number on the website of the hotel) and had a very pleasant conversation, selected a room, and thought all was great... until I got the confirmation in my email and found they had booked me into Anaheim rather than San Fran/Fisherman's Wharf. So I called to cancel (of course) and then got the runaround about whether they had space available. I called central reservations and was told there was space available, but only for a minimum 2-day stay (I only wanted one night), but only the front desk could override. Front desk said they couldn't override... and that their schedule showed no space. Meanwhile I was looking at their own website's schedule which DID show space available. Front desk said he didn't know why the website said there was space. So bottom line: with a big outfit like this, that has multiple properties around the country, make sure you confirm where you are booked. Front desk's best guess of what happened to me? "Perhaps he or she in central reservations hit the wrong button and pulled up Anaheim instead of San Francisco."

title: “Old Fashioned in the Best Way!”
text: I travel constantly and am deliriously sick of the standard Marriott wallpaper, carpets, etc. I was so happy when I came to the Carlton in NYC, an Autograph property of Marriott, and discovered that Autograph hotels are really distinct. The service at the Carlton is great, the rooms and hallways beautiful, as are the lobby and the hotel bar. Very old fashioned. The rooms are not large, but they are nicely furnished, with a safe and very large screen flat tv. For Marriott Platinum and Gold members, the breakfast has few choices, but with AMAZING croissants, marmalade, and best of all fresh yogurt with fresh berries and granola brought to you from the kitchen. This is now my choice hotel in NYC, and the location gives you great access to different subway lines. My only complaint - no coffee maker in the room. But the coffee maker in the hotel business center made up for this!

title: “Some deterioration...”
text:
I visited have this hotel on various occasaions and have noted some deterioration over the past 6 years.
Specifically: 
1) a rather curt attitude anmmong thr staff (and 
I have stayed at this hotel frequently over that past six years and have noticed a regrettable decline in quality during that period!
Specifically: 
1) A torrent of rust when I turned on the whirlpool jets in the bathroom resulting in a torrent of rust and a need to drain the bathtub with the resultant shameful waste of water. (and a crack in the bathtub for good measure.)
2) A room service receptionist (telephonist) who chastised us for ordering a pot of coffee at 9 am when there was coffee available in the lobby (she wanted me to cavort naked in the lobby to recharge my coffee addiction??)
