3) No room service for breakfast, except for crappy continental??? - sacrilege!! And we were reminded that the kitchen closes at 10:30 am for breakfast when we breezed in at 10:15 am. We knew that.
4) Replace the cushions on the couches....pleeeeeez!!
Still a good hotel.... downgraded one notch to 4 stars from 5.

title: “Very good conference hotel!”
text:
I know that flagship hotels like the Hyatt Regency are supposed to be able to handle conferences and such, but they made it look easy! From having session rooms mapped out, to having plenty of staff available to guide you, everything was top notch! It is difficult to single any one person out, since they were all consistently polite and helpful, but Brittany, at the lower level front deck was simply awesome. After the first time I introduced myself and ask for directions, she was sure to catch my attention everytime I passed her desk to make sure I was headed the right way. Brittany is very, very focused on customer service!
My room was very nice, with a work space separated from the sleeping area, and a great shower.
I look forward to my next stay!

title: “Service makes it # 1”
text: We recently spent one night at the Lenox Hotel after a fall foliage trip through New England. I see now why everyone rates this hotel #1 in Boston! From the moment we stopped our car at the door, we were greeted as though we were special guests of this lovely establishment. The doorman, Peter, was extremely gracious and helpful and set the bar high for the service to follow. Well, the bar never dipped and everyone we encountered during our stay was extremely friendly, always helpful, and NEVER too busy to attend to our needs. We were upgraded to a junior suite which was a fabulous corner room with 2 beds that were absolutely some of the most comfortable I have every slept in. The room was very spacious and the cold bottled water waiting for us in the fridge was a nice welcome. Other hotels could learn a great deal from this establishment. I highly recommend spending a few extra dollars when in Boston and stay at the Lenox. You won't be sorry!!!!!!!!!!!

title: “Scammers and Thieves”
text:
i stayed at this hotel for two nights, courtesy of my friends at Yoshi's SF, a jazz club i played at last night. i'd stayed at the Kabuki once before a few years back, and liked the look of the place, so i was looking forward to coming back.
room service is vastly over-priced, but worse than that was my girlfriend ordering an egg-white omelette one morning, only to be old the next morning that such an exoic dish was not available; this from the cook herself.
the most annoying staff member was the one most overpaid: $35 for valet parking is excessive, but not out of the ordinary in higher-priced hotels, but this guy was never there to answer the phone, was never ready to take the car when i drove up, to the point of my arriving after a morning workout at the Y (the hotel fitness center is barely worth the name), stepping out in the freezing cold, only to have the guy ignore me and go chat up his limo-driver buddy lollygagging behind me in the lot. when my girlfriend wanted to get a cab to shop in Union Square, he told her he'd call her a cab, and when she arrived downstairs, he said the cab 'couldn't come' (oh, really? SF on a clear day and the cabs disappear?), and tried to foist her off on another one of his limo-cronies. this morning, when i was on my way to work out, he was scamming some other guest who was clearly in a hurry to be about her business, but, what the hell, anything to make me wait (i'd called down ahead to have the car brought around; again, he never answered). he then didn't bring the car around, just pointed to the car wedged between two others in the handicapped space; i had to lean out the driver's side to ascertain the direction he'd had the wheels poining, otherwise i would have side-swiped the crammed cars next ti me. on arrival (we were a little early and had to leave our bags with him)he brought up three out of the four bags we'd left with him. lucky he found the other in short order.
worst of all, we'd been using the IPod dock/radio alarm in the room, a nice touch. unfortunately, we realized the IPod was still in the dock when we arrived at SFO for our flight this morning. beyond any doubt, the IPod was in the room. we called, were disconnected twice, and inally put in touch with the Lost & Found dept. who assured us there was no IPod found in the room. i repeat: there is no doubty of exactly where it was left, and when i called and had to leave an answering machine message for the hotel manager, i never received even the courtesy of a return call.
never again with these crooks.

title: “NYC Room with a View!”
text:
We chose the King Bed Sky View Avenue Studio because we wanted a room with a view on a high floor. The room and the view were spectacular. There are big windows on three walls looking up and down 8th Avenue and down 44th Street towards Times Square. We had room 3410 on the 34th out of 36 floors. We chose the Intercontinental because the Sky View rooms allow the customer to pay for and reserve a room on a higher floor. Many hotels would only make this allocation based on availability at check in. The views offer a tremendous, balconly like city scape of Manhattan. The view did not include any particularly famous buildings but was stunning anyway. Go ahead and spend the money for this room if you can, you won't be dissapointed. Our boys had a Sky View Double room with a nice view to the North. 
The beds in both rooms were as comfortable as any hotel beds we have slept in. These are true pillow top mattresses. The pillows were great. The bathroom has a nice big walk in shower with a glass door. 
We had a good but expensive breakfast in the hotel dining room. Europan is a nice quick service choice for breakfast just down 8th Ave between 43rd and 42nd streets. 
We tried the Meatball Shop based on the hotel concierge video and thoroughly enjoyed it. 
There is a subway station entrance immediately adjacent to the hotel entrance with walkways that connect to 34th St and Times Square lines.

title: “Central DC location”
text: Hotel is located near the White House and near several metro lines and stations. Nice property with a somewhat quirky layout so be aware there are some very long walks from the elevators to some rooms - so ask if that is an issue for you. Our room was spacious and well-appointed with a double sink in the bathroom which was a nice surprise. We had no issues with the AC system mentioned in other reviews so hopefully they have fixed their HVAC problems. We used the valet service – yes you can find cheaper but it was worth it to us to avoid the hassles of parking in DC. We had no problems with wifi which was included since we were HH members. Hotel has a nice restaurant on ground floor, however, do yourself a favor and try one of the numerous nearby restaurants to get the full DC experience.

title: “Seahawks roost.”
text: My son and I just stayed a night here. The good. Great downtown location. Nice clean room with flat screen TV and comfortable beds.Free wireless internet. The bad. Room was small, (two queens), with no coffeemaker, fridge, or microwave. Though there is a Starbucks across the street. For those of you unaccustomed to city parking... I'm sorry but it sucks. Overnight parking on a Sunday at the hotel was $32.00. The good news is that parking on Sunday in Seattle is free if you can find an open spot on the street.(We did) Gotta move your car by 8am or pay $4.00 an hour for street parking.($4.00 a half hour in some spots). Nearby underground lots charged anywhere from 12-15 $ for day parking if you parked befor 9am. So basically expect to pay through the nose for downtown hotel parking. I reccomend calling any hotel ahead of booking to clear this up. Lots of good shopping and eats as well as Pikes Place Market within walking!

title: “Excellent Stay”
text:
Was here for a week at a conference and enjoyed our stay. Room was clean, large, and well-maintained. Staff was helpful and attentive, which made the conference even better. There is a nice Einstein Bagel shop in the lobby area which make breakfast cheap, good, and inexpensive. Not too far to walk to Michigan Avenue or to the Navy Pier in the opposite direction. Another couple of blocks and you're at an El stop. 
Between the hotel and the Magnificent Mile are several decent and inexpensive restaurants. Seemed to be in a good part of town and never felt threatened at any time during the stay. Would consider staying here again if looking for something downtown.

title: “Enjoyed my stay”
text: This hotel is the one where I say whenever I attend the Graduate School. The location is convenient and personnel there are very helpful and pleasant. Edith was especially helpful when I checked out. She told me how to get to the Metro station that would get me to Washington Reagan National Airport.

title: “Lovely boutique hotel near Union Square”
text: We spent two nights at Petite Auberge ... wish we could have been there longer. Location is great - on a fairly quiet street only a few blocks from Powell and Union Square, and also a short walk to Chinatown. Loved the delicious breakfast (huge!), also the fun afternoon wine and appetizers served in a charming fireside common space where we chatted with other guests. Rooms were very clean and well-appointed. OId but charming hotel, full of European character. Very fair price. We would definitely stay there again!

title: “I am sure you could find better”
text: I did not like this place at all - if you like the old style - flowery and old then go ahead. I thought the rooms were old and needed updating - there were dead bugs in my window the bathrooms were old and very basic and small. the service was OK but I just think it needs a lot of work - I had a suite and it was aged. The internet didn't work and you had to pay. I would not stay again. they do have updated rooms but they are exactly the same but with newer furnishings.

title: “Great place to stay!”
text: Great place to stay!

title: “Very European”
text: ... and by "very European" I mean extremely small, spartan, but clean rooms; no control of temperature other than the window; friendly and helpful person at the desk; and no parking. It's also very affordable, and close (2 blocks) to the fancy shopping district in downtown. The hotel is quite old, with a neat little lobby area. Upstairs, about the only thing that's changed in the last 100 years is the carpet, wallpaper, and plumbing fixtures. Inside the hotel, it's relatively noiseless, but since you'll need to open a window (even in winter because you have no control of the radiator) there will be noise from outside. That may bother some people. No breakfast in the Hotel, but do NOT be tempted to go across the street to the 24-hour diner: I love horrible greasy eggs bacon and hashbrowns, but this place charges $7.50 instead of a reasonable fair price, like about $4.50. The world's most ridiculously expensive bad food! You'll be better off taking a bus or walking to Chinatown and getting dim sum for breakfast for about 1/4 the price!!! Anyway, if you're looking for a basic clean room, not travelling by car, and willing to put up with some inconveniences (just pretend it's 40 years ago), this is a great place to stay for the money. I'll definitely be returning to the Union Square Plaza Hotel next time I'm in San Francisco!

title: “Gorgeous rooms in the wrong location.”
text:
I had an enormous suite, big bathroom, fabulous kitchen with stove and refrigerator plus a washer/dryer in the room!! 
the problem is that although the location is central to both the theater district and to good shopping, the area itself has absolutely nothing and is very cheesy.
The management was really nice to me when I wanted to move my room away from the construction site next door. The great bellman whose name I forgot, (tall African American young man), was also incredibly helpful.

title: “Great Views of Marina”
text: We spent six nights at the Sheraton in a room with a lovely view of the Marina. Each room has a small balcony with room for two chairs. Of course you hear planes - it is next to an airport! There is a bus shuttle for $1 which takes you along the front and near the Gaslamp Quarter. Free wi-fi is provided in the lobby area and a bank of computers is supplied for guest use. There is a Starbucks, Restaurant and Pub (Quinns). We ate in the pub and I recommend the Pacific Chowder (scrummy). The staff are all courteous and good natured. We had vouchers for the buffet breakfast which was very acceptable with a wide range of choices.

title: “Comfort and luxury at bargain prices with Amex Platinum FHR rate!”
text:
Hubby and I booked 2 days at the NY Palace at the Amex Platinum FHR rate. $509 plus tax per night bought us a huge (for NYC) corner King room on the 29th floor; free great breakfast, late 4pm checkout and get this, folks - a $110 meal credit at Gilt, the incredible restaurant on the premises.
Now to the main details: The hotel is traditional and gorgeous, with all the gilding and luxury your eye can muster. Check-in service is efficient and cordial. Speedy elevators. The room was quite huge. Furnishings were traditional (if you're W type, do NOT stay here, as you will perceive this as quite stodgy), with the exception of the flat screen TV. Comfy bed, excellent Frette linens, smallish wardrobe closet, great desk space, two armchairs, side tables and a killer view of the cathedral. 
Marble bathroom was small and no dual sinks in sight. Shower was not separate from WC area. No fan in bathroom, so mirror fogs up quite rapidly. Toiletries by Molton Brown, pretty standard. Still, the room was huge and a bargain, considering all the other benefits. At some point, the Dorchester management group will have to renovate and enlarge the bathrooms, since technically they are not really 5 star (compared with Four Seasons quality).
Internet was available at $16 per night. No problem, excellent wireless connection (I Skyped for 60 minutes, no interruption in service). Minibar well stocked and electronic - no need to keep track of anything.
Breakfast was GREAT - Amex sprung for $50 for 2, the rest was ours to pay. Now to the amazing thing: Diego, the concierge, had arranged for us to get a $110 credit at Gilt, the superlative restaurant on the premises (see separate restaurant review.) Apparently this is not really available as a rule, but since Amex stated "one lunch or dinner" as their added benefit and Istana, the casual restaurant is closed for dinner, we managed to swing this incredible deal. Dunno if management will continue to approve this, but you can always try ;-). 
We never used the spa or fitness room, but I asked and gym clothes are available if you forget yours. In sum, I'd go for this deal in a minute any time I'm in NYC. The New York Palace is elegant, comfortable, cosmopolitan and located in the most central area of Midtown. Service is gracious, efficient and polite (they were insistent on nightly turndown with bedtime chocolates). Don't see how you could go wrong, quite frankly.

title: “Old hotel and not kept up well”
text: Concierge room open only 6:30-9:30 am and NOT on the weekends. Electricity in room went out and two outlets didn't work. Service was less than acceptable although the service in the bar was great. Nice pool and courtyard but only a few rooms open to that setting. No balcony and if you open the outside door you get smells from the kitchen and lots and lots of outside noise. Tried to pull one over on us and told us we were on the executive floor until we checked out the rooms and found our room was the same as all the others. Would not stay here again even though close to the mall.

title: “Great Stay”
text:
September 10th we stayed at the Comfort Inn in Boston, and found it too be a very nice hotel. The front desk were friendly and helpful, the room was clean, and comfortable, and they had a excellent breakfast in the morning. 
They have a shuttle that takes you to the closest T station, (jfk u mass) which is a short drive away, and from there it's not long to get downtown to the sights of Boston. 
They do have resturants part of the compound of this hotel, but it's a little walk around the cornor, not directly connected with the hotel. 
If not wanting to pay the high cost of staying directly downtown Boston, this is a great location.

title: “Good stay on short business trip”
text:
I stayed at the Raffaello while I was in Chicago for a short business trip. I booked a negotiated price through a travel sight endorsed by WIlliam Shatner so the price was a quarter of that at the Four Seasons and was pleased with the value. The location of the hotel was ideal with most of my meetings at the Four Seasons up the street, but would have also been ideal if I just wanted to see Chicago. I was in the smallest room on my floor, it basically fit the bed the dresser and a desk, I was rarely in the room so this was not a big deal for me, but if I were traveling with my wife it would not have cut it, therefore if I am not traveling alone I would avoid the low price deal and book a more spacious room. 
The room was clean and well maintained, tempurature control was perfect, but the shower took a while to warm up. The bed was comfortable, but I needed two of the flimsy pillows to sleep. I feel bad for housekeeping with all the water that must come out of there due to the half glass, half open doorway. I used the workout room in the morning and it had a very good assortment of weight and cardio equipment especially for a hotel this size, which was a plus. The elevators are small, but unlike other reviewers I never had a long wait.
Overall the value for the dollar was very good, I would stay here again.

title: “PennsLanding Hyatt great location excellent staff, GREAT deal!”
text: reservation included duck tour. Arrived at noon, Bellboys were great, desk had tickets ready, took care of scheduling our tour immediately! Room was top notch, had breakfast (included) in hotel--very nice! Great view! Bellman recommended safest & easiest way to walk to South Street! It was just a great choice that I would highly recommend and would go back to in a minute! Staff was super!

title: “Fantastic service and perfect room well worth the price.”
text: Stayed here one night and wish we stayed longer. Room was super clean and comfortable bed. Service impeccable. Would stay again - I think it's the best hotel in Boston. We walked to Flour for a treat and Sportello for the best eggs ever.

title: “Lovely hotel”
text: Nothing but good things to say about the Hayes Mansion. Yes the room we were in was not huge but it was very clean and comfortable. Building and grounds are absolutely fantastic. We spent a three day weekend and were the only people in the pool and hot tub which were also lovely. Would stay again. Only potential problem is its location which is quite out of the way, but the upside of this is that it is a huge property and quite quiet. There was a large wedding on one of the nights of our stay and our room was in the same building as the ballroom - no problems with noise whatsoever.

title: “Worth the Stay!!!”
text: I stayed at this hotel because I was attending a meeting at the Convention Center. Talk about how close it is - some of us stayed at the hotels near by but nothing was as close as this hotel. The staff - they were great. They had recommendations on where to go - which was a pleasure that they had real up to date knowledge on the area. They have a restaurant on site and the food was reasonable and good. I would stay at this hotel again in a heartbeat.

title: “Just the same as a bunch of other hotels at this location”
text: Hotel nothing special, another branded hotel, could be anywhere. Perfect location for all sites around fisherman's wharfe. Has a small pool and deck area, some of the others do not have this. Try to get a 5th floor room overlooking the bay - these are by far the best from a view perspective. Don't get me wrong, nothing wrong, decent size rooms, clean, though breakfast prices are very expensive. Shop around, though all pretty much the same size. PS Take a look at the Suites at Fisherman's Wharfe

title: “Great service!”
text: My husband & I stayed the first night back from our honeymoon at the Courtyard. We pricelined it while on our honeymoon, wanting to stay by ourselves, and not with my MIL, the first night back before making the eight hour drive to our new home (we got married and left for our honeymoon in my husband's hometown). Everything was perfect. We barely waited 10 minutes for the shuttle, and the shuttle driver was so nice! He gave us a really nice talk about marriage and was just very friendly. Once inside the hotel, we asked where we might get some ice cream (I couldn't really find any in the airports on our way home), and they offered to take us to the Steak n Shake in Easton for milkshakes with the shuttle (even though it was well after midnight, and the Easton shuttle was done for the evening). We decided we weren't up for the trip, so we got ice cream at the nearby McDonalds and hung out in our room. We did take a dip in the hot tub; it was really quiet, since it's primarily a business hotel and most everyone was probably in bed. Our bed was very comfortable, and the bathroom was nice and clean. We'd definitely stay here again, between the nice rooms and great service!

title: “Wonderful stay!”
text: Just returned from a 4 day stay and cant say enough good things about this hotel. From the breakfast buffet including great made to order omelets, afternoon happy hour, awesome staff (except for Ronnie), spotlessly clean suites, plus a great military rate.....made for a five star stay! Some reviews have written about noisy air conditioners which I found to be the exact opposite as ours was extremely quiet, we also never encountered any problems regarding lines at breakfast. Embassy Suites will definitely be my first choice of hotel should I return to the SA Riverwalk.

title: “Not Impressed”
text: This is a brand new hotel but needs the finishing touches. Billiing it as "Times Square" hotel is pushing the limits. It's between 8th and 9th on 39th. Upon entering it's obvious the place is new and you would think the staff would be pleasant and helpful and the roms would be perfect. Guess again. The front desk staff was either ignorant or just plain unwilling to be helpful. When booking the room I failed to notice there was only valet parking for $55.00 (expensive even for NYC). so I asked what other options there were. After a 5 second dumb stare she she said the valet parking or I could park on the street. I again asked what other options there were, she had no idea. Turns out there is parking across the street and another place 4 buildings back. Upon arriving in the room it was clean and neat. The bed was comfortable, as were the pillows. However, upon closer inspection you'll notice trhe trim work isn't done around the windows, the fridge barely kept food cold and already had scratches and dents as did the bathtub.

title: “A pleasant stay”
text:
Booked through Priceline for 80 all inclusive.
Check in was very friendly and attentive, with a smile. 
The location is great for anyone into baseball and football, as it is in walking distance to both stadiums. The building is an ugly 1970s structure which pales in front of the Hilton in front. 
The room was ample although I was given a room with a view on the back of the building. The king bed was very comfortable, with again a LCD TV. The work station is kind of awkward, with very little place to put a laptop. Internet connection is around 12$. The bathroom is large and well supplied. 
The restaurant in the hotel is typically expensive, but there is not much in terms of places for breakfast...I wouldn't try that greasy spoon next to the strip joint. It is close to the Wharf Rat, if you want a good beer. 
The gym is well equipped, however the pool is smallish and claustrophobic. 
Overall, enjoyed my stay.

title: “Very nice”
text: The room was clean with good toiletries, towels and bedding. The lobby was nice. All employees were very nice and helpful. The only down side is the location. It is a short walk to major attractions, but the area is really more of an office area so not a lot is going on in the immediate area. I would definitely stay there again. I got a good deal that made it worth a short walk.

title: “Tired hotel needing an upgrade...”
text:
We stayed here for one night on a recent business trip. Our room was decent enough, although the decor in the room and hallways does leave much to be desired. Sort of a vintage 70's style. The shower was slow flow, and had old hardware which unfortunately only produced ice cold or scalding hot water. The pub downstairs pumped out bagpipe music which was disturbing until somewhere between 10-11pm. This could be heard by patrons on the lower floors.
I cannot comment on the food as we did not eat here. Parking was 19.00 with unlimited in/out across the street. Valet was 34.00 (?). Internet was not free in the rooms and we did not opt to get it.
This place is considered a 4 star on priceline, but it would only be that with a multimillion dollar upgrade.
I would not pay full price to stay here as there are probably better hotels for similar rates nearby.

title: “Very nice”
text: This is our regular hotel for when my family is in the San Diego area. Has been for a couple years now. I go to college in san diego so whenever they visit me, we stay here. It's clean and pretty well kept. The staff is friendly and will do their best to fix any problems you may have with the rooms. For the price it's definitely worth it!

title: “Fabulous Hotel”
text: I stayed here for three nights with four other girls and the only complaint I have is that the elevators get packed when everyone rushes down to get the great breakfast in the mornings. Dennis Hambright was very friendly and had great recommendations for us to see and do - the hotel was very quick to remedy a minor issue with plumbing and brought ice and extra pillows and towels very quickly when requested. The breakfasts were great (you get serenaded by the staff) and the hotel even had a Mexican buffet for dinner one night. Very convenient to Water Tower, Magnificent Mile and John Hancock Building. Place also seemed very dog friendly as we saw quite a few coming and going.

title: “The Driskill-not as bad as previous reviews, but read on”
text:
My wife and I travel extensively for work and pleasure on both domestic and international trips. Upon approach, The Driskill, is a stunning, beautiful old restored structure, the interior lobby is magnificent. 
The front desk staff are arrogant and unhelpful. Billing errors were made. Staff occurred to be inconvenienced by our insisting that the bill be corrected. A "professional" and "service oriented" front desk staff would make the difference between an above average and an excellent rating for anyone staying at The Driskill.
I am certain that many of the negative visits listed here begun with bad service at the front desk and went down hill from there. It is a bit pricey, the place has been well maintained and when you look at the place from a historic standpoint, it's great. Valet Parking is waaay over-priced for comparable cities. $21.00 a day?--Come on, Sausalito, Ca is only $12.00 a day!
Room service was excellent. The young man delivering our meals was one of the best we've had--anywhere in the world. Nice young college kid. Maids were also wonderful.
We would suggest a room on the 7th street side of the hotel 4th or 5th floor, otherwise, if there is an event in the ballroom at The Driskill, you might as well go down and attend the event because you WILL NOT be getting any sleep until it is over. Very Noisy.
So in short, can the front desk staff or send them for customer sensitivity training, lower the parking rate, enjoy the Driskill until it goes BK again. (as history has repeated itself many times here)

title: “Comfortable and friendly”
text: The staff were friendly, receptive and quick to respond to requests. When we ordered room service, the food was excellent. As for the rooms, we were extremely comfortable - no complaints. The hotel bar is very classy and the bartender, in addition to being cheerful and welcoming, makes excellent cocktails!

title: “Great Location, but a few infrastruture issues”
text:
We stay las Friday and Saturday night. The location is great - next to the A train at Canal St and an easy walk to numerous restaurants. 
A couple of problems - no hot water Friday night and Saturday morning and one of the elevators wounldn't stop at our floor. The elevators were very slow as well. On other complaint, the bottom sheets are too small for the mattresses and keep slipping off.
The staff was gracious and credited us one night's room charge when we check out. Would go back if the opportunity presents.

title: “Good location”
text: The hotel is clean,large room. bathroom is good. It is an old hotel liike most in the city so I thought it was fine considering the age. The location is close to shopping,restuarants,rite aid. The subway is next to the hotel a plus if you take it. The down side of the hotel being next to the subway you get the strange people at night. Hotel does have a guard in the lobby to keep the panhandlers out. I think the hotel is fine, ive stayed here many times. The staff is friendly & always helpful. Enjoy Philly

title: “this hotel sucks”
text: booked two double rooms for 4 nights thru hotels[-] looked great on web major mistake didnt get rooms we reserved well got one double and one king not what we were told we were getting the double had a kitchen sink drainage problem took them 2 full days to even come look and fix and only happened after i told them i was calling corperate which took my complaint but havent heard a darn thing back imagine that anyway couldnt get ice from there machine the entire stay was told to go across street to neighbor hotel??? ok pazying 660 for two rooms to go across street to get ice??? got stoppped up sink and to top it all off maid service was awful had to go to front desk every night to get coffee/toilet paper/essentials you would expect to be left do your self a favor stay somewhere else!!!!!!

title: “An overpriced LaQuitna!!!”
text: Let me begin by saying that, I have never been so highly disappointed in a hotel stay in my life. I just returned from a 3 night stay at the Waldorf (Sept 7-10). While the staff were very polite, that did not make up for the terrible accomodations of the rooms at the hotel. Upon entering, the lobby is nice - nothing out of this world, but that is about as good as it gets. We stayed on the 12th floor. When we got off of the elevator to the 12th floor, there was a stinch that reminded you of an elderly nursing home. It appeared that it was being covered up by a whole can of Lysol. The wallpaper was peeling, and the lighting was quite dim. Finally, we entered the room. If you love old elegance, this might be the place for you, but it is done on a budget. Our room had a huge square cut out in the ceiling. It looks as though it had been sheet rocked and painted. The comforters had blood stains on the backs of them. It was very stuffy in the room, and even with the air on it was still quite humid. Don't even try to wash your hair in the shower, as the water pressure is tooooo low. The rooms were very dusty. Dust was flying everywhere. I went to the Front Desk Manager to ask for a refund, and to see about moving to another hotel. I told him that in my opinion the hotel appeared to be an overpriced LaQuinta. Even on a good day, a brand new LaQuinta would give the Waldorf a run for its money. Needless to say, he would not give give us a refund for the 3rd night stay. The first 2 nights were on Hilton Honors points. BEWARE-even if you do have points, do not waste them here. Use them at another Hilton hotel in NY. I have stayed at various hotels in NYC. This is by far to be a 5 star hotel, definitely becoming a falling star.

title: “Older Building but remodeled”
text: This hotel is older. It is oddly located with a huge empty parking lot in front of it. The decor has been recently updated and the layout of the suite I was in was great! In the living room area there was a couch, TV, and even a stereo, which was a nice touch since I'd rather listen to music than watch TV. The age really showed in the bathroom (small) and closet (it had a wooden door that was off the track, and the doorknob kept falling off). The room also had a musty smell. The hotel was doing some upgrades while I was there. A new AC unit was installed right as I checked in and the carpet was cleaned the morning of the second day. (There was a tag left on my door warning me about the carpet being wet.....which I found to be inconvenient.) The staff were all helpful and friendly. This is not a place to stay for pleasure but it works for a quick in and out of town.

title: “Great service”
text:
Friendly staff
Champions bar cool to hang out after long day
Rooms are nothing fancy but very comfortable beds
Pool is big but didnt get a chance to use
Lobby wait times can be a bit long
Ask for shuttle to manhattan beach, they won't tell you about it and is very nice to spend day at manhattan beach
Safety is on top of my list, here anyone from street can go into room areas, not good.
Has starbucks on site
Wifi is not free in rooms is like 19dls/24 hrs, free at lobby so inconvenient.
Can't really walk anywhere, if go outside to your right nothing but hotels and then airport, if walk to your left more hotels and shady areas.

title: “Absolutely incredible and perfect!!”
text:
After 12 years of business travel finally I find a hotel that is literally perfect. Amazing because they are only a year old and their staff act as if they have been a solid team for years. The guestrooms are thoughtfully designed with power to the bedside tables, instant responsive a/c, quiet-quiet rooms, quick check in, very quick telephone response. Lecturing at this hotel and notice that they use brown table cloth for their classroom set up. The material is suade like smooth and here's the kicker - the staff lightly and lovingly sponge the table tops down! Their a/v staff and function staff all amazing. I am getting tired of pinching myself. Bottom line! I used to work for many of the larger national chains sucbh as Westin who truly do offer inconsistent service and hotel experiences. This Kimpton hotel is not to be missed. A serious wow from a road weary speaker who has visitied Montana, Mississippi and now Illinois in just the past week. 
Check out their near perfect overall review score. My suggestion is that this hotel offer itself as a school of learning for many Westin & Fairmont Hotel General Managers who think they run perfect guest experience hotels and quite frankly through direct prolonged experience do not. This hotel ANTICIPATES versus REACTS.
My only hope is that whatever work culture magic that is occuring remains and deepens.
Check out my other reviews. Many are harsh because the hotel services are either ridiculous orneedlessly badly managed and/or operated. All of my reviews are meant for the hotel general manager to review with their department heads as options and ideas on how to specifically improve. This place is simply a.w.e.s.o.m.e.

title: “Service as Good as Home”
text:
I am Very Happy with my Extended Stay at the Studio Plus Hotel In El Paso Tx. Because as I arrived the Saff treated me with respect, promtiness and very helpful maner,
the room was clean, and the room service during my stay was excellent.
the amenities are just perfect for long stays, all appliances worked and the constant care from the stuff attending any need and offers of help are outstanding.

title: “Good price/location”
text:
We stayed here in September 2005 for 3 nights as part of Virgin's "King to the Road" tour. 
The location was pretty good, only 5 min walk to the seafront. The rooms were clean, fairly big with 2 double beds, tv, air con. The bathroom was tidy and sufficient for 2 people. The only bad thing about the room was the smell of cigarettes coming under the door from the corridor. We were on the ground floor, and all rooms were non-smoking however we were at the end next to a fire exit where people smoked all night!
Our car parking pass never worked once to get in/out of the car park. We got a free t-shirt and some 2 for 1 drink vouchers when we checked in, was was quick and easy.

title: “Faded and tired”
text: During a recent business meeting I had the opportunity to return to the Omni Parker House. While I had fond memories of visits to the hotel years ago, it was dreadful during my most recent visit. The guest room was one of the smallest I've seen in modern times; the walk in closet was nearly the same square footage as the guestroom. The room had one small window looking out over a light well, a very small desk and one chair (desk.) Twice I asked for a room change to no avail. There was only one electrical plug on the desk so I had to go to a nearby convenience store to purchase a multi-plug unit for my laptop and phone. The bathroom was tiny and the water pressure left a lot to be desired. All in all, even if they'd charged $50 a night (which they didn't) it wouldn't have been worth the money.

title: “Very nice experience!”
text: I am extremely picky when it comes to cleanliness of a hotel and this hotel was very clean. I used to live in Memphis (about 4 years ago) and wasn't sure what to expect from this hotel. Others in the area and in the downtown area that cost much more had disappointed me so I was pleasantly surprised to find this hotel. I would stay here again and again. I had business in the downtown area/Madison Avenue area and the drive down Poplar was pleasant and easy. There were many great things about my experience. The fitness center was very nice and open 24 hours. The hotel staff was very kind and helpful. The breakfast was amazing! I couldn't believe the amount of food...the taste...I mean, this is a free breakfast! The cook on staff actually made me a waffle one morning. This is not your typical continental breakfast. It was like a mini breakfast buffet at a restaurant. Overall I must say that out of all the resorts and other hotels I have stayed at, the hotel staff at this Staybridge outdid themselves. I highly recommend this to anyone else who is as picky as I am about where they stay. Thanks!

title: “Fantastic Place To Stay”
text: Location could not be better, you can walk to Times Square, Rockfeller Centre, Empire State. Rooms are large and quiet (views aren't great, but who cares) and in great condition. Don't hesitate to stay here!

title: “great stays every time”
text: 3 separate stays in the last year. First two in a queen suite and 3rd trip was standard queen but wound up getting upgraded. The location is convenient to the horton plaza, and gaslamp. The staff is friendly and the restaurant is awesome. The lobby area has has a nice feel to it. The hotel often times runs really good deals, so sign up for their newsletter!

title: “Better than expected”
text: The hotel is better than the typical roadside springhill. Room was mostly quite although bed was worn and sagging was acceptable. Had paul mitchel soap that many marriott family hotels are going to. Had microwave and fridge something i think all spring hill brand has. Staff while friendly didn't seem as professional as other places. Example was trainee couldn't figure out how to check me in and had to wait for help, had forgot something a bit later after valet parked car, they had me go find the car on my own rather than escort me or go get it for me although was polite, room service never answer phone so had to go down to bar and order. Though the roomservice salmon was very good and faster than expected once ordered. I asked about shuttle to pike market and was told shuttle goes only on the hour and will drop me several blocks away as they dont go there- seems tacky, ended up having my friend pick me up since i didn't want to pay a cab or deal with parking and was only like a mile away. I've been sour on the spinghill brand but this was an experience that improved the brand image for me, guess it helps when expections are low. Oh and the elevator was a fast one, so many are really slow so i liked this.

title: “Good hotel, great location, great value.”
text: A good priced hotel, located in the middle of the turistic zone of Washington D.C. It´s really close to the White House, Capitol Hill, Nasa museum, the underground, libraries, restaurants.

title: “Wonderful hotel”
text:
We were traveling on an Alaskan cruise and decided to spend a few nights before the cruise, I booked this hotel way in advance in it was a great deal. The hotel staff was very friendly and accomodating, the concierge, was very knowledgable and helpful with everything. 
This is an older hotel with alot of charm. but clean and upgraded. We truly enjoyed our stay. It was a little bit of a walk to the sites, but not too far (and I am not a walker) 
there is a pool table down stairs and quiet lounge just beautiful and inviting (with a fire place and everything!)
I would highly recomend this hotel!

title: “Fantastic!”
text:
What a great hotel. From the beginning of our stay to when we checked out, the stay was perfect. 
When I checked it, I was greeted promptly, and I was able to get my original room switched to a front facing room very quickly with no problems. The room was great, with a giant comfortable bed, great TV.
I was in DC for business so the proximity to the Metro (literally half a block away), made it easy to get anywhere. 
A perfect hotel to stay in. Plus, making the reservation through Marriott.com with a AAA discount, I got my room for $99 per night, A STEAL!
I highly recommend this hotel for everyone who wants to come stay in DC

title: “Best Hotel in Town.”
text:
If you need a retreat from the hustle of LA - the Wilshire Crest is your best bet. Quiet, in a residential neighborhood, but one block's walk from restaurants - the Wilshire Crest offers large comfortable immaculate rooms, excellent beds and linens, spacious work areas and vanities, expanded digital cable and large TV's - everything a business or family traveller could want. This is not the right hotel if you want loud parties, a pool, a bar, or a restaurant open till 2 AM - but the complimentary breakfast is amazing.
I have found my oasis.

title: “Fantastic hotel in a fantastic location”
text:
This is a fantastic hotel in a fantastic location.
I stayed one night in June 08 and was upgraded to a suite as the hotel was fully booked! The suite was beautifully decorated and well equipped.
My stay was trouble free and the staff were friendly and knowledgeable.
Would recommend to both the business and holiday traveller.

title: “Not as impressive as the Renaissance!”
text: I stayed here two weeks ago for a long week and a half trip and about half way through I decided to change hotels to the renaissance. Although the rooms were nice the staff really wasn't great. They weren't rude or anything but didn't make me feel like I was anything other then someone making them money. The food was decent in the district but the service was kind of lacking, probably due to the business level (it was really busy). Overall not a horrible hotel but I've had much better. In fact I actually went to the renaissance hotel a few blocks away to finish out my stay and man on man they blew my socks off!

title: “Great!”
text:
I had already booked this hotel and then read the reviews...some bad. We were pleasantly surprised though! Great location, large room by NY standards, nice personnel who are very informative about things to do, places to eat, etc.
Don't believe the reviews by picky people, this is a nice clean hotel and in a great location! Don't know about other rooms, but we were in 1132. Very nice!

title: “Great Location!”
text: We ended up staying here 2 nights; one night we had previously booked and a second night when Hurricane Irene was arriving. The staff was so friendly - my 10 year old daughter commented several times that she thought everyone was so nice! Compared to the other hotels in Boston; the hotel was reasonably priced and was in a great location; right across from the Prudential Center and the wading pool.

title: “Didnt even get past reception!!”
text:
I cant believe this type of establishment can still be in buisness. We didnt even get as far as the rooms. We were greeted in reception by rude staff and also 4 members of the NYPD as a staff member had pushed a guest! The wait for an hour to get a room was the best experience as every time a guest checked in they went to their room to swiftly return to complain about one of the following:
Other people in the room already
Room not cleaned in months
Dirty underwear in the room
Over flowing toilets
A mouse
etc
We then decided to ask to check our room prior to paying (yes upfront) and we were told 'no as it wasnt hotel policy. Pay, go check it and then request a refund if you arent happy! If you want somewhere better try next door!'
The place is the pits i wouldnt even stay here if they paid me its that bad.

title: “Van, Jessica, and Nils = a great stay at The Liaison”
text:
I am pleased to say the staff at The Liaison gave exceptional service. I was checked in and greeted by Jessica. She welcomed me with open arms as if I was a guest at her owm house. I had a couple of questions about parking, the construction, and the lobby area. She answered them all efficently. I stayed in #827 on the newly remodeled 8th floor. My room was exceptional, very clean, and included a iPod dock that charged as well (a big plus for me because I left my iPhone charger at home). Van and Nils checked me out in less than 5 minutes. They asked me about my experience and by the time I completed my sentence I had a final reciept in my hand. 
I vented to van about my horrible experience at a night club the previous night, he wrote a list and suggested places I should try next time. Van made my weekend complete with his outstanding service.

title: “Okay”
text: Fairly clean room although bedroom bedspread/comforter would have been better if exchanged for a duvet cover. Thought most all chain hotels had made the switch away from bedspreads. Free happy hour drinks were nice. We left too early to take advantage of the breakfast buffet and instead had the continental (which was not great at all). No free wifi as per usual with the Hilton brand unless one is gold status - too bad if one spends their points. Glad this was a one night stay. Shuttle service was very good.

title: “Nice place...”
text:
RIght smack dab between Chinatown and Metro Center, this is a great hotel for people looking for a place close to the Mall and the heart of DC. The Spy Museum is close by, as well as dozens of great bars and restaurants (I recommend Ten Penh).
For what I paid for, I felt like I had to walk a long ways to get to my hotel room on the first floor. The rooms were fantastic though, high ceilings, and comfy bath robes for guests to wear. Very spacious. Hotel staff were very friendly. They even offer you a pet goldfish for the duration of your stay!
This is a very modern-euroesque hotel, not like your common everyday hotels. The decor is very interesting, and every hotel has a type of theme. If you got the money go for it, but if you are looking for a great bargain this place is not for you. Of course, DC is not known for its cheap hotel rates :-)

title: “Great hotel; very contemporary feel”
text:
We stayed at the Hilton Polaris while visiting family back in Columbus. The hotel is fairly new and is decorated in a contemporary style. It actually had lots of design elements that resemble the Conrad Hotel in Chicago, which is Hilton's extreme high end division. Service was very good. I was happy they had my Hilton reward bonus ready when I arrived. I usually have to remind them.
Our room had an interesting desk that allowed for a very functional work area. The shower was great. Bed was very good. The only downside was the view. Parking lot and i-71. Not very inspiring. The Polaris area is packed with every chain restaurant possible and a huge mall next door which is great if you're looking for a shopping weekend. Location is okay but it seems a bit far away if you decide to go downtown for dinner or something.
Overall a great hotel. I just wish it was downtown.

title: “Fantastic!”
text: This hotel is amazing.. Brand new hotel and could not be in a better location. From the Valet to the Housekeeping staff, this property is top knotch. We had a room on the 16th floor that overlooked LA live and the rooftop pool/bar. Room was spacious and very comfortable. The bathroom was quite large and the beds were perfect for a great night sleep. The business center was a bit pricey but had everything you need. Close to USC and many great shops and restaraunts. Concierges was the best ever! Offering airport transportation would be a great perk for this property. Thank you for a fabulous time...

title: “Good hotel for visiting Beverly Hills”
text:
Our family of 4, including two small children, stayed here June 27-29 as part of our west coast vacation. Located at Pico and Beverly, this hotel is right beside Beverly Hills. We found this to be a convenient location to visit Beverly Hills, Bel Air, Santa Monica, Universal and Hollywood. The area feels fairly safe. 
We had a clean, modern 2 bedroom suite with a living room, kitchen, and two bathrooms. It was reasonably priced for such a large suite with a complimentary breakfast. We faced the interior of the hotel where there was no view, but we preferred this since we had no street
noise at all. (In LA you won't spend much time in the suite anyways if you are a tourist). The valet parking was easy (no delays). 
There is a Ralph's grocery store within a short walking distance.
Overall, we were pleased with this hotel.

title: “Frequent Visitor”
text:
I'm frequently in Dallas on business or with the family and we either stay here or at the Doubletree in Richardson (depending on the price). The last time I was there (last week in June) I was able to get a king size room for only $80. Not bad for a nice room in a good hotel in a great location.
And for the location it just can't be beat -- just across 75 from Northpark Mall (best shopping in Dallas) and just off Greenville to the east which is a major road that allows you access to numerous restaurants and clubs. And there's an In-N-Out within walking distance(just south of the hotel property past the adjacent office building that it shares a parking lot with, then cross the street and walk past the office bldg on the corner).
Friendly staff and we've never had any problems. Only complaint is, as mentioned elsewhere, the lack of free wifi. But I noticed on this visit that - at least my room - had access to a free AT&T hotspot. So even though I would have to pay for the Hilton wifi - the AT&T was free. 
Definitely watch the price though. I believe this is a prime hotel for business travelers and the price can reflect that. I've seen it at prices that are way too high for what you get - but that's usually during the week (right now prices start at $170 for a week night if you check the website). Weekend stays are usually more affordable. As much as I enjoy this hotel and its location - $170 before tax is too much. That's why I checked "average" for the value. At $80 it's great - at $170 it's overpriced.

title: “Basic hotel within walking distance to harbor and sights”
text: This is a no-frills Holiday Inn that has obviously seen better days. Certainly could do with some renovations but room was pretty comfortable but small bathroom. Walls were thin in that I could hear people in the next room, fortunately, they kept quiet but I could certainly see possible problems with "noisy neighbors."The staff I met at the desk were incredibly welcoming. Breakfast not too great, would recommend finding another place nearby. Easy walking distance to many tourist attractions including the harbor. Would probably try a more upscale hotel next time I am in Boston.

title: “Sound barrier. Would have been nice to have had it this weekend.”
text:
The lobby was absolutely beautiful. And as we got a suite, our room was actually 2 rooms that were very spacious. HOWEVER, our room was next to outdoor speakers that played music 24/7! Both my husband and I would wake up at odd hours because we could STILL hear this music playing. It was almost like being next door to a nightclub that never shut down. Plus, we could hear the traffic too well, especially as we were on the top floor!
And then there were the neighbors. Okay, couples will do what they do in a bedroom. To put this delicately, what happens in the bedroom should stay in the bedroom and not wake up the neighbors! (In their defense, they really were trying to stay quiet -- my husband slept right through everything -- but if there had been ANY sound barrier between our rooms, I wouldn't be talking about it)
Pros: lobby, location, actual bed, staff, historical-ness of the building
Cons: NOISE, decor so feel less dingy (brown carpet, tan walls and ceiling, brown and red furniture. Just way too much brown), smallest refrigerator we'd ever seen, valet cost more than expected ($24.50+tax), TVs need updating, have to pay for Internet in your room unless you have Wyndham by Request (which we did, thankfully)

title: “Wonderful hotel for Couples”
text: My wife and I stayed here as a getaway for the weekend. We were pleasantly surprised. The staff is extremely friendly and is always willing to help. The hotel is very clean and they provide a wonderful turn down service with a different dessert every night specially prepared by the chef. It can be a little noisy at night but it isn't something that takes away from the charm. The beds and pillows are the most comfortable I have ever had at a hotel. We would definitely stay again.

title: “Great Location, Phenominal Service and a Great Value.”
text: The Hotel is in a really great location near Union Square. Parking is easy in and out with little wait time to get your vehicle. The staff was exceptional especially for San Francisco. The rooms are very nice and they take great care of you.

title: “OK”
text: Very friendly and helpful staff. Parking very expensive. Overall, facilities were clean and nice (nice television in room). However, the light switch in our room was broken and the air vent rattled loudly. Also, the exercise room was way too warm and there was no way for guests to adjust the temperature. Exercise room had two treadmills, recumbent bike, elliptical machine, free weights, and a single television with remote. There was decent food within walking distance.

title: “Graduation”
text: Excelent arrive steady departure. Great breakfast and pool sleep great. I have two litte chihuahua walk around block excellent area quiet and secure

title: “THe SoHo Grand is the best place to stay in NYC”
text: Since January of this year I have stayed at the SoHo Grand 5 times and everytime has been incredible. I have traveled to NYC many years and have stayed at many different hotels, mainly in mid-town but I will never stay anywhere else from now on. The service is excellent in every area of the hotel. The doormen are so friendly ( even remembering you from previous stays), the front desk is extremely professional yet personal. The rooms are so beautiful and comfortable. The view is incredible. THe concieres are absolutely the very best. Every restaurant they have recommended has been excellent, ones that I go back to again. If you need show tickets, they can get them. They really help with anything you need. I have traveled extensively and I can truly say that this is my favorite hotel. I will not stay anywhere else in NYC and tell all my friends about it. The SoHO Grand knows what customer service is all about and everyone of their employees buys into it. You can tell when a place is managed well by the pride that their employees display and every employee in that hotel is proud of their job and works very hard to make every aspect of your stay perfect.

title: “Excellent value perfect location.”
text: Price won't be beaten really good for Midtown Manhattan. The room was very basic but was bigger then I'd imagined and very clean. Shared bathrooms but they were spotless and always free. Just 10 minutes away from Penn station it is very easy to get to from JFK. Location really couldn't have been better 5 minutes from both the Empire State Building and Times square with the Rockefeller building, MSG and Grand Central easy walking distance. 5th avenue is also at your doorstep. Street noise was loud at night but I'd imagine most midtown hotels would be. Service wasn't exactly helpful not rude or anything just not very friendly. Couldn't open our window and room got quiet warm at night but there was AC so not too bad. If like us your hotel is simply for a few hours sleep its the perfect place.

title: “Very Classy Hotel - Brilliant Location”
text:
Very classy hotel in the middle of Mid-Town. 2 minute walk to 5th ave and 5 minute walk to Time Sq, literally right bang in the middle of all the action.
Rooms quite large for New York and well appointed
Everywhere has a classy feel but be aware such class doesnt come cheap, food and drink in the hotel are quite expensive ($8 dollars for a beer etc)
You get what you pay for however and it really is a very good hotel

title: “If you want to be near Harvard this is the place.....”
text: On my last visit to Harvard Business School, I had the opportunity to stay at the Double Tree by Hilton, like all Hilton hotels this could not be different, their rooms, common areas throughout the hotel in general is quite nice. But what for me was the best thing is its location, if your destination is to be at Harvard or visit Harvard Business School this is the hotel. You can reach HBS facilities practically walk if you like walking, driving these to almost less than 5 minutes, you have a great view of the river as well as near the hotel amenities like a Starbucks, a supermarket quite nice, definitely that is the place if you go to register or visit HBS. I hope you enjoy your stay and visit the beautiful city of Boston ....

title: “Perfect Hotel”
text:
The Drury Plaza Hotel was our home for two days while visiting San Antonio. The hotel is on the Riverwalk and is in a perfect location for Riverwalk activities. Just a walk to the basement of the hotel, a turn to the right and we were at the heart of the Riverwalk. Everyone, from the front desk to housekeeping was friendly and helpful. The room was of average size but very comfortable as was the bed. Parking was valet only and at a cost of $19 a day, but I think it was worth it because my automobile was secure and the valets were very helpful in giving us directions to our destinations. 
 The breakfast was very satisfying as was the 5:30 kickback. What other hotel gives you 3 alcoholic drinks and heavy h'orderves (baked potatoes, mac and cheese, vegtable trays, hot dogs, etc.) every afternoon? 
 The hotel lobby was very spacious and beautiful with stained glass and even an antique car. I am very pleased that I chose this hotel for our visit to San Antonio. I would definitely stay there again and would highly recommend it to my friends.

title: “Just O.K.”
text:
We stayed at this hotel during an overnight visit to colleges for my daughter. The location was fine and I liked having parking onsite. However, our first impressions of the hotel were not great. The night desk clerk who checked us in was professional but not very friendly. The hallways to the elevator are dark and narrow. If they were recently painted I couldn't tell. I would hate to see what they looked like before. The room was average. It was clean enough but looked dated and worn. The tub felt like it had a tub surround on it (like a bubble underneath) and had burn marks on the edge. The air conditioning fan is very loud, so much that when it goes off it wakes you up to complete silence or outside noise. The flat screen tv was very nice. The best part of the hotel is Ron the morning desk clerk! He was friendly and very helpful. He even printed us a map and gave us directions to the colleges. Without him I probably would have rated the hotel "poor" but, we left smiling because of him. 
If my daughter decides to go to college in Boston I will look around for a different hotel to try. I didn't feel that this one was worth the cost.

title: “Perfect Hotel for NYC Stay”
text:
I stayed in the Hilton Garden Inn on West 35th Street with my cousin for 5 nights and I don't think we could've chosen a better hotel for our stay. The reason for booking this hotel was because of the option to have 2 double bed in a room which seems to be a bit of a rarity in New York City. 
The location could not have been better for exploring Manhattan Island and the surrounding boroughs. There is a subway right outside the hotel which we used for getting all around the island as well as Brooklyn and a mall trip in Queens (The Queens mall is pretty sweet if you want all your shops in one location, and it's a fair bit cheaper than Manhattan). Although the subway was useful when we were a bit tired, we were able to walk to most of the big attractions easily. The walk up to Times sqaure took about 10 to 15 mins and further up to Central Park another 15 (Top of the Rock is a definite must do on a clear day).
The room was pretty big and we had an awesome view of the Empire State Building. It had a 32 inch HD TV with quite a few HD Channels. It had a coffee machine and complimentary wireless internet access which was very useful. If you need to print boarding passes or anything there is a business centre with a laserjet printer. The shower was insanely good and complimentary Neutragena shower products were replaced daily. The beds were comfortable and the hotel was generally pretty quiet. Previous reviews mention problems with the frequency of the lifts, we personally didn't encounter any problems and we were on the 9th foor. The hotel bar was pretty cool, we met some interesting characters there. The drinks were a bit on the pricey side though.
We had an evening flight back home and the hotel were very accommodating by giving us a late 2pm checkout and a secure location to store our luggage whilst we enjoyed the last few hours before we departed to the airport. Fredrick was kind enough to book us a private hire taxi car to the airport which had a fixed rate so the meter wasn't ticking up in the heavy NYC traffic - I would definitely recommend this as it makes the journey back less stressful and the cars are very comfortable. 
Overall it's a sweet hotel and would definitely go back to stay there again.

title: “Urbane urban experience”
text:
I've been to hotels with more dramatic entries, faster elevators, larger rooms, more stylish restaurants -- but the LA Intercontinental combines all these elements into a beautifully balanced hotel that has few equals. I probably should give it 5 stars, but I'm taking off 1 star due to the location -- which (in typical LA fashion) requires a drive to get to anything.
The hotel itself was wonderful. Excellent efficient entry and registration. Very helpful staff. Very clean and luxurious rooms. What more can you ask for? Oh yeah, casually elegant restaurant.
The only downside was some weird plumbing failure in the outdoor hot tub. That disappointed the teenagers. Let them suffer.
The Intercontinental is an oasis of civility in a sea of barbarism.
By the way: we were able to afford 2 rooms for a weekend due to a stellar deal on that certain unnamed internet site that allows you to bid your price. Bid low.

title: “Unbelievably comfortable sleep”
text: The Omni Parker House was a super choice for my recent stay in Boston. Unfortunately I only stayed one night though and could have stayed forever. The feeling of history that surrounds you in this hotel is unmatched. The check in was quick and easy, I was given a call on my cell phone when my room was ready and was upgraded to a deluxe room on the top floor. My room overlooked the graveyard at the Kings Chapel. It was great. The room was pretty small with the 2 beds, but speaking of the beds, oh my, I have never slept in a bed that was so comfortable. My friend could not stop talking about the bed, the sheets, and how extremely comfortable of a night sleep it was. I got a surprise knock on the door and recieved two pieces of the famous Boston Cream Pie and two bottles of water and a book about the history of the hotel all served on a beautiful tray. The treat was so unexpected and delicious. This hotel is so conveniently located to all of the historical downtown freedom trail sites and is a two minute walk to the T station. Breakfast the next morning at Parkers was nice, expensive, but very tasty and lovely. Everyone in Boston was so nice, and helpful. I definitely want to get back here to stay again soon.

title: “Great hotel - would return”
text: This is a jewel of a hotel. We were very impressed with the staff and service, the size of the room and bathroom - both were larger than expected. The sole caveat was that the bed was less firm than we are used to. (We will ask for a firmer one next time.) I was also surprised that the local phone charge was $2.28 and that the wifi charge was fairly high (I didn't use it but used the free computer in the business center instead). However, all that noted, I have stayed at several hotels in Manhattan and so far OTA is the best value. It is in a great area. Two restaurants around the corner, the Manhattan Diner and the Fatty Crab, were also excellent.

title: “Highly Recommended”
text: Beautiful hotel, expansive rooms, lovely views, amazing staff and excellent food! Loved that Universal Studios/City Walk is just around the corner, too. Location, location, location, this is definitely my hotel choice if I plan to visit LA again.

title: “Hotel Plaza Athenee...So central”
text:
The place is perfect, near Maddison and Park, outstanding the room is comfortable, quiet and clean The first choice in NYC Walking distance to most things Central Park, MOmA, Gugenheim, 
Intimate bar and beautiful restaurant.

title: “Good not Great, sorry but rooms not 4 star”
text:
We booked throught bidding Priceline about a year ago so we had a great rate of $199/night plus taxes which may account for the room we had....but if your hotel is claiming 4 star should not all the rooms measure up to that rating????? I was prepared for a small room but did anticipate "charming"..as you might expect in Europe. The staff are excellent, the lobby is lovely however the regular rooms (I am sure the suites are much better) were "just basic" bed was good, room was clean but the room was so small (and we have travelled Europe extensively and this is the smallest room we have ever had) the bathroom was tiny and old, they do have free coffee in the lobby BUT no coffee maker in the room, no bar fridge in the room and you need to get ice from room service. Due to a last minute change in plans our NYC portion of our trip was 4 nights not 3 which were booked with the Algonquin..so I had to scramble to get a room for our additional night. The Algonquin only had rooms avail starting at $450 so did a priceline bid expanding our search to other areas of NYC so our first night in the city was in the Empire State Building area at the Affinia Dumont hotel which was fabulous (their lobby was small) BUT huge newly renovated beautiful room, separate kitchen, loved the location again through priceline last minute at $299 + taxes and worth every penny. Hindsight ...we would gladly pd the higher price for all 4 nights at the Affinia.
Suggestion to the Algonquin...when your guests are assigned to those tiny rooms I would suggest you throw in some comps like breakfast or a drink at the bar as goodwill to offset the likely disappointment in the room size.

title: “Friendly and Convenient”
text: I was a resident of San Francisco from 1992 until I moved to Seattle in 2006. I stayed at Beck's quite a few times when visiting San Francisco since my move. Staff has always been friendly, rooms clean. Very short walking distance to many restaurants, shops, bars, MUNI and beyond. As another reviewer stated, deluxe rooms are a bit more spacious, but I have never been disappointed with any room I've stayed in here. If you are a AAA member, be sure to let them know when booking!

title: “great hotel; great price”
text: this hotel was very nice. one of my favorite things was there was a pool on the roof! i mean come on, thats awesome! the room was very nice, and the hotel was very clean. it is right on the riverwalk, so you are in walking distance over everything cool and like a block away from the alamo. the staff was very nice and the restaurants in the area were very tasty and reasonably priced.. i have nothing but good things to say about this hotel.

title: “Went through all my things and the worst hotel ever!”
text:
Never stay here if you want your privacy and belongs to be safe.
We went to lunch and came back to have been locked out of our room.
Someone had come into our room, packed all our clothes in a crumbled mess, and touched our clean underware to place our things into another room with duck tape on the windows, and no tub or upgrades, and already had another family checked into our nicer room without our knowledge or permission.
We felt completed disregarded and disrespected for having a discounted room rate.
We were only entitled to the worst room in house since they were sold out, and refered to some inkeepers law, saying they did it all the time.
We felt completely violated that they some stranger had handled all our new purchases, and clean clothes, and threw our shoes in bags with our night clothes.
Don't ever stay here!!!!!
It was a nightmare, and they talked down to us, and were rude and horrible!
The rooms are dirty, and moldy, and the shower had water above our ankles.
Don't let the new lobby fool you.
They are young and arogant, and completely unprofessional in their services.
I am horrified by the experience, and my handbag was still in the room with the new occupants enjoying our view and room.
If it is the last hotel in Chicago, go north, but don't stay in this scary place!
Just beware.

title: “Forget the luxury get into the location, location, location”
text:
The hotel was very busy yet the check in staff did their utmost to get us a great room.
They were helpful throughout our stay, we had delayed luggage - thanks KLM!
Situated in a pretty perfect location on E Wacker Drive, with a stunning view every time you exit the building.
If you're not in town to go galavanting around as a tourist then there's a breakfast place and bar right next door. 
If you are after luxurious fixtures and fittings with large rooms, then sorry this isnt for you.
However if you need a functional place to sleep with some old worlde charms thrown in then you cant go far wrong here.
Our room had a fridge with icebox, a microwave and a flat screen TV.
Rooms up in the tower section were nice and quiet, but one of our windows was stuck very slightly open so you could hear the sirens late at night.
That may pose a chilly draught during winter time.
Shower was fine, not a NYC power drench but it did the job perfectly well.
Our only gripe was having to wait a while at busy times to get one of the 2 elevators servicg floors highter than 10th.
Its a 5 minute walk to/from the Blue line 'L' and if you have hand luggage then save yourself a cab fare and get the train from O'Hare.
We had full set of luggage and it was still no hassle getting the 'L' train back to the airport.
There are bus stops right outside to the museums and its an easy walk round the corner to get buses up and down Michigan Avenue to the other attractions.
We bought a 7 day CTA pass for our 5 night stay and it easily paid for itself.
I would have not qualms in staying here again if visiting Chicago.

title: “DO NOT GO THERE!”
text:
Upon arriving at the Renoir it did not seem so bad but after spending a total of five minutes in my room and then attending a show that evening when I came back to the hotel I was accused of smoking in my room (which I had not been in for more than a couple of minutes the entire evening). I asked the manager to enter my room and check it when he let me back in and he refused. Neither my husband nor myself have ever smoked and I am in my 40's and am not a child (and didn't expect to be treated like one but was).
I asked upon checking out the next morning for a receipt of any charges and was told that because I filed a dispute on the smoking there would be no charges, a few days later a charge appeared on my credit card for $167.10.
Between the transients outside screaming, breaking bottles and fighting with each other and the plumbing and hot water pipes banging against the walls it was impossible to get any sleep whatsoever in a second floor room.
This was the absolute worst hotel experience of my life and unfortunately it was the second night of our honeymoon. They also charged us for a third person in our room when there wasn't one. I don't know how they will prove these charges but it will be amusing to find out.
If you have any choice in the matter, do not stay at the Renoir, no ventilation or air conditioning, so you HAVE to keep the windows open.
Sincerely,
A very dissatisfied but honest Customer who will never return to the Renoir

title: “Excellent except for the construction work going on.”
text: Stayed at the Century Plaza for 3 nights. Got a room on the PH (Penthouse) level at the rear of the building with good views. Was a little surprised to get a good room so easily, as we got it cheap on Travelocity, we just assumed they were quiet. Found reason next morning when the building site came alive around 6am. No mention of it when booking or from the hotel reception when checking in. We didn't complain (although we did mention it at checkout) as we were due to be up early the next 2 mornings anyway, but it would have been nice to know. The location of the hotel is fairy good considering you are basically in a financial are with a few office towers. The Westfield shopping centre, which was across the street, was ideal to grab some food and had a Macys and a Bloomingdales amongst others. It was a 15-20 minute walk to Rodeo Drive and the area seemed safe enough. Also, a bus form the Big Blue Bus Company leaves from around the corner to go to Santa Monica. It takes about 30-40 mins dependant on traffic but only cost 75c per person one way, an absolute bargain! You can get the details and location of the bus stop from the concierge who we found most helpful as we had no car and needed to know where we could get to easily on foot or with public transport. Overall an enjoyable stay, but if I was going back to LA, I would probably stay somewhere else just to compare the location.

title: “Great for Graduation Get Together”
text:
We needed a place to stay to house us, my elderly parents and my sister and her one year old. We were so happy with the Marmara. The three room suite, while spare, was clean, the beds were comfortable and our views of the triboro bridge and the empire state building every night were great. 
We loved being able to have breakfast in the apartment and for everyone to be able to take NYC at their own pace.
The staff was very helpful and attentive. We had an "at home" party immediately following graduation and they provided champagne glasses for everyone. Other than a glitch with their credit card machine on check out, everything was great. There is no attached parking to the hotel and nearby parking is pricey - to be expected on the upper east side.

title: “Helpful staff, vintage decor, no view”
text: Every interaction with the hotel staff was first rate during our 4 day stay. Decor is adequate, and if you like older hotels you will enjoy this one. Our window had no view at all, just a light shaft, pipes, walls, but otherwise no complaints. Fridge but no microwave, no more electrical outlets than you'd expect in an older property, but adequate for our needs. Location near Union Square is good. Front desk was efficient for both checkin and checkout, and when I accidently left some items in the room and returned for them a few hours later, the housekeeping manager was there in a short time with them neatly packed in a ziplock bag. Everyone was friendly ahd helpful, and we would definitely stay here again.

title: “A good park/stay/fly hotel.”
text: Very reasonable, older style motel two story outside entrances but clean, quiet and close to the airport. Contact direct to save money next time rather than booking through a service like Stay123. Bed was very comfortable, no flat screen tv but what was there was adequate. Hotel manager was very efficient and conscientious. I would stay there again as it beats airport parking just next door by $30.00 for the same two week period and your hotel is basically free.

title: “Great Location, Service and Price”
text: I enjoyed the TownPlace as it is close to everything in a short walk (River Walk, Alamo, etc.) but is not on the river where at night it can be busy and noisy. Best of both worlds for us. Spacious suite rooms, newer property and the staff was super! I have stayed at this hotel twice and it has been great both times. The breakfast is better than most of the ones I have had at this price range. No complaints on this hotel, just good times.

title: “Great Location, Beautiful Hotel, Great Pool, Awful Coffee!”
text: Stayed for 3 nights in October 2010. Arrived at 11am but we were allowed to check in early which was great. The suite was small but we were not intending to spend a great deal of time in the room so it didn't really matter. Plus points were gorgeous rooftop pool, TWO rooftop hot tubs, great location directly on the riverwalk. helpful staff. The hotel is beautiful and spacious inside and provides good service. The only negatives were small towels in the bathroom and only two for four people, the breakfast queues were enormous although we were staying at the same time as around 5 million line dancers so the hotel was full. The content of the breakfast was also limited although when you are trying to cater for that many people I am not surprised. And the coffee was atrocious! I had to go to Starbucks around the corner immediately every morning. I didnt make it to the evening reception for free drinks and snacks as we were out all 3 nights so cannot comment. All in all a good stay.

title: “Great spot to barnstorm Manhattan from!”
text:
We spent Thanksgiving weekend in NYC with the family, and selected The London as our base of operations. We had stayed there 'back in the day' when this was the Righa Royal Hotel, and this was our first time back in the new incarnation. The London has a touch of swank to it in a still fantastic location. Located off Broadway on 54th St. the hotel is central to all that makes NYC special. Rock Center, 5th Ave, Radio City, Broadway and Central Park surround you, just blocks away.
The rooms are very spacious for the price, and the service is enough to let you know you are in a good hotel, but not over the top. The lobby bar/restaurant have a good vibe to them.
