The Gordon Ramsey restaurant is top notch with a formal dining room and a more casual setup, Maze. There is a unique Chef's Table inside the kitchen that sits feet from the Executive Chef so you get the front row in a very unique show.
If you are on the upper floors you get a fantastic view of Central Park and the river. Lower floors not so much. Life is good at The London, and if you are on a romantic getaway, or bringing along the whole family travel team, this is a place for comfort, space and superb location in one of the worlds great cities.

title: “Friendly, reasonably-priced family run motel.”
text: We stayed at this motel with our 8month old child. We arrived in the evening and the hosts were very helpful in getting us and the baby settled. They semed a very nice, friendly and helpful family. We thought the rooms were very clean with all you would need and expect from a motel. Pricing was reasonable for the area, which is generally expensive. I have never left a hotel/motel review before but felt motivated to because I was pleasantly surprised.

title: “Great location, very nice hotel”
text:
Recently took my two teenage boys to visit their college-attending sister in San Francisco. Chose the Argonaut for the location and because booking a suite at the Argonaut was a better value (it seemed) than booking two rooms at other, downtown hotels. I was very happy with the choice. Great location at the cable car turnaround. An easy and very fun cable car ride into downtown, easy walk to Pier 33 for the fun tour of Alcatraz. A fairly easy walk to North Beach and other great locations for dining. 
The room was very spacious with a great bathroom and flat screen TVs. Deep bathtub with jacuzzi jets. Really nice decor. Some find it kitschy, but I found it warm and inviting and a nice change from the neutral, bland business hotels. Great art on the walls. 
Service was good, although like others I noted the concierge service was a little spotty. Front desk, front door, and bell service were all excellent and friendly. 
I chose a non-view suite, but in fact we had a nice view of Alcatraz and the Bay, even on the 2nd floor. 
A few downsides...the pull-out sofa bed was not comfortable for the boys, but our king bed was very comfortable. Walls are very thin and the water pipes and some other sounds are very loud. 
All in all, one of the best choices in and around downtown San Francisco. I would definitely stay again.

title: “Better choices elsewhere”
text: Our family spent one night here on an overnight shopping trip. It's very conveniently located to the highway, Southcenter mall and airport. The suites are spacious but I felt the couch and carpet in my suite were dirty and could use some updating. We were facing the back of the hotel and were awoken by the LOUD train going by. All the other nearby hotels had free WiFi but here at the Embassy they charged $10. Seriously, in this day when I can get free WiFi from a coffe shop Embassy should reconsider this charge. Also other nearby hotels had free parking but again, Embassy charged $10 for self parking. And when we stayed there it was pretty busy so we had to park in the far lot behind the hotel. I could have parked on the street for free and been closer to the front entrance. We never got to try the breakfast. Our teenaged kids slept in till 9am and unfortunately they shut the breakfast down at 9am sharp on weekdays (even though it was summer holidays). So overall I would rate this hotel below average and not a good value. There are many places to choose from in this area so look elsewhere.

title: “Amazing TRENDY HOTEL”
text: I have stayed at numerous hotels in Hollywood, but this was by far the best hotel in Hollywood. The room was very spacious (800 square feet) compared to about 400 square feet at other hotels. The rooms decor was gorgeous, the TV has REAL cable, great views, nice size balcony with drapes for privacy, in the middle of everything, and very polite / amazing professional staff (bellman, valet, front desk, concierge). This is my new favorite Hotel and will be staying there many more times to come!

title: “Break-In”
text:
We got there on Friday to take my mom to see here sister who was getting ready to pass away. When we got there we did not have enough blankets and I went down and asked for two at 3:00 that afternoon. Went down 2 more times before we finally got two at 9:30 that evening.
We went to the continental breakfast the next morning that consisted of nothing more than toast and some stall donuts that came out of a vending machine and a jar of orange juice that hair all around the inside of the top and when told, the young lady just wiped the top and put it back on the juice.
After the breakfast we went to the hospital only to get back and find our room had been broke in and $700.00 missing. The manager never came to talk to us or reinburst us for our time there. The worst time we ever had in any hotel.
Our bags were locked up.

title: “Beautiful contemporary Tribeca gem”
text: We stayed 3 days at this relatively new Hotel on W Broadway over a weekend in January. The staff was delightful, with easy and courteous check-in. The room was beautiful and spacious, and included a nice view over W Broadway. The flat screen hi-def TV was awesome. The bed was extremely comfortable. We utilized the restaurant in the hotel (French) 3 times, and it was quit good. There are many other dining choices within easy walking distance, as the Hotel is in a busy, lively area. We were all over Manhattan from this location, as we had business in the East Village, and the Upper East Side. We had no trouble finding cabs to and from the Hotel, although the Hotel is right on the subway line.

title: “Hilton Quality on a family budget.”
text: My husband and I recently decided to take our 2 daughter 4 and 6 to Sea World and then onto Corpus Christi to see the ocean. Being from Lawrence, Kansas I had NO idea where to start when it came to looking for location, etc for hotels. I stumbled upon this hotel and after reading the reviews booked it. This hotel was the room quality of many Hiltons we have stayed in, but at a budget level. The shuttle to Sea World was AMAZING, the driver was SOOOO helpful telling us his honest opinions on stuff. There is a 24 hour walmart down the road which is convenient. There isn't much around it as its in a new development, but as a VERY picky wife and mom I 100percent recommend this hotel again. Can't say enough good things!!!!

title: “Filthy and Disgusting, with Rude Employees. DO NOT STAY HERE.”
text: Upon arrival we were advised that there is a high level of break in's to cars, and no security. The hotel is like a maze with several different elevators going to different parts of the hotel, the staff were not friendly or helpful. The lock on our door was broken (part of the handle and fell off when I closed the door to our suite) The suite was old, stuffy, and dirty, with mold in the bathroom. I slept on top of the sheets, in my clothing. The air conditioner did not work. Upon leaving down the stairs (the several-elevator system was to confusing) we discovered shopping bags filled with garbage in the stairwell. Very gross. The price was $150USD... we complained to the manager about our repulsive experience... he took off $5. By far the worst hotel we stayed at on our drive from Seattle to L.A.

title: “Stay Here!!”
text: This is by far THE best Choice Hotel we've ever stayed at! The staff was extremely helpful and courteous, always with a smile. The hotel is modern and up to date with a simple but clean look in the rooms. They even put a welcome note in our room and a sign in the elevator that we were staying with them because I am a choice hotel member (not all hotels do this). We felt like we were a part of an extended family when we were there. The breakfast was also great! And the property is about 5-7 minutes from the inner harbor (shopping, restaurants, etc.) Only thing to keep in mind is that this is more geared towards business travelers. Keep up the great work guys!!

title: “Bugs and terrible housekeeping”
text:
I stayed at this hotel in a room with my sister when we visited the area for my brother's graduation from OSU. The location of the hotel is great but that was basically the only positive. I wasn't expecting the hotel to be fancy but I was expecting it to be clean and I was disappointed. Upon entering our room for the first time my sister found a dirty men's sock on the floor. Needless to say, I assume this means the carpet was not vacuumed between guests and it doesn't seem the housekeeping staff was very thorough. When I pulled back my blankets to get in bed I also found a tiny little worm wiggling around in my sheets. That's right, there was A WORM IN MY BED! I even took a video of it with my cell phone because I was in such disbelief. It was disgusting.
The next day when the housekeeping staff cleaned our room they left the comforters crumpled up on the floor rather than put them back on the beds when they made them and they must have let a gigantic fly in because we had to get rid of one upon returning to the room. At least there were no worms in my bed the second night (that I saw).
Overall I would say this hotel is conveniently located but absolutely disgusting.

title: “Good Value, Better Location, Great Customer Service”
text: In the heart of downtown Denver, walking distance to PAC, Coors Field, 16th Street Mall, Sams (great breakfast and wait staff). Themed floors, comfortable beds, attentive staff, parking on site, AND they gave a room discount when I told them the name of a friend who had referred me to the hotel! We will return in the fall to enjoy the "street life" in the area, a show at the PAC, variety of cuisines...all within easy walking distance of the hotel!

title: “An excellent choice in Midtown near 34th Street and MSG”
text: We had to travel to Manhattan on short notice and found a perfect spot for our 2-night stay at Holiday Inn Midtown on West 31st Street. The entire experience exceeded out expectations, especially for a new hotel. The warm and friendly staff greeted us quickly upon our arrival. Our rooms on a high floor included a spectacular view of the Empire State Building. The King rooms while small, did provide enough space for 2 guests and were nicely appointed with very comfortable beds, linens, etc. A nice HDTV was also in the room. Another good amenity which we took advantage of was the restaurant, where we had a delicious breakfast. It is a very nice Italian restaurant in the evening with an extensive wine list. The hotel also has a business suite area with computers and a printer, plus a private weight and workout room. For the money, and for the convenience of not being above 42nd Street, I'll be sure to come back later this summer when I return to New York City. Highly recommended destination!

title: “OK for short stay only”
text: I stayed at Hotel Angeleno for a short stay in February 2008, as part of a world trip. It was ultra modern and the rooms were very compact – I think it would be difficult to stay here for an extended period of time, due to the lack of space, but for a short stay it is OK. Given that I was on a world trip, there wasn’t nearly enough room for luggage. The rooms contained quite a good mini-bar and even had a small balcony, but were still quite stuffy. There was quite a bit of traffic noise coming through into the room, which wasn’t conducive to sleeping. A lot of the surfaces in the room seemed dusty also. The reception staff were friendly, but the porters were not reliable. I gave one of them a large tip on the basis that he would return in an hour to help us, but he never turned up as promised, which was frustrating as I then had to tip another porter to help us. There is a limited room service menu, which I ordered from on the first night, and I must say that the food was excellent – it was one of the best meal’s I had in the US.

title: “The best location, good value of money and quality, close to Central Park. Nice view from the Windows, which look at 7th Avenu.”
text:
Manager of the Reception Elizabeth is very kind, polite, responsive and very professional. We will recommend this hotel to our friends who are going to New York. 
Regards,
Russian family Miroshnichenko

title: “Great hotel, great location, great value”
text:
Great Location! We walked everywhere and/or took the local transportation. The hotel staff was very nice and very helpful. We loved the feel of the botique hotel. The beds were comfortable and the rooms nice and clean.
We would stay here again and again!
The only problem we encountered was at a breakfast place on Taylor street and cross street O'farrell. I had my wallet taken out of my purse while I was sitting at the table. I was lucky enough to catch the the thief........but the breakfast place (Which was labeled "best breakfast in town, Zagat award" did ABSOLUTELY NOTHING! Didn't offer to call the cops, didn't offer to kick the thief out. ( The thief got scared and got her food to go after I caught her and retrieved my wallet back.) Didn't comp our breakfast.
Other than that, WE LOVE SAN FRAN AND THE SERVICE IN MOST AREAS! THE DONATELLO IS AWESOME!

title: “Very Nice Hotel - On a Side Street”
text:
You usually can't go wrong with a Doubletree hotel (chocolate chip cookies!) ... I wasn't familiar with this one - it's new and a bit off the beaten track, but not hard to find, very new, and very nice! 
It looks like they must have recently torn down an old building, with a fairly small footprint, on this lot, then built this new 27 (+/-) floor hotel. That makes for a very small lobby, but that's not an issue. There is a nice breakfast restaurant behind the lobby. Each floor only has 7 or so rooms on it ... a very vertical hotel!
We checked in very early and our room wasn't ready, but the front desk staff was very friendly and helpful ... the front desk clerk called for a bellman, who took our bags very quickly and stored them in the back. We then went out for a short lunch and returned to check into our room. Another bellman showed us to our room ... very professional and very friendly (made us feel very welcomed!)
Room was very small (though not bad for NYC), but modern, clean, and comfortable!
There is a new underground parking garage (under another hotel) diagonally across 29th street, which has a very reasonable rate for Doubletree guests. Our room on the 21st floor had a view of the Empire State Building.
This isn't the heart of the tourist district, but that's not necessarily a bad thing. It's a short walk to the Empire State Building, the Macy's main store, Madison Square Garden, Time Square, etc. A good location to see mid-town.

title: “Totally Positive Experience”
text:
We stayed Christmas night at the Palace rather than traveling back to Sonoma County where we live. Yes, the rooms are on the small side (this is an old, though totally elegant, hotel) and ours was tastefully furnished. I'd requested, and received, a quiet room, having read about someone's unpleasant experience where their room faced Market Street (this, I agree, might have been unpleasant). Our room was also on the same floor as the pool and spa (also requested and received). We did have room service, a quick pizza and salad before going to a party, and found the service prompt, the food and price also satisfactory. The spa and pool attendant was gracious, as was each employee with whom we came in contact. My only complaint would be that the pool needed additional water - the water level was low. But it was indoors (many California hotel pools have outside pools, if they have them at all) and I thoroughly enjoyed the swim, sauna and jacuzzi.
Yes, the parking is another $40 plus tips. This is the heart of the City, and the parking garage around the corner would have been about the same for the time period we stayed. I must report that ours was a thoroughly positive experience, and we would return to the Palace.

title: “Overpriced and really old and tired”
text: We stayed one night in Mayand paid $160 for the night and were so disappointed, I have stayed in better back packers, the carpets were stained, bedding grey and were not even advised that there were coffee and tea making facilities downstairs.

title: “Great location”
text: Great location in the city. Rooms are slightly dated, but fully functional with everything is in very good condition. Free sweets in your room (yum), free cookies at reception, and free popcorn. The "world famous" pancakes next door are over rated, so don't bother (especially when the Q is huge at the weekend!).

title: “Loved My Home Away From Home”
text: I moved to Homewood after staying at another hotel nearby from co-workers talking of how great this hotel was, and I agree. You wake up every morning with a free breakfast that not only has cereal and bagels, but fruit, potatos, eggs, waffles, etc. In the evenings Mon-Thurs there is a menu of what is served each night from meatball subs, to cajun food, and the best part is free wine and beer! The people are very friendly and the atmosphere is wonderful. I will be returning and will be booking here again!

title: “Great stay!”
text:
My family of four (husband and 11-year old twin girls) stayed at the Nikko for 4 nights. I had booked an Imperial floor room with two queen beds both for the space and the amenities. Had read reviews about tiny rooms, etc. When we arrived we were offered an upgrade to Imperial Executive Suite for an additional $50 a night. We went for it and were glad we did. The Imperial Executive Suite on the 22nd floor had big windows with a nice view, two queen beds in the bedroom, a living area separated by a partial wall, a large bathroom, a half bath, two televisions, hallway... not huge but lots of space. Beds were very comfortable with lovely bedding, bathrooms were great-- Furniture was otherwise a bit tired as was the carpet. But the room was perfect for us and very, very quiet. We slept really well-- not a sound from the hall or from other rooms.
We really like the included buffet breakfast at ANZU --since we had coupons for two people for each day, we had breakfast there twice with all four of us. The other two days we had nice continental breakfast in the Imperial Lounge which was also included. We enjoyed the 5-7pm wine and hors d'ouevres in the Imperial Lounge. And we especially loved the large indoor pool, hot tub and locker rooms with saunas and steam rooms. This, along with free wi-fi was all part of the Imperial package. Our rate wasn't cheap, but nor was it particularly high considering all that was included--We paid around $250 a night. A splurge for us, but worth it particularly given the reviews for other rooms in the hotel. 
We had a great stay!

title: “Spotless”
text:
Everything except Filini was perfect from start to finish... but the rooms, service, bed, bath and sleep were impeccable, so it deserves a 5 regardless. 
Rooms - should be like this in every hotel. Modern, spacious, huge windows, lots of light regardless of which side view you get. Bed, pillows and sleep excellent and above. Spotlessly clean. 
Perfect for business traveller - rooms include good size desk and the network cable - internet speed is really extremely fast as advertised, finally could have a full quality video conference. The concierge could serve to other hotels as an example of how to to the job properly and make guests happy, was on top and above for all the requests. 
Location is also good, right in the loop and short walking distance to everything - N.Michigan, Millennium park, CTA stations, near north/Magnificent mile. In case of rain/snow, it's also connected to the underground Pedway. 
Spend your bucks on a better breakfast though, the expensive buffet at Filini doesn't offer anything special. Also lots of items at the bar in the evening were not available, and the pizza/snacks are very ordinary at best. After one evening I've switched to far better places that Chicago has to offer. Still a perfect hotel though.

title: “Grand old hotel”
text: Stereotypical English like hotel set close to a major shopping area but a 5 minute walk to waterfront. Generously sized rooms full of the mod cons ypu would expect and polite and efficient staff. As a base to explore Seattle this is ideally located. Not spectacular but very nice nonetheless.

title: “I was really impressed with this hotel!”
text: I consider myself a fussy person when it comes to hotels and this is the first time I have taken the time to rate one.. Firstly, we arrived on a Thursday of Easter weekend, at 12:00, and got right into our room. I also noticed the beautiful flowers in the lobby. Secondly, the room was beautifully decorated and bright. At night, we stopped in the bar. It was extremely comfortable and attractive and the service was great. Fresh trays of olive and cheddar crackers were served if you just having a drink. We also sampled a cheese platter. It was delicious. The elevators are recessed and lead into an archway before you reach the rooms, therefore, eliminating that ringing elevator noise. The bedroom is also recessed behind the bathroom which helps eliminate noise. And best of all, the heating system was silent! The white duvet covers are changed for every guest. The bed was soft and comfy. I loved sinking into it. The bathroom was marble with french wood and glass doors leading in. The ammenities were generous and the towels were large. We enjoyed the restaurant for breakfast. I ordered a bowl of mixed berries. It was a generous portion, enough for two. Then I had granola on plain yogurt. It was very good. The French pressed decaf coffee was excellent and didn't make us jumpy afterward. It was a great experience and I wished I could have stayed longer to enjoy the city of Philadelphia!

title: “Great location”
text: After reading some of the reviews, wasn't sure whether to book The Time. In the end there was a good deal on 'Quikbook.com',so we went for it. I booked 2 suites for three nights and confirmed direct with hotel a week before arrival as I hadn't used Quikbook before. On arrival they'd overbooked and only had one suite available, so my son and partner had to have a king room! However they were transferred the next night to their suite and our bill was accordingly reduced. The suites were great -not huge, but that's N.Y. for you. Our suite needed redecorating in places and the sink was cracked,but our son had a great suite newly done with jacuzzi bath( room 1118).The rooms are quiet and the beds are SO comfortable , the bar funky, and the guys on the front door really helpful. However by far the best is the position-just round the corner from Time Sq, and we actually preferred this boutique hotel to the large soulless mega hotels which are around the same price. If you go and don't want to get ripped off ( as you will at any of the establishments around Time Sq/Broadway/7th Ave) head left out of hotel -there's a great deli shop on corner of 8th, and a wide range of less expensive restaurants/cafe's on 9th Ave.Top tips- avoid Carnegies Deli/ Stage Deli- poor food at an exhorbitant price with not so friendly waitresses who complain if they are not given at least 18% tip (18% is the norm throughout N.Y however), do venture down to Little Italy and try the pizzas at Lombardis, go up to the revolving restaurant at Marriott Marquis- and sip a cocktail and view the night lights of Manhattan-amazing. If you are into fine food and the best service ever, try the menu fixe( a la carte is really expensive) at Petrossian (58th St/7th Ave) @ U$ 39 pp and finally, think twice about visiting the Statue of Liberty if you are only in N.Y for a few days- it will take up at least half a day -maybe more-with all the queues, and there are so many better things to see and do.

title: “Great Location in the Heart of Columbus”
text:
Right in the heart of Columbus. Actually stayed here in the winter of 2007 (no option for that) on the way to Illinois. Walked to the arena to catch a Blue Jackets game and then walked to bars & restaurants nearby. Its was $85 a night back then. 
Pro:
- great location
- clean
- decent parking
- decent sized rooms
Con:
- none I can think of
Would definitely recommend.

title: “Very Nice Place”
text:
I'm accustomed to staying in more luxurious hotels for business travel but we have new cost restrictions and this was on of the offerings.
I have to say that I was pleasantly surprised. It's located close to Times Square, but far enough away not to have to pay the TS rate. The lobby is comfy and I was greeted with t smile by all of the staff. I got 2 free bottles of water.
My room was a nice size, clean, comfortable, well lit, flat screen, comfy bed, no noise from the neighbors.
I would definately stay here again and would recommend to others.

title: “Conveniently located business hotel”
text:
Stayed here for two weeks for a business trip to New York
positives
- even if you aren't in New York on business, its location downtown (very close to very many subway lines) makes it a good place to be based out of
- is no frills - which is a good thing (quick checkin/checkout)
- free wifi
- comparatively cheap (compared with, for example, the Andaz Wall Street, which is much fancier)
- rooms are very quiet
negatives
- the deluxe room (with 'kitchenette') has a sink, small fridge, and some plates and silverware. Can't really compare to apartment style hotels like the AKA chain. They really could at the very least provide a toaster (and a bottle opener! seriously, how I am going to open my beers??)
other notes
- never ate the breakfast there (or any food there) can't comment
- really noisy bar next door, but you only really notice that upon walking in the main entrance.

title: “Don't believe the bad reviews!!”
text: As a travel agent as well as a former Property Manager, I do not know why people write such bad reviews. This hotel is gorgeous, airline pilots stay here, has doormen, brass & marble everywhere, 2 huge chandeliers in large lobby. You are greeted by a towering live flower arrangement on a table at least 6 feet tall (including table). The staff is very friendly (as to people who say anyone is rude, my experience has been that if you are rude to them, then perhaps they are going to be rude back to you?). Room large, well decorated, wallpapered with trim insets for contrast, bathroom has large, deep bathtub, pedestal sink, new fixtures/towel bars. Excellent location, 1/2 block to subway.

title: “gym cost of 10 dollars was a bit of a surprise”
text: I was given a 46th floor room with a beautiful view looking west towards New Jersey. Needless to say, being at Times Square has its advantages but also its disadvantages--one has to wend one's way through the jungle of people just to get to the hotel. The service was fine except for when I had checked out and I asked to store one small and light valise for a few hours with a baggage storage person who kept hinting ever more loudly that he would not be in later in the day when I was due back to retrieve my bag ie. he wanted a tip. I thought this was a bit offputting. The only other thing that was a bit offputting was use of the excellent gym nicked me of 10 dollars. I think for over 300 a night, this should be offered to guests or at the very list 'gym use for a fee' should be clearly posted on their Westin internet site. Bed was profoundly comfortable as per usual of Westin hotels.

title: “3rd rate hotel”
text: The hotel/motel was in a seedy neighborhood. The room was not clean. Mildew in the bathroom, a bent paper clip in the commode, a used bandage in the bed, and the floors had not been vacuumed. The sheets were suspect. The staff was neither friendly or helpful and on particular occasion actually rude. The room was non-smoking, but the hallway sported ashtrays in use. The only good thing was the air conditioner did work. It was the only hotel in town for our son's graduation from Air Force Basic Military Training. I found the courage to endure as he had for his training.

title: “Room”
text: The hotel is wounderful right up to 5am, then not so much. I was place on the 3rd floor next to their very noisy nieghbor. It sounded like they were doing road construction right outside my window. Not something a person traveling for 10 days wants to hear every morning.

title: “Great Value NYC Hotel”
text: We spent the weekend at this hotel and had a great experience. The location is great. It is across the street from the UN building. It is close to Grand Central Station and wonderful bus routes. The Hotel staff was friendly and very helpful. The room was clean and the view of the river was grand. I think this hotel provided a weekend stay in NYC at a great value price.

title: “Look at candid travelers photos -this is EXACTLY what you'll find-HORRIBLE”
text: Please, please, don't stay there, even if you're on a budget. There are other budget hotels in that area, I am sure any of them will be better than West Side Inn. Look at the candid traveler's photos on this website - they are so true. This is exactly what you'll find there.... may be even worse. We were on a budget, really on a budget and did not mind staying at a less than good hotel. We were ready to be not very comfortable. We were ready for old and dirty rooms with no service at all ....We were not ready for this!!!! We felt like we didn't save anything, rather lost, cause it was so so so horrible. Don't belive the nice-looking pics of their rooms, I am sure it was taken somewhere else. Jail cells must be better than this.I am sure there are rats there and they've make all those holes in the walls and doors that are painted 10 times over with horrible brown paint. We were constantly worried that someone will come in and mug us or perhaps even kill.....

title: “Nothing Grand about the Hyatt”
text:
Coming from South Africa a supposed “third world country” to the Big Apple, I was more than somewhat unimpressed by several aspects surrounding the Grand Hytatt, a hotel with a supposed four star rating and since my interlude, would not make it my destination of choice in the future, nor would I recommend it to anyone asking me.
In South Africa, hotels of this calibre provide you in the normal course with coffee, tea, (sometimes even hot chocolate) biscuits and/or rusks (all of which is replenished) and more often than not complimentary bottled water and sometimes fruit and/or a bottle of complimentary wine as well as a dressing gown and slippers and a refrigerator in good working order. 
Three couples booked in at your hotel during mid July this year, which does not come cheaply. Only upon request were we provided with coffee and tea, which was similarly not replenished unless on specific request. The fridge in each of the three rooms was not working and the replacement fridge for my room was ceremoniously dumped to one side of the room and not even reinstated from where the other had been removed. I also found your bath towels to be quite skimpy. 
When I brought this to the attention of the manager on duty, I was given vouchers for breakfast for one day for each of the couples, which only included juice (served reluctantly) tea or coffee (had to eventually help ourselves after waiting for approximately 30 minutes and having received no service at all) and one entrée. No fruit, cereal or pastries were included. 
Whilst the room itself and the bed were comfortable and nicely decorated, the room was not cleaned over the whole duration of our 5 day stay. The bed was made, the soap etc replaced, but the room itself or the carpets was not cleaned. Unbeknown to me, I had dropped a wrapping to the side of my bedside pedestal on the first day, and when I was packing to leave noticed that it was still there, not to mention the odd bits of “dirt”, which similarly did not move over that period .
In addition, one of the couples with whom we were spending the weekend left a gift for us at reception. Needless to say we never received it and on enquiry my request was simply dismissed and I informed that “its not on the system” and so intimating that as such it cant possibly be there and there is nothing further than can be done. Several follow ups were made and similarly summarily dismissed.
Over and above this, we booked tickets through your concierge. Whilst it is perfectly acceptable that a nominal fee in respect of services should be charged, it is completely unacceptable that a service of 75% of each ticket was charged and was not brought to our attention or mentioned, when making the necessary enquries/request.

title: “EXCELLENT STAFF AND LOCATION”
text: The staff was excellent!! The location was excellent!! A wonderful breakfast was included. Walking distance to several area attractions. We also used the trolley service that was located one block form us. We saw the broadway hit, Jersey Boys, which was right next door!! Everything was great!!! We had a great stay!!! Beds were very comfortable!!! We are planning to return later this summer.

title: “A little disappointed”
text: Westin's are a favorite hotel choice, but I should have followed my own advice: if you want a quiet room, call the hotel yourself - don't book through Kayak, Priceline, etc. I booked a king bed through Kayak and when we arrived around 8 p.m. the beautiful front lobby desk was empty. A big party was going on in the hotel - DJ cranking the tunes and lots of laughter. After several minutes of waiting, an employee came from the restaurant area asking if we'd been helped. We said no, and by then, a line of 4 other couples had formed to check in. 3 desk clerks popped back out from the rear office, one by one. Check in was slow. They could not find our Preferred Customer number in their records, and sent us to a Queen bed room. We had booked a King. After much concern and searching, they found us a king bed room. We asked "is there a wedding tonight?" and the reply was "is this a weekend? There is a wedding here EVERY weekend." Well. Wished I had known that. At 2 a.m., police came and removed the rowdies from our hallway. So much for a romantic weekend with my hubby. The hotel made amends by buying our breakfast, our in-room movie (which was $17+ ) and our overnight parking. Be aware the walls are thin in this older building and if you are over the party room, you will rock and roll right along with the party until it stops around midnight. You can turn up your TV loud enough to hear it, but you will still hear the event below. The room was nice, bed was Westin comfort but pillows were not. And we were so hoping for those Westing pillows! Looks like the room was updated but the bathroom re-do is so awkward. The huge mirror only has dim back-lighting and was so close to the wall, it covered the only wall plug. We had to fight to jam a hairdryer into the plug. Hopefully, other rooms have their mirrors installed even 1 more inch away. The magnifying mirror is positioned off to the side of the counter and is not useable unless you are very tall and can lean over the very high and long sink counter. It looks good, but isn't efficient. Breakfast was also disappointing. We had a fairly long wait to get seated in the restaurant that was only 1/3 full. Never got water in my glass until the last 10 minutes before we left. The server said "I'll get your water as soon as I get a minute. We are very busy." I asked twice for water, and got the same answer - "as soon as I can get around to it". The situation got worse, as the wedding party came in and filled the remaining seats. The kitchen and wait staff were overwhelmed and literally walking around asking "who ordered the breakfast tacos?". Oh Westin, what happened? I was counting on you for so much more. Especially since our room was $200 for the night. . .

title: “Great business hotel”
text: Easy access, nice rooms, excellent meeting facilities and good food. A very nice business stay. The staff was professional, responsive and friendly. The room was extremely clean and the TV was great! Room service was prompt, friendly and the food was very good. Work out room was nice sized but could use some updates. TVs didn't work on some of the machines.

title: “It Got Better”
text:
We stayed in Cottage 519, one of the few two bedroom cottages that is suitable for two couples. Cost was $230 US/night for four people, very reasonable in San Diego. Our two runners just loved the proximity to the clean beach and grassy park for their long morning runs. The two walkers were also happy with the area although we left it every afternoon for other hiking destinations, shopping, or tours.
We all loved the many choices of places to eat near by (ex. The Mission for breakfast) or a ten minute drive away (ex Hash-a-Go-Go for great breakfasts).
Our cottage was simple, clean, and airy. Our first impression of the area was that it was crazy and we wanted to leave the next day. Turns out that day was the best weekend beach day of their spring break. It calmed down after that and by the end of our time there, we were wishing we could stay one more night. Make your reservations well ahead if you want a two bedroom cottage.
We'd go back to San Diego happily and we'd recommend this place to you as long as you don't want posh.

title: “Lovely stay...will recommend to friends”
text:
We loved staying here. The rooms were nice and had everything we needed. We asked for an lake view and got one without paying extra. Our room was almost on the water and we saw views of beautiful austin skyline. Bed was comfortable.
The cafe was great and open till late. Room service was prompt and delicious. Valet parking also was fast and friendly.
The only small cons were that the location was over the bridge from downtown and the day we checked in it took a while because somebody checking in before us was just taking too long and the self service kiosk didnt work at all...

title: “Great hotel, good location!”
text: Excellent hotel well situated near Times Square. The hotel staff is friendly. Bathroom is very spacious and bed is so comfy. You won't be disappointed. I was offered a complimentary drink upon check in and the concierge staff is always ready to help with questions. Recommended if you want to stay near Times Square.

title: “Nice hotel with great views”
text:
Not a super fan of Lower East Side/Bowery but thought of checking out this hotel.
The studio room was very nice, very clean, very large for NY. 
A living area with TV and views, a desk, and two sofas. Lot's of storage, bathroom with two showers and an Empire State view, bedroom with another TV and more great views.
Views are really amazing. Floor to ceiling windows. Williamsburg bridge on one window, the Empire State on the other.
Could stare out of those huge windows for hours.
Restaurant and room service are really nice, loved the food.
Mini bar is incredibly well stocked.
Turn down service.
A very handy and enormous Whole Foods is on the corner of Chrystie and Huston.
Gemma (the restaurant of the Bowery Hotel) is a short walk away.
Service is very very informal. But fine.
The reception area is odd, with the front desk on the second floor, and the main entrance not always manned.
That didn't feel very safe.
A very good experience over all.

title: “Abysmal treatment at the Crowne Plaza Beverly Hills”
text:
We had two rooms booked at the Crowne Plaza Beverly Hills which were booked by our tour operator approximately six months ago. On arrival in LA we mistakenly went to the Crowne Plaza beside LA airport (our tour operator gave us the wrong address). When we attempted to check in there they directed us to the Crowne Plaza Beverly Hills, but only after phoning them
first to confirm that we were definitely booked in there. 
When we arrived at the Crowne Plaza Beverly Hills at approximately 7.45pm, having driven almost 400 miles that day to get there, we were told that we were on the guest list, but that our rooms were not available, as some other guests had wanted to extend their stay! 
They offered to book us into the Intercontinental Hotel for the night, but then had the audacity to say that we that we should come back down to the Crowne Plaza in the morning for breakfast! (They told us this was only about two blocks away, but in fact it was about six). When we asked if our rooms would definitely be available the following night the receptionist did not seem too sure. He at least seemed a bit embarrassed by the situation, but the other receptionist on duty implied that we should be grateful that we were going to a five star hotel instead. 
What was even more annoying was that shortly afterwards a large party of Russian tourists arrived and checked in, so they obviously did have rooms available.
The upshot of this was that when we arrived at the Intercontinental (in a taxi paid for by the Crowne Plaza, after a struggle) we realised that it was indeed a far superior hotel, and our tour operator was very helpful in arranging for us to stay there for our second night in LA too.

title: “Excellent service and great location!!”
text: We stayed for 5 nights at the Mondrian Soho and had an amazing time!! The rooms were clean with a huge bed and equipped with iPad and free wireless which really helped!! The staff were amazingly polite and helpful - best service I have experienced in NYC! Location is great for shopping in Soho and easy access to the subway. We received a great deal via booking.com. Thank you for making our stay so enjoyable!! T&P

title: “valet/concierge(customer service) was their best asset”
text:
Ok the good list: Valet/concierge and room service customer service was outstanding! Location was ok, not much shopping in close proximity, bars/clubs are a $7 to $10 dollar cab ride one way. The room rate was a fair price. Yep thats the whole good list.
Ok the bad list: I was not informed when I made res that there was a gay/lesbian convention goin on at the hotel, I have nothing against that but when your having a girls weekend away its not ideal! They took the lounge chairs and towels off the pool deck around 11 am to make way for the gay/lesbian party that was going on later which I could hear from my 17th floor room well into the night. The pool was bitter cold, there is no hot tub and half of the day the pool area is in the shade. Nobody came to take food or drink order poolside. When i found somebody and asked for towels and water they acted as if I was a bother. The room had no microwave or useable frige only a very expensive mini bar. The bathroom was extremely small, there are no balconies, the lounge bartenders were RUDE AS HECK! I dont see this being a four star hotel, just 4 star prices! I would not recommend this hotel nor will i ever stay there again.

title: “Busy hotel in heart of Times Square”
text: We stayed here because we had to attend other events in the hotel and friends were also staying here. It had been 12 years since we had stayed here and they seemed to have maintained the hotel and done some improvements. The hotel is absolutely huge and quite busy. The main complaint I have about the hotel is that there is no place where one can escape the crowds and craziness of Times Square except in your room. Everything else about the hotel was excellent. The elevators are extremely efficient as you type in the floor you want on in the hallway and it tells you which elevator to take. There is lots of security and each vehicle is inspected upon entering the hotel area. The staff is friendly and efficient. The food is good and room service also very efficient. There is a lively bar scene at night and the Marquis Theatre is right in the hotel as well. However, we found the View Restaurant a huge disappointment - would not recommend that one. There is a very large workout room as well. It is within easy walking distance to Central Park and the theaters are all right there as well.

title: “Great Value”
text:
I’m a Hilton Honors member and although we don’t travel as often as we’d like to, my wife and I prefer Homewoods over most others. We count on clean rooms, great value, courteous & friendly staff – and Del Mar did not disappoint us.
1. The gentleman (not sure if he was Mgr or Desk Clerk) who made coffee early Saturday & Sunday was very nice, and knew about adding salt to tame the bitterness of an early brew.
2.We didn’t see any hot chocolate packets down by the coffee & tea one night, so the Desk Clerk just said he’d check with the kitchen and send some up to our room – awesome!
3. Plenty of parking up close at no additional fee
4. Breakfast choices were tasty and dinner at Bistro39 next door was excellent
5.Pool and Spa were very clean, easy to operate, and good temperature

title: “Wonderful hotel”
text: I truly enjoyed my experience. The hotel was in a wonderful location, close to shopping! The staff was very pleasant and helpful. The front desk manager was very helpful assisting me with a package issue, valet were super friendly and the pasta dish I had for dinner was delicious! Should I be back in Dallas I will be staying here again.

title: “Clean, comfortable, good bargain”
text: A clean and comfortable double room, in a hotel with a pool, hot breakfast, luggage carts, and other nice touches -- all for about $80. A good deal all around.

title: “The staff was so warm and friendly”
text: We enjoyed our stay at the Alden. The staff was so accomodating and so very friendly. The hotel location was perfect for walking to local restaurants. The rooms were comfortable.

title: “OK - Not Great”
text:
Tucked away in a business park, the hotel is very quiet. One of the few I've stayed at where I didn't need the white noise of the air conditioner. I didn't see any kids at the hotel.
Pet peeve: They put a receipt under the door at night, but it's not zeroed out even though they have a credit card on file... so I still have to stop by the front desk to get a receipt that shows I've paid the bill (important for reimbursement by my travel office). When I stopped by at breakfast to get an updated bill, the desk clerk said she couldn't zero it out until I was ready to check out, because doing so would automatically check me out. Doubtful. I just did it at a Chicago area Hyatt Place within the past several months. Please Hyatt Place - put a receipt under my door that I can walk out with, and not have to wait at the front desk for closure (like most other major hotels do).
The lobby area is nice, and the complementary breakfast is pretty good (standard at Hyatt Places, I assume). They have hot and cold food, as well as lots of fresh fruit. 
Sleeping rooms have a distinctly musty smell - maybe from a hot humid summer? I can vouch for two rooms, since I was first put right beside the ice machine and elevators despite having requested a quiet room. I changed rooms to one farther down the hall - much quieter.
Otherwise, the sleeping rooms are very large, with a separate "living area" which has a huge 42" flat screen TV, a small fridge, a big sectional sofa, and a small work area. Lots of convenient electrical outlets.
However, the wake up call feature on the phones doesn't work (and it's not clear that it doesn't work when you set it at night). Thank goodness for my internal alarm! Also, this hotel (or this chain) doesn't provide body lotion. Bring your own.
I wouldn't mind staying here again - it's close to the airport and our office - but I'm certainly not locked into the idea.

title: “We have been loyal - no more”
text:
Because we have family near this hotel, we have stayed their often over a 15 year period.. Each time we go, something isn't working - this time it was one of the two elevators servicing a large part of the hotel. These are small elevators, and they have to be used to transport laundry and cleaning trucks of the staff and the guests. The elevator that was broken had been broken for over month (see other reviews to confirm this). There was a sign on the door of the elevator that it was temporarily out of order. This is dishonesty. 
We were there on an off week. There were very few cars there when we came back to our room late at night, yet they charged us $10 a night to park, something that should have been waived during this period. They were skimpy with soap (i bar), quality of towels, shower cap,etc. We are sad, as we really looked forward to staying at this unusual place. Housekeeping was not a problem.
The breakfasts that we had in the restaurant were just fine, but the service varied according to waitress. One lovely young lady (whose first name begins with a V) was so nice that we would walk in and ask her which tables she was serving, and we would sit there. 
On the last day, I used the business center to try to print out my boarding passes. I brought them up on the computer, but the printer didn't work. The desk clerk said she would print them out for me, and I asked her for my three dollars back for use of the computer. She said she couldn't do it; I would have to contact the owners. When i said that I wanted to contact the owners, she readily gave me my money. 
This is a great location - the hotel should be razed and a new hotel built there.

title: “Grand old lady!”
text: This is a beautiful, classic hundred-year-old hotel - the apartments (we had two) are spacious, clean and elegant. Don't expect a usual hotel experience as this is self-catering and the rooms are only serviced weekly - this was exactly as we wanted! We did not have a car so cannot comment on parking. The wifi is excellent, no complaints at all! Hotel staff helpful and friendly. Our apartment faced Sutter Street and there was a lot of traffic noise. Easy walk to the shopping centre and the cable car. Highly recommend the Steinhart for a unique experience!

title: “Georgetown is great, the Inn is not”
text:
I payed a lot to stay at this hotel, because it was recommended to me by a business partner. What a partner :-)
The hotel is an old dump. Ugly small rooms, close to no service at all. Expensive internet and noisy schoolkids in the hallways (wonder what they payed). 
In the middle of the night the fire alarm went on, and everybody rushed to the street. Except for the staff. They were nowhere to see, and we ended up going back to the rooms on own initiative. 
Only one good thing to say about this hotel: The breakfast is good.

title: “Very nice hotel - but take a cab!”
text: Stayed at this hotel during an interview, so I was not footing the bill and have no idea of the price. But the room was very nice, comfortable beds, clean bathrooms. My big mistake was that I walked from the Bart train drop-off on Market St - this hotel is straight uphill from that point and I was spent!

title: “Good Location”
text: This hotel is in a good location if you are staying in the area to visit some of the local sites. Hotel is walking distance to Fisherman's Wharf, Pier 39 and Ghirardelli Square. It really is a typical, older hotel in a city. It is a clean hotel with average decor. The bed was very comfortable and the staff is friendly and helpful. It was our anniversary and we had a bottle of champagne waiting in the room. The hotel is pricey, but I am very sure every other in the area is as well. The hotel bar is a bit odd. We stopped there for one last drink and it felt like we were in a breakfast nook. Would we stay here again if in the area....probably.

title: “the heartbreak hotel was fantastic. not a bad word to say about it!”
text: the heartbreak hotel was fantastic. from the day we checked in to the day we checked out the hotel staff couldnt do enough for you. they are so friendly and polite, nothing is to much trouble. the bedroom was big and comfortable and was cleaned every day with freash bedding, towels, flannels and even freash soap. the whole of the hotel and pool was very clean. there was a free breakfast every morning that gave you a wide selection and all you could eat. they also did bar snacks from 3pm till 10pm which were very tasty and affordable. in the evening there is a large screen that shows elvis in concert in the dinning room which proved very entertaining. the hotel is a 2 minute walk from graceland but to be honest there isnt much around that area for you to do other then the fantastic graceland tour. you do need to get a taxi to other places such as beale street about 15 mins away. there is a free shuttle that goes to sun studios, rock and soul musem and beale street every hour from 10am to 6pm and then another free shuttle that will take you just to beale street and the last shuttle returns to the hotel at 10.30pm. becarefull in beale street and keep your purse close to you as people may try and bump in to you to get your purse, local people told us this. but other then that a fantastic place. would definatley recommend this hotel to any one and would stay there again.

title: “A Gem of a Hotel!”
text: This hotel is a real gem! It is in a really good position, is not too large, and the staff are really helpful, and, contrary to what we expected on visiting America for the first time, are not waiting around for tips all the time! The furnishings are superb, rooms comfortable, and the icing on the cake was that every evening between 5 and 6pm they put on wine and beer tasting with nibbles for all the guests in the lounge! You can spend the whole hour or just pop in. Also, if you are not a breakfast person, you can just pick up a complimentary coffee and biscotori in the mornings. We only stayed for three nights, wish it had been longer!

title: “An absolutely cracking bargain!”
text: As budget hotels go this has to be one of the best. The room was very clean and comfortable and the staff were very friendly and helpful. The location provides easy access to major tourist attractions and in addition to the hotel restaurant, there is also good food to be had within easy walking distance. Easy, free parking was also a bonus.

title: “The hotel is very good and should we visit LA again, we will definitely stay here.”
text: My family and I stayed in Embassy Suites Los Angeles International Airport North for four nights from 10th to 14th June 2011. The hotel is very close to the Airport and a complimentary shuttle service is provided to and fro by the hotel. This suite comprises of 2 queen beds and 1 sleeper sofa which can easily accommodate 5 people. The room is equipped with all the necessary amenities such as coffee maker, ironing board, microwave oven, fridge etc. Daily buffet breakfast is served. My family and I had a very pleasant stay. The complimentary shuttle bus from LAX was prompt and even the bus drivers were very courteous and helpful in loading our luggage on to the bus. The front desk staffs are all very helpful. However I have to compliment on one Mr. Michael who is the most outstanding guy among them. Another one is Mr. Ryan who is also very helpful. The breakfast is good but the menu is the same throughout my five days stay. The in house restaurant offers very delicious food. On the whole my family and I enjoyed our stay throughout. Should I visit LA again I will definitely choose this hotel.

title: “great experience!!!”
text:
My Husband and I were on a quick romantic getaway for the weekend and found this hotel absolutely charming!!! We both travel extensivley, domestic and international and were still quite pleased. The rooms are small but have character to spare, the elevator is certainly not swift but who cares its an old hotel that sees value in history. Just relax and enjoy.
Th rooftop porch is beautifull with an amazing view and the resteraunt is pretty good too. Everything you could want is within walking distance as are the trolley and a very good public bus system.
 If the noise is bothersome than you shouldn't be staying in the Gaslamp at all and the hotel has you sign an acknowledgment that you are in an "entertainment zone" so you cant say you weren't warned. 
The staff was wonderful, we couldn't have been happier

title: “Great Location and very friendly and clean”
text: We stayed here because of location, and it was just perfect. It was walking distance to the market places and Finneal Hall (SP?) and close to the subway. Little Italy (north end area) is just a 10 minute walk from here. Would def recommend this hotel. The staff was extremely friendly especially the maids. This was also exceptionally clean hotel. Perfect for a long weekend. A big plus for us was that there is a starbucks in the hotel! Although, you can find one or a dunkin donuts on every street corner

title: “Never will stay here again”
text: We stayed here for three nights in April with our three kids (two adjoining rooms). The rooms were okay but nothing spectacular and it was so noisy being in Times Square it felt like our beds were in the middle of the street. Two nights in a row our 5 year old was up crying at 11:00 pm because it was so noisy with all the traffic noise and sirens that she couldn't sleep. New York was great but will never stay in this hotel again.

title: “The 70's show at good price”
text: The location is good, but there is not that many things in immediate walking distance, mainly some bars and a small grocery store. There are however a city bus stop close by, so this will help you guys on a budget. The rooms and furniture are from the 70's but nothing was broken or dirty. A bit thin walls and windows helped to let some noise in from the busy street outside, didn?t bother me at all, but if you are used to complete silence, it might. Staff was generally helpful, except that they lured us into taking an overpriced and slow airport shuttle instead of a regular cab. We lost $30 and had to get up at 4:30 instead of 5:30. Obviously they were seeing some part of that cash. Contact me at 40ounce at d4rkn3ss dot net.

title: “Little gem in center of San Francisco”
text: I stayed here for a week in late Sept while visiting friends. Having lived in bay area for number years and stayed in SF on business a number of times I was surprised at what a great job had been done of remodelling the old Monticello. Its a beautiful hotel and very close to all amenities - Cable Car, Union Square, China Town and Westfield Shopping Center. The rooms were beautifully decorated and I got interior room which was extremely quiet. There is no gym/swimming pool on site but they have an agreement with a local club to use their facilities for a small fee. The beautiful french toiletries in the shower room were a nice touch as was the in-room robe and free wifi... ! There is a commitment from staff to ensure your stay is a great one and its very noticeable. I have travelled all over the world on business and the attention here was some of the best of a much higher ranked hotels. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “restaurant”
text: Came to visit for a night with my sisters, it was our first sister trip and we were also celebrating for a birthday and graduation so it was very special. We were told that the restaurant closed at 10pm so we got there by 9:30. As we walk in, we confirm the closing time with the bartender and told us they closed at 9. They suggested us to the bar area where they were still serving bar food, which we did not want. Talked to RAUL and asked if we can have a full menu service because we were told the wrong information. Kindly the restaurant opened up the kitchen for us which was so nice of them. RAUL was our server, and I have to say he was an exception to your hotel. He really made us feel special and took great care of us. Not only did the food come instantly, but it was amazingly good! So i want to thank the kitchen staff in the restaurant and especially RAUL! Oh and to top it off, he gave us a complimentary tiramisu cake for the birthday girl, and that cake was one of the best tiramisu cakes i've ever had! Overally, the restaurant was excellent!!!! Also, I wanted to add that Manny the security guard at night was very friendly and helpful to us! We loved our stay, and Westin Riverwalk made our trip very special so THANK YOU!!

title: “Stylish and good value”
text:
This is well located close to Union Square, that clicked a lot of boxes - clean, comfortable, quiet, efficient service. We were given a corner room on the 16th floor. The room was a little smaller than others in the hotel, but with the advantage of a fantastic view up Nob Hill. The room itself was not spacious but perfectly adequate for a couple of nights.
I did have a few irritations ... in 2012 I was really shocked to be charged for WiFi - and at $16 a day its not that far off what I pay for 1 month at home! I'd also expect access to the gym to be complimentary - instead we were charged $20 per room for access. The gym itself was pretty well equipped for a hotel. The pool was big, but very disappointing as it was so shallow as to be unusable for a third of its length.
Finally, the area does attract its fair share of interesting characters at night - something that did make us feel a little uncomfortable when walking back in the evening, although not to the point of feeling threatened. Its a real disappointment that one of the doors to the hotel is closed in at night, and the other (side) entrance was locked on a key card without a member of staff at the door itself. On one night I was "tailgated" by a homeless person who then caused some mischief in Reception. A member of staff at the door would have avoided this.
All in all a very good value hotel - a similar quality to the W but significantly less expensive.

title: “not bad at all!”
text: We stayed one nite for an early Valentine's Day trip. Check in and out was quick and painless, the property is clean and maintained. We missed the happy hour (which is 2 drinks per person, either wine or beer) but we made it to the breakfast, which was fine. Cereal, juices, fruit, yogurt, waffles, sausage,eggs, etc. The pool looked nice, but small and the weather kept us from it. The room(king suite) was very large and looks just like the pictures online. Didnt have much personality, but good nonetheless. Had an elevator and many different vending machines, ice machines, and laundry area. Right on the edge of downtown, close to aquarium, restaurants, etc. Paid close to $200 which was a bit much, but it was clean and everything worked! And parking was free.

title: “Expensive mistake overall”
text: The rooms are very small, but the space is cleverly used and most users only stay a few days. The lack of well lit open spaces for families to gather (as rooms are so small!!) was a problem for us. The only lit area was a very noisy and expensive, posey bar. We had some difficulties with service in trying to buy tickets for nye. Although the management made some efforts to put things right, we probably will use a different hotel next time. Expensive mistake overall.

title: “Very nice stay”
text:
I can't seem to figure our why there are so many negative reviews about this hotel. My one night stay was very pleasant, staying on the preferred floor gave me a nice room with a great bed and bathroom with bath and shower. The furniture was nice and while some part of the walls were cracking in the corners, it had a classy feel to it. The staff was usual DC, burned out from too many foreign guests and snotty tourists. The breakfast was nice and location, for me, was perfect. For tourists, it's a bit far from the metro, but reasonable.
The biggest problem I encountered, and one that is becoming all too prevalent at high-end hotels, was the alarm clock. I prefer the radio to wake me rather than ringing telephones. However, I (being an adult with a PhD, serving as an officer in the US Army Corps of Engineers, knowing how to fly a small airplane, program my VCR, write statistical script, and change my oil) could not figure out how to set the alarm clock. The service staff was of no help and the desk clerk said they could not put instructions in the room (she never explained the reason for this impediment).
Still, I really like this hotel and the gym was excellent. The other reviewers must be used to the Ritz or Four Seasons.

title: “Nice Stay well appointed room”
text: Stayed at this Holiday Inn express for one night while family was in hospital, as the other one we were staying inn near sea world no longer had room for us (also reviewed). I wish we had come here first this HIE was much decorated nicer in the rooms and the rooms seemed to be a little larger. Had a much better smell than the other HIE we stayed in as well. The breakfast was standard hotel breakfast rolls, biscuits, pancakes and eggs. The lady working the buffet was very nice as there was a problem with the pancake machine she worked on it for several minutes so we could have pancakes (and the buffet was closing in just 10-15 min). She could have just blew us off and said that it was not working. The only complaint that my wife had was that we were in rooms facing the interstate and she could hear traffic (i didn't), so if you are a light sleeper ask for something away from the highway.

title: “It was almost home away from home.”
text: We enjoyed our stay at the Union Square hotel so vey much and it was beyond our expectations . All of the staff members where so friendly, cheerful and service minded. Location of your hotel , with the cable car just outside was an easy start to the day and ever so delightful. Bertil and I are looking forward to our next visit already.

title: “An actual review (great time!)”
text:
We stayed there in April 2009 after attending a funeral in PA.
This was my first trip to Manhattan and I am from California. I took my wife (an experienced NY visitor) and 4 others (I rented 3 rooms for a week) 
I seriously spent about 20, maybe 30 hours at night looking for the perfect hotel.
I finally stumbled on the residence Inn near Bryant Park. We were right in the perfect location and it was a fantastic view. The view, that’s why it took me so long searching.
We stayed on the 34th floor (everyone else got stuck in lower rooms, but I was paying)
facing the Empire State Building and Macy's.
The rooms have some older fixtures (80’s or 90’s) but I wanted a spotless place with the view and a lot to do. The third floor is all dedicated to families and long-term business travelers. I really like having the kitchen and I was looking forward to the NY Deli’s. The teens had one room and they stocked up on food and traveled everywhere in NY on the subway (no problems with crime) and the other couple hit the shopping mainly. 
I spent a lot of time looking and found that many top hotels post their own reviews or so it seems and it’s hard to find a genuine review. I could go on about the amenities and the sites nearby the hotel but I will keep it short

title: “Good hotel for families, but not so for business people”
text:
Located in Japan Town in SFO, Hotel Tomo is a European-style hotel. Accommodation is good, walls are painted with Japanese-style cartoons, which is very fanciful and great for the kids. Very clean and restaurant is good as well. Staff is wonderful.
However, if you're looking for a hotel where you can conduct business online in the morning or evening, I'd suggest going some where else. The "fast" speed Internet connection is very intermittent. I couldn't even get onto the network the morning we left.

title: “It is what it is”
text: We booked on Priceline for $122 per night, an absolute bargain for Michigan Avenue on the weekend of the Magnificent Mile Lights Festival. While The Drake is old and I prefer newer hotels the price couldn't be beat. The room was acceptable, the hotel location is fabulous and the staff was great. We were even able to extend our checkout time by one hour without any issues. All in all I would highly recommend The Drake if you're on a budget and want to stay on Michigan Ave. If you prefer newer hotels you should consider something else. For $122 a night booked on priceline I would definitely stay here again! This place has charm and character you won't find in other cookie-cutter hotels.

title: “friendly service but terrible security”
text: i stayed here and my truck was broken into between 1pm and 5 pm. There was grounds keepers and staff everywhere but no one payed any attention to my car alarm as someone walked away with my center console and other items. The SAPD actually told me this is very common for that area!

title: “Great airport location but get some new TV's please and gym equipment”
text:
Great super helpful staff
Standard fare property as to be expected
Restaurant is 3 star out of 5, great staff, food is as expected, typical menu of salmon, wings, steak, etc. Breakfast is decent as well as prices are good.
Rooms are typical brass fixtures and bright colors. 
Gym is awful- an eliptical, a bike, a treadmill, and a half sized nautilus machine. NO DUMBELLS or any free weights. Has a pool and a jacuzzi that look clean. 
Right by airport so not much for food outside of the hotel other than a McDonalds.
TVs are ancient...ancient
Bathroom door is weighted and will not stay open so hot box in bathroom given no fan either.

title: “Rooms were very nice”
text:
Went for a 3 day business conference 
The rooms were clean and well appointed but I didn't spend any time in it.
The staff were helpful in trying to track my lost luggage and all were very polite and pleasant.
They directed me to local shopping to replace my clothes & toiletries and suggested where I could find the best prices.
However if you want to go downtown it is a $35-$40 cab ride each way and the shuttle from the airport took an hour to make it.
My only issue was with the conference room that smelled musty and caused my alergies to go crazy. I was so stuffed up that even with antihistamines and decongestants I could not pop my ears on the plane and it took 10 days to get over it.

title: “Great....again!!”
text: Whils visiting San Fran for the second time, my partner and i used the Del Sol for the second time.It really is a great place to stay.As other posts have said its in a safe area with plenty of resaurants within a short walking distance.The parking is free, a big plus in SF, the breakfast is nothing to write home about but as i have pointed out a short walk puts pay to that. As some posts have also said that it is just a motor lodge, and yes it is, but it has a charm of its own and being a old fifties style motor court only adds to that. We used the hotels recommendation of eating at The Brazen Head. Strange name... but great food!!.We intend to go back in 07 and will be staying here again.

title: “Stay was OK”
text: The Hotel was OK, room was clean and modern, lobby (was a bank) is impressive, limited parking, breakfast was good. Not the safest area to stay, better off closer to the harbor. Staff was good. They refused to give me the 1000 bonus points as advertised when I booked the room, I am not happy with that.

title: “Location Location Location”
text: We spent five days at the Tuscan in March. We found the staff very helpful especially Jose. The one hour reception was very nice. To our surprise, not only did they have wine, but they also had beer, soda and juices with an appetizer. They did have coffee and tea in the morning. I think they should have not stopped serving their biscotti - mistake. I agree with other travelers that the rooms are small, and the street noise is sometimes annoying. All of the hotels on Fishermans Wharf are pricey and so for the money - I would recommend this hotel to a friend. We found it on sale on the internet. The Safeway was great for saving money on food. But also less than a block away was a Subway. There was a little place down the road (Hollywood) that had an exceptional breakfast for under $10,00. The fruit was some of the best I have ever had. We did not have a car, but I did hear complaints not only at this hotel but other hotels as well that it was very expensive. Also - I would advise getting a map on arrival at one of the stores on the Wharf - a lot more informative than the one they give you at the hotel.

title: “Fantastic stay!”
text: We had a great stay at this hotel. The check-in process was quick, and the front desk staff was extremely friendly. The hotel decor is hip and fun, and our room was clean. I loved the Aveda toiletries! We had lunch poolside. It was a bit chilly, but snagged seats next to the fireplace. There was a manager's reception (ie free wine), which was a nice touch. I would definitely stay here again, especially if going to a Padres game. The hotel is only a block away.

title: “Beware”
text: We called the Holiday Inn and booked for Holliday Inn On-the-Bay. Upon arrival, we were advised that our reservations were for Holiday Inn Bayside. Upon arrival at Bayside, we checked in only to find out that the room was very small, smelled musty and the halls were very dark and dreary. The hotel is definately in need of a makeover. We tried to get into On-the-Bay only to be advised that they were booked. They offered to change our reservations to the Downtown location which was unacceptable to us. We ended up staying at one of the competition's locations which was extremely nice and located on the Bay at the Marina. Would not recommend the Holiday Inn Bayside to anyone.

title: “Nice hotel”
text:
We stayed here last september in a superior queen room. The hotel is clean and so was the room. It was very warm in DC at the time and the airco was functioning properly. Also the pool was great and clean. We stayed in the updated part of the hotel so everything seemed fairly new in the room and hallway.
The location is a bit further from where it all happens but definately not too far. 10 mins walk to the white house and national mall. Only downside was a rooftop bar accross the street which was quite noisy in the evening/night.

title: “Beautiful Hotel and location!”
text: Stayed at this property on 02/20/04 for a night. The property is huge and very elegant. The rooms are very comfortable and the views are amazing. Looking forward to returning for a longer stay.

title: “Absolutely loved Hostel Chocolat!!!”
text:
I stayed here for one week in October with my friend, who stayed in the hostel in May 2010, so the hostel was recommended initially by her.
We had no problems checking in, the room was basic, but it had a bed and there were bathroom facilities so that's all I cared about. I found the bed very comfortable, temperature in the room was sometimes a little chilly but I just put more layers on, as I would any where if I was cold.
Internet was reasonably priced, 20 mins for $2. Reception always had change, I'm sure my friend and I were constantly bugging them, but they were all really friendly. Veer was really helpful and friendly, he gave my friend and I a map and highlighted the best shopping areas! Very important for 2 girls!
Most times I was in reception (usually bugging the staff) I also got talking to other people staying in the hostel, everyone seemed social and nice.
The bathrooms were always clean, apart from one day although it was cleaned within an hour, so the cleaners are spot on. The bathroom next to our room developed a leak from the bathroom on the floor above, and this was fixed within 12 hours.
People coming back from nights out/trips could be noisy along the coridoors but I brought ear plugs knowing I'm a light sleeper. That's hardly the fault of the hostel anyway!
My friend and I are about to book for another week in the new year at this hostel. I cannot wait to go back!

title: “smaller boutique hotel...excellent location...great staff”
text: Older hotel and since space is at a "premium" in San Fran, there was no view (unless you consider a brick building a view). Staff was amazing. Upgraded to a suite for an xtra $50 a night. Well worth it. Were at "club level", which included a nice continental breakfast in the morning and a very nice hosted cocktails/beer/wine and yummy home made pizza reception in the evening. Suite was small, but super well kept and clean. Beds very comfy! Would highly recommend. Just a couple blocks from Union Square.

title: “Poor Freeway Motel”
text:
I'm a Marriott fan but this place is very, very noisy with the freeway right next to the property.
I will not get into talking about the food here!
I've stupidly stayed here too many times on business - never again - there is construction work here this weekend - constant pounding - I wasn't informed in advance - every time I mention it to the staff they smile at me like I'm imagining it - the construction workers are clearly demolishing the roof of the adjacent building but the Marriott staff are in total denial - why didn't they announce this?
Renovations must happen but I had multiple hotel options - I'd never have signed up for this.
Proximity to the Galleria is a bonus compared to the over-priced JW Marriott around the corner.
I've stayed there too in an executive room and was woken by water pouring through my window at around 4a.m., dripping loudly onto the window sill - room maid said it's been happening for years.
Wake up Messrs. Marriott - customers have choices - I'm moving to the Hilton tomorrow thankfully - not much better - more expensive - but marginally better

title: “Slash 40% off of the price and i would probably stay again”
text: The hotel lobby, swiiming pool and restaurant were great. The rooms on the other hand were only above average, the sleep quality was the same as what i would get at a best western and the fact that you have to pay extra for parking when i had already paid a rediculously high amount for a standard room. The fact that the hotel is located in downtown seattle is a good reason to pay a little more but paying extra for the extravagant interior decorating made the cost of this hotel not worth the price. Slash 40% off of the price and i would probably stay again, downtown seattle isn't Maui or Dubai.

title: “Great location, not a great hotel.”
text: The good thing is that the hotel is very centrally located. We walked to Central Park every day, ate on restaurnat row as often as we could, and never worried about traffic. When we arrived they were doing a remodel, something the hotel failed to mention when I spoke to them to confirm my reservation. I had to call twice as both times they had not confirmed the room I asked for. We did get the correct room when we checked in. We waited in the elevator lobby for 15 mintues, amidst all the move debris, before the night manager finally recognized we would need the elevator for the 4 bags we were carrying. No offer of help was made to us. The room was swelteringly hot with no way to control that other than opening a window, one of which was not installed properly. The bathroom could barely contain the sink, commode and shower, let alone the addition of 2 peoples toiletries, etc. There was no closet, just a small armoire that did not allow for clothes to hang poperly. The room safe is also in the small armoire, so try and imagine 2 suits, 2 tuxes and various other items of dry cleaning for 2 people fitting in there. We were there for 4 days and the staff never bothered to greet either of us with the exception of check in and check out. Some other good points: the lobby was nicely appointed, the sushi place was good and again the location was perfect for a leisure trip to NY. This is definitely not a corporate/business hotel.

title: “Great hotel for New York two streets from main section!”
