text: Wonderful hotel everything is very clean and free internet which is great. It is only two streets (1 minute walk) from the main Times Square so you are right in the action. Nice free daily breakfast. Rooms are small but it is NY you can't expect much more - great hotel glad i went there.

title: “A plesant stay”
text: A nice and clean hotel near Soho within China Town. Even if beeing in a busy part of town the room was quitet. Staff was friendly and service minded. The room had free internet access that worked well.

title: “Very nice hotel.”
text:
I stayed for a few nights in early December 2011. Overall very pleased with my stay. A lot of reviews claim the rooms are too small. I had the 'Standard Room' and found it a very decent size. I was traveling by myself. Very friendly staff. And it's all about Location Location Location. 2 metro stations right nearby. Excellent choice of restaurants nearby including some nice vegan restaurants. (Try Maoz Vegetatian) it was awesome. 
Pros: very secure (I locked myself out within the first hour and had to goto the desk to tell them. They checked my id which I thought was excellent on their part so that they just wouldn't let anyone in)
Very friendly staff. 
Great location. 
Nice rates. 
Mostly clean
Nice shower
Chilled bottled water
Cons: light dust, a few stray hairs on bed sheet. 
Sub-standard tv. It claims to be hd, but it looks standard to me, kinda small too. 
Very noisy past 6am. Don't plan on sleeping in due to lots of traffic noise, as well as hotel noise. 
Cafe Solei does not deliver just drinks to your room as the in room menu claims that it does, you have to order food too. 
Movies are overpriced. 
So overall, I would certainly recommend this hotel. Especially of its just for one or two travelers. I ride the metro so many times and it's very nice to have close access to the whole city via the metro. Did not eat at the Cafe so I can't rate their food. If I travel to dc again, this will be the first hotel I check out again.

title: “Tripadvisor gem”
text: The Tripadvisor reviews prompted me to book a 2 night stay at this hotel. The outside appearance is misleading - inside: very nice staff, clean rooms, and efficient downtown shuttle. The breakfast ( yes, the waffle iron is a fun touch) is available early 6:30AM and was also good. Definitely recommend.

title: “High quality”
text: I was a little disappointed in wireless internet not being included in the price, but otherwise a ery good stay. I ate at the restaurant and was server by Stephanie, she was very personable and the food was great!

title: “Makes you feel at home, even though your away.”
text: Having stayed at several San Diego hotels, Residence Inn Mission Valley goes to the top of my list. With the courteous Staff (Tawny, Jo, Shamar, Shelby, Courtney, Lindsey, and even the manager Todd), this hotel makes me feel at home. Keep up the good work and I will continue to see you guys monthly.

title: “Like the location”
text: My room was big and comfortable. My view was of the Interstate ramp, but I didn't get a lot of car noise. The free van ride was very nice and the hotel was close to historic sites. Had to pay for a fridge, but I knew that going in. Only problems were that one elevator wasn't working, and morning shift front desk help seemed to take care of loudest customers first.

title: “Ideal quiet location yet central in NYC”
text:
We stayed here in August 2012 as a family of three, so took a double double room, which was great for us. 
Check in 
When it says 16.00 hr. check in, they mean it, no room for manoeuvre for us despite having been travelling for 18 hrs. and being 3 hours early. So we dropped our luggage off, changed in the lobby public toilets and went out for the afternoon. 
Staff
Were efficient and managed transaction with competence and speed but were not “warming” in interface with customers.
Luggage / Airport transfer
We were able to leave our luggage on our last day in luggage store as we were leaving late evening for Newark Airport. We arranged a private car to take us to the airport, which was so easy, via the concierge. $90 for three of us, 40 mins to the airport. We chose to do the return trip this way back as on arrival we had taken the Newark Airport sky train, to main line train to Penn Street station and walked to the hotel (approx.15 - 20mins). It was 85’C that day so we were roasting by the time we got to the hotel.
Room
We were on the 12th floor and had a corner room so had two windows facing different direction allowing us a wider city skyline view and great sunsets!
The blackout blinds were appreciated and were great cutting out the neon city lights at night, but hey, you are in NYC, you would expect lights.
The room was a good size, allowing us all to have room to move around, which I have heard is a blessing and rare in NYC.
The room was lovely and clean, the beds are a good quality and comfy, mattresses hard so good for sore backs too.
The small kitchenette was perfect for us to be able to store water/ juice and snacks and grab a coffee when we needed. 
This was the first time we had been to New York and what a place!
Clean, friendly, feels really safe, busy, open all hours and loads to see and do.
If someone told me I would be buying my daughter jeans at 00.45hrs I would have thought they were mad – nope – I was, as I was buying jeans at that time!
Take comfortable shoes because you will walk miles as it is so flat and easy to find your way around the city.
Food
Carnegies Deli, famous for sandwich sizes – blimey, half a cow in 2 slices of bread!
We had breakfasts at nearby diners, reasonable costs and good value for money.
Baked by Melissa, cupcakes – tiny little cupcakes, less than 50 calories each, self-selection, lovely collection to taste and not feel guilty as you will walk the calories off easily.
Good veggie restaurants
Roxy’s in Times Square. We weren’t too impressed as I am sure the food would have been good, but the service was awful. We got a grunt on arrival to go up the stairs to be seated. We ordered our meal, my daughter and I shared a main course and finished the meal first and whilst my husband was still eating, the waitress took away our dishes, and gave us the dessert menu, hubbie was still mid pizza at this point. When we were asked if we wanted to order a dessert, we said no thank and had the menus removed at speed and the bill slapped on the table – hubbie still mid pizza! No option for having a coffee there then!
If you are into photography there are hundreds of photo opportunities here and a shop worth visiting is B&H – a 4 storey shop of camera equipment. It is worth going to for the experience of seeing green boxes full of camera equipment whizzing over your head on roller rails en route to the check outs.
Location
The hotel is walkable from Times Square – approx. 10mins - we were surprised to see how small it was and that it is triangular! Everywhere else accessible. If you want to be closer to the shops, aim for closer to Grand Central Station
Subway / Metro/ Tube – we heard it referred to as every title!
There is a tube station up on the corner of 50th / 51st which links you to loads of stations so you can get over the city easily. We got the weekly pass and it was certainly good value for money as we used it at least 4 – 6 times daily.
The carriages were clean and well kept, only once were we squashed in the tube, the rest of the time there was plenty of room.
Sights
We went to see loads of iconic sites from the Statue of Liberty, Battery Park, and Empire State Building (Just after 2 people had been killed and 11 shot by police!), Wall Street, Central Park, Soho, Little Italy, Chinatown, Grand Central Station, went to see Wicked at Broadway and of course Ground Zero.
Weather
We were there the e last week in August and it was hot – on average 85’C during the day and down to 19’C night. One episode of rain – well rather drenching than a shower!
Would we go back – yes
Would we recommend the hotel - yes

title: “For NYC, the price was right”
text: Took a chance on a good price on The Pod since I was on a budget and afterall, finding a hotel that may or may not be a dump is pretty risky if you go for the lowest price. To my surprise, my stay was pretty good. Yes, you have to share a bathroom down the hall, so bring some shower shoes and cleanliness was good. I had a single room which was very small. Felt like I was an officer on board a ship with a single room. Nothing fancy. I lucked out and had a room on the inside so street noise wasn't a problem. I'd recommend that you get a room away from the street if at all possible. The front desk and bellhop were courteous. If I could get the same deal as this time, I would do it again

title: “Excellent (budget) hotel”
text:
Stayed for 3 nights at the end of September, had a great stay. Room was large and clean, may be a bit warm in the summer without A/C but wasn't an issue for our stay. The view from the top deck is great.
The best thing about this hotel is the location - it is an under 5 minute walk to the Space Needle and from there the monorail/walk to downtown, or there is a bus stop opposite the hotel with regular buses that go across town. The neighbourhood felt safe and friendly and really close to lots of independent restaurants and bars. Make sure you walk up the hill (it is a bit of a step climb!) into Queen Anne proper for the best views and a beautiful neighbourhood.
I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Best Value Downtown ; Historic building with all the conveniences”
text: The Magnolia Dallas is my first and only choice for downtown lodging. It is conveniently located, and has its own historic charm with all the services travelers are looking for. The Magnolia Dallas offers a great value , meaning what you pay compared to what you get . Hint: ask for a corner room, the views are fabulous! The staff is genuinely appreciative of its guests and go out of their way to ensure you are satisfied with every aspect of the services.

title: “Good location and price”
text: The room was spacious and clean. The beds are comfortable. Walls are thin and internet access is poor. The great service and parking helped compensate for that. Easy access to the 15 and to North San Diego County locations. We wish our stay was longer to appreciate the golf course and swimming pool. Our family will return.

title: “NO SECURITY CAMERAS AND HORRIBLE CUSTOMER SERVICE”
text: There are no security cameras in the hotel at all for GUEST security. We had a man enter our hotel room; we are still unsure how he got in and touch my 12 year old child. This is still under investigation so I won’t say much but what I will say is that front desk hotel staff was very inconsiderate and did not go out of their way to help. Security did come and it was investigated. There was no lock down procedure. There are no cameras to catch anybody. We spent all morning in investigations since 3am when it happened. When I went to hand in my keys I was appalled when I realized that they fully expected me to pay for my stay even after everything we had been thru. And their reasoning was that nothing had been proven yet. Absolutely no excuse for the way we were treated. The front desk staff was very rude and even complained about being called into work for this incident. If you stay at this hotel, check your rooms before your children go in and make sure every door is shut and secured in every way.

title: “A+ Hotel”
text: Great quality! Rooms clean, well furnished- no refrig or microwave BUT they have a complimentary food bar at night complete with beer & wine. What a great amenity! Registration was fast & courteous. I would stay here again & give this place a 4 star thumbs up.

title: “Customer Service”
text:
EVERYONE from the valet parking, to the restaurant service, to the cleaning service were so unbelievably friendly, personable, knowledgeable, and accomadating! It was truly an enjoyable stay- I will recommend to everyone and will definitely choose to stay there again! THANK YOU!
-Andrea
PS- I also want to give a special shout out to Joyce Alvarado and Norma Garcia, servers in the restaurant/lounge area- extremely lovely ladies!

title: “Economical Tourist Hotel in Great Location”
text: The best thing about this hotel is the location, between Central Park and Times Square, close to most of the tourist attractions. You can find some great price deals for this hotel (check a few websites and don't pay the rack rate). However, you get what you pay for: the rooms are basic, don't expect much in terms of amenities, you get charged for wireless (although if you sit across from the concierge desk, you can access free wireless from the Starbucks next door), the bathrooms are tiny and there is no mini-fridge or coffee maker in the room. But if you are out and about during the day and mainly come in to sleep, it is completely adequate.

title: “A Great Hotel in Midtown Manhattan”
text:
Excellent hotel, French style. One of the best I've stayed in Manhattan.
Breakfast is awesome and the waiters extremely attentive.
Toitelleries from L'Occitane and a Bose sound system in the room.
Go for it.

title: “Outstanding Hotel and Staff”
text:
I have stayed at the JW Marriott in Chicago two years in a row for a conference and loved it both times. The location is not far from shopping and sightseeing on foot or by cab. The staff was always attentive but didn't hover. I love the bedding, deep bath tub, adequate room to move around the room, and all of the amenities. The food and beverage for the conference was outstanding. 
The lobby bar had excellent servers, selection and really, really good food. I opted to take my computer down there one night instead of staying holed up in my room and ordering room service. The workout facility in the lower lever was quiet at night, and well used in the early morning but had plenty of quality equipment for the demand. Fresh towels and cold water were constantly refilled. 
Any outstanding hotel in a large city will have a high price, however the JW Marriott earns their fee. I hope my conference is in the same hotel next year.

title: “A Most Convenient Location”
text: In Boston for college tours and visits. Perfect location, very central and close to public transportation, restaurants and shopping. Rooms were comfortable and clean. Poor toiletery amenities though; no shower cap, cotton balls, Qtips etc.

title: “We wanted cheap and conveniently located, and that's what we got!”
text:
The DaVinci is cheap, clean, functional and conveniently located. How much time do you spend in your hotel room in New York City, anyhow? A good choice for travelling with a friend for a few days, probably not a good choice if you're travelling with your family or spouse for a longer stay; there is just no privacy at all. 
The staff were cheerful, if not helpful. They did allow us to leave our bags when we arrived - they have a super late check-in, which I hate. The bags are left unsecured in the hotel lobby without any identifying tags or anything, so I wouldn't leave your laptop or any other valuable item there. 
The "complimentary breakfast" is cold white rolls and plastic-wrapped pastries. And coffee. But if you're travelling cheap and cheerful, a jar of peanut butter and some fruit (there is a fridge in the room) rounds out your breakfast pretty nicely. 
The free wireless worked in the lobby, but our connection dropped constantly in our room.
The rooms are super-small - even for New York - one double bed and we could touch the wall on either side of it. 
This hotel was a quick walk to Central Park and the Ed Sullivan Theater and right near many major attractions and subway lines. 
If you're used to travelling on a budget, this hotel will be a gem. If you normally stay at higher end hotels, you will be very disappointed. No concierge service, the staff did not know the city well.
Our room keys demagnetized every time we left the hotel, which was annoying and probably our fault. They have one tiny elevator which fits three people tops and takes forever - you CAN take the stairs. There is a restaurant on-site that we didn't try.

title: “Average hotel, a bit dated”
text: There is nothing really wrong about this hotel but the decor is s bit dated. There is a strong smell of air fresher in the corridor but I can imagine that this is use to cover up the original bad smell. Staff are nice though

title: “Best hotel in Times Square”
text: The first time I stayed at the W Times Square was 6 years ago, and I had a fantastic stay. I'm happy to report that my return visit was just as great! The hotel's location in Times Square can't be beat, and the hotel does a wonderful job of helping guests escape from the busy NYC streets (love the street level entry). My "Wonderful" room was clean and modern, and included the most comfortable lounge chair ever. The Living Room is a great place to chill and have a drink while listening to great lounge tunes. To top it off, all of the rooms include Bliss products. I have no criticisms, but the rooms could use a fresh coat of paint and some additional soundproofing (I had very noisy neighbors next door). I've stayed at many hotels in Times Square and the W continues to hold the top spot on my list. I look forward to my next visit!

title: “Great Location, Aging rooms”
text:
We stayed in Room 905 for one night 4/26/08. We received a free upgrade to a king room for $299 a night, but our room was not available until after 4pm. Not a huge problem, b/c we left our suitcases with porters and went sightseeing---until the next morning when housekeeping banged on our room door at 8:30am--how is it that the room is not ready until 4pm, but housekeeping starts before 9am?
Room service arrived promptly and the portions were adequate.
The bed was super comfortable and was turned down. We had a king bed, chair with ottoman, flat screen TV, walk in closet, desk and chair. All in all, it was the largest hotel room we have ever had in NYC. The decor is aging, the carpet was worn around the edges and the draperies were 1960s granny style.
All service personnel are polite, welcoming, helpful and sincere. There was a Denzel Washington movie filming at the hotel, which meant that the Park Ave entrance was closed periodically, which made it difficult to hail cabs. The Starbucks is convenient, but a venti nonfat latte cost over $6, almost double the normal fee.
We would probably stay at the Waldorf again due to the size of the room and the location, and would expect superior service but a dated room.

title: “Mixed feelings!”
text:
I had a business trip to New York recently and needed a hotel for one night. As an SPG member I decided to use points and chose to stay at The St Regis. 
On arrival and on check out the front desk staff were very courteous and professional, something I wasn't sure of given this was basically a "freebie". Even though this was a reward booking I was shown to a butler suite. I was attending a business dinner so had my shirt and suit pressed - which was complimentary. Unfortunately they were late back which meant that I was pressed (no pun intended) for time leaving the hotel, however this was really was more a minor inconvenience rather than anything significant. 
What disappointed me about The St Regis was that it smelled! My room had a very strong smell of mildew. It also needs a make-over. The decor is dingy and drab, which combined with the smell left me feeling disappointed - and frankly a little itchy! It's a shame really because the only other St Regis I've stayed in was in Singapore and it was great, which is was why I selected this hotel in the first place.

title: “Basic with nice staff”
text: I made a very last-minute reservation here due to my daughter's illness. I had an email from a previous stay granting me a free night (after no water, no hot water, etc. 2 years previously). The manager had left for the day and the night staff could not promise to honor the offer at the author of the email was no longer an employee of the hotel. I decided to stay anyway. The rooms are very basic but clean. Nice linens with no bedspread (much cleaner, thanks). Lots of hot water. Breakfast included, very basic also; no fruit. The next morning, the manager very nicely granted me a free night - Thanks for the night and thanks for the kindness.

title: “A Taste of the Elegant Old Days”
text: What a wonderful surprise! Traveling on business and the local group I was visiting booked this hotel. It's an old mansion that's been tastefully converted to a hotel. Located in a residential neighborhood not far from downtown, this hotel's recently reopened restaurant has been rated one of the city's 10 best! It's small and very elegant and fabulous without costing an arm and a leg. Now for the sleeping rooms -- no cookie-cutter rooms here. Mine was a nice size with very high ceilings and a 4 poster-canopied bed with all the upscale comforts. No closets -- a wardrobe. The room had cool patterned victorian wallpaper. The bathroom was huge with a footed tub and a double sink. Although it seemed old fashioned it had a good shower and upscale toiletries. I recommend this highly!

title: “pleasantly surprised”
text:
stayed here in march for a business trip. Actually was in jacksonville area during the spring break season. Got a great rate for this property on a weekend stay.
Staff was great. Room was clean and spacious. Access to airport is great--only a mile or less.
Would recommend this hotel for any business traveler in area.

title: “The Orchard Hotel is the Best!! You have to stay at The Orchard Hotel”
text: I just want to share with you the wonderful experience to my 1st visit to San Francisco and The Orchard Hotel. The hotel staff of The Orchard Hotel has given us a memorable vacation that we can't stop talking about. Tony Llanos whom is the Controller of the Hotel has highly recommended that we go and visit the hotel for approximately 1 year now. I am impressed with the condition/cleanliness of the rooms as well as the customer service. The staff all around does express the true meaning of "Customer Serivce". From the time we arrived till we departed the hotel. The staff immediately honored each request that we have with no hesitation. The Hotel sits on a great location, we were out and about everyday of our vacation and were close to everything. I would highly recommend this hotel to my friends and family of Hawaii!! This is the place to go on our vacation. Mahalo to everyone at The Orchard Hotel, we will return with more of our Friends and Family!! A Hui Hou!! (Until we meet again).

title: “Great Location Novatel Hotel”
text: Staying at the Novatel was a pleasant surprise since it was the first time for us in NYC. We stayed there from March 26 to March 29. It has a convenient location and surprisingly quiet despite it's location near Times Square. We went to see Hairspray at the Neil Simon Theater which was so close that the line extended out the door of the hotel so as soon as we exited we were in line. Service was excellent. Only problem, unlike most hotels these days, coffee maker was not provided. We normally have to get a cup of coffee to warm up and get our engine running.

title: “Radisson RB - the Best”
text:
This hotel has the best staff I have ever seen in a hotel. The delivered 5 star service - they were always smiling. The free breakfast is great and so are the drinks in JJ's the hotel restaurant. We found the menu to be extensive and they even made us an item that was not on the menu. 
The policy with the USA Today as mentioned in another rating is that they will credit you .75 cents per day if you do not want the paper. They do not charge anything extra for it. This is their deal with the USA Today.
They also have a brand new incredable fitness center with new cardio equipment and television for each. We truly enjoyed this hotel and will be back!

title: “Great Hotel Near Pike Place”
text: Homewoood Suites is just 10 blocks up hill from Pike Place, easy walk to lots of shopping. Our room/suite was great, separate bedroom, large bathroom, living room, kitchen, 2 flat screen TV's and outdoor patio. Pleasantly surprised by outdoor pool/hot tub and billards room. Hotel offers complimentary breakfast and amazing "welcome reception" from 5PM-7PM daily which includes dinner, beer and wine and cookies...it was fabulous!

title: “Hotel Okay, Customer Service stinks”
text:
We were there on a family vacation. The shuttle service to and from the airport was excellent.
The accommodations were fine and clean.
The problem was the party next door. It started on Sunday night at 9:00 PM. There appeared to be a lot more than 4 people in a room meant for 4 people. Most of the "kids" in the room were teenagers - who had no respect for anyone around them. They had more than one room and were running up and down the halls.
I called security at 11:30 and he came and told them they needed to be quiet, that "someone" reported they were making too much noise. The TV remained extra loud until about midnight. The door to the room kept opening and closing every 15 minutes with kids sneaking in and out. I'm not sure if there was sex or drugs going on, but it was very
suspicious. 
In the morning around 9:00AM, the running around continued, I called the front desk and asked for a 3:00 checkout, since I had gotten virtually no sleep. Ashley, from the front desk said that was not possible. I explained my situation to her, and she could care less.
I asked to speak to the manager, she said he was off today, I asked to speak to someone and she said she was in charge. I told her she seriously lacked customer service skills. 
So, bottom line, don't stay for a family vacation - and don't ask Ashley to listen to you.

title: “Mostly good”
text: Excellent location with easy access to downtown and the North end. Subways are very close which is an additional bonus. You can get there on the blue line for $1.25 from the Airport, and quicker than a cab ride. On the negative side, like most Millenium hotels it is a little shabby; carpet was heavily worn and cheap to begin with, no coffee maker and no tub. Since I got the room discounted on priceline I didn't have super high expectations. Mostly a good experience.

title: “Great Location, nice european-style hotel, friendly staff”
text:
I stayed 4 nights at the Opal, and had a great time in San Francisco.
Good value for my money (reservation through booking. com - apx. 100$ per night including taxes). I was upgraded to the deluxe room, didn't seem as luxus, but maybe it was considered so because it was quiet and remote from the stairs and elevators and facing an inner lane (which I consider as a plus).
Breakfast was very very modest: bread, butter, hard boiled eggs, apples/oranges, juice and cofffee. A good start for the day, but there is self service coffee and tea 24/7, so you can refill..nevertheless, I expected more, and seen better in other hotels in the US for the same rate per night..
The hotel staff was very friendly and helpfull, multilanguage (besides english I heard italian and spanish), thank you Angela,Paula and Alex :)..
Bottom line - very good location, close to most atractions and transportation, good value for the money relative to the high prices in San Francisco, but be prepared for it is not the Hilton or the Drake...

title: “loved it!!”
text: Very comfy. We had a lovely two night stay and enjoyed Memphis very much. The pool and spa here was an added plus.

title: “Eh, not worth it.”
text: It's NOT a 4 start hotel like some places like Hotels.com rate it. The rooms are fine but the hotel is on par with a Hampton Inn or Holiday Inn. In fact, I much prefer the Hampton in just a block or two over. You have to pay $10/day for internet and it goes out every 45 seconds, the lobby is tiny and while the staff is nice they aren't very attentive. There are better hotels with free internet that are cheaper.

title: “Reviews did not match my experience”
text:
Boy, what a dissapointment. After reading the previous reviews, I was quite excited to visit this hotel. However, the three main things I look for all failed. 
1) Water pressure - There is nothing worse than seeing the water dribble out of that shower head. It just takes so much longer to get wet and rinse. This is a basic request that even a Motel 6 can match. 
2) Internet service - What is the point of free wireless internet when the connection is so slow that it is rendered useless? 
3) TV - So, let me get this straight. I am paying $330 for an old TV (no flat screen) with rounded edges? Channels on the guide that don't exist? A clicker that does not work?
Very poor value.

title: “Decent Columbus Hotel”
text: I stayed at this hotel for a work trip. Here are the pros: very nice lobby, bar, friendly staff, decent location. The cons: the food was not great, the room was SUPER tiny, shower in the bathroom needs an update. The location is a bit on the outskirts of town, which might be a plus for you if you prefer a quieter area.

title: “Good Stay at the Marriott”
text: I only have good things to say about this hotel. We stayed for 4 nights in a great 2 room suite. We found the staff to be helpful and always got a cab within 2 minutes of requesting one from the valet. Naturally our breakfast in the hotel restaurant was a little expensive but we expected as much and only ate there once. I would recommend this hotel to anyone planning to go to San Diego.

title: “I had high hopes...”
text:
This was my first stay at a W and will probably be my last. I've always heard how great they are, but now I think the reality is that they appeal to a certain type of traveler.
This hotel is conveniently located on the Orange "L" line and was a straight shot from Midway Airport. Also it was very easy to navigate Chicago and all the sights from here. Fortunately I did not spend that much time in the hotel; I just slept there.
When I walked through the doors into the hotel everything went dark and there was loud music playing, as if I was in a nightclub or bar. Directly in my path were several sofas and various types of seating, with people all around. I could not see a check in area anywhere (it was off to the side in a corner with no directional markings). Once I did find the check in area there was a long line waiting for two men standing behind podiums with spotlights on them. Despite the fact that there were many "workers' milling around and seated at other desks in the lobby, these two were the only ones checking in guests.
My room was small and I expected that. I did not expect to be without some place to hang my clothes, however, so I just hung them on the shower rod. The walls of the room were also thin. I could hear the televisions and conversations of my neighbors quite clearly. Otherwise I have no complaints about the room; it was basic and everything was clean and in working order. 
If you want a trendy/hip hotel with atmosphere in the lobby area then you will like this place. If you want rooms with a bit more space (and a closet), more lighting (even the elevators were dark) and a more traditional feel, then you can probably find that nearby.

title: “Decent hotel, but felt scammed by some of their business practices”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for 5 nights in April 2010. The location was pretty good - about 5 blocks from the heart of Times Square, and the price was reasonable, given the high prices in NY City. I chose this hotel for its location, price and the fact that reviewers gave it more credit (4-stars on average) than the official hotel rating (3-stars).
Our room was ok, but nothing spetacular - probably 3-star level. I felt the bathroom was pretty old school, and it reminded me that I was in a 3-star hotel.
I did have two big issues with the hotel. I bought tickets through the hotel concierge for the new King Tut exhibit in Times Square. The concierge confirmed that the hotel sold the tickets at the same price as at the box office. After buying the tickets I found out at the box office that this was not true. Though not a large fee ($4.50/ticket), I felt it was only fair that the hotel refund the additional service charge. They refused to do so. I felt this act displayed poor customer service.
Secondly, watch out for the parking service. When I checked in late on Saturday, I was offered two rates - $40 for self-service parking and $45 for valet parking. I chose the latter. Upon checkout I found out that there was an additional $45 in/out fee. When I questioned this fee (it was not listed on my valet receipt), I was told that the valet service person mentions this fee when a car is dropped off. There was a "no in/out' notice on the valet ticket, but I missed this during the busy exchange of luggage, etc. My understanding was that 'valet' meant that I could take the car out and in when needed. Fortunately, I only took the car out one time. I ended up paying $270 in parking fees for 5-days at the hotel. I saw some local signs that promised monthly parking for $150/month. I felt like I was taken advantage of in this case.

title: “Terrible customer service; all they care about is $$$”
text:
My husband and I would both advise travelers to avoid the La Quinta Manhattan. We had a five-night stay in late October 2005 and witnessed firsthand how terrible the service is.
I should preface this review by saying that we have stayed in several NYC hotels in the past, and are past residents of NYC -- we know that not all rooms will have a stellar view, and one might get a room that overlooks an airshaft. Be prepared for this, and remember that many, many people in NYC have apartments with similar views. Also, many, many hotel breakfast rooms use styrofoam plates and, yes, these plates may melt when hot toast is put on them. I mention these things because these are some of the complaints that have been lodged against the La Quinta by other Trip Advisor members. These are things that will occur at any NYC hotel in this price range, and travelers should expect this.
Our complaint about the La Quinta is their inattention and indifference to customer service. At times the staff members were unquestionably rude. Examples:
We had a plumbing problem that took 2-1/2 days to fix, because the front desk did not communicate at all with the engineer about what the problem really was. They wasted his time and ours. He never came with the right tools, and couldn't even fix it in the end.
The housekeeping staff dumped a pile of soaps and shampoos in our room the first day, and never monitored the supply again.
The employee running the breakfast room was surly and sometimes downright rude. The coffee/hot water machine was difficult to figure out and there were no instructions. If this employee encountered anyone wondering how to use the machine or having a problem with it, he chastised them in a voice loud enough for everyone in the room to here. On October 24th, we heard him sarcastically ask people that he was "helping" with this machine, "Can't you read English?" He did this three times! (Many of the guests at the hotel were not native English speakers, but the way the coffee maker worked was not apparent even to those of us who were.) When my husband accidentally spilled some coffee and burned his hand, this employee made rude jokes about the incident as he cleaned up.
The man running the gift shop where one could buy tickets for an airport shuttle bus tried to con my husband into making a reservation without revealing what the price was. My husband's first question had been, "How much is it?" and this man did everything in his power to get my husband to sign up for the shuttle without answering the question. (The shuttle was $45 one-way to LaGuardia airport. We used a cab and paid $27 each way, including tip and tolls! Obviously, a much better deal!)
Hot water in our room was dependent upon the demand in other rooms. At times, tepid water was all that we could get, in the shower and the sink.
The remote on the TV did not work well.
The room door was difficult to open, with metal scraping metal on the bottom of the door frame.
All this for between $219 and $329 per night.
We will not stay at the La Quinta Manhattan again. Never!

title: “Don't stay at the W”
text:
W hotel was an overall disappotionment. Unfriendly staff, dirty rooms with stained bed sheets and hair in the wash basin. Bathroom door was a flimsy sliding door and a noisy fan that couldn't be turned off.
Extremely noisy hotel and the room had paper thin walls. The sexual escapades of your neighbours were fully audiable. Disgusting. Weird people hanging out in the hotel lobby.
I would not recommend anyone to stay here. There are much better hotels at the same price in a nicer setting.

title: “Nice stay at the SoHo Grand!”
text:
Was there at the end of June for two nights. The room was not as large as I would have liked, but the amazing views, and service, made up for the size. I was on the 10th floor and had a corner room with SW/SE views of the World Trade Center and the Hudson. 
Room was very clean; enjoyed the bath products and complimentary internet. Had continental breakfast one of the mornings and the pastries/coffee were very good. Overall, the staff was very nice, but the hostess was incredibly charming and friendly. 
Fantastic location for shopping and dining in SoHo. Five to ten minute walk to Chinatown and Little Italy, and about a ten to 15 minute walk to the World Trade Center and downtown. 
Various subway stops within a few blocks.

title: “Would stay again”
text: Great location near Galleria. Def a Mon-Fri business hotel, as it was pretty empty during our stay (Thur/Fri nights). The redo in the lobby looks fantastic, but the sleeping rooms are indeed dated. But they are clean and quiet, so no complaints! Exec Lounge staff are friendly and helpful. Pool is bigger than expected and they have a nice very shallow (1 ft) pool perfect for infants.

title: “below the average”
text: We went to visit NY city and we booked Radisson Lexington Hotel. The service at the reception was the worst we had. We booked the Executive and were given the Guest room. The room and corrider are dirty. You have to bring your laptop to have access to internet or you will have to pay in very to get access. We tried but the payment was complicated so we simply gave up. The City of NewYork is beautifull city and we forget about the hotel. The hotel should be 2 star or below.

title: “Enjoyed our stay at Hotel California”
text:
Pros- Excellent location. We walked with luggage from BART station. Felt safe walking to hotel at night, but would venture too far past it from Union Square. The decor was cool and casual. Lobby was inviting. Our room was perfect and clean. The bed was comfy. They are small boutique rooms. Don't expect a lot of empty space. Had everything we needed though. They offer a shot of tequila at check in. Wine & cheese every day from 4-6pm. Friendly staff. Price was good. 
Cons- Thin windows and location allow for street noise. Be prepared. We were expecting it, so it didn't change our good feelings of the hotel. But if you need a quiet room to sleep this might not be your hotel.

title: “An Excellent Hotel”
text: The hotel is very conveniently placed for sight-seeing and shopping. The staff are efficient and helpful. Our room was lovely and the potions and lotions in the bathroom were by Aveda. We used the restaurant twice during our stay. The food is good but the chef doesn't seem to know quite where he's going - some dishes are huge and rustic Italian-style, others are more French - beautifully presented and the portions much smaller.

title: “More of a hostel than a boutique hotel”
text:
Not sure where the really good reviews of this hotel are coming from. (Perhaps the hotel management that monitors this website and advertises the overall Tripadvisor rating on theirs?) It is quite economical for a downtown hotel, and the staff is very friendly. The flower arrangements are great. And that's the sum total of the really positive stuff I can write.
We reserved a double room with en suite bathroom. The room was set up really oddly - the bed was sort of stuck in the middle of the room, with the head of the bed hitting open air, so our pillows kept falling off. The bed itself was REALLY SQUEAKY, to the point that my husband, who can generally sleep anywhere, was kept awake by it. The "kitchenette" sink doubled as the bathroom sink, which to me, is a little gross - there was no sink in the bathroom. The "kitchenette" was a microwave and refrigerator with a few cabinets with dishes. 
We stayed in this room for one night before complaining to the management about the bed. The day manager (Rose) was really cool, acknowledging that the rooms with the double beds ALL have the problem of the squeaky mattress,and that they are not currently replacing them due to economic considerations, but hope to do so soon. She upgraded us to a Queen room, which was decidedly less squeaky and set up more nicely.
Then the A/C kicked in. The rooms do not have individual A/C control - it's centrally controlled for all rooms at the front desk. When we went to bed, the A/C was running constantly and we had to call the front desk to turn it off. In the morning, they turned it on again and it ran constantly, and i had to call the desk at 7 am again to turn it off, because there weren't enough blankets on the bed to keep us warm. 
The continental breakfast was typically mediocre. Their pastries tended to be kinda stale.
This is a hostel, not a "European style boutique hotel." Furnishings were the absolute cheapest - the least they could have done was to go with colorful, cheap IKEA furnishings to make it look more bright and cheerful like some European hostels do. IKEA mattresses certainly would have been a higher quality.
All in all, a "meh" experience.

title: “The Best”
text: This was the best room I have ever stayed in. It was amazing. We had never stayed in downtown Chicago before and the people who work here were very helpful. If/when I go back I will definitely be staying here again.

title: “Old World Service with New World Amenities”
text:
I recently have stayed at three Ritz-Carltons (Philadelphia, Toronto, Dallas), the Westin Kierland Resort (Scottsdale, AZ), and various other high-quality hotels. I spend more than 100 nights per year in hotels, and I can say without any reservation that the Omni Parker House has the finest staff of any hotel I ever have visited (including destination resorts such as the Hamilton (Bermuda) Princess and the Fairmont Lake Louise). The Omni Parker House combines incredible historical location, an unmatched ambiance that is saturated with tradition, and beautifully-maintained original craftsmanship to provide the best of both worlds if one enjoys honoring the past while enjoying the comforts of modernity. 
There are many nice buildings in my travels, though. What sets the Omni Parker House apart is the management and literally every member of the staff with whom I ever have had contact: the loyalty ambassador who is cheery despite my turbulent, frequent schedule-changes; chambermaids who are never intrusive yet always vigilant about my individual needs; the bell staff (which I never need but from whom I always get a courteous and sincere greeting); the food service folks who literally cater to my desire to have a nice glass of wine and a fruit basket in my room. If something is not running to the staff’s satisfaction, I have had senior management apologize to me directly! Unheard of! They really, really care.
I could stay at any one of about a half- dozen hotels that are well-located for my business in Boston. It is a no-brainer. This is home away from home, and while I am fascinated and in love with the building, it is the people that make it great. It is one-of-a-kind, at the very top of the industry.

title: “Amazing visit with kids!”
text: We stayed at the Palomar for a long weekend with 2 boys ages 4 and 9. The hotel was beautiful and the staff was incredibly helpful and friendly. Our King suite was perfect, just the right touch of luxury and comfort, it was incredibly clean and the robes and slippers were a big hit. What was most surprising was how kid friendly the hotel is, our boys were treated to a welcome gift bag and juice boxes at happy hour but the hotel still maintains a quiet and luxurious environment. Kid friendly AND luxurious are two features that you seldom find together but the Palomar had both. We will definitely return, it was a fabulous stay!

title: “Overall Nice, Great Location”
text:
I just recently returned from a weekend trip to Chicago with a few buddies of mine. We stayed at the Marriott Chicago/Magnificent Mile. It was a 3 day, 2 night trip:
Rooms: I have done a bunch of travel in the last couple of years and have stayed at many different types of hotels/resorts and different chains. At this Marriott, I thought that the beds in the rooms were some of the most comfortable that I have ever slept on. The pillows were extremely comfortable as well as the bed itself and the light featherbed that was on it. I have been told my other people that all Marriott beds are like this, but all I know is that the beds at this Marriott were extremely comfortable. The rooms contained an ironing board, Iron, Bath and Body Works Shampoo and Conditioner, plenty of towels, with a flat screen TV, small table and chairs, and high speed internet (available for a small fee). The room itself was not extremely big but had a decent view of the city. (I heard some rooms, the view is not so good!) The carpets and bathroom was clean which is always nice. The hallways were also quiet at night which was a plus.
Lobby: We stayed at this Marriott over the weekend and the lobby and lobby bar were extremely busy. The lobby is an open space with lots of tables and couches for you to sit on, relax, and have a cocktail before heading out to the city for the night. The prices were reasonable for service at the bar. It was a very nice lobby experience. Also in the lobby was the bell desk, front desk, and the concierge which was very helpful in finding nearby restaurants and bars.
Location: This hotel I believe is in a great location. It is right on Michigan Avenue in the heart of the “loop.” (I hope that is what the immediate downtown is called.) It is very close to “ Rush St. ” and all of the hotspots of downtown. There is great shopping close as well as many great restaurants within walking distance. At the hotel, we valet parked our car with the hotel and never once removed it from the garage as we could walk anywhere we wanted to go or just take a short cab ride.
Service: Check in was extremely quick. All we needed to do was give our last name and our reservation was pulled up. The staff was quick to have our bags brought upstairs and tell us where all of the amenities of the hotel were such as gift/sundry shop, pool, coffee bar, lobby bar etc.. The concierge located in the lobby was very helpful with making reservations and providing lists of nearby restaurants broken down by type of food and location. Finally, the valet and bellmen at the front entrance were very quick to hail us a cab, or to help us go in any direction that we needed.
Pool: There is a pool located on the 9th floor (I think) but we did see or go in it.
Overall, Our stay at the Marriott was great and provided a great “home base” to go and do whatever we wanted to do that night in Chicago . I would recommend this hotel to friends and family and would stay there again if I was to once again, visit the Windy City .

title: “Wonderful hotel with Wonderful staff!!!!”
text:
My husband, parents, and I traveled to see the City at Christmas. It was a beautiful hotel with extremely helpful staff. This is a wonderful boutique hotel with a cozy atmosphere. The hotel was decorated tastefully to go along with its name. The 2nd floor had a beautiful sitting area with goodies out for you to snack (there was always a little something available)! The Christmas tree and poinsettias were very pretty, making it feel so festive in the hotel. 
The staff answered our many many questions, always making sure that we could find our way "home". We would definitely recommend this to someone who would like to be in a smaller, less commercialized, helpful environment. We really really enjoyed our stay and will DEFINITELY be back!

title: “problems with cleanliness.”
text:
My recent stay here at this hotel was a disappointment. This Hyatt seems to have problems with cleanliness. Once checked in and into our room, I discover dirty towels on the floor from the previous guest. The air conditioner vent has black soot around it, looks like it’s never been cleaned. Stains on the carpet, used soap bar in tub, need I go on? I called front desk to have dirty towels removed, when back in my rooms a few hours later after dinner they were still there, had to call again.
The beds were lumpy and uncomfortable, furniture in the rooms were in need of update.
Another issue is the parking. You can self park at a lot across the street for 16.00 with out in/out privileges or pay Hyatt 21.00 + tax to valet your vehicle , they seem to have you over a barrel here since it would be wise not to park your car in an unprotected lot in Downtown Houston.
The breakfast buffet is very small and cost 15.00 a person….they have someone making omelets but as for other breakfast items not much of a selection.
On a positive note, the air conditioner worked well and kept the room cool. 
This is a very busy hotel and saw many different groups, (youth soccer teams, and large family reunions) the staff was pleasant but had a hard time controlling the teens in the lobby area which were running wild and throwing food. Only half of the elevator banks were working which lead to a pile up of people trying to get back to their rooms. I don’t think ill stay at this hotel again, it just didn’t feel clean to me, the kind of place you wonder how clean the sheets might be. If staying in Downtown Houston, I suggest Hilton Americas. Much cleaner and better staff.

title: “Great weekend getaway”
text:
My girlfriend and I stayed the weekend in this hotel had a great time, I have stayed here before with my boyfriend so I kinda knew what to expect and I was excited to stay here again. 
Pacific Terrace is such a cute Boutique hotel. We had a ocean front Jr suite and the room was great as well as the view. The weather was amazing. The belIboy/valet was super friendly and nice the whole time. The hotel doesnt have a restaurant but they have room service from nearby restuarants and it was pretty good and pretty quick. The free breakfast they have in the morning is better than most hotels that offer the same kind of thing, lots of variety.
Over all, I really like most everything about this hotel and I will be definitely be back sooner than later.

title: “A perfectly fine hotel: not a "luxury" property, but a nice place to stay.”
text: Set a block from Union Square and amid great restaurants and similarly rated 3 and 3 1/2 star hotels, the Donatello neither "wow'd" nor disappointed. The hotel is well maintained, clean, safe, quiet, and pleasing to the eye, reminding one of a "faux luxury" hotel from the 1980's. The staff was friendly and accommodating, the rooms very spacious and clean (the hotel photos are accurate), and the in-room free wireless excellent. The top floor lounge was especially pleasant and cozy, with terraced views. The rates (mine: $114 average per night) were a bargain, justifying its high rating on TripAdvisor. If you're looking for "luxury" digs, go to the Ritz Carlton or Four Seasons, and spend 3-4 times more for the gilt and mirrors. But if you want a nice place where you don't feel you're being ripped off, check this place out.

title: “Good location for us”
text: We planned a family Chicago trip with our grown kids and grandkids. This hotel had a decent location for what we wanted to do and offered a king with sofa sleepers for kids. There was a last minute special offered so we booked it. Rooms were small for “suites” but adequate, as we weren’t spending a lot of time in our rooms anyway. An average free hotel breakfast was included. The pool is pretty small and was jam-packed the two evenings we went. Rooms were clean, staff was friendly and helpful. The nearby fire station had quite a few calls so it was pretty noisy one night.

title: “Very professional, but fun hotel”
text:
The location is wonderful, right close to Union Station (which has an excellent food court). This is a large hotel, with lots of steel and glass, but a big beautiful lobby filled with sun. We appreciated the amenities and the staff was very helpful with advice and, well, help. It's a good location to start from if you are touring washington, as the tour busses go from Union Station. You can also walk to the capitol, botannical garden and other places. (Washington is very tourist friendly in general).
It's more expensive than some of the other places we've stayed, but we wanted to be in the city and it was very well run. No issues at all with cleanliness, service, etc. These folks are pros.

title: “LOCATION AND VALUE!”
text: my boyfriend and i stayed at the moore november 2008 and LOVED it. the front desk personnel was friendly and attentive to our questions. we wanted to bring the bed home with us it was so comfortable! the street noise is to be expected downtown; but the walls seemed sound proof to us. we honestly didn't hear any other guest. SUPER CHARMING hotel i recommend to non family travelers on a budget who don't care for gyms, pools, or room service.

title: “One of the best!”
text: The Hotel Burham was a welcome refuge from the bustling big city of Chicago. With it's smaller size, beautiful renovations, comfortable rooms, excellent location and exceptionally pleasant, professional and helpful staff I would stay at the Hotel Burham again and recommend it to other travelers with no hesitation. This is Ritz Carlton treatment at prices the 'average joe' can afford. Two thumbs up for the Hotel Burham!!

title: “again and again”
text: Our eleventh trip to Boston to see family, Red Sox and Bruins. The one constant is the superb care, meticulous accommodations and predictable excellence of the staff, the rooms and the wonderful food at the Commonwealth. We'll be back again this summer.

title: “Good base for touring the city”
text: The hotel is one vertical slice of a 4 hotel block. The foyer is small and there are some handy guest computers to make your bookings from - reception will print your tickets. Check-in and departure were smooth, pleasant and quick. The room is neat, clean comfortable and functional. V comfortable bed. Breakfast is good value. Perhaps I expected it to be a bit more avant garde in style and to have more guest facilities - eg bigger foyer, rooftop bar, and the like. The street outside needs some refurbishment but is safe enough and the location is great. Not one of New York's great hotels but a good resting place after a hard touring day.

title: “Mediocre Housekeeping Service”
text:
Positive -This hotel has LARGE rooms as compared to many other hotels in the area. The only disappointment we experienced was the housekeeping. Twice we came back after a day of sightseeing to a room where the iron and ironing board weren't put away, the bed wasn't made completely, and the fold out couch/bed wasn't a 'couch'. We expected to see a room as pictured/discribed. One where we wanted to sit and relax. The minimal was done - I could have and did do better to make it comfortable for our family. Who wants to straighten beds and couches on vacation? After speaking to the manager the first time I expected better the next day. Unfortunately, it wasn't. The housekeeping staff need to finish the room correctly and NOT assume what the guest wants. Personally, I like to see the decorative pillows back on the bed and not the floor as well as the throw blanket on the foot of the bed and having a couch to sit on. Little things that make the room seem clean and pleasant weren't done. However, when I did bring this to the manager's attention the first day and the next (as I expected it to be better); she immediately handled the situation that surpassed our expectation. 
Positive - Staff very friendly & helpful. 
Positive - Location is wonderfully close to shopping and restaurants. Many homeless are around but they are friendly and non-threatening.
Positive - Adjusted parking fee, option to be 'green' with towels/linen with a $5 hotel reward card for doing so

title: “Fabulous rooms and location can't be beat with impeccable service!”
text: Tom and Michael were both very helpful everytime we had a question or need. Rooms were even better than we had pictured. Lots of room. Location is a block from subway which made everything easily accessible. Highly recommend!

title: “Needs to do better - it's living off its reputation”
text: Elegant hotel in a great location if you are a tourist BUT for the price we paid (we had a suite for the three of us), we've stayed at hotels with better amenities and definitely much better service. The frontdesk staff were helpful but the rest of the service was disappointing for this standard of hotel, especially in the Cafe du Parc where breakfast was served and housekeeping. Some staff were barely polite and most were cold and impersonal. I expect more of an Intercontinental.

title: “Get what you pay for, sorta!”
text:
I just spent a weekend at this hotel with husband while attending a convention downtown. It was easy to get to, right off of the highway. Having stayed at other Hampton Inns I was expecting a certain amount of quality.....but did not get it. Upon check in I was informed that the king size bed I thought I had reserved was only considered a "preference". As in I guess my reservation said that I “prefer” to play roulette and see what size bed I will be sleeping in. Basically this hotel will stick you with whatever room they feel like sticking you in. Needless to say I was not happy and the desk clerk told me that it was Cowboys training camp so I should have felt lucky to have a room at all! Much less one that was non-smoking. 
I can truly say the only reason I did not turn around and go to a better hotel on the northside of town was that it was late and the convention started early. Oh, and their pool was broken because of maintenance. But I was told I could go 6 blocks away and use the holiday inn's pool (hmm....maybe they have a king size bed available?)
Off to bed...and I have to say a single bed does not fit two people comfortably. 
The next morning we had the continental breakfast which looked like a swarm of starving wasps had rolled through it and eaten everything. There isn't enough room in that area and I hope they remodel that area some day. The parking is free and it’s a good location which is about the only thing you get for staying at this hotel.
If you can spare the extra bucks, upgrade to somewhere nicer. This place is small and well.....not worth it. You can stay at a much nicer hotel off of the 410 loop for the same price.
But if you want to be within walking distance to the mall I guess this is the place to go. I won’t stay here again! Go some place else and pay for parking on the riverwalk!

title: “Wonderful hotel, location and service”
text: Stayed here in November with my sisters, daughter, niece and Mom for Mom's 70th birthday. The concierge, Anna was fabulous. She made our mother's birthday trip special by upgrading her room and sending a special cake and wine for the occasion. The hotel is beautiful. The rooms were lovely. Chic hotel bar. The service was fabulous and the location couldn't be better. We walked right out the front door to Central Park. It is within walking distance to so many wonderful NYC sites. We couldn't have picked a better hotel. Highly recommend.

title: “Great Christmas Vacation!!!”
text:
My wife and I decided to take a Christmas Vacation to NYC from December 18-21. We got a great deal on a standard room with queen size bed on the Doubletree website ($130 CAD). I was a bit nervous to see the place judging from some of the reviews here, but I am not sure what all the negativity is about. We were greeted by a very friendly and helpful front desk person, and were provided the excellent warm chocolate chip cookies upon arrival. We had arrived at 8 AM, and were not able to check in that early. However, the hotel was able to put our luggage away for us until we returned at lunch time. Check in was quite smooth and we were into a room, as they said, by lunch. We were on the 6th Floor and thought the room was great. Not large, but cozy and I found they made great use of the space. The room had been recently renovated, and was bright and clean. We enjoyed the flat screen TV, and found the bed to be very comfortable. It was greatly appreciated each night after long days touring the city! The bathroom was clean and modern, with no complaints.
With regards to the noise, though we were facing the NYPD and FDNY stations, the noise didn't really disrupt us that much. Maybe if it was the summer and you had the window open it would be noticeable, but with the windows closed it didn't bother us. The hallway noise was noticed (thanks to the young children running up and down the hall), but as has been suggested could probably be drowned out with a towel under the door.
Overall, I would highly recommend this hotel as a great home base for your trip to New York. The rooms are clean and modern. The location is fantastic--within about a 10 block radius you can walk to Central Park, Rockefeller Centre, Trump Tower, Times Square, Empire State Building, Fifth Avenue, Madison Avenue. We were there in the middle of the transit strike, and weren't terribly effected because of our proximity to everything. And now that the strike is over, it is good to know the subway is right next door as well.
I recommend the Broadway Diner across the street. You can get a great breakfast there for $5. The food, service, and prices are great. 
The only negatives I would have were that they told us toll free calls were free from our room, then charged us for them. (They were quickly removed when we pointed it out to them.) Also, we were told the luggage storage was free, then were charged $3 when we picked up our luggage. 
Overall though, I would come back to the Doubletree Metropolitan again. If you ever have the chance to see NYC at Christmastime, I would highly recommend it. Nobody does Christmas better!

title: “Omni Berkshire-great location-great room.”
text: Went into NYC to see Jersey Boys. Valet parked and went to our room early without a hitch. Quite a large room for NY on 21st floor. Beautiful bath with whirlpool tub and pink marble shower. Beds were sumptuous. TV was a little dated. Wonderful, upscale neighborhood, surrounded by great stores and restaurants and walking distance to theatre.

title: “Beach house feel, exceptional service culture”
text:
I really enjoyed my brief stay here, and will organise next family US vacation to come back again. Service was outstanding.
The rooms vary a lot as there are some old, apartment style buildings and a modern hotel buidling. I had an apartment and loved it. Yes, it is a little basic, but it has all the detail of a nice beach house. Wooden shutters, while walls, casual furnishings. It is very big though, with a large lounge, large bedroom looking over the marina and separate bathroom. All was very comfortable. The rooms come off an outdoors walkway which some may have a problem with, I did not mind at all. There was also a small individual balcony.
All facilities where good. Breakfast was ala carte due to off season but was first rate. Pools etc look good but I did not try them. Marina is a very nice environment.
I had a car and found the location very good as it was easy to get in and out of and a chance to warm up prior to hitting the mad freeways. 10 minutes to the zoo, same to the airport.
Best was the service. After some bad experiences with a lack of flexibility and customer focus at other hotel chains, I was very pleasantly surprised when I had to change some arrangaments here. I was given assistance that saved me a lot of money, at a loss in revenue to the hotel. A big change to quoting policy we are used to from most. I am now committed to returning the favour and will be loyal to Hyatt as much as possible as a result.
Price was very good, may have been off season special though.
Overall, keep in mind this is a regular Hyatt experience, with pristine rooms and ulta chic furnishings. It has more of a holiday house feel, but very warm and the location on the marina puts you in instant holiday mode. I think this would be a great option with kids, given the size of the apratment as well.

title: “The Rim”
text: good location, at the RIM where you can find many restaurants & cafes. 5 minutes to six flags & 15 to 20 minutes to sea world. 15 minutes to san antonio downtown.

title: “We discover something new about Barton Creek with every visit”
text: In his Tripadvisor reply to our review of this resort last August, the General Manager, Mr. Walsh, had mentioned "looking forward to some incredible Fall golf". Although time flew by for us, in December we received and immediately purchased a Groupon offer with a 1-night stay and 18 holes of golf for 2. Then, in February, some friends to whom we had recommended Barton Creek came back with a glowing review of the 8812 Wine Bar & Grill and a great story about getting lost, if only for a short time, on the nature trail. Realizing in February that we were running out of time to use our Groupon, we finally called the hotel and booked a great AAA package rate for a 2d night, as well. Our amazingly helpful reservation agent was the 1st of many employees who went above and beyond any level of service and friendliness that we could have expected during our stay. As for the golf, now we know why it is so much fun to play courses designed by PGA legends like Palmer and Crenshaw. The irony of all this is that, as we were leaving on the last morning or our stay, we realized that, for the 1st time, we were finally noticing the hotel's large and sparkling swimming pool, the tall shelves of books in many of the hallways, and a semi-circle of a dozen huge wooden rocking chairs on a large patio overlooking a canyon and golf course which we could also see from our room. Our recommendation is to book a stay of least 2 nights and to not be surprised if you want to come back and visit again. We have stayed at many hotels and resorts in the Austin area and we enjoy Barton Creek more than any other. We will be back!

title: “Service with a smile!”
text:
What a great experience!
The staff in the hotel were courteous, helpful and friendly. Our room was very clean and well-appointed and we cannot praise the hotel and its staff enough. A couple of staff are worthy of special mention because their contribution to our stay helped make the difference.
Albert - the concierge - is worth his weight in gold if you're a tourist and don't know the area. Nikki, who works in the bar, is a shining example of what a customer-facing employee should be. 
Choosing the Sheraton Gateway was a trade-off fo us, as tourists. We needed somewhere close to the airport after an 11-hour flight but wanted to be fairly close to the 'touristy' places. We made the right decision and wouldn't hesitate to say there again.

title: “Hotel Chelsea - great location with little comfort”
text:
We were looking forward to our stay in the renowned Hotel Chelsea, but when we arrived.... it was with disbelief that we entered the room. It was small, dark, dirty. Really, really awful.
The staff kindly put us in a better room the next day, but this one was still not at just average standard.
The hotel has a great location, has ambience and a great vibe, but one should not pay too much importance on a nice, tidy room.

title: “O'kay for one night”
text: Stayed here as a late arrival and couldn't get to Anacortes till the morning, typical Red Roof Inn.

title: “Friendly staff, great place and excellent location.”
text: Stayed here in Feb 2011, family with 2 small children. Luckily we avoided the blizzard. Location is hard to beat if you want to be near Magnificent Mile etc, room was excellent for the price we paid, even allowing for the fact that prices are low at this time of year. It is next to a fire station which the kids loved, and the firefighters were almost as friendly as the hotel staff. Daily free breakfast was excellent, for us and the children. The staff at the front desk and the door were very friendly, they made themselves very popular with the children (helped by various candy bars, popcorn and cookies) and were most helpful when we needed a quick repair job on a toy car!! The maid service was good. Pool was COLD!! (in Feb though...). But seriously we have no complaints and shall stay here again when we next visit this great city (in summer).

title: “Josh, at the front desk, was awesome!!”
text:
We arrived early to start our shopping & adult/no kid time!! Our room wasn't available, Josh at the front desk, was very accommodating stowing our luggage & putting our champagne in the kitchen's fridge. 
The next morning upon checkout, Josh was back, with a big smile. Since it was such a beautiful day, he recommended Navy Pier, instead of spending the day inside!! He was right!! 
We also had breakfast at their in house place, Dine. Our server, didn't catch her name, was great. 
Overall, we had a fantastic getaway & having Josh & our server, was an extra bonus!!
Thanks,
Holly Million

title: “Go elsewhere if you are an average-to-light sleeper.”
text: This is a beautiful Hyatt Place. Love the amenities and the people who work there are very nice and attentive. So it's a shame that it is not better soundproofed for the nearby train which blows all night long. We actually had to depart after the first night because neither me nor my teenage kids could sleep. If you are a deep sleeper and don't wake easily, it's a great value. If you are an average-to-light sleeper, I would suggest you go elsewhere (or bring earplugs --which the hotel didn't have available, unfortunately). There is free parking and large flat-screen tv in the room which is very nice. Showers are pretty roomy too. But sleep is more important to me.

title: “Whatch out for scams...”
text: I went to Boston to see a concert at The House of Blues and decided to stay here because it's so close to the venue. The hotel was ok-- we just wanted a place to crash. However when I checked my bank statement, I saw that I was charged an extra $100. When I called to find out why, they accused me of taking the alarm clock radio. My boyfriend is a police officer, and I am a teacher. We would NEVER take something from a hotel (or anywhere) that didn’t belong to us, but they would not give in. I ended up paying for the clock-- which was probably worth half that price. Maybe it was an honest mistake on their part, but I just wanted to put this out there. Take an inventory right when you check in, or it can be a VERY expensive night.

title: “Great location, Very Happy with Stay”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Grand Hyatt for Easter weekend, Friday through Monday. We got a rate of $116 a night through the Hyatt Web site, which included the breakfast (AAA special). We were given a nice interior room, with view of atrium. Nice room, the usual furnishings you would expect from a better hotel. The bathroom was very nice.
If the buffett breakfast had not been free, we would not have had it. It was OK but on the first day I found 2 hair strands in the oatmeal (gross!), food was mediocre, and the wait staff, despite their best efforts, were overwhelmed.
The front desk was very nice and helpful, the concierge NOT! Do not waste your time waiting in line to speak with them. One of them actually made us wait while he was on a personal phone conversation.
The location of the Grand Hyatt can't be beat. Easy and safe access to the Metro, all our restaurants were within walking distance. We easily walked to the White House, Federal Triangle, and National Gallery/Archives -- part of the what's interesting is to be in the city and see the sites along the way. However, you can easily get to the tourist stops via the metro, if you don't feel like a leisurely walk through the city.
We will likely stay here again, given the location, special pricing, and room comfort.

title: “Heater too hot....water too cold”
text:
I checked in at 10pm on Halloween to find the air condition blasting in the room. So much so that even after turning on the heat it took a good 15 minutes for the air to heat up. You can't close the black out curtains which means the occupants of the adjacent building - which in true New York fashion is almost close enough to touch - can see everything. I set the heat on auto and the target temp to 75. Aside from the fact that it blew so loudly that I could barely sleep, i also had to get up and turn it off in the wee hours of the morning because it stayed on non-stop pushing the room temp to over 80 degrees. The water was freezing cold in the morning and refused to get hot except for a few seconds during my shower where I was scaulded. The continental breakfast had travel coffee cups but no tops to them: useless. When I asked the front desk about a cab he told me "sure they're outside just grab one". Famous last words. 
The only silver lining: checked thoroughly...no bed bugs. I guess that's all you can ask for in a NYC hotel nowadays.

title: “Really Great Hotel & Location!”
text: Just got back from staying at the Executive Hotel Vintage Court. Me & my partner stayed there for 10 nights and I can highly recommend it. The location is good - very close to Union Square (which is central in San Francisco). The hotel doesn't look spectacular from the outside, but inside it's great. It has a wonderful cosy lounge with really comfy settees and chairs and a gorgeous decor based on a 'winery' theme. Lovely paintings in the lounge of vintage wine and stuff. There was a log fire blazing in the lounge every day we were there, and it always felt really cozy. In the lounge area is also a computer where you can access the internet (for a fee). In the mornings in the lounge, the hotel serves delicious complimentary danish pastries, muffins and coffee and tea. In the evening between 5-6pm they service complimentary red and white wine. The hotel staff are always really helpful and friendly too. They would always immediately try to deal with any queries or anything we wanted. We stayed on the 7th floor in the room called Davis Bynum Winery. (Every room has a nameplate on the door and every room is named after a winery!) The room was very comfortable - really good comfortable bed and pillows, nice warm radiator, aircon if it got too hot, flat screen TV, ironing board, comfy chair and ensuite bathroom with a good hot shower. The maid comes every day to make up the room so it always looks clean and tidy. They also provide complementary toiletries and there is a good hairdryer in the bathroom. The only downside I suppose it that we didn't have any view from our hotel window - it just looked out on to the backs of some quite ugly backdoor buildings - not onto the street at all. But we didn't really care. I really like the location of this hotel too. It was only a 7 or 8 minute walk to Union Square, where Macy's and other shops are. About 4 minutes from the hotel is a really good book shop called Borders that is open until 11pm and has a really good coffee shop upstairs. They don't mind you borrowing books to read while you have your coffee and pumpkin bread etc. There are also Starbucks in the vicinity and a really fantastic diner called Lori's Diner that serves wonderful food at very reasonable prices. We are vegetarians and thought we would have trouble eating in the diner, but they serve lovely vegan salads and other really nice veggie food. Really good - I can highly recommend this place. Also in this same street, about a minute from the hotel is the cable car stop. This takes you right into downtown or in the other direction to Fisherman's Wharf - where all the adorable sea lions live on Pier 39. I'd advise you to get a travel pass asap though, because the transport can get pricey and you have to use it alot as the hills are enough to beat anyone. We got a 7-day pass for $24 dollars. We could use this as much as we liked. If we hadn't had this, a one-way journey on the cable car would have been $5 a time, and other public transport about $2. So it really saved us loads of money. Well I hope you like my review. I could waffle on about how great San Fran is forever, and I can highly recommend this hotel and will certainly stay there again next time I visit this city.

title: “hidden treasure”
text: Stayed here prior to an early morning flight out of CMH. Great price, fabulous staff, nice suites. About 10 mins from airport, but much cheaper than closer hotels. Free parking while I am on my vacation." Room" was really a suite. I didn't need all that room, but didn't complain. Very clean and well maintained. Full (free) hot breakfast. ONLY complaint is that, even though it's right of I-70, it is tucked away and hard to find.

title: “Gross”
text:
Found clumps of hair in "clean" towel. Room was run down: torn carpet, banged-up furniture, bathtub's enamel was peeling. Maybe things a person could over look if it was a really cheap hotel, but because of its convenient location to many sites, it is a pretty expensive hotel. Bed linens were at least clean. But, here was the grossest part: almost every other towel had crusty-looking stains on them, but it got worse. When my son opened up a "clean" towel on the last day and it had two huge clumps of hair in it...I almost got sick. How can that even happen???
I do have to compliment the restaurant for wonderful service and food.

title: “Good location, small rooms”
text: My husband and I stayed here for a little weekend getaway. It's a beautiful hotel with lavish decor, however I found the rooms to be a bit on the small side. Our king room was basically just big enough for the bed and to walk around it. The bathroom however was huge with lots of room on the counter. Nice hotel with lots of character, but I would probably opt for a more practical hotel next time. Definitely too expensive for the size of room you get.

title: “Great location, fine hotel”
text: The location was great, close to restuarants and just enough off of the Miracle Mile that you don't feel under the swarm. Parking is $42 a night, well within the market price for downtown chicago, but an amount that will need to factor into your budget.

title: “Could have been better”
text:
Motel is old style and is showing it's age. The location was okay. General cleanliness could have been better. Breakfast was under par. You get what you pay for.
Staff was friendly.

title: “The W gets a WOW”
text: I stayed at the W in downtown San Diego at the beginning of the month. The place was immaculate and our room was off the hook! If you go you need to talk to a guy that works there named Greg Brebner. He told us all the cool places to go at night, best places for happy hour, and seemed like he was there whenever we needed anything. The restaurant has some incredible cuisine as well. The pool is fun, seemed very private, and the outdoor bar The Beach was a great place to sit by the fire and enjoy a cocktail.
