title: “Excellent customer service and beautiful hotel”
text:
Planned a last minute getaway to San Francisco last weekend. After reading customer reviews on TA, I decided to select the Omni Hotel. The hotel was awesome! Customer service impeccable. Cleanliness was excellent. Front desk clerks and doormen learned our names quickly and called us by name for the duration of the trip. I would strongly recommend the omni to visitors. Staff very knowledgable on what's going on in town and recommended the best ways to get around. Great location in that it was in the downtown area but a couple of blocks away from all of the hustle and bustle on traffic and people. Would definitely stay there again.
A great place to eat Chinese food is the R & G lounge on Kearny Street (two blocks behind the Omni) food was excellent and very affordable.

title: “Great Price, Amazing Location!”
text:
I stayed at the Cosmo for 3 nights with 3 of my girlfriends! We absolutely loved it! Mind you. There was 4 of us, and the room is very tiny! We had a two bedroom and there isnt room for much else! 4 girls in New York and their luggage...you can imagine how tight it was! But it doesnt matter, your in New York City, in a great location. Really great breakfast place nearby, and the best part? The subway is literally steps from the front door! You can get to anywhere super fast! We all felt really safe there, and the staff was nice, and didnt bother us at all, even though we were loud some nights! :) 
The only thing we didnt like about this hotel was the water pressure from the shower. It felt like you were being beaten haha but other than that, there are zero complaints! 
:)

title: “Pretty Cool- I was leery at first..”
text: So we booked this for my birthday. Of course we waited until the last minute but I am kind of glad that it happened. The hotel itself if very cool- They just don't build them like that any more... The valet was very prompt and courteous.. The front desk staff was very professional as well. The barkeep was very friendly and we liked her... Ok here come the downsides. 1. The Pool- It is tiny and when we were there was full of very badly behaved children whose parents seemed to have abandoned them. The grounds needed a bit of work but when the brats, I mean children left, the water was nice and refreshing. 2. The room size. I have had rooms in NYC that were larger than this one and it only had a full bed that was rock hard with only 3 foam pillows... Ugh.. The BF and I laughed that we could bounce quarters on it because it was so hard. 3. The bathroom is TINY. And before you say anything, I realize that it is a historic hotel. But it was very clean and only blocks away from everything. Plus we overlooked the grounds at the Alamo. It was very cool. We will stay again and see how it goes.

title: “Low budget hotel and better than expected”
text:
After spending a week in another budget hotel in SOMA (south of Market Street) which I had endured homeless persons all over the streets, pot smoking in other rooms of the hotel, and substandard restrooms down the hall, the Hotel Tayor was a joy to stay at. Located 3 blocks west of Powell Street, Union Square and the Cable Cars, it is handy for theater and within a couple blocks of at least 6 major hotels, if you still want to feel important and well off. 
The Hotel Talyor is best if you plan to have a stay at least 7 days so you can use the great weekly rates. I was in two different rooms, because at check-in the manager asked if I could move later in the week to allow a group arriving later that wanted to be all on the same floor. Very polite staff, and if you ask, they will let you use their personal computer for a short time. 
Both rooms were above average, with bath, shower/tub combos, lots of closet space, cable TV, and mini fridges. No AC, but one room had a fan.
Older elevator, but persons with wheelchairs will have a difficult time with the steps into the lobby. Don't expect the Hyatt or Westin, but expect the room to feel like staying in the spare bedroom in your brother's house.

title: “Excellent location, complimentary breakfast (unusual in Manhattan)”
text:
Very nice and excellent located hotel, really close to Bryant Park an Times Square. Nice and helpfull staff, nice view from upper floors and corner rooms (surcharge). Rooms are very clean, the complimentary breakfast is uncommon in Manhattan and nice to have :-) .
Rooms are not large and little bit pricy, but its directly in the centre of Manhattan, thats why ... 
It is in walking distance to Times Square, Bryant Park, Public library, Grand Central Terminal, Empire State Building etc. etc.
We stayed at this hotel for 6 nights, it was already our fourth stay there and we plan to come again next year ...

title: “Great place to stay with a friend!!”
text: Great place to stay with a friend the mini suite offered each of us a seperate bathroom and closet. Perfect for two woman on a "girls trip".

title: “The best hotel of our three week holiday”
text:
This is by far the best hotel of our three week holiday in Wyoming, Montana and Colorado, the room is spacious and the beds are so comfortable, the breakfast is different every day and lots to choose from, but best thing of all is the staff they couldn't be more helpful.
I would recommend this hotel to everyone.

title: “Great Stay at the Jurys”
text:
Based on the reviews, the Jurys seemed like a reliable bet for great stay in Boston. While our stay was similarly satisfying like other reviewers experiences, I felt that it was a little overpriced for what you got - although it IS downtown Boston. 
The room was clean, very nicely appointed and had an extremely large bathroom with heated towel racks - a nice touch if you ask me. The bedroom area of our Deluxe King room was pretty small, however, but adequate. 
One disappointing feature of the hotel is the exorbitantly priced Valet. $40 per day, and all they do is drive it to the nearest private parking garage with whom they have a deal with. You would do yourself a favor by utilizing one of the THREE parking garages within a block of the hotel: 
(http://maps.google.com/maps?near=350+Stuart+St,+Boston
,+MA+02116&geocode=&q=parking&f=l&hl=en&sll=42.350052,
-71.071318&sspn=0.001947,0.005021&layer=c&ie=UTF8&ll=
42.35171,-71.071308&spn=0.007786,0.020084&z=16&om=
0&cbll=42.350935,-71.070727)
The hotel has an Irish Bar - Cuffs - and they serve up an amazing lobster bisque! The bartender even served up my Guinness properly - with a shamrock design in the frothy head. We had a mind to skip our dinner reservations at Grill 23 across the street and just stay here! Of course, we're glad we didn't, as the meal was tremendous at Grill 23 as well!

title: “Good place to stay in mid-town”
text: No questions - this place is good to stay compared with other places around.

title: “Prime spot.”
text: i go stay here often when I am in town on business. Great staff and awesome rooms.

title: “Reasonably priced hotel in New York City”
text: Our recent visit to Manhattan was richly enhanced by the luxury, quality, and location of the Lucerne Hotel. Conveniently located on 79th and Amsterdam on the upper west side, its just a short walk to Central Park and plenty of shopping and restaurants abound. The Lucerne was recently rennovated, yet retains it old world charm as evidenced by the exterior facade and inner stairwell with its thick concrete walls and winding wooden staircase. Our room at the Lucerne was just right. Small but luxurious, it was just right for two. The well appointed room had a window with a decent view, a very comfortable queen bed with outstanding bedding, and super nice feather pillows. Best of all, the room had a large walk-in closet and a nook that includes refridgerator, microwave, and upper cabinets. Just to prepare a quick snack and store some of the yummy foods that pervade Manhattan. The nice sized bathroom has a walk in glass shower, nice large tiled flooring, and a marble vanity. Guests are greeted by the hotel's super nice doormen. The lobby is comfortable and inviting, the consierge is knowledgeable and well informed, and on Thursdays at 5:00, guests are treated to fruit and wine. The Lucerne is an excellent place to stay when visiting New York. I will definitely stay there again.

title: “What a Great Hotel!!! Great Price!!!!”
text:
What can I say?? This was a great hotel in a great area,(right near the Empire State building, Macy's). It was first class all the way! We arrived really early 8AM and I had requested to store our luggage before the 3PM check in. They did even better and gave us a room immediately!!! We had a view on the 9th floor and it was exactly as described in the room descriptions. The front desk, the porter were great right down to the cleaning staff. The only downfall was that there were renovations outside of the building right around the block and there were a few homeless people sleeping up near the corner of the street(not near the hotel entrance). You did not hear the noise and the people did not bother you.
I would highly recommend this hotel to everyone and would most certainly stay again.

title: “Stay away!”
text:
Please! stay away from the Horrible Hotel, the rooms are not much bigger than closets, the tv did not work, the toilet leaked all over the bathroom floor, the beds are horrible, the shower curtain was half as wide as the tub so it was impossible to take a shower without getting water all over the bathroom floor.
do yourself a favor and stay very far away from this absolutely terrible hotel! 
consider yourself warned

title: “Comfy Cool.”
text:
If you’re looking for something a little different than the cookie-cutter type hotel rooms that could be in any chain anywhere in the world, try this. Great minimalist-style while at the same time managing to be cozy. Beds were very comfortable and everything was scrupulously clean.
If you’re turned off by the comparison to a hostel - don't be. It was nothing like any hostel we've ever been too. It’s more like house sitting in your hip buddies’ loft. Great eating and drinking establishments within walking distance. Overall an experience we would repeat.

title: “Love this Boutique Hotel”
text: This is a great midtown boutique hotel! Wonderful staff - they were friendly and very helpful (they even upgraded us)! Every time we passed by them, they would smile and greet us, always volunteering their help. The hotels is in a great location, convenient to everywhere (subway, shops, restaurants, etc.). Cute restaurant/bar connected to the hotel. Clean and quiet rooms with comfy beds. Pretty bathroom with nice products. Definitely a nice place to stay when you're in the city!

title: “Security & Customer Service Issues a problem”
text:
This hotel was pretty much what I'd expected, given the reviews here, but security and customer service issues were a problem:
Security: no locks on my room's window. True, it only faced an alley way, but still....also no locks on the opened window in the hallway by my room. (I got back after midnight and it was still open.) Again, this window also opened up onto an alley way, but it would be easy for someone to climb up the fire escape and enter the hotel through the window. And none of the windows had screens, so watch out for the pigeons that roost on the window sills.
There was no chain, deadbolt, or peep hole in the room's door, just a standard lock more suited for inside doors. Not too comforting for a woman traveling alone. 
Guests are asked to leave their room keys at the desk when leaving their rooms. I was never asked for ID to get the key back. 
Checking your luggage means leaving it in an unlocked and unattended area of the hotel's basement. No one to check if you actually pick up your own luggage when you retrieve it.
Staff: Generally unhelpful - when I booked the room at the website, a continental breakfast was included. When I checked in, I was told there was no breakfast anymore. The clerk said she'd check with the sales manager, and get back to me. She never did. Only when I checked out did I learn that the clerk actually *is* the manager. It wasn't the fact that they advertised a rate that included breakfast, but the fact that they totally ignored the issue. I wonder if they'd ignore other more important customer issues? 
On the positive side, the bathroom was very clean, the location good, but given the above security issues, I wouldn't stay here again.

title: “Look Elsewhere”
text: Stayed at The Whitehall for a Saturday night pleasure trip. There are many nice hotels in downtown Chicago, and I will not include The Whitehall on the list. Check in process was very cumbersome - we had two rooms, one was ready, and one was not. It was 3:00 P.M. This caused a myriad of problems when we finally got the second room later in the evening. Keys didn't work, they kept wanting us to sign some forms that we had already signed but made us wait for 10 minutes for them to print the forms. The car valet took forever - there phone was busy for 15 minutes, and when I called the front desk, noone answered. I went to the lobby expecting a throng of people.....one guest at the front desk....no other cars lined up, no other guests. The shower problems mentioned in another review were similar to ours. We were on the 21st floor - the shower would litterally just shut off (twice for me, three times for my wife). Finally, the T.V had to be over 20 years old - barely could be considered a "color tv". On a positive note, the furnishings in the rooms were classic, attractive wood and gave the feel of an upscale room. Nothing else about the experience was even on par with a Holiday Inn.

title: “Awesome hotel for the Solo Traveler”
text:
I stayed at the Ames for a 4 nights vacation this May. It was my first time in Boston, and I chose the hotel based on the reviews and the location - it's super central, near the Subway station, the old state house and Quincy Market. I chose well!
The room is very comfortable. There's enough room for your luggage, the bed is great and the bathroom is spacious and comfortable. The shower was amazing. My room was far from the elevator and it was very quiet.
When I arrived at the hotel I found out my suitcase's wheel broke. The Bell-boy called the maintenance guy who immediately arrived and fixed it for me! The ladies at the front desk were very nice and friendly and gave me some tips about Boston, so I had everything I needed to explore Boston easily.
You have quite a few coffee shops and restaurants around and the great Washington street where you can shop till you drop is very close. You can walk to the North End, Back Bay and Downtown easily, Boston is very walkable and easy to navigate around.
Overall, I had a great stay. My room was great and comforting after a long day of touring the city, and its location is the best you can ask for.

title: “Great staff!”
text:
The staff is very friendly and the rates were good. The breakfast is "to go", with no hot foods. The rooms are clean and the laundry facility makes it nice. 
There is no elevator, but the buildings are not too large to waalk the stairs and the hallway. The business center is extra large, and an added benefit.
The coffee is great, and the staff makes it a great stay.
I recommend it.

title: “Quality Chicago Hotel”
text: The hotel is ideally situated in the heart of anything I want to do - restaurants, subway, walking, the river, etc. Staff have been nice. I forgot toothpaste (again) and they actually provided me with a real travel sized tube of toothpaste. Thought that was great and really shows their commitment to the guests. Concierge is helpful with dining suggestions and doormen have been great. Would definitely stay here again.

title: “Very convenient hotel with modern amenities”
text: I've stayed at the Hyatt regency DFW on several occassions, especially when landing late at night at DFW. Very convenient access from the terminals, I can get to bed within 30 min after landing. The facilites are very modern, the hotel looks sparkling new (and clean). The rooms are a generous size, the bed is comfortable, the bathrooms are clean and contemporary. They have all the usual amenities. Very reasonably priced rooms and the staff are helpful and accomodating. The breakfast is good but prices are high, as with most hotels. For business travel, it fits the bill.

title: “Great location, odd hotel”
text: The location is great as long as you want to be in the hustle and bustle of Times Square. The hotel has an unusual entrance in that you have to take an elevator from the street level to the lobby and then another elevator to your floor. The lobby is not at all glamorous and had a strange odor during our entire stay. Although we thought we had a reservation for two rooms, each with double beds, we were informed when we arrived that the fine print had indicated that this was not guaranteed. I had actually called the week before and was told that double beds would not be a problem. They wound up coming up with one smoking room with double beds and another non-smoking room with a king and a rollaway. The rooms themself are nothing special but do have unique views of the Times Square area. We have stayed at other hotels in NYC and found them to be more user friendly and enjoyable.

title: “Really nice hotel in great location”
text: I tagged on a weekend in San Diego after spending time in Tijuana on business - not so familiar with San Diego having only ever stayed for a one night layover on a previous holiday - Trip advisor reviews looked pretty good so booked based on that . I loved the location - directly on the bay. I got to see cruise liners and military ships just meters off the shoreline. Staff at BW Island Palms went above and beyond their duties and as a single female traveller they offered lots of advice and ideas. Stayed in the Casa Del Mar building - was a little dated but clean and comfortable beds. I had room service one evening from the hotel restaurant which was really good and pretty reasonable. After this trip will very much consider San Diego as a holiday destination in the future

title: “Outstanding customer service”
text:
I am a fanatic of Doyle Colection hotels for their exceptional customer service, and my stay in the Dupont Circle was well in line with my expectations. 
Very friendly staff at the reception, first asking for your preferences before giving your room. Fantastic conciege, too. Rooms are OK, large and with superb comfort. 
My room was a bit noisy because of the bar terrass. No problem: the receptionist immediatly proposed me another room in a quiter place and ensured my luggage was moved in the new room while I attended my meetings. I am not sure many hotels offer such a service. 
Will clearly stay there again when I'll be back to Washington.

title: “Excellent Hotel, Great Experience, Highly Recommend”
text: We stayed here for one night and the other four at the Hyatt Regency because that was were the conference was located. However, the Hampton Inn and Suites were so much better. They had free breakfast and snacks, free internet, and an excellent room. This was a great choice and we highly recommend it to all Chicago travelers.

title: “An engaging experience!!!”
text: My fiancé and I were blown away by the service provided to us at the Thompson LES! Shivali, Megan and Noah helped my fiancé to plan the most romantic and surprising proposal. They went above and beyond the call of duty, and we can’t thank them enough! I would recommend this hotel to anyone who is looking for a cool neighborhood to hang out, shop and eat in.

title: “Good Hotel for the Price”
text:
You really can't go wrong with a Hampton Inn. When I was looking around for a hotel for a trip to San Diego I found this hotel to be much cheaper then the downtown choices. 
We were pleased with our choice. This Hampton Inn is about 10 miles from the tourist areas of downtown San Diego. Parking is free and we never had a problem finding a spot. There is a decent breakfast in the morning, the rooms are clean, the staff is pleasant and helpful, and there is a large plasma TV in every room.
Driving into town was easy since this hotel is located right of Hwy 163 so the cost savings far outweighed the drive time.
If you are looking for a great option in San Diego give this Hampton Inn a try.

title: “Much better than I expected!”
text: After reading some other reviews I wasn"t sure about staying there. But the fact that it was so close to the stadium, I thought that it was worth a try. I was very suprised! It was clean and plenty of front desk help. The rooms were very nice and clean, and the bed was very comfortable. I'm suprised about the bad reviews but I know that you can't please everyone! I would stay again!

title: “Friendly, but disorganised”
text:
The stay began badly because when I got to the room the receptionist assigned it was already occupied (there was a suitcase on the bed, though no-one was there. The receptionist apologised but could not explain how this was possible given the computerised system and electronic room keys.
Room was adaquate. 
The swimming pool is about the right size for two people. Be careful thre are extra ledges arouind the side where you may not expect them. There is no changing room at all, just the toilets and the towels dfown thee are tiny.
The waffle machine at breakfast wasn't working very well, although there was toast.

title: “Nice Hotel - but thats it”
text:
We stayed about a week ago and the first impressions are a clean & tidy hotel. The front desk staff on check in kept us waiting whilst they were talking but were quick at allocating the room in the end.
Our room faced the WTC Site and you can hear the building work but its not to loud.
We had one breakfast at the hotal and it was expensive!! However this was overshadowed by the waiter who when he picked up the check and realised we had not left a tip on the credit card receipt he went mad!!!! Slammed the folder closed, muttered under his breath and threw his pen down. We normally add the tip in cash not credit so the waiting staff do get it, but we didn't get chance as we actually had not finished our breakfast so needless to say he didn't get a dime!
Apart from that the hotel is okay, not special as we found that the rooms needed some TLC, a bit of dust on surfaces & the shower was dirty and needed a rinse out. For the price we paid it was fine but I wouldn't stay here again.

title: “Disappointing! Not comparable to a standard Hampton Inn.”
text: I normally enjoy booking at Hampton but this one was quite mediocre compared to it's peers. Room smelled humidity, bathroom is not clean! Although night staff was nice, the day staff was quite cold! I will not return evev the location is quite good for a visitor to NY.

title: “Wonderful if you get a deal and use some helpful hints”
text:
I was very pleased with my experience at the Clift, although I am glad I read this website before getting there. The room was pleasant and clean. The bed and linens were so comfortable. And the staff was extremely pleasant and helpful.
Firstly, my husband and I arrived at the hotel at 9:30 in the morning, and they let us check in early (no added fee). Our bellman chatted with us the entire way up about cool places to go and see while in town. And when we wanted directions to drive to Muir Woods, they already had them printed out and found them for us very quickly. 
For people who were dissatisfied with their visit, I think you have to know what you are getting into. This is a hip, trendy spot that caters to people who fancy themselves as hip and trendy. This is NOT a family oriented place where you spend the afternoon with your kids hanging out by the pool.
That being said, the picetag for this hotel is slightly excessive... we got a deal through orbitz where our room ended up costing about $150/night for a 3 night stay (fri to mon), and I would have been annoyed if we had paid full price for the stay. Also, the bahroom is small, but as my husband and I are pretty thin and short, so it didn't bother us at all.
Some helpful tips:
1. Ask for an interior or courtyard room. We did, and they were happy to oblige us with one on the 4th floor... we heard NO traffic noise.
2. Don't park here if you can help it... it is overpriced! We rode the BART into town and walked the few blocks to the hotel, then rented a car only for the day we needed it at Enterprise at the Nikko Hotel (about 3 short blocks away) for $25/day and returned it the same day so we didn't need to pay for parking. Alternatively, there is a lot 1/2 a block down the street on Taylor where they'll park your car for $18 overnight.
3. The hotel restaurant is also overpriced... skip it and try Scala's Bistro at the Sir Francis Drake hotel on Powell. The meals at Scala's excellent in quality. The portion size is perfect (NOT huge so there is room for dessert). 
4. Place the Do Not Disturb tag on your doorknob if you want to sleep in. The cleaning crew are serious about their business and came around at 8am to check the room, and again at 9am to see if we were gone so that they could clean the room.
5. $10 for ethernet connection?!??!?!? You can walk to union square and use the free wi-fi while sitting outside and enjoying the park.

title: “Slept like a baby”
text: I stayed at the Hilton Checkers Jan. 5 on business. The room was very nice, clean and well appointed. I don't usually sleep well in hotel rooms, but the bed, linens and quiet of the room helped me sleep through the night soundly. The hotel staff could have been more helpful about pointing out the bar/restaurant, roof-top pool, etc. None of this was mentioned upon check-in. I would stay here again, knowing I'd sleep well and have a luxurious room in downtown LA.

title: “Perfect location!”
text:
The location of New York Inn is amazing! You can walk for everywhere! Just some blocks from Times Square!
The staff is really really friendly and veeeery kind!
I really recomend!

title: “Excellent place to stay”
text: This hotel and Washington itself was an unexpected delight in our 2 week tour of New York and Maryland. We stayed for 2 nights in August but wish we had stayed longer. It was a very comfortable and elegant hotel. Our room was clean, large and quiet. The gardens were beautiful. We had a problem with the air conditioning but they fixed it without us asking. The hotel is very close to the subway and a quick 2 dollar ride into central Washington. It is also across the street from a variety restuarants and cafes. Would definitely return.

title: “Awesome location with really cool vibe”
text: I stayed here with a friend of mine on our first trip to New York July 2011. It was a quick weekend gettaway to see some broadway shows. This hotel was really cool! The room was compact but pretty sweet with a bed that folded back into a couch for more room, "mood lighting" around, a glass shower and full legth glass window to look at New York. Plus, it came with a really good price. It was just a couple blocks to get anywhere we wanted to go and there was a club and AMAZING Sunday brunch all offered in the hotel. The people staying there seemed to be a hip crowd in their late 20s, early 30s. The only negative was using the bathroom or taking a shower being that I went with another female friend - it was a small space and you do not have privacy. But we were hardly in the room so it didn't matter too much.

title: “European Boutique”
text: A lovely little european style boutique hotel with a cheery dining room for breakfast

title: “Great Hotel, Great Location”
text: Stayed at the Doubletree for a conference and was very impressed with the attentive staff and facilities. Rooms had wonderful views of the city and beds were extremely comfortable.

title: “Days inn Payne branch Rd. INDY”
text: We travel to Indy every year for a convention. We picked this hotel because it looked nice! No way buddy! Hotel was short handed and our room wasn't service 3 out of the 6 days there. The other 3 days, the maids would try to walk right in...we were told they were short staffed. Don't get me started on the FREE wifi...that didn't work either which was bad news for me because I had work to do! Beds were okay- bath room tub was peeling...not alot of water pressure.

title: “A night at the Hotel Brexton”
text: We recently spent the night at the Hotel Brexton during a very busy weekend in Baltimore (Dragon boat charity races, Living Social deals about to expire, etc.). When we first arrived, I was concerned that the intimacy of the hotel and the central location would mean that it would be noisy - my main concern when spending the night away from home. It turned out that, despite being booked full, it was wonderfully quiet. The room was attractive and comfortable, with a nice view and all of the amenities we could want. We especially enjoyed the little garden area; it was a peaceful place to enjoy morning coffee. The staff was wonderful, from the general manager's assistance in making our reservation to Eboni's help with navigating the city using the Charm City Circulator. We definitely recommend the Hotel Brexton as an excellent place to stay while visiting Baltimore.

title: “Good Price, Good Location, Knows it's demographic.”
text:
Stayed here with a friend for a recent trip to NYC. We stayed in a a bunk bed pod, which we both enjoyed. The room was small and the picture of it on the website is a pretty accurate representation of the room. The room included a stand-alone sink and vanity area, which we found quite useful . Each individual bunk had a personal reading light and small flat screen tv. Each room also includes an ipod docking station, ours was unfortunately malfunctioning.
The bunk bed pods use shared bathrooms (which is why the in-room sink was so useful) and we found that the bathrooms were clean and convenient. Our pod included a little sign over the door indicating which restrooms were occupied, which was very useful for planning showers and such. 
The elevators were a little bit slow, especially during "rush" hours, but this is pretty common in many older New York buildings, so it didn't bug us much. There are brightly colored murals on the wall and music plays in the hallways and bathrooms. 
The location was great, it is on the east side in midtown, and is quite close to several subway lines (notably the E and the 6). 
The one note of buyer beware is that this hotel is aimed at a very specific demographic. Young, hip, and ready to party. As a result the guests can be little louder and rowdier than one might want, but I can't fault the hotel for appealing so strongly to it's demographic. 
For under a 100 dollars (including tax) it was a fun experience. I would recommend this hotel to anyone willing to try something a little different, and who is pretty easy-going.

title: “What a great stay!”
text: I came to Boston to attend meetings, but brought my husband to have a quick weekend retreat. Our room was amazing - simple, streamlined and modern. We spent some time in Woodward (bar/restaurant in Ames) and met some incredibly nice people....the food, drinks and atmosphere were all top notch. While Lauren behind the bar could have been a bit warmer and friendlier overall the service in Woodward was great. Charles the concierge at the Ames was fantastic with restaurant recommendations. I will definitely recommend this hotel to others and will for sure stay there again.

title: “The concierges saved the day!!!”
text:
Hotel Commonwealth is excellently located right next to the metro station with loads of restaurants, pubs, a 711, and ofcourse, Fenway Park, the home stadium for the Boston Red Sox team. The rooms are fabulous...large, quiet, luxurious and very comfortable. 
But the one thing that makes this place the absolute tops is the staff...we landed there around 9pm and my colleague discovered that he had left his cellphone in the cab that brought us to the airport. Samuel, the concierge got into action right away, calling up all the cab companies in Boston to check whether the cab was theirs. Fortunately, the phone was located and all was well! 
Then on the day we were leaving, I discovered that British Airways would not take a golf club unless it was packed adequately to prevent any damage to the Club. Again, the concierge, this time it was Bryan, who told me to head off for my sightseeing tour and not worry about it, because he would make sure that it was packed securely. And sure enough, when I got back to the hotel, it was all done...he had got hold of some fedex containers and bubble wrap and packed it super securely!!! 
Thanks guys, you prevented the trip from being a disaster and turned it into a wonderful one. Hope to be back sometime.

title: “Good hotel, comfortable stay.”
text: Check-in was smooth and front desk staff was fairly helpful. Rooms were clean and well kept, rooms on the east side of the hotel have fantastic views of the river, Cambridge, and Downtown. The property is a bit out of the way from the main parts of the city, but it was easy enough to hop on a bus to Central Square and take the T wherever we needed to go. Overall it was a good stay for my wife and I, and given the rate we obtained we would not have a problem staying there again.

title: “Convenient, quiet, good service”
text: Two friends and I spent two nights here and was very pleased. We all stayed in one room with two queen beds and there was plenty of room for all of us. The location is only two blocks from Grauman's Chinese Theater, the Walk of Fame and the Hollywood Highlands (which had great restaurants and shopping). Valet parking was $20 per day and well worth it. We did not use our car and walked everywhere. Free breakfast was included which was on the fourth floor which was where our room was. The desk clerks were extremely nice and helpful. They recommended places to eat and answered all our questions. Internet service worked perfectly plus we noticed a computer open to the public on our floor. Only one slight problem - the tv remote would not work - but someone was sent up and he promptly fixed it. Despite being in the hubble of downtown Hollywood, the room was very quiet.

title: “Satisfactory Stay in the City”
text:
I stayed at the Duane with a friend in a Superior King room. It's a boutique hotel, and was a decent value overall for a peak weekend in NYC in a good location close to lower Manhattan and SoHo/Village. It was very clean and our 6th floor room was quiet (with the exception of our neighbor slamming the door to their room occasionally). Others have commented on the subway rumbling; I'm a very light sleeper, and was not bothered by it.
I've been to NYC several times, so expected a small room, and that's certainly what we got. However, the space planning could be better. They should consider replacing the (quite comfortable) king bed with a queen or nixing the platform that takes up several inches of prime real estate (and has very sharp corners). My friend and I bonded while getting ready in the tiny bathroom, and would have appreciated another mirror in the room itself. There was only one outlet (in the bathroom) so we had to move furniture to access others. We didn't eat at the hotel, but the restaurant seemed popular both Friday and Saturday nights.

title: “Management - Please read this”
text:
I am a frequent guest at this location. After the renovation was mostly complete, the overall feel of the hotel was clean and new....BUT...on almost every trip, the housekeeping is a real sore spot. When I stay in a hotel, I expect the bathrooms to be clean. Clean to me means not having to sweep the hair of previous guests off the floor or rinse it from the sink. On many occasions, the bathroom floors and entry wood floors were just plain dirty. Very much so. I have washed blood off the floor, wiped up whatever my shoes stuck to walking in the room, etc. 
Routinely finding hair stuck to pillows is also not something I value - same for food on the floor
. 
Some rooms seem to have been poorly outfitted with the updated furnishings with floor lamps missing already and cable wire just strung across the wall or running across carpets to the new wall mounted tv in a few rooms.
Overall, since the location is convenient for my stay, I have put up with the lack of care the housekeeping staff displays, but am strongly considering taking my business up Rte 1 to another major chain where I have not experienced this type of indifference. If I was a GM here, the housekeeping supervisor would be looking for another job.
Sincerely,
Starwood Preferred Guest - Gold Level

title: “Great stay!”
text:
Just back from a week stay at the Courtyard Marriot San Diego LIberty Station. This was an altogether pleasant experience from beginning to end. The staff, from the front desk to the restaurant, deli and housekeeping were excellent. They were consistently friendly, polite and very helpful in regards to remedying a tiny concern we had. (missing sofa chair in our room). The rooms are well appointed and very comfortable. 
 In terms of location the hotel is near the airport, however, if you know San Diego this is not far from the city at all and also very close to Old Town. We had a car so the ample free parking at the hotel was a bonus. As parking in the city can be tricky we did cab it one night at a price of 16 dollars each direction. Parking at Old Town in the various San Diego State Park parking lots (free) or on the street never gave us a problem. I personally would be more than happy to stay at this hotel again and expect I very likely will in the not too distant future. Great stay!

title: “Terrific hotel and staff !”
text: Stayed at Hotel Cass on January 19, for 4 nights in corner room 1508. I`m Platinum Ambassador within Priority Club and was very impressed with their treatment of me and my status. I originally booked a queen room but requested a king on my reservation. When I checked in, the lady at the front desk recognized my status, welcomed me and addressed me by my last name, upgraded me to a corner king room and in addition credited my account 2500 bonus points just for being platinum. The hotel itself is completely renovated and everything has a new look. The room is very high tech, huge TV, lots of outlets, night-reading lamps on the bed, brand new carpet, wonderful high-pressure shower head and even a safe. Service was exceptional especially considering that it`s only a Holiday Inn Express. It rivals the full service hotels and even better than most of them. From valet to front desk to housekeeping and breakfast attendants, everyone seemed ready to help and always smiled and greeted me with good morning and have a great day. The head valet guy always opened the door for everyone coming in and going out of the hotel. And of course, free WI FI and full hot breakfast is included which is a great value. There are two elevators and they are fast and efficient. Valet parking is $40 (in and out privileges) and is very competitive considering that most surrounding hotels charge at least $45 or $50. If you want great value, a clean and modern boutique hotel, at a great location and with courteous and professional staff, the Cass Holiday Inn Express is the place for you.

title: “Wonderful Service, Clean Hotel”
text: The moment we arrived at the hotel, we were impressed with the service. The doormen could not help you enough with unloading luggage and opening doors. On approaching the desk we were assisted straight away very efficiently. They found our booking and said that they would find us a better room, it took less than 5 minutes to check in which is just what we needed after a long journey. Although it was a bit of a trek from the lifts, the room was spacious and clean and the view over the city and bay was magnificent. The room was well equipped and the complimentary coffee and newspaper delivered at the time you specify every morning is a great idea. The only problem we did have was the cost of the drinks in the bar - far too costly so we just drank and ate elsewhere and brought our own drinks in for a nightcap. The hotel also had no problem with us ordering a takeaway and taking it to our room. The location was not really in the tourist area and was a major walk to anywhere, however we hired a car and had it valet parked in the hotel (this was rather costly also but not bad compared to other car parks in the area). A beautiful place to stay with very unintrusive yet efficient service where nothing was too much trouble. Thank you to all the staff.

title: “GLAD TO BE BACK!”
text: Me and my sister have just returned to the New Yorker for a 5 day stay,we got the same room as last year which was massive,2 large queen beds overlooking the hudson river,large flat screen in the room,i emailed before we travelled and asked if there was any chance of an upgrade,emailed straight back and said we could have same room! We like this hotel due to its location,5 minute walk from Penn station,10 minute walk to bus station (we used the train to get from Newark $12.50,and the newark airport bus to get back $15.00),both of these were easy use and so much cheaper,cost us $85 in a taxi last year! The location is great,5 minutes to Macys,10 minutes to Times Square,10 minutes to 5th Avenue,Maddison Square gardens is across the road,across the road is Mc donalds,burger king,wendys and plenty of cheap places were the locals eat,we used these,great food and very cheap. The hotel has great security,need to show pass before using the lifts, a $300 deposit is required when checking in either by card or in dollars,when checking out can leave your bags in storage for a dollar a bag until time to leave for your flight home. Some reviews sound so bad,i can only say i have been twice and if i return to New York this will be my choice again,excellent.

title: “Awful; Good Thing It Was Free...”
text:
Was booked here overnight for free by US Air because I volunteered for a flight the following morning. The hotel's airport shuttle took almost an hour to pick us and others up at CLT. Driver offered nothing but lame excuses, when a simple apology probably would have sufficed. Upon arrival, checked into hotel and observed/experienced the following:
1. Ripped and stained bed sheets (very disgusting). Very worn bedspreads. Skimpy pillows. Dirty drapes. Dirty carpet.
2. Toilet ran continuously after flushing.
3. Never received the requested wake-up call.
4. Indifferent staff.
5. Not enough vans immediately on hand for the morning shuttle.
If it was a good place to stay, it's not anymore. Plenty of other options (Mariott, Hilton, etc.) nearby. 
If I was paying for it, and it wasn't so late at night, I would have de-registered and walked out. Avoid like the plague.

title: “Great location, great service, comfy room”
text:
My wife and I stayed a night at the Edgewater for a single night. We took advantage of a breakfast promotion that gave us a waterside room, breakfast, and free parking for $299
The room was nicely furnished in a rustic style. Very small, but it had high ceilings which really helped. The small balcony provided us with a great view of the water, though I would have liked to be a little further out (the building is a long rectangle that sticks out into the water) so that we could have seen more of the water and less of the adjacent pier. Watching the traffic on the water was really interesting, with tug boats meeting up with cargo ships and constant ferry traffic.
The room seemed very clean. The bathroom was excellent, with stone tiles and a very nice stone-lined shower with plenty of water pressure.
Things were a bit noisy through the door from the hallway, but perhaps to be expected on a Saturday night. I didn't notice any noise from adjacent rooms.
The desk staff and valets were very courteous and helpful. We were supplied with a voucher for breakfast, which we ate in the restaurant. We had a very sizable meal and ordered juices, and all of it (including the gratuity) was covered through the special deal. The waiter was very pleasant, and we felt obliged to go ahead and tip despite the voucher.
All-in-all, I would definately consider returning to the Edgewater, but It is a bit overpriced at rack rates. However, most downtown Seattle hotels are overpriced, and the Edgewater certainly has one of the better locations.

title: “Chic in great location.”
text: Close to Union Square and theaters, great hotel with excellent service. Love the pacman game in the lobby (the one kid-friendly thing there). Not a hotel for families unless you are ok with the dj/bar scene at night. (My kid loved that).

title: “Fancy smoking in a non-smoking room stay here....mmmmm....???”
text:
Just completed a 5 night stay here. This is my first trip to New York and we realised quite early on that the location of the hotel was perfect. 
We negotiated a good deal via e-mail and booked about 3 months or so in advance. 
On arrival at the hotel we were greeted by the doorman who took care of our cases straight out of the taxi and on entering the hotel we were offered a slightly larger room for $30 a night which we declined. 
We were located at the end of the 4th floor. The room itself was very small by hotel standards but did include all the amenities specified on the website.
After the first night it was clear that either someone was smoking in the corridor or in one of the rooms on our floor and the smoke was either coming under the door or through the air conditioning. We went to reception the following morning to enquire whether the floor was solely non smoking and they advised it was but they did allow guests to smoke in the them on the 4th floor........what ????.....who was staying ont he floor the Sultan of Brunei or the president ????? Either they are non smoking or they're not. We were told that if it was "bothering us that much" then we could swap rooms. On the basis that it would have been a big hassle to move rooms and if we had have moved other smokers could be allowed to we declined.
We ended up putting towels around the bottoms of the doors to limit the cigarette smoke.
We are still in New York as we had plabbed on going to Atlantic City but the bus service was not running due to the snow. We decided not to opt for the $500+ for the additional night at the Iroquois and instead opted for the Hilton Garden Inn at Times Sqaure, where the rooms are rather larger and the reviews on trip advisor some what better.0
Gregorys coffee shop across the road serves great coffees and snacks.
Used the gym, although you have to call reception in advance to use the sauna. You also have to request ice as there is no ice machine....seems like a hassle to request to have the mini-bar emptied if you require use of the fridge. Why not ask in advance and let the guest decide ?
Didn't use the restaurant, but did go to the Indian on 44th street towards 5th Avenue, was probably the best Indian I've had in the US, but not perfect.
Pros: Great nights sleep, nice bed, good location, dvd library, free internet and printing facility in the library.
Cons: The lifts are slow, they allow smoking in the non-smoking rooms/corridors, the shower was pretty poor as you had to have the tap running at the same time as the shower, bath didn't drain quick enough so showered in inches of water, toilet blocked on first day - sorted it myself. The noise from the adjoining room was very loud when they used the toilet (i presume) - my wife described it as a large boat coming into dock.
From a value for money perspective I'd prefer the Hilton over the Iroquois if coming again and there's more space.....depending on what floats your boat it may be to some peoples standards, particularly smokers.

title: “appreciated manager”
text: We stayed at the Westin with another couple. The special was "stay 2 nites, get the 3rd night free" ended up costing 176.00 a night plus tax. This isn't so bad for a North Michigan Ave. hotel. Our friends were on the top floor. We were on the 18th. They managed to have no coffee 2 of the 3 days and no towels 1 of the 3 days. Was it because they were at the end of the hall and housekeeping ran out? Don't know; but it was annoying to say the least. Turns out the front desk manager, Kelly made up for it and gave us enough certificates for dinner in the restaurant. Tried to pay with those certificates and the waiter said, "Oh these are for room service" So we put them on our rooms and Kelly took them off. Turned a bad experience into a major thank you.

title: “Great place to stay”
text: I can't say enough about the staff, we felt welcome from the moment we got there and the waitress at the breakfast was the best. This was a very convenient hotel. They had a laundry room so we could wash our granddaughters softball uniform and she was ready for 3 more games the next day. THe Garden Inn was close to restaurants and a theater.

title: “Wonderful place”
text:
We stayed only one night on our return from Beijing.
Our room was spotless and very quiet.
Highly recommended.
M

title: “Great View”
text: Nice bedrooms perfect for the Family , the staff were very helpfull specialy at the Bar, the view was great and it only took us 5 minutes to walk to all the restaurants and Bars

title: “Understated elegance in the heart of manhattan”
text: My husband and I enjoyed a weekend in Manhattan at the Library Hotel. We found our accomodations to be clean, our room was a good size (for nyc standards) and the hotel offered many amenities not found out other hotels, including a wine and cheese reception each night. Given the location, amenities and cleaniness we found this hotel to be an excellent value and hope to return soon.

title: “Really needs updating.”
text: Room with kitchen nice idea, but this place REALLY NEEDS UPDATING. Room decor is old and dreary, which makes it seems "not clean", even though it's cleaned daily. For some reason, they skipped cleaning our room one day.

title: “Good take”
text:
This is a bit out of Pike's Peak area, but a good take for a family. We were able to get a nice Suite for less than the cost of two rooms downtown. The hotel is on a trolley line that runs downtown very quickly and frequently. There is a cove across the street with three good restaurants - Duke's Chowder house is a good casual call. Buca di Beppo is a fun Italian place three blocks away. 
Hotel has a gym (sort of lame, but there), pool, and business center. The include breakfast is very complete - eggs, oatmeal, etc - not simply rolls and coffee. 
Not the best take for a business traveler who needs to be downtown, but it was a great fit for our family visit.

title: “Comerica Park/Ford Field location”
text:
Fantastic location for Tiger games at Comerica Park or Lions games at Ford Field. One short block away. Hotel is decent, but plain and nothing all that special. Very small pool in the lower level of the hotel. Purely a location stay.
Greektown is a block away for good food and some old school bars.

title: “Pretty good for what I paid”
text:
My wife and I stayed in the Marina Tower on Saturday November 20th. We thought it might not be too busy on the weekend before Thanksgiving but it was quite full. We got this hotel for a priceline bid of $65 and given the choice between the second floor or paying $20 for the top floor we opted for the top floor. 
The view of the bay and city skyline from our room was incredible. There was a storm passing that night and we got great pictures of the city with the changing weather. Being close to the airport we could hear the jets taking off but we brought a fan with us for white noise and had no trouble sleeping.
The room was average sized and the bed was a bit firm but not overly so. The bathroom was clean and the only thing missing was a vent fan. The balcony had 2 chairs and a small table.
Although I hate to pay for parking, from previous stays around downtown San Diego the $22/day fee was par for the course. The parking lots are off to the side of the main enterance and can get congested at times. The overflow parking is not paved and was a bit muddy during the storm.
Overall it was a good value for what we paid. We only left the hotel to attend a football game at Qualcomm Stadium and had no trouble getting to and from I-5. With this in mind not being close to restaurants, shops, etc. was not a big issue; but, would prefer to stay in downtown within walking distance of the Gas Lamp Quarter otherwise.

title: “Great hotel near Penn Station and Times Square”
text: We took the train to NYC with the family. The hotel was One block from the station, and close to Times Square. We had a great time! The staff was friendly and helpful. The hotel was fairly clean and well kept (the shower cleanliness was my only complaint). The continental breakfast every morning was a little hectic, but what do you expect when it is free (or included in the price). Overall, I would stay there again without hesitation.

title: “Beautifull artwork, poorly designed lobby”
text:
The Hyatt Regency Convention Center hotel was absolutely beautiful. The lobby and hallways were filled with strikingly beautiful artwork. Even the walls next to the elevator were lined with leather with detailed stitching. 
We stayed on the concierge club level. The staff at the concierge lounge were friendly and welcoming. In fact we dropped into the lounge several times each day to pick up a cup of coffee and chat with the staff. For me, talking with the staff at the club lounge was one of the highlights of our stay at the hotel. 
I also liked the hotel's fitness area. It was well designed and there were plenty of machines for everyone who wanted to exercise. 
But the main reason to stay at the Convention center hotel is its proximity to the convention center. It was just a short walk across the street to the convention center. Especially in a city like Denver that can have quick changes in weather that was a big plus.
The major down side of this hotel is the poor design of its lobby. The lobby has a number of opposing energies. There are several beautifully serene pieces of artwork that envoke the feeling of nature and ancient cultures. There are also other pieces of artwork that are fantastically vibrant and modern. Unfortunately they are all stuck together in one big immense room, so the room has no overall feeling. 
In the corner of this immense lobby there is a mini nightclub/lounge area. The brash loud nose of the lounge spills over into the entire lobby. When I was checking in to the hotel, the front desk staff were repeatedly apologizing for the loud noise. 
The funny thing was that the band was fantastic. It's just that after sitting for several hours on a plane and then sitting on a cramped shuttle bus not everyone wants to listen to loud rock and roll music while they are waiting to be checked-in.
But overall, there were many wonderful things about the Hyatt Regency Convention Center Hotel. If I attend another convention in Denver I will definately stay there again.

title: “You get what you pay for.”
text:
Admittedly, I stayed here because it was the cheapest room I could find before I got to Phoenix and I just wanted a place to sleep for one night.
Let me explain the set up there. There is a main wing perpendicular to the road, an outdoor pool and parking, then a short wing parallel to the road creating a T. Though the front clerk seemed like a high school student with no training, the check in was smooth enough. I was checked into the rear wing. It seems to be occupied by long term residence. They were cooking on the upstairs walk way and were talking to each other from many units away from each other. It was a little noisy but I tried to nap about 5pm. I get a knock on the door and it was from someone looking for someone else. I called the front desk and asked for a room in the front wing but is told none were available.
I couldn't sleep now so I tried to get on the internet. After repeated failure, I call the front desk and she said, "Lots of people tell me that but keep trying. Eventually you connect." I think its more a case of eventually people give up and stop calling the front desk. So I walk to the front lobby and the w-fi worked there. People are calling for rooms and she is telling them that the rates are double of what I paid.
I left for dinner and returned about 11. People were still talking to each other outside. I was tired so I fell asleep okay. I got a phone call at 1 am asking for the same person the afternoon visitor asked for. You could still hear people talking and yelling outside, especially as cars arrived and left the parking area at this time. 
Then at 5 am, I got a pounding on the door again while calling for the person again. I looked out the window and told the person she had the wrong room. At 730 when I left, that female that was knocking at 5 was still sitting on the stairway in front of the room and asked if I could help her.
Final thing, they say Continental Breakfast. They had a dozen bite sized muffins on a lobby counter with no drinks (hot or cold) or water.
Bottom line, it was cheap (on a very busy weekend because of spring training) and very convenient to the freeway. I would stay there again if I was by myself and could specifically stay for the front wing. I would not bring my family there under any circumstance.

title: “Wonderful hospitality”
text:
When we walked in the door, the Guest Services Manager Barbara Parker immediately asked us what we wanted to see in San Antonio, then suggested a tour package. They were so Interested in making our stay comfortable and fun. We enjoyed our stay.
Our GPS had trouble finding the hotel, making us go way out of our way. Call the hotel for better directions.

title: “Excellent hotel”
text: There's only two things this hotel needed to make the best for me, a microwave and mini fridge in the regular rooms! We stayed three nights and the staff was excellent very professional and acted like they where truly happy to see us!

title: “As good as all the reviews say”
text: We stayed here for 2 nights in August. Contrary to what others have said our room was quiet even though it was right next to the elevator. The layout of the room was perfect and included a kitchenette and sitting area. It was really clean and the bathroom offerred the best water pressure of all the hotels we stayed in on our 21 day holiday. The evening reception meal, while nothing special was adequate if you were looking to save money on eating out. Although the building itself is old it is well maintained and has some beautiful art deco features. The bed was comfortable. The location of the hotel was excellent and only a short walk to Beale Street. A great little shop for snacks and groceries was close by. Aside from any of that what really makes a stay memorable is the friendliness of the staff and this hotel is exceptional. I'd particularly like to single out the lovely and helpful man who did the valet parking for us, I think his name was Jerome. Overall we would stay here again and recommend it to others.

title: “Really cool hotel!!”
text: Stayed at the new Yotel Aug 2011. Room was small (as us the norm in NYC) but very well designed - glass bathroom and bed that retracted into a sofa at the touch of a button made the room feel more spacious. Glass wall bathroom with curtain for privacy - only share a room with someone you know well!! Free muffins were good for breakfast. No frills, but very comfortable, clean, nice design. Fast and easy check in/out. Location wasn't amazing but was fine... Nice view from rooms. Would stay again!

title: “Fantastic stay at the Hyatt Place!! Would stay again. :)”
text:
We stayed for one night at the Hyatt Place after our cruise, before flying home to Canada. The staff was amazing!! The friendly and capable shuttle driver Tony, picked us up at the airport and brought us back the next day on the free shuttle. Tatiana made us feel very welcome when we arrived at the front desk. She booked us into a beautiful room that was simply gorgeous. Clean, spacious and elegant! The king sized bed and the bedding was so comfy! The carpet was spotless as were the lovely granite countertops and beautiful bathroom amenities. We loved the cozy sitting area in our room and the huge flat screen TV. 
Christina from the front desk was so helpful in informing us about the local area and she drove us to the local mall. (they provide free shuttle service within 5 miles from hotel) Christina was a delight to chat with! 
We had a delicious complimentary breakfast before leaving for our flight. Great variety of cereals, breads, muffins, fruit salad, yogurt, juices, coffee and designer teas and fresh fruit. (My husband also loved the complimentary Granny Smith and Red Delicious apples available at any time) 
The weather was cool and overcast on the day we arrived so we decided against using the pool but it looked beautiful, inviting and clean. Would definitely make use of the pool on an other visit. The gym was clean and had some good standard (6 or 7) machines which was enough for a quick workout. Again everything was clean, clean, clean!
We were thoroughly impressed with our stay at the Hyatt Place by the IAH Airport in Houston and would stay there again in a heartbeat. NO complaints and a HUGE thank-you to the wonderful staff for making our stay so pleasant.

title: “Wonderful Hotel! Lovely Room! Superb Staff! Great Location!”
text:
We stayed at the Orchard Garden Hotel for one weekend night in April 2010. I love the Hotel, the location, the room, the staff. All made for a perfect stay. We were taking friends from out of the country for their return flight home and chose the Orchard Garden for our their last nights stay in the US. We were not disappointed! 
You can't go wrong here. Even though the hotel was close to capacity you seldom saw any other guests. The rooms were quiet and restful. The bed was so comfortable. You're a half a block from the Bush Street enterance to Chinatown, 3 1/2 blocks from Union Square, 2 1/2 block for the Powel cable car line, 1 block from parking. We will definitely be back!

title: “Did I mention the internet costs extra?”
text:
New York is a truly great city, and if you stay at the Roosevelt you'll be in a good location to see a lot of it. Occupying a block all to itself on Madison Avenue and West 45th Street, it's easy to walk from the hotel to the Empire State Building, Grand Central Station, Times Square, the United Nations Building...in fact anywhere in mid-town Manhattan.
But did I enjoy my stay? Frankly, no. I was working, not touring, and that means for me I'm looking for service and value. And I didn't find much of it. Yes, the lobby is seriously impressive, and has probably featured in a dozen Hollywood films. But I wasn't sleeping in the lobby. My 4th floor room was down a long gloomy corridor, and looked as tired as I felt after my transatlantic flight. The rack rate for that room is, I was told, more than $400 per night, room only, during December. That must only be for the location, because the room was nothing special - functional but rather empty, in fact, with no touches of comfort, no fridge, no mini-bar, no sofa, no coffee table (and no coffee).
To me, one of the most important details in a hotel room nowadays is the provision of good quality, Wifi internet, and for it to be included in the room price. At the Roosevelt, there is Wifi but it's not included: it's $15 per day, PER DEVICE! so if you've got a laptop, and an iPad that's $30, thank you very much. I am told, but didn't verify, that I would have paid again had I tried to use my computers on a different floor from my room! Paying for the internet sticks in my throat in New York: it's widely available for free at most cafes and restaurants, as well as shops like Best Buy and Staples. So why make hotel guests pay if they want to work in their rooms? "Because we can", seemed to be the answer. I refused to pay the internet rate, and took my devices elsewhere, and resented it every time I did so.
Tip 1: take your own travel kettle: there is no facility in the room for making a hot drink so take your own, plus tea bags, coffee, sugar etc. Paper cups are provided, and they will take a hot drink.
Tip 2: Three minutes from the Roosevelt Hotel across Madison Avenue there is a great bar/restaurant called Cinema The Brasserie at 2 East 45th Street. Lovely food, super service, friendly people. Oh and guess what? The high speed internet is free! Why don't they do rooms too?
Tip 3: you can get a taxi from the hotel for $60 fixed price to JFK airport. The door man will fix this. It's the same price as a yellow cab on the street, so don't be put off because the hotel cab is a fancier vehicle.

title: “Terrible Dishonest Service-Beware of this hotel!”
text: I have never had a worst experience at a hotel than at this location. Basically, we left Sea World and arrived at theNorthwest San Antonio location. The clerk that checked us in at first stated that his system was down and he could not find our reservation. When he was able to get back on the system, he said he could not find our reservation/confirmation number, but that they had plenty of space available. He did not divulge that there was another Days Inn within four or five miles of that location. Being unfamiliar with the area, and knowing that we were in fact in the Northwest area of San Antonio, we stayed at this location. When we decided to stay another night, we made another online reservation. Upon arriving home, we discovered that we had been charged double for two different nights. When we filed a complaint with Days Inn, they discovered that we had actually booked with the other Northwest location. They claimed that since it was a so-called "booking" error that we were not due any recompense. I feel that we were dealt with in a dishonest manner by this hotel. I feel extremely let down by people not using even basic good business practices.

title: “Great resort, rooms okay”
text: The location and resort are wonderful. Minutes from Sea World and right on the beach. Resort offers activities (boat rentals, wave runners, water trikes, etc) or you can relax on the beach or in the pool. They also have a great kiddie pool. I especially liked the poolside cabana which offered drinks and food. The rooms are okay. THey are clean but they are in need of renovation. Would return to this hotel. If you are looking for a beach atmosphere and you are not going to spend a lot of time in the hotel room, this place is great.

title: “Nice hotel with expensive internet”
text: The hotel is difficult to find when you arrive by bus from the airport. It stops right next to the hotel. You have to find your way through a shopping mall.. But the hotel is fine and the prices reasonable. You can have breakfast in the restaurant or in their Starbucks. Coffee facilities in the room. Their internet is expensive - more than 10 dollars a day !!!

title: “Really Outstanding Service and Value”
text:
Stayed at the Amalfi for an anniversary weekend getaway in mid-August. We chose the Amalfi because we felt the rate we got was a good value given that it included valet parking and complimentary breakfast (all rates include the breakfast). 
Really glad we chose the Amalfi. We had a corner king room on the top floor. It was an odd shape for a room, but there were basically 15-20 feet of windows that provided an interesting view. The bed was comfortable and the television large, although we never could find the TV remote (only the DVD player remote). I think we could have easily had this taken care of, but we weren't too worried and didn't feel like dealing with it. We had brought some movies from home, so we just watched those. Bathroom was nice and well lit for a hotel in a city center. The theme, a modernist take on the style of the Amalfi Coast in Italy, at first seemed strange for Chicago, but in reality it's a nice way to give some more character to the urban-modern style -- made it feel unique and added charm.
The thing about the Amalfi though that really made it worth staying there was the amazing service. For it's class (upper mid-range) the service was better than I would say we normally recieve. Easy check-in, easy check-out. Really polite, friendly and helpful staff. Excellent breakfast and complimentary cocktail hour (good quality on the beer and cocktails). A nice free perk for our anniversary left in our room. Can't say how impressed I was with the service given the value of the hotel.
Finally, for those who are going as tourists, the Amalfi's location is actually really good. It's on a quieter side street, but the walk to Loop and Museum area attractions is not bad at all (10 mins depending on lights), while it also has proximity to Michigan Ave and the Magnificent Mile. Also near lots of dining options.

title: “Kind, helpful staff and a comfortable hotel!”
text: I wasn't sure about this hotel given some of the previous reviews that I have read but I am a Platinum Priority Club member and wanted to give it a try. I was so pleased!! Not only did I stay here but our larger team used the facilities for a 4-day meeting. All of the meeting space was just perfect. We used several rooms in the Plaza section. My room and the entire hotel decor was lovely. I really enjoyed the lobby area as well. The location was great and there were many fabulous places to eat and shop nearby. The staff went out of the way to be super kind and helpful. I am very grateful to Dale with IT/Audio for his expert help and to Ingrid for making my check-out experience top notch. The room was a little warm for me but given the time of year and the heat, I simply closed the curtains and that helped. The 9th floor, outdoor pool was WONDERFUL, especially at night. The view is spectacular and it is just fun to be on a roof-top pool!!

title: “Very Nice Hotel”
text: Stayed three nights-------perfect location, public spaces were beautiful. I wish the price had been a little lower, but it is high season in NYC right now. We went to the bar for a cocktail. Service was a little slow.

title: “Will definitely go back”
text:
Stayed here twice in July. 
Great hotel, sports bar and Starbucks in lobby , FedEx Office also, beautiful poolside courtyard- could do with a bar there :-), very well equipped gym. The rooms and bathrooms were a bit small.
I was grateful for the luggage scale and flight schedule monitors in the lobby.
Would definitely stay here again and recommend to others.

title: “great, affordable hotel”
text: The Orchard is great, little hotel with a fabulous location. It has friendly staff & is quiet and comfortable.

title: “Perfect stay!”
text: My wife and I stayed here for one night last October. It was a great hotel. We caught the water taxi to the airport which made the commute super easy. I would stay here again!

title: “Would give this a miss next time I visit NYC”
text:
Our stay at the Westin was an odd one in that first impressions were not good, then the place grew on us and then it went downhill from there.
Check-in in the early hours of New Year's Eve went smoothly and we were assigned a room on 29th floor - deluxe king. It was about 2am and our key wouldn't work. That was finally solved and then we got into a room. It was located right next to the express lift shaft. The sounds of lifts passing was like a passing motor vehicle. There were four of them.
The room wasn't the cleanest I had seen either. There were long hairs on the desk chair and dust on the furniture.
We went back to the front desk and asked for a change of room which was greeted without a problem and the next day the change took place, albeit that there was confusion between the front desk and bellman as to whether the room was available or not, buy hey, this is a big hotel and it was busy. No problem.
Our next room on 40th floor was much better, away from the lifts and had an even better view of the first, looking across Manhattan with a view of the soaring Empire State even when lying in bed! 
However, be warned that this is not a quiet hotel. There may be heavenly beds but the noise of people and doors clanging in the corridors simply couldn't be avoided and this was through until our departure on 6 Jan when the New Year crowd had all gone. Also, housekeeping arrive on the corridors about 8.30am and talk loudly. This simply wasn't on. 
Then there's the decor. The rooms look a bit like they've been furnished out of Ikea. Okay for while I guess but I'm not sure I would want to check into this hotel in say, 5 years. The rooms will be falling apart. The brushed steel sinks and units reminded me of a cross between prison cell ones (not that I've been arrested!!) and operating theatres, and our "heavenly bath" had yellow staining by the taps, so we used the "heavenly shower" which was like, er, a regular shower. However, yes, the heavenly beds are just that, heavenly, but like I said earlier, shame about the noise outside the room that woke us.
Having said all this, the views were great, Bar 10 and Shula's were excellent. The staff in these establishments far exceeded that of the hotel staff which is very unsusual I think.
What grated on us at the end of our stay was that housekeeping just gave up on the last day and didn't bother attending on us. We made a request at 2pm and another at 7pm and 8pm and then at 9pm someone finally brought some towels. This made us late for plans for out last night in NY and the attitude of staff was appalling. The front desk made no apology said it was "sold out" so housekeeping was on a "request" basis. 1) I did request it, 2) how would I know that the place was sold out anyway, and 3) I have never heard of this system in this standard of hotel before.
When we finally got out that night, someone came and made the bed and took the rubbish but that was it. No refill of soap, water, coffee, tidy up etc.
Then, on the day of check out, a $250 charge had mysteriously appeared on our bill from the health club. Not thinking this would be a problem if I raised it, I was greeted with suspicion and unprofessionalism. A call was made in front of me to the health club and I was made to wait. I was then told that I had signed a check and that it was being faxed over. When it arrived it clearly was not my signature but had my name on it. It also had a different room number. After a further wait and sample of my signature, I was told that the amount would be cleared and that they would investigate further. I understand that this may not have been the hotel's fault, or it may have simply been an error but what I did not like was the way I was made to feel as though I was pulling a fast one, and how there was no apology for the mistake and for taking up my time. During my waiting at the desk, I also discovered that I had been charged an extra $50 per night on my rate. 
In essence, the majority of front desk staff could use a training course on hospitality and customer relations. 
We then left, rather annoyed, tainting our stay at the Westin but certainly not New York! In future we'll stay elsewhere, and for $429 and $329 a night respectively, it will be in a far superior hotel if we avoid the holiday season.

title: “My stay at La Quinta Inn Dallas Uptown”
text: This LQ property is very well managed. I have stayed at this location numerous times when in Dallas. The location provides quick and easy access to many areas of Dallas. The staff has tenure and some even call you by name - great atmosphere.

title: “Digusting!!! damp & mice droppings- wouldn't even give us a refund.”
text:
The hotel was diguisting sheets were dirty, the curtains had mold and mice droppings on the bathroom counter. We arrived at the Roosevelt at 12:30 am as our flight was delayed. When we arrived our room was not ready so we had to wait 30 minutes. All we done was checked in, then look at room for 10 minutes and then checked out. The front desk would not refund our hotel first night hotels fee, as we had booked through priceline. That night we went to Grand Hyatt , but as I'm a students, my sister and I couldnt afford to stay in the Grand Hyatt throughout the whole of our holiday ,as its quite expensive but it's beautiful hotel, So we had to spend the next day finding a another hotel for the remainder of the trip.
Its not 3.5 hotel, I will never recommended the roosevelt hotel. Buyers beware!!!!

title: “A wonderful Midtown gem”
text:
My husband and I stayed at The Shoreham for our first ever visit to New York and we'll definitely tstay there again. 
The location was perfect. It was near great restaurants, close to the major art galleries, concert halls, Central Park and the subway yet it was surprisingly quiet, especially in the evenings, given its proximity to major thoroughfares. It was also only a couple of blocks away from the subway for the D train which is the line that takes you straight out to the new Yankees baseball stadium within about 25 minutes.
And all the staff, from those on the main desk to the porters, the cleaning staff, the bartenders and waiters were simply fantastic. All were genuinely friendly, helpful and polite. 
We arrived at the hotel considerably later than planned due to delays at the airport and were concerned that perhaps the hotel might have given our rooms away. And because of traffic our taxi couldn’t park right outside the hotel. But as soon as we got our luggage out of the taxi the hotel porter came straight up to greet us in the street and took our luggage into the lobby and then straight up into the room while we checked-in. 
At the check-in desk we were immediately offered complimentary cold drinks which were life savers as we hadn't had a drink for a few hours and we were very hot and tired by the time we arrived. 
We stayed in their Junior Spa suite and when we got into the room it was lovely and cool as the air conditioner had been left on in advance of our arrival. 
The bedroom area was comfortable and the shower room was quite large with great water pressure and super clean with lots of towels. The only thing I missed was one of those extending wall mirrors that has a magnifying lens on one side because I don't have great eyesight and because of the sink I couldn’t get close enough to the main mirror. But there was lots of lighting in the bathroom which was helpful. 
The air conditioner unit was easy to operate and relatively quiet for an air conditioner – there was a slight hum but it didn’t keep us awake. Before arriving we'd read some reviews which said the decor was a bit tired. And it was as there were a few scuff marks here and there on the skirting boards and the furniture in the lounge area did look a bit worn in places but that didn't bother us. There was plenty of room and it was spotlessly clean. The bed was reasonably firm with nice linen and there was lots of good lighting by the bed. There was no wonderful view as the room but again that wasn't a priority for us. The elevator was big enough for 2 adults and 2 suitcases but no more. The room was also quiet and we didn't hear our neighbours except when they were outside in the corridor.
We ate dinner at the hotel a couple of times, on our first and last night, and both times we were impressed with the standard of the cooking and the quality of the food. The bar and waiting staff were great and mixed great cocktails - my husband said his Manhattan was one of the best he'd every had. And as one of bar tenders had just recently finished his doctoral thesis in American history he was very interesting to talk to and a really nice chap.
