Before arriving we were concerned about tipping especially as we'd heard stories from friends who'd stayed elsewhere who said they always had to have their hands in their pockets ready to tip everyone. But at this hotel the policy is to automatically add on a service charge to say the food or drink bills, which is what we're used to in the UK, which meant we didn't feel obliged to be constantly tipping within the hotel because we knew staff weren't relying on tips to survive.
On the ground floor of the hotel there is a lounge area behind the bar/dining area which, when we were there, had a great display featuring all the best 'on trend' clothes, bags and jewellery as picked from Harpers Bazaar magazine. It was closed when we came across it and I only wished I'd discovered it earlier as it would have been nice to have gone in to have a closer look at all everything before hitting the shops. Although I’m not sure if that’s possible but the window display was still pretty slick so you could see lots of very nice things which really wetted the appetite.
Security was very good in the hotel - visible but low-key - the staff on the main door remembered us from Day One so we came and went as we liked and we felt very safe all the time we were in the hotel. In fact security in general was pretty high in the whole area because while we were there the UN General Assembly was taking place which meant large numbers of diplomats were in town and staying at nearby hotels. There were teams of police practically on every street corner and police cars were constantly patrolling the area. The only downside was that we couldn't get in to visit the UN at any time during our stay. So if the UN is somewhere you want to see don't visit New York during the last two weeks in September when the UN General Assembly are in session. 
Another tip is that the hotel has very good complimentary maps and also stocks complimentary copies of Time Out New York magazine. And their 24 hour coffee/tea area is a great amenity too. They have two internet screens in the downstairs lobby which you can use whenever you want and there's a printer which is also free to use. And once you get a password from the main desk you can also access WiFi. We never got to try out their gym but we had a look 'round and the equipment was what we were used to back in the UK and it looked very clean and well lit with lots of mirrors. 
The hotel also arranged our airport transfers to and from JFK. The cars we both clean and spacious. However, when we arrived we took ages getting through immigration and consequently the driver charged us more than we'd been quoted because of the extra waiting time so bear that in mind if you pre-arrange a taxi pick-up. There seemed to be plenty of taxis at the airport but it was nice to hop into a large air-conditioned car on a hot day.
Lastly, like other trip advisors we found that booking direct via the hotel’s website was more expensive than booking via a specialist travel website. We used a site called newyorkcityluxuryhotels.com who were excellent and able to get us the Junior Spa suite for the same price as a standard room at the hotel.
All in all we had a great time in New York which was due, in no small part, to staying at The Shoreham. If it were a publicly quoted stock we'd be buyers! My husband is already planning our stay there next year. We hope you find the above information useful. Please bear in mind it was our first stay in New York so we don't have any other New York hotel experience to compare it to but even still we really enjoyed our stay at The Shoreham and hope you do too - the staff really are pretty special here.

title: “Run like hell you're not safe here.”
text: Looks ok in the pictures but is a complete dump located in the tenderloin of SF. If you value your safety don't stay here. Hotel was extremely overpriced and misrepresented on the website. Booked through hotels.com and couldn't get any money back after reserving for three nights. Walked out after twenty minutes and found something safe in the marina.

title: “California the way it should be, a perfect hotel for San Diego Sightseeing.”
text:
I just returned for a 3 night weekend stay here with a 45 person family wedding party from Midwest and Eastcoast, and it was really nice, relaxing, hip, trendy and well managed. The rooms are really cool, very Cali in feel, and the bars, pool, and beach lounge great to hangout. Its 3 blocks to the train, and easy walk or taxi to everywhere, or walk, or rent a bike. You can stay in the convention hotels, or the typical sterile ones by the Gaslamp district, which they all looked nice, even the Courtyard and Embassy Suites, but those are cookie cutter hotels that you may as well be in Minneapolis or Atlanta.
The W nails it again, with a nice value property thats unique in decor, feel, mood and ambiance, and everyone in the wedding party loved it, from age 65 to 18.
Rent a car, and take in the sights of Del Mar, La Jolla, and even LA is 2.5 hours north for a day trip.
I stay 4-5 star everywhere, travel 120 days a year, domestic and international, and this hotel at $150 is a delight.

title: “Don't Bring the Kids”
text:
We attended a wedding at the park recpetion center The "Garrison". It was very nice..and very beautiful at night. 
The wait staff..not so nice. There is a older woman who waited on us who was downright mean. She freaked that we had kids at our table. She refused to bring out our food until we removed are children from the table afarid she would "Hurt" them. My daugther had her shoes off. Under the table. She kicked one of her shoes at me. And on top of that was very rude and far too old to be interacting with people--especially children. 
Might want to call ahead to make sure Granny isn't working the day of your event if you have kids attending a wedding.

title: “Good Hotel in a Great Neighborhood”
text: Hotel appearance was clean, simple and modern. Room was kind of smallish but good use of the limited space. Modern appliances in rooms. Location was great with everything within in reasonable walking distance. Definantly well-priced. Only negative was parking was confusing and a little distant from lodging

title: “Nothing like the Affinia!”
text: This was the second time we stayed at the Affinia and, again, we were delighted with the service and the accomodations. We were upgraded upon arrival by the reception staff so that our two rooms could be next to each other - of course, no extra charge. Everyone was pleasant and helpful, from the bellmen and valets to the room and reception staff. Hotel location is excellent - right in the middle of everything and close to great breakfast cafes and restaurants. We travelled with a one year old and have nothing but good things to say about the Affinia. We will certainly stay here again on our next trip.

title: “Quiet Mid Town Sanctuary”
text: Great hotel in central location - turn right out the front of the hotel and in 2 minutes your on 5th Avenue, turn left and in 2 minutes your in the thick of Times Square. Stayed in a Superior room on the 15th floor at the front of the building - good sized room, quiet with a super comfy bed. The foyer is the type of space you will either love or not - its very dark and edgey and feels a bit like a club - would be great in winter when you are after a cosy retreat - but equally cool on a summers day. Service at the hotel is great - nothings too much. Breakfast is wonderful - highly recommended - I think between us we tried most of the menu and its all lovely. If I had to be really fussy I would say the only draw backs would be - limited hanging space and the bathrooms is a little bit tired. STK restaurant at the back of the hotel is great for meat lovers - not the cheapest around but well worth it. All in all - we would stay again as being in a central location in a comfy, quiet spacious room with style is great in such a hectic city!

title: “Happy in El Paso”
text: After visiting back in town to visit family and friends we stayed at the Comfort Inn and we were amazed with the hotel and the customer service we received there! The breakfast is awesome, the staff is courteous, the location is great and I will definitely recommend this hotel and stay there again! Thank you :-)

title: “Typical Airport Marriott”
text: Nice room. Easy check in and check out. Sport bar food was average but good and fast service with free wifi. There was also free wifi in the lobby. Parking at the hotel is very expensive, we talked to the front desk and got them to reduce the daily cost.

title: “Would never go back”
text:
I called while on my way to make a reservation and specifically requested a crib. We arrived late evening, exhausted and ready to go to sleep. After calling several times and even visiting the front desk for over 2 HOURS to ask again and again for the crib and consistently getting "it's coming" they eventually said they could not find one. By now it was nearly 11 pm at night and my 15 month old was so tired. I wish they would have told me that when I called for the reservation or upon arrival.
The next morning we tried a swim in the pool before leaving... the water was so low it was obvious it was not going through the filter and the top had bugs all on it and needed a skim. 
I was unimpressed and would not go back!

title: “Great location if you are passing through”
text:
You can get to the hotel from the walkway, We came in from Terminal E and it was an easy walk. We went out at Terminal C and used the free shuttle bus which runs every 15 minutes but it would have been as easy to walk.
Usual Hilton hotel and had a good nights sleep. 
We also used it on the way home as we were early for check in so we had a meal at the bar/grill and then staying in the hotel and worked on our computer. It would have been better if we could have found comfy chairs in the bar/coffee area.

title: “Will look for other options next trip”
text: Great location, good price. This is about the only positive thing I can say about this place. Front desk staff is rude. If you are debating between this place another, take the other. I read reviews about the rude staff and brushed it off thinking how much will I interact with the front desk. There were so many little things I needed to contact them for that it became more and more frustrating to get any answers. Something as simple as "What is the WiFi password" (which changes daily) turned into 3 calls and 35 hold time. Asked that only the bathroom be cleaned and somehow that translated into fresh towels and empty the trash. The toilet was not cleaned nor was the tub for the 5 days I was there. Everything in the room damp. Our clothes actually felt wet when we got home. $18 parking per day parking, only to be treated like we weren't guests. The only time valet service was polite was when my cute daughter was visiting with us. Sad! When I tried to the contact the hotel about these problems, they have not responded.

title: “Great Location!”
text:
Best thing about this hotel is the view over Central Park and proximity to mid-town.
We had booked a non-smoking Junior Suite on a high floor but when we arrived they only had lower floor suites available. We were convinced that a smoking suite would be fine and we could get a much higher floor. BIG MISTAKE!! As soon as we exited the lift the stench of smoke was overwhelming and the room wasn't much better - the sheets, whilst clean had an overpowering smell of smoke. As it was quite late we stayed one night then switched to a room on the 11th Floor - view was still good and this room was much, much nicer.
Hotel appeared to be run my middle-aged men who weren't really interested in being too helpful, they had an air of superiority which was a bit annoying! 
Good hotel if Central Park and Mid-town areas are where you want to be but would personally try something different next time.

title: “One Night In Austin”
text:
This was a day trip for my husband and I only staying one evening in Austin. This hotel is by far one of the least expensive in the d/t area. Upon arrival, you are allowed to leave your vehicle in the mandatory valet area ($12 a day) long enough to check-in before they park you. Valet staff was personable and friendly. Check-in was met with a smiling face and quick processing. Our room was on the 4th floor just beyond the elevator overlooking the portico and valet area. Not the best view but we were only there one night. Room had a king bed and all areas were clean. Only noise we experienced were the other patrons passing by our door, some with rolling luggage, and other "people noise" on and off throughout the evening.
Check-out was smooth. We didn't partake in the complimentary breakfast but it was bustling at 10am. Husband ran in for a cup of coffee before leaving.
This hotel is the closets to the State Capitol, which was our main point of interest while in Austin. We were about six blocks from 6th street which is in walking distance, but the weather was a bit damp so we drove there. I would recommend La Quinta for the value and convenience!

title: “Quiet and Comfortable”
text: As an IT consultant, I travel for business to the Dallas suburbs of Southlake. The Doral is more remote than the Marriott Solana, but it is newer and the rooms are much nicer, and the beds more comfortable.

title: “Sommerset Suites Hotel”
text: My stay was mostly business but the room was so comfortable and the pool was so clean and warm it made my stay feel like a vacation!

title: “mixed Views”
text:
Chinese owned, nearly new and finished to a high standard. 
Very narrow building with only 3 rooms (?) per floor. water for bathing was turned down to the minimum in room. Poor aspect with views over back alleys. Convenient for downtown but a bit of hike for uptown with the nearest tube (subway) about 1/2 mile and not that easy to get a cab in this quiet backwater. Convenient for chinatown or the over priced restaurants in Little Italy. 
Breakfast is served in a cafe down the road from the hotel, owned by the same people, the choice is limited and the food is poor. Our food and drinks were cold and served on paper plates. We complained but they were not interested in either a refund or an alternative. we ate elsewhere for the remainder of our stay

title: “Great value, great hospitality. I'd like to single out Babette in Food. And Beverage and Rosie in Banquet.”
text: Strong value, great service so I could focus on my business project. Thank you!

title: “High rates, small room, bad service”
text:
The hotel charged me on avg 150 per night for a one double bedroom with no private bathroom. We had to share the bathroom with some 8 other rooms and that meant that we sometimes had to wait 30min to be able to use it.
 The phone was not working and we lost for 2 consecutive nights the wake up call. After arguing for the 2nd time at the reception they agreed to knoch on my door for the remainder of the stay.
 The cleaning crew knocks and storms in your room at around 10am. The only defense you have is to lock that special mechanism that lets the door open only a little One day i was naked and the roommaid entered and screamed, at least it was funny.
 The room is ultra small (under 6sq meters for sure) if you'r going with your lover you will have trouble navigating inside the room, it is so small that you can't even pack all your bags at the same time, you have to do 1 at a time and leave the reste in a corner or something. Ah, it has nowhere to put your clothers, only one closet that only fits some pants/coats, so you will have to leave your clothing on your bag and do alot of exercise to open it daily since there's no room. Ah you also can't use the phone in your room at all without paying, even local calls and 1800 costs you something, they are really looking for easy profits.
 In conclusion,I felt bad with the service provided x the price but i had no other choice of where to stay. I advise those going to NY to search for better values like hotel 414 or even Park Savoy that offers bigger and better rooms with private bathroom AND continental breakfest for similar prices, too bad they were already booked for the time i was on NY...
 The only pro of the hotel is its location, 2 blocks from lines 123 express station and 4 blocks from Central park, but the location on hotel 414 and park savoy are much better than this one.

title: “Construction Zone”
text: Just spent three nights here. Very clean. Rooms were very small. Wifi was spotty on the 12th floor. Front rest was a bit hard to understand but very helpful. You can check out the leave you're stuff in secure storage to spend the rest of the day in the city. Only BIG problem is that there is a new building going up right next door. At 7:00 sharp the jack hammers start up right on the other side of the wall!

title: “Delightful”
text: My colleague and I stayed at the Orchard in early November and found it lived up to all the rave reviews we found on this site. Wonderfully convenient to Union Square; Starbucks two blocks away. All of the staff were friendly and helpful. The rooms are large by San Francisco standards and very well appointed. Huge glassed in showers a real treat.

title: “Great if you want to be downtown”
text: I'm not sure what the other reviewers are talking about, but we had a fine stay here. We stay in Philly several times a year, but almost never stay downtown. This time it was a last minute booking, and this Sheraton was the only hotel in town that had a room for under $300 a night. The stay was fine. Comfy bed with a very clean room & bathroom. The view from our room on the 23 floor was amazing. Front desk staff was super friendly. We didn't have time to use the pool, so we can't comment on that part. The only thing that is annoying is the uber expensive parking fees ($40/night), but that is EVERY hotel inside of the city. Free parking really only comes outside the city limits. Downtown is also limited with places to eat within walking distance at night, but if you have a car it isn't a big deal.

title: “Beautiful hotel and very well located.”
text: Very luxurious with beautiful lobby, very nice rooms, excellent swimming pool, good bars and restaurants and all you can expect from a 5-star hotel.

title: “Good place to spend the night”
text: Stayed here for one night just passing through Columbus. The room was clean and smelled fine, and the parking area felt very safe. As with any place where the room doors open directly to the outside, noise can be a problem. I had one noisy group of people getting back to their room at 4 in the morning wake me up, but other than that I had a restful sleep. The area is very commercial, and you will find pretty much every store or restaurant you can think of within walking distance. The hotel is also right next to the Perkins, so grabbing a quick breakfast there and heading out was a nice way to start the day.

title: “Great place to stay”
text: Stopped for three days on the way to NZ, and enjoyed immensely. Room pretty good although can get a bit noisy outside, saying that my 5 year old slept perfectly. The reason for 5 is partly for location but mainly for the excellent staff, for example we arrived and I had lost the suitcase keys. the desk guy managed to find a saw and had freed up our possesions before I returned with (superb) coffees from opposite 7-11. Nothing seems to be too much trouble. Will certainly stay again on next trip over to NZ

title: “One Night”
text: The lobby is on floor 12, parking on floor 11, room on floor 27 at the top. We only stayed one night for a quick trip to San Diego. In that 24 hours you really do get dizzy circling the parking lot up and down to the 11th floor. The hotel is a bit aged but clean. The suite divides the bedroom area from the living area which make both seem rather small. As it was only one night stay it was OK as we were out of the hotel most of the time and there only to sleep. II went again I would stay closer to the Gaslamp area for less driving to eats. As a Starwood member we were given a choice to have free internet in the room.

title: “Hated it, never go back”
text: Air wasn't working properly and a security guard had to reset it a replace a filthy filter because apparently they only have 1 maintenance guy and he went home sick, Sink was clogged, phone didn't work, and was overseen and passed off by valet when leaving.

title: “Very clean”
text:
Pros:
1. Clean space, which is v important to me
2. Clean duvet covers that get changed - hurrah!
3. Free wifi
4. Free shuttle that will take you downtown (this hotel is by IUPUI, so not near Circle Center)
5. On the IUPUI campus (have business here)
6. Front desk folks were helpful and welcoming
Cons:
1. Walls were a little thin - could hear laughter in next room, and it didn't seem like the folks were being too raucous
2. Bed and pillows were a little hard. I prefer down. 
3. Bathrooms were a little small given that this is Indiana and the rooms were large.
Summary - If your business brings you near IUPUI, this is a good option.

title: “Decent hotel - relatively good value”
text: Rooms were typical Hilton Garden Inn. Nothing spectacular. Check in was easy. Staff was REALLY FRIENDLY. The breakfast in the AM is basic, this is not four-star dining. The bed was ok. The water pressure was really bad. I really liked the location of this hotel. It is very near a new upscale mall complex with great restaurants. There is a movie theatre next door, the surrounding scenery is better than most. There are 3 dining locations in walking distance. There is a restaurant called Gallery Bistro that is AWESOME - less than a mile a way. You could do worse on business travel.

title: “Amazing hotel, great experience.”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for two nights and had an excellent experience. The wait staff at the pool was excellent and for a small roof top pool, it is one of the coolest ones I've seen. On the downside the sun didn't hit it until around 1pm because it was shaded by the building, but oh well, I'd rather have the sun later in the day anyway.
The hotel lobby is beautiful and the downstairs bar is really cool although a little pricey. The food at the restaurant was awesome and the restaurant had a really nice look to it.
The rooms were very nice too, and a decent size for a downtown hotel. The only negative was that the champagne glasses were spotty and I had to call down for some fresh ones. They sent them up right away, apologized profusely, and offerred me some dessert from the restaurant to go along with the champagne. In the end it turned a negative into a big plus for me.
The workout area was also really nice, with brand new nice equipment, a stereo, and an HDTV.
Overall, I had a great experience and next time I stay in downtown Dallas, I will definitely be back.

title: “5 Days, Four Nights”
text:
Stayed at the Tremont for 4 nights in november 2003. Don't expect the "Ritz" and you won't be disappointed. My wife and I considered it 'value for money.' The room we had on the 7th floor was clean and tidy. 
Tried the breakfast (ONCE) and it was like eating in a crematorium..Deadsville !! Would I stay there again...YES.

title: “Excellent!!!”
text: From the reservation, to checkout, this hotel was FANTASTIC. The room was big (for a family of 4), never had any issus, the front desk staff was very helpful with directions, or shop questions, or hailing a cab. I would strongly recommend anyone stay here in the future. This is a great place, on the UWS, away from the hustle and bustle, but still accessible to everything. With the subway a block away, everything is easy to get to. Great job to all the staff. Thanks for a great weeklong stay!!!

title: “Great location, nice hotel”
text: We had a nice, well appointed room at a fair price. The location can't be beat as Metro Center is a short walk from the hotel. The only negative was the poor service we experienced at the restaurant. It took forever to be seated for breakfast and our order was taken only after we complained.

title: “Apartment complex turned hotel, and it works!”
text: Property was originally designed as an apartment complex with large rooms which all have small outdoor porches and sliding glass doors. In the center of the property is a nice pool and lawn and landscaping. Great for sitting on the porch after a long day of visiting silicon valley tech companies, and unwinding with a cold drink and pleasant view of simple but well-kept flower gardens. I was impressed with the work-out room, was very large and had good equipment. There is also a large laundry room. The property is in walking distance of several restaurants. This property is a bit more expensive than your average Fairfield, but it's location and amenaties are worth the premium. Book early, as in the past I have had to stay elsewhere due to it's popularity.

title: “Good Location”
text: Stayed here many times.Staff always pleasant and willing to help.Rooms decent size and have all mod cons..Good buffet or ala carte breakfast.Pool and gym ok.The hotel public areas are being revamped at the moment so there is a little disturbance but no noise heard from guest floors.The sushi bar was always worth a visit.The hotel is joined on to a mall so is handy for shopping and has all usual big American name shops.Mall also contains good food court and a Wagamamas which is a relatively new British owned noodle bar!Never had cause to complain at The Copley.

title: “Great Service and Location”
text:
We booked three rooms during our stay. The hotel is very old and therefore some of the rooms are small and there is no air conditioning in the hallways. However, what is lacking in modern hotel layout/amenities, they make up for in service. Also, the historical nature of the hotel is tourist location in itself and you may even see a ghost. There a several "T" stops, restaurants and tourist attractions near by and the hotel is on the Freedom Trail. Great Location!
 We had called to make our reservations and all of our preferences were met upon check-in. Also, we contacted the loyalty ambassador prior to our arrival to arrange for room service to celebrate a special event. Not only was everything delivered according to plan, but was complimentary.
 One of our rooms ordered room service that was delivered later than usual and was given complimentary. However, it had only been a half-hour and the guests didn't even considered it late.
 Also, there was an issue with another hotel guest doing inappropriate things in the hallway. One of the guests staying in the rooms we booked saw the event and contacted the front desk. Even though there was no way this could have been prevented, nor was it the hotel's fault, they guests were offered free breakfast vouchers and all of their previous room service was waived. They went above and beyond the expectations for our stay and we greatly appreciated it. 
 We loved Boston and hope to stay in that hotel when we visit again!

title: “Our stay at the Four Seasons was well worth the expense. Their customer service was impeccable.”
text: We celebrated our 11th wedding anniversary the weekend we stayed at the Four Seasons. We were greeted with a card and a lovely plate of petit fours in our room, which was a wonderful, thoughtful surprise. It was a very nice personal touch and we truly appreciated the extra effort by the staff. The entire weekend stay was great.

title: “Cancels reservation due to overbooking”
text: My wife booked a reservation at this hotel weeks ago and gets a call the day before saying they have overbooked and they cannot take her. One hour so sar into room reservation beaurocracy and no solution yet.

title: “Great location”
text:
We stayed at this hotel between 9th - 12th Dec 2006 and this is the second time we have stayed here. The staff are friendly and helpful and the rooms are very clean, we even got upgraded to the junior suite on arrival which gave us an extra room to store our suitcases!!. The free coffee & muffins provides a kick start in the mornings.
The location is brilliant, you are only 5 mins from the Empire State Building & 5th Ave. 
We would definitely stay here again.

title: “We loved it!”
text: We had a wonderful stay at the Lenox Hotel. Initially, we were thinking of staying in the harbor area (because we have small children and wanted to be close to the Aquarium and the Children's museum). We are glad we didn't. Service was great! The staff was very friendly. My kids got hungry at 10:00 pm so I called room service and asked them for cereal and milk - and I got it! We forgot the kids jackets in the car, so we asked to be brought in - and they did. Also, after we checked, out we asked if we could leave the car with them, while we grab breakfast and walk around. That was not a problem. These may be little things but made our stay so much more pleasant and hassle free. The location does not get better. Close to everything, including T. We, however, walked everywhere. We stayed in a junior suite and it was the perfect size. Free internet is a big plus. Other hotels we looked into charge per day. I highly recommend it. I wouldn't stay anywhere else.

title: “The InterContinental New York Barclay feels like home!”
text:
On a recent visit to NYC we had the pleasure of meeting Guest Relations Agent Leslie Pagan. When we checked into the hotel on a very cold winter day, she warmly greeted us and made us feel right at home. Leslie is a big part of why we stay at The Barclay when we visit NYC. She exemplifies good customer service and is a winner in our book! We look forward to seeing Ms. Pagan again on our next visit in March to New York.
The Intercontinental Barclay is in a great location if you are visiting New York City. Just a few blocks down from 5th Ave and all the shops you can imagine. The bar has great drinks and appetizers. The rooms are very nice, very big for NYC standards. The beds are some of the most comfortable that I have slept in for a hotel. 
We keep coming back to The Barclay, because it feels like home!

title: “Amazing trip”
text: I was a little concerned as there are so many bad reviews but this place was great. We booked a park view suite and it was an amazing view. It was the largest room I have ever stayed in in New York. The bed really is amazing. The staff were great and friendly and the location is incredible. Highly recommended!

title: “Haven on the Wharf”
text:
We stayed here with teenagers for four nights while we did SF. At first I'd wanted to have another hotel with a pool, but in fact the weather was far too cold anyway (40F below Vegas!) so it didn't matter, plus I could see that the Argonaut was a cut above the other hotels nearby (and pricier of course). 
If you want a character hotel in this area, the Argonaut delivers. It's a conversion, v. tastefully done, from an old cannery, and it works. (Though there is a downside - read on.) Decor-wise it is v. good - like an old ship I suppose. Lovely lobby/lounge, with huge fire and v. cosy leather sofas, polished wood floors etc - nice after the chill of an SF July! We didn't really use it enough, because we were on a hectic schedule - kept missing the free wine tasting too! (Note- there should be free newspapers there)
Our rooms were on the fourth floor – there are insufficient lifts for the population here, but that is one of the downsides of being in what amounts to a listed building, and it is tolerable – and standard. The décor was stylish – nautical theme – and the bathroom fine. The downside for me was that the window faced into the enclosed internal space of the old cannery, and it dawned on me in the middle of the night that if there were an earthquake there was NOWHERE to run to! We’d be crushed and canned in the hotel. (I assume the conversion was earthquake-proofed, however?). Not a comfortable thought. Made the place claustrophobic and bad karma while I thought about it. But I got used to it I suppose. Corridors were also claustrophobic (definitely don’t stay here if you suffer from claustrophobia and earthquake fear)(though I don’t suppose earthquake-phobes go to SF!).
Coffee machine was OK, though as I found everwhere in the USA, utterly insufficient creamers – they must drink their coffee pitchdark. I ended up buying milk from a 7/11 nearby.
Nowhere near enough hooks – or possibly none at all? – in the bathroom. Unusual bathrobes! Ie, one was zebra striped and the other leopardskin spotty….
The restaurant (Blue Mermaid I think) was nicely done – again, nautical/sailing ship/harbour feel, and more ‘downmarket’ than the lobby – more roughhewn. TV over the bar, etc, and dark wood and ‘pubby’. But fine to be in. It opens off the street as well as a ‘real’ restaurant. However, it is also too small for the hotel I feel, especially with off-street custom to boot. The big item on the menu is chowder, which was very good (I’m no expert though), although I was a bit irritated when the server told me all chowder has clams, when in fact you could get crab chowder as well (which was v. good).
We quickly found that the San Franciscans have an obsession with Sourdough, alas, and it is just about impossible to get any other kind of white bread, which I found very irritating, as SD has a peculiar taste and it would be nice to get ordinary bread as well. You can have the chowder served in a ‘bread-bowl’ of a hollowed-out loaf. There is a big SD bakery along the wharf.
Food was expensive, but then I found all the food in the USA expensive. Breakfast waffle was good, but something like $15. Don’t bother trying to have tea if you are English – it’s warm and cat’s. Next day I brought down my Assam t-bag (carefully hoarded from the UK!) and asked for hot water and made my own, and that was better (though of course still not proper tea – and WHY is the coffee in the USA so bad unless you have cappuchino??!)
Service in the restaurant was OK, but could be improved I felt. 
Front desk staff were good – told us how to get free Internet, which was much appreciated by teens. 
Doormen were v. good – and spectacular in their uniforms. 
Warning – SF is direly short of taxis. Why this should be in a recession and unemployment I don’t know – plus what’s with the unemployment and the fact that apart from one taxi-driver, every single one in the USA we took had a new immigrant driver? (And loads of non-American shop assistants everywhere too!)(plus ads in the shop windows saying they are hiring) Are the wages too low for Americans?
The taxi situation in SF is so bad we ended up just about walking all the way back along the Wharf from the baseball stadium, and when we had brunch at the Cliff House on the Pacific coast, about a half-hour taxi journey (don’t ask the cost – horrendous!), there was NONE on the way back, and we took a bus home (loads better value – something like $2 I recall). It was even hard flagging one down around Union Square. Note to SF Tourist Authority – put more cabs on the streets!
The Argonaut is well situated at the posher (relatively!) end of the Wharf. I was surprised at how tacky the Wharf was overall, and it could do with a good chi-chi-ing up (another note to the SF TA!), and clearing away the tacky stores. There are some nice ones there, plus nice restaurants (No, NOT the Hooters – who let that garbage in?!), and the whole area could be really nice if the tack were cleared away and it was pushed upmarket.
Ghiardelli Square is nice and chi-chi, though even the Ghiardelli chocolate is not as good as it should/could be – American chocolate is awful, and even the Lindt imported is a different recipe, and really yukky. Shame. I think if Americans were allowed to taste proper European chocolate they’d never touch their own muck again! Weird, as when one has good food in the US it’s superb! Why do they put up with rubbish chocolate? (Ditto, the Kettle chips on sale are only ‘Kettle-brand’ and NOT the real thing – again, why not import the real ones?)
We also ate at the nearby Italian restaurant (Chipotle?)(whatever that is!), and it was good (cheerful, large, gingham tablecloths), but, again, far more expensive than it should be (as we found everwhere in the USA we went). But recommended with that limitation. 
The cable car turnaround was just next to the hotel, which was handy – BUT the queue is an hour long….it seemed inexplicable to me, until I heard from a taxi driver that the cable car runs at a huge loss to the city, and is only a tourist attraction. I think the fare to Union Square (direct) was $5, so for five of us it was more expensive than a taxi! The queuing time is unacceptable – and at the very least they should issue timed tickets, so you can buy one, then go away for an hour (to Ghiardelli’s coffee shop!) and come back and board immediately for your timed car. They hung around for ages – presumably the line can only take so many cars simulataneously. There should be much more information about the cable cars – I only read in a book that they work by being dragged along a moving cable, for example. They are missing a trick there. The queue was just as long for the return journey from Union square (so we took a cab back.)
One definite recommendation – if at the Argonaut take the time to go round the attached museum there – you can’t miss it next to the entrance. It is free and very informative about SF, its origins, harbour history, anything to do with the sea etc etc. V. good indeed. It’s only one floor and you can do it bitesize as you go in and out of the hotel.
There was also a good series of wall posters along a corridor about the old canning factory which was very informative. 
I feel the hotel makes a real effort to both make the best use of its location and construction, and is very distinctive. Makes if different from the chain hotels, though pricier.
When in SF with teenage boys, definitely definitely do the rocket boat – unless you’ve got a bad back, or don’t like the feeling that any moment you are going to be drowned….the boys loved it! Zooms around the bay, and careers all over the place – lots of splashing (you wear rainhoods). Don’t miss it. A thrill ride all of its own.
We also did the Old Fireengine tour of the Golden Gate – separate review if I can find it. In brief – fun, even for jaded teens (‘better than I thought it would be’ said one, who’d thought the thrill of a fire engine was long behind him….). It careers all over, you are open air (they give you huge warm jackets – much needed). They put their heart and soul into it, but you had better like Judy Garland….(!). Quite pricey, but then everything is….
(San Francisco is full of French tourists – weird. You never see them anywhere else. Maybe it’s because SF is quite European in style.)

title: “Dreary place in an exciting neighborhood”
text:
The biggest thing that sticks with me about this hotel is that the whole place seemed dull, dark, and uninviting. The street entrance is unremarkable, and the lobby was like a cave. The staff I dealt with were nice enough, but they couldn't brighten the mood of the place if they had flowers growing out of their ears.
The room seemed dated, with several relatively minor items in need of repair, but more importantly there was no art on the walls and the room was a dull monochrome color scheme. The room was comfortable enough, but I couldn't get past the depressing feeling. I was also disappointed that I had to use wired internet, but at least I could connect.
As many have said, the best part of this place is the location, a short walk to Times Square and all the excitement (and food) there.
I'd recommend this place on the basis of location and price, just know what you're getting into.

title: “Superb”
text:
A beautiful room, stunning bathroom, comy bed, excellentiPod dock from B&W (will buy one!). Staff were very pleasant, bar was friendly though not that exciting considering there are many good palce in the neighbourhood. Its lovely to walk around the area and to come back to the hotel to relax.
Breakfast room service was a little disappointing but the Brasserie was fun for late night drinks and Ria, the Michelin starred restaurant is superb - will review seperately.
We will return for sure. Highly recommended!

title: “Really nice stay and high-tech large screen TV”
text: We were both incredibly impressed not only with the soft, inviting decor of the hotel but also with the TV. Yes. For those of you who like to have the gadgets with your TV, this is the place to stay. You are able to connect your PSP (for example) so that you can play games on the large TV (which swivels from the couch to the bed). So, if you have kids or even kids at heart, this is an extra comfort worth staying here. On top of that, the room is spacious with a comfortable bed. The staff was also very courteous no matter what time of day you checked in, walked in, or even checked out. You are just a walk away from a couple restaurants and you have easy access to Hwy 270. I would definitely stay here again. Thanks!

title: “Fantastic - the Hyatt is more then the sum of all its parts!”
text: My husband and were in San Antonio for a wedding the first weekend in December. After reading some of the reviews I knew the Hyatt was going to be nice but I did not expect it to be perfect in every way. Our stay exceeded all expectations. The staff was curteous and helpful all during our visit. Love "Chaps" we had a wonderful breakfast every morning and I found the prices to be very reasonable, the food is delicous, and the chef making my waffle in the shape of Texas was marvelous. We had late night drinks one night, a late night dessert another, plus the Jazz band playing in the lower level on the water were great as you sipped a margarita. The Riverwalk is at the doorstep, of course in December it is more then gorgeous and festive. As you check in and out the staff does a wonderful job moving people and giving each guest at the counter their undivided attention. The elevators fly up and down and one never waits long for the lift. The Alamo is just across the street - and to see it all lit up at night or in the early morning mist, is a bonus. As far as parking goes, well maybe $21 is a bit high for valet parking but when you come back into the city after visiting and the parking garages are full and traffic is bumper to bumper it is fantastic to be able to just drop the car, the keys, and go your merry way. You don't have to use the valet parking - for self park in and out you pay $15 and the garage is just across the street. We took the car out once a day so we opted for the $10.00 per 24.00 hours. The rooms are nice and large, the beds are soooo comfortable, and the view of the atrium was perfect. The Hyatt just added to our wonderful weekend in San Antonio visiting old friends. I highly recomend this hotel.

title: “We'll definitely be back!!!”
text: One of the most enjoyable, friendly, cheerful, wam stays we have ever had the pleasure to experience. Comfortable, modern and clean room, extremely friendly and enthusiastic staff (evey hotel needs a Tisha, thank you so much for the wonderful surprise lunch you packed for us!!). From the general manager on down, you all deserve our most sincere thanks for making our stay memorable.

title: “Perfect experience”
text:
This hotel was perfect. It was a brilliant location - lovely building, REALLY close to Union Square and we had no trouble with noise. Just a block or two away and the streets get a little mroe dodgy so this was ideal.
The rooms were lovely with enormous windows, the service was excellent. Would definetly go back.

title: “The Overlook”
text: Oh my word. This hotel is so so bad you simply must stay in it. The bed broke. The sink broke. The bath was broken. The bathroom lock was broken. There was mud, yes mud, dripping from the windows. We wrote our names in it. The hotel is so cavernous and abandoned you'd swear it was haunted. The travel agents called it the 'Roach Motel'. Need I say more? Yes. We had to queue, QUEUE, in a line of people to complain. The maid walked in twice. The iron was dangerously wired. The view was of a brick wall. The location was difficult to get to. There was blood crashing in giant waves from the elevators. That's not true but we half expected Johnny to come a knowcking with his axe. Avoid

title: “Smokey”
text: My sister, our friend and I stayed one night in the Residence Inn Downtown Memphis. The hotel was close to Beale St and other points of interest. When I made our reservations I had requested a two bedroom suite that was non smoking. When we got to our room I noticed the strong odor of smoke and two ashtrays. I immediately called the desk. I was told that we could change to a one bedroom suite which would not have been large enough and wasn't what I had requested anyway. The front desk was not very worried about the problem at all and did not offer to compensate us in any way. I emailed the hotel chain and still was not given an apology. I do have to say that the hotel was clean and the breakfast was nice. I would not stay there again fearing that I would have to sleep in a smoke filled room again.

title: “The best value”
text:
This is my second time staying at the Red Roof Inn and I would not hesitate to return again if I make it back. I saw a friend's hotel in Chelsea for slightly cheaper price and it was not a patch on this place.
We were on the 15th floor which has great, direct views of the Empire State building 2 blocks away.
The hotel is centrally located in the Little Korea area - a lively street, and a walkable distance to Times Square, subways, many food shops etc etc...
The only downsides of this place are the queues for breakfast which seem even worse than the last time I was here, and the deathly slow elevators - which of course become more of an issue on the second top floor... but the views from there make it worth it - we could also see the tip of the Crysler Building...

title: “living on its name”
text: i visited the waldorf with my girlfriend and her family (mother, father, sister) for the fact there was 5 of us, we decided to book one room, with a promise from the hotel they would be able to give us a fold out or camper bed. When we arrived we were informed the hotel did not do these things! After my girlfriends brother decided he'd sleep on the floor, we got up to the room. the view from the window was marvellous, but the room itself was disappointing. for a start, I'd been in touch with the hotel more than three times in order to have chocolates and champagne prepared for my girlfriend as it was her birthday, there was nothing at all. The room was too small for three people, yet it was meant to be a family suite! The staff diden't seem too bothered to help us with anything because we tried to be economical with the trip. Overall it's a nice place, but it's not great.

title: “Always Enjoyable”
text: I've had occassion to stay at the Wolcott three times. The rooms are great and the staff is always accommodating. This hotel has reasonable rates and is convenient to port authority and MSG among other important landmarks.

title: “They should be ashamed”
text: I am not allowed to use the words I would prefer to use to describe this place. They should be ashamed. Without a doubt the worst place I've ever stayed. It's like paying to sleep in a really seedy dorm room.

title: “Hard Rock Hotel Chicago: I'll be Back”
text:
I checked into the Hard Rock in mid-December for a holiday shopping trip with my girlfriend and was blown away by everything. The staff was incredibly kind and knowledgeable, the hotel was very cool but low key and the beds were insanely comfortable. 
I will definitely visit the Hard Rock again.

title: “A true resort experience at a reasonable price”
text:
We were looking for a clean, decent family hotel near the natural beauty of the Sonoran desert close to scottsdale where my husband was attending a conference. What we got was a gorgeous resort with the amenities, and service I associate with a more expensive price tag. We were able to do some incredible things (jeep tour, trip to sedona and grand canyon) because we weren't broke from the hotel cost.
The physical site is aesthetically pleasing and well maintained with courtyards, fountains, tasteful art and decor with a sense of place. You can see beautiful squaw peak from the river ranch!!! Don't miss the lazy river at sunset--wow! The pictures don't do it justice! 
One caveat is that although I believe the whole resort is wheel-chair accessible, bare in mind that the various facilities ( river ranch, spa, camp, restaurants) are quite spread out from the suites and casitas. My family was fine with it, but I could imagine that anyone unable to walk a few city blocks would need to ask the staff for particular rooms or golf cart transportation to facilities. I'm sure they would be helpful!
The service was outstanding. We got prompt service every time we needed anything: ketchup, extra towels, etc. Of note: Dave, the concierge, was upbeat and extremely helpful with all of our sight-seeing. He even upgraded us at no charge to a "pure room" when he heard that one of our children had allergies.
The room was a two room suite with 2 queens and a pull out sofa with a balcony. The beds were delicious and the air did feel very fresh--not sure if it was the "pure" room, the dry desert air or both.
The river-ranch was a blast and my kids really enjoyed a morning at cayote camp. Jane, the director is professional, loving and creative. In just 3 hours my kids brought home fired-clay bowties, decorated cowboy bandanas and excitement about what they learned about the desert flora and fauna. I wish they could have gone more--they got so much out of it.
I had the good fortune of receiving a phenomenal deep-tissue massage at the Tocosierra Spa on site. I considered going to one of the fancy local spas, but decided to go here for convenience. I was so glad I did because the massage therapist, June, ranked with some of the best I've experienced both in skill and care.
I recommend a reservation here without reservation!!!

title: “Nice hotel”
text: Stayed at the Crown Plaza just before christmas.Chose this hotel due to its location and the good deal I got. The hotel was very nice. The public areas were quiet and welcoming. The only problem we had, was that the room we had booked had been given away when we arrived and we were given a smaller room. This was rectified the next day after complaining and we were moved to the executive room we had originally booked. Had been led to beleive that all rooms in new york tend to be small.Not so.Our executive room had two double beds and a sofa bed, and still lots of room. Nice extras such as a Jacuzzi bath, towelling robe and a safe. Staff friendly and helpful. Good location, short 5 min walk to central station.

title: “Great stay at Hotel Triton in San Fran”
text: Great hotel, very funky and different with fabulous location for good price. Rooms arent huge but definately room enoough for the time spent there.

title: “GOOD BASIC ACCOMODATION”
text:
We stayed overnight at the Fairfield in Charlotte Northlake after missing a connecting flight on a weekend when all of the airport area hotels that US Airways contracts with were full because of an athletic event. 
The airline told us to find our own accommodation, and another traveller in the same situation told us that she had found space at the Fairfield. 
It was a long $45 cab ride from the airport but at that point we were not going to look for something closer. 
The room was clean and had adequate space, there were no odor issues, and the mattress was better than the one that we had slept on at the resort we had just left. The room came with a microwave, a small fridge and a kitchen sink. 
The continental breakfast was decent, with the self-serve area kept tidy. 
Some earlier reviews complain of a weak Internet signal, but it worked fine in our room. 
There were no noise problems. 
Check-in and check-out were fast and friendly. 
If you need a cab, you are best to ask the front desk to arrange one well in advance as there may not be any in the area.

title: “Started badly but finished off fantastic!!”
text: Long story short. Requested a king room six months prior to stay as a rewards member. Girlfriend checked in and was given room with 2 queens. I was on a plane flying from Dallas arguing with a desk clerk trying to get a king room and was told they were sold out and they could do nothing about it. Said I would be there at 630 to speak to the manager after getting off a hot and crowded plane. They changed the room immediately and brought the key to my GF. When I got there, there was a bottle of chilled Clos du Bois Chardonnay and a personal note apologizing for the inconvenience. That made up for eveything!! Fantastic rooms that are definitely a suite, 2 flatscreens, fridge and microwave, modern fixtures and big modern shower, free food and well drinks and draft for around 3 hours at a manager reception. Do yourself a favor and stay here if you need to stay downtown. Right next to the Toyota center, a couple of blocks from Minute Maid Park as well as the main convention center. Will def stay here again!!

title: “Really a bad option”
text:
Booked 4 nights and prepaid so that we could get a better price. Really bad idea.
I stayed in room 316 which they had said would be ok for 5 guests. Not good ......too small.
Couldnt sleep one single night, there is a bar-terrace in the buidling next to the Hotel and the noise goes on until 2am. every day!!! yes everyday and it seems as if the people are in your room... you can hear all conversations clearly, thats how close it is. One elevator, which wasnt working some days so we had to use stairs and these were very small and dangerous. I dont understand how this Hotel has a license........or how Best Western can have such a bad hotel on its sites......No TV in one of the rooms.....and the other TV had only 4 or 5 channels available, really poor. Not a good choice......
Staff were really helpful at all times, no complaints there at all.

title: “Clean, handy but very hot rooms!”
text:
I stopped here in April whilst on a Hen party and found it to be a pleasant hotel and very handy for major attractions. The subway is less than 30 seconds from the hotel door which made it really easy to get about. Whilst the hotel itself doesn't have a restaurany or bar there are plenty of places nearby and the little cafe underneath the hotel does a really good breakfast/brunch. The reception staff even called us a takeaway pizza one night after we had returned from an evening bar hopping. 
There were 3 of us in one room with 2 double beds but there was not really much space for anything else in the room. It got very cluttered after all of our shopping trips! The bathroom was clean and tidy but very small. The room was very very hot and we didn't have air con although we did have a noisy ceiling fan. Some of the other guests did say that they had proper air con. Whilst we were there there were road works going on outside the hotel which woke us up at 8am most mornings but obviously this is not the hotels fault. We did ask to be moved but the hotel was full. 
Despite my comments re the room I would stop here again if I was going on another girlie trip as we were rarely in the room. If I was going for a more relaxing break I'd probably look elsewhere. Then again is New York meant to be relaxing? A big positive for me was its location to Century 21 - a big discount dept store where my credit card took a real battering!

title: “A nice hotel close to old town San Diego”
text:
This is our first stay at the Crown Plaza Mission Valley. We were looking for a hotel close to old town and this fit the bill (Disclaimer: I am a Platinum Priority Club Member). Outwardly this is not a typical Crown Plaza hotel. It’s an older hotel that is more reminiscent of motel (your room door opens to the great outdoors instead of an inside hallway). But what it lacks in modern appeal they make up for on the service end.
Here’s the Good:
Rooms are very clean with modern drapes, bedding and a flat panel TV. We were upgraded to a “Leisure Room” with a nice view of the golf course next door. We stayed there on Halloween night and it was very quiet around our room. No wild parties to note. The hotel theme is Polynesian with waterfalls in the court yard, a super clean pool and plenty of tropical foliage. The sushi bar in the lounge was unexpectedly very good. The staff at the hotel was very friendly. From the front desk to the maids to the restaurant staff, everyone either greeted us with a “hello” or a “good morning”. To me that was important. Usually you don’t get that even at a four star hotel. 
Now the Bad:
The pillows for our bed were very stiff. I did have some trouble getting sleep due to constantly trying to keep my neck comfortable. You are close to Interstate 8 so you will get some of that freeway noise. Also, how about some HDTV to go along with that flat panel you guys paid for?
And the Ugly:
Not that we needed it but our room AC/Heater did not work at all. My wife wanted to turn on heat in the middle of the night because she was a little chilly but no dice. Also the alarm clock was unplugged from the wall so we plugged it back and set the time ourselves. (Maybe the maid should tip us?)
All in all, our stay was pleasant. I wish I knew about the shuttle bus to old town San Diego. I would have taken that instead of driving. My bad for not asking. Next time I’m in the Mission Valley area again. I would definitely come back. And this time I’ll use the Pool and the Spa.
Note to Reviewers: I read some of the reviews for this hotel and it always cracks me up when I read how people are outraged to find out that they have to pay for parking. The hotel’s own website says you have to pay for parking so why the outrage? Do your research before you checking in so you won’t be so shocked at the sticker price of staying at Crown Plaza or any other fancy hotel. Also, a reviewer complained about fake Hawaiian feel to the hotel. Well Duh! If you want real Hawaiian feel, Honolulu is a 5 hour flight away.

title: “Disappointed”
text: Our family reserved two rooms at this hotel in October. We arrived at the hotel on December 8th only to be told our reservation was given to someone else. When we explained that we had made those reservations weeks ago, They said " Sorry we dont guarantee a room, our hotel was overbooked." They then suggest that they are trying to accomodate us and preceed to book us in a hotel that was less expensive, dirty and far inferior to this hotel. No refund was given, no empathy, just a smug manager with a nasty attitude. The whole situation was very upsetting, you would think we would have gotten a courtesy call, they had to have known they overbooked. I haved lived in the city my entire life and have never experienced anything like this. They had this attitude, like they were doing us a favor by sticking us in a sub par hotel in exchange for their mess up and we should be thrilled about it. Anne C

title: “Love the hotel!”
text:
I was debating where to take my girlfriend for a weekend getaway in the city, We usually go to the Mayflower hotel or the W hotel. 
This time I thought I suprise her and decided to try another hotel, I looked online and checked the Kimpton site for their hotels and found Hotel Rouge to be the type of hotel I would like to checkout with its funky style.
I then checked the reviews on Yelp, there were some good reviews and some bad ones, so I was hesitant to make a reservation, finally I decided to go for it! Made a reservation online with some request, upon arriving at the hotel, Steven welcomed us and he made us feel at home. 
He managed to get the room I wanted, when we checked into the room he even called to make sure everything was good. Room was big, the bed very comfortable and the design very chic! Reminds me of my own condo but mine is all white. :-)
We also had a light snack at the Bar as well as the complimentary cocktail drinks which was part of the deal when you book online, and Rigo our bartender was extremely nice and funny guy!
My girlfriend just fell in love with this hotel and its design, she decided it is the best hotel she been too and forget the 5 star hotels, they charge you triple the price and it's only for the name not the services..
We decided from now on stay at the Kimpton hotels and the Rouge in DC, infact will stay there for my girlfriends birthday weekend.

title: “one of the best hotels I've stayed in”
text: The staff is excellent. Everyone is helpful, nice and pleasant. The breakfast was great. The person taking care of it was on top of everything and worked hard to keep the food coming and tables clean too. Which at times was hard as the place was full every night. They also have a nice business center and pool. We took advanage of it everyday. WE had a wonderful stay and would surely stay there again if we are in the area. Also it was very quiet at night too. There are also places to walk to for dinner. Which is always nice.

title: “Excellent”
text:
I had a fantastic experience at the Andaz Wall Street. As a Diamond, I have high expectations of Hyatt properties, and my experience has exceeded my expectations across visits. 
From the friendly greeting in the lobby from the staff member who remembered me, to a special upgrade in recognition of my birthday, to friendly and attentive staff at the Wall & Water restaurant (who also remembered me), I have had an excellent experience.
The rooms themselves are big and modern (I had an incredible suite on the most recent stay, but have also had very nice "standard" rooms), and the location is good downtown. The concept is also great (e.g., free minibar) -- and they had a helpful running map for my 7-mile run along the East River.
One nit: the complementary Diamond breakfast ($50 credit) needs to be taken in the restaurant, and cannot be applied to room service (unlike the Andaz 5th Avenue, for example). 
I am very much looking forward to my next stay.

title: “Good but not great boutique hotel”
text:
Spent two nights (Friday/Saturday) at Hotel Max. Booked the hotel online via orbitz. Package deal, decent price.
The good:
1. Great location. 5-7 minute walk to Westlake Transit Center.
2. Nice, helpful front desk and front door persons
3. Clean room, flat screen TV, mini refrigerator in the room
4. Nice pillows and linens
5. Room was decorated very nicely. Didn't use the A/C, which are "in window" units.
6. To access the various floors, you need a room key. Extra safety, is always a nice thing!
The not so good:
1. Thin thin thin walls. It's an older building, and while I realize there is nothing the front desk or hotel can do about the thin walls, it's still disappointing. Especially when the couple next door decides to have fun at 2:43am. Was woken up to the sounds of a live porn recital. :-)
2. Overnight parking is $40. WOW!!! 
3. The bathroom was tiny. Efficient, but tiny. If you are a big and/or tall person, good luck manuvering the shower. Dropped the soap and had to step out of the shower to pick it up, and I take yoga on a weekly basis!
4. Left a travel pillow in the room. Called the hotel to see if they could ship it too me. "Of course, my pleasure." For a shipping cost of $20. Apparently, they only federal express items. I guess USPS doesn't stop at Hotel Max. Left a message to have the manager call me to discuss. Will be interesting to see if he returns the call.
Overall, it was a decent but not great hotel. After staying here and Kimpton Property in Seattle, I would probably return to the Kimpton. They offered upgrades for minimal cost, walls were thicker and still nice boutique feel.

title: “Don't let the location put you off - this hotel is absolutely fine.”
text:
The hotel is a short walk to all the main tourist spots, subway stations are nearby for going farther afield and walking back to the hotel even late at night was no problem. The rooms were clean and a good size and the breakfast room with 24 hour tea, coffee and soft drinks was really handy. A special word for the staff who were really friendly and helpful. We'd have no hesitation in booking again.
Newcastle, England

title: “One of the Best Values in the City”
text:
From the Friendly and Energetic staff at Check in until the time I left excellent stay! Small but updated rooms, great bathrooms, dozens of channels for everything you want to watch plus the location is perfect. Not in the middle of all the noise of the city but right in the middle of it all - between 6th and 7th Avenue within walking distance of everything!
Great parking only a few steps away and the Doubletree validates your parking to save you big time - this is a treat in the city and as a regular traveler this will be noted! The only concern - call ahead for getting my car did not work, called at 6am and asked to have the car for 6:30, did not get the car until almost 7 and there were only two of us picking up our cars, the stafff had no clue what they were doing - but keep in mind - they are not part of the Doubletree just the parking choice. 
I hope they keep the price and value where it is ...there are so many other options nearby but this is the best!

title: “FANTASTIC!”
text: I went to New York last week with my mum. We stayed in the staybridge suites fantastic location and if you get lost just head for port authority bus terminal!!room was very clean and fresh bathroom was lovely and big, clean towels daily and room was cleaned every day also. we had a great view out the back window. Breakfast was nice, toast, cereal tea coffee something for everyone. would reccomend this hotel to anyone. staff are friendly and helpful. if i ever return to New York i would certainly go back here without a doubt!

title: “Pleasant Stay”
text: I stayed here while my son was a patient at Johns Hopkins. One of the reasons I chose this hotel was because of the free shuttle to the hospital. The rate was great and the room spacious and clean. I had the same problem with water all over the floor after a shower. Longer shower curtains would be most helpful. The shuttle service was not as dependable as it could be. They acknowledge that there are some issues and say they are working on them. Other than that, this is a nice hotel and the staff is very friendly and accommodating.

title: “Courtyard by Marriott Liberty Station was an outstanding place to stay!!”
text: My husband, daughter, and I stayed at this Courtyard by Marriott for seven nights from June 12-19. My husband was attending a conference at another hotel, but when I researched nearby hotels, this one stood out above all the rest! It was new, sparkling clean, and extremely well-maintained! Our room was on the fourth floor with a beautiful view of the pool and the bay. Everyone on staff from the front desk to the cleaning staff were friendly, helpful, and very efficient. The front desk staff was probably the most helpful that I have ever encountered during my travels. (Our family has traveled extensively and frequently.) When asked for suggestions on eating and entertainment, they were always right on target. They checked restaurants for us, offered us pool towels to take to the beach, and went out of their way to make our stay wonderful. We took every suggestion that they offered, and we were never disappointed! We have traveled to San Diego and the La Jolla area several times, and enjoyed this hotel much more than others that we have stayed in. I would highly recommend it! We will definitely be back! (I normally do not write such lengthy reviews, but this hotel definitely warranted such a review.)

title: “Nice accommodations, Clean, Warm and accommodating staff.”
text: Great price, extremely nice staff made my trip to Phoenix for a job interview less stressful. I had to stay an extra night on a very busy weekend in Phoenix and they went out of their way to help me out. Got the job and now will be coming to Phoenix on sales calls. I will absolutely stay with them again.

title: “a delightful experience in a lovely friendly hotel”
text: I'm adding my positive comments to those already mentioned. We were in Houston for a wedding, and thoroughly enjoyed the accommendations at the Magnolia. The hotel is gorgeous, wonderfully decorated, spacious lobby and common areas, nice sized room with amenities...absolutely nothing about which to complain. Love the southern hospitality!

title: “Comfortable, Cozy, Lovely Service”
text:
Just returned from a two night- mid week get away to Boston. First time staying at Jury's and I chose it based on Trip Advisor reviews. Although a bit pricey - Service was wonderful, they couldn't have done more! We are newspaper addicts and they not only leave the Boston Globe at your door but were happy to send along the New York Times as well. Room was small but quite cozy, bed was heavenly, bathroom lovely. Appreciated the windows that opened and the towel warmers and bathrobes. Although the bar is amazingly loud when you come through the front doors the rooms were quiet as could be! Didn't eat at the restaurant, but then there are so many wonderful restaurants in the area.
I would go again, great location!

title: “Convenient stay!”
text: Overall, we enjoyed our stay here. We stayed here on a Saturday-Tuesday, and every front desk person we encountered was extremely helpful and friendly. The only issue I did have was that our room did not get serviced until Monday, which would not have been a huge deal except we needed towels. In the hotel's defense, Sunday we may just have missed our service opportunity. We had do not disturb on the door in the early AM and assumed the room would be serviced while we were at breakfast and had removed the do not disturb, but it was not. When we left the hotel for our day's activities, it still had not been serviced when we returned. On Monday, I asked could the room please be serviced. They did not clean the bathtub though.The breakfast included in the cost of the room was decent, and we would stay here again for the cost. It was also in reasonable driving distance of everything we needed to do, which was great for our gas budget!!!

title: “Not that great for the price”
text: We stayed at the Grand Hyatt for a work trip. The hotel lobby and restaurants are nice however the rooms are old and out dated. The toilette looks like a toilette you would see in a locker room and there is really nothing too exciting about the rooms. The customer service is average at best and they do not go the extra mile for the customers. I will not stay there again unless is paid for by my company. The few good things about it is that you can get to the metro from the hotel without having to go outside and there is a starbucks on location. Other than that everything is over prized and under performs.

title: “Truly a great hotel”
text: From the moment we arrived nothing was too much trouble. All the staff were very helpful and we would not hesitate in staying again. The position is excellent being just round the corner from Times Square but our room overlooking the courtyard was quiet and relaxing. This hotel really knows how to look after their guests.

title: “Great location downtown Chicago”
text: I have stayed at the Omni several times with my husband. Not only is the location great (just off N. Michigan Ave.) but the employees are really helpful and courteous, the rooms are very clean and spacious (king-size bed in bedroom and sitting area with desk, comfie chairs and wet bar. It's a great deal for the money! Close to theatres, shopping and restaurants. The restaurant in the hotel serves an outstanding breakfast-buffet or order off menu- and uses organic and locally-grown products as much as possible. I highly recomment the Omni Chicago.

title: “Location, Location, Location”
text:
As the title says, the location was great. Easy walk to virtually everywhere and a subway station just across the street. The lights of times square were a stones throw away.Travelled with my wife and teenaged boys. We were upgraded to a club floor which was a large room with a Mac computer. (Great for searching restaurants). The lobby and room were fine. Service was excellent. Never used the gym. Never ate in the hotel because Shula's (even for breakfast) is overpriced. Lots of great breakfast places around.
Concierge was lacking. The rates for a car to Laguardia and Yankee tickets were ridiculous. 
Would stay here again.

title: “We'll be back for more”
text: This hotel is perfect. Its a home away from home. The staff are so helpful and friendly, they couldn't do enough for us. The rooms are spotless (beds are surprisingly small - a standard double but very comfy), the wine and cheese reception is much more than that....hot chocolate, coffee, latte's cakes biscuits and fruit available all day, just perfect when it's snowing and freezing outside. Great location, just off Times Square and perfectly safe. Absolutely loved every minute of our 5 day stay here, will definately be back will recommend it to all of my friends and family.

title: “Fantastic Experience!”
text: We stayed at the Sofitel Sept. 16th-19th and the staff went above and beyond to make this a special trip. My boyfriend proposed to me in Chicago and the concierge was involved in every detail to make it a special weekend. The room(s) are stunning (my boyfriend upgraded us to a suite the night he proposed). Both of the rooms décor and views are incredible. The food in the restaurant was very good and the brunch had some nice little “extra” touches. The location is fantastic too ( just a few blocks from the mag mile and the lake) ….the hotel is in a pretty upscale neighborhood/shopping area.. If you wanted a suite, I highly recommend room:1801 – the room had a huge bathroom and floor to ceiling windows of the city. Overall the hotel was pretty close to perfect (good value too considering what you get).

title: “Stay for the Location and Price”
text: I stayed here 2 nights in July with a friend. The hotel and bar area is up to date but the rooms and pool need to be updated. My allergies lite up like the fourth of July while staying here. But this is a good location to the downtown area, Stubbs and UT. This hotel was more affordable compared to the downtown hotels. Younger crowd here. Hotel does offer club access with some room packages. Club access allows you to enjoy a VIP room with drinks, TV's, computers, coffee, breakfast and happy hour. Great hotel if you want low price, great location and do not plan to spend alot of time in the room.

title: “In need of TLC”
text:
As a Starwood member, I always make a point to book one of their properties if they are available. This was our first stay at the Westin Columbus and we were looking forward to the charm of this historical building.
The few staff members we ran into always greeted us with a smile and their service was standard as far as the Westin goes. The lobby and building itself were indeed graceful and we were really looking forward to our two room suite.
As we crossed the threshold of room 555 we were slightly disappointed that our historic room had at some point simply become old and shabby. Both rooms were very dark and lacked just about everything you come to expect from the Westin. There were multiple light bulbs burnt out and a few electric outlets that just didn't work. The ill fated minibar was unfortunately plugged into one of these outlets and the odor coming from inside led me to believe that something was definitely past its prime.
The bathroom, tiny as it might have been, was probably the nicest room in the suite.
We always look forward to the signature Heavenly Beds but we're again disappointed. That poor mattress was probably as old as the building itself. You were greeted by the box spring when you sat on the edge and once you were laying down, it took effort to roll out of the pit your found yourself in.
Strangely enough, this was the first Westin we stayed at that did not have a guest survey form in the room or delivered with your statement. I did alert the manager at the desk of the electrical problems and the odor in the minibar. His response was a small giggle and a "we'll check into that.".
Our final impression of the Westin Columbus was that of an aging beauty queen; graceful in appearance but in need of a little TLC. If your looking for a Starwood property in Columbus, your probably better off at the Sheraton north of town.

title: “Nice hotel. Clean/new rooms, comfortable bed, very central location”
text: I found a great air/hotel package online and stayed 3 nights. As others have already mentioned, this hotel's rooms are on the small side, but they are well thought out and not claustrophobic. The king size bed was very comfortable. The bathroom only had a shower, but it was spotless. I think it's a great home base in midtown if you're sightseeing, or in town on business. The hotel staff was friendly and helpful, the maid did a great job each day. There was a bit of a traffic jam in the breakfast room my first morning. The layout didn't seem to be as well designed as it could have been and for some reason the coffee urns are hidden outside the dining room area next to the business center. But the food was plentiful with the fairly standard offering of cold and hot cereals, waffles, bagels (toaster available), pastries, yogurt, fruit and fruit salad. Other than needing to improve how the food is laid out, the only other minor complaint is the rooms aren't wireless... you can only access wireless from the 1st floor (although there are internet cables for laptops in the rooms). I recommend this hotel and would definitely stay again.

title: “Perfect spot to explore L.A.”
text:
The location, price, and amentities of this inn are unbeatable for L.A. I would describe the Brentwood Inn as a combination of a B & B and upscale motel. 
Located within a couple miles of Brentwood, UCLA, and Bel Air to the east and Santa Monica and the coast to the west. Extrememly nice and helpful employees. I would absolutely recommend the Brentwood Inn for anyone wishing to have an on the go trip in L.A.

title: “beautiful hotel, great location”
text:
we checked in pretty late and were given a handicap room and didn't receive the amex upgrade (neither of which are complaints) but other than that the staff was very attentive and service-oriented. our room was pretty large and unlike other handicap-accessible rooms i've seen, it didn't seem like things were positioned lower and there weren't support bars on walls. there was a small foyer with the mini-bar that could be closed off with double doors and i love the bath/shower wet-room often seen in asian hotels. my main complaint with the rooms is we first had foam pillows which were squeaky, so we requested down. they were extremely firm. i asked for softer down pillows. i'm not sure if they were switched out because the pillows were still pretty firm.
the fitness room has basic cardio machines, dumb-bells and some strength machines. it has a nice yoga studio room too. the spa has a great wet room with jacuzzi, steam, that mist shower thing. the spa menu is quite pricey. i enjoyed my facial but if i lived in boston, this wouldn't be my regular spot cuz of the prices ($195 for a facial).
breakfast at asana was pleasant. they had birchermuesli on the menu which is my top vacation bfast food. and they make it well here. good service, food isn't amazing but it's very good and pretty presentation. definitely seemed like lots of business meetings conducted at the hotel restaurant.
