big plus is the location. above prudential mall, close to newbury, easy to get to the green T stops and red line areas are easy to reach via the Mass Ave bus just a few block walk away. (i can get my flour bakery sticky buns in just 10 min via the #1 bus to MIT!) overnight parking is $45 but on the central parking website (which is underneath the hotel), there is a printable coupon for $25 overnight. MO is a nice addition to downtown hotels since a lot of the hotels around are old and dusty. OH, and i do find it bothersome that many high-end hotels continue to charge for wi-fi.

title: “Location only good thing”
text: Location great otherwise you a a complete burden for the hotel and its staff . Took ages to check in about 40 min queue . Staff typical NY rude , rooms VERY basic and not that clean , desperate to be made over .

title: “Perfect”
text: I surprised my special friend with a birthday trip to DC by train. The hotel is located within walking distance from Union station which made it very convenient. We had a bit of a wait before check in so we were able to browse the Union station shops and enjoyed brunch at B.Smith's exquisite restaurant. My friend was very impressed with the hotel and could not believe I went to such expense for him. I was very pleased when I realized I could take advantage of the winter rate. The only clitch I experienced was the fee I was quoted for a special room service birthday surprise didnot match my check out fee. But to me, that was minor based on the happiness I was able to present to my friend. I would definitely stay again. We didnot rent a car, so we were pleased that the hotel is strategically located to alot of the museums and other points of interest. The most exciting point was we could look out and see the Capital. What a treat to see the Capital lit up at night. We had a wonderful time, thanks to the hotel and staff.

title: “great location, friendly staff”
text: fyi: construction on parking garage is completed now (no more jackhammers). fantastic location. I walked EVERYWHERE except the zoo, which was over 3 miles away--took a quick Metro ride to that though (L'Enfant Plaza and Smithsonian Station are both VERY close by). Had read bad reviews of restaurants so didn't eat there until last day of a week long trip--I wish I had eaten there earlier (21st Amendment Grill). the burger and fries were FANTASTIC! and be sure to grab some homemade fudge from the gift shop ($8 per half pound) it is superb. as for staff, there was supposed to be a $10 per day charge for a microwave, but when we were checking in and told the lady that we would need to heat our toddler's food, she said she would just give it to us, and the employee with the microwave arrived upstairs at our room before we did! also helpful explaining the metro system.

title: “Just okay”
text:
Okay, here is the good:
1/2 a block from Bart so easy to get to and from the airport without taking a cab or shuttle.
Room has been updated.
Nice lobby area.
No need for a car since you are right off Market street with all the public transportation near by.
Here is the okay:
Kind of a bad area at night. Market Street here isn't the best.
Not a lot of restaurants nearby other than Burger King nearby.
Hotel restaurant was only open in the evening for dinner on weekends. No lunch or breakfast here. Breakfast should be their busiest time.
Thermostat in room didn't work the first night and froze to death until they fixed it.
Check in desk clerk was kinda a grumpy old man.
The computers in the business center had a charge to use them. What????
There you go. Hope this helps.

title: “Fantastic service”
text: My family of four recently stayed at the Crowne Plaza Beverly Hills and the service was the best I have ever experienced. As soon as we arrived the Conciege and staff bent over backwards to make us feel welcome, even to the extent of escorting us to the bus stop and telling the bus driver where we wanted to go as we were from outside the US and a little unsure of where to go. We absolutely loved our stay at the Crowne Plaza, the beds were extremely comfortable it was quiet and we walked to Rodeo Drive. We would stay there again if we ever come back to LA, thanks so much!!

title: “last time”
text: We go to philly once a year to see the flyers and have always used this hotel because its so close to the wachovia center.The last 3 years the quality and service has gone WAY downhill and the prices way up.They did a renovation a while back but things are worse than before....missing covers on the outlets...broken furniture...no exhaust in the not too clean bathrooms....and plenty of attitude at the front desk.We stayed there on 3/9 to 3/11....I had made reservations on 1/18 for 2 rooms,the rate was supposed to be $108 per night per room($474 total)When we checked out we were told our total was $738.We explained that we made reservations at the lower rate but they refused to check into it,saying they couldnt do anything and gave me a card with the managers #...(still waiting for a return call)..from what Ive read in these reviews that's not gonna get me anywhere....so i'm calling my credit card company to stop payment....maybe then they'll call me.

title: “going home to see mom”
text: after much traveling, i realized that i had not seen my mother in a while so i went home. booked the hotel last minute and ended up in the Hyatt. have stayed there many times before. got a delayed flight so i didnt end up there until about 1 in the morning. checked in. quiet. the valet was full so i parked across the street. went into my room. the contour of the room as always was a bit unusual. the bathrooms are dated. very dated. the room itself was clean and nice. nothing special. slept and then got situated. it was busy in the morning. overall not a bad stay. its just a very sterile hotel. not much of an experience. i used to remember it being nicer.

title: “Do not stay at the Hyatt Saint Claire”
text:
I attended a convention in San Jose (at another hotel) and stayed at the Sainte Claire. I had booked through Expedia and the hotel clerk couldn't find my reservation. That isn't so bad and stuff happens. It was that night when I went to bed that bad stuff started to happen. I went to sleep early (still on Eastern time) and woke up a few hours later with a feeling of something biting my legs. I got up turn on the lights but couldn't see anything. Figured I was dreaming laid down again and felt these little bites again. This time I got up pulled the sheets off and checked the mattress. There was a thick (down?) pad on top of the mattress that looked to be stained with what looked like blood and stuff I couldn't imagine or want too. I told the staff about the biting and dirty mattress the next morning as asked it to be cleaned and changed. It wasn't. Should have complained more but didn't. 
Emailed Hyatt when I got home and heard from their people who said that they would talk to the hotel manager and I have not heard anything since. Don't stay here or at least in room 533.

title: “Great marketing, poor reality”
text: I have had better service and cleanliness at many mid-range motels. The restaurant and bar were not open, which we were not told in advance...our bathroom had dirt in the corners...housekeeping thought we were leaving a day earlier than we were and asked us about this more than once... While some of the front desk staff were lovely, others were haughty rather than polite or hospitable. If we had been at a $65 a night motel, the service would have been what I would have expected, though I would have still been dismayed by the restaurant's closure. We went there expecting (and paid for) much more than we got.

title: “Very Nice Stay”
text: WOW - some of the reviews scared me. We stayed on 10-13. Hotel is super clean, modern and well apointed. Staff was helpful and friendly. The hotel property was very nice, clen and well maintained. It was a great value, and only about 7 miles to downtown if that. I will stay again.

title: “Lives up to the hype”
text: Very nice, we had a few problems with the room smelling like smoke, but that's because some previous douchey guest decided to smoke in the bathroom and after finally figuring it out... The robe is what smelled like smoke, so after 4 days it got better, but the overall service and overall convenience of this was great. They responded to anything and everything regarding requests. You can't really ask for more than this place, for $200 a nice in the heart of time square, really? amazing!

title: “Hard to fault”
text: We read numerous reviews of NYC hotels before picking one and were not disappointed with the Chandler; good price, clean room with ipod docking station, flat screen tv, free wi-fi and air con, big bathroom with walk in shower and bathrobes, easy walk to the Empire State building, Times Square, Macys and Grand Central station and will definitely be staying there again and recommending it to others. Also the Thai restaurant opposite the hotel is good and cheap after a long day seeing the sights.

title: “Grumpy unhelpful staff & construction next door - BEWARE!”
text: I stayed at the Salisbury Hotel in January of 2007 & absolutely loved it. Great location, reasonable rates & helpful staff at that time. Since the, it is as though the whole establishment has stepped into an alternate universe. The staff, many of whom I remember well from my previous visit, would not even look you in the eye when you approached the front desk. Their answers were curt, dismissive & extremely unhelpful - here's a quick example...I heard a hotel guest go to the front desk & say that she thought she might like to do a cruise on the Hudson River. Without even looking up at her, the staff member at the front desk replied gruffly, "the pamphlets are over there"...& that was it. Sorry, but for the exorbitant rates this hotel is asking now, with average rooms in need of a face-lift, & an unadvertised construction site right next door (imagine sleeping with an operational crane your room & you will get the idea)...my advice to you...take your much needed dollars to another hotel - there are plenty to choose from in Manhattan that will service you better than the Salisbury these days, I am very sorry to say.

title: “Great Location, Clean, Friendly Staff”
text: We arrived in Wash. DC. via train from N.Y. The hotel is a short couple of blocks from Union Station. We were meeting a group of friends there and one of our friends got lost and the front desk was very helpful in trying to give her directions. They could not be more accommodating to us during our stay helping with recommendations for restaurants and sightseeing tours. Our rooms were very clean and were very comfortable. We definitely would return. Special thanks to Michael Long, Surrah and Johnny at the front desk.....

title: “Great Hotel, Great Service”
text: I stay at this hotel regularly -at least several times per month on business and occasionally with family for visits to D.C. Just one day at this hotel and you will feel you were on vacation for a week. The location is great as is the service, staff, and food. If possible -pay the extra $75.00 for the 8th floor club access and have a great breakfast, snacks, drinks, newspapers, etc. in a quiet setting. The lobby bar is under rennovation but I'm told will be finished in a few weeks. CVS and Starbucks across the street is very convenient when you need essentials -but the hotel has amazing coffee as well. Cabs and car service available all day and night -staff will help you get where you need to go. I reserve 5 star ratings for world class resorts -but this property is pretty close!

title: “Loved it !”
text:
We stayed at the HHH 5 days in september and I simply loved it. The staff is extremely friendly and helpfull, they helped us out several times, nothing was too much. Our room, # 116, was spacious and cosy. With a living, bedroom and balcony. It really felt like our own little home in LA. For the rate ($129) it was really the best deal we could get in LA. 
Location on the hill is great, you have great views. They have a shuttle service which can bring you up and down whenever you want. The pool at the hotel downstairs is rather small, the one on top is bigger.

title: “Wonderful Hotel in the Heart of OSU”
text: I had a great stay at the Blackwell. Wonderful hotel and conveniently located. It certainly was a bit pricey, but with the offered airport shuttle and town car service included in the stay, it was well worth it! Would definitely stay here again.

title: “NASTY, MOLDY, DIRTY!!! Horrible Stay!!!!!!!”
text: THIS IS THE WORST MOTEL I HAVE EVER SEEN!! Please do yourself a favor and do NOT stay at this location!!!! This motel is horribly discusting!! The rooms are fithy dirty, definately not suitable for children or anyone for that matter! Clearly there was a water leak that had been leaking for years I'm sure, which you could clearly see they simply just tried to paint the stain, however there was mold growing all along the wall and door frame!! The carpets, bathroom, and bedding were absolutly discusting!!! We asked for extra clean sheets to line the room with and they hastled us about getting more sheets. The walls are paper thin, we heard everything from the people next to us talking, doors slamming, people upstairs and the water running all morning from people showering. The only reason that we decided to actually stay here was becuase we arrived at 1130 PM and we were too exhausted to search for another option. Absolutly horrible!! Again, do yourself a favor and book at a Motel 6 for the same price!!!

title: “Amazing!!”
text: Awesome hotel! STAY HERE!! Not only do you get a free breakfast they serve dinners on sertain nights for FREE! Excellent room! Clean clean clean! Service was beyond helpfull! If I could live here I would! Haha deffinitley get a suite! It's like a mini apartment! I don't know what else I could say to tell you how great this place is overall!

title: “GOOD VALUE GOOD LOCATION”
text: We stayed at the Moore Hotel pre and post cruise to Alaska. We had a suite witha seperate bedroom for our nephew who was traveling with us. It is not the most modern of hotels 100 years old. If you arte into historic this is the plaace. The rooms are clean. It is a bit noisey due to traffic out side. No Air condiationing, but you don't need it. Walking distance to everything including busses to Sea-Tac. Night desk clerk robert, knows all the good spots to see..Would stay there again

title: “Pleasure Staying at the Palomar”
text: Excellent service. Room was comfortable and quiet despite being above an Old Navy Store and on Market St., but a bit small, with no drawers for a long stay. We ate at Fifth Floor for dinner and it was heavenly. Conviently located to everything and concierge Virgil is the best!!! More swanky than luxurious, but we enjoyed it.

title: “We will be back!!!!”
text:
Great place to stay!!!
Staff was great!! all of them. The location was perfect..quick walk to the 1 train or the A-C-E trains. Rooms were of course small, but for a budget they very clean. Shared bathrooms are not as bad as it sounds...worth it , if its gonna save you at 150 bucks a night.
If you want fast elevators, huge rooms and private baths..go stay at a newark airport hotel or spend 500 bucks a night in manhatton. This place was perfect..walking distance to hundreds of hundreds of great places to eat and tons of shopping....don't listen to the "nit-pickers"

title: “If you want to be treated respectfully, then do not stay here!”
text:
The hotel itself is updated and inviting with it's colorful, modern, decor. The rooms are large and whimsical. Our room was on the top floor, in a corner, located next to an emergency exit. It was loud and when the wind would blow it sounded like we had a banshee in our bathroom. 
All of those things are fine...imaginary banshees I can deal with. What I was upset about is that my husband and I booked the hotel through our spg card and were quoted a rate. When we checked into the hotel the manager refused to accept this rate. He wanted our AAA card. Fine, it was on our keys to our car that was valeted so he said we could show it later and they would change the rate. The next day, we show him the card. This was now unacceptable and we needed to show him paperwork. Ummm...my husband and I are here to celebrate our anniversary and to meet with family who have flown in to town. I didn't pack paperwork. Mr. Boyd was quite discourteous, rude, and would not listen. His attitude is poor and he should not be representing Sheraton. As a manager he should have better people skills and at least be willing to hear what the issue is before he flies off the handle and attempts to belittle guests. My husband and I left calmly. We refused to let Mr. Boyd's negativity and rudeness hinder our anniversary weekend.
I would say if you want to be treated poorly by the management, not have the hotel honor your room rate, and not sleep soundly then stay here. Otherwise, look for other options! My husband and I were married at a Sheraton in Maui and have made it tradition to stay at a Sheraton to celebrate...but after this stay we will be rethinking this tradition!

title: “Extended due to the snow!”
text:
We arrived at the W on Lexington Avenue on the 17th December for a 3 night stay and were not dissapointed. I had emailed in advance to ask for a nice view if possible as it was both mine and my husbands birthdays, we were nicely greeted on arrival and told of complimentary breakfast in the room on the morning of our birthdays which was a very nice surprise. 
We had a very enjoyable stay, the Cosy room was very small however clean and well done so did not feel cramped. On the 20th we were told our return flight was cancelled due to snow in London and the next available flight would be the 26th December!! Very sad that we would miss Christmas with our family back in the UK we called to extend our stay however the best available rates were almost double what we had initially paid per night, however we were told the website offered lower rates and indeed it did, almost 50% less than the rate given over the phone (thank goodness for the iPad!). We extended our reservation online, and were given a complimentary upgrade at the desk as we were there for an additional 5 days (we did have to ask for it). We then spoke with the very helpful concierge team who reccomended some ideas for Christmas day and booked everything for us. We had a very comfortable stay, the upgraded room was a lot more comfortable and the daily bliss products were a very nice touch, the only let down was that all of the rooms overlook each other so you have to be careful and always close the curtains which many of our neighbours had not realised!
On the 26th, we were advised of yet another cancellation this time due to the Snow in New York, what a nightmare! Again we extended our stay and was told we could keep the upgraded room. We checked out on the 27th to face yet more cancellations and delays at the airport and finally arrived home on the 28th December, a very long and expensive weekend break in New York. 
The W on Lexington Avenue certainly helped to make our extended stay more comfortable. We did have to ask for certain things like the larger room or WI-FI password which under our difficult circumstances it would have been nice if they had acertained our needs such as offering say $20 of complimentary laundry as we had run out of clothes, but as I also work in hotels maybe I see things slightly differently. 
The lobby bar was very comfortable and the Whiskey Blue bar were both very nice serving up some delicious cocktails. In summary the staff were very helpful, the hotel was very comfortable and the location was great, within walking distance of most major attractions. I would definetely stay in another W around the World and reccomend this to my friends.

title: “Great location but nothing spectacular in the rooms, and noisy.”
text: Room is good, very large with a huge bathroom. Location is close to the convention center and easy access to mass transit. My only real complaints are the noisy streets below and the lack of a coffee maker in the room. I understand I'm in the city by my corner room is really loud, I can hear everything happening on the street 16 floors down. I also find it strange I don't have a coffee maker in the room.

title: “Looking for convenience in Chicago?”
text: This property, just off Michigan Avenue and south of the congress expressway, is convenient to the Art Institute, Orchestra Hall, the Museum Campus, including the Field Museum and Adler Planetarium -- and to Grant Park, Buckingham fountain and the Bean...at the north end of Milllenium Park. A food service operation, which I did not try, is on the ground floor and is accessible through the hotel lobby; a coffee/donut shop is just around the corner -- I was told it's open 24x7. The hotel itself? Modest. The lobby is basic...two seating areas, both with half a dozen chairs, more or less...no tv, no coffee bar (no continental breakfast is served). The staff was pleasant, friendly and attentive. We were there for Bike the Drive, and the staff made sure our bikes were locked up overnight and we had not trouble getting them at 5:30 am the morning of the ride. (Lake Shore drive is bicycle-only from 5-10 am the Sunday before Memorial day.) The room was consistent with the hotel -- basic. Small, with a small closet, one small chair, and a little room around the twin beds. I wondered why the window air conditioner was unplugged when I entered the room...found out later; the switches were broken and the only way to turn the unit off was to unplug it. Oh well. Best feature: clean, functional bathroom, nice hot shower and heavy terry cloth towels -- a real surprise. I was expecting those thin, lightweight towels found in economy operations. Parking across the street (for overnight stays) was not cheap: $35, a $5 discount if you have you stub validated; otherwise it's $40 with no in/out. This is not an unusual price for parking in downtown Chicago -- be prepared to spend at least $40 a day.

title: “So So Hotel”
text: The Location is good and the Room was clean, so far the good Things. The Room had nö real window, only in the ceiling, which should Be at least mentioned when you Book the Room. For a Three Star Place Not Bad, but there are better options at their Price Level in the City. I paid almost Three hundred USD per Night.

title: “Upper East NYC”
text: We stayed at Affinia Gardens Upper East and enjoyed. Excellent location in a good hotel if you like to stay in a residential neighborhood very close to just about everything! We stayed in a patio room with a large patio where we enjoyed a waterfall and the green around while sipping a glass wine in the warmth of May.

title: “Need a cold shower?”
text:
The biggest problem with this hotel is that they do not have HOT WATER. Every morning I was forced to take a 2 minute shower because that was as much as I could stand of the cold water. 
I spoke with management and their reply was that they have ONE hot water heater AT THE OTHER END OF THE HOTEL. Their advice was to let the water run for 5-10 mins (1. Tried it, didn't work & 2. Charlotte is supposed to be on water restriction b/c of the drought - good to know they are doing their part!) or ask for a room on the opposite end of the hotel. As if new guests are supposed to know to ask to be on the side of the water heater. 
Other than that, the stay was tolerable. Yes, they are renovating, which means boxes strewn throughout the floors, but the staff was nice. However, the cold showers were unbearable and despite the renovations, they have no plans to correct it. Even shelters provide hot water for showers. I'm an adult and I was miserable, I would hate for a kid to have to put up with that. Stay away, especially if there are kids involved.

title: “A good place to be trapped...but trapped you are. Beware of the expense report.”
text:
I stayed at this hotel in April, 2010 for a variety of business meetings, including a couple at the hotel. The hotel's facilities were fantastic: stylish lobby; roomy guest rooms with great design, wonderful and flexible desk area, and comfortable bedding; and a huge conference center that appeared to be recently renovated and avoided some of the typical hotel-ballroom-blandness by having several locally-themed displayed on Texas businesses and leaders that were actually pretty interesting. The fitness center was great: a wide range of cardio equipment and free weights, open 24-hours, nice towels, even a wine refrigerator filled with cool towels to use post-workout! I was very impressed with the physical plant of the hotel; it's significantly nicer than its 1980s-looking exterior would suggest and certainly was a refreshing change-of-pace from usually design-less airport hotels I've stayed at in other cities.
Service-wise, I had a mixed experience. I had dinner at the fancy steakhouse in the hotel; the service was superb. The front desk and housekeeping service was good. The meetings staff seemed to do a good job. I had a more mixed experience in the business center, where the staff was laughably inflexible. I had dinner in the restaurant off the lobby one night, and the service there was horrible -- I waited forever to be taken to a table, and once at the table my server was slow and disinterested. Nothing is more frustrating than watching the staff be more concerned about re-setting the tables for breakfast than it is about clearing your food or bringing something out while it's still warm.
The hotel is attached to DFW's parking garages. There's nothing nearby -- all restaurants, stores, etc. are either within security at DFW or outside of the (huge) airport complex (WAY beyond walking distance). So, in one sense, the location is very convenient, as no other hotel (except the other Hyatt) is on the airport's grounds. The downside, though, is that the on-airport location means that the hotel has you trapped when it comes to services and meals. It knows this...even though the room rate was reasonable, everything else was NOT. The most ridiculous was the business center, where computer access to print cost a minimum of $9.00 (plus a certain amount per page). An envelope cost money, as did copies, etc. I had some documents to copy that were sort of complicated (i.e., some pages needed to be copies, others didn't; some had to be blown up, others shurnk), and it was my strong preference to do the copying myself. The staff in the business center initially wouldn't allow me to do that, saying they couldn't be liable if I were injured by the copy machine. Come on. When I promised not to sue they agreed to let me make the copies so long as the business center associate stood next to me; this showed me that they were less concerned with liability and more concerned with nickel-and-diming me. I bet they sure are glad they didn't miss out on one chance to charge me $.10.
The restaurant prices were also absurd. There is an a la carte, classic steakhouse attached to the hotel. It was a lovely meal, and a very nice restaurant at which you expected the prices to be elevated to match the quality of the service...but the prices were crazy expensive; it was nearly $100/person for a salad, entree, and glass of wine (and that was ordering with caution!). The regular restaurant wasn't that crazy, but my chicken breast entree was $26 -- add a salad and an iced tea, and you're talking a $40 dinner. The coffee bar's prices were similarly high. So, being connected to DFW is very convenient...but you PAY for that convenience!
Overall, absent the bad experience in the restaurant and the bean counter in the business center, the hotel was very nice, but the hidden costs were higher than normal. So, balance the great facility and desire of being connected to DFW with the off-airport properties that are less expensive and have access non-hotel owned stores, restaurants, etc.

title: “Convention Center Location”
text: This modern hotel in the heart of downtown Seattle is large with about 30 floors of rooms, located across the street from the Washington Convention Center, down the street from the flagship Nordstroms store, and several blocks from Pike Place Market. The lobby is classy. The rooms are quite standard but clean. The carpeting on the floor of my stay looked dirty, worn and in need of an upgrade. On a positive note, the fitness center and swimming pool are really nice. This hotel is especially good for business travelers and conference attendees.

title: “Good value for money with windows that open”
text: Centrally located for shopping and other hotels.I was attending a seminar at the Grand Hyatt on Pine St and enjoyed the 10 minute walk each way at the beginning and end of the day. The staff were helpful and friendly. Rooms are clean and I like the Save the Planet program they have in place. I only ate a light breakfast in the lounge/dining room but the staff were pleasant, the ambience agreeable and prices appeared average.

title: “Lovely Views, Efficient”
text:
Did not 'upgrade' for $20, but still had a room with view over railroad yards and bay. Had requested no feathers due to allergies and they had thoughtfully put an air cleaner in the room.
Apart from that, typical Hilton, no charm, but efficient. Walk to Gaslight district not too bad, but if you want to be close to restaurants etc, there are better choices

title: “My new favorite in NYC”
text: I don't stay in hotels in NYC often since it's easy to go home to NJ, but do stay on a quarterly basis for a work meeting. We've previously stayed in a Marriott around Grand Central, but this month, moved to the Hyatt 48. Great hotel! The room was small, but did have an amazing shower/bathroom (I think you're out of luck if you want a bathtub), very comfortable bed, and, most important of all to me....it seemed like the room was soundproof (when it came to outside noise). I did stop by to see the lounge, but didn't take advantage of the free beverages/snacks...maybe during the next visit. They provide turn down service and all the staff I encountered were very pleasant. It's also located right next door to an amazing Greek restaurant. Definite thumbs up for Hyatt 48.

title: “Nice hotel, good breakfast & bar, noisy room by elevator”
text: We stayed five nights at the Park South Hotel and really liked it. The location was pretty good and the subway stop was 1/2 block away. Breakfast was very good with warm, fresh bagels alongside sliced meats and cheeses. We had a glass of wine one night in the bar, which was great. Hotel staff was helpful each time we spoke with them, so I am lost on the post about the unfriendly staff. The only problem we had was that our room (#201) was right by the elevator, so it was noisy. We thought it was the pipes making noise for the first couple of nights, then realized it was the elevator. We were so tired after jam-packed days exploring that it did not bother us while sleeping. I simply would not stay in any room ajacent to the elevator. Overall, nice place, and we'd stay again.

title: “Not disappointed”
text: This was our second stay at the Belvedere and it was as enjoyable as the first. If we return to New York we would definitely stay there again. The location is great both for the proximity to some of the tourist attractions (you can pick up a sightseeing bus within a couple of minutes walk) and for the variety of restaurants within walking distance.

title: “Perfect place”
text: My husband and I loved the time we spent in this hotel, it is near Broadway and we could walk to everywhere we wanted. I booked an evolution room, which was great, big and comfy, really nice with a great view. We just loved our stay.

title: “Great service, great location, great amenities.”
text:
I really enjoyed my stay at this hotel, we had a junior suite with two twin beds, and they are, twin beds. They were small and very uncomfortable, but aside from that the room was fantastic, they bathroom was large, lovely and well lit. The services provide from the hotel were great, the food was great for the banquets and the everyone was really nice. Location was fantastic too!
Within easy walking distance of the Paramount and convention center too!

title: “location”
text:
Stayed here again as I had before. It`s not until you go back you begin to remember how good this place really is. Service is first class & they are always ready to help.
The location is the best for everything. 20 yards away Times Square. You are in Broadway on this street.
Once again if going to New York,I would not even think about going elsewhere.

title: “good hotel”
text:
We did not have a booking for this hotel and arrived at 11 am - we were given a great clean room overlooking the pool. the hotel was spotless the staff were friendly and the hotel was in a great location off the freeway - 5 minutes to sea world and about 20 minutes to the zoo you are also about 15 minutes away from mission bay etc and coronado which is lovely.
the hotel food was ok in quality and price.
the pool was a good size and clean towels were alway available for use. overall a great hotel.

title: “great location”
text:
The Crockett Hotel is in a great location, our bedroom looked straight over the grounds of The Alamo. We stayed there for 5 nights in August as a special treat for my husbands 60th birthday. The hotels' buffet breakfast in the morning was good and it was fun being able to make Texas shaped waffles too. The coffee could do with being a bit stronger but thats the only thing wrong with breakfast. It was nice having the little pool outside and a welcome place to go in the afternoon when it got very hot, it was great to cool off. The Riverwalk shopping mal was just across the road and a great place to eat. Our room was a good size and a very comfortable bed. We had no problems with noise though I think anyone near the ice machines would have had some problems with the noise from them. 
Most of the staff were very nice and friendly though the reception staff were not as friendly as other staff. We arrived a day late due to being delayed at Dallas airport and we had a very rough start to our holiday because of staff shortages at Dallas. We arrived at The Crockett very tired and disappointed we had missed the first night of our holiday but the girl on reception showed no sympathy or concern for us, her only concern was to tell us we couldn't have a refund (even though I hadn't asked for one as we had booked through an other company) and then just handed us the key and returned to her computer. But overal, it is a great hotel and I would stay there again.

title: “Great staff”
text:
This hotel is very near the airport and has all the usual amenities. The room was fairly standard and a teeny bit run down. However, the excellent staff made up for any perceived detraction. The people actually made a point to be friendly and acted like they truly cared that my partner and I had a great time. A special acknowledgement to front desk area personnel Marcus and Bernice and the breakfast room attendant and the cleaning lady on the third floor (sorry, I forgot the names). They were the type of folks I wish worked at every hotel. 
The free breakfast is excellent and plentiful with fresh fruits along with eggs and meat. Hot coffee or tea is available 24 hours a day at no charge with urns in the reception area and coffee packages for the pot in the room. There is also a free daily USA Today newspaper and a small lending library of books to borrow and return. There are two computers in the front desk area for guest use with attached printers. 
The hotel pool is small but quite nice. There is a good hot tub in the pool room, too. I saw the exercise room and it had a few running machines, but I didn't use it. 
The price was very competitive and was quite reasonable for the amount of service we got. 
Oh, the beds were very luxurious!

title: “Great quiet hotel near Union Square”
text: I stayed here several nights in March. The first few nights my friend from college days and I shared a double room on the 9th floor. The last few nights my husband joined me and we had a king room on the 6th floor. I really liked almost everything about this place. It was very quiet and peaceful. The rooms and bathrooms were clean and spacious enough. The beds are very comfortable. It is very close to union square - a block or two away. Close to many good restaurants and art galleries, etc. I will stay here again! One thing they could do better - soap! They gave us two pieces of tiny tiny soap. In fact, when my husband and I checked into the king room, there was only one tiny tiny bar of face soap. I did not eat at the restaurant there or use room service, though my friend used room service for breakfast one morning. The staff there is great. Friendly, helpful, they would do whatever they could to be of assistance. Nice place, and reasonably priced for that location.

title: “Great Hotel. Great Stay”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the Omni for five days. Our first vacation without the kids.
The hotel was beautiful. Very elegant.
Our room was very spacious and quiet. A big plus. We are Omni Club Members so we recieved complimentary breakfast each morning. This was very appreciated since everything in DC is overpriced (except the blue point oysters which are priceless). If you aren't a member, apply. It's free and it's the first hotel membership that we have that really came in useful.
The hotel had complimentary highspeed wireless internet so bring your laptop. The pool area was very nice although the hot tub wasn't working. You can get a cold beer and a hot snack without leaving the pool area.
My only complaint is the hotel is pretty far out. Fortunately there is a nearby Metro stop. There are a lot of restaraunts nearby, but they close early. Had a tough time getting a late night meal (after 9:30).
If you stay at the Omni and you fly into Reagan National, cab it to the hotel. Don't take the shuttle the hotel recomends. You'r on the shuttle for quite a while (the hotel is one of the last stops). Also, the cab actually turned out to be cheaper than the shuttel.
This was a great hotel.

title: “Good solid choice”
text: I have no complaints about anything. Well almost nothing. The place was clean, decor pleasing, staff always helpful, if not real close it was an invigorating 15 minute hike to Alamo square. Rooms were comfortable and clean. I'm sure they don't need heaters much and when it was 23 degrees outside ours was rattling like a helicopter trying to keep up. Parking is always a problem in SA and our 18 a day charge added up in a hurry. They had a more than adequate, if a little pricey, breakfast buffet that kept me going through the day. Still for the price this was a great place and my picky family would recommend it to anyone.

title: “Beautiful Beach front Hotel”
text: My wife and I stayed at the Hilton San Diego Resort and Spa at Mission Bay from May 31 thru June 2, 2012. Hotel was located a few miles outside of downtown San Diego in a quiet area right on a beautiful beach. The hotel was conveniently located near the San Diego Zoo. Our room was updated and very comfortable. Hotel had a great pool and restaurant which was reasonably priced for breakfast. The only negatives were that the hotel charges $32.00 per night for parking and charges $15.00 per day for DSL. We used the free WIFI in the lobby to check emails. Also, we felt the concierge misinformed us regarding parking near the Padres stadium. She recommended that we take the hotel shuttle to the stadium because parking was difficult to find and expensive. Well, the hotel shuttle was $50 round trip whereas parking was easy to find and only $15. Overall, though, we had a nice stay at the hotel and would stay at this hotel again while visiting San Diego.

title: “Fantastic hotel & staff!”
text: We asked for a room on the top floor, with King bed, Non- smoking, and quiet. That was exactly what we received and more! From the minute we walked in we were treated with smiles, courtesy, and efficiency. The desk clerks, Terry & Shannon, were spectacular. We asked for information about restaurants and were given excellent choices plus printed out directions on each one. Our room was very clean and kept exactly as we wished throuhout our stay. The manager was very pleased to hear that we enjoyed our stay and said they have been doing everything possible to change their previous poor reviews. They have accomplished this and the Marriott Corporation should be proud of this hotel and in particular, it's staff!

title: “Unique and Personal”
text: I stayed here with a large group for my brothers wedding, which was also heldin the beautiful banquets. My entire family agrees that not only was the hotel beautiful and the location ideal, but the attentive and genuine service we received from each staff member made it exceptionally memorable. It felt like the omni was part of the events and.the wedding could have ONLY been held there. Maxi and the Bellman, front desk staff were amazing and obviously enjoyed their jobs. We were "thunderstruck"!

title: “Bugs! Worst place ever!”
text: I was looking for a good deal since I was planning to stay a couple weeks visiting my husband at Lackland AFB, big mistake picking this place. Walking in I was immediately regreting staying here. The place was covered in dirt, carpet was extremely dirty. I just couldnt believe how much dirt was in this place. Years and years of dirt accumulated. We complained right away and they had the cleaning lady come in and vacuum. She literally vacuumed one spot and left. The next morning, we woke up to a gigantic cockroach climbing up the wall from the head of the bed. We also found a couple of crickets on the side of the bed. We killed them and cleaned up the place ourselves. Took a drive to get some food, when we came back, there was a small lizard there to greet us near the closet. This place was absolutely horrible, infested with all kinds of bugs and filth. The management was no help what so ever!! You definitely get what you pay for.

title: “"great location"”
text: Recently spent two nights here, location is excellent for visiting downtown memphis. Our room was on union street and had great view. Room itself was ok for our needs, staff were all friendly and polite and service and food in bar/restaurant was excellent. memphis was great place to visit and if ever got chance to return wouldnt hesitate to stay here again.

title: “Sleep Over the Ocean”
text:
I had been told that these extremely popular cottages were almost impossible to reserve, but sometimes calling in the morning will snag a cancellation for that day. That's what we did.
Our cottage was squeaky clean but small and old-style. WE LOVED IT. We were out in the middle of the pier over the Pacific Ocean, 25 feet above the sand/water. We could see and hear the roaring ocean from inside (lulled to sleep by the sound of waves) and outside on one's own deck (no privacy outside, however). The pier is closed to outsiders at sunset, and we often walked out to the end to be amongst the waves and feel them pound and shake the pilings.
The cottages feature a kitchenette with m/wave and reefer, comfortable but small beds, and all the ambience of staying RIGHT ON THE OCEAN in the middle of a "city". 
It's pricey, even in the off-season, but what a woinderful experience!

title: “Hotel cuts corners in odd ways.”
text: A 3 room suite with 2 bathrooms, one with a tv, but the shower door is crooked and won't close. San Fran is known for great coffee but the in room coffee pot is a cheap monstrosity even Walmart wouldn't sell. The coffee in the restaurant downstairs is undrinkable. There are 11 different kinds of hard liquor in the suite but no tea. The room is gorgeous but i can hear every word from my neighbors tv, every noise they make, even when they drop their toilet seat. $300 for this?!

title: “Outstanding Customer Service”
text: I stayed here for three weeks on business. The premises was very clean and new. The bed was extremely comfortable, just like I like it, firm but soft at the same time. The kitchen had everything you need to make dinner and store food supplies. The free breakfast was good, although a little crowded at times and the workout facility was good also. There is lots of places to eat and drink in the neighborhood. Try the pizza place about a half block from the hotel, dollar pizza and it is very good. The high speed internet was also a big plus and it worked better than I have had it in many other smaller hotels around the country. I had a minor problem with the room air conditioner but a call for service fixed it immediately. Also I needed to change a reservation and doing so on line caused the rate to increase substantially but after calling the local sales manager (Patricia) it was fixed with no problems. It is rare to stay at any hotel in a large city and receive "true customer service" like they want you back and care about your trip. But at this hotel in NYC it still exists. I have not received this kind of customer service in very many places but this property ranks at the top, thanks to Patricia and her dedication to customer service. I will be back.

title: “An Excellent Experience”
text:
Everyone I dealt with at this hotel had one word that was not in their vocabulary and that word was NO.Tthey were able to accomodate anything I asked for. The rooms were spotless and very well appointed. The wireless internet worked great but it did cost extra. The room price was very good for a downtown hotel but the restaurants and bar were a little pricey but probably no more so than a downtown hotel in any other big city. The dinner in the restaurant was delicious. The only criticism I would have is that I ordered a house wine and the waiter poured about three sips into the glass. 
Other reviewers here complained about the lack of a refrigerator but my room had a refrigerated minibar with plenty of extra room in it. Yes, the items in the minibar were overpriced but no more so than any other hotel. 
 I would agree that the valet parking at $21 costs more than self parking. So, park across the street or around the block at the parking meters and keep plugging quarters in the meter. What do you expect in the middle of downtown? The best way to get the car is to call ahead for it. The wait was not long at all. When we stayed there the hotel was full but there were plenty of valets on duty.

title: “Staff made the visit great -”
text: This will be a mixed review - in some things this hotel excels, in others, not so much! Unless you are there on business at the convention center; it is not that convenient to the attractions in Boston; so you will cab or drive everywhere. One of the tourist trolley lines does stop there, so that is a possibility, and the hotel does sell tickets. The restaurant is not great, is very pricey, and has limited hours- and again, there are not a lot of alternatives close by. For some reason, room service was far superior to the dining room - rather unusual. There is a starbucks in house, and a nice lobby bar. The rooms are standard Westin - although smaller; especially the bath and closet. If you are family you may have a problem. there is a business center in house, staffed by very friendly people - but again, pricey. Parking is $39 PER DAY if you use their garage - there is limited on the street parking. What made my stay here excellent was the staff - the conceriege was one of the best I have ever had (and I travel often and use them regularly!); the bellmen, valet parkers, and room service waiters were all great. Even the Starbucks staff were extra friendly! Service is my #1 priority - and I was here on business - so the hotel worked well for me. I would stay personally if I could get a good deal to offset some of the pricey aspects such as parking & dining.

title: “No complaints but no wow factor”
text: Booked for 4 nights. Awkward car drop off at front door. Room Ok, small for a suite, dark. Furniture showing wear. Nice TVs, big bathroom. Some staff very attentive, others routinely forgot to follow through on specific requests. Not a bad place at all, but not a luxury experience, either. More likely to book at the Sofitel across the street on my next visit.

title: “Budget motel, but very nice”
text: This is a budget motel with good location and free parking. For me as a well-fit European, it is within walking distance to Fisherman's Wharf, the city centre, Lombard Street and more. The room was clean (most important), no disturbing noice from the outside and OK in size, although a little strange furnished. The staff was helpful and I will definitively stay here again.

title: “Beware of parking situation.”
text: I was looking for a decent hotel for reasonable price and this is where I ended up. The location is near the airport so a bit away from the hustle and bustle of downtown but just a short car or can ride. I was in the marina tower, 7th floor, facing downtown. Couldn't have asked for a better view. I Spent most of my day on the balcony. The hotel and room were clean and the check in process was quick and easy. The best part of my stay was the comfort of the beds. I could have stayed in it all day! The worst part was the self parking situation. Parking is $22 a day and I had to park my clean car in a dirt lot. I don't have a problem paying for parking but I expect at least a paved lot to justify the charge. This one reason alone would make me look at other hotel options in the area for future stays.

title: “Hip meets Comfort At Hotel Erwin, Venice Beach”
text:
Hotel Erwin offers a comfort-centered hotel with a local (street) arts oriented theme that conveys to the sense of place and authenticity of the Venice Beach location. The roof deck is a hidden gem...the only place that allows one to take in the beauty of the beach while remaining above the frenzied activity of the Venice Beach Promenade. A private NY High Line experience....overlooking the Pacific.
The Erwin's rooms have a comfort, a bit like staying at a friend's hip but homey condo on the beach.
The food is also a real treat...comfort food with a hip twist at athe hotel's diner style restarant with an attached street-side dining alcove.

title: “Visit at St. Anthony”
text:
I loved staying at this hotel. It was like spending time in a luxury hotel of days gone by.
These kinds of throwbacks from a grand era cannot be duplicated these days.
I also was impressed by the "snacks" offered in the afternoon between sessions.
The bananas foster, cake cubed with various toppings was such an unexpedted treat!

title: “Good hotel for business / airport”
text: I always have a good experience at Courtyard properties, and this one was no different. Hobby airport area isn't the nicest, but it's convenient. The hotel property is secure, free parking, wi-fi, decent fitness room. The hotel is clean and modern, and I especially like the lobby/bistro area. It's a comfortable working space with plenty of outlets. The food at the bistro is pretty good, and it's very convenient. The hotel and bistro staff were very friendly and accomodating. I will stay here again when in S. Houston.

title: “I wanted to love this hotel, but the hotel just wouldn't let that happen...”
text:
We went to DC for my fiancee's birthday. It's a cute hotel located in a nice area. The staff were friendly and welcoming. We checked in around 10pm and stayed in room 718. The room was spacious and the view of the circle was great. That is where the good stopped.
1. Construction on the 8th and 9th floors commenced at 9am. I like to sleep late on vacation. The noise was ridiculous. Hammering, sawing, banging, etc. It was like setting up a cot in a construction site. I called down and was told there was nothing they could do, the hotel was full, but if something else became available they could move me to a new room. Since that didn't happen, we awoke to the same noise the following day.
2. Around 6pm on our first night, a maintenance person came in to say that our A/C was leaking to the room below. He looked at it and went away for almost an hour to find a part. Not only were we trying to nap after a long day of site seeing, now we couldn't shower for dinner because we were expecting him back. The bathrooms open up into the room so I wouldn't have felt comfortable with a stranger there while showering.
3. When leaving, we had to take the stairs instead of the elevator because the hallway and elevator area was filled with a dense dust and fuel smell which worried us to take the elevator. 
Overall, it was a big disappointment. Aesthetically, it is a cute hotel. But if you want to relax, don't stay here. Also, no mini bar, bathrobes, etc.

title: “Loved the Location!”
text:
My grandparents took my cousin and I on a cruise that left from Seattle, so we stayed in the Sheraton one night. I typically really like the Sheraton, and this stay was no exception. I loved that we could walk so many places from the hotel! Since it's right on Pike's, you just walk down a few blocks to get to Pike's Market, which was great. And there's a bus/subway station right around the corner (we took a bus to U of W). The next morning, when we weren't sure where our ship was docked, the staff was very helpful with getting us to the right place. It was also a surprise to find a pool/spa and gym on the top floor! 
Overall, great stay. Would definitely recommend it.

title: “Great location to see a different part of Manhattan”
text: This place is very easy to get to from several different subway stations - all an easy walk away. What we liked the most about the location is that you can walk to Pier 11 for the water taxi and enjoy the shops, dining and people watching at Pier 17 - South St. Seaport. If you don't want to walk, the Andaz had bikes you can take out for 2 hours. Also, being so close to the water, it's a bit cooler with a breeze versus being in the heart of steamy Times Square in the summer. Going into the lobby, the check in area is a bit odd. There is an island in the middle of the room with laptops and tablets and some of the staff are dressed much like tourists. So it was a bit confusing on who worked there at first. The staff are super friendly and can give great advice on dining or activities and if they don't know, they happily look it up for you. Biggest complaint on the lobby is that is can be crowded with guests and having the check in located in the center of it all is a bit awkward. Also, the lobby muffins in the mornings and snacks in the afternoon are a nice touch but don't always count on it. Muffins are tiny and once they are gone...they are gone. Fruit and coffee was always available. Room was large and the beds were very comfortable as they are very firm. Our room had a huge shower and the window looking into the sleeping area was frosted so you do have privacy. Mini bar fridge had a coke, diet coke, sprite, 2 bottles of regular water, 2 bottles of sparkling water, on bottle of black tea, one bottle of OJ, one club soda and one tonic water which is all free. For snacks, it was one bag of plain chips, one granola bar and one candy bar. There was some beer and hard liquor that if used, you were charged for. Fridge is very small and ours wasn't that cold. So if you have leftovers, you need to be creative on how you cram them in there. Speaking of cold, it was tough to get our room air to get really cold. One weird note is that we had several small mosquito's in our room. The staff said they are around due to the humid conditions. Also, if you are a light sleeper, bring earplugs or a white noise machine. We were awoken at 5:50am on a Saturday morning to a concrete saw due to road work on the street below. The room air fan does not make much noise compared to other places, we usually count on that white noise to drown out city noise or inconsiderate hotel guests that talk loudly in the hallways. As a platinum members, one of our preferences is a hight floor and we were given the lowest floor. And yes, the lighting in the bathroom was terrible.

title: “Near Virginia Mason”
text: Visited a relative staying there during his wife's stay at Virginia Mason. The hospital is owned, apparently, by Virginia Mason. Can't believe it. It is like walking into a 1960's downtown cheap flop house. The appliances and furnishings are, seriously, out of the 60's. They still use bedspreads. During my visit there, I didn't even consider checking out the bathroom. I would not stay here for any reason, ever. I think that it is time for a extreme makeover.

title: “My friends and I had a blast and will definitely be back.”
text: When I performed an internet search for some type of girls' outing that included some combination of a hotel stay, drinks, and a spa service, the Alden was the only hotel that had the complete package. The Alden has employed a marketing genius:) My friends and I had an absolute blast! The staff was gracious and attentive, the martini kit and pedicures perfect. The ONLY thing I wasn't pleased with was the couch that made out into a bed. When we pulled it out, there were a couple of dead bugs in the linens. I'm sure this was due to lack of use. I've told several people since about our great experience and expect them to make their own reservations in the next few months. I work downtown but had never paid the Alden much attention. After the great time we had, I chose it for a happy hour this week. My friends and I were pleasantly surprised at the happy hour menu and wine list. We will definitely be back.

title: “Great Inn (not hotel) in a great location”
text:
Took a quick two night getaway to Seattle and decided to try the Inn at El Guacho. Glad we did as the Belltown location was amazing. The staff were all delightful and while I missed the full breakfast that a B&B might offer the coffee and newspaper were a welcome start to the day. 
Our room was at the back (corner) and had a comfy queen bed and lots of space with a great sofa and flat screen TV.
While all of this was great what I really liked was the funky vibe of being above a fab restaurant in a cooly decorated space.
Don't go if you need a chain hotel but if you like different, funky and friendly this is an inn worth visiting.

title: “Great little place, comfortable and good value with personal service”
text:
Really great little stopover hotel, a cut above other off-highway places we've visited! 
Our room was comfortable, smart and clean, and we also liked the very new pool and fitness center. The service was really great - it's the kind of place that the staff remember your name and know the local area in depth, and the owner is on hand for a chat.
The location was convenient for the airports and driving to town, so we liked it, but do be aware that you will need a car to get in and out, unlike a city-center base. As someone else pointed out, there are a few (pg-rated) signs for gentlemen's clubs along the highway, but as it is a drive-only area, this had no impact at all on our stay, and I would absolutely be happy to have my family here. 
Overall, we greatly enjoyed our stay, and would certainly recommend it!

title: “Nice stay but...”
text:
My wife and I stayed here one night while attending a wedding and although we enjoyed our stay I was surprised at how quickly the extra fees and taxes added up. Let me start by talking about the positive points. The front lobby was very open, modern and inviting. We stayed in a corner room on the 5th floor... it was clean, spacious and had a nice view of the downtown area. 
The service people we dealt with were all helpful and professional. No question about it...it was a very enjoyable stay.
 Here's my complaint/concern...we paid $179 for our room which I thought was fair for the market. What I wasn't anticipating was $26 for parking, $12.50 for Internet use in our room (in all fairness it is free in the lobby) and three different room taxes that made the actual cost of the room another $50 more. I usually do a better job of researching that sort of thing so I was a bit surprised. Another TA poster had mentioned free parking in "room tips"..that has obviously changed. The additional costs certainly diminished the value of the original price of the room.

title: “Sanctuary - The Name Says it All.”
text:
From Magda in reservations, to Mr. Schwartz our concierge, to Rudy & Olga behind the bar, & Vivienne at the front desk, Sanctuary was just that, a place to get away, relax, & enjoy. 
Cheers,
 - Sebastian.

title: “Excellent choice for Boston”
text: We stayed here for the Boston Marathon 2012 and I have to say it was perfect for us. I hate to be hostage to the usual inflated prices of breakfast or a cup of tea at hotel, internet charges etc. I like to be able to make my own and given that we were there for the marathon we had specific dietary and timetable requirements so having the little kitchen was a must. The room was very nicely decorated and adequately sized. The bathroom had a great shower and the bed wasn't bad. Plenty of towels. The location is wonderful-easy walking distance to the park, restaurants shopping, a gym ( the hotel one is tiny) and its relatively quiet. I would recommend the 4th floor rooms (we were in 301 which btw doesn't smell of cigarette smoke anymore!) because the sound carries from the room above and Im a nervous wreck the night before a Marathon :) Staff were delightful and extremely helpful. They could improve it with better pillows and more TV channels but a minor complaint. Definitely recommend and will stay again. Thank you Boston!

title: “We expected more from a Courtyard by Marriott and we got it”
text:
We have stayed in many Courtyard by Marriott hotels around the world. We generally like them because of their upscale look, highly consistent good level of service and attention to details. This hotel even though a bit dated, met our expectations and therefore is one that we would recommend to our family and friends. It only needs a little more updating ( elevators, carpets, hallways, etc. ). The staff at the reception desk were great. 
This hotel is very good. Not excellent but very good.

title: “The best spa retreat ever!”
text:
This was my eighth trip to Lake Austin spa and it never disappoints. I have tons of tips and tricks to share as well. :)
Definitely go during the week, as the spa gets busiest on the weekends if possible. You will want to book your spa appointments if you have specific ones, way before you get there to get the best times. Especially if you like a massage before bedtime. If you aren't sure, don't stress it, as my last visit I didn't book a thing before I got there, and I was fine booking them on day 2 of my trip.
I would recommend a facial with Carole Cole as she is AMAZING and if you like extractions, she can do the job. She is very skilled and I am extremely picky on facials. My group also said Erin is amazing and does a fabulous job as well.
Go have your makeup done with Kiah S in the lakehouse spa shop as she does a great job and will help you with all the products there. 
I can't believe I have gone there for 8 years and never tried the acupuncture. Big mistake! I thought I didn't need it because nothing was really wrong with me, but now I am totally sold. You must see Aaron and he does get pretty booked up. I had a headache from sitting in the sun at the pool and he got rid of it in a few minutes--it was crazy cool.
I would recommend the Texas Starry Nights to be booked before bedtime if you are an overnight guest. You can get a 9pm and it is perfect before you fall asleep. 
Personally I love the Lakehouse Lavender scrub and I loved the Seaweed scrub as I am not big on massages. 
I would also recommend the full pumpkin body wrap. It smells like you are baking pumpkin pie. It does get warm and a little "insulated" if you don't like that sensation. Your skin will thank you and you also get a long massage with it.
If you want a killer hair cut, you have to get the little lady from Paris to do your hair. I am sorry I forgot her name but it is like Elsie or something and she is probably in her 60's and has been there a long time. She is outstanding. She gets booked up so make your appointment right away.
I was not impressed with the pedicure I had, but that was 2 years ago. So I skip that as there are too many other cool things they offer and so little time. :)
Tips for the spa:
*Go an hour early if you are an overnight guest. You will want to relax in the hot tub, sit in the sauna, and chill out in the steam room. I also love the hot tea they have and it is so relaxing to sip some tea beforehand.
*Shower at the spa--they have amazing shower gel, lotion, and even shaving cream. You can leave your razor at home as they provide really good disposable ones.
*Everything you need to get ready is in there...hair spray, blow dryers, mouthwash, even tampons. 
*If you are modest you can wear a bathing suit in the hot tub. They have this little spin dryer for your suit right by the extra towels in the hot tub area.
*You can exchange your robe every day for a fresh one if you want! (I can't believe I didn't know this fact)
*And if it is cold, they even have THICKER robes--just ask for one at the robe desk right before you go into the locker rooms.
*Eat lunch at the Aster Cafe which is up at the spa. It has a different menu than the downstairs eating area and it is delicious.
*There is sunscreen in a huge pump dispenser (SPF 15) at the pool so don't worry if you didn't bring any.
FOOD
The food is amazing and will take a little bit for you to get used to, if you don't normally eat pretty healthy. I travel with a mixed group of girls so I see both sides to it. :) Your system is going to be de-toxed from all the healthy eating. The portions are small compared to normal restaurants but feel free to order two meals at a sitting. Nobody will bat an eye at you I promise. I do it all the time. 
They have a new French chef (instead of the Southwestern style they used to have) and he is AMAZING. Hello to the goat cheese, beet, and fig pizza. (You must try this) Yes I hate beets and figs but when they are baked, they get all sugary and taste like candy. Best pizza ever. I also had the corn soup every single night for dinner which has fresh avocado in it. I hate avocado and was eating it! Everything tastes so delicious. I normally don't even like tomatoes but these were heirloom, fresh, and out of this world. Just try everything is my best bit of advice.
You can order room service any time you want. You can get the regular dinner menu from downstairs for the room service (even though you don't see that menu--I got one from the dining room the first night from Hal and he told me to keep it up there all week long--he rocks) so don't think you are stuck with just the limited menu in your room. They also have wine for sale and it was really good. (I would recommend you bring your own though it is cheaper if you are drinking it in your room only.)
Always order all the desserts. There are three a night. Trust me I know. LOL It is bad when you like all three of the night and try and eat them all. So say you were warned. Yes they are low fat, but most of them you won't know it. 
They do have gluten-free dining there. They also will custom make whatever you want. We had one in our group who was gluten-free and also dairy-free. The chef made her special meals and a special dessert even. You just need to let them know in advance so they can do it for you. 
Try the tarot card reading with Paul. It is an extra fee but so worth it. I have done lots of readings over the years in different places, and I am very picky. I was pretty skeptical but each person in my group raved over their reading. I got a 50 minute one, and was thrilled. Bring a notebook to write down all the answers and bring every question you can think of. It is THAT specific.
FITNESS CLASSES
They have lots of classes and lots of levels of classes. Try something new. I have never been disappointed in any of the classes. The teachers are all outstanding. 
CLASSES
They also have speakers come in, have cooking classes, astronomy classes and aromatherapy classes for example. Each week it is different but again we have never had a bad time at one. 
You will definitely want to sign up for the free boat cruise. It is scenic and we always enjoy the trip. I am sorry I forgot the name of our female boat captain but she has been there a long time and knows some amazing Texas trivia. It is FUN. You can sit in the shady side on the back if you don't want the sun. She also does it when it is cold and provides blankets and hot chocolate so don't miss it no matter the weather.
Also make sure you kayak a little bit and take a nap in a hammock.
There are cats roaming around that live there and all have been there a long time, have names and are well loved there. I believe "Ben" the calico is the most famous spa cat according to one of the front desk staff members. He hangs at the downstairs pool. None of the cats will bother you so if you don't like cats, don't worry at all. And there are only like 5 of them that I saw there and I think their main job is to relax at the spa as well. 
Your room will be totally comfortable. We love the beds, the nightly turn down service, and the lavender spa toiletries they provide. Make sure you ask for a room with a porch as I do love to sit on the porch and relax. You will want to light the candle out there as mosquitoes do occur at certain times of the year. We have asked the front desk for extras of those when we wanted to hang out on the porch for an extended amount of time.
Don't bother with clothing or makeup. Everyone walks around in a robe. They eat meals in a robe. All you need is your workout clothing and your bathing suit. Other than that, forget it. They even give you flip flops that you can keep. 
More tips:
*Sign up in advance for their monarch program and they will give you a cool tote bag when you check in
*They serve a light appetizer every day at I think 3pm in the room across from the check in
*Get frozen yogurt in a to-go cup any time of day by ringing the doorbell to the kitchen (right next to the coffee machine). Give them one of the BIG paper cups if you are like me and want a lot. Also it tastes better when you swirl the two flavors of the day. 
*Another frozen yogurt tip....go to the Aster cafe at lunch time and they have DIFFERENT flavors of the day than downstairs. We love this treat when we are laying out at the pool up top on a hot Texas day.
*Beat your roommate back to the room after turn down service and steal the card on her pillow for yours if hers is better. LOL (They leave cool little cards on your pillow)
*This is really a GIRLY place and very very few guys ever go. I think it is cool if they do, but most guys when they get there always say they feel a little weird being the only guy there. I would definitely not go there with my boyfriend as it is such a great girls' getaway trip. It is the perfect sister trip, mom/daughter trip, or best friends' trip. I wouldn't recommend it for couples at all.
*Try the green iced tea. It is like no green tea you have ever had and I can't seem to duplicate it at home whatsoever. It is very unique and I look forward to it every year. 
*They don't offer soda/cokes but you can buy them at the restaurant for $2 if you are dying for one. I think you should do the de-tox for the week. :)
*They have the best lip balm there for $5 and it has spf 15 in it. Get some and see for yourself.
*They used to sell better lavender candles there and I don't care for their new "natural" formula as well as the old ones. (In case you loved them in the past and wanted to order some more online from them...they have a new formula and it is not the same. This also goes for their whole lavender line of shampoo and etc.)
*Sign up for the lunch to go (for free) the night before you leave and you have a yummy sandwich and apple for the plane ride home. It's like my last slice of heaven before I leave. My friend is gluten-free and they made her a gluten-free version.
*Tips are included in the spa services
*I still tip the maid daily of course, and the owner of my company always gives the servers an envelope of $ from all of us before she leaves.
*They have umbrellas in all the rooms in case it rains.
*Just ask at the front desk if you need anything at all--they will bend over backwards to help you.
Love this place and can't wait to go back!

title: “Noise!”
text:
Had high expectations of this hotel in Wrigleyville but was very let down. The main reason appears to be the room I was assigned, right next to the booming beats of the music/games store next door. The music was loud, and I mean REALLY loud, for most of the three days I was there. It only really affected me on the first day as I wanted to sleep after a long flight, and I was offered a room change on the second morning, but didn't take it as I knew I was going to be in much later on the other nights.
Sadly, I then fell ill on the final night and had to stay in the room, with my head banging from the sounds from next door. This continued until well after midnight and I didn't sleep at all before leaving very early in the morning still under the weather.
I was unable to hear the music from the corridor on the second floor so would assume it was better on the other side of the hotel - just my bad luck to end up in one of the bad rooms. The room itself was huge, comfortable and well appointed...just let down by noisy neighbours. I like Wrigleyville as well, close to plenty of entertainment and almost right next door to Belmont Station, 20 minutes to downtown with very regular trains (which ironically I couldn't hear at all!) Breakfast basic but helpful.
Probably would stay here again but would double check my room first.

title: “Great location, good breakfast included”
text: Our room was quiet (at the back of the hotel) despite being close to Times square and the staff could not have been friendlier. We were also able to leave luggage with them for a whole day after we checked out which was helpful. There are definitely cheaper options but this was a good compromise between price and location.

title: “Great Everything!!!!!”
text: Stayed here one night. We had a great room, great service and paid a great price through priceline. Bed was comfortable but was queen size and only bed in room. Make sure you ask for king bed if that is what you are used to. Had great service at check-in. Quick and friendly valet(expensive $23) but had received such a great rate that we could not complain. Chatted with various staff (while riding elevator) asking us if we were enjoying ourselves and San Diego. All were friendly and professional. Pool small but lounge beds wonderful (if you can snag one). Would highly recommend. Decor is contemporary, art deco and tasteful.

title: “Visit Family”
text: Clearly upbeat New York place, out door deck and disco was hoppin

title: “Very Nice and Economical”
text: A very nice hotel. My wife and I have stayed at numerous hotels in Chicago. This hotel was particularly nice in that it was close to "The Mile" and very close to other boutique shops, quaint restaurants and other attractions. Most places in Chicago from the hotel are within walking distance. When someone wants to visit Chicago I feel they should stay close to Intersections of Rush and Ontario Erie Superior. Those areas will be great for first timers because there close to the restaurants and the downtown tourist attractions. If you want to visit Millenium park, old town, museum campus and Soldier field I would stay on the other side of the river. Its a matter of personal preference. The James was very nice for what My wife and I wanted. Had a decent bar area and a nice looking restaurant. Although I can not say anything about the food as I did not eat there. The bellmen and the concierge are very nice and extremely helpful in navigating the city. The concierge was particularly helpful for me on decidng where to eat and what attractions to see. Would definitely stay there again.

title: “Nice, convenient, green building, great service”
text: Spent a very nice night here. Was in town for a conference and found the Intercontinental to be a great place to stay. The room was comfortable and well-appointed, the location was very convenient to hip bars and restaurants in SOMA neighborhood, and I was very impressed that such a large chain hotel is LEED certified. Great service, great lobby and common areas.

title: “Great, affordable, family-friendly resort!”
text:
Wow - where to begin...
I lived in the Phoenix area in the 1990's. My family hasn't returned there - together - in over 10 years. Boy, have things changed!
My husband and I were searching for an affordable place, close to the city, that was "family friendly (we have a six-year-old son)." After researching private rentals, resorts (including the AZ Grand)....for what seemed to be an eternity....we found the Legacy. At first glance, I was concerned about how "family friendly" a golf resort would be, and I remember this area wasn't the best years ago...I searched and searched online and couldn't really find any "totally bad" reviews about this place - some people mentioned noise issues....some comments about rude staff....and the other biggie were complaints from singles or seniors about all the kids around the pool, resort, etc.. - THOSE reviews SOLD THE PLACE for us! I wanted a rental where our entire family could feel comfortable - including our child. He's not some out-of-control nutcase - but he does like to jump and swim in pools...and, sometimes, he can get excitedly loud....so I wasn't interested in staying somewhere that frowned upon children. After looking at hundreds of photos online (yes - the pool IS that awesome), video's, etc., we booked a one-bedroom suite.
When we arrived, it was apparent the area had changed A LOT in a decade. The grounds and area surrounding the resort were beautiful and well-manicured! My allergies were actually going nuts from all the flowers and trees around the grounds.
From the get-go, we were greeted by nothing but friendly, helpful staff. The concierge hit us with the "time share" pitch once - which we declined...and we weren't bothered with it again. Our request for a second floor unit was honored and we were located in Casita 6 - which was a bit away from the main check-in area and pool. I kind of liked that - honestly, the units close to the pool seemed too "busy." If you are interested in solitude, I definitely wouldn't recommend staying in them (and they are more expensive). The pool opens at 7 a.m....complete with music and lots of boisterous, festive sun bathers. Casita 6 was the farthest from the main area....and it still was only about a five minute walk up to the pool and main, common areas.
THE CONDO LAYOUT: Just an FYI - each building seems to house four one-bedroom units (two upstairs, two downstairs) and four jr. suites. If you rent a one-bedroom, your unit will be on either end of the building - sharing only one common wall (if you are on the bottom, you share the ceiling, too). The jr. suites are wedged in the middle....hence, if you get one of the jr's - especially on the lower floor - I could see how they could be rather noisy (all walls, except for the floor, are shared). SO, if you want a quieter experience?? Rent the one-bedroom, upstairs....or, at the very least, request a jr. on the top floor!
