Oh, and building 12 is the only "smoking" building - something to keep in mind if you smoke OR are allergic to smoke...
The one-bedroom was beyond perfect! Over 800 sq. feet with a patio, full kitchen, dining room table, washer/dryer, stall shower AND HUGE Jacuzzi tub. Everything was neat and clean. The fold out couch accommodated our son perfectly....and the king-size bed in the bedroom was gigantic. We had some issue's with the Wi-Fi - the front staff was responsive and helpful...but I don't think the problem was on their end. I would recommend bringing a LAN cable to wire into the internet. Our room had one in it.
Housekeeping came every day - including Easter! We called a couple times for extra towels and tp - the response was beyond speedy.
Although I am not a golfer, the course looked gorgeous! They really take care in landscaping this place. The pool was the best I've seen at a resort...maybe ever (and I actually enjoyed hanging out there all day - anyone out there with kids knows what I'm talkin' about....you get tired of spending hours are the same-old, dull, square-tangular hotel pools...and the kids always wanna hit the pool). In addition to the main pool you see in the photos, there was a small, circular "child" pool (only 1.5 ft. deep)....it was about the size of a Jacuzzi. 
Speaking of Jacuzzi’s - they have two: one for everyone and one for adults only (in a separate, quiet area). Pool also features a giant-sized chess set, ping-pong table, bar and grill area, towel service an lots of seating.
FOR THOSE CONSIDERING THE AZ GRAND: About mid-week, we got word from the Legacy that the pool would be closed one day for maintenance. Of course, we were disappointed...however, the Legacy worked out an arrangement with the nearby AZ Grand Resort; guests could use their pool for the day. I was actually happy about this as we looked at the Grand as a possible place to stay (we were intrigued by the water park and reviews...however, the price was a bit out of our range and the room looked small....so we went with the Legacy). 
We showed up at the Sedona pool at the Grand....and we COULDN'T BELIEVE HOW DUMPY this place was in comparison to the Legacy!!! I was so happy I didn't shell out $$$big bucks to stay there. The Sedona pool was very small, we couldn't even find a place to sit....and outdated. We actually SNUCK INTO the Oasis water park (am I bad?) - and it reminded me of Disney World....just totally busy and hectic.....no seats....disgruntled staff....yeah, the Oasis water park looked neat - but you know what??? After an hour in the wave pool, my son found us and asked if we could go back "home" to the Legacy because he was tired of the place. 
I was shocked by the Grand - when I lived in Phoenix, it was known as the Pointe at South Mountain. If was a premier resort BACK THEN. Except for the water park - and the $$ fancier price - it still looks like The Pointe...only 20+ years older with no updates. I know they have added on in area's....but, for what they want a night?? I was less than impressed....
Let's see....what else.....
They Legacy did have daily planned activities (crafts, hikes, games) - something for everyone. We didn't have a chance to attend any, though. There is also a playground, on-site restaurant, bb-que area, shuffle board and tennis. Lots of attractions nearby (Gallagher’s has GREAT food. It's at the corner of 32nd and Baseline...travel through the Grand, up 48th St. and visit South Mountain Preserve for ALL LEVELS of desert hikes. The preserve is near the Pointe's/Grands golf course - you'd never even know it's there if you weren't looking for it....and there are miles and miles of serene trails. Another great attraction is the sunset "steak run" horseback ride through South Mountain. Even if you HATE horses, you have to try this. You saddle up and ride through the park at dusk, to a steakhouse. After dinner, you ride back through the park at night - you can't beat the views! And, the Desert Botanical Gardens and Papago Park are a must see....also, on the off chance you get a rainy day and need to go somewhere indoors with the kids, try Amazing Jakes (Google it - too much to list)). 
The only "complaint" I really had was one morning, the city of Phoenix turned off the water to our unit....which was a little inconvenient....but that's about it...and the water was back on within an hour or two.
SO, if you are a family thinking this "golf resort" won't welcome your kids??? THINK AGAIN! BOOK IT!! It's an awesome value....so much so that I'll be returning in August (for a rate less than $80 a night for a one-bedroom?!?!?! GREAT!).
IF you are a single or a senior looking for a quiet get-away?? The grounds and golf course are lovely. Just be aware that there are lots of kids staying at this place....you will be outnumbered :)
If you're looking for complete solitude and are bothered by boisterous vacation-goers - you may wanna try Sedona, Sun City or Fountain Hills....
I will never stay anywhere else - my family would kill me!

title: “Very Good Value”
text:
Bettter than expected. Nice hotel, pleasant helpful staff, very good breakfast choices. Close to Market and subway lines, moderate walk to old city area.
While the general location is convenient, the immediate 2 or 3 blocks around the hotel does not look very nice. We had no problems and felt safe enough during the day, but I can fully understand how people could feel uncomfortable, especially after dark. Probably would spend a few bucks and take a cab after hours.
Enjoyed our stay. Good value for money and would return.

title: “ABSOLUTELY ABHORENT”
text: These people at this hotel are absolutely rude and discourteous at BEST. Not to mention, the house keepers do a very poor job of cleaning the rooms because my sheets were not clean and bath towels had blond hair clinked in the towels. And I am african american so i can assure you that they weren't mine. There were also gnats and 3 dead roaches behind the nightstand. The bed felt like i was sleeping on pure springs and like it had been purchased at a 1985 motel auction. The shower heads have no HEADS whatsoever and just sprays out continous water and the water would ONLY stay hot for 5 minutes. Please dont waste your money on this establishment because rest assured, you will be very disappointed. Not only is it downright filthy the people who work their,especially a gentlemen by the name of Sam, treat you as if THEY are doing THE favor for you patronizing their business when its actually the other way around. Their customer service is downright provisional & discourteous.

title: “a wonderful experiance”
text: i stayed at the embassy suites with family for a graduation trip to the university of illonois in Champagne. We booked 3 rooms at the Embassy for a few nights and thoroughly enjoyed our trip. The Happy Hour is a brilliant idea! The rooms were in excellant condition and housekeeping kept them very tidy. The only issue we had was that when we received our luggage, one bag was missing and we were already in Champage (2 hours away) It took a few calls back and forth to get to the bottom fo the issue but the missing luggage was finally found and sent to us.

title: “Good Location, average hotel, expensive parking”
text: We stayed 3 nites in the Historic rooms at the back of the hotel. The rooms were average and clean. We had a rental car as we were going to explore Muir woods etc, however we found the parking at the hotel was over $35per nite which was more then the rental car !. The great thing about the hotel was the location. Right on Union Sq with all the shops and eating places. Great Breakfast just 2 doors from the hotel at a reasonable price.

title: “Deserves The Respect of An Aging Old Grand Dame That She Is”
text: She's wrinkled, she's lost a few inches but dresses up beautifully. This grand dame still shines even though the makeup is no longer enough to cover the flaws - surgery required. The rooms are spacious and beautiful. We weathered hurricane Sandy there and were thrilled with the high level of service we received from the veteran staff.

title: “Peaceful property...”
text: I recently stayed two nights at this property with my sister who was visiting from the midwest. She reserved our room through priceline. I was very pleased and loved the location. We were right next to a restaurant and the adult pool. It was quiet and beautifully landscaped. Our room was clean and well appointed although we got spotty cell service. We had a wonderful time and would return again if we could get the same rate we got on priceline. I know there were other guests who paid MUCH more than we did so I was very satisfied.

title: “Loved It!!! Great Place. Great Location.”
text: Stayed at the Renaissance for a 1 night getaway(8/18/06). We enjoyed it!!! Valet, check-in, housekeeping....all A+!!!! We were upgraded to a club level floor 26th to our surprise....big and spacious, great view and quiet. Called down for the car and it was there at the doorstep in 6 minutes....Awesome!!! Forgot toothpaste and it was delivered, complimentary, in 4 minutes...along with mouthwash and a toothbrush. Always called us by Mr. and Mrs. Was a bit leary going into the weekend by the previous reviews but no complaints here at all. Very busy weekend with Cubs/Cardinals, Air show and PGA in town but felt like the hotel was handling it. Besides in the lobby, didn't see many guests at all. I would stay again.

title: “Class All Way”
text: Top of the line hotel with all the amenities and great, great service. Wonderful downtown location near all the attractions and restaurants with beautiful views.

title: “good size and amenities for families”
text: a packed hotel full of families on a summer weekend in DC. Rooms are good size, with 2 queens in bedroom and an extra sink there as well, ok bathroom (no makeup mirror), and a living room with a pullout sofa, desk and second tv. Microwave and small fridge in a closet, safe, huge towels (and requested extra towels speedily provided). Helpful bellman. Decent work out room. Breakfast was pretty crazy given number of people there (20 minute prime time wait for made-to-order omelet), but large food selection. Lack of free wifi was annoying, but lots of internet kiosks in lobby. Parking is noted as "limited", and none was available when we arrived about 5 on a Saturday. They have an arrangement for self-parking at a discounted rate ($23?) at Ritz Carlton a block away (a bit annoying in hot DC, and even Ritz Carlton employees didnt know which elevators went to garage, but some DC hotels have no parking at all)! You may want to request a 2nd floor room to avoid having to wait for an elevator (interior stairs near waterfall from 2nd floor take you right to breakfast area/manager's reception area).

title: “Great hotel... avoid the parking lot next door!”
text:
The Hotel Layne is great. This is a difficult part of the city because it is so close to the business center, some great entertainment, and scary crime. The staff is family-run, and they've got a buzzer at the front door. You press the button and they peek through the window before unlocking... this actually made me feel very safe!
The rooms are small and have an (empty) minifridge, TV, iron & board, a bed, a chair, and a sink. Our floor (3rd) had a communal toilet and shower, but it was only $60 for the room so this didn't bother me. There was no alarm clock so i had to figure out the one on my cell phone.
So, this is seriously a no-frills hotel. I didn't mind because everything was very clean, the staff responsive, kind, and helpful. Free coffee in the morning, and those danishes my family likes to take camping. All in all, a great place and I'll be going back.
One final note though, and this is about the parking garage next door. The staff there is NOT helpful, especially when we found out someone THREW UP IN MY CAR!! They did clean up, for the most part... and they refunded $40 of the $45 we paid to park there. I really don't want to recap the conversations I had with the guy there at the time, I'd get too mad. This happened because they will leave a window rolled down so they can easily move double-parked cars. Someone was on their way to their car and thought mine was a toilet. I am still finding flecks of mother-of-pearl vomit with bits of hair. I want to do a DNA test and find out who this drunken culprit was.

title: “Musty Driskill Inferior Service”
text: First time visitor... As we entered the Driskill we are greeted with an unexpected whiff of sewage that permeates the long entrance and foyer. I made a brief remark when we arrived at the front desk, to make sure they had noticed the bad smell. The front desk agent, rather unconcerned, explained the smell as the result of last "week's main break." We confirmed our "deluxe vintage room" and are assured in our minds that the luxuruious room {based on online photos} for which we paid for will more than make up for this inconvenience (cost $350/night). As we start to check in with the front desk, our reservation gets mixed up with another guest with same last name, a problem which haunts us a while longer. Then we are assigned a room but find out that our request, in the online reservation and confirmed with the front desk agent for a king bedding, was overlooked; we waddle back to the front desk and we are switched to another room to accomodate us. And here it gets interesting...we find out that we had been sent to a room with at a lower category at the same price, mind you - even though the front desk agent assured us that the new room is of same category; essentially we were downgraded without our knowledge. At that point we are getting sort of miffed and we ask for a manger who initially denied that this was a downgrade. While I am on the phone with the manager to move us to a room within the category we paid for. At the same time my spouse notified me that the electronic but antiquated looking lock is not working. We ask the front office supervisor to move us after we found ourselves sitting on the couch for about a half hour watching patiently and slightly annoyed as engineering, bellmen, and security come and go to fix the problem; and then we decide to summon the manager on duty, Matthew, explained the experience and requested to be moved to different room. And we asked to be compensated for the hassle. After a long discussion, he offers us an UPGRADE, as compensation, and it turns out that the "pgraded" room is the one initally assigned to us - the room from which we were deceiptfully downgraded from, a room with broken lock and less amenities. When I confronted the manger about the deceiptful front desk practice of not disclosing a downgrade he dismissed it. He offered us another room, same category we paid for and we arrive at a, well a dungeon, a dark room, and just like the previous room, characterized by worn carpet and aged decor, it was aweful. To top it off, we also discovered that, by accident, one of the staff people had slipped us accidentally the MASTER key inse our room key packet. By now we are completely disenchanted, quietly return the master key to the individual, well knowing, if we'd report this incident to management, it would likely result in firing. Completely disgruntled and frustrated, we decided to walk to the front desk, speak to Matthew, retrieved a reluctant apology, and decided to check out without staying a single night. We have travelled for 25 years, and this is the first time we have checked out of a hotel without, well, staying. Avoid and stay away from this faux overpriced historic hotel if you want avoid dismal service and worn decor. Security was a serious concern.

title: “Fantastic Location”
text: Stayed there with my husband and 9 year old daughter. We got married while we were out there. Couldn't fault the location and would only stay there again based on that. Rooms were clean but felt the service was below standard. The bell boys and cleaners were really friendly but the reception staff sometimes weren't very much so. Got quite excited hearing about peoples free upgrades and complimentary bottles of wine for birthday etc, but we got nothing, not even a smile whilst waiting for our limo to take us to our wedding ceremony. Rest of the wedding party had to wait two hours when they checked in as their rooms weren't ready and had to wait an hour for some ice, and that only arrived after two more calls down to reception. The room manual said that children get a bubble bath of their choice and a tote bag with colouring things in but we never got either, even though we asked reception twice. As I said, we'd only stayed there again because of the location and if a good deal came up. You don't spend a lot of time in your room to be honest. On a positive - it was nice and quiet, we got some cookies in our room for 2 days in a row and the choccies were nice.

title: “very disappointed”
text: I've always stayed at this motel when I come to Graceland, and have been very satisfied. But its as changed so much since last year that I can no longer recommend it. The bathroom was very dirty,we went and got clorox bathroom cleaner and cleaned it our self.The tv couldn't pickup the Elvis channel very good. It was very fuzzy and statically. And the same movie played over and over all day long. We complained and kept getting put off. The desk clerk that worked that morning was very rued. But when we checked out we talked to Tracey and the manager (Alka Matil) and they we're very nice and apologized over and over. We did get a refund for one night which I did not expect. All and all, I still think I would stay at this motel again, because it is so close to Graceland and most of the staff are very nice.

title: “good experience here”
text: Well maintained property. Room was large and quiet. Breakfast was good quality. Staff were helpful but occasionally distracted. We bought a razor from the shop, but no-one was around to pay. Later we told the desk clerk and they added it to the bill, but that was the only hitch in an otherwise good weekend stay.

title: “Not recommended”
text: I had a bad experience at the hotel. Was awaken in the middle of the night by a man in my room. I screamed and chased him out. Upon calling the front desk, the desk clerk said he was security who was checking to see if anyone was in the room at 2AM because they wanted to check someone in to it. I've logged 100s of hotel nights and never had that happen. I couldn't sleep after the incident and tried to work, but the wi-fi didn't work. I asked the desk to have the manager meeting me at 6:30am when I check out. The desk assured me this would happen but it was a no-show. When I connected with management, it was explained that the computer system failed and showed that the room was empty. They claim they called the room a few times. I'm a light sleeper; perhaps the ringers doesn't work. I didnt hear a knock on the door either. Apparently, the security key over-rides the dead-bold which I had locked. Un-nerving. Naturally, the hotel waived the stayed which helps my company but not my lost night of sleep. It offered to put me up for free if I'm in Dallas.

title: “Great location and great value”
text: Our weekend rate in July 2010 was about $160 per night and evne though the rooms are small they are newly refurbished. The breakfast is very good and the location is incredible.

title: “Relaxing and quiet”
text: Very nice relaxing. Clean with wonderful ammenities. Common areas for relaxing and a very well outfitted fitness center.

title: “Great location!”
text: The best thing about this hotel is its location. It is close to Union Square and in walking distance to galleries, the waterfront, Nob Hill, restaurants and the shops. The hotel staff were helpful without being overbearing. The complementary apples on the front desk are a nice touch as is the lounge on the top floor. The only downside of staying at the Donatello was the hopelessly slow wireless internet connection. This aspect of staying at the hotel could impact on guests returning to the Donatello. Other than this though the Donatello is worth a look in.

title: “Best customer service and felt like home....”
text: Although I am more into the small hotels with classic interrior design, I must admite, after 2 nights at the Elysian I was very impressed. I had to think later why did I enjoyed the saty despite the fact that the interiors are not my cup of tea, I realized they had the best customer service, young, very well trained and up beat personnel. I t was cozy and warm and ate 4 times a the 2 restaurants, 3 times at Balsan and once at the fancy one. I really loved the bistro, I would go back just for a meal, it does not feel you are in a hotel, teh food was very good and it had a realy nice atmosphere.

title: “Great Value”
text: This was the first of 5 hotels over 7 nights; What a surprise! Reserved through Hotline for $38 (yes! $38 excluding taxes). Room was 'roomy'; service was pleasant; breakfast was ok nothing special; Hotel was exceptionally clean. Only concerns were 1) hotel over zealous with air freshener. When you first walk in you think, wow, they keep this place fresh but throughout stay the freshener seemed to seep through everything. I even asked the staff if it somehow was coming through the vents. 2) room bathroom (toilet and tub area) quite small. Overall though this was a pleasant place for us to crash after 12 hours driving. Bonus: shopping center across the street to walk to!

title: “Great Location/Smallish Rooms”
text:
Four friends met in NYC from across the country. My husband and I stayed at the Warwick before so I suggested it to my friends. The rooms are smallish and need a bit of refurbishing, but the location is great. 
The bar is too small and it is hard to get a seat because non-guests are there as well. It would be a god place for a glass of wine or little pizza, but there is always a wait. However, I would stay there again because of the location.

title: “Beds and showers are truly heavenly!”
text: My family recently returned from a stay at the Westin Time Square. The beds and showers were truly heavenly. The view from the top floors were great. The location was perfect. We could walk to all the theatres and shopping. The subway was down the street so it was easy to get to Central Park, Battery Park, Soho, Little Italy, etc. Our only complaint was housekeeping. One time our room was not made up when we got back at 3:00 p.m. so we had to call housekeeping and then leave for 1 1/2 hours. I did find that when we left a big tip the room was better but they always missed something.

title: “Paramount Exceeds My Expectations Again!”
text: As a returning visitor, the Paramount helped me procure a room rate that beat all others. My room needs at booking couldn't be guaranteed, but at check-in were granted. The front desk staff were exceptional, from check-in to check-out! The rooms were clean and comfortable. I have stayed here 3 years in a row and will continue to return for business, for years to come. Thank you Paramount! Keep up the great work!

title: “Between Average and Very good”
text: We stay two nights and is really nothing bad we can say. Great location, great room, great service, but even that I wasnt feeling that extra that a nice hotel makes u feel. There was always a lot of people around the lobby area, we expect a better decoration in the room but we like it.

title: “Sneaky good - Exceptional service”
text:
This one snuck up on me. I found myself more and more impressed by the Mansion. Here's why the Mansion is sneaky:
1. Its Dallas - who knew?
2. It was pouring at arrival and there was a guy there to grab my bag and hold an umbrella for me to get inside the lobby.
3. Check in was all of a minute.
4. Bellman had my bag the whole time from the point I arrived to the point I entered my room. I never touched the bag - nor did I have to ask for a bellman.
5. Complimentary car service provided by the hotel (sweet ride too).
6. Well done room. Size is right. Bathroom is up to date and well done.
7. Seating area. Plenty of room. Didn't feel like it was squeezed in there.
8. They actually followed up on things. I asked for the WSJ, and it was there on the door handle every morning. 
The rooms were decorated well, and offered the services you would expect of a fine hotel - minibar, internet, turndown, etc. They were also the right size. I don't think you can have too big of a room, but you certainly can have a room that is too small. For example, the Four Seasons in Maui is too small for the money, and perhaps the Halekulani - but the Four Seasons in Lanai is huge and the Mansions rooms are similar, but not as big as the FS Lanai. 
My only bark: The rooms need flatpanel tv's.
I didn't eat at the hotel restaurant, but I hear it is good. I had room service (breakfast) it was actually, quite tasty (breakfast taco) and arrived quickly (25 mins). There is a bar too.

title: “Perfect Stay with a great staff in a wonderful city !”
text:
We stayed at the hotel during our first time visit to NYC and we loved every minute! The room size was good especially for NYC. Great breakfast buffet and evening reception.. Free internet service, robe to use while in room (with wonderful slippers!!!) and turn down service with chocolates is a nice little extra. The park ave location is perfect in being close to the village, but just outside of the crowds and hustle.
The staff was friendly and courteous from the moment we arrived until we left. The evening reception was relaxed and comfortable, making a great place visit with friends and to un-wind after a long day in the city.
The hotel and the room we had was very and neat and clean, and overall even though hotel Giraffe is on the small side it makes up for size by being very quaint, warm and inviting making us feel like we have a second home in the NYC. Something the larger hotels can never match.
We highly recommend and are planning to stay there again

title: “Great location and very cheap but suffered from bites :(”
text: Stayed here for a week in February with family. The location is fantastic really close to times square and the staff were helpful but you have to be willing to tip well for good service. Our room did appear to be clean (a little shabby and old looking but that was to be expected with the price as it was very cheap), however I did suffer from bites more than likely from bed bugs which did spoil the experience. So if you are going to stay here be sure to cover up because the bed bugs will bite.

title: “Don't stay here if you're a wired person”
text: I've stayed here many times to cut cost as I go to conferences in NYC. You know you get what you pay for. But tonight I'm just angry as hell. I think it's bad enough to pay for internet access but understand the profiteering [-] want some money. Here is my beef and why I am totally dissing this hotel. My flight was canceled so I booked in here to wait the latest NYC blizzard. So I pay for my internet. But wait I have an iPhone and ATT is abysmal in NYC. I don't ever have problems at home but there you are. No 3G. So I call up the front desk about the internet connection I paid for and they say it's by device! WTF. I'm so angry. So let me go on about how drab and how you'd only want to stay here to pinch pennies. I stayed at the Pod Hotel for my first three nights and while this was no great shakes at least they offered free internet. I told the front desk this review was upcoming because it shows a complete lack of understanding the customers of the new millennium. Don't stay here.

title: “Convenient and”
text: My husband and I stayed here for 4 days. The bed was huge and comfy! The room was quiet and clean. WiFi is free. Desk staff were friendly and helpful. The hotel is in a great location to the Space Needle and the monorail. We walked downtown every morning, and took the monorail back every afternoon. Parking is connected to the hotel, which made it easy to come and go after hours. Cheap parking ($12 compared to $25 for downtown rates) is a plus! QFC is open 24 hours and is within a block from the hotel, so it was easy to grab breakfast and snacks. Citizen, a kick-butt coffeehouse, is also within a block away.

title: “Excellent service, hotel revamp made it much more contemporary. Great fitness center and room service.”
text: The italian restaurant Via Mazza around the corner is very good and Exhale Spa (next door) is great for yoga and core classes.

title: “Simply excellent”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for my three day two night visit in San Francisco. It's great! Especially the location. It's close to everything. And what's more, the hotel is clean and the staff are friendly. 
If you want to explore the city, Cova is the one to stay. I highly recommend it!

title: “Holiday Inn Hotel& Suites-Wolfchase Galleria”
text: thoroughly enjoyed my stay here the service by the staff was excellent especially Kim and Olivia who went out of their way to make our stay a great one. Lots of places to eat and shop in the immediate area. The hotel was extremely well maintained. Only complained was the internet connection was slow at times.

title: “Very clean an priced right.”
text: Very good price Rooms were very clean and bed was comfortable. Close to michigan avenue (magnificent mile shops and restaurants). Would definitely stay here again.

title: “Impressive”
text:
Enjoyed the Courtyard very much. Very clean. Friendly and willing staff.
Was close to everything in Boston. Restaurants and shops down the road.

title: “Great Place to stay with your dog!”
text:
We stayed 3 nights in Nov. at the Ocean Villa Inn in San Diego. It's a great place to stay with your dog! The lower motel rooms have tile floors, ample space for a large crate and a patio which connects to a common dog run. They also have a dog wash area, laundry facilities, microwave, small refrig. and continental breakfast. The beds were okay, and the room was clean. It's only a short walk to Dog Beach and across the bay from Sea World. (Sea World has 3x7 kennel runs for $5/day-bring your own bowl & kennel mat). 
 On the down side, the room did not have enough lighting (only 2 lamps), the toilet ran and the ceiling fan was quite noisy.
 Great place for dogs & their owners, but place needs a little maintance/upgrades for the humans. We would stay here again, just because it's well set up for dogs.

title: “Beautiful views and wonderful service!”
text: We are from Houston and had been craving a weekend getaway. We chose Four Seasons because we were sure to have a pleasant stay. We certainly were not dissappointed. We had dinner on the patio and walked around the lake that is nearby. The staff was so pleasant and accomodating. Anytime we are looking for an escape I would choose the Four Seasons Austin for an easy and relaxing time.

title: “Great hotel, clean, good location, free breakfast, airport/cruiseport shuttle!”
text:
This Holiday Inn Express property is directly across the street from the historic EL CORTEZ Hotel, and is the former hotel annex & banquent rooms of the El Cortez so the rooms are historic, but remodeled and CLEAN! Midge & Zuyla at the front desk were FANTASTIC at checkin and during our entire stay! Jose, maintenance engineer had to play shuttle van driver for entire hotel and the Rodeway Inn across the street. Jose was so cheerful, efficient, PATIENT, and helpful with van service to airport and nearby restaurants. This Holiday Inn Express has free shuttle service to the San Diego Cruise Port, which made me choose to stay at this property over nearby Hilton hotels, even though I am a Hilton HHonors Gold member. I am now a proud Priority Club Gold member convert and am treated with care & respect by Priority Club (take notice Hilton HHonors). Thanks for a great stay!
Great mexican food dive tip: POKEZ Mexican Diner on the corner of Tenth Ave & 'E' Street. A real dive, scruffy, grungy, yet friendly atmosphere and staff, but the food is FANTASTIC and cheap! Try the Unsual, Usual "Joey Special", a HUGE plate of delicious green tomatillo marinated boneless chicken, rice, beans, veggies, smothered in green sauce and melted cheese! Steaming side of fresh, hot flour tortillas. Comp chips & salsa, only a buck for seconds. Soda is only a buck, no alcohol. Cash, Visa/MC. We are going back to both!

title: “Great hotel, Staff”
text: This was a great hotel from the friendly desk staff to the helpful houskeeping everyone made my family feel welcomed. Jerry at the front desk was a stand out his helpful ness in securing a crib and high floor room was appreciated. The interior was beautiful with a waterfall that my 22 month old just loved. I have stayed at several hotels in the area and even thought this is not centrally located it is by far the best in service and quality. great job Embassy Suites!

title: “Good place, GREAT place”
text: We can't say enough about this wonderful hotel. Rates are well below average for the area (including cost of parking). We got a last minute deal and stayed in a corner room that was immaculate. Beds wonderful, bath luxurious and sparkling. View fabulous. Casual, but very, very nice here...a $85 million renovation helped. We took a nice walk over to to 9th Avenue where there are many reasonably priced restaurants, we had a beautiful diner breakfast for 10 people and infant at a place right on Times Square. We went to Times Sq. at midnight on a Friday - what a fun spectacle. Free entertainment. hotel about 1 block north of those red neon steps.

title: “Fine, If You are NOT High Maintenance...”
text:
...and you know who you are! I was attracted by the "idea" of this hotel. We recycle, and the free loaner bikes appealed as well. I assumed the hotel would be sort of a green/no frills place, so clearly not high maintenance people, it was fine for the price. We did not find bins for recycling, or separating trash. Room was clean, fresh towels, even when we hung them up in the "universal sign" that we were willing to use again. Not complaining, just not really "green". 
The photos online are a bit deceptive, the lobby is MUCH smaller than it appears, but the room we had was much LARGER than we expected. (Interior room, only noise was across the open court). It was our first time in SF, and we were not prepared for the homeless situation in the city, and near the hotel, even though we had heard, and read about it beforehand. Our take: worse than NYC, DC, Being aware of our surroundings, and taking a cab at night (pretty cheap, city is not that big) made us feel more comfortable. Daytime walking to the bus/streetcar not a problem, just be aware. Our rate was over $110, a fair price, if you want BETTER than a Good Hotel, you need to pay a lot more! The bed was comfortable for me, (firm) slept soundly, which is not my norm! No AC, but not needed in September, open window on higher , interior floors was plenty safe and cool. The hotel across the street is a "sister hotel" and they have a restaurant we went to for breakfast and one burger night. Really tasty food, well priced. 
The decor is fun, young, trendy, yet the mix of guests was really a mix of ages, maybe just looking for a good deal. The staff, which we encountered, (4 different people) were all very helpful, friendly, and knowledgeable. Handled large group check in, very quickly as we waited for some info.

title: “Very pleasantly surprised”
text:
We used this as a weekend trip between Boston and Orlando. It was slightly further than we thought from the metro but it was a flat walk and relatively easy with four cases.
On arriving at the hotel, it was busy but there was no delay in getting booked in. We were on the top floor and the size of the room really surprised us. The lounge was big, kitchen adequate for a short stay and the bedroom lovely and big. We couldn't believe how quiet the room was considering the traffic outside and the fact the hotel was full. This was helped by good planning in putting the bedroom as far away from the corridor as possible. The staff were extremely helpful. The location is good for getting away from the centre of town but close enough to the main sites, particularly by metro. All in all a really good stay.

title: “Great place to stay in the heart of the city”
text: Came to town on a business trip and didn't want to stay in the big chains. So glad I didn't. This little hotel has all the charm of the French Countryside, complete with the hand-written receipt. Left the window open at night and enjoyed the ding ding of the trolley, and blissfully slept in for the morning. Everyone I ran into was friendly. Would totally recommend it to anyone.

title: “So Helpful and reasonable rates.”
text:
I had stayed at the Chelsea Motor Inn before and liked it so I knew the Coventry would be great as well. It did not disappoint. The staff was so friendly and very helpful with directions. Our room was clean and located on the back hall so as to be quiet.
The next morning the desk clerk gave us a tip on how best to get to Yosemite and we appreciated that. Also, the free parking.

title: “Awful. Awful. Awful.”
text: This place is, without a doubt, the worst hotel in which I've ever stayed. I travel frequently for work (a non-profit at that), and I've never seen such filth. The room is roughly the size of a standard jail cell, the hot water takes 15 minutes to come out of the shower, the heater has only one setting (SAHARA DESERT) and is entirely stifling, workspace is crammed, and a whole host of other issues. The cable on the TV (that only consists of 30 channels - two of which are 'hotel information', three of which are the same TBS channel, and several that are mislabeled - has already gone out twice, and I've only been here for two hours. Absolutely awful place. Rude front desk associates that seem to not want to be bothered with 'issues'. Avoid at all costs. Definitely not worth $155/nt and Priceline totally got it wrong by rating it three stars.

title: “great location and staff, I would stay again”
text: From doorman to housekeeping, everyone was friendly and helpful. The room was well supplied, even with umbrella and flashlight. We were there during Hurricane Sandy, and staff stayed in the hotel so service was continued. There was a complimentary wine and cheese on a couple of afternoons. The metro is just a block away on Broadway, and the hotel is located mid way up Central park, close to the Natural History museum. After the storm we walked to TIme's Square,(there was no metro after the hurricane), it took an hour. Easy walking to to Lincoln centre. Revolving shower head with great water pressure, nice tub and bubble bath. Fluffy towels, and comfortable beds/pillows. No excess street noise noted, but traffic was reduced. The neighborhood has a variety of local restaurants.

title: “Nice Modern Hotel”
text: We stayed at the Palomar while attending the flower show. We arrived around noon and checked into our room right away. The front desk and all staff are very polite, helpful, and professional. The hotel decor is tastefully done with a modern look, but cozy feel. The morning coffee in the living room is very good (I am picky about coffee). We did not eat in the restaurant because the menu was a little strange. You may want to check it out before making reservations. The room was small but comfortable. The bed was cozy and I would have slept through the night except for the garbage dumpsters on the side of the building being emptied at 5am. The Palomar is in a good location. Near shopping and places to eat. Also within walking distance from the convention center.

title: “Wonderful location and hospitality”
text: Like most Kimpton's, the hospitality was first rate - especially at the wine hour. In the case of the Chicago Monaco, the location was also first rate. Very centrally located. We had a river view room that included a window bench that offered a great place to stretch out and read while viewing the river.

title: “Scammed”
text:
I was traveling from NY to LA with my boss and his girlfriend. We had been traveling all day non-stop when we finally pulled over at the first hotel we saw. At around 1 am we got a room went to sleep. At around 8 am we left. When I went home to visit I looked at my mail and found a letter from the holel stating that an iron and ironing board was missing and they were charging me $48.00. Thinking it was a mistake I called up and was told that the items were missing therefore they charged me. When I explained that I had never seen an iron or ironing board and had only slept there for about 8 hours, I was told that the housekeeping checks all rooms after customers leave and that they were in there before I rented the room. I again stated that I did not take the items and asked if he was calling me a liar. He stated that it was found missing by the housekeeping. 
Not only was I charged for something that I did not take but I was called a liar. The hotel is not very clean nor is it in a safe area. There were mattresses leaning on the sides of the building. Beware of this place, next time it could be you and it could be the tv they charge you for.

title: “Yotel became the highlight!”
text: I stayed 5 nights at the Yotel April 12-16. I was currently on vacation with one of my friends. We came mostly for the NY Imats show, but our hotel experience turned out to quite pleasing. So much that some days we would get out of bed late just because we enjoyed the room so much. I really had no problem with the size of the room. So comfortable, the ipod jack in the wall.... omg we had our own party in there.Not to mention some of the nights there we did not even need to leave our hotel to party because we were already at the place to be. They even made sure no one made it on the floors where the rooms were located. VIP treatment!There was a galley on every floor where there was ice water and other beverages available. Free muffins and coffee and tea for breakfast. The crew was so helpful and polite. Not once did I enter and exit with out someone addressing me. Over all I enjoyed my stay and will be back at the end of this year for my next vaction. Keep up the good work Yotel!

title: “Not really worth it”
text:
Paying for internet irks me. $12 for the priviledge of logging on in the privacy of your own room seems ridiculous in 2012. Internet access is free in the lobby which explains the constant overload of people hanging out there.
I don't mind paying for parking (well no, that's a lie) but $48 per night is extreme. That tops what I've paid in every other major city. What's more, the garage is pretty gross. Sort of half broom closet/maintenance storage area and half garage. I didn't feel safe in there, didn't feel comfortable leaving my car there, and found it pretty tight to maneuver in. Next time in D.C. I will park at nearby Union Station which charges $22 for 24 hours.
The room itself was fine. Quite large, very clean and fresh smelling, comfy gigantic bed and nice pillows. The walls must be pretty thin as I heard a baby crying for awhile along with sirens outside throughout the night. It happens. Nice bathroom, good shower pressure and great towels. Nothing extravagant, but clean and nice. Not sure it deserves a 4* rating though.
The location can't be beat and the city is awesome. Great for walking, tons to see within walking distance, lots of museums, restaurants and theatres nearby.
At check out, I was served by a man who struggled with understanding even the most basic English. I will probably look for a different hotel next time.

title: “Excellent hotel at a reasonable price in a perfect location”
text: One of the best Hilton brand hotels I've stayed at (I'm a Diamond member and have seen many). Clean, comfortable, reasonably large rooms, particularly for Manhattan, ideal mid-town location, great staff, reasonably priced, impressively fast internet (and elevators). I will definitely stay here again.

title: “Great hotel and superb location - will visit again”
text:
Our friends chose this hotel after a lot of web research - there were some mixed reviews, but we were all delighted with our rooms, the service and the breakfast. The location is fantastic, close to all the main attractions. The staff were great at reception, the concierge and in the restaurant - the only criticism was with the bar staff - mind you there were busy the night we used the bar (but knowing some basic drinks and passing something else off was poor as was the replacement drink - hey but I guess it could be our British accent).
There is free wifi in the lobby area and two free computers - so well sorted for keeping 'connected'

title: “Very convenient”
text: Stayed here for 2 nights on my way to LA from London. Very enjoyable stay . Location is ideal and service top. I recommend

title: “Right in the middle of everything.”
text: We stayed here mainly for the location and we were not disappointed. A short five minute walk to Times Square. Another short walk to our Broadway show. A shorter walk to subway stations everywhere so everything in New York is within minutes. Take a minute to study the subway maps and you can go anywhere you want. The rooms were more spacious than we expected for NYC, even for the four of us. The A/C was working fine, the bathroom was clean, the beds were very comfortable, and the room was very quiet even being so close to the action. The elevators are somewhat small and they tend to get full easily. You can use the one at the end of the hall; that one is usually empty. The business suite has everything you need to check mail, print boarding passes, etc. The buffet breakfast is very good but somewhat pricey. You can walk five minutes and get a bountiful breakfast at several places nearby. The room has a microwave oven, a small refrigerator, and a coffee maker. The safe was huge by hotel room safe standards. Three iPads and a laptop fitted easily, with room to spare. The best place to buy groceries is just around the corner at the Food Emporium on 8th and 49. Street food is awesome. The best I had was at the Halal guys. You have to walk and there is a long line. They're that good. We will stay here on our next visit for sure.

title: “Nice hotel at great location”
text:
First of all, we were there for a conference that my husband was attending, so the hotel was chosen for us. We stayed at Hyatt Islandia in MIssion Bay. A nice location right on the bay, a marina on one side, close to Belmont Park & the beach & "boardwalk" area. 
The hotel room wasn't ready when we arrived at 3:15 so we went for a ride & some lunch/supper (it was 6:15 "our time" so we were hungry). Returned to the hotel a littel before 5 and were told the room still wasn't ready so they offered us an upgrade to a Marina Suite. While we were debating the relative merits of taking a suite, the original room became available, but the offer was still out there, so we took it! Had a bedroom w/2 queen beds, TV, a patio w/2 chairs overlooking the marina, a little wet bar area, and a living room w/TV, table, chairs & sofa/pull out bed. Decor a bit shabby, the sofa was uncomfortable to sit on to watch TV, but we were hardly in the room so it wasn't a big deal. What a kick to sit on the patio and see pelicans and a seal or two poking around the boats in the marina! They nickel & dime you to death there, however. $10 a night to self park (altho' we did have under the bldg. parking, which was great when it was raining) and $20 night for internet connection! Business travelers have come to expect WiFi at the better hotels (think Omni), not that price for a dialup connection! 
The bathroom lighting should have been better - kind of hard to put on even the little bit of makeup I use with the lighting provided! Even the connecting area where the wet bar and another counter with 3 mirrors were poorly lit. They have a "thing" they do there to save water - they say they'll only change your towels and linens every three days to conserve water (save our planet) unless you call and tell them no thanks. I certainly did call and say we wanted fresh towels daily, thank you very much. We've been on a couple of cruises where they do something similar (there's a REAL need to save water in their case), but they do it in a better way...they say if you want the towels refreshed, leave the used ones on the floor, otherwise hang them back on the rack to dry if you plan to reuse. I think that's more user-friendly than making a customer call to say they want clean towels.
All in all, I would recommend this hotel. It's a nice location, close to the beaches and the highway both, and the facilities seemed very nice. We did not use the pool, but they have a small sandy area with chaise lounges they call a "beach" for those that want some sun with no water. it's not really a beach, but you get the same effect for sunbathing. Breakfast at the Blue Bay in the hotel was good - we had the breakfast buffet which was standard hotel buffet stuff - scrambled eggs, breakfast potatoes, fruit, bacon, sausage, french toast, biscuits, gravy, syrup (I think I'm leaving something out, but can't remember what). We did not have any other meals than breakfast there (I ordered an omelet off the menu one morning, it was very good).
We tried to go to the Islandia Grille on the Thursday night around 9:30pm...hours on the door said open 'til 10:30 but all the doors were locked. We just wanted maybe an appetizer and a drink at the bar. A bartender came out and said they were closed. Hmmm...was that a management decision or just the bartender's choice??? We did enjoy a drink in the Towers Lounge a couple of evenings...comfortable chairs and loveseats to sit in and chat, and a decent sized bar if you wanted to sit there. No food (at least not that we saw). 
Front desk staff were very nice, concierge was knowledgeable and the bell captain was great for giving us directions to Petco Park (to see the Padres).

title: “Nice location”
text:
The hotel was ok, it is old, it has a nice location, it is right there in the Riverwalk. Breakfast was complete but after one or two days is boring. 
They had a Happy Hour. We thought it was going to be something nice with some music since they have a piano... But we were very disapointed. The drinks were ok, food was not interesting at all, it was more for children and family than a happy hour.
Our room was small, it was a suite with small kitchen, it had a microwave and very small coffee maker, but no cups or glasses or plates. 
Not a romantic or modern hotel.

title: “Great stay at the Grand Hyatt NYC”
text:
Positives: Friendly, helpful staff. Very clean room. Modern decor. Very comfortable beds with high quality linens, down pillows, down comforter and pillow top mattresses. Quiet. Flat screen TV with lots of channels. NY Times delivered in the morning. Great location. No wait for elevators. 
Negatives: My room was not ready for check-in until late in the evening. (However, the reception clerk offered 2 coupons for a breakfast buffet for the inconvenience). Water pressure weak. Water temperature not hot enough. Dim lighting- not bright enough for comfortable reading. Minimal amenities (no lotion, no coffee maker). 
I will definitely return to this hotel in the future.

title: “In all ways a great stay at Affinia Manhattan.”
text: We found and booked this hotel over internet and we really liked it. We spent three nights in a fresh "new" refurbished Studio Suite, 1 Queen bed and a small kitchinette. It was a bit more expensive than a standard room but it was really worth it. After hours of walking and several experiences outdoors we felt like coming home to "our apartment". Maybe it was because the style and colours were a bit Scandinavian. All service was excellent. The concierge ladies are worth special thanks. The hotel restaurant (20% off the cheque) was busy and the food was very good. The location close to Penn Station and subway is convenient. We took the train from Liberty Newark Airport and arrived very close to the hotel entrance!. We are telling our friends of this, for us, new gem.

title: “Great location and value”
text:
My husband and I stayed here two nights during the Blizzard of '09. The location is great. Within walking distance to National Mall, White House, monuments, Chinatown, and many more. We were given a room on the 8th floor looking out to the Spy Museum and the Holiday Market. Room is spacious if strangely configured. The sink is outside the bathroom, which I personally don't like. The room and the hotel were clean. My only gripe is that the room furnishings looked cheap, the closet door did not close and TV had a very limited number of free channels. Normally I would not care about the TV, but this time we had to spend moret ime in the room since it was snowing outside and the entire DC was closed. The staff frienfdy but a little slow. Could be because they had only essential staff due to the snow.
All in all, this was a great value for $98/night (AAA rate)

title: “Top of the line stay at the Elysee'”
text: My huband and I just stayed at the Elysee' to celebrate his 60th! The staff is professional and could not be any nicer. The accomodations are beautifully appointed and spotless. The coffee bar on the second floor is open all day with a wonderful staff there as well. The location is excellent for restaurants, museums or just for strolling. This is always where we stay when in the city. Kudos to a well run establishment! Teresa R.

title: “Very impressed!”
text: I stayed at this hotel for convenience sake. The seminar I was attending was being held there so that's a no brainer. I was very impressed with this hotel and it's staff. Front desk staff during check in @ 11:30pm-great. Wait staff during breakfast in the restaurant Brasserie 7:45am-excellent. Very clean hotel. Even the bathrooms (in various locations on the first floor) were clean and smelled nice!!!! The hotel is across the street from the airport. I was on the 14th floor(1402) at the end of the hallway. There is a big picture window at the end of that hall and you can see planes taking off from that view. Way cool !!! I only had breakfast in the hotel (the buffet). It was $19.95. Pricey, but not bad. I intended to eat my monies worth. The fresh fruit was delicious. Sweet. My only issue was the room was not throughly cleaned. I'm a woman and I check for these things, but that was taken care of. Really nothing to make a stink over, but enough to give a 9 out of 10.

title: “Viva Chancellor!”
text:
We are from Veracruz, Mexico, and we personally planned our visit to San Francisco, no travel agents in the middle, just the phone and Internet. My husband suggested The Chancellor Hotel as the best option. I wanted to stay at the Best Western Motor Inn Civic Center (cheaper), but after reading some reviews about its "sketchy location", we bet for The Chancellor, and everything was absolutely great! (then, we went to Civic Center and, yes, it was sketchy). At first, we were worried for some comments we found here on TriAdvisor, but every single doubt was answered via e-mail by Kevin Vossen, who gave us a special rate of 109 per nignt plus taxes. We also requested for a room with a view, and we got it: 1204. We were there from November 4th to 12th, 2006. Check-in process was made in minutes, and that was something I appreciated, especially after finding out part of our lugagge was missing. Every member of the staff was absolutely nice and helpful, even the Tour Desk lady, who receives some bad reviews from time to time... she even said "Nice jacket" to my husband, when he was wearing a colorful one ;) (Thank you!) I guess talking about Chancellor's location is not necessary, because everybody knows it's perfect! Cable cars are steps from the door, wonderful stores around, Walgreens (24-hour open) in the corner of the same block, and across the street, Lori's Diner, the most delicious restaurant we have ever found. Decorated in 50's style, fantastic milkshakes, hamburgers... all the menu is perfect, so, don't miss it!
San Francisco has a lot to offer... Our top ten (not arranged in a special order): 1.-Golden Gate Bridge (we walked it!), 2.-Japanese Tea Garden (relax!), 3.-Japantown and 4.-Chinatown (very different from each other), 5.-Alcatraz (amazing views), 6.-Lombard Street (so different), 7.-Victorian houses from Alamo Square (you will feel in a movie), 8.-Castro District (the gay and friendly neighborhood), 9.-Haight Ashbury (so hippie... Janis Joplin and Jimmie Hendrix lived there), 10.-Cable Car and Railway museums (we talked to a lady who told us cable cars from Veracruz were in San Francisco in 1982!)... Bonus.-Ghirardelli Square, where you MUST get a brownie! 
**SOMETHING VERY IMPORTANT! Don't rent a car, because you will spend so much money in parking lots. Try to get a 3-day, 5-day or 7-day MUNI pass, which are valid for cable cars, railway and city buses. We got our 7-day passes (for 24 USD each) and they were worthy. Transportation system in San Francisco is great, you will find a big map in every bus stop, so, if you make a mistake (like we did), there's nothing to worry about, you just get off the wrong bus and take the right one just by showing your pass, no extra fare!
**Just a suggestion for The Chancellor: check your website, because you can't make a reservation through it. That's what happened to us, so we tryed by e-mail and we got a positive answer from Kevin Vossen.

title: “Good hotel, reasonably located”
text:
I stayed at this hotel while attending a meeting that was occurring there. Overall, I found it to be quite comfortable. 
The beds are great! The other room furnishings are reasonable for a hotel of this category. I didn't use any of the other hotel amenities. Parking was expensive but comparable to other hotels in downtown Washington DC. I did enjoy being within a safe walking distance of a number of excellent restaurants. All of the staff were extremely polite and efficient.

title: “Birthday fun at the W”
text:
We stayed at the W Hotel for my birthday and had a very nice visit. I had read some negative reviews earlier so I contacted the hotel directly and they assured me with 2 phone conversations that they opened last summer and have now worked out the original issues.
We checked in about 3:30 pm and were given the suite I had booked 3 months earlier. We had a WOW suite (#1401) which in on the north end of the hotel so it has a fabulous view of American Airlines Center and all the large electronic boards in Victory Park. (If fact on Sunday, American Airlines Center aired the entire Stars game on the large monitor so we sat in our room eating yummy takeout from nearby Luna de Noche for brunch at the suite's dining room table and watched the game.)
The suite is over 1000 square feet and has 2 complete baths, a large room with a sectional couch that seats 6-7, a chair, a dining room table with 6 chairs and a desk with a chair. There is a very large Flat Screen TV mounted over the desk that was great for watching DVDs (bring your own) or regular TV. Two sides of this large room are floor-to-ceiling windows so the view is great. (Drapes close to make the room dark enough to feel like a movie theater.) There is a 150 square foot adjoining terrace with a couch out there. It was fun to stand on the terrace and look directly down on Victory Park and watch the people come and go from the games at American Airlines Center.
The separate bedroom is nice size with more windows (but you hear no traffic because you are so high up), a chaise lounge and another wall-mounted TV with DVD. The bed is like a Westin heavenly bed so it was very comfy. The bathtub is nothing special but was good enough. The room had the Bliss sinkside 6 which is 6 of Bliss' most famous products so that was extra nice. (In fact the suite had 1 set of 6 in each bath so I had plenty to take home for future trips.) (If you are staying at the W you are entitled to 20% off all Bliss products in the Bliss spa on the 16th floor.)
The room did have gray-blue paint on some walls and I can see how some people would find that bit dark and dull but we didn't have a problem with that due to all the great windows. The furniture is modern but still comfortable. There is a mini-refrig, a safe and 2 closets in the room too.
The only issue we had was that we had to call a couple times for the staff to pick up some trash bags that we had left outside our door after we cleaned up after a small party. Perhaps no one does that from 2 am to 8 am? We called again and they came pretty quickly. We just didn't want our neighbors complaining about trash in the hall.
Overnight Valet is $24 and it did take a bit of time to get our car out but it was Saturday night about 11:30 pm and lots of people were coming to Ghostbar (their trendy club on the 33rd floor). I mentioned that at checkout and they took it off my bill so that made the 30-35 minute wait acceptable. 
Be sure to walk around the hotel and see the BLISS spa on the 16th floor (I had a wonderful manicure there and they have a steam room, shower and quiet room), the Larry North workout room SWEAT (where we saw Dallas Cowboy quarterback Troy Aikman working out) and Ghostbar on the 33rd floor (cover is free for women and $20 for men). You really should go walk on the glass terrace that sticks out over the sidewalk where you can look straight down 33 floors. It is very cool. You can go from 8 pm to 10 pm before the crowd or later when it is busy and people-watch. There is also a very nice lounge/bar on the ground floor by the checkin desk with comfy couches and the 5 star CRAFT restaurant (from NYC) is on the lobby floor too.
We didn't try room service so we can't comment on that. (The chocolate cake sent up by the general manager for my birthday was very good so we can recommend that.) The pool was closed for temporary repairs on our visit but usually it is open and it is very unique and cool for it is on the 16th floor which is in the middle with the W building: the bottom 1/2 of the building (floors 1 to 15) is the hotel and the top 1/2 of the building is the condos (floors 17-32).
Overall, the W Dallas is a very nice place. The staff is young like the other reviewers mentioned but we found them to be very friendly and helpful. 
FYI: We brought our 2 small children and no one ever stared at us or acted unfriendly. Granted most guests are under 30 with no kids but you could bring your kids here is you wanted to.
More and more restaurants are opening in the area so it will just be easier and easier to stay down there and walk around and not need a car. House of Blues is coming soon and Dick's Last Resort, Luna de Noche and Hooters are open now. 
We recommend this hotel for a special Dallas weekend with modern accents. I live in the area and I don't know of any other hotel like this in Dallas.

title: “MUCH NICER PLACES FOR THE MONEY”
text: I booked a reservation at this hotel after reading the other positive reviews of this hotel. I seriously don't know what hotel those folks were staying at because this place was a dump!. The first problem was that there is no where to park. If you aren't lucky enough to get one of the 4 spots in front of the hotel, then you have to park in the beach parking area. The problem with this is that you have to move your car between 3 am - 6 am. Their solution was to park 2 blocks away at their sister facility. Our room was run down and in the back of the hotel- so our view was the back of a wall and a vending machine. The staff were rude. The hotel is on the board walk. However to get to the beach you have to pass the public bathrooms and then walk down 50- 60 stairs...try carrying beach chairs and umbrella down that! Basically this is just a glorified motel. We ended up leaving and found a room at Ocean Park Inn- I am sooooo glad we did this. For an $80 increase we had a beautiful room with a balcony, directly on the boardwalk/beach, fantastic location to shopping, restaurants, bars, etc. Wireless internet. Secured, under-ground parking. The staff was absolutely incredible! Ocean Park Inn has my repeat business in the bag!

title: “Reasonably priced hotel with a facade of luxury”
text:
The Club Quarters, Wacker @ Michigan is a classic downtown property that provides a budget-priced experience (for members, at least) in a convenient location. Unfortunately the hotel itself isn't fantastic and has some significant drawbacks even for business travelers. Read on for more...
LOCATION:
 The hotel is located on the southern bank of the river, less than a block off of Michigan Avenue. With easy access to the El (CTA) trains from the State terminal, and the main business district within a 2 minute walk, the hotel is perfectly situated for business or pleasure travelers, whatever your goals in downtown Chicago.
ROOMS:
 The rooms are basically postage stamps. Long and narrow, with the bathroom at one end and a single window facing the world on the other, the bed(s) fill nearly the width of the room. Each has two nightstands and a desk/workstation with a pull-out laptop desk. The TV is mounted above the work area, pointed generally at the bed. The bathroom contains a curtained shower stall, not a full tub.
AMENITIES:
 Club Quarters certainly strives to provide a sense of luxury and up-scale hospitality, but the results are half-hearted at best. Many floors offer "bottled water" complimentary in the elevator lobby -- however, their definition of "bottled water" is providing empty bottles which you can fill from a dispenser installed in the wall. All rooms have wireless internet, but it is 802.11B for the geeks out there -- which is to say rather slow. Their coverage and external Internet connection is pretty spotty as well, as even when signal is available, Internet access is terribly slow. The main lobby seems particularly afflicted. While there is an Italian restaurant attached to the hotel at street level, it stops serving at 10:00 PM. The only food options to be had in the late evening are take-out from nearby restaurants, which the hotel will charge $2.50 to deliver to your room. Unfortunately, the mid-week operating times listed in their foodservice menu seem to be out-of-date, and the two Asian style restaurants I called would not deliver at 9:30 PM, even though they were advertised to be open until 10:30 or later.
STAFF:
 The staff was generally personable, but seemed more concerned with security than guest services. The building seems to host offices on the side opposite the hotel rooms, and so lobby staff accost you for a room key or luggage check tag anytime you walk through the front door. Considering that you need a keycard to activate the elevators at all, this is a level of paranoia that seems somewhat misplaced. Nonetheless, they effectively addressed the one issue I encountered during my stay, and were generally pleasant if not overly service-oriented.
Overall, this is basically a place to sleep... Their great downtown location is by far their largest asset, and the room was clean and comfortable, even if cramped. If you're planning to not spend much time in your room, this would be a great place to base out of for a business or leisure trip. If you're planning to work from your hotel room, or need to use the hotel as more than just a shower and bed, you might want to try one of the larger chains in the area. At Club Quarters, you will definitely get exactly what you pay for... which is to say possibly enough, but definitely less than with a major Chicago hotel.

title: “Outstanding location and service”
text: Large, beautiful room, excellent service for this hotel in a prime New York City location

title: “Nicest hotel we've stayed at in NYC”
text:
We've stayed in maybe 10 different hotels in NYC over the last 3 years -- the joys of having a child in college in the city. We usually go as cheap as possible -- given that all the cash goes to pay for college.
We picked a one bedroom suite at the Dumont for this trip because with our daughter along we would have had to get two rooms at a regular hotel. So the suite was less expensive than 2 rooms at pretty much any other hotel. The place is very, very nice. We wouldn't think twice about going back when then the economics work out.
One thing to consider in the one bedroom suite -- the bathroom is entered through the bedroom. So if somebody is sleeping on the sofa bed and they want to go to the bathroom in the middle of the night, they have to go through the bedroom. This was just the slightest bit awkward for my daughter but worked out okay.
Again, I wouldn't hesitate in the future.

title: “A quieter Times Square Hotel”
text:
I travel quite frequently to New York on business and have never really found a hotel that offers exactly what I want. .To be fair I don't think I ever will. This time I thought I would try the Muse as its rates were pretty good.
When I travel I look for quiet rooms, business facilities, a good location and helpful staff. This rather cute boutique hotel offers good value for money in an excellent location ( if you are looking to be right in the middle of a tourist area), In all seriousness it is a good hotel but be warned there are NO quiet rooms. I know many have said that you can request quiet facing rooms but they don't exist. Building work is on going nearby and this is noisy. There is also a constant background generator noise in this hotel which is distracting but you get used to it after a while. The rooms are pretty good, especially if you get one on a higher floor which I did. In terms of food, I ordered breakfast in my room which was the worst room service breakfast I have ever had in New York and it cost me $38.00. I found the doormen very helpful but the staff on reception were terrible, with the exception of one lovely lady who was on duty in the afternoon when I checked in. Having said all this, if you are visiting New York for the first time and want to be in a good location this hotel beats the competition in the area. Oh and for anyone travelling on business, this hotel has no business centre. There is an internet cafe nearby.

title: “Apartment-style units are a great plus”
text: When traveling with kids you just can't beat these apartment-style units, with two separate bedrooms, a living/dining area and a full kitchen. Great location, generally quiet, very clean and comfortable. Well-trained staff as you would expect at a Marriott property. Just a couple of suggestions: replace the old residential-model toilets with commercial pressure models that don't require frequent maintenance, and upgrade the breakfast. I realize people can stock the kitchen with their own breakfast makings, but not everyone wants to do that. The choices in the lobby are mostly sugary cereals, frozen waffles, pastries and hard-boiled eggs. Even Fairfield Inn can beat that. Also, as a previous reviewer noted, there are no king beds. Overall, though, the spacious, comfortable units; the location near shopping and restaurants; and the bargain prices make this a highly recommended facility.

title: “Fab location”
text: Every time I have an early flight out of BWI I stay there. Always ask for their park and fly program rate. It is cheaper than rack rate. Even tell them if you are a Starwood Prefered member. You get good service. I have never had any problems with this location at all. I like the idea of leaving your car there and they will pick you up at the airport. Just tell them the location you are at the airport. The rooms have been re-done in the past yrs and are fabulous.

title: “What a Gem!”
text: We completely enjoyed out two-night stay here in August. The staff was incredibly accommodating and personable and the room was clean and comfortable with a lovely river view. Not the greatest location but anywhere in Boston is easily accessible. Love those warm cookies, too!

title: “Friendly Hotel, Pretty Glass”
text: This hotel is in a great location. A very quick walk to Pike's Place Market, and even downtown or the Seattle City Center. The hotel appeared to be very new, and everyone, even the visitors staying there seemed friendly. The beds were very comfortable. Our family wished that the hot tub would not have been so small as to only accomodate 4 people at a time. It was the smallest hot tub I have ever seen. I also became disturbed after my husband pointed out the mold growing around the perimeter of the bathroom and coming out of the vent in the bathroom. Everything else about the hotel was fantastic, hopefully they will deal with the mold quickly, which we did mention to the front desk. This was a nice hotel all in all.

title: “Unprofessional and a total mess”
text:
Let me preface this by saying that I am sure the hotel is fine when there is not a lot of guests there. Clearly the hotel staff was overwhelmed and not able to handle the influx of guests.
The room: was small, but nice view of "downtown" weird wetness to rugs. Don't ask
The hotel itself was connected to a business office and there are some fast food places too. No find dining really, but hey, it's indiana.
There was the 35h Annual Black expo going on, which I was not attending. The whole weekend was filled with the hallways smelling like marijuana. The nights were loud and there was no hotel security to keep the younger guests in check. It was basically, a free for all.
I sent a letter to Hyatt Corporate. The fact that illegal drug use and the free for all loud roaming of the halls at 3 and 4am makes this hotel a place I wish to never return to.

title: “Space in New York”
text:
Spent 4 nights at the Radisson for our first visit in NYC. Picked this hotel because I could get a junior suite for a good price (as advertised in an online newsletter from hotwire). This suite was essentially two rooms connected together which meant we had two full bathrooms which was very much appreciated as we were a couple with a 7 year old. He slept in the "living room" while we had the "bedroom". I ended up paying $209/night. TIP: I also signed up with the free Carlson points program which gave us FREE internet at any Radisson hotel. 
When I booked the hotel, I could get a complementary upgrade to the next level of room (if available) if I advertised on a social network that I was going to this hotel. I did that and although they didn't have any availability for a regular suite (it has a balcony), the check-in gentlemen gave us vouchers for a free breakfast at the attached restaurant. Considering that the breakfast was $20/plate, it turned out to be a good deal. Other days, we had breakfast down the street (either Lexington or 48th) at one of several delis for much cheaper. 
Our room was on the 25th floor and I was happy about that because NYC is a noisy place 24hrs/day. There were 5 elevators servicing the hotel and we never waited long to go up or down. The hotel itself was very quiet. 
The location was a bit of a walk from the tourist areas but it was well worth it to have a suite at that price. 
Overall, we

title: “Great Location, but a little pricey!”
text:
My husband and I make an annual trip to Chicago for a meeting and chose to stay at the Westin Michigan Avenue. Overall...a great location on Michigan Avenue, but that came with a few issues.
We are members of SPG and were booked on the awards floor, however our room was located directly behind the elevator and the noise of the elevator kept me awake into the night. 
The rooms themselves were the typical Westin Heavenly Bed and very nice and clean, but small. The restaurant in the lobby was nice, but a little overpriced. 
One thing I did notice was the traffic in the lobby during the day. It seemed to be a place that many of the hotel patrons camped out...maybe because the internet access was free down there. 
Overall...it was an okay experience, so this year we will be trying another hotel..

title: “Amazing Location”
text:
Started our USA road trip with 4 nights in the FS San Fran & was very happy that we did. 
Rooms are huge even by american standards and those special little FS touches are all evident.
1. Got upgraded on arrival to a corner room, not such a good view but then again I dont think many of the rooms have one.
2. If you're jetlagged & up at strange hours, there is coffee & delicious little muffins on offer down near the reservations desk. 
3. Location of the hotel is excellent, close to all the shops, esp a big shopping centre (West-something or other) that has a GREAT food hall in the basement with massive organic market - good alternative to eating in the hotel. 
4. Bellboy recommended a winery in Napa - V. Sattui - honestly if you do no other wineries make sure you visit this one. They have a great outside area where they serve barbequed bits & bobs, you can buy all the salads / drinks / desserts from their shop. Make sure to taste their award winning Rose - I'm not a wine fan but I could have drunk that bty the gallon. 
5. Have breakfast at least once in the FS, their pancakes are to die for. Plus the restaurant has a great view. 
Am going back next year for a wedding in SF and will definitely be booking the Four Seasons again.

title: “Don't waste your time or money!”
text:
Terrible Hotel! My husband,two friends and myself booked two rooms at this hotel to celebrate a birthday. Most of the promised amenities were not available. Neither room came with heat or blankets for the beds,the website promised down comforters. When I finally got maintenance to bring some bed covers,they consisted of one polyester blanket per room. No hot water kettle,coffee or tea,and the local/organic snacks consisted of Pringles and M&M's. The tub was covered in grout and the shower leaked,when you finally got it turned on. To top it all off our friends had an extra room mate, a very large cockroach! Wi Fi was down the whole time and work on unfinished rooms began at 7:30 am. New paint,carpet,fancy tv's and furniture mean nothing if the basics don't function! I would suggest management take a trip to the Bay Area and visit a real boutique hotel.
For the money you can book a much nicer room closer to or right downtown.

title: “What a find!”
text: I was in town to attend the wedding of friends. I usually stay on the East side of town, however,they had made a group reservation for out-of-towners, otherwise I never would have known about this gem. It is well located with easy access to theatres, shopping and the Tribeca area. Very clean and modern. Most of all, the staff is the most accomodating and warmest I have ever come across. They are all anxious to please, from the bellman to the front desk and beyond. There is an outdoor terrace which has a complimentary happy hour as well as coffee in the lobby in the morning. As a travel agent, I will recommend this to my clients, as well as stay there again on my next trip into New York.

title: “Nice place”
text:
Not a bad place to stay.
Loved the balconies and rooftop pool.
There was no sauna or hot tub.
Ask for a room on the front of the hotel. Better view of downtown and less noise.
You are just a few blocks away from 16th street pedestrian mall.
The hotel doesn't look like much from the outside, but the inside is nice.

title: “Your personal belongings are not safe at this Hotel.”
text: My wife had her purse stolen from the lobby bar while we were having drinks there. Area was near where employees were. Hotel says no cameras (post 911 no cameras?). Hotel GM said he could not control what happens in bar area as every walk of life comes through.
