You must keep your eyesy on your belongings every minute because Hotel can not guaranty safety oand will not stand behind it.

title: “Great Location, Great Hotel”
text: The Tuscan Inn is ideally located near Fisherman's Wharf and easy access to cable car and bus lines. The hotel staff members were very helpful and friendly. The concierge was attentive and arranged several activities, shuttles, etc for our group of 4. The rooms were well appointed and kept very clean by a a great housekeeping staff. An enjoyable addition to the stay was the evening wine reception where fellow guests and travelers could mingle and visit. I would definitely stay here again

title: “Couldn't have been happier!”
text: We checked in to Four Points because of its proximity to LAX. The hotel caters for travellers awaiting flights, and in our experience does this very well. We found our room very clean and very quiet. But the highlight for us was the flexibility it offered, and its obliging staff. We were offered a late checkout because of our late-night flight, and the hotel offered to hold our bags if we wanted to go off and do anything for the afternoon. The concierge pointed us to the trolley bus to Manhattan Beach, where we spent a relaxing afternoon and dinner, before returning to collect our bags and use the courtesy shuttle to LAX. The whole experience was a pleasant surprise, and we could not have been happier with a pleasant last day in LA, at the end of a fabulous US vacation.

title: “Great boutique experience!!”
text:
Tucked away in the heart of San Francisco's Union Square is this fantastic inn. Everything from the bathrobes to the friendly service and the wine and cheese to the great breakfast. 
It was well worth the stay in this charming and cozy inn.

title: “Free Everything!”
text:
This hotel is fantastic. I should stress that I have never stayed at a Homewood Suites before so I didn't know that they included so much in the base rate, but we were blown away. 
Among the things that this place provided for free were 'light dinner' (which could really suffice as dinner i.e. meatloaf, lasagne etc), alcoholic drinks every night we were there (Mon-Thurs), free hot breakfast, free in-room internet and a free shuttle to major sites. We were upgraded to a suite which was very roomy and had a great kitchen. It was a very nice room. 
The only negatives with the hotel were that the comforter/doona was scratchy (as a previous reviewer noted), and that the business centre broke and despite assurances of "it will be fixed in two/three hours", it never was. Everything else about this hotel was excellent. 
The location is right near downtown - it's only a 5 minute walk (maximum) to the heart of downtown Seattle, and only 10 minutes or so to Pike Place Market. We walked basically everywhere, including to the Seattle Centre, the wharf to get the Bainbridge Island Ferry, and to Pioneer Square from this hotel. We only had to get a bus when we went to Fremont.
I would definitely recommend the Homewood Suites Hilton for Seattle. What a great place!

title: “Roomy, nicely decorated and excellent location”
text:
Myself and two friends stayed in a one bedroom suite the weekend after Black Friday. I saw pictures of the renovated rooms and wasn't disappointed at all. There was more than enough space for 3 people and their luggage. It was also great that there is a refrigerator and small kitchenette in the room, with bowls, glasses and utensils. I had assumed the fridge would just be a mini-bar, as all hotels never seem to let you use the in-room fridge to chill your own drinks in there and was pleasantly surprised that it was just a normal fridge, allowing me to keep my bottles of water in there. 
Everything seemed clean and the maid service replenished our toiletries (which is good, sometimes they don't). Bed was comfy and although we didn't seem to get the pillow menu at check in, the standard pillows seemed good enough. 
The only con was the thin walls that seemed especially thin in the morning when you wake up to other people in another room talking and the fire station sounds (sirens, etc). We also got a complimentary bottle of wine from booking online and sharing on Twitter/Facebook and when we checked in, we were told it would be in the room when it was ready (we got there early). It wasn't so we followed up and were told it was coming up shortly. It didn't. It eventually came the next day so at least we got it eventually!
The location is also awesome. I usually stay closer to Times Square because no matter how late, there's still stuff to do near the hotel. There's less stuff to do at this location but it's still stellar. Right across the street from Madison Square Garden and Penn station. Easy access to the subway. 
I would definitely stay here again!

title: “A return visit that went well”
text: I've stayed at the Embassy Suites downtown several times. Overall, this is a good place to stay and with the (relatively) remodeling, the rooms have been refreshed. This time I was in a corner room. I was quite surprised how big the living room was - almost too large really. The bedroom was a big cramped with two queen beds, it would have been better with a king. It did have a small sitting room between the bedroom and the bathroom (which was quite tiny). Overall, recommended although depending on when you book it can be quite pricey relative to other hotels in downtown Indianapolis.

title: “Excellent conference facility - OUTSTANDING front end service - Disgusting in room dining”
text:
I stayed at the Hyatt Regency at Reunion for a conference this last week. Our group also held two private receptions in our suite during the trip.
To give this review proper context I need to provide a bit of history as to how I have provided ratings in the past on Trip Advisor and my travel experience in general.
If you note my other reviews you will see that high praise is well earned or I do not give it. There are too many people who rate standard and acceptable service as 5 Star / excellent. I use the “Star” rating on Trip Advisor to demonstrate exactly what I experienced in relation to hundreds of hotels I have been to all over the world; from dumps in Eastern Europe, where we shared a BR and shower with the entire floor of rooms, to true 5 stars in the US, Europe and Asia. One star is a warning against staying at a dump – 5 star means on par with the best in the world at up to $1000 per night room rates.
With this in mind the Hyatt Dallas at Reunion has provided one of the best front end service experiences I have ever had with a few exceptions – a definite and strong 5 star. See my staff kudos below for details. Food in the hotel was fair to absolutely disgusting, (<1 star for in room dining – 2 stars in the restaurants) I ordered, from room service, the crab and goat cheese dip which was unappealing in appearance as it looked like soup rather than dip. Worse it tasted like warm vomit - no kidding, no exaggeration – When I complained they did not even take it off my bill. Interestingly enough, I ran into another convention attendee that had the exact same dish and the exact same opinion except he said that it actually made him ill. Restaurants in the hotel were not good even for convention food. Hot foods were served cold and tasted like something out of a box that had been micro-waved. Fresh fruit had been over chilled, were watery and had chunks of rind on the melon slices. No excuse that they are undergoing a $2Million restoration including the restaurants. It is the hotels job to ensure quality food. 
Rooms and Environment:
Furnishing were standard business class (a low 3 star). The Wolfgang Puck (Asian fusion) restaurant 560 was very good although the wait staff was slow, uninspired, and low class. The view made the experience worthwhile. At 50 stories up and a revolving view it was truly amazing. It is very expensive ($30 and up for entrees) but good food cooked properly. The view makes the higher than warranted prices worth it! A definite 4 star for the food and view combined- the General Manager and the Sommelier really added to the experience, they were knowledgeable, friendly, and professional.
Location:
The location was great. walking distance (15 - 20 mins) from down town and the west end restaurant district. Lots of excellent choices, hard to go wrong. 
Lobby:
The Lobby was impressive and the elevators were fast and efficient. We actually rode the lobby elevator to the top floor so we could ride it down! It was like the "Drop Zone ride". I have attached one pic I took from the elevator from about the 20th floor.
Details:
On day one of a 4 day trip we arrived at the hotel. The lobby is HUGE as one would expect of a large conference hotel. Bell men were at the ready and the front desk was well staffed. We were taken care of very quickly by a friendly helpful front end. Several of our rooms were not yet available and bellmen appeared in droves to take care of storing our baggage. We were told that our bags would be delivered to our rooms as soon as they were available. With our check in complete half the group went to the rooms and the rest of us sent directly to meetings and or elsewhere. We also informed the front desk and concierge desk of our pending reception in our suite. They immediately set up a table for check in of our guests and spread the word of our meeting so that the staff could direct lost guests to our table. Unfortunately the staff was VERY large (more than a dozen at the front desk, at least 10 bell men and more at the concierge desk) and the lobby was ENORMOUS; see the photo with the 2.5 story water fall below) and not all the staff were informed of our event and several guess were missed in the process. We also had 4 sets of business cards lost while in storage. The staff (including two bell men, the front end manager and at least two security personnel) turned the hotel upside down looking for the cards and when the cards did not turn up immediately they had a 24 hour print shop reproduce new sets of cards in about 5 hours including time for two proofs.
The concierge was amazing in helping us get set up for our first reception that took place only two hours after our arrival. Conference services kicked into gear and we had drinks on ice, light finger food, extra seating in the suite and a multi-site conference call set up almost immediately. They even produced a sign for our company for the Lobby and put our event on the Hotel lobby board without being asked – just “because we thought it would help”.
Avis was to have picked up another colleague that was going to arrange a rental for our group and provided the worst experience ever- lazy, uncaring, and with a poor attitude. In response to the Avis mess a hotel driver came to the rescue. He drove our colleague all over town trying to get issues resolved for our stay and participation in the convention. For three hours he did everything he could to help resolve issues. When offered a gratuity he replied “no thank, you’ve had a tough day and I am just happy I could be of assistance”. WHAT! Incredible. We called on him time and time again during our stay and each time he was both an excellent guide and outstanding assistant – gratuities later accepted.
We also adopted a Bell Man / Concierge who was faster to respond to issues, needs, and requests than anyone I have ever seen. Without our asking, he had housekeeping make additional stops by our suite to ensure that it was kept neat and clean for our guests at all times, kept ice on the drinks throughout the day, and ensured that food was kept fresh – no old unrefrigerated items stayed out for long enough to make someone sick.
When I left to pick up our business cards, before I got in the car, our driver asked me if I had the data and or documents I needed to have reproduced with me. Since I was picking up I did not need anything but this level of attention to detail and care for my situation is outstanding.
KUDOS!
Although all of the front end and security staff were truly excellent there were two Specific Standouts:
Victor – the Bell Man / Concierge and our Driver Paul were outstanding. Equal to or better than my experiences with the staff at the:
• “W” Hotel and the Joule in Dallas, 
• Intercontinental in Prague, 
• George V in Paris, 
• Savoy in Moscow, 
• Peninsula in NY and Shanghai,
• Willard in Washington DC.
NOTE TO Management of the Hyatt: Please do not post a generic reply to this posting as you have done for others. If your reply is a standard “thanks for staying , sorry for the issues, better luck next time” it comes off as uncaring and unprofessional. If you take the time to reply please note what specific actions you will take to fix the problem ares described herein and to reward the staff that made our stay successful!
Thanks.

title: “More bang for your buck!”
text: The hotel staff were very helpful. The rooms were clean. Most of all, it was very quiet. If you're on a tight budget and are in need of a room/kitchenette, I suggest Crossland. Its easy access off 290 and 610.

title: “Almost Perfect...small issues”
text: This hotel is unbelievably beautiful and in one of the most ideal locations in DC. The Smithsonian’s, White House, and some of the best restaurants are only a short walk from the Willard which allows you the chance to enjoy the cityscape that much more. I was really amazed at the historical nature of this hotel which really elevated the experience. The intricately detailed rooms are spacious and have one of the most comfortable beds in my hotel experience. The Concierge was absolutely fantastic and was able to recommend numerous events and even offer nominal advice on directions. If you plan on staying at the Willard I would recommend speaking to one of the Concierges ‘throughout your stay. I only have a few qualms about the Willard. The bar items offered in the room (water, snacks etc) are ridiculously priced. We actually walked to the CVS a block away to load up on provisions. Also I used the business center for 3 minutes and turned in my time card based on the honor system. The hotel actually charged me $1.50 for my internet use, LOL. I think 1. This should be a free service for hotel guests and 2. The diminutive charge should have been waived based on the amount of money the hotel demands. All in all, this beautiful hotel was almost perfect and I would recommend to anyone traveling to DC.

title: “Will defintely be back!!!”
text: Beautiful hotel, everyone was extremely friendly, rooms were clean and beautifully designed, the suite had a gorgeous view of Bryant Park. Service was wonderful. You could not beat the location!! Free wi-fi and free valet parking Sat/Sun. Loved every minute of my stay!!

title: “Business traveler? Maybe. Tourist? Think again.”
text:
A business conference recently brought me to the Hilton Baltimore for a few days. Our group had reserved about 85-90% of the hotel’s 757 rooms, and with normal tourism and other business travelers, the hotel was at full occupancy during my stay. That said, the hotel is certainly better than average as far as Baltimore hotels go, but service and facilities do not have the average tourists in mind.
First, I should start by saying that the hotel was excellently designed for the most part. The lobby and common areas are beautiful. The complimentary navy and orange color palate is warm, yet trendy. In five years, people will probably be asking, “What were they thinking?” That said, for the time being, the color scheme is very cool. The rooms are excellently outfitted, with sophisticated, masculine dark woods; draperies and flooring in subdued oranges, beiges and light greens; and bathrooms featuring high-end Kohler fixtures. The views of Camden Yards are unbelievable; we had a better view from our hotel room than friends did that actually went to the game. It’s spectacular.
The hotel caters to business travelers, and that is evident throughout the hotel. A UPS Store is located on the second floor, which features a 24-hour business center, which came in very handy for me. The hotel offers tons of flexible meeting and event spaces, which are among the most beautiful I’ve ever seen (this goes back to the trendy but short-lived color theme point I made earlier...). 
So where does the hotel fall apart? Service is a large issue. With any hotel of this size, a staff makes or breaks the guest experience, and at the Hilton Baltimore, much is left to be desired from the service standpoint. Throughout the duration of my stay, there was never more than two bellhops on duty, and there was never more than one at the hotel entrance (in fact, there were usually never any to be found...). The bellhops seemed to “hang out” around the concierge desk in the air-conditioned lobby rather than at their appropriate post. The concierge desk is another story. There were four on duty when all I wanted to know was where the UPS store is. No one was at the desk, so I walked right up, hoping they could point me in the right direction. They were engaged in a conversation, and even after five minutes, didn’t even acknowledge me standing there, directly in front of them. The front desk had 3 employees working, with a line of ten guests at any given time, arranged by velvet ropes that made me think I was waiting for a teller at the bank. I feel bad for the front desk attendants in that they never got a break, but it took an hour to check in...again, going back to the understaffing issue. Our floor had four maids on, which I thought was actually excessive, but somehow our room managed to not get serviced ONCE since we checked in. I walked up to the cart once when we needed towels, where two maids were speaking in Spanish and making rude comment between themselves about me coming up to them. Wanting to make a point, I asked them if I could get some towels in Spanish. They were obviously embarrassed about what they had just said, and then told me that they don’t have any towels. I asked why not, and they said they were being cleaned, and that all they have are “dirty towels,” and they offered me one. Are you kidding me? You’re going to offer a guest at a Hilton a dirty towel? Come on, housekeeping! Get your act together. We encountered this problem on several occasions throughout our stay (not being offered used towels, thank God, but rather not getting towels or getting not enough towels) and it was obvious that they don’t have enough linens for 757 rooms at full occupancy. I ended up walking down to the pool to get a pool towel so I could take a shower and not miss my meeting. (By the way, the pool was a letdown - very long but about 3 feet wide...I felt like I was in NYC and not baltimore).
There were also some design issues in the hotel - there are not enough power outlets in the room, and one out didn’t work at all. There is one outlet on the lamp, but that isn’t enough to charge all your devices as a business traveler. The lampshades are so cheap that they’re battered and won’t bend back out (like seen in the one picture provided by another traveler...) The garbage cans, especially the one in the bathroom, are really cool looking but don’t even fit an empty water bottle...not at all practical. Also, while not a design issue, the hotel charges $13.95 for high-speed internet, even to H-Honors members that aren’t at the top-level status. The business center is $7 per 15 minutes of computer access, and 50 cents per black and white copy (I dread to imagine what color copies cost...) They also wouldn’t let me check out late (despite being an H-Honors member) because they couldn’t offer everyone in our group that option despite that we all traveled separately, had different times to leave, and not everyone was a H-Honors member like I was. I have stayed at many Hiltons, and they’ve never asked me to check out before 2PM, and, in some instances, even 7PM. It felt like a cheap motel where you might pay by the hour, not a four-star Hilton that I was paying over $200 per night to stay at.
As far as restaurants go, there are much better options in Baltimore than those offered on-site. Room service breakfast was not rememberable, and for $30, I got two slices of french toast and three slices of bacon. They add 22% gratuity (15% distributed to server and 7% administrative charge), state and local tax, and a $5.00 delivery fee to every room service order. I hate being told how much to tip, and then the greedy hotel takes a chuck of the server's tip for itself.
On a closing note, the location can’t be beat if you’re going to the Baltimore Convention Center or an Orioles game. If you’re coming for the Inner Harbor, the walk is long (especially on a hot day like we experienced) so you may want to consider other hotels. The Renaissance is a great hotel with probably the BEST location in Baltimore near the Inner Harbor. The Intercontinental Harbor Court (Sonesta Harbor Court after May 31) is a great hotel, but will be even better after Sonesta takes ownership and does its proposed renovations. The Hotel Monaco is also a nice hotel in the downtown area. If budget is no concern, the brand new Four Seasons is the best of Baltimore, which no other Baltimore hotel can compete with. 
All in all, the Hilton is an average business hotel, but there are much better options (like those I just named) for tourists.

title: “Glam on Madison Avenue - the Morgan NYC is fabulous!”
text: I stayed at the Morgan Hotel on Madison Avenue during my last business trip, and as a former New Yorker, I have to say it was a unique and fabulous experience. My standards are very high in terms of quality of room, location, waitstaff, room service, and quiet solace needed after a busy day, and the Morgan hit every mark. Their complimentary breakfast each morning at their restaurant Asia de Cuba is FANTASTIC. Really sets the day off right. And you simply can't beat the location - central to everything without feeling like you're in the annoying throng of Time Square or Grand Central. The staff fall over themselves to take care of you, it's really lovely. I even had a private deck up on the 19th floor with a clear view of the Empire State Building!! Can't beat that.

title: “Hotel has huge noise problems”
text:
The rooms are comfortable and the staff are nice. But this hotel has HUGE noise problems. The doors,windows and walls are not noise proof. Infact they must be extra thin, because we could hear everything around us.
We had a street facing room #412 and we could hear the traffic and drunk people at night fihgting loudly.
We also heard all the noise in the hallway and all the acitivty going on in the room above ours.
We didnt sleep well at all beacuse of all the noises, thumping, banging, screaming, etc that we could hear around us.

title: “Impeccable Service”
text: This was our first trip to NYC, and I chose the Hilton Garden Inn based on location and my expected quality of the Hilton hotel line. From the doorman to the front desk to the concierge, we couldn't have asked for better treatment or friendlier people. It was sad to leave NYC after 4 days, but what would have made it sadder is that my husband left his house and car keys in the room when we checked out. We stowed our luggage at the front desk and were taking our final stroll through Times Square when I received a call that the keys had been found by hotel staff. I felt so fortunate that they were so proactive in letting us know before we left the city rather than just placing them in the lost and found as I know many hotel chains would have done. We were able to retrieve the keys before heading back to Texas, and will definitely stay with Hilton Garden Inn for our future trips to NYC.

title: “Pleasantly surprised!”
text:
We had a great long weekend at the Plaza 50! My husband was in New Jersey for business so our children and I (8 yr old and 8 mo old) joined him in NYC for a long weekend. When we arrived at 3:30am they did not have a Jr. Suite available so we were upgraded to a 1 bedroom suite. It was beautiful! It was newly renovated and very large. The bathroom was small, but the kitchenette and large living room more than made up for it. The entire suite was impeccably clean. 
I have travelled many, many times and this by far was the nicest budget-minded hotel I have ever stayed in. The beds were extremely comfortable (new).
The hotel lobby, hallways and elevators are not at all impressive and very small, but the large clean rooms are a pleasant surprise when you open the room door. We could not hear a peep from other guests through the walls or hallways.
The other bad reviews must have gotten older rooms before they were renovated. Ours was perfect. We will definately stay there again.

title: “Customer Service is Dead”
text: Back in October, I booked (with confirmation) two king rooms with city view through booking.com. When we checked-in and I finally got to my room (the absolute farthest from elevator), it was a queen room with dirty curtains, a toilet seat that appears unsanitary (lots of yellowing cracks - gross), and a non-city view of electrical boxes and four walls. I contacted both the Front Office Manager and the booking.com customer service reps to try to get moved to the room type I expected. What really set me off is that it took two calls to each to finally get an apology - unacceptable as they did agree that a mistake was made and we did not receive what was originally confirmed. Since they were sold-out that night, they offered me a measly $30 for our inconvenience and to move each of us the next day for the remaining three nights of our stay. For a luxury property that advertizes "impeccable service and promises a truly memorable experience," they did deliver on one count - an experience I really hope to forget.

title: “Great experience for a great price”
text: My experience at this hotel couldn't have been better. I called the hotel ahead of time to test the customer service. I decided that if the person who answered the phone sounded unhappy, or like they were just going through the motions, or like they hated their job, then my Double Tree experience would have ended before it began - meaning I wouldn't have booked a room there. When I called, the lady who answered was pleasant and very helpful. When I got there they treated me great. The room and bathroom was clean and comfortable. In a nut shell, I can tell that the Double Tree staff operates with a spirit of excellence.

title: “Was OK”
text: The hotel itself was positioned pretty good. Only about a five minute walk to Times Square. Water five minutes to your right. Cheap hot coffe from deli across the road. Laundromat just on the next corner. The staff were ok not overtly helpful. The rooms are average and I mean average. If you are just looking for a bed in a good location it would suit you. Mostly clean. Mostly used for tour groups.

title: “Fantastic stay at the Hotel Commonwealth”
text:
Our son is a freshman at BU and based on the reviews on Trip Advisor we had tried to stay at the Hotel Commonwealth for his visiting days and drop off but it had always been booked. Finally because we made our reservations very early, we got in for Parents Weekend. What a pleasure! It was certainly worth the wait.
We booked one of the larger rooms looking out on Commonwealth Avenue. It was perfect - it was very spacious and there were two distinct areas. One had a very comfortable king bed with large flat screen TV with a DVD built in. Near the windows was a nice sitting area with another flat screen/DVD combo TV. There was plenty of room for us to request a rollaway for our son to stay with us which was an extra bonus. We never felt cramped even with the rollaway. They had all the tech amenities - free wireless Internet and the phones had LCD screens for info and were cordless. The bathroom was large and a separate room for the toilet which was nice. The soaps and shower gel was very high quality and smelled delicious.
The Eastern Standard restaurant is attached through a hallway. It is a separate building and the food was excellent, much better than the usual hotel food. This may be due to the fact it has its own entrance on the street and seems to have a lot of local business. It has a pub like atmosphere and specializes in fresh seafood. We returned for lunch twice and loved it, but when we tried to go late on Friday night it was too noisy for us because of the busy bar scene.
Every member of the hotel staff was excellent. BU Parents weekend coincided with the Head of the Charles regatta and the Hotel was the official hotel for the race. The front desk called our room to make sure we knew that they were operating a complimentary shuttle to the regatta and that there was a hospitality tent for hotel guests. It was wonderful - they had a clean, luxury van waiting to drive us to the race. When we got there we couldn't believe the tent and food - it looked like a wedding! White linen tablecloths and fresh flowers on the tables, a buffet for breakfast that included fresh crepes, followed by a lunch buffet of stuffed crab, pumpkin risotto, shepherds pie, deserts. There was even hot chocolate with homemade marshmallows. All the food was catered from the Eastern Standard restaurant and each guest received a goodie bag to take home with a jar of the restaurant's special spice mix. This was all complimentary. The tent was right on the bank of the Charles River near the finish line so it was a wonderful location to watch the regatta.
We really loved this hotel. Every detail is well thought out. As an example, we were constantly amazed that despite the fact the hotel was full, every time we pushed the button for the elevator the doors opened immediately. When we called for the rollaway bed it came almost instantly. We have stayed in several hotels in Boston within the past year - the Westin and Marriott in Copley Square and the Marriott in Cambridge and this is definitely our first choice for a hotel in Boston. It didn't cost any more than the other hotels and we left feeling it was money well spent. We can't wait to return.

title: “Great start point!”
text:
Stay here two night at the start of the Great American Crossing Tour, great location, a stones through from Time Square.
Fiona, my wife, bumped into Snoop Dog, but he didn't ask for her autograph!
Very pleasant staff, would use it again

title: “Very Disappointed by the Facility and Customer Service”
text:
I have to say I am VERY disappointed and upset by hotel facility and particularly, its customer service. 
Here is my story: the first night I found the toilet in my room was not working, the water tank couldn't refill quickly after flush...but the problem was fixed after I adjusted the location of its water plug, however, on the second night, after I returned from all day meetings, I found the problem became out of my control, so I called the frontdesk to have maintenance staff checked it over, however, the problem was still not fixed, I was told that i may use the bathroom across the hallway which is empty. But later front desk called me and said that I could have only two options: either use the public restroom in the lobby or change to another room! Just imagine the hassel packing up in late night and moving to a different room for toilet's sake, or, imagine someone wearing gown and walking across the lobby in the morning just because he needs to use public restroom?? that's ridiculous and totally unacceptable! I explained my frustration and tried to work out a solution with the front desk staff but the response I got was very cold, non-negotiable, without even an apology! The frontdesk staff just hang up the phone even before I finished talking! 
Anyways, I don't want to make this review too long, just it helps you in planning your trip in D.C.

title: “Looking Tired”
text:
I've stayed here a few times. It is very well located in the middle of the Jewish area of Los Angeles and close by the many synagogues - especially the Young Israel of Century City which is three minutes' walk.
The staff were very friendly, and I was given the star treatment which I think they give to everyone.
But the place is beginning to look tired and the rooms are in significant need of updating. Given that I'd stayed the previous night for two thirds the price at the Crowne Plaza in LAX with its refurbished rooms, I hope this one is on the list before my next stay

title: “Great Rooms, If You Can Get in Them!”
text:
The Loew's is a very nice hotel in the middle of downtown Philly, six blocks from the historical area (Liberty Bell, Independence Hall, etc.). The lobby, halls and rooms are nicely decorated and furnished... including plush Hilton-style beds and refreshing showers. Loew's First members get automatic room upgrades, if available, and our upgrade got us a corner room on a Club floor (30th) and access to what could have been a very nice continental breakfast on the 31st floor (also Club). Loew's First members get a welcome gift, and ours was a nice bag of assorted Philadelphia products... some pretzels, some caramel coated popcorn, cookies, and candy. Staff throughout our four day visit were very pleasant and helpful, never failing to say good morning or hello. 
The upside to being on a Club floor was the spectacular views to the north and west (city hall nearby, and the massive art museum in the distance). The nicely appointed corner room had a flat screen TV and free internet access. One minor drawback was that the afternoon sun really heated up the room if the heavy drapes were open on the west side, and the AC struggled to cool it down. 
We were a bit surprised to hear a yappy dog barking two of the mornings... surprised that dogs were allowed in the hotel, and surprised that the inconsiderate owners would leave their dog to bother the other hotel guests. No problems with noise at night, thank goodness.
A significant downside to being on the Club level was the required electronic key access, which gave us many problems. Not only did we need the key to access the room (3017), but also to get the elevator to stop at the 30th floor, and to stop at the 31st floor for breakfast. The key frequently did not work for us, even when kept isolated from other cards, the cell phone, etc. As you can imagine, this was a frustrating, embarrassing problem on an elevator with other guests. I had to get front desk help four or five times during our stay, and I didn't get the sense we were the only ones who had this problem.
A second downside was the failure of the staff to keep up with the morning ebb and flow of guests at the Club level continental breakfast on two out of the three mornings. This meant we had to ask and wait for plates, glasses, silverware, skim milk, and bagels, as well as a clean table. On our third morning we gave up and went across the street to Reading Terminal Market for breakfast. The breakfast staff on the Loew's club level was very nice, and there was a good selection of food when available, but they just seemed overwhelmed.
We made our reservations on the Loew's website, and I paid $219 per night, plus $30.66 occupancy tax per night. Typical of downtown locations, we had valet parking at a rate of $34 per night (plus tip each time we needed the car).
Bottom line is that I still like the hotel. Staff and decor were a big plus. However, the problems with the electronic keys got to be a constant irritant, and being on the Club level just made it worse. 
I may try somewhere different next time.

title: “Outstanding”
text: We stayed 4 nights the last week of August 2011. Our suite was lovely, bed was amazing, views terrific and the floor was very quiet, 9th floor. 24 hour doorman, room service a bit pricey but very good. Local restaurants are delicious, Mikeys and Tinys for vegetarian friendly, many more for sure. Great candy store across the street. This is a happening neighborhood. I will definitely stay here next time I come to the city.

title: “Great service”
text:
I attended a 2 day meeting at the W Hotel. It was my first time staying at a W and it was definitley a different/positive experience. When I went to the check in desk, it is very different from any other hotel I've been too...candles on the desk...kind of a sexy atmosphere. I have to say that the doorman, the check in, concierge, housekeeping, catering were all very professional and helpful. I lost my cellphone in the taxi to the hotel and the concierge was able to retrieve it. Everyone was so nice and friendly. The food at the meetings was great too and just a different experience. My room was gorgeous! I loved the decore. It had a whimsical, sophisticated feel to it. The only thing I would recommend is more lighting in the halls, I found it too dark as did my co-workers. I would say this hotel is more appreciated by the 20-30 something hip crowd. It has a night-clubish, schwanky, trendy feel to it. The lobby is loaded with candles, some special effects lighting and music. It's quite the hot spot to hang and have drinks in the evening. 
The meeting space at the hotel was great and our meeting was a sucess! The food was fabulous and the catering staff was right on top of things! Some of the older/conservative people mentioned that the hotel was a bit dark and very funky, but they just chalked it up not being "in" anymore and still thought the meeting went well(which was plenty light) and had an overall good experience staying there. At our meeting, I loved the pitchers of water at out tables, some had lemon swirly slices, lime slices, orange slices, strawberries in them with made them appealing to the eye and a touch of flavor. Just little things like that make it nicer. Anyway, I would recommend the hotel for a meeting especially with a younger crowd and I would recommend it for a romantic getway! It would be a great place to go with friends too and just live it up in the city! There is so much to do in that area! I wished I had time to extend my trip and play! I would like to go back sometime soon!

title: “Good location and cheapish rooms”
text: This hotel is located just outside the city and in a good location for local eateries and shops. The rooms are large and some have excellent views of Washington. Breakfast is very good and there is free wi-fi in the lobby. I would recommend this hotel for business or leisure

title: “Fantastic”
text: stayed here for 9 days whilst visiting relatives.Fantastic hotel and staff and very clean.

title: “Mid west beige”
text:
Melting pot of mostly ethnic corporate travellers and low socio-demographic profiles as the Presidential Towers complex also houses what they refer to in US, section 8, housing for low income households. Not that this was of concern but making note of the diverse array of people this complex provides housing for. 
Bland and basic standard fare for corporate stay. Furnishings pretty ordinary but practical. Security a bit over the top but assuring. Beware having packages delivered. Packages addressed correctly rendered me deceased and sent elsewhere. Lost luggage delivered to the complex by the airline was like an Easter egg hunt til found it was sent to the valet that closes Saturday 3pm and does not re-open until Monday 7:30am. No-one has access on Sundays according to Tower management which I still find difficult to swallow. I recommend Habitat as a starting point but next visit would prefer to not stay downtown, although this has come with familiarising myself with Chicago and inner neighbourhoods over the two months I have been here.

title: “Convenient location”
text: Rooms were clean, and staff was very accommodating and helpful with directions. We were in town for marathon and needed flexibility for late checkout; staff was very gracious to accommodate a reasonable request. Location is very convenient. Rooms were clean and bed was comfortable. My only complaint was valet service did not include finding a solution for parking. With no spots available on site, we were told we could go park 6 blocks away. Fortunately with the weekend, we were able to find parking on street.

title: “Too Good To Be True---But it IS !!!”
text: Far Exceeded my expectations, Staff even remembered our names. Location great for shopping,restaurants. Room very uniquely current and comfortable..The Pillow choices were fun, We tried a few.Just Loved it !!!! This is our new home away from home.. If youre looking for a wonderful hotel near the magnificent mile, Affinia is the place for you. Told all my family and friends about this exceptional Hotel...... Thanks Affinia for making my pre holiday celebration a true "OVER THE TOP" experience....

title: “NOT up to Hampton Inn Standards”
text:
Hampton Inn's are our Go To Hotel chain. Very disappointed, This property does NOT meet up to the standards of other Hampton Inns.
Mouldy bathroom tiles, No bathmat, Very noisy A/C - No quiet mode/low speed.
Very Limited TV channel selection, We were in the area for GOLF. Players Championship, Golf Hall of Fame etc. NO Golf Channel ? This is golf country ?

title: “Hotel certainly not work the price”
text: First problem was the charge of $15.00 per day for use of the internet, even for a Marriott rewards member. Second no free breakfast, even for rewards members. Third, the hotel is showing a little wear and tear in the public areas, the bath towels were not fluffy and limp. Plus side it was clean and quiet, although a colleague who stayed on the side of the hotel bordering the elevated rail reported noise issues. Staff was friendly. If you drive, plan on being charged $52.00 to park. Walk to a number of good places to eat. Hotel borders Chicago River walk. If you have a choice, look for other options in area.

title: “Great Place, TERRIFIC Amenities but got no sleep”
text: This property is really nice. We had to travel to Boston Mass Hospital & this was recommended by the hospital for us to stay. The hotel was clean, there are so many amenities, the staff was nice & the continental breakfast was not just coffee & donuts like so many other places. But for some reason I just could not sleep, the beds seemed comfortable. There were not any loud guests or partiers, but I woke every morning exhausted. Other than that the place was very nice.

title: “Much more than your typical chain hotel!”
text: You get all the standard amenities you expect from a Holiday Inn, but so much more at this hotel. The food is simply prepared but fresh and cooked to order which makes a world of difference. The staff are exceptionally friendly and courteous. You should note, the street name has been recently changed to West Durango so if you use GPS it will react a little strangely as you arrive at the location. It's also short, but tricky route off the Interstate and you will not have one of those sky high signs to guide you. The hotel does not look like you typical Holiday Inn from the outside and it's not - it way above average.

title: “Very un-happy”
text: Well our night started out with the other group we were with getting there room and it had not been cleaned the bed was not made and the was garbage and dishes all over so they meet us and went to our room to wait for their new room upon entering out room we found a used "CONDOM" right i the middle of the floor. So no we had to go andget a new room ,which is when they told me i could go somewhere else if i wanted (nice buisness practice)well we ended up takeing the smoking roo because it was the only thing open get to the new room and it was dirty also garbage on the floor and dried upo yellow flem in the sink. while we where there our friends got to there room and it had no working air conditioning and no cscreen in the window so they couldnt even open it because they had a 2 and 1 year old with them. so needless to say we where very unhappy and as of now i have conmtacted management and nothing has been done

title: “Great Place”
text: We sure enjoyed our stay. We walked to Navy Pier. Had a wonderful cocktail at night and a nice hot breakfast. The room was very quiet and we slept really well. We will stay here again.

title: “Great Experience”
text: We did not even know about this hotel, until recommended by the Baylor Hospital Hotel, and now we stay at the Indigo whenever in town, especially on visitsto Baylor. The hotel is historic, yet up to date in every aspect. The staff was not just friendly but highly motivated to see that the guest's every need was met, great service abounds at every level. The bar and grill was conveniently located in the lobby with a great menu and the same great service as the rest of the Indigo. We recommend the Indigo without reservations!

title: “Business Trip to DC”
text: This is a solid business hotel with a great executive lounge. The front desk was friendly. Food trucks lined up every day at lunch time-great food with lots of variety. The Metro is right outside and there's a bike share stand next to it. Rooms were comfortable. The well equipped work out room was large and featured complimentary washing/drying machines-that was an unexpected bonus! The pool was a mild disappointment-it's under four feet deep on both ends. All staff were great.

title: “Last 8 days in NYC”
text:
on our last 8 days we moved uptown nearer to the museum mile.
Less interesting restaurants here but great transport (bus and subway) to downtown east and west. Staff at hotel fabulous, nothing too much trouble. Small boutique with about 40 + rooms, small breakfast area with excellent array of food for all cultures. Extreme logistic management enabled all to be catered for, as well as check out, in and all manner of tourist questions. Very professional. Neat and to the point.

title: “Worth your time!”
text: I recently stayed at 60 Thompson after finding a stellar rate on the hotel's website--the "Thompson Shopper" deal, available on Sunday nights. After reading several reviews on Trip Advisor, I thought it best to request a room on a high floor, which I did by calling the hotel. When my girlfriend and I arrived, we were pleased by the attentive, professional bell staff and by the fact that our room was on the very top floor. The room itself was quite large (especially compared to the one at the Hudson, where we'd stayed the night before) and appointed in a tasteful, if slightly institutional, manner. The Frette linens were a real treat, as were the Fresh toiletries. The minibar was well-stocked and the room service menu pretty comprehensive. We visited the Thom Bar downstairs for a cocktail around five in the evening, and it was quiet and relaxing; when we returned to the hotel much later that night, it was quite busy and the music was playing loudly, so we were doubly appreciative of our room well above all the noise. I thought the staff was very professional and especially friendly for a SoHo hotel. Overall, I'd recommend 60 Thompson to travelers who'd like to be conveniently located--it's a short walk to lots of great boutiques and restaurants--and appreciate a slightly more subdued, adult, trendiness. Look on the hotel's own site to get a good deal, though--it's honestly just not worth the $400-plus rate they usually charge.

title: “great location, clean and comfortable”
text:
I spent three nights at the hotel at the end of February 2010. Our room was very clean, the beds comfortable, staff was friendly and the location was great. Breakfast was good, not great; but it was included and that was a bonus. Complimentary apples, cookies in the afternoon and coffee bar was very nice touch. The woman at the concierge desk was very helpful and accomodating. 
My only criticism (and this really stood out for me) was the use of disposable everything!! At breakfast there was disposable cutlery, plates, bowls, glasses and cups. In our room there were disposable glasses!! Firstly, I dont' like using disposable products and secondly, in this day and age, the amount of garbage produced by this is unbelievable.

title: “Service is a gamble”
text:
The MGM is a very new and nice hotel, with many cool amenities and technology in the room that makes it nearly worth the $300/night. It is modern, nicely designed and clean, and the casino is large, airy and comfortable. However our service was marginal, and if you are paying that type of price for downtown Detroit in the winter, service should be top-notch. 
We requested a comp into V because we were hotel guests and not local kids. After waiting around in our room for a half hour for them to try to hook it up, they called and said sorry, we would have to pay the $30 cover. So, we went down to V and paid it and it was a small, lame club. Later that night when we returned to the room there was a message from V saying they would comp us after all. Did they think we would be waiting in the room all night after they said we would have to pay our own cover? 
Instead of a "Do Not Disturb" sign, they had a light hooked up to the door where you press a button for "Privacy" or "Request Service." We thought this to be easy and cool, however, they still need to look at it and try to honor our request. We put the "Privacy" light on so they would not come into our room for turndown service. We left to eat dinner and came back, and there was a message on the phone telling us to call the front desk to retrieve our message. We called the front desk and received a recorded message confirming that we had requested privacy and giving us a number to call if, in fact, we wanted the turndown service. The whole point of the "Privacy" button was that we did not want to be bothered that night. It was not an efficient system. Furthermore, both mornings of our stay, the housekeeping staff opened the door while we were sleeping, even though the Privacy button was lit.
The valet parking is divided into "Casino" and "Hotel" side. They told us we could retrieve our car on either side. We had parked in the "Hotel" side and tried to pick it up on the "Casino" side. Of course the car was sitting over on the Hotel side for a half hour while we waited in the cold outside the Casino.
There was a cool-seeming computer screen/TV in the bathroom but it was broken the whole time so we were not even really sure what it was supposed to be.
Two of the lights in our room were busted so we were in dim lighting at night.
Upon arrival, we opened the minibar to check it out, pulled out a couple of items and replaced them. Later on we saw a small sign on top of the dresser stating that the minibar is electronic and if anything is removed we will be charged. I called the front desk and was advised that if anything was removed for longer than 13 seconds, you are charged for it, even if you replace it and do not consume it. I was very glad we got that $60 8-oz bottle of vodka back in the fridge in the prescribed time frame! Watch out for this - we were distrustful of being nickeled-and-dimed for everything from that point out.
They boast a large number of penny slots, but in fact there were only a few true penny machines. Most of their video slots are 2 or 5 cents. We were disappointed by this and ended up doing most of our gambling at Greektown down the street.
I had some money comped on my players club card, but it stopped working out of the blue before I could retrieve it. I chose not to stand in the long line to have them fix it.
We did like the Italian station at Breeze but the lines were long. They have 2 Starbucks but only one was ever open.
It may be worth checking out for a special occasion, or to say you stayed there, but we will not return. If they charged half as much I probably would stay there again, but next time we'll try the new hotel at Greektown.

title: “Moore or less”
text: Satisfactory basic hotel. We had an ensuite room. Room was dated, with chipped paint et. but it was clean and neat. Bathroom was clean. Great location, Short walk to everything. Very helpful front desk staff. Two criticisms: no tea/coffee making facilities in room and noise from neighbouring rooms- thin walls. You get what you pay for, and this was the cheapest accommodation I could find in seattle.

title: “Great Hotel, Great Value, Great Location”
text:
I recently had the pleasure of staying at this hotel during a business trip. For the most part, D.C. hotels are grossly expensive and underwhelming in amenities. This hotel proves to be the exception.
The hotel is well located near the Potomac tidal basis and walking distance to the Jefferson Memorial and Washington Monument. In contrast to many D.C. hotels which are shoehorned among office buildings, the Mandarin Oriental offers a standalone hotel with restaurants, bar and spa. 
The rooms are clean and well appointed. Although my room was not especially large (though larger than many cosmopolitan hotels), it was designed to give the feeling of spaciousness and the bathroom was large and modern.
The staff deserves special note. Throughout my stay, I was greeted by a remarkably friendly staff who constantly asked if they could help in any way. 
I could not ask for a better value for this Washington gem.

title: “Clean, Comfortable, Good Location in Mid-Town”
text: Can't add much more to the bazillions of good reviews here. Good location for Broadway shows. Hope they don't get a swelled head and raise their rates as they are already not cheap, but about on par with similar hotels.

title: “This hotel has it all at a great price”
text: Hotel reminds me of the great European boutique hotels. Room was small but had everything - fridge, microwave, safe. good lighting. Very nice, 24 hour fitness room with bottles of water. On site bar and restaurant with inventive happy hour specials. Location was great - very close to Horton Plaza, about 5-8 blocks to Gaslight and Convention Center. My only complaint is walls are a bit thin - hope you don't have a loud neighbor. Great value.

title: “Loved the Fairmont”
text: The location is probably the best in the city. A walk downhill to most of the attractions whether Fisherman's wharf , Union Square or the San Francisco shopping center.The service was very good and we really enjoyed the food at the Tonga 'Chinese Restaurant' on our last night at the Hotel. The Lobby is majestic.I was blown away by the old world charm of the hotel

title: “One of my favorite hotels anywhere”
text:
I have been staying at the Warwick for 2 to 3 weeks a year, whenever I am in town on business. It is a friendly place located equidistant between Central Park and Time Square. It is right across the street from MOMA and only a few blocks from Radio City. The location is perfect for doing business in mid-town and for tourists. 
The staff at Randolph's (the bar/restaurant) are outstanding. It is a fun place to relax after the day and the food is quite good. It can get crowded in the early evening before curtains go up in the many theaters, and then again later in the evening after the shows are over. 
I put value as "very good." I am always on an expense account when in NYC, but notice sometimes the rooms are quite a bit more expensive. It is NYC though, and the room is on par with what you will pay anywhere really. There are more expensive hotels that I don't like nearly as much. At some times of the year the rooms are quite reasonable.

title: “Location, Location, Location”
text:
Just returned from a pre-holiday weekend in the Big Apple. This hotel is right in the middle of the action, but you're in a quire, world away, jsut looking down on Times Square and the thousands of people. Pull the drapes and you won't see the millions of lights and action. It's quiet and your sleep will be great. We had 2 children traveling with us, so the suite was perfect to give all of us the space we needed.
Ask for a corner room...we had 2701 and could look out over Broadway and down Times Square. BEst view in the house...
Hotel held our luggage both before check-in and when we checked out, but were staying the whole day.
Ginger's Restaurant was wonderful for breakfast...full buffet with omelets to order.

title: “Nice hotel, but one small issue that created a tacky factor”
text:
I recently stayed at the Omni for a meeting that was being held at the hotel. I would like to start by saying that the staff was wonderful. They were very pleasant and helpful. The hotel itself is nice, but a bit worn. It could use an updating. The configuration of the room was a little odd, and the bathroom, although a decent size, was configured poorly. There was very little counter space (I mean very little). The hotel had a decent sized gym. There was also a pool, but it was small and the area around the pool was not particularly attractive.
The hotel has an attractive location. It is directly connected to a mall, which also contains many places to eat, as well as a movie theater and an arcade. There are also many bars and restaurants in the area. The hotel is very close to Conseco Fieldhouse and within walking distance to the new Colts Stadium.
Now for the tacky factor. Traveling for business, I usually send my materials ahead to the hotel where I am staying so that I do not have to carry them on the plane. For this trip, it was a small-to-medium sized box with 17 presentations inside. The Omni charged $10 to receive and hold the box for my arrival. This is the only hotel that I stayed at that has ever done this. 
All in all, the Omni was a nice hotel with an attractive location. I would stay here again. However, that charge just left me with a tacky feel about the hotel.

title: “Great location, comfortable room”
text:
You can't beat the location! Just a short walk from the T, right in the middle of historic Boston. The staff were friendly, the room was incredibly comfortable - great shower, fluffy pillows, and cozy bed. I slept like a rock. Concierge parking was fast and easy. 
There are lots of inexpensive places to get a sandwich nearby, and, of course, Quincy Market is just a stone's throw away. You don't stay here for the view - which is outside!

title: “A Grand Old Hotel, with Excellent Service”
text:
The Fairmont Olympic is one of those grand old hotels that you can't help but enjoy. On my visit, I had a suite. It was quite spacious, but the furnishings and decor of the room was a bit too outdated for my taste.
That's pretty much the only negative thing I could say about this place. The rest of my stay was excellent. The food was always wonderful, and the service was second to none. A nice surprise was when I first arrived. As a Fairmont President's Club member, I was already checked in the moment I arrived. The bellman who opened my door handed me my key and let me know I could go right up. Super convenient!
It's also well-situated, closed to shopping and tourist attractions.

title: “Excellent Spot for an Airport Stay”
text:
Beautifully maintained hotel with great service. We only stayed the night after a flight and before departing for San Diego, but it was perfect. Beds were comfortable, and the room was fresh, clean, and best of all, quiet! 
They have a Starbucks right in the lobby for a quick (but good) breakfast, and a restaurant on site for buffet, a la carte, etc. There is also a small pool.
The hotel offers a complimentary shuttle, and is within walking distance of car rentals, so perfect as conduit location for more travel.
Highly recommend!

title: “Great location bad service”
text: The room was clean and the cleaning staff was prompt and friendly. The desk staff less friendly and not as fast. One of three very small elevators was out for the four days we were there. We were on the 18th of 22 floors and it was a lot of standing in front of the elevators. We found out later that the one elevator had been out for 3 weeks! Concergie did not want to help with bus/train schedules and suggested we take a taxi everywhere, not. Chicago has a great public transportation system that should be easily managable for most travellers. The location and cleanliness made it worth the price.

title: “Exceptional Customer Care”
text: The Manager of the Howard Johnson Fenway; as well, the Assistant to Robert Sage of Sage Hotels Ingrid Tapia have bent over backwards trying to accomodate my return visit. My October 2009 one night visit didn't go well. Since then I have been offered a free night when possible by the management. Sadly, my two attempts to return I have had to cancel. I regret that very much. The management leadership could not have been nicer to me ! David D. of Philadelphia

title: “50th Birthday Celebrations”
text: Our party of five have just returned from NYC and stayed at the Hospitality House. It was great, very central, clean and everyone was very helpful - especially Sam!! He guided us re tours, restaurants and anything we asked. We got caught up in the Hurricane but nothing was too much trouble for any of the staff during our extended stay. My only grumble would be that there was only one bathroom in our 2 bedroom apartment for five ladies but it wasn't a disaster by any means.

title: “BED BUGS!!! This hotel was below my lowest expectations”
text:
My boyfriend and I were recent guests at the Days Inn at 1660 Whitehead Court in Baltimore, Maryland. Frankly, our stay was not enjoyable or even at the lowest of our expectations.
I contracted a rash after my first night in my hotel room. I went to the walk in clinic and they confirmed that they were bed bug or mite bites. There simply was not any other reason for this rash that appeared on my body. It had only got worse throughout my stay. We had taken a nap and after I had woken up I noticed that the rash had gotten worse. I went down and told the evening desk attendant who wasn’t wearing a name tag about my concerns. Not once did he apologize. Rather, he insinuated that I had gotten a rash from going out during the day into the city. Even though I was permitted to spend two days here by the staff knowing that I am under 21 (because I have a credit card to guarentee the charges,) the attendant simply said that there will be no compensation because I am under 21 and that I should have come down when I first woke up instead of waiting until later in the afternoon. I told him that I wasn’t sure where this rash had come from but when I woke up from my nap it had gotten considerably worse. I asked for housekeeping to change the sheets or to inspect the bed and he told me that there is no housekeeping on the premises and he “wasn’t going to call someone to come in just to change the sheets.” He changed our room and said nothing else.
There were people with carts outside the room at 8 in the morning and you can hear the highway from your room. 
Whenever I had called to speak to the manager he was never there and the same front desk attentant continually hung up on me. I wouldn't let my worst enemy stay in this hotel.
 Our stay was not enjoyable or even at the lowest of our expectations

title: “Nice hotel with good, but noisy restaurant in the backyard”
text:
Metro Hotel... 
we´d stay there for three night. The room was nice furnitured and had a window to the backyard. The staff is very friendly and relaxed.
The hotel shares the backyard with a french restaurant (good food for reasonable prices!). 
This turned out to be a real problem, because the were guests of the restaurant arriving 11h p.m.(23h), which were served in the backyard until 1h a.m. (1h morning). After this very noisy (americancs are regretably tent to be very loud in restaurants) an annoying experience the staff of the restaurant started to pack empty bottels and to trow empty boxes an cans into the backyard. We tried to complain at the front-desk of the hotel - but without any remarkable reaktion of the restaurant staff. 
We can NOT recommend this hotel for a stay before a long-distance-flight, because you need your sleep before. This hotel is neither recommendable for travellers with very young children or pragnant women. For disabelded persons: there is no elevator and you have to carry your luggage yourself up the stairs!
For all others the place is a nice place to be - if you have your earplugs with you. ;-)
Britta & Hubert

title: “Excellent Service”
text: My girlfriends and I stayed here for our "weekend get away" June 21-22, 2012. The location was perfect for Easton and Gahanna and the lower room rate let us spend more on shopping and dinning out. We had connecting rooms which were clean and well kept. All of the hotel personel that we came in contact with were welcoming and professional. We'll be back!

title: “Nice Hotel, But needs updating”
text:
The Millennium UN Hotel was nice, but needs some serious updating. I was in a one bedroom suite and the furniture was old and some of it chipped. The room was also very dark and almost dreary. When I checked in everything in the mini-bar was warm, and I called to have it fixed. 
Service was very quick but the repairman informed me that a whole unit was needed and it would take several days to get this accomplished. His suggestion was to call room service for ice. I cannot believe that there was not an extra minibar in storage, but ok. Then the shower was another whole mess. There was no liner in the shower, so everytime we took a shower the bathroom floor became a small pond. I informed the front desk of this, and it never got fixed. The view was beautiful although, overlooking the east river possibly. Livingroom was well appointed for entertaining, had a couch and two chairs. There was also a dining room table. The nice part was that there was also a half bath. 
So my girlfriend could use the master bath, while I shaved in the other half bath. Staff was courteous and nice, but could have paid more attention to detail. Overall I would return, but maybe ask for an updated room if there are any.

title: “make sure you specify a renovated room”
text:
Stayed here twice - first time, we got a nice renovated room with marble bath at the end of a hallway (very quite). Second time I think I forgot to specify renovated room, or they interpreted "renovated" = "upgrade" because they upgraded us to a small suite. But it wasn't renovated, and boy did that room pale in comparison with the one we stayed in the first time we were here! 
I called down to the front desk and asked if any renovated rooms were available. They told me there was one on a lower floor if that was OK, and I said that was no problem. The manager actually ran the keys to our new room up to us in about 2 minutes! THAT is service! Kudos to you, Fairmont Olympic. The new room was also a suite, and the renovated rooms are SO MUCH NICER. Nicer bedding, cleaner-looking lines, nice paint tones, newer finishings like light switch face plates, nice new marble bathroom. I would probably give this place 3 or 4 stars if I had stayed in the original room they gave me during that stay. 
The hotel itself is in a good location - if you're heading out to I-5, you just go straight up the street a couple of blocks and you're there. Lots of restaurants, the SAM, and pike place market within blocks. 
There's a hotel car that can take you around the downtown area. The first time I stayed, I was having dinner at Canlis as part of the "find a key and get free dinner at Canlis" thing in October (I was graciously invited for helping! :) and I mentioned that I needed a taxi to one of the valets. Well, he told me to hang on and that he'd see if he could get the hotel car to take me. It was free, so they gave me a free ride to Canlis, which I must say is not exactly in the "downtown core", either. You guys are the best! The second time we stayed, it was a busier night so we had to wait about 20 minutes for the car to take us somewhere, but the driver was great, again (different guy). We were going to Kneehigh Stocking company, which is a speakeasy-type place and purposefully difficult to find. Well, our driver was so thoughtful - he made sure that he knew exactly where this place was before he would drop us off, probably so he'd know where to pick us up later that night, but it was really nice of him. 
The terrace lounge has some REALLY great drinks, if you like cocktails stop in and try a couple. All in all, I would definitely stay here again - great service, even if all the rooms aren't updated you could always try to ask for one that is.

title: “Perfect would be an understatement”
text: If you want to be treated like royalty 24 x 7 then stay at this hotel. It is fantastic. Extremely attentive personnel wait on you better that you could possibly imagine. The rooms were immaculate. The gym is spectacular. If you want to have a truly enjoyable work-out experience then wait until you go there. It is covered but outdoors with beautiful plants all over the place so you feel like you are in a tropical garden while you are working out. This hotel is worth every penny spent.

title: “Incredible Staff,Terrific Stay”
text:
We chose the Chancellor based on reviews on this site and management responses and were totally happy and impressed with our choice. Every staff member was genuinely concerned with our comfort and patient with our requests for directions and restaurant recommendations. Rex and Alicia in the bar were gracious, funny, and informative; the housekeepers were quite pleasant and extremely thorough, and the front desk staff were quick and efficient without being curt. 
 The location is excellent, easy to acess public transportation, shopping, and a great selection of restaurants. Our stay here was the highlight of our 3 city vacation and we'll be sure to stay here again on our next trip. Great job Mr. Tyler!

title: “Excellent location, ok hotel”
text:
The four stars is for the location of this hotel right slap bang in the middle of Times Square.
Whilst the hotel was OK it is not the best W that I have stayed in. The fitness centre was very good and was not too busy. The rooms were a decent size for New York but could have been brighter, the hotel staff were polite, and by the time I left I had just got my head around the two different lifts required to get to the rooms on the higher floors.
I would definitely stay here again for the right price, but it is not my first choice hotel in the area.

title: “Would Have Given and Above Average Rating...”
text: Stayed here while in NYC on business. It was fashion week and all of my usual picks in Midtown were either sold out or priced beyond my comfort level. This property is conveniently located adjacent to Grand Central Station. Was greeted by staff at the top of the escalator and was guided to the self check in (my request). Check in process was quick and accurate. Elevators are a little confusing. Signage is really small so you have to learn by experience which ones to take for your floor. Room was actually pretty spacious by NYC standards except for the bathroom. It was very small and the toilet was literally wedged between the tub and wash basin cabinet which was uncomfortable for a good size man. Fortunately I was traveling alone as it would have been very inconvenient to have two trying to using this bathroom. Otherwise the furnishings were tastful and everything was in good condition. Very nice bar area with lots of windows. Probably won't consider this property again due to the small bathroom.

title: “Top of the Mark - not so top!”
text: Great deal on room. Nice Room. Friendly front desk BUT terrible hostess at the Top of the Mark lounge/restaurant. Very rude!!!!!!!! Surprised the facility allows for such staff.

title: “Three star hotel with a 5 star location.”
text: Great location on Michigan avenue. Hotel was as I expected based on the reviews I read from tripadvisor. The rooms are small. Too small. I think most people have grown accustom to larger rooms at any price level. Where the room disappoints there is nothing else about this hotel that wins you back. I should have stayed at ANY other hotel. I had friends who stayed one night at the inter and two more y the embassy suites nearby. Embassy was nicer.

title: “Great location, good hotel”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for 2 nights over the weekend. We were greeted at the taxi by the door staff and helped in with our luggage, the check in was good and then another guy took us and our luggage to our room. 
The staff were very helpful when we were trying to make decisions about where to eat, what tours to do and how to get there. 
The room was nice, nothing out of the ordinary, mini bar, safe, loads of hanging space and coat hangers, TV etc... 
The bathroom was quite small and there was no where to dry wet towels apart from on the rack above the toilet....I didn't like that. The shower was over the bath, which isn't a problem normally, but it was annoying that you couldn't get in at the bottom on the bath as it was too sloped, so you have to get in the tap end and get straight in the water...again..not a massive issue...when the shower stopped I could hear water under the bath but not drained away, like there was a layer between the floor of the bath and the bottom? weird.
Breakfast offered is tea, coffee and hot chocolate and there is a wine reception every evening 5-7pm.
This was the 2nd time we had stayed at A kimpton hotel and we received a $10 mini bar voucher to use because of this.
Location was excellent, 2 mins from union square, cabel car stop, subway lines..etc
All in all it was good.

title: “The Keating experience”
text:
The Keating Hotel needs to be experienced. My stay in April was delightful. It has nostalgia and history along with amenities of today. It plays with the senses with it's contemporary decor combined within the structure built in the 1800's. One gets a little glimpse into the past while being in the pulse of the Gaslamp District of downtown San Diego. 
As a single female, I felt safe. Everything I took in during my stay was within walking distance, so I had no need for a vehicle. There was always someone at the front desk to greet me when I came and went.
After having the delectable treat which was left each evening on the nightstand and before crawling into a luxuriously made up bed, I opened the windows and the drone from all the activity and outdoor patrons at the many restaurants and bars provided a wonderful white noise to fall sound asleep to.
In the morning if you chose to sleep late, the darkening shades did a superb job of keeping the room dark. Otherwise the shades could be pulled up to let the sun's rays come pouring through the windows into the room. 
One word of caution...if you decide to use the Jacuzzi tub, make sure the water in the tub is filled to cover the top jet nozzles...otherwise it provides a fountain of arching streams of water crisscrossing each other and shooting out into the room!

title: “Nice Hotel, Great Service”
text:
The Elan is a nice hotel at the edge of Beverly Hills and West Hollywood. The Hotel staff was very helpful and friendly.
Our room was a little small and faced a inner courtyard with no view but with little to no street noise. The room had great access to the hotels free wi-fi but I had no service to my carrier ATT
Room was 108. The breakfast was ok and the evenings wine and cheese was nice.
The Beverly Center Mall is across the street but I would recommend The Grove or The Century City shopping center for shopping and dining.
I would also like to recommend a diner called Swingers about a mile east of the hotel. The food is great and a place to eat after taking in the nightlife as they dont close till 4

title: “Weekend In Seattle”
text:
I stayed at the Westin for the weekend with my 15 year old niece. We had a standard double room with was beautiful. We had great service from the concierge, who helped us with the monrail and advise on sites to visit. 
The only criticism I have is that there was no wireless internet, so my niece could not use he handheld devise, which did not have the Ethernet capability. I also had to pay for internet connection for my laptop. I really resent having to pay for internet in my room when you can go and get free wireless in the lobby coffee shop.

title: “Very nice hotel with very nice staff!!”
text:
We booked Hotel Monaco for our 5 year anniversary weekend in Baltimore. Upon arrival, we were greeted at the front door by very friendly staff who helped us unload our car onto a luggage cart. We were led into the building and up to the next floor where the front desk/check in is (I did find it odd that you had to go up a floor to check in). Check in was smooth and easy and they even gave our 10 month old son a book and a game from a treasure chest. We booked a King room and brought our sons pack n play and had plenty of room to set it up. The room was spacious, clean, and pleasant. The bed was so comfortable, had clean white linens, and very comfortable pillows. We found a bottle of champagne in our room (for our anniversary) which was very kind! They also offer a nightly free wine hour in the lobby living room, which is a nice bonus! 
The only "problem" we had while staying here was that our television did not work. We called the front desk and they sent someone up right away. However, they were unable to fix it and said they would have to come back the next day. Typically, we dont care about TV, but having a baby with us, we had to go to the room much earlier than normal to put him to bed. They offered us "free breakfast" which turned out to be a voucher for free coffee and a pastry which in my opinion is not breakfast. Oh well. They did fix the TV the next day as promised.
Overall, I think this is a great hotel with a very helpful and friendly staff. We had a pleasant stay and would return again!!

title: “Super Friendly”
text: This is one of the nicest, friendliest hotels I've stayed at and the price is excellent. We're staying here again the next time we're in San Antonio. We stayed for three nights and enjoyed the nightly complementary drinks and snacks (snacks weren't great but the drinks were and the bartender was super nice) and relaxed on the terrace. There's a pool, hot tub, laundry room, workout room, and free wifi. Also, the decor is fresh, modern, and spotlessly clean. Wonderful stay!

title: “poor standing but OK for one night”
text:
poor standing but OK for one night - the owner was very nice and helpful but do not expect something greatest at such price.
Anyway, the neighborhood is cool

title: “A great hotel in a convenient location”
text:
This hotel was everything we hoped for. We had a spacious room that was very quiet and had a nice view. It is very convenient to the light rail connections to/from the airport and the monorail transportation to the Space Needle as well as walking distance to the Public Market area. The price was quite reasonable for what we received.
I've seen many complaints about the valet parking fees, but parking in downtown Seattle is expensive everywhere and to be able to take a car out as many times as you want for a single day fee was very convenient.
 The only complaint is that we could have used a mirror outside the bathroom.

title: “Great hotel - Weird staff stuff”
text:
I stayed at the Hotel Monaco years ago and it was great. I've also been to the Kimpton properties with this name in SF and Salt Lake City. My most recent stay had so many weird staff behavior things that I thought I was staying at the Tower of Terror Hotel. But I really like the hotel -- it's very clean and comfortable. The bar/restaurant is great too.
The first encounter was when I went to the elevator after checking in. When I was waiting for the elevator, two housekeeping staff were sitting on the couch next to the elevator and the staff door was open with another person talking to them. So I was witnessing the staff breakroom there on my floor next to the elevator!
