The next odd staff encounter happened when a housekeeper followed me to my room and yelled in bad English asking when I'd be leaving for the day. I told her a time. But then when I went to leave before that time, she chased me to say she didn't realize I was checking out. ok ....
Lastly, I checked out and told the front desk that I needed to check bags. I was late to my conference. They called the bell services and then I waited and waited right in front of the front desk at a chair. Finally, I asked for an update and they called again. I was right in front of them waiting impatiently with my bags looking at my watch and they couldn't help!
The staff need some help with training. Otherwise, this is a top notch hotel. Very clean, great location, awesome perks with wine in the afternoon and coffee in the morning, and a nice bar/restaurant.

title: “Relief when escaping superstorm Sandy in this hotel”
text:
We first stayed in Fairfield Inn two blocks away on 37th st., which lost power and therefore telephone and water in superstorm Sandy. We had been trying to find another hotel, but Marriott Central Reservation stated none available in Manhattan. We walked over to this hotel hoping to find a room. The receptionist said, come back at 1 p.m. Maybe. So we did, He said, sorry, none available. Then we asked, when? Answer maybe at 3 p.m. So we walked out rather unhappy. 2 minutes later he is running after us: "a room is available". This was a fantastic relief after the bad situation in the Fairfield Inn, 
The rooms are much more spacious than those in the Fairfield Inn. Equipped (as usual) with croockery and cutlery. (Nt that much food could be bought on the streets in the aftermath of Sandy.). The hotel is very large, so during breakfast crowds could and did happen. 
Breakfast menu is acceptable with some limitations, no waffles for example and the usual bad coffee characterizing most of these establishments . For 5 o'clock the only thing they provide is a reduction in their booze price. No food, no free drinks.
We stayed in the hotel on miles. Had we wanted to stay for one more day, the price (then) would have been $550 per night (!!!)
In summary, Residence Inn gave us a refuge from Sandy, we are grateful for that. Their attitude towards providing the"freebies" of breakfast and happy hour are on the cheap side

title: “Great Pit Stop for a Weekend”
text: I went to the Men's NCAA Basketball Tournament in Charlotte and this hotel was a short 4 block walk from the Arena. The hotel is also right across the street from the NASCAR Museum. I had a king size room that was clean and comfortable. The wi-fi worked well and the TV was fine. There are lots of hotels in the heart of the city, but this was a great place to stay if you don't mind walking a few blocks to all of the action. The parking is $10 a day, with in and out privileges. All in all, this was a very nice hotel and I wouldn't hesitate to stay again when in Charlotte.

title: “Great stay at the Edison”
text: Stayed at the Edison December 22. Very busy Christmas week. Everyone was very accommodating and welcoming. Bellman took care of our car and bags. Location is excellent to Times Square and Theater District. Rooms are large for NYC hotels. Great rates.

title: “Perfect Choice for Business”
text: As a frequent traveler, I need hotels that not only have comfortable, clean and quiet rooms, but have a friendly and helpful staff. The staff at The Jewel exceeded my expectations, going above and beyond to make sure that my needs were met. For that, I am appreciative and will return for future business stays.

title: “Excellent”
text: Was sorry I was only staying 1 night for business ! Beautiful and comfortable room. Clean and quiet. Nice breakfast spread. Friendly service. Would only stay here on return visit.

title: “5 Stars for Convenience”
text:
This hotel was a great choice and is perfectly situated for touring the city & seeing Broadway shows. The rooms are large and comfortable when compared to a typical Times Square hotel but, the Doubletree itself felt more secure than some of the obscenely large hotels in the area. This was most evident when the surly night-shift doorman checked guests for their room keys before allowing them access to the street-level elevators. Throughout our stay I was surprised that I never had to wait much more than 15 seconds for an elevator after calling for one. The 3rd level lobby elevators take you to your floor where you will find a mere 13 guest rooms each, a luxury in itself.
Our 33rd floor room was very quiet and was what the hotel referred to as an allergy "Pure" room. These rooms have a large, portable HEPA air cleaner and the white-noise it generated while powered-on only added to a good nights sleep. The Hilton "Sweet Dreams" bedding in these rooms also have special mattress and pillow encasements to help reduce dustmite and feather down allergens. All of the allergy-pure rooms are located on the 33rd floor so they're sure to have great views. One disappointment with our room was that it's 2 flatscreen HDTV's did not receive a HD signal... but, who goes to Times Square to watch TV?
Our room was also one of the "Times Square View" rooms that ended with the room number "03." This room really overlooked Father Duffy Square, which is part of what most people refer to as Times Square.(see photos) The best thing about the Duffy Square view room is that it has a 180° view of the city and is entirely surrounded with a curved wall of windows. The room is slightly smaller as a result of this layout but provides one of the most panoramic and romantic views available in Times Square. This room is perfect for couples or a small family and was very reasonably priced when I booked it JUST LESS than one month in advance through the Doubletree website. I guess they were trying to sell-off unused rooms because just a few days after getting my very low rate, the hotel was sold out. Don't forget that Doubletree offers a 10% discount if you have AAA.
Note: The "real" Times Square view rooms end with the room number "01" but, have less windows. For New Year's Eve and the ball drop, this room cannot be beat.
We didn't eat at the hotel's restaurant but I did stop by after hours to check it out. It was nicely decorated and appeared to have a fairly big spread for breakfast. For lunch or dinner I suggest heading west to the 300 block of 46th Street, just west of 8th Avenue. There are a couple dozen nice, "real" New York City restaurants to choose from. The hotel's business center was easy to use and had no waiting line. For a $12 fee I used the center to print boarding passes, prepay checked baggage, and upgrade our seats in advance of the flight home... all of which would have cost at least $100 more at the airport.
The car service we used to and from the airport provided curbside service at the hotel's front door. The doorman assisted us each time even clearing a us path through the crowd to our car when departing. Adjacent the hotel's entrance you'll find an enclosed Wachovia Bank ATM as well as an entrance to a subway station. There's a convenience store about 6 storefronts north of the hotel on 7th Ave., and the Times Square Information Center is 2 doors south.
Overall, I'd have to say that the front desk staff and lobby baggage handlers were very helpful and friendly. The concierge was just average, and who cares if the young man working at the lobby's bar was less than interested in serving beverages. This is one of the few hotels in Times Square that provides an in-room refrigerator (and microwave), and it's nice to have a refreshment in your room while enjoying the view. This is NOT one of New York's trendiest or most luxurious places to stay but it is clean, secure, nicely appointed and reasonably priced. If the hotels in Times Square were rewarded stars for convenience, this one would surely get 5.

title: “Excellent staff but slightly inconvenient location”
text: We stayed at this hotel for two nights before heading up into the mountains. All staff within the hotel were excellent - I cannot give them enough praise! They were polite, helpful and really friendly. When we enquired about what to do within the city they provided loads of information. The rooms are very nice - large, clean and very comfortable and the coffee maker within the room is another nice touch. I think the hotel recognise the fact they are a little out of the way by providing a free shuttle service which is a major bonus. However, there are shops nearby and Caitlins (think I've spelt that correct) is fabulous for breakfast and a two minute walk away. We had a hire car so the complimentary car parking was great but I don't understand why a hotel does not provide free internet as standard nowadays. Free internet is available in the reception area but it is a bit of a pain hanging around the lobby! Overall this is a really nice hotel, and it's a shame it's not conveniently located a bit closer to the city centre. That said though I wouldn't hesitate staying here again if I returned to Denver.

title: “Very good price/quality relation”
text: Very nice hotel, with strong price/quality relation. Big, comfortable an clean room with also very clean bathroom. Great location, 5 minutes walk to times square. In my measure, a 4 star hotel.

title: “Great”
text: I am writing this review from the Majestic and can honestly say that this is by far the nicest $129 a night hotel I hve ever stayed in. The rooms are very quiet and nicely decorated. The bathroom is huge and well appointed, the bed is glorious! My only complaint is that there are no glass glasses. The breakfast area was a little conjested this morning but was just loading up a tray to bring back to the room, no big deal. The location is great but we are walkers and don't mind the 10 minute walk to the MM.

title: “Average Stay at The Time”
text:
I was relatively disappointed with our stay at The Time July 21-23 weekend. The room was nice, but there wasn't enough space to put clothes - no drawers! Also, there was no where to sit, other than a single well worn desk chair and the bed. The room had space for a couple of small swivel club chairs. The shower room was fine. My disappointment was that there was nothing outstanding about this experience. When I stay at a boutique hotel, I expect a couple of outstanding things. 
Here are a few observations: When we booked (a couple of months ago) we were not made aware of renovations in the hotel (restaurant was down). Maid service was OK (bed made, bathroom tidied), but the room wasn't thoroughly cleaned, for example dirty glasses left on the desk. And the jelly beans weren't replenished! The TV was amazing (gigantic flat panel) but we had to shake the cords around to get it to work (electrician came and he did same!) We called down for wine glasses and they brought up to totally different sized glasses! It's all in the details. All in all, I probably won't stay there again, or even recommend it. It just fell short of my expectations!

title: “Hoped for more.”
text:
The Campton Place is clearly a great property, but we booked a last-minute, "low" rate and had an accordingly quite small, low-floor room with no view. Perhaps we should have asked what it would cost to upgrade.
It's a city hotel, so one expects small rooms and high prices. Perhaps if the public spaces were larger or more inviting, we would have felt happier with our choice. With hindsight, I may have preferred a nearby hotel in the 175-200 range.
On the plus side, the flowers in the (small) lobby were lovely. Staff was pleasant. The free, semi-private business rooms were a good amenity. The California-king bed was a dream. The decor was tasteful... The "feel" of the hotel is right on. Despite feeling disappointed with the value for money, I was always happy to return there in the evening. It's on the quiet side of Union Square, so it felt like a sanctuary.
I would only recommend this property to people who are willing to pay rack rate and demand a great room for it.

title: “Beds are hard”
text:
The hotel is a bit hard to get to – the front faces away from Colorado avenue, in fact you must turn right onto cherry creek drive then turn right into the hotel (if you’re heading north on Colorado)
I like a clean, quiet, comfortable room, with some amenities nearby (restaurants, etc). this hotel fit everything except for a few items:
Number one – the bed was way too hard. It has a control to make it softer, but didn’t seem to work. Unfortunately because the bed was so hard, I doubt I'll stay here again, which is unfortunate because the hotel does have several things that I did like.
There’s construction going on and it’s a “must” to have your car valet parked as there’s no parking. This caused us some concern as we just had our jeep restored. We were assured that it would be parked in covered and secure parking, however when we were walking to Mike’s camera, we could see our jeep sitting on the street (didn’t sit well with us)
There’s a restaurant on-site, it’s not bad, has a limited menu, though. No lunch and room service is only from 5pm – 10 pm. The morning breakfast buffet is outrageously priced ($12.95 per person). Didn’t stop by to see if they had anything other than the buffet. 
There are a few places within walking distance, Panera Bread, a Cafe Rio Mexican Grill and a Garbanzo Mediterranean Grill. We didn’t bother with anything other than the Panera Bread, because the menu at the other places just didn’t seem right.
To get to the Panera Bread, however, you have to walk in the path of cars coming into the hotel. 
We did find a good Chinese restaurant that delivered. Golden Shanghai, www.goldenshanghai-denver.com

title: “We had a great experience at the Carlton Hotel and would recommend to everyone!”
text: We went to the Carlton Hotel in NYC not knowing what to expect and was so blown away with everything it had to offer. The hotel itself is beautiful with a great sense of elegance, wonderful example of crown moldings in the halls and in the rooms. The room was quiet and peaceful, the king bed was so comfortable we wanted to sleep the day away. The staff gave great service with a friendly smile everyday with good directions to food and arts. We have been back for a week and I still am talking about it to someone everyday. It made our stay in NYC memorable and the best vacation I have taken in years. I recommend The Carlton Hotel in NYC to everyone that wants a beautiful designed boutique hotel that is well located in heart of Manhattan.

title: “five stars in a three star hotel”
text: Sofitel, and Palomar were booked so checked into the Latham for a weekend in Philly. Art fair going on in the Park just one block away, and Rittenhouse was happening with sidewalk traffic until early in the morning. Hotel staff very knowledgeable about the area, and very helpful. Recent renovations and upgrades, have made them part of Preferred Boutique hotels and the staff is very proud of it. Room on the larger size for a Boutique, with full size closet , in room safe, and plenty of dresser draws to put things away. Bathroom is marbled with a deep sink, and plenty of counter space for amenities. Shower head is energy saving, so dont expect a blast of water, but plenty of hot water available. Beds extremely comfortable, without spreads , so none of the hotel hebe jebees. Plenty of towels, ironing board in closet, stocked mini bar, good lighting on desk so perfect for business travel. One suggestion to the hotel is add a light in the closet.

title: “Historic and hospitable Willard Hotel in Washington, DC”
text: I recently took a group to the Willard Hotel and was overwhelmed by their group sales and concerige services departments. From the first point of contact until we checked out, my group was catered to completely. On severel days guests were brought afternoon snacks compliments of the hotel. It is very restful and relaxing once inside and away from the buzz of DC. The location allows walks to the historic Mall, restaurants and museums on neighboring blocks. Definitely worth the price.

title: “back again!!!”
text:
I have been many times to this hotel and I am on my way back again!!! I was just there in may with a few girls for a weekend and the service was outstanding!!! The concierge managed to get us into our favourite place for dinner even though reservations there are usually a month or 2 in advance.
I love the fact that it is so central to everything and yet being across from the park is like an oasis in the city. My spouse has never been to this hotel (usually go with the girls on shopping trips) and I am excited that he is finally going to experience staying there himself. I have been telling him for years that its the ONLY hotel to stay at in the city!!!
See you in August!!!

title: “don't do it”
text:
This was the last stop on my summer holiday this year and I was very nervous after reading the reviews here. It was worse than I could ever have thought possible.
The staff at check in were incredibly rude and totally unhelpful.
To my horror we were staying in the last tower right at the back looking out on to the public car park. I was less than impressed with the security aspect of it, the doors to the tower are permently open!
The room was pitch black when I opened the door so I found my way to the curtains and for a second was pleased with the veiw until the stench hit me. It was an overpowering smell of damp. I thought maybe it just needed to be aired so I didn't complain.
We had arrived late after a long drive so we just had a quick look around before we went to the " restuarant" for dinner. The queue of people getting in to cabs should have been a warning to us. There were including us 10 people in the room and we were told that if we wanted to sit outside we would have to wait as there was a rush on!!!! 
So we said inside was fine, with a huge sigh the hostess pointed at a table. The service was some of the worst I have ever had. The menu was interesting to say the least, I chose the angel hair pasta because it was the least vile thing there. If you like your pasta in huge clumps with mouldy cheese added to it before it gets to you, then this is the place for you. The waitress came back for our bill which came to 40 odd dollars saw the hundred dollar note and had the cheek to ask if we wanted change!!!
The walk back to our hell hole was when I really started to hate the place, there are no lights unless the people in the little houses leave their lights on so you have to walk on an uneven tarmac road in the pitch black.
The smell got worse in our room with the result that we had to keep spraying perfume to mask it. We didn't bother complaining after having witnessed the check in staff and those in the cafe, we just stayed out as much as possible.
I would never stay in that dump again as long a I live for any amount of money. The whole place needs to be knocked down and rebuilt. It is filthy, old, dingy and disgusting. If you don't mind having to wear shoes all the time and using bottled water to clean your teeth and rusting taps and mouldy walls and celings don't bother you then this is the place for you.

title: “Lovely, lovely, lovely”
text:
My girlfiends and I spent one night at the Biltmore on Memorial Day weekend after days spent hiking in Sedona. What a wonderful place to get cleaned up! The buildings and landscaping is beautiful! We had a resort room with a balcony which overlooked the small parking lot in the rear but also the lovely Camel Mountains. Our room was clean and the bathroom was huge enough to handle three women, no problem. The beds are luscious, pillow top, down everything, crisp clean sheets. 
We headed to the Paradise Pool, there are eight pools on the property, as well as hot tubs. Knowing the history of the hotel I had visions of Old Hollywood Glamour. Unfortunately the Paradise Pool was more like Spring Break, very crowded, loud rock music playing and a bunch of TVs playing in the private cabanas that open up to the pool area. There is a bar a water slide. We hit the water slide and then headed over to the more serene Catlina Pool, that provided more of what I had expected. 
For dinner we checked in with the Concierge to ask about Southwest food in the area. HIs response was almost robotic and the directions to the restaraunt were already printed out on cards. We felt that the Hotel was probably getting kickbacks from the place so we asked the Valet guys instead and they were able to recommend some local, authentic places. The Valet guys were helpfull and friendly, I recommend talking to them. 
When we returned from dinner we had the great pleasure of finding a complimentary s'mores buffet set up around a camp fire with large Adirondack Chairs. There were sticks provided for the raosting and also multiple beverages. It was magical, the Hotel and grounds look particularly gorgeousl at night. A movie was being shown to kids above the pool so they could float and watch. The historical tour is only available on certain days of the week. There is printed material available but it mostly just lists the owners. We enjoyed strolling around the building looking at al the old potographs and exploring the ballrooms. 
 We slept like babies and awoke to our ordered room service breakfast promptly delivered and hot. We ate on the balcony and watched the sunrise. On the way out I stopped at The Cafe to pick up some food for my flight home. The line tok a very long time. Other than the mild inconveniences everyone was friendly and the Biltmore provided activites and serentiy. And we didn't even try the spa! Some people there looked bored, maybe they go to places like that all the time...I was thrilled to be in a historical and beautiful setting. Go, go, go!

title: “Love this Inn!”
text: The manager is a lovely english gentleman! Very helpful staff and really the most lovely Inn ever. We were there for a game at Camden Yards and loved taking the water taxi to the Inner Harbor. We were sorry when we got home to read about Ft McHenry. We should have made it a point to go there. Good reason to go back though! I will stay at Henderson's Wharf in a heart beat!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Thanks, We loved, loved the breakfast! So much attention to detail!!!!!!!!!

title: “Hotel Commonwealth Was Great!”
text: Recently, my daughter, a Boston University student, needed surgery. We lived at Hotel Commonwealth for a recuperative, post-surgery week and it could not have been better. They met us at the door with a wheelchair when we returned from the hospital; they were friendly, gracious and accommodating to our many guests; and they even sent someone to pick up dinner for us in downtown Boston when my daughter was craving gluten-free pasta. Amazing.

title: “Absolutely Wonderful!”
text: This hotel is truly wonderful--from the service to the rooms, our stay was simply exquisite. However, if you are looking for a traditional hotel room, this may not be the place for you. Hotel1000 is truly modern--and of course, our favorite thing being the bathroom that is separated by a huge glass wall. The option of an automatic screen sliding down for privacy if sharing with a friend. My boyfriend absolutely loved the water that filled the tub from the ceiling! The rooms are smaller than a lot of hotel rooms we've stayed at, but was worth every penny. Every amenity was met, from the plasma, internet service, robes, linens as well as the cute bar downstairs--it made our stay in Seattle a wonderful one! I will definitely be back!

title: “Amazing time”
text: I had a Wonderful time in newyork and at the hotel. The staff was amazing and great help.I am actually gonna be coming back in nov and Im hoping to stay the manhatten again.

title: “provides exactly what is needed”
text: we arrived at the lexington rather anxious having read the recent reviews..This hotel provides clean basic accomodation. Our room was just about big enough but had everything we needed. House keeping is a wee bit haphazard. first night we didnt have a duvet but when we rang reception a duvet was quickly delivered. The second day we didnt have hand towels but the next day we did...This hotel is very central with friendly reception and bar staff.michael and valentina you were super friendly and helpful..I certainly would use the lexington again as it is vey central to everything and it is priced to suit.

title: “About what you'd expect from an airport hotel”
text:
This was my first time seeing or staying at this hotel. I have to say I was pretty shocked upon pulling up in the parking lot...the hotel could best be called orange. WOW. I was a little nervous about what the inside would be like, but was pleasantly surprised. It had typical decor, amenities and rooms. 
I stay at Red Lion hotels pretty often and have found there to be a range of what they offer. I would say this one falls right in the middle. There were no glaring flaws (carpets were clean, room was average size, decor was farily modern) or amazing features (parking was outside, view was parking lot). 
We didn't eat at the restaurant which was in the parking lot, outside the hotel, so I can't weigh in on that. There was very little plane noise throughout the night, but I could hear some in the morning. But considering that this hotel is literally across the street from the airport, so that's to be expected. I was a little disapointed that I was charged $10 for outdoor, self parking. Perhaps this is an airport hotel standard.
All in all, it was about what I would expect from an airport hotel...close, convenient, and reasonably priced.

title: “Needs some work”
text:
We were visiting Philadelphia to tour Independence Hall and the Liberty Bell on July 1, 2006. Center City Philadelphia is nice and the tour was awesome. If you're ever in Philadelphia you have to get a cheese steak from Tony Luke's. It was awesome. There were a lot of local residents that were patronizing Tony Luke's, which is always a good sign for me.
Now, back to the hotel. I have stayed in different Marriott properties. This one was disappointing. We only stayed one night. My children and I didn't take a shower or bath that night. We waited until we got home the next day because the tub was in such bad shape. Some of the enamel had come off the tub where the drain was located and was rusting. There was also some sort of buildup on the other end of the tub that left a filmy residue. I didn't want to bathe in such a horrible tub. 
The breakfast was also mediocre. They served the typical continental breakfast with pastries, cereal, juice, and two waffle makers. I suppose I have been spoiled by Baymont Inn Kissimmee and Residence Inn Elizabeth City. Both hotels served not only the usual continental breakfast items, but hot items as well, like eggs and sausge. The morning we ate breakfast at the Fairfield Inn, they had to shut down one of the waffle makers because their circuits kept overloading. When this happened the juice machine didn't work. 
The wonderful staff at the Fairfield Inn Philadelphia Airport were awesome but could not make up for the obvious neglect that Marriott has shown this hotel.
This was my first stay at Fairfield Inn and my last. Marriott should put more time and money into repairing the properties that need it.

title: “First Rate”
text: Surprisingly fine hotel. Great location near the airport, only 5 minute ride by hotel bus service. Public areas are spacious and attractive. Very nice outdoor patio complete with pool, hot tub and cabanas. Super friendly and helpful staff. Good food at standard hotels prices (a little expensive), but quite good. As good a hotel as many higher rated and more expensive ones. Everything was new and spotless. Excellent value. Oddly, the only exception was the concierge who could definitely improve his people skills.

title: “Better than city centre.”
text:
Our flight arrived early and we took a bus from the airport to the hotel. Approx. 40 minutes. The Hotel had our resurvation and stored our bags until the room was ready at 3:00p.m. We walked uphill to the north several blocks turned left and came upon a beutiful lookout over the ciry and the bay. It was a warm and sunny autumn day and we spent over and hour enjoying the view and walking through into the upland housing area. It was the perfect way to start our 5 days in Seattle. 
The Hotel staff were extra helpful throughout our stay. The rooms were clean. I would definitely stay there again but not in the summer as there is no air conditioning. Great restaurants within the surrounding 2 block. For lunch the metropolitan grocery strore has some great soup and sand. The transit system in Seattle works really well. We found Seattle to be one of the friendliest places we have ever been.

title: “A hotel that's good for your conscious”
text:
If you are concerned about saving the planet and you recycle - this hotel will make you feel good about your stay in Seattle. Room lights are activated with your door key, shower water is less than full volume when it comes out of the spicket, and you have to request to have new sheets and towels daily. The only time we felt inconvenienced by the "green" atmosphere is when one of us had to go to the bathroom in the middle of the night and couldn't turn on the bathroom lights without lighting up the whole room. Like I said, all lights are activated at once by your hotel key. 
While you will feel green at your contribution to the planet, this hotel will take your greenbacks by charging you $10 a day for wireless service, $34 a day to park your car and way too much money to eat in the hotel. 
The upside is that the location enabled us to walk everywhere -- oh yeah, and we saved electricity and water.

title: “Great stay!”
text: I would recommend anyone to the Shoreham, I had a great stay! One thing that definitely caught my attention was the service at the front desk. When you get there, make sure you ask for Henry, he was very helpful and very courteous. Henry was there for me whenever I needed anything and was very patient with me. Also, the complimentary glass of champange at check in was a plus! I will deffinitly book again with Shoreham.

title: “Absolutely Loved This Hotel!”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Nine Zero in July, 2006, with our 2 small kids, aged 18 months and 3 and a half years. From the moment we arrived, to the time we left, the staff at the Nine Zero went out of their way to make us feel like valued customers. We had a lovely room with 2 Queen-sized beds, and a huge bathroom. We often stay at Kimpton Hotels around the US, so we belong to their customer loyalty program. As a result, the first night, we were greeted with chocolate truffles, strawberries, and a huge bottle of designer water. And in the evening, the complimentary wine hour can't be beat. I had also asked for a room on an upper floor, which we were given. All in all a terrific experience! 
Location: right in the heart of things in Boston, a short walk to Boston Common (literally right across the street) and the financial district. Close to good shopping, and the acquarium, which is amazing. I highly recommend this hotel to anyone who wants a nice stay in Boston. We are very discriminating travellers, and we were very impressed.

title: “very clean”
text: we had bought our room off of hotwire & was afraid of the price but when we arrived it was very clean & smelled clean, the staff went out of their way to accomadate us. The breakfast could have been better, but we were just passing through going to California to work, so it took care of our needs, it was very quite & there were a lot of places to eat nearby, within walking distance.

title: “We enjoyed our stay tremendously”
text: We stayed at the Embassy Suites Downtown October 14th - 18th. I had read were people complained about the noise from the lobby and from the road, but we were on the 9th floor and did not notice any of these. Managers reception in the evening was great as was the morning breakfast buffet. The reception area was rather cool but we just grabbed a light jacket. The staff was super freindly and the evening doorman is the best. He would greet us at night "How's the family this evening." My son thought he was the greatest. We enjoyed our stay and it was even better with my company picking up the tab while I was at a conference while the wife and son explored Chicago. It was close to the bus lines and about 6 blocks from the "El" trains. I highly recommend it.

title: “Disappointed”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Surfer Beach Hotel for a weekend getaway. I booked the "junior suite" because we enjoy having the space. The description in Expedia for the junior suite said "...the balcony offers beach/ocean view....". The room given to us was Room 419 which was the corner of the "L" shape building. There were no balcony (other than if you open the front door and stand in the hallway. The extra room only had a sofa bed which would be nice for family with kids and had nothing else. The TV was in the bedroom so if you were sitting on the couch, you would not be able to watch TV. There were 2 TV's in the room, (which was odd) one mount to the wall which wasn't working and one standing on the cabinet which worked but none of the two remote worked for the TV. I noticed all the other "regular" rooms had a balcony and they all faced the ocean but we got the corner "suite" with no balcony or ocean view but we paid for it. 
The hotel was an older hotel but you can tell it was renovated which I knew when I booked it. It was at a great location and we enjoyed the sunset...standing in the hallway, at the end of the building, near someone's window. Because of how the rooms were situated, people do walk by your window to get to their rooms. We had people walking by and talking loud, late in the night and early in the morning. There was no air condition and we had the windows open for air but had to shut them because of the noise (music, people talking). Even though the king-size bed was comfortable, my husband and I didn't get a good night sleep. 
Also the free internet had very poor signal. We were not able to use the wifi at all during our stay. We would not return to the Surfer Beach Hotel.

title: “It was OK”
text: It wasn't a bad place for the price. Parking was a little strange. They billed the wrong credit card. Not a huge deal. The room was clean. Very small. We would stay again.

title: “Convenient for Business”
text:
I recently spent 3-nights for a trade show. I always enjoy booking with Hilton because you come to expect a certain level of quality and cleanliness. This room was impeccably clean and the service was very good. Housekeeping staff was exceptionally friendly on the 8th floor. I put this in for any managers scanning the reviews (hahaha). Some of the doors were showing their age and the bathroom tub could use an upgrade; however, the refresh of the overall space makes this hotel more than comfortable. All of the bathroom fixtures and tiles were newer. Great make-up job!! You also get free (incl. in the price) internet which is quickly becoming an industry standard, as it should.
Walking over to the SL1 bus for the trade show was very practical, 15-minute walk, but practical. The hotel is also willing to shuttle you. The bus is free making it a great alternative to getting a car. This saves you a significant amount of coin in Boston. Getting back at night is a little tricky. Cabs run about $20-$30 from downtown. Still less expensive than parking both downtown and at the hotel.
I find Boston hotel rates to be astronomical on the whole, I guess that is just the Boston economy and good old supply and demand. Makes me want to toss the tea sometimes! Bad joke. If going back for a show, I would consider the Seaport hotel. It is located right in front of the convention center. This is simply for practical reasons. Nothing bad to say about the Hilton Boston Logan.

title: “JAX MICROTEL”
text: My family and I stayed at the Microtel near the airport and the location is unbeatable for getting to the airport. The staff was nice although most of the people we came across at the desk didn't seem happy but for the value, it couldn't be beat. My only complaint and it's not really a complaint was that the beds were too soft and that you seem to sink into the bed. But that was just me my family slept very well and were truly rested. Breakfast could have contained a better selection, but that doesn't affect my opinion of the facility. If I had to stay in Jacksonville again, I would definitely stay at the Microtel, big hotel comfort, but at a truly reasonable price.

title: “Novotel made my stay quite enjoyable”
text:
I spent a great amount of time researching hotels in the Times Square area and after reading the reviews on here I decided go go with the Novotel for a number of reasons. One was the proximity to all areas in Manhattan that we needed to get to by walking. 
I made the reservation through Expedia and got a very good rate by pre-paying the entire amount 3 weeks before our trip. Anyway, we arrived on Saturday afternoon and were given a room on the 31st floor with a view of the river and a lot of buildings. Now this of course was not what I had envisioned when I made my reservation. I really wanted the Times Square view. It wasn't really for myself because I've been to NYC on many occasions, but it was my girlfriend's birthday and I knew that having that view would be very exciting for her. So after we got to the room, I immediately went back downstairs to the front desk and explained to them my situation. The front desk clerk wasted no time in switching our location from the riverside view on the 31st floor to the Times Square view on the 27th floor. There was no hassle or problems whatsoever and she appeared very happy in being able to accommodate my request. After we got to our room, the view that we had from that location was INCREDIBLE!!!!! I couldn't have asked for better. There was only one thing that was somewhat irritating and that was having to catch an elevator from the street to the lobby and vice versa. But other than that, everything was good.
The room was somewhat small, but very cozy and clean. We had a great selection of TV channels as well. We didn't spend a great amount of time in the room however. We were literally steps away from the Broadway Theatre where we saw The Color Purple on Saturday night and 1 block up from Caroline's Comedy Club where we had made reservations for on Sunday evening. All the staff at the hotel were very pleasant from the security guards to the front desk manager. We had a very exciting time and I most definitely would come back and also refer friends and family to the Novotel for future trips to NYC.

title: “Comfortable Stay in Downtown San Jose”
text: I stayed 3 nights at The Fairmont San Jose. The hotel is located in the heart of downtown San Jose, and is within walking distance to a number of locations. The hotel lobby is beautiful, and the staff was friendly and attentive. The king sized rooms are quite large and spacious, and I slept comfortably -- I really liked how the bed was accompanied with pillows of different firmness levels -- very nice touch! If you sign up for the Fairmont President's Club (free to join) you get complimentary WiFi during your stay, otherwise you pay a fee for internet usage. A couple of things I did not like: Parking was outrageously expensive -- $26 a day! I stayed in Room 1202, and the bathroom sink was clogged, and the shower alternated between scalding hot and freezing cold water while showering....it was extremely uncomfortable! If it wasn't for those 3 complaints I'd give a 5 star rating, but unfortunately that wasn't the case.

title: “Excellent Everything”
text:
I have found this hotel the best i've stayed at for a long time, and for someone who's usually ultra fussy, that says a lot. I'm actually surprised it doesn't have a significantly higher ranking. having stayed here 3 times, i absolutely love the decor, the rooms are mighty big, and the heavenly bed, well it's REALLy heavenly. so much so that me and my friend alwys try to stay here whenever we come up to nY. the only thing going against it are it's high rates. so far i've been booking thru hotwire/priceline type of websites. very clean, nice decor, service is pretty good, excellent location.
now i just gotta find a good price again so i can stay here for my upcoming visit to NYC.

title: “Good hotel”
text: I have read several reviews talking about breakfast. I agree that some full service Holiday Inns will give you either free points or breakfast and this does not. I will always take the free breakfast. I stay often enough points don't matter. But I've been coming to Chicago twice a year, for three days a week or more, for 4 years. This is the only hotel I stay at. Clean rooms, GREAT service. It is pricey, but well worth it. And if your work is paying for it, who cares?

title: “terrific place”
text:
My husband, daughter (18), her friend (21) and I stayed in 2 rooms in the Hyatt over a weekend. I asked that the rooms be on the same floor but made no other request. When we arrived, we were told that the rooms were connecting. Fantastic!
The Proximity to Grand Central is really convenient. Not only can you access transportation but the shopping and food court were great. 
The shops on 5th are within easy walking distance as is the theater district although it is further away. Central Park is also within walking distance, especially if you stroll down 5th Ave. 
The complaints I saw on this site were not a problem for us. For example, our bathroom had a huge vanity for our stuff. The bathroom was very clean. Someone had complained about employee attitude, particularly at the check in desk. Our staff member was cheery and professional. 
 The room was spacious, comfortable and quiet. I didn't hear a peep even from my daughter and her friend next door! The only thing I would have liked was a view but in NYC, I didn't expect it. 
There's a coffee bar in the lobby that sells delicious muffins, fruit and Starbuck's coffee every morning. 
I would highly recommend Jacks for dinner before the theater. It's just off Broadway so you are very close to all the theaters (we learned that traffic before the 8 pm shows is a disaster!). They have a tapas menu and regular entrees all of which were excellent, arrived right away and were reasonably priced. We went there on the advice of the Hyatt concierge who also sent us to SoHo for shopping (another good idea!)

title: “best vacation stay ever !!”
text:
my wife and i recently celebrated our wedding anniversary at the comfort suites-alamo/riverwalk..from the moment we walked into the registration desk area and were very graciously greeted by the general manager, ray velazquez, we knew that we would be treated well during our stay..and treated well we were..ray was very impressive, impeccably-dressed, well-spoken and anxious to satisfy our needs..during our stay it was obvious that his attitude to please and courteous manner trickled down to his staff. we had no surprises or issues during our enitre stay (4 nights)..
as soon as we entered the suite we were very impressed . it had everything that we could possibly need to be comfortable during our stay.; two very, very comfortable beds, a large flat screen tv, a desk, sofa, fridge and micro-wave..the suite decor was well-appointed and color co-ordinated with lamps, pictures and other niceities..very nice !!
the inn is located several blocks from the alamo, an easy walk. the inn also had a courtesy van that we used everyday. the van dropped us off at either the alamo or riverwalk areas and picked us up when we were ready to return to the inn..just in time for the manager's wine and cheese affair every evening from 5 to 7 pm where we were pampered by georgia and della..every night there were abundant snacks and featured hors d'ourves and, of course, wine and beer..quite a satisfying way to end the day and/or start the evening..
we were also treated to an excellent hot breakfast buffet every morning with a different featured item each day and plenty of juices, coffee, pastries, muffins, bagles, cereals, etc.. and, georgia was there to help get our days off to a great start !
the city of san antonio was very impressive as well.. it was very well laid out, easy to get around in, lots of sites to see. the people were extremely courteous and it was clean. we saw no trash laying around and no panhandlers to harrass us.. several times, while we waited for a trolley or bus, people would come up to us to inqure as to whether we needed any assistance in finding our way around. we were quite impressed by their concern for us.
while at the inn we met one of the owners, sherry, who was warm and friendly. it was obvious that she and her entire staff were caring and courteous. .she introduced herself and asked how we were enjoying our stay. we had to truthfully say that we were being treated so well that we were sad to have to leave. .but we did reluctantly leave to return home and talk about the wonderful time we had at the comfort suites-san antonio.
we definitely recommend staying here-you will not be disappointed...

title: “Great hotel in a not so great neighborhood”
text: My mother and I stayed at Hotel Diva for a shopping weekend in SF. As everyone knows, SF has good areas and bad areas right next to each other. Hotel Diva is in a good location in terms of proximity to shopping and tourist areas but is very close to some blocks that you don't want to walk around at night, although most tourists do. The hotel itself is wonderful, with great rooms, a funky fun atmosphere, and helpful staff. I would stay there again, which is why I gave it 4 stars instead of 3.

title: “Funky but noisy”
text:
I recently stayed at the Ace for 2 nights when in NY on business. I had been pretty excited about ACE having a hotel in NY because I'd stayed at their hotels in Seattle and Portland and very much enjoyed both.
There are a lot of things to like about this hotel if you enjoy alternative, hipster decor. It is a very cool place although I can't help feeling as though some women might find it a bit too masculine in character.
When you travel on business you still don't like to feel like you're getting reamed every which way so it's great the hotel has free internet and breakfast. Overall the staff are friendly and in line with the hipster vibe of the place.
My biggest complaint was the noise. I stayed 2 nights and as it was mild, the first night I had the window open. No problems as my room faced the courtyard. The second night however an adjacent air conditioning unit (not from a room - this was like an aeroplane) was on and made an enormous racket. Even with windows closed I struggled to sleep. As it was day 2 and my stuff was unpacked moving room was not practical so I unfortunately had to put up.
My complaint at the front desk was met with a typical hipster-like shrug and it did definitely leave me with a bad taste having not slept and then having to front up to all day meetings.
So - worth checking out but choose your room carefully and don't expect any sympathy if things aren't perfect.

title: “Location good, everything else bad!”
text: I am normally very satisfied with Holiday Inns but this is an exception! The hotel is well located but has no other points in its favour. Reception staff were rude and unhelpful, we were originally allocated a room which was occupied when we entered and when we returmed to reception we were clearly regarded as an inconvenience. Noise from traffic, the railway line, the nearby airport and the naval air station is very intrusive. Rooms are in need of updating, car parking is scandalously expensive and many rooms are a long way from reception and other facilities. A hotel to avoid and one which the Holiday Inn chain should be ashamed to be associated with!

title: “We'll Be Back!!!!”
text: This was a business trip; therefore, our stay was short but VERY enjoyable. The Magnolia is truly a hotel that we will return to when we have more time.

title: “excellent and exceptional.”
text:
Well kept place, perfect location, and the staff are exceptional !!! 
We are here for a week, and I have to say this is one of the highest levels of service I have experienced in any hotel anywhere. pricy and good. Good wifi. fast room service.

title: “Believe It, It's True. The Orchard Is Fantastic.”
text:
My Wife and I stayed at the Orchard from the 17-25th March 2005. We picked the Orchard following the reviews on this website. Our local travel agent didn't list the hotel, so we booked direct. From the first moment we walked in I was confident we had made the right choice. Many people on this site have already said many wonderful things about the hotel. All I can say is believe every good word you read, It's all true. I am struggling to find a fault to mention. The staff are all wonderful and always had time to help with all manner of stupid question I was asking! 
We chose a King Suite, which for the money, was an absolute bargain (£150 per night). The room was huge, we could have slept a family of four and still had room to spare. The room was extremely clean and everything always worked. The housekeeping was extremely efficient and we always returned to find the room in perfect condition. 
My wife and I are normal people who wanted a nice hotel to spend our holiday. By using Trip Advisor we have found a gem of a hotel which our travel agent doesn't even list. More fool them, this is a wonderful hotel. If you want to stay in SF, don't go anywhere else. Believe what you read.
It's a great hotel.

title: “Great bed! Nice amenities.”
text: I liked this property. The place was clean and our room was well equipped. One note, the walls seemed very thin. The only downfall for us was the location. We were very far from "downtown" Seattle and were relient on taxis to get back to the great food and nightlife we were looking for. The beds were very comfy though and there was a great mini kitchen. All in all, the property was fine. Parking cost us $15, but I felt good about the garage. We were only 3 blocks from the Key Arena and the space needle, which if that is what you want to go to Seattle for, the its perfect. We were more interested in spending time in downtown, but other than that, its a nice hotel.

title: “Very special hotel”
text:
My husband and I were in San Francisco on vacation and stayed at the Campton Place for five nights in May 2005. We are seasoned travelers, both for liesure and work, and have stayed at some world class hotels. The Campton Place is definitely right up there with best in class, but it stands out even among those hotels because the service was so exceptional. We felt completely at home there and by the time we left were on a first name basis with the restaurant staff and the bell hops. Yonas, a doorman/valet, is just an incredibly nice and pleasant person and gave us great recommendations and information on where to go to dinner, sightseeing, etc. Thanks, Yonas!
It´s the little touches that really matter in distinguishing one world class hotel from another, and the Campton Place has it!

title: “Friendly, helpful staff”
text:
We've been here twice, and the staff is absolutely the best thing about this place. They are extremely friendly and helpful. We first stayed here while closing on our new house. They accommodated us with late checkout on our last day so that our pets could stay at the hotel rather than be at the house during the move-in, which was great. When it appeared we were going to miss even the extended deadline, I called and was told, "Don't worry about it." 
The rooms have the amenities you'd expect at this price point. (Although no hand lotion.) The bathroom is on the smallish side and the fittings are showing some wear. 
I see some reviewers have complained that rooms were dirty, and that has not been my experience on either visit. The TV in our room swiveled from bedroom to living room just fine. 
The location is great if you have a car -- plenty of restaurants within 5-10 minutes. It's true that there's not much within walking distance. I think you'd be safe walking to American Airlines Center and back for an event, especially in a group, but I can understand why it might *feel* unsafe to someone from out-of-town. There's not much along that walk that's open at night. 
The hotel sits on Harry Hines, which has five lanes. (or maybe six) If you're troubled by street noise, ask for a room away from the road. 
My biggest complaint is that the wifi is *very* slow.

title: “nice hotel”
text:
family of 4 with 2 teenage girls stayed in august 2010 for 5 nights.
hotel near Montgomery BART so easy to get to and from airport. one of the reasons we picked it.
Near shopping area of union square. bit of a walk to north san fran pier 39 etc.
room was quite small for a family of 4 with teenage girls.
on floor 3 overlooking vermehr place. sleep was interrupted every night due to trash collection at 4 a.m. plus some vagrants looking through bins.
room and hotel was very clean.
free coffee every morning - which could be collected outside of first floor restaurant.
didn't try food at hotel so can't comment however the restaurant looked very nice,
good location for south of city - easy access to open top bus tour (to golden gate etc.) also easy for china town, shops.
I would stay here again but would need a bigger room for 4.

title: “New menu and always good”
text: The value, comfort and location of the Magnolia Hotel Houston continues to be my favorite downtown location. Within walking distance to Astros Baseball games. The menu is updated and the food was great. Sign up for email specials and you'll get the best room rates and upgrades.

title: “New England tour;”
text:
We stayed the Hilton Downtown for 2 nights as part of a self drive tour booked from the UK. We picked up our hire car from Logan International airport and drove to the hilton without any problems. Valet parking only. The hilton is in a good area for access to sight seeing, the trolley tours are only 5 min walk as is quincey maket. ( if you want the shopping malls, prudential etc then maybe not the best location for this).
The hotel did have good customer service but felt 'forced' sometimes unnatural !. The rooms were well presented and clean, we stayed on the nineth floor.
We had breakfast in the hotel resturant once and it was good. We had a drink in the bar once and found the 'background' musc too loud, you couldn't talk so we left. I guess the bar is catering for after work drinks with an upbeat vibe rather than than a relaxing bar lounge - this purely a personal choice- not a negative for the hotel.
Free WiFI in the lobby or library room good, pity you had to pay for WIFI in the room.
Overall a good cean hotel in a nice position but maybe more for business than the holiday traffic.

title: “Great property for family vacation!”
text: We did a mini-vacation this weekend at the Hyatt Hill Country resort, and overall I was very impressed. The facility is very nice (although large - we were at the very end of one of one of the buildings so it took us quite awhile to get back into the elevators and heart of the action), and all of the staff was very pleasant. The rooms were nice although we did have two maintenance issues while we were there (leaky faucet and issue with the card reader on the oustide door of our room). Overall, they fixed these quickly and followed up. I would have preferred not to deal with these type of things since we had such a short time there that weekend to enjoy and it took nearly 30 minutes to get in our room at one point. But beyond that, they had a lot of things included in the resort fee which was nice. We enjoyed riding bikes for a little bit, played ping pong, our 6 year old son tried out a few of the special activities they had planned, and we enjoyed smores and watching a movie on the lawn on Saturday night. We actually had read ahead of time about the water facilities at Wild Oak (their sister vacation property down the street), and were able to get wristbands for free and without being sold so that we could go over and enjoy the indoor/outdoor pool area, water slides, and faster lazy river that they had. Having access to both was key! Like I said, they really focus on families which is nice and I enjoyed the option of all of the kids activities although the food service was slow and pricey and the pool/lazy river at our property were quite crowded. We went down to the riverwalk on Saturday night for dinner and that was easy enough. It's also right by Sea World if you wanted to go over there. I would probably go back to this hotel again if we could get a good rate.

title: “Great Value - Perfect for a One-Night Stopover Between Flights”
text: We stayed at La Quinta one night on our way to New York City from Australia and one night prior to our return to Australia. We found this hotel to be great value and in an ideal location for a one-night stay prior to flights. We were impressed with the variety of the free breakfasts, the fast speed of the free WiFi, the reliability of the free shuttle bus, the courtesy and efficiency of the staff, the cleanliness of the rooms which were not large but certainly adequate for a one-night stay, the close proximity to takeaway outlets - a petrol station with an array of food and other general commodities two doors down, Mc Donalds next door on one side and Taco Bell next door on the other and, of course, the excellent price for the room. We had a late departure on our return visit and it was no problem extending the stay for another half day in our room which cost less than $50 including taxes - perfect when facing a 15-hour flight! Another review commented on problems with the lifts but, for us, the three lifts were in working order throughout our stay. As this is an airport hotel, it is not in the best area but fine to venture out to the shops in close proximity. Although situated on a busy street, we found that, by being higher up, we did not experience any traffic noise from the cars`below nor was there any noise from planes. We would most definitely recommend this hotel for value for money, cleanliness, many free benefits and staff efficiency and courtesy.

title: “Can't believe this is a Starwood brand hotel”
text:
I'm a Starwood junkie and this hotel was F-A-R from the experience of a Starwood property. My room on the 19th floor was supposedly far enough from the elevator where I couldn't hear it but each night I could hear it moving up and down. The hinge on the top of the door was broken, the shower was lined with plastic instead of it being ceramic. As I moved in the shower, I could feel where the plastic was worn away and lifting from the original adhesive. Plus, my bathroom sink would fill with water if I left it running as I washed my face. 
I did ask to change my room but they had none other avail because it was filled to capacity. And that's probably because their rates are cheaper than other hotels in the area - so that's its only strong suit. They said they could move me the next day into another room, but I didn't think the rooms could get any better and didn't want the hassle of having to repack all my items. 
Bottom line: don't be lulled by the name...it is not even close to being anything luxurious. Even my 2 co-workers who also stayed here agreed they would not come again (and we come to NY often for work and normally stay at the Westin Times Square but the rates were too exorbitant for our stay). We just wanted to get the Starwood points (I know, maybe a little selfish), but we won't make that mistake again. We agreed we should have stayed at a Marriott this last time.

title: “Disgusting!”
text: There was no window shade on one window in our room. The front desk person said he would give us a sheet to hang on the window! The walls were thin. We could hear the person next door sneezing like he was in our room. The shower temperature had a mind of it's own and exposed heating pipes in the bathroom could've burned our skin! We ended up leaving a day earlier and staying at a four start hotel for only $50 more.

title: “Good Place”
text: Staff was polite and the room had the cleanest smell we've ever come to know in a hotel. The location is a bit farther from the attractions, but good just the same. Not too many places to eat around.. though. Access to the hotel is easy coming from either way, which was pleasing to us. Bed was comfy and room spacious enough. We'd stay again!

title: “Great Value and Great Location”
text:
We stayed 3 nights at the Drury Inn over the 4th of July weekend. We really loved this hotel. The hotel is very historic in nature and we found the rooms to be large and comfortable. The breakfast was above average and the evening cocktail hour was a very nice touch!
We really loved the location of the property. It sits directly on the Riverwalk, but a few blocks down from the busier portions. So you could easily walk 5 minutes to all the action but actually have the luxury of staying in a quieter location. 
We give it 5 stars because it is a good value and a really nice property with great customer service. We used the SAV coupon code on line when booking the room and we got a rate under $100 over a holiday weekend. We would not hesitate to go back to this property. 
You can read our entire trip report on our Sunnytripreports website.

title: “So Comfortable -- Loved It!”
text: I stayed at the Campton on business -- the hotel was chosen through a corporate travel department. I was a little leery as -- although charming -- many boutique hotels in San Francisco are too outdated for my tastes. I had no reason to be nervous. First, the location can't be beat -- less than a block from Union Square and very close to the Financial District (Market St.). All employees were quite friendly and accommodating. Stepping off of the elevator you see lots of mirrors and notice that you have to take a few steps up to get to a number of rooms -- again, this scred me. But once I entered my room it was perfect. The bed was full of pillows and soooo comfortable. The bathroom was gorgeous. I heard not all rooms were this way, but mine (615) has a separate tub and shower, and the shower was surrounded in marble and free-standing, which was very nice. I wouldn't hesitate to stay here again.

title: “Hotel Commonwealth”
text: Just a one night stay in preparation for a long drive up the coast to Maine. We arrived tired and harried, and the charming young people at the front desk cheered us up immediately by being so personable and welcoming. We have a college student in Boston, and will surely stay at the Commonwealth again.

title: “Very Convenient - Great Shuttle Service"”
text: We flew in from Seattle and needed a hotel to spend the nite and then take bus to Woods Hole and the ferry to Martha's Vineyard the next day. The hotel had a free shuttle which picked us up at the airport, then the next morning took us to the bus terminal. There is a subway about a block from the hotel - we took that into downtown Boston to spend the evening which worked out great. The staff was very helpful, the room clean and quiet. There is a very nice walking/jogging path along the water behind the hotel. There are no restaurants or Starbucks nearby, but if you just need a place for a layover between flights, or convenient public transportation, this is a good choice - reasonably priced. There is a small take out cafe on site. Oh...and they give you a chocolate chip cookie upon arrival - yummy!

title: “Small but clean”
text: The Motel is a little hard to get to but the staff was friendly. The room was small but clean, but for the price it was about right. There was only one member of the staff that spoke or understood English. Overall the room was very dark, with only two small lamps in the whole room. There was nothing by the desk so if you wanted to read or work on the computer it was very difficult. The bathroom and shower lights were on timers and would shut off on you if you didn't hurry. The King size bed was very comfortable to sleep in, but the pillows could have been a little bigger.

title: “Nice Central Location--Amazing Service”
text: I stayed at the Loews for business for 4 nights and unexpectedly had to stay for a 5th night. The staff was very accommodating and helped throughout the week find restaurants to eat at and of course negotiate a better price for my 5th night at the hotel. The hotel is only a block away from the famous Reading Terminal Market and convention center along with a few blocks away from the Constitution Center. I had an outside room which meant the whole wall along with the bathroom was windows. It was nice and kept the room feeling larger than it really was. I loved the long spacious bathroom and the complimentary bathrobe provided. I do want to note that internet and bottled water is not free, but they do provide a nice afternoon lemonade or water down stairs in the lobby. If I visit Philly again for business and I have a say I would stay at the Loews again because of the service received.

title: “Location, location, location...”
text: The location of this hotel was perfect! Travelling as a single female, I felt safe no matter what time of day or night. The price included a continental breakfast that was not extensive, but quite sufficient. The breakfast was held in the reception/lobby area and not conducive, but they’ve done their best. The staff was at all times attentive, charming and helpful. The hotel and rooms were spotlessly clean - always a very important factor. When in New York you don't spend much time in your room so it being very small was not an issue for me. The street noise levels were quite high. For those light sleepers I'd suggest earplugs. :-) I found the Econo Lodge Times Square a welcome haven after a hectic day's sightseeing and walking. Lovely! Thank you all. You are stars!

title: “Great Hotel in Central Location”
text:
We were in San Jose on 10/27/07 for a family wedding and stayed at the Hotel Montgomery based on location/recommendation. After reading reviews on TripAdvisor we decided to stay here instead of the Fairmont.
This is great boutique-type hotel. We had a slight problem when we first checked in... there was someone in our room (3rd floor) doing some type of cleaning/repair. And the floor and room smelled somewhat of bug spray. However, that was the only incovenience we experienced.
The check-in was smooth and fast. Yes, the elevators are a bit slow, but we had no problem waiting a few minutes. The room was a bit small, but very nice. One of the most comfortable beds I have ever slept in! I couldn't really hear the lightrail noise outside. We didn't have a very large bathroom either; shower/bath combo, but it was sufficient. I wish there could have been a bit more counter space on the sink, but they do have a bench under the sink where you can store items. Water pressure in the shower was just okay. It would have been nice to have a bit more pressure, but it did its job.
Check-out was just as fast and courteous. Parking is limited. We parked in the self parking section next to the hotel. $20 day. Parking spaces are very tight and were pretty much filled to capacity.
The only improvement I might suggest is serving breakfast. They do offer room-service/continental breakfast, but nothing from the stove or griddle.
All in all, a very lovely hotel, with just a couple minor inconveniences.

title: “Great food”
text: This is an awesome hotel. The breakfast is a very excellent size, and the kickback was delicious and filling. The free popcorn and soda was great too. The rooms were also great. The beds were very soft and nice. The pool was disappointing though.

title: “excellent location”
text: We stayed 5 days here,the location is excellent,very central.prize is resonable,room is fine but the problem is with room tempreture control,we can not controll tempreture from our room,its control by menegment office........,lots of good resturants nearby.

title: “Really nice retirement home.”
text:
I love Boston. I love the hostory and the people and the countless unique things to do here. I hated this hotel.
Check in was very hurried and brash. The front desk in general seemed very dismissive and lacked interest in anything. The concierge lady seemed like she had a cult following, and I was too impatient to wait through the line to discuss dinner options, so I spoke with the front desk instead. They hadn't heard of any of the restaurants I was looking for (hungry mother, beehive, bondir...) and when I asked for suggestions, they came up empty. One girl even admitted to not really spending any time in Boston. No one here seemed to love their job. 
I was accompanying someone holding a meeting here and staff were slow to respond to requests. I think my breaking point is when they shooed my friend and I out of the lobby while we were on break trying to have a quick bite. The way we were "suggested" to not eat in the lobby was downright condescending. This same attitude was given to the other guests at the meeting and could have been alleviated at the get-go by offering a key card to get everyone into the "counting room" upstairs. I have NEVER, as a GUEST, been asked to leave the lobby for snacking. 
Rooms were ok. On the larger side for the city with enough room to fit four comfortably. Lots of closet space with a convenient kitchenette. Bathroom was outdated with not enough counter space and harsh lighting. The views were excellent. Free laundry on the 24th floor (the guts of the clock are also housed here - pretty cool) and yes, the depressing bar and lackluster continental breakfast. Free Internet! Housekeeping was spotty, but then again, I didn't give them much time as I spent a lot of my time in the room. You have to use your key card to get ANYWHERE. 
The location was just ok. I like the Intercontinental and Nine Zero MUCH better for everything. Honestly, I would have even preferred HolidayInn over this.
Also getting seven zillion phone messages and flyers about their timeshare was really tacky.
On the last day my friend was visited by someone a little higher up in the food chain, asking for the person who booked the room. He wanted to know if everything was going ok... Too little, too late. How do we begin to say that the staff here was in need of some positive energy and curiosity about the city it serves?
Do stay here if you are a family in need of the space. Or, apparently, if you are retired or over 50. Lots of that demographic seemed to like this place for the history or the lackluster/robotic directions to Quincy market, north end, and the oyster house.
In the end I felt like an 8 year old trapped in a fancy retirement home, full of fear of talking too loud, not being dressed correctly, and putting my elbows on the table. :(

title: “Very Nice Hotel, Well Located”
text:
The good:
-- Well located for Georgetown's main street (M St) and pretty-well for Foggy Bottom metro station (4 blocks, less than 10min walk). Lots of great food / shopping in Georgetown, and, very near all the Washington attractions.
-- Fairly recently built, with nicely appointed rooms
-- Great breakfast cafe and Starbucks right out the front door
-- Friendly staff
This was a very good stay. Only things that don't make it a 5-star are the following: 
(1) Doorman ordered our airport car to collect us at 4pm pickup for 6.45pm Sunday flight from Dulles -- it was 4th of July weekend so I could understand him booking it a bit early, but, it turned out to be way earlier than necessary for a domestic flight, leaving us at the airport 2hrs and 15min ahead of the flight. I should have had them call early afternoon on the Sunday to get a better sense for traffic, and adjust car accordingly, so part my fault; 
(2) Concierge could have directed us better towards local bike rental options -- there were a few, and some with better bikes than others -- and it didn't feel like he knew the options available and prices. We ended up finding them ourselves. For a upper end chain, I should think they would have Georgetown services down cold. But the staff were otherwise very friendly and quite helpful.
All in all a very nice hotel to which we would return.

title: “Elegant with quirky elements, heaps of individual style and great service”
text: This is my second stay at the Palomar and it is a unique experience. I should say that this trip I stayed in a two 4 star hotels, the Grand Hyatt, the conference hotel in DC and earlier the Hilton in Salt Lake City and one 5 star-the Grand America in Salt Lake on my way back through. The last was an upgrade as the Little America has a conference and was overbooked. Although the luxury quotient was high there (Italian cotton hand wipes & marble toilet stalls in the public bathrooms and a large room with sofa and chairs, the restaurant service was indifferent and the atmosphere somewhat generic (rose prints hanging on wall, etc.). In contrast, I found the Palomar both elegant, personal and a touch quirky (the animal print robes, etc.) The room arrangement was appealing, including the placement of the work area and even the configuration of the lobby sofas was well designed. That combined with the staff's attentiveness made for a very pleasant stay. I should also mention that I was in town for the VSA International Art and Disability conference to present a lecture on the findings from my recently completed doctoral research on the working lives of professional visual artists with disabilities. So, the art-theme of the Palomar was particularly apt. I have been coming to DC for conferences for decades and have stayed at a variety of hotels from the Tabord Inn to the Mayflower to the Embassy Suites and a number of other Hyatts. The Palomar's location near Dupont Circle but on a quiet street and attractions are unique and is my top choice for my coming trips.

title: “Excellent weekend getaway!”
text:
We stayed at the Lakeway resort and spa over new years eve and were very impresses. The rooms were large, comfortable, clean and nicely decorated. The service was comparable to some of the 5 star resorts I have stayed in in the past. We had room service brought in for the kids in the morning and it was prompt and very reasonable for the quality.
My wife and I would love to return to check out the spa and other amenities in the future. I know we will be back.

title: “Accomodating for families”
text: After reading the reviews of this hotel my wife and I decided to stay here for our daughters wedding. The hotel rooms were large enough to fit all five of us in one room. We had 3 teenagers with us and everyone had their own space. The breakfast attendant was extremely warm and personable. The young lady at the desk was friendly and helpful (Harissa, maybe), Daniel was cool as ice, and Boris seemed proud of his team. Its rare that you see front desk people helping other departments but here if you sit and watch its like looking at your family. For this reason we would like to applaud management for putting together a nice group of workers. From check-in to check-out (Denis) we enjoyed our daughters wedding and we wanted to share this. Thank you

title: “Great weekend getaway”
text: MY wife and I stayed at the Sheraton for a romantic weekend. The location was great for shopping and dining. Our room was amazing with a great view of the river and the lake. The staff including the general manager went out of their way to take great care of us and even added some nice perks to make our weekend more special. I have stayed at many of the hotels around Michigan Ave and never had better service; this is why I will be staying here again the next time I am in Chicago.

title: “Slept through the storm”
text: Stayed here while in town for Seahawks game, also turned out to be the night of the BIG storm. At the airport the next day found out we we're one of the only ones who had power all night and the next day. The wind was crazy, but the room was still quiet enough that we slept right through it. Room was nothing special, nor was the breakfast buffet. Stay at the Embassy Suites nearby instead.

title: “Great Location, Marginal Service, Marginal Quality”
text:
I have stayed at the hotel twice for company recruiting on the UT Campus. Being a UT Alum, I loved the atmosphere of the hotel. The Burnt Orange pride runs deep in the decor and its really nice to see some of the historical items from the university. The location was also an easy walk over to the Jackson School of Geoscience. 
My biggest complaints were in the quality of the guest rooms. The bedding was awful! It's very nice looking, but is super scratchy and uncomfortable. Also, both times I've stayed in the hotel, my toliet broke. The toliets are also SUPER LOUD, so you can commonly hear the wooshing of other room's facilities. The lighting in the vanity area is very poor. The shower in my room leaked water onto the floor. The last time I stayed there, one of the guest rooms even flooded! For a $250 per night room, you expect to have better quality. It's not awful, but it is marginal.
The staff in Gabriels was the highlight of the trip! They were so helpful and friendly. Other staff I encountered could learn a thing or two from those staff members! I had a billing mix up where I was charged for another person's room in addition to my own, and it took about 6 weeks to get the ordeal worked out. The ATT staff did not seem to care that it was causing issues for me. They assured me several times it was fixed, but it wasn't. Finally, I was able to get with a supervisor (even though I had asked to speak with one to start with) and she was able to clear it up.
I just expected more from this hotel. I think with a few minor tweaks, it could have been a great experience, but for me it wasn't.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: We are two couples from Sydney Australia who stayed at the Casablanca Hotel for 8 days in the middle of September. We found the hotel oustanding in every respect. Need to view this hotel as 'the total package'. It is located right in the heart of Times Square, rooms and bathrooms are spotless and well furnished, decor in rooms and hallways is impressive and the piece de resistance is Rick's cafe on the second floor with access to 24 hour coffee, snacks etc and free wine and cheese every evening. Also free internet access in the cafe. This was a great place to relax and meet other guests. This is a boutique hotel so will not offer all the amenities of a larger chain but this is what made the hotel so far as we were concerned - smaller, friendly staff and place to relax and socialise outside of your room. When we arrived one room was very noisy and we asked to be moved. This was no problem and we were quickly located to another room on the other side of the hotel. Received excellent service from all staff with a special mention for Zishan and Hassan who were exceptional in providing information and for their courtesy and friendly approach. The hotel is certainly not in the budget category but we considered it worth the money, especially given the substantial complimentary breakfast, all day snacks and free wine from 6pm to 8pm. We would definitely return.

title: “A Hotel run by 20,30 somethings with no general manager in site”
text: While it was certainly a fun girls weekend, the hotel did not rise to our expectations. The snotty attitude of the people running the front desk was not appreciated, especially one girl in particular.
