I signed up as a grand guest which was a waste of time since they never put the amenity in my room and when I asked for it, they seemed bothered and said I never entered in my preferences (which I did online before my stay). Still not sure I received my $75 food & beverage credit... The only friendly staff were the door men and that we appreciated. On a Friday night, there were about 6 of us who tried to get seated and buy drinks for the night in the Church Lounge. Again, more snotty attitude from the host/hostesses. When they finally seated us, no one ever took our drink order so we up and left and had wine and drinks in the room - too bad the hotel lost out on the revenue we would have generated that night. I know it's NYC but the rooms were really small and nothing that special. Cool neighborhood but would rather stay in Soho, especially Trump Soho whose attention to detail and customer service was impeccable, when we visited their 7th floor bar/deck.

title: “Great access to LAX”
text: Parking is $25/night or $32 for valet. There are cheaper options nearby if you don't mind a couple of minutes walk. Good for a night's stay before or after a flight in/out of LAX. My room was $101/night which was better than most area options. The rooms are pretty room, a bit dated in appearance but perfectly service-able. Finding it and getting in and out take a bit of getting used to as it is not ON Century Blvd, like most other chains.

title: “What it lacks in Pizzaz is Made up for in Staff Friendliness”
text:
I've stayed at this property on 2 occasions. It's very close to the airport yet far enough away that you don't hear jets taking off all night. 
It seems to be an older Hilton property so it doesn't have all the sparkle and shine of the newer hotels. It's now become a hotel I truly enjoy staying at, however.
The rooms are spacious and comfortable. The beds and linens are in great shape. There's more than adequate workspace in each room and the bathroom is nice.
I can't rave about the newness of the spaces but I can rave about the incredible staff! I stay in hotels 3-5 nights per week, 44 weeks each year. I have had many experiences, good and not so good with hotel staff. This staff is world class! What makes this so? Everyone I've encountered truly seems to enjoy their job and truly enjoy interacting with the guests. When I say everyone I mean the front desk staff, the security staff, the wait staff at both the restaurant and the sports bar, everyone.
Kudos to the management for assembling such a wonderful team.
I can highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Good place to stay”
text:
We stayed here for 3 nights while on a sightseeing holiday to Washington DC. We were using the 'Old Town Trolley' tours which had a stop just up the road at the National Cathederal so this place was ideally located for us.
The rooms were comfortable, had breakfast in the room one morning but didn't receive an option to have it the other 2 mornings. The staff at the desk were not overly friendly or helpful but the man at the concierge desk was lovely.

title: “Good hotel”
text: This appears to be a well-maintained hotel. There is enough space in the room to move self as well as baggage. My room had a coffee maker, TV, Table, Chairs, laundry facility, hair dryer, WiFi access but no Microwave Oven. Internet access is also available near the lobby 24 hours free of charge. The 14th floor (roof top) restaurant offers a good view of Denver city. The hotel is also close to the football stadium. Hotel shuttle is available from/to the city.

title: “"Hotel Greatness"”
text: I have just returned from 5 days at this Incredible hotel while attending a trade show at the convention center next door. From the moment you pull up you are aware that you are not at just any hotel. The check in area is spacious and accommodating of a rush hour of guest checking in or out. The rooms are on the larger size than most hotels you will stay in as well as somewhat plush in their furnishings as well as modern. My view out the window was spectacular and I couldn't resist posting it on my Facebook page. There is a great Lobby bar that is open to the whole area that makes it convenient to stop and enjoy a glass of wine or cold beer to take the edge off of the day. The gift shop is enormous and catered to the unusual, rather than the same old, same old. And of course, the restaurants. This is what I enjoyed the most. From fine dining at Bob's Chop & Steakhouse with a great menu and wine selection, to not being up for something so formal and hanging out at the sports bar, to the casual at a third location inside the Hotel. Convenience to the convention center via the second floor made the transition back & forth simple & convenient. The people were cordial and at always available to help, and to cap it off when I had to leave suddenly because of a medical emergency and had to go the airport at 4:30 am, I was treated to a stretch limo ride to the airport at the same fare as a taxi. I left with a big smile!!!

title: “Comfortable stay”
text:
We stayed at the Alpha Inn and Suites (previously Econo Lodge) for 3 nights, and overall it wasn't bad! The guy on the front desk was friendly and helpful (even if English wasn't his first language), and he gave us a huge room, from which you could see downtown, Golden Gate Bridge and Alcatraz.
The main building is accessed via a locked gated door which you access using your keycard. The room was clean and had a comfortable bed, walk-in cupboard, bathroom, TV, telephone, fridge, microwave, table and chairs, 2 sofas, and coffee maker. It was about 4 times the size of the hotel room my husband stayed in last time he was in SF. The noise wasn't too noticeable considering we were on Lombard Street! The main negative for us was that there was no safe, despite the website saying 'safe in every room' and the keycard saying 'keep your valuables in the safe'.
Some other things to note:
> There's no lift – so make sure you can carry your luggage up and down 3 flights of stairs!
> Breakfast consisted of 1 small chocolate muffin. However, there's a Walgreens right across the road, and a diner further up Lombard.
> If you're not a fan of thin towels, bring your own!
The area seemed fairly safe, and the location is good – just walk down Divisadero and you end up at the marina district. If you're feeling energetic you can have a very pleasant walk 2 miles to the Golden Gate Bridge (turn left), or Pier 39 (turn right). 
Having researched SF hotels on Tripadvisor, we weren't expecting to get a lot for our money (especially on Fri/Sat, booking only a few days before our stay). While the whole place would undoubtedly benefit from a spruce-up, we had a comfortable stay. However, if you're the kind of person whose holiday is ruined by chipped furniture/mismatched decor, I would recommend looking elsewhere...

title: “The Omni, a perfect location for taking in Washington”
text:
Just got back from a 4 day stay at the Embassy Suites hotel in downtown Washington with our family of 5. I'll break it down to Positives and Negatives:
Positives:
1. Location, location, location. Even though a bit of walking is needed to take the M transit, it still is possible to walk to all the sights if your family is up for some walking. Plenty of restaurants within a few blocks along with other stores.
2. Room size and layout. With a family of 5, there is usually an odd man out in most hotels. Embassy has two queen size beds and a queen sleeper sofa. Also has two sinks outside the bathroom, needed with 2 daughters.
3. Breakfast. The food was very good. Made to order omelletes. Pancakes and other hot foods. Fruits, cereals, bagels, etc. Our family are not big eaters, but this was great for getting out and seeing the sights without looking for a place to eat breakfast every morning.
4. Staff. No problems with check in or check out. The Concierge was most helpful in arranging tours and suggested eating.
5. Quietness. Outside of some late night sirens (This is DC), no late night surprises.
Negatives.
1. Parking. $20 a day to park. The garage was 2 blocks away also since their own parking was full. Inconveinent if your planing on using your car often
2. Lines for eating breakfast. I hate buffets, but understand the situation. Most tables are either taken or need to have the left over tray removed to sit down. No place to leave your trays when your done creates a mess. Recommend getting up early (opens at 7:30am) to get in and out and be on your way.
3. The managers reception is nice, but mainly just for drinking. Food is minimal and average at best. Still free and yes, I'm being picky.
4. Pool. The pool is very small and rather cold. Kids liked it but not warm enough for me. Hot tub is crowded full of parents and cold kids.
Overall It fits our needs. I would recommend shopping around for the best price, since you getting the same room no matter what.

title: “Picture are Deceiving!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Yuck!!!!!!!!!!”
text: This hotel is quite deceiving. The pictures on the internet make it seem very nice. But it's old and rundown. The view I had was of a brick wall! Extremely noisey, even thought we were in the so called "quite zone". Banging sounds all night long. Car alarms. Front door view was of a parking lot and dirt lot along with the freeway. Maid service only supplied a few towels for 3 people. Room was run down and not very clean. Elevators took forever! Pool was dirty. Overall I would never stay at this hotel again. NEVER BELIEVE WHAT THE INTERNET PICTURES SHOW YOU! Staff was not very pleasant either.

title: “This Roach Motel was unbearable...”
text:
We had just got back from staying at this establishment this last weekend. Being picky about where you rest your head is a different story, we just wanted a place that was fairly clean for our return from the convention. A recap:
Night 1: [----------------------------] size of roach inside the shower, largest I’ve ever seen in Northern America.
Night 2: Room heater had broken down and the hot water was not working… cold night in San Diego…
 Night 3: The Maid had left the room window open after cleaning, which left easy access for anyone who walked by to pop off the screen and have their way with our valuables 
When I approached the faculty – they said that it was procedure, and guaranteed that no one could have gotten into the room. From the looks of the room screens, it looks like it was very possible. I would recommend not staying in this facility for all the reasons above and for the fact that it was very expensive even for the area. A big mistake I will never make again.

title: “Not So Great”
text: Well, I booked through American Express Centurion (my hubby has a black card) and the rate here was great, that I will say (395/nt). I booked 2 rooms for a girls' overnight. It stank! The rooms were really sort of run down and dirty, it was unlike any other Ritz I have ever stayed in. My husband has had better experiences then me here so maybe the fact that I requested 2 adjoining rooms limited the room choice. But rug was dirty, it was far from luxurious. Service is good, I will say that! Excellent concierge desk (but unable to get reservations at good restaurants so make them on your own. They booked us at the Bubble Lounge, which had I not known better, would have sucked). Sort of lame experience and I had high expectations because it is a Ritz after all!

title: “Just Meh”
text:
I stayed at this hotel February 15th, per the recommendation of a local colleague. My room was on one of the Starwood Preferred Guest floors. I also liked the hotel’s “green program”, which gives guests credit if they stay more than two days, and decline the sheet and towel changing service. If I were to rate the hotel just for its room, I’d give it 3.5-4 stars. Nothing fancy, but better than the average. The room a/c or heat worked fine.
My issues, and reason for downgrading are:
1. absolutely horrible service with getting a taxi cab. Three of us were to meet other colleagues at the Veracruz restaurant (see review elsewhere, excellent by the way). None of us were from Dallas. The door man said we could take the hotel’s SUV (seems odd that a hotel featuring green services has a Suburban available, why not a Prius, or something? Do you really need 4 WD in Dallas). Anyway, I gave the doorman the address (408 N. Bishop in Oak Cliff), and he said it’d be $5 each. That rate seemed a little higher than a taxi for what was supposed to be a ten minute drive, but not ridiculous. Shortly after entry, and after programming the GPS to locate the address, the driver informed us that since the restaurant was not downtown, it’d be $25. That was not the worst thing. The driver then proceeded to check his bids on eBay while he was driving in heavy traffic and on the freeway. I was in the front seat, and didn’t see these shenanigans, but one of my colleagues saw the whole thing. He only almost hit a Jersey barrier a couple times, and had to brake severely as well, to avoid running into someone. 
I am always leery of these “black cars”, and should have known better. But, we were already running late for our dinner with others. But, in the future, never again. It appeared to us that the doorman and the car service were running a nice little side business.
2. I specifically asked for a room away from the elevator and ice machines. My room, XX77 was directly next to the motors that operate the elevators. I noticed this initially, but see 1 above, we were already late, and it would have taken extra minutes to change rooms. I was tired when I got back, and went to bed. Hearing the noise, I used my Bose earphones (same as one sees on airplanes) to get some rest at first, and then burrowed in pillows after the headphones were not comfortable to sleep on one’s side.

title: “Certainly not the best hotel for the money!”
text:
Right from the start, the hotel doesn't offer amenities offered in 2 star hotels! Our room had ants in the bathroom and overall was not clean.
NO GIFT OR SNACK SHOP ON premises. Your would have to drive twenty minutes for late night snacks. Restaurants in hotel are NOT part of hotel.
You have to pay for coffee in your continenal breakfast package. Parking is $25.00 per night extra on top of your $260.00 rate. Personel were
cordial but had no authority to make any changes.
There are ALOT better hotels for the money to stay in, don't pick this one. I won't again!

title: “Unbelievable Caring Staff”
text: Due to a family medical emergency I had to fly to DC. I walked into the Westin and asked them if they had a room because they were close to the hospital. I told them I didn't know how long I would need to stay. They told me not to worry that they would have a room for me as long as I needed it. Everyone at the hotel was very caring and always checking in with me everyday to see if they could do anything for me. I would like to give a big thanks to Vikram and Kevin who went above and beyond taking care of me during the week.

title: “Home in America”
text: Nice Hotel with good ambience. Provides Nice breakfast and evening snacks. Rooms are spacious and good. House Keeping staff is very cooperative and effiicient. Having Ample parking space.

title: “Great Oasis in the Middle of a Cute Neighborhood”
text:
We stayed here for a wedding, and we are very happy that the couple chose this hotel for us. The recent renovations seem to have really updated the rooms, which are a good size, and with good amenities. It is a little noisy however--especially if you get a pool side room. Also, for the interior rooms other friends told us that they could hear people coming in and out of other rooms and closing their doors. 
The public areas are particularly charming, and the restaurant is very good. We enjoyed a casual brunch there, sitting on the patio overlooking the pool. Some of the pool activities can be a bit noisy--we witnessed a very pumped up exercise session--but it all adds to the charm of this community gem.

title: “Worst San Antonio Hotel Experience”
text:
We "named our own price" on Priceline, and ended up with this Hilton. This was our fifth trip to San Antonio in the past 4+ years, and the first time we stayed here. On our previous trips, we have stayed at Marriott properties (Springhill Suites Crossroads, Towneplace Suites Airport, and Fairfield Inn North Star Mall). By comparison to the Marriott hotels, this Hilton was awful.
First off, the hotel has a four-level parking garage, and happily charge $10/day to park there. The Marriott's have free parking. The hotel has no free breakfast, with room service or restaurant choices being very pricey. The Marriott's have free breakfast. They charge $10.76/day for internet access. The Marriott's have free Wi-Fi. This lovely hotel even charges $0.50 for a local call... guess what... Marriott's are free. 
The hotel itself has a decent lobby, but when the elevator opened on the 5th floor, I felt like I stepped into a bad motel. Everything is terribly outdated... the carpets, the wallpaper, the paint, the furniture, the lighting, the bathroom... the only redeeming features of the whole place were the decently comfortable bed, and the 32" LCD TV with HD programming. Of course, the movies we checked through pay-per-view were about $30 each!
The lighting in the room was horrible... we had every light on, and it barely reached the level of mood lighting. The bathroom was small and cramped... the door was busted up, the lights were half out, and the towel rack was inside the shower, for whatever sense that made. To be honest... the shower was so nasty looking that we didn't make use of it during our two night stay. 
The first time we went to leave the parking garage, our room key didn't work at the exit gate. So, not only was parking $10 a day, but we were being held prisoner. There is a "help" button on the exit machine, which I pressed... and was told that someone would be right with me. After a few minutes, and with a half-dozen cars waiting behind us, my wife ran to the lobby... which is, of course, pretty far from the garage. They finally remote-released the gate, and we were free. We were told that they'd comp the parking for our inconvenience, but they never did. 
The staff was very friendly, but the hotel is miserable. It is probably only alive due to the conventions that go there. It felt so old, especially compared to all of the newer (or brand new) Marriott's practically next door. As for price, the Marriott's I mentioned are all a little cheaper, and don't charge for parking, breakfast, or WiFi. 
We basically got this Hilton for half-off thanks to Priceline... but in hindsight, we'd rather have paid regular price to stay elsewhere.

title: “Great Business Traveler Value”
text:
I stayed here as a cheap value to attend a convention at the Moscone Center. You can't beat the price for such a central location. It's not far away from Moscone by bus (4 bucks RT) or taxi (18 bucks RT), and I feel more comfortable here walking around at night, and there's a lot of cheap food options nearby.
Hotel Tomo is a little dated, but it was cleaner than many hotels I've stayed at. The rooms have a large college dorm feel, lots of utilitarian IKEA-type furniture. Bath is clearly old, but clean. Toilet did not flush well. Incredibly minimal bath light, and toiletries provided are cheap, I was glad I brought my own. My bed was pretty comfortable overall, pillows a little too soft for my taste. I could not hear traffic noise, but when I slept in one morning I could clearly hear loud children from somewhere nearby (either daycare or school). I could hear other rooms as well, I had some loud neighbors that felt like slamming doors and stomping loudly in the middle of the night, which kept waking me up. But I could not hear normal, low-noise activity from other rooms, or much from the maids, so the walls aren't totally paper-thin.
Free Wi-Fi, no password required, is provided but is extremely slow. There is a small fridge in the room, and a small room safe, both of which can be locked. The TV in my room did not work well and did not seem to have all the advertised channels, but I wasn't really that interested in it, so I didn't care all that much personally. The staff is very polite and call you every evening to ask if you have problems. I am satisfied overall.

title: “Agrivating from the 1st min.”
text: The front desk clerk made us wait 45 min because the room wasn't clean and he said they had 2 housekeepers cleaning it. I felt like it was caotic. We got to the room and the bathroom floor wasn't clean so I found old contacts on it. The front desk didn't tell me when breakfast was or where the room was he just gave me keys with the room number. During the 45 min of waiting he told us about all the hotels problems and brought his cigarette into the lobby. When we checked out we left an expensive pillow in the room but when we came back to get it 1hr later housekeeping had our pillow case in the trash and had claimed my pillow as their own. I know for a fact hotels are to give you 30 days to claim your forgotten things.

title: “Do not stay here!”
text: We booked this hotel a month ahead of time, online, on the Kitano website. Two weeks before we were due to arrive, we had a family emergency. We tried to cancel our reservations only to be told we could not cancel. This is unheard of. Any decent hotel allows cancelations prior to 48 hours arrival. Here it was two weeks ahead of time and we were told we couldn't cancel because we received a 15% discount by booking on their website!! The resevations desk let us talk with a manager on the phone, and we got the same answer, because we got such a 'good deal' on the room we could not cancel. Now we're out 2 nights costs on top of our family issue. Buyer beware in this place - we won't do business here again!!

title: “Another great Kimpton property!”
text: I've stayed in a number of Kimpton properties in Boston and Washington, DC and have never been disappointed; the new Palomar in Philadelphia continues my great experiences. From the valet greeting me and telling me to let the front desk know that I drive a hybrid car because it would get me a discounted room rate to the beautifully appointed, super quiet room, I couldn't have asked for more. The staff is so kind and friendly, the rooms are thoughtfully laid out and filled with little conveniences, and the bar and restaurant were excellent. We even had a celebrity chef sighting in the bar! Overall, another excellent Kimpton experience and one that reinforces why the brand is my absolute favorite among hotels.

title: “Value for $$ with no expectations”
text:
Me and my friends stayed here during our weekend trip at NY. Very good location just a block away from Times Square. Very cheap- we wanted a place just to keep our bags and rest for couple of hours. 
Only drawback we noticed after landing at the hotel was they had common restrooms per 3 rooms. Since the hotel was not occupied much we had it for ourselves. 
Price was damn cheap. Good reception. You have to ring the bell everytime you enter to open the main door. No breakfast served here but there are tons of bistros outside. 
I would rate 4 since we expected nothing but just a room to rest.

title: “Most affordable view!”
text:
Upon checking in for a 5 night stay our room had not been occupied for some time it had seemed. The apartment/suite was dusty and had to kill about a dozen spiders which were mostly on the ceiling corners. We called the front desk and advised them and the next day the room was spotless, we were also generously comped and treated to a buffet of leftover goodies left in our room by the housekeeper after each day that we got back from our daily activities.
The view is priceless and right behind is the Yamashiro castle which we loved walking up to each night and looking out at the city. As you drive up to your hotel it has a coded gate which adds a sense of security especially if you are parking a nice pricey sports car in your very own designated spot. There is a continental B-Fast down at the base hotel(Magic Castle Hotel)in morning which isn't spectacular yet the staff try their best to please which more than makes for any of the faults you may experience during your stay.
A big thank you to the staff for pampering us!

title: “We were spoiled!”
text: I don't think I could stay anywhere else but here if I get back to NYC. The location was so convenient to Central Park, Time Square and the American Girl store. The breakfast buffet on the 1st floor was OMG so good. A small problem in our room was resolved above and beyond our expectations. They did not give my points with Hilton Honors because it was booked through travelocity (at about 150 less that the usual price) BUT they did give us a super nice room because I was a Hilton Honors member. Thanks

title: “Strategic location”
text: Hotel located in a nice neighborhood, close to metro station and 10 minutes walk from Times Square. The rooms are spacious, clean and the furniture is modern. The staff is friendly. The only bad thing is breakfast, but the hotel is surrounded by great places that serve good breakfasts in typical American style.

title: “Great location”
text: Staying in Chicago on business and decided on this hotel for central location. You can walk to all locations on mag mile, Ohio and state st. Comfortable bedding, larger than normal rooms, great Internet. Breakfast had something to be desired. The egg's were awful, rubbery and tasteless.

title: “Good hotel, excellent room”
text: Good, clean, modern hotel in great location. Excellent bedroom layout. Lovely bathroom. Very comfy beds. Room had fridge, cooker, microwave and sink area which was ideal for long stay (all pots, pans and cutlery too). Staff genuinely helpful and very pleasant. Stayed in room 304 which was quiet but close to stairs and we used these rather than wait for lift (The lifts were busy but we didn’t find this a problem). The free breakfast was a great start to the day and of good quality and we had no problem finding a table. Plastic pots freely available to eat breakfast in room if desired. , the staff were very professional. The bus station opposite is not a negative - it has excellent value for money restaurants and bakeries at half the cost of eating elsewhere in the area and the entrance steps are just opposite the hotel. We ate there a couple of times as did the others on our trip. We bought beautiful pastries to take home on an evening. Metro tip – buy a card and just top it up – you can use it for multiple people. Each journey per person is $2.25 no matter how long or if line changes needed. Thoroughly enjoyed or stay. No problems. Would recommend this hotel.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: I loved this hotel. The location was perfect and the staff was great. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Very Loud Hotel”
text: This is the worst built hotel as far as thin walls go. We checked in on Friday, along with over 100 private school students between the ages of 12-16. They checked in around 11pm and were extremely loud and uncontrolled. After 3 calls to the front desk over the period of 1 1/2 hours I finally went to the desk in person to complain. The young lady was very sympathic, but advised that she was the only one there (they DO NOT HAVE A NIGHT MANAGER!) and tried her best to quiet the students by calling the guardians, to no avail. They finally quieted down at 1am. We were moved to the 4th floor the next day, but it was no better. Again, no sleep that night. We had our 3-year old with us, and our trip was ruined due to lack of sleep. Truly, the walls are so thin that we could here snoring, drawers opening and closing, toilets flushing, and another bodily function I won't mention. While the staff was extremely professional and sympathic, we were in a bad situation, and was not offered any type of discount. If you want a good nights sleep, DO NOT STAY HERE!

title: “Birthday Nightmare”
text: The pictures that show the exterior and interior of the Hollywood Downtower were VERY MISLEADING. Our room had NO SHOWERHEAD, a huge black stain on the carpet, multiple broken lamps with disgusting stained lamp shades and dirty laundry left behind by previous guests. The other tenants were inconsiderate of others, making extreme amounts of noise at 3,4,5AM!!! At one point, we distinctly smelled illegal substances coming from the room across from ours. The day staff customer service was unprofessional and the front office was cluttered with miscellaneous items. The price was economical but not at all worth the hassle. There is one good thing. When I notified the night staff that the showerhead was missing, the staff did come install one promptly.

title: “The King Lives”
text:
Stayed here with my wife and some firends and had a great time. If you are coming to do Graceland, it's a hard location to beat, right opposite. They have a free shuttle bus that will pick you up from the airport, you just have to call. The hotel is perhaps ageing a little, but everything worked and it was clean. Didn't try the food in the hotel, but it is Memphis, so everything is BBQ or deep fried! We ended up back at the bar most nights, where they play Elvis DVDs. They have a free continental brekky that hits the spot. 
There is a free shuttle bus that takes you to Sun Studios (well worth it) and then into Beale St. There is also a shuttle back from Beale that starts at 6:30, hourly to 11:30 I think. Don't miss BB Kings for music and atmosphere, City Cafe for ribs, Civil rights museum for some perspective and of course Graceland. I'm not a huge Elvis fan, but I got a lot out of the whole experience. I think a cab from the Hotel to Beale is about $15.

title: “Nice stay and perfect location!”
text: This was the second time I have stayed at this hotel and it did not let me down. Our balcony had a view of many of the major museums and a large fountain. While the lobby had an amazing small outside seating area closed of to anyone but guests. It was truely a very nice stay.

title: “Exactly what you would expect”
text: This Hilton is exactly what you would expect from a hotel/conference center. Everything done well. Nothing distinctive. Long walks if you are located in some sections of the hotel. Service was fine. Room was OK. If I didn't know I was in a Hilton, it could have been a Marriott, a Sheraton, ... It is close to the airport, which is what we needed.

title: “Enjoyable stay”
text:
We booked a King Premier as they are at the back of the hotel and bigger. It was pricey and we had to pay for a decent nights sleep. Good job we did because our friends were at the front and had no sleep. We slept very well and the beds are amazing. The room was extremely comfortable and kept very clean by the housekeeping staff. 
I had arranged with the concierge for a bottle of wine to be put in our room on arrival, plus we had asked him to organise a cocktail making experience for us. Unfortunately none of this had been arranged as this individual left their employ just days before but had not passed on the instructions. Such a shame as it was a special birthday treat for my husband. Many thanks to Melissa who arranged the wine and cheese/fruit platter a few days after our arrival.
One of the lifts wasn't working for the our entire stay (5 nights) which was a pain especially as the lift took up to 10 minutes to arrive. Yes we should have walked up or down but it was 85 degrees out there and was in no mood to get any hotter.
The free coffee and wine was a lovely touch and we enjoyed a glass or two on several occasions. I would recommend this hotel to friends as it is ideally located, but as NYC has other areas to explore, next time we will stay at the Kimpton towards Soho.
Thank you for a very enjoyable stay.

title: “Not fancy but a good hotel at an excellent price”
text: We enjoyed our stay at the Bay Club Hotel. The decor is a bit tacky, but this hotel is great value for money. We paid $125 for one night, which included a great breakfast buffet (toast, pancakes, scrambled eggs, bacon, sausages, home fries, fruit, coffee, juice, etc.). The parking fee was only $5, much cheaper than other San Diego hotels. There was supposed to be free wireless in the room, but we couldn't get it to work on our iPad, so that was perhaps the only negative. You could hear the people in the room above us walking around a lot in the middle of the night, but that is often the case in hotels. I'd recommend a room on the top floor if you can get it. You can hear boats passing by, but they don't make a lot of noise. It was nice to sit on our balcony in the evening and watch the boats pass. The pool and hot tub are great. All in all, a great experience for not much money.

title: “It's hard to rate a hotel when they don't honor your reservation!”
text:
We (my husband, son and I) booked and prepaid this non-refundable reservation through AARP/Expedia on January 9, 2012. We researched hotels and selected Holiday Inn Inner Harbor based upon the Holiday Inn reputation and its proximity to Camden Yards and other places we wished to visit in Baltimore. We arrived at the hotel via taxi from the airport approximately 9:00 p.m. on May 26 only to be told that there was no room for us that evening, and we had been moved to another hotel. We were given a letter to this substituted hotel which indicated the Holiday Inn would pay for the 26th. When questioned on whether we were expected to move back to the Holiday Inn on the 27th, the letter was amended to add the night of the 27th to our “reservation.” We were asked how we arrived at the hotel, and when we told them by taxi, we were given cash for cab fare to the substituted hotel, and another cab was called for us. 
I understand that the evening staff was doing what they were told to do, and at that point we were all tired and just wanted a clean bed for the night. However, I find it completely unacceptable to not be advised our reservation would be changed when we had made and paid for that reservation almost 20 weeks prior to our stay. It appeared that a large group was staying at the Holiday Inn and we were left with the distinct impression that we were unceremoniously tossed aside for bookings that would bring in a higher rate per night.
While the hotel we ended up at was clean and the rooms well kept, we had reserved a room at the Holiday Inn with two queen beds. When we arrived at the substitue hotel, we found we had been given a “suite” with a king bed and a pull out sofa bed. We found the room, the meals and the service to not be of the quality we thought we had booked at the Holiday Inn. We also were now approximately ¾ of a mile farther away from where we intended to stay and where we intended to visit, adding additional expense to our stay.
This experience was a thoroughly disappointing way to start a family vacation, and while I would have had to forfeit our prepayment should I have tried to cancel our reservation, it seems that there was/is no obligation on the part of Holiday Inn to honor the same. Be assured that I will not be making another reservation with this hotel!

title: “Beautiful hotel”
text:
Hotel was beautiful Daniel at the reception was great, room was on the 4th floor a little noise but we were fine with it as we were out most the day walking around so we were stuffed by the time we got back we slept thou the noise.
Bellman was wonderful

title: “We had a wonderful stay at The Barclay! Highly recommend!”
text: It was our first trip to New York (five ladies) and we found The Barclay to be a great location, within walking distance of shopping, Broadway, Times Square... you name it! It quickly became our "home away from home". We had two connecting "Deluxe" rooms, which worked out perfectly for us. The beds were very comfortable (pillow topped I suspect). The Barclay is a heritage hotel, so what it lacks in size as far as the bathrooms, is made up by the beautiful architectural details located throughout the hotel. The staff was very helpful. The concierge and the bell staff (including doormen) were great at making suggestions for restaurants, pointing us in the right direction, etc. We will return!

title: “Perfect stay- 100% hotel in every respect. Amazing value!”
text:
In short, this is a fantastic place to stay. Affordable, well located, clean, comfortable, convenient...the list goes on. I can't fault it and I'm still so impressed by it!
Our 'suite' which includes everything you might need, even a kitchenette with fridge, freezer, ice maker, dishwasher, utensils, sink, coffee maker etc etc was so clean, well decorated, simple/effective to heat and cool, roomy, the biggest and most comfortable bed EVER and was a joy to be in. The inclusive breakfast was excellent, varied and well attended, the service was polite, attentive and professional. Brilliant cleanliness, service and courtesy from cleaners with wonderful fresh bedding, fluffy towels and replenishments daily. I really can't see how anyone could say anything else but perfect. Have no doubts about staying here!!! The only way you could top it would be if you had major £££ to splash on a hotel with all the major luxury factors or significant aesthetics. But even if you are someone, like me, with high standards, you won't be disappointed. I would not book anywhere else in NYC again. See you soon, Staybridge!

title: “Great Baltimore Place”
text: Beautiful new green building. Amazingly comfortable beds. Great views for the top floor bar area. Peaceful and quiet. We enjoyed the stay and would stay there again.

title: “Wonderful find in Chelsea!”
text: I was skeptical about staying in a hotel brand that I'd never tried before, but this turned out to be a great find. We had an upgrade to a nice suite on the 18th floor. Very comfortable and clean room. Quiet location in the flower district, but easy access to get around to everywhere we wanted to go. One block from subway, and only 2 stops from theater district. We were able to walk to Greenwich Village for dinner, and felt very comfortable on the return walk late in the evening. The bar was fairly empty (rooftop bar closed due to the cold and renovations), but was pleasant enough. John at the front desk was excellent, very receptive to our needs. Would definately recommend and stay again!

title: “Cannot recommend it highly enough!”
text:
What a wonderful, wonderful hotel. One of the comfiest beds I've ever slept in, piping hot shower and the Wolfgang Puck coffee was a nice touch too. Furthermore, the staff is some of the most helpful and genuinely friendly I've ever encountered. Along with the Lucerne at 79th and Amsterdam, one of my two favorite hotels in the city.
Plus you have the lovely Manhattan Diner across the street -- my favorite diner in Manhattan, worth many, many visits. Try the Mediterranean Platter.

title: “Something has changed here...”
text:
I am a frequent vistor to DC and often stay at the Melrose because, frankly, the price is a cheap as a non-service budget hotel. Saying that, I never expect a lot during my visit for the price. The one thing they had was friendly staff and decent service.
This past visit was totally leisure travel. I noticed an unfriendly almost cold reaction from most of the staff - just the opposite of prior visits. I asked the friendliest person I saw "what happened to all the smiling faces…" . They shrugged their shoulders and said- "new company, new problems..". 
Sorry to hear that one of the friendliest places to stay is turning into a roadside staffed motel - but then again for the price….

title: “Nice Hampton Inn”
text:
Spent one night here before a flight - talk about convenient - mere minutes to the airport.
We were given room #301, which was HUGE. It had two beds, a flat screen TV, small fridge and good sized bathroom. Very clean and comfortable.
The room was located at the end of a hallway overlooking the covered driveway and loading area at the front of the hotel. It was incredibly quiet, but because the room had two windows overlooking the driveway, it was illuminated all night and was a bit bothersome.
Our fridge didn't work, so we called to notify the front desk. They sent up a replacement fridge, which ran so loudly that we ended up unplugging it so we could sleep.
The light in our bathroom flickered when in use and the TV remote needed a new battery, all of which we reported to the front desk upon check out. 
A few problems, but certainly nothing to get worked up about. Overall a very good stay.

title: “Very Comfortable Stay”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for one week during a Convention from Sunday July 2 through to Sunday July 10.
Considering the enormous size of this place (23 floors & 1,400 rooms!) we thought the professionalism and friendliness of all the staff made the stay a unique one.
The room was very comfortable with a king size bed, larger than normal bathroom, sitting area, desk and entertainment area. Very strange though: considering the reputation and rating of this hotel chain, that if you wanted a refrigerator in your room you had to rent it!
The Convention Special rate we paid, for the two of us, was $144/night + tax. A great discount off their normal room rates.
Otherwise, the location to all the major sites in Philly, the SEPTA rail station and, of course, the Convention Centre was ideal for the purpose of our stay.
Regards,
L & M from Oz

title: “Ideal Choice”
text:
We chose the Cow Hollow after reading reviews of many San Francisco hotels on TripAdvisor. We were a little concerned as it was our first trip to San Francisco, but we couldn't have made a better choice. 
The Cow Hollow is ideally located - we walked to Ghirardelli Square and the cable cars in about 15 minutes, or used the buses which run along Chestnut Street, one street over from Lombard. The local neighbourhood on Chestnut has plenty of restaurants and shops, and we enjoyed just walking along there in the evenings. 
Our room was large and clean, with a view of the Golden Gate Bridge. A little noisy some nights from the restaurants below, but it is a city location after all. The staff were friendly and helpful, and the free parking was a definite plus. The restaurant a few doors down in the same block on Lombard was good for breakfast. 
We had been tempted to stay in the Fisherman's Wharf area but were so glad we didn't as when we visited we found it was seriously touristy/seedy. We were happy to escape back to the Cow Hollow.

title: “Terrible staff and outdated hotel”
text: Terrible hotel staff at desk. Unable to talk to manager. Said manger is not in building. How can that be when it is 10am on a weekday. Just gave an 800 number to call. When you do call you get run around transfrered from one person to another. Overcharged for room. No towels in pool area. Desk says housekeeping will bring them never does. Room wallpaper peeling. Old tube TV's with poor reception. Would not recommend or stay here again.

title: “Bryant Park - excellent!”
text: We chose Bryant Park hotel because it's location and Travellers' Choice award. It is very modern and trendy. The staff were absolutely lovely and were so friendly and helpful, we really felt so relaxed and pampered staying there. Our room was amazing, a suite overlooking Bryant Park and the side of the library, which was awesome! Bathroom was luxury - with Molton Brown products. The hotel is perfect location for sight-seeing, right near the subway, about 5minutes walk to Times Square, only a few blocks from Empire State Building and the Rockefella, and just next to 5th Avenue! They also gave us some ideas for places to go for brunch, which were great. The service here is amazing, and the rooms are so modern and cool, it's a shame we were not there to enjoy it for longer! Cannot wait to return :-)

title: “It was ok”
text: Let's start with the good. The location is good, we like this part of San Diego. The staff is very nice and helpful. The trains didn't really bother us like they did for some others. We heard them in the evening the early night, but they never woke us. As for what is in the middle, neither great nor horrible, I'd say the breakfast qualifies. It is breakfast, but I wouldn't call it particularly delicious by any means; rather fuel for the morning. Now for the bad. The furniture was rather worn in the room, particularly the coffee table; really could use replacing. And finally, the parking was horrible. Although we were able to park each night in the garage, for which you pay and that's ok, the spaces were terribly small. One morning it took a 25 point turn to get my car out of it's spot.

title: “Not jaw-dropping exciting but nice hotel, fab location!”
text:
The hotel in conveniently located right above the 49th station on the N R W subway lines).
We had a normal room - which I got at a good rate (read not their normal website rates... I don't think it is worth the money at that rate). Anyway since we got there a bit early, we had horror scenarios of inward facing rooms with views of the air-con vents! Thankfully these fears were all unfounded and although we did not get a room looking out onto Times Square, we were facing Broadway and the Hershey's Building instead. 
The room was ok size wise and everything worked except that there wern't central controls for the lights ( = several trips out of bed to turn off the room lights). 
The bathroom was acceptable... the bath linen was nice. Only complaint which I can find (at a push) was that the air in the room seemed to be very dry and arid; am not sure if it was the effect of the heating (very effective) although we only had the heating on for short periods. 
The concierge (Omar and Davina) were SO helpful and I would highly recommend using them as a sounding board to enhance your trip to the Big Apple!
Overall though, I am happy with the room for what I paid.

title: “Great location.”
text: We were looking for a affordable hotel near Times Square and found the Edison Hotel. We are use to large hotel rooms and found quite the opposite. The bathroom was so small the toilet seat would not go down because it would get caught on the toilet tissue dispenser. Everytime you wanted to raise or lower the seat you would need to move the paper roll. The bathroom water pipe to the toilet was painted silver and the paint was peeling badly. The shower was very nice and had plenty of water pressure. The closet was big enough but probably had 10-20 coats of paint on the coat hooks. All in all, the hotel had a very good location(1/2 block off Times Square) and clean but small rooms that are not well decorated. Also, there is no view.

title: “Stylish, modern hotel in a great location”
text:
My wife and I stayed in four hotels in our recent trip across the US and this was our favourite. The location is great and was one of our key reasons for choosing Eventi. We arrived by train into New York Penn and it's only a short 5 min walk to the hotel. Being located on 6th Avenue at 30th Street means you're pretty central for the typical tourist area. The Empire State Building is just around the corner and Times Square is a 10 min stroll north.
The hotel itself is very clean and modern in terms of the reception area and the rooms. I was amazed, everything looked brand new. The room was very spacious with a generously proportioned bathroom. The décor made the room feel very special and the bed was extremely comfortable.
The staff were very helpful and check-in/out was a very swift process.
We paid £148 per room per night which is fairly pricey, but I didn't feel like I'd been short changed. The hotel and location were worth it.
My one issue with the hotel was the wi-fi access. Supposedly free, but we never managed to get it working. You have to fill in your details and wait for an email which gives you the necessary login details. Spot the big error here - how can I check my email if I don't have wi-fi?! 5 months later, the email still hasn't arrived...

title: “Location + Price= Can't Be Beat In Houston”
text: First off, the room is not going to wow you. I had a standard room and it is indeed small, with no view, but by yourself and even with one other it is more than manageable. If you are going to spend a lot of time in your room then maybe this isn't your hotel of choice. However, if you are just using it as a base of operations/place to sleep and relax, then it is hard to beat Club Quarters if you are on any type of budget. Smack dab in the middle of Houston within minutes of everything for less than $90/night on the weekends. Young professionals unquestionably should consider this place first and foremost.

title: “did not feel safe here”
text: We booked this hotel ahead of time as I was to have surgery in Houston. When we got there I did not feel safe at all. It was directly off the freeway. Our room was to the outside and I didn't think it was safe. The room was old, but clean. the air condition did not work well. I asked to cancel the room and the staff was very nice and let us. We then moved to another hotel. The price was good at only $70 but I felt much better when we moved.

title: “Mother's Day Overnight in the City”
text:
Love everything about this place....location, price, location, service, location...well, everything except parking. But there is something exciting about double parking on Powell Street on top of the cable car tracks to get valet service. Old-style building with really slow and small elevators but the room interiors have been nicely appointed and the beds are super comfortable. Great place for a late night lemoncello.
Stayed here half a dozen times. Never been disappointed. Price is reasonable for San Francisco Union Square.

title: “Could not have asked for a better trip!”
text: My son and I just returned from a trip to the Washington DC area on Friday the 27th. We stayed here and loved this hotel. We arrived very late on Monday due to a delayed flight and the hotel staff was very helpful in getting us bedding for the pull-out and some fliers for food delivery companies as the in-suite dining was closed. We began every morning with a fresh and ample breakfast and then just went down a couple of floors to the Metro. We were able to get to anywhere in DC area in less than a half an hour. The hotel is next to several great restaurants and since I was traveling just with my son, I was pleased that the area was very safe. I would recommend this hotel and its very helpful staff .

title: “Fabulous stay at the Affinia Dumont!!”
text:
My boyfriend and I have just returned from a week in the fabulous Affinia Dumont! We booked our flights to New York back in August, and then took time to research various hotels using trip advisor's reviews as our guide. Having booked the Affinia Dumont on the backing of previous reviews, we were not disappointed! 
We arrived at night, and were in awe of the view from our room when the bellboy pulled opened the curtains! Along with the magnificent Chrysler Building and the New York skyline just outside our window, the bell boy informed us that the building in front of us was the HQ of Opus Dei, corner of 34th st and Lexington, as mentioned in the Da Vinci code...nice little touch! We stayed on the 35th floor (room 3504), and every night we slept with the curtains open just to take in the spectacular scenery, (Worth requesting a high room before you go).
We had a lovely big room (suite), king size bed... extremely comfortable! There was a kitchenette off room with fridge, microwave etc., and a safe in the closet. No problems with heating and there was always hot water. Daily maid service, always clean.
The location is great, quiet residential area, able to get a good night's sleep to recharge for the next day, in comparison to hotels in the busier Time's Square district! There is a supermarket and a drug store conveniently situated just outside the hotel. TIP: The Murray Hill Diner around the block on Lexington Avenue does a great breakfast! and it has a great New York City diner atmosphere too. The staff were courteous, helpful, and friendly, and always greeted us with a smile. On the day we were leaving the bellboy arranged for us to travel to the airport in a private car for a flat rate of $65 including tip and toll charges. He said it would be 'a nice clean comfortable car'. To our surprise it was a white stretch limousine!. I was worried that when we arrived at the airport, the driver may have
asked us for a lot more than $65, but sure enough that's what it cost!
The Affinia Dumont is a fabulous hotel in every way, and we would have
no reservations about recommending it to others. It deserves to be in trip advisor's top ten most recommended hotels. We will definitely be returning to the Affinia Dumont on our next visit to NYC!!

title: “Pretty damn good for an airport hotel.”
text: Just there for few nights, for work. Nice resto, nice bar. Beautiful lobby. When I found the room i was in noisy, i was shifted to another swiftly but the young man at the front desk. His name was Justin, I think. Lovely service. It's near airport so there is noise, of course. But it's a great option if you have to be close to the airport. Business centre was in its own room and it was quiet. Oh, and there's room service.

title: “Perfect location”
text:
The hotel is situated in the very best place in the city. It is at half a block from Michigan Ave, where you have all the options for shopping and transportation and it is very close to the lake.
It is and old and historical building very well adapted to moder life. Beautiful and confortable bedrooms and bathrooms. The conmon areas are decorated with good taste.
The service is good. My only complait is the very high price of the internet service in the bussiness center.

title: “Good place to stay with family when visiting Chicago”
text: We just returned from a 5-day stay. The hotel was perfect for my family (2 adults and 2 kids) for our spring break visit to Chicago. The hotel is within walking distance to the Magnificent Mile and popular restaurants (Geno's East, Ed Debevics, Weber Grill, Carsons). The hotel gets business travelers and tourists, so at the breakfast buffet you will see people in suits sitting next to a table with kids in pajamas. The breakfast is good (waffles, cereals, eggs, fruit, yogurt, bagels, etc.). The hotel small is pool, but the kids still had lots of fun. Parking is in an adjacent garage that connects to the hotel ($40/day for hotel guests). I would definitely stay here again. Amanda Masters, the guest services manager, was very helpful in helping with my reservation.

title: “Great hotel for your $$$”
text: Hotel to my surprise was a great hotel. For the price you had a very comfortable bed, great pillows. Hotel was very clean, free coffee in the lobby. Rooms came with a fridge, microwave and a coffee maker. Conveinent to White House and many other locations. But what stood out the most was some of the staff. The bartender at the quaint bar in the lobby was amazing. He treated my kids with respect. Provided them with snacks and kiddy cocktails, even taught them a few magic trick. The waitress in the grill name Ines also was amazing. Giving our group extra attention, again treating my kids with care. She provided service beyond what most waitress will do. The only fault in the hotel was the valet parking. You can only park by valet, which if fine, but we had to go in the hotel and find someone to help us out.

title: “Great hotel, great location”
text: I stayed 2 nights at this hotel and it was a great experience. Nice room, friendly staff, great service. Location is excellent, walking distance from most of the main attractions in Chicago downtown. Internet and breakfast included, Internet was good but I think breakfast is their only weakness. Didn't like it. But overall, it was a great experience.

title: “Location, Location, Location”
text: The hotel works beautifully if you have a new student at SMU. Other wise, it's OK. The shower is nice, but the rooms are small. The suites work well to keep a student in your living room if you want them in with you. If you aren't doing womething with the school, then there are better places for better prices for what you get.

title: “Solid hotel, but there are much better Four Seasons”
text: We stayed here for 2 nights and it was a pleasant stay. The service was top notch as expected at a Four Seasons but we had a few issues. The room was a king bed; nothing special at all but nice. We were on the 11th floor with a city view and we were stunned at the level of noise. It is literally like the traffic is just outside your window - i had to check twice whether a window was open. I cannot believe that there are not doube paned glass windows. Try to get a floor as high as possible and perhaps the noise won't be so bad or stay away from a room facing Market street. The front entrance is ridiculous and it would have been nice to know that you cannot park out in front but in the rear of the hotel in a bit of a convulated path to get there. On Friday night, we stood in line for a taxi or house car and we waited for over 30 minutes while the incompetent doorman gave our vehicles away time and time again causing us to be late for dinner. That really soured our experience.

title: “Great Location, Big Rooms”
text:
When I booked this, I honestly didn't know if I did the right thing. Well, I did the right thing. The staff is friendly, the location is great. It is away from the tourist areas, but still withing walking distance of Times Square. Since my wife is a lite sleeper, we requested a high floor. We upgraded to a suite facing the Hudson and cruise terminal. The views are amazing. I thought I would want a city view , but this was amazing. The ships, boats, aircraft carrier views were great. The floor to ceiling windows are a real treat. My wife slept great because we hardly heard a sound from the streets.
I will come back and stay at this hotel next time I visit New York City.

title: “Amazing Location”
text:
We traveled to NYC in Oct for a long weekend getaway. I have been to New York several times but this was my girls first time visiting. The location was the best I have ever stayed. It is located in the heart of Times Square (keep in mind I love being in the heart of the city). Central Park / broadway shows are all within walking steps of this hotel. The rooms are clean and the beds are comfy. 
The hotel is pricey but its New York City, everything is expensive!!

title: “Reasonable airport hotel”
text: Having read some of the other comments, I would emphasize to anyone thinking about staying here that this is an airport hotel. Our accomodations were nice, there was a free breakfast and free wifi, and we swam in the indoor pool in the evening. There was a drink machine just down the hall and our room was spaceous, clean, and comfortable. There's a shuttle to and from the airport, although we did not use it. We got a great rate online, obviously better than some of the other posters. The Days Inn is certainly not the Ritz but it was fine for my family. Again, it's an airport hotel. Enough said.

title: “Exceptional Experience”
text: Stayed here for one night July 5th. The Iroquois is a lovely small hotel, gorgeous atmosphere, with the most attentive staff I have ever experienced in any hotel. I highly recommend it to anyone wishing to stay in the Midtown area, as the hotel is literally within sight of Times Square and a short walk to Rockefeller Center.

title: “Solid choice and convenient, safe location.”
text: I was pleased with my decision to stay at park 79 hotel. The rooms are small but not extremely cramped. The bathroom looked brand new and everything wa very clean. The service was friendly and prompt every day, every shift. Best of all, the location allowed easy access to a vatiety of sights and experiences. We felt very safe in the area. My only complaint was that other guests were loud when returning at night, and the wooden floors inthe halls caised the noise to echo- it was annoying.

title: “Friendly staff, large clean rooms, great location FREE WIFI”
text: After an unfortunate experience at the Latham hotel, we happened upon the Warwick, late in the evening looking for a room. They couldn't have been more accommodating and gave us a reduced room rate. The room was twice the size of the Latham hotel, and spotlessly clean. There was a large air-conditioned lobby with free iced tea and lemon water. It was a pleasure to stay at the Warwick!

title: “Passable”
text: New decor, pretty and clean room, very friendly staff. Breakfast was as expected,no frills. Complaints: my credit card was denied and I had to use another. It should not have been denied, it was my Marrott Rewards card, and I had just paid the bill. I had to use another card and now will not get the extra points. I asked to use one of my free nights and was told I had to make those arrangements in advance. I don't have to stay here again.

title: “great hotel in a great location”
text: When I booked this, the price was low so I was expecting something sort of marginal in terms of comfort and cleanliness, but I was wonderfully surprised. I had a great room with a comfortable bed and beautiful bathroom. I'll stay here again!

title: “Beautiful Hotel in a great location!”
text: We stayed at the Pacific Terrace Hotel the first weekend in October (2012). We had stellar weather and the hotel was really wonderful. The location is perfect - right on the boardwalk, only about a 30 second walk to the beach. The pool and hotel grounds are well maintained. There are plenty of places to walk to while you are here and the main attractions are very close - Sea World was only about 10 mins away. We stayed in 2 different rooms (I booked last minute and that's all they had for us). I would definitely recommend the suites over the regular rooms - they are much larger and that made it more comfortable for us. The full ocean view was awesome, too. This is a small boutique hotel, so they don't have their own restaurant - but, my husband and I both agreed they did a great job with breakfast. Having breakfast at the hotel was very convenient. Lastly, the staff really made the biggest impression on us - they are all very friendly (and sincere about it!) and they do everything to help accommodate your needs. I will recommend this hotel to my friends and we will return to this hotel when we visit San Diego, again!

title: “central location, quiet room”
text: The hotel has been designated some sort of historic hotel landmark, and has been beautifully renovated while retaining its charm of an earlier era. I spent two nights here with a friend in a quiet, attractive room. The window faced onto an interior space looking into some office windows, but this meant there was no street noise and felt very peaceful. The room itself had 2 Queen beds, a little sitting/kitchen room, a small dressing room, and bathroom - all very comfortable, attractively decorated, and immaculately clean. We had a well-prepared and filling breakfast both mornings in their dining room, and at surprisingly reasonable prices for a hotel breakfast. There is also a comfortable and attractive bar. All the personnel were efficient and friendly.

title: “"THE BEDS ARE TO DIE FOR!!!!!"”
text:
My wife and I have stayed there the last week of August for the last 5 years. The beds are the most comfortable I've ever slept in. The hotel staff has always been TOP NOTCH. Everything the great city of Detroit has to offer is at your fingertips. Looking forward to returning again this year. 
Please remember to go to Forty-Two Degrees North for the breakfast buffet. Made to order and Alfresco even. The views from this restaurant of the Detroit River and all of the excitement the goes along with it makes breakfast very enjoyable.

title: “Great Value for NYC!!”
text: The Salisbury is in a great location within the city!! Its clean, the staff is friendly and helpful. The hotel is an older building with basic features, but the room was much larger than I expected. If I got back to NYC I will certainly considering staying at the Salisbury again.

title: “Cheap and well located”
text:
Not much you can't say about the hotel as it's a Best Western and you really couldn't expect too much from them. The hotel is only a few blocks from train station so it's very convenient getting around town. 
The room is not big and renovation is needed as it's pretty old. The bed were comfortable and it's not the cleanest hotel I had been to but the price is very reasonable for a short trip to New York.

title: “Business visit”
text:
I stayed here for four night whilst seeing to some business nearby. Standard hotel, I would say three star sort of level and it is out of town. The bar is excellent. There is a full gym which requires you to swipe your room card to get in. The pool was not looked after and if you are a smoker, you have to smoke in the car parking area as there is no facilities for smoking in. The fine for smoking in the room was cautioned to me as 100 dollars or so.
The facility is suitable for short business trips and is more adequately described a a motel, rather than a hotel.
Nothing is here for families or kids if you are after entertainment. This is a business hotel.
Positive comments: The bed. The bed is first class Sheraton comfort. I could sleep in it for a week. Very comfortable beds and adequate working space in the rooms.

title: “Perfect position, great room, fair price.”
text:
This is a new hotel and was still finding its way when we stayed there but considering that everything went well. The pool on the roof wasn't yet open but it looked a very promising facility with a comfortable seating area and great views. Unfortunately the rooftop bar appears to have been contracted out to be run as a bar/night club so was only open in the evening when it attracted a lively and youngish crowd from outside (it had its own separate entrance and elevator from the street level). This meant that we couldn´t go up for a drink, for instance, at midday. We didn't eat breakfast in the hotel because we walked to our daughter and son-in-law who live nearby. However we understand from other guests we knew that it is more than adequate.
Location is perfect within easy walking distance of all parts of lower Manhattan from China Town and South Street Seaport in the East to the riverside walks along the Hudson to the West, Wall Street in the South and the wonderful High Line Park to the North. And for shopping nothing can beat Lower Broadway, just around the corner!
We got a great week-end deal, three nights for the cost of two nights.

title: “GoBrewers!”
text: In town for family vacation to see different MLB ballparks. My family of 3 stayed mid-week for a Tigers game. This hotel is right downtown and within easy walking distance. The hotel staff was very pleasant and accomodating assisting with luggage, parking and directions to our next destination. The hotel was clean and comfortable. The rooms are a little smaller then some of the newer hotels but I attribute that to a building in a big city. The breakfast was average - nothing special but just fine. Be aware that Detroit is a shell of a city. Very depressed area. Walk with a partner.

title: “Executive Lounge makes the difference”
text: My wife and I were here for a CME conference at the convention center she was attending. We booked 3 nights as this is the only hotel that has a covered bridge to the convention center so you can walk right over regardless of the weather. You can choose to self park or valet. We opted for valet at a cost of $30 a night. But there is a covered walking bridge to the parking garage next door if you want. Our room was on the Executive lounge floor with a King size bed and lots of room on the granite top writing desk. We upgraded to the Executive King room for $19.95 a night as it included WiFi ($15 a day otherwise) and access to the Executive lounge. The lounge offers private access with free continental breakfast and snacks and appetizers in the evening. Coffee and beverages included as well. An adult bar is in the lounge for an additional charge. The coffee offered is much better than the coffee you get from brewing yourself in the room. The fruit and pastries are fresh and of restaurant quality. If you want to get the most out of your stay and have added value upgrade to the Executive Lounge. I am thankful we did! PS. The blanket included on our bed was very very warm. If you like a cool night's sleep as we do just use covered sheets as the comforter will lock in all your heat.

title: “Price is Right”
text: I found a great rate for this hotel online so decided to give it a try. I just wanted a basic hotel with clean, friendly service, basically a place to crash with no complaints after busy days of touring. I was very pleased with my stay. The staff was very helpful and friendly. The room was basic but just what we needed, nothing special, but nothing to worry about. I liked the location, it was easy to get anywhere in the city via the very nearby subway station. We requested a room higher up and they were more then happy to accommodate. Was exactly what I was looking for.

title: “awesome experience”
text: Although using Hotwire is a crap shoot, boy am I glad that it was this hotel. This was my first time in LA and the experience could not have been better. We had a car, but we were able to find street parking, which is free and without restriction on Wilshire between Selby and Manning. Parking on Manning you'll have to move every two hours, but can park after 6pm until 10am the next day. I know they say the charge for parking is comparable to surrounding areas, but $30 + tax and don't forget tip per day is a bit much. That being said, the valets there were very friendly and greeted us each time we approached the hotel. I heard the hotel had been recently renovated and it showed. The lobby was nice. We loved the strawberry water and the free coffee and tea each morning. The rooms were exceptionally clean. Not only could I see that our room was clean, it smelled clean when you opened the door each day. I loved the toiletries in the bathroom. We had lunch in the restaurant and we were not disappointed. Prices were reasonable for lunch and the sandwiches and potato salad was devine. The complimentary use of umbrellas provided in our room was a nice touch and needed, considering it rained our first night there. We walked to Whole Foods nearby and bought fruit and snacks. We ordered room service on our last night for dinner. I don't think the same chef was there. My club sandwich was greasy and my sisters salad hardly had any chicken but we ate most of it anyway because we had an early flight. I went to the business center to print our boarding pass for the next day and discovered that it would cost us approximately $7 to use the computer and print our passes. I called the front desk however, and they were able to print them for us. Since they already provide free in room wi-fi, which I love, there should be a way to print the boarding pass, since wireless printing technology is out there. All in all, our trip was awesome and this hotel played a big part in making our stay enjoyable. The location is central to anything you came to LA to do, so if you don't want to see the sights then get away to have a restful sleep, this hotel is for you.

title: “Enjoyable Stay!”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for 2 nights and it was a very good stay. I picked this hotel because when traveling with our young children, we like to have an indoor pool where we can hang out. I was surprised to see how many hotels in Columbus had outdoor (seasonal) pools. This hotel had an indoor one, which was very important to us.
Overall the hotel was clean, extremely quiet, and the staff was very friendly. When we travel I appreciate when hotels are quiet, and this was so quiet it was hard to believe there were other guests in the hotel! We saw them but we never heard them. I booked the room by calling the hotel directly. They offered the same price i was getting on the internet and it was nice to talk to someone to request the exact room that we wanted. They were very accommodating with my requests and answered all my questions over the phone w/o a problem. When we arrived, we found everything as we had requested. The pool was a little on the small side but it served its purpose. However, the area around the pool could have been a bit cleaner. My husband used the exercise room and said it was perfect. 
The only problem we had with the hotel was at the restaurant. One time we ate there, they had nothing on the Kids Menu that we requested (but they did the next day). One night when we had dinner, they totally messed up my husband's supper and ended up giving it to him for free. I think there was a problem with the chef. Also kids eat for free and while we gave them the coupon for the Kids Free Meal we were always charged for it and i had to ask to have those charges removed. I don't understand why i had to request this all the time and wondered if it was a scam. The staff was always nice about it and removed it w/o a problem and they were very nice to the kids. They offer room service but we did not use it.
The room was clean and quiet. The beds were comfortable and the room had a fridge, a microwave and even an ihome charger/radio that allowed us to charge our ipods and iphones. We also appreciated the free parking. 
Overall we had a great stay and would definitely return to this hotel when we were in the area again but we might skip the restaurant and eat elsewhere. The area around the hotel has every store and restaurant one might need to shop at. They also have 2 markets nearby.

title: “Great experience!!!”
text:
We needed a place to stay for 3 months while we waited on our new home and we definately picked a winner! The staff and accomodations were great! The location was ideal and the full breakfast buffet and Tues-Thurs evening meals were tasty and saved us a lot of money! I'd gladly stay there again and would highly recommend this hotel. As a Soldier I felt appreciated and supported by Nathan and the staff; two thumbs up!!! 
CPT Derek Strong

title: “Excellent Value”
text:
Based on the price and what you get, this place was better then expected. Updated with clean, new furnishings, comfortable bed and sofa sleeper. Breakfast was plain but enough to get you out the door to your destination. Parking is Free . Walking Distance to all attractions by the river or on the street level. The Alamo, La Villita, and The Riverwalk. Walking on the street level at night back to the Hotel, I DO NOT recommend, not safe. Don't risk. I did it with my family. Walk on the riverwalk level or take a cab.
Friendly Staff. Congratulations Management, Good Team. I think they went above and beyond their job descriptions. Ordered us a Pizza. Directions. We also left something of value behind and they returned it. Thanks....

title: “Setting the standard.......”
text:
First impressions are good, the hotel is constructed on massive concrete stilts so it looks quite impressive. The bell boy was quick to get to us and take our bags, and walking in to reception you realise this hotel is brand new... cutting edge design and an uber cool feel to the whole place. The elevator has got to be the best elevator i have ever been in, cannot explain here, just go in it! 
Got into the room and was impressed again with the design and layout, room size is not massive, however the bath certainly is! A glass wall which seperates the bathroom from the living room enables you to watch the flatscreen whilst soaking....
It was dark when we arrived and we were on the 14th so an impressive nightscape of New York and the Empire state building meant it just felt wrong to close the curtains.
Go downstairs and there is a very cool bar, full of smiley faces and generally very good atmosphere. 
Would recommend to anyone visiting NY.

title: “Boutique hotel with a great location”
text:
Two weeks prior, I was in town with several girl friends and we stayed in a boutique hotel in SoHo. This time around, with my husband, we decided to stay midtown on 5th for several reasons...shopping on 5th and Reebok CrossFit on 5th. For a quick weekend getaway, we wanted to be close to everything we wanted to do. The Reebok CrossFit gym was right on the corner for our daily workouts and shopping was a few steps away as well.
Location: Great!
Rooms: Its smaller than other boutique places in NYC we've stayed at but not the smallest room we've stayed at either. They managed to fit a desk/dresser on one wall with enough room to pull a chair out before hitting the foot of the queen bed. 2 side tables and a side chair. A small closet with a safe tucked inside. Clean room and bathroom but needs an upgrade due to visible marks on the bathroom sink and desk.
Restaurant: We only had breakfast there, a bit pricey and they got my husbands order incorrect and didn't offer to fix it. We were in a hurry so we didn't pursue the issue. 
Bar (Top of the Strand): They had the whole thing shutdown one night from 4-10p for a private function and they sent up a free drink coupon that same night. We found that odd but I suppose it was meant to be for the next night? We did enjoy the bar/DJ the following evening and the view of Empire State was spectacular. It was raining that evening so the roof was closed but the view was nevertheless fantastic.
Front desk/reception: Pleasant, we arrived early so they didn't have our room ready but they did call us when it was which was much appreciated.
Doormen: Pleasant and helpful when they were there. I'm not sure if they had shift work or they weren't supposed to be there at night but it wasn't consistent. One doorman stood in the foyer while we were trying to come in from the rain. Another doorman was fabulous in hailing us a cab.

title: “Delightful Hotel and Amazing Staff”
text: We arrived at the Arctic Club Hotel a little before check-in time and were greeted with a smile. One of the two rooms was not ready so we left the luggage in the other room and went out to explore the town. The front desk was nice enough to call us when the second room was ready. We loved the little details at the hotel like the walrus room numbers, the absolutely beautiful ballroom, the explorer decorations, the free internet and printing, and the warm cookies. We couldn't resist lounging in the bar area and partaking in the fancy-schmancy drink of the day. Our bartender made a champagne, vodka, chambord concoction that was delicious! A week after our stay, when we came back from our Alaskan cruise, we wanted to walk around Seattle, and the hotel staff were nice enough to let us keep our luggage in the hotel until we had to leave for the airport.

title: “A glimpse of luxury, but not in our room.”
text:
Like others, I read the reviews on here and was excited about having a night in this location. After one night, however, I'm sure that there must be other places a little further away from Union Square with much more appeal.
We arrived early, hoping to store our bags for the day. Instead, we were told that we could check in but that the room was at the front of the building, so could be a bit noisy. In hindsight, I should have remembered the statements on Tripadvisor about the noise and turned it down - so I'm partly to blame for my complaint. We're usually able to sleep through most things and didn't mind one night, but it was so loud! It felt like there wasn't a window between us and outside at all.
