Aside from that, our room was cosy and the hotel was convenient for the BART and restaurants. The bathroom was a little old and battered, but it was easy to ignore. They also tried to sting us with ridiculous phone charges for calls that couldn't be connected, but luckily (after some strong words on check out), these were cleared. We're still waiting for the refund back onto our credit card though.

title: “Affordable, compact NYC swank”
text:
Yes, the rooms are tiny. That should not be a surprise to anyone who has stayed in Manhattan. But they are spotless, stylish, and very well designed - bathroom shelves, a roomy closet, good bedside tables, pocket doors, an iron and a place to use it.
The lobby is very cosmopolitain. The Library Bar and attached restaurant are super convenient - nice enough to entertain friends, but casual enough to just hang out in when you don't feel like going out. 
Desk staff is lovely, elevators are fast, beds are comfy, walls and floors are thick enough to keep sound to a minimum. And the location is fantastic.

title: “Too Isolated For Us”
text: When visiting San Diego my wife and I normally stay Downtown near the Gaslamp District. This time we stayed at the Sheraton on Harbor Island. If you don't mind being away from the action the hotel is nice. We walked around the marina and the island looking for something to do. We finally got in our car and went to Ocean Beach to watch the sunset. Then we went to the Gaslamp District to party. On the way back to the hotel a group of bicyclists named Critical Mass were doing their best to obstruct traffic the entire length of Harbor Drive from the Downtown to the Airport. At the main intersection between the airport and the Sheraton dozens of them rode in cirlces obstructing the intersection for about 8 minutes. When we got back to the hotel all the $22 self parking spots were taken. They finally let us valet our car without charging us extra. When we got back to the room it was hot. The air conditioner wasn't working. They sent a maintenance man up to fix it. He found that the system that shuts off the AC when the balcony door is opened wasn't working (even though the balcony door was closed and locked). He had to bypass that system to get the AC working. In the future we'll stay downtown near the Gaslamp District where we've never had problems.

title: “Great Hotel, Great Service, Great Stay!”
text: I had a wonderful experience with this Holiday Inn. I typically stay at Marriot Hotels but was unable to this time and I found the Holiday Inn that was located closed to down town Dallas and every where I needed to go. This hotel has changed my opinion of Holiday Inns and I would recommend this hotel to anybody and I would definitely stay in this Holiday Inn again. I experienced great service from the time I walked in the hotel until I left. The rooms were very clean and everybody that works at this hotel has great customer service.

title: “A Bad Experience”
text:
The hospitality is very bad. The manager is very rude, 1-800 calls from the hotel aren't free and they are very expensive, the room is dirty, the bed is full of hair,we had to change the sheets at 8:00 in the evening. We Had a HORRIBLE EXPERIENCE. I recommend not to go there.
DONT GO THERE!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

title: “No problems”
text:
I read that the previous reviewer had problems with the service, but I'm pretty sure they are not because of priceline.
We booked through priceline for 2 days. Quick check-in, got a great room on a high floor (facing fox studios). Did not have any problems at all. Of course, we did not order any food. Valet parking is $30, usually dont prefer it but there is no choice here. However, the valet was flawless, never waited for more than a few minutes. The room was very spacious, with a separate study area and balcony. 
On the other side, nothing is free in this hotel (nor did I expect it to be). Internet access is $10/day, even toll-free calls are $1, the minibar seal is better left unbroken. Called to find if they have a DVD player, but they did not. I think the hotel needs to start thinking about upgrading to flat panel televisions as well. 
The area is clean and upscale. The Westfield Century city mall is nearby and walkable. The food court there is a possible alternative for food. For everything else, a car is needed. Rodeo drive is just 5-10 mins by car. Parking is surprisingly cheap at rodeo drive (sometimes even free). To those visiting Disneyland (we did not), it is probably better to stay in/around the Anaheim area and save on commute time. For exploring western los angeles (hollywood, beverly hills, universal studios, santa monica etc.) this location is great.

title: “Four Points LAX”
text: I took advantage of the FOUR POINTS LAX Park and Travel program for a business trip and was completely delighted with my experience. Not only is it a great value for a longer trip to leave your car there, but the hotel accommodations were excellent. Best pillows on the bed which made the quick overnight a pleasure. The room was very nice and clean and well appointed. The ammenities in the Restaurant and Bar are beautiful. It is all upscale. The check in person was helpful and extremely friendly. I will definitely do it again.

title: “Perfect choice...”
text:
I stayed at the Orlando in L.A. for one night but could have stayed longer. Located in the Beverly Center area of L.A., the hotel is situated perfectly. 
The Orlando is a contemporary-style property with a chic vibe. My room was spacious, clean and comfortable. The bathroom 
was really nice with a nice assortment of toiletries. I was on the fourth floor facing Third Street, had a beautiful view and street noise was not a problem at all.
The staff are friendly and very accommodating. I arrived early and my room wasn't ready. The desk personnel took my cell phone number and called as soon as the room was ready.
There is a pool and restaurant/bar on the premises, and the hotel is within walking distance of several restaurants, cafes and stores. Magnolia Bakery, of New York fame, is across the street as is the Traveler's Bookcase, my favorite travel bookstore! 
I would stay at the Orlando again as the rate of around $200 is reasonable given the location and quality of the property.
Parking is $29 per night which is a deal considering I received a $63 ticket for parking on the "preferential parking" streets of the surrounding residential area. Live and learn!

title: “Great Hotel”
text: I was relunctant to book this hotel after reading the poor reviews, but the price was too good to resist. My stay was wonderful. I was only there one night, but would definately go back. We were able to check in to our room early and it looked like the room had just been renovated. The vanities were granite and the decor was very nice. The desk staff was very pleasant when I checked in and out, and helpful with directions. They only offer valet parking, but we asked about alternatives, and we were directed to a garage around the corner that was $15/day. The hotel is walking distance to Camden Yards. Other reviews complain about noise, but we were not in our hotel room until very late, so it wasn't an issue. I would definately recommend this hotel, especially for those like us who don't spend a lot of time in their rooms, but still want a nice room to sleep in.

title: “Budget hotel, good location, does the job”
text: This place is nothing fancy, but serves it's purpose, was much cheaper than other places in Hollywood and is well located just off Hollywood Blvd. They also let you store your bags in their office after you've check out (my flight back home wasn't until the evening).I'd stay again no worries.

title: “A slice of heaven!”
text: I cannot say enough great things about this fabulous hotel. I am a very particular traveler, and have stayed in some of the most spectacular and luxurious hotels across the globe... Hotel 1000 is right at the top of my list as one of my favorites. From the moment you step out of your car and are greeted by their fabulous valet staff, you know you've arrived at somewhere special. The staff is exceptionally friendly and helpful - even offering cold champagne at check in. The rooms are so technologically advanced, it's amazing! I cannot say enough about the "H1K'. If you get a chance to stay here, don't pass it by. You will NOT be sorry!

title: “Great Central Location”
text: We chose this hotel because of its close proximity to the DCPA since were were in town to see a show. The complimentary Wi-Fi was a bonus, and we appreciated the covered parking attached to the hotel. The staff was very nice and helpful, the room was very clean, and the central location was great. We would definitely stay there again.

title: “I LOVE this place!”
text: I stayed overnight, and this is my first stay in this hotel. I can't say enough wonderful things about this hotel. I slept on a cloud of a bed with soft sheets and a soft light comforter. I had curtains that blocked out the light from outside and a NICE flat screen TV to watch. A hot shower with lots of power. I know cities and I carry soft earplugs to block out any background sound. Best sleep I have had in years.

title: “Outstanding Place to stay”
text:
Great clean place close to the Riverwalk. Hostess Georgia Rios was so friendly and made by family feel so at home. I watched Georgia work the breakfast area as if it was her own home. She was so bubbly and friendly and wanted to care for our every need. The whole staff was the so friendly and wanted to make our stay as pleasant as possible. I don't know who is in charge of hiring, but whoever it is has found the magic formula for hiring great people. 
The hotel was clean, spacious and very well maintained. I told Georgia that I would be back next March for the Alamo Celebration with the Masons.

title: “Clean, good breakfast, super easy commute to airport”
text: Great room and bathroom. Very clean and an excellent continiental breakfast. Not easy to get into garage ... very little warning that is in the location it is. Stayed on our last night of a San Fran trip flying home from San Jose. Neighborhood seemed a bit sketchy but no problems at all and staff was pleasant aand helpful.

title: “Good choice if you're not planning on spending too much time at the hotel”
text: I stayed here for one night before running the San Diego half marathon. The location was good for that since the hotel was approximately 5 miles from Sea World where the race parking was located. The hotel was clean but not remarkable. It is located right off the highway, but is very quiet. The hotel staff was very helpful in giving us a great recommendation for Mexican food in Old Town- Cafe Coyote. There is a $12 a night charge for parking per car. This was a fine place to sleep, but I wouldn't go out of my way to stay here.

title: “A great place to stay, especially if you're going to an event nearby.”
text: We stayed here for a weekend with our daughter & her family, while our daughter was standing up at a friend's wedding. The staff was very helpful with arranging adjoining rooms, a toy for our granddaughter, a crib, and late check-out to accommodate a nap. I have no idea if this is a convenient location for anything but a wedding nearby because we didn't really go anywhere else. There was a children's park within a mile and the area is lovely to walk around (though no one in LA walks), and there was a great restaurant not too far away that accommodated the adults and our grandchild. There was a heated pool which was a great way to spend some time with our granddaughter. The restaurant staff was very kind and allowed her to have run of the room. The food was also good and fairly reasonable, a double bonus. The hotel offered wine every evening to guests.

title: “Loews service is great.”
text:
I stay at this property around 20-25 nights a year. The staff is friendly and professional and many have been in place for longer than I have been staying with them.
They will start a full remodeling this fall and will move to the top tier in Denver when they finish.

title: “Good location and price”
text:
The Omni Jacksonville is a good place to stay for the price and location if you want to stay in downtown. 
I have had issues with staff banging on my door at 9:00 am to check the mini bar or housekeeping barging in around 10:00 am. If they could fix these issues I would highly recommend the Omni, for now I can only give them an average recommendation.

title: “This is a conference center...not a typical resort.”
text: Think of a colllege campus on steroids -- there are multiple hotel towers and separate wings. All room access is exterior corridor style. LOTS of walking, with two major conference center buildings and numerous meeting buildings. I never did find the Spa or bar. Rooms are very clean and real maintained, but design tends to be more formal...many of our attendees referred to expecting to see the Rat Pack. However, the gardens are fabulous and the staff is superb. Wait staff supported formal dinner functions flawlessly, and no matter where you went, someone was offering to be of assistance. AV support was excellent, lighting was good, and support of a large food show was very good. One hint: Sinks in bathrooms are REALLY low; I'm only 5'2" and had to bend to brush my teeth, so if you're tall, expect to do a LOT of bending over! :-) Plenty of hot water however. The pillows are awful - think ancient and hard!

title: “Best Beds!”
text: I loved this hotel. The beds were absolutely wonderful, one of the most comfortable hotel beds I have ever slept in. This says a lot because I travel all the time. The rooms were spacious and the staff was always friendly and helpful. I will definitely be back!

title: “very good customer service”
text: Mr Anwar at the front desk gave us a very good service . He was very polite and very fast in replying any questions we had.

title: “Could've been better.. front staff not helpful at all.”
text:
Stayed at this hotel for Comic Con 2011... we paid $302 a night after taxes, which is hard to swallow considering this hotel normally commands around $129+taxes/nt, and I see why. Located in the Downtown area, this hotel is close to a lot of restaurants and bars, as well as the mall.. however it is also rife with homeless. They are fairly non invasive compared to San Francisco, so that was a positive. Rooms were smallish and my room was not very clean (toenail clippings on floor, bathroom a bit dirty).. but it wasn't bad. Linens were fabulous, as was the water pressure in the bathroom. A lot of hotels have a noisy bathroom, this one does not! We were able to bathe and use the restroom at night without waking the others in the room. However --the bathroom does have the pull doors, so that can get clanky.
You can decline housekeeping during your stay and receive a $5 voucher for the gift shop.. however be warned you have to put the placard about housekeeping on your door (small print). We declined housekeeping by leaving our do not disturb sign up 24/7 as we have done with other hotels and were denied our vouchers... when asked, the front desk staff were not able to verify if our room had been cleaned or not. Seemed like a gimmick to not pay out the vouchers.
The front desk staff here are awful! We were booked for a club room floor, but were put on the 23rd floor instead. I had 3 people in my room, and was only given two keys and no breakfast vouchers... nor was I told about the Club Lounge or any other hotel amenities. I had to return to the front desk for my 3rd key and breakfast items. I inquired about checkout times and what time I had to have my car out of the parking garage on our last day, and could not get a straight answer. I would have appreciated being told about what elevators take you where in the hotel, as we had to figure out the elevator hopping by ourselves and it was very confusing for the first 2 days. I also was not given the shuttle information and maps provided by SDCC to the hotels to give to the guests... all the other hotels I visited in past years as well as stopped by in on this visit had their information prominently displayed. 
Breakfast (the buffet) was very respectable. Lots of cold and hot items, the orange juice and cottage cheese here are excellent (lots of places have yucky versions).. the wait staff was amazing. Very polite, helpful and quick to respond to your needs. The waitstaff was the best part of this hotel. 
Parking: It's not fun getting up to the 12th floor, but it's not the nightmarish corkscrew other reviews have said it to be. With that said, I never moved my car the 4 days we were here because it wasn't worth the hassle for me. 
In short... I wouldn't return unless the rate was $149/nt or less. The negative items outweighed the positives, and I've stayed in better hotels for less than the $300 we were charged. A lot of basic hotel procedures were skipped by the staff here, including being helpful and properly cleaning our room before our arrival.

title: “Nothing bad to say, but was just OK”
text: I travel frequently for work and find myself in hotels at least 75 nights out of the year. Fairmont hotels are supposed to be "breathtaking" and "top notch." While I can't really say too much bad about this hotel, I'll just say I don't think it would be worth the month for a regular rate. We received a corporate rate of $229 per night and I can honestly say I've received better rooms at a Hilton Garden Inn. The room wasn't ready when I arrived at 4pm which was odd because check-in was at 3pm. So I waited a while and was assigned a room on the 5th floor. It was just OK, nothing real special about it, just a standard hotel room. The food in the bar and restaurant is WAY overpriced, but I guess that is to be expected for San Francisco. If you want to get to the attractions of SFO this hotel is not real convenient, but it is a short ride on the trolley or by cab. Overall I'd have to say it wasn't BAD, but for the price most would pay for a regular rate, I'd check out less expensive options.

title: “Not that great”
text:
I would have to agree with the previous poster regarding the service. I'm not a person who requires hotel employees to go out of their way to be friendly but no one at the front desk ever greeted me or showed any interest in me, whatsoever. They behaved so strangely, for example, when I checked in, I gave my name and the employee pulled out a piece of printed paper waved it at me as if to show me the print (which I couldn't see) and said my name aloud as if to say to me: "Here, I found your paperwork!". When I checked out, the clerk assumed that the woman standing next to me was with me (she wasn't -- ok, he couldn't have known that) but after getting both our room numbers, he printed my paperwork and then turned to her to give her her paperwork. By that point, he was ignoring me. The other clerk, stood behind him watching their interaction and I had to gently flag down that person to hand my bag over to him. None of this was terrible, of course, but I've stayed at lots of JDV hotels, and the service is always top notch. I'm guessing that this hotel is not owned by JDV but is simply "sold" by them.
I hope when the management responds to this posting that the manager discloses the hotel's relationship to JDV.
On another matter, I found the room very noisy. I stayed near the elevator (and although there was a utility room between my room and the elevator), I could hear the elevator opening and closing all night (and into the early morning hours). I am not a light sleeper but I would have to say that the other guests that returned to their rooms saw no problem with talking loudly and laughing loudly as they tromped down the halls to their rooms. In addition, the doors to the rooms are on heavy springs so after being serenaded by other guests in the hallway, I got used to the loud slamming of their doors when they entered. There are also a lot of noises in the room. There is some sort of ventilation system in bathroom that you cannot control that makes a lot of noise. (I closed the door to the bathroom to lessen it). In addition, there was a refrigerator (which was empty), which turned on only once and scared the living daylights out of me. I quickly got up and turned it off.
Lastly, both my friend (who stayed on the top floor near the rear of the hotel) and myself had trouble regulating the temperature in the room. The first thing you have to be aware of is that the switch marked "air conditioning" is both the A/C and the heat. So, if the room is cold, turn on the A/C and then set the thermostat to the temperature you want and the heat will come on. Even with the "A/C" turned off, one night, the room was on the warm side because, I am guessing, the person below me must have had their heat turned up high. I didn't want to turn on the real air conditioning in February just to combat the heat from downstairs so I put up with it.
The hotel has a cute motif and the neighborhood is pleasant. We had a car but used public transit which was easy to access. I can't say that I would return to this hotel any time soon.

title: “Freezing..”
text:
We stayed in queen room with two beds although we were looking for one king size bed. The receptionist said that they didn't guarantee single or two beds, they didn't have one because we were late! Anyway the room was clean and really large, bathroom was clean, too. But we didn't have a miniref in the room and I didn't ask why not because it was a one night stay.. Then, the room was freezing; although we turned off the AC it was still cold and we had to cover quilt.
Breakfast room was fine, we were seated. Actually I can't say I was satisfied with the breakfast itself. The service was good but in fact the continental breakfast can be better. We had better continental breakfasts in SF and NY hotels. My brother and his wife chose to have breakfast out. They told they were freezed in their room, too. 
The subway station is close so if you're looking for a clean, safe and a budget hotel, you must check this hotel.

title: “Love the Hotel”
text:
Love the view from the room even thought we had the economy special. We could see the Alamo and the Riverwalk. It seems that all the rooms have great views. 
Jose Rosales was a great help during checkout. He was helpful and pleasant.

title: “Days inn San Antonio Lackland”
text: We had a good time.Nice staff, hot breakfast, comfortable beds, wifi and cooling and heat good. Hot showers. I know it is an older hotel but it served our purposes. Very close to Lackland AFB and not too hard to find. Several other hotels nearby.Parking was easy too, didn't have to park far. We were in the inner section by the pool. Didn't use the pool but it was very nice too. I was really impressed by the hot breakfast. Didn't have to worry where to go eat. We were there for our graduate from BMT and it was so nice to be close by.

title: “** Do Not Stay Here**”
text:
I stayed here for one night and will never stay here again. In fact, I will never stay at any W Hotel again because of this experience. I know it is New York so I expected to pay a lot for a nice room, but the room wasn't even close to being nice. The room was very worn...it felt dirty and was in major need of an overhaul. Wallpaper was peeling off the walls. The hvac unit in the room was broken and blew freezing cold air all night. I have never stayed in such a small hotel room in my life and I was in one of their bigger rooms. The room next to me had an all night party going and I could hear everything. 
 But the cherry on top was of course the bill. $60 for parking...I took the train up and hence had no car to park, but they charged me anyway. State Tax $30.82; Occupancy/Tourism Tax $2.00; NYS Javits Ctr Tax $1.50; Room Tax $18.40. Another $60 for "Concessions & Commissions". I did not have the time or the energy to argue about the bill on my way out, so the W Hotel one that battle as I am sure it was their intention.
 I left feeling completely ripped off and taken advantage of. There are a lot of hotels in the Midtown area to choose from, so do yourself a favor and stay somewhere else. The W was terrible in every respect.

title: “San Deigo Vacation”
text: La Quinta Inn San Diego Old Town is a very nice place to stay. The hotel staff is very friendly and helpful. The hotel is clean and well maintained. The beds were extremely comfortable and we slept very well. We had a king bedroom. The room was very clean and well maintained. The pool and spa area was also very well maintained. Although the hotel was next to the freeway and airport, our room was very sound proof and we didn't hear any noise. The breakfast was pretty basic, waffles, toast, muffins, danish, some fruit, hot and cold cereal, juice, coffee. They do charge $10 a day for parking, not a fan. Parking is underground and secure, but little tight if you drive a large vehicle, but it's doable. Overall, I was very happy with our stay. The location is great and convenient to get to all the attractions, old town, seaport village, coronado island, sea world, airport, balboa park, mission bay beach...all within 5- 15 minutes to get to these.

title: “Excellent value”
text: Rooms are clean, well eqipped and laid out, excellent value. Breakfast is marginal, but overall you cannot find a better value in this area. Also the shuttle drivers go out of their way to please. Great Value, Good service.

title: “Comfort in the Big Apple”
text: I am a big fan of Hampton Inn in general, and this one in particular. While the price is over twice what I usually pay for a Hampton room, it IS right where you want to be in New York City. Located in the Theatre District it is close to many things - walking distance to Times Square, Central Park, Lincoln Center, Rockefeller Center - and it’s a block from the 50th Street subway stop on line 1, so you can take a subway to almost everything else on Manhattan. The breakfast is first rate - with a different hot egg dish every day plus waffles, hot and cold cereals, fruit, juice, etc. Coffee and tea are available 24/7. The rooms are quiet and comfortable, and the staff, well, the staff is just exactly like the staff at any Hampton Inn: kind, competent and friendly. So unlike what you might expect to find at a “budget” hotel in New York. There is a Rite Aid on one side, and a Starbucks on the other, so what they don’t have in the little hotel gift shop you can get right away. Take in a show or two, go shopping in Times Square, FAO Schwartz, or along Fifth Avenue. Have dinner at Rosie O’Grady’s. Your room is only a walk away.

title: “Sophisticated Hotel”
text: This would have to be in the top 3 hotels that we stayed in on our 9 week holiday around the U.S.A. We arrived at 6 a.m. in the morning from a Salt Lake City flight obviously our room was not ready, but this gentleman worked very hard to get us into a room as we had not had any sleep for nearly 35 hours. It only got better, the room was first class, the staff made you feel at home, the manners and politeness were the best that we had come accross. This hotel is very centrally located to most attracttions in New York City it has a private sophistcation about it, the dinning and lounge areas are very relaxing and put you at ease, the roof top bar is worth a visit for the views. Anyone looking to get away from the usual tourist circus this is the place for you. A special thanks to the management team, your doing a great job, keep on doing it well, you leave the rest behind.

title: “Stay at the Novotel”
text: This was our 4th stay at this hotel. we have always enjoyed the hotel and service, and highly recommend staying there to anyone visiting New York.

title: “Organ monkey will pick your pockets”
text:
Booked hotel room four months in advance. Called and requested a double bed no smoking room for a late check-in. Arrived 11:00 pm and was informed a $30 surcharge for the extra bed?? I realize i pre-paid through Hotwire at a fair and reasonable price, but $30 for a double bed over a king??????????????????
Never again....Shame on Sheraton, and shame on me for not booking through Marriott.

title: “Ismeta is the best!”
text:
I would just like to recognize a wonderful employee named Ismeta who works in the breakfast room. She is the friendliest and most welcoming person I have ever encountered at a hotel. She makes you feel like family, and that truly means a lot. She not only welcomed us to breakfast each morning, but she even remembered details, such as what type of yogurt (etc) I like. She took great care of us during our stay. I cannot state enough how wonderful she is. She really made our stay a good one...despite the fact that our room wasn't ready when we checked in (and that was even at 4:30pm and check in was supposed to be at 3pm!!). At the time, I was quite mad because of this, and I would probably have chosen another hotel if it weren't for Ismeta...I can honestly say that when I am in Chicago next time, I will definitely stay here again---and it is because of Ismeta!! 
As far as the room itself, we stayed in a two room suite, and it was plenty of room for 4 adults and two infants. Having a full kitchen is really nice when traveling with an infant. 
In addition, the hotel is in a really good location and close to many great restaurants. There was always a line for the elevators, though...and that got a little old after a while.

title: “Good Price, Great Location”
text: I stayed here for a conference and was generally pleased with the whole experience. WORD OF WARNING: they are renovating, so make sure to ask if they are finished or be prepared for a short menu at the restaurant without much seating. There are actually quite a few restaurants close by, so be sure to talk to the concierge. Also, ask for the discount valet parking, we got ours for only $10.

title: “Good hotel and location”
text:
Good hotel room-----small fridge was useful for bottled drinks. Also, it had a coin operating lanudry room on the third floor which was very helpful because spenting 10 days in JAX--second of 3 different hotels during the 10 day trip, Nov 2009.
Complimentary breakfast was good with individual cereal package and milk. "Activia yogurt" and others choices were available.
Southside Blvd ----this strip has all kinds of restaurants and hotels to choose from.
Very satisfactory stay.

title: “Great Value”
text: Great value for price. Nice, clean, spacious rooms. Sheers on windows, exterior corridors, Wi-Fi, coffee maker, great breakfast set-up. Restaurants close by & easy access to I-95. Friendly staff !

title: “The best i New York? Amazing hotel!”
text:
Prior to this trip, my wife and I had decided to avoid booking a hotel i the busiest tourist areas of New York. The Andaz is situatet in a relatively quiet area, however all major attractions are only a short walk away. As the hotel is close to the harbour, there is a wide selection of restaurants and cafes where it's possible to have an enjoyable meal. 
The hotel itself is amazing! The style is very modern and european-style, and the staff is attentive towards the guests needs. Rooms are spacious, and there is complimentary wifi internet; an important perk to keep in toutch with friends and family, as well as the office.
This is one of the best hotels I have ever stayed in; and probably one of the best in N.Y.

title: “Wonderful Hotel”
text: We had a wonderful time here. We stayed during the week, meaning prices were lower and we got a 4-night deal so it was even less. We had a room on the 16th floor and we could see the Golden Gate on a clear day, beautiful view. Parking is relatively cheap compared to the rest of the city, they have a garage next door with direct access to the hotel elevators at $16 for 24 hours. For the rest of the trip we took advantage of the MUNI system (google "MUNI 511" for planning which ones to take that day) which was pretty easy and had several stops near the hotel for ease - we went to Alcatraz, the Golden Gate Park, the Bridge, Union Square, the Port, Market Street, Fishermans Wharf, and Ghirardelli Square using MUNI. Theres also a Safeway nearby for a cheap dinner in your room. Lots of restaurants nearby as well (mostly Japanese of course). The fridge in the room is kinda small but does fit breakfast items to save a litle money. The shower was really cool, just keep your towel/clothes off the floor or they will be soaked. My one complaint is that we could not control our own room temperature, or at least we couldnt figure out how. We are warm sleepers and it seems the hotel has the system switched to "heat" after a certain hour, which was no good for us (it was also September, still mildly warm outside). So we slept with the sliding door cracked and window covers pulled passed it. This also meant a little more noise coming in - I put cotton in my ears. Also, you share a balcony with the room next to you, so be careful about that. The room itself is cozy, if a little tight. But we were out all day so who cares. The bed and pillows were wonderful, we both loved it. They are pet friendly and we had our cat with us and they did not charge us a pet-fee (they may for dogs). The only reason we would not stay here again would be to experience somewhere else, though this hotel is just outside of "downtown" and so was quieter, but still within easy reach of all the things you want to do. :-) Oh yah, free internet too. And they did discontinue room service.

title: “Great Experience”
text: I'm a frequent Starwood user and this hotel came up in my wife and I's search for hotels in New York. I'm so glad we booked here. It was a wonderful stay. The rooms are first class and this is the first time I can say the rooms were actually better than the photos depict. The service was excellent as well. We will be staying here again on our next visit.

title: “Best La Quinta in Houston”
text:
Should you ever need to stay on the east side of Houston just off I-10 and 15 minutes from downtown (depending on the time of day), this is currently the best choice. La Quinta Normandy is very new. As a result, so are all the fixtures, carpet, TVs, luxurious King beds, bathrooms and so on. For a budget hotel, this place is positively luxurious.
The pool was clean, the breakfast decent for being included (eggs, bacon or sausage, along with fruit, cereal, bread, bagels etc) and the staff was friendly and helpful. I cannot think of anything that wasn't right with this place, right down to the microwave and bar fridge in every room. A great bargain!

title: “Nice Hotel”
text: We enjoyed our stay here very much. Lovely hotel. We did need to wear our ear plugs for sleeping but it is New York City and is to be expected, although the bottom half of the window didn't seem to seal properly and may have added to the problem. The room very clean. We would only have one complaint and that would be the wifi connection. We always had to log in and I would say 90% of the time you could not log in. The hotel may want to look into getting a more efficient system.

title: “Downtown Los Angeles”
text:
Great location in downtown close to Disney Concert Hall. Beautiful historic building. 
Parking is quite expensive at the hotel but we parked across the street on a lot for fraction. Weekend parking is a deal for $5 a day.

title: “Concierge is the best thing about this hotel...”
text: Courteous helpful staff. Robert Brooks, the concierge, was invaluable in answering all kinds of questions. He is a rock star!

title: “Time Square Treasure”
text: My aunt and I stayed at the Marriott for 4 nights while on a shopping trip to NYC to visit her granddaughter. I have stayed at this hotel on 4 separate visits to the city. I love being in the heart of Time Square. It is a beautiful hotel with the lobby on the 8th floor. I really like that because then the lobby is not clustered with people trying to check in/out and those exiting for the day. The elevator system is great. The rooms are very large for being in the heart of Times Square. They are extremely clean and well stocked. The Marriott is within walking distance of any Broadway plays, 5th Avenue, great restaurants and shopping. It is also very possible to walk to Macy's and Central Park from here as long as you enjoy walking. Part of the charm of NYC to me is walking the streets, mingling with the people and seeing the sights. Try the Starbucks in the hotel is it great. I have never been served at one with such efficiency and courtesy. It is a little pricey but for the location I was willing to spend the money.

title: “Great hotel”
text:
Stayed 4 nights at the Bradford.
Staff were friendly and helpful, rooms above average and great breakfast.
Location is good,great restaurants nearby.
Would strongly recommend this hotel.

title: “Love The Edison”
text: My friends and I stay at the Edison a couple of times a year, and have been doing so for 10 years or so now. Love the location, love the lobby, even the rooms we have always had have been comfortable and clean, despite what others have found. Staff is fantastic; on this stay we asked the first day for extra towels and they were there every day from then on. Cafe Edison and Sofia's are both great. Bobby on the door is the best.

title: “Much Ado About Nothing”
text: Bullet points: $10 a day for wired internet with a short cord; room service menu that says the burger comes with salad but no salad; same burger comes in a picnic bag with plastic fork and ketchup only; had to ask for real silverware, mayo and mustard; oh, no salt, pepper, or salad as mentioned; really lazy bartender and stupid slow waitresses in mock cafe that couldn't even remember to charge us for 3 cocktails but had to be begged for service; awful dried-out chicken on the salad; no breakfast room service; and the greatest sin of all, the local baseball game channel wasn't available. $200. a night to stay in this? Can't wait to redeem those Hilton Honors points.

title: “Great Hotel in a great location”
text: We upgraded to a junior suite and had a fabulous room overlooking the Hudson and the harbor with windows on two sides. We also could see directly into the WTC site. The room was spacious, and the layout terrific to allow one person to sleep while the other watched TV in the other room. The staff is very helpful. Because several subway lines are located right at the hotel, it is very easy to get around or you can easily walk to Little Italy ( what's left of it) or Chinatown, Tribeca or around the FInancial district. The only downside is that the internet in your room is not free.

title: “Condescending Management”
text: Booked on Priceline, called hotel direct day before arrival, and again day of arrival, to specify non-smoking room with 2 double beds. Trainee checking us in was PAINFULLY slow - told me what room she had selected, but by the time she actually punched it in the other clerk had given it away - that was last room with 2 beds. COndescending manager made big play of "extending the courtesy" to see what he could do, and said when you book on "first available" services you only get whatever is left, and any other customer who books through the hotel website will have first advantage over you. We got it straigtened out, but he was a prick.

title: “Great location, great hotel”
text:
Really enjoyed our spacious quiet room. Hotel has an excellent gym and a small 
Starbucks coffee stand. Looked like a nice hotel for meetings as well as just the weekend get away we were doing. Valets were very efficient, we never waited more than a couple minutes for our car.

title: “Excellent Hotel!”
text: We just returned from a one week stay at the Manhattan Centre Hotel. We had an absolutely fantastic time and I wouldn't hesitate to recommend the hotel to anyone. The staff was very friendly and attentive and the rooms were perfectly clean. Can't wait for our next trip to New York!

title: “What a find”
text:
I hesitate to even write a review about this wonderful hotel because I would love to keep this little gem secret so that it does not become too popular. 
Seriously, this place was a great find. The hotel was running a promotion for weekday stays in January. If you can believe it, I got a luxury suite for only $239, including a full breakfast. Suspicious and fussy people (like me) me might conclude that this place must be a dump to be offered at that price, but they would be dead wrong. The place is terrific from top to bottom.
The front desk and lobby are very small, but check-in was a breeze. The two relatively small elevantors were very efficient, keeping wait time to a minimum. The best part of the place is the recently-renovated suiites. The living room is bigger than most home living rooms. It was beautifully funished with a sofa, easy chairs, an antique desk, a table to eat at, a nice little kitchen for those who care about that in NY (including plates and silverware, a refrigeratory, microwave, etc.), and a big wall-mounted HD television. The bedroom was also very large, with a beautiful king bed, a large closet with everything from a robe and clogs to an umbrella. The bedding seemed brand new and the bed itself was fabulous with plenty of pillows. The bathroom was small, but did have counter space, and the rainfall shower was a nice touch.
The staff and service were very accomodating, from the front desk to the very attentive door staff.
The location was great (on 50th between Third Avenue and Lexington), and there are a ton of eating options nearby. 
My only constructive criticism is that it is hard to plug a laptop into the wall at the desk in the living room, which could also use a touch more light for reading. But these are just nits.
I am a frequent traveler to NY, and this place will be on the top of my list when I need to stay on the East Side. My only concern is that this place will raise its rates so that it will go from a steal to a price more comensurate with the great accomodations and service it offers.

title: “Location is its best feature”
text:
My wife and I stayed three nights here in January '07 while on a group tour. We had booked a room with a king bed when we made our reservation three months ahead. But they gave us a room with two singles, saying they were totally sold out. The next day they were able to move us while we were out, and that was a plus.
The hotel and rooms were just a little bit tired, though acceptable. Our tour group was supposed to have breakfast prepared for us in a private room each morning, but on our second morning in the place there was no breakfast, no staff, nothing to take care of this.
The hotel gave us vouchers for the American breakfast in their dining room, and that made up for it. 
Overall, it wasn't a bad experience, and the staff did its best to be helpful. However, I would probably try somewhere else next time.

title: “Don't believe the reviews you read!”
text: I picked this hotel solely based upon trip advisor reviews and I'm sorry I did. I don't know what type of hotel the other reviewers are used to staying, but unless your thing is small rooms, hard beds, rough sheets, thin towels and loud a/c's then this hotel is not for you. Also we went out all day to come back to uncleaned room. The only good thing about this hotel is location, but Homewood Suites is next door and looks nicer and with bigger rooms I would recommend that hotel for the area instead.

title: “Small, expensive, dark”
text:
I was traveling with my husband and his parents. We booked this hotel via Priceline and clearly stated that there were 4 people travelling. As my husband and I checked into the Hudson, we were surprised because we were only given a room with single double bed (smaller than queen). We had to pay extra $90 for upgrade in addition to the price we already paid to Priceline. 
PRO:
Location. Close to Columbus Cir.
CON:
1. The room was small
2. Hallway was dark, so was the bathroom
3. The AC was badly positioned behind one of the beds and it blasted air the whole night directly to us. Our other option was to turn the AC completely off :(
4. Hidden charges (see story below)
My husband made a phone call to Priceline 800# using the phone in our room to complain and guess what, the hotell charged us CONNECTION FEE. Beware of hidden charges from this hotel. When we asked the front desk why there is no note on the phone warning us about the connection fee, the receptionist said: "oh, it is in the manual in the drawer"
I will never stayed in this hotel again and don't recommend this especially for family.

title: “Disappointing”
text: Beware of being offered upgrade. Standard room with two double beds was upgraded to "Superior" room with 1 x king size. Assumed room would have sofa bed for daughter only to find travel bed which when opened meant not able to walk around the room or use drawers. Room was drab at bed and located close to elevator and ice machine which prooved very noisy due to 2 inch gap under the door. When complained was told no other rooms available despite booking family room. Felt let down.

title: “Love this hotel after the renovations!”
text:
I have stayed at this hotel multiple times on business related trips, but this month was the best. The newly renovated rooms are awesome! I love the bed! And my favorite part is the Crabtree & Evelyn bath products :)
4* coz' the breakfast could be better.

title: “Great for a quick trip”
text:
I stayed at this hotel with my family for one night. It is conveniently located right off the freeway. There are fast food restaurants nearby and other Marriott properties are located across the street (a Courtyard and a Residence Inn).
There isn't a microwave or refrigerator in the room, but it is clean and nicely decorated. The breakfast was fine - typical continental breakfast items as well as a make-your-own waffles. The breakfast area was kind of crowded, but we managed to grab a table.
I would recommend this hotel for a brief stay - you may want to choose a hotel with larger rooms and a microwave/refrigerator if you were going to be there more than a day or two.

title: “Great Stay”
text:
I was a bit concerned about staying here due to the few not so great reviews but decided that the majority of reviews were good so booked anyway.
When we got there, as some people had experienced, neither of our rooms were ready and we were told to come back later. OK so thats not a great start but its only a big problem if you make it one. We just stored our luggage free of charge at the hotel and went out!!!
When we came back the rooms were ready and they turned out to be really nice! They were a good size and cleaned daily. There were 3 girls in our room and plenty of fresh towels were left for us every day.
Its a perfect location and we all had such a great stay there. The majority of the staff were pleasant and helpful and the housekeeping staff were lovely!!!
I would definitely stay there again.

title: “Worst hotel experience - EVER...DO NOT STAY HERE!!!!!!!!”
text: I am completely disappointed and dissatisfied with this hotel, and despite its convenient location, will NEVER stay at this hotel again. We requested a 1pm checkout when we first booked this hotel, and did not expect it to be an issue. BUT, when we checked in, we were informed of a $20+tax fee for a 1pm late checkout. This was not listed anywhere on the hotel's website, and it is a complete sham, as we could've stayed in a nicer hotel for less than $20 more and would not have had to pay the additional fee! When we questioned this late checkout fee, the manager was exceptionally rude, and instead of answering our questions, kept repeating that he had to follow "rules and regulations." As if the $20+tax fee was not enough, when we got to our room, we were greeted by a sign that warned of a $15+tax fee if the towels or sheets had any marks on them upon checkout, to include makeup, toothpaste, etc. This is completely ridiculous as simply wiping one's mouth after brushing one's teeth would leave a mark, as might wiping one's face after removing makeup. The plain white towels were in terrible shape, as were the sheets (multiple holes). Isn't bleach supposed to be used following each guest's stay? I would not recommend this hotel to anyone that does not want to be 'nickle and dimed,' or nervous about touching the towels for fear of yet an additional fee.

title: “Almost a resort in a perfect South Park setting”
text:
I've stayed here on business before and really liked the location and the nice comfortable dining room for breakfast. My wife and I are here for a week house hunting for our move to Charlotte.
We were given one of the newly renovated suites. It was comfortable and well appointed. Again, breakfast was really good with omletts, waffles and pancakes made for you. Of course the service excellent and friendly. 
Too bad it was February and we couldn't use the pool and our private deck.
The location is in the heart of south end shopping and business. We ended up buying a home only 4 or 5 miles away.

title: “Like the location”
text: Stayed here for one night in June, but have stayed here before when on business in Chicago. Great location for business/shopping/sightseeing. In between Michigan Avenue's Magnificent Mile and the Loop and next to the Chicago River. Rooms very spacious and clean. Gym has a wonderful view, as it is situated on the top of the hotel. Bar next to lobby, very busy with good atmosphere. Cannot fault the hotel. Prefer it to the Westin - my previous address when in Chicago.

title: “Go for the Penthouse!”
text: We took a quick trip to NYC and then decided to stay a few nights. Originally checked into a 'regular room' and it was just small and bland so checked to see if the Penthouse loft was available and went for it. Invited some friends to join for dinner on our private rooftop patio. Ordered caviar and Mac n cheese, drinks and had an awesome time! Loved walking around Soho as well. Had such a blast, plan to do it again!

title: “Worst hotel I have ever stayed at.”
text: I live 2 and a half hours away from this hotel. I booked 2 weeks in advance for a king bed tower room for my boyfriends birthday. When we checked in we were put in a room with two double beds. I had my printouts showing proof of my booking. They told me they were out of rooms and since I had booked a special daily deal there was no refund. The bathrooms were filthy and the tub had a gross film all around the inside. The maids also did not leave us any towels both nights. I have stayed in many hotels and this was by far the worst ever. The photos on the internet are so decieving it's unreal. Horrible experience.

title: “Not bad really”
text: Ok, for anyone about to stay at this hotel you really need to lower your expectations. First this is not a 5 star hotel. Ok? This is at most a 2 star hotel but don't let that stop you from booking or staying here. I found the front desk folk to be quite nice. When we first went to check in our room wasn't ready. No biggie since it was about 11am and I wasn't expecting it to be ready. We dropped off our bags and came back a few hours later. Still the room wasn't ready and since it wasn't the lady upgraded us to a suite. Now if this happens to you don't get too excited. With the suite you get a fridge, a microwave and a sink along with a living room type deal. I will admit though that it was nice to have the extra space. I found the room upon checking in to be clean, the pillows to be slightly better then most 2 star hotels and from what the mister says the bed was comfy. For him to say the bed is comfy he is telling the truth since he has a lot of back issues. For me well a bed is a bed, I can sleep on almost anything. As for the location of the hotel well it is a bit of a distance to most anything but the location I would say is a safe one. There is a 24 hour Dunkin Doughnuts about a block away and the red line is a couple blocks away so that was nice. Now the question. Would I stay here again? Hmmm well maybe only if the Ohio House is full or I couldn't get a good rate at the Days Inn over in Lincoln Park. But I think my travels to Chicago are about over since in 6 months I will be moving out there and making the wonderful windy city my home :) I heart you Chitown!

title: “We liked it here.”
text:
We stayed here for 3 nights on a girls' trip and chose it because of tripadvisor reviews and price (we got a "pay-for-two, stay-for-three" deal off their website). First of all, the beds and pillows here are really terrific...I wish my mattress at home was as comfortable. The rooms are big and the decor is nicer and a bit quirkier than the usual hotel box. All staff we met were extremely friendly and helpful and front desk staff gave us a super recommendation for dinner. The location is a little out of the way of downtown, but we enjoyed the walk through Seattle Centre and Belltown in the morning and the monorail trip back in the afternoon. The hotel is on the edge of the Queen Anne neighbourhood which has some really great homes, nice shops and lots of restaurants. Upper Queen Anne is about a 20 minute walk away and although it's severely uphill, we thought it was worth the trip for the shopping, eating and views from Kerry Park. 
The only downer was the wifi. We couldn't get it to work in our room on days 2 and 3. Front desk staff gave us a cable so we could access the internet from our laptops and we were happy enough with that. Overall, we really enjoyed our stay here and would definitely recommend it.

title: “Excellent hotel”
text: I thoroughly enjoyed my stay at this hotel. The suite was nice, bed very comfortable, the living area spacious enough and the seats were good enough. The only issue I had was with the flow of water in the shower, the manager explained that the flow was regulated to be slow to conserve water. I thoroughly enjoyed the breakfast at the hotel. I love the location of this hotel, it is central and close to many places. The staff at the hotel were outstanding.

title: “Great Stay @ The Crowne Plaza”
text: Our stay at The Crowne Plaza was excellent. The room was fresh and clean and exceeded our expectations. The view from the 41st floor was spectacular. If I had one word to describe why our stay was excellent is "Leo". Leo's friendlness and willingness to help and most of all his professionalism exceeds them all. He stated many membes of his family were in customer service and we could tell that he is definitely enjoying the passion he's been blessed with. We need more Leo's of this world. Thanks again for everything. The three ladies from Texas will definitely be back to visit the Crowne Plaza!

title: “Sleek hotel in great location”
text: My teenage son and I spent four nights at this newly renovated luxury hotel in the Theater District. The hotel was beautifully decorated. The rooms were plush with great bedding, a wonderful bathroom and balconies with views. The staff was amazing -- very well trained and helpful. I would highly recommend this hotel. Right across the street were several restaurants including Legal Seafood. Starbucks was a half block away. Boston Common is very close. Many historical sites are within walking distance. I would definitely go back.

title: “Nice overall”
text: You will be dissapointed if you expect fancy modern hotel. the hotel is old and may need some renovation work here and there. But the location is awesome and is close to just about all the main attactions in San Diego area. Has a really nice harbor view and mission bay is just around the corner. I stayed in this hotel for three days via Priceline booking. I read some review before and some were a little negative on the hotel so I went in with not much of an expectation. Overall I enjoyed the stay here and would recommend it to anyone who is visiting San Diego area..

title: “Ok if you need a place to sleep and leave!”
text: Staff wasn't too friendly. Acted like they could care less...(did they even notice me?) and the mirror across the beds freaked me out a little. The ac unit was too close to the bed and bedding was clean but well used. Dark bedspread didn't help the decor. Clean enough...but wouldn't stay here again.

title: “Not a magical experience whatsoever...”
text: The Brookshire is conveniently located near the Inner Harbor, but other than that the Brookshire has nothing else going for it. The room we stayed in was located on the 4th floor with a view of the building next door where pigeons had their way with the rooftops and brick walls – you get the idea. So the view was absolutely terrible and the worst I have ever had – of course none of the staff informed me of this when I booked the room. We stayed for 3 nights and within about 10 minutes of walking in the room we quickly discovered that this was not what we had wanted or had expected. The following is a breakdown of ‘all of the problems we found: the heating and cooling system within the room did not work (maintenance took a look at it 3 times before it worked – the system is completely antiquated and needs to be replaced); the carpet was dirty and had cigarette burns on it; the walls were completely dirty (scuff marks and muck all of them – we were afraid to touch them); the king size bed blanket had a hole in it; there were very few towels to speak of with – holes in a couple and they also smelled funny; the bathroom floor was completely dirty with paint spray all over the place; the shower drain did not work (maintenance was called up and after 3 attempts to fix the problem, you still stood in about 4 inches of water when bathing – clean your feet after each shower); when booking the room we requested a microwave and a refrigerator – we didn’t get either (the 2nd night we finally got the fridge, but never did get our microwave); the breakfast was just as everything with the hotel, nothing special. They had plenty of items to choose from, but the items had zero flavor and were cold every morning. The television systems for On-Demand movies were not functioning, which is a bummer when you want to spend some quality time with your special someone. There is absolutely nothing “Magical” about this hotel and turned out to be the Hotel of disappointments. They did do something unexpected, which was give us a $50 credit off our bill but as everyone knows is too little to make up for the experience. I have stayed in Hotels that cost $80 per night versus the $180 spent per night rate at Brookshire and have had much better experiences – honestly I just don’t get it. As far as the staff goes, the only person in the entire hotel that had personality was the gentlemen that provided service during breakfast but other than that they we not the people that should work in a hotel that claims to be “Magical”. I regret choosing this hotel and would dissuade others to not stay there as well.

title: “wonderful staff wanting to be sure you are enjoying your stay.”
text: Great staff, lovely modern lobby and breakfast room. Clean, good size room with granite counter tops in kitchen and bathroom. Great location if you are going to see a show at the Paramount Theater. Great breakfast. The buffet area is kept clean and well stocked. Close to everything, only 8 blocks from Pikes Market. If I had to find something that wasn't perfect it would be some noise coming from the highway. It didn't bother me, I feel asleep quickly and I slept well in the very comfortable bed but my daughter was bothered by some traffic noise. I would go back for sure and I would recommend it to friends.

title: “Good but with issues”
text:
Pros: Good rooms but with problems (see below). Nice Lobby/bar/business areas. Helpful staff.
Good resturants/bars in easy walking distance as are two T stations.
Cons: Some rooms suffer from noise, our first (20th floor) had noisy air con units below, second (4th floor) had elevator noise all night, third (21st floor) was great.
An issue Hilton should address is WiFi, it’s free in lobby and business area, but in rooms you have to pay $15 a day, during our trip $75 motels gave free WiFi so a $300-$350 a night hotel should offer it free in room.

title: “Customer Service lacking”
text:
Beautiful property but severely lacking in customer service. Had to call THREE times for room cleaning on Day#2. Reminded clerk TWICE to add my rewards number for credit. Nice fluffy towels .... with STAINS! Requested refrigerator for room. Staff delivered it and sat it outside in hallway. Room service was not good at all....French onion soup with cheddar cheese?? Wedge salad with spicy buttermilk dressing and marinated tomatoes?? Not a nice meal.
Location is great. Property is beautiful. Lots of "little" things made it below average in my opinion. All boils down to lazy staff.

title: “Beautiful hotel with FABULOUS staff!”
text: I would highly recommend this beautiful hotel, firstly for the amazing staff, the style and comfort of the hotel itself and for the location, within easy walking distance of Boston Common and Fenway Park!

title: “Fantastic Friendly Hotel”
text: We stayed at the Fairfield Airport property for one night, arriving into DIA after midnight, collecting our luggage and calling the Fairfield from the bank of hotel phones near baggage claim area. The receptionist was extremely friendly, and explained where and when the van would pick us up, which was within 8 minutes from calling. Check in was very quick, and friendly. Room was basic but updated, with bright and clean duvets, coverings and tons of pillows. Very large bathroom with all the basic needs. Never heard airport noise. The following morning, the hotel arranged to drive us to our rental car company on Pena Blvd, in their airport shuttle. Their's was full, so they made the effort to call the Courtyard next door to bring us. The price, cleanliness, friendly service, use of free computer in lobby, excellent free breakfast and location can't be beat! Will definitely stay again if in the area.

title: “Great location, quiet clean rooms”
text: Heard some bad reviews on check-in process, rooms, price but overall we were pretty happy with what we got. Only problem was that it did take quite sometime to check-in (for everyone except the Diamond Club). No micro but it did have a mini bar. Room were decent sized-was expecting something really small but was happy that beds were comfortable and clean. No view but what do you expect from an area with so many gigantic buildings. Was happy with the proximity to Times Square. Loved that they had an open market in front of the hotel sunday morning. Husband loved the street food on the corner-cheap, tasty.

title: “Worst ever”
text: In my 40-plus years of travel, this hotel might be the worst place I ever stayed. Dirty and smelly. From our room, you could see something black at bottom of pool below so we checked it out and it was that dirty. There was no "closed" sign but I can't imagine anyone getting into that water. In lobby, signage said eateries open until 11 p.m. but they were never open, day or night. Asked clerk to print out our boarding passes and he said the printer was out of toner. Lobby and hallways were warm. The breakfast buffet was not bad. Will never stay at another Clarion.

title: “Great place to stay in Manhattan”
text:
Stayed here for a few nights starting on New Years Eve. The hotel is in a good location, within easy walking distance of Times Square and Central Park and the theater was just around the block. We saw Mama Mia, a very entertaining and fun show. The hotel room had plenty of space and was very clean. Our room (which did not face the street) was very quiet. The hotel staff was very friendly and helpful. The hotel concierge was especially helpful. There was a very good complimentary breakfast included with the room. Even when the line was long it didn't take too long to get your breakfast. The line just shows that it's a good breakfast. If you go early there is no line. There is a parking garage at the hotel, for a charge. If you are going to leave your car in the garage for a few days, just be sure to get everything out that you may want during your stay. You can not go to your car to get something while it's in the garage. The cost of the room seemed to be in the middle between the cheaper hotels and the very expensive. I would definitely stay here again while in Manhattan.
If you want to be in Times Square for New Years Eve, you seem to have two choices. Make a reservation and pay big bucks to go to a party within sight of Times Square, or be very uncomfortable standing in the street for 12 to 24 hours on sore feet without food, water, and a bathroom. The police control the movement of people in each block starting early in the day, but they did so in a very respectful and congenial manner. They were all great. We decided to go for a carriage ride in the park and dinner instead, and then later stood on 7th Street for three hours to watch the ball drop from a 1/4 mile away. Actually, the fire works over Central Park (to which we were closer) were more spectacular. So we can say we saw the ball drop at Times Square, and enjoyed the fire works over Central Park.
We had a wonderful trip.

title: “$27.00 cab ride from IAH airport”
text:
We stayed at this hotel when air traffic control delays caused us to miss our connections in Houston (IAH) with no vouchers for overnight accomodations provided. An internet search seeking low prices lead us to the Suburban Extended Stay Houston Airport. The name of the hotel lead us to believe it was close to the airport, but it was a $27.00 cab ride EACH WAY, to a hotel with bars on the front desk and a security guard. I suspect low income families are living in many of these rooms. 
We would have saved money and felt alot safer if we had stayed in a nice hotel closer to the airport that offered shuttle service.

title: “Close to everything”
text: Very enjoyable hotel. Convenient and close to many sites! Just a few blocks from theatres and Times Square. Easy access to Grey Line Double Decker Bus Tours. Clean and modern facility. Very accommodating staff! Definitely going back and will stay here again.

title: “Stay away from room 453”
text:
I chose this hotel because of its location and because I like the idea of staying in a historical building while visiting D.C. on vacation.
When I booked the reservation though the hotels online website, I specifically requested a quiet room. I think it's a big slap in the face when the hotel puts you in one of the noisiest possible rooms in the joint. 
Room 453 has two shortcomings when it comes to noise. First, it's located directly next to the service elevator. So, you get to hear every single trolly/cart being pushed up or down the hallway. Second and even more unacceptable was the fact that they setup for banquets in the hallway by my room. For a few hours on Saturday there was constant noise from the banquet staff setting up every course that was served that night, and having the smell of food and especially fish waft into my room really angered me.
The fact that I specifically asked for something, and they did such a horrible job in placing me in an appropriate room, I will not be staying at this hotel on any future visits to D.C.

title: “I should have taken my girlfriend!!”
text:
Having to drive a truckload of my daughter's stuff to San Diego wasn't fun, not to mention my baby moving away to college, and I needed a place to stay and park the truck (and it's contents) overnight. I was referred to this hotel by someone in my company familiar with the area, and he definitely steered me the right direction! By the time I got there, I had lost my marbles, and everyone put up with me quite well; exhibiting a great deal of patience through my lack of brain function; they were all very nice, and polite to the finest detail. The grounds were nothing short of a garden; palms, roses, etc., and meticulously maintained. From my balcony, I looked down onto a clean, clear pool and yard. The elevator was fast and smooth. The door lock functioned just fine, and I walked into a room with a four-post king size bed. The slider opened out onto a balcony that looked out across the Hotel grounds, across to the nearby hills, and yet still seemed private. The tv was neatly hidden in an armoire, and there was a gaming control tucked in there as well, although I didn't get into that. The room was clean, bathroom and shower as well, right down to the vacuum patterns on the carpet. I actually took photos with my phone and sent them to my girlfriend, just to make her regret not coming along! Even the evening guard/ lot attendant was great! I apologize as I do not remember the gentleman's name, but what a great guy; knew the area, was very personable, and was happy to offer suggestions and directions. My daughter and I dined at Trellises, and we both just sat and relished in what we had requested of the chefs. The service was both fun and attentive, all the while professional. I will never again be able to have that moment with my daughter, that last dinner out together as she grows from being Daddy's lil girl into an independent young woman, and Trellises created nothing short of a perfect setting. Thank you, to the staff and crew of Trellises restaurant and Town & Country Resort Hotel, for what you do everyday is now a memory and moment in time that I, and my daughter, will always have. When I come back to visit my lil girl, I will be sure to bring my girlfriend, and hopefully we will stay a little longer to enjoy your hospitality!
A weary traveler and Dad

title: “Opaque but not bad for the price.”
text: After I read the reviews of the Elan on Trip Advisor and in several publications, I expected an incredibly hip hotel experience. Perhaps my expectations were too high certainly considering we didn't pay a whole lot. The room was rather bland filled with IKEA type furniture. Perhaps this where the "hip" quotient arrives from. Yet, this furniture is not holding up well and is showing signs of wear and tear. The bathroom was styled nicely in an inexpensive manner and looked like something a young up and coming couple would have in their first apartment The staff was friendly in that L.A. way letting you know that this hotel job is just temporary until their acting skills are discovered. The entire hotel experience was rather opaque reflecting on the entire hotel's ambience. The neighborhood is not too bad, within walking distance of Melrose etc. But, I forgot, nobody walks in L.A.! We were rather incongruous as we strolled down Beverly Blvd. If you can get a really low price, the Elan Modern Hotel is not too bad. It's just rather opaque.........Whatever that means.

title: “Nightmare”
text: I had a class to attend on Monday, so I thought "I will just stay there Sunday and be there".,Well when I walked in "I thought O my Goodness they have trailer park hotels". I quickly changed my mind about staying. Yes it was that bad. I returned the next morning to go to my class and, once we got in class we realized the ad was on, but was not cooling. The teacher stopped class and asked the maintenance crew to check it out or move us to another room. They said all rooms were booked. Liar liar pants on fire, there were 4 rooms available. They must have forgot the doors to the rooms were open. But the air was not working in any of them. So they turned the temp down in the room we were in, and class continued. We were told there was a restaurant we a Buffett downstairs and a gift shop for snacks. Liar liar pants on fire. The restaurant was closed breakfast, lunch, and dinner. He gift shop was also closed. Not one staff member knew by they were closed. When we had a break, I went to the restroom, and what do you know, NO ac. It was hot as hell. Lastly some guests took there kids out to the pool area, and he came back with a ton of mud on him. The dad was Furious, I mean who wouldn't be. There was no mud or a place for mud in the pool area, as it turns out he got it from the steps on the pool, it was cement. They company patched the pool but didn't close it. The guy working on the pool spoke no English (figures that common her in this city). Run run run from this HELL-TELL (hotel).

title: “RE: Nice place”
text: I was very pleased with this hotel and would recommend it for families. We stayed for 5 days with our two kids, ages 9 and 4, and it was a great place for them. The room had a beautiful view of the Bay, and was clean and fairly spacious. I thought the waitstaff at the hotel restaurant were pleasant and accomodating of kid-friendly requests. The grounds are lovely and it was a pleasure just to walk around. It is extremely convenient to Sea World and has some nice little amenities, like printed directions to most major tourist sites from the hotel, free (to guests) cruises of the Bay on the Bahia Belle, and kayak/pedalboat/windsurf rentals on the beach right outside the hotel doors. Lots of little shops and places to eat within walking distance (terrific little burrito shack right around the corner that we would have walked right by were it not for a tip from hotel staff) and of course the ocean is just a block away. It was a low-key, hassle free visit. I would rate it excellent except that it was fairly expensive. Still, I feel we got what we paid for and that is worth a lot on vacation!

title: “Good hotel”
text: I have been staying at this hotel for the last 10 years, the staff is friendly and specially the bar staff and Rosie of room service, the hotel is somewhat dated but very clean and nice. They do have flat screen tv's. but they are falling behind the Marriott down the road, because they have made an extensive remodelation.i heard that they were going to remodel next year, hopefully they will.

title: “Pleasantly Surprised!”
text: Having read the various earlier reports on this hotel, we arrived with geat apprehension after a long flight from UK via LA. Pleading tiredness, we aked for a quiet room and were immediately allocated one on the top floor and at the end of one of the wings. Consequently it was well away from any noise and actually gave us a partial view over the bay. The room itself was clean and perfectly adequate - the inflatable mattress was fun to play with! That said, we achieved our quiet stay at the expense of a route march to/from the ice machine or, even further, to the elevators. However, it was certainly worth it as we were well away from the numerous school/youth parties that the hotel seems to specialise in. Undoubtedly they would make for a noisier stay in a more central room. The parties also seemed to have agreements with the iHop for breakfasts, so we preferred either the danish/coffee option in the lobby or the Johnny Rockets, which was extremely convenient and good value, even providing impromptu song/dance routines by its waiting staff! Additionally, the nearby Safeway store is very handy for stocking the in-room fridge with wine, etc. Above all, it's a question of location, location, location! This hotel is difficult to beat on those grounds, the staff are all extremely polite and helpful, and the rooms are perfectly acceptable, if not luxurious. Well worth considering for a few days in the City.

title: “Great find in an otherwise pricey city!”
text: We stayed here over President's weekend for a big volleyball tournament at the Convention Center in D.C. I wanted someplace within walking distance of the convention center that wasn't too expensive. I booked the Holiday Inn because it fit the bill. What a pleasant surprise when we arrived! The place is more upscale than I expected. It was clean and pretty; even the hallways where the rooms were, were elegant. If you want something close to the Convention Center that is very reasonable for the area, this is the place to stay! Rooms were spacious and clean and had two sinks: one inside the bathroom and one right outside the bathroom so that two people could be getting ready at the same time. Although it would've been nice to have breakfast included, the breakfast options in the restaurant were reasonable except for the price of $3.25 for a cup of coffee. However, if you ordered either their cold or their hot and cold buffet coffee was included which made it worthwhile. The cold buffet was $10.99 but included bagels with lox plus the coffee plus fruit, cereal, muffins etc. The hot buffet was only $4.00 more. Whether you come here for business or pleasure this was a pleasant surprise in an extremely pricey city!

title: “Great stay”
text:
There were many hotels to choose from in Memphis and I choose this one based on the reviews and good value. We were not disappointed. We spent 2 nights there before going to Clarksdale, MS and then another night before flying home. The rooms were clean, spacious, and the staff awesome. Breakfast had a great selection of hot and cold items along with healthy choices. Tuesday night was the managers social. We thought this would be snacks but it was an excellent taco dinner with good wine and beer. We had no need to go for dinner after this very tasty meal.
Also loved the roof top patio. Great view of the river and city.
Special call out to Olga at the front desk for making us feel so welcome.
Would definitely recommend this hotel and would stay here again.

title: “The Mayfair Hotel”
text:
We stayed at the Mayfair Hotel from December 23-30, 2008. We enjoyed our stay and would do it again. It's small, but it's location next to Times Square made up for it. We are from Texas and had never been to New York City before. The staff were friendly and helpful. Here's a short video I made of our room:
 http://youtube.com/watch?v=gcLPwO-P4l4

title: “We really enjoyed our stay. We'll be back”
text:
Had no idea what it was going to be like going in, and had no expectations, just a few friends getting together for a change of pace with a lot of fun and relaxation in mind.
It was a great Boutique Hotel with no stuffiness built in, it has a a fun decor and a friendly, down to earth staff.
It is decorated with a bit of a retro funky style, which is hard to describe... but for a young group of friends looking for an affordable, clean and pleasant place, with a flair of its own I wouldn't have an issue recommending it. 
It was the first time that we got together like that and really we look forward to doing it again. The hotel was clean and quiet in the room area. The Beds were cozy and comfortable, and the rooms were more spacious than I expected... but if you wanted the louder active area with a bustling youthful vibe, you could have a cocktail downstairs. 
Really enjoyed the visit and hope to go back soon.

title: “Disappointing”
text: Our room was never cleaned the entire weekend of our stay. We were "checked out" of our room a day early. And no one seemed to be able to answer what happened, other than to try to say that I originally made my reservation for only one day. I had the paperwork to show my reservation for 3. The front desk attendants were very friendly, but I definitely didn't feel like the hotel overall had a "customer is always right" attitude. Then our bill was wrong (only was charged for two days instead of three), which they tried to explain was due to my only having reserved one night (but getting charged for two?!? What kind of sense does that make?!?). However, I was honest and pointed out the billing error and paid for my room, yet never got offered any sort of compensation for the fact that our room was never cleaned. I was very disappointed to say the least in the level of service we received.

title: “Best value for points in Austin area”
text:
