I used my Marriott Reward points to stay at this hotel last week. I have to admit, I selected this hotel based on the reviews I saw on TripAdvisor and the fact that a 1 night stay required half the number of points of the other Marriott brands in the Austin area.
The earlier positive TA reviews are all spot on. This hotel is practically brand new (as of Jan 2011) and is super clean. The hotel was designed with the business traveller in mind, so there are lots of conveniences that aren't always available in other hotels of similar price. The rooms are roomy with a desk and sofa, and very well lit. Free internet access throughout the hotel, free (and very ample) parking. Helpful and friendly staff. Workout area is nice and clean. There is a nice meet & greet area next to the lobby which comes in handy if you need to meet friends,co-workers, or clients; there are 2 computers with internet access available for use in this area as well. There is also a small bistro in the lobby where you can order coffee and some (simple) hot meals. The location is good if you need to be in the north part of Austin, but only so-so if you need to be downtown or close to Univ of Texas campus during rush hour (traffic on I-35 going south is terrible during rush hour!).
I normally stay at the Doubletree near campus, but considering the rates there are more than double the rate at this hotel and the rooms are practically identical, I think I'll be coming back to this hotel instead - even with the extra 7 mile drive to downtown/campus.
If you're using Marriott Reward points, this is the best deal in the Austin area hands down.

title: “Not a 4 star”
text: Got this hotel through Priceline at a really good deal, if I would have paid full price it would not get this many stars. Our room was small and you could hear everything happening in the hallway. We also get a knock on our door at 6:30AM on Sunday with our valet receipt. Our bed was squeaky, a couple tiles in the shower were loose, and our fireplace did not work. When we checked in I asked what kind of room we had and their response was "we are booked full and don't have any more rooms" well thanks, but that wasn't my question. After getting settled in the room and heading back down as we walk by the front desk and someone else asks if they have any room available. I overhear the staff respond with we only have rooms available on the first floor...oh. I wouldn't rate this so poorly but it is classified as a 4-star hotel. The services and rooms we had were not even close to 4-star. I will probably avoid The Edgewater next time I am there unless I get another great deal.

title: “Best deal for downtown with trendy/clean and spacious rooms”
text: A group of friends chose this hotel due the proximity to the Key Arena. We were going to see Eric Clapton! We had 5 different rooms. All were spectacular and comfortable. Definitely the best deal with parking included and walking distance to the Key. Plan to stay there everytime.

title: “Fantastic time was enjoyed”
text: I Arrived at the hotel from the airport via a shuttle bus service, no problem. We had flown over from England, so we were a bit tired, even though it was only 7 PM local time, to us it was 3 in the morning. We stayed up for as long as we could but gave in at 9PM. I must say I had the best nights sleep I had had in a long time the bed was sooo comfortable. Got up early the next day and started to explore, the hotel is very well situated for all the touristy things at Fishermans wharf and the bus and tram services were all close by as well. We did everything that tourist do, Alcatraz (close by) Biked the bridge(close by) Lombard street (close by). We also went to Cobbs comedy club which is just up the street from the hotel. We ordered room service a couple of times, which was excellent. Overall I would say, a quality hotel in a quality location, in a quality city.

title: “In need of a total overhaul to live up to past standards”
text:
I have been staying at W on Lexington for a decade. It's become a bit of a dump and management appears to be putting it head in the sand so to speak. I will find a new NYC hotel to stay at.
The rooms have been redone and now look like something you'd see in Austin Powers movie with shag rugs and lots of metallic objects.
The service was never a strong suit but has gotten worse. Many of the folks feel like they are beneath the job they are doing and don't really try. I called Whatever Whenever multiple times and no one even bothered answering the phone.
Neither the TV nor the phone worked in my room so I had to have engineering come up.
The gym (aka Sweat) is really quite bad for a hotel at this price point. I think a new gym may be under construction as it is sorely needed.
Net net the hotel needs a real face lift.

title: “Interesting stay at XV Beacon”
text: Spent almost a week at XV Beacon in prime season - we had one of the larger rooms facing onto Beacon, which put it in the $500 a night range. Unlike the comments of other reviewers, it really wasn't too noisy at all... The location downtown was hard to beat and the concierge and staff were amazing. Loved the mercedes shuttle, which was cheerfully offered. The room was very tastefully decorated, had a SUPERB mini bar - quite nice bathroom. The bed could have been better and I share the other reviews griping about the air conditioning... it was working, but the room was on the cusp of being too warm to sleep comfortably. We were a little apprehensive about the Federalist restaurant - it looked rather drab, but the food and wine list were world class. The cranky old elevators take a little getting used to. Overall, we liked it... not sure it was good value, but we left with a positive impression.

title: “just wonderful -- cannot recommend highly enough”
text:
Our experience at this hotel has been great.
We arrived around 11 am on a Saturday and were able to check in early. The room was large and clean. (We had two double beds, a table, a large dresser with a flat screen TV inside), a comfortable bathroom with really high ceilings. In the evening, the room was turned down with chocolates placed next to the bed, together with a personal note from housekeeping. 
We are Select Guest members, so we got free breakfast drinks and newspaper delivered to the room. 
Everyone we encountered has been nothing but pleasant, helpful, and accommodating. The hotel has fresh fruit and very tasty lemonade in the lobby in the afternoon. One of the nights, when my fiance and I were coming in, the concierge presented me with a beautiful red rose (my fiance did not order one, this is just a completely random, nice gesture -- many thanks to Omni for that!). 
The lobby is good size and beautifully furnished. The location is convenient. We had a great time and are sad to be leaving tomorrow morning.

title: “Very Comfortable Hotel”
text: This is a great place to stay when visiting Indy. Has the signature comfort beds which is awesome. Rooms very clean and nice. We stay there whenever visiting Indy. It is located within walking distance to downtown. Also connected to the convention center which is a must have for us. Front desk staff is amazing and helpful. Our 2-room reservations were messed up and they compensated us by giving us a gorgeous 2-room connected by a living room. Just lovely. We couldn't believe how fantastic the front desk and the manager handled this. They made absolutely no issue of it and assured us immediately we would be taken care of-and we were. That is HUGE for us. We highly recommend this hotel.

title: “love that Adagio”
text:
Loved the location Loved the room Loved the decor
We had a meeting in a beautiful room on the top floor - amazing view - everything was top notch!

title: “Great hotel and great staff!”
text:
Set in downtown Dallas this hotel is within easy reach of the 6th Floor Museum, Deeley Plaza, Old Red Court House museum, Pioneer Plaza, Dallas World Aquarium and Dallas Heritage Village to name but a few. The rooms in this boutique hotel are beautifully decorated in bright colours and are well furnished. Everywhere you go in the hotel it is beautifully clean and well maintained. The Phi restaurant serves excellent food at a reasonable price. 
A real plus is the hotel's courtesy car & mini bus - available to take guests anywhere within a 3 mile radius and then a quick phone call to the hotel gets you picked up and returned to the hotel. The drivers are friendly and knowledgable - especially with advice on the best places to eat.
In facte every single member of staff at the Hotel Indigo was wonderful, they are all very helpful, polite and professional and nothing is too much trouble for them. 
Special thanks to Mike Owen (Manager) for his assistance and kindness when there was a hitch.
So if you're thinking of visiting Dallas in Texas I highly recommend the Hotel Indigo. We had a fab holiday and have wonderful memories.

title: “Oh, so quaint”
text: Loved everything about this hotel...It is old and romantic. We had a huge room with a lounge area which did come in handy for tv viewing..And the staff are beautiful, so friendly and so accomodating. Old style charm is what this hotel showed me and if we visit DC again, we need no longer to search for accomodation again as Hotel Lombardy will be our choice...Oh, and the walk to the White House and Lincoln memorial is very easy and beautiful

title: “No value at all”
text: We stayed one night. The rooms are ok but weird. You will be nickled and dimed at every turn. 9 dollars for a bottle of water!! The staff all look and act like they are the models for calvin klein. Just a strange place. I will not be back.

title: “Great Place to Stay”
text: This hotel is very clean, and the staff is very friendly. Upon our arrival, we were briefed on the attractions of San Diego and also a map of how to get there by various means of transportation. We were given a room with microwave and refrigerator for a very good price. I strongly recommend this hotel/inn to everyone who wants to get the best bang for their bucks.

title: “Awesome!!”
text: We got a great deal from otel.com so I thought maybe we'd end up with a room next to an elevator or something. We had a huge corner room with a wrap-around balcony! Everything about the room was awesome! The hotel staff was courteous and helpful. My only complaint was the poor signage in the underground parking garage. We kept getting lost, but it wasn't really a big deal. By the way, overnight parking was an extra $43 per night, but that's pretty standard in Chicago. I would definitely stay here again!

title: “Great location and price”
text: This hotel was near everything we wanted to see, so we walked to most of the attractions. including Broadway plays,Central park and a good pizza place a block away.Clean and friendly would go back again for sure.

title: “Nice hotel poor location”
text:
Stayed 3 nights in June and thoroughly enjoyed our stay, particularly in the courtyard at night having a few drinks and conversing with fellow travellers. Car was nice and secure behind locked gates. Free continental breakfast. Staff polite and helpful, room quite large.
Bad news was the location- no bars nearby only takeaways. Plenty of convenience stores mind though the miserable asian shopkeeper next door reminded me of the one in the movie ‘Falling Down’. Seemed a bit industrial with car repair shops abounding. My son felt ill at ease with the local groups of youths hanging around but I think the threat was more apparent than real. Long drive to anywhere-downtown LA and Santa Monica .Shame because obviously the hotel could not do anything about the location.

title: “Better choices in the area”
text:
I've stayed at this hotel around a dozen times in the last few years, mostly when I can't get into the Embassy Suites down the street. As a Hilton Diamond member (their top level), you'd think I'd be treated like royalty - think again. My last trip found me on a lower floor, my room key wouldn't work to get me into the executive lounge and they didn't even provide the complimentary bottled water they promise to Diamond members. I asked at the front desk if they could send up the water and after about 10 minutes of whispering in the back room (what on earth could they be talking about?) they promised they would send it up while I was out to dinner - but of course no such luck. I even double checked to make sure they had my Hilton number on the reservation.
They had handed me card when I checked in with the Service Manager's name and email address so I sent her an email asking her about these and a few other problems. Admittedly, these were fairly minor problems but when you spend 100 nights a year in a Hilton you do expect to be treated better. I got back a form letter with a promise of a better response from the "department heads" but it's been several weeks with no response.
They are doing a remodel of the rooms - thank God - the old ones were very very dark and you could not read to save your life. I used to have to go into the bathroom to read anything the bulbs were so dim. The remodeled ones are nicer with upgraded bedding but are still very average in size. 
Location is very close to LAX but of course so are about 20 other hotels. The noise from the planes seem to be much worse here- I don't know if the construction or if small differences in location around the airport make that much difference but it's always very noisy here. The place is usually packed with people attending conventions, trade shows, etc. in their extenise meeting space. If you're not of those folks, you can do much better at other hotels in the area (Embassy Suites North, for one.)

title: “"Excellent location, helpful staff and delicious breakfast"”
text: Great hotel if you want to experience what NYC has to offer. The location is perfect - right next to Timnes Square, yet rooms are as quiet as you can get in such busy city. The service is excellent - our rooms were upgraded free of charge upon our request, breakfast was always fresh and delicious, the concierge was very informative and helpful. Rooms are small but comfortable. The only disadvantage I can think or is lack of places to sit in the lobby - we were a large group and waiting for everyone standing was a bit annoying.

title: “Noisy, poor water pressure, and uneven service.”
text:
The title of my review says it all. After I requested a quiet room both when reserving and at check-in, I was given a room that looked good on the surface (end of a hallway) but that ended up being awful, when starting at 4:15 am the garbage trucks began reversing down the alley ("beep beep beep") outside my window. The manager on duty the next morning did graciously offer to move me to an interior room, but his explanation that the trucks only come "sometimes" and that it is "out of the hotel's control" didn't help me to understand why I hadn't been assigned an interior room in the first place.
The room to which I was moved was on the top (12th) floor. Water pressure went from poor in the previous room to downright awful in the 12th floor room. Two consecutive mornings around 7 am, the water was literally about the pressure of a weak sink tap-- it took 20 minutes just to wash my hair in the trickle. 
The real coup de grace was when it took 35 minutes for room service to deliver an empty tea cup to my room. I called three times to reception to inquire about the delay and received a shifting story each time. The clerk ultimately offered to have the manager, Sebastian, call me back "right away". 30 min after that, the clerk called to say that Sebastian was "helping other customers" and would be slighly delayed. Two hours after that, I left the hotel for dinner. The next morning, when I asked to speak with Sebastian pre-checkout, I was told that he was in a meeting and not available. I expressed my disappointment at the general poor service throughout my stay and invited Sebastian to email or call me at his convenience to discuss; needless to say, he didn't bother. And hence my negative review on TripAdvisor. Any "apology"/PR management that comes in response to this review is completely misplaced and belated; the hotel could have rectified things during my stay or shortly thereafter, and they failed to do so.
All in all, given the choice in DC, I see no reason to settle for a poor night of sleep, a terrible shower, and uneven service for ~$300/night!

title: “THE BEST OF EVERYTHING”
text: At our recent stay at the Manchester Hyatt we found the quality of service unsurpassed, starting with the concierge, specifically Philip and Mercedes, always doing their best to make our stay enjoyable. Cathy, and Benazon went out of their way, along with Ben our bellman to help us find a certain type of medicine for my wife and myself, even personally driving us there. Basel was also one of the most helpful managers we have met. We are frequent travelers to San Diego, and we never consider any other hotel than the Manchester Hyatt. The staff are more friendly and welcoming than anywhere we've ever been; we always feel like we're home when we arrive.

title: “Great stay with an old lady”
text:
I'm very perplexed at reading the review from the folks from "Down Under" dated 7/26 because I was at the Brown palace at the same time and experienced none of the problems they describe. First of all, I did book directly with the hotel after receiving my weekly bargain email from Travelzoo. In my opinion, anyone who does NOT book directly with the hotel puts their trip in the hands of a third party. So if I may be so bold, that was mistake #1. My room was on the 6th floor and a "split corner" room - translation "tiny". But hey, I knew that going in - I got a bargain rate. In the end, I got what I expected. Here's the rest of the story.
THE ROOM - The bed was a true queen as requested (not something less as suggested by my Aussie friends). It was comfortable and clean. I am picky about the bed - I need a good night sleep, and this one gave it to me. The linen was fresh, white and clean. Certainly no burnt spots. The shower (no bath tub) had a single head that sprayed water of the temperature I desired when I desired it. The water pressure could have been higher but it was not a drizzle. The bathroom linen was plush, plentiful and spotless. Indeed, the entire room was immaculate. I've really never been in a cleaner hotel room - which leads me to the next topic.
THE PEOPLE - Since they are seldom mentioned first, I'd like to comment on the maid service. Every time I saw a maid in the hotel, they were friendly and attentive - helping a first timer at their hotel find his way. What I found interesting is that I had the same maid for the 3 days and 2 nights I was there. And she came twice a day, once about 8:00 AM and then about 5 PM. There was a time (in the AM) that I was not ready for her. I asked her to come back later and she did - with the same high quality of cleanliness as if I was on her schedule. Another person who sticks out was the lobby pianist the evening of Friday, 7/24. The lobby pianists I saw at the Brown Palace were average to very good - except this guy - he was fabulous! I wish I'd have got his name, but he was a thin fellow, and (forgive the ethnic references, but I find it necessary) seemed to be middle eastern or possibly Indian. Anyway, this guy had a full repertoire of pop, jazz, and classical. Time and again, when done with a particular offering people within earshot would applaud loudly. By the way, the only food I ate at the Brown Palace was in the lobby. I had the chorizo mussels and the cheese selection. Both were wonderful. Next time, I'll eat in a restaurant - I'll let you know. To continue with people - everyone I encountered at the Brown Palace was friendly and professional. Emphasis on friendly - which makes them exceptional.
THE ISSUES - Only one. I absolutely HATE valet parking, and that's the only kind available at the Brown Palace. If you have a car, be prepared for the typical wait and confusion that valet parking provides.
THE UPSIDE - A comfortable stay in a fabulous location (even my friends the Aussies gave the place 5 stars on that!). I'd go back in a heartbeat!

title: “American Girl Getaway”
text: We stayed here during our recent visit to the American Girl Store. Our room was clean and comfortable. The staff was extremely friendly. The breakfast was good and Ms Paulette was super nice. The halls were quiet. The only thing I could find wrong with the hotel was the need for elevator. The staff did offer to assist bring luggage to my room. Would stay again

title: “Wonderful hotel, wonderful location”
text:
I stayed at the HGI during the Easter Holidays and what with the cold snap at the time, it was a lovely and warm hotel to come back to. 
It's ideally located in that it was just around the corner from the hustle and bustle of Times Square. As a mother that likes to get away on her own sometimes I felt totally safe both at the hotel and in the city. I came for rest, relaxation and to do a bit of shopping and I acheived all three.
As has been said numerous times, the rooms are very spacious. The large king-sized bed was absolute bliss, coffee-making facilities were on hand, and I definitely made use of the fridge and the microwave. There is a supermarket across the road on the right of the hotel called the Food Emporium but beware, they have started a 3-month renovation so the deli section upstairs will have limited choices. I had breakfast at both Pigalle and the Olympic Diner and between all three I didn't have to spend a fortune in restaurant bills.
The reception staff were nothing but courteous and helpful towards me, even when I had ongoing problems with my credit card they showed amazing patience. The concierge were wonderful and well-mannered. I got a "hello" every time I came back. They didn't even raise an eyebrow when I'd come downstairs in my pj's and bedsocks in the middle of the night and use their business room to go on the computer. What can I say, the time difference played havoc with my body clock:-). 
My only minor complaint would be that, because it was freezing over the Easter period in New York, my heating was on all the time which can dry you out. And as I don't like the cold it was a minor detail to put up with.
All in all a wonderful stay. Great hotel, great staff.

title: “appalling but at least I wasn't on the street”
text: The hotel where I had been booked didn't have my reservation on file, so at 12:30am I was looking for a place to stay in Seattle - on a Saturday night in July. Half an hour and many phone calls later I found a room here. As soon as I arrived I spent another 20 minutes calling more hotels, but no luck, so I stayed. The hallway smelled of urine, the room smelled of stale booze. The carpet and easy chair were very stained. The bathroom looked like it belonged in a tenement. There was no hair dryer, no alarm clock, and no iron. And for the pleasure of not having to sleep in my car I paid $105. On the up side, the sheets were clean and the shower had decent water pressure and lots of scalding hot water. So keep this hotel in mind if you're ever stuck in Seattle with no hotel room on a weekend. They'll have a room.

title: “Fantastic location, expensive for what it is.”
text: The hotel was in a great location with lots of good restaurants and bars nearby. Felt a bit more like an authentic neighbourhood and not very touristy for a true New York experience. The room we had was tiny, quite cold and the air con/ heater noisy when turned on. Some of the front desk staff were not very helpful, I asked on two separate occasions for recommendations for a restaurant (breakfast and dinner) and was recommended to the same place twice. I went there on my first day for breakfast as I didn't know any better but there are lots of amazing places close by that I event to over the 5 days I was there. Compared to other hotels we have stayed in across the world, this felt very expensive for what it was, although it's a peak time and so guess this affected the price.

title: “Good, clean and comfy”
text:
I've stayed here before (and reviewed before). The hotel is only a few min from Pershing Square metro station which, without a car in LA, is a blessing though the metro doesn't go to all the places you want to.
Hotel is nice, beds are very comfortable, OK gym, rooms are very clean. Service and staff was generally very good apart from the concierge one time wasn't that helpful in giving me bus directions and advice. There are a quite a few cafes, convenience stores located next to hotel for snacks, drinks, etc..
You can get to the hotel in less than an hour by public transport. Take the bus which runs every 1/2 hr to Union Square then it's only 2 stops to Pershing Square on metro and a 5 min (uphill) walk. This costs less than $10 in total - much cheaper than the $60+ taxi.

title: “Loved this Hotel”
text: The only complaint I have is the noise level from the street. Fortunately the hotel must be aware of this as they provide complimentary ear plugs in each room, which I took full advantage of. The staff was excellent and gracious, the food at the hotel restaurant was very good and the service was great. The price for my hotel stay was affordable due to the conference rate, but outside of that, I believe I would have felt the published rate was high at $350+ a night for the room.

title: “Spotless clean and Courteous Staff”
text:
I stayed just for 2 nights, but the suite was everything a single person could ask for. Pillows, washer, functional and clean kitchen, recliner, hi speed wifi.
If they had an airport shuttle, I'd have given them higher than excellent.
I will surely come back to them whenever i come back to Dallas. 
I confirmed my opinion of the hotel with the other guests, some of who have been staying here for over 4 months! One of the best candlewoods I have stayed in.
I'd specially like to thank, Senedu and David at the front-desk for being exceptionally courteous and taking care of me as if I was family. Thank you guys! :o)

title: “Great Location!!”
text:
As most people know, it is next to impossible to find an inexpensive hotel in a prime loation in San Francisco that is not a "dive". The Sheraton happens to be that next to impossible hotel. 
Good:
Hotel was clean
Rooms were clean
Hotel is near all the main Fisherman's Warf attractions
Almost across the street from the end/beginning of the Trolley
Little cafe in the hotel that is open late and serves alcohol
Fun outside space at the hotel with fireplaces - LOVED THIS! Relaxing after a long day of walking and site seeing
Under $100 a night if you keep your eye out
Bad:
Rooms were a little outdated
I have stayed at a few hotels in San Francisco and this by far is the best! I will be stayign here again for sure.

title: “Jeffery, Concierge Coordinator”
text: We were looking for a great little place close by, knowing the neighborhood is a challenge. Walking distance, too. Jeffrey suggested a fantastic place called Taboon on 52nd and 10th Ave. One of the best meals I've had in NYC. Great bar, too. Every bite was delicious. A perfect little corner resto about 5 minutes from the hotel.

title: “a value but dissapointed”
text: this is a good value if you're a 20 something staying in pacific beach for a few days. for me visiting my 22 yesr old daughter, it was mediocre at best. don't stay in room 42, they pick up trash just outside at 6 am. one thing for sure, it had the best water pressure, unless you're at a spa. it was like a exfoliation treatment. if you can afford more, step up some from this dated motel.

title: “Close to everything”
text:
Connie Wilson is a wonderful ambassador for this hotel
Perfect location and great for families

title: “Great Service”
text: This hotel is amazing. We felt like royalty. The staff attends to your every need - whatever paper you want, whatever temperature you like... We had a great view of the bay bridge and could walk to Chinatown, the Embarcadero, Union Square and cable cars. It is a longer walk or a quick bus ride to Fishermans Wharf but that was fine with us since it was so crowded. We had better restaurants near us including the hotel restaurant. I thought this type of personalized attention only came in $1000 a night rooms. makes for a very special visit.

title: “Just another Holiday Inn----however.......”
text:
This is your average Holiday Inn. Nothing fancy, nothing terrible, however, it is in the most awesome location. A half a block away is the Betsy Ross house (yawn) but still nice to know that it is there. My collegue told me Benjamin Franklin's grave is right across the street. I know this sounds crazy but my collegues traveling with me said that this hotel has paranormal activities in it. I did not observe any however my associates said that things were moved around in their rooms etc. I rollerbladed to all my favorite places downtown. I love this location. I would urge all travelers to be a bit careful when venturing out at night.
 I did find the street noise to be a bit loud at this hotel. I was on the 4th floor and could hear sirens and loud cars throughout the night. I really liked the microwave and the fridge in my room. There is a convenience store close by. Caution: This is an expensive area so be prepared to pay a little bit more for things wherever you go in this neighborhood. I do think that it is worth it though. Nice rooftop pool

title: “Top Location, Staff and Facility”
text: My wife and I stayed at the Courtyard by Marriott in the Capital Hill/Navy Yard location on Sep 22-25. We were there to see a Brewers/Nationals game as well as use our location as a base to see some of DC's monuments (ML King, FDR & Jefferson) and a few Civil War battlefields. Their staff is extremely courteous and helpful with getting settled, & getting around the area-especially if you are inclined to walk. The hotel has been there 7 yrs but is sparkling & very well maintained. Parking within the building. This is an area with lots of new apt/condo construction and only a few blocks from National's Park for baseball fans. Plenty of great restaurants within a short walk on 8th St such as Belga Cafe & Senarts.

title: “OK Stay, great location close to LAX”
text: I stayed at the Westin LAX several years ago and had a great stay. This time after I walked in my room and set my luggage down I noticed there was dust on the dresser,tables etc. I don't usually complain but it just seemed like the room hadn't been used in a while. I called the front desk and they sent someone up right away to wipe things down. The hotel was a great location close to LAX and offered a shuttle to and from the airport. This Westin just isn't as nice as other properties I've stayed at but I did enjoy the heavenly bed, very comfortable. Also we used the pool which was ok. The workout facilities were really nice but I didn't get a chance to use them.

title: “It's why the Ritz is the Ritz”
text:
Some hotels benefit from their location. This isn't one of them--in the sense that there are no sweeping ocean views or mountain vistas. So no "halo" effect from the setting.
The Ritz excels, then, based on the quality of its rooms and on its service, especially on the latter. From Alex at the front desk, to the housekeeping staff to the valets, the service was impeccable.
The room was no slouch either. Loved the bathroom--big tub and shower, side by side, plenty of room for toiletries, an awesome haridryer and a makeup mirror that's actually short enough for my use.
The only thing that seemed out of place was the phone, which was tucked away. Maybe it was embarrassed by its looks, which were out fo the '70s. But that's very minor because, frankly, who uses an in-room phone anymore?
Thanks to all at the Ritz who made our one-night stay an affair to remember.

title: “Go on, treat yourself!”
text: My wife and I were meeting up with a couple of very standing friends. They came from Australia and we came from England. Lots of our friends who had visited san Francisco before suggested nice hotels, but we settled on The Fairmont for no particular reason. When we arrived, it was just such a lovely experience, the lobby is a good size and old fashioned enough to be opulent. Our friends arrived from Australia at 11am, not a good time as the hotel would not allow them to enter their room until 3pm, a real minus point for anyone travelling long distances and needing a rest and something the hotel should address, it is very off putting to be so tired and denied a room for 4 hours! Other than that, the hotel is a great experience. The rooms are well furnished with all the amenities you could need and the breakfast dining on a par with anywhere else i have stayed in around the world at this price. We did not eat our evening meal there so i cannot comment, but one place to dine in San Francisco and must not be missed under any circumstances is Gary Danco's, but book weeks before your trip as it is fully booked every night without fail, in fact, book there for every evening, the menu is so comprehensive it would take a month to try everything. Back to The Fairmont. Situated at the top of Nob Hill and with cablecar access right outside the door going to Union Square or Fishermans Wharf or Golden Gate Park, it's positioning is perfect. Just one thing to try during the day, hire a bicycle and cross The Golden Gate Bridge, carry on to Sausalito and catch the ferry back to Fishermans Wharf, but put on sun block on your face as the wind, even a gentle breeze, can give you a very red face in the morning. Next day try the Natural History Museum in the G G Park, between the museum and walking in the park, that could be a 2 dayser, but go there on a trolley bus, it stops right outside gate 8. Union Square shopping is great (if you like shopping) and Chinatown is another experience. Lombard Street has to be walked down, just to say you have done it, and walk back to the hotel sometimes just to work up an apetite for afternoon tea and a shower before taking the cablecar to Gary Danko. You can tell my trip to The Fairmont was such a joy, the bed was out of this world too, mind you, I would have been dissappointed if it wasn't!

title: “Central location”
text:
We stayed at the Hyatt because they had a special rate for a wedding we were attending. The building was very impressive as was the lobby. There was a slight wait at the concierge to check-in, but the service was friendly and helpful. We had early check-in, and sure enough our room was ready. Our room was 2117, and as we approached through the hallway, it was littered with room service items. We figured since people had just checked out and housekeeping was just getting around to cleaning it up, but for the duration of our stay there was constantly trays outside. 
Luckily our room was well appointed with the updated linens and decor. The room was bigger than I imagined with a king size bed, tv with cable. The bathroom was definitely New York sized though, and I didn't feel like it was the cleanest hotel bathroom I've ever been in. But it did have nice Lemon + Lavender scented toiletries. As well as a so-so hairdryer. Our biggest complaint was the noise. The walls were paper thin and we could hear the guy next door sneezing and coughing as well as people talking in the hallway. Another complaint was the price of room service. Yes, this is New York, but $8 for a cup of coffee + $5 delivery charge + 15% gratuity + 2% tax? We're talking almost $15 for one coffee. I don't know who was able to afford all the plates of food we kept seeing in the hallway. 
Our checkout went smoothly, and we opted to do it through the concierge to avoid any strange charges to the room or whatnot that come with travelling. Then we left our bags with the Bell desk, which cost us $2 a bag.
All in all, it was an average stay. I've never stayed in a hotel in NYC as I've always stayed with family, so it was my first experience. I'm hesitant to say if we'll stay here again, but for the price ($269/nt) I guess it was good, and it is definitely centrally located right next door to Grand Central Terminal and 2 blocks from 5th avenue shopping, and our shuttle to the hotel was right around the block. Apparently a cab to Laguardia is $20 from Grand Central and the shuttle we took with the New York Express Shuttle Bus cost us $12 a person one way. Depending on how many people are travelling together, a cab may actually be cheaper, but we were happy with the shuttle bus.

title: “Nice Place”
text: Stayed here in July. Centrally located. A good value. Room/Bath seemed small, but everything in NYC is. We are a family of 4 and needed space (1 bedroom)..This was just what we needed as our long vacation headed into NYC. Bed was very comfortable. Room very clean. Not noisy. Not a fan of the dining options but jeez it's NYC you can find something anywhere. Staff very accommodating and polite. reat views the higher up you go. We were 29th floor. Morning breakfast (continental) was adequate. Tiny coffee cups aggravated me as I'm use to my DD large each am, so for that I had to walk a block. Overall it's enough to get you going.

title: “Location Location Location”
text: Folks this hotel is in the smack middle of everything. A taxi ride to pier 39 is $11bucks and if your lazy and want to take a cab to union square vs the trolly its like $4.50. Airport cab fare is $35.00..Homeless people are all over the city not just near this hotel. The rooms are very nice and the staff at front desk will get you anything you need at anytime of day. If your on business the wireless internet is fine..I would suggest that anyone looking to book a room here get a free privledge card number first at holiday inns website so that way your morning breakfests are free. If you dont then the buffet breakfeast costs $15. Overall this hotel did the trick and the price was great.

title: “Definitely stay here!”
text:
Great find and a great buy! 
I was at a conference in Baltimore and booked a standard room. The suite I was given was actually much closer to a one-bedroom apartment at the same price. The hotel is one block from the Inner Harbor so very convenient to all touristy things. Good breakfast in the Cloud Room with excellent views, good treadmills,great beds,professional and friendly staff. Definitely will recommend and will stay here again.

title: “Very Chic, Modern & Great Service”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the clift for valentines weekend. This hotel is very modern looking. From the moment we checked in to the moment we check out, we had great customer service. We were always treated like VIPs. Our room was the standard King room. The room while being a little small, worked out great. Our bed was amazing and the decor made the room comforatable and refined. (bathroom was tiny....only one of us could be in there at a time). The room had huge mirrors that made the room seem bigger. 
The Redwood Room at the Clift is a great lounge/bar. The only draw back is the only way to get a table is if you get bottle service. 
Hotel location was close to Union Square and cable cars.
I would not recommend this hotel for older couples...the hippness might be lost on them.

title: “Warm Welcome From Start to Finish@Rodeway”
text: The entire staff of Rodeway is a great team of down to earth professionals. I was greeted by Aastha, a down to earth front desk attendant. She recommended a great Indian restaurant in my travels downtown to catch John Legend And Sade Concert at 1st Mariner Arena in Baltimore, In addition upon my late evening arrival Kumar welcome me with a warm smile. Off to my king size bed (bst sleep I ever got traveling) bed was comfy I woke up thinking I was at home on my memory foam mattress. The breakfast the next day hit the spot. The housekeeping staff was polite, also met Shawn who has a ever present smile on his face. The staff enjoy working at Rodeway Inn and it shows by their warm demeonor. To top it off can't beat the value for a clean, cosy room with large bathroom,, fridge, cable tv, free wifi in room. and cold AC, recommend it in your travels in Baltimore Area. Albert El Tiraflecha Dominguez

title: “Amazing stay! Will be going back....”
text:
I stayed at Hotel Palomar from March 29th to April 2nd. This is during the Cherry Blossom festival and, as it turns out the US March break. I arrived around 11am and they let me check in and go to my room. A room that was so comfortable, so quiet and so nice I still can't believe it. My room was on the back of the building so I didn't have much of a view...but to be honest I wasn't in Washington, DC for a hotel view. The rooms aren't huge but extremely comfortable. Every staff member I came in contact with was so pleasant and so helpful. The lobby is beautiful and the restaurant is quite nice too. 
The neighborhood has lots to offer in terms of restaurants. From Starbucks, a Cafe, Japanese, VIetnamese, Vegetarian, Pizza. Everything you could want. If that's not enough and you want to go "downtown" it's a very easy 5-7 minute ride on the Metro Rail - even in the rush hour.

title: “Luxury!”
text: All out extras: gift bags, in room breakfast, amazingly soft bathrobe, plasma tv. Above and beyond expectations!

title: “Worst Experience Ever”
text:
This was my worst hotel experience ever. I was surprised since it was a Days Inn, and the reviews on this website are mostly good.
Dirty sheets and blankets, TV had 4 working channels, HBO was fuzzy (funny since outside the window in the trashy area below was the sattelite dish). We were supposed to get nonsmoking but we got smoking. Cockroaches.. It was terrible and we will let everyone know.

title: “Relaxing and Excellent View”
text: Always a great place to stay. Walking distance to all downtown locations. Good security and friendly staff. Been staying here for many years and many more in the future!

title: “Great Hotel In Fantastic Location”
text:
Have just completed a 10day stay at Novotel Times Square and very pleased with all aspects of this hotel.
The check-in was fast and friendly and even included an up-grade to higher floor with fantastic view of Times Square. Rooms are quite large and have the advantage of window opening for fresh air. The lifts are large and quick.( no endless waiting) Housekeeping is also quick and efficent. The foyer area has the added bonus of ample comfortable seating if necessary for later airport departures. Computers and printers are also available foc. in foyer.
The dining area combines in-door and outside terraces with ample variety of servings. A supermarket and pharmacy are located on the outside street corner.
Hotel location is the best. Right near corner of Broadway amongst the Theatres and walking distance to Times Square and Central Park. The subway is very close by and is the only way to travel round Manhattan"s other districts. So impressed with this hotel we have re-booked on return NY. lay-over in JUly.
Highly recommend, you will not be disappointed.

title: “Only average, best avoided”
text:
The Beekman was our major "spend" for a week in NY, we chose to spend a few nights out in Queens to save money, and finish off the week with a couple of nights in the supposedly nice Beekman Hotel on Manhattan.
We booked a stay in the Beekman via an online booking agent, which is where our problems began. The booking had been cancelled by the Beekman due to payment not getting made as of our time of check-in by the booking agent. Not their problem I guess, but the manager we spoke to had to be the rudest person I met in NY all week - we were obviously in a spot of bother, and the best she could offer us was a different (lesser) room, which would have been OK, except she insisted on charging us UPFRONT for the full room rate, plus some. As finding a room at such late notice in NY is next to impossible, we were forced into taking this room. When I tried to reason with the manager regarding the price, suggesting that the rate they were supposed to have been paid by the agent (and which we had booked at) was approximately half of this value, she refused to cooperate. Her perogative I guess, but a terrible attitude in general.
The room itself was indeed massive (I think it was one of their "studios"), but it was in a different building, with no porter service offered. The room was in a fairly decrepit state (possibly why it was still empty), and not clean enough by any stretch. The sheets on the bed were also threadbare and rough, which is not what you expect when paying over US$450 per night! The only good thing was access to a (very old and broken) kitchentte, and the minimal street noise we were subject to due to our location - necessary as we needed to have the windows open for ventilation as there was no cooling or heating to speak of!
Overall, I would not be recommending this hotel to anyone - if you book a few months in advance, you can get a lot nicer in Manhattan for less money. I could have forgiven some of the failings if it weren't for the most obnoxious management I have ever come across - if the hotel wants to accept business from agents, then they should be more accomdating to problems such as we had, rather than viewing them as a means to double their money.

title: “Great location and functional hotel”
text: I can't fault this hotel - great location and helpful staff. We found it a good base for sight seeing. It's nothing special in terms of design though and so if you wanted to get the full Washington hotel experience this might not be for you.

title: “No vending machines!”
text:
Beautiful hotel - large, picturesque, and all the good looks I could want. Great location - about a block and half to the Woodley Park/Zoo Metro Station.
The room was not ready when we checked in (around noon) and they called us to inform us it was ready not long after. Left a few bags with the bellhop. Returned a little after 11 pm - our room key was waiting in a card holder for advance check in.. after a long walk we found our room which had just one king sized bed. Although this wasn't an issue for me, it was for my travel companion who was very upset that we were given one bed. I realized others may be upset over this so I'm mentioning it. It was a big bed with more than enough room for several adults to sleep in. The room was slightly worn out, but in excellent condition overall. 
The biggest complaint we both had was the absolute lack of even 1 vending machine. It was the overpriced bar or be thirsty. (All the shops close early so there's no place to buy a bottle of water or snack) and room service and the bar were way too expensive.

title: “Great place to stay for a family vacation!”
text:
Cool hotel with a funky feel. Rooms are stylish and clean. Staff is friendly and helpful. The location was great!
Room was perfect for family of 4. Kids loved the roof top pool. 
Nice free wine hour every evening.
You can see Petco park from the pool. 
Only real con was $40 to park! Yikes!

title: “A Good Stay”
text:
We've just returned from a three night stay at the Mariott. The staff was very helpful and always with a smile. The room and the bathroom were very clean and the bed very comfortable. The room size, though somewhat small, was typical of the size you would get at any major city . The bar on the 37th floor offers magnificent view of the city and is well worth the ride up the elevator. 
The hotel is in a great location. It is near the shopping center, a 10 minute walk from China Town, a very short walk to the cable car, and around the corner from SF muesum of modern art. 
This hotel is a great place for both buisness and pleasure.

title: “Great hotel in excellent location”
text: We had three in a deluxe double room. The room was large, clean, value-priced, and very comfortable. The location was excellent, near the Four Seasons Hotel and close to Georgetown and the Foggy Bottom Metro. Had a neighborhood feel. Hotel staff was friendly and always helpful. We didn't eat at the Landmark restaurant, which is on the property. We've stayed in D.C. many times, and we will definitely stay here again and would recommend this hotel to others.

title: “Kind of Run Down - Location Good If You Want Midtown”
text:
I stayed here in mid-July with a group for a conference. It is a small hotel, rooms are actually large for NYC, it is an old hotel and it does not appear that any major improvements have been done to it in the last fifteen years or more.
Everyone in our group (11 persons) had problems with their Key Card for their room. This happen all three days we were there, which is not fun when you have to go all the way back down to the lobby to get a new key two out of three times you want to get in your room. The problem seemed to be with the Key Card machine at the Front Desk, but that was no consolation when your key did not work.
Several in our group mentioned the A/C in their room would not cool their room down enough, mine was ok but I had it set on the coldest setting.
There is no restaurant in the hotel, this was not a big inconvenience as there was a Starbucks on the corner a half block away, and a good place across the street that was very popular with locals. Which I went to every morning.
The bed was comfortable, I was on the 5th floor and traffic noise was not bad enough to keep me awake. Lower floors I think this could be a problem.
My room was clean and the Wi-Fi did work well, that was a plus.
The roof top bar is very small and has no real view of anything so not as great a place as it might seem.
Subways are not too far away 3-4 blocks but you are not really bay anything touristy except maybe the UN. 
It is a good walk to Times Square, not something I would want to do more than once.
I have stayed in much worse places, but I can’t honestly say I would not recommend to friends unless they had reason to be in this part of the city.
If I was visiting NYC as a tourist I would stay no more than one block off of Times Square, that is where everyone wants to be.

title: “Great Stay and Location”
text:
We stayed at the MO for four nights in March. When we arrived in the morning to check in, we had to wait but did not mind at all because we were able to watch Angelina Jolie being filmed in the hotel lobby . Our room was ready and we walked thorough the film crew in between takes. This was a wonderful start to our trip. We received a complimentary upgrade through our Amex. Our room had a view of the Jefferson Memorial. I am not sure what everyone is complaining about in regards to location of the hotel. The hotel is so centrally located and its only 2 blocks to the national mall. The subway is only a block a way but we never used it. The hotel has a walkway behind the hotel that drops you within a block of the Jefferson Memorial. I assume everyone on trip advisor who complained about the location may not be in the best of shape as we did not find the hotel far from any attraction. In fact the hotel is across the street from the treasury department where you can go on a tour to see how money is printed. 
Our room was very clean. The breakfast we had was great and was included in our amex fine hotels and resorts program. We also received a $75 credit towards spa products. The hotel staff was extremely helpful and friendly. We used the hotel transportation to and from the airport. I had left some papers in the car and the driver made every effort to find me and return them to me. The drivers were so courteous and friendly. We did use a taxi at night to go to dinner at Capital Grill. The bellhops were great at getting us in a taxi and giving the driver exact directions. Would have no reservations in staying at the MO again. We had stayed at the Willard before but I prefer the MO, more modern.

title: “A nice surprise”
text: This was a nice surprise for us given that we had never stayed here before. The decor is very modern. Room is inviting when you walk in. It was very clean and a comfortable bed. The fact that they would accept a pet made it even nicer. The staff is welcoming and inviting.

title: “Beautiful hotel, good Location, good service, great rooms.”
text:
Really loved this hotel. The front desk staff was very helpful and friendly. The rooms were good sized and very modernly designed. Was very impressed.
Didn't go to the restaurant, went up to the hotel bar a few times. The spot was really well designed. Wasn't too impressed with the bartender though who messed up my $12 dollar drink. He had to look up how to make an old fashioned, and thoroughly messed it up. 
But besides that little hiccup, the place and the staff was wonderful. Wouldn't think twice about booking there again for my next trip.

title: “Jolly Madison - Customer Service could be improved”
text:
I stayed at the Jolly Madison Towers from 14 September for 5 nights. I travelled with 5 friends to celebrate my 30th birthday.
The main reception looks nice apart from some of the furniture is a bit shabby. The staff on reception were ok but not overly friendly. The concierge/bellmen were friendly. The member of staff who booked our return taxi to the sirport was not very friendly and did not seem happy to have to call and arrange this.
Our room was on the 7th floor which did not have great floors, The four others were on the 12th floor and had much better views. The rooms were quite small but perfectly adequate. The bathroom was nice but the rest of the room could have done with a bit of re-decorating. The air conditioning worked well but was noisy,
The bar was good for happy hour with half price drinks but about the same price as other bars outside of this ($7 for fruit juice and $12 for vodka and orange). The barman who was there on our first two nights was really friendly and gave us good advice on where to go for food and drink. The barman who was on the other nights was not that friendly.
The location of the hotel is excellent as is only 5 minutes walk from the Empire State Building and Grand Central Station. Times Square is only about 10 - 15 minutes walk. 
As for New York itself I loved it and would defintiely go back. Not sure if I would go back to this hotel as although the location is very good the reception staff and some of the bar staff could do with some customer service training.

title: “EXCELLANT”
text:
What a great place, great linens. I'm sure they were Peacock Alley. Newly remodeled. VERY clean , terrific staff,cleaning and repairs. We broke a bottle on the steps and immediately someone was there to clean it up BEFORE we could even call them.
Will be here again

title: “Different than other Homewoods”
text: As a family with young children, we prefer suite style hotels, so we have stayed at quite a few Homewoods. This one, on the inside, was the same as any other Homewood. The rooms were clean, plenty of towels, updated kitchen and bathroom. The bed was very comfortable. Our kids loved the outdoor pool, and the breakfast was a typical Homewood variety of hot and cold items. The part that was different about this Homewood was that the rooms are set up to appear more like townhouses, which means that they have doors leading directly to the outside. Typically we avoid hotel rooms that lead directly to outside, but the setup was much nicer than a motel style with exterior doors. The other difference that was somewhat of a pain was that to reach most of the rooms, they could only be reached via stairs. Carrying suitcases and tired kids up a flight of stairs is not a huge deal, but somewhat inconvenient. I can imagine that this would be a bigger issue for an older person or someone who has difficulty climbing stairs. When we visit a hotel, we usually like to grab a luggage cart and take everything all in one trip. This isn't possible at this hotel, so if you have more luggage than you can carry up the stairs, it might take several trips to get all of your belongings into your room. Staff members were friendly and everything was clean. We would stay here again if we couldn't find an available room at a more typical hotel style Homewood Suites.

title: “It's ok for the price..”
text: First time in the city,didn't want to spend alot for a room we wouldn't be in much.The room are bigger than most,very clean,good quiet area.Two blocks away from restuarants.You have to share bathrooms,wasn't ever a problem.You only have a sink in the room.It's not bad for the price you won't anything else in the city for that price.I would stay there again.

title: “Great Location”
text: I was there for a conference in the UN. This was a minute's walk away from the UN building. It has amazing rooms. They're massive. you have a living room, a kitchen, a bedroom and an ironing room. Its a whole apartment. 15 minutes walk to the times square. The view from the top of the tower is amazing. There is a nice cafe in front of the hotel which satisfies all your cuisine desires. I proffered picking up some stuff from the Gourmet store across the road and cooking myself. Its highly recommended if you're traveling with your kids or with your family. The television has a great set of movies. You can get here from JFK at exactly 45 dollars in the Yellow cabs, fixed rate. Do not get into the cabs which are not the yellow ones. They charge you double the price. These drivers come upto you the moment you leave the airport and offer you taxis. The hotel provided me with a limousine for my departure to JFK for a mere 60 dollars.

title: “Sleepless in Seattle”
text:
Wonderful hotel in a very convenient location. Short walk to monorail and Pike Market. We stayed in a corner King---the room was immense with great views, very contemporary look, gorgeous bath amenities. The entire staff could not have been more cordial--Special kudos to Sarah at the desk and the concierge for his restaurant recommendation(Blue Acre--Fabulous!)
Dallas Cowboys also stayed while we were there. If and when we return to Seattle, we will definitely book here. A totally marvelous experience!

title: “Very good experience”
text:
Our family stayed at the Doubletree for a reunion during the last week in July. We had a very pleasant stay and were treated very well. All of the employees seemed very friendly and seemed happy to help us with anything we needed. The hotel is a bit out of the way from most of the attractions which the city has to offer, but we were able to drive to the downtown area in about 10 min.
We checked in a bit early on our first day, but they still had our room ready as we had reserved it. Our 2 double bed room was clean, but a bit small. It had the typical furnishings, but they had to be a little closer than normal to make everything fit. Also, the room had no safe, fridge, or microwave. We asked for a mountain view room (see pic), which was a nicer view than the other side, although there were housing projects to look at right below our window.
The hotel food was decent. Not bad but nothing to rave about. They have several good sized comfortable sitting areas in the spacious lobby and lounge area, and they have a smoking area with benches situated outside the front entrance. Although there were some bums who occassionally came around after dark scrounging cigarettes or asking for money. The hotel needs to take care of this. 
A few other items of interest: there is plentiful parking, the airport shuttles ran on time, the gift shop was typically way overpriced, there is a sizeable shopping center across the street, the in-room television internet connection is VERY slow, the housekeeping was usually prompt and did a good job, and the hotel seemed very clean and well kept. 
Overall, we had a good experience at the hotel and would recommend it to others.

title: “Another Great Stay!”
text: My husband and I took our in-laws with us on a trip this year to Houston to watch the Astros play the Rangers and they loved the Hilton. They were extremely impressed with the hotel overall. From the time we arrived until the time we checked out it was great service! You couldn't ask for a better location to the park and what amazing views you get of Minute Maid Park and of Discovery Green. Thanks again to the staff at the Hilton for making our stay so wonderful!

title: “Nice, cheap and clean with a good location”
text:
I stayed at the Hotel Mayflower for 8 nights, when I attended the JavaOne conference and this hotel is well worth the $127 I paid per night. The reception staff are very nice and they help you with all your requests and the only remark I have, is that the complimentary breakfast is a bit boring after a few days, but on the other hand, it's included in the price, which is not so common in the U.S.
If you get a room which faces Bush street, then I advice you to get som ear plugs, because there are a lot of traffic and there are also lot's of ambulances and fire trucks on this street during the nights.

title: “It is okay if you can get a deal”
text:
This hotel was completely okay and only okay. Now that being said we were very glad we went through priceline and only paid $50 a night for our room because that is all it was worth. There are much better places around to stay if you are paying the full price of 100+ dollars a night. I would equate it more along the lines of a basic moderate hotel rather than the upscale rating most places give it. The hotel is definitely old and shows it in places. The bathroom in our room was clean enough but definitely could have been cleaner. The duvet cover also had stains on it. The view out of our window was straight into another room due to the hotels u-shape cut out. You literally could look straight into their room onto their bed....probably not most people's desire. 
Parking is on the expensive side for $31 a night for valet. You can park your car yourself in a nearby garage however you have to pay $18 every time you leave the garage. So if you plan on using your car you might as well settle on the valet price because at least it does include in and out service.
The sleep number beds also seemed to be a big deal to the hotel. However they are nothing more than a glorified air mattress inside a mattress covering.
It was only several blocks from the inner harbor and an easy walk so that was nice. However if you are going to pay full price there are better options available in the Baltimore Inner Harbor/Downtown area.

title: “Very nice hotel”
text: We stayed for 2 days during Cherry Blossom festival, using our Marriott points. We were very pleased with the quality of the hotel. Very well appointed and kept. The breakfast and dinners were well done. Quite an array of foods and beverages. No alcohol at happy hour though. We look forward to coming again and staying here. It was a great location just off the Mall. Only a couple of blocks away from many of the great tourist attractions. One review mentioned no grocery stores. I think they will have groceries delivered to your room for you if you fill out a form and submit it to the front desk.

title: “Great choice for a long weekend”
text: Two lifelong friends and I spent a terrific weekend at Hotel Monaco in San Francisco. The staff was uniformly friendly, helpful and interested in our comfort. The room decor is zany (reminds one of a big top in the circus) but comfortable. We loved the location: close to cozy little restaurants and Union Square shopping. As others have mentioned, the wine reception is a great way to transition from daytime activities to evening dinner. The restaurant and bar are excellent if you don't want to venture out in the evening chill, and the wait staff is very accomodating. I'll be back.

title: “GREAT HOTEL IN A GREAT LOCATION”
text: So convenient to everywhere. Great room with a view. Would recommend its location to everyone.

title: “Step directly into or away from the cocophany of Times Square”
text: This Crowne Plaza hotel is really a part of Times Square. Note that the lobby is on the 2nd floor, and that one enters through the parking garage from either 48th or 49th Street, or through a small doorway on Broadway between those streets. It's a big, somewhat impersonal place with good employees who make you feel welcome (we experienced a friendly valet, desk clerk, concierge, and housekeeper all in quick succession). Views of the Hudson River from our 44th-floor room were remarkable (the "other" side of the hotel overlooks the bright lights of Times Square). The bed was quite comfortable, bathroom was well-appointed; both were very clean and in good shape. Elevator service was able to keep up with a busy summer weekend crowd. In-room wifi seemed pretty expensive ($14.95), as did in-house breakfast buffet ($30). "Restaurant Row" (46th street between 8th & 9th Avenues) is only a block away.

title: “The website to this hotel doesnt tell you everything.....”
text:
My husband and I took my parents to NYC for the first time, this past week. The website to this hotel showed some great photos! location looked great, etc. We got there and a few things were a bit different.
First off- what they fail to tell you is the location of the hotel is literally right next door to the New York City Parole Center...as well as on the same side of the street about 6 adult book stores, liquor store, etc. We arent prudes lol we thought it was actually really funny that no one mentioned any of this in any of the reviews....but after we came back and forth from the hotel many times, passing all of these locations, its not really the kind of people you want to hang out with. I would think the Sheraton would have done a bit better with this. Its pan handling central, drunks on the sidewalk, etc. all of it is something you run into, getting in and out of your hotel. 
The vending machines....nothing in them is cold. all of the soda is warm, etc, and they didnt work. It cost us $9 for 2 cans of soda because the machine kept eating the money and the person up front we talked to said they couldnt do anything about it...super. 
The beds are absolutely awesome...so soft, you just fall right asleep! 
The lobby is really small, but clean, the staff is wonderful, the do yourself a favor and stay away from the restaurant.
Its called the "gotham bistro" however it looks like a conference room that has some tables added. the server we had was wonderful and the fact that everything sucked wasnt his fault. we tipped him well because he was just wonderful.
we ordered breakfast...a "stack of pancakes" was $12. when they came out, they literally were the size of a lid on a large "to go" soda cup from a fast food restaurant, and they were paper thin. the "stack" of pancakes was 3 of them. you could tell they were the type of pancakes that you just had to microwave to cook them.
i ordered my breakfast and just had the classic...bacon, 2 eggs, toast and homefries.
i asked for my eggs to be over medium. they came out hard as a rock..no yolk, etc. the bacon had clearly been sitting for several hours...and every one of the meals we got was cold. 
our breakfast, for 4 of us, was $70....re-freakin-diculous. I should have went to mcdonalds instead..
keep in mind...we arent picky people...we roll with the punches, but this stuff just stood out and we really arent complainers. when everyone thinks the same thing...something is wrong...
oh and here's the kicker...our train left at 7am, so we needed a cab at 530am (we were heading to boston before coming back home to seattle) and we asked the front desk the best way to go about that. the lady kindly let us know that in NYC you cant call for a cab....and that the hotel doesnt have any cabs that time of the morning so we would have to take all of our luggage to the next block and get a cab there....PASSING THE PAROLE OFFICE, THE LIQUER STORE, ETC AT 530AM WITH ALL THE CRAZIES OUTSIDE GOING THROUGH THE PANHANDLERS, ETC. yeah...not safe. they didnt seem to care.......they said oh well, you have to take your luggage and walk. 4 adults, 6 pieces of luggage...not cool.

title: “nice downtown stay”
text: hotel old but upkeep is meticulous.. rooms was large with nice appointments and refrig..no ice machines which is a pain but brought to room in only minutes when requested. Very friendly staff. great downtown location. just a really neat older hotel.

title: “Sweet Stay!”
text:
PROS: Great front desk service...very courteous & accomodating. Rooms were avg size but nicely furnished. Location...right on the Riverwalk, lots of restaurants to choose from. Right across from the ALAMO!!!
CONS: Parking...22 dollars for self park on the garage. Small bathroom. 
SUPER PRO: The price! Got this room for $118/ night on a weekend on Priceline when the room was going for $200!!! =)Will stay here again over and over and over!!!

title: “Fantastic”
text:
My husband was relunctant to go to New York City, so I tried to be very careful and get a hotel he might like.
The Lowell definitely fit the bill. The room was large (for New York standards) with a small kitchenette. The service was outstanding and the food was great. I would definitely stay here again.
The only thing I would change is I wouldn't eat at the Post House again. I ordered my steak medium and the inside was still raw. From what I could see of the other steaks served, this was typical.

title: “great business option”
text: The lobby is rather shabby and assuming, but the rooms are very large by NY standards and the working desk in the room was one of the largest I've seen. Very easy to get a few hours work in comfortably in the room. The 2nd floor lounge area is great. The street is very noisy, so the room actually comes with ear plugs!

title: “Beautiful park view”
text: Arriving at 10 pm, the park view room we had booked and paid 1 month in advance was not available. We had a room switch to a city view room. The next day our room was still not available so we were left for 3 hours without a room! Finally we were switch to a upgraded park view room and free wifi connection for our whole 5 nights stay. The room was very spacious, the sleep quality was excellent and the hotel location is ideal. If you like to train, the basement gym is ok but a bit too small

title: “Great staff and service! Convenient for LAX”
text:
I stayed here on business so I wasn't able to select any other properties. That being said, I know I will choose to stay here in the future. The frequent shuttle service makes this easy to get to and from the airport. 
The hotel staff were second to none during my stay. Being a frequent traveler, I had access to the lounge. I found the food and selections to be ample and well stocked. 
My room was fine and standard Marriott decor. There was nothing amazing about it, but I have nothing negative to say about it either. 
The fitness center is very good here,but the small pool and hot tub was much smaller than I expected for a hotel of this size. I had to use the concierge service for a taxi, as well as storing luggage and they were very friendly and helpful. I will most definitely return.

title: “Excellent Pre or Post cruise hotel”
text: Wonderful location close to the pier. Easy walking distance to several restaurants. Room was very clean and large. The shuttle was only available for the trip to the pier so we used the commuter bus for our visit to Long Beach. The concierge was wonderful and very knowledgeable. Our room overlooked the pool and waterway and we saw a ship leave which was nice. The coffee was expensive and in room was single pods but the last morning we found a coffee shop across the street which was great. I would stay there again because of the cleanliness and convenience.

title: “Difficult not to love, but...”
text:
This was my first time in Boston and I chose this property because of the location and the price range. I stayed for 6 nights. I read all the reviews before so the renovation was not a surprise. For me, it is difficult not to love this hotel. I had room 402, quiet and in the back, and the jackhammer woke me up only once around 7 am. My solution was to get breakfast as early as possible and just get out and walk or sit in the park. In the afternoons/evenings everything was fine and quiet. As it was very hot weather, I was happy that the airco was working fine throughout. What irritated me though was the toilet, which was pretty much unusable as it nearly always clogged up whatever I did.
Room cleaning was excellent, everything was clean throughout the week I stayed there and people at the reception and everybody else were very nice indeed. 
I consider this property a VERY good deal at the price it charges. If it were any more expensive, I would change my mind. I would pay more though for better sanitation but I would definitely NOT want to be there when THAT is done to a Victorian building.
So, all in all, I can recommend this place, and the room 402 is great. Location is simply unbeatable: internet cafe accross the street, great stores all around and walkable distance to just about everywhere...

title: “Avoid”
text:
Definitely the worst Hilton I have ever stayed in. Reception was OK and staff friendly enough but as for the room it definitely needs a severe upgrade. 
- wallpaper peeling off the walls, 
- musty/smokey smell in a no smoking room
- air-conditioning/heater more in place in a dark satanic mill than a modern hotel room - so loud that I had to turn it off as soon as I went into the room
- dated furniture
- bed had seen better days
- room cleaning left something to be desired
etc.

title: “Not up to my expecations”
text:
So, when I lived in NYC, I frequently went to the lounge in the lobby. I really liked it. (Contrary to some of the other reviewers, I think the drink prices here are actually pretty reasonable for a bar of this class in Midtown.)
However, I was not that happy with the hotel itself. While cramped rooms are part of life in midtown, other hotels do a better job of utilizing the small space. The room had two small closets, one with drawers and the other with hangers. However, the one with drawers was so fill on mini-bar items that there wasn't really much space to actually put stuff. Also, the desk essentially blocked the other closet. The desk itself was also a concern since it didn't have a desk light by it and there was only one available outlet nearby. 
The lighting was also a concern. I know they are going for a specific mood, but since all the lights were on dimmers, perhaps they could have put higher wattage bulbs in and allowed people to dim the lights if they want. I did not want to try to get a floor lamp given the already limited space.
The bed and linens were fine, though not outstanding. The bathroom products were excellent, and the bathroom was well-designed and aesthetically pleasing.
Compared to other hotels in this price range in Midtown, I'd have to say that the Royalton is average, or slightly below average, in terms of room comfort. The staff I talked to were all great, and the bar/restaurant at great as well.

title: “Huge room!”
text:
We only stayed for 2 nights. The front desk were very efficient and checked us in and out very quickly. The room was huge with spacious seating area including a couch and desk. The king bed was very comfortable. Room had microwave, fridge, tea/coffee. The LCD TV had lots of channels. Breakfast was yummy, with the usual cereal, waffles, fruit, toast, pastries, hot food (scrambled eggs, sausage, hash brown), coffee/tea.
We were happy with the location as all we wanted to do was visit NASA museum which was about 20 kms from here. It's also very close to the Airport.
The wi-fi in the room was excellent. We had great signal strength and speed was great.

title: “Great location, big room, no noise from other rooms”
text: We had a great stay at this hotel. I'm a neat freak and won't pay this kind of money for a dirty room; no problems at all with that. Surprisingly big for new york standards, bathroom a bit small on counter space though. We could walk everywhere from here, or easily get to the subway station. Great concierge staff, courteous front desk staff. No problems with noise and the hotel was really busy when we stayed over St. Patty's day (didn't hear drunken partying in the middle of the night). We got a great rate booking with Priceline, and would definitely stay here again for future trips to NYC.

title: “Ask for the upper east side”
text: We got a room here for a week in August via Priceline. One side of the hotel backs on a major highway so we made it clear to the front desk that we wanted the downtown/Puget Sound side of the hotel. They gave us a hard time because we had used Priceline and others were paying full freight for the good side. But in the end they caved and gave us a high floor on the good side. The room was nice and the view was very nice. The only problem with the hotel is that it's on a steep hill and walking back from all the downtown attractions really works those buns. But there are some convenient bus lines nearby, and the new public library is a (steep) block away.

title: “Great rooms and amenities. Especially...”
text: Great rooms and amenities. Especially recommended if you are going to a concert downtown as they will drop you off there or anywhere else downtown. Caution: I parked in one of the near-by garages (ungated) to save on valet parking, and one of my hubcaps was stolen.

title: “Gem at SEATAC”
text:
This is a fantastic place not only for an airport hotel .. but for all business and holiday in the Seattle area!!
While we stayed only for one night, we wished that we would have stayed longer !!!

title: “Great hotel in a wonderful location”
text:
I stayed here this past weekend for two nights and enjoyed the hotel very much. I am a Marriott Silver member and I assume that's why I got moved up to the 34th floor and even had a view of the Empire State Building. The room was very clean and lots of room, esp compared to may other NYC hotels. It included a microwave, full refrigerator, since and dishwaher along with plates and silverware like all Residence Inns. Housekeeping did a great job keeping things clean and fresh in the room. The beds were quite comfortable and several types of pillows. The bathroom sink area is smaller, but the reset of the room was fine, but I was by myself.
The lobby is not huge, but plenty of room for checkin and the concierge along with the small market place for drinks and snack purchases. The concierge helped me with some restaurant ideas and booking a boat tour around Manhattan Island. The hotel is only a few block walk from Times Square and not far from Subway stations. Bryant Park is only a block away. The breakfast was good for something to eat in the mornings. It is very busy on the weekends and they even have a note in the elevators about how busy the elevators get at certain times during the breakfast.
The only problem I had was not really the hotel's fault. There is a door to the next room if you want adjoining rooms. Those doors do not hold back any noise though. The group in the room next to mine were very noisy when they came in and esp when they came in at 1 am or 4 am. The noise did not last real long but still a little annoying. 
Otherwise I liked the hotel very much. I would have no problem staying here again as long as I could get a reasonable rate. I understand it goes up quite a bit more during the summer on weekends, but then I think they all do in NYC.

title: “Great hotel and location”
text: Upon arrival we were greeted by friendly staff from the moment we opened our car door. There was a greeter welcoming guests right through the front door.
