The check-in process was pleasant as well. When I booked the room on their site, I noted that it was our anniversary and would prefer a higher floor. To my surprise, someone really read that! The front attendant wished us a Happy Anniversary and proceeded to tell us we would be on the top floor with a balcony, an upgrade compliments of our hotel. Very nice gesture. The entire weekend was great. Several well known restaurants all within walking distance. St Elmo's Steakhouse, a let down to say the least! I had to send my steak back twice and the waiter was annoyed that I would bother him for this.Veggies were totally undercooked as well, maybe that's s was they should be known for undercooked food? And you're gonna like it! That was the attitude, skip this place for sure and go next door, cool vibe good food.

title: “Disappointing Downtown Hotel”
text:
I stayed at the Westin Downtown Denver for 4 nights in July attending a conference. The hotel while lovely with a great location but has some signifcant issues. I was given a "patio room" on the 4th floor. There was a large patio outside the sliding glass doors, it would have been great if there had been some privacy, there was none. It had patios on either side that was only separted by fencing and at the end various people walked by on their way to the pool. I arrived 11:00 pm after a 4 hour flight delay, when I checked in I asked if I could still order room service and was told I could. The room service menu can only be found via the TV guest services channel, I found this annoying I would have preferred to read an actual menu. When I called to order the phone rang and rang for about 5 minutes before someone picked up.
The food during the conference was awful, 2 days in a row they served the same entree (dried chicken) for lunch, the other offerings weren't much better. They push that they are a "green" hotel and ask that you skip having the room made up with new sheets and towels daily. I don't have a problem with that, except that by day 3 I wanted new linens and the room made up and indicated that on the door handle. The room was never made up, I had to call to get it done.
Some other minor complaints, the ice machine on my floor was out of order for my entire stay and the room keys stopped working several times through out my stay.
Lastly, my husband met me at the hotel on my last night, when I checked in I gave the front desk his name so they would give him a room key. I needed itemized receipts from room service in order to submit my business expenses, I was assured that they would be in my final bill, they were not. When I asked for them, they arrived but had my husbands name as the guest, he was not the guest listed for the booking, he was not on the credit card on file and he was not even at the hotel when the room service was ordered. When I called the front desk to have this fixed the hotel personnel argued with me. It took some time but they finally found the receipts that I had signed.
One or two of these issues would be understandable but obviously something is very wrong for there to be so many issues.
On the good side, the location is great and the room was comfortable.

title: “Sleep on the floor”
text: Went two weeks ago to this former 5 star hotel. They redid the Ambassador East(why the name change). The redo is with the modern touch. The bed has no box spring so you end up sleeping 12 inches off the floor. C'mon guys this was not a good idea. The pillows were the most uncomfortable I have ever had. The room was small but clean just don't like the modern flavor, call me old fashioned but I like to climb up into bed not down into bed. The Pump room was okay, they just didn't improve on what used to be a great hotel..

title: “Wow...if you're coming to Boston and want to be near town, don't look anywhere else”
text:
I've learned to lower my expectations with most hotels, regardless of cost. This hotel is awesome - we stayed here prior to an early a.m. flight tomorrow (very convenient to Logan), and I can't think of a better way to start our New Year's vacay. 
Beautiful room/suite; decor is contemporary but tasteful and creates a very calm, comfortable yet stylish atmosphere. Thoughtful attention to details; free internet & wifi, VOIP calls, coffee, full compliment of hair dryer, nice shampoo/body lotion, etc.
The room we had was very spacious - if you're a business traveller, you could easily stay here for extended stays and be quite comfortable. There's a kitchenette (unobtrusive, but a great touch), nice bathroom with great amenities - even bath salts!! Which I gladly used in a hot bath on a cold night. 
We had a nice sitting area with a flat screen TV - great for hanging by yourself or entertaining for business, big window with sweeping view. Separate bedroom with corner windows - another sweeping view and a nice change from most small, dimly lit rooms. Also a flat screen in the bedroom, Bose w/iPod adapter, etc. This would even be a nice set-up for a family if you had adjoining or adjacent rooms - room for privacy with nice mingling space too. 
Again, just a really nice hotel, great staff, and convenient location. Would DEFINITELY highly recommend...regardless of what you're in Boston to do or see.

title: “Entire hotel smelled like smoke or heavy perfume”
text:
I arrived in the early evening, and was told there was only one room left. When I went to the room, it smelled strongly of perfume. The windows in the room did not open to be able to clear out the smell. I went back to the front desk, and it turned out that there was only one room left with a king size bed - I could get a different room with two queen beds. The second room smelled like smoke, and the windows also did not open. Both strong perfume and smoke give me a headache. The front desk clerk's attitude, while not specifically rude, was not particulary helpful. Finally, she told me she would have the night manager, who came on duty at 9:00 pm, have a room "cleaned" for me. I checked again around 10:00, and she still indicated that this would happen. A room was NOT "cleaned" for me, and I spent the night (and a large part of the next day) with a major headache, due to the smell of smoke. 
The hall outside the conference rooms where I was attending a two-day seminar also smelled like smoke.
The hotel did have two internet machines in the lobby for guest use, of which I made liberal use to make a reservation at another hotel for the second and third nights of my stay!

title: “Big hotel - right where it needs to be.”
text:
Spent 7 days here to attend an expo/conference in SF. I had booked a king bed and was allocated a twin, reception staff could not have been more helpful and upgraded me as the booking records clearly said King Bed!
My room was not very high up (so some street noise from O'Farrell) but was huge and was easy to get to. The rooms are not super modern but had all the required - WiFi and big flat screen. It looks like there is a very large upgrade programme underway but this never affected my stay. Fitness centre is good enough, has multiple of all main machines and good set of wieght machines and free weghts too. But no rowers? I mainly went running in the sunshine!
The very central location meant the expo centre was an pleasent walk every day and shopping (at the eves & weekend) and cable cars etc were just a short walk down the street.
Hotel bar was OK and had good wine slection. 
If you shun franchise eating (I do) then Pinecrest Diner (up the Hill on Mason St.) for breakfast and Fish and Farm (right opposite the Taylor St. exit) are both great. F&F has SF's #1 rated Burger.

title: “Wonderful - can I move in for the winter?”
text: I generally don't write reviews. But this hotel exceeded my expectations by far so I decieded to write to stay every aspect was wonderful. Service equal to a 4-5 star hotel, clean new hotel, beautiful and updated rooms, a nice breakfast. Way to go Phoenix Drury Inn. One note this hotel is North of Phoenix about 12 miles or so........it worked great for us but check out its location to see if it works well for you. If so you'll be in for a pleasant surprize.

title: “Descent hotel but noisy”
text: The hotel was okay- without any frills, it's a good hotel for a stopover. The room was clean, close to LAX and offers free shuttle bus. But it's very near to the airstrip so that I have to hear airplanes taking off every 5 minutes- and the noise didn't stop until the very late night.

title: “Terribly hip hotel”
text:
I stayed here for four nights with my fiance on a trip that combined work and pleasure. We both lived in NYC for many years and wanted a small hotel with a convenient location and good amenities. The Tribeca Grand delivers on both fronts; being in Tribeca is a great location for transportation all around the city and the hotel itself is quite nice. The hotel is super hip, maybe a little too hip for our taste. The bar and lounge areas were packed on the weekend, and although we were on the fifth floor, we could hear the noise loud and clear. We didn't see the white noise machine until we were leaving, but I have to assume that would have helped! 
The rooms themselves are nothing special. Like all NYC hotel rooms, they're very small. My fiance was working during the day from the hotel and the desk/chair are definitely not made for that purpose. It looks hip, but it's not very comfortable. We were placed in a handicap-accessible room for some reason and although it meant a large bathroom, the shower basically flooded the bathroom each day. To be fair, I assume that other rooms don't have that problem.
The staff is very friendly and accessible and the hotel is clean and up-to-date, but I've stayed in other hotels that offered better rooms and less noise.

title: “Very nice, great view, incredibly friendly service.”
text: We stayed for 3 nights. Once you get over the "jaunt" from the main hotel part to the tower, it is great. Request a corner room with a terrace. Very large room, more windows and beautiful views of the city. Happy hour every night with snacks and free breakfast were average. We only went one time. But.. if you have small kids, I'm sure it is a great bargain. Every single employee (and I mean EVERY single person working at the Hotel) was incredibly friendly, helpful, polite, etc..

title: “New Hilton Hotel”
text: I prefer the Hampton Inn on 23rd, but I could not procure a room. I enjoyed the stay and liked the room, I arrived at 10 am and had my bags checked after 15 minutes. The delay was caused by a woman that had used her debit card to secure a room, Hilton placed a hold on the checking account in an unspecified amount, the same has happened to me in the past. Always use a credit card when placing a reservation. The area is not lively, short walk to the subway, MSG etc.. The room was small, well furnished, view of Empire State Building, not much of a view with only 28 floors. I was placed on the 28th, I had some special needs and they worked to solve the reservation I had placed. I will most likely choose another Hilton location when reserving in NYC again. Great for a MSG event.

title: “Highly Recommend, would definitely stay again.”
text: The hotel was beautiful inside, the rooms were spacious and the staff was very pleasant and helpful. The restaurants were very good, the bar seating was very comfortable. The Metro is literally across the street. We had no complaints. Everything was wonderful!

title: “Great location; No issues with this property”
text:
Room was clean and comfortable. Very convient to Times Square and good views from the room. 
Fitness Room was very good. Nothing special with the bar and restuarant. You are so close to some great pubs and dining, why deal with the hotel!
Would definitely stay again.

title: “One of my favorites in the city!”
text:
I have stayed in many great hotels in Washington DC and the Fairmont is one of the top on my list. In fact it's my first choice. The rooms are big, luxurious, clean and very well appointed. The washrooms are also large and very nice. The room service (although pricey) is amazing. When I stay here I feel like i'm treating myself to a guilty pleasure.
Great location, a short walk to Georgetown.
I'm surprised it's only 19 on the list as I have stayed at several of the top 5 and comparatively speaking this should be in the top 5.

title: “Simply the best”
text:
Very clean and chic hotel. Got a one-bedroom unit - very spacious and comfortable. The furniture and appliances are new and well maintained. 
The front desk staff is knowledgeable and professional. Was provided a nice information package upon arrival, which had great recommendations for the restaurants in DC.
They also serve full breakfast for free - very nice addition.

title: “Outstanding service and terrific location!”
text: We recently spent the week-end at the Amalfi Hotel for our 27th wedding anniversary. The service was incredible from check-in with Karine through asking for near-by restaurant recommendations. The room was clean and well appointed with robes, slippers, Aveda bath products, and complimentary wi-fi. The bed was very comfortable with nice pillows. We loved the location close to the river and walked to everything we wanted to do including Millennium Park, an architectural boat tour, shopping on Michegan Avenue, Oak Street Beach and the Hancock Building. It was close to night activities too, such as Andy's Jazz Club and the Redhead Piano Bar. The complimentary happy hour was way beyond expectation with wonderful drink choices and wonderful food in a terrific atmosphere. The continental breakfast was perfect for us with coffee, pastries, fresh fruit, cereal choices, and much more. We were planning to stay at a different hotel at a higher price and changed to the Amalfi right before our trip. We are so glad we made this change and will stay again on our next trip to Chicago.

title: “finest and most responsive staff anywhere...”
text: i have been here almost three weeks and am happy to comment that, without exception the staff and service at the resort has been outstanding......the restaurant staff (frank and alberts) in particular has been wonderful....the day manager matt went out of his way to ensure that all was well with myself and all other guests.....the wait staff to include tom and cheryl were excellent....tom may have been the finest, most polite, enthuiastic, attentive yet not overbearing, and knowledgable waiter i have ever experienced (i travel the world extensively)....the food was excellent and the chef scott robuck must be complimented on his efforts and interest in creating a perfect dining experience...chef scott went out of his way to be certain that my food was prepared well and to my liking as he visited my table several times in my stay.......the resort experience was excellent while the restaurant (frank and alberts) and staff, was PERFECT in every aspect......i will return....myles fisher...villa 7128

title: “Nothing Special, but Not Disgusting. Worth the price for the location!”
text:
I was extremely worried about booking this hotel after reading the most recent reviews, but we were satisfied with our stay. The furniture and decor were outdated, but cleanliness is really what mattered for just one night. We found no mold, no stray hairs, and no strange odors anywhere in our room. It was only a few blocks from Beale St for half the price of the other hotels nearby, which can't be beat. The staff was friendly, and check-in and check-out was quick and easy. 
Our only complaint is the elevators, which other reviewers have already touched on. The doors would open before the elevator (on the right, the left one seemed more reliable) came to a complete stop, and it would move up and down with the doors open! My suggestion would be to park on the highest level of the parking garage and take the stairs, if you think the elevator will bother you. 
We enjoyed our one night stay at the Econolodge in downtown Memphis and is a great choice if budget and location are both priorities.

title: “OMG! Be advised on the location.”
text: The location to the city and nearby sights is suitable, if you dont mind driving thru the dirty streets. I was a little intimidated by the location - this hotel is located within the hispanic community/barrios - something the web page neglects to inform travelers of. As a matter of fact, there is a project located right across the street. Upon check-In, the room we were 'given' was okay to the view but the smell was of urine covered up w carpet cleaner or air freshner. If you require security and you're traveling w children I would not recommend this Comfort Inn. I usually enjoy the reasonable pricing and amenities of the Comfort Inns but this is one I will surely gladly pass up on!!

title: “Ideal location”
text:
We stayed at the Hilton Garden Inn in Manhattan last weekend. I agree with many other reviews that accurately state it was ideally located, with a Subway stop right outside the hotel and within walking distance to the Empire State Building and Times Square. The staff were very helpful and the rooms were nicely furnished and clean (although some are smaller than others). We would definitely recommend this hotel if you are visiting Manhattan. We had to speak to the staff about our room and their service was very good and nothing was too much trouble to them.We also found the wifi invaluable. 
There have been some comments on trip advisor regarding the lifts , we waited only a short time for one of the three lifts to arrive to our floor. They do get busy and crowded but it wasn't a problem for us.

title: “I live around the corner. I have put my family members at the Broadway For Years”
text:
I have stayed there on occasion as well. I trust this Hostel for my family and loved ones. 
Since I live in a very small apartment, I need to have a great place for my extended family to stay when they come to visit - it seems there is always someone from my family at the Broadway.
It is very clean, the staff headed by the Manager, Jeremy, are excellent.
I will continue to have my family stay there, in fact as I remodel my apartment, I will be ther too next month.

title: “Not terrible- Parking is expensive though”
text: Came to DC for one night for The Pixies Show. The hotel is about a ten minute walk from the Metro, not too bad at all. The beds were super comfortable, and the front desk staff were pleasant. Its really a good deal for Downtown DC. I read some of the other reviews about the neighborhood and the "residents", we didnt encounter anything like that at all, but then again, its cold, it was a Tuesday night- but also- we didnt walk around like we were expecting someone to assault us. We just went about our business. I would stay here again, if it ever came up.

title: “Great Manhattan digs in TriBeCa -- and Cheap”
text:
I had a lovely stay at the Cosmopolitan in 2001, not many months before 9/11. Its having being so close to the disaster scene (just a few blocks away), I don't know how affected it was by September 11th's events. However, when I stayed there, I thought I'd found a true NYC gem, at great prices. It's located in the heart of TriBeCa, surrounded by great restaurants and nightlife. Looking out my window onto Broadway at night, I had a view of outdoor cafes and trees lit up with sparkly lights, and (sad to say now) another view to the south of the World Trade Center, towering above the hotel, lights ablaze even at midnight.
The hotel has a VERY unassuming exterior, looking more like a nondescript office building circa 1900 -- which it probably was, at one point. But inside, the lobby is clean, well-painted, and with all of its retro charm in place -- gilded elevator doors, old crown moldings cleaned and restored, and a general air of small, cozy comfort. I found the rooms to be the same. Modest, but wholly comfortable. A double bed, a sitting area with two chairs, an armoire and two chests of drawers, and a very clean and roomy bathroom (by NY standards). And all at less than half the price of most other Manhattan hotels. A great neighborhood, a great hotel, a great bargain.

title: “Small rooms, quirky style, great location”
text: The best thing about this hotel is the location, being close to the cable car, street trams, good shopping & decent restaurants. The room & bed was very small, & the bathroom tiny, but all is forgiven because of the convenience of the hotel. Difficult to find a place for a good, healthy breakfast though, & was dissatisfied with the lack of breakfast buffet at the hotel (or any restaurant). As per other USA hotels, no tea making facilities or fridge were available in the room. Laundromat was quite a walk too. Room was noisy, but acceptable. We wouldn't have a problem staying here again, but may investigate other options with larger rooms & onsite buffets first.

title: “The Westin was Fabulous”
text: I just spent 2 nights and 2.5 days in San Antonio having some work done on my car. I decided to stay at The Westin La Cantera since it was close to shopping and had a shuttle to/from the malls that I could utilize. The hotel was great. The rooms were nice and comfy and had most amenities you would want. The food at Brannon's Cafe was fantastic. We did a wine tasting of Texas wines; went to the fire pit to do the s'mores thing but they didn't have it due to rain. When we mentioned no s'mores to the staff in Brannon's at dinner, they brought out a s'mores for each of us. The gym/Spa facility is great. I had the best massage I've ever had by Chris - if you go, you must sign up for his hot stone massage. I will be going back just for that!!! Starbuck's in the lobby too - big plus for me.

title: “Loved it!”
text:
Just returned from a weekend trip to Chicago. I wanted to write and tell other readers I really enjoyed staying at this hotel. I am pretty picky about where I stay, and when I walked in the lobby and hotel room I knew I would like it. The hotel is conviently located near Michigan and Rush street, and a few blocks from Lake Shore drive. We will always stay at this hotel when in Chicago and plan returning every few months. We had a perfect weekend and stay. Tip: Pizzano around the corner is a great "local" place to have pizza and pasta.
Also, Tripadvisor has been great with hotel choices. They haven't been wrong yet. Thank YOU!!!

title: “Great place for a city stay”
text: The location of this hotel is its greatest asset. My adult son and I stayed here for three nights and walked everywhere- to Pikes Market, the Space Needle and everywhere in between. The rooms are small, but clean. The bathroom has very limited shelf space for toiletries, but not a huge problem. The room was quite warm even with the heat off so we propped the window open which made it manageable. Seattle's Best coffee for the in room coffee maker was a nice touch. We parked at the parking garage next door which was $23/ day for guests.

title: “dirty and bad smell”
text: dirty room that was not cleaned for 3 consecutive days during my stay. i you can invest a bit more into your stay in baltimore i would go for other places to stay in. the air conditioning was not working and there was no possibility to open the window...

title: “LOVED IT !”
text: I stayed there at Comfort Inn for 2 weeks.I liked it so much yeah its small but I found everything I needed. The staff was just awesome! all of them were so helpful and friendly. I will defiantly going to stay there If I had a chance to go to New York again. As for it's location its only 2 minuets away from Macy's. It also had a free breakfast every morning there muffins were so good. I just have a little tiny request somebody must tell the dark skin with a brown hair lady standing at the first desk to smile yeah she's helpful and everything but If she had a smile on her face if I asked her anything it would be better.

title: “Well located to Balboa Park Museums and Zoo”
text: Located near Balboa Park in area with a large number of good restaurants. A bit worn but very clean and comfortable. Quiet. Large kitchen and pantry. Great shower. Comfortable beds. Free breakfast certainly ample. Staff were all very cordial and pleasant except for day desk clerk, who was rather curt. A 'thank you' and 'come back again' would have been nice.

title: “Why the fuss?”
text: The reviews were in and they were wrong....My room brought me closer to New York in all the worst ways...no soundproofing so every street noise above a whisper wafted through my window--and the plumbing is so audible that when someone flushed I could not hear the tv, really. I booked the larger room..larger to a Lilliputian. It was almost impossible to take a shower without flooding the bathroom. The service matched the rest of the experience..my phone buzzed so loud I had to cancel a conference call..was told it would be fixed and had to call three times to make that happen asked three times for a mending kit...no taxis On the plus side...the location is good. It is actually in the city.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: A nice propery. A small but deep pool kept the kids busy. The free shuttle service to anywhere within 5 miles was great. If you want to explore the 16th street mall or go to a Rockies game or Bronco's game, this gets you very close. We actually walked back from a Rockies game, though that might be too far for some people. Great Breakfast. The evening meal was adequate but did come with free wine and beer - very nice. Easy access to the highway (just one block to the exit). Highly recommended.

title: “Lucky find!”
text: We needed a room for New Year's Eve. I stumbled upon the RS and was surprised to find that they did indeed have rooms. We ended up with a mini-sweet, which has two double beds and a fold-out sofa - which was perfect for the five of us. The rooms were clean and neat. The rates were reasonable. The staff was courteous, efficient, professional and very accommodating. The beds were comfortable. And there is a quaintness to old hotels like this that adds as much to the stay as anything else -- if you've ever heard a steam radiator softly clanking as it stirs to life, you know what I mean. And when it was all said and done, we could walk outside and be just a few blocks away from Times Square. We were so pleased that we ended up staying three nights in all instead of taking the train back and forth to my brother's place in Connecticut each day. My other brother had a room at the Marriott in Times Square during the NYE festivities. I imagine he paid a lot more to be there, but I would much rather have stayed at the Roger Smith, where there was peace and quiet and at most, a handful of people in the lobby at any one time. I'll be back to NY and when I return, I'll definitely look first at the Roger Smith!

title: “Not bad, not good”
text: The hotel is the closest to the LA convention center. The room are extremely small and the walls are paper thin...all we did was listen to crying kids all night in the room next door! The room was clean and well stocked. Nice decor

title: “GREAT CUSTOMER SERVICE!!!”
text: I have to admit that the beginning of my stay was horrible there was a lot of traffic near my room and room and people kept slamming doors waking me up all through the night. As well as the internet kept kicking me off throughout the eve, The next day I complained and not only did Ashley help me out with the internet but they moved my room to a quieter floor and really took care of me William the manager also really helped turn my stay around and I will stay here again when traveling to NY. Their commitment to customer service is commendable and I felt like they resolved all of my problems with a great attitude, and helped my stay turn from bad to great!!

title: “Great location. Great service. Great hotel.”
text: I booked a room here at the last minute for a little birthday weekend fun. The room was clean and a great size. I also loved the view out our window. The woman who checked us in was polite and helpful. We never made it into the bar because there was a private party going on, but we enjoyed our drinks in the lounge area and felt well taken care of. I love the neighborhood and the easy access to the subway. I will definitely be back!

title: “Perfect vacation !”
text: Stayed at The Hotel Wilshire from June 25th to July 1st with my son-17 years old. Enjoyed every minute of it. Great staff, Miguel, Tatiana and Judith at front desk were all very helpful and friendly. Marcos at The Roof was the best, friendly, professional, thoughtful. I can go on and on. Beautiful, clean and spacious room. Food was delicious. Great location. I greatly recommend it. Will certainly be back if I return to LA.

title: “Good service but should be better.”
text: I'm a royal member of their hotel program so I chose this hotel when traveling to SF. Its a pretty new hotel but the rooms were a little smaller than expected. But, very clean rooms and close to shopping as my wife just walked couple blocks to bloomingdales so she loved the location! But, improvement can be made on service as the door man was busy chatting with his co workers and wasn't doing his job. Front desk was good but maids had no eye contact, no greetings, maybe no english?... Anyways, for lots of money I spent, hotel needs alot more improvement on the service front!

title: “Affordable Upscale in an upscale area”
text: My wife and I spent the weekend here. We were on the 18th floor with an outstanding view facing north. The room was very clean, but there is wear and tear around the carpet and furniture edges.The beds are absolutely fantastic. I can't rate the food because the prices are laughably high. I ate at the mall or a restaurant down the street. My wife was there for a convention, so she had a chance to eat. She found the food very mediocre. The parking situation is a time consuming challenge. You can pay a hefty amount for express parking and valet or park underground and compete for spaces with aggressive visitors to the mall. You can drive in circles for 5 -10 minutes vying for a space. The traffic around the hotel, like the rest of Houston, is thick and constant. Even at midnight. Who are these people?

title: “FANTASTIC”
text: Our first stay in NYC was great and the biggest reason was our stay at Fashion 26. From the very first impression to the outstanding staff and the excellent rates made our stay very enjoyable. Every staff member we came in contact was very professionbal and they all went out of their way to provide information or take care of our needs. We will definately return to Fashion 26 on our subsequent visits to the Big Apple. I highly recommend this hotel. The location was great and again, the rates were fantsatic. The room was big - for NYC hotels - very confortable. I love the bar on the roof with the excellent view of the city.

title: “Surprised”
text: The hotel is hidden but its quiet and safe. I enjoyed my stay and was surprised at the attention from staff. Every staff member you encounter talks to you and the room was very nice for 75 bucks. I had small issues such as water marks on the mirror and needed a couple extra towels but I called down to the front desk and it was very quickly taken care of and apologized for several times. I guess there is a change over in staff and I think its helping. I will definitely stay here again.

title: “Great location, great value, top service”
text:
I stayed one night at this hotel during a business trip. My room was large and the bed was comfortable. The view on the river is great (I was on the 7th floor). 
The hotel is located downtown at walking distance to the historic Philadelphia. 
There is a private parking which is a must in downtown Philadelphia.
The free breakfast was good.

title: “we loved this hotel”
text:
We have returned home from new york today feeling very tired but very happy.
New york was very tiering but luckily we had a lovely hotel to go back to. We couldn't of asked for more from the staff all of them were really friendly and sorted anything out for us straight away.
Nothing was too much trouble.
Coffee was always available and they kept our room spotless for us. We had a lovely view onto central park. We were far enough from the main centre to avoid all the noise. We felt safe in a city we didnt know. Thankyou to all the staff who made it a pleasure
for us.

title: “Nice room, comfy bed”
text: Stayed the night on New Years Eve...enjoyed the room and really thought the bed to be very comfy compared to most hotels. However the front desk didn't seem to have a clue as to what was being offered for the night and being a pet friendly place we wanted the fish bowl in our room and we had to ask for a fish three times. Little pricey but the room and our view was worth it.

title: “Simple without the frills.!!!”
text: My husband and I stayed for 10 days in this hotel at the end of May beginning of June 2009. The room was spacious enough, adequately clean, towels were changed daily and even though we had asked for a room away from the elevators which we didn't get, anyway it didn't bother us too much. we also asked for a fridge to be put in the room which was very useful for drinks etc. The best part about this hotel is its location being in the heart of Times Square. We would go back there again.

title: “Nice green hotel.”
text:
I arrived in San francisco with a sinus infection. I called the hotel to find a local doctors office and they referred me to one who was 4 blks away from hotel. Btw great doctor. We used the Bart system and got off 1 stop 2 early on a one way street and walked 5 blks to doc office. So after doc apt. I called to make sure there would be a room available. She said to me they were sold out the night befor and she would do here best to have a room ready. Well we got there at 2:15 and we were informed that there wasn't a room ready and if we wanted to check in the room that was ready was a "superior king" & it would be 30$ more. I only paid for it cause I felt near death. Basically I felt ripped off when I opened the door to my "superior" room. I didn't have the energy or time to sit and wait for my regular room rate. If you get a good price book it just don't get suckered in to the upgrade. Also wifi never worked. But on the other hand it was a very clean room. Not much wow factor but comfortable. Staff was very helpful and nice, not counting my check inn. Great location and I even made it to our cruise to Alcatraz which was really cool.
All in all it was ok.

title: “Good location. Expensive Parking”
text:
We drove from Vancouver to Seattle to spend a nice weekend in the city and catch the King Tut exhibit at the Seattle Science Center beside the Space Needle. 
The room was very nice - two comfortable double beds for my wife and I plus our two kids. Everything is up to date, clean and modern.
We walked to the Space Needle, Pikes Market, FX McRory's (near the stadiums) so the location is very central.
We paid $140 plus tax per night using the Hotwire site. When I checked the Sheraton website, they claim to guarantee the lowest price but the lowest I could find for the exact same room we were in was $309 per night. Other nearby hotels...lowest price I could find on Expedia/Travelocity was $179 per night.
When we arrived, there's a valet who seemed to be guiding the cars past a weird curb...too bad he walked away because I hit the curb with my aluminum rims....ouch! The parking was VERY expensive....$44 per night plus tax. I found an open lot a two blocks away for $20 for 24 hours. Considering the higher price of a downtown hotel, the parking charges, the more expensive restaurant meals, etc....I would have been much better off (financially) to choose a hotel just outside the city and drive downtown for the day, rather than staying there.
King Tut and brunch on the Space Needle were both great!

title: “Perfect Location - Which is what you're paying for.”
text: This was the perfect location for us to stay for our first time in San Francisco as it was on the touristy side of town. It was just a few blocks from Fisherman's Wharf and a few from Ghirardelli Square. We took a shuttle from the airport and the cost was $15 p/person, however, that meant we didn't have to navigate and drive in the crazy traffic. It was about an hour drive in a shuttle as they drop others off on the way. The beds were comfortable and the room was clean. Bathroom was big and large enough for 3 of us to have all our toiletries in there. They have a wine/appetizer social every evening so you can begin your night nicely. The front desk staff was very helpful and helped us with directions, calling a towncar to make it to the airport, and also was accomodating when we had to change the time last minute due to flight changes. The thing to expect is a higher price; you're paying for the location. It was definitely a good place to stay and a central place to start your sight-seeing, but a bit pricey. If you sleep lightly at all, ask for a room on the interior of the hotel, not with a street view. We had a room with a window on the wharf side of the hotel and the view was not worth the noise you heard early morning hours from the bars closing and also the trash trucks, buses and taxis.

title: “good location”
text: We got this room for a decent price on priceline. The location was great, situated between 5th & 6th streets. The a/c wasn't working properly. They were doing what they could to help but the room was still muggy. Parking is only valet, $25/night. Due to Hurricane Ike, most hotels were full. Had they not been, we would have left because of the air.

title: “Good for families”
text: This hotel seems to attract mainly families with lots of young children, which frankly didn't appeal to us as a young couple. Although we never had to wait for an elevator, the elevators got very crowded quickly, unlike most other hotels we've stayed at. Our room was quiet enough. Breakfast was filling (eggs, potato, cereal, etc.) and looked like the Costco food court, lots of guests chowing down as much as they can. I didn't appreciate having to pay for parking in their enclosed lot. Also, the lobby seemed to be full of smoke despite it being illegal in California to smoke in/near the entrances since 1995. I wouldn't recommend this hotel to friends, but the breakfast is definitely a good value for families.

title: “Great if going to National's game”
text: Stayed here to see a National's game with my family. Perfect location. Only a couple of blocks from the park. My family and I felt very safe and had no trouble with feeling unsafe on our walk back at night. Very nice rooms. I loved the firm matress and pillows becasue often they are both too lumpy. Staff very nice as well. When going to a game, choose this hotel.

title: “Clean hotel”
text: We stayed here with 4 teenage girls. most of the hotel staff was friendly. The morning gal needs to smile. The evening staff was very friendly and helpful. Our rooms were roomy, comfy and clean. The hotel is located with in walking distance to the T. There is a Target behind the hotel which was very convenient. You can get to downtown on the T in 15 min. We went to a Red Sox game and took the T. It takes about 30 min from hotel to park. not too bad. The pool room was very hot! made it uncomfortable for us watching the girls swim. they had a little lounge area with a small bar, pool table and sitting area.

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
We reserved at The Blue Moon knowing little about it -- and what a wonderful surprise we got! The hotel was adorable, immaculate and warm. The staff was first rate and friendly, and our room was perfect.
We heartily recommend The Blue Moon for anyone and everyone looking for a charming European style hotel experience in a hip, up & coming New York neighborhood.

title: “Beautiful and Charming!”
text: Gorgeous building, terrific staff and wonderfully comfortable beds (with lots of huge pillows)! The ambiance is sophisticated and tranquil. Anytime we chatted with staff they were absolutely helpful, polite and genuinely friendly (in Spanish AND English). Our stay involved a large group of friends and we were all accommodated superbly. Upon (early) check-in, we were even offered an upgrade on our room for a minimal fee to a huge suite we loved! Also, the location is very accessible. Our stay was fantastic and we definitely want to return to The Sorrento in Seattle soon.

title: “Very nice pool”
text: The room are kind of small with crt tv, didn't know they still exist. The decor are very outdated, bathroom are okay but could be better. Location are okay but kind of noisy right next to the stadium and railroad track.

title: “Great Location”
text:
This place more than met our expectations. Clean , well decorated rooms, and such a great location and of course the price couldn't be beat. We were at the back of the hotel so there was no street noise, the beds were very comfortable .
The staff was very helpful, check-in and out was easy. Did have a lunch there and it was fine.
Above all the location is so handy for walking and the cable car is outside the door. This can't be beat.

title: “Best park & cruise in Jacksonville”
text:
Very friendly and helpfull employees to make your stay grear.
Great breakfast in the hotel and many resturants near by.
Great location with a Walmart close by.
Park and cruise service was excellent both times we stayed.

title: “Nice hotel but ask for a room that is not on the side of the airstrip...”
text:
Rooms are comfortable, very clean, they have all amenities. Check-in is very fast and staff is great. There is a small shop next to check-in where you can get soem water and food, excellent. 
The next morning we had breakfast in the lobby which offers a buffet with a lot of choice and next to that they can cook your breakfast to anything you like. Great breakfast service and very good food.
There is only one but to the hotel, you should ask for a room that is not located on the side of the airstrip. The first plane comes in at 06.00 am. We arrived in the middle of the night and I really could have slept another couple of hours, but when it was landed I was right awake and looking out of the window where the noise was coming from you can almost look into the plane so close is the strip from some of the hotelrooms.
Next to that it has a great shuttlebus from and to the airport that runs late and starts early. Parking is also available with enough places. 
If you ask for the right room this is a great hotel !

title: “GREAT LOCATION”
text: The Westin is located in the heart of the shopping district and within walking distance of wonderful restaurants. The rooms are very comfortable (especially the Heavenly Bed) and the service of the staff is great. I stayed at the hotel for about 2 months (during the week) and always stay there when in Seattle.

title: “Yet Another Nice Stay at the W SD”
text:
Reserved a Wonderful Room at the W San Diego for a 3 nights stay. Before arrival, saw that I'd been upgraded to a Cool Corner Room (on account of SPG status). This was a welcome upgrade as I'd stayed in a Wonderful Room before and they are, to say the least, quite cramped. Cool Corner Rooms are a great deal more spacious - both the room itself and the bathroom (which has ample counter/sink space, a large soaking tub and a large walk-in shower, Bliss bath products that they restocked daily). I did arrive a couple of hours early and so my room wasn't ready. They did offer a Wonderful Room that was available but I chose to wait an hour or so for the Cool Corner to be ready. Lobby isn't a bad place to sit back and chill and wait.
The lobby was being remodeled and so the entrance in to the property had been moved over a bit on B Street. Some signs of the remodel around (curtained-off areas, different layout) but they've done a fairly good job of making it as subtle as possible and even possibly undetectable to someone not already familiar with the property. Bit of a bonus, IMHO, to the remodel is that the lobby bar wasn't around. Returning to your hotel to a packed, club-like atmosphere in the lobby with a bunch of hipsters boozing it up all loud and rowdy can get quite old, especially when you're in town on business. And so I liked returning to and leaving from a quieter, more subdued lobby. 
As for the Cool Corner Rooms (beyond the bathroom), there is a well-stocked minibar, LCD TV with a decent channel selection and quite the expansive PPV selection, good workspace/desk, DVD player, iPod docking station (which also comes in handy for charging your iPhone!), a lounger and ottoman, and very comfy bed with pillows I can't help but want to steal everytime I stay at a W. I do wish the chair at the desk was more comfy than stylish as the lack of wireless in the room (though there is wired high speed internet for about $13/day) confines you to the desk when working and the chair gets old fast. There is plenty of space to spread out and let all your stuff spread out, as well (a few more drawers would help, though, as I like to unpack everything when I check in to a room rather than live out of my suitcase. There are a number of drawers around, but spread out and in the nightstands or bottom of the closet, rather than a single, well-placed dresser).
Valet service was decently prompt when I'd call down ahead of time to have my car brought up (though one time, the call didn't do much good and I had to remind the valet once downstairs). Room service was prompt and tasty. Maid service was good, as well. Very helpful staff, from check-in to check-out and at all times in between.
I guess I'm old at heart because, though well within the W's target age demographic, I like my hotel to be relaxed and chill rather than rowdy and crazy. W's are known for lively bar scenes in the lobby and I usually just put up with that because I'm fond of the other aspects of the hotels. So this trip was particularly nice for me on account of the lack of the lobby bar due to the remodel. Though there is still the bar on the 2nd floor and you can expect, if getting in to the elevator at night, to have to put up with a few seconds of drunk and annoying people sharing the elevator with you as they go to and from the bar. Can't win em all :)
All in all, though, a nice property and very convenient to airport and good parts of town (though this can be said for most places in SD proper). I appreciate the fact that, though the staff certainly leans towards being young and hip, I've always had good, friendly and professional service here (as opposed to some similar hotels where the staff is more pretty than professional and more cool than competent).

title: “By Far The Most Convenient, Relaxed, Unique, and Fun Beach--Side, Beautiful View Hotel In The Ocean Beach Area, A Thoroughly Awe”
text: My Boyfriend and I stay here every time we are in the area( we both used to live in the area also) and we always have such a great time. The rooms are small (it is a small building) but are clean and well-equipped. We always try to get one of the third floor rooms that face the beach, most rooms have French Doors or Balconies, which means smokers can do their thing without any problems. I am actually writing this from Room 320 right now, looking down at the OB Pier. The hotel is on the corner of the street that runs alongside Ocean Beach and Newport, the "main drag" of OB, where much of the local action is. Ocean Beach is a very liberal, creative kind of town, and very different from any other beach area in SoCal. The Ocean Beach Hotel and it's friendly staff is a must-stay for us, everything is within walking distance, I would recommend it to anyone who really wants to get the most out of visiting OB.

title: “The Best”
text: My wife and I were able to go on a trip to celebrate our anniversary. We wanted something that was unique and my wife found The Joule. We were looking for something that combined elegance, art, and architecture. We found that to be true. I cant say enough about The Joule. I have read some of the reviews that spoke of bad service. I cant say enough about the service. They were excellent. They seemed eager to work and acted like they truly enjoyed their job. We went to the Rangers game and when we came back to the hotel, there was a complimentary bottle of champagne and two glasses for our anniversary. We were disappointed about the hours of the Charlie Palmer and the bar downstairs but found an outstanding place to get a drink directly across the street. In closing, we will be back. I look forward to going back to Dallas just to stay at The Joule

title: “Week Long trip to NYC”
text: Clean room. The staff is friendly. Overall the hotel is expensive so bring your money. The breakfast buffet is very good. I will come back. I did not try the resturant but I bet it is just as good as the breakfast

title: “historic building!”
text:
Just returned from my 5-night stay at Radisson Martinique in New York. The hotel is on 32nd street (Korea way) near metro station and lots of commercial business. The front desk staff was very kind and helpful, the room on 14th floor was clean and large enough for two people. No frills. No mini-bar. Silent. Good shower.
The building is marvelous with mosaic floor , marble stairs and walls...
Internet free for guests at the business center.
Inconvinience? The hotel propably has agreements with air companies and the hall entrance is 24 hours packed with flight attendents, pilots, co-pilots and suitcases and more suitcases!!!!! Quite often , a huge bus is parked in front of the hotel, picking up or dropping off the air company staff,which makes geting in or getting off the hotel quite complicate! It rained the two last days I was there and to get a cab I had to walk away from the hotel entrance under the rain as there was always a bus on my way!
If like being in a crowded area, lots of cars, lights etc... this is your place!

title: “Avoid at all costs, and i am serious about this”
text:
We had a reservation at "The Penn" for a "Superior with 2-Double Beds", for 2 guests for 3 nights. Total costs would have been USD 873.44. This after a recommendation, and checking out the internet site where this room is perfectly presented thru pics.
After one of those rather long haul delay arrival experiences one can have at JFK, we were looking foreward to our stay. At entrance we had to line up and wait about 45 min. (!!) till we were served. The staff was okay, but sadly not friendly. The lobby is huge and looks realy great for an entrance, they obvious put alot of efforts to keep this part of the hotel clean and shiny. 
Then...we entered our room at the third floor. The corridors to the rooms are poorly lighted/ dark, the corridors carpets show vissable stains, it looked more like entering a floor wich actualy has been closed for the last 5 years, left alone due a allergy to any kind of cleaning. The roomdoor is the original one from the once oh so luxury past of this hotel (bck to 1919!), but looks more like entering a prison in the modern world. Then we entered the room, I have been travelling thru Africa, and other third world countries, where you know you sometimes have to accept low luxury standards. But this room looked even worse......
Lets start with a more deeper view: The sheets in the beds showed visable stains, and i am not sure if they were realy fresh...their smell did not even came close to soap. The carpet in the room looked like it had a maximum 1,5 minute turbo cleaning leaving 60% of all dirt very visiable behind. This is the first time i actualy felt very uncomfortable, better said dirty, walking barefeet on a hotel carpet. (and no...i am not a hygienic-weenie)
The room had no romance at all, dirt und dust was visable on lights, chair and in the bathroom (second hand hair smiling at you from the walls after "some kind of cleaning" had taken place....)
The windows were dirty, on the inside, the "museum-suspect-looking airconditioning system" was dirty. The curtains had visable stains, and looked somehow not cared for. On the wall was one painting only with again visable pieces off. This room looked like abandoned, and had no friendly welcome aura in the most minimum way. 
A small fridge was "parked" somewhere in a corner, the television showed cleaning stripes like you see them when you clean your television with a wet towel after 10 years of dusteating...to be short....it looked like we entered a room for the homeless (with all respect for these ppl) who cannot afford anything more then a bed and a once a year cleaning. 
Noise....came from the neighbours till 3 am. The walls are like paper. A few loud fist drums from our side on the "paper-walls" finaly brought some silence
We left this hotel after one night and found a better place two streets away at the Wingate hotel, and that even for half the money! (tip!!)
If the Penn realy is so good as they try to present themselfs in the internet, they failed 100% to do so with our reservation. If all rooms look like ours did (wich i do not hope so) this hotel should be closed down on instant.

title: “1st class - a true Detroit gem!”
text: We stayed at the Inn for while in town for a performance of Riverdance at the Fox Theater. We almost felt like our stay at the "Inn" was an event in itself! The staff is excellent, and go out of their way to make you feel at home. If you have any questions concerning the area, or about the history of Detroit, be sure to ask Steve (bellman / shuttle driver) - he is a walking encyclopedia, and is more than happy to pass on his knowledge of both the Inn & the city. My wife & I grew up in Detroit, but didn't know this place existed until we stayed there last weekend - it won' be our last stay!!! Everything the other reviewers have posted here is true - a first class operation - you will not be disappointed!!

title: “Close to LAX Los Angeles Airport”
text: This is a great hotel to stay at before your flight or if you have just arrived, they have a free shuttle service to and from the airport. Staff are very friendly and efficient. Their is a great restaurant and lounge bar onsite, the restaurant has a very relaxing atmosphere with a good menu. There is a pool at the hotel for a swim or to simple relax around. We stayed on the 12th floor with fantastic views to the airport especially if you are a plane spotter, the room was spacious, clean and relaxing I would recommend this hotel to anyone, we had no problems what so ever. The beds were very comfy which is hard to find nowadays and rooms sound proof from airport noise.

title: “Definitely not the greatest”
text: This place appears great on the surface, but if you're a clean freak or just even picky, you might not be happy. After thinking that our room seemed "ok" (definitely decorated in the late 70's?!) I discovered that the shower had cracks in the tiles and was peeling, and it was very difficult to turn the water on for myself and my children. Also, after trying to kill one of the bugs flying around in the room, I ended up swatting the lampshade and a huge pile of dust flew off. After that experience we looked a little bit harder at the room and even found a gigantic spiderweb up on the ceiling near the curtains. Totally gross. Room service pizza was disgusting - about an inch of grease sitting atop the pepperoni - we had to take tons of Kleenex and sop it all up before we could even try it and that still didn't help. Then the $9 pizza turned into over $16 somehow on the final bill. The day we wanted to go to Universal we got there 15 minutes earlier than they said the first shuttle would run over there and there was already a shuttle full of people on and leaving. We were not allowed on and were told to wait. The $9 they charge per night for parking is actually $10 after they add the tax plus some entertainment tax of one kind or another. My kids liked it (of course - they're kids and not paying), but believe me....you can do better!!

title: “on the circle”
text: We stayed here for a Jackson Browne concert the front desk helped us pick a bar close to the murant theater and they helped out with all our side trips with great advice . Rooms were clean and beds were really comfortable. Would return again the Hotel is just off of the Indy circle in the heart of downtown Indy. Great stay thanks to all.

title: “weekend soccer tournament”
text: i had booked this hotel because price was right...and also in sd for a soccer tournament so i needed a room that i can make breakfast in a hurry... with that said i booked a kitchenette room which was 200.64 for fri-sun. but i thought the kitchen part of room can be better it was only 2 little electric burners with a smoke alarm too close so for any reason your food has a lot of smoke there goes the alarm. i think they should move smoke alarm a bit farther... u do have a micro and fridge in room... overall it was ok for us just to cook and sleep you can hear people on top alot with showers the parking is small and tight for trucks

title: “Pricey but worth it”
text:
Price –definitely high, but it's because of the location and great condition of the hotel. You can ‎find more affordable ones further from downtown. If you want to treat yourselves – this ‎hotel is a good choice.‎
Location – Wonderful, lovely neighborhood. You can have a nice walk to downtown or walk ‎shortly to the subway station (green or orange line). There are restaurants and pubs nearby. ‎We walked to a theater to see a show.‎
Rooms – Fab. Large, clean, modern, lots of space in drawers, the bed is comfy, we had an amazing view ‎‎(on floor 22). You get good quality soap and even a hand moisturizer. The only negatives are ‎very insignificant: the toilet flushes in a really strong current so it's loud like the ones in ‎airplanes…. and the shower stream could be stronger, but really it's fine the way it is.‎
Facilities – We used the pool and Gym. They were great because before 10am they're practically ‎empty. The pool is small (standard hotel size) but sufficient and comfortable for swimming if ‎only you and one or two others use it. Same goes for the gym.‎
Overall we enjoyed this hotel so much it was totally worth the money.‎

title: “This is a Great Hotel”
text: In a city of fine hotels, this hotel stands out in my opinion. It is centrally located and provides easy access to everything in NY. The hotel itself has great amenities starting with the free continental breakfast and ending with the complimentary wine and cheese in the evening. The rooms are exceptional and the staff is always courteous and gracious. The room decor is high quality and they try to make your stay as comfortable as possible. I highly recommend this hotel.

title: “good choice and location..get a room in front”
text: This was my first stay at the Residence Inn though I have many friends stay here while the kids were at soccer tournaments. Great for families because of the big breakfast, convenient to a move theater and dining, and pool and basketball court make good hang out areas. My room and the hotel was clean and updated overall. I didn't get the creeps at all in the kitchen or bath, though I did point out to the staff that they could use a few repairs in the bathroom. The fact that this is a great location, just a minute from the highway made it easy to understand why Mariott would choose to put a chain hotel here. However, the hotel sits right by a railroad track and at least 4 trains went through from 11am to 6am. It isn't the train noise so much that wakes you, but the hotel must be located near a street crossing, because the darn engineers blow the horn, alot. I recommend asking for a room in front, perhaps it is better. This was the only negative I could see of this hotel.

title: “GREAT HOTE, GREAT ROOM, GREAT CUSTOMER SERVICE”
text: We loved it, we walked in because we canceled our other hotel at the last min. and they got us in within 5 mins. And it was wonderful. Nice pool great breakfast great customer service,. We stayed here for 3 nights and the bed was wonderful. We are staying here again in a couple of months. Loved it

title: “Terrific”
text: Just like being at home. Supplies everything you need, free hot breakfast, large suites with kitchenette, all appliances, even dishwasher and garbarge disposal, dishes, pots. Very friendly and helpful staff. Also stayed at Staybridge in San Antonio. Now when I travel I look for Staybridge. Would recommend to everyone. Check out their site.

title: “Perfect”
text:
Perfect for what we needed- not visiting the city for long GREAT location and perfect size. Bit small but to be expected in the city. VERY helpful staff and VERY clean room. Overall very happy with this hotel. It appeared very busy but all staff were helpful from check in to check out. 
Thanks

title: “Terrible”
text:
I stay at hotels at a lot. Often once a week, definitely multiple times a month. This was the worst hotel I've ever stayed at. I had to change rooms 4 times due to the awful stale/musty/cigarette smoke smell including at 1am when I was awaken from a dead sleep with a pounding headache from the stench. 
The staff could have cared less. They went through the motions only because they had to. The staff walked around with dirty, stained and untucked shirts. What a brutal dissaspointment.

title: “Best hotel stay I've had in ages”
text: JJ, Elizabeth, and Nicholas are the bomb. Best hotel staff I've ever had to deal with, and never short for award winning suggestions on where to eat. Went to Charlotte for business and stayed in a suite room. It was clean, spacious and comfortable with a decent view.

title: “Best kept secret at Hobby”
text: This is a wonderful, recently renovated Days Inn owned by a very nice family. What a big surprise to see such nice, new, clean appointments in my room with all the comforts of home including a CD player at a Days Inn. Clean and comfy with a great interior feel. The only thing that I would change is a better quality towel but then this isn't the Ritz Carlton. Breakfast is OK with several choices but not important to me. Also, really like that they save the recent additions of the USA Today so I can catch up on reading and puzzles. My husband is a hotel snob and was very impressed by the place. No elevator for those that need it. Great value for the $$,

title: “Very good location and facilities but hotel lacking charisma and attention to detail”
text:
This is my third stay at the Nikko hotel in San Francisco in the past 10 years and I can say that the hotel still delivers a great location, unobstrusive service and very good hospitality in general.
The affluence of asian visitors to the hotel is notable and so is the hotel's Japanese heritage. In everything from the hotel's restaurant (ANZU) and the room furnishings, you can sense the Japanese quality flair.
The hotel, however, has not greatly evolved and under new management changes recently, probably should refresh very soon. Some details tell the age and lack of attention to detail quite dramatically, such as the torn (and sewn) drapers, the 1980's sound system and closet doors, for example.
The experience sums up as positive in great part due to the prime location, a few steps away from Union Square, Market St and many other relevant places in town.
This is the kind of hotel where service goes unnoticed and happens behind the scenes. You almost never bump into service people, however, service is conducted impeccably.
The quality of the food is very good, but probably not the best Japanese/Asian that one can find in San Francisco, and of course that will always be a challenge in a city with so much Asian influence and so many gourmet alternatives.
The hotel's fitness center and pool are a highlight and very good to excellent.
The lobby lacks charisma and sense of belonging. It transmits the ethos of an empty office lobby or train station, not much to see, do or enjoy. It could have a vibrant bar scene if it wanted, but for some reason it is kept eerily empty.

title: “Surprisingly good!”
text: Due to an unpleasant experience in the Monarch Hotel, we decided to check out and find another place. We passed by Motel 6 and they have a reasonable price of $150 per night for 2 double beds. The staff is friendly and even upgraded us to 2 big king size room for FREE as their 2 double beds is full. The room is clean and big. Nothing to complain with this price and good service.

title: “Amazing Weekend! Would do it again in a heartbeat!”
text: My friend and our daughters took some time over February break to go to Boston. We found a package thru the Aquarium and booked at the Hilton. It was right in the middle of everything. The kids got backpacks from the front desk filled with goodies, we got a complementary upgrade on our room, and the package included an in-room movie with roomservice delivering popcorn and soda. The package also came with 4 tickets to the Aquarium and 4 tickets to the Children's museum. The kids were amazed, my friend was blown away by the quality of the Hilton, and I was really really happy with the entire weekend. We can't wait till next February!

title: “Great hotel for a conference with outstanding customer service”
text: Stayed 2 nights here for a work conference. The conference room itself was fairly standard, however the staff made the experience well-beyond standard. The sales and event manager, AV director, catering director and server were extremely helpful, friendly and attentive to our every need. I would definitely use their services again for work events!

title: “Great Location Crappy place”
text: If you want to be in Times Square for under $140 then go for it but if you want a nice or decent place this is NOT it. No smoke alarms or AC in any unit

title: “A great find in NYC”
text: I stayed at On the Ave with my two daughters in early June. We booked the hotel based on a referral from a close friend and recommendations we had seen here. We reserved the suite with two queen beds and a small sitting area off to the side, with a door closure. We were prepared for construction (the reviews all advised of this), and also asked for a room on a higher floor to avoid the street noise (fire station across the street and early morning construction crews). Unfortunately the first night was a major disappointment. We were given a room with two queen beds, but no sitting area. It was on a low floor, and very loud. They moved us that night, but the room wasn't any better. It was in a corner with brick walls out the windows. Fortunately the next day we were moved to a very nice room - the one we had originally expected and reserved. The rest of our stay was very pleasant. The bellhops were awesome - so friendly - always remembered our names. All the hotel staff were really great. Beds were comfy and the room was spacious. We were able to get a portion of the first night's charge credited to our account, which helped to right the wrong. All in all, this is a really nice hotel in a terrific location. I look forward to staying there another time, when there isn't construction...

title: “The Good & The Bad”
text:
First the good. Great location. Just around the corner from the Verizon Center and within walking distance to great restaurants and museums. Kimpton Hotels have a "cool vibe" and Hotel Monaco DC does not disappoint. Standard hosted wine hour, morning paper and fully stocked mini-bar. The bed was horrible. It definitely flight like an old mattress. This must be unique to Hotel Monaco DC because I stayed in Chicago a few weeks prior and the bed was great. 
Overall service was good, but the morning housekeeping crew was very, very jovial and while they might be a blast to have a drink with it was way too loud in the morning. I also forgot to put the DND sign on the door knob and the crew knocked and opened my door as early as 8am, which I thought was a bit rushed and early for a room that was reserved for several days. Wireless was down for 24 hours or so, which was frustrating as a business traveler, but I assume the hotel was doing what it could to solve the problem as quickly as possible. Even with these issues Kimpton Hotels will still be my first choice because the pros have always outweighed the cons.

title: “I JUST LOVE THIS HOTEL”
text:
This is my choice for a NYC hotel. Location is great and the rooms are comfortable. What sets this hotel apart is the staff. They are just amazing. I don't get treated this well at a Four Seasons. I am a HH Gold, so maybe that helps, but they really seem to like people. 
Only minor thing is room service. It comes from Mustang Sally's and really isn't that good. But this is NYC, there are probably 100 places to eat within two blocks of the hotel.
I will be back!

title: “Pleasantly Surprised”
text:
After reading a few previous reviews of this hotel/resort, we were hesitant to follow through with our plans there June 9th-10th.
However, we are now glad we followed through as our stay was a pleasant one.
Fort Rapids is conveniently located just of I-70 near the I-270 beltway. You can see the building from the freeway. However, access from Hamilton Ave. was not marked and was a guessing game the first time in. Once there, we were impressed with the imaculate landscaping on the exterior grounds. We arrived around the 4PM check-in (a 2PM check-in was available with Holiday Inn club membership). There was no waiting and we were immediately checked in by a very courteous staff.
The interior of the resort was decorated appropriately in a western theme. Our room (Cisco the Kid) included a King bed and a set of bunks enclosed in a "fort". The room was clean and everything worked as expected. This was important as we traveled with two 12 year olds and a 10 month old baby.
The bunks included a plasma tv that the 12's loved. One of the three elevators at the tower was out of order but there was never a long wait for the other two. 
The waterpark itself was very nice with plenty to do for everyone.
There were plenty of other amenities on the property as well as a nice restaruant, bar and gift shop.
There is an abundance of restaurants on Hamilton Ave. just a block away from the resort. There is a mall and stores just a short distance to the south. In conclusion, our stay was pleasant and above expectations. Almost Disneylike. I'm assuming most of the problems experienced by other reviewers here happened when the hotel was at or near capacity and the staff was taxed. The resort was busy but not crowded during our stay on a weekend in June.
Hope everyone's stay is as good as ours.

title: “Trip to see daughter in play”
text:
This is our second time at the London. After our first trip in 2007 we swore we would never come back; but we get so many emails from them we thought we would give them a second chance. My mistake. Compared to two years ago the staff upon arrival is still distant and rude. Yet the Ritz knew my name etc. Not here.
Lacks warnth. Mistakes with food and beverage. Overall no better than last time we won't be back.
Dr Upton 1511

title: “Lovely property in downtown Memphis”
text: We met my sister and her husband in Memphis, because it is about 1/2way between our homes. We booked in advance and got a very good rate. The online reservation system really came through, and were able to accommodate our specific room requests. The front desk, manned by Felicia on one day, and by Lois on the other two, was delightful. Both were so very friendly and helpful. The room was classy and comfortable, and very quiet for being on the "courtyard" side of the hotel. The "Bistro" serves killer soups and sandwiches. Loved the loaded baked potato soup. Thumbs up!

title: “It's a great hotel!”
text:
This is our 6th year staying at OTA. We come down twice a year. The staff is always courteous and professional. The rooms are clean and nicely appointed. We have never had a bad experience. Sunday morning, we checked out and Atira and Dennis of Security were very helpful and pleasant. We are looking forward to our September visit. 
THE ROOMS A

title: “Excellent Experience”
text: Fantastic location, beautiful hotel. Service was great. Booked thru hotwire - 2 adults and 1 child - we ended up needing a bigger room (2 beds instead of one) it was no problem, and they waived the additional cost. Very contemporary, beautiful property. Yes, the room was painted a steel gray color, but it was not gloomy - very sleek and stylish, well appointed and laid out. Great city and/or river views from all sides of this hotel, situated right on Michigan Ave. An ideal location, close to everything. 24 hour room service with an extensive menu. There is a beautiful bar in the lobby (where guests get a free appetizer). We dined at the China Grill, located just South of the hotel, with access through the hotel just past the elevators. Gorgeous restaurant and bar, with the same high level of service as the hotel, and the food was fantastic. My son absolutely loved the whole experience - can't wait to stay here again! Don't hesitate to stay here for business or leisure..a sure bet.

title: “Best hotel in Hollywood!”
text: We stayed one night here in a suite and it was amazing! The room was big considering we have a 15 month old baby. Plenty of room for him to run around. Great views from the 14th floor. The pool was great temperature considering the weather was cold. Close to Universal City Walk and Universal Studios which we walked to both days. This is our second time here, and we will always continue to come back here each time we are in the area. The managers and staff are very helpful and always there to assist. Thank you again Sheraton for making our stay again memorable.

title: “Fabulous Trip”
text: We spent 4 nights at the Renaissance as a "three generations girls trip" -- Grandmother, mother and daughter. We had a tremendous time at the hotel. Great location with the Grayline bus stopping just outside the door, the subway within the same block, the TKTS booth 1/2 block away, and lots of Broadway shows & restaurants within easy walking distance. The staff members were friendly and helpful. The rooms were much larger than expected for NYC and were comfortable. We stayed on the 16th floor and still could hear some noise from the street but it did not disturb our sleep. Overall, a great place -- We would stay here again and recommend it.

title: “Quality”
text:
So much has already been said about this hotel and it is nearly all correct. The staff are superb, from Nina Sweet and all those on the front desk to the doormen, especially Brendan who was always cheerful and helpful whatever the weather.
I could go on and on about the wonderful style of the hotel, the sheer quality of all who work there, the excellent positioning, the high quality bathroom and products, but these have all been said before.
If you are thinking about a hotel in Boston, book this one. You will not be disappointed.

title: “Wonderful big hotel”
text: The Monaco is a very well run, wonderfully decorated Hotel in the center of SF. It is big and therefore a bit impersonal, but it has all amenities and the rooms are in an excellent condition. It is a bit pricey but worth the money if you can afford it.

title: “Great hotel - cold showers”
text:
The Tuscan inn is in many ways a perfect stay for an SF-holiday. You are at Fisherman's Wharf - a block from the excursion buses, walking distance to the piers etc. Plus the hotel restaurant is more than a hotel restaurant, it is a very good one - hotel or not. Rooms are good, cleaning was excellent .The hotel also has a special treat. At five every afternoon the let you taste local wines in the lobby. Which also means you get to chat with other guests, share experiences etc. You also get free coffee in the mornings. 
The downside was a very unsecured supply of hot water. More than one I had to take a cold shower - not very nice in November.

title: “Disappointing”
text: Stayed three nights here at the end of June. I was expecting far more, given the numerous positive reviews on this site. My main complaint concerns cleanliness: the sheets and blankets had several stains, and the carpet had lots of pet hair, as if nobody had vacuumed. The halls reeked of cooking food (and not in a good way). Management was friendly, and the internet worked very well. But unless you're staying for an extended period of time (when, presumably, you would be bringing your own toiletries) it's a bit annoying to come for a short trip and have to supply your own bath products and have no housekeeping (especially when the room could have used cleaning).

title: “Great spot, excellent customer service”
text: Jayson at the front desk is awesome! I showed up with all my luggage after walking from another not-to-be mentioned hotel. I was exhausted and frustrated that the other hotel (where I'd had reservations for 3 weeks) had given me the wrong room. Jayson let me check out the room at Vagabond while I left my ID at the front desk to make sure it was acceptable before I booked it. It was VERY nice, especially for the price and location-- new granite counters, nice big TV, and most important, it was CLEAN. Plus, a CLEAN fridge and CLEAN microwave. Great place for a great price! And they should give Jayson a raise-- he's wonderful with customers (and I seriously looked like I'd been dragged off the streets when I walked in, but you'd never know it-- I still got the best possible treatment). Customer service is extremely hard work (I know, I used to work in hospitality), and he does it very well. Also, free breakfast, and I only paid about $15 more a night than the not-to-be mentioned place.

title: “Great Value & Location, Charming Hotel”
text:
I was a little hesitant to stay here, given the mixed reviews. I have stayed at the Lowes & Sofietel in Philly, & liked the Radisson Warwick the best. The location is prime, within walking distance to many great shops and resturaunts. The building itself is older, and seems to have been renovated relatively recently. The rooms were clean and the beds comfortable, and the menus for both the resturaunt and room service were outstanding and the prices reasonable.
Dont be afraid to try this hotel - you will be pleasantly suprised!

title: “ok, but was not what I expected”
text: I don´t normally stay at Le Meridien hotels but my company booked me here by accident. First, I was disappointed at the lack of bell service upon arrival at the hotel. I´d just arrived from Madrid so was tired and did not feel like lugging my own luggage which is what happened. The reception staff were friendly and prompt, and the concierge was really helpful in giving me some tips. The room was a disappointment. So I am used to being an SPG and a Marriott platinum member so usually get upgrades, but even basic rooms at these hotels were better than this. It just didn´t cut it. Overall the stay was ok. However all my subsequent San Francisco stays are now at the Westin St Francis which is the standard I expect, but admittedly much more expensive.

title: “Perfect location and helpful, attentive staff.”
text:
Located smack bang in the centre of downtown San Diego this hotel is perfect for a 4-5 day city explore - which is what we did. If you're travelling by car it's extremely easily accessed from the main highways into (and out of) San Diego - but beware the valet parking cost is $32 per day.
We paid extra for a corner room with a city view and the additional space was well worth the money. We slept well - bed was really comfortable and the road noise was surprisingly low for a city centre location.
