All the staff were very polite and attentive and weren't sniffing for tips. We did tip a few but never felt under any obligation to do so. Special mention must go to the Concierge service - in particular Mark and Lee Ann - who provided assistance above and beyond the call of duty. We will certainly return to a beautiful city and I'd be surprised if we don't stay here when we do.
Only minor qualm was the lack of an integral Spa, however preferential rates are available at one 4 blocks away which I can highly recommend.

title: “A bit quirky but admirably efficient for a business meeting”
text: This place is a bit odd on first arrival, a conglomeration of buildings varying from rose garden cottages to 1960s style high rise in concrete. Rooms could use some major updates. However, numerous swimming pools and a convention center onsite make it a great destination for conferences and families. While it doesn't exude the atmosphere of a luxury resort it is difficult to fault anything specific and it certainly serves its purpose well.

title: “Not for business travelers”
text:
Staff was unfriendly and not flexible with reservations. Had to postpone my trip to Houston because the city was being evacuated for Hurricane Ike. I was still charged for cancelling my room. Unbelievable. 
Great location, but so are a bunch of other hotels for business travelers.

title: “family friendly”
text:
My 7 and 8 year old granddaughters and I stayed at Squaw Peak last weekend. It is a great hotel for kids and their grandparents as well! The staff is friendly and attentive and the hotel is well maintained. It is very beautiful, with many pools. The water slide and lazy river were great fun. 
All of the restaurants have kids' menus and the food is fine. The only complaint I have is that none of their restaurants was able to serve HOT food - it was always lukewarm. This remark is only being made because we ate at their restaurants for three days and they never got that right. My only other comment is they need to buy new towels. This may sound petty, but I hate dingy, thin towels. 
I would definitely return to this hotel. It was truly a pleasure staying there.

title: “Novotel, fantastic location, perfect”
text:
Hi, like many others I use tripadviser before I book hotels, however being to New York on many occasions I was disappointed to read some of the negative comments about the Novotel. We picked this hotel for its location and it certainly didn’t disappoint.
We arrived at approx 2pm and went straight to check in, we were told that check in was after 3pm however there was a room available and we were given our keys immediately. Our room was on the 10th floor which is only 3 floors up from reception, which has a wonderful observation deck of Times Square, however due to the worst snow fall in 5 years it wasn’t safe to go out on to it, pity. The bar opens until midnight and has 2 large TV screens showing mostly sport, our barman was a big Manchester United fan and he had the English premier league highlights show on. The bar is expensive a glass of beer (not a pint) and a whisky was $24; the rate was $1.40 so that was about £16.
There were comments about the lifts being slow, but that was not the case, also someone mentioned building works going on, well on arrival as we went to our room, 1016, I noticed that the room at the end of the corridor, some three doors away from ours was under some sort of construction. During my five days in the hotel I only saw the workers once and didn’t here a sound from the construction work.
We had a double double room with a fantastic view of Times Square, there was plenty of room and spotless. Our maid always had a smile, as there were three of us in the room, so we were short of towels, however our maid noticed this and supplied more without us even having to ask.
Breakfast we gave a miss as it was mainly continental style and as we were on the go all day we wanted a hardy breakfast. We went to Roxy’s Deli, just down from the hotel, however be aware after 11am the breakfast menu finishes and the prices go up. We found this out the hard way when or three breakfast’s came to $91 over £60 ouch!!!! And that included a gratuity of 18%. 
A place I would recommend to eat, would be Emmett O’Lunney’s Irish Bar & Restaurant just around the corner from the hotel, we enjoyed the food and service so much we ate there on three occasions during our stay. Beware of the Nachos starter it could feed 4 people. They had a specials menu that changed every night and a main meal from the a la carte menu was about $15.
Be aware of the yellow cabs we got a ride from Wall St to Columbus Circle at Central park, one day it was only $14, the next day it was $24.
Overall I can’t fault the Novotel and I would use it again.

title: “Huge room - and clean !!!”
text: My husband and I stayed at this hotel from July 24 to July 28/05. The room was huge - we had a one bedroom suite - bedroom with a king bed, living room with pull out double sofa, and kitchenette, there is a walk in closet, with a safe, and another closet with shelves for further storage, the bathroom was perfectly fine also, the rooms were cleaned each day and towels replenished every day. The room was great, it could use a little freshening up but otherwise it is clean and serves it purpose well. Had no trouble with hotel staff and the breakfast was good for the price, it included bagels, toast, fresh fruit, cereal, juices, coffee, tea, as well as butter, cream cheese and jams for your breads. Highly recommend Angelo's Pizza which is next door. The hotel is on 57th, very close to Central Park and 5th avenue which was great, and easily within walking distance to Times Square area. The subway is just down the block also (on 6th Ave). It was a great experience and I would highly recommend it. Don't be concerned with the hallways, somewhat dingy, but the rooms made up for that. My only negative thing about it, is that the doors tend to slam shut, so it is quite loud, you just have to be aware of that when leaving and ensure you close the door yourself, closing it slowly behind you - but that's it. It's worth checking out.

title: “Loved this hotel”
text:
We were very surprised especially because of how great the hotel and rooms were for the money. Very clean, rooms and everywhere we ventured in the hotel, and friendly staff. The bellman was very helpful and went over everything in the room when we arrived, which we appreciated. We did use room service one morning and it arrived on the time exactly when we specified. The food was delicious and hot and was more than enough for the price. Room service personnel were also friendly. One night we came in very late and the TV was not working. Was showing a "lost signal". We called the front desk and in less than 5 minutes a maintanence man had arrived and fixed the simple problem. He was also very personable and kept apologizing for the inconvenience. It was no big deal to us since it was fixed in a very timely fashion. Will admit that we were concerned when we were placed on the 4th floor facing the main street because we were worried about noise. We never had any problems at all. It was very quiet. Beds extremely comfortable and loved the bathroom and how clean it was kept. Would highly recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a place to stay in Denver.
Thank you,
The Wood Family

title: “A Top Hotel with the Personal Touch”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the XV Beacon as part of our 30th Wedding Anniversary. They certainly did their part to make our stay memorable. From the immediate upgrade to the Commons Studio to the bottle of Sparkles and Nibbles awaiting us in our room the experience was simply superb. The personal touches like setting up the room in the evening with music playing and a kind note on our bed informing us of the weather for the next day all contributed to the very special character that this hotel has. All the staff were very considerate and helpful often anticipating our needs before we had even expressed them. 
We had breakfast at the Hotel restaurant which again was excellent (just had fresh fruit and granola with toast), it was well presented and the fruit very fresh. Meals at the restaurant however are expensive.
The only possible criticism would be that the air conditioning is a little noisy and on the first night this was a little disturbing. We found however that we were quite comfortable with the air conditioning off and one of the windows open (it was early October). Street noise was minimal and certainly quieter than the AC unit.
Overall a great experience. I would recommend this hotel to anyone wanting that extra special hotel experience.

title: “Hip and Popular”
text: This remodeled motel is very hip. The bar is always packed. The pool has a great view of the Dallas Skyline. My wife and I enjoy staying there, and it is conveniently located near the Bishop Arts District.

title: “Nice location”
text:
Duration of stay: June 29 - July 2, 2007
Booked: via Priceline at $160 per night
We were travelling through DFW and during this time, many flights were canceled and/or delayed due to weather and we were concerned as to whether we would make our reservation. I spoke with Yvonne of the Millennium and even though we booked through Priceline, she held our reservation until the next day, which most hotels can not do due to their agreements with Priceline. 
The room itself was pretty average. We have stayed at the Grand Hyatt and the Hilton on 6th Ave (both booked via Priceline) and I feel these to be of better quality. Our room was on the 19th floor overlooking Times Square. It was a nice location.

title: “Good airport hotel”
text: Transit stopover. Nice quiet, clean room, with great bed. Used gym as well, and it's very good. Overall, enjoyed the stopover, and as they say "I felt better when I left than when I arrived".

title: “A great hotel!”
text:
We stayed here while my husband was attending a conference in Boston. It was very conveniently located close to the Hynes Convention Center and the Prudential Mall. Boston was a very walkable city but we ended up getting a Charlie pass that was good for 7 days so that we could ride the subway and buses to a few locations that weren't nearby (Harvard, Quincy, Mount Auburn Cemetery). We were very glad that we had this option most days. You can buy these in the airport right by baggage claim.
We arrived at the hotel early in the morning on a Thursday and were told that they could hold our baggage until a room was ready. I checked back around noon and we were able to check into our hotel room on the 22nd floor with a beautiful view of Boston! The next morning when my husband took a shower he noticed that the water leaked from the shower onto the bathroom floor and so we called the front desk to see if there was anything we could do. They immediately told us they could put us into a different room but that it wouldn't be ready for a few hours. I left my luggage in the room and went exploring again. When I came back and inquired about the room, I was told it would be ready in about 20 minutes. When I inquired again, they said that the room they had reserved for us to move to had a slight problem with the heating system and so they upgraded us to a room with a panoramic view! It was a wonderful gesture and such a beautiful view. We felt so lucky!
The rest of our stay was wonderful. We enjoyed the fitness center and the pool, although the spa was a little bit on the small side. We enjoyed the free internet in the lobby and the complimentary water bottles. Our TV remote had a glitch and so they gave us a free in-room movie, which was nice. 
All in all, the hotel exceeded my expectations and we had a very enjoyable four nights there. I would recommend the hotel to family and friends. Thank you Hilton!

title: “Central, but otherwise average”
text:
Stayed for single night as part of a package so not sure of price.
Extremely busy and crowded in reception (and outside on Lexington). Queues!
Standard room was okay but soundproofing didn't work and very noisy all night.
Breakfast was standard fayre and okay. Generally hotel looked over-worked and tired.
Having said that it is a very convenient location for this part of town.

title: “great value!!!”
text: great location,very nice rooms,great price(booked package on travelocity) definately would stay here again.

title: “hampton inn- perfect”
text:
Stayed here 19-23 November. This is a hotel in a perfect location- MSG minutes away, Times Squate, 10 minutes. However the street is comparatively quiet- considering this is NY! 
Hotel room very clean- spacios (2 adults in 2 double bedded room), bathroom sppotless with loads of fresh towls every day.
Staff in lobby always chatty and friendly- breakfast great- plenty of fresh fruit as well.
Internet access a bonus- always eady to use the computers.
Would highly recommend this hotel- great budget too.

title: “Great NYC experience”
text:
I had visited NYC with my family and stayed very close to Times Square. This trip (3 girls in mid-20's) was a different experience, and the hotel we chose definitely assisted with it.
The Best Western is in the heart of Chinatown, and offers a unique experience from the typical "tourist" stay. Reminder, you are in the middle of traditional Chinese culture, so you will be exposed to smelly fish markets, etc. This hotel is walking distance to amazing Chinese restaurants and delightful Italian cuisines in Little Italy. It is also very close to subways. The neighbourhood is pretty quiet at night; nothing like staying in Times Square. 
There is excellent security, who directs you to the main lobby on the second floor. The main entrance may be decieving because the front door is in between other stores. 
The rooms have a modern style with excellent bathrooms. Room sizes may seem small but are actually great compared to most NYC hotel rooms. Breakfast buffet is included, with a small selection and variety of food.
If you drive to NYC like we did, there is an underground parking garage around the corner. It is not conveniently located close to the hotel so it's better to drop off luggage at front door first.
The best part about staying at The Best Western is that you are surrounded by locals more than tourists, which gives you great exposure to NYC culture. The price is great for the value; there is no need to pay nearly triple the price just to stay in Times Square. It is also very close to Canal Street, which is known for its great shops if you are interested in the famous knock-off products.

title: “Great hotel”
text: My dad and I stayed at this hotel on vacation. We knew we didn't want to stay in the middle of all the hubbub in the city but wanted to be in a convenient location. This was perfect. Very close and convenient subway access. The staff were extremely accommodating and friendly. One of the best staff of any hotel I've stayed at. Everything was very clean. Very comfortable bed. Overall great hotel! Will definitely stay here again.

title: “Affordable Luxury”
text: The outstanding staff, huge rooms (by NYC standards), and even bigger bathrooms, by any standard! Not very often that you find a garden tub in a hotel, even less likely to find one in a major city. I would reccoment this hotel to anyone for the room, but the staff makes it even better.

title: “Helpful staff, so so room”
text:
The hotel was... ok. We also had the unfortunate experience of inadvertantly booking during comic con. Our rate was over $90 something dollars on the cheapest night and $135 on the weekends, but it was one of the cheapest in the area during that weekend. We stayed four nights. We booked months in advance, but due to a missed flight arrived very late at night and was told our room had been given away! Even though we called from the airport updating them on our arrival status several times. Once we arrived, the staff was very helpful in securing us a room at another property for the night (and paying for it of course) and the front desk worker just getting off his shift was even nice enough to drive us there himself instead of having to make us wait for a cab. 
We had a room in the very back building so no traffic noise to speak of. We also overlooked the pool which was warm and clean when we used it. The whole building smelled like old people. The room had a desk, fridge, microwave, table, tv, and two beds all stuffed into one room so it was a little cramped. The wifi came in great. There was a bus stop right outside the hotel which was very convenient since we did not rent a car. 
During checkout, our bill was not correct due to the initial error of us not staying the first intended night. The front desk staff and manager were helpful in resolving this issue for us and we were refunded the amount we overpaid within a week. Our flight didn't leave till late so they let us store our bags at the desk while we went out on more adventures. 
I would not recommend the restaurant, however. Because of our troubles, the front desk issued us free breakfast vouchers. Because we weren't paying, the waitress actually went out of her way to ignore us the entire time we were there.

title: “Good Location - Nothing Else To Recommend”
text:
I really wanted to like this place, as I felt that some of the previous reviews sounded a bit petty. However, despite the excellent location it would be very difficult to recommend this hotel to anyone else, or to envision staying there again. It's not absolutely terrible, but just crummy enough to warrant serious hesitation. We really didn't have any serious problems during our three night stay, but can easily imagine that if we had, they would not have been rectified. The only issue that we did complain about (a lack of fresh towels) was treated with disdain, and then ignored, by the maid. However a different maid gave us five fresh towels and an apology when we brought it up again.
Good points - location / reasonable room rate (for New York).
Bad points - poor maid service response / erratic elevators / very small room.

title: “Family Suite and Good Pizza next to Seattle Center, Perfect!”
text:
Loved this place! Slightly funky decor, nice indoor pool, roomy family suite (sleeps 5) with a great micro-pub/wood fired pizza place right off the lobby. What a great find for a family with teens!!!!
Walk to Space needle, monorail & museums. We arrived early a.m. and were pleasantly surprised that our room was ready and that we were welcomed with free coffee and pineapple cupcakes in the lobby. If we're ever in Seattle, this is where we will stay!

title: “Mediocre”
text:
I am truly surprised by the enthusiastic reviews of this property. To begin, it really is in no man's land. If you are doing business in the industrial parks of Kearney Mesa, then perhaps it makes sense. If you are visiting San Diego as a tourist, you may find the central location somewhat useful, but you will hardly feel like you are on vacation. Kearney Mesa is, to say the least, not one of the prettier parts of the city, and the reviewer who was concerned about nighttime safety is not being unreasonable. I suggest the Mission Valley property instead as far as location goes. No amount of rehab of this hotel is going to save it from its lousy location and lousy layout.
This property is really quite large and if you are down at the far end (buildings 12-18), you will have a real hike through a slightly confusing maze to get to breakfast and to the rather small pool. Forget about walking food back to your room. It's just way too far away. The breakfast is not bad, but get there early if you want to avoid the ill-behaved children's soccer teams. The evening reception is disappointing. The chili is from a can. The wine is vile, and making matters worse, they chill the red wine. The only beer is Bud lite. Not even ordinary Bud (not that either is any good."
The rooms are not terrible, but they are not true suites. They are all studios. In other words there is no separate living room. The kitchen has pretty much everything you need to cook a decent meal and there is a grocery store just a mile west called Food for Less, which is actually a pretty good grocery store with really good prices (Amsterdam Gin for 14.00!) but is pretty down market in appearance. If you need signs to tell you what is on what aisle, forget it. Very good produce.
If you are enthusiastic about Asian dining then this is your neighborhood to be sure. There is a superabundance of Asian dining opportunities in Kearney Mesa. If you would like your children not to ask you what a so-called "gentlemen's club" is or "adult bookstore" (even though real gentlemen and real adults don't go to these places) you might want to look for another property. If jet airplane sounds from Miramar sounds like freedom to you then you might like this place. If they sound like tax dollars going up in flames you might not like it.
Room maintenance was very attentive on an internet access problem. No wifi in the rooms. You have to plug into the cable.
The property is worn down.

title: “Basic but good value for the price”
text: Located a long way from downtown Seattle but the plus was that it was closer to Boeing factory tour and whale-watching cruise. Paid $70 a night for 3 nights. Room was clean and quiet. Wi-fi worked fine. Used the guest laundry - only one machine and dryer but met our needs. Continental breakfast was adequate and well-stocked with the basic items. On-site free parking. You get what you pay for and this was a good deal for the price. Just don't leave vaulables in the room.

title: “Great hotel at a great location”
text: Hotel is very near to Union Square and 10-minute walk from underground station with direct line to the airport. Just around the corner you can take cable car to Fisherman's Wharf which is quite nice. Most importantly rooms were clean and we were very satisfied with the staff. Highly recommendable, especially if you can get a good deal.

title: “very disappointed”
text:
just got back from Hilton Union Square. Booked my room through priceline, so I think that's why I was placed to a very small and out-dated room in Tower 1. The window in my hotel room is even smaller than the one in my kid's room back home. Not to mention the view is looking at parking garage. Stayed in many hotels in SF, this is probally one of the worst rooms. Being a HIlton Honor member doesn't help at all. Charge me $15 for using fitness center ( because I booked my room through priceline, ) and $50 for overnight parking.
Always booked my hotels through priceline whenever I visited SF ( visiting SF at least once a month), Marriot at 4th st gave me the best room and fitness center is free even thoguh I am not Marriot member. Besides, Marriot's fitness center and in-door swimming pool is so much better than Hilton. Feel regret for being a loyal Hilton Honor memebr for many years. Applying for Marriot member now.

title: “A great experience”
text:
This was the first time that we had stayed at the Giraffe Hotel.Normally we stay at the Metro but that was undergoing work. It is on Park Avenue South and East 25th. Perhaps it is a little further away from the main action and a few blocks from Penn Station but it more than made up for that in the quality of its rooms and breakfast. For New York it was also quite quiet. Our bedroom had a little balcony so we could overlook the street action. There is also a roof terrace but because the hotel is only about 12 storeys you don't get much of a view, however it is a nice place to sit with a drink. The breakfast is excellent with fresh fruit salad, yoghurts, bagels, toast, croissants, boiled eggs and a variety of drinks -teas, coffee etc. There are proper plates and cutlery and the room is light and airy with no television thank goodness.
All the staff are friendly and helpful and there is a facility to check in on-line for your flight in the breakfast room.
While we were there there was free cheese and wine each evening from 5 -8 pm
We would definitely stay there again.

title: “Watch the game from your room!”
text: I stayed here for two nights on a business trip. I really didn't get much of a chance to see or use the hotel amenities, but overall I'd highly recommend this hotel if you want to be in the Gaslamp area of San Diego. Be aware that driving in this area is difficult. There are very congested one-way streets and often they block-off areas for special events. But I like the area for easy walking access to countless restraunts and good running paths. Parking is ridiculously expensive, but, comparable to all hotels in this area. All staff members that I encountered were exceptionally friendly and professional.

title: “Good value!”
text:
Good location, relatively quiet neighbourhood, blocks away from Union Square (great atmosphere) with all major subway lines nearby. A lot of restaurants near the hotel.
Very small room (but we had the smallest room on our floor), decor little old-fashioned, but really clean. Bathroom was shared, but always clean (even late in the evening or early in the morning). Friendly staff, helpful.
Great hotel if you want to be in a good neighbourhood in Manhattan for not too much money. Just don't expect big rooms or a modern decor!

title: “If you like NO FRILLS........”
text: From the moment I pulled up in my rental car and the "bellman" looked at me with disdain, until the moment I checked out, my stay at the Raffaello was completely disappointing. The location is great, I'll give it that, but the minute you enter the lobby, it becomes moot. The front desk staff were unwelcoming and not of the caliber nor polish that a hotel demands. I never got so much as smile or a sense that they were happy to have me. I was asked for my credit card and not once did either person look me in the eye. Instead, I received a perfunctory explanation of the coffee bar in the lobby. There was NO bellman to take my bags to my room. I did it myself. The room was spacious, but devoid of charm. The walls still sport their original plaster, albeit covered in an ugly ochre paint job. The bathroom was tiny. A glass shelf installed above the sink meant that every time I bent to wash my face I banged my forehead on the shelf. There is a small closet, so filled with bathrobes, slippers, a safe, an ironing board, an iron, etc., that you cannot hang one item of clothing in it! There is NO room service yet each night a breakfast menu is on each bed. Why??? I could go on. The only saving grace is a young blonde concierge, who's name I didn't get, who helped us both nights of our stay. He was wonderful and some other hotel should go scoop him up immediately. I will never go back to the Raffaello, nor recommend it to anyone I know. The last night of my stay one of the elevators was out of service. It was a Saturday night. I, and a dozen other guests, waited more than 15 minutes to get to our rooms. No one said a word to us or apologized. Disgraceful. For $350 per night this hotel has a long way to go to justify the cost of the stay. It is lacking in every standard set by other hotels.

title: “Good Hotel Near Union Square”
text:
I liked this hotel a lot. It's in a good location that makes it easy to walk the 2 blocks to Union Square. It was quiet and well decorated. The only complaints I have:
1. The room we stayed in had the outside of the shower / tub broken and was fixed with a bad patch job. It just didn't fit in with the feel of this nice hotel.
2. The day we checked in the A/C was broken. The front desk staff never thought to inform of this. I had to find out when I called down later as the room was really hot. A/C didn't get fixed until the next day when we checked out. I think it would have been good customer service to inform us they were having problems upon check in. We did ask them for a fan and they brought one to the room. That was a nice surprise.

title: “OK for price”
text: I stayed in May. I was in town for a job interview. the price was excellent for value, received and the location, next to Japantown, was convenient. The hotel was a bit 'echo-y' in the halls, and the rooms often had doors between them, but I had no trouble sleeping. And , again, for the price it was great.

title: “Location, location, location”
text: This is a very clean and serviceable property near two T stops in the fun neighborhood of Back Bay, central to Pru Center and Copley Square. Very fair room rates, clean, & with a responsive staff. Room definitely was budget but quite large. Disconcerting was the light for the bathroom lit both the bathroom behind a door, and the open- to- the- rest- of- the- room sink area, blazing the whole room with light during those late night excursions to the ladies room. Forced air heat is quite loud. All in all a very affordable spot. Tour buses stop right outside for boarding, so if you have a room on the Huntington side of the building, be sure those drapes are closed if you don't want to show yourself off to the folks on the double decker!

title: “Great, with some minor details to improve”
text:
Great room,with comfortable bed, spacious bath room and big flat screen TV with perfect image (pretty uncommon in New York). Good storage and nice lighting with predefined lighting schemes. Free minibar (except for alcohol) and Bigelow bathroom products. Clean and still mostly fresh, even though you could see some signs of wear in the bathroom.
Service was very helpful, but the lounge check-in/check-out was maybe not so good from a logistic point of view. Trying to serve coffee & beverages at the same time as checking in guests at least left me unattended at a couple of occasions. I did however enjoy the free wine/cappucino once it arrived.
Nice bar & restaurant if you want to stay in the hotel. Breakfast really enjoyable, but (as always in top hotels) expensive. All in all a hotel I would definitely recommend, especially if you can get a good weekend deal.

title: “Incredible!!!”
text:
This place is not called Paradise for nothing! We stayed with family in the cabanas for 3 nights. 
We rented all three rooms and it was great to leave it open during the day but then have the privacy at night. It was absolutely incredible to go and let the kids swim in the bath water temperature pool that was absolutely immaculately maintained, then come back to the room to relax and the kids could go look for sea shells on the beach. We had bon fires at night-(I recommend bringing wood or buying some if you are traveling from a far distance like I was). We roasted hot dogs and made s'mores. It was AWESOME. The rooms were as immaculate as the grounds, I don't know how they do it with the sand from the beach just outside your door but they did a great job. Sea World is just down the street and we were able to sit out at our bon fire and watch the fireworks from the park on the weekend nights. The small kitchen area was great as well, the microwave was great for heating my nephews bottles and the fridge allowed us to keep hot dogs on hand for the bon fires. There are tons of activities that are offered as well and my only regret was not making the time to use the jet skis and kayaks-they had kayakers leaving from the beach in the morning just outside our door- (How cool is that?). They also offer an unbelivable spa and my mother recieved the whole treatment-she absolutely loved it! Overall I would highly recommend this resort. We only stayed the short 3 nights and then went on to Anaheim but didn't want to leave and plan to return for a full week next year!

title: “So pleased with this find”
text:
Ok, so Korea Town might seem like an odd place to stay when you are in LA but I can tell you that you won't find a nicer boutique hotel in the whole town.
Our room was huge, the bathroom was huge and clean, the staff were friendly and helpful and the neighbourhood felt safe.
It should be even better when the restaurant and bar open up.
Thanks guys, for making our stay in LA so enjoyable.

title: “Positive experience, lacking attention to room details”
text:
The location of the Grand Hyatt was perfect for our needs - walkable to the New Amsterdam Theater, 5th Avenue shopping, museums, etc. The public spaces were impressive, and check-in was very pleasant. Staff at check-in were extremely welcoming and professional - paid extra attention to our children which they enjoyed.
The Positives: At both check-in and check-out the staff at the registration desk were very friendly and helpful. Maud, in the bar, was extremely nice and made us feel at home. She was kind to our kids and made it a point to include them in conversation. The concierge gave us a very helpful recommendation for a family dinner on Saturday night. 
The guestroom itself had fairly hip decor and was spacious for NYC standards (Rm 2651). We were a family of 4 (2 adults, 2 kids), and the room with 2 double beds was large enough to accommodate with our minimal luggage. The beds were very comfortable and the bedding was neat and clean. The thermostat was adjustable down to 65 degrees (we like it cool), but no lower. The bathroom was small, but adequate, the the toiletry amenities (shampoo, conditioner, lotion, toothpaste) were very nice. The hair dryer worked once you hit the test button on the plug. We had a good-sized window with a nice little half-couch. There was a long desk area under the wall-mounted TV, and it housed a small refrigerator, safe, and microwave.
The Negatives: While overall the room met our needs and was comfortable, there were certain details that seemed easily fixable, yet when I brought them to the attention of the hotel staff, only one was rectified. 
1. The refrigerator wasn't working - this was fixed on Saturday.
2. The floor lamp near the couch was obviously broken (tilted shade, standing at odd angle, not working). This was reported on Saturday morning but was not fixed.
3. The specialty light on the bed near the window was missing from its socket. There was a switch, but the light was simply gone. This was reported on Saturday morning, but was not fixed.
4. The curved shower curtain in the bathroom was installed incorrectly. Instead of curving out into the bathroom to allow more room in the shower, it curved down toward the floor which made the shower curtain continually come open at the ends. We did not report this since technically it worked, but we thought it very odd that a bathroom "feature" could be installed incorrectly and no one had ever bothered to fix it.
5. The towel hook near the bathtub was not properly installed and each time we took a towel off the hook, the hook fell to the floor. The mounting screw needs to be properly tightened which should be a simple fix. I plan to share these comments with the hotel staff, and hopefully it will be fixed.
6. On Sunday morning the alarm clock began going off at 7am, and in our sleepiness, we could not determine how to turn it off. We just kept hitting the snooze feature and by 7:30am we eventually just gave up and got up. We are not sure how this was turned on since it had not been a problem on Saturday morning.
Overall we had a good visit at the Grand Hyatt. Our kids enjoyed the hotel, and the positives outweighed the negatives. With a little more attention to the details, this hotel stay would have been very good. They have great potential, and we would probably try them again if the rate was right.

title: “very good location”
text:
We stayed at the Chancellor hotel for 3 nights on a tour of the USA. Be booked through email and got a nice comfortable room with a view of Union square as requested. The location of the hotel is perfect... everything is literaly 5 mins away. The hotel was clean and the personel helpful. Valet parking is convinient but a bit expensive at $30+tax!
personally we prefer staying in B&Bs but the Chancellor hotel is one of the best hotels we have ever visited.
Philip & Irsa, Nicosia - Cyprus.

title: “Great Hotel, wish it was closer to Union Square.”
text:
The room is great for a city hotel: good size, clean, up-to-date. Very happy with the service as well, great staff and very helpful. We had a 5th floor room and it was much quieter than I had been told. 
It was pouing rain and the walk to Union Square was longer than I had expected. The beds were not real comfortable for my taste. 
Would stay here again.

title: “Not First Class”
text:
I stayed at the Casulo for one nite - - and that was enough. The noice coming from the atrium kept me up way to long. Didn't get enough sleep and it showed the next day.
Reception lacked much friendliness ad professionalism.
They forgot my wake up call. 
Rooms are decorated nice - -but it is trying to be first class and it is NOT!

title: “We Liked It Fine”
text: My wife and I had already booked our stay before we found this site, and then were horrifed when we read some of the reviews, but we had a perfectly event-free stay at Red Lion. You may want to consider that we only travel once or twice a year for pleasure, so we may not be as sensitive to some of the finer points of a hotel's performance as the seasoned business traveller. We didn't use the internet during our stay or eat at the hotel at all. We were there for three nights the weekend before Memorial Day weekend. We didn't hear a single train horn all weekend and then, ironically, heard one as we were walking through the lobby on our way to check out, but it didn't seem overly loud. I always travel with earplugs, and the air conditioner did wake me up a couple of times, but it wasn't so loud that I couldn't go right back to sleep. The room didn't seem dirty to us. The shower had good water pressure, though it leaked a little around the temperature knobs. We didn't hear anything through the walls from other rooms, no wild packs of teenagers roaming the halls. The front desk staff was friendly enough. The pool wasn't open, but they were cleaning it and getting it ready, so we assumed it would open on Memorial Day, which is customary where we're from. Getting to the entrance is a little tricky if you're not familiar with the area. Google has a program you can download called Google Earth, and I used that before our trip to view an actual satellite photo of the area and I didn't have any problems. Coming west from Denver International Airport, take the Quebec St. exit, take an almost immediate right onto the Smith Rd. exit, at the top of the ramp take a left, go straight after the stop sign and then an immediate left onto the frontage road which will take you right to the entrance. If you go left at the stop sign instead of straight and then left, you'll find yourself on the ramp back down to the highway. Coming from the south on Quebec, just be careful to turn right at the stop sign at Smith Rd, so you'll go onto the frontage road instead of straight, which will put you on the ramp back to the highway. There's a large shopping complex about a half-mile to the south with fast food, some sit-down restaurants, and a SuperWal-Mart. I think that maybe reviews are usually written by people who have bad experiences, which is why I took the time to write this. We had a good stay.

title: “Family DC Getaway”
text: We were treated very nicely by the entire staff. The kitchenette really helped cut down on our costs along with the continnental breakfast. The room was extremely spacious with kitchen area, living room area, bedroom, and bathroom all seperated. The only problem we experienced was that we went in October and the heating and air system could not be operated at the same time. They had the air already turned off and we happened to have a couple of fairly warm days.

title: “Stay-cation for holiday weekend”
text:
We have some beautiful resorts in the Phoenix area that offer great rates in the hot summer months. For Memorial weekend I choose the Arizona Grand. We wanted a "stay-cation" where we could enjoy a weekend together with 4 adults and 2 children. 
We had a wonderful time as a family but I can't give the hotel all the credit. 
The rooms were ok. Two room suites. TVs were old/small and there weren't a lot of frills. For us it was still ok. Small pools by each of the buildings was nice. The water park was a shock because of the crowds. Standing room only on Sunday. Felt like everything was dirty and crowded and not very relaxing. The next day was better. We got down to the water park at 9:00 am and there was a long line waiting to open at 9:30. However, we did get a nice spot and it made a big difference. Employee told me they have an average of 6000 people on a summer holiday. 
The food in the water park was WAY over priced and you can't bring anything in. Drinks almost $10- a corn dog was $6. I generally don't complain about the cost of hotel food but since it was a Stay-cation it bothered me more. 
The hotel has a well known restaurant at the top of the hill (hotel is at the bottom) called Rustler's Roost. I don't think I have ever had a good meal here but the atmosphere is amazing. Especially for you out of towners...you can see all of the valley and it is a spectacular view. The grandkids danced to the live band and went down the big slide. Kids ate free and our bill was cheaper than the pool grill. The cotton candy bouquet after dinner was all of our favorites. Entrees were just so-so. This is defintely an experience and not just a meal. 
Food was MUCH better at the mexican restaurant in front of the hotel "Aunt Chiladas". Pricey but good and we enjoyed one last family meal before everyone went in their separate directions. 
We enjoyed the weekend - biggest complaint was the crowds.

title: “Not Quite As Good As I Remember”
text:
We have stayed at Lenox a number of times over the years, and I remember it as being a first class hotel. Not sure if we've been staying at better hotels recently, or if Lenox has slipped a bit. It is still a very good hotel in an excellent location. But, our room was quite small and the bath was tiny, without any updates to provide additional storage space or light. The desk lamp was broken, and flickered non stop, the radio didn't work, there was no coffee maker in the room, nor were there any menus for the on site restaurants. And, no newspaper was provided. Those are all relatively small complaints, but they added up to making this a 4 star v 5 star review. 
There was complimentary coffee and tea in the lobby, but we didn't discover this until we were on our way out for the day. Would be nice to be told about coffee at check in, or to have card in room giving that info. Is it only me, or does it seem like more and more hotels are removing their coffee makers from the rooms? 
The hotel prides itself on being eco friendly, which may be why they don't provide every guest with newspaper. But maybe they could ask guest at ck in if they'd like a newspaper delivered to room. 
 I look forward to having coffee in morning in room, as well as scanning the newspaper, whenever I travel. Sad to see this little luxury is being less common even at best hotels.

title: “Thanks again trip advisor!”
text:
We weren't sure exactly when we'd arrive in NYC so we couldn't take advantage of some other hotel deals or advance reservations. We checked trip advisor and based on the reviews made a reservation. The location is very convenient to everything. Although other reviewers expressed concerns about the proximity to Port Authority and the parole office we never felt afraid. There's plenty of pedestrian traffic and lots of people around. The free breakfast is quite good although it's so crowded seating becomes an issue. At the same time we shared tables with friendly folks from around the world! The staff is very nice and one night 2 of the folks at the desk broke into song and entertained us with their lovely voices!
The rooms are quite clean although small and cramped once your luggage is in. I'd do without the kitchen (also small) to have more space. The hotel doesn't have a service elevator so guests and staff use the 3 elevators and wait times are rather long. 
The free washers and dryers were quite wonderful to have after a few weeks on the road. It gets a bit busy so you have to be patient!
I've spent a lot of time in NYC, most hotels are quite expensive and don't offer even close to what this hotel does. I spend most of my time in NY out and about so most of the inconveniences I found are minor. This hotel is a good 
value!

title: “Nice, But Not Worth The Money”
text:
Stayed at the Omni during a college visit to San Antonio. The hotel is in a great location to explore downtown San Antonio and the Riverwalk area. The Riverwalk is an enormous tourist attraction. If you don't like big crowds and your idea of fine dining isn't "Dick's Last Resort", then you might want to try a different location.
The service at the hotel is fine. The hotel has a slightly tired feel to it. It advertises itself as "one of the top hotels in the nation" according to some magazine. That might have been true 10 years ago, but it felt like a nice hotel that was priced like a five star hotel. We stayed in an Ambassador River View room. If you look at the pictures on the website, the room looks very spacious, but they have used some kind of wide angle photo lens as the room is quite ordinary in size and overall very average for the $337/night room charge. In addition you will get hit with about 20% in local/county/state taxes, so you should factor that in when you consider the cost. The rooms are again nicely furnished, but not really up to my expectations given the cost. The air conditioning unit is really old school. It was incredibly noisy, was one of the old ones that kicks on and off every ten minutes during the night, and blows so much air into the room that you wake up with a dry throat. I only add this detail to give an example of why I think this hotel is not really what you'd expect for the money.
The breakfast buffet is a great option, about $14/person. There are a ton of dining options on the Riverwalk, but again you will find that there are huge crowds. Suggest you get outside of downtown and check out an interesting neighborhood. We found a restaurant in Alamo Heights and there seemed to be many interesting choices in the area.
If I had paid under $200/night, I might have felt like I got decent value, but at these prices, suggest you look elsewhere.

title: “Yowza!”
text: Rooms are not what they look like in the picture, I'm pretty sure this was a motel 6 previously with giant murals on the walls to make it look "boutique"... We had booked 2 nights, but immediately after check in were disappointed and stayed one due to "hotel policy" charging us, and booked a beautiful room at the OMNI downtown!! Needless to say, I will not be going back.

title: “Reliable name on older hotel”
text: We reserved 4 rooms to have a family holiday get together and the hotel could not have been nicer or more helpful. The rooms have been recently redone as the hotel changed from being the Adam's Mark to Wyndham. Everything was clean and comfortable including the mattress. I rarely sleep in hotels, but I got great sleep for the two nights we were there.

title: “The Best Hotel I have ever stayed at!”
text: Everyone at this hotel are professional, helpful, and very nice! The Valet is exceptional, the Front Desk employee's are very helpful, and extremely nice. The rooms are so worth the price. There is a frig, microwave, dishwasher, coffee pot, couch, Flat screen TV. The bedroom has a desk, computer chair, another flat screen TV, the bed(s) are the Most Comfortable beds I have ever slept in at a hotel! They serve a great breakfast each morning with excellent choices. Mon-Thurs they serve a free supper which was outstanding! They also offer Beer, and wine for free with dinner. I was very impressed with this hotel. I know we all hate business trips, but I hope they have them more often in Indianapolis, so I can come stay here more often. Oh, I failed to mention... our driver that took us to our meetings each day was the BEST! He had a good personality, extremely nice, and very professional! If you are debating on a hotel to stay at and really want a TOP NOTCH stay.... Homewood Suites is the answer! Worth the money!

title: “Luxury boutique hotel for a great price”
text: A wonderful location a block from the Water Tower, closer to the lake. The rate was super, and then we got upgraded. There were obvoius upgrades to the bed and the TVs, view was ok. Decor in general was done well. Staff was pleasant. Don't go for the lobby bar, etc if that's how you spend your hotel stays, but it's Chicago, there's a ton of places to go. One tip on parking, the self park that the hotel recommends is only a block away and if you're not planning on in and out privileges save the extra 3 bucks a night and go directly to the garage. It's 26 per night with no in and out and 29 with in and out.

title: “Friendly staff”
text: This was my second visit to the Roger Smith and it did not disappoint. The staff are magnificent; I was recovering from an emergency operation and they went out of their way to be helpful and seemed genuinely concerned. They upgraded me to a suite which was fantastic. The location is excellent and it is like a home away from home. I strongly recommend it; and the prices are very reasonable.

title: “Fun for all..”
text:
We have stayed here many times and enjoy it. The last time we scored an amazing room rate (usually $200+ a night, was only $99) and I noticed a few changes... no coffee in the room, less amenities, overall not as high-end. Perhaps with the economy in the current state they are trying to appeal to larger crowd. 
The rooms are a bit outdated but comfortable.
The restaurants are fun especially in the summer months when there is live music (I heard they cut the live music last summer because of the economy.)
Love movie night by the pool.
Love feeding the ducks.
Enjoyed the Fine Dinning restaurant. 
Can get VERY crowded especially on Holiday weekends and beware of the jellyfish!
The Bayside rooms are the best.

title: “Excellent and good value hotel in Boston”
text: Compared to most other overpriced hotels in Bean Town you get a really good break at The Buck. Good sized rooms, a location just around the corner from the T (Subway, Metro, Tube) and in walking distance from the nicer prst of the Back Bay brownstone-streets. Breakfast perhaps not the greatest, but staff exceptionally helpful. And old hotel, yes sure - but with plenty of charm. Parking next door to the hotel at reasonable rates. A Boston winner.

title: “clean but dated”
text: I stayed here courtesy of an airline due to a flight delay. This place is about 20 minutes (no traffic) by freeway from the DFW airport. After waiting 30 minutes for the hotel shuttle, we ended up taking a cab for $35. As other reviewers noted, the place is dated and worn out. They have tried some room updates like a microwave, coffee maker, mini- fridge and blow dryer. The rooms are larger size and clean at least. The staff was friendly, but missed my wakeup call.

title: “Comfortable hotel in a central location.”
text: I stayed at the Sixth Avenue in for one night before a cruise. All the staff were so friendly--the registration desk, cleaning staff, and restaurant. The hotel was much quieter then I expected, given the age of the building and the fact that there were a couple large groups that night. And the bed was so comfortable!

title: “Great Hotel”
text: This Hotel was great, I just wish we could have stayed longer. The staff were very professional and culturally diverse. This was a bonus. I wish I could have taken the bed home with us, it was so nice. The hotel is located just 5 minutes from the White House and 2 minutes from the subway. The subway is clean like Montreal's Metro system and it is easy to use. There is free tea and coffee provided in the morning in "2 go cups"...which is a bonus. Parking is 32.00 per day...but I knew that before hand. We booked on hotwire.com and were very happy. This hotel is great and in a great location.

title: “Very good hotel with great staff and a great location.”
text: We stayed at the hotel for a week, the staff were excellent, very friendly and helpful, especially the ladies serving breakfast. However, we think the breakfast was rather limited for a hotel of this class, it consisted of a selection of fruit juices, coffee/tea/hot drinks, toast, bagels/buns, some cereal boxes, a selection of mini pastries, some yoghurts - and that was just about it. We were also a little disappointed with the fixtures in the bathroom, we asked to change rooms (which was granted) and were offered a bottle of wine in compensation. Again, the staff were very good and understanding. Overall, the hotel was very satisfactory, its in a great location on Park Avenue with some very nice steakhouses and other restaurants near by. The Empire state building is about a 15 minutes walk away and 5th avenue/south section of Central Park are very walkable. There is also a subway station very near the hotel which is handy.

title: “Great Hotel and Staff!”
text:
I had never stayed at a Kimpton hotel before. I was not sure what to expect. The Helix surpassed all my expectations. The hotel was extremely clean, and the staff went beyond being helpful. The bed was also the best hotel bed I have slept on. 
The staff always had a smile and were more then happy to help out with anything I needed. You won't be disappointed!

title: “Superb Stay in the Inner Harbor”
text: Top-notch (and sincerely friendly) service from arrival to departure. I was in the lobby when the hotel's computer system went down for a brief period and while it didn't affect me I was impressed how the front desk handled other guests with great aplomb. Great restaurant recommendation (Cinghiale) and transportation coordination by the concierge. We were also impressed with the quality accommodations. First class all the way.

title: “Now that the remodel is done, we are back!”
text: Now that the remodel is done, we are back! Hotel looks great. Location is excellent (right next to the 6 and E). Staff is very nice, especailly Marlyn who checked us in!

title: “Great location, comfortable rooms!”
text:
This is the second time that I've stayed at the Silver Cloud - both times I stayed here was for Pride Weekend with a group of friends. This hotel is modern and well-appointed, with clean, comfortable rooms and a location that is fantastic - whether you are planning on spending your time downtown, on Capitol Hill, or elsewhere! Check in was a breeze - the front desk agents were all VERY helpful and friendly. Our room was spacious - located on the 5th floor. I love that this hotel has FREE Wi-Fi, a mini-fridge and microwave in each room, and full patio doors that open three-different ways! (There is no patio though - just a juliet balcony). The rooms also have Aveda amenities - which is a heckuva lot nicer than the generic amenities that most hotels at this price point would offer. The beds are very comfortable - had a GREAT sleep all three nights I was there. There is also a nice pool/hot tub and gym facility in the basement of the hotel 
My only complaint about this hotel this time around is that we didn't receive housekeeping service one of the days we were there. This is despite being out of the room all day - I returned in the evening to find all the beds unmade, none of the towels or amenties replenished, garbages unemptied, etc. I hate making my bed at home - I certainly enjoy doing it less in the hotel. Anyways - after a call to front desk - one of the friendly desk agents was nice enough to bring up four bath towels, and four hand towels along with some shampoo and soap, etc. (Thanks shaved head guy - sorry I didn't catch your name!). Despite this - I will stay in the hotel again and again and again!!

title: “Nice Hotel, Great Location, but Overpriced”
text:
We booked this hotel through Hotwire and paid $127 for the night. I would suggest that if you live in the area, not to drive your car into the city. The parking fee is outrageous ($55.00 per night) and the valet service is horrible. Both times we need to check our car out, we waited for 20 minutes. The valets definitely do not move like they have a purpose. When we decide to do another overnight stay in the city, we will definitely come in on BART and then use other forms of public transportation or taxis.
The Front Desk staff was very nice upon check-in and gave us a room with two double beds. For the price that you pay, you would expect your room to come with a larger bed, but we did not feel like paying more money for another room upgrade. The room was tastefully appointed, but small. It reminded me of the smaller size of hotel rooms that I have stayed in across Europe. Our room was immacualte and the bathroom was very nice. the Heavenly beds and comforters are excellent, so it kind of made up for the small beds. Our view (if that is what you can call it) looked inwardly over some courtyard/alley and directly at the tower across from us. However, if we looked to the left we saw a corner of Union Square and gazed upon The Cheesacake Factory atop Macy's.
The restaurant food is overpriced and not that wonderful. We have many favorite restaurants in the city, so I would recommend travelers to venture out into the city for more fabulous and better priced food. All in all, it was an average hotel stay. Having spent time at various other Westin establishments throughout my traveling experiences, I expected more from this hotel so that was kind of a downer. However, the location of this hotel is fantatstic and is probably why the hotel can charge such exorbitant rates.

title: “It was okay”
text: The hotel was clean and nice decorated. The bed was comfortable and lines clean. The a/c was making a rattling noise when we arrived. We complained to the man who brought us room service but no one came to do anything about it.The next morning we complained AGAIN about it to the front desk person. The food was good and room service came quickly. You have to pay for the internet and there is no free breakfast as with some hotels. The parking is also very confusing we parked in the Greenway parking and were charged 10 dollars for the night. We were also charged 14 dollars for parking in the hotel parking lot. When we complained about the a/c she did take both parking charges off our bill.

title: “Excellence all round”
text:
We spent Christmas and New Year in San Francisco and chose the Omni for our place to stay. From the moment we arrived (before we got out of the taxi) we were made incredibly welcome by Daryl the doorman. Our experience at check in was really personal and we were given our Select Guest beverage vouchers for our morning drink. My daughter was really pleased to see a Birthday cake in our room when we opened the door. This was arranged by the hotel and no charge made. The room was very clean an plenty of room for the three of us. The room service was always on time, and one time when it wasn't we were given some muffins as an apology! The maid service could not have been better either.
The bar was cosy and friendly and like the restaurant a little pricy but quality food and drink.
There is not one thing I can genuinely say I could remotely think about in a negative way. All the staff were a pleasure to speak to, the service was always excellent and the decor of the hotel was very seasonal. The Christmas tree and decorations and Christmas music in the lobby were welcoming and cosy. Frequent warm apple cider, apples and ginger cookies were a welcome treat each evening.
We were made welcome and felt part of the family during our stay away from home over Christmas.
I stay in many hotels in the UK as part of my work and I can honestly say that the Omni has been the most pleasurable hotel stay I have ever experienced. This may sound over the top but it's true. I would certainly use this hotel again if in San Francisco.

title: “never again”
text: was supposed to be a relaxing night away, was all but that. the heater did not work in the room. the number bed we had was very uncomfortable, and noticed the shampoo and conditioner in the room had already been used and not replaced by the maid. also, the coffee pot was filthy. will not stay there again and will not recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: “Loved it”
text: We really loved it. We had one of the rooms on the upper floor (bathroom down the hall) and had a great view of the Bay. The room had a great "European antique-y" feel. The location was perfect - we even walked back from the baseball game. And it was a great value. Can't wait to go back.

title: “Fantastic old Chicago nostalgia”
text: This is a fantastic hotel, with great service from all. The location is wonderful. We ran along Lake Michigan in the morning. The El is right outside the door. Endless shopping and a great museum within walking distance.

title: “Loved every minute of our stay”
text: Ink48 was a fantastic part of our NYC experience. From the minute we arrived, staff made us feel like rock stars with extra attention, extra touches and all of the other extras that make a stay memorable. The location was terrific . . . easily accessible to Times Square to the subway to Central Park, to great Hell's Kitchen restaurants, to everything we wanted to do during our stay. The roof-top bar was absolutely AMAZING, with views that were spectacular. I would highly recommend this hotel for anyone looking for an experience to write home about.

title: “Truly a 4 star hotel!”
text:
Really enjoyed my stay here. It was nice and clean and quiet. Excellent proximity to LAX, without the noise that is sometimes experienced at airport hotels.
Fabulous wine and cheese party for guests the evening that I was there.
Only problem: only valet parking was available and I hate valet. I parked off site, which was a bit of a pain

title: “Tired but friendly and right in the action”
text:
I had stayed in this hotel 15 years ago so it was a nostalgia selection. The staff were helpful and the foyer welcoming. We wanted a king room so were in the east wing - a bit of a maze but staff showed us the way. The room was clean and spacious with a tiny but newish bathroom. I did not master having a shower with a constant temperature - I was screaming at boiling or freezing water. 
You don't spend much time in your room but facilities are basic. No fridge, no coffee machine. I guess you get what you pay for. I booked on their website so was eligible for free wifi which was a bonus. 
You are close to absolutely everything and there are so many local eateries to try. The down stairs cafe has a good breakfast menu although staff are a bit abrupt. But I find that just part of being in NY. 
I stuffed up my booking dates and the staff could have penalised me a days fees but were very understanding and accommodated us as far as they could. 
Yes it was an okay stay but maybe I'll try somewhere else next visit.

title: “Only place to stay in Denver”
text:
My wife and I fly to Denver four or more times per year to attend Broncos' games. After staying at the Four Seasons we won't stay anywhere else. The service is excellent, the rooms modern and clean, and the beds the most comfortable of anywhere we've stayed. We especially like that we can walk to Mile High Statium from the hotel within a reasonable time. The hotel is located close to downtown with a varient of restaurants and bars within walking distance.
Note: We're from Seattle, so walking distance may be a bit longer than some would like.

title: “great location, friendly staff”
text: The Back Bay Hotel is tucked away just minutes walk from the hustle and bustle of Boston's great shops and restaurants. The room was what you would expect from a city hotel; stylish and well equipped although a little on the small side,it was spotlessly clean with a very comfortable bed and a large than average, nicely furnished bedroom. The concierge was very helpful and overall the staff were very friendly. We didn't eat in the restaurant-preferring to sample some of Boston's great restaurants instead, but the prices looked reasonable for a city hotel. Overall a great hotel to stay in for a stay in Boston.

title: “The best location..period”
text:
I have been coming to this property for over 18 years now and seen many changes thru the years. The recent renovation has been an improvement as the grounds are just beautiful. This property takes such great care to maintain the beauty of the landscaping. The pools are more suited to the little ones as they are all very shallow so if you have young kids it's perfect. They have 1 jacuzzi and 3 pools all clean and well kept.....the poolside drinks are really good too! try a mojito made by Jeff...he is the best! 
We love the tower rooms as the view is incomparable to any other, however I was a little surprised of the condition of a few minor things. Our bathroom sink had a huge crack in it and seemed to leak thru a bit, how does one crack a sink that new and heavy.
We stayed on the 17th floor and the room was large and clean. Nice light ocean colors along with a great sitting area makes it a very pleasant atmosphere. Our room was facing the ocean and what a spectacular view! We also had access to the regency Club, which had been renovated since we had last visited. It looked clean, comfortable and well thought out except I was unimpressed with the selection of evening bites and choices as there used to be many more options now it's just vege's, cheese, crackers and 1 dessert selection. They still have an honor bar which is nice and offer nice beverage selections. In my opinion, for the extra money to have access to this level, they could offer some hot items or even maybe a light protein or pasta? The morning fare was nice and offered cold items along with pastries, cereal, bagels, fruit, juices and yogurt. 
I was really disappointed with room service. This is one area I think this location suffers badly. There are 2 options of on-site restaurants and no in-between except for an Einstein bagel shop. It could be hit and miss , but with a Hyatt brand I think the food at this site could use a big improvement and must be looked at seriously by the hotel especially for the price. There is a really good casual fish market right down the boardwalk that rocks! and the fish is all locally caught...a must! I didn't try the buffet breakfast at Red Marlin, although I heard people saying it was very over-priced and not worth it. I would also suggest going to the Hyatt Manchester at Seaport village where they have a seafood restaurant called Sally's, it is right on the marina and the sushi is incredible!
The concierge service is pretty non-existant at this property now, so it seems which is unfortunate. I noticed the lack of assistance in that department over the weekend and it was sad to see that such a needed position was not be executed properly. The concierge I asked 1 question to seriously told me "I don't know" and never even bothered to find an answer...wow.
Pro's: Lovely rooms in the tower and Marina Suites, nice bathroom amenities, comfy bed, decor was nice and clean, beautiful grounds and views..location..location..location
Con's: lack of concierge, front desk knowledge and help, minimal restaurant choices, expensive room service compared to quality of food

title: “Best of Boston!”
text:
I can't even begin to say how much I love this place!
It's so cozy, the staff is diligent, you cannot beat the location and I wish I could go back more often. They are so accommodating and pet friendly! Our dog Lily loved traveling with us and I'm sure it's the nicest hotel she'll ever stay at too!

title: “Nice Hotel Close to Everything”
text: We just came back from spending the weekend at the Hilton Garden Inn in Inner Harbor Baltimore Maryland. The hotel is in walking distance to everything and the water taxi is right down the street if you don't want to walk to the aquarium etc. The bed was very comfortable and the room was pretty large with nice big bathroom too. The only complaint I will make is that during out whole stay here we never got cleaning service. It would of been nice to have our bed made and fresh towels on Saturday upon returning from the day exploring Baltimore. Also I would recommend that you do not eat breakfast (unless of course it is free w your stay, which it was for us) at the hotel. They charge 12.99 per person for the breakfast and it was definitely not worth it. There are so many other place you can walk to right in the area and get a delicious breakfast/brunch paying half the price. We would stay there again though since it is close to everything and a nice clean hotel.

title: “Can't Beat the Location”
text: The Hilton Gaslamp is a wondersful small hotel in comparison to the massive Marriott and Grand Hyatt. Contempory desigh throughout. Its location far surpasses any of the others in regards to proxmity to the Gas Lamp Quarter. The hotel sits at the foot of 5th Ave which is packed with resturants and shops. So after your conference you have any only to go out the front door of the hotel and you have alot to do and chose from. The hotel sits across the tracks from the conference center which means it take all of 5 minutes to get to your session. Our room looked out over the pool and across the tracks to the conference center. The Trains and there noise did not disturb us at all. The frieght trains only ran once in the morning and once in the early evening.Outstanding bed, too comforatable. Large room decorated nicely with an easy chair and lamp along with a study desk. Plenty of towels, they provided even more very quickly upon request. Good sized brightly lite bathroom with plently of hot water. The staff were very friendly and helpfull with directions and information. Have breakfast at Richards Pancake House.

title: “Edison hotel time sq”
text:
"Hell is murky, and all the devils are in it" I luckily managed to get a room upgrade easily so do ask for one if unhappy. (had booked queen- size revamped room...got a dungeon! ) .Reception staff seem to be on some kind of anti-depressants on the whole...glazed eyes and confused expressions tinged with a hint of annoyance. security men are great though.
Great pianist in the bar, which was cozy and atmospheric. My upgraded room was a dream! My original dungeon was a thing that will haunt me forever though. Great location, nice lobby area, good shop and deli attached. Just stick up for yourself if you do stay there, and you will be fine. Had to fight through Expedia for my refund for swapping a night due to flight delay. Reception staff seemed deliberatley obstructive in regard to this and denied ever hearing about my 24 hr flight delay!

title: “Same old hotel”
text:
I stayed at this location many moons ago but I really don't remember the last time. What I remember is that the entrance to this hotel wasn't as crazy. 
Because the hotel stands at the corner of Harbor blvd and PHW, there is no entrance from PHW, so you have to turn right to Harbor first then make a u turn. This was annoying to me. The parking is valet only and it costs $30, but I guess other hotels charge pretty similar prices.
The hotel itself is just another Embassy Suites. I was only staying one night so I didn't use any facilities. I would stay for a business trip again.

title: “Perfect location to everything!”
text:
My husband and I went to San Francisco to celebrate our Anniversary. We loved the location of the hotel to the wharf because it was an easy walking distance. The F Line was right around the corner which took us down the the Ferry Building and the Bart line. 
We never had to rent a car with the easy access from the hotel to everything.
The hotel had an incredible free breakfast buffet, rooms were clean and staff very helpful and friendly.
The Wine Country Tour was a lot of fun with a shuttle from the Ferry Building and then a ferry back. A full day of history of SF and areas to the first stop to wonderful knowledge of wine making. V'Lattui a must!
We had an amazing trip!

title: “Westwood Winner”
text: Stayed at the Hotel Palomar in Westwood for three nights earlier this month for a business trip and absolutely loved it. Got a great rate for a comfortable, clean, and stylish room. Staff is especially eager to help without coming off condescending or pretentious. Especially loved the free happy hour (they were generous with the wine pours!) and the iPod docking station/alarm clock. Since I was here on business, the free internet access was also appreciated. Unfortunately, I didn't bring a camera to take pictures of the place to attach to this review, but actually, I think the pictures they have on their website are very accurate.

title: “Like Kimpton but disappointed by Ink 48”
text:
Booked Ink 48 through Snique Away. We like the Kimpton brand very much. Ink 48 has some things going for it but some things going against it. Overall we were disappointed with the Ink 48 and would recommend it only with caveats, e.g., probably not a good hotel for first-time visitors to NYC, anyone with mobility issues, or anyone who is concerend about dark streets in a somewhat transitional area. 
For: Modern hotel with contemporary furnishings and finishings. Great service - friendly, knowledeable and professional - as we have found typical of Kimpton hotels. "Print" restaurant is very good and realistically priced for dinner. The rooftop bar is a fun and vibrant place to go for a drink, particularly if the weather permits being outside. Price was good through Snique Away. 
Against: Location is the biggest drawback - it simply isn't convenient as has been mentioned in several other reviews. Subway is about 10 minute walk thorugh an area in transition (car dealerships, repair shops, halfway houses). Same for getting to Restaurant Row and theatres. There is nothing close by for breakfast so you're captive to the hotel restaurant.
We booked a "City View Premier King Room" based on the Kimpton's website photos. We were assigned room 602 which did not look like their photos, specifically the window was half the width of the one pictured and there was no seating area apart from one lounge chair despite their pictures suggesting there was another small seatng bench / loveseat. The room was large, but most of the space was taken up by the entry and an overly large bathroom - the bed and sitting area were quite small. Our room appeared to be an afterthought in the conversion of a former industrial building to a hotel. Disappointing
The one redeeming thing about the location is that it is quiet. And the bed was very comfortable making for a good night's sleep

title: “Staff was great, beautiful room/suite, great location for theatre lovers.”
text:
We stayed from May 25th thru May 29th. When we arrived we were a bit disoriented upon arrival to the 7th floor lobby. It Is quite dark, and we had to orient ourselves. Our flight was a morning flight, and we arrived early in the day. We left our luggage there, and they said they would call when our room was ready. We went out exploring, and we soon rec'd a phone call that our room was ready. We rec'd a room called a "cool" room or something like that. It was a corner room with spectacular views. We had booked our room with Amex Platinum Travel, and we would have rec'd an upgrade if one had been available. The room was a bit small, but then again, we are in NYC. After two nights we were upgraded to a suite on the 44th floor. Gorgeous! Oh my gosh! It was so spacious. We saw four plays in three days, and we went to the Intrepid Museum, just never stopped. It was so nice to come back to the room, and kick back. 
I loved the Bliss bath products. I missed having a bathtub. Only showers here.
Ate at the Blue Fin restaurant, which is part of the hotel property. Food was very good. 
This hotel is centrally located in the theatre district area. Expect some noise from the outside just because you are in the MIDDLE OF NYC. No big deal.
Our room was sparkling clean. Housekeeping staff did a wonderful job.
Shout out to Francis at the front desk for taking such good care of us.
Nice that there is a Starbucks right across the street.
Will definitely return to this hotel

title: “A great boutique hotel”
text: I recently spent five nights here while visiting San Francisco. It reminded me of a small hotel I stayed at in Paris. The staff is efficient, and courteous. I was assisted in getting a cab and making airport van connections. The restaurant was quaint with beautiful decor. Breakfast simple yet sufficient. This hotel is the best kept secret in San Francisco. Clean, neat with great customer service. I will be staying here again on my next visit.

title: “Wonderful Experience”
text: It was small, clean and quiet! I felt like I was on vacation even though I was there for work. The staff was friendly, and everything was clean. For the price, it was a wonderful place!

title: “Very good location for a cheap hotel”
text: If you want to party in NYC then this hotel is just right. You dont have to worry about spending much time in your hotel because you won't want to. However, if you are just looking for a place to sleep you can not beat the location and cheap price of this hotel. I liked staying here because we were there to enjoy the city and not spend much time in the hotel. Our room was not very cozy or clean but hey for $100 in Times Square what do you expect?

title: “If you liked the Shining - stay here”
text: It's obvious the place has history - just go to the second floor and walk around unlit banquet rooms furnished with weathered leather, dark walnuts and smoke stained carpets. Might be a great place for a murder/mystery deal - but for you family and/or business travelers - not a chance.

title: “NICE HOTEL IN PHX”
text:
Good Hotel, food, gym, swimming pool
helpful staff
free shuttle services
very good location
reasonable price

title: “Luxurious yet warm and welcoming”
text: The Brown Palace is a hotel that exemplifies luxury and comfort. The rooms are beautifully decorated and the attention to detail in style and cleanliness is impeccable. Everyone we came into contact with at the hotel was friendly and eager to help. I also loved the central downtown location as you can walk or take a short cab ride to several of Denver's attractions. I will definitely be returning to this hotel when I need a place to stay in Denver.

title: “Hate to say it - BED BUGS - Seriously.”
text: My husband and I stayed at this Hotel in 2007, while on a "mini vacation" we had also stayed at other Hotels during this trip. 6 weeks later I had to visit my Doctor because of a rash on my shoulders, and arms. I had Scabies (Bed Bugs) the first thing my Doctor ask was "Have you stayed in a Hotel, or Motel in the past 6 weeks?" Since we had stayed at other Hotels I was not convinced of where I had picked up the Bed Bugs. Flash Forward; November 2009 my husband had a convention that was scheduled at Hilton Palacio del Rio, so that is where we stayed. Wrong choice 6 weeks later guess what Bed Bugs AGAIN! I can seriously say that we love staying at Hilton Hotels but Hilton Palacio del Rio is out of the question in the future. Sorry.

title: “A bit disappointed - expected more from Sheraton”
text: I spent 5 nights there. I rated this hotel with just 3/5 stars as I think you have a right to expect more from this chain. The most annoying was problems with internet – any browser couldn’t open the login site, neither from laptop nor smartphone.
