I finally called quest service, they transfer me to external tech-support company and I spent like 20 minutes with very nice guy who helped me login into internet.. But it shouldn’t be like that. Then breakfast – you pay like 20USD for buffet but the choice was very limited. So for me – another “-”. Location – if you are going to visit Universal City or Hollywood – very good choice (one stop by metro from Hollywood blvd. – Kodak Theatre). If Santa Monica or downtown – take another one. Be aware – 100% no smoking hotel. There was also strike of some employees during my stay - just in front of the hotel – bit loud … but ok, it happens - appreciated that the hotel manager addressed quests with letter explaining situation and apologies. So generally – hotel ok, but from Sheraton you expect more…

title: “Always a pleasure”
text: While travelling on business I have stayed at several hotels in Philadelphia, however the Park Hyatt remains my favorite. The location is excellent and the sevice is professional. The mix of the old world charm and modern amenities make you feel as if you were in a cloistered hideaway. Simple elegance at its best.

title: “Recommended”
text:
The Marriott at SEATAC is a perfectly acceptable, completely average Marriott property. Good, expensive restaurants, accurate, pleasant staff, accommodations acceptable without being outstanding in any way.
Marriott offers internet connections at an outrageous price - similar to its competition. All hotels should get with the program of complimentary internet connections.

title: “Great stay at RB Inn and Spa”
text: Myhusband surprised me for my birthday with a stay at the Rancho Bernardo Inn. Even though we live in San Diego, I felt like I was on vacation. Great service, excellent food and a beautiful property...very quiet and relaxing. We also enjoyed first rate spa services at their beautiful spa that has one of the most gorgeous pools and cabana setups I have ever seen at a spa. In addition, our massages were done in private Japanese style houses. The following morning our children joined us for our Thanksgiving dinner on the Veranda. Overall, it exceeded my expectations and I would recommend it to anyone - whether for business or for pleasure.

title: “Convenient downtown hotel”
text: Convenient location at a moderate price. Includes breakfast. The good news it is free. It is not much. Towels are thin. Air conditioner is noisy. Rooms are very generous in size. Two flat screens. Free internet; good connection. Refrigerator, microwave, desk.If you need a generous space for a business trip. Pool and Jacuzzi were nice. Exercise room is not much but I was the only one there.

title: “Perfect space for wedding or an event”
text:
I've hosted a marketing summit at The Blackstone the past two years. I have been completely happy with every aspect of the event from working with Ashley, the amazing event director who was great at helping to create the perfect event to Swank AV who went above the call of duty to make sure the sound and AV went off without a hitch to the support staff that almost magically appeared whenever I needed them.
The crystal ballroom is BEAUTIFUL and the perfect backdrop for a wedding. I would highly recommend this venue for any event

title: “Park et Fly great experience”
text: Convenient location right off of rt 36; very clean facility; staff are awesome. The gentleman i spoke with when making reservation was "very" helpful et when we arrived everything was taken care of including notation of when we needed shuttle to airport et when we were arriving. Everyone was on time. Our flight was delayed coming home(1:00am)et i called to let them know--very nice with no problems. The driver on the return trip was great--friendly et helpful AND this is my first experience on an airport shuttle when the shuttle was actually warm et we have had many many other experiences. Thank you! We would return here without any reservation at all!!

title: “Perfect Location”
text:
The hotel decor is a little tired, but the room was spacious by NYC standards.
Staff were friendly and helpful and answered all our needs.
There was no kettle or fridge in the room, but the hotel supplied a fridge for us on request.
Location is fantastic on 7th Avenue close to Central Park and Times Square.
We had an evening flight from NY, so we wanted the hotel room as late as possible. They willingly gave us a late checkout.
Note there is a charge for luggage storage of $3.75 per item (bit of a rip-off as I'm used to no charge storage)

title: “Nice room -- rude front desk staff”
text:
It was a very nice hotel, however the front desk staff was a bit stiff and rude. Although check-in didn't officially start until 3 pm, I arrived at 2:15 hoping for an available room. Even though I am 7 months pregnant and was in desperate need of some rest, the woman at the front desk told me there wasn't a single room ready and under no circumstance could she give me a room 45 minutes early. So, I sat in the lobby until 3 pm when she let me know a room was ready. The whole thing was really disappointing.
Other than that, the room was nice and clean.
Valet guys were super nice and effecient. I wish they were running the front desk!!

title: “The real Fawlty Towers!”
text: Stayed two nights at this hotel after a very long flight across the pacific. The front desk concierge (male) and entire hotel is exactly like Fawlty Towers. The concierge guy cannot understand any accent other than American (we're aussies), the bed was way too soft and we both slept like a banana and leaning into each other because there was no give, bathroom is the size of a coffin, and the breakfast is great if you like eating sugar and pastry. It gets a bit warm but if you open the windows, it can be a bit noisy. Good location though and it has tea and coffee making facilities in the lobby.

title: “Wonderful location. Wonderful price. 1st class stay!”
text:
The Fitzpatrick Grand Central was one of the best hotels i have stayed at. The staff was beyond helpful. The room was cozy and the bed was a cloud. LOVE IT. The location was GREAT. We walked to times square regularly. Very close to theaters as well.
STAY HERE! YOU WONT BE SORRY :)

title: “Not as cool as they think they are”
text: I'm not that demanding for hotel rooms. This place was very hip, but I would like (a) a working shower, (b) a toilet that flushes without having to reach into the tank, (c) an outlet to charge my laptop while I sleep. The shower controls were almost falling off (the water volume control didn't work at all), the toiilet didn't flush without manually opening the tank and fiddling with the valve, and the handset on the in-room phone didn't work. To their credit, they were apologetic and offered me a free breakfast if I stayed with them again, but I won't be doing that.

title: “stay was very nice”
text:
rooms were nicely done. This place has an amazing history. Loved everything about it.
Rooms were not the largest but plenty of room for 2 people to enjoy.

title: “Nice little hotel with great location and price”
text:
This hotel is less than one block east of the Magnificent Mile (Michigan Ave) and within walking distance of many attractions such as the Navy Pier, Millenium Park and the Art Institute. It was three blocks to the "L" Red Line which we took to the Cubs games. 
The decor was nice, the beds were comfortable, everything was clean, and the staff were friendly and helpful. The bathrooms were small, but the size of our rooms was more than sufficient. The elevators were also quite small, but there were three of them, so we never had long to wait. This was just what our family needed for a busy four days in the heart of this amazing city. There were coffee shops and restaurants on every block, and we walked 3 blocks to Yolk on Grand & McClurg every morning for a great breakfast.
Wifi was free in the lobby, but cost about $15/day in the room. We paid for one day and otherwise managed quite well in the comfortable lobby.

title: “Great Evening”
text: Had a great meal at the St Regis restaurant and had impeccable service from Mateo and Marisol. They were both attentive knowledgable and courteous. They made my date feel special and catered to her every need. It was a great start to the evening which ended just as well. I highly recommed the waitstaff and the creative food on the menu. Hats off to the chef as well.

title: “Awesome stay, but poor water pressure!”
text: I booked this hotel because it was convenient from the airport and not too far from my future-in-grandmother-in-law's house. After reading reviews online, I made sure to ask for a top floor room, which we weren't guaranteed because apparently the third floor is reserved for flight crews. When we arrived we learned we were able to get on the top floor (YAY!). The front desk was polite, although it took her awhile to check us in and give us our room keys. She also had a large tattoo on her right arm, which doesn't bother us, but could bother some. The room was very nice, clean, and much bigger than expected. The bed was comfortable enough, although we both woke up with stiff backs. The water pressure in the shower was practically non-existent and it took almost 20 minutes to rinse my hair. Breakfast was good, but the "hot" items were actually cold. I LOVED the Texas-shaped waffles! I didn't get a chance to use the pool although it looked SO inviting and was empty every time we saw it. Overall, our stay was great!

title: “Great place to stay if you want to do things in Hollywood!”
text:
I really had a good experience at this hotel. The only complaint I have is that the comforter had some non-removable stains but the bed itself and bathroom were clean aside from that. There was not a lot of noise in the area even though it's in busy Hollywood. I was able to rest well. Restaurants around the area are good and the location is perfect and non-expensive for exploring the Hollywood area.
I give this place a thumbs up if you are traveling in Hollywood and want a non-expensive place. Priceline.com gave me a good $55.00 a night deal for this hotel. My stay extended for 4 nights.

title: “good stay and good time”
text: my atay at the residence inn was wonderfull, great attentive staff with a clean room . I loved the fitness center and was impressed how prompt housekeeping was when i called the front desk for some trash bags and within minutes they were knocking on my door with them. To park your vehicle in their garrage was a little pricey, but that was my only gripe. Loved it and will go back.

title: “Needs refershing...”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for a family wedding. The location is very good, the rooms are spacious but seem very stale and in need of updating. The staff were helpful and pleasant. I suppose the thing that summed up our stay was the fact that there was a room service tray on the floor outside the room when i checked in on Friday and on Sunday, it was still there, prompting me to call the front desk to ask if it was part of the decor. It quickly disappeared at that point. That's a sign of pretty sloppy management in a hotel in my view.
The gym is quite small though reasonably equipped. It was far too warm for working out and no a/c control was in sight to adjust it, so I propped it open with a towel to let the cool air in from outside (it was in the 50's the weekend we were there). I just do not understand the concept of $12 parking at a suburban hotel with tons of space. Note to management: Just increase the rate and include it. You basically need a car to get to this property and to go anywhere once you are there. This annoyance has spread from downtown properties where parking is a problem and the fees can be justified to the 'burbs nation wide. 
The wedding by the way was great, but that had little to do with the hotel.
This Crowne Plaza was not of the overall high standard we have experienced at other properties of this chain. New decor, beds and a general sprucing up along with some management discipline and tweaking of service could easily turn this into the 4-star and up experience that many others in the chain deliver.

title: “Horrible, Horrible, Horrible”
text: Where do I begin. We are definitely not picky travelers but this hotel took us to our limits. First, upon entering the hotel we were greeted with a long line and a forty minute wait to simply check in to our room. Once inside the room, there were no towels and the bed was lacking a blanket of all things! The room was dark, there were stains everywhere (especially in the hallways), and it looked like one of the lamp shades may have caught fire at one time. Our view consisted of garbage that was thrown on the roof. The next morning we woke to a church service across our hall that was extremely loud. To top it off, we each had to take a shower without hot water. When checking out, we discovered that we were not the only ones who had issues with the hotel. When one man complained about the cold showers, the attendant said, "that seems to always happen when we have a full house." Run, don't walk away from the Holiday inn- city center in Columbus. Spend your money wisely and go anwyhere else!

title: “Great 9 nights spent, great location and friendly staff.”
text: Stayed in this hotel for 9 nights and after staying in several others I must say it was an enjoyable stay. The location is perfect just 2 blocks off Central Park on 7th avenue. The room was nice and spacious and was clean. The staff were particularly friendly and went out of their way on occasions more so Ricky ( Ricardo Alvarez) in reception. I would recommend this to anyone staying in NY, it's good value.

title: “Excellent Service”
text: The physical attributes of the hotel were amazing, everything was clean and felt like walking through an art gallery, but the service was outstanding. Employees treated me and my girlfriend as if we were their personal friends...knew our names and were very considerate! A must visit!

title: “Nice but not 5-star”
text: We stayed the beginning of December 2004. Pleasant and helpful staff. They made a mistake in booking a popular restaurant arranged 2 weeks in advance of our visit but corrected graciously. The lobby is small with tasteful, modern style and expected displays of theater pieces. No pool and meager exercise room. We chose the deluxe room facing the city (#709). There is a bit of traffic noise even that high up. Possibly the mountain view would be better for traffic noise control. The room was small/average size with modern touches including sofa and lounge chair. Very large drafty windows but great, expansive views. Large marble-tiled bathroom with deep spa-like soaking tub and spa shower. Missing a few small details such as non-working sink-stop and slowing draining sink. Also, the shower door when opened would hit the rain shower spout. Engineering eventually came to remedy some of the problems. Very comfortable bed with high thread count linens. The two adjoining restaurants looked fantastic but did not imbibe. A short stroll to Lodo and Larimer Square make this a great location. Complimentary Cadillac Escalade driver is available. Pricey at $295 per night but overall a nice but not perfect experience. A top 5 choice in Denver.

title: “Best place to stay in Auatin!”
text:
The Wyndham Garden Hotel in Austin is the best place to stay while in the Austin area. The Hotel has the Live Music Theme going on!!
The Folks who work here treat you like family! 
Say Hello to Cassandra/Manager for me! She can give you the 411 on all activities taking place in Austin at the time.

title: “A very good budget option”
text:
I spent 1 night in the hotel and was pleasantly surprised. The hotel is well located and easy to get everywhere from. Room was basic but very clean and for $120 for an en suite room in NYC excellent value for money.As a female travelling alone I felt very safe.
Staff were continually friendly and helpful, offering to help me carry my case up the stairs which was kind and unexpected!
The only negative point is that there was a lot of street noise - I will definitely bring ear plugs next time I stay!

title: “Don't Be Deterred By The Noise”
text:
We booked a cruise and stay package and were slightly concerned when we discovered that we were staying at the Hilton Millenium after reading the many reviews commenting on the noise from the reconstruction of the WTC. 
Yes their was some noise but this was more than offset by the wonderful views over the Hudson River and the superb sunsets.
Rooms are comfortable and well furbished and staff were friendly and helpful. We normally enjoy eating and drinking in the hotel in which we stay but prices were exhorbitant so ate out instead.
Although in downtown Mnahattan the Hilton Millenium is only a 20 minute subway ride to Times Square and a 10 minute walk from Seaport which has some excellent eateries and pubs.
All in all a very enjoyable experience.

title: “Fashion Week beehive”
text: If you are doing anything at Lincoln Center this is the place to stay. For Fashion Week it was the hub of activity. It has a lovely bar area on the mezzanine and is next door to a stunning rooftop bar/pool area that has a forever present waiting line to get in. Only blocks away from a walk in Central Park, Columbus Circle, Mandarin Oriental Hotel and Robert's and Museum of Arts and Design.

title: “Nice place but horrible room”
text:
The main building (lobby) was lovely and this is a charming property, but I experienced several problems that made my stay unpleasant.
First, I had to park in a lot across the alley because special event tents were set up in the inn's parking spots. Second, my room--first floor of John R. Carriage House near that building's entrance--was a nightmare. It is right next to a busy street. Also, there is a door inside this room (not the actual door that you use to enter the room) that opens out to the street-side front porch. The deadbolt wasn't locked, and the staff couldn't find the key to lock it. The windows weren't secured in any way either, and one of them had a crack in it. I did not feel safe at all, even though the staff assured me that I had nothing to worry about. Couldn't change rooms because everything was booked.
Finally, it was freezing in the room, which didn't seem to have any heat. I had to have the staff bring me a space heater (was supposed to be in the closet but wasn't).
The manager was nice and comped me one night for these issues, which I appreciated. I just want to warn others about the drawbacks of my particular room. Avoid it, and I think you'll like this place!

title: “PLEASE LISTEN TO THE WARNINGS FOR THE SAFETY OF YOUR FAMILY”
text: I just want to start off by saying that we did have fun for the most part in the waterpark. We decided to get away for Labor Day weekend. Our two year old is sick and getting surgery in a day and we all needed a break and thought Fort Rapids was the place to go. Boy, were we wrong. I explained the need for a clean room over the phone after I saw the reviews on line. There was a note on the account and when we got there, the nice lady who checked us in ran up there to check the room. She assured us it was clean and everything woul be okay. The room was fun and a cute theme. I went into the restroom. It was a complete nightmare. There was hair in tub, dried gel on the counter and feces on the toilet seat. We promptly got dressed and went down to the pool area. It was perfect for my two and six year old. Older kids would not really enjoy it as there are only 3 slides for them. The lifeguards are not very attentive or helpful. Two of the big slides dump into the lazy river, so often, you will get people that are running through trying to get up, usually they are polite and just pass by. Then, a group of 4 kept pushing through everyone and came to us. We were so pushed up into another group and they could not pass. Instead of waiting, they kept pushing into us and laughing. It had turned into a terrible game of bumper boats and I was not enjoying it. They bumped my two year old's head so hard of the side of the river that she was crying and bit her lip. I asked them very politely to stop and they started screaming profanities. The lifeguards just asked them to keep it down. They called my family every name in the book and followed us around the park. Finally, I had enough and yelled back (not one of my finer moments in life). Needless to say, we checked out and went to the WONDERFUL AND CLEAN hotel across the street. To sum it up; terrible food, rude staff, DIRTY DIRTY outdated unkept hotel. Even outside was gross. The weeds are very over run and the fountain in the front was broken and full of dirty stagnant water. I know that there are people that love this place, but there are also people that have horror stories. I honestly do not know how this place passes any health code checks. Please save yourself some time and money and look else where.

title: “Great location”
text:
Wonderful, central location. Take a walk up the hill to the park, etc. Hotel food service is a bit blah, but there are so many great places to eat that the hotel food should not even be considered! The rooms were clean and fairly spacious, the hotel is undergoing a renovation and looks great! There US a hospital nearby, so light sleepers beware sirens are noisy, on the upside, quality care is always nearby! 
If you are driving parking is an additional $40 a day in a nearby parking garage...not a good deal really. 
Overall a pretty decent hotel for the money, location is the main draw.

title: “Good Value”
text: This place is nothing fancy, but is in a great location in Chinatown and the subway is 100 yards from the front door. Clearly a 2 star property in terms of services (of lack there of). However, room was very clean, the 1 person at the front desk was very friendly and helpful, and all of the fixtures were in good working order. The 30" flat panel TV seemed relatively new. I've seen older posts that the hallways were run down and the beds uncomfortable. However, that was not our experience. Both double beds in our room were comfortable and the hallways were clean and well kept. Perhaps there has been some recent renovation since those posts.

title: “Trendy hotel very close to Times Square”
text:
My wife and I spent a weekend in NYC and enjoyed our stay at the Room Mate Grace. However, like most hotel rooms in NYC, it was fairly small. However, we expected that, so that was ok. It's less than a block off Times Square and is very near the TKTS booth, in case you are looking for cheap, same-day theater tickets. 
Rooms: As I mentioned, the rooms are small (and clean) but are fairly trendy - as is the rest of the hotel. The rooms have no bathtubs but a very nice tiled shower instead. The shower and toilet are adjacent (but separated by a wall) and both use the same sliding door. When the door covers the shower, it does not cover the toilet area and vice versa. The room also had a safe that was big enough for a laptop, a small refrigerator, an iPod-compatible radio and free WiFi. It also included a small flat screen TV, which was installed on the wall, so that you can watch TV in bed. 
Exercise Room: Very small but included an exercise bike and weights. There were also a few small TVs in the room, attached to machines. The room overlooks 45th street but the windows are shaded for privacy. The room also includes a water cooler.
Food/Drink/Other: The hotel does not have a restaurant but they serve breakfast in an area dedicated for that. They serve coffee, toast/bagels, fruit, yogurt, etc. The front desk does sell a limited selection of snacks and drinks (including alcoholic drinks). There is a bar that is adjacent to the pool, which always appeared to be open. I think that you could even get a drink while in the pool. I didn't try out the pool or the bar but both looked nice. There was also a sauna/steam room just above the pool area. 
All in all, it was a very nice yet trendy hotel. Everything was very clean, which was great.

title: “Roomy with a View”
text:
When I decided to stay a couple of nights in Denver, i took in consideration the sites to see in Downtown and near the Convention Center area. The Clerk at the Front Desk was friendly, courteous and helpful. 
As I entered my room, I saw the King size bed, flat screen TV, and the large window. I loved the in-room safe as it held my 14-inch laptop. 
This hotel is next to the Convention Center (Love that 40 foot Blue Bear). Also, it is located one block from the 16th street mall. The also famous LoDo is a short bus ride along the 16th mall. I had gone to the jacuzzi which is located outdoor of the pool area. Since it was a warm morning, it was a nice time soaking in the Denver air. 
The first night, I had gone up to the Peak's Lounge for a better view of the Denver evening lights. I took a table next to the window, so I can enjoy what Denver had to offer. The waitresses were polite and friendly everytime I needed a drink or food service. 
The next morning I visited the Altitude Restaurant for Breakfast. Since this was a late breakfast the service was spot on. I wanted something different, so I ordered the Texas Benedict. Not getting into a food review, all I'll say is that I enjoyed it. 
The Strata Bar on the lobby floor was just as inviting as the Peaks Lounge. The plus here is that you can connect to the free WiFi while enjoying a drink, coctail or coffee. 
I enjoyed my stay at the Hyatt Regency Denver, that when I return, I will stay here again.

title: “Great little motel!”
text:
We stayed here on one of the many stops of our trip and was very impressed with this little motel.
Clean and bright, the rooms are small but are perfectly serviceable because when your San Diego - what are you doing in your room?! The shower though was fabulous!
Free intermittent wi-fi, we didn't try breakfast so cannot comment on that. The harbour outside is lovely and within driving distance to the Old Town which is a must see in San Diego.

title: “Great Customer Service”
text: This motel is a great place to stay with excellant customer service by the managers at the hotel. They are now a Super 8 motel and have many amenities to offer to tell you honestly. They offer free wireless internet, free continental breakfast and they truly do care about their customers. Great place to stay..

title: “One Night Anniversary Treat”
text:
My wife and I live in Brooklyn and for our 2nd anniversary we decided to spend a night in the city at a top hotel. We decided on the Mandarin because we have never even been to the Time Warner center and knew the Mandarin was the newest luxury hotel in the city. While the prices were way high we decided if we are going to do this lets go all out. When we booked the room there was a glitch in the pricing system and all rooms were going for $166. We decided to book right away and see if they would honor it. They did not but did offer up upgrades in class of room if we bought a standard rate. We did this and got a premiere Central Park view room for standard room price - still thats $750 for one night. We also got 20% discount on all spa activities although we had no plans on doing that.
We checked in Friday at 3pm - took the elevator to the 35th floor to the elegant lobby. Our room was ready and check in was very fast. We then took the guest-only elevators (key cards required to operate) to our room on the 52 floor. The floor hallways are very tastefully done, best I have ever seen, and we proceeded to our room.
The room was also very elegantly designed and felt very new. While the room was not large the bed was quite comfortable as was the large ottoman by the window. The view was great although obstructed by the Trump Hotel across the street. Still we could see most of the park and up Central Park South - quite attractive. The bathroom was big. We loved the soaking tub and the shower which has a rainshower feature where the water comes pouring out of a large multi-hole showerhead fixed in the ceiling.
When I booked I informed the reservations agent it was our anniversary and the hotel delivered complimentary champagne, cake and chocolates that evening - a very thoughtful gesture that made us feel special.
In the afternoon we used the pool which is nice but more for doing laps than relaxing but still there was only one person in it besides us so we enjoyed the 30 minutes we stayed.
As an extra treat we saw Lance Armstrong in the elevator on our way to dinner
The bed was very comfortable for sleeping that night.
The next morning we had room service deliver breakfast. This was the only major disappointment of the stay. The eggs were watery and a glass of apple juice was $8 EACH!. We should have bought apple juice at the Duane Reade across the street and kept it for the morning. The $70 breakfast was not worth it.
All in all while this was a very expensive 24 hours but as a one-time-only treat we had a great time and felt adequately pampered. Im sure there are better hotels values in NYC but I'm not sure they can all provide the same level of luxury.

title: “Great location and good value if your expectations aren't too high...”
text:
Stayed 3 nights here and have no issues recommending it for a family type vacation. 
The Good:
- Stayed Wed-Fri nights, booked and paid for a Std Rm, was upgraded to a partial ocean without asking... nice.
- got $150 discount for a 3 night stay through the Blue Sea Website only (... not on the BW Corp website)
- Very comfortable beds (had two Queens in our room)
- 1st floor partial ocean view rooms had a very large patio area (smaller balconies for the upper rooms) 
- Ample parking (which is hard to come by in that area) with their two parking lots and underground garage.
- Clean rooms, grounds, and pool area.
- Free WiFi worked flawlessly
The not so good:
- Parking spots were all compact... most large sedans/trucks spilled over to the adjacent spot (typical was 2 cars for every 3 spots). No complaints from Mgt so no issue.
- TV remote didn't work so had go old school and push the buttons on the actual tv :-)
- Bathroom bulb was going out... sometimes the bathroom had light, sometimes it was dim and flickery... didn't bother me enough to call for maintenance... told the front desk when i left.

title: “Quality hotel in the heart of it”
text: We came here the middle of an ice age -15+ windchil jan2011l. The hotel was our salvation. Beautiful comfy rooms overlooking times square 2 x king size beds. Not massive room but fine. Hotel areas were nice, cool lounge playing chilled musics and a bar restaurant with an awesome view over times square. Couldn't be more central so as soon as you step out you are in the thick of it. The perfect base for exploring on foot

title: “where the beautiful people stay”
text: This hotel is one of those places that makes you feel stylish just by being there. It is very styled, the way that most W Hotels are, but it still has a bit of the Seattle vibe. The location is great, esp. if you are there for business or high-end shopping. The in-house restaurant is pricey and has some weird hours, but the food is pretty good. The rooms were very comfortable and the Bliss products are a nice touch.

title: “Great value in a well designed setting”
text:
The Andaz is a new brand from Hyatt Hotels, and it reflects their collective expertise in hospitality. The San Diego Andaz used to be the Ivy Hotel, so it is in a building with true architectural history, but that has been sensitively and artfully renovated. It is located in San Diego's very, very busy Gaslamp District, which is close to a sports stadium and the convention center.
Andaz makes effective use of technology and the check in process is smooth and fast; in fact, you can check in ahead of arrival if you want to, and just pick up your room key when you get there. Guests are greeted by hosts with iPads, all of whom were quite gracious, though probably could use a little more training about when to stop talking. (Ours even said, "maybe I'm giving you more information than you want...")
One of the most impressive elements of the decor is a sophisticated incorporation of the arts. Even the area rugs on every floor were custom weaves based on art. There's a captivating modernist mural on the main floor that managed to be edgy and sweet at once.
We booked a suite for $340/night. It had a wholly separate living room and a flatscreen TV in both rooms, which seemed a little like over-kill to us but probably appealing to the sports fans that swarm the Gaslamp District. Andaz offers complimentary soft drinks in the minibar and ice on every floor. The living room furniture was a little bit of a mishmash; it looked as though it started midcentury modern and then they decided they need a more comfortable sofa, too, and added it.
The bathrooms were spacious and attractively designed. They have large walk in showers but no tubs. The amenities were high quality.
The bed was simple and comfortable. The closet was located in the living room rather than the bedroom, which was neither ideal nor an insurmountable problem.
The food service options in-house were limited. There is 24 hour room service and breakfast and lunch on the roof until 2pm. The only dinner option on property is Katsuya, a sushi restaurant designed by Phillippe Stark and owned by SBE, an LA-based company with a distinctly nightlife cant. The space was large yet beautifully designed and the sushi was excellent, but this isn't a place for a quiet dinner after a long flight.
There is also a nightclub on premises and it is LOUD. There is heavy security on Friday and Saturday nights because of the club but it did little to control the room pounding noise from loud guests screaming in the halls and elevator and even louder music. In fact, the host even said when we arrived, "we can't promise it will be quiet but let us know if you want to change rooms." Sleeping was not easy.
The Andaz San Diego on the weekends is probably most perfect for 20- and 30-somethings who are using they rooms as luggage storage while they party all night or hook up destinations. We liked it a lot but regretted how little sleep we got.

title: “Luxury at the Big House”
text: We stopped at the Liberty Hotel over the Labor Day weekend on the way to a mid-week vacation at a B & B on Cape Cod. We can endorse this hotel on any number of levels. The first is the fact it is a converted jail. That quirky setting prompted us to stop there in the first place. It truly is a visually stunning make-over and the pictures and video documenting the work are worth watching. Have no idea if the original folks checking into said establishment were as impressed with the atrium as we were, but they might not have been into sightseeing like we were. Words like wow cannot do it justice. However the reason for coming back to this lockup for future visits to Boston would stem from the friendly staff (at check in, at the alibi bar, at curbside, etc) and the close to everything location. The nearby Paramount was an absolute hit for breakfast and we owe that referral to the safffers working the front door. Since we had confirmed reservations out on the cape, we had no choice but to leave or we would have gladly stayed for a longer sentence.

title: “Great Room, Great View”
text: Tremendous location with view of the original Washington Monument and park. One block from the Walter's Museum and the Peabody Institute. The staff was extremely helpful with computer, transportation and directions.

title: “Excellent Value”
text: I spent two nights in a studio suite. The hotel is old, but clean and comfortable. I was on the sixth floor and had a nice view of downtown and could even see the distant lights of Tijuana. The suite was spacious with a large bedroom/sitting area, large walk-in closet, small bathroom, a small dining area, and a cramped kitchen. The bed was comfortable and had a nice comforter. The bathroom looked old and worn and the kitchen was not much better, but the towels were oversized and quite plush. The complimentary breakfast was small and modest, but still a nice way to get a cup of coffee early in the morning. I had two dinners at the hotel's Inn at the Park restaurant and both were excellent. The food was well-prepared, the service top-notch, and the evening entertainment (a lounge act singing showtunes) was delightful. The rooftop deck was closed for renovation, but I had been up there a number of times in the past and can attest to it offering some of the finest views of San Diego. Overall, the Park Manor Suites are an excellent value for those travelers who want close proximity to Balboa Park and downtown San Diego and are willing to forgo some luxury.

title: “Happy with the Newton”
text:
We stayed at the Newton for four nights while settling our daughter into Columbia University. It is only three subway stops from there and actually walking distance (mile and a half). 
Our room overlooked Broadway but not too much traffic at night so noise not a problem. Everything very clean, en suite bathroom modern and clean. Prompt and thorough maid service. The desk staff very friendly and helpful with maps, advice, directions etc. Quick subway ride to Times Square etc and sightseeing bus stops right outside. This is a great budget (although not so budget at the end of August) hotel with no frills. No complaints at all. What made our stay was the excellent Key West Diner next door which serves a good and very reasonable breakfast with great service. They offer room service to the hotel too although we didn't try that. Other interesting restaurants to be found close by on Amsterdam.

title: “Best hotel in IN!”
text: It was clean and modern. Liked the view from the room that I stayed. The staffs are very friendly. I will definitely stay in the Marriott again when I go visit in IN. The best hotel in IN!!!!!

title: “Best value for park and travel.”
text: My husband and I took advantage of the Double Tree park and travel package, when flying out of the San Jose airport for a business awards ceremony. The service throughout was fabulous. The convenience was great. The shuttle to and from the airport was very quick and efficient. We will stay at the Double Tree when flying out of San Jose in the future. The hotel was very clean and comfortable.

title: “Lovely. Plenty of room!”
text: This hotel is very elegant, very old New York and in a superb location. I love that they have left original architectural details from the past untouched while upgrading to the standards of today. The room was large by NYC standards and quite beautiful. The sheets, pillows and towels are great...very comfortable bed and linens. I highly recommend this, it really completes the NYC experience. Enjoy!

title: “Great for the price”
text: Hotel was great. Staff very friendly, free internet handy, elevator ancient but great music and very quirky. Everything was quite old, but everything worked and was very clean. Great location to, can definitely recommend.

title: “Elegant and modern”
text: Hotel with a nice modern style, helpful staff good location and good cocktails in the bar. Rooms small, but what do you expect in New York???

title: “Wonderful place, wonderful experienxe”
text: Thoroughly enjoyed our time at this wonderful, scenic and comfortable location. No real criticisms, just a great place. Can't wait to return.

title: “If you get the right room you would love this hotel but if you get a bad room it’s not a good place to stay”
text:
Our room did not look like the other photos on here so we must have been in one of the cheaper rooms, however we paid $104 a night when a few people are saying they only paid $60 a night.
The room was tiny! We usually stay in budget hotels but this was one of the worse rooms I have seen. The bathroom was also tiny with a small shower and toilet and the sink was in the bedroom. The room was also dated- old tv with no cable. We didn’t have breakfast included but had I think a 20% off voucher for Dave’s deli next door.
I think the worst thing had to be our toilet blocked and room service had came in to make the bed and did nothing about it so we couldn’t use the toilet for the rest of the trip.
It very noisy when the theatre came out after a show which was across the road and I think it was a garbage truck at around 6am every morning woke us up.
The good points were- the reception were friendly and helpful. They booked a minibus which was much cheaper than a taxi back to the airport for us. The location was great you could walk or get a cable car everywhere.
I think if you get the right room you would love this hotel but if you get a bad room it’s not a good place to stay.

title: “It's a winner!”
text:
Great hotel! Great location! 
But, that can be said of many Boston-area facilities.
The key to this one is the staff and their focus on service.
From the doorman to the front desk to the concierge to the
bartenders, they "get it."
Attentive, friendly and efficient -- and, always with a smile.
My next trip to Beantown is a "no-brainer."
In my book, the "C"-port gets an "A" !

title: “Fine hotel”
text:
This hotel is about 10-15mins walk from penn station/macys, and is quite OK. Service was excellent, and the rooms are nice and clean. The rooms are not very big, but I assume you get what you pay for. A/C in rooms but is very noisy. Flatscreen TV and Safe.
Overall a good hotel.

title: “Great Location, great concierge.”
text:
The hotel is well located for shops and tourist attractions. Concierge service, by Dale, was excellent.
Rooms clean and well appointed but our was tiny and had a window that gave us a view of another room (and their's our ours, I expect). Otherwise excellent spot.
Valet paking onsite offered but it is available cheaper locally. Large carpark next left parking for 24hr period $29.
Would highly recommend for a cheap stay in San Fran.

title: “Nice location”
text: My wife and I were in Seattle for a wedding and stayed in the hotel for two nights. The location is convenient with easy access to freeways and local attractions; a few blocks walk to downtown. The room was spacious, clean and quiet. The provided breakfast was very good. Parking is valet only and was $18 plus tax. We enjoyed an excellent dinner at the small "Place Pigalle" restaurant which is near the end of Pike Street (look for the large brass pig and you're very close).

title: “Very Good”
text: Stayed there 10/28 and 29th Room was very nice and reasonably prices Had a decent breakfast and very clean facuilty I have stayed in a lot more expensive hotels that was not nearly as nice. Room had mini fridge, micro, coffee pot along with a nice sitting area.

title: “dressed up motel”
text:
There seem to be two types of room, double queen bed which is just about right proportioned (furniture:room ratio) and king bed with smaller room, and that was what I stayed, furnitures & fixtures are obviously too large for the room and very little space left even for only one person. Something always blocking my way so moved it or moved around. This is upgraded property from the old motel, and it is still pretty much a motel no matter how you look, a nicer & newer kind of motel room may be. Almost everything in the room looked reasonably new and modern, only exception was TV which was last decade leftover. 
Stayed on 5th floor, only one elevator serving so this was everyday problem, slow and inadequate. Also there is open air penthouse bar on the 5th, not far away from the room so this could be noisy and no privacy. (there are corridor window which everyone kept them shut) , hotel is very near the landing path of nearby airport so it could be noisy at time. few sea view room on the 5th or 4th should be among the first choice.
Staff were helpful and friendly, boutique style lobby was attractive and nice but has nothing to do nor correlation with how the room looked. Location is near little Italy as everyone said but there are also many other choices at the same price. Parking is potential problem whenever occupancy hits 60% plus. Shuttle service available to the airport and zoo,etc. looked nice but didn't use so cannot comment.
Overall this is unique, if you want to try to stay in modern/very clean motel then this should be good. The rate we've got at the time of stay was not very attractive so might not come back as said, there are many other choices...

title: “Good value for Chicago !”
text:
We are Europeans and made a roadtrip in the US this summer.
We booked our stay at the Four Points through the Sheraton website. We paid 150$ per night, tax included.
We decided to stay there because we wanted to be in Downtown Chicago, and the Four Points was the best alternative we've found. In fact other 3/4 stars Chicago hotels are horribly expensive.
I still think that 150$ per night is very expensive for a hotel room, but when I saw the other prices in Chicago, I was happy to get this rate at Four Points.
Hotel's good points:
- Very well situated, just 1 block from the Magnificent Mile !!!
- Very clean rooms
- Big standard rooms, well furnished
- Nice bathrooms
- Nice swimming pool
Bad points:
- VERY noisy street, you MUST ask for a NON street-facing room !!!
- Hotel is still in construction, there are still some works under progress (parking garage & restaurant not completed for example)
- Staff is strange: they smile and say "hello" anytime they got the chance, but if you ask for ANYTHING, they want to get a tip ! We asked at the front desk for a self park in the area, and they looked at us saying: "we're not sure about that", i.e.: give me 5 bucks and I'll tell you where's a good self park
- As there is still no parking in the hotel, you'll have to pay crazy prices for a self park in the area, expect to pay around 30$ a day... I never saw such prices in my whole life, totally crazy !
About Chicago: nice city, but too expensive. Everything is too expensive in Chicago. I mean: Paris or Rome are the best cities in the world, and they're cheaper !!!

title: “Great room with professional service”
text:
While my room was on a lower floor, the staff was nice enough to upgrade it to a full suite, making the stay very pleasant. The living furniture was a bit dated, possibly also because of the brown color theme. The bed was as always, comfortable with good breathing sheets. Amenities were plenty and the Keurig coffee was excellent to get a fresh cup of coffee or tea.
Downstairs lobby was very nice - spacious and brightly lit and that gave an airy feel.
The valet parking could be slightly chaotic at times but overall the staff was very efficient and helpful to get the car.
This is a great hotel to stay if you want a very comfortable room with fantastic and courteous service.
It is true that you must drive to this hotel, as in most places in Southern California, but it's also quite central to most tourist destinations.

title: “Clean and comfortable, no frills”
text:
My best friend and I recently stayed at this motel for a couple of nights during our visit to Austin for Thanksgiving. After reading previous reviews, I wasn't sure how this place was going to hold up, but we were pleasantly surprised. Check-in was very easy and there was plenty of parking. Luckily, we had a room on the first floor and we could park right in front of our window to watch our car. I'm always skeptical of motel parking lots, so this was not a reflection of the place itself. Our room was very clean, and we had no problems with noise or bugs. The a/c unit was a bit quirky, but I figured it out and the room stayed at a comfortable temperature throughout our stay.
Yes, this place is not in the greatest area, but if you've ever been to Austin, there really aren't that many areas that feel safe. The outside of the motel was well lit, and there is a Denny's and convenient store right next to it that provide even more lighting. I'm not sure if it was because of the holiday, but I did notice police cars patrolling the area, so there was really no reason to feel unsafe at any time.
If you're looking for a place that has tons of amenities and waits on you hand and foot, this is not the place for you. If you're on a budget and want a comfortable place to rest for a couple of nights, I highly suggest staying here.

title: “First class everything at the New Yorker”
text:
Travelling from Australia as a family of four with kids aged 8 & 5. We were originally booked into a midtown apartment but, while in Vancouver and with only 36 hours notice, the apartment suffered a terminal plumbing issue and became unavailable. After three anxious hours late night searching on the 'net we found the New Yorker. Despite calling at 03:00 NY time, the front desk staff booked us straight in, for 14 nights, room with 2 double beds, and even managed to arrange early checkin as we flew overnight via Toronto.
Without exception, the staff were great - curteous, efficient, friendly. The room had a point blank view of Empire State Building. And was everything it should have been (well, maybe the bar fridge should be standard). Bathroom was completely functional though a little cosy on space.
Location, location, location. The hotel is beautiful and one of those fabulous NYC iconic spaces. Deco vintage but refreshed for contemporary needs. Tick Tock Diner was perfect for breakfast and we had a fine dinner at Coopers, the hotel restaurant.
Overall, it was more expensive ($350/night) than we had budgeted for but, for a hotel stay, it was fabulous, fun, and a great introduction to NYC. Highly recommended.
Les, Samantha, Elsa, Joel.

title: “Top Class hotel ; lovely experience in Chicago”
text:
This is one of the best downtown hotel that I have ever stayed which is top class and business friendly. I have stayed here twice so far this year and all I can is, you just won’t go wrong for selecting this wonderful hotel for corporate events or personal leisure trips. Staffs are really friendly and all the business facilities it offers are really good. The restaurant manager last time offered me a complimentary breakfast for having to wait 5 or 6 min extra for table on a busy Sunday morning. 
Hotel is great for leisure hunters or shopping enthusiasts as it is just 1 minute away from the heart of magnificent mile. Since I'm a eco-friendly travel enthusiast, last time I found that the CTA metro station is just 2 min walk from the hotel (Brown line – Chicago avenue station which comes north bound from the Loop) 
Room facilities are great, great bed, quality toileteries and loved those HD channels playing on the large 36' lcd TV.
And, for all those who are a bit nipping type and love to read negative comments, yes I can write one in your favor too. This hotel does not have a pool and I really don’t see that as major drawback because you are staying in downtown and there are many better activities yards/blocks away in my view than relaxing in a pool. Whole heartedly would recommend to anyone!

title: “Best Hotel in San Diego”
text:
My girlfriend and I just got back from a WONDERFUL weekend in San Diego. We stayed at the OMNI From Sept 23-25 (Friday thru Sunday). The pampering started from the minute we arrived. The minute we pulled up to the hotel, the valet was opening my door and the bellman was taking our luggage out of the car. 
Check-in was a breeze. I told them my last name, and they handed me the keys, and that was that. No forms to fill out or anything of that sort. When we arrived in the room, music was playing, and to our surprise, there was a bottle of champaigne with 2 glasses and a card wishing me a happy birthday. I have stayed at many hotels all around the world, and this is the first to do anything like this. It was awesome.
Some tips about staying at the hotel:
1. Make sure you register for the Select Guest program!!!! It gives you the opportunity to have complimentary beverages and a newspaper in the morning, as well as a late check-out up until 5pm. That was a great help for us since we didn't want to leave until the evening. Also, the select guest membership gives you deals and special rates for later days.
2. I highly reccomend the Valet parking ($24/night), due to the unlimited in/out privelages. Make sure to call down to the valet on your way down, and when you get outside your car will be there waiting.
3. The breakfast Buffet at the restaurant is also very good. We had a seat at the window on Sunday morning, and just loved it!
We can't wait to go back to the OMNI Hotel San Diego. It's the best location, best service, and nicest hotel in town

title: “Lovely Grounds But Other Problems”
text:
I just returned yesterday from a 5-day conference at the Town and Country, along with other coworkers. Before leaving home I read the previous tripadvisor reviews and knew some of the concerns. I stayed with a coworker in a "bungalow" facing one of the 4 swimming pools, and at first was pleasantly surprised by the size of the room (included sitting area), vaulted ceiling, dark colonial styled furniture, and colorful wallpaper (although dated). We had a lovely view of the pool and tropical vegetation if we kept the drapes open, although people could then look into the room. The bathroom wallpaper was pealing in places, but not bad. The room was clean, and well-supplied with towels, etc. The handle on the bathroom sink kept coming unscrewed. The room clock/radio periodically made loud humming noises, so we finally unplugged it. The mattresses were VERY firm, too firm for me. The walls were somewhat thin, as we could hear the doors slamming closed next door, the service personnel rolling their carts back and forth over the cobbled walkway outside, and people talking as they walked by. After the first night we turned the room AC fan up on full to help drown out the noises. 
There is a charge for all calls outside the resort, including 1-800 calling cards and local calls, and you have to pay by the day to use the exercise facilities. We got parking included with the conference fees, but other people staying there had to pay. 
There were billing problems for many of the folks from our group, which still weren't resolved when we left. A PO had been issued by our employer to cover room costs, but the front desk hotel personnel (usually "interns") insisted upon billing someone for each room. Some of our group got angry and refused to give them a credit card #. One supervisor was told her credit card would be billed for the total cost of the group. 
Two of my coworkers said they had problems with their rooms, and called for maintanence, who promised to be right there and never showed up. 
The food at the restaurants onsite was overpriced, so most of us went to the mall next door to eat, or drove to other San Diego locations. The tram system is right behind the resort, and very handy to travel about town. It even goes all the way to Tijuana. 
I wouldn't stay at the T & C again, especially at the rates our employer was charged. The best things about the T & C are the grounds (lovely tropical flowers, vines and roses everywhere with gazebos, trellises, benches, and the pools), and the location next to the trolley system and mall. It's worth walking through to see the resort grounds, but stay somewhere else if you have the choice, unless you get a super deal.

title: “It's OK but something didn't quite click”
text: I had an ok stay at the Sheraton last week -- i keep thinking it should have been better, but i don't think it would be my first pick on a return stay. The hotel is VAST -- two giant towers, and all the amenities (gym, club lounge) were in the other tower. They couldn't (wouldn't?) move me. The gym is giant (two floors, state of the art) and the highlight of the hotel. Staff seemed to try hard, but seemed pretty incompetent in all my dealings. Room was OK, nothing special. I would look at other options before booking here, especially for the price.

title: “Great Place in Downtown”
text: This hotel is very nice and near the Arts Complex and 16th Street in Downtown Denver. The hotel was clean and our room was very comfortable. We ate at the PI Restaurant for Breakfast and the buffet was a mixture of hot and cold items and was very affordable. The only thing that I didn't like was the $29.00 per night for parking. I should have done my homework better on this but overall this is a nice hotel, within walking distance of all Downtown Denver has to offer.

title: “An excellent choice”
text:
The suites are often a great value. Excellent property well located, quality in house restaurant.
Check this hotel and often an awesome deal.

title: “Nice Hotel”
text: This hotel is not to bad. There is nothing fancy. Just the average Holiday Inn express. I do love the breakfast buffet thay have. Only one negative thing to say about this place . When you walk up to the lobby there was a lot of ice by the entry door. Had to ask if thay could put some salt down so nobody whould fall when thay are getting out of the car or shuttle bus.

title: “Inn at St Botoloph a very quirky boutique hotel”
text:
Location wise it is a great choice, The Inn at St Botolph is located on a quiet safe corner of Back Bay Boston very close to the Shaws at Prudential center, and the MBTA stop. The rooms were clean and though our queen suite was small and had a small kitchen (no oven), shower (no tub), and no table to eat at, windows that could open for fresh air was a major plus. Another plus was the nespresso coffee station set up for guests in the basement breakfast room. Except for the nespresso, the breakfast was very limited, serve yourself english muffins, yougart, granola bars, canned juice and not what you would expect from a boutique type hotel. 
But be warned that this Inn experience is not for everyone, you have to be tech savvy to stay here and in good shape. There is no lobby when you enter and no help with luggage up the stairs into the front hall. They send you a long code to open the front door and another for your room by email 2 weeks before you arrive and the codes only work up to checkout time on your last day. Also they charge your credit card in full for the total stay and the cancellation policy is very severe. I guess they are set up that way so you never have to talk to the staff which they keep in the basement in a room next to the breakfast room. The staff had an attitude so I didn't really want to talk to them anyway.
I generally consider myself and my husband pretty adept at figuring things out even though we are in the over 50 age group and have multiple engineering degrees between us, but we had trouble figuring out how to work the shower, to work the satellite TV we had to read the instructions but, the real kicker came when it took us a half an hour to get their can opener to open up a can - it was one of the new types that cut the can but not the lid.

title: “Wonderful Experience”
text:
We stayed overnight at the Orlando while visiting friends. When I called to confirm my reservation, they had us down for 2 queens instead of a king. When I pointed out that we had reserved a king they were hesitant to change is (stating that they were full for the weekend) but called me back in 5 minutes and stated that not only would we have a king bedroom we would be placed in one of the newly upgraded rooms. The room was beautiful (especially the bathroom!) with a wonderful view of the pool. Everything was clean and smelled brand new.
There were a few things we thought were odd
1. No door on the shower. The floor was covered in water.
2. Last minute details had been left undone (a cord stuffed up into the ceiling in the bathroom, the door needed repainting where the old locks had been pulled off, some of the furniture/mini bar were scuffed) I'm not sure if they placed us in an "almost finished" room and planned to come back to those details...but it really didn't affect our stay too much.
3. We appeared to be the only ones staying on our floor. For a hotel that was "booked" there was an eerie sense of isolation around us.
We LOVED!
1. The room had lots of space! Our two year old had more then enough room to spread out his books and read on the bed or the couch. He was in heaven, and WE loved that we weren't right on top of each other.
2. The toiletries. I know it's silly, but the soaps were AMAZING! I wish I could have bought a "regular size" set to take home with me.
3. The robe, slippers, and pillow mints made us feel like we were in a luxury hotel.
4. Customer service is wonderful!
We will definitely be staying at the Orlando again. It was a wonderful experience for a fabulous price!

title: “Sexy-cool Place in Funky Pacific Beach”
text:
Tower23 opened around six years ago about 10 miles north of San Diego. It's located in Pacific Beach and either you will love the its edgy-funkiness (like Venice, California 20 years ago) or you will wonder what a sexy-cool hotel is doing in a neighborhood like this. If you have a large sense of entitlement, and seeing some grit and edge will just ruin your martini or G and T, do yourself a favor and stay in La Jolla just up the road. In PB, you are far more likely to score a tattoo than a designer boutique.
That said, the hotel is a modern minimalist gem. All glass and white walls. A video loop of surfers plays endlessly on a small monitor the unpretentious lobby. The action here is in the Bar/Restaurant JRDN (pronounced a little surprisingly "Jordan", not "jardin.") Serving mostly very good food and a lively scene, it's particularly packed on weekends when the weather is good. The other great space is the Tower Deck on the second floor where white-towel covered lounge chairs surround something resembling a wading pool. I think it's six inches deep and I have never seen anyone so much as put their foot in there, so, hey, maybe it's just a water element or something. Nomenclature aside, it's a great place for a hang or a tan or to watch the joggers, surfers, runners and homeless people walk, run, or waddle by.
The rooms are clean and uber-minimalist, almost sterile if it were not for the drop-dead views. I recently stayed in a Sanctuary Suite and loved the extra space and the jacuzzi tub looking out over the crashing waves of the Pacific. The bathroom also sports a small sink, a stand-alone shower and small slightly depressing room with a toilet. I am hoping it's fluorescent lighting is a green gesture and not a design choice. Yikes.
Most if not all of the rooms have terraces on which you can see and/or hear the crashing of the Pacific. With "art" like that, who needs art in the rooms? 
This is not a place you come for white glove service, but the staff is young, attractive and happy to be helping you in any way they can. They try really hard, but sometimes you can really feel them trying and the strain shows.
Bottom Line: This property is my first choice when I come to San Diego for any reason, business or pleasure. It's perfect for a romantic weekend, or whenever you want to get-away from it all. A recent four-day stay undid months of work/life stress. And if it worked for me, it might just work for you. Give it a try, I don't think you will regret it.

title: “Grea staff”
text: Had an issues with the company where I was leaving my car for long term parking. Terry at the front desk was patient and very helpful. And worked it out for me. Later on she was my server and waitress in the little restaurant. The food and service was very nice. I do hope they gt the resraunt up and running soon. It wont work long the way it is going as hard as Terry and the other girls work. people are just to impatient Thanks again Terry you were wonderful. .

title: “Will not stay here again!”
text: We have traveled extensively, and this has definitely been our worst hotel experience. For our first room the keys issued did not work twice. Maintenance was sent up to fix. After half an hour of that, we requested to be moved to a different room since our idea of a weekend in Memphis did not include watching the door lock being repaired. Second room had key problems also. With one exception the hotel staff uncaring and unresponsive. Mini bar and snack refreshment counter - entrapment. Despite never touching the items or opening the refrigerator - due to warnings from other travelers - we were charged well over $100 dollars on my final bill AFTER I checked out. My phone call to hotel was not returned. Only received an email response after writing to their parent company. Their system for handling several nights at different rates is a nightmare requiring the guest to recheck in every day the rate changed. Did not receive without asking the $5 vouchers promised to be under our door for "green" refusal of maid service. We were there for a wedding and were suppose to receive welcome bags prepared by the groom's mother. They were sitting behind the counter but never given to us and many others. Had to go back and ask for them. Light bulbs burnt out in two lamps. This hotel definitely needs to work on its customer service in dealing with problems from unhappy customers.

title: “Very pleasant stay; would return”
text:
I visit New York frequently but usually stay in midtown for business reasons or close to Central Park out of habit. I decided to try a new neighborhood on a weekend trip and am glad we landed at the Tribeca Grand. The hotel has an interesting location and unusual layout, being more or less triangular in shape. The staff (mostly in their 20s, I'd guess) couldn't have been friendlier or less snooty. Our room, a Grand King, was spacious enough for two people, although there wasn't a lot of space for luggage (small closet). We thought the modern decor was pleasant and never had any problem with noise from the lobby (we were on the 7th floor). Although the room did not have a coffee maker, we were happy to discover a good quality free coffee machine next to the ice machine very close to our room (I believe there is one on each floor). 
The neighborhood is quiet but there are excellent restaurants in walking distance. We didn't try the hotel restaurant. Subway access is very convenient for multiple lines. What's not to like?

title: “Great Hotel - Wonderful Location”
text: My partner had never experienced the great shopping that the Dallas area had to offer, so we decided to take a weekend shopping trip to the Big D. I wanted to choose a hotel that was close to a major shopping area so we chose the Westin Galleria. The location was supurb! Very easy access via car being located at the intersection of the LBJ an the North Dallas Tollway. The hotel had very clean rooms and a nice bathroom. Our room, a King Deluxe, was located on the corner with sweeping views of the Metroplex. Being located within the Galleria complex made the trip especially wonderful. I was able to enter the Galleria each morning to dine for breakfast or brunch or to pick up my morning Starbucks. It also came in handy as we could return to the room to drop off our packages. My favorite hotel feature had to be the fragrence. The entire property smelled of white tea. I would highly recommend this property!

title: “Awesome”
text: One of the cleanest, most well maintained hotels I've stayed at recently. We somehow ended up in a handicap accessible room, so the bathroom was different (a shower only- which was fine). We had an early flight the next morning, and the shuttle service left something to be desired - far too many people in the shuttle and the driver didn't seem all that familiar with the airport layout. Overall a good stay.

title: “Concierge”
text: We would like to say thank you to Tatiana the concierge at the hotel for her fantastic assistance on our first day in Los Angeles. She was so helpful in all our requests and took her time with us so we didn't feel rushed into making quick decisions. Thank you Tatiana, very impressive.

title: “A peaceful little motel island in the city”
text:
We stayed here for 3 nights and really enjoyed ourselves. The retro motel atmosphere is fantastic, things have been kept up to date though, no worries there.
We wanted a place away from the city bustle and with easy parking as we had a rental car for the next 2 weeks of our trip but intended mainly using public transit while in San Francisco. The Ocean Park delivered on both counts, we slept like babies and the off-street, often covered, parking was just what we needed.
Some people here mentioned noise from the street car outside, we hardly heard anything even though it was close (and great for a direct trip to downtown). We did notice ear plugs were provided for the light sleepers though, a nice touch.
Service was over expectations. Our luggage got delayed at SFO and even though the airline decided to deliver it to the motel at 2am when reception was well and truly closed, we found a note under the room door in the morning letting us know our luggage was secure at the reception.
Highly recommended.

title: “Noise and smell in 409”
text:
We arrived late in the evening and we were tired from our journey. They gave me the keys to our room but when I put the card into the door in the 5th floor it would only show some yellow light. I returned to the front desk where they seemed to be confused what yellow means, they only were familiar with green (door supposed to open) and red (won't let you in). They gave me new keys, I went upstairs again, did not work again. Returned to the front desk one more time and they gave me another room. This time it was 409. Remember this number, if you ever get it assigned, reject it! Read more to learn why.
When we entered the room we immediately realized the smell from some chemical cleaner. It was nasty but we were tired so we stayed. Also there was noise which we thought came from the AC in our room. So we also ignored that for the time being thinking we could turn it off before going to sleep. After having been to the bath room we switched off the AC in order to be able to sleep. Surprise: The noise would not go away. We checked where it came from and we learned it actually came from the central AC of the entire hotel which was literally right in front of our window, see attached picture.
We were too tired to go down and get another room but it was a terrible night. With continuous noise it was difficult to fall asleep and when I woke up in the night I could barely continue to sleep.
From my point of view a hotel must be clean (including lack of smell) and provide good sleeping quality (i.e. no noise). In terms of those two top priorities this hotel failed completely. There can be no other rating than 1*.
If you consider staying there - reconsider!
If you still consider going there, make sure not to be put into a room such as 409, 509 and probably even 609 will be too noise to allow acceptable sleeping quality.
The corridors and the elevators look very dated, the furniture in our room looked new and good, though. If it didn't smell one could say it was a decent room.
Unfortunately when they updated the room they forgot to install a switch for the lights. Instead they put multiple lamps. When you leave the room you have to walk to every lamp and individually turn them off.

title: “Poor Housekeeping and disinterested staff”
text:
The service you get from the front desk is depend on who is working at front desk. Some of the front desk staffs are arrogant and unpolite.
Housekeeping is very poor and do not attend our request properly (disinterested and useless). They did not change towels. We requested several times towels and shampoo . each day we had to stop at the front desk for requesting towels and shampoo.

title: “Mostly great stay - good deal, no major issues.”
text:
Not my first time in a Kimpton and I can’t complain because I booked 2 king rooms at $105 a night! Crazy deal in the summer in Chicago. This hotel was in a great location and we walked most everywhere or took cabs which were about $8 plus tip to most locations. 
Hotel Pros:
Great Location
Cool old building updated to modern features
Really fun lobby
Free wine at 5 (my favorite)
Clean rooms
Quiet location
Great deal
Kimpton Points and free internet with my rewards membership
Good water pressure in shower
Aveda products (don’t have to lug shampoo)
Free coffee
Hotel Cons: 
Door lock broke and engineer had to come replace it (but gave us a $30 comp)
Power blew with hairdryer use (took 30 mins to get power on – building is old)
Slow / busy elevators
VERY small rooms (but we expected this in the city)
THIN walls (you can hear your neighbors)
Bar downstairs sucks – tried to use our comp there and the cocktails were HORRIBLE (but they gave us something else b/c we told them so)
In the Loop – ideally would have liked to stay river north but this location was worth the price savings
Restaurant ACROSS the street from the Cadillac theater is awesome – but closed on Sat and Sun
Hotel restaurant was overpriced and not that good for breakfast
Would I stay here again? Probably if I got as good of a deal. Not necessarily a 4 star hotel though, more like 3 ½. I still can’t hate on Kimpton though.

title: “Great great great”
text: Stayed for 3 nights and really enjoyed every moment.Great location next to all restaurants and bars.Great,large rooms with huge bathrooms.Great service from everyone working at the hotel.A great experience.

title: “Very good hotel with potential to be excellent.”
text:
Our tower room was on the 45th level with a superb view of St. Patrick's cathedral and the New York skyline. The room was spacious, clean, well appointed. The minibar drinks are VERY expensive - appr. $12 for bottled water - but we were provided a fridge for free in which to store our own drinks. Staff is friendly and efficient, the concierge advised us on how to obtain the best seats for the Broadway show of our choice. The location on Madison ave. is a blessing since all the interesting sites - museums, Broadway, 5th avenue shopping, Central Park or just about anything else - are within walking distance and the room insulation is excellent since inspite of the central location the room was quiet and peaceful, a rarity in New York city. 
Housekeeping, however, lacks training. My bathrobe was removed on the third day and never replaced. Our water glasses were removed and, again, not replaced - we had to call customer service (could not find a housekeeping button on the room phone) to send up fresh glasses, towelettes were not replaced in the morning. This is real pity because with well-trained housekeeping staff that uses a checklist, this hotel has the potential to be excellent.
Another area for improvement would be for the restaurant Istana to provide snacks and not only cocktails and drinks after 3 pm. One can find something to eat at the bar but we do not generally fancy the bar atmosphere. Food is, however, not an issue in NY since restaurants abound.

title: “Nice room, Its OK. Good for a family.”
text: We used the hotel as our vacation base for LA. Its very convenient to the freeway. The parking is mandatory valet. $15 per day plus tips. That seems to be normal for the area. We had a room with a loft. Nice LCDs displays with HD programming. Room was clean, and staff was very nice. Breakfast bar is in a small room. It can get a little crowded and noise. Food was normal free fare. The road has a lot of traffic during the day. Our room was in the back. Noise may be a problem in the front. There is a mall with a very nice food court about 15 minute walk. There is also a grocery store across the street. Overall, it was a slightly above average hotel.

title: “Best place ever!! Hospitality second to none!!”
text: Me and my family had the time of our lives here I swear!! Excellent hospitality, took care of our every needs. Rooms were super-comfy, swimming pool, service, food.. From start to finish everything was take care of for us.. They made us feel like royalty!! Room service, restaurant, bar, office, view - excellent! - we hardly needed to go outside! Thank you Westin at the Domain.. My son wants to go to your place and your place only for our next vacation - I totally agree with him!

title: “Excellent service, but hotel needs updating!”
text: I've been staying here on a weekly basis for the past few months. The amenities for Platinum members makes it a good option in Center City. Shawn Zenszer in the club lounge is always extremely helpful and accommodating. The recent renovations to the gym were a great update, but the rooms are outdated and could definitely use some improvements.

title: “Perfect spot”
text: My husband and I recently had a quick trip to New York City and stayed at the Michaelangelo hotel for 5 nights. We found this hotel to be in a perfectly central location, close to Time Square, Broadway and 5th Avenue and useful tube stations. The hotel was beautiful, luxurious, very clean and quiet and we were upgraded to a larger room on arrival. The free breakfast was very sad, just tea, coffee and soggy pastries and if you wanted juice you had to pay for it. But there are so many cafes with good breakfasts close by. I would definately recommend this hotel if you can find a good last minute price.

title: “Very nice”
text:
Feb/March is a good time for hotel rates in Boston as it is freezing and not many want to travel there. I'm a Rewards member and I was updated to an executive suite. Huge bed w/tons of pillows and lovely furnishings/state of the art TV, etc. I also received free breakfasts for being a Rewards member, otherwise would have paid $16. The buffet is a full breakfast (all you can eat style), everything you could want and very nice service.
I think I paid around $100 w/tax each night - it's normally close to $200. Not too many complaints - drunks in street below (many pubs nearby), dim lights in bathroom and vanity, sitting area near bar by the door was a little dusty and couch could have used a steam clean, but still ok. 
Once they know you are a rewards member, you get better service. Doormen/bellhops were very nice, too. The restaurant outside of breakfast is not too great - overpriced "California"? gourmet or really, they're just trying to get creative and it doesn't really work too well. The Times pub across the street has consistently good food for a decent price if you can handle casual dining.

title: “EXCELLENT experience hosting conference here”
text: I work with a major environmental organization that hosts a large youth conference each year. Typically we stay at larger corporate hotels, but decided to go smaller and more local this year with the Carlyle. We were extremely happy with our decision - the level of personal attention and care given to all of our requests was incredible. The staff were friendly, attentive, and helpful, not to mention patient with hosting 50 young adults for a weekend. Not to mention - the food was excellent! I would definitely recommend the hotel to other organizations, but also to friends and family coming to visit the city.

title: “great staff but room not worth the money”
text: We recently stayed at the Four Seasons for two nights. The staff was exceptional, food in Trio was delicious,location was very good. The room was disappointing. Small bathroom with a half door on the shower tub combination which caused water to get all over. Not a luxury bathroom for room that costs $525.00 a night. The bed was comfortable but there was nothing about the room that was exceptional. The grounds are pretty and the hotel is walking distance to all the great spots in Austin.

title: “Truly a treasure!”
