text: We spent three nights at Hotel Windsor in Philadelphia. We had two very comfortable beds, an efficiency kitchen, and a balcony overlooking downtown area in the museum district. Staff were very friendly upon check in/out and helpful when needing local information. Be sure to meet Lee at the Mace's pub next door, and experience the WaWa convenience stores that seem to be everywhere. Walking 6 blocks, we used the Chinatown to Chinatown commuter bus ($20RT) to go to NYC two days in a row and felt we were successful in seeing the best of both cities over a short stay. The Hotel Windsor proved to be the best decision I made when shopping on line for a comfortable hotel in Philadelphia.

title: “Very low graded Quality Bed”
text: I barely could sleep there. First, the bed was full size and was too uncomfortable,may be it is too soft. Secondly, I requested for the quiet room, the gentleman assigned us RM 601 where is located right above the traffic light. I was woken up by couple times of "siren" from ambulance and times of buses came by in the middle of the night. Valet Parking is $32/day. Self Parking is $28/day. There are limited amenities in the hotel, don't expect there is fitness center, pool, sauna or steam room. No daily newspaper. There are about 4-5 pc in a circle as a Business Center in the middle of the lobby. However, there was still one thing impressed us was the front desk staffs, they are friendly to customers.

title: “Very nice stay but not "wow"”
text: I don't know if I'm just becoming a hotel snob or what, but while I liked this hotel I didn't think it was "wow", or even as luxurious as other Kimpton properties I've stayed in. Location could not be better for easy access to public transportation, and easy walking distance to the Fishermans Wharf area. The doormen and bell hops were some of the nicest I've encountered - very friendly, prompt service, helpful with suggestions, and just all around wonderful assets to the property. Check in/out was quick and efficient, and our room was ready when we arrived. The lobby was nicely appointed and a nice place to hang out and people watch. Missed the wine reception, but water appeared to be served all day. Would have been a nice touch to add coffee as well. We had a king room with a view on the 3rd floor. The room was a bit small and the couch was so uncomfortable we didn't even sit on it, but had all the necessities. The bedding was very comfortable, although it would have been nice to have had a blanket in the room as the comforter was thin (sure they would have provided one if asked though). The view of the Golden Gate Bridge was less than spectacular - probably would not pay to upgrade to this if we returned. Had no problems with noise from neighbors or from outside. Everything was very clean and fresh, and the large pump bottles of shampoo, conditioner, and body wash were a nice touch. Took me some time to figure out that the hair dryer was hidden in plain sight, hung up in a bag next to the shower. Used the business center to print our boarding passes and was very pleased with the facilities. As great as all that was, I just didn't feel like the place was luxurious enough to justify the price (even for SF) and wasn't "wowed". That said, I would stay here again.

title: “One of the best place to stay”
text: I recently went to Washington DC for my birthday and i have to say first off that i LOVE that city. Lots of things to do and ESPECIALLY see. During my trip there I stayed at the Capitol Skyline Hotel. When i got there after an overnight flight i was helped right away. i was able to check in and get my room instead of waiting til 4pm to check in. i LOVE that i was able to do that and sleep. During my stay there, the staff was really helpful. Especially RAY MITCHELL. I must had bugged him the whole time i stayed there but he was really helpful from the Metro (it's location and what Metro Line to take) when i wanted to go to the Zoo or just get around town. He also recommended places to eat. I have to say that if & when i do go back to DC i would definitely stay at this hotel as well as recommend my friends. the price isn't so bad either. The location was a 20 minute walk away from all the museum so it wasn't too bad. I LOVE it....... thanks Capitol Skyline for making my stay there great and Thank you Ray for guiding me during my time there. If you go to DC stop by and say "HI" to Ray Mitchell.

title: “Hollywood Celebrity”
text: We have stayed at this hotel three times now - I love it for its location and friendly staff as well as the free internet and continental breakfast. Just a quick walk and you're right there in the middle of Hollywood and just around the corner from a subway station with easy access to all the LA sights. Great terrace our front for catching some morning sunshine. The staff are fantastic - always super helpful and polite. Will be staying there again in the near future, already looking forward to it.

title: “Great hotel and great location”
text:
This hotel shows up as the Crown Plaza Magnificent Mile and also the Avenue. A little confusing but according to the person I talked to the hotel was called The Avenue hotel right before being converted to a Crowne Plaza. I am assuming they did not want to change some of the signage so they kept Avenue in the name. 
Arrival: We were driving on this trip and had a parking package booked. We arrived in the evening and had no problem finding the hotel as it has a great location just off Michigan Ave on Huron St. The front door person met us quickly upon arrival and took our car.
Check In: The relatively small check in area was a bit congested as an air crew was checking out an the other desk was occupied for some time with a person that apparently had never stayed at a hotel before and had many questions. :) When are got to the check in desk the lady apologized for the long wait (it really wasnt long at all) and advised us of a room upgrade due to our Priority Club Platinum status, upgraded to a location suite. Also, she told us we had a coupon good for a 15% discount on breakfast at the Sky Lounge on the 40th floor and a coupon for a free drink at the Elephant and Castle Pub on the ground floor. 
Room: Our suite on the 30th floor was nice. The front room had its own small closet (with extra pillow and blanket), a nice leather sofa (pulled out to a bed), a comfortable zebra pattern chair, mini bar, work desk and an flat panel TV. A small hallway seperated the front room and the farely small bedroom area. The bathroom was off the hallway in between the front room and bedroom. The bedroom was a little small in that there wasnt a lot of room between the foot of the bed and the windows but the far side of the room had a closet area that was fairly deep and plenty of space for luggage and to hange clothes etc. as well as an iron and ironing board. The bed was pretty comfortable with the newer bedding that the newly renovated Crowne Plaza's have. The sleep kit is also provided, I cant remember exactly but think it was some lavender spray and some eye shades. The bathroom was nice enough with a medium sized vanity, Neutrogena shampoo, soap and lotion. The shower was the only problem as the pressure was not good at all. The TV in the bedroom area was an older CRT but not a problem for us but just seemed out of place with what seemed to be newer furnishings. The channels on the TV are extensive, cant remember exactly how many but a lot more than you normally get at a hotel. Free wifi is available and not limited to one login etc but it can get slow at peak times.
Sky Lounge Breakfast: With discount coupon in hand we decided to try out the Sky Lounge breakfast. The room appeared to be a converted executive/club lounge with a very nice view of Lake Michigan and the city. When we first arrived we were not impressed with the food offering. It was just not a huge buffet. Potatoes, scrambled eggs, sausage, bacon, breads, a few pastries, fruit and cold cuts and some cereals. Not a huge offering but everything was well prepared, not dry or over cooked. Really good to be honest. Service was excellent the morning we were there with just one person working the room but he did a great job as we wanted for nothing. I was not particulary pleased with the tables as they are just too small for the size of plates they are using. Typically those style of tables are used in lounges and the plates in club lounges are smaller so it is not a problem. I really think they would do better getting bigger tables and in particular possibly some high top tables as you could then see out the windows as you are eating breakfast as the windows are too high to view while sitting. The cost of breakfast with coupon was $17 each including tax before tip and I thought that was a bit high for the offering but given the service and quality I did not mind the price so much.
Elephant and Castle: Had a drink the night of arrival and breakfast on the day of departure. Drinks are a bit over priced but for a Chicago hotel, that is the price. :) The service was really good and friendly. Nice place to have a drink but cant comment on the food for dinner. Breakfast has a limited menu but the price is pretty cheap. The morning we were there there was only one server for some reason and he was working hard but very much behind. It did not bother us as we had time but some others got a little impatient. The price was right at about $8-10 per menu item including coffee in the price but the size of the portions are small. The quality was "OK" but not as good as the food in the Sky Lounge. If you just want a small cheap bit the Elephant and Castle is fine but if you want more the Sky Lounge may be a better choice. This place serves its purpose and although nothing spectacular it is fine.
Misc: We did take a look at the fitness area and the pool. The fitness area was a nice fitness area, not huge but seemed adequate for a workout on the road and the pool which was closed for the winter was pretty small. If a pool is important to you on your stay, this is not the place. 
Departure: Quick check out with the front desk person stamping my parking ticket as being paid and then went over to the valet window just off the lobby to get our car. 
Summary: Very happy with our stay. Comfortable room, fantastic location and very friendly staff. I will definitely make this my first choice in the future for stays in Chicago.

title: “great location”
text: It is right near Grand Central in the heart of midtown. Near lots of shopping, including some in the building. The workout room is fine. There were some issues keeping the room cool. Fancy soap products.

title: “Location, location, location”
text:
My husband and I stayed in the old section for 3 nights in March & would not hesitate to stay here again.
Room: Small room & bath but size wasn't an issue for us. The rooms have character with the tall ceilings, crown molding, & marble bathrooms and the furniture updated for a modern feel. The Westin bed & linens made for a great night's sleep. Room included flat screen TV, safe, coffee maker, hair dryer, shampoo/conditioner/soap/body lotion. Bath robe and slipper were not provided. No free wi-fi in room, but free wi-fi in lobby.
Location: Perfect for site seeing and shopping. From the hotel we walked all over the city including Embarcadero, Fisherman's Wharf, the Marina, Pacific Heights, China Town, & Nob Hill. If you're up for shopping, the St. Francis is literally only minutes walk away from Macy's, Nordstrom, Bloomingdale's, Sak's, Westfield's shopping center and many others.
Michael Mina's Bourbon Steak House in on the property, as well as another nice bar. They have a Starbuck's in the lobby (converts to drinks in the pm) so you can use wi-fi while sipping.
The St. Francis is still regal.

title: “Good Hotel, Excellent Service”
text: I stayed here one night on business as the hotel I usually stay in in Dallas was booked. The location was not ideal for my purpose as it was not within walking distance of the office or restaurants. Upon check-in, I inquired about getting cab service into the city and the man at the desk explained that the hotel offered a complimentary car service and he could arrange it for me to get to the office that day and the next morning. It is a bit of a sales pitch for Acura, but a much nicer ride than a taxi, plus free bottles of water too. The room was clean, spacious and had a great view of the city, but I did not like the set up of the bathroom one bit. You enter the room and to the right is the vanity and the shower, practically right in the room, with the toilet being the only part behind a closed door. The shower curtain was see through, so if you were travelling with someone, it better be someone you don't mind seeing you shower! While walking towards the elevator, I encountered one of the Managers walking the hallways. He introduced himself and asked about my stay. We had a brief conversation, I mentioned the helpful check in employee and he seemed pleased and wished me well for the rest of my stay. It is very nice to see Management out and about surveying the property and having interactions with guests when things are going well, not just a Manager who is called to the desk when there is a problem. Other than my issues with the location for my purposes and the bathroom configuration, this was a wonderful hotel with excellent customer service.

title: “Excellent weekend getaway”
text: Hospitality was superb.Exercise room was state of the art with steam room and sauna included. The hotell was in walking distance of many shops and clubs.

title: “Not Everything is Big in Texas”
text:
My husband and I just stayed here for a weekend getaway. All said the hotel is just OK for a 4 star hotel. We got a king room on the 15th floor and it was really small. The bed took up the whole room. I felt kind of clausterphobic in the hotel because I could not do anything in the room but lie on the bed, the windows in the room do not open, there are really no common areas to hang out in. I wanted to order breakfast in room, but there is no where to sit and eat. The pool and workout room were indoors in the basement. 
The Good:
Comfortable Bed
Friendly Staff
Location
Free Wi-Fi
The Not So Good:
No outdoor pool or lounge area
No common area for gathering
Small Room (if you get a std room)
Air conditioning is over the top in the bar and restaurant
I could here the ventelation system all the time, even though I turned off the air conditioning
Room needs updating
I would probably not stay here again because there are so many other hotels in the area that have the amenities I was looking for.

title: “Francisco Bay Motel”
text: My daughter and I stayed here for one night; it was supposed to be two, but we were both so disappointed in the room that we left SF earlier than we'd planned. I booked this room because Trip Advisor rated it as one of the best in San Francisco. Well, the rooms were about the size of a shoebox, and the hotel is not close to the cable cars. My daughter and I walked a few blocks north then East to go to Pier 39; the reviews said the neighborhood was good, but there are no coffee shops or markets nearby; homeless people stand with their pieces of cardboard around the hotel, and there is a warning in the parking lot not to leave ANYTHING in your vehicle; lest it be stolen, I assume. The hotel has no lobby; there is a window you check in at, and it's about as impersonal as you can imagine. The location right on Lombard street is noisy; the hotel is a tiny parking lot away from four lanes of traffic on a very busy corner. We expected a lot more and were basically disappointed. This was my daughter's first trip to San Francisco, so I wanted it to be at least an average room, but this is, in my opinion, not even average. There was room for the bed, then a TV and a desk, and that was about it. This hotel does not deserve its #6 rating as one of the best hotels in San Francisco.

title: “Marriott West Loop Excellent Value”
text:
I just stayed two days at this hotel over the Thanksgiving weekend. I received a great rate of $71.00 per night on the hotel's website. I've noticed that this hotel frequently has great rates on the weekend.
For a reduced rate, this hotel was excellent. It's an older property - - built in the early - mid 1970's at least - - it not a little older. I would not pay the rack rate for this hotel and there usually is no need to do so if you do your homework.
Service: excellent. Every staff member was polite, professional, and helpful.
Decor: Dated and in need of an update - - but in good repair. Nothing was worn out, broken, or dirty.
Room size: adequate room - - about average for a corporate hotel these days. It was not huge, but not cramped either. The room had all of the usual ammenities but did not have a mini bar or laptop safe. It was equipped with high speed internet for a fee of $9.95 per day.
Views: This hotel is surrounded by other buildings so you won't get much of a view in most rooms. My room overlooked the wall of the parking garage next door. Limited direct light into the room.
Cleanliness: Very clean - - everywhere I went, the hotel was clean and in good repair. My room and bath were very clean.
Bed: excellent. this hotel has the new Marriott bed and it's very comfortable.
Restaurants: I did not use the hotel's restaurants as there were lots of options in the immediate area.
Concierge Lounge: Fairly typical of Marriott Concierge Lounges. It was clean, comfortable and offered a very nice breakfast buffet.
Parking: $10.00 per day for self parking in a connected garage.
Location: Very good but not excellent. It's about a 20-25 minute walk to the Galleria Mall and about 15 minutes to the stores and restaurants on Post Oak. It's about a 7 to 10 minute walk to the shops and restaurants at Uptown Park. All-in-all, this is a good location that allows you to walk to lots of shopping and restaurants - - although you'll be the only one on the sidewalk. People just don't walk anywhere in Houston.
 You can stay at the Westin Hotels at the Galleria or the JW Marriott at the Galleria - - or at the Hilton on Post Oak which puts you right in the middle of all the shops and restaurants there, but you'll pay a lot more. The 15 - 25 minute walk was not a problem for me as the weather was excellent. Also, the hotel has a complimentary shuttle that runs at scheduled times that can take you to the Galleria and back. 
In summary, if you're willing to give up newer, more upscale furnishings and be a few minutes' walk away from shopping, this is an excellent choice. It's clean and comfortable with excellent service. I will definitely stay at this hotel if the occasion arises - - as long as I can get a discounted rate.

title: “Average Monster Conference Hotel”
text:
Went for a meeting. Very large hotel. There were 30 people in line to check in, with 3 people at the desk. The checkin time is officially 3, but they couldn't get me into a room until 4. 
Location is fine- I prefer the Westin further up the Magnificent Mile.
The room was undated, but signs that its an old hotel: worn out faucets, lots of caulk, 30 year old keycards on the doors. (funny how hotels will never replace 30 year old hallway doors, no matter the extent of other upgrades). The place was reasonably clean and maintained though.
The usual nickel and dime here: 12$ internet, 20$ to use the gym, $50 parking if you need it, etc. I somehow don't mind paying the luxury hotels for this, but resent paying Sheraton because I don't think that it offers anything more than a mid-range hotel such as a Hyatt Place (and there you get free breakfast, free internet, etc.)
I'm not sure what it is, but despite the ongoing attempts to update the Sheraton's image, I can't find anything to like or connect with. The value proposition is pretty mediocre. I'll be back if these is a meeting or something here, but wouldn't go out of my way.

title: “Perfect”
text:
Stayed at Hotel Monaco Jan 1, 2009 through jan 4, 2009.
The building itself is awesome - historically significant (and why wouldn't you want to stay in a Hotel with some history in DC?) with wonderful details - marble inlaid floors- incredible moldings - look up- way up - the ceilings are incredible. 
We stayed on the 3rd floor facing the Spy Museum. The rooms' decor was very well done - neo classic furniture, high end carpeting, drapes and bedding with a flat screen TV. Love the large bust of Thomas Jefferson! Rooms are small - but the ceiling height and oversized windows make them feel just right. Room was very clean and well maintained - as a matter of fact they were installing new draperies in some of the rooms which were not occupied so we got to peek in at quite a few. they are not all cookie-cutter- each was slightly unique.
Location - COULD NOT BE BETTER. Even though it was cold - (especially coming from Florida!) we walked comfortably to The White House, Capital and all the Monuments. You are surrounded by The Smithsonian - all within a 10-15 minute walk.
Nearby restaurants I highly recommend - Jaleo (1 or 2 blocks south), Clydes (one block north past the Verizon Center) and Zola (next door). Poste inside the Hotel is also very good but has a very limited menu - we had breakfast there each morning since that seemed to be the only breakfast place in the area - the truffled frittes and home made doughnuts are fab!
Staff was very friendly. Fellow travelers were a mix of young, old, couples, families - very comfortable to sit with them in the lobby over a glass of complimentary wine (or beer) in the late afternoon when returning from sightseeing.
Would absolutely stay here again! Looking forward to it ...

title: “Once again another great stay”
text: We stayed in October when we were in town for Quarter Horse Congress.Had a great stay checkin was fast and front desk clerk was friendly.Our room was great.We did see police patolling the area, which we feel is a relief to know they are trying to keep the area safe.We see this as a bonus rather than a negative.Lets face it crime is everywhere. Each time we stay we see where they are making improvements to the property.We will continue to stay at this property as it is a great deal and their customer service is great!

title: “Hotel 41 - Good Things Come in Small Packages”
text: We returned to Hotel 41after our first trip in 2006. What a gem ...great location, clean, comfy, safe, and a friendly helpful staff. We were there for 5 nights and didn't have a single problem. We especially appreciated the people who worked there because they were so ready to be of help with directions, subway info, a little on-line search to answer our questions about venues, printing our booarding passes. etc. When traveling it is the sights that we go to see, but it is the people who really made the difference. We shall return!

title: “Good location/Poor service”
text: Just returned from four nights at this hotel and found that their customer service has much to be desired. On Sunday night 4/5 there was a fire alarm and everybody was removed from the hotel for more than an hour. No explanation was offered by management. As soon as we returned to our rooms the alarms began again. There were at least a half dozen times when the alarms went off shortly thereafter and nobody new what to do. There was a near riot in the lobby and we had to demand that a manager talk to us about what was going on. There was no explanation given other than some sort of a malfunction. Many of us were left with scared kids and lots of older people coming down 15 flights of stairs more than once. From that point on it was hard to feel safe in this hotel. No compensation was offered or given when asked by this hotel. They plainly do not have their act together and I will never stay nor recommend this hotel to anybody. Tripadvisor is an excellent site to research places to travel and I do not make a habit of putting my opinions on the site. I just feel the this hotel was so egregiously wrong that they need to be called on it.

title: “Great Location”
text: The main reason we selected this hotel for our three night stay, was for its location. Although San Francisco is a fairly small city, this hotel is in a good central location for everything. The hotel room was quite spacious, we were on the 5th floor at the front of the hotel, overlooking the street and opposite a night club. There was quite a bit of noise into the early hours during a couple of the nights, not too excessive but if you were in a room on a lower floor it may become a problem. We had no problems at all and would certainly stay here again.

title: “Beautiful hotel, although location isn't great”
text: This is a gorgeous hotel, great rooms, great bed, and good service. The workout center is nice and if you get a deal or can afford the club level, it's lounge (with complimentary drinks/appetizers/breakfast) was excellent. We had drinks in the afternoon and evening (with a great view overlooking the city) and also had breakfast there each morning. The hotel is very large and close to the House of Blues (if you'll be catching a concert there). The beds are EXTREMELY comfortable. The valet parking service could use some improvement (slow and lacking in professionalism), but overall the hotel is great. The restaurant is one of the better in the city (with views and a bar that is right on the Chicago River). We didn't eat there though, so I can't comment on how good it is. The downside, for us, was location. It was not convienently located to anything we wanted (shopping, El/subway stops, etc.) So that meant a lot of walking and/or cab rides. I would definately recommend the Westin on the Mag. Mile over this one (which we've also stayed at) as it beats it on every level. Overall, though, it's a great hotel that is beatiful and has nice rooms.

title: “bad experience for a very steep price”
text:
Service is not great (some nice people but useless).I was sent first to a room already occupied (door opened, bed undone and a laptop on the desk!!).I mentionned that to the front desk but got unnoticed. The telephone in the other room did not work properly and the operator did not answered (I could only dial operator). Went downstairs to be told to go to the restaurant to order my dinner. Did that and waited an hour to get the meal I ordered. The food was bad (looked like canteen foodl) and the accompanying bread was from the day before ( cost of the meal 35$!!).
The room was noisy (the air conditioning was close to the bed!).
The only good things are the confortable bed (if you wear ear plugs) , the nice TV and a nice location. The gym is nice too.
Conclusion: avoid unless you do not mind to pay 495$ a night. Avoid the restaurant of the hotel (priority number 1)

title: “Lots of character and great location”
text: Big rooms, convienant location to food and nightlife, very friendly and helpful staff. Hotel was very unique.

title: “wierd place”
text: the desk clerk acted like she was really working hard to get me a room which i had already reserved and prepaid. maybe it was to make me feel special but it was unnecessary. the restrooms on the mezzanine level were locked most of the time. I went to the pool around 7am (it opens at 6am) just to have coffee. when i tried to leave all the doors were locked (the card keys would not work). had to pound on the windows to the lobby to get out! just a lot of small stuff which added up to "wierd". the outdoor pool is very small. the waterfall looks nice and makes so much noise you cant stay for long. it is a nice hotel but i expect much more from a hilton.

title: “Great little hotel!”
text: This place was great for the price. We paid $139/night and felt it was a good deal for the area. It is 2 blocks to the beach with lots of restaurants and shops within blocks. It was very clean, the staff was super friendly, and the furnishings were nice. The decor is more like a boutique hotel rather than a chain, with wrought iron lamps, oak headboard, funky upholstered chairs, and hand-painted border. Parking was $4/night which seemed fair. Continental breakfast was served in a clean area with a spacious courtyard available for seating. We would definitely go back.

title: “Fantastic Stay at the Marriott!”
text: My boyfriend and I booked this hotel only a week before our stay and got a great room with a great view of the ocean and Petco Park. Valet staff was fantastic and fast. They were very curteous as was all the staff. The front desk, concierge, housekeeping staff, etc. were amazing. They were very professional and helpful at all times. The room was a good size and very clean. Room service was fast and all the requests we had made online prior to our stay were made. We asked for extra towels and extra pillows and they were there waiting for us. I can't stay enough good things about this hotel. It's minutes away from the San Diego Zoo and only 15 minutes away from SeaWorld. it's near a lot of shops downtown and if you're in town for a Padres game, it's a must do! The ice cream store, the Marble Slab is right across the street and it's delicious! Perfect for a midnight snack as it's open very late, especially on the weekends. Trophy's is a great sports bar and grill, also right across the street. The Altitude Bar on the 22nd floor is fantastic as well. We did order dinner and breakfast from their restaurant, Soliel @ K, and I do have to say I was disappointed there. It cost much more than its quality. However, I do have to rave about their apple juice. The best apple juice I've ever had. I'd go back to this hotel in a second!

title: “We had a great experience with this hotel!”
text: As we were heading towards Chicago, we knew the downtown hotels would be too expensive. Traveling with the family, we were trying to save money. We found this hotel, which is located just on the outskirts of downtown. The hotel looks brand new and the price was very reasonable for the location. We were also very impressed with the customer service that received during our stay. The best we've seen in a long time. They were very friendly and gave us directions to where we were headed. The room was a great size for a family. We had plenty of space. We'll be back again! Did I mention Free Parking!

title: “Very pleased and quite lucky”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Embassy Suites Hotel Convention Center from April 27-30. We were able to get our room through Priceline for $95 a night. As you might know, when you go through Priceline, you bid on a room in a general area, a star- rating and a price. This can be a bit of a gamble, so we felt quite lucky to get this hotel for this price. 
We flew into Reagan Airport, and took the yellow metro line to the Mt. Vernon stop. It was about a 10 minute walk from the stop to our hotel. We found this to be quite manageable with only two pieces of luggage.
The hotel is quite new, and everything looked fresh and current. The suite set-up was very convenient. As you walk through the door into your room, there is a living area with sofa, chair, end tables, desk and tv. The bedroom had a comfortable bed with lots of pillows and also another tv. The room was very, very quiet. We found this set-up to be perfect, as my husband slept a bit later than I, so I was able to go into the living area and watch the morning news, while wrapped in the thick terry robe that was in the room.
Each morning the hotel offers a free breakfast with made-to-order omelets and many other breakfast options. I know that some other advisors mentioned that the breakfast area can get quite crowded and they found it difficult to find a place to sit. We didn't run into this at all, but perhaps it could have been the particular weekend that we were there.
There is also a free manager's reception in the evening that offers free drinks and munchies. This was very nice after a long day of touring and before going out to dinner.
There is a Circulator bus stop not far from the hotel. This is a wonderful way to get to the mall area, and a wonderful way to get back to the hotel, when it seems that your feet just can't walk another step.
With the hotel offering the free breakfast, free drinks, a pleasant staff and very nice and new accomodations, my husband and I feel that this was an excellent value, and would surely want to stay here again.

title: “Tribeca gem”
text:
The Grenwich is a great hotel. The rooms are interestingly decorated and well appointed. It feels less like a big city hotel than like a very well designed and staffed private members club.
The location, in Tribeca, is great for downtown, and for restaurants and bars. Less good, of course, if you are in NYC for Fifth Avenue shopping, Central Park etc. But Manhattan is a small place, and everywhere is in reach.
The food and bar at the Greenwich are absolutely outstanding. the restaurant in house, Locanda Verde, does some of the best Italian food I have eaten - it would be one of the very best restaurants in Bologna, Rome or any other foodie Italian city.
The small touches at this hotel, like the free minibar and constantly replenished basket of very fun old-school American snack (things like Smuckers, as well as normal M7Ms and other typical brands) really make a difference.
There is one weakness I think the Greenwich hotel has compared to the traditional five star hotels like the Plaza, Ritz Carlton et al is with the concierge. I felt that as a smaller and more recent hotel the concierge desk did not have the contacts or the pull to make hard to get reservations with restaurants in the city. We asked for a few reservations that weren't possible, and, although I can't be certain, I think the concierge at one of the big name city hotels might have been able to make it happen.
However, this is a minor weakness in a very excellent hotel, and I would happily recommend it to anyone for either a holiday or for business.

title: “Affordable Luxury near Rittenhouse Square”
text:
I stayed here for one night on a combination cash and SPG points. I was pleasantly surprised by the look of the hotel. I read somewhere that it was a former Ritz property. The room was spacious with a large desk, flatscreen TV and a nice view. (11th floor). The only issues I had with the hotel were the self-parking. I understand that it's going to cost money, but as someone else said it still stings to pay good money and then get put over the barrel for parking. Also, it would be nice if the elevators brought you up to the lobby. It was confusing when I popped out into the mall and then had to find my way. A little signage might be helpful once you exit the elevator into the mall. 
And I still think free wifi would be a decent thing to offer as it would cost them no money. But I would totally stay here again.

title: “Hotel Diva in San Francisco”
text: Hotel Diva tries to come across as a "sexy hotel", right down to the condom in my safe and the note "safe sex" :) Still, its just another hotel, but a good one. The location, a few hundred meters from Union Square, the price, good and clean in addition to free Internet are all things makes this a good alternative for travelers. Being next door to Starbucks is not a bad thing either, and everything that you need is very close by.

title: “Royal Treatment at a Non-Royal Price”
text:
My fiancee and I stayed in the Loews Hotel this past Saturday for our anniversary. We had a room on the 24th floor with a beautiful view of the city. We paid $204 for one night and that included the room and valet parking and all taxes. The room itself was beautifully decorated, the bathroom was huge, it was wonderful. The location could not be more perfect and every single staff member was amazingly helpful. Special Thank you to Mark the concierge who helped us out a TON on Saturday night. Great hotel, will definitley stay there again next time we're in Philly.
P.S. When we checked out Sunday morning Blake Lewis from American Idol was checking out right next to us!!

title: “Good location in downtown Phoenix”
text:
This hotel is a short walk from all things in downtown Phoenix--Diamondbacks, Suns, Convention Center, Science Center, theaters, other more expensive hotels (where they host conferences). They have a hotel shuttle so you can avoid renting a car if you plan to remain in the downtown area during your stay. The room was comfortable although the furniture is a little cheap--saggy couch and mattress. Very spacious though, nice LCD TV, I like the fridge/microwave/sink and desk area...and the A/C works well!
The breakfast is pretty basic but it's free. The marketplace has some snacks and drinks which can come in handy in a pinch. They have a pool too.

title: “cheap if you want to see NY”
text: great location, free wifi and Internet connection, avarage service, SMALL ROOMS with poor bathrooms, there are about 20 rooms and only 3 bathrooms available so you may wait to get to the washroom, the walls are very thin so you can hear your neighbours talking/laughing etc

title: “Convenient Location, Nice View!”
text:
I live in San Diego and stayed here with friends for a bachelorette party. The room was very comfy, and had a spectacular view of the Coronado bridge and the bay. The hotel is conveniently located! We were able to walk to the restaurant and many bars & lounges. One of the things I loved the most is how quiet the room was! There were people staying in rooms next door, and you couldn't even hear them in the hallway. The trolley stops right outside of the hotel also, couldn't hear that either! I loved that there was a little sitting area in front of the windows with the view, it was a very nice touch. We were very satisfied with our room! 
The only not so great thing is that you have to park in a garage across the street by the ballpark. I still gave the hotel a 5 because in downtown San Diego, parking is NEVER good.

title: “Judge and Jury's no longer out!!!”
text:
Stayed in this hotel in early June but have been a bit negligent in writing a review. I, as always, paid close attention to Tripadvisor reviews. Not let down in any way- a great hotel. Very modern, clean, well kitted out rooms - which I feel were spacious. The hotel is located well and only a couple of blocks from the Common and Newberry Street.
What really made the hotel (as with all hotels) is the staff. They were helpful, professional and treated you as a friend - particular praise to Joanne in reception and Emily in the bar! The bar is a really jumping place which may be the only negative in the eyes of some travellers looking for a quiet place to relax in the evening. 
Suited me just fine - going back next week.

title: “Large & comfy room, nice staff, room service $$$ expensive”
text:
Stayed in room 1015 for three nites - huge suite with a queen-sized bed and THREE closets. Considering I paid $169 on quikbook for a double room, the upgrade was amazing/wonderful. Partial view of Empire State Building. Room was clean, comfy and huge. It could use a little love: carpets are frayed and bathroom sink was missing hardware. Bed was very comfortable and street noise wasn't bad on the tenth floor (A/C muffled most hotel and street noise - and since bedroom isn't near hallway, it was great not to hear doors slam all the time). Water pressure in shower was good, tho the showerhead sputtered and shook. Two robes in room and plenty of pillows. 
This could be a really great hotel with a few changes - some minor room updates and more even service. When I arrived, there was no one to open door or greet me. Considering I was schlepping three bags, a little help would have made a great first impression. 
Computers were down and check in was delayed til about 3:45, an inconvenience that would've been better tolerated if staff had communicated updates to all travelers waiting. An offer of free wifi and a refreshment would've gone far on a 95-degree day waiting in a lobby.
Most of the staff encountered were professional and helpful, especially the woman at the front desk who arranged the upgrade to a suite. 
The room service charges were outrageous, not a surprise but still always a disappointment to be gouged. There are other hotels, such as the Lucerne on the UWS, that don't feel compelled to rip off customers. 
Murray Hill is not a very exciting neighborhood but it's safe and an easy walk to Grand Central, Macy's and midtown. There's a dearth of green/open space in this neighborhood, but the hotels are often so well priced compared to other areas, you can live without the park. 
Would recommend this hotel if you're looking for a large and comfy room and if you can get it for cheap.

title: “Great location”
text: Stayed here on Memorial Day weekend. It was crazy busy and the hotel was totally full. They warned us when we checked in and even though it was full we still had a great time. Seaport village is just outside the front doors as well as the USS Midway. The Midway is awesome and I highly recommend it! The pool is indoors and had way too much chlorine... Other than that I have no complaints. Breakfast was great and the happy hour was fun. The hotel did a great job handling all of the people. We will be back!

title: “Good location, lovely staff, worth paying for a room on a high floor.”
text:
Room was clean, not large but adequate. We had a twin room on the 15th floor which was quiet and we got sleep on every night. There was some noise from the door going to the fire escape and stairs but generally it was very peaceful.
The staff were polite and very helpful. The toilet seat was broken when we arrived but maintenance were very prompt and came to replace it immediately.
The housekeeping team were satisfactory and did tidy and clean the room every day as you would expect though it was usually quite late in the afternoon.
There is not very much storage in the bedroom though and we had no where to leave our cases. Also there was only one chair so we ended up sitting on our beds instead. Not a big deal but means that it felt a bit cramped at times.

title: “An extra charge for everything”
text:
The first room we were assigned smelled of tobacco. 
Got another one .
That had a worn office chair and traffic from the road below came through too loudly .
They charge 12$ for internet, They charge 22$ for Parking and they even charged 5$ for a small package that was delivered prior to my arrival. That was withdrawn after my complaining.
We had flown in from Europe. This international 4**** airport hotel did not have a plug adapter for european appliances.
Room service meals have extraordinary many extra charges (+ at least 30 to 35%)

title: “Wonderful time!”
text: Really enjoyed our stay here. Perfect location in the heart of the theater district, walked everywhere. Room was spacious and luxurious.

title: “You Got To Love Howard Johnson at Fenway”
text: Last month we went to a Red Sox / Yankees game at Fenway Park. We got the tickets early in ther season and planned to make a weekend out of. With a little research we found Howard Johnson Inn at Fenway Park and it didn't disappoint. It 's reasonably priced and is right behind Fenway, (just a 5 minute walk to Fenway). Even though normal check-in isn't until 2 PM we got there an hour and a half early (just to park in there lot), we were able to check-in. We stayed in room 222, which if you looked out the window you could see Fenway Park. Actually any even numbered room will have a great view of Fenway Park. (Rooms 218, 220, 222 have probably the best view of the players parking garage area on Van Ness St). The front desk staff was great, they had a lot of local knowledge and gave us some suggestions on things to do. It was too cold to go swimming but, they do have an outdoor pool. It's close to many restuarants and bars such as Boston Beer works, Cask and Flagon, etc. It's also next to many T-stations including Kenmore Square (about 15 minute walk). Its not the most luxurious hotel in Boston however it was a great stay and would recommend it to anyone.

title: “My SF "home away from home"”
text: Having gone five times at this charming boutique hotel ,I can say only that it is one of the most lovely and welcoming hotels in America. . Done up like a literary salon of the '20's, there is an excellent wine bar and restaurant ; each room is comfortable, though small for large groups, with everything kept in tip top condition. The staff couldn't be better. I recommend the REX to anyone going to San Francisco for their first or whatever visit. It is conveniently located near Union Square, with the Square's shopping and theatre opportunities. Give yourself a treat and stay at the Rex!

title: “Fabulous RESORT! A one stop shop for an amazing family getaway!!”
text:
We chose this resort based on trip advisor reviews. We wanted a nice hotel, with a pool, outside of the riverwalk madness, but still close enough to visit all the San Antonio attractions. First of all, I can't say enough good things about the Westin hotels. They are consistently great quality, but this was quality on a whole new level!
I'll keep it simple. I'll list the pro's 
and con's. Please be patient, there 
ALOT of pro's! 
*Hotel property is outside the 
madness of the city, yet close enough to visit all the high points!
*The property has everything you need. There's seriously no need to leave the resort. It's all here!! Huge family pool (which is open 24/7!), adults pool, poolside bar, poolside restraunt, buffet breakfast, poolside grill, all-day activity schedule (which is concluded every evening with a kid friendly movie on the lawn), kids playcare, a pre-teen/teen facility for evenings, 
sports club/lounge, 4star restaurant, spa. I'm a little out of breath, but you get the point. 
*Starbucks!! That's right! Located just inside the main entrance. 
*incredibly helpful concierge.
*BEAUTIFUL scenery!
*3 golf courses (2 of which are located onthe property.)
*Upscale mall about 5 minutes away.
*Fiesta Texas is about 2minutes away.
*Sea World is about 15-20minutes away. 
*Riverwalk is about 15minutes away. 
The Con's
*There aren't a ton of restaurant options off property, if you'd like a change.
*If you go during the winter the resort may not have as much to offer, since the pool and lawn activity is the major draw. 
*The food and drinks can be expensive at times. 
*Our check-in experience was not the greatest, even with us being Starwood Preferred guests. (We were charged twice for our room, and we had to stop in at the counter 3 times to straighten it out.)
As you can see the pros far out weigh the cons. It was an overall fantastic resort! We've already recommended it to several friends, and we intend to go back. I wish there were more of these type resorts in Texas!

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
Really nice hotel with wonderful views. The price was really good for Newyork and very close to the subway . Restaurant was very good althou a bit on the pricy side. 
Loved the fact that they had bottled water available 24 hours.

title: “Choosen thru trip advisor”
text: Very well situated clean hotel with garage, lift. Cable car next door. Cheerful and helpful staff (they called twice to Alamo and taxi). Fridge and microwave in room. Nothing glamorous but interesting price, at least for SF (16% tax).

title: “Great location!”
text:
We stayed two nights at hotel Pennsylvania in New York, from the 19th of August untill August 22nd. We had a room on the 16th floor and our roomnumber was 1617a. The room was very basic, muffy and the tv wasn’t working. 
The location of this hotel was great! Right across the street from Madison Square Garden and the subway station and five minutes’ walk away from Times Square. 
The convenience of these facts makes it worth considering for a second stay in this hotel. But, we found out (thanks to the NYC forum) that the hotel is nowadays in terrible condition and will be torn down soon. That is a pity, but we are sure we can find a better hotel near Times Square!
Have fun in NYC!

title: “AVIOD THIS HOTEL AT ALL COSTS”
text: My partner and I stayed here two nights, and believe me, two was enough. The receptionist was a nasty piece of works, who clearly hated her life. We had been travelling for some time, and were shocked at her rudeness. Furthermore, the room we requested to start with wasn't available. We had be travelling for some time, and were ready for a quiet drink, but were told the bar and restaurant was closed... without further explaination. What surprised us was that even shitholes in New York, IE: Hostels, supplied us with really lovely food for breakfast... and was much cheaper. When we got to the room, we were surprised with the so called "Captial hill view" you could barely make out the view, and the website had cleared changed the photos to give the impression the hotel was next to captial hill, which was in fact lies. The bathroom light didn't work. The Heater was really noisey, the TV was really hard to work, and was an old tube tv... which somehow managed to charge me for a movie I never watched. The internet was slower than dial up..and the lady at reception gave us the wrong directions to town, and told us to go to a bar near the hotel, which happened to be closed. Aviod this hotel at all costs.. you're better off staying under the local bridge. NEVER go here !!

title: “Surprise”
text:
Not wanting to stay at one of the over priced hotels in midtown Manhattan, we stayed at the Murray Hill East Suites based on recommendations from friends. 
The building is located two blocks from the drop off point for the Newark Express bus at the back of Grand Central Station. We were surpised when arriving that it does resemble a hotel with a 24 hour reception and concierge service. The accommodation was busy with travelers from a few different countries. It was the week of the New York marathon which might have been a factor but we got the impression that this was normal.
It is clear that this had previously been an apartment block and the accommodation comprised of a large lounge area with bed settee, bedroom with two queen sized beds, kitchen and bathroom. There was a problem with the heating in the room when we first arrived. We were told it was in fact a problem in the whole building and could not be fixed till the following day. The reception provided a heater within a few minutes which we were able to keep for the duration of our stay.
The accommdation is clean and comfortable without being luxurious. It is a bit dated but this is something that we've found in New York in general on previous visits.
The building has a couple of good quality diners within a minutes walk (try Scotties for good value). There are some local bars in the area which are ok for a quick visit. 
If you choose not to walk too far, Manhattan is best navigated by the Subway system. Grand Central is the nearest subway station (about a 5/10 minute walk) with Times Square a further 10 minute walk. This isn't a huge problem but it can be a bit tiring after a day sightseeing or shopping.
At $235.00 a night (plus tax) it is in the same price range as some hotels but you do certainly get more for your money than just a simple room.
I would certainly recommend the Murray Hill Suites especially to families or groups of people.

title: “just ok”
text: one of the furthest out of the airport hotels but free shuttle though it just runs to a loop and not a discernable timetable. Lobby is deceptive as the rest of the hotel which we saw and our room was tired and somewhat dated though large. However very good and comfortable bed and pillows. Restaurant was above average. Hotel staff very helpful

title: “Perfect - in almost every way!”
text: 10/21-25/2012: From the in-room thermostat to the wide, bright windows the room appointments could not have been nicer! The firm, comfortable beds had extra pillows. The fresh updates made my stay here delightful. The complimentary toiletry items had a lovely fresh fragrance that I loved. The coffee station in its own nook was convenient with a one-cup brewer with coffee and tea provided. With extra mirrors and many lighting options, how could you not be comfortable here? The desk has its own lamp and convenient power outlets available. The television stations were limited, so if you are used to watching a lot of TV you might be disappointed with those selections. Also, if you are used to complimentary breakfast, it is not featured here, although there is room service and a very convenient food court with different selections along with a convenience store on the lobby level with most anything you might need from snacks, to gifts, to toiletries. Likewise the Wi-Fi is not free which I found surprising. You can sign up for service by the day or longer if needed. I stayed here for a conference in the attached convention center. Within walking distance are restaurants and shops and the area seems very safe and comfortable to be out & about in. I hope that you find your stay here as nice as I did.

title: “Bad Looking Hotel, Poor Housekeeping, Small Rooms, Stay Somewhere Else”
text:
Hi,
 I stayed here to visit the wonderful museums; the location is excellent. This hotel used to be a Holiday Inn and I wish that it still was! The modern 1960's decor is terrible, very dark lightening everywhere, even in the rooms and hallways. This makes the single female traveler feel very unsafe with the poor lightening in the public areas and especially poor lightening in the hallways.
 The Internet was expensive and there are no fridges or microwaves in the room. Room service charges $12.00 for a glass of wine! The rooms are very small and there is no counter space in the bathroom. I have to keep my make-up and more (toothpaste, etc) outside of the bathroom, which is a royal pain.
 My room view overlooks the roof top of another building; it is very ugly. Overall, please stay elsewhere. I would recommend the Hyatt across the street.

title: “Old building, standard rooms, high ceiling, good views, good location, great views.”
text: Located at the top of the hill, has great views of the bay, steps to chinatown and union square. Rooms are standard compared to other same quality hotels, ceilings are high, gives a comfy feeling. Closet is a walk-in one, and the lobby is very nice.

title: “Clean But LOUD! No Sleep!”
text: Not a bad place from a cleanliness standpoint. Cheap amenities -- no shampoo in room, have to request at front desk. Free coffee and donuts. however, it is very loud. You can hear doors slamming, people stomping around upstairs, and talking in the next room. I hardly slept. Least soundproof hotel I have been in. Not so great for $101 per night (including tax).

title: “Good hotel in a great location”
text: Stayed here with my wife & daughter for nearly two weeks. The hotel is clean, modern & well appointed. The location is perfect, walking distance to many point of interest, & with Grand Central Station on your doorstep the whole of New York is easily accessible. We upgraded the second week to Club Hyatt which included a larger room & access to breakfast & canapes etc which was great. The only negative would be the charges for wifi are a bit steep, but overall the Grand Hyatt New York help make our trip to NYC a fantastic experience, & we would stay there again.

title: “Exceeded expectations”
text: It's tough to find downtown/Back Bay hotels which live up to their price-range promises. The Colonnade delivers. They deliver on all fronts, but what impressed us most was the staff: friendly, conscientious, and professional. We now know what our Boston hotel is; no reason to go anywhere else.

title: “Horrible”
text: I booked this for one night for us and our 3 boys. It seemed like a good price and close to the airport. The room was filthy and smelled terrible. The bathrooms were disgusting. Probably the worst place I have ever stayed. I usually try not to be picky especially when I've booked for cost and convinience...but this was just awful... We couldn't sleep because everything was so dirty and smelly and the staff at the check in are unfriendly. I would never go back here or recommend that anyone else does....Unless you have extremely low standards!

title: “Great Experience”
text: Loved this hotel. Great rooms, great attitudes on the part of staff, wonderful location. A wonderful surprise. I'll stay here again and again. Great gem in the middle of Seattle. I've never been treated so well by each and everyone staff member I came in contact with. The bar is a great little find as well. Loved the service and the menu.

title: “The Good, Bad, and Ugly”
text:
The good: location was awesome, beds comfy, rooms clean enough, those working for tips fairly helpful, maid service good, close to the action yet still good for sleep, water pressure in shower good, gym good enough in a pinch, felt safe. 
The bad: entire hotel floor smelled like a giant ashtray (to be fair... so do the streets of New York in most places), the check in took forever after a long day of travel
The ugly: encountered a pissy britches front desk staff, information staff horrible at providing hotel information and directions (this does not include the concierge staff- those guys were pretty helpful)
The truth: I would stay here again

title: “Great Place to stay on the Riverwalk - comfy, clean, a little pricey”
text:
I stayed here on the recommendation of the bride & groom (we were in San Antonio for a wedding) and overall I was very pleased with my stay.
SERVICE - The front desk was very cheerful, friendly, and accommodating. 
The concierge took on the challenge of helping us get a rental car last minute...and even though we put him on the spot he was able to help with with a very friendly attitude & he even asked us how the car was working out the next time he saw us in the lobby. Check in/Check out went very smoothly. No complaints at all.
Housekeeping was very persistent (one day we decided to sleep in and forgot to put up the "DO NOT DISTURB" sign) and they tried to come in to clean our room 4 or 5 times that morning! 
Room Service - very high quality food, not too expensive.
CLEANLINESS - The hotel was very well kept and inviting. The hallways, lobby, elevators, and area outside on the Riverwalk were very clean and well maintained. The room was very spacious and clean.
ROOM - The view from our room left much to be desired. But we didn't want to pay the extra money just to have a Riverwalk view (our friend had a suite overlooking the Riverwalk and it wasn't much of a view either). But aside from the view, the room was clean, spacious, and comfortable. The products they provide in the bathroom (soap, shampoo, etc.) are very high quality and smell great.
LOCATION - The Westin is located close to the "heart" of the Riverwalk but it still requires a bit of a walk to get to the part of the Riverwalk where there are bars & outdoor restaurants & cafes. So if you want a prime location on the Riverwalk this is not exactly where you want to be. But again it's not too far of a walk.

title: “the Melrose - a VERY nice hotel”
text: My daughter and I stayed at the Melrose Jan 5th- 10th, 2005 and found it to be a very good experieince. I've read the other postings (the positve one are why I chose it) and I'm surprised at the negative postings. The staff couldn't have been nicer, from the valet to the front desk to the kitchen staff. We had reserved a "suite" which wasn't available, but I didn't even bother to protest, as we were more interested in two double beds than the sleeper sofa. Our room was decorated beautifully, including two chairs and a table instead of the sofa. The webpage does show a bigger room, but we had more than enough space. The only complaint I would have is that the heat and air doesn't respond much, but we could open the windows to allow some cool air in and that solved the problem. It was too warm. There was a delay in finding our car the first day, but not after that. We only had breakfast in the dining room and that was very good. The bar is supposed to be a comfortable meeting space but we didn't try it.. Having stayed at Relais & Chateau properties in Europe, (very expensive and chic) I found this comparable and more than half the price. I would definitely book it again. I would give it four stars easily...

title: “Great location, impressive customer service”
text:
Stayed for 3 nights in a standard double room with two of my girly mates in late Feb 2011. NY followed crazy 4 days in Vegas so we were looking for a little R&R and a chance to catch up with some friends in our fave city. Booked through Asda travel, around £150 per night in total which we thought was pretty reasonable for 3 people midweek. We were allocated a room on the 25th floor.
First with the positives:
- Room very clean
- Considering this was a standard double, I actually thought the main room was not a bad size for NYC (remember we had 3 adult women sharing). We had enough space for three large suitcases on the floor without killing ourselves walking about the room. Bathroom small but perfectly formed.
- Hotel in middle of refurb and we were on a brand new floor. I thought it looked great and lots of nice decorations in the hallway. This did lead to our only complaint though (see below).
- The one complaint we did make (see below regarding the refurb noise), was dealt with superbly - immediate unqualified apology and $100 comp'd to our room to spend on dinner. Nice touch and although the issue we had was very annoying - it was enough to help us forget about it and get on with the holiday.
 - Hotel is in a really great location. 10min walk to Times Square, right next door to Grand Central, and fab delhis on Lex. Really couldn't hear much noise from outside.
 - 5 Mins tops to check in and out and only a short wait to leave our luggage with the bell desk on our last day ($2 per bag charge)
 - Liked the buzzy feel in the very grand lobby - makes you feel like you're really in the thick of it which I think people look for in NYC.
 - Fab service in the restuarant at dinner - very attentive red head who was charming and provided fautless service
 - Nice view from 25th floor
Now with the not so good:
- Only one restaurant in the hotel and the food was VERY rich (a little too much for our pallette). I'm sure when I stayed here before there was more choice and a cocktail bar ?
- Mattresses were so soft that two of us had bad backs in the morning. Our other friend who is the only one to sleep on her side had no problem. Guess bed firmness a very personal preference and dependent on the way you sleep!
- Refurb work was being done on the 26th floor immediately above us. We were woken up on our first day at 7am and honestly thought someone was about to come through the floor. Sounded like very loud dragging sound and very noisy banging. It was continuous so we couldn't go back to sleep after 7am :-( 
Exactly the same on morning 2 and we'd had enough. I phoned the front desk and as I mentioned above - they offered what I considered fair compensation and if we insisted I think they would also have moved us. We said don't worry as we had to get up early on the last day anyway and were more than happy with the way they handled it.
I really thought the service in the Grand Hyatt was great - I think that says so much more about a hotel than the official star rating. Have stayed here a few times now and would definitely go back - no question.

title: “Very accomodating staff”
text: This is an older hotel that could use some updating, but everything was very clean and above all else the staff was very accomodating. I traveled with a group of little old ladies and with all their needs and requests the staff was pleasantly willing to do all they could. This was a "yes we can" attitude which was so refreshing.

title: “Great Historic Hotel with Modern Conveniences”
text:
A great old hotel that has been updated with modern conveniences. The rooms are small but the beds are very comfortable. A flat screen TV helps to make the most of the space. The bathroom is much smaller than newer hotels but very functional. The only thing you'll miss is a big counter since there is only a small ledge over the sink. The free wi-fi is an awesome touch.
The best thing about this hotel is its location. Its right in the heart of Union Square, steps from the Powell BART stop (very convenient for travel to and from the airport). In fact my room overlooked the trolley turnaround! Although I enjoyed this site, if you are sensitive to noise you may want to ask for a room that doesn't since there is bell ringing indicating the trolley is ready to board from early in the morning to late at night. Since I am used to city noise, this didn't bother me a bit! I was attending a conference and only had to walk 5-minutes to the Moscone Center. And I didn't feel uncomfortable walking around late at night.
Overall, I was very pleased with this hotel. It was an amazing bargain for the price and the convenient location couldn't be beat!

title: “Great location, comfortable bed, room was clean, great price!”
text:
Free parking! Great price (AAA), clean rooms, comfortable beds, friendly (couple) manager- very helpful with suggestions on restaurants,
sights to see, locations, transportation around city. Would recommend
to friends!

title: “Wonderful Experience”
text: Stayed at the Mayflower Park in Feb 2005 for a few days and had a wonderful experience. We were able to obtain the Entertainment rate which was 50% off the rack rate. Room was very large and we had a view of the Space Needle. Front desk staff was very helpful with last minute dinner recommendations. Did not eat at the hotel because it was on the expensive side and there were so many places to eat within walking distance. Monorail entrance is located next to the hotel and the underground bus stop is down the block. Definitely would stay at this hotel again.

title: “Very spacious rooms”
text:
Very spacious and confortable rooms, though the kitchen is a little bit old fashioned.
Excellent location a few minutes walk away from the bustling spots and helpful staff.
We would have love a free wifi internet.

title: “Clean, plush and comfortable”
text: Rooms are spacious, clean and the beds are VERY comfortable. Starbucks coffee in the room. Fitness room is very nice. Good location, walking distance to just about everything. Highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Excellent hotel with style, comfort and history in the heart of San Francisco”
text: Had a wonderful time - 20th anniversary - the last week of August 2010. Customer service was excellent and we especially appreciated the great service provided by Marichu Alvarez. The Westin St. Francis on Union Square is at the heart of it all and the cable cars are right out in front. Service and comfort were the best and no complaints whatsoever. We will return to this hotel whenever possible - at least once a year if not more. I highly recommend this hotel to anyone staying in downtown area of San Francisco and anyone wanting to experience a good stay in "the City."

title: “Great location, modern room, good breakfast”
text: My wife and me stayed after Christmas and had a pretty positiv experience. Check in was smooth, staff is friendly and the lobby is modern. The room is typical HGI except for the size but it is Mahattan. The hotel is clean, one has to have a key to get up to floors. The breakfast staff is very friendly and the food was good. Macy, subway and lots of convienance very near. It is worth a stay.

title: “A little gem on our way to Ausrtrailia.”
text:
Shows its age (the only reason for the slight down grade).
BUT... Very clean. Very accomodating personnel. Nice continental breakfast.
Beautiful gardens with fresh flowers all over the place, inside and out. Large pool.
More like a resort setting than an airport crash pad. No full service restaurant but an attached
24 hours full service Denny's restaurant and lounge. 24 hour shuttle to LAX.
All this for $84 in 2011.
Kudos.

title: “Nice place. Nice rooms”
text:
My wife and I stayed here over a long weekend. I booked it via priceline on a whim. I bid and won $60/night before taxes& fees. 
I really liked this hotel. Very clean rooms and a nice location. We didn't rent a car and found this hotel very convenient. We could walk to the metro and stroll to Georgetown. Lots of restaurants were found just a quick walk away at Dupont Circle. It was fun passing the various embassies nearby.
The most fascinating thing about this hotel: It used to be called another name (Vista International) and they changed the name after D.C. Mayor Marion Barry was caught smoking cocaine here in 1990. Apparently we were staying in the same room (812) and the concierge and bellboy let us know the room's unique history. Wow!
One drawback: No outdoor pool. Just a small indoor puddle. No big deal.
A tip: Skip the tacky New Orleans-theme bar attached to the hotel and head to a place called the Brickskeller. It's a bar up the street that has been run by the same family since 1955. Very interesting, friendly and original place.

title: “simple but a great bargain”
text:
I read some bad reviews on this place before I went, but I was just looking for an inexpensive place to stay near the wharf,
 Simple, clean, comfortable describe this place to a T. It even has free parking which is a BIG deal in this area. You are in easy walking distance of all the tourist areas on the waterfront without all the cost.
 I also read the staff was unfriendly. I didn't find that at all . They gave me a nice quiet room and helped me park so I wouldn't get hemmed in. Upon checking out, they asked me if everything was all right.
 Room was dated but very clean and comfortable. Bathroom was HUGE and clean.
 If you want glamour, this place is not for you. If you want to save your money for all the fun in SF, then give it a try for a very good bargain

title: “Great hotel in NYC”
text: Stayed at Hotel Lola June 7th & 8th located on 30th between Madison & Park. Was pleasantly surprised when we entered the lobby....beautiful! The room was very clean and spacious enough and a very nice bathroom but on the small side ! No view but that didn't matter since we were out of the room most of the day. I got a decent rate and would stay here again when I return. Great deal!

title: “Excellent value”
text: We stayed here for 5 nights in July 2009 while in the San Diego area to visit SD Zoo and Sea World. Our one bedroom suite was clean, comfortable and very spacious for 2 adults and one child. We had a king bed in the bedroom and the couch in the living room folded out into a bed. There was an extra mattress pad on top of the mattress and the check-in agent even offered to bring up another mattress pad when we checked-in, so we had 2 cushiony pads and the bed was comfortable. We did request 2 beds on the top (3rd) floor and didn't receive either request, so that was a slight disappointment, but it turned out just fine. Our room looked out over the pool and was a nice view. There was minimal noise from being so close to the pool and they closed it promptly at 10pm. Our room had free WiFi and there was a laundry room that was free (bring your soap).There was a free, full breakfast every morning with eggs, waffles, breakfast meats, pastries, oatmeal, cereal, juice, etc. Tues-Thurs night there was a free "dinner" that we were surprised to see. The first night they had grilled hamburgers and hot dogs. There was tap beer and saki, too! If you'd like to grill your own food, they have a really nice patio area with 2 propane grills and they provide the utensils. It took us about 30 minutes or less to get to Sea World, zoo, Coronado start to finish. The neighborhood was very clean, nicely landscaped and seemed like a business park type of neighborhood. A CostCo, Target, CVS and many other stores were nearby. Overall, considering the full kitchen, the separate bedroom, cleanliness, good customer service and good location, food included, this hotel was a very good value and we would not hesitate to stay here again in the future.

title: “Clean, quiet, convenient!”
text: In all of the great American cities that I have visited, there is one hotel that stands out for some reason. Either it is convenient to the major attractions, especially a Convention Center if that is the prupose of the trip, as some of them are for me. It could be close to fine restaurants, fun bars and lounges or sports venues. It also needs to be full service, with a caring staff, easy parking, comfy, clean beds and rooms, and an overall great experience. The Marriott Downtown Philadelphia is all of these. Although the SportsComplex is not adjacent to the hotel, it is easily reachable by car, cab or the Broad St. Subway line. It is a block from the newly expanded Pennsylvania Convention Center, across the street (literally) from Reading Terminal Market, a MAJOR East Coast attraction and treasure, and around the corner from the historic and magnificent Philadelphia City Hall. It has enough restaurants and bars within walking distance to make it tough to choose just one! The staff is courteous, including the parking valets, bell men, front desk, housekeeping staff, etc, etc. The rooms are quiet, even though you are on a very busy street in a major ciy and the beds are too die for, making it hard to get up and be ready to face the business day. So, my suggestion is to go for a long weekend to fully enjoy it! Get to Old City and see Independence Hall and the Liberty Bell. go to Penn's Landing and enjoy the panoramic views of the Delaware River or take in a game, at the Sports Complex, where there is a major league team always in season. A great hotel for a great American city!

title: “BAD STAY”
text: My stay here was an unfortunate start to my family cruise vacation. Poor service, dirty rooms, especially the bathrooms! And overall poor experience!

title: “Love it!!!”
text:
This is an amazing small hotel right on the wharf in San Fan. We had a delux ocean room and woke each day to the Bay bridge and the ferries going out to the famous Alcatraz !
The staff were amazing in every way and nothing I can say will explain the service and quality of this hotel.

title: “Classy and well-located”
text: We were in Manhattan for an event and stayed at The Lucerne with our adult children. Well-located on the Upper West Side, it was our first stay at this hotel and it exceeded our expectations. Easy to get to, convenient valet parking, lovely spacious lobby. The room was large by Manhattan standards and perfectly appointed. The staff was gracious and very helpful.

title: “Great location for family with shuttle service for attractions.”
text:
We had a great stay thanks in part to Mariano Soto, the evening desk clerk. He suggested our meal locations every evening. He was able to suggest ones that we could walk to or he could get the shuttle to bring us. Each meal was great food and decent price.
The hotel is an older hotel, but they have redone the rooms. They aren't perfect rooms, but the location is good enough to get past the old room. Having two Queen beds with a good hotel staff make it a great family hotel.
We made it to Seaworld, Zoo and airport using the hotel shuttle. We were able to catch the Old Town Trolley Tour by just walking to the bus sign. Location was very important since we did not rent a car for the visit. The hotel staff helped us get tickets to some of the attractions, and suggested we buy etickets and print them at their computer for better deals.

title: “Location, service and style”
text:
Stayed here for 3 nights at the end of August. From being recognised on arrival by their excellent General Manager, Nabil Moubayid the whole stay was just perfect. First thing to note is location, about a 10-15 walk from the blue line at Clark/Lake it is easy to get to from the airport and with the Red Line stop at Grand close by everywhere in the city is not too far. Just a block or so to Michigan Avenue and with restaurants and bars on your doorstep its an ideal location.
Service at the desk is friendly, and efficient with minimal wait. As has been noted ensure you join the InTouch program for WiFi and other extras. The bedroom was spacious with comfortable beds and the bathroom had good quality toiletries. The Gym on the 17th floor was well equipped and spotless. Plenty of towels and cups for iced water. Looking out over the city as you exercised was something I'll remember for a long time.
Our deal came with breakfast and this was again all that you would expect from such a great hotel. On our final night it rained heavily, we had hoped to discover more of the city rather than more of the hotel however we stayed in for the bar and the restaurant in Sable which is part of the hotel. So glad we did the drinks and the food were fantastic and for anyone staying here they are a must. This hotel has had some great reviews which is why we booked it and I can see why it rates so highly. It may not have the huge lobby areas of some hotels which make you go wow, but you don't stay in reception and here the investment has gone into first rate service from all the staff at the hotel. For my next trip to the US I'm looking at Boston, I'll be looking to book another Kimpton and hoping it matches this.

title: “The Pool”
text: I stayed there at the Days Inn for 2 days and I liked the rooms, and the friendliness that I was given at check in. I was at the pool and jacuzzi and liked how clean it was. I also liked the breakfast in the morning..mmm.. good Texas shaped waffles!! I will definitely recommend it to my friends and family. I also like the rate I was given, not to expensive considering they have cable, HBO, and big flat screen TVs! Over all.. good rating.

title: “absolutely nothing special”
text:
Our first time in N.Y
The hotel is an 70' styled hotel and its overprized.The position is great.I missed an air coz u cant open the window in N.Y so the air condition is going to kill ya.I like fresh hotel welcome reception and this hotel wasn't for that prize what it should be.ok for dirty N.Y city.Not for us.I am sorry.

title: “A pleasure for all reasons”
text: I've been staying in Boston for over 30 years in a great variety of lodgings, from really expensive to a night in the lounge at Logan Hilton after they lost my reservation! So I took a chance on this place, principally on location, next door to the T. I thought it was outstanding from the moment of check in to my 5.00 am departure the next day. Room exceptionally clean, instant wi-fi, etc. Well worth a visit

title: “Good Location, Crowded Lobby”
text: Stayed here 1 night on HHpoints over Thanksgiving weekend. While the location is wonderful, the management of crowds was poor. When checking in, a staff member in the entranceway looked at me with a puzzled look as we removed our bags from a taxi. The check-in/out line was quite long - even using the Hilton Diamond area, I waited for close to 15 mins to check out. The Executive lounge was crowded and to capacity both in the evening and in the morning. The room was nice size and comfortable. The location is nice close to 5th Ave shopping, Central Park and Times Sq/Theater Dist.

title: “Good value in the financial district”
text:
Millenium Hilton is located directly across the street from the new construction at ground zero. The noise from the construction will not be a bother at the higher floors. It is conveniently located near a subway line and there are plenty of taxis out front. Also within a few blocks are some decent food selections (deli, sushi, fast food). These are all far less expensive than eating at the hotel.
