I was surprised and disappointed to see that nine years after the horrible 9/11 attack on the world trade center, that the location is still not much more than a giant hole in the ground. I was expecting to see more progress. The hotel staff is friendly and I would certainly stay here again.
Here is a tip for travellers coming in from JFK. To avoid nasty NYC traffic and save at least $45 on cab fare, take the Air Train from JFK to Jamaica Station. At Jamaica Station transfer to the E subway line which ends at the World Trade Center (roughly 14 stops). Once at the World Trade Center, find the Church Street exit. This will let you out directly across the street from the Millenium Hilton. There are ticket kiosks that sell Metrocards at the Air Train JFK terminal and also at Jamaica Station. It was just as fast if not faster than taking a taxi, much less hassle than sitting in traffic, and far cheaper.

title: “Great but very, very posh”
text:
Just returned from a five night stay at The Sofitel.
Going for a 21st celebration the hotel noted this and left a complimentary bottle as seems to be the norm now. 
Rooms were very well looked after. At times felt a little under dressed though as many seemed to be their on business and we were there for pleasure. Did receive some funny looks in the lobby but hey who treks round on holiday in a suit, I do that at work back here!
One or two slight problems. We were told by the doorman that as it was Parade on Thursday we should leave at 12pm for a 6pm flight as traffic would be heavy and we could be in traffic for sometime. It wasn't and we arrived at 12.30pm. So 5 and half hours of waiting for us. Secondly a charge for the inhouse restaurant was placed on my bill - despite me never visiting it. Thankfully this was soon cleared up. 
Visited the Red Flame once and found it to be fine for a quick grab and go.
Overall I'd say 4/5, it's a really nice hotel, maybe aimed at the better dressed traveller on business in my opinion than twenty somethings on a few nights break.

title: “Good choice for overnight stopover for transit in CLT”
text:
I was doing an overnight stopover and needed a hotel close to CLT airport. Hotel offers free shuttle service, which was smooth and with short waiting time. 
On the arrival got room assigned quickly - also scored an upgrade to suite as Club Carlson Gold Elite member. 
Room was of usual Country Inn standard - something I would classify as usual 3 star in the US. Bed was comfortable. Due to being a suite, I even had 2 bathrooms, of which I used just one.
Did not have breakfast due to early departure.
Shuttle back to the airport was on time and quick.
All in all, fully met my aims - good place for overnight stopover while transiting in CLT.
However, if you are looking for seeing downtown - I would suggest something in the city centre.

title: “Comfort in the middle of the city”
text:
I have stayed at this Hampton In before and it did not disappoint this time either. I got a King bed room this time, and the bed was comfortable as expected. The bathroom was clean, the water was hot and of sufficient pressure.The breakfast did not have as extensive a selection as before, but had 4 waffle makers, pastries, fruit, yogurt, breads, coffee, and juice.
The exercise room is open 24 hours, but I was too tired to use it. The pool is open 8am - 10pm each day, so I missed that as well, but it looked like it was clean and maintained.
The staff is friendly and helpful - they even helped me once when another hotel had bumped me. The Hampton Inn staff did a better job of finding me a room and giving me directions than the other hotel that bumped me did.
The hotel is a short walk under the convention center from the Hard Rock Cafe and other attractions along Market Street, especially the Reading Terminal Market.

title: “Just Average”
text:
If you choose this place is either bussinesss or for the next door sport ground so do not complain, it is enough. I would not come here for vacation\holiday\relax etc...
I stayed 2 night while working at the shipyard, and it has been no more than fair, staff ?? just average.

title: “Nice but, too noisy!”
text: We stayed 2 nights at the Amalfi. The first night was Thursday and it was fine. The second night, Friday, was a completely different story. There is a nightclub next to the hotel, only separated by a wall. The club played extremely loud dance music with booming bass until 4 am. The front desk said they could go nothing. In the morning, the management said the "sounds of the city" were not under their control so they would not work with me on reducing the bill. I paid good money and expected a restful night's sleep. But instead I had to drive all day on 2 hours of sleep. The Amalfi did not provide a quiet or restful environmnent. The bell man told me as we were leaving that many customers complain about the night club and it's ridiculously loud music. Beware of staying here if you go to bed before 4 am. We will not be going back!

title: “Ocean Park Inn made our vacation stay a relaxing pleasure!”
text: My wife and I had stayed a Ocean Park Inn several years ago but we were checking out other places on the beach. However, the several front desk people I talked with were so helpful and full of information. I called back several times to disuss pricing (I made reservations several months in advance of our stay), accomodations and amenities and each time I was more impressed with the front desk service and attention to detail. As a former purchasing agent I'm used to asking detailed questions, pushing for the best pricing, etc. Each person was helpful, informative and courteous. From the time we arrived until the time we left our stay was relaxed, the room quiet, the pool and spa clean and the staff friendly and helpful. The breakfast area had just been remodeled and we were told that the rooms would be updated next. The family ownership seems to be working very hard to be a restful vacation retreat. Richard

title: “Great family location”
text: This was a family weekend get away and we could not have selected a better location. We enjoyed the stay so much. Barton Creek is a very family friendly facility! The staff was outstanding. Everyone from valet, front desk, concierge to waiters were friendly and very helpful. I would recommend any family to select this location for a vacation.

title: “New, beautiful, clean hotel”
text: This hotel is new, beautiful and very clean. Rooms smelled clean and fresh. Staff was delightful, very helpful and friendly. Bedding was clean, smelled good, comfortable. Mattress and pillows were nice and comfortable. There was absolutely no road noise at night which is very important to me; however, I'm not sure if the interior walls are extremely thin or if people are just that inconsiderate. It was the weekend of the rodeo and people came & went at all hours. You could here them stomping above you and in the hallways. Our room was 310 and right by elevator. I think a room on the fourth floor and at the end of the hallway would be ideal here. I did call the front desk about all the noise and he did check it out for me. The facility had security at night and the parking lot was well lit. There was an indoor pool but we didn't get to use due to lack of time. Internet was free but again we didn't use. Free continental breakfast was good and typical for this type of hotel. I will definitely stay here again but maybe just ask for a different room location.

title: “Fantastic stay”
text: I was at the hotel during January 2012 for a business trip and was thrilled with the hotel. The location is fantastic with the hotel being within walking distance of theatres, shopping and Central Park. The room was exceptionally clean and very comfortable. The view isn't particularly impressive, but those are hard to come by in NYC. The complimentary continental breakfast and evening wine and cheese is a nice touch. In short I was very happy with the hotel. It's location and value are hard to match. Would definitely stay again.

title: “Great hotel”
text: This hotel was absolutely great for a vacation. The rooms are large, well decorated and immaculate. The hotel is in a great location, safe and close to the Metro. The staff couldn't have been more cooperative and pleasant. Parking is $20 extra, but guaranteed; some of the more expensive hotels told us we might have to find our own parking! I would recommend this hotel to anyone going to DC.

title: “Clean motel and friendly check in by Raj”
text:
Stayed during Labor day 2012.
We had two rooms 213 and 214 we stayed for one night, My first impression looks like la Quinta.
I was wrong, I had really easy check- in and once in my rooms I noticed tidy, clean room, the rooms have a good seize bathrooms and decorations are up to date. Beds are very comfortable and the sheets look new. Overall a good experience and would stay here again much better than la Quinta. The breakfast is ok, ready to get you started.

title: “Great Western-style Hotel”
text:
A beautiful hotel wth gorgeous rooms, comfortable beds, beautiful bathrooms, and great toiletries.They are furnished with Western decor in a tasteful manner ( not over-the-top tacky) . 
Staff were super: professional, helpful, and friendly , with the exception of one very young lady in the gift shop, who was borderline rude and indifferent--most unusual for friendly, hospitable Texas folks.
The room was so lovely and cool that i was too comfortable to move to the outdoors heat!! 
The only factor that would make me reconsider a future stay is the hotel's location. While it is directly across the street from the Convention Center, it is not within walking distance of the tourist-intrest areas of Ft Worth. However, the MOlly Trolley stops at the hotel.

title: “Great Stay...would return!”
text: My husband and I came to Chicago and stayed at the Intercontinental for one night. We were able to check in at 10:30a and had absolutely no problems. Staff was very nice and helpful. Our room was a corner room with a great view and clean. There was some wear and tear on the desk but for one night it didn't really matter. They do need to invest in a exhaust fan for the bathroom as it steamed up and it appears that it is causing the paint to come off as there were several areas on the walls and ceiling that had been damaged. Overall a great stay for the price I paid through hotwire.com.

title: “another fine H.G.I”
text: friendly staff. Aked for some pizza delivery menus at about 11pm at the front desk, and we went with the one the lady reccmonded (sarpinos, I think) very good. The location was great for everything we wanted to do. there are several convience stores wihin a block or two. walking distance to just about anything you would be in that area of chicago for. even the free casino shuttle to the hammond horseshoe was only several blocks. $39 a night for self park seemed a little steep, then we noticed some of the other surrounding garages. turned out on par, if not reasonable in comparison. Beds and pillows were super comfy. price seemed to be better than other close hotels, and can't imagine an extra $20 or $40 a night gets you anything that much better. they let us check in at 12:30pm, only we were worried because we were right next to the elevator (proabaly because those get cleaned first). turned out as an advantage as we didn't notice any extra noise, and then didn't have to walk all the way down the hall either. will stay here next time for sure.

title: “Hotel in need of renovations”
text:
I stayed here for one night when I couldn't extend my stay at the Westin Copley Place. I thought it would be nice to try a hotel in a different part of the city. 
The service was adequate but the hotel itself is dark and old and in desperate need of a renovation. The decor is outdated and the furniture needed replacing. On the upside the room was clean and had a comfortable bed. 
There are better 4-star properties in Boston. Maybe I would consider staying here if the hotel is updated.

title: “Beautiful grounds, but a pathetic hotel”
text:
I had a business meeting at Humphrey's, so my husband and I stayed at the hotel. The landscaping is lovely, but the buildings and parking are a joke. 
We reserved a king room and were told we had been "upgraded". We were given a room with two full (not queen) beds. I see from other reviews this is a common ploy at Humphrey's. We went back and insisted on a king room and were given one. Both rooms we saw had been "renovated" but they still had an outdated feel, with cheap carpet and noisy air conditioners. The linens were of good quality and plentiful, however. 
The parking seems to be a big problem too. I don't think the charge for parking is unfair, but if they charge they need to provide a space. Everyone seems to be crammed together at one end. Additionally, the shuttle driver wanted to park in the spot we were in. Instead of just asking us to move (or clearly marking the space) he made up a story about it being an illegal spot so we would move. He then parked in the "illegal" spot 30 seconds later. 
The whole placed seemed very "halfway". Humphrey's is pretending to be a nice place, but they are seem to be putting all of their effort into the landscaping. Don't bother staying until they decide to work on being a hotel.

title: “I'd stay here again”
text:
Did a sister's get together at this hotel over President's Weekend. I agree with most of the other reviews.
A few things:
- This is a typical Marriott property. 
-Really nice & helpful staff. We felt welcomed every time we came through the doors.
-Nice pool area with fire pit. We sat out in the sun a bit but was too cold to use the pool and it was small, not for swimming, more for dipping.
-Great to have Trader Joe's & Von's nearby. We stocked our mini-fridge and ate breakfasts in the room.
- Did not eat in the hotel restaurant or use the bar but we did eat at Sammie's Woodfired Pizza near Trader Joe's - excellent!
- Nice walking path that goes past a Marina and down to Spanish Landing Park and beyond. Would be great if they had bikes available for use.
- Airplanes do land and take off frequently but not until about 6:30 a.m. It was never loud enough to wake us up.
- Free parking is a great perk. You will want a car here unless you do not mind walking a few miles to catch the trolley or to take a bus. The Old Town Trolley tour has a shuttle pick up next door at the Homewood Suite but they only pick up and drop off at a specified time per day.
- We did not have a balcony but there was a decent park & water view ; there were a few rooms with balconies overlooking the water(I would guess those are the suites).
- Room was spacious enough for two people and, other than some loud people coming in late, we had no troubles with noise.
My only real complaint is it was not warm enough!
I've stayed a few places in Sam Diego and so had my sister. So far we'd choose this place or Humphrey's Half Moon for our next trip.

title: “Exceptional service, great location, and fun for all”
text:
We recently returned from a wonderful stay at the Paradise Point. Originally went for business and took the family but turned out to be a fun and relaxing trip for the whole family.
We chose a one bedroom bungalow with king bed and sofa sleeper right by Paradise Cove (got a great deal). The spacious room was nicely renovated and had a mini kitchenette. We were just steps away from the sandy beach which the kids loved. We spent part of the day at Sea World which is within walking distance (but we opted for the short 2 minute drive since we have a little one), and then spent the rest of the day just playing in the sun and sand. At night, there are fire pits to keep warm and for making smores.
The rest of the hotel has a lot to offer and service was excellent all around. There are several pools, two restaurants (ate at Barefoot which was excellent), miniature golf, bicycle/mini carriage/boat rentals, and more. Unfortunately, we didn't have time to explore a lot of the hotel since we only stayed three nights and the kids wanted to go to Sea World for two of the three days. We could have easily stayed at the hotel the whole time and enjoyed every minute.
The only negative I can say is the high parking charge ($25 nightly), the beds were on the hard side, and the sofa sleeper was not comfortable at all but when are they ever comfortable.
We will definitely go back and hope to stay longer to fully enjoy all that this place has to offer.

title: “Perfect SPG PlatinumStay”
text: I would happily stay here again. All of my benefits were acknowledged and offered immediately when I checked in. Better yet, the clerk was so sweet and cheerful. The lobby bar and restaurant are good. My suite was perfectly sized and functional with a view of city hall. One caveat, some of the exterior ninth floor rooms have a large ballastrade just outside the window which cuts part of your view. Since I was a guest for just one night, I wasn't going to request a change. For some clientele the modern design might be a little much, but I thought it was great. I'm already considering a weekend in my schedule to return. Rittenhouse Square and the shops/cafes is only 5 minutes. The Westin may have the advantage on location but it's like any other Westin you could find. The workout area is filled with cardio equipment and some free weights, otherwise it's too smal for any weight machines. I did not mind, but if you want a full gym experience, this won't work. Concierge was very approachable and engaging which is nice in a hotel.

title: “Fine Setting for Girlfriends' 50th in New York!”
text:
Myself and 4 friends visited New York City to celebrate our 50th birthdays. Arrived Tues,July 5 and departed Sunday,July 10. No regrets, just fond memories.....
Hotel: Is a boutique hotel 1/2 block off Broadway. Very chic, quiet, comfortable beds, large rooms, AC, refrigerators, coffee bar, LCD screens (one in bathroom too), fresh continental bkfst with large assortment, wine hour at 4 pm. 
Location: Great spot. Right across the street from theatre hosting 'Book of Mormon'. Very active avenues on either end of the block but super quiet on the street it is located. Quick walk to Broadway and Time Square on one side, and 1/2 block to yummy eateries on other.
Price: As high season was in bloom, reasonable for location. We paid about $370/nite for 3 people. ($20 less/nite double occupancy) 
Taxi were quite reasonable $5 for close destinations, $10 to Met museum, $20 from Little Italy in heavier traffic, $31 - $36 from La Guardia airport including tip and tolls.
Dinner each eve including drinks, tip, and tax $25 (remember local eateries)
Comments: We had to push and push the front staff to change our room, as we originally had a brick wall out our window. Finally accommodated us.
 Breakfast does not have hot items, but pastries and bagels were always fresh, a couple of fruits, good coffee choices, several spreads, cereals, and fresh juice. 
At 4 pm is a wine hour. Are generous with the wine (one white and one red) offered with an assortment of cheese and crackers. Some variety of appetizers on different days would have been nice.
Super quiet rooms. We never heard anyone else and I hope they never heard us.
Beds so soft, still, and comfy. 
Activities: Each of us picked activities for us all to participate in on 'our ' day.
Statue of Liberty/Ellis Island, Museum of Metropolitan Art, Museum of Natural History, MoMa, Greenwich Village lunch tour, Macy's, 5th Ave, visit to Meat Packing District, China town, Little Italy, SoHo, Empire State (evening with audio tour was wonderful), Carriage ride through Central Park(not necessary if you've already toured Central Park), Chelsea Market, stroll the overline, Midsummer Nite Swing (got rained out so went to a Piano Bar :) instead).
Food: One of the friends is a resident of New York so she was able to recommend local restaurants and eateries that aren't widely advertised -many along 8th ave. Sorry don't have all the names, but also good selection in 'restaurant row'. 
Tasty martinis on top floor of 'W' hotel. 
Remember to always take breaks, real 1.5 hr breaks for special coffees, ales, cart food, and baked goods all day, every day!!
Enjoy your trip and your stay!

title: “You decide”
text: The room was nice except for the sheets were not cleaned because we found hairs in them and we found a dirty sock on the side of the bed in plain view. Also the bathroom was a sliding door and didn't close tightly so you didn't have privacy.

title: “Great Location”
text: The hotel is in a great location near the end of the f lines and near the cable cars. Easy to walk to Fisherman's wharf. A little dated, but clean...Parking price is $40/night - outrageous....

title: “Staff”
text:
I know we returned hom in May and it is very remiss of me not to have reviewed our stay in The Custom Hotel. iIwould like to say what a great hotel the Custom is. Very comfortable and the staffare friendly and professional. In particular I only have words of praise for Tomas. He is a credit to your establishment, professional and very knowledgeable.
Sharon and Ian Richards

title: “Safe bet”
text: We stayed at the Hyatt for a wedding weekend. The location of this hotel is great as you are within walking distance to many of Chicago's attractions and you are very near public transportation. We chose this hotel on this trip due to costs and location and we were not disappointed. The room was a decent size and very clean, however, the bathroom was small with poor lighting and very limited counter space. The staff was helpful and courteous. A helpful tip, on the day you leave make sure you give valet parking at least a half hour notice. When we went to leave we were told it would take them a half hour to get our car or we had the option to go and get in in the basement.

title: “Better for a short stay”
text: I stayed at the Westin for 5 nights for a business trip. This was not the best hotel in town for such a long stay, but it would have been fine for a one or two night stay. The beds are very comfortable and the room was clean. It is within walking distance of many office buildings and restaurants, although not as close to these as other hotels. The rooms do not have refrigerators. Even though I asked for one when I checked in, it was never sent to my room and I did not bother to ask again. The restaurant has very good food, but it was very expensive even for hotel prices. I did not have a room service menu in my room and when I asked for one I got a photocopied sheet of paper. The menu was very limited and extremely expensive, even for room service. There staff was very friendly and it was easy to get a cab the day I checked out. Overall, I would stay here again for a short trip but would choose a different hotel with more in-room ammenities for a longer stay.

title: “Above average, and worth another try.”
text:
This property was not as well maintained as some of the other Embassy Suites properties we have been to, but it is still worthwhile. We were here for four nights, and had meetings in the hotel. The banquet staff was outstanding, and made up for the physical shortcomings of the facilities.
Front desk staff was also helpful. Housekeeping was uneven, doing an incomplete job of cleaning for half of the days. Bed was comfortable, and the sitting/work area was very well done. A colleague did have some maintenance issues that they attempted to fix several times without success.
Restaurant was decent, but pretty limited. The breakfast was very good. The hospitality reception was disappointing when the food was only popcorn and pretzels. When they added veggies, cheese, chips and salsa, and so forth - as they did for two of the evenings - it was pretty good. Guess one should never complain about free drinks, anyway.
All in all, this is a venue that we would use again, and this is a hotel that is pretty convenient to the airport and to this part of the Denver area. Closer to the airport, downtown, and up north are all hotels we have used that we like better, but this one was a good enough value to rate another visit.

title: “Frat weekend type of hotel”
text: Stayed here recently based on it being a Wyndham and its proximity to certain downtown events. First off noticed the dated in design and serious deferred maintenance issues. Many doors looked like they have been "kicked in". Was told by a local that the property is for sale but no interest so explains why no new money being put back into the property.The "riverwalk" area is dissapointing as well. It looks like an idea from the 80's that didn't stand the test of time. I took a short stroll on it one afternoon and it felt urban and a bit unsafe. Agree with the comments that the staff are nice. Feel sorry for them as they are doing the best they can. Beds are horrible. No hot water. Ran out of towels both days. Dirty carpets, chipped paint. Popcorn ceilings. We went to an event across the river at the Hilton and it emphasized what a dump the Wyndham is. That all said, what a great venue for a Fraternity weekend bash! They should target that market. They won't care what you do to those rooms.

title: “Good quality but view and breakfast could be better”
text: The standard of the hotel is general good quality. But for us it matters to daylight and some kind of view from the window. So having a view to interior corridor is not enchanting. Breakfast being cerials and toast was not a little dissappointing. Two smaller things that takes the score a bit down from otherwise a very good hotel in a central place.

title: “Great Stay at the Omni”
text: We had a great stay at the Omni San Francisco over the Memorial Day holiday. Although there was no view, our room was well appointed and clean. Staff was friendly and service was above average. Service technician replaced our television set becuase it was not working. Location, in the financial district, was good even though rather dead on Sunday and Memorial Day. Close to the Embarcadero and ferry building where restraunts were open on Sunday afternoon. We would stay here again on another trip to San Francisco.

title: “Spotless, small hotel in Chinatown.”
text: Location = crap, unless you like or need to be living in Chinatown. But for value and cleanliness, it's hard to beat. One kind of expects a fleabag here, but what one gets is a spotless, new modern hotel, with ample space, all of the basic amenities (minus parking, which is hard to expect in New York City anyway), TV, clean bathrooms and attentive service. Would recommend overall, unless you have kids - in which case the rooms are probably too small. Also, don't come here if you're not used to the sounds of the big city - the Manhattan Bridge is going to be 20 yards from your window, with trains running every 3 minutes. Lullaby music to MY ears.

title: “Wonderful experience”
text:
My husband and I planned a weekend getaway and found a great deal at this Hotel. We researched the area and were excited about the Uptown area. Upon arrival we were greated by wonderful bellhops. We did the self-park just to save a little bit of money...we don't mind parking our own car! The front desk staff were so friendly and really made us feel welcome. We asked them for a great local restaurant and we were pleased with their suggestion. Elevators were slow but they are in the process of upgrading those so it was understandable. 
Our room was great! The bed was super comfortable and our room overlooked the pool. I did not like that the tv did not have a menu for ordering movies but it was fine. I read a review about no menu in the room. I found them menu in the book about the hotel. I did think the prices were high but not any higher than other hotels. 
The restaurant is being updated so they set-up a bar in the lobby and they also have a restuarant in one of their banquet halls. 
The location could not have been more perfect. It was nice being able to walk to just about everything.
We could not have asked for more...well maybe faster elevators but that is minor in my eyes. 
We plan to stay here again!

title: “Family Trip”
text:
Visited over Labor Day weekend when the area was quiet and a little easier for us new NYC visitors to navigate the city. Most famous attractions are a little further uptown, but that was fun to travel and explore. Hotel is very close to a couple of subway stations, walking distance to numerous restaurants, shops, we even walked to Liberty Ferry area, but that may be a little much (30 min or so) for older people or small children. Service in hotel is great. Rooms great. Didn't try the restaurant because we walked to some other small family style restaurants in the area - thanks Trip Advisor! 
Nothing to complain about this time. Book it!

title: “Nice Cute Place”
text: We stayed at Sleep Inn and Suites early March, its a nice cute place. It is clean and comfy. I like how the rooms are big and there is plenty of room to put luggage and bags around the room. Our main focus for the trip to Baltimore was the Aquarium which was loads of fun. This hotel was pretty close to the Aquarium and the staff were super frendly. We called in advanced cuz we got lost and the Manger on duty made sure we got to the hotel with the quickest route. I would def recommend this hotel.

title: “Central location - Okay Stay”
text:
Not the nicest hotel I have stayed in, but okay. Additional fees for internet and fitness center add up. Room was small, bathroom was tiny. Unfortunately, I was under the weather during my business stay, so when I wasn't working, I was attempting to relax in the room. Bed was comfortable. TV channels were not ideal...very few of them with nothing on. I was close to the elevators, and you can hear them humming non-stop, every hour of the day...but I got used to it as white noise in the background.
The lobby looked like it would be fun to hang out in...bar with plenty of seating and opportunites to mingle and people watch and flat screen tv's.

title: “Well-Located Hotel With Drawbacks”
text:
Went to Philly last week for the Annual Flower Show held at the Convention Center. Hotel is 10 mins. walk from the Convention Center, City Hall and centrally located near restaurants and shops and most tourist attractions. Street signs pointing the way to tourist attractions are great. 
I was on the 14th floor and had 2 double beds. Nice linens and good shower. I requested a small refrigerator that was delivered to my room shortly after I checked in. Was not too happy with the heat. It came from a wall-installed air conditoning unit and I had to keep it on 80 to get the temp. to 76. It was very noisy.
The staff were wondefrul...very friendly and accommodating. The included breakfast was nothing special...juices, coffee, tea, scrambled eggs, biscuits, bagels, cereal and hot cross buns. Oranges, apples and bananas were also availble. Would have been nice to have some yogurt and cut fresh fruit.
I paid a little over $200 for the room with a sr. discount. Not worth the money but the location and proximity to the Annual Flower Show was considered in choosing this hotel.

title: “Great hotel for our family”
text: This is a very nice hotel in a good location. Convenient to Subway, restaurants, sights. We had a deluxe double plus rollaway for family of four and it was fine. Nice bathroom! I would stay here again if visiting Boston!

title: “Fine for some”
text: I have stayed here a few times, and each time it has been pretty good. Rooms are small, tv's are small, no mini bar or anything like that. Its a business travelers hotel, so the frills are not there. The beds are a bit hard, and they had no extra pillows or blankets available. On my last trip I found out that the doors to the rooms have no soundproofing at all. I was awoken several times by people talking in the hall, and it sounds as if the door is open. Always clean and the employees are always friendly and helpful. In the end, I will stay elsewhere from now on.

title: “dont go here”
text: Checked into this hotel and then straight back out. The check in staff were friendly, but this hotel is in a bad area, shares a parking lot with a Shoneys and looks like your car would be stolen in about 5 mins. The hotel is definitely beyond its use by date. we were just passing through and got the hotel from priceline so not sure how close it was to get to airport. If your with your family i wouldnt feel safe staying at this hotel. Room was clean looking but bathroom was tiny and had a weird tiny square toilet which i assume was futuristic in 1960 when it was probably installed. The Photos on the website are extremely flattering and dont really represent the overall look of the place. The staff seem like theyre doing the best they can with the bad location and old rundown building.

title: “Disappointing”
text:
First day I checked in, my tub was leadking - easy fix, but I should not have had to call maintentenance to do this - maids should have caught this. Second day no maid service AT ALL until I called at 6 p.m. - then didn't change sheets. Third day coffee was not replentished, and I had to request my sheets be changed. Sleep was not well with the air conditioner not going off at all when it got to the correct temperature. Was disappointed with the fact there was no refrigerator in the rooms. For $50 you could get many of them and put them in each room. If each room normally goes for $449, but I paid $189 for conference rate, you can still get them and be money ahead and make many guests very happy. Some in my party had kids and wanted milk to put in a fridge, but you didn't have them. Front desk said you didn't have any either. For an upscale hotel, one would think that would be as basic as having a hair dryer in the room. The fact the bathrooms are so small, a fridge would make up for this. 
We rented a car for one night, and the cost to park was way too expensive - $32 a night??!!

title: “Great location!”
text: We spent one night at Homewood Suites and then one night at the Conrad and got a chance to compare both. The Conrad was definitely a great experience, with a friendly staff. We were there during Halloween and everybody had a costume and the staff seemed genuinely happy! Too bad the breakfast is not included though but not an issue since there are plenty of choices around. I suggest going to the Corner Bakery on Michigan street (take the stairs up from Illinois street which is the street next to the hotel). Would definitely recommend this place.

title: “Friendly staff and great location :)”
text:
I had went with my mom prom shopping to NY for aweekend and being that she loves Marriott we stayed there. I wanted to stay at the W but im kind of glad we stayed there. The service was AWESOME: first our rooms got messed up but one of the front desks (his name was Sye :)) and he upgraded us AND gave us a discount then when we needed to check out the conicerge (Tony) and bellhops were also really friendly in helping us get to the airport on time. And you get a great bang for you buck your like in the middle of everything (Forever21 across the street AHH :D) and my room seemed really spacious.
If i was gonna be really pciky the only thingy i didnt like were the slightly small bathrooms and the uncomfortable towels :S hated those towels!

title: “Lovely”
text:
The location of this hotel is perfect and our room had a great view of the town square from the window. The staff were efficient, the 3 course meal at the hotel restaurant was excellent and the room was spacious and clean. The subway station is right next door to the hotel, however, the entrance to the station was closed on the weekend (it was open on Friday) so you have to walk an extra block from the other street exit. 
There are not many places to go in the evening in this area though. 
Advice: if you want to go up the top of the Washington Monument, queue up around 7.30-8am to get free tickets for that day only otherwise they'll be gone. If you can, book tickets on the internet before you go (around $1.50). The best site is the Capitol building, Washington Monument and Lincoln Memorial, however, the reflecting pool had been drained and had no water there!! The museums are excellent and free but you'll have to queue to get past the thorough security pass wherever you go.

title: “Historic Area Motel”
text:
Very adequate motel within walking distance of historic sites in downtown Philadelphia. A nice free shuttle if you prefer not to walk.
The motel rooms were clean and adequated maintained. Shower spray could not be adjusted. 
The breakfast is a typical motel free breakfast with cereals and breads with coffee and juice.
Parking is expensive at $17.50 per day in addition to room rate. Parking was convient.
Penn's Landing is across the street with musem and tours. Good resturant.

title: “Great place to stay with group!!”
text: We stayed at The Soho Loft about a month ago and had a wonderful time! I was traveling with 10 friends and it was between this or a 3 star hotel we found in midtown so we decided to change it up a bit. The loft is in the most amazing part of Manhattan! If you are not familiar with Soho it is the prime location, great food, fashion, nightlife and easy to get everywhere. I would def suggest staying here if you are coming to Manhattan with a group of friends!

title: “Great Location + Excellent Amenities = Must Stay Hotel”
text:
I honestly cannot say enough good things abbout the Westin Hotel in Seattle. My wife and I stayed there from 10/20-10/22 and again from 10/26-10/27. As per my normal review format, I'll provide an honest assessment of the pros and cons. I'll also include some useful travel tips.
POSITIVES:
1. LOCATION: The Westin Seattle, located on the corner of 5th Avenue and Stewart Street, has it all in the all-important category of location. You are in close proximity to all of the major Seattle attractions: Pike's Public Market, Elliot Bay Waterfront, Pioneer Square, Smith Tower and Seattle Center/Space Needle. The Westin Seattle in the center of some pretty major shopping areas including Macys, Nordstroms and two malls: Pacific Place and Westlake Center (which also is a station for the Monorail that leads directly to Seattle Center). Just about everything you would want to see in Seattle can be done quickly and conveniently from the Westin Seattle.
**TRAVEL TIP 1 - Bartell Drugs: Across the street from the hotel is Bartell Drugs, a typical drug & sundries store. This is a good place to get inexpensively priced snacks, drinks and OTC medications (as well as prescriptions). It will save you money compared to using the mini-bar.
**TRAVEL TIP 2 - Airport to/from Seattle Westin Hotel: I recommend NOT taking a taxi-cab to and from the airport (which will be costly, between $35-45. Take the shuttle bus: The Gray Line Downtown Airporter (round trip tickets are good for 12 months and cost about $35. It stops right at the Westin. Take advantage of it.
2. ROOM FEATURES: Standard quality features with 3 notables: The beds are excellent (comfortable and clean), there were cordless room phones (a nice touch) and room safe for valuables (I personally think every hotel should have one). There are also standard room amenities such as iron, hair dryer, TV and coffee maker (with complimentary Starbucks coffee... of course). NOTE: They will provide the USA-Today newspaper by your door each morning, but will add $0.75/day to your bill. If you aren't interested, let them know in advance.
3. VIEWS: Whether in the North or South tower, you'll have a fantastic view of the city. I recommend requesting rooms on the upper floors for better views. On my second stay, I was in room 2434 North Tower ... I could see Space Needle and Mt. Rainier (at least I believe it was Mt. Rainier).
4. STAFF: Friendly and very professional. They are quick to resolve any potential issues that might arise. Of special note are the bellstaff (exceedingly helpful) and the concierge (knowledgeable of the area and will work hard to get tickets or restaurant reservations).
NEGATIVES: To be honest, there aren't a lot of negatives. Just standard hotel things you will want to avoid.
1. "REFRESHMENT CENTER" (mini-bar): Overpriced consumables. Why bother? Do you really want to pay $4.00 for a snickers bar or $3.50 for a can of Pepsi? (yes, these are actual prices). Go across the street to Bartell Drugs and get them for a fraction of the cost.
2. LAMONT'S GIFT SHOP: Again. Why bother? The sundries are overpriced and who would really want to purchase souvenirs from the hotel when the entire city is out there with items of better quality and authenticity. 
3. INTERNET SERVICES: The in-room internet is $16/day. There is also an internet room in the lobby that charges a fee for usage. You'll do better finding a coffee shop or bookstore that provides free WiFi (they're everywhere in Seattle). However... there is one benefit to the Westin Seattle's internet service:
** TRAVEL TIP 3 - Free Boarding Pass Printing: Although the internet room in the lobby charges a fee for internet usage, you are allowed to print your airline boarding pass for free. This is fantastic (a big plus, especially for Southwest Flyers who want the 'A' boarding pass).
CONCLUSION: The Seattle Westin has it all when it comes to location, service and amenities. If you are staying in downtown Seattle, you won't be disappointed.

title: “Hotel was nice and staff was very kind and helpful .I'll be back.”
text: This was my second stay at the hotel and both times staff was kind and helpful . I appreciated that they did not mind doing their job with a smile and they make you feel welcomed.,

title: “1920's elegance + every modern convenience!”
text: The Monaco Baltimore Hotel is a lavishly restored / preserved building from the 1920's with a stunningly beautiful entryway (a white marble stairway, Tiffany glass, towering ceilings, lavish red carpet)--an opulence amid which we could easily imagine Scott and Zelda Fitzgerald feeling right at home! Yet our (very large) room had been wonderfully updated with a state-of-the-art television, very fast Wifi, a truly elegant marble bathroom, and luxurious bedding. The staff was unfailingly friendly, helpful, and attentive, and the convenient location in Baltimore's Harbor area couldn't be better! Just down the street are all the attractions of the Harbor area and many chain stores and restaurants. Three blocks in the opposite direction, there are many independent ethnic restaurants and boutiques. In the historic preservation of hotel properties, there is always a delicate balance between preservation and the needs of today's guests. More than any other such property I have ever stayed in, the Monaco Baltimore gets it EXACTLY right! HIGHLY recommended!!

title: “everything in its place”
text: Staff, restaurants, bed, amenities, all perfectly sorted and as expected. I slept great and was treated fairly. Nothing flashy, nothing difficult, and nothing disagreeable just what I want in a hotel. Pool is silly small....

title: “Great Hotel...Great Service”
text: We stay her about 1-2 times per year. The service is excellent. We really appreciate how we are treated at check-in and in the restaurant. The rooms are clean and we are very comfortable here. One of the best Marriott's we visit on a routine basis. Very convenient to the airport and a shuttle service is available which is key for us.

title: “Make sure you don't pay full price for this hotel”
text: Picked this hotel because of its location to Time Warner Cable Arena, and the price. Not a bad location, but the renovations going on at the hotel didn't make it worth the bargain price. Instead of wake-up calls, someone from the front desk would come bang on our door to wake us up. The pipes burst at one point and we had NO water for the day. The bathroom was cramped and not very clean, and the shower flooded the bathroom several times because it only had a half door between the shower area and the rest of the bathroom. However, there is plenty of parking ($13 a night) and a great on-site cab service to downtown areas.

title: “Great Place to stay”
text: I am an SPG gold member and often stay at this hotel when in LA. Absolutely one of my favorites. Rafael at the front desk was great. Pool is awesome. Valet is pricey, but convenient. I think it is $24 a day. Self Parking is $15. Starbucks in lobby, thats if you need to go down there.Because starbucks cofee is also in the room.Have stayed at this hotel approximately 6 or 7 times and have always ejoyed my stay. Great staff, all of them. Free wifi for SPG gold & Platinum members. Nice gym area. And thats all i can think of.

title: “Excellent stay near airport”
text: This hotel has very nice, clean rooms with quality furnishings at reasonable prices. Very conveniently located for an air traveler. Staff is freindly and made sure I got to the airport in plenty of time!

title: “Great hotel, highly recommended”
text: This is a great base to explore San Diego. Only minutes to the zoo and with free parking and a lovely area to walk along the water - there's a great playground about 5 minutes along the path which our kids loved. The breakfasts are very nice and so are the evening reception light dinners. It was great to have an early dinner with the kids without having to go out, although there are plenty of places to eat nearby. Rooms are spacious and new, everything was very clean and it's great to have the kitchen to make a quick snack.

title: “Very good experience, better than others in this motel chain”
text:
We stayed at this Comfort Inn for several days in May and found it to be very comfortable, more so than others I've stayed in on driving trips. The room is what you've seen many times before, but it's also really clean. (I felt okay walking barefoot on the carpet.) The sheets were fresh and crisp, and the bathroom, while not new, was well cleaned. It had a microwave, small frig and a safe (which you can opt out of paying for).
Front-desk service was professional, and the lobby had a coffee stand, filtered water and an internet work station. Free wi-fi is a good benefit, and you can get passes to a nearby gym. Breakfast included sausage and eggs (hard-boiled or microwaved rounds), little yogurts and a waffle station, plus fresh fruit. It has a small pool and some days I saw people sunning there.
Though on a busy street, it's situated so the traffic noise is muted. It's not a pretty area, but a little way down the block is a Starbucks with a shaded outdoor sitting area, though Swork, past the stoplight, has better coffee. Very near is a Walgreens, which sells wine, so bring a corkscrew for an end-of-day glass of wine. We walked half a block to La Fuente for a good Mexican dinner. Also in walking distance is Spitz, a kebab restaurant with good Yelp ratings, though we didn't eat there. Target and Macy's are a two-minute drive away.
Our check-out receipt included a printed thank-you card, which I've never gotten before from a modestly priced motel. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “First time in San Diego”
text: We were only in California for a short time, having come over for a Wedding in LA. We decided to drive down to San Diego and booked into the US Grant. What a fantastic hotel. The foyer is stunning. We had our car parked for us. We had a fabulous room with a huge bath tub. Great location beside numerous restaurants and bars. It was a great introduction to the city. Only drawback was the fee for internet access in the room. However, it was free in the foyer.

title: “Ouch- $300. per night!”
text:
I realize this is New York City, accommodation is expensive. The 2 best things for us: location and breakfast.
Anywhere else, this is a 3 star hotel, tops. The bathroom looked worn. Carpet in the room didn't feel clean to me.
I may stay here again, but try to get it at a price that's not so painful!!
Our room was large, and breakfast was well worth it for the kids.

title: “Worst Hotel I've seen in years”
text: Don't even think about making a reservation... Poor service, tiny old rooms, paper cups in your bathroom instead glasses, noicy A/C, empty minibar, antique TV etc. will never ever go back.

title: “What a lovely surprise - one of the best in NYC”
text: The NYC East side Marriott was a fantastic surprise for us. We must have been in a newly renovated room because it is very hard for me to imagine that all the rooms can be this nice, and I am rather picky – you can look at my other reviews for NYC rooms and you will find this ranks higher than most. The room furniture seemed brand new and very tasteful. The beds were better than the most of the luxury chains, with 300+ thread count sheets, full down comforters (and an extra one in closet too), partial down pillows AND regular pillows, lovely soft chenille throws on each bed -all so clean and new. The mattresses were the highest quality. The toiletries in the immaculate marble and granite bathroom were quite nice higher end products in great packaging and a perfectly clean double shower curtain and plush towels were also very pleasing. The bathroom was quite luxurious compared to your average NYC 4* hotel, and better than any of the 4* hotels in NY I’ve been at in last few years. The plasma TV had many channels including HBO. The staff were friendly and courteous and efficient – checking in took 2 minutes. The hotel is opposite the Intercontinental and “W” hotels and a block from the Waldorf Astoria. It’s location is fantastic and there is a subway line right there, not to mention easy access to the better restaurants on 2nd Ave. The room we got was absolutely spotless, as were all the public areas and hallways leading to it - a stark contrast to some of the ghetto 4* hotels we have stayed at in NY before. The lobby area is quite small and not fancy, but very clean and much more appealing than the lobbies at other NY establishment – highly polished stone, nice furniture, clean carpets. The only “older” spot was the elevators which were a bit small and cramped and showed a bit of age. There is a small gym on the very top floor which you need to take two separate elevators to get to, no matter which floor you are on. It’s a bit cramped, but has gorgeous views of the city, and was very clean, with stacks of fresh towels ready to go. The only negative I can state about this hotel was that the noise level from the street was quite high, so the windows didn’t have enough sound protection for my taste, perhaps an issue on lower floors, as indicated by other reviews. I used ear plugs and all was fine. I highly recommend this hotel, but you may want to be sure you end up on a renovated higher floor, in case the other reviews are indicative of other floors or rooms that were not similar to ours.

title: “everything wonderful, but bring your own pillows”
text: We enjoy staying at this Wingate hotel on our trips to and from Phoenix for medical treatments. The staff and cleanliness of hotel are very good - the breakfasts available are excellent, beds are comfortable - but the pillows are not - Bring your own pillow for comfort.

title: “A fine hotel in a quiet spot”
text:
I was in doubt as whether to give 3 or 4 stars to this hotel, because it excels in some points but may use some renovation. 
Arrival: the lobby is marvelous. With the cascade, foliage and lake, really nice. Coi fishes require a lot of care, so it gives you a measure of how well it has to be maintained in order for the fishes to grow, and they seemed in good shape. The girls at the reception and all other services were extremely friendly and all of our small issues were well attended. A+
Room: The room was facing the garden, basically it faced a palm tree but it was ok, it provided good shade and kept the place cooler. All amenities were available in the room. Bathroom was ok. But we had to move some furniture (my little one tends to fall from the bed so we always need to create some barriers around his side of the bed) and we noticed that behind furniture the vacuum cleaner had not been used in quite a while. Daily cleaning was done, but from time to time you have to dust behind the beds too!! That took some points off. Also rooms start being worn out a bit, although this is not a big issue in my opinion.
Premises: very nice. We did not use the pool as kids liked the beach (see previous review for details), it was clean and calm (at least in the morning). Overall it is all well kept and clean.
We had breakfast at the restaurant and it was fine. We were away most of the day so you may want to refer to other reviews for local activities. 
I have to add that it is well located, in 15 minutes (driving) you can reach almost anything, which was the main reason of picking this hotel instead of the Coronado Loews. We did not regret the choice. It is placed in a friendly neighborhood too.

title: “Style with a Smile”
text:
We stayed at The Benjamin for 4 nights in Feb 06, having booked direct with the hotel for a daily rate of $249 inc breakfast.
We were a little apprehensive shortly before arriving, as there had been a number of recent poorer reviews on trip advisor.
However, we could not have been more pleased with the hotel and the service of the staff there. Nothing was too much trouble and everyone we spoke to was courteous, pleasant and extremely helpful.
The room was more than adequate (although don't expect 5 star)and we did not find noise a problem.
The breakfast was included in our price and well worth it as it set us up for the whole day, until the evening when we had dinner.
The hotel is a great base for all tourist attractions, shops and Broadway and we felt perfectly safe navigating our way around the city.

title: “HarborBLINDside Inn --> BEWARE!!!!!!!!!”
text:
I don't even know where to start...so I'll use their own Harborside Inn of Boston card that I found in my room for reference. First, on the top of the card it says "Classic Location & Comfortable Cost"--which I tend to agree with both but not in the same sentence. Yes, to be fair, this hotel is in a prime (or Classic--whatever that menas) location --T stop (Blue Line) right outside your front door, Aquarium down the street, North End fairly close and the Harbor within view (if you stand on the street --not from anywhere in the hotel with no virtually no windows). The Comfortable Cost is also true --at $160 it is a value--if other factors hold true --which they did not. For example, if you require your room to be cleaned once a day --be warned--this is NOT the place for you. Upon check-in, I was amazed that our room was so dirty. It should have been more clean, but instead of calling the front-desk we went out to explore Boston and start our vacation. The next day upon returning to our room at 4 pm, we were VERY SURPRISED to see that our room had not been cleaned. When I called the front desk, the first words were not I'm sorry (no, that would be too Four Seasons or Ritz for this place), but "We're just really busy." Okay, I'm pretty certain (and to be fair I have stayed at these hotels too) that a La Quinta, or Hampton Inn or one of the chains that are more bargain priced would have cleaned our room at least 1 time per 3 day stay. The management team decided that dropping a bag of towels off at our door would suffice. The next day (Day 3) we came back to our hotel around 3 pm--thinking that we would come back to a clean room--NOT SO! When asked about why this was not done for a 2nd day in a row, the management team said that first, that they were very busy (okay this excuse is worn out management team, like after the first time I heard it) and 2nd that the hotel service team had said we left a RED sign outside of our door (indicating that we would not like our hotel room serviced). I can't see the logice in that -and it was simply not true. Yes, hotel staff we DON'T want our room cleaned the entire time we're here --especially after I had already called down to them to indicate that it wasn't cleaned before. SCARY --!!! Please be advised that the management staff is terrible at this hotel! I've stayed at probably no less than 500 hotels in my lifetime, and I cannot think of a worse experience. When you are trying to differentiate yourselves in a competitive hotel lodging market like Boston's, the easiest way to do so is by having friendly, dependable service. This hotel fails on all levels. Even the check-in staff people look like they were scared of the management. When I went to address the issues in person with the Assistant Manager he said he was not able to make any management decisions and that the Manager would return the next day. Hello...is this 2005? Obviously we had some very strong feelings regarding our stay. Please, please be very wary of the price of staying at this hotel vs. the experience. Like the review on August 20th, left from the visitors from Salt Lake and the one before....as of late, this place seems like its going down like the Big Dig (which is VERY close to your hotel). Other negatives regarding this hotel....NOISE...two LOUD bar/nightclubs right below the hotel itself, the claustaphobic rooms (a window the size of a notebook and that's it), yes, there is vaulted ceilings--but I honestly was scared that 1/ a bat was going to fly out of the ceiling or 2/ exposed LOOSE brick was going to fall on me 3/ of the bathrooms--they are downright GROSS!--if you like dirt and grime these bathrooms have it and of course the peeling paint to accompany it 4/ unfriendly staff and management.
BEWARE BEWARE BEWARE! Don't get Harbor BLINDSIDED at this Inn.

title: “First Class - not one complaint”
text: My significant other and I recently spent 3 nights at The James and on the last day I said, "I wish we could stay longer". That good! The room was immaculate and a very pleasant surprise from the moment you open the door. Everything is high tech. Plasma TV, CD/Radio, Projection alarm clock (love that so much bought one today). If you wanted room service you got it from David Burke and the mini bar and liquor selection was plentiful. They even have a four legged friend menu. The bathroom was pleasant with bathrobes/slippers and upscale products provided. The bed was the best in a hotel ever. Linens were crip, white and fresh. Maid service twice daily with turn down service. Safe in room, ice delivered, iron, hairdryer all top of the line. The filtered window shades blacked out the light and matched the modern decor. Mid-century style with funky chair/ottman, cubes and a table with nightstands gave us plenty of room and felt like comforts of home. The staff was courteous and accommodating. The library, free internet access, in room wifi were extras we didn't expect . Bar/lounge areas seems to be frequented by locals enjoying cocktails and appetizers in the lobby. Funky artwork. Location, location, location. The best place we've ever stayed not only in Chicago. Highly recommend.

title: “Wonderful Stay!”
text:
I just wanted everyone to know what a wonderful stay we had at the Brookshire Suites on November 30, 2005. We attended a concert at the Ramshead and I reserved two rooms through the online reservations system. The package price made it very affordable to stay overnight, but I have to admit a little apprehensive.
The customer service was excellent from before we arrived to our departure. Someone called me to make sure that I wanted to reserve two rooms for the same night since both were in my name. After I assured her that I did, she asked me to please call if I needed anything else.
When we arrived we were greeted by a very engaging youg man with complimentary wine, beer and delicious homemade potato chips. The wine and beer were a welcome sight, but we are still talking about the potato chips!
The desk cler was very friendly adn helped arrange dinner at the Blue Sea Grill, which was great by the way. I am not sure if I am spelling right, but I believe it was Azzizi, She was both professional and attentive. The valet was courteous and polite. The next morning we were amazed at the wonderful breakfast that was included in our package price.
All in all we had a great stay and are looking for more reasons to come to Baltimore and stay overnight at the Brookshire Suites. I have stayed at much more expensive places and have never felt as comfortable and been as well treated as I was at the Brookshire.

title: “Nice place to stay... Great location”
text: This was the first time I stayed at this particular hotel in D.C.. Room was a decent size and clean. Bed was comfortable. Very helpful staff.. I needed a late checkout and they were very accommodating.. My only issue, and it isn't really with the cleanliness, comfort, etc of the room... It is the parking. If you have a car... The hotel has an arrangement with a "nearby" hotel parking garage. The garage is approximately 1 block away.. While not terribly far, it is just far enough to be slightly inconvenient.BUT... All-in-all.... A very nice stay...

title: “A great location”
text: The hotel is located 2 blocks from Central Park and a few minute walk from Time Square. The lobby is small but fairly normal for a New York Hotel. The bell staff was courteous and helpful. When checking in the female hotel receptionist was rude and clearly disliked her job. We booked our room online and requested a king bed. The female clerk told us that "Online reservations don't guarantee anything." Um what? She told us that if we would be willing to wait a few hours we could have a King bed. We had no problem waiting. The room was clean and in great shape for the age of the building. I would recommend staying here it is in a prime spot. Go to the Broadway show ROCK of Ages it was incredible!!!!!!!!!!

title: “Great Hotel, Great Location”
text: The Belvedere provided everything we needed for a four night stay. The room, including the bathroom was spacious, well appointed and above all clean. The housekeeping staff did a tremendous job each and every day. The in-room security safe was a bonus with a personalized combination that you applied each time it was secured and it was ideal for storage of a laptop computer and other articles. The hotel is a short walk to Time's Square and three different subway lines. If you are interested in sightseeing the Belvedere is right around the corner from the main office of a major provider. We had heard in advance about slow elevators but did not experience any difficulties at anytime in waiting for an elevator. Overall it was a very positive experience and I wouldn't hesitate to return or to recommend the Belvedere to anyone considering staying in midtown.

title: “Great Experience at Eastgate Tower”
text:
I booked Eastgate Tower after reading many reviews online. My wife and I stayed for 3 days/2 nights. I was originally a little worried about walking to/from the hotel at night, but the walk from Grand Central to Eastgate was only about 10-12 minutes. It's about 3 blocks south and 4-5 blocks east of Grand Central Station (we travelled mostly by subway around the city). The best route (especially at night) was simply walking up 3rd ave. and then over 42nd st. to Grand Central. It was fairly populated and well lit at night. Take the shuttle (subway) to Times Square and you can go anywhere in NYC.
The hotel was very spacious and clean. It wasn't the Ritz, but for $135 a night I thought I got my money's worth and more! We didn't need any help from the staff, so I can't really comment on them.
I have nothing negative to say about my experience. I would stay at the hotel again! Especially if I were to take the kids.

title: “Funky Hotel”
text: Great location, lovely staff. I always stay here when in in Chicago

title: “Not worth the money.”
text: My husband and I stayed here February 12, 2011 for his 40th birthday. It was our first night of full sleep as we had a baby in October. I have never reviewed a hotel before, but feel inclined as I didn't find any negative reviews on the hotel when checking it out on the web. I was not impressed. The room cost the same as other waterfront hotels, but with a view of a brick building. The cold water didn't work on the bathroom sink; the only thing we requested was a bucket of ice for drinks and after a friendly, "we will bring that right up", it never came; the bed cover had a dark mark looking like a makeup stain or mud stain that I wish had been considered dirty and replaced; the dark curtains didn't cover the windows by design so only the sheers and no ability to get darkness in the room; we were woken up about 9:00 a.m. by maids yelling at each other in Spanish while vacuuming either right out front our door or in a room where the door was open while they were cleaning. We will not waste our money at this location again.

title: “Recommended place for a conference”
text:
I staied there in one of the appartments not in the towers. I was there for a conference, my girl friend attended me and enjoyed the hotel, spa and city.
The service was very friendly and helpfull at all times. Especially the desk clerks who helped us also in issues NOT concerning the hotel (finding the way and public transportation lines to several places, etc.).
The room was nice, clean. The appartment had 3 rooms. The style was typical american :-) A bit kitschy for our age (~30years) but nice.
On the way through the convention center you cross a very nice garden like place. Ways to the convention center are nice and short. The convention center is very nice, big rooms, fine acoustics.
Gardens are well prepared. The whole place is very well done and clean. Big palms and nice smaller trees and bushes really give a nice impression. You don't feel as if being in a city.
Trolley and bus stations are within walking range, so that you don't even need a car to get to San Diego city. Also a big and nice shopping mall is within walking distance (you'll see squirrels on your way to the mall ;-). Pools are nice and clean, just a bit too small for real swimming but great for relaxing.
Compared to european standards, the rooms are not very well isolated. Both regarding temperature (but with air condition in the room) and noise (you sometimes heard people outside if they were talking loud).
The price never the less is not very cheap.

title: “Near the ships, 7-days of parking free included. Shuttle to the ships. This worked well.”
text:
For what I paid that included parking, this was an excellent value.
I used 123stay.com to book this hotel and to get the 7-day free parking (park and cruise). I looked at a lot of options and the consistent issues among ALL the hotels shuttling to the ports was difficulties with the shuttle. So, I ruled out the hotels near the airport and took the Holiday Inn Express neart the Stadium so that if any problems occurred, the cab rides would be inexpensive. 
TIP: We tried to book directly with Holiday Inn using points, but they charged a fortune for the parking. The best rate was through 123stay.com. I registered with their site, had no problems with them. and their Instructions were good, The hotel had their reservation, All done via the Internet. And, I had a printoff with the reservation number. 
LOCATION:
This is at 1701 Russell Street. A GPS was essential, and will still benefited from printing off a mapquest street map because it's hard to envision that I-295 heading north dumped right onto Russell Street. You don't want to get on the wrong road spurs and head across bridges, etc. 
The area is a bit industrial and no restaurants nearby except a Subway across the street. Eat before you arrive or plan an excursion and bring along your maps. On the way to the ships, we passed the Stadium. It really seems within walking distance, but not particularly good for walking alongside the roads. Heed other reviews if you are going to the stadiium.
THE ROOM: Clean, quiet. And, really that's all of what we needed for this overnight stay. 
Our room was small and overlooked the gated parking lot. The TV was old, and the bathroom was clean. The sink was outside the BR in the hallway. Good towels. Two queen beds, good mattress, and a ton of pillows for each bed. No hallway noises. This might be different if there's a game at the stadium, so sometimes, maybe you can ask for a quiet room. Maybe some other reviews mention which ones. I think we had to bring all our luggage up to the room. There was no option to store it downstairs.
THE BREAKFAST:
This was just fine. The night before, we heated some microwave dinners in the oven by the soda machines and sat in that room. Better than eating in the room. The food was a hot breakfast, nice selection of breakfast things. Good coffee, juices, yogurts. 
THE STAFF:
The night-staff person on duty was new, but was handling numerous requests with politeness and calm and clear instructions. Most people were concerned about the shuttles to the boats the next morning.. Obviously, they too had read a lot of reports for the hotels offering the park and cruise.
THE SHUTTLE to the boats.
They handed out a small instruction note, gave us a choice of shuttle times available. I do think you should do that on arrival or before if they'll allow it. They used two shuttle buses per run. One had the luggage, the other the people. 
TIP: The vans are a bit hard to get into if you've got any handicap --especially if those front runners take all the good seats leaving YOU to the hard-to-get-to back seat. AAAaaargh. If you've got problems, I suggest alerting the driver, give him you tip early and ask to board first.
True to their word, we never saw the luggage again until it appeared in the ship's stateroom.
TIP: Make sure you understand where the van will pick you up after your cruise or event and make sure they have a cell phone number for you if they can't find you after you've called for a pickup. 
PARKING LOT:
Locked and lit. I was confortable leaving the car there. They give you a card or a code to get in. To get out, the gates open automatically as you approach them. I think the extra two days parking was at $5.00 / day.

title: “Very nice hotel”
text:
We enjoyed our 5-night stay here. The hotel was quiet and the beds are so comfy!
The staff was friendly and helpful, and we loved that sherry was provided in the afternoons. We had two rooms on upper floors, at the back of the hotel. Our views were great and there was no street noise. The rooms are not large, but quite adequate.

title: “Okay but spendy”
text: This hotel is pretty nice. We were there for a business trip, and the price was up there but competitive with other nice ones in the area. Doors are thin and noise easily comes both from the hall and the street below. Room service is prompt and super friendly, but a little on the expensive side and the taste is average at best (dined in 3 times, yeah it's lame). They really bend over backwards to make sure you are happy at the hotel in general. The gym is pretty good, plenty of machines if it is busy. The bed was quite comfortable, and the shower was nice/powerful. Good location within walking distance to a lot of attractions. Overall, if I had to stay in the city, I would stay there again (especially if it were on someone else's dime).

title: “Great location, but”
text:
The grand hyatt is a hotel located right in front of Union Square, where all shops, restaurants are. The location is perfect, you can walk to chinatown, the cablecar is one block away and macys, bloomingdales, apple, etc are around the corner.
The hotel was once a 5 star, now the rooms seem old, though spacious (king room has more space than 2 queen bed room)the bathroom is really old, ugly, but clean.
200 dolar a night, was not very cheap, but the other hotels in this location, Marriott, Four Seasons are much more expensive and luxorious, of course.
Breakfast is ridiculous, it cost 16-20 dollars, depending on what you eat, but the buffet is so small, you could easily go to a starbucks (in front of the hotel) or macys to have a coffe and some pastries.
garage is extremely expensive, about 50 dollars/day.

title: “Extremely clean, owners nice, close to airport and will stay there everytime.”
text: This is the second time we have stayed at this Super 8; it is extremely clean, smells nice, the staff and owners are very accomading; you can even print your boarding pass on site at no charge. You can leave your car at the hotel for almost half of what the airport charges and they will take you to the airport whenever you need to go and with just a phone call to them when you return they are there within minutes to pick you up and return you to the hotel and your car, with offer of coffee or whatever ever you need. One hint; I booked thru Hotels.com and in talking to Sam (owner) he said he could give a better rate if you call the hotel direct. The pillows could be more comfortable but this is the only thing that I see they can improve on. The Continental Breakfast has a good variety of items, more than most usual Cont. Breakfast.

title: “Beautiful Hotel”
text: This is a very nice hotel. Service is great. The only downfalls of the hotel is that the bathrooms are not very private, the sink is in an open area and the toilet and shower are behind a frosted glass door. So if you want privacy this isnt for you. The other is on the internet it has a pool, when we asked where the pool was we were told it is at a sister hotel on Connecticut Avenue, not very practical when the kids want to swim. The hotel sets in a good area as well. When we were looking all the hotels seemed to look nice but wasnt sure about the areas. I am so glad we stayed in Dupont Cirlce. The hotel is close to many eateries and stores and the metro is across the street. We seen some of the other hotels when we were there and on the internet they were beautiful but the areas of some of them not so good. Actually got to see a motorcade go into the White House.

title: “Great one evening stay!”
text:
I would recommend! Clean, quiet, discrete. Center of everything. I actually hesitate to put a review up because I don't want EVERYONE to know! ;-) I wish I would have been able to put the great outdoor patio to more use, but I was only staying one evening.
The only suggestion I would make has to do more with ATT cell phone service. But that seems to be an issue all over NYC, not the hotels fault.

title: “Very nice, great views, but not very close to things”
text:
This hotel is very nice. The rooms are very nice, the beds super comfortable, and the bathrooms are awesome. We spent one day seeing the memorials, leaving the hotel on foot, and returning 4 hours later. A long walk but very nice on a warm day. There are no stores other than a CVS within a 1/2 mile radius.
Overall, we had a great stay and would return. Staff was very helpful and friendly. The only things which were disappointing are the following (but we admit these are minor):
Swimming Pool - only luke warm.... I expected warmer. No hot tub, which was disappointing.
Fitness Room - asked us to leave because my 11-year-old children were not allowed, even though we were exercising together and using the equipment responsibly.
Room -- no coffee pot, have to order always from room service.
Mini-bar -- no wine, had to always order from room service.

title: “The Customer is King and so is the Dog!”
text: My husband, dog(Shelby), and I have stayed at this Hotel Monaco twice and the one in Portland once. We joined their Kimpton Hotel loyalty plan and have been treated like treasured guests ever since. Their stated goal is to be the "most loved" hotel company and they have certainly endeared themselves to us. On this trip their dedication to top-notch customer service was evident even before we arrived. We were staying downtown to celebrate my husband's birthday. I had reserved an upgraded room online, but then worried later that it might not be one of their dog-friendly rooms. I called to make certain it was all okay and spoke to a really nice woman (wish I'd gotten her name) who assured me that there are dog-friendly rooms of each kind and that our reservation was all in order. She noted that we are members of the Kimpton In-Touch program and that we were going to be there for a special occasion. She asked if we would like to have a bottle of wine or champagne in the room. I stammered a bit and said that actually we are micro-brewed beer hounds. She said she would see what she could do. So, we arrived downtown around 1pm and thought we'd see if they would let us leave our car there while we went to eat lunch and wait for our room to be ready. We were delighted to find out that our room was already available and we could unload the car. The valet was very sweet to our dog and helped us juggle the luggage, dog, jackets, keys, etc. Inside they have an adorable chalkboard with the names of all the dog guests posted. They also give you a little gift bag with dog treats, a dog toy, and clean-up bags. The lobby has a lot of seating areas, a fireplace, chess set, and complimentary wine around 5ish. I'm not sure what the decorating scheme would be called, but it's warm and comfortable as opposed to a lot of the trendy places with hard surfaces and mod colors. Our room was decorated in a similar fashion to the lobby and included a sofa, lounge chair and desk with desk chair. There was also a bed on the floor for our dog. The bed for the humans was huge and had crisp linens and lots of pillows. The bathroom was a nice size and instead of those little bottles of shampoo and such they had large dispenser bottles in the shower. Probably better for the environment. After dropping our things we went out to explore the city. The hotel is in a great central location and you can leave your car there and walk all over the place. When we came back a couple of hours later there were three bottles of Pike Place Brewery ales chilling in a bucket of ice. There was also a personalized card written to my husband wishing him a happy 56th birthday. It was signed by the Chief Concierge, Jesse Peterson. Too cool! The next day we had a really delicious brunch at the adjoining restaurant, Sazerac. After we returned home I filled out an online questionnaire and gave them high marks for making us feel so special while we were at the hotel. I then received a 'thank you' email from the Director of Operations and it wasn't a form letter! These people are SERIOUS about customer service. I have recently slacked-off on writing reviews because it's time consuming and I feel a little bit like "why would anyone care what I think", but when a company puts so much time and effort into making sure I'm happy I'm glad to talk about them to anyone who will listen.

title: “Corner King rooms rock!”
text: Worth the $60 upgrade at the desk. The rooms are at the end of the halls so very quiet, and have two windows for extra sunlight and showtime. Stayed here with the wife. Nice comfortable bed. Great location for great dining, the mag mile and the red line. Fast elevators, great front desk, lively bar. I never saw a concierge nor any serious 5 star luxuries but still was a very nice hotel. Liquor store right around the corner and many dining options. Check out grand lux cafe for breakfast on michigan ave.

title: “Awful”
text: This hotel is a nice idea, but not a nice place to stay. It is loud and echoing and roooms are oddly laid out. The AC will only work if you are "moving in the room" so be prepared to wake up in a sweat. Despite some weak attemps at double-glazing (basically just put another window inside the existing window) the street noise in incredible. The fire department makes at least 3 to 5 full light and siren runs each night.
