Rooms are not ready when promised, staff does not call as promised when rooms are ready, you are constantly being "carded" by staff to ensure you are who you say you are (my id was checked twice during check-in). The proximity to Horton plaza makes it a hang out for street persons who harass you the second you walk out the door. Proximity to gaslamp means that folks come stumbling in shrieking at the top of their lungs at 2:30am... In addition absolutely no attention paid to my significantly premier status with Marriott. Last - internet connection is very weak and not wireless in rooms. All in all - way too much money for the "quality of the experience"...

title: “Good Budget Suites, but Under Construction”
text: Chose this location as our overnight stop on car trip to and from L.A. because of it's pricing and easy access to I-10 each way. The property was obviously built in the 80's, so it's a little old - looked like they were in the process of doing some upgrading both in and out of the rooms. The landscaping was all removed and they were in the process of installing irrigation systems all around the property. The rooms are a little old, but the property, rooms and pool were clean and well maintained. Arrived at 7:00 PM the first evening after a 1000-mile drive to find that the "happy hour" (Monday - Friday only) was going on. Complimentary wine, beer, munchies - a very pleasant surprise. Good free breakfast in the mornings as well with cooked to order eggs.

title: “Great location, great hotel!”
text: My wife and I always stay at this hotel whenever we go to NYC. We have stayed at a number of other hotels in the Times Square area, but always ended up bak here. Now, whenever we go to NYC, we only stay at The Renaissance Times Square.

title: “Awful, Avoid this hotel”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for two nights on a vacation. It was awful. My own complaints are very similar to the other reviews. We booked on priceline. We also called to confirm a smoking king room (and also emailed). When we checked in we were told we could not have the room we had requested (and they confirmed). The hotel manager (sounds like the same one discussed in earlier reviews) told us "thats what you get for booking on priceline" and said that we should have booked through them instead. The front desk staff was extremely rude. 
This is no four star hotel. The rooms are dirty and dingy. Ours faced the driveway on the ground floor. All night there were cars driving in and out, idling their engines. Our window was blocked by a wooden beam and cement post. The washroom was tiny and the tiles were caved in around the faucet and appeared to be rotten underneath. 
The rooms are also extremely small. I do not know if this is all rooms, or just the second class rooms that they relegate people who do not book directly through their site to. 
We asked for guest robes and were told we would have to "sign them out" (again, duplicating the treatment of an earlier reviewer who felt like a criminal). The location is the only positive feature...but it is not worth it! There are so many nicer (and less expensive) hotels in the area with the same location.
When we checked in (in the early afternoon) there were still dirty breakfast dishes (with dead flies floating in the orange juice) left outside our door in the hallway. It was dirty and dingy. We requested an in room fridge (none were available) and to get ice we had to walk to a different building, and then up an elevator and down a hall. 
I felt very poorly treated. For the amount of money that they charge, this hotel is not worth it. It is not the same class or standards that you might expect from other hotels in the Sheraton line. It was awful. Do not stay here.

title: “Just about everything is perfect...”
text: ...but they can improve a couple of minor details. The location is great for a night in the city. We walked from Union Station - very manageable if not much luggage and the weather is good. It is also walking distance to The Chicago Theater , the Trump Tower and a variety of other nice places for food and entertainment. The check-in was painless, the staff is friendly and the place is very clean. The king size bed was elegantly comfortable and there are hair dryers in the room. The ladies appreciate this touch. My suggestion is to improve the music system in the room. We had the cheapest AM/FM radio you can imagine, which didn't even work. No Aux port to play our mp3 - so we were left with the TV - where you had to pay for a decent music selection. In the morning we like to make our own in-room coffee - and they have upgraded the coffee makers. It is a single cup brewer - but they only had one cup of regular and one cup of decaf. Small details - but that is the difference between a 4 star and 5 star experience in my book. The view we had was underwhelming - the back of the hotel overlooking roof AC units - but that may have been because we requested the king bed option. Overall I would stay here again - but request a front facing room, extra packs of coffee and bring our own music player - just in case.

title: “Perfect place to stay in LA”
text:
I enjoyed everything.
Place is very nice and clean, cozy.
It is very convenient to stay there if you have or rent a car. We drove around to all the beautiful beaches and of course Hollywood.
The two cons: over night parking for the car is expensive, I think like $36, so if you not going to travel around, maybe do not rent a car and do not pay more for parking than your car rent cost-just get a taxi.
And also breakfast pretty pricey. I rather go somewhere to the City but of course if you stay for business, it is convenient to eat there, and we did too sometimes.
I loved lounge bar. Cozy.

title: “Good for the money”
text: I've stayed at this la quinta at two different business travels, I can say its location is great, you can easily drive to this hotel, rooms are big, it is not a new hotel, so I noticed that some parts of the room seemed worn, specially the tub at the bathroom. If you've stayed at la quinta you know what to expect, I didn't found any disguising or happy surprise here.

title: “Wedding Stay Happily Ever Afte”
text:
My then fiancee and I blocked rooms at the hotel back in February when they were heavily under construction. I was concerned about this but was assured that the renovations would be complete by our wedding date in October. As it got closer to our wedding, I came upon this website and noticed more than one bad review. I was panicked by this and called the hotel and asked to speak with the manager Anthony. He was not in but called me back first thing the next morning. He assured me that most of the renovations were complete and that my wedding party/family/friends staying at the hotel would all be taken care of. As it turns out he was correct! Most our our guest were in brand new rooms that were gorgeous inside. A few were in partially renovated rooms (new furniture and all) but all of our guests had nothing but favorable comments for the hotel. The room that I stayed in (germantown suite) could use a bit more renovations (hole in the wall in the sitting area) but was still a clean and comfortable room. I stayed at the hotel the night before the wedding with a few of my bridesmaids and the staff was extremely attentive to each of us. 
One thing I think that could use some improvement is the continental breakfast. Not much offered and the juices and milk sit out on the counter instead of being kept on ice.
My guests, my husband and I were all extremely pleased with our stay here and my husband and I plan to go back again for a weekend to relax and enjoy the area more.

title: “Uber Chic!!!!”
text: The place was really welcomming. Love the Hip Lobby! The Lemonsgrass scent upon entering the lobby was really refeshing. We will defently stay again. As mentioned in ohter reviews the lobby was the place to be with a welcoming bar and pool table area. We order a pizza from Tony's and stayed in the lobby with our 15 year old daughter. We had a great time. In addition if you have small kid they also provied board game. Yes!! I said board game NO electronic games!! YEAH!! Good old fashion fun! The next morning before leaving we decided to take advanatage of the Chef made breakfast! Excellent! and Not to expensive! Will definetly stay again!!!

title: “Great hotel!”
text: My friends and I stayed at the Intercontinental for a week during Thanksgiving 2012. It was also my birthday weekend so we wanted to relax and see the city. The hotel is beautiful. My friend who is workout fiend raved about the gym and the hotel. You can't beat the location we walked to Union Square, church, Tropisueno restaurant, Sbuks, it was all in walking distance. Everyone was super helpful the concierge were always happy to help us check out a new part of the city. Even the bellman Ernest was so pleasant and friendly every time we saw him. The front desk staff were professional but not as charming as Ernest or the concierge I think. They seem a bit closed off (shrugs). We were there for a week so we got to know everyone. The rooms were clean with awesome view. We were on the 20th floor. Just incredible. The beds are extremely comfortable. Since it was my birthday the hotel manager sent up sweet treats and a bottle of champagne which I thought was really nice! My only complaint would be housekeeping not as on it as you would think they should be. Our plates and champagne glasses sat there for three days, along with the ice bucket...but meh..maybe they did want to risk if we weren't finished. But I think it was pretty clear. The hallways are clean. You do experience some noise if kids are running around..yep that happened the last two days we were there. You could hear them, but maybe an isolated thing..not sure. If they could fix one thing it would be the room doors. They slam automatically, even if you try and do it quietly. You could constantly hear doors slamming especially in the morning...not a major problem, if you're a light sleeper it could be. We ordered room service. The food was delicious I thought, one of my friends didn't like the french onion soup but to each is own. I stayed at the Intercontinental in NY and loved it. I think I really like the decor in the NY location better dark wood, cobalt blues, and creams. The San Fran location is more earth tones which I think can make it look outdated even though it's a fairly new hotel. Overall I great place to stay while in San Fran, I will definitely return!

title: “Comfortable, adequate”
text:
Got a fantastic deal on Priceline for the Intercontinental Barclay during a busy weekend in NYC.
Pros:
- Amazingly comfortable bed
- Blackout shades
- Clean
- Big TV
- Good water pressure in the shower
Cons:
- Depending on where your room is, can be REALLY loud due to street noise and have poor natural lighting
- Tiered pricing WiFi. $12 for slow WiFi, $16 for better WiFi. Come on, guys.
The UN Assembly was going on during my stay which created some annoyance getting in and out of the hotel. Had to go through TSA-esque security every time we wanted to come in, which I understand, but had no idea it was going to be like this.
We also stayed on the 6th floor and man, was it noisy. If you're sensitive to this, you will DEFINITELY want to ask for a higher floor. I live on a busy street in Miami and I'm very used to street noise, but even this affected my sleep a bit. Not sure if the UN Assembly madness added to this.
Location-wise, it was close to the subway and you've got quick walking access to 5th avenue and Rockafeller Center, so needless to say, we were able to do a good amount of shopping easily.
Great for: people on business, people interested in shopping, people interested in tourist sights.

title: “Great hotel - don't worry about the bad reviews”
text: Stayed at the Roosevelt for four nights; was slightly concerned at the mixed reviews but am very pleasantly surprised - front-desk staff were great, room is large and in good shape. Good value for money Concierge staff were as good as it gets - Christine helped me with a number of issues and is a credit to the hotel. As long as a I can get a reservation I know where I'll be staying in NYC in the future.

title: “Outstanding!”
text: We were in Boston to celebrate my wife's birthday Since this was our first trip to Boston I carefully researched hotels by reading just about every tripadvisor review on top rated Boston hotels. I didn't think any hotel could live up to the incredible reviews written about The Lenox. I was wrong. The Lenox met and even exceeded every expectation we had (and we had high expectations going into this trip). The location is excellent (we walked or rode the T everywhere, even from/to the airport), the hotel is beautiful and comfortable, and the staff is excellent in every way. When they found out that it was my wife's birthday they did everything they could to make her stay special. In her words she felt like a princess. The only downside is the pressure that puts on me now that we're home. I hesitate to mention names for fear I'll leave someone out. Suffice it to say that Dan Donahue, general manager has assembled a top notch staff who understand how to be professional without being pretentious. It's no mistake that The Lenox Hotel is number one in Boston. They certainly deserve it.

title: “Convenient”
text: Our two day stay at the Donatello in Union Square was wonderful. Chinatown was just a few blocks away as were two of the cable car routes. We enjoyed walking around and found wonderful places to eat and drink. The staff were very helpful and our room was located on a quiet side street so we could rest well in the afternoon and evening.

title: “Nice Place, Fine Staff”
text: We moved to this hotel after a bad experience at the Tempe Sheraton Four Points. What a difference, like going from purgatory to heaven. Staff was friendly and helpful, room was beautiful and spacious, pool was very nice and relaxing. No complaints at all.

title: “Great Choice for the area”
text:
Stayed here 30 years ago when I was performing across the street in the now long gone abc theater. Was a nice welcome back to see the place again.
 While some areas are showing signs of age the attentive staff quickly addresses,and more importantly resolves, any problem.
parking in the area is high, needs reasonable self parking WITH in/out priv. Not everyone is on a Hollywood expense account......
Balconies are fun and make for a great hollywood fantasy. Room service is top notch. Restaurants are fantastic.
Great location for events as well as a visit to the BH area

title: “Great place to stay and very reasonably priced!”
text: Well I grew up around here so I pretty much know most of the hotels downtown. My friend and I stayed here so we could go out for her birthday and crash at the hotel. This hotel was the cheapest out of most of the ones we found and in a good place. It's right up the street from the harbor and you can catch a cab very easily around there. The hotel also has a free shuttle that will take you anywhere around Baltimore. It was really nice on the inside. Kind of small but very nice. It was clean, the beds were very comfortable. I highly recommend this place!

title: “Conrad Hilton Chicago”
text: This hotel was wonderful, the Staff, the product, the service - it was perfect. Attention to detail and every staff member always had a wonderful smile on their face. I just had a wonderful experience.

title: “a good idea!”
text: The hotel is pretty nice close to alot of restraunta and also not a far walk to the national mall area, The front desk is very helpful and friendly, Kyle at the desk help us are whole stay he sent us to nice restraunts and also told us about a evening tour which was awesome it was called on board bus tours, The continetal breakfast is ok. If you are looking to stay some were with good service this is the place, The hotel could use a renovation but it was a wonderful stay we will be back.

title: “Great location, price and confort”
text: The title pretty much sums everything up, we had a great time.

title: “Could be better, great views”
text:
Once I found the entrance for parking I found this was an average Marriott; (as others have mentioned) parking is horrible.
Check-in was fine, nothing special - no instructions. Room was standard, bathroom was a little small; food was ok, staff could be friendlier, the conference rooms were cold, very cold.

title: “Ok, but not great”
text: The staff at the hotel was friendly and accommodating. The lobby was modern and inviting. The room appeared fairly clean, but was very old, out-dated and run down, especially the bathroom. There was a large enough gap between the door and door frame that we could actually see out into the hallway. Our room was located on the first floor, right inside the outer door and the noise throughout the entire night was terrible. With the noise from people coming in and out of the hotel, the noise in the stairwell and from the rooms above us and across the hall, we were awake more than we were asleep!

title: “A great location!”
text:
The Marriott Waterfront is perfectly located, close to downtown and Belltown. A great place to base yourselves for a family vacation (we were very happy with the deal we received booking a package through the marriott.com web site -- airfare, hotel and car rental.)
Unlike many hotels, this one was very quiet. We stayed five nights and never heard the folks on either side of us. The waterfront view from our room (652) was very nice, and the small balcony was a plus.
You are in easy walking distance to Pike Place Market and some wonderful restaurants in the Belltown neighborhood. A great find was La Bella e Vita on 2nd Avenue between Battery and Wall. Or just walk across the street to Pier 66 (we'd recommend you stick to the first floor, which they call the Bell Street Diner. An excellent menu, very fresh fish nicely prepared and if you like micro-brew beer, try the Manny's on tap. You can't get it in a bottle so enjoy it while you can.
For breakfast, the Fish Club in the hotel offers a great buffet for a reasonable $14.95 per adult ($7.50 for children) or order off the menu (check out the French Toast). But most days we just walked up the adjacent stairway to the Pike Place Market and dropped into the Le Panier French bakery. There is also a great little donut spot at the south end of the market -- about $2 for a half dozen mini-donuts that you just watched them make.
One caution: If you are staying for more than a couple nights and have a car, you might want to park it for $12 a day in the Art Institute parking garage to the north of the hotel. Turn right out of the hotel, go up a block to Wall, turn right on Wall, turn right at the next light and head up about a block to the garage's upper entrance. If you park on that level, you can walk through the garage and take an outside elevator down to Alaskan Way and you end up about a half block away from the hotel. A bargain compared to the $30 per night for valet parking at the hotel.

title: “Decent, solid, convenient”
text: Generous rooms, great service, excellent location for train and metro. The perfect DC base for business.

title: “Fabulous Stay”
text: I stayed at the Hotel Palomar for a girls weekend in SF in October. The hotel was great. The highlights of this hotel are its excellent service, the bar area & its location. The service at this hotel is top notch from the moment you step foot in the lobby. The location was great -- literally within a 2 block range of excellent shopping & restaurants. The hotel has an excellent happy hour in their bar, which is comfortable and modern. There is also a hotel dog at the happy hour, which was nice. Our rooms were comfortable and spacious. The bathroom was not huge, but was modern. The view, however, was of the office next door & the glass roof of the container store. A little bizarre, but we were hardly in the room, so it didn't matter much. We ordered room service breakfast, which was solid but nothing special. I would recommend this to anyone coming to SF for a weekend of shopping, sightseeing & fun. I would stay here again.

title: “Bait and switch; beware.”
text:
I booked two rooms more than five months in advance of the Philadelphia Marathon - one standard room and one suite (at considerably additional cost). We had stayed at the same hotel for the marathon on 2005 and stayed in a standard room at a great price. We were very pleased then with the size of the room and the friendliness of the staff and expected this visit to be similar. 
When we arrived, we were reminded of the poor parking situation, which was to park across the street at a cost of $33 per night (the hotel only offered a 15% discount v. validation and there was no valet). In addition, upon attempting to check-in, the staff refused to acknowledge our presence and when we asked to check-in, we were referred to a kiosk (mind you there was no one else in the lobby and two obviously idle workers).
That was minor compared to the tiny size of our "suite", which had one double bed and a cot folded up against the wall. I'm not quite sure where this was supposed to go since we could barely turn around in the room. We did have a stovetop, microwave and tiny fridge jammed in the room (all totally unnecessary in Philadelphia where there is not a grocery store nearby). I cannot stress enough how SMALL this room was and that I paid extra to have a "suite." Did I mention that were were right next to the elevator which was quite long at all hours of the day and night? I should also note that my 2 year old daughter was staying with us, so keeping a toddler asleep amidst constant elevator traffic was a challenge. All of this was quite frustrating considering my the extra cost, the substantial advanced booking, and notification provided to the hotel that our toddler would be staying with us. I communicated my concerns with both the front desk and Hotels.com and was told that they cannot guarantee that the rooms assigned will match the description at booking--talk about a bait and switch!
If you are considering booking a hotel through an online hotel broker such as hotels.com, I strongly caution you to consider booking directly through the hotel as these brokers book large blocks of rooms and try to fill them without any regard to what is actually promised at booking. Hotels.com would not provide any reimbursement of find us another hotel with suitable accomodations. Rather, they only offered to mail (yes, snail mail) a $50 gift certificate, which I could then send back to them to credit my credit card that was charged for these rooms. I was told I should expect to see this in 6-8 weeks, by which point I'll supposedly have forgotten all about this debacle and decide that I should use it to book again on hotels.ocm. Guess again. Being frugal does not make one a complete moron. I should also mention that my booking permitted me to modify my reservation, which I attempted to do on three occasions. The hotels.com phone jockey supposedly executed this change, but in the end, I was stuck paying for three nights when I only stayed two nights. Club Quarters was completely unhelpful and unsympathetic as well. 
Long story short, never use an online hotel broker nor expect consistent quality oustide of a four-star hotel.

title: “nice stay”
text: I stayed here while visiting the medical center. It is very close and the shuttle was nice. Never waited more than 15 minutes. Free parking is nice. breakfast was fine. the public spaces are well maintained and the staff very plesant. our room was comfortable and very clean. overall i find this hotel a good value and will stay here again.

title: “Room ok, but hotel staff not at all helpful”
text: When we checked in, the male attendent at the front desk was brusque and didn't explain what the "green card" was for (it is needed to control the air conditioner in the room). When I went back down fo the front desk and asked him, his tone and demeanor implied I was ignorant for not knowing! He grudgingly signed us up for the airport shuttle, but didn't provide any info (like where to wait for it or how to get hold of them on our return). The rooms are ok, nothing lavish. Beds are a little hard and a/c wasn't overly cold, but the room served its purpose.

title: “Outstanding service and cleanliness!”
text:
I stayed here Oct 08 for about a week on business in Phoenix.
Despite some very minor complaints I gave this hotel five stars for service. The friendliness of the staff at this hotel is excellent across the board. The cleanliness of the rooms and the efficiency of which the housekeepers do their work is superior to any hotel I have stayed at. The only place where the staff was consistently more friendly was at the Cozumel Palace in Cozumel Mexico.
The hotel and rooms are kept very clean and if you want fresh sheets each day you are there, you place a little card on the bedsheets. You might think you automatically get clean sheets ever day you stay at any given hotel but you would be sadly mistaken. 
The breakfast for a continental offering is outstanding with little "egg patties" Sausage, Cereal, Bagels, Oatmeal that you can add nuts, raisins and Cinnamon to, Three juices(Lemon, Orange, and Apple)
The Wireless internet in your room works consistently, although slow. You can't surf pictures or send large documents but I never had a problem logging on.
The property is safe, well kept and clean although next to highway 17. There are three well known franchise restaurants on the same road as the hotel with a mall across the highway with 3 or 4 main franchise restaurants and a full mall.
The area outside the block of the hotels is a little depressed with some pan handlers but I never felt unsafe.
I was asked for money or food a few times and when I said no, I was told "thank you anyway, god bless!"
I would definitely stay here again when in phoenix. Although I would rather stay somewhere with a restaurant and a bigger breakfast, the service level of this hotel make up for any minor complaints I might have.

title: “Great location, good value”
text:
I've stayed here twice now; once on business last summer, and over the July 4th weekend this year with my wife and 20-month-old daughter. I chose it over the Union Square boutique hotels I usually frequent for a couple of reasons -- the location (closer to to Yerba Buena Gardens and the carousel, half-block from Market for convenience to the street cars, etc.), the size of the rooms and the potential for a decent view, and the fact that they were offering a decent holiday weekend special rate.
Despite booking via hotels, we had no trouble getting a 23rd floor room. It was a bit close to the elevator, but we had no complaints about elevator or hall noise. The room, as I expected from my previous stay, was larger than those in most of the affordable Union Square hotels -- an important consideration with a toddler in tow. Our floor-to-ceiling window afforded a nice, if unspectacular, view of Yerba Buena Gardens, SBC Park, and the bay beyond. We elected to skip the crowds of the Pier 39 fireworks on the Fourth, but got to see at least five different fireworks displays from different areas around town from our window -- a pleasant surprise.
The room appointments were perfectly acceptable and clean; the fabrics on the chairs showed a little wear if you looked carefully, but were clean and stylish. The in-room safe provided a convenient place for my wife to park her purse and some of the small but expensive items she purchased while there.
I've never had occasion to try the onsite restaurant , Jesters-- it's pricey, and didn't seem like someplace that would deal very well with a toddler. There are plenty of other places to eat nearby, and we were there to see SF, not hole up in the hotel all day and night.
In-room internet access is $14.95/day, which is the highest I've seen anywhere in the country (including several Manhattan, Boston, and Chicago hotels). In a way, that was a good thing, since I decided it wasn't worth it and had a good excuse to ignore my e-mail for the duration. Phone charges can also be exorbitant, as I discovered on my first stay there -- my cell phone battery died and I'd forgotten my charger, so I had to use the room phone for a couple of local calls and a toll-free conference call, which altogether cost me nearly $100. Didn't make that mistake this time. 
Since I've been to SF at least two dozen times, often for a week at a time, over the last 15 years, I know my way around and know what there is to do. Given that, and since we weren't trying to do shows and such, I only had occasion to consult the concierge once -- to find out whether the cable car schedule was different on the Fourth of July holiday. Didn't know, and was distracted and not particularly friendly; otherwise, the staff was at least cordial and in some cases friendly.
If your usual accomodations are the Four Seasons, Ritz-Carlton, Hotel Nikko, Pan Pacific, or the like, you'll probably find the Argent a bit of a come-down. It doesn't have the character of the Prescott, or the affordability of the Andrews. But if room size and location are among your prime criteria, you should definitely give it some consideration.

title: “Third visit...always perfection!”
text:
This was our third Park, Sleep, Fly stay at this hotel...staying both before and after our trips.
Service, rooms, restaurant are all great. Plus, the shuttle will take you to area restaurants in between their airport trips.
The covered parking is a plus when traveling during the winter.

title: “No frills, but can't beat price and location”
text: In many ways this is a perfect hotel. You stay right in the center of downtown, and while the whole place could benefit from a makeover, it provides exactly what you need when on business - a clean room, a great bed, and a great location. No frills, but basically, and let's face it, a hotel room is where you spend time sleeping, showering, and spare time on the internet. The price is right, and if you want a good, basic hotel in Chicago I would stay here again.

title: “Good non-USQ option”
text: If you'd like to avoid the pack of Union Square hotels and don't mind being away from downtown, this is a good option. In a converted Victorian building across from the park, it's a quiet, relaxed, friendly place. It's not the W--if you need granite bathrooms and turndown service, you'll probably be disappointed--but it's a notch above the Holiday Inn rank and has a lot more character. The complimentary breakfast and wifi access are nice additions, and the staff was uniformly helpful.

title: “Really not as expected!”
text: I was expecting too much from this hotel given the reviews but let's face it, the hotel is really not that great. In particular, do not expect great and confortable rooms, they are very very small. Just expect small and clean hotel and you may be fine with it. To be honest, I did'nt like it. The lady at the desk was very nice, in contrast to the guy who was kind of 'cold'...

title: “The gem on Wabash”
text:
My gal pal and I have traveled extensively over the past three years within and outside of the United States. So far the Silversmith has been one of our best finds for the money. Just a few of the highlights were cleanliness of private and public areas, helpfulness of the staff, conveniency of location and quality and cost of the food within the hotel's deli. 
It was surprisingly quiet considering it's location next to the L Really, we hated to leave but took comfort in the fact that we would definitely return.

title: “Don't let the three-star rating fool you... fabulous location!”
text:
Our family stayed here from August 27 through August 30 in a Bayside suite. There were a ton of both pros and cons to this place so I'll go through all of them.
Pros:
1- Location was incredible. We had a bungalow on the private beach and it was very quiet.
2- Great for families as Mission Bay has no waves so the little ones can not stress over getting pounded by waves.
3- The kitchenette was adequate. It had a coffeemaker, fridge, stove, sink and place settings for 6 people. Also had wine/beer opener.
4- The staff was incredibly helpful, especially since my husband forgot my birthday-- they delivered a special treat as well as some other extras. 
5- No charge for parking and if you have a bungalow, you park right next to it. VERY convenient.
6- The Bahia Belle (a paddleboat) does a one hour tour of the bay and all you need is your room key card to get free admission.
7- There are lots of watercraft rentals that are reasonably priced (40$ per hour for a large paddle boat).
8- The private beach is well maintained. They rake it every night. There are lounge chairs as well as canopy beds on the beach.
9- Free breakfast!
10- We slept like a rock. Beds were very comfortable.
Cons:
1- The suite is not really a suite-- it's a two bedroom condo that has very outdated furnishings. With that being said, you are literally 20 feet from the surf and I doubt the property wants to upgrade furnishings with so much sand and salt water outside your door.
2- The rollaway bed was outside the bungalow when we arrived. My daughter screamed because there was a bug on top of it. When we rolled it inside and undid it, there was what looked like rat droppings inside the sheets. Housekeeping immediately gave us another rollaway bed. 
3- The bedroom air conditioner worked great BUT the living room air conditioner didn't do the job-- maybe it was because we were constantly going in and out of the patio door? 
4- The pool charges $10 per towel so bring your own beach towels. 
5- Bathroom looked like it hadn't been updated since the '70's. Housekeeping didn't leave enough towels or toiletries for five people. They left enough for two people but eventually figured out how many people were in the room and adjusted everything!
6- Don't order the room service pizza. It's awful. The cobb salad was very good and their prices are extremely reasonable. 
7- For out-of-towners, GPS can get funky on Mission Blvd, which is the main drag along Mission Beach. Just be aware you may lose GPC capabilities.
Overall:
I wouldn't want to stay here for a honeymoon simply because the rooms just aren't special. However.... If you are taking a family vacation I highly recommend this place. There is a lot of security, it's very quiet, it's near an amusement park and a few minutes from Sea World.
Our family thoroughly enjoyed ourselves here. For around $300 a night, I expected nicer furnishings etc... but honestly, the location made up for the slight disappointment. With all the sand we brought into our bungalow I'm relieved the furnishings were a little outdated-- there was no guilt over sand on the couch or carpet. The sunsets were just gorgeous, the weather outstanding and just so very relaxing. 
Our 14-year old and 11-year old walked back from Belmont Park by themselves w/o any issues-- it's a very safe area. 
There aren't a lot of restaurants right at Mission Bay Blvd/Mission Blvd but I recommend going up (north) Mission Blvd to Pacific Beach (about 10 mins (away). We ate at a place called Fat Fish and it was fantastic! Two lobster tacos, beans and rice for around $10! Five people had lobster or carne asada entrees and three beers for under $100. 
I wanted to give this place a 4-star but I couldn't do it because the bungalow was just very average. But the location is a 10. Just incredible.

title: “Don't Waste Your Money”
text:
I selected this hotel because the reviews seemed reasonable, the cost was good and the hotel offered a free shuttle and breakfast.
The rooms were clean, but in desperate need of updating. Our room was hot during the day and never seemed to reach a comfortable level.
The shuttle service was ridiculous. What the hotel doesn't tell you is that the shuttle only (supposedly) runs at the top of the hour. However, the top of the hour would arrive and no driver or shuttle would be in sight. When asked, the staff would rattle off their policy about the "top of the hour" despite the fact that they weren't providing their service. 
The staff in general had little knowledge about the area, the shuttle service or the services offered by the hotel. Even when we received an answer about something, it would be contradicted by the next staff member we encountered. 
Overall, this place just wasn't worth the hassle, despite the value.

title: “Wonderful boutique hotel in Manhattan!”
text: We stayed there on January 8th for 3 nights. This was our second time to NYC and it was a great experience. The staff was wonderful and the rooms were beautiful. The complimentary continental breakfast was a great experience. Much more of a spread than I was expecting. Unless you require a full hot breakfast each morning, they had a lot to choose from and plenty of it. It is located in a great neighborhood. I highly recommend this hotel when traveling to NYC.

title: “Definitely A Business Conference Hotel”
text:
My husband & I recently stayed at the Westin while he attended a business conference. The hotel is located near downtown and the Charlotte financial district. There is very little to do or see without a car. I walked to the downtown area and there are many bars and restaurants. I took the trolley which stops directly at the Westin to Atherton Mills(a renovated cotton warehouse) to shop and browse. The Westin's bed was definitely "heavenly" as advertised...the "heavenly" shower was just 2 shower heads together...nothing special.
The room was on the 21st floor and we had a great view of the Charlotte area and could see for many miles. The room was pretty standard with decent amentities. The best was the Starbucks coffee packs for the in-room coffeemaker. There was a in-room mini-bar which was pricey.
The restaurant was overpriced and not that great. Their continental breakfast ran about $12 and their full breakfast buffet was $20. There was really no where else to eat breakfast except a "snack bar" area off the lobby that sold coffee and muffins and snacks. 
They have a wonderful fitness center and lap pool, however, they charge $5.00 a day to use it.
They have both valet and self parking. The self parking is in the covered garage and it cost $15 a day.
There are many nice restaurants within walking distance to enjoy in the evenings.
As I said in the title...it is definitely a business conference hotel.

title: “FANTASTIC PROPERTY - Love the $$$ !”
text:
When in Los Angeles, we always stay at Hotel Bel-Air, currently closed for extensive renovations. Although not wealthy, we are loyal Four Seasons guests, and had high expectations ; we feared we might be disappointed, especially in the perspective of swapping from an opulent old style resortlike place hidden in the canyons, to a high rise city hotel.
Different it was, but we had a great time.
First approach was not on the best note, as we litterally had to wait in line to reach the valet parking area. From then on, all went smoothly.
Front desk attendant welcome us asking how the drive had been from the Santa Barbara property (good system). Wa had booked a Deluxe Four Seasons Suite, requesting the highest possible floor, which was only the 9th floor. Asking for a higher floor, she proposed a room upgrade, that would be on the 16th floor, for a fee. I felt it was stingy, as 7 of our last 10 nights had been at Four Seasons properties. It showed on her screen. I declined. I only take complimentary upgrades, and felt that a token of recognition might sometimes release the pressure of the $$$ hunt ... The front desk manager fgot out of his office for a personal welcome.
We proceeded to the Suite, along with the Bellman. It was exquisite, albeit rather smaller than we thought it would be. Not a problem. The view was awesome, from the Design Center to Griffith Observatory to the Hollywood sign to Downtown to the ocean : we felt the 16th floor would not have purchased a better view.
Exquisite decoration (special mention to the carpet pattern), plush bedding and seats, 2 large flat TV sets, ample storage, 2 french windows (seats and coffee table out there would be nice), beautiful marble bathrooms (showing its age : toilet in the bathroom, so un-Four Seasons) (special mention to the oversized shower stall with a great shower head and at last good water pressure).
We only used the restaurants for breakfast each day. Perfect outdoor seating, great menu, beautiful execution, spotless service, Four Seasons price tags (possibly Beverly Hills price tags, too). We tried once the pool area for breakfast, but service was not up to standards there.
Although quite compact, the pool area is very pleasant. The upper deck allows for a quieter scene, away from kids, and for some sun until 6.30 pm (in august). Pool attendants are very gracious. We did not order food there, but it looked very good and tasty.
On our last day, in order to catch the last Air France flight to Paris, we wanted to have time to carefully pack our 240 lb. of luggage, and requested a late check-out, hoping for some recognition of 10 nights in Four Seasons properties across the South West. Well all we had was a blunt no, even for an hour ; until I said I was ready to pay (the all around $$$ hunt) : so it was 50% of the daily rate, for occupation until 6.00 pm. Well, we shelled those out !
This is a great Four Seasons property. It has been beautifully renovated. It is up to all and each of the brand standards. We had a lovely time, and thoroughlly enjoyed what was offered. Being loyal FS guests, we know and appreciate all this. I really find bothersome is the obvious $ hunt. Not nickel-and-diming you really, but the slightly sour note that they are your big dollars at every opportunity, never acknowledging the obscene amount of money you are spending there. I understand this is a business, not a charity, but come on. I remember discussing the company policy with the GM of One&Only Reethi Rah in the Maldives ($1.800 per night), to whom we expressed how surprised we were by all the daily attentions : the owner's directions is that they splurge on customers, it does not cost them much margin, but the customer feels cherished.
Unfortunately, this is what is lacking here.
Would we return ? In a heartbeat, until Hotel bel-Air resume business. We feel so welcome there, beyond our $ ; just a question of feeling, because they must be after our $ absolutely the same way !

title: “Nice location - Very Pricey”
text:
Location was great. Helpful staff. 
They now are selling units as timeshares - got VERY sick of the "time share sharks" continually harassing us.
Would go back IF I COULD GET A DEAL - for full price, it is not worth it.

title: “Almost lived up to expectations”
text:
On arrival, I asked for an upgrade as it was my wifes 40th birthday. He asked his boss who said that would be no problem, then gave us the keys to the smallest room on a low floor. Small room, no view, and a bathrobe that had seen better days. I asked what the room had been upgraded from and was told their was nothing better available. ie It wasnt really an upgrade at all.
Next day i got a much more accomodating member of staff who immediately gave me a choice of 2 large rooms on high floors with king size beds. We took one, and from that point on the hotel was great!
Had a peek in a suite (room number 2922) which was lovely with great views of Chrysler building etc. Maybe next year....

title: “Pearl hotel, New York”
text: Great hotel location to all attractions. We had a suite that included a lounge. Stayed for 4 nights. Would definitely recommend and stay there again. Only disappointing point was that the self serve buffet breakfast was fine but the use of paper plates and plastic knives and forks was a complete no no for me. I would advise any visitors to take their own plate and cutlery next time!!!!

title: “Decent Hotel, Great Fitness Facility”
text:
Rooms facing Bryan Steet contend with train noise deep into the night (at least ours did on the 6th floor). Hotel is older, but remodeled. King rooms are small. Parking garage across Olive could use some attention, particularly the elevator area (dingy and dirty, not a good first impression).
"Draft" bar pleasant - plenty of TVs for Monday Night Football and decent prices.
The best thing about the hotel from my perspective is the large gym which has clearly undergone a complete renovation - almost Vegas resort quality.

title: “Daddy-daughter trip”
text:
My two daughters and I stayed here three nights. The location was ideal...about a 3 minute walk to the Trolley turntable. It was a great value since I bid the rate on Priceline...paid just more than half of the standard rate. The room was average with a view into an "alley".
We rented a car from Enterprise for the day just a few minute walk down the street for $40. Parking at the hotel was around $30/night.
Location was everything on this property. I wouldn't be heart broken if I ended up with this property again on Priceline.

title: “The best hotel experience”
text:
I am a single father of five children and we decided to go on a trip for sea world and the San Diego zoo. This hotel very capably offered us a room that was big enough to accommodate all of us in one room. The service was impeccable as in that whenever we had a need they supplied it instantly. They offered rides to events at no charge and the breakfast saved me from buying a breakfast meal for five days! All you can eat breakfast, loved it! It was quiet at night and the pool and hot tub are very family friendly. The drivers and other hotel staff were by far the most customer oriented people I have encountered in years. 15 minutes from the airport, and 15 - 20 from the zoo and sea world. This hotel will definitely get my business again. The televisions were new flat screens and the channels were many. Again the staff is incredible and watched out for our needs to make sure our stay was beyond pleasant. Make sure you visit the grocery before you get there as their location makes it a little tough to get to the store. I am incredibly impressed. Thanks to the staff and our drivers especially Sam who was very personal and made sure we had fun. Most people complain because they do not read the other rules of the hotel like the 8 dollar a day parking charge and then complain because they did not read the rest of the information about the hotel. Those people complain about everything. Try not to buy into that stuff. It was incredible. 
Carl Polly Seattle Washington

title: “west tower”
text: We were at first disappointed when the shuttle driver told us that we were in the west tower, because of the reviews I read here, but our room turned out to be beautiful, we had a great view of harbor, and did not hear any airport noise at all. (we were facing south) They did try to nickel and dime you for everything, and we did not use the gym, because they charged you $10 to do so. What we did for a car rental was use Enterprise, they came and picked us up, and there is free on the street parking right in front of the hotel, in which there were spaces available even during Memorial Day weekend. We used our car for the day, and then turned it in that night (Enterprise allows you to turn it in right there at the hotel) and did not have to pay the ridiculous amount that the hotel wanted for parking. There is a store about a block down with a deli and cheap breakfast, where you can get drinks for your room. Only other complaint was at times there was little hot water.

title: “So Nice!!!”
text: We booked a room via Hotwire and Wow!!! This place was amazing. The room was a newly renovated room. It was really nice with a great view of the water. The bed were super comfortable. The staff was quick and friendly.We would gladly stay here again. Thank You!!!!

title: “Close, but no cigar”
text: Stayed for four nights in June 2008 while attending a wedding in the area. Rooms okay, not great. Bathrooms need updating and remodeling. Tile/grout dirty and dated. Beds were comfy. Sewage system seemed overtaxed. Lots of trouble in several rooms with toilet issues and sewage smell. Offspring not happy that television stations did not include Nickelodeon or The Disney Channel. (Oh well.) Room service was quick and the pizza we ordered was very good. Dining room service was lackluster. We were asked for our meal order before even being asked if we desired beverages. Lots of prompting was necessary to get the server to take our orders. Food okay, but we ate elsewhere mostly. Carpets in the common areas were extremely dirty and outdated - brown and beige - did not complement the overall decent appearance of the hotel at all. Pool area was nice and had a security guard/towel person at all times. Water temp in pool was a bit chilly, but refreshing if you like that sort of thing. Front desk help were very nice and attentive. Very nice property location, but San Pedro isn't exactly a resort area. Would be a nice stopover prior to a cruise, I imagine. Nice walking paths around the marina.

title: “Great location, nice room with breakfast”
text: Just came back from a 2 day sight seeing trip with grown daughter & her two kids (8 & 12). This hotel was perfect for us. It is located just 2 blocks from the metro in a pretty residental area within walking distance of the Capital. ( We left the car in multiday parking & took the metro into town. Saved a lot of money & headache that way.) When the front desk realized that there were 4 of us, he upgraded us to a larger suite without any increase in cost. We moved from the original building to the annex. And the price was right--significantly less than $100 a night. The facilities must have been upgraded since some of the other reviews were written. Our room was large, clean, and well layed out. The bathroom was small but nicely done and very clean. The free breakfast was one of the best I've ever seen. We did have some problems with the elevator but they were working on it. I would love to go back . It made Washington fun & affordable.

title: “Nice for a short stay.”
text: The hotel lobby and restaurant are very nice and the location for airport access is outstanding. The shuttle service is convenient and timely. I stayed in the center wing and it had a bit of a Motel feel. The hallway seemed like an enclosed external walkway and the room quality is in line with what you would expect from a place with outside doors. The lobby, reception and registration were vastly different from my room. West tower may be better. Overall, not bad and I would stay again if it were a very short stay with an early flight.

title: “Historical Hotel With Great Amenities”
text: For a historical hotel that has kept its charm and elegance the Brown Palace can't be beat. The price was less than similar hotels (Marriott, Ritz, Hilton etc.). Our large king room overlooked the stain glassed atrium and was furnished nicely. The bathroom was up-to-date with wonderful soft towels, and the shower included a rain shower head. Turn down service with ice was discretely done. The atrium hosts afternoon tea, and later in the evening cocktails are served. Fabulous piano playing can be found in the atrium or the Ship's Tavern restaurant on a daily basis. Ellington's serves a fabulous breakfast. In fact the Ship's Tavern restaurant must still be the place to have a great lunch. A steady stream of people filled the tables. This hotel is also very close to downtown/LoDo restaurants, museums, the convention center, and business offices. Furthermore, we easily rented an Avis car which was only 1 block from the hotel. If you need to be in downtown Denver, this hotel has ambiance, history, and location for the traveler. Take time to enjoy the Brown Palace.

title: “Sufficient”
text:
When I arrived at the airport, I came into Terminal D and had the worst time finding my way to the Marriott. I would not necessarily blame this on the hotel, but more-so the airport itself (which has a terrible layout). I had to walk outside in the cold all the way to Terminal B, re-enter the airport and finally crossed the walkway to the hotel. 
The hotel itself is nice, everything one would expect from a Marriott. We had a room on the Concierge Level and I have no complaints about the room or its cleanliness. The bed was soft and had a plentiful amount of pillows. The Concierge Lounge was nice, with a full bar and h'ordeurves. 
The parking situation is a bit of a pain...but being at an airport, you can't ask for much more. 
As far as the restaurant/bar goes, the staff is great and the atmosphere is nice. The menu could use a few more options and it's definitely pricey. 
The only good thing about the location of this hotel is if you have an early morning flight. There is absolutely nothing else around except the airport. The closest thing is a Ruby Tuesday.
The hotel staff were a bit lacking. The front desk was not overly helpful and did not seem like they cared. We would leave the room mid-day for a bit and request maid service...only to come back to an untouched room. This was very disappointing.

title: “Not really impressed”
text:
I don't like to be only negative, so first - the positives. The rooms and hotel in general were clean. The staff was friendly and helpful. The hotel has resort-type amenities such as a large pool area, fitness center, lobby gardens, and restaurant/tiki bar, as well as a business center. 
So for the negatives:
1. Stayed on the 2nd floor, and our room did not have central heating and air conditioning. Instead, there was a wall-mounted unit which didn't blow enough hot air (was in the 30s outside) to heat the entire room. In addition, the windows aren't sealed very well, so if we opened the curtains, there was a quick, palpable drop in temperature in the room.
2. Parking is $13/day.
3. Hotel is in a dead area. There is essentially nothing interesting in the immediate area around the hotel, just a few lofts apartments and office/indutrial buidlings. While technically on the riverwalk, it is on the nature trail part of the riverwalk - 15-20 mins. walk to the central tourist area. There are no shops/restaurants on the riverwalk section near the hotel. It is far enough away that the hotel staff recommended either a cab or trolley ride (trolley runs 9a-9p) rather than a walk. If you end up driving, you still end up paying too much to park downtown and you defeat the purpose of getting a hotel in the downtown area.
4. The bathroom isn't that small, but it has little/no counter space.
The only type of stay I would recommend for this hotel is for families with children, who might enjoy taking advantage of the resort amenities. For business, singles, couples, or party travelers, would be adequate but would leave issues to overcome in order to enjoy yourself.

title: “Perfect, pet friendly overnight stay”
text: We were going to NC to pick up a new puppy, and wanted to bring our adult dog. We were so happy that there was a Sheraton available to stay at near the pick up location. Knowing that Sheraton was a pet friendly hotel we immediately booked our stay. The hotel was beautiful, and clean, with a great lobby & bar area. The staff was wonderfully pleasant. The room was spacious and modern, and the bed was very comfortable. The room service breakfast was on time and very good. We would definitely stay again if we are ever back in the area.

title: “Great hotel, great location, great service!!!”
text: Everything about this hotel is wonderful!!! Stayed there Super Bowl weekend for a cheap getaway from the Twin Cities with the girlfriend. Took the El Train from Midway and had to walk over the bridge to get there. A short 2 minute walk. The second we got there we were greeted by an extremely friendly staff. Offering us bottled water during a very relaxed check in process. Our room was very nice, spacious and clean. The only issue I had was the tv. The cable wire was loose in the back and it had to be tightened a few times. But I was there to have fun and unwind so spent little time with the tv. The happy hour had 2 very friendly bartenders that kept the drinks coming! In 2 days probably had 10 crown and cokes with a generous amount of Crown. The dual showerheads in the shower made to a relaxing way to start the day after a great nights' sleep on the comfy beds. And the location of the hotel is amazing!!! Walked to the Hancock Building, Millenium Park and everywhere in between. A ton of bars one street up on Hubbard and the Magnificent Mile is a 5 minute walk. Excellent Hotel for a cheap price!

title: “The Best Place !”
text:
You cannot get a better place to stay in New York than this...
In the Manhattan region, walking distance to every second place (its another thing that we went in the end of winter and it was still cold for our Indian skins). You can see the Empire State Building from left side of the property if you are in the upper floors (the lower floors would give you glimpse of other buildings). 
But although the distances are really less, if you take a cab, you might have to pay through the nose, as you'll have to go round in circles in the 'one-way roads'. Take a map with you, get to know the direction of the traffic, and simply by crossing the roads each time you'll be able to save a lot.
Coming back to the property, the rooms are really small... but the room service makes up for it. If something you want is not available, they'll connect you to the nearest vendor and without any call charges too. 
A small restaurant in the Ground Floor caters to the room service, but I'd say its the best... loved it ! 
Free WiFi, free incoming calls, et al. They also have a discounted airport transfer service.

title: “Very nice weekend at the Hyatt!”
text: We booked a stay at the Hyatt Penn's Landing through Priceline for $100 and were more than pleased with our accomodations. The hotel is situated right on the river and offers some wonderful views. We had a 18th floor room with a view of the river and boats. The staff was friendly and helpful. The room was beautifully clean and comfortable. The bed was nice with lots of pillows. The bathroom had upgraded granite countertops and moen fixtures. The only thing that some may not like about this hotel is that it is a bit of a walk to town. The footbridge is a good way to avoid the traffic and then it's 3-4 blocks to get to where all the action is. But, for the price, I think you can't beat it!

title: “A real Gem! Just loved this Trendy Boutique Hotel”
text:
Wow... After reading the other comments on TripAdvisor, I decided to book 6 nights at this hotel for our familly vacation. We were pleasently surprised with the great boutique hotel. 
First of all, location... it's a half a block away from Times Square... Great Irish Pub next door, and two very good Italian restaurants up the street and a Starbucks just a accross the street. 
The continental breakfast was fantastic... from 7am to 12noon, we started our day off with Fresh Croissants, a Bagel coffee and orange juice. This was in a great setting with relaxing Zen music playing...
The Pool, wet and dry Sauna and small gym are located on the second floor just steps away from the pool... wow, this is were they spend the $$$... what a nice setting. The pool is more for adults, but my 6year daughter enjoyed it just the same! And so did I, with the swim up bar, what more can you ask for.
The rooms were clean. We had a "superior" room with a king size bed... spacious room.... only a few drawbacks, no door to the bathroom area so if someone was in the bathroom at nite, the ligth would shine into the bedroom area... but very large shower and toillet area with modern fixtures. The room could of used a radio alarm clock and a small table... if I had been there on business, would have prefereed working on a table than sitting on the bed.
Friendly staff, we had great service.... 
The bar, located in the lobby, is buzzing Almost every night... a real trendy spot.
I will definalty stay there the next time I am in NYC...

title: “"Best Girls' Weekend Ever"”
text: My girlfriends and I came in on a Saturday for an overnight girls' weekend. When we arrived we were greeted by a "gentlemen" name Frank who escorted us from our car to the hotel. He collected our luggage from our vehicle and took us to the front desk where we met Dion. Dion was very nice and courteous. We told Frank we were here for one night and we told him what we wanted to do for the weekend. He was very knowledgeable of the area. He knew just where to eat, tour, shop and party. We had the best time ever. We took the Ferry to Staten Island, ate lunch in Seaport, shopped in Soho and partied in Manhattan. Frank made sure we had everything we needed to have a good time and feel safe. He made sure we took the right cabs and explained everything in detail where everything was. Everything was in walking distance. Our room was just right, we had a beautiful view of the river and the seaport. The room was very spacious, we had a large TV and a beautiful bathroom. They had a wonderful buffet for breakfast the next day. Everybody was very courteous, warm and dedicated in making our stay pleasurable. We definitely want to come back to this hotel. I highly recommend this Best Western and ask for Frank for all your needs during your stay.

title: “LOVE SEATTLE”
text: the hotel is In the heart of the city, best transit system, cool misty air. the people are very pleasant and helpful La Quinta staff knowledgeable the rooms were quiet for in the city. the amenities were pleantiful great layout of the lobby. the thing we did not care for was the tight parking and only one lane to drive up to front door

title: “Bad bones - Ok skin....”
text:
My partner and I love a modern, chic hotel. This is why I am a big fan of the W brand. However, I also like new, which the W Lakeshore is not. At first glance the property looked amazing but as you looked closer you could tell it was an old hotel that had a lot of issues covered up by dim lighting and modern fixtures.
The Bliss spa was awesome. One of the best spa facilities I've been to and very reasonably priced.
On weeknd nights the the lobby turns into a hip hop lounge with hundreds of people. We had to wait in line to simply get through the front door of our hotel. It seemed to be a very rough crowd. The concierge said they planned on getting a different DJ to try to distract the current crowd from coming to the W.
Overall, it is a great location. Helpful staff and you can definitely get good rates. However, if you are hoping for something new and modern, this place misses out on the new.

title: “impeccable service, unique traditional style”
text:
Walking into this hotel was unbelievably refreshing after the hapless amateur service I received at my previous hotel in suburban Boston. The minute the concierge addressed me I knew this hotel knew what it was doing. Every employee is truly helpful and gracious, without seeming put-on. It's just an amazing feeling to know that the hotel actually cares that you are there.
The room decor reminds me of my grandparents and that's a GREAT thing-- the furniture is solid and of classic 1920s oriental style, which is very rare in this day of techno mod style that gets so boring after you stay in trendy hotel after trendy hotel. I loved feeling like I was stepping into an older time, without feeling like I was sacrificing any comfort or cleanliness. 
I had a junior suite with a city view-- kind of wish I'd upgraded to the harbor view, but oh well. The room is lovely.
All in all there are just great vibes about this place. I will try to stay here again (though next time I might not be on business with my company paying the tab). But the I think the price is worth it for the great style and service.

title: “Steer clear -- the Hotel Icon was a terrible experience.”
text:
I booked this room via Priceline. I was given a room on a floor that was being painted and the smell was terrible. All I wanted to do was take a long bath and relax in my room. My weird little room didn't have a bathtub, and just a drain in the floor with a shower head attached to the wall -- no walls or stall around the shower. The paint fumes were so bad that I couldn't relax in the room. When I called the front desk and asked to be moved, I was told that as I had booked thru Priceline, a move would be considered an up charge. I was quoted a charge of $40, just to be moved to a room with a bathtub. They also said they could not be sure that my new room would be away from the paint fumes. I declined to pay the $40 for the move, and to escape the fumes I went down to the bar to watch a little TV. I had a few drinks and cleared my tab and went to bed. In the morning, I looked at the bill that was slipped under my door and saw that someone else's bar tab had been charged to my room to the tune of $147! 
I took a shower in the weird cattle trough area, which got the entire bathroom floor wet. I then spent the next 30 minutes coaxing the water down the drain with towels so that I could dry my hair without standing in inches of water. Upon check out I argued my bill and got the rogue charges removed, however, it took the Hotel Icon almost a week to credit my account the $147. 
I WILL NEVER, EVER STAY AT THE HOTEL ICON AGAIN -- it was a horrendous experience.

title: “Ransomed...for my parking pass.”
text:
Booked on bonus time.
Room not ready @ check-in. 
Had to listen to the classic sales pitch before I got my parking pass. 
It gets real tiring when you have to deal with pushy, unrelenting sales pitch.
Elevator #4 not working.
Keys had to be re-programmed twice, took over a half hour to get in my room. 
Arturo needs to learn how to program keys.
Asked for a receipt when returning the movies, woman @ the front desk argued with me, telling me that I didn't need one. If I trusted your abilities I would not have asked for one.
I question if this bonus time is even worth it.

title: “Unexceptional, but solid”
text:
We had a decent enough stay at the Hilton, just a few guys, in Los Angeles for business. We had pretty typical rooms, not one of the big corner rooms -- those look very big on the floor plans! But our rooms were just typical, although I'd say the bathroom was exceptionally large. Nice bathroom. I'd stay here with my family and kids, without hesitation.
 We had executive floor access, and I was pretty underwhelmed by the breakfast offerings there. I am beginning to think having executive floor access is quite overrated. Of course, getting free yoghurt and cereal and muffins and orange juice is not to be scoffed at on vacation is it? We'd probably have paid $15 for all that, if we had eaten downstairs. Enh. Eating at hotels is never really a treat, is it?
 Otherwise, the bar service at the hotel bar was average, the drinks were...average, but at hotel-lobby prices. It was ho-hum. 
 That's about all I saw of the hotel! There was a mini-bar, which we didn't use, and there were some nice fruit baskets in the room when we got there. It was pretty nice, but it just didn't blow me away.
 This hotel is close to the red line's Universal City stop. Indeed, for $1.25 we rode all the way from the airport to the hotel. Two things you should know before you do this. The first is, it is a pretty long ride, and it was pretty rowdy on the green line from airport to imperial. But once you get to Universal City, the hotel is *uphill* significantly from the red line station. This may not be obvious from google maps, but it is a serious uphill climb to the hotel, so be in good shape or try to hail a cab...or just sweaty and exhausted and fall down in the lobby like we did.

title: “Very nice experience”
text:
Booked in for two nights-a bed and breakfast package at $159/night. Decided on this property over a couple more centrally located downtown because of the price and because they offer free parking.
Upon checking in, I noticed a very rude guest in line behind me. I wont go into details, but I asked the associate, Jodi, to please make sure I was no where near this rude woman. Jodi was very sweet and took care of it. She also made nice small talk while checking me in and inquired during my stay if everything was ok.
The property, only about 6 weeks old, was very clean. Our room was on the 8th floor. The room was clean and the air con worked perfectly. The bathroom was very standard; nice big shower, but I was somewhat disappointed to not have a tub. 
The Heavenly Bed was nice, though the sheets were pretty stiff. Hopefully with washing they will soften up. We did sleep soundly both nights.
I would stay at this property again has we come to Austin to visit friends, not necessarily to party downtown. The Domain area is nice. We had a lovely dinner one night at North, visited the Apple store, American Eagle, and Coffee Bean and Tea Leaf. (I was super excited to have a Coffee Bean in Texas!) 
Even though we had the breakfast package, we awoke after ten both mornings so just took a coffee and muffin at Coffee Bean and Tea Leaf. We did have drinks and snacks one evening in the hotel bar. They had good happy hour specials.
I did find it odd there was no literature in the room to tell me about the area or the offerings of the hotel.

title: “Simply great!”
text: We have spended one week in Candlewood Suites and I must say that I was really impressed. It's perfectly situated, they are really helpful and it was clean and confortable. Oh! and they had free WiFi, which we didn't know. Simply great!

title: “Nice hotel, OK location, Mediocre Service.”
text:
Before booking our trip to NYC, we had decided that we wanted to try out a few neighborhoods. We decided during the week we visited that we would try to stay at 2-3 different properties (although it might be annoying to continue to move around). After spending 2 nights at The Standard in the Meatpacking District, we moved on to Ink48 in the Hell's Kitchen neighborhood. I will say, before visiting NYC, I only knew of Hell's Kitchen as a TV cooking show. 
As many Kimpton hotels are, the property was beautiful. New, trendy, modern, larger rooms (especially for New York). However, Hell's Kitchen as a neighborhood is a bit off the beaten track for me. It is not a FAR walk to Times Square (but it's not the Meatpacking District). It's a bit more worn, ethnic., less choices for food, etc. I will, say, however, the view from the rooftop bar was amazing. This is probably one of the best views I saw in NYC. Our room, however, faced away from the city (although we paid for a city view through our travel agent- who also mentioned to the hotel that we were VIP customers). 
Ink48, as a whole, did not make me feel like a VIP customer at all. They did not allow us to check in until after 3 PM. The hotel front desk assured us that he would call us when a room was ready. Standard check-in is at 3 PM. We arrived back to the hotel at 3:15 and he never did call us. At this time a room was ready, but it was neither on a high floor nor a city view. I was a bit disappointed. No one helped us with our bags, the front desk staff were very short with us, they would not allow for a late-check out even after I expressed my disappointment with the service. After checking out we had the hotel hang onto our bags, we returned to the hotel before heading to the airport to get our bags (and it took 20 minutes for them to bring them out- even though the lobby was empty). The concierge also held out his hand and waited for me to tip him (I was disgusted- to say the least)! 
Some perks at Kimpton, that I do find great are:
- Wine hour once a day 
- Pet- friendly (they even had treats at the door for pets) 
- Coffee bar in the morning! (this is great especially when a Starbucks is not near!) 
If you are looking to stay in NYC, I would recommend the other Kimpton property, Eventi, over this one. The staff, service, and location of the hotel just was not worth the 400 dollars a night we paid. I will probably stay at Kimptons again in the future, but I will probably skip Ink48!

title: “Beautifully renovated public spaces make for a special experience”
text: We stayed 3 nights at the Palmer House in April. The hotel has recently been renovated in the Art Deco style it originally had. The lobby now gives the feeling of the hotel's first glory days at the turn of the 20th century. Beautiful restoration of the ceiling and decorative elements. The rooms/bathrooms are on the small side but comfortable and well equipped. Ask for a room farther from the El as some of the front-facing rooms can be noisy and dark.

title: “Nice looking, large modern rooms, but away from everything.”
text: We loved the hotel, room was large & very clean. They do charge for internet. The hotel is a little secluded, it's far from restaurants and local attractions. But if you are looking for some time away from the city and to stay in your room for a romantic weekend and want to use the hotel's restaurant or room service for all your meals, then this is the place to stay.

title: “Friendly and good location”
text: First night stayed on the 4th floor, second night stayed on the 7th. Walls were thin, but got to overhear a hilarious fight between a couple about how bad a gallery opening food had been. Staff was friendly, room was clean, no complaints.

title: “Vintage Beauty”
text: We stayed here on a business/pleasure trip. We stayed in room 311. Our room was beautiful. However, the bathroom was built for a short person, because the toilet is so close to the wall, that one must sit side-ways. The bed was very comfortable, complete with luxurious sheets and pillows. There is some street noise that may bother light-sleepers. The valet and desk staff are all very professional and helpful. This is a great place for honeymoons and special occasions!

title: “Very disappointed”
text:
Reading some of the other reviews, I wonder if we were in the same hotel. I stayed at this hotel many years ago, and immediately booked when I knew I was going to SF. What a difference between then and now and how the years have taken its toll on this hotel. 
The rooms are quite small by US standards and not up to the normal Marriott standard. We were in a room on the 4th floor and the room looked quite dirty, in fact the toilet was dirty, with urine stains from previous occupants and dust on top of light fittings etc. 
The reception area doesn't look very inviting and the breakfast buffet is what you would expect from a lesser hotel, and again not up to Marriott's normal standards. 
As we were only there for 1 night, I was asked how the stay had been at checkout and I commented that it would be nice when the hotel had been refurbished (and I was serious), but the polite receptionist told me the hotel had already been refurbished....Mr Marriott, get you money back, because it still looks a very tired hotel.
Location is great for Fisherman's Wharf and all the tourist things, but I would look at other hotels in the area before I returned.

title: “Pleasantly Astounded”
text: My oh my. I read all The reviews and took a deep breathe and booked our rooms. The service: exceptional The Value: exceptional. The experience: exceptional. My husband, daughter (2 y/o)and I loved it and the food for breakfast, was amazing and made to order. The bartender for happy hour was spectacular and the ammenities were superb. We worked out daily and enjoyed the equipment and in door swimming pool. We have routinely stayed at 4 Seasons and Fairmount and other 5 star resorts. And yes while those are great so are the prices. But staying at the Embassy suites, we weren't spending thousands of dollars a nite, we spent a couple of hundred and felt totally catered to. Thanks to all the staff at the Jones Maltsberger location. Well Done Embassy Suites Int'l Airport! We are pleasantly astounded and will definitely be back!

title: “Upscale and Modern....”
text: This hotel is right in the middle of everything. It's a short walk to all the major shopping areas as well as Rockefeller Plaza. Nice Gym The staff is extremely helpful and kind. The rooms are a bit small but I feel the amenities make up for it.

title: “Crazy foyer- great hotel”
text: We visited san Francisco on the second leg of our honeymoon, coming straight from Vegas. Having exprienced, above and beyond hotel service from the Bellagio, arriving at the W and fighting our way through crowds of people outside the main doors and then through a crowded foyer, with 3 heavy bags was a bit of a culture shock and the hotels main and only problem. Whilst the food, hotel, bar, rooms and general nature is superb, the foyer and reception area is just kind of stuck there as a last resort and can make checking in and asking for concierge advice a little tricky. Granted, we were in town during the week long sales force conference, taking place over the road, but still thought the service at W, could be better and certainly more personable. Perhaps this was due to the hotel being crowded around the reception area at most times. However, all in all a great hotel, top location, amazing food (breakfast and room snacks- immense) and would stay here agin, albeit not when a conference is in town.

title: “old but decent”
text: I stayed at the Park Manor Suites last night (11/22/03) after a wedding. The rooms were cute and having the kitchenette was a plus. It was nicely priced for a hotel in such a convenient location. The hotel does show its age and the furnishings were well worn and not the highest quality. My friends stayed a couple of doors down from me and their room was slightly different and nicer, so maybe your experience will depend on the room. Although it was November, the room was really warm and stuffy. I could have really used an air conditioner. The walls are extremely thin too. All in all, I would stay there again for the location, but I would prefer to stay somewhere more well-kept.

title: “Amazing”
text:
Amazing Room - Suite on floor 50, could even see times square!!
Amazing Location - turn right up to central park or left to times square. All within 5 mins of walking
Amazing Hotel - Even with Starbucks coffee shop, what more could you ask for!!
Returning later this year - can't wait!!!!!
If you get the opportunity ....... BOOK!!

title: “Good location, great little English Pub attached”
text:
Had our last 2 nights of a 6 night stay in Chicago at this hotel . Very friendly check in staff, told us we were a little early, so they checked our bags in , had about 2 hours to fill, there is a great bar next door called the Elephant and Castle, so I popped in there to watch the England v France Euro 2012 game . The wife went shopping on the Magnificent Mile which is situated at the end of the block , that's one of the great advantages of this hotel , it's great location . Room was fine, air con system was quite old and noisy, so it was a case of only when absolutely neccessary . I did think the bathroom was a bit outdated and did look well used, and to be fair it was quite small. 
Obviously you are ideally situated for whatever you do in the evening, some really good restaurants nearby . Overall a pleasant hotel with very friendly reception staff and concierge . If you are looking for a hotel for Michigan Ave shopping, you won't go far wrong with this one.

title: “Absolutely horrid!”
text:
Well where do I start?
This hotel is terrible. Receptionist speaks little English and not very helpful and confused by very simple questions.
