Our bed linen was dirty upon check in so we asked for some clean sheets that we would have put on ourselves but was told he didn't have access to linen cupboard and gave us two towels to sleep on.
Then our room had ants. When trying to speak to the man he wouldn't get off his mobile phone to talk deal with issues.
Motel has a pool but I guess your skin may fall off if you use it, its absolutely filthy.
As you will see from my other posts I am usually easy to please. Therefore trust me when I say stay away.

title: “Service has gone down the tubes!”
text: We have been staying here for 20 years because we fly out of LAX. This had been our favorite hotel but this last visit was really poor! NO hair dryer in the room! No nut/chex mix given with drinks, no voucher for $20 off food when we park our car for 2 weeks. NOTHING anymore! The room was small and bathroom tiny. We have been Priority Club members for years and years but never again do we plan to stay at this hotel. No service, no customers! No free newspaper anymore either!

title: “Great location! Nice and clean!”
text: We stayed here for one night while visiting family, including our niece and nephew who are attending OSU. The hotel is new and clean. Only drawback is that the doors to the bathroom and shower in the room do not block light at night. A bit disruptive in the middle of the night to have the whole room illuminated. Pretty decent freebie breakfast in the am. Nice firepit outside for enjoying a cocktail. Fantastic location for visiting OSU!

title: “Basic, old hotel room”
text: I must be missing something. I see all these wonderful reviews and my experience was the opposite. My husband and I stayed this past Saturday night. We arrived at 7:30pm only to find out that the parkling gargage was already full. Great. Where to park? I call the front desk to ask for suggestions and they are no help. Finally we find street parking and carry our belongings up the street to the hotel. The check-in process was pleasant. We get to our room, It's a very basic, old hotel room. Feels pretty run down and not so clean. Bummer. We try to use our cell phones. Service is terrible. Can't make a call. We try to use the free wireless. Can't connect. We call the front desk, and are given an 800 number to call for assistance. After 4 attempts with the guy at the 800 number we give up. Unable to connect to the interenet and plan our next day. Very frustrating. Would I stay here again? Absolutely not. There are far too many choices in San Diego.

title: “Fabulous staff.....great location...”
text:
6 of us futzy 60 something friends stayed at the James for the past 3 nights. Location is perfect, one block w. of Michigan and a few short blocks n. of the river. Staff is welcoming, attentive; Concierge Keaton (hope it's spelled right) was extremely welcoming and helpful. The lobby is quite beautiful in a subdued, modern way. Rooms are spotless, and the cleaning staff seemed tireless in their efforts to keep our rooms just so. Beds extremely comfy. Appreciated the pretty console/fridge/good window shades/great look of the bedrooms.....
Downside: our rooms (two double beds) had no individual reading lights over each bed, unless we just didn't figure out the system. The "reading corner" had no lights. I suppose it's designed for laptops, but a light would have been great. Pretty bathroom, but the door between it and the bedroom was cumbersome and kept coming off track. Would have appreciated a mirror in the bedroom, so if the bathroom was occupied, one would still be available. The reading corner could be a great place for a built in vanity or desk, with lights. Closet was in the bathroom, so if it was occupied, again, you were out of luck. No exhaust fan in the bathroom. 
I'd still recommend this place, particularly for singles or couples, and I would certainly stay there again. Just a few changes would make it topnotch. The staff, location, lovely modern design and cleanliness made up for the few glitches.

title: “Average stay, great location”
text:
The room was really small. Corner room but couldn't tell. Room had a king bed with about 3 feet all around it and that was the whole room. Had a window but was behind high headboard and couldn't look out. Shower, no tub. Couldn't stand at bathroom sink with door open. Had to put my duffel in the room hall and some stuff in the small closet. Tiny corner desk, couldn't walk by with desk chair out (and only chair in the room.) No minibar but did have a coffee maker. I talked to other guests and they said the rooms with 2 queen beds were larger and they offer a King suite but didn't see it. Bed was comfortable but had 4 pillows that were so hard and thick it gave me crick in my neck. 
Breakfast in the cafe was good, services was OK, most people were having the Sunday buffet so the off the menu service was a little weak.
Valet parking was fast and efficient. Front desk staff was very pleasant.
Location is great, cafe/bar has a view of the wall of the Alamo grounds.

title: “Incredibilly BAD service”
text:
their service is the worst I have ever experienced!. On the phone at least, their front desk don't understand/answer your questions but instead keep saying "bye". I asked this front desk person's name for future reference, he somehow got scared and stopped answering my calls. I called back many times. Later on while cancelling my reservation, the other person from front desk finally answered my call but does not know anything about cancellation policy or how to cancel, and like the last person, he interrupted me by a "bye" and hang up the phone. 
very irresponsible, no wonder there's only ONE Carter Hotel, and I wonder how long can this ONE survive based on such service.

title: “Better Options Nearby”
text:
I was disappointed in this hotel. There were some good aspects: nice hot breakfast and good location near downtown, 6th Street, and Capitol. There was a fridge in the room which I didn't use, but would be nice for some. Wireless internet was free. 
But, so many drawbacks. I had to strip the bed and remake it because housekeeping obviously didn't know how to make a bed and mine was "short-sheeted". The carpet was dirty. I had an accessible room and the shower spewed water all over the bathroom floor. The HVAC was noisy and I couldn't get it to stay at temperature. We ordered a cab for getting to our meeting in the morning and the driver called at the last minute to cancel so we scrambled for a cab.
The cost was only slightly less than other hotels in the area, so you might want to choose the Hilton, Courtyard, or Radisson.

title: “What a wonderful hotel!”
text:
My mother and I stayed at this hotel for our first trip to Boston. We were delighted with the attention to detail, cleanliness, location and most of all the friendly staff who made our stay so wonderful. 
We got everything we needed, from all the requested accommodations in the room to a water bottle on our way out every day in preparation for our walk. Our concierge Nick answered all the questions we had and booked our tours, gave us restaurant suggestions that were totally on point and gave us a train discount card as well. The hotel has 2 amazing restaurants as part of it so we always had a place to eat and hang out after a long day without going anywhere. The train station is literally next door so we really had all the conveniences at our fingertips. Also our room overlooked Fenway park which I thought was very neat. 
We felt so welcome and well taken care of. I will absolutely come back to this hotel in all our future visits and highly recommend it.

title: “Great Bargain and Very Nice Room”
text: This is a great hotel, great price but also the room was very clean and nice. Bed was very comfortable and staff was friendly. We will definitely stay here again.

title: “Outstanding for what it is...”
text:
Aloft is a cheap, quick, overnight hotel brand. In my book, Aloft Phoenix Airport is great for spending the night before an early flight. I've booked at this property every single time I fly out early. For one, with SPG Gold & Platinum, you get free vehicle parking. All guests get a complimentary airport shuttle, I want to say hours are 4am-Midnight. I have even had them pick me up from the airport and get me back to my car in a complementary town car before... the modern aesthetics and contemporary design create a pleasing environment. The w xyz bar is a nice touch, and the pool table and 24 hr pool and fitness center round out a nice set of on-site amenities. 
Alina at the front desk was simply amazing. I was trying to arrange an in-room amenity at another property I was flying to the next morning, and to do so, I had to print, copy, scan, and fax. Alina helped me do this using the computer and copier, and I was able to arrange the amenity successfully. Well done!
Full Disclosure Time...
The beds are NOT comfortable. It's an Aloft, not a Westin. However, I would like to see this addressed, considering air travelers do enjoy sleeping in a hotel room. The alarm clock does not make noise...it blinks. NOT helpful if you use a sleeping mask. And beware, the hair dryers are very underpowered.
However...
Complimentary bottled water. Win. Power outlets RIGHT next to the bed. Win. HDTV with full HD signal and connection center. Win. In-room recycling. Biggest win. 
Just keep in mind this hotel is not a getaway property. You're not going to be rested. But you are gonna get great service in a great location for flying out of Phoenix.

title: “It's no wonder this hotel is #1!!!!!”
text:
Here is the lowdown.
 A stay at this hotel will ruin you for other hotels! From the moment that you enter the sumptuous lobby and are greeted with a smile by the staff and concierge, you know that you have stepped into a place with class.
First:
We requested a large corner room on a high floor when we made the reservation. (We learned this trip trick from reading other trip advisor reviews) The room itself (2221) was large and impeccably well designed and very comfortable. The bathroom was beautiful!!!
Very large with a separate shower and tub.
The bed was the most comfortable that we have slept in in all the years we have traveled.
Second:
LOCATION LOCATION LOCATION!!!
Perfectly situated 2 blocks from Times Square and subways and 2 blocks from 5th Avenue and shopping!!!
Who could ask for a better location?!!
Even though we were right in the middle of all the action,..... the room was so quiet!! Didn't hear a thing all night long.
In closing:
This hotel is not number one without good reason.
Our best wishes to the Sofitel's continuing success.
Thank you for making our stay one we will never forget!!
And THANK YOU TO TRIP ADVISOR for once again coming through with another winner!
Thanks again,
Michael and David
San Diego, California

title: “Best value for your money”
text:
We stayed at this hotel back in February 2012 for a week and it certainly provided us with value.
The rooms were larger then I expected, with a sitting area, in addition to a dinning table. A small kitchenette tucked off to the side provided us with great meal flexibility. While we still had the option to eat out, we made use of it once or twice in an effort to mitigate the overall cost of our trip. As someone who spends the majority of their time out of the hotel when travelling, the room size always has been the most important part of travel. I enjoy lounging after a long day of walking Manhattan end to end. In terms of location, this hotel was place perfectly. A five minute walk to Grande Central Station provided us easy access to the metro.
There was nothing particularly exceptional about the service of the staff, it was on par with what you'd expect. We arrived early on the first night, and the staff said they would get our room ready faster, and allowed us to store our luggage at the hotel until it was ready. There was no free wifi available in the rooms (there was for a fee). There was, however, free wifi in the main lobby. It was a touch annoying running downstairs with our laptops.
My main gripe about this hotel was the elevator. An odd thing to complain about, but I've seen molasses move quicker. We were "lucky" enough to get one of the highest floors. By the end of our trip, that luck felt more like a curse. We had to ride those infernal contraptions that much longer, being stopped every other floor!
All in all, a very good experience at this hotel. I have, and will recommend to others in the future. In terms of value for your dollar, this hotel is really a no brainer.

title: “Second time at the Trump...I'll be back a third time for Lollapalooza in August.”
text:
This is a follow-up to an earlier review.
My second stay at the Trump was amazing. I honestly can't find fault with any part of this hotel. Service is impeccable and unobtrusive. I had just stayed at the Mandarin Oriental New York for one night, so I had high expectations, but the Trump was perfect in every way.
This time I was in a spa room on the 14th floor, whereas the first time I was in a room that was probably a condotel room with a kitchenette. In either case, the room was impeccably decorated and furnished.
My only regret is that I was a solo traveler and didn't bring the girlfriend along, but we're making a trip in early August for Lollapalooza and already have the Trump booked. I'm sure we'll use the spa during that visit, so stay tuned for another review in August.

title: “Great Stay”
text:
We stayed in New York for a week and had a great time. 
This Hotel really added to that. The location is very nice and near different metro stations. We really liked Soho and were happy we were not staying in the touristic Time Square area. 
The room was really nice (very new) and very spacious (especially for a New York hotel). The bed was amazing! The bathroom was also very good. No noise (eventhough we were sleeping on the streetside). Friendly staff as well. We could really recommend this Hotel.

title: “well run boutique hotel in mid town”
text:
I found the Hotel Giraffe a satisfying experience not least the well appointed and spacious rooms. The Hotel provides free wifi throughout, and has a cosy informal lobby which also serves as a club like lounge for the guests where breakfast is served; and also drinks and cocktails in the afternoon. Service is efficient in an unobtrusive way.This hotel is conducive for longer stays as it has the feel of service apartments, and located in a centrally located yet relatively quiet neighborhood with a residential feel. Room decor is elegant in an understated way(perhaps a touch somber with hues of gray dominating)Their king suites are well configured, but if possible, ask for rooms ending with 06, which faces Park Ave and has better natural light. There are some nice touches as housekeeping puts on classic music in the guestrooms in the evenings
One minor complaint was the card keys we had sometimes played up. Another limitation is the hotel lacks knowledgeable concierge which some larger more touristy hotels would have. Whilst two subway stations are close by, unfortunately this are confined to only one local line(line 6). Overall recommended

title: “Great hotel and services”
text: We visited Chicago for the first time from New Zealand and very much enjoyed our stay. Breakfasts and drinks at night were a great plus as was being able to do our laundry. The rooms very large, clean and ours had a great view. The receptionist was very helpful and let us book in early, and the lady who welcomed us into breakfast was so lovely she made our day. The hotel was close to everything, but we also appreciated being able to eat in P J Clarke's when the weather was too bad to go out. Would definitely stay there again.

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text: Pleasantly surprised at the quality. You expect this at a full service Marriott but the hotel was clean and in a great neighborhood. Several very nice restaurants next to the hotel. Great ftiness room.

title: “Great Location, would happily come back”
text:
Great hotel only one block away from Pier 39 and Fisherman's Wharf. Selected this hotel because of its good name and central location to a great number of facilities in San Francisco. The room was great, a good size and very comfortable. The outlook was miserable though but I suspect not many rooms had a great outlook as we were in quite a busy area.
It was nice to sit outside the hotel where they had log burners that would keep you cosy, for those that have been to San Francisco in the summer will appreciate. It can be hot one day and strangely cold the next.
The hotel has free wi-fi in the lobby but chargeable if you want it in your room which I felt cheapened the hotel as many other "lower" class hotels offer free wi-fi through out. My only other gripe would be the $50 per day car parking charge, I appreciate the area is expensive to park a car but I do feel that level of charge to paying guests is a bit steep. Overall I would come back here again if I return to San Francisco.

title: “Great Stay at the Hilton Phoenix Airport”
text: My husband and I flew into Phoenix at the end of June 2008 and spent the first two nights of our holiday at the Hilton Phoenix Airport. We contacted the hotel via the courtesy phone in the arrivals hall and the mini bus arrived in around 10 minutes. A warm welcome awaited us at check-in, along with two bottles of refreshing water! We booked a king room on the executive floor (which is the fourth and top floor of the hotel). The room was large and also contained a settee, coffee table, desk and chair. There was an in-room safe, coffee maker (teabags also provided), hairdryer, iron and ironing board. Our balcony faced on to the pool area. The room was spotlessly clean and the bed lovely and comfortable. The bathroom was small, but nicely furnished and had a large selection of Crabtree and Evelyn toiletries. We did not hear any noise emanating from rooms either side or the hallway. Our package included breakfast and on the second evening we ate in the hotel restaurant (there is also a bar which also serves meals). The food was delicious and the service very good. There are other hotels in the vicinity, which may also serve food, but we were quite happy to eat in the hotel. We had pre-booked a Gray Line tour for the second day - "Valley of the Sun" - and thoroughly enjoyed this. Special thanks here go to our tour guide Charlie, who also picked us up at the hotel and dropped us off again at the end of the tour. The hotel also has a fitness centre, business centre and small gift shop. At the end of our stay we travelled by courtesy transport back to the airport to pick up a rental car and for a nominal $5 charge we were driven directly to the car rental centre. We made our reservation via the Hilton website and consider the rate we paid (particularly in view of the favourable £/$ exchange rate) taking into account the quality of accommodation and delicious breakfast, to represent excellent value for money. We found every member of the hotel staff we came into contact with during our stay to be very friendly and helpful. If we should fly into Phoenix again, we will definitely stay at this hotel.

title: “Very nice hotel...but $40 per night for valet???”
text: Went to LA for a concert at the LA Sports Arena. I found this hotel on Trip Advisor and it looked like a great place to stay for the night! Upon arrival, the staff was very professional and helpful. The rooms were big, recently remodled and very nice. Our room was on the 9th floor with a neat view of the Disney Concert Hall and surrounding buildings. When we left for the evening we took the hotels courtsey car to LA Live for dinner. Our only complaint was the valet parking...the Sunday-Thursday rates are $40 per night and there is no self parking!!! Just thought this was extremely expensive considering you're already paying a higher rate to stay at a such a nice hotel...

title: “What are they thinking? Under Construction”
text:
Overall, the hotel was very good. Clean, comfy beds. What got to me was that the lobby is being remodeled and the rennovations can be quite loud. So the guy at the front desk puts me in a room on the third floor, so I can get as close to the construction noise as possible. I truly wondered what I did to offend him..
It's nice that they make noise only from 9 to 5 during the rennovation. Too bad I was in the room trying to work from 9 to 12 noon. I couldn't hear myself think. 
They have a very nice restaurant on the top floor. Very nice view of the city. Other than the construction, it's not a bad hotel.

title: “Great location - okay rooms”
text:
We stayed at Harborside Inn over Labor Day weekend. You cannot fault the location....we took the T from the airport and got off after one stop right outside the hotel. Quincy Market is right across the street and the historical sights of central Boston are a short walk away. All of the tours seemed to start one block away at the Aquarium which was convenient as well.
The hotel itself is fairly no frills. The lobby was nice and people seemed to be taking advantage of the 4 computers in the lobby. Our room was large enough and the decor was quite modern / 70's ish. The linen was decent quality and the bed reasonably comfortable. The bathroom was clean and large. Our only issue was the blinds on the windows -- we had an atrium facing room -- and the blinds (flimsy plasticy type) did not close enough to block out the light. The flat screen TV also had a blue light that was distracting and enough to keep a light sleeper awake. No room service.
All in all the location was excellent and we would stay again if the price was right.

title: “Great Location, Good Hotel”
text:
This hotel is in a great location nearby to Times Square. Staff went out of their way to make our stay comfortable. One elevator was broke which lead to long queues when leaving and entering the building.. The hotel however were apologetic and we were greeted each day with a drink and cookies!
The room was on the small side in comparison to other hotels. However it was clean and everything we needed was included.
We also managed to get complimentary early and late checkout which was great!

title: “A good choice”
text: The hotel was good. It was clean and quiet, except that the noise of door-closing did disturb us a little bit. The housekeeping was very prompt and efficient. The room was spacious and comfortable. We used the laundry service too. We tried the breakfast in a nearby cafe (Frontier) which was good as well.

title: “Great Stay, Great Value!”
text: I chose this hotel because it had amazing reviews so I decided to take my chances. I was not disappointed. The location was great, close to the airport and downtown (offers a shuttle). There's a restaurant next door just a few steps away. The staff was very courteous, and helpful. The rooms are modern, spacious, and clean. The value is great, this hotel should be rated higher than it is. I will definetely recommend this hotel and will be staying there again for my next trip to Charlotte.

title: “Tired but trying hard!”
text: Had three nights here as part of our trip to Washington, New York and Boston for my 60th birthday. I had stayed at the Stanford many years ago when it was in its prime but found it to be tired and sadly a little shabby. They were doing some renovation work whilst we were there which didn't help as the lift was often out of service and there were dust sheets and noisy workmen everywhere. It was not cheap to stay here but the location being so good makes it just about value for money. However, if I ever go back to New York I would stay elsewhere.

title: “Cancellation Scam”
text: We didn't actually make it to this hotel but I wanted to share our cancellation experience to warn other unsuspecting travellers that some hotels have a very hard nose approach to cancellations and furthermore set up their cost structure to maximise their take. The reservation was made directly with the hotel a couple of months in advance over the phone. It took several additional calls to ensure we had a booking and eventually the hotel sent an email confirmation (which for some reason had 'modification' at the top and was odd since this was the first communication from the hotel). At no time on the phone was there mention of their cancellation policy and it was hidden in the reams of information at the bottom of the email they sent. In addition the rate we were quoted was $329 for the first two nights and then dropping to $209 for the next night and then $289 for the rest of the stay (a total of 6 nights in all). Overall an average of $289 per night. Their cancellation policy states one night penalty and yes you have guessed it, instead of the average or even the lowest we were charged $329 cancellation fee. Their policy states that any change or cancellation within 7 days of arrival has a one night penalty and I called them 4 days ahead of arrival to cancel. I was told that if I spoke to the manager he may be able to reduce the fee but I made several calls to try to speak to him and was told every time that the manager was either off duty and would be in at 11pm (NY time) or was unavailable. I also tried to email the manger but never got a response from him. The only other communication I received from the hotel was that they had charged my card the $329. My recommendation is to avoid this hotel if at all possible unless you are absolutely sure you won't have to cancel within the 7 days prior to arrival.

title: “Wonderful experience”
text: Wonderful experience- Abdul went above and beyond to make sure our stay amazing and he was very accommodating to all our needs. Great location- very easy to get too. Would definitely stay at this hotel again and recommend to my friends and family.

title: “Noisy area & small rooms”
text: We thought we were being smart by pre-paying a few weeks in advance for a special rate. Well it turned out that the special rate got us the cheapest smallest room in the hotel. The room was so small, there was no dresser for our clothes and not even a chair to sit on. Construction in the area kept us awake at night. We asked if we could upgrade to a larger room and they told us that all of the rooms were basically the same. So then we called the main office and asked if we could move to the uptown Hilton on 53rd and they told us no. So a valuable lesson was learned - never pre-pay unless you are really sure of what you are getting.

title: “You get what you pay for (a dump with fresh paint)”
text: This hotel was very cheap but there were problems. The sink and bathroom wall was dirty. Once I pulled back the sheets, there were greasy looking stains, along with something reddish brown smeared on the sheets, along with a hole. I called the front desk and was told that they would check to see if there were clean sheets and bring them to my room. The hotel staff came to the room with the blanket. I explained the blanket was fine and showed him the sheets. He went back downstairs and returned later with two flat sheets. I took them and had to change the linen myself. YUCK!! With another "!" During the night my family and I sweated so bad we were wet. The air was turned down as low as possible and blowing as hard as it could. However it just did not work. I spoke to the manager at checkout and he was completely unconcerned. Probably had heard the complaint before and just didn't do anything about it. His attitude was "Oh really. So what...I got your money. Now get out. Too bad for you." He did nothing. So I'm doing what I can by giving him some free advertisement. Travelers spend a few more dollars and stay somewhere that will be cool and clean.

title: “I think previous reviews are not fair.”
text: I have stayed at this hotel at least 8 times a year for the last 2 years for business. Some of the reviewers here either don't travel often or they really don't know locations, for example "Doubleblowjo" . I'm not sure if you realize this but you must call once you have arrive at the airport to have their shuttle pick you up. If you feel you're that important to have a shuttle waiting for you, try the Fairmont Hotel Downtown San Jose and be ready to pay $200 plus for a room. Remember the Holiday Inn Express is a value hotel, key word "VALUE" . I feel that their price does reflect their value $100 or so for a room, $80 if you come in on a weekend. They would not get a 5 from me but a 4 is well deserve specially for their cleanliness.

title: “Great location”
text:
I think the location of this hotel is hard to beat: Boston's small Chinatown, and the theatre district, are literally on its doorstep. Within 5 - 10 minutes' walk are the interesting districts of South End, Bay Village, Beacon Hill and Downtown Crossing. Sights of interest such as the Boston Common and the Public Garden are also within this walking distance. Despite very good transport options close by, I suspect most tourists will simply need only to head out on foot. Other reviewers have talked about ambulance and other street noise but I was at the back of the building and didn't hear anything over a three-night stay.
The room design and decor is meant to be hip and modern; clearly this won't appeal to all. I'm not quite sure why some object to the screen between the bathroom and bedroom, as the toilet has a solid door and the shower has a glass door. Unless one were particularly noisy using a basin, it shouldn't matter, but each to his or her own, I guess.
Staff were overall friendly and polite. Drank at the bar once, and found the staff there very good and efficient. 
My room had an unusual and unpleasant smell intermittently for the first day when the air-conditioning was used; the cleaners obviously tried to conceal this with room scent. The problem recurred briefly at least once. I didn't raise this with the hotel management. Additionally, one night I'd lost my room key and it took 20 minutes to get served at the front desk, as there was only one staff member available, and several people ahead of me. 
SPG members get free wifi, with up to three devices per account, which was good. Overall, a good, rather than excellent stay, in a really well-located hotel. I'd had a very underwhelming experience at one of the W hotels in New York, however, my Boston experience was positive enough to make me consider this brand again in the future. And I'd very probably stay at the W Boston again in the future.

title: “Great location”
text: Stayed here in connection with a conference. Very nice hotel.

title: “Alright, but didn't meet my Hampton Inn expectations”
text: Booked this hotel because my husband had a medical appointment at Indiana University. (not the best travel circumstances). From past stays at different properties I have a very high opinion of Hampton Inns. While the hotel wasn't bad, it also wasn't the best Hampton Inn I had ever stayed at. Rooms are very small, breakfast was wonderful, staff at the front desk was mildly cool, staff at breakfast were wonderful. There was a water main break directly in front of the hotel, so the water in our room was "chunky" and discolored, and they provided bottled water in the breakfast room, but it was still disgusting to watch the water come out of the shower in the morning. Because we were staying there with a medical appointment we were told parking was compped (valet parking only for $13/day). It didn't show up on our check out statement - but was on our charge account when we returned home. Location was pretty good for dining and shopping.

title: “Excellent all round hotel”
text: Two day business conference with three nights stay. Excellent facilities - massive flat screen tv, sofa, marshmallow bed, tele in the khazi! Restaurant food I couldn't fault - that was three breakfasts, two lunches and an evening meal. Staff very friendly. Only things to watch for - mini bar expensive and the breakfast can take a while - leave yourself time. Location was excellent - superb atmosphere in town in the run up to the super bowl.

title: “Was here two weeks for work and it was as comfortable as home.”
text: Friendly, attentive staff. Great room. Comfortable bed and linens. Awesome food in the restaurant, Lola. Central location within walking distance to many sites and attractions. Fast wifi and a newspaper everyday. Would for sure recommend this hotel for business or pleasure. If I'm back in Seattle I will stay here again!

title: “Something was cheap”
text:
We didn't reserve any motel in San Antonio in advance, so we used HotelCoupons to have one as we walked in.
The rate was cheap and room was well maintained. However, it's close to I-10. If you are sensitive to noise, you should ask a room away from highway.
Everything was as advertised. However, the Wi-Fi was slow. The breakfast had only coffee, orange juice, muffins, and sweet rolls. The bath towels were thin and rough.

title: “Conveniently located near U.W.”
text:
The University Inn is walking distance from the U.W. Seattle campus. Walking to and from the school was easy - plus there is a Starbucks and a variety of restaurants along the way. There is free parking at the inn so leave your car behind and walk ... a lot of people do! Continental breakfast in the lobby is nice - you can make your own Belgian waffles or have some fruit, cereal, yogurt. We also like the "breakfast-to-go" option where you can pick up some breakfast items or have them delivered to your room. If you prefer something heartier and have more time (because there's usually a wait), the Portege Cafe has *wonderful* breakfasts - their specialty French toast dishes are absolutely delicious!
Our room was on the Roosevelt street side, so it was noisy. The mini-fridge made strange noises as it cycled off and on so we ended up unplugging it at night. The A/C is wall-mounted, so the bed nearest it gets very cold while the other side of the room is okay. The bathroom is standard - one sink and vanity (with the wall-mounted hairdryer) is outside the door with another sink and a large counter space is in the bathroom itself. That makes it convenient for two people to brush their teeth at once. Wasn't crazy about having to hold down the button of the hairdryer to make it work, but maybe it was just that particular dryer.
The front office staff is young, helpful and courteous. They were always smiling and welcoming when we returned from our trips to the campus. We liked the big bowl of candy on the counter, too!
There is a small laundry room on the lobby level, and the use of the stacked washer and dryer is free for guests! Bring your own laundry detergent and fabric softener. Guests have use of the PC and printer near the front desk - also free. It's great for printing boarding passes or maps/directions to places.

title: “Great location and hotel - awful noise!”
text: We stayed at the Hilton Fisherman's Wharf for four nights at the beginning of August. We received a warm welcome from the reception staff, who were very friendly and helpful. The parking valet was also very happy to help. The elevators are a little old and slow and worried my claustrophobic girlfriend. We stayed on the second floor in room 207, which was a twin as opposed to the King that we requested. This didn't bother us and we were too tired to fuss. The room was clean and well-appointed. There was an excellent range of toiletries in the bathroom. That night, we realised that the window backed onto the main road and suffered from a broken clasp - thus, around 90% of the outside street noise was allowed into the room, making it VERY difficult to sleep. In the end, we resorted to ear-plugs. The location of the hotel is fantastic, being sufficiently set back from Fisherman's Wharf to avoid the crowds. It is around a ten minute walk to Pier 39. One day we walked from Union Square and it probably took us about an hour, stopping en-route to see Lombard Street etc. We returned to the room one day to discover that the maid had left our door open; however, luckily nothing had been taken. I intended to complain but had completely forgotten by the time we checked out. I would definately stay at the Hilton Fisherman's Wharf again, but I would certainly not stay in Room 207. Go for one around the corner opposite the lifts (starting at room 220 I believe).

title: “Great Value, Clean and Nice Staff”
text: We stayed here this past Friday night after desperately searching for a reasonably priced room close to downtown. This one had the best reviews on TripAdvisor so we took the chance. It's true, the location is odd, but it didn't inconvenience us in any way. 2 minute drive to Old Town restaurants. Rooms are big and clean, pool is large, well kept and sunny. Breakfast is simple but nice bonus. Free internet access in lobby was great too. Would definitely stay here again. Liked this better than Westin Horton Plaza which as 3 times as expensive and a lot less clean.

title: “Couldn't have asked for a better place to stay!”
text: This hotel is located on the lower east side, one block from a subway and within $15 cab ride to most of the attractions. We would definitely recommend this hotel and will likely stay there in the future. Balconies are not for anyone afraid of heights! They are very narrow and small. Unless your a smoker, wouldn't invest the extra money for a balcony. The tub was beautiful however we were so busy and on the go, we didn't get to enjoy it. So if you are going on a short trip and a nonsmoker, probably just a room without the balcony and tub would be sufficient. Request the highest room they have available, a corner room if possible facing north.

title: “Great downtown location - Don't bid on it though”
text:
I ended up at this hotel by bidding $150 per night for a 4 star hotel in the loop area of Chicago on priceline.com. The average room in the area was $250, so I did pretty good. I enjoyed the location, right next to th "L" and plenty of restaraunts and theatre within walking distance. 
We ended up with room 401, all the way in the back of the hotel with no view except the roof over their eeting rooms. I guess that's what I get for bidding on a room. As hindsight, I wish I had just booked a room at the hotel with a view and paid whatever their rate was. It was a clean hotel with very friendly and helpful staff. Parking was expensive, but probaly less than most downtown hotels.
I would stay there again and pay full price, the only reason I marked the room down was because of the room I got, not their fault, mine for bidding!
Recommendation - It would have been nice to have in-room coffee maker.

title: “There is no need to ever leave this hotel--spa, Elway's Restaurant and 50,000 square feet of gym makes it complete..”
text: This is the loveliest and best run Ritz-Carlton I have ever stayed in. I was told it was 100% occupied when my husband and I were there, but we never felt crowded nor waited for a service. The beds were amazingly comfortable, the bathrooms luxurious and spacious, and when you pushed a button for the elevator it arrived within seconds. The spa was beautiful, and the massage I had was the best of many I have experienced all over the US. Elway's has its entrance off the main lobby and serves food that was spectacular in a city already filled with fabulous restaurants. Denver is a wonderful place to visit, and my stay at the Ritz-Carlton transformed a great trip into a truly memorable one.

title: “Impeccable hotel”
text: Any time I return to San Francisco, I plan to stay again at the Chancellor. It's classy without being snooty, everyone who works there acts like they like actually enjoy their jobs. The rooms are clean and simple with comfortable beds and nice amenities--the free wireless internet access is a definite plus! Perfect location in Union Square. The only reason I would hesitate to recommend the Chancellor is because I don't want the competition! A truly great and affordable place to stay in San Francisco. Highest recommendation.

title: “would definately stay there again!”
text:
We had the priviledge of staying at the Hilton Garden Inn on 03/12/05
with our family. We stayed in the 2 bedroom suite. We were greeted by Tony who was very helpful and courteous! He helped my daughter find a secure place in the hotel for her concert grand harp and provided us with excellent driving instructions. Upon check out William was very helpful and let our children stay in the room an extra hour while I was tied up in a meeting. The breakfast that came with the room was a buffet and was good. The hotel was located right downtown in the circle center. We would definately stay there again and look forward to the next visit.

title: “This was a nice hotel with a fantastic...”
text: This was a nice hotel with a fantastic location next to the convention center. The only disappointment was that they charged for using the computers in their business center. They also charged .59 or .69 cents per print! For the price of the hotel room, I expected these services to be complimentary. I was very disappointed by these ancillary charges. Otherwise, it was a nice stay.

title: “No room at the Inn”
text:
We had just arrived at the Parc 55 after a tour of California taking in Monterey, Santa Barbara, Sequioa, Kings Canyon and Yosemite. We had no trouble with hotels, everything going smoothly. Hotels had been booked using Travel Republic and paid for months in advance.
Imagine our consternation when at registration we presented our hotel vouchers only to be told that we had no booking and there was a massive convention - i.e. no rooms. We've been here before in Denver several years ago and ended up 2 couples sharing a room.
However to the rescue came Sarah the registration clerk. Since we had proof we that we had in fact of a booking, she pulled out all stops and after half an hour wrangling with Parc central registration she got us 2 rooms. Thanks very much Sarah you rescued our 3 days in San Francisco. It seems Travel Republic agents Gullivers had not actually secured a booking even though they issued the hotel vouchers. It seems to be normal practice for us to pay up front and agents to book only a few days prior (thereby sitting on our money), and sometimes this backfires - it pays to check.
However after this problem had been resolved the Parc 55 was an excellent hotel perfectly situated near Union Square and only a short distance from the BART which made it simple to get to the Airport.
San Francisco is great with so much to do. One highlight that you can do cheaply is to take the ferry to Sausalito (a picturesque seaside town situated across the bay) and then get the bus back over the Golden Gate bridge to mission street (round the corner from Parc 55).
We found excellent brew pubs - 21st Amendment and Rogue Ales - the meal in the 21st Ammendment was excellent.
We visited the usual suspects e.g Fisherman's Wharf, from where we walked down Columbus Street to Union Square. A longish walk but i recommend it - it takes you off the beaten track passing Coit Tower and Washington Square where you can stop for a beer at Rogue Ales.
All in all Parc 55 was a great choice and an excellent hotel, only problem, as with city hotels, is you don't get anything free - $4.50 for water in the room and $14.99 for 24 hour wifi. All the hotels at other destinations gave free wifi - we overcame this by taking our ipad to Starbucks.

title: “Great Holiday Weekend!”
text:
We love, love, love the Kimpton chain of hotels, and had been dying to stay here. Finally got a great deal over the President's Holiday weekend, go figure..
Drove up to SF from Santa Cruz, short 1.5 hour drive and there we were. Breakfast and Irish Coffee at the Buena Vista, located right behind the hotel.
Room was really big, two queens, faced the little courtyard. Didn't ask and/or pay for bay view, didn't get it. But did get comfy beds, Raid the Mini Bar coupon, fridge for our champagne from home, we were set.
5pm wine time is great, really crowded, but this was a 3 day weekend. Lots of kids at "happy hour" which I found a bit much as they took up all the chairs (that is the parents problem, now isn't it). This hotel offered wine and hot toddies, yum!
Again, great room, with great shower amenities as usual, per Kimpton. We always love the bathrobes for use during our stay. Hubby always puts his on and says "Rarr"...stupid thing we do..
Great location on Fisherman's Wharf, adjacent to the Hyde Street cablecar start. Walking to Pier 39, Hyde Street Pier. Not a lot of food choices, but do your homework and you can get some good Italian food on the waterfront.
Had some crab chowder at the attached restaurant Blue Mermaind Chowder House. Was good. Expensive drinks, but that is ok if you have one.
Again, we are huge fans of the Kimpton chain and the Argonaut did not disappoint.
Tip: per the valet, if you do not plan on going in and out of garage, you can park in the lot behind hotel cheaper than hotel valet parking.

title: “Mistake”
text:
Booked this room last minute, thinking it was another Super 8 that I had stayed at before. Just needed a room for a few hours before an early morning flight. Arrived at Midnight to find this was NOT the Super 8 I had stayed at before on several occasions.
This was the smallest hotel room I have ever stayed in. Bed was uncomfortable and old. Bathroom was filthy. There was hair in the tub still from the last visitor. I simply fell into the bed to sleep for about 4 hours before my flight. In the morning I discovered that the toilet was clogged.
$50 for a room is usually a good deal. Not for this. I have stayed at other Super 8's, including the other one near the DFW airport, which was very new and clean and not much more than $60 from what I recall.
If not for the price and the friendly front desk, this would have been a Terrible rating.

title: “Repeat horrid stays here. No more”
text:
Came here three times now with my fiance for business trips nearby. Horrible staff overall, with few exceptions. Rusty dishes provided in these studio apartments, as if you would eat on them or with them.
You must repeatedly beg for basics like soap, do not disturb door signs..towels..
Now it has been three visits where DAILY, the staff mysteriously put down in the computer system that we are "checking out early". ??
Keep in mind, this means the keys no longer work in the door each time, the maids help themselves to the room, barging in to clean what they have AGAIN mistakenly been told is an empty room!!
 I can understand an error of this kind once..even twice. But every single time we are here and on each day? Where does it end?
For us, it ends today. No longer staying here and wasting money on being abused over and over again. Management claims to have resolved the horrid issues when you finally have enough and complain. No such thing has happened. It has and will continue.
Front desk Rep Alissa rudely argues with you, trying to convince you with a nasty tone that her COMPUTER says your dead key works, before reuctantly giving you YET ANOTHER DEAD DOOR KEY/CARD you discover once you've again gone back to your third floor room. Absolutely horrible service!!!
Maintainance Engineer Tim makes sincere efforts to provide new keys and with a smile and apology on behalf of the others, particularly Alissa who is blatantly nasty in his presence. ( he is not her boss, so she apparently doesnt bother to hide her unprofesionalism from even him) He tries. He cannot make up for repeat visits of abusive treatment, cigarette butts piled HUGE and sprawled BROADLY as a repeat smelly eyesore outside of every entryway outside, rusty and filthy dishes in the cabinets...It is a real shame. Never again.
Good bye Residence Inn on Deerpark. Enough is enough.

title: “Chili Peppers in San Antonio”
text:
We decided to go to see the Chili Peppers in San Antonio and needed a hotel. We chose The Westin Riverwalk and what a GREAT choice. The Director of Rooms, Jami Champagne, is amazing. She pointed us in all of the right directions.
We had a GREAT weekend…the hotel was excellent, dinner at Biga was amazing and breakfast in bed (pancakes and french toast with mimosas) rocked. 
Thank you for the excellent customer service and for the great stay. We will definitely stay with you on our next trip to SA.

title: “Newish affordable north Phoenix Hotel with free perks”
text: Free is their motto: breakfast, internet, parking, popcorn + soda in lobby, happy hour food+drinks (not for the health conscious) New and modern with small fridge in room. Shopping ctr. nearby with movie theater, P.F. Chang and TJ Max. North of 101 loop with 25 minute drive to central Phoenix or Scottsdale.

title: “Hotel Nikko”
text: The hotel was beautiful. I stayed for business for 3 nights and 4 days. The rooms were well appointed and the bathroom was very nice. The rooms were cold and it took forever for it to warm up even with the thermostat at 75 degrees. I didn't get a chance to try out the restaurant but the room-service was good. The bar had seasonal drinks and provided us with a good place to chat and hash-out strategies in a lively environment. I would certainly stay here again.

title: “Excellent service”
text: I recently stayed at the Quality Inn Central Denver (three times over the space of one month) and I found this hotel to be excellent in all respects. The staff were outstanding and really could not have done more for us, the shuttle bus and it's drivers were great, really freindly and very helpful, the breakfast was really great. You are aout 10 minutes drive from Downtown Denver, but this means it a bit quieter here and you have the facility of the Shuttle bus which runs on the hour every hour between about 8am and 11pm. Although we didn't eat in the restaurant in the evening, the food that was coming out of the kitchen looked great. I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a great hotel at a great rate!!

title: “Excellent hotel and a good value”
text:
The staff at this hotel is remarkably good. Everyone knows their job and when they promise something it gets done. Everyone is very friendly and efficient. The bartender at the Atwood makes a terrific martini - which is a lot more rare than it should be.
Rooms are very nice - comfortable, clean and attractive. Smaller than some but certainly not cramped. Beds very comfortable and the AC system very quiet - a huge plus for me. Cool that you get an actual room key - not a plastic card.
The building is very cool and the recent upgrade did not destroy the charm. Location is very convenient to public transportation and within walking distance of most attractions. Loved the complimentary wine and beer each night.
I can't think of reason to stay anywhere else in Chicago.

title: “Great Hotel, Good location, Good price”
text:
Visited in July '04
First: the location. It is not IN downtown, but rather about 5 blocks from Downtown and about 5 blocks from the Space Needle. We didn't rent a car, so we walked everywhere, something I enjoyed doing. The area seemed safe, although deserted, and this was the only tall building within a 5-block radius. A police station was nearby, so I would assume that the area is more or less safe. One definite minus: no decent restaurants around the hotel (within the 5-block area). 
The hotel itself may look unappealing on the outside at first sight, but, in fact, it has a very nice mural of some whales, which makes it look that much nicer. Inside, the lobby was clean, although not very spacious. The hotel has a exercising room, a Jacuzzi and a small sauna room.
The elevators seem a bit out of date, but they work, and that's all that matters.
Check in: VERY smooth, no problems whatsoever. 
Room: Clean, comfy, spacious. One problem (not their fault) we needed two double beds, they didn't have that type of room when I made the reservation, so we opted for a room with a bed and a sofa sleeper. The bed seemed to be good, the sofa sleeper was not so good. Nevertheless, everything else about the room was good.
One minor point: the light switches for the bathroom control both the bathroom and the sink area and are located outside the bathroom! (Some engineer needs a reality check!) But that was not a big problem.
Their self-serve expanded continental breakfast was better than I expected. They had fruit, pastries, oatmeal, cereal, fresh-baked waffles (you make 'em yourself), and more! 
Checkout: Also, no problems!
The staff: SUPER FRIENDLY! This is the first time I've seen staff this friendly! Truly exceptional! In most hotels that I've stayed in the past, the staff would put on their usual smile and greet you with that. The guys and ladies at this hotel were REALLY TRULY smiling and were genuinely interested in making your stay the best it can be! Two thumbs up!
Overall, I was very satisfied with service, price, etc! The location's not the best, but I was very happy for what I got!

title: “Above & beyond our expectations!!”
text: Had a ladies getaway weekend and it turned out fabulous!! Hotel was extremely clean & the staff was so friendly and personable!! Centrally located so we just walked around for 3 days enjoying all that San Antonio had to offer!! Will definately be staying here on our return trip!! Thanks for everything!!

title: “Really Know How to Treat their Guests!”
text:
My husband and I have stayed at this Doubletree numerous times and always have a wonderful experience. Everyone you come in contact with greets you with a smile. The hotel is always clean, beds are very comfortable, and of course, the warm, chocolate chip cookies at check in are delicious! Only thing that would make it better would be to offer a lighter weight bedding. While I love down comforters, they are just too warm in a hotel room.
In addition to the usual eggs, potatoes and bacon, the breakfast buffet always has plenty of fresh fruit, yogurt, oatmeal, and various breads, muffins and bagels.
Good wireless internet in the rooms.
Walking distance to Chili's and Red Robin.

title: “Swanky and close to everything!!”
text:
I adore this hotel! I've stayed twice and plan to return. The valet was prompt and courteous when we pulled in. The front desk was extremely friendly and greeted us with a warm cookie... mmmm. The lobby and bar area are so ritzy and posh looking. For the price of this hotel, I really didn't expect that! The room was very clean and the beds are super comfy. Before dinner, we had cocktails in the bar. Very good drinks and friendly bartender. 
It's so close to the Hobby Center and downtown has such a variety of things to do for nightlife. The shuttle was really convenient and quick. All in all... this is the best hotel in the area and it's a steal at their prices!

title: “Very Nice Hotel - No Complaints”
text:
We actually made a last minute decision to spend a saturday night in downtown chicago. I went on Priceline.com and bid on a 3 star property for $90.00 and we got a room at this hotel. The normal rate is $250.00 a night so I felt like we got a great deal. I couldn't have gotten a better value anywhere else.
This is actually a very nice hotel right in the heart of the city. We were close to all kinds of shopping, resteraunts, and bars. The hotel lobby is beautiful with a large glass atrium. The staff was friendly and efficient. Are room was a very nice one bedroom suite with a nice view of the city. I would highly recommend this hotel for someone in the city for the weekend. The "suites" include a seperate sitting area with a couch and t.v. This would be a perfect set up for a family vacation. I felt that this was one of the nicer Embassy Suites I have ever stayed in. The room includes a free breakfast buffet, which was comparable to any resteraunt.
This is really a great property and I would not hesitate to stay here again. At the end of the day since we only paid $90.00 a night this is probably the best value I have ever found. The normal rate of $250 a night would seem a little steep, but if you can get a reduced rate online I would definitely recommend this property.

title: “Wonderful Stay”
text: My husband and I stayed here to celebrate our anniversary. Everything was perfect from the moment we pulled up to valet the car. All staff were very friendly and helpful. While checking in they asked what brought us to the area and I told them it was our anniversary. The staff remembered us and many wished us a happy anniversary as we passed through the lobby on our way to dinner. The rooms are large and very comfortable with beautiful finishes and decor. Plenty of room for two to get ready in the bathroom. The jetted tub and large shower were so nice. We visited the rooftop pool and hot tub for a few drinks at the pool side bar. It was wonderful. We returned to our room to find a bottle of champagne and some chocolate truffles from the front desk. What a sweet touch! The location is perfect for a nice walk on the river. We will definitely stay here again. Fee internet is also a nice touch and we had no difficulties with it at the pool or in our room.

title: “A good place to base your trip”
text: The hotel was good. Kinda small in places, (the elevator is NOT for the claustrophobic!!) but clean and comfortable. A bit outdated here and there, but honestly. If you're going to NYC and need someplace close to the action (this place is three blocks to a subway) that won't break the bank, try it out. We had a good time and didn't have a problem with the staff, the price, or the location.

title: “Fabulous and Solid”
text:
Fabulous and Solid
The Beacon Hotel is:
-Very nice
-Perfect location
-Live up to expectations
-clean and comfortable
-impeccable Service
- fabulous brunch on Sunday
-Courteous and helpful staff
We will be back. First time staying and cannot find any fault with this hotel. Hope everything stays the same next time we are in there.

title: “Perfect Place To Stay”
text: My friend,her daughter and myself stayed here for 3 nights and I would deffinately stay again. We requested an early check in, and was able to get in at 11am, the room had 2 rooms;one with a queen bed, the other with a full fold out coach and full bed. The staff was friendly and helpful and the rate can't be beat for NYC (our room was 250$ a night). There was a great deli next door with a fantastic food bar of freash and homeade entrees, and the hotel is about a half a block from TImes Square. Mind you the hotel is older and a bit worn but clean and safe. We all agreed we would stay there again.

title: “Great Place To Stay”
text: I was here for the NCAA Women's Final Four event and my only qualms about this hotel was that room was a bit tad small and my internet connection kept going out requiring me to constantly re-connect to the internet, other than that this hotel is great. I didn't have the money to eat (just too expensive) at the restaurant attached to the hotel, but it was great. The hotel's customer service was superb and if all businesses operated from the standard Teatro works from all businesses would be perfect. The shuttle (Tahoe Hybrid) was a nice touch and the driver dropped me off everywhere from the Aquarium to post office. The bed was great (as well the chocolate that came when room was cleaned), the shower was perfect and now I can say I stayed in an authentic 4-5 star hotel. This is at the top of the best hotels I've stayed in. I'm now kind of hooked on "boutique" hotels, which is much better than the run of the mill hotels. You can't go go wrong with Teatro.

title: “Recommended”
text: I recently moved after living in LA for 15 years and was back in town on business and needed a reasonably priced room near LAX. This hotel fit the bill. It is recently renovated and very clean. The style in the rooms is kind of retro and there are flat screen tvs, a nice bathroom, a good sized closet. Beds are comfortable and the free breakfast includes everything from eggs, waffles, and oatmeal to yogurt and fruit. Management is eager to please - even sent me a follow-up email. The only downside is that the rooms are a little small.

title: “excellent hotel”
text: This is a very nice hotel in upscale location, 10 mins on subway to downtown dc. Rooms are very stylish, large, with 2 tvs and the most comfy beds and linens. Breakfast included which was very good as well. Metro station underneath hotel, in shopping mall, easy to get around. Very safe neighbourhood with loehmans, lord taylor etc on doorstep as well as cinema and many restaurants. Staff kind and hardworking. Would have no hesitation recommending this hotel, great value for money in dc.

title: “What a Hidden Gem!”
text:
We love to stay at the Moorpark, and this visit was our third time there. Beautiful dark wooded decor, with a contemporary warm flair. Rooms are very spacious and the beds are the best! Service has always been amazing, with the exception of the curt woman who works in the breakfast room, who tends to be very condescending! The pool is amazing with the cute little cabanas, and the lobby fireplace is always burning!
Pros: Location, Decor, Rooms
Cons: Internet access (has never worked for us in any room we've stayed in)

title: “A really fabulous location!”
text:
This hotel really is in a fabulous location. We traveled to DC with our 11 year old son for a family vacation and it served us perfectly. 
1) Location: Great! A short block and a 1/2 from Air & Space. We walked to the Lincoln Memorial, White House, Capitol, Bureau of E & P, Mall museums and Natl. Archives. The Metro stop was very close but we never needed it. The neighborhood is mostly government buildings. It was quiet and felt safe. Really ideal for touring.
2) Room: Very clean and comfortable. Nothing extraordinary, but nice. No hot water issues or elevator problems as some others have reported. We did hear the train at night, but it was not a problem for us.
3) Food: Others were right when they said this is not an area with much for dining. Everything shuts down when the Mall and local offices close @ 5:30. There was a McD's and Quiznos and the hotel restaurant, but we tried to dine before we returned from touring. We breakfasted daily at the Starbucks in the hotel which is so handy!
4) Misc: Check-in and out was fast and easy. Parking was an exorbitant $25/day in the garage underground, but we expected that. We bought Old Town Trolley tix in the gift shop and picked up the tour easily at Air & Space. This was really convenient and a great intro to the city. 
All in all, we were very pleased and would return. Yes, it is overpriced, but the location is so good, especially if you have kids, that we couldn't complain.

title: “Best in San Diego”
text: I don't know what is wrong with the people who posted negative reviews.. My fiancee and I stayed at the W last weekend and it was great!! The concierce was great, the room was great and the food was great.. I don't know what the regular rooms are like but anyone who has stayed at a W knows that you should always get a Kool Korner King. The room was spotless..Huge bathroom and a great bed.. It is very close to the Gaslamp and all of the major attractions. They also have a complimentary town car service that is available to hotel guests for use in the downtown area. Yes it is expensive, but you get what you pay for. The lobby "living room" is a great place to hang out and have a drink after a long day of walking around.

title: “Affordable haven for families and smokers”
text:
Aesthetically, the Beresford Arms leaves much to br desired, especially once you get past the lobby. The furniture and amenities in the rooms are outdated, appointments are cheap and unattractive. The location of the hotel is good, except that being next door to a hostel means excessive late night noise.
The real reason to stay here is for the space. Rooms are large, and those with kitchens are convenient and make itnpossiblemto save money on food.
We stayed in a first floor room with a window that opened on an ugly light well infested with pigeons and littered with trash. Noise from workers in the hallways woke us each morning.
Staff are friendly and accommodating, and the hotel is near a number of affordable restaurants and convenience stores. The bus to the Mission stops right outside the door.
In conclusion, this place scores well for convenience and price, but completely lacks charm. People who need the apartment hotel setup and have minimal expectations in terms of amenities should consider staying here.

title: “Worst Marriott I have ever stayed in. The nicest part of this hotel is the lobby.”
text:
This will be my last stay in a Marriott. The service was terrible and it started on arrival with the valet. My wife and I are not picky customers and this is the first time I have ever written a review. For the second time this month, we received a room with two double beds vice the king bed we reserved. I even called to confirm that we had a king room reserved. The front desk clerk told me "you should have checked in earlier". (We checked in at 8pm) The first incidence of this was in Boston at the Marriott Copley Place, the second, at the Wardman Park.
There is no place to get anything to drink in the hotel after midnight. We woke up thirsty at 1am and were surprised to find no bottled water in the room and our in room refrigerator broken. The AC was also broken. After a long walk to the lobby, the clerk seemed bewildered when I asked if there was anywhere in the hotel that we can buy bottled water. When the answer was no, I asked if they could give me change for a twenty dollar bill, to which the answer was "no". Hmmm.
The mattress was the type you typically find in a Residence Inn. There were no blankets on the bed other than the sheet and what is typically under a comforter. This turned out to be fine because it was hot in the room and the AC sounded like a Hemi and blew hot air.
Never again!

title: “Fabulous!”
text: I will definitely be booking all of my overnights at this hotel. Absolutely loved my stay! No pool or restaurant, but with all of the walking in the city and cafes nearby there is no need for these ammenities.

title: “Only thing good about this place is the location!”
text:
I stayed here for one night with wife and kid. The major point for picking this hotel was its proximity to Union Square. I paid $169 (before tax) for Premier King with parking package. Just about the only thing I liked about this hotel is the location. The room itself is average at best. The Premier rooms are pretty big compare to other hotels and you also get free wifi. The service is non-existent. I called housekeeping for more pillows and they never came.
I probably will not stay at this place again.

title: “Smallest room ever! Good price though on Hotwire”
text: Room made me claustrophobic as it basically was a queen bed surrounded by 4 walls. There was a little desk by the door with a small flat screen TV. The room was old concrete with a piece of modern art above the bed. We got the room gambling off of hotwire.com for $59 so I can't complain too much. Great location in Union Square. Roughly $25 for overnight parking and you have to call 30 minutes ahead to get your car.

title: “Worked for 4 adults and a 2 year old!”
text: We've just got back from our 3rd weekend trip to San Antonio, staying this time for one night in the Homewood Suites. I booked a double double online for $135 and everything was fine. The room was pretty big with the 2 beds in one, and a living area, kitchen and TV behind a bed on the other. The sofa in the living area pulled out into another double so our party of 4 adults and a toddler were more than adequately provided for. We were next to the lifts in the 6th floor but heard nothing. There was no double glazing on the room windows but the bedroom was at the far end so we heard no street noise either. I saw on Trip Advisor that people complained about the valet parking but the price is for the night, not for the day. So we turned up on the Saturday morning, valet parked, deposited our bags with the concierge, spent the day in SA, checked in about 5pm. On Sunday we checked out, left the bags with concierge and picked up our car late afternoon. For $16, thats not bad!! The free breakfast is buffet style and was plentiful - all 5 of us ate well. You can access the riverwalk from the hotel (at the quieter end) which means it is centrally located and easily accessible to all the sights like the Alamo, Riverwalk, La Villita and Hemisfair park. Really enjoyed our stay - will use this hotel again everytime we visit SA.

title: “Well above average but not excellent”
text: Excellent location. Clean modern rooms. Excellent breakfasts. Very helpful staff. One consistently unsmiling, unhelpful person on reception prevented an excellent review.

title: “Quick weekend in San Antonio on the Riverwalk”
text:
My husband and I decided to go to SA on the riverwalk for just one night. We stayed at the new (under a year old) Embassy Suites Riverwalk. We arrived early...about 12:30pm and knew our room wouldn't be ready. The valet drivers suggested we leave our luggage in the car since their valet luggage closet was full. We were happy to do that. The front desk clerks were kind and informed us that our room wasn't ready, but we came to enjoy the riverwalk, so we went and found a place to eat and watch the 2nd half of the Texas A&M game (which they won!! whoop!). 
We went back about 3:00 and were told everything was ready. After getting our luggage, we went to the room. WOW...it was awesome! We were so impressed! We vacation in Mexico on the Riviera Maya every summer and have always had beautiful rooms at any of the resorts we have visited. The Embassy Suites had the same exact feel. Everything was top notch! The bathroom was gorgeous. The living room was very comfortable and bedroom was perfect. The bed was so comfortable! Each room had a nice flat screen tv and the kitchenette had a nice fridge and micro. The seating area was a good space for 4 people if need be.
Our room was a corner room so we had 2 big sliding windows. One looked out on Houston Street, the other had a peek a boo view of the river. We had a balcony that we could sit out on if we had chosen. There was a wedding being prepared for and performed just one or 2 floors below on the rooftop area. We could have watched the whole thing, except we left for happy hour and more riverwalk excitement.
The weather was just perfect for a nice stroll along the water. It was a wonderful weekend and I am so thrilled we chose to stay at the ES on the Riverwalk!

title: “Good hotel with great location”
text: It's a good hotel with very standard Marriott services, room amendeties are little dated, it's not dirty as some other reviewed. Hotel is very big as it's part of the GM building. The restaurant on the 72nd floor is amazing. Hotel is very convenient, has food court on the bottom level, Starbucks and the GM show room on the 2nd floor, CVS and the People Mover access on 3rd floor. Walking distance to Greek Town, COBO center, Joe J Stadium. Make sure to request for river view room, it's worth it!

title: “Wonderful Hotel”
text: This was my first time staying at this property and it was wonderful. Next time I shop downtown Chicago, I will try to stay at this hotel. Great location, beautiful rooms, and the lounge was a lot of fun. The only thing I would change is the amount of staff on at the front desk for a Sunday check-out. There were only two individuals checking people out and the line was almost to the enterance of the property. I would have used the in-room check out screen via the television, but it was not working.

title: “Hell's Kitchen gem”
text: We spend a night at Ink48 as a late anniversary celebration. Our room was magnificent (we did get an upgrade) on the 14th (really 13th) floor, overlooking the Hudson. The room was furnished in the typical quirky Kimpton style, but the sofa and chairs were quite comfortable and the platform bed was heaven. The enormous bathroom (seriously larger than some Manhattan hotel rooms) had a great soaking tub, a multi-head shower and nice amenities. The Hell's Kitchen location is fairly convenient (Manhattan is an easy walking city)located within easy walking distance of some great restaurants. Staff were helpful and of course wine hour and the morning coffee service are nice perks. I think this is my favorite of the NYC Kimpton properties.

title: “Needs alot more improvement”
text:
We just had a 3 night stay at the Blake, that we renamed, but cannot post the rename on a public forum. I will say that the young staff has allot to deal with. They seem to have spent our 3 days there, apologizing for the condition of the hotel. Shame on the corporation that owns this hotel, your staff is its only shinning star. (I am not an employee of this hotel)
Our 1st of many complaints was that our room had no A/C & the room smelled. We were switched to another room, same funky smell. It seemed only one elevator was actually working. I timed a few trips. No kidding, 5 minutes wait for an elevator. Every time we used our room key, they did not work. We had to wait for the elevator to go down AND back up, 7 different occasions. Our house keeper accidentally picked up some of our personal hygiene items with the towel laundry. Our room was never really cleaned, trash emptied or room dusted.
 On our last morning, we did not have hot water for showers.
The room decor is brown? 
The upside, the pool & cabanas are quite nice. Good location. Great view.

title: “Solid Hotel and Good Location”
text:
Stayed at the Park South Hotel in Mid-September and found this to be good value hotel with a very convenient location. 
The free breakfast was a big bonus and was great quality too. The hotel decor was smart and contemporary and proved a relaxing place to stay for our vacation. Value for money was excellent and I would certainly recommend a stay here. There is an underground station two minutes walk from the hotel which gave great access to the city. There are plenty of bars and restaurants close by and the hotel is close to the Chrysler Building, Empire State, Grand Central and Macys. 
On the downside, we found housekeeping somewhat lazy and the room was not always as clean as it could have been and storage is very limited. Be prepared to live out of your suitcase if you are here for more than a few days.
Tip: Book a twin double room as we did for the same price as a standard double, you get much more floorspace in your room.
Well worth a look at.

title: “Average hotel - good value for the price”
text: Stayed here over 4th of july weekend, room was clean and very spacious, good value for the price, i would stay here again for my next trip to california. the room had a large bathroom and a fridge.

title: “Great place to stay”
text: Recently stayed 3 nights at this hotel. What a perfect location to be at in New York City. Just south of Central Park and close to just about everything. Hotel was clean, rooms were clean, neat and beds were very comfortable. Maid service was excellant. Our rooms were ready when we arrived at approx. 8:45am. Staff were very friendly and professional. Elevators to the floors were quick. Would definately stay there again and again.

title: “Good, peaceful base with great location for a Hollywood tourist visit.”
text: We slept well (4th floor on the back) and loved the food at the diner in the basement. Very clean and large room, Smelled and looked much better than expectations for the price, given the going rates in Hollywood. Friendly, and they let us check in early. Wifi free but slow.

title: “Provide recycling bins and this hotel would be absolutely perfect”
text: My son, daughter and I stayed four nights over the school spring break to explore LA and tour a couple of area colleges. We arrived late night and the drive to the hotel was daunting! Wow. LA driving is intense! The drive from LAX to the hotel seemed "hit or miss"; barred windows, street signs heavily laden with graffiti, definitely a strange vibe. When we arrived at the hotel, however, we couldn't have been more pleased. Everyone, and I mean everyone at the Holiday Inn Express was friendly and welcoming. The valet staff (if you choose this option as opposed to self-park), the front desk, housekeeping; everyone had a smile and a genuine interest in making sure we were comfortable. We could not have been more delighted. Rooms were spacious (two queen beds), very clean, and didn't have that "layer of way too many travelers been here" film that so many hotels seem to have. Our view wasn't much, but we weren't here to take in the view from our hotel room. A very short walk to Graumann's Theatre, the Kodak Theatre, El Capitan, California Pizza Kitchen (CPK), and more. Blocks from In 'N Out Burger and Mel's. Can see the "Hollywood" sign from the mall balcony near CPK. Excellent access to 101 for a quick trip to Universal Studios and/or Warner Brothers. There's a 24 hour market and a 24 hour Subway directly across the street. The hotel also offers beverages and microwave meals in their "concession" area in the front lobby. The complimentary breakfast buffet was quite nice and the sweet lady who manages the buffet takes obvious pride in her work. All in all, a wonderful, affordable experience. Wouldn't hesitate to stay here again.

title: “Trendy Elegance with a touch of Weirdness in Midtown NYC”
text:
This is a strange hotel in the middle of New York City, on a popular street pretty close to everything. I say it is weird because it is a very narrow building and is not marked outside, so you can walk right past it if you are looking at the other hotels across the street. The ancient Algonquin, City Club and Iriquois Hotels are all in the same area.
My Priceline rate was $100 a night, plus fees and taxes which brought the two night charges to $245.77. This is a really good price for this hotel in this location and I walked from the Bryant Park airport bus stop two blocks south. Between 5th and 6th Avenues at 44th street, the hotel is in a great spot.
The hotel is part of the little known Morgan Chain of properties which prides itself on the unusual, I think. I got the booking though Priceline and it is rated as 4 Stars, which I think it deserves, especially given the posted prices which are in the $500-700 a night category. Does the hotel measure up to others that demand these prices? Probably, but at these prices, it is great.
For anyone going to New York City for the first time, it is usually a shock to discover that the city and state nail visitors as much as 25% in taxes, fees and anything else they can think of to add on to a hotel bill, so it is always smart to consider this before you accept a quoted hotel charge without the fees and add-on costs.
My room was certainly elegant, but had a lousy view of nothing but nearby roomtops. The bath and amenities were superb and bedding, linens and lighting excellent. Large flat screen TV was great. The hotel sells everything (all kinds of stuff) in each room, from large contianers of the shampoo and body lotions to tee shirts, hats and "intimacy kits" in two versions. Refreshments, such as nuts, wines, etc. have the usual exorbitant markup. 
Staff at check-in and check out were great. Bell staff were helpful and freindly.
The lobby, with Bar 44 and a large lounge area, was very popular and busy both nights. This entire area, (lobby and ground floor facilities), is very dark and, while not depressing, reminds one more of a night club rather than hotel lobby. This is not a problem, but I do not think the hotel is a great place for families as it's too "up scale" or sophisticated to appeal to children.
