At this price, I would go back again, but at posted rates, it is not a hotel I would choose.

title: “Not much here”
text:
This hotel is very basic if that. The bed was all springs so very hard to sleep but is was quiet. I requested a wake up call at 6:00 am but never got a call and luckily since I could not sleep on the springy bed I was awake anyway. 
The location was good and right next to the bus to LaGuardia and the subway. I won't go back.

title: “Everything written in these reviews is true!”
text:
My wife and I stayed for three nights after a cruise to Alaska. I'm late in writing the review as we stayed at the beginning of August. We chose the Inn based on the reviews in Tripadvisor and we weren't disappointed at all. It was a fantastic room, perfect location for walking to Pike's Market or the Space Needle. Found a great breakfast spot 2 blocks away, C J's Eatery. Even the Cyclops across the street had great food and a fun spot to sit outside with a drink.
Love this hotel and would stay again without hesitation!

title: “Consistent with other reviews”
text: Our check in experience was sub-par, the staff are just not friendly at the front desk. Our room is nice, housekeeping staff was great, I asked for hypoallergenic pillows and extra conditioner, came back to my room and both requests were fulfilled. I agree with some other reviewers, the structure of the hotel itself is old. I wish they would play up the retro (or at least not new!) aspect of the hotel. I haven't seen anything in the hotel that acknowledges its age. Overall I think this hotel is comparable to other hotels in the area (everything is old), the pool/water park is entertaining. I don't not like this place I suppose (pardon the double negative).

title: “wonderful wonderful wonderful”
text: I have stayed in a lot of NYC hotels, paid more, and got a lot less. Great location near theatres and Times Sq, friendly staff, free breakfast, 24 hour coffee, big clean rooms, parking attached, free internet access. You can pay $300+ a night somewhere else or stay at the HI Manhattan and get it for less.

title: “A nice time in San Antonio”
text: The room (bedroom and sitting area) was very comfortable and clean, and there was a door to separate the two so I could watch TV while my husband slept. The bathroom was large and immaculate. I would have like a small refrigerator for leftovers and there was certainly room in the dressing area. The pool area was very nice, the chaises were very comfortable, too. Towels available, even late in the afternoon. The lobby was extremely comfortable to hang out in, and nicely decorated. Able to get some work done with a coffee or wine in the afternoon looking out at the beautiful river walk. The bed was a king and I slept great, even though the pillows were a little too hard for my taste. The hotel is situated on a nice quiet area of the river walk, but not far from all the activity if that's what you want. The air conditioning worked great, even though it was very hot outside. The staff was friendly and helpful, the little store well stocked with all the necessities we forgot to bring. Room service was speedy, and the BLT was good. My only 2 complaints (and no hotel is ever going to be perfect) is that the valet parking was extremely slow and very expensive ($30 a night, and it took an average of 30 minutes wait for our car, even after calling for it ahead of time -- the gentleman ahead of me waited nearly an hour.) This might keep me from staying there if I had places I had to be on time for (like a wedding, or dinner reservation, and this is why I rated the service as average) Also, the hotel doesn't have HBO, but they do offer free internet service. All in all, I really enjoyed my stay.

title: “Challenging to Find”
text:
We stayed with another couple for five nights last month. The hotel itself is nice and service good.
We had a rental car when we arrived and found the hotel address and the auto entry are two different locations. Access to the hotel is difficult. When we wanted to take a cab anywhere there were hardly any to be found. Had to use a local limo service instead as the location/access is not very conducive to getting a sufficient number of cabs to wait for guests. This is a nice hotel but the location is not great and I doubt I would ever stay there again.

title: “No air conditioning? Had to turn on the toilet? C'mon”
text: This Hilton was always a little shabby for the price, but you cant beat the location for a 6:30 am flight. This last trip, however, was pretty bad. The air conditioning does not work when the temp drops below 50F so I was told to 'open a window' to cool down the 78 degree room, but of course, the window won't open. On top of that, someone had turned off the plumbing to the toilet and the remote control didn't work. Great place.

title: “Convenient Conference-style hotel”
text:
The hotel is huge and impersonal, a bit outdated, but nice. The restaurants lack personality, but are adequate.
The room was super clean and spacious.
Staff were very helpful.
The free shuttle from the airport are all shared at LAX. The Hilton shares with one other hotel, it seems to come every 20 minutes but it's more often normally. There are more than one, but when I was waiting it took longer than 20 for some reason.
It's on a route for a $3 trolley to the beach and shopping, tickets at the conceirge, that is worth it. Great views of the beach and beach houses, really good shopping and a taste of LA life if you have an extra 3 hours to enjoy a restaurant and shop.
Overall I recommend it!

title: “Will never stay anywhere else in Manhattan!”
text:
The location is actually really nice for NYC--harbor views etc
The room and bathroom were clean and very large. The beds were
super comfortable.
There was no noise from the hallway or other rooms even though the hotel was
fully booked.
Got a good (for NY) weekend rate on the internet.
Can't say enough good things!

title: “Was very happy with my stay at the W”
text: I checked into the W early and no problems getting my room at 11 a.m. The check-in lady was very nice and it all went smoothly. My room was very comfortable. Great bed, nice bathroom and everything was clean and modern. The W tries (and succeeds) at making everything cool and they really are able to pull it off well. Before I had arrived, I was a little skeptical wondering if I was going into an 'IKEA' type of a place. Not at all! Had breakfast at Rice and again the service was great and the food was wonderful. Looked around at the pool and spa on the second floor and thought they were both beautiful. Took advantage of their complimentary Acura SUV service which gave me a ride to the Gas Lamp district where we had great Thai food at a restaurant called Rama. The concierge had arraned that! All in all, a definite good place and I'll be back.

title: “Too small”
text: Stayed here for a week on holiday. Room was far too small for two people with luggage. Might just be OK for one person. Shame as hotel was in a very convenient location but just not suitable for us. Be warned, there is a railway line very close to the hotel and, especially if your room faces the town, it is noisy all day and night - the hotel does provide earplugs!

title: “A Pleasant Stay”
text:
Stayed for one night on business and plan on going back next week. Not more then a mile from inner harbor, little italy, fells point and canton. The room was clean, I liked the working sleep number bed!
There was free internet which is a plus to me. The 2 staff members that I spoke to at the front desk where more then pleasant. With my great internet rate, I will be coming back again.
The hotel is charming with a little touch of a bygone era. 
OK, one bigggg complaint: whats with the parking....$31.00 a day, you have to be nuts but if you need in and out privledges, I don't see what else you can do..

title: “great place for a family”
text: When we travel with our daughter we try to choose Homewood Suites. While not in the middle of the action, this hotel met all of our needs. The extra bedroom has become a must when we travel as a family. If you are in Austin with your family, consider staying here.

title: “A little too pricey for the amenities offered”
text: The Guest service was outstanding and the valet parking very accommodating. The room was quite small and the sheets were too rough (no where near soft). No coffee maker or refrigerator was in the room. I did request a coffee maker and when I tried to make my coffee the next morning it was broken. No coffee for me! Apparently the dumpsters are emptied very early in the morning and that woke us up at the crack of dawn. I must say for the price I could have stayed several other places and been more comfortable.

title: “Easy to Love...”
text:
While this hotel may not be located right in all the hustle and bustle of Michigan Ave., that is actually a good thing. The location still has plenty to offer - Harry Carey's across the street and more restaurants and bar/clubs less than 1/2 block away. 
One of the major pluses is parking. There is a "green" parking garage attached and we received a discounted rate for being guests of the hotel; every little bit helps in Chicago! 
We stayed in a "studio suite" which is basically a standard room with a kitchenette. There are only three of us and this was plenty of room. But no division (which I was aware of when I booked) and when the sofa bed was out, manuvering around was tricky. And while this is not solely a problem of the Residence Inn; I wish hotels would realize that whoever sleeps on the sofabed actually needs a good night sleep too - my 11 yro daughter dreads anytime she has to sleep on one. (And no, she's not the Princess of the Pea fame). But I digress.
Breakfast is exceptionally busy but the wonderful lady who runs it (as of October 2011) is amazing! The weekday fare is better than the weekend with more variety and time for replenishing. But no matter what she greeted you like you lived there and tried to accomodate any way she could. 
Lastly, I felt the room was clean for the amount of traffic these rooms see. I would absolutely stay at the Inn again!

title: “Fantastic Staycation”
text: As locals, we're likely to be more skeptical of a place than a tourist but we found Andaz a great surprise. The staff was very friendly (what? a free glass of wine at check in? Free water and snacks in our room?!?) and even offered to text us when our room was ready. The hotel was hip enough to remind us of a New York hotel we recently visited. The hotel must rock the rooftop pool on the weekends since we were there on a Sun. night and the DJ had the uber chic 20 somethings entertained. Only thing preventing a 5 star is the fact that our room faced the street and I could see it being louder on a Sat. night.

title: “Nice Hotel”
text: Overall the hotel was nice. They were able to check us in early. It was a bit of a walk to Pike's Place but not too bad. I would stay here again n

title: “PERFECT Honeymoon stay!”
text:
My hubby and I stayed at the Radisson April 8-10 for a quick honeymoon getaway. Location was perfect right on Congress and more than easy walking distance from 6th street. Check-in was initially a bit rough, our room was not ready at 3pm (even though we did call twice that morning/afternoon) and finally at 4pm when we'd gotten angry from waiting my husband approached the front desk one more time and had to vent his frustration to get our room. The upside to this is they ended up upgrading our room to a nice lakeview suite (room 1162) and I will say it was a really nice room along with free valet for our 2 day stay. Very clean, nice flat screen tv, very powerful a/c, and the best part...no smoky smell!!! I can officially say though that I will never invest in a sleep number bed. I realise this is something Radisson boasts about having, but my husband and I can best compare it to a King sized air mattress that you can inflate and deflate, and thats exactly what it felt like. Plus somehow thru the night my husbands side adjusted by itself and ended up on the hardest setting. The only other glitch we experienced with the hotel itself was a toilet that kept running and when we called to report it, the front desk asked my husband if he had opened the tank and "jiggled the handle" in which my husband curtly replied "I'm not on vacation to fix your toilet, send maintenance". They showed up shortly after and fixed that issue. 
We did sit down at TGI Fridays during our wait time to check-in and ordered 2 margaritas (my fav) and the sampler appetizer. The food itself was great, very hot and fresh. The margaritas however were the worst I have EVER had! We ordered the berry rita and a mango rita and both tasted like someone had poured salt in the mix resulting in a taste that literally made you want to vomit. Now, there was salt on the rim (which is strange itself because in my experience when you order fruit ritas they typically line it with sugar) but the salt on the rim was def not enough for the awful taste in the mix. We sent them back and explained why we did so. Our waitress was apologetic and we ordered a few beers instead. So, food was good but at $8 a margarita, I wouldnt even attempt it again. 
Overall, we had a very nice stay. We ended up in a nice upgraded suite and valet that was always very prompt and efficient in retrieving our vehicle. I'm not sure that I would stay again though based on other reviews because I know if my room had the infamous "smoky old smell" I would not have enjoyed myself at all. So, if you can book room 1162 than go and enjoy your stay, if not than good luck!!

title: “I have no words”
text: I complained to the staff that I could not sleep at night because of the noise that going on outside. They did not do anything about it. I found that very rude but the hotel itself was very nice. Hope you get better staff.

title: “4 night stay,”
text:
Overall our experience was very good. Elissa arranged a change to a room that overlooked the river (rather than the parking lot). That being said, the bus noise is louder on this side, but the view is worth it. 
Michael Ruiz, chef, did a superb job in accommodating our needs for gluten free. A nice gentleman to talk to.
Thanks to our server, Raul and to Daniel, the restaurant supervisor. The dining experience is sincere and warm and lovely on the river.

title: “A bargain with drawbacks”
text: Got a terrific internet deal averaging $85.00 per night - a great deal for 2 queen beds and a kitchen. My daughter, who lives in the area, moved in with me for my stay (vacation from apt with roommates). Room furnishings, kitchen very dated but clean. Hotel is actually 2 buildings, one with restaurant, one with main desk & small room with computers for guest use. Restaurant breakfast brunch is poor and WAY overpriced. There are no restaurants or activities in immediate area, but if main purpose is to visit GWU or State Dept., it's ideal. Metro stop is a fair hike, especially if in dressy shoes.

title: “Just what we needed”
text: My boyfriend and I just got back from spending a week in New York. The Belnord was great: the area is nice with lots of restaurants and little shops, and close to 3 subway lines. The bathrooms were always clean and the rooms were tidied every day and beds changed. The room was small, but that is to be expected, especially for the price. Double bed was comfy and the response to our demand for a new blind for the window was very quick and efficient. All in all the Belnord is perfect for those wanting a comfortable but cheap place to stay in NYC. It is hardly more than a hostel in price but much nicer to stay in. We had a great time.

title: “sooo great!!”
text: we've been staying here for years. we love this place. great location. friendly staff. we've never done much cooking, just breakfast and the kitchen's great for that. bed's are comfy. only problem this last time was the early morning trucks and all the construction noise.

title: “Great Location”
text:
The hotel has an excellent location where you can walk everywhere apart from Graceland.
All the staff were friendly, helpful & polite at all times.
My only complaint is that all rooms have a full kitchen and someone had cooked the night before we arrived, which resulted in this very unpleasant smell for the 2 nights of our stay, even with the windows open & the cleaner trying her best to get rid of the smell it still persisted. It put my husband off booking that type of hotel again. Everything was very clean and the bed really comfy. McEwens restaurant next door was really nice for dinner.

title: “Soft beds little rest.”
text: The hotel as a whole is nice. It was not what I expected from a Wyndham Hotel, however it was clean except for the one pillow case that smelled like puke and urine. The hotel to its credit took care of it right away but it still sullied the experience. The beds were very comfortable and the suite was very roomy. The thing that I disliked the most was the noise. You could hear every little thing on all sides of the the walls. Upstairs, to your left and to your right and outside. The baby crying was in the room, and the guy using the toilet well you get the idea. So if you don't mind noise its a great hotel. One thing that was great was Du Par's restaurant right next door it was open 24/7 and the food was excellent as was the service. It made everything better when you got up and went to eat. And the prices were fair and the staff made you feel like you were the only one there. Oh and I don't know if there was a free breakfast because we did go to find out.

title: “Noisy”
text: Like many other Embassy Suites we had a great breakfast, friendly hotel staff, very nice common areas. The room we had was facing the airport. It sounded like the jets taking off right under our window! It was the noisiest room I have ever stayed in!

title: “Coolest Hotel”
text: My Aunt, cousin and I came to the Big City from Louisiana to do all the shopping we could. Friends had told us about the Indigo (without going into great detail so as not to spoil our surprise). We checked in and were absolutely amazed at how different it was but we still felt as if we were on a relaxing vacation. I loved the decor - thought it was very cool. That was enough to have enjoyed the hotel but we also experienced staff that always smiled and were very helpful to some southern girls. I've told everyone about our stay. Everyone going to Chicago for a visit or some shopping should get to stay. Thank you!

title: “Fantastic stay in a lovely hotel.”
text:
Booked the Belvedere after reading reviews and decided to book the executive King room which was at the back of the hotel on the 6th floor. Lovely room, small kitchenette which was great too and a lovely bathroom with sunken bath, shower was nice and powerful too. Staff were very friendly and efficient. Hotel is a short walk to all the action too.
Definitely recommend this place to anyone.

title: “Sofitel NY hotel during UN & Presidential chaos”
text:
Well-located, lovely hotel, beautiful lobby and public areas. The rooms are on the small size with queen beds, but very nice bathroom. W. 44th St is interesting, with many hotels, clubs and restaurants, and right in between 5th Avenue shopping and sightseeing, and 6th Avenue with more commercial and near the theatre district. The bar, lounge and restaurant (Gaby) is a french brasserie type and nice, food not great but good, with excellent wine selections. 
Hotel is also convenient to Grand Central Station, NY Public Library, and Rockefeller Center.

title: “Fabulous place to stay downtown”
text: This is a beautiful hotel right in the heart of downtown seattle. short walk to Pikes place market and a lot of hotels and shopping. The room was beautiful, the bed was very comfortable, the view was amazing, excellent blackout curtians. Many other reviews complained that it was run down and crowded. Although a very busy hotel we found it in excellent condition. every room has an amazing view we had a city view and enjoyed it so much. only possible improvements would be the showerhead was leaking and lacked some water pressure, the check in process took a very long time and the hallways smelled a bit like machine oil. I would not hesitate for a moment to book this hotel again.

title: “Good location....check in needs some work”
text:
I arrived at the Logan airport and decided to take a water taxi to the hotel. This is a great thing to do if you have some extra time to spare. The water taxi dock lets you out right in front of the backside of the hotel. Walked into the lobby after 3pm to find a line of about 15 people waiting to check in. First sign that check in would not be an easy process. When I finally get to the desk, I am told that the hotel has no rooms that are ready and they can't even give an estimate as to when my room will be ready. Check in time is 3pm at this hotel. I was told that there were a lot of late checkouts from the night before. The hotel was totally booked during our first night. You do not allow a lot of "late checkouts" when you have a full night. Front desk staff was not very apologetic about not having my room ready. After waiting an hour, I went back to the desk. This time, I was at least asked for my phone number so they could call me when the room was ready. This staff person also gave us 2 drink vouchers for our room not being ready. We went to the bar and had our free drinks. Close to 5pm, our room was finally ready. Once the room was ready, check in was a fairly simple process. The room was nice. We had a partial view of the harbour which was a plus. The room had a frosted glass sliding window type thing between the sleeping area and the bathroom. While this looked neat, it was very impractical. If someone went to the bathroom in the night and had to turn on a light, it illuminated the bed and woke up whoever was trying to sleep.
Location was great for the aquarium and for walking to the North End. T stop was not too far away. Fanueil Hall was also a close walk. Hotel is a little pricey to have the check in issues that we experienced.

title: “European feel”
text: My husband and I stayed for three nights in The Majestic, and were quite pleased. It is an historic building with charm. Our room on the top floor was small, but adequate, with a very comfortable bed. The hotel was sold recently, and the bar was closed, due to the lack of a liquor license. But breakfast in the lovely dining room was generous (fresh fruit, cereal, pastries, hard-cooked eggs, cheese, good coffee). There were free copies of newspapers (San Francisco and NYTimes) and classical music playing. The hotel is about 1 mile from Union Square (walkable for dinner) in a residential neighborhood. We were able to find street parking within 2 blocks of the hotel every night. I recommend this hotel, and would stay there again.

title: “Absolutely Perfect NYC Hotel!”
text:
My family stayed at the Andaz 5th Avenue in April and as a party of four adults, we wanted a luxurious, modern hotel in a great location. We'd spent ages researching hotel options for our stay in NYC and had kept a close eye on TripAdvisor reviews; we were pleased to see the positive things previous visitors had said about this hotel - and boy, it did not disappoint!!!
In advance of our trip, we had emailed the hotel’s Director of Rooms, Connie Wang mentioning that this was a special occasion and from the moment we set foot into the hotel, we knew we had made the right choice! Our rooms were upgraded - my parent’s had a Loft Suite and we had a Loft King. The rooms were absolutely fantastic! Having stayed in many 4/5* hotels previously, the rooms here were definitely a class above the rest! Upon arrival, our friendly host Joy seamlessly checked us in, and then escorted us to our rooms in the North Tower - which we later found to be extremely quiet. Both rooms were incredibly spacious (especially compared to rooms in some NYC hotels) and ultra modern, with very high ceilings, amazing bathrooms and a complimentary mini bar (non alcoholic beverages and snacks). My parent’s suite also had a separate lounge area with sofa and coffee table and second plasma TV. Connie had also arranged for some wine and fruit, as well as a card for my Mum’s Birthday which was another lovely touch!
The Andaz 5th Ave is in the most perfect location for exploring the great sights of NYC - right on 5th Avenue, opposite the NY Public Library and only a few minutes walk to so many great sights. Breakfast in ‘The Shop’, the Hotel’s restaurant was great and we also had dinner here one evening and you couldn’t fault the food – great choices and fantastic quality.
Of an evening, the hotel provides complimentary wine in ‘The Library’ lounge area (6-9pm); it was nice to have a glass of wine before heading out for the evening. Also, tea/coffee is available throughout the day here which was welcome when you didn’t fancy a full breakfast - although the area did get a little crowded at times. We had drinks and some tapas dishes in ‘The Bar Downstairs’ one evening, which was also very nice. The bar has very funky atmosphere and seemed to attract the local NY crowds as well as tourists/hotel guests.
The hotel is located 2 mins from Bryant Park, which is a lovely area to relax and rest your feet when walking around NYC! We dined one evening at the ‘Bryant Park Grill’ and the food was amazing! (recommend the Kumquat and Grand Marnier Duck with apple & gruyere crepe - delicious!).
Overall we couldn’t fault a thing with this hotel, the entire experience was perfect from start to finish. From the décor to the location, the service to the food - it was all great and our hotel choice really made our stay. A big thanks to Connie for making our stay in NYC extra special! Now that we’ve discovered this hotel we won’t be staying anywhere else in NYC in future…we’ll definitely be back!

title: “Five day break”
text: This hotel was in a perfect location for times square,theatres etc.The rooms were small but were clean and the maid service was very good.The down side was it is still under a lot of construction and the reception area was always very congested.The lifts were always going off.You felt as if you were living on a building sight.One of our rooms were to the back of the hotel looking onto a brick wall. There was an large fan running all night and the noise of it was terrible.Staff ok.Would we go back no.

title: “Different style of resort, very family friendly.”
text:
Paradise Point is a very different hotel or resort than any that I have been to. Our room was a duplex style, sharing a wall with only one other room. It had a king sized bed, small sitting area with loveseat and coffee table, and a bathroom with a door separating the vanity from the shower and toilet. Bed was comfortable, but pillows were lumpy. There was a small patio with two chairs in the back, which was sort of fun. There are five pools around the resort, with one pretty close to all rooms. One is an adult only pool. All have hot tubs. We were closest to the waterfall pool. I did have to scoop out some bugs from the hot tub before we used it, but I didn't take offense to that, just wished someone had used a pool skimmer to clean it beforehand. 
I booked our stay on priceline. In addition to the price I paid for one night, a $17 resort fee was charged per day. This allowed access to the free internet and recreational activities including tennis, bocce, and croquet--none of which we used. We hoped to get a bocce ball set to take to the beach, but were informed that they all had to be used in the recreational area only, which I guess is understandable, though not ideal. There is a putt putt course right on the grounds too, which had an additional charge (disappointing). 
We checked in behind another family, and were shocked to hear the price for parking. I think they charged them $32 per day or something. This is silly, because at least in the area our room was in, there was one parking spot marked for each room number. I was lucky she didn't charge us for it, which I'm guessing was only because we booked through priceline.
I wouldn't recommend this for a couples vacation necessarily, but would recommend it for a family getaway, given the recreational activities onsite and the relative isolation of each room compared to a highrise hotel.

title: “Family Fun !”
text: Having a toddler and two teenagers, the Squaw Peak Point Hilton kept us all busy...the water park was a great retreat. Although the hotel does show its age, it is clean and well maintained. The restaurant Rico was a bit of a disappointment service was very slow . But the hotel enjoys a great location and offers something for all ages.

title: “lovely service”
text: Stayed here Thursday, Feb. 23. Best price available at LAX; extremely nice people. I was given a room that was so recently rennovated that it still smelled of paint and all the fresh textiles which stimulated my alergies; the extremely kind manager was able to move me to a room which had not yet been rennovated but was none the less very nice and comfortable even very late at night and when the property was almost fully booked. Very good shuttle service in the a.m. to airport terminal. The dicey freeway situtation in LA makes it sensible to stay at the airport before an early morning flight and I will go back to this place.

title: “Room for Improvement”
text:
Definitely some highlights - location, decent sized and well equipped rooms which have generally been very well designed. The designer must have been a man who does not wear contact lenses though as the underlit bathroom makes both putting in lenses and putting on make up something of a challenge.
The free-flow of the lobby is unusual and would be even better if it worked. Sadly there were either too many staff (typically talking to each other), or too few (one one occasion I waited in an unstaffed lobby for five minutes with only the staff blackberry for company), and not many actually seemed to know what they were doing - apparently a bit of everything reasonably competently rather than a specific role very well.
The real low-point is the restaurant where this laissez-faire attitude among the staff is even more frustrating. The breakfast service is, for now, definitely worth avoiding. A pot of tea in a half empty room - 15 minutes if you are lucky - food (OK but nothing special) perhaps within 50 minutes of entering the restaurant. None of the staff appear to have any idea what they are doing and management and direction are conspicuous by their absence. Even if you are not paying; it is just not worth it
In summary, a new hotel which must undoubtedly get better

title: “Lovely, clean hotel in a great location!”
text: A beautiful hotel not too far from the airport. Roomy, clean, every room has a balcony.

title: “Great experience”
text: When I stayed at this hotel, I was surely pleased with all the services and extras offered. The staff was most pleasant and knowledgeable of the area and made great suggestions on how to make my say in Ft. Worth enjoyable. Who knew so many good restaurants were close by and tasty. The suite that I stayed in was newly renovated complete w/flat screen TV and the most confortable bed. I even inquired as to the type of bed it was. Anyway, thanks to all at Hotel Trinity for making my stay in Ft. Worth ejoyable without breaking the bank. I didn't mention the great rate, but very affordable for all of the extras and worth every pennie.

title: “Great location, Quality hotel”
text: Great location -- Nice, safe area and very close to Fisherman's Wharf and boarding for the double decker tour buses. It's not cheap but nothing decent is in San Francisco. We never even looked at the pool or spa so cannot comment on those things.

title: “Best option if you want to be on the UW campus”
text: We have stayed at The Deca many (8?) times in the past year, and we've also tried the other motel/hotel options around the UW campus. The Deca is the best option in the UW campus area. The rooms are quiet, and the windows open. There are decent views from the upper floors. Nothing fancy, and personally I'm not a fan of the "pedestal" antique sink style where you don't have any counter space, but with that minor "complaint", the rest is fine. After trying several spots in the area, The Deca is definitely the best for us when visiting our UW student. (Hey, if you're not going to the UW then why are you looking outside of Downtown Seattle in the first place!)

title: “Establishment was remarkable”
text: Hotel and room was clean and comfortable .the room stayed in was facing the courtyard and there was a wedding that night. The frontdesk informed me and gave me the option to a different location.but I was ok as I was not going to be back in the room that early. The rate I got was great for a location like this one.overall we has a great time and enjoyed our stay

title: “Great hotel, lots of character”
text: Stayed here in September while attending a convention. Since I hadn't booked it myself, I didn't bother to use tripadvisor to research it first. Which made it a nice surprise when we checked in, since the hotel was everything I usually look for. Lots of character (it used to be a jail), luxury (the bathrooms and beds were great), and unusual touches (the lobby becomes a bar, and they have special events for dogs, art shows, fashion shows, etc.). The location is also great, located across the bridge from Cambridge, near Beacon hill, and within easy walking distance of lots of historical attractions in downtown Boston. Price seemed steep - we got a special rate of $259 as part of the convention, but I've heard the regular rate is almost double that.

title: “All good, except the parking situation”
text:
I stayed at Hotel Indigo Dallas for one night with a couple of friends. We didn't spend much time at the hotel, but were mostly satisfied with our experience and the downtown location. Staff was friendly and helpful. Wireless internet was included in the rate, and our top-floor room had a nice view of the downtown area. Breakfast in the restaurant was okay, but nothing special.
My only complaint was with the parking situation. The garage is conveniently located next door. However, it is not staffed on weekends, and instead there is a machine that requires cash payment in order to allow a car to exit. Unfortunately, not everybody considers this ahead of time and brings cash with them. With only one exit lane, we had to wait ten minutes while the person two cars ahead of us searched for cash to pay the machine. I suggest installing a credit card reader to expedite the process of exiting the garage.
Other than the garage, the stay was fine, and I'd consider staying here again if in downtown Dallas.

title: “Great Place and Location”
text: Indianapolis is agreat town to visit, and the Marriott is centrally located for exploring the city. The hotel is very clean with fresh cut flowers in the lobby every day. The pool is not gigantic, but the kids seemed to enjoy it very much. Highly recommend this property to anyone.

title: “Not quite wowing”
text:
I booked a room at the W Chicago Lake shore for a girls Friday night out on the town. Since I work for another Starwood property, I get a hefty discount on rooms and the price was definetly a steal. We used the valet parking which was $41 a night with unlimited 24 hour re-entry. A little pricey, but better that trying to find a parking spot. Upon arrival, the check in was swift and easy and the staff was polite. The gal who checked us in put us on the 30th floor so that we would have a nice view of the city and was it ever; We had a great view of the John Hancock Building. The room was clean, there were two double Heavenly beds that were awesome as always, and a plasma TV to enjoy. The Bliss toiletries were amazing, but the bathroom was a bit strange. The door consisted of a wicker moving panel that slid over the entry-way opening. There was also a cutout in the wall with wooden shutters that closed to cover it. The bathroom was nicely decorated, but all in all not a lot of privacy! 
The conceriege was knowledgeable about the city and was very helpful. He provided maps of the city and showed us where to go. 
After a late night out we ordered room service (which is open 24 hours) which was good, but a bit pricey. We ordered the Sirloin Cheeseburger ($16) and the Chicken Wings ($12). The delivery gentleman was prompt and courteous.
We asked for an extended check out so that we could do some shopping and it was granted for 2 pm. The staff was polite at check out and the bill was correct.
All in all it was a good stay but I have two things to complain about. I purposely booked this hotel because it had an indoor pool. Upon check in, the gal told me the pool was on the 7th floor and that I should check it out. When we went to go for a swim, we found out the pool was closed for maintenance. That was very dissapointing as it was not noted anywhere on their website. I would have booked elsewhere, like the Sheraton Towers if I had known this. The second thing is that after heading off to bed at 4 am (bars are open until 5), we were awoken at 7:30 by a banging on the wall. When I called down to the front desk, I was told they would check into it. 20 minutes later, I heard it again and called the desk. I was then told that they were laying carpet in the room above us. I asked if they had to do it at 7:30 in the morning and they said that they were under contract and had to do it then. This was unacceptable. They knew that they would be laying carpet so why were put on the floor directly below? I was offered no apology or compensation. I hate to believe that they treat their guests so poorly and hope this was a one time bad experience, especially for the money most people pay to stay at the W Lake shore! 
Like I said, it was a good experience, but with other Starwood properties to stay at in Chicago, these oversights and lack of being able to deliver a wowing experience have made me think about staying elsewhere next time.

title: “Great Location/Excellent Service”
text: We stayed for one night as a little get away and were very pleased. We got an outstanding deal that included continental breakfast in the dining room and parking so we were able to save some $$ by driving in instead of taking the train... Our room was large (for NYC) and well appointed, if a bit outdated. The service was excellent and included a complimentary dried fruit tray and lovely personalized welcome note. Staff was friendly and helpful and we were within walking distance of great shopping & dining and also close the the subway. We will definitely plan to stay again...

title: “Awesome location, good value hotel”
text:
Have just stayed here for a weekend. Booked through Expedia and got a reduced rate for a 4 night stay. We were on 45th St less than 5 min walk from Times Square so at the heart of all the action. As said previously the hotel itself is very basic, definitely no airs and graces and the rooms are tired and dated. However, most importantly the rooms were clean and no bedbugs!!! There are no facilities at the hotel but two doors away the Cranberry Deli offers an exhaustive range of good value food and is open 24 hours a day. We wanted a good value hotel in an awesome location and this is what we got. If you, like us, just need a hotel to lay your head down after spending all day and night in the Big Apple, then this is your place. Would recommend and stay again. Also do try and get a meal at the Bond 45 restaurant just across the road from the hotel - the food was amazing!!!
P.S. Don't forget your earplugs, the downside to the location is that it can be noisy!!

title: “Great Place - Great Value”
text: Very friendly staff. Excellent location. Very good value for the money.

title: “I simply ADORE this Hotel.”
text:
I stayed there on 2 occasions in July and August and it is as wonderful as previous times I have stayed there. My arrival was very late around 11.00pm and when enterting my room the lights were on, soft music playing, bed turned back and slippers waiting. What more could you want at that time of the night! It was like coming home. Staff there are always wonderful - many have been there for years. The location of this Hotel is fabulous - so close to Times Square and great shopping on 5th Ave, was also within walking distance to some of my bsiness appointments and an easy walk to Penn Station to catch the train for further appointments. Highly recommend this Hotel too for ladies travelling on their own as always feel very safe here.
W Dobson - New Zealand

title: “Great Location, Great Staff”
text: We have stayed here twice - once at Christmastime and once around July 4th. We love the location - near Times Square but away from all the hubub. The staff has always been wonderful, the rooms clean, the breakfast in the a.m. ample and fresh. The rooms are actually a good size for NYC - I visited a friend in a neighboring hotel and you could not move in her room with the bed - but here no problems at all.

title: “Good location and standard Marriott Service”
text: Spent 1 night here while on business in downtown Denver. The location is excellent as it's an easy walk to the business district and LoDo. Service, price and amenities were standard Marriott quality. There is a big Starbucks in the lobby which is very handy in the morning. There is also a full convenience store just across the courtyard from the lobby (in the adjacent office building lobby). Highly recommend the convenience story for quick snacks or supplies. Way cheaper than the standard hotel gift shop you normally find at these kinds of hotels. The hotel seems to have some pretty big conference space so the lobby can get a little hectic. Other than that, I would definitely stay here again on my next trip.

title: “Good deal for the price”
text: The Adante Hotel is located in a convenient spot and is a good base for a weekend of sightseeing. The rooms are what you'd expect from a budget hotel: small, utilitarian, and lacking the amenities that you'd find in higher-priced hotels. The rooms are very clean, and the management was professional. I had no problems checking in or out. The rooms were quiet, although you could hear the sounds of the city below with the window open. The window was open because there is no A/C. This is not a horrible thing given the frequent breeze in SF, but you'll want to know that there's no A/C ahead of time. I lucked out with a weekend of beautiful cool weather, but you'll want to check the weather forecast before booking here to ensure you're not in a heat wave. The murals painted on the walls are kind of kitschy and fun in a weird way. I would stay here again if the weather was cool enough.

title: “Fantastic Hotel”
text: What a great place to stay. Absolutely beautiful!! The beds are so comfortable and the staff is outstanding. In addition Roy's is located right by the hotel. Roy's is a fantastic restaurant-don't miss it. The only downside is the price! If money is no object then I highly recommend this hotel.

title: “GR8 PLACE FOR THE BUDGET TRAVELER”
text: We paid $103.00 per nite plus 15.5 percent tax and 24.00 parking per day, hotel was approx. 4 blocks from the inner harbor. Hotel check in went smoothly, allowed us to check in early. Room had microwave, fridge, and coffee maker. Only complaint about the room was that the bathroom was extremely small. Bathroom sink was in living area. Maid staff were very accommodating with extra towels, toilet paper, etc. Hotel bar very small, however there was a bar outside next door called the Pratt Street Ale House which was a fun place to be. Would stay here again, cannot beat the price. A few blocks away from football and baseball stadiums.

title: “Great View, Ok Hotel”
text: I traveled on business the first week of May. The hotel was nice. Great view, clean, good food in the morning for a hotel. The staff however could use some improvements. I do not ask for much when it comes to service. However, they seemed preoccupied every time I was at the front desk. They also did not seem to care about me as a customer.

title: “December stay”
text: Our stay was perfect, from the valet to check in, everyone was polite and cordial. Our room was very clean and comfortable. We would definitely stay here again.

title: “Nice Place. Good Food.”
text: Stayed one night. Nice newer hotel. Has a full bar and restuarant. Ate dinner at the bar and the bartender was very nice. She made you feel welcome. All food is prepared fresh and homemade. Clean and nicely accomodated.

title: “Wonderful Location”
text:
What a great location directly on the Riverwalk. Lovely hotel with some beautiful decor throughout, but the rooms seemed a little tired, not as clean as one would expect from a Hilton. I found someone elses soap in the shower the first morning I was there and cleaned up some hair off the vanity.
Breakfast buffet is $20 and is decent. Not much choice for a less expensive breakfast near the hotel if you are a single female and don't feel comfortable walking in a strange city when it's dark in the early morning.
The margaritas at Ibiza, the hotel's restaurant, are very good. I sampled quite a few from many different places while I was there and those were the best. And fairly priced.
The rooms have mini fridges for use which is a nice touch and the hotel offers free coffee and tea throughout the day in the lobby. 
The Original mexican Restaurant down the river was a good dinner choice for a group and the food was outstanding.
The river cruise is recommended, but do so during the day so you can plan where you want to visit next.

title: “Disappointed”
text:
This was the 2nd time that I stayed at this hotel. The 1st time, it was absolutely fantastic! This last time, not so much! My disappointment started the second that we walked in the door and were greeted by a giant construction tarp that was covering the entire lobby. I booked my reservations on the hotel's website and there was no mention of any remodeling at all. Turns out, not only are they remodeling the lobby, which doesn't effect much other than the immediate feel of the hotel, but they are also remodeling that the 2nd floor lounge area and the 3rd floor. 
The 2nd floor is where they have their complimentary happy hour service and their complimentary breakfast service. There were signs directing you to the 3rd floor for both of these events. I don't know why they moved it to the 3rd floor, it's under construction as well. Drinks and breakfast was served at makeshift tables surrounded by construction tape and hanging plastic tarps. Not exactly the relaxing, romantic atmosphere my wife and I were expecting.
Now, onto the accomodations. The first time that I stayed at the Magnolia, I was blown away by my room. It was large, immaculate and more than I expected. This time around, it was nothing but an average hotel room - plus a giant stain on the carpet, an air conditioner that never shut off and a bathtub/show faucet that felt like it was going to fall out of the wall. The bed had 2 of the smallest pillows I've ever seen on it. No extra pillows in the closet or anywhere else for that matter. We called down to get some extra pillows sent to the room. After waiting 30 minutes, we finally gave up and left for dinner. On the way out, we stopped at the front desk to ask about the pillow request. The guy says, "aw geez, I sent your request in as soon as you called, I don't know what happened. I'll have them in your room before you get back from dinner". That was great but he never bothered to apologize or anything. Luckily, the pillows were in our room when we returned.
10 minutes after we got into our room, a guy, with all of his bags, comes walking right into our room. Apparently, he was given our same room when he checked in right after us. I travel a lot for business and that has happened to me before so I didn't really think about it again, accidents happen. However, after returning from dinner later that night, we found out that neither of our key cards worked anymore. When I went to the front desk to get them to fix the problem, all that the guy said was, "oh, they cancelled all of the keys issued for that room because it was given to 2 different people". He never apologized for the mistake with the other guy or for the fact that our keys were "turned off" and nobody bothered to tell us.
Will I stay at the Magnolia again? I have to admit that I probably will. The location is absolutely perfect and I'm assuming that when the remodeling is completed, the whole place will go back to being a beautiful hotel. At this point, I'm 50/50 on this place. The 1st time was amazing and the 2nd time was not so great. I'll give them 1 more shot. If it's half as bad as this last time, they'll lose my business for good. They are lucky that the 1st experience was so great. It's all that's keeping me from getting really upset about this latest visit.

title: “Good location, excellent service.”
text:
We stayed in this hotel for two nights in June, one of which was my boyfriends birthday! Due to the late arrival we were able to check in straight away and our room was fresh and clean as soon as we entered it! We were too tired to venture out so we decided to try the hotel restaurant. The food was exquisite, just enough and excellent French food! 
The hotel is in a very good location on south Michigan avenue which was just 1/2 mile walk into the centre of the city and the magnificent mile! We enjoyed walking up the whole of michigan avenue and stopping at the bistro's that met us on our way! 
This hotel made our trip very easy and we didn't get hassled by early housekeeping even when we forgot to put the do not disturb sign on! 
Good hotel, good location and all round good stay! 
Thank you Essex Inn! 
(only sour point was the undercover pool! It was very hot whilst we were staying and we would have liked an outside pool! However, it is the windy city for a reason and can have a chilly wind and in the middle of the city I can understand why not!)

title: “Tiny room - too claustrophobic for anything but sleep!”
text:
I stayed at the Hotel Mela in early October 2007 for one night on a business trip to NYC. Someone else chose the room for me, and as soon as I arrived I was sorry I wasn't staying at the Marriott Marquis (where I've stayed many times). My review is pretty much word for word what "Amaklo" said about their stay (I think we stayed in the same room!)
The room was literally only 2 feet wider than the queen bed. I had to go out to walk around Times Square until I was ready to sleep - I didn't want to be in the room! I also had to move the basket of food away from the TV to watch it, and the "closet" wouldn't fit full-length clothes! The bathroom was thankfully not extraordinarily tiny. 
Everything was clean, nice linens, etc. The staff was very friendly. It's conveniently located in the heart of Times Square. However, I will never choose to stay at this hotel again due to the size of the room.

title: “GREAT PLACE TO STAY!!!!!”
text: Just got back from Phoenix...stayed at the Budget Lodge...very impressed...clean, affordable rooms, that were walking distance from downtown activities and rail service to north Phoenix and Mesa. Beds were always made and new towels left every afternoon, when we came back to property. Dan and his staff do an awesome job!!!! Would stay again!!!!

title: “Loved the Aloft and staff is great! We will definitely be back.”
text:
Was in NYC with my cousin to gather up my daughter to move back to North Carolina.
The hotel is easy to get to, parking was inexpensive a block away, room was very clean, comfortable, and love the Bliss products. 
Left my duffle behind (at the parking structure) and Abraham at the parking structure held on to it until Juan, Director of Security, very kindly went and retrieved it for me and shipped it to my home.
They go beyond the call of duty.
Breakfast sandwich and crumb cake were awesome for breakfast.

title: “Front Desk lacking”
text: Upon arriving at SEA-TAC I called the hotel to get shuttle information - I was rudely told to hold. After several minutes I hung up and redialed. It was answered and hung up abruptly. I called again and was placed on hold before I could say a word. I waited for 4 minutes (I timed it). When no one came back online, I hung up and redialed and finally got a real person. The Front Desk clerk, Lena, was not friendly, welcoming or patient when I asked how to meet the shuttle. When I arrived at the hotel, she was sullen, unwelcoming and gave off a very negative impression. The room was decent, clean and comfortable. Good customer service was sorely lacking. With so many hotels to choose from, I probably won't stay here again.

title: “The Gem of Philadelphia”
text: My wife and I first discovered The Rittenhouse back in 2005. Since then, we try to get there at least once a year. In fact, we won't stay anywhere else in Philadelphia now. The rooms are the largest I've ever seen in a "standard" room, featuring huge bathrooms with separate shower/soaking tub. The service is always gracious and friendly and concierge is consistent and helpful. We have visited the Adolf Biecker Spa, eaten at Lacroix and had drinks at Bar 210 and in all ways we have found service and quality on par or better than other luxury hotels. On our last stay, we were bumped up to a top-floor suite - truly a great way to travel with a small child. I recommend this hotel happily and without reservation. In fact, we're going back next month.

title: “Funky Spot!”
text:
My husband, 14-yr. old son and I stayed here for 6 nights. It is off the busy streets of San Diego, but just a few minutes from downtown and the airport. We could ride bikes (provided by the hotel) or walk to restaurants and the San Diego Yacht Club. Beautiful view of SD. We mostly went up the coast to Ocean Beach/Mission Beach, which were just 15 minutes away. They also have outdoor concerts and I got to hear Ringo Starr & the All Starr band while sitting in my room! Not everyone would like that, but it's a perk. Check out their concert calendar before you book. They shut down concerts at 10:00 pm, so it isn't a late-night issue. I think it would be fun for couples - there is a good restaurant with live music each night adjacent to the hotel.
Big pool, beautiful grounds and areas for walking/running along the waterfront. Staff friendly, rooms clean and comfortable.

title: “Loved the Marriott Marina, Great Views!"”
text: Stayed at the Marriott Marina San Diego, 8/6-8/7. Had a great high floor room with an incredible view of the harbor. If you're staying on the weekend make sure to ask for a harbor view because there are fireworks on fri and sat nights in the summer. Place was huge, actually felt like a Vegas hotel for all the activity, but once we got to our room it was nice and quiet. Nice pool area, crowded and filled with kids, but still ok. You're in walking distance to the gaslamp district, the trolley, and a short drive to beaches. Can't wait to go back!. If you're a Marriott Elite member there is a members lounge with free breakfast but it is totally packed, not worth the wait.

title: “Convenient, Good Value”
text:
Stayed here for five nights while visiting family in the surrounding area. This hotel is convenient to the municipal bus line, neighborhood cafes and grocery shops. Rooms are comfortable with internet access plus a computer and printer in the lobby. Staff was helpful and friendly. We had a petit queen room and it was adequate for two.
Would definitely stay here again.

title: “Wonderful Elegant Hotel”
text: I just completed a weekend stay at the Mark Hopkins. This hotel is a beautiful, classic and elegant architectural landmark. I booked online using a "weekend" package that included an upgrade to a mini-suite which turned out to be a gorgeous two room suite with separate living area with a sofa, upholstered chairs, a dining table with four chairs, a hallway with a beautiful bath off of it and a bedroom. It was like staying in an elegant tastefully decorated manor. The robes provided and the Penhaligon products in the bathroom were lovely. The room was clean clean clean, the furniture, upholstery, carpeting, and draperies were of the highest quality and like new. The front desk staff were extremely polite and helpful and granted our late check out request with a "my pleasure". The head of housekeeping was in the lobby one morning and personally came over to me to inquire about our stay. She was lovely and personable and gave me her business card should I "need anything". And no, I'm not a celebrity or weatlhy. To top it all off, our rate also included the breakfast buffet for two held in the Top of the Mark except on Sundays when it is held in the former "Peacock" room off of the lobby. The buffet was tasty, fresh and bountiful and even at $23 dollars if we had to pay for it, it was worth it considering it included all this, coffee and orange juice. After all folks, breakfast in a hotel in this city isn't going to be $5.95. I have stayed in many luxury hotels and this ranks right up there with the top five. What did I pay for all this luxury? $329 per night which isn't cheap by any means but it was well worth it!

title: “Good deal on Priceline”
text: Have booked this hotel twice through Priceline and for the price I paid ($45/night), it was a good deal with the expected service from a 3-star hotel. Nothing spectacular, but I would recommend this hotel if you're looking for a clean, decent place to stay in San Jose.

title: “Very good budget hotel”
text:
We stayed four nights at this hotel. Our renewed room was very nice: excellent and beautifull bathroom; very confortable queen beb; free wi-fi; safety box; hairdryer; work desk; cable tv; everything clean and working properly. The coffee machine and chocolates at the lobby were very usefull. 
The negative points are of minimal importance, if any: there is no room service, but we never use that anyway in any hotel, so no problem for us. No minibar, but an ice machine at lobby. Small reception, but we didn't go to NYC to stay at a hotel reception. No restaurant, but a plenty of restaurants nearby.
Of note: we stayed one night at the more expensive Sheraton, and our room at the Herald Square was much better than at that hotel.
If you want luxury (and paying for that) look for other hotels, but if you look for a simple and nice hotel just to have a good sleep at night after a day full of activities, this is a really very good one.

title: “AVOID!!! Vile Disgusting Place”
text: Receptionist didn't even look at me and grunted when repeatedly asked questions! Toilet was cracked, floor was so filthy you could taste the dust in the air. The place was absolutely CRAWLING WITH MICE - you could literally watch them scurrying around the hallways and i woke to found one chewing on our (threadbare) carpet. I stayed for 3 days and didn't even wash because the bathroom was so disgusting! The shower was held in place by wire attached to the foam board ceiling which was mostly pulled down! Also in the 'red light' district! Not a good area at all - times sq is close but you'd be better off sleeping on the streets. My poor sister cried herself to sleep every night it broke my heart because i didn't have the money to take us elsewhere and had unfortunately prepaid over the internet

title: “Great location and free parking!”
text: We stayed there for a weekend in October. The staff was very courtious and helpful. The rooms were clean and the size was fine. The site was perfect for our visit to Fishermans Warf, could not get any closer. This is an excellent place for the money if your not looking for fancy room service or special amenities. There are plenty of places to eat and play with in a few steps. The free parking was a welcomed surprise, considering the rates of the near-by hotels are insulting.

title: “Disappointing”
text: Exterior facility and check-in fine, but then we went to the room to a broken security lock on the interior door. Opened the door to a filthy, stained carpet, a child's bathrobe on the living room floor, the bathrooms were not clean, there were electric problems and we lost power to one bedroom on day two, you would not think of walking on flooring without shoes - it was sticky and nasty. A patio with indoor/outdoor carpet that was shredded and a coffee cup full of cigarette buds. My sister had stayed there 4 or 5 years ago and it was nice; now it is in horrible condition. I was embarrassed that I had made such a poor selection for my family, but I had always thought that your hotels were good quality.

title: “Great stay - okay location”
text: This is a beautiful hotel. It is very clean, the rooms are comfortable, and the staff goes out of its ways to be friendly. We got an incredible deal on priceline, but were still given a very nice room with a view of the water and city. The bed was very comfortable, and the pool, whirlpool, and gym were spacious and very clean. The only downside is the location. It was a 30 minute walk to Fanueil Hall. Public transport required the Silver T bus line to south station, and then a switch of at least 1 time to get to most areas. As a tourist, the hotel feels a little too removed from the heart of the city. But the incredible service and value of the property nearly offset it. As the area around the hotel further develops, the appeal will definately increase.

title: “Construction Warning But A Great Hotel”
text:
We just returned fron a two night stay at the Algonquin to celebrate my birthday. It's a lovely boutique hotel but with horrendous construction noise! 
Our first night was in Room 1205. It was a cute, sunny room with a big bow window and window seat. It wasn't a large room but we're used to that in the city. When shown to my room, I noticed the construction site down below but thought, hey, we'll only be in the room to sleep so it shouldn't be a problem. At 1 AM I cursed myself for that thought as the construction was just stopping for the night. It resumed again around 6 AM with jack hammering, loud "backing up" beeps, and an air horn going off every 15 -20 minutes. 
Needless to say we were exhausted and it was ruining my birthday. On the way past the front desk, we expressed our complaints and were cheerfully moved to another room, 507, in the inner court.. This was even an upgrade to a larger room with a king size bed at no extra charge. It was much quieter but there is no escaping the air horns from the construction site. We both slept soundly for our second night. Try to get a room numbered 9-12 on each floor (ex 509 for the fith floor) as these rooms are on the front side of the hotel furthest from the construction site in the back.
We thought the hotel staff was great. They were all very friendly and greeted you as you went in and out of the hotel. We got a kick out of Matilda, the hotel cat , who lounged around like the Queen of Sheba.
We ate our breakfast a few doors down at the Red Flame diner. We had very expensive drinks ($16 each) in the Blue Bar to celebrate the end of my birthday. The drinks were wonderful.
We also went to see the musical Curtains starring David Hyde Pierce from the Frazier show. It was a fun, entertaining show! We can't understand why it wasn't packed. We purchased our tickets online thru www.tdf.org for $36 each. 
In spite of the construction, we would stay at the Algonquin again. We love the older style hotels in New York City as they all have such a unique character that you don't find in the chain hotels. The Algonquin is in an excellent location for exploring the city and you can't beat the friendliness of the staff.

title: “Pleasant experience”
text: Stayed in suite which was large. Comfortable beds, nice value. Service was friendly. Lots of parking. Area is in better location than other hotel chains as far as being in an acceptable neighborhood. Lots of off-site food locations close by.

title: “Great location in the middle of Times Square”
text:
This hotel's location is great- right next to Times Square, and only a couple of minutes walk from 5th avenue and Rockefeller Center. As other reviews have pointed out, the rooms are small, but that is to be expected of NYC hotels and even though expensive compared to much better places in other cities, the rate was average for NY. The room was clean, small, with a huge LED TV set. There was a small fridge that I didn´t open and that about it. The bathroom was very clean and seemed pretty new. The only negative part are the elevators; they have two far from each other, and they are small and slow, very slow. Front desk was helpful and we were able to keep our bags in storage after check out.
We only stayed one night on September the 7th, and it cost 249 plus tax. 
As I always say: location, location, location. If you want to walk to Broadway and see shows, this is your place, right in the middle of it. I don´t have much experience with other hotels in NY, and even though the location was great, I will probably try to find another option for my next stay in NY.

title: “Pleasantly Surprised!”
text:
I have to admit, I groaned when my Hotwire hotel was revealed. I have never stayed at La Quinta property, but somehow made the assumptions that all La Quinta’s are “crappy”. I’m happy to say, I was proven wrong! My husband and I had truly enjoyed our stay. We stayed 4 nights during October 2011.
*King Bed Suite: The rooms are clean, spacious and modern. I think this property may have had an update because the paint, furniture and décor were in great condition. Our had room many electrical outlets, sofa, flat screen, microwave and mini refrigerator. Average size bathrooms with shower and tub.
*Service/Hotel Amenities: The staff was friendly and helpful. No bellhop. Free wifi and breakfast daily. Parking available, but it’s $36 a night :/ There is Cupcake shop and Argo Tea Shop in the lobby.
*Location: Great location. The hotel is located in the heart of downtown, so there’s pros and cons to its location. (The cons were very minimal)
-Pros: Walking distance to El train, shops, drug stores and restaurants. 2 blocks away from Sears Tower!
-Cons: Business close early. The scene is “dead” during evenings and weekends. Not many bars in the area.
*Random Tips:
-Giordanos’ Pizza: 4 blocks away from the hotel. The lobby has Giordano’s coupons.
-Car Rental: isn’t needed to explore Chicago, but if you do rent, there’s an Enterprise located in the hotel parking structure. If you do a day rental, you can avoid the daily parking fee, by returning to car to Enterprise, since they are located in the same structure. 
-Take a Drive to Wisconsin: As a huge cheese lover, I was over the top giddy when I found out Wisconsin was only an hour away. We rented a car for a day and drove to explore Milwaukee, Wisconsin. The highway from Chicago to Milwaukee has many cheese themed shops and a shopping outlet with 5% sales tax!
-Pet Friendly: Throughout my stay I saw a few people checking in with their pets.

title: “Avoid at all costs”
text:
A simple warning -- stay away from the Claremont Hotel. The rooms are stifflingly hot without A/C, some rooms have flea infestations, many room keys open doors to other rooms (a friend had a mentally unstable guest walk into her room this way), and my first floor room had a large, ground level window with any lock or security features. Add to this cleanliness issues, weird smells, and an utterly disinterested management, who treated these problems with a shoulder shrug, and you can see why one needs to avoid this hotel. 
In short: the money you might save with their rock-bottom room rates is **NOT** worth the discomfort and potential security risks you'll have to put up with.

title: “What a wonderful find”
text: My wife and I took my daughter and several of her girl friends for a weekend escape to the Inner Harbor in Baltimore. We selected the Marriott Waterfront Hotel as our base of operations since it is right on the Inner Harbor. From the time of check in until our departure around 12 noon the next day we had a wonderful stay. We were given connecting rooms overlooking the Harbor with a great view especially at night. In the morning we decided to order breakfast in bed and it arrived right on time at 9:00 am. The staff had such a nice attitude about them. I can only say this is a great place to escape.

title: “Not your typical hotel "decor"....not a diamond in the rough, but not bad for the price.”
text: found a coupon in a travel guide at the Interstate rest area. The coupon advertised their standard room for $44.99. Since we usually stick with the larger "chain" hotels, we wondered if it could be worth checking into. The Staff was very helpful and let us look at one of the rooms....and didn't try to upgrade us to something more expensive. However, after driving 12.5 hours, we decided to reserve a room with a jacuzzi tub (negotiated for $90). The decor was very different with serene scenes painted on the walls and "mood lighting". The room, bedding, and tub were clean. However, the carpet was due for shampooing and there was no iron or coffee maker. The mattress was a bit firm for us, but overall gave us the overnight rest we needed. The Continental Breakfast consisted of cereal and muffins, coffee, and an open pitcher of juice and carton of milk. Mostly, I'd recommend it for the room's atmosphere and price. But, be prepared to sacrifice a few ammenities and a good breakfast.

title: “Great location for a reasonable price”
text: I'm so glad we decided to stay here - the staff were friendly and attentive, the location was awesome and the rooms were very nice. I especially enjoyed having queen sized beds - it seems like most hotels in the Times Square area don't have them! Breakfast was amazing to say the least - the 24 hour coffee station was also a bonus. (Cookies and apples too!) To keep it short, this hotel is worth it - close to the action of Times Square but at a reasonable price!

title: “Thank you for a great stay!”
text: Walking distance to great attractions, neighborhoods and downtown. Clean room and friendly staff.

title: “we liked it!”
text:
Just came back of 7 nights vacation in NYC. we stayed at the "red roof" in a 2 double bed room. the hotel is located in a nice and "full of life" area, just 2 steps away from 5th ave., Empire State Building, 34th st and more. and that means good location! it's close to the subway, the bus, PENN station, to good restaurants. 
Other than that. the room was really nice and big (ours was the biggest on the floor according to a map of the floor that was next to the elevators). The bath and toilet were clean and have been cleaned daily. we had a refrigerator, microwave and a coffee machine inside the room.
The breakfest was small but good for us, as it saved us money... (everything in new york is expensive...).
And yes, as others wrote here before, 2 elevators are not enough, but we don't think it's a good enough reason for not choosing this hotel.
If you are looking for a nice modest hotel, with great location, this hotel is for you. 
I would certainly stay in this hotel the next time i'm in NYC.

title: “Great location but maintenance issues overshadowed the stay.”
text:
My husband is a Hilton Diamond Honors member and we choose this hotel for its proximity to Seattle Children's Hospital and downtown attractions.
We were in Seattle for a nine day stay as our daughter was having surgery. On the day we brought her to the hotel (a Friday) there was no air in our room (812). We were unable to open the windows because our room (812) overlooked I5 & the noise was unbearable. (witht he windows closed, you don't notice the noise as much.) Saturday morning we called the front desk & were told that several rooms were in the same condition because they were upgrading the a/c & heating. We asked for a floor fan. I called again about 12 hours later and was brought a $10 Walmart style fan. Sunday morning, they came & installed the new blower in our room but stated that it was not hooked up to the a/c function. Our room temperature was over 80* by 4pm with no air circulation. Monday we got up and it was sunny in Seattle - rare, I know, but it does happen. I called and asked when we would have a functioning blower and a/c unit - we were told not anytime soon. I asked for a new room - we had three nights of a stuffy, unbearably hot room. They called back & were prepared to move us to a new room with functioning air. As we were moving out (immediately after an urgent, unplanned return to the hospital), they came in to connect the blower and a/c. (They don't like to overpromise per Larry, Maintenance Manager.) At this point, we were half moved into the new room and our daughter was in severe pain.
All was fine in the new room (536) except...... the shower didn't drain. We called the front desk again the next morning. Larry, my favorite maintenance guy, showed up & was frank about the fact that this particular room has plumbing issues. And they would comp us two free nights for our trouble. At this point, I was not moving again and took the working a/c over the poor drain.
Both rooms required a full wipe down with my clorox wipes - the kitchen and bathroom walls, the top of the frig and other surfaces were gross. Maybe I was sensitive to the germ issue because of why we were there...
Crystal (front desk) and Larry (maintenance) were at the top of their service game and we appreaciated that. Others not so much. We wish we had been told their would be no air over the weekend - if not at check-in then with a note under the door. It was incredbiliy poor planning to have a group of rooms (at least two floors) without blowers or a/c over a weekend without notifying the guests in advance.
After check out, I reviewed our bill and had to call the hotel and ask about the promised two nights that were to be comped. It had not been done automatically.
While our stay was not for pleasure or business, we did expect it to be an easy stay and not a complicating factor in our daughter's recovery. I was stressed enough about nursing our daughter to have to deal with maintenance issues.

title: “Good Residence Inn”
text:
No complaints about this Residence Inn. Maid service was fine, parking good, location is great. Within walking distance of restaurants, shops and my favorite, Whole Foods. 
The gym is very small though, 5 or 6 cardio machines and not enough room to stretch, yoga, etc...
Breakfast was good, standard fare.
The evening reception was good, beer and wine. Tuesday had a small keg from the NXNW brewery down the street, which has excellent beer. I usually don't eat the food at the reception, but I did try the pizza, which was pretty good.
Wireless internet worked ok, a bit slow which is usual for most hotels I stay at.

title: “cant go wrong”
text: recently stayed at wall street holiday inn and was very impressed. got the room from priceline on a whim and was glad i did. the staff was great and the room very clean and comfortable . some odd shape room but had all the comforts of home. front desk staff was unbelievably helpful and friendly. even if i had to pay full price would be very happy to come back here.

title: “A Beautiful, Comfortable, Family-friendly Hotel”
text: We stayed here with our two sons, ages 16 and 8 for two days. The location is just wonderful. Steps away from the Boston Commons and easily accessible from everywhere we went. The hotel is just beautiful and historical. Clearly this hotel is popular amongst all types of travelers - business travelers, couples, families, sports and other groups. The high speed internet in the rooms is not free, but it is very easily affordable. There are many choices of restaurants right in and near the hotel. We loved everything about our stay.

title: “Great little hotel”
text: Ok so the rooms aren't big - who cares - you're in New York!!! We were up and out by about 9am and didn't get back in til 10pm. We had 3 rooms (2 twin and 1 double) all were clean and had reasonable sized bathrooms in. We weren't disturbed by noise as previously mentioned only people coming and going but that's to be expected anywhere. The hotel is right near a subway stop which takes you straight into Manhatten in under 10 minutes and Central Park is a good 10 minute walk. The hotel is cheap, the rooms and public areas I found to be spotless, the staff we spoke to were friendly and the only bad thing I can think to say is there's only one lift! They let you store your bags if your flight is later than your check out time too. All in all I loved New York and wouldn't hesitate to stay at this hotel again.

title: “For La Cumbre Meeting”
text:
Very Nice Hotel...
Great Location, Bay Views...
New Look and Modern.
Good Service

title: “I can not wait to spend more time at Homewood Suites”
text:
I have never visited Chicago before and had no idea where to stay. I got on my favorite travel site and found Homewood Suites. I read some nice reviews and saw some nice pics, but you can never be too sure. I am more than pleased with the choice staying at Homewood Suites. Lets start with the All-Star staff working the front door. These guys rock, if you want to know about the city just ask, if you need something just ask, they remember who you are and always make you feel welcome. Now lets move to the 6th floor where the lobby is....Great staff, super friendly, very very clean, nicely laided out room. right next to the lobby is the breakFEAST room. They guys know to lay a spread out every morning. They even do dinner Monday thru Thurs. 
Now the room, its a great suite, not overly large but large enough to have other people stay over. Great kitchen with everything you need to cook if you want (side note....Dont cook in the room there are so many resturant option all around the hotel) . I guess the only thing I can say is that the bathroom is kinda small but the tub and shower is a very nice size so I guess it all works. I loved the bed and sheets, very soft and comfy. 
Over all I love this place, I can not wait to spend more in my new favorite city of Chicago and stay at my HOME away from HOME at Homewood Suites.

title: “PUBLIC - Chicago”
text: Excellent hotel. Very cool spot. Nice rooms, solid service. I would most certainly stay there again.

title: “Perfect!”
text: I found this hotel through Expedia and picket it because it was midtown and within walking distance of Penn Station with good reviews. We arrived around 12:30 PM and were able to check in then. The men at the desk were personable, professional and nice. We went to our room and found we had a view of the Empire State Building. Our room had a king sized bed with great linen. We had free wireless internet. There is a roof top bar which had only a few people in it when we went up, but we had a nice drink and watched the green lights on the Empire State and the lights of the city. In the morning, there was a terrific free European style breakfast and we sat near a fireplace. I would say this was a perfect spot for us! The only drawback is the block has a porn shop which wasn't open and it was filled with papers from garbage left in front of other buildings. The hotel was well decorated and secure. The staff was friendly and I can give a special shout out to Ronni Rodriguez on the desk!

title: “Excellent hotel close to Reagan Library”
text:
