Rooms are very comfortable and large...bed was hard like I prefer and bathroom was clean and had excellent water pressure in the shower....The hotel had a great workout room.
Hotel close to restaurants,presidential library and hwy.

title: “Great location, eco-friendly, amazing value.”
text:
Stayed here on a short break while travelling with my girlfriend - we got upgraded on arrival and were really impressed by how comfortable the room was. Service was really good and the location was really amazingly central, right next door to the gate to China Town too!
Really recommend this place - randomly too it's an extremely eco-friendly hotel too.
SHORT SUMMARY:
Pros: Tidy, very comfortable and eco-friendly.
Cons: None I can think of.
Stay if: Looking for a nice holiday location, good romantic place.

title: “Delighted, both times”
text: I've stayed at the Dumont twice, once for business, once for a trip with one of my daughters. Both times, I was absolutely knocked out by the warmth of the staff and their kindness. Everything was sparkling, and when they saw how excited my daughter was to be traveling, they upgraded us to a high-floor junior suite so she could see the Chrysler Building at night. Best. Nightlight. Ever. Truly a little gem, slightly and perfectly out of the way of the Midtown madness.

title: “The Stephen F. Austin made our son's wedding experience amazing!”
text: From beginning to end our experience with the Stephen F. Austin was amazing. David Lopez and Miguel Diaz made sure our every need was met. The food and arrangements for our son's rehearsal dinner were superb. We would be glad to let this hotel be the destination for any future events we might have in the Austin area.

title: “The best location to stay in!”
text:
This is the best hotel to stay in if one is a tourist and is looking to explore the city and its culture. It has the best view as soon as you step out the back entrance of the hotel which is pier 39 and the bay. Lots of great restaurants, great transportation of trams, street cars etc and best of all, everything is right there including an IHop. You can even walk to the Embarcadero which has this awesome Thai restaurant called Osha Thai and the Farmer's Market. And Johnny Rockets is right outside your door! The only flip side was that housekeeping chose to ignore the Do Not Disturb sign a couple of times. Staff is helpful and very cordial and the rooms are spotless and super clean with an adjustable pillow and mattress setting. Great price of a 100 dollars a night was the rate i got on the hotel website. Have gone back again since. 
108070900

title: “Excellent boutique hotel”
text: My husband and I stayed here just one night, but we both wished we'd stayed at least one more. We were on the 7th floor (room 709 is a nice one in the corner) in a deluxe room. Nice natural lighting, free wireless, very clean and cozy room, and plenty of space for the two of us. I had asked for "the best room at this price" when I booked, adding we were celebrating our wedding anniversary, and when we arrived in the room, there was a nice bottle of wine and two glasses on our bed from the management with a card congratulating us on our anniversary. Nice touch! The front desk staff were always very pleasant and helpful. I would definitely recommend this hotel as one of the nicest for the price in a large city. The neighborhood is ok if you don't go much further than a couple blocks off of Sutter.

title: “Hotel where hearts make it a home”
text:
Having a job that moves you around a lot means that where you stay is important to your sanity. I have just the place,The Homewood Suites in Houston,Tx!
From the first moment I stepped into the lobby to check in I was welcomed by smiles and helpful people. It didnt stop there either,maid service,maintenance,kicthen servers,and hotel management have made sure that not only me but every guest is at home here.
 The front desk staff knew my name in one day! It is amazing what good people, good service and an awesome attitude by the staff can make being away from home for week like being on an ALL the wonderful staff at Homewood Suites you are AWESOME!

title: “Extended Stay Very Eager to Please!”
text: When I first got to Extended Stay, I was a little uncomfortable. I was in the very back of the hotel on the ground floor, and I felt vulnerable. I called the manager, Mr. Patel, and he said that he would change my room if there was any possibility of doing so. Well, he found a way, and I moved to a second floor room in the front area. The second room was the same size and had the same accomodations, but, I felt safer there. In addition, I accidentally left my Nook (electronic book), a card, and some other items. I called and Jheri at the front desk said they would mail it out as soon as possible. Everything arrived, and I really appreciated the effort to go the extra mile with mailing everything and with changing my room.

title: “good value if you book on the right website”
text:
This is a good hotel close to LAX. A free shuttle bus took us to the hotel. We stayed here two nights and used the bus across the road to get to santa monica for only 75c each way.
It is not as fancy as other Marriott HOtels and the front desk staff appear to dislike their jobs. We changed rooms as the first room was located with the view of the carpark.We asked to move to a room facing the pool , which was more pleasant.
There is a good bar which we ate at.A $15 beer and sandwich special for dinner. The Starbucks on site makes awful coffee so aviod that.
Overal I would probably stay here again for a short visit to LA.

title: “Very Good Urban Visit”
text: If you wish to see a City full of Architecture, Art, Museums, ride the T to almost all places and walk through the snow this is a good developing site; the development is of the shopping park and local work places, frequented by cats in the giant yards and seagulls still looking for the Port of the Tea Party. The best T however was the train sub, near to Andrew T and with its own bus to the station this Hotel reaches most of Boston, ill supplied with maps and tea in the rooms and decent Planning but filled with built form of each sort of an Architect's dreams, without coordination, but the Big Dig made Boston walkable apart from the tree roots and some of the paved brick that has come apart. Watch your feet for the pieces of metal sticking in the paving in odd places and the litter. Boston needs a Big Vacuum on a large mechanized machine. Machines are large in Boston, that alone makes it a good Boys visit, the white line crossings need care, but if they turn in and run you down as a bookshop lady complained at lunchtime they are liable. The Hotel was large also, the room great, the bed giant, the bathroom well maintained, the plumber very pleasant although we blocked his toilet late Saturday night, the desk people were great, the help in Boston is good, the books and people working charity for children superb. The coffee was American!, the tea absent except in the main concourse, plenty of it, the Hazelnut Milk is great in coffee. Internet OK, relaxation and the Jacuzzi and swim small but very welcome and well maintained. The staff would talk with us that made it great. Very accommodating, I think we were not the easiest customers as first English to land from Somerset ? with questions on simple matters. Breakfast here is booked at table but was great. Wife made and filled herself with Waffle, not her usual trend! This site is fairly new it will become better as companies take over empty sites, the traditional housing around was good, we also saw some coastal and old town, very pretty in summer I expect, we were snowed and poured upon, so felt the pain of cotton millers, but when it was shut for commercial reasons they were earning a much better pay than UK equivalent, so hard work long hours and dangerous to health but in the hey day of USA it would have been high living. However what Union workers actually get from company one knows not. The place is still colonial and very well run by the Mexican and Caribbean work force, African American Indian features are common so one is not completely overrun by Boston finance and high rise, streets wide except in old brick paved. The Hotel was a mine of information of a helpful nature and always there to help with a good smile. However if you go inside Spring Winter take Clothing or Visit Macy's the hotel was well heated but you cannot escape Boston winds and it is dry and desiccating for West Coast English, so after landing buy hand cream, lip salve, plenty to drink, everything is bulk and the rental would be good as they will not allow the wonderful fish slab cooking in the rooms. But stick rigidly with the rules on travel and accommodation, the TSA took the lock off my case, I thought I had been robbed, then left a courteous note inside of a routine check, so I was glad there was no dirty washing, as you can wash everything at this hotel or send it out if you prefer. I took too much but was very glad of the woollens and coat, hats you need hats and gloves, Great visit, thank you. Never saw a Beaver, they obvioulsy have more sense than us English in winter and deserts as the saying goes about the midday sun. Do visit the Muddy. Take a boat trip too. All well set up and wander about with a camera and a pencil, you can draw at Isabella Gardener it is encouraged, they have my eraser my wife "put back" so you can use that too, it is a High Quality Craft shop version for the airplane, which was not as tedious as expected, or buy one of the eraser bears you can find in shops. Visit Red Mango at Hewitt's Cove Hingham, wonderful, even for a boat trip afterward.

title: “Comfortable nights sleep”
text: I stayed at the Country Inn & Suites at Denver International Airport after having driven 13 hours. I was exhausted upon my arrival and just wanted to check in, grab a bit to eat and get some sleep. Thankfully, there are plenty of dining choices in the area. I grabbed some takeout at a nearby Applebee's and brought it back to my room to eat. The hotel is located in a business park just off the highway, but it's very quiet and you hear no highway noise at all nor planes landing and taking off. The room was clean, comfortable and well lit. The bed was exceptionally comfortable and I get an extremely restful nights sleep. I was pleasantly surprised when I went to the front desk to ask the staff for change for the vending machine so that I could purchase a candy bar. The hotel has warm, soft, fresh baked cookies on hand that are free to guests. Much more satisfying than the candybar I'd had in mind, so I pocketed the change. The breakfast buffet was well stocked and I quickly grabbed a bite to eat before hitting the road again on my way to Las Vegas.

title: “Reliably regular accomodation”
text:
Stayed here for one night mid-March 2007 @ $89 priceline and it is perfectly fine. The hotel is part of an office tower block with corner entrances and the hotel entrance is counterintuitively placed. 
Proficient desk staff. The room I stayed in had an interior lobby view and directly across was a view of a glass wall of 200 offices--but tradeoff was I was able to get the free lobby wireless in my room. Robes in the room was a nice touch.
I think they may allow pets--unless the fellow guest in my hall with the small yipping dog snuck Fido in.
Close to Driskill Hotel and an easy walk to bars and restaurants. But avoid the McCormick & Schmick's--it looks nice but the food there is budget.

title: “You couldnt wish for a better placed hotel”
text: We didn’t spend much time in the hotel, but when we were there it was fantastic. Pleasantly surprised by the room size as had heard hotel rooms in NYC were tiny, we had a deluxe suite and it was a great size. I think the best thing about this hotel has to be the location. Be prepared to walk lots to see this wonderful city - well worth the shoe leather!!!

title: “"Perfect Stay"”
text:
We were a bit 'iffy' about coming to the Hyatt Regency to begin with because I had read online from a few people that the service wasn't so great.
But when we first pulled up, we were over-satisfied with the vallet parking guys. They were helpful with all of our questions, very friendly, patient, and 'all smiles.' Going with vallet parking is great because it's just a few dollars more than self-parking and it saves the hassle of having to park across the street with so much traffic. When you need your vehicle, they are very prompt of bringing it back up to the building also. 
The bell staff were very friendly also. They remembered our names throughout our whole trip, and refered to us by name each time we encountered them, which was very impressive, considering the number of people they have to greet each day.
Our room was nice. Just like the pictures on the hotel's website. Everything was clean and fresh. 
The sky pool was pretty small but clean and really all a person needs. Same goes for the hot tub.
The location is wonderful.
The roomservice was perfect.
There is a spa downstairs, a jewelry shop, a gift shop, a bar and a restaurant, so everything was very convinent. Anything you couldn't get in the hotel, was in walking distance of the hotel, and we had a blast. We went there for our honeymoon and will be returning as soon as we get the chance. We were very pleased and impressed with this hotel and would recommend it to everyone!

title: “Upper class hotel worth the money”
text: We stayed at hotel for 5 nights and throughly enjoyed our time. The staff were very courteous and professional, aswell as friendly. The check in was very easy and quick and they let us check in 2 hours early as we were very tired from travelling. Room was spacious and very clean. Bathroom was very good too. They have a town car that will drop you and pick you up as a courtesy within a 3 mile radius. The hotel is on the list of pick ups for most tour places. Has some fantastic food places around the hotel. Recommend it for business as it does have a very good conference area. Love it and will refer it to everyone. Do recommend getting onto the Omni website and signing up as a select guest, as it is free, to get free Wi-Fi and other services.

title: “Nothing to fault , first time in new york , win , win , win”
text:
I booked this hotel on the strength of the trip advisor reviews and it met expectations.
Staff very helpful , rooms compact but modern and cool , breakfast good , and internet access great.
Location also fab as it is so central.

title: “Great Customer Service”
text:
I spent a week at this hotel, and there was not a morning, nor evening, that I walked through the front door and was not greeted with a smile and a kind word from the desk clerks.
The rooms are large, comfortable, clean and fresh. The location is not far from various places to eat and shop, but at the same time, there is not a bunch of traffic noise at night to keep you awake. 
They provide anything you could possibly need, and if its not already in the room, all you have to do is ask... 
I really enjoyed my stay, and will make it my choice of hotels.. not only this location, but anywhere else I have to travel as well.

title: “Good location, with reasonable rooms”
text:
The location is 2 blocks from times square, but you walk by the major theatres to get there and there is an A-C-E subway station just outside the front doors. The rooms were very new and modern, with a great bathroom.
The hotel was reasonable but the concierge service was fantastic...by far the best service I ever received from a concierge.

title: “Is location more important than quality or value?”
text:
Hard not to like a hotel connected to not one, but two high-end malls with luxury shops, upscale dinning and an easy foot commute to the beautiful Back Bay of Boston. Of course, if room quality or bang-for-your-buck matters then location isn't about to fix any of that now is it? 
I like the open atrium feel to the lobby and mezzanine level bar/lounge (Champions Sports). Nice feel to it, modern setting that blends the best of a sports bar (TV's, sight-lines, comfort food etc.) without the closed in, loud, man-cave feel of many such places. Service was good, food was below average, drinks were above average. Starbucks is also attached, which works out well too. Pretty impressive look and feel to this area of the hotel. Unfortunately........
Rooms are smallish, bathrooms dangerously so. If I had three legs I could have put one each in the sink, toilet and tub/shower at the same time without pulling a hamstring. Bed was comfortable, TV modern, desk area workable. Like many, I was turned off by the lack of wireless internet in the room and the gross daily charge to be connected by a cable. Bush League.
The half-moon shaped landing area's of each floor may look cool but they present a challenge for elevator use; six elevators in two groups of three that are a good 20-25 feet away from each other. You need to hit the button and guess which bank will provide your lift. If you guess wrong you need to hustle over to the opposing set of elevators and hope you make it before the door closes. Easy for young folks, tougher for seniors. 
If you are staying in this area, I wool choose any number of alternative property's. Taj would be my #1 choice. If you are a Marriott person and/or need malls attached you could do a lot worse than this location.

title: “Great Location”
text:
We stayed in the Grand Hyatt in April and I would return here everytime. The rooms were a good size especially for NY and the cleanliness and service could not be faulted. Being situated at Grand
Central Station was ideal for getting round the city. Only one complaint, the buffet breakfast was way over priced so do what all the New Yorkers do grab a bagel in the lobby! Fantastic

title: “More than Pleased”
text:
This hotel was a great find. Close enough to everything and the parking lot was huge. The view from our room was great and the bed was extremely comfortable. I was impressed since the price was so very reasonable. The colours of the hotel were very vibrant--golds, reds, and blues. Definitely not your run-of-the-mill Best Western. The dining area for the complimentary breakfast was very pleasant and comfortable. 
The only complaints for the hotel is that their elevators (2) were tremendously slow and their washroom taps (shower as well as sink) don't follow the conventional turning directions (opposite from the usual direction if you want water to be colder or hotter). Oh yes, and their fitness room was extremely crappy (outdated equipment and no air ventilation for a tiny room). If you plan on exercising during your stay, this would not be the place for you.

title: “Nice, but a few issues”
text:
This was our first time in San Diego and we booked this place directly through Hilton on a December "sale" rate.
Pros:
Beautiful location right on Mission Bay
Pool and grounds are well maintained
Central to many attractions (minutes from Seaworld)
Staff was friendly
Room was clean 
There was a 'mini fridge' in the room for keeping a few drinks cold
There is an in-room small safe
Cons:
PARKING!... OMG $32/night!... no joke (for that rate there should be valet parking in a locked area...which there is not...it is simply self-parking in an unlocked area....)
Only one (nice but expensive) restaurant on site and no other options within walking distance.
Older resort is showing its age.
Very limited TV channels
No WiFi in room. WiFi was available in the lobby only.
Overall, our experience here was good. Kids liked the pool and hot tub. The hidden parking fee is a big detractor. $32/night is ridiculous and they can charge this because there are no other options nearby. Mission Bay Park has lots of parking, but there is a 'no parking' bylaw from 2am - 4am preventing anyone from over-nighting there. The fact that there is no WiFi available in the rooms kind of sucks too... It is 2012 afterall.
It was "off season", so the grounds were very quiet, which was nice, and the staff was very good.
We really only needed a place to lay our heads, so next time we come to San Diego, I am not sure that we would return to this place, especially if they don't correct the cost of the parking.
That being said, it was a nice place to relax after a busy day at the surrounding attractions.

title: “What a nice place”
text: The hotel was great. The staff was very helpful. The room was very nice and comfortable. The breakfast was one of the best. The location was fantastic.

title: “Best Buy for the area”
text: Pleasant reception, easy parking, good coffee, big room, squeaky clean, lots of nearby restaurants. What more could you possibly want?

title: “¡¡¡¡This hotel is like being at home !!!!!”
text: We enjoyed our stay in the Westin Oaks Houston Hotel. The facility is outstanding, the service too. The treasure of the hotel is the people who are kind with great understanding of our needs, always serving with a smile in their faces. Our family was deligthed and we will be back there for sure again.

title: “Good Experience With Park & Fly Option”
text: My wife and I used this hotel recently to fly out of the Indianapolis airport. We drove up late the night before our flight and then used the shuttle to the airport. The car stayed for an additional 4 nights. Hotel was nice, what little we saw since we got in so late. Room was clean, bed was extremely comfortable, front desk staff was nice. Shuttle ran on time, both to and from airport. I will note, however, that the park & fly rate was approximately equal to the basic room rate plus what airport parking would have cost, so it's not a free lunch. However, the convenience of getting a gate drop-off, etc., was worth something to us, and it more than offset the little bit of waiting/scheduling necessary for the shuttle.

title: “Great hotel and location - the real new york”
text: Stayed only 1 night for business, but from the super friendly staff to the refreshingly clean room it was great! If you opt for the penthouse (which I was udpated to) it is amazing! Roof top terrace and a great outdoor lounge area. The hotel has nicely updated its decor and is in the center of Manhattan - steps away from Grand Central Station. If you are looking for a central locale and upscale room this is the place. The bar next door and coffee shop are also great. Price was good compared to standard NYC rates. Highly recommended!

title: “Upscale hotel well worth it!”
text: Beautiful suites, extremely courteous and helpful staff. A must stay!

title: “Great stay”
text:
We had never been to Memphis, but we had stayed at the Drury 
Inn in Montgomery,Ala.so we chose to stay here not knowing anything about the area. It was a very good choice because the staff was extremely friendly and helpful. Everything was clean and convenient. The hot breakfast and evening meal was very good and was kept very well stocked. Will stay here again when we come back next year.

title: “great transportation and customer service”
text: I stayed at this location to be near Texas Children's Hospital. The transportation was wonderful. The hotel was very clean and we received great customer service. I would recommed this hotel to everyone. Staying here took a lot of the stress off of a very stressful time.

title: “Beautiful classic old-world style hotel...with a couple of glitches”
text:
We just returned from a 3-night stay at the Fairmont. We stayed in room 675, which is the older main building, not the tower. The room we booked was a queen sized bed, interior courtyard view. There is no view to speak of - you're looking at the room across from you. That was fine and I knew that when I booked the least expensive room. 
Check-in went smoothly and they were able to accomodate our early arrival time of 11 am.
The room itself was gorgeous and fairly large. The bathroom is a bit small, but nicely appointed in marble and the shower pressure is excellent. Great walk-in closet. Has the usual overpriced minibar and the dresser was kind of small if you were staying for more than 3-4 days, but the closet space more than made up for it. Very clean. The beds are the BEST I have ever experienced at any hotel (sorry Ritz Carlton!) and were so comfortable that falling asleep was effortless.
While falling asleep was effortless, actually STAYING asleep provided to be the greater challenge. The walls in the main building are paper thin and the couple in the room next to us on our first night there was having the most major of arguments, complete with things being thrown around the room and profanities abounding. We called security at midnight and things did seem to calm for awhile, but picked up again with the same behavior. We could hear everything. Granted, these people were completely inconsiderate, but even when the tenants changed the following day, we could still hear talking - so just beware that while the rooms are indeed beautiful, your conversation and activities are not completely your own.
The lobby is indeed palatial and deserving of its place in grand hotel history. Complimentary coffee was offered in the morning. We did not eat at all in the Laurel Court, although it did look quite nice.
The other hiccup in our Fairmont stay was the Tonga Room - the lower floor bar complete with fake rain, thunder and lightning. We went on Friday night for happy hour, since we had read multiple times that this is the best happy hour in the city. What a joke. The buffet is a waste at 9.95, nasty frozen egg rolls and overfried chicken wontons with salty noodles on the side. Don't even bother. We were definitely disappointed in the Tonga Room. The "thunder and rain" effects appeared super-cheesy as well - to be honest, they do a better job with that kind of thing at any Rainforest Cafe.
The staff was very friendly. Maid service was great. We requested a wake-up call our last evening there and it was promptly administered the following morning.
Location is wonderful atop of Nob Hill - really can't ask for anything more with the location of the Fairmont in San Fran. 
I'd stay there again with a couple of things I'd change now that I have firsthand knowledge. I'd spring for a room in the tower with the hope that the walls have to be thicker since it is a newer structure and I'd avoid the Tonga Room at all costs.

title: “Quite nice”
text:
We got a good deal on this hotel through Priceline, and stayed here for four nights. It's a fairly basic hotel and the decor is old school, but it is very close to the Roosevelt station, and it's only a 15 minute walk to the heart of the Loop and Millenium Park. We also really liked the free internet in the room.
Our room was on the 4th floor and had no real view to speak of. One annoying problem we encountered was on the first day there, we returned to our room at 5:15pm to find it still hadn't been cleaned. Apparently the cleaner just skipped it, but it was a little annoying.
If you do stay here, be sure to have breakfast or brunch at Yolk which is basically next door. Their Chicken Fajita Omlette is not to be missed.
All in all, the Best Western is a fine choice if you're watching your pennies in Chicago, but if you can afford better, then do it.

title: “Great property. Great staff.”
text:
Wyndham at its finest. Immaculate property and very helpful staff. A gem in San Antonio.
Property is located right on the Riverwalk. Walking distance to San Antonio's downtown attractions.

title: “We'll be back”
text: My colleage and myself stayed at the Crowne Plaza downtown Dallas and foudn it well located comfortable and teh staff were very helpful will be back to stay next time we are working in Dallas.

title: “Nice, Clean Hotel, Good Service”
text: I stayed here for 6 hours before I had to catch an early flight out. Though the shuttle was late from the airport, once I arrived at the hotel, check-in was one of the quickest I have experienced. The rooms were clean, staff nice and the bed was very comfortable. I would definitely stay again if I needed a room in the area.

title: “an over-priced flophouse”
text: I was stunned to walk into the hotel and see the nude photo right in front of me, and then a semi-phallic wallhanging to the left. The staff was pleasant, however. The elevator was barely big enough for 2 people with suitcases, and my heart sank when the door opened on the 3rd floor...8-foot ceilings, NARROW corridor, dark walls, and bizarre photo prints of some of Seattle's oddest citizens adorning each of the room doors. Our corner room with 2 double beds was extremely small, and faced the Federal Courthouse. I was dismayed to see a window air-conditioning unit instead of a more modern central air system. In order to sleep at night, we had to turn the unit on to block the street noises, but the airconditioner was so loud, even on the lowest setting, that my daughter had trouble sleeping. The bathroom had the tiniest sink I have ever seen - even smaller than the bar sink in my home! I had to contort myself to get down low enough to splash my face. The bathtub was clogged, and I had to get tell the hotel staff to fix it . They did so promptly. I was tempted to switch hotels, but the hassle factor was too great, so my daughter and I spent 2 nights at the Hotel Max, which is really a glorified flophouse despite the high price of rooms. The only good thing about this hotel is the location...6 blocks to Pike Place Market, 1 block to Nordstrom, plenty of coffee shops, etc. I would not stay here again unless the room prices were reduced to $150 a night.

title: “Nice Botique Hotel on Upper West Side”
text:
My room was very small, even by New York standards. It was well appointed, and the bed was very comfortable, as was the desk chair. There was no lounge chair, nor was there room for one. The bathroom was large, and very nice. The soap and shampoo were top quality. The lobby had free wi-fi. The free coffee in the room and lobby were top notch. The location was okay - about six blocks from the subway and twelve blocks from Lincoln Center. The price - booked directly through the web site, was very good, but a walk in who was checking in with the clerk next to mine was offered a rate that was $15 less than what I was paying. Try calling the hotel instead of using the web site and see what happens.
The smallest rooms, like the one I had, are too small for two people to occupy if you are planning to relax in the room. There are some nice public areas, however. I plan on staying here again.

title: “Amazing Stay Experience”
text: Overall this was a great stay experience. The location is great, the rooms are clean and new, the staff professional. I had never stayed at a LUXE property until this trip and am very glad I did. The location to the Staples Center was a key decision in intially selecting the hotel but the hotel turned out to be so much more than I expected for the price. I would definately stay here again and recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: “Terrible - worst hotel I have stayed at in NYC”
text:
This hotel was terrible. Rooms tiny, noise unbearable and the service poor.
The rooms are ridiculously small, and they have not panned at all. No side tables on either side of the bed, no powerpoints anywhere near the side of the bed. No powerpoints available near the desk. (I have a lot of gadgets to charge!)
The noise was terrible. We had a room facing the street, which must be a major truck thoroughfare. Trucks thundered down the street 24/7. There was also noise from the bars and restaurants across the street (but you would expect that in NYC). AC the noisiest I have ever had. Also the street noise came though the gaps in the window, I don't think there was any sound proofing at all.
Service was poor to average. Surly people on the desk, doormen who never bothered to open the door (even when you were hauling suitcases) and concierges who could not recommend a thing! My mum was charged $16 for an international phone call that didn't even connect and they told us this was standard practice!
I cannot recommend this hotel to anyone, I have stayed at much better places for a similar price. The only good thing about this hotel was the location.

title: “Big and Impersonal, but Cheap”
text: I stayed at the Double tree Hotel Mission Valley for four nights in May 2004. The hotel is adjacent to a major freeway, so it's hard to miss. It's about a 20-30 minute ride from the airport, depending on the traffic. The hotel offers a free shuttle from the airport to the hotel, but you have to call for it. The hotel offers a ride back to the hotel for $5 per person. The shuttle leaves every hour on the hour, starting at 6:00 am. The hotel is located in a office park kind of area, adjacent to a small mall (Hazard Center), and one trolley stop from the Fashion Valley Mall, which they say has the "best shopping" in San Diego. If you're from any metropolitan area, however, the mall has all of the shops you have at home. My general feeling about the hotel is that they nickel and dime you to death. They automatically give you a copy of USA Today each morning--for 50 cents--unless you tell them not to. Local calls are not free. The business center consists of some automated internet access PCs in the lobby, staffed by a coin machine, not a human being. The hotel restaurants are mediocre. The rooms themselves are a little on the large side, which was nice. The walls and doors, however, were thin, which meant I heard my neighbors all the time, as they talked or watched TV in their room, or as they walked down the hall. No high speed internet access is available in the room. The hotel is right across the street from a trolley stop (the trolley is the local light rail system), so you can take it to Qualcomm stadium, the mall, or downtown. You can even ride it all the way to the border with Mexico. I paid a group rate for my room ($110), but previous posts indicate that you can go much, much lower. The area around the hotel has a Kinkos (good substitute for a business center), a small movie theater, and even a supermarket for those on longer stays. My bottom line: if you are in the hotel for only brief periods (e.g., lots of sightseeing or business meetings), the hotel is fine. You'll be disappointed if you spend a lot of time there.

title: “Exceeded my expectations”
text:
I stayed at the Westin Galleria in early March as part of a conference. I had read some of the previous reviews on TA, and, quite frankly, I don't understand all of the negative comments. 
The lobby was nicely decorated with lots of comfortable chairs to sit in while checking email with the free wireless connection in the lobby. The check-in process was quick, and they even changed my reservation from two queen beds to one king (my preference). 
My room was on the 19th floor and was very spacious. The bathroom was a little bit small, but otherwise I had a large workspace, and two very comfortable overstuffed chairs in the sitting area. There was a magnifying mirror in the bathroom, the Westin two headed shower head, and very fluffy bath towels and a robe. All of the amenities that you would expect from a four star hotel. The "Heavenly Bed" was extremely comfy, as advertised.
The fitness center is located on the 2nd floor, in the mall area, next to the gift shop. I loved that it had 24 hour access (we had a very early start one day, and I got there at 5:15 a.m.). It was very well equipped with brand new Life-Fitness Cardio equipment, several weight machines, free weights, and various other equipment. There were plenty of towels, sanitizing wipes, and a water cooler. One of the best hotel fitness rooms I've been in (plus no extra charge to use the facilities).
The business center (also located on the 2nd floor) personnel were very helpful. The conference facilities were top notch. The catering for the event was also some of the best that I've seen. All of the conference attendees that I talked to commented on how delicious the food was. TJ in business services was very helpful resolving an equipment issue that I had.
We had dinner one night at the City Grill (just turn left from the third floor of the hotel into the mall area). The food and service were both excellent. 
The maid service was also excellent - my room was cleaned by noon both days.
I personally liked the hotel decor. I know some may not particularly like the color pallette, but that is a personal choice. 
I highly recommend the hotel for both the business traveler, and for those planning a shopping weekend.

title: “Palace Hotel - Loved It”
text:
We stayed at the Palace in October which, I later found out, is probably the best month to visit San Francisco. The weather was lovely during the day and quite mild in the evenings. The Palace is a beautiful old hotel that reminded me a bit of the Waldorf in New York City in its traditional style. But, it's not at all stodgy or stuffy. The hotel is beautifully maintained, the staff was extremely pleasant and helpful and the rooms were large, nicely furnished and comfortable. The bathroom, while not huge, was quite adequate and stocked with ample towels, wash cloths, shampoo, etc. The room was quiet and the air conditioning worked well. We got a special rate through a Starwood deal (which the reservations agent directed me to--I thought that was nice) of $300 per night plus tax. The only drawback (and this didn't really bother us because we were rarely in the room) was that the windows faced an interior courtyard and had no view except the windows of the room across from us so we were pretty much facing a blank wall. I guess if you want a view, you probably need to ask for it.
The hotel is a real party place. There were fancy parties and even a masked ball held during our stay. There is a beautiful dining room and a party room on the main floor and we often got to see people in their fancy gowns and tuxes as we left and returned to the hotel in the evenings. The dining room is also where they serve breakfast but it's pretty expensive--figure $25--$30 per person. Fortunately, there is a deli and a bakery/restaurant just a short walk down Market street where you can get breakfast for a lot less.
The hotel is really well located on the corner of Market and New Montgomery. All the trams stop right in front of the hotel. We took public transportation everywhere. There's also a BART stop nearby but the BART has kind of a limited range so we only used surface transportation. We found it really easy to take public transportation. People were really helpful when it came to giving us directions and telling us which route to take and where to transfer. The tram drivers were also very pleasant and helpful. Usually the fare is $2 per person (you need to have exact change or bills) but, because we are all seniors, we got to ride for 75 cents. If you have a car, you should know that driving in San Francisco is difficult because of all the one-way streets and lack of parking. Also, if you park at the hotel, parking is $50 per night.

title: “Great location and accommodations for a family reunion!”
text: I stayed at the Courtyard Marriott for three days and two nights. A block of rooms and a ballroom was rented for family reunion events. The rooms were a good size and contents were clean. My family enjoyed the buffet breakfasts and the comfortable bar area with tv's in several of the booths. Location was in walking distance of several shopping areas, the mall and Macy's. Since the Courtyard's bar area closed up at 11:00pm, our party went next door to the bigger Marriott's bar, which stays open until 2:00am. You have the option of valet parking or self park. We chose self-park and the hotel staff gave us directions to a self-park all day lot which is cheaper than hotel parking.

title: “Excellent hotel in an excellent location”
text:
This is a large, luxury hotel in one of the best locations in Chicago. The location, directly on MI Ave. just north of the river, is great. Shopping is so close. On a cold winter day, it isn't a hassle to walk to many MI Ave. stores.
The staff is very accommodating and was gracious enough to upgrade me (complimentary) to a junior suite because my room was not ready at check-in time. The public areas are truly elegant. They have been restored very well and at times, I felt as though I was back in the 1920's! 
The suite was great! It was in the main building versus the historic tower. I had a nice view to the east and could see a small portion of Lake Michigan. The room was very clean and updated. Bathroom is small, but well appointed & clean. Bed was very comfortable & was had great linens.
The fitness center & pool is outstanding. There is no hot tub or whirlpool, though. The only reason the value isn't 5/5 is that it is extra for internet and extra to use the business center. Very minor complaints, though.

title: “Great value in a terrific neighborhood”
text: We've stayed at the Milburn before and are pleased to see that some of the rooms have been refurbished. We called up shortly before our trip to NYC when nearly all the rooms were sold out and ended up with a room on the 1st floor (there are 2) very close to the elevator that everyone uses to go their floor. It was noisy, dark, and the a/c was not adjustable and therefore extremely cold. In addition, the water in the bathroom was lukewarm, both for the shower and the sink. After one night we requested a different room and were moved to the 11th floor and a larger, lighter room that was very comfortable for our remaining 3 day stay. Great king sized bed, lots of hot water, clean, everything worked. For those of you who don't like the continental breakfast or are there on the weekend, spend the extra $$s and go the cafe upstairs at the Fairway or go across the street to the coffee shop at the Viand. All in all, the Milburn is terrific value for the money and the rooms are much larger than most NYC hotel rooms. The neighborhood can't be beat, and this is coming from a former New Yorker who once lived around here!

title: “OUTSTANDING”
text: Everything was oustanding. The room was beautiful. The Service was extraordinary. The bar in the lobby was fantastic and attracted a great non hotel crowd. I travel quite a bit on business and pleasure and very much rank this place highly. Only negative is the price but you do indeed get what you pay for.

title: “Highly Recommend the Castle Inn Motel”
text: We just returned from a 4 night stay at the Castle Inn on our first trip to San Francisco. It was in a nice, non-tourist location. We had a nice clean room and the hotel clerk saved us a bundle on bicycle rentals. A good location for gawking at the mansions in Pacific Heights and a cheap cab ride home from Fisherman's Warf in the evening. The free parking was a great bonus. Would definitely stay there again !

title: “Great, great hotel.....!”
text: Great hotel, very clean room! The standard room is not big, but enough for the needs (sleeping, shower, WC), very comfortable bed, pillows and big plasma TV with minibar below! This hotel is for each recommendation! Anyway you did not come to New York to stay in the room all day....

title: “Comfortable.”
text: I am always excited to venture into new hotels and this hotel is no exception. The entrance is grand. The clerks could be less subtle, but luckily this clerk Ms. Kitty Mak gave me a warm greeting. She guided me through the whole reception. Wonderful service. My room felt warm. Pillows were comfortable. That's all I can ask for from a business trip.

title: “Friendly staff and a great location.”
text: This was a great family hotel. Staff was always very helpful. We had a double room which was adequate side and very comfortable. Beds were great and the room temperature was easy to regulate. Parking is expensive but it is everywhere in Washington. We could walk to all the sights and there are lots of restaurants around the hotel. Hotel was a good value. Breakfast which was included in the package we bought was good but would not want to have it more than two days in a row. It was the same every morning. Reception was nice but also might get repetitive more than two nights. Pool is small but looks larger on in the hotel photos. Would stay here again. free WIFI was a plus.

title: “Holiday Inn Select, Cherry Creek should not be selected”
text: This hotel should not be a part of family vacation. It's run down, smelly and not part of the Cherry Creek section of Denver that is upscale. It is located within walking distance of several strip clubs and there is a sex swapping club booked in the hotel on weekends.

title: “A Hidden Gem on Wasbash Avenue”
text:
This is one of the best finds that I have ever come across. This fabulous hotel is within walkin distance to State Street, Restaurants, The Theater District and the ever popular The Magnificent Mile. Upon entering the hotel you have to take an elevator to the 2nd floor lobby and it was like stepping back in time with its old world charm. The staff was very helpful. I had a Queen Size Room on the 6th floor on the back side of the hotel so it was very quiet. The rooms are very clean and simply decorated. The bathroom was very clean and spotless. Beware if you have a room on the front part of the hotel the L tends to be noisy especially if you are a light sleeper. As an added feature the hotel has a restaurant called 
Ada's. I had breakfast there and it was good and reasonably priced. I will surely be going back to SilverSmith Hotel when I go back to Chicago. Two very big thumbs up!

title: “A step back in history”
text:
We loved the Marqueen. The early 1900 design was absoluetly stunning. The staff went above and beyond to make sure our stay was good. The staff was extremely helpful in trying to find my husbands wallet after he accidently left it in a cab. They went to great lengths to help us but unfortunately were unsuccessful. It was comforting to know that strangers were still very willing to help a visitor in distress. The rooms are very large and comfortable. The hardwood floor squeaks as you walk across it, but adds to the character of the hotel. Do not stay here is you are looking for all of the modern amenities but do stay at this hotel if you are looking for a historic experience. The lobby reminded me of the Titanic with all of its grandeur. The chandliers and wood work are incredible.
The continental breakffst was sufficient as we usually ate too much the evening before. The Mexican resturant across the street and the Dueling Piano bar around the corner are both a must to experience. The king size bed was very comfortable and we found the maid service was good, with only a bit of a language barrier.
Overall, I would highly recommend this hotel if you want an experience in a turn of the century hotel. You will not be disappointed by the friendliness of the staff and the walking distance from the Seattle Center.

title: “A true love hate relationship with this property!”
text: Just had probably my 14th visit this last week. It is one of the nicest properties around and sits beautifully on a hill over looking Old Town and the bay. On a clear day you can see out to the Coronado Islands. The trade off is the staff. For business and pleasure we travel and stay in hotels over 100 nights a year. About three years ago the service here really took a dive. From us hosting an event over a weekend with about 75 room nights, to just staying ourselves for one night and everything in between... the general attitude from the front desk on up is that they are doing you a huge favor by just existing. We now limit our stay to one night a year as the place itself has huge sentimental value to our family and the location if you are visiting Old Town.

title: “Location, service, fresh and personnel”
text:
This hotel is a real treat. Most rooms have a nice view and are spacious, very clean, comfortable bedding and up to date furniture. Already at the checkin you get a good feeling. Interested, but not overly so, very profesional. After a couple of days the personnel address you by name. Concergie very helpful and easily available. Service overall is one of the best I ever experienced and I compare with a number of Leading hotels in the World. And it is not like they are indirectly asking for tips for every service they do. Solid and distinguished, yet personnel and engaged.
Breakfast is great. SPA facility very professional. Complimentary limosine service is also a good thing. Although it is very close to union square and a nice shopping area. The tram stations are very close by.
The only thing I would point out as less good, was the pool. Hotel guests have access to a fitness companies facilities but it is so huge that it is not really for relaxition but more for Olympic swimming excercise.

title: “upper west side experience.....”
text:
For my first time in new york,i was not so impressed by the hotel belleclaire,though it looked nicer in the photos..it was a so so type of hotel,,
The windows didnt close,We had to share a bathroom,with 3 other rooms...
the front desk staff acted rude at times,,If it wasnt for the concierge Peter my time would have not been good at all..
He knew everything there was to know about the new york experience,from the clothes shopping to the food even down to the night life,,,He got us free tickets to the comedy club Stand Up Ny,plus he got us in free with vip status to the "Crobar" One of the hottest night clubs in NY,,He even knew where i could find the "Soup Natzee"...Definatley made my time more fun,,He even got us to the airport in a mercedes for $60...I would return to the hotel in my next trip to ny,especially to talk to that attractive concierge

title: “Relax amongst the chaos of Los Angeles”
text:
From the moment you walk through the door of the Sofitel LA, you realize you've entered a world of quiet sophistication. I was so impressed at the quick check in and polished professionalism of the front desk staff. We were even escorted to the elevator by the check in agent. ( which requires you to slide your room key to activate--good security). Once in the room, I found it to be comfortable and relaxing. They had soft music playing and I thought that a lot of attention had been paid to lighting. It was soft and romantic, yet still had task lighting for work. The bed was amazing and I really wish I could have taken the sheets as they were of top quality. The bathroom was massive and the rainfall shower head was incredible. The restaurants on site were a little expensive but major Kudos to the hostess with the French Accent who greeted us each morning. She made you feel like you were THE most important guest in the hotel. She was just fantastic! We used the concierge one time and she was efficient and went out of her way to make sure we had dining reservations. The location of the property is amazing for shoppers, as it's directly across the street from the Beverly Center. There are over 15 restaurants of top quality that are all within walking distance. 
Congrats Sofitel- You have an amazing product with this one!

title: “Great Choice”
text: My family of four (including a 6 and 8 year old) stayed here for 5 days in late July. We had a very positive experience. The room was clean and service was efficient and unobtrusive. The gym is presently being redone, but all of the equipment is available in carpeted conference rooms on the 4th floor and this should be done in August. The pool was great for San Francisco hotels, with a large hot tub. The hotel atrium restaurant was actually a pleasant surprise—the service quick, food good and prices comparable to other local places. I found the location of the hotel to be good, mainly due to proximity to the excellent public transportation in the city. There is a Whole Foods supermarket that has prepared food 3 blocks away; the cable car and Union Square are equally close. I would strongly urge travellers to familiarize themselves with the public transportation before going—we did not have a car and felt no need to have one. You can easily and cheaply get to all attractions with public transportation (including an inexpensive trip to the airport on BART with a station a half block from the hotel). For example, we took the trolly bus (# 30 or 46 both work) to a Giants game for $4 for the 4 of us. AT&T Park is about 7 blocks from the hotel. A cab from the airport is $35 before tip. My only complaint is that some parts of the surrounding neighborhood is a little rough around the edges, with more homeless people than I am accustomed to similar areas in Philadelphia or New York. I never felt threatened, but this did come as a surprise to me. Overall, I would definitely return.

title: “Beautiful Hotel that paid attention to every detail!”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Sofitel for three days and from the moment we arrived we were treated with the utmost consideration. Without even asking we received a free upgrade, had truffles and bottled Evian delivered to our room (For no apparent reason) and for our room service breakfast had a basket of fresh French pastries added at no charge. Furthermore, the room was beautiful! The bathroom was spacious and lovely, the bed was more comfortable than the beds at The Ritz Carlton, and the room was impeccably clean. Every employee was knowledgeable, friendly, and took the time to help out with every detail. We enjoyed staying at the Sofitel immensely and will surely be staying there next time we travel.

title: “Great Location...not up to Westin Standards”
text: This is my second visit to the Westin at Copley and I must express my disappointment in the rooms. The bathroom ceiling vent was so full of dust and dirt, it was disqusting. The room was so hot that we had to have the window open to sleep ( air conditioning not working) and the desk outlets were not working for the computer. After looking under the desk we found the wires were cut and never repaired. As a starwood preferred guest I decided to stay at the Westin over the Marriott where the conference was being held but realized what a mistake that was.

title: “well located at Fishermans Wharf”
text:
We arrived early, that wasnt a problem we were checked in right away and given the choice of rooms on high or low floor. We chose high (its only 4 floors) for the view and had read that ground floor rooms are noisy.
The room was 2 queen beds which were comfortable, there was plenty of room, the bathroom was a bit dated.Glad to have tea and coffee making facilities.
The price includes continental breakfast but you can pay for extras, the restaurant staff are helpful and efficient.
The hotel best feature is its location right on Fishermans wharf near tram stop and within easy walk of the historic boatyard, pier 39 and the pier to get the boat to alcatraz. The hotel also has a deal with the bike hire company and gives vouchers for free bike hire which was good, we rode across the golden gate to saualito, and got the ferry back. Sausalito is lovely well worth a visit
A must do, s the Alcatraz trip, well worth every penny, book in advance
plenty of restaurants nearby, we recommend Bobos which the valet suggested, and the Harris Steakhouse
There is wine tasting at 4.30 until 6, this isnt really tasting, its an opportunity to congregate in the lobby and drink the red or white wine, which was very good. Local wine. You may refil as much as you want.
The thing that worried me about this hotel was the fact it allows animals. we saw a dog, however, there was no sign at all of an pet hairs in our room which we wouldnt have liked. Nor did the rooms smell of animals so wasnt an issue
All the staff were helpful and polite

title: “Great Hotel”
text: My husband, four year old daughter and I stayed in this hotel during a recent trip to DC. I was very impressed with how accomodating the staff were. They were friendly, and housekeeping even gave us a tour of the penthouse suite which was on our floor (very nice!!!!) The location is great. It is actually right across from the Williard hotel. There is a food court, mall and metro one block away. A Starbucks is in the lobby, and the hotel is attached to the National Theater. It was an easy walk to the Old Post office, Smithsonian museums, Mall and White House. The room was very nice, clean and spacious. I would definitely stay here again, especially since I got such a great rate on Priceline. I bid $180/ night for the room and got it. For the money, it is a nice hotel for touring.

title: “Charming, clean, and great staff”
text:
My boyfriend and I stayed at the Hotel Boheme in the middle of January. Upon arrival we were a little skeptical as the doorway is slightly hidden between an Italian restaurant and coffee bar/bakery. As soon as we walked in we received a very warm welcome, a map of the area, and an invitation to a glass of nightly Sherry. Sitting in the entry way is a book of historical newspaper clippings and articles about some of the famous people from the Beat generation and the surrounding San Francisco area. 
When we walked into our room we were slightly taken back by the size (small) of the room. The bed had one of those mesquito netting things hanging over top of it, which we continue to joke about now. After our initial shock we began to love our cute little hotel centered in the middle of a great Italian neighborhood and in walking distance of nearly every attraction. You really couldn't ask for a better location.
The staff was superb, you will know them by first name after a day of staying. You are provided a key to the front door so each night you return it is almost as if you were staying with a family member or friend. 
We fell in love with this hotel and are very pleased we stayed at The Boheme. Only one word of caution...it is a very quite hotel, this may be a blessing or in some few cases, a curse.

title: “Recommended”
text:
I liked The James quite a bit. The rooms are smallish, but not insanely so, and well laid out, and the bathrooms are very nice. The housekeeping is very friendly, but a little spacy (I had to call to have them come clean the room once). All the staff is VERY VERY nice and helpful, though -- especially the door men. The hotel has free wine and cheese in the afternoon, and BEST OF ALL: free coffee and pastries in the morning! Which is excellent if you're there for work and don't have time for a proper breakfast. The bed is VERY comfy and the location is great. You will like it,
Note: I was there on business, and the James inadvertently screwed up my bill (they charged the room to my personal card rather than to the company). They fixed this promptly and cheerfully -- I am very happy with the way the mistake (an honest one) was handled.

title: “Such History”
text: Was there last week (Dec 2012) for three nights and what can I say...a magnificent hotel with such history. All staff were fantastic - both personable and professional. Breakfast was really nice (bircher muesli was yummm)...and the location perfect for me - the shops a walk down Mason street in one direction and Fisherman's Warf a walk in the opposite direction...easy. I now know why people from SFO have such muscular legs with so many hills. I loved my room on the 16th floor and had such a good view overlooking SFO. The bed was sooo comfortable and I slept very well. I would definitely stay at the Fairmont again.

title: “Great hotel”
text: We decided to take a few days and head to Washington D.C. with the kids(3 under the age of 10). We booked this hyotel through priceline(nyop) and recieved a great deal. Checked online and saw the valet parking was much like everywhere else in DC, expensive. Located a parking garage on Desales St next tot he hotel and parked there for less than half the cost. We arrived well before check-in time and the room was not available yet. We requested 2 double beds and it was fulfilled. The front desk staff was great and took my cellphone number to call when the room was ready. We headed out to the mall and recioeved a phone call about an hour later letting us know the room was ready. We came back to the hotel prior to dinner and went to out room. The room had a spcous bathroom and the three kids were able to sleep on the double bed. The room was clean and all the staff members we encoutered were very friendly. The concierge was helpful with restaurant recommendations. The Mayflower is located in a great location with easy access to the Farragut North and Farragut West metro lines. There is also a bus stop near by. There were restaurants a few blocks north. The lobby was beautiful and clean with complimentary drinks. Definitely a great hotel to stay in.

title: “Ups and Downs at the Sheraton”
text: Hotel is clean, modern and centrally located in Dallas. We booked through Priceline for $35 on a Sunday night, paid to upgrade to a Junior Suite when we arrived and we received a room adjacent to the elevator shaft. Since the parking lot was only one-quarter full and we saw only one other guest, we did not think it to be a problem. WRONG. We heard noise from the elevators all night. If we had paid rack rate, then we would have definitely asked to be moved. No parking fee was nice.

title: “Great place with a rooftop hangout”
text:
The Pod is a great place to stay. Their rooms are not "roomy" , but they are extremely functional and perfect for the price. We stayed in a bunk bed room, which was extremely small but fun. Each bed has its own TV. There was also a sink with bath towels and a small desk. Above the door, there is an display that indicates which bathrooms are available - this makes shower/restroom trips extremely convenient. The hotel has a trendy vibe to it (think "Ikea"), but its not the slightest bit prentencious. Guests ranged from European backpackers, hip 20 somethings, to grandparents. 
The staff was friendly and helpful. The free wi-fi is a plus - you have to contact the front desk to get a user-name/password.
The rooftop is amazing, but a little tricky to find (only one of the stairwells has rooftop access). Its a great place to hangout and take in a view of New York City. 
For food, there are a couple of take out cafe's/cafeterias and a McDonald's that are a block away.
Location, two blocks away from subways (which was great since we took the airTrain and the subway into the city for about $7!).

title: “Well worth staying here”
text: This is a very good hotel for the money: close to Beale Street and the River, it's easy to walk everywhere; the breakfast buffet is excellent; the rooms are absolutely fine (even with two children in there too); and the staff are friendly enough. There is noise at night (so take earplugs), but what else would you expect in a busy city centre? We really enjoyed Memphis, and the more so, because the hotel was very good value for money.

title: “wouldn't stay again, but great location”
text:
Fantastic location, but NOISY! 
I was here for a three night stay for business. Walls and doors are paper thin! Many disruptions throughtout the stay. Small rooms, decently appointed.
Had plenty of hot water, but had no bathmat or washcloths for first two nights. Fees for internet in rooms, though free in lobby... when we pay this much for rooms, internet should be included! Front desk staff was difficult and unpleasant, but some of the best doormen I've encountered in the city.
My recommendation: spend a little more and stay at a hotel that has good service with decent ammenities. I will not return.

title: “Great location, nice hotel”
text: Nicely updated, comfortable, quiet & convenient. Right on the 16th Street Mall, you can walk, ride the free shuttle or catch the light rail to get around. Bar-eatery and Starbucks off the lobby, retail, convenient stores, restaurants and museums on the mall. Good value.

title: “Fabulous Stay - Great Location - Helpful and nice staff”
text:
We stayed a weekend at TheWit and truly loved it. The hotel is modern and trendy, but not snobby or pretentious. 
The room was modern and clean. We chose a corner room with floor to ceiling windows - which provided nice views. The room was very quiet and we never heard any outside or hotel noise. Another nice feature - rare these days, one window opens a bit - for fresh air. 
The location of the hotel simply could not be better. We parked the car and took public transportation to Michigan Ave, Museums, Willis Tower and restaurants. The hotel is located one block off of the river and a few blocks from Millennium park and is near the best coffee shop ever, Intelligentsia. 
The Gilchrist and Soames bathroom amenities were a nice surprise and we opted for the Spa Bathroom with the extra large modern tub. It was so worth it and the most unexpected detail. The beds were very comfortable and we both slept well. 
As an extra bonus, hotel guests receive free cover to the exclusive club, ROOF - located, yes, on the roof of the hotel. It provided spectacular views and even though it was a little young and showy, but the view makes it worth a visit, even if you are under-dressed! In the warmer months, they have a outdoor area that looked stunning. 
The restaurant in the hotel was okay - breakfast was the better of the meals. The staff, in all areas, were stellar. Each person we encountered was kind, courteous, and seemed genuinely interested in making our stay terrific. We felt like we were king and queen for the weekend at this hotel - something I have never said or felt anywhere else, including a few 5 star hotels. 
The only possible complaint would be the parking, which was expensive, but not out of line for downtown Chicago. And there are inexpensive parking alternatives if you are willing to walk a few blocks. 
We will definitely return to TheWit for the staff, quality, location, and gemütlichkeit, if you know what that means. Happy Travels.

title: “New York Experienced like no others”
text:
We have been going to the Four Seasons New York for years, and despite the fact we have tried or visited other properties like St-Regis, Peninsula, Mandarin, Warwick, The Palace, Gansevoort, etc... we still go back to the Four Seasons and love it each time. Getting into the vast lobby is a very relaxing harbour from the city buzz yet it is itself a vibrant place with our favorite place... the Ty Lounge. Darrin Fitzgerald is the most welcoming at the lounge and been there for years, remembers every guest with impressive level of detail. He makes a special "Sage Cosmo" that is only available in the fall and not on their menu but is just great. He also is an actor and writer, so that gives you a feeling for the quality and depth of the staff there looking out for you. 
The rooms are all spacious, you can get almost any of them and enjoy the experience just as much. We tried all of them but the super Ty Suite on the top which we have never seen. Some of them are stunning, but they are all great rooms. Concierge service is very helpful, always available and frankly all the staff there is great and helpful but never in the way of the experience they want you to enjoy.
Location is also phenomenal. You will be out of the 5th avenue zoo feeling, but so close you can walk to it in 2 minutes. We like to go on Madison and walk up the cafes and boutiques up to the Carlyle which we love for a late afternoon cocktail. The 4S NY is dead center, close to museums, Broadway shows, shops, restaurants, central park, short distance from the financial district and the views from the rooms on high floors are breath taking from either side.
Some hotels are expensive but they don't deliver. The 4S NY delivers. You cannot go wrong going there.

title: “Relaxing girls weekend”
text:
La Cantera was the perfect place for our girls trip. We spent an entire day at the Adults only pool and it was exactly what we wanted. Beautiful views, a clean and relaxing pool, and wonderful poolside service. 
The rooms were wonderful as well - the beds were very comfortable, the shower heads were great, and everything was clean. I also appreciated having a air purifier in the room.
All of us agree that we would love to return with our husbands - it seems like a great place for couples.

title: “Good location for a short break”
text:
OK so it's not the most modern of hotels some of the decor is a little tired but the room sizes are good and the location is good, the staff were excellent, it does have the ability to get a little busy as there's a lot of conventions at the hotel but the location makes up for it.
The subway is about a block away (less than 500m), if your from the UK you won't mind walking so Rockfeller, Times Square and the Central Park are all In easy walking distance, we were on the 41st floor so qualified for the access to the executive lounge with complimentary breakfast / afternoon tea and wifi. It's a nice bonus and the room has a great view down Av of the Americas while your having your breakfast.
In summary it's a nice above mid range hotel with good location - if in need of a little attention - but certainly not something to worry about.

title: “Pleasantly satisfied!”
text:
Following the tripadvisor band wagon, we decided to give the Sofitel a try. We booked an Executive suite on the 24th floor. It had a HUGE outdoor terrace with some patio furniture. (Yes, there was snow and it served as an excellent refrigerator!) The room was big,beautiful and the bed was divine! The bathroom and shower were quite nice, complete with first rate toietries. Only downfall was the smallish closets.
The service was friendly and great. 
Most of the concierge team seemed a little too serious but were helpful. (Erick was great and nice)
We never ate at the hotel, however, we did go visit the Red Flame diner and thought it was good for the price. We did stumble upon a Scottish restaurant named St. Andrews right down the street. What a find! Some of the best food we ever had. (and we dine pretty frequently!) By all means, try this place out. (no, I don't own, or work at the restaurant!)
Overall, I think what we appreciated the most was the beautiful rooms and the subtleness of the hotel and it's elegance.

title: “Can't say enough nice things about this hotel”
text:
We were headed to the city to catch a couple of Broadway shows, and were hoping to stay near Times Square, if at all possible. After realizing that all of the hotels in Time Square were well out of our price range, I found the Westin. Not cheap by any means, in fact, I'd stack it up against any of the Times Square hotels for amenities and comfort. But the price was significantly better, all for a room a whole whopping block away. 
The value for the location isn't even half the story, though. The staff at the Westin was freaking fantastic. It was our first visit, but they treated us as though we had been staying there for years. They remembered our name, and, on several occasions, went out of their way to make sure we were having the best possible stay.
Suffice it to say, this trip moved Westin to the top of my list for hotel choices.

title: “Nice but no sleep”
text:
My experience is based on a short stay during mid-week for a business trip.
First of all the Pacific Heights area is really residential, quiet and old world elegant. There are many absolutely gorgeous homes in the surrounding area. One can see the water views standing on the street corner outside. With that said, if you are the typical tourist, it's really not that close to any touristy spots. I would venture to guess that Union Square is a good 25 minutes walk (up and down steep hills, btw), as is Fisherman's Pier. It's not convenient to any of the trolley stops either. There's a complimentary car service to Union Square in the morning, but the rest of the time you have to find your own transportation.
The decoration of the room is tasteful and elegant. Very comfortable bed but very stiff robe and slippers for some reason (need fabric softener!). 
Secondly, I don't know if it's the location of my room, but starting from 6AM I can hear my neighbor walking in his room, getting ready in the morning. The floor board creaks mercilessly and sounded like a herd of elephants stampeding. Needless to say I got no sleep from that point on. 
Third, there is no central A/C or heat. A/C may not be a problem since S.F. doesn't get that hot in the summer, but the kicker is that when the radiator turned on at 7AM in the morning it gave out such loud pinging noises that I thought someone was doing remodeling work next door.
The breakfast, although touted as gourmet, was nothing to write home about. It's the basic starch, plus boiled eggs, although set in a very elegant dining area.
The service was outstanding. The receptionist was very helpful and friendly without being intrusive. I was impressed when they called and paid for a taxi cab ride when the complimentary ride was running late. 
I think in sum this is a great place if you want efficient and friendly service, great for a romantic weekend getaway but I would advise bringing your own car to get around town and a set of earplugs to handle the noise problems (due to the old building's infrastructure).

title: “Reliable choice with usual Courtyard comforts”
text:
Just returned from 4 nights at the Courtyard on Broaday while attending a conference. This building's a converted bank, and offers solid walls and a decent location as well as all the usual Courtyard amenities (free wired & wireless internet, guest laundry, helpful staff etc.).
It's a 20' walk to the conference centre, but you can walk through the Gaslight Quarter, which is nice. 
There's a 7-11 on the corner of the same block, and I recommend the 'Brooklyn Pizza' restaurant on the other corner especially for a quick take-aways - this has a proper pizza oven and the staff are friendly and helpful.
It's a pleasant 25' walk north on 6th Avenue to Balboa Park for the museums and galleries, and a lot of buses run along Broadway, so travel anywhere in the city is quite easy.

title: “Good Location, with a few drawbacks”
text: I stayed at this hotel for two nights while visiting Chicago on business in September 2007. The location is excellent being between the financial district and the Magnificent Mile. However, the elevators simply do not work properly, and it is not the place to stay should you need to get to and from your room quickly or frequently. I saw several customers have trouble getting to their rooms, and the front desk staff were nonchalant, and would not even allow customers to take the stairs. (This is obviously a persistent problem.) Nevertheless, it is probably good value for your money, and in a good location.

title: “Nice Old Hotel”
text:
The lobby in this old hotel is beautiful and is a great way to begin your stay. Unfortunately, they've filled the lobby with bar tables in place of the quiet classical music of a couple years ago. Do not book this hotel through an internet agency - they have very very small rooms for those who pay lower internet rates. Book the hotel through Hilton, and specify a large room. 
The location isn't bad for the loop area, but its a bit of a walk to the North Michigan area. This is the perfect hotel for CTA availablilty - the elevated is available at the Wabash entrance, and the Red line is available at the State Street Entrance. If you do not use the valet parking, there will be very little room to leave your car while checking in - and they bell hop will be very upset with you.

title: “A Welcomed British surprise!”
text:
I booked the Edgewater Hotel because it had good reviews, and met the requirements for my wife's' happiness: Be on the water or a view of it, and have a fireplace. 
It also provided a close location for the Opera we were attending that night for my wife birthday
Our arrival was met with friendly valet and check-in staff. 
Upon arrival they notified me I had be complimentary upgraded to the Beatles Suite -- now, mind you, I didn't even know what they were talking about. When they told me the history I thought, "huh, this should be pretty cool."
Man. It was AWESOME. The room is HUGE. Decked out in Red and White and wooden decor. Little did I know my wife's affinity for British style and the Beatles. Having the Beatles pictures, books and memorabilia made the stay totally unreal.
Icing on the cake - a CD with all their hits to listen to as we lounges in the spacious room.
The room was immaculate (and my wife is very meticulous) comfortable and cozy with a shower and a large bear-claw tub (ah-yeah).
The restaurant was great - a spectacular view of the sunset, great service and delicious food. At night, I stopped in for a bit and it was a lively and fun atmosphere.
My only regret is that with our planned night out, we didn't have time to enjoy the room and hotel as much as we could have. The next time, the hotel will be the destination. Period.
We had a great time and really did not want to leave.

title: “Great location, great value”
text:
Just got back from spending 6 nights at the Amsterdam Court Hotel. Having read some of the reviews other travellers had posted about the hotel, we were a little anxious about what we might find. However, we were more than pleasantly surprised! 
The lobby and bar were attractive and stylish, and the staff helpful and pleasant. OK - so our double room was not huge, but it was plenty large enough for a couple, and had plenty of wardrobe space and drawers and also a desk. It was nicely (and fairly recently) decorated, and was really clean. The bathroom was again quite small, but well set out and seemed to have been fairly newly updated. The shower was powerful and hot. Our room was cleaned to a really high standard and replenished with clean towels every day. Overall, we were really pleased with both our room and the hotel in general. There is some decorating work being done in some of the hallways, but this did not pose any problems at all. The main advantage of this hotel is the location - it is perfect if you want to be in the thick of things! Times Square and Broadway are just around the corner, but you can (and we did!) walk to lots of other attractions from here including ESB, Central Park, MOMA, Natural History Museum, Guggenheim etc.
I will definitely be recommending this hotel to others visiting NY - its is affordable, pleasant and ideally located.
Hope this helps other travellers - enjoy your trip!

title: “Respectable value for a midtown hotel”
text:
Our visit to midtown/theater district was centered around seeing Broadway shows and dining at Patsy's & at the Oyster Bar in Grand Central Station. The Hotel Mela was a convenient home base for the trip. 
It is walking distance to the theater district and to Grand Central. While our room was small, we've stayed in smaller places in Manhattan that were not as well kept, and we experienced excellent service from the hotel. We booked through a link on travelzoo, which gave us a $200/night rate & included a welcome gift. Check-in/out was a breeze with their polite and efficient staff. 
There were no issues with the cleanliness of the hotel, noise from the surrounding area or inside the hotel. The small rooms are attractively furnished, with comfortable bedding. You can get a good night's sleep in this hotel. 
While certainly not a luxury hotel, the Mela is a fine option for the frugal visitor to Manhattan. Centrally located, it's a stylish "middle class" hotel. 
For those who come to midtown with a car, there is a Hippodrome garage just a block east of the Mela that gives you 12 hours overnight for $12. A much better value than the $40+ a night for the garage adjacent to the hotel entrance... FYI

title: “Noel - he's the man!”
text:
