CSH ticked all the boxes we wanted after extensive research on the internet: a bit of luxury, a bit classy, a bit trendy, location perfect (definitely better than the numerous Midtown options for the real NYC), and the chance of a view. 
It didn't let us down on any front either. There was plenty of trepidation, wondering if we'd made the right choice from the huge number and variety of hotels on offer in NYC. We arrived rather dishevelled, with a start-of-honeymoon argument in progress after a delayed flight from London, and were immediately put at our ease by Concierge and professional top bloke, Noel, with a glass of gratis bubbly.
No need for War and Peace - the CSH was everything we wanted, the right vibe, the right area (for great bars, restaurants and shops), exellent rooms (the Cooper 3 was spacious-feeling - fairly unusual for this price in this city, I'm told), extremely comfy bed, superb view downtown, and very welcoming staff.
Finally, I've always wondered what a concierge actually does, but Noel was superb; a font of good tips about the city, and an affable manner that made my wife want to take him home with us. So we did! Erm, not really.

title: “was I in a submarine...there are cute doors to the rooms in this hotel”
text:
After arriving form Dublin and enduring a long delay at airport to see a long queue at reception desk in hotel was almost the last straw. No that was left to the unsmiling desk staff , has anyone ever heard of customer service in this hotel . No fridge in room and when I requested one I was told that would be fine provided I paid 20 dollars , another near arguement and they relented I got my fridge which was really great as the air conditionong was like behaving like an orchestra. Do not buy a ticket from the tourist desk within this hotel , we were charged 145 dollars for a 72 dollar seat for Mama Mia show on Broadway.
The cleaning staff are lovely and do a good job on the rooms.

title: “We liked the value and service”
text:
My wife and I were here for a weekend getaway. We both liked the quality of the hotel for the price. The room size was appropriate -- not huge, but not tiny either -- and we appreciated the quality of the fixtures and appliances. (She is an architect and can recognize very old stuff or shoddy workmanship, but these rooms were well designed.)
We also liked the service level and attention to detail by the staff. The restuarant/bar was fun and easy-going, though like all hotel food/drinks it's something that you should only do if you want to splurge on your budget.
The hotel is 5-10 minutes from the Dupont Circle Metro station. Of course it would have been nicer if the station was right there, but it wasn't a major incovenience to do the walk, and there are plenty of restaurants and stores along the way on Connecticut Ave.
We would stay here again.

title: “Very good hotel”
text:
We stayed at Morgans in November and really enjoyed our stay. The hotel is well-located, welcoming and comfortable. We upgraded to a one-bedroom suite and really enjoyed the additional space. The rooms seem to have been modernised recently and the bed was exceptionally comfortable, although if we were being picky the bathroom was a little disappointing for a hotel of this standard
The hotel has many features which make it stand out compared to others in New York. The free continental breakfast is unusual for New York and was a real benefit. The Living Room was also a nice extra, while the staff were exceptionally friendly and the relatively small size of the hotel meant you got the know them over the time you were there.
Perhaps because of the closure of the Asia de Cuba restaurant, the hotel seems quite low-key and doesn't have the buzz of its sister hotels like St Martin's Lane. That didn't bother us though and we would not hesistate to recommend the hotel.

title: “Marriott is a good consistent chain”
text:
This is likely one of Marriott's higher end hotels because of the location and I think it should get 3.5 stars but that's not an option--therefore I've given 4. 
In general, Marriott is like the Sheraton, in my view, in that they are chains that have consistent service and quality and this is a good thing. You know what to expect. 
Specifically, this was my third stay in as many years at this particular hotel and for a conference each time. The rooms are clean and comfortable and well-maintained, as well as are the common areas. At the same time though the rooms and the meeting area restrooms are a little worn. It's easy to overlook this considering the cleanliness and the staff attentiveness and pleasantness. 
I prefer smaller, boutique-like hotels, but I was pleased with my stay at this hotel most recently and in the past two years.

title: “Nice stay”
text: Booked a room here at the last minute. Have stayed in other nearby hotels before so i decided to give this one a try. The front desk staff was very friendly and helpful. Room was clean and quite nice. However, not sure if the room above mine had hardwood floors or not, but it sure sounded like it. Could hear the sound of high heels all night as if i were in the room with them. Parking wasn't cheap but hotel parking in SF is generally high anyway. Stayed 2 nights and used room service twice. Breakfast was good but order taker was just so so. Probably won't use room service again but if i have to, at least the sevice is prompt. The surrounding area is nice and has everything you might need. I'd stay there again since the overall service is very good.

title: “Great Location, Great Hotel!”
text:
Stayed here in July 2011 for a week. Mother and daughter trip. We had a great time and LOVED this hotel. To begin, it is in a great location. Everything in Boston is basically walking distance, but this hotel was right in the middle of everything. A short walk to exceptional restaurants and shops. The rooms are classic in design, so do not think you'll get something ultra-modern. My one complaint was that the bathroom in our superior double was very tight. For me this was not a problem but if you are a bit taller or wider, it would be.
I particularly enjoyed the bananas and tea/coffee in the morning and the afternoon cookies with iced tea! The spring water they put in your fridge is so refreshing after running around the city. The staff was informative, polite and professional. 
The hotel itself has so much history to it. I loved the elevators, the old school charm in the hallways and the little displays outside the elevators including letterhead from years gone by and photos of a transforming Boston.
I was inspired to write this review now, because a year later mother and daughter are returning to Boston for a weekend and would not stay anywhere else! Back to the Lenox we go!

title: “Unprofessional staff, Dirty dinning room, Bugs, NOISY!”
text:
Just take it from my title, it says it all. Corporate office of Best Western could care less about complaints. 
Rooms were nice looking but the walls are VERY thin. Breakfast was unkept and dirty. Staff was horrible. Management suggested that I confront a noisy room next to mine at 4 am.
I suggest you look into the other hotels near by. 
My complaints are real. I have documentation to prove it, I gave Best Western a chance to make good on my complaint and they didn't.

title: “wonderful glamourous stay”
text: Lovely hotel which is well known in Chicago for its great visitors Oscar Wilde or Mark Twain.The atmosphere is just unbelievable !You have the impression you jumped back in time...in the middle if the twenties.Service is great...swimming pool lovely...the hall and bar a gem...The perfect place to impress!Will recommend it.Restaurant food is overpriced but good...and it is quite difficult to eat well in Chicago...so if you are desperate just go and eat there.

title: “Wonderful Hotel!”
text: We really enjoyed our anniversary night downtown Detroit. We were there for a wedding and wanted to be in the center of the city. The room was beautiful and I really enjoyed the shower and bathroom area. There were drinks, ( coffee and tea ) in the greeting area of the hotel. Everyone was very helpful. My husband enjoyed the spa and had a massage as I played in the casino before our function. We had drinks in the nearby Sports Bar and enjoyed that. We also had a wonderful room service breakfast as we lounged around the next day. They were kind enough to give us a later check out. The hotel is right in the middle of everything and a good place to stay if you are going to Detroit.

title: “Great location and central to everything San Francisco has to offer”
text: We were received by a warm and quick welcome. The rooms are old with little room to move, but is presented professionally and has all you expect from a good hotel. The restaurant is fantastic. You get silver service and treated really well. The prices are great too and the meals are prepared to perfection. Its a great hotel for those on a budget who expect a liitle more.

title: “Worst La Quinta”
text: Price quoted on web was way less than at check in. No luggage carrier. Shower knob came off in hand, shower head almost came off wall. Older rooms, small. Would never stay there again even if it was free.

title: “Very comfy beds”
text: A very clean and friendly hotel, but overall the best experience during my stay was the beds. They were extremely comfy and i would definitely come back!

title: “Good hotel in nice location”
text: This is a hotel a little outside of Indianapolis (about 30 minutes from the airport), however, nicely located in the neighborhood of a shopping mall with several high end stores. The hotel itself is a quiet hotel with good access to the highway 465. Nicely located concierge lounge on the 11th floor. Running path around a lake directly next to the hotel.

title: “The Perfect Stay”
text: This was the ideal boutique experience with the benefit of Starwood points! The hotel is ideally nestled amongst some of the best restaurants in town and conveniently distanced from all of my favorite neighborhoods and retail that are MUST HIT types of spots. The rooms are spacious, the hotel stylish and clean, and the hotel staff was amazing- the maid even wrote me a thank you note for her tip!!! Since I am a creature of habit when I travel (which is often) this is my new favorite hotel. I'll be back over and over again. Thank you!

title: “Excellent Service”
text: Had a great stay. Holly at the front desk was absolutely wonderful to us. Holly and the rest of the staff were always willing to help.

title: “Great anniversary weekend”
text: We checked in on sat July 2 and everyone on the staff was very friendly.. Kelley the hotel manager went out of her way to make us feel welcome.The room was very clean and comfortable. We had a most enjoyable stay.

title: “Enjoyable stay”
text:
Just back today from 5 nights @ dream... I was very wary about my stay after reading reviews of this site. It just takes some planning to have a great stay. Book a large room with a king size bed, ring ahead to specify smoking or non... Staff are fantastic, very heplful with lots of local tips, concierge was a gift.. As for the rooms themselves, never used the heating once and considering it was -15c while I was there the room never got cold so i dont know what people r talking about (turned the heater on once n it does make a racket but u'll never need it) The beds are from heaven, I cannot tell you how unreal they are!!! Location is fantastic... Would have no problems in recomending Dream...
To make the hotel perfect I would add the i-pods, a dvd player, more channels on the tv and a bigger bath(i'm 6'3" and after 2 days of walking all i wanted was a bath but couldn't fit in..)

title: “I would recommend this hotel”
text: The site of the hotel shows exactly what it's. Very convenient located one block from Dupont Circle. Comfortables and very clean room. Staff very kind.

title: “Fabulous stay in Chcago!”
text: My husband and I went to Chicago with our two kids ( age 7 and 4) and whenever possible stay at extended stay properties like RI or Homewood Suites etc... We love the extra room and free breakfast/reception I booked the trip for a Mon-Thurs stay and got a rate of $179 including valet parking which in Chicago is pricey. The room type I reserved was a King suite. We arrived and instantly loved the property and the area. The staff greeted us warmly and I was impressed with the lobby area. Our room was ready and immaculate. The king suites have a full kitchen - so great for bringing drinks, snacks, heating or reheating things. The bedroom was separate from the sitting area and has it's own tv. (a must have with kids!). The bathroom was spacious and very clean. We went to breakfast every morning - wide array of food offered and well attended to. It was crowded but that's to be expected. The managers reception were great with full meals provided and free wine/beer/soda. We didn't eat there but took some food back to the room. The staff was amazing -- I did not encounter one person without a smile or who was not willing to help. We have stayed at another RI in Chicago and the Homewood Suites but this was the best hotel of the three and would definitely stay again. ($179 with parking/free breakfast AND dinner in Chicago - best deal I've found in a long time!)

title: “Convention Stay...”
text: Went to D.C. for an annual convention. My first visit!!! I promise I can NOT say enough positive things about this hotel and my D.C. experience. A couple of my bffs had arrived two days prior so the front desk staff was expecting me, they were extremely cordial and accomodating. I felt almost whisked away. The Starbucks in the lobby was right up my alley, as were the large water dispensers in the lobby with oranges in one and lemons in the other, nice touch especially in the July heat. The rooms were nice, modern and spacious. Housekeeping was very accomodating, one of my girlfriends has strange towel requests! I ordered coffee and a croissant via room service almost every morning and I would always receive a weather report from the delivery person! I think what I loved MOST about this hotel was it's location and how we could walk any and everywhere (and we did)! This was a great, memorable trip and I would recommend this hotel to anyone!

title: “Fine for a single person short stay”
text:
Attended a convention at Moscone Center and The Mosser was conveniently close by a block. Easy BART access from both SFO or OAK since the Powell station is half a block away. Loved the central Market St and Union Sq locale. Adjacent to the much pricier Kimpton and Marriott hotels. Overall the age, ambiance and size of rooms reminded me of those old Ivy League college dorms ... shared baths, narrow halls, creaky narrow stairs, slow elevators and cool urban vibe.
Desk staff were all very friendly and helpful. Housekeeping kept the place tidy although the beige and brown checkered carpet throughout made the place feel dated. Furniture also showing some wear. This place is a step above a hostel.
The Deluxe Queen I reserved was the size of my children's bedroom at home. Smallest hotel room I've ever slept in. If my spouse joined me we would have found it too cramped. Barely enough room for the queen platform bed and one easy chair by the bay window that overlooked the small side street. 
Happy I reserved a private bath. Good sized soaking tub and shower. But smallest sink ever .... just like a tiny sink in a camping RV. Couldn't wash my face without dripping water onto the floor. Had to be careful when brushing my teeth.
Room itself was well insulated from street noise. I was in room 609 and only heard the AM trash truck. 
There is no air conditioning but opening the single window and activating the ceiling fan permitted sufficient air. Doing so allowed in lots of street noise unfortunately.
Would I return? Yes if I was traveling alone and looking for rate under $200 in downtown SF near a central BART station. Its an adventurous hotel to try if you're willing to give up space and certain conveniences like a gym, pool, and large public lobby.

title: “Definitely not exemplary of the brand”
text: I read below someone had called this hotel "not a good example of the brand". I wish I had read that before I booked here because that describes this hotel to a T. The one bedroom "suite" is actually a studio, though it's large, it's misrepresented. Just like the tennis court- which is a laughable tenth of the size of a tennis court. Completely unusable. The pool is murky, the laundry machines are in need of repair. The room itself is greatly outdated and the bed is not comfortable. This is supposed to be a Residence Inn, a Marriott, a three star hotel and it carries a price that reflects those characteristics. Unfortunately the hotel itself is barely comparable with a 2 star. Save your money and stay somewhere else, if you've ever been to a Residence Inn before, this location is a great disappointment.

title: “We absolutely loved our stay at the Pacific Terrace Hotel.”
text:
We spent 4 days at the Pacific Beach hotel and we enjoyed our stay so much. The hotel is located right on the ocean with a fantastic view. Our accomodations were sooo nice. The employees were wonderful. Ted Tillman, guest services supervisor, was so helpful to us when we booked our stay. Very nice and very professional. The impression we had was that if there was anything we needed from housekeeping to the front desk, etc., all we had to do was ask. Honestly, this was one of the very nicest hotels we've stayed in. There was lots to do nearby, walking on the beach, great restaurants, relaxing by the pool and spa, our trip was so very nice. Because of the beautiful setting and the top notch quality of the hotel, you kind of feel like you're in paradise.
 We will definitely be back.
Doug and Stephanie Mansfield

title: “Made a great 1st trip!!”
text:
I'd just like to thank Herald square for making our stay such a plesant one. The service was great, as was the rooms. 
We'll deffinatley be booking here on our next visit!

title: “ok for $50/night on priceline”
text: It was ok. They let me check in early which was very nice and I should have requested to stay in the West Tower. The main tower is very loud on the weekend and there is a loud night club in the main lobby. The walls are also very thin and I overheard my neighbors at 1 in the morning. (not cool) But, as I said, for $50 (that included taxes) it was acceptable.

title: “Just right!”
text: My husband and I jus returned from a weekend get away in downtown Chicago! The Hampton Inn Majestic was just right!Getting to the hotel and dropping of our bags was kind of tricky..but the wonderful bellmen made it better!We did not opt for valet parking, but used the self park a couple of blocks down.Again, the bellmen were very helpful in giving directions!The rooms are small but nice.Very modern decor.Nice tv and bathroom.Like the previous reviews said, the breakfast area is small..but the staff was very good at keeping things full and fresh...I thought it was fine and better than paying $40!Overall we were very satisfied with this hotel!One funny thing...someone mentioned in an earlier review about the sheets coming off of the bed..and it was so true!!Not sure why they don't fit the bed!!The location of the hotel is great if you are going to the theatre!!

title: “decent hotel with some drawbacks”
text: Check in was helpful but the first room they gace me had not been cleaned. The key didn't work for the second room. The room itself was small but comfortable. The views of the city were nice as the fog rolled in. This is a big inner city hotel. Noise comes with the territory. The location is great for buses or cable cars. Buy your passes from the gift shop. Hotel had good security. This is an adequate hotel when you want to be right in the city. Upper floors not facing Van Ness are less noisy

title: “Fabulous Girls Weekend”
text: Spent a girls getaway weekend here. I'm a native Chicagoan and thought that this hotel was in a great location (restaurants, bars, etc.) The hotel staff was extremely friendly and helpful. The bed was very comfortable and the towels were plentiful. I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone visiting the Windy City.

title: “Economical, clean and a great location.”
text: We stayed in this hotel for two nights in July 2011. The accommodations are very basic. If you are looking for a clean inexpensive place to stay in Seattle with a location in which you can walk to almost everything, this is it. The hotel older but in decent overall condition. The staff was more than welcoming and the free breakfast was also a plus. We will definitely stay here the next time we are in Seattle as you really can't beat the price or location.

title: “Great location, lovely room”
text:
We used to live in DC, so we were actually quite excited to see how the tourists' perspective of our city's hotels. We stayed at the Doubletree in late September 2006. The location of the Doubletree is great - you're near Dupont, Logan Circle, and U Street and not too far from the downtown area either. I remember from when we lived there (2001-2005) that the restaurant in the lobby can be a great spot to get drinks in the evening for happy hour. 
The breakfast was quite good - though not included - and the dining area was modern and chic. We did not eat dinner at the hotel. We used hotel points to stay here so we had a large suite with sitting area and we found it to be beyond our expectations. The decor in the room was quite nice, the bedding was cozy, and we had a great city street view (don't worry - it wasn't that loud). The hotel used to be a boutique hotel, I think, as its image is not that of a typical Doubletree.
The only complaint I'd have would be about parking - we are used to street parking so had no trouble with it, but it is difficult in that area as you are on a traffic circle and there are embassies nearby which hog the street parking. 
We had arrived super late for check in on Friday night (3am) and the front desk folks were helpful enough; we didn't have much staff contact throughout the weekend.
Overall, I recommend this hotel for its location, nice decor, and convenience. Enjoy!

title: “Great Location: very friendly and helpful staff”
text:
Relatives arrived unexpectedly in L.A. and I was at a loss as to where to put them. Hit upon Farmer's Daughter and they were delighted. It is central to a lot of places they wanted to visit. (Easy to get to Pasadena mid-day for the Huntington, great shopping across the street at the new renovated Farmer's Market and Beverly Hill is ten minutes the the west. It was easy to give directions to the beach and the LACMA.
Nice little hotel - a refreshing change from the pretentious hotels along the "strip." If a casual down to earth atmosphere with attentive service is what you looking for, then this is the place to go.

title: “Will NEVER stay there EVER again!!!!”
text: Pictures are certainly deceiving!!!! This was the worst hotel on the planet!! The location was great and even the outside of the building and the lobby were nice, but as soon as we stepped off the elevator...hello hostel. No, worse than a hostel!! The hallway had a feeling of a mental institution and the floors and walls looked as if it were the murder scene from an episode of CSI NY or SVU!! Talk about scary!! The room was so small we couldn't even unfold the rollaway bed, and the bathroom...terrible and tiny!! And the air conditioner was broken- during summertime in NYC!! And to top it all off, they charge per bag to store your luggage, while most hotels store it complimentary...but not this place! I could go on forever. There are not enough words to describe this place...but "worst place imaginable" definitely sums it up!!

title: “Missing the basics”
text:
I stay here frequently for business as I do not have the luxury of selecting my own hotel. The wireless network doesn't work about half of the time, the work out room is sweltering, the running map from the front desk is a tour of local parking lots, the outdoor pool is dirty, the rooms are poorly lit...
On the plus side, check in is quick and the breakfast buffet is great.

title: “Ghetto”
text: Do NOT stay here. It is in a bad area, not comfortable to walk around even in the daytime. The rooms are old, there is no heating, and there was a stench of roach spray in the kitchen area. We checked out within half hour of arriving.

title: “Great value for the casual traveler on a budget”
text:
Save your hard-earned money. Stay here rather than in town and save over $100 per night, plus any parking fees or even renting a car. The walk to the L is only 5 minutes and the ride to the Loop is about 25 minutes. The front desk stocks 3-day passes (but not 7-day) that they can put on your room charge. They answer the phone promptly and they'll pick you up from the airport and deliver you to nearby locations. The area is working class but safe, no shady characters panhandling or loitering in parking lots.
The room is basic Motel 6 flavor, with the dreaded soap and shampoo dispenser on the wall rather than mini toiletries (how do people actually use "shower gel" without a loofa or sponge). Shower was well-pressurized and hot water was hot. They're sticklers about room service! At most midlevel hotel chains nowadays, there are signs in the room to "save the earth" and refuse room service to save (the hotel) on laundering sheets and towels. I was surprised that they insisted on servicing the room after 2 days. Wireless signal was strong and free, and there's free wired internet as well. TV is older CRT rather than flat panel, with the usual assortment of cable channels.
Food selection for the morning was basic, 6-9 M-F and 7-10 S/S. Donuts, bagels, and breakfast sausage/egg sandwiches from Dunkin Donuts, coffee or OJ, fresh fruit, and yogurt. There's about 4 chairs total, essentially you're eating in the front desk area unless you take the stuff back to your room. Food choices at other times are generic strip mall. Subway, Domino's, chinese, and McDonald's are all clustered around the train station.
You do get a bit of noise, since you're in an airport motel and the windows are not fancy triple-insulated. In addition to the overhead planes, you'll hear the whistle of nearby trains. My room faced the back of the property, so I can't comment on road noise, though traffic did seem light at night. This amounts to nothing if you're accustomed to city living.
All in all, this place was full up for the four days I was there and I can see why.

title: “Spectacular Stay at the Awesome Hotel Monaco”
text: We could not have asked for more during our recent stay at the Hotel Monaco in Chicago. We received awesome service from a friendly staff. Every request from a fan for the room to starch for ironing my husband's shirt was fulfilled. We were very happy with the location, the free wine hour, and the room decor- absolutely loved the window seats overlooking the river! Will definitely stay there again and would highly recommend it.

title: “Always Great”
text: We love the Embassy Suites in Portland, Oregon, so decided to seek one out during our travel east. The Jacksonville Embassy Suites did not disappoint. We are finding that the Hilton family of hotels are consistently clean and good. The 2 room unit was large. It had two flat screen TVs, separate dressing table with sink in the bedroom, microwave, refrigerator, desk for the computer. And you can't beat the free drinks, chips and salsa in the evening, plus the free breakfast. All very convenient for travelers. We did our laundry while we enjoyed the evening snacks. The pool area looked great even though we did not use it.

title: “Big Comfy Rooms”
text: I stayed During E3 and the hotel was packed , but the staff remembered my name and i always felt welcomed. The king bed was comfy and despite my size the room felt big. They had Dvds in the lobby to borrow, but the selection was thin. the restaurant was good and the valet helped me with my bags which was nice. this place was a nice surprise for me.

title: “Great Value in San Francisco”
text: We stayed at the Adagio for a long weekend the week after labor day. We found the hotel to be clean and niceley decorated. We arrived at noon and even though this was well before the check in time we were able to get our room and even recieved a comp upgrade to a junior suite. The room was lovely and quite large especially considering that rooms in San Francisco are typically very small. The staff was always very friends and helpful. We had drinks at Cortez and the staff there was also great. Overall, I would definately suggest to anyone that asked.

title: “Great Hotel, Great Location”
text:
I stayed at the Sheraton Hotel and Towers in October 2011 for a convention at the McCormick Center. The hotel was first class and exceeded my expectations for a Sheraton Hotel, which are usually pretty high. The location was excellent. It was right across the river from the loop and you could walk there in 10 minutes. It was also about a 10 minute walk to Navy Pier or to Mag Mile so you were within walking distance of a number of great places.
The only downfall is that it is not very close to any of the El stations. If you want to take the train from the airport, you have to take a cab the last 10 blocks or so, but it only cost about $5 and saved a lot of time and money from taking a taxi all the way from O'hare.
The rooms were spacious, clean and well set up. Elevators were efficient. I did not eat on sight, but many people were speaking highly of the Shula's steakhouse, althought it was pricey. The Concierge was excellent and provided many terrific eating recommedations, with written walking directions to most of them.
If you can get this hotel for around $225 a night, I would recommend staying there.

title: “Typical business hotel”
text:
Not impressed. Typical business hotel in the financial district delivering the absolute essentials. 
Nothing special
Price was not so great either. Actually it was a bit expensive for what it was offering.

title: “Avoid at all costs”
text: I agree with many of the comments others have written. Looking to save a few dollars, I booked this hotel. Few eateries are located nearby, and we had to rent a refrigerator and microwave for $10 a day. Our so-called suite with a queen bed was nothing like it was advertised. Instead we got a twin bed, 6 channels, a small closet and no place to put our luggage. The last night of our stay, all I heard was loud noise, even the music from sportscenter couldn't drown it out. If you love zooming motorcycles at 2 in the morning, this is your place. But for others that want a decent place and a safe environment, do yourself a favor and look elsewhere.

title: “Christmas time get away”
text: The hotel was beautiful. Loved all the decorations around the city. Hotel great location for all the sites and shopping. The rooms were spotless and huge. Loved all the special attention to detail from the fruit in the room to filling up our ice bucket. Can't wait to come back.

title: “The Chicago Hilton is a great hotel!”
text:
My family and I (2 adults and 2 children) stayed at the Chicago Hilton from July 4-July 7 and agree with other reviewers that I can't understand the negative reviews that others have written about this hotel. The Chicago Hilton is a grand old hotel (but very up to date) and is beautiful inside. The front lobby is gorgeous and very elegant. Our room was very spacious with 2 very comfortable queen beds and a nice marble bathroom. The room was very clean and comfortable with plenty of space for 4 people. We didn't have a spectacular view, but I'm sure if we asked to be moved, they would have accommodated us if possible. 
The staff was wonderful. One of our sons was taking medication that needed to be refrigerated and when we realized that we didn't have a refrigerator, I called the front desk to inquire about one. I was told that they do supply refrigerators for a fee of $25 a day. Thinking that was a little steep, I asked if there was another option. The clerk that I spoke to immediately transferred me to one of the managers and when I explained the situation, he agreed to send up a refrigerator to our room and waive the fee. He did this without me even asking! To me, that was great customer service! 
The concierge (Donald) was very knowledgeable and helpful with all of our questions and suggestions. The restaurant in the hotel that we ate in was a little pricey, but the food was good and it was convenient. The hotel is directly across the street from Grant Park, which has nice walking/biking/skating trails to travel on. Very nice landscaping and a nice place to spend some time. Make sure you get over to the park to see the fountain at night, when there is a light show and music. There is a free trolley that takes you to various places in the city, but we were able to see a lot of the sites on foot from the hotel's location. We took a water taxi to the Navy Pier (that was a little too far to walk....especially with 2 kids!) and that was a fun way to see the city and also to rest our tired feet! All-in-all, we had a great experience staying at the Chicago Hilton and will definitely stay there again whenever we go back to Chicago.

title: “Amazing service”
text: We had the pleasure of visiting Denver for the Sweet Adeline International Competition. The staff at this hotel really put our visit over the top. Everyone, from the housekeeping staff, the dining room staff, and the front desk were wonderful. Always ready with a smile and pleasant attitude, it was fabulous! Thanks Jeremiah!

title: “Incredibly, laughably decrepit; not worth it, despite excellent location.”
text:
I stayed at the Georgetown Inn for 5 nights and daily contemplated moving, but stayed as it was convenient for a conference and visiting my son at Georgetown. I am in complete agreement with the reviewer who calls it a shabby shadow of its former self, and surprised by those who found it lovely. My rooms there hadn't been lovely for many, many years. I started in one of their smaller rooms, and entered to find the sole lamp broken and a partially used shampoo bottle w/ hair in the shower. The extremely accomodating staff immediately moved me to a huge suite for the same price as the small room ($234 AAA rate). 
While the suite was enormous, nearly everything about it was very shabby and should have been replaced many, many years ago. Nice things: sheets, duvet, mattress, bathroom tile and countertop, framed art and mirrors. Also The Daily Grill, their restaurant, had delicious food. Awful: carpet, shower, air conditioning, walls, doors, paint. The furniture was sad, beat up, but not as bad as the carpet and walls. The carpet was probably 30 years old, hard-used by hundreds, maybe thousands of travelers, grey-black around the walls (originally gold-orange) and had been patched with an entirely different grey strip in front of the bathroom where presumably no one could ignore the wear any longer. The patch itself was old and discolored. I wore my shoes indoors. The shower would not drain; water above the ankles before I called; still took over 2 minutes to drain even after beleagered maintenance staff worked on it, though clearly it got a bit better.
The suite had 2 air conditioners. Neither worked when I arrived. After maintenance staff got the power on, the living room cooled great (though the condensation from it wet the already disgusting carpet). However the bedroom unit would not blow cool air, despite their best efforts. The staff volunteered to install a window unit, but I opted for a fan (which came swathed in duct tape but was very useful). Walking past the hotel, I noted other guests had the same problem, as on the hottest day, window unit air conditioners suddenly sprouted from the Wisconsin Avenue side of the building. 
The walls and doors were really beat up and marked. The furniture was a mix of 1970s Holiday Inn dresser and nightstands with an overlay of thrift shop lamps. The clock was plugged into a non-functioning 30 yr old extension cord. 
The staff tried hard to solve the mechanical and plumbing problems, but this place should be completely gutted and renovated, including plumbing and electrical, preferably years ago. This is in no sense a luxury or boutique hotel. It is extremely well located for visiting Georgetown University and surrounding shops and restaurants, but the interior is awful, and I'd never stay there again.

title: “Thanks to Darrell, He made our stay worthwhile!”
text:
Thanks to Darrell, he made our stay worthwhile! I was just browsing the internet to stay when I found to stay. Check-in was pleasant, and Darrell gave us directions to restaurants and destinations. He even helped us book shuttle to the airport and the ride to shuttle was only $16. 
Rooms were great and big with comfy beds and good bathroom.
Parking and Internet were a big plus expecially when there is no parking in san franci.

title: “Friendly, Comfortable, Casual”
text:
Not just another convention center hotel, the Magnolia is in an older, interesting building that once housed an oil company. The rooms are quiet, comfortable and clean, with very spacious bathrooms. The furnishings aren't the newest and some of the paint needs updating, but in general it has a pleasant feel. Flat screen tv in the rooms and a decent breakfast buffet with hot foods help. I had no luck in getting a wireless signal in my room and so had to go out in the hall with my laptop to connect. The elevators are old, funky, and slow. Free beer and wine and cookies every night establishes a friendly feeling.
There are ample free internet terminals available for guests. The gym facility is ok, although the spa was undergoing renovation when I was there. There is a nice steamroom, though.

title: “Lovely, Comfortable Hotel”
text: I stayed here during a professional conference. My room was newly renovated and so comfortable. I had a partial view of Ford Field from my window. The conference rooms and the ballroom were great, too. It felt upscale but the prices were reasonable. Across the street is a beautiful community garden. I walked two short city blocks to reach Campus Martius, a city square from which all city street radiate (e.g., Eight Mile Road is eight miles from Campus Martius). There is a small park with a coffee shop. I never realized what a lovely city Detroit was until I was fortunate enough to visit.

title: “Great Location, Clean, and Best Rate”
text: My wife and I spent 3 nights here. Only 2 blocks from the Wharf easy to get around and the resturant next door is great. Staff was very friendly, offered great suggestions for getting around and we enjoyed our stay. Our rate through expedia was $156 a night which is a great bargin for this area. Beds are clean and while the mattresses are not high end they were comfortable. Only issue we had was a crying baby next door but really not the hotels issue just the luck of the draw and we could have change rooms if we wanted. Overall great stay and would recommend.

title: “Kings,Presidents and you”
text:
Once a year, my wife and I spend a Friday night at the Waldorf to attend a social function held there. We have found the rooms comfortable and clean, but certainly not the most up-to-date. You will find heavy bathrobes for your use, and no shortage of pillows, towels and blankets, unlike less expensive hotels.
Although the hotel has valet parking we use a website to locate more moderate priced parking and found it a block and a half way on 50th street, just east of the hotel. 
Since we had tickets to a Broadway show on Saturday, we checked out at noon and left our bags (free of charge!) with the hotel luggage area located in the basement near the automobile entrance. What a pleasure. We walked (15 to 20 minutes) to the theater, then picked up our bags on the way back to the car.
The magical part is however unmistakable. Kings and Queens and the world's leaders have stayed here. This is, after all, the Waldorf Astoria in New York City. What more can you say?

title: “One of the nicest hotels in Manhattan”
text:
Second visit to Hampton on Times Square North in less than 12 months and if anything it was better in 2008 than last year.
Good location - subway close and if you're feeling energetic Central Park is a nice walk away - go up 5th Avenue though rather than up 8th to gaze at all the store fronts! Good restaurants and diners nearby, and don't forget to go to the Heartland Brewery.
Rooms are plenty big enough, beds comfy, everything you need is there and there is the added benefit of the buffet breakfast.
Staff are ever so helpful at all times.
I will definitely be going back - can't wait for my next trip.

title: “Nice Stay but . . .”
text: Overall more good than bad. The room was clean but the carpet definitely needed cleaning. When you walked across the carpet barefoot your feet got blackened kinda quick. The staff was great; very friendly. Breakfast was really good (and included). Clean those carpets and you have a solid 4 star place here!

title: “Good hotel close to universal studios”
text: We stayed here for two nights, one night to go to Universal Studios and one night to the Teen Choice awards. Once we got to the hotel, our bags were taken and the bell man explained the various services and timings in the hotel. There's a small starbucks in the lobby, which I always enjoy. Check in was fast and our room was a decent sized. The hotel is down the hill from the globe entrance to universal. If you want to walk to the entrance it's a little big uphill and some stairs which take you to a bridge overpass. Otherwise the Hilton/Sheraton shuttle drops you at citywalk by Johnny Rockets, but not the entrance of universal. We ordered room service for breakfast and dinner and it was good. Took about 30 to 45 minutes. We also ate at the breakfast buffet which was very nice. Overall was a good stay and really helps to stay beside universal since it's so busy.

title: “Loved the Dana on Mission Bay”
text:
I had read many of the reviews on Tripadvisor before choosing The Dana on Mission Bay. Being from the Midwest and knowing nothing about the San Diego area, Tripadvisor was a great help! Our choice could not have been better. 
 Our room on the 3rd floor overlooked the Mission Bay. The room was spacious. The bed was very comfortable and I loved the plantation shades at the sliding balcony door. The room was clean and most surprising, very quiet at night. Up until about 9:30 or 10:00 you could hear jets taking off from the San Diego airport, but after that it was so quiet. The bathroom was well outfitted with hairdryer, makeup mirror, shampoo, conditioner and lotion. Bathrobes and slippers were also provided. 
 One of the hotel's two pools was just a few steps away. The food at the Blue Pearl was very tasty and the friendly manager was very helpful answering questions about local attractions.This hotel is located in the perfect spot for Sea World, the San Diego Zoo and all the beaches. 
 It was only a short drive to Cabrillo National Monument or Point Loma lighthouse. 
 I would very strongly recommend the Dana on Mission Bay.

title: “no labor weekend”
text: Styaed over Labor day weekend. great location next to marina and seaport village. Easy walk to Little Italy and gaslamp dist. Stayed in the south tower, bay view. Room good size, comforatble king size bed with 5 pillows. Small bathroom, poor water pressure. Liked refrig in room. maids cleaned well, no complaints. Pool area reminded me of their Maui property. Very tropical. very nice. Used valet service that was not bad as long as you called down for car 10 minutes before you needed. All in all, a good stay but something was missing. Can't explain but would proabbly try another hotel next time.

title: “1 year anniversary vacation”
text:
enjoyed the location of this hotel even though it was noisy at times with busy streets, honking horns and sirens, we stayed on the 17th floor in the towers and had a pretty good view of our surroundings and the rooftops, the hotel was clean and tidy.
while i don't have any negative comments, the hotel just didn't have a wow factor and was kinda bland for a high end hotel

title: “Small rooms at the Hudson, but not terrible experience”
text:
booked three nights here in with my husband through a deal on Travelzoo. first impressions: great staff, attentive and helpful. great lobby. DARK hallways. TINY - but clean - room.
you can tell it's a converted Y. I don't know why they decided that dark grey carpet and dark grey walls were a good way to go for their long tunnel-like hallways - but that's the way it is.
After reading reviews here, I knew the room would be small, and it was, complete with a tiny 13-inch television. No refrigerated mini-bar. 
TINY, CRAMPED BATHROOM. If you weigh over 180lbs or have long legs, be prepared for a struggle to use the bathroom. Thankfully, my husband and I are both average height and weight, but even so, I found myself sitting sideways to use the commode because my knees were literally two inches from the wall when I sat down. Yes, the glass wall between shower and bedroom is there, but that novelty lasts for about oh - two seconds - before you wish that the shower floor drained water better and that there was more space in that teeny tiny bathroom. 
There is free internet, windows are not sound-proofed, and there is a big, loud party every night downstairs in the bar/club. We could not hear the party, but we could hear the street noise, and we were on the 10th floor.
Still - I would still consider staying here again. Why? because if you are prepared for these considerations (tiny rooms, dark hallways) because for the price we paid, ($229 a night), you will find that the best part of the Hudson is not the hotel itself, but ITS LOCATION. it was a bargain to stay in this neighborhood - COLUMBUS CIRCLE is a great location, and close to all the trains, Broadway, Rockefeller Center, CENTRAL PARK IS RIGHT THERE... and the neighborhood is a safe walking area at night. You also have a CVS that is open 24 hours kitty corner on 9th Avenue, and the Time-Warner center with the Whole Foods just down the block. You can't beat the location, so for this reason, the Hudson Hotel redeems itself.

title: “Dirty, small, smelly room with ZERO noise insulation!”
text: Thankfully we pr!cel!ned this room, because it is in NO way worth the cost of paying the regular rate. Even at the low cost we paid I think I would have paid more to stay somewhere else. The room was exceptionally small and smelly (seriously, I volunteer at a nursing home and it smelled just like it!). I'd say it was smaller than our last few hotels in Paris, and if you've ever seen a small Paris hotel room you know what I'm saying. The location was fine, sure, but it's not like there aren't 50 other hotels in Boston with a great location. The room was dingy: the bathroom wall looked like someone had puked next to the toilet but the stains never got fully cleaned; the bathroom light switch was so dirty with the black gunk that collects in and around the switch itself like it's never been cleaned or replaced; TV was tiny, but next to it was a HUGE mirror that just looked really odd for a small room; we were not too bothered with the noise of the nightclub (this was a Sat. night stay) because the A/C covered it quite well, however our friends 2 doors down were next to a group of partying girls in an adjoining room who sounded like they were actually IN the room from the loud talking they could hear all night...we heard it, too, and I definately would have asked for a different room if I were nextdoor. The "concierge", if you can call him that, was terrible and basically didn't want to be bothered. We asked him about booking a Duck Tour and his response was, "oh, they are booked up this weekend, but you can use the computer around the corner to check". So, I asked him if he could call for us before we go online to see if there were any times open for us to book online (isn't that his job anyway?!) since he likely has a direct number for booking. So he picks up the phone and sure enough, "they are wide open; just show up down there". Great, glad you were so willing to help. Not. The lobby of this place is actually quite pretty, but this facade is exactly just that: a facade. Didn't try the restaurant, but the bell staff and valet were prettty swift and helpful. Would absolutely NOT stay here again. Worth another $50-$100 a night to stay somewhere more comfortable and accomodating.

title: “Great Little Motel with Free Parking & Near Golden Gate Park”
text: This motel was more than we expected - we’ll definitely be back on our next visit to San Francisco! Everything we had read about this motel, including its photos, gave us a very accurate idea of what to expect. Excellent access to Golden Gate park. The rooms were small but very comfortable and exceptionally clean, They included a refrigerator, small microwave, small table and chairs, desk and nice size TV. The WIFI worked just fine. The hotel staff was exceptional, especially Henry, who insured our stay was comfortable and without incident. The free parking was much appreciated although the spaces are very tight for larger vehicles. Although the motel is near a main street, the road noise was only minimal.

title: “Nice hotel with central location”
text: We picked this hotel based on Trip Advisor and we were not disappointed. The hotel lobby and rooms are very nice. Felt like a 4 star hotel. The rooms themselves are a little small, but then again consider the city where you are staying (they are still bigger than European rooms). Staff was very friendly. BART drops you off 4 blocks from the hotel, so no need to take a shuttle or taxi from the airport. We love to walk and saw the following by foot: Golden Gate Bridge Park, Coit Tower, Pier 39, Artistic Garden, Chinatown (1 block away), Lombard street and many more sites. I would highly recommend it. The only thing I would point out, and this is not a reflection on the hotel, is that we had our credit card number stolen I am guessing while eating out/shopping in Chinatown. I would suggest you pay in cash. The only thing we felt would have made it better is for a complimentary continental breakfast.

title: “Service at the Hotel”
text: We just checked in for one whole week and this hotel's staff has been amazing! Immediately after checking in they made every effort to assure our stay in Washington was above our expectations! From friendly greetings, concierges, front desk and other hotel staff, to above and beyond efforts from Olena, Robby and CJ thanks for the suites and all of the assistance since we have been here, we are only on day two and we feel like we are at home.

title: “Disappointed with service!”
text: My husband is a Veteran & he got some type of "great deal" on the room because of this, called "you served, you stay" or something like that, so I let him book the room, though I usually take care of all our travel arrangements. However, certain days like Christmas Eve and New Years Day and New Years Eve were understandably not subject to this "deal" so we had to pay quite a bit more for these certain days, which was no problem. However, they made us register separately for those days and therein lied the problem! Whenever one of these days came up, they made us check out and then check in again! No, (for the most part) we did not actually have to leave the room, but when we got home every day from sight-seeing, we found that our room cards no longer worked in the elevator - after a long day of sight-seeing with our feet hurting like crazy, this was very upsetting to find!!! The desk person would fix our cards so they worked for that day, so we could go up & rest, but until my husband got home & took care of the "checking in" (AGAIN), and getting ALL our cards fixed again himself, the cards would only work for one time!! These same people were at the desk everyday, saying hello to us morning and night, yet they couldn't seem to get it together: They would say, "did you just check in yesterday" & I would say, "no! I checked in 10 days ago"!! It was a nightmare!! On one day, when we had to check out/check in, they decided, not that they had someone else coming into our room, not that there was anything particularly wrong with our room, but that our room was going down for regular maintainance, and we had to MOVE to another floor!! Another nightmare!! It was definitely not worth the Veteran's deal. The housekeeper (who we never saw) was wonderful, however. She/he even did our dishes, which we never expected! We did run out of things frequently, though like creamer for the coffee (there was a kitchen w/ a coffee maker) and many other things. Our coffee maker did break at one time & we told the front desk in the morning. When we got back at night, the maintainance man was just coming to our room then to fix it. However, he was very nice & got us a new one right away. There was no paper in either room that told what channel was what on the television. Also, the notebook of information in the rooms stated that the front desk had menus for the take-out restaurants (we like Chinese), but the front desk had none. I don't like to rent a car in DC because there is usually no place to park - this hotel was a rather long walk from the nearest subway stop which was Dupont Circle, but walk-able. There was a grocery store nearby where we could buy food to cook and drinks. There was a vending machince downstairs with decent drinks, but not decent snacks. There was a decent laundry facility. It was a nice room with two double beds, which I would've rather had as kings and a pull-out couch. There was a closet for coats and a couple more hangers, but only a three drawer chest. There was a vanity room but it had no door and a bathroom with only a shower. The kitchen was nice. There was no courtesy van to or from the airport (something unheard of in my state), but they did let us check in as soon as we got there in the morning. I won't stay there again.

title: “Great hotel, friendly staff and best location”
text: This hotel is well run and in a great location. Staff is very friendly and helpful. Location is great, near shopping and financial district. Would recommend this hotel to business travelers and families on vacations.

title: “Loved Achieve - Achieved happiness with my stay :)”
text:
What I loved about this place is that it is IMMACULATELY clean, the staff of two, who live on the premises where so very friendly. It was decorated very nicely. 
I rented their smallest room but they had a few different styles. Anthony, who is the caretaker there and extremely friendly, showed me (for a future stay) their 975 sq foot private apartment which is HUGE and decorated so nicely. Although, that apt was not as much as I'd like to spend, but the price was definitely less expensive than a hotel and moreover, if you are thinking of traveling with 6 people I would definitely advise you to take the apt - extremely inexpensive that way.
In a nutshell, the place was extremely clean, the doors were all electronic (made me feel very safe), the staff very friendly, and their body wash and shampoo smelled soooooo good. I'd stay there again.

title: “Beautiful but...”
text:
My family and I (2 adults 2 kids) recently stayed at the Palace Hotel in San Francisco. It's a classic, old hotel smack dab in the middle of it all. A stones throw from Union Square where you can catch the $5 trolley or go deep to find the BART. The guest rooms are very nice and have an old world charm. The public areas are equally beautiful and display the history of the hotel. We received a fairly decent deal through my affiliation with the Starwood.com site I belong to. The staff we came in contact with were kind and curtious. All in all it was a nice stay and truthfully I would go back if I got the same deal.
Here's a brief breakdown of where I think the hotel could improve:
-Close the doors to the rooms that are being cleaned. You can't believe how loud the vacuum cleaners are. We had arrived late (10:30 PM) and tried to sleep in. 
-Give your guests a break on parking. $40 is too much. We parked around the corner at The Hearst Parking Center for $19 a night. Call ahead and get their hours of operation. They close on Sundays. 415-989-4000.
-Cleanup the locker rooms to the pool. Towels were overflowing and lockers were broken. You can put all the fresh flowers out you want but it won't hide these type of maintainence issues.
That's it. The folks at the front desk were very nice and comp'd us a roll-away for my 12 yr old son. The staff who waited on us for breakfast were first class as was the Concierge. Very nice and attentive. Give it a try but take note.

title: “A very nice job overall...”
text: We chose this hotel because of our previous experiences with Holiday Inn Express, all of which have been positive. The price seemed reasonable, and the location near Times Square and right next to the Port Authority Bus Terminal were great for us, since we were first-time visitors to NYC. The staff was really nice and very helpful, answering all our questions and demonstrating a desire to make our visit special. I would stay here again, and I would certainly recommend it to others.

title: “Nice but small”
text: Stayed here during Christmas season and it was perfect location, nice ammenities but a small room... to be expected in the area. It still had everything we needed and would certainly stay here again.

title: “Great hotel if working in Downtown Manhattan”
text: This is a great hotel if you are working downtown or doing business at one of the World Financial Buildings. I enjoyed the room amenities and great service at the hotel. This W surely meets the trendiness you expect to receive at a W. The only drawback of staying at the hotel was the noise throughout the night. I know it is not the hotels fault, but even on the 19th floor I could still hear the construction down below throughout the night.

title: “Good hotel, excellent location”
text:
I stayed here on business after a few days at the Clift hotel down the street. I enjoyed the Westin much more. It's an older hotel with character, the location is better, and it's a better hotel for business meetings. There's a Starbucks type cafe downstairs with plenty of seatings for meetings and was conveinent after paying an arm and a leg for cold room service at the Clift!
You can't beat this location in Union Square. It's even connected to a few shops like Victoria's Secret through the lobby and is close to shopping and convention centers. 
Great service at the front desk- I arrived at 9 am and was still able to get a room. The rooms do need a bit of updating (I was in the older wing) but I think it's part of it's charm. The bathroom was great- lots of room on the counter, great shower head, etc. Bed is comfy and was definitely enough room for two people. I would be interested to stay in the newer wing and compare.
Overall- comfortable stay, great location, excellent staff..... would come again and highly reccommend to friends.

title: “Nice hotel, great service, awesome location”
text:
Very nice hotel. Staff was very friendly and accomodating. The location is fantastic...right near Union Square, close to several tourist attractions. Try the award winning Michael Mina restaurant that's inside the hotel, although getting reservations is tough. 
Nice lounge area & great coffee bar in the lobby.

title: “Clean rooms comfy beds & nice brekfast”
text: Ample breakfast with plenty of choice. We could hear a little noise from the room next door but not too bad. Beds were comfy and clean. Area was very ordinary although we never felt unsafe.Our only negative is that they would not accept our debit travel card which was annoying( the only place that wouldn't in 3 weeks of traveling in the US) We discovered a nice little Italian restaurant nearby called "Cucina Freshca & sons" with good old fashioned service and home style cooked food.

title: “Convenient location to Baltimore Convention Center”
text: Stayed at this hotel this past weekend during a volleyball tournament at the Convention Center. Hotel was convenient to the convention center but was a little unnerving that we were greeted each evening with a homeless person begging for money by the door to the hotel. Rooms were fine, hotel was clean and nice although the cleaning staff did not clean some of the volleyball girls room for any of the three days we were there. However, the concierge was friendly and helpful in recommending a restaurant when most were booked and in helping us to get a large reservation. This hotel is much much better than the Days Inn Inner Harbor which we stayed at two years ago so I would stay again. But I do think the hotel should do a little more to make their guests feel safe in returning to the hotel and not being accosted by a homeless person. Also, one other complaint: pillows were either the giant decorative pillows or they were extremely small and mushy. Wasn't going to sleep on the big decorative pillows as I doubt they change those cases every night and the other pillows were much smaller than normal and extremely smushy so they were not comfortable to sleep on at all!

title: “Choose this hotel!”
text: Hotel was in a good location, rooms were spacious and clean, and the complimentary happy hour & evening milk and cookies were an added bonus.

title: “Amazing”
text: Little things like a hot towel on arrival and an amazing varied breakfast made this an excellent place to stay in San Francsico. Perfect location - away from the hustle and bustle of downtown but there is a good bus service and taxis are cheap - but lacking in SF in general. It is also close to restaus and bars on Chestnut and Fillmore streets. Cheese and wine in the evenings (plus meatballs!), free wifi, biscuits, 24h coffee and tea. The staff are willing to do anything to help. Would definitely come back here.

title: “Excellent”
text: Probably the best choice for hotel in times square.atayed at room 608.it was quiet and exactly what we needed to get some rest after a busy day in ny.best choice! Some of the receptionists could have been more hepful in arranging the options for us to get to the jfk. Overall:excellent!

title: “Great stay but Staff needs Improvement”
text: For the price we paid, it was a good deal. Rooms were very clean, area was quiet and walking distance to Times Square and Fashion Way. Subway was close by and convinient. I have to say when we first arrived we were skeptical because the area was questionable and staff was rude. The area appeared to be bad but after the second night we totally felt comfy walking around an getting to know the area. I went with 2 other girls and we would walk to the pizza stand 2 blocks up with no trouble. BTW, Halal Pizza is the best @ 3am after clubbing! Anyhoo, the only thing I would say needs to improve is the staff. They did not offer us help w/the luggage and when we inquired about someone being able to help us with the luggage they looked @ us like we were nuts. We had to use the luggage cart and haul it up and down ourselves. The night staff was far more helpful, the gentleman who worked the night shift was so sweet and worth going back to stay. The good overrides the bad. The hotel had wireless access, clean rooms, continental breakfast, and quiet location. Rooms are a bit small as expected for NY, wouldnt recommend the room for more than 3 people.

title: “they were wonderful”
text: the folks at the hotel were absolutely great. my mom made a couple of requests that were immediately taken care of. they were also polite and friendly. everything was clean and the bed linens were very nice.

title: “A great experience.”
text:
My wife and I stayed for five nights at the end of May. Our stay formed part of a six week journey around the southern states of the USA, and partly the base for a larger family celebration.
We choose 'The Mark' for its location and reputation. It did not disappoint on the former. The location is fantastic for exploring the art galleries and museums on the east side and Central Park. Just walk out the hotel and turn right.
With regard to the hotel itself we had a courtyard room on the 8th floor. It was excellent; quiet;large comfortable bed, lots of wardrobe storage and an absolutely stunning bathroom. The only downside for us was the 'Creston' room control system. We had a number of issues during our stay relating to the air-conditioning and television controls. Although we had a couple of visits by maintenance the system was still giving problems when we left.
The quality of service we received during our stay was very mixed. Breakfast was excellent but the service haphazard, and painfully slow on a number of mornings. The doormen were very polite, friendly and helpful with a plentiful supply of umbrellas when the rain arrived on a couple of afternoons. This contrasted with the concierge service which we found extremely unhelpful, even arrogant. Requests for assistance in sorting out some issues relating to a brief visit to Washington during our stay were answered with a 'can't do' rather than 'can do' attitude. Even a request for assistance booking a local restaurant for lunch became a major issue. In the end we made our own arrangements; it was easier.
We will definitely stay when we next visit New York. Will we recommend 'The Mark'? Definitely yes, but it comes at a price.

title: “THEY ARE MY FAMILY AWAY FROM HOME”
text:
I have stayed at the LAX Crowne Plaza Hotel for 7 or 8 years, an average of about 2 nights a week.
They truly are my family away from home, and all the customer contact people have become my friends - they truly do take care of the customer and make them feel like family.
I love their new make over work!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
Grampa Fred

title: “Dont be put off by the name”
text: Third stay in SF but first stay at this hotel. I was initially wary of the poncey name and its description as a "boutique" hotel owned by a group with the name "Joie de Vivre". It all sounded a bit camp. However, my granddaughter lives in SF and visited the hotel on an architectural tour and assured me it was fine. She was right. This hotel is very well located in the financial district. You can easily walk to the tourist parts of the city and the BART railway system is very close by (handy to know when you are dragging your bags to and from the airport). The room I had on the seventh floor was spacious and well equipped. The front desk staff were unfaillingly polite and helpful. The special factor of this hotel is the wine tasting every evening for an hour. Guests get together in the lobby and just enjoy some glasses of wine together. This creates a friendly atmosphere in which guesrs open up and share their experiences of the city. Better than a guide book! Also an excellent start to a good evening out. So dont be put off by the name. Just go for it !!!

title: “For $87 a night we were treated like royalty by the staff!”
text:
We stayed at the Quality Inn while attending the AFBF meeting. The staff at the front desk knew most our destinations and had maps to draw walking routes on for us. As no Seattle streets go straight for long, the maps were very helpful!
The breakfast host was fantastic. We stayed four nights and my husband said goodbye to him on the third morning, saying our plane left too early to eat the next morning. No problem, the young man said, I will come in early and you can still have breakfast. We love that kind of service! And the hot breakfasts made for a great start to our days.
Friends of ours also stayed at this hotel. She had left her cane at home, and the hotel loaned her one for the duration of our trip. Again, I think that is above and beyond service.
For $87 a night, we were treated like royalty with great breakfasts, helpful front desk people, and nicely made up rooms each night with out personal hot tub (the hotel pool was gorgeous, too).

title: “Great stay”
text: I really noticed that this hotel has exceptional service. Everyone was very friendly, the concierge provided valuable information on a concert I wanted to see and, given the weather was pretty warm while I was there, it was nice to get ice sent to my room in the evening. I really liked that they had yoga mats available on request . The location is great for 6th Avenue - but not so close that noise is an issue - and I found it easy to walk just about anywhere else. Only a ridiculously minor complaint - the shower curtain is too thick to allow light through, so it's pretty dark in the shower. Renovations were going on and I could hear the noise on the 13th floor. However, it didn't prevent me from sleeping, napping or relaxing.

title: “ONE OF THE WORST HOTELS I HAVE EVER STAYED IN”
text: I stayed in this hotel for 1 night as I couldn't bear to stay for the 10 nights I was booked in for, back in February 2007!!! I have been meaning to write a review on this hotel for a long time and have finally got round to it. Considering that this hotel is based in the centre of NYC, where everything happens, I'm astounded that the environmental health department haven't closed it DOWN!!! I'm disappointed that nothing has changed since 2007, when I stayed there! My visit was a night with bed bugs and I only realised that there was a problem the next morning when I had red spots all over my legs!!! Stay away from this hotel - budget yes, but it doesn;t have to be FILTHY no matter what your budget!!!

title: “Must experience this resort!”
text: We could not belive how gorgeous the room was! We are local residents & felt like we were in a different foreign city. We had the 'Bonfire Kit' delivered to the room & enjoyed the boats going by for over 3 hours while munching on s'mores & walking along the sand. We also had breakfast delivered to our room & brought it outside to eat on the beach. (what a treat!) The service was superb & every staff memeber we encountered said hello & were happy to answer our questions. Had a fabulous time at this super secluded 'South Pacific' type resort & will be recommending to everyone we know. Highly, highly recommend this get-away to relax with very little encounter of other people!!!

title: “Fabulous in every way!”
text:
We celebrated New Year's Eve at the Dana this year and it was fabulous! The suites are well appointed and the floor to ceiling windows have a fabulous view of the city. Each and every detail of the rooms is fantastic, including the shower and bath fixtures, hardwood flooring in the room, and the iPod stereo in each room.
Vertigo's party in the evening had a great crowd and the shots of vodka that flowed from the "V" shaped ice sculptures on the heated patio overlooking the city were wonderful.
Each and every staff member we came into contact with was friendly and helpful and everyone said hello to us and made us feel welcome. 
The location of the hotel is within walking distance of many amenities, including shopping, bars and much more.
The Dana is highly recommended!

title: “Excellent Views and amazing customer service”
text:
This is an amazingly modern hotel ! The rooms start 6th floor onwards so whatever floor you get, I am sure you will have some view and the higher you get the better the view becomes. Being a Hilton Honors member got us rooms on 22nd floor facing the bay, my mother-in-law was awed by the experience, staying here made it a perfect first vacation with her. They don't have an executive / club lounge for Hilton Honors members but they give you breakfast coupons for Starbucks good for ANY drink and ANY food item at their in-house Starbucks. We were also able to use those coupons to get a discounted price (only $10) for the breakfast buffet (more of a brunch.....) ! However the evening HHonors coupons for Odysea lounge were hardly worth anything, the front desk told us those were good for any food appetizer but the lounge folks honored those for only chips and humus serving (weird disconnect). Explained that to the front desk and they comped us some of that expense, Hilton customer service always wins me over !
The hotel has done considerable development around the area and even if you are not staying here, I would recommend visiting the complex and try one of the awesome signature cocktails at their Odysea bar in the evening on the outside terrace seating with a view of the bay. They advertise that the herbs used in their cocktails are from the personal garden of the executive chef, can't get more organic and low carbon foot print than that !! They also have this amazing footbridge that connects the hotel to Gaslamp Quarters, it reminded me of the Helix bridge in Singapore, great piece of engineering. There was a wedding at the hotel when we were there and the bride and groom must have spent almost half an hour just posing on this bridge !
Another tip, if you want to rent a car and drive around don't bother to rent from airport location, the hotel has an on-site car rental booth and with some good planning you can rent only for the day you need the car, return in the evening and avoid steep $27 self parking charge.

title: “Layne Hotel - Authentic San Francisco”
text:
Stayed at the Layne Hotel in San Francisco as a business traveler in late ’05 to attend a conference. I avoided the big chain hotel where the conference was being held in favor of the Layne just a block away. Not only did I save nearly $100 per night, I got to enjoy a much more authentic taste of San Francisco.
The Layne’s décor can best be described as chic in a rustic, bohemian sort of style. The elevator is a quaint old fashion model with a hand-operated door and inner gate, harkening back to an earlier era in this fine city’s history.
The Layne is the kind of hotel where the owner/proprieter notices the small cut on your finger at check-in and offers you a band-aid. The Layne is the kind of hotel where the owner’s mom (who works the front desk in the morning) greets you with a smile and offers you a fresh brewed cup of coffee, rather than pointing you at the Starbuck’s kiosk across the lobby. The Layne is the kind of hotel where the owner’s sisters who cleans the room catches you in the lobby at check-out time to make sure you hadn’t forgotten that bottle of shampoo you left in the shower.
Don't expect a posh decor or a huge suite - just a clean place with a very friendly staff. In short, the Layne is a fine hotel for anyone looking to save some money and escape the cookie-cutter feel of the mega-chain hotels in favor of a more authentic San Francisco experience.
My one piece of advice if staying here - ask for a room on the back side of the hotel if you are a light sleeper. San Francisco is a busy town, and can get pretty noisy at night.
Happy Traveling!
Dean

title: “experience old san francisco!”
text:
As others have said, this hotel is for those who want to get away from the generic chains. If you want a standard tourist experience, you can get GREAT deals with last minute online bidding. If you like staying in b&bs or european style pensiones, this place is for you.
There are very few hotels in this part of town. I used to go the geary parkway motel which has a 1960s drive in motel feeling. Since one of the employees was downright cruel to me, I will never patronize them again. please pick Stanyan Park over Geary Parkway if you have a choice!
few of the reviewers mention that this hotel has been in continuous operation since 1894. if you like that vibe [with a 1980s redecoration] you will love this! Pretend you are a victorian salesman passing through SF. Imagine how early 20th century people would stay here after outings to GG park.
I think the other reviews show more about the reviewers than the hotel. One British reviewer said this reminded her of downwardly mobile seaside hotels in Britain - wow I have never been to a seaside hotel in Britain, and now I guess I don't have to try that! Another guy said he was mad because he had no air con. Dude, this is SF. It is cool every day of the year. Thank your lucky stars you visited SF on a hot day! Next time stay downtown in a chain!
Please try this hotel if you like something different. The room/bathroom/breakfast quality is fine - few hotels offer breakfast more than muffins and here they at least had eggs and bagels etc. they also offer teatime in the pm. I stayed in a single inward looking room - small but quiet. Yes I could see into other rooms - I saw someone in their underwear closing their blind at night! hahahaha. But the interior rooms are quiet.
email me if you have any questions about any hotels in SF and how to get good deals. the worst part of this hotel is that they do not offer last minute specials and you cannot bid for this neighborhood on places like hotwire or priceline. You pay a bit more for the unique experience.
LAST BUT NOT LEAST, I HIGHLY RECOMMEND PUBLIC TRANSIT HERE! PARKING IS 18$ AND IT IS SUPER CONVENIENT TO MUNI LINE N JUDAH!

title: “Inexpensive, Clean, Close to Catro - A bargain”
text:
I wrote a review of this place a year ago so I thought I would write an updated review since I just stayed there. Last year I stayed in the back of the motel and this year I stayed in the front by the street FYI.
First of all - they updated the office and the staff is brand new. Any complaints you see here about the staff are old and outdated. They were friendly and nice if we needed something.
You can't beat the location if you want to walk and/or party in the Castro. There is also a coffee shop across the street and a great brunch place up the street. There is a sundeck where you can sun, smokers can smoke and you can hang with some friends.
The room was clean and quiet (even in the front). There is no air but they supply a fan and with San Fran's cool weather we could cool down our room quite easily. Bed was comfortable - bathroom was clean.
There are secure gates to keep people off the street from getting to the rooms above (all the cruising comments must be old). There was some guy just hanging out on the upper floor - I went to the office to let them keep an eye on him - I walked in there was a San Francisco Police officer chatting at the front desk AND they had an evening security guard starting who walked around all night. So I felt very secure.
A great value for the money - cheaper than places further down on Market Street farther from the Castro. (I've stayed at them and their rooms aren't any nicer AND they charge you $40 a day or more for parking - parking is FREE at Becks)
Close to the Market Street Trolley (F I believe) and the Muni station. There are many things to walk to besides the castro (Kareoke Bar, Barbershops, Chase Bank, a Gym) in close proximity.
If they could invest in new bedspreads the place wouldn't look as dated. (However the kitchyness of the place is part of the charm for me).
It's become my "home away from home" when visiting the Castro due to the inexpensive rates, clean rooms and proximity to the Castro.
If you are looking for a high end hotel experience or somewhere for your kids to watch TV. (I never even turn on the TV when I stay here - I'm too busy) Then you can probably move on.
I'll be back!

title: “Fantastic Hotel & Front Office Staff”
text:
Front Office Manager Amber was so accommodating when I called needing reservations at the last minute. At check in I was welcomed with a smile by Sarah.
