Like Amber, she was so courteous and attentive to my requests. During my check in I was able to meet Amber in person. Both her and Sarah truly made me feel welcomed. I appreciated their kindness and compassion. I could feel that they truly cared about me as a guest of the hotel. The room was clean, spacious, quiet, and all around lovely.... the bed is amazing. I also enjoyed the balcony, and the large HD TV. 
I will recommend this hotel to my family and friends. Amber and Sarah, thank you for going above and beyond for me prior to, and during my stay. I will never forget your efforts! I look forward to my next stay!

title: “Great Stay - Great Location”
text:
I stayed for a week for a convention downtown, leaving my teenager to fend for himself for several of the days we were there. He was able to walk to North Star Mall with no difficulty. 
The room was very comfortable, nice kitchen and comfortable beds. They were made up each day even though they say they won't do that on longer stays.
The breakfast was ok. Lots of restaurants nearby. 
Drive to the convention center was 15 minutes or less each day. Excellent airport access, no airport noise. Free laundry, never crowded. The pool area was crowded but nice enough.
No complaints about this stay at all.

title: “Great location, dated and in need of some updating”
text:
It's a bit of a double edged sword when you find an old hotel with all of the interesting and fascinating features of an age gone by which offers a museum like experience in itself, one which is sitting right opposite Maddison Square Garden (priceless on a game night) and opposite Penn Station (priceless if your sleeper train pulled in after an over night trip from Orlando), where Macy's is right outside your window and a whole range of eateries are on the doorstep, a couple of minutes walk from Times Square and the Empire State Building right around the corner... and then you get to your room to find that it's rather delapidated and in need of some TLC and certainly nothing to write home about or what you'd have chosen had you stayed there previously. 
But then you think about the $94 dollars you paid for the night for three people, the beds that are far from the comfiest you're experienced but provide somewhere to lie your head for the night, lighting that works but is very dim,(perhaps on purpose) decor that really could benefit from some brightening up, carpets that need replacing... but then you find a large roll top bath with a wobbly but serviceable basin and nice clean fluffy towels an ironing board and iron hair dryer and some fab TV stations as standard and you kind of get an acceptable night. 
The hotel is huge, with I believe over a thousand rooms, it's an impressive building and the staff were great, letting us check in at 11am. In hotel facilities were good and meant if you were using this as a stop over you didn't need to go anywhere else if you didn't want to. 
The lobby is impressive and the business centre which you use on pay as you go rechargeable cards was really good and efficient. The rooms let this place down but if you want somewhere impressive to look at from a historical and architectrual perspective, somewhere in a fabulous location with great facilities and staff where you can take a good soak in a deep tub and have a peaceful sleep then this place is for you . So long as you don't mind your room being a bit dingy and grotty yet clean and comfy enough.

title: “OK hotel in Chicago”
text: We chose this hotel for reasons of price and because it was close to the Art Institute and the Chicago Symphony. It was not fancy, there was no complementary breakfast, the elevator was kind of slow, but the staff were all friendly and helpful. There was free Wi-fi, which we were not in a position to use, and the computer in the lobby required a credit card charge. We did not mind hearing the El trains just outside, but some people might find this disturbing.

title: “Love the staff at the Residence Inn Houston Medical Ctr.”
text:
I work for FEMA and my staff and I have stayed at this Residence Inn off and on for the last 4 years working Tropical Storm Allison. The staff are the friendliest I have encountered anywhere. They are always willing to help you in every way possible. They treat me like a member of their family. The rooms are very spacious and clean, and meet my needs adequately. Mr. David Gould, the Manager, also goes out of his way to help out and wants to make your stay pleasant. This appears to be an older Residence Inn but they are continuously rennovating. This particular facility deals with a lot of medical patients because of their proximity to the Medical Center. They treat those people with patience and kindness also. I highly recommend this facility to anyone staying in the area. In fact, our office was located very close by when I started staying there, now we are across town, almost to the ship channel area. I chose to stay where I was and drive back and forth, only because I was very comfortable there.
The only thing I would change if I was in charge and had the funds of course, I would put a recliner in each room. The couch is not very comfortable but the bed is!

title: “If staying in Times Square, this is a great hotel!!!!”
text:
We stayed at the Renaissance Times Square for 2 nights on January 12-14 – great location if you have plans for the theatre. We had a double room and it was very roomy by NYC standards. There were 3 of us (all female - me, my daughter, and my girlfriend) staying in the room, and we never felt crowded at all, even with all of our luggage. Four adults, or two adults and two children, could easily stay in this room comfortably. I checked the mattresses, lamps, headboards, etc. for bed bugs with a small LED flashlight, and saw no signs of any…Yay!
The bathroom was very modern with a nice vessel sink and Aveda products. Really cool, frosted sliding bathroom door! Nice tub and showerhead, and hot water was readily available. There was an adequate number of towels for us in the bathroom. Nice size closet for coats, clothes and luggage. 
There was a nice chair and desk with a power strip for charging electronic devices and a nice big flat screen TV. In addition, there was another nice chair and tray table by the window, which provided additional seating. All updated furniture. There was a mirrored bar area with drinks inside plus bottled water on the desk for $8.00/bottle. We didn't drink any of that!!! 
Check-in went quickly and smoothly on the first floor, after which you must take an elevator up to the 11th floor lobby then switch to another elevator to get to your room. We never had to wait long for an elevator during our stay. I had requested early check in and when we arrived at the hotel around 1:00 pm, our room was ready and we went straight upstairs. 
This hotel does not have any Times Square views, but you can request a room facing 7th street, which provided some nice views of some of the brightly lit billboards. Our room was 1712, facing 7th Avenue. We were not disturbed by any noise from the street. There were room darkening curtains that blocked the light from the billboards outside our room, so no problem there.
We visited the R Lounge on the 11th floor around 3:30 on that Thursday afternoon, and it was not very crowded at all. We sat on the big cushioned bench right by the windows overlooking Times Square. Gorgeous views!!!! We order some “Bar Bites” and a couple of cocktails. Kinda expensive (approx. $70) and the food was just ok, but the views were worth it! Make sure that you get the 99 cents homemade chips and french onion dip - very good and quite the bargain! Very contemporary lounge with nice furniture and a relaxing atmosphere. Also, the waiter placed candles on the table when it got dark. Later that night when returning after an 8:00 show, we noticed that the club was closed for a private party, and were glad we had gone earlier. Hint: if you plan to visit the lounge after 6:00 pm, I would suggest that you go to Open Table and make reservations. And request a seat by the window facing Times Square. It’s awesome!
I would definitely stay here again. We also spent one night at the sister hotel, the Marriott Marquis, which is about a block away. I have done a separate review for that hotel, but I just want to say that if you’re trying to choose between the two, I would choose the Renaissance over the Marquis any day. We paid about $300/night at the Renaissance, and $400/night at the Marquis. The Renaissance was a much nicer hotel, hands down….
bb

title: “Good surprise!”
text: We found this online a month prior, other hotels were booked. We had two nights. Good price. Location was great! At first I was worried it would be in a seedier part of downtown. As Seattle has many homeless unfortunately, this area is no different. But the location is very close to shops, train (light rail from Seatac and monorail to Space Needle), Pike Place market, piers, and places of interest. Lots of good restaurants nearby, especially great Sushi. Bars, coffee shops galore. We did not have a car, but there is some parking around, but we were worried and so had returned the rental car. Didn't need it. Walked everywhere from hotel and stopped back for a break in midday. Clean and comfy bed, small kitchenette with complimentary water and soda. As it was July it could get warm in room, but liked window open and fan on, also had extra fan, good for white noise. Since the area can be noisy at night on weekends, we chose a room overlooking the courtyard. Business area in lobby with several PCs. They ordered our taxi and held our luggage when we got there early on arrival day. Nice views from the roof. No restaurant or pool, this is a smaller hotel with 5 floors. It really was a nice surprise and especially for the money. I would stay here again for sure.

title: “Not So Bad....”
text: I just returned from spending 2 nights at the Wellington Hotel. For the price, the room was a dissapointment! The beds were very comfortable and the the shower was great - never a problem with hot water (room 735). BUT... the room was very small, the air conditioner sounded like a jack-hammer going on and off all night, the shade had a tendency to slowly rise in the middle of the night - and the street lights can be very disconcerting! The room and bath - both old, were fairly clean but someone has neglected to vacuum the closet floor or vents in months! And don't try to get to the lobby in the morning after 8:30 - unless you take the steps. On the plus side, the front desk and bell staff were very attentive and pleasant and the location can't be beat. A special shout-out to Danny who went out of his way to be very helpful!

title: “Frequent Stays reveal great staff, hit and miss on the rooms”
text:
I have stayed 12 different weeks in this hotel over the last year. I have grown to love the location for it's quick access to several different freeways. The staff are always friendly and since day one have always provided friendly service. 
The rooms are always clean, well appointed and newly decorated. During most of my stays there has been something deficient with the room. I have encountered broken phones, broken coffee makers, no coffee makers, broken A/C, broken TV remotes, no internet service, broken lamps, broken clocks and stubborn or broken doors (similar to the report of another reviewer of this hotel). I also had the "change the air filter" alarm on the air conditioner sound off without stopping in the middle of the night. 
The sad thing is most of these deficiencies could be fixed before the guests find them. The good news is the staff have always either corrected the deficiencies or offered to change my room. 
I have never heard road noise as reported by other reviewers. I have heard noise from the floors above me. I always try to stay in Homewood Suites or Residence Inns and I don't find the noise from the floor above any better or worse than any other property of those brands.
I obviously like this hotel as I am about to go there again next week. I think it s a good value and appreciate the service and recognition of the staff.

title: “Wonderful Stay”
text: I am really surprised by the bad reviews of some people. I stayed for 4 nights during May 30-June 4. I was there for my husbands BMT Graduation and I was there with my little 3 month old. I wanted to stay at a more upscale hotel because of my little baby. Didn't want anything dirty or gross. This hotel was AMAZING! I walked in and was greeted right away. The hallways were clean. I walked into the room thinking I was going to walk into a tiny little room, but it was really spacious. I had a King Room with a couch. The room was nice. The bathroom was great. Kinda wished the showers were designed different though cause water got all over the floor and made for a mess, but thats nothing!! I really liked the fact that they had a shuttle that went to the base. I didn't rent a car or bring a car cause I flew to San Antonio. However, I wish the shuttle went to the airport as well, or some local attractions. This would have saved me some money on taxi service. The breakfast was great! They had all sorts of hot items, with little pastries and fruit to take along with me as well. The staff were great. Everytime I needed something, they were on it quickly! The price was great as well! I also liked that it was close to a walmart and target, and a couple restruants as well. They were a little far for walking distance, but I like to walk so I didn't mind the walk! I will definitely stay here again in the future if I return to San Antonio! Thank you for a great stay!

title: “Really quaint”
text:
We attended a conference in San Antonio and decided that using our timeshare was the best way to save money and be close to the action.
We arrived by air and took a taxi to the hotel. We were very early and the room was not ready. Our bags were tagged and we returned after 2pm to find our bags already delivered to our room.
Noise has been a consideration in previous reviews but we had no noise problems. We occupied a two bedroom unit and the "king room" actually had no windows, not really a problem due to the fact that there was no chance of noise being a problem.
The rooms are not appointed in a luxury manner, if that is what you are looking for! The building is on the historic registry and much of the interior is preserved, therefore, the floors are polished cement and the original concrete beams for the building are visible. All explained on a plaque in the elevator and the inroom information. When you take into consideration the historic nature of the building this only adds to the charm.
The wi-fi was a bit limited in the room, but available, and free. Evidently wi-fi had been in the rooms had been added just days before. 
Do not expect any amenities, because there aren't any. I happened into the lobby one morning for the free Starbucks coffee and found the hotel manager speaking to new employees. The quote her, "this is a hotel with no amenties, you, the staff are the amenities, so when people request something, they need to be made happy." 
We never felt deprived of anything. One strange thing--the key I carried kept having to be reprogrammed. I must be magnetic because my husband never had a problem.
The washer/dryer combo is unusual. You must do small loads or the clothes come out in a mangled state, clean, but mangled. At least there is an iron available. 
The location is ideal to access the RiverWalk and in the evening we could look out the windows and see the horse-drawn, lighted carriages taking riders. The Alamo is less than a 10 minute walk from the hotel and you'll never want for a restaurant with the multitude of restaurants steps away on the Riverwalk.
The one thing we missed was having a place to really buy staples to use in the kitchen since this is a timeshare with kitchen facilites. We didn't have a car until the last day, didn't need it, so shopping was limited.
Go to Riverside Suites and enjoy!

title: “Great value and location with an awesome view”
text: This hotel is in a great location in the Embarcadero area of SF. Seems to cater to business people, which was fine with us. Rooms were very clean and modern, and very quiet. Bathroom was small, but manageable - we were on the top floor reserved for Starwood Preferred Guests, so i don't know if that made any difference. Grill on 3rd floor was outstanding for lunch and breakfast. Did not try dinner there. Staff on check-in was cordial, and Concierges we spoke to were always friendly and willing to help with reservations and suggestions. An overall outstanding value in a market with heavy competition. I saw no distinction of a decline in any aspect from the transition from its past as Park Hyatt to current Le Meridien.

title: “Interesting, eye-catching decor with enthusiastic front desk manners and less than enthusiastic housekeeping.”
text: As a group of older women who travel together frequently, we are picky about some things. As mentioned the young attractive front desk and valet and restaurant staff are friendly and sometimes overly solicitous. We ran out of tp in our king suite and there was no back up. There were only towels and drinking glasses for 2 and we were four. No hand towels. One of us left a nitegown in the bathroom and even though she noticed it within a couple of hours of leaving it was not returned. The surroundings almost made up for poor housekeeping. We would most likely return.

title: “Good location, poor breakfast”
text: Ok priced for location (nice enough 15 min walk from Union Square) but let down by a poor view from the room we had (on inside of building overlooking room opposite). Well sized room though and decent bathroom. Hotel receptionists very friendly and helpful. Let down by a very poor self service buffet breakfast in a couple of very random conference rooms.

title: “Worst Hotel Experience of My Life”
text: I went to Charlotte for an event at the Time Warner Arena and I picked this hotel because it was the closest (this was a terrible mistake). We booked a hotel room for 3 people with 2 queen beds on hotels.com. The service we received was HORRIBLE throughout our entire stay. First, we were told when we got there that, because we booked on a third-party site, the hotel does not care about us and we are only there to fill in the gaps (they literally told us this). Instead of the room we booked with 2 beds, we were placed in a room with only 1 bed for 3 people. When we arrived in our room on the 7th floor, there was a band setting up on a rooftop bar directly underneath our window. We called the front desk and we were told that all noise would cease at 10:30pm due to the proximity with the hotel. Boy, was this wrong. At 2:15 am, we were woken up to screaming people and club music outside our window and at the same time a party on our hall that we could hear from our room on the opposite side of the building. When we called down to the front desk, instead of receiving good customer service saying "I'm sorry you were woken up at 2:15 in the morning. Let me see what I can do about that" they actually said, "We can't control what happens outside of our hotel." Only after I explained that Charlotte had a noise ordinance that was surely in effect at 2:15 am would they agree to do anything. The noise finally died down around 3:15am. Do NOT stay here!!

title: “Mum _ dauthger days.”
text: Hi. We liked the hotel. The price was right. Nice room, but to hot so we had troubles sleeping. We couldn't get the temperature down. The AC work but not hard enough. The other thing that didn't work was our request to get a glutenfree breakfast. We specificly ask about it in an email before we arived. That's a pitty. Now we had to buy our own bread and take it to the breakfastlounge. But otherwise, we loved our stay in New York and we will come back!

title: “oops - shared rooms”
text:
My partner and I stayed here mid June for two nights to meet friends before we set off to drive Route 66. Location was fantastic. At check in the member of staff was friendly but I think new to the position/hotel, as she wasn't very confident. We received our key and made our OWN way up to the room as there was no porter around. We found our room and to our horror there was a guy in the shower!!! We quietly closed the door and went back to the desk, where a mother and daughter were loudly complaining about the damp in their room (our friends could also smell damp in theirs). 
The concierge was very apologetic and gave us the choice of two other rooms. We chose one at the front of the hotel, which was smaller but the other one faced an adjacent hotel and empty car lot. We were also given a goodwill gesture of a bottle of wine.
The room was small but well appointed. The bedlinen was clean, and the bathroom was spacious and well fitted. 
After exploring the numerous shops, bars and sights of this magnificent city we decided to have a nightcap at the hotel bar. Soon after two young girls came in and were refused service as they tried to get guys to buy them drinks. It was funny but not what you would expect from a hotel with a decent reputation.

title: “Great location and bike friendly too!!”
text: Hi, I spent one enjoyable week at the Chancellor in October 2005 on a cycling holiday in San Francisco. It would certainly be amongst my first choices of hotel for a return trip. I had a clean, spacious and comfortable room on the top floor (recommended as I imagine the street noise could become annoying on the lower floors). The staff were friendly and helpful, even allowing me to keep my bike in my room which saved a lot of hassle for myself (and probably the staff) when I left the hotel for the early morning bike rides. I didn't like the breakfasts there much and prefered to go over the road and 100 yds up Powell street to a cafe that opened around 6 a.m. (I was jet-lagged) and served good and cheap nourishment (even porridge - great for the chilly mornings). There's a huge bookshop a few doors down from the hotel where I was able to buy all the maps and guides I needed (hint: if you want to cycle in Marin County there's a small bookstore/cafe in the center of Mill Valley that sells a wonderful little cycling map of the area - I didn't see it anywhere else). Anyway, to summarise, a nice, friendly, good value hotel with all the shops, cafes and restaurants you could ever want within a few blocks - but ask for a room near the top.

title: “Fabulous”
text: I am, by my own admission, a complete 'hotel snob'! I travel to New York every December for Christmas shopping, I have stayed at many hotels in the midtown area, some good, some bad but none of them were fabulous, until this year. After reading several reviews I decided to book the Affinia Manhattan and I am so glad I did. I got a fabulous deal by booking direct on their website. The one bedroom suite I booked was fabulous, the reception staff were fabulous, the housekeeping staff were fabulous, the concierge were fabulous. If you're looking for a fabulous hotel in midtown at a reasonable rate then look no further than the Affinia Manhattan, I will be booking this hotel for all future trips to New York.

title: “Great location, great staff!”
text:
After a lot of research, I decided on the Hilton Garden Inn for my family vacation. I booked a month out, but was only able to get a room with a king bed instead of two double beds. Never the less, I squeezed the family (three adults, 7 yo, 5 yo, and twins 2 yo) into two rooms. The rooms were well appointed, no better and no worse than your standard chain hotel room. The windows all pointed into some alleyway, but I don't really stay at Hilton Garden Inns for the view. The beds were a bit stiff for my liking, but that's just a preference. The rooms were clean, and well stocked with a fridge, microwave, LCD flat screen, etc. The bathrooms were clean and a good size.
I booked the Bed and Breakfast rate plan. After doing the math, it made sense to do it since we'd be doing a lot of walking and would need an early start to the day. At $124 a night, I didn't think I'd get two adult breakfasts and all the kids breakfasts (plus the room) for under that. It was a great deal. The breakfast was not your ordinary "continental breakfast". It was a standard American hot breakfast. The first day it was french toast, sausage, bacon, potatoes, corned beef hash, eggs, omelet station, waffles. Plus oatmeal, fruit, pastries, yogurt, etc. It was very well stocked! The second day was the same but with pancakes instead of french toast. The griddle was in plain view and everything hot was almost made to order so it was very fresh! If you're not into the buffett, then you can order off the menu and apply the breakfast voucher toward your tab.
Where the Hilton Garden Inn really excelled was in the location and the staff. The staff was extremely courteous and helpful. When I checked in, I asked for a change of rooms to double beds. They were out, but the staff was very courteous about it. I was given my breakfast vouchers and the front desk person answered all my questions.
The staff at the restaurant was phenomenal! The manager (Brian) was extremely cheerful and upbeat. He was very helpful and made sure our large group was accommodated very well. Every one was always happy and cheerful. They made sure we were happy and cheerful. The large TVs posted throughout also helped keep the kids calm. 
The location is a short 5 minute walk to the White House and about a 10 -15 minute walk to the Smithsonian / Monuments. It's also 50 feet from the Macpherson Metro Station. There's a quiznos, a Cosi, starbucks, and a yogen fruz all within a minute's walk. The only thing is that there are no really family-friendly sit down restaurants. We went to "elephant and castle" an english pub one night, and on another night we gave up after walking around and around and went to the hotel restaurant. It was probably the best burger and fries I've ever had. I can't remember where we went the third night....
Also, since I'm a workaholic, the free wireless + wired internet was nice. they also offered free printing, which I've never seen before.
I definitely recommend this hotel for families with small / young children. It's easy to get anywhere, and is close enough to the metro station if you decide your feet can't take another 15 minute walk back. The staff is awesome and the hotel is nice.

title: “Great Style, Great Price (on weekends)”
text:
Very nice hotel, I love the look here - English Hunting Lodge meets up-to-date mod cons (a la heated floors) in a nicely lived in design that wasn't aggressively trying to be hip. AND, AND I was upgraded to a suite! sweet!!!!! :-) (I think the key here is to check in later i.e. 8pm to have this happen to you.)
The location is out of the way (if you wanna walk to Soho, LES or the Village for example) but the subway is a close 10 min walk.
p.s. A TIP for y'all - I get the best rates for this hotel on http://www.quikbook.com shhhhh. the hotel website sometimes does match it.
One thing to keep in mind: on Saturday nights they host insanely packed and loud parties in the lobby and 2nd floor library, so make sure to stay on floor 8 or higher to avoid the noise - I heard nada from my 18th floor penthouse ;-)

title: “Great Location, Reasonable Prices, but Suites Shrink as Kids Grow”
text: This chain is great when your kids are small, and prices are reasonable for DC. As kids get older, these suites are really suitable for a total of either 3 people, or 4 max with no privacy for the parents. The DC version, enclosing a large (noisy) indoor atrium, has smallish suites that seem only a little larger than regular rooms in nearby hotels I've stayed at, but are divided into bedroom and small livingroom. The result is somewhat claustrophobic if your kids are teenagers. That said, the room was clean if dated,staff was helpful, and the service was fine. Good location for Foggy Bottom and the Mall, and CT Avenue shopping. Above average buffet breakfast choices, average parking rates for DC.

title: “Good one”
text: Stayed here for a night and found that it is quite a good hotel to stay in in the DC area. Good eats not too far from here. It gets a lot of points for its location. The staff was friendly. It is a very big hotel. Will not advice to eat at the hotel. The prices were well pricey.

title: “Omni Chicago has it all!”
text:
Just back from a recent 5-night stay at the Omni Chicago, and I think my 4-year old son summed it up best when he announced on our second night, "I want to live in the Omni Chicago Hotel". The suite was lovely, modern and spacious, with plenty of room for our son to play, as well as a separate sleeping area with an excellent, comfortable bed. The bathroom has ample counter space, and there is also a wet bar in the living area with additional space. A/C kept the room perfectly cool, and was blessedly quiet.
The location is outstanding, right in the middle of the Magnificent Mile, and there are great restaurants and shopping for every taste and budget right outside the door. We took cabs to several museums and the Navy Pier, and the doormen and bellmen were all very helpful in suggesting the best ways to get wherever we wanted to go.
Staff were universally helpful and pleasant, and took time to interact with our son and make him feel welcome. We came to check in very early due to an extremely early morning flight arrival, and we were graciously accommodated. A slight mix-up with the readiness of the room resulted in sincere apologies from the manager (Jewel, who lives up to her name in every way! :) ), a rapid switch to a prepared room, and an offer to enjoy breakfast on the house. Housekeeping was very responsive, and had our room made up during the time periods that I requested each day.
As for breakfast...I can not rave enough. From the homemade, perfect pastries to made-to-order omelettes, the spectacular fresh fruits and artisan bacon and sausages, everything was beautifully presented and, more importantly, tasted as good as it looked. It is well worth the money, and we ate there four out of five mornings.
As Select Guest members we enjoyed the free in-room wifi, the morning delivery of beverages and newspapers, and evening turn-down service. It is free to join, and well worth the few minutes to do so.
We are looking for reasons to return to Chicago sooner than anticipated, in large part due to the excellence of our stay at the Omni. We would never stay anywhere else!

title: “Awesome Hotel & Staff!”
text: This is one of the best hotels I have ever visited. The amenities, such as full breakfast vs Continental & free happy hour for hotel guests, plus beautiful salt water pool, fantastic gym are enough to make you want to move in. The staff is wonderful and work with you beyond any hotel I have ever worked with. I book many Hewlett Packard employees and visitors here and have received only the BEST reviews. Located in the Vintage Park and within walking distances to several top restaurants and many salon services, shopping, etc. You can't beat the location to HP campus in Houston along with safe environment for walking to/from restaurants at night.

title: “Faded elegance”
text: This place flatters to deceive. It sounds proudly on top of Nob Hill and is well located. One past the fierce doorman, the lobby is smart and the welcome was okay but the rooms were incorrect as we were due two twin rooms and were given a double. This was the only Hotel out of 7 or 8 that was like this so not convinced it was our travel agent. The rooms were fine, but that is the best one can say. They were large but the bathrooms tiny and very drab. It all now needs a paint and refurb. The passages were like something out of The Shining! However what really got me annoyed was hey charged for Wifi. Not even Vegas did that. A pathetic extra and summed up the lack of 21st century appearance and outlook. This has been the only place we have stayed in 9 places that charged and was bloody annoying. Not the amount but the principle. The booking of a Taxi to the airport was chaotic. All in all, convenient and good for tram lines, but trading on it's past glories

title: “Westin St Francis...classic hotel”
text: We wanted to go to San Francisco with our sons and their family for a Christmas celebration. We had two babies under one years old and two toddlers. The Westin St Francis provided us with adjoining rooms and Heavenly cribs. We stayed in the historic building and had a view of Union Square. Arrived early and the staff was able to get us into one of the rooms so we could take care of the babies. The location is so great with Union Square across the street, Macy's and all of the great shopping that area has to offer. The hotel staff couldn't have been more helpful. This is the third year we have stayed here and every year we are very pleased with our choice. The hotel parking is expensive but with the babies, strollers and all the "stuff" we will pay the high price otherwise we would park in the public parking and walk a couple of blocks.

title: “Nice room, nice staff”
text: The room exceeded our expectations. We had a king suite, which was very large with a separate living room. The cookies at check in were such a nice touch! The staff was also good, and having and indoor pool and hottub is a definite plus!!! The only downside is the location... unless you want to be in the Harvard Area. Harvard was a short walk, but downtown and most of the dining/attractions are an expensive cab ride away.

title: “Our third visit this year”
text: What else to say; good situation in the earth of Manhattan, a lot of space (suite) and clean. Gently staff, highly recommended!

title: “Choose this hotel on your trip to Chicago”
text:
This is a great hotel.We really like Best Western hotels, but the FREE parking was a great
bonus. We arrived early with no problem.We were told we could park and check in later.The man at the front desk (Mike) was fantastic,every front desk employee should be like him. he was friendly and helpful.Every time we entered the hotel,he greeted us as though we were his good friends.The room was very clean.We were on the sixth floor and had a good view.There is a restaurant on site,the breakfast was really good.We purchased a bus pass
($11.50 for 2 people for 24 hrs) It was a great value.When we return to Chicago-this is what
we would do again.it was a short walk to the stops,and we were able to go to Millenium Park,Grant Park,Navy Pier,Willis(Sears)tower,John Hancock Observatory and other attractions.We were able to walk to Gino's Pizza for lunch(great)and Ed Debovick's for dinner
We stayed in 8 hotels on a vacation and this was the best.(some of the others were great, also- but because of Mike and his warmness we rated it our best.

title: “medical center”
text: nearby the Houston's medical center & that's the only good thing about the location. rooms are very big. the hotel overall is old & not that clean

title: “Not Worth The Money”
text: The blaring music in the lobby when we arrived should have been my first clue that the place is run by teenagers. I asked for extra towels, they did not arrive. I called at 1:30 p.m. to ask that the room be made up, at 3:30 the room was still not made up. The complimentary newspaper was not delivered. The lighting in the bathroom is HORRIBLE. The makeup mirror is worthless because of the poor lighting in the bathroom. Whoever designed the lighting in the bedroom and bathroom needs to go back to design school to learn something practical. The breakfast was obviously microwaved and not freshly cooked. I will not stay here again.

title: “Best value in the San Diego, CA area! We would stay there again!”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Western Inn & Suites in Old Town for 6 nights in March 2012 on our vacation to San Diego. It was more than I expected -- a quiet, clean, affordable room with courteous staff day and night, free wireless (lots of hotels are now charging). The breakfast was cold cereal and coffee, but we came not expecting a full breakfast. However, this hotel is just a couple of blocks off the main Old Town area with lots of great restaurants and within walking distance of the main transit area where we could catch a bus, train, or trolley. No need to rent a car. I would encourage families to stay in this hotel. It's a bargain!

title: “Best Place I have ever stayed!”
text: This place was, by far, the nicest place with the friendliest staff that I have ever stayed! We were in town for a concert for ine night, and have never had a more pleasant hotel stay. I highly recommend this hotel if you have any business at Ohio State or close by. It is pricey, but well worth it!

title: “Very Beautiful Hotel and Great Location”
text: Be sure to request a river-view room for great views of Chicago. Service is first-rate. Very Nice lobby. Easy check-in and check-out. Rooms are the best to be had.

title: “Standard Kimpton”
text:
I've stayed at 70 Park Avenue several times for both business and leisure. The price usually seems to be right ($250 range) which is the main draw, as the neighborhood isn't very exciting. 
The good:
– Because I am a Kimpton In Touch member, I seem to be upgraded at this property fairly often. The corner king rooms over nice views of Park Avenue and abundant light, which is a rarity in NYC hotels.
– The beds are typical, very comfortable Kimpton beds.
– The desk is great and extremely functional.
– There is an extra chair so you won't need to resort to sitting on the desk chair or the bed.
The bad:
– It is nearly impossible to catch a cab outside this hotel. Because it is located downwind of Grand Central, you can forget about getting a cab between 8-10am and 3-6pm. Not handy.
– The rooms are tiny. Closet space is not abundant and the bathrooms are teeny.
Overall, I will continue to stay here when the Soho Grand is at capacity or out of my price range (during the winter). It is clean, the staff friendly and the room is comfortable which helps you forget the size.

title: “Overall A Great Hotel”
text: We stayed at this hotel in march for 3 nights.Found the location perfect for everything we wanted to see.The hotel lobby is very grand.It has a nice seating area and bar to relax in after a hard days sightseeing!! Beware bar prices are quite expensive.The rooms were ideal for the time that you spend in them,only downfall was the lighting in them is quite poor.Overall we enjoyed our stay at the hotel,and would definately return here.

title: “Needs a Revamp”
text: I really wanted to love the Grand Hyatt in San Francisco. The location is fantastic. The staff was so friendly, helpful and welcoming. The city view from our room was lovely. But the rooms...ugh. Really tired and shabby. There were weird stains on the lampshades, holes in the curtains, scuffs all over the walls. The room was comfortable, just really rough around the edges and worn out. Also, when we checked out there were a lot of people waiting for their cars outside and we were told it would take up to 1/2 hour to get our car from the valet. It didn't actually end up taking quite that long for us, but there were others still standing there who'd been waiting before we were. Considering there is a huge parking garage (much cheaper) at the corner of Stockton and Sutter, we could have parked the car ourselves and walk across the street. I would only consider staying here again if the hotel undergoes a renovation. There are way too many other great places to stay in the city for this price.

title: “The people and place is very nice”
text: The hotel is very nice. the staff is great. They are very helpful and nice. Rooms are clean. I like the breakfast and evening meals. The work out room can use additional machines but its pretty good. I would recommend the hotel to others.

title: “Great choice of accommodation”
text:
Thank you to all the wonderful staff at Buena Vista. San was amazing with check in, bookings of tours, information on local restaurants, what and where to see San francisco's best, photocopying maps and making sure i was aok. My back room was quaint clean and roomy and so quiet. Breakfast is basic and quite adequate - juice coffee pastries and fruit.
San Francisco tour bus stops at the front door of the hotel. local restaurants 2 minute walk to Union street, Italian restaurant sensational dining. 
San Francisco is such a friendly city and my first visit started off with such smiles and welcomes at Buena Vista motor inn. The rate for accommodation was so reasonable considering I stayed the first round of America's cup trials.
Make sure you visit Union square, Chinese gardens, Haight Ashbury and wear a flower in your hair, cross the Golden gate bridge, ride the cable car and start that early as the queues get so long after lunch even week days, the incredible seafood restaurants at Fisherman's wharf, Pier 39 and be mesmerised by the local seals and buy some of the freshest tastiest fruit ever from the local market at the Pier. Many wonderful memories from this welcoming city.

title: “Great Hotel in the Heart of Chicago”
text:
I have read the majority of the reviews about the Marriott Chicago Downtown Magnificent Mile. The hotel does have a few flaws: the rooms are smaller, the AC did not work correctly and the bathroom is very very tiny. However, the service was amazing. Luke and Greta at the front desk were amazing. Service is priceless and they provided priceless service. I am a fan of Room Service and I have to say that the room service was very good and prompt and on time. The hotel is located right on the Magnigicent Mile and close to every major downtwon attration. I walked everywhere and enjoyed the amazing city of Chicago. I used Marriot Vitrual Concierge Service and I was impressed when I got back from my day of sighseein that extra pillows and towels were delivered to my room. 
A great hotel on the Magnifcent Mile, which Magnificent Staff...

title: “Everything was INCREDIBLE!”
text:
The people are friendly and very attentive. Even though they do not provide a free breakfast, their restaurant had great food. The indoor pool is clean with no overwhelming chlorine smell and best of all, the water is wonderfully warm! The rooms are beautifully updated and clean. We wish we could have stayed longer since this is the BEST hotel we have ever stayed at.
Next time we visit the Memphis area, we are definitely staying here again!!! Thanks to all the staff at this hotel for the great work and hospitality!

title: “Worth Every Penny”
text:
This was my first stay here at the best western hollywood plaza so i really didnt know what to expect. We got there about 3-4 hours before normal check in time and they gave us a generous early check in.
The room was exceptional and exceeded my expectations of a motel room. The bed was nice, neat and clean (no bed bugs of any sort). There was a coffee maker, microwave and mini fridge. The bathroom was spacious and had a giant mirror on the wall. Everything was spot clean.
To be honest i was very hesitant when booking this room because cleanliness was my absolute top concern. And this motel satisfied every concern of mine. The location cant be beat either, its just a few steps away from hollywood and highland and a few miles away from universal studios so its right in the heard of hollywood. I would DEFINITELY stay here again.

title: “Great Experience at the Michelangelo”
text: We spent three nights at the Michelangelo Hotel in NYC. Nicely appointed lobby and friendly front desk staff. Our room was lovely, with a Bose CD system, very comfortable bed, and a good sized bathroom with a large tub. It was certainly very spacious by New York standards and VERY quiet (OK, our room did face a brick wall but I guess that was the trade-off). Staff were very helpful and self-parking was only $ 23 per day and located right next to the hotel. A great experience!

title: “Great Place, Great Location, Great Price”
text: Just got back form the Red Roof Inn Chicago. First the location is EXCELLENET- ½ Block from everything you want on the magnificent mile, and next to it is the Marriott (whose prices were 3x that of the red roof inn). The rooms were nice. We got a king Suite with king bed and bath in one room and a separate living room with fold out bed and its own bath. We also got a double deluxe with a big room and two double beds. The staff was very friendly and helped us with everything we needed. We had a late flight leaving and we were able to store our baggage after we had checked out and they have internet that you can rent. The are remolding and it looks like the place will be ever better the next time we stay there. This is not a 5 star but it is a wonderful place for the price, I HIGHLY suggest the red roof inn.

title: “Shabby and a little seedy”
text: I'm bolted inside my little tiny, shabby room. The curtains don't match. The a/c works sporadically. The other guests look a little scary. The walls are very thin and I was woken up numerous times as the other guests slammed doors or flushed toilets. There's a lot of street noise from Michigan Av. This room was $200 a night. I can't wait to get out of here!

title: “Great boutique Inn - would stay again”
text: spacious room - king size bed - separate dressing room w/sink, mirror and closet, , delicious full breakfast every day, quaint elevator, very quiet, very clean. staff very pleasant and accommodating, 2 blocks off cable car on Powell, 2 blocks from Chinatown. buy a CityPass before you go. We passed that up and it would have been a great value. We purchased a Muni/Bart/cable car pass at the underground tourist info centre at the bottom of Powell St. Got us most places.

title: “More than our expectation!”
text: We stayed here around New year's day. The stuffs are kind and the room was new and clean. This hotel is so close to the subway station. Breakfast service was also good. Pverall, it was more than our expectation, except for the price. It was expensive a little.

title: “Great Place To Stay in New York City”
text: Recently traveled to New York City and stayed at the Marquis Marriott right in Times Square. The view was outstanding and would say to ask for a Times Square View room. The breakfast buffet on the eighth floor dinning area was very good as was the service. The hotel was clean and first class. Easy walking district to all Broadway Plays and Rockafeller Center. I would stay here again on my next trip to the city. Very clean and very confortable. Room service quick and food was good. The View Dinning roommmm is a rotating dinning artea that allows you a 360 degree look at the city while you are dinning. The food was pricy but the service was very good.

title: “Not the level of quality I expect from Westin”
text: I booked this hotel because it was convienient to LAX and I had a very good deal on the room rate. I would have been very disappointed if I'd paid the regular rate for the room; it was mediocre at best with the bathroom not living up to what I've come to expect from Westin. I only stayed one night so I think my review might have been a little worse if I'd stayed longer. The Daily Grill in the lobby is nice and had the standard hotel breakfast buffet. Parking was $25 for each 24-hour period. The bed was very comfortable and the room was clean. WiFi was NOT free which would have been frustrating had I stayed more than one night. If you're looking for convience to LAX and can get a good deal on the room rate (through Priceline, etc...), then it's a decent hotel. But I would NOT give this hotel a 4-Star rating.

title: “Quick Family Trip”
text: The property is in a good location that is within walking distance to all the sights in Baltimore. It is right in the middle of Harbor East that has alot of restaurants to eat at. The hotel itself was nice and the staff was very friendly. The rooms were clean and offered a kitchen which was helpful keeping our food cold for our kid. The hotel has an agreement with the MAC to be able to use the fitness and pool facilities. If you are a health nut this is a big plus for you, however it is a strange set up if you just want to take your kid to the pool. Parking is a nightmare, but is expected in a city. $32 dollars for valet or $22 self parking with no in/out privileges. The valet lost my car in the parking garage but was able to find it an hour later. I guess that's good. Over all good place to stay. I would recommend it if you had a family.

title: “Consistently great hotel”
text: I have stayed here close to ten times, and every visit is as great as the last. The staff is very professional and accommodating, the grounds are gorgeous, and the guest rooms are spacious and elegant. The on-site gym is reason enough to stay here - it is one of the best in the country. Whether working out with weights or cardio, taking a class, or grabbing a bite at the health-conscious cafe, it is a treat to go to this gym.

title: “This hotel was perfect........”
text: my husband and I went to Chicago for a wedding. We had very limited time so we wanted to stay at a hotel which would be centrally located to everything. This hotel was the best. The rooms were nice and clean. Bathroom a bit small but OK. The lobby was packed which was nice if you like that for ambiance. Location for shopping and restaurants was great. Can't be beat!

title: “update needed”
text: Customer service was great. The hotel needs help. Year after year we stay because we like Country Inn & Suites but every year it gets worse. It is advertised on the outside of the building that they have an indoor pool but they don’t tell you it feels like ice. The Hot tub isn’t hot either, cooler than normal bath water. The pool and hot tub need to be resurfaced as you can see and feel bare ruff cement all over the bottom. The bathroom had mold all around the shower and the faucet and shower head were very corroded. It took ten minutes for the water coming out of the faucet to finally start to drip out of the shower head. The temperature control in the rooms is also very outdated. The employees are very nice and helpful but the hotel it's self is lacking!

title: “Great hotel”
text:
My boyfriend and I stayed at this hotel for 5 nights in march 2008.
I picked it after reading good reviews and would highly reccommend it. Its ideally situated as its a five minute walk from times square and close to the subways. I felt very safe in the vacinity of the hotel.
Our room was on the inside of the hotel and our view was of offices and not very exciting. But I certainly didnt spend much time in the room looking out of my window!
I found the hotel very clean, the staff were helpful and the room although not huge, was perfect for our needs.
The bonus is the breakfast that is provided free. I found that lots of hotels dont do breakfasts as new yorkers eat out. We saved a lot of money that we would have spent on breakfasts.
If I ever return to New York I will definitely stay here again.

title: “Amazing hotel for the price!”
text: We were visiting Denver for one night and were looking for a reasonable hotel near the downtown area. After calling several places and getting quoted approx $200 a night we found the Warwick for $120. I wasnt expecting much but was very surprised when we got there. First of all when we pulled up the valet said parking was $26 per night but then was nice enough to point out that if we parked on the street by a meter we would only spend $2.00! So happy for the savings! The front desk staff was super nice. Then we got up to the room and it was awesome! Comfy king bed with nice linens, private balcony that you can sit on, beautiful bathroom with marble shower. They are also the only hotel in downtown Denver with a rooftop pool which was warm and had a nice view of downtown. The hotel was walking distance to the Capitol.

title: “Great Location..no problem..Great food..no problem...Relaxation.WHAT A PROBLEM!!”
text: Stayed for new years eve and had a nice view of the fireworks. Cudos to Baltimore on that show. My wife and I were wanting a safe vantage point of the show away from the drunk drivers and it seemed we would have been better off out with the crowds, because we think all the drunks were in the hotel! Very thin walls which made hearing vomiting from the neighbors above us easy. Not to mention all the hallway noises. Given, it was New Years, but give me a break, it was as they were in the same room!

title: “Excellent Service”
text: Needed to pull family together for a graduation and the folks in the club lounge were extremely accommodating for us. Shawn Zenszer who works in the club lounge offered to help at every turn! Really nice stay, thanks to the friendly and helpful staff.

title: “Under Construction”
text: I am not complaining about the hotel but it would have been nice to know in advance that the pool was closed. That is the only reason we chose to stay at this particular Hampton Inn. We have two young boys who were very excited about being able to go swimming and the pool had been closed for a week and that was not posted on the website! The lobby and some other areas were under construction as well . The breakfast area was so small that we had to get our food and go back to the room to eat because there was nowhere to sit. The food was delicious and the rooms were very nice and clean but it would have been great to know all of this was going on at that time.

title: “Hotel Sax was okay”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the hotel sax for 2 nights in August. I have mixed opinions about the hotel. While we were kind of neutral about our experience (and wouldn't stay there again), I can understand why others would love it. The hotel is very trendy and chic. We stayed in the deluxe king room. 
The goods: The bed and pillows are super comfortable. Prob the best I’ve ever had in a hotel. The staff was very friendly. Both check in and check out was seamless. The rooms were really clean. The hotel has a really cool & young atmosphere. It’s in a great location. It’s only a block away from the downtown nightlife, and if you’re planning on a trip to the house of blues, it’s pretty much in the same parking lot. It’s a little further from Navy Pier and such than other hotels are, but it is walkable (we walked it) and/or taxis are cheap. Great flat screen tv.
The negatives: The rooms were small and dark compared to what I’ve stayed in before. There was zero counter space (or hair dryer) in the bathroom. The ‘atmosphere’ wasn’t really our style. It kind of has the atmosphere of a ‘party’ hotel in that there’s a pretty well rounded bar in the room, the ‘Studio’ - which is like a high tech game room, Crimson Lounge is downstairs (a very popular club), the House of Blues is across the street, etc. There was nothing wrong with this, but, for example -it wouldn’t be a place I would ask my parents to stay. Our telephone wasn’t working and the a/c started clicking really bad for awhile. They missed our wakeup call but called and apologized. The walls are a little thin and we could sometimes hear the tv in the room next to us. 
Besides the hotel, cool things to do in Chicago: of course go to navy pier and stay for the fireworks. Take one of the boat tours. We took the sail boat one. Looking back, probably would have done the more traditional ones. The zoo is only so-so but good for kids. Look for the hot tix location to get discounted theatre tickets. The staff pretty much know what’s showing at every theatre in town. We saw ‘Alice’ at the looking glass theatre. It was fantastic and great for kids and adults. The green mill was a really cool jazz bar with a lot of history (I guess it was Al Capone’s old hub). Don’t go there if you want to drink and party though. They ask people not to speak while people are playing. Wrigley field was AWESOME. Andy’s Jazz Club was tons of fun and there’s other bars in its proximity (that was our one night of staying up too late and drinking too much). Overall, I would definitely go back to Chicago. I feel there’s a lot we didn’t get to do.

title: “Gotta do it”
text:
I was a tad sceptical having read other reviews but this place rocks!! On approach it doesn't look like much but on entering the lobby you are immersed in the Elvis phenomena straight away.
The rooms although basic are very well appointed and the bed is large enough for 3!! The bathroom was small and the bath really low, in comparison to ones in the UK. Also, for us Brits - beware the loo......low toilet but high water level in there.
Breakfast was basic cereals and toast etc, but all that you would want before going out.
Graceland is but a few minutes walk away and there is a FREE shuttle bus that takes you into Memphis with Sun Studios and Beale Street. Well worth the price.
All in all a good visit. I would recommend staying at the hotel and using it as a base as it is far enough out of Memphis to avoid being in the hub but close enough to get to see all of the attractions.

title: “Labor Day Stay”
text: My mom and I have been staying here for the past 3 out of 4 years every Labor Day (Sunday and Monday) as we attend the U.S. Open. Our stay was good, although, I had to call down and have someone provide the remote for the TV - since it was not in the room upon check-in. And, for $14.00 per day - you can get WIFI in the room - which I think it outrageous! Fortunately I do have a data plan for my IPAD, but I don't understand why I can get free WIFI at the Hampton Inn (the next hotel we stayed in in Niagara Falls for the rest of the week) for a room that costs $71.00 per nite and not at this upscale hotel! Also, the hotel is covered in scaffolding - to the extent i did not even recognize it!

title: “not recommended”
text:
Noisy room, located near elevators. Constant 'whirring' sounds, elevator doors clunking.
Cigarette burns on carpet in room. I thought it was a non-smoking hotel.
Front desk lost my reservation. I requested a handicap shower. Didn't get it. Maybe I should have brought a Doctor's note.
When I return to my room after a long day of training, I find housekeeping still in my room with the door closed. WTF?
A manager called a few hours after I submitted my customer survey, I couldn't speak at the moment, said he would call back. Never did.
I could go on, but why waste my time?

title: “Stayed 3 nights”
text: This hotel offers a light snack at night so eat a big lunch . I'm talking chips and salsa, hot dogs(which I didn't have) one night chicken fingers (they were good). The place was packed every night and every morning, We had good value and would stay again, the front desk staff were very helpful. Thanks for the nice stay!

title: “Quiet Hotel Convenient to Mayo Clinic”
text: Brought my wife down for appointments at Mayo Clinic. Hotel offers Mayo Clinic discount and is a smooth 12 minute drive away down Butler Blvd. Staff is friendly and accomodating. Rooms are quiet and clean. Room a little larger than most in this price range. Free breakfast was very good as free breakfasts go. Bed clean and comfortable. Grounds are well landscaped and clean. The only thing that bothered me slightly was the air conditioning system. It has a large unit under the window and cuts on and off frequently instead of constantly blowing. Bathroom is clean and roomy with a nice shower. Would stay here on return visit.

title: “My new favorite SF Hotel”
text:
Just so you know my taste, The Fairmont is my favorite SF hotel. Kensington Park is another one that I like a lot when the price is right. I don't like to pay over $140 a night to stay in SF. I stayed at Hotel Monaco for five days with my husband while he was attending MacWorld over Valentine's Day weekend. We paid $144 for every night except one, which was $195.
The Good: Clean, quiet and gorgeous with excellent service. The friendly staff made us feel very comfortable. I loved that the cleaning crew was quiet in the mornings. I didn't hear anything in the hallways. I can't stand it when I hear the maids yelling to each other in the halls. Hello! I'm on vacation - trying to sleep here! 
The front desk staff booked the perfect place for a business dinner we were hosting. It was exactly what we wanted. The staff know the city well, which is tough with all of the excellent options in SF. For Kimpton members, they have free Wifi. I consider that essential at any hotel. They even gave us a voucher for $10 worth of goods from the minibar, which was well stocked with lots of different choices. 
I loved that they had a DVD player and stereo with CD's in the room. I didn't have to play everything off of the computer. I fell in love with our goldfish. The location is excellent. Walking distance to BART. Not too close to Union Square so it's quiet and not too far out of the Theater District to be in the Tenderloin. Walking distance from the two best diners in the city (Pinecrest and Dotty's). The free cocktail hour, hot chocolate at 2:00 and morning coffee and tea bar in the lounge by the fireplace were fantastic. They had Wii set up to play one night and another night we watched the Olympics. It's all the little things that make this place so fun to stay in. 
Could Use Improvement:
I ordered oatmeal with raisins and brown sugar from Room Service. I was given only oatmeal with four raisins and nothing else. When I order room service, for $16 (after charges), I expect to be given several different condiment options with my order, in addition to what is listed on the menu of course. Room Service promptly fixed their mistake. The guy was at my door in under three minutes. Still, no milk, no butter, no extra raisins...have these people never eaten oatmeal before? So, the room service is pretty lame. 
Lastly, I agree with the person who said that their pillows are funky. They are like too puffy. I had a hard time sleeping on them the first night but, then I got used to it. And was way too comfortable in that bed because I took about 100 naps.
I couldn't get the radio/ iPod player to work - but that may have been user error/the iPhone wouldn't work with it. 
Other than that, I loved this hotel. It's gorgeous and next time I hope to take advantage of the gym and in-room massage.

title: “We can't wait for our next stay!”
text:
When we first were looking for hotels in Boston, we were overwhelmed by the number of choices. After searching for a couple of weeks we decided on the Fairmont and I'm so happy we did. My husband and I were debating on which room or suite we wanted to book. There are about 11 options and after reading other reviews, we decided on the Deluxe Harbor View Room. This ended up being the best financial move for us. It also gave my husband an excuse to use the savings to eat lobster at every meal! I say, if you're planing on sightseeing, save the money and go for a room.
Here's what we really thought of the place:
Service - Everyone was professional and welcoming. Even though we weren't staying in the most expensive suite, they treated us like we were. I had read such terrible things about Bostonians and how rude they are, but we never encountered this here. The front desk was extremely helpful, just ask and they were on top of it. Nobody hesitated to help. 
Sleep Quality - The bed, pillows, duvet, and linens were amazing! Both of us slept comfortably. Every morning we woke up, we felt refreshed. The bed helped a lot to relax us after walking over 5 miles every day. Plus, nothing beats falling into a freshly made bed and propping up your legs. 
Cleanliness - The space was very clean. Nothing to complain about. They did a great job of keeping the room and bathroom looking brand new. There were no signs of damage or "funny" business. 
Location - You can't beat this location! We had our windows open every night (even on the first floor we felt safe). The breeze from the harbor was our favorite part. When you don't live anywhere near the ocean, you want to enjoy it as much as possible when it's around. We were told by our friends from Boston, to stay in the North End (where the hotel is located). The hotel is situated around a ton of amazing Italian restaurants and sites. Our friends told us to skip the car rental (because parking in the city is near impossible) and the hotel staff told us about the subway/train system. A few blocks from the hotel you can walk to the main part of the city, the rest of the harbor, or to a ton of historical sites. We enjoyed being in the city to shop and sightsee, but my husband and I like our quiet too. This hotel gave us that option. We never felt like we were in any danger walking around. The location was perfect, especially if you want a peaceful night's sleep but be close to the downtown. 
Rooms - The bedroom was a comfortable size, even with all the furniture. We had a ton of luggage with us and we never felt like we were cramped. The bathroom was amazing too. The shower was roomy and the vanity/sink area was really nice. I would have to point out, if you are staying here with someone you don't feel comfortable going #2, this is probably not a good option for you. The toilet closet is just a glass door separating you and the rest of the bathroom. Not very smell or sound proof. 
Overall - We can't wait for our next trip back to Boston. We will definitely book at the Fairmont again. To us, there's no need to look any where else. Nothing could top the experience and comfort we had here. Plus, we loved the boat taxi from the airport to the hotel. What a great way to be welcomed into Boston!

title: “WService Not So Good”
text:
The room was great and the location is perfect, but the service.....not so good. We went with another couple, so we had 2 rooms. One of the rooms was supposed to be river view, one not. This is what we were told on the phone the day before we checked in. When we got there, it was a whole different story. After we got to our room and discovered that neither room was river view (with a balcony), I went down to the lobby to get the problem fixed. As I stood in line for 30 minutes while the girls at the desk spent a great deal of time getting the guy in front of me the biggest balcony they could find on the river, I was told there were not river view rooms left. 
 The worst part is that this whole ordeal was the other couple had given us the room as a Christmas gift, and she wanted it to be so perfect. Not, and then on top of it, they billed our room to us instead of our friends. She was so upset about the room mix up, I didn't have the heart to tell her about the billing mix up. I guess she will find out when she gets her credit card bill.
We stay at embassy suites all the time when we travel, but I have never been treated like I was the ugly step child. Not happy with the service.

title: “ok hotel good staff just wrong part of town”
text: good hotel with great front desk staff just a shame it is near the tenderloin area of the city (more or less a no go area) the hotel itself is clean and secure , we recieved an upgrade as on honeymoon but still room was quite small. opal is ok but next time i would look for a hotel in a different part of the city

title: “Quality at an affordable price.”
text:
Caught up in the European travel chaos caused by bad weather, I had to call the Chelsea Pines several times to delay my arrival, cancel cars etc. Each call was dealt with patience and a ' don't worry, we look forward to seeing you when you do eventually arrive ' . Exactly what I needed to hear in my time of panic and uncertainty !
This care and concern for the client was reinforced when I finally arrived for one nights stay, instead of the original four. Immediate warmth and friendliness from the owner Jay Lesiger plus helpful info on restaurants and the local area; ( Thanks Jay for steering me towards Chelsea Market and the High Line). Over my brief stay all the staff shared the same principles of being friendly and helpful.
And then there was the comfort of my room - the Anne Frances since you ask. Clean, spacious, well appointed. ( The room that is, not Anne Frances ). Are you getting the impression I liked this place ? You bet I did. I will be back there in a shot the next time I visit New York and I would recommend it without hesitation. Perfect location, perfect service, perfect price.

title: “nice”
text: i liked the rooms and the breakfast had changed everyday so it was never the same. Also i liked the amenities and the pool was very pleasant. a lil too much chlorine in the hot tub but over all pleasant stay!!

title: “Great staff”
text:
What a pleasant surprise the James was - very nice little boutique hotel that has lovely staff. Think W hotel without the attitude. Great beds...and I mean great, Kiehls products in the bathrooms, a fabulous restaurant in the hotel and great cookies at turndown.
I'll definitely be back to the James and thoroughly recommend it!

title: “Room 705 - bathroom freezing”
text:
Rooms not available on check-in. Had to wait over 1 hour for room to be cleaned.
Room 705 - spacious and comfy bed, BUT bathroom was absolutely freezing with icy draft through windows.
Reception staff/duty manager - not very helpful. Gave impression that they just wanted to get rid of you.
Breakfast good and good location.
Would not use again.

title: “Mount Vernon Hotel”
text: I was in Baltimore for surgery at Mercy Medical Center and stayed at the Mount Vernon. It was 4/10th of a mile from Mercy. It was clean and the rooms were huge. We arrived late and even though I called and told them we'd be late and they assured me there would be parking in their garage however there wasn't any and we had to use public parking a block away and we had to pay for that which was a little unsettling to walk a block to the hotel at 11 pm but we didn't have any problems. The hotel is located near the Baltimore Basillica which was very beautiful and the original Washington Monument. Baltimore is a great city but you do need to be mindful of your surroundings. The Mount Vernon area is one of the nicer areas of the city.

title: “Lovely hotel in perfect location”
text: The Hotel Elysee has a perfect location. We were able to walk almost everywhere we went...Central Park, 'Jersey Boys', restaurants, MOMA. The club room, where breakfast and afternoon wine/cheese were served, was arranged so one could enjoy privacy or the company of other guests. Our room was small but had every convenience we needed EXCEPT there was no functioning internet connectivity in the room. We were only able to connect in the Club Room using the administration's server. Hopefully, this is a temporary problem. The Monkey Bar was delightful and the food delicious.

title: “Great Stay at Stay”
text:
Excellent Stay. 
Arrived, room wasn't ready but was upgraded to their largest room - which is by no means big - but for NYC standards - was excellent.
This is a boutique hotel - so expect a small luxury hotel complete with a fantastic bar, great environment and retro modern lobby.
Would stay at Stay again.

title: “Stuck in Phoenix for Surgery”
text: I recently was in phoenix for liver surgery and my insurance company book myself and my husband for 9 days in Phoenix Place and while i read the reviews and looked at the photos. I was scared at a first considering I would be doing a lot of time inside a hotel room. First let me say that yes this hotel could use a couple of updates but what hotel that is not brand spanking new couldn't. With that being said the staff, the area, and the hotel itself was wonderful. It was quiet, the AC worked awesome, and the courtyard area they had was wonderful to walk around in when I could walk around. The staff was kind and helpful, the breakfast each day was good, and the walgreens was close. Next trip to Phoenix I will be staying here again, Thanks Nick and everyone else.

title: “Good place to stay”
text: The hotel is in a good location at the edge of downtown just a few blocks from the Space Needle and is near many good restaurants. There was not a problem with the construction near the hotel, but some band nerds staying in the hotel for a band competition kept us up one night. Hotel security snuffed them out pretty quickly. We enjoyed hot breakfast and the firplace in our room we.

title: “This will be our home for future Chicago visits.”
text: From the initial greeting at the door to final checkout, the staff could not have been more attentive. The location is very near the Art Museum, the reason for our visit. The room was spotless and quiet at night. Could not find fault with this property.

title: “Wow!”
text:
I hestitate to write a review as I'd love to keep this place a secret!
The staff are very friendly and helpful. We would phone them from the streets of New York to get advice and information.
The rooms are extremely clean, and very quiet - must be well insulated as we weren't disturbed by any outside noises. Although the rooms are a bit small, there's enough room to store your baggage and move around with no problem.
Free Continental breakfast and internet access is indeed a plus.
Only one elevator, but we never waited for more than one minute for the elevator and we were on the top (9th floor) and the hotel was completely booked.
Perfect location. Just down the street from Times Square and Broadway theatres.
Room rate we received was very reasonable and one of the cheapest I found when looking for a NYC hotel .... and I checked rates and reviews of hundreds of hotels.
The secret is out! This is the place to stay and we will be back.

title: “Poor rooms”
text: Airconditioning wasn't working, room was too tiny, dark and congested, didn't sleep very much. Comped one cocktail and free wifi, should have comped the night stay....Next day got moved to slightly bigger room with zircon working. Got a better sleep but decided to move out and stay at the intercontinental at same rate $350. Service was friendly although manager should have comped the room. Would not recommend....

title: “Love This Hotel”
text:
We are staying here now. We have stayed a few times before, years ago and my teenage daughter wanted to stay her again, instead of the other 4* hotel down the street. Last time we stayed here, they let me have the amenities of being a loyalty member even though we booked through priceline. This time I was told because I booked through priceline, I was not entitled to any of the amenities. We were not asked if we ]wanted 1 bed or 2, even though I have a 13 year old who would have rather gotten her own bed to sleep in. Also, when we got to the room there were used rags and towels on the bathroom floor. I was told someone would be right up to clean them up and this is true. But makes me wonder when I got the call that the plumber was fixing the toliet and forgot the rags, does that mean the floor wasn't cleaned???
I have always liked staying here because no matter how you got the room (direclty or through priceline) they treated you the same. This time I am feeling a little slighted by using priceline. Also, got an older room, where the bathroom sink has a crack in it and alittle worn.
Hopefully, when we need to use the towncar tonight, we will not be told "no", because of the pricleine stigma.
Also, do not know if there is an age limit on the kid's pack, but my daughter was miffed that she wasn't offered one.
We will see how it goes today. Got to leave for Universal.....

title: “Great Hotwire deal.”
text: I was a little skeptical when this hotel was revealed. But for the rate what a value. Great location clean exceeded my expectations. Parking was more than the price listed on the web site. Overall great stay.

title: “Clean great hotel at a resonable price”
text: The staff was friendly and accommodating. We were supposed to arrive in Detroit at 1am for the Final Four tournament. Due to a 4 hour detour we arrived at 7:30 am. After a bit of confusion at check-in, the staff was gracious enough to extend our check-out time to 2:00, despite the very busy weekend. My husband and I were able to get some sleep and take a shower before we moved to our next hotel. The rooms were very clean, roomy, and comfortable. The hotel restaurant was excellent for a breakfast buffet and the views are awesome!

title: “The best business traveler's hotel in Jax with class and style!”
text:
I really like the decor of this hotel, the lobby and the rooms. Staff is professional. The bar is small but has 2 big screen tvs, so you can sip on your drink and be entertained if you're by yourself (as I frequently am, travelling alone). The lady bartender who works there M-W is sweet as can be, and even made everyone a shooter at the end of the night.
The room has adequate seating with a lounger and chaise, as well as a really nice desk. Internet is free and there was a fridge in my room, hidden by wooden paneling. I have to say again, that I loved the decor. Dark wood, paneling at the bed's headboard, earthy and rich brown tones. The bed was very comfortable as well.
Would definitely stay here again! Class, convenience, without all the nickel-and-diming you see at hotels that are 4 stars and above. One of the nicest experiences at a hotel I've ever had.

title: “Excellent”
text: Comfortable Hotel superbly located in Back Bay. Walking distance from Downtown and close to all transportation. Nice spacious room. I particularly liked the fitness centre and pool and the supermarket directly over the road.

title: “Cool hotel, good staff, nice amenities”
text:
Stayed in room #1407 for three nights. King bed, large room and bathroom for the city. The hotel’s design is on the stark side. I generally don’t like design hotels b/c they look cool but are rarely functional (the cooler the shower looks the more it leaks) – and there’s usually an air of snob. The Andaz is different – it’s a really good hybrid of chic and friendly. I was met immediately when I arrived – no real check-in desk, just a bunch of folks w. iPads. I was offered a drink and quickly checked in. Room 1407 is spacious. No view to speak of – but quiet and calm. The bed was good – a little firm, more along the lines of a European hotel bed than American. Great bedding and pillows. Lots of plugs for gadgets. There’s a full-length mirror – it pulls out from wall beside mini-fridge area. Small closet. Blackout shades to assure privacy and good sleep quality. Flat screen TV w. lots of channels – but most of the time I was there the satellite was iffy. Had three room service breakfasts – good food and fast service. I asked for a NY Times and rec’d gratis. Duane Reade (drug store) across the street. 
The only thing I really didn’t like about the room was poor lighting. It’s much too dark in the bathroom and area by the closet mirror. I dragged a freestanding lamp in to help but it was still much too dark. A lady needs her light to primp. 
The 1 & 2 lines are very close. Short walk to stock market, Trinity church, Century 21, South St. Seaport and Century 21. Wall St. is much livelier after hours than it used to be – but it’s still pretty quiet at night. 
Ate in the formal restaurant – very good food and service. Also had drinks and food at the bar. Good drink and the crab cake – while minute – was yummy. 
Pros
Quiet location, good for sleep
Good-sized room for NYC
Free Wi-Fi with good signal
Good work area
Free snacks & water – why don’t all hotels do this? 
Free coffee & lattes downstairs
Friendly staff
Good bedding & pillows
Strong shower strength, very large shower
Cons
Very poor lighting in bathroom and closet/mirror area
Satellite TV was in and out most of my stay

title: “Stay away -Worst customer service”
text:
