Reached hotel at 11 pm , have to wait 20 min to check in 
Asked desk clerk for little late check out for I'm choice GP member then lady with name of Phillips wards came in picture and started screaming that ibdont know why people come with such demand and she don't give a damn and I can complain whom ever I want too
Came to room it was burning hot and still feeling suffocated while writing this comment out of frustation
Fellow believe me don't buy a pig with lipstic or beautiful makeup 
Any very bad experience and on top of that staff felt good for giving me hard time

title: “well used”
text: If you want a hotel close to the airport for an early flight it is very suitable. We used the stay and park but at arrival the staff stated that there was an additional fee for the parking.The staff waved the fee because of the time of booking. For the price I would not stay at the hotel even with an early flight. There are numerous valet parking services on airport road which would be a cheaper solution. Our overall rating is favorable good hotel with friendly staff that could do with some maintenance

title: “Great place for the price”
text:
We stayed here Jan. 21, 2005 and had a great time. The valet parking was easy (even with a Sonics game going on nearby and tons of traffic). The lobby is very quaint and old fashioned, but we did have to walk up stairs to the 3rd floor since they don't have an elevator. They were willing to help carry our bag, though, which we declined since the gentleman was much older than my husband. The room was huge as far as Seattle hotels go, with a separate kitchen area, huge walk-in closet and large sleeping area. Our room faced a busy street (Queen Anne Ave.) with night clubs and restaurants, so we knew right away to go buy earplugs at the drugstore up the street. With those in we slept like babies. There is a coffee shop connected to the hotel which served us the best mocha in the world (don't remember the name but it's accessible through the inside of the hotel). We walked a few blocks to the Seattle Center and hopped on the monorail to take us downtown to shop (which is what you should do if you want to explore Pike Place like a previous poster mentioned- the monorail gets you within a 10 minute walk of the waterfront and market). 
We had a great time here- we liked the old fashioned charm of the place, it was clean, close to everything in Seattle either by walking or monorail, safe neighborhood, and cheap for us through Hotwire. I wouldn't recommend it for older folks who can't walk very far, because of the stairs and everything in Seattle being best accessed on foot. We'd definitely stay there again though.

title: “Great basic clean lodging”
text: The Country Hearth Inn in San Francisco is a very affordable option to some of the over priced hotels available in the Lombard street area of the city. Although quite small the Country Hearth Inn is more than adequate foran overnight when doing some of the cities attractions. The rooms are small but very clean and the management of the hotel are very attentive and thoughtful with there guests. Close to many of the restaurants on Lombard street (which is made up of mostly hotels and restaurants) you will not be better servwd with a good nighhts lodging ata fair price.

title: “Great views, surprisingly nice”
text: Was worried a bit when reading past reviews, but was very pleasantly surprised. Bay view room was wonderful, and on 14th floor was just enough above pool to avoid any day and evening noise (train horns went off all night - but not hotel's fault). Room was very large, with good amenities (fridge, spacious bathroom, comfortable bed and pillows). Registration/check-in staff was very friendly and lobby/concierge staff were great in recommending local restaurants. Internet access was a real annoyance (ridiculous to be charging hotel guests $13/day, when lobby/pool internet is free), and 'free' areas didn't connect easily during high use periods. Didn't try out the restaurants/bars, but pool area was very pleasant and access to seawall for strolling/jogging is very convenient. The mandatory valet parking (even for dropping off/picking up rental cars) is a bit inconvenient, but tolerable. The valet employees were very pleasant and friendly. Overall, decent value for money, especially if using the convention centre. Cheaper places nearby, no doubt, but probably not with the wonderful view. A really nice hotel in convenient location.

title: “OK, especially for the price”
text:
I stayed for two nights after getting a very good rate at orbitz. First night wasn't good - although the room was clean and in good overall condition, I was put in a smoking room despite having requested nonsmoking. The smell was enough that I ended up with a sore throat and the front desk was barely apologetic, claiming the full house conditions that led to this assignment. 
However, the staff the next morning were helpful and accomodating; they gave me the first available nonsmoking room. The tub in the 2nd room didn't look good - bit of rust and ugly residue from a long ago nonslip surface - but all was clean and the room was comfy with no trace of smokers. Staff in the evening next day were also friendly and helpful.
Breakfast was typical packaged continental, improved by everything being fresh, a toaster for the bagels, and hard boiled eggs for some protein. Location just under I-35 meant some highway noise but very convenient, and I could walk to several restaurants.

title: “Luxurious but...”
text: Beautiful Hotel at fair price however be warned; all the extras don't come cheap. Parking, Internet, MiniBar and Restauants are very expensive. They also charge additional for the exercise room. Surprized I wasn't charged $ to flush the toilet! Thankfully lots of local cheap eats. And right on subway line too.

title: “Wonderful Hotel”
text:
Stayed for three nights just after Thanksgiving. We were so impressed with this hotel it made our stay very memorable.
The hotel is situated in the theatre district which is very convenient to everything being only a few minutes away.
It is a beautifully renovated old building and is maintained immaculately. We had a corner room which was very large and had amazing views over the city. The staff overall, particularly the front desk and concierge, could not have been more helpfull and were exceptionally welcoming. Complimentary wine in the evening and coffee in the morning were lovely touches. The foyer was small but very cosy. One very small drawback is that there is only one small bar which is located in the restaurant. We did not notice any noise from the building opposite which appears to be nearly completed. Overall this hotel is a must to stay in while in Chicago and would highly recommend it to anyone looking for something both central with outstanding staff and in very special surroundings.

title: “We walked into our room and knew our vacation had started.”
text: A friend of ours recommended the Sofitel specifically for their bed linens. And she was right. The bed with the milllion count thread linens was so comfortable. The hotel was convenient to the sightseeing attactions, but do not wallk, because nobody walks in LA!

title: “great hotel”
text: We stayed here for 2 nights over July 4th. The hotel has been remodeled and the rooms are spacious,stylish, quiet and comfortable. The location is great- within walking distance of the major DC sites and the Logan circle neighborhood with great restaurants catering more to locals. And the staff is friendly and responsive- a great hotel.

title: “AMAZING BEDS”
text: Wow the beds in this hotel were Amazing. I was there for a wedding and only stayed one night but wish I had a week to stay in this hotel. Everything a spoiled girl would want. The room was jam packed with extras and made me feel like a princess. Wish i had more time to enjoy it. The doorman and staff were so nice and extremely helpful. The bathroom in the rooms were so awesome and had alot of space for 2 to get ready. Will say it was a little pricey.

title: “Disappointing Room”
text:
Sometimes first impressions are accurate. A NYC size room (about 12 x 15) with a tiny closet (had to request more hangars) and no dresser. Expensive parking. No room to put our two suitcases on suitcase stands (there's only one stand anyway). No iPod dock. Dim fluorescent bedside lights. Window open upon arrival (in the 40s outside) and heat doesn't seem to be working properly. Oh yeah - free wine at 5 pm, a flat screen TV and nice bathrobes. I think we got what a friend calls the "Ha Ha Room" - let's give them this room and see if they complain. 
Last week we were in a luxury hotel in Portugal at lower cost, so the comparison is stark. This doesn't feel like a fine hotel...at least not to us...at least not on this visit.

title: “Very nice hotel and helpful staff!”
text: The W Austin was an excellent choice for my recent trip to Austin. The staff and management were particularly helpful.

title: “Charming and sophisticated”
text: I came to this hotel, right off Times Square, warned by previous reviews of its tiny rooms. Well, I don't know what room fairy was looking out for us, but we were upgraded to a king-sized bed with a comfortable room and bath that was quiet, even a block off Broadway! I booked through Tripadvisor/Expedia and don't know whether that made a difference. It also was June, so maybe that made another difference. But we stayed five nights, and the Paramount and its staff proved pleasant and fabulously located. It was the most fun to see a show like "Nice Work" with Matthew Broderick and literally just walk across the street to the hotel door. Love this place! Great restaurants nearby on so-called Restaurant Row, as well. No, we didn't get a low price, and maybe you just get what you pay for.

title: “Perfect Location”
text:
This was my first time staying anywhere near Times Square but would say this hotel is near enough to be in the buzz but far enough away to avoid the noise. Fantastic hotel with great modern facilities, only had 2 small gripes.
1. Not enough seating in the breakfast area.
2. Not enough elevators for he size of the hotel. I felt at times we had to wait ages for one.
Our room was on the 16th floor and had a view of the Empire State Building, the room was tucked away from the elevators thankfully which I'd advise everyone to ask for if possible. The room was spacious enough without being huge, bathroom was good and the bed was very comfortable.
I did see some earlier reviews with mentions of the area, It did appear seedy at times but we saw nothing to make us feel uneasy at all.
Would most definately stay again, we stayed on a Priority Club points + cash so 3 nights for $180 + 30000 points was an absolute bargain.

title: “Good airport hotel”
text: Nice hotel close to SeaTac. The staff was helpful and the room was clean. Nice sheets and towels but bathroom was a little dated and small. We did not eat at the restaurant, but it looks like a good place for breakfast or a quick cup of coffee. The room was quiet. I would recommend this hotel if you need to be close to the airport.

title: “Great place, convenient for visiting Boston without the $$$!”
text:
I stayed here with a friend for one night before a convention in Boston (we moved to another hotel for that). 
The hotel is very conveniently located near the Interstate, provides free on-site parking (rare in Boston!), free breakfast with a decent choice of things to eat. The room was spacious and comfortable, everything was clean and reasonably well taken care of.
The area around the hotel is not the best, so walking around at night is probably not recommended. However, you're less than two miles from downtown Boston, so for location/convenience/price, this place can't be beat. 
This hotel had the fastest Internet access speed I have ever seen at a hotel: something like 15 MBPS down and 9 MBPS up! Impressive.
Apart from a slow checkin due to the large number of people waiting, everything went well at this hotel and I'd be happy to return on another occasion.

title: “Beautiful place, friendly staff, poor quality electronics”
text: I reserved 3 rooms for a 1 night stay since we had an early appointment the next day. Brought along family and 4 little girls with plans of going in the pool at night and relaxing . The place was beautiful, we were told the pool was open until 11pm when we inquired so we were eager to get into it. The pool was not only on the other building but closed, the keys to our rooms were faulty so we got locked out more than once. One of the rooms had a TV that did not work and we had to get engineering to fix it. The parking below was super convenient but the tolls were also faulty. First it wouldn't identity our cards then it charged us double. We ended up paying over $96.00 in parking only for the one night stay. I was very dissappointed and frustrated about that, the whole point of spending the extra money to stay there was to relax and that became quite a challenge. I loved the place and would like to re-visit but would be hesitant due to all the poor quality electronics and additional ridiculous charges.

title: “Don't Go There”
text:
This hotel is very very noisy and it is nothing to say it, if you want to sleep it's not the place to go.
The staff is not very nice, rooms are not very clean (there were cockroaches), you can't control tthe heating, there are no elevators, and this hotel is very far from manhattan activities such as the empire state building, times square and rockefeller center, but near to little italy and chinatown. 
If you are a tourist, don't go there, you won't regret to pay more to have a better room

title: “Great hotel very clean but busy free Breakfast and managers reception”
text: Stayed here with kids over spring break. Really nice clean comfy rooms and beds. Sleeper was okay Wonderful views of downtown buildings like the Tribune from our room. Used the pool and sauna small pool like 3 lap lanes, but great sauna. The breakfast was very busy and it was a long wait for the made to order food. Separate lines for self serve which helped. Entire lobby area was packed and it's a big area! That said they never ran out of food and staff cleared tables quickly. Good food when you found a place to sit. Maybe not as busy at a different time of year Valet parking was fast yet expensive like other hotels in area. This is a beautiful clean hotel.

title: “Convenient and quiet”
text: The hotel was perfectly situated, close to the White House and Mall. The subway could not have been more convenient. I was a little concerned that our room overlooking the atrium would be loud, but we did not hear any noise, even with remodeling in the lobby. The room was clean, and the bathroom was large. In addition, there are a variety of restaurants and shops within walking distance. There is also a brewpub across the street, which made for a good meeting place for our group. The only knock I had against the hotel was that when we checked in they tried to direct us to a self-serve kiosk instead of a clerk, and the kiosk wouldn’t even accept our credit card, so we had to get back in line. It seems strange the hotel would try to remind people of an airport, which is the least customer-service place in America.

title: “The room rates are reasonable, but they will kill you with other costs”
text:
First let me start with the positives:
The airport location is convenient and very good shuttle service.
Martin Gil, The check- in clerk was very pleasant and helpful! 
The pool area is nice.
The negatives:
The room was a dump with the only window facing a walkway!
We were charged $60.00 for 2 beers and 2 burgers in the brew bar. Do not go there, there are plenty of more reasonable restaurants in the area. The waiter barely spoke English and was very incompetent.
The hotel should not charge a hotel guest an exhoribant $19.00 to park overnight outside.

title: “Oh wow. I want to LIVE in this hotel!”
text:
We were only in San Diego for one night and it was very much a "race from the airport, sleep, race back to the airport" trip without much chance to do anything else, but the hotel really elevated this from a stopover to a really enjoyable experience. It's one of the nicest hotels I've stayed at recently.
I was very impressed with the room. Everything seemed just a touch above the usual quality you'd expect at this price level. We were on the 16th floor in a room very close to the elevators but didn't notice any noise.
The bathroom was beautifully designed. They really made perfect use of a rather small area, with lovely tile walls and floor, and the bathroom amenities included fluffy sponges and bath gel in addition to the usual shampoo, conditioner, lotion, soap set. Very impressive.
We didn't eat at the hotel (except for snagging Tootsie Rolls and taffy from the big bowls at the reception desk every time we went in or out) but had a big room service breakfast which was well worth the $18 each that it cost. Again, very impressive, and a good value considering this was not at all something that just got scraped out of a can or a cereal box.
I like their late checkout time (noon) and we were also impressed that when we checked out, our car was already waiting for us at the valet stand without having to ask for it.
The location is excellent, right in the Gaslamp Quarter so there are about a hundred restaurants of every imaginable type within a few minutes' walk. It was wasted on us because we didn't have time for much, but I would love to go back and stay for a proper visit to the area.
Sitting in a nice room having this amazing breakfast, we joked that the ideal thing would be to move in permanently. It only counted as a joke because we haven't won the lottery yet, but as soon as we do... yeah, pretty serious about the idea.

title: “Great Stay!”
text: We just returned from a two night stay at the Best Western Sunset Suites. The outside of the hotel isn't very impressive and it is right off a major highway and intersection, but as soon as we walked inside we were greeted by a very friendly staff and a large, nicely decorated lobby. The staff was very friendly throughout our stay and the hotel was clean. Our room was big and the bed was very comfortable. The AC worked great, which is a huge plus after running around in the hot San Antonio sun all day. I am a rewards member so I have stayed at several BW hotels. I actually like this one better than the Premier that we stayed at once. My only complaint....which is the same at every BW are the pillows. They are too puffy and square.

title: “What a building!”
text:
And so sad that the hotel is just the first 18 stories, then there are 64 more to go...
Perfect location, rather quiet, I do like Radisson Blus new interior design.

title: “Agony at the heartbreak hotel”
text: After having such a wonderful stay in Memphis we checked out or tried to check out of the heartbreak hotel only to be told we hadn't payed our bill. This was of course payed for before we left the UK. The women on the reception desk was very rude and decided she was going to take the payment from our credit card.never give the hotel your credit card just hand over $30 its safer than a credit card. When we arrived back in the UK two more attemps were made on our card. What should have been a wonderful stay was spoilt by this gastly receptionist. This was our 6th visit and our last.

title: “Perfect Spot for Business Trip”
text: I arrived at the LAX Marriott via their courtesy shuttle and this was my first positive impression related to service. Even though my arrival at the property was much earlier than their check in time, the front desk was courteous enough to assign me a room- what she called a handicapped room - and I was able to rest for a while after a long trip from Florida. The room was impecable and the double beds were made the Marriott way - no bedspreads- but plenty of soft pillows and a down comforter. To me it was a pleasure to have a small fridge, and a coffee maker that was kept well supplied during my 8 day stay. It was a business trip and the service provided during the main meals of the day was exceptional. My favorite spot was the Sports Bar after a long busy day, and the menu was not only affordable but also quite tasty for a bar. I highly recommend the chicken quesadillas!! The location is perfect and within walking distance of public transportation as well as the Manhattan Beach trolly. We took trips to Santa Monica and Manhattan Beach for a fraction of what any taxi would have charged us. The pool area is relaxing and inviting, and the lobby provides airline computer kiosks for advance check in, and boarding passes. Every night was restful thanks to the quality of bedding- and I must mention, the bath and body works products in the bathroom were a pleasant surprise. I can't wait to go back to the LAX Marriott. Housekeeping staff was A+.

title: “Excellent Customer Service”
text: Very clean and the customer service was wonderful! As soon as we got out of our car at 11:30 at night, there were staff members holding doors open and smiling. I would not be smiling that late at night if I was working but they were so warm and genuine. The rooms were beautiful and breakfast was so good! It was a wonderful experience!

title: “We owe the staff of River Inn our heartfelt thanks”
text:
We came here with extended family for the funeral and burial of our father at Arlington National Cemetery. The staff at the River Inn were exceptionally kind and attentive to our requests and needs. Special thanks to sales manager Monique, who arranged for our group's accommodations, and also arranged the funeral reception at the hotel. The food at the reception, from the hotel's Dish restaurant, was attractively presented, offered an excellent variety, and was delicious.The front desk staff were all uniformly helpful, as were the bell captains. Housekeeping staff, food and beverage staff, and engineering staff likewise were all pleasant, and desirous of being helpful. 
An example of helpfulness: The room my mother was originally assigned had a heavy, unpleasant odor from a previous smoking occupant. The front desk clerk immediately changed her room assignment, came up with us to assist in moving her to the new room, and was very concerned that a guest had been smoking, as the River Inn is a non-smoking hotel, and will fine anyone who is caught smoking. He later inquired of us to ensure that she was happy with her new room.
The River Inn has an intimate, neighborhood atmosphere. The location can't be beat, in my estimation. The Foggy Bottom area of D.C. is one of the oldest neighborhoods in the city, and it was delightful to look out our windows and view the old townhomes on the street, and the mews behind the hotel. The sidewalks are all brick, and somewhat uneven, so be careful when walking! The hotel is within easy walking distance of grocery and convenience stores, the Foggy Bottom metro stop, decent restaurants, and easy access to the tourist destinations of D.C. You're in the middle of the city, yet it's relatively quiet. The restaurant is cozy and can get busy. My husband and the male members of our family group enjoyed the bar!
We used the small business center to do our online air travel check-in, and to print our boarding passes. WiFi is free, but the internet connection is not always the best, at least in our experience.
After consideration, I give the hotel four stars instead of five. We had some lights that didn't function properly in our room, nor did our television work. We weren't in our rooms enough for that to matter, however. Our Potomac suite had nice big windows that let in lots of light, and good black-out curtains for sleeping at night. The climate control systems were wonky in some of our rooms, the saving grace being the windows which can be opened to let in fresh air, and are provided with screens, so one doesn't have to worry about bugs getting in, or children falling out. The hotel makes heating available in the cold weather months, and air conditioning available in the warm weather months, but guests do not have autonomous control over their individual room systems. 
Engineering staff did come to attend to our t.v., although not at our request. I think housekeeping might have reported the problem to them. I know if we had contacted the front desk and asked them to fix the inoperative lights in our room, they would have accommodated us. We just didn't make the effort to do so. The kitchen can best be described as functional, ideal for refrigeration, heating food, and making coffee (did appreciate the 4-cup coffee pot and coffee beans available to guests there). Valet parking is expensive, $34 per night plus tax. My brother and his family did not receive their wake-up call on the day of departure, although others in our group did receive theirs. Room service was prompt, and the food was decent, but not inexpensive. A local pizzza, sub, salad and gyro vendor called Manny and Olga's provides room delivery, if you want to order out. The food is pretty good, the service is prompt, and the prices are reasonable. You can get the order form from the front desk.
In closing, I'd like to reiterate how helpful, friendly, accomodating, and informative the hotel staff are. The front desk staff and bell captains helped us in many ways, from arranging airport transportation, to answering tourist questions, to handling laundry requests,to expressing their condolences for our loss.We are very grateful to all of them. They were all uniformly patient with our demands and questions. I don't know what aspect of management is responsible for their postivie demeanor, but kudos to the River Inn management for hiring good people.

title: “A Pleasant Stay at Hotel Nikko”
text:
I stayed in a petit queen room while staying here in September 2012, overall it was a really good stay. I was on the 6th floor so the view wasn’t fantastic but the room itself was good it was quite small but it was what I expected having read similar comments before booking.
There was a large flatscreen tv which was nice and the bed was extremely comfortable, there was also a desk to work from which was good. There were the odd scratch or mark on the carpet but nothing to noticeable. I did find that the room was a bit chilly and while there was aircon it didn’t provide much heat/
The bathroom was very spacious with a good powerful shower (which is important!) I didn’t use the facilities such as the gym/swimming gpool or eat in the restaurant but I did order room service twice and I have to say the food was very good. My only issue with Hotel Nikko was the $15 charge per 24hrs for the internet. In a 4* I would have expected this to be included, if you do just need it intermittently there is a Starbucks downstairs with free wifi so I took advantage of this a few times.
Location was great too, right near market – including the Westfield Centre so not to far to walk. 
I would definitely stay here again, maybe next time I’d ask for a bigger room but otherwise all good!

title: “Fantastic Location”
text:
I had business at the US Capitol and this location was outstanding. A mere 2 blocks and we were there. It was convenient and the A/C was working beautifully. The hotel room was quiet and comfortable. The bathroom was a little small but definitely they made great use of the space.
I was in a junior suite and appreciated the microwave and fridge. I didn't notice the elevator being too slow but I used the stairs even though I was on the 5th floor. 
The breakfast was typical continental type so I skipped it and went to Starbucks around the corner. (I pick hotels based on location and sleep quality, not breakfast.) but this is a complete non-issue for me.
They are close to a Capitol bike share location and that was fun to do in the evening as a way to see the mall without actually having to walk it all the way down to the Lincoln Memorial.

title: “Exceptional Hotel”
text:
The Four Seasons is one of my favorite places to stay. The staff is friendly and accomodating, and the atmosphere is beautiful, peaceful and relaxing. The location is convenient for me when attending conferences at the George R. Brown convention center because it is within walking distance. Plus, the Shops directly across the street (which can be reached via the skybridge from the hotel), and the Phonecia Foods market a block away provide a nice place to grab last-minute items or treats like Starbucks and a selection of restaurants if you aren't in the mood for a pricey meal or are in a hurry.
The restaurant in the hotel, Quatro, is fantastic and an incredible experience to enjoy if you want to spend a little time and money for an unbelievable meal. The spa is also fantastic, as is the pool area and work-out center. 
We took our infant daughter this time, and there was a crib waiting in our room. The staff was very friendly too her, and we felt extremely welcome. Many other places I've stayed with a baby have seemed to shy away from offering the same level of service when you have your child, but the Four Seasons is a true exception to this rule.
The valet service was excellent, prompt, and friendly too. Overall, we really love staying here every chance we get, and will definitely look for other Four Seasons Properties for future travels.

title: “European feel”
text: We stayed at the Hotel Fusion with my husband and another couple. We loved it! The hotel is in a perfect location, the interior has that European feel to it - small but comfortable rooms, clean, lots of art hanging on the walls. Very well priced too for waht you get. A place we would stay again - for sure.

title: “A little unsafe, but on the thrifty travelor budget”
text: Thifty - that's it - I stayed here for three days. The US Navy and Military does as well. Contential Breakfast is okay. Safety was a concern, someone reported a camera missing in the room. Outside Vendors were seen not only placing flyers under doors but I saw them try opening each door to see if the travelor had left theirs unlocked (this was reported to the office mgr.) If you stay there - if you go sightseeing - take everything with you so you are not unhappy when you return. Rooms are very basic, okay clean, I've been in better "thrifty" locations. Is close by to the Hotel Circle if you have business there, and a pool and jacuzzi - which the military crowd kept full.

title: “Excellent place to stay in Philly”
text: Service and rooms are wonderful. You can't go wrong if you stay at the Rittenhouse!

title: “Wonderful weekend in Chicago”
text:
My wife and I stayed for one night prior to attending the Strictly Sail Show at Navy Pier. We found
the hotel via the Strictly Sail web site, which had an arrangement with the Sheraton Towers hotel. We upgraded to a 'Deluxe' room, which overlooked the Chicago River facing west. The Club Room was very nice, with a nice selection of snacks in the evening. The staff both in the Club Room and hotel was very polite and friendly.

title: “I LOVE NY!”
text:
What a location, it's so central to everything you would want to see in NY! The rooms are small but clean, you only sleep & shower there anyway.There's a lovely king size bed, and we had a great view of 42nd street from our window. We walked everywhere from the Hyatt. Concierge are wonderful, so helpful with anything you want to see & do. 
The lobby for store is great for snacks, you're given vouchers for free bottled water and tea/coffee.
Let's not forget Grand Central Terminal, there's a great food hall in there too.
I don't say 'if' I go back,it's 'when' I go back, and the Grand Hyatt will be my accomodation when I go back to the Big Apple!

title: “If you enjoy coming to an unclean room every now and then...”
text:
Arrival
I checked in on my reserved Non-smoking suite and I was told... “we do not have a non-smoking room available at this moment...” Even though I had a printed confirmation of the reservation (done through their website). “We cannot guarantee the availability of rooms.” This should have served as an indication of what I could expect. I told them I would come back the next day.
Next day... a room was ready. I thought we were off to a good start and was happy, seeing that the hotel was going through a minor renovation phase (new outdoor sign, new bed covers, new lamp screens, and quick grab n’ go breakfast). This happiness was slowly replaced with indifference and lack of expectation. 
Housekeeping and service
You get a weekly housekeeping to your room, in my case scheduled for Sundays. I travel on the weekends and come back Sunday night to find my room as I left it on Friday. This has occurred so far on 3 occasions. 
The first time, I talked with Jose at the front and he was promptly scheduled it for the next day. 
The second time I talked to another person and he scheduled the cleaning for Monday. Since this was the second time, I thought I might as well call them at noon to make sure they do it. I Spoke to the same person and he assured me it was going to get done. Came back that night to find my room had not been taken care of. I went to the reception to bring this to their attention, Josie this time (Admin. General Mgr.) attended my complain and assured me it would be taken care of.
Tuesday comes by and I come to find: surprise! your room is still not clean. This time I was mad that no one cared. I went to the front to talk with Josie and she apologized several times about it. She wrote: “Housekeeping on Room xx must be done, do not forget”. 
Wednesday: I get a call at work at 5pm, it was Josie letting me know that the cleaning staff was still on the premises and my room was about to get cleaned. That night my room was serviced. 
The third time... I was not surprised. I didn’t even bothered to tell front desk about it. I was tired since I was coming back from a trip. The next day I told Jose about it. Today I will be more surprised to find my room done rather than undone again. I have no expectations for this place anymore.
Overall, if you enjoy coming to an unclean room every now and then, guests keeping the side security doors unlocked using a small rock blocking the automatic closure, as well as receiving mail for another person inside your room, then... this hotel is perfect. 
About the purpose of my visit
Business. 2 Month stay. The company that I work for is located in the Westchase area. HR made the reservation for this hotel, since I was staying on another Hotel down the road that did not include the amenities for staying more than a week.

title: “Nice Room. Good Location.”
text: We had a very enjoyable 7 night stay at this hotel. Our room was quite spacious, with a nice view over the city. There was plenty of storage space. A kitchenette gives the option to cook in! There are so many nice restaurants and bars near the hotel. Grand Central Station is just 3 blocks away, while Time Square is a mere 20 mins walk. I would recommend this hotel, however don't expect a modern hotel as some areas could do with being freshened up. The location, spacious, clean room makes up for this. We travelled to the city from JFK via Airtrain and then the E train for just $15! Great value. A fab trip to try is a cycle tour of New York with 'Bike the Big Apple'. Our tour guides - Levi & George are great ambassadors for the city. Take subway trips to places like Coney Island and to the Bronx zoo.

title: “Best Western was a best choice”
text: I usually travel alone, but this time had a grown son with me so I wanted a spacious room in order that we could both spread out. Not only was it large, with a separate work area including a sofa bed that my son who lives in the area was considering using, but it was comfortable and clean. The hotel had a small but usable exercise room (son worked on the lat pull down machine and the treadmill, while I used the elliptical and the bike), pleasant looking pool (that we skipped this trip), and offered a tasty hot breakfast the next morning in a bright and roomy lounge area. Price was extremely reasonable for the quality. The only reason I'm avoiding the excellent rating was a somewhat loud air conditioner, but noises from other rooms and hallway were non-existent, so once I got used to the air conditioner's cycling on and off, I slept well. Would return.

title: “Tired Hotel”
text:
Minus: Generally noisy--We could hear people in hall: There is no refrigerator: The hotel has a tired feel complete with old hotel room smell. No small store to buy snacks and sundries--we couldn't buy a carton of milk.
Plus: Comfortable beds. Plenty of room. Great Location only if you are flying.

title: “O.K. for Families, A Bit Musty for Price”
text:
We wanted a luxerious, one week vacation for my husband and I, my son 4, and our exchange student 16 for the end of February 2007. Weather was cold but sunny. 
Booked largest bungalow on beach, had two separate areas, one bedroom with separate vanity and closet, and Student slept on comfortable pull out and his own vanity and closet space. Toilet and bath was shared between the two rooms. Space is larger than it looks on the website. 
Kitchen unit had nothing. We bought plastic bowls, dish soap and sponge, cereal, milk, snacks, and ate breakfast in the room each morning. Maid and front desk staff were excellent. 
However, the bungalows were old, toilets back up occasionally (water only not sewage) causing water damage to be dried out and leaving musty smell. Decore nice, modern, and comfortable but the unit just smelled and felt a bit old, musty and damp (my husband didn't think it was noticable). I guess I prefer newer construction. But what can you expect from an updated resort right on the water? 
Water view, beach front, and gardens were spectacular. Great central location. Casual dining on site and for room service o.k. Student thought hamburger awesome. TV channels very limited, no plug in for playstation 2. Pools seem nice. The heated one was too cold but we spent some time in the whirlpool with everyone else.
Good resort for families with older kids (7-16 probably ideal), adults on their own or sharing with other couples. Less expensive room options around the site as good as the beach option. 
Rent a minivan. Driving is easy to all attractions. Ask the resort for a reduced parking rate for longer stays. They are very helpful and keen to ensure you enjoy your stay.
Meal Tips: authentic, inexpensive mexican food at Valentinos in Mission Bay; and, fresh Italian take out back to your room at Cafe Bella, Garnet Ave Mission Bay. 
See all Sea World shows and consider two day pass with backstage tour. Well worth it. Loved Legoland. Both Sea World and Legoland have huge, excellent play areas for young kids. You could spend several hours at these locations with toddlers and preschoolers so bring something to read.
Carlsbad shopping outlet is great and close to Legoland. The mall has a Diner that has the best milkshakes! 
Las Americas is even better shopping south of San Diego (quick drive). 
Coronado bridge and beach great. 
Zoo fun (avoid the petting zoo, disappointing compared to local farms). We did not go to the wild animal park.
Old Town is very quiet and nice. Great mexican food everywhere. Our four year old could not follow the walking tour (too boring) but my husband and our student thought it was great. The shops have interesting art and pottery, and unique imports. 
We will return to San Diego when the weather is warmer. Lots still to see and do in the years to come.

title: “A perfect hideaway in midtown...”
text: I stayed at the Iroquois while I was in NYC on business about 3 weeks ago (late January '05). Everything was perfect. The rooms are small but perfect for one person traveling alone on business. (Reminder: 99% of hotels in NYC have very small rooms.) My flight arrived at 8:30 AM so I was at the hotel shortly by 9:30 AM and just wanted to check my bag with them but they had a room ready for me so I was able to freshen up before my meetings. I had a room on the 6th floor (600) that faced a little courtyard which was quite nice as the hotel is not tall. About 10 minutes after arriving, they called the room to make sure that everything was satisfactory. The bed was amazing, like sleeping on a giant pillow. Wonderul linens and down pillows with big duvet. The bathroom was great with Molten Brown toiletries and a showerhead with unbelieveable water pressure. I was concerned about the handle on the shower because it felt like it was loose so I told them at the front desk when I left to go to dinner around 7 PM, when I returned 3 hours later it had been fixed. The room had a COMPLIMENTARY liter bottle of SmartWater on the desk when I arrived! Nobody offers free anything anymore. The hotel also had complimentary overnight shoeshine service which was quite nice. The Iroqois offers a nice [big] continetal breakfast in your room for $11.95, a steal in NYC. I was on business and paid $260 per night, including tax. That is a steal for 4-stars in midtown during the week. I booked directly from their website, not through a broker. Trust me, you always get treated better when you book directly. This was a superior New York hotel experience!

title: “Price is excellent with hot breakfast included every morning”
text:
The price and location are excellent. The exterior and interior are nice; and the room is spacious.
It works very well if you are a heavy sleeper or an early bird person because the noise is very loud from the airplanes taking off and landing (especially taking off). You can literally see the airplanes take off in front of you from the 4th floor windows. This happens between the hours from 6 am to 9 pm. We stayed for 3 nights and paid $50 each night including hot breakfast every morning (2/18/12 - 2/20/12).
If you are a light sleeper there are other hotels nearby (1 or 2 miles away from the airport) and you do not have to listen to the noise but the price is higher ($20 to $30).

title: “Bring your inhaler”
text: worst place ever. I have stayed in many a Red Roof Inns and have never had such a bad experience. The clerk at the front desk was a charm. It went down hill from there. I choose a room upstairs because I'm a single mom traveling with 2 children and thought we'd be a little safer. I didn't have to worry about being mugged instead I had to worry about being able to breath. Apparently the roof had leaked at some point and the room had a very strong mold odor. We had to cover our noses and breath with a peice of our personal colthing over our faces. All of the rooms had the same issue. We ended up sleeping in the car. When I spoke with another clerk that had come in he didn't want to refund the room cost. My advice, ask to see the room before you give a payment! This experience soured me on Red Roof Inns.

title: “Riverwalk Homewood: Stumbled at first, but found it's feet...”
text:
Did not meet initial expectations, though quickly corrected; would recommend (with caveats), but would definitely stay again.
We booked this for our Spring Break trip; our goal was 1) downtown, 2)plenty of family room 3)brand for which we get points.
Location: On the Southwest end of the Riverwalk, a quieter area, but only a two block walk (across city streets) to the 'happening' part of the riverwalk. Walking along the river was longer, but an enjoyable stroll.
Room: We used the OLCI and selected 10th floor, overlooking the river. Check-in on arrival was swift, and we were recognized for our HHonors elite status. Arrived to find a tray of used dishes outside the door. Room smelled... likely smokey, not musty. Old food in refridgerator (mushy apples, waffles). Call to desk resulted in a string of apologies and a veritable SWAT team of housekeepers to the room. They quickly cleaned the fridge, set up an ozone machine, and brought fresh linen.
Pool area: The roof top pool is small and shallow, but hey, it's a roof-top pool. It's always nice to splash a little with the kids after a day of activity, and what's cooler than a roof-top pool?
Parking: We parked across the street (to the North) in a municipal ramp, cheaper than valet.
Breakfast: Three (or was it four?) hot dishes (egg, meat, potato), two waffle irons, plenty of cereal/yogurt/oatmeal/bread/fruit available. Plenty of sitting room for eating, didn't have to wait, despite a big youth group one morning.

title: “Fun even without Sun”
text: My friend and I traveled to San Diego from Los Angeles just to go to the Hard Rock to see Dave Navarro on July 4th. Although the weather was AWFUL...the pool/spa/party scene was so much fun!!! Everyone at the hotel was super cool and welcoming, and our suite was impeccable! The only bummer was the $35 valet charge overnight...but I guess you get that at every hotel. I will say they had a killer BBQ that was delicious!!!!

title: “Overpriced stay in a centrally located midtown hotel”
text: The hotel lobby is very nicely appointed and the restaurants are a good size. The location is excellent with the exception of subway access. With that said, everything is expensive, even for NYC. Very limited TV channel options, PPV movies are $15 each, wifi is expensive at $8-9/ day as is laundry and dry cleaning. Recommend using one of the local businesses with a block or two for laundry.

title: “Would not stay again”
text:
I am a Hilton Gold member and have stayed in many Hilton Garden Inns. This one was the worst and you are much better off at the Hampton Inn a few blocks away. The front desk staff was too busy socializing to help with check-in, the room was dirty (sheets were dirty and not changed from prior occupant), the walls are thin so the hallway noise is very loud and the walls between rooms are so thin you can hear everything (and I mean everything) happening in the rooms next door. When I went to the restaurant for breakfast the next morning, the wait staff (same problem as the front desk) was too busy socializing among themselves to pour coffee, or otherwise serve guests. 
While most Hilton Garden Inns that I have stayed at have been comfortable, clean and with helpful staff, this one needs a great deal of management and improvement.

title: “Comfortable for business travel”
text:
The LA downtown Marriott is a nice hotel if you need to stay in the downtown or convention center area. The lobby is very bright and inviting to sit down in the lounge for a drink. The pool area is small but good to relax in the sun! 
The room had an odor of smoke, although I had requested a NS room. I tried to move, but hotel was completely sold out so they sent a housekeeping person with a spray of air freshner! 
The bed and linens are very nice and very comfortable. I enjoyed the restaurant, Moody's, for dinner one evening. 
All the staff are cordial and were helpful.

title: “Loud & overpriced”
text:
First room we moved in had dirty bed-sheets & smelled like somebody had smoked in it.
Extremely noisy, you are right next to the runway...
Rooms have poor noise isolation - you hear your neighbour...
You have to pay for parking (18$ self parking, 28 $ valet)
expensive restaurant which is not worth the money

title: “Perfect! Planning our return.”
text:
Amazing hotel in a great location. The room was spacious, meticulously clean, and well appointed. The hotel staff provided great friendly service that exceeded my expectations. We were particularly appreciative of their restaurant recommendations.
Some of the hotel/room highlights included wolf appliances, rack audio system, quality bedding, and a sub zero wine fridge. The breakfast was a perfect start to our day and the car service made our dinners out special. The room mirrored all of the professional photos provided by the Fairmont and I was not disappointed.
Jean, thank you to you and your team for making the start of our honeymoon perfect - we hated to leave and cannot wait to return. I truly enjoyed our conversations and your Maui restaurant recommendations were spot-on. Christie and I look forward to seeing you again soon. In the end there is no doubt as to why your hotel is #1.

title: “okay”
text: We just stayed there on the ninth floor and had awful construction noise from diagonally across the street! It sounded like there were trucks backing up all morning "BEEP BEEP BEEP....". The rooms are really small but you do get what you pay for. We did like the location because we were walking distance to so much...SOHO, NOLITA, Chinatown and Little Italy.

title: “Loved our funky hotel!”
text:
This was our first trip to New York and chose Yotel based on reviews and its location.
The hotel is so funky and cool, it reminded us of Citizen M Amsterdam....but better!
Yes the rooms are small but that's the concept.....the rooms are so well designed with lots of innovative storage space....and the wonderful, comfy, electric bed that folds to a sofa to make more room is a brilliant gadget!
Loved the galley! Yes, having a kettle and few tea bags in room is convenient but the galley kitchen had so much more choice....and a communal fridge....I did buy fresh milk to get a better cuppa! Be aware that the communal fridge is emptied on a Sunday regardless, this is to make sure food isn't left for days after guests have checked out.
The location is great, it was a little further from Times Square than I thought the address suggested but it was my first trip and didn't have any knowledge of the area.
It is about halfway between Times Square and the Hudson.....took about 5 mins to walk into Times Square or closer to 15 mins the day we arrived as we were hit by all the snow from the Nor'easter!
If the hustle and bustle gets a little too much for you, walk down to the Pier/Hudson, it's just a little more relaxing and open so you can catch your breath for a minute!
The bar and restaurant are great too. All low, colour-changing lighting and funky seats....seems to be one of the popular places for young & trendies (not us oldies!) to meet for a drink...we loved the cocktails!
If you need a recommendation for a local bar or steakhouse...try the West Side Steakhouse and Lansdowne Road bar...they are 2 minutes walk from the hotel (turn right out of the hotel and they are on the opposite side of the road).
All in all, we loved our New York base and would definitely stay at Yotel if visiting again.

title: “Friendly staff, free breakfast, exceptional view from rooftop patio room.”
text:
Paid avg room rate online, single night stay included two breakfast vouchers for restaurant. Friendly staff upgraded to rooftop room on check-in. Courteous even with a late night call to our room about our noise level. Mini fridge missing, but didn't need it for one night, the elevator was unusually slow for 5-floors, and ice machine in the lobby.
Decent size rooms, comfy beds, large bathroom had sliding glass frosted door, good if you don't need privacy. Ample towels and above avg toiletries..
Rooftop view exceptional, lounge happy hour good, not too many choices but drinks well poured. Generous appetizers and my burger prepared as ordered.

title: “An Oasis”
text:
The Vagabond Inn is located in a 'rowdy' part of town, as are the other hotels on the street.
What makes this place wonderful is the number of security cameras, someone is at the front desk 24/7 and they are rather assertive about keeping the riff raff out.
This inn is close to everything and if needed the light rail is across the steet.
 There is a pool, laundry. free wi fi, free parking and the rooms are clean.
In a way, the Vagabond Inn is a pretty place to stay.
I really relaxed and would not stay any other place in San Jose.

title: “It is overrated but i still liked it”
text:
I stayed here for a week with my partner last year and we got a great rate because of the External building work.. We didn't actually realise how expensive this hotel could get.
When we got there we were impressed.. it was in an extremely good location and the overall atmostphere was great!
We got dealt with by front desk in about 5 mins and brought to our room on the 8th floor... I didn't find the elevators as bad as ppl say.. there is about 5 of them so only took a minute or two for one to come... The room was a petite queen.. it was big enough for the two of us with all our shopping!!
The telly wasn't a flat screen but had good reception. The room was always cleaned and one day when we decided to eat in our room an extremely nice lady called us to ask if we wanted our room cleaned... I didn't realise we should have tipped the cleaning staff which i regret as they were really good!
I couldn't believe when i seen the price of the room service... shocking.. def not worth it.. even a litre bottle of Vodka would cost over 100dollars with tax and 'delivery' charge!?!
We made about 3 phone calls to ireland no longer than 3 minutes each and the phone bill was $150? Def using payphones the next time!!
Also i found the ppl Staying in the hotel (at the time we were there) quite snobbish.. we got in the elevator one day and a women turned to us and said 'our economy is dropping so much that even you guys can stay here now'..... honest to god we were on a 2 week stay in the US from ireland... one flight cost more than the hotel.. its not like we were wearing rags and we had plenty of shopping bags on us... really dont know where she got off saying that.. anyway despite that one run in and the price of food there everything went smoothly and i would prob stay again for atmostphere, cleanliness and location!

title: “Great boutique hotel in downtown Houston. Highly recommended.”
text: My husband and I stayed for our anniversary. The entire staff was extremely friendly and helpful. The bar staff was GREAT! The valet staff was helpful as well. We went out to a few dinners and they were there to pdrop us off and pick us up. When we were going further they were quick to get us taxis too. We decided to extend our staff because we were having too much fun to leave.

title: “The Good Hotel”
text:
Surprised to find such a small and neat hotel at such a central location and with such reasonable rates.
Reserved a room on short notice. Saved some money by not booking through the hotel's website but using one of the big booking sites instead.
The room was spacious and quiet, but a bit dark. There's a BART station less than a minute away, and a lot of attractions and other public transport within walking distance.
The one drawback was that my sister and her friend didn't feel comfortable walking around alone in that area after dark (but no issues during the day).

title: “Perfect place for an event and accomodations for a birthday party weekend!”
text: The Legacy was an awesome place to hold my husband's birthday party golf weekend for about 35 people. Accomodations were perfect for his friends and our family! We were all able to enjoy golf, the pool and hold a dinner in his honor. The staff is wonderful to work with and very helpful! They were the ones that helped me make it as nice as it was. Highly recommend it for any kind of get together! Everyone was happy!

title: “Great”
text:
We stayed here for 2 nights in March. Check-in was efficient. The employees were all very helpful. What really impressed me about this hotel was the interior design. It really is well done.
The rooms are a bit small. The beds very comfortable and the bathrooms were small as well, but I suspect this has to do with its eco-friendly nature. The breakfast menu was varied and the food very good. They avoid bottled water by serving purified city water and I have always wondered why more restaurants don't do that. It was a nice touch.
We purchased the Awaken Package which included breakfast. they told me it would be deducted at check-out. I am always leery of that but indeed it did not appear on the bill.
The workout and pool area were one of the best I have seen in a downtown hotel . The equipment is first rate and the area very clean and well maintained. The hotel is well situated in the center of town and easy to find. They have chilled towels which is an added bonus.
There is a bit of hall noise that makes its way into the rooms. I always anticipate this and bring a fan for white noise. Curiously, when I was leaving the hotel, the concierge told me I didn't need to bring that as they have fans if the guest requests one. That showed me the kind of effort and forethought they put into their guests.
I would definitely stay here again. I am a big fan of the Grand Hyatt and it will be tough to choose between the two.

title: “Love the stay”
text: Best doorman in town especially Yasir suliman he really helped me during my whole stayed.

title: “Wow, at the Capitol!”
text:
Dirty linens, nail clippings in the bathroom, no phone service for 4 days, valet parking attendant left keys on the outside table while he ran to do another chore.
Breakfast attendant was awesome, however. Wish I could give you her name.
I have tried to send my concerns to LQ, but their site will not accept my complaint. Maybe this will get their attention!

title: “The Extras Make It a Good Value”
text:
This makes a pretty good home base for a traveler to downtown Seattle. Most things are in pretty easy walking distance, though be aware (as I was not) that Seattle is very HILLY walking from west to east. The Vintage Park is on 5th Avenue, which is pretty much the eastern edge of downtown, so most places you go are downhill on the way there and uphill on the way back. North-South streets are mostly flat or have more gentle slopes.
Rooms here are distinctive with their jewel-tone color scheme. Spring for the few extra bucks and go for the King Premier rooms over the standard Kings. For not much more a night, you get about 100 extra square feet of space plus a sofa. The bed was pretty comfortable and the bathroom was fairly large, if a little bland. The tub was kind of shallow for soaking. There was plenty of closet space, though drawer space was limited. There are all kinds of neat doo-dads in the closet, including the tiger-print robe, an umbrella, and thick socks for keeping your feet warm. 
The lobby is smallish, but does host a complimentary wine reception each evening at 5, featuring a local winemaker and some hors d'oeuvres. This is a nice touch, as is the pet goldfish they will provide for your stay upon request. These are signature touches of the Kimpton chain which give it a nice personal flair. 
Tulio Ristorante is attached to the lobby and serves fine Italian cuisine, heavy on the seafood. It's a smallish room serving all three meals, and appears to be very popular as it was packed to bursting on a Wednesday night. Definitely make reservations here. 
There are ice machines only on the 4th, 7th, and 10th floors of the hotel, which is a little inconvenient. There's no pool and I didn't get a chance to check out the fitness room--I got all the workout I needed from the hilly streets. Staff all appear to be eager to please and very capable. It can be a hassle to get a cab, so plan on 5-10 extra minutes for that. 
In the immediate area, the bar/restaurant at sister Kimpton property the Monaco is fun. And Shuckers just down the street at the Fairmont Olympic has just about the best fish and chips I've ever had. 
You can walk to Pike Place Market from the hotel, though it's a bit of a hike. If you do, the great lounge at the Four Seasons right outside the market is a fine place to fortify yourself for that trip back uphill. You can easily walk the six blocks to the monorail from the hotel and hop on that to get to the Space Needle. 
.

title: “Needs Improvement”
text:
The hotel is convenient to the convention center and river walk. The common areas are nice and well kept, but I wasn’t happy with the cleanliness of the room particularly the bathroom. There were several reservation clerks we encountered unfortunately there was a female who lacked in customer service skills and attitude. Basic customer service training and role play should be encouraged for her.
We stopped in the common breakfast area for coffee and observed a man rushing in at the last minute for breakfast. There were several people still eating and an employee removed the large containers of eggs and sausage. Why not leave the breakfast food already prepared until your customers are finished. Once again, it was a poor example of basic customer service. 
The mattress was worn and uncomfortable on the right side.
The charge for parking on La Quinta's lot was $18.00 per day.

title: “A Clean, Comfortable Stay”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Golden Triangle Inn for 2 nights while our house was being tented for termites. I didn't have high expecations, but it turned out to be a very comfortable stay. 
The room was very clean. It showed a little wear-n-tear, but not much. The TV worked perfectly, nice clear picture and the mini-fridge looked almost new. There was an attempt to have some attractive art on the walls. The bed - a king - was very firm and comfortable with three big fluffy pillows. The air conditioning worked well, and was fairly quiet. The water pressure was good and the showerhead was far enough up the wall that my tall husband could fit. (I hate the low motel showerheads!) Although there were noisy kids staying next door, once they were inside their room you couldn't hear them through the walls. There is a small table and two chairs in the room, so you can grab a quick bite, or spread out your laptop.
The staff was friendly. The young woman working the desk when I checked in was very pleasant and professional. When I later came down for an extra towel, she cheerfully gave me a whole stack. I didn't take advantage of the free breakfast, but it's served daily from 6:30-9:30 AM. There is a small dining room just off the reception desk. There's also one outside table where you can sit and eat/rest, but it's right next to the entrance and a busy road, so I couldn't say it was scenic.
The Inn was recently bought out by Best Western and there aren't good signs out yet, so it's easy to miss. I pulled into the Motel 6 next door by accident, and my husband, who came seperately, missed the entrance. The hotel sits right next to I-805, so it's very easy to get anywhere you want to go. Within a 5 minute drive away are a large variety of restaurants - mostly fast food and small local places - so there's no need to eat at the place across the street (which isn't so great). I personally recommend Lolitta's Taco Shop about a 1/2 mile away; a hole-in-the-wall, but best Mexican in San Diego.
Overall, the Golden Triangle Inn was a clean, comfortable stay. I would recommend it if you're looking for a budget motel.

title: “pleasantly surprised...”
text:
As somebody who travels to NY frequently on business I avoid Times Square like the plague, too much of a tourist trap. However, my usual hotels were booked and since it was only for one night I decided to give it a try. The street, directly behind the Port Authority is not the best, but if you can overlook that the hotel is well worth it. 
The positives:
Wifi throughout the hotel
Nice rooms- what you see in the photos is what you get
Very comfortable bed
A small kitchenette- well stocked and came in handy for heating left-overs
Good working area
While not huge, the room design works well and you do not feel cramped
The negatives
The front desk staff that checked me in was incredibly rude and did not make me feel welcome, even though I have Ambassador status with the hotel chain, irrelevant to her I guess! I think that the bellman should be promoted to her job, he was fabulous and really made up for her bad manners. 
There are a few things that I did not check out but important to note:
There is a laundry room in the hotel (finally, a hotel that knows what guests need!)
Breakfast
Bar
Computers in the lobby for guest use
I will definitely stay here again and recommend it to others. If the hotel can work with front desk staff on costumer service it will get an excellent rating from me in the future.

title: “perfection....”
text: Great location, views, rooms.....what really sets this hotel apart is the staff, however! From start to finish, they truly go the extra mile to be sure your stay is top notch. If I could give this property (and most importantly staff) 6 stars I would! If you are looking for the best hotel in Seattle, look no further.....

title: “What a delight!”
text:
I recently stayed at Humphrey's Half Moon Inn & Suites. What a delight! 
We got a suite with a view of the marina and it was absolutely breathtaking. The suite was very spacious, clean and nicely decorated. 
The amenities were very nice as well. We got a chance to take advantage of the hot tub one evening (it stays open late) -- very nice. My only regret is that we were there after the concert season so we missed the performances. Next time . . . oh, there will be a next time for this hotel!

title: “Weekend Getaway”
text:
My boyfriend and I went here in Feb of 2009 for a weekend getaway and used his Hilton reward points for a 2 night stay. We stayed in their standard king sized bedroom. 
Positive
The room was clean and spacious for two people. The bed was comfortable and we were supplied with many pillows. The room had a large desk, stocked fridge which included alcohol, snacks and sodas, coffee maker, a 37 inch LCD TV, and lounge chair. The bathroom was a good size. There was plenty of counter space by the sink, a large magnifying mirror, plenty of towels for two people, good sized shower/tub with sufficient water pressure and hot water, and complimentary crabtree and evelyn bath products. 
Negatives
There were a few negatives which do not make this a 5-star stay. The toilets were extremely noisy. So noisy that you could hear people flushing above, below, to the right and left of you. We were only supplied with one bathrobe. Their food prices were ridiculously high. $20.00 for pancakes....I don't think so. We did not have any complimentary breakfast, however I am unsure if it is related to the fact that this was a reward stay. Not the hotel's fault, but there was a party going on at the room across from us which woke me up in the middle of the night with loud music and noisy people cycling in and out. 
Tips
There is a deli across the street called Pax where you could get good breakfast and lunch items with reasonable prices for that area. 
Do not eat at the Applebee's next door. We were lazy one night and decided to order food to go which was less than stellar and made me a bit sick.

title: “Great for the Price”
text: Considering how difficult it can be to get a decent hotel in NYC, I was pleasantly surprised by my experience at Hotel Alexander. Granted it isn't a 5 star establishment, but the room was clean, and the hotel is only two blocks from the Red Line. Therefore, it isn't too much of a drawback that the hotel is located on the Upper West Side. I was worried about two things before my arrival: bed bugs and the shared bathrooms. While I had no problems with the former, the latter was more variable. Since I shower at night, I had no problems getting one of the two bathrooms per floor. In the morning, on the other hand, it was challenging to find a free bathroom. Also, depending how clean the other guests are, the bathrooms can be messy. For example, one of the bathrooms on my floor was pretty disgusting one morning, while the other was very clean. If the bathroom situation is a deal breaker for anybody, you aren't limited to just two bathrooms, since you can always try a bathroom on a different level if you find that both of your bathrooms are dirty,. Or you could just pay more money to get a private bathroom (which I thought I saw as an option). Additionally, the room I was given was very quiet.

title: “Great experience at Burnham”
text: Spent three nights here before moving to another hotel for a conference. Should have stayed here for the duration. Beautiful, quite hotel in a historic building with an unparalleled location. Staff were uniformly friendly and helpful--all seemed happy to be working here. This will definitely be my Chicago hotel for future trips.

title: “Nice Effort but Terrible”
text:
I found this hotel to be a sad little place. The staff were very kind and really tried to please us. That was essentially the only positive spot we found here. The place was absolutely filthy. Apart from the front lobby, it looked like nobody had vacuumed since the place was first built. The elevators have a nauseating scent too. In the club room, which is a nice idea, there are dead flies along the windowsills. Another story - the rooms. The first room we were put in had some sort of insect infestation. Absolutely disgusting. When we requested that they switch our room, they did enthusiastically. There were no obvious bug infestations in the new room, but it was still dirty. The bedding was also filthy. Bleach would be my strongest suggestion.
Overall, it was dirty and cleanliness is my biggest criteria for a hotel room. The service was kind though, and the location was nice. It was in a central downtown area so it was close to a couple restaurants and pretty buildings. I just wish it was better taken care of. It has a lot of potential with the interior look, which is a refurbished heritage building. It just needs some TLC. Right now though, I would never stay there again and certainly would not recommend it to anyone.

title: “Home from home in Manhattan”
text:
We felt at home the minute we arrived at the Casablanca. Staff were uniformly friendly and helpful without being intrusive, and service was first class. The location couldn't be better - it's just yards from the bustle of Times Square, but inside everything is quiet and relaxed. The perfect place to return to after a busy day's sightseeing.
The room was a little small, but everything was spotless and the decor was just right to give a warm, intimate feel. The breakfasts were very good, as were the complimentary drinks in the evening. The lounge was a very pleasant place to relax.
We will definitely return to the Casablanca and would recommend it unreservedly. An absolute delight!
H&P, Cambs, UK

title: “Nice hotel but bring your retirement funds.....”
text:
Very nice hotel as far as location. Can't really be better for experiencing downtown Chicago. Short walk to Navy Pier, Mag Mile, etc.
My family and I pulled up and were helped quickly at the curb. I was advised on what to do for parking considering I would need my car later for a trip to Soldier Field for a soccer game. $35 for in and out privalege parking. Pretty high, but that is Chicago.
Lobby is beautiful and the front desk staff (there weren't enough of them) were friendly and helpful.
We were put on the 25th floor. The rooms are pretty small with two VERY soft, overly soft, insanely soft, beds. Two bottles of water were on the table waiting for us (if we wanted to pay $4 / bottle!), and an in-room refridge filled with stuff (like $4 for a KitKat and such).
Sadly, after the soccer game I had had no dinner. It was late and I did not want to walk miles for food. You got it. $18 for a Rueben through room service. When I asked if there was a restaurant in which we could dine rather than use room service I was unable to understand the reply, although I asked her to repeat twice. Hiring people who speak English would help.
When we went to bed (you know, the too soft beds) my eldest son and I sweated to death because you sank into the bed so far that heat had no way to escape. If you are a warm body person, you will HATE these beds. The air conditioning was not terribly cool either so it just made it that much worse.
We visited the pool which was nice, but crowded (we were told this is an all day long ordeal) The sun Deck is beautiful too. The next morning I decided to take advantage of the incredible workout facilities listed on their website. I planned on running on the treadmill while my wife swam with the kids. (I run every morning on a treadmill at home, so this selling point on their website was a big selling point for ME) I signed my family in to the pool and then went over to the treadmills and started my warm up. I was then approached by a female employee who told me, in no uncertain terms, that I needed to pay to use the workout facilites. $15 to be precise. Incredulous, I asked her to show me where it says that there is a charge. She said, there just is. I checked the website again and it says NOTHING about the extra charges. Essentially, I spent $200 for one night and was KICKED out of the health club.
I went back to the room while my wife and kids swam. While reading the paper I got the stench of cigarette smoke from the ventilation system. I am an ex-smoker so this is rather distressing for me. Not sure where it came from, but really don't care either. For $200 a night I expect to not leave my room smelling like I spent the night in a brothel.
Long and short of it is that it is a very nice hotel with some nice people working there. Worth $200 / night? No way. Won't do that again. Back to Embassy Suites for us!

title: “Best stay ever!!!!!”
text: Hotel was beautiful and clean. Staff was amazing. Best sleep ever.

title: “Wedding”
text: Wedding venue was'nt clean floors were very dirty, the concrete floors need to be stained and would be easier to keep clean, A/c was'nt turned on early enough for the room to cool down and guests were uncomfortable.

title: “Better value to be found”
text:
The front desk was very responsive to check us in our room on time, every time we asked the same response “room not ready”, until I forced the issue then all of sudden a room came available.
The room was looking old; the bathroom had tiles missing and needs some upkeep. Carpet was dirty and they charge you extra for wireless connections.
The breakfast is nice and complimentary cocktails in afternoon are good
The pool is small and the Jacuzzi is very tiny but nice that it is outside in the nice weather.
$17.00 a day for parking is added fee.
For the price a much better hotel can be found

title: “The Perfect Escape!”
text: I booked my room through priceline.com...got it for $45/night! I was pleasantly surprised when I approached the front desk and said my name...the staff person there...he right away told his colleague that he'd take care of me since he and I had previously spoken on the phone (when I called to request a room on a higher floor). He was so pleasant and helpful. I had just driven there straight from work (after working over time) on a Friday night...It was about 830pm...I let him know I was running away from home...He was so kind...he put me on the plaza level (18th fl--keycard access only), didn't charge me for the fridge and microwave I asked for....(I realized once I checked out)...and the plaza level included free breakfast buffet and evening cocktails...plus it was so nice and quiet up there!!! Just what I needed! Room was nice and comfy (except the sleepnumber bed). I stayed in that room for an entire 24 hours without a problem. It was close to the inner harbour and all the sites were within short driving distance. Self park was $15/night about a block and a half away--nice parking lot...Valet is $31/night

title: “Great for sporting events”
text: We stayed at this property on a Saturday evening to take in a Tiger game. The hotel was very clean and despite a few signs of aging (tub grout being discolored and an outlet not working in the bathroom) the size of the rooms and new carpet/bedding/vanity made it a pleasant stay. We were able to upgrade to a corner room with a beautiful view of the river and Windsor. This hotel is ideal for taking in sporting events as it has direct access to the Detroit people mover. This helps you avoid darkened walks in Detroit (which can be unnerving at times) after the game is completed. They also have visible security on duty at night which is also comforting. (I've not ever felt threatened in Detroit, but it does have it's problems. This added security feature made us feel valued). The pool area was fun for the kids and has a walk out deck to look out to the river. The staff was very friendly and helpful as well. We will definitely utilize this property for our next Tiger game as well.

title: “Perfectly fine but there are better hotels in LA”
text: I like Sofitel hotels generally but this one was a little uninspiring and I think you can do better in LA. Staff were okay but didn't really go out of their way for you which is a shame as one of my favourite things about LA is just how incredibly friendly people are. Location of the hotel was fine but not awesome. It's very well located for shopping though. I was just here for a one night stop over so it was perfectly adequate. My room was clean although nothing special and had a view of a car park. The pool was pleasant enough and pool staff were very accommodating and friendly. The concierge was the star of the show - great restaurant recommendations and bang on every time as to what I was after. I wouldn't not stay here again but it wouldn't be my first choice in LA.

title: “Will definitely stay there again”
text: Our room was large, clean and the bed was oh so comfortable. We asked for a small bar fridge and it was deleivered with 10 minutes. We were in the center of everything. We walked to Central Park, American Museum of Natural History, Madison Square Garden (Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers concert), Chinatown, 5th Avenue, Times Square...you name it. Never used a taxi once. Affordable restaurant and liquor store across the street; supermarket and drug store within minutes walk. Nice bar virtually across the street. I cannot think of a more ideal location. Staff helpful and friendly. Didn't partake of the breakfast due to the long lines but it was not a problem for us. Wife wants to go back becasue she felt she never shopped enough : ) . if we do go back we'll be staiyng at the Hampton Inn. We came down from Newfoundland, Canada.

title: “Very good, but with reservations”
text:
Stayed here to try it out as previously stayed at Soho House (fav), Mercer (2nd fav) and The Bowery (least fav of the three).
My wife and I love design hotels, and The Greenwich lived up to expectations in terms of decor in most cases - in general really well done and good atmosphere all round. Borderline 'Swiss chalet' in some areas, but overall a good, warm design. We stayed in a deluxe Greenwich, and a few weird fittings in the room didn't seem to go very well (chandelier for one), but this was offset by the size, bathrooms and overall feel.
Staff were friendly and helpful in many cases - but there's certainly room for improvement - at the front desk in particular - and the speed of service in the communal areas could certainly be improved.
The spa is as good as it looks in the pictures, although the spa treatments seemed totally over the top price-wise - even for a hotel at this level. It's about double of similar places so I gave it a miss although I would have liked to try.
The Italian restaurant (which also served breakfast) was also good - although the breakfast itself was very lacking in terms of any kind of self service items (juice, cereals etc). By lacking i mean non-existent, with menu ordering only.
The courtyard's lovely.
There were a few negatives, and they would make me think twice about staying again.
Noise: The room was very noisy - we could hear another room like the occupants were in ours. May have been through the air vents or something. Unfortunately for us, the guests in that room were [--] all through the night and were [--] movie loud.
