Several attempts to address this at front desk and get moved were pretty much dismissed and ignored. They said they were full, but to pay this money and not get any sleep is ridiculous - am sure they had higher spec rooms and should have moved us. Not good.
Perhaps that wouldn't have been quite so bad if the garbage truck didn't stop by outside our room at about 4:30-5am every morning for an hour, crushing rubbish. We had a room on the North Moore side, 4th floor, and I was woken up every morning - after an already reduced sleep. Not good again.
The best part of the room was the free basket of snacks and all soft drinks and water being free - not only that but they're topped up each day! A very nice touch.
Having checked my bill, it looks like they charged the posting of a letter I gave them at checkout to my credit card - £0.64p. Nothing technically wrong with that - but seems a bit petty and has never happened anywhere I've stayed before.
I've never stayed Tribeca before, and thought it was a nice change from Soho and Meatpacking, although in general we always walked into Soho as there's not too much to do around the area (although there is a great breakfast at Bubby's just round the corner)
All-in-all a good experience, but certainly wasn't made to feel special which is always what the end judgement comes down to. Why do these hotels insist on not having the front of house sorted out, and a bit more willing to please? Simple things like that are always the easiest to fix, and make the biggest difference to a guest.

title: “Total Disaster”
text:
Why? I'm a frequent business traveler and have stayed at this hotel before. My last trip showed the Roosevelt lack of class. I had a confirmed room purchased using a pricing service. When I arrived at 7pm, after a long day, the counter informed me that there was no room- they sold out. They gave me cab fare to an inferior hotel outside of the Grand Central area. I took the next 45 minutes to call around and found a nice hotel.
Again- Roosevelt showed no class on this one.

title: “Nice hotel, nice location for the valley”
text:
I stayed here for spring training this last weekend. I got a great deal of 120 USD for 2 nights from priceline. I really liked the hotel, it was very clean, the staff were fantastic and the rooms were great. I cant complain about this hotel stay. the location is in the central valley so getting to anywhere is easy with the easy access to the local freeways.
the only drawback was that the pool area this time of year didnt seem to get much sun during the day, but the water is heated so it didnt matter too much. I would absolutely stay here again!!

title: “Omni Hotel was great”
text: Spent a night at the Omni Hotel in Austin. Great place, friendly people. Clean room. The front desk was also very helpful with my questions about the area. I recommend it for families. They had an indoor and outdoor pool too, which was great for the kids.

title: “new york”
text:
Although this is an older Hotel it is full of character and the staff are so freindly and helpfull.
It can be a bit noisy but thats only because you are in the center of everything that is New York. Times Square is right on your door step. Loved it all

title: “Good Hotel, Convenient to Downtown but out of the traffic”
text: Clean quiet place about 10 to 15 minutes from University, restaurants, and downtown. Good free breakfast

title: “If You Like Vomit Stay at The New York Palace”
text:
At The New York Palace we had the worst hotel experience in 30 years!
The sheets and towels and the room had a overwhelming smell of vomit. We immediately went down to the reservation desk and spoke to all of the reservation agents including the reservation manager. Every one of them told us there was a problem with the laundry that did their linens and unfortunately they had been washed with water that had been recycled and they did smell of vomit. We asked for either fresh sheets, to be relocated to a new room or have alternate arrangements made with another hotel. The manager said they would change the sheets but when we came back at 11:30 pm no one had touched the room. The hotel manager said he was sorry and he knew that the smell was awful but there was nothing he could do. We spent over two hours on a Canadian cell phone which cost almost $3.00 a minute and when we asked for a Taxi voucher to take us to a new hotel they would not give it to us.
How can a hotel still take bookings and not notify their clients of this problem.

title: “Phenomenal Service at the Bar!”
text: The service here was EXCEPTIONAL. Don't get me wrong, I enjoyed the small plates and diverse liquor menu, but having it all brought quickly and efficently. Priceless. Oh, and the location (underground like a speak easy) ensured that my BB wasn't bothering me every two minutes.

title: “Very Good City Break Hotel”
text: We used the Charlemark as our base camp for the first 4 nights, and the last one night of our 2 week holiday. This hotel is in a very good location for walking in and out of the city itself. 10 minutes to the Common and Boylston St is parrallel to Newbury St (top class shopping) The room was clean and tidy, the facilities were good and the staff on the front desk were always helpful. The hotel is also a bar/restaurant and the food (Thai) was nice indeed. One minor point was that the breakfast was a little spartan (bagels, doghnuts and fruit) and a suggestion is maybe a yoghurt or two to add variety. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “convenient”
text:
Being just around the corner fron Times Square, the hotel was located in a fantastic position. Was a little bit concerned with the thin boards seperating the rooms. We could here the remotest of sounds including someone ruffling paper and someone else snooring. Not to mention the constant shutting and opening of doors. The rooms were very small, but clean and the showers were large with a constant stream of hot water.
We were not happy with the bar being closed for the whole weekend as the website neglected to tell us this.
The breakfast was a very adequate continental display although i would have liked the opportunity to have had some bread.

title: “Very relaxing, look forward to going back!”
text: The staff was extremely helpful and very courteous! The room was beautiful and very comfortable. The view was amazing. I will definately be back as often as possible.

title: “Nicely redone, with attentive service”
text:
This historic hotel has been nicely refurbished, with attractive public spaces and comfortable, spacious standard ("superior") rooms. The usual high-end urban hotel amenities are present: robes, minibars, cable TV, pay wifi, mid priced room service -- plus there is free bottled water, newspaper delivery, turn-down service, and morning coffee in the restaurant. 
The youngish reception staff are attentive in trying to make sure that everyone's needs are met. 
On the negative side, compared to other choices in the San Diego area, the hotel has no views, nor is the restaurant food exceptional.
On the positive side, one doesn't need a car to roam the city proper; it's only a few minutes (pleasant and safe) walk to the Gaslamp restaurant and bar district, Petco ballpark, convention center, downtown marina and waterfront, and downtown Horton Plaza shopping mall. There is also a public trolley at the front door with lines that go to various other parts of the city, and it is a short (though not super-cheap) taxi ride to the airport.
I would request that hotels such as this that are trying to be "green" consider, one, having recycling bins in the room for guests' bottles and paper, and, two, offer shampoos and soaps that are not loaded with chemicals. I also cannot understand why the hotel put in vanity-top sinks so trendy and huge and tall that a 5'2 adult can't reach them to wash her face.

title: “Not the Greatest Customer Service”
text: When I entered the lobby I thought I was in for a great experience. Not so. The clerk at the front desk rushed me through my check in - when I went back later to ask some questions I was again rushed. My package included breakfast for two - I asked the clerk if since I was just one person could I have room service breakfast instead - she said no and suggested I bring a friend (I'm on vacation in a City where I don't know anyone, but I guess I could have grabbed someone off the street!) I also didn't have a robe in my room - the clerk said not every room has robes, although the hotel's web site doesn't indicate that. They did finally send me a robe but they seemed bothered by my request. One of the shower heads did not work at first - they did finally fix it. The food for the breakfast buffet was boring. The one plus for me was the martinis in the hotel bar - try the cucumber one! Not a 4-star experience for me and I would not likely stay there again unless I got an exceptional deal.

title: “Nice hotel”
text: My husband and I went to Chicago for a day to shop the Magnificent Mile. I got a good deal on the Westin. It's a nice hotel and I must say, from all the reviews regarding the rude workers there, we found every single one of them to be extremely friendly and helpful. I had left my cell phone in the car and we asked them to retrieve it for us. Unfortunately, there was miscommunication between workers as to where it was left for us to pick it up and it took 3 trips down to search the car by my husband only to discover it had been locked away in a drawer the whole time. They were very apologetic. The beds were lovely! The only complaints were that for a 4-star hotel I expect almost pristine conditions. The TV armoire door was broke, the hallways were extremely dirty and needed to be vacuumed and the price of the mini-bar items was outrageous. But it's more about how we were treated and we were treated well.

title: “Amazing hotel in a great location”
text: Brilliant hotel. Had a very Spacious room that was spotlessly clean. Even though its in the centre of things its very quiet at night. Times square is just a short walk away and Macy's is practically next door! In the mornings there was free coffee, tea and hot chocolate which was lovely. Very helpful, friendly staff. Try to get a room overlooking the front as you'll have an amazing view of the Empire State Building! Would definately go back.

title: “The Mayfair is the place to stay”
text:
I actually found this hotel through a friend. We were all scheduled to be at a convention at the NY Hilton on 53rd. Rates at the Hilton were very high, so we looked for a less expensive hotel that was nearby. The Mayfair fit the bill. I was sharing the room with my mother, so we opted for the King room. As stated in previous reviews the room was small but more than adequate for our needs. There was even an oversized comfy chair in the room. The bathroom was very nicely appointed with a bathtub/shower combo, vanity shelf, hairdryer, plenty of towels, mirrors and marble. Our room faced 47th, but we never heard any street noise even though we were on the 3rd floor. There were double windows which worked as a noise insulator. The air conditioning unit worked well. There was a large TV on a shelf over the small built in desk unit. The desk housed a complete computer setup w/flat screen and printer. It was great to be able to check my e-mail. The bed was very comfortable. There were more than enough pillows and the bedding was very clean. There was even an extra blanket in the closet. After getting back late one night, I asked the desk clerk if there was an ice machine as we brought back some sodas. He had a full ice bucket brought to our room immediately. 
 All in all, this was a very pleasant stay. The next time I need to stay in NYC, this will definitely be the first place I check. It is easily accesible to the subway, buses and Grand Central. It is right in the middle of where you want to be.

title: “One of the prime hotels in Chicago”
text:
Locationwise, The Wit is excellent to explore Chicago main touristic attractions. Because of "The Roof - which by the way I prefered when it was open - there will be always a huge influe of people. 
The room we got was excellent with a great view of the Marina City Towers and the Chicago River. The bathroom was amazing, and the room we got had a good size, not tiny as other design/boutique hotels. 
Overall a very good stay. For the right price I would go stay again at The Wit.

title: “Great stay!”
text:
On a whim I decided to take advantage of a flight sale earlier in the year and go back to DC for the first time in 25 years to see the museums and relax. I found a great deal at the Westin Grand and thoroughly enjoyed my stay there.
The room was a nice size, it was very clean, had a comfortable bed and a great bathroom. I didn't eat at the hotel restaurant as I prefer to go out and explore, but I did have a drink at the bar and chatted to staff and locals. Nearby you've got everything from Starbucks to drug stores and Trader Joe's and you're a short walk from loads of restaurants, the Metro at Foggy Bottom and Georgetown.
Being in a residential area also means that the hotel is very quiet and I really couldn't have asked for a better hotel as the base for my exploration of DC.

title: “Fantastic Service, So-So Rooms”
text: The stellar customer service and lobby are the only reasons I would choose the Waldorf on my next stay in Manhattan. The rooms are an average size for NYC standards but dated and in need of some TLC to bring them up to Waldorf standards - particularly the bathrooms. Room was clean but old A/C unit was very noisy. Bathroom were very small. The mid-town location is convenient and you are close to Grand Central Station, which is also a plus. The lobby is grand and well-worth a slow stroll through to people watch and check out the beautiful ceilings and tile work.

title: “Worst hotel I ever paid 150/night for... quality of a truck stop”
text: Went to an anesthesia meeting there, and arrived two days early to see the sights. Arrived late in the evening, and was given a room facing a wall. Had reserved a room with an water view, and upon opening the door, the stench of animal urine hit me in the face. (evidently, they allow pets). Asked to be moved to a room that didn't smell and faced the water. Was given a room facing the road and bay upstairs over the lobby. (no elevator - had to carry bags up two flights of stairs) Room was the quality of a truck stop. Old furniture, small tv, few cable stations. Bathroom had light so dim, you couldn't see yourself in the mirror. If you were over five feet two inches, you had to bend down to get under the shower nozzle. Opening the closet door, we were once again hit with animal urine smell that since it had been closed up, it was so strong that it made me start coughing. Asked for another room. Got another one in the very same condition. Gave up since we had been traveling for twelve hours to get to the west coast and we were exhausted, so I asked them for room deodorizer spray. The faucets on the sink twirled in 360 degrees, so you had to keep turning them to get them to come on and shut off. Took a shower in the morning, and water wouldn't heat above luke warm. Walked out of the room and noticed the dirty dishes left on trays in front of two rooms next to us were still there from the night before. Headed off to go sight seeing and returned that evening, the dishes were still there and the hallway was very smelly from food left on the floor. Asked the front desk to have them removed. After two more calls over two more days, I finally called hotel manager and he seemed perturbed at the request. Said he would get them picked up immediately. Came back to my room in four hours, and one tray had been picked up and two others still remained. The hallway stunk, the room stunk... we stayed out as much as possible. The bed coverings also had animal urine smell.... I know that smell because I've had dogs all my life, and I know it well. Came home and washed everything I hung in closets because my clothes retained the putrid odor. Concierge desk is a joke. They knew nothing about restaurants or activities in the area. Couldn't arrange a simple ticket to the zoo.

title: “Spring Break”
text: I couldn't wait to get back to write my review after we got back from our Spring Break trip. I was nervous about the hotel because there are so many to choose from. My family and I loved the location and everything about the hotel was very pleasant. Our room was very clean, roomy, the beds were comfortable, and it was complete with mini fridge and microwave. The staff was very friendly and helpful, they always greated us when we walked through the door. They offered us a bottle of water each day for our touring and when my older daughter and I would run in the mornings they would also offer us water upon our return to the hotel. The location was perfect for our family, we walked everywhere since the hotel is so close to the Washington Mall, the White House is only a block away. The breakfast buffet and omlets were a perfect start for our busy day, we ate there every morning and it was all delicious. If I were to visit DC again I would definately not hesitate to choose this hotel again.

title: “Good for one short night”
text: We would not have chosen to stay at this hotel but the Days Inn a few doors down was remodeling and could not honor our reservation for a room with two beds. The office staff did give us a room at the same discounted AAA rate but I wonder if they got the best of the deal. The room was small and did not include a coffee maker, 'fridge, or microwave. The room and the bathroom were clean. Breakfast consisted of coffee and a prepackaged Danish. Since we checked in late and were leaving early, the room was okay for us. I would not have wanted to stay there for an extended vacation. The hotel is handy to many S.F. sites and included free parking if your vehicle is small enough for their spaces. The Day's Inn allowed us to park our extended cab pickup at their facility; otherwise we would have had to park on the street.

title: “Excellent hotel”
text: Awesome hotel in a convenient location. Super friendly and informative staff. Rooms were sparkling clean and fresh. The beds at this place are unbelievable! I usually toss alot but I don't think I even moved at all. Great hot showers! We stayed in a junior suite on the 37th floor with spectacular views of the Empire State Bldg, Chrysler Bldg, river and more. We paid $195.00 per night on Travelocity. The hotel's site also offered the same deal. Overall, a great experience. Would highly recommend.

title: “Great location, in the middle of "things."”
text:
Our second visit to NYC found us on a return stay at his hotel. This 40+ floor hotel is top notch, with open, glassed elevators, surprisingly spacious rooms, restaurants, in various price ranges, gift shops, a consierge very willing to assist in getting theater tickets, maps, or answer any questions you may have and a great fitness center. The View restaurant sits on the top floor, with revolving views of the city. After 8 pm there is a cover. Prices begin at $30 . Ratings score it high for views, but mid to low range for quality of food and service. We opted NOT to dine there, this trip. 
We stayed on the 37th floor, overlooking Time's Square...facing ABC studios. Granted directly across from us was a large office building, but the wall of floor to ceiling windows allowed for great views of the down town, (especially at night with all the lights) , 
Location is literally around the corner from Times Square. The Roxy Deli, a McDonald's, ABC studios and the TCKTs discount booth for Broadway show tickets are all right there, in that block, along with favorite street vendors ranging from hot dog, peanuts, and pretzel vendors along with purse and scarf "salesmen." Great energy and something going on in every direction. Super location, near theaters, popular restaurants...open late for dining, after the shows, too. A block from Junior's famous Cheese cake restaurant, Sardi's, to name a few.
Suggest a stay here if you want to be in the center of it all.

title: “Great place to stay”
text:
I loved this place. The staff was friendly and went above the call of duty to make everything right. During making reservations I mentioned that my wife and I would be there during our anniversary and when we checked in they had a fruit basket in the room waiting.
I use to stay at the Holiday-Inn family of hotels but from now on, if there is a Candlewood in the area I will stay with them.
The only complaint, They have some energy saver on the A/C and while your not in the room it cuts off or cuts back, no biggie just would rather come in to a cool room.

title: “Wonderfull Resort”
text: We stayed at the Owners Club at Barton Creek. 3 bedroom, 3 bath detached homes that are a short walk from the resort hotel and spa. We had access to all the amentities, could charge the room etc. The home was fantastic all high end furnishings and decor. If you are vacationing in Austin with a family this is the place to stay

title: “Friendly staff and a great location”
text: Located right down the block from Beale St., this Hampton Inn has a great location and a wonderfully friendly staff that makes you feel very welcome. I never once came into the lobby without being greeted and any requests were dealt with immediately. The rooms show a bit of wear, but are neat and clean with comfortable furniture. Old school thermostats could use updating and the TV's are showing their age, but overall this works well for the traveller who is here for the sounds of Memphis.The parking garage works out great with your key allowing easy access in and out, and if you like music, a room right across from the park works out pretty well. If your looking for piece and quiet however, I'd probably look somewhere a little further from the action, but if Beale St. is your main purpose for being in town this is a nice affordable choice.

title: “updated but small”
text:
Stayed at the WJ in mid July 2011. Was a lovely hotel in a great location. It is evident that it is a much older building, but has recently been updated with quite modern fixtures. The staff was great and always helpfull. Our only problem was that the rooms were extreemly small. Luggage or anything extra CANNOT fit into the room. That was the only dissapointing thing. The hotel has on e resturant which serves Japanesse food and only served lunch and dinner. Getting breakfast wasn't so far off and did not seem inconvenient. Would have been nice to at least have coffee makers though and a bar fridge, but again the room was so small it would not be able to accommodate that.
All in all was a good experience ! But this hotel is suitable for only short trips and the size of the space can really become annoying.

title: “Great!!!!!!”
text: Myself and my husband stayed there 20-25th Nov 2008 our 3rd time in NY, but its the only hotel we would go back to. We were upgraded when we got there room 2735. Great location diner next door serves great breakfeast even takeaway!!! Starbucks across the street for coffee. Subway nxt door - Located within walking distance to all shops 5th ave macys Irish bar (Rosie o'gradys) just down the street so is carniege delli great cakes. If your like me with no sense of direction this hotel is good for you right beside central park and times square. Staff very helpful rooms very clean. Im going back next november with my sisters without my husband and would feel confident enough because of its location. The only bit of advice I would say dont make calls from your room costs a fortune buy card for gift shop in hotel calls only cost 90cent a call. Take a trip 2 jersey gardens worth it bring big bag or suit case with u for the bags if u like to shop like us irish !!! Hope u enjoy it as much as we did. Jen & Keenan (Ireland)

title: “Expected more - Disappointed with the Millennium”
text:
We stayed here on a Friday night, and the hotel was in the perfect location, right on 44th street in Times Square, its just behind (down the street) from ToysRUs. No complaints about the location at all. We arrived at the hotel around midnight and my husband had to go inside and locate a valet. The hotel charges $44 for 24 hours of parking, which is comparable to other NYC hotels. So no problems there, although you would expect the valet to have been readily available when we arrived at the door.
When we made our reservation we requested a king non-smoking room, we were first put into a room with 2 over-sized twin beds (I was shocked - I've never seen this size bed in any hotel), in addition the room smelled of smoke. The front desk sent up a machine to clear the air while we were out walking about in Time Square, we arrived back in the room the smell was still bad. We called down again and they arranged to move us to another room, a bellman brought us a new key, but when we got to the room the key didn't work......finally a security guy came and opened our room with a key, he told us we could go to the front desk in the morning and obtain a new key (not the service I would have expected from this level of hotel). Anyway, we were tired and just wanted to get into bed at this time. This room had 2 double beds and no wash cloths (random I know), but there were no blankets on the beds. Again I was shocked; the bedding consisted of a sheet with a bedspread on top. I don't know about you but I always remove the bedspread, because we all know they don't wash them with each change of guest (EW!). Anyway, I did location a raggy blanket in the closet but it looked clean. 
The bright spot was in the morning, we went to the theater desk and a very helpful gentleman helped us secure decent tickets at a fair price for a show that night; (BTW see Spam-A-Lot it was fantastic).
Overall, we were disapponted with the Millennium Broadway we expected more from this hotel. Next time in NYC, we'll go back to the Marriott Marquis.

title: “great hotel, great location”
text: This hotel is clean and appears to be recently remodeled. The staff was friendly. The continental breakfast was more adequate, even if the space was a bit small for the number of guests. My only complaint was that it seems to take a long time to get an elevator in the morning because of so many people moving to and from the breakfast area. This hotel was a bright spot in a weekend filled with otherwise mediocre service.

title: “Excellence!!!”
text: After this weekend the Westin Downtown has become my favorite hotel in the Phoenix area. It went beyond my expectations. The building itself is modern and beautiful. Our regular room was more of a suite. It was double the size of the regular rooms you get at any other hotel. I am not that easy to please and impress but this hotel is excellent. The staff was very friendly and helpful and usually I am not one to write a review but a certain worker there by the name of Jose Garcia went out of his way to be pleasant and helpful. Let me elaborate, my husband and I went to have dinner at the Province restaurant and there we met Mr. Garcia, as he is one of the cooks. We inquired about the special Puerto Rican menu they had for that night. He was delightful to speak to and very friendly. Our dinner was as delicious as he described it. Thank you to the whole Westin staff and special thanks to Mr. Garcia.

title: “Bad from start to finish”
“Family Fun”
text:
We had a one bedroom suite with kitchenette. What a great location!! So good there were never any parking spaces. I noticed there were cars parked for the hotel that never left the entire time we were there (work trucks etc). Would lead me to believe there were residents in the neighborhood using the lot. As we had to wake up hour on the hour to try to find a spot!! One night we even said FORGET IT as we couldn't find anywhere to park (yes in January) and gambled with being towed!! It would be worth the owners time and money to find alternatives for his guests.
Rooms were great, staff was horrible. I don't think I got two words from front desk during checkin or check out!

title: “Nice Hotel but Watch Out for Breakfast”
text:
The hotel has a great location, and my room on the 21st floor had a great view of Boston harbor. My room was large and comfortable. However, this is another new hotel that, in spite of being well designed and built, fails when it comes to service. 
The hotel would have received five stars if the breakfast had not been so poor. I had a business breakfast the first morning so we ate in the main restaurant. I ordered what I believe is billed as Organic Maine Oats, along with a bagel. The oatmeal arrived as a thin gruel and the toasted bagel was slathered in butter or some such spread. I would have sent both back, but since I was with other people, I only asked that the bagel be replaced with one toasted but dry. The waitress complied with my request, but certainly not with a smile. The breakfast buffet may have been much better than the off-menu food, but I did not get to sample that. 
The second morning I had breakfast in the Concierge Lounge on the 20th floor. The food was good, but all the cereal bowls were hot, as they were just taken out of the dishwasher. The attendant apologized for the hot bowls, a plus for service, but I do wonder why the management thinks that they cannot afford an extra set of cereal bowls so that their loyal customers do not have to pour cold milk into steaming hot bowls. 
For dinner at least, you can walk to the nearby Legal Seafoods and get a good meal.

title: “Nice hotel, shame about the front desk staff”
text:
Stayed for 3 nights.
Check in - Arrived at 4pm for check in and were given room 245, we were'nt directed to it and had to ask where the elevator was!
Room: 
On entering the room it was small but clean, then we saw the balcony - tiny! One chair, we were not happy (we had upgraded to deluxe as we wanted a balcony and we wanted to avoid the noise issue as discussed on previous posts). 
We returned to reception requesting another room - the front desk was very reluctant saying they were full but she eventually said room 251 was still being cleaned and sent us up to find house keeping so we could check it out (after about 10 minutes searching for house keeping we were shown it) - it was a nice big room - had a decent balcony with views of the harbour/carpark.We were then told it would be 2 hours before it would be ready (2 hours to clean a room?)
Small price to pay!! So we got into our room at 6pm.
It was comfortable and clean with modern furniture.
Location;
Nice location for a walk along the harbour front - childrens play area not far from the hotel (just turn right out of hotel along the front). Some but not many restaurants nearby - they looked pricey!
You definitely need a car but Seaworld and the zoo were easy from here. $5 parking fee per night.
Services;
Pool, fairly nice and just warm enough (have to walk through the bar area to get to it and you are on show). You have to ask for pool towels at reception and they often run out (in fact they promised to bring some out to us and yet again they did'nt).
Bar, nice bar with a view serving food which was quite nice. They have a happy hour but service was VERY slow - 20 minutes to get table service (I saw others having the same problem too).
Breakfast, the best service at this hotel! Our waiter was efficient and friendly. The breakfast was varied and I have no complaints there ;)
They also had a small gym and a laundrette which was very handy.
The walls seemed to be very thin, we could hear phone conversations and TV quite clearly from the next room.
Overall, nice hotel, nice location, the staff need some customer service training (to clarify - not all the front desk staff were unhelpful either). For what we paid, I don't think it was worth it.

title: “Budget Hotel in a Great Location”
text:
A group of four of us stayed at The Powell for two nights, at the start of our roadtrip down to LA (see other reviews for the hotels we stayed in).
For a city centre mid range hotel the price we paid is what you would expect. Overall I was impressed. The location is the main draw to the place. First, look on Google Maps and see how close you are to the Powell St BART. We caught the train from the airport (took 45 minutes or so) and we were amazed when we came out of the station how close the hotel actually was!
You are also so close to the cable car route. Right outside the front door is the Powell St turntable. Large crowds of people will be there waiting to jump on the cable car but you can just stand and watch if you want. Great photo opportunities as cable cars are parkign there for you to jump on get a great photo. On the first day that we arrived we decided to walk, up the steep hills and down the other side heading for Fishermans Wharf and it probably took us 30 mins, at a relatively slow pace. Other times, we jumped on the cable car or the streetcars that run along Market Street and down to the Wharf. 
Nearby, there are plenty of restaurants and bars if you want to go for wander and sample some nightlife. Also plenty of shops with Union Square a 5-10 minute walk or so
The hotel is good, I would have marked higher but the rooms are not worth the extra rating. Not because we found them to be dirty or anything like that, just basic and what you would expect for the money. The rooms were clean and served their purpose brilliantly. The only thing I would mention is that the windows could do with being thicker for more soundproofing. The noise from the busy SF streets is loud. Also the curtains are decorative so you can't draw them to try and help muffle the noise. 
The hotel serves a complimentary breakfast, though it is more coffee and doughnuts so don't expect to be filled up ready for the day. We didn't mind, it was nice to get a good cup of coffee before we went to a nearby diner for breakfast.
There is a coffee shop right at the front of the hotel if you want more coffee and they sell bagels etc
All in all, if you are in San Francisco for a short trip/passing through and you know that you are not spending very much time in your hotel I would absolutely recommend the Powell Hotel. If you are there for longer and want more luxury in your room, then you may want to spend a little more elsewhere. The location is amazing though so The Powell will always have that in it's favour.

title: “Wonderful new hotel”
text:
This is an excellent hotel for visitors to the downtown area. While, as a new hotel, it is still working out some kinks (e.g., there was no iron in the room, some lights didn't work, etc.), the staff is wonderful and fixed all these problems quickly. I should also note that the walk-in rain/standard shower is the nicest and largest I've seen at any hotel. Also, the fitness center is marvelous. I've already made two other reservations at this hotel and will keep coming back.
One of the few things I would recommend that the hotel fix is the desk chair- as a business traveler, a good, supportive, height-adjustable desk chair is a must. While the leather desk chair was beautiful, it was uncomfortable, too low, and I ended up having to work on the couch. Also, ice machines need to be made available.

title: “great value”
text:
This is a great hotel. Staff is super nice, workout facilities and pool work. Cool bar and restaurant with a great looking crowd even in the middle of the week.
This is not an Ian Shrager Mondrian type of "chic" place, but it isn't priced like one either. Will definitely stay there again.

title: “Fabulous stay!”
text:
My daughter and I went to NY for a few days to celebrate her 16th birthday. Our first night we stayed here and then we were transferring over to Times Square. Before we checked out, we were very sad to leave this hotel, as everyone was so helpful and friendly. It almost felt like home! We talked with Joey, the concierge/navigator, for quite a while and ended up knowing mutual friends in Louisiana-small world! He recommended places to eat and places to see. He also send up a box of birthday chocolates with a hand written note for her while we were out that night!
The room is small but very nice. Plenty of closet space but little drawer space.The bed is plush and very comfortable. Great view and very little noise could be heard from down below. Joey told us that it was once an all women's residence back in the day, and when it was taken over by the hotel, the rooms became smaller to add a bathroom in each one. But the room, bathroom, lobby, and the hotel itself is very modern, clean and lovely. We even called from The Met to say we were running late and needed a late check-out(normal time is 12) and they gave us the option to check out whenever we needed. I reallly appreciated that as we no longer felt hurried.

title: “Loved it”
text: I stayed here while attending a conference at the Marriott across the street. This was cheaper and more comfortable. As other reviewers have noted, this is a gem of a hotel. It's a true suite, with living room, full kitchen, and bedroom. The living room has a sofabed, sitting chair, coffee table and 32" LCD TV. There is a small dining table/desk next to the kitchen. The kitchen has microwave, two burner oven, dishwasher, coffee maker, fridge. Also plates, pots/pans and silverware. The room was clean and comfortable with no obvious signs of wear. The king size bed was also comfy, though not as high end as you would find in a nicer hotel. There is a regular tube TV in the bedroom. The free buffet breakfast had scrambled eggs, meats, cereal, make your own waffles, etc. There is also a dinner with a different menu Mon-Thurs but I did not have that. There is a gym inhouse, but you can use the Crunch gym next door (same building) that is much bigger and has everything. The entrance is not much to look at; just an elevator to the sixth floor where reception is. But the bellman was friendly and the reception desk was efficient and very friendly. It does cost a lot to park here (I think $42/night so don't bring a car). There is a small store next to reception, open 24/7. Free wired and wireless internet in the room. Only minor complaint is that the walls are somewhat thin so if the neighbor raises his voice I can hear it. Also, I can hear water running next door. But all in all I would definitely stay here again. It's much more comfortable and better value than the big hotels nearby.

title: “Pretty Bad”
text: What can I say but a tired Holiday Inn with some minor cosmetic upgrades. We will never stay at a Holiday Inn again based on our stay here. I booked based on the glowing remarks I had read here. Expected a comfortable stay but instead got a small room with a noisey A/C that after complaining never got fixed correctly. No hot water for two days out of six, rust covered bath drain, painted over chips in bath tub and a tiny bathroom. One morning decided to try breakfast at the Grill, big mistake! Sat down and ask waitress for menu and she flat out just told us to go to buffet and also get coffee there too. This was 10:00 am in morning after the buffet was cold and fully picked over. Couldn't find waitress again to try and force a menu out of her so we left. Also, I'm a priority club member and was to get a paper every morning. After calling desk three mornings in a row decided it must be getting swiped so asked them to hold one for me. No way and they didn't seem to care one bit. From now on we will stick with better hotels or if we want to save $$ we will pick someone else.

title: “Clean, casual, convenient”
text:
Stayed here during a conference that was being held at the Convention Center. 
Surprises: 
valet parking - usually don't have that at Courtyards
Residence inn was attached. Two hotels were combined into one
Champions - seems these are usually associated with Marriotts, not the Courtyards.
I stayed for 4 nights - very quiet and uneventful. It was nice to have a full restaurant in the building although I thought it was lame that the bar closed at 12am when the entire town is open to at least 2am.
The room was clean and seemed as if it was recently updated - looks the same as other "updated" rooms through the chain.
Service was fine - nothing over the top but it was solid. 
Food from the restaurant was pretty good - I had a burger and it was tasty. They've got a few local beers on tap which was nice. Also had breakfast (buffet) one time in the restaurant and it fine for a buffet.
Best part was that this hotel is literally a few steps away from the Convention Center - totally convenient. If I ever attend a conference in Austin again I'll definitely have this hotel at the top of the list.

title: “NOT HELPFUL AT ALL!”
text:
A/C problems in an old unventilated property... no one lifted a hand to help out. THEN, when we tracked someone down, they didn't care. Said I had to "...deal with it". 80+ degrees in my room... 65 degrees outside - IT WAS A MISERABLE EPXERIENCE!
The worst part... ?! My family owns a chain of Holiday Inn properties and I was treated like a dog in a sub par kennel!

title: “What a lobby!!!”
text: Great location and iconic hotel to stay at whilst in NYC. Public areas absolutely top notch but the rooms are just standard and nothing to write home about. All in all a great choice in an ideal part of town. In hindsight I'd do EXACTLY the same again.

title: “Fit Our Needs Perfect”
text:
We had an early flight to catch and did not feel like rushing from home to make it. Found online that this hotel was close and had a free shuttle. I was pleasantly surprised with the hotel. Our room was beautiful, clean, and quiet. We stayed with another couple and they were able to get us adjoining rooms. Had some difficulty with the climate control - it seemed to fluctate dramatically with out touching the thermostat. 
We had a late dinner at Connolly's. The food was good - but I think a little over priced for pub fair.
The wake-up call was on time. When it was time to catch the shuttle, the first one was full - but the second one was only a few minutes behind. That being said, the women got seperated from the men and we ended up taking two shuttles - we arrived within minutes of each other at the terminal. 
No questions asked, I would stay here again.

title: “Week stay at downtown Executive Hotel Vintage Court”
text:
Got an amazing deal of $119 per night for room, valet parking, and internet. For San Francisco, in such a central location, that's incredible.
Valet parking consisted of parking in front of the hotel and locking the car as there wasn't anyone there to hand over the key to. When we finished checking in, they gave us a claim check and we handed over the key. The car was parked in a nearby garage and we were asked to give them 20 minutes notice to get the car back. All very reasonable.
The hotel is an older one, with lots of creaking floorboards and squeaky door hinges. We liked that as it made the place have more personality. There were some updated touches, shower head, modern art in the rooms, bathroom fixtures etc. but not too many to take away from the charm.
Coffee available in the morning and wine hour in the afternoon, both downstairs in the lobby. A very nice touch and a good way to meet others staying there. Cozy fireplace always going too. It rained a couple of days during our stay, and it made for a welcoming touch after being out.
The location was both the best part and worst part of the hotel. It's centrally located, right off the Powell cable car line. Loved the fact that after walking all day, we could come back and rest before heading back out for drinks and dinner. We also used the local bus service (#38L on Geary and Powell) to take the muni out to the Legion of Honor museum and the same bus, the #38L with a transfer to the #28L to head up to the Golden Gate Bridge. There was no reason to get the car out and deal with the traffic because the hotel was situated so perfectly.
Ok--the downside. Noisy, noisy, noisy. Really no way to get around that. This is an urban hotel, there are sirens, and garbage trucks, and street repairs. We were on the 4th floor close to the front (Bush St). You might want to try for higher up and towards the back of the hotel. I slept all 7 nights with earplugs, as did my husband. The trade off of location and value was worth it to me to be so centrally located. You'll have to make your own decision on that.
Something I would like to recommend...the library gives free walking tours that are really good. The tour guides are volunteers, they have a wide range of tour topics, lasting about 2 hours. We went on 3...The Palace Hotel, Nob Hill, and the Civic Center. All very well done, informative, and with humor. http://www.sfcityguides.org/

title: “Perfect location for theatre and restaurants and very clean, comfortable and inexpensive.”
text: We had a perfect stay there--very easy to get to the theatre and restaurants by walking. Although there is no parking at the hotel, there is a garage next door. The room was very clean and quiet. And the hotel staff very helpful.

title: “The stunning lobby and the breakfast parfaits were the highlights”
text: This hotel is a round building buit as a circle which may itself date from the era of the Astrodome in Houston. So, we should not have been surprised that our large room was wedge-shaped with somewhat dated decor and furnishings. Although the windows in the room faced inward instead of to the outdoors, we actually did enjoy our view into the cavernous lobby which has been impressively redecorated by combining the look and feel of native Hill Country Limestone with the semi-tropical plants of South Texas. Hidden among the many items in the breakfast buffet in the lobby restaurant were the best breakfast parfaits that we've ever had - delicious combinations of fresh fuits, granola and yogurt. Our weekend rate had looked like a bargain until we learned of the additonal $ 11 per night parking charge upon check-in. The location of this hotel is very convenient if you need to stay on the grounds of the Airport but it's not really close to any of the popular sights and scenes in and around Austin.

title: “LOVELY HOTEL”
text: My boyfriend I booked this very last minute as the other accomodation we were staying in over in the pacific beach area of san diego had double booked our room for our last night in town, we were a bit wary of staying in a two star hotel but the price was right, $90 for a thursday night and it was only for one night so we took our chances. The hotel was very nice, we had a room with a courtside view, which really means no view at all, but this didnt bother us as we were a stones throw from the ocean and everything else we needed was right nearby.....restaurants, bars etc. The hotel was clean, our room was average sized, the bathroom a bit on the small side but otherwise fine and the shower was great. All basics were provided....tv, fridge, towels....as you would expect. The hotel had a lovely garden and an amazing ocean view and we found the staff here very pleasant and courteous. As far as the general area goes we both much preferred the Pacific Beach area to Ocean Beach. Ocean beach is much more quiet and probably more suited to older people, we are both in our early twenties and Pacific Beach had a great buzz about it. As far as the actual beaches are concerned, again Pacific Beach wins, it was much longer with a proper boardwalk type area for cycling/roller-blading etc with many shops, cafes and restaurants right along the beach, whereas Ocean Beach had none of this although Newport avenue had many shops and esp antique outlets...again prob for the older generation, even Mission Beach has a bit more going for it. We probably would stay here again if we were presented with the same situation i.e. no rooms available in Pacific beach....but we would prefer to be where the party is!

title: “Great Price, Good for Kids, Thin Walls, No Fast Food”
text:
The price for my stay in December was approximately $129 a night, which is pretty good for a two-room studio with King Bed, Full-Sized Fridge, Kitchen Table, Foldout Couch, and RCA Jack friendly Television set. 
I booked two nights on a Friday and Saturday. I had heard, from reading other reviews, the walls are paper thin. I also heard that fast food is not an easy find. Well, it's true. The walls are very thin, and finding fast food was a chore.
Not one night passed without hearing sounds of people talking in neighboring rooms. In the living room, I could hear the family next door talking and watching T.V. In the bedroom I could hear the people on the other side of the wall talking and watching T.V. The loudest noises, however, came from the outside hallway (mostly kids running up and down the halls) and the window, which faced the pool. I was on the third floor, but it didn't help much. The noise from the pool echoed into my room all day and up until 9 p.m. or so in the evening. As for sleeping in, it didn't happen in this hotel. I tried both mornings, and woke each day at 7 a.m. to the sound of slamming doors or kids running up and down the hallway. In some strange way, it reminded me of Disney Land, just outside my front door! On the plus side, the King bed was extremely comfortable! It's just too bad the noise was so loud.
In spite of all the noise, the room was nice and the occupants of the hotel all seemed friendly and family oriented. This is definitely a place for married couples with kids. I felt safe my entire stay.
As for food, it's hard to find unless you plan on taking in a sit-down meal. Check-in time is at 4 p.m. I arrived my first day at 3 p.m. Unfortunately, my room was not ready, and I was told I would have to come back later. I drove around looking for something to eat but couldn't find anything of the fast-food variety anywhere near the hotel. I drove past the local mall, down a few side streets, and eventually found a Wendy’s. The problem is, it was about 15 minutes away from the room, and with traffic congestion somewhat prevalent in the Hotel Circle area, it took me a while to get there and get back. One bit of advice: bring your own food. It's cheaper and you'll thank yourself later. Also, there is no room service, etc., so if you get a late night craving, you’re on your own.
Overall, the hotel was decent. It's loud and parking at $10 a night seemed high, but the people were nice enough. Also, the elevators in this building are very slow! Slow to arrive, slow to open the doors. I couldn’t believe how long I had to wait. Use the stairs if you’re in a rush. It's a good workout and you won't have to wait around five minutes for the elevator to pick you up!
One final comment. It would be nice if the hotel had more parking spots for guests of hotel guests. There are only about 7 total spots in front of the hotel. A business associate stopped by one evening to visit me and had to wait 30 minutes to find a parking spot. Parking in the back for hotel guests is pretty abundant, but you must have a room card to park there, along with a hotel parking pass to display in your window. Also, it does fill up late at night, but most other times it's easy to find a spot.

title: “Decent Stay.”
text: Location was pretty good. Just a couple of blocks from the Harbour. Our room was on a corner where there was a night club. And on saturday night, the music was pretty loud. We had a king size bed, that was ok. The air conditioner was pretty loud. We had the Romance package that came with a "bottle" of champagne and an assortment of chocolates. Champagne was a 1/4 bottle of Brut. NOT very nice. And was warm when brought to the room And 6 lindor chocolates. Valet was very expensive at $32. And it took about 20 minutes for the car.

title: “Great Location”
text: This was our first trip to New York City and the Doubletree Times Square was a perfect!!! Being to be in the heart of Times Square was wonderful!!! Our room was great, we had a great view of Times Square and the Subway and the double decker tour bus stop were right outside our hotel door!!! Would for sure stay here again!!!

title: “Standard Hotel, Great Location, Excellent Customer Service”
text:
The room was adequate and nicely decorated. The bathroom is very small and has an air vent that's loud and could not be shut off or closed. 
Free access to the fitness room which included a pool, hot tub, exercise machine and weights. 
The hotel is located downtown with easy access to many restaurants and shops. The meeting rooms were adequate. Wi-fi access is available for a fee, although I was told that you had to pay for every device. I happened to have a laptop, iphone, and an ipad which at one point I was using all at the same time. 
The concierge and front desk staff were helpful and customer-service oriented.

title: “Failed to live up to expectations”
text:
Web site is very misleading - studio suite was not as suggested by site - in particular, kitchen fitted into cupboard (not a huge problem, but not as web site suggested) and there was no table to work at - big problem; not suitable for business trips. The only table was a side-table with stereo on it which was too high to work on and in any event was uneven so moved about when I attempted to work at it. Had to sit on bed with computer to work - not satisfactory.
Web site also advertised free internet access to each room (I see it has now changed to business centre) which was very important to me (and I had specifically requested it in email booking). No such luck. Offered huge clunky modem for insane sum per night - tried it but didn't work so gave up. Not much help from front desk on advising about obtaining internet access near the hotel - ended up finding some for myself at a USP down the block. "Business Centre" - if you can call it that - had one computer which could be accessed only with assistance during business hours (useless if in business meetings/conference all day and need to use it in evening) - theoretically had wireless available which some people seemed to access but I was unable to access it (not sure why - managed to get 'free city access' from NBC if I held my computer up against the window in my room at an odd angle, but that was too unreliable to use most of the time!). 
Room only had a couple of very old fashioned power outlets and not all of them worked - not helpful if have computer/phone and other devices to power up - I had to unplug stereo etc just to plug in computer.
Not fussed about the size, but some honest advertising would be nice. Decided to take bath to relax one night only to discover plug did not fit properly so water just poured out of it as fast as it went in. Pipes very noisy so needed to avoid using bathroom at night.
Incredibly noisy - I know it's to be expected on level 5 opposite main street but window fittings did nothing to help. Heating/cooling system also very noisy.
Never saw a "complimentary New York Times"
Might be ok to use as base for holiday (location is excellent and there is good cupboard space for luggage/clothes) but avoid if visiting NY for business purposes and hope to do some work in your room in the evenings.

title: “Would definitely stay again!”
text:
My husband, brother, 14 year old daughter, and myself stayed here from July 13 to July 17, 2009. We stayed in room 1029. We had a wonderful stay. The staff are extremely friendly and helpful. When we left on our outings each morning, the concierge made sure we knew where we were going. The location is perfect, central to everything. For example, when walking, we were about 25 minutes to Navy Pier and 15 minutes to the John Hancock Observatory. We had a 2 room suite. The kitchenette had everything needed for cooking (if desired). The beds were extremely comfortable. My brother said the pull out couch bed was comfortable as well. We could hear the fire engines occasionally, but it didn't bother us. There was plenty to eat each morning for breakfast, there were eggs and baocn or sausage, cereals, breads, bagels, and muffins, lots to choose from. The subway was close by as well, which made it easier to get to Wrigley Field.
We would deifinitely stay here again.
We can't say anything negative about the hotel!

title: “Excellent Location”
text:
Like many others on here ,I booked this hotel as it was recommended on this website by other users.
This hotel is located right behind the Kodak Theatre and in between the radisson hotel and a huge shopping mall. 
Staff where very nice on arrival, didnt have the need to speak to them after this.
The rooms are "No fuss" and clean. Furniture is warn and its a little rough around the edges so dont expect top quality but it is CLEAN. If you want decor stay somewhere else. 
Free internet worked fine within the room, breakfast was fine and perfectly adequate for our needs.
Car park is FREE and very welcome in this area as it didnt appear there was anywhere to park without paying. It is on the small side but we managed to get a space.
We booked two rooms that were ground floor and adjacent to each other. Unfortunalty the cellings are extremely thin and could hear the rooms upstairs and people walking around at 6am each morning. If your a light sleeper this will wake you up so try and get a room on the first floor if possible.
I would certainly recommend this hotel to my famly and freinds.

title: “Loved the Alex”
text:
We stayed here for 5 nights in August. My husband and I were traveling with our son who was 8 at the time, so we booked a 1 bedroom suite.
We arrived at the hotel and were very pleasantly greeted by the outstanding doormen who very quickly unloaded our luggage and made sure we didn't have to do anything but make our way to the front desk. Which we did, only to be greeted by incredibly, enthusiastically friendly staff at the front desk. (It was a breath of fresh air after spending 3 and a half weeks in Italy where 'great' 5 star service doesn't even come close to that of the USA). We were given an upgrade to a 2 bedroom 2 bath suite plus breakfast thrown in. A very nice surprise. They told us where local restaurants and shops were located and offered to make a dinner reservation for us at any restaurant we would like.
The staff were all very very friendly. All of the housekeeping staff to the elevator assistant, front desk, doormen and the Town-car drivers that the doormen organize. The front desk staff greeted us by name every time they saw us. They organized tickets for us at the last minute on a show that was sold out. The concierge was great and extremely helpful. As was Mel (Melanie??) at the front desk. Really lovely and always very friendly.
The room was fantastic. The beds were incredibly comfortable. The main bathroom, located in the main bedroom, was large and very roomy (yes, the shower was tricky and cut out a couple of times mid rinsing hair, annoying, but you get over that, just turn it back on). The 2nd bathroom was smaller, and looked like the photos on the website as well as other reviewers photos. We never once ran out of towels as others complained about. In fact, we had 2 showers a day and still never got thru all the towels provided. We could see the Chrysler building from every window in the room (both bedrooms and the kitchen and living area). The room was certainly roomy enough for the 3 of us. I would not say it was "sumptuous" luxury, but it was modern luxury and very comfortable. If you are looking for a grand, stately hotel, this is not the place for you. But if you want a modern and sleek hotel with it's own personality and flare, this is a great place. It is comfortable, you don't feel like you have to 'wear a tie' to breakfast, but, due to the price tag, the hotel maintains a higher standard of clientele.
Liked having the kitchen. We didn't cook of course, but we stocked up on fruit and snacks at the Amish Market down the street. It's a FANTASTIC gourmet deli. We actually shopped there a few times. We had a coffee maker/pot in our room from memory.
Other reviewers complained of walls being paper thin, but we did not once hear our neighbors. One day we stopped back into our room at about 2pm to drop off shopping bags and to make a snack and I did hear a phone ringing and ringing. It was a little annoying so I walked out into the hallway to see if I could determine what room it was coming from and found it was actually the hallway/corridor house phone ringing. So, I just answered it. Turned out, it was housekeeping, looking for another housekeeping staff member whom she thought was on that floor. She was very apologetic and by the sound of her voice, absolutely mortified that a guest answered the phone. It stopped ringing after that. 
Others also complained that hotel staff, housekeeping etc use the elevators, which is true, but we found that if a staff member was waiting for the elevator and we walked up, they ALWAYS insisted that WE take the elevator and they would wait for the next round. They would not ride with us, as they didn't want to make us uncomfortable. A couple times though, we insisted they ride with us.
We had breakfast at Ringo's daily. The first day for breakfast we had a waiter that was obviously having a bad day. He was very preoccupied and didn't give a rats about serving us. We were kind to him regardless, and the next day he was like a different person. Very very friendly, gave our son a hot chocolate (on the house, as it was not included in the free breakfast). I think he may have recognized that the day before he had been a little grumpy. He remembered what we ordered the day before and for the remainder of our stay we almost didn't have to give our orders, he remembered. One note though, we tried one morning to eat in the area outside. We could not do it, ended up moving back indoors. The sounds of New York are great, but not during breakfast. It was very noisy with the sound of traffic, horns, big trucks and also, NOT something you want to do when it is rubbish/trash collection day. The smell was a little overwhelming. 
The location is good, it is in a commercial area. The only better place to stay in terms of a 'nicer' location in our opinion is the upper east side which is more of an upmarket, quiet residential area. Alternatively, if you like a trendy, hip location, then Soho might be it.
Great place. Would definitely stay there again. In fact, look forward to it.

title: “Clean, comfortable, well-located, with charm and character”
text: First let me say that we like old hotels. If you are the Holiday Inn Express type, this is not for you. The Inn at Virginia Mason was built in the late 20's, and has been well restored and maintained. Carpet, furnishings and decor were good quality, in good condition and stylistically appropriate for the era. The bathroom was small but all the plumbing was modern and functional. The hot water room heating system was unusual: like a giant valence hung from the ceiling across the tops of the windows. It kept the room at a comfortable 72-76 deg F (no matter where the wall thermostat was set). The restaurant menu was small but the food and service excellent. The location is exceptionally convenient if you have business at Virgina Mason Clinic or Hospital. The Inn is connected to the clinic, so you can get to any department without going outside (or climbing any hills). It's about a 15-20 minute walk to downtown and Pike Place Market (double that back up the hill). Bus service on routes 10/12 will get you there quickly and cheaply. While you are at the Inn, cross the street to the Baroness Hotel and check out its beautiful Art Deco lobby.

title: “Sufficent”
text: This newly renovated Doubletree is sufficient. It is affordable by NYC standards and was quite clean. It is missing a little of what you'd normally expect: no free Wi-Fi, no coffee pot in the room, no mini fridge, no concierge, etc. However, when you did you ask the staff was friendly. If you don't plan on being in your room much and just want something clean, quiet and modern when you are then this is the place. I do not suggest staying here on a first-time trip. Spend the extra $ and go somewhere a little more attentive. The location is the best part of this hotel- right in the middle of midtown.

title: “A good surprise”
text: We'd streetviewed the locality before we decided to make this our overnight stay between Amtrak trains from San Francisco to New Orleans. In fairness, we weren't expecting too much other than the convenience of its location to Union Station. However, the room was clean, if a little worn, and the bathroom was excellent. The staff were helpful and the light breakfast was OK. It's possible to walk the short distance from the station to the hotel even with large roller suitcases but it's true to say that there are quite a few people down on their luck roaming around the streets. We had time to kill in the morning and the Mexican market, restaurants and entertainment in the square opposite the station (it was a Sunday) and 300 yards from the hotel were superb. All in all, a good choice for our short stop and value for money.

title: “Great hotel in a great location”
text: I stayed last Saturday night with my wife and we loved this hotel. Very clean and attractive property and the hotel staff really shined. My wife said she was "blown away" by their service and we would not hesitate to stay there again anytime we attend an event at Universal.

title: “A great place at a great price!”
text: Super central, super hyped decoration and a great smiling staff makes this hotel one of the best choice to stay in N.Y!

title: “Grossly overpriced”
text: As a professional pilot I travel all over the world. I booked this property because it was the only hotel close to the airport with an available room for a last minute trip. I found the hotel to be very average. I basically paid almost $400.0.00 per night for what would have been $100 or less anywhere else. Personally I would stay away from Boston and especially this hotel if you have the option. Very basic restaurant but expensive and typical Boston snooty employees

title: “Great location!”
text: Street noise is pretty constant, but to be expected given its location. Omar and his staff are second to none. They're very professional and friendly. They're great resources for travel tips and information. The only complaint was WiFi. Reception was spotty and I wasn't able to access email.

title: “Great Service and Great Location”
text: My husband and I come to SF a few times a year and this was our first stay at the Suites at Fisherman's Wharf. The location is great and the view from the rooftop is wondrous. The suites are not luxurious but they are very charming which I loved! From the moment we arrived to the moment we left I felt well cared-for by staff. The rooms are large and the common areas are spacious. Everything you need is provided. We took another couple with us and felt the 2 bedroom set up was spacious enough. In addition, cars are parked in a garage that is secure & safe.

title: “Location, Location, Location”
text: This hotel is all about location, you if you are in shape you can walk to the capital and the national mall and just about anywhere you want to go! It is also close to the bus stop and the metro which I recommend taking if you are traveling on a budge... very safe and cheap. The hotel is being remodeled and it is time. The rooms are outdated and not super clean but with the remodel it should be ready to go in the very near future. It was not the best or the worst place I have stayed, beds were comfortable, nice TV, and the front desk was extremely helpful.

title: “No tipping! Great!”
text:
This hotel was great!
Attended a conference at the new conference center in the Seaport area. I've never stayed at a "gratuity inclusive hotel" before, it was pretty cool!

title: “Great location, amazing beds, large rooms for NYC. Excellent!”
text:
I stayed at the Residence Inn with two friends using Marriott points. We stayed over New Year's Eve, something that other loyalty schemes don't let you do (they black out popular/busy dates). I really rate Marriot Rewards t for this.
The location of the Residence Inn is great. A few steps away from Bryant Park (there was an ice rink there when we stayed), and a few blocks from Times Square. It was easy to get a taxi to other places such as Central Park, and even Rockerfeller Centre when we were feeling lazy! We were ideally placed for New Year's Eve in Times Square.
The hotel seemed really busy (mainly down to it being New Year I guess) so there was often a wait to speak to staff. They were always very helpful though. We had requested a room on a high floor with extra towels and both of these requests were granted. I couldn't believe how big the room was for New York City. I've stayed in other places in NYC where you get room for a bed (or two) and somewhere to put your case, a TV and just room to walk round the sides. This room was fantastic. It had a huge bed (which could probably sleep three people), plus a sofa bed, a kitchenette area with fridge, microwave and crockery/cutlery, and a decent bathroom. Great space for three people.
The bed was amazing - like sleeping on a big marshmallow! I always like Marriott beds. Unfortunately my friend who slept on the sofa bed said that was not very comfortable. Unfortunately the walls seemed really thin as we heard some noises (very loudly) from our next door neighbour that we really would rather not have! Being a Residence Inn, where guests often stay for longer periods of time, beds were not changed daily but there was a maid service and our maid did a great job tidying.
The hotel has free wifi which we were pleased about (I always begrudge hotels who charge you obscene amounts to use their wifi). They also had a number of internet stations that we could use for free to check emails/make plans for New Year etc. The hotel offers a free buffet breakfast. I was pleasantly surprised by. A good selection of cereals, toast/bagels/muffins, plus cooked breakfast items, pancakes, waffles, and fruit juices, coffees and teas. We were very pleased with the breakfast, you could even take it up to your room using paper plates.
I would definitely recommend this hotel. I noticed when I booked it using my points that the rate for when we stayed was $450 per night, so I was glad I used points. But if you're looking for a roomy and comfortable hotel room in a fantastic location, this is highly recommended. Would definitely go back if I got a good rate!

title: “Excellent Experience”
text: Great loaction to stay when conducting business in Indianapolis. The room was clean, quiet, and the staff was freindly and courteous. I will definitely stay here again next time I am in Indianapolis.

title: “nice”
text: i went to this hotel a few months ago and it was in a great area next to a various shopping centers the hotel itself was beautiful i will recommand this to anymore plus very afforable prices.

title: “the worst hotel I have ever been to”
text:
some people who work there are very unpleasant
people behind the desk- not all of them 
every time when I stay there something is broken in a room
or some things dont work at all
this hotel is way too overpriced and theres nothing special about this hotel
they are nuts......
location is good but threre are so many hotels around better than red roof inn in Manhattan

title: “No hotels available”
text: I never write a bad review but our stay was ok and comfy but the breakfast was lacking in a HUGE way. I travel all over the world and stay at many different types of hotels and breakfast is always included from something small to a grand breakfast. I have to say when I wake up it is nice to grab a bite to eat but here everything is extra. They only offer coffee and toast. I ate bread for 3 days and the last day I said, I hate waking up hungry and going downstairs to bread, so we went to Denny's across the highway out of desperation and Im not a big fan of Denny's:(

title: “Good location - very clean”
text: Just in Phoenix for 1 night and this Inn lived upto its name of Best Value. Very convenient location for downtown. Room was very clean with 2 comfy beds, fridge, microwave, TV with many channels and adequate bathroom. The manager and his wife were extremely helpful and let us keep the room into the late afternoon for a nominal sum to accomadate our flight departure time

title: “Great- Lovin it in Greektown!”
text:
My husband and I had a wonderful time, and highly recommend the hotel, location in Greektown.
We went to Detroit for the Red Wings 1st 2006 game and other then the Wings losing to Vancouver we had an awesome time!
Hotel was excellent, from check in to departure. Hotel rooms are large, charming and very clean! Interesting lobby bar and great gift shop! Rooms service great! Free business center to check e-mail and free to print too!
Restaurants Fishbones, Pegasus and Mosaic were each outstanding for very different reasons, we ate at all three. 
The Sunday Brunch at Fishbones, by the most beautiful indoor waterfall was spectacular, too much food to try everything so we will be back and already booked our next room for January 2007. 
My husband and I had a wonderful time, and highly recommend the hotel, location and Greektown Casino.

title: “Excellent Hotel in San Antonio”
text: This hotel was nicely located between the airport and Lackland AFB. The hotel was very nice inside and out. The room was very clean. The hotel has two nice steakhouses within walking distance and a movie theatre right next door as well as many places to shop around the area. The staff was very friendly and helpful.

title: “Good value at the Beacon”
text:
My husband and I just spent 10 nights at the Beacon, in the Upper West side of NYC. We loved the location and enjoyed our stay, despite a few hiccups here and there. Like other people, we had occasional trouble with the elevators; and the toilet blocked twice in the first 3 days, the first time at midnight on the night of our late arrival, after a 30 hour trip, so that wasn't fun. Each time we reported it, however, the staff responded with exemplary speed and efficiency. Finally I just closed the tap slightly so the bowl did not fill up quickly and the problem disappeared.
We chose the Beacon because of its general location and because we could self-cater when we wanted. (Be warned, however, that the extractor fan is connected to the stove top, so if you are making toast it does not come on, and the smoke alarm is pretty sensitive! We were caught twice, and that was once too often!) It was great to be able to shop at the wonderful Fairway market directly across the road, especially at 10.00pm on the Sunday night of our arrival. It was even better to eat in the upstairs Steakhouse Cafe, whose $29 three course meal was wonderful, good food and great value. 
We found the beds pretty comfortable and the decor subdued but restful. The size of the room was a great plus, as was the comfortable furniture in it. 
All in all, the Beacon delivered everything I expected from tripadvisor comments, and we would certainly recommend it, as well as stay there again ourselves.

title: “Don't miss the wine and cheese!”
text: I booked this hotel with airmiles after reading the fabulous reviews. We had a studio with 2 queen beds and a kitchen for myself, my partner, my 5 year-old daughter and my teenage son. It is difficult to please all ages, but we all absolutely loved it. It is difficult to say anything which has not been said before - you will have read about the friendly doormen, the large rooms, the comfortable bed, the great location and the relaxed ambience. However, what sets this hotel apart from any other I have ever stayed in was the wine a cheese evening in the club room from 6-7, Monday to Thursday. Lots of wine, lots of cheese and biscuits, and even bingo on a Thursday evening with excellent prizes. A lovely opportunity to meet fellow travellers and share stories of this great city, before walking a block or two for world class cuisine in any number of nearby restaurants. We had a wonderful stay in NYC, and if I'm ever lucky enough to return, I will check out the Affinia Fifty - hopefully it will not be priced out of my range once the world catches on to the great value currently on offer. I cannot rate this hotel highly enough.

title: “Everthing was good”
text: Good price and location. There was one problem. I ordered two rooms with 2 Double beds. But when I was check-in there was no that rooms. While I was parking my car they find it and everything was fine

title: “4th year in a row”
text: Love the location. Either waterview or marina view is great. Picked up from airport within 5 mins. Front desk is really friendly (ask for Chris). Stayed in new part of hotel with great room on bottom floor with our own patio. Happy hour in the lounge is 1/2 food and drink. Breakfast on the the deck is wonderful in the morning breeze. Kids have a beach just across the street. Hope to see you again next year.

title: “Best Experience Ever!”
text: This was our first trip to New York and we stayed in two different hotels. We switched to the Westin half way through and they made sure it was an amazing and memorable experience for us! We are Starwood prefered guests so our room was upgraded to the spa room with a massage chair and beautiful views. The hotel is close to everything and just a two minute walk to Times Square. Restaurants are located in the hotel and across the street (there is even a movie theater you can access through the hotel). The hotel is beautiful and so are the rooms, we loved the Westin!

title: “Havens above!”
text: It really is a tranquil haven only yards from the manic Times Square. We have stayed in some impressive four star hotels in other US cities but are really glad we acted on the reviews to book into The Casablanca for our first trip to New York. The well decorated rooms are not huge and the views nothing special but , that said, for staff, location, cleanliness, Rick's Lounge and overall ambience this hotel is tops.

title: “Friendly staff, quiet and comfortable”
text: I purchased an advanced, non-refundable rate for $95 a night. Like most upscale hotels there is a charge for everything--wifi, parking, expensive buffet breakfast. This seems to be a disappointing trend. The room was clean and comfortable. The staff was extremely friendly, which really helped because I was in town to visit a sick friend.

title: “An sanctuary in the middle of time square”
text: I recommend this hotel to every one. The hotel has a nice lobby 8th floor, the rooms are great, and the location is superb. We went on business, and it was also easy to visit broadway shows and other things. The action is just steps away, yet you have a quiet place for yourself.

title: “fantastic hotel in every way”
text:
Just come back from 5 nights at this wonderful hotel. 
Beautiful large comfortable rooms in art deco style with heavenly comfortable bed. plus fabulous bathroom. The staff were very helpful and the position excellent. Amazingly quiet for such a prime location. We got a good deal on the room with expedia uk. Highly recommend it and will certainly stay again. Breakfast pricey but plenty of alternatives minutes away.

title: “Check your bill carefully!”
text:
The front desk tried to overcharge us more than $150 dollars at checkout not giving us the room rate that was clearly stated on our reservation. When I noticed the difference and asked to change the rate the front desk staff only VERY reluctantly changed it.
