Also there is a big sign in reception saying that the charge of the safe in the rooms can be taken off at check out if you ask for it, but this is not true. This sign is highly misleading as we asked but were told that it could not be taken off even after we pointed out the sign and the attitude of the front desk was actually quite rude.
The first night we were given a room that smelled really badly as the vent from the Italian restaurant below went right into the room and nothing in the room worked. It took staff about three hours to find out that they could not do anything about the tv. If you stay in winter you will need extra blankets as the duvets are awful! Running a hotel they should know that you cannot wash duvets in a machine. They were lumpy and worse than i would even expect at a backpacker hostel. The worst I have ever had at any hotel I have ever stayed at!!! As they are really just two sheets with some lumps in we asked for blankets, which we had to ask for three times and took hours to get there - after the receptionist making it very clear that we were being a nusciense. 
No point in trying to contact the hotel/reservation team in advance either. We wanted to change our reservation to include one more night. When you e-mail them it says that they will get back to you within 24hours, but after two months I am still waiting. We then called and were told it was fine and that we could have one more night for the same price, but the hotel had not been made aware of this change and we had to pay a higher price for one night because the reservation team cannot communicate with the hotels.
I would NEVER stay at this hotel again or recommend it to anyone. The service was absolutely awful and although it is fairly cheap I don’t think it was good value.

title: “A truly wonderful experience and staff”
text: We came to Chicago out of necessity, because our son had to be hospitalized at UIC Medical Center. Discovering the Chicago South Loop Hotel has made a difficult experience not only more bearable but actually enjoyable. Regina,Jackie, Evelyn and all the front desk staff have gone above and beyond average hotel standards to make our stay as comfortable and stress-free as possible. They treated us as friends, even though we'd never met before coming here. It is worth it to stay here just for the care all the staff---from bellhops to housekeepers to front desk---give to their guests. The location is almost perfect, giving us quick access to anything and everything we need or want to get to, and the comlimentary parking for hotel guests is a huge benefit. Whether we were discussing Southern cooking with the staff of Pearl's coffee shop or picking up mail from the front desk, we enjoyed every minute of our stay at the Chicago South Loop Hotel.

title: “Cookie Heaven”
text:
This 26 room, former English bric-a-brac boarding house is desolately located a few blocks from Union Square (7 blocks from BART). The rooms have great beds with comfortable mattresses and fireplaces. The rooms are decorated with books and have a mini-refrig with complimentary water and soft drinks.
The staff (Andy & Kevin) are friendly and helpful.
There is hot apple cider and cookies (available all day!) in the reception.
There is 5-6:30 complimentary wine (Fetzer) chardonnay and cab with wonderful snacks (reat artichoke dip, crudités, bundt cake).
Buffet breakfast is in charming area with a fire place. There are nice pastries, croissants, scones, French brioche toast, sausage patties, quiche, fresh fruit, yogurt, and oatmeal.

title: “Historic Hotel with Luxury”
text: I stayed at the Brown Palace for one night and was not pleased with a few things about the room. Before putting up a negative comment, I decided to speak to the manager I'm glad I did. He was very professional in listening to my complaints and compensated me for the inconvenience. The staff were very courteous and helpful. The lobby area is beautiful and elegant. I would have liked a bathtub to soak in the artesian well water, but the rain shower was a nice alternative.

title: “Love this place”
text:
We did park and fly package and it's worth it. Very convenient.
Staff well trained and happy with my reservations, everything went perfect. Frontdesk manager was very helpful and cheerful.
We will come back and stay here again!!!!!!

title: “Disappointing”
text:
The Hampton Inn Time Square South is located relatively good and you will find many of the places in a walking distance. We were staying in a double bed room on a high floor (26th) with a great view to a brick wall (i wouldn't imagine they have anything better). The room was very small and it was very hard to handle the stroller for our baby, introducing the crib into the room made moving in the room impossible. The room was clean as expected from hampton network, nothing extra ordinary, the showers were also very small but clean. The service in the hotel is the real disappointment, you couldn't put a smile on the front desk people even if you told them they won the lottery, grim faced and always giving you the feeling that they are doing you a favor for every service they give you.
The hotel supposedly has a free wireless connection to all guests but in our room the connectivity was impossible, only when we went out to the elevators it came back. 
The rooms are also very expensive and i thought i would get better return for the money i spent (354$/night)
I would not recommend staying in this hotel unless you get a deal you cannot refuse. There is a hotel boom in NYC for a while now, and you will find a better hotel with little effort.

title: “Perfect for us!”
text: We just got back from a quick trip to DC. We stayed at Capitol Hill Suites and we really, really liked the place. Great location! Convenient for metro and the Mall/Smithsonian. Neat neighborhood. We did happy hour and dinner at the Hawk & Dove which was just around the corner. Fun. Absolutely every staff member we met was very friendly and personable. We stayed during the week and it was a little pricey but it was likely the same everywhere else. We will be back!

title: “Swanky”
text: We stayed at the Palace the wekend of the 7th of March. What a spectacular hotel. They were so accomodating and even upgraded our room when I mentioned that my daughter opted for a NYC trip with her mom rather than travel with friends on her senior class trip to Orlando. They were so gracious and extremely helpful. The concierge went out of their way to provide dining suggestions, address information and things to do!! We will definitely be back ~ it is well worth the $$$.

title: “Very good service!”
text: Love the place! Spent the past week at this hotel for a conference, The service was great, food delicious, and rooms were beautiful. Everything was as expected. Beautiful views of the city and accommodating staff.

title: “Outstanding in every way!!!”
text:
I stayed at the hotel the the night before my wedding and my bride and I the next two nights. The staff was wonderful to us and far exceeded our expectations. The Villa Suite in which we stayed was unreal...the thing must have been 700-800 square feet. Absolutely beautiful! I had a view of the first hole of the golf course and it was stunning.
We also held our rehersal dinner in one of their resturants and the staff there bent over backward to insure our experience was nothing short of outstanding.
I highly recommend this hotel and the ammenities that come with it!
Great job everyone associated with the Arizona Grand!

title: “very cool new hotel in mid-town”
text: We tried a city-view room which has huge windows facing the skyline. This is a very new hotel with lots of modern features (like being new and clean.) fine restaurant and very good staff. It is a little far west at 48th and 11th (very near the USS Intrepid) but that keeps the price down a bit.

title: “Big Price, basic Hampton”
text: We stayed at the Hampton in November. It was faily convenient to the Riverwalk/Alamo area, however, the walk back at night could be scary. It's the basic Hampton; the carpet was stained. For the price, I wish we had stayed someone more upscale.

title: “Good Enough for me.”
text:
Stayed here a couple of years ago with no problem so after a bad experience at a no A/C HIE we quickly booked a room here for the one night left of our stay. Used my points for a discount bringing it down to $95.00 for a King Whirlpool Suite. Didn't really want the Whirlpool but it's all they had. Room was clean, bathroom was nice, bed was comfortable. A/C was blessedly quiet & working. Didn't go to breakfast but my husband said it was fine.
Only weirdness was of all the things the coffee maker in the room. Full size coffee maker (for coffee packet that makes a small pot) on a nice counter with no electrical outlet. Had to move the coffee maker into the bathroom.
Eh, if that's my only complaint, all and all a Good Stay!

title: “very nice”
text: We stayed three nights last summer. The rooms and surrounding areas were very clean. Customer service was great and it was nice having the hot food for breakfast. The only thing I didn’t care for was the pool area. The outside pool area was extremely small.

title: “LOCK ALL YOUR STUFF...EVEN CLOTHES”
text:
My family and I stayed at this hotel for a week. Given the price, the place and the breakfast is OK. However on the last day, found that a t-shirt of mine was missing. I agree that valuables should be locked, but cant one keep ordinary clothes outside ...??? I wish this hadnt happened because it was not a very good end to our trip.
This experience would not make me trust the place again.

title: “Should have listened to the reviews!”
text:
I would not recommend this hotel for anyone who is looking for a clean, comfortable place to stay. When we got there, the girl from the front desk was outside smoking and talking on her cell phone. We had some trouble checking in ( that was not the hotels fault though) and had to wait almost a half hour to be able to check in. We left to go get something to eat while we waited and when we got back, the girl was outside smoking and talking on her cell again. 
When we got up to the room, the air condition was not on and it was super hot in the room. The beds were rock hard. My friend tried to bounce on them and they barely even moved. There was what looked like a small blood stain on the bed sheet. After about four hours, the room was still really hot. The air condition was obviously not working right. I would like to point out though that when I woke up the next morning the room was freezing. So at one point during the night it seemed the air conditioning actually kicked in and started working. The room was overall clean though. There were a couple places that it seemed the workers were just too lazy to clean. For example, it looked like there was either a chocolate stain or brown nail polish on the heater. 
I had to run out to the car at one point and again the girl from the front desk was outside smoking and talking on her cell phone, while inside there was someone sitting in the lobby waiting for help. I just wouldn't recommend staying in this hotel, especially for more than one day. I have stayed in cheaper hotels that were more comfortable than this.

title: “Thoroughly enjoyed hotel!”
text:
For our anniversary week-end, I chose the Hyatt Regency San Antonio after researching many Riverwalk hotels in San Antonio. My reasons included location, rate and recent renovation. We were impressed with the overall updated look--nice carpet, furniture, decor-- and wonderful breakfast. As senior citizens, we like nice accommodations at a reasonable price. The Hyatt Regency met that criteria. It is easy to exit onto the Riverwalk and be right in the hub of activity, but our room was quiet. Jazz music was played in The Landing at the hotel in the evening so it was nice to come back to listen after dinner.
We did not use the hotel internet connection which was an objection from some reviewers, and the parking garage across the street is expensive, but in checking, it was in line with parking fees at the other Riverwalk hotels. We enjoyed our stay!

title: “Can find better for the price”
text: If you book a suite, don't think it looks like the picture on the website. Also, the sofabed is horrible. Can't say enough about how bad the mattress was. We checked in around 11:00 pm and there was no bedding for the sofabed. It took over an hour to get it. If you want to use your computer, plan to spend $15.00 per day. The location is great. The lobby is beautiful. The rooms are larger than average for NYC.

title: “Comfortable overnight stay”
text:
My wife and I were returning home from Seattle through Charlotte and needed a place close to the airport to stay for a night. We happend upon the Hyatt Place through Trip Advisor and booked a king room for the night. Once we landed it was very easy to take their complimentary shuttle to the hotel and check in was a breeze. The room itself was very spacious and comfortable with a separate sitting area with your own sink and fridge if you needed to store food or drinks. The bathroom was nice (no tub) and the TV was a good size with modern ability to hook up your ipad or dvd player through a separate console. 
The staff were more than helpful and we enjoyed a glass of wine in their small bar area in the lobby as well as a late night snack. Although we did not have the complimentary breakfast the next day it looked fantastic on our way back to the airport.
Both of us said we would definately stay again at the Hyatt Place and next time for longer.

title: “Pricey but wonderful”
text:
Well I don't know how you get a "deal" on this place but I couldn't manage it for the life of me... and I worked hard... lol
We are a family of four - we are in the mid to late 30's and our children are 2 and 4.
We have stayed in San Diego twice before, once at the Welk Estates in Escondito (love it, but only if you're staying for a week or so) and at the Bahia Resort Hotel at Mission Beach - before the reno's.
I really wanted to stay here but the price US$450 scared the bejeezers out of me. This trip I was on business and could write off our hotel stay so I jumped at the opportunity.
I read lots of reviews that complimented the hotel and since it's #1 in San Diego how could we go wrong. Just after I booked I read the latest review about the area being a dump and I got scared... however there was no going back...
We arrived on July 6th at about 4pm... check in was quick and fast thanks to Humberto (Tito), they have parking underneath the hotel for $18 a night which was great because then it's a quick elevator ride to your hotel room. We stayed in a oceanview room on the second floor middle of the hotel. The room was huge, beautifully appointed and comfortable. The balcony was great with an amazing view. The beds are about four and a half feet high with a little step stool to climb up... There is a bar fridge and a mini bar. Never tried the internet but apparently there is wireless...
We got changed quickly and ran for the pool (we had just driven up from Ensenada). There was free wine hour from 4 to 5 and lemonade for the kids. The wine was excellent, white, red and blush and the service was great. We had a quick glass on the patio and then changed over to plastic glasses and went for a dip. The pool isn't huge but is adequate for the most part, only occasionally crowded. The hot tub was great and the view of the surfers was fun to watch.
The area around the hotel is funky and fun. We walked all over... ate at World Famous the first night and Gringo's the second night. I lost my nose ring and bought one around the corner at the tatoo parlour. We felt completely safe and happy in the area and after eating dinner at World Famous walked back along the beach skipping the surf with the kids at 11pm a night. There were a few homeless people sipping beers, etc. but no one was violent or scary. The beach is beautiful and clean and we met lots of the vendors along the way in their little shops who were so nice and helpful.
We ate breakfast at The Broken Yolk on Garnet both mornings... mmm best omelets ever!! Dinner at World Famous was ok, the appy's were great but the main courses were hit and miss, the prime rib was good, the steak not all that interesting. Dinner at Gringo's was ok too.. the appy's were fabulous, however the traditional Mexican food we ordered was not our favorite and we wish we had ordered fajita's instead.
At about 11pm on Saturday night there was a little yahoo going on in the pool, it lasted about 15 minutes before hotel staff cleared them out without incident, however it was very loud for a few minutes.
We had a problem with dripping water over our vanity. I called the front desk and they sent the repair man, who looked at it and told me he would resolve it while we were out. When we came back it seemed to have be fixed, however overnight the drip came back and our whole vanity was flooded including all our bathroom stuff, it was a big mess. I complained when we checked out and they comp'd our parking so $36 credit, which was nice.
So here's our list of pros:
- amazing location, fun, hip and interesting
- beautiful hotel
- fabulous service
- great pool area, fun to hang out at
- wonderful sandy beach
- entertaining watching the surfers
- fun boardwalk to walk along
- comfy beds/linens
- tv was huge and lots of options
- small bar fridge (good for leftovers and cold drinks, etc.)
- lots of good restaurants/shopping near by (walking distance)
List of cons:
- very expensive
- have to pay for parking
- noisy - we didn't mind at all (in fact we like it) but if you're looking for peace and quiet you probably won't find it here between the surf crashing and the people around the pool
We never even went into San Diego proper this trip, we loved the Pacific Beach area so much... we visited Sea World on Saturday and that was excellent, however it's a two day excursion with little people and we didn't get to see everything in one day...
We would stay at this hotel again in a second as long as their prices don't get much higher!!

title: “Simply The Best”
text:
I have stayed in several 4 and 5 star hotels. From the moment I drove up to the hotel, until the moment I checked out, I was impressed. The staff were extremely friendly, professional and helpful. My room, a Deluxe King, was amazing. The artwork, the bathroom (as many others have raved about), the view, the maid service, room service, valet, conseire, the Boka bar and restaraunt, etc. Everything was perfect. And they have bath robes which is a nice touch that not all 4 and 5 star hotels include.
Before my stay at Hotel 1000, I read all of the reviews here. Yes they charge for the bar and snacks but there are warning signs that inform you that it is all electronically monitored. The price for the room and services is well priced in my opinion. Yes it is a little on the expensive side but, the personalized services, the staff, and the beautiful rooms make the price justified. I won't spoil your first experience at Hotel 1000 with any more details.
From my experiences with other accomodations, Hotel 1000 is simply the best.

title: “Airport”
text: Had a late flight Sunday. Bassett mall walking distance. Breakfast was great.Except eggs were powdered. Tasted like it. Other than than that. Would stay again. Shuttle sw service to airport.Quick! Clean rooms. Bathroom clean.

title: “Great place”
text: Pleasant, somewhat old fashioned hotel in a terrific location. The room was small but comfortable, with a small yet serviceable bathroom. Clean and light (our room faced the front street.) Continental breakfast was pretty good. The desk staff and concierge were friendly and helpful. No refrigerator in the room, and the television is small and mounted high on the wall. Minor issues all in all. Great place to stay if your focus is lower Manhattan.

title: “Doing time - and loving it”
text: The Liberty Hotel has two parts; the remodeled old jail and a modern tower which contains most of the guest rooms. We stayed in the tower and the room was excellent. Modern, clean, comfortable and quiet. The hotel maintains the integrity of the former jail and adds a modern design making for a unique hotel experience. The bar Alibi is a great place to relax and enjoy some drinks and while we did not eat dinner in the restaurant, Clink, breakfast was superb. The best part of our stay was the service. The staff goes out of their way to make sure this 5 star hotel delivers a 5 star stay. I know I will be back on my next trip to Boston and I highly recommend the Liberty Hotel.

title: “neither good nor bad”
text:
$1000 for 3 nights/4 days(Dec 7-10) are neither high nor low. The room is somewhat outdated and small. That may be unavoidable considering manhattan's skyrocketing expenditure. 
The location is rather good. First of all, it cost $24.10 from La Guardia airport by taxi and $26.10 to the airport by taxi. The fare is lower than the limousine bus which charges $15 per person and takes much longer time.
Chinatown and Little Italy is just one or two block away, and subway station(Canal St) is just one block away toward southway. You can go uptown and downtown by bus on Centre and Broadway St, respecitively. Those two roads are just one block away right-side and left-side. 
You can go to a disco club(Santos Party House) by walking southway to the Walker St and just going straight across that street. Don't forget the address of the building. 
If you don't insist on staying at a luxury hotel nor at a hotel near the Rockefellow Building, then stay here with comparatively lower price. 
But be careful not to be deceived by the Chinese bell man who showed aggressive attitude to me when he urged to take the hotel's sedan taxi for $35. To JFK airport it is $45 by yellow cab, but to La Guardia, it is just $26+$2 for driver tip. You can save $7 by taking yellow cab.

title: “Great Stay at the Inn at Venice Beach”
text:
We stayed in the Inn at Venice Beach for 5 nights in the beginning of November and were delighted with it. The staff were great - so friendly and really helpful. There was always someone available on the desk to answer any questions. The complimentary cookies and juices at reception were a nice touch. Complimentary breakfast of bagels / toasts / cereals / juices / fruit etc was more than adequate for our needs. The room we had overlooked the courtyard so it was nice and quiet, spacious and clean. We had a rental which we parked at the inn and we never worried about security during our stay.
The location was just great and it was easy to get around - not too far from the airport, but right next to Santa Monica - the best of both worlds! 
I would definitely stay here again, and would recommend it to anyone, particularly because of the staff who were so helpful.

title: “Relaxing Awesome Weekend Getaway”
text: I honeslty felt the tension, stress and worries in my life gone the entire time I was here. I would lay in bed at night and keep getting up just to look outside.

title: “What a bathroom!”
text: With its sleek, modern decor and super congenial staff, it's hard to go wrong staying at the Sofitel when visiting Chicago. The location is perfect for shopping and restaurants. The room was definitely designed with the guest in mind. The enormous marble tiled bathroom had a separate shower and tub. There is plenty of room in the closet to store all your stuff for a long stay. The only downside to this hotel is that it does not have free wi-fi.

title: “Cheap Hotel in A Nice Area”
text: The room was good sized, a little old but not smelly or anything. Considering how much your paying its all that you could expect. I felt safe in the area and they had some cool bars around (just follow the music). There is an affordable diner located next to the hotel, The food was delicious and the portions were large. Only problem was they only stay open till 5 so its a good breakfast or lunch spot. This hotel is a great value considering the location, Its good for those on a budget, especially for younger people looking to pack a room and save cash. I would stay here again in a heartbeat. O and almost forgot parking and WIFI are both free here.

title: “Best suite in NYC”
text: My husband & I stayed this past weekend for 3 days in the Hudson River View Suite.Its probably bigger than most NYC apartments.Great view of the Intrepid,and the last day 2 cruise ships came in,so it was nice to watch.Although we didnt count on the coldest day(we live in Florida),we took a walk to 9th ave(restaurant row)and found some really good places to eat.We also had lunch at Print,the hotel restaurant.While it was really good,its expensive,but it is New York.We took taxis to the MeatPacking District to eat dinner,and walk around.The hotel has a free wine hour,but we didnt go since neither of us drinks.I would have rather had a free breakfast,but thats not an option.Free wifi in the room(for Kimpton members)and we also had the "raid the mini bar credit",also for Kimpton members.Next time I will stay longer to enjoy New York more,but will come when its warmer.And bring my dog,since he loves Kimptons too!If you sign up for emails,you may get a really good rate on a suite,and its worth the money for the view and the space.My husband watched his baseball in the living room,and another tv in the bedroom for me.The bathroom is huge,and I loved the shower with all the jets on the side,and rain showerhead.Umbrellas and cool looking bathrobes in the closet.I need a fan to sleep,and it was there for me.I also asked for a humidifier,the 2nd night I got that too.Pretty much anything you request,they will get for you.Stay here,you will not be disappointed

title: “If you like average and up and down experience, this is the place for you”
text:
I go to San Diego every 2-3 months and I usually stay closer to my plant off Mira Mesa, but I decided to stay downtown and use the Sheraton Suites. Check in went smooth, although they upgraded the woman who checked in ahead of me to the SPG Member floor (she wasn't a member and had no idea what this was) and then gave me a room on the 16th floor (not a preferred floor even though I am a member). The room was nice and clean.
Breakfast was very good, but waited 15 minutes for a glass of apple juice when there were only 2 people in the restaurant. Dinner first night was good and no problem at all with service from the bar. Sasha was excellent. Got to my room and my key didn't work so I had to go back down to the front desk for a new one. No big deal happens occassionally.
Breakfast the next day was good again and this time I only had to wait about 12 minutes for apple juice. My next dinner at the bar was as good as the first and the service was great again. Went to room and again key didn't work. An apology would have been nice but oh well.
Breakfast the 3rd day was good again except this time apple juice never came. Decided to have milk from buffet and not go back even though I had two more free buffet vouchers that came with the room.
After a long day went up to room and surprise surprise the key didn't work. Went down to front desk and the man at the front desk asked me what I was doing with the key. Apparently keeping it in your shirt pocket or pants pocket causes the key to magically lose its program.
Parked on street, got two tickets over 5 nights which was still cheaper than parking at the hotel. Again, room was very nice, the bar staff was excellent, but overall average. Not what I expect from a Sheraton, but not enough to make me not use Sheraton anymore. I will probably just stick with the hotels I have used in the past even though the locations and rooms usually aren't as nice.

title: “5 Stars”
text:
I just arrived home from 5 days at the fairmont olympic hotel in seattle and i would have been content to move in their permanently! i was fortunate to be booked in on a convention rate ($250 per night--and they didn't have the basic room for 5 nights so for $25 more i had a suite!).....that is $25 well spent!! i had a huge king sized bed and a separate living room with sofa, 2 overstuffed pillows to rest my head after a day of shopping, a desk, chair and 2 tvs.....there is a separate dressing area and the bathroom was nice with 2 robes to use.....
the hotel is first class all the way....the staff cannot do enough for you!! i had requested a coffee maker, which for some reason the fairmont does not provide.....when i checked in, there was no coffee maker in the room, so i phoned the front desk.....the head of catering told me that he would get one for me, even if he had to buy it himself.....sure enough, within 1/2 hour they brought me a coffee maker on a silver platter with all the acoutrements!! i was very impressed.....the doormen greet you when you leave the premises and when you return--a nice touch!! coffee and tea is served in the lobby in the early morning.....the carpet is starting to look a bit dated in the halls, but that would be my only complaint--and a small price to pay for a marvellous hotel.......i can't wait to stay on the "gold floor" on the fairmont in boston--where i am going in 1 week!!
by the way, seattle is a great city for shopping! it is small--all of the shops are within a 2 block radius--macy's, nordstroms, brooks brothers, coach, yves st laurent, etc. etc.! heaven for this visitor from canada!

title: “Great location next to convention center, but Executive Lounge is lacking.”
text:
This was a weekend trip to see some music, so I wasn't expecting much in terms of the hotel. When I checked in, I was not given the executive room that I originally booked. Thankfully, I remembered that I should have access to the lounge and they quickly corrected the mistake. No worries. The room was big and comfortable and I had a slight view of the Toyota Center.
Wanting a pre-show snack, I went to the Executive Lounge and was amazed at the space - it was huge! However, it was empty. No body was up there and there was a plate of 4 cookies, some snack mix and a box full of sodas and water. There was a bartender, but there was a charge for alcoholic drinks?!
It seems I missed the evening reception from 5p-7p where they serve complimentary hors d'oeuvres, snacks & sodas. Perhaps I've been spoiled by other executive lounges, but my assumption was free beer and decent nibbles into the evening. My mistake. At least I thought the breakfast would be worthwhile. Nope. Continental Breakfast in every sense of the word. Hard boiled eggs, grits/oatmeal, cereal, juices, soda, and fruit. 
Suffice it to say that I was not impressed by the executive lounge. Otherwise, this is a decent hotel with the level of service you would expect from the Hilton brand.

title: “Room Infested by Bed Bugs”
text:
I spend 6 nights at the Hilton Woodland Hills in June 2007 (room 307). The room, hotel, amenities, etc seemed ok. Slightly dingy, but otherwise not bad. 
After the first night, I noticed a rash on my body that seemed like an alergic reaction to something. It got worse each day. I thought I was either allergic to the soap, shampoo or the laundry detergent used on the sheets or towels, but this had never happened to me before. I bought new soap and shampoo (brands I normally use). The rash was worse in the mornings, and appeared to be be in rows of several inches on various parts of my body (legs, abdomen, back, chest, etc).
I started to research what it could be, and all signs seemed to indicated bed bugs. I finally stripped off my sheets and mattress and found a single bed bug (a flat brown bug about the size of a tick) crawling around between the mattress and box spring.
I didn't bother looking for more. I immediately called the front desk. They sent a security manager with a camera. He was sympathetic, but neither confirmed nor denied anything. He photographed my rashes, took the bug, and offered me a new room on the executive floor.
My main concern was to not track these home with me. They offered to dry clean all of my clothes, which I took them up on. I also asked them to spray down my suitcase with pesticide. As it was getting late on a Fri evening, the best they could do was to produce a can of pesticide, and I sprayed all my bags down myself.
Overall, I think the hotel responded reasonably well. They should have offered to pick up the hotel tab, but didn't, and didn't provide any other compensation. I would have protested more, but I was being reimbursed by my company for the trip.
The second room was clean of bed bugs, but I kept waking up at night and checking under the covers.
While the hotel seems relatively clean, it was a very disapointing stay. I will not return. The Marriott is close by, and I've no had problems like this over there. I travel to Woodland Hills frequently for work.

title: “No surprises”
text: Close to the airport but serene; well manicured grounds, friendly staff providing excellent service , common area well stocked with "goodies", there were no surprises as everything was as expected.

title: “Great location - good hotel”
text:
The best thing about this hotel is the location. It is within easy walking distance of Times Square and the theaters. There is also a subway station just around the corner on 6th avenue. We stayed in a suite with one king and one queen bed. There was plenty of room for 4 "full size" adults. 
The only problem was that the bathroom door was much too transparent. It was slightly frosted, but not nearly enough. We also wished for a small refrigerator. Both of these were small aggravations. There was an in-room safe which we used. The breakfast was pretty standard - just continental style with no meat. If you want a cheap hot breakfast, there's a McDonalds just past the subway on 6th Avenue.
The rate was very good for this size room in NYC. All in all, I would highly recommend this hotel. If I ever come back to New York, I will definitely stay there.

title: “very nice”
text: Different from the run of the mill. Very unexpected and nice. Comfortable and with all the amenities required for a business trip.

title: “Very Pleased”
text:
We greatly enjoyed our stay. The room was very clean, straightened up daily, and re-supplied.
There were a lot of excellent choices for breakfast from hot to cold with staff continually overseeing the service. We even had real dishes and silverware! The hotel staff went out of their way to give great service: When we checked in, they were waxing the floors. One of the men automatically went to get ice for us since the hallway had temporarily been blocked off.The hotesses spent extra time locating and printing directions to a specific store on our homeward route. Although we were close enough to walk, we took advantage of the city bus which took us to and from the Riverwalk area, using an inexpensive pass issued by the hotel. The only drawbacks were the smallish parking area and the lack of a pool/hot tub. There was a room service menu, however, we did not use it. We will certainly stay here again on our next trip to San Antonio and would recommend this hotel.

title: “Good stay and annoying check-out”
text:
I stayed in the hotel for seven days and at my check-in I stressed to the front desk clerk that despite showing my credit card during the reservation I would be paying in cash at the check-out.
On the day of my check-out when leaving the hotel at 5:30 AM, I found out the person responsible for the front desk had already charged my credit card. And despite having the money to pay in cash the clerk didn't know or didn't want to revert the credit card transaction and receive the money.
The result of this action was I have to pay now more than USD 150 in taxes for use of my credit card and had to return to my country with a large amount of US dollars and when I exchange it back to my currency I will be losing even more money.
I found this completely unacceptable, first I told at the front desk the credit card was just for reservations purposes and would be paying in cash and my credit card was charged before I made the check-out. The manager would only arrive later, since I had a flight back to my country I couldn't wait.
Despite this very annoying event my stay at the hotel was very good and I would recommend it, it has sufficient space and a very good kitchen with a full sized refrigerator.
The only thing I would suggest to change was the weekly cleaning, it could be at least at every three or four days, one week is too much time.
The A/C seems to be very noisy also, it could be a problem in winter or summer, since I was there in fall wasn't a problem for me.

title: “Beautiful Property”
text: This was a short stay on the way to Vancouver, but the property was beautiful, well maintained, clean, and comfortable.

title: “Not what I'd expected.”
text:
It was an interesting contrast spending the night in London near Kings Cross at a business meeting and walking around at 10.30pm, we felt slightly uneasy, there was a simmering atmosphere in London that night and I was happy to get back to the hotel. The next day I took an early flight on my own to New York. I flew Virgin Upper in the top part of a new 747 and that was worth the extra money - fantastic service as always from Virgin. 
As I said the contrast on arrival in New York was amazing, I'll talk about the hotel in a moment but walking around Time Square at close to midnight was an experience everyone should have, the people were friendly and the atmosphere electric. Ok the hotel, not cheap so you'd expect it to be good and to be fair it was. The room was sharp and modern and the legendary beds every bit as good as the publicity material would have you believe. But for me the Hotel was just stark and cold. The service was first class but if you want a drink or something to eat you're better off going the 200 yards to Time Square where theres loads of choice. There is a famous Steak House in the Westin, it has an American Football theme and some of the best Steaks you'll ever see although how the guy opposite me ate half a cow beats me !! My room at a view of sorts but nothing to shout home about.
Would I stay there again ?? Probably not but as a comfortable and convenient Hotel for all of NY's attractions it fits the bill.

title: “I want to return...”
text: The hotel is perfectly situated for all NYC hot spots. The suite was everything we hoped for and more. The staff at the front desk were professinal and friendly. We were made to feel like royalty, they opened doors for us, they spoke to us each day asking if everything was ok, the information regarding NYC we received was excellent. I cannot praise this hotel enough. I will definitely return and highly recommend it. A big Thanks to Matt for my NYC cookie.

title: “Great for multi-generational stay.”
text: Loved our stay at The Orchard. Traveled with a group including my 20 something children and parents. Older crowd loved relaxing in the lounge with a drink before dinner while the younger crowd headed out to explore. Easy access to Union Square and great eateries. Staff was friendly and attentive. Room was clean and comfortable with a great view of the cable cars passing by without being too loud.

title: “Scary Entrance”
text: Traveled with spouse for business. We had a lot of luggage, so used a luggage cart, which was immediately available. However, the front door is a pull-open, single-wide glass door, so one of us had to hold it open while the other pulled the cart. And, there were two of those doors, as the cart was in a tiny vestibule between the doors. The lobby was small & seemed clean enough. The hallways & elevators were old & broken-down looking, so we were worried. Arriving at our room, the room's entry light & bathroom light wouldn't turn on, and the room smelled like vomit. After going all the way back down to the front desk, we were given a room that was nice enough. We agreed that if we'd seen just this room, we would have been satisfied. However, after experiencing all the grossness leading up to that, we were concerned whether the room was really clean, or just looked clean. We were exhausted, it was late & we were only staying one night, so we kept it, hoping we wouldn't run into bed bugs. The bed was very comfortable & the bath seemed clean enough, though the toilet left something to be desired. Room had refrigerator & microwave, though someone had left a drink in the fridge. Spouse called the secretary & told her never to book this hotel again.

title: “Conveniently located hotel”
text: My wife and I were generally pleased by our several night stay at the Parc 55 Wyndham, whose location works very well for someone wanting to shop Market Street, or the Union Square area. Automobile access off the Bay Bridge, Fifth Street exit, turns directly into Cyril Magnin, couldn't be easier. The room was spacious, had a great view on the 24th floor and was very clean. The only downside is that a lot of the neighborhood noise wafts up to the rooms. We had a light lunch on arrival in their cafe, food was very good, otherwise ate elsewhere for dinner, but access for a wide variety of restaurants either by foot or short cab rides is excellent.

title: “Poor (no) sound insulation in rooms”
text:
Stayed here for 4 nights. Good location, near to the Mag. Mile. Very large hotel with typical service (both good and bad) that you would expect. Long wait for check-in - the three people on the desk kept disappearing for long periods behind a screen! Lady on the Concierge was not very friendly (as I see others have noted), and looked surprised that I wanted to know how to get to the Art Institute. Worst thing was the sound insulation in the rooms. I had two connecting doors, and could hear everything from next door -conversations, toilet, television - well, I mean everything! Had to sleep with ear plugs in! When will hotels learn that, if they have rooms with connecting doors, these should at least be insulated properly when not in use eg with padding or a sound-proof cover. I paid almost $300 per night, but it was like staying in a 1 star motel. No chance to move room as the hotel was completely full. Apart from that it was OK - but the maid did keep knocking on the door, despite the fact that I had a Do not Disturb card on the door! Also, the soap in the shower gave me a rash!
I think there are better hotels in Chicago for these prices.

title: “One of the friendliest and helpful staffs you will ever find.”
text: We had a wonderful experience at Cassa Hotel. The staff was amazing. They were friendly, courteous and extremely helpful. They went out of their way to make our visit memorable. The hotel was exteremely clean and well kept. Our room was very nice and large by NYC standards. It is also conviently located a couple of blocks off of Time Square in a very nice neighborhood. I could not reccomend this hotel more.

title: “Good average quality hotel with one major flaw”
text:
We stayed at the Hospitality House for three nights in mid January 2009. The rooms are large with ours having a bedroom, bath, living room, and fully equipped kitchen which we did not use. Good location in Manhattan. The heating system needs to be upgraded- was hard to regulate old fashioned radiators. The usual BW complimentary breakfast. A friendly and helpful staff.
BUT each night that we stayed about midnight a garbage disposal truck would starting picking up dumpsters for fifteen or twenty minutes. The noise of the running truck, the operation of the lift mechanism and the banging of the dumpsters was incredibly loud, and it was impossible to sleep.

title: “A Good Night's Sleep in NYC”
text: This hotel offers reasonable rates, good sized rooms by NYC standards, friendly service and an outstanding location. We stayed 3 nights and were pleased to see the property has undergone extensive renovation since our last visit. The room was spacious and very well appointed. We adore this location with its easy access to Madison Square Garden/Penn Station. It doesn't get more convenient than this. Doormen, Bellmen, Housekeepers and Restaurant/Bar staff all especially helpful. Had the opportunity to chat with General Manager, Steve Kipnis. Love the bar/restaurant combo space of Niles and enjoyed breakfast and cocktails and snack menu. There's also a Dunkin Donuts right around the corner! This hotel keeps getting better and better. I look forward to returning.

title: “A+ heres why!”
text: We were at this fabulous resort this past Saturday and had to leave abruptly due to personal problems....then something remarkable happened. As we arrived home we noticed that we had somehow by mistake grabbed an extra set of women’s dresses in a garment bag that looked like ours. As you can imagine we were embarrassed and called the hotel immediately to correct the situation. The staff and management team showed great class and personal attention to the party that was missing there garments. The W team sent a service to pick up the garment bag and return it to the rightful owner as soon as they could. After discussing this with me wife we agreed that if this was to happen to us; the manner in which the hotel handled the concern was 5 star service. This type of attention to every guest solidifies my belief that this hotel is top of the line and a class act.

title: “Convenient”
text:
We booked into Hampton Inn because it was a block from the Convention Center, had breakfast provided, and we've stayed at Hampton Inns previously. It was booked through the Convention Hotel Group for the meeting . Our plane arrival was about 7 hrs late, so arrived at the hotel about 1am. We had called to let them know we were coming and they informed us that our room would be there for us. The room on the 7th floor looked like it had not been refurnished in quite some time. It was across from the elevators, but soundproofing was pretty good. There was about a whole city block under demolition right outside our window. If we had arrived earlier, we might have asked for a new room, but since we were so late and exhausted,and had to be at meetings at 8am, we just went to bed. The hotel was full, so figured we could not get any better room the next evening.
The breakfast room was great. There were 2 hot choices every morning, lots of fruit, yogurt, rolls danish, as well as coffee and tea available all day. When we came in after a long day, there were pretzels with mustard and lemonade in the lobby. The desk and other employees were all very friendly, esp the breakfast room crew. For a meeting at the Convention Center, this was much better than our friends at the Marriott*Convention Hotel) who had the lobby torn up and most of the eating areas closed...for 2-3 times the price.

title: “Great place for a short or long stay”
text:
Spent the last week at Homewood Suites Riverwalk/Downtown while attending a conference with my husband. This place was exceptional and we wish we could have stayed longer. As other reviewers have stated it is beginning to show some wear but was very spacious, clean and comfortable. Our room was large with a living room, kitchen, large bath area and bedroom. There were 2 flat screen TVs which was much appreciated. The breakfast was very good with 2 juice choices, coffee, and tea. An egg dish and a meat was served every morning as well yogurt, bananas,oranges,apples and a good selection of cereals. I was very impressed with the evening small meals. They were indeed meals! One night beef fajitas with all the trimmings which were very good. Always a meat,starch,and vegetable with what ever trimmings were called for. My husband regrets that the day we left he missed meatloaf night. The staff was very friendly and helpful. There is a pool on the roof which is very small but well maintained.
The hotel is on the quiet end of the Riverwalk which is nice. It is within walking distance to all the major attractions and restaurants downtown. We enjoyed our stay here and whenever in San Antonio will stay at Homewood Suites Riverwalk/Downtown. It's perfect for a short or long term stay.

title: “Best hotel ive stayed in in a long while”
text:
ok, i booked this hotel as it was in a very good deal on a website, and was far too good to turn down. Wasnt until after booking it that i read the reviews and started to worry, it really isnt written up as a great place on here.
Boy was i to be surprised!
We arrived at 1930 on a thursday evening, walked straight up to the front desk, no Q's and checked in. This took less than 3 minutes.
Then we were pointed in the direction of the lifts, and within 4 more mins we were in our room, number 738.
The lifts had signs up saying apologies for delays but they are renovating them, and i have to say, we didnt wait once for a lift, pushed the button and one arrived pretty much straight away.
We soon found that there are a couple of elevator shafts in this hotel and if you have your back to the reception desk, then take the corridoor on the left and follow it round, that lift section is really quick.
The room itself was a quad room, 2 large double beds, a bathroom and a huge cupboard.
the bathroom was big, a full size bath, big sink and a toilet. It was cleaned daily, as the bath took a little while to drain when having a shower, (approx 3 mins after getting out and tunring the water flow off) and fresh towels put in the room each day, altho they do ask you to reuse them, but if you dont want to, just leave them in a heap and they get changed daily. The comlpimentary toiletries were replenished each day too. There were 2 plug sockets in the bathroom and a hairdryer. Be warned with the hairdryer, if you have anything longer than eye level it will take a while to dry it with this. Mine is shoulder length and very thick, but with the humidity out there it frizzed very quick anyhow, so only used it to dry off the excess water!
So nothing wrong with the bathroom.
Enter the bedroom.
There are no ceiling lights, only stand alone ones, 2 taller ones and 2 table top ones on the bed side table. These created plenty of light.
There is a closet in the bedrooms, and to describe the amount of space, i would say you could easily get approx 15 fully grown adults in it! It was huge. As there were 4 of us sharing a room, i actually used it to get changed when the bathroom was being used, and i had more than enough room!
There was an ironing board and iron in it, a safe, and two hanging rails with hangers. There were also spare blankets and pillows in there. Perfect.
There was a large flat screen tv in our room, and it had a lot of channels, we had no probs finding anything to watch!! There is an ice bucket and glasses on the desk too next to the tv, but no kettle or tea/coffee/biscuits in the room. If you are there on business, there is also another table with chairs there you can use.
The air con, a lot of people on here have complained about it, i really dont see why. We were in NYC while outside temps were in the late 30's, and we put it on high while out during the day and when we came in, it was nice and cool, we turned it down a bit while in the room as it became a bit nippy and if you are in the bed next to it, can be a bit blowy! (but as i wasnt in that bed, it really didnt bother me at all!!)
The unit itself was located under the window, and certainly done waht it was there to do, cooled the room right down, so no complaints at all about it from me.
The beds. they were lovely. The pillows so comfy, i slept nearly as good as i do in my own bed, and if it hadnt been for the other 3 in the room snoring, id have slept better! The sheets were changed every 2 days, and were all lovely and clean, there was a small burn mark, but nothing to complain about as i know that those sheets are done in bulk and can burn slightly when dried if not done properly, and the throw they put over the bed covered it anyway! You cant get under the bed, so im not sure how people have said that they are disgusting, and to be honest, why would you want to look undera bed in a hotel???
It also appeared to be hoovered every day, i didnt once find crumbs or mess on the floor.
After all the previous reviews on here, i can understand why someone would be so worried about it, but dont be, this hotel is perfect, and for the price, i was so impressed, i even tipped the maid!!!
The staff in the hotel were very kind, we only really interacted with them 3 times. Arrival, which the lady was very pleasant, then to check check out time (12pm, but we managed 1pm at no extra cost) and to actually check out. All the staff we saw were very nice.
Our homeward flight wasn't until 2135 on a tuesday evening, so as we had managed to secure a 1pm check out for free, we then stored our bags in their luggage store at $3.50 per bag. The hotel arranged a taxy to take us to JFK later that night and that cost us $65 with a $20 tip on top, which i didnt think too bad as there were 4 of us, and on previous visits to NYC, had paid over $80 in a yellow cab to get to the airport!
If you want a late check out, between 12pm and 3pm is a $75 charge and any time after 3pm they charge you a whole days rate, which i think is a little excessive, but thankfully we didnt use it!
The lobby of the hotel was very clean and tidy, we sat there for a couple of hours before our flight as we were so tired and worn right out from a very action packed holiday and no one asked us to move or questioned us. There are comfy sofas to sit on and a shop if you want anything.
Can not fault this hotel at all, loved it. Please dont worry about staying here, its all you could want and more.
We didnt use the internet service, or either of the 2 restaurants that are in it, but they all looked and sounded great!
We ate a a few of the nearby delis and cafes. Cafe metro is great for a quick brekkie, and the deli on the corner by the hotel does really good cooked food and lots of little snacks and drinks that you can take back to your room.
There is a subway opposite the hotel and a christmas shop!
Central park is 3 blocks away, and times square is a 5 minute walk away, you can see it from outside the hotel!
There are always taxis waiting outside if you need them, and concierge is there to help at all hours, with special deals on theatre tickets!
Would i stay here again, definately, and i would really look forward to it!
Any questions, please dont hesitate to ask, but if you have any doubts about this hotel, them put them aside, im a fussy person, and i cant fault it in any way shape or form. The best hotel in a long long time for comfort, cleanliness and location. What more can you ask??????

title: “Very Nice, New 4 Points”
text:
This hotel was formerly a Comfort Suites and Sheraton 4 Points bought it and totally renovated the hotel from top to bottom. Really nice place for the money (usually under $100). Rooms are well appointed with nice flat screen tv's, etc., a nice gym and pool as well.
Just one problem with this hotel. It is located in a very suspect part of town. If I were a thief looking for a parking lot full of cars to break in to, this hotels parking lot would be like Christmas morning to me. It simply is not protected enough. The parking is down both sides of the hotel and not in the front where the staff can keep an eye on things. With the cars parked where they are, it would be VERY EASY for a thief to break in to a car or steal it as there is no one to stop them or even see them. 
I asked the staff if they had a night guard walking the grounds and they do not. They told me they had never had a problem and did not expect one. But there are at least 20 signs all over this parking lot warning you they they are not responsible. I have enclosed a picture of one and it is not just a warning, it is a very detailed legal entity that relieves the hotel of 100% of the liability in any way concerning your car. If they hotel thought the parking lot was safe, why are the signs every where? I have never seen signs like this anywhere.
Other than this, the hotel was perfect.

title: “convenient and fits the purpose”
text:
I stayed here in November for a convention and the convention center was within walking distance. There are many good reastaurants within walking distance and the hotel's own restaurant is pretty good too.
The rooms were good, practical and clean. The staff was helpful. Only one free internet station in the reception but good wifi (not free) link. Many of the sights are well within easy walking distance. I will stay here again.

title: “Perfect Location!”
text: We stayed at the Gem for 6 nights and frankly wished we had stayed there for all 11 nights we had in NY. The location was perfect! Walking distance to major shopping in Soho, stone's throw to subway and all the night life East Village has to offer! Oh, and how could I forget about the interesting little shops and galleries in Lower East Side. As for the hotel itself, the staff were very friendly and helpful,especially Anthony and Paolo. The room was spotless and the beds were super comfy. We were lucky to get a great rate for Gem thru Expedia so for us this was a fantastic stay in a fantastic city!

title: “Great Value”
text:
In places like NYC, I tend to prefer a more unique hotel experience and like to avoid the chains. However, I found a rate of $199 at this property and couldn't resist the deal. And trust me, for that price this is a BARGAIN!
LOCATION-
Pretty much couldn't ask for any better location. It's far enough from Times Square (4 blocks) to escape the madness, but still close enough to enjoy. It's right off Bryant Park (think Project Runway) which is my absolute favorite spot in NYC. Plenty of restaurants all around.
SERVICE-
For NYC, pretty good. The staff was friendly and helpful and had no problem accomodating an early check-in. However, on a negative note, the hotel missed the mark on my special requests as a Marriott Gold member. No big deal, but it just shows a hotel's organization and attention to detail is lacking.
ROOMS-
Marriott Standard. Average size hotel room, which is large for NYC! Very comfortable bedding and mattress. Large bathroom with nice amenities. I could not get the in-room WI-FI to work and there was not a DSL connection.
Overall, I enjoyed my stay here. It was a mostly American crowd staying here with lots of kids. If you want a nice, predictable hotel expereince with all of the amenities you usually expect, this is for you.
I would definetly stay here again if I once again found a great deal . Otherwise, I'd probably try somewhere else for a bit more unique experience.

title: “Convenient, close to Inner Harbor and lots of shopping”
text: Across the street from the Inner Harbor with abundant shopping downstairs. Rooms were nice, nothing extraordinary, but you're paying for the location. Walking distance to most IH restaurants and tourist areas.

title: “Overrated and crowded”
text:
The Westin St. Francis is a historic property located on Union Square (a very busy shopping area). Although the original building is beautifully restored, they have added a contemporary tower behind the older building. The overall effect is the introduction of many more people, but the common areas remain the same size resulting in a constant feeling of overcrowdedness and poor service. 
Our room was in the new tower and was very nice and contemporary. The furnishings were tasteful and typical Westin. The bathroom was clean and all components worked well. The only complaint was the elevator which seemed to have an unusually long wait time. 
The common areas were beautiful and restored very well. The lobby is grand and since we were there at Christmas, was decorated wonderful with a huge tree, gingerbread house and the usually assortment of smaller decorations. We tried to have a drink in the lobby, but it was so crowded that we waited for 30 minutes and never saw a waiter. As well, I stood in a line for almost 40 minutes to speak with the concierge. 
The Hotel location is good - excellent if you like to shop. I found Union Square to be very crowded and touristy and lacking the usually personality of San Francisco. It is, though, close to a BART stop, but it is a hike up a hill to get to the Hotel. I feel for the money, there are better locations in the city. 
Overall, I was disappointed with the St. Francis. I thought I was staying in a historical property, but ended up in a cookie-cutter Westin hotel. This is by no means a bad thing, as Westins are very nice. I do think, though, there are better places to stay in San Francisco.

title: “Wonderful!”
text:
Just last month, June 13-17 2007, my party of 6 went to New York and stayed at the Courtyard new York Manhattan/Fifth Avenue at 3 East 40th Street. We booked the rooms by using Marriott reward points, but the rate that we would have paid was $395. The location was the best that we could ask for. 
We booked two double rooms, one for my mother and myself, 
one for my uncle, aunt and two cousins. The rooms were smaller than they generally are throughout the country, but for NYC, they were of a good size. My mother and I had plenty of room, including room to store our luggage. My other family members were a bit cramped, but there are four of them and they tend to be a bit chaotic anyway. The beds were VERY comfortable, especially after a long day of walking! There was also high-speed internet in the rooms (in addition to two computers and printers in the mezzanine, which was great -- so that you can print off your boarding passes). The bathroom was of a good size (pretty standard for anywhere), and the soap, shampoo, etc. provided was of good quality. Housekeeping was great as well!
We did eat at the attached restaurant for breakfast one day, and although it was good, the offerings were limited and when they run out, it took a little while for them to replenish. There were eggs, bacon, sausage, fresh fruit (it was good!), waffles, croissants, bagels, cereal, a selection of juices, milk and other beverages (I may be missing something, but can't put my finger on it).
The better place to eat was Cafe Charlie's which was on the other side. It was twenty-four hours and is a cross between a convenience store, a grocery store and a restaurant. There was food that you could take of a shelf and purchase, a salad bar set-up with many different options, including fresh fruit (delicious and perfect!), and a grill area where things were made-to-order, including bagels, french toast, pancakes, etc. The only meal we ate there was breakfast, and it was great. We did stop in one night after we had gotten back late and got some cake, which was very good (strawberry shortcake, cheesecake and black forest were what we had). This is another good part of the location of the hotel, so I thought it was appropriate to include it.
Back to the hotel: the staff was wonderful, always offering help! When we went to Phantom of the Opera on Friday night and were running late, the concierge ran down to 5th Avenue, hopped in a taxi and brought it to us. They were all very helpful with anything we needed!
The hotel was very quiet, as there were only seven rooms (if I remember correctly) on each floor. We never had to wait for an elevator for more than thirty seconds. There was a gym with a couple of treadmills, stationary bikes and a few more machines. There were two computers and printers that were available for guests to use which was great, as we could check-in for our flight back home and print off our boarding passes. The hotel itself was gorgeous and looks just like the pictures on the website.
The Marriott Company has still not disappointed us!
Please let me know if you have any questions!

title: “Typical Airport Hotel”
text: The Hilton Phoenix Airport is a typical airport hotel - nothing special, but a great location for an early flight, with no parking fees, and a restaurant on-site. The room was clean, albeit sparse. It had a balcony that overlooked the pool, but there were no chairs on it, so you had to take out the chair from the room. The only drawback to this hotel is how far you have to walk to get back to the lobby from your room. Other than that, it is very functional for a traveler using the airport. The Rental Car Center at Phoenix Airport is about a ten minute drive from the hotel. The front desk staff were also very helpful with directions and very friendly.

title: “Great little hotel in a good position”
text: We stayed here for a couple of nights at the start of a 5 week trip up the West coast of the U.S. We found the area very central (we had a rental car) for getting to Hollywood and Santa Monica etc and great for shopping over at Macys and Loewmans. The room looked out on the central courtyard and so it was quiet and you could open a window for fresh air. The room was not large but it was fine for the price and there was valet parking. Heaps of places to eat and shop within walking distance. We had a night at the end of our trip before flying out of LA and tried to book it at Elan but they were full! So we booked at the Sofitel down the road - much more expensive and very noisy - not worth the extra size in room for the price.

title: “A Home Away from Home”
text:
I've stayed at the Belvedere half a dozen times over the past three years and I have to admit that it has become my home away from home while I am in New York. I brought an Adventure Tours group here for three days in July and all of my passengers were delighted with their accomodations.
This is a small boutique hotel with excellent decor and clean, comfortable rooms. Appointments are stylish and baths are completely tiled with marble floors. Each room has a small galley kitchenette where coffee can be made in the morning and where simple microwave food can be prepared and refrigerated. A minor complaint is that elevator service is a little slow. Be advised that the service elevator at the end of the hall can be used by patrons after hours...much faster.
The location is superb! You are steps away from Times Square and close to numerous restaurants, shopping, and sights. Try Mont Blanc, a delightful Continental restaurant next door.

title: “High end feel without the high end price!”
text:
There is a reason that this place is rated #1 on TripAdvisor for downtown Denver. This place is perfect. We booked a 1 bedroom suite for 3 nights to attend the CU Denver graduation. When we arrived, the 1 bedroom suite was too small for us (my mother in the living room and my husband and myself in the bedroom), and the only access to the bathroom was through the bedroom. ....
So, we asked for something more accomodating. They moved us to a 2 bedroom suite for a VERY modest upcharge, and we were thrilled. We got an extremely spacious suite, and two large bedrooms, each with their own bath and an excellent view of the city. The room had all the amenities that made our trip a true vacation. In the full sized kitchen we were able to make tea and coffee in the morning, cook modest meals, and comfortably relax with the entire family in the living area. The hotel itself was very clean, quiet and secure. The lobby is beautiful (especially decorated for Christmas), and we spent a few hours chatting in front of the fireplaces in cozy leather chairs while the temps outside were well below zero! Over the course of the long weekend, we were able to walk everywhere - LoDo for cocktail hour, all the great restaurants, the Musuem of History, the 16th St. Mall, the Capital Building, Larimer Square, and the Convention Center for the graduation. Parking was easy and affordable (included in our room package). The breakfast - also included (!) was NOT skimpy and the dining room is comfortable and inviting. Throw in the free wifi, the bedroom windows that actually open (unlike the Brown Palace) for some fresh air, the helpful staff, and reasonable price, and you have yourself THE perfect place downtown. 
If I had to say anything negative, it would be 1) we wished we'd had a king sized bed (but our beds were comfortable and new), and 2) the hotel doesn't have a restaurant, but Panzano ($$$) is next door and many other great places are located nearby.

title: “Favorite Hotel in Boston - Go for Fairmont Gold”
text: Great location and beautifully furnished. I always try to splurge and stay in a fairmont gold room. Service is excellent and goodies in lounge are great. This is my favorite place in Boston; try the Lobster Benedict for brekafast in the restaurant.

title: “Excelent”
text: Hotel accomodation and service as expected, just the lobby could be better. I had other exeperience with other facilities from Travellodge and it was better than this one in SF.

title: “Not that great”
text: If you stay at the Hotel Bel-Air, you probably have some sort of expectation of what the food, service, and ambience should be at such a highly touted establishment. Unfortunately, this hotel did not live up to my expectations at all. I agree with others who have written that you need to "look the part" to get better service. I was on vacation with my family and looking for a chance to relax - therefore, I decided to dress more casually - although, still in a nice shirt/sweater and dressy jeans or khakis each day (with nicer clothes for evening wear). Despite this, I still had a general feeling of being looked down upon by the hotel staff and hotel "regulars". This is definately not a welcoming, family-like atmosphere - it seems that it would be better suited as a catwalk for you to show off your newest surgical improvement or designer clothing from Rodeo Drive. We went to the restaurant one evening and got exceptionally poor service because all we wanted were appetizers and drinks and did not order off the "pricier" main entree menu (We would have ordered off it had there been more choices and seating in the Pub - not everyone wants to eat Foie Gras or Rack of Lamb after being on an airplane all day). The rooms were nice but the lack of cleanliness was appalling. There was mildew on the bathtub, the tile floors throughout the suite were full of hair and dirt, and the bathroom wall had some sort of disgusting, brown splatter on it. Oh, and the "Business Center" was a joke. It was nothing more than a computer tucked into a small, hot closet that you needed to ask the front desk staff for permission to use. Not what I expected from a member of the Leading Hotels of the World. Don't get me wrong - Hotel Bel-Air is in a gorgeous setting and definately worth checking out. However, I would recommend simply stopping buy for a walk on the grounds rather than staying or eating here. That is, unless you think your appearance and wallet can keep up with the likes of Posh and Becks (and if you don't know who that is, you really don't even belong at this place.)

title: “It's okay, Photos are deceiving.”
text: We booked this hotel for an amazing price on a name your own price website. The photos make this hotel look much nicer than it is. The neighborhood was a bit intimidating... But the service was very good! The rooms were nice and clean. Plus they had Bath & Bodyworks toiletries, which I love. It says this hotel is a 3 and a half stars.. I would say 3 at the most. Parking per night was $15! Valet was $18? FREE WIFI

title: “would not recommend”
text:
we were next to a loud group and you could hear it through the walls. we didn't want to get bothered by the maids so we hung do not disturb sign. But not once, while we were 4 days, do they give us any clean items. all they have to do is hang it on the door like marriott did. no toiletries beside the 1 1/2 that was there that first night. no clean towels given anymore. pillow flattens like crazy, couldn't sleep well. 
location is great. i like the 2 restaurants in the hotel. close to every tourist spot.

title: “Great Stay”
text: I enjoyed my stay at Raffaello. The service was excellent, and the location was great (a short walk to the Brown and Red lines).

title: “Excellent Customer Service”
text:
I stayed at the Lord Baltimore hotel for one night from Sept 30 to Oct 1. I was there with my mother along with hundreds and hundreds of other women attending a conference at the arena.
As you can imagine, having so many people attempt check in at similar times could have been confusing. I had dropped my mom off to check in while I handled the parking situation. She was checked in almost immediately--despite the large crowds in the lobby. I was misinformed about what I needed to self park by one of the attendants outside and had to temporarily park and come into the hotel. I was greeted by Jay Staley who was on duty trying to make sure everyone was taken care of. I explained what was going on and he immediately took my keys and told me not to worry and he would take care of the valet parking. He conferred with Anthony who then quickly handled everything. Even the following day, we had the privilege of thanking Jay when we say him in the morning, and Anthony quickly recognized us when we called for our car and our car seemed to be immediately brought to us.
We encountered a minor heating/air conditioning issue in that the heat was never switched on in our room, We called the desk and within about 10 minutes, two lovely gentlemen where in the room fixing the problem. I had also called the front desk to inquire about breakfast options, Kevin, who was the manager on duty was able to quickly look up our reservations and provide the necessary vouchers.
Breakfast was lovely, We had envisioned mass chaos with so many women trying to get to the same place at the same time, but it was actually quiet and relaxing. I did not get the man's name who was in the restaurant seating folks, but he was also great. He was rapidly getting people what they needed, aiding the wait staff in order to keep the morning going, knowing all were pressed for time.
The hotel lobby is very nicely decorated. The building itself is older in style, the rooms smaller sized, but very clean and with sleep number beds that were comfortable. THe valet parking is $31 or you can self park--around the corner and across the street for $15.
 On my next visit to Baltimore, I will definitely consider the Radisson as my first choice !

title: “This is a great hotel”
text: I just stayed at this location for a week while in LAX on business. The hotel is new and very clean. I really enjoyed my stay. The bed is amazing. If you don't want to rent a car and would like to get out and about, the trolley is a great option. It is $5 round trip and will take you to the Manhattan Beach Pier where there is a bunch of shops and ton's of places to eat. I will stay here again next time I am in LA.

title: “Squaw Peak Hilton”
text: The Hilton in Phoenix North by Squaw Peak is very nice, cozy and has a great atmosphere as well as good restraunts. I loved to walk the shady gardens and just sit outside in the warm Arizona air. The only problem I had there was a very moldy bathtub stopper which I reported to management and the problem was dealt with quickly. Otherwise it was clean and comfortable, very good service and very good value for the money. I would recommend it very highly.

title: “Nice Hotel”
text: Great value, great location. The room was spacious, the bed was comfortable, the bathroom was clean and very nice. Has a separate tub and shower. The front desk was very friendly and knowledgable.

title: “Stylish hotel in a great location”
text:
I stayed at the Park Hyatt for two nights on business. Although a little more expensive than the other nearby chains, it was well worth it (and they offer a AAA discount).
The room was good sized (I had the least expensive room), very clean, and very smartly laid out. Separate tub and shower, quiet, and comfortable.
The hotel is just a block from great shopping and a short cab ride to almost everything else. I would definitely stay here again.
It's not quite to the level of a great Four Seasons (i.e. San Fransisco or Hawaii), but a very classy nice hotel and not nearly as $$$.

title: “Awesome Hotel for the Location&Price!”
text: This hotel deserves a five star rating because this hotel met and exceeded every expectation. The suite we had was great and very spacious with 2 closets, a separate living area and bedroom. Our room really felt like a high end apartment that would go for a million, but only cost us under $400 a night which is a price you really can't beat. The room we had even had a balcony and the views from the windows within the room were amazing. It had a clear view of the Empire State Building and skyline which was pretty unbelievable. Location wise the hotel was great because it was within footsteps of Penn Station, the BoltBus stop was located right on the side of the hotel, and there were plenty of subway stations close by. All in all I would definitely would recommend this hotel when visiting New York because it really is a nice place to stay at with great rates and service. I know that the next time we visit New York we will definitely being staying at the New Yorker again.

title: “Great Hotel and Price!”
text: The Ramada Hollywood was a really great find!! Great rooms & comfortable beds & nice bathrooms. Having a microwave and a mini fridge in the room allowed us to beat some of the expensive LA prices for dinners by bringing back our leftovers for the next day. Convenient location in Hollywood, near some great Mexican eateries and a Rite Aid and some cool bars. 3 bad things: an expensive daily parking fee ($16+), the included breakfast was the same e-v-e-r-y day, and uhhhh, the maids don't knock...

title: “Great business hotel”
text: I've stayed here multiple times, the latest on family business. As always the Fairmont experience is welcoming, professional and relaxing. Great, helpful staff, convenient location, modern lobby and bar that is easy to have a drink by yourself or with guests. The health facility is a little small but the equipment is in good condition so no complaints there.

title: “Great location”
text: The location of the Sofia can't be beat! Three blocks from the Gaslamp District with its night life and many food options, three blocks from the Seaport and ferry to Coronado, and one block from the trolley to Old Town. We found it very easy to navigate around the Sofia, and it's only an $11.00 cab ride from the airport. The room was nice but on the smaller side. This is a European style hotel so we expected that. Check in was super easy. The staff was great and eager to help find a place to eat or directions. Would definately stay here again, only recommend getting room in back of hotel. Had a corner room overlooking street and the noise at night was unbearable, with police and fire trucks going by as it is a very busy street.

title: “Nice hotel”
text: Good location within walking distance of a lot of good attractions in downtown Houston. We didn't like the pillows - you had a choice of a mushy flat one or one that was solid and seemed to prop you head at a 90 degree angle. Inside of the hotel is very nice and remodeled with a number of nice amenities. All in all, a good hotel.

title: “Not worth it”
text: Marriott waterfront. Sounds nice but it lacks a 5 star rating. The view was very nice after paying extra for it.The room was avg size. The problem is it is bare bones. The quality of the staff is sub par at best stayed there 4 nights so had some time there,You get nothing worth the price unless you get this for 100.00. The problem with baltimore is it isthe inner harbour or nothing. If your on business and are not paying it will do but NOT a 5 star hotel. 3 at best...

title: “Back again!”
text:
