It was our second visit to the Hollywood Orchid Suites in two years and we were not disappointed! Got a room at the back of the complex with it's own balcony, a perfect spot to dine, relax with a book/iPad, and soak up the beautiful LA sunshine, with clear views of the hills behind.
Positives:
- Spotless rooms and efficient housekeeping service
- Friendly service from the staff on the front desk
- Plentiful continental breakfast
- Location central to local attractions, public transport, restaurants, supermarkets, pharmacy, retail outlets, departure points for tours/day trips
- Free wi-fi
- In-room safe
- Large, comfortable beds
- We found the other guests to be reasonably quiet throughout our stay
- Basement parking garage
- Coin-operated laundry with washing powder/softener vending machine
- Ice machine and vending machines on basement level
Drawbacks:
- Delivery trucks arriving from 6am at the back of Hollywood & Highland and Renaissance Hotel, however this cannot be helped and is NOT a fault of the hotel. Ear plugs work well to block the noise caused by the trucks.
We will ALWAYS consult the Hollywood Orchid Suites on any future stays in LA, a stay here is very well worth the price paid!

title: “Great hotel, great service, will definitely go back again!!!”
text: My boyfriend and I stayed at the Alex from May 17-20, 2007. After reading some of the reviews posted on here I was a little worried that it may not be a great choice but we booked anyway. All I have to say is that anyone who posts a negative review of this hotel is obviously someone who is VERY hard to please. I have no complaints whatsoever. The staff was exceptionally friendly and even went out of their way several times to assist us with things such as booking a show, tour. The doormen were pleasant and so were the cleaning staff. We had absolutely no complaints with the room as well. We stayed in a studio suite and there was more than enough room for us. We had a kitchen which came in handy, a seating area, an LCD flat screen in the room as well as another LCD in the washroom. We had no problems with the water, our rooms were cleaned everyday and we had more than enough towels. We used their business centre a few times and they have free internet access as well as a printer. My boyfriend used the gym everyday and it was a great looking gym with updated equipment, and televisions on all of the cardio machines. As well, there was fresh lemonade and fresh fruits available to the patrons of the gym. All in all, it was a great hotel and we would definitely go back. We were impressed and as I indicated above, you can't please everyone but the people who have posted negative reviews on this hotel obviously either had a bad day or are people who obviously will never be happy with any place they stay at.

title: “Have stayed here twice and the second time with my daughter and her friends”
text: I have stayed at this hotel twice. The first time was May of 2010 and it was just my husband and I. This time we went July 2012 and I took my daughter for her 16th birthday. We went with two other moms and 3 daughters. This hotel is not the Westen but it did what we needed it to do, and that was provide a place to sleep, shower and change. We were too busy seeing New York to spend much time in our hotel. The second time I went, I saw areas where the hotel was making improvements. When there in July, the staff was great! We had two rooms reserved. we asked if they could put our rooms together so the girls could be together. They did us even better, they offered us a set of rooms that were joined together. They only had one bathroom, and one door from the outside, but it put us all together and was cheaper than having two rooms!!! This was awesome for the girls to be together and awesome for the moms to get to see the girls so silly. The hotel is a block from Times Square. If you can deal with not having room service, a daily maid to make your bed and bring in fresh towels, this place is the best. (we just went down and asked for new towels and got them with no problem) We are already planning trip #3 and this is where we will stay!

title: “Don't let the bed bugs bite!”
text: I was on business travel September 17-19, 2008 and stayed at the Sheraton Philadelphia City Center. The staff was friendly and the property looked nice. However, the first morning, around 5am, I awoke to find a bed bug, the size of an apple seed in the sheets with me. I imagine if I had not gotten up when I did, I would have been bitten. I caught the critter in glass and coverd it with one of the paper coasters the hotel provides its guests and wrote a note to the housekeeping staff explaining the situation. I did not think about it at the time but I should have taken a picture of it. I was moved to another room but still very freaked out and paranoid that I was going to find more or get bitten. Be ware!

title: “Convenient downtown locationNice”
text: Nice location. Next to subway stop and complimentary shuttle ride to Navy Pier.

title: “Road trip to the SE”
text: This BW + Gen X Hotel is very good. The staff is friendly, the Hotel is very clean and the breakfast was above par. I will definitively stay there again on my next trip. We wanted to be close to the Beale Street music scene and the hotel is about a mule away. There is mass transportation available if you want, but we drove down. Parking at the Hotel is included.

title: “Nice View for 10 days”
text: We just returned to Toronto, Canada from a 10 day stay at the Pointe Hilton Tapatio Cliffs Resort. We were impressed with the knowledgeable staff - in particular Anna and Ed. Our first room in the main building was a little noisy the first night. Our room was immediately changed to a quiet room, on higher ground overlooking the complex. The main dining area was just fine. The staff were extremely professional and the food was very good. The only unfortunate experience on this property was the restaurant at the top. The view was spectacular, the food was very basic. After the lobster bisque (which was ok) the rest of the meal was downhill. We paid alot of $$$ and had to wait 3 days for a reservation - what a disappointment. for the same $$$, we would go back to Mastro's Ocean Club in Scottsdale or J&G Steakhouse at the Phoenician - WOW!!!!

title: “Excellent location”
text: The hotel was at an excellent location. One could walk to most places and public transportation was close by. Room wasgood and the view great. Staff was businesslike but not over-friendly

title: “Great Location - Outdated Hotel”
text: Can't beat the location for the price. However the hotel was somewhat outdated and had an unclean feeling to me. The walls are very thin, and we could hear people opening and closing doors all night. My boyfriend and I were only in town for 1 night, so it was convenient. I wouldn’t' stay there for an extended period of time.

title: “deserves the "top value" status”
text:
The only negatives I found in this hotel were the small rooms and the somewhat outdated decor. Being an overnight stay, these things were about as important to me as the color of the manager's socks. 
Everything that did matter met or exceeded our expectations. The rooms were clean and well-arranged. Everything worked to our satisfaction and the bed was comfortable. 
The staff was very pleasant in all our interactions. There was some sorta bird they had with them. This was new to me, domestic ownership of an avian. Despite our evident mutual distrust, it and I respected our personal spaces and there were no problems.
The hotel's location is just perfect. We were able to walk to Rittenhouse for dinner and drinks and stroll around center city a bit. The next day, we took a walk out to the Mall, which I hadn't walked through since elementary school. 
We had no problems with access to the garage. I could see it being problematic, though, if you were loaded down with bags for a long trip. I suppose. Still, I've had much longer walks through airports, lugging my gear around.
Nice place. Will return if we're overnighting in philly again.

title: “Great stay, good view”
text: I stayed on an upper floor (9th) and had an incredible view of the Hearst Tower. Comfortable beds. Excellent service upon check-in and check-out. Seemed pretty quiet overall. Conveniently located to nearby restaurants, movie theater. If you're here for business downtown, imagine it would be perfect location. We stayed here on a Sunday/Monday after the Avon Walk for Breast Cancer. The hotel is a bit older, and the only way this showed was the lack of electrical outlets in the room. Would stay here again.

title: “So sheek”
text:
Just thought I would write a quick review of a great place. When we pulled up to the valet, we got out of the car to hear some great club music. The W on the wall was all lit up in glitzy lights. It made you feel like you were stepping into an LA night club. The lobby was full of young, gorgeous people and again, that great music was going. You felt like you were in this great, trendy place. It was such a nice surprise. 
The room was incredibly clean. The decor was trendy, modern, straight clean lines. Very Zen. The colors were amazing. In our standard room, the details were a plenty. Everything looked like it had taken so much time to design. Each room has it's own flair instead of your plain room. So colorful and cozy. The bathroom was so beautiful. The shower had a solid glass door. The bathroom had a shutter that opened to look into the main room. The bed was huge with nice a nice fluffy down comforter. The pillows were feather tick and so soft. 
We got room service and it was delicious. 
We went upstairs to the bar on the top floor. That was a great place with great drinks and more beautiful people. The view was so incredible. It was great to sit in this flashy bar, with great couches and look over the city and the lake. 
We had a great time and I would recommend this hotel to anyone of any age that wants to feel like a star for a day..right in Chicago.

title: “Decent hotel, but poor service”
text:
This hotel is pretty much what you would expect from a Holiday Inn - comfortable, if uninspired.
What marks it down is the attitude of most of the staff from sharpness at the frontdesk to a kitchen which closes earlier than the stated time.
Myself and my travelling companion had taken a long day trip to Yosemite. On getting back we were hungry and went down for food. We were abruptly told that the serving of food had just finished, despite the menu stating that it was being served for another 30 minutes.
It took three days, complaints to four members of staff and an e-mail to Holiday Inn's head office before my complaint was even responded to. And by then it was too late beacuse I was checking out that day.
Avoid.

title: “Not So Wonderful”
text: I wanted to love this hotel - I love the design and the beautiful Grant Grill - the lobby and even the rooms with historic character. The problem is the lack of attention to detail. After just leaving Pelican Hill in Newport where the service was fantastic this was a big let down. Upon check in when you book with AMEX Fine Hotels and Resorts they should upgrade you if an upgrade is available. They brusquely told me it wasn't available. When I saw how small our room was I called the front desk again and asked if one was available if we paid. They told me they'd call me back - 45 minutes later they called back to say a bigger room was available. Huh? I thought no upgrades were available. We stayed put since we'd already used the room (we have kids!) and didn't want to pay for an upgrade we should have gotten automatically. We stayed in 513 and there were poorly patched cracks in the walls and the room is pretty small. The lighting in the bathroom was bad. The in room movies didn't work. We had a view of the homeless people in the park across Broadway. The paintings in the bathroom was not just weird but down right creepy. The paintings in the hallways just super crooked. The capper was all the drunks coming home at 1-3 in the morning and how incredibly loud they were. I was awake from 1 to past 3 listening to their drunken conversations and doors slamming. The hotel is historic so I get that it will be a bit noisy but come on. They should designate party floors and family floors with walls that thin, I'm sure this wasn't an isolated incident. Finally on check out they informed us that the $100 food and beverage credit we got with Fine Hotels and Resorts had to be used on one meal (I thought it could be used for breakfast and then the remainder lunch, dinner, cocktails, whatever just $100 towards F and B). This was not clear at all. If it had been I would have ordered an extra sandwich and cocktail and hand delivered it to the homeless guy in the park. Bad for the hotel and bad for the customer.

title: “Comfortable, Great Location”
text: I stayed here for 12 days and would definitely stay again. I really never had a problem with the noise. What you get is a large, comfortable room, nice TV with good channels, free parking, and a great location for a cheap rate. The location is awesome, I walked to many restaurants and all the nice shops on Chestnut Street. You could also walk to the water for a nice view of the Golden Gate Bridge. The breakfast at the hotel is pretty bare, just bread, muffins, & juice. But I can say, this is one of the nicer rooms I have had for $89. Tip: the wireless internet will cost you...$5 a day or $30 a month. But free parking...and you can walk to lots of stuff. It's clean and safe as well. I would recommend this place.

title: “"In the Middle of it All"”
text: I stayed at the Double Tree TS over Mother's Day weekend 2012, after picking our daughter up from College on Long Island with my husband, daughter & sister-in-law The location was perfect... Smack dab in the middle of Time Square & all it offers. The staff was very friendly & helpful. The room was very large & clean. The subway was right around the corner, along with a great little deli for a quick breakfast, sandwich or fruit & snacks. A short walk or subway ride to Grand Central station or Central Park for a bike ride through the park We have been to Manhattan many times, but only for a long day. This was the first time spending several days. Stay on a weekday, so you can check out the Morning shows etc.Also besides the touristy stuff, check out Pier 59 & Chelsea Market. & grab a burger @ "Shake Shack", @ Merick park & people watch. Use the subways, they are fast & inexpressive.. You can down load an app for your smart phone,( NY city app), (HOP Stop), or (NY subway maps). Be ready to go, go, go & have fun. I would defiantly stay again :)

title: “Cute hotel”
text: I booked this hotel for $129 a night via Hotwire and it was an excellent deal. The decor of the hotel is very cute, very chic. It is right in the heart of the theater district, but a good walk from Michigan Ave. shops. The bathrooms are pretty tiny though, as noted in previous posts. What I liked most about this hotel was the free wine tasting every evening. After a day out in the city, we would return every night to freshen up to go out that evening, but always stopped downstairs for a free glass of wine before going out. Now, you can't beat that!

title: “OK hotel”
text:
This is a nice cozy hotel in lincoln park suburbs of chicago.
It has a old european style looks and style.
the washroom was small and the bath tub drain was not opening so water was holding up in the tub.
You can hear people walking up/down the stairs, as my room was just next to the staircase.

title: “A great hotel in a fantastic location”
text:
We stayed here for four nights in between Christmas and New Year. We booked on the strength of the reviews on this site and on the whole were not disappointed. The room was very small (it was a petite room) and the bed was likewise small, but otherwise we were very pleased with it. The ipod docking station was a nice touch. 
The location of the hotel is fantastic, just a block away from Grand Central and within easy walking distance of a lot of places. The 'business centre' was really useful and we were encouraged to check in online here for our flight home where we could print our boarding passes etc. Breakfast was good with coffees and teas, juice, pastries, bagels, fruit, yoghurt and cereals. We didn't have the cheese and wine but this was a nice idea and many people seemed to enjoy it.
The only downside was that on the evening of our departure when we wanted a cab to the airport we were told that we would find it difficult to get a yellow cab because all of the drivers change shifts at that time. This seemed to us to be a little unlikely as there were cabs everywhere. We were told the hotel could organise a private cab for $140 - as the yellow cabs only costed $50 this seemed ridiculous! We ended up going out and hailing a cab ourselves without any problems at all. We felt this was quite bad of the hotel and were disappointed as it seemed that they just couldn't be bothered. 
Otherwise we found the hotel to be excellent and would recommend it.

title: “Comfortable Stay and Excellent Customer Service”
text: This is another hotel where we received excellent customer service from the front desk staff. We had an unexpected overnight layover and the reservations agent was extremely helpful in booking our room. Though they had airport shuttle service, when we called for pick-up, the shuttle driver was not immediately available so instead of having us wait, Dexter, the front desk clerk, instructed us to take a taxi and they would pay for the fare. Now THAT'S service! He was also very helpful in getting us settled in. We were a large party and he was very patient with us. The rooms were huge and we loved that the tv's had HD channels. You can tell it's an older hotel, but we still loved it! We will definitely stay here again!

title: “Perfect central location”
text:
Hotel Frank is located on Geary street in San Fran. I stayed mid aug for 4 nights as the start of a mini break around the usa.
The location is excellent, just along the road is popular Ubiob Square where there are big name shops, including Macy's and stops for all the major tourist buses. Also right next to hotel is Powell street where th famous cable car's stop and turn around. Also lined with a huge shopping mall and plenty of other shops, eateries and a few bars off the side streets. 
The hotel room was pretty much perfect, very spacious, the bathroom was huge. Only complaint, the room was a little dark due to the black and white decor and there was a dressing table but no mirror anywhere near it, only large mirror was located in the bathroom which was a bit strange. The radio/ipod dock was a nice touch and also water cooler near reception and complimentary coffee/tea's on a morning till around 10am. 
When checking in staff made us awaer of protestors outside hotel, normally around 7am-8am and then again 5pm-6pm. This did not bother us at all as normally missed the morning one and by the time I got back to hotel after a day's exploring the night time one was also over. Staff were very polite and helpful. We had booked a few trips through other complanies back home before going on hol, staff let us use the floor phone to confirms bookings etc and were very helpful. 
The hotel is very much an affordable boutique hotel right in the centre, the restaurant was under refurb when I stayed but they give you complimentary discount vouchers to other restaurants nearby, one of which a 50's style diner with 25% off, which was very nice affordable food. 
All in all a very decent place to stay.

title: “Amazing location”
text: My girlfriends and I took the train from Portland to have a girls weekend in Seattle. The Roosevelt Hotel was so close to everything that we wanted to do. We walked everywhere, even from the train station, and saved so much money that we would have spent on cab fare or a car rental. I would stay here again and again!

title: “Great Base to Explore San Antonio”
text:
Charming Old Style hotel very close to the river.
Rooms are well appointed
Staff is super friendly and helpful
Best restaurant of all 3 Marriott full service properties

title: “It was okay...”
text:
The Sheraton Indianapolis is in a great location however the property has some issues that need to be addressed before I stay there again. The first problem is the parking garage. It’s under construction and very difficult to navigate through. I suggest taking the additional insurance at your rental car company if you plan on parking at this hotel. I stayed at this hotel when it was a Radisson and I must say they have upgraded some features during the transition but are not done yet. While the changes such as bed linens and toiletries have been made, the rooms are still in need of remodeling. My room had an old air vent which made it difficult for me to sleep well, the carpet was also dingy and in need of replacement, the bathroom also needed retiling and my room had a dank smell like it use to be a smoking room or something. Oh yea… only a few of their elevators were working and the morning wait to get to the lobby was upwards of 5 minutes. 
On a better note the staff was very friendly and made up for the hotels physical appearance. Aside from the $2 charge for a small tube of toothpaste I was very pleased with the level of service I received. While self parking I ended up in a valet space because they were full. I let the bellmen know and they were very helpful, one of them moved my vehicle for me and the other one helped me with restaurant recommendations while I waited to get my keys back. 
They also have a Starbucks located in the lobby which is always a plus for me. This property isn’t all bad, I’m sure once they finish their remodel it will be a great place to stay but until then be prepared for a few inconveniences.

title: “Excellent hotel in a very good location”
text: I found this hotel to be excellent in just about every respect. Efficient, friendly staff, comfortable rooms and beds, and really excellent facilities. I would recommend it especially for business travellers.

title: “Latham not honest”
text: Latham hotel charged us for a night we did not use due to a screw up with reservations. The front desk came up with multiple reasons, always changing. The rooms were small - the only good thing I found was the location.

title: “Wonderful !!!”
text: Stayed only two nights (3/11-3/13) but what a reprieve it was. Arrived early (11:30 am) but front desk gave us a parking pass so we could walk some where for lunch. Many restaurants nearby to eat and enjoy the ocean view. Came back at 1:30 to change for the beach and a room was ready. Great 2nd floor room with partial view of ocean. Listened to the ocean in the night while a sleep was peaceful. Office management & staff were great! Been coming for 20 + years to this inn. This was by far the best. Loved the renovated rooms. Very short walk to the beach. Enjoyed the tea & pastries in the morning. Laundry facilities for those longer trips. Good size refrigerator in room for cold drinks and leftovers. Will always come back here!

title: “Purpose: Served”
text:
Living about an hour and a half out of Los Angeles, we booked a room at the Raddison because we had plans in the city on a Saturday night, and again on the next Sunday morning. Not having to drive back and forth was worth the stay regardless, but make no mistake, this is primarily a business-type of hotel.
Upon arriving, the parking lot was under construction and valet was the only option for hotel parking. Being the starving college students that we are, we opted to park in a near-by lot for airport parking, which worked just fine. 
Check-in was a breeze. The staff was very friendly and we were allowed into our room a good 45 minutes before the listed check-in time of 3pm. 
The Saturday we were there was also Final Four day, and we had allotted time to watch both games in the room before going on with our evening. The television reception of CBS 2 was tolerable at best, but thankfully, with the hotel's free internet, we were able to watch both games in high-definition on my laptop.
Our plans for the night in Culver City got canceled, so we were left with the frenzied task of finding something to do in the area without a car (parking lot charged more for ins-and-outs). This is no knock on the hotel itself, but there isn't much to do in terms of nightlife in the general vicinity, and that wouldn't be a problem for most guests of the hotel. We opted for a little bit of a cultural experience and wandered LAX for a few hours topping it off with a late dinner at the McDonalds in the international terminal. A real fun experience, to be completely honest. We got back to the hotel around midnight and the lobby was empty. Almost creepy. Again, that comes with the turf. Looking back, The Custom hotel a few miles north would have been a better option had we known our plans were scrapped. 
PROS - Nice, modern rooms with super comfortable beds and good air conditioning. The view was also great. We requested a runway view and got quite a bit of amusement out of that. The two double bed set-up didn't feel nearly as cramped as i've experienced in other hotels. The biggest pro, hands down, was the sound-proofing of the place. The double-pane windows let NO sound in whatsoever even though planes were coming in constantly a few hundred yards from our room. 
CONS - The elevator system was laggy and confusing at times. This may have been fixed by now. Also, out of boredom, we tried to locate the stairwell. found one, but it was downright creepy. rusty pipes, dark, and odd stains and splatters on the walls. Again, nothing that was too big of a deal, and the hotel was/is going under construction. One more thing was the pool area. Because of it's vicinity to the airport as well as Sepulveda blvd, the pool and spa area was very noisy (nothing anyone can do about that, obviously), but when we arrived, there was nobody out there midday on a Saturday. That, combined with the 70s, horror film architecture of the pool area and the imposing Eastern-European looking office building in the background, turned us off from taking a dip. 
Overall, though... it's a great hotel for anyone traveling in or out of LAX... especially the closeness to the airport, the quiet rooms, and great prices. Had our trip gone as planned, the Radisson would have catered to our needs perfectly.

title: “decent, but not four star!”
text:
I lived in chicago for about 10 years & now live in the burbs. We went for an overnight outing downtown to celebrate my husbands birthday. Booked our room through hotwire for about $80. A decent hotel for this price, but if you are paying full price the $200 would be better spent somewhere else.
Pros: Good location, updated room decor, decent size room, bed VERY comfy, Big window & great view (our room faced the river with the hancock building in the center of our view-wonderful.) I did the phone check in (800 #) the morning of our arrival & that person was very helpful, arranged a room with a view & had a crib waiting in the room when we got there.
Cons: Lobby/service/amenitys/over all vibe, on par with a 2-3 star hotel (very average) When my husband called the hotel directly a few days ahead to confirm the reservation, the person he spoke to was VERY rude & when he requested a king, she pointed out that he made the reservation through hotwire and that he should be happy to get what ever they give him. The crib they had for us was a pack & play & was FILTHY/stained, so we wound up having our 2 year old sleep with us. The "coffee pot" makes just one cup & we were only given enough coffee for that 1 cup, no cream/sugar. (when I called the front desk for some, they did bring it)
Overall: Good location, room had a modern style, Good views, average amenities. Worth the discounted rate, But if you are looking for something "grand" save your extra four star bucks for somewhere else.

title: “Nice place, big rooms, good location, nice price”
text:
We spent 4 days here before we went to Port Townsend for a wedding. We had always just passed through Seattle and wanted to see a bit of it. 
The hotel is several blocks south east of the main downtown area and is near the new library. Still everything is easily walkable. For instance, it is about 8 blocks to Pike's Place Market; maybe 6 blocks to Pioneer Square.
This is a very nice, cozy little hotel. Amenities like a business center and fitness area are there, but are minimal. Also, no pool or spa. That being said, the price is also much lower than more full featured hotels.
On the plus side, at 5pm every evening, there is a free wine tasting in the lobby that starts off the evening in great style.
The staff was very friendly, helpful, and accommodating. 
The rooms are very big and well appointed. A small maintenance issue was taken care of immediately.

title: “Bayside”
text: Great hotel. Its nothing fancy, just a Holiday Inn. The bell hops were awesome and provided some rides to local places for a tip even when they were not required to do so. The desk people were pretty accurate for some good places to eat as well.

title: “Good hotel, good location for downtown Jacksonville business, Landing, and convention center.”
text: The building has a few decades under its belt, but rooms have been updated to current standards. At least in my 10th floor room, the sliding doors to balcony need to be replaced with more soundproof one, to reduce city street noise, which was noticeable. Parking was good with plenty of space and reasonable price ($10). Easy walk across the river to the convention center.

title: “Worst attitude - will not stay again”
text: Two nights with DH here was the last straw - I will not stay at this hotel again. Perfect location for business, but not worth the nonsense. The W New York has confused snobbery with with exclusivity. It seemed like every staff member went out of their way to make us feel like they were doing us a favor to let us stay there. Small room, unusable space, and street noise just aren't worth it.

title: “Very Nice”
text:
One night stay for a shopping excursion with the spouse. Upgraded to a corner suite room which was huge. Location of the property is very convinient, right on the water and a short walk to Pike St Market and downtown shopping. 
The staff was outstanding. They not only accomodated our requests but were extremely pleasant and professional.

title: “You will love it! Full of character.Good central position.”
text:
Just returned from 4 night break and loved every minute. - 2 double beds in room and still lots of space. Bathroom is a little small but adequate for the 4 night stay. Staff could not be more helpful, always very polite and friendly. Hotel is spotlessly clean and always smells lovely whatever time of day. Beds are so comfortable, great after being on your feet all day. Definately go for a high floor, we were on the 8th floor and could hear some traffic noise - did not bother us too much as we were so tired from being out all day. If you are looking for a secure, friendly clean hotel with character this will will not disappoint.
Especially attractive at Christmas time with beautifull tree in lobby .
Special mention to Norman on reception - a pleasure to deal with.

title: “Chilled out hotel in the city”
text: This was the first stop on our trip and we were amazed at how friendly everyone was. The staff were fantastic, very helpful with advice on the city, even compiling a list of bars they though we might like. The room was nice, we only dipped in the pool once for 10min as it was a little cold. The adjacent restaurant Chambers does great cocktails. The only drawback is the location, we had repeated warnings from different people not to walk around at night so we didn't, having said this I definitely felt very safe at the Phoenix Hotel. Overall a lovely relaxed hotel with a nice atmosphere to the place.

title: “Deadly”
text:
Ok, so my wife and her collegue had a presentation to make and the ACS conference here in Denver. I booked the room through Wyndham (I am a Wyndham employee) and got a good deal on the room. When we got there the room number was handwritten, the AC didn't work and it smelled BAD. The girl at the front desk was nice enough to set us up at the Days Inn for no extra charge (since I had already paid the Wyndham property). It's a good thing she did. What would have been our second night there we found out from the local news that a man was SHOT TO DEATH. http://www.kjct8.com/news/29013540/detail.html 
This link is to it. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!!

title: “Good location but bad service”
text:
The location of the hotel is great because you are a couple of blocks from Boston Commons, Chinatown, Theater District and Downtown. It is also next to a subway station which is very convenient for visiting places a little farther like Fenway Park, the MFA or Fanuei Hall. 
But other than location everything is downwards they didn't respect our reservation our airplane got a delay a we arrive late and they have given out our room and there was no more rooms available because of a "pipe problem" they took ages to solve our problem but finally they sent us to the Radisson. One of the two elevators was out of order so it took a while to get up and down from the Lobby to your room. The room was in general quite good and they gave us free internet. But again if you want to grab a snack at night the vending machine in our floor was out of order so you have to walk to other floor to get something or use the elevator that was not out of order. 
Other detail is the restaurant in which we only ate there once, first is too smal and it get crowded in the mornings for breakfast so we have to wait for around 15 minutes and other days we better decide to go to Au Bon Pain or Mc Donalds just a few steps away. The breakfast in the restaurant was plain and a bit pricy. About 80 dollars for four people and nothing really special. Don't bother in eating lunch or dinner in the hotel, Boston has great places to eat. 
Overall the hotel was not very good and I was dissapointed because it didn't have the same quality or service as other Doubletree Hotels in other cities.
I will definetely not returning to this hotel.

title: “Great location”
text: We stayed here fir 3 nights and had a ball! It is in a fantastic location and we just walked and caught public transport everywhere. It's the hub really! So much atmosphere even if fishermans wharf s a little seedy. The staff were great and the rooms were lovely and clean we stayed in the second building which has a Denny's attached to it and the breakfast was really fresh and lovely. Great place to stay!

title: “Very Nice Property Great Staff”
text: Very good property and good staff with minimal issues (coffee, tissue, toilet paper not restocked).

title: “First Class Boston Hotel”
text: We had a brief stay on a Saturday night in January. The hotel looks classical but seems to have been built quite recently. We had a "junior suite" - it was very spacious, very well appointed and very comfortable. We were travelling with another party who had booked a basic room. She was upgraded on checkin to a junior suite to keep her within proximity to us - very kind. The two restaurants attached to the hotel are very good but were packed out on the Saturday night.Location is adjacent to Fenway Park and Boston University - I would have prferred to be a bit closer to Boston Common. The staff were very efficient, helpful and friendly. Overall, a very good experience with perhaps location and the cost of parking my only quibbles.

title: “Nice hotel but...”
text: Saturday Dec 15th 7:00am they were doing maintenance above our room (hammering). It did not stop until 10:00am. We didn't go to bed until 3:00am that morning (we did a little parting on the river walk). I told the front desk and they told me the workers go to work at 7:00am. This is the worst stay I've had at a hotel. The people and the rooms were nice but that doesn't matter if you can't sleep. I would recommend in the future starting maintenance later in the morning when people are out of their rooms. I would not recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: “Ok - great location for IAH - but tired”
text:
I stayed here for one night after flying in from the UK.
First thing to say is that this is a great hotel if you want to stay near the airport, I picked up my rental car & was in the hotel within 5 minutes. Plenty of free parking.
I was upgraded to a Club Floor room, but it was very tired. For example, the cupboard under the TV was missing a door which appeared to have been ripped off.
Bed was comfortable & the room pretty quiet.
I had the buffet breakfast which was ok.
Overall - great location, but needs some work

title: “Fantastic Location”
text: I stayed here for 3 nights with 5 friends at the end of a fantastic road trip in California. We found the hotel by chance but once we entered the reception we knew that we wanted to stay here. The location is fab - just a short walk to all the sights on sunset boulevard and a short drive from the Hollywood Hills. The hotel was recently refurbished, the rooms are fresh and spotless. There is valet parking for $30, which was fairly steep but because if the location we were happy to pay this. we stayed in a room at the back of the property overlooking the pool. I would recommend this side as there is a fairly busy road to the front. We didn't eat here but the smells from the restaurant were always great. Would absolutely recommend and would go again.

title: “The Paradise Hotel - NOT a family resort!”
text: The Paradise Hotel is located in a quite neighborhood, and outside appears a charming motor-hotel complex, with parking right outside your door. The manager lives on site. We stayed a week, and had these problems: The microwave was half broken, at time firing and popping like it might explode. Also, the hot water leaves ALOT to be desired, so showers must be quick. Also, there is free wireless internet, but the cable only has a few channels. To name a few, CNN, FOX, basic channels, HBO and also a dedicated porn channel. I MEAN dedicated, as in non stop porno's 24 hours a day. At first we thought it was some kind of mistake or joke, but i guess not. It's quite strange...in fact, this may very well be the strangest hotel I've ever stayed in. At $325 a week ($60 a night) for a king-size room with a microwave and mini-fridge, it is moderatly priced for the city, but could offer a little more for the money, I think, as I've stayed at dozens of hotels for 45-55 a night and got a higher level of quality. However, like alot of weekly stay hotels, it's not filled with bums or druggies, and is quiet, so if your a drifter with a little cash in hand, this is a pretty good bet. Especially if you have a liking towards XXX-rated flicks!

title: “Wonderful Hotel, Fantastic Staff”
text:
Good location only a short walk from the major sites. The hotel staff was wonderful and very helpful. You could tell the staff loved NYC and wanted their guests to enjoy it, too.
 The beds were very comfortable and the free Wi-Fi was a nice plus. The free breakfast buffet was very well stocked with a number of fresh fruits, yogurts, cereal , waffles and such.
 A gem of a hotel in NYC.

title: “Cheap and Cheerful”
text: Just spent 3 nights at this hotel and it is very very basic, but cheap. My daughter and I had a room overlooking the park, but the windows were so dirty you couldn't see much. My friend and her daughter had a really crummy room with no natural sunlight. The beds were comfortable and the shower good. The complimentary toiletries smelt really good. The subway is very close and it takes approx 10 minutes to get into Times Square. The one redeeming feature is that the staff are really so very friendly and helpful.

title: “Great stay! Would stay again”
text: There are a lot of bad reviews of this hotel. I was a little concerned about staying there. But it was great! Beautiful lobby, efficient service, friendly staff and - best of all: nice room! I mean the room was BIG when compared to what you normally get in NY. Everything was clean. Sure, a tiny bit of wallpaper was peeling off in the bathroom. But so what - who even cares? The room was comfy and quiet. Can't beat the location. I'd definately stay there in the future.

title: “Awesome for Families!!”
text:
We came to the JW during April and had a great vacation, The pools and lazy rivers were amazing and really helped with Scottsdale's hot weather! The food was great and the hotel was very big ant beautiful. Our room was spacious and comfortable. The hotel was centrally located and very close to shopping and restaurants. Would recommend this place to ANY family looking for a 
kid-friendly and nice hotel located in the Phoenix-Scottsdale area.

title: “Overall Dandy, but One Serious Flaw”
text: Winter weather grounded us in Boston unexpectedly for the night. With a late arrival and planned early departure, we decided to stay right at the airport. We had enjoyed the Harborside Hyatt very much the last time we were stranded, so anticipated a good stay. We received a nice welcome and the room, albeit on the airport side instead of the water side, was lovely and well-kept. Unfortunately we found the internal soundproofing on this floor (4th) to be severely lacking. Noise from adjoining rooms and the hallways was easily heard. No one was being obnoxious; they were just conversing or going about their 3:50 am departure. A well designed, well built hotel would muffle these to-be-expected sounds adequately. Consequently this time we have to give sleep quality a "poor" and if there is a next time, ask if there are better insulated areas.

title: “Great location, top notch staff!”
text:
Just stayed at this hotel earlier in the week for a work event. The Hilton New York location can't be beat (it is literally between Times Square and Central Park on Sixth Avenue).
The event staff was first rate, you can always get a cab easily, and the shopping and siteseeing are at your fingertips. There are even a couple of close Subway stops.
I have stayed at this hotel a handful of times, and they have always been very accommodating - even when needing to tack on an additional night's stay due to a cancelled flight.
Even the guys at the bell stand are great, but it will cost you $3.50 per bag to have them hold it. It is awesome that they have the luggage storage room staffed nearly all day, though!

title: “Friendly service- good value in winter”
text:
Stayed on the 4th floor facing the circle in early December. Price was very low (104 with AAA) but it is winter. 
Rooms were huge-walk in closet, queen bed, living room area and kitchen. I liked the shampoo/conditioner/soap pump in the shower, cute touch. As some mentioned you do hear sirens occasionally, I think i might have been woken up once or twice but not a huge deal for me. Certainly not something you hear the whole time. 
Staff was super friendly and always said hi and opened the doors for us. 
The only less than stellar thing is the location.. For sight seeing tourists like us (who make the mistake of going to cold cities in the winter:) ), its too far to walk in the cold to downtown/museums/places to eat. We took cabs everywhere we went which got a little pricey. Any other time of year would be fine though AND the cabs are affordable (and so much more friendly then the Boston cabs i'm used to). Honestly what you lose in proximity you gain in value( all the hotels i saw downtown were super fancy looking). Its about a 15-20 minute walk to downtown georgetown also which is cute and has restaurants and fancy shops. You can walk to the Lincoln monument also (15 minutes). 
Overall, a great stay!

title: “Business Travel”
text:
The hotel is very nice and has been redone even though it is an older property.
The hotel staff was extremely helpful and it was clear they wanted to make my staff very good. Someone had smoked in my room (non-smoking rm) and I told the front desk because I didn't want to get charged for smoking in the room. They were immediately responsive. However, a maid had left a dirty rag on the counter and when they asked I told them. They said it wasn't what you would expect from a Four Seasons and upgraded me to an Executive Suite, including a note, wine and candy. I wasn't even complaining. I just didn't want to pay a smoking fee but they way they handled the problem will make me a Four Seasons Customer again. In fact we have reserved the Four Seasons for my step son's upcoming wedding. Management was extremely good!

title: “Disappointed”
text: Stayed there over a busy holiday period. Badly understaffed, hotel was sold out and service was terrible everywhere. Breakfast line was too long everyday, Happy Hour was not happy at all, again long lines. Even check in was delayed due to severe understaffing. That a hotel that charges such an inflated price provide such bad service is not excusable. Great downtown location, poor service. will look elsewhere next time.

title: “Not a winner”
text:
This property feels like a shopping mall. We had a hard time even finding where to check-in. The rooms were average. The views from the room were beautiful. Its location is great for sightseeing and is a few minutes drive from the airport. There is a Starbucks inside but the line is always long. They do have a pool and a hot tub but you feel like you are in a spaceship while swimming. 
The rooms are average and the property overall is just strange.

title: “Would go back in a heartbeat!”
text:
Picked up the Hotel Palomar thru Priceline and what a surprise. Very pleasant greeting at the door and the front desk and the lobby was small but nicely decorated.
Our room, on the sith floor, was very well furnished with a nice mix of textures and colors and a very comfortable bed. I would definitely go back to this boutique hotel and pay the standard rate. 
It's also located about 1 block from the cable car turnaroud (and BART station) on Market Street. This also puts it about 3 blocks south of Union Square and one block north of the Moscone Center.

title: “Good business hotel close to the airport”
text: The staff at the hotel is very friendly and helpful. They are knowledgeable about the local area and quick to respond to any questions. The facilities themselves are a bit dated and a refresh is needed. Rooms are clean and well provisioned.

title: “Some security concerns, plus limited choices provided with the complimentary breakfast”
text:
I have stayed there several times. Very clean. Convenient location. Quiet. The staff is accommodating. I have a concern about the security, as the lobby was not manned at all times. While this area of Philadelphia is relatively safe, it is unrealistic to leave the lobby unmonitored. 
The breakfast is two tiered: a complimentary breakfast and one cooked to order. The complimentary breakfast does not provide boxed cereal, oatmeal, hard-boiled eggs, yogurt, orange juice or hot tea. It provides coffee, bagels, sweet rolls and fruit. I did not observe anyone making use of the a la carte breakfast but perhaps that is more likely to be seen on the weekends. I believe that the hotel should be able to provide hot tea, boxed cereals, yogurt and hard-boiled eggs as part of the complimentary breakfast. Guests shouldn't have to venture elsewhere for a reasonable choice at breakfast.

title: “Impressive!”
text:
I stayed at this hotel while traveling on business. Thankfully I didn't have a car, because I'm not entirely sure where I would have put it (they probably had a parking garage that I didn't see). The hotel staff was undeniably professional at every opportunity, and the lobby was very upscale.
The hotel provides free wifi and a fitness center, along with a decent (albeit pricy) continental breakfast. The room was comfortable and clean, with an overhead shower (see picture).
I probably would have not picked this hotel on my own just based on price, but as my company arranged the stay, I definitely felt that the experience was worth the value paid for the stay. One nice thing they did was run to the end of the street and flag a taxi when I needed to go anywhere.

title: “We Just Loved the Alexis!!!”
text:
We stayed three nights prior to getting on an Alaska cruise and choose the Alexis for its tremendous location, uniqueness, and overall charm. We were not let down one bit during the three nights we stayed there.
Upon arrival, we were immediately upgraded to room 419; the John Lennon Suite. It was great. The entire hotel has wireless free wireless internet, a tremendous amenity. The fitness center is just down the hall; super. The staff could not be nicer and more pleasant. Also, the concerns we had about noise from reading the reviews never surfaced and we all slept like babies for the three nights we were there. 
What truly makes the Alexis special is its location. Go out the hotel and turn left and a few blocks away is Pikes Place Market. Turn right and another few blocks is Pioneer Square. Go down the hill and another few blocks is the Waterfront. A short cab ride is either downtown or Seattle Center. A car would be a tremendous trouble and completely unnecessary.
In total, a great hotel for either the business or weekend getaway. We highly recommend

title: “Great place to stay downtown Los Angeles!”
text:
We really enjoyed our stay at the Hilton Checkers.
The rooms are SOMEWHAT small, however, more than adequate for a KING size bed, a possibly 42" flat screen TV (could be bigger, but that's my estimated guess of the size), a desk, closet and a bathroom. So don't be put off!! 
We had a great stay, with a very comfortable king size bed on the 12th story.
The roof top pool and gym are adequate, not in the sun enough, but you can't have everything!
The front desk staff were more than helpful, when asked for directions to a local shopping center, we phoned down and they said to pick up the directions when we are leaving.
Well the lady at the desk typed out the directions and had them printed out for us!
It was a very welcoming, comfortable stay. I got a very good deal through priceline, and was still treated as if we were returning guests.
The only gripe would be about the parking. BUT having been in LA for two weeks, this is normal and not beyond reason with what other hotels charge from downtown to Santa Monica. It is $40/ Night to valet park your car, there is no self parking.
HOWEVER, there is a park and lock about 4 blocks away, and it is $10 for the night, we parked at 1am, and felt secure to walk to the hotel. However it is not come and go, but I would doubt it would amount to $40 for the night.
If you happen to be there on a Sunday, you can park on the street next to the hotel (only 2 slots and a few more the next blocks) for free until 8am monday morning.
Besides the parking, which isn't unusual for Los Angeles, this Hilton was very comfortable and welcoming, would stay here again.

title: “my home away from home”
text: i just got back from my 2nd stay at the Hotel Zaza in Houston. From the moment i walked into the hotel i immediately relaxed. The hotel is gorgeous, the rooms great, the food amazing and the spa heavenly. Soon after my arrival i saw Justin and Rida the amazing hotel Concierge's who have gone above and beyond what i have found in any other hotel. Luckily for them i didnt have them search for spin classes for me to take but i was offered. But both of them do anything to ensure an enjoyable stay at Zaza. When i wasnt relaxing at the pool (which on the weekends is a fun scene but very classy ) i found myself at The Monarch Bar/Restaurant which has amazing food and drinks and awesome staff too many to name but i have to mention Travis and Gideon. All i can say is i hope they open one in New York soon but in the meantime i am going to go look at my calendar and see when the next time i can get back to the hotel Zaza in Houston is.

title: “Awesome stay”
text:
I stayed at the Revere with my nine year old twins who are seasoned travelers. The staff was lovely. A complimentary dessert was sent to my children the first night along with a complimentary breakfast.
The room was beautiful and roomly. It was also close to Boston Common and the T. What more could you ask for?

title: “Fantastic hotel that takes you back to another era”
text:
If you love the "Thin Man" movies of the 1930s, you'll love the Carlyle. It opened in 1930 as a fabulous uppercrust residential hotel (much like the one where the fictional Nick and Nora lived) and still retains a lot of the original atmosphere. 
This is probably the only hotel left in NYC that still has elevator operators. The service is outstanding and friendly. Bemelman's Bar is a not-to-be-missed experience for anyone who likes classic places. You can sit and watch a lot of fascinating people while you drink your admittedly expensive but excellent cocktails, enjoy the delicious (free) bar snacks and listen to a live pianist playing jazz standards.
If you can afford it, get a suite here, as we did (for $805 per night including daily room service breakfast, which wasn't much more than we'd have paid for a standard room at other high-end NYC hotels that weekend). The suites really give you a vintage residental feeling. They are very spacious and nicely decorated in an old money, slightly shabby chic way, with hardwood floors, antique furniture and carpets. The beds are extremely comfortable. It's a bit like staying at a rich aunt's house.
Our suite had a tiny kitchenette in addition to the 1 1/2 baths. (I couldn't help but think of Nora "offering" to make scrambled eggs -- watch the movies and you'll get the joke.) It is true that the "master" bath in our suite was tiny, because the hotel is over 75 years old and they've kept the original architectural footprint. It didn't bother us, since the bathroom was in excellent shape and had been updated with stone tile and a jetted tub.
The hotel restaurant is very good and the "Ladies Who Lunch" special 2-course menu offered on weekdays is a value at $24. I recommend the carrot-ginger soup and the salmon with black lentils - yum.
If you have a strong preference for everything brand-new and shiny, this is not the place for you. If you need a huge spa-like bathroom, look elsewhere. Looking for a trendy bar? Not here. 
However, if you'd like a taste of a more genteel (but not stuffy) era, you can't find much better than the Carlyle.

title: “Three rooms later...I am finally happy !!!”
text: Travelling with a young family there are a couple of things we look for, space, comfort, location and friendly service. First, I need to thank the amazing staff at James for taking such great care of us, especially Julie, James, Sara, Jason, also the maintenance electrician and the great staff who cleaned our rooms. We checked in July 1st, got room 1621, King Loft room. My boys were so excited that they had their own quarters and a projection tv to boot. They had movies that we could borrow and it was great, only problem, I did not sleep the whole night because the A/C was really noisy. The next morning they explained that this is the newer units and it's set to come on when the temperature is a certain degrees. Julie asked if I would like to go into a Deluxe Double room in which the AC units were quieter (I should have listened to her). I didn't want my boys to be disappointed and thought it would be fine to go into another room with a smaller AC. Room 1721 provided to be the solution, so I thought. The second night, we moved into this room, same, King Loft. The room was warmer but a lot quieter and bearable, I thought YES, I am happy...not !!! For the third night, the temperature in Chicago reached 103'f and my room was a crazy 83'f. I didn't sleep the whole night. The kids slept in their underwears only, we had a fan sent up, but my husband and I couldn't sleep at all. Fourth day, morning, I spoke to Sara and told her, I can't do it for another night, downgrade my room...just need good AC room. I packed up all my stuff and told them they can move it while I am out. By the time we returned from an afternoon at the Field Museum(we were suppose to go the Shedd too, but the electricity went out there) all our stuff had been moved to room 1114. The room is perfected !!! Not as luxurious in space but AC is great. I am writing this review on our last night here. The hotel is located in an ideal location to shopping and dining. I read other reviews where they said the hotel is this or that, but I have to say that this hotel has two things I appreciate service and the staffs willingness to make their customer's happy !!! I would definitely come back...but maybe not in July.

title: “Beatiful room and view! Friendly Staff”
text:
I loved my stay at the Baltimore Hyatt. 
Nea checked me in and gave me an absolutely stunning room with windows on three sides. I wished I could have stayed in my room the whole time! She also suggested I join the Hyatt's reward program to get free internet, which was very helpful since I was there for about a week. 
Jesse was the greatest from the bell staff, he was so friendly and helpful! He certainly is an asset to the Hyatt. 
Hotel was in a great location. 
I wasn't impressed with housekeeping so much though, I had specifically left a note asking the housekeeper to not change the towels (trying to save the environment one towel at a time) but on the fourth night of my stay I asked to have my sheets changed, and she didn't, so I asked again the next day and they still didn't get changed. It didn't make sense to me that on my last night I would finally have clean sheets. It doesn't appear that the hotel has a "green program". The environment is a big issue and hotels should be doing their part. I would really like to see the Hyatt adopt a program like that.

title: “Excellent hotel, top notch staff, and great location”
text: Large, clean, fancy rooms and bathrooms. Friendly, efficient staff. Quiet escape in the middle of NYC. Centrally located within walking distance to Times Square, Central Park, Museum Of Modern Art, 5th Avenue shopping and dining, etc. Any issues we had (which were minor) were handled immediately and efficiently by a friendly staff).

title: “Beautiful classic hotel! Relive the grandeur of old!”
text:
While we had some concerns based on other reviews, the appeal of staying at a classic historical treasure won out. And we weren't disappointed!
If you stay here, make sure you slow down and take a moment to enjoy the beauty. The most obvious is the main lobby with the gorgeous mural on the ceiling. But all around you are smaller, more subtle works of art - various statutes, paintings, ornate fixtures, and ornate trim all over the place, inside and out. 
We had a room on the top floor with a private elevator that only went to the top 2 floors (and the fitness center, I believe). So there were no long lines and not stops at all 23 floors. 
Our room on the executive level had two beds, two bathrooms and was very large. Everything was in great condition and clean. Even the rooms had touches of elegance - pay attention to the details everywhere, even on the lamps. We did not hear any noise from neighboring rooms at all. 
The executive lounge was above average for a Hilton. Don't miss the original recipe brownie created right here at the Palmer House for dessert!
While the hotel has been completely renovated, if you want a super-modern experience, go someplace else. But if you want to experience history in luxurious (for the day) setting, with all the modern conveniences thrown in - this is the place! Make sure you check out the hotel's website (not the Hilton one) to get the history before you go.

title: “Great place to stay for the Nike Women's Marathon”
text: Wonderful location. Close to Union Square. On race day all I had to do was role out of bed and my pace corral was at the hotel! Close to all night diner, good restaurants, Starbucks, trolleys and shopping. had a suite with two baths so we could be with our kids but not BE with our kids. Great price and nice staff. Great minibar!

title: “Comfortable Hotel in nice Dupont Circle area”
text: Attended a conference and found the staff to be friendly. The hotel lobby while cute was comfortable and with wireless connection. Because the weather was cold, the outdoor pool was not available for use. Food served in the restaurant was good and overall experience was positive. Will be back.

title: “If you like being robbed and lied to, come here.”
text: Never have I had a worse hotel experience, not even in a hostel: 1. Housekeeper stole a pair of jeans and a t-shirt. Three front desk people did nothing to retrieve the items. The lying hotel manager said he would refund a night's stay but never did. 2. When we arrived, the front desk placed us in a room below ground level with a view of the underside of cars and said nothing else was available. When my companion complained, a room was suddenly--miraculously--available on the top floor. 3. The building is at an angle toward a busy street where sirens scream during the night. The hotel has no quiet side. The windows are not soundproofed. Even with my earplugs in, it was impossible to sleep well. My companion who usually sleeps like a log was awakened repeatedly. Spend your money wisely elsewhere! I wish I had.

title: “Great girls getaway!”
text: Love this space. My friend and I have gone several times. We just went in June and are going back in November. The staff is very nice and the food is great and very healthy. The spa is never crowded, they have plenty of common space to accomodate the few rooms that they have. We love the excersize class and speakers. You will not want to leave. Don't go in January as they drain the lake.

title: “Best Barista!”
text: I have been to this hotel twice now for a work conference. The hotel is nice and clean and the staff was generally helpful and pleasant. In particular I need to mention Tia, the barista at the Starbucks in the Lobby. I am a 'bux addict so the cafe's presence alone was a plus for me. However, Tia really made the trip great. After a much longer than expected flight I groggily ordered a latte before I even checked in. As most baristas do, Tia asked for my name to write on the cup. She was smiling and very personable. The next morning I headed down for my morning fix. I was a little grumpy thinking of all I needed to do/see during the conference, how to keep up remotely with my normal work responsibilities, and also coping with the guilt of being away from my family. I ran into Tia on the way in the lobby. She gave me a big smile and a genuine "Good Morning Jenn!" Most employees put their head down when they are not behind the counter so Tia's attitude was a very pleasant surprise. I'm sure she doesn't realize how that alone set a much different tone for my day than I had initially started out with, and I am thankful for her kindness and smile. So if you find yourself here and see Tia, throw her some tips because she definitely deserves the love!

author.location: Center Moriches, New York, United States

title: “Bed Bugs Bed Bugs”
text:
We came to Columbus for the Softball World Series, on the weekend of September 5th. Working two jobs Thursday night I was exhausted after the long drive. Assuming everyone in Ohio has the same health dept. codes as far as sanatizing and disinfecting as Michigan was my WORST mistake. We were only at the room for a max of two hours after our softball banquet, to sleep and then we would be gone all day the following day. 
Lord do I wish I would have found this website before bringing bedbugs back to my home. All four girls that stayed in our room didnt see any visable signs of bedbugs but after many hours of cleaning and researching they are sly little bugs that hide! Needless to say I called for a manager last night and was told "Raju" was out til 9am today. 
My first response was anger but now I am at a loss these are by far the worst type of pests I have ever dealt with or heard of. If anyone has any legal information please contact me. This is ridiculous and I have already spent 150+ and now am looking into an exterminator. I have contacted the health department and was advised to seek legal representation. 
I wouldnt send my worst enemy to this dump, not to mention there was a crack pipe found in one of my teamates rooms too!!

title: “Doubletree hotel in Westminster”
text: We have stayed at the Doubletree Hotel in Westminster almost a dozen times in the past two years. The service has been wonderful, the rooms are clean, and the hotel is reasonably priced. We will continue to stay there when we are in Denver.

title: “Great Hotel Though a Little Expensive”
text:
My girlfriend and I booked this hotel from Expedia for the night for £85, it was somewhat last minute so I didn't mind paying a little extra to stay somewhere nice.
Literally 30 seconds walk from the Stock Exchange the reception might seem a little unprepossessing due to the small area, but the staff were friendly and helpful.
We had paid for a standard room, but then as we searched for our room, found it was in fact the executive suite! Therefore it makes it very difficult to rate the quality of a standard room as this was a large corner room with great views, nice bathroom, supremely comfortable bed and large seating area - both with large HD tvs.
The location is obviously a little distant from Midtown, but the Subway is only a minutes walk at most. All in all if you can get a deal it's worth coming.

title: “Turning into a dump.”
text: I used to love this hotel but now it is turning into a dump. Besides taking cold showers and no apology and no explanation except "we are working on it", the hotel has a serious mold and plumbing smell problem. Not sure if they had a flood and didn't fix it properly, but it's bad. I moved to three different rooms and finally the last didn't have the odor but it was so deep into the carpet dirty -- it was unthinkable for a hotel charging over $ 200 a night. This hotel has a great location and for some reason they are NOT putting money into replacing wallpaper or carpets. My guess is that they are going to run it into the ground and then start all over again. The housekeeping dept. is in need of some serious training about what is clean. I

title: “Good location base”
text: We resisted advise to stay in the heart of Times Square & really enjoyed the location of the Blakely. It was convenient to the theatre, Central Park, TOTR, & the subway entrance.

title: “Boutique Hotel Close to Union Square”
text:
This is a small 8-floor hotel only 2 blocks from the heart of Union Square shops. I chose a junior suite which had a separate small bedroom (with tv) and a living room (also with a tv) as well as a shower/bathtub bathroom done in white marble. Pretty much everything in the room was virtually spotless. The king size bed was very comfortable and clean. The living room had a loveseat and arm chair that were both comfortable to sit in and a glass top dining table where I was able to get some work done - their wi-fi is free throughout the entire hotel. There is also an outdoor area on the 3rd floor where you can apparently get coffee, smoke, read or go jogging too. The hotel offers room service through their Japanese restaurant in the lobby-although it closes on Sunday nights. The front desk staff was also helpful and friendly enough. The Union Square location is great for avid shoppers and theater goers, although others might find the area a bit dull, especially on weekends. 
If you decide to stay here make sure to ask about the "donation" you'll be making to some Asian Women's Center, which is a $1/per day donation that will be added to your bill. I'm sure they mentioned this to me and I just forgot or something...

title: “Great staff, but overrated ranking”
text:
This hotel is a great example of how different types of hotels appeal to different types of people. If you are a family with lots of kids who would sacrifice room quality for quantity (size), the Magic Castle is perfect for you. If you don't have kids, you may be disappointed in the quality of the rooms.
The staff at the Magic Castle is the best I have ever seen in the US. They go out of their way to smile, assist, and otherwise be polite. As an example, I asked for directions to NBC studios, and they promptly looked up the best route on mapquest.com, and gave me the printout, while concurrently advising me of the best / worst times to drive. Unlike other hotels that have a good staff, at the Magic Castle they seem very sincere. They deserve the oft-mentioned recognition. However, there is one downside: the check-in counter is very narrow (as is the front entrance), so they can only serve one person at a time...when they try to accommodate 2 guests, it becomes quite chaotic. 
The location is also excellent. Its one long block off of Hollywood Blvd, so its easy to walk there. 
The room comes with free WiFi and the 'free mini-bar' was also a nice touch. The breakfast may not fill up some people, but I was personally happy with it. 
I had a suite and the room was huge--much more than my wife and I needed. It would be great for kids. Unfortunately, the bathroom was very small, with peeling paint and tiles and an unintentional retro look of the 70's. The beds, carpeting, and furniture looked like it was several decades old, though the bedding was excellent and the downturn service--complete with tomorrow's temperature and soft music on the new stereo--was very nice. Sadly, it seems lost on the tiny TV and cheap (thin and harsh) towels...the plusses and the minuses cancel each other out. 
There was one other major disappointment with this room. The first was noise. It may be far enough from Hollywood Blvd to not hear anything there, but if you're on the ground floor with a room on Franklin Ave, good luck trying to sleep unless you turn up the tiny AC unit and drown everything out with white noise. Trucks seem to rumble on Franklin all night long, and you can hear every footstep in the room above you. I would have switched rooms but I also knew the hotel was full during my stay, so I didn't bother. As comfortable as the bedding was, it was hard to sleep with all the racket.
If my wife and I return with our kids, we would definitely stay here again--there's lots of room for them to run around, and the cheapness of the room will alleviate any fears of their misbehavior. Based on this scenario, I could see them as being the best that LA has to offer. But would I return without them? I am sorry, but I could not recommend it. And having stayed in several other hotels in LA before, I can't quite fathom how its #1 overall. 
Respectfully submitted.

title: “Awful Motel, Awful area, Avoid”
text: We booked this for one night before flying. The area was so bad we had to put a chair behind the door in case anyone tried to get in! Gangsters pulling up in the carpark all night with ghetto blasters at full pelt. My husband went out to get a pizza and was accosted by hookers. We stayed in the room all night as we were scared to go out. Would avoid it at all costs and pay a bit more to be safe. The motel even charged our credit card twice.

title: “Great hotel - great location”
text:
The hotel was beautiful, the staff was attentive. Our room was very clean.
We could walk to shopping, and the area was not too busy to do so.

title: “memorial day weekend”
text: I booked a DELUXE KING....it was a terrible room, very small for their "now we're talking" deluxe. Come on..and what are they talking about the Renovated? The bathroom was horrible...terrible lighting, scratchy towels, didn't look DELUXE TO ME! Old bathroom from the sixties, and NOTHING Is the room was luxury for the price. I beat hotel that should be ashamed in charging what they do...a farce....the photos seem to reveal that the deluxe were way better than supreme....I cannot imagine...MEDIoCRE...d grade hotel...Will never return...too many options. DON"T WASTE YOUR MONEY!

title: “Good hotel at a very good price in LA”
text: Easy to find. Good price. Pleasant room. Did not hear the airport at all. Good room service. Have to valet park is the only slight negative, but they were very fast at getting the car. It was always waiting for us by the time we got to the entrance.

title: “Great Location!”
text:
I had the privilege of staying at the Marriott Copley Place during a recent conference I was attending. The hotel was fantastic. It was very in the perfect location. It was attached to a glamorous mall with superior stores, i.e. Coach, Tiffany and Co, Lagoste, etc. The mall was right across the street from the train station and the hotel was near a lot of restaurants and bars.
The hotel lobby was clean and the staff was top notch. The room was nice and big and the bed was unbelievable. I was upset every morning when I had to get up to attend the meetings I was there for. What I loved was the hotel was full of professionals and no matter what time of day it was the hotel was always busy.
Champions sports bar located in the hotel has some great drinks and the prices are not to bad. The hotel's parking rates and valet rates will surely hurt your pocket but since I arrived to Boston via train and the hotel was across the street that did not play a role in my stay.
Furthermore the conference room we were in (Regis room) was very comfortable and nice as well.
I definitely recommend this hotel to anyone needing to do some business in the Boston area and for those who can afford a little more expensive hotel for recreation purposes.

title: “Wonderful Boutique Hotel”
text:
This is the best place to stay in Boston if you want a really great location, a cool environment in your room and great customer service. We are from Chicago and when we travel, we are very picky about accomodations and service. XV Beacon meets our needs in every area. On the last trip, we had originally only booked 1 night, but a snow/rain storm came in a shut the airport down so we needed to extend our stay another night. The front desk person, Owen, politely informed us that they were actually booked for that extra night, but that he would work with reservations to get us on a waiting list and would let us know as soon as possible if they could manage to extend our stay. In just a few hours, Kate called our room to let us know that they were indeed able to extend our stay and we didn't have to switch rooms either! This was on top of what Owen had already done earlier in the day by getting us into our room well before check-in, in an upgraded room no less, because we needed to access the internet for business purposes. The last night we were there, we decided to go out to dinner and when we walked out of the hotel and asked the doorman to hail us a taxi, he suggested we let, Mark, the driver of the hotel car, take us where we needed to go. It was perfect. We probably tipped him more than we would have paid for a taxi, but it was worth the convenience. When we were done with dinner, we called him and he came and picked us up too. After a long, stressful week spent on the cape moving stuff into a truck...that ended up getting extended because our vehicle broke down...then a drive to Boston to fly home only to have a storm further delay our return home, the extra night and pampering at XV Beacon helped us to decompress and enjoy a couple of days! Thanks for everything!! We will be back!!
Amy and Rick

text: no comments made by my choice, survey sucks when it will not let you continue when you do not want to make a comment. bery bad programming by survey authors, Hotel staff is great, survey staff leaves a lof to be desired.

title: “good location, poor restaurant”
text:
i just visit new york city for a bussines trip, i had a very good staying at this hotel, the location is perfect , the staff very friendly, and the rooms are great .
the only place i won't visit again is the restaurant, the food is very poor and the actitud of the waiter just awful.

title: “fantastic location, bad service”
text: upon arriving at the wellington hotel we were greeted by a load of teenagers behind reception and from there were told that somebody had overstayed their stay and there was no rooms avaliable! you can immagine after a 8 hour flight that we were obviously not impressed but after reading previous reviews it was kinda expected and heard of before. luckily they said their was a room avaliable in a hotel around the corner and paid for us to stay the night there instead which the very friendly bellboy carried our suitcases and showed us the way. the hotel was called the blakley and we were over the moon when arriving and hoped that the wellington was just as nice! the next day we had to wait till 3 pm to check in at the wellington but were able to leave are suitcases whilst we explored. when we finally arrived at our room we were not impressed especially after putting us up in such luxery! the rooms are very basic and have jsut the essentiallys apart from plugs which there was on 1 of and the bathrooms are tiny!!.. but even after all of the negatives i have listed i would no doubt go back, it is situated in the most perfect position and is perfect for a base just aslong as you dont spend much time in the hotel..which in new york you dont tend to do! and dont expect to much! one other note take extra money for tiping! you have to tip absoloutly everyone and everything

title: “Great location, room, service”
text: The Michelangelo was perfect for us. This was an anniversary trip, and we wanted a nice place in mid-town Manhattan. The room was comfortable and reasonably quiet (for 51st St.), service was excellent, concierge suggestions were perfect, and the location was great. This is at 51st and 7th, just off Broadway, walking distance from plays, jazz, museums, shopping, Rockefeller Center, Central Park, Times Square, all the things that NYC visitors need.

title: “Best Hotel”
text:
I stayed at the Benjamin over the 4th of July and it was fabulous. 
Cannot say enough about the staff - they were wonderful. The rooms were nice, clean, large and centrally located (midtown). The staff was superb! Will stay again, no question!

title: “Good if you get it at the right price”
text:
Stayed here for business recently - and didn't manage to get a cheap price, but was late booking.
It is a very historic hotel right in the middle of the loop area of downtown Chicago -very well placed for most of the big attractions. 
The foyer is fantastic, and you can feel the history in the walls - but the bedrooms are pretty ordinary for those who pay the full price.
There is very limited wifi and it is expensive (although the starbucks across the street (not the one in the hotel) has got free access!

title: “Weird Location at a Great Price”
text: Our experience was okay, but the hotel was out of town, located on a dark street. Breakfast was limited and not too tasty. Front desk was left unattended several times. Wireless did not work.

title: “Oasis within the City”
text:
I was looking for a central located hotel in DC and like to avoid chain hotel.
This hotel takes you an era of hotels long forgotten; the service is superb from the moment you check in.
The rooms as tastefully decorated and have to say my bed was just so perfect I got a great night sleeps.
