The other beauty is to be able to have breakfast which is served, a true luxury these days. Sitting watching the world go by while you eat is a great way to start the day. The restaurant staffs are very friendly and the food is fresh and sets the day off perfect.

title: “No cell reception or Internet in rooms”
text:
We paid $249 a night for 2 beds, 2 adults&1child. Subway location great! Shower great! Bed super comfy! Look beyond that, my daughter lost a part to a toy so I was under the bed and dresser FILTHY!!!
Manhattan Diner just down the street amazing food And service!
Room very outdated, a/c worked ! 
One ice machine on 11 th floor . 
A little pricy for me, especially since we just needed it to sleep and shower. Neighbor hood very safe feeling , staff very friendly , bed comfy and very refreshing shower! My cellphone did not work in the room and no wifi in the room , ok in lobby, hotels computers you pay to use.

title: “San Diego Chic”
text:
I loved the Pearl! It seemed to channel a very Palm Springs/West Hollywood vibe. 
The restaurant was definitely the highlight of my short stay, the risotto was some of the best I've ever had. 
The salt water pool was always heated, although the weather in San Diego was very nice.
The staff was very polite and more than happy to share their ideas for the best sights in San Diego.

title: “What a lovely Hotel in a lovely City!”
text:
What a lovely hotel! The rooms were large and very well decorated. The Four-Poster beds very nice. Probably the best shower I have had in any hotel ever!.
Service was excellent! The Clerks were all very helpful. The cleaning staff were non-english speaking for the most part, but still understood what our needs were.
The Madrid dining room was quite nice!. We enjoyed breakfast buffets and menue items as well.
We found the hotel just a few blocks from the acclaimed Riverwalk. We were actually close to many attractions including the Alamo!.
We spent a great week there and the rates were very good!

title: “Nice Place to Stay in NYC”
text:
My husband and I spent Labor Day weekend in NYC staying at the Radisson. It was our 4th stay in New York and this was one of the nicer hotels. It's out of the Time Square hustle and bustle (I don't care for Time Square), but still centrally located. It was a 3 block walk to the subway which we rode for the first time. We did a tour of Central Park and Rockefeller Center which we walked to. We also saw 2 Broadway plays within easy walking distance. We did take the subway down to our tour of the Brooklyn Bridge and the Chelsea High Line Tour.
Our room was on the 22nd floor and was very quiet and clean. It was small, but had a nice size closet and the bathroom was adequate. After all, you're in New York. How much time will you spend in your room? The bed was really comfortable also.
We came in early and they did store our luggage with a charge of $2.00. The bellhop walked us out to the curb and got our taxi for us on the way back to the airport.
A word about the the establishments next door. Raffles is nice but you can get the same breakfast at a deli on Lexington and 52nd for half the price. There is a bar called Tienna (or something similar) which we thought was the hotel bar. We went in for a draft beer about 5:00 and they charged $11 each for the beer, plus tax and a $3.45 service charge. Two draft beers cost nearly $28.00. There are other places around where a happy hour beer is $4.00.

title: “Great hotel, Great Locationl”
text: My overall experience was great! The staff was more than helpful. We stayed in a Serene King room. The rooms were average size for a king hotel room. The beds were excellent. The bathroom was on the small size but the shower was larger than a hotel shower and very unique. The bathroom was open to the bedroom but there was a nice curtain to cover the window. The view was of an office building but there were large floor to celing windows that I really liked. We only had a drink in the bar-on the first floor (kinda weird you walk into the restarurant) it was OK. The Dana is in walking distance from many great bars and resturants. I booked online and got a "weekend package" which included parking which is usually $40+ a night and a $50 dollar fuel card, which paid for all of my gas to get to chicago and back. The room only came out to being $303. If I could get a deal like this again I will be back! It was a great experience

title: “Excellent and upscale hotel and conference center”
text: This hotel's staff have been trained to the ultimate in customer service and this hotel truly encompasses the vision of JW Marriott. The common areas are immaculately clean and hospitable and the rooms have been cleaned to an impeccable level. The bedding, and beds are comfortable and my stay was relaxing and tranquil. I would definitely stay and eat here again. I was 110% satisfied.

title: “Top Hotel”
text: Staff were very warm and friendly, rooms are exceptionally big. Location wise its very central less than two blocks from Macy's, five blocks from Grand Central Station/Times Square so really close to the hustle and bustle if you wanted to shop it was the ideal location. The checkin girl was friendly she asked was there a special occasion and my partner told her that is was my birthday, so whilst settling in to our room we got a knock on the door and we got a treat as a compliment from the hotel.

title: “A good choice when visiting New York City”
text: I have had the pleasure of staying at the East Side Marriott on various occasions. Everyone I had the opportunity to interact with was eager to assist me and enthusiastic in doing so. This hotel is located away from the heavily transited Times Sq, but close enough if you wish to walk towards that area. The rooms are a bit small in sq footage and some street noise should be expected -- especially when staying in low floors. Stay here you won't regret it!

title: “Mixed experiences at the Hudson”
text: Whilst there were good points about this hotel, I have to say I can see where many of the negative comments posted are coming from. I think it depends on whether the beautiful design makes you more forgiving of other issues. We stayed here because we wanted a unique NYC experience and appreciate good design (you can stay at a Hilton in any city after all), and we did get that and enjoy our stay. This was definitely a plus point, it looked great. We were lucky with our room too as had upgraded to a superior room after reading reviews, so we has plenty of space, it was a corner room so plenty of windows and light, clean, cool design and a suprisingly decent sized bathroom (and high enough up on 17th floor to avoid being disturbed by the noisy bar). Ask for room 1700 if you want to be certain of a decent room!! The bar looked great and was always busy, but we quickly discovered that this was a beautiful place for pretentious, unfriendly people(both staff and residents!), so sought out more down to earth places to spend our money and didnt really take full advantage of the communal areas. It would have been nice if someone had told us (even apologised) for the sky terrace being closed for renovation, as this had been a factor in our choosing to stay here: instead when we asked, we were told 'you know what, its closed' - well thanks for the info! Whilst some staff were friendly and helpful, I have to say that generally that wasn't the case and there was a definite feeling that we ought to consider ourslves lucky to be staying there rather than the other way round. Location on the edge of the fantastic central park , the amazing whole foods market in the Time Warner centre and subway opposite a real plus (it was easy to explore the whole of manhattan using the subway, though if you intend to spend you time discovering the rather more interesting and 'real' downtown, you might consider staying south of midtown). Overall, we were happy with our room and impressed by the design, but the snobby vibe meant that really we didnt fully take advantage (or want to) of the facilities it had to offer. An interesting place with not-so interesting people. I enjoyed the stay but not sure I'd go back.

title: “Clean, quiet, friendly (and a great bed)”
text:
Very quiet for a mid-town location. The rooms are reasonable sized and the beds are very comfortable. 
What particularly impressed me was that when left a shopping bag with expensive shoes/handbags at night next to the computer / lobby area, the next day the staff returned (with all the contents) to us!
Frankly, I wasn't optimistic but was very impressed by the honesty of the staff. 
The LCD TV is nice (but no HD).

title: “Lost my reservation and then were rude...”
text:
Short version of my story:
I reserved room for a conference back in July (for a Oct/Nov conference) and received confirmation email the week before my stay confirming my stay 10/30-11/3.
When I arrived on 10/30, I was told that my reservation was cancelled. I asked why it was cancelled because I did not contact them. They told me that I called in early October to cancel. I NEVER did this. In addition, I showed them the email that showed reservation confirmation that I received the week before. They were completely uninterested. They told me they could give me an overflow room for ONE night (even though my reservation was for 6 nights) and then I could call the next morning to see what to do. I asked to speak with a manager to discuss how my reservation was cancelled without notifying me via phone or email, but they would not allow me to speak to anyone...very rude and condescending...My room was cramped but clean (I will give them that) but the wireless did not work in the rooms. I tried to have a drink at the bar later that night (I needed it!) and the service was horrendous. There were two bartenders yet they could not handle light bar traffic. I would never stay here again.
In short, they were rude, did not acknowledge they made a mistake and had no interest in helping me out. I am very high on Hilton Honors program because I held my destination wedding at the Nassau Bahamas resort (and booked over 100 rooms for my group). I am very disappointed and do not plan on using hilton ever again. I ended up at the Kimpton Rouge and had fabulous experience.

title: “great Marriott location in DC”
text: I have been staying at Marriotts in DC for about 10 years. The JW on Pennsylvania was my usual....until 2 years ago. They were booked and so I ended up at this Courtyard. I LOVED it. The desk staff is great (thanks Stephen for your smile all the time). The rooms have the great Renaissance bed package. It is quiet and clean. Good restaurants near by and a Whole Foods just a 10 minute walk away. Easy to catch a cab and a 10 minute walk from the Metro.

title: “Wonderful Weekend!”
text: I took my husband away for a surprise birthday weekend at Le Parker Meridien and had a wonderful time. Instead of finding a dog sitter I packed the car with our bags and 2 greyhounds and headed for the city. Upon arrival we were greated by the valet (paid extra) and at the desk I was pleasantly told that they were upgrading us to a larger room where our dogs would be happier. Our room was clean and spacious, the bed was comfortable, and the bathroom was fabulous. The hotel was a perfect location for Broadway and Central Park, as well as getting a taxi or subway. We enjoyed restaurants like The Burger Joint (in Le Parker Meridien), Calle Ocho (81st and Brodway), and Sarabeth's (40 Central Park South). I highly recommend this hotel to anyone. . .especially if you are traveling with pets.

title: “Fantastic Stay”
text:
Like many others using this site, we wondered what we had in store after reading many of the greatly contrasting reviews of Le parker Meridien and having flown home today after a fabulous week in NY we can safely say the hotel was perfect.
Admitedly there was an initial mix up when we were given keys for a standard king room not the junior suite we had booked, but this was immediately rectified on return to reception. Now the standard king looked really nice but if you can, do opt for a suite if you are staying at the hotel for a bit longer, as the additional living area gives a much more at home feel and a chance to sprawl.
Our bed was really comfortable, shower fantastic and the Syence toiletries so good I bought some to take home (never before been inclined to do so). As for air con/heating we seemed to be able to control ours and could open our window enough to let fresh air in if the room became too warm, a different experience to other guests judging by previous reviews. 
Breakfast at Norma's is a must even if it is only a one-off, it is expensive which is a shame as we drew the line at one visit! Having said that the portions are so plentiful not to mention exceptional that you will almost certainly be full until evening.
Staff were all helpful and polite with no sense of snootiness that you sometimes get in like hotels, and we felt able to come and go as if the place were home for our days in NY. As for the lifts, my partner loved the Tom and Jerry cartoons, thankfully the lifts were so fast I wasn't sent to coventry for too long ! As for waiting for the lifts to arrive, I guess they could be a bit more speedy but not so that I would raise as a concern.
Do use the pool and visit the top floor to take in the wonderful views of Central Park. Views only beaten by that of the revolving restaurant at the Mariott Marquiss on Times Square. Please don't be put off of staying here, we thought it was perfect and I would have every confidence that if things weren't right that there would be someone to help you fix whatever it is that was wrong !

title: “Fine”
text:
The hotel was fine, room was fine, clean and secure with A/C.
Staff were helpful, but I didn't really need any help.
I didn't have a car, and relied on Public transport, which is an infrequent (hourly) bus. Would have a car again in future, but for the price was just fine for me.
However, the local Starbucks, 24 hr Denny's and Mexican close by were great bonuses!

title: “Great stay”
text: We also stayed over a week for a soccer tournament. The location was close to the airport, close to the I-70 and close to Dicks Sporting fields. The staff was top-notch with Mama and Chuck's hearty breakfast and the nice manager reception every night. As for hordes of kids running wild, i think that is a bit over stated. There were lots of kids playing cards and such early in the evening but by 10 pm you could hear a pin drop. We had a great time and would reccomend to any family or team.

title: “Friendly Hotel”
text:
We arrived several hours before the official check in time and were given our room immediately. This was a great start to our 3 night stay.
For NY this was a very good sized room. The bed was very comfortable. The bathroom was modern and again a good size.
There was plenty of wardrobe hanging space and a safe in the room.
All the staff were very friendly and helpful.
The location is excellent for all the usual NY attractions. We were able to walk everywhere, from Battery Park to Central Park and everywhere in between. 
Highly recommend this hotel to anyone wishing for a good value high quality hotel.
The hotel is on East 44th Street 2 mins walk from Grand Central Station.
Tip 1: Taxi from & to the airport is now a fixed price $45 each way. This, in our opinion, is the best way to get to and from the airport as it is door to door and relatively inexpensive and you don't need to lug bags around,
Tip 2: For breakfast we took a short walk up east 42nd street to a KFC/Tim Horton (between Grand Central and TGI Fridays) and had an excellent breakfast bagel, hash brown and very large cup of coffee (and very nice too for NY standards) for $12 for 2 of us, excellent value and kept us going for the whole morning.

title: “Bring a tazer to protect yourself!!!”
text: I AM SO DISSAPOINTED IN THE Super 8 Motel chain!!! My family and I had a HORRIBLE experience where we actually feared for the safety of our family and ALL the representative had to say was that the hotel owner has the right and they support him in NOT ONLY allowing a HUGE party in the back with people coming in droves off the street but THEY ENCOURAGE him to do so!!!! I am so disgusted! My family had to go in the middle of the night to find another hotel...I only hope the motel chain investigates this because they do not understand the severity of my concerns...

title: “Decent stay in Dallas”
text: We stayed at The Magnolia while attending a wedding in the Dallas area. The staff was friendly, our room quite clean, the happy hour very nice (yes, it's only beer and wine ... which is what most hotels have during a 'happy hour'), and the breakfast quite acceptable. Yes, the elevators had an odd smell; however, I attribute it more to the humid climate and the fact they are probably not air-conditioned ... and we didn't find them all that slow. The biggest downside was that, like most hotels in large cities, the only parking at the hotel was valet parking ($24/day + tips). Another oddity ... housekeeping was quite discreet. The rooms in our party weren't made up until after 4:00 pm. if they were made up at all.

title: “good hotel, good location”
text:
We had a great time at the Fairfield Inn in Old Town. While it's not in the middle of all of the action in downtown San Diego, it's in a safe, quiet neighborhood and is very close to Old Town bars, restaurants, and cultural sites. It's also only about a half mile walk to the trolley, which can take you into downtown San Diego. The hotel is right off the freeway, which makes it very easy to get to via car. Considering the proximity to the freeway and to some bars in the area, it is very quiet. We had no trouble sleeping.
The room was clean and spacious; however, we did feel that despite having the air conditioning on all day, that the room was a bit damp. That is probably my only complaint about the hotel. The room was otherwise great-- the bed was comfortable, the blackout shades really let us sleep in when we wanted to, and the toiletries were high quality!
The staff was friendly and offered us a few suggestions about places to visit in the area. They were also kind enough to inform us that if we didn't want to pay the $15 per day parking fee for garage parking that we could park anywhere on the street for free, because there are not many parking restrictions in the area. We stayed for 3 nights and never had trouble finding a spot right next to the hotel.
The breakfast was standard continental breakfast fare. The pool was a standard hotel pool. The facade of the hotel was cute and had Old Town charm. Otherwise, it was a good stay and in line with what you would expect at a Marriott chain hotel.

title: “great hotel, great location”
text: Went for a long weekend with a lot of extended family. Hotel was in a great location, you could easily walk to the inner harbor and all the attractions and places to eat/shop. Some family members had rooms on the smoking floor which smelled awful and the hotel was great about switching rooms for them. Unless you smoke I would make sure to not book a smoking room, you will just end up with a headache from the smell. I'm actually shocked that hotels even still have smoking rooms available so lesson learned to double check. At the hotel you also have access to a private gym and pool which are awesome by the way! Anyway I would not hesitate to stay again!

title: “Loved the looks, location and service at this hotel”
text: The Hotel Contessa is located conveniently to the Riverwalk. My room was very nice, well-maintained, large and quiet. The staff was very attentive and the group that I was meeting with at the hotel appreciated the lounge area next to the bar as a good place to sit around and chat after our conference was done. I heard several compliments about that in particular in regards to using the Hotel Contessa as our meeting space. I would definitely recommend this place to anybody looking for a place to stay in San Antonio.

title: “Perfect for hotel for friends in an awesome neighborhood”
text: This hotel was great! The staff was so friendly and accommodating. The room was small (but from what we heard, every room in NY is small) but extremely clean. For 3 girls in their late 20's it was perfect location! Great bars, great food and great shopping all within walking distance. I will definitely stay here again.

title: “convenient and handy”
text: We stayed here 4 nights during a conference and loved the amenities-- all day long coffee and tea at the lobby, free internet, and warm breakfast. The suite is not big but has all we need -- refrigerator, microwave, iron, and hair blower. The room is clean, bright, and most of the time quiet. The only thing we might want to complain is the music during weekend nights. We were not sure where the music came from. It sounded like from a bar or pop in the hotel. Although we still could fall asleep with the music, I am sure it will certainly bother some light sleepers.

title: “Great Sleep”
text: Booked two rooms for a four-night business trip. We were assigned different-sized rooms on 12th floor. It was a fabulous sleep. The decor feels a bit harsh in the common parts and I didn't use anything except the wi-fi which was fine. But it was just incredibly comfortable beds, linen and pillows. The first thing my colleague and I both remarked on after the first night was this. I had a smaller corner room but it was great double-aspect windows to see the sun come up. Location is fine - overnight parking is cheaper a block down - about half price.

title: “Great hotel great location!”
text: Staying with family--2 boys ages 10 & 13. They loved the breakfast and pool. Hotel is 5 minute walk to the "T" which takes you anywhere you want to go. Great room on 9th floor with awesome city skyline view. This was our first trip to Bah-ston, but definitely not our last!!

title: “Great one night stay!”
text: We stayed here in a queen suite with our 3 children. As it was a corner room we could see the marina and the bay. The overall look of the room was just a bit dated, but we still enjoyed it. The kids loved the pool, and according to some locals it was very cool outside so we had it to ourselves! (We're from Canada and were not about to let a little cool keep us out of the water!) For the room we had, and the location, we were happy with the value. The only noise I heard was when a seagull woke me up! Will stay again when we are in the area.

title: “Awesome hotel!”
text:
I have been to NYC a number of times. This was by far the best hotel experience I have ever had in NYC. The Renaissance was so chic and polished. The staff were extremely professional, and I can't say enough about the room. The room was so beautiful and comfortable, so that I found myself not wanting to leave it. I was also amazed at how quiet the hotel was and how well insulated the walls and windows were from the noise of Times Square. 
My partner and I went for a cheaper room at the Crowne Plaza around the corner because work wan't going to pay for the room at the Renaissance for the Satuday night. We regret leaving the Renaissance and would have gladly paid the extra $40 to further enjoy the ambiance and quieteness of the Renaissance. 
This was overall an excellent hotel experience!

title: “Terrible service”
text:
The service we received when we first arrived to this hotel was just plain poor. I expected a lot more, had heard and read great reviews... but don't' be fooled. 
First, the valet. There were three of my girlfriends that stepped out of the car, not one valet person was there to hold the door open for us, not to mention, just stood there and watched us take our bags out of our car without even offering any help. 
Second, the front desk. Granted we arrived 45 minutes prior to the "formal" check in time. We actually expected our rooms to not be ready until the gal at the front desk says that she thinks it might and tells us to take a seat in the lobby. After she had helped three other people, over a period of 15 minutes, it was not THAT busy, we finally go back to her to find out status. She had forgotten that we were waiting and just THEN called to check on our rooms. Luckily our rooms were ready. 
Third, the Spa. When I first walked into the spa, i thought how cute and quaint. Not a bad setting, but the massage was horrible. I had asked my masseuse to focus on my shoulders and neck and upper back as I am highly ticklish. She must have spent 10 minutes in my much needed areas and the rest of the time had me squirming all over the table as she tried to massage my lower back and legs. Why bother to ask me if I want her to focus on an area if she's just going to ignore me? 
A decent hotel, but first impressions are often times, lasting impressions. Stay at your own risk.

title: “Awesome”
text: The Marriott Marquis is centrally located close to all the attractions you need to see when you are in San Diego. The hotel has excellent service and amenities and is highly recommended if you are planning to spend any time in San Diego.

title: “Room for improvement”
text: While the staff was very nice and helpful, we stayed in a very nice room,but our a/c did not work properly. It kept turning off. So all night we kept having to get up and reset it. Not a restful and fun night.

title: “Mixed feelings!!!!”
text: I did not check reviews before I booked this hotel and that was a mistake. A lot of the negative reviews I read, I experienced. The room was abnormally small and did have a bad smell to it. Our heater was spitting out water from the top and made a loud noise. The best part of the room was the bathroom, which was very clean and it looked to have been remodeled. I guess for the price it wasn't too bad.

title: “Great Hotel in lovely area”
text:
The Hotel is modern with great rooms. Service was also really good. We (my partner and 2 teenagers) were upgraded to executive rooms which was a nice surprise. The hotel has a nice bar, restaurant and a lovely lounge area outside with fire pits to sit around. Really stylish and a nice way to spend the evening outside. The pool looked nice but was not open yet when we were there (Easter). A nice touch is also the different flavoured waters that are for free in the lobby area.
We areally enjoyed the very pretty neighborhood with its many small restaurants with terraces, cafes and small shops. Very cool and trendy and much quieter than down town. A breath of fresh air after spending a week in Manhatten. Our 2 teenagers really enjoyed it there too. All the museums are free and also the Zoo which is worth a visit. All in all we had a fantastic time in Washington with it's great service and lovely people.

title: “Girl's night out”
text: I reserved two suites for a girl's night out birthday celebration. When we got to the hotel around 5pm, only one room was ready. We did request two double bed suites next to each other, which they were trying to accommodate. We had 6pm dinner reservations which now meant we would all need to freshen up in one room. The front desk apologized and sent up a bottle of wine and a cheese tray. I thought that was a nice gesture for our inconvenience. When we came back from dinner, the other room was ready. We missed the cocktail hour so I cannot comment on that, but we did go down for breakfast the next day, and even though the hotel was full and there were a lot of people, the lines seemed to move within reason. We opted not to have cooked to order breakfast, as that line was longer. We did the hot buffet (eggs, bacon, potatoes, pancakes) and that moved along well, with lines forming on both sides. The bed was comfortable and the sink in the bedroom was a nice feature so one could be getting ready in the bedroom and the other in the bathroom. There was a half full bottle of pop in the fridge and was obviously missed during cleaning. Other than that, the room was very comfortable for the little time we were there. We opted for the self-park and the parking lot is a bit of a maze. Look up for the signs and the hotel is near the theater. Once we got our bearings, it was not bad. Overall, I would go back and recommend this hotel.

title: “Beautiful hotel, on water close to gaslamp”
text: Stayed here to watch the 4th of July fireworks for a really good deal through local promotion. Rooms were very nice, clean and good views. Also liked there is a Fox Sports Grill on site.

title: “Hotel valet damaged our car in their garage”
text:
The hotel is unprofessionally run. The staff is rude. Few amenities for the price. No high-speed internet as advertised. 
The valet damaged our car when attempting to pull it up from their very small garage. The front passenger side was gauged causing $1600 of body repair. My wife and I communicated with the head manager who refused to admit fault and their very amateurish insurance carrier was uncooperative. We are now stuck with a $1600 repair bill.
The bottom line, you may save money on the room, but you may also have your car mangled. Don't stay in this hotel.

title: “Beautiful property with great service”
text: Spent one night at The Adolphus with my wife while attending a conference. We splurged and got a suite with a balacony. The room was clean, comfortable, and had every amenity. The public areas are elegant and the entire hotel is very clean.. Everyone we interacted with was friendly and was ready to help with any need that we had. We did not dine in any of the restaurants but did order room service for a snack that evening and breakfast in the morning. Top marks for that service and food quality as well...

title: “ok for a budget hotel”
text:
I stayed 6 nights there.
The staff is friendly and the rooms are clean.
The room was quite big for a motel .The mattress was good.
I wanted something cheap so that was fitting my budget just fine.
It is located in Hollywood so it quite convenient to run the underground.
However it is in a so so area of Hollywood where you have a lot of prostitutes at sunset so it dangerous to go out at sunset.
I found the breakfast disappointing as there was only a selection of pastries and a pot of coffee so as i wanted tea the day receptionnist told me to take water from the tap in my beaker and to put it in the micro wave and there was no milk either .
It is a good place to stay if you are on a budget .

title: “Nice hotel in a good location”
text:
We got this hotel with a good deal on Priceline, so the "value" question is tough. It seemed to me to be primarily a business hotel, but that offered no problems for my family of four using it for vacation. Despite the "stigma" of being a Priceline customer, we were given a choice of one king bed or two doubles, and our room had a river view.
The hotel was nice, the staff was courteous, etc. Even though it is a business hotel, the attached mall seems to make it an obvious pick for vacationers.
One drawback was the lack of free WiFi in the rooms -- you had to go into the lobby to get free WiFi. The parking is steep at $35 per night ($42 for valet and to be able to take your car out), so figure that into your price, but that's typical of any hotel in a city such as this.

title: “Enjoyed it very much!”
text: I paid for my room through priceline, received a king size. Everything was very nice, the room was clean, the bathroom was also clean (and big!) The beds were SOOOOOOOOOO Comfortable, i wish i could take it home. It was VERY close to the Alamo, and the riverwalk as well. Everyone was nice, the person that checked me in wasn't that personable, but he got the job done effieciently. The valet guys were awesome and everything else was pretty great. I'd go there again!

title: “Very comfortable and contemporary rooms”
text: The best part of the room is the recliner. It was a great added touch to a guestroom and made for a great workstation. The room was very spacious. I highly recommend going to the roof top bar for a drink as it offers a fantastic view of Chicago. There was nothing disappointing about this property.

title: “One of the best hotels in San Francisco”
text:
Through the years I've stayed at most of the well know hotels in San Francisco, and I would have to rate the Pan Pacific as one of the best. 
The hotel is elegant, dignified and classy, but in an understated way. 
None of the hussle and bussle you often see at some of the other large SF hotels. The service has always been top notch...from the parking attendant, bellman, front desk staff, bartender, etc....all the service employees have been wonderful. I usually ask for one of the larger king rooms on the upper floors with a view of the city. Great marble bathrooms w/separate show and bath, and a TV. Parking is expensive as is the case throughout SF.

title: “Greatest hotel entire trip!”
text: We stayed her for three days and it was absolutely amazing. De staff is so friendly and they do everything to let you feel comfortable. We travelled with our four children, age 11 and 14, and they got ice cream at the swimming pool, candy, soda and chips, as much as they wanted. So we had to temper them now and than. They even made us some coffee at the day we were leaving. The two bedroom suite was spacious, but a bit old. Some stains in the carpet and a bit noisy. Next time we'll ask for an apartment in the main building at the swimming pool, i think they are better. For us this hotel was a great experience and we hope to return someday.

title: “Amazing Hotel for a trip of a lifetime!!”
text: The Paramount hotel is an amazing hotel in NYC. The location is awesome and about 1/2 a block from the heart of Times Square. It is right in the middle of the Theater district. The decor is elegant, clean, and very modern. There is a great lobby to gather and the staff couldn't be more helpful! I would highly recommend this hotel to everyone!

title: “Amazing find!!!”
text:
I was coming in for a conference and needed to get in a day early so I took a chance and booked at the Revere a property I had never heard of .... Amazing !! I wish I could have stayed here instead of the conference hotel but logistically it would not work. 
From the champagne at check in to the amazing meal at the Rustic Kitchen the deluxe room amenities, beautiful modern decor in a spacious room, free water and wifi are always a plus!! 
You get everything older building that has been completely upgrade with modern luxury

title: “Absolute Perfection!!!”
text: I am just now booked another stay at the Palomar , I think this will be my 3rd stay. Always wonderful in every way, the staff especially.

title: “this is a very good hotel”
text: The location for our purposes was perfect---event at Lucas Stadium. Staff helpful, rooms well appointed, decor of common areas elegant but welcoming, variety of restaurants. This is a top notch hotel

title: “Good value on weekend rates, Worth checking out.”
text:
We stayed here on a weekend rate for a getaway. The room was decent with unique decor. Bed & bathroom were fine, what more do you need? Good TV and wireless internet. Hotel dates to the Depression era (I stayed here in the 1980s when it was the REALLY funky Bismarck) but has been remodeled and modernized. 
The only issue we had was the elevators...they were fast but small, and at busy times get swamped. Tip: Go behind the normal elevators and take the service elevator. It's much larger, faster, and you pop out behind the bell desk. 
The wine happy hour in the evening was a blast and the wine steward was a lot of fun. The lobby decor was funky and fun, some might find it a little strange. 
Overall the staff was quite friendly and helpful even though the hotel was very busy. Location is convenient and plenty of (typically EXPENSIVE) parking garages nearby.
We got a decent nightly rate about $110 including the rapacious Chicago hotel taxes & fees. (About 16%) True bargain hotels are getting rare in Chicago but this one is a decent value for downtown, especially on a good weekender rate.

title: “Nice stay with just a few issues”
text: Spent a week here on a business trip. Staff was very friendly and helpful. The room was extremely clean and comfy. Location isn't that great although it is fairly close to the airport. There are only fast food restaurants in the immediate area but not much else. I never really had a problem with noise although I keep my a/c or heat running constantly to help me sleep. I never had a chance to check out the pool or fitness areas but they appeared to be nice. My only issues would be with the location and very poor internet service. They advertise "high speed" but it's far from that. At best, it's slightly better than dialup which was frustrating for me when trying to take care of work issues online.

title: “Chic”
text:
I was visiting clients in the Financial District and this was the only hotel available so took it. Arrived really late at night (volcanic ash was happeing and I was coming from England) and was greeted by very friendly staff who checked me in very quickly and even managed to find a glass of wine for me (it was VERY late) as I was clearly exhausted and needing a little something as a pick-me-up.
Room was fabulous - loved the various light settings and the loft style. Was glad of slippers as the floors were wooden and would have made a huge noise.
Liked the fee snacks and the free soft drinks - just enough to tempt if needed.
Realised in the morning I had forgotten my wash bag - but literally across the road at the mini mart there was all I needed. Toiletries in the hotel were lovely.
Particularly liked the huge shower/wet room with the rainforest shower head. Beds were big and comfy and the blackout blinds worked fine for me.
Only downside (which I mentioned to the staff at the time) - as a woman i like to be able to see to put on my make up. bathroom is all black tiles (super cool to look at) and not enough light for make up. Likewise the pull-out mirror was in the darkest place in the room. can I suggest a make up mirror on the table or similar for us ladies?
Loved the communcal area and the free internet access (30 minutes max but never needed that long). Great for free teas and coffees, and wines and juice in the evening.
This hotel has a lovely style about it, feels individual and as a solo traveller I felt really safe.
Was close to the subway for going up to Times Square etc and also close enough to walk to see some of the sights.
Would I go back? Of course! Loved it!

title: “Great for families”
text:
THE GOOD: We came here for our spring break to escape the cold in Michigan. Usually we go to Florida, but my kids had never been out West, so we thought this would be fun...and it was! The best thing about the resort are all the pools. The lazy river is even bigger than I expected ! There is something for all ages at the River Ranch pool area, which is good because my kids range from ages 4-14. Each building also has its own smaller pool too, and that's where we made lots of friends. The weather was beautiful and we ended up just hanging at the resort more than we'd planned. The place was packed with families....kids running EVERYWHERE. No big deal because 3 of them were mine. If I had come for a quiet week with my husband, I would have left. There is a very peaceful adult-only pool at the fitness center that I snuck over to once. 
The room was good, but not great. Funky smell at first, but I always bring candles. It also seemed dark to me, but maybe it was our location. Since we are a family of five, it was a little tight in the suite after a while. If we were to go back, I would definitely consider upgrading to a casita. There was a little fridge, but it didn't work very well and no microwave.
THE BAD: The Hole in the Wall restaurant (yes, that is the real name). We ate there once for breakfast and once for dinner. Neither was good and it was VERY over-priced. The service was not good either. The Lantana Grille had much better food, but was even higher priced. Cocktails by the pool are $10 for a small cup and usually weak. Only once we got a good bartender.
THE UGLY: We had toilet issues from the start...it wouldn't flush correctly. Plunger man had to be called a few times. Then we had a massive overflow that wouldn't stop. Our room was flooded in a few inches of water and it took a long time for anyone to come. When a guy did show up, he was not equipped to handle the job and had to call someone else. Finally, a guy came with a wet vac and a big fan. The carpet was still soaked though (squish, squish wherever we walked) and was never actually cleaned, nor was the bathroom tile. That's just gross! We were able to move to a new room after they finally realized how bad it was. I understand that these things happen, but an apology for our inconvenience would have been nice.
Overall, we had a great time. We played putt-putt once and tennis once, but mostly hung out by the pools. The fitness room is nice...I should have spent more time there : ).
The spa is okay. I had a massage that was a waste of $100. My daughter had a teen facial that she thoroughly enjoyed, so I guess it depends on who you get. If you like steam rooms, this one has major steam! The resort is not luxurious, but it's nice and a great place for a family vacation.
The Old Spaghetti Factory downtown is not far and we had a great dinner there. We also loved Cowboy Ciao in Scottsdale~ trendy with unique and delicious food. Not so much for kids, but they were accomodating and made cheese quesadillas for us. We also went to Rawhide Western Town. It's about a 30 min. drive, but lots of fun.

title: “Don't bring kids or high expectations!”
text:
Well, this is just not a five star hotel. The carpets in some hallways were soiled, the carpet in our lobby was soiled, the bathrooms were outdated, there is no pool. In fact, it really doesn't have a lot of features. There is a good bistro on the corner, a very, very, very expensive restaurant were you can have a $500 breakfast buffet (we had three adults and two kids). The people -- service -- were indifferent. We pulled up to the hotel at night and there was no one. Nada. You had to walk in and beg for help with the car and luggage. If the hotel is moderately busy, you'll be finding your own cab. Although there is no pool they are supposed to have a deal with the Marriott across the street to use that pool. In fact, although we dragged ourselves over there, there is no longer such a deal. Certainly, this is not a kid friendly hotel for many, many reasons. I don't think I did a great job in describing the hotel and why we hated our experience, but there you have it... We'd never stay here again and probably wouldn't try the chain the experience was so bad. Don't get me wrong, if we were staying at a 3 star hotel and paying 3 star prices, we'd have been fine.
Now for some good: At night, the main lobby is beautifully lit (it's not quite as nice by day). The location is very good.
If you are looking for alternatives I'd recommend the Fairmont (for a fancy hotel), the JW Marriott (it's sort of a big convention hotel, but you can use the pool because it has one), or the Embassy Suites.

title: “Agree that this place isn't too great”
text:
I stayed here a few days looking for a cheap hotel while at a conference since the conference hotels were really booked. Here are some reasons why the place is less desirable:
* Run down neighborhood (as noted in previous comment)
* The hotel desk has a glass panel in front of it
* I had to pay a $10 deposit to get a remote control for my TV. The remote only had about six buttons on it.
* The TV only had ~10 channels. Two of them were very graphic porn channels.
* To get an idea of the neighborhood, there were signs that said that you cannot have any guests come to your room.
* The wifi reception was very poor in my room (I realize that this can be fairly normal...)

title: “Good, turned REALLY BAD!!!!”
text: Checked in late (10:30 on Thursday night) Outside doors that were to be locked at 6 p.m. were open, first bad sign....got to my room, and it was pretty nice.. Clean, good internet connection. Unpacked, went to find soda machine, and ice, and snack. Only ONE snack machine in entire hotel.....are you kidding???? Took cash to soda machine, but cash didn't work at first machine., Went to another soda machine, and cash didn't work there either. Had to use a debit card to soda.... Second night, same thing, but went to bar to get apple pie....was good, and reasonable price.....Oh, and outside door by room STILL left open and unlocked. Third and last night, arrived late, 11:30, and after preparing for bath, only to find there was only a hand towel in bath....Not a wash cloth, and not a bath towel to be found. Then I found the dessert dish from the PREVIOUS night, was still in the room too! UCK!! So....I call the front desk....rang 20 times no answer....waited 30 minutes, and called again....rang 20 times, (yes, I did count...) no answer.....Just gave up, went to bed after emailing Hotwire regarding problem....Got a response email by morning, asking me to call Hotwire...I did. They put me on hold, and called hotel themselves. Hotel said they never heard from me....WELL OF Course they didn't, cause they didn't answer the phone!!!!! Hotwire just kept repeating the same thing over and over....they haven't heard from you....I finished that call, thanking them for not helping me....Went by the front desk on way out....was told they didn't hear from me....guess they all use the same customer service manuel......No comment about not answering phone...but was told I should have come down to the front desk and asked for towels. So here I am, a woman traveling alone, late at night, outside door to hotel open, and I am supposed to go walking around the hotel to find towels.....NO WAY!!! To top it off, while packing up my clothes, I found a dead bug (roach) in the drawer with my clothes.... I would not recommend this hotel to a dog....they should have offered me a discount....or Free night.....Just Aweful ending experience........

title: “Average Hotel”
text: Nothing extra special here. Be sure to get all items from room when you check out. Went back next day for items left in room day before, items managed to check out too. Staff was not very helpful in this. You need to speak to this person, no this person and talk to so and so.

title: “Good hotel, decent decor, thin walls”
text: The hotel is in a decent location downtown with a nice bar in the lobby as well as a Shula's restaurant. The rooms are nicely decorated, bathrooms are large enough, the walls are a bit thin though so you will hear your neighbors. The beds are really comfy. The workout facility is in the basement and is not huge so it fills up very quickly.

title: “Downtown location, very close to 9/11 site, friendly staff”
text: So, if you're wanting to see the 9/11 site while in NYC this is the closest hotel. Our room actually had a view staright into the whole site, which is pretty amazing right now as the memorial is open, but they're working on all of the other buildings on the site. Lots to look at. Also, if you're on that side of the building (probably west) you will have a decent view of the Hudson. Also, you are close to Wall Street, just across the street from St. Pauls Church (where they have an awesome 9/11 display - must see) and close to Trinity Church (very old church, cool old cemetary and National Treasure's secret "Heere at the Wall"). Plenty of ways to get into Midtown from here, cab or subway. And not too far of a walk to South Street Seaport.

title: “Wonderful for Families !!”
text:
This was a wonderful property for our family. We stayed here over Thanksgiving to go to Sea World. The motel is set up like little cabins with front porches. Inside the walls and ceilings are all white washed wood. There is a mini fridge and microwave. Our room was (#289) across from the playground, so my husband and I were able to relax on the front porch and watch the kids play. The playground is very nice. My kids loved it.
Although we did not take advantage, the motel offers complementary breakfast and happy hour with free beer, wine, sodas and snacks.
Great Value !!!!!

title: “Disappointing”
text: A bit disappointed with this hotel, not just because the exterior is undergoing a presumably much needed facelift, but because the overall impression is sloppy. The staff are very friendly, but our phone did not work, the hairdryer didn't work, the pen didn't work(!) the music centre alarm went off at 6 am because it hadn't been cancelled........ Just not what one would expect from a boutique hotel. Nice wine between 5 pm and 6 pm in a rather dingy lobby with very repetitive music. Expensive breakfast. Good touch was a complimentary bottle of wine to celebrate our wedding anniversary. Well situated close to Malls and restaurants.

title: “Renovated, perfect for one in Time Square”
text: The Paramount was a great affordable option for one person in NYC. There single rooms are small but renovated, nicely decorated and functional. I happened to look online on their Twitter account before booking and got a Twitter discount (10%, if I remember correctly and a free drink at the bar for mentioning them). They accepted to store your bags the day you check-out and only ask for a $2 per bag fee which I thought was reasonable. If you are flying in and out, it's also a less then 10 minutes walk to Port Authority, a main bus station where you can get direct buses to all 3 airports that serve NYC. I found the shuttle buses to be way more efficient and cheaper than the Super Shuttle especially for a place like Time Square (got in on a Super Shuttle and it took 2 hours to get to my hotel because they dropped most people before me!). This hotel also offers water mixed with fruit in the lobby while you wait to check-in or out. That was a nice touch on 90 degrees plus day! My only disappointment was that they don't seem flexible on early check-in. I arrived at 1 pm and couldn't access my room before 3 pm as stated when booking. They did store my bag for free on that day so it was alright, but it was the first time I couldn't do an early check-in in a hotel of such category.

title: “Never Apologise, Never Explain”
text:
In March this year, I booked a 4 night stay at this hotel - I clearly specified a non-smoking room (since I am asthmatic). I spent a distressing and uncomfortable first night, due to the overpoweringly unpleasant musty smell of the room. But it was next morning that I found that all rooms on that floor were for smokers. Indeed there was a California State notice on the back of the door warning guests of the health risks of sleeping in the room.
The next morning I requested (and was given) a different room for the remaining 3 nights.
When I asked why I wasn't allocated a non-smoking room when this had been booked 6 months earlier, the counter clerk responded - "It hadn't been possible to allocate rooms so far in advance".
What on earth did that mean?
I set out my dissatisfaction with teh arrangements on a feedback form. Four weeks on, I have heard nothing from the hotel.
I accept the fact that errors can be made. However I deplore the fact that at no point has anyone from the hotel attempted to explain or apologise for this disgraceful lapse in customer care.

title: “Disappointing stay - I don't expect I'll stay here again”
text:
I'll start with the things that were good. I liked the lobby and the bar/lounge downstairs. Their concept around a self-service food area seemed to work pretty nice as well. Normally I go out for meals but this was really useful when I got in late the first night and just wanted something beyond what a vending machine would have available. I liked the room design in general. I don't need/want a huge hotel room. The flat screen tv was a good size.
Now the bad. The wifi didn't work in my room. I was at the end of the hallway. The signal strength basically wasn't strong enough. If I walked out into the hallway it worked. Just not in my room. I talked to support - they couldn't get anywhere with me. It wasn't a deal killer but I'd rather sit on the bed and veg a bit while I watch tv with my laptop. I was able to get on the wired network but that meant I was tethered to the desk in the corner. Granted it was very fast Internet. The location of the ironing board was completely non-obvious. It was around the bed in the corner in a hidden space behind the headboard. The hot water didn't work. Okay, it made it not completely frigid but it wasn't even lukewarm. EVER. It wasn't even a time of day thing. I think this is just an old hotel that was refurbished and they did a bad job. It wasn't just me, either. My two other co-workers had the same issue with the hot water.

title: “Good hotel in good location”
text:
We stayed in the hotel for 3 nights. Overall it is a nice hotel in good location.
The things I like,
- It is not far from the metro station in Dupont circle.
- The room is nice and spacious. There is free WiFi.
- Although there is no coffee maker in the room, there is free coffee and milk (cream, slim mile, and soy milk) served in the lobby from 6:30am-9am.
- 5-6pm Happy hour in the lobby serving free drinks.
The things I don't like,
- The wall is thin. I stayed in an odd room having 2 doors connecting to adjacent rooms on both sides. I could hear the lady talking on the phone in one room, and a couple arguing and their dog barking in the other room. Fortunately my neighbors were quite at night so I still slept well.
Oh, it is definitely a pet friendly hotel as I saw many guests with their pets.

title: “Great Hotel with Great Service”
text: It was a great experience. Well worth the money. I highly recommend it.

title: “Great Location, Ok Place to Stay”
text: After reading all of the reviews about this hotel, I wasn't sure what to expect, as there were as many good reviews as bad. We stayed here for 4 nights and found the place OK. It is old building, but clean, staff is very friendly & helpful and the location was great. Only one of the two elevators was working, but a five minute wait isn't really a big deal. I was with two other ladies and we felt very safe walking around the area after dark. I think for the price we paid the place was better than I was expecting after reading the reviews. The room had a microwave and fridge, so we were able to come back and have a cool drink. People have to keep in mind that in New York City, if you can get an OK place for less than $200 per night, you shouldn't expect real luxury accommodations and we were in the room only long enough to shower and sleep so I would recommend this hotel as an OK place and a great central location.

title: “Westin's Jekyll and Hyde approach”
text:
Stayed at the Westin for the annual conference and the hotel showed its worst when it had to do with our personal needs and very good when it had to show its quality vis-a-vis conference attendees. I would not recommend this property as there are too many attributes that simply make Westin in Denver a non-heavenly experience. To start with, bookings were all messed up and I did not get a room I booked. I supposedly got upgraded but I am already a preferred Starwood member so it was not much my wife and I got for having to sleep in two beds (my king bed reservation was not honored). It took 3 phone calls and 25 hours to have the safe in the room fixed. The hotel dry cleaned my jeans (and ironed them) contrary to my written cold wash only laundry request - and then I had to ask them to remove the charge after they said they would and did not do so. I had two bills on the checkout and had to call to have it rectified so that I could check out. The maid took unread publications and threw them away and the the porter upon our arrival had no interest in helping us check in. Even though the outside temperature was 79 the pool was not clean not warmed so that we could use it. So on a personal note this is an F.
On a corporate note the conference was great and the hotel was very accomodating and addressed my dietary needs (vegetarian).
I guess the above pushes the great to F+/D- still - a kind of grade that makes you want to book another property next time I am in Denver.

title: “Routine "convention" hotel; great location”
text: Nothing really bad nor good to say about this convention-center hotel except that you really can't do much better location-wise. If they are not hosting a bid convention when you are going, you should be able to get in on Priceline for very little money, in which case it is absolutely the best place to stay. I paid $75 a night (rack rate 4 times as much) for three nights.

title: “Great hotel in the middle of everything”
text: We live in the suburbs and stay downtown occasionally (after a cubs game, for a night out at the blues clubs). The only complaints I would have is the lack of a bottle of water in the room. Every hotel needs to have at least one bottle of water in the room, even if they charge for it. Second thing would be the valet. Our car was almost taken by another family because the valet was not checking the tickets. Other than that, great hotel!

title: “Nice Hotel Generally, Service Varied”
text:
Generally a nice hotel, well kept, clean. Walls not terribly well insulated. Funky decor fine with me. Most staff very friendly and helpful. Holly and Fallon were particularly friendly, smart and helpful. Some exceptions (a woman whose name starts with G was not very welcoming and a man whose name starts with M was kind of obnoxious.) The exceptions were unusual for a Kimpton.
Nice coffee bar, the Caribou Cafe across the street. Fitness Center could use some weight equipment. No broadband in rooms. WiFi didn't work for me.
Generally an okay experience... would return but might be reluctant to use for an extended stay.

title: “REVIEW OF THE LUXE HOTEL SPA”
text: I really enjoy my trips to the luxe hotel sanctuary spa. The pool area is very peaceful and beautiful. Excellent service from all of the spa staff make every visit great and they really make us feel relaxed. I really recommend this spa for a relaxing day of pampering yourself .

title: “Good Hotel & Good Price for NYC!”
text:
This hotel is located a very short walk from Madison Square Garden and Penn Station. It's about a 15 minute walk from Times Square. The hotel room was bigger than I thought it would be, and very modern. The price is around $150/night which is a good rate for NYC.
I thought it was in a very good and safe location for Manhattan. Its kind of hard to find on W 32nd St because they don't have a very robust sign outside of the hotel.
The bed was big and comfy, the room came complete with a flat screen TV, iron, and ironing board. It even had a small desk.
Everything was clean.
My room didn't have much of a view at all (just another building next door).
Definitely a good price, for a pretty good quality hotel centrally located in Manhattan. I would stay here again if I got the room for a similar price and I recommend it to others.
Breakfast was included in the cost of the room.

title: “Avoid with care”
text:
Five stars for location, one for customer service. I always got fantastic customer service whenever I travel in US but this is unusual for 4 star hotel. Their floor staff walked out due to pay dispute (money and conditions) and was picketing outside hotel for 4 days. 
It was not the noise or crowded entrance, it was inability of management to handle the situation, both communication with guests and simple lack of friendliness towards customer who decided to stay instead of leaving. Temporary staff (to clean room) was scared to make eye contact
TIny room, 70's deco, bad food. Gym and business centre were tiny as well.
There was not even feedback forms offered at the of stay. 
Avoid if you can.

title: “Wonderful!”
text: Loved it...W Hotel never disappoints. EVER! Stayed at the W City Center the previous weekend and equally wonderful! THANK YOU!

title: “Nice Stay at Embassy Suites”
text: Stayed here for 2 nights after spending 5 nights in NYC. Took the Amtrack to Philly which I would highly recommend. The Embassey Suites in a nice 3 star hotel in a pretty good central location. The suite was very large and the exterior of the hotel was nice. The suite was slightly outdated and because the hotel is round the suites are a bit odd shaped. The bedroom was not large and does not have King beds. The fridge is also nice for keeping bevergaes cold. Maybe I would have enjoyed this more if we hadn't traveled to NYC first. The historical sites in Philly were okay and were about a 15 minutes walk from the hotel. There is a FRIDAYS Restaurant on site which is nice. Also there is a laundry available downstairs which we didn't use.

title: “Beautiful traditional hotel”
text:
The Elysee is a beautiful traditional hotel in New York. Perhaps for the slightly older crowd though - there were times it felt we were 30 years younger than anyone else - but all the same a great place.
We got upgraded to a suite which was bigger than our flat back home and even had a grand piano in it. An amazing room!
Every afternoon there is free tea including wine and cheese - make sure you make the most of it as it's really good quality.
One of the best hotels I've stayed in in New York.

title: “loved it”
text: Coming from France we spent seven days there, touring around. The room was perfect. Very tidy and comfortable. We stayed on the good side of the building, meaning not direct to Lombard Street - interstate 101. Location is great by the way. One or two times we had trouble parking the car though, late at night. We cooked ourselves breakfast but had coffee and muffins down at the reception. Very nice hard working people. Good souvenir.

title: “Management had zero brain cells, Poor customer service, Concierage was clueless”
text:
We stayed at the Monaco for a wedding. The wedding was lovely, but I can not say our interaction with the employees of the hotel were the same. We entered the hotel and were given a key that we found out didn't work when we got to the room. I went down to remedy the issue and was told our credit card was denied. I went back upstairs to retrieve my husband and they ran it again and it was fine. He came back up to the room and the key still didn't work, so went back downstairs to get another key. She reswipes they key and we go back upstairs to what we think is our room. We walk on someone else because they have given us the wrong key. Mangement finally comes out says I see you are staying for two nights, my response "No it is for three" . She says it is not her fault we walked in on someone else. I leave to let my husband handle the situation. We are offered dinner, but cannot use it because we have wedding things planned all weekend. 
We ask the concierge about brunch and zero recommnedations. I also witness a gentleman ask for a recommendation on where to find a black suit jacket. Again no answers. I pipe in with "There is a Banana Republic and Jos two blocks away." It is absurd I know more about DC than the hotel and have only been there two days. 
Overall the customer service was horrible. The beds were comfortable and a good location. I like the Monaco in Chicago, but will NEVER stay at the one in DC again.

title: “We love this place.”
text: We stay at this hotel at least 5 nights a year for business and for leisure. It is very conveniently located, the staff is usually very helpful, rooms are clean and very comfortable. The only problems we have had is with the made-to-order breakfasts sometimes being very slow, and sometimes when it is very busy, things run out during breakfast. The foodservice staff can be a bit iffy, but that is a small problem considering how wonderful everything else is. One thing I especially like is this hotel set back just far enough from I-10 that it is pretty quiet.

title: “Size doesn't matter!”
text: Don't be blown away by the hugeness of this hotel! The staff is very personal and friendly. E.g., the nice attendant brought me not one but two towels during my workout in the 24/7 health club, and I didn't even ask for one! The lobby atmosphere is that of a hyperactive UN-- in a good way. This hotel gets lots and lots of the international crowd, and their flight crews, too. This facility really has everything you need, as impersonal as it may seem at first. Yes, it's big, but it does a great job if you are looking for reasonable rates and want a sure bet in the most popular part of town.

title: “Loved Hotel Pennsylvania!”
text:
I was pretty torn as to whether to book this hotel after the mixed reviews I’d read on various hotel sites but decided to go for it as it was such a reasonable price and looked like a good location.
I can honestly say after staying there for five nights, I’m really glad I took the risk! The location is perfect, directly opposite Penn Station, 5 minutes walk from Times Square and Statue of Liberty is about two blocks away. There is also a subway stop right next to the hotel so it’s definitely worth buying a 7 day fun pass because although nearly all the major sites are within walking distance, it’s exhausting walking all day in the August heat and then going out in the evening!
The reception is quite impressive and very busy with people constantly coming and going and lots of security. There are three souvenir shops, a coffee shop and an internet room. There is also an entrance to Lindy’s from the hotel lobby which sells the most amazing cheesecake!
Me and my friend opted for a standard twin room. The room itself was large by city standards; two double beds, TV, desk, wardrobes with plenty of hanging space and still enough room to open suitcases on the floor. Most importantly with the soaring August temperatures, the air conditioning worked perfectly. The bathroom was again quite roomy and although it could have done with a lick of paint, was clean and had everything we needed. The only thing missing was a hairdryer so don’t forget to bring one.
Tips
If you’re feeling brave get the train from JFK to Penn Station, saves quite a few dollars.
Go to Serendipity’s restaurant – a real treasure right in the centre of NY (225 East 60th Street between 2nd and 3rd Avenues New York, NY 10022) – their frozen hot chocolate and humble pie is out of this world!
If you go to the Guggenheim art gallery after 5:45pm on a Friday you don’t have to pay full price and can just make a donation – the queue goes round the block but moves really quickly so it’s not as bad as it looks.
Try and check out a sports game, we went to watch the Mets play at the Shea stadium and it was the highlight of our holiday – really entertaining and very American!
Century 21 by Ground Zero is full of designer bargains.
Try a comedy club in Times Square for a different kind of night out, I’d never been to one before but it was great fun.

title: “Very nice place to stay in Columbus”
text: The Blackwell hotel is located on the OSU campus and run by the Fisher College (economics studies). It can easily compete with any other four to five star hotel in the US. The rooms are spacious and nicely furnished. It was always very quite in my room and had a decent sleep in the very comfortable bed. Service stuff is extremely friendly and always helpful. I especially enjoyed the limousine transfer from and to the airport.

title: “Very comfortable!”
text: Very comfortable and clean hotel. Had a great stay in a nicely decorated room facing the street. Queen bed. The only thing we didn't like was the high and hard pillows, which made our necks ache. Otherwise it was perfect and we recommend this hotel!

title: “Don't stay here”
text: I never stayed at the Hotel Riverview but live in the neighborhood. Believe all the negative reviews. This place is downright scary. There are drug addicts and transgender prostitutes that frequent here. I always feel sorry for the unknowing tourists I see arriving outside this hotel. STAY AWAY!

title: “Frank Sinatra's favorite!”
text:
Magnificent old Hotel. Sinatra's favorite.
Staff is great, 4 restaraunts are great, water pressure is outstanding.
Offered a $30.00 upgrade to room with sitting area per night. Declined but will take them up on that tomorrow night.
Rooms are small, as to be expected in a historic hotel, but I'm sitting here surrounded by thousands of dollars of furnishings, wall work, heavy wooden panelled door, etc.
This is a subtle but important note as I sit back and notice things. If I look around my room and ask "could this be a guest room in a Southern Plantation, or Rhode Island Mansion?" my answer is Yes. When I ask that at the Hilton/Hyatt/Marriott, my answer is No.
Then I ask myself, "how many days do I have on this planet? how many days do I want to be in a generic box?"
Internet is $11.40/day.
View: Lake Michigan or City, ask at desk. I took the Lake, and have nothing between me and the lake but one road. No buildings, this hotel is on the lake.
Large window says "Caution Do Not Open", to appease the lawyers living amongst us. I slid the window up 4 feet last night. When was the last time you slid a hotel window up? Especially a new dark stained aluminum double paned window? No screws or restrictors. Gotta like a place that still says "don't do that" but lets you be an American with the choice to do so if you want.
Phone system is nice. Set wake up call for 6:30am. Heard it, ignored it, rolled over. Went off a second time, ignored it, rolled over. Security knocked on my door 15 minutes later, "Security, just wanted to make sure you received your wake up call". I was extremely impressed that they knew part of their job is to make sure I make it to my early meeting!
The bar says they served the 2nd drink in Chicago after Prohibition ended.
4 internal high end restaraunts.
Right on the shopping wonderland known as the Magnificent Mile, across from Bloomindales.
If you're tired of generic Hyatt/Hilton/Marriott experiences and want a change, try the Drake.
Thanks to BiddingForTravel for allowing me to find out about this hotel!

title: “No complaints”
text: Hotel and room were clean. Staff was friendly. Food from room service was tasty. Location was convenient. Price was reasonable. I have no complaints at all. Would stay here again.

title: “Perfect for Solo Traveler”
text: This was my first stay at a Club Quarters and it was great. As with any hotel, know what YOU need to be happy. For me, this was the perfect hotel for a solo trip. I was attending a conference held at another hotel nearby that actually wanted more than twice the price for a room. The building was built in the 1920s and little touches still show that - marble in unexpected places, small elevators. My room was small, yes, but everything was clean and in good condition - nice bed linens, nice carpet and wall covering, attractive furniture. I had a bed, two night tables, an armchair, and a wall-mounted TV. And a superb little desk with an ergonomic chair. That's what made me happiest - a work space where I could actually work! Lots of natural light, good bright desk lamp, plenty of outlets, a dictionary and thesaurus, and free wireless internet!! (This is not a standard feature at many other hotels in the area.) Also, the lobby has two computers, a printer, and fax, and even though they're not the newest, fastest models, just having that free access is another big bonus. The room was on the front of the building and had a nice view of the canal. The bathroom had a large walk-in shower with a shower head that adjusts every way imaginable. (If you require a tub, you might be disappointed, but I was fine.) The bathroom also had an easy-to-figure-out heater that made it nice and toasty. There was only one problem the first morning, a hairline crack in the shower head that allowed water to drip out. I let the front desk know. Not only did they offer to move me to another room if I wanted (which I didn't, the room was fine otherwise!) but I gave them my schedule and they had the maintenance guys in to fix it while I was gone from the room so there was no inconvenience. As so many other reviews mention, there is a fill-your-own-bottle water station by the elevator (they provide bottles). There is also a courtesy closet if you just want to grab an extra towel or pillow. If you're used to being waited on hand and foot, this might be off-putting, but I love the freedom of just walking down the hall and getting whatever I need whenever I need it. In the room, there was also a little fridge and microwave, though I think that varies room to room. If you want a taxi or help with your bags, they can take care of that. I prefer to walk, and there are several good places to eat within a one-block radius, including an Italian-style restaurant essentially attached to the hotel. Other quick notes: construction crews are doing some work on the lower floors, which I didn't even notice until I took the stairs and smelled the paint. There are only 2 elevators - so don't be in a hurry. I didn't use the fitness equipment, which I think is in the basement.

title: “Not Happy With Location”
text: I usually feel very comfortable in any Omni Hotel, however I was not completely satisfied with this stay. Inside the hotel is beautiful, rooms good. The outside of the hotel is the reason I would never stay here again. It's location is in a very bad area with bad smells outside and I'm sorry to say homeless people around building. I feel terrible for anyone who does not have a home and I'm not suggesting in any way they should not be allowed to walk or stay where they choose. That being said, I was not comfortable wih the hotel surroundings. We walked accross the street to some sort of food court and walked right back to the hotel! It was very dirty and the smell inside this building was alwful. If you choose this hotel be careful from your walk from the parking deck to the hotel. We did not find it to be well lit. The hotel inside is beautiful but the surroundings are very poor.

title: “Average”
text: Stayed here for a night. I found the hotel build tinny so you could hear a lot that was happening in the building. Personally I'm not too keen on the modern furnishings - there was a cheapness about them. Not bad, but not great either....

title: “Awesome hotel!!!! It's a must!!!!”
text: My teenage daughter and I stayed there for five wonderful nights! The hotel was clean and quiet with a friendly staff!!! Our room was a very nice size for NYC, also. The location couldn't be better, either. Very close to 5th Ave shopping, Rockefeller Center, and Times Square. Would definitely stay there again!!!

title: “Cozy, a little too cozy”
text:
the location was great, the staff friendly enough but:
only eggs or bland cereal for breakfast (would some Smacks kill ya?), very tiny room with almost no surface space to put your stuff, and way too hot at night. all in all I have to say it was an average stay at a quite pricey hotel. cut the prices by a quarter and you might get good value.

title: “Amazing experience”
text: My mom and I were in NYC for a wedding and had an amazing experience in this beautiful and comfortable hotel with a friendly customer service! The rooms were clean, as a matter of fact we had our rooms cleaned twice a day which was amazing! We had a choice of watching free movies in room from their complimentary movie rental service! Amazing staff, helped us around to get to airport and wedding on time! We were walking distance from time square which was very convenient! I highly recommend this hotel, and will only stay here the next time we visit NYC!!

title: “Courtyard Phoenix North is good for travelers to the area”
text:
I stayed at Courtyard Phoenix North/Happy Valley for 2 nights in March 2011. I was traveling all over the Phoenix area, so I needed a nice, clean hotel not far off the interstate. This was exactly what I needed. I normally don't stay in suburban areas like this, but like I said I was traveling all over and wasn't at my hotel much beyond sleeping and eating breakfast. The hotel was very clean, the free breakfast was good (for what it is), and the staff was nice.
My room overlooked the pool area (which I didn't use), so it got a little noisy at some points. While this wasn't enough to bother me, you might want to request a room not facing the pool if you think it would be an issue for you.
There's just about every chain restaurant you can think of in the immediate area (again, this isn't something I normally look for), but if you want to go more intown it's maybe a 20 minute drive -- not bad.
I'd definitely stay here again.

title: “I Recommend this hotel”
text: I recently stayed 3 nights in this hotel for my kid's tennis tournament. We were in a great location for dining/shopping, and the hotel was very easy to get to. All of the staff did a great job and the free breakfast had a wide variety of foods, including eggs, sausage, and fresh fruit. Coffee is available all day! The rooms were pretty soundproof, which was good for me since I'm a light sleeper. Housekeeping staff did a great job about replenishing toiletries, and we always had plenty of towels. The pool looked nice, but it was not warm enough outside to go swimming yet--maybe next time!

title: “Horrible night's sleep”
text: I stayed at the Westin over the 4th of July weekend. There was a huge group (300+) staying there at the same time. This group was incredibly noisy. They lined the hallway of my floor all night long, talking loudly with each other. Worse yet, at 2:30a.m., somebody tried to get into my room. Apparently the front desk was so disorganized that they gave the person a card key to my room, believing that my room was unoccupied. When I checked out at 4:00a.m., the hallway was still lined with noisy people from this group, and I could barely walk through the lobby it was so crowded. When I complained to the front desk, they were rude and dishonest. They told me they refunded me for the night, but I later found that they did not. I will not stay at a Westin again!

title: “Very nice stay”
text: Love to stay at this hotel. It is so close to great shopping and Fiesta Texas. It is always clean and the beds are comfortable. The only con for this hotel is the amount of pets that are allowed.

title: “Top notch service, property and location”
text:
I travel to NY on business 4 out of every 6 weeks. I stay inn high-quality boutique hotels because I like the sense of home away from home. I have high expectations that the "little things" are important, but not always delivered. I do not write reviews mostly because I am hard to impress and typically do not want to advertise my best secrets. 
The Bryant Hotel is an exception. They deserve the accolades. 
When you enter the property, if you pay attention, you will see 5 star service. Eye contact and a warm welcome from the doorman, the front desk and the next two employees you meet to get to the elevator. YOU CANNOT UNDERESTIMATE THE QUALITY of SERVICE at this level. I think this is more than training and policy, this is the best of hiring practices......
The room is perfect, layout is well designed, roomy for NY, and clean. The bath, bed, TV, iPod port, and well stocked fridge was first class. 
I worked late (2am) one night and decided to grab a night cap at the bar downstairs before they closed. In college, I worked at restaurants and bars and know how long the shifts are and difficult it can be. The bar was wrapping up their evening when I arrived and yet I was made to feel welcomed and not rushed as I ordered what was probably the drink of the night.
