These folks are professional and are rare.
Ate one breakfast down-stairs and one at another restaurant. It was, again, a high-quality level of service......
When I checked-out, I made a mental note of how the individual employees performed at this hotel. To a person. It was remarkable. I know I will be back.

title: “Not all it's cracked up to be”
text: This hotel is very reasonably priced and is in a great location. The bathroom was also nicely updated in the room. However, the carpet was badly in need of replacing with stains pretty much every where. But the biggest problem I had was the mattress. I have never slept on a mattress as bad as the one in room 1004. And I had two mattresses in this room and both were horrible. Every time I moved in the bed, I heard and felt the springs in the mattress. The hotel attempted to remedy the problem by flipping the mattress which did nothing. For that reason I can not recommend this hotel.

title: “Great stay, great location”
text:
Just returned from a night at the Hyatt Regency Chicago. This Hyatt is right on the Chicago River on Wacker Drive. The room was nicely decorated and very clean; the virtual tour on the hotel's website is an accurate depiction of the room. The bed was comfortable; not too hard, not too soft. Good feather pillows. Bathroom was a little sparse but nicely decorated just like the room and comfortably sized. Tub/shower combo with bowed out curtain rod, single sink. An upgrade to a "deluxe room" was available for an additional cost, the description of which included a larger bathroom, bathrobes and other amenities, but since we were only in town for a single evening, we decided not to do it. I was comforted to see that after 2:00pm the elevators that access the rooms were only accessible with a room key. 
The fitness center of the hotel was very good; room-key access only, Lifecycle equipment, plasma screen TVs on the wall and headphones that connected to the individual machines so you could hear the TV. Free weighs and nautilus weight circuit was also available. Networks restaurant was average in quality and what I have come to expect for hotel restaurant prices (e.g., $10.00 for a hamburger at lunch). Big, a bar in the hotel, was good. Service at Big was friendly and fast. Service at Networks was unobtrusive and served its purpose. 
The location of this hotel is great for shopping on the Magnificent Mile (a mere two blocks from the hotel's front door), visiting Navy Pier and the museums. I would certainly return to this hotel and would recommend it to others.

title: “Sheer Excellence”
text: It’s my 4th time in this hotel and it never fails. This time I got upgraded to a suite along with a complementary bottle of wine which let me relax after a rough business day and travel into the city. Their gym was under construction so I got a complementary voucher to the one across the street. Location is great and the staff is amazing. I will sure continue to use this hotel every time I am in NYC.

title: “average hotel in a terrific location”
text: I know NYC hotel rooms are small, but our room was too small. It is a Starwood hotel but they seem to not want to display the connection. Virtually nothing in the hotel says Starwood, although the staff told me that this hotel used to be a Sheraton. I can see why it's not any more. The hotel is just not up to Sheraton standards. The bed was good; no room service; the bathroom was tiny; the view was decent from the 22nd floor where our room was; there was a wide/flat sreeen TV that made everyone look so wide--like a funhouse mirror! It is only a block or so from Radio City and various other NYC attractions, but to say that it's at Times Square is a stretch. It's probably a half mile away--a 10 block 10 minute walk. The restaurant serves only breakfast. For the visitors to NYC who figure that they will be out all day and only sleep in the room, then it's fine. To us, who are familiar with Starwood hotels all over the world (Gold SPG members), this is a lesser cousin.

title: “Great property for the price, remodeled rooms equivalent to higher end chains”
text:
Stayed with my wife and kids at this hotel for a bowl game at the Charlotte stadium. Location is very convenient to highway and has multiple restaraunts close by to eat. I am in sales and travel every week. After the remodel I feel like this hotel has beds, linens, pillows, TV, breakfast, decor equivalent to the other major chain hotels like Hampton, Fairfield,Holiday express etc at a much better price.
Rooms were clean, each bed had about 5 pillows of various size etc which I really like, linens were clean and soft. Curtain closed completely and allowed us to sleep as long as we wanted. Continental breakfast was good. Bathroom was clean and adequately equipped

title: “Great room, great location”
text:
Booked a room through Priceline at about half the regular price. Pulled into the valet area expecting to pay a pretty penny to park my vehicle, and I was not disappointed. $35 for valet is pretty excessive, but what else are ya gonna do, I guess.
Check-in and other staff interactions were smooth and painless - they even switched our room from 2 doubles to a king without any protest, which isn't always a given when you've used Priceline. Room was spacious and spotless, with a good view of the harbor and the surrounding office buildings.
Great location downtown - about six blocks from Pike Place market, right in the retail core, a couple of blocks from the monorail station. A great base for exploring. I fully recommend this hotel, even if it is a bit nondescript and corporate.

title: “Brought back memories”
text:
We had a couple of days to spend in San Antonio so my wife, my dog Miss Maizy and I looked for a place to stay. We are retired now but up until last year we traveled to every continent except Antarctica in our business. We had a lot of memories of being in SA on the River Walk and many tropical hotels around the world. These memories plus now being more cost conscious on fixed incomes, we came across El Tropicano. I read all of the reviews and chuckled because it seems that folks either loved or hated this place; it had the ring of our polarized political parties. We decided to give it a try since we like funky, off-the-beaten path restaurants and hotels rather than the more cookie cutter chains. Our visit turned out to be a real treat and stimulated me to post this review to clear up some of the comments.
Pet Policy - Our first task was to call the hotel, which we always do, to clarify the pet policy. The representative told me nicely that their hotel rules were to charge $100 and limit dog size to 20#. OK, rules are rules, but we stuck with them and booked a room. I immediately called PetSmart Dog Hotels and booked Maizy there for $40. 
Staff Friendly - We found the tone and hospitality of the staff to be first class. We went to our room which was very clean and well equipped... pretty much exactly what we expected. My wife went downstairs to get some info on transportation options and engaged in a discussion with the hotel manager about the history of the hotel and how much we liked the funky tropical decor. The manager was nice enough to offer us an upgraded room and even offered to send someone to move our stuff from one side of the hotel to the other. All of the staff we talked to during our stay were friendly and helpful.
Location and Transportation - After doing some research and using the transportation system we do not understand the reviews that are critical of being off the beaten path. The trolley that drops you off right at downtown part of the River Walk is literally across the street from the hotel. Additionally, river taxis are available down the stairs to the river next to the hotel. Only down side is that the last trolley run is at 9 pm on weekdays but taxi fare is only $6 back to hotel. If you like to walk, it is only 10-15 minutes depending on your pace. You can pay $50-100 more per night and stay downtown if this is an issue... your call.
Room Layout - Both of our rooms were very clean including linens and furniture covers. I think some folks were critical because of the small bathroom. Again, you can pay the big bucks if you wish. The bathroom had everything we needed and again we like the funky layouts and the memories of many tropical hotels we visited over the years. The fact that flight crews are regulars at this hotel told us that the noise level issues mentioned in some reviews were over the top. Our upgraded room was right next to the pool but we had no issues with noise.
Parking Fee - It is $18 with in and out privileges right next to the hotel. Fees at downtown hotels are higher. What's the issue with this? Park your car at the hotel and use the local transportation.
Decor and Care - I've already mentioned the fact that we just like this style. Additionally, landscaping was very nice with crews working on the grounds daily. Interior decor was very colorful, i.e. tropical and refreshing. The bartender was quite friendly and offered a lot of local info. Breakfast room was in the large lobby and again friendly servers.
Locally Owned - One of the appeals of this hotel is that it is locally owned. Our hotel fees were going into the local economy, not to LA or NY. The hotel also provides a list of locally owned restaurants in their association.
In summary, if it is not obvious by now, we liked this hotel very much. If you have issues with bright colors, a small bathroom, having to ride a trolley 5 minutes or pet policy, go somewhere else; but, if you want a friendly hotel with a funky look, that is clean and connected directly to the local transportation options, then give this a try. We have no affiliation whatsoever with this hotel, financially or otherwise; only the desire to put some clarity into these reviews.

title: “Recommended”
text: The friendly staff upgraded our room to a king size (from queen) without being asked, the room was FAR bigger than expected - 12 ft ceilings, lots of room to walk around the (huge) bed, efficient but quiet air con - and generally very clean (under the bed could have done with hoovering). Bit dark perhaps but lighting was fine. The lifts worked perfectly until our final day when maintenance work was being done on one of them. The decor could do with being updated but that was really our only complaint. The steak restaurant linked/next door to the hotel was FANTASTIC!! Great location too - close enough to the action but on a quieter street so not too much noise disturbing our sleep.

title: “First Class all the way!”
text: I only wish that most hotel owners/managers had the privilege of staying at the Mark to see how business truly ought to be conducted. It truly sets "the Mark" in the industry as far as I am concerned. Not only were the staff professional and efficient, the room was the most outstanding and comfortable I have ever seen in New York. Not even the most minor dissapointment. There are not enough "stars" to describe this property.

title: “Disappointed”
text:
Our research indicated that your hotel provides a good location and 3 star rated accomodations. However, when we checked in, we noticed that the hotel and our room was not very updated. In addition, the bathroom lacked ventilation (no fan), the shower and tub drained water very slowly, the towel hanger was rusted, and the bathroom door was very old and needed repainting.
Because of these problems with the bathroom, we believe that insects were breeding in the drain area. Specifically, my daughter was bitten on the cheek by a large mosquito in the room and my husband had to kill the insect by swatting the mosquito on the ceiling. We were very upset to find a mosquito in our hotel room and my daughter has been suffering with a cheek wound that has not fully healed in over 2 weeks.

title: “FINE VINTAGE HOTEL”
text:
The St. Francis is a great, grand hotel. We stayed in the original wing, which features small (cozy?) rooms with comfy beds and a giant hi-def TV. "Simple elegance" sums this place up nicely.
Expensive internet fees ($15/day) and sky high valet parking costs ($57/day) are the only real drawbacks I encountered
.
A great location--you're right on Union Square--and a friendly staff make this a solid choice.

title: “Very pleased”
text: I have stayed at numerous hotel / motels aross the U.S. I have always been pleased with the service and quality at Super 8 and my last stay was no exception. The front desk personnel were curtious and helpful and the room was as expected; comfortable and roomy. Thank you for your quality service.

title: “The Elysian Raises The Bar on Luxury”
text: The Elysian has raised the bar on luxury accommodations in Chicago. The hotel decor is elegant, but not stuffy or pretentious like the Peninsula. The staff is extraordinary. Many defected from other luxury hotels in Chicago to be part of something special. The rooms are warm and inviting, filled with enough tech to impress even the most jaded traveler. Rates are pricey, but you get what you pay for, and factoring in the no tip policy (nice touch) the Elysian is well worth the price.

title: “great location, huge room”
text: This is an old historic building. Great location, just steps from the train lines and steps from most of the tourist stuff south of the river. I would be leary of a room overlooking the tracks, but ours didn't so I can't speak to that. We didn't have much of a view but the room was quiet. Our room was HUGE, in fact when we first walked in we walked into the living room & didn't initially see the bedroom and were briefly upset at the thought of only a pull out sofa. But then through the large bathroom we found the bedroom. Space and more space. Small fridge. Not high class finishes but fine. Restaurant downstairs, we had breakfast once there, it was average.

title: “great hotel”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Hyatt for a company Christmas party the weekend before christmas. Although it was quite packed because they had all of us from the company and a football team who was playing the colts the next day plus all their fans.I thought the elevators were slow but they had signs apologizing for that and they stated all the elevators were not working due to them updating them to suite their hotel better.I would definitely stay at the hyatt again. The rooms were nice and clean. I had no problems with the heat or the rooms being dirty or anything else.The only complaint i did have was the hotel not being blocked off from the mall. At the begining of the night we got hear the gaurds yelling at kids whos parents obviously were not watching them like they should be.
Which is in turn not the hotels but the parents fault !! I did enjoy the Hyatt and will definetly go back!!!

title: “Havana is a Boo-tique Hotel”
text:
From check-in to check-out Hotel Havana disappointed. Havana claims to be a boutique hotel yet the Cuban theme lacks any historical significance to San Antonio’s Mexican heritage. From incense and soft candle light in the lobby to velvet sofas and the dangerously dim romantic lighting in the elevator, Hotel Havana would seem to be an ideal getaway for couples looking for a nostalgic setting. However, if nostalgic boutique means catering to everyone and their dog (literally, they take pets), then Hotel Havana ranks right up there with Holiday Inn. The only differentiator I could see was the mini bar merchandise buffet confronting you in each room, complete with t-shirts and sock puppet monkies at $25. 
PROS:
- Neat old building
- Easy access to river walk
- Relatively clean
- Big SMEG fridge in each room
CONS:
- Unprofessional staff
- Noise transmits easily through walls and ceiling
- Way to dim lighting
- 17 dollar a day parking
 Specific gripes:
1) My wife and I checked in and were given the worst room in the place – directly on the lobby. In addition to the noise from the lobby a family with young kids was in the room over ours. Within 15 minutes of check-in I was politely requesting to be moved citing overhead noise as the reason. After initial comments of “we’re booked sir” they discovered a hidden room somewhere for us to move to. Wow, I thought that was awesome service until the girl who checked us in basically said she was doing us a favor but not to expect it to happen again. According to her it is up to us to disclose special requirements like not liking children running over our head while we try to sleep. Then she made us wait while she checked the room we had been in for mere minutes and then complained because the room would have to be made up again. We hadn’t even sat down and the room was in the condition it was when we walked in. Perhaps she was expecting a 5 dollar bill for her immense trouble.
2) Room service breakfast arrived 45 minutes late and stone cold. This meal consisted of coffee, a basket of tortillas, and an omelet for $35 + $5 tip. Wow.
3) We were told prior to arriving that parking was no problem, just park in front of the hotel. We learned at checkout that this tiny, cramped parking lot cost $17 a day. Awesome deal.
4) We attempted to checkout early and told the desk staff that something urgent had come up back in Houston. We had to correct the bill we were given as they hadn’t applied our Living Social coupon and then had to sit down in the lobby for 30 minutes while they attempted to find our coupon and then find the person who could fix the mistake. Lovely.

title: “Good Hotel”
text: Stayed at the Marriott for business, and overall this is a good this is a good hotel. The setup is a little strange though, and I would suggest requesting a room on a high floor. My room was right on the street, and it was a bit loud. The breakfast was very good, and the location is perfect for visiting FW. The rooms were clean and comfortable although they were a little on the small side. I would stay here again.

title: “Excellent Service Nice Staff”
text:
We stayed here for 2 when first arriving in LA after traveling to Las Vegas and San Francisco we re booked our last 4 days in LA here, they gave us a good deal before we left if we returned and I got upgraded to a junior suite leaving my daughter and boyfriend in the standard room (thats the breaks being the children Haha!!).
Staff were very polite and friendly, car parking secure, location a mile from Highway 1 giving access to all of LA and a short drive to Universal and The Grove Shopping Centre (a must visit place).
Some OK restaurants down the road (a but a car ride) shops opposite cater for essential needs and there is a Burger King and crappy looking Chinese, there a really good Chinese restaurant/take away about 1/4 mile down Lankershim on the opposite side by a Mexican
The rooms were very clean and pleasant for the price.
The pool is a bit of a waste of space.
Breakfast was adequate for free with plenty of nice fruit and good coffee.

title: “Not a bad Westin stay”
text:
We stayed here the night before our honeymoon. Keep in mind I stay at Westin hotels a lot for work and am a bit critical of them. So we checked in we were just so excited to start our honeymoon. The front desk clerk Orlando really could care less that it was my honeymoon. I am a gold member with Starwoods and I ask to see if there was anything he could do for an upgrade considering my status and it was my honeymoon. Mind you it was in the notes of our reservation that it was our honeymoon, I also mentioned it and still not even a congratulations. Also I was not acknowledged as being a Gold member either. Never offered my complimentary gift, even after I told Orland that I was a gold member 
He mentioned that the hotel was sold out and there was no way to get an upgrade. He gave us our room key and we went up to the room. This hotel has a few years of age on it and defiantly needs a bit of upgrading. This is in comparison to the Long Beach Westin. 
The room was small and so was the bathroom. I called downstairs to see if there was something that they could do. They put us in a suite on the third floor it was a little nicer and defiantly bigger. The service it self was the big thing, it took multiple calls to make anything happen. No one was nice or was willing to do anything but the bare minimum.
There was one manager on the express service line that was helpful. Besides that no one at this hotel cared about our stay.
This was a convenient hotel to stay at when flying out of LAX there is a free shuttle that runs every 15 minutes. The rooms are about average. If you get a good deal I would stay there for the convenience and that would be about it.

title: “Gorgeous Spotless Hotel”
text: If we are in Chicago again we will definitely not hesitate to stay at this hotel. It is unbelievably quiet & very clean. Each & every member of the staff we fastidious & polite. We took advantage of the use of the house town car twice which is not only a savings but more comfortable than taking a taxi. We ate at Nomi for breakfast every day as this was included in our stay. The food was as good as the best breakfasts we have ever had in our travels. Had cocktails out on the patio of the restaurant one afternoon which was very relaxing. I can't express how attentive the wait staff & hotel staff were during our entire stay. Everyone working the concierge desk was very helpful. The location is perfect & in walking distance of many attractions. And did I say CLEAN, CLEAN, CLEAN..which is a big pet peeve of mine. I never got to meet the manager but hats off to him for developing & training a fine staff!

title: “My Place to Stay in San Antonio”
text: Great service, ambience, super location and a reasonable price. What more could you ask for?? I recommend it highly.

title: “Average”
text: Average in all areas.....Not sure what I was expecting. It probably was a nice hotel 20 years ago, but it is in need of a total refresh. Very value oriented! So you will get what you pay for.

title: “Decent room, good location, great price”
text: The hotel is in a great location. It's right in the middle of downtown and just a few blocks from the subway ("L train"). There are a lot of restaurants nearby. I got a free upgrade to a suite because I printed a coupon from the hotel's website just before my stay. The room was large, clean, and had a refrigerator. Aside from the older model TV in the room that didn't have a great picture, I have nothing bad to say. The hotel has free internet access in the lobby (sometimes there's a short wait). Rooms that face the street have a nice view, but you can hear some noise. I would stay here again.

title: “Cute, older hotel with great location and reasonable rates”
text:
This is a smaller, older style European budget hotel. Small, quaint, simple rooms. Close to everything but reasonably priced for those of you not spending much time in the room. I stayed here several times on business. Nothing fancy but a good launching off point and very reasonably priced. Liked the location - close to many things so you don't need a rental car to see the city unless you want one. 
Certainly not the Westin, which I love to stay at on business travel, but this is adequate for the economy minded.

title: “Very nice, small hotel rooms for New York”
text:
Nice clean rooms. Modern styling. Very nice showers with great water pressure and lateral jets.
Price high compared to non-New York hotels, but good value for New York.
Staff very friendly, helpful and accommodating. 
Great location for our needs - just 3 blocks south of Central Park and 1/2 block from 5th Ave.
Only a block or so walk to subway station.

title: “Near Perfection!”
text: We had the distinct pleasure of staying at the Marriott Marquis last month. What a wonderful hotel! It's a big, hustle-bustle hotel, a microcosm of the city itself. The room we stayed in was large, immaculate, and comfortable. We looked out directly on Times Square, the crossroads of the world. The staff is energetic, attentive, and professional. What more could you ask? The location is superb. One can walk everywhere, and indeed we did enjoy walks to Central Park, Fifth Avenue and Union Square. The food in the "coffee shop" is delicious and fairly priced. The dinner buffet is a particular bargain for a quick relatively inexpensive meal before the theatre. We experienced none of the famous elevator problems that other Tripadvisor reviewers have noted, although we were at the hotel on what appeared to be a fairly slow weekend for New York. To the extent a $200 a night hotel room can ever be a bargain, the Marriott Marquis certainly qualifies.

title: “Exceeding Expectations”
text: The Talbott makes it a priority to exceed the expectations of their guests. I recently stayed at the beautiful property with my 3 teenage children. I was a bit reluctant to book at the Talbott because the property does not have a pool on site - I was sure that this would disappoint my teens. From the moment we stepped out of our car and were greeted by the friendliest door man ever, (learned our names and used them the rest of our stay) to our departure 5 days later, our stay was AMAZING. The high ceilinged spacious room, the frette towels, the Molten Brown amenities, the apple television, turn down service with chocolates on our pillows, and of course the top notch staff were just a few of the things that impressed all of us. We have stayed at similar hotels and paid $500 a night. We will be returning in the near future - The Talbott is our hotel of choice when visiting Chicago!!

title: “Not happy!”
text:
Have stayed here many times while staying in NY. This time I was so disappointed. Bathroom was filthy and carpeting hadn't been vaccumed. The toilet seat was filthy. They said the place was full and couldn't give us another room. After 1/2 hour on the phone to the front desk and being put on hold twice they said they would send housekeeping. They offered 2 breakfast coupons but said they couldn't do anything else. No one ever contacted me to see if things were ok. Also one washcloth and it was never replaced for 2 days. Time to go back to another one of my favorite places in NY.
Westin, Michaelangelo and Soifetel.

title: “Loved it”
text: Just come back from 5 days in New York - Stayed at the Warwick. Found it very comfortable. Staff very pleasant. Good location - easy to walk to all the sights. Didn't get a room with a view but what the heck. Would recommend this hotel. HJM

title: “Good bargain in Heart of Seattle”
text: This hotel offered a fine bargain in the heart of Seattle. I had a King corner room which was quite nice. The hotel is older for sure, but the staff was friendly, everything was clean, and it is right in the best part of town. There is a Seattle's Best almost in the hotel lobby which was convenient for a quick breakfast which was great, and you get all this at a much lower price than the typical hotel in this area. My only complaint was that the wireless internet access was slow and unreliable, perhaps because I was on the 6'th floor?

title: “Standard Embassy Suites”
text:
I stayed at the Arboretum Embassy Suites while the fires were burning in Austin. We were evacuated and were very lucky to get a room. Thank goodness for my diamond status with Hilton, as the staff at the front desk said they were only able to provide rooms for people with Hilton Gold and above status. We felt very lucky to have a place to stay.
Like all Embassy suites, the facility was clean and well taken care of. Because of the fires, I don't think the staff were prepared to be completely full and seemed a little stressed. However, they were always very pleasant and accommodating. Clearly, too much work being placed on too few staff, but totally understandable given the circumstances.
I was a little disappointed with the evening reception though. Most Embassy properties offer more than popcorn and chips as the food for the evening reception.

title: “Not the Best, Not the Worst, But not a 3.5 Star for Sure”
text:
Used Priceline name your own price so I knew it was a gamble which hotel I would get but since I chose 3.5 stars or better I knew it would be a decent hotel. Well.....decent it was, 3.5 star or luxurious it wasn't! Most hotels booked through Priceline will allow you to call after reserving and request bed size and non smoking room. This hotel would not cooperate in any way with that request. It was late Friday night and we called to let them know we would be late check in and they informed us most all non smoking rooms were already gone and we would have to take our chances. I would rather book another hotel and pay double than stay in a smokers room so I was fairly stressed. Sure enough, when we arrived all non smoking rooms were gone, but we were offered a suite upgrade for $20 a night. I readily accepted it. It was called the "Grand Quarters" and the gentleman checking me in told me it had the only jacuzzi tub in the entire hotel. That sounded wonderful. I was taken to the room- it was small and had a quirky layout- not even a couch so I don't know how it could be called a "suite." The tub was large and a good layout, I filled it up but it did not come on. I called maintenance and he came up promptly and after a bit of time to fill it up again. he determined it must be the circuit breaker and reset it. It started working and lots of gunk came out of the jets, which I expected. I always clean my hotel jacuzzi tubs with dishwasher detergent/bleach combo recommended by Jacuzzi for regular maintenance. So it was not a romantic start to our weekend to say the least, but after a couple of hours we were settled. I ordered breakfast for next morning and left it on the door.
Bed was comfy except pillows were too hard for us- ordered softer ones the next night. Room was very quiet- our location had no rooms above and not even below- it hung out over parking garage. 
Next morning the breakfast arrived right on schedule. Forgot our side of bacon but all else was there. The extra fee was only $1.50 which is impressive and the 20% tip was already added. We added a $5 tip to deliverer. We had ham and eggs, potatoes, toast, and french toast which was all prepared to order and scrumptious! Our bill was only $23 for tip and all! Very good deal for room service. 
We enjoyed a leisurely morning and did not leave our room until about 1PM. Maid service was still on our floor and saw us leave. When we returned a few hours later our room had not been cleaned and maid service was gone. We needed to get ready for dinner so we could not have them clean it. We made a call for clean towels and they were delivered promptly- along with our softer pillows. 
Have to also say- our room service dishes remained in the hall all day long! Strange. I think it might have had something to do with the remote location of the "Grand Quarters" as it was away from the rest of the hotel and did not use the regular hotel elevator. 
Rest of stay was fine. Check out did not have the extra $20 per night on my bill so I asked them when this would be charged and they said it had not been charged. Attendant ended up charging me $20 for both nights upgrade which I though was fair since I had to deal with the state of the jacuzzi and no maid service.
By the way, this hotel is close to airport and you do hear an airplane take off now and then and it is loud,but not too bad in the room and it is over fast. Wasn't near as big a problem as all the strip clubs in the area- sure were well lit at night though not noticeable during the day. Not the best feature but to be expected by an airport I guess. Also- location was not near downtown but was a quick 10 minutes away. Good location overall.
Probably would not stay here again, but might check other Crowne Plaza locations. Enjoyed the 2 bottles of complimentary water.

title: “What a nice hotel!”
text: Great experience. The lobby was very welcoming, front desk staff was very nice. I wish we had bottled water in the rooms. Would stay here again. Great Place!!!

title: “Unbelievable value and very safe”
text: I stayed here with my 8 year old son. It is a beautiful historic hotel both inside and out. For me the location was not important as I was travelling by car. There is free parking that is secure. Inside the hotel there are literally hundreds of security cameras monitoring entrances, stairs and hallways - I felt safe. The rooms were nice - there was noise from the road but this didn't affect my sleep. The Hollywood sign was visible from our room window - how good is that? The staff of the hotel were very friendly and helpful. Around the hotel there are a few restaurants. - try the Colombian one about 2 minuteswalk down the road. The price is unbelievable given the central location and nice hotel.

title: “NYC”
text:
We chose this hotel due to the fact that we were going to have to park our van overnight for four nights. The overnight parking was only $10/day!! Incredible price in NYC. Also,
the hotel is only 2 blocks from Broadway and all the major attractions in Time Square. The hotel is located in what is commonly known as "Hell's Kitchen". We also chose the hotel due to the rooftop indoor pool, since we were traveling with our boys. Loved it!!!

title: “"No Frills" NoPa Hotel”
text: I stayed here one night, on the second floor, in room 114. Like the title says, it is a no frills room. There is just the basics. You have a bed, a table, a chair, a flat screen tv on the wall, really no other room decorations. The room was clean and the bed was comfortable. The room looks over the garden/patio. It was very quiet and there was virtually no street noise. There was noise from the restaurant however. The noise from the restaurant actually woke me up on Wednesday morning at 7:00 am. It is okay because I wanted to be up early but could be a problem if one wanted to sleep in. The staff was very friendly and helpful. The neighborhood is just fine. I have seen more "homeless" and "panhandlers" in Union Square and Nob Hill. This neighborhood is primarily younger (20s - 30s) I would stay here again.

title: “pretty decent place”
text:
First of all, if you are looking for a wheelchair accessible place, this is not for you. Otherwise, read on.
The hotel is located at the corner of an intersection (30th and 8th) and it doesn't really look like a hotel from the outside (looks like it's connected to a convenience store) so be careful if you are driving and looking for it. Once you find the hotel's door, you need to get buzzed in and then climb a flight ot steps to get to the front desk. This might be tricky for those of you who have heavy luggage or multiple suitcases. But once you get past that it's pretty good.
I booked a triple room at the Chelsea Star for three nights but before I left for New York, I heard about a huge snowstorm that was going to hit the U.S. and Canada on the night I was supposed to be leaving.
I called Chelsea Star and told them that I might be delayed because of the storm, and I was told that my reservation would be honored even if I arrived a day late. I was supposed to arrive on a Monday, but the storm pushed my arrival to Tuesday, so I told the hotel that if they wanted, they could rent out the room for Monday night. 
When I arrived at the hotel on Tuesday, I was told no one had recorded
that I was going to be arriving late and that my triple room had been taken. I was very distraught, but fortunately, the guy at the desk was
very nice and he said that the Chelsea Star would upgrade my reservation and put my friends and I in an apartment suite and only charge me the triple room price. 
I forgot to ask the check-in guy's name but he's a soft-spoken Caucasian man with curly-ish black hair. If you want great service, go to him. He made suggestions for transportation (where to go to use the subway, what kind of metro cards he thought we might need) and
pointed out a few things we could do (ie. take the free Staten Island Ferry to see the Statue of Liberty). He also suggested a decent nearby
breakfast place :) You can also ask for Lilah. She's very nice too. 
But I wouldn't recommend talking to one of the night-staffers (guy with a Russian accent). He wasn't exactly rude, but he seemed bored/
disinterested, which isn't something you really want in a customer-oriented business. Before I left for New York, I spoke to this guy on the phone about being delayed because of the weather and he wanted to charge me for arriving on Tuesday instead of Monday, even though I had already explained to him that I had called the hotel about the situation the day before. 
I can understand it if a hotel charges me for being late or for cancelling if I call the day before or on the day that I am supposed to be checking in, but I informed Chelsea Star about the situation two
days before I was supposed to arrive, which is their deadline before they start charging cancellation fees. 
But I found everything and everyone else to be quite good :)
The hotel was located in a good place, just steps from Penn Station. The apartment suite is actually in the building next to the hotel. My friends and I stayed in room 1N, which was on the first floor and facing the street. The room itself was pretty good (2 double beds, private bath, small tv, kitchenette with sink, microwave, mini fridge,
cups, plates, utensils) but in the early morning, noise from the street did wake me up sometimes but I tend to be a light sleeper. 
The room was comfortable and clean and gave you what you needed. I checked for bed bugs and I was happy to see that there were none (mattresses were wrapped in plastic to prevent bug infestation). Housekeeping also showed up each day to tidy up, and hot water and pressure were pretty good in the shower. 
The only drawback I really have to say is that heating for our room was very strange. It was generally ok, but at night, sometimes it became very hot, and we had to crack open the window while we slept. 
I'd stay here again, but I think it's because I lucked out with the apartment suite. I'm not sure how things are for people who stay single, double, triple and quad rooms. I checked out the shared bathrooms near the front desk and thought they were ok. There were two rooms with only a toilet (clean but only enough room to sit down on the toilet) and one room that has a toilet and a shower (it's a private room made for one person). 
There's 2 computers near the front desk, which costs $2 U.S. for 20 minutes. One of these computers is in a small room. You can get coffee
and hot water in there in the morning but don't expect it to be a common room, because it's sort of small. But there's a little rack in the room that offers cards that describe NYC restaurant and attractions. It's a good resource if you're not sure about what to do.
All in all, I had a good time at Chelsea Star and I would recommend this place (or I guess the apartment suite) to other student travellers.

title: “The Liaison Capitol Hill is THE place to stay while in DC.”
text: The Liaison Capitol Hill is THE place to stay while in DC. I doubt that you could find a nicer place to stay... from the friendly door men, the helpful concierge staff, the desk staff and housekeeping. The location is wonderful for walking to Union Station, the Capitol and the mall for the many attractions and museums. The entire staff made us feel welcome and pampered. I look forward to our next stay with Liaison.

title: “Affordable small indoor waterpark for the kids.”
text: Had a weekend stay with 4 kids. They enjoyed the pool the most as it has plenty of activities for all of their ages. The hot tub was nice also. Staff stated they are working on the slide for the children some time after Christmas 2011. Able to feed all of the children a good breakfast in the morning. The children loved the pancake maker and the breakfast attendant took time to show the children how to work the machine. Plan on visiting again soon.

title: “Great location, I would stay again”
text:
I visited NYC and stayed at Stay for 8 nights.
The hotel location is more than great just a couple minutesaway from Times Square. The staff is very helpful and polite and the lobby is a small piece of art. The room is tiny but this is expected in New York and since I only needed it for a shower and a bed it was fine (bathroom was a bit dark though). Very good housekeeping.
Free wifi at rooms would be a major plus although sitting at the lobby is relaxing
I would stay again...

title: “FANTASTIC HOTEL”
text:
We stayed at the Westin using a vacation time share and was not disappointed. We were upgraded to a better room which overlooked the river, the living space in the room was huge as was the bathroom.
The hotel is linked to a shopping mall via covered walk ways so being able to have a wonder around the shops is very easy. The covered walk ways also lead you to the Prudential Tower so in the winter months when temperatures are below freezing this is a fantastic bonus.
The palm restaurant is overpriced and you wont get value for money. For 2 steaks we ended up paying over $100, this was not served with fries, salad or any sort of sides which was a little disappointing.
The tour bus stops are close to the hotel and Boston Common is about 10-15 mins walk away from the hotel.
The Westin was a fantastic hotel and when we next return to Boston we will make sure this is where we will stay everytime!

title: “Boston GEM”
text:
Nice accommodations -- great location!! tucked around the corner from the big hotels... this hotel was a find for us on a weekend that everything seemed to be booked... STaff was very helpful.. although there is not a bar at the hotel there are options within a block...area was safe with many reasonable dining options nearby.. We had the full breakfast buffet that was well worth the price charged. Rooms were comfortable and clean. I would definitely stay at this hotel again. 
Do tell cab drivers that it is the Courtyard on Exeter ST.

title: “AVery nice and romantic”
text:
Very clean, Very nice rooms and bathrooms. If you are looking for a gret place to stay outside up uptown Charlotte, this is it.
My wife also loved the spa...

title: “Home away from home”
text: The hotel was very comfortable, and the staff was amazing - attentive to our every need. We were celebrating our anniversary, and the staff made sure we had a wonderful stay. Coming back after a day touring the city was just like coming home. We recommend the hotel and will definitely return for another stay whenever we come back to Boston.

title: “Perfect”
text:
Well, I am sitting in my room at the Hotel Contessa as I write this. I slept well last night. The sheets were a little too starched for me, but it was very comfortable. This room is a king suite. It's very large: separated living room big enough to accommodate 6 adults easily, Separate bar area, huge bath room, and separate bedroom. Tons of drawers and closet space. The hotel is very well designed from they layout of the floors to the decor that you don't notice unless u want to. In other words, it is not flashy, but very comfortable. If u look around, u see everything flows. The in room menu has a section for pets and the mini bar also has pet snacks along with people snacks. So, one can assume it a pet friendly hotel. The staff is very attentive. What makes it five star in my view is the little things...smiling Valets, a call to our room after we checked in to ask if everything was satisfactory, real stemware and barware in the room...comfortable furniture everywhere...it goes on and on.
The restaurant here is so wonderfully NOT San Antonio river walk fare. The river walk restaurants offer boring Tex Mex and seem to offer way too much deep fryer previously frozen food. The restaurants on the river walk seem a little worn out and boring. This restaurant, Las Ramblas, features fantastic fresh continental gourmet. Not to be missed is their tapped...exquisite. I had asparagus with manchego (sp?) cheese with truffle oil, my comanion had the shrimp skewer. We both noticed that each was prepared fresh...it was that noticeable and evident. For dessert I had an heirloom tomato tart. Had I not known, I would have not known it had tomatoes in it. It looked like a piece of pie, lattice crust on top. It tasted like nothing I have ever had...served with a Ginger creme and fresh berries. 
This hotel is a vacation in itself. The bar was bustling last night and a contrast to the bars on the river walk. It is elegant and cozy. Overall experience was very positive and we will be back. We are from Houston.

title: “Wonderful!”
text: What a nice little hotel! Immaculate, friendly, safe, and in a great neighbourhood. I loved the Beacon and I will make it my "home base" whenever I am in NYC in the future.

title: “Edison good value and central”
text:
Went as a group of eight. Was a little wary after some of reviews. Yes the rooms are tired and in need of refurbishment but for a centrally located hotel in New York you cannot beat this. If like us you do not spend long in your hotel room this is fine for the price you pay. Could do with tea and coffee in the room but we just went to deli in the foyer and took a cup to the room.
Ate a few times in the deli in the foyer and this is quite good and service efficient.
It's not the Waldorf but you get what you pay for

title: “Small and impersonal”
text:
The hotel's lobby looks nice, but it is not relaxing. There are many restaurants and bars downstairs, and it is pretty loud and busy. I stayed in a small room with a full sized bed, and paid over $300. The room is old looking, with chipping paint. There is no coffee maker in the room, and you have to pay for internet. I was on the 16th floor, and you could still hear the traffic. I could also hear the maids loudly speaking in the hallway until about 11pm (on a weeknight).
The bellhop charged me $2 to hold my small carry-on suitcase for the day when I went to work. It's just ridiculous to charge for something so petty. I normally would have tipped for good service, but to charge this up front was off-putting and I did not tip on top of that.

title: “Great hotel”
text:
Stayed for 4 nights. Very nice room on the top floor (as I had requested) and so a great view of the water and distant airport.
Very helpful staff. Ask them to book the Duck Tour for you so that you don't have to queue.
Excellent location so that you can walk to all the usual tourist sites.

title: “Great location & big rooms for NYC but some shortcomings that will mean I won't be back”
text:
As somebody who has started travelling to NYC at least once a month on business I am desperately searching for that hotel that just works - doesn't need to be fancy, it just needs to work. Sadly The Benjamin isn't that hotel. 
The location (Lex & 50th) is great, the rooms are big (mini-suites) which makes a change for NYC and the hotel restaurant is good. However nice as these things are they don't make up for tired/grubby looking furniture & decor, in-room wifi that is so pathetic AT&T 3G was a much faster option (and a lot cheaper!), and NOISY rooms that mean despite a fancy sleep menu, a good night's sleep is hard to get. 
So my search continues....

title: “Excellent location and superior staff”
text:
I booked this hotel through hotwire for a cultural trip for our 10th grade class. We booked five rooms for our class and chaperones and stayed five nights. Because our hotwire booking included complimentary breakfast, the hotel honored that commitment for our group even though their policy had changed. The breakfast was just right for us. We had the kids eat an hour before we left for the day and they were good to go until lunch. The location was great for us to execute our itinerary which included sites as far north as The Cloisters and as far south as Battery Park. 
The rooms we booked were junior suites with two beds and a pullout couch in each room. Our room was always clean when we came back from our sightseeing excursions. The view from our window was a hoot -- someone in the building across the way had the torso of a mannequin on their patio. For many of the kids and myself, this was our first New York experience and it was a smashing success. Thank you, Avalon hotel for giving us a great home base for our trip!

title: “Unimpressed”
text: I was shocked at the dirtiness of rooms that cost over $400 per day. And no ipod players; no honor bars so no refrigerators.

title: “Nice hotel but somewhat noisy”
text: I stayed at the hotel on Friday, July 23. The hotel was very nice, and the staff was very friendly. I loved the Nautica theme! The rooms were nice sized, but I woke up at 6:30 a.m. when the guests in the adjacent room got up. I could hear almost every word of their conversation, and they were speaking at a normal level. Also, the ice machine was three to four doors down, and it's behind a door. However, it's necessary for the door to be open to access the ice, and you could hear it whenever somebody got ice. Parking was $32.00 per day, which was slightly above what appears to be an average rate of $25.00 per day for San Francisco. After paying the room rate, taxes and parking, the room came to about $355.00 for one night. For just a little more than half that amount, I would opt for the Grosvenor Suites Hotel, which is older and does not have a lobby to speak of. However, if you're looking for a good location and a nice size room for a reasonable price, I would recommend the Grosvenor Suites. If you're looking to impress somebody, then I would stay at the Argonaut Hotel.

title: “Great hotel”
text: Had a problem with a sister hotel in the city so called and the staff at Microtel was wonderful from the first call. Booked 3 rooms for 2 nights; they put us all together and even an adjoining room for us to watch our grandson while the others went to the UT game. Wonderful stay - will use Microtel again.

title: “Basic but Spot On”
text:
After a 10 hour trip and a 30 minute taxi ride we were welcomed by a very pleasant receptionist. The rooms were basic but large comfy beds, and plenty of clean towels did make up for no room with a view !!. Breakfast was included in the price which again was
the usual american style, waffles, toast, english muffins with plenty of juice and coffee.
 On leaving the hotel, reception printed our tickets, in fact they were most helpful arranging the taxi to the airport, I would recommend this hotel and would stay there again.

title: “very pleased”
text: I stayed here for the Beale Street Music Festival, and although it was about a 20 minute ride to downtown, the hotel was very nice. We had a king-sized bed that was very comfortable, plenty of desk space if you need to get some work done, a nice flat screen tv as well as a microwave and mini-fridge. They also offered a complimentary breakfast with cereal, muffins, bagels, and waffles. It was an excellent deal.

title: “Very helpful staff, rooms are better than outside appearance”
text:
The outside appearance looks very unappealling. The rooms were much nice than I expected. Rooms were clean, large and had many amenities..small fridge, microwave and coffee maker. 
Downtown location was okay but was rather noisy. Parking is an additional$10

title: “only average”
text:
Excellent locartion,close to Universal and hollywood.Roomy, clean and quiet free, shuttle to Universal.
Did not like the cost of parking, wifi,breakfast.Also did not like the fact that they did not explain the ease of use of the near by subway.They did not keep discount coupons and were very pushy to sell us organised tours.and expansive tickets
We were missing constantly shampoo,soaps etc...
To summarise: only average with important pros but many faults as well.
too expansive for what that was offered

title: “Great stay!”
text: I really enjoyed my couple of nights here. I stayed in the Bay Tower which is the smaller hotel approx 10 min walk from the Marina Tower. I was on the 7th floor with a stunning view of the marina from the large balcony. The rooms are very big and nicely decorated (30% bigger than Marina Tower rooms I was told). Bed was super comfortable. I walked through the Marina Tower which is a much bigger hotel. The lobby is more impressive and the bar/restaurant there was more happening, plus there is Starbucks there...the Bay Tower just has a bar/restaurant. I was more than content with the Bay Tower though! I reserved through the Sheraton website and got a ridiculously good deal, $130ish. I paid 4 times that much for one night at a hotel in Santa Monica! Location: it's a bit far from downtown, but if you love to walk, as we do, it's fine, plus you are walking by the water so it's really pretty. A cab to the zoo cost $20 incld tip, cab from the Gaslamp was $15 with tip. Given the great rate it made sense for us to stay a little further out and take the occasional cab.

title: “Great Location and Service”
text:
The hotel is in a prime location in Boston - Copley Place, and has indoor connections to the Copley Place Mall and the adjoining T station. The staff are very courteous and helpful. 
Couple of negatives - depending on the season and offers, the rates are sometimes too high. Also, for a hotel of this calibre, they could offer free internet and complimentary breakfast, but they dont.
Apart from these, a great place to stay.

title: “Not your Four Seasons but....”
text: OK, I feel that the Grant Plaza definitely does not deserve the negative reviews it has garnered on this site. Sure, you're not going to get pampered like you would at the Four Seasons (which is like ~400 bucks a night) but for a budget traveler like me, this was perfect. It's got everything you would want: central location: close to Powell St Stn (about a 10 minute walk), in Chinatown. Not to mention clean beds, clean bathrooms, and a TV. I also arrived at the hotel at around 10 in the morning and even though check-in time was at 2pm, they let me go up to my room (although it hadn't been cleaned yet). Of course, I've stayed in better hotels, but this is SF, and to get a room downtown for 70 a night is a steal. I would definitely recommend this to the budget-conscious traveler who won't spend that much time in their hotel room anyway and only need a place to sleep and shower.

title: “Convenient for the Airport”
text:
A nice comfortable hotel near the airport with good views across the harbour. Just had the nachos in the bar so can't comment on the restauraunt but the breakfast was fine. We only had a few hours in San Diego as we were visiting family all day but we really wished we could have stayed here longer.
You get a courtesy bus to the airport and we had a lovely driver who's wife came from Scotland!
They tried to charge for overnight parking so we took the car back to the hire depot and walked back to the hotel along the sea front.
Had a peaceful hour sat outside the bar overlooking the marina.

title: “Great Customer Service!”
text: Doug and Kathy are doing a great job! They were very helpful in assisting me with my reservation. No doubts,next time i'll stay in this hotel!

title: “I got Bed Bug Bites!”
text: Came here last weekend for a 50th birthday celebration. Three people in our room. Room was outdated and old but the bathroom was redone and was nice. The lobby was lovely. We went to the bar for a drink and appetizer before going out for dinner and when we arrived all the tables that were empty were sitting filthy with dirty glasses. No one offered to remove them for us. So we left and did not stay for a drink. Champagne was delivered to our room as a gift from a friend and the man that brought it would not open it for us. But really the worst part was when I got home a couple days later my back was itchy with a rash. I asked my husband to take pictures of it and we now realize it was bed bug bites from The Waldorf. I normally stay at the Benjamin or Affinia hotels but because it was a special birthday we thought it would be fun to stay somewhere "fancy" eek never again!

title: “Great base, great value”
text:
Stayed here for 4 nights from 18th June.
Had read all the reviews and I think I knew just what to expect and it didn't disappoint.
Check-in very quick and efficient, very friendly staff on arrival. The room was very spacious, lots of storage space etc and was clean and cool - good air-con worked very quickly.
The bathroom was on the small side given the overall room space, but it didn't detract from the overall experience. We didn't eat in so only made use of the fridge for keeping drinks cold, so I can't really comment on the suitability of amenities in there.
Staff very friendly and helpful and always on hand (24hr).
This hotel is ideally located for the NY visitor, it's quiet enough not to be a problem for very light sleepers yet not far from many of the main sights. No great views, but you get what you pay for and in the Eastgate, the money you save by not being in a swanky area or overlooking Times Square for instance can easily be redistributed to help you enjoy much more of NY. Anyway, who wants to stay in Times Square?
Happy to recommend this to anyone considering a 'budget' hotel in NY.

title: “Go somewhere else, price is not that good.”
text:
We stayed 2 nights @ the Valley Inn in July 2006, we were there for Moto GP and flew in and out of San Jose. I found this place on Hotels.com and contacted them directly to book. Price was fair, property was horrible! We arrived really late @ night, got lost, the owners who live on sight we asleep and were not answering the phone, we stood outside trying to wake them up for 45 minutes before we were able to check. (just to clarify I did let the owner know we would be arriving late in the evening) 
Once checked in we went to the room and we were disgusted. The room was hot, and I mean hot, muggy, & smelledof mildew. The sheets were mismatched and stained, the carpet was dark green with stains and bald spots throughout. The bathroomhad 2 towels (there was 3 of us) and the towels we the size of wash cloths. Shower had no water pressure, no tollietries were provided in the room. Air conditioner was at the same height as the bed closest to it, so when we had it on to try and cool the room, the person in that bed would freeze because the air was blowing right on them! 
All in all, hated it, also it was in a bad area, close to the airport, yes, but kind of scary neighborhood. My advice, look somewhere else, don't be cheap, pay a little more for a better product.

title: “Small rooms but very nice staff”
text: We stayed there during Hurricane Sandy. The staff was outstanding. Even without power it wasn't too bad. They tried their best to make us comfortable. We were there two days before the storm and enjoyed our stay even though the rooms were very, very small.

title: “Great stay!”
text: This is a very nice hotel. I got a great deal through hotwire and, because of the price and the fact that it is in Manhattan, I was not expecting much but only to sleep and do some shopping and sightseeing. Boy was a surprised! Everything is pretty much walking distance from this hotel. There is even a subway steps away. I almost never get a free breakfast (95%) when I stay at hotels, no matter the stat rating. Thus, I was surprised to not only get breakfast with my stay, but get smorgasbord. The only problem I had was that my room was taken due to the fact that I did not call in a late check-in (a day later, ops!), but they quickly accommodated my needs even though this was my fault. If I was on a budget to NYC, I would stay here again, although I would want to explore another hotel next time in town, but that is just personal choice. Also, if you do want to stay in this area, there is a Hilton Gardens hotel right next door. After keeping the prices, don’t waste your time or money! Pick the Hampton.

title: “Would be better off at homeless shelter!!! Perfect if your looking for drugs or a hooker”
text:
This is by far the worst hotel I have ever been in!! Upon walking in there were two ladies at the front desk let me stand and stare at them finishing thier personal conversation before even saying one word to me. Then it was what can I do for you about 5 mins later, Amy is the one who at first helped me she was very rude not sure if she was having a bad day or but I did nothing to be treated like crap. I should have left right then, after checking and walking to the room I see a roach crawl right in front of me!!! When I went back to the front and told amy about this she completely denied the bugs and told me I couldn't have my money back. I decied rather than donate my hard earned money to them I would stay,(should have left) 
The shower curtain covered in mold and torn room had a fowl odor. The towl had a brownish stain on it like blood sort of washed out! I for the first time ever was afraid after that to touch anything for fear of getting herpes or any other infection!!! I didnt stay I left there and went next door to the comfort inn who which is about $10 more but was like being in a castle compared to there.. Would never ever go back to any Best inn and suites their new name should be worst inn and suites!!!!

title: “Why so negative?”
text: After reading all the horror stories below, I was a little worried about what to expect. The hotel was fine, a standard tourist hotel. I paid $145 for a decent-sized room with a king bed. The bathroom wasn't huge, but I didn't expect it to be. There was a separate area for the sink/mirror. Service was fine, location was great. My only complaint was the lack of a "Do Not Disturb" sign to hang on the door.

title: “you can't get better in the heart of Hollywood”
text:
We decided to book our stay in Hollyowwod at the Orchid Suites after reading all the good reviews about the Hotel and we were not dissapointed at all. It lived up to everything.
The staff here are so helpful and friendly there is nothing they wouldn't for us. Our room was so big and comfortable and we found the fact that we had a kitchen a wonderfull plus for us. There was two TV's one in the living room and one in the bedroom. The bathroom was also a good size and had a bath. The lounge room sofa and chairs were so comfy it was a dream after a long day sightseeing to come to our room and sink into them.
The breakfast that the hotel provided each mornings was lovely and although it only consisted of pastry, fruit and cereal as well as coffee we found it more than adequate for our needs. We only got to use the pool once as when we were there in LA they were having very mild weather and the pool was a bit cold.
The laundry was well equiped and they also had a ice and vending machines as well. The free parking for guests was also a big plus. Free internet was provided and I used it alot.
The shopping center next door had lots of wonderful food places and we didn't have a bad meal once.
While we read on other reviews just how close the hotel was to Hollywood itself we couldn't beleive how true it was. only about 2 mins walk and there we were standing on the Hollywood stars and we were out front the Kodak Theatre.
Tour buses, Wax museums, were also just there after a short walk.
I honestly can't say a bad word about this Hotel and would reccomend anyone to stay here.

title: “Great rooms and Service”
text: For the amount of money you pay, this is one of the best values for a nights' stay in Downtown Detroit! It's very clean, airy, with friendly and accommodating staff! Plus it's attached to the casino (for some late night to do) and its on the strip with the majority of the nightlife of Downtown Detroit. :)

title: “Nice hotel with a lot to do around it”
text: Very friendly and helpful front desk staff. Nice welcome after a day traveling. Room was clean and decent size. Pool area is nice and clean as well. Although we didn't venture out of the hotel due to the weather, there is plenty of shopping and dining in very close proximity.

title: “Decent stay”
text:
I had a slight reservation regarding staying here given some of the recent reviews on this property. However, I opted to stay here after two rather annoying incidents at the Marriott right across the street (BTW, strike three on the Marriott as I went over there to meet with a coworker who is a Marriott slave - only to find the main restaurant was closed and everyone shoved into a conference room which doubled as a bar and restaurant!).
My overall experience was fine. Checkin was quick and uneventful (I got two cookies on this arrival!!!). The hotel is undergoing renovations so as of March 2012, you will see a fair amount of work taking place - especially on the first floor where they are totally gutting rooms. 
My room was on the 4th floor which took a while to get to. The room itself was quite large, spacious, with a bar set up, and large living room.
The air conditioner was not working and this was one of the first really warm days of the year. I opened the windows in the living room and the bedroom which made conditions better. I was told that the maintenance people can easily reset the air conditioner, but found that it was odd that you would even have to do that in a room that was recently renovated.
The hallways were somewhat noisy on my floor - a large convention appeared to be there. It wound up not being an issue given how tired I was but a light sleeper might have been a bit more concerned.
Breakfast was standard for DoubleTree - and much less expensive than you find at a lot of hotel breakfast operations ($12.00 I think).
Staying here is more likely to be done if you're part of a group or are a Hilton fan....

title: “Nothing special”
text:
I recently returned from a 3 night stay at Hotel on Rivington. I thought the people staying at the hotel were a bit self important. The hotel itself was trying to be really funky. The elevators are lined with leather and I found they really stunk. Room was ok, sparse. Comfortable bed and nice sheets. The amenities were great.
The service was there is you asked for it, but we felt like the hotel was run by kids. Not much experience and not overly friendly, which is fine.
After a few initial glitches (call for room service at 1 in the morning: wrong room, etc.)it actually improved. I asked the conceiarge a few questions which were well answered and had two surprise lovely breakfasts in the hotel restaurant on the last 2 days.
All in all, there really is no choice for that area, as it is really the only hotel. Love the location. I suspect this hotel may disappear into oblivivian as it really was trying hard, yet nothing special. I really hope they can make it work.

title: “Awesome Staff !!!!”
text:
I have been going to this Holiday Inn for 5 years, And the staff is awesome they make feel right at home. From the front office to the bar, food, cleaning ladys.
Just complete all around.
Beds and rooms very clean
Pool clean
Shuttle service & staff is great.
Bruce B, Maggie C, George D, George W, Greta H, Susan H, Caretlq, Anna, Michael, Simo
Thanks Again for a job well done.
Customer for life.
Gary F
Jacksonville Fl

title: “Convenient to Memphis Attractions”
text:
Rooms were nice, staff was very helpful and accommodating. Because it was Elvis week, the hotel was pretty full, but when we requested a late check-out, they didn't hesitate to push it back for us. The indoor pool was great for the kids, and the fitness area was one of the best I've ever used.
While most of the attractions we wanted to see in Memphis were several blocks away, the hotel itself is at the north end of the trolley line on Main St., allowing us to reach our destinations inexpensively and quickly. 
Everyone in Memphis was very kind and friendly. We stopped on our way back from taking our son to college and wanted a day to do something different. I would definitely plan another trip to Memphis; there is a lot to do and see, and we only got to a small portion of it. Great city; great hotel!

title: “A gem downtown and close to everything!”
text:
I originally wrote this review on Yelp. 
Let me get PARKING out of the way: We parked in a parking structure on Mason across the street with in and out privileges, for $27 a day. Yes, it's a lot, but where else are you going to park?
Loves:
- Perfect location! Walking distance to so many restaurants and stores. We walked to Chinatown and Fisherman's Wharf, too.
- Friendly and helpful staff at check in.
- Beautiful headboard, comfortable beds, clean (they bleach them :) sheets, and pillows that melt like marshmallows.
- Three cute, different chairs in the room
- Gorgeous lamps (we took so many photos with them)
- Mini fridge
- Free Wi-Fi 
- Matching robes!
Meh:
- The dresser had small drawers. I was only able to stack two shirts at a time. Plenty of hangers, though.
- Water pressure was low, but hot water was immediate and didn't go cold when someone flushed somewhere.
Places you should walk to and eat (we did!): Farm table, Golden Era, Brenda's French Soulfood.

title: “good choice”
text: old fashioned hotel,but with some unique features,central to most tourist attractions,Madison square gardens and Empire state building for example.

title: “Will definitely stay here every time I go to Manhattan and will reccommend it to friends and family”
text: An awesome experience. Stayed there for 5 nights. Took my daughter and her two friends to see New York for the first time, to celebrate my daughters 23rd birthday and to see the Macy's parade. Upon arrival they gave my daughter a bottle of wine, had balloons and a cake in our room. Excellent staff service. Excellent location. 4 blks to Macy's, Empire State Building, Times Square.. Parade passes right in front hotel. Awesome for families with young children..slightly bigger then hotel rooms. Equipped with full size refrigerator, microwave, sink, dishwasher, dishes, pots and pans, utensils, plates, crock pot, knives, portable electric stove, sofa bed. Includes free breakfast. We got our money's worth. I will be staying here whenever I visit Manhattan. good deli's nearby and a great Italian restaurant nearby.

title: “Good location for mid-town business”
text: This Hilton was updated just a couple of years ago and looks and feels great. It's a busy mid-town hotel with great lobby bars. The rooms are compact, but have all the necessities that you need and some of the luxuries that you want! The front desk is well staffed and the elevators are fast!

title: “Resort is a little over selling--bad food!”
text: I attended a 4 day meeting at the hotel. I read the Trip Advisor reviews and was prepared for the worst. That probably helped, because it was better than I thought it would be. I didn't have problems with the staff...they were all helpful and polite. The technology didn't work so well, though. Meeting room wireless was spotty. The food is average...and when you consider "average" in the world of hotels, it's not great. I travel a great deal, so my standards may be high, but in southern California, I would expect a lot of great, fresh healthy food. Not so much! It's more like hotel food available in Indiana. No thank you! All in all, it wasn't as bad as I suspected, but except for the views, it's not a real resort where everything is over the top. The weather can't be beat, but you don't have to stay at the hotel to get that!!

title: “Great place to stay in a very convenient location”
text: Knowing how hard it is to find an affordable place to stay in New York City that seems worth the money, I turned to Tripadvisor for suggestions. While The Sanctuary didn't have perfect reviews, the majority were positive (and I'm well aware some people are never happy regardless of circumstances). Overall, my fiance and I had a great experience staying on a Tuesday through Thursday during the week. The room we stayed in was a bit small (I wasn't surprised by New York standards though), but very well arranged and had everything we needed. Not much of a view from our room, but I don't expect to stare out the window much when I'm in New York. For only being a half a block away from Times Square, we were impressed with how quiet it was. The staff were incredibly friendly and helpful, even helping us with rather last minute arrangements for transportation back to the airport. As some other reviewers have mentioned, the breakfast was simple, but I was impressed by the fact that there was breakfast and it wasn't an additional charge (I've stayed at several really nice hotels where they don't offer anything other than maybe a restaurant or direct you to the local Starbucks). The food was good and the coffee was hot, which meets my morning standards. Free Wi-Fi in the rooms too, which is always a plus. Convenient location to Times Square and Broadway shows while not being too far of a cab ride or subway transit to other locations. Overall, I would definitely stay here again and recommend it to friends.

title: “Outstanding Service”
text:
After a disappointing stay in Beverly Hills at Mr C the Four Seasons in New York showed the difference between four star and five star plus. The rooms were large the bathrooms huge, beds incredibly comfortable and curtains that really did black out the room.
The best bit though are the people from the Concierges who know everything and can ake miracles happen to the bellmen who greet you and say farewell.
I can't recommend the hotel highly enough.

title: “Nice Hotel, only OK location.”
text:
Chicago was the starting point for our 3 week trip in the States. We originally booked this hotel online coming up to the time we were due to go away. Starting to panic, we just looked for a nice, recognizable name somewhere that looked accessible. 
We were pleasantly surprised. We aimed for something cheap and cheerful and that is what we got. The hotel was nice, it was clean and comfortable whilst not being too over the top. 
Rooms were nice, again clean and comfortable which is most important for me and spacious enough. It also has Internet access for guests in the lobby. The staff for the most part were nice but had maybe one or two members who could have been more helpful or even just friendly! The hotel had a restaurant which again was nice but again nothing too fussy, if that is what you're looking for.
The biggest problem with the hotel I found was perhaps the location. Whilst it was perfect for sightseeing in the Grant Park / aquarium, planetarium and museum area, it was a little out of the way for the rest and for night life etc. We found ourselves most nights just ending up in the hotel restaurant because we were so tired from walking all day and hadn't the energy to walk a ways to find another decent restaurant, which was very disappointing.
Overall, the hotel surprised us as we were starting to worry over its location. We received a lovely welcome and in general we were happy with our stay.

title: “Sundowners in the City”
text:
Location is right in the heart of Manhattan two blocks from Times Square. Like others have said the street outside can look a bit seedy but no-one ever bothered us, and you very quickly reach the biz and the Subway.
The room was clean, fresh, well appointed with kitchen, great shower, TV. We even, if you knew to lean right then look left, had a view of the top of the Empire State Building, total bonus! And it was quiet through the night.
Boy, the breakfast room was busy, even saw someone eating standing up, although there was an overspill area which we never actually had to explore. We were lucky enough to enjoy the Sundowner Reception that they have midweek nights; similarly busy but people were friendly and happy to chat.
The concierge desk was very helpful, especially Cari who fixed us up with maps and tours when we didn't quite know where to start. We wouldn't recommend the City Sights blue hop on/off bus however. We missed our city cruise waiting for a blue bus while about 3 red ones came and went. We discovered through overhearing another guest that the concierge could arrange a shared van transfer to Newark Airport, and that saved us about 30 bucks over a taxi.
One or two minor problems; one day our room wasn't cleaned, but housekeeping came as soon as we contacted them. We were billed twice for renting one movie, but that was easily corrected. On the other hand the two bell guys gave an amazing impromptu rendering of Hit the Road Jack while we waited in the lobby for our airport van. So cool, Jersey Boys watch out!
Minor complaints sound really lame knowing how badly New York has suffered since Sandy hit. Anyway, what is needed is to get back working and showing off their great city to a slew of tourists, so good luck to NYC.

title: “Cool, Comfortable, Convienant and Great Staff”
text: Last minute walk up reservation (minutes from airport) but given same rate as online. Super friendly staff (from desk to bar tender). Modern chic atmosphere. Nice bar/lounge leading to great outdoor patio area. Loved the art wall showcasing local artists! No unnecessary literature in rooms (low carbon footprint) but all needed info easily accessible with remote via big screen HD television. Great night sleep, even hung out until noon check out. Not luxury but nice change from the standard hotel room, definitely will look for Aloft hotels in other locations.

title: “Very nice hotel”
text:
This hotel is very nice and recent.
This hotel has a very good location. Very conveniant to sleep there.
The underground was very close to the hotel 10 min by walking.
We will go in this hotel again in we go to NY !
Room was giant, clean , and recent
Nothing to say about the personals...
wifi was available.

title: “We were totally satisfied!”
text: We stayed at the Talbott last weekend for what was our first trip to Chicago. It did not disappoint in any way. The desk staff was welcoming, the room very spacious, clean and comfortable and the breakfast was scrumptious. Probably the best feature I found was Tim, the concierge. He was extremely knowledgeable and helpful. He gave us a number of options when we asked for reccomendations and was quick to secure reservations for us where needed. Directions were always on point and he seemed genuinely interested in making our stay very memorable. Absolutely personable and helpful! When we return to Chicago the Talbott will definitely be our hotel of choice!

title: “Rooms vary a lot”
text:
My colleague and I stayed in two separate rooms at the Monaco, and even though we both reserved Monaco Queen rooms, hers--on the 3rd floor--was cramped and got a fair amount of street noise, while mine--on the 10th floor, a VIP floor--was very spacious and peaceful, with a nice view. The rooms were very clean and comfortable, with excellent amenities. Front desk, bell, and housekeeping staff were all courteous and helpful, although the person checking me in forgot to tell me about hotel amenities like the evening wine reception and Kimpton InTouch amenities like free wi-fi. We had breakfast each morning at the hotel restaurant, Sazerac, because our room rates included continental breakfast. The food was quite good but service was slow most mornings.
The hotel is reasonably close to both the Convention Center, where our conference was held, and Pike Place Market, where we liked to go in our spare time. Overall, it was a very pleasant stay. The rooms were not remarkable, but the gracious service was definitely above the norm.

title: “Couldn't Have Been Any Better!”
text: My wife and I just arrived home from vacation in New York from October 1st-8th. We found that with this being our first trip to the city it was difficult to choose from the multitude of accomodation options available. We couldn't be more thankful for having chosen the Cassa.
