The location is ideal within only a short walk of Time Square and only steps from access to the Subway. I am an avid runner and was easily able to take the subway to Central Park for daily jogs. Our room (King Bed) was of good size and very clean/modern. The building is in very good condition overall and elevators are fast/efficient. The staff is the real treasure of the hotel. Front desk personel was continually helpful in providing direction and advice in terms of enjoying the city in addition to continually offering assistance with any accomodation questions/thoughts we might wish to discuss. Really, we didn't have any questions as the hotel was exceptional. Will definitely recommend the hotel to others and will quite possibly return.

title: “Amazing hotel, perfect location; believe the hype!”
text:
This hotel is amazing. Beautiful, historical architecture, large rooms with great accommodations and an incredibly friendly staff. Besides the grandeur, the hotel is also right in the heart of Downtown Austin, off 6th Street where all the action happens at night -- live music, bars and restaurants everywhere. 
We stayed in the Historic King Balcony room which -- obviously -- has a balcony attached to the room. View was great, plus allowed for an end-of-day cool down outside, people watching and breakfast in the sunshine. 
The hotel is as beautiful in real life as it looks in the pictures and the experience is worth the money if you can afford it. It certainly isn't in everyone's budget, but if you can make it work, you won't be disappointed.

title: “Great location, clean, and well run - but pretty average for a Hyatt.”
text:
Stayed here three nights with my wife for fun - we chose this hotel because of the proxmity to the National Mall. The location is great - Union Station metro is less than 5 minutes walk, the Nat'l Mall is a stones throw away, we spent a lot of time all over town and concluded at the end of the weekend we had made the right choice.
The room was updated and very clean. The staff we interacted with were helpful and friendly.
We had a Regency Club room and while it was a nice amenity, the actual club was nowehere near as nice as other Regency Clubs I have visited. It was pretty small, dark, and just not that great.
Overall, we were pleased with our stay and the hotel - I think what keeps me from rating it higher is that it is a very average looking property there is no wow factor. It's certainly more than adequate, there's just not anything special about it - it's like the Toyota Camry of hotels. That said, the location is excellent and we had a great weekend rate.

title: “In the middle of it all”
text: The Marquis is a great place to stay if you want to be in the middle of Time Square. Hotel is well kept, and shows like the Marriott flagship. Friendly staff is everywhere you look and willing to help with everything. The rooms are quiet despite the kaos in the street below. Great place to stay if you bring kids as the room is always 5 minutes from the action. Ask for a Time Square view, high floor, great to watch the people. Room service is prompt and delicous( also a bit expensive, this is NYC after all). Enjoy your stay and don't miss Toys R Us. Its an adventure in it self.

title: “Never stay here!”
text: Whew, this place was bad. The pool had such a scum on it that I wouldn't let my kids in it, the whole place smelled, and in the middle of the night drunken guests called my room and made obscene comments. I was literally scared of this place, and when I reported it to the desk, they just said they couldn't stop the calls because they were coming from within the building. Sounds like the beginning of a teen horror movie, doesn't it?

title: “OK hotel. OK service. Great location. No repeat visit from us though.”
text: The location is great. The front desk service was fine however on the 2 occassions we asked concierge for assistance, we were treated rudely and dismissively. In fact I found the concierge treatment quite upsetting. 1 query was about Alcatraz tours and we were rudely told "they are all sold out" and no further effort was made to suggest an alternative. The second query, I asked where a certain street was and the guy looked at me and said "I have no idea what you are talking about" . Just so rude. It's a shame the helpful front desk staff can't also do the concierge work. Rooms are exactly as pictured and described but many parts of the hotel ie) hallways, show signs of wear and tear. On a few occassions we were waiting for ages for lifts as they were being used by maintencance staff. There was just something not right about this place, we couldn't put our finger on it. It's like a mediocre hotel pretending to be exclusive. Don't get a street side room - very noisy.

title: “Good location and value, but small rooms”
text:
The Newton hotel is good situated. It is 10 seconds walking distance from the metro station (96th station). There are McDonalds and Starbucks near the hotel. The rooms are ok - clean, (equipped with microwave, coffee machine, TV, air conditioning, fridge, iron and hair dryer) BUT they are very small. Quality of sleeping was average, because the air conditioning was loud and the bed was not very comforable. Wireless internet was not complimentary and we paid also for luggage lockers in the luggage room.
But globally I would recommend this hotel, because of good situation and price. I know - it is pretty expensive, but it is still less expensive than lots of other hotels in Manhattan.

title: “THEY GET IT!!!”
text:
I don't know why this hotel is not ranked No. 1. They have the right concept when it comes to complete hotel hospitality. I originally booked for two nights (Friday & Saturday 9/14-9/15). Got there and we had the standard room in the main building. However, I'd requested a riverview and newly renovated room and called the front desk. I could get the suite in the new addition for only $10 more a night. Great! We transferred to our new suite in the newly added San Fernando Tower and were blown away. Talk about WOW factor. We could smell and see the newness of this addition and our suite was huge and we liked the way the bedroom was partitioned off from the living area. My husband said it was like a house. We had a fantastic view from our huge balcony with a table and two chairs. We looked smack dab onto the popular San Fernando Cathedral, the main park of the River Walk and all of the surrounding views. I could even see a glimpse of the El Mercado market. We had a flatscreen in both the living area and bedroom and a kitchenette with microwave oven, coffee maker, mini fridge and sink/faucet area. There was plenty cabinet space throughout the suite. The bathroom was cavernous with plenty of marble counter space for all of my necessities. When we saw the suite I added on another night I was so impressed. We were on the 9th floor right across the hall from the inside jacuzzi/pool and one of their many open-air terraces. We found a quiet time Saturday night where we (just he and I) enjoyed the jacuzzi, cognac, and smooth jazz being played on their Satellite Watercolors system.
There is another public area on the 15th floor of the tower where there's an inside lounging area with comfy sofas, chairs, lamps, etc., attached to an open-air terrace with lots of tables and chairs. In the main building on the 22nd floor is the fitness room, rest rooms, laundry room, another big open-air terrace and the roof-top pool with two jacuzzis. There is a second laundry room on the 5th floor.
Of course the big pull of this hotel brand is all the incredible complimentary services they extend. You can't beat the free breakfasts and evening meals but to get THREE, count 'em, THREE alcoholic drinks for free is simply unheard of. That is until you stay here. Every evening we were on the 2nd floor at 5:30 for our evening "kickback". They served foods like hot dogs, chicken fingers, salad, nachos, chips, mac & cheese, chili, soups, pasta & meatballs. The drink options were mixed drinks, beer and wine. Every morning we worked off all of these calories by spending a productive hour in their fitness room. One could get an excellent workout on one of their 5 treadmills, an elliptical, a bike, three weight lifting machines and free weights. There was a flat screen TV as well as towels and water fountains. Oh yeah and excellent roof-top views of surrounding San Antonio, including the Hemisphere Tower.
Let’s not forget that the building is a piece of history in itself. Formerly The Alamo Bank, built in 1929, one can learn about its history through pictures with placards in the basement and see exhibits of the back-in-the-day vaults and locking mechanisms used then. The Drury brand constructed and lengthened that end of the Riverwalk as well. Very interesting stuff. There is a Chase Bank currently in the building.
Wi-fi was free in the room which is a huge plus for me!
The staff is very friendly.
When I return to San Antonio I no longer have to think about where we will be staying. Hands down it will be the DRURY PLAZA RIVERWALK.

title: “Average hotel. Not as nice as some Kimptons.”
text: I thought the rooms were a little odd, kind of dreary. The decor was some blend of "trendy with a seaside theme." That said, the beds are the same from one Kimpton to the next.....fabulous!!!!! The most comfortable beds in the world! (In my humble opinion, that is.) Room service was prompt, bar and restaurants were "ok." I'll probably stay there again to get my Kimpton points but it is not my favorite hotel. Not bad, just average in every way.

title: “who cares about the noise with prefect ten and tartinins.”
text: I took my wife to NYC for her 32nd birthday and I couldn't have picked a better place, If your sick of the norm go to Tribeca Grand. Close to soho , canal street, Little Italy. Good service over all barmaids could be a little nicer but who cares after a couple of drinks. Doormen and Front Desk very helpful, Mike A at the Concierge Desk was very help with places to eat and go to. Rooms were clean, make sure you ask for a gold fish at front desk. Cd player in the room with cool music, plenty to do. Far enough away from Broadway, Time square, and Plant hollywood but close enough if you want to take the subway up town. Don't stay here if you go to bed early Church is hop'n until 2 am.

title: “Amazing! Book it!”
text: Great hotel! I spent weeks deciding which hotel to choose for my bf's surprise 21st Birthday trip. I eventually chose Grace and it was well beyond my expectations. Champagne on arrival, clean, modern, stylish and comfortable room. Everything we needed. The hotel gym, sauna, steam room and pool made the stay, especially as there is a bar separating the pool and the lounge so it becomes one big party area! Had a few great nights of entertainment, including an 80's night and a new band playing. Jeff the barman is a star and one of NYC's top 10 barmen! Just do it, book it, you won't be disappointed.

title: “Memorial Day weekend stay”
text: Stayed for 3 nights, no complaints. Room was clean, yes could use update but for price and location is exactly what we were looking for and would not hesitate to stay again.

title: “A home from home in the Big Apple”
text:
What a wonderful hotel. My fiance and I stayed for six nights in April for my 30th birthday and we couldn't have picked a better place to stay for our first visit to New York. In fact, staying at Casablanca we felt like privileged members of an 'in-the-know' club and felt sorry for people who go to New York and spend their money on bland chain hotels.
We found Casablanca in the DK 'New York Top Ten' guidebook and when we saw it was so highly recommended on TripAdvisor we knew we had to book. I was hesitant about staying near Times Square because of the noise and crowds but, as other reviewers point out, you can barely hear a thing from outside. The fact that Casablanca is a relatively small hotel also makes for a calm atmosphere, especially in Rick's Cafe, which is a great place to unwind - fantastic after a day pounding the streets of NYC! 
The wonderful breakfast, cheese and wine, and complimentary snacks throughout the day all added to the great value of the Casablanca, but the highlight had to be the wonderful staff. Everyone seemed so pleased to have us stay there and were always smiling, ready to chat and pleased to offer suggestions. One morning I mentioned to John at reception that we were going out shopping and he promptly handed me a 20% discount card for Bloomingdales, plus gave us some great tips for shopping downtown. (If you stay here, make sure you ask for lots of tips on where to go as they will always be good ones!)
I read a few reviews before we booked that mentioned the bedrooms are small. We didn't find this to be the case and we booked a queen room, the smallest. There was plenty of room to move about - lots of closet space and a lovely bathroom with very nice toiletries and gorgeous soft towels that were changed twice daily. The temperature of the room we also found fine and the bed very comfortable.
The only thing I would mention about the hotel is that it doesn't have a bar - this didn't bother us at all (there is complimentary wine between 5-8pm and plenty of bars around Times Square) but I guess for some people this might be a disadvantage. I found it made the place feel more like home to be honest but it depends what kind of experience you want from a hotel. If you want excellent service, excellent quality acccommodation and to feel at home as soon as you arrive then pick Casablanca - you will have a great time.

title: “Second time and it's a whole lot better!”
text: This is my second stay here and I just have to say I'm really impressed with what the new owners have done. I stayed here on business right after they took over and there where some real challenges. The place looks totally different. The lobby is remodeled, they put me in a wing that has been totally rehabbed and the rooms look brand new! Planning my trip to Indy I checked reviews before I came back and was surprise how many positive ones there where. A few negatives that seem extreme but I guess you can't please everyone. I enjoyed my stay, thought the restaurant was good and will stay there again!

title: “A Fine Hotel”
text: My wife and I did an overnighter at the Lombardy last weekend (8/6/11) and could not have been more pleased. Made the reservation through "Historical Hotel" site and the price was very fair. The room was wonderful and the location is ideal, close to restaurants, Metro, etc... Only negatives were expensive parking (valet) and breakfast, although delicious, cost $41 which was a bit over the top. That said when we come back to DC we will stay at the Lombardy.

title: “wonderful hotel”
text: We stayed for 4 nights at the Argonaut - our second stay here. The hotel's location at the end of Fisherman's Wharf and almost next to Ghirardelli Square is just about perfect for vacationing travelers - very convenient, yet quiet. Service is excellent, beds are extremely comfortable, and rooms are well decorated and clean. The hotel's restaurant, Blue Mermaid, is very good (although we liked Capurro's across the street better for breakfast). The bowls of fruit in the lobby and the wine hour in the afternoon are great added touches that make you feel good that you decided to stay there.

title: “Superb Customer Service”
text:
I have stayed at a number of Residence Inns this past year and many other Marriott hotels. I traveled with my family over the holidays to Chicago and Residence Inn with the suite concept is the only way to go. I read some reviews about the lady who works the breakfast area, and all of them had positive things to say. I would completely agree with all the reviews. The lady was extremely personable and very interactive with all the guests. If she could help you in any way, she did. One morning, toward the end of the breakfast time, she went table to table checking on all the patrons and even started to deliver stuff to people. She was amazing. The managers should give her a raise, because I would return to the hotel just because of her treatment of the guests.
On my two interations with the front desk staff, they were very cheery and provided for a positive experience.
The room was very clean and quiet. I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: “Disgusting with Roaches!”
text:
We were in town for dog show and stayed here. After some of the reviews on here, I was concerned, but a friend had stayed here 2 years ago and said it was good. I explained at check in that I was concerned and they assured me that my room would be a clean room. We go to the room, it is older and dated, but do-able. Later that evening, we spot cockroaches on the ceiling and on the dresser. I FREAKED OUT! I go to the front desk and they offer to move me 3 doors down. They apologize & send me on my way. I inquire about the cockroaches being in there (knowing how they travel) I am assured that there won't be any. The next night, we kill 2 more roaches. They can also be seen in the light fixture in the bathroom. DISGUSTING! We travel all the time for dog shows and we always stay at budget hotels. NEVER have I had to deal with roaches!!!
I went down to front desk to get towels and there was a lady whispering to the clerk that she needed to change rooms. I pulled her aside afterwards and she told me that she had roaches as well. We were on the lower level and she was on an upper level. So it wasn't just our rooms.
also, the service is not the best. We had a couple of great clerks, but one morning I asked if the water in the pot was hot so I could make tea. I was told that it was. Pumped the water into my cup....it was room temp (maybe even cooler). clerk acted like it was no big deal. 
BEWARE!

title: “Did not live up to Westin standards”
text:
I'd like to preface this with two points. 1. I am a Startwood Vacation Owner and am very familiar with the Westin name 2. There was a cheerleader convention the weekend of our stay.
We stayed at the Indianapolis Westin overnight on 12/12-12/13 and we very disappointed to find out that there was a cheerleader tournament that weekend in Indianapolis. There were children EVERYWHERE,everywhere in the elevator on all the floors, etc. Our room was on a westin executive floor and still there were children running up and down the hall. When we arrived, even being gold members, there was not upgrade availability. When we got up to our room we were disappointed in the whole room. It was small and outdated. The bathroom was tiny. You could barely stand in the bathroom and close the door and while it had a heavenly shower (plus) the tub was so small,it was hard to use both shower heads. Our bed was extremely comfortable. Location was excellent and central to the RCA dome which was our final destination.
I usually don't complain and when I asked for any kind of upgrade and expressed my displeasure, the staff did apologize profusely and gave us access to the 15th floor lounge for a free breakfast the following morning. Excellent customer service, however, I have to be honest in my review of the hotel. 
My advice to management, when you know there will be large numbers of children, reserve a floor for your guests who don't want to be disturbed at 6am or 1 am with children running down the hall or yelling down the hall. I understand the revenue invovled with booking a large tournament like that and don't get me wrong, I love kids...I have 6 of my own, but this was an overnight trip where I just wanted to relax since I had a night away from my kids.
Overall review: the hotel could use an upgrade and should hold rooms for gold/platinum members when they have groups of kids like this.

title: “Great Price, Great Location”
text: We just returned from a girls weekend in NYC, where we stayed at the Travel Inn. I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone who wants to be close to the action while still staying within a modest budget. We were only about 4 blocks from where the action of NYC started and we walked everywhere we went. The rooms were a little small, but they were clean. We had an excellent view of the Empire State Building from our hotel room. We also had a deli right next door that served really good "NYC" food where we ended up eating 2 out of the 3 days that we were there. I would definently stay there again when I come back to NYC.

title: “Wonderful stay!”
text: Wonderful visit...a true resort with numerous amenities, quality service, and stunning location.

title: “Worth the time to find”
text:
What an awesome hotel. It is worth it to go around 465 to this hotel. It is on a quiet side street, semi-secluded, and was worth the time it took to get there. What a great place. The room was so clean, we slept like babies in the huge king bed. The room was quiet and comfortable. A great find after the long travel week we'd had. We would stay at this hotel any time we were in or going through Indianapolis. The bonus was there is a new Cracker Barrel in the same parking lot. Really nice.
PS: The laundry room is on the fourth floor, not the third as we were told.

title: “A bargain in San Diego”
text: Our ten night stay at the Vagabond Inn on Point Loma was great. Rooms are comfortably furnished with newly remodeled bathrooms. This location gets you away from the noise and traffic of the city although you're only five minutes from the airport.Parking is free--a bonus in this city. The pool was warm and included both shallow and deep areas--good for adult swimming and kid playing. The desk staff is very accommodating and the cleaning staff did a fine job of cleaning up the beach sand we managed to track in. A great bargain in our favorite expensive city.

title: “Great value and service”
text: While attending a convention stayed at the hotel. I was surprised as the spaciousness of the room and the evening reception made stay very enjoyable. Price also included free wireless internet connection and full breakfast.

title: “Welcome Home!”
text: My wife and I stayed here for 6 nights when visiting the LA area. When Jerry's Motel says "where you feel at home", they mean it! I was very impressed with the helpfulness of the staff when needed, but also being left to our own. Due to the nature of our visit, we were in the room until mid afternoon most days, but never once did we get housekeeping banging on our door to come in, and we didn't even have the "do not disturb" sign out. When we did leave, by the time we got back, our room had been serviced beautifully. I appreciated the complimentary snack bag provided when we checked in. The only issue we encountered was on our first morning there, when we experienced some plumbing issues and were without a toilet in our room for a few hours. The staff was great in not only getting the issue resolved quickly, but giving us access to their personal bathroom while everything was being taken care of. We will definitely be back when we find ourselves in LA again.

title: “Nice Staff but Dirty, Noisy Hotel”
text:
On the positive side - convenient location, nice staff, comfortable bed
On the negative side - dirty room, forgot to clean, construction next door, loud nightclub on ground floor.
The ultimate gross-out was when someone came down to complain that there were hairs in his bed. Filthy hotel. Not set up for business travelers either.

title: “Good location. Staff less than great.”
text:
If you are looking for a NY hotel then this is a great location from which to explore. 
The hotel is accessed via lift from 42nd . The luggage check is at street level too if you are early or are checking out but still have time to sightsee. 
The hotel is clean and well presented. Rooms are very nice and reasonable size and you will get a good nights sleep . Upper floors have a (limited) view of the Empire State building. 
Check in was reasonably speedy but checking out could be a pain at busier times as there only ever seemed to be 2 people at the desk. The concierge was helpful to a degree but had to be prompted rather than volunteering any assistance. Staff in the lobby bar were dreadful unless you actually sat at the bar itself, taking forever to come over, slow service and even forgot our orders. 
The hotel is still nice despite staff failing to deliver the service they should.

title: “Disgusting”
text: Although the hotel is conveniently located to attractions, the hotel itself is disgusting. It may appear ok at first glance, but the staff is terrible and the housekeeping staff does a horrible job. On the first night in the hotel, my friend found someone else's socks in her bed! Yes, that means they never changed the sheets from the previous guests! When we called the front desk to complain, they only offered to give us a complimentary breakfast. And that was only after we complained, first they accused my friend of lying! Horrible service, disgusting hotel! I will NEVER stay here again and Hilton will only be an absolute last resort in other cities.

title: “Better than other Mission Valley hotels”
text:
I stayed at the DoubleTree by Hilton San Diego in Mission Valley for only one night, but I would have been happy to extend my stay. The hotels in Mission Valley are, in general, a bit dated. However, the Doubletree stands out as a clean, modern hotel amongst the dinosaurs. 
Mission Valley is a very central location for getting around San Diego. However, Mission Valley itself is not the nicest area. A short hop on the freeway and you can be in downtown or at the beach, both nicer areas than Mission Valley.
My room was very clean and comfortable, with floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking Mission Valley. "Modern" decor often means cold, but not in this case. Look at the included room picture and you'll understand. The bed was comfortable and the bathroom was immaculate. 
The hotel lounge has a nice Happy Hour daily, and the lounge overlooks the outdoor pool area. The weather was not warm enough for me to take a dip, but the pool still looked clean and inviting. The San Diego light rail stops right across the street from the hotel, which is convenient for getting around if you don't want to drive and fight for a parking space. 
Speaking of parking... The only reason I am giving four stars instead of five is the $16/day parking fee. I found this charge to be excessive for the Mission Valley location. This is not in the heart of a crowded downtown San Diego, where high parking fees are the norm. 
Still, I would recommend this hotel for its location, its comfort and the professionalism of its staff.

title: “Cramped, not what I expected”
text: The room was a suite, a small conventional Hotel Room with another small room attached. There was a problem with television reception. The bathroom was cramped. Everything was clean, though, and we slept well. We checked out after one night when we had booked two nights. Everyone was friendly, and the breakfast was fine. Parking was difficult as described before.

title: “A great choice if you are looking for a chic, contemporary property”
text: LOVED the Dana Hotel. It was very modern & contemporary without feeling stark. I usually stay at the Palmer House for its very 'old school' feel; but decided to switch it up and was not disappointed. Its also in a convenient location to great restaurants / attractions. I will absoluitely stay here again.

title: “Old and smoky smelling”
text: I travel a bunch and strongly advise against this Marriott. The staffis fine, but it looks like the hotel hasn't been updated since the 1970s! It has a smoky smell and people I traveled with (other rooms) complained it was dirty. We all checked out early. The hotel has design boards indicating they willbe redecorating, but until then, skip this location.

title: “Gorgeous hotel!”
text: Beautifully decorated, absolutely lovely hotel in every way - bathrooms, lobby, linens, first rate. Everything new and sparking. Excellent value!

title: “Basic hotel, but clean and comfortable for the price”
text: Stayed here for our last 2 nights of a 2 week trip to New York & Boston. It was clean & comfortable, and very basic, but there were no rooms available with en-suite facilities. Luckily, the bathroom was next door to our bedroom, so that was convenient, and at no time did we meet anyone else when we used paid a visit. The breakfast was a bit wierd. You were supervised by a young lady who handed out bread and/or pastries from various covered plates, it reminded me a bit like being back at school. There were no other options, just juice, tea, coffee, all of which were served in paper cups, and then of course bread and/or pastries. Despie that fact that there were signs in the hotel stating No Smoking, there was a very distinct smell on our floor (3rd?) of cigarette smoke!

title: “Clean and in the Center of NYC :-)”
text: I stayed at the hotel for weekend and was very pleased with the rooms and the hotel staff. The reviews are pretty accurate in that the hotel is small (which I did not mind because I was never there for an extended period of time) and the elevators are slow because there are only two that service the entire hotel including the staff. I found that the elevators were hard to get during peak times, especially during the complimentary breakfast. However, you cannot beat the location! Its great to be four blocks away from Times Square and the Metro. Also, I had a nice view of the city from my room. I was happy with my choice.

title: “Great hotel! We will definitely stay again.”
text:
Perfect location with comfortable walking distance to waterfront, Pioneer Square, etc.
Right next to the light rail station which is a great way to ride in from the airport. Staff was super friendly and helpful, lovely atmosphere!

title: “dishonest location”
text: this place is in a poor part of town and is not near enough to union station or anywhere else, its big with generally big rooms but paper thin walls so hopefully those in adjoining rooms wont be noisy I found it clean and my room was kept clean, I was there 2 weeks and had to rely on taxis for transport, these were easy to get and cheap and could be hailed from the street outside. sightseers should stay closer to washington in a better part of town where you can walk around safely. might be acceptable if rooms very cheap and you had a car and were confident driving in DC traffic

title: “A gem in Seattle”
text:
We booked for 2 nights here before a cruise and can say the stay was very pleasant. We had requested a top floor room and this we had - no problems with traffic noise. The view was of the adjacent high buildings - yes you could see the carpark but the awesome buildings made up for that! The bed was huge - linen perfect and pillows made for a truly comfortable nights sleep. The jetted bath was welcome at the end of a long day walking/sightseeing in Seattle. The room was quite dark but this is the character of the room and it really seemed comfortable and cosy albeit not small. We would certainly recommend the hotel for a pre-cruise stay. We were grateful for the services of Aaron (concierge) who arranged a taxi to Pier 91 for only 25 dollars! Aaron was also very helpful in advising us how to get around. We used the underground bus a lot just to get from one end of the town back to the hotel after a long day but it is also easy to walk.
A real gem in Seattle - don't forget to look up to see the walruses (?) on the outside of the building.
We had breakfast one day in the restaurant but the bakery two doors along is good also!

title: “Good Hotel in Excellent Location”
text: Stayed at the Hilton Garden Inn for just under a week in February, check in was very smooth and we were directed to the room on the 22nd floor, initially I was worried as we were put in a room next to the lift and in the past this has been a problem but only now and again could we hear the lift. The room was big compared to New York standards and fist impressions were very good. The bed was comfortable and enabled a good nights sleep ( apart from the odd noise of the lift). The bathroom was very clan and the maid came in daily and did a fantastic job. The location is excellent with most of the sites within walking distance but for those not wanting to walk the subway was 1 minute away from the front door with the taxis on 5th and 6th a couple of minutes more. I was all in all very happy with our stay and would go back if we return to the big apple!

title: “Good value at The Timbers”
text: The exterior of the The Timbers does not convey the classiness and comfort waiting inside. I agree with the previous review's comments except for the noise level. The hotel was nearly full of guests due to the snowstorm and delayed flights at the airport. We had a studio suite with 2 queen beds, first room from the lobby on the second floor #201 next to the elevators. When you opened the room door, you could clearly hear the noise from the lobby and the hallway, but when you shut the door, you couldn't hear anything. With the TV on low, you couldn't even hear the elevators. Very quiet room. The studio suite is about the size of a regular hotel room but with microwave and refrigerator. No bath, just a shower, and unusual bath fixtures (see photos). Busy staff due to the storm, but they handled everything very well. We paid $99 per night Sunday through Tuesday and that is a very good value for this property. Well attended and managed breakfast is from 6am to 9am and they should make it 10am, not everyone is in town on business. Exercise room is still under construction. Be sure to check out the unusual fireplace in the lobby. We'll definitely stay here again.

title: “Lovely Hotel, But...”
text: A few weeks ago my girlfriend and I had the pleasure of staying at The Public, and we found the staff incredibly friendly and helpful, the rooms and public areas tastefully decorated to provide a very pleasant and relaxing ambiance. The Pump Room and lobby area, where there was a roaring fire, made the experience very nice, indeed, until we hit the weekend, when those areas filled up with so many outside people that it didn't feel possible to fully enjoy those facilities. There's apparently an influx of very chic folks in the evening on the weekend, making the area very loud and so packed that it's very difficult to squeeze in. That's fine if that's your thing, but my girlfriend and I were really just looking for a cozy place to chill out. Having said that, I want to emphasize that our stay was mainly very pleasant, and we were fine just heading up to our room on Friday and Saturday evenings. Plus, the location was great. Lots of restaurants and shops in the surrounding area, and the Magnificent Mile is only a 10-minute walk away. I highly recommend the hotel, but urge a little caution if you're not up for the weekend scene.

title: “Our second stay and just as pleased!”
text: This is our second stay at this hotel and we enjoyed it as much as last year. We were greeted by friendly staff and our 2 rooms were available when we arrived at 1230 the day of check-in. The complimentary breakfasts were excellent with a different hot item each morning, and multiple cold item choices. While quite busy, the extremely efficient staff kept things replenished. We enjoyed being able to have hot chololate or tea/coffee whenever .The location is great- just a block away from several theaters and 2 blocks from others. Walking to Times Square is easy (if not in a blinding snowstorm like we had while there!). We would stay here again anytime.

title: “Better without Bugs”
text:
Like it's sister, Hotel 17, these types of hotels are not for everyone. If you are just interested in a place to store your luggage, wash up and have a bed to rest in, then it is perfect. 
There is no lobby to speak of and some rooms are quite small with shared bathrooms. The hotel has an old charm to it though and does not resemble the plain chain establishments that go hand in hand with cheapness. Decently furnished with some style. 
The area, although not seemingly anything special, is central enough for getting to some of the more absorbing parts of Manhattan. A good parking garage is located the next block over to the east and the Empire State building is just a few blocks up.
Would really like to give this place a better rating but severely itchy legs can put a crack in anyone's good time and bed bugs do not get a high rating in my book!

title: “Yet another wonderful stay”
text:
This is my second stay at Beverly Garland's Holiday Inn, and decided to return recently when I was attending a conference in Downtown LA. 
Traveling in LA it is important to have a car, and as a Priority Club member (the frequent stay program for Holiday Inn), the parking rate was discounted to $11 per night, instead of $14 per night.
The breakfast buffet is a reasonable $12.95, and the hotel restaurant is quite pleasant. There is an outdoor lounge area connected to the bar inside the restaurant, so you and your travel companions can enjoy a pleasant drink outside.
The room was very clean and quiet. Our room had a small balcony, and it was easy to get to the parking lot from our building.
All of the staff are friendly, and were very helpful in the few instances we needed something. I recommend this Holiday Inn for leisure and business travel, if your business needs aren't too extensive.

title: “Location, location, location”
text:
Reading previous reviews for this hotel did make us wary before our trip. However, as a previous reviewer quite rightly said, it is all about setting expectations. 
We were first time tourists to New York and so location and price were our prime concern. You'd do extremely well to get a better location for the price we paid. The hotel is just a stone's throw from Times Square, the main centre for tourists and Broadway theatre goers. There are plenty of subway stops, there is a 24 hour convenience store on the corner of the block and the Gray Line tourist buses leave from around the corner.
The best thing about the hotel (other than its location) was its cleanliness - a major plus point. The room was a decent size, it did have a view of a brick wall, but we didn't care as we were out all day and being away from the street it also meant the room was quiet. The only notable negative was having to sit side saddle on the toilet due to its proximity to a wall, but I don't remember this spoiling my holiday! 
Didn't have much interaction with the staff, but they seemed alright. The lifts were incredibly slow and like another reviewer you call both lifts and see which one arrives first!
Like most hotels in USA, there was no restaurant, but there are plenty of breakfast diners in the area (and eating out is a better way of getting a feel of the real New York).
At the end of the day if you want a 5 star hotel, then book a 5 star hotel. If you are like us, i.e. tourists wanting a pretty decent budget hotel, then it is worth considering.

title: “Brilliant!”
text: This was another really great experience in New York staying in a super hotel right in the centre of it all. From the minute you enter the doors you are treated with friendly efficiency in a luxurious but relaxed atmosphere. Great value!

title: “Not as good 2nd time”
text: This was our 2nd time at the elan and after booking this hotel i sent them an email requesting the same room i previously had.This request stated the dates i stayed and my details and was sent 5 months before my stay.The room i requested was in the back corner with its own private little courtyard or anywhere in the back section.When we arrived we were given a small room in the middle of the hotel with outside courtyard joining half a dozen rooms.When mentioned to staff this was not the room we booked they then moved us to a junior suite that was much larger.We thought this was great only problem it was facing the same courtyard with another 6 rooms.Could not open our curtains the whole 5 nites we were there and had no privacy.A reply to my email would have been nice as i have sent many requests in the past to various hotels and always got a response.This was the only issue as staff were friendly and helpful,rooms comfortable and good location.

title: “Business meeting in Boston”
text: Enjoyed two nights at the hotel. The king bed was comfortable, room was large with adequate closet and in room safe. The bathroom was small. Overall the room was clean and in good repair. The Concierge was extremely knowledgeable and helpful. Lactation was excellent. We were able to walk to all of the historical and shopping districts. Subway is very close to the hotel.

title: “Exceeds Expectations”
text: This is a lovely hotel, and the staff is top-notch. The rooms are a decent size, and the price is reasonable for the neighborhood. It's within easy walking instance of both the River Walk, and, of course, The Alamo.

title: “Amazing Location”
text:
Stayed in this Hotel for a weekend during March.
The hotel itself is nice enough, with staff being friendly and helpful. The room was clean, tidy and a good size although could have done with a refurbishment.
Breakfast was ok, if a little over priced
The best thing about this hotel is the location. It's away from the really tourist area, it's just off one of the really busy chinatown streets, it seems to be a liveley area from early morning to late night. Seemed to be a really safe area to walk around too. It's also only a few hundred yards away from the beautiful Little Italy.
For people who want to do touristy things the hotel is near 5 subway lines that can get you to most parts of the city really quickly - including the airports.

title: “Very good stay.”
text:
This was a very good hotel. The price was right (even though it was the off-season discount), everyone was friendly, room was clean, balcony led right out to the ocean, beach was nearby, lots of places to eat were very close, and there was very little about it that I think could have been improved. They even came up with a free glass of wine on my first night.
That said, there were a few things. The bathroom was just a little tacky and badly maintained (though clean and not bad enough to affect my enjoyment any), they charge $20 parking - which if you're paying full price would seem almost like an insult, but I paid half so it didn't bother me too much... there is no onsite restaurant. All of the extra charges (parking, etc) made me feel like I was being nickel and dimed, and if I'd had to pay full price it wouldn't have been worth it. They did have a "continental breakfast" one morning - which was a danish and an orange juice - and $9 for an omelet and some sausage. While I can understand them charging for the hot stuff, you can get a better continental breakfast at a place half the price.
Go on the off season and you'll have a great time for a decent price... go when it's full price and you'll probably feel a little cheated. Not because it's not a great stay - it is - it's just not worth $500 a night plus parking. 
Oh, and watch out for the birds.

title: “A destination location in Boston”
text: We booked a weekend package to celebrate my husband's 50th birthday. The hotel delivered perfectly! The room was elegant and spacious with stunning views of the harbor. A lovely touch, the hotel delivered a complimentary bottle of champagne as a gift for his birthday. We had dinner at the hotel restaurant, Meritage, where we were served by knowledgeable, attentive staff and provided with a diverse selection of scrumptious courses. Our package also included use of the hotel spa, the exercise facilities had adequate up to date machines, but the pool and jacuzzi area were a real treat with a large well designed pool and lounge area, endless supply of fluffy towels and lemon sliced water for a thirst quencher. An after dinner walk out the hotel doors and onto the waterfront boardwalk is also a treat. We could not think of a better destination to celebrate a special event.

title: “Recommend”
text: Spacious room, very clean and well maintained, modern property, very accommodating staff, reasonable rates vis-a-vis comparable properties in the area. Amenities include breakfast, refrigerator and reliable wifi, all important to me. Easy drive to downtown. My second stay in a very short time (work related), both times "walk in," no reservations ahead of time, and would return. Recommend.

title: “Birthday Weekend”
text: We could only get away for a few days so we chose to head to Philly. We arrived at the hotel on a side street by car and I ran around to the front to ask where the garage was and the Front door person walked all the way back around the corner with me to take the car!. We were 1 hour ahead of check in time and waited in the bar and had very nice local brews to sip while we waited. When we got to our room we were very happy! The room was lovely and the spa tub was luxurious. We had wine hour in the lobby and the wines were very nice but the popcorn was truly yummy. I am a Kimpton member and it was my birthday so we got complimentary champagne and chocolate covered strawberries! The Location is fabulous; I will be back soon.

title: “Outrageous Prices on Extras”
text: Ordered a bottled water while sitting at the pool, and literally took over 1/2 hour to get it - at least they didn't charge me. The "free" continental breakfast, in my opnion, is SO minimal that it is probably a ploy to get you to order off the breakfast menu. And the breakfast menu prices are OUTRAGEOUS! The markup is criminal! And the worst, NO FREE INTERNET. Again, price gouging here with charges of 50 cents a minute. $12/day to park is just another way to get your money... this is not like a parking garage in a downtown area where parking is hard to find... this is just a parking lot for the hotel.

title: “Nice hotel a little out of the way”
text: This is a good hotel. I disagree with a previous review that ripped the hotel. For someone who claims to know NYC, the review didn't show it. The rooms are average NYC size which are generally small. But the appointments are very nice, the staff knowledgeable and helpful and the location tolerable unless you are spending your entire time in midtown. Contrary to what was earlier written, cabs do line up. I had no problem getting a taxi. There is construction going on next door. And the road around Battery Park is a mess. You will experience noise during the weekdays and on Saturday from about 9-5 in the city view rooms. I am very sensitive to hotel noise. But considering the construction ends before evening, it isn't too bad. However, to balance out the location and the construction you need to get a room for under $350. Over that, I would look somewhere else. Especially if you are going to midtown most days. I have found Ritz Carltons and Four Seasons somewhat stiff in terms of decor etc. And you can expect the services and restaurants to be pricey, but the overall experience is fine. One recommendation to management, designate one or two floors as quiet areas. Prohibit people who insist on bringing offspring from staying on or visiting those floors. I have the feeling that most peole who bring children to this category hotel are just looking to tell anyone who will listen that they stayed at the RizCarlton with their legitimate or otherwise kids. Keep them away from me.

title: “Would Stay Again”
text: Nice hotel with all the requirements for a business stay. Although I didnt get to see much of the area, it still proved much better than the Financial district previously stayed in. The wine on arrival was a nice touch as well!

title: “Value and Convenience in Central Hollywood”
text: The hotel is convenient to central Hollywood (and the Hollywood Bowl) and better value than some of the nearby competition. The included breakfast is terrific, with both traditional and healthier options. The pool is nice enough, though not particularly pretty (can they spare a potted palm or something?). The views of Whitley Heights are stunning. Although I’m American (and lived in Hollywood for a decade), I liked the international flavor of the guests. My biggest complaint is the $20 daily parking charge; it takes away from the value pricing. I recommend dropping stuff off and parking on the street (but read the signs) or in a cheaper lot nearby. As my wife and I arrived separately in two cars, the hotel parking was out of the question. We walked to the other end of Hollywood Boulevard for a nice French dinner at the W---but be careful of the W’s downright unAmerican 25% service charge on meals and drinks. Other restaurants are closer--like Mussos and Franks, and a cool looking Latin American place (both on the Boulevard). For the 20 somethings, a number of ’hip" clubs are within walking (or short taxi) distance. But don’t overlook the traditional and more divey (yet safe) bars like Boardners and the Frolic Room. There’s a shopping mall down the block from the hotel which was (and is) a huge disappointment to locals, except for the Kodak Theatre (for the Oscars etc.) But some of the foreign visitors seem to like what seems to us a bizarre collection of merchandise on offer.

title: “Just what we wanted”
text:
We stayed at the Doubletree Guest Suite Times Square in early January 2007 and enjoyed our stay. The room is spacious for the price, with a large living room with wet bar and a good sized bedroom with 2 double beds. The bath was large also, with two sinks. There is a microwave, coffeemaker, and a refrigerator separate from the mini-bar. Coffee supplies are refreshed each day. We didn't need the sofabed, so I can't tell you if it was comfortable or not. The regular beds were fine...a little soft for us, but we like superfirm beds. 
The suite looks like the pictures -- not overly luxurious but clean and comfortable. Plenty of closet and drawer space. Neutrogena shampoo, lotion, conditioner and soap.
Small quibble -- bathrooms could be a little more soundproofed. When you are in a suite, you are sharing with several people...'nuff said there.
Didn't use the exercise room...it is small, not as small as some others. Business center seemed fine, though they charge for something simple like printing out a boarding pass. The in-hotel bar and cafe didn't seem particularl inviting, but you are steps aways from any food you could want. 
Staff was exceedingly friendly and helpful. Check-in cookies good as always. On the whole, we were very happy with this hotel.

title: “Very good option”
text:
We stayed for six nights in this hotel and it turned out to be a very good choice. The location is great - close to the city centre and all forms of transportation. A good idea is to get a multi day MUNI pass so you can hop on and off cable cars, streetcars, buses etc at will. The city's transportation services work really well and we also used the BART to get to and from the airport (it is only a short walk from Montgomery Street Station but rather steep).
The hotel is a bit tired around the edges but overall is well maintained and our room (top floor facing the street) was spacious, well equipped and surprisingly quiet for an inner city hotel. We didn't use the restaurant (and neither did many other people as far as we could see) but there are many dining options in the area.
The free WIFI worked well during our visit.
Value for money this hotel was exceptional. We did an online booking directly with the hotel on a pre-paid and non-refundable basis at only $107 plus tax per night.

title: “Park 'n Ride”
text: We stayed for one night in February before setting sail on a 7 day Mexican cruise. They offer park and ride which we always look for when going on a cruise. The hotel was very nice and the room very clean. They have a lovely restaurant and great bar which we took advantage of. Hotel staff were attentive and friendly and if sailing from San Pedro we'll definitely stay there again.

title: “A typical chain hotel”
text:
My husband and I stayed at this hotel during a business trip for one night last May. The hotel definitely needs a facelift but it still provides guest’s basic needs just nice. The bed isn’t bad at all, the bathroom worked okay but the room service foods tasted nothing special. 
If you’re looking for a place to stay where you want to stay close from Manhattan crowds (Fifth Av, Time Square & Central Park), this might be a good place for you. 
don’t forget to taste the infamous gyro street vendor parked beside the hotel every night after 6PM! One of the best foods I’ve tried in NY only for $4 (so long Gray’s Papaya!)

title: “A classy hotel”
text: We stayed here on a recent college visit to the DC area. This lovely hotel enhanced our stay in DC. I was thrilled to find free valet parking when we arrived. My car was whisked away and I did not have to deal with driving in DC until I was ready to leave. The room was clean, beautiful, and kept up very nicely. House-keeping responded quickly to my request for more towels. After a long and hot day walking around DC, I was offered iced-cold complimentary water bottles upon my return. The concierge was very helpful and accommodating in giving up Metro directions, suggestions for a quick bagel breakfast, and driving directions. And the icing on the cake is that they are just a short walk away from Krispy Kreme and Hello Cupcake, two places to soothe a sweet tooth. All in all, this is a very classy hotel and I would stay absolutely stay here again.

title: “Never staying there again”
text: Upon check-in, the staff was very nice and accommodating. But after a long day visiting family in the area, my fiancée and I went to bed. I did not get a wink of sleep due to the fact that our room was near the elevators. The guests that came to the floor yelling, laughing, and banging on and slamming doors at all hours kept me up. The next morning, my fiancé pointed out a vase near the elevators that had urine in it. I guess someone could not get into their room quickly enough and decided to relieve themselves in a vase. On no sleep, I approached the desk and told her I was checking out. She asked my fiancé for the room number, I gave her the room number. She then stated the total and asked him if he wanted it on the card. The reservation was in my name, I approached her, and she refused to look at me or communicate with me to settle up. I was paying for the room. This experience after no sleep and just finding urine in the hall, I found very disrespectful. I will never stay there again. Note: my stay did not coincide with any major sporting events or concerts.

title: “The staff made this Sheraton shine”
text:
Nice, clean, huge hotel with a great location. The 16th Street Mall is right outside offering lots of store and restaurant options and it wasn't too much of a walk to the light rail stations. The room had a decent view of the mountains and seemed pretty fresh and new. As with most of the hotels at this level, you have to pay for wireless, which is always very frustrating, and there was no microwave or fridge. I was happy that the TV offered more than the usual 15 channels of just sports and cable news.
What really made my stay was the service. They helped out from checking in at the front desk to trying to get to the airport on my last day. I was attending a large convention that took place in the hotel and they always seemed on top of things. Usually I don't care about the service level beyond getting me checked in and out on time, but I really appreciated the staff here.

title: “Really good for short breaks”
text:
We stayed here overnight after a cruise before flying back to the UK in November 2012, we had two rooms. 
Both rooms were large and very clean, the beds were particularly comfortable. Both of our rooms has balconies and overlooked the bay which gave us spectacular views. The air-conditioning units were very old and rather noisy but they did the job so we just blasted it out until the room was ice cold and then switched them off. The rooms both had kitchenettes with microwaves, fridge-freezers, a hob, etc. We didn't use any of these but this would be great if you were looking for a low-cost weekend away and didn't want to eat in a restaurant every night. The cupboards were full of plates, bowls, cups, glasses, pans, cutlery, etc.
They have a number of cabana-style single story rooms overlooking the bay which I think would be fantastic. There were a number of cars parked outside of these with trailers attached for surf-boards/kayaks so I think this place attracts a lot of people who want to go out on the water. 
When we got to the hotel we were in search for something to do and the front desk/bell hop staff were extremely helpful and gave us some maps and ideas for things to do. We ended up doing a trolley tour of San Diego and Coronado which is a must if you have a few hours to kill. 
We ate dinner in the Hotel restaurant which was really good, typically massive portions, but of a good quality. They had a reasonable wine selection and it was not too expensive (about $20 for a nice bottle). We also had breakfast from the buffet in the morning, which was reasonably priced and most importantly hot (nothing worse that stone-cold hotel buffets!!). 
The hotel also runs a free paddle steamer boat trip with an on-board bar which takes you around the bay at night, the round trip takes about an hour but you can go around as many times as you like. We all thought this was great fun, the drink on board wasn't too expensive - about $4 for a glass of the red wine we drank at dinner in the restaurant. 
They have a nice bar in the hotel, next to a pond that has a couple of rescued seals in it, which was great!!
I would definitely stay here again if I found myself back in San Diego.

title: “Wow! Great happy hour!”
text: Blast!We stayed here with 4 other couples for for a getaway weekend. Great place and within walking distance to the L, which can get you anywhere. Yes, the rooms are tiny... Why are you sitting in your room? Friendly service and clean. We got a great deal on room rate and had a blast!

title: “Great location, great hotel, friendly staff.”
text:
This hotel was recommended to me by a friend living in SF.
Location was great, easy access around SF. Nicely decorated, room was unique and the building had character. It's not a tower of 1,000 identical rooms typical of the big chains.
Staff were very friendly and attentive.
Valet parking at the hotel is $45/night but there's a public car park a block away that provides self-service parking for $35.

title: “A must stay.”
text: Peabody is an excellent hotel. Customer service was excellent and room was great.

title: “Good location, small room, broken air conditioning, poor service”
text: Our room was in the "anex", meaning we had to take the elevator to the 4th floor, get off, go down the hall, around the lounge, get on another elevator and go up to the 7th floor. Not a lot of fun getting the comp coffee from the lobby in the morning. Our A/C stopped working and our room was 78 degrees. The service man said it was on time delay and left. 30 minutes later (and now 80 degrees) we called again. This time he drained a pipe in the ceiling and the air came back on. Same thing 2 days later, and no air again the morning we checked out! So, on a 4 night stay we had no air 3 times. SF was having a bit of a heat wave during our visit, so no air was not an option! We won't stay here again.

title: “Noisy rooms limited sleep”
text:
Wow, this was definitely one of the noisiest hotel rooms I have stayed in, in a long, long time! I was amazed how well I could hear what was going on in the hallway--the noises were so clear you would have thought my room's door was wide open. Even little noises, like the rustling of a plastic trashbag, came through loud and clear! I usually travel with a white noise machine to block out any sounds that could interrupt my sleep, but this hotel was so noisy that the white noise machine made no difference. Every time someone on my hallway slammed their door I woke up from a sound sleep with a start! I am not kidding, and I typically am a solid sleeper. 
Please note that I was staying on the 8th floor. The "Club" levels on the 9th and 10th floors were full. Perhaps it's better up there.
Also note that the hotel is incredibly isolated--there are no restaurants or shops or anything you can walk to, just office buildings and freeway. Not very hospitable neighborhood overall.

title: “Great stay at Embassy”
text:
Just returned from 3 nights at Embassy Suites Convention Center with my two teenage daughters and myself. It was our first visit to DC.
 We checked in early and were given a room on the 15th floor right near the elevator. We had a view only of the building next to us. We never encountered a problem with noise. We had a king suite and my younger daughter slept on the pull-out sofa. It was so nice to be able to spread out in two rooms. 
We used the mini-fridge daily to keep our water bottles and fruit cold.
The breakfast was great. It included made-to-order omelets and eggs(had to wait in a bit of a line), ready-made scrambled eggs(the girls did not like them), sausage, bacon, potatoes,pancakes, bagels, muffins, toast, yogurt, cereal, fresh cut and whole fruit, variety of juices, coffee, and tea.
Complimentary cocktails and snacks(chips, cheese and crackers) were served from 5:30-7:30PM. It was crowded but not more than I expected.
The hotel was in a good location(1-2 blocks to Metro Center) and within walking distance of many attractions and restaurants. Concierge was always polite and helpful.
My only weak complaint was that the pool was very small and so cloudy that the girls would not use it. I did not either.
We checked out the work-out room which I planned on using, and it looked like there was plenty of equipment. Never actually used it because I was so exhaused from walking all day!
Overall, I would definetly recommend this hotel, especially for families.

title: “Greatest Customer service ever!!”
text: My family and I stay at this hotel quite frequently. In March 2012, we were staying for Spring Break and my son became seriously ill while we were vacationing. We had to take him to the ER for an acute asthma attack!! My son was in intensive care on oxygen for 3 days of the trip! The staff at the hotel was so pleasant and helpful to us. They were very concerned and asked about him every day as my husband and I took turns sleeping at the hotel and hospital. Upon my son's miraculous release from the hospital, the docs told us he was well enough to finish out the rest of the few days vacation and the staff welcomed him back with gifts and cards signed by the hotel staff!! I truly appreciate the staff turning this most difficult situation into a celebration of my son's healing!

title: “Quality hotel in Union Square area of San Francisco”
text:
A good quality hotel very close to Union Square and all the usual chain outlets. Located on Powell Street with a cable car stop outside the main entrance. Room was smaller than expected, but it is one of the older hotels in the area. Room was comfortable, and we were given a corner room on the 15th floor as I had requested a city view because we were celebrating our 25th wedding anniversary. Plenty of restaurants within easy walking distance.
Tom and Laban, the "Beefeater" doormen are always happy to help and provide directions/guidance if asked.

title: “A lovely stay.”
text:
I was a bit worried from reading some negative reviews but I have to say I experienced nothing exceptionally negative during my stay. We were checked in early without prior notice and the room was clean, on the same floor as the front desk. The staff were friendly and helpful. We did not stay for the wine reception but the morning coffee and tea are good quality; note available usually until 11 am. We went out to buy breakfast and would come back to eat with coffee in the lobby which was really cozy and pretty.
We requested a goldfish in the room and got it. The room was cleaned daily. On the last morning we ordered breakfast and it arrived on time and was fresh. I guess the room is a bit snug, it's unlike other four star hotels where you can probably waltz through a standard room but the soaring ceiling and original details made up for it to me. Stand up shower only, but very spacious, good showerhead.
We tried eating at Poste the first night but where turned off because three diff. people there were unable to seat us or say whether the kitchen was still open (it was only 9 though) and there was hardly anyone there. We tried again on our last night and again it took three people to get us seated. Not sure what's going on but we were not in a rush and it was no big deal. The food is pricey but imaginative and well presented.

title: “Average Hotel...”
text:
The front desk people are not very friendly, the tour desk lady was extremely unfriedly - no smile, no greeting and makes you feel like you are the rude one. Maybe it is just me, thinking that most Japanese are friendly. 
The room was big, the toilet is quite big, but the room looks old.....the power switches are at odd places, very high on the wall (had to use a chair) or very low near the entrance. 
Our flight wasnt till 11pm, so we pay extra to stay till 6pm. Our room pass didn't work when we try to use it at 4pm. Had to go to the front desk to get it 're-programmed'. The front desk didn't even say anything, only - it should work now. 
I dont know if I will recommend this hotel to others...

title: “Great Location, Nice rooms & Staff”
text: Spent 2 nights at this trendy hotel. The location is great, about 200 metres from the Common, and the Freedom Trail if you are into Boston's history. There are dozens of really good restaurants and pubs within a 5 minute walk in almost any direction. The rooms are nicely appointed, very quiet. We had a view out over the cemetery and the Common right on Tremont St, and it was still quiet at night. Staff were great too.

title: “Felt a little mis-leading...”
text: My husband and I decided to do a last minute vacation with our 14 mos old daughter. We chose Amalfi Hotel for the great pictures and ammedities. The hotel was not as extravagant as we thought and the room was on the much smaller side that we were lead to believe it was going to be. The staff were great and the location was good. We ended up shortening our stay and going to another hotel. The breakfast service was one thing we liked by having it on each floor, however, 2 days in a row, it was moved to another floor since there was low volume on my floor. Not as good as I thought it was going to be for our first stay in Chicago.

title: “you can always be sure what you get with four seasons”
text:
this was third four seasons hotel we were staying in and again they fulfilled highest expectations. 
nice breakfast, excellent conceirge , perfect pool and gym at the poolside. 
yes, almost forgot. very nice idea with house cars.

title: “Perfect!”
text:
This Hotel is Perfect! Something for Everyone! We stayed with our two toddlers. This hotel is amazing , The pool area is like paradise and the entire grounds are covered in a very tropical feel. Very clean to say the least. Our room was clean and beautiful the view was outstanding of the lush green grass and the bay... The room type was a bay front room with a fire pit on the patio. I stayed at this hotel 6 years ago .. So returning and seeing all the upgrades and remodels was very nice... 
Now to address the Staff.... 
They were VERY helpful and polite . I feel Whitney at concierge went way above and beyond. I had several needs and she met Each and everyone of them with no problems and no hesitation. This was a very special day for our family and She made us feel special! Thank you WHITNEY you are definitely an asset to the hotel .
And one more person I would like to recognise is Edit. (front desk) she granted us a late check out until 1pm. That was very awesome! Thank you girls . We loved our stay and will be returning soon! I would Highly recomend this hotel to everyone !

title: “Great hotel for D.C sightseeing”
text:
Hotel is located adjacent to the metro so it is very easy to get to and from Ronald Regan Airport. We arrived early and were able to check in with no problems. Checkout is also a breeze. The front staff is very nice and attentive. They have a hosted wine hour every evening and cookies are out in mid afternoon. If you are a Kimpton In Touch member (which is free) you get a $10 raid the mini fridge coupon and free internet. The hotel is located across the street from the Portrait Museum, a couple blocks from Ford's Theater, and a short walk from the mall. The hotel is located in a neighborhood with lots of food options and shopping. There is a CVS across the street which we went to buy snacks. 
The only quips I would have is that the shower had no shelf (besides for the soap) at all and the only place you had to place shampoo and etc either on the floor on the top of the shower door. There also seemed to be a wedding or some sort of event on the 1st night there (sat), in which they were like setting up the appetizers right down from our room in the hallway. It was shrimp I think, so the hallway reeked for almost a day afterward. I just thought that was very peculiar. Also the rooms are not completely sound proof so you can hear people in hallways in the morning. 
We stayed in a basic room on the 3rd floor. It was small but I think that is expected for a city hotel, plus we didn't spend a lot of time in the room. The hotel is also eco friendly with recycling in rooms, which I wish more hotels had.

title: “A very good surprise”
text:
One of the best room plans I ever seen. Very functional comfortable and pleasant.
Excellent service, good views over San Francisco and staff very courteous.

title: “Perfect location, great government rate, luxurious, friendly service”
text:
I made a last minute switch from the Intercontinental to the Ritz. With my government rate, the price was identical--$200--also the same price for the Marriott Courtyard. This hotel did not disappoint. 
First, the staff was very friendly, and quickly accommodated my request for a room at 7:00 a.m. on the day of my arrival. The hotel, while luxurious, is not pretentious with its guests; you aren't giving the once over when strolling the lobby in casual attire. 
As other reviewers mentioned, the lobby could use--well--more space and furniture. Still, it's lovely, and hopefully, you'll be spending more time in your room than the lobby. 
The bathroom is wonderful with a large soaking tub and separate shower. The bed and bedding are soft and comfy. The location can't be beat, at Boston Common. 
My only warning comes from a cab driver regarding the towncar waiting outside. The towncar he referred to is not the one apparently provided by the hotel. He stated that the doorman will ask guests where they are headed. A private towncar will be parked in front of the hotel. If the guest is headed a long distance, such as the airport, the doorman will recommend the town car. According to the taxi driver, the private town car will charge $40 for the airport ride. The price is approximately $21 for a taxi. Therefore, if you are told otherwise by the doorman, the information is incorrect. Take the taxi not the towncar.

title: “Don't stay if you want to sleep”
text:
We booked the vacation to relax as a couple with out our kids. We had spent four days prior at Disney with the children. We were excited for a little Rest and Relaxation. 
We stayed in the 600 building for two nights. The view was nice. 
However, the alarm in the vacant room next door at five in the morning that was loud enough to wake us up was a bit annoying. More annoying that the staff took 45 minutes to turn it off after I called.
The beds were very uncomfortable. 
The family in the room above us, probably wouldn't appreciate the fact that we could hear their every word due to poor insulation. 
The concierge was fabulous and the massage that we had was wonderful. However I felt worse the next day due to the horrible beds.

title: “Modern, nice, location is perfect”
text: We discovered on a previous, week-earlier, trip through Boston that we needed to be close to Fanuiel Hall, Quincy Market, and the Freedom Trail -- this hotel was perfect for that. We found our atrium-view room was modernly appointed, with contemporary furnishings. The atrium view is nothing to brag about, however, since it only looks down to the front desk. I can't stress enough how the location is the best part -- we walked all around and really enjoyed ourselves. A couple more details -- the bed was comfy and the linens were really luxurious. The shower had fantastic tile. The lobby of the building reeked of stale cigarette smoke, but the rest of the building did not (I suspect the old couches are to blame and should be thrown out!). We didn't get breakfast or transportation with the purchase of our room, and that's okay with us -- we knew that beforehand.

title: “Slipping....”
text:
Came to the Donatello four years ago with my family and found that it was great.
Good location, quiet with a large room that the four of us could share happily.
This time it was just me, meeting a friend on my way to the UK.
When I arrived the room was dirty. I was tired so I didn't want to wait for someone to come but i phoned down to reception and told them. They were not apologetic and were happy for me to leave a note for the cleaner the next morning. Which I did and still no apology!
When I asked at the front desk for directions I was never informed that the concierge was upstairs. It was interesting how you would stand there and wait then when they were free they would not walk towards you and ask if they could help just look at you and wait until you walked over to them! Interesting approach to customer service.
When I came before there were pastries and coffee upstairs each morning. I contacted them before my arrival to ask whether or not they supply anything gluten free and i was not advised then that this facility no longer available.
I also remembered the sauna and spa being a welcome addition so my friend and I looked forward to this. However when we spoke to the concierge who showed us how to use the controls even he did not tell us the the sauna no longer worked! So we sat there for half an hour like two stuffed lemons getting chilly!
The morning I was leaving to catch the plane to the Uk was the morning of the first flight disruptions due to the volcanic ash.
The lobby had a kiosk where you can use the internet but the room was locked and the key could not be found!
Eventually they broke into the room and we queued to contact our airlines.
So not a great experience and no I would not go back or recommend.
d
r
t 
e.

title: “Great location - very comfy bed to relax into!”
text:
Great central location, we walked almost everywhere from here. The bed's the best thing about the room - very comfortable and big! The room's not huge but I guess it's in keeping with New York room sizes. Good, powerful shower, no mini-bar, good service throughout the hotel by the staff. The inclusive breakfast was good, ample choice of fruit, waffle maker, pastries etc etc. We had a view of the Empire State building from our room, it also was on the front of the hotel on the 10th floor, but we weren't at all disturbed by noise from the road as it's a quieter side road - we found it was definitely better than staying on one of the main Avenues or in Times Square.
The free wi-fi and computers/printer in the lobby were a great help - being able to research restaurants/activities then book and print off confirmations at the same time was a real benefit. I'd say this is a business hotel which serves travellers very well, but doesn't include the extras such as a spa/gym/pool/restaurant which you may like, but would probably also pay more for. For those who've stayed in other Marriotts, this doesn't compare to the resort-style hotels they manage, but in terms of location and service, it's still got the Marriott quality.

title: “Excellent location but....”
text: Stayed in October 2011 as a pickup and return point for a coach tour. Hotel is within easy waliking distance of most museums and attractions. Rooms clean and comfortable but we had the room next to the elevator and the noise from it, in the middle of the night, sounded like a howling gale. Breakfast first morning was chaotic. One queue for tables and another for food, but no sign of any organisation.Too few staff for the number of guests. However on our return it was much better. Breakfast buffet excellent with the muffins deserving a special mention. Staff pleasant and helpful.

title: “Absolutely awful. Avoid like the plague”
text:
This place is absolutely horrible so be advised. First, upon checkin I asked them about reserving a place on their shuttle to make a flight the next day. They said just be there 10 minutes in advance and you will have no problem getting a seat. I asked again and got the same answer. The next morning, I was there 30 minutes in advance and when checking out asked yet again getting the same answer. Then, when the shuttle arrived it had exactly one seat available on it with three of us wanting to get on. I went back to the front desk and they said, "sorry it's full, whereupon I said you then get me a taxi and you pay for it. They refused." Fortunately, some nice lady overheard the conversation and gave us a ride. Even if we had waited for a taxi, we would likely have missed our flight and this place couldn't care less. Other places either have a signup sheet so this doesn't happen and you know in advance or pay for a taxi when they screw up. Not this dump.
To add to this, even though I slept through it, some idiots were wandering around the hotel at night and banging on people's doors. The management did nothing about this, and some idiot above us stomped around all night waking my wife up. This place is a completely mismanaged dump so stay there at your own peril. Never again for me.

title: “zam088”
text:
We check-in without reservation,and,were greeted with a smile,eye contact.,.
Hotel had a good clean curb appeal,that attracted my family....rooms were clean,.
only thing can be up graded are T.V,.from 25'' to maybe flat screen !!

title: “Clean, quiet room”
text:
My husband and I traveled to Indianapolis for me to attend the Women of Faith conference. Having had surgery recently, I needed a place that would be quiet and be able to get some good rest to have enough energy to volunteer at the conference. We were very pleased with the accommodations and even though there is a stadium across the street, and a Bob Dylan concert was going on across another street, our room was very quiet.
My question is though - why do they have to have so many things lit up in the room? The clock was like a beacon and the thermostat was lit up too. I used washcloths to cover them up so the room wasn't so light!!

title: “An awesome staff from management down!”
text:
The location was good, the staff was excellent! I always received warm and courteous assistance. The managers and staff that I met seemed to take pride and pleasure in their job. I was very comfortable, and felt at home.
Ashley W.

title: “Great location and excellent service”
text: Early check in with no hesitation and location was great. Close walk to Mich Ave and many great restaurants. Staff was extremely helpful handling us at check in with three children.
