Rooms was nice, clean and beds were very comfortable. Will be back to enjoy when in Chicago. Bellman and doorman were great!

title: “Fabulous Value...”
text: I've been staying at the Amalfi hotel and I'd have to say it's got to be the best value out there. It's immaculately clean, the staff are lovely, and the complimentary breakfast offers fruit, yogurt, juice and pastries. They also have a complimentary cocktail hour. Could it get any better?

title: “Excellent hip hotel, cool and friendly, perfect location”
text: This was our second time at the Bryant Park Hotel, we loved it two years ago and it lived up to our memories of it this time too. The interior design is very hip, unexpectedly so given that is is located in the historic 'radiator' building. The bedrooms are large, airy and have great views, the beds are big and comfortable, the bathroom is large with a great shower, the interior design is elegant and contemporary. The staff are friendly and professional and the restaurant for dinner is pleasant (although one quibble is that the food is overpriced for what it is, there is better quality/value to be had in many other places in New York). The hotel lobby is very small, really just a check in area and the lifts. The location of the hotel is perfect, very central but quiet - Bryant Park is a gem, and it's a short walk to many of Manhattan's main sights as well as key shopping streets. I would stay here again next time I'm in New York, it is really excellent.

title: “One of the Best Marriotts”
text: I have stayed at many Marriott's- by far this is one of the Best. Not the biggest but clearly a leader in all aspects of what you expect from this hotel chain. Special mention for the friendly attitude of everyone who works at this property.

title: “Great”
text: Stayed at Hotel Vitale for one night this month with my mother. We thought it was absolutely great. We arrived very early (at around 11 a.m.) and they gave us a room very promptly despite our premature arrival. Beds were very comfortable and the location was perfect. Bar downstairs was perfect for an evening cocktail to enjoy the lovely weather. Will definitely return.

title: “Great staff and services”
text:
We have just returned from The Legacy having booked 11 nights in a one bedroom condo. All staff were very gracious and very proactive. We particularly booked here for the golf and were not disappointed, Mr Gaffney the manager and the golfing support staff were so professional in all their roles.
We had not realised that daily housekeeping was part of the package and here staff really personalised the service with different little touches each day i.e. flannels shaped in various ways, flowers etc.
Our only complaint was with the jacuzzi, which if your neighbours above chose to use theirs was extremely noisy. This unfortunately happened at 10:30 pm and 3:30am. The staff did respond quickly to our complaint at 3:30am and the noise ceased. We could not fault the facilities or staff. My husband and I would both recommend this resort to all age ranges.

title: “Overpriced hotel compared to other choices in Boston”
text: This hotel came highly recommended but we were disappointed. We arrived after dark after a long journey from Australia via New York. The staff at reception were cold and disorganized. The wifi was down and staff seemed unconcerned about it. The room was quite small, although the beds and bathroom were terrific. The location is good - central - but when we pulled up outside the next morning in our newly-hired rental car to get our luggage, again the staff's first reaction was cold, asking us to move on as quickly as possible even though there was plenty of space in front of the hotel. Not welcoming or helpful, would not stay here again.

title: “Nice Stay in a Nice Location”
text:
Since you are reading reviews, you will go in with the knowledge that this is a boutique property with small rooms. Our recent stay was just for one night, so we could wander around and enjoy the holiday events in Chicago. The location is great, close to Michigan Ave, Rush Street, nice walk into the Loop. 
Yes, the rooms are small, however for our family of 3 we were fine. We were originally booked in a queen room, via priceline. I called inadvance asking for a room with 2 beds - was told it wasn't guaranteed, but they would try. Unfortunately - we were stuck with a king and no cots/rollaways. So, the three of us shared a bed (2 adults and a 8 yr old). Enough room for us. Shower was nice with H2O products. Nice bathrobes and full size hairdryer. I must say, they have very comfortable beds too!!!
We did have a drink next door at LM, as the lobby bar opens at 3:00. Hotel does offer room service and the prices were not as bad as I have seen elsewhere.
For the price/location/service - I would definitely stay here again!
*thanks to housekeeping for finding my daughters pillow and sending it out!

title: “Nothing special”
text:
Business hotel, with nothing special. 
It's very big and honestly very sad, the furniture is old, it remembers the 70's. 
The breakfast is close to the reception, in an open area, but is too big and too many people have to wait to take some hot dishes or a juice...
If you have to stay few days is ok, also because you are close the typical area of the Fisherman Wharf and also to the center of the city.

title: “Very nice hotel”
text: My husband and I stayed here in October 2010 while I attended a convention at the Phoenix Convention Center. We found the hotel very nice and what we expected. The hotel is used a lot by businessmen and the pool is quiet. The free buffet breakfast is fabulous. The location isn't great but value for price, you get a huge room and it is much less expensive than downtown. We took the light rail one block from the hotel to the convention center. Easy Peasy! We paid $110 per night and I'm very happy with my choice.

title: “Good location for good price - all you need to explore New York City”
text: We have been visiting Manhattan and stayed for 5 nights in the Red Roof Inn. It was the second time in New York and also the second time in this hotel. The hotel is very good located to explore the city. The breakfast included in the price is good enough for the beginning of an exciting day in Big Apple. We have enough space in our room and we were satisfied of the cleanliness of the room. We will go again to the Red Roof Inn the next time.

title: “Wholeheartedly recommended”
text:
Hollywood Orchid Suites is in a great location just behind, and a two minute stroll from, Hollywood Boulevard. It offers free secure underground parking which is a great bonus.
As a first timer in LA I would recommend hiring a car if you fancy it. We used ours every day and found it really useful for getting about what is a pretty big city. Driving in LA is really not too bad even for someone getting used to a LHD car.
If you want to walk from the hotel it's only a short walk from the Chinese Theater (which also contains a multiplex cinema) and the Walk of Fame. A few minutes further west and you're on Sunset Boulevard although a fair walk from the Strip. The whole area feels perfectly safe to walk around in, even at night. If you want to go further afield there is a metro station right where you walk out onto Hollywood Boulevard.
The staff at the hotel are really friendly and helpful. We were fortunate to be given a free upgrade to a huge suite when we stayed in September. It was really a one bedroom apartment with full separate kitchen, dining area and etc. From what we saw of the other rooms they were all a good size. The room was very nice and clean and we were glad of the air-con at night. The hotel was also surprisingly quiet, not what you expect from being in the middle of a bustling city.
Amenities include a decent size swimming pool and a nice rooftop garden with sun loungers. Good free wi-fi in all areas of the hotel.
Breakfast was fine with a variety of croissants, breads, cakes, cereals, etc. but a little cramped for sitting space. We ended up taking ours up to the roof garden a couple of times.
All in all an excellent experience and a great place to base your LA stay.

title: “Great location!”
text: We stayed here in October for 5 nights and could not fault the hotel. We were in a junior suite and had a lovely view out over the wharf. Any requests we had were met straight away and the staff were all friendly and cheerful. Enjoyed the wine tasting a few nights. It was for my 40th so was an ideal spot for local attractions and although the wharf is very touristy there is a great selection of restaurants and cafes. We walked to the bridge from the hotel - took approximately 2 hours..... Would come back here anytime

title: “Coffee Lovers will love Hotel 41 !”
text: Stayed at Hotel 41 in April. Was given a small (10ftX10ft?) room that was dirty, even a shoe print on the wall! Called the front desk immediately and was given a better bigger room the next day. The breakfast for us was perfect. good coffee, bagels , muffins, cappuccino and espresso. Great location if you want to be in the heart of midtown Manhattan. Nice young staff. Bar a bit noisy and crowded at night.

title: “Stay AWAY if at all possible!!”
text:
We were looking for a last minute place to stay and thought that the Sheraton close to the Inner Harbor would be a safe bet. BOY, were we wrong!!
The lobby wasn't bad... it appeared to be ok when we walked in with the exception of the strange Sheraton logo projecting onto the marble lobby floor. It wouldn't have been so strange except that the hotel appears to be more classic than gaudy. 
From the time you leave the lobby it goes from normal to bad to gross. The elevator had cardboard as the flooring, the guest room had no closet doors but the room was so small that anything extra probably would have been too much and that apparently includes having handles on ALL of the dresser drawers! 
The bathroom had a handicap accessible standup shower that we definitely didn't ask for and what they claimed to be the "Sweet Sleeper bed" couldn't have been any more uncomfortable - it had as much spring to it as the floor did. 
This place was quite sad for almost $300 a night! Keep your fingers crossed that your neighbors are quiet, that you're not hungry (room service stops bringing breakfast at 10 am), the hotel "guide" is a stack of stapled sheets of paper and hope that your skin isn't too sensitive because the "facial" soap was more like a heavy-duty industrial scrub. 
For some strange reason they "renovated" some parts of this place and put in a big wide screen flat panel TV. They should have used those funds to replace the broken dressers or maybe even print a real welcome book instead of the stapled sheets!
And make sure to check your bank statements – they overcharged the credit card by about $35.00. We’re still waiting to see if they credit that back and trying to figure out where that charge came from.

title: “Extended stay”
text: Overalll Not bad, except for the fact that an employee barged into the room around 12:05pm because he thought the stay had ended. The employee was not aware of the fact that I paid an extra $10.00 to stay until 3:00pm .The employee did not knock or speak loudly. He Just tried to open the door, fortunately the dead bolt lock was on. Rest was a little hard I told him to contact the front desk because we are suppose to check out at 3pm.

title: “wonderful”
text: fantastic location and wonderful atmosphere with staff that cant do enough to help

title: “Get the town house if you have the budget!”
text:
Stayed two nights in the two story townhouse. Nice comfortable living room downstairs with wet bar, upstairs bedroom and bathroom. #702 was I think the best room possible, on the 7th and 8th (top) floor in the corner with windows on two sides. The views of Pike Market and Puget Sound could not be beat. Fun to cruise the market and be back at your room in two minutes. Entertained some friends in the room before going to dinner, everyone enjoyed!
Beds were like sleeping in a cloud!

title: “Wow what a great job!!”
text:
Wow, what a great job this hotel had done! I stayed here several years ago and I'm so glad I gave them a second chance. The renovation looks terrific! I don't know where they found their new staff, but everyone I encountered was friendly, courteous, well informed and some pretty funny. They did a very good job of keeping a smile on my face. 
They re-did the sleeping rooms which are much brighter, clean and fresh. The marble bathroom looks great. I heard they're getting all new flat screen TV's in the rooms too. .
I almost fell to the floor when I went down the next morning to use the fitness center. It looks like a Bally's, TV's on the treadmills, flatscreen's, free weights, new equipment and its twice the size as it was last time I was there.
I was hesitant to try and order a latte at their cafe, since they serve Starbucks, thinking it would definitely not taste right. Well I was wrong, I tried their special (Chocolate Carmel Late) and it was fantastic.
I'll definitely stay here anytime I'm in Philadelphia. GREAT JOB!

title: “The worst experience in the US ever”
text:
We have chosen this hotel due to it's central location close to Central Park. The rooms were booked and 100 percent prepaid in advance. We have also asked them to pick us up from the JFK. The problems started with the pick up: our flight from Vegas was delayed for cancelled so I sent to the customer's relations manager a message that we would be 12 hours late and that we woukd take another flight. He has immediately confirmed that and promised to send a driver later. Nevertheless there was nobody at the airport and we were obliged to take a taxi. When we finally came to Warwick that manager has told us that he had received my message about the delay only in the morning and had no chance to send the driver. Besides, they told us that there were no rooms available as we hadn't informed them about our late arrival. The argument that I had informed the customer's relations wasn't accepted as "it is a separate department!!!" it was really funny to hear as they stay next to each other. Finally they gave us one temporary room for 2 couples with the promise to arrange the rooms till the evening. Our friends have got their room quick enough but it was probably the poorest in the hotel with the windows facing the walls. We have got ours later in the evening and it was really according to out request. That was the ONLY positive moment of all our staying at that hotel. Another problem arised later when they informed us that our friends had made a reservation one day earlier so they would live the hotel also one day earlier. All my arguments that it was absolutely impossible as we were a group and had made the reservations together were not accepted. Only when I found the file with correspondence they accepted it and even apologized. Nevertheless, one day before the departure our friends were told to leave the hotel. Again I spent an hour trying to prove that it was their mistake. Again they looked at the correspondence and apologized. But it was not the end of the story! When we were to leave the hotel they charged our friends one additional night. That time all my arguments were not accepted and they reccomended me to discuss it later by correspondence when I am back home. 
I do understand that it is New York and the occupancy rate is very high. Nevertheless, it was my first experience of that kind in the US: very unfriendly staff. 
There is Hilton next to Warwick and it was my great mistake to choose that hotel. What I am rally sure about is that I will never come back to Warwick and it is the first time I can say that I would never reccomended this hotel to anybody.

title: “Fabulous location”
text:
We stayed there for our honeymoon in August 2009. On arriving we were amazed by the reception area, it was spectacular. However, we were disappointed by the rooms, extremely basic, no amenities apart from a bed, tv, safe and bathroom. Would have been nice to have a fridge
Good points: fabulous location, opposite Madison Square Gardens, good bar next door, helpful conceirge
Bad Points: You get what you pay for, no little extras or special things, especially as they knew it was our honeymoon. The phone costs a fortune, we made 3 calls to England,which were short calls and got a bill for $44. Breakfasts were expensive, Eggs Benedict cost up $34. We ended going to McDonalds every morning for breakfast (not exactly very healthy but certainally the cheaper option!)

title: “Ideally Located, Spoilt by Noise”
text: We had pre-booked this hotel, having researched the area around Union Square. The Donatello is an older style of hotel in a good location. However, whilst staff were helpful, the hotel was let down for us by two things, as follows: (a) the room, whilst of a good size, was not as well equipped as others of its class (e.g. it did not have a dressing table) and (b) we had a poor sleep on each of the two nights we stayed because of noise from the street below - the windows in our room, on the 8th floor, were not doubleglazed our sound-proofed. We would not go there again.

title: “Mixed review--Good room;terrible bathroom”
text: My room was spacious and well appointed. However the bathroom was cramped and only had a shower with a door that did not close altogether. There was minimal space in the bathroom to hang used towels.

title: “Lovely Hotel”
text: Went to the Hilton for a weekend get-away. Part of our plans included walking across the Brooklyn Bridge which is only a few blocks away. We walked many blocks uptown, though Tribeca and the next day, downtown through the financial district. We've lived in New York all our lives and have been to Ground Zero many times but from our room we were able to look right down onto the site. It was a spiritual and sobering experience. Hotel is across the street from St. Paul's, which is a must-see. Lots of good shopping in the neighborhood. If you can, park in a garage off-site as the hotel charges $55.00 for 24 hours and then $25. if you're one minute over!! Rip-off.

title: “Wonderful Hotel, centrally located, helpful folks, clean, bright”
text: This was the most restful, easiest to find, closest to all the theaters...hotel. It was clean, tidy, plenty of hot water, and very helpful with gaining tickets to all events (even a reservation at Sardis)

title: “Just ok, some issues”
text: If you've ever stayed at a W hotel, then you know this chain is a bit different. Some say the W stands for weird. The hotel is very dark in the lobby, halls and rooms. First room I checked into was supposed to be non-smoking but I could smell smoke residue and an abundance of perfume trying to cover up the smell. Second room smelled better. When checking out in the morning, front desk had no change and the airline check-in kiosk was not working. Was sent to valet stand to get change and the concierge to get a boarding pass printed. Would have preferred that didn't have to go elsewhere for these services. I would choose another hotel when in this area next time.

title: “Perfect in Every Way!”
text: What's not to like? Comfortable, clean room. Excellent location - walk anywhere from here. Right on the subway line. Metro cafe on the corner has excellent, inexpensive on-the-go food. We loved the place and would stay there again in a heartbeat.

title: “Handlery Union Square hotel”
text:
Lovely hotel right in the thick of Union Square and not too far to get to Fisherman's Wharf and all the attractions down at the pier.
Didn't offer connecting rooms and for us being a large family this was abit of a pain but the rooms were lovely and clean, very well presented although they were the smallest rooms we encountered in our whole trip.

title: “Would do it again”
text:
New and clean. Convenient to Times Sq and Subway stations. Helpful staff. Only 5 rooms on my hallway so not too much hallway noise. 
I made a costly mistake and parked in the wrong garage. Make sure you use the one just up the street that they validate for because it will cost half as much.

title: “Good value for money”
text: This was our first motel for our 4 week trip in the states. The outside of the motel had a great look but the rooms were okay. They were clean but dark (not many lights) and the air conditioning wasn't working properly. It did work, but with a lot of noise so we had to turn it of during the night. All with all a good value for money motel.

title: “GREAT VALUE”
text: Recently spent a 3 day weekend in San Antonio. Had a great time and the hotel was a big part of a pleasant stay. Good location, good food, great band in the bar, and friendly staff. Jim B

title: “Clean room, excellent location, coffee shop on main floor a godsend!”
text: The room and bathroom were very small, yet this didn't bother me because I read the reviews ahead of time. Our room was clean and very functional considering we didn't spend much time in it. The location of the hotel is very close to everything worth exploring in downtown Seattle. We were within walking distance to the waterfront, Pike Place Market, many restaurants and shopping venues. The elevators were a bit noisy, but we didn't have any problems with them. Adding continental breakfast for just a few dollars is definitely worth it. For the price, we'll definitely stay again next time!

title: “Excellent Stay!”
text: Fabulous hotel! The staff were so pleasant, we were always greeted with a smile not just from desk staff but maintenance and breakfast staff as well. The rooms are small as others have posted but that is NYC. They were clean and the beds were very comfortable. It was so quiet too, we never heard anyone in the halls and no traffic outside. Elevators do take a while during peak times - we found the weekday mornings a little less crowded than weekends. The breakfast had an excellent variety and the warm cookies at night and coffee, hot chocolate, and fruit available all day was wonderful. Young woman at concierge was very helpful. A couple minor issues in the room and maintenance was there immediately. Free wi-fi and business center. Only a few blocks from times square and one block to nearest subway station. Overall, we could not believe the courteous staff, quietness, and little extras this hotel offerred! Without a doubt, we would stay again! A huge thanks to the staff at this hotel!

title: “The Renaissance was awesome.”
text:
I really enjoyed my time at the Renaissance. The place was very nicely decorated and you could tell that the hotel was fairly new. When I checked it, the staff was very friendly and were even accommodating when I asked for a high floor. I had the choice of a king bed or a high floor, and I selected the high floor with two beds. I think that was a better option - because I ended up having a view anyways (because my rate had prevented me from getting the full water view). 
The beds were amazing as they usually are and the room was very nice. There wasn't a refridgerator, but all the gadgets in the room was neat. There was a flat screen tv that would swivel if you turned it toward the desk, or the other bed. The alarm clock was one of those where you can wake up to your ipod. The desk was neat because in addition to plugs and ethernet cable inputs, you could also make your tv your computer screen via the cables they provided. It also had a/v and other inputs that I didn't use. 
There was a little nook that held the coffee maker next to the closet that was nice. The bathroom was really simplistic, but was top of the line. It would have been helpful if there were one of those magnifying mirrors, but that is just my personal preference. The shampoo and conditioner they provided smelled really good. I liked the recessed lighting over the tub, which was pretty large. 
Now the negative - 
* The walls are paper thin. I was having a private telephone conversation, I don't think I was loud at all - but my neighbor started banging on the wall like it was some apartment building and I was still in college. I know my conversation was late (I WAS still on California time), but it shook me up and I felt uncomfortable. 
* The parking cost was insane - $39/nt. But since it was an upscale hotel, it's expected. The parking lot around the corner is cheaper, but be prepared to pay as well. Their breakdown is odd - I don't know the cost for less than 2 hours, but 2-10 hours is $20 and up to 24 hours is $27. I flew in on a red eye and decided to take a nap, so, my first day I stayed economical and the car stayed in the lot. So, that's pretty much it on the negative. 
Boston as a whole was amazing. I loved the transportation system. The silver T line was right across the street from the hotel. If I knew better, I would have just taken the silver line from the airport. (It's the line that connects the airport to the rest of the lines - and the hotel is right next to the stop.) It was also nice that there is a Starbucks connected to the lobby. The concierge was really helpful and they sent me to the No Name on the wharf across the street. It was really good.

title: “Pure perfection”
text: I stayed at the Waldorf earlier this month with my mom and sister and it was incredible. Before I even arrived I was in contact with the concierge, Celso, who did an amazing job putting together and itenerary for us. We stayed in the Towers and our suite was quite spacious for 3 ladies who don't travel light. The check-in for the Towers is not in the main lobby and it was peaceful, easy and the staff was wonderful. Breakfast in the lounge each morning was the perfect way to start our day. I cannot say enough wondeful things about The Waldorf and the professional, friendly and efficient staff they have. I highly recommend this hotel for any occassion ~ it is pure perfection!

title: “If location is more important than luxury accomodations this is the place”
text:
We come to Chicago a lot for our little get-aways and we usually do Priceline and we usually get the same 3-4 hotesl, so I was surprised when we were awarded Hotel Sax. $90.00 throug Priceline. Below I have listed the Pro's and Con's of our stay.
Pro's:
The hotel is located right in the heart of everything, shopping, dinning, sightseeing, it is next door to the House of Blues, adjacent to a bowing alley and has a nice resturant and lounge on-site. The lobby is well appointed, upscale anad classy, with a concerige . Front desk quickly upgraded our room when we complained about plaster falling from the ceiling. 
Our upgraded room was nice size, the bathroom was large (huge actually) and it was pretty clean. The kingsized bed was very comfortable (not the pilliows).
Con's:
Our first room was smaller than our guest bedroom at home. The queensize bed took up the entire room. The bathroom light was a heat lamp that glowed red - no other light in the bathroom. Directly over the bed plaster was falling from the ceiling from an old leak. 
The upgraded room had floor to ceiling mirrors, wood paneling and a faux alligator skin wing back chair - icky. The 1960 style dresser with the glass inlay top had visible dirt and other unidentifiable sutff underneth it.. The wallpaper had pictures on chanderliers and other wavy lines on it. The bathroom had green 1970's faux grasspaper wallpaper and floor to ceiling 1/4" cermaic titles - a heat lamp, but luckily one other small lightbulb.
The hallways were very dark (poor lighting) with silver shinny wallpaper.
Summary:
The hotel is managable for one night or if you don't plan on spending much time in the room. I would not pay full price $150 for the two rooms that we were in.

title: “Great value for money choice in Chicago !”
text: Stayed 3 days in the Days Inn Chicago which is very convient located. Area offers sufficient pubs and places for going out, and walkable distance to the Lincoln Park Zoo (free admission !). If you don't mind a longer walk you can even make it to downtown. We got a nice big room with 2 double beds, though I think this was bigger as the usual room in this vintage hotel. Excellent bedding, clean room and well varied breakfast offering fresh donuts, pastries, waffles, cereals, fruits, juices, good coffee etc. Unfortunality the hotel does not offer on-site self parking but the valet parking is reasonable priced for USD 22 with in and out priviliges.If you are on public transport a metro station is nearby. Got a good rate on the Days Inn website (advanced purchase discount). Would definitely stay here again.

title: “Good location”
text: Stayed at the Westin first weekend in December. Had a great stay with the exception that my 14 month old picked up some broken glass from the bedroom floor, and put it into her mouth. ( which must have been missed by housekeeping before we checked into our room). She was fine, but it shouldn't have been there. On the upside the view from our room which was on the 27th floor was amazing and the location of the hotel is really convenient. The heavenly bed is very comfortable, and there was a great buzz in the lobby of the hotel with the all the Christmas activities going on in the Union Square area.

title: “A Great Location, A Quiet Night”
text: My family stayed at the Hotel Beacon in a one bedroom suite while spending a week in NYC. It is in a great location, close to the 72nd St. subway and Central Park. The suite was clean, sufficiently roomy, and, despite what I had heard about NYC, the nights were very quiet. There arent a lot of extras (pool, exercise room) on site, but in a city like New York, who needs them? It is a walking city, which gave us plenty of exercise. We would not hesitate to stay at the Beacon again. Bonus: The Fairway grocery store is right across the street.

title: “Great Value. Good location”
text: I loved this little place. The rooms were sparkling clean. The free breakfast was adequate. It was right on the bus route to Santa Monica. Opposite a Ralphs if you forgot to pack anything and a stroll from the huge Westfield Mall at Century City. Our room had a spiral staircase and two TVs which was great for 3 adult women travelling together, it seemed to increase the space a lot. We only stayed in LA two nights so didn't bother with car hire. It was a short cab ride to Rodeo drive and a cheap ride back to the airport on day 3. We booked a day tour through the front desk and then when we were picked up by the tour company we decided to change tour type. This involved getting a partial refund from the hotel reception at the end of the day. We thought they might fight to keep their commission but it was handed back to us with a big smile and assurances that our good day was their priority. Amazing.

title: “Best pick in University Place”
text: Not the best Hilton Hotel in the country by Hilton standards, but it is the best hotel in the Universy Place area. The staff is friendly, the hotel clean, and rooms comfortable. The only complaint is the parking lot, it is pooly laid out, and can make for quite a long walk to the lobby. I've stayed at most hotels in this area and had some rough experiences...except at the Hilton.

title: “Do not stay at the Hotel Pennsylvania”
text: Due to an emergency at the small home we booked at, the agency we worked with sent us to this nightmare of a hotel. The lobby was fine but the room itself honestly should have been condemned. First off, it smelled like cheap disinfectant. In hindsight, it may have been pesticide because I've heard that they have one of the worst bedbug problems in the city. Huge cracks in the walls and ceiling and worst of all, a peeling, rusty, filthy bathtub. Thick dust on the mirrors, in the corners, and coating the heating unit. All of the vents were choked by dust balls. They had removed the headboard and something large on the wall of the bathroom leaving gaping holes and toggle bolts. The bed was like a rock, the pillows were old and creepy as were the sheets and towels. Between the bed, the loud street noise coming from the uninsulated windows and the broken heater which made the room stifling hot, we hardly slept at all which spoiled our first day of a two-day romantic NYC getaway. My husband took pictures of the room to show that we weren't exaggerating. We left as soon as the sun came up. I honestly wouldn't board a dog at this place. I'm AMAZED that the board of health doesn't shut it down.

title: “Best value within the Inner Harbor area”
text: The Hilton Garden Inn is quickly becoming one of my favorite hotel chains because it offers a lot of bang for the buck. This hotel is walking distance to every attraction in the Inner Harbor area (Harborplace, the Museum of Science and Industry, the Aquarium, the Power Plant, etc.) and a very short ride away from Orioles Park at Camden Yards and John Hopkins University. In addition, it is a very cozy and well kept hotel, which is sparkling clean and modernly decorated. It has the feel of being a steal, as it has the appearance of a much more expensive hotel. I guess the only thing I did not experience at the hotel was the food, as I took the opportunity to experience different restaurants around the area. That restaurant roundup is, by itself, worth at least a weekend trip. Overall, a very enjoyable experience.

title: “exceptional room with very accomodating staff”
text: We just returned from a 3 night stay in San Francisco's wonderful hotel. We have traveled the world and have been quite impressed by the level of service and the degree of attention we received from this fine hotel staff. Each and every request was satisfied. It was of great import to have a fitness center and much to my surprise that even though a bit dated and less equpment than some, the very nice thing about this one was the fact that they actually had a service to launder gym clothes. I hate traveling with "ripe" gym clothes. Location was "excellent". Near watrefront, North beach, Union Square (unfortunately my wife got me there 2X) and China town all within easy walking distance. We had a studio suite and it met our needs quite nicely...

title: “Nice hotel.. Rough part of town”
text: We stayed in the Monte Carlo suite, the bed was comfortable, bathroom was clean except for mold on the bath mat. Carpet throughout the hotel is dated and dirty. Employees are great and helpful, loved the cold drinks as we came back each afternoon. The biggest regret about the hotel is the area it is in. It's nice to be close to most things, but we disn't feel comfortable walking after dark. (and we walked a lot of different areas in SF!) not much that can be done about that, but it might make us choose a different hotel next time.

title: “Gorgeous, tech-savvy and a departure from the madness of Midtown”
text: We stayed at Conrad NYC while working through our bucket list to stay at every Conrad property. The rate was great; $219 for a Saturday night. The doorman was friendly and helpful and the bellman/Tio was terrific and gave recommendations for lunch in Chinatown and dinner in Little Italy plus a great breakfast tip. However, I specifically asked the front desk rep for a room AWAY from the elevator and we were assigned the room right AT the elevator (beware room #_26, 226,326,426,etc) BUT the view was so amazing we didnt care. Plus it was a really quiet room, sadly we DID hear kids running the halls (at a Conrad?) but still slept great. The room is very sleek. A large TV greets you with lots of options and the lights are all on a wall panel (pretty neat). The bellman walked us through all the features. AND THE SHOWER! wow, it is a rainforest shower and also has a handheld to help soothe those sore legs from sightseeing. The bed was comfy but actually quiet low to the floor, so it was hard to get up from. Nice closet space and those great Conrad slippers. I requested turndown which didnt happen at 6pm as requested, but I called the FD and it was prompted handled. ONE complaint, you have to call room service for ICE and it took 2 calls and 30 minutes to get. That is no bueno... The location was good, but hard to navigate the neighborhood due to some street closings from the WTC construction. The nicest surprise was just out the back entrance is a small plaza with GREAT GREAT GREAT shops and restaurants! A SHAKE SHACK, Francois Payard Bakery(ohh emmm geee) and Harry's Italian. Great pizza!.....we went to the rooftop Conrad LOOPY DOOPY bar for the Proseco popsicles ($17)..neat idea but expensive. it was roasting hot up there and the popsicle melted into the prosecco to flavor it in about a NY minute, so.... but it was a great stay. Def take some time to walk around the entire structure to check out the massive art collection.

title: “Good but not up to normal Langham standards”
text:
We love Langham hotels and stay regularly at the Langham in London and have also stayed at the Langham in Pasedena, LA. Both are wonderful, and we are due to stay at the Langham in Shanghai early next year. One of the reasons we chose to have a weekend break in Boston was because of the Langham.
The experience at the Langham hotel in Boston was good but not in the same league as in London or LA. In Boston, as we have experienced in all Langhams, the staff were superb and service was always efficient and friendly. The current refurbishment of the entrance and lobby definitely detracted from the feel of the hotel though; and we were not made aware of this taking place at the time of booking. It had the effect of dividing the bar and restaurant areas from the bedroom areas of the hotel and detracted from the total Langham experience in a way that did not happen when the London hotel was being extensively refurbished a few years ago. More should have been done to make the entrance and lobby more welcoming during the refurbishment, and this would not have been difficult. 
Additionally, the corridors on our floor were surprisingly bland, dated and cold; white wallpaper and no pictures. Again, this is not the Langham feel that is so prominent and wonderful in London and LA. The elevators are badly in need of refurbishment. Our room was good, although again, the bathroom lacked the feel of other Langhams we have stayed in.
We visited the Boston Harbour hotel for dinner on one evening and the ambience was much better. We are due to visit Boston again next September and are undecided whether to stay at the Langham or to try the Four Seasons or Boston Harbour but our loyalty to Langham hotels and the many lovely stays we have had in them will probably mean that we will try the Boston Langham post-refurbishment.

title: “FANTASTIC”
text: This place is great. Friendly, large rooms, great location.... this place has it all. Internet and tea and coffee on tap. I would really urge you to go to this hotel - we will definately come back. Brilliant hotel. You wont be disappointed!

title: “First Class”
text: Loved this hotel. This was the first place we stayed when we arrived in the US. As soon as we walked in the lobby we were delighted.... it's amazing. Real old style class. We had a deluxe room which was a pretty good size actually, and very nicely done. You really feel special to be staying in the Peabody. The position is great too.. you can walk to Beale St in 3 mins, but it's quiet. Basically loved it and wouldn't stay anywhere else if we come back. Do a bit of searching for prices and you might get a bargain... we booked through Hotels.com and got a third off.

title: “Great Value”
text: I was very pleased with this room. I have stayed in hotel/motels all over the country and this one is great. Rooms have TV's, frig, irons and ironing boards. Beds are comfortable and pillows are full. Rooms are clean; even the corners. The price is unbelievable. You can pay over 4 times more for a room 7 blocks away! This is my third different stay at this motel and it is great every time. I have stayed at the Ritz and for the value and results, I will come back here everytime.

title: “Overall a positive experience, but with a few negatives”
text:
First, the negatives. I understand that hotels need time to prepare rooms for their customers, and that rooms may not be available before the official check in time, which for the Peabody is 4 p.m. However, I've gotten spoiled over the years by hotels that are efficient in getting their rooms cleaned and ready for the next customer promptly--and the Peabody was slow, slow, slow. Our room wasn't ready until 3:30 p.m. and the hotel staff acted like we were being granted a great favor by being allowed to check in a half hour early. (We'd gotten there mid-morning and kept checking back every two hours to see if the room was ready.) We were part of a conference group and everyone else we talked to had the same experience. Also, the hotel has adopted the growing practice of charging a mandatory service fee--$10 at the Peabody--to use the pool, gym, and Internet. Hey guys--if it's mandatory, just build it into the room price. Finally, the lobby coffee service (no coffee pots in the room, although you may be able to ask for one) runs only from 5:30 a.m. to 7:00 a.m., and when I got there at 6:30 a.m., they'd run out of cream and lids for the cups.
Once we got to our room, however, we found it to be spacious, quiet, and comfortable. And, the hotel location is great. If you can get a reasonable price and don't mind a 4:00 p.m. check in time, it's worth considering.

title: “A birthday surprise!”
text: What a beautiful little hotel just around the corner from MSG. Pulled to the front of the hotel and the doorman pleasantly greeted us, got our bags and valet parked our car. The lobby is spacious and well appointed with lovely Gastro-bar. Clean and spacious rooms by NYC standards and timely, friendly room service. The best surprise is the price point for this very attractive package!

title: “Perfect place to stay in Chicago”
text: We could not be more pleased with our three night stay at this lovely hotel. It is the perfect location for walking to all that Chicago has to offer, from sightseeing to museums. Our riverview room was wonderful. What a great view to come back to every day & night. We highly recommend the nearby Shaw's Oyster Bar for great food, music & service.

title: “A solid choice”
text: My son and I spent two nights at the Inn during a recent trip to the East Coast and enjoyed the experience very much. The Inn is clean, quiet and architecturally very appealing.It's not cheap, but for a few nights, we thought it well worth the price. The location, so close to many of Baltimore's most interesting places and historic sights, is a special plus. Our only negative was the presence of some troublemakers outside our window late at night. Security shooed them away within minutes. We'll stay here on our next trip.Jeff Standaert, Fircrest, WA

title: “Overall it was a very pleasant experience”
text: My boyfriend and friends went to celebrate my 30th B-day in San Francisco it was difficult finding a Hotel that would accommodate 13 people. Being that is was my first time going I didn’t know were and what hotel to choose from I came across The Opal, it had reasonable prices online and was able to book with them over the phone with “Nick” very nice and informative. I had remembered after the fact that I have AAA and called customer service to find out if they give discounts they told me yes I would just show my card when I check in and get the discount. My posse and I got there at 1am in the morning as I’m checking in the lady tells me they have no more parking and will have to park a block away, I was annoyed at the fact that if I booked 2 Jr. suites they should have enough parking to accommodate the cars arriving. I then ask about the AAA discount the lady tells me she can’t override the price only a manager can and he comes in the morning. I was upset and tired that I opted to fix the problem in the morning. We get into our rooms they are not what expected for Jr. Suites small rooms we had to rearrange our sleeping arrangements. The next morning I spoke with a very pleasant rep “Angela” at the front desk I explain the situation of the parking and AAA, she begins by apologizing she tells me how the discount works which is not how I was told over the phone the 2nd time; I was unable to get the AAA discount but I did get 2 days of free parking worth $30 a day and a bottle of wine for my birthday which I was very satisfied with. She also was very helpful in giving us recommendations for restaurants and things to do in the city. I didn’t have any problems after that as a matter of fact the last day of check out was fast and easy “Carlo” checked us out told us how to get to the Golden Gate Bridge. I realized a day later on our drive back that I forgot my dress and my boyfriends dress shirt in the closest. I called right away they have a lost and found rep “Miriam” she was polite and helpful she said they did have it I asked if they would be able to ship it to me with no hesitation she said of course we can do that for you. I now have my belongings and back home with great memories to look back on.

title: “Great place to stay”
text: This is a great hotel, I would highly recommend it to anyone visiting the New York area. The staff was very nice and helpful with every and all questions. WTC,Battery Park,Centry 21 all at your doorstep. Subway stops to take you any where you wanted to go. I loved the excitement of Uptown,but it was nice to come home every night to the quiet of The Cosmopolitan Hotel.

title: “a disappointment”
text:
the envoy club suites was recommended to us by friends . on arriving, it was a terrible disappointment!! our one bedroom self contained suite, was rather old. the carpet stained, windows dirty. bath plug broken.thankfully, however, to their credit, they fixed us a plug when requested on the second day. the springs in the sofa bed, stuck into my daughter's back, giving a very uncomfortable first night. the cleaning maid was very accommodating and put an extra comfort on top to improve things a little. the bathroom and kitchen, though old, was clean.
i had booked a few months early, and specially requested a rollaway to be added for when my 23 year old son arrived, and confirmed this several times with reservations., and also on arrival. to which, no-one ever said, they were subject to the day!! so, we found, that the night my son was to arrive, there was no rollaway available!!
i definitely would not recommend this hotel, unless you desperately need to be next door to the hospital. this part of town is not as pleasant as staying on the west side, especially upper west. true, you are not far from centre of town and the 15 bus is close by to catch to and from lower manhattan. however, if you are looking for somewhere with a nicer view and surroundings or pleasant area to walk, don't book here.

title: “Used to be great dump, for the price”
text:
The Hotel 17 is a classic Lower Manhattan dump, and it always has been. However, it used to be terrific place, for the price. I do mean FOR THE PRICE.
First off - the neighborhood is really choice. There's almost no place that could be better- Gramercy is a great location, bar none. It is residential, and there are no hotels to speak of- except two that are extremely expensive. This is why the 17 has upped the price so severely. So there is that. Of course, if the 17 is going to command these prices, keep in mind that all of Manhattan is very accessible- you don't need to pay these prices for a crap hotel in this area.
The 17 used to be such a great dump. Though not fancy, and with the bathrooms down the hall, all of this was clean, clean, clean. Now they don't bother, and the rooms are triple the price. The beds were always so uncomfortable that sleeping on the floor might be better for some- but who could argue, for the price and location?
Well, now you can. Although I have always liked the 17, I would not pay the current rate. For what they are charging, I would be fine in Brooklyn,or at other places in the NYC area.
It's still a good little place, I'm sure- if you want to pay those rates. This is an old hotel, and one that is known by artsy performance types as working for us. It doesn't any more. If you seriously want to pay $160 for the Hotel 17, you go right ahead. It isn't worth it, as a hotel- the neighborhood might be, but let me reiterate- it's Manhattan, you can get where you need to go, anyway.
If you get a great rate, worth it. It's a sort of charming place with a great vibe- the bathroom down the hall thing really works, the way they have it set up. If you're desperate for a room in the area and willing to pay the current asking price, then do it. If you know how to do better, don't.

title: “Good central hotel”
text:
I booked this hotel through priceline and for what I paid I liked what I got. 
PROS: It was centrally located and trendy. We were in the 11th floor facing 45th street and the room was quiet. The bed was very comfortable and there were lots of soft pillows. The bathroom was well appointed and had nice big fluffy towels. I loved the huge shower head. I forgot my toothpaste and after calling the front desk I got a courtesy tube and two toothbrushes. 
CONS: The carped looked a little dingy and had a couple of large stains, but other than that everything was clean. I did not like that you had to pay for wi-fi. The magnetic keys were a bit touchy and I had to insert them several times to get them to work.
Overall I liked to hotel but I probably would not pay full price to stay here again.

title: “Should be #1 in Memphis”
text:
For about the same price as the Talbot Heirs Guest House B&B in Memphis, the Madison Hotel offers a "boutique European hotel" experience as an alternative to a funky artistic B&B. The Madison Hotel is very clean and nicely decorated in a contemporary-ish style. Original 1920's wood windows in the bathroom and the bedroom. Air conditioner works great. Upscale Moulton Brown toiletries from London. 
The rooftop bar provides the local flavor -- a fantastic view of the mighty Mississippi River. Valet staff super-courteous - I left my glasses in the car one night, and my cell phone the next night; the valets found them and delivered them to my room with a smile. In fact, the entire staff is well-trained. I will stay here the next time I visit Memphis. Highly recommended.
P.S. The Madison Hotel is 2 blocks from the famous Peabody Hotel in downtown Memphis. Call the hotel for directions from the airport; Google Maps is wrong, due to a recently installed trolley line on Madison Ave. The I-55/Riverside Drive approach is most scenic.

title: “Good location if you want Midtown, mediocre hotel.”
text:
The lobby belies a somewhat dated hotel behind the scenes. Staff service was all over the board from helpful to downright rude. I was not impressed with the cleanliness of the rooms either. Dust, hair in the bathroom, grungy carpeting all added to the feeling that things we're a bit slip shod. It felt like a 'cattle' hotel - designed to move the masses not cater to guests. 
The bar was ridiculously overpriced even by NYC standards and you will be charged to store your luggage before or after your stay. 
We were here for a small conference and honestly the 'ballroom' was dated, dirty, poorly lit and in a sub basement. The restrooms were about one notch above a gas station (in the woman's room only one door had a working lock). They were obviously not updated with the rest of the hotel. Not an inspiring place to learn something new! 
If you needed a place to stay centrally for a night or two, this would be okay, but with all the lodging options in a city the size of New York, I'd look elsewhere first. But note that I think the concierge service is a third party service not connected to the hotel so don't expect the staff there to even be able to tell you where things in the hotel are located. 
Oh, icing on the cake? The gap around the door in our room was big enough to see in and out of! Hey, a free peep show for people passing by in the hallway. ugh.

title: “I loved it and I'll be back”
text:
I was at the Austin Airport and needed a place to stay for one night. I called this hotel using the courtesy phone and from the moment they answered to the moment I checked out they were amazing. The hotel is very clean and well kept. They offer a free hot breakfast, a free airport shuttle, and free local & long distance calls within the US. They also have free WIFI and if that wasn't enough...every day they have warm cookies for your to snack on with unlimited coffee and tea in the lobby.
Most importantly though, the guest service was amazing. The team is so friendly, courteous, helpful, and professional. 
I recommend this hotel for anyone who needs to be out by the airport in Austin. You can't beat the value and the service is second to none.
Thanks for showing me some true Texas hospitality.

title: “It's TIME to make some serious changes”
text: I checked in for a 2 night stay and it started off well. The front desk informed me I was upgraded to a nicer room. As soon as I walked in and put my bags down, I shuddered to imagine what my original room must've looked like. There were empty bottles of cheap wine from the mini fridge around my room. After calling to complain, they assured me I wouldn't be charged for the bottles, but didn't send anyone up to clean my room. There were vomit stains on the sofa, the room smelled like stale cigarette smoke, and the lamps and light switches were either cracked or completely not functional. When it came time to check out, sure enough I was charged for the wine bottles and a slew of other items I never took. Although they promptly removed the charges, there will have to be a LOT of changes made before I consider The Time again.

title: “Great place to stay”
text: This hotel is attractive, neat & clean; a great place to stay. The staff was very friendly and helpful. It seems a bit out of the way, but it's easy to get to and there's a lot around; food & shopping. Plus it has the little free things other "upper scale" hotels nickel & dime you for, such as free internet, free breakfast, and a business center where you can work online & print (boarding passes!). Great place.

title: “Location is good but not up to par for the price point”
text:
Great location, near places like Starbucks, Whole Foods, restaurants, embassies and close enough to walk to Chinatown, the Smithsonians, the White House, etc.
The hotel puts up a good face (lobby looks nice, facade looks good) but in the interior, the age of the building shows. While the rooms are nice enough in terms of furniture and size, the bathrooms are a bit small. Wi-fi works very well. The hallways & elevators are not in good shape, much as they have attempted to dress them up a little (good try, but not enough). The exercise room has a couple of workout machines but the weight equipment is extremely outdated (1980s). As a frequent business traveler, I need to have access to a decent (not state-of-the-art) gym and this one falls way short. It could be a big improvement in the value for the buck to modernize it more.
My bigger issue is that the price point does not match the property. While staff is friendly, lobby looks nice, and the location is very good, I expect more of the physical qualities for that money.

title: “Hot, tiny room and surly staff.”
text: Booked a prepaid rate 10 days in advance. Called the hotel on the afternoon of our arrival to say we'd be arriving late. When we arrived we were given a tiny room with no windows. The incredibly noisy air conditioner, even when cranked to capacity, could only get the room temperature to 87 degrees. The desk clerk was surly and dismissive when we asked for a different room. I'm writing this at 3:30 a.m. because it's impossible to sleep in this cramped oven.

title: “Adequate”
text: I don't think the hotel deserves the bad rap it seems to get, although it is at best average for its class. The room was fine; quite large actually. The staff were fine. I resent paying for internet, but that's endemic with 4 star hotels. I got the place cheap via Hotwire, so it was good value.

title: “Excellence in Customer Service”
text: Christmas for singles or couples,... Awe inspiring Lobby and immediate recognition of your name throughout your stay, you truly feel like a VIP...wonderful pool and workout room...The staff treatment of you = VIP.

title: “Convenience?”
text: Really, the only reason I spend more money staying here vs. nicer places at the same price or equal places at a lower price is convenience to the area. On my last stay, they wouldn't allow guest to park at the garage - even if you PREPAID parking when you made your reservation. They claimed it was full of guests of the hotel, some dance convention. I sensed this was not true. I believe it was NOT used for the guest, but just attendees of the convention. The garage should be reserved - or at least enough spaces should be reserved for paying Hyatt guest. Especially if we PREPAID for parking. Again - that is the only reason I stay there.....so probably won't next time seeing that this is a risk you take. Incidentally - parking was provided in the McCormick Convention center as a concession. Walking at a brisk pace, it took me 25 minutes to get to my car from the hotel lobby.

title: “Starwood Preferred Guest = Preferred Treatment at "W"”
text:
Great weekend trip to NY with the family at the W on Lexington. As a Gold SPG member travelling with a family I was concerned about the size of the rooms however the hotel upgraded our rooms to Spa Suites. The service and overall experience reminded me why I stay 40 nights a year at Starwood properties as a "Road Warrior" so I can reward the family. The W came through with spectacular (and quiet) rooms, great overall service, great fitness center, super comfortable beds, and the girls loved the Bliss products. 
Best stay in a NY hotel ever!

title: “Renewal of vows”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the trump as we were renewing our vows in Central Park. The hotel was excellent.
The staff could not do enough for us. The park suite we had was wonderful with views overlooking Central Park. 
Location was excellent. Right next to Columbus circle and 59th station so easy to get everywhere. 
Would recommend this hotel to all. Would love to stay again on next trip to New York.

title: “Loved the Mystic!”
text:
I am a boutique hotel lover so this place fit the bill for me. It was in an excellent location a block from Union Square and next to China Town plus parking is directly across the street. It is an old building that has been upgraded with trendy decor. The staff was really friendly, professional and accommodating. 
I paid $129 for my room through Hotels.com and felt I got a great deal with the location and room. My room was huge, especially for San Francisco so I am not sure if I was upgraded or not. I had a spacious king size bed with giant wall mounted TV screen in one room with a attached sitting room with couch, desk and coffee table and my bathroom was completely brand new. I must have been placed in the newly remodeled rooms which are great! The layout and decor were great and I felt very comfortable in the room. I could see Union Square from my window. Probably the only complaint here was the towels, which were average. I prefer soft fluffy towels.
I was on the 7th floor in the back so I did not hear any noise at all from the street or bar as others have mentioned. The second floor has a small bar with live jazz music and a restaurant which was very nice and had a sophisticated and trendy crowd. They serve a free continental breakfast in the restaurant with fresh pastries, juice, milk, coffee, cereal, oatmeal, fruit and hard boiled eggs. The staff again was very friendly, cleared tables immediately and kept items constantly replenished. They have one computer in the lobby with free access and printing but it was rarely being used.
The only things I could see fixing are of course new towels as mentioned and some people may complain their are no bathtubs in the rooms. I do like to take a bath while away. Oh and the elevator is painfully slow but really you should be relaxing, right?

title: “Great hotel with great staff”
text: We stayed in the Palomar as part of our Honeymoon. The hotel is ideally located, being within walking distances of restaurants and the Metro. All of the staff were very friendly and helpful and we were given a complimentary upgrade. Our room was very spacious and breakfast had a good range of options. The wine reception was very enjoyable with a great atmosphere. We will definitely stay here again.

title: “OUR STAY IN DECEMBER 2011 AND JAN. 2012”
text: The Mark is THE place to stay ! The design, the rooms, the bar, the restaurant where we eat very well and all the staff make that you feel like at home ! When the theaters for musical comedies or the Met opera were sold out, the Concierge, particularly Isabelle and Gilles, have found very good seats and we were never disappointed ! In December 2011 we have so enjoyed our stay that we were already back to the Mark at the end of January 2012 ! Marie-Jo Lunati / Geneva / Switzerland

title: “First rate experience”
text: My sister and I stayed here from August 1st through 6th. We felt like we were living the dream. Valet parking was so convenient. Right at the start, checkin was quick, efficient and very friendly. Our room was spacious, clean and well laid out. Room service was super, and when we requested extra towels,(we like a lot) the housekeeping service fell over themselves to provide them. Breakfast was plentiful and hot and oh my, the happy hour. Let me just say, for us it was dinner, there was plenty of food and a good variety. The cocktails were an added bonus. One day we requested to have our car pulled out at a certain time, and when I went to double check on the request early, they pointed to our car and said, "you mean that one." Wow!

title: “Great location, free breakfast”
text: We have stayed here several times and each time it has been great! Check-in process was easy, having a suite is great when traveling with children or for a girls getaway weekend. Rooms have been updated in the last year. Breakfast offering is great. Staff is very helpful. Evening reception also kids you free drinks and appetizers. My suggestion is get there right when it starts that you are able to find a place to sit. Restaurants and tons of shopping are all within walking distance. This is our favorite place to stay when we stay in the city. PARKING TIP: Self park in any lot within two or three blocks of the hotel and it is about half of the price of parking at the hotel.

title: “Sincere thoughtful service”
text: Pros: I think that the management has done a good job in training staff to be happy when they give sincere thoughtful service. We arrived well before standard check in-time and would have to wait a few hours for housekeeping to clean the rooms. Sasha at the front desk suggested an upgrade to a suite (only $50 more/night) which was available immediately. The upgrade was well worth those extra hours of fun in NYC!! Once we got into the room, we wanted some ice and I was on my way to finding the machine when a nice gentleman from housekeeping approached me and to offered to bring it to my room. Then he said "Have a nice day". I was especially impressed with ALL the housekeeping staff because they always greeted you with a smile and seemed genuinely happy that they made you smile back. Cons: $8 just to sign onto the internet at the business center. Shower has glass enclosure and no privacy, so no-one elsse can use the bathroom while you are in there. Overall, the hotel is a little spendy, but gracious service is priceless (and doesn't cost the hotel anything!!)

title: “Great Value”
text:
This hotel is a great value for its walking proximity to the Galleria Mall and short drive to Downtown Houston. I've researched other places nearby with similar amenities and location and found this Extended Stay America, (formerly Homestead Suites), the best value for your buck.
Good:
Housekeeping comes twice/week complimentary to replenish your room with fresh towels/soap/linens. Secured parking w/cameras in the parking lot, secured door access key cards, and secured laundry facilities make this facility safe and secure. However, the best attribute to this hotel is its friendly and courteous front desk staff. Thank you Zeba, Illia, and Ashley for all the hard work you put into making my stay safe and welcomed. This hotel was my home away from home. You ladies are the best.
Bad:
Terrible free wireless connection. Not good for business traveler's needing Wifi. However, not entirely the hotel's fault as a third-party services this hotel's wireless connection. Starbuck's free Wifi is walking distance nearby down the street along Westheimer in front of the Mall.

title: “Great location, charming hotel”
text:
My daughter & I went on a bus trip to NYC to experience New Year's Eve at Times Square. The location was ideal for this purpose & also for getting to many other sights & transportation.
This is my third time at the Edison & I find the hotel to be quite charming. I would rate it 3 or 4 stars. It's attraction is it's great location~ near Times Sq., on 46th St (restaurant row) & in the Theatre District, plus close to TKTS & the Times Square info centre where there's some internet access, bus passes etc.
We had breakfast at the cafe in the lobby. It was fine BUT they only take cash or travellers cheques as payment. The dinner specials always looked very interesting. Danny's deli next door is also great with fresh fruit, hot buffet choices & sandwiches available. Some items are sold by weight & I must say their orange juice was the best I've ever had! It's also open 24 hours!
We really enjoyed our stay there & would go back in a flash.

title: “A wonderful, magical place!”
text: My wife and I stayed at The Greenwich last week, we needed a local vacation during some repair work on our apartment. Our stay was amazing, the staff is way above par, the cleanliness and atmosphere also were outstanding. We picked the hotel because we loved the interiors we had seen before. The rooms are super comfy, the bed was like home. You also have to see and enjoy the pool, a true wonder in NYC, not to mention the amazing music and atmosphere in the lobby lounge area, we enjoyed a few drinks there and will be back! Overall, it was a great, quiet and relaxing place to stay.

title: “Loved the Catamaran. Can't wait to go back!”
text:
We loved our stay at the Catamaran! The location is perfect, the grounds are beautiful and everything was clean and well attended. The service was awesome. 
I will start with the service at this resort. When we arrived (quite early) our room was not ready but they offered to call our cell when the room was ready. I thought, ya, sure. Well they did call! Our deluxe king garden room was on the second floor very near the lobby, a great central location. The room was good size, well appointed and clean. Nice flat screen TV and a fridge. Large closet. Comfy bed. The next day we got a call in the morning that the water heater had broken in our building and we had to be moved. That was a bummer as we had unpacked everything, had gotten groceries etc. I asked where we were being moved to. They said they would give us an upgrade to a BAY FRONT room. We packed our stuff and got assistance will our move. The view from the bay front room was awesome. The room was bigger, the bath and sink area was huge (double sinks, yay!), there was an even bigger flat screen TV as well as a couch. The bed was still nice and comfy (there is nothing worse than a crappy hotel room bed!). We had a room with a second floor balcony maybe 20 feet from the bay board walk and the white sand beach of Mission Bay. I was sooo happy that water heater broke and was very impressed with the management for taking such good care of us. But, it gets better. We left for the afternoon and when we returned to our room the management had provided us a wine and cheese tray as well as a card apologizing for any inconvenience! We have traveled to lots of hotels and have been on several cruises with various problems that have popped up and never, ever, have we been treated so well. After staying in both rooms I would recommend paying the extra cash to have a bay front room. I think it is well worth the view and the people watching. 
The location of the Catamaran is great. It is located on Mission Bay, which is a much quieter location than on the Pacific side of things. But, if you want to see the Pacific you just walk one block over and you are right there. There are great restaurants, shops and groceries within walking distance. We rented a car while in San Diego but your really don’t need one in this location with public transportation being what is and with everything being so close. (Parking can be a pain and you usually have to pay. Watch the parking signs on the street closely, we almost got a parking ticket!) Our favorite restaurant was just a few steps from the Catamaran. It is called “World Famous” and is right on the beach. Go at sunset for an incredible view! They have the best lobster bisque soup I have ever had. 
The grounds of the Catamaran were very tropical. Lots of palm trees and flowers. They keep ducks, geese and other birds on the property-- lots of fun to watch and photograph. The pool and the hot tub was clean and good size. The spa seemed very nice as well (a little spendy though). The lobby has a huge waterfall. 
We did not eat on the property but we were there on Mothers Day and there were lots of people paying $40/person for the buffet. I guess it must be good. 
We would not hesitate to recommend the Catamaran. Everyone from the front desk staff to the maids to the gardeners were very friendly. We hope we can go back sometime very soon.

title: “very comfortable and clean”
text:
We stayed here for 3 nights. The rooms were clean and bed was very comfortable. It had a refrigerator and microwave which was a bonus for such inexpensive price. The Manager was helpful and polite. We needed printouts for our Universal Studios visit and he gladly printed for us for free.
We would like to stay here whenever we are in LA.

title: “Not worth it”
text:
For a hotel with a recent refurb, this hotel has a long way to go.
Note for the business traveller: no platnium / club lounge.
ROOMS: with 2 teenagers it was too small. As a platnium guest I did not get an upgrade to a suite and there was not enough floor space for 4 suitcases. Washroom/toilet is the smallest I have ever seen in my 25 years of travel. If you are a person of size, forget about using the toilet 'cos you will not fit in the space between the door and the bath. Sink/mirror space was tiny and useless. Room was quite noisy and you needed a strong arm to attempt to open the window.
SERVICE: not great at all. Concierge was grumpy and very unhelpful on 2 occasions and on another occasion while waiting for the tour bus to pick us up, the concierge (french guy) said.....hang on, I will call the company as the owner is my boss ! WHAT?
When I called the guest services line it was a great experience with follow up calls about 10 minutes later to check if everything was ok. BUT after calling for a corkscrew and then realizing that there were no wine glasses in the room, I had to call them again. About 10 minutes later a lady from room service called me asking why I didn't ask for both at the same time. That put me over the top.
RECEPTION / BAR:
Again for a hotel that had a refurb, the reception and bar area are very very badly organized and designed. The seating for the bar is the reception wating area so as we sat down for a drink after a long day, we had to negotiate through and then listen to large noisy groups of travellers, some with suitcases in the same area. This is the most pathetic set up I have ever seen.
Swimming pool was very small, uninviting and with the cold spell in San Fran, not inviting at all.

title: “Ranked #1 for a reason”
text: My husband and I stayed one night at the Elysian and if you are looking for a luxury hotel that puts the emphasis on service - this is the place to stay. The staff are all exceedingly pleasant and accomodating which, being from Chicago originally, is something you hope to see projected to visitors to the Midwest's biggest city. Ordered room service up to the spa and for breakfast and it was delicious and speedy. There was a delay in getting in to the room we had originally booked, so we were automatically upgraded to a gorgeous Gold Coast suite at no extra charge. Every little request we had was handled quickly and politely.

title: “Very nice hotel shame about the wireless”
text:
Myself and my girlfriend stayed here for 4 nights from September 29th. It is a very nice hotel, we had a suite on floor 26 and so had an excellent view of Times Square. Basically all the previous reviews are ptty much bang on, it's a very nice hotel in the best location in New York City. 
My one issue would be the Internet, it's one of the few hotels left that don't offer free wireless. They charge you an additional $12.95 for 24 hours, in this day and age and given it is the centre of New York City I found that surprising and disappointing. The moment you step outside the front door though you can instantly pick up and connect to 5 or 6 free wireless Internet connections that are available in times square.

title: “Fantastic Argonaut”
text: Fantastic hotel, fantastic setting and fantastic city. Loved the Argonaut - very homely and the quirky rooms were so comfortable. We had the best view and the staff were always polite and friendly without being intrusive. Definitely a city and most definitely a hotel we'll come back to again. No complaints at all. Highlight of our trip to US.

title: “Good hotel with some outrageous fees. Book it on priceline to save.”
text:
The good: This is an older but well maintained Hilton property, so you can expect a decent stay with no major problems. Rooms were quite nice with comfy beds and quality linens. The hotel is literally across the street from the Seattle airport so it is convenient. Another bonus is the fact that this hotel sells a ton of rooms through priceline for very low rates. Bid there to get the best deal, and save 50% or more off your stay. We got a very low price on the hotel itself, comparable with the local "Super 6" kinda motels, and a much better room of course. 
Now, the bad: They do their very best to nickel and dime you to death. Parking is a moderately outrageous $21 per night. There is a fee for internet access. Breakfast will run you about $15 for a couple eggs and some toast. Upon checkin, we informed the front desk that we would only be parking for one night, not the second night of our stay. We were assured that we would only be charged for one night. Well, you guessed it, we got charged for two nights. They fixed it but it's still annoying. The staff was okay, but not the most friendly you'll ever encounter. Finally, this hotel is huge, with multiple wings that barely connect. You need to take more than one elevator to get to some rooms. If I had major mobility issues I would avoid this place. Overall a very decent room with a couple minor hassles and some concerted attempts at price gouging.

title: “Washington D.C Sightseeing”
text: The hotel is very convenient as it has the metro subway system below the hotel. You are only 2 or 3 stops away from the major attractions. Union station to hotel either by taxi ($10.) or 3 metro stops. You can take a 15 minute walk to some sights. Close to Chinatown and Ford theatre. Great pub restaurant across the street. However, the lobby is not condusive to relaxing after a hard day sightseeing.

title: “Second time - NIGHTMARE!”
text:
Had a semi-bad experience about a year ago and the general manager phoned me about that and PROMISED me the next time I booked to contact him and he would get me the best suite available at the time of booking. Therefore, this review will mainly consist of my EXPERIENCE this time around rather than describing the hotel amenities, etc.
I went ahead and booked it (two rooms in fact with the referral I gave my Aussie friends) and contacted the GM IMMEDIATELY after booking the room- Christopher Hosmer. He was out of town and I booked a non refundable rate. I was told a suite would be unavailable but I would receive a junior suite (with french doors), which I was happy with as this would suffice for my purposes. 
Upon check in I was told I had a "junior suite" but when I entered it was indeed the large room, no divider walls after countless calls and a written confirmation (on Marriott's site). I went downstairs and spoke with Richard (the evening manager) who insisted the room assigned was a junior suite (which did not meet the specifications if you look at the room details of the junior suite - two televisions, french doors, etc on their site under room details). My battery was dead on my phone and I was unable to pull up the confirmation and stumbled through luggage to look for the printed version for my two night stay. 
Finally, Richard emerged with a confirmation stating it was a "larger room." I was beside myself and ready to move to another property. As I was calling other properties in desperation and considering leaving the city, Richard finally came back out and stated he would be able to give me the junior suite for the two nights booked under my name and apologized, shook my hand, etc. I happily went to the new room, which was absolutely fine.
We ended up having a great time but after such a delayed flight from LAX and then meeting my friends, we ended up sleeping in until pretty late to get a late start on the only full day that I had there. 
After check out, my friends advised me the Marriott would be charging me an additional night in fees and said I did not fully prepay this, which I did (even have the confirmation and charge made in July) when I was already back in LA. I contacted them and will be disputing this with my credit card company. 
Never again will I trust this hotel and there is no way this can be made up. I was completely lied to and mislead and this is not the way to treat customers - ever! This is my own opinion and I truly dislike writing reviews that reflect a negative opinion, but the truth should be out there and people should not have to deal with crooks who run a hotel. 
I think Tony Soprano would do a better job then the persons managing this property.

title: “Gorgeous and a top notch experience except for...”
text: Stayed at this property in May 2012 for business and happened to coincide with American Idol finals. The hotels size made certain it wasn't overrun with crazed fans, the staff was terrific-friendly, welcoming and not at all pretentious. Spa and massage was divine. Only complaint was that I got very sick during my staff and needed to find a 24 hr pharmacy in the area on a sunday night. Unfortunately the club level concierge wasn't prepared for this not so odd request because it took about 35 minutes for a call back. After searching on my own, I found a CVs store only 10 Minutes away by taxi vs the eventual recommendation by the concierge for a pharmacy in silver lake- 25 minutes away! I took matters into my own hands and went to the closer one. Other than this letdown the hotel was a top notch place as you would expect from the brand.

title: “New Wave Experience (for younger crowd)”
text:
