My wife and I and two friends were spending a long Canadian Thanksgiving in New York City - our first time there. We booked this hotel back in June and got a great introductory rate. The hotel is a 10 min walk from Times Square, so very central. What a crazy place. Everything is purple and it appeals to a young crowd. The staff were really friendly and helpful. The theme of the hotel is like a cruise ship. Your room is 'cabin' - and the smallness that that brings. The room is very open with no door to the bathroom. So if you're at all shy about sharing your bathroom business, be forewarned. To save floor space the bed is motorized and folds up into sort of a couch size when you are not sleeping. Everything is pretty cool, but it is far from a classic hotel that us 50ish types are used to. 
The food in the restaurant was good and beer on the outdoor patio was nice. Very warm nights for October. Heated towel bar was a nice treat - but then they provided one ply, rough toilet paper and a purse size kleenex bag. Hmmmm. Oh, and the mattress.... It was hard and only 4" thick. Took a bit of getting used to. Our friends asked for and recieved an extra mattress pad that seemed to help.
So, in the end, the staff were great, the theme was interesting (especially if you are younger), the place was clean and it is centrally located. Would I stay there again? If the price at the time was less than a 'standard' hotel - yes. Otherwise, I would go elsewhere.

title: “Working Play”
text:
Went there with my spouse for a conference. I thorouhly enjoy the atmosphere and my wife enjoyed her days at the pool and Spa day. Golf course was great and the staff was excellent right down to the valets.
We celebrated my wife's birthday at Tuscany resturant and that was great.
My wife's experience at the Spa just added icing to the cake.
Can't wait to go back next year!

title: “Absolute disgrace!”
text: First room we found a pin on the floor, then after further exploration we discovered food, paper and a sock insert in the room. Security came and quickly removed the pin as evidence and advised management would come to see us. Which they never did. Travon on the front desk was lovely and did his best to find us a clean room which as two further room changes still hadn't happened. I asked to be escalated and was given Suzan/ Suzannah who has been rude, left us waiting an hour, and took me to view the 4th room we could may possibly find clean and suitable. I just walked in the door and a small plastic washer type ring greeted me on the floor! Perfect for my 11 month old to swallow. Upon further inspecting a huge lump of lint with long black hair was on the floor just under the skirt of the bed! She claims she inspected the room on her hands and knees herself! What a joke. This is our second stay, we had come here on our honeymoon and loved it. This time it's just disgusting. If you are traveling as a family with small children go somewhere else. It's not acceptable that even our 4th room is not beautifully cleaned. The sad thing is we have 7 more nights to stay in this feral hotel! NEVER EVER AGAIN!

title: “Ask about elevator before you book! Check in is at 4 PM, none earlier”
text:
Just returned from a 3-night stay at Roosevelt. 
First of all, the staff was cordial and friendly uniformly. They tried their best with a tough situation. The place was down to one smallish elevator. Because this place is popular with cruise folks with lots of luggage, this meant LONG waits during rush periods. I would not book a room until all elevators are working.
Second, my cable TV did not work most of the time. They would fix it; then it would go out. I was there on business so -- apart from the World Cup Final -- this was no big deal. However, if you were there with kids.....
Good things about hotel: Staff; location (near Convention center, Westlake -- where airport train comes in, and Pike St. Market), price is high but this is downtown Seattle. Vonn's restaurant next door has Sunday buffet brunch for $10. It is nothing special but worth the $10. (Excellent bacon...) 
My room was a little stodgy but clean and quiet. AC worked well. Free Wi Fi in lobby + one public computer there; pay wi fi in rooms. Nice big TV but cable didn't work well.
Bad? Elevator (being repaired) and check in time. Bad cable TV. One ice machine on 3rd floor. If you are big ice person, this could be a pain. I didn't care.
I didn't have a car so I can't comment on parking although it seemed to be right next door. I came from airport on Grey Line Shuttle ($15) and was dropped right across the street. And I took light rail train back to airport (short walk over to Westlake from Roosevelt); long walk at airport through most of parking garage to terminal.

title: “Comfortable Stay”
text: This hotel is great for a business trip or short stay. The staff is excellent, room comfortable and clean, and breakfast delicious. However, the bathroom sink is set too far away (close to the mirror) and it was not easy to lean so far forward to use the sink.

title: “Disliked the Sheraton Gunter Hotel”
text: I was highly disappointed with the Sheraton Gunter Hotel in San Antonio, Texas. The weather was quite cold during my trip and the room's heat wasn't working. The thermostat was stuck on 68 degrees. Maintenance came up and "fixed it", but the heat still never worked. They had to come up again and futz with the settings and it finally went up 2 degrees. The windows in the room were so thin we could hear everything on the street below. Our bathroom was filthy, also. I took a bath my first night there and had to stare at the disgusting filth underneath the sink while I bathed. Our toilet was so stained I could barely tolerate sitting on it. The coffee machine was lousy, I thought it was going to start out hotel room on fire. The lobby smelled of stale butter, it was gross. I would never stay at the Sheraton Gunter again.

title: “Wonderful LITTLE Hotel”
text:
This is a wonderful hotel. While the rooms are small they make up for them in price. The hotel staff was very helpful and the were always there to help. A great place to eat breakfast is right next door at the little cafe. For two people you can get out under $10. 
Subway station is close at the corner of 35th and 6th Ave and you can get to about any where from the trains that stop there. Dont be scared of the subways they are the best way to see ALL of New York.

title: “Enjoyable first time stay”
text:
We stayed here 17-21 June, on 21st floor. I can see why other reviewers have commented on the age/decoration of the hotel, it could probably do with a refurb, but we found our room large, clean and comfortable. We didn't wait long for the lifts either. 
The best thing about the Wellington is its location. Diner underneath (used 3/4 mornings for bfast), other diners/delis on next block (Premier deli - good for snacks). 10 mins to Times Square, theatres nearby(saw Jersey Boys - fab), subway on corner, we walked to Rockerfeller Centre. We brought a travel kettle and instant tea with us for an early morning cuppa as no facilities in room for this. 
I gave very good instead of excellent due to noisy air-con, but this is probably due to the hotel's age.

title: “Disappointing for a Westin Property”
text: My husband and I were recent guests at the Westin Riverwalk hotel. Upon arrival the concierge was friendly and happy to be of service, as was the front desk. We were able to check in early which was much appreciated and welcomed since it was pouring outside. As we entered our Riverwalk river view room on the 11th floor we couldn't have been more dissapointed. I quickly called after being reassured by the front desk that we had a view (our only view was the top of the parking garage). We were told we could upgrade to another room for a small fee. This was absurd, and something we have never witnessed in a Westin property. When booking, be sure to fully understand the type of room you are getting, descriptions aren't always the best and most accurate. The lobby was pretty and the hotel bar was nice; however, the rooms could use a little love.

title: “Felt like a millionaire!”
text: This hotel was amazing! Everything was fantastic from the minute we walked through the double doors into the very awesome bar. The check in was seamless and we were given a fabulous room overlooking city hall. It is in a remodeled YMCA and is a very cool space. The guestrooms are a little small but the space is very efficient. It was so clean it felt like we were the first people to stay in the room. I loved everything about this place except leaving!

title: “Worh the laet check-in wait”
text: The Hampton is located just around the corner from the Convention Centre which is central and ideal for tourist as well as business users. We did not appreciate the late check-in time of 4pm after arriving in the city late morning although once we were in the room we were pleased with the standard. The facilties were great and warm or cold drinks were freely available all day with free breakfast every morning if you needed it. The excellent Reading Terminal Market is a stone's throw away which was our prefered spot for a morning brew to watch the world go by. When in Philly, give this hotel your consideration

title: “Quick getaway”
text: This was our second time staying at the Omni. Great hotel, location and the staff is always nice and helpful.

title: “Totally hooked up my parents!”
text:
My parents were planning on going to Chicago for my father's 81st birthday and their 43rd wedding anniversary. When I asked where they were planning on staying, they replied 'Red Roof Inn'. Noooooooo! I quickly called Blu Aqua Hotel and booked a 2-night stay (my treat!) for them. Blu Aqua was awesome! They first looked to see if there were any specials they had for seniors. They didn't at the time, so they offered a breakfast and balcony room package deal. 
Blu Aqua upgraded my parents room to a corner room (much bigger) with wrap around balcony. They had beautiful chocolates waiting in their room (a birthday and anniversary gift from hotel). They also allowed my parents a super late check out.
While in Chicago, my Dad got his wallet snatched (not anywhere near the hotel). The Concierge totally helped Dad cancel his cards by looking online for phone numbers, etc. This would have taken a huge amount of time (and a lot of stress) for my non-tech savvy parents to do this on their own. I totally appreciate how Blu Aqu took care of my parents (especially after the wallet snatching - and helped make such an enjoyable trip).
My parents are older (Mom - 72, Dad - 81). It's nice to know someone (Blu Aqu) is looking out for them - when I'm thousands of miles away. THANK YOU, Blu Aqu!!!!

title: “Palmer Hilton building is much preserved lady from another time....”
text:
The Palmer Hilton Hotel is lovely and very large which is fine. The lobby alone makes for a great meetup space. Here for a few days, I must admit that I felt the front desk was very cold and actually snippy when I tried to clarify a few things about my reservation. A late night request for a razor meant that I would have to wait for housekeeping to bring it up. As they did not service my room during the few hours I was gone, I though better of it. 
The room had a small queen which I suspect is a double. Normally, I would have asked for a queen but I was too tired during my visit to argue. The room lacks things that one finds in other Hiltons such as a coffemaker although there is a Starbucks in the basement. You cannot get a better location in the Loop but I think there may be better rooms elsewhere and certainly a better front desk. Every time one approaches the front desk, well there seems to be at least three employees that are not actually working and that gives the Palmer Hilton and United States Office feel- unless you count the hip hop music coming out of the Potter Lounge. 
Plus: Bed, the bedding and the towels. Closet for bags. One luggage rack, ( two would be better). Lovely lobby. Fine TV, many but not all channels. Business Center is adequate. Location!!! 
Cons: no coffemaker in room, iffy housekeeping ( but it is very clean) and a front desk that could be improved.

title: “Great location”
text: Really enjoyed our stay at Hotel Abri. The location was great-near lots of shopping,restaurants,1 block from the cable car stop and bus stops. Comfortable bed and modern decor. The rooms look much bigger online, but I guess that's to be expected staying downtown. The price was great for staying in San Francisco. Our room looked out on to the street so there was definitely a noise issue(I just wore ear plugs). Overall: very friendly hotel staff, great location, clean rooms. We would stay again on a return trip.

title: “Great Location - Overall Good”
text: I was nervous about the bed bugs due to what I had read here. But the price was right so I took a chance. When I got there I realized how great the location was and the room was just fine. I was also nervous about noise; there are tons of rooms in the hotel and mine overlooked a busy street. I usually ask for a room at the end of the hall to avoid noise, but I got a room in the middle of the hallway. I actually didn't hear my neighbors at all on any of my 3 nights - very pleasantly surprised. There was a "demonstration" on bed bugs outside the main hotel doors; a group was trying to warn guests that bed bugs are an issue there. I didn't have any problems with that, though. I will go back again.

title: “It wasn't terrible...I guess...”
text: In retrospect, I am disappointed with the Sheraton experience. I stayed for 5 nights at Sheraton Gateway LA. I will start off with my first impression, as you walk in, it might be broad daylight outside but they keep the lights so dark and dim it made me feel like I needed to whisper in case people were sleeping. The room was spacious, we had 2 queen size beds, a bathroom, tv with cable. The wifi is not free in the hotel room its like $12 per hour to connect to it unless you are in the lobby. they do offer internet access in their business centre though. There is a free shuttle from LAX airport to the hotel, if you arrive via Amtrak train or greyhound bus station check out flyaway or flyoway shuttles, its about $7 to the airport then take the free hotel shuttle from the airport to the hotel. All their staff were helpful and friendly and relatively knowledgeable. Breakfast is expensive, $21 for buffet breakfast but they do offer a la carte menu too around $9-$18. There is valet parking, but be careful if you get lost of need to ask a question about self parking, the valet came up to me and his attitude was to get out and give him my car or get out of the way because "you are blocking the shuttle" i was very upset by this on my first day, i had to somehow find my way around the area to get back to the hotel but when I mentioned it at the checkin counter the girl was understanding and she did ensure i was not charged for parking my car as their way of apologising for his behaviour. Valet parking is about $30 a night, call me stingy but i think thats a bit much. your alternative is to park at the self parking garages near by they charge about $12 a day, however, do be careful and some will not let you go in and out without having to repay at each exit and entry. The location to the airport is very good, however, if you want to explore the Los Angeles you either need a car or need to be prepared to walk and use public transport - which isnt all that fantastic but it IS cheap ($1) per ride. Bus station is about a 5min walk from the hotel. They do also offer tours to hollywood, disneyland etc, which I took advantage of, a tour company will arrive to pick you up from the hotel, they take you to their location where you pay for your tour, then drop you off at your hotel at the end of it. I think I had some sort of allergic reaction to something in the room because I was very itchy for a few days afterwards, maybe it was the type of cleaning products they used on the sheets im not sure though. The bed was not all that comfortable, perhaps it was just that bed, the feather pillows werent all that comfy either, however, I was told afterwards that you can request in advance to have the pillows changed to foam onces. Checkin staff were great helpful and good attitudes, valets are valets what can you say, concierge staff were pretty good, cleaning staff did a good job. they do have a small laundry facilities ($2.00 in quarters only) per load and per dry. they only have 1 washer and 1 dryer. No fridge in the room. There is one outdoor pool with an in ground hot tub outside and it was nice hanging out there. As for value for money, I would not stay there again myself but it wasnt bad. It just wasnt a great experience for me.

title: “It's all about the location!”
text: This hotel has got to be the perfect location! you can walk to absolutely everything from here. We were at Faneuil Hall in two minutes, all the main shops even quicker and the Fleet Centre is no more than a ten-fifteen minute walk. Excellent! However the walls were paper thin and the carpets had seen better days. Our room was tucked into a tiny corner and was small. Even for a city centre hotel. Other than that it was a pleasant enough place. Great breakfast from room service.

title: “Clean Friendly well priced”
text: When my sisters other plans for her vacation fell through we got a room here last minute. It was a great price friendly staff and clean. The bathroom was roomy fresh fruit and pastry the next morning. It's a decent place the wall are a bit thin so you could hear the kids next door most the night and the bed was not very comfortable but all in all not bad if I had another last minute need I'd check here first

title: “Perfection is how they make you feel”
text:
Perfection takes many forms, and for us perfection means exceeding expectations and making us feel special. Honestly, RARE! We went expecting a nice old 4-star that we were happy to win on Priceline for a reasonable rate. What we GOT made us feel like special guests at a loving relative's private estate. (or what we can only imagine, since (hah!) don't HAVE such a relative).
 That being said, if your idea of perfection is perfect walls, a giant bathroom and big elevator, than you're likely to be disappointed. This might have been one of the smallest bathrooms I've seen in a hotel, there were a few spots on the ceiling and wallpaper that wasn't perfect...the air conditioning unit is a wall one that can seem motel-like if that kinda thing is important to you. It is not what is important to us. This is a HISTORICAL hotel. You are experiencing history, elegance, a feeling of being taken care of that well surpasses a small spot on the ceiling that could use a little paint. (and the ac unit is controllable to your liking)
 Let's face it, most of the time when you stay in a 4-star you feel pretty nickel & dime'd to death. Parking, internet, room service...you feel like every time someone offers to do anything for you, no matter big or small, you better be prepared to tip. This place made me WANT to tip, without feeling obligated in any way shape or form. So much so that when we checked out, we brought an envelope of cash to the front desk and asked if they could please make sure that room service got our tips as we had received service three times during our two-night stay and never had the opportunity to tip. 
TIP: JOIN Omni's membership group online before you go!!!! It's FREE, and you will get FREE internet, plus FREE room service breakfast drinks. Seriously, have you EVER had that in a hotel before for free? No? Me neither. You even have your choice of HOW you want it delivered...in room, or knock on door, and you pick a time. We had tea (me) and coffee (husband) each morning, for FREE. And they offer add-ons if you want them that are way-reasonable in cost.
TIP: Enjoy a drink in the lounge...it is dark and comfy and the servers are EXCELLENT and friendly. They bring you munchies with your reasonably-priced drinks that include wasabi peas and nuts...I love that wine comes in 6-ounce and 9-ounce choices. Husband loved their special manhattan. You can just FEEL the history in this special place. We loved that you can get a bottle of sparkling water to share for just four bucks too.
TIP: Be sure to read the signs that are around about the history of the place...it's astounding and so interesting...I swear you can FEEL it there!
I leave you with one last thing that made our stay so special...when we checked in, I mentioned that it was my husband's birthday we were celebrating, and the cute sweet gal offered to send up a "cupcake". I said sure that would be great. What showed up was way MORE (again, see exceeding expectations) than a cupcake. I have posted a pic, but it was a great cake with oranges, petit fours, brittle and more. AWESOME. 
 Again, we were made to feel special, and that is what a hotel should be all about, and why I happily rate this 4-star hotel 5-stars in my book. Thank you Omni Shoreham for a GREAT stay!

title: “Love the Hyatt Place”
text: We stayed at the Hyatt Place in Columbus Ohio for nine nights in October 2011 and had a great stay. We were there for the All American Quarter Horse Congress. I wasn't sure about the location in relation to the show but found out after our arrival it is only a short, easy drive away. The hotel itself is comfortable like other Hyatt Places. The beds are outstanding and I really like the suite feeling of the room. The kitchenette area was nice with refrigerator. I also love the availability of a quick meal or a glass of wine in the lobby. These hotels are a great value for the money. I always choose Hyatt Place where available.

title: “Simply Excellent”
text:
The Acme is a great hotel in a great location. We stayed for 2 nights out of a 9 night trip to the US for a friend’s wedding and the Acme was by far the best hotel we stayed in.
The rooms are very well thought out; the decor is fresh and trendy, the room is spacious yet cosy and the in room facilities very much ahead of similarly priced hotels. We had other friends travelling with us and they chose to stay in a different hotel, their reaction upon arriving at our room before heading out for dinner confirmed we had struck gold.
On top of the hotel exceeding our expectations its location proved to be excellent for access to dining, nightlife and the Magnificent Mile.
Without a doubt if the Acme was a chain I would be looking for their sister hotels before any other chain when travelling to a new city. I highly recommend this hotel to all travellers.

title: “Stylish dog-friendly hotel in a great location”
text: Hotel Monaco provided us great service and recommendations on places to go in the area to experience San Francisco in a short amount of time. Their restaurant is colorful and trendy without being garish, and their location is perfect. I highly recommend Hotel Monaco, especially to vacationers passing through the area who expect the best.

title: “HIGHEST RECOMMENDATION!”
text: The Omni Berkshire Place is absolutely top notch! I have stayed in both the Benjamin and Le Parker Meridien in New York and much prefer the Omni. The location is excellent -- close to 5th Avenue shopping, Central Park, and subway service. The staff is absolutely great -- friendly, attentive, concerned about your well-being and comfort. The hotel lobby and lower floor are clean, well appointed, and well maintained. The room my daughter and I shared was great -- spacious, neat, newly remodeled -- just perfect for two women spending a few days in NYC. The beds are comfortable and the linens are great. Even the bath towels are oversized and soft. One of the greatest things about staying at the Omni is that you should be sure to sign up for their Select Guest program. It doesn't cost you a thing -- but the benefits are wonderful. When you are a member, you get free wireless internet service (a $14.95 value per day). Also, you are able to request a free beverage to be delivered to your door each morning -- and at a time you specify. This service was impeccable -- always delivered on time and beverages were hot each morning in insulated containers (both coffee and hot chocolate). We even got room service breakfast delivered a couple of mornings -- and it was less expensive than going to Starbucks. Additionally, if you are a member you are able to request a quiet room location, away from elevator if you wish, etc. -- as well as extra towels, blankets, pillows. It was all there waiting for us when we arrived. We had cocktails one evening in the downstairs bar -- very nice. You won't be disappointed if you stay at this very nice property!

title: “A welcoming boutique with so much flair!”
text:
This hotel is in a great location close to restaurants, shopping, and public transportation. The staff are very helpful and very hospitable. The rooms are basic but the decor makes up for it. The fresh oven baked cookies and wine hour put this hotel over the top of all others. 
The corner of Grant and Bush Avenue is a very easy place to hail taxis despite what the concierge may say. He kept pushing me to rent the hotel's town car which makes me suspect that he earns a commission for every booking. The concierge kept emphasizing that the town car is guaranteed to accept all credit cards whereas most taxis do not. However, when I tried to pay by credit card, the town car driver wanted me to pay in cash! Then he gave me a dodgy looking receipt that will most likely be questioned when I make my expense claims. For a more economical way to get around, the Montgomery BART station is only 3 blocks away. 
All in all, I will stay at this hotel again but I will not use the hotel's town car service.

title: “Great Location, Pricey Parking”
text: The Latham's main selling point is its excellent location in beautiful Georgetown. The bedroom and bathroom were small, but comfortable and tastefully decorated. There was no view, as the window faced the wall. I especially liked the breakfast vouchers at the Madeline Cafe, which was so much better than the usual hotel breakfasts one gets in America. This perk was mitigated by the ridiculously expensive parking, which is not included in the room rate. We managed to get a good deal on the room, so the stay was worth it, but I don't think it would be if we had paid full price.

title: “A beautiful historic hotel”
text:
I was pleasantly surprised with the New Yorker Hotel as I had read mixed reviews. Front desk staffs were great and very accommodating, and the Bell-Desk personnel were friendly. Overall, the group that greeted us made our arrival very pleasant and set the tone for great things that followed.
Although a lot of renovations and upgrades have been made, the hotel still has a historic feel to it, which makes it that much more welcoming. However, be prepared to spend time in "smaller-than-usual" hotel rooms.
The room cleanliness could certainly be better (I found an old plastic wine cup in our room, which looked like it was left there for years); however, the housekeeping was very responsive when we asked for extra attention.
If nothing else, the location of the hotel beats most other hotels: Conveniently located near a subway station, only a block away from Macy's and the shopping district, great restaurants around and a beautiful view of the city (we were on the 37th floor, with a fantastic view of the Chrysler and the Empire State Buildings).
I won't hesitate to recommend this hotel. I hope you'll enjoy your stay as much as we did.

title: “Nice place to stay- Especially for Northwestern Hospital”
text: I recently, unexpectedly needed a room near Northwestern Memorial Hospital. With no reservation, I went to the front desk in the evening and was helped by Nanaly (I think that is how it is spelled). She was very gracious and arranged a room for me at a great rate even though the hotel was very full. She was also able to extend my stay when I needed it. Even though it was a standard room, it was very large for downtown Chicago. Very quiet and perfect for what I needed. I was there for a family member in the hospital, so I didn't get to check out all of the amenities. The location can't be beat- just walk across the street to the hospital. The restaurant in the lobby was very good too- good food and fast service. I ate there several times. I would not hesitate to stay here again!

title: “Wonderful”
text: My husband and I stayed here the night before flying from the airport. The room was wonderful, the staff very courteous and they provide a free shuttle to the airport. The breakfast was well appointed. A computer is available in the lobby area for guests to use. We were able to get a room for $70 by calling the hotel direct and asking for the best price. This room was definitely a bargain and not what you would expect for this price.

title: “We ended up at the Clarendon for almost the same price!”
text: This was not at all what i was expecting from the rave reviews everyone has left for this place. Yes, i love saving money on a hotel room, but not at the risk of my health or safety. In the short distance from my car to the check in desk i was nearly accosted by homeless person and had to take cover as i heard gun shots that sounded like they were directed right at me. Finally made it to the front desk, whew...we're safe. So safe, our room or i guess all rooms face the Fire Department that is just across a small street. Just as we were getting in our room the sirens sound, just a nice reminder of how close we are to help if we need it, by the look of the place it was probable that we would. Not ten minutes later more sirens blaring out our room only it's 4 cop cars that are rushing down the street only to stop a few blocks down. We got a chance to get settled in, as in we sat in our bed instead of on our bed. How old was that bed?? I'm not sleeping here!!! We checked out our next choice was going to be the Clarendon Hotel just up the street, very, very competitive with the price of what we were paying at the Budget Lodge. We should of started out at the Clarendon, this place is beautiful. The rooms were amazing and so cold, a nice change from the stale hot room at the other place. The bed we were told after an amazing nights sleep were the same beds that are used in 5 star resorts, temur pedic. The pool was beautiful, the roof top deck was amazing and the view was stunning. The staff was so friendly and inviting and gave us some great tips on where the locals eat and what's new and exciting in the area. All in all we will be coming back to Phoenix next month and you can bet we will not be staying at the Budget Lodge.

title: “Great Hotel - Beautiful Lobby”
text:
This was a great hotel for my wife and I. We came to the city to get away and it created a great spot that was easy to access very comfortable.
The room was nice and well kept. The staff were all friendly. The parking was $57 a night.

title: “Great hotel - do not deal with Alexander at reception”
text:
Beautiful hotel, great grounds, excellent pools and service outstanding in all restaurants/pool. We stayed in one of the suites which was a decent sized room with great flow to the room. Our only issue was the noise of the road nearby however, by the second night, it was obsolete! 
At all times we encountered friendly, courteous staff with the exception of Alexander at front reception. He is not working in the right field. He was unfriendly, unhelpful and even lied to us a few times. When we requested a late checkout, he lied to us again (despite being Elite members) and when he walked away, we asked Brian who gladly accomodated our late check out. Truly, not acceptable for this standard of hotel, for elite members or for any clients paying the fees/rate of this hotel. 
Overall, great location, lots to do and definitely recommend for families with young kids.

title: “This place is a bargain”
text: We had a couple of days to spend in San Francisco after our Napa tour as part of our 35th wedding anniversary. I had stayed at several places in the city over the years, and always liked the Union Square location. We had a king suite here, and it was very comfortable and roomy. The staff are remarkably helpful, and the price is quite reasonable. This place sure beats the impersonality inherent in some of the larger hotels in the area...the other reviews highlight the advantages of staying here, and we agree with them wholeheartedly.

title: “What a perfect way to end the weekend”
text: I stayed at this hotel on a weekend when I was attending a concert in Boston. The staff was amazing. I had enrolled in the Omni Select Guest Program but wasn't sure I would be able to take advantage of the program since I had booked through Priceline; however, I was offered the opportunity to upgrade to a large deluxe room if I was willing to wait a few hours, which I gladly did. I did get a chance to see the smaller rooms and I would not recommend them as there is barely room for a bed and desk. The large deluxe rooms are wonderful and I had a great view. No interest access in rooms, only in the lobby. I personally don't like to use my computer where people can see my business. Also thought it was strange that hotel staff recommended a bar down the street for a drink when the hotel bar was open. Only other issue: as a Select Guest member you are entitled to two complimentary beverages and newspaper in the morning - I originally chose one time and then decided I wanted to check out earlier so called room service and asked if I could have an earlier delivery and they never showed up; however, Nicole at the front desk (thank you, Nicole!) went and got me a cup of coffee to go as I checked out. Would definitely stay here again.

title: “Wack , Completely Horrible”
text: the service was quite rude, the construction was annoying, the rooms were crummy, they only had one washer and dryer, the pool was freezing and the breakfast was just okay.

title: “A great hotel”
text: If you are expecting a typical American hotel, this is definitely not a good choice for you. We loved the European flair to the quaint hotel with a cozy atmosphere. Everyone from the owner/manager to the front desk was extremely kind and helpful. This hotel adds a touch of class to your stay in New York.The hotel and rooms were clean. A nice bathroom touch was being provided with toothbrushes and toothpaste. The continental breakfast was simple, well done and charming. The choices were unique and delicious.The subway is conveniently located a block away. We would highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Pleasantly surprised, given other reviewers ranking”
text: I read all of the reviews for hotels within our price range when we travel, and try to judge from the middle of the pack whether or not it is a good fit for us. The lower ranking made me a little leary, but the photo of the exterior looked nice, and the location and price were good, so we gave it a shot. We were pleasantly surprised at the cleanliness and decor of the room. Fairly new renovations have given the rooms a modern look with a few "luxury" touches. The bedding and window coverings were nice quality. As noted by others, the room is small but serves its purpose and the bath is not too small and has a glass vessel sink in the main room. The little extras provided were nice, (shower cap, toothbrush and comb) in addition to the regulars. Free wi-fi in the room, plus a computer in a walled "business center" in the lobby. There was an iron and board. The toilet seat is the kind with no lid, so there is no place to set toiletries and if you place anything on the tank, it could fall in! The breakfast had a decent variety, and though it appeared hot, it was actually cold, we did not ask for assistance with that, so nothing bad to say about the staff. They were helpful when we asked, and offered suggestions for a few of our questions. We felt like we were maybe 1 block outside of the REALLY safest part of downtown, but that may have just been perception, as the street is well lit, and we were impressed with the Police presence throughout the downtown area. It was an easy walk to the Inner Harbor, and water taxis or buses took us everywhere we wanted to go, we didn't have to take our car out of the lot they recommended, (no in and out parking). Baltimore was a bit of a risk for us as a vaca destination, and it was a pleasant surprise, which includes the hotel.

title: “We loved it and would certainly choose the same again”
text:
We spent our holiday in Chicago and picked this hotel based on price/reviews on trip advisor and alike. We were there for 9 nights.
The location is excellent, two minutes walk to the lakefront, same distance in opposite direction and you are on Michigan Ave. Bus stop around the corner on Michigan Ave, tourist office very close by.
Agree with earlier comments regarding the sleeping sofa - terrible. It may worth investing in new ones, as most of guests seem to use the additional sleeping place.
Unlike bedsheets and the rest of the room, the towels did not always seem that clean. 
Staff was very friendly and helpfull. Great view from the pool on 30th floor ! And wonderful sunrise over the lake from our room on 16th floor. .
Many people mention the convenience store accross the street - it is dark, dusty and outdated. Worth walking couple of blocks to Potash Brothers Market ( 875 N State Str) for a cleaner shop and a better sellection of food and beverages.
We took the train from the airport. Did not know that there was no elevator/ escalator at Jackson st when changing to red line. The walk from Chicago St. to the hotel is about 10 - 15 minutes,all this acceptable if your luggage is not heavy. 
Would be nice to receive a local Chicago newspaper instead of USA Today.
Alltogether we think it was a great choice and we will certainly choose the same when back in Chicago.

title: “Basic Courtyard; Easy Access to I-35”
text:
We stayed at this Marriott Courtyard over a college football weekend. The front desk staff was friendly and check-in was a cinch. Parking was plentiful and free. 
Our room was clean with a king-size bed and foldout couch that easily accommodated four people. The bathroom area was on the small side, but a door separated the sink from the toilet/shower, which made it easy for multiple people to get ready simultaneously.
From our room on the 7th floor we had an awesome view of downtown Austin, with the Frost and Capitol buildings and UT stadium lights in the distance. The sunset was especially nice. 
Getting to the hotel for the first time took a few attempts, since it's located off an access road where several highways come together. We could see the "Courtyard" sign easy enough, but it took a few "Texas turnarounds" before we arrived in the parking lot. Still, the hotel offers easy southbound access to I-35, and we were able to get back and forth from downtown Austin and the UT campus without issue. 
There is a restaurant/bar located next door to the hotel. We didn't go there, but it was hopping on Friday and Saturday nights. Would probably be a decent place to grab a drink before calling it a night. Also, there is a Target, McDonald's, Walgreen, etc. on the other side of the highway. 
Lots of UT fans were staying here for the game. You can probably find comparable accommodations in Austin, but this hotel offered the lowest rate on this particular weekend.

title: “Great Hotel!”
text: Want to go to Camden Yards? Need a hotel? Pick this one. This hotel is great. Rooms are nice and the lobby is excellent. Very convienent hotel if your going to Camden Yards. About a 5 minute walk to the inner harbor but if you know where your going it should be safe. Inner Harbor is beautiful and so is Camden Yards. Breakfast was excellent. Overall an A+ hotel. No complaints at all, will come back.

title: “Best wedding ever!”
text: I visited the Holiday Inn in uptown Charlotte for a family wedding. I must say it was the best wedding ever! The venue was outstanding and the staff bent over backwards to make sure we had everything we needed and were comfortable. My cousins wedding coordinator (Rachel) was very friendly, easy to work and professional. She made sure the wedding party was exactly were they needed to be at the right time so the bride could enjoy her day. We also loved the convenient location of the hotel, close enough to walk to everything! I can't wait to grab some girlfriends and make a return trip.

title: “Laura was great!”
text: We originally booked a room at the hotel across the street from the Marriott, but they did not have our reservation once we got there. So the competing hotel sent us to the Marriott, where we had the best experience! Laura helped us get the rooms we needed for the night, and she even got it paid for by the other hotel that lost our reservation. After a long, hot day of being on our motorcycles, it was wonderful to have some true southern hospitality, relax and be treated right! Thanks again, Laura!

title: “Best Holiday Ever!!!!!!!!!!!!”
text:
We arrived at the hotel on 8th of jan, a family of 5 and we stayed for a week. as we arrived at the hotel from our stretch limo the buzz of the streets totally shocked us. 
All we did all week was SHOP. it is the best place to shop ever specially in jan sales as everything is sooooo cheap!
i would definately stay here again if i ever visit NYC again. Best stay ever!!

title: “You can Dream if you get a quiet room”
text:
Almost a nightmare! The room we were presented with upon arrival was on the 7th floor, next to the elevator. Our king size bedded room was very small, but did wow us initially with the large screen tv on the wall and cool blue lighting. The bed itself was excellent. Unfortunately, it ended there. The tiled shower stall had no place for the soap and no towel bars to hang towels....so much for trying to save water. At 2 am, I was awakened by brief loud talking in the hallway (indication of poor soundproofing around the door) and then a door shut hard creating a loud noise. When I finally tried to rest again, the elevator shaft made irritating noise as did the air-conditioning blower. The temperature was set at 70 degees and could not be adjusted. Lastly at 8:14 am, the clock alarm, which had been preset, went off. Enough, I said...we're getting a different room.
I went down to the lobby, not expecting much to happen, but was pleasantly surprised that one room would be coming available. We went back upstairs, packed our belongings, and left them in the room as instructed. Later in the evening, indeed, when we checked in at the front desk, were given a new set of room keys and went upstairs (10th floor) to see what was awaiting our arrival. Two nicely made double beds, same large tv and cool blue lights. The bathroom did have a tub, so we had a place to put our bar of soap...just no towel bars. We had a great sleep in this room, except for the periodic air-conditioning blower switch. We slept in and did enjoy the second room. I would be hesitant to recommend this hotel at the present time as it is still being refurbished. And if someone does stay here, make sure you are away from the elevator!

title: “Terrible”
text: I have been to NYC many times and this is probably the worst place I have stayed. This includes the fact I have stayed with my poor college friends in the past. The lobby is dressed up but the furniture is nasty. RUDE RUDE STAFF. They don't put bottled water in your room or have a minibar. The courtyard marriott at least does that and thats half the price. I would equate the lobby to being in a bus station. THe restroom in central park was cleaner than the lobby restroom. THE ROOM IS STANK. Nasty stained carpet that stinks, mysterious stains on the nasty bed spread, hairs in the tub. The concierge doesn't know anything, suggested a "nice girls breakfast" at Ann Mollies, some sewage smelling bar around the corner. I would spend the extra 50 bucks a night for a nicer room. The only positive...and this is a stretch, is you don't want to be in the room so you busy yourself all day long so you can pass out and not think about what might be in the sheets. Sorry for the negativity but its very true. Yuck

title: “Very Nice!”
text: Our overall experience was very positive. Upon arrival our room was not ready, but we had a glass of champagne and enjoyed the lobby - lots of people watching and a great space. Reception was very pleasant. Room was well appointed and clean. We did not receive our turndown service 2 of our 3 nights, but a very small point. Great location for watching the July 4th fireworks! Also close to subway so easy to get anywhere in Boston.

title: “Exceeded Expectations”
text: The hotel staff was excellent. They are exceptionally pet-friendly. In fact, Sergio went out of his way to give our dog some special attention. And, took the time to show us a special pet "relief" grass area on the 9th floor patio. The hotel itself is very modern, clean, and "green." It's in an excellent location. For the level of service we received, the condition of the property, and pet-friendly policy, I would have expected to pay a LOT more. I would recommend this hotel/location to anyone! (A special thanks to Sergio, Darren, and all the friendly staff!!!).

title: “Great location”
text: The location is perfect, walking distance of walk of fame. Room and bath were nice, clean. The front desk is not so friendly, but i didn´t have any problem. Free wifi, refrigerator inside the room, ice machine and laundry in the first floor. Parking is U$10,00 a day, and you have to pay every morning for each day.

title: “Lovely hotel, warm staff”
text: By far, one of the best experiences I've had at a hotel. A small hotel (boutique), but our room was spacious. They offer twin beds instead of full in rooms with two beds but don't be fooled by that. The beds were just like full size beds and the room was tastefully decorated and very clean. The bathroom was lovely with marble tile floor and sink. Each staff person I came into contact with was genuinely warm and friendly (not in that overly customer service training fake way - genuine!). The front desk staff gave us great referrals to local restaurants, and the restaurant staff were the best! The breakfast scrambles are not to be missed. Elegant facilities. Super staff. Great stay. It's a five-block walk from the nearest Bart station, with two blocks uphill if you're coming from the airport. Wouldn't be easy to flag a cab, so consider that if you're taking Bart and dragging luggage. I got a great rate from a corporate training referral, so don't forget to ask about any special rates when you book. Definitely would stay there again.

title: “Great place to work and relax”
text: Stayed four nights on business. Ample room to set up a computer and printer. Separate bedroom and living room, so enough space to spread out. Staff was very friendly and helpful. Only issue was the cleaning staff. One day they did a very minimal job. One day they didn't show up until 7 p.m., at a time when I was working, and they entered the room without giving me any time to answer the door. Yes, I could have dead bolted the door, but I really didn't expect the cleaning staff to show up at that point. These two issues aside, I enjoyed the stay and look forward to returning.

title: “Close to capitol”
text:
Popular place, weddings were taking place while we were there. We were able to walk
to the capitol. We took a guided tour of the capitol and it was excellent.
 Parking if available and exspensive so we found parking on the street but
pretty far walking distance. 
 Coffee in room, which is very nice. We made use of the exercise room which is top of the line.
have eair buds and individual t.v. monitors for each piece of equipment. 
Pool and a great hot tub too!

title: “Perfect Location!”
text: The Warwick is an older and smaller hotel. The rooms are nicely decorated and a good size compared to other hotel rooms in San Francisco. The only drawback is that there is no air conditioning system, but not a problem as long as you dont go during a heatwave. Our toilet leaked a bit, but we figured out that all we needed to do was jiggle the handle. the weahter forecast was left on the bed each noght with some chocolates during the turndown service which I considered to be a nice touch. Staff was friendly and courteous, always eager to answer a question or engage in conversation if you had the time. Price was great. Walgreens accross the street was super convenient. We tried finding cheaper parking in the area, but other garages seemed a bit shady, especially when you can smell alcohol on the attendents breath. So we decided to go with the valet parking at the hotel for $35 a day with in and out priveledges. The location was amazing. We were able to walk to the beginning of the cable car line at powell and market st in just a few minutes (5 blocks). I recommend starting there, otherwise you might get passed up at other cable car stops because there is simply no room for you. There is also a subway at that same intersection. Buy a muni pass!. you can use almost every kind of transportation at leisure for unlimited rides. there are other tour busses that charge an arm and a leg to drop you off at all the tourist spots. with a muni pass, all you need is a map of the city to see what lines you need to catch. Super convenient for out trips to fishermans wharf and the ball park. We skipped the transportation for our trips to Yerba Buena Gardens, union square and chinatown. It was a nice stroll through the city. by the end of our trip my husband, 4 year old and I were all sad to leave. the location and price of this hotel really made out trip.

title: “Mediocre”
text:
Arrived the hotel prior to check in time, the friendly receptionist was kind enough to let us check in early. However the room we were allocated was on the 16th floor right next to the elevator. And it was a interconnectiong room with a non-sound proof door, so you can hear what channel TV next door was watching. We were too tired to complaint until much later the day, we realised that during the day the elevator seems okay but at night it made a weird loud noise consistently all night, it was impossible for anyone to sleep, so we called the reception, they seems aware the noise problem on the 16th floor, and immediately moved us to 4th floor, far away from the elevator which we really appreciated. 
The 2nd night we were there, the fire alarm went off in the midnight. It was not uncommon in a hotel, and most time it was false alarm, however the delayed announcement over the radio was quite confusing, and the reception line was unable to get through, so we were quite worried, so were a lot other people. 
The hotel lobby was very dark but I guess it was the theme they were going for.
And i think it must be an American thing, the room does not come with complimentary tea & coffee maker, so you cant make a cup of tea in the cold winter night. not the hotel prob, just FYI. 
Otherwise, the hotel was in a good location with lots restaurant near by, walking distance to union square and the market street.

title: “Beautiful Hotel, Outstanding Service”
text: This was our 5th stay at this hotel and it continues to be a star in the Hyatt chain. From the moment you approach the front desk, every employee exudes friendliness and a sincere desire to provide a high level of service. The hotel is architecturally beautiful and the rooms are nicely laid out and light. The beds are comfortable. We were on a AAA Breakfast rate and we were allowed to choose any entree off the menu or buffet plus coffee or juice. The Altitude Restaurant (actually on the ground level) served tasty breakfasts in an elegant atmosphere. I can't recommend this hotel highly enough. It's just always such a pleasure to come back here.

title: “A true gem...best kept secret in Houston!”
text: Great location in downtown Houston. The hotel is quite beautiful, beds are very comfortable. The rooftop terrace and pool area have a wonderful view of the city. Great place to relax! The staff were very accomodating. This is truly a gem of hotel.

title: “Great location, nice room, great staff”
text:
Our stay in the hotel Mela was great. The location was perfect, just off the busy Times Square but the hotel was relaxed and the staff were helpful (especially when we wanted to book a restaurant in Brooklyn). 
The rooms were small but clean and nice, and we were out and about all the time anyway so it was more than fine for us.

title: “Nice and Friendly”
text: I enjoyed my stay. The front desk staff was very nice as well as the service staff. I would stay here again if I had a trip planned to Houston.

title: “Great cheap place!”
text:
Wonderful place to stay in NY if you have a low budget. I booked one room at the hotel's site and I had no problems. Receptionists were very kind with us. All cards are accepted (even my Italian Postepay debit card).
The room was small but clean and quiet, with a big cloakroom. The bathroom was shared with another room, very nice and always clean.
When you arrive they give you vouchers for breakfast. You can have it just few stars below the hotel in a nice coffee shop called Nana's Treats. The owner was very kind and friendly with us (try his wonderful pastries).
The location is great, just few steps from the 5th Av and five minutes far from Union Square. Many subways stops near around.
Absolutely suggested!!!

title: “Fab location very comfy bed but watch the flies on the buffet”
text: A wonderful central location with plenty of helpful Staff (although the front desk is woefully undermanned) and a grand welcoming lobby. Annoyingly the rooms have no safe and there are not enough safety deposit boxes. The bed is as comfortable as all reviews say. Its a good job as there is building work going on at the hotel plus right outside my side of the hotel. Watch the buffet, one day whilst waiting for the cereals to be re stocked i noticed a small fly crawling across all the meat and then another crawling over the bread. It was 90 degrees which was unexpected in October but it made me feel very sick. As Boston is so accessible it is good to have such a perfectly positioned hotel. I managed to get out to everything from this hotel for 5 days.

title: “Nice place to stay in SF downtown”
text:
I stayed here for a night during Labor day weekend and paid about $200 incl. tax AAA rate.
The hotel is in a very good and nice location. Its right in union square neighborhood close to all trendy shopping centers and upscale restaurants. Cable car stop is right around the corner.
The first impression was very nice. The hotel felt upscale (lobby area is very tiny) and had nice & clean interior. The room wasn't very big but decent size and it didn't feel tiny or congested at all. The bathroom was very nice, very spacious and had all amenities needed. I was worried about the noise since it was in a busy street. To my surprise it was very quiet inside. The room smelled nice and the bed was very cozy and clean.
There are few downsides too but nothing big for the location.
There was a microfridge, safe, iron, and free WiFi but no microwave very (disappointing). The fridge was filled with stuffs like water, juices and so on, which would cost to use and there is not much space to put our things in. I was surprised to see that they still have old CRT TV and no LCD like most hotels in this price range do.
There is no complimentary breakfast or parking (which is common in SF hotels in this area). There is a parking garage (Stockton-Sutton) in about 0.3 miles, which is relatively cheaper and closer than other garages. It costed us about $6+$14 for overnight use with one in & out.
Since this is in a nice location in SF downtown, this hotel is worth the price otherwise it would not be because you don't get much for the money. There is no pool or gym.
There is an attached restaurant called Daffodil in the lobby. It looked very nice but the menu wasn't very interesting for lunch or dinner. The breakfast costs $21 for the items you would normally get it for free at Holiday Inns. We didn't go to the restaurant and it was mostly empty.
If you want clean, quiet and nice hotel with cozy bed & spacious bathroom for around $200 in a superb location right in the heart of SF downtown, this is it. Go for it you would not regret it.
I would stay here again and recommend this place.

title: “The price via Priceline was good for us!”
text: We purchased via Priceline.com as a "NAME YOUR PRICE", but overall we liked it, better than the cheap crap we ususlly stay at, close to the new LRT which we used to take us to downtown Seattle, (approx. 40 MINS, $5 return) safe, convenient. Room was clean, big, had a flat screen in it, but we ended up at a ajoining room in which the door to the other room was paper thin, so we could hear them. It was worth the price we paid, except you have to pay for parking when you stay that close to airport. ($10 per night)

title: “Staying here is a must!!”
text:
We stayed (as part of our honeymoon) in this wonderful hotel which is perfectly located about 30 seconds from Time Square (to the left) and 6th Avenue (to the right). From start to finish all of the staff (especially Patrick Donnelly) were welcoming, helpful and accommodating. The hotel itself is modern, contemporary (call it what you will) but the height of black and white gothic New York cool.
There are numerous eateries, deli's and bars for breakfast, lunch and dinner if you want to venture outside although given its sensational location the hotel was perfectly quiet; and this alongside the super comfortable bed and pillows and an awesome power shower made for a relaxing time when inside the hotel/ the room.
As for all tourist trap sites (which we loved) such as Rockerfellar Centre, Central Park, Fifth Avenue, Grand Central Station, Empire state (and Magnolia Bakery!) etc all were within reasonable walking distance.
In summary, this hotel was perfect for us in terms of style, location and everything else and we cannot recommend highly enough that you stay here!

title: “Good stay at Mount Vernon Hotel, would recommend”
text:
We visited Baltimore for our son's graduation and wanted a different place to stay than our typical haunts way outside of town along the highway. We've made at least 15 visits in the last four years so have plenty of hotels to compare. Because our visit fell on the same weekend as the Preakness, we knew things were going to fill up fast. Seeing the positive reviews here, I decided to book Mount Vernon Hotel because of location, price and because it included Wi-Fi and breakfast. Most of that turned out to be true. 
The hotel is very beautiful, the rooms clean and the staff exceedingly helpful. But due to their being completely booked, we had some issues. This hotel used to be a YMCA and the rooms are not uniform, so I should have thought to ask for a room with a window--I've never thought of not having one and how claustrophobic it would feel. 
So, Night #1 in the first room: low ceiling, no window, no closet (not even a coat hook for our dress clothes) no working WiFi, broken coffee pot and a telephone that kept inexplicably buzzing (as if the phone was off the hook) until we pulled its plug. The lamps, etc. were sort of second-hand shop. We also paid for the hotel parking lot that night, but pulled our car into the garage to find that they have about 15 spaces for the entire hotel, and they were all taken. We had to pay for another lot across the street. The desk clerk took the charge off the room. (We aren't complainers, we just didn't want to pay for parking that didn't exist.)
In the morning, I asked if we could be moved to another room if one became available because my husband was really claustrophobic. Since it was now Sunday night, they did have enough checkouts and we could move. They had us call later in the day and had new room keys for us when we returned to the hotel that night. Night #2 was a completely different situation. The new room had a closet, very nice furnishings, a window (!) and the WiFi signal was strong. The coffee pot even worked! 
The breakfast was great both mornings, with an actual cafeteria with hot food including french toast, eggs, bacon/sausage and hash browns. Staff was very very nice at every interaction. There is so much to do within walking distance that I would like to stay there again when we have more free time.
So, make sure you ask for a room with a window! Even looking at a brick wall and a glimmer of sunlight made a big difference. You won't find a better bargain.

title: “Sleek and modern”
text: Oasis in a chaotic, busy area. Nice rooms and nice lounge area to return to after being out in the city. Lots to see and do within walking distance of the hotel. Higher floors offer nice views of the city, especially at night. Staff is professional and friendly.

title: “Our second visit - not as good as the first.”
text:
We stayed at the Doubletree in December 2009 and loved the experience. Our second visit was not quite as impressive.
CONS:
Broken desk chair couldn't be adjusted and stayed in the lowest position.
$20 per day internet fee! We thought this was really high and when using wireless it was very slow. We switched to wired and it was faster. But $20 is the absolute highest charge we have ever had - anywhere.
No vending machines! If you want pop after 11 pm when the gift shop is closed, you have to venture outside and find a store. So, be prepared!
There was no price list for the tray of snacks anywhere in the room. Be aware - if you so much as pick up a snack to LOOK at it, you will be charged. 
On our second day, housekeeping did not replenish the coffee or cups.
The room has newer style bedding (no comforter) but everything is looking a bit worn, especially the carpet and the window seat fabric.
PROS:
The location! A fabulous location!
Ample outlets! We had no problem charging our iPods and phones.
The shower head, water temp and volume of water was FABULOUS! This was the best shower we have had in a hotel in a long time!
The window seat was convenient, especially since there is only one chair (the broken desk chair) in the room.
Free internet in the lobby.
The hotel was VERY busy when we were there and I think that can have a negative effect.

title: “Good location bad heating in cold weather”
text:
The hotel is located in a great neighborhood, right next to Central Park and near great eating and cultural life on the Upper West Side. Rooms are on the smaller side but decent and well appointed based on the cost relative to most hotels in Manhattan.
As mentioned by other reviewer, heater was broken/not working in our room on a very cold night. I asked front desk to send someone to fix, which they said they'd do, then didn't. On second request, I got a cockamamie story about the hotel system only turning on heat when outside temperature drops below 45. Not sure I believe a hotel would allow internal temperatures to drop to 46 before giving us heat. Didn't appreciate being lied to, if indeed the hotel was just trying to save money by cutting back on heat. We had to double-up on blankets, so that was our solution.
I can't say this is a bad hotel or a bad deal especially given the hotel's other good features -- great location, clean and safe, a classic old pre-war hotel near Central Park, etc. Just be aware it's not perfect, and if very cold outside, be prepared.

title: “Good airport hotel”
text: Older facility but very comfortable. Good room, excellent work area, usual amenities, but needs a safe. Wifi needs some work - outside carrier, inconsistent, may be good on desk, not on bed, but okay in bathroom! Concierge lounge small but comfortable. Restaurant good for breakfast.

title: “Great lodging - verify parking...”
text: I had the same experience as another review. We were flying out early in the morning, so we made plans to arrive the night before & leave the car parked for 5 days. I specifically asked about motel parking and was told it was free for 7 days and then there was a fee after (I spoke with someone on 2 seperate occasions). Since we were only going to be gone 5 days - I thought we were set. Upon arrival, I was greated by a very friendly gal who gave me the paperwork for my car and "reminded" me of my parking fee. I explained all of this to her and she told me I should never have been told parking was free for a week - there was a $5/day charge. I told her I was not sure I would be staying there - there are too many places locally you can stay & park free that I wanted to go to the car and talk it over with my husband and I would her know what we decided. When I went back in, she told me that they would NOT charge me for my parking if I would stay - so we did. She was super friendly and handled the situation very well. The room was very nice, clean, and the bed was comfortable. We had the New York lady shuttle driver to and from the airport - she is fabulous! This is a great place to stay, very convenient to restaurants and the airport....just make sure you understand about parking fees. I was pleased with how my situation was handled but also know what I need to expect for the next time.

title: “Happy New Year 2009”
text: Being a New York Native and probably moving from the area for the last time in my life, I wanted my New Orleans wife to celebrate New Years Times Square style. Well the NYPD ruined that with extra tight security and limited room in Times Square so we celebrated the ball drop in Central Park with the fireworks. It was very cold that night, very cold -4 or something so we stayed outside 45 minutes only. Back to the hotel it was wonderful, elegent great service, excellent rooms, food, lobby, doorman. One time coming back the doorman said , "Welcome back home" I like that! The little extras make the money worth it. the view from my room was of St. Patricks catheral, I cried as I opened the drapes. The location of 50th and Madison is great and central to everything, Saks, Rockefeller center,shopping, Times Square everything. The hotel had a very Europen flair as did most of the other guests, I felt as I was in Europe without taking a flight. Stay there if you can, its worth the money. Stay on the club floor as the breakfast is free and very nice.

title: “A downtown delight”
text:
My first trip to the Omni Parker House was absolutely delightful. Although they were quite full and busy at the time, the staff was courteous and very helpful. My room was on the small side and did not have a view of the city, but I didn't mind - most of my time was spent outside of room exploring the wonderful shops that were within walking distance from the hotel. The hotel is situated in the middle of all the action - close to the T, close to great shopping, and close to Faneuil Hall: what more could you ask for?
Stepping into the Omni Parker House, I felt like I had somehow traveled back in time. It's elegance and class are otherworldly. 
I unfortunately did not have the opportunity to try the famous Parker House rolls, but the continental breakfast was exceptional - particularly the smoked salmon. 
I'm looking forward to my next trip!

title: “Love It!”
text: The hotel is conveniently located at the lower Manhattan, surrounded by a few Metro stations, so getting around in the NYC is very easy. Neighborhood is nice and safe, quiet at night, lots of descent restaurants around. The room was small, but normal using the NYC standard. However, the room was clean and beatifully furnished, so we felt very comfortable in there. The staff was friendly. They also have underground parking right across the street from the hotel so it was easy to move our luggages.

title: “Nice Hotel Close to Times Square, Subway Line”
text: My wife and I vacationed for a week in NYC. We stayed 7 nights at the Distrikt Hotel. Our flight arrived in the morning and they were able to accommodate us with an early check-in. The staff was very friendly, greeting us as we came and left the building. The room was very stylish and clean; there was plenty of room for 2. There is a subway entrance on the same block as the hotel, and it is about a 5-10 minute walk to Times Square (depending on how crowded the streets/sidewalks are), so the location was great.

title: “Top Notch!”
text: I, along with my husband and 2 college-age sons, stayed at the Hilton Garden Inn-Times Square for 3 nights in early January, 2012. It was perfect in every way, beginning with a welcoming warm smile from the bell captain. Our rooms were not ready by check-in time (not due to housekeeping but to the guests who were still hanging out in the rooms) so we were given 2 other rooms that were actually in a better location in the hotel. The front desk was well-staffed, the concierge was very knowledgeable, housekeeping was efficient, our room was immaculately clean when we arrived and throughout our stay, internet service dependable and FREE, the breakfast buffet was delicious, elevators lightning-fast, our every need attended to with haste. The location is convenient, especially to theatres, and is just far enough from Times Sq. that you don't get the noise but can get there in a matter of 5 mins. There are several nice restaurants nearby, both pricey and affordable choices. We actually had a better experience at this hotel than at a 5-Star hotel we stayed in during a trip to D.C.! We will make this our hotel choice when visiting NYC and plan to recommend it to others as often as we can.

title: “Most shocking experience ever”
text: This Motel cannot be recommended to anyone! Seriously! If you enjoy drunk junkies/gang members pounding on your door at 3am telling to let you into your room than you are at the right lace. Okay this service isn't for free, and after such an experience you pay for 2 nights even if you only slept there for one. Apart from that there were blood stains on the bed, a tough woman at the front desk which is stabbern and arrogant. In addition the phone didn't work even when dialing 911. Again this cannot be recommended.

title: “A wonderful stay!”
text: My two sons and I took the train from OKC and the hotel was within walking distance from the station. It was also a short distance from the hotel to Sundance Square, the Sid Richardson Museum (free), and several great restaurants. We booked a terrace room because we wanted to be sure to be on a higher floor, and we loved it. From our 16th floor patio we could see all of downtown Ft. Worth and beyond. We brought in dinner from the Chili's across the street, and ate it at our table on the terrace. The room itself was very clean and well-appointed, but was pretty cosy when we had the rollaway brought in. If you want lots of room, get a suite. We were shown one, but decided to sacrifice the space for the terrace. The staff was very friendly and professional, and the little desk clerk who checked us in , Shaunte, was especially accommodating. The kids loved having Internet access, a plus, and the only minus I can think of is no on-site restaurant (therefore no room service), although there is a little cafe connected to it that serves breakfast and sandwiches.

title: “a dump with bad service”
text: I stayed at this hotel once and, in my opinion, it was a dump. But I did not review it here because I was too busy at the time. But now I feel compelled to do so. A business colleague checked in for a two night stay. At check in, the hotel told her she needed to move after the first night to a different room, so she should pack up and move to a different room in the morning. She was not told this at the time she made her two night reservation. When she asked the hotel why she was not told about the move at the time the reservation was made, the hotel's agent just shrugged his shoulders and made a sort of grunting noise. Really bad service to inconvenience a guest like that. And as I said, the hotel is a dump anyway. There are LOTS of better options in the area.

title: “Just keeps getting better”
text: Our 3rd stay at the property was complete with 9+ hour power outage that adversely effected much of SoCal, but the staff was prepared and gracious with their provisions & hospitality. Outstanding location, Location, LOCATION... As a youngster growing up at kennel on Pacific Coast Highway in Malibu I'd gaze over the wall at the ocean; as a guest at PTH (from Santa Fe, New Mexico) I gaze from the balcony, inhale deeply, and feel young again... Phil

title: “Fantastic hotel with unparrelled service!”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Fitzparick during a recent weekend trip to the city. Our experience was fantastic! The service was great and the hotel impeccable. Chris, Chris and Leo were helpful, polite and very accommodating. We could not have asked for more. The room was clean, quite and huge! The hotel's location allowed us the ability to walk everywhere we were interested in going (Time Square area and Central Park). We will stay there again. This was by far one of the best overall hotel experiences we have ever had!!

title: “no 5th star because of bar staff”
text:
We were staying two nights at this Hilton and had a pleasant stay. Good location in Boston with many nice bars and restaurants around the corner. There is a great shopping mall which can easily be accessed via the sheraton on the other side of the street. There are all kind of stores with a big Microsoft store which opened August 23rd this year. The hotel includes a Starbucks, a business center where there are 5 computers with internet access and printers. The concierge and the people at the reception are very friendly and helpful. Breaktfast buffet is good and more than adequate.Room was fine and clean; as you expect from a Hilton room.
We were two times at the bar: first evening the bartender was very friendly and efficient. Next evening the lady at the bar gave us the feeling that she didnt care too much about her guests. So we just had one beer this evening and went to bed. Sorry, but this ruins the whole impression.
Just forgot: many of the sight seeing tours have a stop to get on and off just across the street.
Conclusion: I can recommend this place, but for spending the evening you'd better look outside.

title: “Perfect location!”
text: We were able to stay in Seattle for 2 nights and really enjoyed the city. Hampton Inn was only a few short blocks from the Space Needle and less than 2 miles from Pike's Market. We were able to walk to every attraction we planned to see. The suite was very nice and had a large kitchen and separate bedroom. We could even see the Space Needle from our balcony. The cookies and breakfast were very tasty. Everything was very clean and comfortable. The only amenity we wished they had was a pool/hot tub...but we wouldn't have had much time to enjoy them anyhow. I used my hilton honor points to stay and thought it was a great value for the amount of points used.

title: “Good location, not much else”
text:
I've stayed here many times over the past 6 years on business trips to NASA. The view from the rooms can be great if you get one overlooking the lake, but most of the rooms are musty smelling, have old, tired looking decor, and broken fittings. Stay clear of the restaurant, the food is pretty bad. 
The rates are usually quite low, so its not a bad deal, just don't expect it to be up to the standard of most Hiltons.

title: “Palomar SF-Wonderful”
text: Stayed here on our Honeymoon. Found a great deal for this Hotel stay on travelzoo. Excellent location in SF. Staff were fantastic. Wine in the evening, ice cream in the afternoon. A little Goldfish waiting for you when you get to your room. The staff were so kind to us. Sent us a bottle of Pink Champange and chocolate covered stawberries and upgraded our room to the huge jacuzzi tub..Very comforatble beds. This hotel was great. No street noise or from other rooms. Excellent stay. Highly recommend this location and hotel

title: “Outstanding boutique hotel in NYC”
text: For the price this is probably one of the best boutique hotels in NYC. Location is pretty good and a short walk away from the Disney land of time square. The lobby is undergoing some renovations so you have to check in at the penthouse. The room was relatively spacious and had a modern feel. I was extremely pleased with the amenities (bath room and bath products, robe, in room safe, free internet, breakfast, penthouse access). More importantly - I had some of the best sleep ever here - the bed and pillows were so comfortable. The hotel was quiet and service was professional. This place is very very clean. Housekeeping and management do great work. I will almost certainly come back and stay at Morgans.

title: “Spacious Rooms!”
text:
I enjoyed my short but pleasant stay at the Warwick. I stayed just a single night, but spent quite a bit of time in my room doing work and recovering from a long flight prior to a meeting the next day. My room was spacious! A queen bed, large work desk, walk-in closet, luxurious bathroom, and the bonus -- a balcony! Everything was clean and comfortable, and the option to open the balcony door, sit outside, and have fresh air was a treat. I had a nice lunch at the hotel's restaurant, and the front desk welcomed me warmly. This hotel is a bit of a hike (~15 min. walk) from the main 16th St. shopping district. But frankly, that area is a bit rough around the edges, and I appreciated having some distance from the "main drag" and a more residential feel at The Warwick. In fact, the hotel was formerly an apartment building, which explains the large rooms.
I have just three complaints regarding service: 1) I arrived a bit before check-in and was told that my room wasn't ready, so I went to the hotel restaurant for lunch. However, after I did check in, the desk gave me a very nice coupon for the hotel restaurant which, since I didn't have time to dine there again, would have been very nice if the clerk had given it to me while I dined there to wait for my room! 2) I was a bit late after my meeting to get back to the hotel for my airport shuttle. Although I had told the doorman when I left that I would be expecting the shuttle, he didn't communicate this to the shuttle driver and as I arrived the driver had started pulling away! My taxi stopped him, but it was a close call. The doorman is supposed to pay attention to these details! 3) Because I was so rushed to retrieve my bag from the front desk for my shuttle, and likely also due to the altitude adjustment, I was extremely thirsty. When I asked the clerk whether she had a small bottle of water or even a cup of tap water that I could have, she referred me to the restaurant bar -- which I did not have time for! Surely the reception desk at a hotel as nice as The Warwick can keep a stock of water for guests who request it -- especially given the change in altitude and dehydration that many visitors experience when arriving in Denver from other regions.

title: “Disgusting”
text: How does this hotel get away with saying that it is three and a half stars? I've stayed in nicer two star motels. Everything is old and filthy. I was given a smoking room (my guess is because I paid through Hotwire). I asked if they had anything else but was told no, so I figured it wouldn't be too bad. Wrong. I could barely breathe. The room smelled worse than a Vegas Casino. I don't even think a smoker would stay in that room. I kept the window open all night (that's right, the window actually opened).
