It was so overwhelming and disgusting. The carpets and walls were dirty, the television picture was blurry and there was dirt in the sink and shower. I wouldn't even pay Hotwire's low rate to stay there again.

title: “Great experience. Definetely will come back!”
text:
This hotel is a great choice for its location, cleanness and price. It's not the cheapest place to stay, but it really worth the money you pay.
The staff is friendly, the rooms have great size and you can't beat the location... Attention ladies, Macy's is just across the street... not to mention all the other great stores...
From now on, this is the hotel I would stay in NYC and recommend for all friends and family.

title: “Another Great Weekend at the Gansevoort!”
text:
This past Saturday I had the pleasure of obtaining a Manhattan suite for a little mini-vacation to break up the tedium of the winter. My daughter and her two friends, all in their early 20s, wanted a night out in the city and always prefer the Gansevoort as they really love dancing at the rooftop bar! Of course, we also love staying there because the service is excellent and the room service is good also! While we usually book a deluxe room with a small balcony, we had received an upgrade to a Manhattan Suite thanks to a manager who was most accommodating--Ms. Jennifer Wheeler. Upon check-in were were greated by John, one of the friendliest valets you would ever want to meet. Since we arrived quite early, approximately 11:00 a.m., the room was not yet ready but was in the process of being cleaned and upon return from breakfast, it was ready. The girls were impressed with the suite which has a living room, an extra half bath, a bedroom, and a full bath with a separate tub and steam shower. They were also impressed by the complimentary bottle of wine and the chocolates. The 13th street location is great and the girls had a good time visiting a few of the local clubs as well as the rooftop bar before retiring to the extremely comfortable bedding in the suite. 
Unlike some who have been in rooms that were said to be noisy, there was no noise at all inside the suite. However, depending on what floor you may be on, it is possible that you could get hear some of the music from the downstairs lobby bar or the rooftop pool although this has never been an issue for us as one of the main reasons we like the Gansevoort so much is because of the nightlife you can enjoy right on the premises. Typically the lines to the rooftop bar can stretch a good way down the block but if you are a guest you can take the elevator right on up and can get in without any problem.
Once again my thanks to the staff for providing the ladies with such an excellent weekend! We have already booked a room in March as my daughter plans to celebrate her 22nd birthday there. At this point, I can't think of any hotel that she would take over the Gansevoort and she has been lucky enough to experience a good many in the city. Thank you, Gansevoort staff, and we'll see you in March!

title: “Loved the Regency Club, and the building”
text:
We recently spent 5 nights at the Hyatt Regency San Francisco and would recommend this hotel to anyone wanting to stay in the city centre and use public transport.
We arrived by Amtrak, on their shuttle bus from Emeryville which dropped us at the Ferry Building. We headed over the road, luggage in tow, but had difficulty finding the entrance to the hotel. There are several doors visible on the Ferry Building side of the hotel but they are all 'exit only'. We had to walk right around to the other side of the hotel, to the entrance on Drumm Street.
But after this not so good start, we were greeted well at reception. I had requested some degree of water view (despite having only been able to book a city view) but the room pre-allocated was apparently at the city end of the hotel. However, the gentleman checking us in very kindly moved us to a room with a view of the water. Our room was a Regency Club King on the 17th floor, with an angled view of the Bay Bridge. The room was a decent size (although an odd, angled shape), well appointed and comfortable, fairly newly renovated I would guess, but some things seemed to have been designed for design's sake and didn't quite work from a practical point of view. There wasn't much storage space – much of the floor space in closet was taken up with the safe and left very little space for storing luggage. The enclosed part of the bathroom had the toilet and a large walk-in shower, but there was nowhere to hang towels except over the shower enclosure door. The TV set into the bathroom mirror is an interesting gimmick, but really just a novelty. The toiletries provided were 'white ginger' or some such, which I didn't find at all pleasant – the smell reminded me of public toilets, which isn't a particularly attractive perfume! I missed the lavender-citrus products Hyatt used to provide.
I did find the chaise longue comfortable, and my husband appreciated the large flat screen TV which could be angled to wherever you wanted to sit. And I greatly enjoyed the view, being able to watch ships in the bay and the historic streetcars running along Market Street and around onto the Embarcadero.
The Regency Club was excellent and we made more use of it than we'd thought we would. We were surprised, however, to find that it closes at 9pm. We had been given a card at check-in to show the times when, variously, breakfast, snacks, drinks and dessert are available. But when it said dessert 8pm-9pm, we didn't realise the Club would then close at 9pm. Breakfast had a good selection of fruit, a couple of different danish or muffins each day, cereals, and bread and bagels to toast. The snacks during the day were just apples/oranges and cookies, plus 2 or 3 kinds of trail mix or mixed nuts. In the evening there was a different hot item, eg chicken wings. Then dessert was 2 different kinds of cake, which varied, plus small chocolate brownies. There were coffee machines and a juice machine (orange, apple and cranberry, I think) always available, and fridge stocked with cans of soda and bottles of water), to help yourself any time the club was open. 
I'm not sure that the honor bar system works – my husband enjoyed a beer most evenings and duly completed the slip to say what he'd had and put it in the box. But although we often saw other people taking alcoholic drinks or with drinks at their tables, we never saw anyone else complete an honor bar slip. We thought the honor bar prices were pretty good, certainly cheaper than the mini-bar in the room.
There were 2 PCs available which we found useful, although often other guests ignored the signs asking people to limit their use to 30 minutes to allow others access.
At the desk there was always a form where they asked people to sign into the Club, but very few people seemed to do this. Access to the Club was not well controlled. There was never a member of staff at the desk, only those who were replenishing the food at times when it was available. Although supposedly you can only access it from certain elevators, with an authorised room key, several times we saw people who had found their way up there and were having a look around, and from their conversation they did not appear to be RC guests. Only once did I hear a member of staff challenge a group as they entered and ask them to leave. Another time someone asked a member of staff how much the food and drink cost, and when it turned out they were not RC guests, their group was asked to leave.
The hotel is very handy for public transport, which is excellent in this city. There's a BART station right outside the hotel, on Market Street, as is the terminus of the California Street cable car. Stops for the streetcars and trolleys are also very close. The nearest place to buy a multi-day MUNI passport is over in the Ferry Building. As others have reported, the parking charge at the hotel is daylight robbery! $57.00 per day, including tax. However, we did know about this when we booked. Aside from the cost, we found having to use the valet parking inconvenient and a little restrictive.
We enjoyed looking at the architecture of the hotel, inside and out. It is certainly an interesting building. And if you've seen the movie 'Towering Inferno', the elevators may look very familiar – except they're actually inside, not outside as in the movie. We found all the staff to be friendly and helpful (well, except for the lady at the Budget car rental desk who was singularly unhelpful, but she was not a hotel employee).
We are glad we chose to stay at the Hyatt, we liked the location and we particularly enjoyed the Regency Club. However, when we visit San Francisco again I think we'll stay a little further out where we don't have to pay for parking and can have immediate access to our car.

title: “Great Hotel - very hip”
text: Stayed with a friend and was a really cool hotel. Favorite part was the Acura SUV that drove us around when we requested for it ahead of time. Service was good and the hotel seemed new. My only complaint, which isnt bad at all, the showers are frosted and not completely blocked off so it's a little strange when staying with a buddy, but overall 5 stars, will stay again

title: “Great Hotel”
text: Stayed here Jan 11th to Jan 14th 08, fantastic place to stay, only 10min walk from Times Square. Recommend room 1821, it was a huge corner room overlooking the Empire State building. Had it not been for the abrubt reception staff and a unhelpful concierge this would have been 5 star.

title: “We were scared, WE WERE WRONG. It was just what we needed!!!”
text: We read the reviews, we re-read the reviews, we said "no way" it could be that bad. The staff was polite, attentive, and accomodating. The room was worth the price, the parking was excellent, the access to everywhere we needed to go was easy. The nieghborhood was older, but we never felt unsafe. I'm not sure what the bad ratings stem from, but our experience was "just what we needed!!!" Thanks.

title: “No Parking”
text: Maybe I should have known better as I have been in SF before, but shouldn't the hotel info sites indicate if there is any parking available?? Me and my rental car cirlced round and round to get anywhere NEAR the Marina Inn and avoid 2hr limit zones. I would suggest a good place to park for the next traveler but I never found one, finally the parking gods had sympathy for me 5 blocks up on Lombard St.

title: “Great location”
text:
We stayed at the Holiday Inn during the Oscars in 2004 and I have to say the staff there are extremely helpful. They helped us book numerous taxis/tours and nothing was too much trouble. Even the bartender was very friendly! The little restaurant is nothing special-food is ok, but as it is a budget hotel we didnt expect anything posh!
The rooms were of adequate size and just like the standard Holiday Inns we get here. They are very clean and the beds are very comfy which is the main thing! We were facing the main road and we did hear a bit of traffic but this didnt keep us awake.
The location is unbeatable. Just round the corner from Hollywood Boulevard and the Walk of Fame with all the major attractions (about 5 mins). All in all, this hotel felt safe and comfortable and the staff were courteous and well presented. Not bad for a budget hotel!

title: “Nice Hotel but Check Your Credit Card”
text: Hip, comfortable hotel with friendly, well-trained staff. Rooms are small but well-appointed. Free wireless was nice, but there was no desk to work at, so my laptop truly had to be a laptop. A little hard for the business traveler. The roof bar, reserved for guests and their guests, was a great place to hang out. Location is great for Soho, Tribeca, downtown shopping, eating, and hanging out. The only thing that marred my stay was a $54 charge to my credit card I received a week later in the mail for a "minibar" charge. Since I did not use the minibar at all, I called the reception and the staff person removed the charge (supposedly - I'm waiting for confirmation that my credit card was credited). She did not apologize or say that it may have been their mistake, leaving me with the feeling that she thought I was being dishonest. It's too bad because a simple apology for the misunderstanding would have given them a loyal guest who travels to NYC often. The whole thing leaves me with a bad feeling about the hotel, which is disappointing since the stay itself was quite nice. Check your credit card after you stay there!!

title: “Traditional Rooms are small”
text:
I booked via hotwire.com, did not where I was going to end up and was very pleased to see that I was given the Omni. I paid $108 plus tax incredible value. When I arrived I asked the desk clerk to put me in a NON-hotwire room, he said “the traditional rooms are all the same”. If this is true I would have been very disappointed if I had paid the going rate of $260 for a double bed, small bathroom which has no room for your toiletries. I must warn in my opinion the traditional room is suitable for only one person.
 When traveling, I am a stickler for a clean quite room with a comfortable bed. The Omni met and exceeded my requirements, the staff was friendly and courteous. 
The hotel is located in an excellent location for business and leisure. The Omni is easy walking distance to the waterfront, Faneuil Market, North End, Financial District & Boston Common.

title: “Spectacular view”
text: We visit NYC a couple of times per year and like to try hotels in varied parts of the city. We were very pleased with our recent 2 night stay at the Eventi. We reserved 2 rooms: one for myself and my husband, and one for my grown son and a friend. The front desk staff was delightful, and we were upgraded to rooms on the 22nd floor (there are 23 floors). Each room was smallish (typical of NYC hotels), but the floor to ceiling windows framed a spectacular view of the city (with the Empire State Building just to the northeast), which opened up the space beautifully. The beds are remarkably comfy! Our bathrooms were generously proportioned, and I loved the large walk in shower with the rain shower heads in the ceiling. We found a nice selection of salad/soup/sandwich restaurants in the area when we needed a quick bite, and Starbucks was just up the street (always a plus). A quick taxi ride or a 15 block walk gets you into the theatre district. We go to the theatre but avoid staying in the Times Square area, so this location was perfect for us. I recommend the Eventi without hesitation.

title: “Your the Best”
text: From the smiling face of Debbie when you check in, Then to relax in evening with a complimentary drink, made by Mark.(Fruity-Drink,no rum please) Wake up in the morning to have Breakfast made by Lassandra, just like home. This is the best hotel Choice in Indianapolis, IN.

title: “Rough start but overall pretty good”
text:
I stayed here over the November 11th weekend as part of a package deal for the Nascar event. Upon arrival my taxi cab driver was having problems putting through my c/c and the valet service were a little rude because of the delay and I seemed to be the one they were giving the gears to. Sorry for not driving up in a Rolls. 
Checking in was smooth and quick, the staff were courteous and helpful throughout my stay.
My room was fine, nothing special but very clean and no complaints. We had breakfast in the dining room twice and breakfasts were okay, some in our group weren't too excited about the steak dinners one evening. The lounge was nice but a bit on the expensive side at least for me. If you aren't too concerned about where your having a drink in a fancy setting, go to O'Connor's Pub across the street. Very inexpensive beers and cocktails.
Never had a chance to use the pool, probably if not for the rude valet I would have rated a little higher.

title: “Well situated on Upper West Side”
text: A convenient moderately priced hotel close to restaurants, shopping, subway and Lincoln Center. Rooms are clean and functional. Service efficient and professional. No frills, but all of the essentials necessary.

title: “Parker meridien, great service, good value and pool in nyc”
text: My wife and I took a gaggle (9 total) of teenage girls to celebrate our daughter's thirteenth birthday. Other friends had recommended the parker meridien. I felt that the serviece was very attentive and the junior suites were of a good size. The problems that occured to others are there and should be noted that they may or may not bother one depending on circumstance. We reserved by phone and were upgraded on arrival by asking. We were in the off season with no large groups. The physical plant is wearing, but hte rooms were redone and nice, but no privacy in the suites. All large hotels have bad, cheap rooms especially in this day and age of large groups and hotwire. Don't expect perfection when a large hotel has 200 passenger groups, or your rate is 50 percent off the rack rate. Every business knows its business better than the customer. In a forty story hotel, cheap rooms will be on very low floors. In NYC that means noise. I stayed at other luxury hotels in NYC. If you want excellent service and amenities you will always pay for it. The parker meridien has its pluses- great pool, location, the suites are nice for a family.

title: “Showing its age and dirty in the corners”
text:
To start off I would be back thanks to its Price and location. 
The only major issue I had was with the overall cleanliness of the hotel. The coners and edges of the hotel room was fill with dirt. Our light switches in the room were dirty due to much use and the elevator carpet looks like it has not been cleaned In very long time.
The overall ambiance of the hotel is little older but fine. Make sure to get breakfast included in your initial hotel package.

title: “Restaurant at Hotel Indigo”
text: We visited the restaurant, 1909 Bar & Bistro at Hotel Indigo at the Alamo and loved it! Our server, Mike Marotta, couldn't have been more attentive, and the order was spot on. Mike was professional, but friendly. He knew the menu easily and gave great recommendations. If you stay at Hotel Indigo, visit the restaurant and make sure you ask for Mike!

title: “Great Hotel, better location”
text: My wife and I have stayed there several times and have never had a bad experience. When we stayed in early 2010, I noticed that the property was starting to get a little worn, but saw none of that when we stayed there last week. Great staff, hotel, value and a killer location on the Mag Mile.

title: “We enjoyed our stay there”
text:
We spent 3 nights at this hotel and we enjoyed our stay there (although I must say that I had been pretty concerned because of the bad postings in this forum). Our room was on the 12th floor and we had a beautiful view on the Public Garden. The room was definitely not as big as ones home but had a cosy atmosphere. The carpet looked used but the room (bedroom and bathroom) was clean. There was a TV, a hairdryer, 2 phones, an iron and an ironing board, a desk, several pieces of furniture to store one’s clothes, and 2 chairs. On the 12th floor near the 6 elevators was an ice machine and a snack vending machine. 
The staff was friendly and quickly responded to our demands. 
The location of this hotel is great: only one block away from the ‘T’ (but you won’t need to use the subway if you don’t like because you can reach pretty much everything on foot in no time).
If we ever stayed in Boston again we would definitely go and stay in this hotel again.

title: “Almost booked”
text: Was going to book as I saw the website and was faciniated by it. Saw a lower rate but when I called in to request for a Sunday stay I was put on hold for 5 min. Let the agent know that I saw a lower rate and after having me on hold said to just book it on line. I understand why as it was an advance pay. But she should've got on line and explained it to me. Didn't ask why I was coming or have you ever stayed here before. Very poor reservationist, not welcoming at all.

title: “Awesome”
text: Great view of Downtown San Diego. The kids and I arrived just in time to see fireworks in the distant sky. Clean, quiet and spacious rooms with separate bedroom, bathroom, and lounging/ business areas. Two TVs so the kids and I could watch our own shows. The staff was extremely helpful and courteous- answered all questions and requests with a smile. Overall Great Experience!

title: “Northwest hospitality with cultural diversity”
text: Traveling for a job interview is stressful enough. Add a a three week year old infant and you hope that the least of your concerns is the accommodations. The staff at Watertown made the stay perfect for the conditions. Most notable was the staff. From reservation to packing the car, the staff's friendliness and willingness to serve rivaled the customer service of hotels 4 times the price. Kudos to hiring managers who assembled a great team. Though located in a densely populated urban setting, the room was spacious and offered a great view. Further, underground guest parking limited the exposure to Seattle rain. Overall, a wonderful stay.

title: “The room says it all”
text: We stayed for one night and it was fantastic. With a location like that just give me the room and get out of the way. It is definitely not a lux area but sleeping over the water was pretty cool. Room are nice and clean.

title: “Verrrrryy Basic”
text:
I can't honestly say this hotel was even CLOSE to being worth the money. However it wasn't a terrible experience. 
Cons: Super simple, TINY rooms, no free internet (just wifi not wireless?)
Pros: Good location, friendly staff, right next to the subway
Basically, if this is the cheapest place, and you're not fussy when it comes to luxury as far as hotels go, OR if you just need a (small but clean) place to sleep- this is going to work for you

title: “Adequate...and that's about it.”
text:
Got this hotel randomly through a Priceline search...usually this lands you at generic business hotels, which is what I wanted, but in this case, a "European Style" small hotel, like a pension. Carved out of an old apt building, lots of small rooms down winding halls. Mine opened to an underground walkway. The room was TINY -- I mean, like, Japan small, with a twin bed (!), no way 2 people could share the room. But, mattress was comfortable, AC worked well, and the room was quiet (not that you'd be able to hear much over the noisy AC).
Everything was old and kind of worn, but clean and worked. Almost no storage whatsoever, no iron in the room (& no room to iron anyway). Bad cable. Bad lighting. Very stingy with towels, and one morning, I was grossed out to discover my towel was already wet before I had used it. Free wireless internet was good. Front desk staff very nice. Lobby cat very cute. I didn't make it to the breakfast.
Location is very good, on 16th at T Street, ~10 min walk from U Street metro (Green/Yellow) or 15 from Dupont Circle (Red). Close to the best restaurant / bar areas in DC.

title: “Location”
text: I have spent two nights in this hotel for my business trip to New York. The location of the hotel was very good which is a cross the street from Central Park. The room size was very good however the bathroom was small. One thing worth mentioning about the bedroom, which I didn’t find in any other hotel, is the lights’ motion sensor which turns the lights on as soon as you step on the room’s floor. The breakfast buffet was good however it had limited choices.

title: “Great Hotel Great Location”
text:
Have just got back from 5 nights at the Belvedere. Having read that some staff in NY can be unhelpful and sometimes rude, there is none of this at this hotel. Staff were always polite and helpful. The room was fine with a king bed, smallish bathroom but ingenius curved shower curtain rail, little kitchenette for a coffee, or keeping drinks cool. We had a room on the front on the 17th floor. It wasn't too noisy - it is NY. Go up the Empire State - you can still hear the noise on the 86th floor!
Elevators not a problem for us and we were on the 17th floor. There are two main elevators which hold 8 to 10 people (without luggage) but in the morning when everyone is heading out they can fill up. They still stop at floors requested where the people waiting cannot get in. Their lift 'call' is then cancelled and they must start again. It's the same with any hotel. This aint a 4000 room Vegas hotel with express elevators.
Location good for subway and close to Times Sq and Broadway. We walked from the subway at 50th with a single case on wheels direct to the hotel in about 5 minutes.
Only problem was checking in when our room wasn't ready (it was 2pm and check in is 4pm) but they said another room was available. Upon getting to the room it was a twin queen 'deluxe' not the 'king' we had booked. When I went to reception I was told that was what was available and when I mentioned I had booked (online) a king the receptionist said that is only a request. However they said we could have a king the next morning which we did without problem. My point here is that the 'king' is more expensive than the 'deluxe' but was told it's only a request!! 
This is why I gave 4/5 rather than 5/5.

title: “Clean, Inexpensive Accomodations”
text: This was our first experience with Candlewood Suites. The washer/dryer Cupboard area was a welcome ammenity for us after a four day road trip. I am sorry to hear a previous tripster had a very bad experience, but we had quite the opposite. We washed/dryed clothes without incident and I was quite amazed at the whole "honor system" setup in the Cupboard area. Our room was spacious, clean with full kitchen setup. Restaurant leftovers went into the fridge and we made full use of the coffee pot and microwave appliances. A real bargin for the money!

title: “Best Customer Service”
text: While an older facility, it has been spruced up nicely. The room was clean and spacious; the welcome amenities were appreciate; the lobby bar was friendly; but it was the above-and-beyond attitude from the front desk made all the difference.

title: “Very pleasantly surprised”
text: My husband, our daughter, and I stayed at TownPlace Suites Indianapolis Keystone the evening before we were to move her into her dorm room at Butler University. The front desk staff were very helpful and accommodating; and inquired sympathetically about how the college move went. We were also very pleased with the Keystone area, and the many dining options, casual and upscale, nearby. We definitely plan to stay at this Marriott property again when we visit our daughter.

title: “Good hotel for the value”
text:
I travel to San Jose for work and the Four Points has everything I need. Some rooms are smaller than others but I generally don't spend much time in the room while in town. 
The highlights are the comfortable beds, many restaurants within walking distance and nice TVs (remotes are a little sketchy). The downsides to the hotel are a slow elevator (only four floors tall though) and the internet is very slow which makes it hard to accomplish much late night.
All in all it meets my needs and I can usually get a room for $200 or less and get my Starwood points out of it.

title: “A good night's stay”
text:
The Resident Inn Charlotte Uptown offers both convenience and comfort. The hotel is located adjacent from the football stadium and within walking distance of the Time Warner Cable Arena, home of the Charlotte Bobcats. There is a parking garage which costs $10 per night for guests.
The staff was very friendly and helpful. They can get somewhat overwhelmed if there is a rush of people checking in. I had a room on one of the upper floors with a view of the parking garage, so unfortunately didn't see the cityscape. 
The room was nicely appointed and the bed was very comfortable. The living area is separate from the bedroom offering plenty of space to spread out and for privacy if needed. What I thought was one of the best touches was the option for the hotel staff to get groceries for you at no additional cost. They only charge the cost of the groceries themselves to your room.
The breakfast buffet was very good. There was a good selection of both hot and cold foods. The seating area is large enough, but can be crowded early on and might have to deal with couples reading papers who are oblivious of those around them.
I would definitely recommend the hotel if you are in Charlotte.

title: “Awesome, worth every penny. Highly recommend the Hotel Beacon”
text:
I booked this hotel through www.booking.com.; and read reviews from others at TripAdvisor which cinched the selection for me. 
The front desk staff were warm and friendly and allowed me to check-in immediately, even though it was several hours before the stated check-in time. The concierges were helpful in steering me to the subway station and which trains to take to get me to my destinations. The subway is only a block and a half away.
The room was impeccable, large, recently renovated and decorated in soothing colors and comfortable furnishings, especially the bed. It felt like home with all its amenities. I was really fortunate to be given a king suite rather than the standard king room I reserved. Perhaps because of the high floor the room was very quiet and the views of the city were awesome. 
It is an eco-friendly hotel which resonates with my choices for the planet. My only regret was that it was a one night stay. 
Perhaps the only thing they could add would be bathrobes.

title: “Terrible Customer Service”
text:
I had a reservation, made directly with Embassy Suites, for a two-double-bed non-smoking room for my family of four. When we arrived at 10pm with our tired young chilren, the check-in man said, "Here's the deal" and I knew it was not going to be good news. 
He informed me that they had overbooked the hotel. He said he only had two rooms left, a one-king-bed smoking room or a one-king-bed conference room. With four of us, those rooms were of absolutely no use. Why did I bother to make a reservation if it meant nothing? Showing basically no sympathy for the situation they put us in, the man offered no assistance...no apology...no suggestions...no attempt to find us a room at another hotel. What do we do at 10pm after a long day traveling with two tired young children and now with no place to stay? Fuming, we put them back in the car and drove five hours home, completely exhausted.
Needless to say, we will not be making any more "reservations" with Embassy Suites. How can you trust that they'll have a room for you when you arrive?

title: “Not impressed with the Century Plaza”
text: I stayed here for 4 nights, before moving to the world class Beverly Hills Hotel. This hotel is very bland, the lobby does not have much character and kind of reminded me of walking into a large office building, just very plain and lackluster, not at all like it was years ago. I stayed in room #631, which had some issues. Two of the three telephones in the room did not work, one of the lamps in back of the chair was missing a light bulb, the balcony was FILTHY, stains on the balcony carpet, cigarette butts left in the corner from the previous guests. The entire 6th floor had a musty smell to it as well, they should invest in some air freshener. As far as the staff, the most outstanding was the valet, he was very friendly and kind, went out of his way for the guests. Housekeeping was bad, they left trash in the room, knocked on the door at 7:45am even with my do not disturb sign out. I got a decent internet rate of $209 per night, plus tax, which was not great but not bad considering this hotel is close to Beverly Hills. Also, the pool can have potential if the poolside attendents actually do their job and bring guests drinks, all they were doing was standing around talking, not waiting on the guests....I think this hotel ran better under Westin management.

title: “Very impressed would stay again!”
text: Rooms are simple but comfortable, who cares if it's a bit dated it's excellent value for money. Very close to down town, Space Needle and loads of great restaurants! Breakfast is good and the staff are exceptional and very helpful. Free wireless internet in room, newspaper, parking etc etc it's very good value will definitely stay here again if in Seattle.

title: “Nice Hotel!”
text: Superb location next to the Empire State building. Finding a good and cheap hotel in Manhattan is not easy, finding a hotel that is also well located... hard. This one is cheap, very good, and steps away from the train station. The rooms are great and clean, the breakfast is very good and the staff is great too.

title: “Excellent property”
text:
What an excellent property. As a fellow Marriott employee, I had such wonderful conversations with the employees...and the funny part; they didn't know I also worked for the company until I mentioned it. The room was excellent appointed and the harbor view was amazing! The staff has been one of the most attentive and the AYS department deserves a pat of the back!
Great job, we'll see you again!

title: “disgusting”
text:
Having just arrived back home from the carter hotel i have never experienced a hotel with staff as rude as they were and rooms so dirty.we never saw a maid during our 5 day visit and never had clean towels throughout our stay.it was disgusting.we had a bath and sink full of rust and we stayed out on the streets of manhattan for as long as we could so we wouldn't have too long in the room till the next day we were straight out again by 7am,it made us cringe staying in that filth.
We will be returning back to New york in the future but we will NOT be staying in that dump. I would not recommend that hotel to anyone,it isn't fit to be a hotel and needs to be condemned.we re-named it as the hostel!

title: “Just Right For Our Needs”
text:
We chose this hotel for its location and ability to accommodate a family of two seniors, four adults, and one child. It's rather close to the airport and not that long of a drive to our attraction destinations, San Diego Zoo, LegoLand, and Safari Park. The seven of us were split up into two rooms that had two double sized beds, one for the women and the other for the men. Sleeping on the sofa bed wasn't bad at all.
There was a placard in the room informing you of the free cooked to order breakfast and approximate wait time during the breakfast service time so that you would have to plan your breakfast time accordingly to avoid the long lines. When went downstairs for breakfast, the stations were labeled and there was a greeter who can answer your questions. I just don't know why other reviews criticized the long lines and lack of signage of the different stations for hot and cold breakfast items.
We didn't have to wait long to get our van from the valet. We would time it just right in requesting right after breakfast. Because we would have an early start for our destination, we might have missed the long line.
All of the key cards for our room would have take several attempts before the door lock would turn green. The next day I told the front desk and they re-keyed our cards and had someone check the door lock. I didn't think that there was anything wrong with our cards. Upon on return to our room, we had the same thing. We just had to be patient in getting the door unlocked. At least it's not like a password that can potentially lock you out after three failed attempts!

title: “This hotel is terribly overrated!”
text: The standard room is too small. When you open the door, it will hit the bed. There is no airconditioning in the room; the room is too warm. The view from the window is a brick wall. The bellboys are rude. The parking is too expensive: 57 dollars per night. Do not go to this hotel; it is terribly overrated!

title: “Amazing resort”
text: From the moment we arrived to the moment we left this place was excellent in every category. We arrived on a Friday afternoon check-in was quick and we were hoping to catch a ballgame after a quick conversation with the concierge, he had got us 2 tickets for the game as quick as a flash. The room was lovely and had agreat outlook to a stream with ducks that you woke up to on a morning which was nice. The pillows in the room were the best I have ever slept on in a hotel. The landscaping of the resort was beautiful and there were always staff gardening tidying up reparing putting greens and generally keepinhg the place tidy. The heated pool was lovely and fairly quiet as well. The barefoot grill was a good setting with bar type food that was nice. And at night the mood changed again with beautiful lighting that accentuated the resort and gave it an entirely differnt look again. The only negative I would have if you could call it that was that it was a little far from downtown and if you were catching a cab in each night it could soon add up.

title: “Wow what a great experience!”
text:
I just stayed at Travaasa Austin and have to say that it was the best getaway I could have asked for.
The food was creative and delicious and the wait staff was remarkable.
I was surprised to find out about all of the included activities and tried to fit in as many as possible. I completed the rope challenge course which was a huge feat for me since I do not care for heights; it was a huge accomplishment for me and made me feel like I could accomplish anything.
You have to try the equine experience; it was great learning about how to work with horses and understanding how to communicate with them. Norris and Betsey were great teachers.
I had the "On the Road Again" massage, I discovered that I like Willie Nelson's music and the hemp oil used for the massage helped work out all of the aches and pains. Alex was great.
All of the staff on property was knowledgeable and friendly. I will definitely be coming back.

title: “Over priced and dated”
text:
We stayed at the Crowne Plaza for one night prior to a flight home in the morning. Having seen Crowne Plaza hotels in London (which are very high quality) this was very disapppointing.
For a start it took as a while to actually find the entrance to the hotel. There seems to be no clear entrance to the lobby....the door is very small and is next to a large entrance to the convention centre which seems to be part of the hotel. The lobby is OK and the staff seemed friendly upon arrival.
However, once you entre the lunge area you see that the hotel needs updating. The lifts are small, dirty and look almost industrial. The corridors look grubby. The room I initially was put into looked nice enough and the bed was comfy. The air conditioning unti was not on....it was a very very old unit by the window and once turned on took ages to even start cooling the room down.
On my bed I had a small pouch containing ear plugs, a sleep CD and some sleep spray....and I later discovered why. When i went to bed I turned the air conditioning unit off because it was so so noisy. I then discovered that the road noise was even louder! Upon closer inspection it turned out that the inner pane of the double glazing was missing, and the noise from the highway directly outside was so loud I couldnt sleep. 
I called down to reception who, to give them their due, were very helpful and arranged for a security guard to come up with a key to another room...which was much better. Although obviously moving rooms in the middle of the night when I had a morning flight was not the best situation!
Another point to note is the condition of the pool 'area'. There is a sign directing you to the 'pool, sauna and hot tub'. It seemed that the sauna no longer existed and has been boarded up for some reason - yet the staff still seemed to think it was there as I asked them! I am a keen swimmer, but the pool did not look very clean or inviting - it had a green murky colour to it. And the hot tub looked like it needed a good clean, with dark brown mouldy marks on the bottom.
On the plus side there is a computer in the main lounge area which offers free internet access (I thiink the business centre is not yet open), and the rooms with functioning double glazing are perfectly comfortable, if rather dated. 
The charges for this hotel are way overpriced.......we were luckily able to get a large reduction upon check out because of the problems we had. My advise is to stay elsewhere though!

title: “Still a Ritz fan......”
text:
I begin by saying there is no doubt this is a wonderful Four Seasons and my stay there in no way diminished our vacation experience. 
However, in that we like to stay at different places in the city from time to time we chose this over either of the Ritz properties in NYCity so as to try something different. 
We booked a two bedroom suite and much attention was given to our arrival before the trip by a member of the staff. However, litte of what we discussed with her regarding requests was prepared upon check in. I requested a rollaway in the LR for my 20 year old daughter be made up and in place upon our arrival. It was not. I had asked that it be made up just like the beds in the rooms....it never was. SHE asked the ages of our children so she could have age appropriate welcome gifts. We told her they were "children" in their 20's but Beanie Babies were still given. In more than one email correspondence my husband told her we were travelling with our son and dauhghter in law but we were given one BR with a king and one BR with two twins. They claimed they were under the impression that we had three small children in tow. And of course they were fully booked and this was all they had available. 
Each morning our room service order was just a little bit off. One pot of coffee instead of the two that were ordered, missing orders of eggs, just little things but still irritating considering what we were spending. 
As to the quality and appearance of the room....nothing to shout about. Mini Butler in the LR had a broken door. Decor was as it was advertised and presented but nothing to jump and down about...bland, boring. Master BR was very roomy. Attached double was quite small. LR was just average. Furniture not very comfy. 
Concierge was very attentive when we did use him. Door staff was excellent. Location was the best of any of the properties i've stayed at in NY. 
But all in all, it was just an above average visit. I am happy that we tried it. But I still prefer the Ritz Cartlton

title: “Relaxing vacation, excellent property and service”
text: This is our second time staying at this hotel the week after Christmas, each time has exceeded our expectations. Both times we have reserved the tower southwest high floor corner suite (aka VIP Suite)which has beautiful ocean, pool and marina views. The location is on Mission Bay close to sandy beaches, La Jolla, Old Town, Sea World and many other San Diego attractions. Excellent service, attention to detail and cleanliness.

title: “Loved the beacon”
text: Stayed at this hotel in June. Fab location with loads of shops in the vicinity - Gap, Banana republic, Filenes, Children's Place, Sephora, Also cinema is within walking distance; subway 2 minute walk away and Beacon theatre next door. Can't fault the place other than lifts under repair and they were very slow while we were there. Probably repaired now! Would definitely stay there again as area is clean and feels safe.

title: “FIRST ROOM REEKED OF INDIAN FOOD!”
text: My boyfriend and I stayed there solely for its location to a festival that was near by. That was the only benefit of this hotel and that it had a table in the room, but i think all do these days? We arrived early and there was not any rooms available to check in early, they did hold our luggage for us. When we returned we were given the key to 104, immediately when we walked into the room there was an extreme odor of Indian food. After sitting in the room for a few minutes and getting headaches we decided to complain. Luckily they font desk was able to place us in a room on the other side of the hotel. Our new room 108 only smelt like musty old clothes. The hotel was old and wasn't in the best shape but I have to admit I never saw any bugs. Another thing that bothered me is that on their website they still advertise that they have grab and go breakfast, that is untrue, they provide nothing. The parking that they charge you $15 for is a block and a half away. Lastly, the bath and body products they provide had a bad smell and the shampoo was really runny. For how expensive the place is it is not worth the money, Next year I will be paying a little more for some quality.

title: “Great Stay and Great Location”
text: Took the Family here in June and really enjoyed our stay. Prices are a bit steep but we knew this going in and prepared months ahead of time. Stayed here for the location and service. Located a few blocks from Columbus Circle and right across the street from Central Park. Subway access is very convenient and purchased passes for the week. Found the staff here very helpful and got a room upgrade once we checked in. Can't say enough about the Concierge Service at this Hotel. If we had a question about anything the Concierge Desk was there to help. They helped us with what Subway Train to catch for the Yankee's Game we attended and helped with Restaurant selections. Can't say enough about the Essex House - Would stay here again if in NYC

title: “Wonderful Old World Hotel--BY FAR THE BEST IN DC”
text:
Stayed here over the Fourth of July with my family. This hotel is like the luxury hotels that I remember when I was very young. Everything is extremely professional. The staff all know the guest names--nothing is overlooked. I travel a lot on business and pleasure and its a rarity to encounter service of this quality in the United States. Other than the Ritz Carlton in San Francisco (my favorite city hotel in the US), nothing else comes to mind. 
Another attribute that struck me was how good the food was. I know the Obamas love good food and chose this as their hotel while awaiting their White House move. This is some of the best hotel food I have had (again the Ritz Carlton San Francisco comes to mind). All ingredients are fresh and local and expertly prepared by the chef. We stayed for the Fourth of July and the hotel hosted an enormous party with entertainment for children--again really excellent food and so much of it. 
The location also simply coudn't be better for a visit to DC. Its right across the street from the White House--need one say more?
The property is beautiful and historic. The hotel is the product of merging two old DC homes (MR. Hayes house was merged with Mr. Adam's house). It is maintained perfectly and is kept meticulously clean. However, keep in mind that it is old, so the rooms while beautiful are NOT sound proof. Little sounds do travel here (as they do in old historic houses). If you are a very sensitive sleeper, this hotel may not be the best choice. However, by opting to go elsewhere, you will miss a wonderful, historic, oldworld experience.
I have traveled to DC a lot in the past few years and stayed at a lot of its hotels (3 of the Ritz Carltons, the Fairmont, The Mandarin Oriental, The Mayfair, The Willard, etc). This is by my favorite hotel in DC. It carries my highest recomendation.

title: “Good hotel”
text:
We stayed at hotel Belleclaire hotel, New York, from 02/02/09 - 08/02/09. 
The hotel has the perfect location, on 77th street right near the 1,2,3 subway (on 79th, 1 minute walk). 
Upon arrival we were greeted by the doorman and entered the nice clean lobby. Obviously newly decorated. The hotel is simple in that it just has the lobby and then the rooms upstairs, but to be honest thats all you need in NY. At check in we were given a free upgrade to a king size room!! I was still expecting it to be small, but was pleasently suprised! Huge king size bed, spacious room with desk, flat screen TV, fridge, seperate walk in closet and big en-suite with bath. The bathroom had fresh clean fluffy towels everyday and was well cleaned. 
the room was cleaned thoroughly everyday and at night chocolates were left on our pillow, along with a card showing the next days temperature! nice touch. 
There is a 24 hour diner across the road, which has everything food wise, and you can also get a delivery to our room. (We didn't avail of this). 
All in all Id recommend this hotel, as it is quite reasonably priced (~€70 - 80 per night) in the middle of Manhattan and a stroll to Cental park.

title: “Some Good but a lot bad”
text:
I travel a lot so here is an unbiased review:
We went to Indy for a night with our 3 year old, Saturday the 24th visiting the childrens museum, Colts game on Sunday the 25th of November.
We arrived and were greeted by very friendly valet, check in was smooth, $30 to valet is a bit much. The hotel is in a bit of a war zone it seems, a lot of construction, chain linked fenced area across the street but a hop, skip and a jump from Lucas oil stadium. 
We stayed in the Louis Armstrong train car #004, the rooms are small, very narrow and long but we expected that. After the museum we went back to the room, went out for dinner and came back to swim. 
- The pool is freezing, not so much the water which I would say was around 78 degrees, but the pool itself is about 200 - 250 feet from the entrance and right in the middle of the first floor. So the air was cold, there is no separate room for the pool, the air is freezing but my son was excited to swim. 
- The rim of the pool is filthy, people were writing their names in the black oil on the tiles. 
- The pool towels were the size of a washcloth. COME ON GUYS, SPEND SOME MONEY ON REAL POOL TOWELS!!!
On to the room itself
- The room itself was a cool idea but it is old
- The chairs had arms that were falling off and were old and dirty.
- The bathroom was small, also, the fan did not work. If you are going to have a small bathroom, at least make sure there is a working exhaust fan
- The linens were terrible quality, the towels were scratchy and India made garbage
- The bed sheets were like sleeping on construction paper, anytime you move the sound would wake you up because the sheets were stiff and made with what appeared to be no natural fibers.
- The only thing you really touch in a room is the linens, these were imported garbage.
- The beds are SMALL, full size, my wife and I slept on one bed and it was incredibly small and we are not big people
- This is a train station, the advertisement says you can hear the subtle rumble of actual trains as they pass through the station, IT LITERALLY SOUNDED LIKE AN EARTHQUAKE!!! I thought the building was collapsing, so did my wife.
All and all, we will never stay at the Crowne Plaza again, the people were friendly but the accommodations were sub par at best and that is being nice

title: “Great location”
text: We enjoyed our stay at the Belvedere. The location was great - one and a half blocks to Times Square area and many theatres. Hell's Kitchen area was 1/2 block the other way which offered any type of restaurant that you could think of. The neighbourhood was safe and traffic was quiet at night. Our only complaint was the double bed that was tough to share. Rooms were good size and offered microwave, coffee maker and fridge.

title: “Problems at the Bulfinch”
text: I hesitate to write a poor review based upon 1 bad experience. However, I believe the problem that I experienced speaks volumes about the management of the Bulfinch. I stayed there one night. My initial greeting and the appearance of my room was good. However, the problem began at approximately midnight when a hotel neighbor began knocking on a nearby hotel room door and calling for someone to let the neighbor into the room. I don't want to go into too much detail about the neighbor, but suffice it to say, the knocking and yelling created disturbing noise for a full 2 hours, until about 2am. Being a frequent traveler for business, I realize that some amount of noise from hotel neighbors comes with the territory. And, I do realize that a hotel does not have control over the problems that may occur with its guests. However, the hotel has absolute control over how they handle such a situation, and the Bulfinch fails on many levels. Problem #1: the hotel lost the master key. Problem #2: the hotel let a guest know that they lost the master key. Problem #3: the hotel allowed guests to be disturbed during prime sleeping hours for a full 2 hours (approx midnight to 2am). There is absolutely no excuse for this lack of management control. As an aside, another guest on my floor had placed a room service tray outside the door (which I noticed sometime around 9pm) and this tray still sat at the door by 8:30am the next day. By itself this might seem picky, but again, I think it is indicative of a bigger problem with management. Had management responded timely and properly to the extraordinary circumstance of one of its obviously distressed guests (my hotel neighbor), I would have been writing a very different opinion. I did wait a week to write this so I could settle down and have some perspective. Hopefully, the Bulfinch will learn from this experience and hone its management skills so as not to put any future guests through what we had to endure.

title: “Modern hotel with great views!”
text:
Stayed here during our honeymoon and it was a good modern hotel right in the middle of the city centre. 
The rooms are nicely decorated and very well equipped (with an iPod/iPhone speaker dock) and we loved the view of the Bay Bridge (although it was through a narrow gab between two other office buildings).
Loved the breakfast as well - not the usual breakfast buffet but rather well made breakfast dishes such as pancake or a generous fry-up. Will stay here again the next time we are in SF!

title: “Great location”
text: Close to great dowtown attractions and nightlife. Very peaceful place to stay. Make sure you call ahead and ask about all the additional fees and taxes. There is plenty to do for all ages at this hotel.

title: “NYD with the Madisons”
text: Awesome location, beyond comfortable rooms, hospitality amazing, very affordable !!!! Most of the staff was informed and helpful, they went the extra mile to assure ourcomfort and safety. Absolutely the BEST of the BEST !!!!

title: “Nice Hilton”
text:
The Hilton in the University area of Charlotte is a nice, modern hotel that is close to shopping, businesses and I-85. 
The lobby is modern and the check-in process easy with a friendly associate.
The room was nice, clean and comfortable. The bathroom is small but we were there for one evening, so no big deal.
As a Hilton Honors Diamond member, we got free buffet breakfast in the restaurant but that was not that good. Service was good but some of the food was just below par. I would not have wanted to pay for it.
Overall, a very nice hotel in the Hilton family.

title: “Great location”
text: First trip to Texas and spent three nights at Townplace Suites and loved it. Great location, literally 100 yards to Riverwalk and Alamo. Terrific hotel, modern, clean and staff was great. Will recommend for certain!

title: “Wow!”
text: This hotel is just wow! Huge room, bathroom divided into two sections, that is sweet. Great service, good bar. Computers and printers for free in the basement. Fast and free WiFi. There is simply nothing bad about this hotel.

title: “Chicago- great place to visit”
text: The location of the House of Blues Hotel was great- the room was a little small but very clean. When flying into O'Hare Airport I would recommend taking the CTA (the Chicago Subway) to the hotel. For $2.00 you can take the Blue Line to Clark and Lake Street- it takes about 35-40 min but it's alot less than a cab. We went to a Cub game at Wrigley field- great time- would def. recommend seeing a game if possible. Also walk to the Navy pier lots to do, from the Navy pier we took the water taxi to the Sears Tower- $6 ride on the Chicago river to the Sears Tower- we got to our destination while getting a scenic ride down the river. Must go to lunch at FOGO de CHAO (661 N LaSalle ST)- go for lunch b/c its alot less expensive- amazing food- (they give you 15 different types of meat where you can have as much as you want- unlimited sides and salad bar- lunch is $29 per person- dinner $49. Great place!

title: “Great Customer Service at the ES”
text:
We booked this hotel at the last minute choosing not to stay right in downtown since the hotel rates were somewhat higher than at the ES. From reading previous reviews, we knew the ES is a little outdated but found the hotel to be very clean and well maintained. Check in was efficient, and Frederick then showed us to our room thoroughly explaining the amenities of the hotel on the way. We took advantage of the hotel's free shuttle service over to 6th Street since it was raining. We called Frederick when we were ready to return to the hotel and he was there within 5 minutes. 
ROOM:
Nicely sized and appreciated the 2 room suite especially with a teenager. The shower had plenty of hot water and the king bed was very comfortable. Our only complaint was the sofa bed sagged horribly and and sloped down towards the foot of the bed. We requested another pad which helped just a little. The extra bar sink came in handy for applying make-up, brushing teeth, etc. when someone was in the shower. The 2 flat screen TV's were nice, too. We heard no noise from outside the room and the curtains kept the room so dark we slept later than we anticipated!
FOOD:
The breakfast selection was consistent with Embassy Suites and very abundant - Eggs, bacon, sausage, potatoes, fruit, oatmeal, cereal, pastries and breads. The best part is the cooked to order omelets and pancakes. The chefs were friendly and nothing seemed too much for them. We got drinks at the Manager's reception one night during our stay.
The $13/day self-parking seemed a little high but it is much less than other Austin hotels. There are computers in the lobby and also in the business center for guest use.
We thoroughly enjoyed our short stay at this Embassy Suites. We were always greeted with a smile and they seemed to appreciate our business. We would definitely stay here again.

title: “Unworthy of a Category 5 Starwood Designation”
text:
We had the choice between the US Grant and the W. We made a bad choice.
We asked well in advance for an early check-in and a room with a view. We got the early check-in for a room on the topmost floor. Our view was of the San Diego Jail. At least we were high enough to not see the homeless sleeping on the streets all around the hotel.
1. Our room was tiny. 
2. The swimming pool was EVEN TINIER than our room. 
3. The "bath" towels were also tiny. 
4. The walls between the rooms were so thin that we heard our neighbor and I was constantly being awakened Sat evening to 3:30 am Sunday morning, at which time I called the front desk and I suppose someone finally got the errant guests to settle down. 
5. There was no free Internet service to check our email. 
6. There was no complimentary coffee service in the morning lobby. 
7. The car valets took excessive time in attending to us, both on arrivals and departures. 
8. While we have stayed in hotels with no Jacuzzi or air tubs in the room, I can't remember staying in a hotel with NO BATH TUB WHATSOEVER. There was no tub in the (tiny) bathroom that we had. 
9. The elevators were lit by violet LEDs which made them dark and disconcerting.
The W is pre-occupied with being hip and cute with its ever-present "W" theme; e.g., call "Wheels" when you want the valet and call "Whatever/Whenever" if you want room service. 
For the prices charged, W is woefuilly inadequate.

title: “NICE hotel”
text: We always love Marriott properties and this one was particularly nice. Contemporary lobby for small gatherings off the bistro with lots of tables and computers. Great location to the zoo, Sea World and downtown San Diego. Updated rooms. $16 overnight parking was our only negative.

title: “New York 1st timers”
text:
Our 3 night stay was just wonderful. Staff from front desk to cleaners were helpful, polite and friendly.
Excellent location in midtown Manhattan.Next trip to New York will stay here again.

title: “One of the most delightful stays ever”
text: My sister and I moved my daughter to Seattle and my travel agent recommended this hotel. We stayed 5 nights and it was truly exceptional. The rooms and lobby are beautiful and the beds very comfy, but the best thing was the staff. They were friendly and welcoming and helped us with everything we needed (mostly directions). After 3 days, we felt like family. I have never stayed at a hotel with that many kind and attentive staff members. There wasn't one crabby one in the place! Even the housekeeping person left a note to "have a nice day". This will definitely be my go-to hotel in Seattle.

title: “Hmmmmmmm”
text: This hotel is very basic and the walls are very thin. Rooms are small and very basic. Breakfast not the best and staff are little too relaxed as in they don't pick up the phone. Not a nice place for a chic city

title: “Excellent weekend”
text: We had a great weekend at the Hotel Wilshire. It has beautifully designed rooms that are clean with very comfortable beds. The bathrooms are really nicely designed with everything new. The rooftop pool and restaurant provided incredible views of the Hollywood hills, including the Hollywood sign. It's a great place to wake up and have breakfast in L.A., whether on vacation or on business.

title: “Absolutely Horrible”
text:
I booked three rooms for three days in November for a training class we were to be in. One of the ladies arrived early in the evening, however, the other lady and I did not get in until 10:30 PM. We both had been up since very early and were very tired when we arrived. The security lock on my door was broken, there was a dirty towel hanging on the back of the door in the bathroom and the bathroom was dirty. I did not sleep all night worrying about the door, but since I had not heard from the other two, I did not feel I could leave that night. Early the next morning I called both my co-workers and told them we were leaving and finding a different hotel for the remaining stay. I asked them to pack and meet me at my room. When the one lady arrived, she just opened the door and walked right in. THE DOOR HAD BEEN UNLOCKED ALL NIGHT. Here not only did the security lock not work, but neither did the handle lock. 
One of the other ladies had no heat in her room and there was a gap of approximately 2 inches under her door. She said that she actually went out to her car to get warm before we arrived, but there were some suspicious looking guys hanging out in the lot so she went back to her room.
We also heard on the news the next day that there was a rapist in the area. Imagine how I felt that I had booked these rooms for two of my employees and myself!!
When I checked us out and wanted to speak to a manager, Raju would not be in until the next day. when I did speak to him, he gave me $15 dollars off the price of the two rooms.....big deal!!
One out of the three rooms had no problems.
I just wish I had seen this website sooner.

title: “Go elsewhere”
text: After reading some of the reviews here, I felt I had a good idea on what to expect. First, the rooms are definitely small. Crazy small. Bathroom barely fits the sink and toilet and then there is another room for the shower (some rooms have diff. configurations, but all bathrooms are split up). Basically the room is a bed and long desk with a flat screen tv propped on it. However, everyone here talks about how great the customer service is, but I had the opposite experience. We got in late after driving for 5 hours from Whistler. Once we got there, the night manager checked us in. She didn't ask if we needed help with our bags or anything. So we grabbed their luggage carts ourselves (no idea where the bellperson was at this point) and loaded the cars ourselves. Then we got to the elevator. Basically, in order to get these luggage carts into the elevator, you need a degree in Geometry. So we're dead tired, trying to get the luggage carts into the elevator, and the night manager is just standing there talking with the valet guy or possibly the bellperson. Nobody even offers to help or do anything to help us. They just let us struggle. Unreal! I'm not sure where the customer service comments come from, but we definitely did not see anything remotely resembling customer service. Do not stay here. The Roosevelt (where we stayed before departing for Whistler) down the street is cheaper and ten times better.

title: “Greeted by "Sherriff" Daniel”
text: Great accomodations for a party of 4 women sharing a suite with king size bed and queen size sleep sofa. Comforts of a studio apartment with the benefit of two rooms. The attention at the front desk was excellent. In particular Daniel who wears a Sherriff's badge that a guest gave him. Gracious, attentive and accomodating. A warm welcome and a kind farewell.

title: “review for The Fairmont in Dallas Texas”
text: I stayed at The Fairmont for a few days while I was attending a business conference that was also at The Fairmont. My whole experience was excellent and I would recommend this hotel. My experiences were at check-in, their bar, and with Tony Bennett luggage hold/bell services which were all pleasant.

title: “Hotel in wonderful location.”
text:
Received a very warm welcome from all the staff at Chelsea Pines - even when we arrived at 11.30pm with large suitcases that needed lugging up the stairs. Very clean rooms with soft towels for the bathrooms, although don't expect a power shower. Great breakfast facilities, sitting in the conservatory area eating NY muffins was lovely. Have a computer room that was ideal to check out local restaurants and book in for our return flights home as none of us had brought laptops. Free WiFi connection. Provided info on the local area, which is just ideal to explore the lovely Greenwich, Meatpacking and Chelsea area. We were advised to turn left out of the hotel originally, but much preferred the area on the right - check out Cafe d'Ariola (sp?) 2 mins walk towards meatpacking area where they serve brunch on Sat and Sun 12-2pm, lovely food and champagne and simosas topped up constantly within the $30 price! The newly redone hi-line walk which used to be a railway track is a lovely walk on a sunny day. Cocktails at The Standard Hotel (pricey) and meal at the Standard Grill under the hotel - brill. The subway is about 50 yards away and we also used a taxi to get us back from the top of 5th Avenue and it cost approx $10. I had very good communication from the hotel prior to this trip via e-mail and the website is exactly what it is - right down to Charlie the cat! 
I would recommend this hotel to gay or straight people - We were a group of 6 straight females getting away from the families for a long weekend celebrating a 40th birthday and the hotel totally suited our needs - clean, friendly, great location and affordable.

title: “A great hotel close to everything in midtown”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Warwick Hotel for three nights this summer. It has been, and continues to be, our favorite place to stay in the city. The hotel is beautifully maintained , the staff is always pleasant and helpful. You're within walking distance of shops, restaurants, theaters and there is easy access to bus and subway lines for going to lower Manhattan. The rates can be pricey but if you plan ahead, you can get good deals.

title: “Great hotel but remember the ear plugs”
text: I stayed here for a night at the beginning of June. The room was large and comfortable, it was lovely to have coffee beans and a grinder in the room (next time, could I request dark roast?) and the concierge gave good directions to me, Ms. Direction Challenged, for a great run. My one quibble is not the hotel's fault: located across the street from a major hospital, the sirens were constant and I was extremely happy I brought ear plugs ...

title: “Spartan, clean, good value”
text: I stayed here with a friend while we vacationed in Phoenix. The hotel is spartan, but very clean and a good value. It was within walking distance to many activities and restaurants in downtown Phoenix. My only complaint was that the "breakfast" seemed more like a pre-breakfast snack to me (donut or apple and coffee) and wasn't available until 7 (we were up at 6 sometimes). We also had our windows open at night and heard the rabble across the parking lot most nights.

title: “Cockroach sighted in bath!”
text:
I've stayed in quite a number of budget hotels, including Super 8, but this one is the pits - on my third and last night there, I stepped into the bath to find a cockroach there. You can see it in the photos. It ran away somewhere, and while this can happen, it does tend to suggest poor hygiene standards. The bathroom was the worst maintained part of the room, with a large hole in the wall around the shower head (perhaps where the cockroach came from) and several chips in the bath. The room looked the worse for wear and tear also, so I'd advise Super 8 management to thoroughly renovate this property before they lose business.
I was in room 144 and neighbours in room 143 caused a lot of noise in the evenings, revving their pick-up truck engine at past midnight, and they also left a pile of rubbish outside their door, strewn all over the place. My experience at this Super 8 was not up to standard.

title: “Great location”
text: Great central location near times square and the subway. Rooms were clean and comfortable - although we had to change rooms as we had booked a queen room and were given two singles. The staff in general were not very helpful - and when we wanted a taxi to the airport, we were told the normal cabs were metered and would be $65-70, so we were booked a private taxi for $60. The driver, I felt, was a friend of the staff member when he arrived. As we drove to the airport, we went past a NYC taxi which said 'Manhattan to JFK - flat rate $45'.

title: “Comfortable but pricey”
text: Valet parking is $46 for a 24-hour day. If you want to park on the premises, it's valet only. Everyone expects a tip. We had to pay two people to just bring up our luggage (one to get them out of the car and to the main desk, one to get it to our room). There's no concierge/lounge available on Saturdays. The food selection is minimal in any case at this location. We had a nice room on the concierge level with a partial view of the water and wharf. There is no airport shuttle. The pool is indoors and fun, albeit small. There weren't very many children the night we went, but it would be hard to navigate in the pool with a lot of kids there. There's an outdoor deck overlooking the harbor in the pool area. At least this location offers an in-room safe.

title: “Not a "boutique" hotel -- but solid value, great location”
text: I had a pleasant two-night stay at the Inn of Chicago in a standard queen room. The location is great, the room was clean and quiet, and the bed was comfortable. However, they describe themselves as a boutique hotel, but they lack the charm, attention to detail, and small creature comforts that I associate with that term. The most charming parts of the hotel are the lobby, bar, and rooftop terrace. The décor of the room was kind of blah. The queen room was very small—acceptable for one person, but would have been far too small to be comfortable for two people. There was a decent-sized desk and swivel chair. There was one small straight-back chair, but I’m not sure why they bothered with it, since it wasn’t really comfortable for relaxing or reading and didn’t have an end table next to it so it wasn’t useful for eating or having a cup of coffee. There was a coffeemaker in the room, with paper cups and generic coffee, but no tea. The bathroom was tiny, with a pedestal sink, no counter space at all, and just two small glass shelves for toiletries. It was so small, in fact, that the towel rack was actually mounted on the back wall of the bathtub/shower combo, which I found incredibly odd and inconvenient. The soap dish was mounted directly under the showerhead, which meant that it was constantly full of water, rendering it unusable. There was no fan in the bathroom. They offered orange-scented shampoo, conditioner, and soap, but no lotion. There was no in-room safe. The TV was a good size flat panel, but it lacked premium cable. It’s these small details that, in my mind, distinguish true boutique hotels. The Inn of Chicago is simply a smaller, solid, mid-range hotel. It was acceptable and pleasant, but not a place I would actively seek out for a future stay.

title: “Great B&B, walking distance to the San Diego Zoo!”
text: I mainly selected this place because it sounded nice and was walking distance to the zoo. The rooms have personality as others have said and my wife really liked it. Breakfast was good and the area is great, no complaints!

title: “Great stay, loved our room and service”
text: I stayed at this hotel last week and was very impressed with our spacious room and the attentive staff. While one would expect great service at a Hyatt, I feel that this property goes above and beyond to maintain a very high level of customer satisfaction. The location is perfect, close to Michigan Ave and Navy Pier.

title: “Fantastic trip”
text: I have just returned from four nights at the Wellington Hotel and feel I must defend it. I had already booked this trip as a birthday present for my boyfriend so was horrified when I read some of the reviews for the hotel on this site. However, upon arival I was more than pleasantly surprised. This hotel is in a fantastic location, within walking distance of many major attractions and with a subway station right outside the door. Okay, so the rooms may not be up to The Ritz standard but who really cares? Our room was clean and tidy, the staff were all happy and polite and the diner downstairs was lovely. I would definately return here as it is a great base in a great city.

title: “Comfortable stay at solid Hilton property”
text:
Just returned from spending a weekend in San Diego at the Hilton Mission Valley. My partner had booked the room through the Hilton Honors reward program, so the price was definitely right.
We had a king bedded room on an executive level floor. The room was nicely decorated and had all the necessary comforts for a relaxing weekend. The bed was especially comfortable. . .nice and soft yet firm enough for a good night's sleep. The room size was above average. 
The hotel is located off a major highway, so it would be advised to request a room at the back of the hotel. Not much of a view from there either- just staring at a hillside, but nice and quiet. The hotel is easily accessible to Old Town, Balboa Park and the zoo, and shopping (Fashion Valley Shops).
Parking is in an underground garage and runs $10 a day with in and out privileges. There are some spots for free in the front of the hotel but they are very limited and quite small.
The staff was friendly and gave good directions (printed sheet with directions to most popular sights was very helpful to have hroughout weekend). Freshly baked chocolate chip cookie at night was nice touch.
No complaints regarding this property. Was very satisfied with stay.

title: “Absolutely Amazing!”
text: My boyfreind and I stayed for one night during the weekend. We did have reservations at the Top of the Hub, we ended up canceling them, because the hotel was so nice. The resterant that is connected to the hotel is called "Mooo" . We got room service and orderd from Mooo. We both had the filet, witch was excellent! We had the studio suite, witch consisted of a fire place, serieo (with sround sound), TV/DVD player in the bathroom, a rain shower head, a tub with jets, and a IPOD dock. It was on the side of beacon street, so the view was nice. The staff was so plesent... i would go back with out a doubt, Its the pefect setting if your looking for romance.

title: “The Westin Tabor made Denver stand out as a city that cares about Service!”
text: My stay at the Westin Tabor was in conjunction with an event at the Colorado Convention Center, and having never been to Denver before, I was concerned that the hotel might be too far for me to walk to the event. Once I got there, all my worries faded! The hotel was perfectly situated with just enough walking required to clear my mind before and after the meetings. It is so close to everything that makes downtown Denver great, and I couldn't have asked for a better location. The staff was wonderful throughout, from the doorman to the room service waiter - but especially the front desk agents who were always helpful, attentive and caring. The room was perfect - with one small exception: the alarm clock REALLY needs to be updated, and of course the alarm went off at 6am to a hispanic station (I did not set it, but I did need to get up anyway, so it wasn't a real problem). Otherwise all was wonderful, and I would not hesitate to recommend this hotel for anyone traveling to Denver.

title: “Outstanding Service, Beautiful Rooms”
text:
I’ve not given any hotel a five star rating during my years on TripAdvisor, until now. Mostly, The Ballantyne deserves it because of the level of service, which is among the best I’ve ever experienced anywhere. It’s also due to the beautiful rooms and level of comfort you receive here.
Check-in was a breeze. My partner and I were making a swing through NC with our two 90-ish moms. We were given a great combination of rooms that made our accommodations a two bedroom, three bathroom suite with a connecting living room. With comfortable beds, large bathrooms with all the amenities, and balconies overlooking the golf course, this was, by far, the most luxurious place we have stayed for some time. From our balconies, we could see Charlotte in the distance and enjoyed the golf course view.
From the moment you get out of your car, to the front desk and concierge staff, to the housekeepers, everyone wants to please. A special shout out goes to the wonderful housekeeping staff who were very friendly and even brought extra little treats for the moms each day. I consider them to be the best housekeeping staff in any hotel in the U.S. The room was made up twice a day and everything was immaculate.
The fitness center was very well equipped, with water and towels placed at each piece of CV equipment. To be honest, the staff in the center were too busy looking pretty to be of help, but that doesn’t affect my rating. The indoor pool was lovely and there are plans for an outdoor pool. We did not use the spa, but wish we had.
The traditional tea service was a hit with the moms. Again, it was the service that made this little “event” special. Very warm and friendly. Breakfast was fine. Our other meals were eaten off-property.
This is THE place to stay in the Charlotte area. You can tell by the cars in the lot. A Maybach owned by a well-known professional athlete was conspicuously parked in front. It is a little strange at first to find this luxury property right off a main road in the middle of contemporary shopping centers, but once you’re inside, the outside world does not intrude.
