We got a great rate for what were had from the hotel’s Web site. We were also ten minutes from SC, which had cheaper gas. I know, we pinched pennies on gas but splurged on a great hotel. We wouldn’t have wanted to stay anywhere else.

title: “Hardly 3*”
text: This hotel doesn't really deserve a 3* rating. Its more a 2.5* rating in my mind. Anyway, its an adequate airport hotel for over night stay but if your a light sleeper i wouldn't recommend it as the rooms arent really soundproof and the aircraft noise is very very loud! I had to move rooms twice as i couldnt sleep and i dont consider myself a light sleeper. Its no wonder they provide earplugs in an amenity bag on your bed.

title: “Great location; Not ideal service”
text: My wife and I recently visited Mahattan for a long early December weekend. We were pleasantly surprised to learn that the hotel was situated in the heart of Times Square. It was a hectic weekend with so many in town to do some early Christams shopping. Because of the crowds, we ended up spending more for our hotel then we generally do on less busy wekends in NYC. The room was large and clean. The bed was comfortable. It was generally quiet. The concierge was helpful in obtaining post theatre reservations, although, a bit sassy. I would recommend it, except that I have had more pleasant experiences and more afforbable experiences at more boutique type places.

title: “Great Memorial Weekend stay”
text:
We had 4 teenagers and 2 rooms. Excellent stay. 
We requested 2 rooms next to each other. Arrived at 11am Saturday of Memorial Day weekend. One room was available and they said they would get our other room as close as possible. We ended up with the room next door which was great. 
Not so great pull out beds but you don't expect they would be that great. 
Excellent location to Navy Pier and the Watertower and Michigan Ave. shopping. 
Would stay again when we visit again.

title: “Nice 1st impression”
text:
"We've upgraded you!" Who doesn't love hearing that! I booked a Cityview Premier King under the Rough Draft opening rate. The "upgrade" was to a 14th floor suite.... but overlooking the river. I appreciated the upgrade, but after a number of visits to NYC, we'd never had a city view (usually a brick wall view). Michelle at the front desk seamlessly changed us to an 11th floor Cityview Jr. Suite. We didn't regret giving up a larger suite for this room--it had GREAT unobstructed views of Times Square overlooking 11th Ave. (however, the hotel is JUST at the wrong angle to see recognizable buildings like the Empire State or Rockefeller Center)
Oh.. and the bellman was incredibly friendly and apologetic after we entered the 14th floor suite to see it was 1. a river-front (which wasn't what we'd wanted) AND 2. that housecleaning still hadn't refreshed it from the previous guest! The staff is definitely the star of the hotel--even if they're just passing you or waiting at the elevator with you, they're striking up a natural, unforced conversation.
After staying at the Hudson Hotel (near Columbus Circle) a number of times with their postage-stamp sized bathroom, it was great having a double sink, shower AND tub. (The shower alone at Ink was the size of the Hudson's entire bathroom).
I've seen complaints here about ink 48's location. We found it GREAT! You walk down 48th street and in a few blocks you're right in the middle of Times Square. We were in the city for a concert at MSG--we walked to and from there. We walked another day up to Rockefeller Center, then up 5th Avenue and through Central Park (up to 72nd street). It was also great to walk through neighborhoods like Hell's Kitchen instead of staying directly in the midst of tourist central. We stopped into quite a few local neighborhood stores (read: they didn't carry "I heart NY" shirts!) It was a great taste of local flavor. Although I didn't get a chance to utilize it this visit, I liked the "runner's map" they had to show you great routes and distance markers along the river bike path for 2, 3 or 6 mile runs.
The complimentary breakfast (bagels, croissants, coffee and juice) was a nice move.
Room for improvement: The room rate was supposedly 48% off for the "rough draft opening." I booked for two nights at $265 a night. I think charging $500-$700 per night that I'm seeing on their rate calendar is simply insane. I've stayed at a Ritz-Carlton for MUCH less than their non-discounted rates. And although it's a nice hotel, it's NO Ritz-Carlton. They need to revise their full-price rates to be realistic. Although I have no complaints about service or accommodations, $265 is, hands-down, the most I'd spend to stay there again...and, $265 is hitting the ceiling of what I'd pay.
Also, small complaint: we could hear our neighbors raise and lower their blinds. it seems that to accommodate large windows, the walls are thinner near the window area. Nothing worse than hearing neighbors next door to ruin the feelings of privacy in your room!
I parked on my own at a garage a block away (at 49th St and 10th ave.) for $27 per day. I did that because I couldn't see the valet rate on their website. ... A good move considering another reviewer said valet was $65 per day. I'm sure with that $65 rate, the valet probably parked cars in the same garage that I was in!
And I agree with another reviewer who commented about the water bottle. The last few hotels I've stayed (and of comparable price points) have offered free bottled water. it seems to be a trend now in hotels. At Ink 48, there was a liter of Poland Springs on the shelf next to two glasses. Totally not even near the mini-bar. We thought it was complimentary... until on our last day, I looked at the mini-bar price list and saw that it was $7. They should put a note ON the bottle instead of burying the price in the snack drawer.
To summarize: Great hotel. Super friendly staff top-to-bottom, moderately spacious for NYC hotels with great views of city and river/NJ. The "48% off" rate is what they should charge all the time. $65 valet per day is off the charts insane. 
I'd stay there again if I got a rate comparable to (or slightly less than) what I paid last weekend.

title: “Very pleased with stay”
text: We stayed here because it was the official conference hotel for my husband's conference. The location was great. Not right in the middle of the Riverwalk, but on a leg of the Riverwalk. Could walk to the mall or the Alamo in no time. Our room was clean, water hot for showers. Pool is small, but that's ok. Fitness room was large and had many machines. We had a small fridge in our room and a great view. Bed was comfy. We only had 2 small drawers to put our clothes in, which I thought was odd. Staff was pleasant and helpful. Right downstairs by the Riverwalk is a great place for happy hour! 4.50 drinks and 4.00 small plates that are some of the tastiest I've ever had. A mix of Asian and Latin flavors. There is a place in the lobby where you can get Starbucks.

title: “Nice Labor Day weekend stay”
text:
Stayed for two nights at the Hilton Manhattan East over Labor Day. Nice modern lobby, front desk efficient and friendly, elevators lightning quick. Room was fairly small, even by Manhattan standards, but felt cozy rather than squished. Bathroom was fairly sizable, however, and nicely accessorized. Best of all, one of the quietest hotel rooms I have ever stayed in (maybe because it was older construction with better sound insulation). Very relaxing place to return after a long day exploring Manhattan.
I did feel that several standard services were not provided/unavailable. First valet parking was not offered (just for the weekend, per the receptionist). Also the concierge was MIA for extended periods (i.e. 5-8 PM on Sunday). And the fitness center seemed like it wasn't cleaned over Sunday PM, or longer. Perhaps some staff shortage over the holiday? Nonetheless would not hesitate to return.

title: “Clean hotel, good value, fun location”
text:
Great hotel - extremely clean, good value, and close to all the lower Manhattan tourist attractions, like the Statue of Liberty, the Museum of the American Indian, and the Brooklyn Bridge (make sure to take a walk across the bridge - the photos can't be beat!). 
Very safe neighborhood, since security guards are everywhere to protect the New York Stock Exchange and the Wall Street finance houses.
One tip: take a printout of the map showing its location, since taxi drivers have trouble finding this small street.

title: “Look at other hotels before confirming this one.”
text:
This hotel is a poor relative of the Ritz-Carlton family of hotels. Of course the room was clean - although it was overly cluttered with furniture - I suspect there is a standard list of furniture that is put in rooms and no lateral thought that if the room is a bit smaller - perhaps less furniture should be included. 
Avoid a "City View" - basically the view is of another tower block/skyscraper. The room I was given was extremely dingy - due to a window that was half the size of the standard windows. Surprisingly, there were no tea and coffee making facilities in the room perhaps an attempt to encourage you to use the expensive room service.
Be very careful of using the telephone in the room, the charges are not specified but a call to a mobile phone for 30 seconds was at $15.
charged
Service was poor, in particular the service in the bar was very slow - perhaps the hotel has cut costs and reduced staffing - if that is the case - its shows.

title: “Great place if you do not shower or use the internet”
text: First, I would like to state, the staff was great, very nice and sympathetic. This is a great place if one is travelling for pleasure and you prefer to bathe rather than shower. Every time someone in the hotel flushes the toliet or turns on the water, the shower becomes SCALDING hot, I was constantly adjusting the temperature to adjust to the extreme changes. If the shower was the only issue I would give a higher rating; however, the internet issues were atrocious. I was attending a conference at the Hyatt and due to company restrictions could not stay so we decided to stay across the street at the San Carlos. We arrived on Sunday and could not get an internet connection until I returned home. We actually had to "borrow" wifi from Arizona State and even that was iffy. Another guest mentioned she had to sit in the stairwell in order to get a signal. My colleague and I carried our laptops to S'bucks, Subway and the Irish pub next door so we could work. It was horrible. I would only recommend if the hotel updated their plumbing, wireless and cleaned the carpet more frequently. Oh, one more thing, if you decide to stay, bring earplugs; you can hear EVERYTHING from the rooms next door.

title: “Great location and value”
text:
Just stayed at the New Yorker for 2 nights with my teenage son. We were in town for his Spring break to see some sights and a show.
 The location across from Penn Station and Madison Sq Garden is excellent- convenient to the blue and red subway lines. Just a few blocks from Times Square, Theater district, Midtown, etc. 
Our room at $169- was typical NY small with a double bed. Nicely furnished. Flat screen TV. Free wireless that worked well. I saw no need to upgrade to the "faster" wireless at $9.95 a day.
We arrived early on Monday and they were able to put us in a room at 12:30 instead of waiting until 3:00. I found no issues with unfriendly service, though we did not have a lot of interaction.
All in all, a very good value and location for NY.

title: “Very nice”
text:
Location is great, right in Times square, the views of the rooms are amazing.
The lobby is nice and there is good music and nice people at night.
The Blue fin restaurent down on the first floor is great, good food, good drinks and terrific views of Times square!
The beds very confortable,the only bad thing was the shower, they is no pression, but I would definitely go back anytime!

title: “Building is old, musty rooms”
text: We paid $200/ night and not worth it. Very old, dingy rooms that they have tried to remodel best they could. Water slow to come out of pipes, rooms smell like Smoking Rooms from the 1960's. Look a little more North up Michigan Ave would be my suggestion. Dk

title: “Loved it!”
text: Awesome hotel experience. Everything was gorgeous. My boyfriend and I stayed for two nights. One night the water was cold but they had notified us before hand that would be an issue. Other than that it was a memorable experience. Loved the showers and bathroom. The barista was very nice and made delicious coffee and lattes. Would def recommend if visiting NYC.

title: “Great location!”
text: No frills hotel but clean and safe. Our room was on the 8th floor with a bit of a river view And small but we spent so little time in the room that it didn't matter. Staff was friendly and helpful.

title: “Nice Hotel”
text: We stayed here for 1 night and we thought the hotel was nice. The location of the hotel is not to far from the White House and the National Mall. There is a Metro Rail Station about 3 blocks from the hotel.

title: “Lovely hotel with outstanding views in a great location!”
text: First impressions of the hotel are amazing - very impressive from the outside and the lobby is breathtakingly beautiful. The rooms have outstanding views over San Diego however the money has definitely been spent in the lobby and bars and not in the rooms. The rooms are looking a little tired and not at the same standard of the public areas of the hotel. Location is great - the hotel backs onto the Seaport Village which is a lovely little area to potter around in and has a gorgeous marina to enjoy in the sunshine. Seal Tours and the Trolley Tour are also available from the Seaport Village - both are definitely worth doing! USS Midway Museum is about a 15 minute walk and is a great day out also. Overall a gorgeous hotel in a great place, would highly recommend.

title: “A lovely hotel with helpful and friendly staff”
text:
The hotel more than met our expectations. The room was great, the staff were very helpful and friendly. The happy hour was a great way to relax at the end of the day. The buffet breakfast was more than adequate. The hotel is in a great position for walking to the Heritage area and the restaurants. It is only a short walk to the baseball stadium.
Parking is expensive but then it is a city hotel. The staff always brought the car round relatively quickly.
One negative - the directions to the Johnson Space Centre were out of date which meant we were given a much longer route to get there.
We would definately stay there again if in Houston. Thanks to tripadvisors contibutors for helping us decide on this hotel.

title: “Had higher expectations”
text:
The only reason I'm giving this place a 2 out of 5 is because of the front desk agent that checked me in and the night auditor who checked me out.
Arrived to the hotel about 6:00pm on a Saturday evening,
The hotel is difficult to locate without a gps. You HAVE to pay for parking. On Fri / Say nights it's almost $20.00!! Seriously? Pay parking?? Who does that anymore? The parking garage has many levels, is quite small, poorly lit, no air circulation, and smells like something died a long time ago.
Front lobby is typical. BIG front desk / registration area with marble counter tops. The gentleman who checked me is was totally helpful with honoring my request for a high floor (He gave me 20th floor out of 26 floors) and getting info for a pastry shop becuase I had a sweet tooth. Posted directions to the South Tower were sparse. Elevator smelled kind of funky but was fast getting up to the 20th floor.
Now the room...Typical king sized bed 'overstuffed' with fluffy down comforter and down pillows, flat screen tv, three drawer dresser, small desk with coffee and coffee maker. There was no mini fridge / cooler. The view was...ok. Too many office buildings and other hotels were blocking any view. There were dust bunnies on the window sill and cracks in the glass of the window. I could even feel a crack with my bare fingers and feel air coming in from the other crack. Safety hazard !! I threw the top down comforter on the ground. I had no reason to use it. Besides, hotels never clean those things. The thermostat is a motion censor. So once you fall asleep it goes into "sleep mode" and only kicks one every once and a while.
Now the bathroom...The grout in the stand up shower area was pink. Grout is not supposed to be pink. It was moldy and disgusting. The housekeepers obviously need to pay more attention to the other areas of the shower than just the walls. The toilet / sink area was kind of claustrophobic. Right next to each other. The sink itself was nice but small. I did find two dirty towels. One was a face towel that had pink / red lipstick on it and the other was a hand towel that looked dirty. I put those aside on the floor so I wouldn't get confused on what was clean. There was no fan in the bathroom. Also, while checking over the bathroom, I could hear the people talking the room next to me. Thin walls. Ugh!!
Finally got to sleep around 10:00pm. I was woken up by fire engines and police cars going through the streets with sirens BLARING at 3:00am even though I took two sleeping pills!! This continued off and on for about an hour. Obviously the walls and windows were not soundproof enough / built well.
I couldn't take it anymore so I checked out about 4:30am to take the 2 hour drive back home. The gentleman at the front desk was apologetic and offered to move me to a better room but I had enough and left. He was also nice enough to comp my parking fee.
I did not get a chance to go to the restaurant for dinner and breakfast. I did not bring my laptop with me but I'm sure they charge for wifi.
I get the fact that Baltimore is one of the oldest cities in the nation but that is no reason to skimp on the things people these days like and want. Who doesn't like a nice quiet, clean room and quality surroundings.

title: “Great location & perfect service!”
text:
We have stayed at the Fairmont Georgetown on (3) different occasions. It's location just 2 blocks to the heart of Georgetown shops & restaurants, and 3 blocks to Foggy Bottom Metro stop is top-notch! This is a very upscale hotel with fantastic service, yet doesn't feel stuffy or formal. The rooms are spacious, clean and very comfortable (love the beds!); the concierge very helpful; and the breakfast buffet is wonderful!
We liked being able to walk into Georgetown for shopping & dinner, and the proximity of the Metro stop made it extremely easy to get to the monuments and Washington Reagan airport.
You can often get a nightly rate that includes buffet breakfast for 2 and parking. I think this is a 5-star hotel at 3-star prices.

title: “We always stay here when passing through. But still ...”
text:
We've grown to rely on this Days Inn when visiting close relatives in Worthington. Clean rooms, comfortable beds, convenient location, and it's close to a corporate park where we like to walk the dog.
So we can recommend it, but with some comments:
1. The previous reviewer is right. Some rooms are very small. (Others aren't.)
2. Desk staff aren't the friendliest people in the Midwest.
3. This time I noticed mildew around the bottom of the molded shower inset.
As my mother would say, this motel is "perfectly all right." We'll keep staying here. If it wasn't so familiar I'd probably be less critical.

title: “Excellent Stopover”
text:
When we arrived to this hotel , we were very tired after a long intercontinental flight and with much pleasure we found out everyone, from the courtesy-shuttle driver to the receptionist to the restaurant staff, to be very welcoming and friendly.
Our suite was awesome, well kept,with modern decor, very comfortable and with huge beds. No noise from the airport whatsoever
The central atrium hosts every evening the free manager reception , where you get tasty light appetizers and drinks.
We also liked very much the restaurant Aerobistro, it has a good dinner selection. My husband had penne arrabbiata with lot of shrimps, and my Cobb salad was rich in blue cheese and bacon - which I love.
Breakfast is included in the room rate and served in the bright central atrium; if you wake up early and are on the go, you can grab pastries (yummy) and a cup of coffee , even before breakfast hours.
A very nice hotel to rest in , if you have a flight the day after, but we saw families who where staying there for their Los Angeles vacation
Highly recommended !

title: “Perfect Stay- Hotel Solamar was flawless!”
text:
From start to finish, the Hotel Solamar was perfect. A welcomed addition to downtown San Diego. The bell staff was extremely attentive, and check in was flawless. I was shown to my King Deluxe Spa room, and it was awesome. The colors were very well paired- chocolate brown and light blue- my favorites! I decided upon arrival to have a massage in my room. I called the concierge, and had a massage therapist at my door in an hour!! 
The soaking tub was a great treat, (although tough to navigate if you're short like me!).. The amenities were all Aveda, and well sized!
It is true, the pool/bar area is totally chic- and NOT suitable for families/kids- which I think is one of the best features of this hotel! Its just nice to have an oasis in San Diego thats relatively kid-free. Spent an entire afternoon out at the pool- it was like heaven. 
I cannot recommend this place enough- stay here if you think you're cool enough!

title: “The Best Western at Longwood Medical”
text: Very nice clean hotel. The front desk staff was very freindly and helpful. The perfect Hotel to stay at when going to Fenway Park, not expensive to park and easy walk to Fenway. I highly reccommend this hotel. The AC in the room worked great, the beds were very comfortable and the hotel was quiet. I plan on staying here again when I go to the the Red Sox later in the month

title: “MSDC Gala”
text: attended a business affair at the Loews on Friday 12/07/12. It was a pleasure from the beginning to the end. everyone was so helpful and friendly. The room was beautiful and spacious. I would recommend this hotel to anyone coming to Philadelphia for business or pleasure. Also the location is great, near City Hall and shopping.

title: “Perfectly situated”
text: Perfectly situated for all tourist requirements. A very short distance to Faneuil Hall and Quincy Market. A 10 minute walk to Boston Common. Our room was exactly as described and was very clean and comfortable. We found the hospitality of the Bostonians very pleasurable and would certainly stay here again.

title: “Good value; great location.”
text: Great location; right across the street from city hall. If you can get a government or AAA rate, the price is good, too. Breakfast is included, and you can even eat supper for free, at their "evening snack bar". (Though it isn't really...um...good.) Rooms are bigger than you'd think for a downtown hotel. I'd go back.

title: “Great stay”
text:
The Westin Market St. is a well located hotel with good facilities. Located on 3rd St. about a 5min walk from Union Square makes it ideal for shopping and good restaurants. 
The service was good enough and the rooms had all the facilites you expect from a 4* hotel. No swimming pool here though!!!

title: “Aloft Phoenix Sky Harbor Airport”
text: This a wonderful hotel very close to Sky Harbor Airport. The hotel is still clean, fresh, and seems new. The rooms are comfortable, clean, and well appointed.

title: “Fantastic Location”
text: Loved the location, been to NYC several times and chose this hotel for its central location, not disappointed! We had a great view down on Times Square. Friendly and helpful staff.

title: “Loved the Hotel!”
text:
EVERYTHING IS PERFECT. WOULD STAY AGAIN...
Two things I did not like:
a) could not 2 beds and had to pay $25 per night for roll away.
b) parking is steep at $35 a night.
But I loved the service, location, condition and great rate I got.

title: “My thoughts...”
text: Overall, not a bad hotel. Some things to note and my comments: Underground Parking is USD$10/night with very tight spaces. No air-conditioning. With windows open, fairly noisy. Rooms are not bright enough even with all the lights on. Carpets could use a wash but fairly clean otherwise, especially bathroom. Friendly staff.Good value. Would stay again.

title: “A true Paradise”
text: The name is perfect to describe this hotel, it is a true tropical environment surrounded by lagoons and beaches and pools, tropical plants , beautiful birds and lovely ducks, besides the rooms that are so spacious and in one story, two-unit appointed bungalows with a patio. It is like living in a true tropical island with all the environment surrounding it . A unique unforgettable experience. the staff is very friendly . I really enjoyed it.

title: “Excellent hotel in an excellent location”
text: We absolutely loved this hotel. It had an entrance right onto the riverwalk. The hotel has been converted from an old bank building, beautiful. The hotel has free drinks and appetizers in the evening. It also has a fantastic breakfast. The rooftop pool and hot-tubs are really nice. What a view! We loved our standard room, very luxurious. The only con for this hotel is the $18 valet parking.

title: “Not a pleasent experience”
text: We recently stayed for 1 night in one of the king bedroom suite at BestWestern Hacienda. The room had a strange odor and felt very stuffy. I enjoy sleeping on hard bed, but the bed was even hard for me. Also, both me and my wife woke up with a bad headache the next morning - not sure if it is related to the stuffiness.

title: “Great Hotel! Great Location!”
text: Wife and I stayed over Memorial Day weekend. Can't say enough about it. Staff was friendly and attentive. Walking distance to Magnificent Mile and Lake Shore Dr. One block from Rush Street bars and restaurants. Two blocks from the subway. Beautiful rooms with minimalist design. Hugh windows afforded great views from 30th floor. Bed was incredibly comfortable. Luxurious bathroom. Room service prices surprisingly reasonable. Only complaint: all bathroom lights controlled by one switch and at one setting, which is very bright. Bottom line: would recommend the Sofitel to anyone looking for a great hotel experience.

title: “Excellent location, friendly staff and exceptionally clean accommodations”
text: We stayed at the Orchard Garden for our first trip to San Francisco and picked it -- after reading reviews -- for its location, green status and price. Although we did not have the promised mini-fridge in our room until the second day, and that one did not work properly, our stay was excellent. The room was small, typical for San Francisco it seems, but immaculate. And I don't think I've ever slept in a more comfortable hotel bed or used a better hotel-provided robe. It's a little weird that the bathroom door is a slider and does not close all the way or lock, but it was just my husband and me, so it didn't matter. You cannot beat the location -- about 5 short blocks from Union Square and a block from the Chinatown Gate as well as close to all forms of public transportation. The staff was very helpful and friendly and gave great recommendations for restaurants. We also got a great deal booking directly through the hotel's website and pre-paying-- three nights in a 10th floor room with a view for $362, including tax. Where else in San Francisco can you get that?!

title: “Not a "Choice" hotel”
text: There were ants everywhere in the room. The wireless would not work and the front desk manager said it was my laptop(which has been working fine everywhere else). The window in the room would not shut all the way. Getting out of the parking lot is scary, traffic is going 50 mph with a merge ramp just prior to the driveway, constant rushing traffic. For the price, no thanks.

title: “Great value for the location”
text: Another great hotel from the Kimpton family of hotels. This place is off of Union Square but still near Bart and other public transportation options. The rooms were small but unique and comfortable. I had a corner room with a good view of Nob Hill and Market on the 12th floor. As with all of Kimpton establishments, there is a free hosted wine happy hour from 5-6pm for guests and coffee in the morning. The hotel restaurant - Jasper's - offers solid food and drink choices. A great place to sleep after a long day in the beautiful city.

title: “Kids bunks like concrete”
text: Stayed for 2 nights with 2 teenagers. This was a great hotel, clean, and the decor in the kids suites make such a wonderful change from the chains. BUT. our stay was spoilt by the mattresses on the kids bunks - they were so hard my kids ended up with bad backs after 2 nights. Such a shame because our bed was very comfortable. Location was good with access to cable cars virtually outside the door. Felt safe staying here, I would recommend the hotel if they fixed those kids beds. We walked back from the 4th July fireworks at the Pier (along with thousands of other people) but the homeless people didn't bother us even the beggars used 'please' and 'thank you'. An extremely polite, interesting city.

title: “Cozy and friendly”
text: Stayed for two nights . In the heart of downtown of Indianapolis surrounded by many attractions and restaurants. Very friendly staff . Rooms are clean and well maintained. High speed complimentary Internet. Perfect combination especially with acceptable prices. Breakfast which was part of the deal is average however serves its purpose. The lobby is so nice and overlooks two streets. It is one block circle center mall entrance.

title: “Average Hotel, Big City Expense”
text:
I mulled given this a 2-star review, but I think overall the Sheraton has enough redeeming qualities to warrant 3 stars. Overall, this hotel is in an optimum location, but it abuses it's position by jacking up the prices. I've rented rooms in NYC for less! I've stayed at this hotel a few times over the past couple years, all for conferences being hosted in the facility. If it weren't for that convenience factor (and conference rates), I almost certainly would look for an alternative in downtown Denver.
The good: The valets, bell staff, and counter reps are excellent and friendly. The Mix bar off the main lobby is phenomenal, and despite its being in a hotel, the prices are surprisingly decent (still inflated, but not as much as you might expect). The staff definitely helped go the extra mile when I couldn't find my GPS unit (turns out I'd stuck it in a random pocket in a bag -- oops).
The ok: The rooms are in pretty good shape. This last trip, my room (2 double beds) was absurdly large with at least 20' of windows overlooking the pool. They have good sound insulation, too, which is important.
The bad: There are a few negatives to this hotel. First, the price is too high. I'm sorry, but this is Denver, not Manhattan; prices should be more consistent with the region. Second, parking, food, and internet access (e.g., breakfast in the restaurant) are also absurdly expensive (self-parking is $24/night, and the breakfast buffet is around the same price... that they're still even charging for internet access is galling). Getting into the parking ramp can also be a bit confusing (due in part to all the one-way streets). When I arrived this time, the entrance to the garage was actually blocked by 2 semi trucks.
Third, continuing with some of the "bad" here... I was rather distressed to walk out of my room and see a large cockroach in the hall. I immediately went back into my room and called the front desk, who promised to dispatch someone immediately to address. Is it an isolated incident? Let's hope so, but it certainly gives me pause.
Finally, my only other issue was in the morning... despite the aforementioned "good sound insulation" I was awoken around 5:30am by loud music from the pool area outside/below my window. I called the front desk and they promised to dispatch someone to resolve the matter, and the music did stop within about 15 minutes. This is a good reflection of the quality of service, but you have to wonder about the person (likely an employee) who felt inclined to turn on loud ambient music outside guest bedrooms at 5:30am.

title: “Great Location, Lots of Fun!”
text: This is definitely not your typical hotel but it is fun and after a long day, it was nice to come home to a place that was homey. The hotel is located in a great residential neighborhood with coffee shops, good local restaurants, 24 hour drug stores and accessible to public transportation and taxies. The rooms are large. We stayed in a family bunk room and after a long day of sightseeing, it was great to have the kids watch TV in their room while my husband watched the one in the living area and I read in my room. While the bedrooms are really alcoves, it is actually more spacious than a standard hotel room. The kids had a twin bed over a double bunk while we had a queen that was really comfortable. The bathrooms are tiny but fully equipped with Aveda products, hairdryer and of course, leopard robes. The very small staff was very accommodating and extremely helpful in making restaurant recommendations and providing directions. If you have a sense of amusement or adventure, I would recommend staying here. If you don't, then this may not be the place for you.

title: “Soaring Views”
text:
My one night stay at this hotel was very nice. I was on the 15th floor with incrediable views of downtown.
The room was very nice. It is large by city hotel standards. It has a large wardrobe closet in the hallway, a desk & 2 chairs, a coffee bar w/Nepresso (no charge). 
The bathroom was very nice. It had a soaking tub, seperate shower w/ a regular shower head & a rain head. 
The TV in the vanity mirror was nice, but a "low signal" kept it from being anything more than frustrating. Probably operator error, but come on it's a TV how hard should it be to use?
I ordered room service for dinner and breakfast. I must say that I was not impressed. Bummer, because usually Four Season meals are good anywhere, room, pool, restaurant. The service portion was absolutely terrific; which almost made up for the bad food. 
The following is just my pet peeve: In a downtown hotel why are they charging for wireless internet? If we were on an island or somewhere remote it would be much easier to take. 
Thank you for reading.

title: “Hotel was close to Fisherman's Wharf and very clean.”
text: We stayed in Holiday Inn Express in Fisherman's Wharf for 3 days. The hotel was very clean, the staff was always willing the help with any questions we had. The continental breakfast was very good.

title: “Gorgeous”
text: We stayed here over Christmas and New Year 2010/2011. This hotel is beautiful. The rooms are lush (if you are able to get a room that is not in-facing that is). The staff were great and nothing was too big or too small. We didnt find any attitude or snottiness from any staff member - it was all great! Don't miss out on the restaurant downstairs - especially for brunch!

title: “Pleasantly Surprised”
text:
After reading some of the reviews on this hotel I was a little concerned but it appears Marriott has gotten their act together with this hotel. We went over Labor Day weekend (crazy crowded) but everything flowed pretty well, we had a great time and we will definitely return. 
The good: 1) Everyone was extremely friendly and helpful during check-in. From the bellhop to the person checking us in. A great experience. 2) Slides, lazy river and pool were great and everything seemed to run pretty smooth considering the huge number of people using the facilities. 3) 18 Oaks Restaurant was amazing. Great service and food. 4) Room service was friendly, helpful and the food was great. I was amazed during Labor Day weekend that our food always arrived within 30 minutes. Very impressed.
The Bad: 1) Selfish people that drop a towel, magazine and hat on a handful of chairs early in the morning and don't show up until mid-afternoon to use them. Marriott needs to find some way to combat the abuse of this system. I hate going to a nice hotel and having to shark for a nice spot to chill out. Life is too short. 2) On the subject of chair sharking, the cabanas were sold out so you cannot buy your way out of the problem. 3) The hotel needs more tubes for busy weekends. They ran out and people get really weird when this happens. We finally gave in and bought a tube for $10 that our daughter decorated and used all weekend. It was great to have this options but we shouldn't have to do this. 3) Hotel staff (bar/waiters etc) at the pool were not as friendly as the staff in the hotel. A smile and friendly attitude would be nice. 4) Drink prices were really high. I understand it will be a little higher but paying $5 for a diet coke is a little stiff. 
Summary: We will return and this is a great family spot for a summer trip. Just be prepared for crowds in the summer.

title: “My 'go to' hotel when in Dallas on Biz”
text: I travel to Dallas frequently on biz trips (over the past 4yrs) and have stayed in many hotels there.....but the Renaissance has become my hotel of choice. It is conveniently located, has easy ample parking, and has the right mix of service and style to not be stuffy and very comfortable. The staff is top notch and friendly, particularly Erin Dowell and the folks the work in the concierge lounge. Housekeeping, desk, and valet staff have also always been great.

title: “Nice Boutique Hotel”
text: Great hotel in downtown LA. Had a room on the 8th fl facing Library since the building is not that tall views from the room windows are not that great. Roof top pool area was very nice with great views of some of the down town skyline. Hotel bar and Checkers restaurant were very nice. Hotel staff were very professional and friendly. Would recommend this hotel to any one and plan to stay here when I get back to LA.

title: “EXCELLENT HOTEL IN EXCELLENT LOCATION”
text: I spent many months trying to organise my stay at the Crowne Plaza in Times Square as it was my first time to New York and wanted it to be a nice stay for my birthday. My room was beautiful and looked right on to Times Square and I could see the Empire State building as well which was incredible.( Unfortunately I was right next door to the cleaners rooms who were very noisy early in the morning but once they had finished calling out to each other and cleaning all the rooms it was very quiet.) I did request to move but they forgot about it so I just stayed put as it was a very comfortable room other than the early morning noise and I felt very safe in this room, travelling on my own to this incredible city all the way from Australia, was very important to me, they also forgot about my birthday, which was very upsetting, as I had thought someone would have just wished me a Happy Birthday, but unfortunately there were no little niceities like that or friendliness at the Hotel, there was only one staff member who actually said hello to me during my eight day stay. There were a few other little incidents which were very upsetting but on the whole I would still be happy to recommend this hotel to any one thinking of staying there though as you cannot beat the location, straight out the door and Times Square is right there. It is safe and clean and comfortable and a very nice Hotel. Coming from Australia I had never experienced such cold weather, 2 degrees is unheard of in Australia, and after a day out and about I was so happy to get back to the warmth in the Crowne Plaza and back to my beautiful room and just sit and watch the lights on the Empire State Building. I was also lucky enough to be on the Conceirge level which had a lovely lounge area with beautiful views also, it just would have been so nice if the staff had been a little friendlier and kinder to someone who was on their own or to anyone really, it dosnt hurt to ask how was you day or how are you today, or Welcome to the Hotel and of coarse a Happy Birthday would have been so lovely and meant so much, still it was not done on purpose I know how busy they are and they do have excellent Management at the Hotel, if it could just be passed on to the staff who are actually at the Hotel, then it would be a first class Hotel. I do hope to return again with my family. I also wanted to recommend the Addams Family on Broadway it is the most wonderful show with Nathan Lane and Bebe Neuwirth and if you are wondering what show to see this is definately the one and you can purchase your tickets from the Theatre itself, something I didnt realise at the time. After I left New York I went to Hawaii for 14 nights and experienced the best hospitality and when I arrived there was a most beautiful belated birthday/welcome basket left in my room from the Hotel Manager and I was so grateful that my birthday was acknowledged even though it was a few days later, it still meant the world to me. It is the little niceities that are remembered and treasured forever.

title: “Not the Loop but a Great Bargain”
text: I stayed here my second time a while ago and have been pleased both times. The motel seems trapped in the 50s but in a very pleasant, quaint way. The rooms are clean, quiet,and comfortable, and a bargain at 80something dollars. Amenities are few ( wi-fi, a free breakfast, free parking). But if all you want is a place to sleep in Chicago, it's hard to beat. Granted, the motel is way north, but it's a very short drive over to Lake Shore Drive and you can thus be in the middle of the Loop in fifteen-twenty minutes. No complaints here.

title: “A charming experience”
text: This hotel is quite charming and low key. Front desk was friendly and accommodating, the rooms were clean, comfortable (w/ a TV, microwave, and a school boy fridge) and unique. The bathroom could use a fan and curtains for the windows, but that's a minor complaint. There's nothing fancy about this place, but I didn't find it the dump that others think it is. Highly recommend, and would lodge here again.

title: “Highly recommended.”
text:
We stayed in The Royalton for a week in April. The staff were very helpful and friendly. Rooms excellent, and we particulary liked the ipads in the rooms with free internet access. We dined in the hotel restaurant twice and food was of a very high standard and quality. We were also treated to two complimentary cocktails for my birthday! Very nice and excellent customer service. If we visit NYC again, we will definately be staying at Royalton. 
There is a diner across the road - 'Red Flame Diner' that was very good value and kept us full until the evening. 
Very handy for subway stations, Bryant Park, Times Square and shopping!

title: “Don't Bother”
text: We obtained a package deal through the hotel which included Broadway tickets. The total cost was no package. We paid a premium price for a room with two beds and an air conditioning unit that was hanging out of the wall. Our view was of an alley next to a seedy building. The lobby is outdated. When I questioned the price for this basic room, I was told that I "should have done my homework when searching out a NYC hotel." For the price, this was a total disappointment. I will be "doing my homework" and we will not be planning a stay at the Belvedere in Sept. 2011.

title: “This is a delighful place to stay”
text:
Our vist from Leeds, England was extended because of the flight/volcano problems. What should have been 12th to 21st became to the 29th.
Thank goodness we were in this hotel. We cannot fault the help and support we had, the friendliness of all staff, the family atmosphere, the small cosy feel (this is why chose it in the first place) the mini kitchen (unusual for a NY hotel) and the top class restaurant.
There was never a day that we did not feel at home and felt among friends. 
From desk staff to concierges and housekeeping we did not have one single grumble, minor blips were dealt with immediately and believe me they were only minor.
This was our third trip to NY and for the fourth we will certainly choose this hotel.
Congratulations to everyone involved there.
Dave Thomas, Leed, England

title: “Good Value and very friendly”
text: We were going to the Inner Harbor as a family vacation and found this hotel to be perfect. The location was perfect, two blocks from the Harbor we parked the car and left it entirely for our trip. The valet parking was $32.00 a day, but not unreasonable given other location. The staff at this hotel could not be nicer, they were helpful, friendly and really made it a pleasure to stay. The hotel was very nice, rooms were clean, bathrooms were clean and the free breakfast was great to get the day started. We would definately stay there or recommend on another trip to the Inner Harbor.

title: “Extremely inviting experience with excellent sevice.”
text:
When we drove up to the Magic Castle, we were amazed how enchanting the castle looked. We entered the lobby and were greeted by Lisa who was so friendly. Prevoiusly, a few weeks prior we spoke to Marcus, who I really felt badly for., having to deal with two suspious women from New York who thought the hotel sounded too good to be true. He was so patience and sweet. When we first arrived and signed in we were greeted with a orange refreshing beverage.. The room was upgraded to a jr. suite at no extra charge. The rooms were so tranquil with classical music playing.. sweet smelling shampoo and soaps in the bath. Lisa had arranged for the tour bus to pick us up at the hotel, which also was great. Marcus had come in by then and graciously introduced himself, a real gentlemen. He offered us cool cucumber water and plenty of snacks. The strip is a block away, so it pays to leave your car at the hotel and walk.
 Overall I would recommend this hotel, based on availibility of rooms, price ,cleanliness and the friendliness of the staff.

title: “A lot of icing, little cake.”
text: I am having a hard time understanding the positive reviews for this hotel. I guess some people go for image. I was looking forward to a nice stay based on what I had seen on BW website and the reviews here. I was disappointed. This is the type of hotel that has a fancy lobby and nice pictures and decorations throughout the building, but as for substance--lacking. My room was supposedly upgraded to a larger room, but if this was the case I'd hate to see the smaller rooms. The room had fancy colorful furniture, but was small and lacked certain things a higher-priced place like this ($170) should have. There was no hair dryer, no microwave, and I am still not sure if I was using shampoo or some type of lotion (the tube didn't really say clearly). Their windows were stylish, but who cares when the view is lousy and they are small and only open slightly? They have a parking garage, but they make you leave your vehicle for them to park (it costs extra to park) and then if you want to take a drive later, you have to wait for the staff to get it. I did this and it took them a long time to get my car. There is no real parking space, so I had to pull up in front of the hotel in a small space. If there were others wanting in at the same time, someone would have had to park on the street or drive around the block. Also, the location is dull; nothing of real interest withing a couple of blocks all around. There is a restaurant adjoining the hotel, but not owned by the hotel, where I ate dinner. The food was okay but not great. The only really good thing about the hotel was I didn't have to pay for it since it was a business trip.

title: “Loved the Jr. Suite, but had to move from the basic room (simply too small)”
text:
We were booked into a basic room (reservations made by our daughter). Since we had baby-sitting duties, we quickly found that room just too small. The front desk staff were very helpful in moving us to a Jr. Suite on the same floor as our grandchildren -- despite a very full house. The suite was ample and well equipped. I was also very impressed with the business-friendly conditions: computers linked free to printers; free wi-fi throughout the hotel; adjacent English pub/restaurant with reasonable service and adequate menu offering.
The location is excellent: 6 blocks from Millennium Park and the Art Institute; excellent top-flight restaurants in easy walking distance; 1 1/2 blocks from the Blue subway that connects to O-Hare.
Bottom line: good location at a value price with all the business amenities. A real bargain!

title: “loved it!”
text:
We moved to the Milano after a very disapointing one night stay elsewhere. For the same price we got a clean, quiet, spacious room and excellent help from the staff. The difference was like night and day. 
We'll definately return. Your best value in downtown San Francisco.

title: “Fantastic location and very quiet”
text:
Great location, very quiet rooms which is brilliant for Manhattan. Rooms are small but well equipped. Staff are ver helpful and friendly.
The Red Lantern restaurant next door is a terrific NY diner.

title: “Terrific Experience!”
text: Our room was recently renovated, spacious and comfortable. The bathroom impeccably clean and thoughtfully appointed. We were amazed at how well we slept- heard minimal NY night sounds and the room darkening shades allowed us to sleep in a bit! The location is very convenient for walking and subway rides to anywhere. We found plenty of great restaurants right nearby. All staff we encountered were pleasant and helpful. We will definately stay here whenever we travel to NYC!

title: “Parking was Outrageous! $48.00 per night”
text: Although I slept just fine in my hotel room...I was shocked that the parking is $48.00 a night-FYI.

title: “Good stay over a weekend in August”
text:
Booked a 3-night stay over a weekend in August for a tourist trip for me and my senior-citizen Mom. Booked a 2-bed room and requested a higher floor for street noise suppression based on other reviews here on TA, and the property was able to secure one for me (not sure if my HH Diamond status helped that or now), and it worked out well...room was quiet at that level. In room fridge/microwave were appreciated and well-used. Beds, bathroom, and climate control were all good.
My Mom suffered a back injury the morning of our 3rd day and we had to check out a day early; the front desk handled that with no problem/issue and also had no problem crediting my unused HH points which I had used to pay for this trip (again, not sure if my HH Diamond status helped on that front or not, but it was handled well). The restaurant also was very helpful to me in facilitating a to-go order so that I could bring breakfast up for my Mom.
The property offers no self-parking option and $35/day for the valet service (plus applicable tips, of course), but this seems to be the norm for most hotels in the downtown core from what my shopping around of other properties revealed. The location of this property can't be beat...walking distance to all the key DC attractions and McPherson Square Metro station directly across the street.
The only nit/glitch we encountered was that the hallway air conditioning (and apparently the A/C in the front lobby as well) malfunctioned on our last morning, making for a sweaty checkout and luggage loading process; luckily this problem did not extend to inside the guest rooms or that would have been disastrous.
I would definitely patronize this property in the future.

title: “Do not accept Room 516!”
text:
We had booked to stay seven nights for a vacation in Chicago. Having saved on the the flights we decided to upgrade our hotel to the Omni. On arrival we were allocated room 516. This has to be the worst room in the hotel. There is a sundeck on floor 5 meaning directly outside our windows people were walking by all day - absolutely no privacy. Then the gym is directly next door to the room and is noisy. Add to that the wireless internet didn't work. And finally the hotels own music starts playing outside the hotel at 5am and you can clearly hear it in the room.
Why would a hotel who has guests staying for seven nights put them in such a bad room? Of course we were going to complain - they must have known that? So guess what I am now telling the world to avoid the 5th floor at this hotel at all costs.
The next morning we did complain about the room. The receptionist said she could do nothing about it until we had spoken to the manager. Whilst they offered to phone us we felt it would be too easy for them to reject our request for a move over the phone. After waiting an hour in the lobby we approached the desk again. This time the other receptionist said that she could authorise the request to move. Why the first receptionist hadn't asked the second is anyone's guess? It's a great example how one poor or poorly trained member of staff can affect the reputation of the entire hotel.
When we were moved (to the 20th floor) the room was fine. 
On departure there was an item on the bill from the room bar that we hadn't used. This was removed without fuss but shouldn't have been on the bill in the first place. Also on checkout the receptionist on duty mentioned that if we joined the loyalty program we could get our internet for free. Since one of the reasons for wanting to move rooms was the Internet why had none of the other staff mentioned this. We signed up and the charge was credited to our account.
Marco, I'm not sure what you do in your hour long stand up meetings each day? But it doesn't seem to be providing consistent and good customer service at the front desk. There were just too many errors on the customer service side to recommend this hotel.

title: “Great Location”
text: Modern uninspiring on the outside, pretty nice on the inside. Wide & busy lobby lacking however any sitting area to do any people watching. Room was clean and decent size and so was the bathroom. The best feature is the location a couple of blocks from Central Park and Rockefeler Plaza and very close to MOMA (Modern Art Museum). If your looking for something very classy w/ character try the Waldorf Astoria also a Hilton (we stayed there the following week) or if visiting Lower Manhattan try the Millenium Hilton right across from Ground Zero close to Wall Street and Battery Park, a favorite w/ reviewers on this site.

title: “Everything but the cleanliness of the carpet edges was great.”
text: I loved the uniqueness and the character of the hotel. It was a very pleasant stay and I would recommend the Adolphus to others. Please just play more attention to the carpets (especially around moldings and door edges). All employees were pleasant, professional and helpful.

title: “GREAT HOTEL CENTRAL LOCATION AND VALUE”
text: We stayed at Copley Square Hotel last week. It is 2 mins from Prudential Centre and 5 minutes from all major attractions. The room was spotless, quality furnishings and bedlinen. Newspaper delivered every morning. No coffee in room but free in lobby. Wine tasting every evening at 5pm to 6pm. The room was not overly large but suburb quality. We had Queen Room, large shower. Highly recommend. We stayed 4 nights with 1 night free. The Hotel is modern with a bar attached which is always busy. Restaurant and Breakfast a bit expensive. Would go back.

title: “The service was outstanding!”
text: We went during a rainstorm and spent most of the time in the hotel. When the rain let up just enough, the staff was extremely accomodating and helpful in finding things for us to do. While we were indoors, everyone made a great effort to make our stay comfortable and enjoyable. We highly recommend this hotel, if not for the service alone, but the rest of the hotel is pretty good too!

title: “Fabulous and relaxing hotel!!”
text: My sister and I stayed in this hotel for a getaway in the first part of March. Hotel Vitale exceeded our expectations. It is a beautiful hotel and really gives you that "spa" feel. The small touches from lavender in the halls, great turn down service, lighting and room furnishing were just what we were looking for. The staff was great and very accomodating to help us with our late check out. We had massages in the spa which were out of this world relaxing. As two young women we felt very safe here and looked forward to returning to our hotel each night. The location was great across from the Ferry Building and it was wonderful to be able to easily cross the street for phenomenal coffee, sandwiches and gelato. It is also close to transportation. Also special thanks to the concierge (Jerry?) for helping me ship purchased wine home. We will be back!

title: “OK Hotel.....”
text:
We a family of four stayed for 4 nights in this hotel. The room looked very nice and trendy but was very small and the washroom was not the best... "There was an incomplete translucent glass window is all that stands between the toilet and the room. Taking a leak ? Indigestion ? Gas ? Your companion will hear every detail. Also no shower doors, so the toilet floor gets soaked" I stole this quote from a fellow traveller and I agree, in fact that water getting on the washroom floor was quite dangerous. The hotel has the nerve to charge 4.50 for a diet coke, really outrageous and in my opinion plain greedy. Love the location, and found some bakeries and restaurants in the area that we much cheaper and just as nice in the area.
The other aspect that I did not like was the pool was 5 blocks away at the Marriott which was a shame.

title: “Excellent hotel at prime location”
text: Fine hotel, very nice and spacious rooms, good services (business center, fitness). Cleaning was done well and promptly. One remakr is that they did not re-fill the mini bar during my stay but that is not really a big issue.

title: “University Place”
text: If you need a hotel near the hospital chain this is a very nice, clean hotel. It is a bit out of the way from downtown (approx. 1 mile) but generally $5 bucks in a cab will get you there. The only real downfall I believe was some rudeness from the front desk.

title: “Quiet and comfortable”
text:
Two beds and a pull-out couch, plus a refrigerator and desk made this a perfect room for three of us. The room was clean, beds were comfortable - soft (but not too soft!) with cozy bed covers. Flat screen TV with a clear picture enhanced our Olympic viewing experience. Daily breakfast was good quality, but without a large variety of food choices. Great to have Starbucks on site, but there was no soy milk available, so we didn't get to experience it. The pool was not very inviting; small, odd shaped, and cloudy. A few minor drawbacks, but overall a good choice.
We used points to stay here so can't really say much about the cost.

title: “Good for an overnight”
text:
Stayed May 30 - June 1st, 2008 with my husband and two children ages 8 & 6 years old.
The good-easy access to I-10 (can see it but can't hear it); decent continental breakfast in a good size room; comfortable beds and pillows; laundry facilities available; stairway between parking lots connects you to Rudy's - great place to eat!
The bad-Housekeeping only emptied one wastebasket; hairdryer vent needs to be cleaned; need to update electrical outlets - not enough for all our gadgets to recharge; toilet wouldn't shut off after being flushed; not much space to walk around.
Good for one night.

title: “Great stay!”
text:
Elegant lobby, excellent service. 
(Although we had a charge on our bill that didn't belong there, but getting it removed was no problem at all.)
Comfortable beds, clean room, great location.
After having read some previous reviews, we were wondering how our stay would be, but I guess it might depend on where your room was located. We were on the 21st floor and it was great!

title: “Great weekend getaway”
text:
I love it! I will definitely be back(: 
Its close to the zoo, beach & downtown.

title: “Convenient for Universal Studios”
text: A standard Hilton with nice big rooms and a decent size pool. Parking is not free (this is LA!) and you walk or take a shuttle (free) to Universal Studios. Bar is nice although a little expensive. Rooms were comfortable and the large windows/views (of the freeway/hills) good. Elevators seemed to have a mind of their own and can take a while to stop at your floor.

title: “practical, great location, cozy”
text:
The hotel was situated in a great area close to the arts district (Broad St.). It was super easy to find and has a lot of character. It is a boutique hotel--so no business center or gym although they do give you gym pass for one nearby if you ask. Paid parking is across the street from the hotel, but the attendant is not the nicest--rather sarcastic and rude. I parked at the lot one block down from the lot in front of the hotel (between 13th and 14th on Locust). The attendant was amazing and parking was less expensive ($15/day). They do not have a restaurant yet, one will be opening soon and that'll be exciting--the prospect of a hot breakfast. In the meantime they deliver continental type breakfast to your room at whatever time you dictate which is convenient and nice. Free wifi! Free tea/coffee/hot chocolate and fruit in the lobby, I was there for a conference so I frequently got coffee to go on my way out which was awesome. My conference was at the Marriott and convention center--safe good walk (about 6 blocks). Amazing area for shopping along 13th St. heading toward the Marriott with a lot of trendy good restaurants and actually all the streets around. Close to Pine St. where you can find amazing antiques (Between 13th and 11th on Pine). Friendly staff although I wish they would've smiled more :). Cozy room, I stayed in 301 queen room, it faces Locust St. which can get loud at night so bring ear plugs. Wish I could've caught the wine and cheese nights but forgot when they were so I'd go down on occasion--but alas missed them.
Single woman travelling, I felt completely safe in this area of the city. Hotel is on the same block as the train line--super close easy access...but if its nice out, walking is lovely.
Would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone going to Philly!

title: “Refused to change reservation due to death in the family”
text:
I reserved this hotel through an online booking service with a rate that was not refundable or changeable. That's fine, I understand that certain low rates come with restrictions and limitations. However, the hotel refused a request to change my arrival date by 2 days so I could attend my father's funeral. I think this shows an astounding lack of sensitivity or customer service - how can you stand behind corporate policy to this degree? I don't know if the Indigo hotel management could not or would not make a change - or if it was an Intercontinental corporate order.
Regardless, I will never again stay at any Intercontinental property and urge you to avoid them as well.

title: “Quiet gem”
text: What a lovely hotel. The front desk staff was nice enough and the bar was rockin' when we arrived. Restaurant/bar area seems to be quite the place to party for the 20 somethings. Rooms are very clean and the Tempur-pedic beds are perfect! Our balcony opened up to the water and overlooked the tower deck. A delightful place. We'll recommend it and visit again.

title: “Changed my view of Washington from negative to positive”
text: These people deserve some serious respect. Ted, H, Jersey, Helena, Pat and the rest of the team made this one of the most enjoyable and relaxing stays in a capital city I have ever experienced. Excellent food, which stands alongside the best restaurants in the world, no hassle, total chill, but attentive when required (find me another hotel in the world that will find a guest tequilla and cigarettes at 2am)The Amnesia Bar is a "Concept" that delivers!But seriously, if you want to unwind in a nice atmosphere, if you love art and music, if you hate business hotels, if you love life, this is the place for you. I will never stay anywhere else in Washington!! I have 10 other collegues who will say the same!Cheers steveb

title: “Dirty old hotel rooms”
text: Come on - Stains on the carpet and stains on the office chair? really???? all for the low price of $250 per night - what a bargain!! The lobby and conference area is fine. Everything else was disgusting and they should not be renting these rooms out for these rates. The reveiws here said to ask for a newly renovated room. The clerk told me they are all the same and recently renovated. Ha! Ha!

title: “Location, Service, Food: Excellent”
text: Well maintained hotel in the center of a great city - helpful staff, delicious food. Attended a conference which went off well with all the added assistance. Had a nice work-out area. Would recommend it to others.

title: “A NYC treasure!”
text: We stayed here from 11/8 to 11/13 and had a great experience. The room was comfortable and clean. The staff were helpful. The cost (for NY) was reasonable. We had a fridge and microwave. A huge Food Emporium is a block away. We walked to Broadway shows (Book of Morman and The Heiress) and Times Square. The restaurant in the hotel is a fabulous French restaurant. We had breakfasts andcother meals there. We have stayed in many hotels. This was one of the best experiences we have ever had!

title: “Loved the Wingate Inn, Will return”
text:
First trip to NYC (07/05-07/08)as a Birthday surprise for my Husband. We had a great time. The Wingate Inn is a very nice hotel with friendly staff, extremely clean rooms, and a great location! The street that the hotel is located on is dead after dark, there is nothing open, but once you get to the end of the street closest to Macy's, there is a Starbucks, McDonalds and all kinds of little places to stop for a quick bite. Very close to Subway and taxis are everywhere. Walking distance to Macy's, Time Square, Empire State building, Penn Station, Madison Square Garden, etc.
The hotel was very quite, with only 6 rooms to a floor, we always had a good-night's sleep. We did get an early morning wake up by a trash truck, but that happens at home too.
Breakfast in the morning was great and very convenient. The breakfast room was a bit small and crowded at times, but here's a hint: go down early, make your plate, and take it to your room, that way you avoid the line at the waffle irons.
The manager, Elvis, was most helpful!!! Kudos to him and his staff. He was always there, I wonder if he ever goes home, LOL. He was always available to suggest a great restaurant or other points of interest. We will definitely return to the Wingate Inn!!!
P.S. If you like Mexican Food, checkout Mi Nidito near the Times Square Area. A nice quaint little restaurant with a great atmosphere, great music, Best Margaritas and food!!! If you have the Margaritas, be careful, you will get drunk!!! LOL

title: “My favorite NYC hotel”
text: This hotel ticked every box for us. Friendly, helpful staff. Quiet. Clean. Elegant but chic decor - lots of muted colors, dark wood, granite. (The only thing that didn't make sense was the glass panel on the bathroom door. It's frosted, but still awkward if you bring guests up for a drink. This is not an enormous problem, but something to be aware of when you use your room for potty breaks when you're hanging out with friends touring the city.) It's a little pricey, but this level of accommodations with all the extras - free continental breakfast (w/ hard boiled eggs), lemon ice water, tea & coffee in the lobby all day, happy hour menu, free wifi, 2 bottles of water at turn-down, gym pass (though I didn't use this) - are worth it. The rooftop bar is a fantastic spot for resting between activities. The staff up there are also wonderful. We were treated very well. We highly recommend and would stay again.

title: “Top drawer hotel in a great location....”
text:
Everything you read about this place is true - it is first class all the way. The staff are wonderful - so friendly and helpful but not stuffy at all. The facility is immaculate and the rooms are totally over the top. I had a Premier Park Deluxe room which was the size of an apartment. The bathroom with the open air rain shower was the best.
This hotel is 5 star all the way - if you are looking for a low-key approach to luxury it can't be beat.
One thing I will mention that surprised me about it was that the location is a lot better than you might think for leisure travelers. I had the impression it was amidst a mostly commercial area that was dead at night - it's actually much more residential and an extremely short walk to all that Georgetown has to offer. The Foggy Bottom Metro station is also a brief walk away and can get you to the Nat'l Mall/Downtwon area very easily.
Overall - I hope to stay here again - it was sad to leave!

title: “Fantastic!”
text: We loved it! The staff was wonderful and very attentive. The room was spatious, clean, and very comfortable. It was a fantastic stay!

title: “Thoroughly unimpressed”
text: While the hotel is obviously new, modern, and well designed, the management clearly has not put ANY effort into their guests' experience or training their staff. I arrived late at night at 11pm and was met at reception by a woman who could best be described as 'sullen'. There was no mention of having anyone helping me with my bags, either at the valet station or in the lobby. While my room was spacious and the bed comfortable, the heat was cranked up to 75 degrees -- it was nearly 2am before the room cooled down enough for me to fall asleep. Despite the fact that I hadn't requested a wake-up call or ordered breakfast room service, someone started banging down my door at 6:45am. (After a late night of travel, I had no intention of getting up before 8am before a busy day of meetings.) I assumed they had the wrong room and stayed in bed. Much knocking and door bell ringing ensued, followed by an angry phone call and a member of staff rudely telling me to open the door for room service. I told them I hadn't ordered room service, asked why they were insistent on waking me up, and they actually had the nerve to start arguing with me! As I was leaving for meetings at 9am, I mentioned this to the concierge, and while he was apologetic, made no offer to compensate for my poor night's sleep. Even a 2-star Hilton Garden Inn would have offered a free drink at the bar in apology! For a 4.5-star-wannabe hotel, a bottle of wine sent to my room would have a been appropriate at a minimum. When I returned between meetings briefly at 2pm my room had not been made-up. By 4pm, it finally had been, but with dirty towels left on the bathroom floor and garbage in the trash can -- an extremely lazy job. Forget simple niceties such as balt salts or shower gel, or even fluffy towels for that matter... Enjoy a flower in the bud vase or a chocolate on your pillow? Despite the price, it ain't happening! The newness of the furnishings can't make up for a BARE MINIMUM EFFORT when it comes service and guest experience.

title: “Good family hotel”
text: Stayed in a queen suite- like a small apartment, very convenient and pretty good value for this area. Pool area is nice though was pretty crowded during our stay. The hotel is not really close to any attractions but is centrally located so its not hard to drive to wherever you might want to go in the area.

title: “great stay at the W New York”
text: We stayed at the W New York and we had a great time. Our cozy room was small, but we knew that when we booked. Everything was very well laid out and it was fine seeing that you don't spend much time in the room. It was spotless and the bath products were fantastic. This hotel is in a very good location. We were about a 10 minute walk to Times Square and we were just up the street from Bloomingdale's. There is plenty of shoppin on Lexington and lots of great places to eat Nearby. The only negative would be that the music in the lounge was quite loud in the evening.

title: “Excellent Riverwalk Property”
text: Great hotel close to all the riverwalk action. Hotel staff was friendly and very quick upon arrival allowing us to check-in 90 min's early. The rooms are all suites and very large, big enough to entertain people. Bedroom is separate with a King Bed or 2 Queens. The main area has a sofa bed, plenty of seating, a 4 seat dining table and mini refrigerator/microwave The free breakfast was amazing, hot and cold items galore. Managers reception was great, free beer :).

title: “Good hotel, just plan for extra time to park”
text: My partner and I visited this hotel in late October on a Saturday night for an event in Dallas and stayed the night to avoid having to drive home in the middle of the night. The hotel room was clean, roomy, quiet and the beds were comfortable. The restaurants and bar in the hotel, while pricey (which is to be expected) were quite good. The only minus to the hotel is that it is a convention hotel. If you are staying here when there are sporting events going on (this weekend there was a World Series game and a football game happening) as well as weddings or conventions, the parking can quickly become problematic. The valet parking is $22 a night and when the hotel is crowded for events, it quickly becomes the only option. They will retrieve your car as quickly as they can, but a visitor to the hotel needs to be aware that they should add 30 minutes to their schedule whenever they need to drop off or pick up their car so that they will not be late. Fortunately I read the review of another visitor on this site and it warned me to pad my schedule and his advice was what allowed us to get to our event on time without any difficulties. Aside from the crowded parking, the hotel is a great place to stay in a very good location in downtown Dallas.

title: “This place almost ruined my bachelor weekend :(”
text:
To start this off, let me just say I wish my best man would've booked our group of 8 at a Motel 6 instead of this place. BEWARE of the pictures on this site, the professional photographs DO NOT portray the condition these rooms are in. That is because there are no pictures of the rooms! We booked 2 rooms for 2 nights with double "queen" beds for around $450.
Once we arrived, which was around 10:30 P.M., (our group hit the casinos on I-35 on the way down here), we tried paying with cash, and were told that they do not take cash after 10:30 P.M. due to safety concerns, and I quote the night manager, "for personal preference." When we were told this, we reluctantly sucked it up and still put both nights on the original reservation maker's card. We requested 2 rooms by each other, (the place was had to be around 10-20% capacity), but they chose to stick us across the hallway from each other on the 7th floor. Again, we sucked it up, hoping to just enjoy the weekend after realizing we were only going to be sleeping at this place, inebriated, after 3 A.M. anyways...Once we started making the trek to our rooms, we start realizing how musty and thick the air was in this place. To compound on that, it was extremely cramped, one of the group members said he felt claustrophobic and the hallways looked like the inside of the Titanic, the part where Leonardo Dicaprio's kind was allowed to stay.
We get to our rooms, open the door, and it was like humidity slapped us in our faces. The room's temp was around 80 in both rooms! We tried kicking on the A/C in one room, but the unit just continued to make a constant clicking sound and wouldn't fully kick on the cold air. In the second room, the A/C unit had wires coming out of the bottom of it that were laying on the floor by one of the beds. We tried to give it a chance, but after cranking the temperature down to 64, the room never got below 75...The complimentary trays that include the coffee, cups, etc., were extremely dusty and obviously hadn't been touched by a guest or a maid in weeks...The beds DO NOT come with comforters. They have a bottom sheet, a blanket in between that and another top sheet. That was a bit shocking to me as well, since the picture they do have on their site has a beautiful bed with a nice green comforter and neat pillow covers. Again, this was very misleading. They also state on the site that they can comfortably fit 4 people in a room on their site, we had trouble putting our 4 bags on the floor to allow enough room to walk around without hopping over the "queen beds"...I put apostrophes around queen beds to emphasize sarcasm...They were twin, maybe full beds. 4 dudes, 2 twin beds, you do the math.
A patron in our group decided to call and report the broken A/C. He first requested a refund due to the complete misrepresentation of the rooms on www.hotellawrence.com, we were promptly denied and they did not offer a refund for the second night either. Frustrated, he then asked to be changed rooms at least, and if so, asked if we could again be moved as a group, since our A/C unit was not operating well, our room was dirty and was very unkempt. They denied this request. But that sweetheart up front sure did offer us the "Loft" rooms for $400 a night to get a comforter on our beds! We then changed our clothes after getting situated in the rooms and went to talk to the front desk.
I went with the cardholder, and the person who called in about the broken A/C units. I wanted to go down and just ask a few polite, but direct questions. I first asked if they had a policy they could show me that says they could not take cash, (we planned on leaving and disputing the charge with our banks for buying services we did not receive), and she stated that it is hotel policy and her preference. She did NOT answer yes or no. I repeated my question, and then she started to get what seemed to be offended. After she answered no, they do not have a policy anywhere, she said she didn't have to have one, which may be true. She then told me she should not be talking to me, but instead should be talking to the cardholder, since both rooms were in his name! The nerve! I guess I just ask the hard questions? I was still a guest and should've been treated as such. She then threatened to kick us out, told me I should've called her if I had a problem with my room, instead of coming down to the desk to talk...ummm...She called me a jerk as well...Dirt of my shoulders really...It still infuriates me to know this place does business though. We ended up grabbing our bags around midnight after that front desk debacle and left. Didn't even say a word to the front desk. We decided to take it up with the bank after the weekend and let them handle the hotel.
For the record, I did say it was for a bachelor weekend, but we hadn't had a sip of alcohol before we checked in, and we believe we were mistreated just for the type of group that we were, (a bunch of twenty-somethings visiting a town for a good weekend). They wanted us to pay nearly $450 to stay there for the 2 nights, wouldn't refund us, tried kicking us out, called us jerks and were completely rude. 
We then proceeded to stay at a hotel about 2 blocks down on Lamar St., called the Omni. It cost twice the price of the Hotel Lawrence, valet cost $28 a night, but I didn't bat an eye at putting a card down on MY bachelor weekend for the Omni for 2 nights, IT WAS FANTASTIC! 
For all that is good on this planet, PLEASE, PLEASE, DO NOT STAY AT HOTEL LAWRENCE. YOU'VE BEEN WARNED.

title: “Nothing Special”
text:
We recently stayed at this hotel for a weekend trip.
