Overall, the hotel was just alright, as the location is fairly convenient, but after saying that, if you find any hotel in the downtown area, it will be convenient.
The hotel is clean, the staff is pretty friendly, and the rooms are very small, especially the bathroom, which was terribly small.
Our air conditioning unit wasn't barely working and it was pretty loud at night. The elevators are very slow as well. 
I am not sure if there is free wireless internet service but there is one computer for public use.
Anyway, if the was price is right, i'd stay there again but this wouldn't be my first choice.

title: “Pretty but impractical rooms”
text: This is an old hotel that has been remodeled into a trendy looking Kimpton. Very pleasing decor, and nice staff but impractical for sleeping. Currently under renovation and finding the door to even get into the hotel is a challenge. No parking but valet. No restaurant currently but many in the area. They offered a very basic and free continental breakfast with some fruit and pastries but by the time we made it to the lobby right before time was up at 9:30 a.m. (on a weekend - it would have been nice if time was later), there wasn't much left. The happy hour is nice but no alternative beverages if you or someone traveling with you does not want or cannot drink wine or beer. They had water but nothing else. Room was lovely to look at but not for sleeping in. Large gap under the door so lots of hallway noise. Air Conditioner never cooled the room well even though we kept setting it lower and it turned on and off sporadically with lots of noise that made it difficult to sleep. Lights all around the outside windows so the glow comes into your room all night around the edges of the drapes. No tub - only a huge shower that you could fit 2 or 3 people in with one of the rain heads that look nice but do not work well for bathing or shampooing. No place to put your legs to shave. Pretty but flat sink that splashes water everywhere and can't be used for much. Fridge with pricey juices and a basket of pricey snacks on top ($5.00 or more for a granola bar or a bag of M & M's - go to the drugstores nearby or bring your own!). This could be a pricey problem for parents with kids or teens who help themselves before they realize the cost (listed on a small card laying on top) of all those drinks and snacks that appear to be free for the taking! Or try to explain to the kids the "intimacy kit" laying in that basket! Then the beds - huge wooden platform with a mattress on top. First you hit your shins on those corners every time you try to walk around them and then the mattress slides all over the place. When you try to sleep you realize they are hard as rock since there is no box spring! Rooms are very small so not much space for sitting or anything else. Wanted to like the hotel and the location is great for SMU but there are much better hotels with more room and better beds for a lower price a short drive away.

title: “Good suites, so-so business services, funny tween girls”
text: I stayed at the W because it was the most convenient in the vicinity for a business trip that offered the meeting facilites we needed. The suites are big and comfortable. Good beds, good showers, etc. The business side is a bit iffy. We told them we needed to stream video to someone, for which they charged a substantial fee. The meeting rooms were large enough and comfortable enough, but the lighting is somewhat dim. I can only guess that hangovers and dissipated appearances dictate soft low lighting? But the necessary arrangements were not in place at the appointed hour. Little things that require minimal investment, like high speed printing and copying, are not on offer and there is no real business center. But I must say the conference catering was quite good. Another letdown was slow elevator service in the early morning because on lift is used for freight service. Not a good thing at a busy time for us. Overall, service was better than average, but somewhat irregular. On the bright side, some boy band was staying there, so we were treated to the spectacle of screeching, rampaging tween girls which added some high humor to the visit.

title: “Jewel hotel in quiet area but short walking distance to Times Square”
text: I stayed in December 2011 with 2 girlfriends. Booked a 2 bed apartment with kitchen facilities and a fantastic view overlooking Chrysler building on 32nd Floor. Found the staff to be very pleasant, especially the doormen. It is in a superb location as it is within walking distance to all major attractions. Central Park was probably the furthest we walked to but still took only 35 mins with plenty to see and enjoy on the way. The hotel bar was quite expensive, as are most of the bars in New York, but the food served was reasonably priced and of a very good standard. The rooms were very well serviced, clean and comfortable and the addition of the kitchenette was an added bonus - but do bring your own tea bags and coffee/hot chocolate sachets. Next door is a great little Irish bar with an exterior balcony which was very popular when we were there. The Organic Amish supermarket and deli cafe was the best find just up the street - you could buy takeout or sit and eat. Fantastic quality and choice for hot and cold food and very big portions - not for the faint hearted unless you share. We had lunch then ordered the most superb sandwiches for the flight back to the UK - the other passengers were drooling when they saw our feast! Plenty of restaurants within walking distance for breakfast lunch or dinner. We did the Greenwich Village/Soho walking food tour which was the highlight of our trip - so interesting and rich variety of food intake and culture. I am planning to come back to New York in the summer of 2012 with the family and will return to The Alex as it is ideally located and quiet bearing in mind it is in the middle of the action and the hotel facilities were extremely good as were the staff. Highly recommended.

title: “Superb European Style Hotel for an Excellent Value.”
text: We had the pleasure of staying at this jewel of the Pacific Northwest the night before our cruise last week. We were pleasantly surprised to find that the hotel also offered a complimentary pick up and departure in a luxury vehcile with driver; a definite bonus. The checkin was seamless and we were graciously welcomed by Desmond, the Head Concierge with an early checkin. Not sure whether it was due to Perfect Escapes or Desmond taking a shine to us but we were upgraded to a full one bedroom corner suite which was lovely. The hotel had an old world elegance with superb bedding, a marble bathroom and a very comfortable living room. The restaurant was as elegant as the hotel was charming and the food very tasty. We were however told that the "Continental Breakfast" included in our package enabled us to order anything off the menu, but when we checked out, we discoverd there was a $25 maximum sand had to pay extra. Thus we were mislead about that by someone. The hotel was still lovely tho.

title: “Nice Little Hotel for Price”
text: Nice little Hotel. Area was very nice full of Restaurents and Shopping. Room very comfortable, nice beddings and free bottle water everyday... Wow. Breakfast got all the options and it's free. Staff very helpful too. I will go back any time...........

title: “Don't Bother Staying Here”
text: We were eager to stay here, reading the hotel reviews. We had previously stayed in the Hay Adams and were expecting even more from the Willard. Although the lobby was beautiful, the people friendly, rooms spacious although dated, the overall experience was less than pleasant. The doormen did not greet you or help with bags. To call a cab, was beyond their duties. We returned in the rain, and I had to jump out and get the umbrella for my wife. We asked for wake up calls, which never came. Breakfast looked much better than it tasted. The service was terrible. First the eggs, then the toast five minutes later, and was delivered cold and toasted on one side. The package included a food allowance, but with such bad food it was useless. On the plus side, the maid service was excellent, the rooms clean and the concierge was most helpful. But, for us, it is back to the Hay Adams.

title: “40th birthday bash for the boys!”
text: This hotel is superior. From the personal service to the cleanliness of the rooms and common areas. There is very little to be desired in the way of personal service. The Front end manager Farrell Sledge was top notch in his service. He went above and beyond the "usual" service. The beds are fantastic.

title: “Great hotel, will stay again.”
text: I just came back from a stay at the Andra. Wonderful boutique hotel. I was getting a little worried from some of the negative reviews but found my stay very nice. Staff was nice, frette towels, starbucks coffee, new york times paper daily, FACE bath amenities. Nice modern decor. The only thing that needed work was the bathroom floor - it needs a good bleaching and scrubbing. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Satisfied”
text: The location was close enough to walk to Times Square easily. The rooms were nice and clean.

title: “Love the bed...it's so comfortable.”
text:
We stayed here, because Parc 55 was overbooked (we originally made reservations here). Thankfully we had another option for a place to stay, because I wouldn't know what to do if that were to happen. When it was time for us to bed, I fell asleep right away. I usually wake up in the middle of the night & at one point thought I was home. I like this hotel & it would be nice to have a chance to stay here again.
There was some noise, but it was ok.

title: “Beautiful Hotel- Exceptional Service”
text: This hotel is simply beautiful! We recieved amazing service from the moment we pulled into the driveway! The rooms are beautifully set out and very spacious with simply gorgeous decor! We were lucky to have a balcony looking over Beverly Hills which was very nice at sunset and to sit for a couple of drinks! The hotel had a very relaxing feel! I didnt want to leave! It is expensive but very high quality- I believe we got what we paid for :)

title: “Great hotel and outstanding location”
text:
I lucked out and got Le Parker Meridien through Priceline for two nights...so i actually didn't know the specific hotel until i purchased it ...needless to say the price of this upscale midtown manhattan hotel was really more than reasonable and i was very happy with the way things turned out....The room was just fine...maybe a little smaller than those in less congested areas but -- come on -- have you ever been to hotels in Europe or Japan (talk about small rooms !)... There was construction going in a building adjacent to the lobby so it was very noisy there...and i was a little concerned... but 35 floors has a remarkable effect on dampening out any such noises.... it was quiet as could be...not even street noise....
Needless to say the hotel is in a wonderful location...a gazzilion restaurants around...(but don't forget to check out either the Carnegie or Stage Delis nearby for overwhelmingly large and delicious sandwiches, desserts, etc...put your diet on hold !)....The bathroom was clean and perhaps renovations had been done recently but i found everything just fine (large flat screen tv's ,etc....). Kinda wished that they had a coffee maker in the room -- but no such luck..... The maid service was excellent ... and the view from 35 stories up was lovely....

title: “Great size for New York”
text: Great base with good location and specious rooms for New York. Check in was kind of slow but very welcoming. This is a good hotel for what we paid.

title: “Amazing hotel”
text:
Great hotel, very nice staff, great location, great bar and restaurant.
The wine tasting at 5pm everyday is really making the customer comfy.
I just loved my 4 days there.
And I discovered my best cocktail ever made by Mike at the Sable Bar : try the Boulevardier (if you like bitter).
Will come again !

title: “Perfect location - closest to Boston medical”
text: Hampton inn crosstown Boston is the closest hotel to Boston medical. My husband and I have stayed there on many occasions for his visits to Boston medical center. The hotel is very clean, the staff is friendly and very accommodating and includes a nice breakfast and a shuttle although we generally walk less than one block. I would highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Excellent hotel in really convenient midtown location”
text:
We stayed here for 7 nights in September 2012 and had an excellent experience. 
The room was large (we paid for a room with 2 queensize beds) and with a decent size bathroom. Staff were helpful and friendly. While the bedroom looked a little bit tired in places (some chipped paint, some staining in the bathroom) it was very clean and it's nothing that would stop me staying here in the future. We had a little bit of traffic noise from the street, but no worse than I'd expect for Manhattan.
One of the biggest plus points for the hotel is its brilliant location. It's about 3 blocks to Grand Central station which is really convenient for the subway and which has lots of options for grabbing breakfast / coffees. There's not a huge amount going on in the blocks immediately around the hotel but it's so easy to get the subway at Grand Central (or if you want to go downtown there's also a stop at 33rd street for the 6 Train). You can also walk very easily to some of the attractions around midtown - it's about 10 minutes to the Empire State Building, 10 minutes to Bryant Park, 15 minutes to Times Square / Broadway etc. 
If you join the Kimpton loyalty scheme I think you can also get free wifi in the room and $15 from the minibar.
Great hotel and I would highly recommend it for midtown.

title: “The Twilight Zone”
text:
This was, by far, the strangest place I have ever stayed. I was first struck by the trendy (and cool) facade that lacked any indication that I was at the right place (no name on the building, no address on the door). I was told by a staff member that this was to increase curiosity and draw people in. Once I got in, I wanted nothing more than to get out.
Let me elaborate. I like to be pampered, but pampering I did not get. Instead, I got a tiny room with just inches between the wall and the bed. I got funky lights (decorated with nightmarish body parts) that worked only half the time. I got a hidden thermostat, requiring a secret trick to access (many thanks to the wonderful housekeeper who took pity on me while I was freezing and shared the secret). I got a television almost too small to see, that would not stay off. Really. I'd turn it off, and a few seconds later it would come back on. No one seemed to be able to fix it. I got a tiny bathroom with only a sheer curtain to separate it from the rest of the room (okay, there was a door, but there was no wall between it and the rest of the room. I had to close the shower curtain for privacy). I got some weird metal tray, which looked like a soap holder, sticking out of the wall, which injured me as I tried to walk past it (was it for a housekeeper's tip?). I got a tiny bedside table just big enough for a phone, and a little stool underneath it that I pulled out to use for my water glass. Nothing else would fit on it. I got a hallway that made me feel like I was on my way to my execution. I got no towel racks, save the little buttons sticking out of the wall. I got no ice bucket. I got no drawers. I got no blankets, until I called housekeeping. What I did get, however, was good service from the staff. They made my stay somewhat bearable.
The lobby is trendy and cool. The bars are okay, but overpriced and meat-markety (I truly thought I was going to be able to read in the library; much to my chagrin, it was just a trendy pub, albeit with hilarious photos of cows in stylish hats).
Overall, this place is just plain strange. It is uncomfortable and overpriced. Luckily, my friend and I had a good laugh at each new eccentricity we found. However, I will NEVER set foot in the place again.

title: “Excellent hotel with a good rate!!!”
text: My husband and I along with my daughter and her friend stayed at the Homewood Suites for 2 nights while on a trip to San Diego. I booked it based on the reviews on Tripadvisor. It is a beautiful hotel, great suites with a kitchen and two tvs, clean and modern. it is in a great location, near downtown San Diego and not to far to the beach. The breakfast was very good in a beautiful dining area. Service was good and it was overall a comfortable hotel at a very good rate. I would recommend this hotel to anyone with no fear of finding anything bad.

title: “Classy Historical Hotel..!!”
text: We recently spent a night in Seattle for the purpose of attending a concert. We chose to stay at the Mayflower Park Hotel. It is centrally located in the heart of Seattle and was just a short six block walk to the theater. The hotel built in 1927 has been immaculately renovated with attractive decor and our room was large and comfortable. We were concerned about the possibility of traffic noise as our room was above a busy street but in fact the noise was minimal and we had a great sleep. The staff were friendly and courteous......an enjoyable place to stay!!

title: “Marvellous Magnolia”
text:
April 26th 2006
Just returned from a three night stay at the Magnolia. Liked the hotel - check in was polite and efficient and the room spacious, modern and clean. Liked the 'Happy Hour' in the bar from 5 til 7pm, but was a little disappointed by the rooftop swimming pool that looks a lot bigger on the pictures than it actually is. There also didn't seem to be anywhere to sit near to it. It did look impressive by night though. Downtown Houston is a bit dead at weekends by day but is very near Minute Maid Park - a stadium tour or an Astros match are well worth doing. At night Downtown becomes quite lively - enjoyed Sambucca Jazz Cafe and the Irish and Sports bars on Fannin. Hotel bar quite friendly, but finished at 2am. All in all a good value stay at a pleasant and friendly hotel.

title: “Amazing Location, Somewhat Tired Historic Hotel”
text:
This historic hotel is located in a truly fantastic midtown area. Literally steps from a lot of great NY sights, restaurants, etc.
The rooms are stately and clean, and the bed is truly fantastic. Comfortable, excellent sheets, overall great bed experience.
The bathroom is old and tiny, and the water regulation in the shower (temperature) can be tricky. Like all hot or all cold!
Service was spotty - my key didn't work one night and no one picked up at the front desk after more than 30 rings, so I went all the way downstairs again. Some staff just don't seem like they want to be there.
Overall, great hotel, great location, nice rooms...just needs a bit of updating perhaps and the staff (especially for the competitive New York market) needs to perk up a bit.

title: “Hilton Garden Inn DC = Great Hotel!!!!”
text: The hotel is located across from a metro station and is a few blocks from the White House. Great location. The staff is very helpful and polite. The rooms are awesome! Especially the beds. Need to find out the brand of matress.

title: “I stayed up all night rather than sleeping in the bed”
text: This hotel was absolutely horrendous. If I'd have had the money, I would have left in the middle of night for next door. Our room was ridden with TICKS and they crawled everywhere. I decided it was easier to keep watch and sit with the most covering clothing i had on the bed keeping watch and watching TV than dare to sleep there. It was absolutely horrendous. Every room was liek that and it's right next to a strip club. Under NO circumstances should you stay here... I'm not just someone who is mad at the hotel; it's legitimately a place not even fit for the worst of people. Should you stay here, be prepared for ticks to spring from the walls and crawl over you while you sleep. Where long clothes and check your bed when you wake up for blood spots from where they bit you.

title: “Wonderful Experience Overall”
text:
My husband and I stayed at this hotel on the night of our third wedding anniversary, and it's nothing fancy, but worth every penny we paid and more.
I'll start by listing what I liked about the hotel:
-Located around a lot of dining options. (We chose the Dave & Busters right down the road, and it was awesome!)
-Clean! (With the exception of the cigarette smell explained below.)
-Some smoking rooms are still available. (The hotel is primarily non-smoking, though, I believe.)
-Pool looked very pleasant. (We didn't get to actually swim as I had wanted to, but it looked better than most outdoor hotel pools.)
-Plenty of free, well-lit parking.
-Wonderful free breakfast! (It consisting of biscuits, gravy, sausage patties, and eggs, as well as the typical continental breakfast fare--fruit, toast, cereal, juice, etc.)
-Very positive and welcoming attitude from the front desk staff; and also willing to answer our questions about the hotel and the area in general.
-Located in a safe area, and this point can not be emphasized enough! (It is very easy to unintentionally wander into a bad neighborhood in Jacksonville.)
-Comfortable Bed.
Things that could be improved:
-Keeping extra front desk staff on hand while training new employees--especially during check-in hours! (We waited about 30 minutes to be checked in because the supervisor was assisting another customer, and the trainee did not know how to process a Hotwire reservation. We are understanding about this--even though we were on a tight schedule--but others may not be.)
-The smell of cigarette smoke throughout the entire floor we stayed on, even though the floor had non-smoking rooms as well. (This is not something that bothered us so much as probably bothering others who are non-smokers. Hotels we've stayed at in the past typically have an arrangement where an entire floor will be dedicated to smoking rooms as to not bother those who do not smoke. Either way, if you are sensitive to the smell of cigarette smoke and/or do not smoke--even if you have a reservation for a non-smoking room--I suggest requesting a room that is not on the third floor.)
-The lighting in the bathroom should be explained at the front desk. (Perhaps more hotels are like this than I realize, but the light in the bathroom is on a timer, where you twist the timer and then flip the switch. I felt kind of dumb after telling them we had a maintenance problem, but I can't be the only person who has never seen that before.)
All in all, we have paid tons more for 4 and 5-star hotel rooms which were not nearly as pleasant as this one we only spent $40 for on Hotwire.

title: “Hotel Carter N.Y.”
text:
Fantastic location - nice service, friendly staff
The worst thing - noise.
Affordable price comparing typical prices in N.Y.
Carpet needs to be changed and TV set should be renewed. But who watches TV in N.Y....

title: “Good NYC alternative”
text: We were looking for a reasonable place to stay in Manhatten and this seemed a good bet. We chose the renovated room with two Queen beds and were very pleased with the comfort and cleanliness. Hostel prices but better quality. We phoned ahead to inform them that we would arrive in the middle of the night and they held our room as promised and checked us in at 2am. The desk staff on duty throughout our staff were always friendly. I don't believe they have a full maintenance staff so when we had no hot water in our private bath, we were forced to use the shared facility because there were no other comparable rooms available and we didn't want to give up our two beds. Short of running into dripping people wrapped scantily in towels, running between shared shower and their rooms, we had no real complaints. The neighborhood is safe and quiet and restaurant selection is wide. Proximity to Riverside Park, Central Park and the subway are all nice features.

title: “Our place in New York City”
text:
We love the Park Central. It is unbelievably well located, right near Central Park, Carnegie Hall, Times Square, City Center, 57th St and Fifth Avenue.
There is a huge number of Europeans in the hotel and that gives it a wonderfully cosmopolitan feel. On the elevators, we talked to people from India, Ireland, Spain, Italy, Germany and France. And that was two days.
 The rooms are comfortable, although few have good views. Some face on the inside and you look out at brick walls. Corner rooms have spotty cell service sometimes.
 The restaurant is okay, but many better places just outside. The bar is expensive.
 These are nits. The staff is friendly, responsive, and we love the atmosphere and location of the place. It is our spot in NYC. We are very comfortable there.

title: “True review of Holiday Inn San Fran”
text:
We stayed at this hotel in late April for 3 nights.
Firstly its a long way from the International airport,we shared the many mini buses that operate and it cost us approx 18 dollars per person from the airport but coming back you can ring one from the hotel magazine which cost only 10 dollars each.
The hotel is nice enough and has most of the features you expect from the Holiday Inn chain,including an outdoor pool which considering it was the hottest april on record was well used.
We didnt eat in the hotel but the food looked ok the twice we visited the bar.Although the resturant seemed a little overpriced.
The staff were very welcoming which was nice to see.
We walked to almost every place we wanted to get to(wear flat shoes) 
Fishermans wharf is a must and we both loved it there(even though its touristy) with plenty going on for most tastes.
Jacks was our favourite bar with a pint costing 2 dollars(they also have strongbow and newcastle brown on draft!!) food was also very reasonable in there.
The Irish bar behind the Arganaut Hotel is also another pleasant bar with live music.
We also walked all the way to the Golden Gate Bridge from our hotel which took for ever but was worth it and then after a stunning ice cream at the beach we walked back.
All in all we loved our stay in San Fransico and would def return one day,maybe even to the Holiday Inn

title: “Superb Hotel”
text:
We stayed here for 2 nights (Friday-Sunday) and I cannot believe the deal I got on hotwire. Whoa!!! It was about $130 a night, verses over $300 a night on expedia and the hotels website. 
Aside from that, the hotel was excellent. The service was great, the lobby was really pretty and the room was "heavenly". Having a new room was wonderful, it was really decorated lovely but hip. The bed was omg, so comfy!!! They are called Heavenly Bed's for a reason!!!!!!
The bathroom was great, big sink, marble floor and sink! There was also a mini bar in the room and a flat screen!!
The location of the hotel was excellent, we walked around but because it was just way to hot (100+ with the heat index) we had to take cabs. 
Friday night we went to the Tom Petty concert at the Wachovia Center and grabbed a bite to eat and drinks beforehand at McGillins Olde Ale House. They have a happy hour friday from 5-7 and they had pitchers for like $4.00. The food was pretty cheap too and pretty good! It was crowded! Definitley a popular place!
Saturday during the day we did some historical sites, but headed back to the hotel because of the excessive heat warning. 
Saturday night we headed out to Tria before going for dinner. Tria was trendy. Its a beer, wine and cheese bar mainly, but they have many, many different kinds of all three. They also have a light menu with salads and sandwiches etc. There is a menu on their website. I still talk about Tria now! It was really nice! 
For dinner, since we picked a Tria (we had some kind of cheese platter with bread and dip, medly of olives and homemade garlic parmasean potao chips) we went to Amada for a few Tapas and Sangria. My boyfriend had the red and i had the white which was really good!! We had a few tapas which were excellent. After dinner we headed to Tin Angel, and had a couple drinks and there was a band playing so that was nice. 
All in all, the westin was really great! I will definitley be looking into more westins wherever else we go. And i would stay here again if and when i go to philly again!

title: “Excellent”
text:
My husband,daughter(aged 13) and myself stayed at the Staybridge for a week at the beginning of April. We had a 2 bed room on the 28 floor, and contrary to other reviewers, had absolutely no
problems with lifts! Our room was next to a stairwell and was extremely quiet-no noise at all!
We also had no problems getting a table at breakfast, which we found more than adequate.
Front desk and concierge were very helpful.
Must-sees in NYC include walking across Brooklyn bridge (free) Metropolitan museum of art and museum of modern art,stores on 5th Ave (don't miss Saks!),water taxi round Manhatton,9/11 memorial, Rockerfeller at night, Empire during day!

title: “Great location but needs updating”
text:
The courtyard is in a great location for being in the downtown area. You are within easy walking distance to all the major attractions and places to eat. The people mover is also readily accessible to get around if you do not want to walk.
The rooms on the other hand are getting very dated. Our room was upgraded during our stay and was in poor shape. The bathroom had drywall that was peeling due to water damage and the tub would not drain. Climate control in the room was not working. The system shuts down the cooling feature this time of year "as stated on the control panel". The only way to cool the room was to open the window. This is not conveinent due to having to leave the drapes open and letting the noise and light in from outside.
With some updating, the hotel would be worth the price. Currently though there are other hotels in the area that are nicer and you can get them for the same price or cheaper.

title: “Excellent”
text: Excellent stay. Staff over the top courteous. Breakfast made to order anything. Standard free drinks reception. Above average work-out facility. Perfect location.

title: “Definitely not a 4 star hotel”
text:
Won this via Hotwire at a decent price for the location. But there was hair in the bathroom behind the door, the room felt kind of gross (carpeting mainly) and the beds were TINY. How they were considered doubles was beyond me. At check-in, only one room of our booked 2 room stay was available. The clerk, when asked about bypassing the LONG line to check back for Room 2 later, replied "you'll have to wait, everything in life requires a wait". THIS was our check-in/first impression. Ummm, NOT customer-service friendly.
Our TV went out and a lightbulb was burned out. This took 3 separate trips to have both fixed and when the TV was pulled out from the wall, the NASTY debris under the dresser was sickening. The room was VERY hot although we had the A/C at 60 for 4 days straight and kept the blinds closed.
The hotel was overrun w/a tourist group and the last 2 days were horrible in getting elevators. Just be warned if you see a huge group milling in the non-existant lobby that you're in for a wait. There were 1,000 in town, we probably had 200+ of them at the hotel. All trying to visit each other in their rooms and meet in the Lobby at the same time. 
Although the location to Times Square is excellent, I really didn't feel this hotel had anything else going for it. In fact, if I would use Hotwire again, I would purposely NOT choose Times Square area just to avoid this place.

title: “Great hotel in a great location”
text: This hotel is a great find. It isn't too expensive for the excellent location - right around the corner from the Empire State! The staff are very courteous and always spent time ensuring you knew exactly where you were going! We were able to walk to Times Square or could take the tube to wherever we needed to go. The rooms are a decent enough size (especially for NY) but a bit of a squeeze with two cases. The bathroom was a really good size though. Fresh tea and coffee are available downstairs in a little sitting area/breakfast room. There is a tv and books in there, plus free internet access. Overall this was an excellent choice. It was perfect for our 6 night break.

title: “great & comfortable!”
text:
I really enjoyed my stay at Hotel Nikko. It's in a perfect location! We were on the 14th floor and actually had a decent view of Union Square. I had absolutely no complaints about the room. The bathroom was huge with a a bath and a shower and updated look. The bed was so comfortable and clean. There was complimentary coffee.... etc. 
Overall, def. recommend it! It was reasonably priced for the area that it's in. I suggest parking at the garage across the street b/c it's $29 compared to $54 for a day.

title: “Great Value when you're not looking to spend on the Ritz..........”
text: Minutes from Fishermans Wharf & Pier 39, Great value and clean rooms. If found this hotel to be very convienant, and well within my budget. Rick, the owner was sincerely appreciative of my business.

title: “Great Art Deco Experience”
text: I really loved staying at this hotel. I found it extremely reasonable compared to other hotels in the area. It is in a great location right next to neuman marcus off Michigan Ave. It is walking distance to the rail station. What I loved best about the hotel is the authenticity of the art deco experience. The rooms are tastefully decorated adhering closely to its original design of the the early 1930's and 40's. The ceilings and doors are short, so for those who are tall, you may find it slightly claustrophobic. While there are decent views, you don't get the floor to ceiling experience as you would at some of the more modern hotels because the windows are old fashioned small. The staff was very friendly except for the bar. I found the bartender rather aloof. I stayed in a one bedroom suite so it felt very cozy like a 1 bedroom apartment in the city.

title: “Character”
text: This was a get away after the holiday busy season for my wife and I and the Driskall lived up to the billing. As they say, location, location, location. Right in the middle of downtown on 6th st where you can walk anywhere and walk we did. Walk to the Capitol or to a restaurant or to a bar or just downstairs to the hotel bar or restaruant. Room was big and comfy. Great trip

title: “A Total Success”
text: I chose Kimpton's Hotel Monaco in Washington, DC for a long awaited sister reunion this past week. We were a party of six for one night. Every single staff, from the bellman to the front desk, to the bartender at the complimentary cocktail hour, to the maids and valets provided outstanding service. I don't have to tell anyone who travels how important excellent service is -- and how hard it is to find. But what you need to know about this home away from home -- is that you are treated like royalty there. We thoroughly enjoyed every aspect of the visit. The concierge was a prince with last minute reservations and help with a perfect jogging route. We felt as if our needs were the most important in the entire hotel. Our connecting rooms were perfect and immaculate. The location is outstanding -- we walked to everything -- and the restaurant does not disappoint. The decor is unique and fresh and comfortable and the "raid the mini bar" promotion added a bit of whimsy and fun. I will go back to this hotel and will recommend it highly to out of town clients.

title: “Nasty...Better off spending more $$$$ elsewhere”
text: I stayed at the Essex in July 04 and did not have a pleasant experience. The reviews were decent and the price seemed right so we booked it. When we got to the Hotel we were discuted by the nasty appearance. The rooms were dingy, smelled, and felt dirty. It took me 5 minutes just to get the shower to work properly. You could hear the loud noises the shower pipes made all the way down the hallway. Not worth it. Spend a few extra dollars and stay somewhere nicer. We dreaded going back to the Hotel room each night.

title: “Very hip- as advertised”
text:
We spent a week in AZ and Phoenix was at the tail end of our trip. We chose the Clarendon because it seemed to have a "cool" vibe, and weren't disappointed. All the things were were looking for were there from the comfortable pool side seating and very nice roof-top deck to the excellent restaurant. It seemed like a party spot, which was fine except there was quite a bit of late night door banging.
The front desk staff were amazing and took care of all our needs, which included places to go, things to eat, arranging transportation. Unfortunately, we also needed them to deliver soap, coffee and cups that were missed by room service. 
The restaurant & bar were excellent, perhaps a little expensive. We had dinner at the restaurant once, but I wish it could have been more. We love Mexican food and were blown away by the quality and service.
If I had to make some suggestions for improvement, they would be to enforce the no smoking at the pool. It is clearly posted and staff were out there, they just didn't say anything. I looked forward to using the spa, which was out of commission. And this is likely the only time I will make this comment...more pillows!

title: “Great location, convenient shuttle”
text: Great location if you're visiting the San Antonio Seaworld. The staff are very helpful. Hotel itself is very clean. The shuttle bus that goes between the hotel & Seaworld is a big plus. We saved a bunch on parking, also the shuttle parks right in front of gate, so saves us from having to walk across the huge parking lot.

title: “Great Location”
text: The Mayflower Hotel has a very friendly staff and great vintagy-downtown atmosphere. We stayed on the 6th floor and had a beautiful view of the City. The location was so convenient to everything: China Town, Nob Hill, Union Square, public transportation....The hotel was very quiet and low key. The price was very reasonable for being in the heart of everything. Definitely a repeat.

title: “Nice stay good location”
text:
I like the Normandy Hotel it’s located in DuPont Circle/Woodley Park area of DC. 
Pros nice sized rooms for the city, clean, very nice toiletries provided, charming great music playing in the lobby making a nice vibe, an indulgences hour with free wine and cheese, free water and cookies all day. 
Cons the Internet was working of an on in my room for the entire 4 night stay made several complaints to the front desk but they failed to correct the problem. I did not have breakfast because they charged $16 thought it was too much for what they were serving. 
No pool or gym on property it’s a block away at another hotel. 
If you don’t mind walking the subway at DuPont and Woodley Park is about 5-8 min walk. Tip I found it easer to take Woodley park metro stop over the DuPont stop. 
Over all good experience and charming hotel. I would recommend it for adults but not for a family with kids.

title: “Decent downtown location, nice property, but pricey and small rooms”
text:
Stayed 1 night here on a wedding trip. Review...
GOOD:
--Location is basically on the Riverwalk, though a remote corner of it
--Common areas and facilites are nice
--Rooms are well-appointed and clean
BAD:
--Expensive for San Antonio, even downtown
--Rooms are small
This is in a good location, and reasonably nice, but pricey. Not a bad choice, but maybe not the best available, unless you get a good deal.

title: “Loved this elegant hotel!”
text: Loved staying at this hotel. They arranged prompt service to & from airport. Our rooms were interconnecting & exactly what we had asked for. The rooms were high end-marble in bathrooms, large tubs, exquisite decor. Beds were VERY comfortable. Enjoyed turn down bed service @ night. The hotel was located convenient to Times Square and within walking distance of the Broadway shows. We will definitely stay here again and would recommend this hotel! The only negative was the continental breakfast-only served croissants. Most nice hotels serve a full continental breakfast with an assortment of breakfast items and choice of juices/milk/coffee.

title: “Incredibly comfortable stay in a great central location”
text: My boyfriend and I chose to stay in the New York Palace for our week-long trip after reading positive reviews about the hotel and finding a good rate on one of the hotel booking sites. I must say I found the process of searching for a hotel in NYC incredibly overwhelming as there were so many places to choose from and the last thing we wanted on our first joint visit to the city was an uncomfortable hotel stay. All our concerns were instantly alleviated when we arrived to the hotel. The staff were friendly and courteous and allocated our room quickly. The room itself was large with big wardrobes and bathroom. We had all the extras we needed like an iron/ironing board, kettle with tea/coffee, lots of hangers, bathrobe, slippers and a well stocked minibar. The views were spectacular and the optional breakfast was delicious although more expensive than what you can find in local coffee shops around the area. We dined at the restaurant attached to the hotel one night as a special treat and it is definitely worth a visit although it is definitely an expensive special treat. The only downside to our experience was that construction work was taking place next door to the hotel at the time we stayed and it woke us up over several nights. Although this was not the fault of the hotel I felt they should have communicated this to us when we checked in so that we could agree to change rooms if the noise bothered us too much. After the third or fourth night of disrupted sleep we spoke to the hotel manager about it and he dealt with our feedback superbly by changing our room and providing us with some compensation. I feel this is often the best test for any business - how they deal with you when things go wrong and this hotel was excellent. I would definitely recommend the New York Palace for a stay in NYC and would stay there again on a future trip.

title: “Great location close to Broadway shows”
text: Beautiful boutique hotel one block off of Broadway and Time Square. Modern black and white decor with art deco touches. Very spacious for a NYC hotel. You can walk to your pre or post-theater restaurant or theater in10 minutes. Hotel is very "green" and takes pets.

title: “This hotel is just fine”
text:
I stayed at the Sheraton City Center in Baltimore for 3 nights on business, in July 2010. After reading prior reviews, I expected much worse. It was a typical business-class hotel in a downtown area, nothing more, nothing less. 
I was upgraded to a corner room--nice to have windows out 2 sides--by being in the Starwood Club, which is free. They told me a refrigerator could be supplied at an additional cost of $20 per night, which I found ridiculous.
The gym was good, two rooms full of lots of cardio equipment and limited weights and machines, but the major problem there was the temperature. The place was like an oven, and on my final day there, the water coolers were both empty. Staff brought in water bottles, but they disappeared quickly. The pool was small but popular.
Head bellhop was VERY helpful with directions, and all staff were very courteous. Not sure why prior guests seem to have had issues--either those staff members have been replaced, or maybe those guests had issues of their own.
Not enough hangers in the closet (6), but a nicely upgraded (albeit small) bathroom. Huge king bed, and not much street noise (I was on the 9th floor). A good-size desk and TV. Yes, everything was dated in decor, but when traveling on business, that doesn't really matter, does it?
THE BEST PART was the gyro stand on the corner. Exit the front of the hotel, turn left at the end of the block (which is actually right there), go to the next corner and it is across the street. Literally a two-minute walk, and this is some of the BEST street food I have ever had (and I've had street food in Beijing, Hong Kong, Bangkok, Guadalajara, Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City, Chiang Mai...you get the picture) . You get a huge lamb gyro (with or without hot sauce--if you like spicy, get it!) for $4, or $4.85 with a can of soda. Best deal in town and outrageously good. I took 3 gyros home, and would almost go back to Baltimore just for them!
The hotel was fine and certainly not deserving of the negative remarks of the kind in some other reviews.

title: “First Class Hotel”
text: We had a wonderful week in New York which was made extra special by staying at the Hotel Elysee. What a wonderful location, shopping,historic sites, Central Park all easy to get to from E 54th street. Our room was lovely, spotless and very quiet (we faced the street) loads of space to hang cloathes and store luggage.The chaps on reception were so friendly and helpful with a great sense of humour, we even managed the E-train on the subway thanks to their advice. The breakfasts and wine and nibbles in the afternoon were superb served by happy friendly girls who could not do enough for you.If we go back to New York we will definately book Hotel Elysee and also recommend it to friends and family. Bill's Piano bar across the street is worth a visit too

title: “Good hotel - Great Service!”
text:
When I came in the lobby the hotel looked pretty worn down to me. A very friendly staff member welcomed me to the hotel and even offered me a free upgrade just because I looked so tired when I arrived. Got a fabulous room at the 39'th floor with a view over down town and the Golden gate bridge.
I used the concierge service a couple of times and it was great. They really took the time to help me to the max. 38 USD for a breakfast was a bit excessive.

title: “Wonderful! Excellent Customer Service, Excellent Property!”
text: Tristan was super helpful with my reservation process over the phone. It didn't stop there. We arrived: smooth, quick ckeck in by Tammy. The room was spotless and everything was perfect, not to mention room to spread out &a full kitchen to prepare a meal. Great location, close to everything: NASA, Kemah, Baybrook Mall, Restaurants, even an HEB grocery store. We got back around 6pm on Wednesday &were thrilled to be greeted by Tristan &have an evening reception prepared, the food was delicious, served with salad, also beer &wine. This is definately where we will stay when we come back to the area. If you have to be away from home, this is it.

title: “Awesome for spring break!”
text:
Traveled with my husband for our spring break. He is an avid golfer; I am not but that didn't stop me from having a wonderful holiday at the Legacy!
Pros: manicured grounds, spotless rooms, awesome food, wonderful pool area, oasis of greenery in the desert, top notch driving range and practice greens, barbecue area, very accommadating staff, lovely views, wonderful flowers, fees like you are in the country in the middle of a huge city, The Farm, which has three restaurants, a garden, a massage place and a artisan boutique is a 7 minute walk away, another golf course, the Raven is a 25 minute walk
Cons: can't really walk to any nearby shops or food stores; thin walls but who stays in their room all day? Old and small TV sets but again, who goes there to watch TV? The annoying part, being a little bit hassled to attend time share presentations. We were asked twice but they must have had their quota because they didn't call us back to attend.

title: “Best Value in Columbus!”
text:
Since two of my kids live in Columbus, we make occasional trips there, and have stayed at several different hotels. This was our first time at this property, but it will not be the last!
What first impressed us was the cleanliness and orderliness of the property. Next was the friendliness of the staff. Our room, #134, was one the ot the cleanest rooms we've stayed in anywhere, regardless of price. Included were a microwave, fridge and coffeemaker.
The complimentary breakfast was very good, and included make-your-own waffles, sausage, sweet rolls, bagels, fruit, cereals and even hard-cooked eggs.
We paid $121 for two nights, the lowest rate we've seen in Columbus.

title: “Funky Atmosphere in a Great Location”
text: From the time we checked in to when we left - we were amazed of the funky design and interior of this hotel. Located on the Upper East Side and near various subway lines - hotel was a great location for us. The picture perfect weather allowed the restaurant exterior doors to be open with table sitting on the balcony. We were upgraded when we checked in and asked for a quiet room. The room was just that and nicely furnished. You defintely felt you were not in a Marriott - by any stretch. I continue to be very impressed with the Renaissance chain - no two are alike.

title: “Great boutique-style hotel!”
text: Stayed at the Bristol for two nights in late november with my boyfriend and a couple of friends and it was by far the best hotel we stayed in during our trip (San Diego/Los Angeles/Las Vegas). It's a boutique-style hotel, quite cozy and charming but still modern. Rooms are not big but perfect for a couple and the bathrooms have a delightful slightly retro style. Staff was quite friendly, which is always a plus. The location is great, just a 5 minute car ride from the airport and a short walk from the Gaslamp quarter. This place is a gem and I fully recommend it to young couples and friends travelling together - San Diego is a lovely city and the Bristol is a great place to stay.

title: “Teeny rooms so be prepared”
text:
I read previous reviews of this hotel which were quite positive and I decided to stay here for one night for business. On the positive side, It was quite clean, renovated and the lobby was basically a place to check in with an elevator....the restaurant was off the lobby. It's in a great location off Fifth Avenue and 40th Street. 
I was shocked at how small this hotel is in comparison to other Courtyards/hotels I have stayed at in Manhattan and other large cities. I am actually a New Yorker so I am very familiar with Manhattan and this hotel was located very close to where I had an early business meeting so I thought I would spend the night rather than having to take a very early train in from the suburbs. I checked in about 9PM and the room had a queen size bed, a credenza with a flat screen TV, two night tables and a small bathroom (usually considered the size of a "half bath"). This was the entire room for $419 per nite (including all taxes).
It was a good thing I only needed to sleep here and check out since there was no chair (other than the desk chair) to even sit on and you bumped into the bed each time you tried to move around the room! 
So.....I still say this location is great but be prepared to be claustrophobic in the "queen size" room or book a King or double bed room for a bit more money to have more space.

title: “Great hotel in NY”
text: Sofitel is well situated and with excellent service makes a great place to stay in NY.

title: “Best Customer Service”
text: We checked in, and found that we had mucked up the reservation, which had us arriving and departing a day early. The desk guy checked with his manager and moved us a day, which included crediting the pre payment and wiping out the no show penalty. The hotel is great, a nice restoration of a famous structure in a very nice residential area near the Zoo, shops, restaurants, metro, Rock Creek park, etc. Everyone from the Doorman, the Parking Valets, etc. is razor focused on the customer experience. Our room was large and nicely appointed, everything in good shape. Highly recommend!!!

title: “Already planning my next trip!”
text: Spent 2 nights at the Courtyard Marriott Washington Convention Center and could not have been more pleased. Chose this particular location due to it's proximity to the Verizon Center (for an Andrea Bocelli concert and a Washington Capitals game). The location of this hotel just cannot be beat! Within walking distance to the White House (20 minutes) and Capital Hill (25 minutes). The National Mall is 10 - 15 inutes. There are a ton of great restraunts to choose from, for breakfast, lunch, or dinner, you will not go hungry! I need a return trip just to try them all. The area around the hotel feels super safe, great for a morning walk to Stabucks (only 4 minutes) or a late night stroll. The staff at check in could not have been more accomodating (room was not ready at 11:00AM) (nor did I expect it to be) but they gave me a call on my cell when it was. Came out from behind the desk to orientate us to the property....made us feel like we had been there a dozen times before. The lobby is modern but not super spacious...which is to be expected as it was a bank in it's earlier life. The room was as expected...all the needed amenities....super clean and quiet.....not on the "big" side but was a 6th floor corner room overlooking the corner of F and 9th. Would highly recommend as a great "home base" for a visit to Washington.........

title: “Classy alternative to Peabody”
text: Greeted at door by smartly dressed,pleasant staff.Valet parking inexspensive and quick.Check in quick and painless.I had to change my reservation previously and the desk staff were very pleasant and helpful over the phone.The King room was small but decor was nice.Bed (which took up most of room)was very comfortable with feather duvet and nice pillows.Bathroom was nice size with large shower.Turn down service and free newspaper out side your door was available but over 4 nights they forgot our room about twice.We recieved a free breakfast voucher for every night we stayed.Hotel is within easy walking distance of many restaurants and attractions.Try this hotel as an alternative to the Peabody

title: “DO NOT STAY HERE IF YOU VALUE YOUR FAMILYS SAFETY!”
text: The hotel staff gave out keys to another person to view our room while we were in it. After this episode frightened my children and upset my husband and myself, the hotel staff refused to do anything to appease the situation. Upopn checkout they even charged full price for the stay. After weeks of us having to "chase" the management, they finally issued a credit of $50 which was not even equal to one's nights stay. There mistake ruined our family vacation, due to very tired children who were afraid to sleep the next days events were a disaster. We booked 3 nights total, a credit of at least the one nights stay would have been fair upon checkout. If you value your peace of mind and your familys safety - DO NOT STAY HERE!

title: “Great way to spend our 25th Wedding Anniversary!”
text:
Stayed here to celebrate our 25th Wedding Anniversary and wanted a special place. We got that and more! We mentioned we were staying there for our special day and needed dinner reservations. The concierge were top notch! They got us a special table at Mario Batali's Del Posta. When we returned we were surprised to find a bottle of champagne in our room waiting for us with a lovely card. We ordered the romance butler bath and at $120 had a beautiful rose petaled covered bath with roses and candies not to mention the sensuous bath!
The location was great as only a short walk to Bowling Green subway and a short ride uptown. You can also take a taxi as the door man called one quickly and uptown was only $7 plus they took the short route avoiding traffic. The Battery Park was nice to stroll and sit watching the harbor and overlooking Statue of Liberty! Very safe area, as police presence is here frequently.
The room was a harbor view room upgraded for us, and a view of the harbor overlooking the statue of liberty. We got a north corner room, would not recommend as our north window we could not open the curtains as they are constructing a building next door, very loud but at 5pm they stopped til 8am next day. Make sure to request a high room over floor 5 and not the north side.
Was nice to have a large bath, with separate bath and marbled shower and separate toilet area, the bath is larger than most NYC hotel rooms!
Cant wait to come back!

title: “Overall, a good experience, but standard rooms are dated”
text:
We recently stayed at this property and had a good experience. 
My main complaint is that while the suites are newly refurbished and easily up to 4 star quality, the standard rooms (while clean and well maintained) look very dated and are. at best, at a 3 star level. We had been upgraded mid-stay from a standard room to a suite. It is my understanding that there are no plans to refurbish the standard rooms, which would definitely influence my choice to stay there in the future if an upgrade were not available, especially given the number of similar properties in the Back Bay area. As for the standard room being small, it is a typical big city hotel room, no smaller than I've seen elsewhere. 
It is also a large conference hotel that caters to groups, so elevators can tend to be slow at times (especially for floors above 27, which is served by only one elevator bank), and staff may be overwhelmed and slow to respond too (e.g. long waits for deliveries from bell staff), although not a big deal. Although service is overall quite good, one shouldn't expect boutique hotel ambiance and service.
Pros: Front desk day staff is very friendly and accommodating, well trained and great to deal with. The hotel is in an excellent location in the Back Bay, with shopping, good restaurants and other amenities within a short walk. The new Marriott bedding system made for a very comfortable sleep. The breakfast buffet at Champions was very good and well maintained. 
Cons: Front desk evening staff, while professional, is somewhat brusque and not particularly accommodating. Room rates seem to be high compared to area alternatives, but that might be a function of the fact that they attract groups and don't need to offer much discounting to fill their rooms. The standard rooms really need updating to be competitive with other area properties, especially at those rates.

title: “Good location”
text: My friend and I stayed here in December. The location is great except there is construction going on all day and night. I would ask for a room away from the construction. The room was nice although not exceptional. The staff was very pleasant. The overnight parking fee is exorbitant but that is true of most hotels in Boston. I have stayed at most of the hotels in Boston over time. I would rate the Four Season as the best hotel so far but it is very expensive. Overall staying at the Back Bay hotel was a pleasant experience at a personable and small hotel in a great location.

title: “Good Location for the money”
text:
we neamed our own price on the room and for $100 in that location around all the attractions you get in walking distance it is a goooood rate.
Our room was clean and really big with a small patio you can sit on ... (and get the free DC wifi) 
Our room wasnt ready as we arrived in the morning so the guy at the reception (Andre Hooker - he is sooooo nice) send us an short and nice email as it were ready - nice service!!!
The only thing that isnt sooo cool, the windows arent that good - you can hear the amtrak arrive and much noise from the streets around...
Would stay here again !

title: “oasis in the city”
text: I stayed there for a short time during a busy conference week. The place was quiet and clean. I loved the flowers and the easy access outside. Breakfast was served in the morning and I could eat it at one of tables set outside. Good way to start the day! The staff was friendly and helpful, and made me feel like a welcome guest. Because of the minute size relative to the huge blocks/hotels nearby, and because of the many flowers in pots and hanging baskets I felt like I was staying in an oasis in the city. All these while within walking distance to the Convention Center.

title: “Fantastic Location”
text: The location is the best. One block from the main strip of restaurants and bars. About 5 blocks from the convention center. Rooms are small but they are clean and maintained. The staff was very friendly and helpful. Nice breakfast included; eggs, toast, bagels, cereals, fruit, danish, coffee, juice, etc. Definitely would stay here again!

title: “Great location for visiting GW”
text: The Hotel Lombardy is a wonderful little hotel in Foggy Bottom near George Washington University. It is literally a block away and the perfect location for a potential student to get a feel for campus life. Our room had two beds, a kitchenette, and a dressing area. After doing a swing of the big cities in the northeast, the hotel definitely had more of a genteel feel with a desk under a big window and shutter-door in front of your regular room doorway. The staff was very helpful. I would definitely stay here again. It is a few blocks to Embassy Row and the Metro station.

title: “Perfect Hotel, Odd Location”
text: Marble tile, glass elevators, beautiful atrium, 2 flat TVs in the room, sauna avail, etc... Way more interior "glitz" than we expected at the price we got through Priceline. That said, you better have a good map of Charlotte handy and a car... The roads are very confusing and very few restaurants are nearby. Hotel restaurant has limited selection and is rather pricey.

title: “Nice hotel, but nothing special”
text: All the extra fees annoyed me. Fee for wifi, fee for parking, outrageous fees for the mini bar. Seriously, you'd pay the same price for one can of Coke that you would buy a 24 pack with. That is just unnecessary. We booked on Hotwire, so got a great deal. It was a convenient location, clean (which is key), and the service was very friendly. However, there was no TV guide in the rooms, or any local take out menus. Simple things, that would've helped out a lot. Overall we were pleased with our stay, but it could've been better. Had we paid more than what we did with Hotwire, we would've been unhappy.

title: “Unbelievably terrible service”
text:
Terrible. Checked in to room that smelled so bad. It was humid & smells of mold; it was as if the room hadn't been used in a while. Turned the air on and opened the door to try to get some fresh air to circulate into the room (can't open the windows) and the heat-a/c unit smelled as if it were burning and just blew out more sticky air.
Next day. we came back after lunch to be locked out of our room. Front desk claimed we had checked out and they had given our room out to someone else and had no idea where our things were and refused to take responsibility for them, repeatedly asking us if we were sure we hadn't taken our things with us and check out. UNREAL. Had to show our confirmation email that we had booked 3 nights and call our agent to confirm as the front desk receptionist refused to believe us. It ook about an hour to get someone to come up to the room to check to see where our belongings were, as the hotel was incredible understaffed. Tried speaking to the GM only to find out he was on a shuttle run. After checking to see if our belongings were in the room, it took about another half our to get a room key (they didn't let us into our room, we had to go downstairs to get a key). The room hadn't been cleaned and to top it off, it wouldn't be cleaned until the next day, as they were so understaffed. We asked for towels and they told us they had nobody to bring them up to us for about 30 min. absolutely ridiculous.
To make matters worse, front desk receptionist gave us a set of bad keys; we had to go down to the desk, yet again, to get keys that worked. Next day, we get locked out again at the end of the day. after about an hour, we finally get a set of working keys, only to find ANTS in our bathroom. 3 am, we just want to sleep as we had an early flight the next day. Not happening. Went to the front desk and they claimed everything was locked and they had nothing for the ants until about 9 am the next day. We tried explaining we had a 6 am flight but they had nothing for us. Seriously. worst service ever. 
Unbelievable experience; extremely rude and careless staff; never again.

title: “W is for Weird”
text:
Not your father's business hotel, and maybe not yours either. The lobby becomes a disco with a DJ at night. Coming home late from a show, expect to wander through crowds of drunk people gyrating to loud music. Say hello to the big bouncer stationed by the elevators to keep these people confined to the lobby.
Welcome to your room. Strangely shaped, you say? Yes, why *didn't* they take another 15 sq ft or so off the ample bedroom to make a bathroom that isn't so small you can't open the door all the way without it banging into the sink?
How do you like the decor? What shall we call it? Hmmm, maybe 1980's Playboy Magazine Chic? The broken lampshade and the towel rack that falls off the wall whenever touched do spoil the mood a little. But don't worry: I'm sure the maid is used to mopping up the water that is just naturally going to wind up on the bathroom floor from the shower stall that has neither a door or a curtain.
That being said, the location of the hotel is excellent. When you're feeling down about your room, you can walk across the street in one direction to the Marriott to see what an affordable hotel looks like or across Lexington to the Waldorf Astoria to see what a really nice hotel looks like.
With any luck, you won't have to wait until 6:30 pm to get into a room because the Starwood Preferred Guest in your room is exercising his privilege of "late check out". Thanks, guys, for the compensatory free bar vouchers; I don't drink.
I was in a two-day meeting in the hotel, and I will say that the meeting rooms are superb. I've probably never been in a nicer hotel meeting space, and the catering for the meeting was also excellent.
Everyone I dealt with at the hotel was professional, cordial and eager to serve.

title: “Charming treasure”
text: The best old world charm small hotel I've found, central location. The living room is my favorite place to relax and enjoy tea, wine, snacks and breakfast. Can't wait to go again

title: “Great overall everything..”
text:
I had the opportunity to host a small meeting at The Curtis this week - every single thing was perfect. Rick and Alma attended our meeting and were able to accommodate my group's last minute requests with ease. All of the catering was perfect. Check-in was friendly and efficient, my room was clean and contemporary, and the location made walking to dinner and attractions very easy. The whimsy in the decor at boutique hotels can sometimes appear too intentional - the subtlety encountered at The Curtis made exploring even more enjoyable.
I would definitely return next time I am in Denver.

title: “great view, lots of little annoyances”
text:
Based on previous reviews, I booked a room in the Bay Tower. The view was awesome...but there were other minor things that detracted from my stay. (1) The water for my shower was only lukewarm 2 out of 3 mornings. 
(2) The walls are paper thin. I could hear people talking next door & in the hall, also heard every time people in the room above flushed the toilet (they are VERY loud), walked, & took a shower, etc. 
(3) The website doesn't state that it's about 1/4 to 1/3 mile walk from the Bay Tower to the Marina Tower where the main hotel and larger conference venue are located. I love to walk...but not in business shoes.
(4) Food prices at the hotel restaurants are about the most outrageous I've ever seen, even for a higher-end hotel in a major city. $9 for a bowl of oatmeal?! $15 for a hamburger?! Thankfully the deli/diner half-way between the 2 buildings had great, inexpensive food for breakfast & lunch.
If you are going for a conference, I'd recommend staying at the Marina for convenience sake, unless the view is all that matters.

title: “Needs remodeling.”
text: This hotel needs remodeling. The bathroom corners are dirty and moldy. We had a room with two beds, which are not queen size but full size. Way too small. The view is nice but not spectacular. Staff was pleasant. Would stay again if the price was right but not really up to HI standard.

title: “Brilliant, friendly service, excellent value for money”
text:
4 of us stayed in a family room in the hotel. The room was spacious enough to accomadate 4 adults. The room was clean, the beds were comfortable, and the shower was really powerful.
The service we received was excellent, no request was too big or met with a "no can do attitude". Everyone of the staff we dealt with was friendly courteous and knowledgeable.
The buffet breakfast was excellent...lots of choice, great coffee! 
A big bonus was the hot tub area, which was huge, and very quiet...we had it to ourselves everytime we went. 
Overall excellent value for money.

title: “Wonderful stay at the Conrad!”
text: Just returned from a four night stay at the Conrad. We got a great deal with their Dec. special. The breakfast was great (a special thanks to Luis!) and the location couldn't be better. The service (bell staff, front desk, housekeeping, servers at the restaurant) were especially polite and service-oriented. Couldn't ask for more!

title: “Great stay in a great hotel”
text: Stayed 2 nights to attend the Army/Navy game and was very impressed. The hotel still feels very new and is very clean. Rooms are large and the bathrooms very nice and spacious. The hotel is a bit of a drive to FedEx Field, however, if you were visiting DC for sightseeing, there is a Metro stop about a block away. The hotel is also very close to Union Station and there are a few restaurants to walk to. Price was excellent for the services received, however, there is a $30/night charge to valet park your vehicle.

title: “Amazing!”
text: This hotel is very well located! On its lobby there is a jazz bar with excellent music! Very nice staff and rooms.

title: “be aware of payment”
text: DC is a widely spread town geografically, so the location of the hotel is good for exploring. Metrostation is some 10 mins on foot, and if you are with a company then the best to explore is by taxi ( roughly 10 usd to Lincoln memorial, Union station or Georgetown). Rooms are of decent size, some worn and tear clearly seen especially in the bathroom, but this is not 3 stars or more hotel in european standards.Strange smell bothers once entering the room, some old damp. I understand this is prevailing in the whole hotel, as our friends changed 2 rooms and smell was present. You can switch conditioner on , smell might get weaker, but still there. Breakfast was good, choise of cereals, yogurts , fruits, even waffels to make by yourself, and very helpful staff down there. No caffe or bar close around, Dupont circle is some 25 min on foot . Our worst experience with hotel was payment that is why we rate front desk staff as incompetent. On arrival during check-in the total amount for 3 days stay was put on hold from my credit card , in the morning of check-out it was put on hold one more time. On check-out we paid cash, as it was our last day in USA (we are overseas tourists) and wanted to spend our last cash. 5 days after our leave hotel deducted and credited at once the first hold of funds from my card while still keeping the second hold allthough it was already paid on check-out. I had to go through claim process at my home bank as i suffered some 50 usd loss due to exchange rate and extra Visa operations. Very time-costly experience due to malpractice of hotel.

title: “Mixed Bag”
text:
This hotel while quirky and cool, with friendly and knowledgeable staff, and having a great location to explore downtown Boston neighborhoods (Back Bay, South End, Beacon Hill, Downtown, etc.), also has small rooms and bathrooms, is a little more expensive than we'd hoped for (certainly given the size of the room), and has a horrible air-conditioning system. 
Our air conditioner (located in room 508) was a tiny window unit that blew light cool air inconsistently, would freeze up if left on high, and would also leak water after time no matter the setting. We stayed there 3 nights while on our honeymoon, and getting up in the middle of the night to adjust the air conditioner is decidedly un-romantic. 
Still, if you're looking for great location for the price (most hotels in Boston exceed $200/night, and this one was about $160), and like the "hominess" of its staff, this is good hotel. I'd give it a grade of a C+/B-. (Note to the staff: UPGRADE YOUR FRIGGIN' AIR-CONDITIONING UNITS PLEASE!).

title: “comfortable hotel”
text:
My family stayed here for two nights early April.The hotel is quite small but very comfortable.There is no restaurant or bar inside the hotel but there is a small breakfast area which provides a continental style buffet breakfast free of charge.During the day urns of tea coffee and hot chocolate are available for guests,free of charge.
Bedrooms are clean and well equipped.Plenty of hot water and fresh white towels along with complimentary toiletries as well as cofee maker.
 It is a good 25 min walk into Times Square,we found the area close by to the hotel a little quiet and isolated at night which made us feel a little unsafe.
 Staff at the hotel were very friendly and take pride in making sure the hotel is run succesfully.
Overall we had a pleasant stay but if we return to N.Y. we will definately stay somewhere more central and in a more pleasant and safer area.

title: “Great location, staff, and room”
text:
i had an early flight into DC so I was happily surprised that they let me check in at 10am. I got a room on the 6th floor (there are 9 floors) facing west, and the direct sun in the late afternoon was very nice after a cool April afternoon walking around the city.
Staff was very friendly and professional. There's a Trader Joe's just a couple blocks away to get a bottle (or two of wine) for the room :) The Metro stop for Foggy Bottom is close by too which gets you all over the city. Dupont Circle is just a short walk away for restaurants and nightlife. Yes you might hear an ambulance in the middle of the night, but this is a big city - buy some earplugs if you're such a light sleeper!

title: “A gem of a hotel with the friendliest staff you could ever wish for”
text: Wow - what a gem of a place - fab location and very affordable. From the moment we arrived - the reception staff were efficient, friendly and attentive. We had a lovely room on the 9th floor - twin exec and it was comfortable, clean and modern. The safe jammed on day 2 - the engineer was up and sorted it out within 5-10 mins. My son spilt a drink on the bed - no problem - housekeeping were there to change the sheets early evg. Every morning and nt - somebody greeted us in reception - so helpful - loved it!!!!! We have stayed in big chain group hotels in NYC but this was by far the best place to be - personal touch goes so far yet costs nothing.

title: “Nice/Contemporary, but not comfy”
text: Nice, stylish and clean, however the most important thing to me when travelling is comfort. Room needs a more comfortable place to sit and work, relax or eat. etc. Other than that, it was very nice.

title: “Nice hotel!”
text: Had a nice stay here. Hotel very clean and nice location in Tribeca. Easy access to Broadway and restaurant decent as well.

title: “Great location”
text: We stayed four days. Easy walk from Penn Station. We enjoyed our stay and will recommend it to our friends. Great selection of restaurant on 7th Av south of 28th St.

title: “Comfortable Friendly Hotel in Excellent Location”
text: The first hotel of our trip to SW USA certainly set the standard. A great welcome after a long flight. Really friendly and helpful staff but we found the concierge service knowledge a bit patchy. The rooms are really nicely furnished and comfortable But the downside is the view ( or lack of it at the back) Definitely worth upgrading to bay view room. Excellent location On edge of Fisherman's wharf and with the cable car terminal a few steps away. Good bar and restaurant and bonus of free wine reception every evening. Would definitely recommend

title: “Almost as good as a weekend in Japan”
text: The staff, especially the bellmen, were very helpful in arranging transportation for me to the opera and to the train station. I was able to get a free upgrade and a late checkout too. I had not stayed at this hotel for 9 years, and the surrounding area in Little Tokyo is much livelier than I recalled from my last stay. The Japan American museum is worth a visit, with the lovely Chado tea room.

title: “A cozy room in a happy hotel... :)”
text: This hotel was a great experience! Fun lobby & nice people... especially Jerry Mac who helped us with our late night check-in, clean room, no problems... I'll be back :)

title: “Very nice stay”
text:
I was nervous about this place after reading some of the reviews, particularly about the service, but my two-night stay here was just lovely, and I found the staff to be particularly friendly & helpful. 
The rooms are ample size and very clean. My only annoyances were paying $10/day for internet service and $7/day for uncovered, unprotected self-parking.
All in all, an excellent stay, and I would likely stay here again.

title: “good hotel”
text: My wife and I stayed at this hotel for 3 nights. Staff was very attentive, professional and courteous. Concierge desk outstanding. Restaurant staff excellent. Room was clean and of adequate/standard size. Good King bed. Very fast elevators. Good location on the "Loop", we walked everywhere. Only drawback - our room on back side of hotel looked over elevated train tracks and we never got used to the sounds of the trains rumbling by. If we returned, would ask for room on side away from train.

title: “last night of a long trip”
text: Probably this hotel gets a lower rating because I was tired and ready to get home! The front desk person was unprepared although we had reservations (this was a large group so there were a good many of us). Room was okay, clean and comfortable. There's a Cracker Barrel across the parking lot, not a favorite restaurant of mine but we were seated quickly and the service was prompt and professional. One of my traveling companions loves browsing the Cracker Barrel store and said they had a good selection of souvenirs, gifts, etc.

title: “Wedding”
text: Very nice. Rooms small, but for $99 it was good, My daughter has problems checking in. Also she was very over charged on her credit card. Needs better way to get to bar. You have to walk thru dining room to getto bar

title: “Great Hotel! Not as kid friendly as I thought.”
text: I booked this hotel under after reading a website that said that the Conrad was one of the most kid friendly hotels in Chicago. It stated that they greeted the kids with cotton candy at check-in and gave them an age appropriate toy. My other deciding factor was the fact that they had a DVD player in each room. I have a 3 year old daughter and she likes to watch "The Incredibles" each night before going to bed. Well, I have to say that the hotel was absolutely beautiful, but there was no cotton candy or toy greeting my daughter at check-in. Oh well, it was not a deal breaker by any means, but I did expect it to be more kid friendly. We actually didn't see any children the entire time we were there. It didn't matter to us, but they also don't have a pool, which could be a downer for those that want one. The room was great, the staff was very helpful and friendly, and the location was right-on!
