The room was nice and spacious and I didn't hear a peep from anyone the entire 3 nights. I thought that we were the only ones there it was so quiet! If you are looking for a more kid friendly hotel, spend a little extra and go the to the Ritz-Carlton. There is an excellant playground right across the street for them to get some energy out. And from what I hear, they have a cookies and milk turndown service. Don't get me wrong, I would totally book the Conrad again if it was just my husband and I, but I don't know if I would book again for the 3 of us.

title: “Treated Like VIP's!!”
text:
We booked this hotel because of the location but ended up loving it for many reasons. Trisha and Elisha the concierges went above and beyond. They booked us tee times, directed us to the best "hot spots" and made sure that our weekend was beyond!! We stayed in a HUGE room that had charm unlike some trendy hotels. Not everything can be brand new and polished.
If you are ever going to Austin STAY AT THIS PLACE!!! You will not regret your choice.

title: “Fantastic Value For Money - Except for Parking”
text:
Booked this through Priceline earlier in the year... was my second time staying at the Swissotel. The lobby is very open and well-lit. They have flavoured water available free of charge as well. Staff is very professional and helpful. When you go to take the elevator, it's a bit different! Punch in your floor at the bottom before you get on the elevator.
The room itself was very clean, had a nice view of downtown Chicago and was everything we expected. We also made use of the pool on the top floor of the hotel, which had an even better view which my 6 year old son loved. The pool was a tad chilly, but not too bad. They also have a hot tub. The pool area was a bit crowded but manageable. It also seemed as though someone was getting swimming lessons when we first arrived, so that seems to be a service that is available.
Location wise, the hotel is excellent. It was a 10 minute walk to Bobby's Bike Hike, where we had a tour the next day. It was 5-10 minutes over to Michigan Ave and ample restaurants within walking distance. Millenium park is a few blocks away, the river is right outside the hotel, etc. It was about a 25-30 min walk up to Water Town Plaza where the Lego store is.
My only beef was the fee for parking since we had scored the rate through Priceline. If I remember correctly it was $50 per night. We ended up parking in a local garage which was about a 10 min walk since we didn't require the car for the duration of our stay. It worked out fine. Link to local garages is here: http://www.millenniumgarages.com/

title: “VERY small but clean & great location”
text: The hotel is in a great location. The rooms are VERY small, so if you are not good in small spaces, forget it! The room is he size of a double bed - no kidding. Its clean and the shared bathrooms are clean and pretty good. The bunk bed rooms make the rooms feel very small. If you on a tight budget, and have very little luggage, this is the place to stay. NB: The air conditioners are a little noisy, and theer are still some of the original residence living in the hotel who smoke and are a little out of he ordinary.

title: “Incredible value for Manhattan. I'll go back again.”
text:
Hotel rates in Manhattan have skyrocketed in the last year, so I was very excited to find a nice room for under $200/night. I was on the top floor (11th) facing the back and was not bothered by noise (mentioned in other reviews), other than the usual NY noise. I did look out a window at the front of the building, and the view was better. The heat/ac unit was new and worked perfectly. My room was small, but the layout made very good use of the space - with newer looking furnishings, including a flat screen TV. It didn't feel cramped, and everything was clean. The was very little space between the end of the bed and the desk, but a little stool was provided, and it worked just fine. The bathroom was larger than I expected and the fixtures seemed new. There was a full tub and shower. Free breakfast is offered and it was not crowded when I was there mid-week. There was a waffle maker, as well as fruits, toast, bagels, cereal, yogurt,hard boiled eggs, and juices. 
Overall, I found the hotel to be very clean and comfortable, with all the amenities I needed. The service was friendly. The rooms are not plush, but were MUCH better than I expected for the price. Plus, the free breakfast can't be beat. I felt safe in the neighborhood at night, and it's a short walk to Chinatown, East Village, Little Italy. There's a subway station 1 block away on Delancey (F train). There are hundreds of bars and restaurants in the area, with quite a few bars concentrated on Ludlow Street, so it was quite active, especially at night.
I have never stayed at a Comfort Inn, but I will definitely go back to this hotel.

title: “Going Downhill Fast.”
text:
I have stayed at this hotel a multitude of times over the past ten years, since it was a Doubletree, and feel it has gone swiftly downhill in quality over the past year. The past three times we have stayed in the last year, there have been HUGE room parties that have been noisy enough to hear through concert-quality earplugs. I also feel like the bathrooms are never really clean and the room is sort of stale-feeling. Call me old-fashioned, but I like my room to smell like it is actually clean, not just dusted from the last person.
My last stay last week was with my newborn, who somehow slept through most of the noise from a party two doors down. They had a cooler in the hallway! Being that it is Philly, I did not want to meet my "neighbors" to ask them to keep it down, but by 12:30am, I had had enough. I called down to the front desk and was promptly put on hold for five minutes, before I could even say anything. When I was answered, the front desk person said they would send a manager up to investigate, but the noise of the party did not decrease, nor did I hear any knocks on a door, so guessing nothing happened. I did not want to change rooms, because I did not want to wake up my baby and be shuffled around in the middle of the night. The party died down around 2:30 and we slept in until 8 and promptly checked out.
Most of the time, my husband and I are literally just sleeping here, as my family does not have enough space at their house. The hotel was an affordable alternative. Now, with a baby, I don't feel like this is the sort of place I want to stay. I will definitely be looking for a new hotel to stay at, even if we have to go downtown.
I called Customer Support to complain and they said gee thanks for the complaint, but did not offer anything in the way of a discount or refund, just an apology for the bad stay.

title: “Oozing with charm”
text:
Just celebrated my wifes 40th Birthday at the Waldorf Astoria...somewhere she's always wanted to stay. OK the Hotel may be living on past reputation but it's still an amazing place oozing with character and charm and ideally located.
The rooms where spacious and clean with the most comfortable beds you could imagine. I requested a room change after the 1st night due to the noise from the extraction units outside...no problem...we were moved instantly (a high floor room is recommended)
The service from staff was 1st class 5 star...not rude at all...very helpful and courteous
Yes a one off experience & no doubt the budget seekers could get more for their money....

title: “Rude staff and Old smelly rooms”
text:
We stayed here for 3 nights in May, what a disappointment!
From the minute we walked in to check in the service was terrible. I have never come across such rude staff, they are not interested in the guests at all, we are gold card members with this particular chain of hotel, that meant absolutely nothing to them, as we couldn't of been given a worse room. Definitely needs renovating.
The room was disgusting old and smelly.We had a lovely view of a brick wall.
Also the parking is extremely expensive.
I would not recommend this hotel, and would never stay there again!

title: “Pleased with the Sheraton”
text:
We stayed here for 2 nights after a cruise and were quite pleased. Got it via Hotwire for around $130/night (more like $155 including taxes) and subsequently read some reviews about construction noise so had some concerns. Not an issue. Our room was on the 25th floor and was quite nice. A typical "conference" hotel. Located in an area with lots of nice shops and restaurants, particularly in a shopping center only 1 block away. Also an easy walk to Pike Place market and the waterfront. 
The Greyline tour buses and airport shuttle have a desk in the lobby and it was convenient as we took a tour to Mount Ranier one day and also used the shuttle to get to the airport. The room was fairly spacious with a big window ledge you could set things on, a large table for a desk, two chairs and a table for a reading corner, 2 beds with comfortable bedding. Attractive decor. 
We checked out the pool and it was OK. Kind of small and very crowded with families both times we went. The whole pool is 4 feet deep -- no shallow or deep end. My only minor complaint was that it was difficult to access the free internet. They had one computer located at the check-in desk and I had to check 4 times before it was available.

title: “A Series of Disappointments”
text: I begin this by saying that I am not wealthy nor a snob. Someone else was paying for a group of us to stay at this beautiful hotel, with access to the Concierge Club, to celebrate three birthdays. We had a similar trip two years ago to the R-C in Boston to celebrate another birthday in our group and could not say enough WONDERFUL things. They sent the birthday girl a basket, fell all over her, met every expectation and request. This hotel was definitely not on the same level as its sister. Upon check-in, there was a problem where we were told we would be charged an additional $300 per night. This was rectified quickly by the manager. Then, the rooms which were supposed to have queen beds had full (we were sharing), the Concierge Club only served wine, no liquor (Boston offered liquor all day), and not even the kind of wine we asked for. How hard is it when four guests are all asking for pinot grigio to get a bottle for them? Seriously??? You are the Ritz-Carlton, and you told four guests to go out and purchase their own bottle of wine, and that you would pour it for us. Thanks! We could have done that WITHOUT the Concierge Club. The food in the club was inconsistent (lousy breakfast, ok lunch, great sushi). Again, the main reason for our trip was to celebrate the birthdays (two of them were 40th) and it was stated on our confirmation so the hotel was aware. Not once did anyone even mention this. Please do not think I am a snob, I'm a regular schmoe who has worked in hotels and knows the importance of consistency throughout a brandname, and how to treat those paying at the top level. For the quality of this hotel's service, we could have stayed at a Marriott or Sheraton.

title: “Older ES in suburban location”
text: An older hotel that is overdue for updating. Rooms are clean but dated with older furnishings. Cooked to order breakfast is good as usual with ES, but nightly reception was just fair with very basic snacks. Fairly convenient location near freeway but have to drive a bit for any good restaurants.

title: “Good Hotel!”
text: I will come back, thank you! Not the best hotel I ever have been at but it suit its purpose.

title: “wonderful experience from front desk to check out”
text: Very nice stay,upgraded room.Concierge service the best.Room spacious ,very clean.Only problem is nightclub across the street on a busy night .Still loud at 2 a.m.,just indulge enough before retiring,take some tylenol p.m.s or go join them.Take trolley,filenes,fenway.Will go back asap.

title: “Cold and loud”
text: There was a Microsoft convention the week I stayed there, but usually this hotel averages $150-$160 per night after the $10 parking fee. That is high for just an average HIE that is not very new. The location is good, but there are not many amenities or restaurants within walking distance. The hotel is loud because the rooms do not have double windows. I brought my ear plugs, so I was able to take care of the noise issue for about $.99. I stayed in the 6th floor (highest level), so the rooms had very tall ceilings; therefore, it took forever to heat the room. I was so cold that the first two nights I had to sleep with my jacket on. I finally requested double blankets to the Latino mades. They were super nice, and they are really the only reason why I would consider coming back to this hotel. If you are driving an SUV you will have a hard time parking since the space is so so tight. Overall an almost below average hotel that is overpriced.

title: “One of the most unique and charming hotels I've ever seen...”
text:
We just spent our anniversary weekend at the Figueroa Hotel...and what a wonderful experience it was! The pictures online do not do this hotel justice...as soon as you see it you immediately feel the history associated with it! The decor is amazing...and everything is just beautiful! The pool/jacuzzi area is an oasis in the middle of downtown! So relaxing to sit out there around the beautiful plants, flowers and birds while sipping a cocktail. The staff was attentive, polite and very helpful. A VERY special thank you to Uno for making sure we had such a great room! The walls, the ceilings...all of the decor was an experience in itself. It was a special experience to be inside the room looking out at all the huge modern buildings including the Staples Center while at the same time being inside a room with such history and charm!
I highly recommend staying with Uno and his wonderful group of employees at the Fig...it is an experience you will remember and in our case cherish! You can stay at a Marriott or a Hilton no matter WHERE you travel...you will be hard pressed to find a hotel with such charm and personality at this hotel anywhere.
Thank you again Uno...and everyone at the Hotel Figueroa for making us feel so welcome and being a part of a very special weekend for us!!!

title: “Hotel Carlton, San Francisco”
text:
Located within walking distance of Union Square and the Civic Centre, the Hotel Carlton offers excellent value and a very welcoming atmosphere. The reception staff were very friendly, the lobby a comfortable place to hang out with daily "happy hour" complimentary wine from 5.30-6.00pm. 
The rooms are very comfortable (we had a King Sized bed) and provide adequate space. 
Not too many negatives to comment on - the complimentary wifi was inconsistent and the elevators a bit slow, but otherwise I'd highly recommend staying here. The general location is a bit on the "gritty" side, but gives a perspective of the real San Francisco.
The patrons were of all ages and nationalities.

title: “A special place in NYC”
text:
We live on Long Island and choose this for a weekend retreat. It was a perfect boutique hotel. The service was excellent. The atmosphere warm. The food excellent. 
We walked to many locations and felt as if we were coming home each time we returned. 
We will definitely go back

title: “Gross!”
text: We stayed here one Saturday evening as we were visting Philadelphia for a concert. The hotel prices across the city were extremely high due to the marathon and this was the most reasonably priced place we could find in the downtown area( $180 for the night). I read the reviews and figured we could deal for one night. We are honestly not picky but please let me tell you this place was DIRTY! Hairs on sheets, crumbs all over bedspreads, warped carpet, filthy bathroom, and doors that looked like someone dipped their hands in grease and wiped them all over it. Overall it was GROSS! We only slept there but this is not a place I would want to spend a weekend. Only plus was close location to Old City restaurants and attractions. We won't be back...don't do it!

title: “Luxurious Experience”
text: I found out about this hotel by using bing. As soon as I saw it I knew I had to go there. I live in NJ , which is not too far to travel and decided to go the the NY location. From the moment I got there it felt simply surreal, like I was dreaming or something. There was so much to explore and the food was to die for and very affordable..I highly recommend this hotel. I had stayed in the Waldorf Astoria last year and didn't enjoy the experience half as much as I enjoyed the Yotel. The staff there are very helpful and so you can be as autonomous as you like, starting with the touch screen check -in, or receive as much help as you need. The entire hotel, especially the rooms have the feel of being on a cruise; and i love the fact that the bed slides out for when it's time to sleep... . I recommend that you go to this hotel at least once just for the heck of it. it's an experience you will not regret.!

title: “Nice but cool”
text: Stayed at The Novotel for 5 nights from 9th March 2004. Found the hotel to be smart, clean and friendly. Room was small but acceptable. We were on the 11th floor with view of times square, street noise was not a problem althought the room felt cold and had a natural temp of 75 which could be increased to 90 with the air con but returned to 75 very quickly. We ate breakfast in the dinner under the hotel next to the entrance and had a good evening meal at the irish pub Rosie O`Grady`s just along the next block. We choose the Novotel for its reasonable price but would pay a little more and stay somewhere else on our next visit.

title: “Good stay. Great value”
text: This place has such a great value for the price. Quiet, clean room right off the freeway so its convenient. I take classes in sylmar which is why I stay at the good nite inn because I don't feel like driving back and forth from campus to my place. Service is great. I always ask for an early check in and they pretty much check me in before the 2 o clock check in time.

title: “Relaxing hotel”
text: Great hotel in Hotel Circle, loved it. Very realxing.. nice bed, shower, nice pool. took kids and teens with me and they really liked it. would stay again.

title: “Perfect”
text: I loved this hotel. I was the last of my friends to arrive, and they were all already out on the town. Greeted the minute I got there and they had my own key waiting (very friendly service), even though my friend had booked the room under his name. The bed was amazingly comfortable, and the bathroom was spotlessly clean. Just one of those rooms where you notice the small touches - seemed like they thought of everything. Not to mention the entire hotel is beautiful and right in the middle of everything. If I find myself in Chicago again I will definitely choose this hotel.

title: “VAcation layover”
text: My wife and I were headed for Orlando Florida and wanted to spend the night somewhere after the long drive from Maryland. We were refered to Microtel and had never heard of them before, upon our arrival we were impressed. The hotel itself was really great, the grounds well kept and the rooms were fabulous. We have recomended Microtel to friends and will continue to recomend them. We will also be staying there again next year on our next trip to Florida. The rates are outstanding for the quality of the rooms and the service.

title: “You get what you pay for.”
text:
We booked a reservation online and from the photos (advertisement), it looked great!. However, upon arrival, we had to wait outside the glass window to check in. Nobody was attending the front window so we stood outside waiting for someone to assist us for approx 5-10 minutes. Keep in mind that around the corner is not a safe area (kinda ghetto).
Once we checked in the room, it was NOT what we expected. 
This hotel might be haunted. The entire night I kept waking up, thinking someone was in the room with me. I tried to search online for the history of this hotel but couldnt find any information. 
I thought I was just imagining things so I just went to sleep.
I woke up in the middle of the night right after what appeared to be an out of body experience. Upon waking up, the room was cold.
I couldnt sleep the rest of the night. I watched TV and walked around the room and noticed what appeared to be blood on the box spring of my bed.

title: “great location, nice room”
text:
This was my first trip to New York, and we could not have asked for a better location. I was traveling with 2 friends, one of whom slept on a "cot" which she said was quite comfortable. The concierge was helpful, the lobby is lovely. We did not eat at the restaurant as there is so many other places to go. 
there are no ice machines, but a call to hotel services has some brought quite quickly, and the ice bucket is filled with the turn down service. Because of the location I would definitely go back again.

title: “Hundreds of trip advisors can't be wrong!”
text: I found this hotel on Trip Advisor and, following the rave reviews of other travellers, booked it for a weekend. It is a small, very friendly hotel. It is not opulent like one down the street, but it is much better in terms of staff and extras. The continental breakfast is enough to get your day started. The wine and cheese reception is lovely, however, I would prefer a choice of wine -- there were six bottles of white open and they were all Chardonay. The staff are all friendly and helpful and, because there are so few, one gets to know them giving the the feeling of truly being in a home away from home. My room was at the back of the hotel which didn't afford a great view, but it was so quiet with none of the traffic noise from the street that I would request a back room again. I would definitely stay at the Elan again if I am ever in Los Angeles.

title: “Little extras are nice”
text: Although we missed the blooming cherry blossoms due to an unusually warm winter this year, our stay at the Kimpton Monaco was delightful. It's great location made it an easy walk to most of our destinations--didn't take the metro at all and a cab only once. It's right across the street from the National Portrait Gallery and a pick up stop for the Grayline Double Decker bus tours. The staff is very friendly and helpful with directions and recommendations. We loved the complimentary wine reception each evening with appetizers. The only disappointment was the cost of breakfast. After the first morning, we ate it elsewhere.

title: “Great Choice for a City Stay!”
text: I stayed at the Hilton during the last week of April for a business meeting and was pleasantly suprised by the quality of all the hotel had to offer. For a busy business/convention/tourist hotel,it was in excellent condition,appearing to have been recently renovated. Rooms were large,clean and modernwith all ammenities you would expect. Walking distance to theaters,etc.. I extended my stay on a saturday evening for $ 179. I would stay here againeven for non business purposes.

title: “Nice surprise”
text: We were pleasantly surprised with this choice of an airport hotel. The rooms were clean, they had a manager's "meet and greet" the evening we were there...wine, beer, soda, soup, cheese and crackers, fruit, etc. Ample enough that we didn't even bother going out for dinner--although there were plenty of restaurant choices close by. Breakfast was fine--things were spread out so there weren't any crowded areas. We'd definitely choose this hotel again.

title: “A good choice for New Year”
text:
We stayed here for 6 nights over New Year this year and had a good stay.
Positives - Location well placed for 5th Avenue shops, Radio City and just a few blocks to Times Square. We walked everywhere or took taxis for getting Downtown. 
Room was large, modern and comfortable. Plenty room for suitcases and shopping bags!
Very good breakfast options and no evidence of long queues other reviewers had warned of. Really good if you are a Gold Hilton Honours members as get free coupons every day.
Small store within hotel to stock up on drinks and snacks if needed. 
Room service excellent.
Negatives - lobby was always crowded with people sitting and lying everywhere with laptops and devices to get the free internet. It was a bit strange and intimidating!
Not all of the hotel has modern rooms, we had booked a modern one then got upgraded at check-in to what turned out to be an older room on a higher floor. We didn't like it at all so we went straight back to lobby to get upgrade cancelled - strange I know, but the modern room was just so much better!
Room service is not all night, just until 1am. We made this mistake on New Years eve/morning after returning from Times Square celebrations. Also make sure you get a key for mini bar, they had run out when we were there so it was a very sober and hungry night!
I recommend if you can get a good price, we used Hilton's own website and found it to be fair.
Enjoy!

title: “Services and Staff were GREAT!!!”
text: Our stay was a very pleasant experience thanks to the services, location and especially the staff. Everyone working there went above and beyond making our stay pleasant!! We will be planning another trip soon and we will defiantly want to stay there again.

title: “Great Location”
text: I've often looked to TripAdvisor for guidance when looking for a Hotel but this is the first time I've actually written a review. I was looking for a Hyatt property as I am a passport member and so that limited me to 48Lex, Andaz on 5th, Grand Hyatt and the Hyatt Regency on the Hudson. After looking at all of these reviews my wife and I landed at 48lex and we were not disappointed. The staff was friendly and helpful getting us to our room even a little early for check in. We were upgraded to a corner suite that had an amazing view of the city with a modern yet comfortable feel. The lounge area proved to be a major plus for my wife in that it had a complimentary cappuccino machine that had amazing coffee. We used the concierge to get tickets to Mama Mia and although very convenient we feel we may have been able to get a better deal in Times Square. However for what we were asking of him he did his job and was courteous and helpful. The price for the room is a bit more than we would every pay out of pocket but it seems all hotels in Manhattan seem to be comparable. Full disclosure our night was free but they treated us as though we paid full price. We enjoyed our time so much we have already booked a three night stay for December.

title: “Perfect location & lovely rooms”
text: Everything was outstanding. Loved having a Keurig coffee maker in the room. Would love to stay here again! It was not inexpensive but worth it. Beautifully decorated too. With a wonderful restaurant attached.

title: “Reservation NOT Guaranteed!!!”
text: I too was screwed by this hotel's overbooking. Made an online reservation in early July for a Sept 24 stay. Used a credit card, and got a confirmation email stating the reservation was guaranteed. On August 19, over five weeks later, they called and basically said sorry we overbooked and your on your own now! I talked to the reservation manager and the only compensation was to give me a list of other hotels I might call! I have made a formal complaint with the Choice Hotels corporate office but so far am just getting the runaround. They say the Comfort Inn Denver must itself resolve the problem. I will update if it is resolved to my satisfaction, but for now, make a reservation at your own risk!!

title: “Great location”
text:
This is a nice cheap hotel right on the Riverwalk. It's at the end or start depending how you look at it. It's really quiet here so you can get a good nights sleep.
All of the resturants and shops on the Riverwalk are a 5 minute walk away, if that.
Very clean rooms, very friendly staff.
The hotel bar is cool too, you can order food in there, which is way quicker then if you went to the resturant in the hotel. Same food and prices and it's open later too.

title: “Great!!”
text: We always stay at LQ and this hotel by far is one of the best we've stayed at. The front desk was very nice and helpful. The hotel also had a great pool and beautiful view of downtown.

title: “Quiet, central hotel”
text:
This was the quietest hotel I've ever stayed at in NYC. I guess because it's new - we stayed in rooms on the 2nd and 3rd floors and never heard traffic or other room noises. 
The rooms are very small as you'd expect. The beds are comfortable as others have said.
The elevators are painfully slow to use so we were glad to be on lower floors so we could take the stairs. We didn't eat the breakfast - with Hot & Crusty Cafe bagels nearby we gave the typical Holiday Inn Express breakfast a miss.
The front desk staff were pleasant and helpful. I wish we'd gotten this on Priceline, but the rate wasn't horrible for NYC considering there were 4 adults in the room.
The biggest "minus" for me was the size of the bathroom - very small and very few "surfaces" to place towels, items on, more of a problem because there were 4 of us.
I would definitely stay here again and recommend to friends, especially if you can get a good price on the room.

title: “Loved it”
text: We arrived at the hotel and were immediately greeted by the valet. We walked in and were warmly greeted by the desk clerk. The hotel was beautiful, and our room was large, and comfortable. We loved the decor. The only thing I wouldn't recommend is the restaurant that is connected with the hotel. The hotel was excellent! We would stay there again.

title: “Wellington review”
text: My impression when we arrived in the Hotel was that the front desk personel was unfriendly and not very helpful. The room was very dark and the price was too high for this .

title: “Excellent Vacataion Getaway”
text:
This is a wonderful property to stay at for a family vacation. We had the presidential suite, which had excellent views. The grounds are gorgeous! There was a beautiful waterfall just outside our room and in addition to being close to the waterfalls village, we were close to another pool that was kind of in a secluded area. It was a very nice spot for a swim without the kids as there was no one else there. The room was immaculate and provided plenty of space for a family of five with children ranging from 3-19. It did not feel like we were in a hotel at all and having two bathrooms was a definite plus. The pool area was exceptionally clean and the kids had so much fun they did not want to leave. Even my three year old, which up until now would not get into a pool, loved it and didnt want to get out. The pool has a "beach entrance" where you walk into it, instead of having steps, so I think this made it easier for him to get used to it at his own pace. This was also a great location for smaller kids to play. We had a wonderful time and are looking forward to returning next year. 
If you are stayng over the weekend and are going to waterfalls village, make sure you go early to get good seats or rent a cabana. There are other pools at the property that are less crowded.

title: “Nice Rooms - Poor Bathrooms”
text:
We stayed for 5 nights in LA.
They were very ameanable to our religious needs as orthodox Jews.
Rooms are good sizes but the bathrooms are POOR!!!
When i mentioned this to the manager he said that he knew they were bad and acknowledged they were some of the worst in the business!!!
As it was our honeymoon they gave us access to the business lounge with complimentary breakfast and internet.
Location was good and maximum 20min drive to everywhere we wanted to get too.
Parking wasnt cheap - $17/day

title: “Nice enough hotel but very misleading promises and billing”
text:
We booked a substantial block of rooms here for a wedding and were promised a 25% discount if guests booked before a given deadline. But guests quickly discovered that the price they got was barely better than the price advertised on the hotel website for ordinary guests. Why? Because on any given day the actual rates they advertise and charge are, officially speaking, discounted between 10% and 20% off some imaginary "full" rate that, in practice, they never charge anyone. So our people were getting 25% not off the rate they would have gotten had they booked without the wedding discount, but off the imaginary "full" rate; which means that, in reality, the 25% discount was more like a 4% or 5% discount off of what they could have gotten just walking in off the street. Prior to arriving to the hotel, at least two guests called and e-mailed the hotel to get precise quotes on what their rates would be; e-mails were not replied to, and the people reached on the phone could never answer the question or find the reservation. It was like the William H Macy scene in "Fargo." And then finally, on top of all that, the final bills were larded with a $12 DAILY "Service Charge - Add-On" which, according to the contract, relates to things like the concierge service, daily newspaper, Wifi, gym, etc. - in other words, things they advertise as benefits of the hotel and that you would assume were included in the price.
Having said all that, it is a nice enough place as long as you get one of the rooms with a window that doesn't face a brick wall. It is very well located for a stay in Downtown LA, and the price you eventually wind up paying isn't terrible for a cute non-chain hotel in downtown (over a 9 night stay, all taxes and fees included, the price averaged $181/night, with the "wedding discount", for a room whose window looked at a brick wall). But the frankly deceptive billing practices did leave a sour taste in our mouth.

title: “Not impressed; well below average”
text:
I travel for business a lot and usually always priceline my hotels, and got this one via priceline for $60. It was the Sunday before Memorial Day, I had to travel on Memorial Day out of Baltimore Airport, so I'd figure I drive in a day early and have fun in the city.
What a below average experience:
1) Parking was a nightmare. The selfpark garage for the Sheraton only allows SUVs to park on the first level. Meaning if there are no spots you cannot go down lower levels, however you ONLY find that out after you are down there and there are cars behind you looking to park. Thankfully, a Valet guy was walking buy and was able to hop in and back my SUV up through the narrowest of alleys and garner me a spot that Houdini would have had difficulty finding. Unreal. I tipped him a few bucks for his effort. I have never seen a more dysfunctional parking garage, especially for $24 a day
2) The rooms are beat up. Old furniture, shower had plenty of mildew and ancient wallpaper in the bathroom. And it was clear the toilet had not been cleaned if you get my drift.
Also the rooms were cramped. Could not see how two people could fit with any comfort. Oh, and there was a hole in my window, not a crack but a physical hole. Yes, a hole the size of a thumb at the base. It looked like it has been there for a while. Have some pride and fix that management
3) Elevators. LOL. Be prepapred for a 5-10 minute wait and I am not kidding. I was on the top floor and it was frustrating waiting 5-10 minutes just to get to your room
4) Margarita at the hotel bar was $9. LOL. Those are NYC prices
The crowd in the hotel that night was painfully obnoxious, though I do not blame the hotel for that. There was a Heavy Metal concert in Baltimore which attracted some of the most bizarre people I have ever seen. Not sure why 25 years olds cover themselves with tatoos. You realize one day you will be 40 and will look even more stupid? Lots of heavy metal people loitering around in black tee shirts with dyed black hair
The Lacross championships were also in town, so there were a lot of drunk college kids in the hotel, but oh well. That actually brought back memories being drunk in college. I am sure I annoyed plenty of 40 year sold business men in my college days. LOL.
I walked down to HarborBay which is a few blocks away. That was a good time, though the seafood I had was terrible down there. You'd think on the water they could learn how to cook shrimp.
Just a lousy experience. I just did not like this hotel and if you look at my many reviews, I am certain not particular. But this place was weak.

title: “A Remarkable Experience”
text:
As a meetings planning coordinator for my employer, we held a four day meeting at the Renaissance Montura. There were 140 employees in attendance. 
I was very impressed with the professionalism I encountered with the hotel management and banquet staff. The customer service was outstanding. They all exceeded my expectations.
The sleeping rooms were clean and neat, and the beds were comfortable. The meeting space was very accomodating to our needs. Food and beverage service was great.
Most importantly, the meeting attendees had positive comments about the hotel staff and the hotel property.
With all this said, as the opportunities present, I will hold more meetings at the Renaissance Montura.
For many years I have planned business meetings with many chain hotels throughout Southern California. The Renaissance Montura is a 5-Star hotel in many respects.

title: “Very pleased!”
text:
- Excellent location
- Comfortable, supportive, king sized bed
- storage space for luggage
- free access to in-room safe
- reasonable bathroom amenities 
- good sized writing desk for planning your day
- helpful staff (didn't call on their help much though)
- slightly noisy with ventilation ducting and noise from the corridors but acceptable still
- refurbishment work not a problem (carpet laying still when we arrived)
- near Union Square so some noise associated with proximity. Not too bad. 
Not a large room that we stayed in but we merely slept here. It puzzles me as to why people expect a tennis court sized room....are they coming to sleep and visit the city or stay inside the whole trip???
We would recommend this hotel.

title: “Good value and great location”
text: We were very happy with our stay at the Belle Claire. Neighbourhood was good - safe and not too touristy! Excellent location with subways closeby on Broadway at 72nd and 79th Sts. We stayed 2 nights in an economy room with shared bath first - room was very small and a bit stuffy, never had any problems with shared bath room - clean and no one else used it when we needed it! Overall pretty good value. We upgraded the next 2 nights to a Queen room with private bath. This room was excellent, very roomy, good sized bathroom and clean. Very comfortable - we even got a view towards the Hudson river. Staff were helpful. The Manhattan Diner across the street was also very good. If we visit NYC again we will definately stay at the Belle Claire again.

title: “Would stay again”
text:
Room was very clean with ample soap, towels etc. Room was quite small but that was to be expected in an historical venue. Hotel is directly across from the Alamo and near the trolley station and Riverwalk. The front desk clerk seemed uninformed about the area, but tried to be helpful.. The pool (which we didn't use) was small but there were plenty of fresh towels and chairs around. The only negative about staying downtown is the high price of parking. Seems that the finite amount of parking should be considered by hotel management and a way worked out to benefit guests and staff alike. 
Would consider staying here again.

title: “First class all the way”
text: I am an event planner and brought a group of 150 people to the Arizona Grand for our annual convention. The resort staff was the best I have ever worked with. The food was absolutely delicious and the facilities were beautiful, functional and clean. The property is absolutely gorgeous and we were treated like royalty. I plan on returning for a leisure trip so that I can enjoy more time at the water park and spa. We had several golfers in our group that raved about the golf course. I highly recommend the AZ Grand Resort for a conference or for a family vacation.

title: “Its not worth it!!!!!!!!”
text:
Do not stay here unless you want to be ignored, put on hold, charged un realistic amount of money for room service, I just do not understand this click of a hotel concept whom would possibly want to 250$ and up a night for these experiences?? Could someone please explain this to me???
Stay at the Fairmont Olympic next door great service, super friendly staff very welcoming made us feel totally at home and we were not even guests aghhhhhh...............

title: “Fantastic stay for all ages”
text:
Recently spent 5 nights at the Liaison with my husband, 5 year old twins, in-laws and 16 year old cousin visiting from Italy and we all had a fantastic time. The best part of the hotel is the location...short walk to Union Station which has shopping and many dining options. Other Pros:
rooftop pool (lots of seating and it's open late. Nice bar for drinks right there as well), room was clean and modern and beds were extremely comfortable (after the first night home my daughter said the hotel bed was more comfortable than her bed!), concierge was very helpful in recommending dinner options and getting us reservations, the gentlemen working outdoors always had a bottle of cold water for us. Our room was on the 8th floor and although we didn't have much of a view it wasn't noisy at all. Elevators were fast as well. The food at Art and Soul was great (breakfast one day and room service one night) but was VERY VERY VERY expensive. If I had to think of a CON it would be that the bathroom is small and there really isn't a countertop around the sink. This was our first trip to Washington and we loved it so we'll be back and we would choose Liaison as our resting spot for sure.

title: “I wish I had read the reviews instead of trusting the pictures.”
text: We had three rooms in the hotel. One had tears in the sheets. One had wet towels on the sink. Two of the tv remotes didn't work. The toilets did not flush as they should have. The breakfast consisted of an open loaf of bread, bagels, and rolls. There was dry cereal -- but no milk. (It was to be there "in 20 minutes", but it never made it.) The coffee pots were empty. When the worker was told, she went out to smoke before she made another pot. There was a hot waffle iron, but there wasn't any mix. There was one napkin on the counter. You had to go to the reservation desk to obtain a plate or bowl. The help was rude.

title: “Very Special”
text:
Memphis is a super place and staying downtown is the icing on the cake. The Madison Hotel is VERY, VERY special. It's got great art, great decor, great and comfy rooms and a great staff.
Be sure to give it a try.

title: “Exceptional boutique hotel with minor issues”
text: My fiance and I stayed at this hotel for 2 nights over the x-mas holiday. Firts of all, the location is beautiful, nestled in the middle of Pacific Heights, which is essentially several square blocks of mostly older mini-mansions. Parking was never a problem right on the street alongside the hotel. At check-in, we were told we were upgraded to a "junior suite" at no additional charge, and we didn't even request one. The hotel is very antique-looking and charming, with creaky wooden floor planks and all. The free breakfast buffet was very good (fruits, cereals, toast, muffins and fresh squeezed o.j.) and the staff was great. We were treated to nightly turn-down service and the staff went out of their way to make our stay comfortable (bringing us a space heater when it got a little cold and calling taxis for us whenever needed). My only complaints are that there was some renovation going on during our stay and it was quite loud, but it was quiet at night and we were out all day sightseeing so it wasn't a huge factor. Also, our upgraded suite was on the dining room level, which is essentially underground, so we had absolutely no view. Other than that, it was very comfortable and a decent value for San Francisco.

title: “A sleepover hotel”
text:
We have stayed at this hotel a few times this year. Very convenient to Los Angeles Airport, rooms are nice if you get a remodeled room but please do not expect a soft pillow, they are like rocks! I am taking my own pillow with me lately. 
The shuttle service is spotty, it is not always every 15 or 20 minutes as they will tell you. Be patient and plan ahead if your time is tight. 
We will go back with our own pillows and allowing plenty of time to get to the airport.

title: “Very Nice Place, Great Location!”
text: We recently spent 3 nights at the Inn at the Market in Seattle, Wa. The Inn over looks Pike's Market and it was wonderful to gaze down at the market or to the bay for a beatufiul view. We had a city side room which was a bit noisey for us but we are not used to city sounds. The room was lovely. The beds super comfortable, along with the pillows and bed linens. Our room had a large bathroom which was nice. We had evening turn down service and a daily paper. The staff was very accomodating and professional. There are many restaurants right outside the property. They also have a lovely rooftop patio/garden that looks on the bay if you need a rest. We would stay again!

title: “"Loved Hotel"”
text: I had a wonderful stay here at the Sheraton. I thought the staff did an outstanding job and was very please with my accoodations. I always read the stats of any hotelprior to checking in and to my suprise I was wrong. I searched hotels on houston and found this hotel to be of great value and it was. The lounge and staff made me feel right at home as I am from another country. "Thank you Staff at Shearaton for making my stay a pleasant one"

title: “Starlight Room”
text: Go to the TOP! Dance with the stars!!! Watch the city twinkle like a land of stars or diamonds at night.

title: “really a luxury hotel”
text:
I stayed at the DuPont with collegues while we were in Washington for a Congress.
The DuPont is really welll ocated with spacious rooms, clean, and with a really good service.
Definitivey a good hotel to explore Washington

title: “Excellent Location”
text:
As i was taking the trip to NY with my 27 year old daughter i was a bit worried about the negitive reviews, although the Hotel requires a complete revamp everything was clean, and the hotel staff very helpful, room was large ; bathroom small ; strange with wash hand basin outside bathroom sited in room, A/C did not work : downside was all rooms when their toilets flushed the noise was unbelivable also no easy door closures, so you heard a constant slamming of doors through the night. Did not use Resturant, used Deli on corner good value for money
Location Excellent
Staff Excellent
Room Clean (Need revamp)
Bathroom Small Shower Good
Flush & Doors Noisy
A/C (Not working)
 KELLY & EMMA CARDIFF S WALES

title: “Nice but overpriced...”
text: I've stayed at many Marriott before and always had good experience but I can't say the same for this one. For start, it was expensive. I booked a room for 4 people and specifically requested 2 double beds. At check in, the staff told me they didn't have any of the room type I requested and that I would have to live with a king and a roller bed. I was too tired to argue so I took it. So it was 3 people on the king and 1 on the roller. The king bed was nice and very comfortable. However, the roller was not comfortable at all and my friend couldn't sleep all night. The hotel itself was very nice and our room as nice and clean as expected. However, at 6 am, I was awaken by the construction outside my window. Whatever you do, do NOT take out the drinks from the fridge because you will get charged even if you don't drink it. I simply took some stuff out to look at them, at check out, I had to argue with the front desk for charging me. Overall, I would say it was a nice hotel for couples, but not for singles.

title: “Very good location, with staff interested in helping your experience.”
text: This hotel is not going to impress you if you only stay at 5-star hotels, but it is very clean, and the staff work hard to give you a great experience. The complimentary breakfast is quite good, and the location makes most of downtown very convenient for walking or riding public transit. If you absolutely must have wi-fi in your room, you might want to consider elsewhere. I was never able to use the Internet on any device from my room, and others I spoke to had the same experience. Most public spots in the hotel had perfectly fine wi-fi, and it is free, and reasonably fast.

title: “Very nice”
text: Stayed at the Westin Dec 30 thru Jan 01,2007. We went to the Bears/Packers game . The people and staff were very kind. Our luggage was lost and they helped us out on were to find things to tide us over until our bags FINALLY arrived. The beds were wonderful. The rooms were a little too warm for our taste. All in all, a very nice hotel.

title: “Stay Away”
text: To begin with this room had very poor housekeeping. Missing a towel, a lamp was unplugged and never plugged back in and there was a dirty cleaning rag left on top of the microwave. Fan in the bathroom was broken. We should have left then but were very tired. Traveling cross country from CA to TX. The girl at the desk, Sara, did come at once with the towel and she was very accomodating. It wasn't until I looked at the blankets that I realized how bad it was. They were all pilled and had holes in them. They did appear to be clean but I could not sleep well using them. The lighting was good. They had a good breakfast.

title: “great stay”
text:
Recently returned from a stay at this hotel with my daughter. We loved it. Room was huge. with great comfy bed. Great to have a kitchen with stove, big fridge freezer and microwave oven. Coffee and tea provided too. We had a great view of the Chrysler building.Good little diner round the corner (Murray Hill Diner) and deli next door serves great sandwiches.
Subway is close by; and Macy's within walking distance. Great for shopoholics like us!
This hotel is a good choice if you like more space and kitchen facilities. and dont mind being a little bit out of all the chaos of Times Square.

title: “A Perfect Fit For a True NYC Experience”
text: As a New York resident, I was suspect about staying in a New York hotel. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Hotel Giraffe was the perfect option after getting engaged. The room was spacious, clean and beautiful, we were given a bottle of prosecco after we noted our engagement and, because we arrived so late, we were "upgraded by necessity" into a suite. The staff was extremely friendly and helpful. If I was an out-of-towner, this is definitely a better option than a traditional chain hotel.

title: “More then I expected”
text: After making reservations I was reading the reviews of the Menger Hotel, I was was having second thoughts about canceling them. Was I glad we went ahead it was everything I expected it to be and more. If you are going and expecting Ice machines, vending machines, and a video arcade on every floor this is NOT the place. If you are expecting to step back in time and spend some time in an exceptionally nice restored hotel then the Menger is the one place to stay. Everything we wanted to see or do was convenient to the hotel, Riverwalk across the Alamo Plaza, RiverCenter around the corner up Blum Alley, Alamo next door, Trolley tours, tourist info center, city buses, all this within easy walking distance, we spent three nites and if we ever return to San Antonio you can bet the Menger will be at the top of the list. Really had a great time and would recomend the Menger to anyone

title: “Just average. Pool under construction-bad news if you have kids!”
text: If you read the reviews, you will notice that people complain about the small size of the rooms and rightfully so. Not a lot of room to move around in there. When we arrived, they informed us the pool was being remodeled. We were NOT happy to hear that. They told us we could use the pool at the Rivercenter but of course, we would have to pay the parking fee over there. I asked the Manager for a better answer and was informed we could use the location at the Market Square and not pay parking. We went there but, still a hassle and not convienent. We did a lot of sight-seeing so we paid the steep price for the valet service. If you are going to hang on the river, I suggest you skip the valet and park it yourself. The valet garage cannot hold more than two vehicles so you may end up waiting a bit. The entrance to the Riverwalk is fairly new and you are not too far from the resturants. A little over- priced for me. Will not stay there again due to the small rooms.

title: “Fantastic, but it is what it is! If you want luxury, pay for it elsewhere.”
text:
We stayed here from April 20 - 25 2011. It was roughly $159 per room per night for three of us before tax, which is added onto the price on arrival. This is standard practice in some NY hotels, it's not a con.
The woman on reception was nice and checked us in quickly. We had a room on floor 7 which was split into two. We had a double bed in one, two singles in the other, with the bathroom (shower and toilet) in the middle. Each room had a TV and a seperate sink, and one room also had a microwave. There was also a table and chairs. The rooms are a bit basic and tired but there's nothing wrong with them generally. The doors lock, the beds are comfy, everything works. They serve thier puropse well.
The location alone makes the value for money of this hotel fantastic. There's a subway station two minutes away (79th & Broadway, 1 & 2 lines) that takes you straight to all the action in under 10 minutes. It's also right near Central Park and only a block from Broadway.
Overall the place is great for people who just want somewhere cheap, safe and convenient to sleep and shower. If you spend any more time in there other than to do those things then you're doing New York all wrong anyway!

title: “Absolutely Fabulous”
text: Stayed here for two nights, what a start to my tour of America. Loved this place. Thick carpets, big, comfortable bed, fully equipped kitchen, nice furniture, and what a view, Madison Square Garden twenty feet across from the hotel. I would happily have spent my whole holiday i this hotel. Penn Station underneath MSG, Maceys on the corner, transport at your front door, beautiful palatial lobby. It cost £150 per night, very reasonable for Manhattan.

title: “Surprisingly wonderful!”
text: Because of some online reviews I was a little worried however, we had a great experience here. I stayed for business travel with a 5 year old child. The room was large compared to others I have seen in the area. The furnishings were nice and the room had a rerigerator and microwave. There was also a substantial closet with full size ironing board and iron. Upon request we were given a coffee maker for the room. There was a continental breakfast of danish, juice, and coffee. For those needing more to eat IHOP is literally across the parking lot. Free parking was another park. My favorite part of the stay was the friendly service and good value. I found this motel a hidden gem in the city. It is within convenient walking distance to Crissy field, the Exploratorium, and Palace of Fine arts and not too bad of a walk to Ghiradelli square which I did easily with a 5 year old. I will definitely be back to stay at Presidio Inn again. I think the star rating should be higher.

title: “Great business hotel in heart of the city”
text: The hotel is just off of Michigan Avenue (Miracle Mile) by the John Hancock Blgd. The rooms were adequately large, with a super soft and comfortable bed, very nice bathroom with a rain shower, and a stocked minibar and coffee maker. The bar downstairs in the lobby gets crowded at night and the service is less than great (surly bar staff), but the rest of the staff are good. The doormen are great with getting you a cab. Lots of restaurants and shopping in the blocks around the hotel so it's a great choice for enjoying the local digs.

title: “Nice little hotel!”
text:
The reviews are true! This hotel was a great find in San Francisco. For the price I'd have to say that I don't know how you'd beat it. 
We arrived early and the front desk was accomodating saying they would call immediately when the room was available and giving us a brief overview of the area. I'm confident in saying that if I had any questions about the city the hotel staff would have been more than happy to answer them. They did give us a great recommendation for a local Italian restaurant and seemed to truly enjoy talking about the neighborhood! 
Location, location, location. We loved being in North Beach. It was near many major tourist attractions but had such a different vibe than the Union Square area. It was truly a cool neighborhood with restaurants & cafes; a great place to "come home" to after exploring the city.
The room was smallish but spotless and we thought the bed was comfortable. It was very uniquely decorated. Everything worked fine. 
Complimentary sherry in the evenings was a nice touch.
Overall this is an excellent choice for many travelers. However, if you need a big hotel with many amenities then this may not be the place for you. I will definitely be back and make this my San Francisco hotel in the future. Very highly recommended.

title: “AWESOME!!!”
text: This was our first trip to Chicago. We splurged a little and stayed at the Palomar, and it was worth every penny! We absolutely loved it. The room was spacious, and clean. We stayed in the deluxe spa room, and again it was worth the extra money. The room was big, the bathroom with whirlpool/hot tub was clean and inviting. Even the location of this place was great, a block off Michigan, and surrounded by lots of stores and restaurants. But the best part of pur stay without question was the SERVICE. Anything you need, the concierge at the Palomar has you covered. Bobby was the gentleman that took care of us, and he was fantastic. He got us in for breakfasts, dinners, and even entertainment that was unavailable on our own. And everywhere we went, people greeted us like they knew we were coming. If you're staying in Chicago, you can't go wrong at the Palomar!!

title: “Fun and Unique”
text: I've never stayed at a hotel like this before, but it was a lot of fun. The lobby had computer kiosks for the check-in process, but since I was with a group, the hotel staff did our check-in for us. The fourth floor has a restaurant (or two?- I'm not sure) and a lounge type area. I didn't check it out at night to see if it was busy. Our "cabin" was small, but not uncomfortable. The only thing I didn't like about the room was the lack of privacy in the bathroom. The only thing that separated the bathroom from the bedroom was a partial glass wall and curtain that could be pulled across. The bed felt like it would be uncomfortable because it was hard, but I slept very well. Breakfast was available in the lounge- muffins, coffee, and tea were free.

title: “One of the best San Diego waterfront locations”
text: The Hilton San Diego Bayfront Hotel is one of the best locations for views of the harbor, Petco Park and the city. Conveniently located within a short walk to the "Gas Light District" where there are many fine restaurants, bars and the light rail system or trains north to Los Angeles etc.

title: “Nothing Fancy but above slightly average”
text: This was a good half way marker for us while traveling to Texas. Well off the beaten path of the road where you are not bothered by the noise of the interstate. Rooms were clean, staff was nice and pleasant, pool was small yet adequate. I have stayed at other Fairfield hotels and found this one to be in line with the others. There advertisement was all true with stated amenities. All and all, it was a pleasant stay.

title: “Great Location... Ok Hotel...”
text: Great Location... but there are many other hotels very close that may be better and cheaper. The pool is very small and the sun only hits on one side so there are about 8 chairs available. The pool needs a skimmer. Nobody eats at the restaurant because it is way over priced and there is good food just down the walk. The room was ok but the bed was bad. The comforter was itchy and felt like a Brillo pad. The TV was ok ... fuzzy and the elevator closest to us was not working!

title: “Great value; good location”
text: My husband and I were very pleased with our 3-night stay at this Quality Inn, Seattle Center. Couldn't have a better location for getting around Seattle. Also, we were able to walk to restaruants without any problems. Our room and the bathroom were small but clean and comfortable. Breakfast was excellent. And we had covered parking. Also, a guest laundry was valuable to us and not available in many motels. The price for Seattle accommodations fit our budget-minded travel requirements very well. Only problem was very poor internet connections. Called about the problem and was told that the hotel was not getting good service from their provider. A little annoying.

title: “Last minute accomadation”
text: Turned out really good. Easy to find on Boylston. Free Internet and printer(nice). Friendly staff at check in. Thought maybe would get a better deal booking directly with the hotel, but got a cheaper last minute deal on expedia- prepaid. Room was all we needed. Clean, cool. Private bath. Nice view of brick out the window. Room had a queen bed and a hide-a-bed sofa if you needed more sleeping space. Hallway was a little bit noisy in the morning being in front of the elevator but nothing crazy.

title: “Nothing Special”
text: I booked the Michaelangelo for a recent business trip and was not bowled over. The reviews here made it sound much better than it was. I stayed 5 nights in an "Executive" room. It was very large for a NY hotel room. The decor was fine - nice, but nothing notable. The television was very small - I'm guessing 20 inches. That just doesn't cut it in today's hotel market, in my mind. The bathroom was clean, shower head was adequate, and it was decorated nicely with lots of granite/stone. My room was very very noisy. I was on the 5th floor and faced onto 51st Street. I did not ask to move because I don't think the 7th Ave side would have been any better. And whoever wrote that the airconditioning units are noisy is right - I ended up turning the thermostat way down during the day so the room was freezing when I got in at night and just tried to stay comfortable under the covers. The bed was comfortable, but again - nothing notable. The bedspread was a little past its prime (and I thought about the reviewer who said it used to have buttons that have since all disappeared - mine was the same way!!!) I recently stayed at the Sofitel and would definitely recommend it over the MIchaelangelo if you want to stay on the West side. All in all - nothing is wrong with the Michaelangelo - it just doesn't deserve to be ranked where it is on Trip Advisor.

title: “Good weekend stay”
text: My wife and I stay here quite regularly when we visit Seattle to see a football game. The shuttle from the airport is always on time and operates almost 24 hours a day. The rooms are typical Marriott and always clean and functional. The restaurant is good with some very good items and others quite normal. If there is a large convention in the hotel (which occurs quite regularly on weekends) be careful where your room is(stay away from pool side). The hotel is old but has been remodeled very recently but the noise in the hallways and especially around the pool can be very annoying. Standard complaint is the charge for internet usage.

title: “Lost reservations + impolite staff= :(”
text: This hotel is beautiful and in a great location, but if you stay here be sure to confirm then reconfirm your reservations. It took 30 minutes to reserve two rooms and when I called to confirm about three days before my trip, they could not find the reservation so I had to start over. When I arrived at the hotel, they only had one room reserved. The staff member found another room but said I had to contact the Marriott reservation line to make sure they did not charge me for the room twice because just because she could not find the reservation did not mean it did not still exist...seriously?!!! The general attitude of the staff was rude and unhelpful. This hotel would be perfect if it were not for the people running it.

title: “No Problems here”
text:
This hotel was fine, no problems at all. We had two rooms, a double and a twin on fourth floor. Hotel is normal Holiday Inn standard, staff helpfull and friendly. Hotel is clean and tidy and in a great position in Fishermans Wharf. We were able to walk to everything in the area and had easy access to transport to City & Bay - all buses, trams, trolly, cable car & boat.
I would reccomend this hotel to anyone, or any family. Hotel bar is OK, had free drink every night as Priority member, suggest you look for food outside hotel as local choice is fantastic.

title: “Great family rooms”
text: We were really pleased with our room, a King Kids Deluxe. It had lots of space. There was a sofa bed, king bed, bunk beds, with the bottom bunk a double size, plus a table and four chairs. Great for a family on a trip. There's also a great gym, small pool which does pool-side drinks and food service. The shuttle buss runs hourly too and from Universal and is very prompt. The only down side is that on top of the not cheap room rate, they then charge you per day for parking - it would feel so much better if they didn't try and make extra money this way. However, we would stay again just for the room size and quality.

title: “Great value in Inner Harbor”
text:
We stayed for a full week in May 2004, attending a conference at the Baltimore Convention Center. Hotel is directly behind Brookshire Suites, two short blocks from the Harborplace, and a maximum five minute walk from the Convention Center. 
Lets face it - almost all of the Inner Harbor hotels are overpriced, tired, and in need of revamping, so the brand new Hampton Inn is a pleasant change. Very clean, nicely decorated in Hampton tradition. Good indoor pool in basement, very small gym (saw noone in it), and small business center, also in basement. 
All rooms offer free high speed internet if you have your own laptop, free local telephone calls, fridge, microwave, etc. Free continental breakfast is good, and (while we were there) the hotel was offering a complimentary Manager's Reception Monday and Wednesday nights.
Suites just have larger rooms and sink benches. None of the suites have seperate bedrooms, and both myself and colleagues were bumped out of our originally confirmed suites into standard rooms until we complained. 
The hotel is still going through some staff teething problems. Staff attitudes ranged from extremely helpful, to disinterested. Housemaids did an average to poor job of daily room servicing, and the staff on the weekend didn't seem to be able to cope with simple duties like keeping the breakfast buffet supplied.
On the whole though, comparing the price and quality to other Inner Harbor hotels, this new Hampton is a great deal.

title: “Love our stay!!!”
text: We recently stayed at this hotel and the hotel is not ordinary Holiday Inn. This is very contemporary and eclectic hotel. The staff at the front desk is great, especially Veronica and Gloria. They went above and beyond for me. The staff in the restaurant is very professional and efficient. The staff serves a great breakfast buffet for $10 and the service provided by Vanessa and Ana is excellent. The rooms are great and impeccably clean. I did have little problem with the shuttle running behind, but the manager Sal took us in his personal car. Now this establishment has a lot of professional people!! I’ll be back soon!!

title: “perfect hotel”
text: Just a wonderful place. Great location. Helpful and friendly staff. Elegant yet casual. Great restaurant.

title: “Nice stay”
text: We spent a night here while my little son was having tests at Johns Hopkins. There were a few little glitches with our room upon check in, but these were quickly handled by the staff. Everyone (front desk, maintenence, and valet) were really nice and the kids loved the crab hats they received at Crabby Hour. You cannot beat the location, we had a balcony room that overlooked the aquarium. You could walk to many restaurants and of course the aquarium in less than 5 minutes. The only negative was there was fairly loud music coming from the lobby until after midnight. All of the rooms open onto the lobby so I did wonder why the music was on so loud for so long on a weeknight. However I could tolerate it so I never called the front desk and complained. We would definetly stay here again.

title: “Very Nice”
text: I stayed here for 4 nights in June and really enjoyed it. Perfectly located for seeing the sights of Philadelphia. The hotel is clean and the staff are friendly. Just one word of warning though, I’d booked a ‘twin’ so expected 2 beds, but they told me a ‘twin’ was a single. I would stay there again.

title: “Very good services, great room, excellent stay”
text:
Excellent staff, very good location, beautiful hotel and room, very clean, thanks!
The hotel is well located in Downtown area & very good value for money. Free internet in lobby and room.
We found it was within walking distance of some shops, and we were given a map and clear instructions by the front of house staff. It is a fantastic hotel, and worth a detour if you are in Los Angeles.
They also gave us complimentary juice/ bed tea/coffee in the morning delivered to your room at your choice of time.

title: “Not Up To Expectations”
text:
We were booked into the hotel by an airline as "distressed travelers". That means we had a voucher for the hotel and the restaurant. Our room looked nice until we looked a little closer. The carpet was in bad shape especially around the bar sink. The ceiling over the shower was broken through from water damage. 
Like most of the "nicer" (read more expensive) hotels, they want to charge you for internet. I don't get this because cheap hotels along the interstate in the midwest seem to be able to offer internet access for no additional charge along with towels and a tv.
My big complaint was that they took our meal voucher in the restaurant but in the morning, the amount of the voucher ($14) appeared on our room charges. It took a great deal of arguing to get it off the bill.

title: “Close to the airport. Best bar in a bar close to an airport, the staff.”
text: The greatest part about this place is the fact the have a fully stocked bar. Another great fact it is it is 5 minutes from the airport. But the rooms are clean and the staff is great. But the icing on the cake is it has one of the greatest bartenders in the world. Jen. She knows all of the drinks, is lovely, and has great jokes. Stay here.

title: “Great location and value”
text:
We spent 6 nights at the Tremont Hotel and were very happy with the service we received. The staff responded very quickly with any requests, which included oiling a squeaky door and fixing a burnt light bulb in the bathroom. The hotel is well located just across the street from the Hancock building and a 5 minute walk to the lake. The restaurant next door, Ditkas, was great for an afternoon lunch, dinner or a late night drink.
The main elevator did stop working on the last day (Memorial Day) and that was a bit of a problem with the number of guests, but the service elevator was available. The rooms could be updated, but the bed was very comfortable and reasonably sound proof.

title: “3 nights on business”
text: You will be unpleasantly surprised if you are expecting "typical" Crowne Plaza but it isn't bad by comparison to most other hotel brands--It is just a bit dated. It is very close (a couple of blocks) to the convention center which is VERY nice. I would stay again.

title: “Value for Moneyvalue”
text:
I have stayed at Hotel 41 twice now, once in Summer and again in Winter last year. The first time I stayed in the summer I had a standard room which was very small (I have stayed in similar sized rooms in London however!). The room was generally clean apart from around the bed area (I dont think there is enought room to get a hover arounbd the bed). For two people the room is a little cramped and you virtually have to climb on the bed from the bottom. As it was summer and about 90 degrees, the air conditioning was really needed, but proved to be noisy at night - A good tip though is turn the temprature right down during the day to as cold as pssible and then turn it off at night to get a good night sleep.
My second visit in November I chose a superior room (not much more money). Room was bigger with a fridge, which was handy. 
All in all the hotel is good value, breakfast is good with bagels etc. Staff friendly and if you do have any problems they are always on hand to help. The hotel is centrally located for everything and is less than 1 min walk from Port Authority Bus station which is handy if travelling from airports by bus. It is also a short distance $5 taxi ride from Penn Station, which is again ideal for the airports. 
All in all the hotel offers value for money

title: “enjoyed my stay here”
text:
stayed here mid oct 2007,used their suttle bus from the airport ,no charge.
rooms very nice ,clean and comfortable,also in room safe.
very good continental breakfast,big selection.
about a ten min walk to the waterfront attractions.
front desk staff very helpful

title: “Chicago baseball weekend”
text:
My 13-year-old son and I stayed for a baseball weekend. The hotel is conveniently located between Wrigley and US Cellular. I was looking for a reasonable and safe place to stay and I was very pleased.
 The staff was pleasant and helpful. The room was clean and comfortable. An east / west and north / southbound bus is available right outside the door. The "L" is a friendly shuttle away. I would recommend this hotel to anyone who is looking for a simply lovely experience in Chicago right outside the hustle and bustle of the city.

title: “5 Star Service!!”
text: My family and I recently stayed at the Magic Castle Hotel! The minute I walked in the lobby, I felt at home. Checking in was easy and painless! The front desk agents were all friendly, walked us to our room and they explained everything about the hotel. Within walking distance to all the major Hollywood atractions, this hotel is ideal. Our room was spacious. We got a 2 bedroom suite with a ktichen. This was great! The breakfast is great! Juice, great scones, cereals and fruit! We ate out by the pool and even met another family that was staying there. This is not your typical hotel. If you are looking to be treated well, you must check this place out. We came back from a long day and was suprised to see our beds were turned down with chocolate on our pillows! Overall, great stay! I wanted to say a special thanks to Gretchen and Mike, who planned out our entire stay! Thanks again! If ever in LA, we will make sure we will stay here!

title: “Great experience!”
text: The hotel and room were very clean and the kids enjoyed the pool. They were having problems with the phone lines and the staff was dealing with that problem well with warnings and apologies, etc. They were fixed by the next day.

title: “Good location, older hotel”
text:
We stayed with our family of 4 in this hotel for 2 nights in a 2-queen bed room. The beds felt older but my husband (who is very picky about beds) found them comfortable. The room is quite large, and as mentioned by other reviewers, the staff was very accommodating.
However the rooms could use an upgrade- the furnishings in our room were a bit worn. Also there is construction ongoing across the street which started up about 8am on weekdays. The two queen bed rooms are NOT available with tubs (only showers) and the plumbing system is very old....leading to weak water pressure in the shower and a very slow draining sink. 
The breakfast buffet included hot eggs and sausage as well as a variety of other standard breakfast fare. Make sure this is included in the rate when you book the room.
If I were to return to Boston, I would probably look for a hotel in better condition.

title: “great stay”
text: Just got back from Chicago and had great stay at the W City Center. Hotel was in a great location for us. Trip was a sports wknd with 3 other buddies. we went to a Bulls game and a Bears game. Took advantage of the Acura experience on the way to both events. Dillion was able to arrage this for us before we even landed in the city. After arriving at about 10 pm on the Friday we were given rooms beside each other. Not sure why this seems to almost be impossible at other hotels, but it was a lot more convienient and a nice surprise given our late arrival. Hotel was in a greet location for us and rooms were a good size. I would stay here again if I was going back to Chicago.

title: “Good value for your money”
text: stayed there for 6 nights Aug 2011. Hotel is clean and has a great gym and good neighborhood. will stay there again.

title: “Personal Service at its Finest!”
text: We loved the Hotel Adagio. It was a quaint, boutique hotel in the heart of all the action in San Fran. Upon our arrival, there was a bottle of wine, a hand written welcome card, and a detailed list of attractions to see including a brief (also hand written) explanation of each spot. The room was quite spacious and it was filled with lots of windows to see the city views and buildings. The bell hop was passionate about the city and ALWAYS welcomed us back interested in where we went and what we did. In this day and age, personalized service is a lost art and this place is bringing it back. We would definitely return for our next trip to San Fran!

title: “Great Location, Great Views”
text: We stayed at this property in March 2012. Everything was great. Would definitely come back.

title: “Home from home”
text:
Quirky hotel in a residential area. Don't go there if you expect to be waited on and have lots of staff being nice to you in the hope of a tip, but if you want to deal with genuinely friendly staff in a good value hotel with nice rooms and awesomely comfortable beds then this is the place.
It has its quirks, such as sometimes you have to ask for the aircon wall unit to be fixed and sometimes the TV remotes just don't work or are missing, but these are minor and are attended to when you ask.
Overall the rooms a large and pleasant and best of all there's parking without the usual ridiculous LA parking fees and expectation of a parking tip.
I've been many times and keep coming back.

title: “Dark, broken and lame”
text:
This is one of my worst hotel experiences. First of all the place is very dark. Dark wood. Dark walls. Dark elevators. My room keys did not work, so I had to go back to the front desk 3 times just to get the door to work. Lastly the Internet is very clunky (and 9.95 a day which is lame). Works on my iPad but cannot get it to work on my laptop. Works at every other hotel in the country, just not this one. 
Ps its way overpriced too.
Fail.

title: “Excellent experience for this weary traveler.”
text:
The Sportsman’s Lodge is an incredible bargain in luxury. The Sunday buffet is like a luxury cruise ship complete with towering ice sculpture, prime rib, fresh turkey, baked ham, fresh seafood bar, omelet chef, about 30 entrees, and a separate desert and confection room.
