The rustic surroundings include many ponds filled with giant coy and swans –both black and white. During warm weather be sure to sit outside and enjoy a wonderful country atmosphere of serenity in the midst of bustling Studio City. 
The Patio Café offers excellent meals and service. Their Blue Plate Specials are good bargains and all the food is home cooking. 
The heated pool was just rebuilt in February of 2005 and is very relaxing with a poolside cabana featuring a full bar. 
The rooms are traditional hotel rooms and not the PLASTIC hotel rooms that so many of us are accustomed.

title: “GRAND OLD HOTEL - kids wanted to go back - super convenient location”
text:
Started out on our 15 night trip out west with 3 nights here. Arrived on an AM flight, grabbed car and drove downtown to find the hotel. It was only about 1pm and I didn't expect them to be able to check us in but they did have rooms ready. I had hotwired it for $109/night and knew it was a lower class room - I mentioned my SPG number and was upgraded to a street view room instead of inner room. We had considered mor expensive hotels near Fisherman's Wharf and after touring that area are very glad we stayed FAR AWAY from that area.....
Very pleasant staff - Fantastic Pool - Steet car and subway right out front, cable car nearby as well. Great shopping 3 -4 blocks away - californai pizza kitchen takeout counter 2 blocks away made for easy in room chillaxin with movies at end of long day.
Park at garage around corner to save $$$ - Free Wifi in lobby only - in room connection very expensive.

title: “Great hotel for NYC stay”
text: Have stayed at different hotels in NYC and wanted to write a review on the Hilton Garden Inn--it was so good to find a good hotel, very clean, great location! The hotel is newer which explains the great condition of the rooms. The staff are excellent. My hotel choice for when I return next.

title: “Ignore the past bad reviews - now under new management”
text:
Reviews of this hotel under previous management should be ignored. Now a Holiday Inn Express, the property has been refurbished and upgraded to the standards of Holiday Inn. The rooms were clean and well appointed, the beds very comfortable.
I was quite pleased to find my choice of pillows on the bed - both soft and firm. As in most Holiday Inn properties, there was a complimentary business center conveniently located in the lobby.
The hotel is located only a mile from the beach, and is priced at about half the cost of the Holiday Inn hotels across the street from the cruise terminals. The only gripe I would have about the hotel is that the elevators are so s-l-o-w... but that is a minor problem.
Would I stay here again? You bet!

title: “Not worth the price - stay at another high end Seattle hotel”
text:
I have stayed at hundreds of hotels around the world and most of the high-end downtown Seattle hotels. Just had my first stay at the Sorrento. I will never go back though I can see it's appeal for others..
Pros:
 Victorian look. 
 Friendly staff - when you can find them. 
 Small intimate feeling. 
 Great quality food at the Hunt Club.
 Room Service breakfast was great quality (overnight cooked steel cut oats and whole grain pancakes).
Negatives:
 A/C couldn't get the room temperature below 80F. When we arrived, the room was over 90 F. 
 Cleanliness. Stuff still in the trash can in the room. A completed survey card still sitting on the desk in the room.
 Aged infrastructure. Toilet ran frequently during the night for minutes at a time. A/C is a window unit not central air. A/C was so noisy (chirps, rattles, etc.) it kept waking me up. I'm used to central air and not window units at high end hotels so this might not be a problem for you. 
 Hunt Club restaurant (was original reason to stay actually). Very disappointed that the service was not nearly on par with say the Georgian at the Olympic Four Seasons (Fairmont now). Expected better treatment, better staff knowledge of their wine list, more attentive service. The food did taste quite good though and was reasonably priced for the quality.
 For a $250 dinner and $300 night at the hotel, I ended up feeling like I would have rather stayed home. I only managed a few hours of sleep. I've never felt that way before following the same routine at other Seattle area high end hotels or around the world.

title: “Don,t be put off by the location”
text: The level of service we experienced from the staff from booking to arrival through to leaving was exceptional nothing was a problem. Although the room decor was a little dated everything was cleaned to a high standard and we felt very safe and well cared for. The only negative point is the location, it is on a busy road which is a little run down in appearance, but don,t be put off , everything else makes up for it! That includes the courtesy shuttle bus and the very patient drivers who together with all the staff helped our stay be so much easier! Thank you

title: “Great expectations outdone”
text: Wonderful property with a gorgeous room with impeccable service. Great location and very friendly and helpful staff.

title: “El Paso Marriott, very nice !”
text:
El Paso Marriott, very nice !
we stayed here twice this year, we were flying out our flight was canceled do to weather, so we went to get somthing to eat, we were across from the El Paso Marriott, so we decided to stay ther, fist of all i was impressed with the front desk personel they were very nice and very helpful, the room was nice we had a great nights sleep and got our flight out the next morning,
very close to the airport, 
Eddie

title: “Hidden Gem Near The "Big Guns"”
text:
"Great location and very friendly staff. Located half a block from Lexinton & 51st Subway and Waldorf Astoria. Close to Rockefeller Centre, Radio City Music Hall and Sachs 5th Avenue for those who can afford to shop there as well as some superb restaurants.
Thanks to Fabio, Gabriel and Bobby who were most friendly and helpful and went out of their way to ensure we had a memorable stay.. Even let us store a bag at the hotel while we visited friends in Upstate New York for 4 days. Thanks also to Roberto from the limo company that the hotel arranged to take us to the Airport.

title: “Not the best Embassy Suites”
text: We made a reservation at least 3 weeks ahead of time requesting a lower floor suite. This particular Embassy Suites is 12 stories and I'm not great with heights and made that very plain to them. They didn't seem too interested in our request. You guessed it! Our suite was on the 11th floor damn, my worst nightmare. Now parking. At every Embassy Suites I've stayed at we've had complimentary parking unless of course you use valet. This one in La Jolla you park yourself and it's a $19 a day, I'm serious! Wow...horrors. Please make sure if you're looking for your microwave and your refrigeratorcheck inside the closet next to your bathroom. Internet service? You bet and it's $9.95 a day to use. One more thing, when the air conditioner comes on at night you REALLY hear it when trying to sleep. Bring your ocean machine and earplugs or take a xanax. We did like Indulge the restaurant. Dan the bartender was personable and made our stay most enjoyable considering the other challenges. I believe you can find better deals elsewhere in La Jolla.

title: “At this price how can I complain?”
text:
New York always presents an issue for me. On the one hand you have the larger full service chains charging upwards of $300US per night and on the other you have the bargin basement flea traps--this property is right in the middle of that spectrum. 
The rooms are small but efficient uses of space. The bathroom, especially the shower could have been better designed in my opinion. On the positive side there was free wi-fi (which I am using to write this review) and great Wyndham appointed bedding. The housekeeping staff could either benefit from better training or supervision or both. We stayed for 4 days and each day there was a less than satisfactory attention given to the cleaning of our room. In particular, the shower curtain was FILTHY! Before we could inform management (day two) it was changed. 
The cafe pictured on the Wyndham.com site is not the one in the "lobby" of this property. Additionally, you have to make a trip to the to get a bucket of ice--quite a trip from the 18th floor. 
All of this aside, I stayed here for less than $175 a night and the location was central for our visit.

title: “Basic but good hotel”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for four nights on the first part of our trip to LA,Vegas and San Francisco. As we had only paid $35 per night we were not expecting much and were surprised when we arrived to find the room was large, very clean and exactly what we needed. As we were spending every day of our 4 days in LA sightseeing we only needed a place to lay our heads and this hotel certainly did the job for us.
It is located about a two minute walk from the metro station which is on the Red Line and will take you to all the tourist spots ie Universal and Walk of Fame. The area is not the greatest as many tramps seem to have set up home there but to be honest they do not hassle you if you quietly walk past them.
There are not many places to eat in this area, however we did find a lovely Mexican about a 10 min walk from the hotel (come out of the hotel turn left then right at the traffic lights-walk for about 10-mins and its on your left
Breakfast at the hotel is also very very basic but OK (coffee and muffins, fruit)
This hotel is not The Ritz, however if you are looking for a basic, clean cheap place to stay whilst sightseeing in LA I would recommened it

title: “Great location and value”
text:
I have lived in Houston and have worked near the Galleria area many years. The location is great as the hotel is located just within the walking distance from the Galleria Shopping Center and is surrounded with many fine restaurants all around.. Close by is the uptown an upscale shopping and condominium high rise that has fancy boutique stores and fancy restaurants. Next to the Sheraton is the Intercontinental Hotel where many head of the states and high profile government officials stays when they are in Houston.
Over all it is located at the cross roads of many major highways thus making it easily accessible and not far away from the two airports that Houston is serviced by major and regional airlines.

title: “Terrible experience not recommended”
text: I stayed in this hotel on business for 5 nights. I had to move rooms twice the first time because of the traffic noise and the second time because of a problem with the water pipes in the room. The people on the reception desk had terrible customer service and always made it seem like it was my fault that I was having issues. I very rarely complain at hotels but in this case I was unable to sleep for the first 3 nights. I didn't have my towels replaced by the chamber maid as I would have expected for this class of hotel. I also found that the porters would only acknowledge you if you were pulling up to the hotel in a limo it was trying to be an upper class hotel but was miserably failing. If you are considering staying here please look elsewhere!!

title: “Liked it...”
text: Stayed at the Moderne in June 2003 and I would do it again. It's really close to everything and the price is right!

title: “Very comfortable beds. Great location. Great staff. Good restaurant.”
text:
In Boston for a graduation and combined leisure trip.
The Colonnade was very comfortable, convenient and friendly.
Highly recommend and would go back.
Restaurant excellent.

title: “Blown away”
text: My stay at The Pearl was great. It has such a fun, hip and energetic feel with a mid century modern look. Bathrooms are gorgeous. The place has a great vibe and the little touches like the handwritten welcome note from the manager was really a nice touch. A great find and an excellent value minutes from all the well-known San Diego attractions. I will definitely be back and soon!

title: “Close enough to everything, but a dissapointing experience...”
text:
This hotel is within walking distance to most attractions in DC (five minutes to the Mall and the White House), and that was the reason why we came back for a second visit. Still, I think we will look for another hotel next time we visit the capital, simply because this was the second time we got a room facing the back, and there is a really noisy fan of some sort back there, that made it hard to sleep... In other words, the soundproofing is not good (understatement).
The rooms are contemporary in style, and the round showers is a fun detail, but the overall size of the room is another reason why we would think twice about coming back here. We had two bags each, and had to climb over our luggage.... Upon arrival, the reception clerk couldn't find our reservation in their system, but fortunately they had available rooms. That could be the reason for our small room, it might have been the last one he had (but I find that a bit strange, since we had another room last time we were there, and that one was even smaller...). 
The hotel does not serve breakfast (except an expensive in-room service), but there are several places serving both breakfast and lunch just steps away from the entrance. There's also a couple of CVS's close bye. 
Yet another reason why we would look for another hotel next time, is the parking. You have to use the valet, and they are expensive. Several of the other hotels down the street offer cheaper valet than the Donovan House, and it will be interesting to see if they are cheaper in general the next time we travel to DC.
We made our reservation through a travel website, and will make sure not to use that one again. The stay was booked and payed for in September of 2011, despite that, it wasn't in the hotel's system. Since I was told by the reception three (!!) times that they would take care of getting hold of the payment from the website, I thought everything was fine. Untill about a week after we left, when I discovered the hotel had charged my card for the two nights we stayed there (without even getting my signature and verification). It all resulted in several phone calls, and extra stress during our holiday, and we got back the money they had withdrawn after a lot of unnecessary discussions. With the exception of the first guy we talked to upon arrival, who was really nice and helpful, the rest of the staff didn't seem to know what customerservice is...
But hey, if you're travelling light, do not have a car, do not need a lot of help from the hotel staff and like the contemporary style of the rooms; go for it! But I would not pay more than $150 pr night, to get best value for my money.

title: “Still best place on Manhattan”
text:
After I stayed here before, expectations were high on our stay in the last week of March 2011. And again we were not dissapointed. I took some friends on their first trip to NY and the eastcoast.
The staff at this hotel makes the difference - again. I stayed at several W's and the staff at the door, the bell desk and the concierge make this a wow-experience again. We felt at home and taken care of again.

title: “Fantastic hotel”
text: This hotel is cute, clean, interesting with a spectacular coffee shop attached. My children loved it, the staff were very on the ball.

title: “Great location in downtown Denver.”
text: My husband and I stayed at the hotel for a conference. The hotel was very clean and our room was spacious. We loved the free wi-fi. It was very easy to access and worked great. The bed was comfortable.

title: “Would definitely stay at the Palace Again”
text:
Great hotel, I would definitely stay here again. Even though it's a huge hotel, it doesn't feel like it. Everyone is friendly, helpful, and efficient (I stayed on a Tues-Weds). 
In its price range (I paid $385 for a week night on business), it was fantastic. The room was spacious, the bed was incredibly comfortable, and I had a partial view. It was quiet and the relaxing music already on when I got to my room, and the chocolates next to the bed were a nice touch. 
It isn't ultra luxurious like the St. Regis, for example, but in its price range it cannot be beat. For such a big place, they seem to put a lot of thought into making your stay comfortable and inviting. I already said it but the staff was really great - they handle your bags quickly, make change, get you to your room, get you a cab, all without being asked. It's great and a good location too. 
Only positives to say about this place (to provide context: my other recent stays are: Four Seasons Boston, St. Regis New York).

title: “Totally Fab”
text:
As an interior designer, I give the Hotel Palomar 5 Stars for an incredible job turning an old Hilton Hotel into a gorgeous, contemporary haven. I can't wait to go back. The hotel is relatively close to Love Field, and North Park Mall. After I was finished with work, I checked out and had them drop me off at North Park (no charge hotel car), checked my bags at the North Park courtesy desk and shopped to my heart's content, then took a quick cab to Love Field. Worked out great. 
The restaurant, Central 214 was delicious. My favorite was the Key Lime Pie, and warm peach cobbler. Entrees were great too. Kimpton Hotels allow pets, and what a treat to be able to take a pet and not have to stay in a dive. They welcome your pet with a sign in the lobby....too cute. Full service, even for pooch.
Next time I plan on trying the spa. My trip was too short to fully experience all the amenities the hotel has to offer, but suffice it to say, I will definitely be back.

title: “Even better stay than the last time”
text:
This was my second stay at this hotel and it was even better than the last time.
Check-in experience at the Elite desk was super fast and friendly.
The hotel was really bustling and there were several conferences, weddings and events being held which resulted in somewhat slow luggage assistance. But all the staff seemed friendly, if not a little over-worked.
The concierge lounge is closed on weekends, but I was kindly supplied with breakfast vouchers. It was one of the better breakfasts that I had on my long trip. Yum.
We had dinner in the Sports Bar – food was okay, but overpriced for what it was and the service was hit or miss.
I think I may have been given that same suite as my last stay. This time it was spotless. No one in their right mind could fault a Marriott bed. Great sleep.
Thank you so much to the Steven and all of his staff for making my partner’s birthday extra special. I wish we could have stayed longer!
I’d really like to linger a little at this hotel – solid 4 stars out of 5 and amazing value for money for a full-service Marriott! Looking forward to my next stay....

title: “Great airport hotel”
text: Reasonable price for room close to DIA. Bed comfortable; staff friendly; very clean. Breakfast good.

title: “This is a very noisy hotel so stay next door at the Fairfield Inn.”
text: The doors at this hotel are on some sort of super-spring and they slam very loud. You know when your neighbors are coming and going as though they are upset while doing it. The suite I stayed in had a conjoining door on both sides of the room with no sound deadening. I had to listen to snoring on one side of me and conversations and children singing badly on the other. The ceilings are very loud. The people upstairs sounded like they were running around stomping their feet constantly. The internet was super slow and helped make my stay extra stressful since I do a bit of work on my computer. Other than noise and slow internet, the rooms were fine and the location is great but there are other better options in the area than this if you prefer to sleep. My colleague has the same complaints that I do and was staying across the hall. I live on the road and stay 200+ nights per year in Marriott Hotels. This has been the least sleep-friendly hotel yet. Just too noisy.

title: “This hotel is amazing.”
text: This hotel is fabulous, terrific staff and lovely rooms. The view is amazing.

title: “Hmmm, ok hotel . . . I guess”
text:
I normally stay at the Omni Chicago or Renaissance . . . so Talbott is no comparison. Good things are: Staff is very helpful and friendly, location is only 1 block from Rush St & add another block for Michigan Ave., internet is free, the room is very clean and all amneties are in the room. 
What I was not so impressed with . . . I had a view of an alley, the furniture and look of hotel is very very aged and not impressive. And the worst, I had an A/C window unit that was so loud it kept me up through the night and it was too hot to turn it off!
Overall, I had no icky experiences and for those who are tourists whom will not be in the hotel very much but want to be in the middle of the action, not a bad hotel to stay in, but maybe not as enjoyable for frequent business travelers who strive for somewhat upscale really comfy suites. I travel to Chicago monthly, and I booked at Talbott to save just a little money on the hotel, I am going back to the modern, Omni Chicago, it is not that much more at all, really.

title: “Stay here instead of the Intercontinental”
text: Booked off Hotwire so I got a pretty price. The lobby is beautiful with a little garden area. The rooms were huge and immaculate. The fitness center was the nicest hotel gym I've been in. I only had limited interaction with the front desk but they were pleasant. Room service was pricey because they hit you with a ton of fees, but the food was great. My only complaint is that I wish the hotel was on Michigan Ave.

title: “Location great, rude front counter staff, average place”
text: Like other people reviewing this place, I would have to agree that the front desk is rude, non helpful and dishonest. My parents own timeshare at a beach but decided to go to New York. I arrived first before my parents who had to pay the $60.00 guest fee to allow me in the room before them, what a joke. The blonde helping me could not find the reservation, once she did she took a credit card and told be there is a hospitality fee of $25.00. I asked if it was a one time charge and she stated yes so I did not think much of it however at the end of the week they planned on charging my card $175.00. I explained to the front that I never signed anything agreeing to have that charge on my card and it should have been explained at time of reservation not check out. In the end you have to pay $25.00 a day for not being a member...I'm still trying to figure that one out. The bell boys seemed nice and helpful. We stayed in a remodled room that was nice but not roomy. Tight area for 4 people. Elevators worked and yes there was a short wait but who doesn't wait for elevators. The best I can say is the location. You can take a short walk to central park and time square. Don't get a room on central park "view" because there is no such thing. Your room is in the direction of Central park with a direct view of an office building. It was a decent stay however I can't say that I would stay here again due to the rude staff at check in and out. Business center only had 3 working computer that linked to internet.

title: “Above average”
text: The Nyma is a good hotel ,exactly what you need for a family trip to manhattan.It is well located,the rooms are clean and the staff are friendly.Well,not all of them.The guy who works at the restaurant should adopt a new service providing attitude.

title: “Nice Hotel Great stay”
text: My wife and I came down for a conference and had a great stay. Very nice hotel with a beautiful insdie area that was very relaxing after driving down from Upstate NY. I guess if I had one complaint it would be aboput the charge for internet. Todays day and age I would rather they just include it in the price. It seems that charging $9.99 a day seems petty. I know, if you are a Hilton Member of a certain rating it includes the price but still seems petty. Overall a nice stay. One comment all the rooms face into the center atrium. I was worried about noise but actually overslept this morning and almost missed the start of the confernece so noise is not an issue. We are headed to the coast tomorrow for the pleasure part of the trip.

title: “wonderful location”
text:
This hotel has a great location, wonderful views. However, it needs new mattresses and furniture in the living area. For the price, some upgrades should be made.
The staff was pleasant and very accomodating.

title: “Very good stay”
text: I stayed at this hotel July 6-8, 2012. We had a great stay. The hotel staff was great, especially Latoya, who cleaned our room. She went out of her way to help us even with small requests that I could have done myself. She had such a great personality. The facitilies were pleasant and it appears that they are in the process of upgrading and modernizing the decor. Overall my family had a comfortable and pleasant experience.

title: “No Frills”
text: Me and my boyfriend stayed here for the last 3 nights and there was nothing special about the hotel. It was very old and the room was very small but had a microwave and fridge. Were currently travelling the world and so not looking for anything fancy however we did pay over £100 per night here which is definately not worth the money, then again you will pay this anywhere in San Fran. The breakfast was a massive dissapointment, this was served between 7 -10 however if you got there after 8 there was nothing left of the small muffins and pastries?! They also provided sachets of porridge but no milk or hot water?! The location was not bad but was about an hour walk to the pier but there is a lot of transport available. There is also a grocery store and laundrette next door which is handy

title: “Good location - take a cab from airport”
text: The place is nice and the location is awesome with great access to Little Italy and downtown. The room was clean with a noisy vent in the bathroom that shut down during sleeping hours. My main complaint is the airport shuttle takes forever, you are better off taking a cab.

title: “Outstanding!!”
text:
What a gem! I fell in love with the Hotel Beacon. It's meager star rating (due to lack of amenities I wouldn't use like an in-house restaurant or room service) does not do this property justice. I stayed in one of their renovated two-room suites on one of the top floors. I even had views of the Hudson River! I could easily have spent (and was prepared to spend) $500++ for a midtown hotel and not gotten as nice a room. 
My two-room suite was incredibly spacious, spotless and soothingly decorated. One side had a very comfortable living area with a dining table for four. The room also had a great fully equipped kitchenette with stove, refrigerator, and microwave. It was also fully stocked with plates, glasses and flatware, which I used for my take-out meal from gourmet grocer Citarella just across Broadway. There are other numerous dining options, including a great little diner adjacent to the hotel, Starbucks just a few steps away, plus plenty of restaurants of all types. Who needs a dreary hotel restaurant?!
The bedroom side had a very comfy king bed, large flat screen TV with a bazillion channels of cable, and iPod docking station with speakers. The bathroom was small but beautiful & functional. The all-cotton towels felt great, and there was a full array of "emergency" items in case you forgot your toothbrush, razor, or needed to mend something.
All in all, my stay greatly exceeded my expectations. The Hotel Beacon is a fabulous value for Manhattan, right smack in a great neighborhood and convenient even for my business appointment in midtown. This is now my "go to" hotel in NY.
Note: The hotel is currently undergoing renovations, which always makes me shudder because of the potential noise & disruption. Don't let this scare you off. I can honestly say the renovations had no impact on my stay whatsoever. No renovation-related disruptions at all.

title: “This hotel is just friggin...”
text: AWESOME! I have stayed in the Park Hyatt Chicago Downtown and I desired to stay in the Peninsula due to its high star rating, but I don't think I will be staying in either when I travel back to Chicago. The Residence Inn is where it's at for me. It's not on the Magnificient Mile but just right off from it and I think its location provides this hotel its charm factor. This hotel is just like an apartment in New York City! When we arrived, we were promptly greeted by valet, the front desk accomodated our requests, there's a small computer 'room' on the first floor (free of charge) and the complimentary breakfast will get you full- no bagels, no crossiants, but real breakfast food is available to you. The hotel staff were very pleasant and made our stay enjoyable. Great value all around. I shall return, lol!

title: “good value for price”
text: We were looking for a hotel close to the pier and public traffic as we only stayed one night in SFO. Hotel has bus station in front and trolley is also only 5Min walk away. Rooms are quite old fashioned but clean, bed comfy. Room was very big as i reserved a 2bed queen. No problem to leave the bags stored if flight leaves late.

title: “Very Comfortable”
text: Very Comfortable, from the staff who welcome you like an old friend, to the well appointed, and cozy guest rooms, this is a great place to be at-home-away-from-home.

title: “Outstanding Spa and Service”
text: Stayed one night, ate in the lounge and in one of the restaurants and had a massage at the spa. The Spa was fantastic and we definitely received great service. The food was very good - had a light lunch in the lounge and the breakfast buffet in the morning. It is not far from the museums but definitely not in a night time hot spot, but it is DC, we took cabs to go out for dinner and drinks. Great water views. Our room was nice, we had a regular room, not one of the suites. The bathroom was AMAZING, it was almost the same size as our room and had a spa tub. Nice turn down service at night and the bed was sooooo comfortable. I did not want to get up.

title: “awesome service, fantastic spa, great in-room dining”
text:
Stayed here for two nights and had a wonderful time. My room was spacious and traditionally furnished. The bed had good quality linens and was comfortable. The robes - plush. I liked the L'Occitane toiletries as well.
I ordered room service several times. Each time, the food came on time and was delicious and nicely presented. Try the eggs benedict with smoked salmon for breakfast -- a bit salty but very tasty (the eggs are done perfectly).
My favorite part of the stay was a fantastic deep tissue massage I got at the spa (I received a $40 off coupon at check-in). After the massage, which was some of the best I've ever had, I spent some time in the heated pool and hot tub/whirlpool. They also have a steam room, but I could not take any more heat. The ladies' locker rooms are nicely appointed, spacious, and have a good array of creams and lotions. There are carafes with orange infused water, some kind of fruit drink, and a selection of teas with honey.
I also tried out the fitness center, which is not large, but equipped with a nice variety of machines.
The location cannot be beat.

title: “Excellent Digs, Amenities, Services for Touring the Big Apple”
text:
Short version: Clean; amazing value; incredibly warm, friendly, accommodating staff; good location.
Long version:
We needed a place to stay for a film festival in the East Village. I chose the Hampton Inn because I needed two beds and a place that was very clean--I was traveling with a very persnickety person. Thanks to reviews on TripAdvisor, I selected this property over others closer to the East Village. I'm so glad I did!
(1) Check-in was a breeze, with very friendly, warm staff. The woman explained what they had available, where to find it, etc. She also shortly after we settled in to make sure everything was to our satisfaction. At the front desk they have Otis Spunkenmeyer cookies, mints, and other snacks that are gratis. They also have free coffee available 24 hours in the lobby. 
(2) The room was a great size for Manhattan standards: Two double beds with great, fluffy comforters and three pillows per bed. They had a little lap desk for people who want to use their laptop while lying in bed, two dressers, and a desk. Everything was spotlessly clean, including the bathroom. Great water pressure, and lots of hot water. Plenty of towels: two large ones per person, two washcloths per person, and two hand towels per person. 
(3) Breakfast is included. They had cereal, fruit, yogurt, some muffins, toast, PB, honey, biscuits, and a hot chafing dish with sausage and waffles. Breakfast is served from 6am to 10 am, and on Saturday morning they left the food out slightly longer to accommodate the later risers. 
(4) Free internet. 'Nuff said for this huge plus. They also have a computer and printer down in the lobby, which we used to print out boarding passes. This was also free. 
While it appears that they cater to the business traveler, they were very friendly and helpful for the tourist crowd: Take-out menus, maps, tour recommendations....they were like "just ask!" 
The only negative---which is really quite a minor one---is that the properly is located right near the Holland Tunnel. Traffic backs up on the street that the hotel is on, so your taxi may drop you off a block over to avoid getting stuck in the traffic. 
It's a quick walk up 6th Ave to Houston, Bleeker, and Spring streets right into the heart of Soho. 
We paid a ridiculously cheap $159-$189/night, booked through the hotel's website. 
While I generally try to avoid patronizing sterile chain establishments, I would make an exception for this property. We will definitely be back!

title: “Terrible”
text:
Oh my God!
I am a hardened traveller and this was the worst hotel I have ever come across. The website is false advertising. The room was extremely small, so small in fact that there was nowhere to open my case other than on the bed. My feet hung off the end of the bed. I am tall but I have never had this problem in a hotel before. Lastly, the room was insecure with a window opening onto a courtyard that couldn't be locked. I asked to be moved but they claimed they had no other rooms so I moved out to the Astoria around the corner. MUCH better!.
Compare my photos - The first is from their website, the second is what I actually got.

title: “Nice hotel, great location”
text:
Stayed at the JW for business and extended the stay to pleasure for the weekend. Great location, right off of Union Square. San Fran is a great walking city and this hotel is right in the heart of things. Just a block from Union Square, the cable car stop, tons of shopping. Loved it!
The room was very nicely appointed, roomy and comfortable. I did not eat in the restaurant however, was served several meals as part of the business meeting. The food was very good.

title: “Westin Copley”
text:
4 day stay. Beds great. Location convenient. Nice view. Room amenities fine. Windows actually open - can get fresh air.
Elevators not working one morning at prime time. Slow to inform guests of issue and did not seem to have a plan. No update and no courtesy message that usually happens later apologizing for the inconvenience.
Pool: not easy to access: ladder type access only but ladders are built into pool wall and required a giant step between deck and first toe hold. Lots of challenges for children and older swimmers. No convenient or well marked shower - communal shower off a hallway.
Business center outside hotel and beside a noisey construction area.
Ate breakfast at the restaurant most mornings: despite advertising the smart or super foods including berries, the breakfast buffet did not have many - for berrys, had strawberries one of three mornings. No tomatoes ever. Modest selection.

title: “Surprised by bad reviews”
text:
I must say I'm surprised by the poor reviews because our stay was the complete opposite. Though we had a brick wall view of the building behind the hotel our room was nice and quiet and everything else was great. I lived in Houston for several years and downtown has changed quite a bit. Where it once was a ghost town after 6 p.m., it now has lots to offer, including sporting venues, shopping and restaurants. 
As for the Club Quarters, my husband has lodged frequently with this chain for business travel. We've also stayed at the CQ in Washington D.C. and found this one to be in line with the rest of the locations.
In fact, our stay was quite comfortable. Our requests for extra towels was responded to in a reasonable time frame. Yes, the room was small, but we knew that ahead of time. That's one of the reasons its such an affordable hotel brand. Our room included a generous desk area with TV, several books and a cabinet that held a mini-fridge and microwave. Not too many hotels offer the last two in a basic room for around $100 a night. The bathroom was very functional, clean and well planned. I think overall CQ's do a great job of wisely using space. 
This location in particular, I was told by the manager on duty, is the site of the old Texas State Hotel, built circa 1920. The tiled lobby floor is original! The lobby was beautifully furnished as were the hallways. We also appreciated the exterior architectural features. 
There is a restaurant at the lobby level Bistro 7 (i think it was called) where the staff prepared a small take-away breakfast for us after check-out. 
The only cons were a couple missing towels upon check-in and the $18 overnight valet parking rate. I expect that in Chicago, but not Houston. 
Otherwise, I would rate this hotel four stars for a budget-friendly, clean facility with an excellent location. Happy travels!

title: “Loved Chicago and the Omni!”
text:
My husband and I stayed at The Omni from 10/4-10-7. The staff was very friendly and professional and the hotel was kept up very well. The one thing I thought was a bit odd was checking in and out of the hotel on the 3rd floor and not the ground floor and the 2 sets of elevators that they had. We were on the 19th floor and had to get off on 3 and then take a different set of elevators to the ground level. Same thing when we came in. Other than that, I have no complaints and loved the turn down service they had. Our room was clean and nothing was broken. The tub filled up with water a lil while showering and we should've called down but didn't bother. There is a separate space to watch tv which was really nice. y husband and I wished they had a sofa though instead of the 2 comfy chairs they have.
We ventured out alot as it was our first time in Chicago and wanted to try and get the most out of our stay so we didn't eat at the restaurant.
They had a car service that dropped us off at the Navy Pier which was very nice. Front desk always answered any questions we had regarding getting around and were very helpful!
The Omni is located right in the heart of the downtown area which we absolutely loved.

title: “Below average from other Westins”
text: For my business travelers, this hotel is ok for a very quick stay but not for a long comfortable stay as most Westins. I am a platinum member and was upgraded but to a very outdated room. Beds are the standard fluffy beds at this hotel, furniture in rooms a little ran down, showers do not have the dual shower head that I absolutely love and look forward to at every Westin stay. Staff friendly but did not provide all hotel amenities until being asked (executive lounge, fitness area, etc). If I am in LA for more than a day I would not recommend this hotel. It is very good for a day layover that has a great location by the airport.

title: “Great , spacious and reasonable price”
text: Not the most savvy Hotel in NY but you cant beat price and location. Its in a neoighborhood like setting and quiet. Our room had a kitchenette which is perfect for small children that constantly want something to snack on. I would recommend this hotel!

title: “Bed Bugs!!”
text: I thought this was a pretty nice place, until the itching started the day I left (stayed Thurs. through Saturday night at the end of May 2009 in a double room on the 10th floor). It got progressively worse for several days. I called the hotel to let them know, and after sitting on hold for several minutes, they asked if I went to the doctor (no, I didn't think medical attention was necessary or useful), and acted like they had no idea there were bugs. Maybe it was only our room that was infested, but it was like nothing I've ever experienced. My daughter showed up Friday night and never noticed anything. I don't have bugs at home and have never had them before or since.

title: “a fair choice”
text: Good location, and a clean well air conditioned room with a bathroom of fair size on the newer side and ease of a fridge and microwave in the room. The beds were comfortable and our main complaint is while the parking is free; you get what you pay for. The lot is miniscule (15 cars max) and usually full; not that we were thrilled about parking there and leaving with a damaged rental car, all spots are tight, and parking on the street in that area is not easy. We have had better luck parking further south in the Dupont circle area. Also, the restaurant is only fair, and the room service is limited in menu and time served, But if you do not have a car to park, and are not eating in the hotel, this was an OK choice. Free WIFI with hotel code.

title: “Dont waste your money!”
text: I am a Hilton Diamond card holder and as such I stay at Hilton hotels frequently throughout the year both on business and pleasure and I am in no doubt that this establishment is the WORSE for customer service - none, tiny rooms -I booked an executive room on the 41st floor - great view that was it, poor housekeeping - room not cleaned to a high standard, the Exec Lounge was a joke - cramped, tables not cleaned, food quality poor and the Breakfast offer was so mean we didnt use it after the second night. On top of all this they charge you to leave your bags which cost me $18 for two hours despite spending nearly $2500. For all those Hilton Honor Members I was not offered a room upgrade (despite complaining about wafer thin walls and the noise from my fellow guests keeping me up all night for two nights) or American Breakfast despite my diamond card status. I was fortunate to stay at The Waldorf Towers on my first night in NYC - a complete contrast despite being another Hilton property it was 1000% better!

title: “Would Stay Again”
text: The hotel had everything we needed for an overnight stay to attend a funeral service. The rooms were spacious, comfortable beds, fridge, microwave, dining table, iron and board, etc. Make your own waffles and cereal were perfect for the kids. Would definitely stay again.

title: “Excellent business class stay in University neighborhood.”
text:
The Watertown is, hands down my favorite places to stay in the U-District. The staff is very friendly and the hotel is well kept. The hotel and rooms have a modern aquatic theme with bright clean bathrooms, comfortable queen beds, ample closet space and gorgeous views of downtown Seattle. The rooms also come with complimentary Aveda products, fluffy bathrobes and free parking. The Watertown also has a small workout room to squeeze in your morning run on a rainy day as well as business meeting rooms for your convenience. 
The thing I really like is that they actually put time and quality into their continental breakfast. Last we were up they served sausage and eggs, a variety of cereals, soy milks, juices, bagels, smaller sized pastries, granola, fruit and very delicious organic Greek yogurt. The coffee and tea flow all hours and in the evenings they have fresh baked cookies and complimentary wine/beer bar. Really, The Watertown has everything in one place. 
They also have two sister hotels; the University Inn just a block away and the Maxwell that just opened in Belltown.

title: “Great location and price”
text: The area directly around the hotel is a little grimy but the location is really great for the price. The staff were really helpful, the price includes good wi-fi in the rooms and breakfast and the hotel is pretty new so our room was spotless. It's only a 10 minute walk to Soho and Greenwich Village and even less to the Lower East Side. There are plenty of restaurants and bars within walking distance and the subway is one block away. It's a good choice if you want to be near Soho etc but can't afford to stay there.

title: “Great location but NOT a hotel as such!”
text:
Just returned from a three day trip to NYC, staying at West 57th Hilton Grand. This is technically a vacation club property but is available for hotel-like stays. It does have a complimentary continental breakfast(nothing hot except oatmeal) which was fine. The rooms are very modern, very clean and ours(room 1409 I think) was quite spacious--can't fault anything about it. There is no restaurant or lounge on property, no gift shop etc. although there is a minimart two doors down and restaurants within two blocks. My only real beef is that we paid 
600 dollars per night--outrageous considering the lack of hotel features. Additionally, we went with a couple who had taken advantage of a sales presentation(two hours); their price was $169. We, being from Maryland, for
some reason cannot take advantage of that offer so the difference in price was
hard to take. We took in a couple of shows and had a lovely evening in the lounge of The Warwick Hotel which wasn't far from Rockefeller Center. Had fun walking through Central Park and enjoying the holiday windows(one tip--do not try to go window shopping on the weekend!! Monday morning was far less crowded.). Radio City Christmas show was spectacular, as always!

title: “An Airport Oasis”
text:
We first enjoyed the Grand Hyatt DFW during a 4 hour layover. The cocktail bar was an oasis of calm comfort, greart service, drinks and food. Going home, we missed our connecting flight and were standed at DFW at 10.30pm. It was such a relief to be able to walk up to the GH after a stressful afternoon of flight delays and missed connections. The room was stunning - integrated electronic contols for lights, curtains, air cond - very impressive. A full room service meal at 11pm was also very welcome. The bathroom is amazing - huge, lots of marble, more electronic controls.
Determined not to miss our rescheduled flight, we checked in 4 hrs early and had a finbal dinner at GH. It was also excellent. We left thinking that we were very lucky to be standed at The Grand Hyatt - everything was impeccible and it's a destination in its own right.

title: “Fading Beauty”
text:
This was our third, nonconsecutive Thanksgiving at the Wladorf Astoria (2001, 2010 and 2012). Always pre-pay since I have found the Hotel extends a small discount. I booked a suite plus two additional rooms.
Suite 860 has not been updated since our stay in 2001. The first room I occuppied 890, I was greeted with a broken bathroom door (As if someone punched the door. The door was cracked with two small holes and two different color paints on the door) The wall oin the bathroom, over the door was covered in black mold 6 inches by 1 foot. If the door was in good repair I may not have noticed the mold issue. The Housekeeping supervisor was summoned to my room and had no explination but offered to clean the bathroom. I was changed to room 867.
Peacock alley: We had Thanksgiving reservations for the 3pm seating. We were finially seated at 3:30pm (not too bad). The table had no silverware, napkins nor glassware. The hostess stated she just wanted to seat us and someone will be over shortly to complete the setup of the table. Oh no Turkey. The buffet kept running out of Turkey (I am not a fan of Turkey but come on, its Thanksgiving)
Oscars:
When I made the room reservations, my the written e-mail confirmed a $50 breakfast credit at Oscars included with the suite reservation. I reveiwed my parents incidental charges prior to checkout on Friday (they stayed in the Suite) and NO credit not was applied. The front desk agent stated,"that was NOT part of your room rate". I asked to speak with the front desk manager, he checked my reservation on line and stated the same. I stated,"this is an easy fix, we can solve this now or I can dispute the charges with my credit card company" I was credited and later that day when I reviewed my reservation on line, it clearly stated on the second page of the confirmation, a $50 credit will be applied to breakfast at Oscars"
No evening houskeeping service. During previous stays, houskeeping would freshed up the rooms, replace towels etc while we were out. The houskeeper for the 8th floor could be seen sitting in her office in the main hall of the 8th floor yet she never seemed to make it to ours rooms. Both in 2001 and 2010 the rooms were straightened while we were out.
Upon checkout I called the 1-800 number to complain. Saturday evening at 6:55 pm I recieved a call, on my cell phone, from a manager. I was at the country club with friends and family just sitting down to drinks in the lounge (Yes, some of us still do that) and asked him to call back on Monday or Tuesday. No call was ever recieved.
12/9/12 I was in NYC for the weekend and decided to give the Walforf a second chance (Fool that I can be) and had breakfast at Oscars. I was seated at a table with dirty linen. Specifically a dirty napkin. I asked the hostess for a replacement, she said,"Maybe if you arrived earlier this would not be a problem (it was 9:30 am) and then she took a napkin from a dirty table that was just vacated and handed it to me.... Classy.
Steady yourself, This is the worst part.
My parents recieved at letter from Ana Tijan, Director of Rooms, Waldorf Astroia, outlining my complaints and offering them a free upgrade on their next stay. I was protecting my elderly parents from the multitude of issues at the Hotel and much to my embarrassment, Ms Ana Tijan was nice to outline all the issues in the letter. I spoke with Ms Tijan on 12/14/12 to tell her how embarressed I was with the letter and her response was,"I sign a lot of letters that other people write"
I was transferred to the GM, Mr Eric Long, spoke with his assistant, and I am waiting for a response.
I suggest a visit to the lobby, it is fine exapmle of art deco. Yet, there are many other fine Hotels in NYC to stay.

title: “Elegant and comfortable”
text: I had a long travel day and had to be up at the crack of dawn for a meeting. Check in was smooth. The room was clean and cozy. Room service valet was polite and accommodating. I slept like a baby! The meeting facilities were professional and comfortable.

title: “Great location, good value and comfortable”
text:
Our travel party consists of two adults and one 3-year-old and we stayed in a room with two queen beds which was plenty for our family. I booked via the Best Western website, which gave the cheapest rate compared to booking.com and other booking websites. 
Our stay did not start off to a good start, when we were left waiting for about 45 minutes for the free shuttle that never came. As advised to do so, I rang the hotel up after we'd picked up our luggage at the baggage claim to let them know to send a shuttle to pick us up. We were waiting and waiting in an area where there were lots of buses and shuttles (and no doubt breathing in a lot of fumes - not great for our asthmatic son). I rang the receptionist up again to enquire, and after putting me on a short hold to find out why our driver hadn't arrived, she came back on the phone and apologised profusely, then told me to take a cab to the hotel where I would get reimbursed for the cab fare. Apparently the driver had a matter come up urgently, which was understandable, but a replacement should have been dispatched. Needless to say, hubby and I were pretty annoyed, but other than that initial hiccup, service we received for the rest of our stay was fine.
The beds were comfortable, and we slept quite well. Breakfast was included, and it was nice not having to think about what to eat for brekkie. The selection was decent enough, and it gave us good energy to start the day with and see us through to lunch time. The location was great, and we walked almost everywhere, even to the zoo (although that is not recommended unless you're ready for a 1-hour hike, one-way). The ferry pier for Coronado was also nearby, where we spent half a day cycling all over the island.
For the location and the quality of the room, it was good value for money.

title: “Nice hotel, great location - walls a little thin though.”
text:
Had a great three-day stay at this property. Free wifi allowed me to stream movies on my iPad, so plenty fast. Lots of HD channels. Comfortable beds.
A few minor complaints: parking lot filled up quickly and we had to park somewhat further away than I would have liked. The maid service came at 4:30 each day - a bit later than I would have liked. And the walls were pretty thin. Each night revelers in the room next door sounded like the were in our room. If you are a light sleeper, consider earplugs.
All said though, I would recommend this property.

title: “Great addition!”
text: Just stayed at the new Westin at DTW. It's excellent in every way, and a great addition to the new Northwest terminal and the Detroit area. I'm a 100% traveller and know my hotels... this is first rate. It has all the typical Westin amenities (double shower head, pillow comforter, etc.) as well as a new movie system, a day bed in front of the large picture window overlooking the lobby, etc. The decor is very contemporary and quite attractive, with a bit of a Japanese rock garden motif. I also tried room service for breakfast the both the service and food was first rate. A good choice.

title: “Great Stay of you Count the Perks”
text: This is a very nice lavish hotel right on the riverwalk. Our rooms were riverview (some of the river) with floor to ceiling windows. The breakfast buffet was quite filling and good quality. The staff members were always very helpful. Internet service was about 4-5 Mbps and reliable. Parking was available directly across the street. My sense of value though was augmented by the fact that I was able to snag a San Antonio Tourism special offer which included free room upgrade, free daily parking (normally $25), free daily breakfast buffet (normally $18), and free daily internet (normally $12). Those perks made it a good value for my wife and I and a memorable trip.

title: “A GREAT STAY”
text: The check-in employees were more than willing to meet every need. Rodney, was exceptional at the front desk and he was willing to assist everyone he came in contact with. The drivers of the shuttle van were great and the hotel's policy to drive guest within a 3 mile radious of the hotel is smart. We were able to go out and eat and enjoy the sights. The ladies in the Concierge Room were also exceptional and did much more then required to include looking up items on the lap top and making some great recomendations. I felt more of the staff were highly professional and really cared about their guests. Not to sure about the restruant staff as I ate there a few times but was not greated with the same respect and friendilness as the other I come into contact with.. I would go back over and over.

title: “This New York Hotel gets it right. . .!”
text: This may be my favorite New York Hotel. I'm thrilled Le Parker Meridien is now part of the SPG family of hotels.

title: “Are You KIDDING With These Reviews?”
text:
I feel compelled to write about my experience at the Night after seening so many "above average" and "excellent" ratings; either the people posting have had no experience as hotel guests or these reviews have been planted by the people behind the Night. If you're looking for an inexpensive hotel and your expectations are very low, the Night might be OK. Otherwise, look elsewhere.
The first room I was taken to at the Night was so small that I could barely open the door without hitting the bed; I couldn't even fit my luggage in the 10" deep closet. When I asked to move to another room (I was staying for 7 days) I was taken to a room that was only slightly bigger. I've stayed in a lot of hotels in NYC, and these rooms are the smallest I've ever experienced, with the possible exception of rooms at the Paramount.
The beds are comfortable.
There was no 24 hour room service and the hotel restaraunt (pricey and mediocre) closed early. The staffers (who were the only GOOD thing about the hotel - lovely men and women) had no idea of what restaraunts would delliver to the hotel or where there was a 24 hour diner. (I often worked late into the night.) The gym - an Equinox - was an eight block walk, and you needed to get a pass from the desk. Each pass was $15, and the fee was billed to the room instantly, whether it was used or not. 
I didn't get messages, I didn't get wakeup calls, faxes didn't show up, and a room I'd booked for a business event was filthy at the appointed time. There's one elevator and it's slow if it's working at all - it can take ten minutes.
The location is good (if you like Times Square) and again, though they may have been incompetent the people who worked at the Night were great. 
If you're 21 and visiting from Iowa and intend to do nothing other than sleep in your room, then MAYBE the Night's for you.

title: “Good location”
text: Thanks to previous reviews we expected the overpriced parking and typical Hyatt room. The location is probably the drawing point for this hotel as it is a convenient downtown Denver location. We were treated courteously and experienced no problems. The bellman almost beat us to our room and we had very brief waits for our vehicle. I appreciated the added security of needing to use your room key in the elevator to access the floors between 6 pm and 6 am. The rooms are nice sized for 2 adults and we were comfortable.

title: “Interesting location ...plenty to do”
text: I stayed a couple of nights at this property. Standard Hilton Garden Inn. Spacious rooms, free internet, helpful staff, decent breakfast. I checked in late in the night and realized that i had not availed my corporate discount. The person at the front desk told me to go to my room as it was well past mid-night and he would take care of the changes. By the next morning everything was sorted out. The hotel is right in the middle of the Polaris Parkways with plenty of eating options within a mile of the property.

title: “Functional, reasonable, recommended”
text: in town for a couple days and needed a hotel near the airport where i was doing business. Straight up, no frills kind of hotel and reasonably priced. Clean, tidy and unremarkable - I would stay again. Free high speed internet was a real bonus but the free coffee in the room was pretty unpalatable

title: “Worst hotel ever...”
text:
Where to begin... My wife and I were going to Seattle to visit family, and decided to try this boutique style of hotel. This is not the first time staying in a boutique hotel, but certainly my last here. Having worked in hotels in the past, I know how to treat the customers, obviously these people do not.
When we checked in, and we were not offered any bellstaff for our bags (5 bags for 2 people is bulky), we went to our room, and small it was. That is fine, we were expecting this, so no big deal. As soon as we got there we went down to RedFin which wa a GREAT rest. The people there are amazing, and VERY friendly... Too bad it is not part of the hotel. They warned us to go down if we wanted a beer instead of ordering through room service. This way we could save the $3.00 added fee for delivery. I went back up to my room, and then came down again 10 minutes later. The maintenance staff, housekeepers, staff, and just about everyone has to fit into the 2 SMALL elevators. The staff does not ahve their own elevators. I had to fit in there with the bellboy, and his cart (not an easy fit, and I am not big).
We went out the next morning and left the towels on the floor, no coffee, no tea, and no more shampoo, conditioner, or soap. We came back that evening and guess what... No towels, no coffee, not tea, no shampoo, no conditioner, and no soap. We called down and got all of the above, but of course we tipped the service.
Next day we got up and went out again. We step out and it is raining... DAMN, we forgot our umbrella in SF. So we are stuck walking around int he rain. all day (staf at the door does not open door, and does not offer anything for the rain, or to get a cab for us). We come back to the hotel and guesswhat we don't have???? YUP, no towels, no coffee, no tea, no shampoo, no conditioner, no soap. But we also seem to be missing my wife's birth control pills. someone STOLE my wife's pills!?!?!?!?!?!?! they were there that morning (she took one).
Next day I go out early in the AM to meet up with a buddy. I came back with coffee for myself and my wife. I have 2 cups of coffee in 2 hands, and the doorman is too busy texting on his phone to open the door for me!!!! i had to stack the cups before the doorman noticed I was there. Speaking of doormen, is that really what they are there to do? open doors is their job... But God forbid they do their job. They spend the entire time talking to each other (Cracking jokes), on their phones, or texting (1 guy did offer to get us a cab on evening)...
Checkout day was the straw that broke the camel's back... We go down to check out, and a few things came up. I asked about a cab to the airport, and I was told that the hotel would have a town car take us. GREAT, for only $5.00 more I was all about that. Nice, BIG, comfy towncar or a cab... Not a tough call. We check our bags in and get our 5 bag tags. My wife and I went out for a while and came back for our bags and the ride to the hotel. NOW the fun begins. I go out back to go to the restroom, and I saw the door to the baggage storing area WIDE OPEN, and NO ONE was around the room. I waited for over 20 mintes, and no one showed up to close the door. I could have gone in and taken anything i wanted during this time. I went back outfront and gave the guys my bag tags, and they came out with the wrong bag... I mean COME ON!!!! So we get the right bags, and get to the towncar. All of a sudden some lady decided to get in the car with us. I guess the hotel overbooked the towncar, andwe were supposed to share our car with another lady?!?!?!?!!? 
So in the end, I would say do NOT stay at this hotel. The size is small, but the service is horrendous. I would have expected more from a Best Western hotel in the projects of San Francisco.

title: “Bed bugs!!!!!!!”
text: Do not stay there, the place is full of bed bugs, don't stay even if they give you rooms for free....

title: “Overpriced For The Average Couple/Family”
text:
The hotel is ideally placed if you want to be in the centre of things; which is a double-edged sword. Good if you have a few days to spend and want to see the majority of the tourist attractions or near transit links to see them. However, for that same reason, all the bars etc are very expensive for many blocks around. The average beer price is between $5 - £9, even more expensive than the UK by some margin. Food, except junk food, is also every overpriced, likewise in the hotel bar/restaurant. Presumably due to the historic status of the hotel, the windows are on the thin side and obviously no double glazing or noise abatement. Therefore, it is fairly noisy, unless you are quite high up.
It has a nice entrance. Unfortunetly, interesting architecture does not make a great hotel. Although the bag handlers and security were pleasant and helpful, the staff behind the counter in reception were fairly unsmiling and officious with that false politeness and brusqueness that the service sector is famous for in America; especially in NYC. My girlfriend was in floods of tears within 10 minutes fo arrival, partly due to rudeness and also a mix up with then hotel that may or may not have been the hotels fault. The duty Manager, in the end, when she dropped the aforesaid atttitude and actually started smiling and acting like a real person - treating us like people/customers - tried her best to sort out the situation, which was done a few days later. To me, this should be the default attitude of all staff, not something you eventually get to when staff drop that defensiveness that they have. To be fair, this was attitude we experienced throughout the city...Small towns in PA & NJ were a welcome relief from this......
The room was was clean and the cleaners did a good job. The view was good too. However, it was an odd shape and fairly uninspiring and I have stayed in bigger/more personal/welcoming three-star hotels and B & Bs throughout the UK. On this basis and having seen the bill, I would say the rooms were quite over-priced, if not very overpriced. The room was not four-star by any stretch of the imagination. There is better value, but more welcoming hotel rooms/B & Bs to be had in NYC. For example, in the second half of the weekend we rented a welcoming, airy and warm appartment in the suburbs via AirB&B. If you want your own space and better value - especially if you are a couple or small family/group of friends, I would recomend doing this instead. In essence, this is a three-star hotel pretending to be a four-star hotel, seemingly because of the architecture/lobby

title: “Fun and comfortable hotel”
text:
Spent the weekend at the Hotel (was in town for a music festival.) Staff was very friendly. The concierge desk is very attentive; they contacted us a week in advance to see if we had any things we wanted to book in advance, unfortunately they couldn't get a dinner reservation for us at the Girl and the Goat but everything else they did was great. 
There were a few mix ups with a room change / stay over for us - and after getting locked out of our room twice it did get resolved (just took a lot of time for their error.)
The hotel location is great. Took the train in from Midway - the stop was one half block away. There isn't a lot going on in the financial district around the hotel during the weekend but that was fine with us - less street noise and it was still very easy to get to everything. It is a several block walk to Millenium Park etc (got in a couple good early morning runs along the waterfront). Also their car service (via Acura) is good for being dropped off - but book early, as it was completely booked for the evening when we checked in at 4;30 PM.)
Original room was interior court yard view which was supposed to be quieter. Unfortunately it was directly across from the eleveator and so we moved to an exterior room on a high floor. With the exception of one siren vehicle in the early hours street noise was not an issue.
Had a two bed room and it was very comfortable, bathroom was great and everything was very clean and well maintained.
The first floor has bars and restaurant and walk through it to get to reception. It is a fun young vibe but not for everyone. Had dinner at the bar one night - the bar tender was great but the kitchen was very slow (decent food.)

title: “Really a boutique...”
text: Disguised as a "biggie", this sleeper offers boutique character and comfort. The staff is outstanding and very accommodating to individual needs. Surprisingly quiet rooms surpass oct NYC hotels. Excellent restaurant and bar, but shuts down a bit early for NYC.

title: “Good Location, Good Deal”
text:
Stayed here for two nights in June. Found a good internet deal. Good location for all public transportation around town
Compared to other hotels downtown San Fran a very good price.
As noted in other reviews the rooms are very small but very clean and comfortable. This is an older hotel but again very nice condition.
Nice large flat screen TV.
The elevator is so tight and small I took the stairs most of the time being on the 3rd. floor
Here is my only complaint. Heard steet noises most of the night. Garbage pick up was very noisy. So if you stay here ask for a upper floor. My son-in-law and daughter were on one of the top floors and did not have a problem with the noise.
I would stay here again if I was able to get the same rate and a upper floor.
Did not eat at the restaurant downstairs but it looked very good but some what expensive. 
Did not have a car so did not have to pay parking fee that I believe was either $30 or $40 a night.

title: “Sleek and comfortable”
text: Fantastic apartment/hotel hybrid. Not like a regular hotels, in a good way. We had actual fancy martini and champagne glasses in the room. Great views, amazing customer service, central location, wine and cheese happy-hour. Can get a touch confusing trying to find your way back to your room, but I managed. Loved this place.

title: “Location , Location Location....not so good.”
text: The Hotel website was somewhat deceiving, really hyped it up. I was dissapointed it was not what I expected at all. The employees at desk were very helpful and tried to make us comfortable but I was alittle freaked out about the hotels surroundings, quite an eyeopener could be looked at as good for our kids or not.

title: “Very Enjoyable”
text: Spent two days at the T&C Resort. Had a suite on the first floor - it was VERY nice. The staff was excellent. Would highly recommend it for your stay in San Diego. Easy access to the I-8 freeway. Close to Old Town and Downtown area.

title: “Great Deal Great Hotel. You should stay here!”
text:
My boyfriend and I stayed the night here on a day trip from Portland. The University Tower was BY FAR the best deal we found in the city when you consider what you get. The rating says it's a two star. I work in the hotel industry and can say it's easily a three star. The staff is excellent and the building is well designed inside and out. The lobby is beautiful and includes free computer kiosks which were very convenient.
It's not right downtown, but it's a short drive away. Also, our specific room was miniscule but we paid only about 90 bucks for it! WELL WORTH THE SHORT DRIVE AND SMALL room. If you decide to upgrade to a suite this is the perfect Seattle hotel.

title: “Very impressed”
text: I was very impressed with this hotel. The hotel is clean and modern with many facilities. The rooms are great. They have free internet, a small gym, and breakfast is included in your rate. The location is wonderful. You can eat at restaurants nearby on Fisherman's Wharf or catch a cable car (two block walk) and go up to China Town. I cannot fault this hotel!

title: “decent hotel in great location.”
text: I have stayed at this hotel several times. It is definitely becoming more and more run down. My room was either too hot or too cold. The service in the restaurant at breakfast was not very good but Bar 10 was great. The room service staff is also excellent. The biggest positive is the location which cannot be beat.

title: “Great choice”
text: Lots of great points about this hotel. The bedrooms are great and really spacious : living-room and small kitchen in case you want to cook your own meals. The hotel is really well situated with a metro station at a five-minute walk. The staff is welcoming and eager to help you. I would definitely come back again!

title: “well run property in great location”
text:
See your room first. When I arrived, the first room we were given was extremely small with a horrendous view. I immediately called the front desk and complained. The manager showed me to a very nice and much bigger room that was perfect. We did NOT book the smallest room and my husband is an elite marriott member so I was disappointed at first but the hotel recovered quickly. 
The hotel is very nicely decorated, tasteful and hip without being over the top obnoxious. It was quiet and peaceful. The breakfast area was especially lovely. The concierge had many good recommendations and excellent advice. The rooms were quiet despite facing the busy street. The cocktails at the bar were strong and well performed. 
I would not hesitate to stay here again.

title: “Great place to stay”
text: I've stayed here several times and continue to be impressed with the pre-trip help and the service when I arrived. For the price and what you get I believe it's the best deal in mid-town. You can get nicer but you also will pay $200-300 more. It's in a quiet part of town and five minutes from subways. A great deli is a two minute walk down the street with great food. Plus, you're a ten minute walk from Central Park. I can't recommend it enough.

title: “William's favorite in DC”
text: This is one of the finest hotels I've stayed at in a long time..I don't often get to DC and I usually look for discounted rates..I should say that as long as you book during one of their promos to recieve a discount on the room the price would be reasonable. Otherwise, as one would expect lodging in DC is rather expensive. But this hotel has excellent customer service and the rooms are impeccable. I would have thought that Internet access in the rooms would be free but it is not. However the hotel's location within walking distance of Union Station makes it an ideal spot( because I hate to have to look for transportation after I've been on the road all day). Also you are about two blocks from the Metro.

title: “Historic Hotel”
text:
Great hotel....you must stay here for the views of the lake and for the history. You will not find the largest rooms or the modern amenities in the restrooms of newer hotels but the fine details or workmanship and history makes it worth the stay.
I wish they offered a behind the scenes tour of the place!

title: “Loved our stay!”
text: To start, I am a travel agent and have stayed at numerous hotels (I was not traveling as an agent this time). This was a great hotel by comparison. Not luxury but very nice. We were traveling for a cheerleader competition so the close proximity to the convention center is our reasoning for choosing this property however it was a little further than I thought (about 6 blocks-they told us 2). The rooms were clean and crisp with modern furniture. Bathrooms were updated and worked great. The air conditioning was not the greatest but was good enough. The view was amazing and we didn't even have the monument view which would have been even better. We had connecting rooms (a king corner room and a room with 2 double beds) which were requested and delivered as promised. One of the rooms was not ready upon check in (even though it was late) but that wasn't a big deal. I thought the service was great. People were friendly and very helpful. There always seemed to be several staff members around to help with directions, information or anything else you might need. Parking was great and convenient though a little expensive. The hallways were a little dated. The wallpaper was peeling a little but since I didn't sleep there I didn't care. The 9th floor pool was a little dissapointing. However this is one of the few downtown hotels that has an outdoor pool. Like many other reviews I agree it was little more than a pool amoung a vast concrete roof with a few lounge chairs. The view from there was amazing though. It overlooked the monument. There is a lot of potential there and I think they could make the pool area great. The location of the hotel was perfect. We walked everywhere. There was so much to see and do in the area. I would stay here again.

title: “Comfy, laid-back, somewhat retro and very unique”
text: We stayed at Humphrey’s for a mini staycation, partly because we’ve always wanted to stay there, but mostly to escape some long-term house guests for a night. My only complaint about Humphrey’s is that I wish we could have stayed longer. Our stint was quite brief but long enough for us to enjoy the lovely harbor view and super comfy king-sized bead, tour the grounds, enjoy a leisurely breakfast, stroll around Shelter Island and meet Humphrey’s resident free-range parrot. We thoroughly enjoyed the semi retro/semi Tiki vibe at the place and found the overall gestalt to be exactly what we were in the mood for. And the gardens were lovely. The one bit of advice I would give is to go elsewhere for breakfast and skip the on site restaurant. There was nothing wrong with it per se, but there are certainly better breakfasts to be had for the money (though the view and ambiance were quite nice). Oh, and FYI - the restaurant and room service close at 9 pm during the week, as does the Bali Hai restaurant down the street, so this is not where you want to be for a night cap or if you’re a late diner. Aside from that, it’s a great choice if you’re looking for a unique San Diego experience on the moderately upscale side.

title: “Great stay”
text: This was a wonderful stay. Comfortable bed, clean room, and very clean bathroom. More than enough linens. Awesome breakfast.

title: “squeaky wood floors”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the Prescott August 26 & 27, 2005, because we generally like the Kimpton Group hotels and wanted to try a different one (we would normally stay at Palomar).
We stayed in a club level room. It was tiny and seemed to be no different from the non-club level rooms that we peeked into whle they were being cleaned.
Our major complaint is that the Prescott's floors are wood. So you hear every move that the guests above you make. Our upstairs neighbor seemed unusually restless at 3 am. Also, the cleaning staff made an unacceptable amount of noise at 8 am cleaning the room next door.
Also, our room looked worn and dated. Like the hotel was last refreshed in the late 1980's. It's time for new carpet, wallpaper, and paint!
As a final insult, a trim piece from my wife's car was missing when it was returned by the valet parking staff at the end of our stay. We've complained, but the hotel hasn't made it right yet.
We wouldn't stay here again. The Palomar is a much better value within the Kimpton group hotels in San Francisco.

title: “Kind of feels like Cheers....”
text: Many hotels have great facilities and a great location (you can't beat the energy of Dupont Circle)....and the Palomar is right up there with the best of them in the boutique category. What sets the Palomar apart is the staff. From check in to check out...in the restaurant....the concierge...at the front desk, at the front door...picking up the car....house keeping...room service...all were welcoming, friendly and courteous professionals. We expect to be back in D.C. many times over the next few years and will be back at the Palomar.

title: “Excellent location”
text: On Google maps it didn't really show how close this hotel was to a T station, but it literally is 10ft away from Kenmore. I personally would stay here again because it is perfect for accessing the T to go any where else in the city and it's only a street over from Newbury St. My biggest con which might sound very petty is they didn’t have a coffee maker in the room. They had a filled refrigerator with drinks and candy along with draw filled with snacks which of course are extra $$, but no coffee maker.

title: “Beautiful Architecture in Hotel!”
text: We had a very nice stay! This is a classic hotel with beautiful architectural design. Staff was friendly, restaurant was good, rooms were clean. We would certainly stay here again!

title: “Nesting bed for Nasty Truck Drivers”
text:
