This was by far the worse place I have ever stayed. I am female and I was there to visit a friend. I found out that the owners of this hotel also own a trucking company (Nationwide Carriers) and they run the trucking company out of the hotel. I saw a ton of 18-wheelers around back. That is why their parking lot is full of potholes. 
When I was there, I was walking out the front door and two nasty, dirty truck drivers approached me and said that they have a community room (I think it is room 146 if my memory serves me correctly) and I look like I like to have fun and asked me to come to their rooms. I was scared, and I lied and said I was waiting on my husband to come to the lobby. The truck drivers said they stay in the hotel for free because it is their home office for their company and they love to have fun. 
This hotel is also lurking with prostitutes, who know about the trucker room. You can see these women walking around the halls and the management is aware, but they don't care. They allow these women to come into their establishment to "please their drivers". 
I am a family oriented person, and I did realize such things existed. All the other negative comments about the rooms are correct, from holes in the ceiling to one of the hallway walls completely exposed to the outside world. It is not safe, and after one night I was out of there. I am writing this review to warn people about the dangers they are in with these horny, nasty truck driver's they have lurking around the place. One truck driver said to me they are bored cause they don't have a car and their boss won't let them drive the big truck, so all they do is walk the halls looking for a "good time." Everyone - beware!
Oh yeah, and the black lady at the counter is VERY RUDE, and the Indian guy that was there the next morning was acting and talking like he was a rapper, and he was rude. Just a really weird experience for me. I won't be going back!

title: “Amazing stay. Perfect location”
text:
I spent 4 nights in a 2 double beds bedroom on the 14th floor at this hotel. I was in New York for business, the location was good. Located in Lower East side, it takes about 8$ for a cab ride that drives you on Union Square and around. The staff was very polite, every day we were given cookies or other goodies to eat. 
The beds are amazing, the pillow a bit less but it's a question of taste. I like firm pillows and I am never satisfied in any hotel so that is just me. The lobby is amazing, very design. The front desk is on the second floor but don't worry, a doorman is always downstairs to answer your questions or help you. 
Nothing bad to say, I would definately go back.
Well, yeah there is one thing : I was a bit disapointed to see that the glasses in the mini bar area were stained with water, wich doesnt help me to think that those rumors are true about the maids in hotels (in general) arent washing the glasses hahaha

title: “Delightful hotel, thoughtful staff, attention to detail ensures we will return.”
text: My partner and I took advantage of a great promotion and got a $289 room for $89 per night. The price was the only thing that was reduced though! The service and thoughtfulness of the staff was way above par. The queen room was on the smaller side, but lovely and clean. The high ceiling (12'?) gave a wonderful feeling of airiness to the room, however. The attention to detail in the decor is wonderful. The robes were thick zebra print terry, perfect for curling up against the down pillows. Another great note was the height and power of the shower. We are both over 6' tall and the shower head was at least 4" above us, plus showered down with a good amount of force. A+++

title: “Clean comfortable quiet affordable”
text:
My husband and I stayed here for 3 nights in February on our anniversary trip to SF. We got a great deal on our via Travelocity and for what we paid I didn't expect much- just a clean room and decent bed to sleep on. I was pleasantly surprised to find out we ended up with a King bedroom (thought we were getting a queen) on the 4th floor. Our room was on the alley/ backside of the building so it was fairly quiet. The staff is decent- not overly friendly, but helpful. 
The bed was comfortable and the room was a good size. The bathroom is a little small with no vanity, but that wasn't an issue for us.
Based on the reviews I had read we didn't plan to eat breakfast there. "Breakfast" is coffee/tea and a TINY selection of pastries, fruit and yogurt. Mel's Diner is right next door and serves typical diner type food. There is also a place across the street, but I don't think they do breakfast and it is cash only. Starbucks was our bet for a light breakfast and there was one 5 mins walking distance. 
The location is great! We were a 15 min walk from China Town and 10 mins from Union Square. It is also very convenient to the Muni and BART (we flew into Oakland and took the BART into SF and walked 10 mins from Union Square to the hotel). We had no issues with the area and although it does seem to boarder some questionable streets we never had any issues when we were out walking around (morning or late at night- past 12am). 
We would definitely stay here again.

title: “Will return again and again!”
text: Two night stay at the JW with a friend to just "play" in the city. Service was outstanding from valet parking to departure. We did not dine onsite but did get a tour of the spa and wish we had more time to use those facilities. Rooms were soundproof and comfortable. Bathrooms in the standard guest room were incredible. We only live 40 miles away but will return to what will be a world class hotel in no time.

title: “Great value Near Galleria Area, Greenway Plaza, Houston”
text:
I have been a regular business traveler to Houston and stay at Crown Plaza River oaks frequently. I also stayed at near by Galleria hotels as well as the ones at West belt area. This is a great value considering the price paid and service. I work at Green way plaza and Crown plaza river oaks is walkable. Location is fantastic. Costco, LA fitness are with in a mile. Lots of parking in a near by deck. The rooms size is good, but the color scheme and carpet is little pale. Time to update the paint. The pool is very small and not much use. Breakfast is very good with hot and cold options, but little expensive. Reception staff are excellent. Especially Shaila and Anna Marie are super nice, very friendly and always been very helpful. 
In summary an excellent value with an outstanding frond desk staff

title: “Excellent Hotel, Best staff ever.”
text:
We stayed in this hotel for three days during our trip from Dallas to Memphis. Beside the fact that the hotel is close to downtown it also has a great staff. They helped us to get tickets for the Mavericks ( great experience) and always tried to make our stay pleasant. 
The rooms are big enough and the beds were great. So too all the travelers from Europe and especially from the Netherlands if you want to visit Dallas book this hotel.

title: “Better than expected - WOULD stay again!”
text:
We got our reservation for Club Quarters - Philadelphia through Hotwire. Initially, I was disappointed when the hotel was revealed as this hotel, since I knew nothing about it. Immediately I went to tripadvisor to read up. I felt somewhat better but was still quite scared that we had made a mistake. I am usually very picky and didn't think I was going to enjoy my stay.
As we drove to the hotel, I started to feel better... we passed quite a few good restaurants and a lot of shopping that looked interesting. There was a mall directly across the street (which is where the hotel parking is). 
As we entered the building, it seemed fine. It is more of a private club atmosphere than a hotel. There isn't really any "service" such as bellboys, etc. but this was fine with us since we are pretty self-sufficent and were only spending a weekend. The lobby had a very comfortable feel and check in was quick and easy.
Our room was a pleasant surprise... not spectacular but definately comfortable and had lots of extras. Other reviewers have mentioned the room/bathrooms size and I agree with them...the rooms are NOT huge but ours was a great size for us. It had a microwave, range, coffepot, tea kettle, fridge, a bar/desk area for eating of working, free wireless usage, a tv AND dvd player (which was great since we brought some to play on our laptop). The bathroom was very small but was fine with us since we didn't spend much time in the hotel room.
If you want modern and sleek (which I personally love...) THIS IS NOT IT, however I really enjoyed staying at Club Quarters. I would definately stay here again!
My only complaints: no extra pillows in the room and the walls needed to be washed. However, it still was cleaner than our stay at the Loews last year (which has a great look). Our room at the Loews was REALLY dirty!

title: “Great rooms, location and views”
text: We were pleasantly surprised by the high quality of this hotel. Rooms have are new look and feel, well lighted and very clean. Our room was west facing, offering wonder views from the 10th floor. We booked on a special holiday rate of $119./night, a fantastic value. Hotel is in easy walking distance of the Reading Terminal Market, which is a cornicopia of ethnic foods, crafts and local products. Independence park is about a 20 minute walk, but you can hop on the Market St subway and get there in 5 minutes. If you have a car, be prepared for the $35 daily parking. Overall, parking is pricy anywhere downtown, so mass transit or taxi's are recommended.

title: “Historic and luxurious”
text:
Recently I was in San Francisco on business and a friend who lives there suggested I stay at the Archbishop's Mansion. As a frequent business traveler, I get tired of big sterile hotels. The Archbishop's Mansion is full of charm and antiques. Each room is done as a different opera theme - I was able to peak in several rooms and all were beautiful. There are so many antiques including a mirrow that was in Lincoln's bedroom. The mansion is located on Alamo Square Park which is surrounded by some of the most beautiful Victorians in San Francisco. 
It is a quiet residential area but not too far from downtown or great places to eat.

title: “Friendly service and value for money”
text: Booked our accomodation through wotif.com, from the moment we got there we felt welcome. We ate at the hotels restaraunt and i had a crab cake sandwich which was excellent. Special mention to the concierge Mary Mastrobuoni, who made our stay more enjoyable by answering all our questions and being a great help. She made the effort to speak to us every time we were in the lobby and our stay in Philadelphia wouldn't have been the same without Mary's help.

title: “Not bad at all”
text: We were hesitant to stay at this location due to some of the bad reviews, but were pleased that we did. The reviews about the lobby and hallway conditions are extreme. We felt that given the existing age of the hotel that Westin has done a good job with the upkeep. The staff was nice and the room was just a nice as any other 3-4 star hotel. We enjoyed our visit.

title: “Great place to stay in NYC!”
text:
Originally I had planned to stay in budget accomodations in NYC, and move here towards the end of my stay to relax in my own room. However the place I did stay in at first was so bad I had to leave. I spent a frantic morning rushing around trying to find somewhere, eventually heading to the Pod. I explained my situation and asked if they had any rooms free. The man on the desk kept getting distracted by the phone, so another man, I presume the manager, came over to check on me. He found my reservation and said my room was free now if I wanted it. They blocked it off while I went back for my bags and checked me in fine, earlier than normal but with no hassle.
I was in a single room with shared bathroom, the room was small but modern and very clean. With a small hangar area, a stainless steel sink, tissues and towels, a flatscreen tv, and desk with alarm clock with an ipod dock in it. This was VERY helpful for charging up my ipod before travelling home! Esp as my ipod crashed during my stay but I could run it down and recharge it and it worked again!
There was little noise from other guests, when you could hear someones TV walking the coridoors you couldnt hear that in your room. The worst was some young teenagers who were in and out of each others rooms and whispering but loudly in the coriddors. But this wasnt a big deal, and most hotels will have noise in them!
The shared bathrooms were toilet, sink and shower, again modern, clean and absolutely fine. They play music in them from reception which was a nice touch, and the showers have shower gel and shampoo if you dont have your own.
The staff were so helpful in getting me in when I was upset, the rooms cleaned to a very high standard, the location was great only one avenue from 51st St Subway which was a quick interchange (or walk) to Grand Central and connections there. There are a couple of places on the corner which serve food and drink, so you can get breakfast or lunch quite easily.
Good hotel, and one I would stay in again without any fuss!

title: “Nice room in a Hotel with poor service.”
text:
I booked 3 nights in New York to celebrate my Wife's Birthday. Looking for Hotels this one was highly rated and right in the middle of Times Square, so it looked like a good choice. Charlie who took our bags as we arrived in our Taxi was GREAT! a hard working and excellent helper, it seemed to stop there however. The Bellman lost our luggage until we called him 30 minutes later asking for it, I was told they would get to it when they could! Not the right answer for me to hear.
The next day the maids forgot to refill the amenties in the room, so we called for replacements and after 40 minutes they arrived, not great service. The head of guest services did appologize to her credit, but service never really got better. The resturant for breakfast was very nice, fresh OJ and a good spread. The hotel air and heat worked well. The bathrooms are small for a hotel, and the room decore was a little tired and frayed. I will probably book at the Marriott next time.

title: “Loved This Hotel”
text: Newly renovated, luxurious hotel. Everything was beautiful and clean. Located right next to a cable car stop. Our room faced the cable car route, but I did not find it to be too loud. Sound proofing between rooms also was good, I couldn't hear anyone. Nice views. Cheaper than the rates of the Fairmont across the street where my husband was attending a conference. Other reviews have mentioned the pocket doors on the bathroom. Ours had that, but the toilet itself was way at the end of a long walk in closet and sink area, so I don't think the door is an issue as far as sound as other people stated. At least in our room it wasn't. Hotel is located at top of NOB HILL, so I think it's amusing that some reviewers didn't like the hill climb. If you aren't ambulatory, better book elsewhere. This is San Francisco, yes there are hills! Take a cab if you aren't up to it.

title: “Great location, awesome views!! But beware wedding season and drunken guests.”
text: This hotel was in a great location and the view from our Inner Harbor view room on the 26th floor was awesome! Within walking distance to Little Italy for dinner and Fells Point for cocktails. Extra towels and pillows provided as requested. There were many weddings at the hotel that day, which later became our only disappointing experience...when the guests became our drunken neighbors. The yelling and banging until 2am reminded us more of a frat house than the beautiful hotel we had checked into only 12hrs earlier. However, hotel security did handle the situation promptly after we called the front desk, and the neighbors left their room to party elsewhere. In the moring we received a letter of apology and complimentary room service....nice touch and great customer service!! Otherwise, the accomodations and stay were wonderful, and we would go back again (maybe NOT during wedding season though).

title: “Garbage!!! Ignore the name Omni! Replace with Super 8!”
text: So I booked this hotel based on experiences in other Omnis. This is more like a super 8. Nothing about this hotel other than the loby. The room is very small and the ventilation is soooo poor that if you are unlucky enough to be on a floor with a smoking room, yes they have them on the same floor, then you are basically SOL. We might as well be smokers. Our cloths smell, our room smells. Its disgusting. Restaurant is extremely over priced to an insulting extent. Its very basic menu and not very well prepared.

title: “Great small hotel”
text:
The hotel is located between the convention center and LODO near the 16th pedestrian mall
That is perfect location for business and eating and the theater
The room was very nice with operable window to enjoy the Denver air and interesting decor
Staff was helpful on the best tradition of the boutique hotel
Worth a stay

title: “Awesome long-stay hotel in Dallas..”
text: Amazing staff, wonderful breakfast, and efficient housekeeping. To top it up, the kitchenette is a boon for vegetarians and long-stay people. Parking is free, and there are quite a few decent eating joints outside, in case you don't feel like cooking.

title: “Bad”
text:
I've been left waiting for 3 hours for my room. Looks like somebody gave a late check-out without checking availability.
Managers didn't solve the problem just trying to win time while the room was being cleaned.
When cheking-out some expenses were not included and took 20min in front of front desk to include. No care at all with quality.
Service a side good overall idea and infra.

title: “Top marks”
text:
Booked this hotel on the strength of previous reviews and wasn't disappointed. I can't fault anything about this hotel - perfect location; super-friendly staff; large, clean room (with state-of-the-art entertainment system!); and great value at $149 a night. 
Parking is $30 per day - although I'm told that this is standard for San Francisco.
My wife, a travel journalist, says this is one of the best hotels she's ever stayed in anywhere in the world, and I find it hard to disagree. We'll be back.

title: “Good hotel, centrally located so you can walk just a few blocks to everything”
text:
Visiting DC spots with the nephews. Did the standard DC tourist trip and the hotel was well placed only few block from mueseums, tourist bus/trolley routes and a number of good resturants (Gordon Biersch, Hardrock, Fuddruckers) close by to support two teenaged boys.
Rooms were clean and well turned out. We didn't have a frig but when I called down they sent one up about 30 mins later. Also they had some floors going through renovation so they were not open, it didn't impact our stay but for future guests they may get one of the improved floors.
The only issue was that noise from the hallways seemed to pass freely into the room. For myself I sleep like a rock but my wife had some issues because there seemed to be a group of young adults who after 1:30 AM (and the bars closed) decided to randomly roam the halls visiting friends, have a feeling they were a part of a bigger tour group. My wife said a group would go by every 30-40 mins, she woke me up around 4 AM and we called the front desk who sent some folks around but pretty sure those roaming the halls finally called it a night.
If you are on an exterior room (even room numbers I think) recommend a high floor because the surrounding streets and sidewalks are fairly close to the '3rd' floor level.
The lobby has a full on starbucks and the breakfast buffet is quiet good if expensive ($20 for an adult, $10 for child 17 and under). Didn't try the hotel resturant or bar due to the nephews but menu looked good and the bar seemed well stocked. Lobby overall was one of the better ones I've seen.
Overall it was good visit and the front desk apologized for the problems of the night before when we checked out but only so much can be done.

title: “Staff makes this Courtyard shine.”
text:
In the big scheme of things a hotel is a hotel and the difference between three and five stars is the attention to the little things. The staff makes all the difference at this Courtyard. The hotel is nice and the location convenient to Baltimore's inner harbor.
We got a room on the 14th floor and loaded our bags in on a hotel cart. When we got to our room, the attendant who was cleaning other rooms on the floor came and got our cart and told us to settle in and she would take care of the cart.
It was that way the entire weekend. It was as if the staff believed it was their job to take care of guests. This hotel represents the best of what I like about the Marriott brands.

title: “Nice hotel for conferences and exploring DC”
text: This is a tired Grand Hyatt-it definitely needs updating-no makeup/shaving mirrors in the bathroom, slightly worn carpet and drapes; didn't have the amenities you'd expect from a Grand Hyatt (although there is a Starbucks in the lobby and you can print your boarding passes from computers in the lobby). But, the people are fantastic-very friendly and helpful and the location is great. The hotel is easy to get to from the airport-take the blue line (metro) for ~$3.25 to the Metro Center stop which has an exit to the hotel. It's only three blocks to the Wash DC convention center and an easy walk to the Mint, Spy Museum, Natural History Museum, or many points of interest. Try Cuba Libre restaurant on the corner-fabulous mojitos (especially the Passion Fruit) and their pulled pork (Lechon Asado) is incredible. Also a couple of blocks away is a turkish restaurant, Zatinya's which has a bright atmosphere and wonderful mediterranean food (make reservations-it's popular).

title: “Great family stay!”
text:
We just returned from a great family vacation in DC and Williamsburg. We stayed in a two bedroom Capital suite and it was extremely spacious. The Four Seasons did not disappoint with their extras for the kids. When we checked in, they wheeled out a bunch of stuff animals for the kids to choose from and of course had the robes for the kids and an age appropriate book on each of their beds, including the roll away bed I had requested. Twice they brought up desserts for the kids, which was a great treat for them! They also had a stroller for our 5 year old, which was handy for all the walking we did. Mel, the concierge, did a great job of reserving a car for us, booking a tour guide (we had Kathleen, who was wonderful!!!! Highly recommend that!) and recommending dinner places.
We did use the indoor pool, which the kids enjoyed. We also ate dinner at the Steakhouse on site and the food was great. We ordered room service each morning, and it was prompt and tastey. Overall, it was a typical Four Seasons experience with great service at a great hotel.
We enjoyed the Georgetown location...there is an icecream shop right outside of the hotel.
My only slight complaint was we booked through AMEX platimum and received a $200 spa credit--yet I called twice to book a facial and they never had someone on staff who could do it. They also don't do nails. So my only option was a massage...which I wasn't in the mood for....

title: “Beautiful Hotel, Great Staff, Central Location”
text: My wife and I stayed at the Conrad Indianapolis last week and it exceeded what we had anticipated. The lobby was gorgeous and the valet and front desk were very friendly. We were offered a bottle of water several times and people took time out from their work just to greet us and open a door. The room was immaculate and comfortable. We had a great view of the Artsgarden below. Had zero complications and everything worked flawlessly. The bed was very comfortable too. Location is right off the Monument Circle and is way better than the other major luxury hotel in Indy (JW Marriott). Will definitely stay again when we visit Indianapolis next.

title: “HIGHLY RECOMMEND”
text:
The hotel was great from day 1. 
Great & fast service- ask for some extra towels and they were braught up in 15 minutes.
Excellent room.-The beds were very comfy, flat screen t.v, lovely bathroom, very clean. EXCELLLENT VIEW!! In new york, most hotel views are of the wall of another building so you don't see much but this room had an amazing view for the price.
Location- chelsea is getting fixed up little by little so its not as busy as times square which may get one who isn't comfortable with new york yet. your in between times square and downtown only a few blocks away. Times square was like 8 blocks and downtown i took a subway because is was a few more blocks. The subway was right down the block. You are right next to 8th avenue where they are tons of restaurants. 
98% recommended.

title: “It's Clean, friendly but...”
text: After arriving at the hotel with a 7 hour drive behind us we were exhausted ! The check-in was fast and the front desk staff was THE BEST I have ever dealt with ! They were awesome ! We got the parking pass and directions to the garage, ok Big trucks don't fit ! So they give us directions to a lot nearby. OK so truck is aways away & not that secured. Up to our room, WOW it is nicely decorated, super clean , modern with everything you could ever ask for. All is well until we try & sleep. The A/C fan was very noisey, the matress was so hard , I was beside myself to go to sleep, then it started ! We must have had the " River dancers" in the room above us , I guess the floors have no insulation at all ? Then the alarm clock went off ! Should have checked it before I went to bed. So, it is a good place but it maybe not the most restful.

title: “Stay Away From the Hotel 17”
text: I love funky, quirky, cheap, historic hotels and I am not terribly hard to please but the Hotel 17 was a huge disappointment in every aspect except one--the shared baths were nicely remodeled, super clean and always available. I booked a room for two nights over New Years. The queen bed I booked on Orbitz turned out to be just a double (although I had confirmed this by phone knowing I was sharing the bed with my brother), the room itself was teenie weenie (think cabin on a cruise ship), the furniture and in-room sink were cheap and run down, there were no bed side lights and even the overhead lighting was not good enough to read by. And the front desk staff... look, I can wait a few minutes while you round up your personal call but don't make me wait 10 minutes, not once, not twice, but three times. I chose the Hotel 17 for its location AND price. I could have gotten the same price in several other much better hotels a little further uptown and next time I will.

title: “Great Downtown Location & Convention Center”
text: Traveled with kids, the hotel was conveniently located to downtown. Parking attendants were great help and pool was fun for the kids (nothing real special but worked well for us). Front desk upgraded our room which was nice. The breakfast was purchased as a add-on to the room rate and was good (buffet and ordered off menu). This is a good, clean, affordable downtown Hotel. and yes you have to pay for parking very typical (you can park in a private overnight somewhere else, but why?)

title: “Comfortable and convenient”
text:
Have stayed here several times on annual visit to Boston- hotel is convenient to T at Hynes and the Prudential Centre which is full of shops and restaurants.Easy walk to Newbury St. Breakfast for Honors Gold/Diamond is in a separate room and was adequate.Wi Fi is free in the lobby (expensive in the rooms). Beds are very comfortable.
I keep returning for locational reasons rather than anything really special about the hotel itself.Try to get a high floor room with a lovely view of the Charles River.

title: “Great location.”
text: We ended up at Hotel Contessa after our original Spring Break plans fell through. They were very accomodating and made sure our stay was pleasant. The location is great; right on the RIverwalk, but not in the midst of the noisy restaurant/tourist area. We were given a suite with a King bed when we had reserved a suite with 2 beds. I pressed a bit on this issue and they found a way to accomodate us even though initially they said there were no doubles. Their bellmen and concierge are very helpful & have good suggestions for dining and transportation. Housekeeping was slow to respond to requests, but it WAS spring break so they were extra busy. There was a problem with repeated false alarm fire alarms which was a bit annoying. We didn't have a chance to enjoy the pool, however, it looked very nice. They have a nice happy hour with half price drinks and tapas.

title: “Gloomy hotel--needs a facelift inside rooms”
text:
Sheraton Downtown Los Angeles was a disapointment. It is gloomy inside the rooms and they had curtains on the windows limiting the views and making it darker than needed.
There is no pool and the exercise facility is next door at Bally's in the Mall. This is a 1980's type hotel next to a Macy's--when building a hotel next to a shopping mall was seen as a cool thing--as if you are going to need to stay overnight to go to Macy's.
The stay was mediocre and more is expected from the Sheraton brand especially in a Downtown LA location. 
The hotel had escalators to get to the elevators--basically you have to drag your luggage around so go light on anything you bring. We waited 15 minutes for help with our luggage and gave up. The people that did help us in our 3 day visit were very nice, but overall, they seem understaffed and a bit disorganized.
The mall is like a ghost town with the shops closed early b/c they cater to the office 9-5 crowd.
Overall it was just an average stay. Parking was in the $25 dollar range.
There aren't alot of choices downtown LA--the quality of hotels are very dated and poorly maintained. So with this standard the Sheraton is above average. Comparing the hotel to what the Sheraton should provide it is about a 4-out of 10.

title: “Sheraton Gunther nice but really really small rooms”
text:
Just came home from a stay at the Sheraton Gunther in San Antonio, TX. Here are the pros and cons.
Pros
* Very Clean Hotel & Rooms
* Staff very nice and helpful
* Across street from Riverwalk and Majestic Theatre
* Great restaurants within walking distance
Cons
* Room was extremely small
* Bathroom was smaller still and toliet not in good placement with rest of bathroom
* Tub had not a drip but a consistent run
* Housekeeping did not replace towels even when insturctions to do so were followed
* Pool is misleading there is no pool bar, room service will bring a drink to you at the pool but pool is nothing special
Everything aside, we had a nice stay at the Sheraton but this is no 4 star hotel. We booked this room through Hotwire and for what we payed we were content but I would not stay here again. The room is really really small!!

title: “upper west side gem :)”
text: This hostel/hotel is all about value for money. The staff were fairly helpfull and very friendly; special mention to the guy who checked us in! We booked a 2 bed private dorm - fairly large room but way too basic for my liking. It kinda made me a bit uncomfortable having basically just a bunk bed and a sink, but hey that's all we needed. There were 2 bathrooms on our floor, the older one having the best hot water and the newer one being a pain in the bum to work out. Either way they were both very clean. It's location is the best thing about it I feel, being right on broadway it was close to central park, subway stations and some great places to eat. As two 17 year olds, we felt very safe walking around here at night. The internet and tv in the lounge room was also very handy and a good way to meet other people. Only downside to this hostel/hotel, is that someone drank my pepsi from the fridge; not cool! Overall, would stay here again :)

title: “Meeting space”
text: This is a great place to hold a business meeting. The location is very convenient. The hotel lobby and meeting space is very nice and clean. The meeting space is also equiped with A/V needs including free WiFi. The catering is very good and the staff is attentive.

title: “I turned around and ran back to Canada”
text:
It's taken me this long to write a review because I tried to forget.
The room I'd reserved had been given away. I'd stopped for groceries, having reserved a room with a kitchenette. The manager, whose name I knew from my phone call, claimed in person I'd not reserved this type of room. I'd spoken to him two days prior, and had the reservation printout. He denied everything, including what was in black and white.
He said that instead, I should use the microwave in "the breakfast room" during limited hours. They'd described it as a nice, relaxed dining room. It was a tiny, fluorescent lit square. Like eating in a public restroom. 
A nice clerk quietly told me my room had indeed, been given away. The room they tried to give me stunk of vomit and harsh disinfectant. There was no bathtub. The new, flesh-coloured paint was applied sloppily over decades of old paint. Though I arrived an hour past check in, they were doing repairs in the room. The repairman yelled at me for coming in. 
They had claimed on both their website and on the phone, that they had renovated and were offering a "limited time" low price. I have luck with sales, so I went for it. The renovations were minimal. The basic dinginess was still there, just covered with new but extremely cheap furnishings. E.g. the lobby smelled of sweat and fried food, but they'd put out searingly bright plastic flowers and a rug.
As I was at the desk trying to get my credit card reimbursed, the repairman stomped past with his ladder and glared at me. I still don't know why. The one desk clerk was a very nice young man.
I arrived excited to be attending a festival for the weekend. I tried a couple of other hotels, but they were full. I missed the festival, because I drove back to Canada as fast as I could. Missing my events was better than sleeping at the Travelodge.

title: “July 4 2008”
text: My Boyfriend and I stayed at the Westin Times Sqaure for 5 nights for my birthday which was the 4th of July. I honestly do not know how anyone can say anything bad about this hotel. Check in was super fast and we even received an upgrade to a corner room eventhough the hotel was 100% full. The room and view was incredible. The room was always clean and housekeeping did a great job. The heavenly bed is really heavenly!!! I have never slept in a better bed than this one, after a long day of walking New York City it was nice coming back to such comfort. The staff is very polite and always willing to help. They even sent up a bottle of wine for my birthday... I do not understand how anyone can say anything negative about this hotel... It was a great experience.. Would stay there again...

title: “Intimate with excellent service”
text:
I chose to stay here based on TripAdvisor reviews. I stayed for a week... coming early to a conference so that I could enjoy San Diego for a bit.
This is a smaller Hilton and I think that is one of its best assets. The staff knew me and greeted me when I came through the lobby. I never had to wait for an elevator or have it stop on every single floor of a 30 floor hotel (like some of my friends who stayed in the larger hotels did). My room was on the 11th floor (with a view of the convention center and the marina) and was always well taken care of. One day I left a note for housekeeping asking for an extra bottle of conditioner since I have long hair. The staff remembered that request and left extra in the bathroom for the rest of my stay. One day I happened to be in the room around lunchtime when they came to clean the room. After I left I just notified the front desk that I had been in the room when they wanted to clean it but that I would be out for a few hours and they could come now. It was no problem. 
The pool is small, but the concierge gave me instructions for using a lap pool nearby. There was a basket of fresh green apples at the reception desk everyday. Usual amenities in the room (ironing board, hair dryer, etc). 
One appreciated perk is the free internet access. Several other hotels had daily additional charges for this service. Also, there is a free kiosk in the lobby so that you can print out your boarding pass and check-in online for your flights. 
This hotel ended up being closer to the side of the Convention Center where our conference was (South side) than the anchor hotel (Marriott). Great opportunities for eating abound within walking distance. 
The staff is excellent. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “I fly through DTW just due to conveiince of this hotel”
text: I frequently get stranded due to connections. SO I have a safe conveninet wonderful place to stay. Also when I travel to Europe, this is the best place to recharge as you adjust to time differences. Great people, great place.

title: “Nice, Convenient Airport Hotel”
text: We've stayed at the Doubletree Seatac four or five times in the past few years, and we've always enjoyed our visits. The hotel has a convenient airport shuttle that picks up guests on level 3 of the airport parking garage at stops #1 and 3. The shuttle runs 24 hours per day, and it makes about three trips per hour (no phone call or reservation is needed). If you don't want to wait, a good alternative is the nearby taxi stand; fare to the Doubletree should be less than $10 because of the hotel's proximity to the airport. On a recent trip, we landed at Seatac after midnight and were picked up within five minutes. The check-in process was courteous and smooth, and we were given a nice corner room with a balcony on the 9th floor (accompanied by the delicious chocolate chip cookies). Ever since I was a child, I've enjoyed watching airplanes takeoff and land, and this hotel provides an eagle's eye view of the airport (unless you're on the east side of the tower, in which case you're stuck looking at the snowcapped Cascades and/or Mt Rainier). Despite its proximity to the airport, the room was surprisingly quiet. At 1am the lobby bar was still very active with a jovial but well-behaved crowd, although the bartenders were understandably ready to head home to their families. I was able to purchase a reasonably priced bottle of Oregon pinot noir for in-room consumption. The room was spacious, clean and well appointed. My wife really liked the Crabtree & Evelyn "Citron" toiletries; I liked the very comfortable bed and blackout curtains.

title: “Great position, perfectly functional, rather expensive”
text:
Clean and very nice size room for Central NY.
Check in speedy and polite, Concierge very pleasant and helpful.
Position could not really have been bettered.
Not much else to add.
Recommended for a short stay, but anything longer than two or threee nights and you might want to cxonsider a hotel with more facilities.

title: “Great location and service”
text:
I have stayed here on my past 3 visits to San Diego. Here's why:
i. Really close to the airport (about 10 minutes drive). They also provide shuttle service for a small fee.
ii. Close to Little Italy and downtown SD, which means you don't necessarily need a car to get around if you are here on business.
iii. Clean, comfortable rooms with good views.
iv. rooftop deck is great for having cocktails and looking over the harbor.
v. restaurant is good, food is decent but they could work on improving their wine list. It is California after all :)
I would definitely use again.

title: “Would definitely recommend!”
text:
Being from New Zealand, and on a tight budget, we were purely guided by the other great reviews of Jerry's Motel on Tripadvisor, and we were not disappointed. 
The motel was a quick drive to loads of LA attractions, and the owners could not have been more friendly and helpful, even printing us out maps so we didnt have to rely on our sometimes unreliable GPS. A welcome snack bag was provided on check in, which was much appreciated after hours of driving in the heat!! Rooms were very clean and comfy, and just what we needed. Thanks again Jerry's we hope to be back soon :)

title: “Embassy Suites Hotel and Dinning”
text: Lassanda, was a great cook at breakfast time. She was always kind and made sure breakfast was fast and excellent. Debora was the front desk clerk, and she made sure all our needs were taken care of. The first night I came in my sheets were dirty and when they found out the went out of their way to accomidate me.

title: “The Lodge is a Wonderful Place for Business Meetings”
text: Stayed at the Lodge for several nights for a corporate training program. It was a wonderful experience in every way. The staff was polite and attentive, the food was great, and the facilities top-notch. Rooms were clean, large and very comfortable, and the bathrooms were oversized with both shower and jacuzzi tub. The Lodge has many great locations for group gathering and socializing at the end of the day, including a wonderful lounge with fireplace, pool tables, and small meeting rooms. I look forward to returning some day.

title: “PURE LUXURY”
text:
We had a fantastic stay at the Sofitel New York, and strongly encourage anyone looking for a hotel in NY to choose this one. The rooms are very spacious and spotlessly clean, with extremely comfortable beds, large windows with nice views (we looked out at the Rockefeller Center, our parents looked out at the Chrysler building). There is a great gym, an excellent restaurant and free internet in the lobby. The location is great, between 5th and 6th Ave, a short walk to just about everything in midtown.
What really sets this hotel apart from others and gives it the #1 spot that it so rightly deserves are the people who work there. Every single person was extremely friendly, well mannered and helpful. From the second our taxi pulled up outside, we were greeted with big smiles and service beyond what we would ever have expected.
We had two standard rooms reserved and upon checkin, one was kindly upgraded to a suite. Furthermore, the hotel manager came out to personally introduce himself to us and to ensure that everything was ok. My parents were there to celebrate a very special anniversary and the hotel could not have done more to make this a trip to remember. From the champagne, to the specially made cake and the beautiful suite, we were all in awe of just how much this hotel and its team members really care about their guests. In the 4 days that we were there, it was actually impossible to get past the front desk without being warmly acknowledged by whoever was on duty. Housekeeping was outstanding - they kept the rooms looking like we were the first people ever to stay in them, I have never seen a bathroom sparkle so brightly before, and the turndown service was a nice treat to come back to after dinner.
We all agreed we would never stay anywhere in New York again other than the Sofitel. All the people we met during our stay, from the manager to the concierge, front desk, housekeeping and restaurant staff, we now think of as our friends. Whoever reads this review, I hope you get to experience the satisfaction of staying with them also. We can't wait to get back there again one day soon.

title: “Great hotel”
text:
Stayed at Club Quarters Valentines Day weekend ( Saturday Night). Room was very clean and nice. Bed was comfortable. Bathroom was also very nice and clean. Check in/out was very quick; less than 3 minutes. Very close to downtown Phila and close to many restaurants. Davio's is in the hotel. You can get a discount if you charge the bill to your room. 
Very good price for the hotel from Expedia. If you are looking for a clean nice hotel at a great price at a great location, this is it!

title: “actually better than before”
text: Been staying here once a year for 5-6 years and it's the same value and safe haven for travelers. There has been some painting, some sprucing up and some mild updating. What remains is a convenient place within 4-5 blocks from a multitude of subways, great restaurants, Union Square with a great farmer's market Fri & Sat. For someone traveling alone especially this place is so safe. You need three different keys to get to your room. The people there this last time were universally pleasant and helpful. The morning coffee was good and it makes a difference to be able to go downstairs instead of having to go outside for that first cup. The price is right especially comparing other NYC properties. Yes the bathroom and shower are down the hall but the robe they have for you is warm and the slippers work. Never had to wait for the facilities. They will also let you store your bags if you aren't leaving NYC at the check out time and since there are so many subway stops around you can spend the day being a tourist and then come back later to pick up your bags. A great place!

title: “Good for business travellers”
text:
Stayed at the Sofitel for a short 3 day business trip in Chicago. 
Loved the welcoming staff and first impression in the hallway. Breakfast was very enjoyable too. I got a standard room at the 19th floor which gave good views over the city. Room is positively basic, in line with expectations of a 5 star hotel. Gym is small but modern and very clean. 
Would probably stay again.

title: “Just OK”
text: The location of the Best Western is very convenient in Old Town but the rooms are just OK - pretty clean and basic. The worst part of the trip was when a colleague had items stolen from her room and the management was less than helpful or cooperative. So be very careful with your valuables and use the safe even if leaving for a short time.

title: “Disappointing Marriott, Extremely Outdated Rooms”
text:
I stayed here for one night along with 3 colleagues and booked all 4 rooms under my Marriott credit card as a Platinum Elite member.
Upon pulling up to the valet in front of the hotel we were immediately approached by the stoic-faced valet. It was 10PM and I kindly asked him to wait a minute while we decide what we are doing with our vehicles. I had learned from other tripadvisor members that there is parking directly across the street in the World Trade Center. So one of us ran across and spoke with a parking garage employee and he confirmed that you can park overnight for $10. The garage is well light and secure. So we headed across the street and spent $10 each instead of $30 at the Marriott. Ha!
When we approached the check in counter we were greeted by the robotic front desk manager. He was very matter of fact and had little personality. He informed me that he didn't have any king beds as requested because the hotel was near capacity, which seemed odd since we were one of the only few people in the hotel lobby area, which is very large, impressive, but smelled liked old fashioned air freshener. It was terrible.
As a platinum member I am guaranteed my room type. He stated that he had king beds on a lower floor. I said that would be fine. We then found out that he issued me a king bed on the 5th floor and my other 3 colleagues 2 doubles on the 5th floor. They were too tired to complain. 
My room was spacious but I felt like I walked into a room that was decorated circa 1992. I was dumbfounded. I only stay in Marriott properties and I have not seen anything like this in years. The carpet was hunter green with pink designs and worn. I kept my flip flops on. The lamps that flanked the bed were pink with cheap dirty off-white shades. The tv was old-fashioned tube tv and small. It looked silly on the armoire. The drapes were just as old and unattractive. It felt plain awful and so did the mushy bed. I did not feel or look like a typical Marriott Jameson bed. 
I must say the bathroom was upgraded with marble-looking counters and floors and lots of lighting and mirrors. 
The decor in the hallways matched the rooms.
The concierge lounge was fine for breakfast.
This hotel should not be booking any more rooms until they upgrade them. Shame on you Marriott.

title: “Liked the hotel, but had Priceline issues there I have never had before.”
text:
I liked this hotel but did have a Priceline problem I had never had before. As all Priceline users know, the room is only guaranteed for 2 adults. Apparently there are places where two adults can sleep in a double or full size bed! I have just never stayed in such a place before. But my friend and I are both small, so when we heard about the $50 upgrade price, we said no, we would just sleep in the same bed since it was just for one night. We got to our room and it had two full size beds, so we thought maybe the desk clerk had jus been confused about what type of room we had. We were shocked to get up the next morning and find a $50 charge stuck under the door for a "upgraded room". Had to catch a flight very early so we didn't stick around to argue, but I have stayed in MANY Priceline bid hotels and never been offered just a double bed. It has always been either King or two double or even two queens. So Priceline bidders beware. 
I thought it was a nice hotel, small rooms and bathrooms as to be expected in a old hotel. The staff were friendly, but we obviously had communication difficuties. would still be willing to stay there again, even with the issues, but I would book directly with the hotel. Very close to the Transit line and on Freedom Trail.
 Parking is a nightmare in Boston and especially in this area. Paid $40 for self parking across the street.

title: “Beautiful Stay in San Diego”
text: My boyfriend and I spent a night at this hotel. We absolutely loved it. Everything was great, the early check-in, the nice, clean spacious room, the $9 upgrade, the free breakfast, the free evening reception, the business center, and the short travel to the Gaslamp District. We will definitely be coming back. The service was great, from the front desk persons to the valet. Our only complaint would be the concierge. She was very unhelpful and a lil rude. We didn't get much information from her. We just googled points of interest and were fine.

title: “Good ...but expensive for what it was when we stayed”
text:
We picked this hotel based upon the high Trip Advisor rating and the fact that it was family-friendly. I always find it difficult to give a hotel a rating because the criterion are relative depending upon where you are, with wide variations in quality and amenities across both countries and continents. Make no mistake however, this is a good hotel. Equally, this is no five star hotel. 
The location, being within a few blocks of Bloomingdales, Saks, Tiffany and the Chrysler building is excellent. The hotel is a fantastic choice for families. The beds are comfortable and the rooms spotlessly clean, bathrooms are functional if not luxurious The views are good (although no sign of the Chrysler Buidling from room 2508 where we were). As described previously, the staff are efficient although by no means exceptionally so.
So what is the problem? Well none really aside from the fact that I was paying $600 (£300) + tax per night for what is a mid-range chain hotel. Perhaps the comparison is unfair, particularly given the fact that we probably visited NYC on the busiest weekend of the year, but I couldn't help expecting more for the money. I have read gushing reviews but where people paid half of this rate or less for rooms here. That would be fair value but we could find nothing on Priceline, Hotwire etc that came close. Perhaps we have been spolied by what you get in Singapore or the Far East for £300 (true 5 star luxury).
We too got the hotel car back to JFK at $55 inclusive of toll but excluding tip and this was a good choice after the world's smelliest cab on arrival! Also, for breakfast, the hotel kindly recommended Maddison's which is two blocks away on 1st Avenue. We ended up having breakfast there three times and it was a fantastic experience with great American breakfasts (bacon, two eggs and hash browns for $7 with unlimited coffee) and a real '50's ambiance.
All in all, I would return to the Courtyard. It's a good hotel and our family enjoyed it but I would not pay $600 plus tax per night for it. If you can get it for a more reasonable rate, do not hesitate to stay there - particularly if you are a family with children.

title: “Esther B.”
text: If you want to stay downtown close to shopping and great eating establishments near, plus a hotel to provide you excellent service, the Red Lion is the place to stay. I look forward to a business or personal trip to the Emerald City (Seattle) for a great stay at the Red Lion on Fifth Ave. There is dinning/lounge right below and very convenient if you want to stay in....The staff provide excellent service and the hotel is beautiful, very professional staff, clean rooms and parking is very convenient for you. I have never experienced any problems with reservation or assistance needed.

title: “Outstanding service”
text: We stayed at this hotel as a weekend away. We've stayed in Times Square many times at many different hotels and this hotel is the one we will stay at from now on. The location and service were excellent. The staff at the hotel were the best, especially Patrick, although everyone was great. They went out of their way to see if we needed anything or they could help us in any way. While the rooms were small they were clean and had everything you need, even an umbrella in case it rains. We can't wait to go back.

title: “Lovely property, fantastic service”
text: Easy cab ride to Soho district from LaGuardia and an excellent two night stay at the Trump Soho at a very reasonable rate for a 5-star hotel in New York City. Most impressed with the service. Excellent front desk, bellhop, and concierge service ensured a hassle-free stay. Just a 15 or so minute taxi ride to uptown. We were on the 24th floor with a nice view of Empire State Building (but also the side wall of an adjacent building). Room layout was great (Deluxe King) and beds are amazingly comfy. Huge open bathroom with separate rain shower, toilet stall, soaker tub with huge window overlooking the city. Only little glitch was the porter who showed us our room features forgot to tell us that there is a sliding wall to close the bathroom off from the main area. As there appears to be no door, I was glad I asked about it otherwise the seeming lack of privacy would have kept us (hubby and me) from booking there again. In-hotel restaurant Hotel Quattro was very good and convenient. Just a note: If you purchase the bed & breakfast package it states that a continental breakfast at Il Quattro is included. In fact, they have stopped this buffet set up and you can order any breakfast (hot included) from the menu...an even better value and choice. Hotel is just a few blocks walking from all sorts of boutiques and retail shopping. One block away seafood restaurant AquaGrill was fantastic and a jazzy, fun spot to dine. So there you have it. We would definitely stay again.

title: “Convenient location, renovated rooms, and free wireless!”
text: We were looking for a hotel that would be close to some of the major attractions, including Sea World and Fiesta Texas, and would still allow us to easily drive into the city. The location of this Econo Lodge fit the bill, with the unexpected convenience of having a mall right across the street. The rooms themselves were recently upgraded with new carpets and furniture. A great feature was the free wireless, which you often have to pay for in higher end motels. In this case it was free, and it definitely came in handy when we wanted to look up local restaurants for dinner. Overall, I would recommend this hotel. Can't beat the combination of location, quality, and price!

title: “Best business hotel to stay in while in Denver”
text:
I have stayed at this hotel twice and have had great experiences both times. The hotel staff is friendly and accommodating...I did not arrive at the hotel until 2:00 AM due to flight delays, and was so impressed with how nice and welcoming the front lobby staff was even at the late hour. My room has been thoroughly cleaned each time I have stayed here, and I really appreciate the extra Starbucks vouchers I was given as a business traveler. 
The breakfast is wonderful, and the hotel fitness center is great, especially for a hotel of this size. I would highly recommend business travelers stay here, as it's the perfect distance in-between the city and the airport. Will absolutely stay here next time I travel to Denver again.

title: “The Queen of Hotels”
text:
If the walls could speak in the Waldorf Astoria they would be able to tell a fairy tale in every room.
The Hotel was a luxurious Hotel and also nowadays it sets a very high standard. I specially appreciate that you can see the history at every corner and many of the people working there seem to be there already for a very long time.
Sure, the rooms are not immaculate but the effort of the Team is great! Specially make sure you either enjoy any of the great Buffets (Oscar for Breakfast or the Sunday Brunch)
Windows can be opened (why not) and I would recommend this place to any in NYC! I just love it!

title: “Very nice hotel w/free shuttle service”
text: Ditto to what everybody else is saying about Silver Cloud--it's a great hotel. I found the staff really accommodating and quick to help. My room was equipped with a microwave oven and a mini-fridge, which gave the room a home-like feel, which I like. I particularly appreciated the complimentary shuttle service. Nice touch.

title: “Below my Expectations”
text:
I stay at Marriott properties around the world 120+ nights a year for work, and consider myself well-versed on what to expect from their hotels.
I have stayed at just about every other Marriott property in Downtown Chicago over the past few years, and have always looked forward to the chance to stay at this hotel because it is the flagship Marriott in Chicago.
I was delighted by several aspects of my stay, but really disappointed by others.
First, the good points: The room, which I booked on the hotel website, was only $159 a night. It had recently had a "soft" renovation, meaning new carpets, furniture, wallcoverings and bedding. The hotel's lower levels were under renovation, and the areas which had been redone (all the meeting rooms, the restaurant, and the concierge lounge) were really nice. The lobby, which was still torn up, looked like it will eventually be great based on the renderings.
Now, the bad: The rooms really needed a more thorough renovation. The bathroom was very tired, and had been redone on the cheap like one of those home improvement shows where they have only $1000 to spend. The tub, tile, and ceilings were old and shabby. The room was really, really small for a Marriott. The hallways are dark and shabby, and according to an employee I know who works at the hotel, are not due to be renovated. They need it badly. The concierge lounge, even with the hotel at full capacity due to a large trade show, is closed on weekends, and due to the renovations, there are few other options on-site for gathering places with colleagues. The elevators were really slow.
I think the basic problem here, like a lot of large city hotels, is that the building is about 30 years old, has gotten a lot of traffic over the years, and needs a major renovation moreso than cosmetic improvements..
Overall, I think Marriott really has failed with this property. Considering that Chicago is one of the nation's great hotel cities, they have come up short here in an area where there are many terrific competitors. I'm back to the newer and fresher Courtyard or more luxurious Renaissance for my next visit.

title: “Not worth the money”
text: Stayed over due to a strom and a missed fligh, we stayed at the marriot at Indianapolis and the difference is overwhelming, this hotel is not worth the money I was charged, the room was ok but it needs renovations and better cleaning service

title: “Luxury and service await”
text: My husband and I have stayed here twice for romantic weekend getaways and it was even better the 2nd time. The rooms are luxurious - DVD player, TV in the bathroom, some rooms have bathtubs with a view - and the service is unbelievable. We had afternoon tea in NoMI and ordered room service when they were booked for dinner - great food and they were very accomodating to our special requests. On our 2nd visit, we were promised the 17th floor (2nd highest, highest available the night before) and they put us on 9. We reminded them we were promised 17 and after profuse apology and a short wait in the library, we were moved to 14 and given a certificate for free afternoon tea or drinks as consolation. The room was an upgraded corner room with lake view and even better than we expected anyway so we weren't disappointed. Hyatt does something special when training their staff - they're the friendliest I've ever met. And you always get a complimentary check-in beverage, escort to the elevator, and your bags are whisked away and magically appear in your room.

title: “Great location, beware of alley-side rooms”
text: This is a great place to stay if you are on a budget, and seems typical of other older hotels I have stayed in - nothing flashy. The location is great for the north end of Michigan Ave., and it is about a 5 minute walk to the subway. The down side: my room was adjacent to the alley: between restaurant deliveries and daily garbage trucks I certainly didn't need an alarm, even 7 floors up. A similar phenomenon for the interior noise - anyone getting off the elevator down the hall sounded like they were two feet away with sound channeled through an ill-fitting door. Little noise coming through the walls, but the doors and windows may as well have been open. The staff were quite helpful and eager to please - I noticed that they went out of their way for a couple of different parties checking in while I was there - very friendly. A better room location would have made this 5 of 5 for me.

title: “Nice hotel but bring own pack and play”
text: I had a business conference here and extended the stay to visit nearby family. Like many hotels, wireless was extra. We had our baby with us and asked for a crib and fridge. Despite being requested at the time of reservation, we had to call down once we arrived. Both were brought to the room...the fridge worked fine. The crib was an old wobbly pack and play. On the positive side, they provided baby shampoo and lotion.

title: “Fantastic Hotel - Beds superb!!!”
text: My family and I used the hotel just as a one night stay over after a very long journey from London to Los Angeles. We arrived around 10.30pm in the evening (Fri 5 August) and were exhausted! However, we were greeted at the Hilton by wonderful staff. They were extremely courteous and very helpful. When we went up to our rooms (we had 2) we all had a lovely double bed each and they were the best beds we have ever slept in. The pillows were also luxurious. We were a bit worried about aircraft noise but to be totally honest I think the first one I heard was around 7am when we awoke. So all in all, a fabulous hotel. Would definitely recommend.

title: “Great location and comfortable bed”
text: Yankees and mariners game was great and the front desk was busy, yet they still changed one of our rooms to a double queen from a king which was great service. Beds are great and the location is wonderful.

title: “overrated & bad”
text:
To cut a long story short our stay at this sheraton was terrible & horrible.
Worn rooms with little bathrooms. Outside incredible noisiness. Rude behaviour of the reception staff. No possibility to change the room. Avoid this location.

title: “Crown Plaza Time Square New York”
text: Very nice hotel, clean, and friendly staff. Location was perfect, right in the mix of Time Square. Our hotel room was very nice and private with a great view of time square. In hotel parking. I would definatly stay here again.

title: “A Small Gem in a Perfect Location”
text:
The first impression this hotel makes is interesting with valet and bell staff greeting guest at the curb (at least in the heat of the summer). This may seem an odd criticism, but the very helpful bell staff (and the one who greeted us was very courteous, cheery, and helpful) wore dark pants and well worn white polo shirts. Frankly, some of the formal attire of the big chains is silly--not to mention hot in the summer heat--but for a property like this, something a little classier or distinctive would make sense. Make no mistake, this is not a large property and its smallness adds to its charm. Another criticism, though it is a small property, I think it is under-served by elevators. Wait times can be, though not always, off-putting.
Some reviews on tripadvisor suggest a tired property. That isn't my experience. While some updating never hurts, I wouldn't give this hotel a knock on that point. Rooms are large, well decorated, functional, quiet, and have good beds. The rooftop bar is cozy but what a view (even surrounded by real skyscrapers).
For people interested in the beach, Navy Pier, or the North end of Michigan Ave, this hotel is really in a perfect location. We didn't eat at the hotel, but the restaurant adjacent to the lobby looks pleasant and has a great patio in the front of the hotel.
Finally, staff always makes a difference and our interactions with bell staff, front desk staff, maintenance, and housekeeping were all excellent. Finally, I think a concierge would be nice touch at this very good property and could make it a standout in its competitive price point.

title: “Disappointing”
text:
The people who work at Loew's are terrific - -friendly and accomodating. No problems there.
The room was ok - but the TV was at right angles to the bed -- with no way to change the position of the bed OR the TV. Smallish room, so the entertainment center needed to be where it was.... but the TV should have been on one of those lazy-Susan-like extenders.
Saturday mid day a VERY loud band encamped in front of the hotel. We had wanted to nap... but on the 14th floor, the music was so loud that napping was impossible - even with earplugs. When we complained, the hotel could only tell us "they have a permit on weekends." So... if you want to spend any afternoon time in your room on summer weekends, avoid Loew's. (And the Marriott on Market Street - right across the street and would have the same problem.) We left a day early rather than spending another afternoon with the banging drums.
And my usual complaint - it makes me crazy that city hotels still charge for internet connections! Seems to be common in large hotels.
Sole Food - the restaurant in the hotel - excellent food but pricey, bleak atmosphere. Convenient, though.

title: “Very clean & comfortable with friendly staff. My choice for downtown Houston.”
text: The Magnolia Hotel is very clean and comfortable with a very friendly staff. It is my choice for downtown Houston. Roomservice is great with fabulous food. Good value.

title: “What's not to LOVE?”
text: What a great find! Great location, reasonable rates (for Manhattan), great service, clean well appointed rooms, nice bar / restaraunt. Just got back from a 5 day business trip with my wife coming along to shop / sightsee while I was working. We both had a great time, even though the property has only been open a couple of months service was top notch, everything was NEW, beds super comfy. Property is located close to subway / Madison Square Garden / etc in the heart of Manhattan, I'd go back in a heartbeat.

title: “Not impressed”
text:
I have been traveling to NY for work every few weeks and this was a recommendation from some colleagues. To say the least I was very disappointed, especially based on rate. Upon arrival there was a long line with only two people behind the desk so waited over 20 minute to check in. When I finally did get up to the desk they were actually very rude.
I had reserved a king room, but was given a room with two queens. The beds were comfortable, but the sheets were very scratchy. After my day at the office I came back and both my cards did not work, when I went back downstairs to get them reactivated they told me to 'keep them away from credit cards'. Both cards were in different places in my purse, neither by credit cards. 
And to top it all off in the middle of the night my balcony door blew open! There was a storm with winds blowing but still, just tells me the latch is not good. Glad I was on the 12th floor or it really would have freaked me out.
With all the choices in NY, I won't stay here again.

title: “Great location”
text:
I stayed at the Westin River North over President's weekend. The hotel is in an excellent location - about 2 blocks off Michigan Ave. I got a great deal on Westin's website - $159 a night with parking included. Parking was $41 every 24 hours and this is something you cannot avoid if you drive to Chicago. Several of the hotels I looked at had the same type of deal. 
When I checked in, the gentleman at the front desk said that I had only booked the parking package for one night (which I didn't!) I showed him my confirmation and he assured me he would fix it in the computer. Unfortunately, when we checked out, our bill was $200 more than it should have been! No worries though, they immediately fixed it...just make sure you check your bill. 
The hotel itself is lovely and we had a really nice view. I would stay here again if and when we return to Chicago. The bed was comfy and the room was clean. We had our small dog with us and they were very accomodating. We usually prefer Starwood properties because many are pet friendly. 
All in all a great weekend!

title: “Remarkably Poor Service/Technologically Challenged Stay”
text:
I stayed at the Parc 55 for a conference and stayed an extra weekend to enjoy San Francisco. The conference brought 10,000 people to town so it wasn't my first choice but was obligated to be nearby the convention center for the first four days of my visit. The lobby always reeked of cigarettes either from the street or from the bar, even early in the morning. The room was smaller than I expected but tidy and comfortable. I couldn't get the in-room safe to open upon arrival and asked for someone to check it. "Engineering" came to the room and flipped the power switch which was inside the fold of the door and looked at me like I was a complete moron.
I tried to sign up for the high speed internet ($49/week) on my Ipad and got on just long enough to pay the fee and then it crashed and never worked again, despite 4 calls to the "customer support" number. I wasted at least an hour collectively -plugging in the tablet computer, checking the IP address, adding the Wi-Fi, checking the network connection with multiple different support staff to no avail. They did remove the fee and told me if I could get back on they would cover the cost of it, but I was never able to get back on. I had to do all my work for the conference in the smoky hotel lobby.
The third night the television volume went out. I didn't watch TV but called the front desk the following morning when it still didn't work and asked someone to look at it while I was out for the day. I returned late in the evening and it wasn't fixed. No note, no message, and now the phone wasn't working so I had to go to the front desk the next morning to complain about this. They acted like they had never heard of this problem and offered not even an apology. This was finally fixed that day while I was out.
Finally, on the last night, my bill arrived with a charge for two bottles of water that I didn't drink. I had to have the charge removed rather than just checking out and RUNNING for my life out of this hotel. Again, not even an apology but lots of questioning as if after paying over $2000 for my room that I was going to try to scam them out of $9.74 for their two bottles of water.
It's unfortunate I had to stay in a place without any hospitality in such a lovely city. It really was unpleasant and I wouldn't stay here again.

title: “Fantastic Hotel”
text: 3 nights at this great hotel. Room was clean, stylish and comfotable. Location is great near convention center, SJSU, historic SJ and HP Pavillion. Nice touches like robes, IPOD player, cd player, cushy chair.... We overlooked the patio that was busy on Friday and Saturday nights. Food in the Palomar restaurant was great, we sat at the bar. If you likes Westins but on a smaller scale this is the place.

title: “Nice upgrade, but....”
text: My colleague and I checked in for one night for a business trip. We checked in around 4pm and all of the double queen rooms were taken. The front desk was nice enough to upgrade us to a King suite. But the refrigerator is no work and all night the room smelled like smoke. It was obviously the room next door was smoking because the smell got stronger in the evening.

title: “Free Parking and Breakfast”
text: A commercial or industrial building converted into a hotel. A bit of an odd setup/layout but clean, accomodating staff and quiet. About a mile plus walk to the restaurants or Downtown, I was lead to believe it was much closer.

title: “Friendly New Yorkers- Great Service!!!”
text: We stayed at the Crowne Plaze Times Square, NYC during April School vacation week with our children. The room was fine, clean and nicely done. I've stayed in more plush hotels but this room was fine. The hotel had a nice city feel and the location could not be beat! My experience with the hotel staff was excellent.....I truly did not expect NY to be so customer friendly. We asked to be moved to a room overlooking Times Square (we had really got a great deal on the web and did not expect to get any good view)- though they could not give it to us the first night they called first thing in the morning and said our room overlooking Times Square. They moved our things and that was that!!! We had a great week, great hotel stay and great service!!!! Would love to go back to NYC!!!

title: “Disappointing considering it is a Sheraton....”
text: This past weekend we visited Baltimore with our two very young children for a seminar my husband had to attend for his job (which was in a nearby town). We arrived around 7:30 pm and ended up ordering room service since there were not any restaurants within a two-block radius of the hotel. I thought it was a little pricey ($27 for a little pizza and a kids grilled cheese) but my husband said that is what happens when you order room service. The room was rather warm and when the air conditioning was running it was a little loud. The room would be considered by most very plain and cheaply decorated. I asked my husband when Sheraton Hotels became such dumps. The bathroom was very large but certainly not nice. Saturday morning we were gone from 8:30 am until 1 pm and by 1:15 we were out of it again until 5 pm. All of those hours and no one was able to clean the room. There were not enough towels for four people and we did not even bathe the kids. When we got back at five my husband wanted to get a shower since it was so warm out but he could not because all of the towels were dirty and sitting on the dirty floor. When he called down to reception they transferred him to housekeeping and they did not even offer to come clean the room. They eventually brought some towels over. We were highly disappointed in this hotel and my husband says he will never use Priceline again. We had entered in "inner Harbor/downtown" and boy, was this out of the inner harbor loop. The room was disgraceful, no one was helpful other than the room service employees, and the location was ridiculously far from the inner harbor. Overall, it was an extremely disappointing experience. We will never return!

title: “A night in Times Square”
text: The biggest advantage of this hotel is its location. By being at the center of the action in Times Square, it makes one overlook all the shortcomings of a hotel of the brand quality of Hilton. The lounge is small and the reception area can get very crowded during peak season times. There were a few confused tourists who did not know which way to go to take the elevators since the street level entrance does not take you to the hotel lobby but you have to take an elevator to go one flight up to reach there.

title: “Nice Staff, Busy Lobby, Nightmarish Parking Garage”
text:
Lobby is great. Staff is very friendly and helpful. Rooms are nice, as are the bathrooms (despite being in California where I would expect low-flow showers, the one in my room had a delightfully strong water flow).
The underground parking garage is the stuff nightmares are made of. Tight turning radius, poor visibility around corners, very difficult to navigate aisles, hot stuffy air...my pulse rate goes up 20 points just thinking about that parking garage. I never want to be six stories below ground in a maze like that again.
While the hotel is decent overall, they do nickel and dime you. $20 to self park. $13 for internet. Take whatever price you get and add $33/night if you have a car and want to check e-mail.

title: “Great stay at the Sheraton”
text:
We stayed at the Boston Sheraton for 6 nights in April and truly enjoyed our visit. We reserved a Club level room, 27th floor, which was wonderful. The room was spacious and had a lovely view of the city. We had a king bed and a hide-a-bed, and we had a roll-a-way bed brought in. Once we pushed the chair and 2 foot stools aside, there was plenty of room during the day for our family. 
We enjoyed the complimentary breakfast each morning in the 29th floor Club lounge (friendly staff busily attending to the room). The Club lounge had complimentary cold drinks, fruit and granola bars in the afternoon and an espresso machine available at all hours. It was sure nice to come back to the hotel after a busy day with our kids and be able to stop in there to grab cold drinks and snacks instead of having to buy something. There were free appetizers and beverages available to Club room guests in the main floor restaurant, which we actually just ate as a light dinner several times. Pretty substantial appetizers, considering it was free. 
The concierge was able to obtain for us a pair of great tickets to the historic 100 year Fenway Park game with the Red Sox vs. the Yankees just a few hours before the start of the game. We never got to tell her thanks for the great tickets, we had a wonderful time at Fenway. 
We found the staff at the Sheraton friendly and helpful during our stay. We found the Sheraton to be family friendly and comfortable. If you're able, getting a room on the Club level is worth the extra money. The other family who we traveled with agreed that we would stay at the Boston Sheraton again the next time we're in town.
Tip: Valet parking is expensive. You can self park in the garage. There is also a surface parking lot just across the street which is cheaper and easier than navigating a garage.
Tip: Take the subway (the T). It's easy to use, inexpensive, and takes you all over. We took the T to Harvard, the town of Quincy, the JFK musuem, and around Boston. Stops are located within a block of the hotel. 
Tip: Pinkberry on Newberry Street. Enough said.

title: “Charming and tasteful”
text:
