We booked our stay at this hotel from the Hotels.com website and got a great deal. Considering how expensive the rest of the city is, knowing how little we paid (roughly US$82/night inclusive of taxes) made it that much more enjoyable.
Don't expect to see a big Best Western sign when looking for the hotel. We had to circle around a few times after getting confused with the one-way streets and not being able to see it the first time around. At the suggestion of another reviewer, we parked in the neighbouring garage and paid $29 a day, which was $30 less than if we had valet parked with the hotel. It was pretty hassel-free, just expensive.
While the hotel is on a main road and close to the sights, it's near the sketchy section of Taylor and doesn't feel totally safe sometimes. The number of homeless people and policemen actually surprised us. It wasn't really an area I'd feel comfortable wandering around in.
The hotel is charming and doesn't feel like any generic Best Western hotel. The lobby is tastefully decorated and always felt busy. The rooms are small but had everything we needed. You'd likely go stir-crazy if you had to spend a whole day in there, but it was just right for an evening of TV watching. With the queen size bed, they still managed to squeeze in a desk, sitting chair, ottoman, closet and full bathroom.
Our room was located right next to the elevator, and if we were ever to return, we'd request a room further away. The doors aren't very sound proof and the old-school elevator makes a loud dinging sound each time it arrives at the floor. We mostly took the stairs to avoid waiting for it. And like any old building, the floors aren't sound-proof either so we often heard the neighbours above us walking around.
Good points: great price, clean, well-decorated, plush towels, in-room safety deposit box, friendly and helpful front desk staff, complimentary coffee in the lobby in the morning and wine and cheese in the afternoons.
Not so good points: sketchy area, not very soundproof rooms, small rooms.

title: “Good Location for Vibiana”
text: We stayed here for a weekend to attend a family wedding at Vibiana. The hotel is in a great location and is accessible by SuperShuttle from LAX for $16 pp. The front staff was quite helpful, but oddly had little knowledge of the surrounding area. Otherwise, the hotel itself now has all of the Hilton branding and features, but has tried to keep the Kyoto Grand vintage. Good rate as well for the wedding guests.

title: “Great!”
text: GREAT HOTEL FOR THE PRICE... A little far form everything, you need a car to move. Staff is very helpful and for parking you have 3 options, self parking is complimentary. If you join the loyalty program internet service is free.

title: “Fantastic Hotel”
text:
No words, except.... fantastic, fantastic, fantastic !!!
Perfect for City sightseeing.

title: “Good location, ok room.”
text:
Stayed at this hotel at the beginning of July. We got a 40% off deal but even then it was quite pricey. The lobby is very grand with marble and fountains. The room, compared to the impression the lobby left was a bit disappointing. The bathroom is very small and the bath is barely deep enough to paddle in but the shower is nice and powerful. The beds were comfortable. We had a room with two double beds so it was nice to have a larger bed to ourselves but it may be a squish if you end up sharing a double bed.
There were no coffee/tea making facilities nor a fridge/mini-bar which was a bit disappointing but we lived. There is a lovely large television offerring a variety of services including TV internet - $9.95 for unlimited use for 24 hours. We signed up to this as we had to book the next leg of our trip. Unfortunately, the internet service kept crashing so we eventually gave up and asked for a refund.
Our room was not cleaned one day but that's not a huge problem. The staff at the reception were helpful.
The location is the main advantage of this hotel. Centrally located and right next to Grand Central Terminal so all the sites are within an easy walk or a subway ride away. 
I would consider staying at this hotel again if deals were available but definitely not if charged full price.

title: “This hotel is truly amazing!”
text: We absolutely love this hotel. The staff was truly amazing but there was something incredibly wrong with the bed in our room. Each morning, the bed held my wife and I hostage, preventing us from waking up in a timely manner. Wonderful experience.

title: “Good value for D.C.”
text:
We stayed at the Fairfield Inn, 500 H Street in Downtown D.C. from Aug. 30 to Sept. 2, 2011. Here are the highlights:
The hotel is located in Chinatown, which is northwest D.C. near the Verizon Center. Chinatown isn't big, but it's loaded with very affordable restaurants, mostly Asian (Try Full Kee, across H Street from the hotel. Very good.)
The closest Metro stop is a block away. If you prefer to walk, the National Mall is 10 to 15 minutes away through safe neighborhoods.
Chinatown itself is gentrifying rapidly. You will see some panhandlers -- one engaged us in conversation in an effort, successful I might add, to make a buck. But the neighborhood felt safe if a little raggedy at the edges.
The hotel staff was very friendly. The continental breakfast is the usual for a Fairfield -- make-your-own waffles, hot oatmeal, cold cereal, muffins, yogurt, bagels, bananas etc. The breakfast area does get crowded during the morning rush.
The rooms are done in understated Chinese motifs. We had a view of an alley, which wasn't a big deal to us, but if it matters, you might want to specify that you'd like a view of something else.
We paid $170 a night, although I know from other reviewers that there are times when better deals can be had. On top of the room rate, the parking fee is $33 a day, and includes valet service. We decided to park the car ourselves at the nearby Gallery Place garage and hoof it. The 24-hour charge there is $22, so we saved $11 a day.
The attractions closest to the hotel include the Verizon Center (where the NBA team plays and they have concerts and so forth), the National Portrait gallery (terrific art museum) and the National Building Musem (we didn't make it there.)
Considering the convenient location, the renovated rooms and the accommodating staff, I'd say the Fairfield is a good choice for someone looking to stay in central D.C. for under $200 a night.

title: “Poor air quality”
text: We have stayed at several Embassy Suites in recent years and they have ranged from good to excellent. This one was awful and for one simple reason. It is filthy. Every chair was stained, the carpet was stained and the walls covered in marks. I was afraid to sit on any of the furniture. The bathroom sink was cracked as were several of the tiles. The room had a musty smell and the air quality was poor. We arrived late at night after a long day of traveling and didn't begin to realize how shabby the room was until daylight the next morning. I would not recommend this hotel to anyone other than cockroaches and it definitely isn't worth the rather hefty price tag.

title: “Lovely hotel but forewarning would have been appreciated”
text: We cancelled our confirmation in a similar prroperty after being reassured by the (then) reservations that our top 3 requirements would be accommodated- 2 beds, amazing views and great public areas for entertaining during our all too short NYC visit. To our great disappointment both the highly acclaimed front garden and restaurant were closed for renovations and the promised view was only just accesible by practically climbing out of the window! After speaking to the attentive duty manager we were moved to a room with fabulous views, however we did have to compromise by sharing the one queen bed. Other minor issues were dealt with promptly and efficiently by the staff. This is a very pleasant and well maintained hotel but we would have appreciated notice about the (obviously scheduled) renovations and more than likely postponed our first Mondrian experience until next year's trip.

title: “Undesireable”
text: Look at my photos, they speak for themselves, it is just really run down. The managers reception is really chips and sodas.

title: “Very disappointing, pick another hotel if you nead to be close to the airport”
text: We picked this property because of the enticing rate and the Ramada name but were very disappointed. Booked and was given a king room only to find it was not cleaned after the prior guests. The front desk clerk did not seem surprised and gave us a 2 bed room instead. The second room was not much better. The blankets were stained and the bathroom was dirty. We were given replacement blankets but were told there were no more rooms available at the rate we had booked on line. We checked out the next morning and found a much better hotel to stay at within minutes away at near the same price.

title: “What a metamorphosis!”
text: This hotel was formerly Amerisuites and has had a complete and beautiful upgrade! My husband travels a lot to San Antonio for work and occasionally I will go with him. When it was Amerisuites the rooms were dark and very drab. Now since Hyatt has taken over it is a whole new place. The rooms are bright, have nice upgrades throughout and flat screen TVs. I really enjoyed my stay! They have a nice bar for coffee and wine/beer, the breakfast was great and the staff was absolutely fabulous. I felt we were treated as though we were staying at a 5 star hotel. The staff doted on us constantly and made sure we were happy at all times. I would highly recommend the Hyatt Place if you are looking for something affordable that doesn't have the same drab old feel that most economy places do. Another plus about this location is that is is across from a great shopping center, The Quarry, that has a Whole Foods, several great restaurants and a couple of nice shops like the Gap, Ann Taylor, etc. The free shuttle service is nice as well. They took me to North Star Mall in no time flat! I know that it is also a close drive to all other San Antonio attractions.

title: “Fantastic Hotel, Highly reccomended!”
text: Arrived at this hotel as a lovely surprise from my boyfriend for a few days holiday. We didn't know what to expect but the staff were so friendly and helpful. The hotel itself is very clean and the room was a great size with a huge bed. Lovely bathroom, fresh towels every day, couldn't ask for more! The location of the hotel is brilliant too, right around the corner from macy's so very central. If your'e considering this hotel then go for it its definately worth it :)

title: “Lovely small hotel, great location”
text: Service is gracious. Room was small but clean and nice. VERY comfortable bed. Location is fabulous, right in the middle of the market. Viewing deck has lots of seating and beautiful view overlooking the ocean. Highly recommend it.

title: “Business attending a National Conference”
text:
Have not stayed at this hotel before and when making my reservation became a Sheraton Preferred Guest. Attended the National Notary Association Conference June 2012 and was treated very well by front desk, offering me a room on a Preferred Guest Floor. The room was very nice and the floor was quiet, no hassle or noise from other guests! Highly recommend signing up as a Preferred Guest.
I couldn't leave the hotel between workshops and eating at the hotel was fine, though a little pricey. 
Internet was great. There's an area in the lobby to check your email, etc. Free! No need to bring your laptop, IPad or pay for WiFi in your room.
They are renovating the Spa, Workout facilities so it should be nice when finished.
The pool was average.

title: “Noisey”
text: If you stay at the location make sure you get an upper room and away from the road, the noise from the traffic will keep you awake, otherwise the rooms were very clean.

title: “Enjoyable”
text: I booked through the website which gave the best rates.the room was large and extremely comfortable. the location is excellent for tourist, walking distance to the mall and winchester house, museum , hot cooked breakfast really nice . i really enjoyed the stay here. i would definitely recommend this hotel to my friends and family.

title: “Affordable - Nice - Clean”
text: The least expensive Doubletree that I've ever stayed it.....It is located in war-torn Detroit....but is super upscale and nice. Safe private parking, big rooms with 2 TVs, etc. If you're looking for a place in Detroit - this is it!!

title: “Great hotel for a very reasonable price”
text: I went to an academic conference at the nearby Marriot but found, through Expedia, a very reasonable deal on a four-night stay at the Dana. It was very good value for money. Free WiFi, good food, nice room (packed with electronics, such as iPhone dock and large flat screen), really excellent location, friendly and helpful staff. Never used the spa, but I suppose for many that would be an added bonus. Breakfast service was prompt and convenient, no problems at all. Would definitely stay there again when travellling to downtown Chicago.

title: “Good service and information”
text: This is a good hotel, I had a good trip with my family because of their help. It is very useful for my trip.

title: “Average Hotel! Dour Staff!”
text:
My wife and I stayed here for 3 nights, in the middle of our vacation to Orlando.
We thought the prices of hotels in Boston were quite expensive, so booked through Priceline.co.uk, and ended up here.
The location is excellent and was extremely handy for everything. We bought $10 T-line tickets each, but only used the underground from and to the airport. We could walk everywhere from the hotel, and the good weather added to a pleasant stay in Boston.
The hotel lobby is very grand and heightens your expectation. Reception was efficient enough and we were processed quickly, though girl didn't smile. There was a large school group coming out of lifts when we were going to our room, which we thought would be noisy, but we didn't experiance any noise in the room.
Our room was fairly large, with 2 queen beds though, as other reviews state, the bathroom was very small. We didn't have a view from window. Hotel was very clean thoughout.
One thing that we noticed with every member of staff (yes, every one of them) was, no one smiled or acknowledges us throughout our stay. Even when we were checking out, the receptionist didn't look at us or ask if we enjoyed our stay.
The fire alarm went off at 6.45am on our last day and we had to evacuate the hotel until the fire brigade gave the all-clear. There was a muffled apology over the public address system, but no mention when we were checking out.
We didn't use any of the hotel's facilities or restaurants, prefering to eat at Legal Seafoods closeby and found the Rattlesnake Bar around the corner to be extremely friendly.
All in all, the hotel promised a lot with it's history and first impressions, but turned out to be no more than average

title: “Nice, not -too-expensive, hotel”
text:
Nice, clean. pleasant basic hotel, with very friendly staff, and a few extras like free wifi in rooms and an inet terminal in the lobby and decent free breakfast, for a few dollars a night more than the very rock bottom hotels in the area.
Good straight shot into downtown makes this a reaonable alternative to the downtown hotels if you have business there, plus there are some fun budget restaurants between Hobby and downtown.

title: “Oh my, where to begin, other than to advise AVOID...”
text:
Let me just first say that if you are "mini-me", you might like The Hudson!!! Otherwise, avoid! Other reviewers certainly have not exaggerated about how tiny & cramped the rooms are at this hotel (and at check-in they even claimed that they were giving us an "upgraded" room; can't even imagine what the "non-upgrade" room would have been!!!) - I have never stayed in a hotel room this cramped; if one of us wanted to get something from the closet or go to the bathroom, the other literally had to move onto the bed to make space for movement within the room. THE LIGHTING: they seem to have attempted to be hip and cool with their lighting, but it was so dim that trying to read was next to impossible; and in the bathroom I could barely see to put my make-up on. THE BATHROOM: very, very odd; the bathtub/shower had a large picture window in it facing into the bedroom; you could wave (or whatever <g>) to your partner while showering! I truly have never seen anything quite like that and still cannot fathom WHY they would have done this (to make the room appear larger??!!) - VERY, VERY bizarre! The room was unbearably HOT except for a small vent which was behind the headboard of the bed, so none of the cool air circulated into the room. We often had to go and just stand right above it to try and cool off.
There are ice machines on each floor but no ice bucket in the room; I always travel with some Ziploc bags so got some ice in one of them - I was totally grossed out the next morning when I looked at the bag of melted ice, and it was literally filled with dirt and mildew; it would appear that they don't clean the ice machines too frequently.
The elevators were always full and cramped, so you often had to wait for several elevators to pass you by before one arrived with space to crowd into.
I will attempt to address a few "positives" of this place: all of the very young staff were very friendly, polite & helpful. The lobby is very attractive but also VERY loud because of a nightclub/bar very popular with young singles located RIGHT ACROSS from reception.
It should be noted, as well, that the rates at The Hudson are not particularly inexpensive and in fact are higher than many nicer and roomier hotels with better amenities. All in all, this was one of my worst hotel experiences.

title: “Great NY Find!”
text:
New York City is very expensive. But Hotel 17 is reasonably priced. The location is great. Near Union square and with excellent subway access.
The hotel is well run, friendly, and clean. Service is good. An excellent value!.
AND we had no bedbugs :)

title: “Outstanding”
text: We stayed at this hotel with a group of students who were there for a band contest. The staff was wonderful with the kids and our entire group was made comfortable. The breakfast was really good too. We'll definately stay here again, whether with a group or when we travel for vacation.

title: “Uncontrolled party on the floor kept us awake all night”
text:
This hotel would have been better were it not for the all night drunken party that occurred on our floor. Every 20 minutes a door would slam and loud voices would be outside our door in the hall - all night long! Several calls were made between our two rooms to security to no avail. The hotel did ultimately comp the rooms for that night but the experience really put a damper on what should have been an enjoyable family vacation. The hotel was very expensive and allowing such a ruckus to go on all night was a big disappointment.
The positives of this hotel was the pool and pool service. The kids loved the two water slides and the poolside food service was a redeeming quality. The on-site restaurant was expensive but convenient. There are no good alternatives for dinner unless you have a car - there are no other restaurants worth going to close by. 
The other big positive of this hotel is that it is within walking distance to Seaworld. A pedestrian path will take you all the way and it is about a 10-15 minute walk. There is also a water taxi available if you buy your Seaworld passes from the hotel.

title: “I'd recommend...”
text:
Pros:
- Wonderful, seamless customer service for the durration of my stay... from start to finish.
- Great variety of restaurants, conveniently located in the hotel.
- ALL of the hotel dining options had amazing food (worth the price)... and, of course, great service.
- Awesome view from any room!
- Comfortable beds and pillows!
- Reasonably priced, considering the location of the hotel (right in the heart of downtown Dallas).
- And, although it is located "right in the heart of downtown Dallas," I felt completely safe and secluded from the hustle and grime that you generally find in a metropolitan city, like Dallas... relaxing.
- I was permitted a late check out time of 2pm without any additional charge, since I am a Hyatt Rewards Gold Card member.
- They had user-friendly "check-in kiosks" (much like the kiosks at the airport, used to print boarding passes, etc. without the assistance of an employee), near the front desk (which was fully staffed the entire day, into the evening)... this minimized the amount of time that any guest waited in line for assistance to check in and showed an investment to conserve guests' personal time during their stay at the hotel... very impressed. 
Cons:
- Maybe it was the time of my trip (during a busy weekend for Dallas, with lots of travelers)-- I was there for the Rock 'n' Roll Dallas 1/2 Marathon weekend, but there were LOTS of families there (with LOTS of children)... made for a chaotic lobby experience, every time. However, I do not believe this hotel generally caters to or attracts such a familial demographic.
- I thought the bathroom could have been a little bit cleaner... but this is an area I am very picky on. It might suffice for someone less stringent.
- The valet system was a mess... although you could tell that the people who worked in valet (the drivers, the coordinators who answered phones, etc) were all working very, very hard to meet the needs of all of the guests... the way it was set up prevented them from doing as well as they should have been, considering how much effort they put into meeting everyone's needs. This could use some innovation.
- I could hear the guests in the room next to mine laughing and talking... so, I assume the walls are somewhat thin. (But, at hotels, aren't they all??)
- WiFi isn't free.
- My "wake up call" that I scheduled was late by 11 minutes; however, I was already awake when she called.

title: “Pleasant front desk but sucky housekeeping”
text:
Stayed here for 10 days as my wife is attending a conference. So, my routine is rather similar everyday ie have breakfast with my wife At The nearby bakery( our room didnt come with breakfast) and after sending my wife to her conference,i will shop around and will be back At The room around 1 pm.
But, to my dismay, on those days that i return to The room,i had to sit At The lobby as The room was not done. Besides that, The only thing that was done are The bed and The toilet!!!The desk remain cluttered and The floor was not vacuumed. Even The chair was not put in placed and The wardrobe door was not even closed!! To make it worse,everyday they forget to placed 2 complimentary bottle of mineral water as such i have to personally call The housekeeping myself.
To make it worse, We are a member of The Priority Club and this was The treatment We got.

title: “Classic flower, showing signs of wilting.”
text:
Starting off, this historic hotel is still impressive when you arrive at first. Beautiful exterior and lobby, elegant (if not a bit cramped) wood-paneled elevators, and the Oak Room restaurant that wreaks "old money".
We got an upgrade to a Deluxe room which was around 400 sq ft (quite roomy). We noticed though that the bathroom was quite small given the rooms size, but that wasn't a big issue for us, although it might be for larger people. I was a bit surprised though at the details, ie. the shower curtain was old, and cheap (out of place for the marble bathroom), the shower was low flow so I never really felt like it did anything (Seinfeld anyone?), the room still seemed to have its original fixtures from 1912 (doors and chandelier). The closet door didn't even close completely. Don't get me wrong, the room was very clean and the bed was sumptuous, but overall it seemed like it was overdue for a refurb.
Flat screen TV was fine and there was sufficient drawer space for a short stay (lacking for one longer than 3 days). 
Staff were all great. Kudos to Dragana (PM Concierge) and Mitchell (? AM Concierge) for their fine recommendations. Check-in and out were swift and efficient with a smile.
As for the I read about the additional charges, the property is not geared for the budget minded traveler. It's a full service business hotel where you're getting prime location, amenities and service. 
Quick tip- If you're not keen on paying the $40 day parking, there is a garage at 100 Clarendon (the next block directly behind the hotel) that offers a $27 day rate if you show them a copy of your hotel bill when you take the car out.
All in all we had a great stay and would go back again.

title: “Modern in Perfect Location”
text: I travelled to Chicago for my 30th birthday girlfriends getaway. I booked The James through hotwire.com for a great rate of $124/night. The location was perfect...all the shopping and eating we did were within walking distance. We only drove to clubs. Speaking of driving, the parking rate was expensive which is to be expected in downtown Chicago. The service was impeccable from valet, to the front desk, to concierge. Housekeeping did leave the dirty towels we left of the bathroom floor to be removed when our room was cleaned. The beds were extremely comfortable as we found it easy to take naps and difficult to arise from them. We stayed in a standard double room with no view which wasn't a big deal. I don't know how i feel about the flat square sink but it was in sync with the style. The in room bar was very tempting as they provided martini glasses and a shaker. The flat screen was cool as well as the channel selections. We loved the seating nook in the room and found it easy to adjust the room temperature to our liking. I could tell that the walls were thin but we didn't have issues with noise. I definitely recommend staying if you can get the a great rate.

title: “Unexpectedly nice”
text: We stayed at the GWU Inn for 3 nights and found the hotel to be charming. We were a little apprehensive at first because we did not book the room ourselves and so did not know what to expect. (We had reservations at another hotel which had closed for renovations). The room was a small suite with king-sized bed and a fold-out sofa and a kitchenette. The hotel was very clean and the staff extremely nice. The front desk and bellhops were always willing to go the extra mile. An added bonus...the hotel is VERY close to the Metro station which is the ONLY way to get around D.C! We would definitely stay at the GWU Inn again.

title: “Great place to stay!”
text:
We just returned from a two night stay at the Residence Inn in DC. Our first surprise from arriving at the Federal Center Metro Station, was how close the hotel was. We were carrying our luggage so this was wonderful. The distance is 2 blocks at the most. It was an extremely easy walk, and the Inn is located in a quiet section of DC - Just south of the Mall area. The staff were very friendly and stored our bags for us since it was about 10:30 am and our room wasn't ready yet. They also have ice cold water with lemon or fruit in it in a dispenser in the lobby. We were there when the temperature reached the high 90's and we really appreciated this. We stayed in a two bedroom suite on the 11th floor. The room was very spacious with two bathrooms. It was great for our family of 5. We enjoyed having the complimentary hot breakfast in the morning. There was plenty to choose from, and unlike most places that offer this, plenty of seating. The light dinners in the evening were great too! 
The only negative comments I would have about this hotel would be about the pool area and the location. The pool was pretty small and very cold. The area around the pool needed spruced up a bit and updated. The location is great to getting to the things at the mall, but it isn't very close to many restaurants and things north of the mall. It still worked out, we just ate while we were out at the many attractions. You could easily take the metro to restaurants if you wanted to. There are a few options within a block of the hotel and a starbucks near by too.
The positives far out-weighed the negatives. I would be happy to stay here again.

title: “The Best By Beale”
text:
My friends and I were there October 2004 to attend King Biscuit. We stayed at Hampton Inn and Suites and could have not asked for a better hotel. The suite was beautiful, the balcony wonderful, clean, cheerful, with wonderful views. All of the staff were great, free breakfast super, suite was clean and
large enough for us. Worth the price, we are returning there October 7, 2005, and looking forward to another fantastic stay at Hampton Inn by Beale. Would highly recommend to anyone

title: “Superb practical choice”
text: If you're after a boutique hotel or the sort of place where you're tipping flunkies every 5 minutes, then look elsewhere. If, however, you want a huge room with a full kitchenette and washer/dryer in the perfect location, then Comfort Suites is for you. Very friendly, helpful staff too.

title: “Friendly, Convenient, and Well-Appointed!”
text: This is the place to stay for cleanliness, friendly staff, convenient location to Times Square, and comfort! It is also a bargain. I always enjoy HGI's and this location could not have been better. The receptionists and the concierge were genuinely friendly and very helpful. In speaking with Nicole, we learned that you have to have passes to visit Ground Zero, (talk about the out-of- towners not knowing!). So, she went right on-line and ordered and printed them for us, directed us to the e-train right across the street, and in 15 minutes, we were there! Elevator parking is right next door and we included it in the price of our room...very reasonable $212 TOTAL for three of us in the room on the 15th floor. It was quiet, comfortable and beautifully maintained. Get over the small bathrooms! What more could you possibly need? I plan to return in the summer and this will be my GO TO place. This is a perfect location for a short walk to Rockefeller Center and a trip to the Top of the Rock!!! Thanks to everyone at HGI Time Square for making us NH ladies feel welcome! New Yorkers, you rock!

title: “Good place, Great service!”
text:
My family and I drove down to San Antonio for the weekend from Round Rock, and I had been here before but never with my family. I was surprised how the hotel could accomodate us so last minute and on a weekend no less. 
There were many activities to keep my boys entertained and my wife relaxed. The food on site was amazing especially the Brannons breakfast which we went to every morning. To my surprise the boys loved the pool, but were more entrigued by the other activities held. Especially the game room, which had several various game systems and games to keep every age group of kid entertained. Stephanie, the attendent in the room was amazing with my boys. She helped them, made them feel included and was very down to earth. She was able to keep them in good spirits even while playing with them. This Is just one of many of the great staff that really made us feel like we were at our home away from home. 
Money well spent for a quick weekend get away.

title: “everything was excellent!”
text: Our stay at the hilton garden inn on west 35 was excellent. Very nice staff, very clean rooms, awesome location. It`s definitely the one hotel we`ll be staying at when we come to nyc. Very good job, you guys! Roxi M.

title: “"Customer service taken to another level"”
text:
Can not say enough of the customer service of this Holiday Inn!! To name a few- Nick (front desk), Midge and Maria working in the dinning area, keeping all those patrons fed with a smile on their faces, even with NO AC in most of the hotel except for the rooms for over 3 days!!! We even got a bottle of wine sent to our room from Midge- our daughters loved her!! She cheered up the area with a smile on her face, and greeted every person that walked into the breakfast area.
Kudos to Hans, who was everywhere- front desk, breakfast area, you name it he was there!! After hearing our troubles with a local Hertz rental outfit, who showed up 30 mins late and with a car that could fit 2 adults instead of 4- he came to our RESCUE! By driving us to the airport and dropping us off at a Hertz location there, so that we could rearrange a "new" rental for our drive up the coast to LA!! Now thats what I call "going out of your way to keep your customers happy!!"
If we ever go back, I would stay here without any question!!
If I had to say anything negative about the hotel itself, would be the bathroom in the rooms, "slightly" small- but the beds were comfortable and the rest of the ammenities were excellent, including the shuttle service, Christian, was very accommodating.

title: “Great place”
text: I have stayed in higher rated, higher priced places and this one topped them all. At first the look of the place threw me, but with the sunlight I could see how well taken care of it was. Excellent, clean rooms (esp. the baths), clean very comfortable beds....and the staff was more than accomadating. The shuttle was available whenever we needed it....would def. stay here again!

title: “Great location”
text:
Have just returned from 4 nights at the Warwick. We were upgraded as we arrived and the room was big with a kingsized bed and nice decor. Great location only one block from nearest metro and most tourist attractions within walking distance. Loved NY, went to see the METS which was great and saw Avenue Q also v good and ate in some great restaurants. If you like ribs go to brother Jimmys on West 83rd friendly locals restaurant with the best ribs ever. If going to NY for first time definitely do the bus tours but avoid the horse and carriage ride its a total rip off!
Would definitely return to the Warwick

title: “Very pleasant stay at this hotel”
text:
We came from Orlando, Florida for the swearing in ceremony of my daughter at the US Supreme Court. We arrived much earlier at the hotel than we expected and it was very convenient that the lady at the front desk allowed us to check in early. Also the location of the hotel was very convenient since it is only a stone's throw away from the Supreme Court.
As expected at a location like that, the rooms are not very spacious, but the room was nicely decorated, very clean and everything worked. The small fridge and microwave were very handy.Parking was a problem but the FD helped us out to let us park in the loading zone for some time. When we received a parking ticket anyway the hotel promised to pay for it (we don't know yet if they really will). The room rate was reasonable. We were charged for a roll away bed but it was brought to our room as promised in a timely manner. The breakfast room is nice, the persons taking care of the breakfast very friendly and the continental breakfast (included in the room rate) excellent. Front desk agents and housekeepers we met were friendly and helpful.

title: “Spend the money, stay at a Hilton”
text: Great place to stay. Spend the extra money and stay at a Hilton hotel. We booked our room through Hilton. Do not use hotwire or similiar sites. Booking directly thourgh the Hilton allowed us to check in early. When arriving back to the hotel late at night our air conditioner was making a loud squeaking noise. We called the front desk and immediatley the manager along with maintenance personal showed up. The apologizes were quick to come and got upgraded to the suite without saying a word. I will stay here everytime I visit DC. This hotel is 3 min walk from White House, 10 min walk to the Mall.

title: “Lucked Out”
text: After reading previous reviews, we lucked out. No mishaps in our two nights stay. Our rooms were less than $200/night taxes included. My biggest fear was the bed bugs previous reviews indicated. We checked our beds, found none, and slept well. We got the smallest room on the 11th floor next to the elevator and next to the door that goes to our wing. We lucked out with hardly any traffic on that floor. The room was small and the bathroom was very small. We are not big people and I can see why the room will a problem with bigger people. Bottom line, is that it was a very affordable place to stay at a great residential location next to Central Park. It was a place to sleep and not to hang out. You don't want to spend $$$ just for that. The service desk people were helpful especially Penny. Overall we lucked out after reading all of he complains.

title: “Paradise Lost”
text: If you go here hoping for a clean, serene, resort-like atmosphere you will be sorely disappointed. It felt like a campground. The pictures on their web-site are highly misleading. The room's are old and dirty. The furniture is cheap and worn. The room's air conditioning unit was loud and rattling. The bed was uncomfortable and the bedding was old and coarse. I didn't feel comfortable walking around barefoot in the room and there were insects in the bathroom. We paid extra for a bay-side room and the minute we walked out onto the terrace we knew that was a mistake too. We had no privacy. While sitting on our patio, we had people sitting 10 feet to the right and left of us without any separation. Kids were running by us and there were empty cups and bottles littering the area in front of our terrace. How they get away with advertising this place as a 'resort and spa' is beyond me. We were traveling without our children for the first time and this was NOT the quiet, secluded atmosphere we were told it was. We left after the first night and would warn anyone to stay far away. The accommodations were sub-Super 8 and the price was 4 times as much.

title: “amazing service - great location”
text:
The Custom House was amazing. Our room was a huge suite, just as pictured on the website. Our room was 1 of 2 located on the first floor. This room is basicly in a museum. You walk up one level from the lobby into the Peabody Essex Museum, turn left - and there was our suite. The staff at this hotel was phenominal, answering any and all questions. The front desk staff was also very helpful with late night dining suggestions. I tried to tip one particularly helpful member of the staff when we checked out - and he respectfully declined. The location is perfect, and literally adjacent to the aquarium subway stop.
To prevent confusion: I had seen some other reviews that said daily maid service was an extra fee. This is only if you are using timeshare points to pay for your room. If you reserve through the marriott website and pay a nightly rate, there is free maid service just like any other hotel.

title: “Reputable”
text: As others have stated, it is a neighborhood on the industrial/near an airport w/o much character, but convenient to get to from the rental car area and the room was more than adequate for the reasonable cost. The desk clerk went out of his way to draw a map for me after reconfirming my destination with a phone call w/questions. As a single traveller alone, I was A-okay with it - did not feel unsafe. Breakfast was passable, altho not alot of variety, BUT clean and spacious as noted by others. The free internet in the lobby for boarding pass was extra appreciated. The ease to get on to Hiway 202 and interstates was nice.

title: “Not bad but not good”
text: The place is nice, clean and beautiful. It has an extravagant decor with a hollywood style. The rooms are spacious and everything seem brand new. On the other had, the rooms have a serious acoustic problem. You can hear everything from the other rooms nearby. Everytime somebody slams a door on the same floor you hear it quite loud in your room. There is also a serious security problem. Anybody can go up to the second floor where my room was located. The location of the hotel is also bad. There are many homeless people and strange figures on the streets nearby. I would't go back.

title: “Great location for shopping”
text:
I stayed at this hotel as a combination of price and location for 2 nights before I went up state for business. Staff were welcoming, friendly & very efficient at check in. I stayed in a deluxe room and it is the biggest room I have ever stayed in Manhattan! 
On arrival I was missing a TV remote which was very bizarre but someone came up to my room with a new one within 5 mins of my call. I didnt arrive until around 7.30pm so I basically wanted to chcek in, and grab something to eat before going to bed. I ate at thebar downstairs, always a bit wary to start as a single femle traveller but it was fine and I was able to sit at the bar and not feel awkward. I ate buffalo chicken fingers from the bar menu and although a great flavour chicken was really tough and over-cooked.
In the morning I went to the coffee machine to find no coffee - I decided just to shower and grab a takeaway tea once I was out figuring housekeeping must have forgotten and would notice later. When I returned the coffee had still not been replenished, on my way out for food that evening I asked at reception and they were very apologetic and said it was unacceptable and would be replaced immeditely, on my return there was plenty of coffee in my room.
My only other complaint was the bathroom was not sparkly clean - the floor, shower and sink were just kind of wiped over which is not what you expect. If youa re looking for somehwere with decent rooms, great location for shopping and a bar/food onsite this ideal at a reasonable price. I would go back. I will also note that it was also a little quieter than other hotels Ive stayed in in Manhattan which is a bonus!.

title: “OK - nothing special”
text:
We spent the weekend of May 30-Jun1 here on a baseball trip. This hotel was VERY expensive - its Baltimore after all. Everything else was very expensive as well. We booked a room on the Club floor expecting fine amenities as is the case at every other supposedly 4-5 star hotel we have stayed in. Not the case here. 
Beer / Wine were chargeable items on the club floor. I have NEVER stayed on a club floor where they charged for anything. Food selections were 'ok,' but usually ran out quickly and the 'concierge' there spent most of her time either talking on the phone or talking with people who obviously co-workers and workers and friends in the lounge. 
The bed was Hyatt comfortable - service was inconsistent. First nite, turn down service, next night, not. Called for towels, got one. Requested extra towels in advance - it was confirmed - got none. 
We had a free breakfast rate and the buffet was typical hotel buffet. You could order eggs special and it took 25m to get 2 eggs over easy and coffee refills were untimely as well - too few employees working. Yet if you got up to get coffee the matre'd would come over and tell you you could not serve yourself, and they'd be right over - 10 min later. 
Overall - for what we paid, we would not stay here again.

title: “Great Location, Great Service, Great Hotel”
text: My wife and I stayed here for a long weekend and it was great. The check-in staff changed our room to a single bed without question, and the bar served the best martini I have had in a while. The rooms were well decorated and spacious, although it did get a little tight through the bathroom door. The bell staff was very accomodating and walked my wife up to our room when she arrived late. I would definitely stay here again!

title: “Nice boutique hotel, extremely well situated”
text: Great service and nice, though very small, rooms. Breakfast was good, and the staff was very accommodating of dietary restrictions. Extremely well situated near Times Square, yet quiet and peaceful. The bar got a bit loud and busy, but there was no noise up in the rooms.

title: “typical HGI, but small problems”
text:
I often stay in HGI while traveling. This was a typical design. Rooms were quite spacious. The woman that checked me in was friendly.
The room had a couple small problems: the clock radio was workable but damaged, and the drain in the sink was very slow. Not a big problem, but not what I expected. 
The restaurant was quite busy in the morning and it took a while to get someone to serve me.
Overall, I'd stay there again, but it was a worse experience than other HGI I've stayed at

title: “Loved the Marriott”
text:
My partner and I stayed at this hotel for one night when our flight went tech. 
We were on our way to Taiwan, When we got there we were checked in efficently and quickly. when we got to our room it was a suite not just a normal room. We thought we were in heaven, We used the laundry room which was easy to use and very quick. 
Staff were all polite and courteous when spoken to about something we needed. 
The pool was amazing but we did not go in as there was a wedding on that night and they were using the outdoor space. 
The bed as always was huge and so comfortable
We would deffinately stay here again if in need of a night over in LA. 
Thanks to the Marriott

title: “If you are not a starwood member forget this place”
text:
My travel agent booked us 5 nights at this hotel. I had planned a surprise trip for my husband's 40th bday. Upon arriving at the hotel everything appeared to be fine aside from the crazy parking fee of $45. My travel agent had asked about the cost for parking and they said it was a minimal fee. Sorry but $45 a day is not minimal. We went to our room to find we were put in a room with 2 double beds. We had requested a King bed. We called down and they said there was nothing they could do until the next day. Plus the bathrooms were sooo small. You can't have 2 people in that area that is for sure. So, then that night we went down to confirm in person that we would be switched. The lady we talked to said there was nothing listed for us to be moved. She said there was no way we would be moved until Thursday. The guy we had talked to happen to come out then and we asked him why he did not have us listed as being moved the next day. He said "I'm working on it." Then the lady went on to say to us if we were Starwood members we would have gotten the king size bed. I said to her so me as a paying customer for 5 nights doesn't matter? She said no that is not what she meant. The sad part is I am a starwood member but did not have my membership card with me. It should not matter if you are a member or not the treatment should be the same. The next day we were moved to the new room and it had a sign that said this room is for starwood members. The room was completely opposite of the room we had been in. A bigger bathroom sink. The shower/toilet area was still pretty small. The room had a couch and a TV that actually worked ( our TV remote did not work in our 1st room). The room appeared to be more up to date and we were no longer looking over the bus terminal which was quite noisy at night and early in the morning. 
The other thing is that in this day and age many hotels do not charge for WIFI. But, this hotel charged $15 a day. That is crazy! And they just kept saying go to the lobby b/c it is free there. Who wants to sit in a hotel lobby to check their email and do stuff on the internet. Not us. It was not a comfortable place to sit and get cozy on the computer. 
It also got very noisy in the hallways at night. You could hear everything thru the walls which was not really nice when we were sleeping the night before we left and the people next to us arrived back at 3am to then be a bit loud and wake us. And we had to be up by 4:30 to get to the airport on time for our flight. 
The only good was that the concierge group offered to set things up for us to do, but I had already planned out all of our stuff.

title: “Worse Hotel experience yet!”
text: I have been going down to southern California to see my daughter for five years, and I had my worst hotel experience at the Four points Sheraton in LA. On this trip both my 17 year old daughter and my 8 year old daughter were with me. When we checked in, the women who helped me negatively noted that I had booked with a third party (Price line), and then proceeded to treat me like garbage. When I requested a double bed in our room, I was told none were available, and no alternative solution was offered. When I called to the front desk to request a fold down bed, the same women who checked me in answered the phone, and she told me that it might not fit, and that she would have to check with housekeeping. The woman at the front desk immediately called back and informed my daughter, who answered the phone, “ that there was no way the bed would fit into that room. “ Later, when I was down stairs I asked a man from housekeeping about the bed, he asked me my room number, but nothing happened. A few hours later, I called down to the front desk, and I let them know that I was not happy, and that I was going to call their corporate office and complain. The excuse I was given was that they didn’t know I had checked in yet, even though I was talking to them from my room, which I had been given keys to at least 3 hours earlier when I checked in. Later someone called back and said a bed would fit in my room no problem, and one was finally brought up. The bed fit no problem with room to walk around it, and we could have fit another on in the room. The Ice machine on our floor, and the 2 below us were broken, and my Ice bucket leaked water all over the counter and floor of our bathroom (yes I used the plastic bag). The game controller that is supposed to be with the TV was missing, and the hotel had taken measures to insure you couldn’t plug your own game into the TV, something we do at Marriot hotels all over southern cal all the time. During the whole time I stayed there, not one staff member asked me about my stay, including when I checked out, apparently they don’t care.

title: “SpringHill Suites Seattle”
text:
I stayed there one night, and could not sleep very well with the water dripping in the shower area left over from the previous guest. Also, several times the television signal seems like the voices were dubbed not natural, and the channel guide did not match the actual channels on thetelevision.
Nice that there was a free hot breakfast for all guests including making your own waffles. Also, a complimentary shuttle operates til 9:30 pm to transport guests to the Seattle downtown or the Seattle center area with reservations required. The front desk staff seem to be friendly, and accomodating.

title: “Great Location”
text: Stayed 4 nights at the Affinia 50. Perfect location for our needs and we were able to walk to many attractions. Staff was very nice and room was clean and quiet.

title: “Clean comortable room near-ish the airport”
text: Not too close to the airport, but close to the 101 for travels southward. Near a number of cool eateries. With all the usual Hampton/Hilton amenities. The staff here is what makes the place. Everyone was friendly and accomodating.

title: “Best Night's Sleep in NYC”
text: Spent three nights at the Omni Berkshire, visiting with out of state friends. My 5 year old was with us. The rooms were very comfortable. It was very quiet. We received excellent service, any requests were met promptly and politely. The gym was great and we found the location to be perfect. We walked to the park and everywhere else. My only disappointment was the restaurant. The food was only so-so and the price tag was high. I had heard this, but timing made us try it none the less. I would definitely stay again.

title: “Not worth the money”
text: I stayed at the hotel from April 8 - 11 for a convention and do not feel this hotel is worth the money. We paid $254 per night. Construction is still going on as stated by other guests. Constructions workers and noise is throughout the day. The pool area is small compared to the size of the hotel. The pool area is stark without greenery or space to move around. It is located on the 5th floor, is outside and is no more than 3 feet deep. There is no hot tub. Internet is $9.95 per day and should be free. There is no safe in the room, no mini fridge. The decor is very retro 60s with loud oranges, yellow, golds. The hotel had been open 11 days when we checked in, The tub in our room has a 6 inch crack in it, the a/c in our room whined very loudly when it was on. What did I like - the bedding was comfortable, the riverwalk is easily accessable, the staff was very nice and accommodating. This hotel is just too expensive. Earlier in the week I had to stay at a Quality Inn do to final four being downtown and no room at the Hyatt. At $116 per night, we actually liked the Quality Inn better and felt we received a lot more value.

title: “A real touch of Paradise”
text: This resort is beautiful and relaxing and rejuvinating.

title: “classy and fun”
text: Had a great stay at the US Grant. The Hotel was classy and charming. Every staff member was very helpful. I look forward to our next trip to San Diego and will make sure the US Grant is where we stay.

title: “this hotel is shabby and tired”
text: I brought in 25 people for a business meeting this week. Before choosing this hotel, I had a tour of two different rooms. both were good (for a Holiday Inn). When i checked in Monday night, I found that it was bait & switch. My rom was a dump, the hallways had worn and dirty carpet, low ceilings with dirty paint, the upholstered chair in my room was spotted and filthy, the mattress was visibly lumpy, the doorway to the bathroom was less than 24" wide, and there was NO door, the silvering on the mirrors was flaking off. Shabby, years of deferred maintenance, and badly in need of updating! And a dozen of my guests complained to me about the shabiness of the hotel I selected for them. Boo! I would NEVER stay there again.

title: “a classic that needs renovation”
text: This is a lovely old hotel, but one that badly needs renovation to regain a luxury status. The furniture is worn, the bathrooms outdated. The concierge is knowledgeable. The staff is courteous. The location is ideal. If spruced up, this would be a first-rate choice. A New Yorker

title: “Comfortable but Grubby!”
text: Booked for $85 on Priceline - a great value! Second time this year Priceline placed us there. Location is great. Hotel is older. Lobby is grand. Rooms are worn, a bit dingy and grubby, and the carpeting is need of a deep cleaning. Overall an okay experience - but nothing special. No bed bug bites.

title: “Great Experience”
text: I really connected with this hotel and its rich history. The courtyard garden was in bloom and was very relaxing. The room was pleasant, clean and quiet. The staff was friendly, responsive and informative. I ate dinner at the hotel restaurant and loved the atmosphere and the food. The waiter was friendly, informative and attentive. The food was quite good and average in price for the type and quality. My room was in a newer section and overlooked the Alamo. The river walk, plenty of shopping, restaurants, fast food and entertainment were all within a few minutes walk.

title: “Very good except for the pool”
text:
My wife and kids (age 4 and 6) stayed with me at this hotel on our way back from Minnesota. This hotel has to be the best of the trip. It was spacious throughout and had all of the amenities that you would want. There was free wireless and a business center with a FAX machine and printer. The fitness center has a weight machine, bike and treadmill and maybe one or two other pieces of equipment. Our room had a couch with an ottoman and it had a refrigerator and microwave, all for $80. it was nicely laid out too. 
The hotel doesn't have a courtyard or anything but is located next to a Sam's Club and a Mediterreanean (sp?) restaurant. If you take Rockville Road towards the city, you'll find a grocery store.
We arrived late for breakfast so some of the food was gone. There was a make-your-own waffle iron, bagels, breads, sausage gravy, pieces of fruit, cereal, milk, three kinds of juices and that's about all I can remember.
The limited TV channels and the toxic pool was the bummer of this place. My wife missed her favorite show on Bravo because they only carry 18 or so channels. All of our eyes were stinging after a few minutes in the pool. The hot tub was not overly hot but it was not the chlorine soup that the pool was so the kids swam there too.
It would be a five except for the pool, which could have just been a mistake made on that day. Despite that, we do plan to come here again next summer.

title: “GOOD LOCATION”
text:
We stayed here for a week and found the location and interior very good. The restaurant was a big let down so we did not use it. However with plenty of great places to eat it did not matter.
Nice touch with the evening free wine sessions and morning coffee. Excellent front desk staff, very helpful. Business centre was useful too.

title: “Great People, Great Location”
text:
Really enjoyed our week at the US Grant. While the rooms were nice, comfortable and clean, they were rooms. What did make a difference for us was the staff. From the front desk to the maids, to the concierge. Everyone was great. Good old fashioned customer service. We had the concierge desk assist us with several items (we were playing toursit) and they were FANTASTIC. 
Also - the location you can not beat if you are wanting to see San Diego. We did not rent a car, Taxi from the airport was $15, and you can catch buses/trolleys/etc. right in front of the hotel for $5/day. Plus a lot of places you can walk to. Just a couple of blocks to the Gaslamp resturant district. 
While they are not the cheapest place in town, they are worth every penny.

title: “Good place to stay in Washington”
text: Booked in here for 5 nights as attending a convention. Situated literally just around the corner from the White House and convenient for all the main tourist sites. Very welcoming, helpful staff. Large room, very comfortable bed, and the room very quiet. All the usual facilities you would expect in a hotel this size. Bottled water was provided to the room every day, but there was no in room coffee maker, hence the loss of "one" point. A very minor criticism, however. I didn't eat at the hotel so can't comment on the food. Quite expensive, but I think that had something to do with the large convention I was attending. Would certainly stay here again if in Washington.

title: “Magnolia Houston”
text: Great hotel in a great location. The bed was the best hotel bed I have ever slept in. The room was very nice but a $6.00 bottle of water?? All in all, a great value, great location, I would not hesitate staying here the next time I am in Houston.

title: “Beautiful property lacking in service”
text:
The newly completed remodel on the property is beautiful. From the pool to the rooms it is very well done. There is a slight design flaw in the bay view, balcony kings , with the bathroom door obstructing the vanity. The bigger problem though is the service. The pool service was marginal to non existent on the two ocassions we were at the pool. When I needed local information and placed a call to the concierge I was placed on terminal hold and needed to hang up and call back for assistance.
The one time we wanted to eat in the hotel(marina kitchen) we ended up leaving after 20 minutes, having never received water, coffe or acknowledgement that we were there.. This a beautiful property with a great location. It is very crowded and busy, especially the pool area, but service definately needs to be improved.

title: “Shoreham Hotel NY an unpleasant and overpriced hotel. Avoid at all cost.”
text: If you like antiquated mechanicals (an air conditioner that blows directly on your bed, but can't be adjusted), a bathroom devoid of towels and toiletries, linens that are not changed once during a four night stay, window shades that can not be raised as to provide an outside view, a sofa that was new when Thomas Edison was in diapers and a housekeeping crew that refuses to answer the telephone, then this is the hotel for you. On the bright side, the hotel engineer (whom guests should never have to meet) was excellent, as well as the hotel location and surrounding neighborhood.

title: “Great Location, Nice Amenities”
text:
A friend and I came to SF to do some shopping and to see all the holiday decorations around Union Square. It was great just walking around, it was so pretty at night with all the trees and lights! 
The hotel's location is very ideal, as it's basically right next to Union Square. The decor of the lobby is beautiful. We got a Queen Petite Room and the name of it is spot on. It's fairly small. We didn't mind since we weren't in the room that much. The room was clean and the Aveda products are a plus.
The Starlight Room on the 21st floor is pretty cool for the view and the dancing though a little pricey for drinks. The lobby bar was not crowded like others have posted but it was a Sunday. There's a bartender there that won best bartender in SF I guess. He was nice and seemed to have a local following. I also heard the drag show at the Starlight on Sunday afternoons are fun to see, but we missed it by 1/2 hour.
What would make this hotel even better though is if the staff was really friendly. The service was really just okay overall. Check-in was good. but it actually seemed a bother to get help on a couple of occasions with directions, to get our luggage or to get restaurant recommendations. As some of these employees are the first people customers encounter, I would think the hotel would strive for exceptional service out of them.
Luckily, the price and location overshadowed the service. We got a great rate for the room. At that price and being so close to Union Square, I think we would definitely stay at the Sir Francis again.

title: “A Boston Bargain”
text: We had a wonderful New Year's weekend at the Chandler Inn...at a fraction of the cost of surrounding hotels. Located within walking distance of downtown Boston, on a relatively quiet street, the Chandler was a lucky find. Our room, though small by some standards, had everything we needed, and was immaculately clean. We try to "be green," so we appreciated the minimalist style of the accommodations, without sacrificing comfort. The bed was super-comfortable and the large flat screen TV was great for catching up on the Bowl Games! The staff was friendly, professional and helpful, helping us find an open store on New Year's Eve when we realized that my husband had forgotten his dress shirt. Highly recommended for a convenient, inexpensive, and minimalist experience.

title: “Good Location!”
text: Excellent location to tour the city, Helpful concierge. Good Choice at breakfast. Nice sized room.

title: “Not up to Hilton standards, outdated, daily charge for internet”
text:
I travel quite a bit for business and stay almost exclusively at Hilton brand hotels due to their overall high standards and quality. This hotel was outdated and not what I consider a business hotel. Poorly insulated so you could hear the tv and other noise from the adjoining rooms. There was also a daily charge for Internet. Most business hotels, even some of the lower end hotels, offer free Internet. 
The pool area looked nothing like the professional photos posted on their website. I will post pictures later.
We drove around the area and found there were several options for the same price or less that were better than this hotel.
Hard to believe this was a Hilton hotel. Very disappointed!

title: “Great location if doing business in SE Denver.”
text:
I have stayed at several Embassy Suites hotels around the US and would rate this one as one of my top 5. As per the norm there are the typical manager's reception and cooked to order breakfast. However what sets this Emabassy suites apart from others is the cleanliness of the interior spaces and the excellent staff and servcie. When I first arrived I was a little worried about the state of this hotel. It is an older Embassy Suites. However within 30 minutes of being inside,. I was totally sold on staying here. Everything is clean and maintianed. The hotel has no older hotel smell. Everything seemed to be fresh. At the manager's reception, the wait staff were attentive and helpful. There was never the usual long line waiting for more 'free' drinks. In the monring the staff even refilled my coffee cup. Not usual for an Embassy Suites.
If you are doing business in SE Denver, this is a great place to stay. There are restaurants wihtin 5 minutes drive or on a nice day maybe 10 minutes walk. Whole Foods is direclty across the street. The neighborhood appeared safe.

title: “Prescott Hotel San Fran”
text: Stayed here for 4 nights late August on Honeymoon,room very clean and comfortable,hotel very close to everywhere,good location.Would definatley stay here again.the staff very helpful and the breakfast has a good selection.

title: “Clean, comfy, quiet...”
text: After being on the road for the past 3 weeks we have some hits and some misses with accommodation. This place was clean, the bed was comfy, the area was nice and quiet.. no frills but thats not a problem when you just need a nice bed for the night. Very happy with this stay and would recommend.

title: “Our stay was first class all the way!”
text: My wife and I are commuters in and out of New Jersey and we decided to stay at The W Hotel on a night that we had to stay in the city for a benefit. The experience we had at the hotel was spectacular and made us feel as if we were the only two people staying there. The service was fast, responsive, and courteous. The room was beautiful and the world famous king size bed lived up to its reputation and gave us an amazing night sleep. The best way I can describe how I feel is that The W wasn't just a hotel; it was an experience.

title: “Some of the worst service I have ever seen.”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for two nights while on a business trip. I really tried to like it, as my boss raves about the entire Hampton Inn franchise and there seemed to be a lot of amenities (free full breakfast, internet access) offered for the price. But there were so many problems I was relieved to be on my way home.
First, I called for the shuttle when I arrived at the airport. The front desk told me exactly where to stand, so I did. I waited a good half an hour in the hot sun. Finally, along came the shuttle and dropped some people off. I prepared to get in, but the driver started freaking out, telling me to walk all this way to go somewhere else to be picked up because it was a drop-off zone only and she could be fined. I looked around me and saw other hotel shuttles picking people up and pleaded my case. She finally let me board, and she played loud hip-hop music on our way to the hotel (which is not far from the airport at all, if you are concerned about that).
Upon check-in, I was asked for a credit card. I explained that the credit card used to book my stay was a company credit card, so I didn't have that one in case it was a concern. The front desk person attendant just kept saying over, "I need a credit card. For incidentals. I need a credit card. For incidentals." She wasn't even listening to me as I slapped down my own card. Before I went up to my room, I asked how to use the internet access in the room. She just rolled her eyes at me and said, "plug in your computer. Log on to Explorer." Huh?? Furthermore, I had called this hotel prior to booking and specifically asked what sort of internet access was in the rooms, and I was told WIRELESS. What they actually offered was high-speed via a modem cord, and wireless access in the lobby.
The room was nothing to write home about. A bed with thin blankets and sheets. Rather small. The bathroom was well-stocked with complimentary toiletries and towels. There was no helpful information in the room, like maps, or a list of area restaurants at all. Their guest information book was rather useless. I tried out the internet and was able to figure out how to get on.
I checked in on a Sunday afternoon, and I don't think the shuttle runs very often. But the next night, there was definitely no missing it. Like other reviewers have said, the hotel is RIGHT on the trolley line, so be prepared for some noise. Not only was the trolley itself noisy (it's more of a rail system, not an actual San Francisco-type trolley) but the riff-raff who hung out at the trolley station were noisier. Since the hotel is right on the outskirts of the Gas Lamp Quarter, which apparently never sleeps, people were out there until very late at night. I thought because I am a city dweller, it wouldn't bother me, but it really was quite noisy and I ended up using my ear plugs to drown them out.
The pool is on the second floor balcony but I only briefly took a peek at it. It is rather secluded from the hotel entrance, so I'd feel odd if I were alone.
The breakfast was completely unimpressive. The hotel boasted a sort of "continental breakfast plus," with the usual donuts and muffins but also a hot item and yogurt and cereal. Both days I was there, the hot item was eggs. Also biscuits with no gravy. It looked very unappetizing. The bagels and muffins were very stale. The fruit (tropical fruit like pineapple) was underripe and had flies all over it. The hotel does offer breakfast bags if you are on the go, but I don't know what was in them. Hampton Inns are also supposed to offer warm chocolate chip cookies at the front desk.. the basket was always empty.
On my second day, I lost internet access. After trying every possible option to fix it, I called the front desk for assistance. They gave me an 800-number to call for tech support. The 800-number people told me to call the front desk because it was a local problem and someone at the hotel would have to figure out what it was. When I told the front desk this, they were completely unhelpful. They just didn't care about finding a solution at all. They just seemed to want to "oh well" the situation and hang up. So I went to the lobby to try out the wireless access. That did not work either. I went back to the room and called again. They finally agreed to give me a new cord. This actually worked. But when I returned the bad cord to them, they seemed confused about who I even was. 
I had to call my second night to request a late check-out the next day, which the guest information book said was perfectly OK. I got a very snotty, "Um, I don't think so. Maybe you should call in the morning after some people have checked out so we can even see if we can let you." Click. Now that is what I call great service.
I saved the best for last. I would be remiss if I didn't address the shuttle situation. The hotel offers a free shuttle to and from the airport, and to and from any location downtown within 3 miles. I decided to take advantage of this after a less than thrilling cab ride. Well, the shuttle driver is really something else. She never stopped talking the whole time. I learned that she has 4 sets of twins, the last set born after she got her tubes tied. She is married to the same man she married at 13. The whole shuttle thing was her idea. She didn't offer this information during small talk, she just offered it. She was loud and bawdy, although somewhat entertaining, and showed more guest concern than the front desk attendants. On my last morning, she got into a fight with the front desk because they let a woman who ordered a cab sit there and wait for it for over an hour without noticing and offering the shuttle to her. She also fought with some guests who had requested the shuttle but were late, and kept us all waiting. It was definitely interesting. She also made me wait to go to the airport untill after she finished lunch. She hugged me at the airport.
Finally, upon check-out, the front desk had the right name but wrong address on my form. I pointed this out but they just ignored me.
The bottom line: clean accommodations, amenities leave much to be desired, poor location, and some of the worst service I have ever had at a hotel. This franchise is a disgrace to the Hampton name and needs to get its act together.

title: “Just what we needed!”
text: Boston was a stop-over for our family of five. We had less than 24 hours in the city. The concierge staff at The Colonnade helped me even before we arrived when I called the day before with some logistical issues with timing in our brief stay (getting tickets for a show and how best to get around town). Even as we were approaching Boston by car, I called ahead and the front desk staff was able to arrange an early check in. The room was beautiful, clean, and "just right" for our needs. Breakfast by the pool was delicious and a great experience for the kids. When I find myself back in Boston, The Colonnade will be my home base again (maybe even try to slip away without the kids!) :) Laura from NJ

title: “Clean but old.”
text:
Have stayed at several Crowne Plaza hotels and was not worried about the quality of this hotel since the ones we'd stayed at in the past were beautiful. This is the first time we stayed at this particular one, though, and it was a bit disappointing. 
The pros: Clean bedding/room/bathroom, housekeeping staff was super friendly.
The cons: Pricey (even after booking on hotwire), all ice machines were out of order, the elevators/hotel were outdated.
A few notes: The outside front of the hotel (where you check in) was getting a facelift, which it needed. The construction wasn't a bother at all. The parking lot was lit so it felt safe. The halls going to the room were humid and a little musty smelling but our room was nice/cool/quiet. When I went to get ice the housekeeper told me the machines were all out of order but took my ice bucket to the kitchen to get me some and even brought me more to my room about 30 minutes later. Had a refrigerator in our room that was very cold.
This is a fine place to stay if you're there to sleep. It doesn't have all the newer ammenities of a nicer hotel but is sufficient. We weren't there long enough to check out the bar or pool. Easy access to interstate.

title: “Friendly and helpful staff”
text: I was most impressed by the staff at this hotel, the service was more than I have come to expect at a large chainnhotel. This hotel is located in a part of downtown surrounded by offices, so the "neighborhood" gets very quiet and empty when the business day ends. I had a room with 2 queen beds, it had a decent workspace and enough room to move around comfortably. My room faced in to an open outdoor space, no view for me, but it was quiet.

title: “Not bad for the price I paid”
text:
This hotel is pretty good for the price i paid (100per night). My stay was pretty comfortable though I wish I had a room looking out the street whether then the one with the inner view. I cannot tell the difference between day and night. However, the area is good, it is within walking distance to most sights. 
Pro: 
The internet connections is VERY fast. The area is close to a lot of good restaurants and the inner harbor. The location is also the safest in the area.
Con: 
The breakfast left something to be desire. I am not an early raiser. When I get to the breakfast at 9am (which serve from 6-10), all the hot food (eggs, bacon, hash browns) are already cold. I stayed for 4 nights and for 2 of the nights I was asked for changes from some weird people standing right outside of the hotel.

title: “Awesome hotel-- even better location”
text:
Loved this hotel. 
great location
great rooms -- luxurious--awesome beds--clean--had a suite neat little kitchenette
pull out sofa was terrible instrument of torture, but they brought us a cot which was great
great service
nice little resturant with the best cesear salad we have had in a while

title: “Inexpensive, basic. Very good value.”
text: LOCATION The hotel is not close to anything, so you must have a car. Easy access to I-8 will get you everywhere in the city. PARKING Ample free parking. DESK/CHECK-IN The staff is efficient and friendly. Our reservation, made on the Day's Inn website, was correct on price and room type. ROOM Described as a suite, it is a reasonable size bedroom with attached kitchen. The kitchen has full-size refrigerator, stove and sink plus a microwave. There are plenty of cupboards, all empty - bring your own pans and dishes. The bath is normal size, with plenty of storage and a nice tub/shower. Carpet and tile flooring appear to be newer. Bed and bath linens were all clean and in good condition. Matresses were very comfortable - firm, but not hard. Each bed had 3 pillows of varying firmness. Furniture is older with some wear, but good enough. Ample closet space. Iron and ironing board provided. 25" color TV with lots of cable channels. HEAT-A/C Unit was quiet and digital control kept the room at an even temperature. HOUSEKEEPING Room was very clean on arrival and during our 5-night stay. When the bathroom light burned out, a maintenance man arrived 10 minutes after we reported it. POOL Weather was too cool to try it, but the pool area looked well-maintained. NEIGHBORHOOD The street is almost entirely apartments and condos, so the hotel is quiet in front. There is noticeable traffic noise from the interstate at the back, less so on the sides. Nicolosi's Italian Restaurant next door is very good. Dinners are $12-20, with sandwiches and pizza also available. About a mile north on Waring Road is an Albertson"s supermarket, and also a couple of strip malls. BREAKFAST Free continental breakfast is served in the lobby until 10 AM. Pastries, toast, cold cereal, coffee, juice, milk, and sometimes fresh fruit - that's it. CONCLUSION This place is not fancy. It is clean, comfortable and respectable. It is not in the center of San Diego, but if you are driving all over the city to tourist attractions it doesn't really matter where you start from. The low, low price makes it an outstanding value. We would stay here again.

title: “Avalon Hotel Just OK”
text:
The website is much better than in person.
The rooms do not have carpet and that giives the impression of being cold. There is an odor in the hallways that remind me of my grandmothers apartment, musty. My first night the TV did not work, my co-workers room was smelly from too much air freshener. They did not have the size rooms I booked so 2 out of 3 of us were put in smaller rooms.
All in all, the rooms were clean, they had Aveda soap and shampoo ( which I think is a plus).

title: “pleasantly surprised, secure, comfortable, overwhelmingly wonderful”
text: The hotel was great, the room fantastic and the front desk manager Senedu Hailu was wonderful during check in and went beyond the call of duty on check out. My suitcase had been left behind in the parking lot and i called and she went out after it and "rescued" my belongings. I'm very grateful. In this day and age it's rare to find someone who will do what needs to be done with a "happy" attitude. Please give her my best and tell her to keep up the good work

title: “Warm Repception Absent”
text: I booked my stay in Jury's Boston based on the excellent review posted on trip advisor. It was clean, modern and in great location for shopping and sightseeing, however the staff were extremely rude at times. As the weather was extremely cold and my companion and I were out and about all day on foot we dressed for comfort rather than style. We soon discovered that level of service from staff was dictated by what we were wearing, as we were often ignored and disrepected by some of the staff. It seems we did not fit the image the hotel was hoping to project.
