On one occassion while I was wating in the lobby for my friend I was rudely questioned by female staff member as to why I was sitting in lobby. These experiences made it an uncomfortable stay at times and we got the distinct feeling that we were not wanted in the hotel. We will not be making a return visit to Jury's as we were made to feel like uninvited party guests.

title: “the price is high, but it is Beverly Hills babe!”
text:
I found this hotel very expensive. However, it was worth the money for the location, treatment and ease of stay.
the check-in staff were very friendly; thanking me for being a priority points member - make sure you join these things; they are free and on my holiday here I got lots of perks. (room upgrades, goodies, preferred parking, reduced resort parking rates etc)
If you stay here, you will be pleased by the in-room coffee (I had spent 3 weeks travelling drinking in-room coffee with 'creamer powder', but this hotel give you proper milk. (well, you know the sort in the mini pots but it is better than powder). 
The bathroom is quite small, but the beds and general luxury around make up for that. 
A really enjoyable stay with on-site parking ($22.00) but you expect that in central LA.
Check this one out if you're happy to spend the extra!

title: “regretful experience”
text: First of all, this was probably the worst hotel I've ever stayed at & I travel a lot. Not only was the carpet in the room filthy, but there was vomit on the base of the toilet, the bathroom sink didn't drain & it looked as if there was food, or possibly vomit, blockiing the drain. There was also water in the ice bucket & glasses left from the previous guests & the ice machine was broken on our floor. The hair dryer also did NOT work & the sheets were not fitted, therefore, every time I moved in my bed, the sheet moved with me & exposed the bare mattress. The ONLY positive thing I can say about this hotel is that it's in a good location.

title: “Good experience”
text: Arrived early and was able to check my bags and pre-register. The front desk was helpful and friendly. Room was a little small but nice. Room was on the 43rd floor. Fast elevator ride. Great view of the Saturday night fireworks at the Navy Pier. Comfortable beds.

title: “Does not live up to the hype”
text: Currently staying at Cedarbrook for a dual birthday weekend. Rooms are nothing special - advertised with flat screen tvs - actual small old tv, with horrible sound. Went to bar for drink and to catch a game, and was ignored for nearly 1/2 hour - others came and went, but we had to get up and start to leave before someone took notice. Too busy with a wedding to accommodate regular paying guests apparently.

title: “Awesome Hotel!!”
text: I had the greatest experience at this hotel! The ammenities are incredible and the staff is so accomodating and pleasant, especially Mr. Zeeshan Lakhani. He made sure we had everything we needed and truly added to this wonderful experience. The property is very beautfiul and well kept. I will definitely be coming back, hopefully in the winter time to experience Houston and this hotel during a different season!

title: “Outstanding Place for Mother-Daughter Trip!”
text: I cannot rave enough about the time we had at the Sir Francis Drake. I took my mom there for her 60th bday celebration and they treated us like royalty. Everyone was super helpful, the rooms and decor are very unique, and they have a great location right on Union Square. We didn't really have a lot of price limitations and had tons of options and choices of places to stay, but I am SO glad we stayed here. There is a great breakfast place- Sears- across the street, and they have a Starbucks right on site as well. For anyone considering a similar trip, Hubert Keller's Fleur de Lys is a short walk up the street and totally doable-- even in heels. I travel all the time for work but I really was taken aback at the excellent level of service I received here. I will 100% be coming back!

title: “was surprised, great deal....”
text:
I booked a room on hotwire, $54+ taxes, $66 total for one night, last night, flight was 6am this morning. I stayed at the Coast in Bellvue which is a DUMP so I was expecting the same and was surprised....
this hotel was definitely a good deal, stayed in room #614, it was clean, bathroom was spotless, front desk staff very, very helpful, courtesy ride to the airport on time and the driver was a nice/funny guy. Complimentary breakfast/coffee starts are 5am.
Definitely would recommend this hotel to people needing a room near the airport...also the Roasters Restaurant next door is decent with 26 beers on tap and chicken/mashed potatoes that was good.

title: “best location for times square ( and clean too)”
text:
good clean hotel, very nice inside. This hotel sits in a odd category of very nice and expensive budget hotel. If you have every stayed in a Hilton Garden Inn they are normally the nicest road trip budget hotel in the $100+ range. Sometimes much cheaper depending on location.
The Times square location is probably the best, the cost however matches that of $300+ $400 range.
The hotel however is very clean, all new linens etc. Location is perfect. We arrived into NY at noon for a 2 pm show on Saturday from LaGuardia. We were able to land make it to the hotel, clean up and walk to the show with time to square. If I was on a strict timeline again, this is where i would stay.
cons... expensive like everything else in NYC

title: “Worst of the Worst”
text: We reserved a room at the Lancaster because of a Frommer's recommendation. We realized our mistake immediately by the musty smell and worn 'everything'. We even tried to give them the benefit of the doubt and look at a second room. Terrible. There were holes in the upholstery. A threadbare desk chair. Stains on the walls and floor. I have never seen anything like it. The elevator even stopped working on our way out, and we had to walk down with our luggage. The only amenity they do offer is free wireless internet, which I used to reserve the Four Seasons a few blocks away.

title: “Good Value & handy for The Space Needle”
text:
A good value Travelodge located just outside the Down town Area and just a few minutes walk from The Space Needle and The Seattle Center. The reception staff were welcoming and very efficient, my 2nd Floor room was functional but adequate with a double bed, coffee maker and a.large TV. The bathroom include a shower, toilet and sink though the bathroom door didn't close properly and it tool ages for.the water to heat up. There is a complimentary breakfast and free wi-fi. There is at the time of writing a.lot of road construction work going on nearby.
Overall, good.value for money and i would return.

title: “Would not choose this hotel again.”
text:
We had a reservation for only one night. A couple of weeks earlier we had five nights at the Marriott Marquee. I am just thankful the five nights were at the Marriott. The room was small, bathroom even smaller. The bathroom was smaller than bathrooms on cruise ships. Not a very well lighted room No lights in the dressing area and closet . There was not a coffee maker. We've had many stays at other Hyatts and found them to be much better. 
On the positive side, the bed was comfortable and our room was on the 34th floor so very quiet with the exception of hearing other doors closing. The staff were friendly and helpful. Check in was very quick. The lobby and reception areas were large and lovely so it was a real shock when we opened the door to our room.

title: “Good location”
text: Good location to Civic Center area and walking distance to Union Sqaure. We walked all the way to the Ferry Market but took a cable car back. Hotel rooms are small but with high ceilings. Feels old but iit's clean. Our guide book said flat screen tv's in all rooms but ours wasn't even close. Price for this city is a steal. Sam's Diner across the street is a gem. Home cooked food, simple and well priced.

title: “A NICE STAY PERFECT LOCATION”
text: Just got back from a 4 nite stay at the Helmsley,this hotel is in the perfect location for New york,with central park right across the road,and times square a short walk away,the hotel lobby is clean and classy,felt like walking into New york in the 50,s which is not a bad thing,the room we had was dated but i felt it could have been a little cleaner,marks up the wall and stained carpet but don't let this put you off i,m fussy,Go for a drink at harry,s bar a great start to the nite or a nice end to a evening shuts around 12.30-1.00,the drinks seem a little pricy,but your in New York,the bar staff make you feel very welcome,did not eat at the hotel so cannot comment on the food,but if your looking for a reasonable priced hotel on 5th Avenue i would choose the Helmsley for the price we paid for a 4 nite stay,would i go back,yes it is the hotel that as the perfect location.

title: “Stay in the newer tower.”
text: Comfortable rooms. Would not recommend the breakfast.

title: “The Best Value for My Money Ever!!!”
text:
We were two couples and expecting at least a room that would fit our four large bags. We got this and much more!!! First, the place is brand new (opened two weeks before our arrival!). The bathroom was big enough to everyone unpack our toiletteries. The room service was very good too. And the breakfast, excellent for a complementary thing in a two double bed room for just US$ 175 / per night, tax included. The best thing was the extremely comfy beds - a God gift to someone who was walking 12 hours a day!
The best thing is the location. The price would be excellent even the hotel was old and dirty, ´cause the location couldn’t be better. It is located between 8th and 9th av. At the 9th, just around the corner, there are plenty of restaurants - inexpensive ones. We took a cab at Meat Packing District and in less than 10 min. we were in front of the hotel for US$ 7.00.
At the corner of 8th, there is a subway station (Penn Station) and by the end of the next block lays the center of Times Square! At that this corner is the Minskoff Theater, were "The King Lion" Broadway play is been performed.
One can spend a couple of days just on the surroundings of the hotel (10 blocks away - Times Square, Rockefeller Center, Empire State Building, Bryant Park, Grand Central Station, the best of 5th av, the best of 34th st, etc).

title: “Great place for so less!!!!!!!”
text: I stayed based upon my friends suggestion. This place is great for such a low price. The rooms are very small and this is the only disadvantage. But I spent my time at room only for sleeping and getting ready. I would highly recommend this place for anyone who is not having lots of luggage to carry on.

title: “Very nice new hotel”
text: Stayed here three nights on business. The rooms are brand new, very modern. I had a room facing the parking garage which was sunny and had a huge window. The modern lighting, plenty of outlets for all the stuff I needed to plug in and very comfy bed. The desk was very nicely laid out and functional. Close to LOTS of restaurants. Parking is $17/day selfpark or about $25 for valet parking. I only had two complaints: the conference rooms were FREEZING, and the entire conference area has TERRIBLE cellular coverage. The meeting rooms were DEADZONES and ran all of our smart phones dead searching for service. You could stand near the windows in the front to "catch" a cell, but that was it. Otherwise a GREAT experience.

title: “Attentive Staff!”
text: As a professional speaker I visit many hotels and event facilities, and have used this facility for various seminars. The staff has always been GREAT; very service oriented. In particular, I would like to mention Anthony Montoya. He has always been the person helping me keep the seminar running smoothly by providing exceptional customer service, and attention to detail during the event. He obviously takes great pride in his work. Thanks Anthony!!!

title: “Pleased for the Price”
text: After needing to make a last minute hotel change the night before traveling to DC, I booked a room through Priceline for $175 a night. Somewhat leary of a two-star hotel, I was pleasantly surprised by the decent quality of the room. The service was professional, friendly, and helpful. Our room was quite large and included a small kitchenette. The walk from the metro was an easy 6 minutes and other shopping/restaurants were close by also. While some hotels may be somewhat closer to the mall, this really was a good deal for the location and quality.

title: “Great Hotel!!!”
text: This is a great hotel... very clean, rooms are spacious, beds are comfortable. Good selection for breakfast (I recommend you a buy a package that includes breakfast cause it can be a little expensive otherwise, but it's worth it). The gentleman serving breakfast was very nice and professional... he went out of his way to serve everybody there. It's rare to have such friendly and quality service nowadays. We had a very enjoyable stay. I recommend this hotel. There are quite a bit of restaurants and businesses near by.

title: “Small room, hip people, great value”
text: Stayed one night in a small but comfortable room in the new tower. Walked in to Champagne, woke up to the New York Times, enjoyed the free hot drinks, and found the experience a great value ( booked via Expedia at less than $175). The Aveda bath products made up for any of the imperfections in the room! And my wife and I thoroughly enjoyed the very comfortable bed. Anyone who thinks this place is a dump has never stayed in many New York City hotels....No Dump here; great mid-town location with parking next door and the subway around the corner....

title: “Almost a homerun.”
text:
Stayed overnight at the Silversmith this weekend. We were very pleased with the room and the property itself. It was a great value, and if it wasn"t December in Chicago, we woould have taken more advantage of it't great location. Staff was mostly very helpful.
The room was spare but comfortable, very large, high ceilings and great bathroom. We were thankful the room was in the back of the building, becauuse the El runs on Wabash. The only complaint about the room was the pillows, which seemd to have been scrounged off a sofa. Small, hard and square. Not at all what I wouold have expected.
The only other issue was the valet parking fee quoted by Hoetels.com was 50% less than the actual charge by the hotel. Explanations were not satisfactory for the discrepancy.
All said however, I would go back and take my own pillow.

title: “Convenient and comfortable, inside and out”
text: The location was very convenient. Had appetizers in the bar on the first night - delicious. Outside seating area is beautiful for eating, meeting or relaxing with a beautiful view of the golf course. The restaurant was good for both breakfast and dinner and also used one of the conference rooms. The room was comfortable and well appointed. Though I could see planes landing at LAX - I did not hear an airplane - good sound insulation.

title: “Caruso still carousing in the corridors”
text: Stayed at the Palace for a convention in April 2006. It is just a few blocks from the Moscone Center, and pleasantly situated for a stroll to the shops around Union Square, or to take the Powell line Cable Car halfway to the stars up Nob Hill. (Don't miss the stained glass in Grace Cathedral up on California St in Nob Hill, by the way!) The Palace room was comfortable and clean, and the staff were helpful. Being a conventioneer, I always dined elsewhere, so cannot comment on the food. At night however there were some singing patrons who strolled the corridors at 1-2am going back to their rooms (I guess) - perhaps I even heard strains of the great Enrico Caruso (who was staying at the Palace when the 1906 Earthquake struck). Neverthless, I could have done with the sleep! This time, I didn't try the hotel pool - but was impressed with it last time I stayed here a few years back.

title: “Small but nice, clean and lovely”
text:
We live in DC, and just wanted a quick getaway from the kids for our anniversary. I wanted to be in Georgetown... and I wanted to park the car and walk everywhere. Plus - I wanted a the hotel to have a special feeling (not that antiseptic Courtyard Marriott feel).
There are only 3 hotels in Georgetown: The Rizt Carlton, the Four Seasons, and the Latham. Since the Latham was less than 1/2 the price of the other two... we gave it a try.
And it was very nice: small rooms, but clean. Tastefully decorated. Certainly not the Ritz.... but it still felt special. The linens were above normal... tho the foam pillows were hard. The staff was friendly and helpful. 
I was concerned because there were some poor reviews of the Latham, but frankly, we had a very nice stay - even if it was only 18 hours!
One note: the hotel on site is Michel Richard's Citronelle. It is not your typical hotel restaurant. It is one of the highest rated (and most pricey) restaurants in DC... perfect for a special occasion and wonderful dinner. But if you think you can drop in for a quick burger, it is not the place to be.

title: “Great location,better customer service”
text:
The Edison is a top value choice. The rates are lower than most NY City hotels and the hotel is steps from Times Square.Our room was in very good condition and well maintained by the maid service.The staff of the hotel was exceptional and treated us more like guests than customers.
We plan on staying at The Edison on our next trip to New York City.

title: “Overrated”
text:
My husband and I decided, last minute, to make a short trip to New York. And due to the fantastic location, we decided to stay at the St. Regis.
The good:
*The stuff is amazingly helpful and friendly.
*The St. Regis Bentley is a fantastic perk and the driver is super nice.
*The location is top notch.
*Bathrooms are gorgeous.
*Rooms are large.
The bad:
*Rooms are old and dilapidated. 
*Initially we were put in a room on the 3rd floor, facing a parking garage. The carpet had seen better days and the desk was completely thrashed. Despite the large size the room felt claustrophobic so we asked to be moved to a cleaner/newer room.
*Second room had a better view (19th floor) but was also old and scratched up. 
The bottom line:
This particular property cannot hold a candle to the St. Regis in San Francisco! And at the rates this property charges, they should (at the very least) compete with their less expensive properties in terms of their accommodations. Some serious renovations are in order before I'll stay here again.

title: “Family friendly - very nice stay”
text:
We had a very nice stay at the Embassy Suites Washington DC over our spring break back in April. 
- Pricing seemed very fair for an in-city hotel 
- Had plenty of amenities to keep everyone happy 
- Indoor pool was nice for the kids and in very good shape
- Happy hour with free drinks and appetizer type food was great
- Overall hotel seemed to be very clean. The indoor atrium, fountains and waterfalls were very nice.
- Don't forget they feed the fish twice a day...kids loved that!
- No parking at hotel when we stayed. Ended getting a cheaper rate a block down at the Ritz which Embassy has a deal with. A very easy walk to get the car when needed, and felt fairly secure. 
- Close to subway stations, light shopping, and restaurants
Staff seemed friendly and accessible. Room was kept clean. Overall a great stay, and would certainly stay again next time we are in DC.

title: “Great Location, decent Hotel, Good Service”
text: We were a group of 6 friends from work who were looking at a hotel around LAX airport area and can accomodate in 2 rooms. This was the perfect place as the hotel rooms are pretty spacious and the hotel is well located with regular bus services from airport which is complimentary. The hotel also arranged a day trip to San Diego for us right from the door step. Budget Car rental and Burger King is bang opposite the hotel which are good options to have for a traveller.

title: “Seeing Dr. at Tufts”
text: We had to have some tests done at Tufts so we stayed at the Ramada. The rooms were very clean and I don't think I have seen a nicer staff of workers than here. They were helpful when reserving shuttle times to and from the hospital. The food at the onsite restaurant was amazing. We will be staying here again.

title: “Another great saty!”
text:
Second time here and we will definitely be back!
Awesome staff...from bell man to concierge...Arrived really early-8am- and the room was ready!!!perfect after a 9plus hour flight! Also got an upgrade to a Catherhal view!
Super location..and the complimentary car to Broadway shows is really handy!
Confortable, safe, clean...great beds and bathroom.
Only downside is the automatic minibar and no space to store a bottle of water...but not really a big matter!

title: “Great value for Manhattan”
text: I stayed here over the Christmas break, and it was a wonderful property for $170/night for two double beds, which is quite good for Manhattan. Upon arriving, I parked at the off site parking next door and checked in. The lobby was well appointed, with a breakfast buffet at the back, which serves yogurt, bagels, fruit, and cereal, and coffee is available 24/7. The area gets VERY crowded after 8 am so I would advise going early, or getting the food and eating somewhere else. The rooms have comfortable beds, and are of adequate size, and have wired internet, which was OK, but wifi would have been better. Staff were attentive and friendly, and the night manager personally tried to correct a problem with the internet connection I was having in my room.

title: “I'd rather have been in a Motel 8”
text: Booked a suite for a romantic weekend to celebrate our anniversary. The room they gave us had ripped carpet, poorly equipped kitchette, cigarette burns in the carpet and smelled horrible. They then sprayed the carpet with freshner but that only burned our eyes. Could not give us another suite nor would make other arrangements. The manager admitted she would not want to stay in that room. They eventually moved us to a standard room that had been updated, but the mood was lost and the trip a disaster.

title: “Business became leisure”
text: Admittedly, I'm slightly biased to the Brown Palace being a Colorado resident and knowing the history and quality of the hotel and its staff. I've stayed once as a personal treat and most recently while attending a conference for work, and have been equally impressed on both occasions. The staff are always pleasant, knowledgeable, kind, and willing to help. The restaurants supply good food (inside or room service) and a well trained staff. The Ship's Tavern is the hotel's only casual restaurant and is often extremely busy, but the food and atmosphere is worth the wait and hectic staff. I have had the good fortune to go to the Spa as well and have enjoyed the experience. Honestly, I travel for business frequently and rarely rely in multiple diamond ratings and other awards as I am often am disappointed by these well-ranked, highly priced hotels, choosing to stay at less costly hotels because the arrogance is minimized and I am frugal with the corporate dollar. But, as a Colorado resident, I can proudly say that the Brown Palace is the exception to the rule (even if jeans are frowned upon if dining or having high tea/brunch in the lobby) and I recommend treating yourself and a loved one for at least one night if you are ever in Denver. Just remember to take the tour - you'll never forget it!

title: “fine, but trying WAY too hard”
text: The hotel is fine. It's clean and the rooms are comfortable. The service was good. HOWEVER, if you like to enjoy the ambiance of the place you stay and you don't like places that are trying WAY too hard to be SUPER cool and trendy...then you might not want to stay here. The hotel is dedicated to trying to be the most cute and trendy place I have ever seen...yet it doesn't succeed at it in any way, shape, or form. Each floor is themed...some reviewers think this is fun...I think it's really annoying. Our floor was the "Laugh Out Loud" floor...so when we got off the elevator, the elevator talks to you and it says, "Floor 7, the Laugh Out Loud floor. Hahahahahah!!!" I didn't really think that was funny or cute...so you can imagine the other floors with similar themes. The artwork on the walls included such "funny" things as framed whoopi cushions. It didn't make me laugh out loud...except for the fact that I found it hilarious how hard the hotel was trying. Our alarm clock is a yellow convertible VW beetle. I'll stop there...but, again, the place is fine and we didn't pay that much to stay here, but it's definitely not a place I would be excited to stay at again...

title: “Bathroom size”
text:
Overall stay was nice, but bathroom was small and cramped. Bed was pretty good, but don't 
like the new small puffy pillow concept hotels have adopted.

title: “Won't stay at any other hotel”
text: My husband and I attend the Supercross race in Indy. every year. Our first year we stayed at the Hyatt. The noise from the hotel stair way, loby, etc..., was unreal! From that year on we have stayed at the Westin! You can not believe the difference! The rooms are very nice, counter service is perfect, room service is wonderful. Everything is very updated and comforting!!! The hotel has access to the RCA Dome without walking outdoors (also to the Circle Center Mall). I liked this place so much I had my company book a company meeting here. We reserved 25 rooms and everyone was talking about how they were going to stay at this hotel from now on! It is WELL worth every penny!!!

title: “Great Location - Tired Hotel”
text:
Really enjoyed the 22nd floor and the spectacular view from my room. The entire hotel feels a little tired and dated. The lobby is sort of "art deco" and nothing really says "ta da" welcome to San Antonio. The restaurant is really good but again it's very dated and boring as far as decor is concerned. They have those sad single cup coffee makers in the room (who thought of those things anyhow??). Tried to scam me with $3.75 US VIP water for my consumption in the room (very small print indicates will be added to my room bill). Went down the hall to ice machine and saw that bottled water is in the vending machine for $2.00. Room service will add 21% to your bill if ordered. Great internet connection. Great beds. Great TV. Great for a business trip. Although there was a significant stain on the carpet, the room was fine. Again, very dated and perhaps a serious renovations should be considered. But because of the recession, doubt this will happen. Their sister hotel Marriott River Centre was way better as far as being more updated and welcoming and they are also immediately on the Riverwalk.
Walking along the Riverwalk was awesome although the noise from the Olympic revelers kept me awake one night (Go Canada Go!) Picked up some great gifts at the Five and Dime toward Madd Doggs British Pub (cheap drinks - tequila $4.00 on ice some nights - watch for the specials) try to get in Amy's section at Madd Doggs - she goes the extra mile. The cashier from the Five and Dime allowed me to take his photo to post on trip advisor - really helpful fellow. Go and tell him you saw him on Trip Advisor - he's terrific! 
Great service at the Riverwalk but it's time to sell or upgrade.

title: “Ok if you're without your wife”
text:
I know my way around SF, so didn't mind a stay in this neighborhood. I cashed in my Choice Hotel points for my 2 night stay.
Location is a 10 minute walk from BART. It's one block west of Van Ness, a major north/south street. Busses everywhere.
Office to check in a tiny. You walk across a driveway to an even smaller elevator. It's smaller than those tiny elevators you see in Europe. 
The motel looks like a motor court. It also looks like a homeless shelter. Lots of in and out types moving about throughout the overnight hours. Very noisy for a place with all outside entrances to rooms.
The room:
Small and clean (surprise surprise). Even the bathroom was ok (for a Rodeway). With the lights turned on in the evening, and the curtains drawn, you'd think you were at a Quality Inn or Holiday Inn Express.
A few blocks east of the hotel, on Polk, eat at Brendas. ANyplace that has a line in this foodie city, has got to be good. Brendas is southern style, for breakfast and lunch. I met a friend for breakfast.
Ok. The big question. Would I go back? No.
Next time I'll priceline a 3* for $60.00.

title: “Good place to stay!”
text: We enjoyed our stay and the breakfast was good. The dining area was well maintained by a friendly staff.

title: “Has turned into a dangerous dump!!!”
text: We have stayed there numerous times before and enjoyed it; however, this time were set up right by the main pool area with bands and screaming for hours; ate at the buffet at the Cascades for $50 for 4 people for what you'd get at a cheap picnic. While attempting to retrieve my grandsons' clothing from the pool after eating the dinner, my son was assaulted by a drunk with the security staff then asking my room number in front of this group of drunks. If that wasn't enough with my heart condition, we were then subjected to the phone ringing non-stop for over 30 minutes beginning at 5:30 a.m., before having "security" knock on the door because we didn't answer a wake-up call we never placed! One of the most unenjoyable weekends we ever spent. The Pointe at Tapatio Cliffs has become a disgrace to the Hilton name.

title: “A pleasant stay”
text: We have been staying at this hotel over the years when we go to visit our children in DC. We have enjoyed its convenient location and reasonable price. Now the accommodations have been improved; but the price seems less reasonable than it did previously (with parking costing extra as well).

title: “Hidden Jewel”
text: I was a bit nervous after booking The Whitehall on one of those "you don't know where you're staying until after you pay" Web sites, but we thorougly enjoyed staying there. The room was upscale, clean and comfortable; the hotel's smaller size did not bother us and and its location put us right in the middle or close to Chicago's great shopping, restaurants and theatre district. The staff was wonderful! It's a hidden jewel just a block away from Michigan Ave. and we plan to return.

title: “Very Friendly Staff”
text: My husband and I stayed here for one night. The associate at the front desk (Gustavo Gomez) was very helpful and upgraded our room due to our Starwood Preferred Guest status. The hotel was clean, the staff very friendly, and prices fair (well... comparable to everything else). You can work out at the Bally's across the way, which was a nice little bonus for being a guest.

title: “Comfort indeed”
text:
We were obliged to stay at Comfort because a bigger hotel chain screwed up our booking. The place was most reasonable with excellent accommodation that exceded our expectations. The room was immaculate well laid out with wi-fi flat screen tv and rasteful furniture. There was a comfortable seating area within the room which also served as a worspace. 
The breafkfast which was included was most comprehensive and filling. I am glad we missed out on th more expensive big brother hotel and would give Comfort serious consieration in future

title: “Comforable”
text: Enjoy my a romantic stay at "The Roosevelt" My boyfriend and I found it very comfortable and cozy . The bed was cozy and headboard sturdy . Location was great as well close to some of NYC best restaurants an attractions. Was a great NYC romantic vacation.

title: “Great Priceline Stay”
text:
I had my doubts about this hotel due to all of the negative reviews, but I have about decided that the majority of people who post to tripadvisor.com are either perpetual pessimists or people who are used to exemplary accomodations wherever they go. I have stayed at a number of hotels that have been poorly reviewed on this site and never had a bad experience at any of the ones I've ended up staying at. 
As for the Westin Bonaventure, for $60-$70 per night, this place is awesome. Yes, the parking is high, but with a priceline rate, you're still staying in downtown LA for under $100/night. That's pretty good. 
One warning--be careful if you check in late. The Westin garage is full every night and if you are not a hotel guest who has managed to get in earlier in the day, they will send you across the street to park, which is $50/night. Try to get there early or pick your rental car up when you can park it early in the day. Once you get your car registered with them, you can get in even if the sign says the garage is full.
Yes, the rooms are a bit on the small side, but for a couple, this poses no issues--at least not for us. The rooms are well appointed, and the bath was bigger than the larger Westin room we stayed in out at the airport before we left. We had a room on the 30th floor with fabulous views, great air conditioning and a heavenly bed! Housekeeping was great, and everyone we dealt with was courteous.
The location is totally convenient--a good section of downtown with super-easy freeway access. Room service was surprisingly good, the brew pub had decent food, though service was a bit slow, and there are a ton of food options to choose from in the area, so you aren't stuck with hotel priced meals. It's a walkable area, at least during the day and early evening. 
The pool is fine, with big fluffy Westin towels, but keep in mind it is a "rooftop" pool and a bit on the small side. Also, wear your flip-flops--the concrete gets hot and is pretty sooty from being 5 stories above downtown and near a freeway. Not a luxurious pool by any means, but kind of cool to lay out and look up at the surrounding skyscrapers.
We had quick and easy check-in and out, and while our experience with the concierge wasn't the warmest, he was efficient and courteous. This hotel is enormous and busy--I'm sure they do their best.
Bottom line, the hotel is convenient, more than comfortable, and if you get a decent rate, you should have no cause for complaint. in addition, this hotel has been in a ton of movies, so you'll probably recognize it. It's a very LA experience!

title: “Had higher expectations for the W”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the W for the weekend. We booked the reservation through hotwire. The staff was friendly when we arrived. They accommodated my request for a south facing room to avoid the WTC construction. The room, a corner room, which I think is supposedly a bit bigger than their average room still seemed small even for NY standards. Even though the hotel is new, there was something about it that just didn't quite meet my expectations for a 4.5 star. There were pencil markings on the wall, looked like lines drawn for leveling the headboard I guess from when the bed was installed. There were a few patches on the wall, the room and the pillows had a light odor..like there had been a wet dog there before or someone had smoked in it.
The location, while I knew it was not a lively area I did not realize it would be as sleepy as it was. A bit of hike to the areas North (the Village) where the vibe is a little more exciting and there are interesting places to shop, eat and drink. I never ate or drank at the hotel but I did try to get a drink of water from the bar when we got home Saturday night (12:00/12:30ish) but it was closed. I asked the front desk if I could get some water or if there was a vending machine. I was informed that there was no vending machine but that there was some place on each floor that dispensed water, I found the ice maker, but not the water [maybe I misunderstood]. Water was available in the room for a $8 bottle but I was unwilling to fork over that much mula for H2O.

title: “NASTY PLACE in need of Repairs”
text: Looks great from the outside but, wait til you get into the room. The window had crack in it and they put tae on it. The wall had MOLD on them and stains too. The bathroom had a big water stain around the light and shower tube cieling is falling in. The bedspread was stained with bleach so, I gues the washer here does work. We set in the lobby and a guy came in to complain that a part on his car was stolen and desk clerk said it happens when you leave your car, not our problem. Now I am real concerned about tonight and our car outside. I will say that the pool was nice and warm and that was relaxinging. The brakfast was not a regular comfort inn style but, it was fine. I would say next time, ask to see a room before you check in cause this was not worth the price.

title: “Tired and lacking service!”
text: This hotel has no idea what service is! Just try to order breakfast . Rooms are small and in need of an update. Our room was not what we consider clean, trash still in wastebasket when we arrived. Lacking comfortable furniture and definitely no views of outside from the room. Great neighborhood and that is we're it ends. This would be a great hotel,if they would step it up and update the rooms and offer the service we deserve for the price we pay!! Our room still had packing paper around the chair legs,talk about details !

title: “Excellent stay!”
text:
We visited Washington for the weekend a decided to stay at St Regis because of the location and usually ok standards at SPG.
We where so right.
The sevice was impecable,when we arrived we immediately felt at home,great atmosphere and high professionalism by the team at Regis.
We arrived at the front desk and discovered that our agent mispelled my name so I took a while for retrieving our reservation,we where immediately upgraded,got a complementary drink while waiting.
The rooms are reasonably small but very efficient with great decoration and high quality standards.
Highy recommeded and looking forward to our next stay at a St Regis!

title: “A fabulous 2 nights!!”
text: I can't praise this hotel enough--from the kind employee that let me check in at 10:30am (I was sooo exhausted after a 15 hr train ride) to the doorman that disappeared w/my bags--EVERYONE was super kind and accommodating!! The room was huge--a large bath w/separate shower and HEAVENLY beds!!! Also a fantastic view!! The elevator system was unique but FAST!! The location was perfect--walking distance to everything!!

title: “Thoughtfull Hospitality”
text: We stayed at the Hotel Commonwealth last weekend as a getaway, an opportunity to experience the pleasures of Boston without any of the hassles. Our experience at the hotel was first rate in every way. Prior to our arrival we had made some inquiries regarding entertainment at the nearby House of Blues. The next thing you know the concierge from that facility was in contact with us to offer assistance. On arrival night we were able to call down and quickly get a seat at the very busy Eastern Standard downstairs, perfect. Our room was quiet as a vault with one of the most comfortable beds ever. Everyone we encountered from begining to end was eager to offer assistance in a genuine way. We appreciate that. We have stayed at many Hotels in Boston but can clearly see why this one is rated so well.

title: “Big Disappointment”
text: We chose this place for the night after we got married. The website reservation form said "Harbor View." In our room, a brick wall faced the harbor, and our window faced other rooms! We asked to change rooms and they said they would get back to us, but never did. The heater was a cheap electric room unit: noisy but still left the room cold. The bathroom was like something out of a cheap $29 motel. They also tried to tack on a bogus $5 "connectivity fee" that was never listed in the internet price. The only positives were the full box of Godiva chocolates, and a good breakfast, but those didn't justify the extremely high price. If you want to be on the Inner Harbor, try another place.

title: “Amazing Service but New Technology and Deocor are a Miss”
text:
I stayed at the Bel Air Hotel right before it closed for renovations, and sadly they made it worse.
The Good News
The service is perfection, like nothing I have ever seen, training at its best. They make it so easy and exceeded my expectations. Luckily they did not mess with the grounds during the renovations because they are still a jewel, but parts are a little run down. 
The Bad News
The Decor - Whoever designed the interior of the lobby clearly designed this in a vacuum in London and I would guess never even saw the property. The grounds of the property are warm, quaint and special. The cold black and white styling is objectively the wrong fit for this space. The interior should be like an urban San Ysdrro Ranch with warmth. Sadly all the soft goods need to be redone at once, maybe they should call Ty Warner. The interior is so cold, depressing and out of place it almost ruins the entire resort. 
Our Room and Technology - We had a regular room with Patio, the Patio was much larger than our room. The finish out was superb, the only problem was our room was way to small for the size of the furniture. It is rare that I would advocate more room for lower finish out cost but larger, but these rooms are just too small, maybe they should in close the worthless patios. 
Technology can be a game changer when it is done perfectly like Apple has shown. I think Microsoft consulted on their technology because it is really bad. The Ipad program crashes 10 times in a row before it works properly each time you use it. The lighting system is delayed and will drive you nuts. The wort part is the bang and olsen remote, it is really confusing and is not intuitive at all, these tv's need to be replaced asap. The pay per view movie system is hard to use because of the remote and the selection of movies is very limited. 
So I am mixed, I love the grounds and the service is the best, but it is just not the special place it once was.

title: “Great Location, Find A Good Deal”
text:
We only were in San Fran for a night, and chose to stay at Hotel Frank. Hopefully anyone reading this is fairly web savvy because it will pay off. I was contacted by Personality Hotels on Twitter when I announced I was looking for a hotel deal, and offered a deal better than anything on their website and some extra perks. We had our dog with us, and were left treats for her and a nice personal note from the marketing girl who booked our room for us. We stayed in a junior suite which was plenty big, even with our dog crate. The bathroom was beautiful, very spa-like and the bed was super comfy! 
We did have to haul all our stuff to our room ourselves when we first got there, but service got better over the weekend, and we had better help when we were leaving the hotel. Honestly, for the deal we got, this hotel far surpassed my expectations, I would stay there again anytime. Just don't eat at the sushi place across the street.

title: “The windows ARE soundproof!”
text:
We enjoyed our "view room" on the 36th floor. In the middle of Times Square, I was skeptical about not being bothered by noise. It was quiet except for some sirens from police traffic. Coming from someone who is very sensitive to noise, must say the room was very quiet and the location interesting. We could enjoy all the commotion of Times Square from our perch on the sofa by the window, as it was in the 20 degree range outside. 
This top of the line Marriott, so don't be surprised at the prices of food and beverages. The rooftop restaurant is a must see even if you are not staying here. Just have $$$$$!

title: “Really a Hilton?”
text: Not clean, poor maintenance, overpriced, air circulation issues. They say this is newly renovated, but my room must have been missed.

title: “It is a steal!”
text: Stayed here 3 weeks ago with friends on our first pleasure visit to Chi town. Could not have been more pleased with the cleanliness, hospitality, and best of all, prime location of this Marriott property. Even the complimentary breakfast was really delicious. You can easily walk to pretty much anything. Make sure to book a reservation at the Rosebud Steakhouse right across the street. Will definitely stay here during our next visit.

title: “Not impressed”
text: If you want to go to a game at Fenway, this hotel is OK. Prices will sky rocket during games. I would never choose this hotel again when traveling to Boston. Service was poor!

title: “Frequent visitor”
text: I just returned from my fifth stay at this hotel and as usual it was a wonderful experience. My daughter goes to college in D.C. which gives me the oppportunity to visit several times a year. I love everything about this hotel. The location is amazing, the rooms are beautiful and the staff is friendly and extremely helpful. I recommend that you book a room facing the courtyard. The view is pretty and the rooms are very quiet. I really can't say enough about this hotel as an overall perfect place to stay in D.C.

title: “Rooms okay, but Noisy”
text: I had high expectations after reading the reviews and I'm afraid my experience at this hotel didn't quite match up. It's extremely noisy. Lots of street noise as well as noise from the families trampling up and down the hallways. The rooms are very clean and fairly well appointed. The staff is also very friendly. The food at the free breakfast is not good at all, so that was a disappointment. There is a shuttle that's part of the Anaheim trolley system and it picks up in front of the hotel every 25 minutes. This property would be good for large families who need a suite style room and don't mind the considerable noise.

title: “Great location”
text: A very good hotel - missed the entrance for dropping bags off and the car park a couple of times! Our room overlooked the back of Beale Street (we now wished we got a room with balcony so we could hear the music) as our window didn't open. The rooms are spotless and beautifully decorated. The Hotel is very safe (key card for entrance when it got late and key card for the lifts). breakfast was also good. I would stay here again.

title: “Fantastic staff”
text: The hotel was clean and the staff very friendly. They went out of their way and very amusing. The rooms are compact but interestingly furnished. The bed was extremely comfortablel and the bedding lovely and clean. Only downside is it can be noisy outside at night.

title: “2 Night Stay-Very Nice”
text: We stayed here 2 nights for my son's graduation. It is a very nice hotel. I got it for approx. half price on Hotwire. Check-in went quickly, room was very clean. Close to public transportation. No complaints.

title: “A little disappointed”
text: I was very excited to stay at this hotel but left feeling a little disappointed. Our room was nice but very small and there wasn't a lot of space to store our luggage. The bathroom was extremely small which made getting ready difficult. The beds are very firm and even though we booked 6 months in advance, we were given a room with two beds which we did not need. The rooftop pool is TINY and freezing cold. It was a very hot day but I could not swim as it was way too cold! The lifts are frustrating- they take forever! The staff were friendly and we did enjoy having gossip girl cocktails in the cosy lounge but I think there are better hotels in NYC.

title: “Great price, nice new room”
text:
I stayed a night on 6/28. When I tried to check in the small lobby was filled with bags and there was barely any room to stand. I proceeded to the SPG line and was told that no rooms were ready (this was 2:00 p.m.). Not a big deal since checkin wasn't until later. The woman at the front desk wasn't too friendly and seemed overwhelmed by all of the baggage in the lobby. I asked the front desk attendant to hold our bags and we came back around 6:00 p.m. and were able to check in. 
My room was on the 27th floor (the SPG floor) and had a view of the roof of Port Authority. The room was clean, new, and had a very comfy bed. The curtains didn't close properly, so we woke up very early the next morning due to all of the sunlight. The rooms have an iHome iPod dock/clock radio, but it didn't work.
The elevators were dirty and made the worst creeking noises. We didn't have time to check out the gym. When I asked about upgrades, I was told that the suites were still under construction.
As others have mentioned, this hotel isn't on the nicest block in the city. While it's not unsafe, it is unsavory with adult DVD stores and homeless people flanking the entrance.
I would stay here again as the hotel was affordable, convenient, and clean.

title: “My first hotel choice in NY”
text: This is always my choice when going to NY for the theater as it is within easy walking distance of all the theaters and too many restaurants to name. The Concierge Lounge is perfect to relax and enjoy the view. Speaking of the view, be sure and go to the revolving lounge (about the 44th floor) for dinner or even just a drink as the view is well worth the 1 drink minimum. There is no cover charge if you are staying in the hotel.

title: “Convienent One Night Stay”
text:
Advantages: nice views of Boston harbor, shuttle to Logan airport, clean rooms and bathrooms, easy check-in
Dsadvantage: even though it looks like the location is centralized, you have to take the subway to downtown Boston. this is the only reason I gave 4 stars instead of 5 stars.

title: “Clean rooms, quiest...will stay again”
text:
I was attending a conference at the JW Marriott and stayed at the Candlewood Suites.
The rooms were clean and good sized. The fitness center was nice to get a quick workout in. The WiFi was good speed, which is a plus for business customers. The area has quite a few food options within walking distance. It was a quiet hotel and the beds were comfortable.
I would definitely recommend the hotel.

title: “Location, Location, Location!!!”
text: This hotel was excellent from the moment we walked in with its seaside decor charm to how well maintained it seemed to be! Please be warned it cost us $61 additional (for 2 days) to park at the hotel! New cost to us travelers! The beds were ummmm....."very firm", but we still slept well!! And this is a pet friendly hotel and while we never smelled any pets, there was the constant and undeniable smell of pet odor remover everywhere! So just be warned! For a one night stay this was perfect though! Only one block away from the Red Line Subway station that took us straight to Wrigley Field (which was our main reason for our trip)! And only a few blocks away from the "Magnificent Mile"! Also Walgreen's is on the same corner and super convenient!

title: “Great location, great rooms”
text: They are located in midtown - just a 10 minute walk to the Garden, 2 minutes to Herald Square. The hotel is very nice. The rooms are ok sized for NYC, but they are spotless and very updated. Hotel breakfast was VERY good -- lots of choices. Great family or business destination. Front desk was helpful, except when we were checked into the wrong room, but that's incidental. No bar, but there is one right next door in a restaurant.

title: “Great accommodation for all the family”
text: We stayed here for 4 nights at the beginning of our five week USA holiday. Traveling with three boys aged 21, 12 and 11 this hotel had everything we could have hoped for. It was beautifully positioned on the marina with the yaghts outside our door. The room was well maintained and the staff were very friendly and accomodating. Our boys had access to the pool and wonderful spa (both heated). We tend to use the hotel as a base and come and go as we please and this hotel was an easy walk to shopping facilities and some restaurants. However if we wanted more, it was only a short drive to the city. Overall it was a fantastic place and we wish we could have stayed longer.

title: “Had a great stay”
text: Recently spent 4 nights at this hotel. Staff were very helpful and always available. Hotel is very clean with nice size rooms for NYC standards. Location was perfect for visiting Times Square, Macy's and other attractions. Roof top bar is great as well. Will return on my next visit.

title: “Superb find - Excellent unbeatable location”
text:
Our first visit into the city of New York and have to say that staying here at this brilliant hotel made our vislt to this fabulous city all the more enjoyable. Quiet street in the best of locations. ALL the staff we met were superb, very polite and could not have been more helpful. Free internet 24 hrs a day, complimentary coffee and tea in the lounge area, free use of the gym and great complimentary hot breakfast, lots of seating outside on the patio area. We stayed here for 4 nights and could not have been more happy with our choice of hotel. Within walking distance of all the major attractions close to Macy's, Madisson Square Garden, Empire State building, (view from our bedroom window), Chrysler Building. Grand Central station, Times Square, and both the underground and Penn Station. Loads of places to eat nearby. We walked from the hotel to Central Park and to the other end of the island to the 9/11 memorial and Staten Island Ferry.
Twin and double rooms avaialble all with en suites which have baths and showers and complimentary toiletries available should you forget something, wi-fi in all rooms good quality beds and tv's.
We caught the airtrain from JFK airport to Jamaica, last stop on the airtrain at the airport and then the Long Island Rail Road train from Jamaica Hub to Penn Station about a 1/2 hr ride. Penn station is located 2 blocks from the hotel on 31st . So easy to access and very easy ride directly from the airport to the centre of the city. Cost $5 for the airtrain ticket, payable as you enter or exit the airtrain at Jamaica, and $6 for the LIRR train ride. We caught the underground from Penn Station on the E line back to Jamaica - Sutphin Boulevard $2.25 then airtrain $5 back to the airport, would recommend the LIRR train which was much quicker due to the stops on the subway, felt safe but was crowed on the underground. 
Thanks to all at the hotel for making our stay so pleasant cannot recommend highly enough, we loved our stay in NYC.

title: “Very good hotel for family in New York”
text:
Our family of four went with a group of 35 people to New york City for one week. We would not have picked this hotel ourselves as we would consider it too close to the Times Square tourist zone and that doesn't really appeal to us.
Having said that, we were pleasantly surprised. Yes it is close to Times Square, however instead of going east to Times Square, go west one (long) block to 9th avenue and there is a wealth of small restaurants, coffee shops and funky stores. 
There is a subway station within a couple of blocks and with that you can easily and cheaply go anywhere. The hotel is a short walk to many of the Broadway theatres, and a nice walking distance to Central Park.
The free breakfast included was great for a family but get there early as it fills up fast.
The hotel is clean and well cared for, the staff was friendly and helpful.
If you are looking for a relatively basic hotel in a good location then this should fit the bill. really, if you are staying in Manhattan and spend much time in the hotel instead of out and about you should reasses your priorities.

title: “no worries here”
text: stayed here on sat, night (9/8) for the orioles/yankees games on sat. & sun.. i had room 524, and had absolutley no problem with the hotel or the room. it was perfectly situated with it being a short walk to camden yards and a short walk to inner harbour. had the breakfast buffet downstairs and it as well was well worth the price. the employee's were very helpfull with any questions you might have about the area. would i stay again ? ABSOLUTLEY !!!!!!

title: “Best hotel choice ever!”
text: I booked this hotel at the last minute for my daughter. They automatically gave her an upgrade hours before she arrived. After showing her the cool pictures, she couldn't wait to stay there. It was a huge success. She loved it. Her text to me said, "you rock!" The hotel is beautiful, modern and you can't get a better location! The price was perfect for my daughter and her friend. Would def. recommend this hotel - I am so pleased she and her friend enjoyed it!

title: “Not the best place to stay downtown”
text: We really wanted to like this place -- it's right across the street from Lucas Stadium and we were there for a Colts game -- but it always seemed to fall just short. The kitchen was small, cramped and poorly stocked (silverware missing, ice maker in the fridge didn't work, that sort of thing). And we were informed at check-in that "since it's an extended stay hotel", there would be no housekeeping over the week-end (really? I've never encountered that policy at any other extended stay chain! I don't much like having to take out the trash on a get-away weekend!) We'd spent a week-end at the Residence-Inn-on-the-Canal just two weeks earlier and this place just can't compare.

title: “Very nice!”
text:
Perfect location. Friendly staff. Nice, clean room.
Stayed for one night. We were able to park on the street without issue. Slept very well. Lola seemed to be hopping, but we walked around Belltown instead. We did enjoy breakfast at Lola in the morning. The best bacon!

title: “highly recommend it--am defintely coming back again...”
text: i never really write reviews, but i had to go out of my way to write this one! the staff was so friendly....the rooms clean, updated furniture and flat screen tvs, great location. i'm in the art world and have to start commuting between new york and houston for a major project--and i think this may be my "go-to" from now on.

title: “Do not stay if your looking for a quiet room”
text:
I spent 2 months reading review after review to choose a hotel for our 6 night stay in NY. I was disappointed i picked this one. It advertises as being sound proof. It was the loudest place i have ever stayed!!! We were on the 11th floor end of corridor and it was still unbelievable. There is a fire station just down the street. I dont know if there was more call outs during our stay or what but the way we were woken again and again every night made my heart jump!! It was like being in the middle of a action film. We did not say anything to the hotel as we were already on a high floor. Im in my 20s and for the first time ever i purchased ear plugs and sleeping tablets!
The room itself was very comfortable and plenty of room. The noise between rooms was pretty high we could hear next doors tv, shower, sink toilet. It was endless. 
Room service was terrible. Although the food was lovely in the restaurant. When we rang to ask for 2 champagne glasses with our meal they said they did not send glasses to the bedroom. Fair enough until our food arrived with 2 glasses of water!! Makes no sense. We had ordered starters and main courses and the metal dishes that came with it to keep it warm the waiter said he had to take them as he had another room to go to. We had a microwave in our room so we thought it would be ok and did not rush through the starters. ALL the plates were too big for the microwave so we ended up with cold dinners.
We had booked our hotel months in advanced. The two most expensive nights for us the last two - the hotel decided to renovate the lobby. This was a selling point for us as it was all done up christmassy. The lobby was closed off with no prior warning we just landed apon the scafoldding one morning. This should have been said to customers or the price should have dropped!! We could have done a lot better for the money we spent

title: “Wanted to stay at La Quinta”
text: From calling on the road for a reservation through checkout, I couldn't have asked for a better stay. Every employee gave service with a smile. The room was very clean so I rested comfortably. The breakfast was good and the eating area was clean. There was fresh fruit which was a pleasant surprise. I would recommend La Quinta to anyone based on my stay in January in West Palm Beach and my night in Jacksonville.

title: “Pleasantly Suprised”
text: Having booked 5 days at Hotel Carter last October, we were horrified to read the reviews on Trip Advisor. Well The Ritz Mayfair it is not. But then it doesn't pretend to be. The staff were helpful, the room was clean as were the sheets, and the shower was hot with clean towels. These were changed every two days. For a low cost budget hotel it was sensational, and brilliantly positioned. Don't always believe the bad stuff!! I'd go back.

title: “I do not understand how this hotel has a...”
text:
I do not understand how this hotel has a 3 1/2 - 4 star rating 
Apatently they put all the money in the loby
The rooms are average, walls are paper thin & the worst thing is begging housekeeping to clean your room!!!
Location is the only thing good about this hotel, don't be fouled by the friendly staff, they're all talk no do

title: “The bed was heavenly!”
text: This was my first experience of the Westin's "Heavenly Beds and Bath". It was truly heavenly! It was the most comfortable bed I had ever slept in. The room was spacious. Everything was just right. The location of the hotel is perfect, right on the riverwalk of San Antonio. My room has a good river view. What a beautiful hotel!

title: “I Love This Hotel - Love It!”
text: This is one of my very favorite hotels in the world and it never disappoints. Amazing service, wonderful staff, beautiful, clean rooms - you can't ask for more. I only wish I could visit more often.

title: “just ok”
text:
sErvice was ok, rooms inside also ok but we heard the elevator whole night. at sometime
 we thought we are in amsterdam at a coffee shop. fitness was poor. and 40 Bucks pe Night for parking is a rip off.

title: “Don't ship anything to this hotel!”
text:
I stayed at the Hilton Austin for a conference and left a personal item behind at home so it was shipped to me at the hotel. When I collected the package, I was told to get it at the hotel's UPS store. They charged me a $5 "storage fee". 
Let me point out that this package for stored for a total of maybe an hour and only weighed a pound. 
I have never been charged to pick up a package that was already prepaid and it repulses me that Hilton would do this to their guests!
What a scam!
Note to management: Don't bother with the onsite UPS store unless guests won't get nickeled and dimed by bogus feesm

title: “Would return to this place”
text:
Hotel was in a good location with easy access to public. The rooms were standard rooms but had everything we need. One small point; our room smelt a bit musty and I think this was down to the carpets needing a deep steam clean. 
The rest of the room and bathroom was spotlessly clean.
The pool area and pool were well kept. 
The staff were really helpful and friendly and we’d defiantly stop here again.

title: “Perfect Place for a Chick Trip for Women of Color”
text:
I am a single, woman of color, in my late 40's, who has been wanting to visit Boston since being of grade-school age. My friend and I got an unbelievable 3 night-four day rate on this hotel which included airfare, for less than what some have shared that they have paid for a two night stay in this hotel!! I made a decision to spend more time out of my room than in it, but know that this hotel is perfect for those who are looking for a relaxing weekend as well!!
The Positives:
1. The hotel's location is great, but only if you are able to do the kind of walking that's associated with big cities like New York and D.C. 
2. We were able to catch a bus from the airport to the hotel for the equivalent of two dollars each. A cab would have been a total of $20 for the two of us. We decided to buy a transit pass good for a week which cost $15; a day pass was $9.00. The transit station is a five-ten minute walk from the hotel. My suitcase weighed almost 50 pounds; yet I was able to make it!!
3. The security in this hotel is unbelievable!!! The hotel security were men in suits who "patroled" the lobby area, opened doors for us, and greeted us whenever we encountered them in the lobby on our way in and out of the hotel. I felt safe as a single woman in this hotel.
4. While I am not a fan of sushi, the Sushi/Tequila bar plays salsa music which I love. It has a high-tech look and feel and I was able to get an impromptu salsa lesson from one of the wait staff after the bar had cleared one evening.
5. If you are one who enjoys socializing, make sure you speak to Wayne in the Rum/Champagne Bar and Charles in the Miel Restaurant. They are delightful!!
6. The bathroom was outstanding. It was all marble, oversized, with a glass-encased shower and a separate, long and deep bathtub. It reminded me of those bathrooms one sees in those upscale decorating magazines. Bring your bubble bath, shower gel, exfoliate, and candles!!!
7. The beds were comfortable.
8. We were in room 604, with two double beds. NO VIEW!!! but there were no sirens as mentioned by a fellow reviewer, it was VERY, VERY, QUIET!!
9. The hotel has this little nook in the lobby that contains a Scrabble board and a couple of Monopoly games. I like playing board games so having access to these was a treat!
10. The hotel's Business Center has a limited selection of office supplies available for sale in case you forget something. I did not check the prices.
11. Elevators are fast.
12. We had a probelm connecting to the internet. The front desk was called, the tech crew was there in five minutes and resolved the problem in five more. 
13. Walked to the Barking Crab. This place is as causal as a picnic table in a local park but the food was decent. You can't go wrong with the crab legs.
14. There is an iron and ironing board in the room. I prefer to iron with steam. I had a difficult time getting the water into the iron.
The Negatives
1. I do not like French food which is the featured food for the hotel's main dining room. It is expensive for a working woman like me. When I say expensive I am talking double-digit prices for appetizers and salads.
2. If you are sharing the room with others you need to know that everything you do in the bathroom can be heard by those outside the bathroom. Bad Singing, Cell Phone Conversations, etc.
3. Another reviewer mentioned that the glasses in the bathroom were not restocked daily. I had this experience too, additionally, we had to call housekeeping for washclothes. NO BIG DEAL JUST A MINOR INCONVENIENCE TO ME.
4. Business Center internet five dollars per 15 minutes. In-room internet 15 dollars a day. You do the math. A laptop was left in the room each day of our stay. No problems.
5. If you are a breakfast person and a bargain traveler you are going to have to leave the hotel and walk across the street to a side street next to the fire department. There is a restaurant named VIGA there that serves a $3.50 breakfast special, but I didn't have time to try it.
6. Be very careful in the bathroom if the marble floor gets wet. I almost fell. USE THE CLOTH BATHMAT OR YOU'RE GOING DOWN!!!
7. We were going to order a roll-away bed to accomodate another friend who decided to spend the night. I think it was going to cost $30-45 per night. 
8. Although I'm not a drinking woman I did review the drink menus in both the Sushi/Tequila Bar and the Rum/Champagne Bar. WOW!! I think the drink prices are high; many were double-digit prices in sitandard-sized bar glasses. There was even one drink on the menu that was made with 24-carat gold!!! If you are looking for the ultimate in a glass, this could be the bar for you!!
Other Notes
1. Many of the hotel staff are from cities around the world. If you start a conversation they will gladly interact with you. I like this!!
2. I did not eat in the hotel, nor did I go to the pool or spa, or use the bell men, so I can't comment.
3. I was dissapointed with the different bowls of chowder that I had at several different restaurants during my stay in the Boston area. They were too thick and had no flavor. I recommend a small mom and pop restaurant chain called Kelly's Restaurant. There is a location at the end of the blue line at Revere Beach. It is not close but if you can get there this restaurant had the best chowder and other delights from the sea ( lobster rolls, scallops, fried clams, and even roast beef sandwiches) at reasonable prices. Nothing in the restaurant is over $20!!! They are on the web.
4. Many people recommend dining at Legal Seafood. Try Legal, Try Kelly's, then you decide.

title: “excellent Hotel loved it!”
text: It seems my suit case never cools off. From the moment we checked in until the moment we left this property every thing it promised, it delivered. From the executive floor happy hour to the regular happy hour, the comfy beds new decor in the rooms the parking that was included in OUR room package worked out wonderfully, we are gold members so we got some extra perks, cant mention there comp breakfasts only because i never made it to it. Over all this was an excellent stay, dinning options in and around the hotel worked out for us wonderfully, i would recommend this hotel to all, even the kids, they had happy feet playing for the kids and families with free popcorn, can beat that,

title: “Fantastic Location/ Dirty Rooms”
text: Plus: Incredible location. Overly friendly, efficient staff. Free WiFi (with great tech staff if you cannot connect at first try) Minus: dirty rooms. Chipped paint in the showers. Dirty carpets. Paper thin walls. Very noisy. Red Roof has certainly got the location. This ancient hotel sits mere feet from the heart of Michigan Avenue, shopping, restaurants and only five minutes from Lake Shore Drive. The staff at this hotel are friendly, helpful and quite knowledgeable about the city, the area around the hotel and seem to go out of their way to make every guest feel welcome. Unfortunately, this hotel is dirty, and is in desperate need of new carpets, new bathrooms, new tiles, new windows, new everything. It also needs a full-time cleaning staff who understand how to clean and hotel and make it stay that way.

title: “Fun old building in a good east/central downtown location.”
text: Good location half block off 16th St. Mall; great gathering place for extended family events; close to many venues. Trendy update to old building; expansive suite. CLEAN. Phone reservation staff icey, with a take it or leave it attitude - other staff makes up for it.

title: “Great weekend in San Francisco”
text: Chancellor Hotel was in a good location. We followed some of the reviews and requested a room on an upper level on the backside. We were not disappointed. People were very accommodating and polite. We definitely will use this hotel again. Superb location.

title: “Excellent!”
text: The hotel was in a great location from Michigan Ave, had great staff, and a wonderful continental breakfast! Stayed in a room with a queen bed, definitely very limited floor space. However, with a great location, breakfast, and staff the small rooms are a ok!

title: “Great Place to Stay Near PHL and the CIty”
text:
I spent about a week at the aloft Philadelphia Airport and was really impressed with just about everything.
To begin with, the staff is very helpful and courteous.
The rooms are clean, modern and obviously set up with a business traveler in mind - plenty of power connections right where you want them, and also a device to connect iPad/iPod/iWhatever to the flat screen TV.
The gym at the aloft Philly is very well equipped, including free weights and benches, a couple of elliptical machines, stationary bikes and two or three treadmills. The indoor pool is conveniently located near the gym.
But the front desk staff is the difference-maker at this hotel. I highly recommend this place for a reasonably priced, comfortable and well equipped stay within in minutes of PHL airport.

title: “Always above & beyond expectations!”
text: We have been staying at The Barclay for about 10 years. We keep going back because we are never disappointed. Ms. Annmara Gayle always makes sure every detail is as we expect. She even knows which suite is our favorite and if we book early enough, she always puts us in it. The Barclay is a lovely, lovely hotel in an area, as far as we are concerned, that can't be beat. Its very close to Grand Central and only a few blocks from Fifth Avenue. There are restaurants, delis, cafes etc. all within a minute of the door. New York is my favorite city in the world, and The Barclay helps to keep it that way. (I wish they had free Wi-Fi in the rooms, but its NYC - oh well, there is free Wi-Fi in the lobby)

title: “Fantastic location!”
text: This was my second trip to Chicago. We chose a hotel based on location, and this one was perfect! We walked to Navy Pier and were right on the Magnificent Mile. The standard room was sufficient but still pricey. It was obvious you pay for the location! We loved having the Weber Grill in the hotel! We ate there and also got excellent room service from there. Again... Pricey but worth it! When you go to Chicago, you can expect to spend a lot. However, it's always worth it! Great times, great hotel, and overall another great trip!!!

title: “An entirely satisfactory place to sleep”
text: It's time for me to express my great satisfaction with this hotel as, well, a place to sleep. My wife and I have stayed here 4-5 times over the past 3 years; we've also stayed at Icon, Magnolia, Warwick (pre-renovation), Derek, and Lancaster. Each of those hotels is more interesting, and a good room at the Lancaster - on an affordable night - is a very good room indeed. But the "rounded-corner" deluxe room at the Doubletree is as spacious and comfortable as any, is very safe for a klutz like me who tends to bump into sharp edges, and is exceptionally affordable (at least on a weekend). I've had no problem with noise in the halls, and I'm a light sleeper. The valet parking is unusually efficient and polite, the elevators are quick, and the lobby is quieter than the other hotels I referenced (the cool young crowd at the Icon is just not my thing). The breakfast buffet has gotten worse, however, and needs to be upgraded with decent scrambled eggs, a greater variety of fibrous fruit and cereals, and more full-bodied coffee.

title: “It's all true”
text: Not much to add to previous reviewers; great location, friendly staff, home away from home.

title: “In a New York Minute .... Not”
text: The once grand old dame is a little bit off her game. I stayed during a convention in hot Dallas. While I did receive an upgrade in room, the facilities were a bit lacking. One of the sinks was not working and had to call three times before a person showed up. The beds were a bit soft but all in all, this is an acceptable choice while staying downtown.

title: “Great location, reasonable price, terrific breakfast, free WIFI”
text: We chose this HIE because of it's close proximity to the airport (3-4 minutes) and for the dependability of the chain - good breakfasts, free wifi new facilities etc. We were happy with the choice - although close to the airport, the hotel is away from the Century Blvd traffic, and very close to most rental car lots. Service was good, the room very nice, and the airport shuttle was big and 24-hour. Really the only downside is that there are almost no restaurants within 1/2 mile or so (except at other hotels). However, a lot of local restaurants deliver : we had Thai food delivered right to our room, which was VERY convenient. Look for this option online. We would definitely stay here again if we had to be near LAX.

title: “Nice but Lout”
text: This hotel has a perfect location. We stayed at the hotel when they had full occupency The elevators are small but there are several of them. It only took a minute for one to come by. The rooms and bathrooms were standard hotel rooms for a big city. If you want a larger hotel room you should probably stay outside of Chicago. The staff were very courteous. You can hear sirens and beeping cars (Again, you are in Chicago.). My only complaint is the lack of wireless internet service in rooms.

title: “A decent hotel in a good location at a reasonable price”
text:
My wife and I spent two nights here (July 2 & 3, 2010) and it was a very nice experience. Was it spectacular? No, not even close. But we had proper expectations, and were not disappointed.
I see from its web site that Club Quarters talks about "being a member" but this was never something that came up for us. We booked through a large travel web site (the one with the gnome) and got the room for $146 per night. For a hotel just two blocks from the heart of Times Square, this is a pretty darn good deal. 
The hotel is unassuming from the outside, and has a small but attractive lobby. The street it is on is quiet (on 45th between 5 & 6th). We heard no traffic noise from our 9th floor window overlooking 45th st. As I said, a couple of avenues west and we were on Times Square. Two blocks north and we were at the Diamond District and Radio City, St. patricks and 30 Rock were just a block or two north of that. A location just one block or so more west and north would have been $100 a night more. So unless you object to even the most minimal walking, the location is great if you're in town for some theatre. We were also quite close to the NY Public library and Bryant Park.
Our room was small...big surprise. In case you weren't aware, hotel rooms in NYC are small. Yes, you can pay some serious money and get more typically sized rooms...but as I said, we had realistic expectations. Our little room contained a queen bed, and extra chair, a small desk, a rod for hanging clothes (no closet) and a small bedroom with a shower but no tub. HOWEVER, the design was very tasteful (especially in the bathroom, nice fixtures and a great frosted glass door) and the room was very clean. We spent a grand total of perhaps 5 waking hours in the room and perhaps 13 sleeping hours...and we really didn't need more from our room than a place for our stuff and a comfortable night's sleep. If you're traveling with a family, no doubt you would have been cramped where we were. But the room, while not exactly spa-style romantic, was actually quite a nice place to return to after a LONG day wandering around the greatest city on Earth! (And the AC, which is provided by a window unit, actually worked well and was quiet!! That might be a first for a window unit in a hotel.)
There is a continental breakfast (which is NOT free...what hotels in NYC provide FREE meals???), and a fairly dressy looking restaurant...but we did not avail ourselves and I cannot comment.
Cons: the TV in the room is 20 inches and hangs over the desk, a fair distance from the bed, where you are likely to be trying to watch it. Again, for a quick stay, it was fine for having the news on in the background. But if you'd try to watch a whole movie or TV show, it would have felt small. The bathroom works great for ONE person, but is simply too tiny for two people to share a sink or mirror. Front desk service was impersonal, but not annoyingly so. They were responsive, but not exactly overjoyed either. HOWEVER, when we called for our luggage that they'd been holding for us on our last afternoon, it took a full 10 minutes for it to arrive. THAT was annoying, because we needed to get to the airport.
They have an ice machine and free bottled water...but ONLY at the basement level, in their tiny workout room. We used it once, and it was a minor pain.
