But overall, we had a very nice stay, and I would certainly stay again.

title: “Does what it says on the Tin”
text:
If you want somewhere to stay for more than a week and are on a budget this is the place to go in San Jose. Complete room with all the facilities for a couple or family and at a reasonable price. Cooker, fridge, television, free internet, breakfast etc.. all there and adequate.
Like anywhere in the Valley you need a car, there is little to do around the hotel and few restaurants within reasonable walking distance. 
Children friendly, quiet and peaceful. Overall a young crowd, probably engineers working in one of the startups around San Jose with young families.
If you need clean sheets and towels every day this is not for you - four towels for a week and a sheet change once a week unless you pay a $5 surcharge per day.

title: “Pretty nice, I'd stay again”
text:
After review, and plenty of choices in the downtown area, I decided to give Hotel Contessa a shot. Overall, my room was lovely and quite spacious, the hotel public areas were very nice (bar,patios, etc), the waitress for the patio bar area was very attentive and friendly, everything was clean and smelled nice. The price was very good for what you get, and the location is perfect. Further, the valet service was timely and attentive. But there were a few details, primarily service, that made the stay less than great.
The valet parking is steep ($25/nt) and the only other option (that they shared) was a parking lot across the street for $15/nt, cash only.
I had to call downstairs TWICE for complimentary toothpaste, when no one arrived the first time for 3+ hours. A guest should only have to call once.
There was no caffeinated coffee and no sugar/cream in the room.
On a design note for the rooms, there is a large bar in the living area that could have easily accomodated a sink....e.g., it's a bit annoying to take the coffee pot into the bathroom to get water...
The street side of the hotel is NOISY -- so it might be worth it to pay more for the river side.
When I called the spa for an appt, the receptionist answered the phone "Hello?" I couldn't tell if I had dialed the wrong number. When I asked if I was calling the spa, she said yes, and put me on hold for so long that I finally hung up and called back....to find out they had no availability. That is all okay, but the hold time was too long.
Overall, however, I would give a definite thumbs up. Just a few details could have made a big difference.

title: “Rundown”
text: Terrible experience. Hotel in disrepair. Dirty. Shabby. Non-smoking room smelled heavily of smoke. Saw mice in the hallway. After checkin, I was told that multi-night stays receive maid service just once every 3 days. Big sign in lobby says "No Refunds". Nevertheless, I left after just one night of a planned six-night stay.

title: “Love, Loved it”
text: The service is perfect. From the front desk to all the staff. The food was great for being healthy. I wish I could eat everyday like this. The exercise classes were good. We had a private swim exercies class and it was great. Also, reservations did a great job also. Everything is peaceful and restful. If you want a week of relaxation, exercise if you want and do whatever you want. This is it.

title: “Out of the way gem”
text:
This hotel has become our "go to" place to stay whenever we are in Seattle. It's just beside Lake Union so you don't get downtown prices but the streetcar that's nearly outside the door is a 15 minute ride into downtown. 
We were in a king room which was a real treat as the larger bed also comes with a large sitting area, work table, fireplace and a mini-kitchenette (mini fridge, sink, microwave), a huge bonus when traveling with kids and for heating up leftovers :)
My wife and I were traveling on our anniversary and the front desk was so gracious to leave a sweet treat in the room while we were out for dinner.
Of course, the full breakfast was nice, the pool and hot tub were relaxing.

title: “High at the Hyatt”
text: This Hotel is wonderful, Great location just steps from china town. The only draw back was having to pay 40.00 a night for parking but we would have to pay that price anywhere in San Francisco. The staff is wonderful. Left something behind and they had it in the Lost and Found within an hour. They sent it back UPS. This is a very nice hotel.

title: “Above and Beyond Customer Service”
text: I recently spent several nights in this hotel while attending a series of meetings held on its premises. The front desk staff, restaurant staff, and maid service staff were all very friendly and provided a feeling of "home" rather than just a big city hotel staff. The best customer service experience, however, was after I had checked out. Upon returning home, I found that I had left a pair of shoe covers in my room's dresser. I expected that they would never reappear, but called the hotel the next day. Much to my surprize, the front desk had the shoe covers packed and ready to return to me. I received them by mail within a few days, personally wrapped and post-paid! Throughout my travel experiences, I have accidentally left items in hotels, but have never had them returned like this. This hotel's customer service went beyond my expectations! Thank you!

title: “Hot Tub Out of Service; Everything Else Great”
text: My son and I stayed here with my sister and her daughter the weekend after Thanksgiving. The calibre of the hotel's restaurants was outstanding. Our room was wonderful, the beds comfortable and the service exemplary. Had the hot tub been in service, it would have been a perfect stay.

title: “We will return to the "Inn"”
text: We just returned from a four night stay at the Inn at Union Square. We found this location by reading reviews on tripadvisor.com and could not have been more pleased with the hotel and it's location. The hotel itself was very clean and the staff were all very friendly and concerned with making your stay comfortable. We stayed in room 401 which is a smaller suite with two rooms. The sitting room faced Post street, the front of the hotel. The bedroom window overlooked an alley with no real view but this was good, it made for a very quite sleep time. The breakfast and wine service was held on the third and fifth floor so it was just a walk up or down to eat and drink without having all the foot traffic on your floor. The location of the hotel is right in Union Square, great walking distance from many activities and great restaurants. We flew into San Francisco and took a taxi to the hotel. Leaving from our stay we had an early morning flight and inquired about having a taxi waiting for our trip to the airport. The desk recomended a car service, Bernie's Limousines, which really worked out great. The cost was just a few dollars more then a taxi. The driver professional, the car roomy and clean.

title: “Very pleasantly surprised...”
text: So many outstanding features, other than the wonderful location. This hotel has a good size under cabinet fridge, coffeemaker plus coffee welcome package, decent size microwave, in a compact kitchen area. The room was spotless clean and all linens and amenities fresh and pillows smelled fresh too. We booked a deluxe two doublebed room which still turned out spacious, not cramped. Check in/out was efficient and friendly. They actually acknowledge you even while still standing in line. The staff always greet you, not typical New York. So nice. The location is superb. Close to Times Square, restaurants, stores, theatre area, and subways and bus so convenient. New York hotel business is competitive but this one will get my business all the time.

title: “A Good San Francisco Experience”
text: We stayed for 3 nights at the Monaco with our 9 year old daughter. I had visited San Francisco several times over the years, always stating at Fishermans Wharf. A friend recommended staying around Union Square and it was a far more convenient location for shopping, dining and getting a general feel for the city. The hotel itself was great - rooms are small but with a quirky decoration. This is not a sanitised large hotel chain experience, but an old art deco hotel which has been thoughfully restored and which has a real character. The service is very good. We took advantage of the afternoon wine tasting which was friendly and enjoyable. The concierge staff were very helpful with restaurant recommendations. The only downside was a slow and expensive breadkfast in the hotel restaurant on the Saturday morning. Overall a good experience

title: “Very Pleased with the Hotel Madera”
text:
We stayed at the Hotel Madera for an anniversary weekend away with our infant daughter. We chose it largely on the basis of reviews here. 
From start to finish the staff was cheerful, friendly and helpful without being too familiar.
We arrived early on Saturday AM and knew we would not be able to check in that early. The staff happily checked our luggage. When we returned in the afternoon, our luggage had already been placed in the room and a bottle of champagne was on ice for us. 
The room was wonderful and exactly as billed by numerous other reviewers. 
It was decorated in a sophisticated neutral, unaggressively contemporary style which was refreshing. Our room overlooked New Hampshire Ave and got the morning and evening sun which was great. The furniture was very solid and the fabrics well made. This is not always the case even in top notch hotels. The vanity was black marble and was outside the bathroom proper, which, also as billed, was small but sufficient. There was a nice massaging shower head. The room was also very quiet and we were not aware whether there were even other guests on our floor.
Another example of service excellence: to pass from the lobby to the elevators involved going up 3-4 steps. Every single time we encountered this with my daughter's stroller, the staff physically moved the stroller for us. This was great as I was doing it on the Metro most of the day and it was a great treat to have it just happen in the hotel.
We ate dinner at the hotel restaurant, Firefly, one night and were very pleased, liking it more than another significantly more expensive restaurant we went to the night before. The ambience is indeed "summery" with a golden glow permeating it. The food was excellent and prepared exactly to order. The only mild downside was that we did notice that as the restaurant filled up during our 2 hours there, the staff became slightly less attentive. For example there was a 10-15 min delay in getting the dessert after the coffee had already been served. The dessert was a simple one which required only slicing so the only explanation for the delay was understaffing for the peak periods. Firefly is also apparently open for breakfast and lunch, but we found the Krispy Kreme Doughnut shop at the Dupont Circle Metro entrance very appealing (if a little indulgent).
All in all, while the Hotel Madera is not cheap (nor anywhere near as expensive as you can spend in DC), in our estimation you get a lot of value for your money--a very appealing room in a great location and genuinely helpful, friendly service.

title: “A great place in a great city”
text:
A great place to stay on our first-ever visit to the wonderful city of Chicago. Comfortable, well-kept and superbly situated with everything either within walking distance or accessible by bus from right outside the hotel.
Guests arriving in the afternoon or evening will doubtless be greeted by the bell captain who's quite a character and a mine of information - a friendly, garrulous, wise-cracking guy (think Shrek's comical sidekick voiced by Eddie Murphy).
Just one detail keeps me from giving the room 5 stars - the lack of a mini bar to serve as a fridge. However, now we've got the hang of the ice-machine-on-the-landing routine it's no longer a major problem

title: “OK except for the bites...!”
text:
The location is excellent. The front desk staff is good. The room is fairly quiet, especially considering the location. The room interior is a bit worn, altough clean. The door was damaged. Overall, I get an impression that the hotel is not doing well; the restaurant was out of business. 
The biggest problem we had was the ... bites. On my son and myself. Definitely bed bugs!

title: “Bad experience”
text:
The landlord definitely must have retouched the pictures he sent to me upfront. But if you take a closer look, it is horrible. I stayed in the 'Radio City' room for $3000/month because I was on business trip and was very busy and no time to search for some other room. But the room is absolutely cheap furnished and dirty. Not once the room got maintained and cleaned during my whole stay. When I moved in, one of the closets was filled with detergent. The aircondition and the shower head I had to sanitize with a spray I bought, because the air smelled absolutely bad while operating. 
The mattress, the pillow and the bed blanket, everything smelled dingy and never washed or changed. The sheets and towels smelled like moth balls. I bought a bug protection for the mattress and slept on my own sheets, never used his stuff.

title: “Treated Like Royalty”
text: The entire staff make you feel like royalty from the moment you arrive to the time you leave. Lois the concierge is the best she is always recommends the best places to dine around town. The hotel is modern and comfortable with a great location in downtown Chicago. I have stayed there for the last 10 years when I come into town to visit. It truly is home away from home.

title: “A very pleasant experience”
text: The service staff was extremely attentive and personable. My room was clean, bright and fresh, and was of comfortable size. My only wish would be a stronger wi-fi connection. Wi-fi is free, but can fall off too easily. Over all, this Days Inn was a very good value in this community.

title: “I'd move in tomorrow.”
text:
My Carlyle Suites experience was wonderful. The room was well appointed including a fantastic kitchen, the staff was helpful and the deco decor was very polished. I did not try the restaurant. There's a good grocery store within walking distance too. The gym option was a bit of a hike, but it's in the neighborhood.
I think it's obnoxious to complain about the early check out fee: Why would you want to leave the Carlyle?
Other guests (and maybe housekeeping staff) did tend to slam their suite doors a bit rudely. It was kind of comical though, in a 'What's Up Doc?' way.

title: “A bit shabby”
text:
Any hotel with such a great location must be fairly bad to be priced so cheaply.... and Belnord is.
The bad bits: 
the disgusting stench of stale smoke
the tiny room
the view of a brick wall (ha ha)
the unhelpful (and noisy) staff
charging $5 per bag to hold our luggage after check out
the carpets and bedding looked a hundred years old, plenty of dust in there!
The ok bits (good would be going a bit far as they're actually expected in most normal hotels!):
The toilets were cleaned reguarly and always smelt nice
The hotel itself seemed fairly clean 
We didnt have bed bugs
So if you just want the room to sleep in and can handle feeling a little bit grubby and unglamorous for your stay then it is fine. We had no major complaints as there was nothing essentially wrong with it. However next time i think i would prefer to pay a little bit extra to stay somewhere less dingy!!

title: “If only for the pool”
text:
There is not much to say about the rooms.
They are outdated, the same age as the Elvis pictures.
But they are clean and the beds are ok.
The hotel is cool, the guitar shaped pool also .
And the staff i met (senior lady at reception and the mexican cleaners) is friendly.
The price ?
At this spot right across Graceland it could be dubble.
For every visit to Memphis this is a relaxed spot.

title: “Awesome! Couldn't be better. The price and hotel is unbeatable.”
text: I read reviews of many hotels and looked at pictures. This hotel not only looked exactly like the pictures but was even prettier than the pics if you can believe it. The staff is fabulous and I mean it. Rebecca and Anna are the best but I got to give a special shout out to Rebecca, she was so helpful and accommodating to me even when I left my laundry in the dryer before going to sea world and forgot it. She had it right behind the desk waiting for me. The pillows I had brought were not dry yet and she unlocked the laundry door so I could finish drying them. You don't need to bring your own pillows as they have at least 5 on the bed and they are comfy. She was also a nice conversational buddy at night when things were quiet. Anna was the day person and she was very busy and accommodating also. The breakfast was just what someone would need in the morning and the waffles were great. This staff works very hard in keeping this hotel clean and comfortable. All of the girls run around doing so many things, I couldn't believe how much they care about their hotel. I stayed in the economy rooms which are like a little studio apt right in front of the pool. I am very excited to go back again next year. The owners should be proud of the girls they have cuz they all care about you and your stay. I am so happy I stayed here. sometimes you look at a hotel and you find it is not what you expect, this place is more than you can ever hope to spend a small amount of money on and feel like you are in a very expensive posh hotel. Thank you all of you at Old town inn. You are all so wonderful.

title: “not a better place in san diego”
text: Dollar for dollar THIS is the place. The best free breakfast in town. Two blocks from everything. The trolly to everyplace else is behind the hotel. The view? The harbor is across the street-- Ships come in and out all day--it's '''almost''in a movie set. The airport is 10 minutes away.

title: “great”
text: I saw the reviews of others, some great, some very bad, so I did not know what I was getting into, when I pulled up, I thought I was at the wrong hotel, but I went to the desk and it was the right one, the hotel was great, the first time in my life I feel I got more than my money worth, everything and everyone was great, I enjoyed my stay and would do it over and over again if I could, if I ever get back to Columbus, this is the spot to be at. THANK YOU Crown Plaza Columbus North and HOTWIRE.COM...

title: “Great location and nice hotel”
text: My husband and I stayed for one night. The hotel is very clean. The room was small but that is the norm for NYC. The hotel seems new- everything is in nice condition. The bathroom is on the small side as well but fine. It is not ultra luxurious but our room was on a high floor, quiet and the air conditioner kept the room nice and cool and didn't make a lot of noise which is important. I would recommend it.

title: “Beautiful boutique hotel”
text:
Stayed at the Palomar as part of a site visit for an upcoming meeting. This place is top-notch. The hotel rooms are beautiful, and if you are lucky enough to get one of the spa-bathrooms, even better! My room had beautiful picture windows in both the bathroom and the bedroom area. The vanity area was somewhat limited in space, and if I had stayed for more than one night my stuff would have been all over the room. The decor is modern and minimalist, but classy. 
The TV was the only drawback to the room. I think because it was dish or Direct TV, there was such a delay between pushing the remote button and changing the channel. Annoying, but not a deal breaker. 
I ate dinner in the bar. I was a bit confused when I went in and didn't realize the restaurant was actually upstairs. But the service was great! I really enjoyed the small plates option too. I had two small plates - soup and gnocchi and a beer for around $25. Not bad price for hotel dining. And the food was delicious! I also had breakfast the next day - standard eggs, bacon, fruit, and coffee. Hotel prices, but decent, and quick service. 
I took a short walk in a two-block direction and wasn't too impressed with the neighborhood just outside, however. I got there late, so many of the businesses were already closed. Those that were open were very high-end eating.

title: “LOVE this hotel!”
text: I will stay at this hotel every time I visit Memphis. It is beautiful and centrally located. Really great for our family trip and within walking distance to Beale Street. They were also very accommodating with parking our RV..not an easy thing to do in any metro area. Be sure to visit Blue Plate Cafe right across the park...best breakfast in Memphis!

title: “NO mini-safe or fridge? Come on!”
text:
First off, this is a great hotel! It really is! The location is excellent as it is right beside Union Square. The rooms are quiet and kept clean by the maid staff. The service is or at least the front desk service is excellent as they immediately took care of my room issues - which included switching rooms to get away from the elevator. However, I should mention that the 'bus boy' service was weak. It was not that they were not friendly because they always said hello. It is just that at both check in and departure we did not get any help with our bags. I mean really? It is not that I expect to be 'catered' to, but I am paying for the Marriott and expect the basic level of service. This leads to my next point. Why are there no safes or fridges in the room? I expect better from the Marriott. 
I should mention that we upgraded to the concierge floor and it was well worth it. The service at the lounge was excellent. The food was average however; it did allow us to have a solid breakfast in order to start our busy day. As well, the nighttime refreshments allowed us to 'recharge'
Overall, I would recommend this hotel but, I decided to rate it a bit lower due to my points mentioned above. It is a competitive hotel industry and when paying for particular brands I expect a certain level of service and amenities.

title: “Great NYC hotel in Midtown”
text: Stayed here with my wife for 4 nights last weekend and have to highly recommend this to anyone wanting a really nice hotel, in a great location, quiet, with a good restaurant. Always apprehensive booking hotels online but this was a brilliant choice. Everything is like new in the hotel. We stayed on the 9th floor and could not believe how quiet the room was at night. The room itself was really clean and the bed really comfortable (having upgraded to the king size was a bonus). Friendly staff, great location, highly recommended to any fellow irish travellers to NYC. Only advice I have is ensure you dont get ripped off by the taxi driver from the airport.. after that you learn quick. The return journey booked by the hotel was much better at $70 all in.

title: “Not there yet but ok.”
text: I wish hotel sites would indicate that areas of a new hotel are yet to be completed. But the room (a cozy corner) was nice enough. Bathroom was wonderfully spacious...bed area less so but the bed was truly comfortable and the colors were soft modern soothing. The view of Lady Bird lake from the 13th floor was nice. After the first impression (a good one), the second impression was that everything was a facade...kinda inexpensive versions of modern that I am afraid will not wear well after SXSW hits in March. The staff was informed and friendly but trained to skew their recommendations to W Hotel services... expected I guess but a more total Austin feel would be appreciated. Glad they sent me to Mohawk in East Austin. When they forgot to deliver new linens I requested, they delivered chocolates, water and more and then called to apologize so I think they are on the road to "getting it". In warmer weather, this place with the pool, balconies and rockin' location should be quite the scene.

title: “Well worth it”
text:
An unbelievably good hotel. Harbour view upgrade when booked via BA. Telescope in room to look at statue of liberty - yes its a gimmick but its an awesome gimmick. The location is good in my opinion, close to Soho, Tribeca, a cab ride/subway ride to Midtown. Close to ferries. close to financial district. Its good! Some unbelievable places to eat there.
Service was unbeatable, especially the concierge Racquel - couldn't do enough to suggest and help us book a restaurant for one evening. Great comfortable rooms, massive comfortable bed, clean rooms, massive bathroom. Had an issue with bath plug not working, it took us a few calls to reception but when they turned up, it was fixed within minutes and a complimentary room service breakfast was offered for the inconvenience.
All in all, an epic trip and a great hotel. Thoroughly recommended.

title: “Beautiful”
text: I was in town for a birthday party and stayed at this hotel. The place is beautiful and the bed felt better than the one I have at home. They serve you complimentary coffee in the lobby, and the staff was very friendly. I would return to this hotel.

title: “well worth it!”
text: this hotel is great! right on the marina, close to restaurants; rooms were clean and the staff was amazing - especially johnna, who checked in our large group! she gave us the scoop on where to eat and shop, and resolved our problem within minutes. this woman is the bomb!!

title: “Fabulous location for stay in Soho area!”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for 2 nights after our wedding in Las Vegas in October 2012. From the moment we arrived at the hotel I fell in love with it. We were greeted by very handsome staff from our taxi and the fact all the staff looked so stylish and were so friendly made the place even better! Upon check in we were given a complimentary glass of sparkling wine which was a lovely touch and added to my excitement. 
We stayed in a Corner room, which was cosy but had everything you needed. The bed was very comfortable and the view from the room was brilliant as we could see everything going on in the street below. 
We didn't eat at the hotel as we were out and about during most of our stay, but we did have a drink in the hotel bar one evening which was enjoyable. The main lobby area and reception are very cool and dimly light which give this hotel it's funky, cool and trendy feeling. 
The location of the hotel was perfect for us as we wanted to explore the Soho area during our second trip to NYC. It was close to a number of good resturants and only 5 minutes away from all the shops we wanted to go to in the Soho / Broadway area.
If we we're to go to NYC again (which I'm sure we will), I would definitely stay at this hotel again and would recommend it to anyone.

title: “Friendly Staff and Fantastic service”
text: I didn't think that the room was too bad in terms of size as I had heard all about the rooms in New York being small. The bathroom probably could do with a more modern make over. Fantastic location right near Central Park and a shopping mall in front of Colombus Circle. Nice roof top pool and roof top bar which is the "in spot" in Manhattan. The down stairs bar is a great place to hang out as it is not a sleazy bar (some hotel bars can be very sleazy). The bar staff are all amazing - so extremely friendly and sweet and really interested in getting to know their guests. I cannot speak highly enough of Gerard, Frank, Mike, Nyahale and Sandra. Concierge is fantastic and provide you with great tips of what to do and what not to do in NY and will do all the bookings for you.

title: “Great location”
text:
I recently stayed at the Milford plaza for two nights. I booked this hotel on a recommendation from a work colleague.
The hotels location is perfect. Literally around the corner from times square so it gets an A+++++ for this. And even though it is so close to the hustle and bustle of Times Square it was reasonably quiet.
I stayed in a queen room which had been renovated. The room was smallish however this is typical for New York hotels and this didn't annoy me. The bed was the most comfortable bed I have slept in. We stayed in room 1438 and didn't have any view, only into the room across from us and this was a tad disappointing. Also the electric sockets were no where near the mirror and I had no compact mirror with me so drying my hair was a challenge (a small gripe but I think in a newly renovated room there's no excuse for it.) However none of these things would stop me staying again as the location more than makes up for it.
However one big negative I would say is I found some of the staff very rude. Upon arrival we were asked for a $50 security deposit for incedentals such as Internet. When we explained we wouldn't be using the Internet or such like the receptionist continued with the check in process for a few more minutes before abruptly saying " Ah $50". No please or anything. We then said again we wouldn't be using anything but we paid the $50. When we handed it over the receptionist held up the note to the light for easily 30 seconds to determine if the note was real or fake. She then used a counterfeit pen which determined that the note was real, but then held it up to the light again and proclaimed it to be "not right and I'm not accepting it". When I said it had come straight from the bank she loudly said "well banks give out fakes too you know and I'm not happy with the feel of it". Even though the counterfeit pen had clearly proved it real she wouldn't accept it and I had to give a different note. This was extremely embarrassing as the lobby had been very busy with check ins and I was made to feel like I was in the wrong just because she didn't like the feel of the note. I also had to ask for a reciept for the deposit, which is good I did as on check out I was asked for it and wouldn't have got my money back. I also then used the "counterfeit" note in a large store which was accepted with no problems. I work in an industry where I handle money and I completely understand that she has to be careful when handling notes as I'm sure she's held responsible for her cash float, however when the counterfeit pen proved it was real that shouldnt mean she still has the right to determine if it's real or not. And I believe it could have been handled in a very different way. For this being my first impression of the hotel it wasn't a great one. Only for the fact of the location and the nice room I wouldn't be recommending this hotel. However I won't let it put me off recommending the hotel or returning. I'll just know next time to prepare myself for the not so great customer service.

title: “Small but excellent, especially for price and location”
text: My room barely had enough room for a queen bed, desk and a small amount of walking room but this was precisely what I needed as I was at a conference all day and wanted to wander around downtown in the evening. The price was great given its quality and location, just a few blocks from South Street and everything in downtown was in walking distance. During the night I could hear some of the street traffic below but the bed was comfy and I was pretty tired by the end of the night so slept well.

title: “Nice hotel”
text:
This is the second time we stayed in this hotel. My husband ran the Rock N' Roll Marathon in San Jose this past October and the hotel is conveniently located. It is close to the Convention Center and also we could just walk to the starting line. The finish line was pretty much cross the street from the hotel. The rooms are very comfortable. Wi-Fii is not complimentary but it would if you sign up for their loyalty membership.
After the marathon we decided to have brunch at their restaurant but we found it expensive for what they served. We went to other hotels with a superior menu for the same price or cheaper.

title: “Excellent location & charming hotel”
text: We spent 2 separate nights, with a night in Victoria in between. The first night we had the jacuzzi suite on the 6th floor. Lovely large room and nice jet tub for 2. This room had partial view down Pine St. to ocean. The second night we opted for the basic queen. A very small, but clean and perfectly adequate accomodation. This one was on 12th floor, so really nice & quiet that far up from the street. Excellent location with a quick 7 blocks to Pike's Public Market and only a few blocks to Monorail going to Space Needle. The staff were all very friendly and helpful. As an added review I would suggest Elliott's for dinner, right on the water, wooonderful food!! Skip The Fisherman's restaurant down the street from it (mediocre at best & in similar price range) and as far as transportation to/from airport, the Gray Line Airporter Shuttle is fine coming from airport, but DO NOT get the round trip ticket(s), as the bus never showed up for us after waiting over an hour and finally rushing to take a cab.

title: “A hotel with a historical atmosphere, but ask for a room away from the elevators”
text:
I paid about USD 350 for a large room in this hotel. So quite expensive. Admittedly, the room was large and spacious and - despite the reservations expressed by others about the shower - I thought the bathroom was perfectly fine. I was also impressed by the high definition television, the only one I encountered in the three hotels I visited during my vacation in the USA. This hotel was renovated in 2009 and it bears many of the hallmarks of a high tech hostelry.
But the thing that surprised me about the staff of the Westin St Francis was that they allocated me a room right next to one of the outside elevators (which are used frequently right into the early hours of the morning). I thought it a bit strange - given the amount of money I'd invested for a single night's stay - that they did not at least give me a more silent room. I also paid extra bucks for a view of the bay from my room ; but I found that the panorama from my window offered only the tiniest glimpse of San Francisco Bay.
Although the breakfast cost me USD 25, I thought it was well worth the money. There's a veritable smorsgasbord of food choices available, buffet style, in the breakfast room. The choices were so luxurious that I didn't need to eat again that day until evening-time. 
This hotel exudes a sense of history. Indeed there are several exhibits in the lobby of correspondence received from Winston Churchill, Ronald Reagan, Queen Elizabeth's Equerry respectively about various official stays in the St. Francis. This is a hotel in the grand tradition. So, even though I may have been disappointed by my room allocation, it's hard not to like the place. 
And the location - on Union Square - is just so convenient for many of the major shops including Macys, Ghirardelli Chocolates and Bloomingdales. Also, if you turn right when you walk out of the main entrance to the hotel, cross the road fifty yards further down the Square at the traffic lights, you'll find an Italian restaurant/bistro bar (whose name eludes me) on the right which is really great. Superb selection of Californian wheat beers and exquisitely cooked pasta dishes at competitive prices.

title: “GREAT GREAT GREAT HOTEL And AREA!!!!”
text: My husband and I did a 8 night stay in Southern California (after this we went to LA and stayed at another ‘Starwood hotel’ – the ‘W Westwood’- also a top pick of mine) The US Grant is very nice, upscale everything. The lobby is gorgeous, the people were courteousand had much knowledge about the area. This hotel is in the PERFECT location to everything! I can’t stress this enough We were in walking distance to Petco Park, to the Pier, to the famous SD Zoo, to Balboa Park, great restaurants, shopping, bars etc. The hotel is in the Gas Lamp district…there is an outdoor mall right across the street with great stores, restaurants, bars, entertainment, etc. This hotel was in the best possible location, is clean, beautiful, everything you need! The only thing our particular room lacked was a standing mirror- being so used to getting dressed with one I found it odd. The room itself is beautiful- I agree with what another review said about not much counter space in the bathroom- but there was plenty of it elsewhere. I would absolutely advise anyone who is looking to stay in SD to stay here…..I hope to be back again!

title: “Small but Efficient Space”
text: I stayed at the Sofia hotel while attending a conference at the San Diego convention center. The hotel is located within walking distance of the convention center (about a ten minute walk), and pretty much any store or restaurant that you could ever need can be found within a few blocks of the hotel. There is a greyhound station in the same block as the hotel, so you are bound to find some interesting characters milling about, but I didn't have any problems with any of them. The hotel itself is nicely updated from its previous incarnation as the once grand but recently seedy pickwick hotel. The rooms themselves are very small, but they have an efficient layout (very European). My room had a nice closet unit that efficiently stored the safe, iron/ironing board, my suitcase, and my hanging clothes (enough for four days). However, if I had clothes for a longer stay, or if my wife had joined me, it would have been a very tight squeeze. Also, the bathroom layout was such that only a sliding door separated the toilet and shower from the rest of the room. If you are traveling with a companion and have an aversion to hearing them when they are in the bathroom, then this hotel is not for you. Overall, the hotel was nicely decorated, the staff was pleasant, my room was smartly layed out, and the location was perfect for doing business downtown. It was more than adequate for my needs.

title: “Stylish but on the low end of boutique....”
text:
Stylish and trying but doesn't live up to the Thomson Chain brand and is on the lower end of boutique hotels. No room service on the weekends.....carpetting in the rooms needs cleaning (this on the basis of two rooms)....the room bathrooms have a door facing the bed and the entire entrance (wall and door) of the bathroom is transparent - even if you are travelling with a very close companion, this becomes frankly weird. 
No fan in the bathroom (so a long shower fills the room with steam), ventilation uneven in the room (super cold or no air at all)....no coffee maker in the room, and your closet light is connected to the neighbors - so when you walk by the closet you and their light goes on. They walk by their closet, your light goes on! Digital signal on the television (not that you are in NYC to watch tv but....) is slow and uneven. 
Limited food in the area - remember it's the financial district - but it's close to the Seaport which is a really nice part of the city, fewer tourists and calmer, quieter etc. On the positive side it's quiet and the staff is super helpful.
Like this hotel enough but the weird bathroom issue is enough to have me stay away. Boutique hotel? At between 325.00 a night they need to do better.

title: “Lack of Customer Service means everything”
text:
I have waited almost 3 weeks to write this review as my experience and stay the the Renaissance Los Angeles was not a pleasant one, and as you can see from my many reviews I am usually an upbeat and positive type of guy. 
As a Marriott Gold Member I am a dedicated Marriott patron. We had reservations for my son and I for one night before flying back home. Our reservation was a guarantee for 2 beds and was paid for on a Marriott Certificate, one they gave me for staying so many nights in a designated period of time. 
From the time I walked into this hotel, I don't know if it was because I had my 10 year old son with me or was a "non-paying" guest, but we were treated like second class citizens. The front desk clerk didn't say more than two words to us during check in and when questioned, answered in a curt, unprofessional manner. They told me that my room only had one bed - even though we had a guarantee for 2 beds. When I questioned her, she laughed at me and told me those guarantees didn't mean anything. We had no amenities explained to us, like location of Club Lounge, restuarant options, etc. Frankly they had no interest in making sure we had a pleasant stay. 
Feeling a little frustrated I emailed the hotel after my arrival home and questioned their policy on the guaranteed room. While they couldn't answer me directly, they were kind enough to say they would refund the certificate we used and the $46 we spent on dinner in their restaurant. I was feeling much better and ready to move on. However, now over 2 weeks later, no refund, no re-issued certificate and no response from the hotel. While not every hotel employee can be the tops, I am seeing a patern of employees who really have a lack of customer service.
I have stayed several times at the Marriott LAX next door and found it to be a wonderful property. Next visit to LAX will not be at the Renaissance, even with a free Certificate.

title: “Great place to stay for Indy 500”
text: I stayed here as part of a group for the 2012 Indy 500 and I had a fantastic experience. Even with how many people were staying at the hotel and surrounding area, I never waited more than 5 minutes for my valeted car, there was always someone waiting in the foyer to greet you and there always seemed to be a seat available at the restaurant or lobby bar. The longest I had to wait was at Starbucks at 5 am the morning of the race! I only had one downside, and it's really for meeting planners or people planning to ship boxes to yourself at the hotel; you are charged by the weight of your packages if you ship them to yourself, so be careful!

title: “Good business hotel”
text:
I recently returned from a three-night stay at the Hyatt Regency Denver Tech Centre with three old school friends, who were in Denver for our annual baseball trip. 
The four of us found the hotel to be fine overall for what it is, which is primarily a business hotel. The hotel is about 25 minutes southeast of downtown Denver just off I-25 and is also a 10-minute walk from the Belleview stop on the light rail. Check-in was fast and we found the hotel's facilities to be on par with other Hyatt's we have stayed at and other hotels of the same class. The breakfast buffet offered in the cafe was above average and the sports bar looked promising (10 draft beers, shuffleboard, pool, plenty of TVs), although we did not actually get a chance to partake ourselves. Something that caught us off guard was having to pay $10/day to park at what is decidedly a suburban location well removed from denser areas of Denver.
Our rooms were pretty standard issue with sufficient storage space and comfortable beds. The rooms were clean and housekeeping was very good overall. However, both rooms suffered from weak cooling systems that took an extraordinary amount of effort to cool the rooms into the upper 70's the first 24 hours we were there despite having the systems cranked to full blast. When reported to hotel staff, they shrugged it off and declined to relocate part of our group into another room. 
Overall, I think the consensus of our group was that the Hyatt Regency Tech Centre was a fine, if not spectacular hotel. If my travels brought me back to this hotel though, I would definitely stay there again.

title: “Mike at front desk goes extra mile to help.”
text: First time staying here. Unloaded bags out front, checked in, and when going back to park car it was dead. Mike S at front desk got jumper cables for me, called AAA, and even waited 30 mins after his shift to make sure tow truck arrived. Couldn't have been nicer, very impressed.

title: “Upgrade to concierge”
text: It is worth the upgrade to concierge level. For hotels in the city this offers a very spacious size room and luxury full bath and dressing area. Charging for parking your vehicle is high but that is throughout NYC. Great views of Battery Park and Statue of liberty. On weekends neighborhood is quiet. The appetizers available mid morning and mid afternoon are worth the upgrade for concierge level. As always Ritz service is superior! We even dined downstairs and it was not "hotel food" but the Ritz never is. I would say this is a great place for business travel if working near Battery Park and a great quiet place to stay on weekends for solo, couples or family.

title: “Great location, fabulously helpful staff”
text: We spent 2 nights here and it was very nice. We were able to walk to most of the things we wanted to do. Staff was wonderfully helpful and friendly. I was disappointed that they didn't us duvet covers as advertised. They just folded the sheets over the comforter.

title: “A Relaxing Sanctuary from the Comic-Con Madness!”
text: Comic-con is a lot of fun, but there are a lot of people crammed into one convention center. Racing around to get to panels, waiting in line, and putting up with the crowds in general can be exhausting... so it was amazing to be able to come back to our room at the Westin where everything was clean, beautiful, and peaceful.

title: “excellent service continues”
text: The hotel continues to refurbish and upgrade the rooms. The hotel is conveniently located near my office. Annmara Gayle and the guest relations ladies couldnt be any nicer and more professional. Sean Olmstead is a real professional and very responsive. The hotel is my home-away-from-home in the New York area. Free wifi in the rooms would be a nice service to include. My wife loves the bed linens.

title: “Lovely hotel, great location, wonderful price!”
text: My husband and I wanted a place to stay that was close to Inner Harbor without costing a fortune. Mt.Vernon fit the bill. The owners have done a commendable job renovating the building which was formerly a YMCA. Our room was cozy and clean; we only had to ask for more tissues which were promptly brought to the room. The hot breakfast was a real plus as well, including scrambled eggs, hot apples, breakfast potatoes with peppers and onions, biscuits and gravy. There was also a selection of cereals and breads. You can park across the street in a garage with full in and out privileges for $10 a night! The free Walters Museum is only a few blocks away. We'd definitely stay here again!

title: “Excellent! A charming, comfy, cozy stay, near most everything.”
text: My husband and I were in LA for business but wanted to stay somewhere unique. Villa Delle Stelle was the perfect place. We stayed in the La Petite Suite, which was cozy but so charming and comfortable. Although it is situated in the middle, between two other residences, we never heard the neighbors. The suite was well decorated and I've never slept on such soft sheets nor had towels as plush in any hotel. They really did everything right. Not being familiar with the area, we drove to dinner and other excursions. The restaurant recommendations they gave (handy book in the room) were fantastic. It was a great experience, in a convenient location, close to so much. We'd definitely stay there on our next LA trip.

title: “Loved this Hilton!”
text:
Despite some of the scary reviews, my finace and I loved this hotel! The location was ideal, the rooms were clean, and the view was very nice!
The location is great. You about a 2 minute walk from Chinatown, a 5 minute walk from North Beach (all the Italian places) and a 15 minute walk from Union Square.
The ONLY thing that wasn't great is the fact that we couldn't get a room with one king bed, we got two doubles, but that's a chance you take when booking through priceline.
The view was great! We were on the 21st floor, and could see the entire city beneath us.
The concierge was VERY helpful. He always had good reccomendations when we asked where to go, and mapped out everythign with detail! He was fabulous.
The staff was actually pretty nice. They get busy, but try their best to accomadate you.
Cute coffe place inside too for morning cofee and pastries!
We'll be staying here again!

title: “Decent stay for the price”
text:
We stayed 3 nights in August. Chose this hotel because of value and location. Close enough to walk to the Mall. 
We drove down from NY. Valet took our car ($33 a day with in and out privileges). Porter helped take all our stuff. Check in went smoothly, got a room facing the front of the hotel (the back side faces an office building so there is no natural light). 
The room was fine but felt very wet/humid. We asked maintenance to check the room. The a/c was working but apparently they had just shampooed the carpet and couch. 
Otherwise, the bed was very comfortable. We could hear people through a vent so soundproofing isnt great though they weren't noisy at night. There is a room safe, frig, microwave and coffee maker. Internet costs 15 a day (not wifi but ethernet plug in your room) but there are kiosks in the lobby for you to check emails. 
Breakfast was very good. Held in the restaurant in the lobby. Lots of choices. Fresh cooked egg line was great. The cooks would do six or seven orders and get them right with a smile. As others mentioned, lines can be long but we never had a problem. Lots of fresh fruit, cereal, oatmeal, grits, muffins, bagels, etc. No problem with getting a table. Coffee was just ok but there is a Starbucks across the street from the hotel. 
Swimming pool was small but my 5 year old enjoyed it. A bit cold for my taste but fine. There is a whirlpool also and a small gym.
We walked to the Natural History building in the Mall which was a decent walk. The other days (weekend), we just drove down and parked along the Mall. 
Checkout was fine, no problems with the bill.
Overall, we had a good stay at the Embassy Suites. Good value for what you pay for.

title: “Misleading”
text:
While the lobby and rooms appear to be above average, we were disappointed with the cleanliness, service, and ammenities. Upon checkin, I informed the clerk that I was a AAA member and showed her my card. She told me it was "too late" to apply the discount. I find this hard to believe, being that things like mini-bars and movie rentals can be added at a later time.. why wouldn't a discount work the same way?
The room was comfortable; however, my bathroom had no hair dryer and the tub still had an opened, previously used bar of soap sitting on the edge. It obviously hadn't been cleaned. If I had planned on staying at this hotel for more than one night, I would have left at that point and found another hotel.
Additionally, the hotel charges for WiFi, even for HiltonHonors members.

title: “Perfect for a theater trip”
text: We stayed at the Muse the end of August when we were in New York to see a show. The location is perfect and we were able to walk everywhere. We upgraded to a suite for 1/2 price and had plenty of room. The room was very clean and the staff friendly and helpful. The concierge sent a complimentary bottle of wine to our room when he found out it was my wife's birthday. Despite being just off Broadway it was very quite in our room.

title: “Great hotel in San Francisco”
text: If you want to stay at a really nice hotel with a good location in San Francisco, I suggest you stay at Orchard Garden Hotel. It is only three years old and very nicely decorated. The room was not that big, but it had a big bathroom, bath robes, safe, a docking station for my iPod and more. The staff was very friendly and helped us both with a nice restaurant (Sam's Grill and Seafood) as well as direction when we headed off to the airport. The hotel is located just next to the gates to Chinatown.

title: “Town & County Hotel”
text: I had a lovely stay at the Town & Country Hotel. I loved walking the grounds and seeing all of the beautiful roses. I was there on business, but wish I could have spent more time. The hotel is very centrally located and the staff is pleasant and helpful. The rooms are comfy and cozy.

title: “OK, but doesn't live up to expectations”
text:
The photos and reviews make this seem much better than it is. Let me first say, that the hotel is clean and comfortable - I don't have real complaints - but I also don't think it was special.
The staff was warm and helpful and the decor is dark and sexy. 
The first room I was given had been forced open at one time - you could see the marks from the crow bar at the door and you could see into the room from the hall at the point of entry. I was moved to another room, which was supposed to be a queen. I am a big shopper, so I carry a tape measurer with me at all times - it was not a queen bed. There are also no full length mirrors in any of the rooms. 
The walls were not insulated, so I could hear the neighbor sliding hangers across the bar in the closet and anytime someone walked down the hall.
The good points are the decor and service. The room was comfortable enough and pitch black, so sleeping was easy. 
It was more interesting than a generic chain hotel, but I don't think I'd spend the money to go back.

title: “It may be one of the oldest 'W' Hotels, but it has the fastest lifts”
text:
OK, let me admit it at the start - I like W Hotels. If there is a W in the city I am visiting I will stay in it. BUT, they do vary across the world with the newer ones a lot better than the older ones. This W is one of the originals and it is beginning to show its age in the rooms. It is not as luxurious or as well equipped and the fittings are a bit tired/worn. The restaurant was up to scratch, great breakfast with unlimited strong coffee. Room service was very quick the few times I used it.
As ever it is the staff (not the rooms) that make a hotel and they were top notch. What I like about them is that you can sit at the bar on your own and they know just how intrusive to be. Like most W bars this one was used by non-residents so there is always a great vibe and someone to chat to. Excellent cocktails and draft beers at the usual expensive Seattle prices. The DJ set is definitely an afterthought, the poor guy has a temporary table and speakers, rather than a proper booth. A bit like a DJ at a UK wedding..... 
Special note: I stayed on 19th floor and never waited more than 10 seconds for a lift - they must have some good software controlling them!

title: “Urban Oasis in City”
text:
I stayed here for 4 nights as part of a corp. conference. The venue is perfect for the many conferences weddings and bar mitvas that go on there: nice facilities and great service.
The hotel's common rooms have the feel of a gentlemen's club with stuffed animals mounted on the walls, but the rooms have neutral decor and most windows actually touch the trees in a forest, giving the room the feel of a cozy tree house. (This, however, makes mobile phone access from rooms tricky). There's a spa, two pools, a nice jogging track and health club. There's a free shuttle leaving every 1.5 hours to and from the Galleria shopping area-- but you have to tell the valet or concierge you wish to take it.
There is free cable and WIFI Internet access in the rooms. The rooms are reasonably sized but not huge. The bathrooms are small and the shower heads just let out a trickle of water. The hairdryer is a small, travel size one. The food in the restaurant is good but the menu is small. They have 24 hour room service. 
The conference faciilties are excellent. Comfy chairs and flat screen pasma video screens in each conf. room. We had a choice of three dishes for lunch we had to order in advance and got our meals delivered in an adjacent conf. room. A butler was constantly bringing in snacks and drinks throughout the day. 
The staff are excellent. The receptionist and bellboy remembered my name throuohout my stay. The receptionist even came running out to offer me a bottle of water when he saw me waiting for the shuttle outside. I'd stay here again in a heartbeat.

title: “Magnificent Location”
text:
Incredible location right on Michigan Avenue in the heart of the Magnificent Mile, just a couple of blocks north of the river. Shopping, eateries, and attractions all closeby.
Our room in the new tower was clean and decent size for Chicago (where the average hotel room is tiny) with a small but adequate bathroom. An in-room kiosk with internet service is nice for viewing information about the hotel and area attractions, etc. A guest has the ability to check out using the kiosk, but we did not since we had bags for the bell stand to hold.
Navigating between the historic and new towers was confusing (the pool and fitness area are located in the historic tower), as the stairs and elevators don't service all floors of both towers (I take the stairs whenever possible). Looked exhaustively for an ice machine but had to call the front desk to ask nearest location (wasn't listed on map or in hotel binder in room); nearest location was 7th floor—we were on the 17th! This was very inconvenient. 
We got a very good (internet) rate (and on top of that got a AAA discount) on a busy weekend (spring break/Easter) and we not charged for anything we didn't receive—but be careful since you'll pay hidden fees if you use the minibar, WiFi, etc. Used valet parking due to arriving late and not being able to arrive via commuter train. It was expensive ($57—but normal for the area) but the service was AWESOME and quick and I was confident my car was safe as it was in an enclosed, underground garage. When we were ready to leave and collect our vehicle, it took mere minutes and we were downstairs in the parking garage and checking out our car was seamless. Very nice and convenient.
The staff was pleasant and accommodating, both during check-in and check-out, and the concierge was very helpful when we inquired about good local cuisine that's not well-known to tourists. We had a great experience at dinner on the advice of the nice gentleman helping us!
ONLY NEGATIVE: While the pool facility is beautiful (very large, Grecian-inspired with lots of seating and cool, elevated viewing area—see pic on website), my kids encountered COCKROACHES in and around the pool area. I didn't swim, but noticed the insects were very large and alive when pointed out to me. This ruined the experience for my kids and it's the one thing they remember and tell everyone when asked how their spring break stay was in Chicago. :-(

title: “Pretty good hotel except the coffee is terrible”
text: This is a great hotel for business stays. The food service was excellent, great attitude. The ladies that checked us in in the late afternoon were not very friendly and did not improve as our trip progressed. They need to work on their coffee. There were 7 of us and not one of us could stand the taste of their coffee, it tasted watered-down. We will definitely go back because for the most part this was a good hotel, good location and a good value for the money.

title: “Fantastic Hotel - Will stay again!!!”
text: What a great place! located near everything you want and need to see in Boston. Lovely old charm, wonderful & helpful staff, very comfortable & clean rooms with all the nice amenities! Computers for guest use in the lobby. 24hr coffee/tea in lobby as well. Comfy big chairs and couches to read the morning paper in the lobby. We walked to Fanuiel Hall, super Pubs, restaurants, historic sights, the harbor, took the subway to Harvard, walked to Beacon Hill, Newberry, the Commons. Our favorite area was the North End...only 15 min walk from the Hotel. LOVE the coffees and pastries at Mike's and Modern Pastry too. the BEST ever!! Such a friendly city....this Hotel is not to be missed. You do not need a car or a taxi. You are in the heart of this lovely historic city!!!!! I highly suggest you stay nowhere else! did I mention the hotel rate is cheaper than most? can't beat it!

title: “Overall great value”
text: Great golf! The room was a little noises. I could hear other guest talking in the adjacent room and walking in the room above me.

title: “the sheets were crunchy”
text: OK. my husband and i stayed here just a random saturday night, after dinner and drinks in downtown indy. i'm not sure if we're just spoiled by our amazing bed at home... but the bed was very uncomfortable. and the sheets were crunchy. and, by accident, the bottom sheet came untucked and there was blood stain on the mattress! uck! paint was peeling off the vanity in the bathroom. room was small. view was nothing spectacular. honestly, we recently stayed at the sheraton in downtown indy and it was a much comfy-ier experience. rooms are more updated at the sheraton (and much better view of downtown indy). with all of that being said, the service at the westin was attentive and friendly. but save the money. stay at a different hotel in downtown indy.

title: “Yes!”
text:
My son and new daughter-in-law just had their wedding reception at The St. Anthony Hotel, plus most of the wedding guests stayed at the St. Anthony. From the moment I stepped into The St. Anthony, the staff was welcoming and helpful beyond measure. Huge thanks to Barb, the catering sales manager, Nelda, the conference coordinator, Shelly at reservations, Daniel at check-in, David, our concierge, Celia of the housekeeping staff, Wanda, Samantha and so many others. Each of these individuals was extraordinarily professional, cheerful and helpful--and very good at what they do. We had an issue with one room, which was not appropriate for my physically-challenged father (not the fault of the St. Anthony staff). On a completely sold-out, St. Patrick's Day, spring-break, three-wedding weekend, Nelda managed to find the perfect solution to accommodate my father's needs. The wedding reception was in the Anacosha Room which was transformed into the perfect space for celebrating our special event and beautifully appointed in every way.
The hotel is charming and grand, an old-style Texas hotel boasting a stunningly beautiful lobby, which is a wonderful venue for cocktails or sitting and visiting in the beautiful and comfortable period furniture. Our room was a double queen, double bath, double-closet--very roomy and comfortable. Our two, non-identical bathrooms were definitely "vintage" with huge-old style tubs, slightly curved at the bottom, a step into the past, but delightfully so. Beds were very comfortable. Hotel is nicely located, across the street from Travis Park, minutes to the river-walk and countless restaurants, and a short walk to so many of the downtown sites of San Antonio. 
I stayed at the St. Anthony for a week and felt like I gained a new family. I will definitely return!

title: “Newer Hotel, Great Price”
text: I stayed at the Comfort Inn and Suites in Hollywood, CA during the All Star Game. The hotel is a fairly new hotel with little signs of wear and tear. The price was great!!! The location was great!!! Parking isn't a problem at all. Well, it wasn't for us. You can walk to the subway and Hollywood Blvd. It's just a block over. Sunset Strip, Hollywood High School, and Mann's Theater are all a couple of blocks away. Universal Studies is a short ride away like 5 minutes. The lobby is small and so is the pool. So if your looking for a hotel with many bells....this is not the one. If your looking for a nice, clean, affordable place in the hollywood area. You have the perfect spot. As a matter of fact. The hotel was blocked during the Oscar's, which is one block over because the cast of Lord of The Ring's leased it.

title: “5+ star property but service....??”
text:
I am going to write a review contrary to what everyone else has written based on our experience at this hotel when we stayed there in the first half of August. 
Me and my brother were in NYC on a business trip and had booked a Large twin room. We reached the hotel in the afternoon and asked for a suite upgrade. The online rate was 340++ and the upgrade was another $100. We said what the hell and took the suite. 
When we got to the room we had expected something a lot more. The check in manager did not explain that this was going to be a studio suite, which is what it was. Single room with a sitting area and a bed a bit ahead on the left. As the room had just 1 bed we asked for an extra bed to be put in. Now when you do this keep in mind a good part of the living room will be blocked off with the bed. So I am not sure if the upgrade is worth it especially if you want 2 beds in the room. 
We checked in and wanted to check our email. The internet was worse than a dial up line. The connection kept dropping. We attributed it to the time of the day and left it at that. Next morning we had a meeting and then had a few hours before our next meeting so both of us got to the room to get some work done. Again same issue. The internet would either not work or was absolutely crawling. We called tech support and they reset the internet in our room but still the same problem; slower than a dial up line. 
So I called the front desk and asked for the manager as by now I was pretty irritated. Here we are paying $500 a night and we cant even get reliable internet!!. She said that it maybe an issue with the internet in our room and offered to change our room and so asked us to pack our bags and leave them ready and she would transfer them to the new room when it got ready. 
We packed all and left for our meetings. We get back at 930 PM, take our new room keys and go the the new suite on the 9th floor, room 915. This room was smaller than the earlier one. Maybe the dimensions are same but the way it was set up you at least 10-15% less space in this room that the earlier one (1225). So a tip, if you are going to get a suite dont get the ones ending in 15. 
My brother opened his office bag and realized that his ipad was missing!! How could this be? So I checked my bag; we both checked out suit case and no ipad. So we called the front desk and asked them to check if in case the ipad was left in the room (my brother was 99.99% sure that he put it in his bag). The manager told us that it was too late to call the other room (930 PM) and so he would check with the guest after 9 AM in the morning. This was fine but his tone and attitude was not right. 
The new room then had a litany of issues. They did not transfer the extra bed to this room. By the time we called at 930 PM there was no housekeeping staff at the hotel any more. The room has no bars of soap either on the wash basin or inside the shower. The living room area TV had no remote control. But the internet was working faster :). We had successfully jumped from the frying pan into the fire. 
So I called the manager again and asked him to give the email ID of the GM of the hotel so that I could email him about the ipad issue as well as the other things. He actually told me that he did not have his bosses email ID!!!! This was a joke. I told him that he must be kidding and that if he did not give me the GM's email ID this matter was then moving to Hyatt corporate. Suddenly he found the email and gave it to me!! 
Here is the thing. A guest who is paying Andaz rates does not have time to waste to send an email to the hotel GM. If he is asking for the email ID it is better to give it to him rather than come up with a lame excuse that he does not have it. I did email the GM about the issues and requested him to look into it. 
The next morning the manager in charge came to meet us and explained that he would be looking for the ipad and look at the other issues personally. We returned at around 630 PM that day and the manager in charge told us that unfortunately they did not find the ipad!! This was unbelievable. 
In the hotel's defense, the GM that evening informed us that the hotel would be taking off the value from our bill ($650). This was good as the hotel did own up the responsibility and made good the loss and saved the issue from snow balling.
Besides the above there were lots more niggling issues at the hotel. I already informed earlier that a new room having no soap, no remote control etc. The breakfast quality at the hotel is both over priced and poor service. Or let me rephrase the service was extremely cold. The staff at the restaurant had a chip on their shoulder, why I don't know. 
When you pay $500 a night you are paying almost top dollar and there are a whole host of hotels that would have better service than Andaz. Maybe not in the wall st area but surely in Soho and of course mid town. 
I will give Andaz one more chance, not at Wall Street but at 5th Avenue. After that its back to starwood. Hyatt must realize that the hard asset is great. It is the soft asset that is extremely important at a high end hotel. Our experience at Andaz was very disappointing. I only hope that this is an aberration.

title: “It used to be great. Now, maybe a "meh."”
text:
This used to be my favorite hotel in LA. So off-beat, so well located, so friendly. So it's really a tarted-up motel, so what? It's still great. That was my attitude.
You have to wonder where they went wrong.
We tried to check in on a Sunday night. I know, that's when the least capable manager is on duty but this one takes the cake. Icily "polite" she still managed to convey in no uncertain terms that my wife's request for an extra bed was not only not going to be met, it amounted to an insult to everyone in the hotel, and it showed how unbelievably stupid we were to even request it.
It was unnerving.
Things did get better when the day-shift crew came in and the usual shiny, happy attitude returned, but by then the damage was done. By then the once charming hotel was exposed as an over-priced, over-hyped motel on Fairfax.
At least "Tart" the attached restaurant is as good as ever.
Isn't it terrible what a single person with a bad attitude can do to your reputation?
Avoid if possible.

title: “Amazing location and very satisfied and wonderful hotel”
text: We are all very happy how wonderful the service and very closed to time square about 2 minutes closed to everything. The room are very clean and clean bed and we were totally amazed. We sure will be coming back to this hotel.

title: “Excellent service!!!”
text: The service at Grand Del Mar is impeccable - you will not find better. The grounds are beautiful, the food is great and the golf course is nice (the caddies will impress you with their knowledge of the local vegetation). The only downside that I can think of is that the hotel is about 15 minutes to the beach.

title: “Mixed feelings”
text:
We stayed 23rd-25th of January. My husband and I were getting away from our kids for a little R & R. Husband picked this hotel because of other reviews on this site. We booked through the hotel web site directly and got a government rate which made this hotel affordable to us on our tight budget. With the government rate we received free valet parking and free ($5.00 worth per person, each day) of food from the Starbucks located in the hotel. Husband signed up for the select guest program before making the reservation which gave us the bonus of robes to wear, turn-down service and two complementary drinks in the morning each day with a newspaper of choice. We were also given the options of picking hotel room area because of being a select guest. 
We requested a higher floor and away from elevators. We were given a room on the 12th floor. We also received a corner room, so we had windows on two sides of the building. We had a fantastic view of Indianapolis. Since we had a corner room, our room was probably larger than most rooms. It was very nicely decorated and the king size bed was very comfortable, especially if you like firm mattresses. The bathroom is very small and hard to maneuver in. It has a pedestal sink, so there is no room to put any of your personal hygiene items. Two people can not get ready at the same time in the bathroom. The bathroom door opens into the bathroom, so you have to close it to be able to stand in front of the sink to use the mirror. There is no fan, and since the bathroom is so small, it gets very steamy very fast. A curved shower curtain bar would be of great help to give more room in the shower, because it's a tight fit to shower (we are tall, skinny people). When we checked in, one light bulb was out in the bathroom and I thought the staff would replace it the next day, but they didn't. Not worth complaining about. 
The hotel is connected to Circle City Mall, so it's very useful to be able to walk through the mall to get to other areas in the city when it's so cold outside. We were able to walk just a couple of blocks outside to get to the ISO and to visit the Soldiers & Sailor's Monument Museum and btw there is a elevator that takes you up in the monument for 1.00 (we have lived in the area for 3 years and never knew you could go up in the monument!)
They have a decent exercise room, which we used one morning and it was sufficient to what we use at our YMCA. It got quite crowded around 9a.m. on Saturday morning, so we were glad to have gotten there a little before that. They have a small pool area that we did not use, everyone said the water was warm.
Our stay would have been perfect, except that there was some sort of convention in the area in which many, many, many teens had taken over the hotel. (Remember we were trying to get away from our two teens and our young one). For some reason on both Friday & Saturday night, teens were running around on the 12th floor making lots of noise. On Saturday night, husband called and requested that someone take care of it. 
In addition, Friday night one elevator was not working in the west tower, which is where we were, and we were late getting to our activity due to the waiting of an elevator. (we were on the 12th floor). 
Saturday, there was an elevator out in both the east and west tower. We had rushed ourselves to get to the lobby by the 12p.m. check out time and ended up waiting quite a bit on the west side for an elevator. After 10 minutes, we walked to the east tower and waited another 10 minutes, when the elevator opened, it was full of people. 2 more elevators came to the 12th floor and they also were full. I finally called to the front desk to tell them that we had been trying to get to the lobby for 1/2 hour to check out and couldn't get an elevator. We finally got an elevator and had to squeeze on with our luggage. It turns out that people had been waiting so long to get an elevator that was going down, that they started hopping on the elevator even if it was going up because they knew at some point it would go back down again, hence the reason it kept coming up to the 12th floor and it was full. 
When we finally got down to the front desk to check out. The staff had no idea that there was such a problem getting an elevator. (they knew that two of their elevators were out-they just didn't know that people were getting on when it was going up just to come back down again) 
I was confused why they (the hotel staff) weren't "problem solving" and maybe calling their guests to say that there was a problem with elevators and that they had extended check out time or putting an employee in each elevator to help control the flow of traffic.
The whole lobby was filled with these teens and their groups all waiting for their transportation, it was a total mess. The gal checking us out said that she would call ahead and request our car for us. It still took 45 minutes for us to finally get our car. The whole process was total chaos and then on top of it, the gal trying to get our car couldn't figure out how to unlock the car properly and so the car alarm kept going off when she tried to start it, and instead of coming to get some help right away she kept trying to figure out. Finally someone came to get my husband to tell him what was going on and so my husband had to go and get his own car!
The hotel offered us a free upgrade. I thought they were offering us a free night to try the hotel again, but they were only offering us a free upgrade on a room. This was disappointing because we do live in the area and I am just not sure if I could recommend the hotel again because I am not sure if this is norm for them or it was just a fluke because they couldn't handle all these teens that were in town.

title: “Home Away from Home”
text: This was our first stay at this hotel. We absolutely loved it! The hotel is beautiful, the location is great and the staff is simply amazing. Upon check-in, the staff greeted us with a smile, by our names and with warm fresh baked cookies. :) Great referral by the front desk staff for dinner. Our room was spacious, well decorated and very clean and comfortable. In all of my travels, I have never had a complimentary breakfast so wonderful. The breakfast host was attentive and very friendly. This will be our new Dallas home away from home. Thank you for your hospitality.

title: “Great hotel”
text: Stayed at this Marriott, on a family road trip to Dallas. The staff was very friendly and helpful. There is a really chic Bistro in the lobby with modern furniture. The room was nice with the great "Marriott beds". Had a nice view of the pool from my window. The only complaint I have is there was no a/c in the hallways, and on the elevator, and July in Dallas, it was 102 outside !

title: “Nice, but not impressed, especially for a Hilton.”
text:
First off, I am writing this review based from the opinion as a Hilton Diamond member. I will say that the room rate was pretty low in comparison to local Hilton properties, but at the same time, I got alot less for my money. My room was pretty small, and the bathroom was smaller, to the point that the sink literaly starts to extend over the tub. The hotel does offer snacks and breakfast to Diamond members on their 10th floor. The snacks are snacks, but when i stayed, the room was completely crowded, and it was the first time I have seen packs of children in an executive lounge. The breakfast selection was limited, with no proteins except hard boiled eggs I believe. Again, it was packed. There were 8 people in front of me trying to get a cup of coffee, and I retreated to my room to make a cup there, and avoid all the crazyness. 
If you are in the area to see the sights, then the location is great for this facility. If desire space, and the full Diamond treatment, I would not recommend this hotel. You will encounter DC traffic if driving, so add an additional 30-45 minutes to get to and from this hotel. Be ready to pay $34 to park your car, per night also. I had to go get a print off of my receipt, due to the hotel being paperless. Good luck getting out of the parking garage, my keys failed to work, and I had to show my receipt to the attendant to show I had paid for parking, then sign something, to get out. Maybe it was just a fluke, but still, it was frustrating, and time consuming.

title: “Great hotel”
text: After reading the reviews on this site, we changed our reservation from the Dell to the Pacific Terrace. The hotel was as wonderful as the reviews say, and we highly recommend staying there. The hotel is right on the beach with lots of good people watching opportunities on the jogging path right next to the property. The pool was the perfect temperature and the hot tub was hoooooot!! Go and stay there!

title: “Concierge TLC”
text:
I have great things to say about the Concierge desk. We exchanged wonderfully informative emails before my trip. I got deliciously perfect sushi recommendations while there. They knew my name (even across shift--changes at the desk) and were helpful and friendly at every turn - even assisting us with a Cubs ticket upgrade. 
We were put into a non-traditional room designed for handicap accessibility, when we questioned if there was another room with a tub, there was not, but we got cookies and juice sent to our room. They took care of us and the location can't be beat.

title: “Institutional, Great Service, But Convention Oriented Hotel”
text:
