This is a huge, institutional convention resort. This is not a cozy place. It's huge and impersonal. The service was some of the best I've experienced in recent memory. The service was, in fact, so persistent it was actually annoying at times. For instance, we would recieve a call on our voice mail after every time room service was delivered, or extra towels were delivered, or after we asked for an extra pillow. While we appreciate their concern, it gets old after a week, multiple times a day. 
There was only 1 bar in the whole hotel, other than in the restaurants. There were conventions there when we stayed and the bar/lobby area was packed and unusable. Very disappointing and annoying for such a HUGE hotel.
The bathtub in our room was unable to modulate the hot and cold water (it would either be scalding or freezing, not in between). We had engineering in there 2 times, which upon the 2nd time, they offered us a new room. It was our last day so we declined, but there was cerainly no offer to reduce the bill. 
We are from the Phoenix area and there are a lot of other great places to stay that have much better ambiance and faciities. The service was great but it couldn't save the cold, institutional feel of this convention oriented hotel.

title: “Good overall”
text: Two different stays over 4 total nights. Nice location is walkable to anything in downtown and you can't get any closer to the convention center without sleep in on the steps. Nice common areas and entry. The executive lounge was fine. All the people I interacted with were great. This is an older hotel but it has been updated/upgrade over time. Unfortunately I think even those fixes are showing their age and a complete overhaul will be needed before too long. My only complaints were the $22 valet parking with no self park available (although there are other city parking options to help mitigate this). The biggest surprise was the pathetic "business center". Even basic hotels offer free printing these days without charging you $1+ a SHEET! Everything considered, I would stay here again if my first choice is full.

title: “Great Place”
text: We were quite surprised when we walked in our room and saw a full size fridge, a cooktop and microwave. It was a very nice room and the hotel was pleasantly decorated. The breakfast was fantastic and dinner plans were easy to make with the hotel being so close to many resturants within walking or quick driving distance. My only irratation would be my husband and I were bothered when talking to the people at the front desk they would answer a call and try to take care of us with the caller, instead of putting the caller on hold. Other than that we would definitely stay at Hawthorn again.

title: “Generous in a Crisis”
text: My husband and I live in NY and were without power during Hurricane Sandy and discovered that the Westin was offering free Wifi, power strips to access outlets to recharge and movies to entertain kids in a couple of their conference rooms. And access to their always clean bathrooms! The hotel didn't have any vacancies but this was the next best thing. They made a very hard situation much more tolerable and we were incredibly thankful for their generosity.

title: “Good Location Nothing Special”
text: This hotel is in a great location right near Michigan Avenue and easy access to business or sightseeing events. The hotel is just plain and offers nothing special. It was clean, small lobby, not much going on. The room was a good size, but the price was a little high. The people working there were pleasant enough, helping with cabs, the airport shuttle and how far certain venues were. The halls were a bit noisy and I was awakened several times by loud voices and yelling in the halls. I was there on business so had to be up early and found this to be annoying at best. I stayed over until Sat and wanted to sleep in a little, but the maid or someone knocked on the door at 8:30 AM and woke me up.

title: “Can't beat the location”
text: We stayed at this hotel for 2 nights a few weeks ago. The location is great if you want to see the touristy section of Philly. We were able to go back and forth to our hotel for a break, bathroom, etc, the location was great. The staff from the valet, bellhop & check in were very friendly and helpful (with directions, etc). We had one problem with the AC in our room but we told the frontdesk clerk on our way to dinner and by the time we came back, it was fixed. The room is a little tired looking but we saw signs that they are renovating the rooms. There was also no safe in the room if you need one. We at one night at Buddakan, which is only half a block from the hotel, which was nice too & there are plenty of restaurants in the area as well.

title: “Amazing Experience!”
text: My husband and I were in Chicago for a quick 24 hour visit; a very last minute getaway trip a few days before his making an overseas deployment. I am so happy we chose this Marriott. The rooms are amazing, bathrooms amazing, and the staff even more amazing!! We felt so welcome and were treated not with professional friendliness, but like good friends. Brandon & Albert and everyone else, thank you for making our stay so memorable and absolutely perfect!

title: “DRAB AND A BIT TIRED”
text:
We ended our California trip with a 4 day stay at this resort, on arrival we were not impressed
with the drabness of the place and the dirty paths and hallways leading to our room, particularly unpleasant is the birds mess everywhere, advise a lot of jet cleaning needed.
Our upgraded room was average and our bay view was obliterated by a large palm tree, we were tired after a long drive so accepted the room. Breakfast was 20 dollars a person and there was complimentary Wi-Fi in the Lobby and Pool area. Pool, Bar and Restaraunt staff were very pleasant, not so good on Reception, although they did let us stay in our room on departure day until 4pm, the BA flight is only once a day at 8pm. Shuttle to Airport 20 dollars and taxi
into San Diego town will cost you 60 dollars return.

title: “Bring earplugs!”
text:
We stayed here for 4 nights during a conference at Georgetown university. Perfect location, easy access to the town centre (the shuttle busses to Foggy Bottom metro station stop in front of the hotel), plenty of good restaurants nearby (Try Zed's for Ethiopian food or the Peacock café for a trendy lunch). The hotel itself could use some refurbishing. Moreover, noise isolation was a serious problem. Our room appeared to have paper-thin walls and we could understand each and every word spoken by our neighbours (one of the walls actually had a double door in it). The windows did not keep the street noise at night out, either. And rooms were unseasonably hot.
Breakfast (not included in the price) in the grill room downstairs was good, room service was slow, staff was very friendly.
We'd probably check what other hotels in the neighbourhood have on offer, if we were to come back.

title: “Location,location,location”
text: Having the Herald Square Subway station less than a block from this hotel is the best selling point,as we used the subway exclusively to get around, and then to have a light breakfast included got us started each morning. Our room the first night was a 2 queen bed room as the king we requested was "leaking". It was small,but not unexpected. However the next 4 nights we were in our king room and had a lot of room,considering we were in New York. Very clean and the staff was professional and helpful. A tip: they have a shuttle to the airport for 33.00(LaQuardia)/pp. But our cab ride was less than 30.00 for both of us.

title: “amazing concierge service!”
text:
absolutely the best manager we ever experienced. could not do enough for us. beds were great with great pillows and duvee. we used the dining room for a private party for family, great atmosphere. 5 min walk to museums (LACMA and Le Brea Tar Pits).
easy walk to synagogue (on Fairfax) and Starbucks around the corner. what else does one need in life!!!
I needed a projector and the manager actually drove me around town to find the best rental then took the equipment back the day after we left town. Amazing personality to all the family.

title: “Not great, but not awful either.”
text: I spent 3 nights at the Hampton Inn Downtown Riverwalk. First, it's a bit of hike to the River Walk. At least 3-4 blocks. My room, with a King bed was comfortable, flat screen TV. The bathroom appeared to be recently renovated. Unfortunately when they re-did the shower, in order to get the full effect of the shower head -- the grab bar was in the way. Those kind of design issues hurt the place. The "hot breakfast" was three items -- do it yourself waffles; and two "hot" items in a chafing dish. Usually some kind of egg product and either a meat or potatoes. All processed. Did I eat it -- yes. But if you wanted a real breakfast, you needed to hike to the Denny's down the road. There was plenty of other stuff -- cold cereal, fresh fruit, yogurt, breads and bagels for toasting. But what do you expect for "free". The parking was ample and free. And the rates were considerably cheaper than the big names near the convention center or along the River Walk. Would I stay there again -- if I was on a budget, yes. But if I really wanted to enjoy the River Walk -- probably not.

title: “A fantastic week”
text: We had a week at the Bowery on the recommendation of friends and were not disappointed . The staff were fantastic particularly the team on reception who booked restaurants and trains for us and were extremely accommodating . Our room was large by US standards and the views great . The hotel is near a fire station so many fire trucks on the move with sirens . Not an issue for us but some may find frustrating.For any one exploring New York this is a great base . We walked with ease to the South and shopping galore . Uptown was accessible with ease .Good cafes and restaurants nearby.Would stay again .

title: “Horrible Accommodations”
text:
The weekend we stayed at the hotel a wedding party was staying there. This caused all other hotel guests to become second rate patrons.
They had many common areas closed to non party members, such as second floor bar and resturant, valet and bell service, as well as some elevators. 
The hotrel is tiny and quaint, but way too small to accommodate such a large party. 
We have also stayed at the Omaha property and experienced the EXACT same treatment, due to a wedding party.
The breakfast buffet was horrible and scarce, at best.
However, The evening cookies were a nice treat.
I would not recommend this hotel, but if you choose to stay, call and make sure they will not be busy with a larger party than they can handle.

title: “A nice, convenient, friendly place to stay”
text:
My company has an arrangement with this hotel, and I have stayed several times over the past ten years. I have always found the hotel's personnel to be friendly and helpful, and this stay was no exception. 
The hotel characteristic that I most appreciated was the very large room (suite) - much larger than the Hilton I stayed at in San Francisco the following week (which was much more expensive). I'm not sure if all the suites at this hotel are equally large; however, if not, ask for a room on the 5th floor.
As stated by others, the hotel is quite close to Sky Harbor Airport, but I did not hear planes at all during the stay. The hotel has a nice restaurant - I had only breakfast and a few evening takeaways - and the food was quite good. Internet access was $10 per day, but it was free to me because my company had paid a business rate.
There is also a running path along the Salt River Canal about half a mile East of the hotel. Convenient if you don't want to be cooped up on a treadmill or don't want to run along the streets.
Phoenix has a surfeit of gorgeous hotels, and this Doubletree can't be counted among them. Nonetheless, it fits the bill in several ways for people who have things to do during the day and want a comfortable, friendly, and spacious place to use as home base.

title: “Ok to stay”
text:
Lobby is well done and the restaurant is nice with a lounge/bar.
The hotel has a hollowed square shape to it. The restaurant is on the first floor with nothing but sky up above. This hollowed cavern makes for lots of echoed noise in the morning. 
The rooms are recently redone well kept. The furniture is very nice and the now standard 3ft HD flat screen TV. Like most business traveling hotels, the internet will cost you. 
The staff was very friendly and the location of the hotel is perfect if you need to depart from Philadelphia airport early. Although it is close to the airport there is no noise from the jets. 
There is really nothing in walking distance to shop or eat.

title: “Good Value”
text: I booked the Buckminster by chance through Hotwire's anonymous deals. I paid about $93 inclusive of all taxes and fees. At first, I held my breath as I read somewhat polarizing reviews about the Buckminster. I was pleased that my experience was positive. I was able to get an early check-in at 12:30 although the room was on the small side (room 320). It was, however, clean and quiet (with only a view of the adjacent building). As mentioned by others, the hotel appears to have been renovated relatively recently. The staff was courteous. The breakfast buffett was adequate--basically carbs, carbs and more carbs. I ate only fruits. Of course, the virtue of this hotel is its central location in Kenmore Square. The Commonwealth Hotel down the street would cost at least twice as much. For the price I paid, I thought I got a decent value for my stay. I would book again at this price.

title: “Best position”
text: This hotel would have to be in one of the best positions, with only a few minutes walk to the middle of Times Square. From the moment we arrived we were very pleased with this hotel, we could see Times Square from our window and you can sit at the outdoor area and just look at Times Square, it is fantastic. This location is central to everything, we did have problems with the wifi but they were quick to give us access to the business centre and not charge for the wifi. I would definately stay here again if we were going to New York. This is a very busy hotel.

title: “Perfect, as expected”
text:
We booked 4 nights at the Soffitel seeing all the positive reviews. And we were not disappointed!!! We arrived at 11am in the morning hoping to be able to put our bags with the Concierge. Instead they offered us a room!!! That was very nice considering that the check-in time is at 3pm. We really appreciated this. (We did have the Soffitel Privilege Card)
Everything in the room was very well organized. The room was very clean and had all the amenities. The only thing we could have used was a coffee maker. But not critical at all. We were also given 2 free drinks and chocolates the first night.
The bathroom was big, spacious and had all the little knick-knacks one needs. Cosmetics were all french, a bonus for those who prefer french toiletries.
The service at every level was impeccable and helped to make the stay very very pleasureable.
Although room service was expensive, there were a number of very good restaurants within walking distance to the hotel. As a tourist, the subway was very close, shopping at 5th avenue was 2 mins away, and the museums were either within walking distance or a short subway ride away. The location was excellent.
And yes, I would recommend this hotel to all my friends. And we would stay there agian when we went to NYC.

title: “Great Hotel in the Heart of Midtown!”
text:
We were in Manhattan for the Big East Tournament in March 2009. After doing quite a bit of searching and price comparison we decided to book a room at The Red Roof Inn. We were extremely pleased in every aspect of the hotel.
PRICE--We book directly through the Red Roof Inn website and got the lowest rate we could find on any website.
ROOMS--Although the room was not large, for NYC standards it was fairly good sized. We had 3 adults sharing a room and had plently of space for luggage and to move around. The room included a microwave, fridge, large tv, and beds that were extremely comfortable. The hotel has been newly renovated so everything was clean and modern. 
BREAKFAST--Nothing fancy, but enough to get your day going. They had a nice selection of bagels, donuts, fruit, cereal, and yogurt. The breakfast room was big enough that there was always enough space.
NOISE LEVEL--We found the hotel to be very quiet. Each floor only has 12-16 rooms that are pretty spaced out so I never heard the other people coming home. We were on the 16 floor and the street noise was at a minimum.
LOCATION--We were within easy walking distance to Madison Square Garden. It was less than 1/2 a mile and could be walked in about 10 minutes. We were also within two blocks of the four major subway lines. So if you couldn't walk to the location you needed it was easy to hop on the subway. The hotel is located in Korea town and has lots of yummy places to eat nearby. I highly suggest the Mandoo Bar next door. They have homemade dumplings that were fabulous!
Overall we will definitely stay here next time we are in NYC.

title: “Hip, noisy, unfriendly and packed”
text: Stayed in this hotel as part of our honeymoon, did not enjoy it at all. Pleasing on the eye but very very dark during the day, no daylight. At night the bar fills up with locals, no where to sit down and have a quiet drink, a large amount of outside influence to this hotel. We found the room pleasent but extremely noisy. there was a baby staying across the corridor and we heard it crying the entire night, no sound proof in the walls what so ever. Good location, thats the only thing we enjoyed from our stay in the Clift. Won't be back.

title: “Great customer service, property needs a little TLC”
text:
Stayed here two nights, and property was very nice and very busy. Was originally given a king size bed room, even though I requested a 2 queen room. This did mean a march back to the front desk with small child and luggage @ 10PM, which I wasn't too happy about, but this was quickly remedied and I received an upgrade to their newer rooms.
Newer room decor was nice. A couple of small problems, first the TV or remote did not work. Remote was replaced with the actual remote for the TV (not the normal hotel remote). Only problem with this is that you could not access pay services. Also, no do not disturb sign was provided (called housekeeping) and the bathroom door does not fully close or lock. None of these were huge deals, but quality assurance seems to be overlooked.
The big positive here was customer service. ALL of the staff was extremely friendly and willing to help. The air conditioning in the hotel worked as expected, which seems to be an issue at a lot of properties. Hallway noise is always an issue @ airport hotels, but our room seemed to be well insulated. There were plenty of dining options (not just the cafe/bar that most hotels offer). Parking was the standard $20/night for LAX, but the parking garage seemed to have a ton of spots. 
I would stay at this property again, hoping that my past stay issues were just a fluke.

title: “Quiet, clean and cozy rooms”
text:
This is a wonderful place to stay, in a great location. Lots of restaurants and the subway close by. The room was small, but it doesn't matter when you're really only there to sleep. It was very cozy and comfortable and I instantly felt right at home. The atmosphere is very charming, with unique decor. The staff were all very nice and helpful; we could keep our bags with the front desk after checking out, and the city/subway map provided with the room was very handy! The only downside, to be picky, was that the mattress was a bit soft, and the blinds were a bit dusty. The room was otherwise very clean, with fresh towels daily.
The washroom was down the hall and shared, but it was impeccably clean and I never had to wait even though the place was fully booked. Don't let the shared washroom stop you from staying here! I will definintely stay again.

title: “Do not stay here unless you like Sludge/Sewage in your shower”
text: Sheraton should not have its name affiliated with this hotel. I am shocked there are as many positive reviews on this site about this hotel as there are. Our group of 5 couples just returned from a weekend stay at this hotel extremely disappointed. The hotel is very old/shabby with zero charm. Many of the rooms smell like cigarettes and sewage. Our friends' awoke to black sludge/sewage all over the floor of their shower, and management did nothing to apologize or compensate them for it. The pool is not heated, not cleaned (it is salt water?) and surrounded by cracked concrete and lounge chairs from 1990. The restaurant is also dirty and is not open for lunch. There is no service at the pool for drinks, snacks, etc. The carpet throughout the building is totally worn and stained, there was trash/gunk in the elevators and the functionality of the elevators is very questionable. The most infuriating thing is the photos on their website makes it look MUCH more updated and nice than it really is. The entire place is very run-down and should be leveled. There is no charm to this place, I implore you do not stay here.

title: “Couldnt have been better!”
text: Upon arriving at the hotel, I was instantly in awe of the lobby. From the futuristic elevators to the tranquil water features, I was very impressed. We were checked in by Vanessa, who was so delightful and was kind enough to give us a room on the 31st floor so our view of downtown LA was breathtaking. I was only here for 2 nights but the staff did an excellent job of making me feel right at home. If your planning on staying here and enjoy the night club scene, dont overlook "SUEDE" on the lobby level, sure to provide a good time.

title: “Good Value-”
text:
We've stayed in a few Four Point hotels...this one was not the best but was fine. Clean and modern furnishings. Good bed and bedding. The front desk clerk was super nice.
Good nights sleep- we did keep the fan on due to street noise. 
Looked like there were plenty of restaurants in area. Hotel & parking lot was challenging to find- enter from a one way street so be careful!
Small bathroom-

title: “Decent place- friendly staff”
text: This hotel is a decent option when in San Antonio. Staff was very polite and friendly going the extra mile to give me a bottle of water and a towel when I crossed the concierge desk after running the Riverwalk in the morning. Rooms were clean, however somewhat small. Too many great choices on the Riverwalk to even consider dining in the hotel at inflated prices. Breakfast was an easy choice at Denny's across the street. Enjoyed the concierge lounge as well. All in All- I'd return.

title: “We will be back !!!!”
text: We just returned from staying at the Broadway Plaza hotel. Don't be fooled by it's small enterance and reception area. The flat iron area is not seedy as stated on some websites, we were returning to our room around midnight both nights and had no problems at all. Felt safe at all times. The rooms are spotless, very roomy and beautiful. We were on the 10th floor and had a amazing view of the Empire State building. Beds were comfy and the bathroom was very large. The free breakfast was great. Yummy bagels, donuts and pastries. 24 hour coffee service is a plus. Staff was very friendly and helpfull. We will not hesitate to book our stay there again.

title: “Solid, convenient property with room for growth”
text:
I stayed here while visiting the University of Texas and came away impressed. The hotel is a convenient drive or walk to the Erwin Center, football stadium and points on the northeast side of campus. Walkers should use extra caution since you must cross a highway overpass to get to campus. As the hotel is close to the highway, it is relatively easy and inexpensive to get to and from the airport - $20 in both directions by cab
Renovations are well underway and have already occurred on the 6th floor, where most guests appear to be staying right now. These renovations are likely reflected in the desk furniture and bathrooms, which appeared to be fairly new. The paint job in the room also seemed recent. The management would be well advised to update the elevators, which appeared to be too slow and too few in number to handle the hotel. Times are slow, but they could also benefit from having another waiter or waitress in the evening to handle bar traffic and dinner menu service. Using a lighter color tile in the shower might also inspire more confidence in its overall cleanliness. Upgrading the restaurant quality would also push this hotel closer to 4 stars, when it is a solid 3 1/4 stars without it. All are minor complaints that do not detract significantly from my overall experience and evaluation. 
Free high-speed internet - Ethernet and wireless - is a major plus at this property. The traditional Doubletree cookies at check-in are pleasant and a unique touch for this brand. Whoever thought of that is a genius.
I stayed in a room facing the highway and did not have any issues with the noise. I kept the air system running, which helped to mitigate the noise, but, truth be told, the windows are thick.

title: “Good location but...”
text:
The good bits:
Good location in the heart of Midtown. 
Free tea and coffee provided throughout the day in the lounge
Free wi-fi and fast by hotel standards
Door staff/storage staff were very friendly and helpful
The roof terrace which has stunning views of the Empire State Building (closed until Spring)
The not-so-good bits:
Our booking was not fulfilled: we had booked two rooms through which were supposed to be adjacent and with two beds each. However, they were at opposite ends of the corridor from each other and each had one uncomfortable small 4'6'' bed. This was not good enough and did not make for a good nights sleep. At check-in, the surly staff told us we could get our rooms changed...but the following morning we were told we could not change rooms because the hotel was full all week. Staff generally in the hotel were unhelpful, even my NYC standards (excepting the door staff).
The "contemporary" class bedrooms (512 and 517) were, in our opinion, tiny, cramped and dingy. 512 room looks onto the construction site and work started at approximately 7am in the morning. 517 was even smaller and looks onto the back of a blackened brick building - possibly the most claustrophobic, depressing outlook we have ever had from a hotel window. Our bed linen was inadequate i.e. did not keep us warm during the nght with the heating off, and the "damask" duvet cover in 512 was stained. The bathrooms were tiny although the water pressure in the shower in 512 was good. One of the few "positives" about the rooms was the charge we developed from the dirty, stained nylon carpets which resulted in entertaining static shocks. Further, the corridors smelt stale and smoky. 
The "daily deluxe continental breakfast" (as described on the hotel website with "deluxe" defined in a US dictionary as "luxurious or sumptuous; of a superior kind") was complementary which ought to be a good thing in NYC. However, after the first morning we went out and paid for a proper breakfast at a local diner in W36th St. Breakfast in the hotel is great if you like using paper cups and plates, plastic cutlery and enjoy a scrum for a seat. If the hotel is full (as was alleged to be last week) it will accommodate approximately 350 guests. The "executive lounge" for breakfast must seat a maximum of approximately 50-60 guests. Whilst the food was merely adequate, the breakfast experience was appalling and certainly not "deluxe" in any way whatsoever.
This was not our first visit to NYC and will not be our last. However, we will not stay in this hotel again and nor would we recommend. Hotel Metro can apparently afford to be complacent as it clearly has many contracts with tour operators and therefore occupancy rates are high. All in all, this hotel is poor and whilst the construction work continues at the rear of the building, visitors should be wary of taking any rooms at the back if they want peace beyond early morning. Yet, from other reviews, rooms at the front do not offer quiet either. This is not a problem we have experienced in other hotels in NYC as they have had double/triple glazing. I would respectfully suggest that the hotel website blatantly misrepresents the quality of this hotel. 
However, if you do stay here, do try the Han Bat Korean restaurant next door but one...unpretentious surroundings, great food and service and excellent value.

title: “Loved it!”
text:
I've taken my two children on trips into the city for the day but usually don't stay overnight because it is so expensive. I was able to get a great rate for this hotel on priceline so we decided to stay for two nights. This hotel is an excellent value - I don't think you can beat it. The staff were great at the front desk (Amanda is one I remember) plus the people at the concierge desk were excellent. We were able to buy our tix to the American Museum of Natural History there and saved lots of time online when we arrived. 
The kitchen in the room was great because we went to the little grocery store one door down and got milk (for cereal in the morning) and yogurt. We didn't use the stove or microwave because we ate out for lunch and dinner but it would be great to have a kitchen for a longer stay.
I thought the hotel was in very good condition. Yes, you can go elsewhere to get brand new carpeting and fancier bedspreads and furniture but you will pay a lot more for that. We hardly spent any time in the room and were more than happy with the quality of the accommodations. We really loved this hotel and would definitely stay again!

title: “terrrible reviews are true”
text:
We were more or less assigned to this hotel as part of a soccer tournament.... I had read previous negative reviews and hoped they were not accurate. I was wrong! We actually checked in to learn that our "loft" room had no beds in the loft...in fact the sleeping loft was empty. A bedside light had no bulb and when we asked for one, the man who was to bring it asked to check the lamp himself. Carpets were dirty, beds were saggy and the total atmosphere was dismal almost frightening. They had no other room with the correct number of beds that they could offer us...but staying was not what we wanted to do. 
The only good thing was that we had no problem finding another hotel and the front desk did not hassle us about leaving. Assured us that our credit card would not be charged. We were not the only family who left so perhaps they are used to this.

title: “so so”
text: Very pretty inside one tower, outside is outdated and being renovated. Horrible check in experience, but management did accept responsibility and gave us a gift certificate to return later. I would go back.

title: “Central Hotel for all New York Stays”
text: Had a great 4 night stay in this hotel... rooms were a little on the small side... hotel clean and tidy.....located just above times square.... centrally located for all sights in New York..... would stay here again.

title: “Perfect stay. Wish it couldve been longer.”
text:
I was in chicaco for a job interview and did not book this hotel. I guess thats why I was upgraded to the 5th floor corner suite. The suite was very big, with a nice flat screen TV, nice desk and a confortable king size bed. Because this was a corner room, the windows were full length and made the room feel must larger than it really was. The hotel was very good. The lobby is spacious and well kept. The staff are very polite and helpful. 
The only problem I experienced in the morning. Dont really know why this hotel dooes not have a better taxi rank. This being a mostly business hotel, they know that mornings are the busiest time for people. Its not fun trying to wait for a taxi for 30 minutes in the rain. They must fix this.

title: “Fabulous comfy beds!”
text:
Stayed at Sofitel over Thanksgiving 2008 with my sister for four nights. The reception area is very welcoming and the staff courteous and polite. We had a room on the 21st floor and had no problem with street noise at all. Views were good. The hotel is superbly situated very close walking distance to 5th Ave, Times Square with good restaurants, Grand Central Station (good breakfast venue opposite) and the Rockefellar centre. The bathroom was spacious and it was useful to have the separate bath and shower cubicle. Room service prices are quite high, so we used a local deli for snacks. Being truly British girls we couldn't do without our tea in the morning and I took a kettle and t bags with us, as the hotel don't provide these as complimentary. They provide bottled water each night at 'turndown'.
The bar is great and we drank there on a couple of occassions arriving back worn out and desperate for a Bud. Best of all was the bed..the most comfortable hotel bed I have ever slept in..like snuggling into a cozy nest, especially when you are so exhausted! Didn't eat in the hotel, as we felt it rather pricey. Found good breakfast locally (not the Red Flame Diner - thought it too tacky! - you can do better elsewhere).
Thank you for previous reviews, I booked this hotel on the back of these, and I would recommend the Sofitel to anyone seeking a very central comfortable hotel. It may be more pricey than some others but the extra is worth every penny in terms of location and comfort, and we would stay there again, without hesitation.

title: “3rd stay...pretty bad this time”
text: This was my 3rd stay at Park Central. I stay here because I loooove the location. Close to Times Square and everything ELSE to be honest. Fabulous lobby; very modern. Easy check-in. Friendly Valet, always (it'll cost you $50 bux/night ya'll to keep your car there.) We've stayed in the new part twice before. No problems. The problem is this...the OLD PART. Here's my thing: when I stay some place like NY or Vegas..lets be honest how long are you staying in the room? right? You're site seeing and all I really need is a clean bed (which thank GOD I got, super comfy too). So we go the "old" elevators...that buttons don't work but magically got us to our room. We go down this musty hallway that reminded me of Grandparents old apartment in the Bronx. But it's cool whatever...we go in to the tiny room. You got two lamps and the bathroom light. Other than that pitch black. Perfect for sleep but what the heck?!?! So dark. No coffee maker. Busted dresser that was falling apart at the seams. SOOOO humid in the room...with a busted A/C. Thank Goodness it cooled down that weekend or I'd be dying. Now I shouldn't hold this against a hotel I've been to twice before but have some respect for your property Park Central! Keep stuff up to date...at LEAST make sure you have working elevators that broke down all Saturday during the day and Sunday during the day...the sweet front desk folks let us use the service elevator. How horrible is it that guests have to struggle to get up to their room after a long day? And worse is that the poor people at the front desk have to deal with pretty angry patrons. So Park Central, Slap some paint on it. Do some Checks on your equipment. Respect your property...it's like they gave up on the other half. Sad. On a positive note, I love the people who work there and the location, but this is the first time I actually thought of paying a few extra bucks for a better spot that elevators are in working order.

title: “Passable”
text: Everything about this hotel is satisfactory or a bit better as I expect from a large hotel chain. The rooms are comfortable and a good size. Shower was very powerful which was a pleasant surprise and all areas seemed clean. The neighbourhood the hotel is situated in however is not the best. In England we would call it 'seedy'. It was fine getting down to the tourist areas of Pier 39 by bus and picking up the tram so by day the location is good. For breakfast I went to Sam's Diner across the road which was great and ate much more cheaply and by the looks of the dining room at the hotel ate much fresher ingredients too.

title: “Best value in Manhatten? It may well be.”
text: This is a Hampton Inn and that is not a criticism but it has the outstanding advantage of being cheap (by Manhatten standards) but very well located. W24 Street is not attractive by day or night but it is very well located for bus and metro. The standard room is of a reasonable size for a city famous for calling a closet a bedroom and the inclusive breakfast was the standard Hampton Inn fare but a brief walk into the area produced a really good diner if you wanted to "pig-out" in true American fashion. We spent three nights here and found no problem at all in getting around Manhatten and over to Brooklyn. A tip - use the yellow taxis from JFK but get the cabbie to go via Brooklyn Bridge if you arrive at night. It won't cost much extra (if anything) on the otherwise fixed fare and it is a fabulous approach to a fabulous city.

title: “Wonderful hotel, friendly staff”
text: We stayed for nearly a week in this hotel that we chose because of the ratings on Tripadvisor. We had a great time: a spacious room, very nice people working there (from cleaning lady to welcoming staff), the meals are excellent and Dupont Circle is a great starting place to explore the city as well as Georgetown. The only recommendation we have is to open the pool in May (and not mid June) since we were looking forward to have a swim because of the nice weather in Washington.

title: “Amazing Hospitality”
text: Everything about our stay at the Marriott has been exceptional, if you want 5 star service look no further. We have been treated so well by all. When we first arrived the checking was quick and friendly. They gave our daughters a welcome bag which they loved. To make it even better the bell man Jay went to the back and brought out two teddy bears for the girls. I have to say that Tony has also been amazing so friendly! We are so pleased with our room it has a beautiful view of the Statue of Liberty. We would never hesitate in coming back here to stay the location is perfect. Thank you Marriott you have to be commended for your impeccable service and friendly staff you made our stay truly memorable!!! Please tell Jay and Tony how much we appreciated them there is also another gentleman that was always at the front opening the door and getting us a taxi he was also a star. Until we see you again..... We love NY!

title: “Couldn't be more pleased!”
text: I stayed at the Marquis with some friends, and wow! We had a great time. Our room was beautiful, the location is PERFECT and the staff is the best in the business. THANKS!

title: “'Yes ma'am, you'll be safe round here... and I was!”
text: Arrived at the hotel, book in was quick and effortless, Emilie was the very friendly and most helpful girl, she gave me a room with a fantastic view of the ground zero monument buildings and other amazing skyscrapers. Lovely room, very clean, modern and comfortable. I haven't stayed downtown before, and I have to say, it was a nice change, lovely tree lined streets with town houses and local deli's, which were open 24 hours. I fell asleep as soon as I got in, woke up at 2am, realised I hadn't booked transport to the airport, the concierge was a huge help in arranging a lovely big mercedes to take me. I was hungry, he pointed me in the direction of the deli at the top of the road, I asked if it was safe for me to walk, hence the title of this review. I usually stay midtown, but this area is so peaceful but also typically like the New York you see on the telly. I will definitely stay here again, and would recommend it to anybody.

title: “Great option when going to Nokia Theater”
text: My husband and I stayed at this hotel for 2 nights because we were attending a concert at Nokia Theater one of the nights. We had a junior suite with a city view. The room was great - very spacious and VERY clean. We LOVED being able to just walk a few steps from the theater back into the hotel at the end of the concert. The hotel is right in the middle of lots of shops and restaurants so there are plenty of options for places to eat. The service at the hotel was wonderful as well. Everyone was very friendly and helpful. There was a triathlon near the hotel on the 2nd day, which closed many of the streets in the area, but the hotel did a great job of informing people of the closures and providing directions for navigating the area. We would definitely stay here again if we were attending an event at LA Live.

title: “Hotel was Horrible”
text: Don't stay here. I stayed one night, over priced, service strinks as does the manager. Hotel staff lied to me, Person working 11 - 7AM on Friday night told me he would have coffee waiting for me at 6AM. I couldn't walk my leg was hurting. I told him that over the phone. When I got there he told me there was no coffee. When I told him I just spoke to him on the phone and he said there was coffee he tried to rectify it by giving me a cold cup of coffee. I was pissed. Will never stay here again.

title: “Three star, certainly no more and perhaps less”
text: It's a perfectly satisfactory New York City Three Star. It's a little shabby and the hallway rugs could productively be replaced, but it certainly is convenient to Grand Central Terminal and serves its purpose as long as one is not expecting too much. Rather strangely, the room didn't have a blanket on the bed, thereby requiring a call to get one reasonably promptly delivered. Two warnings: The address says "Lexington Ave." but it's really on the south side of 49th (not 48th) about 50 feet from corner of Lexington. Also, the bell-hops charge $2 a bag to store temporarily for the guests. That's new to me. When questioned, they explain that this charge was incorporated into the recent union negotiations, which is merely another way of saying they are sneaking yet another hidden charge into the hotel experience.

title: “Best place to stay!”
text: My husband and I stayed here for a couple of hours on a stopover, we paid the day rate which was very reasonable. The free shuttle from the airport was fast and convenient both when we arrived and when we left. We made the most of our time in LA and took a 4 1/2 hour tour, it was the best thing we could have done. The concierge was very helpful. Having the room allowed us to leave our luggage there and not worry about it and shower before our next flight. The room was bigger than what I expected, it was renovated and the bed was great. The only thing that could have been improved was the bathroom, the bathtub looked a little old but still good. The hotel was very nice, the staff at the front desk was very nice and helpful, they let us check out an hour later than usual. If we are ever in LA again we will stay here for sure!

title: “The Maxwell”
text: A very friendly hotel with very helpful staff. Having a shuttle available for hotel guests is a real bonus because the hotel is a bit out of the way. The hotel is new so everything is clean and up-to-date. Would definitely stay here again.

title: “Great place to stay for business @ UCLA”
text: If you are doing business or visiting UCLA this is the place to stay because it is only five minutes away from campus. It is very luxurious with excellent service, yet practical and reasonable considering the premiere location in Brentwood/ Bel Air. Plus, you are located right by the 405 and 101 freeways, which will take you almost any where in Los Angeles, of course traffic permitting.

title: “Great Stay!”
text: My daughter and I travelled from Coastal NC to New York to celebrate her birthday. The Pod was perfect for our needs. The rooms are very small, but they were very, very clean. Bringing your own pillow and a soft blanket is a good idea. We got did get a private bath but the shared baths were much larger and also very clean. The concierge was terrible to the point of being funny (it was like she did not know a thing about NYC, she just googled and never offered anything extra). However, there are Ipads in the lobby so it is easy to find your way around without her. We had an amazing time. Also very quiet.

title: “Average, but comfortable stay in Downtown LA”
text:
For my first time in downtown LA, I decided to chance it with the Westin despite the mixed reviews. Overall, I had a comfortable stay, but the housekeeping could have done a much better job. I might stay here again, but for the price, I think the Hilton Checkers two blocks away is probably better. 
Check-in and check-out was quick; although there seemed to only two or three people at the front-desk at any given point despite there being at least 6 or 7 check-in counters. No one at the Starwood preferred guest check-in all the times that I checked.
I got a room on the 27th floor, which was reasonably clean and large enough. The nicest thing about the room was the floor to ceiling view. The king bed was large and comfortable. The flat screen TV had a good selection of channels and movies. The bathroom was very clean, but the tub had a few stains - an indicator of the age of the place, more so than anything else. Plenty of plush towels and a complementary robe. The amount of hot water and shower pressure was also pretty good.
The trash bins in the room were not empty on check-in which leads me to think that the room was hastily cleaned. I immediately checked the bed to see if the cleaning was superficial, but it appeared to be clean enough. Two of the pillows had a couple of small spots of blood, so I was worried about bedbugs. It took a couple of tries calling the front desk to get housekeeping to come and clean the room again. There was no complementary water in the room on check-in, but the housekeeping included this on the second day of the stay. 
The hotel complex is a labyrinth, and the concrete structure is reminiscent of a shopping mall, but I actually liked the architecture. There were some reviews about waiting ages for the elevators but this was not my experience. In fact, I felt that average time I needed to wait for was 30 seconds or less. 
I was given complementary internet access which was unexpected and pleasant - connecting to it was quick and it was fast. Parking and internet costs in general are somewhat astronomical in the area anyway. Overall, I would give this place 3.5 stars. If they paid attention to some small details (like ensuring housekeeping is immaculate), I would give it 4 - 5 stars.

title: “I loved my stay there”
text: I loved my stay there because of the proximity with my business place. Apart from the location I liked ambience and enjoyed my evening drinks. Morning breakfast were awsome. Overall It was a wonderful stay there.

title: “It was ok....”
text:
I was pretty satisfied with most aspects of the room, except the fact that it was EXTREMELY small. I only had a view of the ally out back, but hey, you win some you lose some. The view just depends on what side of the building they have an available room on, so you can't be mad at that...
Cleanliness: can't complain about that. But there was one small thing that was kind of annoying. The shower doors leaked at the bottom and no matter what I did there was always a large pool of water on the bathroom floor after showering. Then I would have to put towels down to soak it up and hence always had wet towels on the floor until the room was serviced again... Not a huge deal, but a bit annoying.
Service: great, very friendly and knowledgable staff and doormen.
Location: EXCELLENT! Right in midtown east, just 2 block from grand central, and you can get anywhere from there so in essence, it was close to everything.
Value: We reserved our room when there were having some kind of special, so we got a great deal and were very happy with the price.

title: “Clean, creative decor, great location”
text:
I was very impressed by this hotel. The room was immaculate and I love the beachy decor. The staff were incredible, providing exceptional and friendly service. The hotel facilities are great and they even provide a free shuttle service which is very useful. The hotel is a 5-10 min walk from the iconic free trolley to the West Village and you can also walk to restaurants and the Farmer's Market.
The price of hotels seem quite reasonable in Dallas overall, my only advice regarding price is to keep checking online even a couple of days before your stay. I noticed a better room than mine was advertised online on the same site I (booking.com) at a cheaper rate.

title: “Put Her out of her misery.”
text:
Although the Towers rooms are still beautiful, the rest of the hotel is tired and worn. 
Unhappy staff who speak ill of their managers in voices loud enough to hear are probably telling the truth. The place has seen it's glory days and those days are gone.

title: “Location Cubed”
text:
Pros: Close to Philly tourist attractions, pubs and restaurants, nice staff
Cons: Parking is expensive (like everywhere in central Philly), strong smell
Wife and I stayed for 5 nights here. Bellman/valet was extremely helpful. Asked for a corner room (slightly larger than other reg rooms because of hallway). Room is ok. Large, but nothing impressive. Old tube TV, really?!? Internet was free for select guests (just sign up for free online), but slow. Walls are kind of thin. Could hear family next door fairly easily. Agreed with other reviewer on smell. Lobby and hallways had a strong scent, but more like "real Febreze" than "fake lily." The hotel definitely shows it's age, and I think they use extra polish and sprays to disguise it's dated walls. 
Overall, a good stay. It's not quite a 4-star level anymore, but it's location near Independence Hall, Liberty Bell and all that Olde Town has to offer, more than makes up for a lack of star power. We got an internet rate of $126 a night, which I believe is pretty good for the area.
Parking is the big annoyance. Pretty much the entire area is pay parking whether in a structure or on the street. Rate for Omni (run by a separate company) is $25 a night (24hr period). I don't think it's worth risking street parking, most only have 2 hour limits and meter maids are out in force. Read a reviewer parked in Jersey and bused over - sounded like a good idea after 5 nights. Or just look into not renting a car since you could walk to a lot of places.
*If you use parking structure for Omni, it's not that far, you step outside and walk around the corner. Find the elevator entrance and use the parking ticket to get through secured doors. Rating is based on my typical "4-star" experience.

title: “Charming, Elegant and Great staff.”
text: The Lennox came highly recommended and it did not disappoint. Th location is ideal, it's very central, perfect for the first time visitor to Boston. The hotel was charming and very traditional in style. The restaurant food was very good. The staff were always helpful. Free Wifi was reliable and fast. Noisy air con can be a problem, but other than that I did not have any issue. A few of my colleagues did complain that with only two lifts it was a problem getting one during the busy period.

title: “Good choice for us, and the price was great!”
text: We chose this motel because of its proximity to our LA family, and we'll stay here again next time we visit. The room was clean and nice. Julia, the manager, was lovely and made sure we were satisfied with everything. The continental breakfast had several kinds of fresh fruit, fresh muffins, bagels and cereal. You could choose to eat at tables either inside or out. A nice experience.

title: “Lovely food, awful staff”
text:
Stayed her in April 2011 and couldn't have been more disappointed. The hotel itself is actually lovely, nice pool, restaurants and very clean. However, the rooms were unbelievably small. Although we booked a twin room they initally placed us in a double, meaning we would have to share a rather small double bed. After a lot of complaining with the manager they eventually agreed to move us to a twin room. It wasn't much better. There may have been two beds but they were so close it may aswell have been one. The room was bare with no character and if you want to watch any tv it all has to be paid for, even news channels etc The bathroom was like a closet with no room to move.
The Library bar was extremely pricey at around $20 per drink where they create a cocktail to your taste, especially when you can go to the normal bar and have champagne cocktails for $12. 
The newly opened restaurant was actually the nicest thing about the hotel. A little pricey but the food is delicious so worth the price and the staff were really helpful. Which makes a change from the other staff in the hotel who were quite frankly rude and unhelpful. 25 degrees is also a nice cafe type place to eat in the hotel. It's very reasonably priced and the portions are enormous and the staff here were lovely. In fact all the waiters and waitresses were lovely in the hotel, it was the bar staff and general staff who were incredibly rude and it's a shame they are spoiling the reviews for the rest of the staff.
The valet staff were much better and can call a taxi to arrive in seconds. However, every time we got a taxi from the hotel we were ripped off by the drivers, one took a very scenic route to universal studios making the price double than the journey home. On another occasion the driver dropped us off 2 miles from the restaurant we asked! Can't blame the hotel for that but the drivers obviously expect rich guests and take advantage.
The hotel is in a great location, right on the walk of fame and next to the kodak theatre. As it's such a big place no hotel will be perfect for every place you want to visit, but this hotel is certainly pretty close.
Overall I was quite disappointed with the hotel. Having travelled here straight from the Bellagio in Vegas it was quite a demotion. It seems to be living off it's famous past time and quite frankly has lost its appeal.

title: “I wish I could move in.”
text: Drury plaza riverwalk is our home away from home. We have been staying there for years. Anytime we have time for a weekend get away, it's our first choice. The rooms in the bank building are really cool, but our room of choice is the two room terrace suite over looking the river and the San Fernando cathedral. The roof top pool is amazing at night, as well as the indoor pool on those chilly days. Kickback is always yummy. Service in this hotel is amazing. Go out the back door to the river, around the corner, and your on the main part of the riverwalk, close to restaurants. Take a river taxi and enjoy a short ride to the mall, or take a short 2 block or so walk to the Alamo. Truly the my favorite hotel in San Antonio.

title: “5-star pampering in Houston”
text: This hotel is not over-the-top elegant, but is tastefully decorated, and the service is outstanding. (We originally reserved a room at the Lancaster Hotel after reading its Frommer's recommendation. Please see my review for more information.) We quickly realized we needed to find another hotel, so using priceline I reserved a 5 star for $167. Five mins later we arrived and were told our room would be ready in 15 mins. (it was 11 am.) When I checked back our room wasn't ready so we were immediately upgraded. Our room was poolside, yet private because of a short wall and a few steps leading to the pool. The pool was beautiful, and our room was large and comfortable. We took a private midnight swim, (it was after pool hours, but the customer is always right at the Four Seasons) and were pampered by the staff. We were known by name as we came and went, enjoyed the fitness area with all the amenities....I only wished we were staying for more than one night.

title: “TBRU Hosting”
text: Great staff. Very friendly. Went the extra mile to make sure everybody was satisfied. Highly recommended!!!

title: “Fabulous ... fabulous ... fabulous....”
text: The rooms were gorgeous, the location perfect, and the service was super fantastic. Everyone we encountered there was super helpful and friendly. The coffee and lattes in the library were fantastic and breakfast and nyt made my stay very comfortable and relaxed. The only issue I had was that there was all sorts of drilling going on late morning with the construction. If you plan to be out and about, it won;t affect you though.,..

title: “A great place to stay while in Denver”
text: I would consider this hotel a great place to stay in Denver based on a recent stay. On the plus side is the location which is close to the downtown scene. The facilities are clean and fairly quiet and afford you the opportunity to prepare food in your room as there's a full kitchen. The downside is that there is no pool or spa, but if that's not high on your list of must haves, then I think this hotel should be on your short list of places to stay while visiting Denver. I would also request a room on the top floor and hopefully without a connecting room door to minimize the noise.

title: “Perfect location! Amazing stay!”
text:
We stayed at the Nikko from April 28 - 30. This hotel is in the perfect location. Everything was within a few blocks walking distance, and it was easy to find so we didn't worry about getting lost. 
I expected a very pretty hotel from all of the pictures and I wasn't disappointed, extremely nice. I've seen on previous reviews that travellers said they felt the hotel wasn't very "home-y" and the staff wasn't very cordial. I don't expect a hotel to feel like home and I was actually relieved to see that the staff doesn't bug by being in your face all the time. When we needed help or had a question the staff was more than happy to help us, with excellent service, but other than that they let us enjoy our stay without being bothered. 
One thing...maid service didn't turn the beds down and we had to ask for extra towels, as there was only one in the bathroom.
The room wasn't olympic sized, but it's the perfect size for two people. We had ample room for our luggage and such and we never felt cramped. We were on the 18th floor, but unfortunately our view was of the hotel across the street. I didn't go to San Fran to gaze out the hotel window anyway : ) 
Concierge lady was extremely helpful and the cute little lady in the gift shop was sooo nice.
We loved our stay at this hotel and will definitely be returning. I wouldn't stay anywhere else in San Francisco due to the Nikko's location and such a good price for an amazing hotel.

title: “Everything you need, and Haagen-Dazs too!”
text:
Faced with 5-days in the same city (Dallas, Texas) attending a conference I chose to stay at The Candlewood Suites on the Stemmons Freeway. Financially a much better deal than staying in one of the conference hotels and it had everything I needed.
I prefer to stay in a suites hotel when I am in a city for more than a few days and the Candlewood was everything that I expected; so I wasn’t disappointed nor was I amazed by any of the services provided.
The ‘Candlewood Cupboard’ provided adequate sustenance when I needed something in addition to the ‘conference food’ I was getting elsewhere, and tubs of Haagen-Dazs for that 3 am snack when I was battling with jet-lag. I only wish that they had had an alternative to the incredibly sweet pastries that are obviously the delight of all Americans. Something bland, like plain wholemeal bread, for those of us who choose not to take on masses of sugar with every bite, would have been appreciated, and perhaps a pop up toaster in the room would have been nice.
The Shuttle Bus was, for me, a bit of a disaster. Not as easy to arrange as they would have you think. I ended up at the wrong rail station on the first morning, and I quickly gave up the idea of using it and relied on taxis ($18 to the Dallas Convention Centre), which the Front Desk quickly and cheerfully arranged for me. 
Next time I have to stay for a few days in another American City I will probably be back at the Candlewood Suites as it is comfortable and does represent value for money.

title: “La Jolla ES is a more upscale facility than other ES's, but less personable.”
text:
Booked directly with a discounted voucher purchased from a private party. I've stayed at several other ES's in CA and this one was the most modern and aesthetically pleasing so far. This ES seemed more upscale the moment we pulled into the driveway. There was classical music piped into the driveway entrance, bell hops ready for baggage assistance, and the lobby/decor was modern and upscale. Attrium was more open and trendy than the sometimes overgrown green houses of other ES's. Perhaps the limited foliage in the atrium allowed for more noise echoing, conveyed in some of the other reviews. Though, I didn't notice the noise up on the 9th floor. I always ask for an upper level floor to avoid the anticipated people traffic from the atrium, which they normally accomodate for HHonors members. Enroll free online. Overall service was professional, but seemed less personable.
The rooms were just as impressive, with a flat panel HDTV in the living room, leather ottomans in both rooms, granite tops on everthing, nice modern decor. Room was very clean. Carpet seemed new. No funky smells/stains. ES breakfast buffet was reliably good, and despite the long lines it moved pretty fast (except for the cook to order line). Suggest getting to breakfast within 1.5hrs of opening to avoid long lines. This place is big ES with 12 floors of hungry guests. The styro plates were a little bit of a let down but perhaps it helped keep things moving. Unlike some other ES's, bussers did a decent job keeping up at this one. Managers reception was reliably good. No skimping on amount of alcohol, but available labels were typically mediocre. Hey, what do you expect for free. Pool was clean and area was well maintained.
The only part I didn't like was the additional $17 parking fee and really tight / limited spaces. I wish I would've researched these reviews to get the tip on street parking. A more personable staff would've tipped me on to that. I also didn't get the usual, "How's everything so far?" evening call from the manager like at other ES's...guess I'm just spoiled. Kid traffic / noise was better than I expected for a Friday night stay. As with most ES's try to avoid weekends and book as a HHonor member. Would stay again if priced no higher than $175. I noticed the prices are really high ($245+) during the week. Overall, I liked this ES better than others.

title: “Direction Home for a Rolling Stone... At Last”
text:
My stay at the Hard Rock Hotel in Chicago rose beyond the ordinary pleasure of staying in a nice, clean hotel room to the point where I was personally and spiritually inspired. I was in town for the Natl. Restaurant Association Show and stayed there for 3 nights. It was my first time staying in a Hard Rock property, so I didn't quite know what to expect.
First of all, the location, and the sexy historic building itself, are spectacular. The hotel is on MIchigan Avenue, just two blocks from incredible not-to-be-missed Millennium Park. One could write a long and rapturous book about all the fantastic things to experience in Chicago within walking distance of the hotel, so let me just try to focus on the hotel, except to say it is in an ideally convenient location. I took the L train there from there airport (blessed $2.25) and only had to walk a few blocks from the Clark/Lake station to the hotel. It's also only 2 blocks to walk to the Metra train which goes right to McCormick Place.
I had a City View Select room with a view of the Chicago River and the amazing Chicago Tribune building. If you care about art, architecture, and the triumph of humankind, than this view is for you. That gorgeous view is going to be to imprinted my brain for a long time. The room was comfortable and functional and in addition to the view had everything I wanted and needed, by that I mean a luxurious bed, a flat screen TV, a bath tub, and a desk with Internet access.
I was on the B.B. King floor, meaning that I also got to hang in between a huge portrait of blues giant B.B. King and one of his real guitars every time I waited for the elevator. There is different musical memorbilia to be found on every floor.
But wait, it gets better... I had read on online before arriving that you can borrow guitars from the hotel. I tentatively inquired about this with the kind, friendly people at the front desk about this. Soon as I said the word, I was presented with a catalog of high-end Gibson guitars that I could check out at no charge, like checking out a library book. A few minutes later, a bellman delivered the "Hummingbird" acoustic model to my room. It was so fun and relaxing to play the guitar in my room (while gazing out at the Chicago Tribune building, no less). 
Oh, and on one of the TV channels, there is some groovy cat named Rico giving basic guitar lessons. I realized that I do really want to learn music theory!
The rooms have complementary copies of the Rolling Stone magazine, and I found some time to hang out in the room and the read the cover tribute story about the 70 best Bob Dylan songs, a tribute to Bob's 70th birthday. This was inspiring because it had been too long since I had appreciated Dylan's genius.
The lobby and hotel bar are chic yet cozy and intimate. Everyone I encountered working at the hotel was friendly, genuine, and happy. There is a button on the phone in the room that says "Everything is Possible," and I dialed it a few times and was to get everything I needed almost instantly (sure, I was only asking for a dvd player and an extra luggage stand, but still...). 
The concierges gave me a great recommendation on a lunch spot (Pastoral wine and cheese, right around the corner --- YUMMY!!), and they also printed out my boarding pass for me. The hotel seemed to have a good mix of business travelers, tourists, and hipster types. I had a few drinks at the bar, and it was quite a comfortable yet hip and glamorous place in which debauch. 
The Hard Rock Hotel Chicago is a celebration of rock n' roll, good old fashioned hospitality with a modern edge, and all the best of the incredible city that is Chicago.

title: “They steal your money”
text: I didn't stay here because after I made reservations I cancelled them and they charge 20 dollars to make a reservation and do not refund your money. The hostel has terrible customer service. They should get audited and shut down for being so disgusing.

title: “Absolutely filthy-- stay somewhere else!”
text: The room was absolutely filthy. I had already switched rooms once, so decided that there was no point in contacting the front desk for another room and concluded they all were the same. The headboard on the bed was stained over 50% of its surface. I don't even want to think about what might have been on the headboard. Instead of using the pillows that were touching the headboard, I used the one in the closet. The bed itself was also filthy. As I do in all hotels, I removed the sheets to look for bed bugs and found a dirty mattress and mattress cover. Both were stained and covered with hair and dirt. The bathroom was simply gross. The toilet barely flushed-- required holding the handle the entire time it was flushing. The towels had makeup on them. To be honest, I couldn't tell if they were stained or if they were used. I woke up at 6 AM and felt so disgusted that I checked out of the hotel even though I had planned to spend the morning relaxing, working and ordering room service. I'd rather sit at a starbucks with all of my luggage instead. Also, while there was a desk in the room, there wasn't a chair. Other than the bed, there was nothing to sit on and it was difficult to work. I will never stay at this hotel again-- I've stayed at 1 star motels that were more hygienic. Absolutely disgusting.

title: “Wonderful, relaxing and great location!”
text:
My husband and I stayed a here last weekend. It was a surprise trip for his 30th birthday. We absolutely loved our stay. We booked a King Premier room on the 10th floor. Everything was clean, quiet and functioning. We loved the decor, the little sitting area, the bedding and the enormous tub. I would return anytime!
Two things that were not necessarily great: 
- overpriced room service: the food was delicious and service impeccable, but the price...yikes! 
- the water in the shower never quite got to hot. Very warm, yes, but not hot. When poured into the tub however it did get hot, so it was fine for us in the end. I'm not sure though why it wouldn't work for the shower.

title: “Great location, very comfortable hotel”
text: I just finished staying 5 nights at this hotel. The room was attractive with high a quality bed and linens. Even on the 3rd floor facing the street it was quiet every night, except for Oct 28 after the giants won the series which was forgivable. The location is outstanding, literally a few steps or blocks from some of the best neighborhoods and attractions, and about 5 blocks from both the muni and bart public transportation systems which I used often. Breakfast is not included in the room charge and expensive to buy in the hotel restaurant, but there are cafes in the area and a coffee maker plus a small refridgerator in the room. The staff were friendly and helpful the few times I needed anything.

title: “Very solid hotel at a fair price”
text:
Stayed one night on business trip. Much to like, so I will start there. For quite a bit under $200: (1) nice and comfortable lobby; (2) warm greeting and fast check-in; (3) slightly larger than average room, well appointed and upscale-looking; (4) very good work area; (5) huge and nice TV; (6) iPod playing device; (7) nice bathroom, including above average towels and soaps, etc.; (8) well-stocked minibar (with $10 coupon for being in the loyalty program -- great perk); (9) very fine gym -- not amazing, but definitely above average and appealing; (10) great location; (11) very comfortable bed and bedding (and whoever is tucking in those sheets must aspire to the bounce-a-quarter-on-it school of bed-making. Breakfast had the usual hotel premium, but not shockingly so, and the food/service were very fine. I missed the wine hour, but the front desk gave me a coupon for a drink at the bar -- another generous step, 
I'm not crazy about the brown-heavy color scheme in the halls, but that is immaterial.
Points off for (1) arriving to a room in which the toilet needed flushing (nothing horrible, debris from cleaning, I think), and (2) turning from the elevator bank to the hall to my room, and there's a rolling trashbin parked in the hallway. 
I'd recommend a south side room for more quiet -- I faced Wilshire (from 18th floor) and was fine with the street noise, but a lighter sleeper might not be.
All told, I'd give it about an 8 on a scale of 10 (with 10 reserved for Four Seasons at top of its game, and, by way of comparison, a 7 for your typical Hyatt Regency).

title: “Pricey if you plan to stay in the small room for any length of time...”
text: As other comments have mentioned, the staff was very friendly and helpful. I, for one, did enjoy the atmosphere of the lobby (modern with Asian influences). BUT, the rooms are very small. Not much room on either side of the bed and hardly any closet space. A big tray occupied the small desk area (I was there for work, so this was annoying) and there was nowhere else to set it. We faced a brick wall, so that was our view. I later found out that if you purchase through a site other than theirs, you get the small and brick-facing rooms (even smaller than the other small rooms mentioned in other comments). Wi-fi was virtually non-existent. Again, I was there for a work conference and still had to work. There was numerous times the network was down. For the price you pay, you should at least have wi-fi that works! Walls keep sound out enough, but the doors are thin and extremely loud when they close. Each morning we had the service staff huddling outside ours, and you could CLEARLY hear everything they were saying...to the extent that that's what we woke up to each morning. Location was very good, which was a plus. Overall, if you plan to not be in your room much this may work for you. If you'll be in your room for anything other than sleeping, go somewhere else for the price...and hopefully you'll get decent wi-fi and breakfast too.

title: “Good deal downtown”
text: Walking distance to Safeco field and you can leave your car in the lot til 6p the day you check out so it was easy to leave our bags, catch Sunday's game, then by the time we had walked back to got our car, game traffic had died down. The room was SMALL but perfectly comfortable for a couple staying one night. Nice toiletries in room and a comfy 2-level lobby area. Friendly and helpful staff. A very good deal. And the Dodgers took 2 out of 3 games!

title: “Lovely Hotel, Perfect location!”
text: When visiting Chicago, we love to stay on or near the Magnificent Mile for shopping, restaurants etc, This hotel is lovely, newly renovated. The rooms are clean, spacious suites with internet service. We were well cared for by staff and enjoyed the little restaurant for a quick snack or drink. Walking distance to most things or a cab ride or bus ride to all else.

title: “Staff and Location Unbeatable”
text: Just returned from a stay at the Beach Haven Inn and was surprised at how much we enjoyed our stay after reading some of the reviews on here. The staff and location are unbeatable!! the rooms could use some updating - but you get what you pay for. the location to Garnet street ( resturants, bars, shops) and the beach was great. we were there for the Pacific Beach Annual Block Party which is a busy and crazy time and we had no compliants! i would suggest staying here if you want a laid back place with a great location and value. if you are looking for down comforters, 24 hour room service and at least $100 more a night then choose a different location.

title: “Ideal location but very dingy room”
text: We stayed here because of it's location to Seaworld (5 mins drive) and the reception area and outside looked really nice. It was only when we got in our room that we were really disappointed, the room was so dark and dingy we couldn't wait to leave the next morning! The lights are too dim, the furniture is dark aswell and it needs a lick of paint to freshen it up. We paid top dollar for this room (just over $134) and it definitely wasn't worth it....we've stayed in much nicer rooms for less than half that price!! Would recommend for location only.

title: “Friendly and helpful staff, very clean and excellent food”
text: We had two rooms on the 20th floor which had excellent views out. Rooms were a good size and staff couldn't be more helpful for taxi's etc. Good location for walking to some of the main attractions and eating out. Internet access was good speed and no issues with download. Lifts are slow but building is old and this adds to the character of the hotel .

title: “Cool Hotel”
text: Very pretty refurbished hotel in the middle of the business section of Houston. Very nice rooms, great beds, central location. A design hotel. I would recommend. There are nice restaurants nearby. 1 block from the Baseball Stadium. Seems that the Downtown section is not the happening part of town. Maybe more active in the Galleria section. Ohh and Houston is misearbly hot. Also went to Gaveston- nice restaurants on the beach.

title: “Four Seasons Service as expected”
text: Spent a night at this hotel in July. Booked through Amex Platinum and was upgraded upon arrival. Room was spacious with separate living room and spacious bathroom with HUGE tub. 2 Flat screen TVS, large walk in closet and nice entry foyer. In the afternoon, our room seemed hot and we noticed the A/C was not working properly. Maintenance was sent up and they could not fix it so we had to switch rooms and ended up getting a bigger room with a better view, Thanks! Service is just as you expect from a Four Seasons. We had dinner at the restaurant Bourbon Steak and it was amazing as well! Very modern decor, great food, great drinks and wine list.

title: “The Best is at the Beacon”
text:
You are now reading a review by an individual who is very biased! I love this hotel! I live in Hawaii and try to visit New York as often as possible.
One of my favorite experiences is to stay at the Beacon. The staff is truely
outstanding. They go out of their way to help in any way possible. The rooms are immaculate thanks to a wonderful housekeeping unit. If you
make a reservation via phone, the manger and his staff will try to
accomodate your request even on busy holidays. Shopping is a dellight.
You do not need to go downtown to find a special goodie, I especially
love the grocery stores and the excellent eateries. It is so convient via
bus and train to see all of New York. Now the truth! I have been going to
the Beacon for over 10 years. I think it is like a visit to my family.
Have fun in New York because of the Beacon. Aloha
.

title: “Superb”
text:
GOOD: I read ALL posts before making the reservation and was skeptical. But I was pleasantly surprised with everything of this fantastic hotel. It is more like Renaissance chain than typical Courtyard all around the country. I was upgraded to a studio as soon as I requested for one. Rooms are be little bit smaller than most (typical) Courtyards hotels. But the they are beautifully decorated, the drapes, curtains were class of its own. All rooms are absolutely sound proof from its surrounding room, which itself is something unheard of any other Courtyard. Receptionist was really nice. 
I needed little bit of milk to make my tea...I went to the Starbucks within hotel. Although it was closed a guy came out the kitchen, open the closed refrig. and simply gave me small container of milk for free !!!
Most striking was the service I got from the valet parking. They greeted us with smile, carried our luggage, opened both the car doors, brought the car within seconds with heater on. Simply out standing. And the charges were far less than anyone else in the downtown area.
Overall, I think they are the best Courtyard in the country - I have stayed in 22 different ones all over the states.
Location was outstanding....forget what other say about high hill walk. You are in downtown Seattle....its all the same up & down toward the water. BTW, it was a very pleasant short walk.
BAD: The noise from a neighboring bar on Saturday night. Our room was all glass with spectacular view but that caught up with the noise from the street.. It is nothing to do with the hotel just the fact that there is a bar next door and that can get rowdy on weekend.

title: “THE WESTIN COPLEY PLACE”
text: The Westin Copley Place continues to offer a great experience. The rooms are always clean, the check in is easy and the staff is extremely friendly and knowledgeable. The location could not be better as it is within walking distance to great restaurants, bars and the best shopping. We love this place and we stay here whenever we visit Boston.

title: “FABULOUS! Can't wait to return!”
text: My husband and I stayed at Hotel Contessa 3 nights, March 1 - March 4. I am extremely picky about hotel accommodations and was very happy with our choice of this hotel.
