It is new as of November 2005. We enjoyed the ambiance, cleanliness, courtesy and amenities of Hotel Contessa. We had never been to San Antonio before and weren't exactly sure about where on the Riverwalk to stay. We were pleasantly surprised at the convenient location of the hotel. It's located towards the quieter end of the Riverwalk. There is more activity and noise towards the other end of the river, but it's only a very short walk from the hotel. There are great restaurants just around the bend of the river near the hotel. The river is located out the bottom floor of the hotel. There is a floor below the main lobby with a restaurant and bar. Outside of this area they have patio seating for the restaurant and there are some benches near the water to sit. As a shortcut to get to the OTHER end of the Riverwalk where some other great restaurants are, we walked about a block and a half (on the sidewalks of the city streets out of the front lobby of the hotel) instead of walking the perimeter of the river all the way to the other end. (The Riverwalk makes a square). Our room was on the 10th floor in a corner. We were given the handicapped accessible room which was probably a little more spacious. The rooms are more like suites. (Although suites are also available). Living room area has a flat screen TV, sofa, small dining room table, and some sitting chairs. There is a small hallway which included a bar, long counter, closet, and safe. Bathroom was very nice. Shower curtain was not a regular straight rod, they have the curved rods so the space inside the shower is roomier. Bedroom had a very comfortable king size bed, long desk, flat screen TV, and closet. The pool, spa and workout facility is located on the roof level. The spa was not yet open. Pool/hot tub area is really neat. There are large windows overlooking the city up there and it's not enclosed overhead. Very nice. Not sure about the temp of the pool or whether it's heated or not b/c we forgot to bring our swimming suits. Workout facility has the latest brand new equipment. We didn't try the bar or restaurant downstairs, but my husband read that the chef is new and the restaurant is beginning to get great reviews. The restaurants we enjoyed were Casa Rio, the Original Mexican Restaurant, and Texas Land and Cattle. Our room was a corner room and faced an intersection and we didn't find it to be very noisy. We were also just a couple floors (maybe 2) from the roof and didn't experience any noise from the pool or huge fans located up there. We rented a car and parked it in a parking lot across from the hotel (not the hotel's designated area). It might have cost us $8 or $9 a day? The avg rate on our rooms was $200/night for the 3 nights we stayed. We hope the rates will stay low, but figure they will probably jump after the hotel is established. Our fourth night in San Antonio we booked a room closer to Sea World at another hotel. (If we had known it wasn't that far away, we would have stayed another night at Hotel Contessa.) It truly made me appreciate the accommodations we had the first 3 nights of our trip! We really enjoyed our entire time in San Antonio and can't wait to go back!

title: “Beautiful grand old hotel - a nice piece of history”
text:
I love old buildings...but when they are hotels, they are often run down. This hotel does not fall into that category at all. It oozes of a day when elegance was grand. The rooms are in good shape, the bathroom updated, but in keeping with the period of the hotel. 
I love when the staff calls you by your formal name and smile. No one (except the concierge) fell outside of this area. They were nice, attentive and knowledgeable. The door is always opened for you, your luggage well taken care of and a cab always hailed when you needed it. The room was always cleaned and the lobby beautiful! A huge bouquet of red roses are a fixture right in the middle of the entrance.
Room service had a limited menu and it was room service. Fairly good. I did manage to collect 3 bouquets of carnations cast out from fellow guests. The staff was very nice here also.
The restaurant in the hotel was nice, but pricey and ALWAYS busy (so others must think it's good also!).
Any pictures you see of this place, especially the main dining room with it's atrium, are true. It's a beautiful old gem in San Francisco.
My only negative was the Concierge. Many of us found (there were 7 of us staying at this hotel for a mininum of a week - I stayed 2) that they were distracted, appeared to be bothered by us and not that helpful. They need to improve this aspect of the service.

title: “Airport Friendly”
text: There are some hotels that I keep coming back to . . . and the Hilton LA Airport is one of them. It's a well run hotel with excellent customer service, very close to the airport with frequent shuttle service and, on this visit, I was provided an upgrade to a two-room junior suite. The beds are super comfortable, two flat screen TVs, comfortable furniture, and, even though I had a smaller bathroom, there's a great shower. I am also a big fan of the Hilton Honors breakfast and evening lounge. While the lounge is rather small and sometimes a bit crowded, they serve a generous breakfast.

title: “Not a 4 star hotel. Not worth it...”
text: I'm currently staying at this hotel for a conference and this is not what a 4 star hotel looks like. I've stayed at many 4 star hotels several times and had a great time time. The lobby looks great and the staff are real nice.The rooms are so tiny and very dated. Bathrooms are horrible. The carpets and the furniture are old and the decor is ancient. There is no view at all, you are pretty much looking into a red brick wall from your room. You have to pay for the fitness center and dining charges are ridiculous (forget about in-room dining). For $250 a night, I'd definitely ask for more than this. I'm very disappointed. Other reviewers said the renovated rooms are nice, but I guess we got one of the old rooms.

title: “Lovely Hotel”
text: The hotel was very nice. My room was quiet and the bed was comfortable.

title: “Would NOT stay at the Opal next time”
text: Booked with Hotwire. CLAIMED to be a 3 star hotel. I would not rate it more than a 1 star. The hotel is old and the hallways smell awful. The room is very small and the bathroom is very minimal - didn't even provide bath soap, a leaning chest for a closet. Parking is expensive.

title: “An ideal place to stay in NYC”
text: This is a wonderful hotel with lovely rooms, friendly staff, a nice gym and in a great location. It seemed centrally located to all the attractions we wanted to see, cab wait outside for convenience but a subway station is right around the corner. It's a great neighborhood for walking and just enjoying being in the city. We will definitely stay there again next time we stay in the city.

title: “Thanks TANYA!”
text:
All in all yeah the affinia 50's above average. Classy joint, good location, clean rooms, very comfortable beds, however I think the overwhelming popularity on this place on TripAdvisor's turned this place into somewhat of a zoo... got kind of noisy @ night, the staff in the lobby could be more proactive and helpful - I had to pull teeth to find a local computer repair place, I suggest a free public computer in the lobby would be most helpful!
BUT MOST HELPFUL EMPLOYEE AWARD GOES TO: (and she knows who she is...) Tanya @ concierge! Tanya let me print out a couple pages instead of being way inconvenienced by ~$7?/hr to use the business center. Tanya also recommended and made last minute dinner reservations @ an incredible Italian restaurant down the street.
Thanks to Tanya we may be back!
Thanks again.

title: “All we hoped for and more”
text: This review is a bit late in the writing however better late than never. This Hotel has been recommended by so many people what more can we add. After being made redundant i fulfilled a dream trip to spend the new year in New York. Well you could not have asked for anything more than the, Inn New York City.Wonderful hosts,Ruth and Elyn,who were so helpful.We couldn't wait for each day to see what goodies would be left for us - we were never disappointed. We stayed in the Vermont suite where the fridge was full of supplies every day along with bagels,croissants,cakes,fruit and plenty of sweets! If you'd like a hotel in a great location,spotlessly clean, great hosts and a real 'home from home' look no further - just don't book when we want to return!!!!!!!!!! The Rees family (49,52,20,18). Thanks Ruth and Elyn for a holiday to remember.

title: “Hostel masquerading as a hotel”
text: I stayed at this hotel earlier this week for one night and it was one of the most miserable experiences I've ever had. I travel to NYC regularly and have stayed at many hotels around the city. Always wanted to try the Pod Hotel because I like small spaces and it seemed fun, hip and modern based on the website. In reality, this is a low-grade hostel pretending to be a hotel and charging way too much for what you get. There is nothing budget about the prices of the rooms, except maybe for the single rooms with hall bathroom access. You can stay at much nicer, full-service hotels for a similar price so there is no big savings benefit of staying here. Biggest problem we had with this hotel: you cannot control the temperature in your room. During the unseasonably cold weekend we just experienced, we literally could see our own breath in the room once the temps dropped that night. They do not provide space heaters or turn the heat on manually, so we literally froze all night. It was very much like staying in a dorm where you freeze during the cooler months because the heat only comes on once its literally freezing outside. I think this is completely unacceptable when you're paying $200-300 a night for a room. Other problems we had: 1. the bellman arranged for a car and said the flat rate was $35 but didn't mention extra charges for using a credit card, even though I specifically asked about credit card use, 2. bed and pillows were extremely firm to the point of feeling like I slept on a floor all night, and 3. no hot water! Per the maintenance guy, the pipes are not insulated so if a room is vacant for a day, the water becomes very cold and you have to run the water until it flushes out the cold water. It took at least 10 minutes to get warm water, which is a huge waste of water. He told us the trick was to turn on the shower and sink faucet and let them run, which is insane. Not eco-friendly and what guest should have to run the water for such excessive times just to wash their face?! The wi-fi was also not working properly Tuesday morning so I couldn't check-in for my flight when I wanted to. And beware that there is also no insulation between rooms so you will also hear everyone on the hall and everything they are doing. After dealing with little sleep (due to noise and the temperature), freezing conditions, hard bed, spotty wi-fi, and cold water, I was very upset that I had booked this hotel. I honestly feel that I should not have had to pay for this stay as it was unacceptable in every way possible. I wanted to speak with the general manager upon check-out but was only given the general hotel e-mail address as a means of contacting him. All around an unacceptable experience and money very poorly spent.

title: “Loved, would definitely stay again.”
text:
We stayed in a suite for a week in April. It was fantastic, if you appreciate old and can handle the average showers. The rooms were massive and the price was to die for. You really can't beat the salisbury's location - we felt like we could get anywhere we wanted easily. It is right near the subway and in walking distance to so much. We adore "old" so relished in the old windows, door frames, door knobs etc. If you like flash you may struggle with the bathrooms but to be honest if you are looking for something with a good price you can't go past this place. We had outstanding service from the minute we walked in the door, contrary to some other reviews on this site. Oh - and one other thing - there are some reviews here recommending you don't stay at the front of the building because of the noise from 57th street. I would say, don't let the noise put you off! We were on floor 7 at the front and just adored having the street view - in spite of the noise. We really felt part of the city! If the sound of traffic means you'll lie awake though I guess reconsider. All I'm saying is that the view at the front is brill - we adored watching busy New Yorkers bustle to and from work! Enjoy.
Oh, ps - there are a zillion great places to eat around the area too. Just look at menupages.com, or ask the front desk.

title: “2nd Stay at Milburn was Great!”
text:
We just returned from our NYC trip and stayed 4 nights at the Milburn. We stayed here about 1 1/2 years ago b/c we were taking our then 2 1/2 year old son with us and wanted "suite" type accommodations that were affordable. Since our first stay was so great, we returned this past week and were just as satisfied as the last time. This hotel is perfect for traveling with kids! Our one bedroom unit had a living room with a small kitchenette. While the kitchenette area is very tiny, it's still so handy b/c of the fridge and microwave. Having the extra space with the living room is a real plus to us so that we don't have to go to bed as early as our son, and it's also nice to be able to spread out and relax a bit more while in the hotel. 
The suite was clean and comfortable; I think they've all been renovated recently with new TV's and the bedding seems better now as well--much more comfortable than what I recall from the last time. Housekeeping and other staff (nice front desk workers!) were always friendly and helpful to us as well.
The 72nd and 79th street subways are just a few blocks away in either direction, there are lots of restaurants nearby, and there are 2 grocery stores basically around either corner. Central Park is also a short walk away. There are also drugstores and other shopping in the area. Being on the UWS puts you in a real NYC neighborhood, which means it's family friendly and easy to get things you might need during your stay. I recommend this hotel highly for anyone traveling with family. We'll look forward to our next stay!

title: “Pleasantly surprised”
text:
I stayed at the Hilton Anatole recently for an association meeting. It is an atrium-style hotel and quite lovely at first glance. Front desk staff was nice and helpful for check-in, but on a later day offered up the room number of one of my female colleagues, which is a major no-no in today's world. Of the two atriums, the one outside my room had some sort of unknown odor - I think it might have had something to do with the plants growing all along the overhang of each floor. The food (room service, restaurant and banquet food) was mediocre at best, but that might have had more to do with the person who planned the events.
The room itself was quite nice, clean and everything worked well. The bed & pillows were super comfy and I loved the clock radio - it had presets to "country", "jazz", "classical", etc. which made it easy to find a favorite station in an unfamiliar town.
The hotel's shopping is excellent and the prices are actually not too bad either. I wasn't crazy about the location which is a ways from the airport and the convention center, but it would be an excellent choice for a meeting held exclusively on-site. 
I would recommend the hotel for business or pleasure.

title: “Where the Literati Met”
text:
After many years of visiting Manhatten, I finally stayed at the Algonquin. It did not disappoint. Refurbished in 2008, it was a charming step back to the turn of the 20th century when it was built (1902) and the Roaring Twenties when it achieved its forever fame as daily host to the Round Table.
The hotel lobby is beautifully restored with dark painted wood paneling, soft lighting, elegant sofas, club chairs and period furniture. The dining area where the famous Round Table still stands, is presided over by a colorful painting of the "Vicious Circle". Fresh flowers, black and white tile flooring, narrow staircases with wrought iron railings and marble stairs, worn with the tread of so many hotel occupants and staff, as well as the tiny, mal-functioning elevators, make for an authentic experience. 
Our room was small. I believe they used the word "cozy". It had a bay window overlooking the 44th Street entrance. But it was spotless and decorated in an Art Deco minimalist style and we were comfortable. I wouldn't want to pay $300-$400 for it but for location and comfort it was a very good deal at $199.
Our valet/bellman was wonderful. He had been there a long time and was nice, knowledgable, helpful. Their desk staff was impersonal and not particularly friendly. The doorman was helpful and efficient. Housekeeping was quiet and friendly.
I'd stay there again for the convenience of the Times Square theatre district with so much to do as well as the period charm..

title: “Convenient airport hotel”
text: we stayed one night at this airport hotel. shuttle took a long time for pickup at LAX- we waited over 40 mins. the hotel is huge, nice and clean rooms with small bathroom. good enough for an overnight stay. free wifi in the hotel lobby. takes 5 mins by shuttle to the airport. we paid US$90 a night (booked at wotif.com), so pretty good value at that price.

title: “Weekend getaway with the family”
text: Just got back right now from our little family weekend getaway with the kids. Nice place down next too the marina. Got a great place by calling with a military discount it cut the price in half! We had a great view of part of downtown and the marina and Coronado island from our room 2506 on the 25th floor in north tower. Staff was helpful and nice. We had this tiny fridge in the room but it wouldn't hold much stuff and we had juices and snacks for the kids and my sons medicine. We called the lobby and they send up an extra fridge and a bigger older one that was ice cold. That was very helpful. We didn't have bath robes, we called and they sent up no problem. We had breakfast at the the hotel twice at the "DW" nice little buffet breakfast kids loved it. The wife and I had some awesome Huge Nacho plate and drinks poolside at the Tiki bar place. It looks awesome at night the pool is lit up this cool blue nice jacuzzis. Starbucks inside the hotel. Parking was steep 26 buck a day for self parking and 36 for valet per day!!! Overall great place close to downtown and restaurants, bars etc. I would go again.

title: “Great Help from Front Desk”
text: I arrived for a late check -in and found the room to have not been made up - I was assisted by Mohammed at the front desk who quickly moved me to an even better room with a very sincere apology- He made a less than ideal situation that I was not in the mood for disappear almost instantly-

title: “PERFECT !!!!!”
text:
I planned a trip to New York City for New Years 2009-2010 for my son's 21st birthday. Not knowing much about the hotels in New York I depended on the location and the reviews when I chose this hotel...I want everyone to know it was the best choice!!! We arived late on the night of the 30th...the front desk people were pleasant and right there to get our lugage. Check in was fast and done with a smile the whole time. We were taken to our rooms and when the door opened the light was on and the rooms was so enviting. It was so clean and looked like they had just redecorated just for our visit. The all you can eat breakfast was WONDERFUL! and held us until out New Years Eve dinner! The front desk people were alwasy there to answer any questions about where to go in the city or where the best place to catch a cab to hold 5 people was. The hotel was just far enough away from the New Years Eve hubbub, yet close enough that we were able to walk to time square to join the other million people who had come into the city. Or check out on New Years Day was quick and once again done with a smile.
I will deffinently go back to this hotel and will tell eveyone I know that this is the place to stay!

title: “good location, good service but small room but comfortable”
text: I've booked a single room with private bath. small room thou understandable in pricey NYC, clean bathroom. room furnishings are from ikea but still comfortable. friendly service with staff, thou i cannot locate the hotel door (lobby) on my 1st night back from 5th ave as it was too small. overall nice experience.

title: “Basic room was a disappointment but upgrade was a big improvement”
text: When we arrived we were disappointed with our room. We booked a basic queen room and it looked shabby, with a dirty ceiling and carpet, and cracks in the bathroom. The shower curtain was too small so water went everywhere, the minibar was humming loudly and when an engineer came to 'fix it' it turned out that he had actually just switched it off so it ended up leaking water all over my husband's suitcase. The bed was very bouncy with a dip in the middle so every time my husband moved I was woken. We complained about the bed and the next day when a king sized room became available were moved to it. It was far better with a comfy bed, more space and a massage chair. If you get a good room it's worth considering staying here as it was a bit cheaper than other hotels in the area, it was very quiet in the rooms, and the extras like free wi fi, coffees, and reasonably priced breakfast were all appreciated. Service was also good. But I wouldn't recommend the basic rooms.

title: “the best place to stay in Philadelphia”
text:
outstanding , luxury, the staff is perfect, works like a Swiss clock
The room was so cozy and perfect

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text: My wife and I stayed here for 3 nights at the beginning of our holiday and 2 nights at the end. The location is second to none. The staff are so helpful and friendly, nothing is too much bother. The cheese and wine reception is a must as it provides an excellent oppurtunity to chat with other guests and share experiences of San Francisco. Will certainly stay here on all future visits to San Francisco.

title: “A fine little resort hotel”
text:
My wife, six year old son and I stayed in at Humphrey's in August 2003. 
Initially we were concerned about the look of the hotel from the outside but once we got into our room it was fine. Nothing particularly luxurious but the layout was fine. The hotel has a very reasonable heated (to a good temperature) outdoor pool at its centre and has plenty of sun beds and seating. Every morning there are clean pool towels on all the chairs and plenty more to use when you want them. 
They also have a hot tub near the pool which was nice and very hot. The service is good. Efficient and friendly. When you order something by phone from the front desk they call you about five minutes later to check that you got what you wanted - a nice touch I think. Location is not spectacular and its a pity that there is no direct access to the harbour behind. Humphrey's has a rather odd feature in that it has a large stage and seating area outside (about 30 ft from the pool) in which is stages very regular concerts for the public. They certainly have some well known artists playing for those who wish to attend. 
However, guests should not be overly put off by this 'feature' (like we were initially!). In fact as long as your room does not face the stage or pool you will hardly be able to hear the concert even when in full flood. Also, the concerts dont seem to finish late so it was never a bother to us at all. Basically, I would be happy to go back to the hotel and would be happy to recommend it to anyone. Whilst we were there we met several families that had been back to the hotel for many years running - indeed they were somewhat surprised that I and my family were first timers. Such regular patronage must say something positive about this hotel.

title: “Great Deal for Elks members!”
text: I booked this hotel through Hotels.com. You will not be offered the same rate as an Elk member if you do this. I suggest calling the hotel direct because it will save you $50 to $70 if you do. If you drive, we highley recommend using their valet. It will take you approx 15 to 25 minutes to get your car, but you could (if you're an Elk member) use the Elks Lodge Bar on the 3rd floor while you're waiting. They have a very nice lobby that you could wait in too. The staff is very well trained, courteous and professional. Their scaffolding in the front of the hotel, but didn't see anyone working on it. Being on the weekend. So that might be something to consider. Our room was very nice. The window only opened about 10", but that's all we really needed. The beds are fantastic... I wanted to bring ours home. The bathroom fixtures are way out dated, the sink is cracked. The was paint on the tile in the shower. The tile looks to be much newer. And we found minor mold in the shower and around the back splash of the sink. We did mention this to the front desk, he took notes of our issues. I still recommend staying here. It's very close to little cafe's, restaurants and bars. Within 1 to 4 minutes walk. Getting a taxi only took like 5 minutes if that.

title: “Just amazing..would stay there again.”
text: My wife and I stayed there 5 mights. Room was very retro and very nice. What impressed us most was the exercise room...fantastic! Staff was friendly and prices surprisingly affordable.

title: “Beautiful and clean!”
text: The food here is delicious! The rooms are spacious and nice.

title: “GREAT STAY, WELL LOCATED.”
text: I booked this hotel for a night while our US NAVY ship was in town for the Seattle Sea Fair. I e-mailed management after booking a reservation through a third party because I had read some negative reviews with regards to room quality when booking this way. I just wanted to make sure that the room had two queen beds as I was sharing the room with a shipmate. Mr. Battersby of management responded that all was good. When we arrived we could not have been more pleased, the hotel treated us great and even upgraded our room. The bed was comfortable,linens were clean and fresh, pillows perfect and the location of the hotel is in easy walking distance of the Pikes Place Market and other shopping. A short bus ride or the monorail will get you to the space needle. All in all a great stay for a couple of tired Sailors wanting to get on shore for a few days and sleep in a comfortable bed for the night. Thanks for the great hospitality. US NAVY CHIEF

title: “Busy location with easy Subway access”
text: I stayed for one-night on business and was upgraded to a suite. The bed was extremely comfortable and the gym was larger than average with quality equipment. There is a subway stop directly outside of the hotel and food options are plentiful. The hotel seems to have recently completed renovations, which were well done. Ask for lounge access - there is warm breakfast and drinks available.

title: “Very sloooow elevator”
text:
Try to get a room with an even number. That will put you in the airport opposite site, and you will not be disturb by airplane flying close to the airport. Also, try to get a room on the lowest floor, since the 2 elevators are very slow. It takes a while to go from lobby level to floor #6...
Good service and fast Internet, clean room.
The parking lot can be easily full, so you may have a hard time to park. 
This hotel is close to all car rental agency. Walking distance. Otherwise it is in the middle of an industrial area, nothing really to do around.

title: “nice hotel”
text: really nice hotel...wonderful lobby and bar/restaurant area in a great location......guest services are comendable and courteous...drawbacks are small bathrooms and really small rooms...nonetheless clean.....would not stay here again only because of the small size of the rooms and bathrooms...we had a double room, for one couple, it would be ok......

title: “Great location, beautiful rooms, disappointingly spotty service”
text:
I love the Four Seasons hotel but the stay here was really disappointing - all because of something that this brand normally does so well - service.
On the good points - great location, right off Michigan Ave, near Water Tower place so close to shopping, the lake. Nice rooms - we had a "premier room" that was really more of a suite.
On the bad - we had problems with room service multiple times - once the order wasn't complete, twice they ignored the number of people we had and didn't bring enough place settings and were really inconsistent with what was offered - one day, large bowl of berries, the next, small; one day lots of bagels, next day, one.
More concerning was the housekeeping. We had one bottle of shampoo when we arrived and one soap. for the sink, the shower and the tub. No washcloths were left and not enough towels. An old cup of coffee was never removed (through both turndown and regular service) and a bottle of champagne sat in a lukewarm bucket of water that was never replenished with ice and that soaked through to the table.
May sound picky but really it's bizarre for this brand. It's almost as if they are into severe cost cutting.

title: “Very pleasantly surprised”
text: A good budget option in Downtown Boston, just next to the Tufts Medical T. Our group requested an early (11am!) check-in and all thirteen rooms were available on check-in, along with complementary cookies. My room was large, clean and comfortable; the bathroom a touch dated but it did the job. The only downsides: breakfast not included, and wifi only at extra cost (though in my part of the hotel there were several free wifi connections available from neighbouring buildings).

title: “Really perfect and a good price”
text: I was escaping another hotel so just walked in here and even off the street yet got a pretty decent rate, $130. The place was immaculate, staff friendly, fitness room really nice and bed gigantic! A great place, close to downtown. Good business center & good wireless connection. As good as a $200+ a night hotel. I'd recommend without hesitation.

title: “Convenient location for Apple's WWDC”
text: Chose this primarily for location 8 blocks to Moscone West for WWDC. Easy to get to hotel from the BART getting off at Powell Street station (4 block walk to the hotel). Hotel is in a great location about 1 block from Union Square. Rooms are small but comfortable. I could also hear street noise from the 6th floor but used ear plugs so noise wasn't an issue for me. Front desk staff and conceirge were very helpful arranging taxi's and giving directions to Fisherman's wharf using the Powell St. trolley. There is no air conditioning but it wasn't required for my stay in early June. There is no restaurant in the hotel but Lois's Diner is right next store for breakfast. Rooms are clean and given that rooms were getting booked up for WWDC, I was quite happy with the room.

title: “Thanks to the Dragon Gate Inn”
text:
We stayed at the Dragon Gate Inn for surgery at the USC Medical Center. 
Our totak two week stay was great and Sophia, at the front desk, was wonderful in continually helping us with any problem that arose.The Dragon Gate has a wonderful location in Chintown. The rooms are spacious with all the extras.We highly recommend the Inn to everyone.

title: “Another amazing stay!”
text: Stayed on July 16th and 17th on the Club floor. Once again, I was treated like the entire staff was there solely to attend to my needs, and like nobody was more important. Or, at least that's how they made me feel. Morning breakfast was amazing. Lunch was even better. I'm not a fan of hors'deourves, but I had some Champagne. But the absolute tops were the desserts! Oh my God they were so amazing. Top notch in every way!

title: “Excellent service at Trellises Restaurant.”
text: We had breakfast with clients at Trellises restaurant on the morning of February 10th. Our waitress, Pati Mulclevicz, provided excellent service to our group. Thank you, Pati.

title: “Nice for the Price, Location Could be Better”
text:
We spent 3 nights at the Washington Court Hotel in August 2012, and we had a great stay. The hotel itself was very clean, front desk staff was friendly and we did not run into any real problems at all!
The rooms are nicely sized with a large bathroom! Clean, comfy, pretty much all we were looking for. The staff was nice enough to arrange for a room early (we arrived at 1pm and check-in wasn't until 3pm) and also held our luggage after check out so we could spend one more day exploring before our late flight. Very friendly! 
There are not many amenities to speak of at this hotel, there was a bar (which was always totally dead) and a restaurant which seemed a bit overpriced considering it, too, was never busy (only saw one couple eating their throughout our entire stay). The staff was always friendly and there is a small gift shop that is open at random hours if you needed a snack or souvenir. Internet is free (password from front desk required) but slow and intermittent at times.
Located very close to Union Station, which has a small number of stores (Express, Ann Taylor, Victorias Secret, etc.) for shopping and some restaurants (mostly casual - Chipotle, Chop't, Yo! Sushi, Corner Bakery, Au Bon Pain, Tony Roma's Pizza). Beyond Union Station ... you have to take a significant walk to get to a CVS or drugstore, and the restaurants that we found to be nicer in terms of dining experience. We thought the location left something to be desired (quite dead after the Capitol Hill workers headed home) and wished we would have stayed closer to the other end of the National Mall (more action in this area). If you are fine walking at night, you can definitely get to other areas within a 20-30 minute walk, however my mom did not feel comfortable doing so (for the record... I felt safe, but I am a 20-something living in a moderately big city, compared to my mother who lives in a small town). 
Would stay again for value ... we got a great price through travelocity secret hotels.

title: “Great deal in Center City, or "I don't know where the hate's coming from"”
text:
When planning my birthday weekend in Philadelphia (visiting family and friends and taking in a Phillies game) I'd originally booked a hotel out by the airport but kept checking around to see if I could get something relatively cheap in Center City. Bingo--up came Club Quarters with great rates and I booked.
Location? Awesome. I took the subway up from the airport and the hotel was only a little more than two blocks away from the stop. Access to the other SEPTA subway lines is the same way. As I prefer to use public transit this was a huge plus. Beautiful huge lobby. Some have complained about the slow elevators but I guess they must have done something because I think the longest I had to wait for an elevator was maybe a minute and it was quick going up or down. Yes, the rooms are pretty small but not overly so--my room, a single, had a queen bed in one section, a workstation in another, then the bathroom, perfectly adequate. Everything was clean and the bed was super comfortable. The free WiFi worked perfectly, and I'd add that this place has the cheapest hotel vending machine I've ever seen! As far as food goes stay away from the high-priced Davio's--for a true Philly experience stroll down 17th Street a couple of blocks and hit up Little Pete's, a 24/7 diner. Granted, you won't get your butt kissed there but there's plenty of good food at reasonable prices. If there's any small nitpick, it's with the free bottled water machines--apparently my definition of "chilled" and Club Quarters' definition differ greatly but that's what ice buckets are for.
Because of the small rooms this is a place for single travelers or couples, not families. Which, I'll admit, is also a plus because you don't have to deal with screaming kids running all over the place. Don't let the naysayers scare you off, this place is fine, cheap and nicely located. Book with confidence!

title: “WORST HOTEL EVER”
text: We stayed at this hotel for the 1st & last time due to it's location. The room was neat but VERY dirty. The bathroom had hair in the shower & on the floor, tub was dirty. The comforter had what looked like a rust stain on it & was ripped. Walls was dirty as well.. To highten the experience we saw a mouse run through the room. They moved us to a new room which had the same issues, but had a nice strong smell of marijuana.

title: “Good location & friendly Staff”
text: Great Hotel... This is an older hotel which is very well maintained, in fact much better than many of the older hotels that I've stayed at in chicago. The hotel is within walking distance to many great restaurants & shopping. Staff was great....

title: “Great hotel, bad spa experience”
text: Hotel is great- luxurious, unparallelled location. But the spa was NOT relaxing at all. Had a terrible massage and then hoped to relax by the pool, but they must open the fitness center to outside memberships- there were TONS of little kids screaming in the pool and dressing rooms, slamming lockers, etc (locker room is shared with the spa)- complete with inattentive parents. When I nicely asked about the kids the staff told me there were many kids swimming there on weekends... I love kids but was at the spa as an anniversary gift to get away from mine! So disappointed. Will be sticking with teh Four Seasons where spa treatments are fantastic and it's not the (ritzy) neighborhood indoor pool...

title: “Average overall, very neat aspect of converted bank, comfortable as always in a Marriott”
text: My fiancee and I stayed in this hotel for two nights in January 2012. It was an average stay, very comfortable as all our Marriott stays are (comfortable bed, pillows). We requested additional pillows and they were delivered later in the day. It was a clean hotel. The room is a decent size, nothing spectacular. We liked the aspect of this hotel having once been a bank - it's a neat feature with historic character. The lobby is quite impressive. I do no believe that breakfast was included (which would be strange for a Marriott) but I believe they had some fruit and pastries out front, but not in a kitchen or eating area or anything. There was not wifi when we were there, which is surprising - all hotels we stay in have wifi included these days. There was a 'business centre' downstairs in the lobby - inconvenient actually. We would likely stay again because the location was pretty great for our needs.

title: “Superb!”
text: My family and I satyed at the Monaco for one night and had a wondeful time! The hotel was in the center of it all. The staff was friendly form the check-in to the valet. We love the window seat and spent all the morning lookig out of it. We had a suite and it did not let us down. The colors were vibrant and inviting, very comfy! The bathroom wa also gorgeous. The jacuzzi was relaxing and the bath products scented the room the whole stay! Overall, WONDERUL!

title: “Give this one a Miss”
text:
We went by Trip Advisor’s rating for this hotel and I can’t understand how it rated so highly. I wonder if we stayed somewhere different!!
The bed was the most uncomfortable one I have ever slept in – hard as a brick. The room was small and pokey – smaller than one we had in New York where you expect a small room. There was a veranda and at 6 am people were standing outside our window chatting and drinking their coffee.
Breakfast was half a muffin and coffee from an urn set up outside in the courtyard. 
We had planned to stay 2 nights here but only stayed 1.
It was close to the water but miles from the main drag where friends of ours were. It was clean... completely white, no clock and a pokey shower/toilet area. 
It was cheap I have to say, but the most disappointing hotel in our US vacation of 5 weeks. We stayed at a total of 11 Hotels - most of them from Trip Advisor - thank you :)

title: “Worst Hotel in 5 years”
text: Stayed here two nights, Nov 2 and 3 and it was BAD. A conference rate of $157 appeared cheap enough but considering the hotel, service, etc it was WAY over priced. The rooms are just right for 4 shoe boxes. on the upper floors the hallways are about 90 degrees. Food is weak to average. Bartender in the evening was the most helpful person on the entire staff but the lobby bar is not very comfortable either. One Star is too many.

title: “Ms. Estrela Estrada”
text:
I recently had to assist my colleagues with the logistics behind an export licensing seminar. The seminar lasted for two full days, and while I manned the front desk, Estrela came buy with some breakfast items for me. She had realized that I was never able to leave my desk, and made sure I did not go hungry. Since I was starving and stressed, such dedication was really appreciated. 
Estrela and Mr. Ortega also were quick to refill coffee for a room of participants struggling to stay awake due to the heavy natures of the topics being discussed. Mr. Ortega even took into consideration special dietary considerations from participants, and made last minute changes to have special meals. 
This banquet team is super professional and sweet. 
I hope they take care of us next year as well ^o^

title: “Run of the Mill”
text:
Valet service is very expensive ($35.00) and drinks down at the bar are also expensive. The room was basically normal and nice with no complaints. Got this through Hotwire and was inexpensive, so overall, served it's need of giving us a place to sleep overnight without the worries of a roadside hotel/motel.
On the other hand, the staff was very friendly and helpful and went out of the way to accomodate us and whatever problems we had (I forgot my toothbrush and toothpaste). They got the needed items to us in two shakes of a lambs tail.

title: “Very Trendy with HUGE rooms!”
text: My husband and I stayed at the St. Giles Tuscany for our Anniversary weekend. It is a very trendy hotel with spacious rooms. It is just out of the hustle and bustle of the tourist areas but close enough to the avenues for shopping. Everyone was very friendly and overall I would definitely recommend it to anyone who doesn't want to stay in the overcrowded areas, anyone looking for a good deal, and anyone who likes boutique hotels!

title: “Wonderful hotel: loved the downfilled comforters & triple sheets!”
text: My daughter & I stayed there Jan30-Feb 2, 2005. The hotel is clean, beautiful, elegant and safe. The location across from Penn Station was perfect for us because we came in on Amtrak. The doorman and desk clerks were courteous and efficient. Everything works as it should. The room was clean, beautifully appointed, and had lovely down filled comforters with a triple sheet overtop, so the top sheets can be laundered as needed instead of those gorpy usual motel bedspreads that you don't know who did what on... enough said. It was absolutely beautiful. We had plenty of towels and a fully done up kitcheonette with all the dishes etc. to ever need. We were on the 16th floor so did not hear much street noise (sirens etc can't be helped). We felt very safe. There was no noise, no children running the halls or yelling or any disruptions inside the hotel. I would recommend it again & plan to use it as our home in NYC if I travel there again. Only thing I would change is add an exhaust fan to the bathroom, but that's very minor on the scale of things; clean, safe, quiet, ok price, & those lovely down filled quilts ...

title: “Small but good location.”
text:
The W is great if you're looking explore the city and not spend anytime in your hotel. It's really just a bolt hole to use as the rooms are a little on the small (and not particularly luxurious) side. I think this W is a little tired and in need of a refurb.
On the plus side, the staff were great, friendly and welcoming. If you're contemplating room service get the cheese burger-one of the best burgers I've ever had. I'd probably stay again if i was visiting nyc for sightseeing and shopping but probably not for business. I need somewhere a little more relaxing next time!

title: “I love this place!”
text:
I had the pleasure of staying at the Holiday Inn San Diego in Mission Valley in March of 2010. I would definetly stay there again and recommend this place to my friends. The rooms were clean and the staff was friendly and helpful. Nice to know there are still good employees and a clean place to stay. 
We will be in San Diego for Super Cross this year and we as well as our friends will be staying here at this hotel. 
Thanks for a pleasant stay!

title: “Clean and comfortable”
text:
This is a clean and comfortable hotel. Chicago is a great city for walking, so we certainly did not mind the distance to attractions. Otherwise, there is indoor access to the El..
Because it is located on top of the Chicago Sun-Times building, it is very quiet.
I don't think i would pay the premium for rooms with the city view again. The lounge has great views.
On the negative side, I would echo other comments regarding the internet connection - it was incredibly slow. If you are on business or otherwise need internet access, this could be a real problem,
Water in the pool was surprisingly and uncomfortably cold.
.

title: “Fantabulous”
text: Stayed in 2 suites - 7 of us total. It was a real value believe me. Mon - Thurs we stayed when full hot buffet breakfast, evening cocktails & light dinner were included. Our suite was extremely clean and seemed to be cleaned as soon as we left out rooms for the day. We had plenty of towels to go around and didn't have to call for extras as we've had to do in other hotels. A plug was fixed immediately when we called it in as well. When we went to dining room, helpers went out of their way to ensure we sat together and that we had what we needed. Our overall experience was over the top. Thank you to Homewood Suites!

title: “A rare find: a charming business hotel”
text: I stayed here for two nights and was surprised at how comfortable and welcoming this large Chicago landmark is. The hotel, particularly its lobby, is an architectural landmark for the city, but I've stayed at famous legacy hotels in other cities that left me cold. Not so the Palmer house. Hilton is doing a good job at persuading its employees to value service and good customer relations. The rooms were comfortable, well appointed, and its executive floors are like a mini hotel within the larger hotel. All good.

title: “Great Stay at the Residence Inn”
text:
My boyfriend and I just returned from a wonderful trip to San Antonio. We stayed at the Residence Inn Downtown/Alamo Plaza. Overall the hotel was great and we were very pleased.
The positives are that the suites have full kitchens in them, a relatively comfortable bed (although for a queen it was quite small) lots of water pressure in the shower and it was VERY clean. The staff was very helpful and friendly. Whenever I called the front desk and needed something, they were at our door within 5 minutes! Although the hotel was not on the Riverwalk, it was only about a 5-10 minute walk max. It was literally a block from the Alamo, so it was very convenient. The breakfast was quite good for a buffet. It was mostly the same every day, but it was good food. Check in and check out was quick and painless (except for one detail which I will describe below.)
There really aren't any negatives about this hotel, I would prefer to call them things I hope the hotel can improve on someday. And some things are outside of the hotel's control, such as the noisy trains that seem to run all night and day. Even with the window closed, we could still hear the trains. It took some time to get used to and I don't think I slept through the night once while we were there because the trains were so loud. Other than that, it was only loud on Friday night because there is a very popular gay bar right next to the hotel. At 3am, it was like a party outside. But other than that, we didn't have any problems with the noise. Another thing that bothered me is that the hotel didn't have a common computer with internet access to use. They did have a laptop hookup in the room, but I don't have a laptop, yet I still needed to use the internet but wasn't able to.
Another downfall was the pool. It was tiny and surrounded by cement walls. I took one look at it and decided that we were not going to be spending time laying beside it. The surrounding cement walls were so high that the pool was in constant shade all day long.
Lastly, something I did find to be slightly negative, is that they wouldn't give me a AAA discount on the cost of the room. They stated that the price that I booked at ($124 per night) was lower than normal and that a 10% discount on the regular room price would have cost more than the promotional rate of $124 that they were currently charging me. I personally think that was a crock. I believe their room rate is always $124 per night and they have just found a way to avoid giving AAA members a 10% discount. That did not impress me at all.
So that is all I have to say about this hotel. San Antonio is a fabulous place to visit. If we return, we would most likely stay at this hotel again.

title: “Loved the Courtyard Marriott”
text: I don't have a bad thing to say about the Downtown Courtyard Marriott. Large room. Very comfortable king size bed. Beautiful, clean and roomy bathroom. Hotel location is very convenient. People mover accessible thru hotel lobby. Nice restaurant in hotel. We had the breakfast buffet and it was delicious. $13 per person, certainly not cheap but since it was buffet we ate plenty and got our fill of food. All the hotel staff were friendly and the waitress at Lorraine's was very helpful and friendly. We definitely recommend this hotel.

title: “Great Hotel, Location, and Staff”
text:
Wow, a little slice of paradise. Amazing location, excellent rooms. Great food. Staff is incredible. For example, when we arrived they had shown we were arriving the NEXT week. We were staying 5 nights in a Michigan Ave Suite on the 30th floor. SOMEHOW I had put in for the wrong dates! (Traveling too much I suppose) Anyhow, without skipping a beat they had us in the correct room.
Great hotel for the kids, the tent they set up in the room and the Candy Man were both big hits (ask for these). Room service was great, high quality. Our suite was HUGE. 
The hotel is a bit on the older side perhaps, but superbly maintained so that did not bother us a bit. We ended up seeing a bunch of NBA stars in the lobby, so my older son got a big kick out of that.
Oh and it is attached to a great mall. So all in all, a bit expensive, but very much worth it. Excellent!

title: “Historic hotel letdown by poor service”
text:
Stayed here last Saturday to attend a wedding. I was disappointed as soon as I pulled into the front of the hotel for valet. The valet didn't even acknowledge us with a greeting when we opened our door, nor did he offer to help or call the bellhop to have someone assist us unload our bags from the car. It was like talking to a zombie where all he did was give me my claim stub for the car. Walked into the hotel carrying all my bags since no one offered to help us and there were probably 3 staff members outside and there was no other car outside the hotel at the time. I didn't say anything to my wife about my initial impression; she told me what she felt on the elevator after checking in that she was surprised about the cold reception we got.
The only saving point I could think of is they have a nice function hall for the wedding that seems to give the place a retro cool vibe. The room we had was roomy and functional. I do agree with another review that if your room is near the elevator you can hear the tone all the way inside your room. 
Upon check out we got the same inept service from the front door staff. Geez there were 4 of them outside when we walked out and no one offered to help us assist with our bags. Oh and yes I got the same zombie service from another valet person. I should never have tipped him for such a lackluster attitude. My 2 cents, if you have to stay in this part of Baltimore then you are better off staying at the Hotel Monaco or splurge a little bit and stay closer to the Inner Harbor and get the Renaissance or the Hilton Baltimore.

title: “It is really nice, but no wifi...”
text: I stayed here with my mother in law during the National Race for the Cure. This hotel is really well located, close to the White House and many monuments. Also, there is a trolly stop right across the street. We found that was a good way to get around the city. The lobby, rooms, meeting rooms, restaurants, etc are all very upscale and nicely decorated. Everything in the room was in good working order. My only complaint is with the internet. There was a bag of wires that you had to use to connect and my understanding is that is isn't free. At the rates this hotel charges, I expect free wifi. I get it when I stay at the Holiday Inn or the Comfort Inn, so I don't think it is too much to ask. Other than that, this place is excellent.

title: “Good location, extremely helpful and hospitable staff!!”
text: We stayed here recently and were very happy with our choice. We read the recent positive reviews and made a note that renovations were complete. I had a seminar 1.5 blocks away and my husband came along to tour Washington. The hotel is in a great spot, very central to everything. It is a block away from the 14th Street historical district (which has a lot of restaurants & a Whole Foods!), a short walk to the Smithsonian & other monuments along the National Mall area, very close to the Convention Center and either the blue or yellow metro line, and not too far from Chinatown. The hotel is very clean and welcoming. We asked for a quiet room and got an internally facing room on the seventh floor which was perfect for us. We liked that our room had a mini fridge and a flat screen TV. A hot breakfast of scrambled eggs, sausage or bacon, various fruits (apples, oranges, bananas), instant oatmeal, various muffins, donuts, and breads for toasting are available. There are also juices, coffee, milk, hot chocolate, and tea. The waffle station was fun to try out as well (it varied between plain and blueberry or strawberry). The breakfast area was very clean and well stocked. We had live Irish music on the first evening we were there - the hotel had a veggie tray and a fruit and cheese tray along with various beers, wine, and sodas. We enjoyed that evening immensely! We got to meet the general manager, Mario Pais, who is a super nice and very genuine person. We also loved having the use of the breakfast area in the evenings to for our take-out dinners. It was much more relaxing to eat in the common area rather than upstairs in our room. It was also very convenient to have access to the microwave in the common area as well so we could heat up our leftovers! In the lobby, there is coffee, hot water for tea or hot chocolate, and freshly baked COOKIES. So aside from the great location, hot breakfast, and COOKIES, I would highly recommend staying here for the superb customer service – Mario, the general manager, really went above and beyond our expectations in making us feel welcomed and comfortable. It was my first time in DC and I when I come back to visit, I will definitely come and stay at the Comfort Inn again. Staying here made the trip a wonderful experience.

title: “Great rate on PL, but valet was quite pricey and slow”
text:
Saved 76% by booking thru PL! Valet which is necessary in this neighborhood was $38 a night. Their parking deck is three blocks away, therefore a little slow having the car brought around.
Rooms on the sixth floor were quiet, although amenities were inconsistent. Our room had a microwave and minifridge, our friends did not. We had a large walk in shower, they had a very narrow tub/shower combo. Beds were a bit soft, and towels a bit scratchy. HVAC worked very well.
Location is ideal!

title: “I love this hotel. My go-to in Chicago.”
text:
Hands down, the best option in Chicago where you can earn points.
In addition, a strong contender for the best in Chicago.
PROS:
-- Luxurious, comfortable rooms
-- Wonderful restaurant and restaurant-quality room service
-- Fitness center and pool
-- Wonderful, soothing lobby
-- Bathrooms are ridiculously wonderful
-- Exemplary service execution
-- Views
-- One of the few hotels of this caliber where you can earn points
CONS:
-- Rooms can be small (but not out of the range of other top-tier hotels in the area)
-- Cabs can have a wait in the morning (all hotels on the Mag Mile have this problem, as the cabs are zooming past to the Loop)
-- The price can get exorbitant

title: “Good Value for Area”
text: Stopped here on a overnighter direct from airport. Parking was difficult, ended up paying $15 on a overnite lot. Rooms a small and cosy but very clean and tidy. Staff are very helpful. Overall, beats a chain hotel in the city in terms of value for money. Would recommend.

title: “would stay again”
text: we stayed at the day's inn new year's eve. check in was quick the room was very clean. the lounge was very nice even though the bartender was also working in the dining room.the breakfast was real nice-biscuits and gravy and scrambled eggs were great!! overall a nice quiet place to stay.

title: “Expectations surpassed”
text:
Centrally located - easy walking to the main shopping avenue(Magnificent Mile Michigan Avenue)
Staff very helpful - very comfortable room and bathroom although the bathroom could have had more shelf space for toiletries/cosmetics etc.

title: “Very friendly & helpful staff”
text: Main things to say about this place was that it had exceptionally good service. We came in rather late at night when a front desk person by the name of Patrick (no relation to the Fitzpatricks I think) helped check in my wife & me in an efficient & friendly manner. Our needs were tended to quickly & positively when we expressed various needs for our family. The doorman was very helpful in suggesting the best way to travel to the airport, & even afterward when I'd accidentally left an article of clothing in the room, the staff helped us to find it a day after we'd already checked out. Otherwise, it was a clean, comfortable, & beautiful room... it's just that what stood out to us was the service. Thanks!

title: “Times Square! Enough Said.”
text: Headed down to New York with a friend. We split a room at the Hilton Garden Inn times Square. Price was a factor, since we were only spending one night, and the room was pretty much a crash pad at 4 am. I have stayed at a few Hilton Gardens Inns. These are equivalent to Hyatt Places, another great set of properties. What I most like about both brands is that the rooms are on par, if not better, than, say, a regular Hilton or Hyatt Regency. This particular property is a short walk from the heart of Times Square, and a healthy walk to 5th Ave and Central Park. Valet parking was about $45-50 for the one night and the parking is adjacent to the hotel. All of the staff were friendly and the concierge was helpful on pointing out a great place to eat lunch the first day. Room details: large bathroom with great water pressure, very comfortable beds equipped with a system to dial in your preference for either a firm or softer mattress. Wi-Fi was fast with a great signal....and complimentary! If you are looking to spend time down in Times Square, this property is a great deal for what you get. I would definitely return the next time I happen to be in New York.

title: “Half term getaway”
text: traveled with teenage son for half term, very good flights to start with with Delta despite having read bad reviews, plenty of room, food was ok and huge choice of films. Hotel was in a good location convenient for shops bars and places to eat, also near Broadway, check in was fast and efficent and although we emailed the hotel weeks before our stay and asked for a room with a view we were on the 13th floor overlooking the car park above the bus station. Rooms were not ideal for sharing with a teenager as you have no privacy and even the bathroom has a glass door, the room was well equiped and clean and although there were cooking facilities there was nowhere to sit and eat. the complimentary breakfast was adequate with cereal pastries and hot choice of egg and bacon or ham, however trying to get a seat to eat it proved difficult at times. staff at the hotel were helpful and informative, do be warned the wait for lifts at peak times can be trying to say the least. Do take advantage of the complimentary facilities mean you can travel light and you dont have to bring lots of washing home. the evening reception Tues Wed and Thur is worth a visit, having spoken to some people we were advised that the rooms in general in New York are small so the rooms here do offer more space. Would stay there again. if doing bus trip use the gray line buses as we used new your city tours and they were a much inferior service. Be warned New York is huge, take comfortable walking shoes and wrap up well if doing bus trip. We stayed for 5 nights and lots we didnt get to see, but we will go back and book a week on the beach to recover, New York really does not sleep. If you go enjoy and make sure you are not straight back to work afterwards

title: “Loved it.”
text: My wife and I stayed here for our anniversary and it was awesome. The staff was friendly, the location was good, and the whole place was just classy. I failed to request a goldfish in our room which I'm sad about but next time i'll make it happen. Love this place.

title: “Marriott West Loop !!!”
text:
Best of Houston!! Excellent location, and services.
Will definitely come back.
Thanks for everything

title: “Starwood Preferred Guest Room was Fantastic with One Exception”
text:
Stayed on the 25th floor - where the seemingly newly renovated Starwood Preferred Guest (Gold or Platinum Members) rooms are located. Had a room facing Yerba Buena gardens with two queen beds.
Rooms were very nice, clean, spacious with high quality furnishings and beds. Very impressive, especially compared to higher end Starwood hotels. On my last day someone checked into the room next door which is adjoined to my room via one of those doors that locks (but can open to connect the two rooms). I could hear EVERYTHING the neighbor was saying on their cell phone and they weren't even yelling. This could have been a major issue and the doors (or walls) need more insulation.
Other than that, a near perfect stay. Oh, the floor to ceiling windows make for an AMAZING view throughout the day.

title: “Boutique Hotel w/ good location and great price”
text: My first time in Seattle and I was w/ a group on business for just 2 nights so I didn't choose the hotel. The rooms were spacious with a couch, but it felt awkward eating room service from the low coffee table since there was no table/chair. Instead there was a work counterop - which I loved because I could spread everything out. The Front Desk and Front Door staff were very helpful and genuine. I love to try the local cuisine when I travel so I felt really lucky at being within walking distance of Hot Pot donuts and several Tom Douglas restaurants. Lola's was in the Hotel and Dhalia Lounge and Dahlia Bakery across the street. I ate at Lola's 3 times, but that is another story I'm going to save for my separate post on Lola's. Convenience store was 3 blocks away and even though I didn't go, a group of people walked to Pike's Market and said it was nearby, but it was uphill. I'll just have to come back to Seattle on vacation!

title: “Perfect for weekend getaway with the kids”
text: We live just outside of the DFW area and decided to go for a stay in Ft Worth and to go see the zoo. First off, I fell in love with the room layout - it was perfect for us as we were traveling with our 10 yr old and 5 month old kids. The rooms are huge and the kids were able to sleep in the front section and feel just far enough away that hubby and I couldn't hear every rustle. Loved that there was a fridge and two sinks. The sectional sofa was huge. Large king bed and they have plenty of pillows in the room, although I'm a pillow hog and they were nice enough to bring 3 more (they were all down pillows and I prefer foam but that pretty minor). Service was prompt (brought pillows in less that 10 min) and everyone we met there was extremely friendly and helpful. The breakfast area was nice and I thought the food was actually good. Was perfect before we headed to the zoo (which was only a few minutes away). We spent hours in the pool - nice sized; one end is 3-4 feet and the deeper end goes to about 6 ft. Pool area had plenty of great quality towels and comfortable seating and umbrella tables. They had a wonderful discounted room rate when we went so it was a great value. Rooms were extremely quiet. We thought it was all just perfect and look forward to going back.

title: “VERY Disappointed with the Afternoon Tea”
text:
I didn't stay at the Waldorf, but my sister and I did go the Cocktail Terrace for afternoon tea service. We were disappointed for the following reasons (I'm excerpting this from a letter that I'm sending the Waldorf):
1) Service - It seemed as though there was no structure to the service. There was no one there to greet people who had reservations for tea--no host or hostess. Everyone just sort of walked in and sat wherever. Our waiter was good, though.
2) Food - The finger sandwiches were medicore. The scones were good, but when we were brought our tray, it didn't have scones. The waiter said that there was some sort of delay and that he would bring the scones as soon as they were delivered. It turns out that we waited a good 30 minutes for them.
3) Tea - The tea was a bit weak, even after I let it steep for 10 minutes. Apparently, they put in too little tea and a lot of water into each customer's pot.
4) Level of formality - For a place like the Waldorf, you would think that there would be some standards of formality. However, there was absolutely no dress code for the tea. Also, the sugars were served in packets rather than lumps as I've seen in many afternoon tea services. One particular incident surprised me: A couple came in for tea, and a woman (who seemed as if she might be some sort of restaurant manager) with a flour-stained black skirt, abruptly informed them that she had no more tea strainers. I couldn't believe it. I mean, only about four tables in the whole place were occupied. Where the heck were the rest of the tea strainers?
All in all, I expected more from afternoon tea at the Waldorf.

title: “Flatotel...it's all in the name”
text: Arrived to this modern and very hip establishment to the smiling, clean-shaven, welcoming faces of three professional and polite young men; what a pleasure. Check in was quick and easy; I provided payment, received my keys and was on my way after being offered maps to assist me during my time in the city. To summarize, the room was spacious, clean, spacious (oh I said that already), with comfortable, clean, plush linens. The hotel is in the middle of the block so the views weren't that great but who cares, this was a great location (MidTown) and was exactly the right price and location for my purposes in the Big City. I stayed in a one bedroom King suite but they also have two and three room suites for extended stayers (one month to one year or more); it's just like a European Flat. There is even continental breakfast, how convenient. I would definitely stay here again because it was a good environment, location, and the price was right. The only negatives I'd add are (1) the HVAC unit was on the brink; couldn't get the heat working on the cool nights and (2) no microwave. :-(

title: “Pricey for what it was, but good location”
text: San Francisco is quite pricey overall, so we were looking for the best place on a tight budget. The accommodation was clean and basic, but it was in an ideal location(Lombard Street). Be careful when you book as they don't send a receipt or email confirming anything and they don't take the money out until you get there, and since its quite pricey, your holidaying budget might get a hit. Overall the location is the selling point here.

title: “Formerly good hotel now just average”
text:
I have been staying regularly at this property on and off over the past decade. Location is still great but the rooms and facilities are getting tired. Soundproofing on the balcony windows was non existent. Even up on the 11th floor, I could hear the freeway perfectly.
The most frustrating thing was the lack of outlets at the desk. This is definitely an older design - travelers have multiple devices to plug in. Instead, the outlets were taken up by the lamp, the internet router, etc. The outlet that I could use was loose and my power kept going out. A modern Hampton Inn has a better design than this. 
I hope they update the facilities soon - if not, I'll be staying down the street...

title: “Unbeatable location”
text: The location is unbeatable and we were served well and cheerfully. It costs, but we chose this route because we had just a couple of days and wanted (a) to visit notable sites by foot and (b) to stay somewhere without hassle. An added bonus was overhearing the political discussions by lobbyists at breakfast.

title: “Beautiful Hotel”
text: Had a wonderful weekend with friends. Really enjoyed the tea in the beautiful hotel. Gallery Bar was fantastic also. Small rooms. Try to get a corner room if traveling with family or large parties so you can have some space.

title: “You Get What You Pay For”
text:
Yes...it costs a few more bucks to stay at the Ritz...but you get what you pay for!!
I would need to right a book about all the thing right with the Ritz. But more important that the awesome room with the most comfortable bed that I have EVER slept on....and the impeccable room service...and the fantastic staff...it boils down to attitude.
A illustration......after long and bumpy ride from Maryland , we checked in and I realized I forgot my phone charger. Not finding any in the pool of abandoned chargers held by the hotel , the bellman WENT TO THE STORE TO BUY ME ONE ON HIS OWN DIME!!!!! Needless to say, I reimbursed him for the charger and complemented him with a handsome and well deserved tip. 
It was a fine example of 'above and beyond the call of duty'.
I must say it is typical of the Denver RItz.

title: “Excellent in every aspect!”
text:
This hotel is perfectly located in a central location where all shops and business is. Inside is very nice aswell the rooms, which are spacious and nice decorated. The bed is delicious...
Service is superb and amenities are wonderfull. Nice bar and crouded, with excellent food.
Don't look more, and go ahead with Palomar!

title: “Friendly Hotel To Go With Friendly Skies”
text: Our experience at the Wyndam El Paso Airport was a relaxing, confortable and exhilirating experience that I soon won't forget! Its very nice to be greeted upon arrival by the front desk staff. After a long day of traveling we were famished! Making a decision to take the Hotel up on its 25% off offer on dining in, we had a wonderful experience! We were greeted and seated immediately. With drinks on the way, we took in the ambience of a tranquil atmosphere. Upon receiving our hot meals from the curtious and kind staff in a great timely manner, we lapped up every bit as we saw our tummies grow. It was well worth it and would definitely repeat this experience on our next trip to El Paso.

title: “Great experience”
text:
This Ritz was all around very good. Very well trained and friendly staff went above and beyond to make our stay pleasant. 
Rooms are clean and comfortable, good bed and bath. 
The location is very near good restaurants, shops, and attractions. It's a challenge to get a car in and around but on foot it's very easy to get to several nearby places including a Metro.

title: “great hotel”
text: The Westin at Detriot Metro Airport was perfict for a over night stay before our morning flight. Checked in about 3 and was driectly in our room with no hasles. Whent to the Delta check in and found out we coudent get our bording passes until six houers before our 10am flight. So I asked the attendant if she could change my set. Got exit row seats on boath ends of my flight at no extra charge. Worth the night stay in it self. We were alowed into the airport through the Westins private TSA secueity check point after a quick backgroung check. Had dinner a few drinks and just people wached. The room was moderin,clean, and very acomidating. Got the valy parking packiage. What a hasle free way to park at an airport. Called the Westin when we landed and my car was out front trunck open and wating for me. Great Job Westin will be back!

title: “A Big Thank You”
text: My mother just returned from the Double Tree as our house has been unliveable for the past 2 weeks,the staff went extremely friendly and I would like to give a special Thank You to Benny in the restaurant for taking care of her special requests in the mornng

title: “Good, but not great.”
text:
My partner and I debated long and hard before booking the hotel for our San Francisco vacation. Would the Hotel Vitale worth its premium price over similar hotels located nearby? We decided to go for it, based on our positive experiences with the Joie de Vivre brand. In the grand tradition of damning with faint praise, I have to say the Vitale was good. It was not, however, great, and as a result I am left to wonder if it was really worth the cost. 
When we checked in, we specifically requested as quiet a room as possible. The woman at the desk said this was no problem, and said that we'd been upgraded to a higher room class. We discovered that our room, which was on the hotel's 3rd floor, faced Mission Street and was directly above the hotel's driveway. More problematically, there were quite a few patrons of the bar/restaurant who were congregated outside this area, and their conversation was all-too-clearly audible from our room. I called down and was able to get another room, although it was a "downgrade" (and did not appreciate the front desk person arguing with me about where the noise was coming from--does it really matter whether it's noise from the restaurant or the valet area? All that I cared about was that it was impossible to sleep!). This new room faced the interior courtyard and was definitely smaller than the first, but it was quiet. Bath amenities were nice (Lather brand), and the room was nicely appointed. 
I had some trouble getting my "Joy of Life Club" perks--I had emailed someone from the hotel well in advance of our stay to let them know we were members, but there was no record of this on our reservation when I arrived. I mentioned it again at check-in, but no amenity was issued. Nothing showed up the following day (during room cleaning or check-in) and finally, on the last full day of our stay, I called down to the front desk to inquire. The person I spoke to had my amenity sent up, but I feel that there should have been more follow-through on my initial inquiry, rather than my having to constantly inquire about this. 
The gym was very small (the size of a guestroom, no windows) but it was clean and had nice equipment. The bar/restaurant's hours seemed oddly limited (I expected that this would be open all day during the weekends, at least, but this was not the case) and the noise that emanated from it (when we arrived at 10:30 P.M. on a Thursday) was alarming--I can't imagine that it's not audible from the second floor of guest rooms, and any rooms that overlook its patio area would probably hear this as well. 
The hotel's location across from the Ferry Building was a huge plus in our book, but might be inconvenient for those not interested in this area of the city. Additionally, the financial district (which the hotel abuts) is a ghost town on the weekends, so if you're looking for nightlife, this might not be the place to stay. 
Overall, I expected more.

title: “Poor service”
text: The staff at the reception desk was very unfriendly and unprofessional. We had booked a room with a kingsize bed, but they did not have any when we checked in. In fact they did not have a room at all because the guest in "our" room had extended their stay. That was normal business for them. It took 6 hours and 3 receptionist incompetence before we got a tiny dated room. The only thing this hotel has is a view to central park and a nice reception hall. The housekeeping forgot something every day-towels etc etc. The indoorclimate was very poor. We were there to celebrate my husbands birthday so the dissappointment was huge!! Would never stay here again.

title: “A bit pricey for the location”
text: If you are a Metro rider this is a hike to the nearest stop. The rooms are nice and breakfast was good. Rooms are a bit pricey so I was glad to only need to stay one night. The staff was very pleasant.

title: “Americas Worst Value Inn”
text: This americas best value inn in Lombard should be called AMERICAS WORST VALUE INN. The most unfriendly, rude, arrogant staff we've ever met named AMER. The room is so small and smells very bad like him. cockroaches everywhere and bugs on bed. Advertisments were all LIES...

title: “Helpless Staff”
text:
The main problem was a non-working door lock upon checkin which resulted in a comedy(?) of errors and kept me from getting into a room until over an hour after arrival. Because this was probably an isolated incident, I won't go into details and I've tried not to weigh it too heavily in my overall rating. But it did lower my satisfaction level and serves as a potential warning on staff competence.
There was also a very large carpet stain in the room I eventually was settled into. I kept my shoes on.
Positives:
- Excellent exterior sound proofing. The hotel has double wall construction - exactly what you would expect, but often don't find, in an airport hotel.
- Excellent temperature controls and performance.
- Great location. I turned in my rental car the evening before my flight (ask the shuttle driver to drop you off near the hotel to save going all the way to the airport and back), then walked to Terminal 2 (4 blocks) in the morning. The airport shuttle appeared to work fine, but I saw several flight crews walking like I did.
- Excellent value with my company rate.

title: “no free wi-fi in rooms, sewer smells, no free shuttle”
text: Not business traveler friendly; no free shuttle from hotel ($50 roundtrip for shuttle or cab with tip) and no free wi-fi in rooms (free w-fi only accesssible in lobby and around pool). Rooms have antiquated plug-in internet access for a fee. Sanitary sewer smell from sink in bathroom.

title: “I'm getting too old to stay in such places”
text: Photos on web (incl. TA) make it look a lot nicer than it is really. A big block warehouse of rooms has the feel of college dorm rooms that need work. Very friendly staff. Just okay for one night on a quick trip in and out of town, but I'm unlikely to return. I used miles and the old adage applies: you get what you pay for.

title: “Best Bed of all Philadelphia Hotels!”
text: I have to say, when I first opened the door I was a little disappointed with the size of the room. Typical RI with a kitchen, living room, etc.. however the best part was when I laid down in bed.
