It was the most comfortable bed and bedding that I have experienced in quite awhile, even better than a WESTIN!

title: “Super hotel”
text:
Very pleased:
Cleaning - Very good
Room - Good size, nice bathrooms
Roomservice - we tasted the best chocolate fondant with pistachio-icecream ever
Gym - Very good
Staff - Mild and gentle, with a lot of good citytips
We didn´t try out the breakfast because it´s hundreds of good diners in a radius of just 300 meters.
Summing up:
Our best hotelstay ever.

title: “Fab location, excellent price”
text: This hotel is a great place to stay for people not wanting to spend over the odds just to be in Times Square, it is only 10 blocks away, about a 10/15 minute walk. The rooms were spacious and we actually had a view of the Empire State Building from our room. Free coffee, OJ and muffins in the lobby at breakfast was a great start to the day.

title: “what do you expect”
text: I was worried when we read the reviews of this hotels. Yes it took a while to check in, the staff at the desk were very helpful. on entering our room we were surprised it was massive so much space,it could have done with a lick of paint. But apart from that nothing major to worry about., room service was fine we always had clean towels and the beds were made every day. Remember people this is New York a little bit of tipping goes along way !!!!!!! The location was fantastic could not be beaten right across the road from the garden and macy's. My advice if you want somewhere just as a base to sleep in NYC book the Penn, and us the money you save on shopping its easy people

title: “Comfortable & Clean”
text:
Stayed two nights (Sun & Mon) 
The hotel staff very friendly & courteous; the bed was comfortable and the room 
was well appointed; the marble-tiled bathroom was spacious (compared to the room!) 
and very nice.

title: “The Freedom Suite is SWEET!”
text:
We splurged to go to the Omni for two days on our way up to New England. We wanted to stay in close to all the attractions but also wanted a true suite..one that has a door to separate the sleeping areas so when the kids go to sleep at 7pm we are not forced to sleep as well. 
The Omni was the only one we could find with these qualifications. We splurged on the Freedom Trail suite (only available on their website) and were SO glad that we did. The kids (age 2 and 5) did not want to leave the room to go out to the aquarium or other sites ! The suite is more than as advertised. First, there is so much room compared to what others noted in the reviews! The living space is larger than our first apt in DC. The kids had a nice quality bunk bed, a table with kids' chairs, a whole wall to color with chalk, dress up period costumes (which seemd to be VERY clean much to my happiness and appeared washable), and books about the area. They also received a fun backpack (cardboard with real straps that they both wore for 48 hours straight minus bath and sleep time) with a canteen, flashlight, and a few other items at check in. They also got milk and cookies delivered to the room the first night. They were in heaven!
I was very pleased with the suite because of the adult bedroom which was luxurious and came with about 10 books to read about historical Boston. So nice to read while the kids were winding down. The noise of our kids for other hotel patrons was not a problem as the air conditioners had a nice white noise effect. 
The hotel of course is ideally located and has all the amenities you would expect at an Omni. I was just so pleased with their attention to the kids' needs and thought our dollars were very well spent!
As a note, the valet parking was costly, but easy when we arrived during rush hour. There is a garage around the corner that charges about $20 a day if you are organized and can get your luggage to the hotel by yourself (not possible when traveling 10 hours in the car with two small children and no DVD).
One more thing, the view was less than spetacular (the cooling vents!!) but really did not detract at all because of the amenities in the room!

title: “Better than I thought possible in Baltimore!”
text: This hotel met and exceeded all my expectations by far. It just opened earlier this year, so it might go downhill in the future, but it was impeccably clean, the rooms were very modern, the bed was comfortable, yet the hotel kept its character as a historic building. There were pictures on each floor of the restoration process - I highly recommend checking out each floor's picture, as it is amazing the change that took place (the picture on the 2nd floor was especially remarkable). The (free!) continental breakfast was very adequate, and the staff were more than responsive to our needs. The only downsides to the hotel was the parking, which was limited (but we had no problem finding a spot each time we left and came back); and the lack of free wi-fi (there was a paying option, but I found a signal from a nearby hotspot for free). Definitely would stay here again!

title: “Great hotel!!”
text: Great hotel , if you want to stay in the heart of times square.. the rooms are a very good size and were always neat and clean.. this hotel is in a very good location close to forever 21, and all the major shops on times square! loved this hotel would recommend to anyone A+++

title: “Good value, clone of Eastgate Towers across the street”
text:
Stayed a single night recently at the Murray Hill East Suites. I've previously stayed at the Eastgate Tower, across the street and a block east of here, and had a pretty good idea what to expect from this converted apartment building. In fact, the Murray Hill East Suites was nearly identical physically to the Eastgate Tower -- my room was a mirror image of the one I had at the Eastgate Tower a few months before. My general perception was that the furniture/drapes/carpets at the Murray Hill East seemed every so slightly newer/cleaner than at the Eastgate Tower, but the furniture itself was identical, and there wasn't much difference overall except for the bathroom; the bathroom in the Murray Hill East appeared to have been remodeled with completely new fixtures, tile, etc. sometime in the last year or so.
The room itself was large and comfortable, with a dining table and chairs, sofa, end tables, arm chair, coffee table, TV stand, and dresser, along with a double bed and one nightstand, arranged in an L-shaped room with the dining table at the top of the L near the door, the couch along one wall, the TV near the angle of the L, and the bed/nightstand in the base of the L. The small kitchen is in a separate room near the entrance door, with a half-sized fridge, full four-burner (albeit small) range, coffeemaker, sink, etc.
The bed itself was nothing much -- at the low end of acceptable -- and the pillows were barely there -- I had to scavenge the two extra pillows from the closet to make up a decent place to put my head, and the first time I looked in the closet for extra pillows I mistook the two pillows for folded sheets -- they were that thin and flimsy.
I ended up not using the high-speed internet access -- I couldn't find any indication of a hotel-provided wireless signal, and there was no wired connection of any kind in the room. Since I didn't start looking until late in my only night there, I decided I could live without it until morning and didn't pursue it. 
Neither here nor there, but this was the first hotel I've been to in the US in fifteen years or so where I was given an actual, honest-to-god metal key for the room, instead of a magnetic card key(another vestige of the building's days as an apartment building). If you're particularly concerned about security and the possibility of someone duplicating the key, I suppose that might give you pause.
Service, in the limited interactions I had with the staff, was courteous and professional, if not effusively friendly.
All in all, this seems like an excellent option in this part of Manhattan, particularly for the price. If I were to return to this customer's location for several days, I'd definitely consider it. Having room to spread out and a kitchen where I could store and prepare meals would be welcome.

title: “GreatlLocation in a fantastic City”
text:
The hotel was perfectly nice, big room.
Great location close to all the shops and the cable car station.

title: “NEEDS A TOTAL REVAMP AND 90% NEW STAFF”
text:
Stayed at the Palace the week before Christmas. This was the 6th year on the trot we have stayed there having a room overlooking St Patricks and use of the Exec Lounge, and I will never go back.
Firstly let me say that the Exec lounge... now called the Towers Club was fantastic and all the staff that work in there should be given a pay increase an probably put in charge of running the whole Hotel.
As for the rest of the place well where do I start. This is an expensive Hotel.. the rooms are verry tatty, bed linen stained, carpets worn out, bathrooms tatty and mouldy. The whole place needs a refurb.
The staff were rude, not interested in helping at all, unless you were flashing big tips about. I even had one guy chase me from the Gilt Bar asking where his tip was. He left us sitting there for 20 mins while he hovered round a table of rich Champaign drinking Americans, got our drinks... 2 margaretas which I might add are the worst I have ever tasted in the world and we could not drink them, then had the cheek to tell me that it wasnt his fault we didnt appreciate good drinks.
All in all there are much better Hotels now in NYC and I for one wont be going back to the New York Palace Hotel.

title: “Disgusting! We walked in the room, saw how nasty it was, and asked for our money back.”
text: Absolutely gross! Looks ok from outside, but don't be fooled! First ting I can say is, they need to clean! Ugh! Dusty, gross hair on the bed, and sticky soda on floor in the room! Out of curiosity, I pulled the sheet off the mattress and saw a nasty, moldy REALLY old mattress!! Looked about 20 years old. This place needs to invest $200 a room for new mattresses, $500 fo carpet, $1000 for new furnishings (they even still have an old tube tv!), and gut the bathrooms. Don't waste your time or money. Luckily we got a refund, but it came with a really, really bad attitude from the front desk girl. I couldn't wait to take a shower after just being in that room for 5 minutes!!

title: “Typical Hampton inn minus the friendly staff.”
text:
Your typical Hampton inn centrally located right across from Camden yards and a safe walk to the inner harbor.
$30 a day for valet parking and the hotel staff is not your typical friendly staff. My wife and I are hilton honors members and stay at Hilton exclusively. 
Breakfast ends at exactly 10am which is too early if you are a late sleeper or have little ones. There are not many breakfast restaurants in the area.
Overall its a typical Hampton inn in a great location for tourists.

title: “1 star was too much”
text:
Don't be fooled by the "location makes this hotel great". Well the location is alright, there are also 40 others hotels with equally great location and similar prices. The cosntruction is one thing, we knew that going in. The cleanliness of the hotel is inexcusable. Let's point for this;
1. Lamp missing power cable.
2. Bathroom door did not close.
3. Bathroom with odd splatter marks on the wall (I didn't even want to guess).
4. Nasty smelling towels and shower curtain (you know that smell when something soaks in water and doesn't get cleaned properly).
5. Scuff marks everywhere.
5. The darkest dingiest hallways I have seen.
6. The creepiest wall paper in the hallway (when we walk out our room and look down the end of the hallway there is a small child playing).
I would add more, but I am actually sitting in the Milford right now and checkout is in approximately 15 minutes. Serisouly, there are hundreds of hotels in this area all in the same ball park. The Sheraton down the streen is nice. I would wander the streets of new york without shoes before spending another night at the milford.

title: “Great rooms, service, and stay.”
text: My husband and I came to Phoenix on a business trip and decided to stay at the Biltmore in the Ocatilla wing. All of the concierge in the Ocatilla lounge were very friendly and helpful, among all of them Leo was a great help during our stay. The rooms were very nice, spacious and clean. Overall, our stay was nice and relaxing, even for being a business trip.

title: “No service”
text: Terrible from parking to checkout. Nothing worked and no one answered. Upon check in the valet was new and told me I would get my ticket at the front desk. The front desk, of course told me I had to go back outside to retrieve my car ticket. Than, I called room service at 10:25pm. Multiple times with no answer. I left a voice mail of my order but no one ever responded and I did not get my order. The two vending machines on my floor were broken, so I had to go down to the lobby for soda and some snacks. Then in the morning I called the valet to bring my car around and no one answered. When I went down stairs at 6:30am, the valet was not at their post and I had to wait a few minutes before they emerged from inside. Terrible service from start to finish.

title: “Great Deal and Perfect Location”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Fitzpatrick Grand Central this past weekend. We were greeted very nicely upon arrival (although the doorman was inside talking and not paying close attention to people going in and out and it's tough opening the doors when you have luggage with you). We had requested a higher floor when we made our reservation, but for the room we requested which was a Queen sized for $149 (great price!!!) they only had lower floors. After a little bit of a search they did find a larger queen room on the 6th floor. I can't imagine what the size of the original room would have been, but this one was a nice sized room and the bathroom was very large with a walk in shower (very euoropean). Each room has robes, but as usual only one, so we had to request another and there are no ice machines so we had to call for ice as well. The bed was very comfortable, but we did experience a heating problem. It was extremey cold in NYC this past weekend and when we awoke the next morning it was very cold in our room. We did try to figure out how to raise the heat but could not find anything resembling a thermostat. We called the front desk and were told to look for the brown panel (no brown panel) so they sent up an engineer, who after some difficulty was able to pry open a silver panel on the heater itself with a screw drive and there was the thermostat - it was showing that it was 50 degrees in our room.
Altough we had a few minor problems, I have to say that the staff was very responsive to our requests. We live in Connecticut and like to stay in NYC every now and then and travel by train into Grand Central Station. The hotel is literaly a half a block away. Also, it is about 1 block away from our favorite diner - the Comfort Diner on East 45th Street. I highly recommend this place for breakfast, good portions, good service and good atmosphere.
Very nice staff from front desk, engineering and housekeeping (get the free turn down service at night and they leave some chocolates and bottled water - free)
We will definitely stay here again!!

title: “Wonderful experience”
text: For a first time trip to New York City and unsure what to expect, we were pleasantly surprised by the employees of this hotel. The staff was extremely helpful from the check in through our check out. They were very eager to assist us at every turn from things forgotten to reataurants and shows. The rooms were large enough to relax in and the beds were so comfortable we wanted to take one home.

title: “Nice but too spendy!”
text: This was a nice hotel, but it was too spendy for what you received. First complaint, wireless was not free. Seriously? Room was pretty small. Other than that, the room was nice and location with being right on Michigan Avenue was very convenient!

title: “Excellent service”
text: We were at this hotel for four nights for a conference. It is centrally located in the Downtown district and we walked everywhere. The hotel is an older building that was very clean and well kept. The breakfast was the usual hotel breakfast. IMPORTANT: The key that made this the best place to stay was HAMPTON'S EMPLOYEES. ALL of the employees were helpful, friendly and genuinely caring. A few that stood out: LaShawn at the front desk had everything under control at all times, Regina made our early mornings easier with her joyous presence (she brightened the room even on the dreariest days) and Tribeca was ever so pleasant! By the time we left this place felt like home! Stay here!

title: “Good, clean room!”
text:
The hotel is average. Don't expect too much, because it is a fairly cheap hotel for Manhattan!
The room was small but clean. We had a little trouble with the shower: It was either screaming hot or ice cold. With a little bit of patience, though, we were able to shower without burning or freezing. The heater was also a little hot, especially at night.
I did not see bed bugs. Even if I would have seen them, the staff at the hotel would have probably moved us to another room. The staff is very nice. They make you feel welcome and help with luggage.
The hotel is located close to a subway station and also very close to Central Park ( a five minute walk). Downstairs is a Star bucks.
Don't get scared by the other reviews! I did and it was totally unnecessary. I would stay there again!

title: “Great location”
text: This place offers you a great location and spacious rooms but the rooms are quite average with old furniture and furnishing. I had to stay here after having stayed at a B&B because of my last-minute extension of stay. I was very dissappointed by the furnishing of the room. It oozed a foul odour and it took me some time to get used to it. But this doesn't bother you, this is a great place to stay at, given its location and room sizes.

title: “Slightly disappointed”
text: Have been to NYC several times but this visit we were up for the US Open and wanted to stay near Grand Central. The first and biggest disappointment was the concierge service. She was not very helpful in offering advice/suggestions for visitors. I had to ASK her AND front desk staff for maps. Upon entering for first time, bellhop just looked at me struggling with baggage. RARE restaurant closed during first 2 days of our stay but opened on a Friday and that staff at the bar VERY pleasant. Will search elsewhere for next week's visit to NYC.

title: “Always a Great stay at Holiday Inn Express”
text: Used my points this time, Stayed on the fourth floor(outdoor pool/Dining area for Breakfast is on the same floor), within walking distance to the Hollywood/Highland Center where the Kodak Theater is located, and of course the walk of fame, HUGE ROOMS( i have pictures) for public transport, MTA Red line subway is nearby as well as a few buses(156 i believe) has fridge and Microwave as well, Hot Breakfast, bacon & eggs or sausage sometimes, always a winner compared to other hotels' Continental breakfast, only thing was the pool wasnt heated and wasnt indoor, for a holiday inn express i didnt expect that.

title: “always good standard at sofitel”
text:
I recently stayed at the Sofitel los angeles, it has a very convenient location if you are going for business or for shopping (a large mall is just in front of the hotel); not that many dining options within a walking distance but who is walking in LA?
staying in the sofitel is always a guarantee to have a nice room and a friendly staff, really good value for the hotel. From the check in process to the room service delivery, the staff was very helpful and fast to reply to any demand (they were telling me it was taking 30 minutes for the room service and always delivered before that with a big smile, very good service). the bar with live band was cool too, good ambiance.
For once i have used a fitness center of a hotel and really liked it. Spacious, good equipment, it was very nice to end up the day by some cardio and weight. 
Little inconsistency on the service (one night they forgot the turndown while i was away of my room), but this was not a problem.

title: “Just got back from the Wellington”
text:
We went to the Wellington for 5 nights as part of our honeymoon before going to St Lucia.
We arrived at the hotel from the UK early evening (after only having to spend 1 hour at JFK coming through immigration which suprised us!), to a not very welcoming receptionist who sent us to the 15th floor to our room.
Upon entering the room we were greeted by a small, pokey, musty, brown room with no closet space and a bathroom which was in need of refurbishment - not what I expected from the brochure we had or the pictures which are posted on their internet site. All in all I wasn't very impressed by the hotel room. We asked to be moved to a different room which would mean that my husband wouldn't have to climb over me to get to the otherside of the bed, and they told us that there were no other availiable rooms. And another thing was that the staff all seemed to be miserable and no one smiled or told us to "have a nice day" - I think it was the fault of the dreary wallpaper myself!
However, what I would say about the hotel is that it has a fab location - very close to central park, rockafeller centre, times square (and tiffanys), 
But if you are going on your honeymoon.... I wouldn't reccomend it!!

title: “Outstanding Service”
text:
I just spent a week in NYC for work. Not only was the hotel stylish, well located and comfortable, I had an amazing experience with the very friendly and professional staff. Without the help from the concierges, Natalia and Clay and the additional help of Jennifer Snowden, Heather Johnston, Melissa at the front desk and Angel Pan, as well as the lovely housekeeping on the 16th, my week would not have been a success.
My colleagues and I will continue to use the Royalton as our base when we do business in NYC.
Laura

title: “A nice place for a reasonable price”
text:
I have spent 5 nights here while attending a conference.
The room was clean and comfortable.
The staff was nice and helpful, a nice extra is the complimentary hot drinks and fruit all day.

title: “But the noise....”
text: I loved this place! They greeted us so kindly on check in, and gave us helpful visitor information. The room was very clean, and the bed was comfortable. The room didn't have a safe unfortunately, so we had to carry around our passports and cash. They had very yummy blueberry muffins for breakfast. I didn't sleep very well because of the paper thin walls, I heard every footstep, and because the airport is so close there were planes flying over all the time. It's excellent value, next time I'll bring earplugs.

title: “good deal and excellent location”
text: We stayed for 4 nights at this place and we would return for sure. The location is perfect, since you are 1 1/2 block from Union Square and 3 blocks from Shopping mall and Market street which is one of the most useful streets if you need shopping malls and quick transportation to almost anywhere. The hotel crew was very kind and helpfull, specially Hansel, who reccomended good places to eat. It is a fact that the hotel is old and certainly has a particular smell specially on walksides and frontdesk, but that is not an inconvenience at all, just to mention that the hotel would be much better if it makes a few renovations. The room was comfortable and clean as well as the bathroom. The rates are very convenient considering the location and facilities.

title: “WOW!”
text: This place is great. We are very choosy about our accomodations and we were more than pleased with Affinia Shelburne. The place is spotlessly clean and very spacious. Nice kitchen area with microwave, fridge with icemaker, coffee maker. Nice granite counter tops in bathroom and kitchen. Plenty of room for hanging clothes in armoir. Iron and ironing board in room if needed. Nice toiletries replenished daily. Great location in a very nice neighborhood. Bars, stores, retaurants in walking area. Just a great place to stay. The employees couldn't have been nicer and more helpful for directions, etc. Please do yourself and you family a favor and try this place. It was a really great experience for us. Bed are fabulous.

title: “Overall nice place to stay”
text: We booked this property because of a business meeting at the beginning of the week which was literally across the street. Arrived into PHX airport after midnight and for the first time in 30 years of travelling, our luggage didn't arrive with us. It was after 2am when we checked in and the desk clerk was friendly, however never having been here before none of what the resort had to offered was explained. We had booked a king suite as we were going to be here for a week and wanted that extra space. The room was in decent shape and very clean, however, being in the biz myself I noticed that there is a lot of preventative maintenance that should be done, ie scuffed furniture, walls, running tub etc. There are 2 pools that we have found, one right outside our room and the other (the water park) a short walk away. Both nice areas, but would suggest to the management to have an adult hour from 10-11pm. There were loads of kids screaming and yelling right up to 11pm close. The water park was ok. We were there yesterday (July 5/12) and found the service to be dreadful. It was hot and had copious amounts of "Bar Crew" pass by, without one stopping to ask if we wanted anything. It was obvious that they were completely understaffed. HOWEVER, 2 days earlier I over heard the service staff complaining how little in tips they were making. Hmmmm call me crazy, but if you actually attended to guests and solicited drink/food orders instead of walking around in pairs gossiping you might actually make some ca$h. Other than Carol, the Concierge and the bell captain and one of the bellman, I found the staff somewhat lacking in enthusiasm. From the front desk, to the water park bar and even the Spa, attitudes were lack lustre. We ate at "The Hole in the Wall" for breakfast. The brisket platter was amazing but breakfast for 2 including tip at almost $45.00 is a little much and again the service was mediocre. We found that at all of the F&B outlets the menu's to be very limited. The food is good, but a little more choice would be nice. INTERNET: Hilton has a great wireless system in their properties, but beware - this property charges $14.95 per day PER DEVICE. In today's world of having a laptop, phones, tablets etc, if you were to get everything connected it would cost a fortune. Overall, this is a great place to stay, especially for self-sufficient people like ourselves. We would definitely come back, as my partner loves to 105+ temps...

title: “great time staying at the Conrad Hilton in Chicago with our dogs”
text: This hotel is really dog freindly ! Upon our arrival they came up with a dog bed, leashes, and stainless steel dog dishes. Staff was really freindly and helpful.

title: “Gorgeous Hotel, Easy Access to Downtown in a Quaint, Quiet Area of DC”
text: We stayed at this hotel over the weekend to tour DC and go to a Washington Capitals hockey game. First the hotel -- it is beautiful, with peaceful gardens and lots of places to sit outside and relax. The lobbby is oppulent. The staff is polite and very helpful. The hotel bar was accommodating when we wanted to watch a Patriots game on one of their TV's. We had a room with 2 queen size beds. The rooms are spacious with plenty of room for a family of four not to feel cramped. Access to the city is so simple. You are a block from the subway, which takes you right downtown. No need for expensive cabs. The subway is clean, trains are plentiful and the price is right. The restaurant at the hotel looked very beautiful and expensive, but we were traveling with kids, so we opted to take a quick walk up 2 blocks to a row of small, bistro type restaurants with outdoor and indoor seating. Very charming, cheaper than eating at the hotel and lots of ethnic choices from indian to mexican to italian to American food. There's even a McDonalds if you are on a tight budget. The kids can have ice cream at Baskin Robbins and visit the nearby zoo, which is within walking distance. I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone who wants to visit the bustling city but would like to return at night to a quieter neighborhood and relax after a long day of sightseeing.

title: “A wonderful hotel, but avoid the parking”
text:
We stayed for one night for a splurge trip to Manhattan. We booked a mini-suite so that we could have room for ourselves and our three children. The room was beautifully appointed, with great little touches throughout, and it was very spacious, especially for a hotel in NYC. We had Hilton Honors, so we got upgraded to the Tower, and had a very nice continental breakfast included in our stay. 
The only negative to keep in mind is that this is a huge hotel, which means that check-in and check out can be hectic, and the parking is a nightmare - expect to wait for quite a while for your car to be retrieved. 
Overall, though, this was a really nice place to spend a night during the holidays, and we would stay there again.

title: “Terrific Value, Super Friendly Staff, Will be returning!!”
text: What a surprise to find this jewel of a hotel!! From the moment you drive up, the valets are super friendly and helpful, the front desk staff was friendly and accomodating. The room was clean and tastefully decorated, it felt chic! Not at all what I was expecting for the price. The evening reception wasquite nice, the room was large, the seating was comfortable and relaxing, it was a very pleasant atmosphere to unwind in. Both my husband and I were very impressed with the value and all the amenities that were included!! Keep up the great job, we look forward to our next stay at The Magnolia!

title: “Perfect for what we needed.”
text: Maybe the rooms, mainly the bathroom, could do with some renovation, but it was fine. The room, towels and sheets were clean, the towels changed every day, we got a massive room, it even had an iron and iron board and a big walk in wardrobe. It was very quite and never had to wait long for the elevator and also we never had to queue for check in or luggage. There was a tv in the room but we never turned it on cause we were a;ways out. Also the location is fantastic, you can walk everywhere. Macy's, Penn Station, Times Square, Empire... all within walking distance. For the price we paid we definitely cannot complain. And for our purpose it was fantastic. We were after a clean room, not expensive, central location and that is what we got. Would definitely stay again.

title: “Best value in San Fran!”
text: We will absolutely be staying here again! Fantastic value for the price. Great service, great location and large, spacious suites. I highly recommend!!!

title: “Reviews are not wrong ! Nice hotel”
text:
Perhaps nothing new when reading through the other reviews. Excellent location near to the White House and metro station (McPherson Sq- one block away - cross the road from the front entrance, left at the junction and then left again and you are there). The hotel is well kept with nice decor andyour room is turned down in the evening which is a nice touch. The room itself was spacious, clean and tastefully decorated, although I noted a few marks on some of the seat cushions and what looked like a cigarette burn on the curtain. A minor point, but just little things that spoilt an otherwise spotless room.
I did not eat in the hotel but the bar prices were on a par with local restaurants. The bar also had an outside seating area, with soft sofas and was popular. The staff, especially the concierge, were extremely helpful in advising upon various restaurants to visit and also had an online reservation system, booking in advance for us. Ovrerall, the hotel was very pleasant and would stay again. 
As to value for money, that perhaps is another thing of course. Looking at the rates for other similar hotels in Washington DC, the Sofitel appears to be in line with them, but at $350 per night + taxes, is not really giving it away. Breakfast was a further $22 per day. Having not travelled to the US for a while, I had forgotten about the dreaded local taxes being extra, which was a further $50 per day. Mind, if you stayed in London at a similar hotel quality, I dare say the rates would also be similar at about $400 (£250) per night.. 
As mentioned by others, in room internet is extra at $10 per day. There is a free access PC in a small room adjacent to the main reception, but it is certainly not private, with the screen facing directly onto reception.

title: “A lovely hotel”
text: We loved Humphreys. I'll admit that the buildings and the door looked a bit more run down than we expected (our doors hinges were old and loose) etc but overall it's a great hotel in a lovely setting. Shelter Island is about a 15 minute drive from San Diego and parking is pretty expensive in the main areas (head for the Horton plaza and validate) but we were happier to stay there than in the Gaslamp district. It's a lovely complex with a nice pool area. We got free breakfast and this made our stay at the hotel as the staff here were at their best and the setting is great with a lovely view of the marina. Our room also had this view and it was great to wake up to this. We loved the room, it was spacious and clean so had no complaints. Some of the staff were absolutely lovely but some of the young breakfast reception staff and bar staff were a bit abrupt. All things considered If I came to San Diego again, I'd stay here. If there is a show on I imagine it would be a great venue too.

title: “Wow”
text: Stayed back in May for a week. It was a really special occasion and the staff went out of their way to make the trip memorable. Firstly the rooms are great and the views incredible. It's definitely worth getting a corner. Emailed Patrick prior for some recommendations on things to do in NY and to arrange a couple of things and his response was fantastic. Really special place to stay, will be coming back.

title: “Good location”
text: Location was perfect at 35th and 5th Ave. The surrounding area is safe and there is a Starbucks in the lobby. Very close to Herald Sq shopping and to subway and Penn Station. Short walk to Grand Central. Rooms are very small, just room for the bed basically. Bed was very comfortable with updated down bedding and pillows. Bathroom was just a shower, but good size, and countertops were marble and everything was new. Flat screen TV was new and modern. AC worked great. There is just 1 elevator and very small, narrow corriders in the halls. Not really typical of a hotel, no lobby to speak of, and no frills whatsoever, but clean, comfortable, convenient. Friendly and helpful desk staff.

title: “Great base to see New York City & Theatre!!”
text: The hotel staff was very courteous; the room was clean and good sized (very spacious for NYC); the location was awesome -- near subways and Broadway (the street AND theatres). A basic (hot) breakfast was included. I'd stay there again in a heartbeat!!

title: “Great rooms. Very comfortable beds, large and roomy and very clean. Hilton executive lounge has great view and good food.”
text:
Modern and clean, excellent entry with comfortable couches and many places for privacy for cell calls, good bar. Rooms are excellent, large and clean, could sleep all day in those beds.
Construction outside at 6 am on north side woke me up and they immediately found me a room on south side. Very nice stay.

title: “Disliked the Service”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for the flower show in Philly since it offered an excellent price which included the tickets. The hotel was fine, rooms were clean, etc. but the service was absolutely horrible. They did not have the tickets for the flower show as promised and it was a great ordeal just to get this issue resolved. The staff were beyond clueless in helping resolve the problem.
They really should be trained in how to be courteous to their guests.

title: “Qualify, clean, affordable”
text: This hotel has a great location-close to major freeway. Restaurants are around. Hotel is very neat and clean. Staffs are polite, nice, and very helful. Price is affordable-value... I will comeback!!

title: “Great Location;--But Very Lame Accommodations!”
text:
Best part of the Holiday Inn on West 57th? Truly a fantastic location!! Close to shopping, theatres, Central Park, great restaurants!
Hotel also has a great concierge! Friendly & extremely knowledgeable concierge staff!
Free wireless was another treat! 
The not so good: Please note: If you book this hotel online (which I did), please read the fine print. Turns out, if you get this great cheap ($250 a night deal, which is really not that cheap) online deal, it's completely nonrefundable!! 
The whole hotel stunk, literally stunk! There was a "tinge" throughout the hotel & in my room. Air conditioner was broken....Hey, it was nearly 80 degrees for 2 days with no air conditioning! That truly sucked!
Will I stay there again? Maybe if this place were a hundred bucks a night, I might consider it....just 'cause of the great location. But for $250 per night--I expected a more pleasant smelling hotel and a few more amenities....Ta Ta to the Holiday Inn for me!

title: “Great place in the Gaslamp, closest to Petco Park”
text:
This is a beautiful modern hotel with staff so cool it's almost painful, though they couldn't have been more gracious or welcoming. Check in was painless and smooth. They ask you what kind of music you want greeting you in your room so that you feel at home.
I had a room with a queen bed, a view of downtown, overlooking the pool deck and exterior bar. The modern room was very comfortable, immaculately clean, and quiet. I had a room right next to the elevator, and it was still very quiet. I heard no plumbing or mechanical noise, and the hallway stayed quiet as well, but for one loud group that went through in the early evening, but apparently didn't return to the floor or were significantly quieter when they did return. There was a long, low desk, flat screen tv, leather chair for the desk, plenty of power plugs for devices, and drawers for storage. The closet had an automatic light and was large enough for my luggage, so I was able to stow everything away and keep the room spacious and uncluttered. The bed itself was large and very comfortable, and I got a great night's sleep.
There's a little wear and tear on the custom furniture and room corners, but minimal and not unexpected considering the hotel's location and busyness. 
The bathroom is beautiful, very clean, with room to stow toiletries and extra towels as well. The glass walled shower had both a wall fixture and a ceiling fixture, so you can choose how you'd prefer to shower. My kids would have enjoyed trying both fixtures. 
This hotel could not be closer to Petco Park and is on the outskirts of the busy Gaslamp quarter. It's close to the Convention Center,and also close to the airport, so taxi fees are reasonable. If you are staying for a couple of days and not traveling far or off the beaten path, you won't need a car, as public transportation is extremely convenient. There's a bar downstairs that gets a lot of traffic, and apparently has an enforced dress code. There's plenty of nightlife in the Gaslamp itself, if you're so inclined.
I found this to be a really nice place to stay, and would certainly stay here again.

title: “Very very small room”
text: We noticed that it was right next to the greyhound station and near the court house, but it was close to the gas lamp district and the horton plaza. The rooms were really small and we noticed the restrooms to be even smaller. Although the rooms were small the Currant restaurant is delicious. The toilet seat definitely needed to be changed. I have never seen a seat cover so worn out that the paints were worn out enough that the brown wood was showing. The amenity charge was not listed anywhere when I booked the room like what other reviewers mentioned.

title: “Nothing but great location”
text:
old and not charming building,tiny rooms which are not pleasant to the eye,the over all feeling is
that except for a great location there is nothing good to write home about.

title: “Fantastic Hotel Experience and Exceptional Service”
text:
I have never been particularly inclined to post a review after a trip that I have taken but my girlfriend and I had such a great time at our stay at the Palace that I felt I had to.
We stayed for a long weekend in May and loved everything about the hotel. The room was exceptional, the service was first class and the atmosphere was great.
It was a special occasion and I had requested some extras (food and champagne) to be ready for arrival. The kitchen staff was extremely helpful, as was the concierge, in sorting this out prior to our arrival. We were greeted graciously and given a room upgrade and everything was exactly as planned. The concierge was also very helpful in helping us procure tickets to the a show as well as provide us with several other recommendations.
Thank you very much for an excellent trip. I will definitely be back.
Nick

title: “Pleasantly surprised”
text:
I had read reviews here and was not expecting much, but was pleasantly surprised. I arrived prior to 3pm but left my bags free of charge. The doormen were always pleasant and courteous, and brought my bags quickly when I returned. The woman at the front desk was very pleasant when I checked in and was quick to send someone up when I had trouble with my room key.
The room was pretty large (for NYC), spotlessly clean, and had a nice bathroom and amenities. The minibar wouldn't open but that wasn't an issue. The view was not great but was better than others I've experienced in NYC, and even though my room was directly behind the elevators, I didn't hear a peep all night. Checkout was a breeze and I had no problems leaving my bags again after checking out. This time it was $1/bag, but I left them for about 6 hours so it was a good value.
Overall, I would definitely recommend this place. This is FAR nicer than any of the other 5 places I've stayed while visiting NYC. It's a great location, the restaurant next door is great for breakfast, it was clean, and the staff was friendly. Give it a try!

title: “Quaint boutique hotel”
text: We have stayed in the Backbay area of Boston previously, and while we liked that hotel, we would definitely choose to stay at the Newbury Guest House for future visits. It's not a huge, grand hotel like some of the others in the area, but if you are looking for comfort and convenience, this is a wonderful option! The rooms are small, but very functional and comfortable, and more importantly, clean and well-kept. The location is fantastic, only a couple blocks from the Copley Green Line and a 3 block walk to the Backbay Orange Line stop. I have to admit, that we were slightly worried about the foot traffic and noise from Newbury street, but that worry never surfaced. It is very quite at night, and we rested comfortably. The complimentary breakfast is also a nice touch as well as the free Wi-Fi. A great job of renovating the hotel!!

title: “Trendy design but needs more staff training”
text: I was at SLS a few weeks ago and the design by Philip Stark is really very creative and the rooms interesting and cozy. The breakfast table is beautifully settled but should have healthier options as breads considering the need for it in a trendy hotel. They had only croissant, should have at least a baguette or french bread, or even whole what bread in a city like LA....The service at the breakfast was confusing but a few servers were better and helped the image of the hotel. Same thing at the reception where Lisa the front desk was very helpful and helped with all the confusions regarding breakfast ( that was included in our rate). In general, a good hotel but needs more training for the whole staff .... At the end the very few ones that were very good helped to build a good image of the hotel but they should not depend on that.... they have everything to become a really nice hotel...

title: “Bed Bugs, Bed Bugs, Bed Bugs!!!!”
text: Bedbugs found in our room. Management very uncooperative. General Manager refused to appear after 4 requests. Stated they would clean all out clothes and mail them to us with shoes and suitcases being cleaned. Did not clean everything. Had to throw away suitcases and clothes. Very unsatisfied with hotel management response/resolution. Would strongly recommend not staying here!!!

title: “Older hotel, with excellent location”
text: We stayed at this hotel for a weekend trip. The best thing about this hotel is the location. It is across the street from the Buckingham Fountain. We have no complaints about the staff, fast and easy check-in and check-out. We slept well on the beds. The lobby of the hotel is really pretty, but the rooms are needing updated. It is very old and dated. I did love the high ceilings in the room. Door to bathroom in our room needed replaced as it was very hard to open and close. I would recommend this hotel to a friend due to the excellent location and price.

title: “Flight delay = nice hotel stay”
text:
Our plane was overcrowded and they needed volunteers to take another flight, so we volunteered in exchange for a flight the next day, food passes, a free hotel stay and $$ towards our next ticket.
The airline booked us at this hotel. It was very clean and comfortable and spacious (both the hotel and our room). The lady who initially checked us in definitely left something to be desired (she was rude) but everyone else was really friendly. The food at their restaurant in the main lobby was decent enough, a bit pricey for it's quality but it was free with our passes so I didn't mind. Our alcoholic drinks weren't covered by the passes but they were good drink prices and the bartender was nice and funny. The pool area looked nice and if we weren't so tired we would have gone swimming. Their breakfast in the morning had a good variety and was still warm. The shuttle was free to and from the airport and both our drivers were very friendly. I'm not sure what their prices are but if they are reasonable I would stay here again.

title: “Mixed!”
text:
I can understand why so many reviews are positive -- this hotel is in a good location, the staff are super-friendly and very on the ball, and the bed is wonderfully comfortable. But I found a number of things "off." 
* We were supposedly in a non-smoking room, but the room stunk, and the staff member who brought up an ozone machine forgot to turn it on, so it accomplished nothing while we were out the day we first requested it.
* The puce blinds had water stains on them and vehemently clashed with the red and beige arm chair. In a budget hotel, this wouldn't bother me, but in a hotel that styles itself as luxurious, the stains were unacceptable and the style choices startlingly bad.
* The bathtub drain was broken.
* The noise from the hallway is unbelievable. Don't think about sleeping in. The doors are weighted so heavily that you'll be woken up by one door after another slamming as other guests leave their rooms. You will also have to listen to the housekeeping staff knocking on other doors and yelling out at other guests before they get to your room.
* The desk is huge, so you feel as if you are sleeping in an office. If you're in New York on business, you might very well appreciate the size of the desk. But if you're there for romance, you'll feel stuck in the work-a-day world!
In conclusion, while this is a decent hotel, it is over-priced. You could certainly do worse, but you could also certainly do better. If you do book this hotel, make sure you get a rate that is at least half of the rack rate (as we did) or else you're likely to feel that you have misspent your money.

title: “Wonderful Stay”
text: I stayed here for four days with my daughters and husband. We loved the hotel. The rooms were clean, beds were comfortable, staff was wonderful, a breakfast to die for, wonderful evening snack time and free adult beverages too. The hotel offers free internet service in your room and free wireless in the lobby area. The indoor pool and hot tub were wonderful, we were in it everyday. The staff was very friendly and helpful. It is in an excellent location, easy to get to Sea World, Downtown and Fiesta Tx. The hotel offers maps and directions to all major attractions. I could not hear traffic or hallway noise inside our rooms (which is rare in hotels these days). I would highly recommend this hotel and we will stay there again the next time we go to San Antonio.

title: “Great location, nice staff, but small rooms”
text:
You simply can't be more central to Times Square, but this is reflected in the cost. I paid $399 and $ 349 for a Tuesday/Weds night. The hotel is quite comtemporary and clean, but the room I stayed in was tiny - barely any room either side of the standard double bed and a closet so small that I struggled to hang my clothes. The air conditioning is also quite loud.
Internet access was $ 13.95 for one day and the registration page says that this is for each device. On the second night I got complimentary internet access. The staff are friendly and customer centric. Nerma at the front desk looked after me and offered a complementary cocktail after my long flight. Decent hotel and superb location, but a bit on the expensive side given the size of the rooms.

title: “DO NOT STAY HERE FOR YOUR OWN SAFETY!!! STAIRS ARE LOCKED!!”
text: Instead of telling you how depressingly mediocre this hotel was in every way other than the pretty lobby and convenient location, I am going to issue a safety warning of sorts: This hotel locks the staircases. On the last day of the convention I was attending, someone decides to pull the fire alarm. Chaos ensues as everyone rushes to the emergency stairwells only to find that they are locked. You can have no idea how frightening this is until you experience it, so if you're into that then by all means, stay here. But unless you like the idea of being trapped in a burning building, I recommend staying elsewhere.

title: “A perfect experience”
text: I chose the hotel based on location and TripAdvisor reviews. The room had a pleasant decor and was perfectly clean. The shower was exceptional. Reception staff was pleasant and efficient. What's not to like? It doesn't have an elevator to the second floor but that didn't matter to me. They gave me a choice of floors when I checked in.

title: “Nice Room -Close to airport”
text: Perfect for one night prior to departure from LAX. Pleasant staff. Very nice, comfy room. Large bathroom. Free wireless. Close to Airport, and many gas stations (for filling rental car prior to return). Several fast-food options close by. We were traveling with a preschooler and an infant. We liked that they had a proper crib for the infant, and not a pack n' play. Only minor complaint is the teeny-tiny elevator in the parking garage. Total with tax and parking was $103 - seemed a fair price.

title: “Excellent hotel in an excellent location.”
text:
We booked the Softel because of all the positive reviews and for it's great location. We were not disappointed at all. The foyer and reception area is very well laid out and decorated beautifully. The staff were very polite and courteous, check-in-check out was a breeze and we also got upgraded to a superior room. The room was spacious enough and the bed was so comfortable. The bathroom was very clean with a great walk-in shower and bathtub.
The Gaby bar was also very nice and a great place to have a relaxing drink to finish the day off. We would definitely consider staying here again. The hotel is advertised as a luxury hotel and in many ways it was, but one small observation was that the iron and ironing board were quite cheap and if you leaned too hard the pattern from the board pressed through onto your clothes. Slightly annoying. However I suppose I'm being a bit nitpicky. Overall we had a lovely relaxing stay and had a ball visiting all that Manhattan has to offer.

title: “Do not rent here!!! Worst experience ever!!!!”
text:
Expect harassment from management for no reason at all. The foreign couple who runs the inn is rude and has terrible communication. The manager calls me after I check-in and demands payment for additional people staying over even though it was only my wife and I there. For whatever crazy reason, he believes I will throw some massive sleepover party and he wants money for it. After telling him that we’re not having anyone over, he calls again and threatens that he will have security take me to the police station. Later, as expected, the security guy comes a knockin and of course, he finds no other people around. 
When the couple felt the need to abruptly end a conversation, the husband would start saying “Money, money, money, money” accompanied by the gimme money hand gesture. When I tried to talk over that annoyance, his wife would jump in chanting the same. Then they would run away from the front desk. It was surreal. I thought I was in an episode of Seinfeld. 
The bathroom is tiny. There is literally about 6-8 inches of space between the front of the toilet and the wall/door. So you cannot sit down normally to use it. The manager’s wife also does the cleaning as they are too cheap to hire staff which explains why it’s not clean there. 
Bottom line, DO NOT RENT here. I wouldn’t stay for free. It was a horrible experience but I hope I can save others from this mess.

title: “Quaint Hotel”
text: We just got back from the Normandy after spending 5 nights there with 2 small kids. Okay, the room is small and there are no dressers but personally, we didn't spend any time in our room except to sleep and shower so getting my clothes out of the suitcase each day and storing them in the closet was no big deal. By the way, love the shower. We really liked the location and it’s sort of a hike, I guess for people who don't walk much but my 4 and 6 year-old didn't seem to mind. It probably took us 10-15 minutes to get to the subway. One great thing is that most places are open late in this neighborhood, unlike downtown, with lots of good places to eat or shop and it's really a lovely, safe area. We like staying away from all of the noise and this was perfect for that. The food in the morning is not super kid friendly. The cereals are pretty healthy but they do have donuts, pastries, fresh fruit, bagels, etc. We loved the cappuccino maker in the room and there is also a little fridge. The rooms are nicely decorated and clean. The parking is under the hotel and is a tight squeeze, if you have an Expedition but we made it and there is a pool and gym available about a block away at the Courtyard Marriott which we did use. We would for sure go back.

title: “Great Time at the Wellington”
text:
We stayed at the Wellington Hotel on the first weekend in February. Since I was afraid the weather might be cold and my friend has a bad knee the main reason I chose the Wellington, besides the bargain price, was the convenience; there is a subway stop right next to the building and other bus and subway lines are nearby. 
We arrived in New York at 6:30 a.m. and went straight to the hotel to leave our bags. Even though it was hours before check in time they let us have the room right away. Being able to freshen up, relax a little and change our clothes after an all night train ride was a big bonus. Our room was very pleasant. It wasn't very big but because it was a corner room and had windows on two walls and a nice big mirror on an opposite wall it felt bigger than it was. From one window I had a nice view over the top of Carneigie Hall to Central Park.
Everything about the hotel was great. The room was tastefully decorated and clean. The staff was friendly and helpful. The location couldn't have been more convenient, just above all the lights and action of Time Square, not in all the crowding and congestion. We walked to the theatre one evening and to Caroline's Comedy Club the next. I would definately stay there again

title: “Always fun in the D”
text: We stayed here for my bachelorette party and they accommodated us well, two rooms a few doors apart. I had been here before, the rooms are clean, updated, and in the middle of all the action in greektown so why not? I feel like we paid a lot for these rooms. I was not necessarily disappointed, i just know you can get better deals. Lively and fun location recommended for socializing.

title: “Rex is the place to stay!”
text: My girlfriend and i just got back from our stay at the Rex. Live jazz, free wine, great amenities--this is the best place to stay!

title: “The Austin Oltorf La Quinta Inn”
text: The service at the Oltorf La Quinta was good. All staff was helpful and efficient. The Inn itself was a bit dated and although a refrigerator and microwave was expected in the room, it wasn't there. Seemed like an Inn frequented by out of town labor forces

title: “Terrible, Do not stay here”
text: This hotel is just terrible. It is not in a fantastic area for a start, yes there is a subway stop right outside the door but its only the local 1 train so you have to walk 7 blocks if you want main trains. The building itself is the worst thing about the place. Firstly you have to walk up a flight of stairs to get to the reception, which is almost pitch black. The reception area itself is the hotels only redeeming quality but even this you would get in your average coffee shop. The staff are fine but fighting a losing battle when people see how bad the place is. The worst thing of all is when you go to your room. Depending which floor you're on you may need climbing gear and oxygen as there's no elevator. The stairways are cramped, dark and tatty (ripped carpet and flaky paint). We had a superior room which was the size of a shoe box with no space for clothes and a window looking at a brick wall. The a/c is too loud to keep on and the bathroom is just as bad. The hotel is also a hostel as there are shared bedrooms and bathrooms at the end of the hall. People will say it's cheap for NY but you will find much better for the same price. The one plus we had was that we got sick while there but the hotel was so bad we didn't want to lie around in it so it kept us out and about.

title: “Best bed in the world but ...”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Hyatt following New Year's Day. We stayed in a 'Lafayette Suite'. Overall I was under impressed with the hotel. The location is great - walk to anywhere and our room had a great view of Boston Commons. The room itself was some what dismal - sort of a muted green that was pretty bland with nothing to liven it up. The furniture was early '50s looking with no ottoman for the chair (I need to keep my legs propped up). We were never able to order a movie from pay-for-view despite numerous attempts from engineering to fix the problem. Room service was prompt and not too bad but limited menu. The only redeeming feature of this hotel was the bed. It is by far the most comfortable bed I've ever slept on. Enough to over come the shortcoming that I would stay again? Probably not. There a lot of great hotels in Boston, many with equally comfortable beds I'm sure.

title: “Definately going back!”
text: Stayed for 5 nights and loved it! Brilliant location, really friendly and helpful staff, room small but I'd prefer to call it 'cosy' ;) We got a room in the middle of the block, looking out onto a small concrete courtyard.... BUT, if you looked up you could see one of the many surrounding skyscrapers so you didn't forget where you were! Initially we were a little disappointed our room wasn't out on the street but after our first nights sleep (which we slept like babies) we were very glad to have the peace and quiet of the courtyard, and of course, no morning sun streaming in our room either. Phew! After each day of being on the go, we really looked forward to coming back to the hotel knowing it was gauranteed friendliness, cleanliness, close to our final sightseeing location, and quiet. Would recommend this hotel to anyone wanting a good place to stay with decent prices and a central location. We miss it already!

title: “Terrible hoitel”
text:
I stay in this hotel for my nephew wedding. The services
 of the hotel is terrible. The front desk staff took us a long
 time to check out. The room that we stay is next to the
 elevator. So there was a lot of nosie. The coffe marker
 they put in the bathroom. Terrible. The TV is so small.
 The parking is not valet from the hotel guest . Terrible.

title: “Lived up to its reviews”
text: It's all been said by others, but I'll add my two cents worth. Great motel that far exceeds expectations. The management (franchisee?) has chosen to add extras like the massage chair in the lobby and additional choices in the breakfast menu and evening snacks that really say "We want your stay with us to be exceptional". The room was spotless. The front desk personnel were friendly and very helpful. We stayed an additional night on the trip back because we were so pleased.

title: “Extraordinarily clean, nice amenities, and they make you feel right at home.”
text: Recently my partner and I visited San Diego and decided to give this little gem of a hotel a try (its been rated in the top 10 on trip advisor forever and was less than $100 dollars a night with our AAA discount!) We were delightfully surprised. The property is well maintained, and the rooms are immaculately clean with nice linens and big fluffy pillows on the bed. We enjoyed the pool area, the cute continental breakfast lounge, and the very friendly and attentive staff.

title: “Great value and friendly staff”
text: I chose this hotel because it was in my price range. I spent two nights here by myself, as I was just taking a few days off before going further north. Upon arrival I needed to book an extra night (I also had to check in very late), which was no problem and cost me less than expected. Since I had never been to Seattle before, I also asked the staff for advice on several occasions. Every time I talked to them or needed something, the staff was very friendly and helpful, probably better than at any other hotel in this price range I have ever stayed at. The only problem I found was that there's a bit of air traffic noise, but it didn't bother me too much. The room wasn't the most modern room, but the friendly staff, good location (walking distance to everything you need) and cleanliness of the room made it very worth staying there, considering it's relatively inexpensive.

title: “Great stay at the Hotel ZaZa”
text: My husband and I recently stayed at the Hotel ZaZa in Houston on business, but also to celebrate our 13th anniversary and one of the first nights away from our toddler. The hotel is beautifully designed and we enjoyed seeing all of the art work. We stayed in a Petite King room and found it to be a great size. The bed was incredibly comfortable. We ate at the Monarch Restaurant for dinner and had a great time. The food and service were excellent. Spencer Lane, one of the Managers, made sure we had a great experience and helped us celebrate our special occasion with a complimentary treat. We'll definitely be back!

title: “Disappointed”
text:
I was disappointed in my selection of a hotel. I used priceline to get a good deal on a hotel and entered in I was willing to stay in South Boston and this hotel came up. It lists its address as Boston but it's actually located in Dorchester (a Boston suburb). Their website said that the local T station was only 1.5 miles away but it's actually 2.1 miles by foot or car (read the small print). We arrived at 10 a.m. on a Saturday and was hoping to take the shuttle to the T station to catch the T into Boston. We waited for 10 minutes and when the shuttle arrived it said it only had 2 available seats. Well there were 20 people waiting. The driver said the next shuttle would be in 20 minutes and again would only fit 12 people. The shuttles service both the Comfort Inn and the Ramada. So when it looked like we would never get to the station before noon I asked the man at the front desk how far the T station was and if it was walkable (keep in mind I have small children who were with me). He said it was only about 3/4 of a mile down the road and it was walkable. So we decided to walk. Well it was quite a long walk and when I clocked it with my car the next day I found out it was actually 2.1 miles away and the walk involved walking through parking lots (again I have small children). Needless to say we ended up driving into Boston every day since the shuttle service was a nightmare, not convenient at all. 
The hotel is also not located in a great place. When you check in they give you a hand out that says they have had recent car break-ins and to remove all electronics from your vehicle. They even go as far to say to clean the area were your GPS suctions onto your window so the potential thief doesn't realize you have a GPS. It surely didn't leave us with the warm and fuzzys. 
The train also runs directly behind the hotel so avoid getting a room on the backside of the hotel. We stayed in one on the front side facing the parking lot so I'm not sure how much the train is heard from within one of the backside rooms. 
It's a very small hotel with not a lot of amenities. I surely didn't pay a lot but I guess sometimes you get what you pay for.

title: “Great location for everything Mag Mile”
text: We stayed in a junior suite - king bed in a bedroom and a sofabed in another area. This was perfect for Mom, Dad, and teen boy. Each had their own TV. Bathroom was nice as shower/tub and toilet were in one room and sink area was separate. Small problem with leaky mini-fridge. Viand Bar is a cozy little place to have pre-or-post dinner drinks. The breakfast at Viand is very good, especially if you can get a stay for breakfast package. The lobby is small. Elevators seem to take a long time, but the security/key card system is nice. The pool is small and not warm enough; would be better if it were warmer. Hotel is half-block from Michigan Avenue so is ideal for all you want to see there.

title: “excellent”
text: My family and I stayed here Memorial weekend and were very comfortable.Room was clean and hotel staff was very friendly and helpful with directions where we needed to go.When we return to the area we will stay here again

title: “Best place on the beach”
text: The best place to stay on the beach in San Diego. Delicious breakfast, yummy cookies at night, great staff. They weren't full so they up-graded our rooms and were very responsive to our every need. Most of the hotels on the beach look a little worn but the Pacific Terrace works hard to keep their property looking nice. We would definitely stay there again! Thank you Pacific Terrace for helping us have a great stay in San Diego!

title: “Great staff at a wonderful hotel!”
text: Excellent attentive staff. Great location with easy access to restaurants, transportation, etc. The room was large enough with two queen beds. The bar was a fun gathering place. Breakfast was reasonably priced and delicious.

title: “Red Eye Arrival”
text:
I reserved a room at The Eliot Hotel at the 11th hour and was really pleased that they could accomodate me. I only needed my room for a few hours in the morning as I was arriving straight off an overnight flight from LA. The staff checking me in at 6AM were really helpful and offered a free checkout extension which was great. They also booked me table at a great restaurant for my client lunch later that afternoon.
My suite was very comfortable and clean. The a/c was quite noisy as was the heating installation but I got used to the noise in the end.
The only issue with the suite was in the bathroom where there was a leak however as i was only staying for 4 hrs it didnt really matter.
The staff were really helpful except for the afternoon receptionist who was rude and agressive.

title: “Wow Hotel”
text:
Being in the tourism industry I get to travel and stay at different hotels. Last week I took a family trip to San Diego and decided to stay at the OMNI San Diego. My wife makes fun of me because even while on vacation, I am looking at details of hotels, restaurants or any tourism related service. I have not been impressed by an hotel in a long time, but the OMNI shure made me say WOW. The hotel is well located and the service is just superb. But the best asset of the hotel is its people. Everyone was of great service and knew when to approach guests, and when to keep a distance and let them enjoy the hotel.
For sure I will be back (soon)

title: “Not bad for a conference hotel”
text: The location was pretty great--can't beat walking out onto the Riverwalk, but being far enough off the main drag to miss the bar crawlers. I hear the hotel was booked solid while we were there for a conference, and the service was slow and overtaxed. There were several account mistakes, and there was always a line to speak to concierge or the front desk.

title: “Very Nice Clean Place to Stay”
text: The hotel was extremely clean as if it were new. The beds were the most comfortable I have slept in in a long time. The maid service was great; anything asked for was given with no hesitations. We had total control over the air conditioning which worked great. Staff was friendly and helful. The lobby was always spotless. The hotel was literally 2 minutes from the airport which can be a plus and a negative. If you are just stopping over it's a great location but may not be a great location if vacationing throughout the L.A. area (too much traveling). I was very happy with this hotel.

title: “More than we paid for (except for continental breakfast).”
text:
Picked the hotel because of its location and relatively low cost but ended up getting more than we needed or bargained for. We got there early on a Saturday morning, checked our bags and went to museums. Came back to a suite on the 34th floor. Sparsely furnished with modern furniture but it is rare to get 1.5 bathrooms in a hotel room. 
The front desk staff could have been more friendlier and the continental breakfast was weak. My wife kept telling me to get this and that but when I went to the table the pickings were pretty bare.
Probably got lucky on the room, but would come back again if I wanted to be in midtown.

title: “A very bad experience”
text: This had to be the worst hotel stay I have had in years. I was on a business trip, scheduled to stay elsewhere but was "bounced" to the Days Inn because of oversold rooms with a huge convention in town. The hotel is in poor condition. Dirty elevators, worn rugs in the hallway, but the room was the biggest shock. It was the smallest hotel room I've stayed in in ages--you had to shut the bathroom door to use the toilet because the bathroom was the size of a broom closet!!! The curtains were worn, old and filthy. In the daylight, the room looked even worse--it had not been vacuumed or dusted in quite a while. The location is very noisy and the old radiator system clangs all through the night when the heating shifts. If you just want to save money, you might be able to put up with this, but the upkeep in this hotel is terrible. Its a pity, because the location is an artistic, fun and safe district to explore. Too bad the Days Inn can't keep up with its neighbors in standards and cleanliness.

title: “Super sexy, we loved The Standard NY.”
text:
We don't usually go Boutique Hotel when in Manhattan, but on a friends tip, we booked a room here. We were only in the city for one night, but our stay here made the most of our short visit. With floor to ceiling windows you knew you were in NY. How great to wake up to a view of the Hudson. Definitely a sexy vibe with the wood paneling, low slung bed, exposed shower and the city looking in at you.
We came in on a Red-eye a little worse for wear, but how can you not smile when you are greeted by the cute boys in the nasty little Bavarian-inspired shorts and yellow checked shirts. Everything is happier in yellow including the street level turn-style entrance. Great transition between the sidewalk and the super sleek lobby, you know you have arrived somewhere special. The staff was so helpful getting us as early a check-in as possible, they took our phone number and called as soon as a room was available. A hotel is only as good as the people working there, A+.
We spent the day up at the Met, Central Park then checked out a few Galleries. Once we returned to the hotel we never had to leave again. The Meatpacking District has great restaurants, amazing shopping, the Chelsea Market, and the new Highline. We recommend enjoying a drink in the hotel lounge, the bartender is more than generous with the Vodka and there's great people watching. We missed checking out the views from the gym, next time.

title: “very comfortable”
text: Very comfortable and wellcoming rooms. Really clean towells, sheets and duvets. Spacious room, although no safe deposit box in the room. Staff was very gently. Breakfast with many options. Nice location within a walking distance from many tourist attractions.

title: “Hotel Could Use an Update, Highest Price Parking on Earth, and the locks don't work unless one understands nuances????”
text: Starting with the rather uneducated front desk staff with such poor penmanship they wrote the number on the card so poorly I could not read it. Then the key did not work until the third trip to the front desk as apparently there is some kind of glitch with the doors and the locks interacting, the only place in the world this ever happened. The Concierge was great but be should not have to leave his post to show a guest how to juggle a door to make it work that is quite ridiculous. Old Hotel Starting to look a bit long in the teeth. As a person who travels the world this is the highest price parking I ever experienced to the point of gouging the guests. Simply because you can get away with it does not make it right. Simply put I will not be back and I am a Platinum SPG member. In some cases I am starting to wonder if Starwood is asleep at the switch with the Westin brand as in some ways they are clueless what travelers today want in a hotel. And the famous sleeper bed was all mushed out in suite 1524 the beds are not made to last forever this one is all saggy and uncomfortable. Thanks but never again.

title: “Good Value”
text: Stayed there for three nights on business this week. The hotel is nothing to look at from the exterior, which is probably why there was no picture of the exterior on their web page. The hotel fixtures, bath and kitchenette, are dated. Looks like from the 1950's. The hotel is clean though....beds are comfortable....and the staff is great! We ate at the bistro on site and the food was great. If you can get past the dated portions of the guest rooms this is a great place for the price and it is close to many sites in DC.

title: “We will not stay here again.”
text:
We have stayed at Westin properties before and really enjoyed our stay. The pick-up and drop-off is very small and takes forever to get in and out of the car. 
The pool is terrible. One of the things we enjoy after a long day of sightseeing is either a swim or relaxing in the hot tub. The pool is small, outdoors, and not heated. There is nohot tub. The fitness room is reasonable.
We don't always stay at upscale properties. But when we do, the kids, ages 7 and 8 have come to expect chocolates at bed time. No such luck here. 
The location on the river walk is bad. Its quite a bit away from the lively part of the river walk with the restaurants and other attractions. 
The mattress was too soft. All the pillows were flat. I am willing to let some of these things go when I am staying at La Quinta, but I expect much better accomodation at a 4/5 star facility.
We will never stay there again, and have already warned our friends about it.

title: “MOLD”
text:
I just returned from DC where I stayed in a first floor room in the Wardman Tower. As soon as I entered the room, I noticed that the sprinkler was covered in moldy dust. Then the a/c vent/heating vent came into view. It was black. Black with mold. UGH. I trekked back to the registration desk, informed a nice woman of the issue who offered assurance that housekeeping would be informed. I should have insisted on a new room, but I was just exhausted after a long day of driving and the idea of packing up and moving overwhelmed me. I went out for dinner expecting to see a cleaned vent when I returned around 9 or 9:30. Nope, still black. 
Hmmm. One of the big issues with this vent is that it is located directly over the bed. Thus, it blows directly on the bed. I decided that I should clean it myself, so I stood on the bed with one of their lovely white washcloths and proceeded to turn it black. Big mistake. As I was cleaning it, large particles of mold blew all over the bed. It was obvious that there was a LOT of mold in and behind the vent. Now what to do. New room? I was so tired. It was one night. I made the bad decision to fold back the top cover of the bed and turn OFF the fan of the A/C, figuring if it wasn't blowing I would probably be okay. 
Wrong again. I woke up at 4 AM with a vile headache and facing a 10 hour drive. It wasn't worth trying to get some more sleep. I packed up, headed to check out with the black washcloth. The gentleman listened to my story, but offered me nothing. Not a word of sympathy, let alone compensation. I couldn't even beg an aspirin. (I tried). 
To make matters worse, I had parked my vehicle in the parking garage. I was told to use my room card to exit, but wasn't informed to use it in the second machine. At 5 AM in total darkness, it wasn't obvious where to use my room card. I had to leave the vehicle, walk back into the lobby, and tearfully request some help. Response? Push a "help" button on the machine. Really? I certainly would have pushed an obvious help button. 
It was a horrific experience from the moment I entered the room to the moment I finally got off the property. This is supposedly a 4 star hotel. That certainly was not my experience.

title: “Loved the hotel and the service”
text: We checked into the Westin St.Francis for three nights. Four girls shared a double room in the modern tower. From the moment we walked into the hotel, the staff were helpful and very friendly. The public areas are very grand and beautiful. The room was a comfortable size. The beds were indeed heavenly! The bathroom wasn't as heavenly as advertised. The lighting and shower could be better. We enjoyed our stay at the Westin and would go back. We would aslo recommended dinner and desert at the Cheesecake Factory!!!

title: “Great Staycation!!”
text: Recently stayed here for a weekend. The grounds are very lush and tropical. The rooms are huge and newly remodeled. The lounge has great happy hour specials and the restaurant is good as well. Definitely reccomend this hotel!!

title: “Great Midtown Hotel”
text: We stayed at this hotel when we went to an event over at Radio City. Nice 10 minute walk from this hotel. Rooms are great, modern. Bathroom was tiny but no real issue for us.
