Their pillow menu is a bit silly. We ate room service. Expensive but good quality. Valet parking was a little steep. There's a garage right across the street and I probably should have self parked. Did not use any other services.

title: “great place to stay in chicago”
text: Me and my girlfriend stay there for 3 nights on the last august ... was great! the position is perfect, near chicago river / lake michigan ... navy pier is almost 20 minutes to walk. Michigan avenue, the loop & millenium park are the centre of the life and very close to the hotel! the room was great even if internet wasn't free (like in all the highest category hotels). I can say only one thing ... if you desire to stay confortable wit ha good amount from price / quality this is the right place for you!

title: “Wonderful service, excellent value”
text:
My husband and I are professionals who live on Long Island and work long days in Manhattan and NJ. Between the 2 of us, we stay in hotels in Manhattan 1-2x weekly. Sometimes I arrive late the night before working so I won't have to commute the next day. While HI Express at 39th St. isn't in the best area and I could pay to stay in a more upscale neighborhood -- but the staff is so accommodating and the hotel rooms so clean and comfortable I keep coming back. 
Evening staff --specifically, Rudy-- is professional, courteous, and makes check-in a positive experience --even if it's 1 AM. Over the years I've had negative experiences checking in after midnight . On one occasion I pre-paid for a room and despite calling to say I'd arrive at midnight -- my room was given away. I received an apology and was offered a refund that took 2 weeks to process..... but needless to say after traveling back home at 1 am and missing work the next day, I want nothing to do with that hotel chain (a big name in the industry, begins with "M").
At this HI Express --not only will they hold your room and offer the best available location but if you arrive late and are a Priority Club member, they offer late checkout. Add to that free breakfast and lovely Christmas decor in the lobby. I doubt there's a friendlier, cleaner, more comfortable hotel at this price in Manhattan.

title: “Smack bang in times square”
text: Modern and hip with great service and free Internet. The location makes it easy to get the best Broadway tickets at the tkts queue and good shopping and eating. Staff helped us locate laundromat and hairdressers v good. Only downside v small room, even for NYC but if you are out and about lots like s less of a concern. Best service we had in NYC.

title: “Exactly as promised”
text: Stayed at Cornell Hotel de France for 3 nights while at a conference at the Hyatt Regency. About a 20-25 minute hike from the Hyatt Regency and Ferry Building (uphill to the hotel) but well worth the walk. Room was small and similar to European style hotels but was clean and staff were friendly. Breakfast started a bit late (7:30am) but was much better than the typical hotel continental breakfast with great speedy service. Very close to China Town and many great food options. I'd definitely stay here again when in San Francisco.

title: “THe mega-conference hotel is located Union Square side but near the Tenderloin”
text: We had a lovely stay at this conference hotel in downtown San Francisco. It has a secluded outdoor pool set in an interior courtyard. We were in the relatively newly renovated side of the hotel. It is located between Union Square and the Tenderloin - gratefully on the Union Square side, but Tourists should still keep their eyes open when they leave the hotel. It is a huge facility! It would not be describe as romantic, but was a very nice business hotel.

title: “poor service drab appearence”
text:
I booked an apartment but the hotel had booked a studio as it was Labour Day weekend we accepted on condition compensation was made and a fold away bed was provided. The
admin is terrible no attempt was made to compensate they have just been taken over and are not up to scratch. My travel co. GTA were great they got us moved to the 1 bed we booked and 1 extra night free without their efforts the Envoy Club would not help they do not care .This building is in need of a make over all rooms look shabby and tired

title: “the perfect hotel in the perfect town”
text:
One week after our return, we still remember the really good time we spent at the bryant park hotel. Me and my boyfriend booked 5 days at new york for our anniversary. For this great moment, we enjoyed one of the most beautifull room we ever experienced with a quite large terrace. The view on the bryant park and the closest buildings was breathtaking ; the bathroom was great and the room was large enough for 2. 
The hotel location is ideal, right in the middle between the 05th avenue and time square. Additionnally, there is a bus stop at the park for passengers coming from newark by 'coach usa'.
We never took the breakfast at the hotel so we cannot tell how it is.
The service is very good and friendly. They made all possible efforts to congratulate us for our birthday and make our stay one of the best 'souvenir' !!! 
All in all, absolutely nothing to say on the 'negative' side, only compliments are to be made. We will come back at new-york and we will come back to the bryant park hotel, that's for sure....

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
My daughter and I stayed here for a mini vacation during Fiesta. From the outside, you would never know this was a hotel, but once inside, we were pleasantly surprised. The staff was great and answered all my questions and were very accomodating to my requests. Homewood is situated on the quieter section of the River Walk which is just great since I understand that the Fiesta celebrating can go on until the early morning hours.
The suite was very nicely decorated and smelled clean. The bed and the sofa bed were very comfortable. The living area had no windows and it was a bit depressing. The bedroom faced an office building so there was no view to speak of. The hotel provided the normal ammenities, shampoo, hair dryer, etc. Plenty of towels and pillows, which I always wind up asking for more of.
Situated on the River Walk, having breakfast and the manager's reception at night is terrific. You can sit by the huge windows and enjoy the boats going by as well as walkers. The breakfast buffet was plentiful and a good variety. The manager's reception was a great way to start the evening. If you have a late lunch and go to the reception, you can forget about dinner. 
The roof pool was small but would have been sufficient on a really hot day. 
The business center was great. Two computers with internet access. Great for a teenager to keep in touch with her My Space and Facebook. A terrific way to save on cell phone minutes.
I would and have recommended this hotel to co-workers and friends. I will definetely consider staying here again if we make a return trip to San Antonio

title: “Absolutely perfect!”
text: My husband, myself and our 4 children stayed at the Lucerne during our first trip to NYC. From the moment we arrived, we were made to feel welcome. We arrived earlier than expected and to my surprise, they had our room ready. EVERY single employee we encountered was so friendly and helpful. Our room was immaculate and huge for NYC standards. Very comfortable beds and large TV's. Plenty of room for the whole family. Very clean with every amenity. We drove to NYC from Ohio and there is a parking garage just 2 blocks from the hotel with very reasonable rates. This hotel is beautiful and in a great area. We were able to walk to Central Park and many other attractions. The kids loved the doormen who always made a fuss over them when we would return back to the hotel. The neighborhood is very nice, quiet (for NYC) and safe. The concierge was able to get us tickets for Wicked and the seats were excellent. This hotel made our experience in NYC unforgettable and amazing. Our kids will never forget how well they were treated and neither will we. Thank you to all the wonderful doormen (especially Pierre) who helped us learn how to hail a cab! We will be back soon, and the Lucerne is the only hotel for us!

title: “Great location, very friendly”
text:
We stayed for three nights in March. The people there were very friendly. I asked for a king size bed on the booking form and got the biggest bed I have ever seen in my life! Our room faced into the courtyard and was very quiet. The location is great. Feels very safe and is just a few blocks from the cable car and some nice cafes and restaurants. Apart from our obligatory tourist ride on the cable car we walked nearly everywhere - down to the wharf (where we hired bikes to go to Golden Gate Bridge), North Beach, Chinatown, Telegraph Hill, Union Square..... The staff were happy to advise us where not to walk through, and the hills were a good work out!
I'd definitely recommend booking this motel.

title: “Excellent in every way”
text:
I had checked out early from the hotel next door because it was so bad, and checking into 6 - boy am I glad I did!
The staff are exceptional, from the concierge, to front desk, to bar staff on the terrace, to the guys out front - all helpful, cheerful, and beautiful!
The rooms are great! Big comfy bed, lovely decor, stunning bathroom etc etc.
The location is great too, a few hundred yards from Central Park.
I'm checking out tomorrow, and I'll be sad to leave. 
Thanks guys!

title: “Excellent in sall respect”
text: Stayed with four other friends for five nights at the Wolcott over thanksgiving weekend. It was fantastic value for money, will definately stay again. Rooms, bedding , towels were clean and fresh, staff were pleasant and helpful what more do you want for a stay in the city. coffee and muffins in the lobby every morning helped start those busy shopping days .

title: “More than expected”
text:
located in George Washington University, a safe and comfortable neighborhood, an easy five minutes' walk to Metro Station Room is old, but clean and cozy. has a desk and chair, a dresser and a cable TV , we felt at home.
The breakfast is toast, donut, and banana, simple but enough to get you started.
There is hot/cold water in the lobby, very convenient. The staff are friendly and helpful. We enjoyed the stay.

title: “Stark contrast from the past”
text:
I was reluctant to stay here when my company booked the reservation. Though I came to find that the hotel was brand new, and no longer reminded me of a roadside motel. There's a hallway, basic services and free high speed internet (cat5).
The room decor is kinda plain, and the bed blanket looks old and ratty (multiple rooms and multiple stays). They could use new bedding.
The cable system has plenty of options and the bathroom is spacious and generally clean (I have encountered loose hairs here and there).
Overall it's a decent stay. The location is great for The Ohio State University, and the staff is generally pleasant.
There's a Damon's restaurant literally in the parking lot that my co-workers love.

title: “Fairmont property on the front, but lacking in Fairmont service”
text:
Having stayed in many Fairmont properties this property around Dupont Circle/ Georgetown was small and grand on the outside. Greetings from the doorman opened the door to a marble lobby and concierge waiting for requests. The property sits in a quiet young proffessional part of DC with an easy to walk to any cafe or nightclub. The hotel's gift shop is closed but it's a short walk to a pharmacy to find some papers or other items. 
The pool is inside and ok for lap swimming. Good fitness centre and spa.
The service seems to be the weakest link for this Fairmont property with housekeeping and turndown service sitting at the top of the list. I did note many supervisors constantly attending to the guests from the front door to the lobby area.
The rooms were not as clean or well restocked as I would have hoped for, but was passable. The mini bar was missing items on check in and never restocked and had to ask for creamers on the 2nd day.
It was average, but not outstanding. 
Would I choose to return? Most likely we would not.

title: “Great service and access to local restaraunts and nightlife.”
text: This hotel is in a great location. You are within walking distance to some great restaraunts and bars if you are into experienceing some nightlife. The staff at the hotel was very friendly and helpful. We even has coffee and cookies brought to our room for no charge. If you go online and sign up to be a Select Guest, you get freebies like morning beverages, evening turn down survice and free Wi-Fi (otherwise you must pay for internet service.) I would definately stay at this hotel again.

title: “It was one of the best says I've had.”
text: We were helped by Xani and everything was wonderful.

title: “Mediocre”
text: This hotel is not on par with others in the Crowne Plaza chain. The rooms are not in good repair, and inquiries and requests to the staff were typically met with indifference. The surrounding blocks are typical of downtown Washington: randomly strewn with construction cones and the occasional boarded-up building. Par for the course during the week, but out-of-towners might not feel safe on the wknd. In the end, you can do better than this place for the money.

title: “In the heart of Chicago!!”
text: We loved it! In the middle the the famous Michigan Ave!! Had a really cool vibe!! Room was really nice. I recommend the city view. It's not much more than a regular room rate. Overall it was a fabulous stay!!

title: “Great hotel, great value, and great location”
text:
I traveled here with my family (husband, two children) for a quick getaway and sightseeing. The hotel location is perfect, especially if you are going to the theatre. We walked to the Cadillac Palace Theatre--about 5 or 6 blocks at the most. Also an easy walk to the Art Institute and many restaurants. The Berghoff and the Italian Village are both just one block away. 
Rooms were an adequate size for four. Each floor is quite small --probably less than 10 rooms. Street noise is definitely an issue, but I imagine that's the case with any hotel in the area.

title: “Nice Hotel in a good location with minimal to no Hotel staff available...really...”
text:
Memphis was an overnight stop for us. The location of the hotel was good so we decided to go for it since it was in downtown and a few blocks walking distance to the key places in memphis downtown, The hotel was pretty good just like the other spring hill suites, with contemporary looks and nice comfortable beds. Our kids loved seeing the Trolley stop right outside the hotel window. The trolley does make it a bit noisy but it was not too bad for us later in the evening. SInce the tolley stop is just there, that was a wonderful experience for us to take the trolley tour of downtown. Nightime around the hotel did not look too friendly due to some people standing around the trolley station/park area , loitering , drinking not sure, etc..Also the evening time in downtown was pretty quiet maybe because.of Christmas weekend approaching, and it did not seem very friendly to walk around with family.
Breakfast was pleasant with the usual accompaniments for a continental/hot breakfast. 
We tried calling the Hotel front desk a few times but no one would pick up the phone. We also saw the front desk guy was always on the phone whenever we walked by OR in front of the TV in the lobby area, So that explains why the phone was not answered. When we did have a few questions, the security guard(Jerry I think...) was extremely helpful to answer our questions about the downtown. 
Overall a good place for a quick stop over in a good location so you can get a good tour of memphis downtown.

title: “Excellent value, okay location, needs a slight makeover”
text: We were in town for a family wedding, so we booked 6 rooms here. Got a great deal of $89 a night over the labor day weekend - considering the inner harbor hotels were well over $100, we took this. The hotel is about a 10-15 minute walk from the harbor area. It isn't in the greatest area, and I wouldn't walk around alone at night, but on a nice day it is a fine walk. The hotel rooms are standard Sheraton - very comfortable bed, flat screen, and decent bathroom amenities. The bathroom itself was tiny - big enough for one at a time. One thing that annoyed me was that we were told we were on the club floor. When my key didn't open it, I checked downstairs and she said it was closed. I tried again when I went back up and it worked, and there was breakfast being served. It did close on the weekend (which annoyed me too because the sign on the door has hours 7 days a week), and no one stocked it with water or sodas at all. If you can get a good rate here for much less than a harbor hotel, take it, otherwise for $20 a night more stay at the harbor area.

title: “Good choice for fun in Chicago!”
text: If you want a GREAT location for seeing Chicago as a tourist this is it. One block from Hancock Center and Water Tower. Close to buses, but a bit of a walk to El. Close to water Lakeshore Drive and Lincoln Park too. Really decent breakfast but a bit crowded and needed more fresh fruit. Evening food half the week too. Quiet and solid but not beautiful building. Good competent friendly staff. We saw everything and got good rest each night. Not really a business hotel. Our room did not have tub, only shower. Nice kitchen and full size refrigerator. Good choice

title: “sportsfan”
text: The best part of my trip was riding the hotel shuttle to and from a Mariner's baseball game without having to worry about traffic jams, parking or extra driving! Spent the extra time enjoying Safeco Field, instead. Our shuttle driver Alex was outstanding! He knew all the best ways to get around town and was very prompt. The front desk was great, even helped me buy last minute tickets to the game. As everyone says, this place is not new, and is motel-like, but you can't beat the convenience. Great location, free breakfasts, shuttle service to the games and a nice restaurant in the parking lot!

title: “Staying at time hotel”
text: Hotel was perfectly located less than 5 mins walk from times square.staff were very welcoming and rooms were average size but very clean.we will certainly use this hotel on our next visit to NY

title: “Bed bugs!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!”
text: What else can I say? My wife and daughter had bug bites all over their face and bodies. It was so bad that afterward when my daughter went to school, her friends asked her if she had the chicken pox!!! When we complained to the front office staff they seemed to be nonchalant about it and made no effort to rectify the situation with a room change. They didn't even make a gesture to compensate us for our inconvenience. I would never recommend this place. If you value your health and don't want to have a pox-face, go elsewhere.

title: “Nice hotel in a great part of town”
text: We had no problems during our stay here. People were friendly and beds were extremely comfortable. Just down the street from Coit Tower and easy walk to Chinatown.

title: “Good People and Great Value”
text:
Rooms with micro and fridge ........worked great and just friendly and kind people who look for ways to help you.
Milli is a great mgr with a calm demeanor and responded to any and all needs or requests.
People like Kirsten were just kind and made the stay here better than I expected.
For the price and location this has to be one of Austins best values in hotel stays
Great little breakfast with eggs and sausage among cereals and rolls made this stay even better.

title: “Beautiful and comfortable but -1 for "resort" fee.”
text:
The Westgate is a gorgeous hotel. Comfortable beds, nice "rich English granny" decor, and a lovely big bathroom. The hotel's location is really convenient to shopping, dining, nightclubs, the convention center and the ballpark. The on-site parking was expensive but we stayed over a weekend and managed to find free overnight street parking for the two nights we were there. (Just be sure to read the signs and know the bylaws for the color coded curbs.) 
We really didn't have any complaints except for the $15/night resort fee. We were told it was for hotel "services". Kind of a bummer when the only service we used was the internet and to be frank, when the nightly rate is $200-$250 one expects that the services would be included.

title: “Great Location. Great Price.”
text:
Check the hotel website for their Sunday night special. (The closer to the weekend, the lower the price gets as long as they have rooms.) We had a King Suite: King bed (very comfortable), sitting area (couch, chair), entertainment center and wet bar (sink, refrigerator, microwave,coffee maker, real cups and glasses, silverware...) Noise was NOT a problem on Sunday night. Very pleasant and helpful staff.
Great location; Easy walking distance to Union Square, Curran Theatre, trolley & more - try Max's restaurant a short block away - more reasonable than the hotel's restaurant and great food (breakfast, lunch and dinner.) 
The ONLY negative is the decor - I'm talking UGLY! But clean and good quality - so turn out the lights and you have a 3+ star boutique hotel at 1-2 star prices! 
Beware the "stay & park" deal - we paid $5 more for parking on the package deal than if we had just gone to the hotel and paid the $28 per day parking. (Might want to call the hotel before booking and compare the package to the regular parking at the time.)
Enjoy

title: “Nice place, clean, safe, good location and affordable”
text: My wife, son and I spent 4 nights at Hotel 17 in mid-July. Not wanting to spend a fortune, we compared Hotel 17 with other "budget" hotels in Manhattan after reading numerous reviews. We were not disappointed. Though the rooms are small (in general, they are in NY budget hotels), we got the 3-person room and were pleasantly surprised by the space we had. No food, coffee, etc. on site but there are numerous possibilities close by. AC worked well, and the place was clean enough for my wife (very clean). Shared bathroom was not a problem. We checked thoroughly for bedbugs and found no signs. Pleasant and helpful concierge downstairs. The small elevator makes for cozy conversations. All in all, if you're going to NYC to see stuff, not to hang out in a hotel, this is a fine choice.

title: “Can't say enough Good about this Hotel!!!”
text: Stayed at The Orchard Aug 21st and 22nd and I have nothing but good things to say about it! Absolutely GREAT location. We like to walk around and see everything when we travel and we were able to walk to Union Square, Chinatown, North Beach, Lombard St., and Fisherman's Wharf and back all in one afternoon. If you don't like to walk as much as us, the Orchard is right on the cable car line! They also had free breakfast with assortment of breads, meats, cheeses, fruits, and drinks and free high speed Internet. They also had DVD and CD players in the room and the room itself was fabulous. We got a great rate through AAA with a king bed and the room was bigger than average - especially compared to other "botique" hotels I have stayed in. They also have Aveda shampoos and soaps! I would HIGHLY recommend The Orchard to anyone going to San Fran for business or fun!!! Truly a GREAT hotel - book without hesitation!

title: “DC hotel”
text:
We picked the Washington Plaza, DC after reading reviews in tripadvisor.
We were not disappointed. 
The room, though on the smallish side, was clean and well appointed.
The staff was helpful, friendly and polite.
We only ate one meal in the restaurant attached; breakfast and it was ok.
It was a little bit of a walk to the museums and monuments, but we like walking so that was not a problem. Cabs are not expensive in DC and buses run everywhere.
The noise factor was there, but it is a big city and there is always noise. We had a room in the back and that cut the noise down. 
All in all, we would recommend the Washington Plaza, DC.

title: “Just needed a little advice”
text:
I was looking for a hotel to stay in for 1 night for a class in Boston. The Comfort Inn (which was my first choice) had no rooms open, I simply asked the Ramada operator what other hotels were in the area of UMASS Boston. Rich replied " I can't give that information while I work here"
I find this ridiculous. I understand the whole competition peice...but really, the Comfort Inn did not have any other rooms available, yet DO NOT allow their employees to give a name of another hotel in the same area. REALLY? Has customer Service decreased while competition is increasing?

title: “very pleasant”
text:
I had a pleasant stay at the Magnolia and it was very convienent to the down town area. 
The only reccomendation I have is to have a little more variety for the Hot breakfast.

title: “Very nice hotel, clean, good service and best location ever !”
text:
Hi
My husband and I were on honeymoon in NY for 4 days. We stayed at the Wellington Hotel on 7th and 55th.
I have booked this hotel because it was not expensive and I really only needed a place to sleep in a good location. 
But when I get to the hotel I was surprised (in a good way).
We had booked a double room (the cheapest) and we got a queen on 23rd floor with a balcony.
We didn't really used the balcony because it was really high but it was still very nice the room was very clear (because we had one window, plus the window door to the balcony)
The room was spacious, with a double bed, 1 bedside table on each side. One desk with a chair and an additional chair, the TV was a flat nice screen. We also had a closet and a very nice bathroom, the bathroom was renovated , it was clear and clean, and every day the housekeepers would clean it and put new towels/shampoo and everything we just needed.
The staff at the hotel was really kind.
The location of the hotel is one of the greatest : not even 10 mn walk to Times Square, 5 mn to Central Park and 10 mn also to 5th avenue. There is a bus stop just in front oh the hotel as well as a Starbucks .
Overall we were very satisfied with our stay.
Note : if you book via the website you get free wifi in the room it was very convenient for us !

title: “Great choice”
text: Just returned from trip. Stayed in 2 bedroom suite. Suite was huge, was like staying in an apartment, actually much larger than many apartments I have seen plus had view of Mississippi from living room. Staff was courteous, rooms were clean and had two bathrooms, breakfast buffet was actually good and location was great. Close to everything in Memphis you would want to do, museums, Beale Street, Peabody Hotel ducks, etc. I initially had booked at Westin but was concerned about Beale Street noise but at Residence Inn had best of both worlds, was close to Beale but completely quiet. Also less than a block away from Rendezvous, one of the most famous bar-b-que restaurants in Memphis. I am very picky about hotels and travel a lot. This was great bang for your buck and I recommend it highly, especially the suite.

title: “excellent, didn't want to leave”
text:
Have just returned from a short (3 night) break in NYC.
Our choice of hotel was (as always) partly down to the comments and photos of other TripAdvisor guests, and previous comments could not have been more right. This place is wonderful.
We booked a Superior Queen (that's what the holiday company were selling) but requested a walk-in shower as we had seen a monster of a shower in the photos. I'm not sure if this was the only reason, but we were upgraded to a Deluxe King with Balcony!! The bed, shower, everything was huge! The balcony was lovely, although in sub-zero temperatures not exploited. But the windows opened, which was a bonus. There were robes and an umbrella (which we had to use....boo) for use during our stay. And a fridge (not a mini bar).
The staff couldn't have been nicer - very helpful and extremely accommodating. We had an evening flight home and they were happy to store our bags and give us use of the restrooms etc. There were some works going on in the lobby during our stay but that did not detract in any way from this being the best hotel we have stayed at in New York.
In fact this was our 3rd visit, and 3rd hotel - if we go to NYC again, I will not need to look any further. Other hotels should take note, and do what The Pearl are doing, as they have definitely got it right!

title: “Great place to stay”
text:
The Westin is probably an option you should consider when looking for an hotel located on Time Square.
Once a year i return to that same location and the Westin always deliver on expectations. The staff is friendly and helpful.

title: “Great place to stay at Fisherman's Wharf”
text: Read reviews of the Argonaut and decided to try it out. Our family traveled to California in mid-July 2004 and reserved 2 adjoining rooms at the Argonaut as we were traveling with our children, ages 19, 16, and 12. The rooms were perfect; a king bed in one with a sofa (not a pull-out) and 2 queen beds in the adjacent room. Both room were beautifully appointed in nautical themes. Really appreciated the hotel GUARANTEEING adjoining rooms as many these days won't. The biggest disappointment during our stay was our visit to the hotel's Blue Mermaid Chowder House for dinner. Went on a Sunday evening, and were seated immediately. Restaurant not more than 3/4 full, yet it took almost an hour to get our food, AFTER giving order to the waiter. Really, how hard is it to make up one chicken fingers kid's meal, 2 fish sandwiches, and a couple of salads??!! Food a big disappointment, too. Far too pricey for substandard service and food quality. We'll definitely stay at the Argonaut on our next visit to SF but will bypass the Blue Mermaid! The wonderful Tarantino's is just a short walk down the street or one could choose from a number of other restaurants in the immediate area. There are a couple of little diner/cafe places a block or so from the hotel, serving great, reasonably priced breakfasts.

title: “Average”
text: Stayed 7/19-7/23 for a conference. Room on 9th floor was small but clean. Carpet was somewhat worn. Bed okay but nothing to write home about. A friend who had checked in the same day told me his 5th floor room had some roaches so he was moved to the 11th floor and had no problem there. No bugs in my room. Hotel has good location and many good restaurants plus subway are nearby. Convenient parking across street. I think if you can get a decent rate on one of the web sites this place would work but would not be anywhere near whatever their rack rate is posted at.

title: “Good on all fronts...”
text:
I stayed as one of their IHG Platinum Ambassadors (Loyalty scheme). Check-in was good...upgraded to a King Premier room (Basically a room on a higher floor)...a great view of SFs freeway! Room was great, as was the bathroom...the bath was deep enough to actually have a bath in, rather than the more shallow ones I've found elsewhere. Plenty of towels and bits and bobs in the bathroom.
Wifi for ambassadors was free...It was I think $15 for 1 day, $35 for 3 days...it worked most of the time..not all. 
TV had a huge number of channels.
We had an issue with the turn down and our door being left unlocked, found by me after an evening out....a call to the duty manager expressing my deep concern was promptly addressed by comping me enough points for a free night in another IC hotel.
AirCon was perfect...quiet but effective. 
We drank in the bar..not overly steep...a HUGE range of spirits in a glass cabinet that takes up the wall adjacent to the bar...to be seen really!
I've stayed here twice now...the location off market and 4th makes it convenient for the streetcar/shopping/BART (Powell) but means the rates reflect that! A good place to cash in your priorityclub points!
There are a good choice of places to eat nearby....check-my review of Mels Diner, also there is a Dennys around the corner if that's your thing. There is also a Liquor store open late right opposite the hotel for emergencies!

title: “Excellent hotel”
text: My husband and I stayed here during our recent vacation to NYC. The room was identical to the pictures on the website and was VERY clean! The hotel staff was very friendly and helpful. There is a room available for you to store your luggage at no charge if your flight leaves after the 12pm checkout. Easy access to the subway and to Times Square! We will definitely stay here again.

title: “Good location but so-so service”
text: Great location, fair price (seeing breakfast is included and parking for downtown NYC is very reasonable). However, both times, on different days, I had to deal with the front desk staff I have yet to see them smile and actually enjoy their job. They made me feel as if I dare ask a question I would disturb them. They either need thorough training on what good basic customer service means, especially in hotels and in NYC or ... be fired if they don't improve their attitude. Rooms are fine, but need to be refreshed (wallpaper was tired !).

title: “Free Breakfast was overpriced”
text: The Lobby was a dump. The attitude of the clerk that checked us in did nothing to approve our opinion of the motel. The room was dirty. I thought maybe they were overbook and we had a room that was in the progress of being updated, but reading other reviews I guess we had the best avaiable. The bed wasn't comfortable even after thoroughly examing the linens for bed bugs. The bathroom was very grubby, the sink and shower both had soap build up. Checking out was pleasant it didn't take long to examine the breakfast area and give your key back. Then as you start your car you get a wonderful feeling knowint there was no way you'd ever have to return to this pit again. If they would tear this Motel down it would definately improve the area. So if for some reason you find yourself sleepy on the 15500 block of 52nd Drive in Phoenix take my advice and sleep in your car

title: “Good hotel in a central location.”
text: We stayed for 4 nights. The hotel is around 10-15 minutes away from Market Street BART station and close to Union Square and the Powell Street cable car. Our room was clean, comfortable and quiet. There was no obvious free wifi. We didn't eat in the hotel but there are loads of restaurants and places for breakfast nearby (we would have breakfast at Starbucks and used their wifi).

title: “If you're looking for a good motel near Downtown, then you should give it a try.”
text:
We stayed for one night after our arrival at LAX. Due to the great location near Downtown we were able to explore LA on the same day without wasting much time.
The motel has a rustic charme, but it's clean and functional. Free parking and free wifi is a plus.

title: “Bed bugs!”
text: We have stayed at the Drury Hotel in Charlotte many times and have always been impressed by the cleanliness. Twice I have written the corporate office to acknowledge their high standards. Unfortunately, our experience in April was different. As usual, the room appeared clean. While visiting the bathroom around 2am, I noticed a bug on my shirt. I killed the bug and noticed blood on the tissue....bed bugs! After turning the lights on in the room, numerous bugs were seen on the linens. On inspection, the top of the mattress showed clear signs of bedbugs. As one might imagine, this was upsetting. We contacted the front desk and were told that we would be moved to another room. The desk clerk appeared at the door with new room cards and an envelope containing the amount paid for the room (part of the cash was rolled coin). I am not sure what they hoped to accomplish with this gesture, but money was not something we were concerned about at that time. We did not want to take bedbugs to our home. We were instructed by the manager to leave our belongings in the infested room. The exterminator would arrive early in the morning and would heat treat our belongings along with the room, killing the bedbugs. Unfortunately, none of this happened. We received a call from the manager at 9am at which time she informed us that the exterminator “only found two bed bugs”, our untreated belongings had been moved to our “clean room”. No further action was taken on the part of the hotel staff. They were done! As evident by the appearance of the mattress, others have been exposed to bedbugs in that room. I hope that they have been informed of their exposure. Judging by the actions or lack of by management during our experience, I would guess not.

title: “Comfortable with Helpful, Friendly service”
text:
My family stayed at the hotel the week before thanksgiving and enjoyed the stay. The room was quiet and comfortable. We were on the 7th floor in 701. View of the building next door was not much to see but for all the reviews talking about garbage trucks and noise the hotel was not bad at all. You are in the middle of New York so there's bound to be some noise. Just a few blocks to Times Square, close to a couple subway lines and Penn station. 
The hot breakfast is very good with helpful staff, waffles, eggs, cereal, etc. Much easier than taking the kids out for breakfast. Coffee was not great but there's a Starbucks 100 yards away.
The best part was the friendly and helpful front desk. We had booked online and must have made a mistake with the checkout date. After talking with the front desk they accommodated us for one more night even thought the hotel was completely sold out that night. That's service you don't find at every hotel. Very thoughtful and a real help since we messed up the checkout date.

title: “Perfect stay for the weekend”
text: Needing a place in the city for the weekend, the Nolitan was a perfect fit. Though set in a trendy neighborhood, I found parking within two minutes just a block from the hotel. From the moment I stepped into the lobby, the staff were friendly and attentive. My corner room on the ninth floor had striking views of the Empire State Building to the left and the Williamsburg Bridge to the right. Though not spacious, the room was quite comfortable and immaculately clean. Initially needing a quiet place to get some documents read, the simple desk with late afternoon sun and stunning views of the city was ideal. In the evening, I met up with friends in the hotel's restaurant, called Ellabess. Dinner was delicious. As a group, we ordered several appetizers. Each was fixed perfectly. For my main dish, I chose the potato gnocchi with duck sausage. It was a perfect dish for a cold winter day. Getting back to my room after midnight, I slept great. The sun woke me up a little earlier than I would have liked. But that was my fault for not closing the curtains the night before. And actually it served me well. I caught breakfast at Ellabess just before their 10 am cutoff. Once again, delicious. I would regret to have missed it. Lingering unrushed with friends, it was a great start to a Sunday. I would not hesitate returning to the Nolitan the next time I am in the city.

title: “excellent accommodation”
text:
What great value for money. The suite is huge and very comfortable. Bedding was excellent including the sofa bed. Breakfast was one of the best we have had in the terms of quality, not selection(only basic, but very tasty).
The service was fast and efficient. Check in at noon and we were given a room, no waiting. The shuttle was quick and reliable.
Great location to airport and even tourist attractions.
After checking in we walked up the road(2 minutes) to Avis and collected our car. Budget is right next door to the hotel. 
There is a $9.90 fee for the internet.
I could not fault this hotel in any way, and will certainly return in the future

title: “Good location but a tiny room”
text: I spent four days in this hotel with my boyfriend. The hotel is in a very good location. Our room was clean but very very tiny and a bit dark. The staff was helpful . At the time we went there were doing some work but from the reviews we read it seems that has been going for quite sometime. I will stay there again because it is very central...

title: “Friendly people but understaffed”
text:
I just returned from a large conference that was held in the downtown area. The Marriott was the designated conference hotel. Our room was very nice and spacious. The hotel staff were extraordinarily helpful and nice. The biggest issue was under-staffing. There were not enough people to help in the restaurant, bar or even at the front desk. As noted by someone else recently, our room was not serviced until late and one day it was not serviced at all. That said I think the staff were working really hard. There were just too many people and not enough help. This is something that the management needs to fix. They certainly knew that the conference was scheduled and I don't know why they didn't gear up for it with some extra help.
But Memphis is a fabulous city for a convention! I would recommend it to anyone.

title: “San Diego Westin experience - Australian perspective”
text: I stayed at the Westin San Diego for a week in mid Oct 2012 for business purposes. It is a wonderful hotel and ideally centrally located for tripping around the cbd and eating out. A full credit to the hotel management, that where I raised minor concerns, they explained the process or reasons for the issues - however regardless, they always compensated me (such as a free breakfast for a meal being slow to prepare). The hotel facilities were good and the room was to a high standard. I would have no hestitation in recommending the hotel to other persons.

title: “We loved it and will be back for sure...”
text: We loved it and will be back for sure to this property :) We often stay at higher end hotels but in this case it was too expensive due to some event in town. Rooms were very clean and the price was right. You can't expect a 5 star room paying for a 2 star hotel. Staff were fantastic and very friendly. It was kinda noisey but it is located on a busy street and they had security in the evenings which was great. We love the city and when we decide to revisit we will definitely come back to stay. We wish we would've known :)

title: “FABULOUS, FIRST CLASS HOTEL!”
text: love love love the trump hotel! it is unlike any place we have ever stayed- the rooms are like being in a spa-from the pillows to the down duvet-the bathroom is unbelievable-there is a TV in the bathroom mirror! The bathrobes are plush and luxurious-The curtains open & close electronically!Revealing the most wonderful and incredible view of Lake Michigan and the Chicago River! Truly spectacular. The donotdisturb sign is also electronic and has a keypad on the outside of the door that lights up. There is a Bose sound system for the iphone charger.The kitchen has 5 star appliances Can't say enough good things about this hotel! If you can spend the extra money- you will not regret it- Only Problem was when we arrived- our booking.com reservation could not be found & it took longer to check in- Finally they got us a room while we were out eating- when we came back and went to the room the keys didn't work- finally the bellman came with our luggage and let us in the room- but the room didn't have a kitchen as it was supposed to have- so the bellman called down and got us a room with a kitchen and it was a much better room! He was even excited for us to have the new room! You won't be disappointed with anything here- you feel like a king!The terrace bar is so magical- we can't wait to return to Chicago and stay at the trump- and we are looking at other trips to other locations to see if there is a trump hotel! Way to go Donald!

title: “A Must Stay!!”
text: My sister & I LOVED this hotel... it was superbly located... quiet for the central location & has such unique friendly included options such as the daily complementary wine & cheese!! you feel at home!! I will definitely stay here again on my next trip!!!

title: “Dirty Room needs a broom”
text: Great Location. Dirty Rooms..If all you care about is seeing the city, this is central enough to succeed and dirty enough to make you want to stay out, exploring in the city. The staff was awsome though, very friendly. They switched us rooms, but, the new room we got wasn't much better. Have Fun!

title: “Great lap pool, better than the room”
text:
I stayed here because they have a 25m lap pool,high above the city. Very exciting, and extremely well-kept, as are the rooms. But, aside from the view over the park, it was no big deal. St Regis is far more luxurious. 
The public facilities are understated and very pleasant. Service is both friendly and professional. And breakfast is delicious. 
However the coffee is awful, Illy, and they charge 8 or 9 per order.
My room had both a tub and shower, but unbelievably, this small stall's floor is sloped, and when your feet start sliding as it gets slippery, falling is (in my case), inevitable. 
Finally, they charge for wifi. At this level, I find it greedy of the hotel to tax you this way.

title: “What a gem”
text:
We decided on this hotel because of other great reviews. This was a terrific hotel. Location is outstanding, the staff were excellent and the extras this hotel put on such as breakfast and complimentary drinks and nibbles in the evening for their guests is exceptional. The rooms are comfortable and clean. We had an inside room which meant it was darker than the rest, however we were not bothered by noise or Time Square dazzle. We recommend this to anyone wanting to visit 'The Big Apple'
Great spot for theatre buffs also.

title: “great stay”
text:
Just finished a two night stay at the Omni. 
The valet and bell staff practically pushed each other out of the way to help us from our car upon arrival. By no means was this a push for any potential gratuity. To sum up the overall valet staff and bell service in one word, "professional". Just so you know, there is a $24 per day charge to valet your car. This includes all day in/out privledges. There is a small sign posted indicating this. Due to the small entrance area, it may not be visible to all. In todays day and age, this is to be expected, especially from a downtown location.
Check in was painless and quick. The issue arose around connecting rooms which I had requested via the company website at time of booking. By the way, I tried to book this hotel at almost every travel web site known to man with no success. Went to the hotel site at the 11th hour and was successful. We were traveling with four children and it was a must to ahve connecting rooms. After what looked like a potential glitch, the front desk manager, came over and handled it, no questions asked. He even upgraded us to the bay view side of the tower and did it with a smile. 
The location of the hotel was great. 10 minutes to Sea World, a few to the San Diego Embarcadero, Zoo and Balboa park. Not far from anywhere. Definitely nothing closer to Petco Park than the Omni if you care to catch a ballgame. They are connected via a walking bridge. You are at the south end of the city's Gaslamp district where there are many restaurants and bars, if you like. The area was very crowded, but clean.
The hotel pool is small and the kids let me know it. However, the staff and the surrounding pool grounds were immaculate. Great service. Not a true test as there were only about 10 people in the pool area. Never the less, a great time. 
We had breakfast at the buufet at McCormick & Schmicks which is located inside the hotel. Not too expensive, but be wary about the drinks. Caveat Emptor, $45 dollars of fresh squeezed orange juice, for 10 servings. Wonder how many oranges we could have bought back home for that amount ? Needless to say, drinks are not included on the buffet menu. Darn good O.J., even for the price. Food was slightly above average, with a nice omelete station. 
Clean, well appointed rooms and bathrooms. Decent size, with magnificent views of the bay and Coronado Island. Very comfortable and open. 
All in all, a great stay. I would definitely return to the Omni on business or with my wife again. Not to sure if I would return with the children. My kids definitley rate hotels based on the pools and The Omni pool was a bit to small for my family's liking. Other than that, Well done Omni.

title: “GREAT Overall”
text: Recently stayed here with my family and found it super from the Location to the Amenities. Just North of San Diego we were able to get in and out of town missing a lot of the headaches and higher prices by staying closer. From I-15 we went down 163 to the Zoo and into Downtown San Diego. It was about a 15 minute ride to Sea World and then heading down Miramar Rd (South of the Hotel) it was about a 20 minute ride to the Beach at Torrey Pines. Shopping was easy to get to whether downtown at Horton Plaza or The Fashion Valley Mall at Friars Ave in Mission Valley. Being North we were also able to sneak out to Carlsbad to the Premium Outlets and Legoland!! Just across I-15 from the Hotel were shopping areas with Grocery store, Drug Store, Restaurants and a Movie Theater. We also saved quite a bit there in Mira Mesa as opposed to being closer in. Also available in the area were Subway, Starbucks and Coldstone. What a perfect place for a family to marshall from for forays into the area. We will be back. The Hotel was quiet and the pool and hot tub was clean. Great job great stay!! People had talked about the freeway noise but we were able to get an inside suite. The noise I heard when I listened for it actually sounded like ocean waves crashing (kinda weird but we've stayed at the beach many times and really the ocean isn't all that quiet). The breakfast was good and I enjoyed the quiet courtyard to read the paper and snack. Thanks and will stay here again!!!

title: “First time in San Diego...”
text: My partner and I have chosen this hotel last year because it´s been located closer to San Diego convention center and Gas Lamp sector. But the neighborhood is very strange and there weren´t no much places to eat or fast food nearby. The management and staff weren´t very friendly and helpful. Good price/quality ratio.

title: “good downtown seattle hotel”
text: Great location with nice upgrades - staff was friendly, room was nice and updated, bathroom and products were nice, very comfortable bed. Got a good deal (mid week), and we got a nice sized room overlooking the city. Nothing necessarily special about this hotel, but we would stay here again if the price was right.

title: “Good location, friendly and clean”
text: This was just an overnighter but access was easy by car from O'Hare and parking was also easy. All staff friendly and helpful. The only issue I had was in attempting to confirm my reservation by phone the day before arrival. I was incorrectly told that I could not confirm my reservation (made through booking.com) because this would breach data protection regulations (...heard that one before..!!.). Managed to confirm eventually but unneccessary fuss. Definitely happy to recommend though. Room very quiet and clean.

title: “Very clean and friendly place to stay. Not to mention really affordable $”
text: Very nice and clean place to stay. Especially for families with kids or people that appreciate a quiet and friendly environment. Initially had a hard time locating the place and would appreciate an option to book online. I’m glad we found this site as it was both reasonable and enjoyable. Would stay there again and recommend with comfort.

title: “Good Location”
text:
This was our first hotel on our Flydrive holiday we were booked here for 4 nights when we arrived weary after a 10 hour flight we were given our room when we opened the door and saw it we could have wept, (bearing in mind that this was an upgraded hotel from our travel company) the room was dark and depressing and you could hardly swing a cat round in the space the last thing you want when you have just been on a long plane journey, straightaway back to reception to have a moan and we were allocated a different room which was much much brighter and much larger than the first one. The hotel foyer is very grand and impressive everyone very helpful, the breakfast was average I have had better, very expensive for what's on offer,we went out for breakfast for our next three days stay. No facility to make tea or coffee in your room but there is free coffee and tea in reception between 4am to 9am which is ok for business men but if you are on holiday it's a bit of a nuisance to have to get dressed and make the trip down in the lift to get a hot cuppa!
Free wifi in reception area but chargeable in rooms which in this day and age should be free everywhere as standard some hotels do it so why not the Freemont! the hotel was very grand the rooms are in traditional style rather than modern, bed was comfortable and a walk in closet was handy as you could store cases in rather than clutter the room.
Downside was a rather large crack in the wash basin which I was surprised had been left, as we all know a crack in anything is a breeding place for bacteria and germs., but after changeing rooms once I couldn't go and change again!
Would we return....No we would prefer a more modern hotel especially the room

title: “Westin Detroit Airport is the perfect start to any travel experience, great service, food and staff.”
text: The best destination for overnight accomodation and great restaurant. The perfect start to any trip. Great staff, excellent rooms, quite and oh so convenient

title: “Great Location for sightseeing historic Philadelphia”
text: The best thing about this hotel is the great location...just 2 blocks from the visitor's center. The room we had was roomy enough for a family of 3. The room might have been renovated recently. Not thrill with the food in the hotel restaurant. Be careful about parking in the hotel parking lot. The car next to our's was broken into. However, I would still recommend this hotel because of it's great location and nice room. We also got a wonderful rate via Hotwire.

title: “Good Location”
text:
My husband had a meeting in the hotel so it was chosen for us. The location right on top of the metro is great! You have to hoof it down the hill and back up to get on but can virtually go anywhere from here. 
Rooms are nice but very small. Few amenities offered in the miniscule bathroom. Lots of service problems. Housekeeping begins banging on doors looking for checkouts by 8 a.m. each morning. Lovely lobby bar but if you arrive at 4:45 p.m. for a drink, forget it until 5 p.m. when they "open up." Employees do not seem at all empowered to offer little exceptions for guests to improve the overall experience. This is definitely a business only hotel!

title: “Great Location and good service”
text:
We were in Jacksonville for the Gator Bowl and stayed at the Garden Inn. The desk and housekeeping staff was excellent and made it a point to make you feel welcome. Very good free coffee, lemon water and cookies were available, however we did not try the breakfast. The area surrounding the hotel had many restaurants and there is a very large theater located next door. There is a nearby mall.
Although it is about 10 miles from downtown, travel is easy both to town and the beach.

title: “Best Hotel Stay in YEARS!!”
text: Cute european-style hotel with lots of character - LOVE LOVE LOVED the whole atmosphere of the place. Tiny trendy and efficient rooms - super comfy beds. We we COMPLETELY blown away by the staff. Everyone was so helpful, friendly and considerate; service was prompt and personal. Walking distance from everywhere you want to be, but just far enough from the tourist stuff to keep the riff-raff from bothering you. Would recommed this hotel to ANYONE!

title: “Wonderful staff, comfortable room, great location!”
text:
Stayed at this hotel for seven nights over the holidays. This was by far the best hotel stay I've experienced in New York City. The staff, from the front desk, to the doormen, to room service and the housekeeping staff were all excellent.
Being from the West Coast, we were on a bit later schedule leaving our room almost every day but our housekeeper never missed a day cleaning our room! She was friendly and professional. Really a lovely lady! The turndown service staff were also great.
We ordered room service dinner one evening and it arrived at exactly the time stated! The room service food wasn't spectacular but acceptable. 
If you're looking for a quick snack, I would recommend 71 Irving. They had excellent chai and their pumpkin lattes were made with real pumpkin--no sugary syrup! Their sandwiches were yummy as well. Really a nice neighborhood place.
This hotel will be our first choice for future trips to NYC provided we can get an affordable rate.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: This was the second time we stayed at the Hotel Manaco. The service was great, location perfect for theaters, shopping and restraunts. The rooms are very clean and tastefull decorated. We've stayed at a few other places in the city and feel we don't need to try out any more. We've spent more and less and haven't found better. Two thumbs up, we'll be back. Suggestion, if you go and plan on returning, it pays to join their "inner circle" we received a bottle of wine, choclate covered cherries and a free upgrade. We felt special :)

title: “Worst experience”
text: Traveling with a colleague to a Meeting. Requested 2 beds. Found we were given a single queen bed in a tiny room. One of us had to sleep on the floor 4 nights. Hotel staff offered minimal/no help. Kept blaming the housing office, and took no action or responsibility. Billed at full price. Worst hotel experience ever.

title: “Charming”
text:
I stayed here for 5 nights and was automatically upgraded to a Junior Suite. It was enormous and very clean. Room service was fast and I highly recommend the Maryland crabcakes!!
I have only one complaint about this hotel, if you bring your own car make sure you get in early as the hotel parking fills very quickly. I was told to park across the street in a parking garage on a saturday night, but when I went to leave the next morning the garage was locked up til 4pm!!
Despite this inconvenience, Id gladly stay there again. The front desk staff are very helpful (Lorraine you're the best!!)

title: “Amazing location, great clean hotel”
text:
My girlfriend and I stayed here over the July 4 long weekend in NY. Hotel was booked as a "mystery" hotel through an online site for a very good price. First off, the location is incredible. You can walk to Central Park, Times square, MoMA, any broadway show, Empire State building, boat cruises, several subway stations etc etc. But since the hotel is off on a side street, its very quiet at night.
The hotel itself is also great. Room was very clean and modern looking, and i think they were all recently renovated. Looks just like the pictures on the hotel website. Staff was friendly and helpful, and free wifi provided. No view out the window, but really while in NYC almost all time is spent outside sightseeing so I didnt care. 
Would definitely return here again.

title: “Beautiful, traditional comfort in mid-town Manhattan.”
text: This is an elegant hotel in a terrific location, near Central Park and great shopping. The rooms are very large by New York City standards, and the staff was friendly and helpful. We only had one meal in the restaurant, and the service there was not so great. The food was ok, but not worth the price. I couldn't even bring myself to order coffee from room service, although i do almost everywhere I stay. Bottom line: This is a great place to stay, but not such a great place to eat, and get your morning coffee after you hit the streets!

title: “serene and romantic corner rooms”
text:
pay the extra $$ and get a corner "wonderful" room. you will get a beautifully serene extra large room with fantastic views and a huge bathroom with separate shower and tub. fabulous shower head, by-the-way! 
when my partner and i arrived, our room was not quite ready, so they gave us two free drinks, and we sipped them under an unbrella on the sandbar you've probably heard about. as you enter the room, a cd is playing to welcome you, which you get to keep (free of charge, yes, i said "free" for you continental breakfast junkies). i had pre-arranged for a boquet of wildflowers to be waiting in the room for my partner, and there they were. and all i had to do was type that request in when i made the reservation. of course, the cost was added to my bill, but you don't get gorgeous wildflowers for "free."
and someone in a previous post mentioned mirrors in the room to make the rooms "look bigger" . . . maybe that's the case in the smaller rooms, but in the corner room, the mirrors are strategically placed in the room and bathroom for . . . let's just say for "other" reasons. trust me. :)
if you come to the W, be prepared to pay lots of $$ for everything, but if you let that go--that's what vacations are for after all--you'll love your stay.
it goes without saying that the bed was dreamy! and while the crowd downstairs is hopping and trendy, your corner room will be a serene and romantic getaway just for you and your lover. :)
enjoy!!

title: “Just Don't Do It”
text:
Nothing worthwhile about this hotel
I checked out 10 minutes after seeing the room and went 2 doors down to the Affini, They would not refund the pre-paid fee, but I was happy just to get out of there.
The other reviews I read have nailed it - it is completely depressing

title: “Really, really, good”
text: My husband & I stayed at this Hotel for 2 nights. We found everything better than imagined, the service from all staff was excellent. The courtesy pick up at the airport, the lady in the gift shop, the receptionist every one was courteous and helpful. The room was large with a sitting area, little kitchen bar and very comfy bedroom. The bathroom was big enough and clean. We are going back next February for a few more nights.

title: “A real letdown over our entire holiday”
text:
Good-
The hotel is in a great location, right off Times Square and central to everything.
The included breakfast and attached bar were also quite nice and convenient. However they were the only good points of the hotel.
Bad-
The service we recieved was quite poor overall. It was hard to get service at the front desk, and when we did have an issue they didnt resolve it for us. The rooms were a lot smaller than they looked and not well thought out with a bit of wasted space. Not good when the rooms are cramped already.
Our air conditioning did not work, so our room was freezing. We complained 3 times to the front desk over our 6 day stay, they eventually gave us a small portable heater that did nothing, even though we were advised we would be upgraded if they couldnt fix it. At the end, nothing was said or done even though we told them again we werent happy with the service.
The showers are a slow drip with no pressure so we couldnt even warm up during them.
Overall, it was probably the worst place we stayed in 2 months throughout America, taking into account the $30 motels we also stayed at elsewhere.

title: “3 Nights in December”
text:
The hotel was ideal for a short break in New York City. My wife and I traveled in December, a few days before Christmas. Although we reached the hotel late in the evening, the staff were quite courteous. Check in was smooth and was done in a jiffy, which really helped since we were tired after a long flight. I chose the hotel because of its proximity to Grand Central Station. Grand Central is a 5 minute walk from the hotel, even when you are carrying luggage. The location is great. Most major NYC attractions are not more than 10 mins away from the hotel. 
Our room was on the 13th floor, and it was comfortable and spacious by NYC standards. The toilets were spacious too with hot water 24 hours. 
The hotel is always buzzing with activity, especially the bar in the lobby area. Great place to get a drink! 
Strongly recommend the hotel.

title: “Good hotel in great location”
text: We stayed at the Washington Plaza in June as part of a combined tour of Washington and Baltimore and really liked the place. We arrived late in the evening and were given two rooms on the third floor which, although spacious and featuring walk-in showers, were not to our tastes due to having seperate beds in each. We then swapped and changed rooms repeatedly over the next few days to find ones that suited us, however the hotel accomodated all our changes and were unfailingly polite the entire time, especially Victoria on front desk. The car parking was limited as we'd hired a Nissan Pathfinder, a car that is at least 6 foot 2 high, however the parking assistants were helpful and explained what special arrangements were in place. The breakfast was nice, albeit expensive, and the pool out front was handy when the sun came out. We'd definitely recommend the Plaza - we even received every parcel we got sent, a first for us in America.

title: “Great Hotel...”
text: Very nice hotel. Rooms appear to be brand new with great bed, furniture, and new LCD flatscreen televisions. Restaurant was outstanding. Unique menu breakfast, lunch, and dinner and much better than expected from a hotel restaurant. Definitely recommend this place if traveling near downtown Dallas.

title: “Very Nice”
text:
We had a very nice time here. The lobby, pool, and room were all great. One negative: fitness center (which is really nice) costs $12/day, though they do waive that if you buy spa treatments that day.
The only other negative is the location: there's a nice outdoor mall next door, but not much else within walking distance, as far as we could tell. But if you have a car then you're fine: it's a short drive to Santa Monica, Rodeo Drive, etc. Try eating outside at McCormick & Schmick's at Rodeo and Wilshire!

title: “Great Area”
text: The Hotel its just OK but needs some upgrade, I stay in the 12 Floor and the elevator wasn't working, The room was comfortable.

title: “It was alright...”
text:
We got this deal on hotwire and would never pay the going rate for this place, which was 279.00/night plus tax. We checked in Memorial Day weekend and the place did not seem too busy. When it was time to check in, they said that our room wasn't ready and asked us to wait 10-15 minutes. We waited and checked back with the front desk 15 minutes later and they said that our room still wasn't ready, and after we showed some fustration the supervisor put us in another guestroom. He forgot to change the number of our new room and we had to return to the front desk after unloading our baggage to the incorrect room and all.
He gave us "complimentary" continental breakfast vouchers for our troubles, but when we used them for the continental breakfast, the waitress explained that it was only a 14 dollar credit per voucher...even though it says "complimentary" on the voucher. The continental breakfast came up to 18 bucks per person including tax, but I would not even pay the difference for this breakfast. The selection was very limited and the food was not that great. It was a good thing that we had a car, cause we mainly ate elsewhere.
Speaking of car, parking is 14 dollars per night and there is no overnight street parking, so you are forced to park in the hotel's lot. Parking is rarely enforced, if at all, and I doubt they will tow any car parked in their lot, because the repercussion from the customer will outweigh the act of towing the car (if that makes any sense). I was never given a parking permit to display on my dashboard even though I checked "self-parking" during check-in, and my car survived through the weekend (and my credit card has not been charged). 
The room was nice. We did not stay in the tower that people here have been talking about. There was no moldy smell. The beds were nice and comfortable. The bathrooms were large. The noise from neighbors were not noticeable, aside from the shutting of the doors. I think there is a fee for the gym and the business center, though we did not check. The pool was alright. I think people preferred the pool to the bay when it came to swimming and laying out. The bay water seemed too dirty.
I think the hotel charges for "housekeeping" gratuity, so we did not tip the maids at the end of our stay. Check-out was hassle-free, like most hotels, but the front desk did not ask if we enjoyed our stay and such. She just said, "You're all set".
This place is definitely a 3.5 star hotel in my opinion, not 4.
P.S.-They will charge you an arm and a leg for any extras, so bring your own snacks and drinks.

title: “Wow!!! What service!!!”
text: From the right on it valet parking to the lightening fast and attentive check in you know you have arrived as you are wowed from the beautiful lobby and furnishings. Once you are in your room things just slow down to RELAXATION! We had a king room with a river view terrace. After I had shed my shoes I noticed a very wet spot in front of the bathroom. When I called the front desk to tell them it was wonderfully resolved by offering us an upgraded room (room on the 4 th floor with a full terrace complete with patio furniture) we were moved and settled in no time. SERVICE is what the Westin understands and delivers. Can't wait to go back.

title: “Why are airport hotels always disappointing???”
text:
Here is the good -
Friendly staff
Great location
Good parking
Nice TV with lots of channels
Here is the not so good-
The room was dirty. I dropped my glasses in a corner off of the bed and had to dig under years of accumulated dirt. I looked around and found every corner to be dirty. 
Long black hairs in the bathroom. Not mine! 
Bathroom needs re-caulking.
The mattress slides off of the box spring.
The carpet is getting worn. Acceptable but worn.
So......your typical airport hotel.

title: “Good place if you need parking and to be close to Moscone”
text:
Attended MacWorld last week & spent 4 nights here. We chose it for the walking distance to the Moscone center and on site parking (and price). The room (Ken Keesey) was quite large so that was nice for a long stay. Very clean and nicely appointed, good bed. Service was friendly and helpful. Wished for more ice machines! Neighborhood has some troubled folks and such but we expected that. Wifi was good but you have to keep logging in :-(
All in all fit our needs and budget.

title: “Marina view was awesome!!!”
text:
We stayed at the Bay Club Hotel as part of a 2 1/2 week trip along the California coast, starting in San Diego. The hotel is conveniently close to San Diego's Lindbergh Field Airport, but far enough away to avoid jet noise. The hotel is very convenient to Old Town and also to Downtown, but it also seems far-removed from all the crowds. It is also conveniently located near Point Cabrillo and Cabrillo National Monument.
We stayed in a Marina view room, upper level with king bed, and we got a very good AAA rate of $159 by contacting the hotel directly. 
It might be helpful to describe the hotel's setting. I didn't quite understand it before I checked in, but was fortunate to have followed the advice of others in selecting a marina view room. This hotel (and others along Shelter Island Drive like Humphrey's) occupies a relatively thin strip of land with the marina on one side and Shelter Island Drive on the other. 
The so-called bay view rooms have a distant view of San Diego, a closer view of San Diego Bay; but they have a VERY close view of the hotel's parking lot, Shelter Island Drive, and the municipal parking lot on the other side of Shelter Island Drive. So, while some travelers may like the "bay view" rooms, my advice is choose the marina view. You can look out from your balcony over a beautiful marina (Marina View)or over a parking lot and/or busy road (Bay View). 
The hotel's breakfast buffet was the best of any hotel on our trip. It included eggs, sausage, bacon, pancakes or french toast, pastries, bagels, fresh fruit, coffee, tea and juices. The great breakfast really spoiled us for the rest of the trip, as did the beautiful view from our balcony.
Hotel management and staff were exceptional. They went out of their way several times to be genuinely helpful to us. We really enjoyed the Bay Club Hotel and would definitely stay there again.

title: “The best hotel downtown”
text: I was so impressed with the Paramount. I have stayed in many of the downtown hotels in Seattle and I have to say that the Paramount is one of the nicest hotels downtown. The hotel is very well kept and modern. The room had a great feel to it and was very good size. The bathroom was amazing. The best part was the bed. Probably one of the most comfortable hotel beds I have ever slept on. If you get the chance to stay at the Paramount don't pass it up. You'll be glad you did.

title: “Comfortable”
text: This hotel is located in Greek Town. Stayed here because I could not find an available hotel on the magnificent mile. The rooms are really nicely done and relatively spacious for a Chicago Hotel. The beds are extremely comfortable. I agree with other reviewers that there isn't much to do in the neighborhood. Lots of really nice restaurants to choose for dining. Great greek food in the area.

title: “great location but very basic”
text:
this hotel was in a great location- close to tourist attractions & Universal Studios. 
The rooms needed upgrading! They were hot & stuffy but clean. The beds had a plastic covering on the mattress which made it hot & uncomfortable to sleep on. The staff were very friendly & helpful. Breakfast was very basic but the pool was nice to relax in. Good place if you're on a budget.

title: “Perfect place to stay”
text: This hotel was absolutely fabulous. The room was spotless, the king size bed was comfortable and the location was magnificent! It was in a very safe neighborhood and within walking distance of great restaurants and shopping, plus the bus stopped right down the street. Gary was a great help in securing our shuttle to the airport and helping us with places to eat. The hotel was very quiet as it was at the end of Lombard street. Great place to stay and the price was right.

title: “Worse hotel ever !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Don't stay here....Seriously!!!!!!!!!!”
text: This is the worse Hotel I have ever stayed in......seriously!!! Got there Friday at 12:00 and was told to wait 30 minutes for the room to be done. Was overcharged $30 for the room (later refunded). Got into the room and after a logn drive wanted to take a shower. Found that the water was going to be off until 6pm. There was a lot of constructiong going on at the hotel at the time. We woke up Saturday morning at 8:00 to the noise of the roof being re done (were not told) about 10 minutes later we get a call saying the water was going to be turned off again and to get up now and shower. Actually we never got the call our friends did and the owner told them to tell us for him. So apart from being woke up we laid in bed for a while trying to relax when the f**kning light falls on our bed. We had to leave the hotel for the entite day to get away from the noise and the fact that we couldn't use the toilet. When asked to refuns money they pretty much said too bad! Worse hotel ever!!!

title: “Best for singles”
text: This hotel is located in a good location for travel to the Loop and other venues and is value priced. Both are important factors in whether you should stay in the hotel. Chinatown is a safe although unique neighborhood of Chinese restaurants and flea markets. It is not a family friendly hotel or neighborhood although ideal for a single or couple who are going to be spending their time outside the room. The room itself is tiny although clean (as in barely room for the bed and a nightstand-small tv no radio or alarm clock). There are no real amemities or services (internet did not work). Overall it is better than Super8 or Motel6 but nowhere near Red Roof Inn or other similar chains.

title: “Great Views!”
text:
Rooms were clean, good sized and great views of Navy Pier. Large bathroom with seperate shower and bath. Newspaper left outside door in the morning. They also have an indoor pool and weight room on 42nd fl.
Check-in was quick. I arrived early and was able to check in at 10 AM too!
I only ate breakfast in the hotel. They have a buffett that is nothing special.
Service was adequate. They do cater to European guests. Concierge helpful with directions and trains. 10-15 min walk to trains and Michigan Ave shops.
One thing to take advantage of if you are flying out of Chicago is to have the front desk print out your boarding passes. SouthWest only allows you to print boarding passes after 12:01 AM the day of your flight, so if you don't have a laptop and a portable printer, you may be looking at 30-45+ min wait at the airport to check in! They were extremely helpful and had it ready for me as I checked out.

title: “Perfect location for LA”
text:
Just a 2 night stay on the way between SYD and NYC.
Excellent location, as on the cusp of W. Hollywood and Beverly Hills as well as directly opposite great shopping venues at the Beverly Centre and the discount stores at Beverly Connection (Marshalls, Nordstrom Rack etc).
The hop-on, hop-off bus stop was also across the street from the hotel entrance, so very convenient for a short stay as ours with no hire car.

title: “Perfect location and friendly staff”
text:
A group of 8 of us stayed here over the weekend. The staff is friendly and helpful. Since it was a birthday celebration, they gave us a suite upgrade. The suites are fairly large, with comfortable beds and pillows. The bathrooms are average size. The room is clean and very comfortable.
The hotel is cute and clean, very up to date, small more like a boutique hotel. 
We took advantage of the happy hour, which for the drink was pretty good. Forget the food, the happy hour food, not worth it. However, their appetizers, calamari, ribs, and pig something was delicious. My husband who is a very picky drinker, was not happy with the bar because they were out of many liquor brands. We did have an awesome time and enjoyed our stay. 
Close to everything, were able to walk, no taxi needed.
Valet parking is available, however the garage right next door is $25 over night parking. Gets full pretty quickly.

title: “very, very good for the price”
text:
I went there for 3 nights with my girlfriend and really enjoyed our stay ! We stayed in a room with a shared bathroom, wich is shared by only one other room. I booked using hostelbookers (297$US for 3 nights) and everything was ok, no problem, no booking mistake. The rooms are very small and intimate. Small sink, small tv, everything is small but quite cute ! The room was very clean, the maid came everyday and we never saw her. The bathroom was also cleaned very oftenly, I never got in a dirty shower. No bugs, no dirt, nothing wrong.
The conditionning air is very noisy but worked fine. There is no kind of free breakfast in this hotel, and I'm not sure that there's an internet access. It is not a place where you'll hang around and where you'll do activities. If you just go there to take a shower and sleep, its very great. It is situated in a very safe burrough of Manhattan and its close to everything by walk : 8 minutes from Time Square, 3 streets from Empire State Building...
There is no better deal in Manhattan, be sure of it, if you're in a budget.

title: “well placed, good value and quality, and quiet night”
text:
Pros:
