Though almost in the Tenderloin, the surrounding area is totally fine, very close to downtown - pretty much is in downtown. Very close to all necessary travel links and shops. Very attractive hotel with generously sized, comfortable and fully equipped rooms. Free WiFi throughout the hotel, though better signal in the lobby. Wine tasting/games etc in the lobby each evening available for free to guests. Free lobby coffee in the morning. 
Though in downtown, very very quiet (you can kind of a hear the traffic a little bit, but very distant). Also couldn't hear neighbours or rooms above and below. Excellent. I was on the 14th floor.
Cons:
none really.

title: “On the Fringe, not.”
text:
Stayed for three nights with 40 university students in mid-November. Five of us came a day early and attempted to check in to two rooms only to find that someone messed up the reservation and we were not booked at all. Panic ensued on both sides of the desk as the hotel was full due to lots of conventions in town. So, here is one of the big tests of how well a hotel is managed. A guest is staring, or more like glaring at the desk clerk demanding justice; and ya, I was that guy. Why should the desk fellow believe me? He could of just blown me off and said, 'sorry, you messed up'. But, it didn't happen like that. Turns out there was one room left with two queens and a foldout couch that could accommodate all of us. The clerk (wish I could remember his name), immediately booked us, dropped the rate, and gave us all breakfast vouchers. Whoa! 
Nice room, nice beds, typical bath, mini kitchen with micro and sink, small clothes space that allowed for kitchen, but it worked. Really clean. Okay, happiness was all around. The next morning two more interesting things happened. First, the hotel gave each of us gift bags with good chocolate and souvenir Seattle mugs, and showed us to our individual rooms that they cleaned up early. Whoa, again! (Oh, and the breakfast was great at the Emerald Grill). 
Then the students' flight was super late due to weather and it messed up the plan for lunch. The desk clerk saw our stress, overheard our conversation and invited the manager of the Emerald Grill to visit with us about making box lunches. I said we only had thirty minutes to which he replied, 'we can do that'. Thirty minutes later 42 box lunches were done and on the bus, including drinks for $10 a piece. Whoa yet again!! I mean, really?
It stayed good. The hotel had our group keys all ready to go, everyone was treated very well, and we had two good morning breakfast buffets that were overseen with great professionalism and care by Sergio. The only downside, and I'm stretching when I say this, is that the location may be two or three blocks into the fringe, or so I thought. As it turns out, it is really easy to walk to most places. May want to cab it to Pike Market, but otherwise lots of restaurants. We used the Urban Spoon app and came up with lots and lots of reasonable choices within easy walking distance. There are also some very upscale eateries nearby too. BTW, all of the employees at this property were very helpful and friendly - day and night. Nice work, Holiday Inn Seattle Center! I'll be back!

title: “Very nice!”
text: We truly enjoyed our stay at the Casablanca. The location was excellent, the customer service very accommodating, and the property was clean and attractive. Our guest room was extremely comfortable and pleasant. We typically stay in one of the large chain hotels such as the Westin or Marriot when we travel to NYC. This was so much nicer, more personal, and more comfortable. We will definately return.

title: “A disappointing experience”
text: This property is in a fabulous location for seeing all the sights. Withing easy walking distance of the White House and all the museums. The lobby of the hotel is very pretty, but the staff is less than helpful and friendly. They messed up our reservation and put us in the wrong room. When we called down to try and correct the situation, the lady got hateful and hung up on us. It was eventually made ok. Our preordered room service was all incorrect and there is construction going on at the the hotel - of which we were unaware. We were awakened our first 3 mornings at 6am by hammering. I complained and they took off $100 from our bill. The room is very small and the bathroom accomodates only 1 person at a time. The bed is very, very soft, so if you require a firm mattress, be prepared to sleep poorly. Overall, if I had to do it again, I would probably bite the extra money and stay at the Willard which is just across the street. We are even Marriott frequent stay members.

title: “An Bargain Stay in Downtown San Francisco”
text:
The Hotel Whitcomb, a historic hotel (temporary site of City Hall after the 1906 SF earthquake) will impress you as you enter the lobby with its marble columns, a huge balcony, crystal chandeliers, wood paneling, and a stained-glass ceiling in the bar area. (I've read that there is still a small jail in the basement too!) There are other remnants of its days as City Hall throughout the building. 
 The rooms that I have stayed in (I've been there twice) are adequate and clean. The few requests that I had (we were missing the TV remote and washcloths) were immediately resolved and the management and staff are extremely pleasant and helpful. It is a hotel that serves its purpose as a place to stay with easy access to public transportation and walking distance to many of SF's theaters and a great diner across the street. Although I would not wander the streets at night because of its location, I was very comfortable and felt safe in my immediate surroundings. 
 My second visit was during the summer, and I noticed that many of the guests were families and tourists waiting for their buses to arrive in the morning. This is an inexpensive (particularly off season) pleasant place to stay especially when you have places to go and things to do!

title: “Great For Long Stays If You Have Transportation”
text: The hotel is close to the airport and center city. The breakfast buffet is nice but that's the only restaurant in the hotel and the area does not provide many others. The rooms are spacious but need updating. There is free internet which is needed since the concierge only works until 10am. I would stay at the Marriott in South Park next time because of the area. This hotel is great for families but you will need a car to get to most attractions. The rooms all have refrigerators and microwaves.

title: “Loved My Stay”
text:
The room is clean and a nice size- I was able to get a king, non-smoking at the end of a hall to avoid a lot of noise. My boyfriend and I were up late, but around 1ish we heard drunk people yelling and because of the way the hotel is designed, all the rooms and floors are in a square and each floor is left open so that whatever floor you are on you can go out into the hallway and look down to see the elevators and entrance way. Also, we put our little tag out to order b-fast in the morning to have ready and when it never came I called room service and they said they never received it and "the kids" must have taken it off. 
Room service is pricey and the French toast cold and the fruit not so fresh, so eat out when possible. Sounds negative, but the check-in people were great, great view of the harbor and walk to North End (try E-UNO!) and to Fanueil Hall without cab ride. If you are coming in through North Station with bags take a cab as its about $5. Only feet from the aquarium as well. You can walk anywhere from here and there is a Starbucks in the lobby- cheaper and better coffee than the hotels (they don’t take Starbucks gc). Also, we spent hours in the hotel bar relaxing with live jazz music, multiple tv's, and great bartenders and drinks. I would stay again. Booked through AAA for $218 plus taxes. See my photos...

title: “Great location & beautiful boutique hotel.”
text:
We stayed for three days in Denver. We loved Hotel Teatro.
The valet staff were very friendly, opened the door when you came back, always a smile on their faces, had good tips about the city and where to shop.
The staff at the Front Desk were nice too. But we only saw them at check in and check out.
The room was very nicely decorated. Clean and bright. Beautiful bedlinnen and details.
I can talk about the bed the entire review, but you just have to experience it. It's huge, it's comfortable, it's beautifull and it's great to sleep in.
The room has an Ihome docking station, LCD TV, free WiFi (not always working), free newspaper and did I mention the fabulous bed :-)
The bathroom has everything you need. A bath and a seperate shower. Not just an ordinairy shower, a rainforest shower. I didn't like it, but I loved it!
The hotel is near Larimer Square, 16th street mall and the convention centre. You can have breakfast at the hotel, but if you only need some coffee and a morning cinamon roll, you can go across the street to Starbucks. You can have dinner at the hotel, but numerous restaurants are just within walking distance from the hotel.
As it was our last hotel in our trip, we needed to use a computer and printer for our online check in for our flight. On the second floor you have a small business centre. There are 2 or 3 computers and a printer. All free to use and free of charge. Very nice.
When we'll return to Denver, we defenitely stay at Hotel Teatro again. Loved it.

title: “A Perfect Stay”
text:
After reading some of the reviews, I was a little apprehensive about booking rooms here for my second stay at a Kimpton Hotel (1st: Hotel Palomar, WDC, Oct '08). Soooo glad I placed more faith in Kimpton's outstanding service than in a couple negative reviews.
The whole experience was fantastic from the moment I pulled up. Yes, the valet parking is expensive (everything is expensive in SD, and Solamar's rates are consistent with the market). Based on earlier reviews, was very careful to reserve a quiet room and specified away from and above pool level. Front desk offered me exactly what I asked for, but also offered an upgraded room away from the pool, but on the pool floor. Made the right choice by taking the upgraded room. The room was around the corner and as far from the pool as possible (#434). Stayed here a whole week and did not once hear a peep from the pool.
Having spent about my share of time at the pool, I can believe that some of the lower pool facing rooms might have a valid complaint about the noise from the pool's bar--especially if they open their windows--so consider requesting a room away from the pool.
One of the reviews complained about thin walls. Don't really know what they're talking about--that wasn't my experience. The side walls of the rooms are as quiet as anywhere else. Yes, you can hear your neighbors when they're talking too loudly in the hallway as they walk by. But that's no different that almost any other hotel I've stayed at (and I'm pretty sensitive to extraneous noise).
If I have to find faults, they are these: (1) The hotel's exterior windows (at least my room's) are getting a __little__ dirty. They open, but not in any way that the hotel could wash them without hiring a professional window washer. This is probably not the sort of thing that would bother most guests, if they noticed it at all (the hotel, firmly in Downtown's center, doesn't enjoy views of the Bay); (2) Got some bad advice from staff member trying to be helpful responding to my subjective questions: was told "nothing to do at the Embarcadero" (it's a nearby park that might be useful for walking your dog at this pet-friendly hotel) and "free parking is tough up by Balboa Park" (that just totally wasn't my experience--maybe I was there on an off day?); (3) Not too thrilled with the light filtering curtain set up--they open & close with rods that are attached to the sheer fabric by a nut & bolt--a pretty flimsy setup that was wearing out in my room. Gee, that's my biggest complaint--closing the curtains. Life must be tough.
Someone mentioned the guests are pretty young here, and that's right. All ages are represented, but the bell curve skews toward the late 20s/30s. During the Saturday night of my stay, Pepperdine U. had a formal event for some of their students, who were staying at the hotel--so my experience may not have been the norm. Surprisingly, heard no ruckus from these kids!
Hotel has a great location in SD's Gas Light District. No shortage of things to do/places to eat. A 5 minute walk from the Convention Center. Oh, the 5-6PM wine hour is a great way to start off a crawl to the nearby restaurants.
Hotel's restaurant (J Six) and poolside bar are very good. Both a little expensive (but still within market prices). Food was at least as good (had both dinner and breakfast here) as 75% of the nearby restaurants, but maybe a notch shy of excellent.
Staff is __extremely__ helpful; if you've never stayed at a Kimpton, you'll just have to understand that this chain sets the standard for service quality. Everyone....front desk, restaurant/bar, valet, housekeeping, and maintenance goes out of their way to acknowledge you and make your stay as comfortable as possible. 
I'd unhesitatingly recommend this hotel to anyone going to stay in Downtown SD. It's not the cheapest hotel around, but it's worth it. There are also other choices nearby if you want to get lost in a megalithic hotel (e.g., Omni; Marriott; Grand Hyatt, all nearby). But if you want outstanding service in a first rate hotel with swanky styling and a great location, but with the classic warm feel of an inn, this is for you.

title: “GREAT EXPERIENCE....”
text: The staff was very helpful and the atmosphere at the hostel was very friendly and enjoyable. I felt safe at all times and the amenities were good. You get what you pay for at a hostel and although it was my first time I had a wonderful time. It was a good place to come back and relax although the beds...were not the greatest..but again you get what you pay for for. Would I got back...yes...but I would get an upgraded room.

title: “Superb stay at the Inn”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Inn New York City in April for 3 nights. It was a special birthday present for me. We were in the Vermont Suite which upon entering was so charming and elegant. There were so many nice touches. The refrigerator was well-stocked and replenished every day. There was a delicious bottle of white wine and a "Best Wishes" chocolate cake upon our arrival. The service made us feel so special. The bed was so comfortable and I loved the fact that all the bed linen was changed daily, including the down comforter. Housekeeping was excellent! The Inn is located on a quiet street on the UWS very convenient to the 72nd St. subway stop. It felt very safe walking in the area late at night. One of our pleasant NY experiences was getting a Gray's Papaya hot dog one afternoon. The hot dog stand is located at 71st and Broadway, just up the street from our Inn. I love NYC! The people are so friendly and warm. Elyn, the manager of the Inn was very helpful and professional. My only complaint is that our stay was too short. Loved, Loved, Loved Inn New York City!

title: “You Get What You Pay For”
text: This hotel has many pluses and minuses. On the plus side the staff is very friendly. There is free parking, however the garage entrance is extremely narrow and only small cars can get in and maneuver inside. The beds are average quality. They also give you tiny soap bars, so I went out and purchased my own. However, they have good shower heads. The TV remote control is old and does not work very well, and I did not get HBO as advertised. There is a small fridge and microwave in the room. They provide free pastries and coffee for breakfast. The locations is good. The price is low by San Francisco standards, but remember you get what you pay for.

title: “Great Price, For the limited budget!”
text:
A friend and I went to Phoenix for a two night stay to attend a game and a concert, both venues were located downtown phx. The majority of hotels downtown were above $100/ night a price my friend or I just could not afford at the moment. Then I came across Americas Best Value Inn, I could not believe the price and it was so close to the venues we were attending. I was a liitle skeptical about staying in the hotel, was not sure what to expect. 
The day of our arrival we were greeted with such great customer service, I thought that was a great start. Then we went to our room, still not knowing what to expect. I was supprised to find the room was clean, it was spacious, had everything it promised microwave, fridge, flat-screen, ac,and internet service. 
My only complaints were that there was no curtain or cover for the bathroom window, our window faced the sun in the evening which made the bathroom very hot in early evening hrs. And the front door had to be pushed hard to be closed properly, which i'm sure would bug the neighbors with the loud slam. Other than that i was pleased with our stay for the price we paid. If you are ever on a tight budget, I would give America's Best Value Inn a try.

title: “Extremely Accomodating Staff Will Go Extra Mile”
text: My trip to DC was for a Class Reunion, and everyone arrived via different modes of transportation. I drove from NC, and once I arrived in the Capitol, I got lost and called the hotel several times for directions. I was lost for 3 hours to be exact. The staff (Josh & Johnny) never lost their patience in giving directions, Josh even used his personal cell, as mine kept cutting off, to get me in. I have traveled as far as Europe, and never met with such polite, patient, and caring staff. They even presented me with a complementary bottle of wine for my troubles, when it is I who should have presented the wine to them! The Bistro Cafe on the premises never disappointed. I would highly recommend this hotel to a friend, and have already recommended Hotel George, to several neighbors--one of whom had come across the Hotel George as a "pet friendly" place to stay when in DC. Accolades to Michael Love, and all the hotel staff, for going out of their way in accomodating our group fwith everything from luggage to umbrellas and canes.

title: “A better Youth-Hostel - Rooftop Terrace closed - Garden closed”
text:
This was one of my huge mistakes on the tour through the States. We expect a lot - we got nothing. As an frequent traveller I stayed in hundreds or thousands of hotels worldwide - but this room is just a bad joke. Totally overpriced for a goodlooking store room.
The facts:
The room: I believe - 9 qm. One Bed - you can´t get out in an normal way. Just a half step between the wall and the bed. They use mirrors to enlarge the room, It is impossible to deposit one or two opened suitcases in the room - or even to arrange your lugagge. You have to wait until your Partner is ready with everything, you can´t use the room in the same time, there is just space for one person or less! 
Behind the bed - there is the Aircon/Heating - so you can´t get sleep or you switch it off. I never felt comfortable. During nighttime it was terrible cold in the room.
The Toilets: Step in, sit down, don´t move. At least, we used the Toilets in the Lobby, they were more spacious then the room we booked.
The Shower: Step in, don´t move, but ok.
Nothing more to talk about. Since october the Rooftop-Bar is closed, even the Garden. So there is not enough public space to hang around and to enjoy the hotel. You just have the LIberary and the Bar inside. Of course the Entrance looks great, its impressing, fantastic architecture. But how much time you spent there? 10 Minutes or less? 
The breakfast is totaly overpriced. Around the hotel there are some nice spots.
At least - the room was clean, the Service ok. Late check-out - just one more hour. 
Save your money - if you wonna have great days in NYC - there are some better places to stay in wintertime. May be, my rating would be better in summer... But - I left NYC absolutly disappointed.

title: “I would not recommend this hotel”
text:
Overall I would not recommend this hotel unless you know NYC. It's over-priced and the service from the staff isn't great. The location, however, is great and close to Times Square and the hotel was clean and modern. Below is some key points from our experience.
- We chose this hotel based on the feedback from trip advisor.
- We were planning to stay in this hotel for 8 nights but ended up moving to the Belvedere Hotel which I would recommend over the Night hotel.
- The room was so small we struggled to store our belongings and 2 suitcases (1 large and 1 medium size). We fell over each other the entire time we stayed there. Luckily we weren't in the room much but the below list just added to our decision to move hotels.
- The bed was a double with a bar at the bottom of it so my boyfriend didn't get any sleep as his feet hung painfully over the edge. So for anyone who is over 6 feet tall I would not recommend.
- The people at the front desk were shockingly bad. This experience has turned me off boutique hotels and we now only book hotels that belong to a chain. There was 1 guy at the desk who was good and in the end we just didn't ask anyone and waiting until he started his shift to ask questions. For example, we were planning to attend the Jets game at the Giants Stadium in NJ so we asked the front desk how they would suggest getting there. They had no idea and then continued to recommend some company they had an alliance to which would have cost us a fortune. They didn't even know where the Times Square information desk was. In the end we found it ourselves and it cost us $20 USD return compared to the $75 USD each way the Night Hotel wanted us to book with them. Another example was when we asked how to dial out of the hotel to make a call. They kept giving us the incorrect instructions so we asked them to put us directly through to the number we wanted to dial they reluctantly did so but it was a struggle to ask them to do anything. Our experience with the hotel continued with several examples like the above.
- The breakfast is very basic. We were happy with the breakfast but just be aware that it's cereal and croissants.
- The hotel is very dark - maybe that's the reason is called the Night hotel. There are very few windows. 
- We have stayed in 4 hotels in NYC including the Sheraton and the Belvedere and the Night is at the bottom of the list.
- I enjoyed their Bee Nice products supplied in the room (shampoo and moisuriser).

title: “bad hotel”
text: in our room there was somebody. one person was there. we booked for two. the rooms are so small for two. we get a new one, but it was more expansive. it has system. the noise from the other side was very loud. we stay there for 7 days. the cleaning service is very very bad to. like all at this hotel. for your money you can get better ones.

title: “It's New York”
text:
Went to New York as a surprise 20th January for 4 days - Travelled by Virgin Atlantic which was lovely.
Arrived JFK about 12.30 got a coach to Hotel was first drop so much better - next time would just get a taxi as similar costs. Booking in to the hotel was very easy lots of people available to assist. Room on 22nd floor was pleasant enough clean and comfortable.
Went out did all the tourist bits Empire State Building lovely but cold on two sides as this was the weekend that it snowed on Saturday. Statue of Liberty (unable to go inside as redecoration being done) but views from the ferry as you pull out from pier of Manhattan beautiful. Central Park in the snow wonderful - a big thank you to the runner who asked if we wanted picture taken of us sooooo nice. Time Square - not square haha.
Hotel very helpful with anything we required and they have a quick system to obtain your boarding passes for return flight.

title: “Great location, Very nice staff”
text: As with the other reviewers, the hotel is "average" but it is clean and in a great location. The location is everything. For sure, you can't beat it. I don't want to gloss over the Hilton service as per usual. It is - but Hilton should be proud. The staff at Fisherman's Wharf are very good. The front desk is well run and very helpful. The hotel room was clean due to the attention the room staff paid to their duties and would like to commend the restaurant staff as they were diligent and helpful. Overall, I would stay at this hotel again if I visited San Francisco. The staff really contributed to our fantastic holiday there. Thanks Bill.

title: “Great in many ways!”
text: This hotel was totally comfortable, clean and accommodating. The staff couldn't be nicer! Very nice full breakfasts in the morning added to the positive atmosphere. I truly recommend this as a wonderful place to stay! I only wish all my business travel met these standards!

title: “pleasant surprise with the kitchen”
text:
This was the first hotel we stayed upon landing in USA.
I purposely chose this hotel so that my family have a good rest before we start our 1 month US tour.
Since I did all the booking, and looked through so many hotel websites..did not remember that the State Plaza suites have kitchen in there.
So when we got into the rooms, my mum and aunt was so happy to see fully equipped kitchen.
And since there's a supermarket next door, they were able to cook great food for the next 2 days we stayed there.
Internet was free in the room, n you can print for free in the small computer room near the lobby.
Beds were very comfy and plush.
So many tv channels to watch.
All the attractions were within walking distance.
Definitely a great hotel to recommend. a great start to our US holiday.

title: “Great place in a great spot but some improvements are necessary”
text:
Stayed 6 nights at the Affinia Dumon with the family. The hotel is superbly located, a few blocks from the Empire building and from the United Nations. The hotel itself is very clean and the staff was very much welcoming and pleasant to interact with. The beds are fantastic, sheets were crisp and fresh and the shower was great, hot with amazing pressure. 
I would give the hotel 5 stars but some issues need to be underscored.
With so many hotels in NYC, each one must provide exceptional amenities, especially if they aim at charging over $300 per night for a room. Here are the issues we believe the hotel must work on
1) No air conditioning in the corridor/hallways. What's up with that? As soon as you leave your room to get an elevator, you are stuck in a corridor with no ventilation. None at all. The air is stall and humid. For what purpose? Save a few bucks? When you are in the $300/n range, you cannot skim on stupid things like that.
2) The air conditioning in the rooms seems old and is not efficient enough, or the insulation of the building is not good enough. When NYC gets very humid and hot as it was when we were there, the air con unit could simply not keep up. There was water dripping from the unit but the room remained warm. Not as hot and humid as the corridors but still warm with some humidity, which made the nights unpleasant.
3) Free wifi. If you provide a service to your clients, even if it is free, provide a good service, or don't do it at all. At the Dumont, the free wifi is terrible. Just plain and simply terrible. Not spotty. Not slow. Just bad. I gave up and went to Starbucks. THAT's a good wifi service.
So would I recommend the Affinia Dumont? If you are looking for a very well located hotel, yes. Can the Affinia Dumont play with the best hotels in NYC? Not at all. There are issues that need to be resolved

title: “" FANTASTIC HOTEL IN GREAT LOCATION "”
text: we stayed at the Edison Hotel last week for 5 nights 9th - 14th and enjoyed every minute of it - so much so that i will come back there again - everyone from the doorman to reception and all the staff were so nice and helpful - had breakfast in the Edison Cafe every morning that kept you going all day and a drink in the Rum bar at night to unwind after the days travel. Stayed on 18th floor in a nice room facing the back of hotel - the rooms were cleaned every day and plenty of fresh towels. Times square was right on the doorstep and very central to all the local attractions. All i can say is keep up the good work - no complaints from us and most definately will be returning. Coffee and tea making facilities would have been nice in the room but there is a Starbucks just across the road - i hear they are doing up all the rooms which will have these facilities included in future.

title: “An absolute hole”
text:
This hotel is an absolute hole and was really disappointing after it was recommended to us by our travel agent. The rooms are incredibly small, the bathrooms are extremely filthy, the service as a whole was terrible (except when we checked out), the air conditioners are so noisy you need earplugs to sleep, my wife has been bitten to death by bedbugs, the shower curtain and tiles were mouldy and black, the room smelt mouldy, the bed was not made up in two days, the towels are small and so old you can see through, the power sockets were falling out the walls, the mini bar sucked, you have to wait on average 2 mins for a lift, the staff walk around with loud blearing walkie talkies which wake you up in the night (unless you wear earplugs), the bed was radiating heat all night (PROBABLY THE BED BUGS), the thermostat in the aircon didn’t work, the TV reception and sound was dismal, the front desk is chaotic all the time, no one offered to help with our luggage, the Internet service didn’t work (thank god for StarBucks), our toilet was broken and did not flush, we found cockroaches in the bathroom over two consecutive days and experienced cold showers.
Overall this ruined our arrival to New York and we found cheaper accomodation with far better service and facilities at a cheaper price 4 streets away.

title: “Good Location - Nice Hotel”
text:
We came to SF during the Marathon this past summer. My husband and I had a room and we also traveled with friends (who were the actual marathon runners!) and their children.
The atomosphere/decor at the hotel was nice. Somewhat modern and in good shape. The rear area of the lobby had 3 computer stations, a TV, tea and coffee. 
I hear there is a nice rooftop area, however, we never made it up there! It's adjacent to the pub next door, which we had a light lunch at after the marathon.
A plus is the chilled water stations when you exit the elevators. You can grab fresh bottle water 24/7.
Our room was small, but just enough for the weekend. The bathroom and closet doors were this neo-metal style - fun and different. The bathroom was equipped with a shower (no tub). There is free Wi-Fi throughout the hotel -bonus!!
Our friend's room had a mini-living room area (not seperate) with a pull out sofa bed for 1 and small table. They had a bathroom w/ tub and a small kitchenette area (sink, micro, coffee maker and small fridge).
This hotel is within walking distance of the Embarcadero Shopping area, the Ferry Station and Market Street. We walked to Union Square and could have walked to North Beach as well.
It's not a touristy area, so after 5/weekends, it's a bit quieter. But easy to get to all of the good spots. 
I recommend this hotel for a short weekend stay (for tourists) and definitely for members longer stays.

title: “Great location, in need of repair”
text: Close to everything but could not get the AC to work. Maintenance changed it out and the second one did not work. Slept in an 80 degree room and they would only comp breakfast which was a hassle. Stay somewhere else.

title: “Very nice!”
text:
Very nice hotel. A bit outside town but right next to Old Town. Check in was fast, the room was really nice, the beds were the best we slept in during our entire stay!!
They have a very good service. We were a bit early for check in, and they let us change into our bathing suites so we could use the pool untill our room was ready. 
Breakfast was average.

title: “Superb location & welcoming staff made for an excellent stay”
text: I stayed at the Milennium Hotel Broadway over this past weekend for a girls weekend and was very satisfied. First of all, the location is perfect. If you are in town to see a show, as we were, you will be able to walk everywhere you need to go. It is also close to Carmine's, a famous NY Italian restaurant. From the moment we arrived, the bellhops, concierge, and valet parkers all made us feel welcome and were very helpful and accommodating. We arrived before check-in so our bags were held in storage until later in the day. We were hardly in the room at all because it was a one night stay and a gorgeous weekend so we were out and about a lot. The rooms were clean, updated, and quiet. Huge flat screen TV, mini bar, two double beds. room darkening blinds, nice views. The bathrooms were also very clean and fairly updated. The only negative aspects I can comment on were the bed linens. While the sheets were fine, there were no blankets, only a thin, slippery bedspread, about the weight of a duvet cover without a duvet inside. And though my bed was rather firm, I would definetly stay here again...in fact, I cannot wait to go back!

title: “Mixed”
text:
We had some mixed reactions with this hotel. We originally booked it because we wanted a different experience from Midtown. However, we ended up a bit disapointed. Its tucked into a boring corner of Chinatown (maybe its technically SoHo, but the surroundings and the writing on the hotel let you know its Chinatown)
We ended up having to cab it quite a bit (you can also subway to most locations within 1-6 blocks) as there was a lack of restuarants and entertainment in the area.
Rooms were small and the rooms were a little dingy. But it was cheap at $160. Don't think I'll stay there again, I'll be sticking to the Midtown and the UWS.

title: “Disappointing for the price”
text:
Over $200 for a single room. The location is not bad - a block off of Pier 39. An easy walk. But I kept trying to shut the window because the sounds from the street were so loud (2nd floor). The problem is, the window was already shut!
Service is fine. Hotel seems a little dated. Comfortable and clean, but I expected much more from a Sheraton.

title: “Convenient for cruise terminal and convention hall”
text: Stayed at the Westin Boston Waterfront for one night, before departing on a cruise from the nearby passenger cruise terminal, so we didn’t need much. We arrived by train, which is about a $6 taxi ride away, or about a mile, for those without baggage. The hotel lobby is impressive and elegantly simple. The room was small-ish, though nicely decorated. Views from the room (facing downtown) were panoramic. If there were any elite amenities for top-tier status, I couldn’t tell it (including any consideration for a late checkout). If you’re sailing from the cruise terminal, you can’t pick a better location; if you want to see anything in Boston other than the convention center, you’ll find this place out of the way and not well-situated. Finding restaurants within a couple of blocks was impossible, so plan on eating on-property if you stay here.

title: “Very upset!!!”
text: The sanctuary is close to time sq. The staff is very friendly. The room is a little small but the rooftop bar is great. The rates are reasonable. The only problem I had was the transportation from the hotel to the airport. I asked the doorman named George that I was checking out so he can setup a cab for my departure. I asked him for a yellow cab but he insisted to get me a black cab which at the end overcharge me and I had a heated argument with the driver. I called the hotel to complain and nothing was resolved. I want to warn all fellow travelers to insist a yellow cab instead of the black cars so they don't over charge you.

title: “High level service and great ambiance!”
text: This is the second time I stayed at this hotel and each time has been the same high level service and great ambiance.

title: “great value for upper east side”
text: Stayed for 4 nights in feb 2009. Great location on UES. Rooms very large, sort of a junior suite, and well appointed except for chintzy curtain fronted armoire/closet. Bed and pillows were extraordinary, one of the most comfortable hotel beds I've ever experienced. In this day and age internet access, whetehr wired or wi-fi should be included in the price of the room.

title: “One Word - Magnifique!!!!!!!!!!! 5 Star Experience”
text: My teenage daughter and I just spent her Spring Break week at the Sofitel. From the moment the car stopped in front of the hotel we were treated like royalty. Every guest is greeted as a welcomed loved one returning "home" from a journey. The greetings, smiles, and genuine attention to every service need or request underscores the superelative service of this hotel. I work in the travel service industry and travel to NY often and have stayed in many lovely hotels in and around Manhattan. With all of the state of the art bedding that is touted by other hotel chains, Sofitel's is far and away the most comfortable. I have chronic lower back pain and can only sleep on any mattress 5 hrs at a time. Well, I slept a full 8 hours on their wonderful bed w/o any kinks, crimps, or negative physical impacts. I fully intend to try and buy one of these beds for myself. My finicky and highly pampered teen ADORED the hotel. The internet access, the friendliness of the staff, and the superb room service - the food is fabulous- had her raving from the moment we entered the room. The delectable Lenotre chocolates each guest receives each evening helped to seal the deal that this is now the ONLY place my daughter wants to stay when we visit NY. Daniel -the best doorman on the planet, Ronald- The most informative and debonaire reservationist ever, Nick -the spot on bellman, and the the classy and helptul Concierge all underscore the serious commitment that the Sofitel makes to serving their customers. The lovely location, critic's choice cuisine, blissful bedding, and stupendous staff all underscore the Sofitel's universal appeal. Make the Sofitel your home base in NYC.

title: “New Hotel... Very modern... Good Service”
text:
We've been at the Dream DownTown for a meeting this week. Everything in the hotel is very new. It has been open for only 6 months. Everything works with buttons, the minibar has movement sensors so that if you move something more than 60 sec it is automatically charged on your bill... Every light has a dimer. It is great except that the bed light works with every other so if you turn out the lights and want to keep the bed light to read, you cannot. 
There is a DJ in the lobby at night and a NightClub at the 12th floor. The restaurant is really beautiful and cosy even if the rates for breakfasts are a little high... The Continental Bkfst includes a fruit juice (100% natural, and really good) + 1 tea or regular coffee but does not includes an expresso or hot chocolate... 
The staff is very friendly and polite. It is a pity that such a new hotel does not have a service elevator... you meet the room service, the utilities man with conference tables and chairs in the public elevators... 
The beds are heaven!!! you feel like you are in a cotton cloud... It is so soft!!! maybe a little too soft... 
The TVs have a special channel to see your bill but mine was blank. I had to go down to the reception to check it. 
I missed the bathtub... only a shower.
Overall a very good stay in a great hotel, only if the alarm won't have set off every other minute during the meeting...
It is close to everything, DownTown... We spent a good time there.

author.location: Santa Barbara de Samana, Dominican Republic

title: “Classy hotel in quiet city centre location”
text: I've stayed in quite a few of the Swissotel properties and this is definitely one of the better ones. It is also the best hotel I've stayed in in Chicago (this being about my 10th visit). It is located in the city centre but being in a dead-end street overlooking navy pier means that it is quiet and with a great shore line view. Check-in, staff, rooms and furnishings are all up to standard but they are all with a European/Swiss touch which is a welcome relief when compared to some of the busier, more American properties in town. Lifts work and very efficiently well thanks to you having to select your floor and then told which lift to take (rather than the usual simple up/down button). The beds are really comfy and better than the more well-known "heavenly" beds of Westin. Will definitely staff here again when next in town.

title: “Great premium room...stay away if you're a foodie.”
text:
Had a one night staycation for our wedding anniversary. We took advantage of the All play no pay package of a one night's stay with 2 massages, dinner, and breakfast included for ~$400. 
We were upgraded to a premium room (in the Boulders). Room was on 3rd floor -tastefully decorated with a great view of the golf course. Very private, big room with a big bathtub and separate standing shower. Very clean.
Spa experience was okay. The massage treatments were good but the waiting/sitting area for before and after your treatment was too small and had high traffic. The person bringing in the towels as well as some of the other employees used this door to the outside to frequently go in and out. This isn't relaxing considering the air is cold outside and you are sitting in your robe (with nothing else on underneath). Hot tea was lukewarm and never checked. Steam room and sauna was nice - gender specific.
Got dressed and went to the Bizcocho for dinner. We were looking forward to it and this was one of the reasons why we booked a stay at this hotel. It did NOT live up to our expectations or any of the previous reviews that we read. El Bizcocho is no longer a 5 STAR restaurant. This was very disappointing considering the reputation of this restaurant. It was more of a typical hotel restaurant and less like a special occasion one. The menu on the website is not accurate since many of the dishes were not offered and the tasting menu is no longer available. Service was slow and lukewarm at best. We actually couldn't wait to leave the dining area. 
Breakfast was a pleasant surprise at the Veranda. Had a "Border" omelet that was excellent. Service was more attentive than it was at El Bizcocho the night before. We maybe should have gone there for dinner (?).
Overall the grounds were beautiful and nicely decorated for the holidays. We liked our room and the grounds but were very disappointed in the food~

title: “The place in NY if you are bringing the kids”
text:
This hotel is everything you could want if you are traveling with children or teens. The location is in the heart of the theater district, recently renovated with three star amenities. it's clean, and nicely appointed with granite counters in the bath. Carpets and paint are new and updated.
The rooms are great if you have kids. King bedrooms have separate TV. Living area has a pull out sofa that will sleep 3 small ones, or two teens, with their own TV. Living area also has a small fridge
and bar area.
Internet access and fitness center are free of charge, and rooms are quiet.
If you are looking for a clean, comfortable and spacious (by NY standards) hotel, this is it.

title: “Staying in a rock star hotel”
text: I've pretty much spent more nights at the Phoenix over the past two years than most people spend at hotels in a lifetime. There is a reason I keep coming back: the amazing staff. Sure the central location is killer (right next to Saigon Sandwich!), the parking included (a bonus), and the new bar/resto (Chambers) serves up some delicious food. But it's the attention to detail and the friendliness of the staff that have me coming back to this Joie de Vivre establishment every time. It's not for everyone, but it's definitely a great place, at a great price. What more can you ask for?

title: “Great rooms but the beds”
text:
Great hotel and very efficient staff, the rooms are great but we all had a poor sleep due to discomfort in both beds. They are very soft with huge covers. Other that that very close to LAX with a free shuttle service , also close to car rental and service sttations for those returning cars
Shame about internet fee's

title: “Friendly helpful staff and clean rooms”
text: Stayed at this hotel, along with a group of out of town guest, for our daughter's October wedding. After reading several negative reviews we were alittle apprehensive about our stay however we were greeted by friendly, helpful staff at the desk and were pleasantly surprised at the cleanliness of our rooms. Whenever any of our party had a problem it was taken care of in a very efficient manner. The complimentary breakfast offered waffles,bagels, pastries, cereals, fruit, juices etc. More than enough to start your day! The housekeeping staff were friendly and kept the beds made and the towels plentyful. Wherever you went in the hotel, down a hall, pool, laundry area, reception area everything was neat and clean. Sea World, the Zoo, the mall, Target, and a ton of resturants are only minutes away. This hotel is located at the very end of the street and there is some road construction going on that you have to manuever around to get to the hotel but we had a very pleasant stay and would definitely stay here again.

title: “OK, but it wasn't all that...”
text:
I stayed at the Alex Feb. 18-21, 2012 room 504
THE GOOD:
Location: One can walk to the UN Building and Grand Central Station as each is just a couple of blocks away. A bit further out, but still walkable are Times Square/Broadway, Rockerfeller Center, St. Patrick's Cathedral, the Chrysler Building, and much more. 
The Price (via Priceline): I booked via Priceline after researching a bidding strategy via a priceline bidding strategy messageboard so I know I got the lowest possible Priceline price. For this hotel it was a steal possible only because the UN was not in session. However, I wouldn't want to pay rack rate or rates offered on other websites. 
Room Size: Excellent by NYC standards. (Standard room)
The Lobby Staff: The bellmen, doormen, porters, etc. were excellent. I feel bad that didn't always get a chance to tip them, etc. Nice people and very helpful. Desk staff mostly ok.
THE AVERAGE:
Decor: It is average for a 4* hotel. Interesting but nice. The room could use an update. It shows a fair amount of wear. Some chipped tile/tub in the bathroom. Tub is nice and deep but narrow. And you have to have some muscles in your fingers to flush the toilet. Does not look nearly as nice as the photos online. We had a view of 45th and the building across the street. Boring and a little noisy.
Beds: Comfortable, but nothing special. I requested 2 beds but did not get them (not guaranteed by priceline but it would have been nice.) 
Consierge: We asked for suggestions on a restaurant that would be entertaining and for two teens and 3 40somethings. He was challenged by this. In NYC with 1000s of restaurants, a consierge should be able to name numerous restaurants to choose from. One of his first offerings was Bubba Gumps. Unfortunately, 2 of us were from Louisiana and Bubba Gump's does not fly with our expert knowledge of such southern/gulf cuisine. We settled for Brother Jimmy's BBQ (ok even tho, again, 2 of us were from the south). He said it would be lively. Well, lively apparently meant really really loud music with happy hour with tons of 20somethings in the bar area. So, not appropriate when we wanted something "lively" for teens. However, the food very good. 
THE BAD: 
Room Temperature: It is winter and the heat is ON. The room was generally too warm for us (72'-75'F) when healthy sleep temp is 65'F. The only way to cool the room is open the window but then there is the street noise. 
Housekeeping: Generally clean, but... I did the "I'm in NYC so I need to check for bed bugs check when I arrived (I found NONE an probably no evidence of any.) and noticed some small blood stains (?) on the underneath side of the white comforter/duvet. I did not complain as I always take it off the bed immediately anyway because I don't trust hotels to change them between guests. The Alex might, but I do this at all hotels. Seriously, how often do you see them on the housekeeping carts? Housekeeping didn't leave enough toiletries or replenish when needed, in my opinion. After the first day, I didn't bother to tip because of this and an incident (read below).
THE WORST:
Housekeeping: On my final day there, I had the "Do Not Disturb" sign on the door. I did not have the inside locks enaged because my friend just left the room within the last half hour or so. I was in the room getting dressed after a shower. So, I was in a towel. Guess what happens? I am a female, and a male housekeeper knocks on the door and walks in unannounced before I have a chance to see who it was through the peep hole (I thought it might be my friend returning with Starbucks or something). And yes, there I am barely in a towel. COMPLETELY INAPPROPRIATE. COMPLETELY UNACCEPTABLE. Had he said "housekeeping" or waited a minute before opening the door or READ THE DO NOT FRIKIN DISTURB SIGN the situation could have been avoided. NOT happy at all about this. When I checked out, the desk agent didn't ask how was my stay, otherwise I would have reported this incident. But, I knew I had this public forum to speak.
OVERALL:
The Alex Hotel isn't bad and if you chose to stay there you will probably be perfectly fine. In my case, it was simply not as positive as I hoped for or expected given the mostly positive reviews. I had a mostly ok stay for a decent price. But, I left a bit disappointed because I had higher expectations.

title: “Nice place for family”
text: What a great enjoyable hotel stay. The room was spacious and comfortable, especially by New York standards. The bed was fabulous and the pillow menu thing was unusual but fun. We stayed with our two little girls and had a great experience. It's a short walk to Rockefeller, which was fabulous for the Christmas season. Overall, it's not as trendy as the boutique hotels, and doesn't have the grandiose lobby of the giant luxury hotels. What it has is a top notch staff that went out of their way to help us whenever we needed anything (special thanks to the doorman that helped us get a taxi in the sleet and rain to go to the ballet), a comfortable bed that I miss and an atmosphere that everyone can feel comfortable in.

title: “Wonderful”
text: This hotel lived up to all the wonderful reviews. Great value and the location was great. I would highly recommend.

title: “LOVED IT”
text:
10 day business trip in LA and had the opportunity to stay here and could not have loved it anymore than I did. This hotel is just great in all aspects: CLEAN, great bathrooms, the best bed ever, spacious room with a refrig and excellent work space. I really liked the room design and layout.
The concierge lounge was THE BEST I have ever been in with a huge selection at both breakfast and evening. They also had a great selection of high end wines during cocktail hour which was really nice! 
The lobby scene is pretty interesting to sit back and watch with an Illy Coffee from the kiosk in the lobby. Many star seekers and actual stars ( if you are into that). I was there during the VMA's so saw a few myself.
Great pool area with a live DJ the couple times I went. Certainly not relaxing, but pretty funny to watch some of the younger set inaction.
If you are middle aged and not into the younger scene this probably isn't a good hotel for you, it is a younger crowd and can get a little obnoxious after a while. The weekend seemed to be filled with groups of people partying and a little out of control, I found it all amusing. 
The location is excellent for highway access and I found the traffic to be minimal the entire time I was there. The valet service is top notch and if you call ahead your car is waiting for you!
I really liked this property and LOVED the beds and cleanliness, will be back!

title: “Great location but you should get more for the money.”
text: Great location but on arrival the room had items from previous guests. After paying over $300/night they wanted to charge an extra $15/day for WiFi access. Why can you get free access at Motel 6 and not at the Hilton?

title: “Bday Weekend”
text: I stayed here for my daughters bday weekend with her friends, we had a awesome time not to mention that Zida at the front desk was the face of customer service knowledgeable and kind. I would surely stay here more often then spending a ton of money at the Hilton

title: “The food was terrible!”
text: We stayed at the Embassy Suites from 3/13 thru 3/17. The room was comfortable and clean. However, the buffet breakfast was not edible. The food (eggs, potatoes, pancakes)was cold and it was only 9:00 a.m. The link sausages were overcooked and the biscuits were hard and not edible. The food from room service was tasteless as well. I have been to several Embassy Suites throughout the country and the food was great. This hotel does not care how the food is prepared for guests. If you are looking forward to a good buffet breakfast and a good room service meal, skip this hotel!

title: “Beautiful Room, Exceptional Staff”
text: We booked our room at the Swissotel on Hotwire for $88 (unbelievable rate!) and were extremely impressed with the Swissotel. The staff was so polite and catered to our every need. The room was oversized, clean, and had a large bathroom. We had a partial view of Lake Michigan, which was an added bonus. On the 42nd floor, they have a spotless workout room and pool with a view of the city and lake from 3 sides. Spectacular! We sat in the hot tub and looked down on Navy Pier. We can't wait to go to the Swissotel again!

title: “Wish I stayed longer”
text:
This has been one of the nicest hotel stays for me, this year. I stayed at the Crowne Plaza for a conference. I stayed there because the conference host hotel was booked. The decor overall - lobby, room, etc. - was very tasteful and classy. The size of the double room is about standard. The workout room had at least 7 cardio machines (with multiples of the same, e.g. 3 treadmills) and several televisions placed in between them. Most hotels that I have stayed in just had about 3 machines (one treadmill, eliptical and bike) and one television. Downside: If you are looking to be in the middle of all the Riverwalk action, this is not the place for you. The active section of the Riverwalk is walking distance but the area in which the hotel is located is desolate at night.
I would definitely recommend this hotel and stay here again.

title: “Denver Airport Homewood Suites”
text: Excellent location (12 miles) from the Denver International Airport with free airport shuttle service. As usual, great breakfasts and evening meals. The highlight was that "standard" Hilton reservations could not give a government rate that matched the per diem rate but the hotel manager, Ms. Sandra Montano, was more than willing to match the per diem rate. Also, even though the hotel was built in 2008, it still looked brand new and the room furnishings were comfortable and not worn. One special touch was the evening meal that inlcuded dessert, and the night I stayed they served apple pie. Certainly they go the extra mile.

title: “Good Upper West Side hotel”
text:
As native New Yorkers currently living abroad, we wanted to stay in our former neighborhood (The Upper West Side). The Lucerne is well located on 79th St & Amsterdam. Close to multiple subway lines and away from the typical tourist areas (Times Square & 5th/Madison Avenue). 
The hotel room was clean and comfortable. Yes, the room is on the small side as one would expect in NYC, but it was not tiny...there was a good closet with a safe and a decent-sized bathroom with hairdryer. We stayed in a room in the back with no view to ensure a quiet stay (I would recommend this as 79th st and Amsterdam are quite busy).

title: “Great choice for families”
text: Stayed during family trip to Chicago. Great experience! Clean and comfortable. Location is unbeatable, we walked nearly everywhere. Would certainly stay again.

title: “Great location with good accommodation”
text: It was the third time my wife and I spend a couple nights in this hotel, but was the first time with our children. The Hotel is ideal located close to Universal Studios as well to the famous Walk of Fame, Hollywood and Beverly Hills. We had no problems with street noise was well with cleaning stuff. Of course some pick people will may complain about the carpet cleanness, but just think, we were on vacation! Use a sandals and done! The Hotel stuff were helpful and we definitely have no complains at all. The breakfast is simple but at same time sufficient to keep you ok until lunch time. Near to the Hotel you also find restaurants, fast food chains and most of all a supermarket (Vons), really important when traveling with children! I do recommend this Hotel for people that want to enjoy outside and aren’t to pick with details (for this kind of people I suggest the Hilton at Universal, that costs at least the double).

title: “Great Hotel!”
text: The staff here are very nice. My friend and I stayed in one room and it was the perfect size for us. The full size kitchen was also nice to have even though we didn't end up using it much. It was awesome being so close to SoHo and even a Whole Foods! Great hotel!!

title: “Fabulous location, beautiful hotel--mediocre service”
text: Perfect location in Union Square within distance to everything! Beautiful old historic hotel. Rooms are small but have great character. We always try to stay at a Westin because of the heavenly bed and the reliability of it all---this hotel met those expectations. However, this hotel (with the exception of the Bourbon Steak restaurant and the Clock Bar) is lacking in customer service. You are just a number. Before arriving, I received four emails about my gold starwood status, free amenity and my ability to use instant starwood points. Their marketing department knows all about this--the hotel does not. I had to ask for my free internet service and make a special request to three people to actually use the instant points. Frustrating but we still had a fabulous time!

title: “Great location, good decor .... book a room high up!”
text: We stayed at this hotel for 3 nights and loved the location and the feel of hotel but have to recommend you ask to stay in either a room at the back of the hotel with a brick wall for a view .... or very high up on street side. ..... We were keep awake the first night by the cable cars and ding ding ding ..... would recommend though ... fun boutique hotel right in the middle of it all!

title: “Always good for business or pleasure.”
text:
I've stayed in this hotel many times and love the location -- both for fun and business. It's just blocks north of Times Square, just blocks south of Central Park and an easy walk to Radio City Music Hall, NBC studios or to the theater district. 
Just about all the rooms are newly renovated. Room service is always fast if you're working and cannot get out. The complimentary breakfast for Starwood members and those willing to pay for it is one of the best in New York or anywhere for that matter. The fine expresso machine, fresh berries and good pastry selection always gets me moving! 
The lobby is inevitably filled with energy: think excited European tourists, business suit clad executives, families from the Midwest and everything in between. The staff is uniformly helpful though on occasion the front desk is simply overwhelmed. Rooms above the 15th floor are quiet at night. 
On the down side, early check in is often difficult due to the fact that this hotel is almost always full the night before. But, if you have work to do you can hang out in the Starwood lounge while working. 
This can be a costly hotel though so check the rates and then determine if location is your crucial deciding point. If so, then this is the place for you.

title: “A wonderful choice...”
text: Our family was extremely pleased with our stay at the Affinia 50. While the bathroom was small, there were quality toiletries. Our room was spacious for a family of 4, especially in a city famous for tiny rooms. There was also a nice "club room" on the second floor. We particularly appreciated the ice cold water with a hint of citrus in the lobby. The staff was very welcoming and had cupcakes delivered as a surprise for our daughters birthdays. We hope to return to the Affinia 50 in the future.

title: “Great Stay!”
text: I never make a hotel reservation without checking the property out on TripAdvisor. So, when I was looking for a hotel for a quick getaway the weekend before Valentines Day, I read the reviews for various hotels (even those where I have Top Tier status and could stay for free) and it was tough with the various reviews about bed bugs, rude and inattentive hotel staff, etc.; none of the things I wanted to contend with on a romantic getaway. So, when I read the reviews for The Back Bay Hotel and most were positive, I booked via Expedia. I was not disappointed! From Sean who greets you on the street, the valet team, Jaime in the Stan Hope Grill, the concierge who tended our bags in the absence of the bellman and the front desk reception staff, first impressions are lasting. The property is well-maintained, the King Suites roomy, clean and quiet and the artwork and sculptures throughout the property are pleasing. Every detail is taken into consideration even down to the potpourri in the ashtray section of the hallway waste receptacles! Our stay was further enhanced by the little extras like complimentary wi-fi, the heated towel rack, stereo system and upscale toiletries in our suite. Breakfast in the Stan Hope Grille was really good and Jaime was very attentive. The location is perfect to explore the city on foot, just blocks from Copley Square. The valet rate is $42.00 per night. Cuffs Bar located on site is a nice place to chill after a day exploring the city. A great stay, can’t wait to come back.

title: “Never Again!”
text: This was quite possibly the WORST stay I have ever experienced and I've stayed in some crap hotels that had a friendly and more knowledgeable staff than this joke of a hotel, not only was our room not ready when we arrived at 6pm, I was treated rudely by the front desk clerk and then he dismissed me to help someone else who got into their room right away. For $509.00 (tax included) a night I expected better service. When my room was ready my room key was tossed on the counter and we weren't even told how to get to it which tower or anything. We then called for a vending machine location were sent on a wild goose chase, never did find it. We called the concierge for a taxi and were told they had them on call and one would be, well we ended up driving our own vehicle, no taxis were available. The laziness of this staff was astonishing! No one at this hotel seemed to be friendly, willing to help or even apologize for their lack of quality service. I will never return to this hotel until changes in staff manners & knowledge of the facility are finally a part of this hotel.

title: “Nasty but Legendary”
text:
My date(s) of stay were much earlier than June of 2007. I actually stayed there in 1999, and again in 2000. In those days, hanging on the wall in the lobby, were a series of b&w
photos...circa 1912. The photos featured primarily, seaman. They had just arrived in Manhattan. They were some of the survivors of the Titanic tragedy. Atop the building, in that era, was a searchlight. The same searchlight that is mentioned in the accounts of the survivors, as they sailed into the city. Many of those seaman stayed at the hotel, At
the time...it was exclusively maritime housing, I believe. Lying in bed, in that little room, as, uninviting as it was...I felt a special kinship with those survivors. If it served their purpose...it served mine, as well. The last time I was there, the photographs had been
removed. The searchlight was dismantled a long time ago.

title: “Walking distance to Staples Centre”
text:
Stayed here when we went to LA to watch the Canucks vs. Kings. Close to the arena, within walking distance, and close to the Metro, which we used to get to Hollywood etc. Our room was a king bed and we found it to be quite small. Not bad since we were not in the room alot.
It is right downtown, and parking is a premium at the hotel. We had rented a car, valet is $38 US per night. Convenient but expensive. Bars and main restaurants expensive but nice. They do have a "food Court" type floor but did not go there with so many other choices in the area.

title: “Beautiful and super clean !”
text:
was only there for one night but experience was perfect for the short stressful situation. Mathew at the front desk during the midnight hours was superb. Rooms were gorgeous and super clean! would absolutely stay here again. 
thanks

title: “Nice staff, but needs updating”
text: The hotel has big rooms by NYC standards. However, I found the bed uncomfortable, the rooms not very sound proof and really tacky with floral wall paper. The staff was very nice. I would not hesitate to stay here again if the price is right.

title: “Excellent value for money in a great location”
text:
OK so the Salisbury could do with a little face lift but nothing major. The staff are helpful and friendly, the rooms are large (which is unusual for New York at these prices) and comfortable but above all else the hotel is in a fantastic location. Just far enough out to be relatively quiet at night but close enough in to be just a few minutes from Times Square to the south, 5th avenue to the east and Central Park to the North. 
We walked everywhere and found the hotel was within easy walking distance of everything we needed. Those places that were a little further out, such as Battery Park and the Statue of Liberty or China Town, we just used the subway which is located at either end of 57th, just yards from the hotel.
The breakfast was a bargain at all you can eat for $4 a head, although it was mainly bagels, donuts, Danish pastries etc.. there was cereal and fruit salad available too. 
The room was extremely comfortable and air conditioned which was a real blessing - yes it can do with redecorating, especially the bathroom, but comfort is the main thing, right? And what do you use your room for other than sleeping? There's so much to see and do in New York we spent little time in our room, so for what we wanted it for, it was perfect. It had a microwave and a fridge and a large walk-in closet. 
Negatives - the elevators can get a little busy especially on a Sunday when the local Baptist Church use the 5th floor of the hotel for their meetings and they all seem to want the elevators, but we found that leaving early and arriving back late (6 o'clock time) meant the elevators were always free. 
Breakfast is served between 7 and 11, but if you arrive between 8 and 10, you have to queue. So get there early or late. Having said that, the lines move pretty quickly and if you don't want to wait then there's a cafe just a few doors away that serves pancakes and bagels for around the same sort of price (although it's not all you can eat)
All in all this hotel is a real find. A great bargain in a truly fantastic location. Would definately use again.

title: “Had a nice time, but wouldn't come back.”
text: Went with 3 girlfriends - Sex & The City style. Opened the door to our Executive Suite, and it looked like most of the furniture that was supposed to be there had been stolen! We literally had a dance floor in the middle of our living space! (We pressed all the light switches hoping there would be a disco ball to no avail.) The room had a slightly musty smell, and we didn't get the bed arrangement that we had requested. We got a King bed and a let-out couch. The let-out couch was slanted and the mattress was about as thick as a slice of Texas Toast. The King bed was as firm as plywood. We requested a room switch, but the only other rooms, or so it was claimed, were much smaller so we kept our room. I will say that the bathroom was fantastic. All four of us could get ready as it was a very nice size. Four long showers and still lots of hot water and good water pressure. The staff was excellent - very very friendly. Food at the Barefoot Cafe was good - and like most have said - very pricey. I wanted to get a pedicure, but at $60 for a BASIC, I said "fuggetaboutit". To be frank, we're not a kid-friendly group, but the kids there were active and had lots of options, so it wasn't a problem at all. Stay here if you get a good deal - do NOT pay full price. (Restaurants: Gringos on Garnet for dinner and Kona by Crystal Pointe for breakfast!)

title: “Good deal”
text:
We stayed here two night for business/tourism. We've lived in the area before so know the lay of the land. The location is good for access to the metro and restaurants and stores nearby. It's a pretty long ride into the city though and the trains weren't very frequent outside of rush hour.
Our room was nice, no major complaints. We did have to ask for a different room at check in as we are a light-sleeping family and the elevator beeps when it gets to a floor! Beware!
The pool is very small, but we used it once, in the afternoon and it wasn't very crowded.
The breakfast set up and food was better than most Embassy Suite experiences we have had. Well-stocked, short wait for omlettes, ripe bananas...

title: “Convenient location”
text: The hotel's location is amazing! It is about a 20 minute walk to Times Square and 5 minute walk to Central Park! The hotel staff was very accommodating and even gave us an upgrade! The decor is very chic and modern. My only complaint is that the nightclub on the main floor got too noisy during the weekends. It was unpleasant to have to yell across the front desk to talk to the receptionist, but once you got up to your room it was fairly quiet. The room is a bit small but it was to be expected since it's located in middle of Manhattan!

title: “Perfectly fine”
text:
We visited this hotel between July 24-July 29. We stayed in a room with a king bed and a sofa pullout, with a refrigerator and microwave combo. Our friends stayed in a similar room without the combo. We were on the fourth floor.
The rooms were clean and well appointed, the bathrooms were also nice.
The cable television channels were about 95 percent sports/news (all of the ESPN channels were included), although there is also HBO and movies/games on demand.
Our friends' room (we each stayed with one child) was laid out completely differently. Where in our room, the sofa was in a corner and opened in front of the king, in theirs the sofa was on a side wall and opened up to one side of the king, making the room appear much larger than ours, although it probably was about the same square footage.
Nothing was "filthy" as some other reviewers have claimed. The maid service did a great job, we had plenty of towels. When we noticed the sofa bed did not have a blanket, we called the front desk and had one within a few minutes.
The beds were very comfortable, although the pillows were too soft for my liking. My wife brought her own, so I slept on two of the hotel pillows and did fine.
The hotel always seemed to be packed, with a combination of primarily business professionals and, toward the end of our stay, military personnel. Several representatives of American Airlines also stayed there during the week, apparently between flights. The hotel offered a free shuttle to and from the airport and nearby shops, attractions.
Not too many families/tourists from what we could tell.
The restaurant was good and offered both a breakfast and lunch buffet most days. The breakfast buffet was $9.95 for adults and the lunch was $10.95. The breakfast featured scrambled eggs, bacon, sausage, pancakes, cereal, grits, etc. and most days an omelette bar.
Lunch also featured about two or three meat entries and various sides and salads.
The food was tasty, the staff very friendly and efficient. The coffee was so-so.
There was also a coffee/snack bar in the lobby. Nice touch, although a bit pricey. The gift shop was very expensive.
The pool was clean, clear and had a big hot tub. It was adjoining a very nice deck area, which tended to get scorching hot during the afternoon. But, it was July in San Antonio, so that was to be expected.
The biggest drawback for this hotel is its location. The 410 loop is under heavy construction and this hotel is right in the middle of it all. Entering/exciting the hotel, especially during rush hour (right next to an exit ramp) was a gamble. There is also little in the immediate area. There is the North Star Mall and a shopping center within a half-mile, but the traffic snarls could make it quitle a long trip.
Once you actually are on the 410, or on the nearby Highway 281, traveling to any of the big attractions are a breeze.
All in all, I would have no qualms about staying here again.

title: “Bed Bugs”
text:
Unfortunately this hotel has bed bugs. I have had bed bug bites twice before so I know them when I see them and for the first time my husband got bitten.
Management changed our room and deducted one nights stay from the bill. 
Come to find out at breakfast from one of our group, his girlfriend, who didn't come, checked some website before the trip and found out the hotel has a history of bed bugs.
If it were not for the bed bugs I would have given it a 3 rating.

title: “Excellent”
text: Beautiful hotel, lovely breakfast, would recommend it to anyone and would defo stay there again....... Easy access to underground going, mid town or up town. Lovely area, walk around, down by sea front. Lovely restaurants especially across the road from hotel an Italian, very funny night in there, look for Antonio Fantastico.....

title: “Excellent accomodations”
text:
The hotel is spotless and clean. My wife and I were impressed with the simplicy of the decor, and the modern conveniences far exceeded our expectations. We paid $125/night and it was a real bargain. The hotel is convenient to the interstate, but is at least 20 minutes to downtown Memphis. The hotel is in a nice part of town, but you still need to drive to restaurants or shopping. The bed was very comfortable. The A/C was too close to the bed, and I was worried that this would be a problem. Fortunately, we had adjusted the thermostat well and didn't have any problems. The TV is a large plasma screen and is amazing. It swivels to either face the bed or the couch. There was an office area for business travelers, and the room had 2 sinks (nice touch). The closet is small and there are hardly any drawers to store clothing in the room, but our needs were met for a short stay.
There are 2 computers in the lobby for guest internet access, which proved helpful in printing out maps and directions. The hotel staff provided a listing of nearby restaurants for every type of cuisine. The continental breakfast was minimal, but was enough to get us going for a few hours. 
Overall, we were very pleased.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: We stayed here in September having chosen it because of the good reviews on trip advisor. We were not disappointed. The location was great. The hotel was clean and the bed the most comfortable I have slept in. The complimentary breakfast was a real bonus as was the coffe/tea/drinks machine just by reception. I would definately stay here again. You get a good deal at a very reasonable price for New York.

title: “perfect place to rest our heads”
text: we stopped at this place on our way to Miami and it was perfect. The gentleman at check in was very nice and polite. great attitude. lobby was spotless and smelled so good. business room in the lobby had 2 computers that were free to use. our rooms were very clean, alot of extras in the rooms(shampoos, soap, iron,refrigerator)..clean towels, clean linens, comfortable beds. there is a swimming pool outside. very close and convenient to I-95. would definately stay here again.

title: “Will not stay here again...”
text: Overpriced hotel, terrible bathroom, does provide parking...but you pay for it even as a guest.

title: “Great Help”
text: Hotel was good, clean, quiet and great staff. Left our car for 7 days, and all good on return. Thanks very much to James the shuttle driver for getting us at the airport, and helping us load and unload 3 heavy coolers of fish that we caught in Mexico. Thanks again.

title: “Noise, limited menu, and more noise”
text: I stay at many Marriott hotels but this one is one that I will never revisit. For a hotel frequented by many business travelers, never have I seen such a poor restaurant menu, tiny lounge area, more noise. If you like sirens 24/7 this place is for you. One block from the hotel is a fire station so sirens are heard at all times of the day and night. Then, when after a sleepless night you want a good breakfast or lunch, you'll be sadly disappointed. Forget dinner. I can only conclude that the hotel management has decided that its guests will walk to other places to dine. There are choices nearby including the Ritz-Carlton to choose from, but don't waste your time going to the in-hotel dining. With other Marriotts in town, keep this one off your list.

title: “Oasis Near the Airport”
text:
If you just want a place to flop, go to one of the budget chains next to the airport. For a more luxe, "Northwesty" local experience, go to Cedarbrook. The free shuttle runs you the five minutes from Sea-Tac to this beautifully landscaped, tranquil hotel. No airplane noise at all in the hotel or the rooms. This is a beautifully-crafted hotel with all the amenities: free wi-fi, free continental breakfast (with tons of smoked salmon and artisan cheeses, eggs etc.), nice restaurant and bar, comfy bedding, big and well-equipped workout center.
The rate was reasonable for such an upscale property. We paid $149. Our room was smallish but had a Keurig coffeemaker, large flat-screen, ample work area and storage, nice bathroom, good task lighting and bed. A nice touch is the "living rooms" scattered throughout the guest wings. Big seating area with large flat-screen and complimentary snacks including fruit, ncandy, chips, bottled water, Haagen-Daz ice cream. You'll feel as if you had a mini-vacation in the mountains at this beautiful property.

title: “A great stay in New York”
text: I am very picky when it comes to hotels and I always read horror stories about hotels in New York. Luckily I found Residence Inn Manhattan/Times Square. The staff was very friendly. The room was small, but that is expected in New York. It was clean and that is very important to me. Overall, this was a good experience.

title: “Disappointed in Vitale”
text:
Stayed here for 5 nights and we were disappointed with the hotel.
On check-in we were upgraded to a Bay view Supierior room,which was a nice touch by the staff as we had mentioned this was part of a 3 week trip to USA for hubby's 50th birthday,the staff were helpful & friendly especially Greg the doorman, he always had good advice re: Restaurants directions etc. 
The location of the hotel was good on the Embarcardero and easy transport links for Bart, Muni,cable cars & street trolley. 
Our room did have a lovely view........but the room felt tired,dark and dingy,
