Carpet was badly stained, the furniture was chipped and marked, lack of drawers and the snack tray was completely dusty and old looking, as though the stuff had been there since the hotel opened, certainly not tempting ! No ice-machines on any floors,no turn-down service or bottled water provided in room
Bathroom had a shower but no bathtub,and the lighting was poor,no electrical point near a mirror for drying hair and poor lighting in room for make-up,reading etc. 
I would say this place is geared towards the business traveler probably staying overnight,and not for tourists/holiday makers.
We had come from staying 5 nights at The Wynn in Vegas which we paid less for than 5 nights at Vitale!
We loved San Francisco and will definitely be back........but not to the Vitale

title: “Bring Extra Money because they charge for everything!”
text: We thought we were getting a really good deal on hotwire so we were really excited UNITL we checked in. We were forced to pay 16 dollars (actually over 17 after tax) a night just to park! You have to pay the parking because they basically lock you in the parking lot where you must use your key to get out. Then you had to PAY for internet per night! OMG this is a three star and they act like they are on such a budget they must charge for EVRYTHING! We asked for a bottle of shampoo and the housekeeper had to verfy when we were checking out before she would give us a tiny bottle of shampoo! We needed a cart to bring our luggage in and they threw a fit!!! They did not want us to take a cart even though our room was at least a mile from the lobby! This is a HUGE hotel and I feel because we booked on Hotwire they stuck us in the crappy and far point of the hotel. I would NOT stay here again UNLESS I wanted to throw my hard earned money away like I just had to do! The only good think about this place was the free cookie they give you when you check in....however with what I paid extra I could have bought a whole tin of cookies!

title: “only okay”
text:
Once this must have been a plush place but age is definately showing. The suites were large, balcony small, all windows frames need replacing. There are 2 laundry rooms, one washer one dryer in each. Be prepared to sweat because there is no ventilation and they are located in what was for me inconvenient spots. Buy the detergent and softener from the vending machine, it's heaper than the hotel shop, get quarters.
Food at the Mexican restaurant was good but there is zero atmosphere. Food, service and plenty of atmosphere at the golf club restaurant.
Tip, they do have shuttles to get you around the property, take advantage of this and tip the guys because you can get a serious workout just going back and forth from the room.
The restaurant on the Cliff was closed for a wedding and is closed Sundays so I never got there. Really wanted to see their wine cellar.

title: “Convenient, Safe and Clean----But”
text: If you are looking for a reasonably priced hotel only two blocks from Times Square, that is safe, clean and supported by a nice staff then the Econo Lodge on 47th Street might be a possibility. I stayed at this property March 10th and found it acceptable--with one exception; the rooms are claustrophobically small. If traveling alone, with minimal luggage you will get by, but I would not recommend this property for couples or persons staying longer than a few nights. If you needed to use the phone you had to crawl across the bed as the space between the foot of the bed and the wall was approximately 6 inches. Rooms do not have their own climate control, and mine was incredibly hot so you get what you get without anyway to adjust the temperature. I like some space in a hotel room, not a lot, but at least enough so two people aren't bumping into each other. I'll end by saying again--this property was clean, safe and a reasonably good value, however, because the rooms are incredibly small I would not stay at this property again.

title: “It is what it is”
text: Ended up here unexpectedly. Usually stay at luxury hotels so this was not our norm but got what expected. This is not a hotel that I would stay at for any long period of time but one night was fine and was close to airport which is what we needed. Bed was comfortable, room was adequate size and bathroom was clean. Lobby area was tidy and front desk people were fine. Have no idea about neighborhood but were able to get good night's rest in quiet room which is all we needed. Obviously if you are looking for upscale hotel with numerous amenities this is not the place for you but if you need somewhere inexpensive near the airport for a night it was fine.

title: “you must tip the cleaning stuff if you want a clean room, tea, or coffee every day”
text:
When we walked into the room the first evening we found a hand written note wishing us a pleasant stay signed by the maid. The last time I saw this was in Cuba where the stuff is under paid. The maid (cleaning stuff) did not vacuum our room, sweep the bathroom floor, or replenish tea/coffee/sugar/ toiletries, unless we were to leave a tip. My “left over” hair (I have long hair) was left on the bathroom floor for the three days we had staid and so were the pillows we took of the beds the first night, and the Stair-stick I dropped on the carpet. The coffee machine was not put in place ( one has to take it out of the cupboard and place it on the desk to connect it to the electricity), and the old news-paper which I placed in the Trash Can, was spread open on the desk as if someone had let the room and will come back to finish reading the news. We had left one towel the floor, to be replaced, and the rest on the hangers to dry, as we were instructed in the note left by hotel management, claiming to be “green”. Nevertheless all towels were replaced. We were told that the stuff is instructed that if one towel is to be replaced all towels should be replaced. When we had asked for information from the front desk stuff, and truly they were very friendly and did their best to help us, we were told that the Head Concierge who strolls in (literally) at 11 knows best. True, he does know a lot, but he also knows how to make people feel very small by playing the "Educated Snob" with a 16 years old kid. The Door Man is very friendly, but for the life of me I do not understand how a Door Man can retire at 55, (three years from now), and can afford to buy a retirement property in South America, unless this is from the” tips policy” at Omni. He did tell us that a specific Coffee Shop is the best for breakfast ( he did not even hear about the one we were asking about) but forgot to mention that the time was 11 am and they do not serve breakfast nor lunch at that time, and we would we have to wait half an hour before we would to be able to order more than just pastry and coffee.
When we booked in I asked for a quite room and indeed we got one. Except I do not understand why the garbage bins have to be emptied every night after 11pm and not before 10 pm which is the time most social etiquette agree as usual as down time.
If one wants to stay at a hotel which is in a convenient location (and there are a lot of hotels which are in a convenient location like this Sheraton which is the hotel we moved to ) and where the stuff is a collection of snobs this is the hotel for you

title: “Now I've seen the worst...”
text:
I've been to some of the best, stayed at some that were average, and now I've seen the worst. The difference is the service. We stayed at the Edgewater for 3 nights over labor day. The service was, without mentioning the price, abysmal. The attitude of the staff was that of a fraternity house, where the guests are NOT members. Guest services was unhelpful with the simplest of requests, and management was rude and snotty. Even the bell boys and valets treated the guests with disdain and outright disrespect.
 This overpriced hotel(we payed $200/night) needs new management terribly and I would not refer my worst enemy there. The new waterfront Marriot is right across the street, which is where we ended up- they know a thing or 2 about service and the edgewater should be taking notes. Don't waste your time here, Seattle is too beautiful a town to have your trip spoiled by a terrible hotel stay and that is what this glorified motel will do!!

title: “Gets better every time I am here.”
text: Unlike the 1 to 2 stars all Days Inns are this is a 5 star hotel! Nice area too. Great staff.

title: “Very nice hotel and friendly staff”
text: I stayed in this hotel for 5 nights. The staff was really helpful. They upgraded the room for the same price. The room was really big one, well equipped and with a king size bed. I really enjoyed my stay there. The only thing they have to improve is the speed of wireless internet connection.

title: “Extremely Pleasant Stay!”
text: Based on the mixed reviews we had read about the Islandia, my fiance and I were curious to see for ourselves what lie in wait. We'd booked this hotel, as well as airfare & rental car, through Hotwire (highly recommended and economical, but that's another story!) for a four-night stay in mid-April 2004. Upon arrival, we were met by gorgeously-landscaped, sun-drenched grounds, everything in impeccable condition. Upon entering the main lobby, we were met by a very cheerful chap who offered to help us with our bags and pointed me toward the main desk. The smiling attendent was cheerful and professional, and we were checked in to a tenth-floor, ocean-view "tower" room in no time flat. The lobby, by the way, was beautiful and comfortable. Our room was spectacular! The view from our little balcony was breathtaking, offering world-class sunsets and picture-worthy vistas of Mission Bay and the Pacific. The breeze that floated into the room was perfect, as well. The room was large, and contained a king-size bed, TV armoire, writing desk and chair, two easy chairs, a small table, and the usual nightstands and lamps. The balcony included two patio chairs and a small table, perfect for cocktail hour! The bathroom was clean and elegeant, with real marble and fine tile flooring. No problems with amenities or anything of the sort. The little complimentary coffee maker even worked like a charm (not to be taken for granted at other places.)In short, between the typical perfect San Diego weather, the location of this hotel, the recreation opportunities of which we took advantage, and the Islandia itself, we had a memorable, satisfying visit. We will happily return to this hotel, and have already recommended it to several friends. Five Stars!

title: “hotel stuck in a time warp”
text:
myself and my partner stayed here for 4 nights during holiday season.We had been told not to expect to much so we went with an open mind.on arrival the lobby was very glam (lots of gold and marble)we had to que for 40 mins to check in which was not great but the reception staff were very nice and very helpfull.
our room however was a disaster,it had damp/mould patches on the walls our bed consisted of 2 mattresses piled on top of oneanother covered in a sheet (damp),the carpet was worn,there was rust in the sink/bath and a damp smell throughout the room.we had a window which looked out on to what looked like the main airconditioning fans for the hotel which needless to say made noise constatnly.we asked could we be upgraded to a better room and when asked for our room number were told that our room had been recently renovated and was the best they had.we opened the window on our first night and it became loose in our hands and was then stuck open for the entire stay, we complained but nobody came to fix it.we spent nearly every minute (apart from time asleep)out of the hotel.
the hotel apart from the above mentioned was very central which was its only good point.
i would never return to this hotel, i would never even think about satying in a hotel like this again.its been a real eyeopener.

title: “Quiet hotel with a great location”
text: My wife and I spent a few nights here on a quick trip to NYC for a concert and some sight-seeing. We scored an excellent deal from Priceline which made this hotel even better. The Kitano is only 2 blocks south of Grand Central, making it an ideal place if you plan on riding around the city on the subway. Two of the things I kept noticing on the Kitano's website were how much they heralded their "sound-proof" windows and their "marble bathrooms". We were both wondering how these purported luxuries would pan out. We were very pleased to find that the bathroom was indeed very luxurious and all marble, with a towel warmer and a great shower/tub. The windows, though, were even more impressive. Our sixth floor room over looked Park Ave, but we never heard a thing while sleeping. The room was overall of ample size and was very clean, with a not-too-hard and not-too-soft King size bed. They even include an umbrella in the closet for guest use, which came in extremely handy during "Snowtober 2011". The front-desk staff and bellmen were very nice and answered all of our questions. The one other thing that we really liked, and it may sound a little trivial, is the fact that the complementary personal care items were hypo-allergenic. My wife has an allergy to latex and derivatives of it, many of which are used as thickeners in lotions, soaps and shampoos. None of their items had these ingredients! She was thrilled. Stay here if you want a quiet, luxurious hotel, located close to Grand Central . We'll be going back again.

title: “Perect hotel in NY!”
text: This was really the best hotel we could wish in NY. Close to Times square but still quit. We had a room on the 24th room with a nice view on the Empire State Building. The bed and bathroom were very comfertable. When we go back to NY we will take this hotel again, without any thinking!

title: “Clean, Comfortable & Good Location”
text:
Booked this hotel be cause of the good reviews from this site and a Very good deal from a third party vendor. Was driving from New York with my wife and 3 boys aged 24, 15 and 11. We booked 2 suites. Check in was fast and easy. Valet parking was also very good but do not remember if it was 25 or 30 dollars for a 24 hour period. Rooms were very clean. Beds were firm and the pillows comfortable. Flat screen TV in both bedroom and suite area. My kids were in a room situated 1/2 way down the hall from the elevator and the picked up on the hotel lobby free Wifi. We were about 7 rooms down the hallo and we could not get the Wifi. We had to order it for more than 10 bux a 24 hour period and it was not wifi but a ether net connection. Not good for my wifes new Ipad 3 but luckily I had my laptop. Room has built in safe, refrigerator, microwave, sink and coffee. Bathrooms were a bit small for a suite but were fully operational. Rooms are quiet and we all had a good nights sleep.
Cocktail hour was nice. Free drinks for all with all you can eat chips and salsa. Free Breakfast as well.. They offer a wide selection with eggs,bacon sausage, cereal, yogurts, fruits, bagels, coffee, juice, pastries and more. A separate omelet station as well. Unfortunately we arrived at the tail end of breakfast the first morning and the lines were very long. There is a sign stating that on any given day those arriving with in the first hour will be served quickly in about 5 minutes or less. Those arriving later will have to wait on line 20 minutes. In any case try to get there early and avoid the long lines. Be aware the buffet was very good. 
This hotel is in a great location. Only a 15 minute walk to the white house and other sites. Very close to public transportation. I felt safe walking around with family even at night.Getting taxis at any time is easy. There are a few good restaurants with in walking distance if you do not want to eat in the hotel. Hotel staff are very kind and helpful. They helped us with directions, providing maps, and offered advice on places to go and good restaurants.
I liked this hotel and would recommend it to friends and could easily stay here again.

title: “Read the reviews to late”
text:
I had already signed up for three nights through Hotels and the night before found this web site. My jaw dropped.
I called Hotels and they held my feet to the fire for one night's charge, so I cancelled the last two nights and decided to try it for one night.
It is the most incredible hotel I have ever stayed in, but not in a good way.
Long story made short: I survived. Quick observations.
I saw no bugs.
The smell wasn't overpowering but there shouldn't be a smell at all.
I left my Mac PowerBook in the shower when I went out for several hours and it was there when I came back.
The lady at the "front desk" was very pleasant.
Much like a prisoner of war must do, one has to take his or her mind to another place when you lay down on the bed. if you think about the sheets and blanket too much... well you just shouldn't.
Outside the window was a fire escape that had empty Burger King bags and cups all over it. I think that says it all.
I got this dump for $72. I marched out the next morning (sort of proud of myself for having stayed) and went to the Edison Hotel for $125/night, clean room, a lot of clear, cable channels, and in-the-room, wireless Internet @ $10 extra for 24 hours. I felt like I was in paradise compared to the Manhatten Broadway.
The place isn't as bad as some say, but it's needless for anyone to stay here unless they are required to book a room as a contestant on Fear Factor.

title: “Great location”
text: The location couldn't be better. It's within walking distance to everything downtown Austin has to offer. The hotel was very elegant and luxurious, just what one would expect from an Omni. Check in was great and the staff was friendly. I got to my assigned room, opened the door and there was a man changing! Apparently the guy checked out and went back to the room. The staff was very friendly and apologetic. They handled it very well. I got my room changed and got upgraded to the concierge floor where there was complimentary drinks and appetizers. The room was immaculate and my stay was perfect! (Not to mention that the rate for military was $99!)

title: “Experience most memorable”
text:
General Manager: Aaron Beaver
Servers: Ernie Mattson, Sharon Mc Grath, Brian Smith, staff at the Arizona Biltmore Resort & Spa, made our 3 day stay, one that we will not soon forget. There friendliness and attention to our requests, were all met which such enthusiam and professionalism. They were just awesome! The cabanas our group rented were an added bonus to our stay. We would highly recommend them to anyone visiting your establishment. With short notice, Aaron Beaver arranged and coordinated with the chef, an outstanding light buffet that was beautifully executed and so delicious. Thank you all for making our much needed get-a-way, a trip to repeat real soon!
All the Best!
Genevieve & Rowland Davies, III
Brick, New Jersey

title: “The lobby bar/lounge servers are polite, friendly and always have a smile!”
text: I stayed at the W for business. We had cocktails in the lounge before and after dinner. It didn't matter who was working, we were approached by the friendliest people. All of the individuals were extremely nice and we received the best service. Especially Rhonda, thank you!!! Although we had many other options for drink locations, we always found ourselves back at the same plush couches where we knew our drinks would be correct and served with a smile. The other individuals we met, like Maria, were also gracious. The W as a hotel could use some improvements but the staff at the lobby bar were the best. I have to commend the W for their hiring of quality individuals!!

title: “Fantastic Stay at the Four Seasons!”
text:
My friend and I were in Houston for business and we loved our stay at the Four Seasons Hotel! The customer service is excellent!
We stayed in a Superior Room with two twin beds. There's a desk with two chairs, a sofa chair, and side table, a night stand, and a dresser of drawers. There's a mini refrigerator filled with food & drinks at an extra charge. No coffee maker. Wi-fi internet is $12.99 per 24 hours. The bathroom has L'Occitane toiletries: shampoo, conditioner, shower gel, lotion, and soap. There's a blowdryer, ironing board, and iron to use.
The best part of the hotel room is the amazing beds, and of course, you get your own bathrobe and slippers to lounge around in. We also found that the room service food was very good!

title: “Felt cheap, overpriced”
text: I traveled across the country with my husband and cats because we were moving. I thought this would be the best hotel/ location of the trip and it ended up being the worst. The staff was great but that was all. The room was tiny (even if it is in downtown Denver), and it wasn't updated at all compared to the other hotels we stayed in. The bathroom was disappointing, everything felt rather cheap for a luxury hotel. I was happier in the 2/3 star hotels we stayed in.... There were quite a few thugs around the area outside, we did not feel safe, and worried about our car in their garage. We knew it would be parked off property but it wasn't a good area from what we observed. We will not be staying at a Kimpton again, unfortunately. I was also disappointed as it seemed this hotel catered to attorneys/ business men as opposed to tourists. This is all based on my opinion staying there one night.

title: “Great Friendly Central Hotel”
text:
We arrived early after a 12 hour flight and was greeted with a smile and able to check in early. The room as we expected from other reviews small but very clean and what I thought was a large bathroom by New Zealand standards.
This hotel is close to everything you need with the Bart & Streetcar just around the corner on Montgomery Street. The Free Wine Hour in the lobby is a great way to meet other guests.
I would recommend this hotel to anyone and hope to return in the future.

title: “Love the Bahia for a family resort”
text: Our family of six ( four boys under 12)retruned from five days at the Bahia. As usual it was wonderful. If you are looking for a classic California all inclusive resort for children, this one is hard to beat. If you are looking for an executive level hotel, you would be better off at the Four Seasons in La Jolla. Tips for families: Ask for the Bay side (private beach) suites as they have large kitchens. The play ground is on the beach for the kids. Yes, the Stern paddle River boat is a little corny, but the kids love cruising on it to watch the fireowrks at Sea world at night. Don't miss the Belmont Park roller coaster. and Mission Beach, two blocks away. Bring your boogie boards, fins and surfing attire as Mission is a classic Southern Calif . surf beach. Tip for travlers to San Diego: A smile, a few "thank you's" in spanish and a couple bucks goes a long way with the room cleaning staff. I got checked in fast, towels, the exact room I wanted and great service every time.

title: “Lovely boutique hotel in Denver!”
text: What a gem! The staff was wonderful, and our room was gorgeous. Luxurious linens and extras. The bell staff graciously provided us with a ride to and from a local restaurant--despite it being a very busy night with a Nuggets playoff game nearby. It was delightful to see the theatrical decor and historical touches throughout. This is really a lovely boutique hotel.

title: “Cool old hotel, wish someone would dump some money into this place”
text:
It was certainly not a splurge, as the rate for my room was very inexpensive.
The hotel, was old and neat looking downstairs. I'd always wanted to stay here.
The room was old, but not in a neat way, it needed to be updated and smelled a little moldy.
I really do wish this place could get a rehab, it's got great potential.

title: “Not a place to stay”
text: I had booked a night here since it was close to the airport and I would be flying out at 6:20AM the next morning. Even though it is close (not walking distance!) to the airport, they do NOT have a shuttle service. I am glad I called to check on this before returning my rental car the night before. Upon entering the lobby to check in, I was greeted with an unusual aroma that smelled like a combination of stale cigarette smoke and food. My room was on the second floor and as I entered the room I immediately noticed the window was open, letting in lots of noises from the highway and airport. I tried repeatedly to close the window without any success. I then made my way into the bathroom and discovered that the bathtub was not clean, containing dirt and hair. I then went downstairs and was given another room. The new room did have a window that would close and the bathroom was acceptably clean, but the room still had the same worn out furniture with scratches. I was glad that the smells from the lobby and hallways were not in the rooms. All in all, not a very very welcoming hotel and I will not be staying there again.

title: “Tourist Hotel Character”
text: As a regular at tourist hotels in America and Britain, I liked this place. Most hotels frown on a family of five and make us feel like we had "one too many." Here, our spacious room was set up for five. It was quiet. We slept all night. We walked to all the attractions. The price was half that of its neighbors. But like any old tourist hotel, it has character and you need it too. Roll with the quirks, and both your feet and pocketbook will thank you.

title: “French charm in a perfect locale”
text: The Sofitel it located just blocks from the best shopping, food and attractions that Chicago has to offer. Upon arrival, you are met by the bellman, and in my case, with an umbrella. Doors were consistently opened for me and the hotel atmosphere is definitely modern Euro-chic. My checkin was flawless and speedy and I found my room to be very comfortable with both a shower and tub available. I has an exquisite view of the city and found city noise to be minimal even though we are just blocks from a large fire station. I enjoyed the turndown service, free wireless Internet and complimentary bottle of Evian every night. I have no complaints except to mention that all these amenities come with an expected price. Nice property with extremely attentive staff!

title: “Great Location and Value”
text: My Husband and I recently stayed in this hotel when we came back from our cruise. We were very pleased with this hotel. The hotel is convienently located on Pike street which is a few blocks from the Pike Street Market. They walk was not bad and the metro station is near for those of you that can not walk. The room was large and clean. It was an apartment style room complete with living room, two televisions, sofa with pull out, full size refrigerator, dishwasher and dining area. The bed was extremely comfortable. The gym had updated equiptment with clean towels and water cooler. This hotel was quite a savings because of the Manager's cocktail party that comes with dinner. I believe the reception is offered Monday through Friday. We had potatoe crusted Cod fish with vegetables, salad, wine, beer and cookies. The food was very good and the service at this hotel was excellent. This is a wonderful family hotel with all the savings. The complimentary breakfast was also wonderful. Breakfast and dinner already taken care of by the hotel- You can't beat that! I will definitely be returning to this hotel when I am in the area again.

title: “Great place to stay”
text: I stayed here for a night and I really liked this place. The staff were very friendly and the rooms were very good. I got a corner room with the mountain view and it was incredible. I like their windows that give you panoramic view. Large rooms with comfortable bed. No free parking and that is expected when in stay in the down town. I highly recommend this place for both business and pleasure travellers.

title: “The best in Detroit”
text: Many travelers have an issue with safety and location in Detroit, so I'll first focus on that. This is probably the best bet for staying in downtown Detroit. While much of Detroit can seem unsafe to a traveler, this location feels safe for anyone due to it being on a busy corner street with plenty of stores and restaurants nearby. I have stayed at two other higher end hotels at or near downtown, and those locations are a little seedy. Anyway, the hotel itself is top notch. This was my second stay at this hotel and both times I have found this to be a very clean, historic hotel. The room, the lobby, the bar, the restaurant, all places were very clean. They have the low-flow shower heads, which I think most people do not care for. Ask for a room with a view of the city because the inner rooms have windows that get hardly any daylight. Typical four star room; nothing that will amaze you if you have traveled a lot, but certainly better than 90% of hotels out there. If you don't travel much, it probably will amaze you. There are six elevators, but only three were working which can cause delays when there groups of people coming and going, a small inconvenience. Nice pool, nice workout facilities, and nice bar and lounge (they make really good drinks). I haven't used the spa. The staff always speak to you as you pass by and the valet people are helpful with directions and hailing a cab for you. The location is a block from the train (people mover). I highly recommend using this if you are going around downtown for sports, Greektown, restaurants, bars, casinos, etc (or just get a cab). Its $.75 per trip and it beats driving and parking any day. I also recommend not venturing far away from downtown, especially on foot, unless you know exactly where you are going. Back to the hotel, it is a historic hotel that was renovated and feels elegant, fancy, yet modern enough. All things considered, the only other hotel downtown that I feel could compare to this hotel would be the Renaissance. If you can book this hotel for a discount, all the better. Highly recommended.

title: “Amazing location, great view!!!”
text: My boyfriend and I just came back from our lovely vacation to NY. We didn't know where to stay and we decided to book our stay at this hotel based on the reviews that others wrote. We have absolutely no complaints!! this place was amazing! When we arrived we were taken care of quickly, we even checked in early. They had given us a room on the 14th floor where we really weren't that happy with the view. I called the front desk and there was no hassle in getting a higher floor. We ended up on the 36th floor (building has 37) with an incredible view of the Chrysler Building, a plus we had was that it started snowing the minute we entered our room!! VERY ROMANTIC!!! The staff was very friendly and gave great advice on where to go and were to catch the nearest subway. The rooms were huge for NY hotel rooms. Our bathroom was VERY clean, the kitchen was clean, and the bed was very comfortable, with a choice of 5 diff pillows to choose from. The location was great and quiet! you're minutes away from the Chrysler building, Macy's, Madison Square Gardens, Empire State, Times square...you could literally walk to all these places. They have great restaurants around the area and a 24hour convenient store in the corner (Must try Charles steakhouse!! Great philly cheesesteak ). Overall, we loved this place and we'll def stay here again!

title: “Cute but a little pricey”
text:
I stayed here for 2 nights with my teenage daughter and three of her friends while they attended a convention downtown. The hotel is cute and comfortable with a bar and restaurant and fitness center (which we did not use). Wireless is free and there is a nice lounge area downstairs with couches and a big screen TV. The hotel is within walking distance to many restaurants. Parking is valet only but there is a parking garage right across the street. A negative is there is no street parking which made drop off and pickup difficult since the girls had so much luggage and we simply could not schlep it down Main St. from the parking garage--my husband ended up having to illegally park on the street and rush in.
Check in was smooth and friendly. There are several free (slow) computers for use in the lobby. The decor is all pastels but not garish--I thought it pretty but wondered what my husband would have thought of it. We chose a Queen Suite to sleep 4. I thought the room a little small and the big coffee table in front of the pullout sofa a nuisance. The tiny bathroom had 1 sink (but nice Aveda products). It wasn't exactly what I think of when I hear "suite" but it was cute and comfortable and had a microwave and fridge which was nice. The queen bed was comfortable and both the living area and bedroom had flat screen TVs--which were outdated, no HD and the one in the living area looked to be going out very soon. The bedroom had a private door--but it was hard to open and close and was so noisy we couldn't close it because if someone had to use the bathroom in the middle of the night it would have woken up everyone. The hotel itself was quiet though even though we were right by the elevator. The only noise was street noise which I got used to.
Overall I would stay here again for this event as it was quiet and comfortable and in a good location. But I thought the rate high as there was no HD television or pool. This would be a nice stay for the business traveler or for locals like us that have an event downtown.

title: “The room was huge and the shower was great”
text: Took my daugther for her 21st birthday. Room was huge for New York. It had 2 sitting areas and the bed was so inviting it was hard to get out of. The shower head was so great I came home and bought one. Great part of town and felt very safe and welcome.

title: “Good music. Terrible bar. You can't...”
text:
Good music. Terrible bar. You can't take your drink to your room, and they close at midnight, so you have to finish your drink with all the lights on while they close up. Then on top of this, they add a 15% service charge in addition to the drink charge. 
I would never recommend anyone stay here.

title: “Lovely Hotel!”
text: Had a great stay in the Omni Parker House in Boston. Rooms are small but then again we had a lot of luggage. The bed is unbelievably comfortable and the room was very quiet so we great sleep. All in all, a gorgeous hotel in a great location!

title: “Disappointing”
text:
Positiives:
Great location
Negatives:
1. smell of urine in the elevator
2. rooms, bathrooms and common areas very dated
3. was told concierge service existed; not true, the front desk staff is very pleasant but admitted to me the not familiar with many of the restaurants and hence were not comfortable making recommendations; the front desk will make reservations for you but the appeared to be the extent of the "concierge" service that the hotel was able to offer.
4. no airconditioning in the hallways outside the rooms.
5. breakfast average

title: “They should be ashamed”
text: My 1st review of my most recent trip to SF. Love it here! Wow, the St. Francis's history. Pretty amazing. It's interesting how they have the original hotel and then the new mega addition behind it. We stayed in the original side. 9th floor. Great view of Union Square. Walking into the room is like going back in time. It's small, quaint. One of the first things I noticed though, was the bed. I really thought "this must be a joke." I did not want to complain too much. It was a business trip for my husband, and I go along when I can. I mean come on. Almost $300 a night? Look at the mattress in the photo. It had two deep depressions on either side. When you laid in them it was worse. There was a big hump in the middle. We like to cuddle a bit, and I am a stomach sleeper. Neither happening here, for a week! One night my husband rolled over a fell into my side and crashed into me elbow first. We probably scared the hell out of our one neighbor. We were on a corner. And let me tell you, thinnest walls ever. You could hear every little word said. That was the end of my sleep for that night. Seriously, was this the original mattress? It was the worst. I also have to add an additional note because I am going to slam their cleanliness. The windows had big greasy face marks all over it, and when you look outside of course that was unpleasant, and the window next to ours which was around a corner so kind of facing ours, had cigarette butts out there. Marred the view a bit. I would open the curtains wide hoping that the housekeeper would see it. Those face prints are probably still there. When we checked out, my husband was putting our luggage outside, and I was in line to get an update bill. I was so hoping that whoever I got would say "How was your stay?" But the didn't. Hmmm. Makes you wonder. Again, since it was paid for by my husbands work, I did not want to raise a big stink. My husband was not happy either, and said he will not book it for next years RSA or any other trips, and here is my review. Sad. One day we were walking around the wharf area and they were delivering mattresses to a hotel down there. I think it was the Mariott. I wanted to yell at the driver "Please take at least one to the St. Francis!" Ugh!

title: “Great Place”
text:
We reserved a room at the Hilton through Priceline.com and were extremely satisfied with the accomodations. The place was clean, comfortable and just an overall nice place. The swimming pool was very nice and my children really enjoyed it. As stated in other reviews, the elevators weren't of the best quality, but that certainly didn't spoil our experience. Highly reccomend Hilton Indianapolis North.
One thing I would caution travelers on. They have a sign that says something about parking with caution under the trees, because they drip sap. Take that seriously, they do drip. There are plenty of other spaces to park though.

title: “Great staff service and great accomodations.”
text: The London Hotel for me has a great location,also very comfortable rooms and suites. The bathrooms are larger than any average NYC hotel bathroom. The staff is very friendly and will make you feel at home always.

title: “The room was dirty, the area noisy, would not stay there again”
text: We were in San Francisco for a day and decided at the last moment that we were going to spend the night in the city. We had an early morning tour planned and so had to stay close to the Pier. It was a weekend, and all the hotels around the city were booked!. We tried everything, calling the hotels, checking online on all the popular websites, etc. We needed a simple, inexpensive place to stay, all the places that were available in that area were well over $250, and this was the only place available at a more decent price. The reviews were mixed, so we took a chance. For starters, we booked the room online, only to get there and be told that they were already fully booked. The attendant at the checkin was very harassed and we felt quite sorry for him, as the hotel was overbooked and he was trying to sort out the situation. We had to wait for over half hour, (at 11pm at night that was not fun!) Finally, he was able to give us a room as two of the other parties who had booked before us had still not turned up. We got to the room, to find that it was not clean, the garbage in the bathroom had not been emptied, there was a used soap bar and towel. The bed was made, but one of the two queen beds looked like it had been used, and the sheets not changed. Basically, it was disgusting! We called up the reception desk to be told that they are sorry that it was not cleaned well, and that the room was not used. Anyhow, having finally found a room after hours of search and waiting, we were exhausted, and had an early morning ahead, and so decided to ignore everything, sleep for a few hours and leave as early as possible. I covered the pillow with my own scarf as I could not bring myself to put my head on the pillow. We were woken up several times during the night by loud noises, car alarms going off (we found out the next morning that a homeless person had apparently tried to get into one of the cars to sleep, and set the alarm off). After a very disturbed sleep, we left the room at 6 am the next morning and checked out. There was breakfast being set up, so I suppose the only good thing is we grabbed a couple of bananas, muffins, croissants and and orange juice and headed out! San Francisco was awesome and I want to go back, however, never staying in this hotel again for sure

title: “Loved it”
text:
We like to get away to the city for weekends once in a while and I was looking for a nice hotel that wasnt too expensive. I love tripadvisor so I looked up S.F and picked the Orchard (which was #1 at the time) They are a non smoking hotel (I know, I know) so were looked further. I finally landed at the Omni and i was very happy. I called their 800 and got a great gal who helped us pick a package. Got a romance package at 170.00 a night which included breakfast, robe, wine and chocolate. The room was a little small but lovely. It was elegant and new. We signed up for their frequent stayer program which gives perks and received a coupon for half off next stay and upgrade which were are using this weekend for a getaway and Christmas shopping. Close to everything. 
Chinatown, Northbeach and Union Square are all within walking. Great hotel.

title: “Outstanding facility”
text: We stayed at the Residence Inn for almost two weeks in July 2011 due to Federal jury duty selection. We dreaded being in downtown Denver for that much time, but staying at the Residence made it a very pleasant experience. Spacious suite, kitchen, and a location one block from the activity on the 16th Street Mall. It’s not possible to think of a complaint or shortcoming. All the staff were uniformly courteous and helpful. In particular, Jill of the desk staff took extra time to sort out our complex bookings to our benefit. We qualified for the government rate, but even at normal rack rates, the Residence is a five star deal.

title: “magical break in perfect location”
text: after the surprise of a lifetime - my boyfriend flew out to the states where I was working to propose to me - he then made the moment more perfect by taking me to NYC for 3 nights to celebrate! He had booked us into a king sized room with a corner view. It was amazing. We arrived at the hotel - which is impeccably clean, and incredibly cool - and upon telling the staff our news, they couldnt be more excited. they gave us a room on the 37th floor with dreamy views of Manhattan. The room was a good space, with a King Bed and a beautiful bathroom with lots of Bliss products (always a bonus). 5 minutes after arriving in the room we received champagne and chocolates from reception. What more could we ask! Plus due to the room being on a high floor it was incredibly quiet despite being in the heart of Times Square. I found all the staff incredibly courteous, helpful and FUN. Would recommend in a second.

title: “Not Happy”
text: they charged me to park my car on their lot, I have never paid to park at a hotel I was staying at. other guests were fighting for 3 hours in the middle of the night, slaming doors, yelling, reving up cars and the staff did nothing about it.

title: “Good hotel by the airport”
text:
I stayed there 2 nights. It was nice a nice hotel. Very clean. Recently updated – flat screen TVs , etc. Pleasant staff. The bed was comfortable. There was a blow-dryer in the bathroom.
There is Burger King across the street. Beyond that, there was not much within walking distance. 
They offer a free shuttle to the airport. It departs every 20 minutes and it was prompt.
There is an extra charge for in-room Wi-Fi access. (It is free in the lobby.) I never used it did - but I overheard a conversation about their charging extra to use the business center. 
Valet is $34 per night (with unlimited in/out privilege). There is a self-park option (which I think was $28 a day).

title: “Roomy and comfortable!”
text:
VERY large room, more like an efficiency apartment. Very comfortable bed, with turned down sheets every evening. The housekeeper would do cute things with my daughter's panda every day that made her laugh when we returned back there each evening. 
There's a small kitchenette with a half-size refrigerator, microwave, dishes, etc. There's a sitting area with a sofa, chairs, and desk. It's very spacious compared to most hotels, including other suite-type rooms. The bathroom was very good with a large walk-in closet. 
The service was very good all-around. It was quiet and very comfortable. The parking is expensive and not very convenient, if you don't want to pay for valet parking. It's in a building about a half a block away. 
We came to Baltimore to look at a college for my daughter, and now that she's enrolling there, we are planning to stay there again when we take her to begin college in August and on future visits.

title: “Good place to stay in on business”
text: Clean rooms, attentive service, friendly front desk personnel, good meeting facilities, good food.

title: “excellent hotel and staff”
text: great location Great place to stay Would stay here again We stayed on the third floor and we had to use our key to access that floor so we felt safe. The view from our room was beautiful wish we had better weather though. Next time we come back it will probably be in the spring

title: “Lovely City Getaway”
text:
I spent a night with my boyfriend for Valentine's weekend. We both love the city, and we really enjoy this location and the hotel. The staff is incredible - always super polite and ready to help you at any time. The hotel is very accommodating, and the beds are super comfortable. 
This is my second weekend city stay here. The first was with a group of friends. Even when they are busy, the staff will attend to your needs. It's exactly what I want in a weekend hotel - heart of the city, nearby everything, modern and comfortable hotel.

title: “Fantastic all round!”
text:
Loved Candlewood Suites the room looked better than the photo, it wasn't huge but more than enough for our needs. Having a kitchenette was so handy, we made our breakfast there every morning and were able to bring food back, though we didn't do any major cooking it was great to have the facility.
Also a a small shop in the lobby with basic food items.
Another huge bonus was having a great laundry in the basement.
Only 6 rooms a floor, perfect.
Staff all friendly and helpful.
Location again perfect 5 minutes walk to times square but far enough away that there's no street noise.
Great little local restaurants and bars.
Try walking up 9th St instead of 8th.
We would come back in a heartbeat! Thanks for a great stay & great price.

title: “Lives up to its reputation of great service & facilities”
text:
Over the Christmas holidays I spent several days at the Four Season's Denver. I was initially looking for a more cozy atmosphere but decided on the Four Season's because I've never been disappointed with their facilities or services in the past. This was my first visit and I was not disappointed. 
From the moment I arrived I was greeted warmly and whisked through registration quickly. In the days leading up to my visit, rates had dropped and reservations lowered my rate in accordance with their new lower holiday rate. On arrival everything was in order, and without having to ask, I'd been upgraded to a deluxe king room. I spent 20 years as a travel specialist and this was one of the nicest rooms I'd ever seen in a city hotel. The walls were covered with a soft umber colored wallpaper; one wall was accented with stonework. The furniture, including the wardrobe/closet were solid wood in a contemporary style. Though I was on one of the higher floors, the atmosphere in the room reminded me more of being in resort or contemporary ski lodge. 
The bathroom was spacious and beautiful, with separate sunken tub, shower, toilet area which was enclosed by opaque glass walls. There was a television behind the mirror in the bathroom which disappeared when you turned the TV off. The TV could be viewed from the tub.
The bed was very plush and covered with luxury linens, lots of pillows, and good lighting. The room had a beautiful glass worktable connected to a credenza like counter that ran the length of the room and lots of space to work. There is wifi in the room but you have to pay for it. There was a wide screen flat panel TV that could be turned to face an easy chair in the corner of the room by the window, or the desk. The room had 3 phones (bedside, bathroom, & desk area). 
Storage included a solid wood wardrobe built into the wall for hanging clothes complete with drawers and safe. A credenza on the side of the room also included hidden fridge with drinks (billable immediately if the item is removed) and drawer of dry snacks. There was also a coffeemaker and assorted coffees on top of the counter. Amenities were L'Occitane. Hotel offers turn down service. Doors are electronically keyed with privacy buttons to light a privacy sign in the door instead of door hangers. 
Food: outstanding. Best room service breakfast ever. The food was fresh and delivered ontime (sometimes early) and was hot. Service was outstanding. Food is delivered on a table and table is set formally for every meal. Tables picked up immediately when you request it. No food trays every stayed in the room or was ever seen in the halls. Everything was delicious. Keep in mind there is a large gratuity and service charge built into the bill. 
Restaurant & Bar: Edge was a fabulous restaurant. Service was outstanding. Great atmosphere though for dinner this is more of a place for singles/couples rather than families.Bar area adjacent to Edge serves drinks and snacks and is a comfortable area for grabbing a snack and getting some work done with your laptop, though I didn't see anywhere to plug in any electronics. The lobby is all glass and it was snowing so the light is great and the view of the outside was nice. 
Business center: I did not use the business center but it appeared to be more than adequate. There is a kiosk in the lobby for printing out boarding passes so no need to use the business center for that. 
Parking: Over the top expensive (more than $30 a night) because I think cars have to be driven to parking garage off property. It's a very long ride to the airport ( give yourself an hour on top of the hour advance check-in you need for your flight). 
The decor in the hotel is sterile but the staff is warm and accommodating. 
There was a blizzard over my stay so I was not able to walk around too much, but the area around the hotel is replete with coffeehouses, restaurants and shops. I'm glad I spent the money to stay here rather than another hotel thinking "oh well, it's just a room and I'm not spending much time there". To the contrary, most of my stay had to be spent in the hotel and I'm glad I spent the extra money to make the visit memorable and comfortable.

title: “Quiet, clean & comfortable stay.”
text: Stayed here for 2 nights prior to flying out of Denver at the end of a 2 week trip through the South West. The reception staff were very friendly and accommodating. The hotel was spotless, well appointed and very comfortable. We took the light rail into Denver for a day to tour about. The area around the airport is quite new and well designed. Would highly recommend this location when visiting Denver.

title: “Independent hotels can be a hit or miss - this definitely was a HIT”
text: The Capitol Hill Hotel is located across from the Library of Congress and a short walk away from the nearest metro stop. The front desk staff person was extremely friendly and called my room 10 minutes after I entered to make sure I found everything to be satisfactory. The king size bed was comfortable and the room was well appointed. The best features for me were free wifi (that was extremely easy to connect to) and the mini fridge and microwave in the room. Additionally, this hotel was very well priced. There are plenty of hotels in DC that are just as well appointed going for $70+ more per night.

title: “solid budget hotel with some charm”
text: I travel to New York a half dozen times a year for work and need to find hotels that are clean, safe, comfortable, and affordable. The Mayfair fit that perfectly. Rooms are very small--I had a queen standard and can't imagine two people sharing this space. The rooms are well organized however, clean , with good beds and bedding, and nice bathrooms . The location is perfect and if you are not looking for a "hotel experience" this is a solid choice. Yes the elevator is small and dowdy--and this is a place to sleep --but I like it and would return again . It's hard to find a hotel under $200 in New York that is not creepy or depressing. This one is a good value.

title: “Good location, good value”
text: We stayed here three nights to visit friends nearby. It's right off the freeway, so it's easy to find. You can walk to a number of restaurants and stores. The rooms are pretty quiet; ours was in the back. The motel has a pool in the interior courtyard, and a hot tub too (but it never looked hot enough). The room has a mini-refrigerator, which we really appreciated, and a little microwave. Decent-sized TV although not too many channels. The room and the grounds were clean. You can get coffee and muffins in the office in the morning, which were pretty good. Towels were a bit on the rough side, but our biggest problem was the bed, which was just too hard. Still, we'd recommend it because of the price and location.

title: “Great location!”
text:
I booked this hotel thru Priceline for a 2-night stay in June 2011. A friend and I were in Chicago for a concert and wanted to make a weekend out of it. I had never been to this hotel before. 
It's in a GREAT location - just blocks from the Magnificent Mile and less than a 15-minute walk to Navy Pier. The neighborhood seemed safe and vibrant - we got back one night after 1:00 AM and there was still lots of activity and we felt totally safe walking around. Lots to do and lots of places to eat within a 2-block radius. For the price, you can't beat the location. The hotel offered free parking, but there are fewer spots than there are rooms, so if you leave, you may not have a spot when you get back. We just left our car there the entire time.
The room itself, however, left something to be desired. There is a sign hanging out front that says "Newly Renovated" - but the sign looks to be over 15 years old, and there was nothing that we saw that would qualify as "newly renovated". The room wasn't really dirty, it was just worn down and old. Lots of scuffs on the wall, holes in the blanket, that kind of thing. They weren't dealbreakers for us, because it was just a place to sleep and shower, but if you are going to be spending a lot of time in your room, you might want to look elsewhere.
The diner at the hotel (I don't think it's affiliated, but it's connected) had really good breakfast for great prices.
All in all, I would stay here again, simply for its location!

title: “Don't stay here”
text: Reserved club room on 10/2003, when checking in they gave me room w/king bed when I reserved 2 queens. Had to go to front desk where they were very rude and told me to wait for a while to see if any rooms had 2 queens..said my reservation wasn't guaranteed..it was since I reserved w/credit card. Told me no room was guaranteed. I fought with them till I got room w/2 queen beds on 8th floor..w/club floor amenities. Took almost 2 hrs to check in. Last day of stay I asked for wakeup call that never came..almost missed flight home. Otherwise, rest of staff excluding front desk were nice enough. Hotel room ok, overlooked fire station and train tracks. Not the best area in town to stay. Won't stay here again.

title: “Enjoyed our stay!!!!!!”
text:
Four of our family members attended the graduation of our grandson from the Air Force
Basic Training the week of Nov. 7th, 2011. 
We stayed at the Springhill Suites on Richland Street, called the "Sea World" location. It is in a
nice part of San Antonio, clean, friendly, shopping center with a Target right down the road
without having to get on the express way. The breakfast had everything from make your own
waffles to oatmeal, with bacon and eggs, orange juice, and many other breakfast items.
The price was very low compared to the benefits of this clean hotel. Would recommend Springhill
Suites,and would stay there again.

title: “Good location & modern, comfortable rooms”
text:
My girlfriend and I stayed at this hotel for our first trip to Chicago. The location of the hotel is ideal for getting around the city, with plenty of local bars and restaurants, and the main shopping area just a short walk away. Red line tube stop is also a couple of blocks away.
Staff are welcoming and friendly, and the room was ideal for us - a good size, with modern fittings and free wi-fi. The king size bed was comfortable, and it was nice to have that little more space than you normally get, as all the rooms are actually suites with a sofa area and sink/fridge/microwave. Good shower too.
Breakfast was fine, although we did get a little bored of the same selection - not a problem if you are staying for a long weekend. At the price we paid, the fact that we had one at all was a bonus. Waffles were good, but they did seem to run low on fresh fruit during the mid week.
We used the pool and hot tub and found both to be clean and very quiet during our time there. The pool isn't great if you are planning on swimming lengths (it's very small), but the gym is there too, so fitness fanatics should be fine.
Our one small issue would be with the lifts, which use a really annoying access card system to prevent non-residents from getting onto floors. A good idea in principle, but more often than not, the cards just didn't seem to work first time.
We were very happy with our stay overall, and would definitely recommend the hotel for anyone who wishes to visit the windy city.

title: “Terrific place”
text: My husband and I chose to recover at the Tremont Plaza after he donated a kidney to me at Johns Hopkins. We needed a place close to Hopkins so that we could return several times during recovery for check ups, labs, etc. The staff at the Tremont Plaza could not be more accommodating. The room was clean, spacious, homey and provided all we needed for our extended stay needs. Nothing is too much trouble for the staff. They are kind and courteous. The deli on the ground floor is great. Always fresh made food that you can take back to room to warm up, or nice restuarant on 2nd floor, if you want to eat there. The value is incredible. I highly recommend that you choose this hotel for your stay in Baltimore. Hotel also has excellent, complimentary shuttle service. I'm telling you, this is the place!!!

title: “Classy”
text: Stayed here for the Boston marathon. It was expensive, but worth it. Couldn't beat the location & the room was large & clean.

title: “Excellent service in Houston”
text:
My stay at Crowne Plaza Houston River Oaks was fantastic. The staff was very knowledgeable, professional, courteous and above all friendly. Mandy Bates was so helpful with all our questions conerning events in the area and places to dine. 
Jackie Franks greeted us at the reservation desk and with that genuine big smile I knew my stay was going to be great. She explained all the emenities of the hotel and assured we knew what the hotel and city of Houston had to offer. This hotel gets two thumbs up. A great place to be with excellent and friendly staff.
Fina

title: “Great location, fine hotel”
text: Super great location, right near the mall and 1 block from a subway station. And the free breakfast saves a lot of $$ The rooms are large suites: it used to be an apartment that was converted to a hotel: so you're getting a multi-room suite. However, the bedroom itself is a bit on the small side. I strongly recommend this hotel to friends: it is an excellent value (the only other DC competitor it has for price & location is the Holiday Inn 1 mile west). If you are looking for a super elegant hotel with a grand, soaring lobby to meet guests, this is not it. The lobby is tiny. But, the service was fine (they held our bags for us for free on the final day) and the price & location cannot be beat.

title: “Worst Hotel and Management”
text: This place is for thugs and criminals. This place was horrible the management was not nice and the carpet needs to be replaced. There was a party going on in the close rooms around me and I got no sleep all night. I called the front desk for security but they did not stay on top of the party. I was afraid some one may get into a fight and maybe start shooting. I want ever stay at this place again.

title: “Just Right”
text: B&B with a great location, even better restaurant, and the right price. Hotel staff is part time as expected for a small B&B but the rooms are pleasant and all the historic sites are right out your front door. Will definitely stay again.

title: “Great hotel in San Francisco”
text: Location, location, location. To experience the best of any city where you stay is so important. Intercontinental Howard St is perfectly positioned, walking distance to transport, restaurants and shopping. Hotel room was spacious, well appointed and modern. Concierge team were excellent, nothing was too much trouble. Would highly recommend.

title: “just ok if all you need is somewhere to sleep”
text: upon arriving to room #1047 i was ferociously greeted by the neighboring guests dog, who almost bit me. would have been nice if front desk warned me about that. king bed size room big enough to accomodate a crib (crib $10 charge). just ok if all you need is somewhere to sleep. bed was awful. for those of you familiar with sheratons sweet sleeper bed , this is not it. best to walk to front desk if you need something most times i attempted to call them the line was busy. waited 45 minutes for bath towels to be delivered to room. mold growing on bath tub walls. location is great. 1 mile away from walmart and 15 minutes away from sea world/zoo. free parking a plus but back parking lot does not have lights @ night.

title: “Bugs!!”
text: I stayed for 9 days during my trip to Austin. For the first few days, there was no real problem, except the shower mat was dirty, and the room was run-down looking. My mother stayed in another room and was woken up by a cockroach on her face!! She complained to the manager, who said it was a cricket and that it was 'cricket season.' Later that night, a huge cockroach crawled on my bed! The only positive about this hotel is it's close to the highway, the beds are comfortable and the flatscreen TV is nice. But because of the bugs, I will not be staying here again.

title: “great service”
text: Billy rolled his cart into the room we were meeting in and it was like the saffron trucks coming over the last hill of the Silk Road. It was like spotting an oasis after crawling across the desert. It was manna from heaven.

title: “A PEARL FOR SURE........”
text:
A great hotel....right in the thick of things at Times Square. Everything is brand new. Located within 10 yards of two large theaters and within 5 minute walk of thirty theaters.
Highly reccomend for the traveller looking for cleanliness and proximity to the excitement.

title: “We Will Be Back!”
text: We live in San Antonio but wanted to be pampered for a weekend without leaving town. Our selection was a great choice. Staff was very friendly. Room was super comfortable. The property is very well maintained. Pools were very well kept and some of the nicest we have enjoyed in San Antonio. Really enjoyed the adult only pool since we had no children with us, Wait staff at the pools were friendly and efficient. Views were spectacular as well. Self parking was a bit of a hassle. A very long walk and few spaces. I know we could have chose to valet park but it was quite busy and the hotel charged a resort fee that included self parking so it was our choice. It was a great weekend and we certainly recommend the Westin at La Cantera.

title: “No complaints, good location”
text: We stayed here last october while in town for the marathon. Great location, close to almost everything, as Chicago is a great walking city. It was clean, service was good, and I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Not what we expected.”
text:
The hotel borders the run down and creepy "Tenderloin" neighborhood, so make sure to walk in the right direction at night when exiting the hotel, especially if you are a tourist, since you tend to stick out a bit... The hotel still only supplies wifi in common areas, unless you are a Hilton Honors member, I think that is pretty a pretty bad policy for a hotel in this price range. The room was quite small for holding double queen beds. The walls and the door was not stopping any disturbing sounds. All and all, i would say the hotels did not really meet our expectations given the price and suggested standard.
On the plus side, it was clean, staff was nice, it has a Starbucks and a bar/restaurant on site in the street level.

title: “Wonderfully Wicked!”
text: During my recent stay at the W Hotel in San Francisco, which also happend to be my birthday weekend, I must say, we had a fabulously Wicked Weekend. The room was great, the bed was comfy, the staff were cool and the piece of Birthday Cake in my room when we got back from seeing the final showing of Wicked...Was Way Wonderful!!! What a cool hotel. Thanks.

title: “My all time favorite hotel stay”
text: I have had a couple amazing hotel stays in NYC at other hotels, but this one surpassed them by far. I was checking in for a 10 day stay and got a complimentary upgrade to the most fabulous room that had a wrap around balcony and sitting area, and I started out with the Deluxe type from a discount site. They could not have been more accomodating and attentive with any issue that came up. The bed was so comfortable with every type of pillow on it. LIttle did I know I was going to be there for Hurricane Sandy, and spending time in my room which was like a large studio apt. by any standards was so comfortable through it all. The hotel is so close to Central Park and everything you could possibly need. During the hurricane not much was open, but thanks to the location; I had no problem finding anything I needed or places open. It is an old Hollywood type hotel with a wonderful international clientele that makes the elevator rides so interesting with all the accents. This is going to be my NYC hotel from now on. In reference to the reviews here; if you request a robe ahead of your stay, it will be there waiting for you. They will fix any issue you have (toilet running, etc) and it is an older wonderful building so sometimes it can be warmer in the halls, but you aren't there very long and better than freezing. My room was 2309 and highly recommned it, the hotel, Randolph's bar, everything. I can see why Cary Grant lived there for 12 years, and why the Beatles and Elvis Presly stayed here when they came to NYC. I am trying to add photos of my views there so hopefully they will show up.

title: “Great stay in San Antonio”
text: I tend to pick hotels cited on Trip Advisor, and now I know why this hotel is so highly rated in San Antonio. The hotel is relatively new, clean, very comfortable, and a good value for a downtown location. But the key value of this property is the management and staff who truly make your stay a great vacation experience. Simply stated, they make you feel at home in San Antonio, providing that extra measure of service, hospitality, and tourist advice. While the name says "Comfort Suites - Alamo/Riverwalk,” the actual hotel location is a few blocks from both San Antonio attractions (next to I-37) --- but the short walk to the Alamo and Riverwalk is easy and relatively safe. This hotel is a perfect choice while in San Antonio.

title: “A haven in an overpriced city”
text:
I have stayed here on many occasions. The price of hotels in New York has increased beyond belief in the last few years. So this is quite a good find
The Candlewood Suites is not a 5 star hotel, but is very comfortable. The Suites are not large, but the beds are good and having your own small mini kitchen and a very large refrigerator make it more like being at home with complimentary Wifi. There are plenty of restaurants nearby and there is a Food Emporium supermarket on 42nd Street between 9th and 10th. Times Square and most of the theatres are not far away, as is Penn Station and Port Authority. A good place to stay

title: “Very Nice Hotel...with a few negatives”
text:
Stayed a couple of days at this Hotel which is well located near DuPont Circle and downtown DC...Loved the historical décor of the hotel. The room was very clean, quiet, and spacious. The bed was very comfortable. Front staff and doorman were very helpful, professional, and friendly. 
There were a few negatives. The bathroom to our room was extremely small. It was also very disappointing to find out that they closed the restaurant which I believe that type of information should have been noted on their website.

title: “Great location, amenities, and price!”
text: I traveled here from Ohio for a business trip and was very impressed. I called from the airport hoping to check in a couple hours early and the hotel manager was extremely flexible. I was able to check in early because they had a room available and I was incredibly pleased. Rooms are spacious, and even have kitchens, which I didn't realize. Overall, my stay was wonderful. I highly recommend this hotel to anyone staying overnight to several weeks.

title: “Excellent, clean, relaxing ... looking forward to future visits!”
text: First time guest ... stayed for 5-night business trip. Despite being a very picky and selective traveler, I can confidently state that my room was very clean and comfortable. I examine every hotel room I stay in for cleanliness, insects, etc., and this experience left me with a feeling of confidence. Room had deep, subdued and relaxing colors, nice wood furniture, and many lighting options. Bed was very comfortable, luxurious sheets and comforter, and thick bathroom towels. Hotel staff very accommodating and friendly - distinctive customer service ... definitely not one of those big hotel chains! Lobby and outdoor dining area very charming and cozy. Wonderful location -- everything is walkable. Relatively quiet, upscale street, with a somewhat quaint yet trendy feel. Pricing can vary greatly, so care should be taken with regard to timing/availability of visit. I am planning a personal visit back to Chicago with wife for a long weekend -- and the Talbott is a must-have piece of that plan, unless rates are high. I would absolutely recommend to both business and personal travelers. I'm hooked, and will definitely be back.

title: “Great hotel! First Class”
text: Was there on a business trip, fantastic property. You can't go wrong with Park Hyatt's!

title: “Let down by a few little niggles”
text:
I went to New York for a week on business and chose the Park Central Hotel for one reason above all others - location location location! I wanted somewhere reasonably central, but not so busy as Times Square and its immediate vicinity, whilst also being in close proximity to Central Park. In this respect it ticks all the boxes - you can walk to Times Square and Cental Park easily, whilst there are subway stops nearby and reasonable quality diners for those nights you don't fancy venturing out! The staff were also good - check in and check out were quick and requests for ironing boards etc were dealt with efficiently. The rooms are also above average size for NY and I didn't feel claustrophobic living in one for a week (although obviously I didn't spend a lot of time there!).
Unfortunately though, that is where the praise ends... My first complaint is minor and forgivable given that it is such a large hotel and therefore hard to maintain - wallpaper peeling off the walls in the bathroom, slightly ripped curtain, other minor aesthetic things. The room was clean though so I don't hold this against them too much.
The lack of free wifi was disappointing. I know other hotels in a similar price range do provide this. $14 per day to access the internet is ridiculous - you are better off buying a coffee in the starbucks next door and logging on for free!
Next, my room safe wasn't working. Admittedly I didn't mention this to the front desk, and if I had, maybe they would have given me a new room, but I was already unpacked by then.
Finally, and most annoyingly, my room (and the whole building for that matter) was SO hot! It was early March, I had both windows open as much as possible and the temeperature at the lowest setting possible and I was practically melting! I tried turning the air con off altogether and it made no difference.
All in all, nothing dreadful, but if little details really matter to you, maybe you are better off looking for an alternative.

title: “The place to stay in SF!”
text: We just had a lovely week stay at this Inn. I assure you that you are in for a treat! Our check-in was great in the the very cozy lobby with the fireplace glowing. Up the old fashioned lift to our little hide-a-way. Very English cottage, large living space with bathroom with deep tub, dressing room and wet bar in a small alcove. Nice ironed linens on comfy bed. The breakfasts were great and varied. Good coffee too! Wine and cheese great to have in front of fire in the evening. This is the place..hated to leave. Would go back in a moment!

title: “Good enough ..”
text: Stayed 3 nights recently. Rooms very clean, beds comfy & staff everywhere very helpful & friendly; very close to subway line; disappointed with fount door service to obtain taxis & no bar/ restaurant /& farther than expected from times square/ theatre District. Booked in a vacation package with itravel.com & would not use it again as flight home brutal ( 1 HR direct flight normally & package had in a 4 HR connection wait,,, )

title: “Rudest hotel staff ever encountered.”
text: For all the time and artistry the owner put into this hotel, he scrimped on hiring employees dedicated to customer service. It is an alien concept to the front desk. I've never experienced anything like it at any other hotel, ever. Like we were an imposition. We arrived early and exhausted and asked if we could check in. Instead we were given a loud lecture by a rude woman whom I presume was a manager of some sort in front of other guests about how "our check time is standard like in all hotels..." Nothing about what they "could" do. When our room was ready, the key couldn't open a door that didn't fit tightly in the frame. So the same rude woman turns up and presto, she opens it in one try after pulling the door toward her. Glares at us like we've never opened a door before and coldly explains that they're "special locks". We eventually got the hang of opening the door ourselves. And calling taxis ourselves, finding restaurants ourselves, etc. We just didn't bother. And that seems to be the way they want it.

title: “Good value, great location, will stay again.”
text: I arrived about 4 hours before check in time. I was allowed to park (great perk, parking is included with the room) and come back to check in. Room was very clean. No complaints at all. Location is fantastic. For any driving to New York, this is THE place to stay. Are there more fancy hotels in the city? Yes, but is the price worth it when the majority of the time is spent outside the room? I go to NYC for NYC not the hotel room, so I was EXTREMELY pleased with the price, location, and quality of the hotel. I will most definitely stay here my next visit to NYC. I found the staff helpful and friendly.

title: “Great value and view”
text: Stayed with my kids for a week. Super friendly and helpful staff, comfortable room with a great view. Great place to people watch and to be active. Walking distance to everything you could need. Clean, pleasant pool and hot tub, and plenty of beach stuff to borrow. Secure parking for a very reasonable rate. Highly recommend to others, and hope to come back!

title: “okay stay”
text: I have stayed at this hotel two times, twice were okay, one was excellent. This last stay was just alright. The hotel is remodelling. The work crew worked right outside my room. For some reason, there was a musty odor in the room which got better after I aired out the room all day. I did not feel safe leaving the window open at night, however. The free parking was a big plus, and the hotel is near most of the SOMA action. The front desk was pleasant but somewhat slow. While I never felt unsafe walking in the area, there are some interesting characters on the street.

title: “No Frills Airport Hotel”
text: There is not much to say either here about this hotel other than its next to the airport . I got this hotel really cheap when I called and asked for a rate. It was a much better deal than the Sheraton Suites or the Marroitt. The staff was pretty nice however, the hotel itself was just plain old average. The free internet was a good plus about this hotel and I managed to get some work done before leaving on my flight in the morning. There is not much to expect from this hotel other than a bed, a TV, and a shuttle to and from Philly international so it does serve its purpose.

title: “Good place for a quick rest before a late night flight!”
text: We took an Alaskan cruise that got us back to Seattle at 7:30 am on July 7. Our flight home did not leave until 11:45 pm. We were able to book a room at the Radisson prior to our cruise that allowed us to go to the hotel at 9 am get checked in & stay until 9:00 pm, when we took the shuttle to the airport. We were happy to be able to sleep, shower and get a meal before our red eye flight! While we paid for the entire night, we were more than happy for their willingness to accommodate our needs!

title: “Excellent value”
text:
The Drury Plaza Riverwalk is a great choice for the money. While the property is a bit worn, the staff are very friendly, helpful and know their city. There is an extensive 'happy hour' buffet every night featuring both hot and cold food, AND, three free drinks, including beer, wine and cocktails. Needless to say, it was very crowded and seating was at a premium. Ditto for the expansive, free breakfast buffet, which surpasses the normal fare.
While the rooms are somewhat tired, they are nonetheless comfy, clean and roomy enough for a couple to spread out in, with surprisingly high ceilings. Views vary according to location, but all are urban. The hotel has direct access to the riverwalk, for those who, like ourselves, want to explore this unique marketplace.
An excellent choice for those looking for value and location, especially for families

title: “Clean and nice”
text: This was our first time stay at this hotel and we thought it was a good experience! The staff was very courteous and accommodating. It was a little higher priced than what we usually like to pay but it had the "extras" to compensate the higher price. Indoor pool, microwave and mini fridge in room etc... We will be back to use the pool!

title: “A Great Hotel”
