text: We stayed here in March as we were on a Hockey tour. The Hotel is literally opposite the Arena so was a perfect location for us as we had two matches to go to in the four days we were there. Also it is right next to China Town (which is nothing to write home about) and also it is not to far from all the tourist attractions. The cost was a little high at $217 per night but the hotel, location and amenities were worth it to us. The Hotel's restaurant we only ate once in as food was really expensive, but very good. Another nice touch was the wine receptions every evening, which were free receptions for those staying at the hotel. The bathroom needed updating but was perfectly usable and the min bar has to be seen to be believed. All in all I would recommend this hotel.

title: “The Best”
text: The best hotel I ever been to. The staff are all great nice helpful. love frankie the door guy,when we come to Boston we will be at hotel commonwealth for sure the baseball room was great,and everything is so clean and neat close to the ballpark,good parking for are car. the staff is what makes it they you better then family real nice group,please dont change that staff. cant wait to come back. forever yours Anthony&Michelle Gulotta.

title: “best little motel in Santa Monica”
text:
very quint and atmospheric motel in a best location,clean ,good price ,nice breakfast and free parking .My husband and I love it,this is the third time we stay there and will stay again..
My room had a fridge,good TV,plenty of hot water...internet service is excellent ..plenty of good restaurants and cafes in a walking distance...Julia,the manager run a good business and is extremely kind and helpful...They can also drop you of to the airport for a small fee...we highly recommend it

title: “Hooker posted ad on Craigslist only to rob me. Thugs stay there.”
text: Horrible..The front desk was helpful. They should do background checks on the lowlife that stay there. Times change. I used to rent monthly years back. wasn't like this.

title: “Wonderful Experience!”
text: I stayed for 4 nights in January. Got a great last minute rate through the hotel's website. I took the "L" from Midway airport, got off at Madison station, and was literally steps from the hotel entrance. The location absolutely cannot be beat! Hotel staff was friendly and helpful. The room was very clean, comfortable and spacious, esp. the bathroom. The noise from the "L" was not bothersome to me. I would definitely stay at the Silversmith again -- very highly recommend!

title: “Best in Scottsdale”
text: Beautiful hotel, quiet and convenient. Service is outstanding. Grounds are beautiful. The Valencia Casita was wonderful and comfortable. The weather was warm for a November trip and the A/C in the room would not maintain the cooler temperatures without several adjustments during the night but that is was minor and everything else was as expected.

title: “A nice quiet place in the heart of downtown LA”
text:
We booked this hotel online and were pleasantly surprised. The room was clean, spacious and modern. The rooftop garden was like heaven on earth, and we did spend some time there reading while waiting to attend Thanksgiving festivities with family. The location is very convenient and it's quick to get onto 101 just a few blocks away. And little Tokyo with its restaurants is a short walk away...yes you can actually walk from this hotel in LA!
The only negatives: No pool or even a hot tub. Parking was costly, but we later realized that there is a lot across the street half the price.

title: “Could have been worse, I guess”
text:
Looking for the silver lining on my extended stay was the staff. They were ALL friendly, helpful, and alway eager to assist. This is from the desk staff, bell staff to housekeeping. Britney was the best. Always had a smile, a big hello, and asked if you needed anything special in regards to your room. The desk staff were absolutly great when it came to assisting with business needs, faxes, copies, at any hour of the day or night. The computers in the lobby area is a great idea.
The rooms were drafty. When the wind was blowing outside, the curtains were moving on the inside. During the rain storms, my ceiling would leak. I thought this odd considering I was on the 20th floor and there were other floors above me. The exterior noise continuiosly intruded upon the room, even on the 20th floor. Anytime day or night, sirens from medical and police vehicles were heard. Every friday night, like clockwork, there was some sort of altercation from the restaurant across the street where you were awoken by fights or gunshots. There were times as you looked out the window Baltimore's finest was putting up yellow tape and questioning those in the area. The activity would settle down about 2:30 am. The food in the attached restaurant, Shula's was overpriced and the wait staff on weekends for the most part were either slow, unfriendly or non existant. 
The area outside of the hotel was dubious at best. Any travel to the west of the hotel had to be in groups. Lexington Market was OK during daylight but there were elements there that still were abusive. The use of the free bus service was helpful to leave the area and head to a safer part of town. When in Baltimore remember the purple and orange line. Many interesting places to eat and partake in the Federal Hill area and at the harbor. 
If I go to Baltimore again I would be sure to stay somewhere else.

title: “comfort inn caution”
text:
I have stayed at the Comfort Inn twice. The first time was alright, the second time the room was unacceptable and management didn't care. The location is close to downtown but the neighborhood is a little seedy. 
While there is plenty of parking you may have to push aside empty boxes of stolen merchandise if you have to park in the back lot. I would only stay here if you got a good rate and just needed a place to sleep.

title: “Needs updating”
text:
Very old and outdated rooms , all facilities are outdated . Would not recommend location for first time visitors wanting to see more of san diego . Had no sleep on 1 of 3 nights of our stay due to a very large noisey group of drunken people getting off a party cruise and hanging around the resort with out being asked to move on for a number of hours after midnight .
Only positives were good food in restaurant and being so close to seaworld .

title: “Lots of Noise, lousy security”
text: I was at the Capital Hitlon for a meeting this weekend. ON friday night at around 3am a group of people came in and made a ton of noise. I called security and it quieted down.. But only for a few minutes. I called security 3 other times and they did nothing about it. Security told me to complain, becuse they are understaffed. Considering I was planning a meeting next year for over 1000 at this hotel, this terribly disturbed me. Manegement was very responsive the next day and updgrade me to a suite, however, they need to do something about this.

title: “Disappointing”
text: The online photos gave me hope, but the amenities are sorely lacking here. The walls are paper thin, many rooms face a noisy highway, the Internet was as slow as dial-up, and the parking garage has such narrow ramps and turns that I could barely get a large sedan out of it.

title: “Wonderful stay, great location!”
text: Was in Seattle for a long weekend conference. Friendly staff, clean and comfortable. Good price for the location. Great location in the heart of downtown convention center district. Easy walking to all the tourist spots. When I come back to seattle with my family this summer, I plan to stay here again, in a bigger room.

title: “Sheraton was great!”
text: My husband and our 1 year old stayed at the Sheraton recently as a long weekend trip to visit friends. We were greeted happily by the front desk. Our room was much larger than expected which was wonderful since my daughter can't sit still for two minutes. We made two requested services that were answered quickly. The location is wonderful: Riverside, walking distance to multiple restaurants/shops, Michigan Ave, Navy Pier.

title: “Take Advantage of Car Service”
text: My wife and I stayed there for a wedding in September 2008, so really don't have that much to offer about the hotel, itself. But one thing we would want to point out is that they do have a complimentary car service to anywhere within 3 miles of the hotel. They don't make that especially well known, which is why I am writing this, so that Trip Advisor users know about it. Given the fact that the hotel is somewhat isolated, and it's a good half hour walk (in the heat) to the nearest commercial area (for eating, etc).,the car service is good to know about. I heard that the food prices are very expensive for breakfast at the hotel, so going to that commercial area is a nice diversion. There is a Rice Food Emporium in that area, which is a very nice and upscale gourmet market, as well as other restaurants. A positive of the hotel is that we found the rooms to be quiet.

title: “Spectacular stay!”
text:
My husband and I stay at the W in SF on a fairly regular basis. I LOVE this hotel. From the moment we enter the valet, we feel pampered. It seems that the W, a Starwood property, has thought of everything. Let me count the ways...
The valet - though we often drive up in a gigantic Ford F550, dually, dump truck totally covered in mud, the valet is always accommodating -- more than accommodating, actually. Our truck in the W valet is a hilarious sight, and I love that they welcome us so heartily. 
The front desk - We've stayed at the W at least 10 times over the years. We have only had great experiences checking in and out. One morning we were leaving to catch a flight before anything (Starbucks, Pete's - anything) opened, and the woman that checked us out went out of her way to get my husband coffee and tea for me. What service!
The room - We usually stay in a corner suite. I love these rooms. The bathrooms are very well lit -- perfect for putting on makeup (this is something that's often overlooked by other hotels). The products are wonderful, and include not just shampoo and soap, but also wonderful conditioner and the BEST lotion. The bathtub is deep -- perfect for a relaxing soak. I sleep astoundingly well in the W beds. I love that the duvets are crisp and white and the pillows are squishy and down. The W rooms feel clean, fresh and new.
This is a small thing, but my husband and I don't have a TV at home, and both of us really enjoy watching HGTV and the Food Network when we go to a hotel. The last three, very wonderful hotels that we've stayed in have not had those channels. The W does. 
The restaurant - I've mostly eaten breakfast at the W. I've only had good meals there, and I believe everything they serve is organic, which I appreciate. 
The bar/scene - The W bar scene is hip and fun. If you're up for it, the bar is generally going off most nights. You can hang at the tables in the bar, upstairs or on the couches off to the side. On the weekends they have a DJ, and it gets pretty riotous. Fun!
Pets - My husband and I had to pick up our new dog at the SF airport, and stayed at the W that night. A dog bed, organic dog treats and food bowls were waiting for us on our arrival. 
Finally, the W uses all eco-friendly cleaners and detergents. Another small, but significant detail. Overall, this hotel that caters to business travelers is also fantastic for leisure as well.

title: “Not a 5*”
text:
I went Boston / Fairmont with my sister, on vacation! 
The restoration was great and the Hotel keep the important thing in architecture and decoration, wich is amazing this days! 
The concierge / front desk staff are very polite and helpfull.
The room (i've got the double double deluxe) was big with very confortable beds and a cozy bathroom.
The hotel area its amazing - the newburry St its great, with 3-4 restaurants in every block, the best stores... and easy to go to other parts of the town !!!
I have two important complains (for the Hotel and already told about it to the Manager):
- there arent security at night on the doors - i almost was stolen waiting my car, then i tell on front desk about it and they send a guard to stay with me... They said the security man alk around the hotel... but I stayed 15 minutes and didnt see him at all...
- the vallet and door men, they are snobish and rude !!! They dont know how to treat a guest !!! 
But the hotel its amazing and I definitely will stay there again !!!

title: “Outstanding location but $$$ and deceiving”
text:
Of course, location is everything for this hotel: right in the middle of Times Square. Hard to beat.
The hotel is so huge it becomes overwhelming. It has 49 floors, 1892 rooms, 57 suites and 6 restaurants. Even if staff is friendly and professional, you just don't feel you belong there. You don't feel confortable. All human proportion is crushed under the traffic going around and the gigantism of the place (high speed elevators, 2 lobby floors, 40 floor high atrium, etc.)
The room was nice, confortable, spacious and up to Marriott standard. But your one the nearly 2000 rooms. No personnal sense here. No need to train staff to recognize who or to great you by your name !
Prices are also overwhelming. All prices (standard room around 500$/night, parking 50$/night, etc.) There are better deals around in Times Square.

title: “Refreshing place to stay”
text:
Normally stay downtown, however decided to give this place a try due to its close proximity to the meetings I was attending on the West side of Fort Worth. 
This is a very nice property, and is very well maintained. The front office is very friendly and made the stay enjoyable, almost like being part of a family. 
They service a light "snack" type meal in the evening along with complimentary beer and wine.
There are plenty of restaraunts within walking distance.
Great place to stay - will definitely stay here on future business trips to Fort Worth.

title: “Happy Thanksgiving”
text: We stayed at the Ritz Carlton Philadelphia over Thanksgiving and our visit was everything we hoped it would be. The staff at the desk, on the executive floor and in housekeeping were very gracious. We had a beautiful room overlooking Independence Hall and William Penn. The views were outstanding. Thanksgiving dinner at 10 Arts left a bit to be desired; we had high hopes for the executive chef who was also the winner of Top Chef, but we were disappointed. The prix fixe menu lacked creativity and the meal itself was either dull or overly salted. Everything else about the property is superb. Will definitely visit again!

title: “Excellent Location and very pleasant stay”
text:
We stayed here for 4 nights in early December and had a terrific time. The hotel is in an excellent location, right in the middle of Manhattan. We had a corner room which gave amazing views over the city and was much bigger than I would have expected for a city centre hotel. 
We ate in the hotel restaurant on the first night of our stay and they food was very good. I had Chicken Lollipops to start and Meatloaf for my main course and could not manage a desert after. It was well presented and both dishes were very enjoyable. The service was incredibly good, we had a chap called Tony as our waiter and he was incredibly polite and attentive. 
The room was always well stocked and presented when we came back to it and the number of pillows on the bed was slightly ridiculous, but in a good way.
The bar area was also a nice place to start an evening, we tended to meet with the rest of our group in this area before heading out. The range of drinks is impressive and the bar staff were always bright and friendly.
We had a really good stay in New York and a large part of that was due to having a lovely base to operate from.

title: “Our Favourite for several Years”
text: We stayed 1992 for the first time at Castle Inn Motel. It's our favourite !!! In 2003 we stayed their for the 5th time. Top Location ! Great restaurants for breakfast and dinner nearby in Polkstreet. Very Quiet location and the accommodations were very comfortable with a refrigerator and microwave in the room.

title: “Nice Hotel”
text: My Wife and I stayed for a couple nights in Memphis in November, just for a quick trip away to see the local Memphis sights. I searched many Memphis hotels on the internet before deciding on the Madison. First off...every picture you see on their website is acurate and realistic. So the hipe is not false...it's truly very elegant. We found the staff to be very accomodating and friendly. We never waited more than a few minutes for our car from the valet. And the restaurant staff was just as accomodating. The only downfall is that Memphis is not a safe place to roam at night....unless you are extremely street smart. Don't carry cash, and never remove your wallet from your pocket, and ladies...don't even bring a purse...Men-carry credit cards only and leave them in your front pocket...just word to the wise... on the bright side, we did see lots of police in downtown Memphis...Thank You Jesus. As for eats...you gotta go to the Rendevouz...Excellent Ribs!

title: “Epitome of customer service: a true story”
text:
My husband and I stayed at Hotel Max for one night on a quick trip from Portland to see a particular exhibit at the Seattle Art Museum. After checking out of the hotel and spending a few hours at the SAM, I realized I had inadvertently thrown away our return train tickets. I called the hotel and was told the room had already been cleaned and the garbage can emptied. I was dismayed but, hey, what do you do. Thirty minutes later I received a call from the hotel to tell me housekeeping had gone through the trash and found my tickets! I was thrilled but totally surprised when they offered to send a driver to deliver the tickets to me at the SAM - all free of charge. Wow.
As a quick side note - I travel a lot for business and let me tell you, regardless of the chain, hotels all look the same after a while. It's refreshing to stay somewhere that actually has a personality. (I do agree, however, the rooms ARE small - but what do you need all that extra space for anyway?)

title: “Working out the kinks, but it's still a Hilton”
text:
I understand that this Hilton hotel used to be the Tudor Hotel, and it did not join the Hilton family of hotels until April 1st, 2010. The giant Tudor Hotel sign that is still on the top makes this Hilton pretty easy to find walking east from Grand Central Station. 
As a traveler who is used to the Hilton Gold and Diamond experience, I was disappointed in the quality of this hotel in comparison to the other ones at which I've stayed. 
There were definitely good points to the hotel, however. The beds and pillows were very comfortable, as one who regularly stays at Hiltons would expect. The blackout curtains kept the sunlight out and on the higher floors (I was on 13), there was very little street noise that made its way into the room. As is also typical with Hiltons, the decorations were tasteful and it was obvious that the company has invested a substantial amount of money in updating the hotel since its acquisition. The rooms were also very clean, which is particularly reassuring given the recent bedbug epidemic in NYC hotels. At no time did I fear that the cleanliness was subpar.
There were also some substantial drawbacks to the hotel:
- My room was not ready at my requested time that I included with my reservation. .
-Being accustomed to the Gold and Diamond treatment, I was not offered a room upgrade (which I understand given it was NYC the weekend prior to Christmas) and there was no executive lounge. Complimentary bottles of water were also not provided in the room.
-The elevators are excrutiatingly slow; not to mention tiny and only 2 out of the 3 were operating. Upon checkout, we waited in excess of five minutes for an elevator. Ordinarily, I would take the stairs; however, that is very inconvenient when you're on the 13th floor and have luggage to take with you.
-The walls are paper thin. I mean, you literally hear EVERYTHING that is going on in the room next to you. This is hardly ideal for a romantic weekend away. 
So, all in all, kind of a mixed bag. At a macro level, it's a clean, comfortable place to stay and the appearance is on brand with what one would expect out of a Hilton. But, it is also very apparent that there are still improvements that need to be made in order for this to be an excellent choice for all travelers.

title: “Classy stay at the Roosevelt”
text: Booked a 3 night stay at the Roosevelt after reading other reviews, have to say from check-in to check-out it was fab. Our room on the tenth floor was spacious, spotlessly clean and the bed was amazing. We never ate breakfast at the hotel as it seemed quite pricy but there is a deli acrosss the road which does great food all day. The bar is very cosy with its leather slouchy chairs and fireplace. The staff were very helpfull and courtious, no problems getting a late checkout, or getting bags looked after until evening after checking out. Looking forward to next trip to NY to stay at The Roosevelt again!

title: “Best boutique hotel in the city!”
text: Have stayed a few times at the Roger Smith - knew someone that had worked there so it was convenient. Location is great - On 47th & Lexington, only a few blocks from Grand Central. The hotel is older, could use a little bit of updating, almost all over, but it's an older hotel, so you have to appreciate it's older beauty. We were able to get a corner suite with a deck. You have to stay at this place to appreciate it's beauty. Will I stay there again...for sure! It's just got old fashion charm!

title: “Thouroughly Impressed”
text:
I don't usually stay in high end hotels, but got used Priceline and this came back as the accepted hotel for my bid. It's probably one of the nicest hotels I've stayed in. Upon arrival, I went to park the car across the street at the Market St parking garage ($12 a day) (It's the same one they use if you use their valet parking), and my wife checked in. She asked if we could get a king size bed, but also put us on the riverwalk side. So even with a priceline price, we still got treated like anybody else. It was a Sunday night stay and the place wasn't too busy, so that's maybe why the upgrade, but oh well. 
The bed was very comfortable and the room was a good size as well. Bath was pretty larger, very clean, and elegant. Great location, since only about a block or so from the main area on the Riverwalk where all the restuarants are. 
I'd definitely recommend this hotel.

title: “Really good location; very nice property”
text:
We stayed at the Fairfield Inn and Suites in July 2011. My husband was doing business most of the time, but I was doing the tourist thing. The location of the hotel is fantastic for the price. It is in the middle of Chinatown and easy walking distance to Capitol Hill and many other DC amenities. What you can't walk to is easily accessible by the Metro -- the hotel is in the middle of two stops on the Red Line -- one of them (Chinatown -- Gallery) connects to the Green and Yellow lines so you can get into both Maryland and Virginia from there. It was a great centre from which to operate.
The hotel has been recently refurbished and feels new, clean and very modern. We were there in the middle of a serious heat wave and the air conditioning had no trouble handling it. Breakfast is part of the deal and it was one of the better ones I've found in hotels. Free wi-fi and DSL internet is also available.
We also spent a fair bit of time in the Irish Pub attached to the hotel -- I did say it was a heat wave! But there were a number of other good restaurants within easy walking distance. I'd stay there again if I get back to DC.

title: “Perfect surprise”
text: My husband and I stayed here for a weekend a few years ago and loved it. Tons of character, comfortable room with plenty of space, outstanding location. We walked or biked everywhere, and the hotel staff were so accomodating, letting us stash our bikes in their storage room. For us, this inn set the standard for hip, urban boutique hotels.

title: “Could not have been better”
text: Before arriving I wondered how Hotel Teatro could possibly live up to its overwhelmingly positive reviews. My 4-day stay, a mixture of business and family visit, was flawless. The room was clean and comfortable with an extraordinarily comfortable bed with marvelous linens that were changed daily. Breakfast in the restaurant downstairs, while not included, was not overly pricy and delicious. The service in every part of the hotel was exceptional. It is only a block and a half from the many fine restaurants on Larimer Square and within easy walking distance of most things you'll want to visit downtown. And if you don't want to walk, they have a free van service to anything within 3 miles of the hotel. I will definitely stay here when I return to Denver.

title: “MUSTY...due for a major remodel”
text: Hotel is very dated, way over priced and very humid, INSIDE the rooms(mold maybe?). When entering the lobby you will notice the smell immediately. The toilet in our room took at least 4 minutes to refill, very noisy. On a positive note, it IS connected to the Galleria. We could have stayed at the Hilton down the street and paid a driver to run us back and forth in a limo and still saved money and the rooms are new there. Side note: the management could put a sign at the third floor exit indicating that the hotel restaurant is located in the mall. We witnessed at least three other couples exit the elevators looking for the restaurant, without success.

title: “L.A. with style”
text:
When you arrive, the first thing you should check out is the pool lounge. A great place to spend some time, and to take a few drinks looking for the sunshine. The rooms are not big, but very confortable. The construction is a little old, but well kept.
Recommended.

title: “Lukewarm shower, and dirty toilet”
text: One of my bottom 5 hotel experience: the toilet cover wasn’t wiped clean, shower was lukewarm, service was slow. Even though I’m a fairly loyal Starwood customer, will try Four Seasons or Sofitel next time in Philly.

title: “A true gem in the city!”
text: Stayed one night. Really nice. Took a cab from Powell St BART station to the Fairmont. It's a classic hotel. Really nice rooms, awesome lobby, and restaurant. I liked the terrace garden. Overall a very good hotel.

title: “Just ok...Highly Average”
text:
First the Positives: Bed was very comfortable. Chair in the room was perfect for working in with the adjustable arms-perfect for laptop or book reading. My room had a balcony so I could air out the room. Front desk staff were pleasant and helpful with dinner recommendations. The Charter House was fabulous! Our server, Johnny was magnificent! The appetizers were delicious and our entres were scrumptious! We did not have dessert, but they looked decadent!
Areas for improvement: Hotel in general had stale/musty/old/cleaning products smell throughout the hotel. In the rooms, the smell intensified. The lighting in the room was poor; very dim. My room had 5 table lamps; two of which did not work. Though I did not have my bed linen or towels changed everyday, the room appeared just barely cleaned. The ice bucket was not emptied and trash was still in one garbage can, though the bed was made up. As a female business traveler, the door did not seem secure with one flimsy latch. At last, my colleague discovered a dean roach in her room upon returning the first night....YIKES! Paying for parking in addition to the room rates is outrageous! And all except one young man, the valet staff were not friendly.

title: “Great location!”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for a girls weekend in NYC and to go to a Broadway show, we didn't spend a lot of time is the room, if you are in NYC that the last thing you want to do! 
this hotel was OK, room size was great for NYC standers.
Location is the best of this hotel! you are near all the attractions, walking distance from time square, central park, you have to try the burger bar, go there early for lunch! awesome burgers!
no real closet in the room, very old TV's very strange on a 4 stars hotel
 Front desk staff was efficient but little bit of less rudeness will be great, check in and out was quick and easy.
housekeeping service was excelent! and super friendly....
overall is a great hotel with a perfect midtown location if you find the right price this is the hotel for you! i paid around $150 per night so it was perfect!

title: “My stay at a Day's Inn”
text:
Room was large, clean and most importantly Quite! 
Hotel desk staff very friendly and helpful.
What I do not like about the survey is that it must be at least 100 characters, for which was not needed by me to get my points across, so now I am having to continue to write a run-on sentence to satisfy a idiotic requirement that is making me like Day's Inn less, even though this is potentially not a Day's in request to make this review 100 characters. There, that should meet 100 characters.

title: “Amazing Stay at a Modern-meets-Historic Boutique Hotel in Downtown San Diego's Gaslamp District”
text: My husband and I stayed here on our wedding night and had an absolute blast! The hotel is in the heart of the historic Gaslamp Quarter in Downtown San Diego. The hotel is San Diego's first, est. in 1890. It has a great mix of modern sexy Italian design and historic rustic brick building. The staff is kept small which makes for a more intimate experience, as they are able to get to know their guests better and their own colleagues. They are extremely nice and personable, and very knowledgeable. Our personal concierges, Brenteny and Carlos, were excellent! We had a corner penthouse suite right on 5th and F St which made for excellent people watching, which I absolutely love! Expect to hear some level of noise, as you are in a downtown historic building. The room had high ceilings, a huge jacuzzi tub, a big shower that rains down on you, a great sound system, and a very very comfy bed. The hotel is centrally located so you can walk to just about everything. We definitely look forward to staying at the Keating again!

title: “Great Boutique Hotel”
text:
The Beacon XV is a great boutique hotel that gives you the look of feel of traditional New England with all the modern touches. The staff go out of their way to assist you with any needs, its clean, cosy and quiet.
Of course Moo's the restaurant is highly recommended.

title: “You can do much better”
text:
We just returned from a brief trip to Boston and stayed at the Midtown for one Saturday night. We chose it after reading reviews here that suggested it if you were going to a game at Fenway due to it's proximity to the park and low parking rates. If your primary focus is to be close to Fenway and pay relatively little to park and you don't care much about the actual hotel experience, this will work for you. On the other hand, I wouldn't recommend it if you are at all looking for a nice, comfortable, quiet and well managed hotel. Everything about it feels budget and truly, it's just a motel that they plunked down in the middle of the city. 
There's nothing horrendous to report, just a lot of annoying issues with the room and the overall accomadations. We were very glad to move on from the Midtown and stay at the Commonwealth which is also very near Fenway, but a quantum leap in experience. Yes, it's more expensive, but in the case of the Midtown Hotel, you definitely get what you pay for.

title: “Nice Hotel, expensive room service”
text: I just stayed one night while in town on business. The hotel is massive with an upscale feel, especially for a Doubletree. The room was updated very nicely and included an LCD television. I felt parking was a bit expensive for a Doubletree though. The room was clean and bed comfortable. The thing I was most disappointed about was the room service. The choices were very limited. Since I didn't want to spend $30 + on a steak or pork chops, I ordered a sandwich. At 7:30, they were out of the beef dip. So, I ordered a side Caesar salad with a side of chicken and a Coke. My total was $40. For that, I would have went out for a steak, not a salad. The hotel is literally a one minute drive to the rental car drop-off which was very convenient. Over all, I would recommend this hotel. I would not, under any circumstance order room service from this hotel though.

title: “Perfect location, friendly staff, clean rooms”
text: Worth every penny. tastefully decorated Boutique hotel, closest very nice, new hotel to Alcatraz, Pier 39..etc. being from San Fran..LOVE IT

title: “Great hotel, fantastic location”
text: We had a great stay at the Salisbury in feb 2012. The hotel is quite old but that doesn't bother us at all. Our room (on the 17th floor) was very big for NYC standards, we had two double and very comfortable beds, lovely big bathroom and a very nice shower. Huge mirrors in bathroom, plenty of space for 2 people to both put on makeup. Only problem is the electrics-they didn't seem to work that well. I don't know if that's a problem with our electricals, or their electrics, but either way my curling tongs didn't ever get to full temperature... Minor problem in the grand scheme though. We also had to wait sometimes for the lift, there's only 2 of them. Otherwise, there's a starbucks opposite, deli next door but one, and a duane reade on 57th and 6th, not to mention being opposite Carnagie Hall, 2 blocks from the park, easy access to fifth avenue (and Tiffanys!!) subway on both ends of the block, with easy access to times square, or it's a pleasant 10 minute walk along 7th. All in all, we had a great stay, no major complaints but the price we paid, we can't complain at all. Wouldn't hesitate in staying here again when I come back.

title: “Not so great!!!”
text:
The rate was good, but you know what they say..."You get what you pay for."
Room was dirty, pool was dirty, entrance to parking lot had glass on it. Our rooms sprinkler system had a bag over it, toilette didn't flush. We were travelling with friends, and their room wasn't even clean. Luckily, there were un-used rooms available, but room was still dirty.
A little investment in the hotel would help...some plumbing work, new paint and new carpeting would spruce things up.
I would recommend if you are looking for a cheap hotel and you aren't picky of a little dirt. Not recommended for folks who are a little more picky of their accomodations.

title: “Marriott was great, but..”
text: We stayed at the Marriott for one night while attending a game in Uptown Charlotte. The hotel itself was very nice, from the lobby to the pool, workout room, staff, I really can't complain at all. I felt like I was staying at a very upscale property, but the price was not bad at all. The room was very clean, although basic. The bed was very comfortable! Parking was convienent but they do charge 12.00 per day to park, but I actually thought it was going to be 20.00, so the discount was a nice surprise. The only downfall at this hotel was Champs Sports Bar. The bar itself was nice, but the bartenders were very rude to us, and to everyone else as far as I could see. We waited 20 minutes for drinks and was then told when we asked about them that 'she had about 20 drinks orders in her head and she forgot ours'. The poor couple next to us waiting an hour for 2 sandwiches, and then they came out cold. Whe asked how everything was they told the bartender their complaints, but she just shrugged and said 'sorry', and walked away. Customer service was obviously not a priority here. Other than that our stay was excellent, and we will definitely return to the Marriott, we just won't dine at the restaurants. There are many more in walking distance that are happy to have your business.

title: “Super value”
text: Embassy Suites offer great value with free full breakfast and free happy hour. We were there for college football, the place was very crowded and lively. Enjoyed the fitness room and the amenities. The hotel was clean and most staff was friendly and helpful. Not the greatest location, but it was so brutally hot outside it didn't matter. Inside was the place to be. Con- slow elevator.

title: “Wish I knew...reservation lost/no room at inn...Never again”
text: I was very much looking forward to a five night stay at The Jewel. I had a prepay reservation thru Hotwire that I had made in February. Armed with confirmation numbers for both the Jewel and Hotwire I arrived at 1030pm the day of check in to find The Jewel could not find my reservation and had no room to accommodate me. I was sent instead to their 'sister 'hotel' the Club Quarters a few doors down. After lengthy discussions with the hotel front desk clerk and with Hotwire this was the only option available to me. I was told that the Jewel's general manager would call me the next day and that I would be re-accommodated at the Jewel the next day for the last four nights of my stay. No call ever came. I was never re-accommodated. I felt as though prepay reservations were shuttled to the 'sister hotel' without regard for the payment having already been made for accommodation at the Jewel. This was a complete customer service disaster. Never again.

title: “Terrific Service”
text: We took our two grandchildren to New York for the Memorial Day weekend and selected the Affinia Manhattan based on its reviews. The service was outstanding! We ordered room service our first night and they were there within 5 minutes. They also delivered a rollaway bed to the room which we didn't really need. The room was a bit small for four people, but we liked having the kitchenette, especially with children. There was a very good deli next door. It was a good experience and the kids loved New York.

title: “Tired hotel.”
text:
Located in the heart of the Theater District, the location is the best thing about this hotel. The easy access to entertainment venues, nightlife, restaurants, shopping and historic sights are the best things about this hotel.
The overall hotel decor is clean, but really tired and dull. 
The room was small and had a very awkward layout. The bathroom was clean, but desperate for an update. 
The noise from the street and within the hotel made a restful sleep almost impossible even from the eighth floor!
Next visit to Boston we will stay somewhere else.

title: “Amazing!...besides the food...”
text: My parents had given me and my boyfriend a certificate for a night and when I made the resrvation I was told that we were going to get two double beds but I asked if possible that I could get a single queen. On check in I was told that I was getting a single queen (maybe it was a king) on the 29th floor. I was AMAZED when I walked into the room on how nice it was! It was alot better than I was expecting. Of course the first thing I do is test the bed and it was probably the most comfortable one I've slept on in a long time. The valet people were really nice and helped me figure out how to avoid traffic areas to get to Pike Place Market and the aquarium. When trying to find how to get to my grandma's apartment the concierge was more than willing to help me with a smile. I think the only problem I had with the stay was the next day we had deciced to have breakfast in the restaurant after waiting about 10 minutes for the waiter to acknoledge us we decided to forget about ordering from the menu we may as well do the buffet since it felt like we weren't being payed attention to. The buffet was decent but could've had more for the price I personally feel like if I had taken the same amount I paid for the both of us and taken it somewhere else I could've gotten ALOT better breakfast.

title: “Fabulous Regency Club rooms”
text: Checked in late one night to a Regency Club level room - 32nd floor in the West tower. I chose the hotel as it was "preferred" by my corporate travel site. The room surpassed every expectation, and I travel for business a LOT. The bed was far-above-average comfortable; the bath was elegantly appointed, and the room layout thoughtfully placed the workdesk behind a partition, behind the bed. This solved one of my business-travel pet peeves, which is having a hard time shutting off work when it's in my line of sight in a hotel room. When I woke it was to a stunning sunrise view out the Chicago River to lake Michigan. I will stay here again on every trip though I usually choose a different chain ("points"). The only caution is that the lobby/bar and other public areas are LOUD and HUGE, filled with leisure travellers even in the middle of the week. Seek out a quiet bistro to unwind after work unless you thrive on noise.

title: “great base for family visiting NYC”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Milburn with our 2 year old and were pleasantly surprised to be booked in a very large suite for $194/night. Size of a good studio apartment. Kitchenette with fridge and microwave and small sink. King sized bed, good quality crib was set-up when we came in complete with nice bedding. Small dining table, fold-out sofa, nice view. Bathroom fairly recently renovated with two sinks (although somewhat cheap materials). The location can't be beat and, although not cheap, it's a good deal for NYC. Very clean. Room had DVD player and you can borrow movies free of charge.
Other relatives also stayed at the Milburn (family wedding) and our suite was by far the nicest. Some of the other rooms were pretty small, some had super tiny bathrooms. But, again, this is New York.
Downsides: they were not able to accomodate early check-in, we were not offered any help with our many suitcases, elevator is excrutiatingly slow, AC is noisy window units. Shower went hot and cold a lot. But these are all fairly minor problems. I would definitely stay here again if traveling with kids or older people.

title: “Wonderful experience”
text:
We found the staff to be incredibly helpful and friendly, the rooms clean, bed comfortable and the location GREAT. The walls are a bit thin so we recommend ear plugs just in case you have noisy neighbors. The concierge was the only low point - she was brusk, and unwilling to really show off what her city has to offer - plus a smile would have been nice. 
Despite the concierge we would most definitely stay at the Red Lion on Fifth again!!

title: “wont stay here again”
text:
With so many hotels in Houston (especially in the Galleria area) I won't ever stay at this hotel again - there has got to be better options.
My problems began when we arrived at the hotel and spent an hour driving around trying to figure out which parking garage that we were supposed to park in - the instructions given to us by the valet were not correct, and I called the hotel twice and talked to two different people trying to figure out where to park and none of them were able to tell us. We finally ended up where we THOUGHT we should be and went to an elevator to get down to the bottom of the parking garage and the elevator was broken - we then found another spot next to the mall entrance (that said Westin on the door) but when we walked in we were in the middle of the mall - another call to the hotel and the person that answered still couldn't tell us where to go - finally frustred, hot, miserable and angry, we just went and valet parked (for a rate of $24 a night). No where were there signs directing hotel guests where to park! 
I went in to the front desk to check in and complained about the parking to the front desk and the guy said he'd give me a $50 food and beverage credit - I asked him if he would comp our valet charges instead (for our 3 nights) and they wouldn't do it. 
I then got to my room and tried to connect to the internet and I couldn't connect. I called the front desk to ask for help and they told me to call a help number - turns out it's a call center in India - I talked to the guy for 20 mins (barely able to understand what he was saying) and finally hung up. I don't believe that I should have to talk to a guy in India for 20 mins at a business class hotel. They should have automatically changed my room or sent a guy up to look at the connection. I ended up calling the front desk and after a bit of run around they finally gave me a new room (with internet that worked). So... over 2 hours from the time I arrived in front of the hotel I FINALLY was settled into my room.
The beds were fantastic and the room was OK - definitely dated - floorboards were scuffed, carpet stained, furniture chipped etc. The shower fixtures worked great but just looked old.
I was there for a conference and I the conference rooms did not have good sound proofing and the chairs were so uncomfortable everyone was constantly shifting in their seats.
Between the parking situation (where I believe they purposely don't tell you where to park so you will valet) and the internet problem - I will never stay at this property again.

title: “Whiskey Bar”
text:
Great scenic bar/lounge at the top of the W Hotel (lakeshore). Arrived on a Saturday night about 10:00pm. It was dead, maybe only 10 people there. 
Music was extremely loud for such a small crowd, and by loud i mean we were screaming in each others ears and still couldn't understand a word the other person was saying. I like loud music and all but that was a bit intense.
We almost instantly decided finish our drinks than hit up another bar a block away. Halfway through our drinks, a wedding party showed up and changed the entire night for us. It ended up being a lot of fun simply because the wedding party included everyone that walked into the room. If it weren't for that, we all definitely agreed we would've left.

title: “everything was ok but the bath tub was not cleaned”
text: the hotel needed some more cleaning and updated rooms the bed was ok and the price was good My overall experience would have been better if the bath tub was cleaned

title: “very exceptable for the price”
text: Friendly staff, good full breafast, laundramat for guests, fridge and microwave in room, and it was a great location for us near our friends.

title: “Great location, friendly staff”
text:
When we arrived at the hotel they told us that we were upgraded to a suite, at no extra cost for us. So we got a room with two twin beds, and an adjoining "living room" with a sofa and a chair. Room and bathroom were clean, and we enjoyed our stay! Location is great, subway at the corner, just a few minutes walk to Times Square.
The hotel has free breakfast, but the waiting line was long, and the breakfast consisted of bagels, cup-cakes and white toast. So we only ate our breakfast there the first morning. You don't have to go far to find a place to eat, so that was ok with us. 
Not the most inexpensive hotel, but good value for the money. 
We'll definetely consider this hotel next time we go to NY.

title: “Nice place to stay.....”
text:
I must say that I was pleasantly surprised with the friendly staff and cleanliness. The breakfast has hard boiled eggs so you can get your protein and, of course, all the carbs you want. I stayed again at this location a few days laters and the clerk remembered me from my first visit. Makes me feel welcomed. :-)
I would recommend this hotel and will be staying here again.

title: “Great hotel, great location...”
text: We spent two nights at The Standard after reading the reviews on Tripadvisor. It was a great hotel; very trendy both inside and out but not at all intimidating. So different from a chain hotel in midtown. The staff also looked the part; they were helpful especially at check in - giving us a south facing room (which are a higher rate than what we had paid). The room (queen standard) was cool. A little on the small side (not much room to have two suitcases open) but the floor to ceiling views were fantastic. Clearly a lot of thought has gone into the design of the rooms. The bathroom was quite unique with a great two person bath and the views are still visible from the bath. The mini bar has a great selection and is really reasonably priced as is the room service menu. And a really comfy bed but our only problem was that the sheets were not fresh on our first night. It is a great location to explore the meatpacking district, the village and chelsea.

title: “A good 4 star”
text:
Staff excellent, rooms quiet, location good for broadway visits-a good value for the price, cannot really adjust temp in room-building has one temp
a nice, tourist hotel-molton brown toiletries are a nice touch-typical small old building new york hotel; good that had computer in little library for guests internet use for free

title: “Fantastic”
text:
The location is perfect although in Times Square and always very busy the interior was very quiet & relaxed.The staff were very helpful & booked A helicopter trip, dinner on a river cruiser, and tickets for the Empire State building for us.
The room was very spacious clean and the view was incredible one window looked down to the river and the other was of the corner of Times Square.The special area which we loved was the Restaurant at the topof the Hotel for upgraded rooms(worth doing) to sit & eat breakfast over looking the New York skyline was,great also the afternoon tea was a treat .

title: “Enjoyed it Very Much”
text:
My sister and I stayed at The New Yorker for several nights. We were assigned here from an auction with Hotwire. 
This is such an iconic hotel!
It was a wonderful experience! The beds and linens were very nice and extremely comfortable. Nice and quiet on our floor. 
The Heat worked great when we wanted it to. Nice black out curtains that were very attractive too! 
Yes, bathroom was small, but very functional & fun - I like updated authentic.
The lobby has such a positive energy to it! Always people coming and going. Upbeat atmosphere. There are plenty of staff near the elevators to answer questions. 
I love the fact that there's a baby grand piano in the lobby. One night two woman sat down and played a beautiful duet for everyone to enjoy. Terrific. 
The TIC TOC diner right connected to the lobby was a lifesaver. What a bonus - good food and good service. 
Glad I experienced this piece of New York history - would stay here again.

title: “Great hotel, great service!”
text:
I purchased this hotel on priceline and was discouraged when I looked at website, did not seem appealing. I couldn't have been more wrong....the hotel is beautiful and the staff is awesome, very polite and helpful in every way. It is definitely on a hill but only a few blocks from Pikes Market and I guess there is a free bus that you can catch for a return trip. The only drawback is if you don't bring your computer, they have a business room but you pay for computer use by the minute.....
We would definitely stay there again and recommend it highly.

title: “Fine hotel experience, but don't ask the concierge....”
text:
I found the hotel and amenities lovely during a hot summer stay in DC. It is a very short walk to Union Station and to the Capitol. It is a slightly longer, but eminently doable walk to the East Wing and National Art Museum and the mall. The pool and bar on the roof were wonderful on a hot summer day.
My issue was when I asked the concierge the fare on local buses. He didn't know and made no attempt to find out. He just laughed about driving everywhere himself. He was completely useless unless you wanted a cab.

title: “Great getaway near Long Beach”
text: When in Long Beach this is great getaway hotel that is located a short 15 min from Long Beach. Located at the port of Long Beach, the tranquil setting that overlooks the the boats docked outside the hotel is relaxing...the friendly staff is typical of all Hilton hotels where customer service is their goal.

title: “Older property, very clean and friendly”
text:
We stayed for 3 nights recently to attend Market. They have a shuttle that picks up and drops off and will take you anywhere within a 3 mile radius. The hotel is older but well maintained,
 the rooms were kind of small, and the bathroom was tiny. The staff was very service oriented and helpful. I got the impression that each time we interacted with them, they got a gold star of some kind, because each employee really wanted to make our stay a great one. We had dinner in the restaurant one evening and it was good food, not fabulous, but we enjoyed the meal. Cookies were available each evening when we got "home", and each bed had 4 lovely pillows. Bedding was comfy. I did not like the toilet in the room, as it was an industrial type. The shower head was wonderful-lots of water and lots of water pressure.

title: “Glad I didn't trust the other reviews...”
text:
From the prior reviews, I thought it would be a run down dump....glad I thought to give this hotel a chance. As of our wedding trip of the 2007 St. Patty's Day weekend, the entire hotel appeared to be recently renovated, and was quite beautiful. We got a king deluxe room for $139 through priceline, and it was worth every penny...I wish there was a way I could have smuggled that bed out and taken it home! And the linens were top notch, as were the Le Source tioletries.
The desk clerk, a Mr. Ajak, was very helpful and even printed out train schedules and maps for us, and the complimentary shuttle really came in handy.
We did not have time to eat at the restaurant the next day, but they had a very nice coffee nook where we were able to get Starbuck's coffee and gigantic danishes.
We are looking forward to staying there again!

title: “Great Location, Excellent Service”
text: Stayed here on 12/22 for one night with my family of 5 for some Christmas shopping. Hotel is in the best location for exploring Seattle, with quick access to shopping, monorail, all the sights. We were given a great room on the 43rd floor with an incredible southern view of the city. Staff was very friendly, and gave our young kids crayons and paper to color on during down time in the room. They were very flexible with late check-out the next day so we could extend our shopping and with pool hours as it is currently under renovation (but opened it early Friday morning so the kids could swim). A great stay, and I would highly recommend the Westin for either business or personal travel while in Seattle!

title: “WARNING - Gave away our rooms for profit on busy weekend”
text: One year prior to the F1 Grand Prix in Austin I booked this hotel for the Saturday evening - 2 rooms at a AAA rate. I specifically made the booking as soon as the date became available on the super 8 website and before the price gouging on hotels began. With confirmation in hand we were told at check in that our reservation had been cancelled. The hotel manager would not allow my husband to use the hotel phone to call Super 8 customer services to find out the reason. It turned out the hotel had cancelled the reservation that day - of course they had been able to resell these rooms at more than triple the cost of the rate I had originally booked. The hotel manager gave no explanation and no help in finding us other accommodation and no apology. The Super 8 customer services, however, when we called from our cell phone, did finally help us out and found a hotel a fewa miles away and eventually honored our original rate. SO WARNING - if there is an event in town - they might resell your room for more profit.

title: “Very attentive staff.”
text:
Luxury hotel, well placed to explore downtown San Diego and coast.
We had planned to stay downtown but as our stay coincided with ComicCon we were unable to get in anywhere- I'm so glad we couldn't, as staying at the Grand Del Mar was far more relaxing. 
Beautiful, spacious room with very comfortable bed.
Staff very attentive.
Excellent breakfasts, even though you are given a menu, it seemed that whatever you wanted they would try and accomodate it.
Would definitely choose TGDM again.

title: “Great location, nice hotel”
text: Wife and I stayed four nights. Very convenient to Central Park, subway, reasonable walk or metro ride to Times Square, Broadway shows ( We walked). Would recommend.

title: “Not impressed”
text: Driving from Dallas to San Diego and booked this hotel after reading many good reviews on Trip Advisor. We were looking for a hotel conveniently located off of I-10 which this was but in a very congested area. I called to book the room and was surprised to find out that it was $175/night with no government rate available. I figured this must be a really nice Hampton if they are charging that kind of rate. The lady at the front desk who checked us in was nice but there were some shady looking people hanging out in the lobby which made me feel uneasy. Got to our room and it was very dated looking, but clean and quiet. Beds were fine and standard Hampton Inn linens. Overall, not a terrible stay..aside from guests slamming their hotel room doors and the sound of bass coming from somewhere above us. Would not stay again, though, and it wasn't worth the rate that we paid. Good enough for one night while making a pit stop in El Paso.

title: “Very Pleasant - No complaints”
text:
I have never had a bad experience at a Kimpton hotel. They are always very stylish, clean, and relaxing. Great amenities, and the staff is always very friendly. 
The Embarcadero is very pleasant to walk along, and the nearby Farmer's Market mall is great for all kinds of dining. Views of the bay are great. It's nice to be in one of the more quiet areas of the city, yet still close to downtown and easy for transportation. 
If you have a car, you can park in a nearby garage overnight for about $10 less than their valet fee.
Also, if you are traveling with pets, no place is better than a Kimpton hotel, because they never charge extra fees and are very friendly to your pet.

title: “So many extras”
text: Wine and beer hour, cookies(coffee and milk), and full breakfast for a reasonable price. This hotel is In a great location by the 16th street mall and free shuttle bus. Rooms are contemporary and very clean. I was contacted by the hotel a couple of times before arriving with offers to assist me and a weather forecast for the week I visited. Staff was helpful. I would stay there again when visiting Denver. A great find!

title: “BEAUTIFUL HOTEL”
text: We attended a banquet/convention on 11/19/11. This hotel is extremely clean and the service is spectacular. We stayed in room 3028 (beautiful) on the 30th floor. It had a very comfortable king size bed and an amazing harbor view. We attended a banquet in the ballroom, which was very nice. The fitness area is nicely equipped. Also, they had a free shuttle service to and from the convention center. Overall, a little pricey, but well worth it!This hotel has a great harbor location. In addition, there are alot of restaurants and attractions within walking distance.

title: “Stay and Park”
text: I am glad I had my GPS to find this place. I saw the hotel from I-93, but in Boston that doesn't mean it will be easy to get to. This Ramada Inn is about 15 minutes from Logan and has an afordable Stay and Park rate. The shutlle to the airport runs 24/7 plus service to the T. The rooms was clean and otherwise okay. The service is that famous Northeastern hospitality (brisk and not too warm). This Ramada is part of a complex with two decent resturants and a bowling alley. i will probably avoid staying here again. They insisted on copying (Xeroxing) my drivers license. I think this is totally unneccssary, an invasion of my privacy and opens me to identiy theft.

title: “Convenience and comfort”
text:
I just came back from staying here during one of the Hilton promotional packages. While I know it can be pricey to stay here during regular times, if you can snatch a deal then definitely stay here. I stayed on the 14th floor in a business suite, which was very big. The view was great- the WTC and construction of the new towers (the work was pretty constant but not bothersome at all. I've stayed in Times Square and it's much noisier there!). The hotel is located in a great spot too- multiple subway stations are literally steps away and Chinatown/Little Italy is in walking distance. Because the hotel is in the Financial District, it's pretty empty during the weekends and a short subway ride away from just about any attraction.
Side note: great toiletries. Peter Thomas Roth shampoo, conditioner, soap, lotion and mouthwash. Great brand, nice extra touch.

title: “Great remodel job”
text:
Hilton recently renovated and upgraded this property, and the rooms are a great improvement, with with flat screen TVs, better mattresses, and, wonder of wonders, the key cards always worked! [This was a major problem the 5 times I stayed at this hotel for the same business conference.] Unfortunately, their main restaurant still suffers from a limited menu, poor execution, and execrable service.
 The refurbished public areas, particularly the pool, are excellent. The traffic pattern from the meeting areas to the restaurant and shops has been improved as well [the former arrangement required you to exit the conference wing and reenter by the main entrance].

title: “Had Great Experience Very Happy”
text:
We stayed at JW Marriot Desert Ridge Resort for three nights in mid-November 2005. This is a beautiful resort with excellent grounds and rooms. Check in was smooth and the room we received was in a very good location, just steps from the exercise room and the “lazy river” pool, and in close proximity to the main pool and the lobby areas. The room was ground floor, with a patio overlooking gardens and the golf course. A room one or two floors higher, with balcony, would have afforded a better view, but we were happy with ours. The room was very large, with king size bed, sofa, coffee table, two chairs, desk, television cabinet, and a huge marble/tile bathroom with both tub and separate shower (glass enclosed). The bathroom amenities were top-notch. The room was immaculate when we checked in and stayed that way while we were there. The room also included a digital safe and small fridge to the side of the mini-bar. The only complaint at all about the room is that the fridge did not keep things real cold, just cool. We had a small ice chest with us so things we wanted to be really cold we just iced down.
The resort is quite large and spread out, so be prepared to walk. While valet parking is offered, it is not mandatory and self parking is available. It is quite a walk from the self park lot to the room wings so people that have mobility problems should be aware of that.
The exercise room by the pool area is open 24 hours and is very well equipped with state of the art equipment. It was busy while we were there, but early morning visits usually found open treadmills. The spa was very nice and offers the typical services. It also has another pool available, but one must pay a daily spa fee to use it. This might be worth it when the resort is full of kids but while we were there we say maybe 4 children. There is also another exercise room located adjacent to the spa, but it is not open 24 hours.
The grounds and the public areas are very nice. There are several dining options available in the resort, as well as a Starbucks for coffee drinks. There is of course lots of out door dining space. The bars at the main pool and the lazy river offer a wide selection of drinks (reasonably priced for a resort) and a nice selection of food (also not priced too badly) and make a nice place for a pool side lunch. We ate dinner at the resort only one evening, at Roy’s, which was excellent. It was expensive but worth every cent. We both chose the fixed price menu which is good value at $33. It offers a very nice selection of Roy’s specialties served in three courses. Roy’s also has a nice wine list and offers some fairly inexpensive house wines (which were quite good) by the glass. We highly recommend Roy’s.
Just outside the gate of the resort is the Desert Ridge Shopping Center which offers a wide variety of dining options and many shops. Hint: if you want to buy liquor, beer or wine to stock the room, Osco Drugs is MUCH cheaper than the Albertsons Grocery store.
Marriot offers a free shuttle to and from the shopping center so you could leave your car parked at the hotel. It runs until fairly late in the evening.
We really enjoyed our stay and rate this hotel as excellent. We were able to relax around the pools, have some good food and drinks, and just chill, which we both badly needed. We found nothing to complain about at all and would not hesitate to return.

title: “Fantastic location & hotel”
text:
I was in San Diego for a conference and my company booked at Pacific Terrace. I was greeted by friendly and welcoming front desk staff and found out I was upgraded to a junior suite with partial view of the ocean. Check in was quick and the person that checked me in was informative and resourceful about the hotel amenities and where to eat nearby, etc. 
My room was large, clean and stocked. That partial view was amazing, not sure why they call it a partial view! The front desk called me to make sure all was well in my room. The room is nicely appointed with free and reliable wireless (important item for me when traveling for business). 
They do not have a restaurant at the hotel, but have a few options: (1) they have participating restaurants that deliver food, and (2) they provide a food card and if you eat at the participating restaurants of that plan they just bill your room. 
Also, they do have a breakfast buffet in the morning which is nice and pretty reasonable in cost. 
Location, it is walking distance to lots of dining options and a Starbucks. The hotel is very close to Interstate 5, literally 6-7 minutes straight shot to La Jolla, and many other areas. 
Downside, public parking is hard to get, but there is valet option of $20/per day. Not an issue for me, but those on a budget, this is a good thing to know. 
Otherwise, the stay was amazing and I will certainly return to stay at Pacific.

title: “Fabulous!!!”
text:
Our recent stay at the Westin St. Francis was nothing short of fabulous! We had originally booked our trip for the week right before xmas, but my daughter and I were fighting pneumonia and we had to cancel our trip. We were very disappointed. I contacted the hotel when we had recovered because we wanted to re-schedule our trip for New Year's week and I knew it would be very busy doing this at the last minute. They could not have been more accommodating. They hooked me up with a wonderful person who re-booked our entire trip for us just as we had planned originally. She gave us the same rate despite the fact that it was New Year's week. I had done a ton of research, as usual, and chose this hotel for it's location and reputation. We had chosen a tower room because I had heard that the tower was newer and had less street noise and a better view. It was certainly a great choice. Our first night there, the concierge sent champagne to my husband and I at the amazing restaurant that she recommended. (Blue Stem) The food was unbelievable. When we got back to our room, the front desk sent up milk and cookies, chocolate covered strawberries, and Perrier. Our kids thought they were royalty. Big hit! The weather wasn't great during our stay, which hampered the amazing view we would have seen. As luck would have it, the day of our departure, New Year's Eve, it was gorgeous, and we could see the spectacular view we had been missing from our room. It was pretty impressive- the entire bay, and the Golden Gate in clear view. With this in mind, we went down and asked if we could stay another night thinking that there was no way because it was New Year's Eve and that the rates would be ridiculous. They were extremely helpful and asked us if we minded moving to the older part of the hotel. We didn't mind at all and the rate was even better than the first room. 
LOCATION- It's amazing. Right in the center of all that is Union Square. Restaurants, shopping, and Chinatown is walking distance as well-which our son loved-being a 12 year old typical boy on the hunt for anything cool. Cable car stops right there in front of the hotel. Mall is walking distance down the hill with Nordstrom and Bloomingdales. Macy's and Neiman's right across the street. 
TOWER VS OLD SCHOOL HOTEL- We stayed 2 nights in the tower and one in the older part. The tower is newer and the glass elevator is fun for the kids. Bathrooms are very pretty and modern. Views are spectacular. The higher you go...the less street noise you hear...but it's still the city and you are going to hear some of it. The older part is quite charming with high ceilings and chandeliers. The bathrooms are a bit smaller-but still pretty- if you care- we didn't. Honestly, we were on the 6th floor for New Year's Eve and thought we'd be sorry we didn't have earplugs. But we were very comfortable and didn't have much more noise than in the tower. (actually we had less hallway traffic) 
THE BAD- The parking situation (which I knew ahead of time) is just ridiculous. They want to charge you $50 a day to park your car at the hotel. Do yourself a favor and park nearby- much cheaper!
THE GOOD- The staff is extremely friendly and we experienced amazing customer service. (something that is always appreciated by us choosy hotel types) The coffee bar near the lobby is great for a quick snack and a latte in the morning. The Oak Room breakfast is pretty good. Skip the buffet and order off the menu-I think the food is better.Beautiful architecture and very grand inside reflecting old San Francisco. 
All I can say is thank you to the St. Francis for providing us with such a great experience. We were very happy with our stay there and hope to return someday soon.

title: “Wonderful Experience!”
text:
My wife and I just spent the last weekend at the Hotel Giraffe on 26th st. in Manhattan. As soon as we stepped out of our cab and were greeted by Jose the doorman we knew we were in for a wonderful experience. It is a small intimate hotel that is Big on making you feel that you are very special. The wine and Cheese served in the lobby was a added treat. We in particular enjoyed the new rooftop bar-very nice place for a cocktail before or after dinner. As an aside, our children joined us for dinner at Bread and Tulips and had a great dinner in a very relaxing setting. A hidden gem. Overall, We plan on staying at the Giraffe many more times. 
WilliamR1954

title: “Superb Hotel”
text: Excellent hotel rite in the city centre, close to Times Square and all the shops, staff very friendly and helpful, rooms a good size and the bed was so comfy, i'd recommend this hotel to anyone going on a trip to New York, cant praise this enough.

title: “great timeshare property”
text: If you are lucky enough to get into this place with time share points you will not be dissapointed unless you know nothing about staying in Manhattan. You are getting a little more space than your average hotel room and a kitchenette which can save you a lot of money. Just grabbing a cup of coffee or soft drinks and snack or being able to heat up leftovers from a restaurant is great! You have everything a normal hotel would have..valet, doorman, conierge etc...but it's a timeshare. The elevators are slow so be patient and leave the extra time if you are on your way to a show or reservations at a restaurant. I am from NY originally and was pleasantly surprised.

title: “We will not be back”
text: Location (if you like to walk outside your hotel to shops, restaurants, etc.) was NOT good. Doorman even had a hard time waving down taxis for their guests! Hotel is surrounded by souvenir shops, banks, and fast food places. Leaves much to be desired! Inside hotel things look up! Our room was large and nice but sorely lacked drawers or cabinets in which to place underware, clothes, etc.. We booked our room at the Setai because of a promotion offered in an ad in the Wall Street Journal, however, when we went to check out we were told our travel agent had not given them that request. Unbelievable! We have asked for a review and will see what they end up allowing. The ONLY reason we stayed there in the first place was to take advantage of this "perk"...then to have it denied...well, you can imagine our dismay. We would definitely NOT suggest you consider staying at this property until they get more kinks worked out! Beware of "bait and switch" if you do. Dismayed travelers from Texas.

title: “5 Star hotel, old world charm in Dallas”
text: I have stayed at this hotel several times and each time it gets better. The hotel is located near Turtle Creek and Oak Lawn. If you enjoy older classic hotels this is a must. The doors and walls are solid, its like sleeping in a huge Mercedes! I've never heard any noises from other rooms. The furniture although an older classic design is beautiful. The bed is extremely comfortable and so is the linen. The marble bathrooms are fantastic. Although an older property everything works great...water pressure,water temperatures, A/C, internet, flat screen tv etc. Usually older hotels are noisy and have inconsistent water pressure and temperatures...not at the Melrose. It is first class. The bar is a must, don't miss it. There are several casual eating establishments in the area but you will need to drive for more upscale restaurants. Parking is a little steep for the area but at least your car is safe. If you are gay the hotel is in the heart of the gay village. Check the hotel for specials you would be surprised at the rates. Enjoy, I can't wait to return.

title: “By Far the Best Deal in DC”
text:
Anyone who doesn't think this is an amazing hotel doesn't stay in DC very often. I do -- and after 14 days in The Quincy, I couldn't be happier. My room was gigantic, immaculate, and tastefully decorated with lovely modern furniture. As others have pointed out, the beds are fantastic. There is also a large "T" couch, a big desk, and an oversized floor mirror. The bathroom is not giant, but the shower is great and there is a separate vanity area that includes a mini-fridge (to store things in) and a microwave. The TV works great and includes HBO, and the wireless internet is free. Yes, it drops occasionally -- but it is more than fast enough for everything other than downloading movies. And although the heat cannot be adjusted quite as precisely as one would like, I disagree with those who say the rooms get too hot -- turn off the heater! I also disagree with the reviewer who complained about not having a fitness room on-site. Frankly, I think the two-block, three-minute walk to Ballys is worth it: it's free, and instead of one or two machines you get an entire fitness center. Finally, the hotel's location is great, just minutes from the red metro and the green metro and walking distance to the Mall.
Bottom line: I would never -- and I mean NEVER -- stay anywhere else in DC, especially at the price, which averaged out to $128.00 per night through Hotels.com. My friends paid the same amount for the dingy Red Roof Inn in Chinatown!

title: “LUCERNE HOTEL (near American Museum of Natural History)”
text: four friends - we stayed January 2007 for three nights; 2 queen beds; kitchenette; and living room area; it was great; would definitely recommend hotel; they were running a winter special at the time too, which was good; plus it included a free breakfast at Nice Matin downstairs, excellent; we had a blown fuse with the hairdryer situation; they fixed it immediately; and I mean immediately;

title: “A Hell of a Toddling, Windy, Big Shouldered Town... by the Lake”
text:
After spending a night in less than acceptable accommodations out in the suburbs, my wife (who is also my business partner) and I chose to move to cooler digs. The Hampton Inn offered us a room at pretty much the going rate for a place in town, about $260-something. We are not from Chicago, nor have we ever been before, so I can’t speak to the value of the actual street address, however, we did find our way around town pretty easily (all credit to the dynamic trio of Google maps, a Treo and my navagatrix wife). The hotel was typical of the properties one finds in a world-class city. The staff, much like virtually every human being we encountered in Chicago, was delightful. The parking at the hotel, again like most other properties, was steep; $38.00 a night! But there is a lot right next door for $20 and one a across the street for $25. In and out privileges are okay at the independent lots, so don’t worry about that.
The rooms at the Hampton were, again, right on par for the type of property they represent; handsomely furnished, modestly sized and nicely equipped with toiletries and little extras (a bottle of water and some cookies). There’s an Italian restaurant downstairs and a sky bridge connecting to a Ruth’s Chris Steakhouse. The property offers a “hot breakfast” which, sadly, leaves much to be desired, like perhaps a good breakfast. The coffee was nice (and is always available) but the selection of breads lacked any whole grains, the chafing dish of eggs tasted like a science experiment gone wrong and the orange juice formula used to be restricted to astronauts. Breakfast is not the best feature of this hotel!
The city itself is just terrific! We enjoyed a pair of blues bands at the packed, raucous (but cool-vibed) “Kingston Arms” blues bar the night we arrived and the next day made the most of our late flight and rented car by touring the whole city. This included a slice of authentic deep-dish pizza (I’m a New Yorker, so I’m a tough sell on pizza, but this a local tradition and it should at least be experienced) and a trip up the Sears Tower. I used to work at the top of the World Trade Center, so I was probably less thrilled than most, but it is quite a view! 
One thing to keep front of mind is the traffic! I live in Los Angeles and even I was freaked out by it. Give yourself an extra hour at least to get to the airport. We didn’t but thanks to a flight delay still made it to our seats… or else we absolutely would not have.

title: “Near Medical Center - downtown area”
text:
Overall: We like the location as we were in Houston for medical reasons. We could take the shuttle to and from the Methodist Hospital, which is only 1 mile away. We stayed here several times during the month of February. As stated in other reviews, the rooms vary greatly in size. We stayed in a handicapped room and it was of ample size. Another in our party stayed in a "petite King" and it was quite small and only had a shower and no tub. The rooms seemed to vary on whether they had showers and tub combos, so I would check on this if this is a deal breaker for you.
After staying for several days, I can say the housekeeping service was normally quite good except the last night we stayed here. They didn't take our dirty glasses and give us clean ones. Not sure the reasoning behind this, but every other time, they swept and had everything spotless. For other hotels in the same area, this price is "the norm" and a great and comfly place to stay - close to museums, the park, and the medical center.
Negative hotel aspects: If you get a pool side room, they leave the radio playing really loud all day long and it can be heard in all rooms (we were on the 10th floor) throughout the day, so if you are looking for an afternoon snooze, this may not be the place for you.
