There is only 1 chair in the room and no "table" just an office desk with a huge oversized chair. They did promise us a bedboard because the beds were too soft for my husband and we were never delivered one.
Yes, there is an automatic $20 valet charge per day. You expect this at most higher hotels, though. The valets are great and extremely responsive. The shuttle service is a huge plus as far as I am concerened.

title: “Something for everyone!”
text: I visited Travaasa with my (all adult) family, and we all had a wonderful time. My father enjoyed the food and the harmonica class, my mother enjoyed watching the sunrise from the porch and the yoga classes, my sister enjoyed the gorgeous pool and i enjoyed all the various other exercise classes. I think we all especially enjoyed the equine encounter with Betsy and Jody, which we really only did because we were curious about it but ended up chattering about it for days afterwards! And the wine tasting with Edward was informative and pretty raucous- not at all intimidating- and he is super helpful picking out wines at dinner. Along that same note, the cocktails are also amazing. We all had a good time at all the different exercise classes, especially the dance ones, where the teachers were fun and also not intimidating. It is also not too far from civilization, so we were able to have dinner out with some family living in the Austin area. The spa was good but we didn't find it exceptional. The staff were all extremely personable. The guests are mostly women, and couples, as far as we could see. Overall, a great place to try tons of new things all day, or just sit by the pool and relax.

title: “Great Customer Service”
text: We had a wonderful time staying at the Country Inn and Suites in San Diego. the customer service and amenities was wonderful. The check in and check out process worked like a charm. the breakfast was hot or cold depending on what you wanted and it was clean.

title: “Charming hotel”
text: This is a small friendly boutique hotel. The rooms are very large for San Francisco and very well maintained. You are within walking distance to Union Square and a large number of stores, restaurants and wine bars plus ready access to the buses, cable car and street cars. Overall, it is a perfect location. Breakfast is included and changes each day. The quality is quite high considering it is included in the price. Overall, the hotel is great value. We will definitely return.

title: “Subpar”
text: I'm here on business, so someone else is paying the hotel bill. Still, I think this hotel is charging a ridiculous amount for what they provide. When I arrived, I was informed there was no valet parking as the valet lot was . At the check in desk, I was told a room with a king bed, which I had reserved several months in advance, was not available. To the hotel's credit, they did offer me free WiFi(although I think that for what they are charging, this should be available anyway). The location is convenient within walking distance of several shops, restaurants and the metro. But the hotel bar/bistro was not open on the weekend. The room is very loud, although I am not on a lower floor, the street noise is significant. Of most concern to me is that the room is not particularly clean. Someone(who knows how many guests ago) left some takeout food in the room fridge and its just sitting there. There are also splatters of something on the second bed. Housekeeping came through the room this morning and left these things untouched. I emailed these problems to the email address provided in the Hyatt welcome book, and the mail was returned as undeliverable.

title: “Very Pleasantly Surprised”
text:
Honestly I was dreading staying at this property because of the overall poor ratings. What I experienced greatly exceeded my expectations. The rooms were comfortable, clean and tastefully decorated. The food was flavorful and efficiently served. The staff was gracious. The work out facility was amazing. Large, spotlessly clean and filled with state of the art equipment.
I wouldn't hesitate to recommend this facility for business groups.
Do take your lint brush, however, the new carpet does have a wierd shedding thing going on.

title: “Great ambience”
text: Loved the room. Front desk staff late night left a bit to be desired but overall a great experience.

title: “Beautiful resort! I would recommend the Royal Palms to my friends and family.”
text: The staff is unbelievable... in a good way! Everything was clean and well kept. The food was awesome. You need to check this place out!

title: “Worst experience ever”
text: I recently stayed at the Wellington and I will never go back. The hotel staff was rude and unhelpful. The housekeeping staff couldn't decide how many towels were needed in our room and the numbers of each type of towel changed everyday. Sometimes we would have 4 washcloths and no handtowels or vice versa. There was a burned out light bulb that never got fixed even after we asked for the problem to be fixed several times. The noise from the air conditioning unit kept us up half the night. The walls and carpet were filthy as was the bedspread. The only good things I can say is that even though the bathroom was small, it was very clean.

title: “Does the trick!”
text:
Stayed 4 nights and paid ±170/night, which was worth it. Location in a residential area makes you feel like a "local" and is very central, you can get to Fisherman's Wharf, Chinatown, Financial district and the Golden Gate if you're ready to walk a little or a short walk from the cable car, and buses on Van Ness ave got us to the baseball stadium easily.
Staff was nice, room was clean and confortable. Wifi works well. 
The street does get noisy at night, but the Hotel is fairly well insulated for noise. Breakfast are very average and bland, but ok. 
All in all, this is not a destination hotel, but a nice little spot to get back to after a day of exploring.

title: “Old and dingy”
text: The rooms at this hotel are in desperate need up an upgrade. Our room was old, dingy, smelled, and beds were not comfortable. I guess if you want to stay one quick night close to Jacksonville airport, this will serve the purpose fine.

title: “Best Broadway Location”
text:
Millenium Broadway has a good location for Business Travel & Tourism.
Great Restaurants within walking distance,Many Broadway shows & good food are the plus points.

title: “Very nice on Times Square”
text:
The Muse Hotel was very nice, clean and neat, centrally located near Times Square, and the room actually bigger than expected (large bed, too!).
The staff was friendly and helpful, although we did get a restaurant tip which was slightly odd. The guy in the reception recommended a sushi restaurant in the financial district, located in the basement... Although the food was very nice and the staff friendly, it was not exactly the kind of place you want to go for a night out. For ordering in it would be just fine, though... You would expect that he would be able to suggest a few restaurants, for example like the ones we visited in the Meatpacking District.
...and in 2010 it would be nice if you didn't have to pay $13 for for 30 minutes internet access.

title: “Wacky and well done”
text: Had 5 nights and must say enjoyed it. Generally the super hi tech, over-the-top wacky hotels bore me. Somehow Yotel (British strangely), worked really well, clean rooms, simple but had everything necessary, bar a bit of skin cream. For some reason for 2 days only 2 of the lifts worked and checking in went a bit wrong, credit card numbers had been left on booking and verified, but on arrival needed to be seen again, 'I wasn't paying' so complications. There's a pretty decent restaurant on level 4 and basic complimentary breakfast, alternatively a good selection that can be paid for. Given New York prices Yotel is good value. Just need to iron out minor problems, desk staff could be more friendly and polite!

title: “Quiet, Grand and Self-Contained”
text:
The Lucerne is situated in the upper west side of Manhattan, 10 minutes walk from Central Park on the right and 10 minutes from Riverside Park on the left... which makes it a fantastic spot for picnics. The delectable Zabar's deli is only 5 minutes away, and you're spoiled for choice from a range of bagel shops and food markets nearby to pack that ever-growing picnic bag.
The area is mostly residential, so it offers a quieter sleeping experience away from the madness of midtown Manhattan. We loved the fact that on rainy days, we could stroll around and find food, water, recreation parks and the American Museum of Natural History on our doorstep. 
The metro station is at the end of the hotel block, which affords easy access to the tourist attractions in midtown, and also meant we felt safe coming back late at night after a show at Broadway or dining out. There's even a cinema in the next street where we caught a late night movie on our last day. Amsterdam Avenue runs next the hotel, and has some great eating places. The street after that - Columbus Avenue - carries lots of retail shops.
We found the hotel staff helpful and courteous. The doormen often greet you on your return from a long day out but remain unobtrusive. Rooms are small, but this shouldn't be a surprise in such a dense city. What the room lacked in size, it made up for in cleanliness and coziness. The bed was extremely comfortable, kingsize even though it was the most basic grade of room, and the air-conditioning unit worked a treat during the humid nights (though it's certainly not the quietest machine in the world!). The only occasional problem might be when guests talk loudly in the corridors on their way to the lift, though once everyone's in their room, there's not a peep.
Hang a sign on the doorknob if you want a complimentary NY Times newspaper in the morning, and request a quiet room at reception when you check in. The staff seem only to happy to cater to your needs, and it truly made for a quiet and relaxing refuge from the hustle and bustle of the city.

title: “Luxury”
text: Love you resort, always enjoy our stay beautiful setting, love the Spa..! The best customer service, look forward to our next visit. The patio at night is so relaxing by the fireplace our family spent hours just visiting with each other, great place! Look forward to next year,!

title: “The Hard Rock San Diego Rocked our Socks Off :)”
text: This was my first time staying at the Hard Rock San Diego - I've stayed at many other hotels in San Diego and this was by far my most favorite experience. We were there for a bachelorette party and we had a blast - I would recommend this hotel for any occaision; the staff is extremely accommodating.

title: “There are probably better value budget hotels in the city”
text:
I was under no false illusions about this 2 star hotel and I would have rated it 3 stars but for some major issues which I consider essential when paying a four figure sum (in Stirling) for a 6 night stay. 
The good things about the hotel...
> Friendly reception staff 
> Free continental breakfast (not European though – food is from the American continent such was waffles and bagels)
> Good location 
The not so good...
> Very small double beds which are quite uncomfortable for two adults 
> No view whatsoever – in fact – I think the window had never been cleaned 
> Extremely noisy air con which meant a very noisy night or a very warm night 
The primary reason for my negative review is that when checking out of the hotel the Bell Boy/Doorman asked me if my family required a car for the airport and all that I needed to pay was a $10 deposit. I accepted the offer and was given back a receipt with a bill for $65 but the standard price for a NYC cab to JFK is only $45, furthermore, I could not cancel the car without losing the $10 deposit that I have just paid. It gets worse... on route to JFK the driver informed me that there was still TAX, tip and toll to pay which resulted in the final bill being nearly twice the amount of a standard cab fare.
The hotel and/or the Bell Boy/Doorman has some sort of deal in place with a private car company so book your own cab and if you do decide to stay in this small hot hotel.

title: “The coolest hotel i've never been”
text: This is a super cool hotel. I LOVED the atmosphere. Amazing rooms, super cool accesories, very good bar. The food is also very good, we had the most delicious breakfast ever. There is also 2 stores inside the hotel, edgy and cool: one is the wonderful opening ceremony. It's an expensive hotel, but it's worth it.

title: “Great location and spacious rooms”
text: We stayed one night here and have no complaints in regards to the room, location or customer service. Finding the hotel was tricky as well as parking. Checked bags to be delivered to room but they refused to deliver unless you were in the room to accept them. A little bit frustrating when you are expecting them to be there and in a hurry to make a play.... Clean room, very spacious, great view. Would reccommend.

title: “Great Location, Quality Feel”
text:
Stayed 3 nights at the Nikko and would recommend for a relaxing San Francisco stay. I booked through Asda travel (yes Asda)after a search by Travel supermarket and got a good rate.
Somewhat bizarrely not the easiest place to find for our taxi driver as the vehicle access is not from Mason street. Location is excellent for Union Square, restaurants and cable cars. Reception were very professional and room was clean, freshly decorated and of a reasonable size. 
We didn't use any of the hotel restaurants or bars but they looked reasonably priced and very smart.
The hotel has a business feel to it but is relaxed and has a nice calmness to it's feel.
Would recommend Lori's Diners (50's diner) for breakfast or Starbucks (on site) for coffee.
Overall a great well located hotel in a fabulous City

title: “A dreamy hotel!!”
text:
I've been to this hotel with my girlfriends, my sister, and my husband and son....it gets better every time I stay!! I highly recommend staying in a Casita. It's like having your own little home! The room I stayed in the last time I was there was close to the street, small and not my favorite.
I love the property, the fireplaces and looking at the Camelback Mountain every time I walk around the property!! 
In the morning we hike up into the neighborhood behind the hotel..it's a perfectly nice hike.
I will say that the hairdresser that washed and blew my hair dry at the Spa (I had a broken arm) was pretty bad...and they overcharged me for the service.

title: “Not worthy of price!”
text: From the description on their website you would think you'd be staying in an "upscale, boutique" hotel. It was a far cry from that. I booked a "suite" for a 5 nite stay. I could only get 2 beds and fridge/micro if I booked a suite. I thought the price was steep (and they raised it on weekends!) but I figured it was a "suite" and would be well worth it. Upon check in at the hotel the front desk person was somewhat rude and things went downhill from there. In our "suite" the room with the 2 dbl beds was VERY cramped. And the beds were just on elevated platforms. I felt like I was in a DORM ROOM and paying an outrageous price. The beds were NOT comfortable at all. The bathroom was even worse. So small you could hardly move AND fixtures/tub/sink were extremely old and seemed dirty. Nice old, clawfoot bathtub but that was about it. Front desk folks were not helpful at all. Original 5 nite stay went to 1 nite and booked another hotel that was much nicer and more reasonably priced.. Wasn't about to pay that kind of money for a dorm room and one that needed upgrading. Not even a dresser in either room. The hotel location is good and that is about all I can say.

title: “What do you expect to see behind the bed?”
text:
This hotel is not bad; it's what you expect from a Manhattan hotel that caters to business travelers who want a relatively nice room for a non-Earth-shattering price.
This being said, I had the most amazing experience when I looked behind the bed. The alarm kept going off around 3 AM, and I couldn't figure out how to turn it off. I tried to unplug it, couldn't find the plug, and moved the bed to disconnect it from there.
When I looked behind the bed, there were two mouse traps, two dirty socks, and something that I really couldn't identify. This was, in short, gross.
The next morning, I told the staff, and they were apologetic, and they upgraded me to a suite. This being said, it was still gross.
The lesson I learned was not to look behind the hotel bed, and this scenario isn't unlikely in other hotels, either.

title: “Lovely hotel, lovely location.”
text: I stayed at The Rittenhouse while I was in Philadelphia for a meeting and I was really pleased with the hotel. The room was sprawling--just huge with an equally enormous bathroom. The bath products, the little chocolate on the nightstand, and the fine towels and linens added a touch of class and comfort. My room was pretty high up so I didn't have any street noise, nor could I hear any other guesets coming or going. The room was quiet. I also had a chance to have breakfast at the hotel and found the breakfast space bright and elegant and the food to be quite good. The best part about the place though is the location in the city. Between sessions at my meeting, it was a delight to wander around the neighborhood and you are situated right on a vibrant square--plenty of shops, eateries, and historic sites to occupy one's time. You can also easily walk to the train station. I would definitely choose this hotel again for quick business trips or a weekend visit to the city.

title: “Good Hotel a little way outside the main downtown area”
text:
We have just returned from a week in Boston where we stayed at the Seaport Hotel. Transfer from the airport could not have been easier. A bus just outside the main exit passes the hotel and we were actually in our room about 20 minutes after boarding. There is a 'T' station just by the hotel too on the Silver Line which provides a link between the airport and Boston's South Station. We found we could actually walk to the Boston Aquarium/Quincy Market area in about 20 minutes and to Boston Common in a few minutes longer.
The hotel itself is about 10 years old and is well appointed. There is a pool/fitness centre and the room we had was very nice with a view of Boston Harbour and the airport on the other side. We didn't hear any noise.
The breakfast buffet in the hotel restaurant was well worth having. Set us up for the day. The hotel is all-inclusive and there is no need to tip any member of staff. In fact, there are notices asking that you don't. One of the waiters in the restaurant actually pointed out that we shouldn't tip him as service was included in the bill. In a few years time, I expect this hotel to be better placed for local attractions as the adjacent World Trade Center attracts more visitors. If you don't mind a short walk to the Downtown area or a trip on the 'T' (costing just $2 if you'd rather ride) then I think you will find this hotel a good bargain. We would stay there again.

title: “Excellent property and location”
text: Enjoyed the location. Very close to excellent restaurants and nightlife. Great food at hotel as well. Great service.

title: “Fantastic area”
text: I've stayed there a few times when I am in the Chicago area, and it's been consistently a great deal for me. If you're looking for an affordable place to stay that near all of the sites, you can't beat this place.

title: “This hotel is awful!”
text:
ONLY KIDDING! - it is fantastic - just don't want to tell everyone as it will be so hard to get a room in the future if everyone knows!!!
Hotel booked based on the reviews for TA.
We arrived on 14th Sept for our 6 night stay at about 3.30pm - no problem checking in (booked through Venere.com and double checked with hotel by email that they had got us booked in - been caught out before with third party bookings so always best to check!) Reception staff were really nice and we got allocated 1004 which is the Museum room on the General Knowledge floor (10th). They asked (and didn't presume - which is nice) if we needed the bellman to take our cases up - we didn't as we had one each but the bellman was really helpful getting our cases out of the car when we arrived and all 3 of the bellman that we met throughout our visit were so nice - never in your face as some can be. 
We got to our room (petite double) and we had expected it to be small (thanks to reviews on here) but to be honest we were actually quite relieved( we did so much walking on our trip that to only walk a few steps at night and in the morning from bathroom to bed and back again was a bit of a relief!) Who needs a big room anyway? We put our cases on top of the wardrobes (had to stand on chair to do this) but they were out of the way up there so left room to walk about.
Facilities in room 
Safe in room - the type where you programme your own 4 digit code so very secure.
Natura toileteries - shampoo, conditioner (took shampoo and conditioner in one but needed this too as water is very hard) shower gel, bar of exfoliating soap, ordinary soap and body lotion. Replenished every day if used. Shower cap, shoe polish, sewing kit, cotton buds and cotton wool balls. Hairdryer (took my 1400w travel one so didn't test the one in room) 
TV, DVD and CD (radio/alarm) - don't try and put the remote on top of the tv! I did this and it slips right down to the back of the mini bar fridge underneath!) I wasn't the only one to have done this (I later found out!) but sheepishly had to confess to it in the morning. A new one was brought up to us right away!
Mini bar - not a complete rip off like they are in this country but beware - if you move it from it's little stand it will register as a purchase even if you put it back! I did this and had to let reception know that I hadn't actually eaten any of it - just had a look (it wasn't the stuff in the fridge but the peanuts etc above that I got caught out by!) 
Bed - Wow what a nice set up! There is what I would call a feather 'topper' on the mattress which is like sleeping on a feather duvet on top of the mattress - it has a sheet on top and you sink in to it. Then you have a feather duvet (covered) on top and I note a review before this which complained about the pillows being too hard. Just ask for a feather one (hopefully you are not allergic in which case you have to let them know in advance I would guess - about the whole bedding setup) There were only 3 pillows when we arrived - two on the bed and one in the cupbord. I just left a message for the housekeeper the next morning asking for an extra soft one and another one was duly supplied. 
Bathrobe - there was only one but if you needed another one then I am sure you would just need to ask - we didn't bother.
Air Con - on demand - a bit noisy - it probably isn't noisy but when you don't have it in your own home it is more of an unfamiliar noise. We soon got used to it and we needed it!
Elevator noise - none - it was right opposite our room door but on the rare occasion it 'pinged' when it got to our floor it was barely audible so not at all a bother.
Noise from other rooms - none whatsoever!
Noise from the street - some but not enough to make any impact on sleep.
Hotel -
Staff - so nice and friendly in a genuine way - always said hello.
Breakfast (second floor) - help yourself style - coffee, tea (water was hot enough to make a decent cup - us Brits love our tea in the morning so it is nice to get a good one to set you up for the day) Juice, cereal, whole and fat free milk, croissants, pastries, muffins, bagels, bread, butter, cream cheese, jams, peanut butter, hard boiled eggs, fresh fruit and fat free yoghurts. It was fab and really started the day off well - on most days we didn't eat again until mid - afternoon!
Wine and Cheese (second floor) - this was such a lovely touch. There was red, white and demi-sec sparkling plus bread, biscuits, cheese, mixed nuts etc. 
There is fresh fruit, cookies, buns and hot and cold beverages throughout the day as well as newspapers to read.
Free Internet - in the little office on the second floor- I used this most days to check/send emails and then to check in on our flight home - you can print your boarding passes out.
Rooftop bar (Bookmark) - we only made this on our last night and we both had a 'Bookmark' cocktail (yummy) at $15 each which I don't think is too bad - you also get a bowl of nibbles. Around $7 for a beer and not bad for wine (sorry I cannot remember price but remember not being shocked!). If you compare these hotel drink prices with those at home it is very reasonable I think. This bar is very popular at weekends with the public and appears to be an 'in place'.
We felt the location was perfect as it is a stones throw from Grand Central Terminal and various other places and when having a drink in the evening (second floor) you can marvel at the madness on Madison Avenue (couldn't say that after a few glasses of wine!)
All in all a fantastic hotel, no gripes about anything (and I am a fussy so and so - forgot to mention the hotel is so clean and tidy!) It wasn't cheap (about £200 per night) but you expect to pay that in NYC and we got our monies worth I would say especially with the breakfast and wine and cheese thrown in. 
We loved this hotel (oasis!) and we would definately stay again or if we couldn't get in we would stay in one of the other hotels in the group - Hotel Elysee (look on website for special offers for Xmas - would have gone this year but hubby cannot get time off!!), Hotel Giraffe or Hotel Casablanca.

title: “Great Location but average service”
text:
Location, location, location as the saying goes for real estate. This hotel is perfectly situated in downtown NYC, close to East village, Nolita and Soho and right off the LES bar scene.
But for hte rest, nothing out of the extraordinary.
I booked a king deluxe room @ 300usd/night and even at this price range you will not get much higher than the 5th floor, with a very limited view of NYC skyline, which is the biggest selling point of the hotel.
Strangely, the girl at the hotel skipped by free breakfasts and I had to get back to the front desk to get it settled. And last but not least a mistake on my bill was showing 3 items from the minibar that I did not consume. So make sure you check your bill.
This is below par 4 star hotel service level.
I probably will not stay again @ this location.

title: “Disappointingly average”
text:
We joined family staying at the nearby Radisson, having just stayed at another (excellent) Vagabond Inn (Bishop, CA). So our expectations were high.
Sleeping and accommodation is basic but sufficient. The advertised breakfast was the sum total of three dry bagels and a brewing pot of coffee. We first had a "non-smoking" room which clearly reeked of old smoke, so we had to change. The staff weren't attentive or enthusiastic at all. No wifi in rooms, just a lonely PC (without a chair) in reception.

title: “Great hotel! Definately will return.”
text: I stayed at this hotel for 12 nights because a family member was receiving medical treatment across the street at Methodist Hospital on Fannin Street. I also stayed there on another occasion for 2 nights. The hotel is clean and nicely decorated. Staff is friendly and always helpful. When you need to get to Methodist Hospital you can use the crosswalk - very convenient. The hotel has a Starbucks, small stopre and a restaurant - Driscols and it has very good food. There is also a lounge, but I didn't visit the lounge. There is also a deli, pharmacy, florist and a hair salon next door in Scurlock Tower. The hotel has valet parking or you may park in the parking garage next door. There is a business center on the 6th floor with computers and desks. The only thing i was not pleased with at this Marriott location is the air conditioning. The central air/heat seems to not cool as it should. You have to put the unit on 59 or 60 degress to keep the room comfortable. Management is aware of the problem, so If you ask for another room, they will accomodate you. That's good, but it would be a problem if the hotel was booked and you had to stay in a room that was not cool. Hotel is great in every other way.

title: “Bad. Simply Stated!!!!”
text:
Poor Room cleaning
They dont inform you about the construction noise.
Maid came into my room while I was in the shower and started cleaning.
Lobby wine moves to another floor but no one knows when you go down the next day.
seems like a bunch of kids are running this hotel.
I felt like I was dealing with teh cast from high school high. 
Will not be back.

title: “Short walk to "Wicked"”
text:
There are a lot of hotels in NYC, obviously, and a lot of reviews to check. As reviewed, this seemed like a nice enough hotel. I was fortunate to get a first hand review from a friend, so we booked a room for three for the 2007 Thanksgiving Holiday.
Here is the bottom line: We enjoyed this hotel. It was in a perfect location for us, the rooms were clean and, for NYC, spacious, and we liked being able to take leftovers from Manhattan restaurants back to put in the refrigerator in the room.
Now, some details: We didn't bother with the restaurant in the hotel. There are too many places to eat nearby that are less expensive.
The hotel is just far enough off 8th Ave to be quiet, as these things go. This is especially true if you are on an upper floor in the back.
I checked google maps to get directions to Wicked and was happy to see that it was just a few blocks away, as are most Broadway theaters. Wicked was dark that week thanks to the strike, but we went to "Spelling Bee" which was in the theater adjacent to Wicked. 
We also walked by the David Letterman/Ed Sullivan Theater, to Columbus Circle for the Macy's Parade, to Central Park, and to Times Square.
I had some trouble with the "for pay" internet in the business center. This service is not provided by the hotel. The company providing this service was very helpful in fixing the problem and refunding my money.
The front desk staff were very helpful as well, but we didn't see them very much.

title: “The Hills meets Jersey Shore”
text:
Chances are you're eyeing this hotel because your corporate office is right around the corner, the problem is this isn't really a functional hotel for business travellers. On the plus side you've got fast and free wifi and the restaurant is lovely in every regard, but its got none of the trappings of a proper hotel (ammenities that make you feel comfortable or relaxed) that are essential when you're trying to work remotely. There is really no separation of space between the hotel's (in)famous party scene (both in the lobby and on the roof) and the rooms. Don't get me wrong, I'm all for a good fiesta, but the last thing I want to do after a long mid-day work session is come back to a hotel with swim-clad drunks playing ping-pong in a darkly lit lobby with a DJ spinning like its Ibiza. I know, I must seem like the biggest stick in the mud, but I really did just pick this hotel because of it's location in Downtown LA (close to my corporate HQ), and this really is more of the type of hotel I'd expect to find in a far-flung corner of the Vegas strip.
Now, that said, if you're into far-flung corners of the Vegas strip this hotel is PERFECT for you, and the rooms are cheap too!

title: “Great hotel”
text:
Great location near Union Sq. Room was large well appointed with coffee maker and large flat screen TV. Large bathroom with storage and walk in shower
Hotel staff were very helpful. 
Great restaurant next door with access through hotel lobby.Great atmosphere!

title: “Do not stay here!!!”
text: First and foremost, the management at this property are rude. The only person who was actually courteous to the guests was fired for fraternizing? I thought this was supposed to be the hospitality industry?!? The wireless internet is ridiculous, only about 15K downloads. The tv's are only 19" with a limited cable channel selection. There is no type of breakfast or anything offered. There is no gym, pool, hot tub, etc. The walls are paper thin and I've had the neighbor from [--] since I've been here. He apparently has emphysemea or something and all you can hear all night long is *cough*cough*cough* (literally). I've been here 3 months and the only reason I've stayed is because I'm on a multi-month discounted rate and if I move I have to start paying hotel taxes again.

title: “Cute Boutique Hotel With Excellent Service & Good Location”
text: This 39 room three story independently owned inn, opened July 2003, is small in size and big on charm. Tastefully decorated in golden yellow, beige, and wood tones, the hotel exudes a bit of European flair that is comfortable and welcoming.I stayed here on a business trip from December 3-6, 2003, having booked this hotel after finding out most others on the Riverwalk were full. I was pleasantly surprised upon arrival, particularly after my taxi driver expressed concern that she'd never heard of it (and relied on my MapQuest directions to get there from the airport).Although there is no restaurant onsite, the hotel provides a continental breakfast each morning from 6-9 a.m. with muffins, yogurt, cereals, pastries, and fresh fruit. There's also a "make your own waffle" station, complete with pre-mixed cups of batter, that will let you cook up a Texas-shaped waffle. An additional bonus is the coffee maker in the lobby that brews up a quick cup of java for no charge.My room (207) was immaculately clean but quite small. The two double beds and TV armoire took up most of the space, and the only place to park the rather large desk chair was between the beds when I wanted to get up from the desk. I found the streetside room to be a noisy, due to the older single pane windows, but on the plus side I did not hear any noise from either the hallway nor adjoining rooms. The beds were extremely comfortable with padded mattress covers, velux blankets, and plenty of pillows. The bathroom was quite large for the overall room, and based on the size of the doorway and the shower configuration (no tub), the room is probably designed to be handicapped accessible.I would definitely return to this hotel, although I would request a room on the back side of the building as other reviewers have suggested. Not only are the rooms quieter, they are much larger in size. Room 107, for example, was twice as large as mine, with a king size bed and a whirlpool tub. Some of the other second floor rooms also offer balconies.The hotel is conveniently located just two blocks from the Riverwalk and two blocks from the Convention Center in Hemisfair Park so I was able to walk just about anywhere I wanted to go. For slightly longer outings to the Alamo and Market Square, I took one of the city sreetcars since the stop was just around the corner from the hotel (50 cents fare, one way). Since I didn't have a car, parking wasn't an issue but for those with a vehicle, parking is $8 per night and close to the hotel.Last but not least, the hotel staff persons are truly an asset to this property. They were friendly and helpful, and extremely accomodating when I requested an extended checkout time on the weekend.Overall, I would definitely recommend this hotel if you'd like to be close to downtown San Antonio attractions but away from the crowds. It's a cozy welcoming place to stay and a good value for the money. Kudos to the owners and staff for a job well done!

title: “Great location”
text: Very good motel; excellent location for sightseeing. Noisy rooms (if you're in the front of the motel).

title: “expensive but worth it”
text:
For the 3rd time I stayed here. Always excellent quality and great service.We paid $509/night. We were on the 46th(top) floor. We had requested that location and got it. This price is for the concierge floor. A beautiful big lounge that is opened with your keycard. Breakfast was great with cheese, meats, fruits,cereals, yogurts, a huge selection of pastries, bagels, juices, hot drinks and much more. This was listed as a continental breakfast but was so much more. Afternoon and early evening(till 8) drinks, soft,water and hot, plus cheeses, fruit,crackers, full size selection of candy bars,fresh cookies. We could have made a meal out of it, and did. We only ate lunch out. Although it is in the middle of Time Square, (Thefront entrance is so hidden when you pull up, it takes a minute to find it) there was NO NOISE<AT ALL. You walk in and are very surprised. Nice lobby and bar, great health club.
The location of this is perfect for theater goers. We walked out the back entrance(cabs can be called for you if needed and covered so no weather problems) and crossed the street to see our first play! Literally within 3 to 5 minutes to most of the shows in the area. We never needed to take a taxi or subway. We walked everywhere.Central Park, MOMA, Rockefeller Center, Fifth Ave. What a ball! It was well worth the money.
The staff was very helpful, desk, concierge, housekeeping(called and brought extra robe within 5 minutes. I have stayed at MANY hotels in New York, in all different locations. I love this one!!

title: “Good Vaue for Money”
text: Good value hotel, staff helpful and friendly throughout, ideal for the Billy Graham Library and good restaurant on the site. Very close to motorway for exploring the area.

title: “Great Guest Service by Diane Cheeks”
text:
I would like to first start off by stating that this is my 2nd stay here at the Sheraton Gateway Los Angeles and the 2nd experience has been EXCEPTIONALLY great!! From the time we checked in, to the level of Guest Service over the phone by Diane Cheeks has been wonderful. All things are extremely important due to the nature of our stay. We are here on a medical trip for our 7yr old son. Diane has made certain that erroneously charges were removed and we had ample enough towels. She always called back to ensure we were okay.
We are grateful and blessed to have been serviced by Diane Cheeks. 
As a result, my husband and I will definitely consider the Sheraton Gateway L.A. for all future stays when we are in the LAX area. 
Warmest,
Freunda "TeAnn" Gray
Room #1020

title: “A very nice stay, thank you.”
text: Had a very nice ten day stay at this very well run hotel. The minor problem of noisy neighbours we had was quickly sorted out by the efficient manageress. Would have no hesitation in recommending this hotel to anyone.

title: “Come for the decor”
text:
This hotel is stunning in its decor and design. Stumble through the dark corridors to your bedroom door and you will be amazed by the sumptuous luxury that lies inside. We stayed in a deluxe loft which had vast amounts of space for two people, a huge desk for working and a long couch to pile the shopping on. The red velvet, mirrored mini bar and deliciously scented candles helped me to name the style- "how I would decorate if my mother never came to visit"
The neighbourhood is great and if you have the time you can walk practically anywhere on the island from this location or jump in a cab and you'll be there within minutes.
The doormen and housekeeping staff and service were truly 5 star. We had a few issues with dopey reception staff, but nothing major. Luckily we declined their offer to hurriedly charge everything to the credit card on file, instead insisting on a printout; despite handing back the iPod two minutes previously and reminding the girl to cancel the deposit, the extortionate $750 was still lurking on there. For a iPod from the 90s! Seriously, you should be giving them out in the cornflakes! Which brings me to the other hiccup- breakfast. We were told we had continental breakfast on the terrace included, after seeing the lame selection I should have insisted on the room service breakfast we should have had with our booking. Sadly I was too polite and English to complain but if you are paying for it, don't bother! There are a couple of cute cafes across the park with a much better selection, where you can find something much more appetising. Especially if you want breakfast at 10am when sweaty cheese and melted muffins were on offer on the semi- outdoor roof terrace. Yes it was hot, so get a chiller cabinet or do a la carte cheese...
Our room was noisy from the air conditioning units clustering around the internal courtyard, a downside of NYC in summer. Buy earplugs or cough up top dollar for a park view room seemed to be the solution. I chose earplugs and a cognac from the minibar helped too!
Overall only a couple of negatives throughout a very happy week here. Can't recommend it enough if you want extravagant escapism in the heart of the city.

title: “Hooker Hotel”
text: We arrived from England having spent 24 hours in transit, the cab driver stopped outside a sex shop, next to which was the New York Inn. Ok, so we're broad-minded, however when we entered it was like something from a Starsky & Hutch setting. The reception was filthy and the corridors were dated and dimly lit - that's the best part of the place! The room initially looked ok with cleanish bedding, so we started to unpack. Went into the closet-sized bathroom, looked above and there was a gaping hole left by missing tiles. The sink was "Barbie-size" and dirty; can't imagine how you could use the shower without placing a foot in the toilet. At this stage we were still reconciled to the fact that we were in New York and determined to make the best of it, however, when we couldn't lock our room door and during our efforts, heard a "gang bang" next door, we thought it was time leave!

title: “Nice location, good size rooms, not my favorite hotel on Michigan Ave.”
text: The location of this hotel is good. It is a short walk across the river to the main shopping area. We weren't able to hear noise from other guests in the hotel, but even though we were on the 13th floor, we could hear a lot of noise from cars and people on the street. The rooms are large, nice kitchen, lots of closets, washer and dryer. The bathtub had some chips out of it. I wouldn't let my daughter take a bath in the tub. One of the elevators stopped working on Sunday morning. I walked up and down the stairs several times trying to get the stuff out of our room to check-out. It was a major inconvience.

title: “There are better places for a lower price at LAX!”
text: The room was small, old, and with smoke smell, although it was a non-smoking room. The complimentary shuttle to the airport was too small, and many people had to wait the next one because we were too many. Fortunately, we were not in a hurry with our flight, because otherwise we would have to take a cab.

title: “Great located...”
text: I was in this hotel some time ago, and mixed up in the first moment when we tried to find correct one, because this hotels old name is Quality hotel Time Square and in that time they were making renovation. Double room was really small, our luggage was staying next to the bed and took all free place. Bathroom was clean and I loved french cosmetics in it.

title: “Right on the Riverwalk!”
text:
Second leg of our anniversary trip to Texas. Stayed in Houston first then traveled to San Antonio and stayed here on the Riverwalk. Our stay was pleasant enough. We arrived around 3pm to find our room wasn't ready. No big deal really. They collected my husband's cell number and called us when it was ready (about 2 hours later). We parked in the garage ($14 per day) and walked along the Riverwalk while we waited. The hotel is right on the Riverwalk and the location along the walk is really phenomenal. The weather was magnificent while we were there, great temperature and sunny the entire time. The Riverwalk truly is beautiful and if you go to San Antonio it's worth it to stay directly on the river.
Once our room was ready we brought our luggage in and tried to get settled a bit. The rooms and the entire hotel are older and you can tell, but everything was clean. The size of the room was nice. The bed was comfy and internet available. We stayed in a room that had a view of the river. The room was a little dark and the bedding could definitely be newer but, like I said, older hotel. The bathroom was sufficient. Small but sufficient. 
The best part of the hotel has got to be the free drink cards and free snacks every evening at 5:30pm. When you check in you are provided with drink cards for everyone over 21. Each evening during free snack time in the lobby, you provide them with your card and receive a free alcoholic beverage. Soft drinks are free without the card, as are the snacks. There are usually a lot of guests there for snacks so get there right when they start serving so you can grab a table. 
Other things to do while there:
Visit the Alamo
Go shopping at the outlet malls in San Marcos
Rio San Antonio riverwalk tours (didn't do this but wish we had!)
Visit the visitor's center across the street from the Alamo
Things to skip or think really hard about:
Ripley's Believe or Not
Louis Tussaud's Wax Museum
:::these are both wayyyy overpriced for what they are:::

title: “Great Room, Great Roof.. Check your tires”
text:
We booked a room at the Madison in July as a get-away. We went on a Thursday when they have live music on the roof top and it was a blast. The river view was great, the breeze kept it cool and the band was great. 
Our room was a superior king and was nicely appointed, not too big but very nice. The Bathroom was large and spacious.
Overall the staff was very friendly and efficient. We did tried to order room service at 11pm, but when they transferred me it just rang and rang. So I went directly to the bar and ordered.
Two things of note: The Valet Parking attendent appearantly hit the curb and put a 3 inch long gash in one of my tires, ruining it. So check your tires before you leave I didn't see it happen and didn't notice til I got home, by then it was too late. 
Also - The hotel does not have a medical concession machine anywhere. I got heartburn at 2am and was out of luck. Take any meds you may need with you. 
Overall - I'll go back, I'll just check my tires and pack my rolaids.

title: “Nice, but overpriced for what you get.”
text: The room was nice, but not fabulous. The view was great. Very convenient location for navy pier and magnificent mile. Would not have chosen but was at conference. Staff very nice, friendly and helpful. For the money I have stayed at much nicer conference hotels.

title: “Just Okay!”
text:
My husband stayed here for one night to be close to LAX for a morning flight. We checked in and arrived in our room, which was clean and located on a higher floor. We had dinner in the bar, which service was slow but, we didn't have a lot of choise since we wer advised not to walk around the area, it was too dangerous. We expected some noise from outside the hotel due to the proximity to the airport, however we were very surprised at the internal noise. All night we heard the running water, and other noises we couldn't identify. 
We inquired after dinner with the concerige about checking-in at LAX and checking bags when to leave the hotel in the morning. We were advised to check-in online and "bag drop" at the airport with no waiting in line. We left for LAX approx. 1.5 hr prior to departure, and discovered the shuttle was delayed 15-20 minuets and the hotel began to use taxis to transport people to the airport. Upon arrival to LAX, we has to wait in line and almost missed out flight.
I would not recommend this hotel due to the noise factor, and the shuttle problem.

title: “All 'round Best Hotel Ever”
text: They had comfy beds and pillows. The staff was extremely helpful. It was located in a safe neighborhood right outside the city of Boston, and right down the street from this great restaurant "Tasca". The hotel is directly across from the T stop. Best sleep i ever had thank you BW

title: “Great value on a budget. Charming and overwhelmingly adequate.”
text:
Looking to save some money on a weekend trip with a friend, we booked a two-twin room with shared bath. For the traveler who spends minimal time in the hotel and doesn't require all the amenities, this was a steal. 
The shared baths were incredibly clean, and always available. Only issue was that hot water was low on supply after 10AM. Room was adequate, with a good (though loud) air conditioner. I might recommend packing your own pillow-case, as the inevitable city hotel odors and allergens might interfere with an otherwise great sleep.
Great location, close to subway and restaurants, walkable to Village or Midtown. Highly recommended for a quaint NYC experience.

title: “Excellent vacation!”
text: My first visit to Chicago was amazing, the W Chicago Lakeshore Hotel was absolutely spectacular! We had a lakeside suite overlooking the beach and Navy Pier, saw 4th of July fireworks right from our room. The W Lakeshore was the best Hotel we've ever stayed in, everything was FIRST CLASS! Every staff member we ecnountered was top notch, especially David Brownrigg who went above and beyond to help make our stay extra special! We will stay at the W Lakeshore every time we visit Chicago, it is perfectly located and have ZERO complaints!!

title: “Horrible motel”
text: We check-in in this motel at New Years Eve to attend a formal dinner dance show, the room smell is terrible bad, gum sticked on top of the headboard, bed sheet with blood spot and some yellow stain near the pillow, a small coffee pot and no coffee cups, behind the dresser at least 3 cigarette butts and the worst disguisting was the used condom! I report these to the desk and definitely want to change the room, it tooks an hour for the desk came up and we showed him the evidences. (I did have a picture to proof it too). We are senior from out of town, requesting ground floor non-smoking room is more convenience for us, but she put us on the 3rd floor, the business is not busy at all.

title: “Loved It -- but not cheap.”
text:
Stayed in a Jr. Suite on the 15th floor. Had a beautiful room with a fantastic view. It was the perfect weekend getaway for my wife and me. 
The extra charges can pile up quickly. For us = $15 internet, $52 valet parking, $12 movie, $30 breakfast. Of course we could've not gotten some of those things, but this was our weekend to splurge on ourselves. 
Our room wasn't finished when we arrived (2hrs before check-in) and they called us on our cell phone to let us know our room was ready. They had taken our bags up to the room and everything was ready for us.

title: “Great Hotel for the Price”
text: Staff was super friendly. They were very accommodating to the marathoners. Room was clean and comfortable. Great location. Painless check-in/check-out. I would consider this hotel again if I stayed in Columbus.

title: “Average hotel, great location for seeing San Fran”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for four nights in late September. Our room was on the executive floor and had view of Alcatraz in the distance. The room was comfortable, with queen beds and a microwave. However, the room could have been better cleaned, and it was not double glazed, so there was a certain amount of noise from air conditioning units and the road (despite being on the fifth floor).
We did not eat at the hotel, mainly because the restaurant was expensive and always empty. We had vouchers for free tea/coffee at breakfast time. When we tried to redeem these, we were told that they only had fruit tea, and a limited selection of pastries. These were not significant issues due to the location, which had numerous other alternatives nearby.
The location of the hotel is excellent. It is approximately five minute walk from fishermans wharf, pier 39, the cable car terminal and very near to a tram stop. In the evenings the location allowed us a great variety of restaurants within a short walk. It was possible to reach China Town, Little Italy, and a range of seafood restaurants on the bay.
The parking at the hotel was $32 + tax per day. This was expensive, but expected in a good location in a big city. On the fifth floor corridor there were a couple of PCs with free Internet access.

title: “Great hotel at Logan - and so convenient ...”
text: This is a great place to stay if you have an early flight: just walk to your terminal in under five minutes. Comfortable room, with superb view across the water to the city; good buffet breakfast; very tasty meal from room service ... what's not to like?

title: “Solid chain hotel experience”
text:
* Above average Marriott experience with decent size rooms for NYC and friendly staff. 
* No free WiFi in the rooms is a drawback - but avail in the lobby.
* Restos selection is a sports bar and Starbucks but so much in the hood making it no big issue
* Rooms decently appointed. No robes but coffee maker, electronic hook-ups and clean and modern decor
* Close to most subway lines

title: “Clean Hotel, Rooms a little dated. Good value overall...”
text: Stayed here two nights in January. This hotel was very clean overall and the service was good. The furniture and decor in the rooms were somewhat dated. Complimentary breakfast was on par with that of a Hilton Garden Inn, except that it was free! Would recommend and stay here again.

title: “As good as you'd like”
text:
This hotel is in a great central location for the Gaslamp Quarter and is clean, modern, well decorated and has a very pleasant staff.
We could not have asked for better treatment than we received and I could find no fault with anything in our room. It was very nicely maintained.
My only "nit pick" would be they should open their bar and hour earlier to coincide with check-in time and perhaps they should plug their food service a bit more. We enjoyed the appetizer selection and the two we tried were exceptional. The breakfast bar was very well stocked and items were replaced quickly when needed.
I definitely recommend this hotel.

title: “Great hotel stay”
text: Love this hotel for its character and ambience. Rooms are beautiful and roomy- suites are a great bargain. Staff is very helpful and family friendly. Cute bar and rooftop bar. You can't beat this location!

title: “Great Location, Terrific Service”
text:
I do not write many reviews, but as there are negative reviews of this property, we thought to add our perspective. We checked into room 2015 on Friday afternoon for 3 nights. The location of the hotel is great. Easy access from the airport, a public parking lot is next door along 16th street ($18 per day before 5pm on Friday, $5 per 24 hours on the weekend before 9am on Monday), walking distance to art museum, Walnut street shopping/eating and historic district, 1 block from the "Plash trolley" that is $2 per ride -we used this in the rain, and 1 block from Starbucks. 
 We were very impressed with the staff - different concierges assisted us on Friday and Saturday and both were exceedingly knowledgeable and helpful, the front desk staff were efficient, but most amazingly, the housekeeping staff was ALWAYS asking if we needed anything else or how we were enjoying our stay...not only our friendly housekeeper, but every staff member as we passed through the building.
 We will be honest about the room. it had a good view, was a good size, nice bathroom with a lot of counter space,big flat screen, and lovely linens. But, the carpets were frayed and looked in need of washing. Then, during the night, we realized the AC was going on and off every 4 minutes. In the morning, we told the front desk and although they could not do anything about the carpeting, the AC was fixed while we were out.
 We stayed at the Sheraton using the "birth year" special, where your 1st night is the regular price and the 2nd and 3rd night is according to when you are born. It made our stay at this hotel financially reasonable for being in a large city, in a great location, and at a lovely Sheraton property.

title: “Good location”
text:
We checked into the hotel on a Thursday. We requested adjoining rooms with family members but upon entering our room, we realized it did not connect. The bellhop attempted to assist us, but the hotel could not accomodate us. This was a little frustrating since we specifically requested this when we made our reservations months ago.
The rooms were a good size and the bed was comfortable. There are several eating options at this hotel, but everything is expensive. We had breakfast in the deli for two of the mornings and had the buffet on the last morning. The buffet was $22 but had a lot to choose from. We did all the typical tourist stuff in DC. I would recommend booking a White House tour if you can, it has to be done in advance, but well worth it.
I would recommend this hotel, it is large and although pricey, was in a good location as the Metro Center stop was right below the hotel.

title: “Completely Satisfied - Good stuff River Inn!!”
text: My wife and I stayed here during a huge snow storm. The entire staff was very helpful and accommodating around check-in and check-out times. The room was very large and included a partial kitchen area. It was also very clean and had a sweet style to it. The hotel restaurant was great and their staff was super friendly. The location was great; it was near the monuments, the shopping in Georgetown, and a Metro train stop. Most of all they were extremely helpful with our ground transpiration to the airport. The snow had most of the city shut down, including most taxis. Their staff arranged for a ride, chased the driver around a few blocks as he couldn't get down the snowy side streets, and called the driver as he was driving us to make sure we made it to the airport timely and safely. My hat is off to this top notch hotel!!!

title: “Sucks, but it's NYC...”
text:
We've stayed at the Riverside Tower twice. Our first stay was ok, though our bed was so worn out there was a valley in the middle of it. But our last stay was really disappointing; we were offered a discount that actually meant an ugly, depressing room, so tiny we had to keep our luggage piled up because there wasn't enough room to either unpack or have the cases around the room.Walking down the corridor to the room when we checked in was scary and I was sure we'd find bed bugs in our bed.
Anyway, the shower is good, the heater works fine and the location is great, two blocks away from Brodway and a subway station. But paying through the nose and having to settle for a crappy room is awfully offputting, though it seems to be the norm in NYC. Shame...

title: “Enjoyable Stay”
text:
I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone considering a visit to Boston. Whilst not in the downtown area it is incredibly easy to travel in and out of the city centre. The hotel shuttle runs throughout the day and we never had to wait more than 10 minutes for a bus. The bus takes you directly to the Airport T station from where it is a short ride into the centre of Boston and all the key sights. An alternative way to travel would be to walk into the airport terminal and get the Silverline T which is a bus - this goes via the Conference centre (not Hynes but the other one!). During our stay there seemed to be a lot of attendees from the Microsoft Conference but this didn't cause us any problems. We found the service at the Irish Bar to be prompt and good - the food is okay too. 
The hotel leisure club facilities were very good - the water pressure in the showers at the pool was much better than that in our room. Being Hilton Members we received a room upgrade and got a great end of corridor/corner room with fantastic views of Boston and the harbour (7th Floor). We were also able to use the Club Lounge which provides a continental breakfast. No problems with housekeeping encountered.

title: “March 2012”
text: We went up for the weekend for a family wedding. The wedding party had reserved hotel rooms at another location at a discounted price. We decided to try Suites because it was in our timeshare group. We were not disapointed. It was very close to were the wedding was taking place, but also in a centralized location. Close to the pier, cable cars and Ghiradelli Square, just to name a few. Makeing the reservations were a breeze. Check in was quick. The staff were very friendly and helpful. The suites were a nice size and very clean and comfortable. Modern furnishings. The elevators were small, but had a beautiful wide staircase which I chose to take. We have a large truck, and the parking spaces were a little small, but we got in and out ok. I would definatly stay here again. I don't really remember if it was noisy or not, so I guess it couldn't have been that bad. I would reccomend this place without a doubt.

title: “Great Stay, Again!”
text: Once again, the Homewood Suites Park Central Dallas has shined. Great suite and comfortable bed with several pillows to choose from. Very clean and quiet. The daily breakfast selection was super. The complementary evening meal and drink (M-Th), was, as always, a great treat…and the food was terrific.

title: “Don't do it!”
text:
1)hotel was dirty
2) hotel was stinky. We stayed in a nonsmoking room but the sheets both nights had been in smoking rooms
3) bugs, most specifically spiders, roaches, and crickets
4) if you put the sign on the door asking FOR cleaning, the housekeeper automatically assumes the sign means "don't clean" because....why? she can't read? (Hotel manager explained this to us)
5) seedy characters - lots of panhandlers and people walking around at night
6) the train is EVERY HOUR - and it isn't 1000 yards away
7) next to a very overgrown lot and several abandoned houses, dead end streets, etc.

title: “Simply Bliss”
text:
I booked my stay at the intercontinental as a surprise city break for my husband. I can honestly say, we have no complaints whatsoever. The hotel is a 5* and trust me, it deserves every one of them. 
When we arrived at the hotel, first impressions exceeded our expectations. The grand entrance, the polished reception and the sweet smelling flowers. Checking in was quick and easy at reception. We were booked to stay in a "run of the house" room. We were asked by reception if we were staying for a special occasion. As it was my husbands birthday at the time, we mentioned this. They made a quick phone call and before we knew it, we were handed our room key to a deluxe 3 person suite. We couldn't believe it. (Special mention to Peter Jones at reception for arranging this and checking us in). 
When we arrived at our room, we couldn't believe our eyes. The was a sitting area with a sofabed (for our daughter), a TV, desk, walk in wardrobe and fantastic views of the Chrysler building, and this was only the first room! We walked through to our bedroom with a grand king sized bed, another tv, an en suite bathroom, a large wardrobe and even more incredible views of outside. Our room was positioned on the front corner of the hotel so we benefited from some of the most amazing views possible.
The room was clean and one of the most amazing rooms that we as a family have ever stayed in. We requested a few extra blankets and a few minutes later, the maid bought us some. 5* service. 
We felt that the hotel was in a great location, it wasn't too noisy or too quiet - just right. We were only a few minutes walk from local attractions, including the bus stop for the downtown loop (i thoroughly recommend that you take a trip on this). There were a few cafe's nearby for breakfast and a parade of restaurants nearby for dinner. 
Overall we couldn't of wished for a better stay in New York. We want to go back in the future and will definitely be returning to this hotel. The hotel was brilliant, and we could not fault it.

title: “Hotel was ok - staff members were terrific!”
text:
Thanks to Josh and Amanda and another nice guy at the front desk, my review is upgraded from 3 to a 4. This is an older property - you can tell by the paucity of electric outlets. Not much charging space next to the bed, and the room had an odd odor which cleared out (or I got used to it) after turning on the air conditioner. It was quiet, wifi worked well even in a room at the very end of a hall, and I liked the underground parking - very convenient in a rainstorm. About half a mile away is a shopping center with a grocery store, excellent sushi restaurant, and other places to eat. Tio Pepes, a Mexican restaurant, is within walking distance, although I did not eat there. 
I attended a conference at the Doubletree and stayed at the Hampton for about $50 less per night and had free breakfast and free wifi; both of which the Doubletree charges for. It was a 5 minute walk over and back each day, which I enjoyed.

title: “A perfect Perch”
text:
I have stayed at the Four Season Chicago many times. The hotel has a great location and staff. The hotel only has one negative.
Since it began remodeling over the past few years, it has no style identity. The room are more consistent than the main lobby. It tries to be comtempory, but just misses the target. I think the lobby has been refreshed 3 times in the past 5 years.
The best Sunday Buffett is now just a memory. You have to go to the Pennisula Hotel for that treat now.
Still the best for family friendly visits.

title: “Right in the middle...or almost!”
text: Very close to the gas lamp district, harbour, SD convention center, USS Midway museum and 10 minutes drive form the airport. Modern with nice rooms, great view and friendly service. Parking nearby but rather expensive.

title: “Stay elsewhere if you are diamond”
text:
I stayed at this Hotel overnight after a long trip from Australia, the kids were exhausted but were very excited to see a gingerbread house in the lobby for Xmas.
Check in was easy at the Honors desk and internet details were sorted so I could get on upon reaching the room.
The room was nothing special and we headed down to the Executive lounge for Canapes and drinks.
They were renovating the lounge so we headed to a small conference room with food all over tables and the poorest choice of nibbles I have ever seen from a Hilton and drinks I had to pay for.
When questioning what was happening the staff advised that if I didnt know the economy is bad in the states and they have cut out the services to Diamond members hence no free drinks and food you wouldnt want to eat in a tiny little room with too many VALUED CLIENTS to handle.
I left in disgust and had to go there in the morning for our COMPLIMENTARY breakfast, after looking at the line out of the sqalid room and watching Diamond members trying to eat cereal standing up I went to the front desk and complained.
There I ran into a lovely lady who gave me vouchers to the buffet and also printed out my boarding passes while I ate breakie.
I cant remember her name but Hilton should give her a pay rise or she should move to a hotel where they look after staff and guests!
You would figure if the economy is bad you would want to look after your repeat customers!!

title: “Great Budget Hotel”
text:
This is a great hotel on a budget. We Stayed 3 nights and found it to be great. It is not fancy our room did not have air conditioning or a fancy TV but we had a great stay. The location is great and you can get around easy downtown. We took the free tour of the Moore Theather located next to hotel. Our room was clean and we loved the towel animals. The bathroom and shower are very small but nice. We found free parking on the street Sunday.
We would stay here again!

title: “Exceptional!”
text:
Took a Spring Training break from March 11-14, 2007 and was lucky enough to draw this resort on a very reasonable Priceline bid. It is a beautiful place and the grounds and all common areas are meticulously maintained. The two room suite was very nice and comfortable and clean. We were in the Mountainside area and our balcony overlooked a beautiful, lightly used pool and whirlpool. 
We had an early flight in and arrived at the hotel at 9:30AM. To my amazement we were allowed to check in immediately!. We had a late flight out on departure day so the day before I called the front desk and asked for a two hour late check out. They advised that they were at capacity and politely declined. Later that evening I went to the lobby to print our boarding passes (free, in the business center) and stopped by the front desk and made my late check-out request again. They immediately and graciously granted a 2:00PM checkout. I guess the point here would be: if you have a reasonable request that is declined--ask again on a different shift OR make your request in person. 
We didn't dine at the hotel other than a decent, reasonably (comparatively speaking, given the surroundings) priced room service breakfast. There are several very casual decent dining choices at the intersection about two minutes north of the hotel.
Only a couple slight negatives:
--In our building noise was a slight factor. We didn't hear other voices, but could hear doors slamming, etc, and the plumbing was moderately noisy.
-- As others have pointed out, the entire property is quite hilly which makes the atmosphere of the place. I really can't see, however, how only but the most fit of older seniors could consider staying here.
We loved this place. Would even consider paying other than a Priceline rate (gasp!) to stay here again.

title: “Very nice!”
text: Lovely and spacious room with a skyline view. Bathroom was exceptional! Champagne & Rum Bar lovely and service was great. Room service was delightful in the morning. I slept so well in this hotel and service was wonderful. Thank you for a wonderful stay!

title: “Great hotel & fantastic staff!”
text:
This was our first stay in NYC! Both the hotel itself and the staff were fantastic!
May not be located in the most charming street but very close to Times square and other great places of interest and a metro stop at 100m.
The hotel room was super clean with nice modern decor with huge flat screen, good wifi and iPod dock radio. All you could ask for was there! We had requested a room on high floor and we got it so it was absolutely great! We also liked the notes left in the evening with weather forecast for the next day and some chocolates!!!
The staff was very helpful and always available for some nice local tips. Thanks a lot!
On our next trip to NYC we'll definitely come back to Distrikt hotel.

title: “Clean and good location”
text:
I enjoyed my stay at the Wellington. The location is good, being a 15 minute walk to Times Square. Also there is a subway station right AT the hotel. The room I had was very good indeed, I had a VIEW of TImes Square and was on the second highest floor. I asked for a room with a view and they gave it to me. Thank you so much!!
The restaurant near the lobby was also fine. No complaints except that it was always VERY busy and often I had to wait for a table, but this is New York! Food and service was excellent. 
The air conditioning unit was noisy and could not be left on to sleep. I also caught a cold from the air conditioning unit. Maybe the filters need to be CLEANED or replaced.

title: “Couldn't rate this place highly enough”
text: I have never had such a pleasant hotel stay. The staff were endlessly helpful. The room and location were great. I will definitely stay at the Hotel Carlton again next time I'm in San Francisco.

title: “great time”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Fisherman's Wharf Sheraton Hotel in San Francisco a week in early November 2012. We had a great experience the hotel is in a great location, the information desk was always helpful in arranging tours for us, and the room was very clean and room service was excellent. It was our 1st visit to San Francisco and we have no complaints. I would defintly go back and stay there again.

title: “SMALL rooms at Hotel Griffon!”
text:
Hotel Griffon has a cute charm to it, but I would only stay here again if the price was very low and I was not planning on spending a lot of time in the room. 
Pros:
Cute, historic charm. Nice exposed brick wall in room and great Aveda bath products. Good location, although we usually had to walk a block or two to get a cab. Continental breakfast was nice. Everything appeared very clean. I requested more towels and they were sent up quickly. We were very impressed with all of the staff, including the front desk, in the restaurant, and at breakfast. 
Cons:
Many people said small rooms, which usually don’t bother me, but our room was beyond small. I actually felt a little claustrophobic because the window looked out into a very small, dark, dirty brick cave-like hole. There are also very few king beds because many of the rooms are too small to accommodate them. Despite booking months in advance and requesting a king bed multiple times, I could only get a full bed. The rooms must also be all different sizes because I was with other people who paid the same rate and both had slightly larger rooms so you may get the luck of the draw on your room. 
The sink and mirror in the room was a little strange but at least there was good counter space. 
The location of the TV mounted on the wall was just too high and awkward. 
The bed and linens were below average and the pillows were definitely very old, as they were extremely flat. 
The shower had very low water pressure. In fact, I think the sink faucet had more water flow and pressure than the shower.
I was on the third floor, close to the elevator and the stairs, right above the fireplace downstairs and there was a definite smell in the hallway that other people wrote about, but I couldn't smell it in the room. 
I could however, very clearly hear every word being spoken in the hallway, even when I could tell that people were trying to be quiet. There was also a substantial gap between the door and the floor which let in a lot of light in the night. 
Lastly, the temperature controls were not very good. Sometimes the room was too hot and sometimes too cold and the basic warm/cool control in the room did very little to change the temperature. 
Verdict: Hotel Griffon tries very hard, but is average. It is probably better to stay in an upgraded, guaranteed King room with a view, but for those prices I would just stay somewhere else, especially with two people in a room. Don't even think about roll away beds or having kids with you!

title: “Austin”
text: Needs major Remodeling, the property is very rundown and the quality of the food is horrible, does not reflect Wyndom quality.

title: “Wow! The JW was the best part of a perfect weekend!”
text: From the moment you drive up, you are showered with kind, caring and helpful service. The staff here are anxious to be at your service. They love working there, and it really shows. This hotel is a well-located, hidden gem. It's low-profile on the outside, but gorgeous on the inside. Timeless decor and a spacious, elegant lobby make for an amazing ambiance. It's spotless too. We live in Marin, but wanted a calm, get-away weekend. This fit the bill perfectly. The Level 3 Restaurant was amazing. The seafood chowder was the best soup I've ever had, and the mac 'n cheese was world class. The best part was our room, the Pacific Suite. It was a comfy home away from home. Price was more than reasonable. You can't go wrong. My congratulations to the management for a job well done!

title: “Don't Stay at the Lancaster”
text: We stopped staying at the Lancaster about 3 years ago because we thought it was getting run-down. This weekend we decided to try the Lancaster again for a weekend stay in the hopes that its owners (the Valencia Group) would have refurbished it. Bad news: they haven't. The upholstery on the couch in our room was stained and ripped, with the stuffing showing; the bed's mattress was lumpy and uncomfortable; the carpet was really grimy; the hallway smelled; the phone handset never worked and never was repaired (though we notified management); and the bathroom sink ran rusty water the first two times we turned it on. The tragedy is that in the mid-1990s, this was a lovely small hotel The hotel has a killer location (which is perfect for travelers who are in Houston for the opera, ballet, symphony or Alley Theater ), a nice staff (who despite failing to fix our phone problem are friendly, caring and attentive) and free wireless Internet access throughout the property. But for their rack room rate, one can do much better in downtown Houston and in locations that are still quite convenient to all the best cultural activities. We won't stay here again until there's evidence that it has been completely renovated and refurbished.

title: “Posh, caring and elegant”
text:
My husband was booked to work for a week in NYC and was put up in the London NYC. The company graciously invited me to join him and I took advantage of the offer for two nights. The front desk staff was efficient and gracious, the doorman attentive, and every staff person we encountered greeted us. The housekeeping staff came several times daily to check if all was well and offered services, such as turning down the bed or to inquire whether we needed anything. 
The room we were given had two beds, which we had requested, due to my light and restless sleeping tendencies (request made in advance but not guaranteed), and was a two room suite, which, having booked at the bottom of the rate range, must be the case for all rooms. The rooms were spacious, although not large by most standards, but very pleasant, owing mostly to the efficient design of the furnishings. The two flat screen TVs, motorized drape controls, very responsive climate control system made the accommodations very comfortable. The bathroom had two lighting systems; one stronger one for grooming and makeup and the other on a dimmer to allow for subtle lighting during sleeping hours. The shower was actually two showers in one long area, with separate controls. The door to the bath was a pocket-type door on a sliding track. Great space saver. Very clever. Slippers and robes were provided. Ten real take-them-off-the-bar hangers with skirt/kpants clips. Iron and ironing board in the room. Hairdryer also. Nice soaps and decent shampoos and conditioners (although, pity, they were not Molton Brown, my very fav.) 
As my husband is required to travel a good bit, and I accompany a good part of the time, I consider myself a veteran traveler. I have a standard bag which includes a goosedown pillow, a white noise machine, sleeping mask, and bamboo blanket. In my experience, hotel pillows are uncomfortable, hotel rooms are generally not quiet (due to loudly closing doors, outside noise, etc), draperies do not really close out light and it is impossible to achieve a comfortable room temperature. I was so pleasantly surprised to find that the pillows at London were identical to my own, the draperies closed impeccably and blacked out all daylight, and the room doors did not slam and clatter when closed. In all honestly, I must mention that there did seem to be endless construction noises going on outside the hotel, even in the wee hours of the morning, but I cannot fault the hotel for that. 
In perusing other reviewers' comments before arriving at the London, I was somewhat apprehensive. Several comments were made regarding the front desk staff. My experience in dealing with the front desk staff over four days' time is that they never failed to be friendly, efficient and helpful. I never once had to wait to gain their attention.
