Never did anyone fail to acknowledge my presence in a moment. I cannot imagine more attentive or friendly service. 
I enjoyed the breakfast offerings twice during my stay, once having eggs and bacon and once having the cold buffet. Both times the service was impeccable, the food perfectly presented and tasty. 
It would be hard for me to imagine what else anyone could want to provide a five star experience. I would be happy to return to the London any chance I get. 
As I commuted from NJ and thus, took four train rides, I required transportation to the train station. The first time I requested a taxi, I was supplied with the hotel courtesy car, which took me to the station. Lovely fellow, the driver. 
Had the pleasure to dine in the Formal Dining room of the hotel restaurant. What a divine treat! Cannot do justice to describe the meal. Suffice it to say it may be the single best dinner I have ever had on several continents over many years of traveling. Almighty expensive, but worth it. In addition, we were treated to a tour of the kitchen, which delighted my husband ( a real foodie!) and myself no end.

title: “Nice property, outstanding location”
text:
We stayed twice at the Liberty on our trip to New England. There were a few hiccups on our initial stay which I was a little annoyed by. However, overall the hotel is very vibrant. The lobby is very nice as are the rooms.
Hats off to the front desk staff, especially Kate and Fiona and Chris at the front door, who are all very attuned to guest needs.
Most of all, I expressed my frustrations with the hotel's GM, Rachel Moniz. Rachel is a real class act, who I believe is dedicated to ensuring excellence at this property. 
She ensured our return stay went off without a hitch and it did.
The complementary cava and sparking pink lemonade at check in was a nice touch. Food at Clink is above average.
I would definitely look to the Liberty as my first choice when returning to Boston.

title: “seatlle vacation”
text: The Roosevelt is a very nice hotel, up to date and very centrally located for shopping, dining and transportation. We booked the room and meal package and ate at Purple - one of the restaurants - it was a very nice addition to our trip. Had a nice stay and will return when next we visit Seattle.

title: “Lovely decor downstairs but only decent rooms”
text:
Like many of the hotels in the area, I would imagine, Hotel Adagio is an older building that has been updated, at least on the surface. The front desk, downstairs lobby, bar area and computer room are beautifully decorated but the rooms are rather simple, albeit clean and comfortable. 
The bathroom sink drained very slowly and we were on the go so much we did not ask for them to fix it, which I assume they would have. At one point, the toilet simply did not flush but kicked into action about 15 minutes later. All of these things I imagine are indicative of older plumbing. Again, everything was functional, but definitely not luxurious. One thing that bugged me about the rooms are that there are no drawers anywhere. There is a closet space where you can hide your suitcase but we were there for three days and it is my personal preference to kind of move in when I stay anywhere more than a day or two. Lastly, one morning we woke up and headed out around 8 or 9am, we returned to the room around 1 and no one had been up to clean the room. We stayed in the room for a few hours and then, upon leaving, my husband asked the front desk for "turndown service". He misspoke as they don't do turndown service, but when we returned later that night, we still had not received any maid service.
We were not clear in asking for the hotel to fix some of the problems we ran into, so I cannot dock them too much for these things as they were not given a chance to make them better. Nonetheless, it would have been nice if they hadn't been problems to begin with.
As for location, the hotel is about a five minute walk from Union Square which is the hub for a lot of transportation options and the beginning of a long shopping stretch. Having stayed closer to Union Square before, the street noise at Hotel Adagio was much less and the rooms much quieter. 
All in all, this is a nice base for exploring the city. Breakfast is available for a reasonable price although there is also a cute diner across the street. There are several computers available for use, although there is a fee. The bar area is a nice little place to enjoy happy hour. The rooms include a comfortable bed and the basics. The room we were in was no frills and its age crept through, but it was quiet and the beds were comfortable.

title: “Ok overall but flimsy doors!”
text:
Recently stayed in a junior suite room for 2 nights. The front desk person said I'd been "upgraded" based on my gold SWP to a junior suite. Too bad that it was already the room type that I had reserved...some upgrade!!
Room was spacious but "heavenly" bathroom was the same size as the closet. Hardly any room to move. Worst thing about the stay was the flimsy pine doors. You could hear every other door being opened and closed throughout the long halls. This was particularly annoying during evening turndown services when you could hear a loud bang every two minutes. You can even hear the phone ring (loudly) from the room next door and the draft under the door is also pretty impressive (no A/C needed). 
Location is great, connected to two nice malls with plenty of shops and withing 2 blocks of Newbury St. Service was average. The bar was very nice. Didn't have time to check out the fitness facility. Overall a nice conference type hotel. Could definitely use a renovation.

title: “This Place Is a Joke!!!”
text: Anyone who simply wants a place to sleep, LOOK SOMEWHERE ELSE!!!! The hotel staff was more than rude, i would even say insulting. Very unhelpful!!!! After calling the morning before arrival, they had cancelled our reservation because the orbitz card declined. After speaking with Orbitz, "the hotel is not supposed to charge the card until after check-out because the account is not opened until check-in". They told us the hotel knew this and shoudl reinstate our reservation. After speaking between orbitz and the hotel for 2 HOURS (mind you we had a six hour drive to get there, and had a 6:30 game to catch), they gave us a new reservation number and said we were set. We get there with only an hour to spare because of the hold up in the morning, and the night staff that is now on has no idea what we are talking about. We give them the names of the managers we had spoken to and told them to call them, they wouldn't!!!! They told us to call orbitz back. Orbitz RE-SENT the fax they sent that morning so we could get into the room. Once getting into the room, it smelled, bed was terribly uncofortable, air conditioner was loud and sounded broken, room service wouldn't bring us a fork. The room and the hotel were a must NEVER SEE!!!! after returning home and trying to find answers, we were sent in circles between the hotel and the corporate headquarters; the end result being NOTHING!!! NOT EVEN A SINCERE APOLOGY!!!! be warned, this place is AWFUL!!! although close to the park, i would have rather stayed an hour away and drove the extra...especially seeing as the hotel for one night cost $195.00. We still have not heard back from the managers and it has now been three days...if your looking for even minimally good service, you WILL NOT FIND IT HERE!!!

title: “Poor Hotel, just Banking on it's Lobby”
text:
The only good thing about this hotel is it's public spaces- like it's lobby- but who cares about that when you are actually STAYING in the hotel? It's better to visit for a drink rather than to stay- there are much better places in new york than here. 
OK so to start, my husband and I were put up here for business and let me tell you that we would never stay here again no matter what. We are originally from New York so we knew to expect the beautiful lobby, but we didn't expect how disparate the match would be from the room to the public area. 
First, we had to bring up our own bags up a full flight of stairs as there was no doorman or bell boy available to help or even direct us to the elevator. Next we had to wait on a line that was literally 45 minutes long just to check in-no exaggeration. Once we got to the front of the line we were told they gave away our room. We had no room. How does a hotel do this? They said that people were checking out this evening and we could probably get one of their rooms at 10 that night. Wow, how generous- they didn't even offer us anything free to assuage us for our trouble.
So we finally do get our room that night after we get back from work and when I got up to where we'd be staying and i thought it was a joke- it looked like a converted closet and we couldn't even find the bathroom because the main door blocks it completely when it is open. The marketing term "cozy queen" was really a disingenuous name. To describe it more accurately you should think of Harry Potter's broom closet- that's about how big the room was. We wouldn't have been able to fit normal luggage in it. Thank goodness we only had carry-ons. To top it off the bathroom was GROSS with old crusty tile. It also was so small that my husband couldn't even stand up in the shower. The room smelled moldy and had a view of a brick wall. 
To make matters worse the staff was overworked and overwhelmed. They were rude because they were obviously understaffed and had to deal with hordes of disappointed people. To tell you the truth, I felt badly for them. The fault and problem of this hotel seems to lie with the management as all the staff i spoke to begged me to fill out a comment card to help them perhaps get more staff and make their lives easier. 
Anyway, long story short, please don't stay here even though it's location seems appealing. New York is an awesome city with hundreds of hotels better than this one.

title: “Good value, great location”
text: We picked this hotel based on the positive reviews and good price. The hotel met our expectations: very clean, spotless bathroom, great location, nice staff. I definitively recommend it.

title: “A nice place to stay, but rooms could have been cleaner and the renovations were not that great.”
text:
The staff was so nice and friendly at this Hampton Inn. As a matter a fact, right as we were checking out there was a meeting going on with all the employees in the breakfast room. The manager seemed very encouraging to the staff and the staff seemed very receptive to the manager. However, the renovations going on were not disruptive but did not seem to be that substantial. The room we stayed in was obviously just painted because it smelled like paint, other than the paint, there did not seem to be any other renovations. (perhaps they were not done yet?) 
The bathroom could have been a little cleaner; there were hairs on the bathroom floor that did not belong to me or my wife, other than that, the cleanliness of the room was fine. The air conditioner was old and would constantly start and stop to maintain room temperature which was mildly annoying. Location is fantastic in regards to access to the Downtown/ Riverwalk area.

title: “Beautiful hotel, bungling management...”
text:
I just returned from a stay at the Joule and found the place itself to be pretty damned nice. The restaurant (Charlie Palmer's), while not particulary innovative or unusual, was damn well perfect. I have written about food professionally and I can say without hesitation that this is a kitchen in sync.
The rooms are exceedingly well appointed, with the bathroom/shower/dressing area almost bigger than the living quarters.
Alas there my compliments come to an end
The management, front desk situation is simply abysmal.We had two rooms booked under a "Cash & Points" award for day one of a 3 nite stay, with the remaining two booked as usual. To this day, after multiple conversations and emails, they never have managed to reconcile our folio. In our last conversation, out of frustration, one of the managament team responded by crediting our card for a 1 night rack rate and asking "will this be okay?" In my mind, this is essentially an admission that they have no idea what is going on there. I have travelled over 300 nites in the past several years--mostly Starwood--and I have never EVER experienced a front desk experience like this. As my colleague quipped, "It's like something out of a wacky Peter Sellars movie" Oh yeah, and twice they forgot our wakeup calls. Whatever.
Likewise the hotel is in downtown Dallas. This is not a problem if you happen to need to be in downtown Dallas, but if I were going to stay in a hotel of this caliber, I would prefer it to be in a more aspirational setting. Put another way, I needed to be in Dallas for work so I was (reasonably) happy to get to stay there. And (bungling management excepted) I would love to take my wife there for a weekend...except I wouldnt want to waste a weekend in downtown dallas...Geez I guess that sounds snobby..

title: “Hilton Baltimore is outstanding!”
text: As a Hilton Diamond member I visit many Hilton properties each year. This is the one of the better properties Hilton offers. It is located right next door to Camden Yards and about six blocks from the Inner Harbor which is an easy walk. The hotel itself is outstanding and seems very new. The front desk staff was quick to check me in (early too - about 2pm) and I was on my way to the room. It was a standard room, but had a nice HD flat screen TV, updated decor and I had a great view of the ballpark. If you ever get a chance to visit here while a game is going on you could grab a 6-pack and watch the entire game from your room. The Inner Harbor is just about six blocks and offers TONS of restaurants and shops and is hoppin' during the summer. Overall this was a great stay and I would definitely return to this property when I come back to Baltimore. Not to mention I got a great rate ($143) since the Orioles weren't in town.

title: “Excellent Hyatt”
text:
I stayed at the Hyatt Regency Chicago for 5 nights in May 2008 while attending a conference. I had a room on the 5th floor overlooking the hotel atrium, facing E. Wacker. The room included a sofa and a comfortable chair as well as a desk chair. The bed was comfortable. Each room has a plasma TV (~42"). Each room has an iPod dock. The room was a very nice size, as was the bathroom. 
The hotel is in a very good location; within walking distance to shopping, museums, and restaurants.
I tend to favor Hyatts, and overall, I was very pleased with my stay.

title: “Our renovation story”
text:
So bad it's laughable. We reserved months ago but talked to the hotel a few times after that including the day before. Nothing was said about renovation.
On arrival we were surprised to find a tarp over what was probably the front door, construction noise you could hear on the street, a makeshift counter, no lobby, no restaurant, no bar -- just plenty of workmen. 
We were assured the work stopped at 6 daily. (Turned out to be untrue.) We were tired so we gave it a try.
Our room: When we came back from dinner, 3 tries with various room keys would not open the door. The night man could not open the door. Only when a master key was produced by another man could we enter. We were told "If you ever want to get into the room, just come down and have a staff person return with you." The room was cold, so we tried the heat. No heat! Up came the night man with a tiny heater.
I could go on about no working tv, half the lamps did not work, no ability to use our own electronics, one working elevator usually used by hotel maids and workmen... but you get the idea i think.

title: “Location, location, location!”
text:
We stayed at the Inn at the Opera as part of a holiday (but needing to work while there) in San Francisco, primarily to visit the opera so location was an important factor in our choice and, on reflection, is the hotel’s main asset.
As other reviewers have stated, staff were friendly and helpful.
We had a ballet room and, like others, found the furniture and layout unsuitable for business use. However, we were moved the following day to another ballet room with a desk and a chair so, if you need these items it would be worth saying so when booking. There is some traffic and other guest noise but we did not find it unacceptable.
Our room was on the seventh floor so lift access was necessary. The lift is small, only accepting four guests at a time, and the wait for it, though never unacceptably long, could be tiresome at times.
The room we stayed in was a little on the small and dark side but did have the benefit of a fridge, micro wave, coffee maker and sink. Wardrobe facilities (I was told that this is closet in American!) were entirely inadequate for any but a weekend stay. As we were staying for nine days this was an important matter. There is no air conditioning.
There was a large flat screen TV with sufficient channels to maintain our interest and an iPod dock and DVD player. WiFi access is free and the speed, though not lightening, is acceptable for business use, however, network contact failed on a regular basis. Fixing this was simple enough, just a matter of logging on again, but it was irritating as were the odd connection delays. There were sufficient points to allow us charge our phones, iPad, Kindle etc. An ironing board and iron are provided. Everything was clean and well serviced, with the odd, minor occasional omission.
The small bathroom was functional enough. The shower was adequate but, I suspect, not entirely working to specification and I would have thought that renovation will soon be needed. The sink was very slightly chipped.
The breakfast buffet was acceptable. However, in our nine day stay, the lack of variety became a little boring. Service was reasonable enough though it seemed that staffing levels were not sufficient to cope easily with a full room. Restaurant and bar hours (5 p.m. – 9 p.m.) seemed rather restrictive. As an Englishman, I may not understand the American way of tipping, but I felt that the pad left on every table at breakfast for guests to add a tip on a daily basis was, well, unsubtle!
We ate once in the Ovation restaurant. Prices were high for the location, about $130 – 150 for two people taking two courses with a glass of wine each including tax and 15% tip. European visitors would need to brace themselves for the shock of the cost of $10 for an admittedly generous glass of house red. Food quality was about acceptable at the price but portions were small by American standards.
At the room rate we paid, and as Opera goers we were supposedly receiving a discount, I would have said that the hotel was a little on the expensive side for what we received but I have no knowledge of San Francisco rates generally.
I would have said 3.5 stars but Tripadvisor don't provide the option!

title: “disappointed”
text: I was thoroughly disappointed in the condition and design of both the hotel and the room for the amount of money it cost to stay. Although everything was clean, it was definitely a motel, not a hotel. Parking was a nightmare and all night we listened to kids running up and down the exterior walkways and car alarms going off and on. Again, the room itslef was clean, but the facility gave an overall low class feeling.

title: “Clean, decent - you are paying for location”
text: Overall a clean and decently run place (although the credit card machine was down when we arrived so the front desk staff wanted me to shell out $140 in cash...ummm...no.) Pool was very nice. Rooms are small - double beds, not queen - but very clean and comfortable. Road noise not horrible. Location is in the center of everything, so if that is what you need, this is really a decent place to stay.

title: “Ok room for the money.....”
text: Small hotel in Wall street area about a block from South St. Seaport. Only 4 rooms per floor ...VERY small but adequate for a night's sleep.... TV remote didn't work and desk never brought new one. Ventilator VERY loud when it cycled at night so I shut it off. Housekeeping made TONS of noise early in the morning out in the hall. Glad it was only one night as a place to crash after a show.

title: “Decent hotel - great location, but the rooms were noisy from the nearby freeway”
text: The hotel was nice and the service was good, but if you had a room on the freeway side it was a bit noisy. The hotel was in walking distance to pikes place and shopping. Great location. Also great views of the city from the higher floors.

title: “Nice hotel -- but cash grabs spoil experience”
text: All the basic amenities that you would expect -- but really turned off by the little attempts to extort extra money from guests. In this day and age I expect wireless internet as a basic service. Most 2 star hotels offer free wireless. So it is a little upsetting to have to pay $12.00 a night just to get a hardwire internet connection. Both I and my wife had our laptops and only 1 of us could use at a time. What is the deal with expensive hotels -- why do they think its ok to charge extra for sub-par internet access? $50.00 per night parking was also very high -- even for Chicago. Would not stay here again until they updated their internet and made it a free service.

title: “Great Stay at the Le Meridien”
text:
My wife and I had a great stay at the Le Meridien. Our favorite part was the location. The hotel is located in the heart of the financial district with easy access from the airport by BART (a few blocks from the Embarcardero station). Although the tourist attractions are not right by the hotel, they are very easy to get to from this central location. Union Square is an easy walk as is Nob Hill and Fishermans Warf. There are also cable car stops a few blocks away. 
We were upgraded to a studio suite at check-in for no additional charge. The room was very nice with a large comfortable bed and extra seating area. The bathroom was nice and clean but nothing special.
Many coffee shops in the vicinity for coffee/breakfast in the morning and a few bars as well for an evening drink.
If you plan on driving, valet parking is very expensive (around $50/day). From my research, this seems to be common in this area.

title: “Fabulous Hotel!”
text: We took our son to Baltimore last weekend for his sixth birthday and chose the Four Seasons based on all the good reviews. I'm happy to say that it lived up to all the five-star ratings. We had a fantastic time! The service was outstanding, the room was beautiful (and spotless), the location was great, and the bed was incredibly comfortable (wish I had asked what kind of mattress it was). The staff wished my son a happy birthday when we checked in, gave him a cute little stuffed crab, and had cake pops waiting in our room. He was so thrilled he asked to come back to the Four Seasons every year for his birthday. We will definitely be back!

title: “Highly Recommend”
text: Great hotel! Everything is within walking distance and it's one block from the park. Hotel has restaurants, bars and a nightclub. Rooms are large and we even had 2 bathrooms in our room. For the price you can't beat it, it's a 4 star hotel. Will defintely stay again,

title: “Great Location and Wonderful Staff”
text:
Stayed here for 2 nights for Bronco/Steelers football game, Had a 1-bedroom suite and it was large enough for myself, son and 2 grandkids. Kitchen made it easy to fix a quick pizza, meal or snack. Rooms were very clean and had a flat screen TV in each room. 
Lobby area was very nice and was nicer than several other pricier hotels in downtown Denver, including the Denver Marriott, Hotel Monaco and Magnolia Hotel. An excellent and plentiful breakfast was included with the price each morning.
The entire hotel staff was friendly and very helpful on directions and things to do in Denver. The hotel is 2 blocks away from the 16th Street Mall and one can catch a free bus ride at the mall to the Union Station access to the Light Rail train to Mile High Stadium. Hotel location is within walking distance to any downtown restaurants or activities. 
This hotel offers much more value for the dollar than most other more expensive hotels and boutique hotels in downtown Denver.

title: “Our Dream 1st Anniversary!!! Totally romantic.”
text:
My husband and I stayed here to celebrate our first wedding anniversary. We got a great rate, the service is out of this world and the hotel is awesome!!!
The staff were amazing, they let us get a late checkout which was so relaxing because were were taking the train home so we weren't stuck checking our luggage or finding a place to hang out and wait. It was so relaxing. We stayed in the Magnificent Suite - which had a separate bedroom and was truly magnificent! There were huge windows in the bedroom with amazing views. 
The bathroom was tiny, but adorable and clean. The bath products (bliss) were amazing - an extra treat. 
The lobby is a really cute place to hang out and the subway is superclose - just like a block or two. We took it alot!

title: “Big room - big room in NYC!”
text:
Great location if you want to stay in times square. The rooms are spacious and great view. 
Suggest you want a room where you can see where the ball drops. Best view in town - compared to surrounding hotels.
The view restaurant - have drinks only. I recommend to visit. The restaurant has an amazing view of the city. It takes an hour.

title: “Love Every Minute”
text:
The Willard is full of history and elegance.
Everything from the service to the room was top notch.
It is pricey but beautiful.
There are many weddings and functions going on but the rooms are clean, spacious, and quiet.
Would return.

title: “Rude, arrogant staff. Extremely disappointed with the service for the price we paid for. Not worth it at all”
text:
Booked this hotel because we've had positive experience staying at other Sofitel hotels.
We arrived after a long 14-hour flight and weren't greeted by any friendly smiles. The bellboy didn't assist us with our luggage and check-in staff was rude and arrogant. I'm a platinum A-club member and yet the service I received and when asked about the possibility of an upgrade (that is something I'm entitled to with my membership), the response I got was "did you request for it?" Well, it is stated that upgrade is available upon request when checking-in. I didn't have to request prior to my arrival. Anyway, was asked to wait for about 2-3 hours before I could check-in at about 1pm.
Was assigned a city view room which was extremely noisy. So, requested for a room in the hills which was quieter but had to wait for another 1-2 hours. We told them we were happy to wait before receiving a call about 10minutes later that there was a standard room available. We took that eventhough it was a standard room because we were tired.
On the next day, when we went to the concierge to enquire about different ways to get to Anaheim (Disneyland) from the hotel, we were told to catch a taxi which would have cost approximately $120/way. We then asked if there were any trains that go there. The response we got from the concierge, in a rude and annoyed manner, was "you can waste your time!" Honestly, I think that was unreasonable and rude. He could have said "there is a train that goes out there but it will take much longer." We managed to find a cheaper and fairly convenient way to get to Anaheim after speaking to a representative at the tourist information centre. We took a taxi to a bus stop and it only cost us $40/way eventhough the journey was an hour longer. However, we managed to see the outskirts of LA.
Concierge also didn't know much about day tours and had to go around to look for brochures, etc. Come on, aren't queries about local attractions and day tours frequently asked questions? Please do not book day tours from the concierge. It is much more expensive than booking it directly from the tour operator at the Chinese Theatre. We were told by the tour operator that the hotel gets a cut off it!
When checking-out, the two reception staff were chatting as I walked up to them. They saw me walking up but continued chatting until about 5 seconds after I got to the desk. I was then given a bill that was $60 more than it should have been. I queried it and she checked the system before giving me the correct bill without apologising.
There weren't coffee/tea or even kettle in the bedroom either. It was only available upon request.
Nonetheless, despite the cost we paid (just a little over USD300/night), the beds were comfortable.
Personally, I wouldn't recommend this hotel to ANYONE!

title: “Very Nice Hotel”
text: Very nice hotel. Building was beautiful... renovations were wonderfully executed. Perfect location if you are looking for a centrally located hotel in San Diego. Service was also very good. The only reason I didn't give it a "5" rating is because there was quite a bit of street noise.

title: “Good hotel for business meeting.”
text: I attended a meeting at the Hilton/Polaris last week. I had a very comfortable, clean and modern room with free internet. My only suggestion is regarding the air conditioning in the rooms. I thought the system was very loud. But the staff at the hotel was friendly and helpful. The meeting rooms were nice, and the food served during the two day event was very good. The hotel is in a great location if you have time to explore while at the hotel. Incredible stores at the Polaris Mall and wonderful restaurants throughout the area will keep you entertained. I think that the hotel and the area would be a great place to spend a weekend. I would go back to stay again.

title: “Awesome in Every Way!”
text:
Basically the Hotel was Awesome in Every Way!
Even though it was raining the whole weekend, the hotel was still happening. The clubs were great. The service was great!!!! 
I am definitely going back soon!!!

title: “Great location”
text:
We had been to Jacksonville area several times-this was a great location-close to Mayo-clinic and the beaches. Easy access to I-95
The staff was gracious we had a relaxing sleep, room was clean and best of all we had friends who lived in the area who had no trouble finding our location.
Great hotel with a complimentary breakfast.

title: “Wonderful weekend stay at the Sofitel”
text:
My fiancee and I stayed at the Sofitel for a weekend getaway from NYC after enjoying our stay there last year. The hotel is central to everything in Philly.
Upon arrival, the front desk rep asked if we wanted to upgrade to a suite for an extra $40, which we were up for. The suite was spacious and very modern. The bed was very comfortable. The bathrooms were big with a bath tub and shower door. The bathrooms were the same size as in a regular room. 
The concierge was very helpful in giving us directions when we asked. It took the valet a long time to get our car, mainly because so many people were leaving on a Sunday afternoon. When he brought the car, he noted that my front left tire was low on air, which i appreciated, especially when the tire blew out on the way home, even though I filled it with more air after leaving the hotel.
My fiancee and I highly recommend the Sofitel.

title: “Keeps me coming back for more!”
text: My 6th time (I think) here over the past few years. Clean, neat, convenient, this property really stands out among hotels. A real pleasure to stay here.

title: “Have stayed there a few times”
text: I have stayed at the Hampton Inn in NYC a few times and would recommend it. It is a very clean hotel with, of course, the big huge breakfast selection that the Hampton Inn carries. It is very close to Penn Station (if you take the train to the city), Macy's, Empire State Building and only a few short blocks to Times Square (yes, you can walk it). The staff at the Front Desk are very helpful and were more than happy to store our bags while are room was being made up and also after check out. This is a very accomodating hotel. There is also an excellent restaurant right across the street, Brendan's Bar and Grill - excellent food! We were there during July 4th holiday and there was NO WAIT!! We couldn't believe our luck this is New York after all and there's a wait in every restaurant. Check them out you will not be disappointed.

title: “Worst Sheraton Ever!!!”
text: This hotel is terrible. There is no hot water at night, so you have to take a cold shower! The wifi is practically non-existent, the air conditioning is noisy, the bathroom is very small, and the rooms are old. I don't have high expectations, but this hotel is really bad. The only reason I stayed at this hotel is because I'm trying to get to platinum in SPG. I truly do not recommend this hotel to people who have high expectations.

title: “Fabulous Experience”
text: From the moment we arrived and walked through the door, I knew we had made the right choice in booking rooms at the Staybridge Suites near Times Square. To be a little more specific, we thought the breakfast was varied, tasty, and plentiful. We even enjoyed the view of the bamboo fence from the huge windows and the music of Christmas carols wafting through the air. The staff, especially Sunny, was helpful, knowledgeable, and courteous. The concierge helped us put together the perfect tour package, and everyone we asked was eager to give us directions…clear ones. We couldn’t help but notice that the hotel next door had a bus to take people to and from the airport, and I’m hoping that by the time I get back to Manhattan again, the Staybridge will too.

title: “Hotel Newton: Good bargain, good service”
text:
I got this place for 4 nights, about $104/nt, tax not included. I did quite a bit of research before reserving this place, and it was the cheapest place I could find that still met our criteria (clean, good reviews, good location). It is located on the Upper West Side of the city, just a block from the 96th St subway stop. So, while it is a ways from many of the attractions we wanted to see, having a subway stop so close made that irrelevant. We were easily able to run the few blocks to Central Park and do our morning run too. 
I wasn't bowled over with the friendliness of the staff at any time, but they weren't unfriendly. I did really appreciate one act of service. The last day of our trip, our flight home didn't leave till 8:30 PM, and we wanted to spend the day in the city without our luggage (check out was 12 noon). The guy at the desk immediately volunteered to keep our luggage in their luggage room, no problem, no charges. There was a $5/day charge to access the Internet. There was also an Internet cafe a few doors down that may have been cheaper, but we didn't use it. Also in the lobby they had two computers and a printer that anyone could use for a small fee ($1 for 5 min., and so on). 
The restaurant right next door was decent for breakfast, but there are also some great bagel places just a few blocks off. Starbucks was across the street. 
Our room was always clean and stocked with bathroom supplies. We had our own bathroom, but there were cheaper rooms available with shared baths. We faced an alley, so no view, but it was sooo quiet, which I loved, and the air conditioner unit was a great constant white noise (yes, I am a picky sleeper). 
My only complaint: there is only one elevator, for the housekeepers and guests. If you come back during the day to get something or to rest, plan to either spend a long while waiting for it, or take the stairs. Now, we are runners, so normally we do take the stairs, but we were on the 8th floor, and I was a little under the weather, so I was avoiding the stairs. The room was very small, but we are used to that from traveling through Europe. The decor was what you would expect from a budget hotel, but we didn't really care. It was comfortable enough.
All in all, I would definitely recommend staying here. It was just right for us, and I hope we can stay here again on our next visit to NYC.

title: “great time..”
text: we stayed here for a stars game and thought it was great.. the rooms were big and comfortable.. enjoyed a few drinks at the lounge bar.. really liked that when we went outside and were asking if there was a shuttle or should we call a cab to take us to the game, there was a limo driver with suburban right there handy.. he took us, then gave us his card.. came quickly when we called after the game- so easy!!

title: “You other reviewers are spoiled!”
text:
To start, THIS IS A DELIGHTFUL HOTEL. Before staying at this venue, I reviewed comments here on TripAdvisor for advice and was quite apphrensive about staying here. Still, because of work, the location was convenient to me and I decided to "take my chances."
Not only did I immensely enjoy The Orlando, I can say I had a better stay than fancier hotels up La Cienega (Hyatt West Hollywood, The Grafton). Without question, other reviewers of this hotel deserve to go spend $500+ a night at The Mondrian or the Beverly Hilton. The expectations for this (admittedly) aging facility are totally over the top, considering its location near what is the cultural center of L.A.
The staff was attentive, friendly and kind. The room was spacious, tastefully decorated and QUIET (granted, I wasn't on the Third Street side). The beds and sheets were great. Breakfast, considering it was FREE for the room deal, was a full breakfast and it was way beyond my expectations. And yes, the bathroom wasn't perfect but the shower was comfortable, not the "small nozzle" of water that someone else commented on. Best of all, the neighborhood was a lot of fun and eclectic, much more entertaining than staying on the Sunset Strip (and better restaurants too!).
No question this place isn't for everyone. It's a boutique on an aging property, but to me that's part of the fun of a boutique and they've done a great job for what they have. The location is excellent, and I would stay here again. The special people have many other choices nearby and the budget crowd can stay in downtown LA, but for my money it was the perfect choice.

title: “Sooooo comfortable”
text:
I loved the Doubletree. Just the bed alone was worth it! I don't know what it was but the bed afforded me the best sleep ever! I had six pillows....unreal luxory.
We got a junior suite...Since I was traveling with a male friend and since we wanted our privacy he took the "living room area" and I took the bedroom. We both had our own TV's and it worked out wonderfully. The Doubletree had a couple of really good restaurants on site. We ate breakfast at "The Cafe" and dinner at night upstairs in the Skydome. We were there during the Cherry Festival so was able to watch the fireworks over DC (one of those pinch me moments" and have dinner and drinks at the same time. Nothing to complain about.

title: “Great location.”
text:
Pros: Great location. 
Cons: Not worth the price you pay, really small rooms, and average service.

title: “Location, Location Location”
text:
PROS:
1) Big rooms
2) Awesome decor
3) Near Magnificent 
4) Subway stop close
5) Food options
6) Great staff
7) Great price
9) The views
CONS:
1) MINI BAR move ment... OMG!! You will be charged!
2) Parking cost a lot, but 1/2 price parking is very close
3) Elevators downstairs dont ding loud, so you could miss your elevator 
OVERALL:
Great hotel and I would stay again. The hotel is decorated up like true rock style. It is not overly flashy.. just classy. The rooms are spacious. Each floor is setup to be a theme. Any room above the 7th floor has a view. Walking distance to the Navy Pier and shops on Michigan Ave. House of Blues is near by. The Loop subway is 1.5 blocks away. The elevators on the ground floor, do signal they arrived, but if you are distracted at all in the lobby area, the music they have pumped in tends to block out the ding of the elevator. ( Ok.. Yes this is weak ding .. no pun intended ). I didnt drive, but the hotel does charge like ~$50 a day to park, but ~$27 a block a way. Although the real question is .. Car in downtown Chicago?? Really.. but if you do have one.. it is pricey to park. I guess the NEW fad in hotels is the mini bar movement sensors. Just remember.. if you have left overs that need to be keep cool.. just toss them because the hotel mini bar IS NOT for you.. it is a $$ making center for the hotel. DO NOT MOVE anything mini bar or you will be charged!!! Do they have a sign.. yes BUT the notice is in small print & if your are buzzed from a night out and want to put a slice of pizza or a soda from the street in the frig to keep cool... FORGET IT..
Beyond the mini bar incident, the hotel is great place to stay in Chicago.

title: “Quiet Room”
text: The room was definitely clean. Everything looked worn though. The shower was not that great...not much water pressure. The room did have a Herman Miller office chair which was nice. The best part of my stay was that it was quiet in my room so I slept well. I stayed in room 421. The restuaurant is great. We ate dinner and breakfast there. I was expecting alot more for a Wyndham though. It was okay but this is a Wyndham that we are talking about.

title: “Don't expect the Ritz, but it is cheap, clean, safe and convenient.”
text:
We arrived about 9am after 20hrs of flying and were expecting to at best check our bags and wander the streets until 2pm. 
When we arrived the guy on the front desk (shaved head, mentioned in a couple of other reviews here) greeted us with genuine enthusiasm and found a room for us to go right up to. 
Yes the rooms are basic and older, but they are clean and the staff were attentive. Free wifi (ask the staff for the password), kitchen and laundry are available. Very convenient to major buses, the BART & trolleys as well (which is important when you've walked up one too many hills). 
Highly recommended for anyone travelling on a budget. 
Basically it's unbeatable at the price.

title: “What a great Hotel and Location!”
text: The warwick was a smaller downtown area hotel that is not far from the Pike's Market and TONS of great restaurants within short walking distance. One of the best restaurants was in the lobby of the Hotel itself! Great drinks and ambiance. Free Parking received with our booking. What a terrific find! I will definitely stay here again when in Seattle.

title: “Great Stay”
text: Nice boutique hotel just steps from Times Square. Stayed four nights in mid-September and it couldn't have been better. Room was a bit small but very clean. Staff very friendly, helpful and eager to please. The breakfast and nightly wine & cheese was a nice touch. Will be back again !

title: “Ramada MESSED UP again - the usual with them”
text:
Ramada - what can I say. Seems like they're ALWAYS finding new ways to screw things up. I booked this hotel through Hotwire and cringed when I saw it was a Ramada. I just KNEW that something would go wrong. And as usual Ramada found a new way to disappoint. Our flight was delayed getting us to our room around 11 pm instead of 11 am as planned. We were told that the hotel was overbooked so we'd have to fend for ourselves and find another hotel room on Fri nite in LA. good luck to us after 22 hours with no sleep. Our room was PREPAID!! But that didn't matter because they resold it anyways! I guess if we couldn't/didn't show they'd be getting double paid for rooms that were not even there. Unbelievable! The next day as we checked in I explained all of the above to the manager and asked him for some LITTLE form of compensation (like the airline did the day before) for their complete disregard for our plight the nite before such as a room upgrade to make up and we'd be happy once again. He seemed to agree but then proceeded to assign us our standard room. There is just something about Ramada's culture that is down right offensive. I hope to NEVER have to stay at a Ramada EVER again.
Hotwire might also be losing some business if this type of treatment continues.

title: “Great quality at an affordable price”
text:
Was sending My wife home to Germany had to wait for the flight. So we picked this Super 8. We had a great night good sleep and the complimentary breakfast was good.
The desk manager Roshan Patel was very helpful and got us maps and info. to local stores for last minute travel items my wife needed. He went far and above the norm I think.

title: “Good Business Hotel”
text: Stayed here for the breast cancer conference in December. It had everything I needed as a business traveler - good desk, plenty of light, comfortable bed, nice bathroom. Would have been even better if there were easier access to electrical outlets from the desk. I had a nice view. It was in a perfect location, allowing me to get out for some wonderful walks (though I rarely have much time) and a nice meal. The concierge was very helpful on several occasions. The coffee shop only had day-old papers on Saturday morning, however.

title: “Good place if you're going to Eye Clinic”
text: We stayed here because my husband was having Eye Surgery at the Eye Clinic a block away & needed to go back the next day as well. Stayed in the motel instead of driving 40 miles. We had a king suite which does have a separate room with a door. Had refrigerator, microwave, and free wifi. For security, the motel key is needed to get in the entrance doors even during the day except the main entrance. The couch & chairs were all hard and we didn't find the bed comfortable either. The area was quiet in the motel/room. We didn't try the pool (inside) but the area looked nice. There are chairs/tables to sit outside in the middle court area. In the lobby area there are computers/printers you can use. They have a Bistro cafe open in the morning & evening -- more of grab & go type place but there are tables you can sit to eat to talk with friends (I think the set up is more in hopes you sit and drink alcohol a lot). We did order from the Bistro both nights. First night, we sat down to eat and the 2nd night we got it to take back to the room. We were pleasantly surprised that the food (turkey BLT & French dip sandwiches) were warm and good. The women working the Bistro were friendly and nice. They also serve Starbucks coffee and can get a latte but no drinks that require a blender. We had some issues with the A/C in the room so just turned it off for awhile. There really aren't any places close by to eat (such as few blocks) which is why we ate at the motel. McDonalds is on the other side of 465 (maybe mile or so) which I drove over to at lunch to bring back --- very hectic place even at 1:45 PM. We would only consider staying there again if/when my husband needs surgery on his other eye. Thought the rooms were pricey -- even if we had gotten a regular room which maybe because of it being located in Carmel (more of a pricey area).

title: “Functional on a Budget”
text:
This hotel is perfect for those on a budget needing to stay in Old Town. I paid half the price of the hotel next door and was within walking distance of the hotel where my conference was being held. As a female traveling alone, I felt very safe walking around the neighborhood at night. 
Two complaints: The room was fine although it still smelled like smoke and it was a nonsmoking room; when I told the cashier (because I had to sign a waiver saying I'd pay $150 if I smoked in the room) she looked at me annoyingly and shrugged. 
Overall, I had a pleasant experience.

title: “Excellent service, location”
text: My wife and I stayed at this hotel this past weekend to celebrate my wife's birthday. We could not have been more pleased with the service, location, as well as the room and its view. All the staff we encountered, from doorman to desk lady who checked us in, to check out, was professional and courteous. Our room had a fantastic view of Navy Pier and looked as if recently updated. From this location we walked to Michgan Avenue, restaurants, and stores. Our room was next to the elevator and there was a slight hum at times, but it was not a hindrance, especially with the special rates that come available from time to time and which we took advantage of. We would go there again.

title: “beautiful grounds, but rooms need some freshening up”
text: just arrived today, as we drove through the resort, we noted how beautiful and serene the environment was. truly a paradise. we felt as though we were in hawaii/maui. check in was a breeze, staff was friendly. however, when we entered our room, a strange odour permeated the room (smelled like a combination of detergent and vomitted baby's milk}. wall paint had chipped off, lower portion of the front door had paint chipped off, bathroom walls and door paint were terribly scuffed. in short - rooms needed a coat of fresh paint. love the hard wood floors and spacious bathroom. so, management, when you have the time and money, please repaint/upgrade the facilities, then it will truly be a paradise in the city.

title: “Our New Favorite hotel”
text: We stayed at Le Meridien in London in June 2010 and had a wonderful experience there, so when I saw that there was one in Philadelphia, we gave it a try. We are very happy we did. We visit Philly frequently and typically stay at the Westin or Sheraton, which are fine hotels, but Le Meridien is just fun. It is very clean,extremely quiet, modern and close to downtown. In fact our room looked right at city hall with William Penn on top! The facility itself is contemporary with helpful staff, valet parking, including a restaurant (although we didn't eat there) and a wine room and bar. Beautiful fireplace in the lobby with plenty of comfortable chairs to sit in. There is an extra charge for internet access (which we didn't need with our smartphones) but a great hotel.

title: “Beautiful property, room alittle small”
text:
Stayed for one night in a king room. Our room was on the top floor overlooking Broadway, but it was very quiet. The walls have the most beautiful molding. While the room was lovely, there was not much space to move around. The bathroom had a beautiful shower with a great shower head, but there was no tub. The towels were a not as plush as I would had hoped for in a luxury property.
This hotel was beautiful and I would stay here again, but I will bring a sleeping mask. There is alot of light that comes in the room in the night. It would have been perfect with blackout blinds though. 
The staff was excellent, best out there. They were so kind and polite and very helpful down to every little detail.
The location is in the Gaslamp just across from a mall. It is an easy walk down to the port to the fish restaurants, the Midway, cruise ships, and train station.

title: “would definately stay there again”
text: My family and I just spent the weekend there. We needed two rooms and the Marriott was able to give us connecting room. For some reasons other hotels find this to be a big issue. Anyway the rooms were very nice. The beds were awesome. Felt like you were sleeping on a cloud. The place was clean and the staff was very nice. The lobby has a nice lounge area which has a fireplace. It was nice to come in from the cold and walk in to a nice warm fireside. The location was perfect. There are 6 of us which made it hard to get one taxi. So we did a lot of walking. It was very easy access to the wharf . Overall a great place to stay.

title: “It was OK”
text:
Thouhg the hotel was good for its price but three things I want to point out:
No free breakfast
No free Internet: $10 a day ...the lobby is not free either as they advertised...
No free parking: $23 a day....

title: “What's happened?”
text:
Really disappointed with my second visit to the Hudson. I had previously stayed here in 2009 and found very little to fault. Yes, the rooms were small - but for me, they were perfectly formed. Add to this some great styling, good service and perfect location I was eager to return.
Unfortunately, upon my return visit last week (from 6 July) I found my stay to be rather less impressive. After a long (and unapologetic) wait to check in, I found my 'Standard Queen' room to verging on the 'tatty' side. First things first; the door lock involved much effort to open/close and was clearly in need of repair. The bathroom was also in a decidedly poor shape with flaking paint, mould on the window and the toilet roll holder falling off the wall.
Inside the main bedroom, the tattyness continued, with a large piece of the wooden wall panelling missing from beside the air conditioning unit. The iPod dock beside the bed was also not working and the TV apparently not working either.
My room was right next to the roof terrace bar, which is a lovely spot. Less lovely were the hotel staff who kept rudely telling me the bar was closed when I was merely trying to get back to my room. Also, if the bar wants to charge $15 for a cocktail, at least employ some decent barmen who know how to mix them.
All in all, a rather noticeable dip in quality from this once fine hotel.
I know the hotel is in the process of being renovated, and the floor (15) that I was on hadn't been done yet - but it seems unfair to charge customers for a room that is clearly in need of said renovation.
There is/was much to still recommend about the Hudson, but it certainly seems to be trading on former glories at the moment. There are far better hotels in Manhattan (for the same or less) offering a far higher standard of accomodation.
Very disappointing.

title: “Good hotel, would stay again.”
text: Good hotel, the room was small but fine for two people. The bed was really great, loved it. The breakfast was delicious and the service was excellent. Two things I didn't like, our room was overlooking the train tracks and those things woke us up at 8 AM every morning with it's lovely "choo choos" and the hotel only has one (really slow) elevator, a 12 story (13 including the lobby) building really needs two elevators, we stayed on the 8th floor so we had to use the elevator a lot. All in all a good stay and I would recommend this hotel to friends.

title: “Great renovations at the Arizona Biltmore”
text: Just returned from my annual visit to the Arizona Biltmore (annual conference for work). The first night I was in a room in the main building which was quite large and beautiful but the echoes from outside made it nearly unbearable to sleep before midnight or after 4 am when they were moving furniture around outside. So they moved me to the Ocatilla Wing. Great renovations to those rooms. The bathrooms in particular were very nice. The greatest improvement at the hotel was the wifi available in the rooms! It is always a beautiful place to stay with a great gym and spa. Just avoid getting a room on the 4th floor of the main building if you can.

title: “High class but not high service”
text: There are a lot of great reviews on here and I suppose if you have money and look the part then you recieve exellent service. My husband's parents planned to celebrate their anniversary with a brunch and spa services. As a surprise their children wanted to pre pay for that. My husband and his two younger brothers went in to arrange that and spent an hour being shuffled from one person to another who either didn't know what to do or were too rude to want to help them. Yes, they didn't look the part. They were in shorts and t-shirts. They didnt realize how fancy a place it is. The hotel doesn't know what the spa is doing, the spa doesn't know what the restaurant is doing, etc. No one could figure out who needed to do what or how to do it. On top of that, they felt as if the staff were looking down on them as if they didn't belong and at one point even a security guard questioned them. I have never been to the Brown Palace, and I've always wanted to go but after how my husband was treated today, I'm not sure I will. It shouldn't take an hour and being treated like dirt to get a simple gift certificate.

author.location: Los Barriles, Baja California Sur, Mexico

title: “Overall, it was great.”
text:
The service was very friendly and prompt, the rooms very nice and clean, and the valet very convenient. The location is just superb. A minute's walk and you are at the White House, and a few minutes later (maybe 10-15) you can be on the Mall.
Negatives? It was 100 deg. F in DC and the room never really got cool enough. I should have complained, but I thought that when the sun went down it would get cool. It didn't. If you have that problem, make sure to tell the front desk.
I will probably stay there again.

title: “ABOVE AND BEYOND/BEST OF THE BEST”
text: The Hotel Indigo, San Diego is awesome! In town for leadership training and this hotel "raised the bar" among the other ones in San Diego. Starting with Kelsey the Sales Manager/Derick the Director of Food and Beverage these are professionals who know the hospitality business. The attitude and friendliness of these two leaders was outstanding. Andrian and Matt took awesome pride during our banquets (always a smile and can do attitude), Michael was our breakfast host and was always one step ahead of our requests (great attitude and service) and our adult beverage servers Adrianna, William and David were always funny, friendly, helpful and very very professional. The hotel Indigo is years ahead of the other hotels in the area. The housekeeping staff were professional and very helpful. Also the valet and bell service was fast, courteous and like everyone else in this hotel "FRIENDLY AND PROFESSIONAL".

title: “Great Location, Excellent Staff”
text: Just got back from a quick trip to chicago to celebrate my sister's 40th birthday with friends. The Marriott Residence Inn was above our expectations. The room was appointed very nicely and extremely clean. The location of the hotel was perfect - would definitely recommend highly if you just want to walk to various trendy sections. Just a few blocks from Rush Street, walked back from Old town, Buck -- great great great location. The staff was very accomodating but I will mention that the girls who work breakfast really stood out -- they were so pleasant with a ready smile and always had nice thing to say to us. I wish I got names so management would know but I didn't. The one bedroom suite was very roomy, the efficiency kitchen appointed well - we thought we would us it but never had the chance. Definitely go the the Drake Hotel bar for a fun time, the bartenders at Knickerbockers next door were great, James Hotel fun, as well.

title: “Great place to stay when visiting New York City”
text: Just returned from our New York City vacation(9/21-9/26/10). My wife and I stayed at the Hilton Garden Inn Times Square. This hotel exceeded our expectations. Great location, staff and service. Theater, shopping, restaurants and the subway are all within a 1-5 minute walk. I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone traveling to NYC.

title: “Fabulous hotel - helpful, friendly staff”
text: My friend and I stayed at the Lafayette 4 to 18 July, whilst visiting my son who was on a placement in San Diego. I found the hotel on the internet and did had mixed views after booking due to some of the reviews. However, the hotel was a fantastic place to stay and such a sense of history. We stayed in room 519 at the poolside and it was spacious and well furnished and the housekeeper kept it spotlessly clean. The public areas of the main building were spacious with lovely seating areas. There was a PC in the lobby for public use and giant draughts and chess boards outside. The poolside restaurant served fabulous meals - we had breakfast there on a number of days and Adam was the perfect waiter and looked after us well. It was also great to be able to sit on the balcony and eat whilst overlooking the pool. The pool is magnificent and was designed by Johnnie Weismuller and I was able to swim 70 lengths in it each day, often early in the morning so the pool parties did not affect me. The parties finished by 6pm each day (usually held over the weekends) and didn't affect us as we went out most days. The hotel provided complimentary tea and coffee all day long (until 10pm in the evening) and iced water was available at the poolside. The hotel was in a great location although not too many tourist attractions close by; however, this did not detract from its appeal and it was easy to get to all the attractions in San Diego (we hired a car). The hotel staff were always friendly and helpful and I will definitely say there again when visiting San Diego.

title: “Hostile experience”
text:
Horrible Experience
We were visiting the city overnight and decided to stay at the mayflower for one night. The hotel is nice and the room well kept. 
The staffing however at least the night auditor Ellias Secko who was on duty on Saturday night was superbly rude, unprofessional and totally not in the line with such prestigious hotel.
Upon check in we presented our ID and card along with a form that was to be for a lower rate. WEthen checked in with no problem and went to bed.
We went upstairs and about 20mns later start, we start receiving calls from Ellias Secko, the night auditor who simply said the form is wrong and the price is going to be changed. He gave me 3 different prices without specifying what my rate will be. Considering the late hour time about 4 AM; we simply asked him to bill the card on file. 
We went to sleep and surprisingly received 4 more calls and we had to go downstairs to answer some questions???? The night auditor starts interrogating us???? Unbelievable.
I end up walking away and reiterated that he can charge any amount he likes and I need to get my two hours sleep before checking out at 7 AM.
I received a receipt under my door with the initial amount, and couple days later saw on my statement that the night auditor charged me about five times the initial amount.
This stay was horrible and we had 0 sleep. 
Any staff member who calls guests in their sleep at 5AM with no reason at such a late hour and start loud arguments in the lobby is simply unacceptable.

title: “Visiting my son”
text: Execellent facilitiies, wonderful staff, good cookies, great suite.

title: “Trendy and inviting hotel”
text:
Everything in this hotel says "Trendy" - it starts with the outside looks and goes through every part of the process you go through when checking in and out of the hotel.
The rooms are small, but have exactly what you need: the bed is electrically folded into a couch and can be used as either. The rooms are all "iOS-ready" - use the music of your iPhone to enjoy the time in the room.
Really like the hotel and would definitely stay there again.

title: “Greatly Pleased With My room”
text: I really enjoyed my stay. The rooms was clean, amazing, spacious and the decor was very modern and beautiful. I liked eating at Jason's Deli and Cold Stone Creamry which is just around the corner. I high recommend staying at this hotel.

title: “nice and clean, good rate”
text:
Very positive experience. Hotel is located in the center of SF so do expect some noise.
Rooms were clean and very nicely decorated. Staff pleasant and helpful. I would recommend it. Parking is just next door $25 overnight. Breakfast was the greatest disappointment and not worth $7.00 they charge.

title: “Great Location... That's About it!”
text: Maybe my expectations were wrong as very disappointment with selecting this Marriott as the hotel for my family vacation. Location is great, however everything else falls way short for a Marriott of this level. I'm an awards member and stay at Marriott a lot and have never written a bad review on any other properties. Service here is definitely lacking across all departments. Maybe it's the SD air but it's definitely obvious. Check in not good as reservation was wrong, had $60 credit per day but main restaurant closed and can't use at Roys or other Marriott's, hotel shows waterslide at pool, however it was shut down and looks like they don't use, rooms outdated (going under refurbishment) which is ok if good service or rooms clean (mold in bathroom, couple fixtures falling apart), Irish Restaurant service and food poor. If the service by staff was more friendly and accomodating I think I wouldn't be writing this review. Not a Marriott I would suggest staying, even if you are attending a convention. Try the Marriott Coronado (just across the water) or Gaslamp which is just down the street as you can still use the pool here.

title: “My Favorite Chicago Hotel”
text:
I travel to Chicago frequently for business, and we discovered the Raffaello back in June. Since then, I've been in Chicago about 8 times and stay there every time. 
ADVICE: Always book a King room. They're much bigger than the double rooms
The staff is friendly, the rooms are spacious and comfortable, and it's a perfect location. It's a 5-10 minute cab ride to our client's offices, right off the Magnificent Mile (though I never have time to go shopping) and a quick cab ride to any restaurant we ever choose to dine in. I'm surprised about the reviewer saying the bellman wasn't around, there's always 1-2 standing there when I get in. I've even been given comp upgrades to a suite, which is FANTASTIC!
No, they don't have room service but you can ask the front desk for a couple places that deliver to your room. They are Italian places, but have extensive menus (not just pizza) and the food is pretty good. In the morning, they will deliver breakfast to your room if you put the order on your door the night before.
all in all, I'd say stay there. It's a great hotel, great location, and great price. I've never paid more than $240 a night, and for this location and quality of hotel, that's a steal.

title: “W not so wonderful!”
text:
Very unhappy-Hotel Location, Valet Service, Lobby, Desk great!!! Elevator and Halls dark, so dark you can't even see the elevator buttons.Entering room, you think maybe you are in an IKEA store. Bathroom is dirty/Accumulated dust on every baseboard/rack/Shower Mildewed/No exhaust fan-and enclosure is such that you can see shadow of every movement of those occupying the bathroom!! No hooks in bathroom, shelves are dirty/rusty and you don't want to put your clothes on them. Room is also very dark..very little "good" lighting, if it had been raining I cant imagine how dark it would have been..maybe this is on purpose to not notice the rooms are not clean.
Room service tray left in hall of neighbor from 9PM Friday night until at least 11AM Saturday (when we left)-did not smell good.
My last stay at any "W".

title: “Very Good”
text: We stayed 3 nights end of May. We got a very large suite, with a full kitchen, outdoor patio, closet, and a safe. Location was very close to a lot of the action, but the hotel didn't get any street noise which was nice. The free breakfast was good. They have a computer and printer that the guests can use. Free underground parking. My only negative comment would be the room wasn't as clean as it could be, I saw some dust in a few corners. But overall I think this hotel is very good value.

title: “Very nice, but hard to get to by car”
text: Stayed at this hotel for the annual AP Conference. Drove down from Napa and to my frustration, several streets leading to the hotel were closed to cars due to construction. Location is excellent with Union Sq just a few blocks away. The room was ample and as in other Marriott hotels I have stayed at, immaculate. Be aware, if you park your vehicle at the hotel, prepare yourself to pay $58 a day for parking.

title: “Great hotel. Best breakfast ever!”
text:
I stayed here with 4 teens, three my own children and an exchange student that is staying with us (13, 15, 16, 17). We got a suite which when you walk in has a living room with a hid-a-bed sofa, comfy chair, and table with chairs and tv. My son slept on the hide-a-bed and he said it was comfortable but I noticed a lot of light coming in through the shutters from the hallway and a lot of noise from the hallway. Next was the bathroom which was fine. The rest of us girls stayed in then next room which had 2 double beds. The room had a sink and mirror outside the bathroom which saved the day with 3 teen girls and there is also a mim fridge, microwave, coffee pot, and sink which was awesome. I called down to get washcloths since only 2 were in the bathroom and with 5 people we needed more and housekeeping brought them in 5 minutes or less. Great service. 
The concierge, Latonya, was the bomb! We asked for a referral to a nearby restaurant that would suit all our tastes (one vegetarian, one who doesn't eat veggies and general pickiness). She referred us to the Grand Lux and she gave us her card and told us to tell them that she referred us. We got there and the wait was 1-1/2 hrs. Ugh! I gave them her card and they had us seated in 20 minutes! Thank you LaTonya! The food was delicious and everyone loved their meals.
The concierge from another night helped me figure out how to get the the Briar theatre to see Blue Man Group. She helped me figure how much it would cost to take the train and which line to take (Red Line) and all the other details. She was also so helpful and I"m sorry I ddin't catch her name.
Everyone that works here was awesome. Our exchange student doesn't speak English very well and while ordering her omelet at breakfast the person preparing the ingredients noticed she was struggling with what the ingredients were so he spoke to her in Spanish to help her. Thank you! She gets so confused by what some English words are and gets embarrassed and he made her comfortable and helped her get what she wanted. 
The breakfast, oh man, it is good. Prepared for you omelets (which are the best I've had in a very long time), biscuits and gravy, hashbrowns, bacon, sausage, yogurt, bagels, etc. The list goes on and on. The only thing I didn't like at breakfast was the pancakes. That may just be personal taste.
Great location also. The trolley to the Pier is on the same block. I loved staying here (even with 4 teenagers). There is a pool but we didn't take time to go to it. Too many other great things to do.

title: “Great Stay”
text:
We stayed at Hotel Lombardy for two nights June 30th and july 1st. 
We couldn't of asked for a better hotel. We stayed in a King room. It was my husband, myself and our two children (3 and2).
The staff at the hotel were wonderful and always very helpful!
Can't say enough about our stay... we will definitly return!

title: “Not very nice”
text: This hotel is in need of updating and mantainace. There are four elevators on the main floor, but ony two were working while I stayed. The room is dark and the wallpaper is peeling off the wall. The tile is the bathroom is cracked and broken around the tub faucet. The bathroom counters are old and ugly. The sleep number bed is broken and not able to be adjusted. The tv is a old CRT tv.

title: “Not the people you expect at a hilton”
text: The hotel has some nice pool areas because we were on the eve of 4th of july there were a lot of families bus also couples who were more party people. You have a main pool near your room and a water park. In the main pool it filled with beer drinking loud people. Not my cup of thea so I would avoid this hotel during holiday weekends. The rooms are spacious and beautiful. The water park has a long lazy river, sport pools and a general ppo but no area were you can really swim. Breakfastbuffet is avaible for $ 15 and the reception has a list of nereby restaurants avaible.

title: “Fantastic Boutique Hotel With A Friendly And Helpful Staff”
text:
The rooms were spacious which surprised me based on previous stays at other hotelss in Chicago. The rate was less than I've paid in other hotels in this city.
I loved the High Definition Television in the room.
Technical support helped me get logged in to the high speed internet connections within a couple of minutes.
The staff was very helpful with directions and recommendations for dining. They helped me print out a boarding pass in the business center at no charge.
The Bell Hop ran down a cabbie for me several times and helped with fare information.
I will be strongly recommending this hotel for business colleagues, friends and family.

title: “Excellent service, hospitality, and location!”
text: The rooms are clean, well maintained, and have an awesome pool in the middle. You really know you are on vacation with the palm trees and the tropical plants next to the pool. Breakfast is excellent.

title: “Ditto”
text: Gotta agree with the TripAdvisor User from DC. I also stayed at The Time during the April snowstorm. The staff could not have been nicer, even apologetic about the weather. However, the restaurant was closed for nearly two days and my suite was tiny. I have stayed in many other NYC hotels and their rooms were bigger than my suite. [The bathroom in a Waldorf suite was bigger.] For the price, there is better. The jacuzzi worked, it just takes a degree in engineering to figure out how to get it going. I do not think I would stay there again.

title: “Quite ok but small things can be improved”
text:
Hotel is nicely located, the price was modest and the room was quite ok but...
-the curtains were old and ugly
-the door is bad because it don't block any noise from the corridor, please add doorsteps at least
-toilet was installed too high (I am of middle height)
-free WiFi is a norm nowadays in most of the hotels I have been; I paid 16 dollars per day and I didn't work properly but constantly dropped me off
Please have a serious considerations with these and I may come back again one day!

title: “Top-flight Business Hotel”
text:
If a business hotel in Baltimore is what you want, consider this one. I stayed here as part of a convention and was really impressed. Staff was friendly. Check-in was smooth, with all that entails during a convention turnover. All functions ran well, smoothly and comfortably. Even the catered food at the events was done well!
The rooms were comfortable, spacious, and well-appointed--much nicer and more inviting than your sometimes-standard Marriott hotel rooms. Mine had plenty of working space and room to roam. I did not feel cramped. The hotel location was good for a visitor spending a few days: Overlooking the harbor, near a number of popular restaurants and nightspots, and near the Italian/warehouse dining district. If you like to walk the neighborhoods, jog, or see some sights, this hotel is a good starting point.
I would highly recommend this hotel if you are staying in Baltimore.

title: “What a relief!”
text:
I stayed at The Carlton last Thanksgiving when my daughter played at Carnegie Hall with her high school symphony orchestra - of course I'm bragging. :)
I researched hotels for weeks before choosing The Carlton. It seemed that every review I read complained about NYC hotels rooms being extremely small and/or having bed bugs. I was terrified. 
I was relieved when I finally saw the room. It was a comfortable size. I think that the room seemed larger than it actually was because good use was made of the space. Also, there were no bed bugs! The room was immaculate. The staff was friendly and helpful (especially the concierge).
I liked the location - it took about 10-15 minutes to walk from the hotel to Times Square. It was close enough to be convenient, but far enough away to be calm and quiet. 
I will definitely stay there when I return.

title: “Jumeirah Jolly good”
text: We spent 6 nights at the Jumeirah NYC at the end of August and had a great stay. We were upgraded to a Central Park suite for $569 per night so perhaps I am swayed in considering this a good choice of the top end New York hotels at the moment. The investment of the Jumeirah group is obvious as is their service quality and the location excellent.

title: “Decent Ramada”
text: Ramada inns in general are starting to get age on them and most show it. This one was showing some age as well, but for the value the rooms are big and the one I had was an extended stay room with kitchenette, sofa and chair and a flat screen wall mounted tv with and adjustable mount so the tv can be viewed from any angle in the room. Another plus if you are a harley lover was Barnett H-D is next door.

title: “Excellent!”
text: We spent several nights at various hotels in Texas -- Hampton Inn in Waco, TX, Omni in San Antonio, and the Inn on South Padre Island. The Comfort Inn in Fort Worth was by far the cleanest, friendliest, and most customer oriented hotel of them all!! Front desk service was superb! Topped all other hotels hands down!

title: “Stellar Service”
text:
If you are looking for a beautiful get away and amazing service, look no further than The Sanctuary Hotel. I have never come across a more accommodating and thoughtful hotel staff in all my years of traveling. I asked for an early check-in because I had plans in the afternoon, they easily made my check in a breeze. When confirming my reservation, the concierge Jimmy (who is simply fabulous) asked me the reason for my stay and I mentioned it was my birthday, when I arrived, the hotel staff signed a birthday card for me and gave me a box of mini cupcakes for my birthday. When I asked for a recommendation for a restaurant, Jimmy not only suggested a wonderful restaurant, but made the reservation for me. 
Every thing about the hotel is simply beautiful. From the lobby and seating area to the statues that line the hallway to the exceptionally comfortable rooms to the amazing rain shower. Not to mention that the City Bliss shampoo/conditioner/body wash/lotion smells positively divine. Sanctuary was an amazing experience for me and I would gladly stay there again.

title: “Pretty expensive - but not a bad hotel”
text:
Spent a couple of days here. Opted for the upgrade to a corner room and it was brilliant. I was here to take photo's of the aeroplanes coming in/out of LAX and the room was superb. It was located right opposite the end of the runway threshold meaning everything leaving on that runway taxied right past my window. Make sure you have a high floor room (I was on the 8th floor) for an unobstructed view.
Spent most of my time in the room witrh room service, so as not to miss many arrivals. A tad on the expensive side but better than sitting in a boring restaurant on your own staring into space or your ipad!

title: “Jax Ramada stay”
text: The room felt damp. The only way I could rid the room of the feeling was to keep the A/C on which was loud and made the room too cold. For a region like Jax it would be nice to have a dehumidifier. I didn't have this problem at the LaQuinta across the street the week prior. I do like your facility better.

title: “Keep coming back”
text:
This is probably my 4th stay at this property, as we come each summer for our Mary Kay Seminar. We've stayed at many other Dallas hotels. Lately, we keep coming back to the Fairmont because it is large enough, but not so massive as to be exhausting to traverse. We love that we can grab a quick breakfast at the Starbucks just off the lobby. Whenever there's been a problem, the staff has been quick to fix it for us, in good spirits. The pool-side food-delivery has been one of our favorites treats on the Terrace. I sleep great in this hotel's beds,compared to usually a tough adjustment first nights at other places.
Each visit, bellman Tony Bennett has been so very cheerful and eager to help. It's nice, on return trips, to know we will be greeted by that exuberant smile and the bounce in his step. When I had to wait inside for a shuttle, he kept an eye out to make sure to tell me when it arrived. When he had to help another guest, he asked another bellman to keep watch for me.
