I felt it was "extra mile" service. The concierge, John, also was very kind and helpful with any question we had.
I've also had dinner and breakfast in the restaurant and enjoyed delicious food with quick, personable service from all the staff: manager, host and waiters.

title: “Good location, for airport and city”
text:
We recently spent 4 nights at the Hilton Chicago O’Hare. Several years ago we were stranded in Chicago for a few days because of bad weather in Denver and found refuge at the Hilton. Since then we’ve been meaning to go back for another look at both the hotel and the city.
We arrived into Terminal 1 and walked to the Hilton; it was a bit of a trek with luggage in tow. With hindsight, even wheeled luggage can benefit from the use of a trolley when navigating between airport terminals. The lady at the Hilton Honors reception desk was welcoming, friendly and efficient and, although it was a couple of hours before official hotel check-in time, she found us a room straight away. I asked for a runway view, although in fact you can see the airport from both sides of the hotel. The hotel is a curved shape and the only difference is that the outside of the curve looks over the multi-storey car park and the inside looks over the terminal building; above certain floors all rooms can then see the airport and runways. We were on the 10th, top floor, inside curve, sort of between the 2 air traffic control towers, with a good view of the goings-on of the airport.
Given the shape of the hotel, the reception area is long and narrow with elevator banks at either end. There isn’t much open lobby space, just a few chairs near the entrances beyond the elevators and some on a mezzanine level above. The restaurants and bars are then further along again, beyond the elevator banks. There is a small gift shop in the lobby area which is open long hours; extremely high prices for basics such as soda but very handy.
The room seemed small, as airport hotel rooms tend to be, but it was comfortable and well appointed. The window was floor to ceiling, and the room a slightly odd shape because of the curved shape of the hotel. It had a king size bed with bedside cabinets either side. There was a (very heavy) recliner chair, small table and standard lamp towards the window. On the opposite wall was a fixed desk area with a large mirror above and an office type chair. Then a drawer unit on which was the large flatscreen TV. Next to that, a cabinet containing the minibar, with the coffee maker and a tray with the ice bucket and glasses on top. Then a wardrobe with full length sliding doors, opposite the bathroom. The bathroom was definitely small – as you opened the door, it barely avoided hitting the toilet. It had a bath with shower above against one wall and the counter top with sink on the other, with the toilet in the middle. Plenty of room on the counter top, and shelf below, but limited access to the lefthand side of it because of the toilet. The bed was very comfortable but the pillows very soft. The linens and other amenities were good quality; I didn’t recognise the brand of the toiletries but they were pleasant and there was a good selection of them.
The hotel is very handy for the railway station for access into Chicago city centre. It takes about 50 minutes by train and we paid $14.00 each for a 3-day CTA pass which we could use on all CTA trains and buses. It may be cheaper to pay for individual journeys but the pass is much handier than having to load money onto a transit card. We travelled in by train on all 3 days which some people would find to be a hassle, but we prefer to stay out of the city centre and travel in rather than actually staying in the centre.
We had planned to eat either in the city or at the hotel but then discovered that there’s a Longhorn Steakhouse out by another airport hotel so we visited there a few times, using the appropriate hotel shuttle to get there. In the same vicinity we saw an area with several other eating options (including Chili’s, Steak N Shake, Culver’s) together with Target and other stores, all within a 10-minute shuttle ride from the airport.
Although it is possible to walk to Terminals 1, 2 and 3 from the Hilton, Terminal 5 is further away and is reached by the airport train. With the amount of luggage we had, this would have been a problem. On our departure day we left our luggage with Bell Services while we went for lunch. When we returned, Bell Services took us and our luggage to Terminal 5 in the hotel shuttle bus and dropped us right outside our airline’s check-in area, which was much appreciated.
One big irritation at the hotel was wi-fi access. With an average rack rate of $299 per night before tax, it simply smacks of greed for Hilton to then charge for wi-fi access in the guest rooms (I believe it was $15.00 per 24 hours, not that this is listed anywhere in the room). What is even more ridiculous is that there is free wi-fi access in the lobby area – not that there is much seating in the lobby area, as mentioned before. So anyone who cares to, whether a paying Hilton guest or not, can access free wi-fi in the lobby. But someone paying $299 a night can’t get free wi-fi in the comfort of their, not inexpensive, guest room. This is crazy, and is poor treatment of their guests by Hilton.
However, we greatly enjoyed our stay at the Hilton Chicago O’Hare and would have no hesitation in staying there on future visits to the city.

title: “Well, at least they are consistent....”
text: Second stay in 4 week period. The ONLY reason i use this hotel is for the kitchen. Because otherwise the location and housekeeping at this hotel are subpar. As usual room was not stocked or cleaned properly. By my third day I left a very large bill with a note on the counter with instructions for what needed to be done and restocked. I should not have to do this - ever. This time i noticed that the hotel also allows grown men to loiter around the property seemingly all day, and these were not hotel employees on a smoke break. I only know this because 3 of my six days there i left early and traveled back at lunch to see them in the same location and again in the early and late evening. And in the morning it was always fun to make my way through the " construction" workers waiting under the overhang outside for their daily pickup. This was my last stay at this property.

title: “RUDE customer Service”
text:
Was very excited to be traveling with our crew for our show to the Los Angeles area. The reviews on line for Hollwood Hotel were great but once we arrived we were all incredibly disappointed with the experience we had there. Our company faxed over credit card info the day we landed. The hotel manager emailed our office production/manger confirmation showing payment the same day However when we checked in 9PM that night the front desk receptionist Devon said there was no payment on file there. 
Our office/production manager back in NY tried to speak with Devon through my cell phone (1AM NY time) but Devon said it was against company policy to talk on a customers cell. She then called him direct. He said there was nothing he could do. The manager was out. 
I offered to put down my credit card just to get the talent checked in since they were beyond exhausted from thier 6AM flight from NYC. One of the crew offered to put the rest of the crew on his credit card and Devon didn't like his tone and accused him of being "belligerent." I was there the whole time and while our crew member was exhausted he did not curse, call names or yell at Devon. He was impatient but that was it and Devon said he was uncomfortable and refused to check us in because the crew guy was "belligerent." He called the manager and got him on the phone and said that we were accusing him of sabotaging our travel plans! THAT WAS NEVER SAID. Then because he was uncomfortable he asked permission by the manager to make us wait for another person to check in. I then offered to deal with Devon and he refused saying that he was "done with us." The hotel manager NEVER called our office person back and one week later we are still trying to get in touch with him!!!!!!!
Long story short Devon refused to check us in and the manager approved that. Rather than be subjected to more rude treatment, our office manager made reservations within minutes at the nearby Wilshire Hotel where we were well received. I was billed for the one hour our talent were in their rooms at the Hollywood Hotel which I am still contesting. 
I used to be in the hotel business and I understand that not everyone is going to be a happy customer. But regardless of any cranky customers, it is your job as a concierge or receptionist to give them great service regardless. We were treated horribly and denied service for OUR "rude" behavior. Glad to be rid of the place and give someone else our business. 
While I was surprised to receive bad service from the receptionist, I was more so dismayed to get it from the manager of this hotel. I would expect better treatment from someone doing business in an area with heavy production crew traffic.

title: “Clean, tiny, dark”
text:
We have stayed at the Belleclaire twice in the last few weeks. Each time we booked a room with shared bath. The second time our room was so small that we had to walk sideways to get around the bed! However, we very much liked the freshly laundered duvet covers on the down comforters--so much better than the usual hotel quilts or bedspreads that don't get cleaned on a regular basis. The shared bath was newly tiled and extremely clean.
I was concerned when we got out of the elevator during the second visit that all of the rugs were covered with brown paper and there were ladders and construction equipment in evidence. However, we heard no construction noise during our stay. I think they were just repainting, so this will be a temporary thing.
I don't know what kind of climate control there is during the summer months. Perhaps they put air conditioners in the windows, but there were none in evidence when we stayed there, nor was there any central air conditioning or a fan. A large, heavy floor-to-ceiling drape hangs over the window and doesn't open. If you book during warm weather, I would definitely ask about this.
All in all, if your priorities are low prices, cleanliness and great Upper West Side location, this is an excellent choice for you. If, on the other hand, you want something spacious or fancy, pay more and go elsewhere.
TIP: At the time we booked, the rates being offered directly by the hotel were lower than hotels or expedia, which also include a service fee in addition to local taxes.

title: “A pleasant value for money one night stop over.”
text:
This little hotel gave the most friendly welcome of any place I've visited. Tracey, on reception, made me feel really important as a guest. The shuttle provided between the car rental place I used and then the airport was really helpful and similarly friendly.
The most advantageous thing about this hotel is its vicinity to Graceland. You can easily and safely walk between the two. If you're unfamiliar with Memphis, this is a little way out of the centre, so if you're more a Beale Street person, look for something in the centre.
The room I was given was clean and comfortable and fair value for the rate I paid. Breakfast is typical I've found of this type of hotel- cereals, some baked items, coffee and fruit.
I was advised not to walk too far out of the immediate area, so, if looking for dining options, it would be a good idea to take advantage of some of the free transportation offered by restaurants.

title: “Perfect location!”
text: LOVE THIS HOTEL! Arrived early and given a lovely room high up and away from the elevator. Staff was friendly and helpful. Wow, free wi fi was an added value, as well as I pads in the lobby for printing my theater tickets and my boarding pass. The roof garden was a peaceful place to escape the city noise and enjoy the view. I love the bar in the lobby with morning fare as well as snacks and beer for early evening. Close to the subway and tons of shopping an restaurants. I highly recommend Pod 51 and I Will stay here again!

title: “Red Lion Hotel”
text: Loved this place is SO clean great service we were there for a night before a trip they bring you your vehicle to the door under the covered entrance & they park it for you.

title: “The worst hotel I have stayed in in my life.”
text:
Lobby is small, congested and not "welcoming" at all. There is no concierge service. Two elevators only for a 25 story hotel. "High speed" internet service was almost as slow as "dial up." Room service was two hours late. They "lost" our order. It doesn't take two hours to make two salads and when we finally got our order, they forgot the salad dressing. Food quality was not what you would expect for the price.
Rooms are small and bathrooms are tiny (by my standards anyway). The rooms and hallways are dingy. The carpet was dirty. The blanket on my bet had old dried blood stains on it. There was no light bulb in the lamp by the bed. It took 6 hours to have a refrigerator delivered to my room which I needed for medication. House cleaning did not service my room until 4:45 p.m. despite the fact that I was gone all day. 
 For $399 a night, inclusive of tax, one would expect a better hotel.

title: “Late review but had to as Gansevoort was so good!”
text:
Going to keep this fairly short. Was at Gansevoort over new year and attended the nye party there!
Ideally placed away from hustle and crowds of 5th avenue. In a very cool area with some great shopping.
Good clean hotel that simply had an air of coolness about it! Pricey but that's good as keeps a certain standard of clientel.
Pool pretty chilly at 7am in winter!
Thank you Gansevoort!

title: “Good location and overall pleased with stay at W”
text:
My wife and I recently made a weekend trip to Dallas for leisure and a concert at Superpages.com Amphitheater. We stayed at the W Dallas and were overall pleased with the commendations and rooms. The W is centrally located downtown and walking distance to American Airlines Arena and the House of Blues Theatre. Very modern and chic bar/lounge near the lobby. Seemed like an it-spot for groups to start at on a night out downtown. We had breakfast two mornings at Tom Colicchio's Craft restaurant near the lobby. The service was on par and the food was delicious, but limited menu. Ghost Bar is located at the top of the W hotel. Beware of the VIP list for those staying at the W. Just b/c you're on the list, doesn't mean you are excused from the $25 cover charge. However, women are admitted with no cover. A little to smokey and filled with convention attendees. Great view of Dallas skyline. 
The rooms where on the small side for the amount paid. Glass walled shower with no door let a lot of cold air flow in. Curtain used to divide room from bathroom. Large window with surprisingly comfortable modern decor couch. We didn't have the opportunity (due to cold weather) to experience the infinity pool, but heard great things from other guests. Highly recommend taking a stroll down the block to eat sushi at Kenichi. Modern furnishings, great booths w/ curtains, and the selection and sushi where to die for. 
ABSOLUTE MUST: if you are without vehicle or rental car, ask about the complimentary Acura Service offered through the W. Driver will pick you up and drop you off at Love Field Airport (savings of $25 each way) plus any location within a 6 mile radius. Doesn't sound far, but everything you need is right around you. No limit on use, just based on availability. Let the concierge know of your plans and they will arrange everything. However, will not travel to Superpages.com on event nights. 
Nice hotel, would stay again if attending events in downtown Dallas.

title: “Good”
text: The room was comfortable and sheet look and smell clean. The only thing I did not like was the floor of the bathtub was stained, it look dirty.

title: “Rooms a little dated!”
text: The lobby and common areas are very nice and the service is good, but the rooms are little dated. Bathrooms are very small for a hotel of this caliber. The vanity is small and the bath is just a regular shower/bathtub combination. Ceiling in the bathroom is very low. I didn't like having plastic cups considering the price of the hotel. On the plus side the beds were comfortable and it was quiet.It is located on the Chicago River and offers and the riverside rooms offer nice views. It is located near shopping and the Navy Pier.

title: “Outside is deceiving; clean, comfortable, good place to stay”
text:
This was our first stop on a week long business trip. When we pulled up out front our initial reaction was "oh oh" it was plain and looked from the outside like it could be disappointing. Very plain, all white with blue, most new hotels have shall we say modern colors and landscaping. 
We asked to see our room first and the room was clean, comfortable and nice. It turned out to be the best night sleep we would get in the next 4 nights! 
Breakfast was good and plenty of variety. Good hotel, worth the money and clean, comfy and quiet!

title: “Happy Times!”
text:
If you like to travel with your dogs like we do, this place is fantastic. The dog beach is right outside, and the rooms have sliding glass doors going out to a shared fenced in dog-run area. 
This was the most relaxed and easy trip that we have ever made with our 2 dogs because of the above reasons. Also, the staff were very friendly and accepting of our dogs, not a bit uptight. They really put us at ease. The rooms are fairly plain and utilitarian. Ours was the most basic one, but some have small kitchenettes. 
Ocean Beach is nearby so it is easy to go into the downtown area there to eat or shop. There are also a few upscale restaurants nearby the Inn. We ate at one called The Bungalow and the food was great as was their wine list.

title: “Excellent hotel but !!!”
text: Excellent location , rooms are good some have great views ours did not but it didn't spoil our stay, I traveled with my son & asked for 2 beds prior to our arrival , they had only got room with king size bed! They rang the room later saying if we paid extra $50a night to have a room with 2 beds. Service poor some days also check your bill regular as on two occasions the same drink cost me $4 dollars more the day after.dont let this put you off as you can eat & drink out the hotel is very good.

title: “Mixed review for a Saturday night stay”
text:
We got a good rate on the room, thanks to AAA, and were generally satisfied with its comfort and amenities. We were not fans of the extremely squishy bedding which they are so proud of, though. I'm sure many people like these layers of luxury and the pillow-top mattress, but we didn't care for it. 
The hotel pool is rather small, so those seeking a Sunday morning swim before breakfast quickly overwhelmed it. For such a large hotel, the pool is much too small. No one could swim laps at all. The exercise room was also very busy, with nearly every treadmill and elliptical in use. 
The breakfast buffet was served in the Turner Fish restaurant, due to renovations in the usual space. Again, due to all the families present on the weekend, it was a somewhat overwhelming scene of wiggly toddlers, sloshing orange juice, and crowding at the buffet. A chef was making custom omelettes, but otherwise the food was extremely ordinary and rather cold and congealing by 9:30 a.m. when we got there. The hash browns were more like cubed, steamed potatoes -- neither crispy nor savory. The oddly sweet sausages were tasty but cold, and the egg casserole had simply been sitting in its container for too long. The coffee and orange juice were excellent and our server refilled both attentively throughout the meal. Nice little muffins and pastries.
Our arrival on Saturday was perfect, with both the valet parking and the early check-in to our room working perfectly. The valet service was smooth at check-out, too. 
We were pleased with the value for our discounted room, but a bit disappointed that the hotel couldn't provide a better breakfast setting for the many large family parties who were overwhelming their dining room and frankly making a bit of a mess. In its temporary quarters, everything felt crowded and cramped. Not the leisurely Sunday morning experience we had hoped for. And the food was just too ordinary for a hotel in this class -- they should spiff up their offerings a bit, and leave less food sitting there for lengthy periods. 
It was fun to be near Copley Square and Newbury Street, and the nearby shopping arcades provided places to stroll without having to experience the weather.

title: “Sleepless in Denver”
text: We were in Denver for a visit with friends and arrived at the airport at 11:15 P.M. It took the shuttle 30 minutes to arrive after calling them. When we arrived at the hotel we were checked in in a timely manner. After going to our room I went in search of some bottled water. Every machine in the hotel was out of water. When I asked the front desk clerk she said that I could walk a couple of blocks to a store in the area...yea right...after midnight in an area I didn't know anything about...I don't think so. We made due with a coke and went to bed. The pillows are very thick and VERY firm which led to a pretty sleepless night. The worst part was the next morning when I was scheduled to take the shuttle back to the airport to pick up a rental car. The 8:40 shuttle never showed up and at 9:15 they finally called a cab for people whose flights were leaving soon. I managed to get on the shuttle when it finally showed up at 9:30. The driver was pleasant but offered no explanation of where he had been. We needed a hotel the night we returned to Denver for our flight home and I chooe another hotel.

title: “Hotel Helix is a great hotel. Very interesting...”
text: Hotel Helix is the most unusual hotel I have EVER stayed in. I loved it. The decor was amazing. The service was GREAT. The location was really good. I will stay here every time I go to D.C. from now on.

title: “Great location, fun for kids but nice for parents”
text: This was our first stay at the Palomar, but we have stayed at other Kimpton hotels in the city. The staff was very friendly and accomodating. My kids (6 and 8) love Kimpton hotels because they are fancy but kid friendly. The gift bags on check in and the goldfish (named Goldie!) in our room made them feel special. A child size robe was sent up for my daughter! We did not complete the scavenger hunt because we ran out of time. My family also enjoyed the pool. The lighting and view was so cool at night. The rooms are quiet and comfortable. The location is great. Easy walk to Michigan Avenue. We love Kimpton Hotels, and we will return to Palomar in the future!

title: “Comfortable Stay, services could be better”
text: Comfortable room, beds and bathroom. Nice location with cafes, coffee shops and restaurants nearby, and only some 10 minutes walk to the station. It would have been better if the carpet and floor of the toilet could be cleaned everyday. The carpet was wet (somebody spilt the water and escaped?!) one day when we returned to the room. We couldn't enter the room cuz the key was not functioning the other day and it has taken sometime before the technician came... lunchboxes had become tea time snacks... Apart from these happenings, the stay was good!

title: “Excellent front desk service”
text: We stayed at The Marmara Manhattan for almost 2 months. Although the carpets in the room need changing our overall experience was excellent. We overcame both a hurricane and a snow storm and we were not effected at all. I would like to thank a couple of people who made our stay easier. A big thank you to Dennis ( front office manager), Ashley, Robert, Maureen and Chris. The management should also consider how an excellent job Mehmet from housekeeping is doing. This was our secon stay at the Marmara, I would definetly stay here the next time I'm in NYC. Elvin Oztek

title: “Super-Happy with Embassy Suites Lakeshore!!”
text:
Couldn't ask for a better location. Within walking distance of everything!! Walked to the hotel from the Orange Line (arrived @ Midway Airport), It was great! 
The service at the hotel was outstanding. The first two nights were low key in the hotel, but the attention to detail from the staff was great. The second two nights we were there was when the Bears beat Seattle to be one game away from the Superbowl. The crowds were amazing, yet the service level was maintained. I was extremely impressed. 
'The only negative observation is the swimming pool. Very small and a lot of kids. I wouldn't let my kids go as there were so many kids in a small area with what seemed like a lot of colds...Good thing we weren't in Chicago to swim anyway!!
For the price, this was one of the nicest hotels that I've stayed in with one of the best views in the city. 
We'll be back--

title: “A mini-Embassy Suites, with nicely updated decor”
text: A good bit of money was spent spiffing up a dowdy AmeriSuites into a very nice mini-version of an Embassy Suites. The room design is clever, with a very large flat-screen TV mounted above a mantle-like fixture, which swivels to allow viewing from the beds or the modular sofa system. The TV is set up to accommodate all manner of audio and video inputs. Desk system nicely done, as is the back bar counter with mini-fridge. For traveling families, it's possible to have some sleep while others watch the TV, but this may not work if you need true separation between rooms. The lobby is totally redone, with a nice Starbucks-inspired granite bar and dessert/bread case, where they will sell you a latte or cocktail. The included continental breakfast is more than adequate, but you can also upgrade at a cost to hot egg-based dishes. Very friendly and helpful staff. TV and computer nooks off the main lobby are handy. Works very well if you need to stuff a family of 4 or 5 into a single room and want to save $50 from an Embassy, but would get cosy if it's for more than a night or two.

title: “Our Visit for Aunt Rose's Funeral”
text: The pricing was excellent. However, the cleanliness was below standard. The mirrors were smudged, we could see finger prints and smudges everywhere we went. The sheets were were not fitted properly on the beds and when we weak up in the mornings the sheets would be half way on the beds. The rooms had a foul odor. Breakfast was good. The hotel staff was very helpful and professional.

title: “Glad I did stay at Holiday Inn Express Last Night!”
text:
Stayed four nights at this hotel in late June with wife and two boys (7 and 4) while in town for a conference. The front desk staff (Jena and Jeff) were great from the moment we checked in. I had several questions about stores, buses, attractions, etc. and they eagerly answered them all. Being a Priority Club member, I was even greeted with cookies! 
I splurged for a King suite with jacuzzi tub - it was great to have the extra space - basically a standard bedroom that had a sofabed, with a smaller bedroom connected with a door. We did look out the back at the adjacent Holiday Inn, but the extra space made up for the lack of a view. The oversized jacuzzi tub was great - like having our own hot tub!
Internet worked well, but does require an ethernet cable. I have just started carrying one with me all the time. There is also a small business center in the lobby with two computers and printers - great for printing boarding passes.
The kids (and I) enjoyed the indoor pool that was actually heated. True, it's not huge, but it is ample. Hey, it's the only decent hotel in the downtown area that has a pool. 
You can walk to the Space Needle and adjacent museums and amusement park in 5 minutes. It's an easy walk with signals to cross streets. You can also walk to a bus stop in the downtown free bus ride zone in about 5-10 minutes. The free ride zone covers a large area. You really don't need a car here. We worked our way down to the waterfront one evening and had a great meal at Fishermans. We took a cab back and it was only $10, including a $2 tip. 
I parked a rental car here the first night - yes, its tight parking, but not nearly as bad as I expected from the previous reviews. I returned the car on the first Monday (original plan - we had it for a week touring around the state - see other reviews for Sheraton Airport Portland, OR; Quality Inn Ocean Shores, WA; Quality Inn Port Angeles, WA; Qualtiy Inn Downtown Victoria, BC) so didn't have to park the remaining nights. 
We ate a dinner at the adjacent Holiday Inn - fairly plain food, but kids eat free - nice budget break during a two-week trip!
I used the washer/dryer facilities one night - the detergent machine took my money - the front desk staff gladly gave me a box without question.
Hint - if you have to have a rental car while in Seattle, reserve it from the downtown location - you can save ~$90 in taxes on a week's rental. It pays for the cab ride to the rental location and the town car ride from the HIExpress back to the airport and more. The hotel will arrange a town car to take you to the airport for a $30 flat rate - less than a metered cab fare.
I would stay at this hotel again and highly recommend it for the staff service, pool, location near the Seattle Center complex (space needle, museums, etc) and proximity to the real downtown, considering the rates.

title: “OK for a One-Night Stand”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the Hilton LAX hotel both going and coming from a two-week vacation in Hawaii and though there is nothing that makes one want to shout praises about the place, it is cefrtainly perfectly acceptable for a one-night stay. The beds were, in both cases, comfortable and restful. It was also nice to have several choices of tea to choose from in the morning and a free and convenient shuttle to the airport that leaves every 15 minutes all day and night through was certainly a "plus."
The cleaning staff was, the nights we were there, inconsistent. The first night, for instance, the bath had not been cleaned very well (there were a number of hairs in the tub) but the second night was far better with every thing neat and clean. 
One of the most disappointing aspects of the Hilton LAX is the fact that though there is a so-called business center, even the use of the computers to access the Internet require an additional charge. In this day and time, such a failure to be traveler-friendly, is rather ridculous.
But would we stay again? Probably. The Hilton is convenient to the airport and though there are few restaurants other than a Carl's Jr. within walking distance, a one-night stand at a reasonable (for Los Angeles) rate make it at least a strong possibility.

title: “Excellent hotel”
text: We loved our time in The Fairmount, we were on our honeymoon and when we checked in the guy behind reception was lovely and upgraded us!!! The view from our room was superb and our bed was huge and comfy. We did not eat in the hotel, but the lobby and overall the whole hotel we thought was lovely and clean. Would love to return to this hotel again

title: “Charged but not given a room”
text:
We booked a room at this location using United miles and planned to stay with my family of five after a day at Sea World. A few weeks before the trip our plans changed and I called ahead and asked to move our reservation three days back. The person on the other end of the line said she had moved our reservation and that it would not not be a problem. I wrote down the time, daye and name of the person I spoke with.
However, when we arrived our reservation cold not be found. After being asked to wait 30 minutes while other guests checked in I was told I would have to pay for a new room. I went around the corner to the Western Inn and found a less expensive room with the same location and better service.

title: “HUGE Dissapointment”
text: We have a large family, and have found that the Comfort Suites accommodate us well. We have stayed in several different locations in several different states and this one was HORRIBLE! The front desk staff was very polite, but clueless. There were no extra pillows or blankets for guests, and the rooms were not clean. At least not by my standards (candies found under the bed that were NOT ours and sticky gum like substance on the comforter). The sofa bed was very small and uncomfortable, and no bedding was supplied for its use. Beds were lumpy and uncomfortable. When I called and specifically asked that housekeeping come by due to several dirty towels in the room, I was assured that they would. However, the front desk actually asked me to bring down the dirty towels to the lobby! When we returned that night we found that our room had not been serviced. We had to go get towels from downstairs and ended up running out of toilet paper in the middle of the night. It was a disaster! We were told that we had a DND sign on our door that's why we were not serviced, BULL!! How do they explain the specific phone call made before we left that day? You are better off choosing a different location if this is the chain you wish to stay in!

title: “Does not compare to the London Hotel in Hollywood...”
text: The lobby of the hotel was tiny with no room to sit. I stayed in a two bedroom suite and for the price I was so dissapointed. Everynight I had to get a new key even though I was staying for four nights and five days. I wanted to try this hotel out because my boyfriend and I had stayed at the London in Hollywood. I would highly recomend the one in Hollywood, however to anyone wanting to stay at the one in New York take you buisness somewhere eles. Most of the people woh work there were stuck up and rud. On the Other hond the concierge by the name in Tim was wonderful!!! The retaurant by Gordan Ramsey has nothing on the restaurant he has at the Londo in Hollywood!!!

title: “Awesome Hotel & Location”
text: We have been staying in this hotel for the past several years, usually a few times a year. It's an absolutely awesome hotel! Very Modern, Clean, just a little pricey, which I guess you'd expect for a hotel of this quality. It is within walking distance & very close to Beale Street, great security, too. Never had any problems with security instances or anything like that. Even the parking deck feels pretty safe. We absolutely love it here! Awesome showers & great comfy king-size beds! Very home-like feeling in the rooms. My only issue with this hotel, which naturally doesn't affect my rating of it, is the extra little charges for everything. Notice, if you pick up one of the refreshments of move them for a few seconds at all, it will automatically be charged to your bill. However, management has always been great about adjusting it back off my bill. But u will need to double check your bill & make sure you were not charged for them. Also, note there is an extra $18 fee daily for parking, which almost all downtown Memphis hotels charge something extra for parking. Overall, we love it though! As a matter of fact, we just got back yesterday & I already have another room booked later this year!

title: “You get what you pay for”
text: The position of this hotel can't be faulted. Access to the lively Venice Beach Boardwalk is but a step away, but a short walk gets you to Main street and some really excellent Resteraunts. It is basic, and the lack of Air con in summer would be a problem, but the facilites were adequate, and the staff were always helpful and very friendly. It could do with a face lift, and a bit of TLC, but then it would probably cost double.

title: “Magnificent”
text:
A magnificent hotel in structure, location and service.
The door man at the time of our stay (Michael) was the greatest assistant/tour advisor/watchful eye for my friends and I when we would get seperated and wander in and out from our shopping frenzy.
The happy hour was great fun, the front desk were brilliant however their cleaning/room service staff were desperately lacking in English completely which made requests (such as where the laundrette was and whether they could come back later to service the room) very difficult.
Hard Rock cafe is not far around the corner and I highly recommend it!
The mini convenience store inside the hotel is a rip off - avoid if possible.

title: “Upscale, trendy, boutique convenience”
text:
I and my husband and 2 teenagers stayed in the Vista King Spa Suite for 2 nights to attend a UCLA graduation for my older son. This was our second stay at this property within the past 2 years. The hotel was sold out primarily with families of UCLA grads attending various graduation ceremonies over the weekend of June 15-17, 2012. Needless to say, the hotel was bustling with people who were continually streaming in and out of the hotel to attend ceremonies. Overall, we were very pleased with our stay. Here are some highlights:
Pros: Great proximity to UCLA, Westwood Village, Beverly Hills and other LA attractions. Nice LA location, our room had a lovely view of LA city lights. Clean, well appointed room with contemporary, trendy decor. A framed picture of our kitty cat sat on a side table (the concierge had emailed us in advance to send a jpg of a loved one in advance of our visit). We thought this was a fun touch! Their friendly professional staff invited us to use the in room refrigerator for our personal use at no extra charge. Premium toiletries, large suite and humongous bathroom with jacuzzi soaking tub and oversized shower. The bed is very comfortable. Lobby is spacious and supplies good coffee, infused ice tea and water. Valet service is prompt and courteous. Blvd 16 restaurant food did not disappoint for breakfast. I worked out in the fitness room...it was busy the morning I worked out but was able to get on a treadmill.
Cons: Room layout. The large bathroom houses the large closet and has no separation of space, so if one is in the shower (clear glass doors) or needs to use the toilet, others can't access the sink or closet. This might be OK for couples, but is inconvenient for people sharing the room for business or with family members (teens, kids) that prefer privacy. We think it would be nice if the Kimpton had a large suite with 2 beds. The sofa bed in the living room (where our kids slept) had one of those dreaded "bars" in the middle and was not comfortable. Hotel can be on the pricey side but there are deals to be had, and I would definitely search for specials. 
I've noticed other reviewers lament the lack of coffee in the room. This was not a problem for us...we actually enjoy padding down to the hotel lobby for coffee...perhaps this is because we were with our kids and wouldn't have brewed in the room anyway (they like to sleep in and we wouldn't want to wake them). 
My husband and I enjoy walking through the neighborhood in the morning. The air is fragrant with various blooms and the architecture and gardens of the area homes are lovely to stroll by.
The staff went out of their way to help right a transportation situation...the hotel "house car" was unavailable to take us to UCLA for the graduation ceremony. The hotel reimbursed us the cab fare (one way) to UCLA which we thought was very accommodating.
We will definitely stay here again the next time family or business brings us to the LA Westwood area.

title: “Great Stay”
text: We had a great experience all around. Much better than Country Inn by far.

title: “not bad, but a little cramped”
text: We stayed in a mini suite type room. This had a half wall separating the sitting area from the bedroom, but there was so much furniture that it all felt very cramped. When the sofabed was open, you could only squeeze by. The hotel has a small indoor pool, very cold water, no hot tub. The Fitness room was modest, with a few weight machines and 3 treadmills. If you use the adjacent restaurant for breakfast, ("Viand") skip the small buffet and order from the menu, it was much better than the buffet. Parking in the garage is $30 per day, but ask for a discount ticket at the front desk and get $4 off. Front desk service was friendly and helpful, and the location is very good, though the small lobby always seemd crowded and a little chaotic. The hotel was very clean and well kept. There are several other Marriott properites downtown including the regular Marriott and the Rennaisance. They have better facilities overall, and are often competitively priced.

title: “Not My Best Choice”
text:
I chose this hotel because it was across the street from the Convention Center, where my conference was. I should have gone with another similarly priced hotel and walked an extra block. Small, a little creepy (dirty/dark), fire alarm went off several times during my stay. Interesting characters outside thanks to the bus station across the street.
At first, I was excited to have the Reading Terminal market right next to me so I could shop for fresh food, but the market is also probably why I had a rodent in my room. Yes, saw a mouse run across the room one night. Couldn't get anyone to answer the phone at the front desk so I had to go down and tell them about it. They looked startled and confused about what to do. Finally a maintenance man came up with a bucket and after chasing the mouse in the living room area, he disappeared. We think he went into the couch so another man came up and they proceeded to shake and beat the couch. Nothing. So they set some traps and left. Never heard anything more so I mentioned during my checkout that they might want to get rid of the traps before the next guests checked in. Again I got a look of confusion since no one knew there had been traps set or was even a problem. I understand that stuff happens, but the lack of follow-through on everyone's part was not impressive.

title: “Trendy and popular, still excellent”
text: This was my second stay at ZaZa for a weekend getaway with my husband. ZaZa is definitely a trendy boutique hotel and very popular, but that doesn't mean you can't get good service. Both times I've visited on the weekend the hotel has been very busy, but the valet, front desk and pool side service has been very good to excellent. It's hard not to be happy with someone handing you a glass of prosecco before you even get checked in. The pool definitely gets busy and a little rowdy, but if needed, the pool staff will find you a lounge chair, and there are quiet corners or cabanas available on the back side of the pool area. I wouldn't recommend a room on the 2nd or 3rd floors near the pool, unless you want to be part of the party during the afternoon. The room interiors are all up to date and comfortable, views vary. The rooms and suites facing the pool courtyard have the best views looking out toward Herman Park and there are other rooms in the wings facing north that should have views of the park. The city views from rooms facing east and west is great at night, but watch out for rooms in the corners that essentially look into the balcony rooms. If you like to be able to open your blinds, don't stay in 802 or anything like it on other floors. These rooms need blinds the open from the top down to avoid letting guests on their balcony seeing you walking around your room. There is art everywhere in the hotel. It is very edgy, often a little risqué or a little disturbing, and always entertaining. The butler's pantry on each floor takes care of your caffeine needs in the morning, and a variety of snacks are available in your room. The Monarch is also a great place for catching up with friends at the bar or fine dining. Overall, this is a great stay in the museum district and well worth the expense.

title: “Delightful hotel”
text: I stayed at the Beacon with family while we were in New York for Thanksgiving. We were delighted when we walked into our 1-bedroom suite! With a hall closet, marble bathroom, comfy living area with fold-out sofa and kitchenette, a roomy bedroom with another closet, and a great view of the Fairway grocery store and the ballet studio across the street, the suite provided a fun and comfortable place for us to be for 4 nights. It was like having our own apartment. The front desk staff were friendly and helpful. We did eat at the Viand cafe on Thanksgiving night and were satisfied with the food and service. Would not recommend the Fairway cafe, though. Starbucks is right across the street. Central park within walking distance. Two things were slightly annoying: constant honking of cars on street below and noise from fans leaving Journey concert at next door Beacon Theater two nights in a row. Otherwise, it was pretty delightful.

title: “Girl's weekend”
text: My friend & I stayed here while in town for Dave Ramsey's Seminar. Got a great deal. Clean & beautiful interior. My only complaint was couldn't get wifi to work.

title: “I expected more”
text:
I drove my wife and two kids up to Fort Worth to see Muse at the Convention Center and we stayed at the Omni, which was very close to the concert but also somewhat expensive ($180/night). Once we arrived, I noticed a lot of hotels in the area and I wish I'd researched more thoroughly.
The room was on the average to small side, everything seemed clean, and the hotel offers free wireless internet. But the lobby smelled weird, like maybe they were trying to "perfume" the air? It was ghastly. And this is a 15 story hotel that doesn't have a single coke machine -- so if it's 11pm and you want a coke, you have to order it from room service, or go downstairs to the bar -- either way, enjoy your $5 coke. $18/day valet parking, which is outrageous but seems to be more or less the going rate in downtown Fort Worth. The restaurant downstairs offered a breakfast buffet for $16, but my kids weren't impressed and so we stopped at a Waffle House on the way home.
All in all: clean and a great location for a convention center event -- but also expensive and not really worth the high price.

title: “Decent hotel”
text:
i got this hotel pretty cheap. 
we only stayed here because the other hotels in LA were very expensive. 
this was a lovely hotel and considering we had 2 rooms at the end of the hotel on the 12th floor which looked onto the runway you couldnt hear the planes coming in 24/7
its located on century boulevard, we had a car in LA which i would highly recommend and it wasnt far to the beaches and around 30 mins from hollywood.
clean and modern rooms and prices of food and drink were very reasonable.

title: “OK but i wouldn't rave about it”
text: I agree with the other reviewers, old world charm, yes but faded glory and the lobby area and social areas a bit limited.Spacious rooms with very comfortable beds[king size]but open to conversations clearly heard in adjacent rooms .Lovely piano bar but a bit dull really.The pianist was very accomplished but I found the repetoire limited and hardly set the place alight perhaps it was to do with the age of the audience, definitely not the young set here[Ok I'm sixty too].The restaurant setting was charming and the service was excellent but I wouldn't say exceptionalThe room service was beautifully presented. and the staff were most pleasant in my encounters with themThe pool and spa was really a highlight of this venue, quite stunningly presented..The lifts were out of the ark, at one stage i waited 10 mins on the 8th floor and gave up and walked the stairs with my bags.As for the comments about the location it depends what you prefer but I did enjoy the walk to and from Union square and Fisherman's wharf as exercise, but the cable car is a very good option for those who can't or wont.If you want chique or boutique, this place aint for you, but if you like must and crust then you will fit in nicely.Enjoyable yes, but overpriced really and a tad disappointing,it could retain it's old world charm but have some modernisation,,pizazz and even jazz .No i wouldn't come back, nor would I say my stay was truly memorable

title: “Not Impressed”
text: First off, the parking is terrible. It's very confusing to find parking garage. The check-in employees are not helpful at all. Never gave any information about the hotel whatsoever. Then when we got to our room, there was a definite smell of smoke in it (it was a non-smoking room) and it's obvious that someone noticed it becaus they had the window open to try to get rid of the smell. By that time, we were hungry so we just kept the room. The location is nice but I would not stay there again because of the parking, and lack of friendly employees.

title: “Above and Beyond!”
text:
As a Platinum, I know what to expect in terms of rooms at the Marriott brands. Assuming they get that right (which they did), about the only way for a hotel to exceed or fail to meet expectations is with interactions with their staff. 
We checked in and mentioned it was our 30th anniversary, which was greeted with a friendly "congratulations!". That was all I needed to hear. 
That night, we hit the town and upon returning, found a basket of chilled mini-champagnes and strawberries. Needless to say, this was unexpected - it was just the perfect nightcap to an all-around excellent stay.
Great hotel with a great staff!

title: “Beautiful Stay on Mission Bay”
text: Great location. Beautiful view, clean, quiet, great service. You can wake up in the morning, have a cup of coffee overlooking Mission Bay, watching the sailboats and kayaks cruise by. What could be better!!!

title: “Not sure what the fuss is about!”
text: Stayed here because it got very high reviews. I prefer to pay a bit more for good service and value. The valet parking staff were very friendly and the room cleaners as well. Nothing special about the desk staff. The room we stayed in was tiny and a cramped bathroom. Reasonbly clean. The beds were extremely uncomfortable and the walls are paper thin. You can hear everything, all words of every conversation and also you can hear others in the washroom, no details needed. When I asked for earplugs, they offered to change rooms, which I wasn't keen on doing at midnight. But he said all rooms are like this in terms of thin walls and same beds. So what is the point of moving? We stayed in the same room. Very cramped space for 2 people. Ok if alone. Parking is 29$ not 20$ as listed in the Expedia website. It was ok, but there are so many better places to stay for same or cheaper.

title: “OK For Just One Night”
text: Stayed one night because the hotel is convenient to I-70 and the weekend rate was great. The room was up to Hyatt's high standards except the air conditioner was very noisy every time the compressor kicked on. The staff was friendly and helpful. The hallways were dingy, the carpet was worn and the elevators sounded lke they were on their last legs. You need a car if you stay here as the only restaurant that I saw within walking distance is a Denny's.

title: “There's not much I can fault about this hotel, it's fantastic.”
text: A great hotel in a top neighbourhood. The subway is 10-15 minutes walk away. The rooms are modern and light with fantastic views. We were upgraded to a junior suite which was amazing. We had breakfast at the local diner as hotel breakfasts are always expensive and we only eat light breakfasts anyway. Shame the rooftop bar was closed but I'm sure it will be lovely when finished. Main downside is wifi is not included. I wouldn't recommend paying for it as wifi is free all over NYC including Starbucks which is only round the corner. Enjoy your stay here!

title: “really pleasant stay at this hip, clean hotel”
text: My husband and I live in the Los Angeles area; but, we often travel to local hotels to take a break from our busy household and our three small children. Our stay at the Angelino was one of these quick overnight get-aways, and we loved it. The hotel has been remodeled since it was a "Holiday Inn" and there are virtually no traces of its former self. The room was a little small, but very cozy. The room was pie-shaped, which I thought was unique and interesting. We had a view of the 405 freeway, which doesn't sound cool as I write this, but was actually extremely cool. You feel like you're on top of the freeway, but you don't hear the noise (expensive double-paned glass, probably). At night, the lights on the freeway are especially pretty. The room service was quick and the food was great. The restaurant on the top floor has gorgeous views of Los Angeles. The pool area was small, but very hip, with nice comfortable outdoor furniture. This hotel could get away with charging WAY more for their rooms, but they don't, so that makes me give The Angelino even higher marks. Give it a try!

title: “Wonderful accommodations and staff, great food and location!”
text: We had a very nice corner suite with a micro and fridge. We could walk to almost everywhere we wanted to go! This was a beautiful hotel and the bistro and bar were great! The staff was friendly and very helpful. The sofabed had a lot to be desired, but when we complained, they brought us a very comfortable cot. The traffic noise can sometimes be loud, but it eventually quiets down. Our entire stay was close to perfect!

title: “Excellent Service!”
text: We visited the Sheraton Baltimore City Center Hotel recently, and experienced excellent customer service. We especially enjoyed a delicious breakfast, and amazing service from Laverne and Andre. They were attentive, personable, and fun. We had such great service, we made a point to tell the restaurant manager about the exceptional service we received from both Laverne and Andre. It made it one of our best breakfast experiences ever!

title: “the perfect final”
text:
after loosing heart with the valancia we booked at the grand del mar,what a great surprise,and what a lovely property,food,pools,and rooms.
from first contact I felt at home veronica was so good with us and welcoming we could not wait to get there.
any way we arrived to a grand welcome,a wonderful gentleman handled our arrival at reception with a great understanding when my card blocked for some reason,nothing was a problem to him yes after five weeks holiday and two car rentals sometimes cards sag at the edges,to cut a long story short I stayed for free in a wonderful palazio suite (my wife paid)
I did not know the hotel belonged to Mr Manchester who owned the hyatt regency towers in san diego twenty five years ago that I loved .
firstly all the food we had at the hotel was heavenly,the service with Adam taking care of us was angelic ,as for the pancakes better than the bellagio las vegas & this says it all for me.
when leaving a small misunderstanding over the resort credit the reception manager on duty did not question my memory of what I thought I agreed with them over the phone when I made the booking (I am wondering if they are wright or I am) to put it simply I am glad the Valancia let us down, this way we discovered the great del mar.

title: “Pretty standard hotel with Very soft beds”
text:
The pluses: 
Generous continental breakfast, clean and tidy premises, free internet access, friendly staff, great location. 
The minues: 
VERY soft beds, drafty rooms, loud heating system (even on low fan), hot water for a morning shower is not a given, plumbing loud enough to wake you up in the morning.

title: “Good Value/Decent clean hotel”
text: Good Value at this hotel & Hotel was Clean. Parking lot is tight - very tight - if you have a big car - good luck parking it! Good Acess to the I-5. No elevator. Felt safe staying here.

title: “Tremont escape”
text:
My wife and I checked into the Chicago Tremont on
December 19, 2002 for a 2 night stay but checked
out the next morning and moved to a different hotel. Even though we checked out in the AM, they
attempted to charge an additional $20.00 for early
checkout. 
We disliked our one night stay because:
 1. Old is ok, but our room was not clean.
 2. Their elevator was out of order and we had to
 use the service elevator. The service elevator
 was also out of order for 30 minutes. The 
 hotel had very few quests but they put us on
 the eighth floor where workers had 6 large 
 coils of steel cable where they were repairing
 the elevator.
 3. The continental breakfast consisted of coffee,
 sour green apples, and hard stale sweet rolls.
 4. There is no ice on any floor, have to order it
 at no charge.
 5. The carpet at the reception desk is a clear
 indication they do not keep the premises well
 maintained.

title: “Wonderful stay in Gaslamp District”
text: Great hotel in a great location. Right across from Petco Park, and it's very convenient to the happenings in the downtown area. Parking is expensive. Good roof-top bar with a great view.

title: “Worst AirCon System ever!”
text: We had a W suite which was much much bigger than we were expecting having read other reviews. Very pleased with the room however the bathroom was tiny. It was also so hot it was like being in a sauna. The air con system was so noisy and had steam coming out of it. We had to call an engineer to the room to sort it. He came very quickly and because of the noise we asked him to leave it turned off. The next day when we returned to the room it was back on. Again that night we needed another engineer to sort it out. It was louded than ever. With it off the room became very hot and stuffy hence my score for sleep quality. Great bar in the hotel. fab atmosphere and service. Hotel location perfect for everything.

title: “Excellent location great value for money”
text:
This was my very first trip to NYC and my partner's second (first trip 22 years ago).
The hotel has an excellent value for money. We stayed there for one week and enjoyed it very much. The location is ideal to discover NYC, near of two subway stations.
The room was nice, good size and clean with walk in shower, which for me is very important - I hate the bath tubes with those dirty curtains......).
We booked an upper level room, which is a bit more expensive than the lower floor rooms, but it's well worth for the view you get.
There are two computers with free internet usage around the corner of the reception desk, which offers you a printer to take print-outs of your google searches or whatever you where looking for in NYC.
We did not take breakfast included as there are plenty of coffee shops around where you can have a snack to take off your sightseeing. Sometimes we bought a coffee down at the restaurant bar (breakfast reception desk) to take into our room. You could either bill it to your room or pay it directly at the desk.
There is a nice roof top bar in the hotel with a nice view to the empire state building and surrounding. 
To get a much nicer view I recommend the Top of the Strand roof top bar - great view (you think you could touch the empire state bilding!) nice long island ice tea!
Friends of us will travel to NYC End of April 2012 and they also booked the upper floor room. Hope they will enjoy as much as we did.

title: “Great Staff & Centrally Located!!”
text:
My wife and I wanted to get away and take in a ball game and do a little sightseeing. Wyndham provided us with a clean room, helpful staff and a fun time. I, especially, appreciated the bartender and her willingness to contact a local tavern to find out who was showing the local game. Marissa went out of her way to ensure we had the experience we wanted!
Tip for the traveler to this Wyndham, ask for the newly renovated rooms. There were a few fellow guests we spoke with that were not too happy with their older style rooms.

title: “Can't wait to go back!”
text: I can't rave enough about this resort. What a fun and relaxing get-away. Grounds are GORGEOUS and well maintained. Pools are sparkling clean. Rooms are super clean and roomy. Staff was friendly and attentive. My only negative remark would be the over priced food by the pool. Prices were absurd and food taste/qaulity did not match the price, but our fun out-weighed that negative. Can't wait to schedule our next stay!

title: “Good Location, Decent Hotel”
text:
We stayed here from Friday to Monday Sept 24 to 27.
Took Cab from airport (about 30 minutes) $55.00.
I understand that shuttle is $19.00 per person but takes twice as long
as stops at other hotels. Felt Cab worth the extra cost if you have at least 2 people.
Nice greeting from Doorman.
Fast easy checkin. 
We joined the starwood membership at no cost and our room was upgraded.
to a preferred guest room on the 19th floor.
Was given the option to forgo maid service in exchange for starwood points 
which was OK by me, however, having this service is part of the whole appeal
of staying in a Hotel for my wife so we declined the offer.
Room was decent with view facing city. We weren't in our room much except to sleep 
and shower.
Very comfortable beds. Nice water pressure in shower although only one shower head.
Good sized HD Tv 37 inches I think.
Sign that there was free bottled water in the credenza which was hard to open.
No water was there but when calling the desk some was sent up.
We were told that this would be corrected, however, we had to call each day to get some.
Sometimes the water was cold and some not, however still a nice feature as it
was a very hot 90 degrees in Denver. We visited the indoor/ outdoor pool area
and the gym and was impressed
Had the buffet breakfast each morning at the Hotel for $17.00 per person on the weekend and $19.00 on Monday. Enjoyed the fresh berries, and fruit, granola,
scrambled eggs, bacon and sausage and strawberry and pineapple smoothies.
Consierge service gave us a map of the downtown along with directions to Coors field
and Invesco as we had tickets to the Baseball game Saturday and the Broncos game
on Sunday. We set ourselves loose on the 16th street mall which is just around
the corner from the hotel and spent the day shopping. Coors field is a nice 20 minute
walk and there is a bus service at the Market station two blocks from the hotel that 
gives you a round trip for only $4.00.
Overall we enjoyed our stay and would book this hotel again.

title: “Beautiful Facility - wish i could get thru to Accounting”
text:
I enjoyed my stay the facility was great. 
However I have had the toughest time getting thru accounting to reverse the erroneous billing on my card. They told me it will take 3 days. Since then have not been able to speak to a human.

title: “worth waiting for”
text: It took a very long time but we were able to book an RCI exchange six months prior to our stay. From the sound of the agent at RCI it was like winning the lottery. They simply don't see space coming up at the Manhattan Club. I then spent the next six months reading alot of very bad reviews and was more than a little nervousl. Our visit was wonderful. I had phoned and requested a specific type of room and on arrival they said the room set aside for us wasn't ready but if I wanted another room very similar to what we booked we could have it. We chose to wait and went for a walk in Central Park which is about five minutes away. On return the room was ready . The one bedroom unit had two baths a kitchen and a living room with an eating area. There was more than ample storage including in the bathroom which is almost unheard of. The bed was great with fresh linens and a duvet. There was a door to close off the bedroom and one bath. There is no question that the room showed some wear and tear but not in any way that made us feel uncomfortable. There were lots of towels and supplies both in the bath and kitchen. The elevators worked very well. We never heard a sound from any other room. The staff was helpful and pleasant with one exception on checkout. I attempted to pay with travellers cheques and was told they don't accept them. The hotel would cash them but not accept them as payment. The young women was rude as well as unknowledgeable. I asked for the manager and she then phoned someone who told her they were accepted. The location is perfect for wakling and the subway. If you go out via the Park Central Hotel there is a subway about 30 seconds from the door. Buses run crosstown on 57th one block north. We did go to the presentation and were shocked at the cost to buy a timeshare unit. The manager who came out after the salespitch found it very hard to accept that we couldn't afford it. He did not like taking no for an answer. We loved Nocello for dinner which was good value and delicous. The theatre is so easy to get to by subway taking about 20 minutes max from door to door. I would go back in a heartbeat.

title: “Excellent hotel in a great location for UW visit”
text: The Hotel Deca is a very nicely appointed hotel in a great location (2 blocks from UW campus). The hotel staff was extremely courteous. The hotel is a bit artsy. The rooms are a good size, clean and plenty of hot water. Coffee shop in the lobby, tables and comfy chairs to sit in while using the free wifi.

title: “Nice mid-priced boutique style hotel”
text: We stayed at this hotel on a business trip in August. Check in late at night was a breeze and the front desk staff were very cordial. Parking was a bit sketchy. We had to park in a dark lot across the street and around the corner, then walk through a group of people sitting in the parking lot to get to the lobby. A bit disconcerting at midnight. The room was spacious and modern. It has a mini fridge and small table to work on. Very nice additions. The bathroom was not super clean. The tiles & grout in the shower are in need of a deep clean, and the towels were pretty rough & old. The bed & linens were clean & comfy. The floor is laminate, and was cleaned with something that made it sticky. I'm a bit of a clean floor fanatic, so that did not sit great with me. Just bring your slippers. I left early the next morning, so I did not even get to the Riverwalk, but I did see that it was right off the back of the hotel- looked like a fabulous location on the Riverwalk, but away from the noise. Overall, it was a good hotel for the price we paid- I definitely would not pay full price for this hotel, but would consider staying again if I got another great rate.

title: “Great hotel”
text: I have stayed at this hotel many, many times. I love this hotel. Become a Select Guest Member. The hotel rooms are good size for NYC and the bathrooms are nice too. The staff is good. The only thing that is not so great is that they do not upgrade guests as they should, especially in this economy with so many empty rooms. Over the years, they have had issues with the heat and a/c controls and keeping the right temperatures in the rooms as well.

title: “AVOID!”
text:
The lobby looks "decent", but in the entrance there are guards looking after people who enter and get out because the street is SCARY.
The elevator smells horrible (well, the hallways upstairs too) And when I was standing near the entrance waiting for a cab to pick me up (and leave) a big guy entered with a HUGE fridge box. The ___ dropped it and it nearly fell over me, he could have killed me.
At night, it IS even more scary. DON'T GO HERE!!!!!!

title: “Slept like a baby...”
text: I have never written a review for a hotel before - but wanted to share that this hotel was really great for us. We stayed in the central tower and our room was clean and comfortable. The maid was so gracious and greeted us with a hearty "HELLO" when we passed her in the hallway. The desk staff was very accomodating and met all of our needs. The Guest Services staff were always helpful and kind. Everyone was so nice. Jesus in the restaurant and Elmo at the bar were really great! Most importantly, I slept well. I usually wake up in hotels because I'm a light sleeper, but I never heard anything that woke me up like doors slamming, or toilets flushing or people talking! It felt like we were alone there, but the hotel was very busy. The pool (although we didn't swim in it) was warm and looked great and was a nice size. Internet was a little slow and parking is 19 dollars a day. We rented a car from the USAVE car rental that was on property and returned it the same day we rented to avoid parking charges.

title: “We will always love the Angeleno”
text:
We stayed at the Angeleno because it was close to UCLA Medial Center where our baby son was having surgery. We were pretty stressed out when we arrived but were immediately impressed by the professionalism and kindness we encountered by everyone at the Angeleno.
People went out of their way to put us at ease and make us comfortable. We had seen the unique circular design of the building as we drove by on the 405 freeway, but we had no idea that the rooms were so well appointed, particularly the linens. 
Our son has now recovered and we are glad this episode is behind us, but we will always have a warm spot in our hearts for the Hotel Angeleno, and we look forward to staying there again just for fun!

title: “Family weekend stay”
text:
I've stayed here now several times in the past ten years. I don't think the rooms have ever looked better or fresher with their new decor and renovation. Frontline staff were extraordinary as usual led by Will at the front drive. Quick, efficient and engaged service at BIG bar as well. Kind and helpful staff at valet, too. Excited to see rejuvenated lobby when it happens.
Biggest and best is hard to pull off- they do it. Kudos

title: “Good view of Inner Harbor”
text: Excellent location for touring inner harbor & views of harbor are fantastic. However, if you are not fortunate enough to get a room with a view of the inner harbor, you should demand a discount as the views of the rest of the city are nothing special. Rooms are clean, but if you stay more than one night, your room may not be cleaned until late in the afternoon. Excellent choice for access to convention center, inner harbor, & stadiums. But if you're interested in high quality accomodations, try the Marriott.

title: “Excellent hotel in a peaceful part of the city”
text: This hotel met all our expectations. Friendly, helpful, polite reception desk staff and concierge. The room was great - quiet, black-out curtains, comfortable bed, clean and modern bathroom. We asked for an early afternoon check-in and to leave our bags in the room for an extra hour past the check-out time the next day while we picked up a rental car - both requests were granted with a smile and no fuss. We highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Worst service I've experienced in my life.”
text:
Housekeeping:
• A dirty sponge was left in our room on day 2, presumably by the housekeeper. It was not removed throughout our entire stay.
• Soap and lotions were not replenished, despite being used, on day 2.
• On day 3, we were only given 2 clean towels instead of the 4 we needed and received the first two days.
• When passing a housekeeper in the hallway, we were ignored and not greeted. No good morning or hello. They looked in the other direction when we passed them. THIS IS NOT MARRIOTT.
Breakfast:
• We ate breakfast all 3 mornings and not once did the associates in the breakfast area greet us or say good morning.
• All 3 mornings, food was running out and not replenished despite 30+ minutes remaining of service. Oatmeal was empty, milk was frozen, bread was depleted and food was removed from the buffet 15-30 minutes prior to the close of service.
• On Sunday morning the toaster literally lit on fire. The breakfast room quickly filled with smoke. NO SMOKE DETECTOR WENT OFF. The staff was barely concerned and did not react with any sense of urgency. This is concerning.
• When food was empty, the staff was nowhere to be found to ask for more. 
• Throughout the breakfast area are beautiful signs describing the “seasonal” menu with fresh fruit. There was nothing fresh or seasonal about the buffet. 
• Cereal selections: there was nothing with more than 3 grams of fiber such as Kashi (still a Kellogg’s product).
Front Desk Staff:
• Every time we approached the front desk, we were ignored by the front desk associate while they finished what they were doing on the computer or phone. The y did not say hello or thank us for waiting or ask us to wait. 
• One day we asked for transportation to Graceland. We were put in touch with “Last Minute Transportation” who ended up abandoning us at a restaurant 3 miles from downtown after we paid $70 even though they said they would pick us up. 
• The next day we asked for a taxi to take us to the Civil Rights Museum. Instead of a taxi, the front desk agent called Last Minute Transportation. We were forced to pay $10 to go 4 blocks away.
Fitness Room:
• The gym was scorching hot – no A/C.
• There were no towels in the gym all 3 days.
Overall Service:
• The staff throughout the hotel was less than friendly. 
• The staff did not smile or say hello when passing. 
• The associates appeared to be lazy and not happy. 
• There were no smiles or pleasantries – we were ignored the entire time.

title: “Bravo!”
text: We stayed two nights at the Argent in Aug 2004. The location is great! Cabs regularly stop for hire. We had rented a car but quickly realized that a car is more of a liability! Parking at the Argent is $36.50 per night if you don't get the 'park & play' rate. The rooms are tastefully decorated with one of the most comfortable beds I've slept in. They have down comforters and crisp sheets. The bathroom tub/shower does need a little work though. Ours had some minor mold in the grout. Other than that, the hotel is great and we will definitely stay here again!

title: “Pretty Std Hampton Inn, not the best location”
text: As another reviewer pointed out, this property is really neither here (Austin) or there (airport) Very standard Hampton Inn, but definitely an older property. Same complimentary hot breakfast, pool, free apples, etc. Rooms are good sized but the furniture definitely needs an update. Some fixtures were very noisy. Friendly staff. It's a 5 min. drive to the airport, but about 15 mins. to fun places in Austin. The downtown HI was more than 2x what I paid, so I went cheaper and used the rental car I already picked up. This hotel also offers free transport to the airport.

title: “Fantastic City, Fantastic Hotel”
text:
Upon walking into the Casablanca Hotel I was greeted with a friendly face behind reception, his first words were, "I'm afraid we have some bad news". I had booked a King Room back in April for our stay in December however they had to give it to another customer due to an over-booking. 
At this point usually I'm sure a battle between the receptionist/manager and myself would normally have ensued however the Casablanca offered me free wine, a discount from our stay and told me that we could have the King Room the following day - without me having to say a word. Sure they made a mistake but they corrected it immediately with absolutely no issues, it's that kind of customer service that I really appreciate.
The rest of our stay at the hotel was fantastic, the shower was so powerful it reached places I didn't know existed! The location is perfect - Times Square is 2 paces away - literally. 
The guys on the front desk were really helpful and have great knowledge of good places to eat, drink etc while you're in the City. They referred us to The View which is at the top of the Marriott Marquis in Times Square - a revolving restaurant/bar that's on the top floor - it was very romantic and absolutely stunning!
I high no problem giving the Casablanca 5 stars - our stay there was something I'll never forget!!

title: “The Magnolia Hotel in Denver offers one-of-a-kind service and trademark accommodations...we love our Magnolia getaways!”
text: We love getting away to downtown Denver and staying at the Magnolia! The staff is incredibly attentive and welcoming. They go out of their way to make guests feel at home. The cocktail hour, cookies before bed (complete with chocolate and strawberry milk!), and the delicious breakfast in the morning are just a few reasons why we love staying at the Magnolia!

title: “You will not regret staying here!”
text: Whenever we come to Phoenix,this is our first choice to stay.Everything is very clean and quiet and we feel completely safe.It is a short walk to downtown and there is a nice park close by. All this at a reasonable room rate.

title: “Great base for a NYC visitor”
text:
I stayed here on a mixed business/pleasure trip and found it to be the perfect base for a NYC newcomer. My room was a little small, but certainly not too small and I think you get what you pay for, and then some.
The rooms are veyr clean and tidy if a little chintzy, bur not gaudy. It was surprisingly quiet too, I had a great night sleep.
The staff were very helpful and patient of my many questions of how to get here and there. 
I hope to return later in the year with my partner, I will definately return to the Wall Street Inn.

title: “sleepless and not compensated on Rivington”
text: Floors 1 - 7 have no views. Bathrooms smell like vomit, but they supply candles. Our neighbors were throwing items off their balcony to the street below. Security was as loud if not louder than the drunken, dangerous guests. We were offered a discount one night, but not the night after. They did move our room, but to a comparable room, not a better room and there were many superior rooms available. Several emails stating a desire to get some kind of discount later and the answer is still NO. So there is no misunderstanding.... If you can't sleep due to criminal behaivor in the hotel, that is not their problem. I was very disappointed.

title: “Beautiful hotel & ideal location but thin walls”
text:
I stayed for 4 nights in March 2012. From outside building looked quite nice, but then then girl on the desk didnt give us quite as warm a welcome as we hoped. She started by saying Hi I need $400 in advance on credit card to cover any expenses you may incurr. Don't know if this is standard in the US. Then we were lectured repeatedly on smoking in the hotel incurring a $500 fine. We understood the first time. generally a poor welcome and not the best attitude. Room looked amazing at first glance, nicely decorated, spacious, clean, great facilities. A slight niggle is that the coffee making facilities had 4 coffee servings and 2 tiny milk tubs, so could only have 1 coffees each in 24 hours, I like a coffeee before bed and a coffee when i wake up so had to keep requesting extra milk and sugar, bit miserable really. Bathroom was well equiped and good size, beautifully decorated. Couldn't fault the cleanliness of the place, the ceaners did a superb job every day, room and hotel were immaculate. There was a safe in the room which was also useful, and iron and ironing board.
Another negative the wlls must have been quite thin as we could hear the TV in the room next door and a vaccuum being used in the room above us at 5am! Also every time another door closed on our floor in the night it made a loud bang which woke us up. bar and restaurant were nice, though fairly pricey. Food was beautiful, I had the pork - couldn't finish the meal! If you take a small bottle of water from the room facilities expect to pay $9 for the convenience. The staff were friendly and helpful for our trip, location was great - close to broadway, times square and central park. On the whole i really enjoyed my stay.

title: “Everything we Expected”
text: Stayed at the Belvedere 16-21 October. Hotel was everything that we expected from the positive reviews on this site. From check-in, which was late at night, to checking out could not find fault with the Hotel. No problem with the elevators, we were on the 14th floor.
