Walked down sometimes for the exercise which loosend us up for the day ahead. Very Short walk to Times Sq and Subway. Plenty of locations for eats. Will stay here again on our next visit.

title: “Great location, good price, rundown hotel.”
text:
My wife and I went for a nice, relaxing trip to Fisherman's Wharf, San Francisco. We got a good deal on the flight and hotel from Edmonton so we booked the Radisson, Fisherman's Wharf with the thought that it was simply a place to sleep. We also figured that the hotel would be well-kept as from past experience the Radisson seems to be a decent chain.
The Good
Great location if you want Fisherman's Wharf (back door connected to the main street of the Wharf)
Pool and fireplace outside (did not use as it was very chilly outside)
IHOP attached (cheap food)
Decent value ($90/night, decent for the Wharf)
The Bad
Rooms are small and rundown (old)
Walls are paper thin (heard bass all night from the Wharf, and could hear neighbors open curtains, start shower, and maids vacuuming at 6am)
Concierge did not know much about cab fares, buses, major attractions (Coit tower, Giants ballgame, etc.) I could find out more on my own by searcing interent.
"Sleep Number bed" did not function (which was part of the reason we chose this hotel)
Got charged 85 cents/local call
Tub and sink drains were not connected, toilet did not flush
All in all this is probably an alright stay for single travellers...not a place for couples and sleeping in/relaxing. My wife would not stay here again, BUT I would if I was just going partying with some buddies. We stayed at the Marriot last year which was much better...I would pay the extra to get somehwere nicer.

title: “The best hotel”
text:
My mum and I stayed here for four nights mid November 2007. I booked after reading all the reviews on Trip Advisor I thought that many people can't be wrong, they wern't. There is a reason this hotel is rated No.1 in New York on so many websites.
What can I say. Our room was small but perfectly formed with everything we needed to make our stay comfortable, Iron & ironing board, huge shower, hair dryer, air con, huge tv etc etc, 
The 2nd floor lounge provided us with a 'free' plentifull breakfast and snacks and coffee 24hours a day and even better in the evening 'again free' wine with cheese and biscuits. The free internet access is a great idea if you have to check your emails we just used it for checking the times of one of the trips we had organised. 
This is one of the best hotels I have ever stayed in and I stay in a few with work all over its just like nothing I have stayed in before, its not flash or ultra modern its also not one of these hotels where you feel like you are walking on eggshells everywhere. 
The staff were superb and on hand any time of day to help, advise, make dinner reservations or simply open the door for you. I appreciate good service and going the extra mile when I see it. The thing is this hotel doesn't need all ritz and glamour its just perfect the way it is. 
The location is fabulous right in the centre of manhattan so its perfect for exploring uptown as well as downtown its also pretty close to 5th avenue which is handy for last minute shopping.
I am happy to say that this little hotel made our stay in New York that bit more special we felt extremely valued customers not just a number like you do in some bigger group hotels.
You must try the itlaian next door as well we ate there one night and it really was quite good.
I would certainly recommend this hotels to all my friends and family if they were going to New York.

title: “Loved the Fairmont”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Fairmont for 2 nights. The location was fantastic and we found it easy to walk to all of Dallas' downtown attractions from her (6th floor museum, pioneer plaza, west end, etc.). More importantly we felt safe walking in the vicinity of the hotel at night which is something we hadn't felt at other locations in Dallas. The hotel itself was beautiful and felt very luxurious. Staff were friendly and helpful.

title: “Great value for your buck”
text: This Hilton hotel is in a very convenient place for touring both midtown and the lower parts of NYC. The accommodation is more than decent, professional staff, and good breakfast. Look out for the discounts, prices change on a daily basis, and when you catch them - the price is excellent for the value.

title: “Very nice stay!”
text: My husband and I took a Chinatown Bus from Washington DC to Philadelphia for a vacation. The bus stop was a few blocks away from the hotel. We arrived before check in and they held our luggage. The hotel is across the street from City Hall and Macy's. It was decorated very nice, the staff was friendly, and the room was satisfactory. We had a great view of City Hall. There was no wireless internet, but you could connect for FREE using an Ethernet cable at the desk. The hotel is in a central location to the historic sites and museums or Riddenhouse Square. There is a lot of shopping areas near the hotel too! The great thing about Philadelphia is that there is no tax on clothing or shoes! If you go to the Philadelphia Museum of Art (famous for Rocky running up the stairs), it is about a $10 cab ride (inc. tax) from the hotel. If you enjoy walking, you may walk a lot to see all the historic landmarks and museums, but it is doable from the hotel. We enjoyed our stay at this hotel.

title: “A decent place to lay your head if you are on a budget”
text:
I stayed hear on business in late February. Stayed here since my work only reimburses a limited amount of my travel expenses.
The Good:
- Decent bed and pillows.
- Room has mini-fridge.
- Included breakfast was nice.
- Free cocktail hour for priority club members.
- Friendly and helpful staff
- Free shuttle to/from the airport
Downsides:
- This location is quite far from the convention center.
- Homeless are all over the streets near this hotel after 7pm.
- Rooms are SMALL
- Walls are THIN (could hear the neighboring room's whining child)
- Hotel feels a bit old and poorly cared for. Rooms were okay, but the overall atmosphere was underwhelming.

title: “Nice Hotel, secluded - a bit nosiy”
text:
Stayed here for one night. Front desk clerk was friendly and we got checked into our room quickly. Used the business center but it was so hot in there that I cut my business short. Room was clean with a GREAT bed. 
Dinner was good with beef stroganoff, noodles and salad. Free beer and wine was nice. No wine glasses - only plastic cups.
Room was nice - bed was very comfortable. Our room was on the 2nd floor and was right across the parking lot from a restaurant/bar called "Sam's Boat". Woke up around midnight with the sound of loud music and voices. If you are going to stay, don't stay on that side. 
Eggs at breakfast were cold and breakfast was served on styrofoam plates with plastic forks and spoons... I stay at lots of Homewood Suites and this is the first one that I have stayed in that did not provide glass plates and regular silverware. At most Homewood Suites, the staff comes around during meals and askes how they are doing with room and meals. Did not see any management at all at the hotel. Just didn't feel "friendly". Location is pretty secluded and is about 1/2 mile from any of the shops. 
I probably would not stay here again.

title: “Good location for business travel, but way over priced!”
text: I stayed at this Marriott due to its proximity to where I was working in the Tech Center. The hotel was okay, but very much over priced. Also i had a room with a window facing indoors, this was very loud as you could hear everyone below in the courtyard area. The staff were very friendly so no complaints there, but there are better places in the area for the money.

title: “quintessentially San Fransisco”
text: We are from Australia and stayed at The Majestic for 3 nights. Booked a standard room but were offered an upgrade upon check in by the friendly staff. We booked The Majestic via the internet as it represented to us what San Fransisco is all about. The Majestic didn't fail to impress, the rooms were lovely, being a small boutique hotel the service was way above average(especially Tim the barman, he's THE BEST!) We have travelled extensively for the past 15 years within the USA so have experienced many, many hotels and motels in about 7 states, this was the most enjoyable stay we have experienced as the character and style of the Majestic is unique and relaxing. The free wine and hors'd'ouvres offered between 4 and 6pm in the lobby is a nice treat. Max the concierge is helpful and obliging. Pacific Heights is very handy to the city with cheap public transport in any direction. It is very quiet and away from the hustle and bustle of the noise of the city but close enough to walk to if your feeling enegetic. The hills are quite steep but take a bus for $1.50 if you dont feel like walking, your ticket lasts for 2 hours in any direction, very cheap and the buses come every couple of minutes. Great restaurants in Filmore and Bells Market is only one block away for freshly made food and supermarket supplies of any kind.

title: “Fun hotel”
text:
We stayed here for a week and had a fantastic stay.
The beds and pillows are extremely soft and comfortable, the rooms spotlessly clean and well decorated, with a well stocked mini bar, TV, DVD and games console. A really nice touch is the wine hour.
Bur best of all are the staff, they are great and the doormen Steve, Kevin, Brett and the others whose names we didn't get, are worth a special mention, you couldn't get better. We also want to thank Jose for topping up our wine glasses, thanks very much.
Excellent hotel and well positioned to see SF.

title: “No space for the shopping bags and offensive service!”
text: I stayed at the Hudson Hotel with my husband. We were expecting a very small room, which is certainly what we got, but we won't be booking such a small room again. It was so small it was actually a bit of a health hazard. I banged my head on the tv a few times while getting out of bed! The only advantage of the size of the room was that it stayed very hot, so if you want to be assured of a hot room in Nov/Dec in New York book this hotel. Our main gripe was the offensive service from the security guy manning the lifts at the lobby. For some reason he singled out my husband to ask to see our room key, but did not ask any of the other 15 people waiting for the lifts. It was extremely embarassing as other guests noticed what was happening and the same guy did this a few times. We complained to reception and were told that the manager would speak to us the following day, however on returning to our room the following day a tray had been left with 2 bottles of water and 2 apples with an apology note from the shift manager - not an acceptable apology particularly when my husband continued to be singled out! It is disappointing that this incident spoiled our opinion of the hotel as the actual reception staff were friendly and helpful. I have stayed in various hotels in New York and this is the only hotel I would not recommend based on the size of the room and service.

title: “Fantastic Value, location and staff”
text: This was my second visit to the Orchid Suites, and just like the first time we we're not disappointed. If you are after luxury then this is not the place for you, but if you are after fantastic location and value then this is perfect! I think it is better than any standard hotel because it is like a home away from home. We had the executive suite and paid around $119 per night. We had two queen beds, large flatscreen t.v, 4 seater dining table and a full kitchen. It is fantastic, escpecially if you want to save money by not eating out every night. It backs on to the Hollywood Highland mall and is about a 50 metre walk from Hollwood Boulevard. All in all, would definatly reccommend.

title: “Carlyle Suites was awesome!”
text: I stayed at the Carlyle Suites during the Thanksgiving holiday. I had a wonderful experience, the staff was very nice and informative and the rooms were spotless. I love the "art deco meets modern" theme in the rooms. And the small kitchen was a great place to prepare breakfast. I would definitely stay there again!

title: “Good base for exploring the city”
text: The hotel is in an excellent location, and it is a relatively easy walk to the harbour, Boston Common and most of the historical sites. There are also plenty of restaurants nearby. Rooms are a good size, are very comfortable and with all the facilities you would expect. Large bathroom with excellent shower. Efficient and friendly staff. If you are looking for a base to explore the city this is highly recommended.

title: “Under-W-helmed”
text: The hotel is well located and clean but the rooms have a lot of problems. 1) Bathroom door is too heavy to close 2) Poor lighting over the vanity 3) If you want a coffee pot you have to request one 4) No exhaust fan in the bathroom 5) The elevators stink with incense sticks 6) No thermostat in the room.

title: “Very Expensive for what you get!”
text:
We booked this hotel for a conference. It's a historic hotel, old and if you are use to the confort of a new hotel and the space that comes with it, the Allerton is not for you.
I won't recommend this hotel for a family, the rooms are pretty small, elevators are super small (you feel like in Europe) and on top of everything they charge more that newer hotels.
They also charged for just using the fridge to storage my toddlers milk!
Staff was ok, not super friendly. 
It is very well located but not worth the price. After the 3rd night we moved to a different hotel that included a buffet breakfast, pool and the valet parking was half of the cost of the Allerton

title: “Fantastic room, fabulous service, awesome locale”
text:
I booked this hotel after reading the reviews and a sweet deal from bookit.com. My husband and I had never been to Cali. We had a wonderful vacation and the hotel had a lot to do with it. The location was FABULOUS! Chinatown was an easy walk as was union square and the $2 cable cars and meeting our bus tour. We asked for an upgrade and were abliged! We had a nice, clean, very comfy room with a nice view on the 15th floor. It was sooo quiet. We were even greeted when we came back from dinner with complementary champagne and chocolate strawberries for our 10th wedding anniversary. Jaron checked us in and was very friendly. I had a friend leave a package for us and they did not forget it. The room was very quiet at night. We really like air blowing on us so we asked if they had a fan and they did! 
We took the Bart rail from the airport without any problems. We rode the trolley and the cable cars all week with no problems getting anywhere! There is a 7/11 Convenience store, Wallgreens, CVS, Subway, McDonalds all across the street or around the corner. Shopping is Kate Spade, Burberry, Prada... We never made it to Yerba Buena Mall right behind our hotel. There was a small ice skating rink in Union Square for Thanksgiving week (I imagine its there for the holidays). 
We don't care for feather pillows, but all the hotels have them.
We did not use anything from the mini bar but had to question a charge on our bill for mini bar usage.
But we LOVED it!! We would highly recommend this to anyone!!

title: “The Uptmost Quality, Service, Location, Decor, for the price. I dare anyone to find a better hotel for the same price!”
text:
I had a 4 night 5 day stay at The Hotel Belleclaire and it was everything that my strict and high expectations could ask for. The Hotel was extremely clean. The staff is extremely polite and always wants to help you. The room is very quaint in size but superbly designed. I stayed in the deluxe queen room, and everything from the bed to the bathroom was brand new, dark wood tones, and very inviting. Service was beyond comprehension. I had a question about the safe in the room so i asked on the way to my room if someone can tell me how to use it. The staff member said "I'll send one up to assist you sir". My room is on the 2nd floor. The staff member that was sent up beat me there. It was incredible(now i believe in precognition). 
Overall it is the best hotel for the money, no complaints at all except they do have the worst irons known to man( put water for steam, ends up all over the place). That is the only thing i can come up with. 
The location is excellent... right in the city and little to no city noise.
There are very convenient stores located all around. Blocks from central park, and right across the street is The Manhattan Diner... It is rated by Trip Advisor as the best diner in the city and let me tell you it could possibly be the best diner on the planet... Everything from the service to the plethora of food choices( my favorites are curly fries, rice pudding, shakes, cheese cake, waffles.... who am I kidding everything is delicious) is so timely, inexpensive, and just a joy to be there.
Trust me... You'll fall in love with it... you will want to write a review just like this. It is that good.

title: “Perfect Location, Hip n Happening”
text: This boutique hotel is right on Dupont Circle....in a great neighbourhood with tons of restaurants, embassy mansions, a 24 hour pharmacy, gardens etc. We only had to take the metro a few times as you can walk everywhere (cabs and traffic are a nightmare in DC!). Our room was modern and stylish, when we arrived the door handle on the shower stall was broken and one of the ceiling lights was burnt out (they fixed the shower handle the next day but the light was never repaired. The staff were great.....offering lots of tips for restaurants etc. My only compliant is that aside from the room repairs, if you want a bathtub instead of just a shower stall you better book way in advance as those rooms are limited.

title: “Just keeps getting better!”
text:
We stay at this motel whenever we visit our daughter in San Diego. It is centrally located, and a great value. Since our last stay, they've knocked out a few walls and expanded the breakfast room to include more seating and 2 waffle machines. The staff is great, especially Randy, the night auditor. I think he's a stand-up comedian wanna be!
The motel is across from a shopping center. Also, if you make a right out of the parking lot, and go about 8 blocks, there is another shopping center on your left with a new Trader Joe's. We stopped here several times to pick up salads and sandwiches.

title: “Customer Service was the best I've experienced in a Long Time.”
text:
Upon arriving at the Embassy Suites Hotel in Downtown Indianapolis, a valet assisted us immediately with unloading luggage, large cooler and many bags. He told us to leave our car right where we had parked it and directed us to the registration desk. He had our luggage and all other items to our suite within just minutes of our arrival. 
For anyone who has not stayed at an Embassy Suites, the rooms surround an atrium which in this hotel was 20 floors of open, bright and sunny space. Beautiful plants and flowers were everywhere. Clean floors, polished brass, everything was clean and bright. The suite was wonderful. Very large "living room" included a 'fridge, microwave, wetbar and coffee maker. A large LCD TV in the living room, Wi-Fi. The couch opened to a double bed if needed (which we did not). The very large bedroom included a comfy bed and really fabulous pillows. (Where did they find those pillows? I want some here at home.) A large LCD TV was in the bedroom plus a sink, mirror and magnifying mirror. The bathroom was very modern in appearance with tub/shower combo, hair dryer. The suite felt very luxurious. Loved it!
But the best part of this hotel is the customer service. Very customer focused and friendly employees. I had contact with 4 different front desk staff during our stay and everyone of them responded to my questions and needs as if I was the most important person that they had talked to in days. The bartender was very pleasant and friendly even with our late arrival ~ after 10 hours of driving, the excellent amaretto sour hit the spot perfectly. Embassy Suites offers a hot breakfast and everyone of the employees keeping the breakfast area clean and stocked were friendly, helpful and fast. It was a very nice experience with not a grumpy employee anywhere to be seen. 
We will be staying at this hotel in the future and I am really looking forward to that stay.

title: “Great place to stay !”
text:
This is definitely a great place to stay. It is right in downtown of san Diego, next to beautiful marina, historic ship and sites... Ralph grocery store is just in a walking distance. Love the way they treat customers at the lobby: two big glass jars of water with fresh cut strawberries every day, hand lotions, warm towettes.... Staffs are nice, helpful. The room is spacious, clean and has great view. Vallet parking is a big plus - fast and efficient. Wireless service charges 12.95/day (wish it is free like other places). we did not use the pools but had a glance throu it - really nice.
Generally, it is a nice place to stay wherer you can walk around without getting headache of looking for parking lots.

title: “Good Value for money”
text: We stayed at the newly renovated Westin Waterfront in August for 3 nights using the cash +points. The lobby was pleasant and it gives you a feeling of well maintained property immediately.The check in was smooth and we got upgraded to a City view. The room was clean, good size, and the everything was in working order. I must say the bed was the most comfortable bed we had on this trip. Although the location in not in the center , it was very close to the subway stop and taxi is always available. For the rate we were paying, it was very good value for the money. You can save on the rate and use it on taxi fare instead of paying lot of money for the dated downtown property.

title: “Washington Plaza Hotel - Excellent”
text:
We came up for the weekend of Oct 8/9th, after finding this hotel online and then checked it on here. This hotel is great!! The hotel staff was professional, took their time and were great in holding our bags for us after checking out to getting us a cab on the way back to Union Station. The rooms were extremely clean and the beds were very comfortable. The hotel is in walking distance to the White House & the other monuments and is in a great location (safety wise). 
Another perk to the hotel is that all the rooms are smoke free!!!
I will definitely stay here again on my next trip to DC!

title: “Good service but decor getting tired”
text: Have stayed here every year now for several years. First the bad stuff; at our last stay, in May of 2010, noticed how the room carpet needed a good clean. This year May 2011, the carpets appear still not to have been cleaned but also need replacing. The bathroom had black mold by the shower on the floor. Pool was closed for our stay. Hotel was designed with either too slow elevators or not enough elevators...wait can be long. Now the good stuff; great service and attitude (especially room service). Hip hotel with good location on P Street...but time for remodel please....will not stay again until this happens.

title: “Close....but so far”
text:
Arrived at this location on a Thursday afternoon for a 3 night stay (A conference here).
Lobby from Parking lot had a very heavy scent like men's after shave. A Ghost? Same scent every day....was it their cleaning products?
Room was ready and staff was friendly and HELPFUL, Bellman who brought luggage to the room asked if we needed suggestions for restaurants in the area and advised us the Space Shuttle was going to complicate road travel.
Room #922 had an odd odor that my roomie described as 'peepee'. I did not catch it but it was not a pleasantly fragranced room.
Why do they build hotels without exhaust fans???? Had to shower with the door open.
HORRID water pressure in sink and shower. Very poor hot water.
Rose at 6 for my swim - pool is not heated it was a while to get used to it. After my laps went to the hot tub - of the 10 jets, 5 did not work.
Returning from our Thursday activities at 10pm our keys did not work.... and then made new keys. (Each evening of our stay we had to have keys recertified.... OUR room was provided as part of the conference we attended so we were concerned we were being effected by the conference's finances.
Workout room was basic....very basic, missing equipment was common.
Continental breakfast was common, Starbucks coffee was almost bitter, but the pastries were fresh.
Looks pretty outside but is just a place to sleep....there would be no reason to 'go there' unless you were in the travel business.

title: “Cheap Grand Canyon vacation”
text: Very out dated inn but great for the poor college student--it's clean but definitely not pleasing to the eye. There are some close by restaurants--nothing really fancy. Although there is a Savers near by and I found a lot of treasures!

title: “The Return”
text:
I was given a room with private bathroom (the type I booked online) that was facing the street (Grant) because it was the only one available at the time that I checked in at approx. 11:30 am. I liked the brightness due to natural sunlight but since it was facing the street, city noise was a constant. The noise was the most disruptive during my 3-night stay, at times being awakened in the middle of the night. Next time, in ANY of my trips, I would remember to try to bring ear plugs, just in case.
My room, just like my first time stay at the hotel in June 2011 visit was adequate for my needs. It was very basic but clean and well kept. There was a box TV (with remote control, this time!) and a refrigerator where I primarily kept water that I purchased from Walgreens. 
The hotel was a reasonable budget lodging during summer time (late August). I always appreciate a clean and safe place to stay for sleep, showering, and staying in to a comfortable bed after a full day of sightseeing and exploring. The price also fit my budget.

title: “Great views!”
text:
This was my second stay at The Magnolia. I love the location, right in the middle of downtown, and the old building, but the best part is the view! Request a corner room, you get three walls of windows looking over downtown! There are a couple drawbacks to the hotel: the carpet needs to be replaced, the elevators are very slow. But the ambiance makes up for it. The staff are generally realy nice and helpful. I went down to the bar area to buy some OJ after breakfast had ended, and Jesus went to the kitchen and brought me two glasses of fresh squeezed for free! 
The shuttle is also great, they took us outside of the stated 5 mile radius. It was so convenient when we went out to dinner not to have to drive! 
There's also celebrities staying there almost constantly. The cast of Prison Break was staying there while we were there, as were the Black Crowes. 
You definitely can't beat the price for such a fantastic hotel!

title: “Book this one!”
text: If you want a change from the corporate blandness of most centrally placed hotels then try the Library. It is a lovely boutique style hotel with lots of nice add-ons like the free breakfast and the pre-dinner drinks and canapés. These are all served in the delightful guest lounge area and its a lovely start to the evening. Rooms can be a bit small, it is Manhattan after all, but are well equipped and very comfortable. As other reviewers have mentioned, the wine bar next door is a great place to dine and always buzzy.

title: “Great Location, Reasonable Hotel”
text:
The location of this hotel is simply not beatable. It is an easy two block walk to the tourist sites in Hollywood. Usually you would have to pay a lot more for a hotel with this location. Having said that, it is Hollywood and not really all that it is made out to be. Be very cautious walking in the Hollywood area at night.
The hotel is clearly an older property and most of the styling is very old and dated. The carpets have about had it and everything has seen better days. However, the rooms were clean and comfortable and offered good wi-fi, microwaves and mini fridges. The room I stayed in had a shower that was very nice but no tub. Some of the rooms look out into a middle courtyard with the pool and all seemed to offer sliding glass doors. Breakfast was nothing to write home about as it was very basic, but it was free.
Overall the hotel is worth the money as the location just cant be beat for the price I paid. I dont think you can expect a four or five star hotel when you are paying just over $100 a night in Hollywood. This is a perfectly good hotel as long as you realize it is a Days Inn and not the W. Set your expectations accordingly and you will be fine.

title: “Bland but clean rooms in a central location”
text: Although the hotel is an attractive, historical building when viewed from its exterior, neither the rooms nor the lobby have preserved much of the past. The rooms are for the most part tasteful but bland, and the primary reason to stay here would be its central location and cleanliness. There is no view to speak of whether your room faces Walnut, 17th St or the back of the property. The staff are not that personable.

title: “Don't stay here if the forecast is rain”
text:
We stayed at the Renaissance Seattle in late August. We were upgraded to a Junior Suite on the Executive Floor. The first night was great and the room was decent.
The second night we were awoken by dripping water from the ceiling. The rain outside was being funneled into our room. The water was spilling over the wardrobe onto the counter and flooding our carpet. We called maintenance and they told us that this happens every time it rains. They instructed us to ask for more towels from Housekeeping and used all our room towels to soak up the deluge. The hotel did refund us the night however, I wouldn't stay there if the forecast is rain. It is possible that the issue was only in our room however the ceiling of the cafe on the 2nd floor showed clear water damage.

title: “Value for money”
text: The hotel is not in a good location, accosted for money by down and outs just going to local shop. But the room we had was very nice and clean. Shuttle to and from hotel and airport good. The night manager was lovely and very helpful. Would stay again but not go to shops at night. Very cheap to stay here so can't complain about value for money.

title: “Avoid the noise!”
text: This hotel is suffering from an identity crisis. Over the weekends, the hotel host a disco on the roof. The noise from the disco can be heard throughout the hotel. We were on the sixth floor and could feel the music in our room. We have stayed in numerous hotels wtih roof top activities and night clubs in the hotelsm, however, we have never experience this much noise. When we booked, we were told there could be slight noise. What they should have said was that there will be extreme noise everywhere until 2 am. Our suggestion would be the avoid the noise!

title: “WOW. First class.”
text: The minute you walk into the hotel you will be very pleased. The room and amenities wonderfull. We had a young guest that used the sofa bed that was very comfortable and the room had a second bathroom that was great.The return to our room after dinner was a surprise desert and a card we had mentioned to the desk on check in a birthday and it was a big hit! Room service was great for breakfast arrived on time and the food was great.We also loved the area for shopping and resturants near the hotel. I will return very soon.

title: “Not much. Yuck”
text: My family and I stayed here in July. Outside exterior next to a loud busy highway, no view. Please keep looking.

title: “Nice staff, but hotel needs help”
text: Staff kindly accomodated our requests to move away from the elevator and have the air shut off in our absolutely frigid room. HOWEVER - our room ("with a view") overlooked the highway, which becomes quite noisy at 5 am (at least there was no game at Fenway across the street, check first!). The wall safe crashed to the floor when we opened the closet door. The bathroom has no fan and no windows, so that gets unpleasant. The mattress creaks horribly. And the internet is slow and not free ($13/day) and doesn't reach to the 6th floor (although you can jack Fenway's network across the highway). Breakfast is fine and is in the Japanese restaurant downstairs. The business center is $15/half hour UNLESS you're printing a boarding pass, which is free. With so many other hotels in Boston, why stay here? It's back to the Kendall for us.

title: “some good, some not so good”
text:
Chose this hotel for one night in Dallas. Upside: Price was right. Alfredo, the night clerk was extremely helpful, as was Jesus for breakfast in the morning. Room was clean. 
Downside: No water pressure in the shower. Only got good water pressure when we turned the water to the full on position which was very hot. In-room, complimentary internet access was non-existant. At least we couldn't access the net and there were no instructions in the room. Since we're not techies, we did without. We asked for a room on the first floor. Although the place was almost empty, they gave us a room facing out, rather than into the courtyard. Very disappointed in this since our room had a patio door leading onto the parking lot. I would expect that unless requested, or unless the hotel was full, they'd assign inward facing first floor rooms FIRST. Then fill in with outward facing rooms as needed. As otheres have said about this hotel, either the televisions or the beds are in the wrong place. You need to lay on your side to watch from bed.
All in all, it's an okay place, and we'd probably stay there again, but will shop around before staying again.

title: “A hotel with a great atmosphere”
text: This hotel feels very European. It has a lot of charm and feels quaint. But you should only stay here if you like old-style , well-preserved hotels and rooms and appreciate that style. It has plenty of charm and the rates were very reasonably. I´d definitely stay at the Majestic again.

title: “Good hotel, great location”
text: The hotel is very good. The rooms are big with clean bathrooms. It is close to the convention center, the theater, and a varied collection of restaurants and bars. The staff was friendly and helpful. I asked to change rooms and they were very accommodating. The best restaurant/bar in the area is Majerle's. They have good burger's and it is a great place to watch a game.

title: “Nice new hotel in great area”
text: This is a nice hotel that has either recently been renovated. My room was clean with a large bed and small 'foyer'. Bathroom was clean and had a sliding pocket door instead f a traditional door which really helped with space. Staff was almost too professional made them sound like robots reciting a speech. Overall a good experience and would stay there again. Hotel is right next to a Club so the bar was actually hopping.

title: “Oh, the views!”
text: We got an excellent rate by using our AAA card, and were astounded at how beautiful the room was. We had views that were to die for. We spent 2 nights here and both nights enjoyed cocktails in the hotel bar, and used the concierge recommendations for dining. Very pleased with everything including the wonderful bath products, the coffee maker in the room featuring Starbucks coffee, and the great reading lights over the bed.

title: “Not as nice as you would expect for a Marriott”
text: Hotel is Right off of the highway, which is nice, however the surrounding neighborhood is very sketchy. The hotel is obviously built in the 60s, and they have redecorated the rooms, but it is still obviously an old hotel. Despite this, I paid over hundred dollars a night for the weekend that I was there. The weekday rates were more reasonable, but still overpriced for the overall quality.

title: “Four Stars, You Kidding?”
text: What does it take to get a 4 star rating? Not much here. Staff was friendly, bell hop was rude. The door to the bathroom the paint was peeling. The room was very small and old looking. BUT,the view was AWESOME and was the only thing 4 stars. I've stayed at Comfort and Sleep Inns that were nicer. This isn't what I consider a 4 star hotel. If you park at the hotel, it will cost you $48.00 per day. We parked at O'Hare Airport in the $9.00 parking lot and took the L-train to the hotel. It was my first time riding the L-train and it was a great experience and tons of fun. It takes about and hour to go from the airport to the hotel on the train. We stayed on the 28 floor and you could hear every siren from every emergency vehicle that was going downtown. That was a shock. Don't expect to get a quiets night sleep. Too much money to stay here. No benefits.

title: “another great experience”
text: Stayed here in jan 2012 again because our first experience was so great. We had a 23 hour layover in Denver as our flights were changed and this provided us with a amazing breakfast and shuttle to and from the airport and the surrounding area. There is a mall close by with a comdey improv but we arrived to late to take advantage of that great opportunity and nor did we get to take in the managers reception. The mall has a bass pro shop that kids and adults loved, even my husband who hates to shop. The mall also has a target and a varitey of dining and shopping places. The shuttle drivers were great by filling us in on the attractions in the area and what the hotel had to offer. A bit more than i like to pay but if you are gonna be here for a while without a car it is well worth it. Its located in a commercial area but the shuttle offers great service. The rooms were great as we had my husband and I and our daughter and son who had a friend. The bathroom seperates the 2 rooms and with 3 mirrors and a frig area everyone had plenty of room to get ready.

title: “Too small, too expensive”
text: This hotel is vastly overpriced for what it delivers, even by New York standards. The room was so small that I felt claustrophobic. The internet didn't work but I got charged for it anyway.

title: “Great place to stay”
text: Wife and I really liked our stay at the Mariott. Everyone was very friendly and helpful. The rooms were very clean.

title: “Solid Hotel For Work, Not Play”
text:
Overall, the W City Center meets, but does not exceed expectations. I stayed there for 5 nights and didn't have one issue with the service or amenities.
That being said, if you were in Chicago on pleasure, you might want to go elsewhere. First off, the location isn't fantastic, as it's in the heart of downtown and the surrounding area is dead. Additionally, the lobby bar doesn't provide much of a diversion (although the decor is awesome).
If you're looking to go out, you should check in with one of the concierges. The ones on staff when I was there had a pretty sound knowledge of nightlife. Although, make sure you're specific about what you're looking for. During my stay I had one arrange bottle service at club no too far from the hotel, and it ended up sucking pretty terribly. I blame this more on myself though, as clubs in Chicago suck in general and I shouldn't have asked about going to one. The bar scene in Chicago is awesome and the clubs tend to attract "clubby" people - you know, the crew cut and slacks crowd.

title: “Why stay at the big box hotels when you can stay at the Rex?”
text:
I attended a software conference at the Moscone Center last week. The conference hotels were the usual suspects at Union Square: Hilton, Marriott, Palace, Westin. When I saw the Tripadvisor reviews for these places I thought why should I (or rather my company) pay all this money to stay at a mediocre big box hotel. So I booked at the highly rated Rex and was glad I did. They upgraded us to a King Executive which was roomier. The bed was extremely comfy; the hotel was quiet at night. Friendly service, nice breakfast room, convenient valet service...and about $60 less than the big boxes.
Slight dings were the musty odor another reviewer mentioned (in the hallways and in the room) and incomplete housekeeping. I didn't get the shampoo replenished for 2 days and then had to ask. Also, didn't get bath towels one day and had to ask. However, these are small things.
Hotel Rex is the best.

title: “great location, not expensive”
text:
We stayed at the Astoria hotel for 5 days. it has a great location, right next to the Chinatown gate and minutes away from the union square (shopping....).
There is a free wi-fi in the "conference" room (there is nothing there but a big table, chairs, sofas and one TV). You can buy your food and eat there as well.
The room is small, but you can manage your way there. A small sink and not the best soaps in the world (but it's really not a big deal)
The front desk's people were bit apathetic but didn't influence on our trip.
It was quite, no noise from the hallway or from other rooms. No sense of insecurity and a nice Starbucks across the street

title: “The perfect escape”
text:
We've been to New York 3 times and each time stayed at this hotel - I simply cannot say enough good things about it! We arrived at 12.30am - straight to the 2nd floor lounge for a hot chocolate and biscuit before bed. It's those little comforts that make you want to go back time and again. The bed is super comfortable and the bathroom spacious by New York standards. The wine and cheese at night, bagels, fresh fruit and coffee for breakfast give you the energy to keep on going in this city that never sleeps!
Excellent location just a block from Grand Central and easy walking distance to pretty much everything...stay here - I hope you love it as much as we do!

title: “Average Hotel but Good for Low Price”
text:
Just got back from a two-night stay that I booked through Priceline for $125/night. I was worried, as I needed two beds and others using Priceline had trouble. Yes, when you call the hotel directly to request a specific room type they are rude and unhelpful. The know darn well that Priceline does not allow users to specify room type, but they act stupid and say “You’ll get what ever room Priceline has requested for you.”…thanks.
Anyway, upon check in we got a room on the 16th floor with two doubles. The room size was pretty good for NYC. There was a large closet and dresser, plus desk and chair. The furnishings weren’t brand new but were fine for the price. The bathroom was actually really nice. It was quite large for NYC and looked like it was recently renovated. It was all granite (floor, walls), and a very sparkly white tub/tiles. The caulk was not moldy (usually most hotels have some kind of mold) and the shower worked great and the tub drained!! (I hate it when tubs drain slowly), also there were lots of mirrors. I think we had a handicapped accessible room.
Some front desk people where helpful, others wouldn’t even make eye contact and treated you as if you were interrupting their lives (this without even knowing we booked through Priceline.) Concierge was only knowledgeable about very mainstream activities. We asked where the main shopping drag was in Chelsea, we prefer funky shopping to big department stores, she didn’t know and told us there was no shopping in Chelsea (she was wrong).
Other than that, it was just a Hilton as another reviewer said... nothing great, not horrible either. For $125/night, I think it was a good deal. It was reasonable clean and quiet with above average bathroom in our room. However, I wouldn’t want to pay their regular rates, I’d stay somewhere else.

title: “lovely stay at the Meridien”
text: We stayed at Le Parker Meridien April 2003 for a week. We took our two sons 18 and 16 and my parents a special treat for their 45th wedding anniversary.The hotel was very well located for shopping and had easy access to the subway for sightseeing.The position of the hotel made me feel at ease to allow my sons to wonder around New York at their own pace as well as my parents.The hotel was extremely friendly and the rooms were very comfortable. My parents enjoyed the pool /sunbathing area in the afternoons while the younger generation did their own thing.The burger bar was extremely useful for my sons and the restaurant/bar was lovely to come back to after a busy day around New York to sit and relax in.I would recommend this hotel for any one and I look forward to returning in the near future

title: “not again”
text:
The lobby looks very old (especially the curtains behind the front desk). We booked a junior suite with a bedroom, living room, dining area, and a kitchen through booking.com but we were given a one-room suite. The bathroom was too small and furniture was dusty. The kitchen fridge had scratches all over and the kitchen cabinets were made from aluminum and they were dusty too! When we objected the front desk was not helpful till the manager got involved (who we thank a lot), we were given a better room (I don’t know why we were not given this room from the beginning!). 
All 2 beds suite (including the 2 we stayed in) are located near the service storage cabinet. The cleaning ladies start slamming the cabinet door from 6 am, very frequently! 
Heating system “automatically” works when temperature reaches 42 F (5 C) regarding of how cold the guests feel. When we asked for extra blankets and pillows, the blanket had holes and the guy who got them to us was very rude and picking his nose while getting them to us, of course we refused to take them! One day the water was cut off of the entire hotel for around an hour. We then were given a really small heater. 
No free Internet access and the wireless was not available on all floors. When we asked to get the wireless after we moved to the other room, we’ve been told that we will be charged again!! Also, they charge you per computer! 
What’s good about the hotel: location, recycling awareness, and free Internet access to airlines website and boarding pass printing. The hotel is over priced and I will never stay here again nor recommend it to friends.

title: “Non Driver”
text: we have just returned to the UK after spending 14 nights at the abovel hotel. As I do not drive during my visits to the united states this hotel was a great location for us . The MTA No.6 bus took you from outside the hotel to Fashion Valley Transit/Mall with access to the Trolly Green Line and return to the hotel using the MTA No.25 or 41 or the No.6 from Oldtown Area all stop outside the hotel reception area. Should you want to walk its a 10 minute walk to the mall/transit area. The hotel provided a first class service and also provide free transport to and from the airport.All staff were very helpful. For anyone coming over from the UK relax and let the Metropolition Transit System do the driving and keep onto your no claims discount.

title: “Still struggling...low end of the Luxury Collection standards”
text:
I've stayed here a few times, when it was a Westin and 3 times as the Fairfax. I think it was time for a major refurbishment, but the present day Westin decor didn't match the architecture and feeling of the property so they went for Luxury Collection. I think they get a C- all around.
Staff at the door, when they are there are lackluster on a good day. The front desk is small with room for only two people at a time and I rarely get a real greeting, just the usual "ID and credit card please". The property just loaded some nicer stuff in the bathrooms and cleaned the place up, but they ignore the aesthetic repairs in the rooms as in chipped doors and trim, etc. The rooms vary widely but are generally not that big and therefore do not lend themselves to a luxury feel. This just does not hit what you expect from luxury collection. The only thing going for it is the location. As long as you don't need to be in the middle of government center, you are a hop from Georgetown, Dupont circle, DCA and where ever else you want to go. Unless I get a great rate, it's not worth the price.

title: “We had a very memorable stay and all for the right reasons”
text: The staff where exceptional, alwasy pleasant, always smiling and offering assistance.

title: “Small room but great location”
text: Rooms are probably ok for one adult but not two and a toddler! I'm afraid very small and moving about proved to be a challenge. Rooms are pricey here but they are very well kept and the furnishings are of high quality. Would only stay here and sacrifice space available if a good deal was going.

title: “Great place to stay”
text:
My wife and I just returned from a long week-end stay at the Orchard. We chose the Orchard because of the reviews and rating on Trip Advisor and we were not disappointed. For the price, the location is great and the rooms are very clean and comfortable. 
The cable car is just at the corner and the bus stop to the Fisherman's Wharf is a five minutes walk. We had rented a vehicle but hardly used it since parking is expensive and hard to find. We used Valet parking for $40 a day. We were traveling somewhere else after San Francisco and needed a car, otherwise you don't need it if you're just staying in San Francisco. The transit system is very good.
There is a very good cafe just around the corner and a good pizza parlor just across the street if you don't mind the wait (long lineup). Union Square is also very closeby for shopping.
The hotel provides a nice collection of DVD's to watch in your room and a wireless connection (Wi-Fi). If you don't have your laptop, there is a complimentary computer in the lobby to surf the internet or check e-mails.
Although very friendly, the staff were not very helpful with the local attractions info and not very good at recommending restaurants.

title: “Great for meetings”
text:
I have to start my review by saying that I did not stay here overnight but was here for 3 days for a meeting ( I live nearby). From a meeting standpoint this is a great hotel. The staff was always friendly and curtious and all the meals were great. 
One concern was with their valet parking. One of the attendants didn't seem like he was awake enough to be driving cars and every morning I had to go inside the hotel to find the valet person. Just doesn't seem to be run with the same standards as the rest of the hotel. 
Otherwise great location and great overall meeting experience.

title: “Dirty, Old, smelly hotel - we are NEVER coming back”
text:
We've arrived on Friday morning 10-10-09 for 2 nights with a 2.5 and a 5 years old.
We had another reservation for the Hilton which we've canceled 24 hours before because at the Millennium reservation center, they convinced us to do so ("great location... right next to toys R us...you wont be sorry...") so when we arrived, after a 40 minuets wait, the receptionist said the room wasn't ready and that we should get back at 4:00PM.
We got back at 4:00 and after a short wait got the keys to the room, when the elevator door opened to our floor I took 3 steps back because of the smell... apparently they put a family of 4 (with 2 small ASTHMATIC kids) in a smokers floor!!! because we forgot to mention we would like a non-smoking room!!!! ( and this is after the reservation center convinced us to stick to this "kids -friendly hotel"!!! and remember this is not a pricline/hotwire reservation, it cost us almost 600$ for those 2 miserable nights)
Make a long story short, after 4 (!!!!) times we called to the manager and bagged to move, she finally agreed to move us to the non-smoking floor but not before 11:30 pm, and again, we are with 2 asthmatic toddlers (which I've mentioned over and over to the manager but besides saying "I'm sorry I can't help you" she didn't do anything)
The smokers room was so dirty, carpet was old, disgusting and had 2 Hugh burned holes in it, a big brown stain on the wall next to the bath, some of the bath tiles were cracked and grout was dirty, it was so smelly that my 2.5 years old son started to cough almost right away, we couldn't stay there for a minute and had to drag the kids until 11:00PM out in the streets.
at 11:20PM we moved into a king room (they promised to bring a folding sofa but of course it took 3 calls and 40 more min. until somebody bothered to bring it).
The next day we couldn't wait to get out of the room (which was much better than the smokers jail but still far far away from even getting close to a 4* hotel - again, a hole in the old carpet, dirty grout, cracked toilet..but at least no cigarettes smell), basically, even the taught of getting back to the hotel in the evening, ruined our whole day, the only good thing in this hotel was the very nice and helpful concierge who recommended on 2 good restaurants.
After we got home I had to wash everything twice in order to get rid of the cigarettes smell...
On Oct. 15 the "Senior Vice President Operations" had the nerve to send us a guest comment card to fill, regarding our hotel experience, I wrote the most horrible review, as expected, nobody bothered to got back... typical...

title: “Stay Far Away”
text:
Recent stay will be our last. First we were put in a large suite with lake views, requested a non smoking room, checked into room, and was sickened by the smell of smoke. Went back to check-in desk and were told again it was a non-smoking room, once we told them there were ashtrays on every table, they moved use to another much smaller but clean room. In the smaller room, the heat did not work, was fixed by a maintenance worker who told us it was blowing air conditioning not heat. Bed was comfortable, bathroom was ok, views from both rooms were terrific. Check-in was a 30 minute wait, 2 people working, and 20 in line. Pool was so bad, even my child wouldn't swim in it. Room service, for 1 sandwich, 1 beer and an omelet, cost $60. Although my family member said the HIlton Sandwich was one of the best he ever had. 
This hotel has a history and beauty almost unrivaled in Chicago, however, it has not been maintained and is now in a sad state of disrepair. MUCH better hotels in Chicago.

title: “Great location, but that's all!”
text:
I had stayed at this hotel twice before, and while there had been a few minor glitches in the past, I decided the hotel deserved another chance, especially because of the great location. I was very wrong! 
I made the reservation for this latest stay 2 months in advance and confirmed all the details with the hotel 1 week prior to arriving. Upon arrival, though, all the previously confirmed details were no where to be found on my reservation. I reserved 2 beds and was given 1. I reserved a smoking room and was given a non-smoking one. The front desk manager said that "a reservation is considered a request and is never guaranteed." She said she would do her best to move us the next day into a smoking room with 2 beds. The next day we were moved.....to another non-smoking room but with 2 beds. After complaining again to the manager, we were moved, finally, to a smoking room with 2 beds.This 3rd room, though, had a malfunctioning sink which made it unusable. This was not fix for 2 days, despite repeated phone calls and in person requests with the front desk.
Throughout all of the problems we had over the 4 days we stayed there we were met with only empty apologies from the manager. No one ever really tried to rectify any of the problems. No one went out of their way to actually provide any customer service. They just smiled and did nothing.
The Millennium Broadway used up their "chances." I will never stay there again (and I'm in New York City 6-8 weeks every year). I used to recommend this hotel to many people who also travel in NYC alot but I will no longer recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: “Great place to stay”
text:
Six of us drove from Toronto for a roadtrip to Chicago the weekend of April 19. After a long drive, we arrived at the hotel greeted by the doorman who was ready and eager to help us with our bags.
The location of the hotel was perfect. Walking distance to everywhere you wanted to go. It was great because i did not want to drive another kilometre while in the City. Had my fill of driving to and fro. Very close the Michigan Ave. Magnificent mile. The hotel is surrounded by restaurants, shopping, nightlife and tourist spots.
Rooms: We had 2 rooms for 6 people and it was perfect. The rooms were clean, tidy and nicely decorated. The HD tvs were a great touch. The towels were soft and the beds were firm. The rooms were on the smaller side.
The staff was friendly and always helpful with directions, recommending restaurants and other points of interest. The hotel offers free continental breakfast every morning which is perfect if you are on the go and complimentary coffe, tea and hot chocolate throughout the day. The lobby is beautiful and welcoming with plenty of places to sit and meet.
Overall, my friends and I had a pleasant experience and I would stay there again.

title: “Nice hotel, good location, maybe not worth the price”
text: Stayed here for almost a week in July, hotel was central to everything right next to Ed Sullivan Theatre (david lettermans tapes his show) and a great cupcake shop.. Went with a group of people we had 2 rooms beds weren't that comfortable compared to Double Tree times square and Marriott Marquis (both I have stayed at during past visits).... Everything was clean a little out dated but you are hardly in your room, 4 girls with huge suit cases fit comfortably in here. If you have never been to New York before you will love this hotel if you have been you won't love it as much as other ones. But for the people we were with this was a good price range for them. Hotel staff was nice and friendly, we took a suburban back to LGA when we left and wow it was so nice and for the same amount as taking a taxi! The driver took his time and wasn't rushed on trying to get us out of the car and make that extra buck (so of course he got tipped better).. The city is great and I love everything about it! convience store right next doork.There is a subway stop right past the Mc'Ds and it will go everywhere on that red line I believe down to canal street, battery park, etc... I have done red bus tour twice and highly recommend it, most of the guides are great, brooklyn tour at night is neat... Also did Statue of Liberty (make sure get tickets in advance) and we missed our actual time to go since we were running behind with a group of 10 but ended up getting put in the short line (so be like 10 minutes late) I recommend Top of the Rock during day and Empire state building at night!

title: “Great location!”
text:
We booked this hotel last minute for a short fall break. I booked I booked 15 days out. Upon check in, the did not have my reservation. I had emailed confirmation. Thank goodness! However it was a very stressful 3-4 hours while I waited for them to get the problem worked out. I didn't know if I should look around for another room or not! The finally called and said or was ok. Too bad the couldn't have done all that while I was there waiting. 
It was in a great location. Just a block from cwnrral park and a 10 minute walk to times aquare. Maid service was the best. Very friendly and great service. 
Comfy bed and no outside noise.

title: “Very impressed, although there were heating/cooling issues”
text:
Very impressed, because we ended up having a really great rate! The front desk wait was pretty long and the lady at the reception really took her time - but overall very friendly.
Free breakfast buffet was AMAZING! 
Free computer/internet terminal was great.
Our room was fine, but my colleagues didn't have heat the first night, and because they "pre-paid" for the room they weren't credited/weren't able to be... but they sent the repair man in and it was all fixed.
Overall great value, great little hotel, location was AMAZING!!!! Walked to all the best shopping and close to subway!

title: “Great Service”
text: Arthur Lormil was very helpful, friendly and went out of his way to make sure things were right. I really appreciate all that he did for me. Michelle Proulx

title: “Superb bang for your buck”
text: Have nothing but great things to say. I was exceedingly pleased and surprisingly so since the price was so reasonable. The staff were totally friendly, helpful and professional. The place was immaculate. The pillows plentiful and just the right blend of soft and firm. Nice area. Close to all kinds of food, etc. walking distance to quite a bit of eateries as well room was great size. Large sitting/office area. Plenty of outlets and lamps. Sink in room with microwave and fridge. Pool was clean and in good repair. Breakfast items plentiful and varied and ms. Paulette will get you whatever you can't find! Small snafu with my arrival date and mgr actually fixed it and saved me money. I have no complaints. I've stayed at far fancier and more expensive hotels and dollar for dollar this best western is is just as good. It's not luxurious. And there is the usual amenities and toiletries available. But you won't be disappointed. Close to lafitness and 24hr fitness.

title: “Perfect for business stays”
text:
I stayed at Candlewood Suites for a 5 night business trip. The room had a full size refrigerator and freezer, a dishwasher, a cooktop, a microwave, and was well stocked with dishes and cooking utensils. The hotel has been renovated since the photos on most of the hotel booking websites were taken. It now has dark wood furnishings and new bathrooms. There is a desk area that is perfect to work from and I was happy with the Internet speed. Additionally, the staff was very friendly throughout my stay. There is a small gym, which I utilized and was satisfied with. 
The only negatives were functions of the type of hotel this is. For example, the chair at the desk area in my room looked like it was the star of a bad slasher movie. It also didn't stay in the correct height position. It wasn't perfect, but it met my needs.
Overall, though, I would definitely stay here again if I had business in the area.

title: “Thin Walls”
text: If large, anonymous hotels with standard equipment placed in non-descript rooms encased in thin plaster walls is your thing - this is the perfect place for you! Well, in all fairness, it's not all THAT bad, but I found out that San Francisco is all about the neighborhoods and boutique hotels. Granted, you may not find them as easily on Hotels or Expedia (or get them assigned through Priceline or Hotwire), but you'll have a much more authentic San Francisco experience at a boutique hotel. Having said that, if you prefer large, run-of-the-mill chain hotels, the Marriott will not disappoint you.

title: “So many better choices than this for downtown Denver”
text: I stayed two nights at the property and was summarily unimpressed. Even though I was on the 18th floor, the street noise was very loud. I am all for public transportation but the ringing bell of the light rail train seared through the windows. On Sunday morning the traffic noise woke me up before 6am. The room was tiny and the bathroom was minuscule ! The rooms are a little tired in decor. I was surprised on how skimpy they were on the bathroom linens (I think because the bathrooms are so small..there's no room for more than two bath towels) and I have had better amenities at a Best Western. The only redeeming factor was the Starbucks in the lobby. If you need your Marriott points, try the Courtyard. Don't pay up for this. Or better yet, find another hotel in town.

title: “College Graduation Weekend - 3 Nights”
text:
I went back to Boston for my daughter's college graduation. Unless you have deep pockets, there is no way you need to spend several hundred dollars a night to stay at this hotel, even during peak.
I want to follow up on my visit to this property. As I once worked around the corner, I already knew the location is was an excellent one, close to both the Orange and Green Line T stations. I did not rent a car for this trip, which probably saved me another $50-$60 night for the car and hotel parking for my 3-night stay.
When I checked out of the hotel this morning, I took the elevator up the second floor and walked to the back of the connected mall, where I exited and walked under Dartmouth Street through a short tunnel that brings you into the Orange Line, Back Bay T station. I took the 'T' to State Street station and picked up the Blue Line T to Airport station, where one minute later a free airport shuttle bus took me to the American Airlines terminal. Couldn't be easier. Alternatively, one could pick up the Green line at either Prudential or Copley station to Government Center and take the Blue Line out to Airport. The hotel is within easy walking distance to all these T stops.
Upon late check in on Saturday evening, staff asked me if I wanted two singles or a king bed. I took the king and was assigned room 1115, which is a great room in excellent condition. I notice the room had a door that would allow it to have an adjoining room for families of four or five members. My only minor complaint with the room, as with most hotels, is that it really doesn't matter if you push the thermostat up or down for more heat or cooling. It appears to be set at 72.5F but it was cool this past weekend, and I really wanted a bit more heat for my very old bones. I really believe the temperature delivered to all rooms on the floor is governed by some master control. The bathroom was small but had a combination tub and shower. There were PLENTY of new, clean wash towels, medium towels, and bath towels. The room had an iron, ironing board, coffee maker with a bit of tea and coffee, hair blow-dryer, and refrigerator (not stocked). There is a Starbucks on the second floor for Starbucks coffee-lovers (not me).
The room had a large flat-panel TV, nice soft bed with nice clean sheets and comforter. Internet connectivity was available for a charge of $12.95 per day (12 noon to 12 noon). The hotel is in the process of renovating the second floor, where it appears they will have two or three new restaurants. For now, they have buffet breakfast and grill type meals on the first floor at Champions Sports Bar. Quite frankly, I believe most people go out to eat in the evening at many of great local restaurants.
The hotel is at least 4* if not 5* in many areas. Once the new restaurants open on the second floor, the hotel will be at least 4^ in my opinion if not higher. Location is definitely 5* if you factor in location and proximity to all the T stops. Shopping is 5* due to proximity to Boylston Street and major brand stores like Apple and Gucci. Attached hotel mall has many, many shops. There is a gigantic Shaw's grocery store directly across from the hotel, where you get numerous food items, deli sandwiches, bakery items, spirits, wine, and beer if you don't feel like going out. Room service is also available if you're lazy.
Champions Sport Bar, located on the first floor of the hotel, serves buffet breakfast and other items throughout the day. Unless you leave the hotel proper, there is no other restaurant at this Marriott. However, it appears that new ones will open on the second floor shortly. I took a shot at the full buffet breakfast on one day of my 3-day stay. The price is $19.95 for what they call the ‘All-American Breakfast’. For this offering, they have an omelet station, sausages, scrambled eggs, bacon, French toast, Belgian waffles, seasonal fruits, smoked salmon, hot oatmeal, cereals, breads, and pastries. By far, it wasn’t the best buffet breakfast I have ever eaten but adequate. Considering the location, you will not find much cheaper. If you’re not up for all that food, they have the ‘Good Start Breakfast’ for $14.95, which includes most of the above except the omelet station, scrambled eggs, sausages, bacon, and smoked salmon. Last, they offer the ‘Healthy Start Breakfast’, which offers breakfast breads and pastries. All three offerings include unlimited coffee, tea, juices and milks, which can be considerable add-ons at other restaurants. Children between the ages of 4-12 (at this writing) will be charged $4.95. Hours for the buffet are from 6:30 – 11:00 a.m.
I booked this hotel a couple weeks in advance for $110/night through a popular bidding for travel web site that uses Priceline.
TIP: If you’re going to be in Boston from for up to a week, get yourself a 7-day transportation pass for $15 at Airport Station (Blue Line), when you take the free shuttle from the airport to the Blue Line (Airport Station). It’s good for buses and the subway (all lines including the Silverline). You will save a small fortune over renting a car or taking a taxi. Boston public transportation is quite good.
Local Transportation - 5* (Get a Charlie Card or 7-Day pass)
Hotel Location - 5*
Local Shopping - 5*
Hotel Overall Cleanliness - 5*
Room Cleanliness - 5*
Check In Efficiency - 5* (late evening)
Hotel Food Venues - 3* (presently)
State of room, towels, and bed linens - 5*
Value 5* (for what I paid)
Service 3* (only because I used few hotel services)
As always,
Happy Travels!

title: “Great location beautiful decor can be noisy”
text:
The Hotel Solamar is in a great location with beautiful decor. The pool is located on the 4th floor. There is a bar with loud music by the pool. If you have to get to bed early or need quiet, the rooms on the pool side or probably not a good choice for the weekends. I stayed on the 8th floor on the pool side and could hear some of the music beat but not enough to keep me awake.
The staff was very friendly. The hotel allows pets, even large dogs, so if you're allergic, this is not the place for you.

title: “Something seems amiss...”
text:
I have stayed at the Biltmore several times in the past and had great stays. The property has "good bones" and I loved that there were multiple buildings and multiple pools - - - it creates a more "boutique" experience, even though there are hundreds and hundreds of rooms. 
I was looking forward to this stay and I was let down. Somethings seems amiss with the property this time. The room I was in needed a renovation (stains on the carpet, hole in the lampshade, bathroom outdated). The AC was not on (perhaps at all?) in the common areas. The furniture in the lobby is threadbare. Some common areas in the hotel smell almost like hay? Weird. Long story short - I think it is time for a big renovation or for someone to throw some money into the hotel. All that being said - every employee I encountered was gracious, beyond the carpet and the fixtures in the room it appeared clean, and the food was good. 
If you are looking for real luxury - you may try Royal Palms. Great property and the onsite restaurant is excellent.

title: “Motel on Hollywood Boulevard”
text:
Typical motel (ex Days Inn) on the edge of Hollywood. Ideal for Metro - Hollywood Western stop. Bus routes pass the property. No food available but on site diner for breakfast or later meal (very good). 
Staff were very helpful and the rooms clean. However first room had no hanging space or draws for clothing. Then had to move again due to servicing needs. 
Not the best place to stay but reasonable for families
Off street parking. 
Be sure you explain your needs when booking. Half of rooms are up one flight of stairs. No lift. Staff will help if needed.

title: “Clean and modern, but tiny rooms”
text: Experienced the smallest room I have every stayed in in a U. S. hotel. Very clean, modern and up to date, but hardly big enough to turn around in. Hotel does have a connected restaurant, but a tiny lobby, and no doorman to help with bags or get a cab. Very convenient to NYSE and Wall Street financial houses.

title: “Great little hotel, extras made it even more special”
text: My husband stayed here for a convention and I tagged along (as I always do when we can get Grandma to come down and watch the kids!) This is the perfect sized hotel -- big enough to offer amenities such as a spa/workout room and a restaurant/bar, but small enough that you don't need 20 minutes and 3 sets of elevators to get to your room. Speaking of which, are clean, cozy and stocked with Aveda shampoo/conditioner. Standard rooms are on the smallish side -- this is San Francisco after all -- and the queen sized bed took a little getting used to, but overall the room was more than adequate. My favorite part of the stay here had to be the evening wine reception with unbelievably delicious (homemade) chocolate truffles and Brian, the very talented (free, but leave a tip!) massage therapist. If I had another week there, I'm sure he could work wonders on my neck and upper back pain! Oliver, the resident golden retriever, was another welcoming employee. Location is great, only a few blocks away from Union Square. I would def stay here again!

title: “Fantastic room and staff - just take a cab for going out!”
text: I can't compliment the staff enough at this Hyatt location. This was my first stay after attaining Diamond Status and all I can say is that while I'm sure I may top this room later on, we have certainly started off with a bang. Fantastic view, fantastic room and fantastic staff. Yes, you need to grab a quick cab ride if your intention is to head out pretty much anywhere, but when you pay half to a third of the price of the Park Hyatt for the room, a few cab rides are chump change and a simple trade-off. We'll definitely use this location again.

title: “Not great but OK”
text:
I have spent 6 nights in this hotel in early January. My impression is that:
1. The area is not as bad as many of the previous reviews imply. There are wuite a few homeless, most of whom seem to have some mental illness, but they are not threatening or problematic, even at night;
2. The hotel itself is perhaps showing its age, but the rooms are OK;
3. Good service to Platinum Priviledge Club members (free buffet breakfast, upgrade to club room)
4. Free wireless broadband is a real bonus
5. Only problem is hot water - very patchy, and at times I ended up with a luke warm shower. Not good.
Overall for the price it is good for business. For a pleasure stay (e.g. a weekend) I would look for more.

title: “STAY SOMEWHERE ELSE!!!”
text: I would highly caution anyone who is considering staying at this hotel. My husband and I decided for our one year anniversary to visit LA and go to Universal Studios, etc. I picked this hotel off of expedia.com based partly on its "close proximity to Universal Studios" and price. We got what we paid for. First of all, the hotel was located in "historic Filipino Town"; while this sounds nice, it actually turned out to be the ghetto. There were bars on every window and door and slums everywhere. The hotel itself didn't have any bars, but that didn't stop us from feeling uncomfortable. The hotel room itself was much like an econo lodge or red roof inn, but in a little worse shape. The furniture was a bit on the shabby side, the linens were creepy, and the bathroom had visible signs of wear and tear (tiles were missing, plaster done poorly). During the night you could hear helicopters buzzing overhead and could see their spotlights looking for people. There was an almost constant drone of sirens. We were suppose to stay 3 nights and ended up bailing after the second. By no means should you ever book at this hotel!

title: “OK but Could be Much Better, Choose Another Hotel if Priced the Same”
text:
During our stay....failed to completely make the room (bed was made, no towels, no glasses, no coffee service), extremely long lines for breakfast, managers reception and elevators.....the room was nice.
Of 6 nights at Embassy Suite Locations during our nine night family vacation, the two nights spent at this hotel were by far the least relaxing. It is clear that the owners of this hotel do not care to make things better, as my concerns are the same ones that go back months in these reviews. Long breakfast lines, poor food and beverage service for the managers reception and the elevator problem could be remedied with increased staffing. it is clear this hotel chooses profit over service. 
If you wish to spend 30 minutes in a breakfast line, 30 minutes in the "managers reception" line or 15 minutes in line to go to your room, this hotel is for you.
 I flame this hotel as I was promised a follow up by the front desk regarding my concerns and have heard nothing. 
Not terrible, just choose something else if available.

title: “Loved The Standad”
text: We stayed one night at The Standard (October 22), It is the kind of hotel my husband and I like best--boutiquey and funky. Our room on the 16th floor had great views of the Hudson and we could see the HIgh Line down below. Great location near restaurants and Chelsea Market. Contrary to other recent reviews, we heard very little noise from our room and found every hotel employee we encountered to be helpful and friendly.

title: “Exceeded my expectations!”
text: Absolutely loved this place! I stayed here for 4 nights with my husband, mother in law and my baby boy. The location is superb, we walked in front of the Kodak Theather every night, the nearby mall is great (plenty of places to eat at night) and the metro station is just a 5 minute walk from the hotel. The bed was very comfy and I really liked the vibe of the hotel. My mother in law stayed at the sofa bed and it was also comfy. Service is excellent...they gave us directions every day. The breakfast, although limited, is very good. If you have a one or two bedroom suite, you also have the option of cooking in the in room kitchen. The only con was that 2 out of the 4 nights, the water got cold in the middle of my shower. Also, if you are really really picky...then you may notice that the paint job in the bathroom is not perfect. Overall, I greatly recommend this place.

title: “Very honest and helpful staff!”
text: I have always genuinely found this hotel to be very pleasant, but I wanted to share a special experience to commend their staff: I accidentally left a very expensive suit in the closet in my room. I didn't immediately realize it and when I called the hotel several months later thinking it was a very lost cause, they still had my suit in lost and found! They fed-exed it to me right away.

title: “stuffy”
text: very cold atmosphere, building and rooms were great. Location is great, would try agian once more, reception was very stuffy, food was very good, don't know if I woyuld recommend to just anyone, attitudes could be improved upon.

title: “Good deal in midtown Manhattan”
text: It's practically impossible to find a decent hotel in midtown Manhattan for under $200/night, but I kept checking until I ran across the La Quinta on West 32nd Street and jumped on it. The location absolutely can't be beat--less than a block from the Herald Square subway station between Broadway and Fifth Avenue, only a few blocks from Times Square and almost directly behind the Empire State Building, and only a couple of blocks from Penn Station. The room was small, as are most NYC hotel rooms, but the bed was comfortable and the bathroom and shower were very good. A couple of nitpicks--it's VERY easy to walk past this place; unlike other hotels in the area there's no banner sign, only smallish plaques on the facade. The elevators are pretty slow, but I was on the second floor and mostly used the stairs. The outlets on the desk didn't work but I'm used to using my laptop on the bed so that was no big deal.
