The free internet worked fine until the last full day of my stay, Sunday, when it was down all day. Fortunately someone in the area had an open connection so I hooked up on that. If you like Korean food you're in luck, as the hotel is on "Korea Way" and is literally surrounded by 24-hour Korean BBQs. If you don't there's a small deli called Speedy's down the block that makes good sandwiches and hot food, and the usual fast food suspects plus some Irish pubs are very close by. For being so close by hot spots the room was pretty quiet. If you're by yourself or with someone with whom you don't mind sharing close quarters you're probably not going to do better than the La Quinta if you want to stay in midtown--I'll definitely keep this place in mind next time I come to NYC.

title: “Good Airport Property”
text: Second time we stayed at this Hampton and used the Sleep, Park and Fly Program. It works out great for early morning flights. The hotel is an older property but in very good shape. The staff including the shuttle driver is very professional, friendly and knowledgeable. It is an exceptional value in summertime and weekends. The only negative we experienced is that the air conditioners are extremely noisy and because of the HOT climate run constantly.

title: “Excellent Experience”
text: We really enjoyed our stay! Everything was so nice. The women who checked us in was so nice and friendly and knowledgeable about the activities at the hotel. We will definately come back for another getaway!

title: “Clean but Nothing Spectacular”
text: We have stayed at the Elegante 3 times on business trips. the rooma are a bit dated but always clean. One small lounge on site that is dated as well. It certainly fulfills the purpose of am overnight stay with no complaints but would not be my first choice for vacation

title: “Hits the Mark”
text: An excellent option if you need to be on the upper east side. We upgraded to a Manhattan suite with Harper and AmEx. No view but a spacious room with lots of light and a galley kitchen. Staff are efficient, and helpful. Room was clean and well appointed although the bed was too soft for me. Flat screen TV in both rooms and in mirror in bath. Daily continental breakfast was excellent but late night room service was a disappointment. Find another late night dining option in the neighborhood. Neither the pizza nor the burger were worth the calories. The free WiFi worked for about 30 minutes before a reboot was necessary. For the quality of the room, price and location an excellent option.

title: “perfect for couples”
text:
perfect in every way.
my wife and i are very picky travelers. we stayed 4 nights in the Serrano in December right before the Holidays and it was everything we wanted. the staff was very helpful...i had an Xmas package for my wife sent there before we arrived...the name on the package was messed up but they still held it and were very helpful. the room was great, not huge but great and comfortable and romantic. very comfortable bed and pillows and a great view. good fitness center. the wine hour from 5-6 nightly is cool. park right next door in the parking garage for $18/day-cash only. no worries on the location in the Tenderloin district...it is completely safe...believe me i wouldn't stay there if it were unsafe. i even went out at night to get something to eat and it was fine...i would recommend staying between the hotel and union square...it's a little sketchy the other way...but not scary.
breakfast is perfect at the Crepe restaurant 2 blocks up the hill on the right corner at Post i think...great food and inexpensive...$12-16 for 2 people. the oatmeal is great. also try Mason Cafe-mid block- 1 block over toward Union Square...service isn't 100% but it is quiet, great food, and good prices...$30 for 2 people.
the hotel's restaurant also has good food and service. we had 20 minutes to eat and drink before going to see a jazz show at Yoshi's in Oakland. we told the host/waier and they got us our food and drinks in a snap...it was a bit early and there weren't any people there so that helped but they were still very nice. cafe bastille has great food and outdoor seating. they also have two other restaurants on both sides with outdoor seating. the whole street is a cool place to be at night for dinner.
if you are into live jazz...go to Yoshi's in Oakland. good food...mediocre service...great music and a great scene. get there a little early and eat there.
if you are an architecture fan...walk up to St. Mary's chapel...just 8 blocks from hotel Serrano opposite from Union square. it is a beautiful cast-in-place concrete structure by Pierre Luigi Nervi. The De Young is pretty cool as will be Piano's museum across from the De Young (under construction Dec. 2006). Golden Gate park is totally beautiful. Libeskind's jewish museum is also under construction by Yerba Buena gardens. should be complete late 2007 or early 2008. We had a view of Morphosis' building for the state of california out of our hotel window. it is in a seedy area but worth the visit (under construction Dec 2006). also visit frank lloyd wright's small gallery on Maiden Lane just off from Union square to the west i think...brick facade with an arched entry...on the block with all the swank shopping. it is a cool gallery, all original architecture, finishes, lighting, etc.

title: “Beautiful Hotel, Super Service, Amazing Cookies”
text: Booked 2 rooms for MLK weekend with spouse, nanny and 3 young children. Staff was delightful, and the location was great. Cafe, starbucks, and johnny rockets all within walking distance, and walgreens was right across the street. When we commented on the delicious chocolate chip cookies, the chef emailed me the recipe and then mailed me a copy of the hotel's cookbook. Really impressed!

title: “Excellent hotel”
text: The hotel is very nice and very clean. Food is great. Excellent hotel.

title: “Got what you need.”
text: Clean rooms, free parking and wi-fi. Great price. Decent neighborhood, would stay again.

title: “Nice hotel, shame they can't manage requests”
text:
Having read the reviews here, I emailed the hotel in advance to request a room at the back or a high floor and got a reply to say my request had been noted. when we checked in and went to our room, it was probably the worst in the hotel, 302, with the train line about 3 metres from the window. I went back to the lobby to ask for another room but was told there was nothing else available without a surcharge.Understandable but annoying if they had already filled all the rooms, but the people who had arrived after us were still at the desk and had been given a room at the back. The only conclusion I could draw was that this was a deliberate attempt to get me to pay for an upgrade. We were offered another room for the remaining nights if we packed up and took our luggage to the lobby before breakfast, but didn't want to waste the time in a short break. 
T shaped room was rather dark, and with the station platform immediately outside and level with the widow we tended to keep the curtains closed anyway. The thermostat for the air-conditioning was in the stem of the T which meant that the room got very hot before it kicked in, then freezing cold before it cut out
Location is very good, a block from millennium park, and VERY close to a station. If we had been given a room as requested it could have been 5 stars, just shows how little it takes to spoil something.

title: “I expected a better hotel”
text:
My partner was here on a conference so I tagged along to visit Philadelphia. According to my partner, the reservation staff was very rude and unhelpful and was very poorly informed about the special conference package/rate. The check-in staff, on the other hand, was very good. She saw that we would be staying for a week and gave us a corner room with a decent view.
The room itself was dated. There was no mini-bar/fridge - even 3* hotels in Europe would have one. The room was enormous but has lots of wasted space. Another arm chair would have been nice. Yes, there was a television, but an old type. I was expecting a hotel of this calibre to have a flat screen tele, not the hulking great thing. All the channels were American. No BBC World Service. So if you want to keep up to date with news in Britain or Europe, you can't ! There is a Japanese channel but the programme is dubbed, and in a rather annoying manner. The bathroom was big enough to have a party in and was generally in a good condition. The shower was VERY nice. The carpet and furniture are showing signs of wear and tear. It was like stepping back into the 90's. May be it can market itself for "a retro experience". The bed, however, was very big comfy. But light sleepers might find the street noise disturbing. We were on the 19th floor and we could hear the buses.
There was a coffee percolator in the room but no kettle, so forget making yourself a cup of tea. That didn't bother me, after all, it's a coffee drinking country. But what got me was the horrible polystyrene cups !! Not only is it wasteful and eco-unfriendly, it is also cheap and nasty! Would you really expect a room costing $175 a night not to provide china cups? Not other hotels I have stayed in, however cheap, failed to provide a proper cups.
I ate there once, breakfast at the restaurant 13. We were greeted rather casually, to say the least. "Are you guys next?" is not the usual greeting I expect at such an establishment. If it were Starbucks, then I would not feel the same way. The waiting staff inside was great. Very friendly and attentive. Perhaps they went to two different training schools.
For such an enormous hotels catered for large conferences and conventions, it is very poorly served with coffee shops. There is one Starbucks in the foyer. Every time I walk past Starbucks, there was a long queue. When the big conference was in full swing, they set up coffee stations in the foyer.Consequently, there were queues everywhere. 
There is a fitness centre which is well equipped and well maintained. The pool looked nice but I didn't use it.
The location is it's best point. The area is not as bad as some of the other reviews suggested. It is close to Macy's (hurray!) and the Reading Terminal Market. Forget the buffet breakfast at 13, go and have it there instead. Broad Street isn't far away, either.
If you are coming for a conference and has to stay here, you will have a comfortable enough stay. If you are visiting Philadelphia (a lovely place to visit) on holiday, then there might be other, better hotels. Oh, yes, I forgot. If you stay here, be prepared to meet the crowds of conference delegates. The foyer gets VERY crowded.

title: “Underwhelmed at the Ritz Chicago”
text: Having stayed at other Ritz Carltons, and researching this location, I was looking forward to a terrific experience. While okay, there was nothing memorable spending 3 nights at this property. Lobby while nice seemed dated, service average to slow in cafe and at hotel bar. If this spa is world class, I am trying another planet. Pool is small, hot tub is hotter (I think) than recommended highest temperature. Room was smaller than I expected, furnishings were very comfortable, but seemed sparse. Staff helpful, but robotic in terms of service delivery and guest interaction. Web site listed a rooftop sun deck. Deck was closed for renovations, which was not mentioned to me when I contacted property prior to making reservation. Perhaps because this property is manged by Four Seasons, some of the little touches experienced at other Ritz-Carltons were missing. For the price, I would be just as happy at other 3 1/2 - 5 star properties within a mile of the Chicago Ritz Carlton. Also, $45 per night for valet seems to really push the envelope.

title: “Loving this hotel”
text:
Staying here at the moment. This is a great hotel well suited to our needs. The plus points are:
- very quiet - you get a great night's sleep
- very clean
- all the staff are extremely pleasant & helpful. I forgot a UK adaptor and when I mentioned it one of them just offered to get me one without me asking
- good location
- spacious room
- it looks stylish
- there is a coffee maker, microwave and fridge (and a very good food shop a few doors along the street)
- continental breakfast is fine/good quality
- comfy bed
- no rip off minibar
- nice toiletries 
- the hotel has a calm relaxed feel to it
Some travellers might find the lack of hotel bar/restaurant a problem but there are plenty places to go locally and if you want chilled wine or beer there's room to stock the fridge. There is a (possibly ?) linked restaurant right next door but it seems empty and uninviting to us.
There is a slight issue with counter intuitive appliances etc - some displaying slightly more style than substances eg the shower/bath contols are a bit complicated and the switches on some of the lights are unusual. The TV controls are not straightforward. However this is nitpicking.
All in all - Highly recommended!

title: “Centrally located & good value for money!”
text: Old hotel with a history and ideal position. Room was clean & comfortable. We were with our daughter & her boyfriend & stayed in a 2 bedroom 2 bathroom suite - very suitable. Breakfast in the restaurant downstairs is good value.

title: “Don't do it!”
text:
Don't be fooled by this clean facade! 
From the second you park your car- your wallet will be raped!
There is no free Parking at this hotel because they leased their parking space(s) inside of the Philadelphia Parking Authority controlled car garage! 
((And everyone knows their legendary reputation.)) 
As a result, you will be billed an additional $20 per day of your stay.
For you non-Philadelphia travelers: this means the Philadelphia Parking authority will hold your car hostage unless you show them your orange Marriott "complimentary" parking card. 
The problem is that Marriott's management chronically "forgets" (wink, wink) to issue this ticket to you upon check in. They will tell you to drive to the second floor on your way out ((though it is really located on the parking garage's 3rd floor )) but good luck getting there because there are more one ways in that garage then in even your worst driving nightmare! 
Now, I know that everyone hates airport parking but this will really tick you off -especially if you are not a local traveler - because if you don't have that magic orange ticket every time you leave this hotel you'll end up paying the jacked-up Parking Authority rates upfront. 
This hotel will act like they didn't know-but since they've already charged you- why would even expect to receive even sub par service? 
When you finally do get into your room it will cost you $3.50 to drink that bottle of water and don't even ask about tv.
Their "pool" is only suitable for hermit crabs...(but everyone can wade to their shins by the stairs)
Over all, this hotel has beautiful corporate gloss, date rape your wallet service and an aggravating parking scheme. 
Staying here won't save you anything because their service ruins the quality towards hospitality will genuinely make you feel like you've burned all your cash in a gold lined toilet.

title: “Great hotel, excellent service!”
text: This is a great hotel, excellent accomodations, great service, located within walking distance of The Alamo, Riverwalk and other historic places. Yes, it is close to a train station, but the sounds were very muffled and the hotel had earplugs on the nightstands by the beds (didnt need them, though!) I highly recommend this hotel for anyone - couples, families, business travelers. Definately worth the price!

title: “Great Location for the Marine Corps Marathon!”
text:
Review listed below but location was excellent! Right across the street from McPherson Square metro on the blue and orange lines for easy access to the starting point for the Marine Corps Marathon. Hotel is also a mile from the National Mall and all the downtown highilights of D.C. Has great restaurants and of course 2 starbucks nearby......
Review of hotel itself:
Reception staff seemed friendly and helpful. Lobby seems cozy with bar and "American Grill Restaurant" off to the side of the hotel. Food was very good.
Room:
Quit and roomy. Free wifi along with in room refrigerator and microwave. Large LCD TV with cable. Bed was comfortable. Bathroom was clean and adequate. I guess your average hotel room. Felt clean which is always a good feeling. Only negative say about the room was the AC/Heating of the room. Fan was noisy and at a set temperature it would cold one minute and hot the next.
We would stay here again given it's location and again great for the Marine Corps Marathon:
Tips for the Marathon:
Also consider Rosslyn hotels since finish line is there.
Expect big crowds on the metro but this is 30K people!
Restaurants:
Ate at Old Ebbits a block down the road on 15th. Great foot and ambience.

title: “Overall nice hotel but NOISY, poor windows, traffic noise”
text: We stayed at this hotel on business in December 2006. The hotel is nicely decorated. The restaurant is a TGIFridays and there is a full service Starbucks right in the lobby. The staff was very nice and the sleep number beds were comfortable. Unfortunately the building is dated and the windows are an odd mix of different sized panes, and there is no soundproofing or double glazing. The hotel is boardered on two sides by extremely busy roads and the traffic noise comes right thru the windows. Would not stay here if I had any choice. Would pick the Hampton Inn & Suites, two blocks away, instead.

title: “Perfect.”
text: Great hotel with fantastic restaurant, excellent location opposite Beverly Center and excellent service.

title: “Convenient Hotel, Quality Service”
text:
I recently stayed at the Grand Hyatt New York just before Hurricane Irene. The hotel was extremely busy with people both coming & going right before the storm. Even with the high volume of guests, every staff member I came in contact with at the hotel was very friendly. Also, the large number of elevators meant that I never had to wait very long for an elevator, even with how busy the hotel was. This was sort of a surprise, since I've experienced far worse wait times at other convention hotels.
 I received one of their newly renovated guest rooms. The furnishings were very contemporary and comfortable. The bed was, in fact, extremely comfortable. Everything was very clean as well. In addition, the room had very strong air conditioning. This came in handy since the weather was very humid at the time. The one thing I would complain about is that all Hyatt Hotels still charge $9.99 per night for wifi thru T-Mobile hotspot. I wish mainline Hyatts would follow their corporate brethren at Andaz and make wifi complementary. 
The Grand Hyatt is by no means a 5 star hotel. It's very large and seems to cater to large groups & conventions. What you will receive is a solid 4 star hotel that is located directly on top of Grand Central Terminal. The people working there are very nice & the rooms are new. I have no hesitation recommending the Grand Hyatt to anyone. The hotel will be even better when construction is completed in the lobby & the restaurants.

title: “a great place whether you're there to relax or explore”
text: It's an elegant hotel on the Inner Harbor with a stunning view if you're lucky enough to get a harborview room. Aside from the creature comforts that the Marriott Hotels offer--those cushy beds and avalanche of pillows--the location is terrific: walk to Little Italy and Fells Point for fine restaurants and interesting shops, or stroll the harbor and take in museums, aquarium, ships, and restaurants--mostly franchised restaurants on the harbor itself. We stayed here for two nights when my husband had a biopsy scheduled at Johns Hopkins. Using Priceline, we were able to enjoy a level of comfort that wouldn't have been available to us otherwise. We checked in on a Sunday night and were upgraded to a harborview room without even asking. At no time were we made to feel inferior because we had booked through Priceline. The only complaint we had was the price of a wireless internet connection--$10 a day in your room, somewhat cheaper in the lobby, but that seemed ridiculous for a 4 star hotel. The $22 daily parking fee was high, but it is the city and you are in a premier location so it's really not outrageous. Since we generally do not eat in hotel restaurants, we can't comment on the restaurant--there are many dining options nearby. All in all, it was a wonderful place to stay during a stressful time, and it would make a wonderful base for a weekend at the Inner Harbor--a lively, stimulating place. We would later stay a few blocks away at the Reniassance on the Inner Harbor; both are comparable & each has its own set of advantages.

title: “2nd stay ...just what I remembered!”
text: Stayed at Omni La Mansion for the San Antonio Marathon. Even though we paid more due to the race weekend prices, our experience was just as pleasant as our first visit. Our room was spacious with a very comfortable bed. The room faced the street, but we were not disturbed by traffic sounds. The blackout curtains used are great for a wonderful night's rest! If you don't want to pay the valet prices, you can park across the street in the parking garage. Would recommend this hotel for a special occasion.

title: “New York Hotel”
text: The Bentley Hotel is a small boutique style hotel about a 20 minute walk from times square. We had a Junior Suite which was large and well equipped. Friendly staff and well worth considering if you can get a bargain. Only thing missing was a refridgerator in the room.

title: “Not worth the $$”
text: Save yourself the hassle and spend a few extra $$ and stay at the Hyatt on the river walk. I was in town for a conference and half of my co-workers were at the Hyatt and the rest at Hotel Indigo. The room was average sized, the ac/heat was the loudest I have ever encountered, and the rooms were not that clean, The location is great but so are the rest of the hotels in the area. The staff was nice and gave me 1000 points on my account for my inconvience of no hot water one morning.

title: “Great hotel for business”
text:
I spent over about 20 nights during a 2-month period, in a variety of rooms. All of the rooms on the exterior were nice, although they varied in their configuration (it's a former office and retail building) and the prices varied from $199-$359. The hotel is new and fresh. I never had a bad room, but the rooms in the interior "ring" were too confining for me (frosted window to a courtyard).
Each room has a nice I-Home brand music-radio that received reliable FM reception and can play and charge your I-Pod or I-Phone. Quiet rooms are even quieter if you run the fan on the thermostat (just the right white noise). 
Access to the concierge level is key -- breakfast was a nice treat (not available on Sat./Sun.), with gourmet coffee made fresh by the cup (espresso, cappuccino, etc.), organic yogurt and honey elegantly served in a glass, fresh cut fruit and berries, and two hot dishes that varied (e.g., eggs and sausage). The bar is a fun place to unwind because it's inviting and open to the 2-story lobby. Service throughout was professional and cheerful.

title: “Great Service”
text: Enjoyed a wonderful experience at this hotel. Great food, excellent facility and most important great staff.

title: “Terrible Service, No Temperature Control in Rooms”
text:
After requesting an early check in time and arriving at the hotel at noon my wife was told that no rooms were available and that they could call her mobile phone when a room was made up. After checking back with the desk multiple times she was finally given a room at 4:30pm - with the indifferent front desk agent saying "Oh, nobody called you? The room has been ready for hours." The bell desk then was unable to locate her one bag, which finally arrived at the room after 6pm. 
She was given a room on the bottom floor of the outbuilding called Parkview, which had a thermostat, but said thermostat wasn't able to regulate the temperature. By late evening it was 76 degrees in the room when the heat turned on warming it up to over 80 degrees. The only way to cool the room down was to open the ground floor window, but the hotel backs on a dark park area and the window didn't have any security block on it to prevent it from opening far enough for someone to slip into the room, so having the window open all night wasn't a safe option. We called to complain and they sent the building engineer down, who explained that they don't have air-conditioning in that building. 
After logging complaints each of the first three days of the stay we were finally given a different room in the main building - while slightly better this room backed on the lower rooftop HVAC system which was so loud that we were woken up several times each night of the last two nights of our stay.

title: “Great Staff and Service, the worst design and construction I have seen”
text:
This is a tough review to write. I really wanted to like this hotel - and the staff was energetic and was trying so hard to make this a great hotel. Unfortunately the staff cannot make up for the facility itself.
Having spent my early career working hotels, I saw this property fell victim to a designer that understands designs but not functionality. In my suite, there were two TV's, I turned on one, they both turned - however when I changed the channel only one wuold. 
The worst as that I could hear the people upstairs when they walked around. I always knew right where they were in the room. I could hear conversations in the next room and knew when the neighbors took a shower or flushed the toilet. I didn't need to set my alarm clock, I found that I was awaken every morning by someone aruond me needing to get up earlier. This morning I was awakend by neighbor who was clearing his sinuses in his bathroom. 
I am surprised that Marriott hasn't learned to establish construction standards and allowed this to happen. Isn't the core of it is feeling like you can escape into your room and get a good night's sleep at the end of the day? 
Hats off to the staff that were warm, freindly and did everything they could to make this a great stay.

title: “My new home away from home”
text: I chose that hotel because of how close it was to the medical center area and the transportation services that they offered. It was only 5 minutes away from MD Anderson Cancer center which was the reason that we were there. The staff was AMAZING!!! The food was UNBELIEVABLE!!! The hotel was just beautiful and peaceful and that is just what you wanted after a tough day of Dr's and more Dr's. Starbucks was just downstairs and what a better way to start your day!!! The rooms were big and spacious, the beds were super comfortable with the soft and better than heavenly pillows and the bathrooms, what else can I say that they were spacious and clean as can be. I have been back to MD Anderson Cancer center and would not stay anywhere else. The BEST PLACE in the Medical Center. Its my new home away from home.

title: “Great location...Serves the prupose...Wireless Internet”
text: I stay here on business once a month...it is in a great central location, right on the main bus line on Van Ness..easy access to the Cable Car and Fishermans Wharf...if you come to the City from the airport on BART, get off at the Powell Street station and catch a cab by one of the nearby hotels, this is one station past Civic Center, but on a better part of Market street...The food in the main restaurant-bar is very good and well presented,a bit overpriced though...I would suggest going to one of the other 1000's of restaurant in the City...the beds are a bit uncomfortable, but the staff is always very attentive...enjoy !

title: “AWESOME!”
text: Awesome experience staying at this hotel. All the front desk representatives and managers were super helpful and made my stay comfortable and stress free but I gotta say Kudos to WAYDE.. He's a super informative Representative that makes you adjust from the time to you arrive till you leave. Thanks Wayde.

title: “Embarcadero elegance”
text:
The hotel is contemporary without being far out. My room was a good size and had a divan. It was very quiet at night even though it was facing the street. There is a good gym and free Internet for those of us without Iphones, etc. The people were very nice and helpful.
The location is a bit of a problem; it is very near the Embarcadero, but you have to walk through (or past) four blocks of the Embarcadero Center complex to get to the Ferry Building etc. The hotel is in a business district and there are not many places to eat at night or on weekends. Also, it is a bit of a walk to get to the BART station. 
But all in all, the positives outweigh the location; I will definitely stay here again.

title: “What a Wonderful W!”
text: My stay at the W Chicago Lakeshore this past Friday, November 30, 2012 was another wonderful night. I have stayed at this Starwood property many times in the past, but have yet to submit a review. Now's the time! Katrina, the W's front desk talent, checked me in and noted my SPG Platinum status. Because there was a radiologist conference at the hotel, she apologized that there were no suites available, but promised the next time I stay at the W Lakeshore, they'd do their best to upgrade me to a suite. I didn't even request an upgrade, but I sure appreciated the gesture! Nevertheless, I was upgraded to a spectacular room (#3010) on an upper floor with a view of Lake Michigan and Navy Pier. As always, the view is truely spectacular! The room was equipped with an extremely comfortable king bed, a chaise lounge, flat screen television, desk, chair, bathroom with walk-in shower, and complimentary Bliss Spa products. Upon inspection, the room was clean and organized. As an added bonus, the W offers Acura Experience which can be reserved to transport guests to local destinations. Of course, I took advantage of the Acura Experience, which dropped me off the Bloomingdale's front door to do some Black Friday shopping. What a great service! I didn't get to hit Bliss Spa or Wave Restaurant located inside the W during this stay, but every one of my past visits has been exceptional. Upon check-out the following day, I called for luggage assistance because I had a ton of shopping bags. Ben Hou, the W's Living Room manager, promptly arrived at my room and courteously assisted me with my shopping bags and luggage. The valet brought my vehicle around and placed my luggage and shopping bags inside my vehicle. Ben and the valets wisfed me safe travels and I was on my way. This was another phenmenal stay and I look forward to returning to the W Chicago Lakeshore.

title: “Great location...highly overpriced”
text: If it were only the thin walls and high priced rooms I would probably still use this hotel due to excellent location, however high cost wireless and a $25 dollar charge to open the refrigerator door is too much. We will never stay here again as there are much better options in the area.

title: “Disappointing for a Grand Hyatt”
text:
We stayed in June of this year, first time in San Francisco. Debated over the Fishermans Wharf area or downtown. Opted for downtown and the Grand Hyatt as I'm a Hyatt Platinum card holder. 
Room was ok, not particularly large, but it was just a standard room. 
Maybe this is the norm for San Fran, but I just though small and the whole hotel just lacked any atmosphere and life.

title: “Lovely weekend at Standford Court Renaissance”
text: We stayed at this hotel for a weekend in September 2006 and absolutely loved it. This is probably one of the best hotels that I have stayed at in San Francisco, and I loved the location of the Hotel, as well. Me and my then fiance were in town for our anniversary and the staff was very nice and friendly, asking why we were in town, and when told that it was for anniversary they assigned us to a very nice corner room on their top floor. Our view was awesome! The room was immaculate. Very large, spotless, and with great amenities. We ordered room service and it was and delicious. I would definitely recommend this to people coming into town on a romantic getaway!

title: “Very nice and comfortable hotel for business & tour”
text:
Hotel staffs were very kind.
Breasfast was very good. (Visitors may choose one among 4 different menu for breakfast.)
Internet was easily accessed by free WiFi.
But there was no refrigerator in the room.

title: “Nice stay in New York”
text: We loved the location of this hotel and the concierge Eric was really nice. We can't wait for the restaurant to open

title: “Wonderful place in San Francisco!”
text: This was a pleasant surprise and close to the Wharf! Free parking is a wonderful perk! Our room was clean and spacious. The small balcony was so sweet! The staff were very friendly as we were quite tired and had our room ready!

title: “No costumer service, and the rooms where unbeliveablely nasty, do not go here.”
text: I stayed in this hotel for 1.5 days with my dog. On the second day after I had been walking him around already for a day half they asked me to leave cuz of my dog!!! Ya makes no sence and wouldn't refund my money eather. If you ask me go to the knights inn down the road same price and much better qualty for your money.

title: “Poor customer service”
text: The hotel itself is fine. Nice, clean rooms in a great location. Got a great price on Priceline. It is in a noisy area -- they give you a pair of earplugs! Customer service was really poor. The people working at the desk were clearly just going through the motions -- not friendly, didn't say thanks, answered questions very shortly. Would be a different experience with happier staff.

title: “Heaven at the Hilton”
text: I am seriously picky about hotels and spent an inordinately long time researching where to stay in New York for 5 days to celebrate my husband's 50th birthday. It was his first time in New York, and I wanted him to get to love it as much as I do. So here's what I was looking for: centrally located, below $400 per night (I had hoped to spend less but this was a very busy week in New York), generally good reviews, in-room movies for the nights we didn't want to go out, a bathtub in addition to a shower would be a bonus. Well, we got all of those at the Hilton, plus we got a room on the top floor (15th) with fantastic views and almost no traffic noise. The room was big by any standards, decked out with a fridge and microwave, great bathroom products, and THAT bed! The bed is the single biggest reason I would go back to the hotel in a heartbeat. It was incredibly comfortable and I had a good night's sleep every night. WIthout exception the staff and service at the hotel were also excellent. Friendly and helpful, and did more than they needed to. I let the hotel know that we were celebrating a big birthday and they laid on a fabulous cake when we arrived. The hotel got other important things right too - housekeeping was top notch and unobtrusive, there were enough removable hangers (not those mean things with the annoying fitting at the top), there were extra pillows in the cupboard. The only downside of our stay was the compressor on the roof of the hotel must have been right on top of our room and was quite noisy. But that is being really picky when we had a room high up and away from traffic noise. It's so rare to find a hotel that delivers on the promises it makes on its website, but this is one of them.

title: “Great Hotel and Conveniently Located”
text: I went with a very large group, and they went out of their way to accomodate us. Everyone in the staff was extremely friendly. The hotel is in a convenient location, it is within walking distance to shopping, restaurants, tourist attractions, and clubs. I highly recommend staying at this fine hotel!

title: “Small room, great location”
text: The room was VERY small and cold in appearance. Also, though it was april, it was freezing outside and the heater wasn't working in the room so my husband and I had to sleep with our coats on! The bathroom was also very VERY small. However, the location is WONDERFUL. It's a short walk to times square, fifth avenue shopping, and subway stations. There is a parking garage right next door which is way cheaper then the hotel parking. The morning breakfast buffet was ok, but once the food was gone it took a while for it to be "restocked." Also, though the fitness room was nice, it was "closed" for the whole 4 days that we were there. There were 2 computers with free internet access which was very helpful and the front desk staff were very helpful as far as directions and recommended places to eat. All in all, I would stay there again for less than 150/nt but if I need to pay more than that, I would look elsewhere.

title: “Shabby, but not chic”
text: Worn furniture, dirty carpets, miserable water pressure, lousy soundproofing and not very helpful staff. The suite was small and not the least bit luxurious. 12th floor and street noise was prevalent. Definitely would not stay here again.

title: “Brilliant!”
text: Spent 3 nights here in April ( before we found ourselves stranded in NYC) Have no complaints at all. Room was great size, comfy, clean & had fabulous view of Times Square. Only little niggle was that the whoosh of the elevators goes on 24/7 & can be a bit annoying if your room is close to them. This hotel does exactly what it says on the tin...it's big, busy & right in the middle of Times Square and has a brilliant buzz. Good security too. We had booked for 2 shows on Broadway & the hotel was practically next door to both of our venues ( a happy accident). The restaurants nearby are mostly chains & quite pricey. You should walk along to 9th Avenue where there are loads of independently owned restaurants. Giorgio's Country Grill has great pasta. We thoroughly enjoyed our stay.

title: “One of the best places to stay in Chicago!”
text:
We had a suite with a full kitchen, living room, huge bedroom and two baths. The floor to ceiling windows provided great views. Service was impeccable. We just went for a local staycation, do some shopping and dine at some restaurants. Excellent getaway.
Pool area was typical hotel. Wish they had a whirlpool. I know lap swimmers prefer a cooler pool temperature, but for kids and parents (over a weekend) a little warmer would have been nice. 
Sunday brunch was excellent and worth it. Rebar was great for a drink. Room service was excellent (actually one of the best of everywhere we stay) with many fun and interesting items available (great desserts).
I would recommend this to a business traveler or a family looking to see Chicago (American Girl Doll bags were everywhere this particular weekend).

title: “Great and clean hotel”
text:
I stayed at Carvi Hotel for a week with my wife and teenage daughter. It was absolutely great. Nice atmosphere, friendly and helpfull staff. While somewhat small the rooms are well above NY stadard; very clean and the size of the rooms is no issue. Also a very nice and quiet street winthin walking distance of anything in midtown.
Be aware of pricing. We found very good last minute deals on hotels.com.

title: “Buyer beware!”
text:
I was booked into this property via Clipper Vacations. It was on their list of budget motels close to the pier and downtown. I had read TripAdvisor reviews, but not knowing Seattle and on a limited budget, I agreed to the booking. I am sorry I did.
I was traveling with my tween daughter and reserved a double double. The elevator was cramped with worn carpet on the floor and walls. Upon entering the room, we both noticed an odd odor. The carpet was worn and had stains. The bedspreads had stains. The beds were somewhat comfortable, but lumpy. The fan was so squeaky, I had to turn it off by unplugging it from the wall. There were no polarized plugs in in the room. The TV was plugged in with an adapter and on a extended outlet addition. The paint was worn and chipped in several areas. The bathroom had chips in the paint over the tile and the shower/tub wall had peeling paint.
To top it off, all double double rooms overlook a 7th Avenue business called "Little Darlings" "an intimate gentleman's club". When I asked to be changed to another room, the staff informed me that the best they could do was to put me in a queen room with a roll away. They did give me free parking ($14 - $12 plus tax) for two of the nights I was there.
The staff was friendly and helpful. There is a decent selection of TV channels. There is a blow dryer available in the bathroom as well as an ironing board and iron. It is within a few blocks of Westlake Center, the monorail and downtown shopping.
Overall, however, I will not stay in this motel again nor recommend it to anyone. I did contact Clipper Vacations to let them know about the problems with this property they recommended.

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
We thought this hotel was great, we arrived middle of the night on a cold night in November and was offered some hot apple cider in the lobby, when we got to our room they had left 2 little mousse cakes on the bed for us as a welcome. The staff were fantastic! Helpful whenever we asked a question. There was a desktop computer in the lobby to make booking things easier and free wifi for guests.
The room was small but thats what we expected for NY. It may have been small but it was very nice. Comfy bed, fairly big bathroom. 
The location was great, only a few minute walk and your in times square!
If we go back i would definately stay there again.

title: “Even the studio room was great! Just avoid the restaurant...”
text:
The hotel was pretty good and we were satisfied even with a pull-out sofa as our bed. Pretty good location, but have a map with you at all times (and a compass if you can't "sense" which direction you are heading. Would reccommend taking the subway wherever you need to go since the main red line (1, 2 and 3), and the blue line are all very! close (Chambers St. entrances 1 block away). Great value for this hotel, I'm betting it will get expensive after the construction is done on the World Trade Center. No problems with noise, but we had a room facing the opposite direction of the site.
There were a few downsides: 1) The restaurant was a huge let-down. There's construction going on right next door where the world trade center memorial and building are being built, so it's not possible to eat on the terrace (20 stories up I think). The service was TERRIBLE at the restaurant. I had to ask for everything twice. A gratuity of 17% was included on the bill, so I couldn't tip according to the (lack of) service (many tourist restaurants include gratuity in New York). So $40 for breakfast; nothing fancy and extremely small portions! Don't be tricked into eating at their restaurant--you will regret it!
2) When we checked out our bill was $200 higher than the itinerary read. It turned out that they had overbilled us every night with over $30 extra. Add tax and there you had it. We went back and they weren't able to explain why that had happened, but we were glad we had taken a look at the bill and compared it with the itinerary that we had printed out. This seemed fishy though, so watch out!
Anyway, aside from these two issues, things worked out well. Bottled water system was nice, could have water with you wherever you went. The front-desk staff were helpful. Bring coffee with you! You only get 1 regular and 1 decaf packet per day. Loved that the hotel was so eco-friendly and energy efficient! Definitely worth staying again!!!

title: “Terrible”
text:
I was recommended this hotel by a friend, and unfortunately something must have happened between her staying there and me staying there...
The room was clean, although the linen was just provided (clean sheet - not sure if the blanket had been washed) bed was not actually made. My room had the bed built into the wall and an open plug source right near my face, so not sure about he alt and safety there. Ceiling had clearly been fixed and patched up (no fresh coat of paint or even an attempt to match up the paint in the room).
Extremely noisy with people traipsing up and down the stairs constantly and doors slamming.
Shared bathroom was always disgustingly dirty or occupied (don't actually know how people can make a place of cleanliness dirty, but they did) - and I didn't have a hot shower in all the time I was there, which (fortunately) was only 2 nights.
Won't be staying here again - it was the only time that I felt unsafe in my entire 2 week NYC trip. I'd rather pay a bit more for a VAST improvement on what you get.
On a positive note, the guy at the front desk was friendly.

title: “Warwick Radisson Very Friendly”
text: Just spent a long weekend at the Warwick Radisson in Center City Philadelphia with three friends. We had very nice connecting rooms. The rooms were very fresh looking with updated furnishings, carpets, and linens. The staff, from the front desk to cleaning personnel, were very friendly, helpful, and accommodating. Had access to the club lounge and found the breakfast service very nice. Rooms and hotel were very clean. The location can't be beat. Near Rittenhouse Square and the shops and restaurants on Walnut Street. I would stay here again.

title: “GREAT STAY.........”
text: My husband and I had a great Experience. The room was modern, extreamly clean, iron available, coffee, and extra products if needed were there(shampoo, soap). Buisness center was very convinient, we were able to use the computers. Pool and hot tub are indoor so, bad weather or not they can be used. Service was also great. Employees were kind, courtious,and answered questions we had. House keeping is great, everthing in the hotel is exreamly clean. I would definatly stay again.

title: “Good Stay, Good Service, Good Food”
text: If you have an early morning flight or simply need a hotel near the airport I would recommend the Westin. With large comfortable quite rooms and very easy access to the terminal made my need to stay over till the next morning that much easier. Oh, and the resturant is excellent with great service too.

title: “friendly and convenient”
text: The friendly and helpful staff made me give this excellent hotel the worthy five stars. Nothing was too much trouble day or night and they were all so cheerful. The rooms are basic but kept clean and adequate tea/coffee provided each day. There is a comprehensive choice at breakfast and the omlettes are great - cooked to order with a choice of fillings. The bar staff were very cheerful and we found no problem in ordering food late in the evening - which was of a very high standard and reasonably priced. A former review stated that there is only elevator availability to the floors - wrong - the stairs are well signed and we managed them on several occasions to the third floor. There is access to internet in the business centre which was helpful in printing our boarding passes on departure. The T station into Boston is a pleasant five minute walk and the trains are easy to follow and very cheap - $15 for a seven day ticket or $9 for a daily ticket. The drivers of the shuttle buses are very helpful and willing to drop you off at the car hire places/airport or train station with no problem at all. All in all a very well managed hotel - keep up the good service and great welcome to Boston - thanks for a very pleasant stay

title: “Not bad but has problems”
text:
When we tried to check in using the computer system at the reception it did not work. We eventually got a member if staff to help us. When we go to the room
It was not the premium room we had paid for. So it was a trip back down to reception. Seemed to be confusion on the room but they eventually gave us the room type that we had booked. Took a while though. Room was on a corner and had a fantastic view. Bathroom had issues. The door is glass so no privacy and slides shut with large gaps. The sink did not drain towards plug hole so water was left floating around after each use. The shower was open plan which was spacious but typically meant that water splashed everywhere.
We consider ourselves quite young still
but really got tired of the booming loud music in the elevator and 'mission control'. The breakfast muffins were nice but we didn't like the strange seating area which involved a difficult procedure to climb into your seat! Funky but not very practical when you have a coffee in your hand.
Location is good but just felt the design
was all a bit weird.

title: “Great location for tourists”
text:
We stayed at this hotel 5 nights for a conference and found it very satisfactory ( particularly since we got a great rate of $210 per night for a king room). It's not luxurious, but it's clean, nice, and has a great location for tourist activities like Broadway, shopping 5th Ave. etc. etc. I think it would be a terrific hotel for a NYC "first-timer" - you feel safe in the neighborhood and it's easy to find your way around. However, if you want to check out what "real" NYC is like, I wouldn't recommend it - having lived in NYC in the past, I find mid-town pretty sterile and prefer more residential areas of town. 
Overall, however, a great deal for the money and very comfortable if you're on the upper floors away from street noise. I don't think I'd pay more than $350 per night, though - lots of other places with more character in that price range.

title: “Brings a Special Sparkle to your trip...”
text:
We stayed at the wonderful Omni for 5 nights whilst visting LA for a jet-setting birthday trip from London.
Our stay was flawless! I wouldn't normally announce such a bold statement; but having stayed at several places through business and leisure trips- I can truly say this hotel and it's team of endearing staff brought a special sparkle to our holiday.
My top three highlights:
Beautiful Rooms
It is extremley spacious and cleanliness is spotless. The bed is divine and the most comfortable slumber I have had in a long while! The bathroom is again well-spaced and all the amenties are perfect. Beautifully kept by great housekeeping :-)
Splendid Bell staff (located near the entrance of the hotel)
This team is exceptional! Often the unsung hero's hence I feel it is important to make a mention :-) They look after everything from calling a taxi, collecting your car, greeting you from your night out, asking about your plans for the day. This warm welcome provides a special touch to the hotel experience. 
Outstanding Conceirge
Team of one but a grand service to all guests. Amy provided regular programmes for our day trips around LA. Her recommendations are superb and never disappoint. If I knew earlier I wouldn't have spent so much time on my personal research!!
She also organised a special birthday cake sent to our room on the actual day. A beautiful gesture and very touching. Amy's personal efforts and desire to ensure guests have a memorable visit have been the 'icing on cake'... Thank you so much and you are an absolute star to the Omni brand name.

title: “nice hotel”
text:
We stayed at the Stalybridge in July for one week, all in all I would say it was a nice hotel with all one would want or need during their stay. The breakfast was as you would expect, eggs bacon, cereal, cakes and muffins, fruit yoghurt, etc. There is a laundry in the basement free of charge with detergent provided. On tues wed and thru between 5 and 7 there was a free wine and nibbles afternoon for the guest. Although we missed it I believe it was very popular.
The rooms however, are rather small, but this is typical of New York. There is the Port Authority terminal across the road which is very handy for catching the bus and subway. Right next door is a very up market night club, the 'sky room' which was amazing and had city views, with the empire state building, Chrysler building in full view.There is corner Pizza bar with 99c huge pizza slices which satisfy any late night hunger pains.
Even though it is only a few minutes walk away from time square it is not in the most attractive part of town, but this did not bother us since convenience was our main priority.
The lift was the most annoying thing of the whole hotel. The wait was extremely long with up to half hour waits for it to arrive on your floor. 
I would stay here again if I was to visit New York again

title: “Huge business hotel”
text:
I have attended many shows at this hotel in 20+ years, but this was the first time I stayed overnight as a guest. The lobby is always packed -- very high energy. The rooms (sleeping area ) are large by NY standards and fairly well appointed (including an in-room coffee maker), although the bathroom is on the small side. Trying to call down on any of the pre-set buttons (like guest services) results in a constant busy signal -- our TV remote did not work, but we had to call the operator to have her locate someone to send a replacement, and although that was done on a timely basis, the person was in such a hurry that he wouldn't even come in or wait til we had tried it before he left.
Location is good -- more or less midway between Times Square and Central Park. If you don't mind madhouse crowds or not-too-personal service, this hotel is perfectly fine.

title: “Go Elsewhere Unless You Like Noise and Bad Attitude”
text: There are two big problems with this hotel: bad attitude from the staff and noise. I booked a lengthy trip, and when I checked in the front desk manager said that there were only 2 rooms available: one right next to the elevator and at the corner of two busy streets, and the other right next to the electrical equipment room, where you hear the elevator rumbling by constantly. The next morning, the day desk manager said there were many vacancies and moved me to a room where I could hear the constant rumbling of the subway. I'm not kidding. Then he told me that for the rate I paid, that was it--despite the fact that entire floors were shuttered because "business is slow." Well, it's no wonder that business is slow. My request to speak with the General Manager was ignored. Who needs this type of treatment when you're trying to enjoy your vacation. Do yourself a big favor. I've traveled to SF many times, and you can find many better places to stay. I got a very good price on my reservation--but there's no such thing as a free lunch.

title: “ONE OF THE COOLEST HOTELS YOU COULD STAY”
text:
I stayed at the Pheonix for 4 nights and couldn't have wished for anything better. From the minute we arrived the friendly staff made sure we had everything we needed, from tips on where to which sights to visit, where the best shopping was throu to where we could find a late night cocktail in the neighborhood. The rooms were generous in size, spotless and had a lovely aesthetic overlooking the palm tree court yard and pool.
I'm not into overpriced up market hotel and prefer more intimate, boutique hotels and this was one of the coolest places I've stayed...
I was visiting SF with my mom and the hotel staff made sure we had a room way from where the pool action takes place and every night was restful and relaxing. (tip - it can be a little on the noisy side until 11pm but who goes to sleep before then?)
Everyone was advising us about how dangerous the Tenderloin area is but honestly I'd rather stay there amongst the colorful characters and cheap delicious restaurants then be in a tourist trap any day. Plus it was only a 5 min bus ride into the Civic and a $5 ride to the Mission. 
Five stars.

title: “What a great find!”
text: This hotel was such a great find. The hotel is inviting, nicely decorated, and has friendly staff. We checked in at 11:45am and they had a room ready for us. Our room on the 3rd floor was spacious with vaulted ceilings. At 3:00-4:00 on Saturday the hotel hosted a chocolate fondue bar for guests. The aquarium is literally right next to the hotel and 1 block away from PowerPlant Live, restaurants and shopping were right in reach too. We upgraded to the Harbor Nights package for an extra $10 and we recevied free continental breakfast (if you want to order off the regular menu they will take $7 off - $14 total), 2 free drinks in the hotel bar, and 2 free drink passes to each of the bars at PowerPlant Live. FYI, parking is not included in the hotel price but there is plenty of parking near by.

title: “My Favorite Hotel in Baltimore”
text:
I stay in Baltimore 5-10 nights a year and have stayed at many different hotels. This one is the best option by far. The hotel just gives of an air of luxury. The staff is always helpful and friendly, the location is great, and the views (no matter which way your room faces) are spectacular.
This is one of those rare hotels where walking in feel like being at home and yet on vacation at the same time!
I always try to stay here when coming back to Baltimore. The only reason it does not get 5 stars is the price. I know that you get what you pay for, but prices have actually gone up significantly since the Four Seasons opened across the street.

title: “Great hotel!!!”
text:
Surprised my husband by booking this hotel room for his birthday!! It's a great and fancy 5 star hotel. The location is awesome, right on the river walk.
The rooms are nicely decorated and well maintained and fairly large. 
The view from the window especially at night is breath taking.
They also provided good breakfast and voucher credit for early dinner. Dinner was mainly pasta/macaroni, salads etc. for the vegetarian options.
The inside of the hotel is gorgeous and royal looking.
We would come back here definitely.

title: “the perfect choice!!”
text: this hotel is wonderful because to put it plainly, its extremey affordable, clean, and provides a hot complimentary breakfast, free wifi and laundry services. The 24 hour staff at the front desk was very helpful, one of them even let me use the laundry room after hours, as i was in a bit of a jam. The location was great, myself, being a walker, walked to hollywood and highland within about 40 minutes, and the very nearby griffith observatory/hollywood sign, and trendy Los Feliz area were even closer. I got well acquainted with the metro system as well. if anyone is looking to get to sunset strip, hop on the 2 express, which is just a hop, skip and a jump away at sunset blvd and north vermont.the subway system is located here as well and is very easy to understand. it took me about 5 minutes, once on the metro, to get to the chinese theatre. anyhow, this hotel superceeded my expectations by far, and i would highly recommend it.

title: “PIMPS! You need to print something? FIVE DOLLARS!!!”
text: Pimps. I paid US$150.00 fro a room for the night...and then they wanted another 5 dollars to let me printup 2 pages of an email. Just like those licorice candies...CHIZZLERS! Oops - Twizzlers!

title: “Nightmare stay and brought home bed bugs!”
text: This is the worst experience I've had in staying at a hotel. Our room was in a building facing a ditch and fully loaded trash bags right outside our door. The restroom looked and smelled like it had not been cleaned in weeks. It even had nasty stains. There was no shower curtains and not pillows. The fridge was dirty and still had food items from a previous guest. The tv did not work. We finally asked to be changed to another room when we saw roaches come out! The attendant said that the previous guest had been there for two months and probably it had not been cleaned after that. Unbelievable!!! why did we get that totally unacceptable room in the first place! The only thing that I have to compliment is that the attendant was decent enough to give us two rooms instead since they had no more rooms with two beds. The last rooms were ok but the worst part is that right after I came back I started getting covered in bites that got infected. The dermatologist confirmed it was BED BUGS! I keep getting bites which makes me think I must have brought them home and Im having a hard time getting rid of them. Whatever I saved in booking this hotel through priceline I have paid ten fold in drs, medication supplies, not to mention the distress and embarrasement of being covered in ugly bites! I wish I had looked at the reviews before I booked this room. Dont do the same! stay away!!!!!

title: “Very nice - great value”
text:
No complaints. I signed up for the "Zip-In" check-in, which took no longer than 10 seconds. Room was very clean, with a small refrigerator and microwave. Comfortable bed. Bathroom was fairly standard, but the curved shower curtain rod is a nice feature. Neutrogena amenities. My room was very quiet - I was not disturbed by any noise from other guests, but I don't think the hotel was fully booked. Breakfast is not included - I did not eat it but a nice-looking buffet was available for $8.95. 
I think this hotel was a good value for the price I paid and I would stay here again.

title: “Not perfect but ok.”
text:
I am laying in bed at this hotel as I write this review on my phone. It's not as bad as some of these reviews make it out to be. Location isn't ideal. Try not to stay in room 202 however. The floor of the room above is squeaky and I can hear EVERY flex of the person upstairs' toes. Quite annoying at bed time or 6am when they got up.
The bed bugs story in an earlier review is FREAKY especially considering I'm laying in the bed right now but honestly I don't see anything remotely unsanitary about this room or I'd be in the lobby sleeping in a chair right now.
The location is ok but you do have to pass through an area of town that's not so great to get here. There is a bar downstairs on the corner that is currently filled to capacity with convention partiers. I cannot hear a peep from it. Seems to be the most soundproof bar I've ever seen! 
No real complaints other than my squeaky ceiling. (sigh)
Checked for bed bugs, do not see anything of the sort but if that changes I'll sure as heck revise this review.
Overall I'd recomend this place for those on a budget.

title: “Reservations are merely "preferences"”
text:
My wife and I had a one night reservation to break up a leg of a Hawaii to Alaska flight. We made the reservation about a month in advance. Upon arrival at 8:30 p.m., we were told that the hotel had no King Bed (which we had reserved), and that my reservation was merely a "preference" which the hotel could decline to accommodate, and they could only give my wife and I double beds. They would not reduce my rate (I paid about $250) or do anything to make up the problem. Usually, if a hotel can't give you the room you reserved, they make some attempt to make it up, but not Hyatt.
The rooms themselves were fairly roomy for San Francisco, and the service by the restaurant staff and bell attendants was very good. The Union Square location is also convenient. However, there are obviously better choices near Union Square.

title: “Repunzel Repunzel”
text:
The recently opened club 49 has commandeered one of the elevators in what is already an inadequate system. We found very few elevators working. the crowds would build withing the holding area as the same letter would be given to all. Asthetically it is a beautiful system, and had it been built to just shuttle guests, it might have been adiquate, however with the various clubs, restaurants, theaters, shops, catering facilities, and gawkers we were frustrated to no end... like Rupunzel being held prisoner on the 33 floor while our dinner reservations slipped away.. 
And speaking of the Club 49....We inquired about it and were enticed to go up. at first we were on the fence until she offered to dicount the cover by half on on the girls and free for the guys. It was still too much..Sit in the lounge on the 8th floor and watch groups of people ride up and the previous group escaping back down. The view is fantastic but the sparsely populated club was way too loud and occupied by gangter rappers grinding up against their "companions" 
Everything else about the experience was excellent, fortunatley you dont need to go to the club with so much to offer in NY...but the elevators are a deal breaker for me.

title: “Average Union Square Hotel”
text: Stayed at the Hilton Union Square for one night in May. I am Hilton Gold and our room looked nothing like the pictures you see here. It was very dated and in need of a refresh. As a Hilton Gold we received a complimentary breakfast -- a pastry and coffee from Starbucks. They do not have an executive lounge, which is quite surprising for such a large hotel in the heart of San Francisco. For the price (~$200), it was not worth it. We would have been better off staying near the airport for a fraction of the price and riding BART into the city for the day.

title: “Fantastic value”
text: Location, location, location. Beyond a doubt, the best value in NYC. This is a no frills hotel...the rooms are very, very small, but reasonably clean and the staff was very pleasant and helpful during our stay. Be sure you try breakfast the Dunhill Cafe right next door. I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone looking for an inexpensive place to stay in the city.

title: “Worst Hotel EVER!! Only stay here if you like false promises!”
text:
Readers, I severly warn you to never stay here!! I booked my rate online, went down, to Boston checked in, everything looked ok.... The next morning they had raised my rate $200 and refused to lower it even though I had the confirmation email!!
I will never stay here ever or any other Marriott if possible because of their total lack of responsibility. It has been almost two months and I am still trying to find a way to get them to honor the rate booked!

title: “Fantastic hotel with great staff”
text: We loved the Fairmont, where we stayed just for one night in a gorgeous suite with an incredible view of Chicago. The room was spotless, and every detail in place. Everything that was supposed to work, did work; not a speck of dust or debris anywhere, and a fresh clean smell; nice furnishings and a very comfortable bed. The staff was also top-notch: professional, pleasant, helpful and friendly. The location is convenient to Michigan Avenue, but just far enough off the main drag to be a very quiet and peaceful location. My only complaint would be that our room was next to the elevator and while we did not get a lot of hallway noise overnight, we did get some sound effects from the elevator shaft itself; however, it was nowhere near as bad as I'd anticipated when we saw the location of the room, so I think their soundproofing is pretty good. We didn't even hear a peep from the fire station across the street.

title: “Hip decor, comfy and clean”
text: Spent the night at the Hotel Tomo while attending a function in San Francisco. The price was right, the beds were comfortable and the rooms were immaculate. I loved the flat screen tv, the excellent wireless connection even from the 8th floor. Our room had a balcony facing east with an excellent view. The staff was very welcoming and helpful, the housekeeping staff never failed to greet us and we were lucky to snag one of the onsite parking spots. Hotel Tomo is close to the Fillmore street nightlife and a short drive to downtown SF or the wharf. It was quiet and relaxing, much more of a residential area than a business district. The onsite restaurant served a decent breakfast with a bottomless coffee pot of excellent coffee, what more can you ask for? I will definitely be back.

title: “just ok”
text:
We booked this via Priceline. When we asked for a king bed, they charged us an extra $20. Sure, whatever, it's just 1 night. They told us we were being put in a "preferred room". The view was of an air shaft. The room was tiny. The bed was comfortable, but the hook on the bathroom door was really low and I still have a scar from walking into it and scraping up my arm. The water pressure in the shower left much to be desired. We were "lucky" to get free wifi that weekend. How do places still charge for wifi? 
Our room was around the corner from the elevator so we were treated to loud talking in periodic bursts throughout the night. As we had driven 7 hours that day, it was frustrating. 
The people we encountered were nice, but the hotel itself was nothing special. I certainly wouldn't go out of my way to stay there.

title: “Horrible Service”
text:
I was very disappointed in the treament we received from the front desk reception. They were very arrogant and not helpful at all. If something was inconvenient for them, they just wouldn't do it. 
I left my wallet there and housekeeping was very nice. They recovered it for me and turned it in to the front desk. After it was turned over to the front desk, I had to return to the hotel to get it 3 times because they could never find a cashier to open the safe.
That was just one example. Really, it was one thing after another. I'll never stay there again.

title: “"Excellent"”
text: This is are second time here and the rooms were large and the breakfast was outstanding. Good value all around!

title: “Great location and great price.”
text: Front desk was very helpful, was delayed on my flight arrival, called ahead and were very accommodating. Parking was a tad but pricey but still do-able. The room big and very clean. Would definitely stay here again and again.

title: “enjoyable”
text: Second stay here. Very pleasant. Office staff very helpful and friendly. Breakfast served until 9:00am. Unfortunately they ran out of waffle mix about 8:40. When I told the desk person he said he would take care of it. The kitchen help apparently didn't want to mix another batch for the last 15 minutes so he just walked around. I again reported this to the desk, and at 8:55 he brought some out and just kind of glared when I got some. Only sour note for our stay. Will go back again.

title: “need to learn to take care of customers”
text:
BOO! These guys have a racket on the internet access. When I pointed out that their posting on Hotels.com was incorrect (misleading at best), the posting listed internet access available in every room in the bullets points. You have to go to a separate tab to get the information about it being a paid service. They refused to comp me the service. I am here for professional conference and I need access for my work. They need to learn that their brand is effected anytime your name is involved.
The room is clean, the housekeeping staff is really sweet. Management you should take note.

title: “Great Decor and Awesome Rooftop Lounge”
text:
I wish I’d brought my camera and some extra time to stay at the Gansevoort. It was a quick trip to NYC and I only got about 7 hours in my suite – 6 of which were sleeping but what a room it was! I had a corner 3rd floor suite with two balconies – one that overlooked the cobbled street in front of the property and another that looked at an Irish bar across the street. As someone who appreciates lighting, I was thrilled to have so many options in the room for setting ambiance such as illuminating just the artwork, dimming the bedroom lights, only using the sconces, etc. I could have easily moved in, especially if it meant daily use of the fabulous rooftop bar and pool. 
The front desk staff was friendly and efficient, especially Mike who checked me in. I do have to say I found the bed a little uncomfortable, the traffic quite audible and the shower had issues such as a showerhead that didn’t move and sprayed the opposite wall when not blocked by my body and a shower curtain that barely reached the tub and splashed water on the floor, but seriously who cares? Look where I was staying - it was a beautifully-decorated suite at the Gansevoort and I loved it!

title: “Great Breakfasts - small rooms”
text: Enjoyed my stay here at the Library hotel, Its in a good location, easy to get a cab outside, very nice buffet breakfast, the only downside was the room size, it was tiny, even though I had upgraded the room and paid extra - they either forgot to upgrade me or the rooms really are small, anyway its New York so you won't be in the room for long anyway, so don't let that put you off.

title: “Kids loved the view”
text: We found this through a travel site for a great price. Got in late after flying from Atlantic Coast, and our room was ready and comfortable. The hotel is a little older, but our young kids loved the view of the bay. It was definitely better than being cramped up at my relatives house.

title: “Great service, staff, and atmosphere!”
text: For my first trip to Los Angeles, my stay at the Renaissance made this experience very enjoyable! The staff was very friendly, especially the restaurant staff. Because of their service and attentiveness, I returned multiple nights for dinner during my stay. The hotel is also conveniently located near the airport and car rental facilities. I would definitely recommend this hotel to those who are looking to be outside of Los Angeles at a great deal!

title: “A charming olde world hotel with lots of complimentary extras”
text:
We had a really great stay at the Queen Anne!
Reception was efficient and reasonably friendly, and at check-in we were given an upgrade to a lovely room with two large beds, a bay window and fireplace. 
The hotel was old-fashioned and very charming, with lovely old antiques on all floors, and a very welcoming lounge which offers complimentary tea & coffee all day, and sherry in the late afternoon. There's also free internet at reception. 
Our room was huge, the beds were comfortable (a little soft for my husband's liking) and the bathroom was small but functional. The working fireplace was a lovely bonus, and we really enjoyed our fire in the evening. The room was also very clean. The hotel's car park was right across the street and we could see the car from our room. Breakfast was adequate in variety but plentiful, and it was funny to see a large queue form at the door of the dining room before they flung it open for the weekend breakfast crowd! There's also a convenience store right across the street - very handy for supplies. We found the hotel very quiet and heard no noise from the street or other guests' rooms. Hard to think of many negatives for this place ... it's not the Hyatt, but if you like kooky old hotels with a lot of character (and a few kooky staff for that matter), you'll find it here. 
We felt very welcome and comfortable here, as though we were house guests, and would definitely return if ever we were in SF again.

title: “Average Sheraton”
text: Came to Boston for a Sox game and stayed at this Sheraton. It is an older hotel because our room looked like it had been poorly refurbished. The bed and furniture was nice and the bathroom was ok, but the room itself looked very old. Maybe we got a bad room in the south tower. The lobby was beautiful and everywhere else was great so maybe we just got a lemon of a room. The person at the front desk was very pleasant and the valet guys were great and let me park for a few extra hours for free, which was very appreciated!! I usually stay at the Westin which is my preferred place to stay in Boston, but we decided to try the Sheraton. I think from now on we will stick to the Westin Copley Square if it is available.

title: “Could be worse, could be better”
text:
This is a downtown hotel with a downtown price and a recognizable name, so expectations tend to be fairly high. In some ways it's good, but overall it left me cold.
The location is across from the minor-league ballpark, a couple of blocks from Beale Street, and about a half-mile from the convention center. Needless to say there are a ton of great restaurants within walking distance (I recommend the Texas de Brazil). There is the usual rip-off valet fee ($20/night) that you expect in downtown hotels, but at least they give you unlimited ins and outs, and it's the same at all the big hotels in Memphis. Be warned, they don't have enough valets so in the morning you'll wait a while to get your car, and in the evening there is a line of cars on the street waiting to get in to the overly small driveway.
Check-in is fast and friendly with a complimentary warm cookie. The hotel is an inner-courtyard style, with glass elevators and a nice area to meet with your colleagues. It seems to be either a renovated old hotel, or an homage to some old-time hotel. There is a TGI Fridays off the lobby, which is unremarkable except that they give you a coupon for a complimentary breakfast buffet there each morning, and it is excellent. There's even an omelette guy.
Upstairs, the hallway carpets are kind of worn and decrepit. The room door was very hard to open probably due to swelling in the humidity, but when I complained they fixed it right away. The room was very small but had a kind of elegant/modern/deco decor to it. The bed was comfortable, but the 7 assorted pillows all flattened to nothing when you put your head to them. The A/C was effective but had some annoying clicks when it kicked on and off. The bath amenities were very nice. The wireless internet worked very well, and while there were very few outlets in the room, there was one on the work desk which was nice. There was a flat-screen TV, but there were only like 10 channels, and not the ones you'd expect. Translation: have stuff for the kids to do, cause the TV isn't going to occupy them.
The room was clean, but the window situation ... there were horizontal wood blinds that had no open/close control (it was broken off); there were drapes, but the pull-thing to open and close them was broken off and laying on the window sill; and there was a disgusting old towel stuffed in around the window frame.
So, overall I'd say it's "okay" but not great; I'd stay here again but only if the company was paying for it.

title: “Just Okay”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for three nights in August 2005.
This is just an average hotel, though it had some good advantages: inexpensive, microwave, fridge, 27" TV. 
Disadvantages were: small rooms, not enough towels, tiny pool, there is a charge for the safe in the room, even though it is part of your room, breakfast was terrible with stale bagels, cereal and aweful coffee, noisy interstate location, shower did not drain well, located in an industrial area.
I would not stay here again on a return trip to San Antonio.

title: “Sooo close to Hollywood Bvld and yet like a quiet Tropical Oasis”
text: We stayed in room 207 on the top floor over looking the beautiful pool. We booked the Magic Castle Hotel from Australia because of great trip advisor reviews, the great price and its great location - literally a minutes walk to the action on Hollywood Bvld. (Due to the Aussie dollar being so good we wanted to pay upfront from Australia - our emails were answered immediately no matter what time of the day or night I emailed and the paperwork required was sent asap. When we arrived we could check in straight away. Our apartment was very clean, very spacious and had been renovated - I purposely requested on on the top floor overlooking the pool (as we read these were the best and we were not disappointed). Think Melrose, think retro, think wonderful friendly helpful staff who provide you with a home away from home and you have the Magic Castle summed up. We could not have wished for a better place to stay. We saw the sights all day and Jason told us where a large fresh and very cheap supermarket was (about a 5 min walk).
