So we cooked everynight in our wonderful kitchen and then sent the kids down with a list for the 24 hour FREE mini bar and free DVD's (where do you ever get that) and sat and ate popcorn, chips, sodas and chocolate whilst watching free movies on our flat screen tv each night (that was a holiday in itself to us). We had one minor issue with a window not closing properly and the maintenance man appeared immediately and fixed it!. The pool was heated, clean with loads of pool toys -the kids had so much fun. A generous breakfast was presented around the pool each morning with delightful pastries and the Darren the owner/Manager was always on hand for a friendly chat. In fact on our last day he let the kids run wild with the mini bar and their backpacks were filled with goodies (thank you for those delightful Hershie Bars that you can't buy in Australia). They even organised to check-us in online on our return flight and print off our boarding passes. I could go on and on about all the positives as I can't find one negative about this wonderful place. It truly is a hidden little gem. We will definately stay here again and are recommending it to EVERYONE!!!

title: “We would NOT stay here again.”
text: The staff was not friendly at all. It was very LOUD (bunches of people in the lobby). The hotel was dirty and the room smelled. We wanted to stay at the Embassy Suites down the road but, they were full so, we were given this hotels number instead. It was definitely not worth the price.

title: “Terrible!”
text:
If you value your safety do not go. High crime area. We parked our car, locked it, within 15 feet of the front door. We were gone less than 10 minutes only to find that our front window was knocked out and the car burglarized . Happened on a Sunday morning at 9 am. Manager was very unconcerned and of course nobody saw anything. The night before we tried to go swimming - the pool was filthy. Overall definitely not up to Hyatt standings. No security, no cameras, no service. 
Lastly we asked the manager if they had had breaking like this recently to which she replied "I cannot release that information". Ummm

title: “Very Pleasant Stay...Again...”
text: This was a return stay at the Michelangelo and it was another wonderful 3 night visit. Have to say that some of the negative comments are surprising. I have always found the staff to be helpful and courteous. Also, the comment about rooms near elevator is credible, since when the elevator arrives for you, there is a loud "ding" that i know would disturb me if i were close. But the comments about street noise is simply part of being in NY. I've stayed at a few places and it is difficult to escape....I find this hotel to be pretty quiet in comparison and i have yet to hear much from other guest above or next to me...The beds are quite comfortable. The coffee service (with some scones, croissants) is very much appreciated and i only wish it was available a little earlier than 7am. But remember there is a place called Duke's Cafe on same block that is open 24 hours and has anything/everything you could need to eat...the fitness center is pretty weak, way down in lower level in small room; but the few pieces of equipment they have are okay. But if you want more than this, I think they have relationship with club nearby if you want to pay up. All in all the location cannot be beat and if you can get a good room rate, I highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Typical courtyard”
text: Typical courtyard would return if in area I like the new F&B concept

title: “My 19th stay in Savoy Suites!”
text: The hotel is in a residential neghbourhood, rather than being in a very central area, but despite all the choice of hotels, this is always my 'home away from home'. Delightful staff, huge well equipped bedrooms, the most comfortable beds in the whole world!, free shuttle bus to the metro (but I mainly use the frequent buses which stop very nearby). And free admissiion to Washington Sports Club.... And free wi fi!

title: “The service was excellent, the room clean and comfy, the breakfast, early and late evening receptions were a nice bonus.”
text: Clean and comfy rooms, polite and helpful service and an affordable price. Even my "picky" wife was pleased!

title: “Good location but hotel has other issues.”
text:
Just finished 6 nights here. Whilst the rooms were clean and the location fantastic, they really could brush up in other areas.
Firstly we booked b&b for a family of 4 yet didn't get "vouchers" for our children. Wasn't too fazed as the breakfasts next door were nothing at all special, especially as you could only have a cooked breakfast. Great if you want to have a healthy start to the day... not!
Secondly this hotel has a real noise issue. Permanently people running around screaming. At times it felt like a youth club what with the hordes of teenaged here an taking over the pool and communual areas.
Lastly we didn't find it dissapointing to be told that if we wanted a drink the courtyard we would have to go to a 7/11 and buy drinks to drink there. I don't think we have ever stayed at a hotel of this size without even a small bar... My wife wasnt too excited at the idea of drinking wine from a bottle out of a brown bag!
Not an unpleasant stay but would not return as plenty of other options....

title: “Clean Motel 6”
text: This is just a regular Motel 6. They were very busy the two nights I stayed. The rooms have recently been painted and new laminate flooring installed. The showers looked to be new as well. It was nice and clean.

title: “Great Stay - Very Relaxing”
text: We stayed in a Signature Suite for 3 days in March; thoroughly enjoyed the experience. The swimming pools / jacuzzis were terrific, especially the one buried in the cliffs near our suite. Breakfasts were great and affordable. The tennis courts need to be updated somewhat, but otherwise just fine. Service was outstanding. Really enjoyed and hope to return.

title: “Lovely hotel in the heart of Seattle”
text: I stayed at the Alexis Hotel years ago and my condo was not far away when I lived in Seattle. Over the years the Alexis has maintained its high quality, friendliness and great service. The location is great--a short walk to Pike's Place Market, a run along Puget Sound, and very close to the funky art, clothing and shoe stores in Pioneer Square. The staff was friendly, efficient and helpful and the room was great. I highly recommend the Alexis if you are planning a trip to Seattle.

title: “At the Heart of San Francisco Shopping”
text: Tremendous hotel! The service was excellent, very accommodating and helpful. Exquisitely clean and comfortable rooms. We didn’t request one but they offer hardwood floor rooms for allergy sufferers. Great location, in the heart of the shopping district. Not a long walk to Chinatown or Nob Hill. Less than a block to a cable-car turnaround that takes you to the Wharf/Ghirardelli Square without any transfers. Parking is expensive but what isn’t in San Francisco?!! I recommend the 5th and Mission parking garage, $30 for overnight versus $40+tax at the Parc Fifty Five, plus, you get a nice walk! This was one of our top 3 vacations(as of June 2007)!!

title: “Wonderful Botique Hotel in Theatre District”
text: The Dream Hotel is located in the heart of the Theatre District. It is in close proximity to transportation (trains/buses), excellent restaurants, museums and the midtown business district. The Hotel has an on site restaurant clled Serafina which provides very good food at reasonable prices. The check in was friendly, efficient and quick. The staff at the front desk go out of their way to make you feel welcome and accomodate specific requests. My room was exceptionally clean with a relaxing decor. The mattress was the most comfortable I have ever slept on (I actually got the brand name) and I had 2 great nights of sleet. Don't miss the rooftop bar for great views and people watching. I have stayed at the large chain hotels in this area and in the future my choice will be the Dream Hotel. My thanks to the staff. Frank Shea

title: “Better options in the area”
text: The 4 Points Sheraton is in a great location, but the hotel was very average and felt overpriced. There are better options in the area that offered more convenient food, business center, or better health clubs. The rooms were clean, but very much a standard hotel room. They do offer a large variety of pillow options. The staff made up for alot of the plainness by being extra friendly and helpful.

title: “Terrible - avoid this hotel at all costs!”
text:
Had a horrible stay at the Sheraton Dallas. The rooms were not clean at all. Dirty bathrobe was left on my bathroom door, hairs were in the bed, mud on the bathroom floor, air-conditioning didn't work, coffee creamers were expired and came out in chunks.
When I tried bringing my concerns to the hotel management via email after my stay they blew me off and said there was no record of any of this in the night managers log, essentially blaming me. Forgive me for not calling the night manager. I had just traveled internationally to be there and had not slept in 2 nights. My first thought was not to talk to the manager.
Don't even look at this hotel! Not worth it.

title: “American Girl Trip with the Nieces”
text: We only stayed one night at the Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers but it was wonderful. I went with my sister, mother and two nieces (ages 6 & 8) for some sight seeing and to go to the American Girl store for lunch and shopping. The hotel is a short walk to Michigan Ave and only 10 minutes to the American Girl store. We discoverd that the hotel is a stop on the Double Decker bus tour, Bonus! Perfect, since we were exhausted from all the walking we did during the day. Our room was very comfortable and the beds were AMAZING! We will definitely stay here again.

title: “Great Boutique Hotel Off Times Square”
text:
I had been trying to get a 4* hotel on Priceline for 3 nights over the weekend but the Saturday night was too expensive so I split my bid and got the lovely 4* Benjamin for Sunday and Monday and the 3* Mela for Saturday.
I was not disappointed and personally I would rate it at 3.5*.
It is either new or has been recently renovated and my room was pristine. It was, however, extremely small with a small double bed. That was fine for me by myself but it would have been cramped to share. I don't know if there are bigger rooms and they put me in a small room because I was by myself, but at the great rate I was paying, I am not complaining too much.
I made use of the hotel's gym which was perfectly adequate and the free wifi - much appreciated. The restaurant was very pleasant and stayed serving until 11, which turned out to be very convenient.
Service was friendly and efficient. I managed to leave a favourite cardigan in the closet and the hotel quickly responded to my inquiry and arranged to ship it back to Dallas.
The great thing about this hotel though is that it is right off Times Square.
The only thing that irritated me was the lack of coffee maker in the room. That is standard hotel equipment and I expect to be provided with one.

title: “Excellent stay, great service, will use again.”
text: My husband and I had the opportunity to stay at your hotel on June 15, 2011. We had to stay in another hotel closer to Navy Pier the night prior, due to a conference. We are fortunate to have had a "back to back" experience with a hotel that cost us over $500 for the one evening, and the Chicago South Loop hotel. After staying at the "other" hotel, we were very refreshed to find a very warm and welcome feeling from your staff. Kevin Rowe was waiting for us at the door and greeted us very warmly, and had taken up our bags to our room. He was very warm and friendly. We met up with him in the elevator a few minutes later, and he struck up a conversation up in the elevator with us. It is this kind experiences that really make us feel as if we belong here. The rooms were very clean and very nice and spacious. We will make a point of recommending this hotel to our friends and family in the near future.

title: “Very nice!”
text: Nice quiet clean hotel. The staff is very friendly and helpful. They also have a good free breakfast. We will stay here again.

title: “Worst Ever! Dont Bother. Far from PHL”
text: Went on priceline.com and got this as a hotel near Philadelphia airport that provided a shuttle. It was nowhere near the airport. It was a 30$ taxi ride. No shuttle from the airport. We slept in the airport instead. Complete joke.

title: “Nice Surprise!”
text: After booking this hotel for the amazing rate I got on priceline I was a little hesitant on what to expect. From the front desk to the room and location I could not have been any happier! I have no complaints! If you are looking for somehere nice, comfortable, friendly, and in a super location, this is the place. I would definitely stay there again!

title: “Attended Women of Faith Conference”
text: We all loved the rooms. Enjoyed the great breakfast. The only thing I noticed was that the front desk staff didn't seem to like their jobs -- polite enough, but barely so, and weren't at all acting like they enjoyed or liked their jobs (or cared whether we came back). I asked the lady I checked in with to see if she could look to see if I was a member of the rewards club, which she promised to do, but didn't. I then asked a gentleman at the front desk on Saturday. He looked it up, but acted like it was a pain. Hotel front desk people generally do not act like that in a nicer hotel, like your hotel.

title: “Beautiful Hotel and Service is outstanding !”
text:
I just returned from a 2 night stay at the Mansion and the staff makes you feel like you are a good friend that has returned. What I love about it is you don't feel like you are in a huge hotel where you are just a number, they greet you by name and aim to please. Drinks in the bar is a must as it is my favorite !! Breakfast on the terrace ,when the weather is nice, is a perfect place to start the day. And ending the day with a delicious dinner in the Library room of the dining room feels like you are eating in an elegant dining room of a friend, nice and cozy.
I have stayed at Zaza,Crescent,Ritz,Palomar,Lumen and Mansion is by far my favorite with the BEST staff/service.

title: “Not bad for its location”
text: The motel is ok, nothing more nothing less. It has good central location, very close to Hollywood blvd and all attractions, subway station, etc. However, I felt like a price is slightly over its amenities. For that price it could've been better, really.

title: “Great Location for Hospitals”
text: I stayed in the hotel while my friend had surgery and you can't beat it for convenience. Parking is attached to the hotel and you can easily walk to several hospitals. The staff was helpful and I was able to store my bags the last day while waiting for my friend to be discharged. The continental breakfast was small but adequate, and the service was quick which is important if you need to eat and get to the hospital. There are many restaurants within walking distance, too. I would definitely stay here again in the future.

title: “great home away from home”
text: This is a great value, and the location is perfect if you need to be in the heart of the medical center, get to Fenway, or have a central spot for the family to go the many wonderful directions touristing / college shopping in Boston. The staff were very warm and accomodating and the Galleria being attached made food and all the little things from the CVS so convenient.

title: “Great Deal”
text: My friends and I stayed at the Renaissance M hotel and found it to be very affordable with a good location. Having booked the hotel off of Priceline it was a great deal for a hotel in the D.C. area. The rooms were not huge, but they were well decorated with a modern flair. We did not stay a lot in our rooms so it was more than adequate for us. The rooms were very clean with comfortable beds. The lobby was attractive. Many places were in walking distance or a short cab's ride away. We ate at the Chinese restaurant across the street one night. The restaurant had inside and patio seating. We found the food to be good-especially the lemon chicken. I would highly recommend the Renaissance M hotel if one can find a good deal at a discount price like we did. I would not however, pay the average price listed which is somewhere around $320.

title: “fantastic value”
text:
Room: We had a very spacious one bedroom suite. It was huge and fantastic. Kids slept on foldout couch. Had tons of room. Huge dressing area, bathroom, etc. Loved it.
Pool: The pool is small and on a rooftop. No lifeguard. I would have expected more from a Fairmont but it's in the city and maybe real estate was at a premium.
Food: The Fountain restaurant was old and tacky. It looks like 1950's disney - aqua green and white painted chairs. Some servers were fantastic, but one was horrible. She is def. not Fairmont material. Bfast was included in our package, but is super expensive otherwise, and I would say not a good value. 
Valet: Car parkers and bell hops are fantastic.
Location: Right in the downtown area, tons to walk to - great great location and on a square where they have a free Fri. night concert series. Good people watching. Also, we were there for 4th of July and could see an array of different fireworks all over the valley.
Convenience: not so convenient to get to your room. We were in a different tower, so drove car up to valets, dropped off, had long walk thru lobby, out a door, across a courtyard, put your room key card into a reader to open the locked door of 2nd bldg, then up the elevator to our spacious suite. If you have small kids or are handicapped, I would demand a room in the main building.
Overall, loved this hotel and the price was fantastic for the size suite we got. What a treat.

title: “Excellent stay, excellent staff”
text:
I stayed at the Marriott with my sister and mother. The hotel is an average one but they employ the nicest, friendliest staff I have ever met. The rooms were adequate, with good sized comfy double beds. Our room was very clean and was cleaned every day. For three women in New York we felt extreemly safe staying here.
The best thing about this hotel was definately the staff. They were so helpful, answering all of the many questions we had, even providing bus timetables for an out of town shopping centre with all the relevant information highlighted.
The hotel was situated close to the New York Library and central to most of the sights. We walked everywhere and although it was tiring, you see so much more of the city.
I would definately go back to this hotel, mainly because the staff made us feel so welcome.

title: “No frills but good stay, I'd stay again”
text: Reading the reviews you'd think people were expecting the Four Seasons. This is an adequate hotel for short stays - clean, decent size, no problems. Staff was very courteous. Easy to get to from highway and prices are good - especially using Priceline.

title: “Standard Marriott, but friendly staff and good position”
text:
Stayed for 3 nights visiting Memphis as a tourist (Beale St, Graceland etc). The position of the hotel is fine if you are prepared to take the trolley into the main downtown tourist area ($1 a ride, and it's fun) or walk for 15 minutes.
Valet Parking is a rip-off, but about standard for city centre Marriotts. 
We did not have a problem with noise - but we had a corner room - you could hear the freeway but not too much of a problem.
The bar is gloomy and unattractive though.
All in all, not a bad place to stay to visit Memphis.

title: “Satisfied my Curiosity but Would not Return”
text:
I and my friend while on holiday in New York took advantage of the lower weekend rates (we paid around $550 per night for a room with two queen beds) to stay at the Waldorf Astoria from Friday to Monday.
The lobby areas were certainly impressive and conveyed very well some of the history of the hotel. They were also extremely busy. This is a huge hotel with a corresponding amount of guests and staff and this can be a bit disorienting.
As stated by many reviews here, the decor is quite faded. The room was spacious but unremarkable, with an old-style TV and old fashioned carpet with swirly green and brown patterns. The bathroom had lovely art deco details (bathroom suite, lights, cabinet) but was fairly small and the paint was peeling off the ceiling. The room windows were extremely dusty and some kind of plastic sheeting hanged over half of the outside of the windows. There was no safe in the room so we had to use the safe deposit boxes area on the ground floor - this was manned 24 hours but inconvenient for storing items which we needed access to every day (eg my laptop, or some items of jewellery).
Internet access in the business centre was quite expensive (I paid around $20 for about 10 mins) so avoid it if you can. 
I was happy to stay there for the 3 days we booked as I always wanted to stay in a grand hotel with history - I would however not stay there again - it's too big, too impersonal, and the decor was just too old for me (and I am 43!).

title: “Close to airport, reasonable rates”
text:
Spent a week here for business. Located close to 410 freeway, so it was easy access to both San Antonio as well as Austin. Very close to the airport and rental car places. Lots of construction in the area, which makes traffic a mess in the mornings and evenings.
Rooms were a nice size with comfortable beds and a sitting area. Good desk for working, with free wired internet. No restaurants in easy walking distance, but some decent places available a short drive away.
Breakfast was fair, with cereal, pastries, toast, waffles. Would have liked some fruit at the buffet for a little variety.
I'd recommend the Comfort Inn for a good, modestly priced stay, particularly if you need to be close to the airport.

title: “Keep looking”
text: I got a great rate ($77) on Hotwire, but this is hardly a 3-1/2 star "customer favorite" as promoted. It is in a good location for access and the room was decent but tired. My main problems were: the parking lot, which filled up at night and was very confusing and narrow to navigate; the general layout was not convenient if you are in the back buildings; the high speed internet was painfully slow, almost dialup speed, and it seemed to go down periodically; the staff responsiveness was poor--I complained about a blinking message light which the operator's suggestions did not stop and it took two days to fix, and the faucet handle that fell off was never fixed. This is probably my last stay here.

title: “Melissa Long, the concierge at the ritz-Carlton Chicago was the best concierge we have ever worked with .”
text: I called the hotel before we arrived and Melissa Long sent us newsletters to help plan our activities. She was always friendly and very knowledgeable.

title: “Pure hotel perfection!”
text:
The staff at the Chelsea Pines Inn gave us the best and most personal service we have ever experienced. The reception is staffed 24 hours a day with the friendliest people making the last week of our honeymoon the best possible. They helped us with restaurant recommendations and reservations, booking a helicopter flight, the best transportation to the airport and even getting us a table at the best drag show in town! 
Our room was bigger than we expected and, as the rest of the hotel, decorated with colorful vintage movie posters. The bed was big and comfortable, the room and bathroom clean and the air condition kept the room nice and cool in the very hot New York summer. 
The hotel is located in the Meatpacking district with tons of restaurants, bars and shops just around the corner. The subway is located a block away giving fast access to northern Manhattan as well. The hotel has a service center with two computers and a printer that is open until 10 pm. 
The breakfast is a mix of healthy options, such as cereal with fresh blueberries, and sweet options such as muffins. Very nice! The hotel has a green and cozy backyard with tables where we had our breakfast every morning. Coffee and cookies are available all day long for those in need. 
When we go back to New York – this is definitely where we will stay!

title: “pleasantly surprised”
text: Was kind of leary because of the reviews I had read. We only stayed for one night and it was a Saturday night. We could hear music a little bit but not loud enough to keep us awake. Check in was fast and friendly. Clerk was accommodating because we wanted a non-smoking. Room was very clean. Two problems we encountered, no vanity in room, had pedestal sink; and no elevator in building. But not big enough problems because it was a great deal overall. I would stay there again if the price was right.

title: “Nice property”
text: Stayed here for a convention. Walking distance to the convention center and close to 6th street where all the nightlife happens. Nice accommodations but ask for an exterior room.

title: “HOTEL METRO”
text: Stayed in New York in The Hotel Metro in 2008 lovely hotel not far from all the centre 2 minutes from Macy's ,lovely rooftop terrace for drinks ,room clean and comfy staff OK ,spent a fantastic week in New York.

title: “Excellent experience”
text: I was very pleased with the atmosphere of the hotel, upon entering the hotel I was greeted by Chef Schlaff,he was very informative. I was very pleased with the cleanliness of the hotel as well as the rooms. I will definitely recommend the hotel to my family and friends.

title: “A Positive Experience”
text: We stayed here in November 2010 and enjoyed our long weekend in Chicago. We did not have a car and were able to walk to the Art Institute, Navy Pier, and do some shopping on Michigan Ave. The lobby of the hotel is fantastic, beautiful, and elegant. The rooms are small and somewhat dated, but clean and have the necessities. Check-in went quickly and smoothly. Overall a nice base for a long weekend in Chicago.

title: “Nice hotel”
text:
Stayed with a friend here for a long weekend (3 nights). Nice sized rooms and tv channels to select, when waiting for the bathroom to become available! 
Just a short walk to the Silver line (free ride) to the airport or to South Station on red line into down town. Tip - buy a 7day MBTA ticket ($18) if staying for more than 2 days, as works out much cheaper for getting around on the underground MBTA system.Can get them on any station vending machine/s.
Better to get breakfast at the Renaissance, just a short walk away as a better choice and cheaper. Can also find restaurants nearby the Renaissance, for evening dinner too. Though would recommend booking a reservation on the weekend, as gets very busy. Surprisingly with local's, rather than tourists?
The Westin Irish bar's menu, is an ok choice and not too expensive, if can't get served elsewhere, like we did on the Saturday night.

title: “Clean, inexpensive, great location, complimentary ear plugs”
text: My husband and I stayed here for the Phish New Year's run 12/2011. When every other hotel in the city was $300+ a night, the Chelsea Inn came in at $170 a night. In the summer it is about $100. Parking was less than a block away for $45 a night. Our room was in the front of the building and on the 4th floor. I liked having the street right outside the window with a fire escape, so I could sit out there and be entertained by what went by, but I suspect the back rooms may be quieter. There are no elevators so if you suffer from any respiratory maladies, or a bum knee, you might want to think twice about staying here. We, on the other hand, love a good physical challenge and a reason to be thankful for packing light. Our room came with a small fridge (which was killer) and fire escape which was like a whole other room for me! After an initial investigation for bed bugs and critters (room very, very clean) we found these complimentary ear plugs. Hmmmmm.......The street is a bit noisy with commercial vehicles stopping on 17th street during the day and at night, a gay club crankin' downstairs called Splash. And Splash has a killer sound system. But we could not hear it on the 4th floor. I can't say the same for the 1st floor, but I just don't know. The folks at the Inn were real nice and we would definitely stay again - but know that the "breakfast" is a bagel OR muffin that is available next door, and you have to take it back to your room. Luckily for us, we partied so hard we didn't need the earplugs and we slep through breakfast.

title: “for that "WoW" experiance your looking for”
text:
Club Quarters World Trade Center – New York
140 Washington Street (Between Albany and Cedar Streets)
New York, NY 10006
Phone: (212) 577-1133
This is my second time in NYC and we wanted to try something different that getting a hotel room in Times Square so we decided to get a room a little farther away from the core of NYC in the financial district. Club Quarters boasts Free Wi-fi, Free chilled water bottles, free coffee and a roof-top restaurant, all for a more than affordable price (if we compare to times square). Now, I was a little skeptical as it’s a no-name brand hotel chain (at least, I’ve never seen others around in other cities) and the pictures posted left me a little dry. When we arrived we were greeted with a smile and enthusiasm (contrary than a few other reviews I have read) and the hotel lobby looked perfect. The location is very fun, close to many of the subway lines and its right in front of the old WTC. 
So, as expected, wi-fi IS free, no catch’s or passwords, there are water stations on every floor with clean, un-used empty water bottles for you to pick up and fill using their water filtration systems AND there is a self-serve coffee machine in the lobby that is also absolutely free. Every morning, we would run down and make cappuccinos and bring them back up to our room. So far so good.. 
We click on the elevator button and in less than 30 seconds our elevator arrives and brings us rapidly to our floor. The hallways smell great and are tastefully decorated. When we arrive in our room, everything is in place as it should be.. a very clean and modern bathroom (shower only, no tub), eco-toilet with 2 flushing modes (not sure if it actually worked properly but sometimes it’s the thought that counts ha ha), our bed and flat screen TV, desk with chain and a 1-seater sofa at the end, along with some storage space for jackets and shoes. “WoW” was the first thing we said when we opened the door. This room was the standard room and it was more than enough. They tempt you with 40$ per night upgrades to suites but unless you plan on spending a lot of time in your room, it isn’t necessary (although we WERE almost tempted LOL). What I really liked about the room was that it looked new.. the toilet counters looked like granite (if they weren’t), new tiles, no cracks, fresh paint and clean when we arrived. That’s really what is important to me when looking for a room. Also, we got the hotel off hotwire and paid about 170$ per night. Last time we stayed in Times Square and paid about 270$ per night at a hotel that is not even close to this place. 
Once installed, we made our way up to the 20th floor, where we took a peak at the restaurant / terrace. It looked great with lots of windows pointing towards the city. A nice view indeed. We didn’t eat their with the exception of a breakfast that was great for 16$’s so I will not comment on the lunch / dinner but the menu looked fine. On the opposite side of the restaurant, you have a sun-room (kind of like a balcony with chairs and tables for you to relax and enjoy the sun and the great view.. from this height, you see ground zero perfectly (along with all the construction going on down there). I was able to smoke a nice cigar and a 6-pack off beer and really relaxed without having to pay for roof-top priced drinks (although, not sure if the BYOB was legal LOL, but much appreciated it was). 
In Conclusion, for a hotel about 15 minutes by subway from times square it was really worth paying less for. I would come back to this place in a second and strongly recommend this place to anyone looking to spend less on nights and more on themselves . This place is rated 4 stars.. I would give it 4.5 stars !!!

title: “Really disappointing”
text: Really quite disappointing. The staff seemed unavailable and distant. There was confusion about the rate I had booked online. The rooms were stale smelling, and not the cleanest. The free breakfast consisted of old muffins, some rolls, and bagels. I expressed my disdain to the manager at the end of our stay, and the impression I got was, "too bad." This hotel essentially runs itself, because of its extremely prime location. The staff doesn't need to put much effort into pleasing the guest, because it will always be solidly booked. You're better off to go off a few miles further south into the downtown area where there is a heavier hospitality competition, and each hotel WANTS to ensure that they get repeat business from you.

title: “Ok old hotel but not for light sleepers”
text:
Stayed three nights here and it was my first time staying in San Antonio in over 20 years. The hotel is definitely an older hotel - the rooms seem dated, the TV is the old tube type, and even the thermostat is the old slider type but the print has worn off so I could not see which way was heat and which way was cold (just had to do trial and error.) But the AC and heat are very noisy. Road noise was not so bad, but of course, could not hear it at all over the AC in the room. Even the ice maker is really noisy--you can hear it all of the way at the other end of the hallway.
The restaurant was nice and the food was good. Service was really good here but I am a light sleeper so I had to change hotels after the third night.

title: “I was happy with this hotel, clean, comfy bed, great staff, great breakfast.”
text: I was happy with this hotel, clean, comfy bed, great staff, great breakfast. To top it off, they have a new shuttle bus that provides transportation to/from the wedding we were attending. Our driver gave us a list of local taxis to call bc we were returning late to the hotel. Makes me want to explore other Hampton's.

title: “Great Location, Great Service”
text:
This hotel was a great find! Compared to the price of most hotels in the area, it was a great deal. Since it was less expensive, I was nervous about booking because in my experience you typically get what you pay for with hotels. However, this place exceeded my expectations. 
Upon arriving, the room I requested was booked, so they gave me a complimentary upgrade to a suite. The room as clean, spacious, and quiet. It was a great location for sightseeing and shopping was very close. Safe neighborhood and public transportation right outside the hotel.
I will definitely stay here again on my next visit!
(The only reason I didn't give it a "5" is because this hotel is not super luxury. However, it is above budget and a great value.)

title: “Pretty hotel but problems with their staff”
text:
On the first morning there, we ordered room service for breakfast. I ordered a side of skim milk with my oatmeal and expected that salt & pepper would be on the tray for my eggs. None of those items were on the tray, and this was after waiting almost an hour for breakfast to arrive. My husband called down to ask for those items and no one brought them as promised. He called again and asked for a manager and was put through to a VM system that didn't work. At that point, I was really irritated and called down myself. They comped breakfast that morning and the next morning but the next morning, brown sugar was missing from the tray for my oatmeal even after I specifically asked for it. We gave up on in-room dining and didn't bother ordering it after that. 
We were less than impressed with State & Lake too. The meal wasn't that great for the price and the service was slow although the restaurant was empty. We also had problems with housekeeping. We didn't want our room cleaned during our stay so we just ordered extra towels ahead of time and thought we'd be ok. Well, we ran out of paper towels and toilet paper so I called the front desk when my husband was stuck on the toilet with no TP. 20 minutes later, no one ever came up with TP so I called down a 2nd time and had to explain the situation in detail for someone to come and help! When the maid finally came, she showed up with TP but no paper towels for the kitchen. At that point, I was done though, you shouldn't have to ask for things 2-3 times! 
The fire alarms were being tested one day and they kept going off in our room which was incredibly annoying too. We called down to the front desk to see when it was going to stop because we were both on business calls when it happened and it went on for over an hour. No one could tell us exactly when it was going to end. 
To make matters worse, my parents had called the concierge and asked for wine and chocolate covered strawberries to be in our room as a surprise one night and the gesture was nice but the hotel charged US for the wine from the mini bar upon check-out! We got it straightened out at the end but it made for a very awkward conversation with my dad when he had to ask if we had been charged for our own gift because even he had problems with the concierge apparently.
We chose this hotel based on a good experience that we had there last year and we were sorely disappointed with everything last week.

title: “Great location!”
text: I stayed here over the New Years holiday for some concerts at Madison Square Garden and couldn't ask for a better location. It is close to Madison Sq., Penn Station and very easy to get anywhere in Manhattan as it is centerally located. I saw a lot of reviews complaining about the room size, but this is NYC, you can't expect a huge hotel room unless you are prepared to shell out a bunch of cash. We had several people sharing the room and it never felt that cramped. The security in the hotel seemed really good and the wouldn't allow non hotel guests upstairs unless they were accompanied by a paying guest with a valid room key.

title: “Didn't stay, but...”
text: I never got a chance to stay here, due to some last minute complications, so I can't much. That brings me to me point: the staff here were very helpful. The aforementioned complications really were last minute, with me having to cancel less that 24 hours before I was to check in. Their site says "cancel by 3 pm the day before arrival" but my email said 6pm. I called to cancel, expecting to pay a fee. But instead, they thanked for bringing the inconsistency to their attention, and never charged me. So even, though i never stayed there, the customer service (at least over the phone) was great.

title: “Love this hotel! Staycation at it's finest!”
text: My family lives in San Diego and when we need a short getaway, our go-to hotel is the Best Western Island Palms. The rooms are wonderful; modernly designed with warmth and taste and plenty of room to stretch out. The staff was great; very nice and always helpful. Our kids love the pool and we always get pool service for lunch which has always been delivered promptly, with the order correct and fresh & hot(when appropriate). Easy, complimentary parking and great water views over San Diego Bay on one side and a wonderful marina view on the otherside, it's a win-win no matter where your room is at this awesome hotel! Thank you Best Western Island Palms!

title: “Great staff! Great Views!”
text: First off let me tell you that I live in the suburbs and staying downtown on a beautiful Chicago weekend is something I look forward to. It was my friend's birthday weekend and we decided to make the best out of it by getting a room and shopping. When I booked my room online, I then called the concierge and spoke to Rhoda who was more then sweet. I told her that me and my gal pals were staying downtown for her birthday for one night. She said that she'd take care of everything! I was worried because that's all she said. When we checked in Friday night, Hannah, who was so sweet and helpful said we had a very, very nice room and asked us what brought us to Michigan Avenue. We told her it was for a birthday and she gave us some suggestions as to where to eat and if we needed anything she'd be at the desk until 11pm. She came around the pod (very rare at most hotels) and showed us where our elevator was. We got up to our room to find we had been upgraded to a suite! There was a table of chocolate covered strawberries and a happy birthday balloon personalized with my friends name by the window. Best of all, there was a birthday card signed by everyone at the front desk. Even the front office director, Sean Vanger had signed it too! The whole night was so fun and breathtaking that we just stayed and enjoyed our room and the gorgeous view! The city is something we treasure and all the great buildings and the views are spectacular! On our way down to the lobby our housekeeper even said good morning and how was our night? As we got off the elevator the bellstaff was eager to see where we were headed and asked us if we enjoyed our stay. Although we were sad to leave, we decided to have them hold our luggage and walked to breakfast. The day was perfect and the staff couldn't be more helpful. If you want a truly amazing experience my friends and I recommend the Westin Michigan Avenue. And to make it a truly memorable one, just let your front desk agent or concierge know why you are there and they will take care of the rest! For all my special Chicago weekends, the Westin Michigan Avenue is our new hotel of choice!! Worth every penny!!!!!!!!

title: “Nice Alternative for Galleria Area”
text:
As a business traveler to Houston many times over the past 25 years, I believe that I've stayed at almost every property near the intersection of Post Oak and Westheimer...through the many name and owner changes. I have spent weeks at the hotels located adjacent to the Galleria while attending training in Houston. I would count the DoubleTree Suites as an attraction to actually consider coming back to Houston for pleasure instead of business. Not being AT the Galleria, only a short walk, was better than being right there.
The rooms are generous suites, with nice furniture and appointments. Our south-facing view was spectacular for sunsets. The small balcony, while impractical, allowed some sense of additional space. We were on an upper floor, the HHONORS level, and found our room quiet and without problem. On a corporate rate, the value for the hotel was outstanding - enhanced with free parking and continental breakfast. The upgrade charge to a hot breakfast was fair.
The bellstaff were very friendly and remembered us as we entered and left through the stay. The front desk were nice, a bit hurried but professional and accomodating. Perhaps the only drawback was the crowd at breakfast - but I understand that there was maintenance on the executive level where breakfast was also served. The breakfast staff seemed flustered with the volume of customers right at 8:00 am.
Again, this is a property easy to recommend and consider as a stay for fun as well as business. If you can get a rate (AARP, AAA, Corporate, Govt.) here below $165/night, it is a no brainer and a super value for the area.

title: “Great 50th Birthday Bash”
text: We wanted to tell you how much we enjoyed our stay this past weekend. Your staff made it a truly special weekend. Vicki Kiang was fabulous as always and we cannot say thank you enough to her hospitality. It's always great to come in and see her smiling face. Let me also so how accommodating Paulina Castanon and Elizabeth Miramontes were. It is so important when you first walk into the hotel and view the elegance and grandeur of the lobby that the staff reflects that as well. These young ladies were so pleasant and attentive to detail and always with a smile. They make that first impression enjoyable and relaxing after a long drive. Each time I walked by they always spoke and acknowledged my by name, which shows they care. You don't find this service in many hotels. I cannot commend the staff enough for their friendliness. Thank you LaCantera staff for all that you do. Missed seeing our favorite Victor Hernandez, but will hopefully see him next time. He's one of the reasons we come back.

title: “Very nice hotel!”
text: We felt very at home in this hotel. Nice breafast, nice with tea and coffee all day, very nice with cheese and wine in the evenings and wonderful when there was live piano music!

title: “Hip Midtown Hotel”
text:
The Bryant Park Hotel is slap bang in Midtown Manhatten, unsuprisingly overlooking Bryant Park that sprawls out from the New York Library.
The hotel is handily 2 Blocks from Times Square, but doesnt attract the mad buzz associated with Times Sq.
Smart Koi (Japanese) restaurant also available in the hotel - quite expensive, but nice food. Reservation required...
Cellar Bar - Smart gothic bar in the basement, drinks are expensive, but this is norm in New York.
We stayed for 7 nights in a Junior Suite - We were housed on the 6th floor. Modern room - Flat Screen LG TV and King Size bed. The bathroom was a real plus point, a massive bath tub, along with a seperate walk in shower. Minibar, but no tea or coffee facilities in the room. Starbucks otherside of BP though.
Being next 2 Bryant Park was twofold. Firstly Byrant Park was a cool place to hang out, a nice green space to chill out in the madness that can be NYC. Free Wireless internet, HBO movies on the big screen in Summer every Monday, clean and very well maintained. HOWEVER the flipside to this can be the noise (music, sounds of rigging being dismantled etc...) from the park - first thing in the morning and also late at night with the big screen. This is very much a personal thing so consider how it may affect your stay. BP has its own web site which I recommend you check out for scheduling and events.

title: “Centrally located in Boston - with lots to do a great, friendly and safe city”
text:
If you've ever considered a trip to Boston, this is an excellent choice in hotels. It is centrally located, near the subway, and a very nice old hotel. 
After taking the free shuttle bus from the airport to the subway, we found it easy to get to the hotel. We basically took the subway everywhere when we weren't walking around. 
We did the murder mystery harbour cruise the first night, which was good fun. The next day we took the red trolley tour and hopped on and off at many attractions, including Fenway Park, and a stop for lunch at the Barking Crab down on the wharf. The trolley tour included a ferry ride across the harbour which was very scenic, and offered good views of the city and the Boston Gardens from the water. There was a nice little street festival in the Italian neighbourhood to the north which was fun. 
That night we went to a Mexican restaurant/tequila bar called Masa, which was just across the bridge, and not too far to walk to. Afterwards we stopped in at the Sweetwater Tavern in the alley just down the street from the Park Plaza, beside the Vault. 
For breakfast, there is an Au Bon Pan restaurant beside the hotel, where you can find some really tasty fresh items made to order. 
Be sure to check out the market, of rent Segways to get around. And rake good walking shoes - there's a lot to see and do. 
A climb up Beacon Hill is worthwhile, as it is a nicer old area, with gas lamps and all. 
These are just some of the things to do - We walked many miles in Boston, and never felt unsafe day or night. 
We love this city, and had no complaints about The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers.

title: “Wonderfully convenient”
text: My husband had his conference in this hotel so we decided to stay here as well and were not at all disappointed. The staff was very friendly and extremely helpful. Our room was very spacious, absolutely clean and to our liking. But best of all was the location of this gem of a place. Located 2 blocks from the 16th Street Mall, and the Theater district (with the Denver Convention Center right next to the hotel), you couldn't go wrong picking this place to stay. Since we're foodies and enjoy theater, this is a place we'll be sure to return to when we visit Denver in the future.

title: “Best Hospitality”
text: Nine Women....Yes 9 women went to Hollywood. Before we left I read many reviews on the Magic Castle Hotel and it always had positive responses. The hotel was located in a great location if you wanted to walk to Hollywood Blvd (stars on the sidewalk), the Kodak Theater and the Chinese Theater. The hotel staff was on the ball and every hotel should be trained by them. If they did not have something you needed they were going to do their best to accomodate you. I have never been treated so nice. The hotel is a little on the older side but the rooms were really spacious and very clean. The daily weather card was a nice touch too. The continental breakfast was tasty and brought in every morning from their local bakery. I really recommend the Magic Castle and if I were to go to HOLLYWOOD again, I would stay their in a skinny minute. GREAT job hotel staff!!

title: “A New Anniversary Tradition!”
text: My husband and I have been getting tickets for a Mariners baseball game for several years now. Each time after the game we would trudge to the car, sit in traffic to get out of the parking lot, and then drive the hour and a half home. Well, no more!!!! On a whim, we made reservations at the Silver Cloud Inn Stadium to stay after our evening game, and we are so happy we did! From the minute we pulled into the hotel, we were treated with great service and people who really seemed to want to do their best to help us. We relaxed before the game, grabbed an appetizer across the street at the Pale Ale Brewery, then leisurely made our way back across the street to the game. After the game, no car and no headache - just a few steps back to our beautiful room. (We requested a stadium view room, which was a fun extra to our trip - we could watch the gate from our window and even see players warming up on the field. Next year we are going to upgrade to a room with a Jacuzzi tub.) We ordered room service desserts (less than 10 minute wait and very tasty!) that night and ate breakfast at the restaurant downstairs in the morning. Our breakfasts were so beautifully presented and so delicious that I took a picture of both plates. We give this hotel a rave review and will be staying there again next year on our anniversary, if not sooner! Thanks, Silver Cloud! *note - We did look in to taking the shuttle to the waterfront. The drivers were very attentive and willing to take us and pick us up wherever and whenever we wanted, but we decided not go so that we could enjoy our time at the hotel and the surrounding area. Seems like a fantastic service!

title: “Relaxing experience in NYC”
text:
We booked this hotel as part of a package holiday and stayed there 3 nights on a room only basis. The location was ideal and accessible to many of the places we had planned to visit. One of the attractions for us became the wonderful and extremely popular cafe next door to the hotel which served a fabulous breakfast and range of dishes to cater for all your needs. 
Back at the hotel our room was clean and comfortable with a flat screen TV and we were provided with fresh towels each day. The complimentary soap, shampoo etc were replaced each day which took away from lugging around these daily necessities. This hotel is extremely busy and it took between 20 to 30 mins for us to be allocated a room upon our arrival. We were able to access wi-fi from the reception area where many of the guests can be found sat on their laptops as there is a charge for access to this service. Both my husband had no complaints about this hotel and thoroughly enjoyed our stay there. The only thing we would advise guests to be aware of is the staff hotel who attempt to recruit guests to take part in a 2 hour presentation involving some type of timeshare with the Hilton hotel group. Whilst we found it difficult to say no to the extremely persuasive young lady at the desk, we did manage to cancel our appointment the following day. All in all this is a good hotel and we would definitely stay there again.

title: “Great hotel!”
text: We just got back from a great vacation in Chicago! The House of Blues was the perfect location for us to get around by public transportation and foot. The room was very clean and the staff was helpful...though we weren't at the hotel enough to ask for much. They also provide more amenities (a blues CD, down comforters and great pillows!) than most hotels I've stayed at. We did have a room facing the club and it was a little noisy when the shows let out, but that was to be expected.

title: “Convenient location in Boston's South End”
text: The rooms were a bit small, but clean and comfortable. Downstairs bar has a nice weekend brunch available.

title: “I am loving Hotel Palomar--goodbye Hilton and SPG”
text:
The economic recession was awful for those of us living for points and status. In the last two years, I wasn't able to travel on business as much as currently. After being downgraded by everyone I had been loyal to for years, I've decided to think about who gets my business now that things are picking up and evaluating whether I got real service or just service I was willing to put up with because I was a top tier member.
Hotel Palomar continually impresses me with the cool stuff they do, but my visit to Chicago has made me believe that they are my new choice when available. I had a meeting run late and was forced to take a red eye, which means I arrived in Chicago at 6 a.m. I was so exhausted and I called the hotel and told them my circumstances and they allowed me to check in early on my day of arrival--real early. I could not have been more thankful.
I get my 4 hours of sleep and go to my meetings and I come back and they have cleaned my room--totally unexpected since I arrived early. Again, amazing service...clothes that were all over the place in a hurry were all nicely folded. The ironing board put away and the bathroom was all neatly organized.
The wine social hour is my favorite part of the Hotel Palomar (along with the fact that they are very pro-dog and I LOVE this new thinking!!). People actually come together in the living room and actually talk and socialize--it's awesome.
And, don't miss their restaurant--always hot.
Hotel Palomar--you were so good to me that I intend to make you my new favorite!!
One other note--the Palomar sits next to Nordstrom, which was a big life saver when I needed a new shirt for dinner.

title: “Nice property- great location”
text:
Nice, clean and upbeat- super location with short distance to the best Jacksonville has to offer in shopping and dining.
One of the nicest bathrooms you'll find at this price - big open shower, thick towels

title: “Comfortable Stay with Great Service”
text: Frankly, I was skeptical despite having seeing the great feedback on the hotel . This was my first visit to US and I was confused with the choices that were being offered. I wanted to stay in hollywood at a reasonable cost. The reservation desk was most helpful in taking my booking and also offered options of pickup. I was given the option of shuttle which was really very convenient since i was travelling alone from Bangalore. My friends were travelling from New Delhi. The checkin was really smooth. The hotel allowed a early checkin for my friends on our request. The rooms are spacious and comfortable. Bathroom was clean and looked new. I had some doubts since some folks had given a review on ageing bathrooms. It had a cooking range with all the necessary utensils, fridge. Towards the end of our stay we used their facilities to cook. Breakfast was complimentary, it was adequate. Wireless was free. unlimited snacks and beverages at the minibar counter in the reservation desk. But i guess the best asset or quality of the hotel is the staff. They are extremely courteous and tried to accomodate our requests. example- when I asked for directions to some stores, the receptionist (jason) printed out the directions from Google Maps. Really I thought it is a great thought process of the Magic Castle Management., by itself the property is very unassuming and boring. But its really the service at this cost that really makes this hotel really good.

title: “Nice Property - Jaded Staff - Poorly Managed”
text:
LeMeridien's around the world are renowned for their lovely appointed rooms, and this was no exception. Nice beds, nice linens, curtains, and contemporary bathrooms. But the staff, who are all former Park Hyatt employees, seem jaded about the recent take over. When I checked in, one young lady made a comment about not having a bellman because it's Meridien, and that we might not be used to the service. 
Also, when they saw that I booked on hotwire and got a discounted rate, they actually told me that I get whatever is left over, that's how it works. So they put me in a double room, which was no big deal at all, I just thought that it was inappropriate to imply that because I got a good rate and prepaid through hotwire that I would be treated differently. 
The service only got worse from there - the next night the 'acting manager' wouldn't allow me to take a bottle of alcohol into my room, citing it was a State of California law. Um, what? I have stayed in many 5 star hotels around the world, and have NEVER heard of such a rule. I surrendered my bottle of alcohol, which they kept until I checked out. The night before check out, I called to get a wake up call for 4AM, and asked them to bring me my bottle of alcohol - she said that the note said that they weren't allowed to, under any circumstances. 
I know some people are reading this thinking I must have been a rowdy guest or an impossible to please person, but that is not the case, I am a physician, stayed in my room alone, and had no intention to consume the alcohol that was purchased in my room, in fact, I had already patronized the mini bar. 
Beautiful property people, however, don't let their poor management spoil your stay.

title: “Fantastic Surprise for my Husband”
text: I used the previous reviews from Trip Advisor to choose the Pacific Terrace for a surprise mini vacation for my husband's 60th. The hotel lived up to all the reviews and more. Location is fantastic, hotel staff very friendly and accommodating, and service above and beyond. I booked the ocean front suite, but did not select any other options. Changed my mind at the last minute, and Angela, the concierge handled everything. We will definitely return. The sooner, the better.

title: “Good stay for McCormick Travelers”
text:
We stayed here for a audition that my daughter had at the McCormick Place, perfect for us for the night, the rooms were nice and clean, our veiw was not that great room 2229 overlooking the water. The smoke stacks that came from just below our room took away from anything that would have been nice to see.
Food was good, beds comfrontable and the overall stay was very nice.

title: “Diamond in the rough”
text: I attended a conference at the Boston Convention and Exhibition Center and took the subway every day. The Andrew stop on the Red Line is only a short walk away. Be sure to purchase a "Charlie Card" to save on transportation costs. Even though I was there for only four days I saved several dollars using that "Charlie Card". When you get off the subway and approach the hotel you may wonder if the neighborhood is safe. That feeling soon went away for me as I had no worries for my safety. The hotel overlooks South Bay mall which has just about every suburban big box store you need -- Target, Best Buy, Marshalls, and others. The hotel is clean and staff friendly. Breakfast wasn't real healthy but tasty and free. Internet access was also free in the lobby and in the rooms. I would return in a heart beat especially after having saved a ton of money at this hotel compared to the downtown hotels.

title: “Very Nice, A Bit Pricey”
text:
This was a great location to stay in Chicago. It was a first visit to the city for 4 days to see primarily architectural sites. The concierge was great, helping with restaurants, car rental, and transit information. Only one bad steer, pointing us to a pizza place that ended up with a 2 hour wait... no thanks! The bar is a great spot for to relax after a full day, but we did not try the restaurant. Lots of good options for food nearby. 
The room itself was very nice. Spacious, and from our 22nd floor east facing room, we had a great view of buildings along the Miracle Mile. We even could see the lake through a couple of gaps between buildings. We are very noise sensitive, but there was nothing to notice, as either our neighbors were quiet or well insulated. 
Overall, it was a good choice, and while expensive, worth the price for all the bad stuff that didnt happen!

title: “Good solid hotel for the money, nice option in place of Palmer House.”
text: In the Loop, near to theaters including Ford Center for the Performing Arts and Palace, and close enough to walk to downtown shopping and Millenium Park. Rooms are not huge by any means but adequate. Very clean, comfortable beds and clean, modern bathrooms. Excellent soundproofing, no street noise could be heard at all. Atrium at the Mall shops right across the street, Corner Bakery Cafe within a block, many other eateries and pharmacies within two blocks. Valet staff attentive and polite. 24 hour onsite fitness center was very popular. Bring your laptop; use of business center involves a fee. Pet friendly hotel. This is a nice option at or a bit less than the cost of Palmer House.

title: “Nice stay”
text: Customer service was great once we arrived. Had I only had the experience over the phone I would have said otherwise since I had the joy of speaking to a somewhat rude person when I called to confirm our stay. Our room was clean and spacious and worked very well having two children with me. The linens were very nice however the beds were hard so I didn't sleep very well. The second night we were there I pulled out the sleeper sofa in hopes that that mattress was softer but it wasn't at all. Matter of fact, there was a bar poking up in the middle.The breakfast buffet was wonderful though. The food was good and the dining area was nicely laid out. When we first got there the tv in the bedroom wasn't working but with a simple call to the front desk it was taken care of. Within 5 minutes a maintenance man came up and fixed it. Overall our stay was very nice. I rated this hotel as average mostly because of the beds and the poor customer service I received by one of the agents there. A good night sleep is very important to me.

title: “Worst five star experience ever”
text: I stayed here with a friend in October 2012. This is our second visit, we gave them a second chance which is all I will say about the first visit. The hotel is beautiful as is the food but the service is appalling. Forgotten breakfast orders, plenty of apologies and promises about not so clean rooms but the piece de resistance was a hypo allergenic duvet which consisted of an old throw. This was pointed out in the morning only to be replaced with a blanket. Come on, go out and buy a duvet in Marshall's. even the holiday inn has these types of duvet for feather allergies. Badly handled and we will never return to this hotel. Avoid at all costs and go to the four seasons. They take the time to train their staff.

title: “Nice hotel and location but not for tall people”
text: I loved this hotel; the service was great; they accomodated by request for an early checkin and checkout with no problem. When the first room was located on a noisy corner they moved me as soon as they had another room. The only faults I found was that the bathrooms are very small. It is impossible for someone like me (6'4") to take a shower without bumping into the faucet control and the amenities shelf and the shower curtain wants to envelope you when the water is turned on. Once outside the shower there is barely room to turn around, when you sit on the toilet your legs stick under the sink....very small. Even in European hostels I have not seen bathrooms this small. I am sure they have room with bigger bathrooms and I would definately ask for that when making a reservation. The only other thing I found is that it could have been a little cleaner and upkept. In the first room, the carpet was fraying and in the second the bathroom wall had soap and water spots on it. Make sure you get a package with free wifi; I had difficulty connecting on the first day but then it was fine for the rest of the trip.

title: “Recommended hotel - with some reservations”
text: We stayed two nights at this hotel and appreciated the always-generous and well-made cooked to order breakfast, the 2.5 hour evening Manager's Reception (free alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages and light snacks) and the standard two-room suite. All the staff we encountered were very friendly and helpful, and the business centre and swimming pool/work-out room and public areas were well maintained and were well outfitted. There were a few drawbacks, however - including a roof top air conditioning unit that was so noisy we weren't able to open our unit's windows at night, the spartan room decor, the horribly over-bright, cold energy efficient coil lightbulbs in all lamps, and the $10 per night parking charge(!!!). Also, our bathroom had some nasty looking dried splashes on the dark wood cabinet doors - a more thorough cleaning is necessary. We would probably return and would probably recommend the hotel to friends and family primarily based on the convenient location, excellent staff and generous food services.

title: “Excellent choice and the price was great”
text: Needed a place to stay close to the airport. Read reviews and made a reservation. The staff was very friendly and helpful. The room was clean and more then met our expectation. We had to be at the airport by 4:00 AM and arranged a shuttle with the front desk upon checkin. The shuttle driver was ready and very friendly. We would definitely stay again and only wish we could have stayed longer. We left more than satisfied.

title: “Very good value hotel”
text:
I'd e-mailed the hotel about booking airport transfers and they recommended Go Lorries who picked us up promptly as arranged. Always nice to get off to a good start.
CHECK IN - smooth and efficient and we were allocated a room on a high floor as requested. Reception staff were very helpful and very happy to offer directions when asked. The only irritation was with the tour booth lady who jumped on us before we could get to the lift and thrust leaflets in my hand trying to sell tours/bus passes etc. I told her we'd take a look, but had already booked a couple of tours online to which she made a face and promptly grabbed them back. Quite amusing really, but it did put us off approaching her again for a couple of days, although I must add that when we did she very efficiently arranged our transfer back to the airport.
ROOM - our room was very well furnished, spotlessly clean the whole visit and the jar of sweets was a nice touch. As mentioned in many previous reviews they're not huge, but considering the extremely reasonable cost not really a problem. We were only staying for 4 nights so didn't want to fully unpack and therefore found it quite difficult to fit both cases in, but again a minor problem which we managed to get round. The bathroom was very small and did feel a bit cramped, but again spotlessly clean and for a short stay quite adequate.
FOOD - we only ate in the hotel restaurant for breakfast on our third day as we were usually out early for tours. The food was very well cooked and reasonably priced, but the waiter although very efficient wasn't particular friendly - just going through the motions would be the best description.
LOCATION - very central with easy access to the cable cars. Particularly good if you like to shop - not really our thing so no reflection on the hotel, but we would probably opt to stay on the Embarcadero if we visit again.
OVERALL - we very much appreciated the complimentary coffee and cookies in reception, especially when going off at silly o'clock for the tours. Also the free WiFi in our room. Extras like this lift The Chancellor a notch above most budget hotels. As I've said in previous reviews, it's all about expectations and this hotel more than met ours.

title: “Exemplary plus:clean,friendly and goes the extra mile!”
text: What a great surprise to find such a wonderful hotel experience in such a large city.There was not a single negative thing that i could write!Friendly, clean always there for you and so anxious to help you and go the extra mile.We will defintely go back here and would recommend to anyone willing to listen!They even remembered our name any time we entered or left the lobby!WOW

title: “Great Business Hotel - Fantastic Location”
text:
5 min FREE shuttle from/to SJC airport. Very friendly front desk, excellent staff. Rooms are nice and roomy, but fancy (it is a business hotel, not a resort). Catered food for business functions are better than most hotels.
Like: Location, Staff, Room size
Dislike: Charge for parking
Insider Tip: Make sure that your room doesn't face the Freeway. Take the FREE airport shuttle to hotel.

title: “New hotel near Time Square”
text:
I guess it is hard to find good mid class hotel in New York. 
This one is really good ONE! 
It's new, maybe one year old on October 2011 and very clean and stylish.
I book corner room for 3 nights at Halloween weekend for about 1000USD total (plus tax)
The room is not huge but big enough for two. Beautiful bathroom with great walk-in shower. View from 22nd floor wasn't the best one in NYC, I was a bit disappointed. 
Location is very good - subway station enhance inside hotel building, Time square few minutes away from Time square and two block away from The restraint row.
Rest on my week in NY had to stay in Millennium UN Plaza hotel which was total nightmare

title: “Truly 5 star”
text:
We were in Chicago last week and stayed for 3 nights at the Trump.
From the moment we got to the check in counter to our departure we had a wonderful experience.
When we checked in instead of the room category that we had reserved they gave a room on the Spa floor with a phenomenal view of the Chicago river and lake Michigan.
Room was spacious and furnishings very contemporary.
Service was excellent and location of the property is great.
Sixteen is a French restaurant and although pricey but the food was very good and the view from the patio was equally good.

title: “OMG!! Pleasant surprise!!”
text: What a pleasant surprise! We booked here for New years Eve because the rooms at the Casinos were sold out. We were in for the Hockey game and New Years Eve party at the Olympia room. Wow!! Were we surprised at the great room, awesome service and convenience of getting on the People mover and to the arena. The room was spotless and the view was tremendous- all for $165.00 New Years Eve!! We will definitely use this hotel when we come to Detroit this summer for Tiger games! Oh, the breakfast buffet was a steal for only $13.00.

title: “Fantastic hotel”
text:
We stayed for 7 nights in September on the 6th floor. We were opposite the office block that leaves their lights on all the time (!) and some of the light does seep in around the edges of the blackout blinds but it didn't bother us. Some overnight road noise (car horns, refuse trucks) but not enough to keep us awake.
The hotel is very clean, the staff couldn't be more helpful and polite. The room was spacious with good facilities. The only thing I would have liked was in-room tea & coffee making facilities for that early morning cup of tea, but drinks are available 24 hours a day in the lobby.
The hotel provides a complimentary buffet breakfast and evening wine and nibbles in the lobby area - which is lovely.
The hotel is located 2 blocks from the subway, and within easy walking distance of the Empire State Building, and Madison Square Park.
The restaurant "Bread and Tulips" is also very good - the service is outstanding and the food lovely - I recommend the mozzarella and tomato sandwich (much grander than it sounds!).

title: “Very Good Value for Families”
text:
Hilton Tapatio is a very good property for families looking for a fun vacation in the sun. We (my wife, myself and two daughters 5 & 9) just returned from a four day stay 4/10 - 4/13 and had an excellent experience.
This resort is a solid 3 - 3 1/2 stars and a good overall value but do not book expecting a 4 or 5 star property. For the $150/night we paid, I was very happy.
All rooms are two room suites with a good layout, comfortable beds and furnishings. The furnishings and room were that of a quality 3 - 3 1/2 star hotel. Very nice and functional, not the bells, whistles and special touches of a 4 or 5 star resort.
The Falls Water Village has 2 large pools, waterslide, 2 hot tubs, bathrooms and pool side service. While the pool area did get crowded, we were always able to find 4 lounge chairs together and the crowds didn't bother us. Basically families with younger children splashing and laughing in the water. The resort has a total of 8 pools (some very small) and the pools outside of the Falls Water Village seemed more quiet, sedate and an "adult setting". They do have some pools reserved for Adults Only.
The pool towels were a bit thin, but we got two a piece and that worked just fine. We found the pool area well maintained and the pool bathrooms some of the cleanest I have ever found. The pool side service was very good and responsive. Just raise the flag on your chair and they were by to assist within a minute or two.
Overall, Hilton Tapatio is a very nice property for a reasonable price. If you want 4-5 stars, luxury at every turn and a quite pool area, this is not the property for you.
If you are looking for a quality spot with very good pool offerings and a reasonable price (vs. $250 + for a higher rated hotel), then you can't go wrong at Tapatio Cliffs.

title: “Excellent.”
text: Good hotel. Clean and friendly. Nice exercise room with free weights. Large rooms. Very good dinner and good bfast. Had to stay in a smoking room though I don't smoke, but I could barely smell smoke. No issues at all. Ill stay here again if I come back to san Antonio.

title: “Excellent value for money”
text: I was fortunate enough to get a suite on the top floor (1803). It's high above traffic, so the noise is acceptable, and it has a small balcony. Room decoration and furniture looked quite new. The room had a desk, a sofa, fridge & microwave oven. There's a safe in the dressing. The bed was quite good. Bathroom is not that big, but well designed and everything worked. Macy's is virtually round the corner. Times Square and the High Line only a few blocks away. Would definitely stay here again!

title: “Comfortable - limited food options”
text:
I stayed at this hotel out of necessity rather than choice - a mid afternoon flight from London meant a late arrival, and with no desire to drive after my flight, an airport stay was required.
Check in was quick - no line at the Hhonors check in position, so I had my key within minutes. The room was fine - nothing to write home about but clean, quiet (for an airport facing room) and comfortable.
My only major gripe at this hotel is the dining options available. You can eat poor quality food in the bar, try and hit lucky at the bistro (a souped up Starbucks for want of a better description), or eat in the either the over-priced Italian, or in the main restuarant.
I, along with my parents who I was travelling with, needed to eat. The menus at all the restaurants are limited, and walking up to Denny's in the dark was not an option, so it was an "all day breakfast" in the main restuarant. The food was cool, the order incorrect and the price was obscenely expensive. "Proper" breakfast the next day was taken at Dennys, where we got 3 truly hot breakfasts for the price of one in the Hilton.
The rooms are fine, the hotel clean and comfortable, and if the dining options could be sorted, I'd have no hesitation in recommending. But the food is poor quality, and massively over priced. I'll tick yes to recommending, but only just.

title: “great location....tiny room”
text:
one block from central park and $99/night...what more could you want?
1. little larger room
2. an elevator that was working when i arrived (6th floor!)
3. hot water 'on demand', not a 3 minute wait
not bad for the price/location...friendly staff..relatively clean... great for individuals on a budget or a couple that likes to be close.. a little taste of 'old new york' here... go for it if you aren't addicted to perfection...

title: “In the heart of NYC”
text: Found the location of the hotel excellent. Convenient access to all of Manhattan by foot or subway and we certainly walked miles but from any direction it is always easy to get back to 42nd street and Times Square. In fact the airport bus stops across the street which was perfect. Four in a room which was why we chose the Westin, and thankfully the rooms were spacious and beds big and comfortable. View to Times Sq from 24th floor. Bathroom was disappointing and shower not heavenly but worked and was clean. Lobby was a little dingy and lots of unused space but overall a pleasant stay.

title: “great place to stay”
text: Great central location, with starbucks across the street, drug store for cold drinks around the corner...We used the bar fridge for our own drinks. The front desk and doormen were more than happy to assist in any way and very friendly. We had one minor issue in the bathroom that was resolved immediately. Would highly recommend this hotel to anyone travelling to NYC. The only downside if I had to think of one, was that the closets were small, so we kept our suitcases in the room out out of the way.

title: “Great hotel, overall very good visit”
text:
We enjoyed this hotel. Comfortable rooms, quiet 14th floor space away from the hubbub of the main street. Elegantly appointed furniture with a very comfortable bed. Bathroom was beautiful with a nice sprig of Orchids in a vase -- nice touch. Service was swift and courteous. Rooms cleaned shortly after our departure. Privacy signs were respectfully regarded. The hotel was close to theatre without being in the thick of the crowds. 
The air conditioning didn't really get cool. I think it was preset at 72 and would not get cooler, no matter how hard I tried to manipulate the thermostat. This made it a bit warm while sleeping under the thick blankets. 
Taxi's may be a challenge to hale right outside the hotel as it's on a one-way street. Better to catch a taxi on the perpendicular streets west of the hotel, 6th or 7th street.
Don't be too loud in the rooms, as the walls aren't very thick. We could hear the couple next door to us copulating. It's not so bad, as this wasn't a protracted or regular even over the 3 night's stay.

title: “Good Location”
text: This was my first stay at this hotel, it was a good location, but needed some improvments. The lighting throughout the lobbey, halls and room was way to dim, even tripped in the pool area because of lack of lighting.
