There is no closet or drawer space in the rooms, but they are clean and the beds are very comfortable. The hotel staff was great, especially Loida!! I stated my complaints and was told they are undergoing renovatons and these items are on the list!! I would book a return stay in the future.

title: “Poor condition”
text:
The best part of my stay was the shuttle drivers. Both were friendly and helpful. Upon recognizing my room.was dirty, I contacted the front desk to let them know of my concerns. These concerns were never addressed. The over all hotel is in dire need of updating or renovation. Overall, I was very disappointed with my stay.
Regards,
David Eckhaus

title: “Holiday Inn Certainly Has Changed!”
text:
I had the pleasure of staying at the Holiday Inn on Nurseryfields earlier this week. I was pleasantly surprised when I walked in to the lobby and saw how nice it was! I had not stepped into a Holiday Inn in over 20 years and couldn't believe the changes.
The room was modern, clean, and had a very comfortable bed.
I highly recommend this property to both business and leisure travelers!

title: “Little out of the way but great place to stay”
text: Chris, who checked us in at the front desk, was a pleasent and friendly just like the rest of the staff we encountered. We found this hotel to be clean and recently updated. Its a funky round building and stands out as you get close to it. The 17th floor restuarant has an amazing view. The rooms were a bit small but laid out well. Very nice secluded pool area with a great fire place. The hotel is located just of the 405 a little out of the way from all the sights but it felt safe and it wasn't too difficult to get to where you wanted to go. We were also happy to find that the tour companies would pick up at the hotel. We'd like to stay here again sometime.

title: “Loud and obnoxious”
text:
Stayed here while on a business trip. It has a great poolside bar for cocktails, two great restaurant options and the cabana rooms were super cool (although a bit dark). Everything seemed to be great and, with all the high security, we were convinced there must be a celebrity staying there. 
In the early evening, the cabana bar started playing music that was really loud but really good. Fine, I thought, by the time I get back from a late dinner I'm sure they will turn it off - there's no way they'd expect guests staying in the cabana rooms to sleep with that music blaring. When I returned at 11pm the music was still going strong. I thought about switching rooms to the main tower where it might be quieter but, again, thought management couldn't possibly keep the music going all night. I was wrong. After a bleary-eyed investigation at 1 am I realized there were literally speakers right outside my room! At 2 a.m. they finally turned off the music. I was exhausted and had a full day of work ahead of me and had just paid a small fortune for the room.
I'm only in my early thirties and usually not bothered by good music. But how do they expect anyone except twenty-something party-goers to stay here?

title: “Excellent value - great location”
text: A friend and I stayed here for a 5 day vacation in early September. The hallways are tiny, but the rooms were spacious for NY standards, comfortable and, most importanly, clean. Good (FREE) continental breakfast and friendly staff. Great location...easy walking distance to Time Square, Rockefeller Center, Grand Central Station and other major attractions and close to major subway lines. For two friends travelling on a limited budget, this was an excellent hotel...highly recommended.

title: “Very nice hôtel well located !”
text:
We spent 4 nights at the hotel Metro, this was our pre-honeymoon trip.
Our room was on the 5th floor, very clean and spacious (2 beds). 
The bathroom was also very clean and nice.
No noise from the neighbours, beds were very good.
The staff was very helpful and friendly, we booked some baseball game tickets and they kept them for us before our arrival.
The breakfast was very good (mostly sweet: fresh fruits, muffins, etc..) , there is a terrace on the roof top with a bar, and a nice view on the Empire state building.
The location is really central: next to the 34th street station (2 subway lines), there are plenty of restaurants just next door, an irish pub, and many many shops just across the street. 
The only thing would be that the aircon evacuation outside was a bit noisy, but it was really not a problem to sleep with it with windows closed. 
And we noticed in our second hotel that there was exactly the same kind of aircon noise. Since there are many big buildings, our room was on the back so the view was on the building on the other side. However, in our next hotel (iroquois) the view was the same. I guess that many hotels in New York have the same "issue"... but when you come to New York, aren't you supposed to spend more time outside than watching through the window
There is free internet access with your PC, or you can access their computer room. Handy to book and print entrance tickets from there.
Anyway, we really enjoyed our time there and would definitely return to hotel metro!

title: “Don't miss”
text:
We stayed for 6 nights in Yotel between August 29-September 4. This is a new hotel so everything is new, no complaints. The room was tiny but we did not mind. The staff was very kind and helpful (Look for Manu)
With this price (149 usd/night), and location, the hotel is a bargain. Free internet, free espresso, coffee, free muffins were a nice touch.
I recommend this hotel to singles and couples.

title: “Great location”
text:
Great place to stay, the staff has a great knowledge of the area.
Rooms are wonderful and cozy. The breakfeast and afternoon wine and appitizers are very good. Very close to cable car stop. 
I highley recommend staying here.

title: “Repeat Customer”
text: My wife & I have stayed at the Magnoila twice now for weekends away. Since we do not have the chance to do this that often we spring for the large suites. They are fantastic! Extremely spacious rooms and very comfortable. The staff at the hotel is always nice & helpful, the restaurant serves up some great dishes and the hotel location is perfect. Our next trip into downtown Denver will include a stay at the Magnoilia.

title: “Once again, thoroughly exceptional!!”
text: Our second stay at the Palomar was even better than the first. Customer service and attention to detail is unsurpassed. The entire hotel staff goes above and beyond to make sure everything is top notch. The rooms are nice sized, linens are beautiful, location is perfect, and the restaurant, 1692, is superb. The complimentary wine happy hour and excellent coffee service in the morning are 2 more reasons to stay at the Palomar! Even the fitness facility, for a downtown hotel, is awesome! I just can't say enough good things about the Palomar.....we will be back and will also seek out Kimpton locations in other cities in our future travels.

title: “great location”
text: great location near time square, subway stations, rooms are tiny but clean, on the downside wifi is not free, staff are good, price is what you expect to pay if your going to live almost on time sqaure

title: “Value & Convenience”
text: Swift and friendly check-in. Generous sized, and very clean room with comfortable bed. Small pool (didn't use). Short drive or walk to a selection of places to eat. Not far from Firehouse Saloon. Buffet breakfast was basic, but acceptable. Would stay here again without a second thought.

title: “Like Home”
text: A very friendly hotel especially for extended stays. I was recently there for 5 days and when you would walk in the door you would be greeted with Welcome Home. A very nice touch.

title: “Excellent property in midtown”
text:
I booked a night at the Parker Meridien using priceline, and then went to the tripadvisor site to check out the reviews. What I read concerned me: there were many complaints about poor air conditioning, snooty service and questionable cleanliness.
Fortunately none of those issues pertained to our stay. The check-in clerk was extremely nice and gave us a beautiful room on a high floor (even though we had scored a cheap rate through priceline.) The room was updated, immaculately clean and in perfect condition. Loved the flat-screen TV on the rotating pedestal. And it was definitely spacious for a New York City room. The weather that day was stiflingly muggy and the air conditioning worked great. (While it is true that you cannot adjust the temperature, the front desk gave us instructions on how to activate the fan.)
The location can't be beat: two blocks from Central Park and walking distance to the Broadway district. Lots of great restaurants in the area as well. One caveat: Any "extras" are extremely expensive, so be very careful before you run up any guest charges. No need to dine at the hotel, as there are plenty of reasonably-priced options nearby. All in all, a perfect stay.

title: “Good service and great value”
text: Stayed one night in June at the Marcel. Check-in and check-out were very efficient. The staff (front desk, bellmen, manager) were all very professional and helpful. The room was small (I was expecting that) and decorated in a modern, minimalistic theme. I feel it is a great value for a nice, clean, comfortable hotel in NYC.

title: “This was an overnight stop following a...”
text: This was an overnight stop following a long flight. Check in went well with a short wait and payment was made by way of honor points. The room was on the 4th floor and had a separate lounge and family bedroom. We found the situation with the sink in the bedroom area in other hotels on this trip so it does not disturb us. We could hear sounds from outside but even though there was a class reunion at the hotel there was no noise. We had breakfast which was an extra cost but we were seated promptly and the meal was good. Location was great for the mall and other shopping but cannot be considered for visiting central Seattle which is why I have scored the location as such. Did not get a chance to get in the pool which looked good and parking was adequate. Overall this was great and depending on price would have liked to stay longer or on another occasion should it arise.

title: “Nice hotel in downtown LA”
text:
I joined my husband as he was attending a conference at the la convention center. We chose the Omni over other the conference hotels based on TripAdvisor reviews. We were upgraded to a room on the 16th floor which was quiet, spacious and very nicely appointed. This room came with access to the club floor for free breakfast, drinks, etc. 
The entire Omni staff we encountered were courteous, helpful and friendly. I used the fitness room, which was a decent size and had decent equipment as well as the pool. The pool area is a little small and the pool itself is narrow and shallow. It was perfectly fine for a quick dip but not a "lap pool" if you are a serious swimmer. 
Downtown la is kind of a wasteland, especially during the weekend, but the Omni is a very nice oasis. I would definitely stay here again if I had business in downtown LA and would recommend it to others.

title: “Very good hotel”
text:
I stayed at the Pan Pacific three nights on a business trip and was very pleased with the experience. I will return if back in Seattle. The room was very clean and perfectly appointed (used to 4* hotels so I can compare). The front desk was helpful and pleasant. The excellent Sea star restaurant (which you can acess directly from the lobby) is very convenient after a long day of work when you don't feel like going out for diner.
A minor point: breakfast is a bit overpriced, no buffet, and the loud music at 7:30 am is not what I enjoy. As Wholefoods is next door, there is the option of breakfast food there (just a practical option but would not even compare with the Pan Pacific, we are not talking about the same things).
Overall, a very good experience.

title: “find a better value”
text:
We just returned from a conference. We spent five nights at the Town & Country. I would not recommend this hotel. The grounds are lovely. They have some of the most beautiful roses. The pool areas are nice as well. However, I do not know if the rooms have been updated since 1985. The hotel has outdated wallpaper, faded bedding, and worn out furniture. I also did not find it to be secure. It seems anyone could wander in and out. While we were there we encountered issues with the air conditioner, shower (not draining) and toilet (leaking). I would recommend checking out the Doubletree that is within a couple of blocks.
Aside from the beautiful landscaping, the hotel is a short walk from the Fashion Valley Mall and the trolley station. It is a convenient location within minutes of area attractions. However, I believe you could find a better value elsewhere.

title: “Great location”
text:
I have stayed in several hotels in San Francisco for business and always in the same area so that I can get to my office. Sadly, there seems to be a major problem with homelessness here. I'm always staggered by the sheer numbers of people sleeping on the streets. Hotel Abri is on one of several streets in the area that are right on the border between the most affluent, tourist-fed area and an area with many homeless people. 
This isn't a problem for a hotel guest, but it's worth being aware that coming out of the hotel and turning right, you realise you're in a prime location for getting around the heart of the city, access to public transport, shops, etc etc while turning left (which I always have to do to get to work) you're passing through an area where a lot of people are sleeping on the streets, begging, asking you for things etc.
Note - this isn't anything to do with Abri, but some people seem to want to pretend that this isn't a reality of the city, so it's worth being aware of it if you're that way inclined.
The beauty of Abri is its location. If you're in SF for a holiday, you shouldn't be holed up in a hotel anyway. From here, you can get to Market street, take the Muni to the Embarcadero for $2, visit China Town etc. 
I tried room service once, but it comes up from a busy street-facing bar/restaurant and I felt like I was bothering them, which put me off ordering again. Bear in mind that this area kicks off at the weekend, so if you're looking for a quiet dinner, you won't be eating at the restaurant attached to the hotel. It's a bar as well as a restaurant and not a quiet one. You will hear street noise, so if you're delicate in this regard, you may want to talk to the staff about where the rooms face. 
The hallway smells unpleasant but the rooms are fine (I was in an Urban Suite). They're clean and roomy and the beds are comfortable. Staff at reception are pleasant.
While not blown away by this hotel (I think it's the lack of a quieter dining area for guests), I will probably stay here again on my next trip - it's clean and convenient, which is the main plus for me on a business trip.

title: “Convenient and good value”
text:
Have usually found Best Westerns to be reliable and this is no exception. Prompt & friendly service, quiet rooms, good facilities (including pool & internet) and nice choice of free breakfast.
Recommended.

title: “Great Place to Stay”
text:
I was booked to stay two nights at the Elan, but due to a water main break the day of my arrival, the hotel had to close for a day. They booked me for one night at another hotel, which they paid for. Then when I did return to the Elan the next day, they paid for that night as well.
The hotel was very comfortable and the staff was very friendly and helpful. I particularly appreciated their generosity in comping for what was really not much of an inconvenience at all.
I definitely recommend this hotel and would stay here again.

title: “Good value hotel, uncommon in NYC.”
text: If you get a room on a high floor which has been remodeled, this is an excellent hotel for the money. We were referred here and have stayed twice, and they have been very pleasant and kind. Comfortable, old-NY hotel.

title: “Nice place, great location”
text: My family of four stayed at the Nine Zero for three nights. The location was perfect. We were right in the heart of it all. The staff was friendly and very helpful. The room was good size, but a little dark. The beds were comfortable and the bathroom was good size. The only negative was that instead of an empty fridge, it was used as a mini bar. We had to take everything out to use it for all of the great leftovers we had. This hotel was super quiet, which I loved. Overall, a very good experience.

title: “We enjoyed our stay and hope to return”
text: Although our stay was our first time at the hotel and only for one night, the entire staff couldn't have been more accommodating. We were looking for an apartment and the desk clerk and concierge went out of their way to offer guidance. The room was most comfortable and there was a complimentary umbrella, which came in very handy! The restaurant which is accessible without exiting the hotel (also a good thing because of the torrential rainstorm), was very good. Overall, a great experience.

title: “I love this hotel!”
text: Great style and service and value. The suites are awesome and a terrfic value. Good location for business or pleasure, right off the 16th St. Pedestrian Mall and a light rail stop. The free breakfast, happy hour and late night cookies add a lot of value and warmth. I never stay anywhere else in Denver!

title: “Disappointing and expensive”
text:
We booked this hotel for three nights at that start of a holiday. The website made the rooms look wonderful but we found that it was not at all like those that appeared on the website. We booked a double/double and had asked for foam pillows when booking but they were not in the room on arrival. Although there were four of us in the room there were only two robes, enough towels for two, two mugs, enough tea/coffee for two, two glasses etc. The bathroom was very tired and in dire need of an upgrade. Water had seeped up the back of the door and the base was rotten and the mirror rusty.
The charge for the in room water was $9 per bottle!! When we phoned room service for a jug of tap water they told us there would be a $5 service charge to bring it up to our room!! After complaining to the Manager we were given bottled water free of charge with the comment that "they were a business"! They also charge for use of the internet and hooking your laptop up.
We ate at the hotel on the first night only because we arrived late and were tired from the flight. The portions were small and the food very expensive for what is was (London prices). Supper for four, three starters, four mains and a bottle of wine $200. We ate out the other nights and certainly did not eat breakfast at the hotel as diners are more fun and better value.
The gym was adequate and the pool very small and cold. 
The only plus side is that the hotel is within walking distance of most things but although we were on the 5th floor our room overlooked the street and was very noisy.

title: “A modern oasis”
text:
I wanted to thank you for a terrific stay at Aloft Dallas. I had a superb time from check in at the Aloha desk with Reagan who greeted me warmly and was up on the happenings for the weekend in the Big D. Thomas also at the Aloha desk was most helpful with the jack hookups and friendly. I had a wonderful room with view of the bronze longhorns and appreciated the design from the rocking retro chairs and plexiglass faux tree trunk coffee table to the sumptuous bed, Bliss toiletries, and efficient use of space. I also loved the jack set up and connection to the TV which was so unique as I have been to many 5 star hotels that don’t have the feature. 
Splash was refreshing and Refuel was an oasis. I would like to especially thank Gil who was a most cheerful and accommodating individual who knows how to anticipate needs. There was a turkey club sandwich that I wanted but it had bacon. He prepared a fresh sandwich for me without bacon and was able to substitute a small salad instead of potato chips thanks to Jesse at the Aloha desk who was so gracious and hospitable. I returned to my room thinking I should have told Gil to heat up the sandwich since there was cheddar cheese and the melted cheese would be so tasty. When I took the sandwich out of the wrapping foil it was heated. I went back to thank Gil and bought a grain bar which he freshly prepared as well and it was piping hot. Gil’s attentiveness and taking time for the little things that make me happy was just dandy!
I finished my stay and checked out with Thomas. Again a fitting end to great weekend. I enjoyed my time immensely and look forward to returning soon.

title: “Almost like staying with friends with a particularly comfortable house.”
text: This must be one of the nicest city hotels in any country. Full of charm, full of books, a large sitting room with papers, free pastries and coffee by day, cheese and wine in the evening. Blissfully comfortable beds and unusually nice dressing gowns, jelly beans in the fridge. For a greedy, slightly sybaritic bookworm, what could be better? Relaxed, friendly yet professional staff. Even the paving stones in the street - Library Way - leading to one of NY's most famous public libraries, is set with quotes on the joy of books. As an author and a travel writer, this is one I'll always remember.

title: “Great location! Great space!”
text: I recently stayed at the Affinia Manhattan for a long weekend. It was incredible. The staff was kind and the service was prompt. The whole group felt as though they were truly being treated to a weekend in the Big Apple. Thank you to all of the people who work so hard & made our stay so wonderful!

title: “Great location”
text: Great location....a few steps from Times Square, Central Park and 5th avenue. The staff is ok. The room is good and the hotel has a restaurant on the lobby. Its an old building, but it doesnt matter at all...

title: “Good value on Riverwalk”
text: Great service, very friendly staff. My room was in need of some updating (e.g., a few cracked tiles in bathroom, old CRT TV) but the bed was very comfortable and the hotel was quiet. Overall good value compared with other options downtown.

title: “Great Place!”
text: My boyfriend and I stayed here for 4 nights in July 2011 and LOVED it! the staff was great, and understanding when i needed my passport to be sent to the hotel because I lost my license in Chicago- Midway airport. The room and bed was comfy and being on the 7th floor, we had a great view of the city. it was great, and we would definitely stay there again.

title: “Great Value, Very Nice and Clean”
text: A group of us stayed here while visiting the U.S. National White Water Center. The hotel was very nice, clean and quiet. Nothing extrodinary, but excellent inexpensive stay.

title: “Convocation 2012”
text: It was a pleasure at the Doubletree Hilton in Detroit-Dearborn. The staff was very friendly and helpful. A very clean hotel. Would definitely recommend.

title: “Fantastic Stay!”
text:
We stayed here for one night on June 6. We were in town for a Broadway show and wanted an average place to crash after walking all over the city. We were pleasently surprised to find this hotel only 4 blocks from Madison Square Garden, yet on a very quiet section of West 29th in the quaint, hipster-ville of Chelsea. The King size room was normal - nothing super fancy, but clean, and enough room to actually walk around without having to climb over the bed. No construction going on anywhere, and a suprisingly low amount of outside noise.
The free breakfast was nice. Egg, sausage biscuits with gravy, toast, cereal, oatmeal, juices and hot cinnamon buns. But the nicest thing was how long they agreed to store our bags even though we had already checked out! They said they would keep bags until 11PM! I know most NYC hotels will store bags, but not for this long. They were very pleasent.
The number one reason we loved them was the fact that we called them from our second night's hotel after midnight to tell them we had left an I-pod in the dresser draw and asked if they could check and see if it was still there. We didn't have high hopes that it would happen, but the woman at the front desk went and got the I-pod and took our address, assuring us that she would have it in the mail that day!! 
Penn Station is right up the street, as is a convenient subway line that will take you to Chinatown/Little Italy. Avoid the overly priced Stage Deli around the corner, but do try Super Mac, an awesome "all varieties" of mac and cheese joint. If you love clothes, you can walk up to Herald Square (W 34th) and shop at Daffy's, a designer's discount store.

title: “Great Staff!”
text:
My husband and I stayed here for a romantic getaway mid-week. We live in North County but had never done the San Diego Tourist thing so we booked a room at the Sheraton Symphony and found it very pleasant.
My husband had a broken foot at the time and the hotel loaned us a wheelchair to go sight-seeing with.
We were up-graded to a one-bedroom suite and provided goodies in our room nightly. We are SPG members so that might explain some of it. However, by the time we came back in the evening, my husband just wanted to ice his foot so the club level concierge would make me up a tray of snacks to bring back to our room.
Yes, the hotel is old and is probably gonna need new carpets soon, but alot of Sheratons are in older properties that have character! That's what makes its a nice experience- its not cookie-cutter opulence. 
We found the hotel very clean and the staff VERY helpful and accommodating!

title: “Try Someplace Else”
text:
The best thing about this place was the proximity to the airport and the timely shuttle. We arrived late from overseas and our ride was just pulling up as we walked out the terminal door. Front desk help was efficient, if not very friendly. The room was not cleaned well, as shower and rug were just this side of disgusting. No "Do Not Disturb" or "Clean Room" sign was available to hang on door, no welcome info in room, and internet access is wireless, so it's a bit of a hassle to get connected. The breakfast was paltry, slim pickings to be sure.
There are several other hotels close by, and if you can find a similar rate, I'd try one of those before I'd stay here at the Days Inn.

title: “Was not expecting such a great hotel!”
text: We had a last minute trip and this was the only hotel with vacancy so we had no choice, but to book it. What a great choice! The room was super clean, yes a bit strong with the cleaners, but I'd rather smell that than unpleasant odors. The bathroom was spotless and they were constantly cleaning it. The room is a bit outdated but who cares it was CLEAN. We were kind confused on how to use the heat, but it worked out fine. The staff were very nice and helpful. I was not expecting this from a New York hotel, after hearing horror stories. Oh and let me add this gem. We asked the front desk for a taxi and they got us a limo - for the same price!

title: “Excellent Service!”
text: My trip to New York this time was mainly business. I got in very early and got kept back hnce a late check-out. EVERYONE at this hotel made me feel sooooo special! They really treated me like royalty. The location was great, not far from shopping and spot on when it comes to Resturant Row! Thank you especailly to the employee who checked me in early and incidently was the same who checked me out late.. THANK YOU ANAMARIA!!! Your world class customer service made me a loyal customer. The coffee shop in the loby had great coffee and excellent sandwhiches! Anamaria, because of you, my stay was very comfortable. Keep up the great work!- Ms. Hema Ramdeo.

title: “Fabulous hotel”
text:
We just got back from a 6 day stay here. We loved the hotel. We had a very spacious junior suite with full ocean view. If you are traveling with kids, here's some things about the amenities that they don't seem to highlight on their website.
Huge flat panel TV with DVD player--we always bring our own movies to give the kids some down time and this was the only time I didn't have to figure out how to rig our personal DVD player to a hotel TV
Guest laundry available in the basement--if I had known, I would have packed less
Microwave and fridge in the room with dining table
Books in the lobby for guests to take or leave the books they don't want to carry home
Heated pool open from 8 am - 10 pm.
I thought the room and furnishings were beautiful. The bed was super comfortable--like an old fashioned feather bed that you sink into. The staff was very helpful. We even had complimentary wine delivered to our room when we checked in. The $20 per day parking was a detraction. Overall, one of the nicest hotels I've stayed in with my family.

title: “Don't stay in this hotel in a windy day”
text:
The interior of the hotel is pretty new, the service is also good, but the hotel hardware is too old. The insulation of sliding door and window in each room had worn out. I stayed there on a windy day. It was like sleeping in a roaring train -- door was rattling, wind was whistling all night. I changed 3 rooms but they were all the same. I was not able to sleep the whole night. 
I strongly suggest: check the weather before you book this hotel!

title: “Nice Hotel”
text:
This hotel is much nicer on the inside than the outside. It's updated and pretty stylish; definitely on the boutique side. Every single member of the staff was extremely kind and helpful. 
Some surprises - both good and bad:
-The hotel is really close to the airport. When I emailed the front desk in advance, I was told a taxi would cost about $12-13. With tip, it was closer to $19 (each way).
-As I did with the taxi, I called ahead to inquire about the price of daily wireless internet usage since I was traveling for work (expense reports and all that). I was told it would be about $13 per day. Turns out... it's free! There was no charge, and the connection was good.
-The location is good in the sense that it's right downtown. More expensive hotels are along the harbor. In my opinion, San Diego's downtown is a little odd, so there aren't tons of merchants nearby, but the hotel is very close to Westfield Horton Plaza.
-The biggest disappointment was that the fitness center was closed for renovation. I wish this was stated on the website.

title: “Nice hotel. Nice people.”
text:
Stayed at the Westin during a conference held in San Antonio. I liked the hotel:
- the restaurant has many delicious and reasonably priced items on the menu. Nice service. Also try the Antipasto items!
- good coffee and snacks from the coffee bar in the lobby
- rooms are large and nicely appointed
- the hotel is close to everything in San Antonio
Overall very personable staff.

title: “Excellent stay! Fantastic Concierge service!”
text: Visited Boston for the weekend with another couple and had a ball! The concierge service was impeccable! He had wonderful suggestions for everything from sight seeing to dining options - and they were all spot on! Rooms were clean and well appointed, though I did find it unusual to have an old tube television rather than a flat screen. The bed and linens were fantastic, we both slept great! The room was a little on the small side, but with so much to do in Boston, who hangs out in their hotel room?! Overall a fantastic trip and an excellent hotel. Would recommend to anyone looking for a centrally located, chic, clean, modern place to stay with great amenities.

title: “Magnificent hotel w/ shockingly low rates & wonderful staff”
text:
I had the pleasure of spending 8 nights here for a work related event and was really pleased with the staff and valet of the hotel who were courteous, incredibly nice, and expedient with any demand. 
There were great rates on hotel sites, I would pick them over many other hotels and the cheap rates were an added bonus. The hotel is within a block of some great restaurants (lebanese, japanese, indian, mexican) and right behind the gorgeous Rock Creek Park which is a quick way to bypass some DC traffic if headed to the airport or over the Arlington Memorial Bridge. 
The brunch buffet on the weekends is an absolute deal. They have a waffle and omelet station as well as plenty of fresh fruit and juices. 
Join the Omni Rewards program for free and you get free wifi, free juice/coffee/newspaper delivery to your room EACH morning, free shoe shining, 2 free pressings each day, etc. It is one of the better hotel rewards programs I have come across so join online before you show up to save time.

title: “Great Location”
text:
I recently returned from my holiday at The Colonnade Hotel, the staff were friendly and very helpful. The location is great for getting around Boston, the T station was right outside the main doors, the Prudential shopping center was directly over the other side of the street, and if you want to ride the ducks, the pick up is outside The Prudential Center, and Shaws a grocery store was about a 3 minute walk away. One tip, ask for the Mini bar to be emptied when you arrive, so you can fill it up with what you fancy. One minus point, check the invoice when you receive it has i was charged with using the Mini Bar, even thou i had it emptied on my arrival, i question it, and they changed it right away. 
I also used Thronton's cafe a few times for breakfast, which is about a minutes walk from the hotel and a lot cheaper than the hotel.

title: “Great hotel in nice area”
text:
Great room, very big with huge bed! Great location, just one block's walk from 72nd subway then 5 minute ride to Times Square and anywhere you want to go from there!
We had a room on the 24th floor so great views of San Remo building and Central Park but building sways ALOT in windy weather, very weird at first!
Very close to Central Park, check out Cafe Viand for sit down breakfast and Fairway and Levain Bakery for take away breakfast.
Great all in all!

title: “Sucks - more than my vacuum cleaner does!”
text:
The best hotel in the worst area of LA - which makes it an undesirable place to stay. We didn't really even feel safe walking out of the hotel in daylight; by night, every person we saw could easily have been a criminal. 
The hotel itself is adequate, but lots of drawbacks.
PROs
- Breakfast is adequate (but not the "full" breakfast advertised, just continental)
- Efficient Staff
- No problem changing our friends' room when they discovered on arrival that it smelt
- Good parking
CONs
- Noisy rooms
- Small rooms
- Some rooms have VERY odd shower entrys
- Disturbing location
- Virtually no storage in room (3 little drawers only)
- Gruff staff
- Beds steamy - even in winter I was hot in a t shirt and undies because of the pillow top bed
- Lots of things not working - one of our lamps, one of the two elevators, the ATM, one of the driers in the laundry
- Not walking distance to any attractions

title: “Very Nice!”
text: Nice hotel, very clean with an okay location. For the price I could have stayed closer to the Convention Center.

title: “Ideal hotel for Fisherman's Wharf in San Francisco.”
text: This hotel is ideally located to enjoy the Wharf experience. The internal quality is superb with very comfortable rooms and beds. There was a free wine-tasting every evening. The staff are very friendly from the uniformed hall porter, to receptionists, the concierge and all domestic staff. The building is a sympathetic conversion of a historic warehouse. Leisure facilities abound and there is a branch of 'Blazing Saddles' under the hotel from which one can hire a bike to ride over the Golden Gate Bridge four miles away. Ferries and boat rides are just a short distance away for trips around the bay and to Alcatraz. The famed Powell and Hyde cable car terminus is just outside. You can check-in online and print your boarding pass for free. The airport can easily be reached by public transport: the nearby trolley line 'F' to Embarcadero and the BART onwards to the airport. For quality and location the Argonaut is exceptionally good.

title: “Can't wait to return!”
text:
We stayed at the Shelburne due to the fantastic Travelzoo rate and the hotel's quiet but convenient location. We stayed in a one bedroom suite which truly felt like having our own apartment. Ours had a wet bar area with fridge and microwave drawer, living area with comfy sleeper sofa, flat screen tv and step out balcony. Bedroom had a king bed and flat screen and 1 bathroom with big soaking tub and shower combo. 
The renovations here were amazing. All the fixtures are very modern and stylish and lighting was very good. A lot of the lighting had dimmer switches which are very useful especially in the bathroom area if you want to have a relaxing bath.
One thing I noticed especially was the sound proofing. I think this is the first hotel in recent memory that I heard no noise at all from any adjoining rooms.
We were very satisfied and would definitely return if the price was right.

title: “Nice location but service could be better”
text: Nice hotel at a great location. However service could be better. At check-in I was told the room they reserved for me was a handicap room and asked if I wanted to change to a different room. I said fine but he ended up giving me a 5th floor room! No view and the drain for the bathtub didn't even work! The electric curtains were nice though.

title: “Great location in the heart of Times Square”
text: Hotel is huge. The rooms are surprisingly big for NYC and well appointed. The restaurant and lounge on the 8th floor are pricey, as is The View but really, you pay for the scenery and the experience there so it isn't so bad, and they do waive the cover charge for hotel guests. Overall the stay was pleasant, but word to the wise, if you are attending for a conference, ask for a room close to the elevator and bring a sweater as the function rooms are chilly. Junior's across the street is a great place to get a cheap and cheerful real food meal if you don't want to pay hotel price for so so food. Internet was a staggering $18 a day, shameful in this day and age.

title: “Lived up to the Hype”
text:
I've stayed at a number of hotels in midtown Manhattan over the years, and in most cases I leave with a much lighter wallet and a sense of regret about having spent so much for so little. That was not the case at Districkt. The check-in staff were incredibly friendly and helpful, even offering several of their personal dining recommendations when I asked about a good place to eat at midnight.
The room was pristine, not worn down and dirty like so many other places I've stayed in midtown. I was also really impressed by the too-good-to-be-true price of $169 when I stayed. I suspect that their prices will go up as they continue to attract so many wary NYC visitors such as myself, but so long as they keep their prices competitive with other hotels in the area, I will be staying here again.

title: “A nice hotel”
text: I have stayed there many times and even once left a bad review. This hotel is a very nice property. We paid $39 a night through Priceline. It is always clean, and the entry way is pretty. The staff always has a little bit of an attitude. I think it may be because the only times I am ever there is for soccer tournaments, and all those kids can make an adult a little cranky. I heard several of the staff arguing with parents who were asking for late checkouts on the last day of play. I remember having the same problem before, but it was not an issue for me this time. I heard quite a few parents complaining who were not with our team. I heard the front desk staff telling people that no more than two rooms per team could have a late checkout. I also heard the front desk staff talking negatively about parents as they left. A bit unprofessional. Personally, my only complaint was that I did not get the double beds that I called and asked for. I called about 5 days before my arrival, and they confirmed that the room would be double/double. I know with Priceline there is no guarantee on what kind of room you get, but I was a bit disappointed. They did, however, provide a king room with a couch pullout. It worked just fine for us although the couch was a bit uncomfortable. The food is always good at the restaurant, and the pool was adequate. This hotel is nicely situated for soccer tournaments that take place at the Spring fields, and it is very close to Willowbrook mall. The parking is also free.

title: “Very nice ... for "a price"”
text:
My husband was going to NYC on business and we had a set amount that was quite substantial to spend on lodging, which was what led us to the New York Manhattan Hotel. We booked a king deluxe room with a fridge and were told on check-in that it was "like a suite." I'm not sure if the person that told us that has ever seen a real hotel suite... 
Nevertheless, the room while smaller than expected was very comfortable. The bed was amazing, the clothing storage space was more than ample and the bathroom was well appointed with towels, shampoo, soap, hair dryer and more. 
The fridge was a bit shaky -- every time I opened the door, the fridge threatened to fall off the (low) shelf it was on. The fridge was plenty cold though and great to have at our disposal. I'd be interested to know what it would cost to get one in a room that didn't have one, if that's even possible... 
With the exception of the breakfast room which was crowded, small and dirty, thus knocking one star off my review, the rest of the hotel was also very nice. The fitness center had good machines and it was great that there were extra towels and water. The one thing I "missed" was a TV remote control. I really would have liked to have been able to change the channel to watch something engaging while I walked on the treadmill! Oh well... 
The downstairs lounge with hot drinks was charming and so convenient to have. I met a friend there and was able to chat comfortably and not feel like I had to shout to be heard. I stopped in to get hot drinks to cap off every evening that I was there. So nice!
The staff was also most helpful. The plug for the tub in our bathroom didn't work and as soon as my husband called about it, maintenance was sent up to fix it. He also asked for hair conditioner for me and the staff brought up several small bottles -- far more than I needed. The front desk staff was exacting with our wake-up calls and the cleaning staff was polite and efficient.
Overall a very good choice of hotel that could not possibly be in a more convenient location -- two blocks from Penn Station and just 12 blocks from Grand Central Station -- but be aware that it did carry "a price."

title: “Could be better....”
text:
I have stayed at the Colonnade twice within the past month. The first time I was on my own visiting a child at BU and the second time I was there with many family members, meeting there from all over. There were some interesting observations: 
Both times I was there, our alarm clocks went off in the middle of the night or pre-dawn hours. The first was at 4 am, the second at midnight. Very odd- this has never happened to me anywhere else I have stayed. I guess the housekeeping staff does not turned off the previous guests' settings on the clocks. In addition, a hotel alarm went off late at night during the second visit; the front desk reported it as a "communication failure." I'll say. Made for a lot of disturbed sleep. 
On the morning of our checkout, the maid could not wait to get her hands on the room and started a massive cleanup before we had checked out. We felt very rushed as a result and had no time for a shower. My brother and his family had it even worse; the maid woke them at 7:45 to clean their room, even though they were not even up yet and by no means had they checked out. 
When my sister made a small complaint at the hotel restaurant, the 
maitre de chastized her. A waiter later apologized. Let's hope the waiter finds a nicer man to work for. 
The bathroom doors in some of the hotel rooms allow for little privacy AND do not lock. (There is a one inch gap in between the two swinging doors.) Good thing I am comfortable with my family and am not too modest. 
Aside from the man at the restaurant (breakfast), the staff was wonderful, particularly the bellmen. The location is great and we got our rooms for a super price. Parking is stiff......and my blanket both times looked like a thrift store reject. I was afraid to look too closely. The first time I went, I got my room through Priceline for $100 and I would do that again- just give me a better, cleaner blanket and let me SLEEP!

title: “Great Location - Good sized lobby”
text: As all other reviewers have stated, this hotel has an amazing location and is within easy walking distance of a wide variety of tourist destinations. The rooms are standard Westin - clean, comfortable with a touch of luxury. I had a beautiful view of Times Square and it was very quiet. I was here for business and the lobby was large, with lots of seating where I was able to hold some one-to-one meetings with no issue. The only complaint that I have was that one night as the restaurant was closed, I ate at the bar and had a mediocre and rather expensive meal. Otherwise, everything else was excellent.

title: “Good location, great price, clean and friendly”
text: Another great stay at a La Quinta with our dog and kids. While the outside area may not looks so great, inside the hotel is very nice. It's also easy to get anywhere from there as the highway is nearby as well as beaches. Very nice and clean hotel, appreciate the "modern" feel of the rooms with really nice decor, vanities, etc. The wifi does need a little tweaking, but overall, would definitely go back.

title: “Awesome Hotel, great location, and EXCELLENT customer service!!”
text: My organization has held our large yearly training/award conference at this hotel the past 5 years and are VERY satisifed and impressed with their continuing high level of customer service and attention to detail. They have a stablized hotel staff that executes formal banquets and setup of training workshops with precision; not turning over personnel, unlike many other hotels, is a key to this success, in my opinion. I would strongly recommend this hotel for a solo stay or large multi-day function!!

title: “PARK CENTRAL Broadway's best stay”
text: OKay! I rate ths hotel as one of broadway's hippest neat and people places to stay . This hotel is warm friendly comfortable . you feel at home here, you never want to leave. The frot desk is sooo nice . Sooo sweet incredibly accomodating I just love Ricky, His name is Ricardo but his guest will soon find him to be a friend! the front desk assistant manager. He will make sure that you have everything you need. And , Oh the "bellman" Carmelo will put all your things in place nope don't you ever carry a heavy luggage!

title: “Not free but well worth it”
text: I have stayed at this hotel at least twenty times and have never had a bad experience. The rooms are comfortable spacious and quiet. The temperature control is excellent. It is an all around wonderful place to stay. I also love the bar in the lobby.

title: “NCRS Visit”
text: Fine hotel...maybe a few $$ overpriced, but probably a good deal for Dallas, Texas area. Hotel staff were all very nice.

title: “Perfect hotel”
text: The Comfort inn is the perfct hotel to stay in L.A for low budget. It is a very clean and safe hotel , with free breakfast, free Wi-fi, free gated parking. I rented a car and I found the location just perfect. I recommend to everybody in fact I can't wait to go back.

title: “Excellent Customer Service Oriented Staff!!!!”
text: We have just stayed our first night in the hotel. The room is very clean, bed/mattress/linens very nice, etc. We are most impressed, however, with the staff at the bar and restaurant. Big Z (Zach) little Z (not sure of her full name) were so welcoming to us yesterday and this morning at the breakfast buffet Bonnie was awesome and so helpful and caring. They are all great at what they do. Wyndham you are blessed with the personnel that has been mentioned, they ensure that your customers will want to stay longer and come back again!

title: “Great service”
text: A nice hotel, not smart, but well located and great atitude bt staff. The restaurant was great. Perfect food and no need to travel to the seedy part of Fishermans Wharf

title: “Wonderful experience; highly recommend!!”
text:
Spent a delightful 5 days here. Had 2 days of biz in downtown LA and decided to add some time on either side of that. Love the location in Little Tokyo. Staff very helpful and friendly. Housekeeping was lovely and on top of all details. Had excellent experience at hair salon in hotel, and I cannot give high enough reviews for the shiatsu massage. Truly exceptional massage at the health spa facility which is on the hotel property, but a separate entity from hotel.
Superlative sushi close by too.

title: “Not a Four Seasons or Ritz standard at all”
text:
Being a fan of the Four Seasons, I wanted to try this hotel as a change when I was in Chicago. I was really surprised the the level of service is not that of a typical Four Seasons or even a Ritz. 
Positive Notes- All the front desk staff, room service and bell staff were very nice and helpful.
Negative Note- The spa attendant's attitude was terrible. She seemed as if that was the last place she wanted to be and was just waiting for the clock to run out for her to leave. The towels and robes in my bathroom had stains on them that seemed to have been set in a while. 
Overall, this one hotel doesn't change my mind about the overall brand of the Four Seasons, but next time, I might just decide to stay at the actual Four Seasons and not the Ritz.

title: “fantasic!”
text:
a group of 8 of us stayed at the shoreham over the thanks giving weekend in 2009, I had emailed the hotel before and arranged to be picked up from the airport, when we got to the hotel we were greeted with a glass of champange(fizzy wine) and told our rooms wouldnt be ready until 3pm so we left our cases and went out the hotel is in a fantastic location, we returned later that day and shown to our rooms they were beautiful 2 queen sized beds, flat screen tv, bose stereo and a massage chair in the corner. room was very clean and beds very comfortable. we were a bit disapointed that our rooms wernt next to each other but were told there was only 1 room on each floor which sleeps 4 wasnt a major problem the lift made it easy enough to get up and down. the other half of our group were on the 10th floor but there room wasnt as big and didnt have the massage chair (not that we spent enough time in the hotel to use it) 
there was a coffee machine at reception which you could use free of charge and free internet also in the lobby. the gym looked good but we wernt in the hotel long enough to use it as were were out exploring the city. we had an amazing time and i would definatly recommend this hotel to everyone

title: “Old Boys club”
text: I booked this hotel for a romantic weekend to celebrate my girlfriend's birthday. My first impression of this hotel is that is a beautiful through back to a different time. The lobby is inviting with a country club feel to it. The nice feeling faded as soon as I attempted to check in. I called the day before, yesterday, to confirm that I had a King sized bed. When I checked in I was told that I was confirmed for 2 double beds and there were no Kings available. I had called 2 times the day before and I do not know how this reservation magically got changed in their system. I explained that I called their front desk yesterday afternoon to confirm the king and was lectured on how reservations were not guaranteed. After being persistent, I learned that they did have kings available, but they were being cleaned. I am now waiting for the room I reserved and confirmed available to be cleaned at 4 pm. I did not get a warm welcoming feel from the lady at the front desk and this has changed my perception of the hotel before I even get to my room. It makes me wonder if the old fashioned treatment of minorities is part of the country club feel of the hotel. Others are getting their keys as I wait. Very unimpressed.

title: “" Guest Relations"”
text: First of all the hospitality was excellent, I'm from Cincinnati and we strongly believe in good hospitality Paulette Hill is the ideal Guest relations personnel! She was very helpful.

title: “As expected”
text: As a Hilton Diamond member I stay at alot of Hilton propoerties. this Hotel, while it's atrium is huge, is exactly what you would expect from this brand. employees were very nice and helpful.

title: “Fantastic!”
text:
I have never written a review for a hotel before, even though I have stayed in hundreds of hotels as I'm a travel consultant, the Luxe Sunset definitely deserves it! 
I recently stayed at the Luxe Sunset and it was perfect from start to finish. I arrived very late on my first night so I had organized a car to pick me up from the airport. The driver was very professional and lovely to talk to after a long flight. When I arrived at the hotel check in was a breeze, it was nice to have a friendly and speedy check in! I ordered room service on the first night and it was very good and nothing was too much to ask even at such a late hour. 
The hotel is in Bel Air and is nicely tucked away with lots of privacy. A car would be handy as its about a 20min cab ride to Hollywood however it was so nice to be away from the hustle and bustle. The freeway is very close to the hotel and I never heard it. 
My room was in the main building and was very nice. The decor was current and the bed was very comfy. I loved the bath products as well.
Overall my stay was perfect but I was most impressed with all the staff I came in contact with who were all very friendly and very helpful! The service was 5 star standard (and i've stayed in a lot of 5 star hotels which wouldn't compare to the service here). 
I have been to LA many times and always find it hard to find a place I like, when I go back I will definitely be returning to the Luxe Sunset! Now I can end my search for the perfect LA hotel...i've found it!

title: “Wonderful hotel and staff!”
text: My family (husband, son) and I recently returned from a 4 night stay at the Distrikt hotel during the Thanksgiving holidays. It was our first trip to NYC. The staff especially Nesha and Hugo were awesome to say the least. They were very helpful and provided all of the information that we requested. After an eventful flight to NYC and every evening after returning from a long day of sightseeing we were warmly welcomed back to the hotel. The hotel was very clean, quiet, modern, and the beds and pillows were super comfy--much needed after a long day. Hot coffee was offered every morning and apple cider in the evening. The brownie, chocolates on the bed, weather card, and turn-down service was also a nice touch. My hubby was also greeted with a mini cheesecake on the night we arrived for his birthday with a handwritten birthday card! The night before we left we asked a gentleman (can't remember his name) at the desk about transportation to Laguardia the next morning, he ordered a car and the driver was waiting for us at 5:00AM when we came down to the lobby. The location was perfect, there were 2 or 3 subway terminals just steps away from the hotel and a short walk to Times Square, Hell's Kitchen restaurants, and the theaters. We also felt very safe walking to and from the hotel. We will definitely stay here when we return!

title: “How bad is that?”
text:
About a month ago I decided to spend a week in San Francisco with my wife at the beginning of April 2012. I selected the Grand Hyatt as our Hotel after some extensive research. I phoned the Hotel and was offered a suitable booking with a package which offered “two-breakfasts-for-the-price-of-one”. Total cost … a not unreasonable $1,700. When the email confirmation arrived there was only one breakfast shown. I then exchanged about five emails with the Hotel to try to have them honour their original offer. They responded each time in a most curmudgeonly way - offering alternatives that were all less attractive than the original offer. After a month of emails I decided they were simply not going to give this particular potential customer a taste of their “expect nothing less than spectacular” slogan.
I finally cancelled the booking and booked an alternative hotel in San Francisco.
The purpose of this review is to give people a flavour of the Hyatt Hotel policy towards guests. I don’t know if the original offer was a mistake or not. No one in Hyatt referred to it in any of the exchanges. However, once made, the Hilton Staff should have set about making a potential customer happy. For the marginal cost of a breakfast they lost at least $1700 worth of business and released a dissatisfied customer into the travel world, without even having stayed at their Hotel.
What a great day’s work!

title: “Everything was great!”
text: Stayed at this hotel for a conference and it was just great. There are two shopping centers attached to the property. The room was good and the bed was very comfortable. The staff are rock stars! They were all so friendly and incredibly helpful. Anything you asked for they would do their best to accommodate. The conference space was nice and the A/V folks were great. All of the food I had was fantastic!

title: “GREAT LOCATION, GREAT STAFF, GREAT RESTAURANT”
text: This hotel is very convenient to Boston Common and the Freedom Trail (If you walk all the way down to Bunker Hill take some breaks and rather than walk all the way back call a cab; it won't cost very much at all), the staff are very nice and helpful and their restaurant is really quite good. Be sure to get the Boston Cream pie at some point in the trip. They have valet parking which is good given the narrow streets in the area. Also try Ernie's Pub down the street for lunch or supper sometime. And, for you coffee/caffeine fiends, like me, they have an on-site Starbucks bar in their gift shop (which is also very nice) and there is a full-blown Starbucks one-half a block away that opens at 6 am (except for Columbus Day). Also, given the construction in Boston add thirty minutes to your destination and ONE HOUR to get to Logan airport. Also, if you rent a car and are returning it in Boston pick a rental agency that has onsite pickup and return - DON'T rent from Thrifty as their site is some miles alway from the terminal and you are at the mercy of shuttle buses.

title: “Practically perfect place”
text: We stayed at this hotel twice because our flights didn't connect properly, necessitating two overnights in Houston. The beds were extremely comfortable. We were not traveling with a laptop, so we found the computers available in the business center very convenient. Breakfast was excellent, and included sausage and eggs, waffles, and yogurt in addition to the usual cereals and pastries. Our only complaint was that the shower temperature was a bit lower than we prefer, but was still warm enough to be comfortable. Overall, a lovely place, and we'd definitely stay here again. Also, we enjoyed dinner both nights at Kung Food, a very good Chinese restaurant next to the hotel.

title: “Great experience!”
text: My best friend and I visited for a long girls' weekend - it was my first time in NYC. The location was great, the hotel staff was helpful and professional, and the hotel itself was clean and beautiful, in spite of the renovations. At the desk, I asked for a room upgraded and my request was accommodated with a smile. I came into Penn Station from JFK, and the hotel was in easy walking distance. We also took in a Knicks' game at MSG, which was right across the street. The subway was easily accessible, and there were always cabs waiting in front of the hotel. I would recommend the hotel and plan to stay there again when I return to New York - which I definitely will as soon as I can. Thank you, New Yorker!

title: “Clean, tidy, handy to city, good value.”
text: Just what we wanted for one night - clean, tidy, comfortable, close to restaurants, free parking (a bonus in that part of town), very friendly staff. Lovely.

title: “Good hotel and decent staff”
text:
We were in DC for couple days and booked an advace reservation with a decent rate.
The room was fine and the service was on point. The restaurant food was good also. On our last day we wanted to try something different and we were starving. The manager refered us to a fabulous Brazzilian restaurant which we loved. Thank you.
The Beacon will be our forst choice in D.C going forward.

title: “great place!! BAD PARKING!!!”
text:
we had a wonderful stay!!! 
for the price i was expecting something far less than what we got. this was wonderful. the rooms felt homey and we honestly didnt want to leave. we had a corner room, which had a beautiful view from the seventh flooor.
a quick one night stay after a bo burnham show, this was all that and then some.
another thing, is the toilets are REALLY LOUD! it startled me the first few times and when youre sleeping, you can easily hear them next door. and the heaters in each room are loud aswell but nothing to complain about.
but parking.....BAD!! it was terrible. we paid 60 dollars. it is 27 dollars for over two and a half hours. we parked, stayed a while and then wanted to leave for dinner, paid 27, didnt know firsthand! came back and had to pay another 27. bull. we were not happy. there wasnt anything anyone could do which sucked. but all in all we had a lovely stay and i would love to stay agian!!

title: “Perfect”
text:
We loved it. We stayed for 4 nights over Easter and we were delighted with our choice. Check in was very easy. We stayed on the 10th floor and overlooked Lexington avenue.
The hotel had nice old style touches that we enjoyed. The downsides of this stay; it was very noisy at night in the room. The street below has constant horn honking and we heard an emergency siren every night. There is no free wi-fi in the rooms but you can get free access from the lobby.
The hotel is well located for the main attractions. We would definitely stay again.

title: “Classy hotel that does many things well”
text: In "Foggy Bottom" near the State Department and World Bank, this government/business hotel now also, from the mix of patrons in its lobby, caters to the always-strong tourist trade. The hotel's convention facilities have undergone a complete and very successful makeover since my visit last year, with new eco-friendly furniture, carpet, paint, and decorative accessories. Oddly, the renovation did not solve the inconvenience of a single set of bathrooms for the entire convention floor (and for lobby occupants on the floor above). Although I did not dine in the restaurant, the food it served to our business group was very good; as to one seafood lunch, terrific. A number of restaurants and taverns are nearby, the edge of tony Georgetown is 5 blocks, but the tourist areas on the Mall are a very long walk, with the Foggy Bottom metro an inconvenient hike as well. I loved my spacious room with its comfortable king-sized bed and overstuffed pillows. The mini-fridge also was nice, although a mini-bar would have been nicer. Two nitpicks: the "business center" reminded me of those email-checking computers you find at foreign resorts. Two PCs tucked into a tiny alcove off the busy lobby for which you vie for time with kids playing games; no printer, no privacy. And the room wi-fi is simply outrageously expensive for a business hotel at $10/day/device.

title: “Great location,clean and friendly!”
text:
Just got back from the hotel metro this afternoon. We spent 5 nights there ,12th-17th Feb. It was a great place. Really clean and tidy. We were on the 5th floor in a room that over looked a building site, but it wasnt a problem, there was no way we would have opened the windows in that weather!! The room itself was not huge but was fine , we only slept there. The bed and pillows were so comfy, thankfully, this turned out to be so important after all the walking! Small but clean bathroom with an enormously powerful shower!
 The free breakfast was great for us, it started us off for the day until we had to stop again. Tea , coffee,juice, fruit, bread, bagels, yoghurt and huge muffins and pastries. Yum. All available in the comfy lounge with chairs, tables and soft sofas.
 The location was great especially for the first time visitor. The ESB one block away, 5th Ave one way,broadway the other, close to Times sq and the TOTR. We got the train into Penn station when we arrived and managed to find our way to the hotel in about a 10 min walk. We used the subway alot to get around and the station was nice and close.
 All in all a great hotel in a great location, Loved it. Will try and load some photos later when I have woken up properly!! Go for it, its great.

title: “An adequate stay”
text: I stayed at the Jacksonville Hyatt for one night for business, and it was just what you'd expect from an older, large Hyatt Regency property. Everything was perfectly adequate, but nothing was stellar. My favorite things about the hotel were the bed, which was quite comfortable, and the staff, who were all extremely friendly and helpful.

title: “great location, friendly staff”
text:
Room was large, although strangely shaped. We had a double without a balcony, with kitchenette and large storage area. Laundry area was conveniently located, which we took advantage of. Decided one day to go to the pool on the roof, was small but seemed to be kept up nicely. 
Make sure you get your luggage out of your car before you park, it was completely valet, I have no idea how hard it would have been to get something out afterward. We walked to the metro, restaurants were nearby. Took metro everywhere we could.

title: “Yup, It's a Ritz (except the fitness center)”
text: Have stayed in Ritz/Four Seasons properties in several cities and this one followed in line; prompt service, individualized welcome card upon check-in (not that I need that kind of thing), clean, comfortable room and beds - and the requisite Ferraris, Porshes and Escalades parked front and center with the valet. We had a ton of luggage including musical equipment, and the bellhops were attentive and luggage was in our room less than 10 mins after check-in. Was a little disappointed in the fitness center - more along the lines of something you'd find at a Hyatt, but still decent. Close to shops, etc. Still ticks me off that the Ritz and other 4/5 star hotels charge an extra $10 for internet access, but guess most are just expensing it through on business accounts anyway, but just include it in the room rate - I can get "free" access at Best Westerns!!! Overall, you'll definitely know it's a Ritz.

title: “The W saved my family vacation”
text:
In another review, I mentioned that the Aloft hotel oversold their hotel and were unable to book my parents a room at another downtown hotel and this was the night before the Texas-OU fooball game. This is the happy ending to that story that occurred at the W.
I had a reservation at the W Hotel for four of us in the party because we were unable to get two rooms at the Aloft. After the Aloft was unable to find us another room, we got to the W around 1am and were welcomed by James at the front desk. I told him that I knew they were sold out, but that if anybody cancelled or didn't show up that night to please let us know because my parents were going to have to cram into our room on the floor because the Aloft gave away their room. He apologized profusely even though the W had done everything right and said that he would see what he could do.
He then went to the back to check on something and came back to let us know that the manager said it would be ok for him to upgrade us to a suite so we would have more room for my parents. This must have been an emergency room they saved in case of problems at the hotel. The W did not have to do this, but they did and I cannot express how elated my entire family was with this. 
And this was no normal suite. It was an enormous suite, with a 6 person dining room and huge balcony overlooking the American Airlines Arena. On a sold out night before one of the biggest football games of the year, the W came through and I will never forget how well we were treated. My parents couldn't believe it either. They still live in a pretty small Texas town and they must have called everyone they knew the next day to tell them about the room and the view of downtown Dallas.
The hotel staff even called the next morning to say they had rooms available if we still wanted to book one more for the second night and that we could use cash and points. So I booked another room for the second night for my parents to give us another bed. But the suite was excellent for that first night after we had all been travelling the whole day and it was so convenient for getting to the game the next day on the DART.
THANK YOU SO MUCH TO EVERYONE AT THE W FOR MAKING THIS TRIP ONE THAT MY PARENTS WILL REMEMBER FOR THE REST OF THEIR LIVES.

title: “Nice rooms and location, but strange issues with ancillary services”
text:
I have stayed at the Belvedere many times for multi-night stays in the past year, and this review is an overview of my general experiences there. The hotel's location is ideal for those looking to visit Times Square, Central Park, or anywhere accessible by Subway. I always love the rooms. They are decently-sized for NYC, the windows open (a definite plus for someone whose sinuses suffer when the air is too dry), the decor is lovely, and there is a small kitchenette set-up, with a refrigerator, microwave, sink and coffee pot. Even when I am in a room next to the elevators, I do not hear them. The staff is always quite friendly, and they often recognize me, since I'm a regular guest.
Now for the downside. The internet access NEVER works. This is not just my issue. I have heard it from many other business travelers staying there. I am not sure of the problem, but I am always told they are "working on it." One or two elevators are often out for repairs, which means waiting an extraordinarily long time for the elevator. Also, there are permanent tenants in the building, and their rooms are mixed in with the hotel rooms. These tenants are generally invisible to me, but a colleague was recently hit on by a man late at night in the gym who claimed he was a tenant. This made my colleague quite uncomfortable. I advised her to call security if it happened again.
One night, I was locked out of my room for several hours until 3am. While the staff was pseudo-helpful, offering to put me up in another room until 8am when the maintenance person was back on-site, this was not acceptable, since I had an 8am meeting, and everything I needed, including clothes, was in my room. When I insisted they call a locksmith, they managed to get me into my room in about 20 minutes. I recognize that quirky things like this happen, but no one offered to run to the drug store to get me toiletries and no one thought to call a locksmith until I insisted. To me, that seems odd in a city and industry that is service-based.

title: “Room in Need of Repair”
text:
The room (#129) was comfortable but there are some serious repair issues. There was mold growing in the bathroom, the toilet was in terrible condition, painting was sloppy, wallpaper was peeling from the walls, and both faucets leaked. Looks like repairs were attempted but were very unprofessional and sloppy.
The hotel building seemed well kept and the grounds looked nice. Although there seemed to be a lot of people there, the area was pretty quiet.
The bed was quite nice (lots of pillows ... I think there were 5 for a king bed), the room was quiet, and the blackout curtains were great. Air conditioner worked fairly well. Wireless internet access was available but signal quality was poor. The room was very quiet.
Parking is really bad. There is a lot of it but the parking area is narrow and difficult to maneuver in unless you have a small car. There is also some on street parking. Watch out for the steep dip after you pass the pool; it's difficult to see traffic coming up the hill.
Lots of restaurants in the area. This is on a busy street so getting out of the driveway can be challenging.
Here are photos of the problem areas in the room:
http://picasaweb.google.com/rmludwig/DaysInnStudioCity?authkey=NTdoDlUbuqw

title: “Unexpected luxury...loved it...great suite.”
text: Boutique hotel feel... Contemporary comforts of a home away from home. Great!

title: “Good location but small rooms”
text: I stayed a couple of days at the Boston Milner during the summer and I would mention as a positive point its good localization near the Boston Common Gardens. However the rooms are extremely small.

title: “GREAT!”
text: after reading all these bad reviews, i was really scared of how the place might be. but overall, it was actually pretty awesome. first we got there around 3:05, so i thought we would be able to check in right away, but the people there said that our room was getting cleaned so we had to wait a while. after about 10 or 15 minutes of waiting, we finally got the keys to go up to our room. my room was the director's 1-2 people studio room. when we got up there, the cleaning person, who is actually really very nice, was just finishing up. the moment i stepped inside the room, my first reaction was "WOW". there was a bathroom to the side, a bed, a tv with dvd player, stereo with greaT sound quality, a cable connection, and a kitchen. i think the kitchen was one of the greatest parts that made yourstay better than a regular hotel room. it came with a fridge, stove, dishwasher, sink, toaster, coffee maker, microwave, just about everything there is to a kitchen, even plates, cups, wine glasses, eating utensils, cooking utensils, napkins, dishwasher detergent, cooking pots and pans, can opener, everything!! it wasn't cold or anything like a previous review said. and the towels were just fine. some things i didn't like was that the yourstay "office" people (since their office is in one of the apartments) were slow. they took a long time to give us our keys. also, another major complaint actually, was that our tv did not really have cable. we weren't sure because we had the tv guide for cable and sometimes the cable channels worked but they came out in either negative color, or just fuzzy waves. the sound came out and everything, but it was just the screen on a lot of the channels. we didn't watch too much tv anyways. we had brought dvds so we just watched those and besides, there's sO much to do around there. herald sq has macy's, herald center, manhattan mall, victoria's secret right across the street, and the subway station is right outside the apt so it was just an awesome place to stay. i think yourstay is really awesome if you are planning to stay for more than two nights, or if you're going to stay in your room and cook a lot. it's a bit expensive if it's only for one night. i stayed for two nights and we ate in our room a lot so it was worth it.

title: “Good location, good hotel for NYC and great staff”
text:
Yes the rooms are small, its NYC. But the location is very convenient, especially if you are working in the garment district or shopping Macys, etc. Close by subway makes getting anywhere easy.
Staff was noticeably friendly and helpful from front desk to housekeeping.
Free breakfast was much better than expected based on other propertis nearby we have stayed at.

title: “A Disaster”
text:
I travel frequently and always try to book my overnights at a Marriott property. Until this stay at the Philadelphia Airport Marriott, I had never spent a disappointing night with this chain. 
My room was lovely, but the bathroom had a myriad of problems: broken hairdryer, tub that would not drain, toilet that would not properly flush. It took 2 days, 4 requests and finally a face-to-face meeting with a hotel manager to get a new hairdryer and a properly working toilet. The tub never did drain properly. The food service is expensive and the quality is marginal. I ordered from room service twice and both times, despite specific instructions (requested in a kind and friendly manner), the orders were wrong (and I was overcharged). After paying $17/day to park, I was not given the appropriate receipts to drive my car out of the garage. I had to pay additional fees to the parking attendant and was told I would need to return to the Marriott to arrange a refund. I understand that customer expectations can, at times, be unrealistic and petty. In my case, what annoyed me more than the actual shortcomings of my room and the restaurant, was the complete lack of customer follow-up at the hotel. Words like "my pleasure" or "how can I serve you" mean nothing if there is no real service to back up the phrases. Marriott needs to take a closer look at this property...it is an unfortunate blemish.

title: “Big and Nice”
text: I just stayed for 4 days in LA and this Hotel was nice, even if it is close to the airport. The wellnes area is small but nice and the service is excellent in the complete Hotel. Shops and restaurants inside are good, so if you are tired and do not want to go downton than this is a good place to stay

title: “Wonderful Hotel from a frequent traveler to New York...”
text: I stayed at the Marriott Marquis Times Square in late January 2007 to attend the New York Gift Fair. The service desk and bellhops were extremely courteous and pleasant. While this is a busy area of town, and I was sceptical of staying in Times Square as I usually avoid this area when I visit New York... this was not bad at all. The hotel did get busy at times, but there is so much space to spread out that it makes a big difference. The lobby bar is very nice and a great place to relax. Beds were super comfortable and wondefully soft sheets. Room service was always timely and couretous. Highly recommended!

title: “Happy with hotel but no AC made my stay slightly uncomfortable.”
text: I stayed at this hotel for one week. I chose it because of its location and because of the price. I doubt you could find a better priced hotel in the area. If you want to spend an extra 100 then you could probably stay at another hotel in Manhattan but this hotel is fairly priced and not overpriced like the other 3 star hotels in the area. I asked for a newly renovated room when I checked in. I also checked in at 6 in the morning so I am very grateful to the clerk who checked me in early with no hesitation. I was staying on 10 floor. The room seemed to have new bedding and curtains. The carpet did not look new but it was not dirty. The bathroom was small but very clean. There was some rust on the toilet but nothing to complain about. Remember that this is an old property in New York city. Because of all the bed big reviews I took the time to inspect the room before settling in. I ripped the bedding apart and moved furniture and looked behind picture frames. I came up with nothing. Not even a dead cockroach. It was very clean! When staying in a hotel in midtown I only have two requests. No bed bugs and the rooms needs to be clean.
