You can't expect much else for the price. 150 a night in New York will buy you a high class room in a Motel 8. That's how far 150 goes in the area. Know what you are buying before you complain. That being said I am disappointed that I wasn't told at check in that the AC was not working. I called down later that night and the desk clerk told me they didn't turn on the AC until April. Which is fine. If that's how they run their hotel I have no problem with that but I would have appreciated being told at check in. They quickly offered an electric fan for the room. I asked for two and they brought the fans quickly. The fans helped a lot and because it was not hot outside I didn't really need AC. This would be a big issue in the summer time. I would suggest calling to make sure the property has AC. My only other complaint is that the smoke from the room upstairs came down into our room from the bathroom vents. I'm not smoker so it did bother me. I was not in the room very often so I did not complain. I would stay at this property again. The rooms are not the best but they are the best that I could afford. There are plenty of cheap hotels in NYC if you are willing to commute. Overall, they have nice clean rooms. Great housekeeping staff. Friendly front desk. Great location. Great prices. Could use some updates but I felt like I got what I paid for. If you have an extra 100 a night to spend then spend it! There are nicer properties. Either way. It's NYC. Enjoy your time and save your money for the city!

title: “Hotel Elysee -- absolutely first rate”
text: What a great NYC hotel. The service was excellent -- the staff very well trained and geniuinely helpful. The continental breakfast was more than adequate and the dining area was different: a casual lounge, much like a luxury home, with sofas, small tables, alcoves. They had free wi-fi in the rooms or you could use the hotel's computer and printer -- all at no extra charge. No nickel and dime-ing. We had a small suite -- it was very nice, HD TV in the living room, nicely furnished. Even the sofa-bed was of high quality. Overall a very good value for NYC. As good a hotel experience as I've ever had in NYC -- highly recommended.

title: “nice hotel!”
text:
the hotel was great,got comfortable beds,nice breakfast,clean,and they got nice attitude.
the point is,the location! because this hotel is very near from Union Square and others shops around here..its good for you who loves shopping :)

title: “Great location with a great staff!”
text: Great stay in one of the best locations in manhattan. Love the staff. Guest rooms have great aveda products and comfortable contemporary feel. Best hotel bed that I have slept in quite some time and the entire hotel just gas a great clean and comfortable feel. Kudos to management as it is very well run.

title: “Everything you need and want served up with a smile.”
text: We stayed at the Silver Cloud Inn while we were in Seattle for a wedding. It had everything we needed and more. Free internet access in every room, flat screen tv's, continental breakfast every day, free secure parking, free shuttle service to area attractions, pool, gym, and comfortable clean rooms. Everyone who worked at the hotel was friendly and helpful. The rooms were quiet, comfortable, clean, and spacious. The lake views were fantastic--you could see boats on the lake and the Space Needle. Several hours after we checked out our son realized he had left an expensive ring on the nightstand, we called the hotel and they called us back in less than an hour to tell us they had found it. So not only are the employees friendly and helpful, they are very honest too. I would recommend this hotel to anyone staying in the area. It was fantastic!

title: “OK hotel, disappointing breakfast”
text: My partner and I only stayed for 3 nights at the end of a long vacation. The check-in was prompt and the lady was friendly, I thought the room was reasonably nice until I saw the bathroom which was ridiculous. Its smaller than mine at home! The you could barely get in and close the door it was that small and the plastic fake marble walls looked like a 70s throwback. I am a big fan of starwood hotels but this one disappointed me, although the staff were very nice the bathroom and the terrible buffet breakfast (which was pricey and pathetic) was a letdown. The location is great for fishermans wharf but aout $45 cab ride to the airport. Although we didn't use the carpark it was stupidly expensive!

title: “Good value but rooms are small”
text:
The rooms are probably way too small, and though it suited me fine, my mum wasn't quite used to the lack of walking space. The bed was springy, probably too springy, as you can feel the other person's every movement. For a double bed, it was also probably too small, though it fit us two Asian females just fine. 
Having said that, I think this place is still good value for money and I'd recommend it to anyone who's on a tight budget and just want a comfy place to come back to and sleep in. 
We arrived way before the check-in time on the first day when the room wasn't quite ready yet, but Shana gladly took our suitcases in and then brought out a map to quickly explain to us how the buses and routes to the attractions worked. Following her instructions, we made our way to Fisherman's Wharf in under an hour from there. 
Like what the others have said, this place is rather accessible to all other places via the buses. Bus 71 and 6 practically takes you everywhere you want to go, via a few transfers. 
To get to the hotel on the first day, we took the shared ride van from the airport (thanks to the tip from another reviewer) which cost $17 per pax. On the last day, Shana helped us book an airport shuttle which only cost $10 per pax.

title: “Very, very nice.”
text:
There is nothing to criticize. Bummer. - ok, maybe the desk chair, when I really try hard.
Warm welcome, welcome drink, beautiful, generously sized room with modern, warm interiors. Free, high quality non-alc drinks and snacks from the mini bar, top range toilettries by Bigelow. Free wine in the evening. Most helpful and enthusiastic staff with an outstanding service by the director of rooms.
This leaves the Wall Street property miles behind. Congrats and highly recommended.

title: “Very Dissapointing”
text: Front desk staff were excellent and the hotel is very well located but as a diamond member, it is a very disappointing hotel. No exec lounge and restaurants are below average. Having to spend 30+ minutes to use a coupon for a Free Starbucks coffee is not acceptable to busy business travelers. The breakfast restaurant is dark and the buffet was not much better than an average breakfast restaurant. They charge $30+ dollars for the buffet. It’s a joke and they have the nerve to charge almost a full tip to have someone pour coffee. Don’t waste your time holding meetings there. Meeting Rooms have posts so you either see the speaker or the screen, but not both. Room was recently renovated, so at least it was up to date. Won’t stay here again, even if I have to attend a conference. Just too many other great hotels in SF.

title: “Great location”
text: Good hotel, quite big, conveniently located right behind Pier 39. Free Wifi, not always well connected. Recommended for breakfast and lunch bakery Boudin, good bread.

title: “great locations!”
text: great location. very clean. free parking. literally across the street from the mercado. and a 15 minute walk to the riverwalk. we walked it at night with sm children. felt safe. lots of people out with families. but i am paranoid and wouldn't reccomend walking around downtown SA anywhere at night. pool not heated so didn;t go for a swim. stay here. you won;t regret it!

title: “Great Vacation, we'll be back!”
text: We had a great trip, even on a budget! The hotel was very nice, we had a great view of the city. It was so convenient having breakfast downstairs - the omelets are wonderful -and the Manager's reception each night (free drinks!) was awesome! The staff was friendly and accomodating. We were within walking distance of the river, the Loop, the Navy Pier, and a quick cab ride to the Museums and other attractions. Parking is pricy, but we found it easy to do without a car and take a cab or public transporation. There's even a grocery store right accross the street! The heated indoor pool was small, but we were there in May and were practically the only people there. I recommend this hotel, we will be back!

title: “Great hotel, great location, great service”
text: Me and my girlfriend stayed at the doubletree for 4 nights in late may. This is my secound time staying here and there is a reason why I decided to book here again. The only bad thing about this hotel is they just recently discontinued the curtosy shuttle to and from the airport. It's unfortunate but it's not really considered a "airport hotel". We arrived early and the from desk gave us a few options if we wanted to check in early. For us it dident matter so we took a 3rd floor room and we were happy. At night I can understand peoples complaints about the freeway (our windows were open the entire time we were there) but the noise really wasent that bad at all, and as forthright trolly noise couldent hear it go by at night. (trolly service ends at midnight). Since we disent opt to rent a car we payed 14$ for a 4 day trolly pass which also covers transit. We went to seaworld (can be accessed by bus) or around a 18$ cab ride from the hotel, we also went to th zoo and it ended up being a 19$ cab ride there. So great location to both of these places. We took the trolly then bus to mission beach which was about a 15 min ride. Fashion valley mall is worth checking out when our staying there it's the next stop on the trolly from the hotel. All in all great hotel, great service and it's worth talking to the guys who grab cars and call taxis they know alot about places around the area. I shouldent also mention they allowed us to check out an hour later, but I'm sure that depended on how full the hotel was. Oh yeah if your polite enough they'll end up giving you some more of those delicious cookies they have, we ended up with about 6 for our plane ride home.

title: “Would stay again!”
text: Hotel was clean, the staff was attentive and pleasant. The location was perfect - close enough to get everywhere. The bathroom shower could stand to provide more room but hey, it's NYC! Would stay here again.

title: “ZaZa.....”
text: My girlfriends and I stayed at Hotel ZaZa for a Girls' Weekend. We had a great time. The hotel staff couldn't have been more helpful. We used the spa and thoroughly enjoyed it. Our room was very large and clean and they upgraded us to a balcony room. The balcony overlooked the pool area. At night, it was very loud, but we were able to get to sleep without major issues. The halls are somewhat dark and the elevator is extremely dark. I wouldn't have felt comfortable there if I had been alone. The location is a great and there is a great cupcake place across the street. You can take the trolley down to the West Village as well. We didn't have a car, so the parking fees weren't an issue for us. We loved the ZaZa and would recommend it.

title: “Bland, overpriced, poor service.”
text:
Stayed in a king suite (1 king bed and one pull-out) with my elderly parents the night before our return to Europe. We're all pretty seasoned travelers, and you don't expect much from airport hotels, but this was surely the worst stay on a 6-week tour.
The pull-out bed was not made on arrival, nor after we had requested housekeeping to come up, despite the friendly receptionists best efforts to get someone to come up. Eventually, I assisted a flustered housekeeping lady in getting it set up, doing most of the work myself. The bed turned out to be so rickety and poor-quality (you could feel every spring individually), I had to call for another 5 blankets to put under the sheets. 
The AC was out of control, there were no plugs anywhere close to the desk, the whole suite was a joke (really just a normal room divided into a 1-bedroom layout, and as cramped as that sounds), the hotel bar/restaurant wildly overpriced, and breakfast extremely bland.
There was a little placard asking us to call the reception if we'd rate any part of our experience below a 10/10 - we figured it's not worth it because this place simply needs a complete overhaul.

title: “Great experience”
text: I always try to stay there when I am in town. Nice rooms and excellent location. Very friendly and accommodating staff. It was nice to have a dining/kitchenette area in the room. Rooms were large and comfortable.

title: “Great for business meetings!”
text: I stayed here in November 2005 in a Suite. The suite was well-appointed, nicely decorated and comfortable. I was very happy with both my stay, service and the minimal food and drinks that were ordered. Very easy to get to airport as well.

title: “A little cliff dwelling.”
text:
The Pointe was a pretty good stay. There was some construction going on, but they did a pretty good job keeping the dust down. Although the layout was difficult to navigate, I really dont mind walking around - and Id rather stay in an interesting place than a box hotel anyway. I had to leave early, so the people at the restaraunt bagged up a little continental breakfast to go. My deck had a great view of the resort, pools, and sunset - and my room was recently updated. 
Con: I was there on business and wish the internet would have been free. 
Overall a good stay. I would recommend for a business traveler if they can get a good deal, or for a long weekend rest.

title: “Best Value”
text:
My wife and I visited a friend in Jacksonville. We stayed at this hotel for one night. We were pleasently surprised how nice the hotel was and in a great location. Quiet area and 3-4 minutes to the wonderful St. John Town (shopings and dinings) Center. Surprised because we paid "a Fairfield Inn price" for this good Marriott hotel. The hotel loby, hallways, carpets, and rooms are very nice. The problems I saw was it's not clean. The low parts of the walls, the corners are dirty. They need a cleaning crew. The hotel has musky smell when you walk in the loby. My room (403) smell urine in addition to the musky smell. We didn't ask to change the room because we were running late to meet our friend. I like the indoor and outdoor swimming pools and the jacuzy. The fitness center is small, but good. It's odd that you don't need a room key to get into the swiming pool, but you need room key to get into the fitness center. If they keep this hotel clean; I would pay double to stay there.
My advice: don't stay in room 403 and watch your little kids because they can get into the swimming pool easily and bring some candles to help with the smell. 
I will stay at this hotel again!

title: “Best location in NYC - next to Times Square”
text: We had just a great time in this hotel. All staff members were very friendly and helpful especially in the breakfast room and in the Saigon restaurant. Would come back and recommend it to my friends.

title: “Great location. Propert in need of an overhaul.”
text:
I lay in bed and gaze at the faded prints of fruit baskets on the walls and marvel at how in 2010, my room looks almost like my grandma's front living room circa 1984 -- complete with rose colored ceramic bedside light. The carpet in the hall and in my room is dirty and worn bare. It smells like a nursing home and the half dead plant in my bathroom adds the final touch to an otherwise dreary and drab room. I expect this out of some gritty, second rate metropolitan city hotel...NOT one in the nation's capital. And at $245/night I am gaggin' on it.
I am here on business. The evening reception is in the hotel lobby bar where christmas ornaments still adorn the bar shelves. HeellLLLoooOOO? It's June for cryin' out loud.
On the brite side, the hotel sits a top the DC Metro, conveniently whisking one off to any location in the city. And it's within walking distance to the national mall. So if you aren't picky about your lodgings (or how you spend your $$), but want a great location stay here. Otherwise, check out another property.

title: “Not amazing, not terrible.”
text: We wanted to get away for the weekend for a quiet birthday weekend celebration. Having only one night to get away and relax we wanted a special place that was neat and had some historic elements to it. The Admiral Fells Inn is definitely historic. It was very clean, the staff was pleasant, and our overall experience was average. Fells Point is a very neat place with a lot of quaint shops and taverns, but if you aren't a drinker or are there to simply get away, this is not a place the place to go. We were up half the night due to the amount of foot traffic and loud bar hoppers. Yes, we probably should have done more research, but I will definitely not return to the area for a quiet get-a-way. They did allow our dog to come, which we appreciated. The Inn was fine, but our experience was proved for us to return home more tired than when we left.

title: “Highly recommended”
text: We stayed here for 11 nights with our two children aged 9 and 12 in a room with two double beds. The staff were super friendly and helpful, greeting us by name every time we went in and out and bending over backwards to make our stay enjoyable. Very pleasantly surprised by the breakfast - a good selection, something for everyone and fresh and plentiful. Location could not have been better. We walked almost everywhere. The room was small, as expected but we were not in it very much so it didn't detract from our holiday. Very quiet rooms with comfortable beds and nice bed linen. No noise at all so we all slept very well. Cleanliness excellent, nice bathroom with good shower. More storage would have been good. There was nowhere to put anything so we had four cases on the floor for the whole time. Everything else was so good though that it didn't really matter. Highly recommended.

title: “Convenient, clean, good value”
text: Nice location, one block from Penn Station, in Koreatown, with 24 hour Korean restaurant next door. Clean, quiet. I had an inside room with essentially no view, felt slightly claustrophobic with drapes drawn, but acceptable. A/c a little weak: could get insufficiently cool. Overall, for its price range ($150 - 175 approx), good value and much, much better than other nearby ones (Hotel Penn, New Yorker). Would unhesitatingly recommend it.

title: “A good place in Midtown Manhattan”
text:
We were looking for a (n affordable) hotel in Midtown Manhattan, somewhere between Empire State Bldg. and Central Park. The Warwick New York is in an ideal location just opposite the new MoMA, off 6th Avenue and about 2 blocks from Central Park, which means you can walk to pretty much all the major Midtown attractions. There are subway stations either towards Central Park or the almost equally close Rockefeller Center
The hotel is a typical elegant city hotel, the staff are friendly and helpful and the room we had (standard) was big and cozy. The beds (boxspring) were very comfortable and the yes, we had a great view of the very close dark brick wall of the neighboring building that some others wrote about, too, but our room was not dark once we switched the light on, so we didn´t mind. We couldn´t be bothered to spend close to 30 bucks per person to have breakfast and opted for Starbucks (there are several shops - also very nice, as they offer free Wifi - because the hotel charges big time!)
So, if you can get a good deal, this hotel is certainly a good option for a city break in the city that never sleeps (though it was very quiet in the hotel!).

title: “Very poor”
text: Recently got back from a tour of the SE of the USA. My girlfriend and I visited about 15 different cities, so that means 15 different motels, spending one or two nights in each. I would say that the Queen City Inn was actually the worst of the 15 motels we visited. The room itself wasn't appalling - it was dirty and crumbling, but we half expected that and it wasn't a major issue for us. The real problem was the service. A frosty reception when we arrived from a woman at the desk who seemed completely out of it. When we went to the room we discovered that there was only one pillow. I went back to the reception and asked for another. A man was at the desk now. He tried to argue that the room is only for one person, hence one pillow. I told him that I had told the woman before that the room was for two people, and had paid for the room on this basis. He wasn't having it. Tried to argue the case that there should only be one person in the room, and therefore one pillow. Very reluctant to give another pillow, I had to really argue my case for one. In the end they sorted one, grudgingly. When we came to check out the next morning he barely grunted at me. When I said goodbye, the man at the desk flat out ignored me and looked at me with contempt. Left a really bad impression, and for that reason I advise other travelers not to bother with this motel. As a side note, their website is false advertising - the rooms are nothing like that (the website makes the rooms look decent, clean and professional, but our room was run-down, dirty and shabby).

title: “PERFECT location in Chicago! GREAT value!”
text: Great hotel. Staff is helpful, positive, and friendly. Rooms are clean and nicely designed. Room #1901 on a corner high floor was great; more like a studio suite! Free wifi with direct booking on the HRH website is key. The location of this hotel is PERFECT. Walking distance to numerous tourist sites, restaurants, public transit, and other convenience stores is PERFECT! I can't imagine a better location in Chicago. Walked to Blue Chicago, The Purple Pig, Gino's East, The Art Institute, Cloud Gate.., the list goes on. Further, the hotel's proximity to public transportation makes it even better; especially if you need to attend a conference at McCormick Place. (Just take the Metra across the street for an 8 minute ride.) The value of this hotel for everything you get is exceptional. I'll be back!

title: “One Hotel - Two parts”
text:
Stayed in this building for six nights in mid May - although it was the Club Donatello which is the top three floors. Problem was that when booking I did not realise the difference that the Club rooms are privately owned, like a timeshare room. Treated as guest to the hotel with full use of facilities but lacked the 'mini kitchen' facilities in the hotel - no microwave etc - but too late to change on arrival. Anyway, the reception was fine, very friendly and helpful suggestions for breakfast. We would recommend Lori's Diner or Cafe Taza. Room was very large and the bed was just great. Furniture was dated - others might call it classic. Lots of mirrors - whole walls. Location was superb - 5mins from the centre and transport.
The big test is would we go back? Yes but would try for the hotel first.

title: “Great Location”
text:
The hotel is well located in the Soho/Greenwich Village area of New York. Great location to stay with many bars and restaurants to choose from and a conspicuous absence of chain establishments, barely a Starbucks in sight believe it or not.
Room was compact but clean, modern and comfortable, and included king sized beds and large flat screen TVs. Heating/Cooling system was excellent. The hotel itself was quiet, however there is a degree of traffic noise from outside. This is a common problem with hotels in Manhattan due to main roads and volume of traffic, no fault of the hotel.
The hotel does not feature an extensive lounge and bar area, but given the location it is not something you would be likely to make use of.

title: “Pretty Good - but watch out...”
text:
We enjoyed our stay at the Hamilton Crowne Plaza. The room we were in was nice - but was a little small. Everything was perfectly clean. The location of the hotel was perfect for us for a weekends sightseeing.
The only problems we encountered were that the room was quite noisy: there was a lot of noise late at night which sounded like people were in the room with us. I guess this is the downside of an older building - the sound insulation is not great.
The staff that we came across were very friendly and helpful.
Probably worth avoiding the offer of cars arranged to the airport however - the price charged was very different from what had been promised.

title: “Location, Location, Location”
text: Our stay at Hilton West 57th Street was great. It was a perfect location as we had an event to attend at Lincoln Center. The room was comfortable and modern. I loved the spa like shower and bathroom. The service was excellent. I also took the opportunity to use their spa services which was great. I might add that this is a terrific location if you are interested in shopping on 5th Avenue, going to Central Park, Carnegie Hall, and MOMA. All in easy walking distance.

title: “Horriable Accomodations, Good Service, Great Location”
text:
My mother and I flew to San Francisco 5/19 for a concert and stayed one night at The Adante Hotel. The hotel definitely needs some work.
1) The room accomodations were unsatisfactory. Apon walking into my room I was horrified by the color of the walls, which were a shade of yellow that looked ike someone had urinated on them. There was a hole in the wall that someone had unneatly covered and painted over. The murals on the walls simply show how cheap of a place this hotel is as they did not even purchase framed photographs for their rooms. The bed spread was worn and torn which prompted my mother and I to go out and purchase Lysol, spray down the bed, and sleep with our clothes on. At night, we were both very uncomfortable because the room was freezing and there was not AC control in the room and the door wasn't sealed correctly so light from the hallway pierced our room. Also, the window's lock was broken and a check makeshift lock was installed but one could still open the window from inside or out with the lock on. This made my mother and I feel very unsafe. The good thing is we only stayed one night, slept only 6 hours and checked out of the hotel as soon as we could in the morning.
2) The service was decent. Julius the manager accomodated me very well and the desk clerk Tony was also very helpful in letting us know places to go around town. However, when my mother and I needed to store our bags, the clerk gave us a key to a side closet and we had to store our own bags - which means anyone could have had access to our things and easily stolen them.
3) The location is good. 4-5 blocks from Union Square. However, when you walk out of the hotel go left not right, as the area borders Tenderloin - a not so friendly place. 
If asked would I stay at the Adante Hotel again, the answer would be definitely be no. The service and location don't make up for the horriable and disguisting hotel conditions. Even though its inexpensive, next time I'll pay the extra $30 bucks to stay at a nicer hotel.

title: “Wonderful location, awesome view, friendly staff!”
text:
My husband, toddler daughter, and I stayed at the Hilton Bayfront San Diego for the first part of our SoCal vacation and had a wonderful time! The location cannot be beat - adjacent to the convention center, across the street from the trolley, one more street to the Gaslamp District. 
 Check-in was smooth and took about 10 minutes, including them accommodating some requests. Because of our requests, our room was switched, and it took awhile to sort out the crib request, but we ended up getting it all sorted out.
 We requested a high floor and found ourselves with an amazing view on the 19th floor, facing Downtown and Coronado. The view was second to none -- really breathtaking. The room was great. We had a king-size bed, chaise, flat screen TV, desk, and a port-a-crib with plenty of room to move. The bathroom only had a shower, and I would've appriciated a tub, but my daughter learned to love playing under the falling water, so it ended up working out. We only ate once at the hotel, breakfast, and had room service for that, but it was wonderful! Really unique dishes, as well as the traditional, which made for a great start to the day.
 The hotel is 15 minutes to most everything in San Diego - Coronado Island, the San Diego Zoo, Sea World, the airport. Access to I-5 is simple and allowed for convenient drives to local shopping areas or attractions. For those with no car, the Gaslamp district is an easy walk and offers a variety of restaurants, shops, and great dessert options.
 My only two complaints with the hotel are that housekeeping tended to come in the early afternoon, during our daughter's nap time, so we had to work around her schedule -- we usually traded trash and used towels for new bags and fresh linens -- and that there is no quick dining in the immediate vicinity or the hotel. The hotel is geared for the business traveler, so I understand not having too many accommodations for families, but traveling with a little one does not allow for many long, table-dining meals, and it would have been nice to have a McDonald's or sandwich shop nearby or in the hotel.
 A major plus for the property is that the staff was always friendly and helpful. When we called to inquire about the crib, they sent it up ASAP. When we walked by concierge or the bellhops, they always greeted us with a smile and asked how we were. The valet attendants were social and friendly even though we self-parked, and the front desk always responded quickly and helpfully to any requests. By the end of our stay, some of the employees recognized my daughter and would talk and play with her as we walked through.
 Finally, one FYI fact - the hotel is not kidding when they say they adjoin the convention center. The center and hotel share a parking garage, which can make things... interesting when an even is going on. We happened to be in town over the International Auto Show weekend, and made the mistake of trying to maneuver through the crowds. I reccomend guests check the schedule for the Convention Center before they come to be prepared for any upcoming events. Also, the hotel is across the street from PETCO Park, so it may also help for summer guests to be aware of any home Padres games and prepare accordingly.
Overall, the hotel was beautiful, the location perfect, and our stay wonderful. Other than a few small personal gripes, we found our stay to be above average and can look back fondly on our time in San Diego.

title: “Fabulous”
text: I loved this hotel. The bathroom was wonderful with seperate shower and a tub where the water fell from the ceiling. Too neat! The king sized bed was extremely comfortable. There was some street noise (I was on the 6th floor), but it wasn't often enough to really bother me. The food from Room Service was just okay. The hotel staff were very attentive and helpful. I was expecting snotty service (which I tend to get a lot when I visit north as I have a very southern accent.), but I felt very comfortable there. The lounge is very relaxing with a rock firepit. Hotel provided free wi-fi. Pike Place Market is very close by. Check in wasn't until 4 and I guess they mean 4 beacause room wasn't ready at 3. But there's plenty to do within walking distance while waiting. Compared with other hotels in the area I found the price to be very reasonable for the quality and services given ($250/night). If ever returning to Seattle I will defintely stay here again.

title: “Very disappointed.”
text:
I booked the Hotel Mela based upon the excellent reviews I had read on here and paid for it using the money that was left to me following my grandmothers death. She loved to travel and New York was a place I had always dreamed of going to and the Mela seemed the perfect choice. 
I had booked a executive/superior room and at first glance when walking into the room it seemed small but perfect but upon looking out of the window expecting to see a view of the street we instead had a view of a shaft with pigeons on the window ledge. The bed was great and I have no issues with the room size as this is described by everybody on here and after all if you are spending all of your time in the room then you are not enjoying New York. I do however object to being charged for a 4 star hotel and paying for top room only to receive a room with pigeons cooing all night and a view of the shaft. The towels we had left for changing on one occasion were just put back on the side of the bath and the bath had hair in it on our arrival. 
This was not what I wanted to remember my grandmother by and it is a shame as the Mela is really well placed and had the potential to be first class for any traveller. I did mention at the desk for a room change but I was told that I could not and the guy just stared at me as if to say are you still here.
Since we returned home My partner has had some health issues which is the reason for the late review.

title: “Close, convenient, clean”
text:
Just stayed one night..went to "Dancing with the Stars" and Universal Studios Tours. Convenient location for both..right in the middle. Cab ride expensive 35.00 from Burbank airport...but walked to Hollywood and Highland mall and saw the Kodak theatre, shopping, Grahmans Chinese. Right own the street from Hollywood Bowl. 
Clean..nice people..actually quiet location.

title: “Wonderful place”
text:
The Phillips Club is first rate in every respect. I had to laugh when I read the above review. That "Italian grocery store" is Balducci's. 
Arguably the finest gourmet shop in NYC. Their flagship store is attached to the Phillips Club lobby. Many Manhattanites travel a good distance to shop there. Do not miss the many varieties of smoked salmon, btw. Best selection in North America, IMHO.

title: “Good value, location, and customer service”
text:
We got a great discount bygoing thru Hotwire -$120/nt. an older building. Not Hilton but charming small room. Beautifully restored lobby. As an architect I appreciate such things. Not cheapy paper thin walls like faux boutique Hotel Fusion. Most importantly our 9th floor room facing Market had air-tight window and black-out drapes allowed peaceful sleep. 
Only a couple of blocks from Market St and BART Powell station. It is kiddie-corner from the Hilton which has a Starbucks. Also another Starbucks on another nearby block. At least1 hop-on-hop-off bus line drops off at the Hilton. We didn't ride it this time but the trolley starts on nearby Powell St. Easy walk to Union Square, Chinatown, Market St or shopping, food, and sights.
The front desk and bell staff were friendly and quick to offer assistance. Wifi is free if you sign to be on their emailing list.

title: “High Quality Hampton Inn - new carpet”
text: I got a chuckle when researching hotels in the Jacksonville Area on Trip Advisor - there is not one REAL hotel (eg. Marriott, Hyatt, Westin, Hilton, local boutique hotel, etc) in the entire top 20! So - compared to what is available in the area this Hampton Inn should be rated a 5 star hotel - but for those who travel a lot it is what it is: a really high quality Hampton Inn experience. The staff is excellent, the rooms are clean and spacious (mine had brand new lovely carpet), the lobby area is clean and modern, the breakfast is basic and nutritious. The hotel is located close to corporate campuses and shopping areas. I've stayed here twice so far and will stay again when in the area - it really is the best around - hard to believe!

title: “wonderful welcome”
text: We stayed here for four nights in July 2005. We were given a warm welcome such as we have not experienced in nine years of travel in the U.S.A. by Frank and Judy. They could not have been more helpful with advice about all aspects of the city. It was a large clean room with microwave and fridge. The motel is in an ideal location. Yes, the parking spaces are cramped but once you are parked forget your car and use public transport. We cannot understand somebody's comment about car park noise which we did not experience whatsoever. We would highly recommend this motel to anybody for value, convenience and friendliness. Once you have found this place stop looking further.

title: “The Worst Hotel On Earth!!!! Caution Do Not Ever Stay At This Rat Hole!!!!”
text: Ladies and Gentlemen, what ever you do, do not ever stay at this place!!!! I live in lower Westchester and my girlfriend and I decided to stay in the city over night for a friends birthday, we booked this rathole because it was close to the party, WHAT A MISTAKE!!!!!!!!!! the place is FILTHY, the place is just gross!!!!!! I booked through orbitz, and paid with orbitz, a month later on my credit card bill I get almost a $300.00 charge from them...... FOR NO REASON, this place really sucks!!!! DONT EVER STAY THERE!!!!! but I will say orbitz was very helpful with getting the charge taken off for me!!!!!

title: “Compact but all you need”
text:
I stayed here in October, 2011. I wanted a hotel that was convenient to sight see and shop in New York and I found it in the Marcel at Gramercy. The hotel has been furnished tastefully. My room was small but I was able to fit a couple of suitcases and still have room enough to move around. I was on the 2nd Floor and facing the street, so my only complaint was that the street level noise was quite loud. Nothing but a pair of ear plugs couldn't fix. The bonus was the terrace on the 10th floor which showcased the New York skyline. 
Tip: Skip breakfast at the hotel and instead head to the Bagel shop on 24th Street. Got myself a bagel and a water for under a fiver.

title: “Great location. We will stay here every time”
text: Due to a late flight we arrived at the Hotel around 2AM (kudos to Carmel Car Service for sticking with us and waiting for us at the curb as we walked out). The staff was very friendly and the room we had requested was still available. The location is ideal for Central Park; shopping; Broadway and Times Square. The concierge desk knows everything and everyone in NYC. The Hilton New York will be our choice every time we make it up to NYC.

title: “Brother's wedding event and lots of out of town family loved the hotel!”
text: One of the best events ever. The hotel went out of their way to help during our stay.

title: “Great stay”
text:
Overall à great stay, Nice people really clean, great bed...
I'll definitly come back!
I stayed twice, about 13 days total.

title: “St. Patrick's Hotel Stay”
text: My wife along with my mother in law spent 2 nights at this hotel to experience St.Patricks Day in Chicago. This hotel is at a great location. We walked to all of our destinations such as Gibson's steakhouse and Lou malnatti's. Our one bedroom suite was spacious with great amenities such as Hermes toiletries. The sofa bed my mother in law slept on was comfortable as well the king bed. Staff were very friendly and took care of us.

title: “Good no frills hotel, great value for money.”
text: We stayed at the St James Hotel for a week in October and wouldn't hesitate to recommend it to anyone who just needs a clean, comfortable hotel to stay in in Midtown Manhattan. Front desk service was generally efficient,courteous and one member of staff was particularly helpful when we asked advice on places to eat. The room was large, clean and the double beds slept two comfortably and we got a good night's sleep every night. Contrary to the recently publicised problem afflicting New York hotels there were no bed bugs here. The hotel is within a few hundred yards of Times Sq and access to anything we needed as tourists. There is a cafe next door and a deli beside that both of which serve good US style food all day at very reasonable prices - we took breakfast at the deli almost every day. Eating dinner in this part of town generally cost us $100 - $120 for the the three of us including wine and service. By walking a few blocks we were able to do a lot better than that. The bus tours and the NY City Pass are really good value especially for a relatively short stay.

title: “Fantastic”
text: Stayed for 2 nights in December. This hotel does what it does quite well. Impeccable service, spotless rooms, lovely amenities. The room was quite large with a nice selection of high end products. The bathroom had a deep run as well as separate marble shower with a glass door - a must in my view for a hotel of this calibre. Our choice of newspapers delivered in the AM, extremely comfortable bed with housekeeping service like stealth - you never knew they were around, yet everything always picked up and immaculate. Location in the heart of North Michigan. Ate breakfast both days at the restaurant - overall quite good. Sunday hosted an unbelievably well stocked buffet. Workout room clean and well equipped with cardio and weights- complimentary for guests. We expected alot here, and we were not disappointed. A great splurge!

title: “Home away from home”
text:
During my move to El Paso, I could have chosen to stay at any number of hotels; but none could match the affordability, comfort, convenience to work and play, and the level of customer service as I received at the Wyndham. 
Having this oasis in the desert to come to at the end of a long day made my transition into my new life in El Paso a very pleasant experience. My room was very spacious, clean, and comfortable. A few times I had to do some work from my room. The wifi was super fast, and I loved using the recliner with fold away desk and outlets for my laptop! The staff was always attentive to my needs and very accommodating. The food selection in the restaurant was delicious. My mornings got off to a great start with complimentary Starbucks coffee and the breakfast buffet.
The courtyard was a great place to hang out with its huge pool area that features a water slide and jaccuzees. I very much enjoyed the covered sitting area where I would either relax with a cold beverage or have dinner.
The Wyndham sets in a great location that made it convenient for me to get anywhere in El Paso. It also sets within a short walk across the street to the El Paso International Airport. 
In all, the Wyndham was a great place to stay; providing many of the creature comforts of home and much more. It made my move to El Paso a so much more pleasant experience! It was a great home away from home.

title: “A great Boston experience”
text:
I can confirm what other reviews have consistently stated, The Copley Square Hotel is a great place to stay! 
I arrived in Boston on a chilly and wet evening but was given the warmest reception by a charming young chap called Ryan at the reception. I had booked here as a second choice (I originally wanted to stay at the Fairmont Copley Plaza but was not prepared to pay the ridicuous single room supplement) and was prepared for a smallish room. I was offered an upgrade for what amounted to £9pn inc taxes and I am so glad I took it....the room was absolutely beautiful, as someone with very similar taste in my own home I appreciated the decor. Apart from being huge (it was a corner room) and well furnished the 6' bed is one of the most comfortable I have ever slept in. Overall it was great value and I appreciated not having to pay the premium associated with upkeeping garndiose public rooms.
The reception staff are very young - probably all in their early 20s - but have a real professionalism and committment to customer satisfaction, although I didn't take advantage of this from the range of services on offer it would appear that nothing was too much trouble. The wine tasting was a nice touch after a long day of sightseeing but in truth would probably not impress a connoisseur.
The Copley Square Hotel has a great location, withn the close vicinity to the Fairmont, Weston, Marriot and Lennox within a stone's throw of Copley T. Everything in Boston and Cambridge is within walking distance (I walked to Harvard and back via the MFA but the average tourist might prefer not to!!), Boston offers so much history, entertainment, nice restaurants etc and is an ideal place for a clutural break. Did I mention the shopping?? - plenty along Boyston Avenue and Newbury Street but best of all the shops at the Prudential Centre are a real bonus. 
If you like to be looked after in welcoming surroundings with minimum intrusion, this hotel comes with the highest recommendation.

title: “Beautiful Wedding but LIED to and received the run around!!”
text:
Wedding
My fiance and I were part of a wedding at this hotel on December 14, 2012. The wedding turned out lovely. Alex did an amazing job. The wedding coordinator was switched a couple days before the wedding but I understood why. The 2nd wedding coordinator never showed up to rehearsal, matter of fact she was never seen again, but Alex who prepared everything and decorated was absolutely amazing. The groomsmen room that was promised was never available. There was another event in the room the entire time, so the men had to get ready in the bathroom on the 2nd floor.
The Room (I begged for after being told no problem initially)
Was beautiful. Exactly what I had requested other than the gm assigned us to a double when we reserved a king.
The Stay
The stay was great but what I had to go through.....
After reviewing tripadvisor and having the wedding coordinator give a tour of the rooms I knew I wouldnt be happy with the outdated rooms but I had already booked our stay. My mother worked at a brand new hotel only a block away so I could have stayed there for a extremely low price but my fiance was the best man and needed to be on call for the groom. With that being said.....I called and asked the front desk if they had any newly renovated rooms. I was told YES, several on the 4th flr but because the wedding was over a month away I needed to call back within 2 weeks of my stay to have my name assigned to one of the new rooms. I called a week and a half before we checked in and was told that those were sales rooms and that he could not give me one of those rooms. I asked him who I needed to speak with, he transferred me to the wedding coordinator. She stated she could put me in line for one but cldnt promise. I contacted corporate (no response). I called the hotel when I got off work that night. The mngr Amanda stated "oh your name just came across my desk". She said that they only had 1 renovated room in the hotel and that she apologized and gave free valet parking. I informed her that valet wasnt important to me, she was suppose to be transfering me to the general mngr but hung up. I contacted head quarters again (no eesponse again). Finally I researched and found the gms contact info. Once I got to him, he stated that there was only one room in the hotel and they didn't like alot of traffic in it, but he put me on hold came back and stated he gave me the room but took someone else out of it (hmmm), he offer 20 percent off....funny I cldnt get early check in because someone was in it, room service stated that we had one the many newly renovated rooms on the floor and that we were lucky. Oh and free valet was no where in the computer when I got there. No free internet. I had a final due that day. I never expected this from the Hilton brand. Never had I experienced this horrible service and lies from a hotel before. I WOULD NOT RECOMMEND THIS HOTEL TO ANYONE. I own a business in the area and all of my clients have heard the story.

title: “Lives Up To Its Rating”
text: Though we live in the New York City area, we recently decided to spend a few nights in the Trump International for a brief getaway. Though we've stayed in other top-rated hotels, the Trump is one of the few that truly deserves five stars. The rooms are well appointed, the service understated but spot-on and the views of Central Park are spectacular. The Columbus Circle location gives you easy access to almost every part of Manhattan via mass transit. We plan on returning at least once a year . . .

title: “Annual Girls Weekend”
text: My BFF's and I (7) had the most fabulous suite at the Kimberly Hotel in NYC. Every year we stay in NYC to celebrate "Girls Weekend". This year we stayed at the Kimberly in one of their amazing 2 bedroom suites. It was clean, very comfy beds and pull out sofa. The bathrooms were beautiful. We were very thrilled with the kitchenette. Our balcony was an added bonus and the views were amazing. The staff was just so accommodating and did it with a smile. The Rooftop Bar & Lounge was a great. Location, location, location!!! Perfect location. We hope to return every year to this fine hotel. The Kimberly Hotel was perfect for our group and we loved staying there.

title: “Fantastic hotel!”
text: I booked this hotel for a night stop over in Venice because it watoday accessable to the airport. I had read reviews on tripadvisor and was so impressed with the service from the moment we walked in.. We arrived at 9am and they let us in well before our check in time and allowed us to have breakfast. Which was perfect after a 15 hours flight. The rooms were spacious and very clean. A lovel walk to Venice beach and a little further to Santa Monica. I would definitely stay there again. 10/10 and value for money.

title: “Feels a bit dated, but nice enough”
text:
The Omni looks and feels a lot like a hotel which was flash in its day - unfortunately that day has passed. Not that it isn't perfectly ok, just some of it is a bit overblown for the standard of the hotel - eg the 10 bellmen mingling around all desperately trying to help you to earn a tip becomes a bit tiring. But thats coming from a New Zealander not used to that sort of thing so it might be perfectly normal.
Other than that the staff were friendly, room service prompt, the room was comfortable and the bed was huuuuge, and the location is ideal for exploring around the MOCA and Disney concert hall, and downtown. 
A warning to NZers (and others) trying avoid staying in Anaheim, and have this place recommended to you by a travel agent (like we were). This is ok for a night, but beyond that it is quite restrictive as the nightlife is dead, even restaurants are hard to get to. Pay the extra money and stay in Hollywood or Santa Monica.

title: “Very hip hotel, large rooms, a bit understaffed.”
text:
This is not our favorite Kimpton, but it is a nice hotel and a good value. The location is a bit out of the way for tourists but the public transportation in DC is excellent so it's not a problem. Like all Kimpton hotels, it has free wifi. Our room was HUGE. As always, the Kimpton bed is the most comfortable hotel bed we've ever slept in and one of the big reasons we stay their properties whenever possible. Also, all Kimpton hotels have a wine reception each evening which is complimentary and features two vintages each of red and white plus (sometimes) beer. It's a really nice feature and something I look forward to. The decor of this hotel is very mod so it's not for the person who enjoys traditional surroundings. The breakfast is good for a three star (it's not included). 
My main problem with the property is that it seemed to be understaffed during my two days there. There was often a line at the reception desk and I had to wait quite a while to get my checked luggage when I left. Perhaps they were just having a bad week staffwise because I've never had this problem at any of their other properties. 
If you enjoy a really modern atmosphere, you'll love Helix.

title: “Cool, best, awesome, comfortable, gorgeous value!”
text: OK, so I tried to get a bunch of good words in there. This is a great find. Very urban cool without the gag factor. Staff is exceptional, rooms beautiful and bed extremely comfortable. I'm looking up the linens online! Puccini and Pannetti's, the Italian restaurant next door is one of my favs in the city, and my local friends love it too! Hotel couldn't be more convenient to everything, especially the BART/Muni station. I come to the city to see my college aged kid and he and his friends think this place is cool too!

title: “Comfortable enough but not plush”
text: I went to LA in January after a business trip to Carlsbad. The Wilshire Plaza Hotel was good value (booked through hotel website) but it's nothing special... it's the old Radisson so you can tell the building and facilities are old. Location is good though, especially if you don't have a car, as there is a Metro station right outside.

title: “Best hotel for tradeshows in San Fran”
text: Having stayed in most of the hotels near the convention center, I recommend the Westin. You don't have to walk thru an endless lobby to get in and out. Staff is very helpful. The location is very convenient to shops and restaurants. The rooms and common areas are clean and the beds at the Westin are the BEST! Just stayed there again and had another great experience. My co-workers at other hotels are planning to stay at the Westin next year.

title: “Fit the Needs”
text: Friendly service, clean rooms and comfortable surroundings - just as promised. Air conditioning unit in room made noises throughout the night. Good location to get around Memphis if you have a car. Parking is free. Great for sports teams, wedding parties. Keeping looking if you want romance or something with character.

title: “What you would expect from a Doubletree”
text:
Pleasant room, comfortable bed, roomy sitting area and warm choclate chip cookies when you arrive. The only negative was that there were sessions for "Healing with Sound" going on and we could hear drums (sort of like the indian drums that you used to hear in Westerns) coming thru the AC duct until late evening. It was a bit annoying. Also, if the AC fan was off, you could hear voices thru the duct. The desk gave an excellent restaurant recommendation across the street ("Grazie") that we enjoyed.
Note: Don't confuse with the Doubletree on International Drive, We did in our GPS.

title: “Fantastic New York expierence”
text:
What can I say about the New Yorker… this is the 14th US hotel that we’ve stayed in for leisure during the past 12 months, and it was by far and away the best!
We arrived after a long flight from the UK and were greeted very warmly by Ana. They had our original request for a high room on file, and not only did they honour it, but also gave us a free upgrade from a View room to a corner View Deluxe. 
The room itself was reasonably sized for Manhattan (where the rooms are usually smaller than elsewhere in the US), clean and well fitted out with flatscreen TV with cable, bath/shower etc. I believe they have been recently refurbished, and are blessed with a quiet and modern air conditioning unit – something that so many other American hotels lack. We paid the extra for a view room, and boy was it worth it. We had a full-length view of the Empire State Building from the windows on one side of the room, and from the other a view of One World Trade Center, the Statue of Liberty and the Hudson. We could spend hours just looking out those windows! There is also free WiFi throughout the hotel. 
The hotel retains its original 1930s Art Deco style and much of its original charm. If you want a modern glass and steel building then look somewhere else. It’s located a comfortable 10 minute walk from the hyperactivity of Times Square, and is just a block from Macy’s (ladies!). Penn Station opposite provides convenient access to the Metro and transport to JFK. The diner next door does great breakfasts, if you have a large appetite. 
We can’t recommend the New Yorker highly enough, and it’s definitely worth paying the extra for a view room.

title: “Stay away from the Braxton”
text: I have stayed at youth hostels, and low budget hotels in the Middle East, all were pleasant and clean. The Braxton is the worst hotel experience I ever had. It is filthy and so musty it is at times hard to breath. You have to pay for all your nights up front, and if you check out early you are charged for an extra night. If you must stay there request to see the room before you pay.

title: “I would stay at the Trump to get the feel of what Hyatt use to be”
text: Location is the key for this hotel. Room temp and noise from the A/C - Heat is very disturbing. They have put in a flat screen to keep up with the times but the same old bed.bath and tile is from 1984.

title: “Spacious room”
text: Two king size beds was the reason I booked this location, and I loved everything about this hotel once I got there. The rooms are very large, the decor is clean and contemporary, the pool was very nice, and the hotel seemed brand new, even though the manager told me it is four years old. Staff was very nice

title: “Clean and Central”
text:
Our room was comfortable with plenty of room and everything was clean. The view from the room was of a brick wall, but we just used the hotel to sleep and shower. The location was perfect for using public transportation, we took the BART from the airport and were within 10 mins from the hotel (walking). It's pretty much in the center for going around the city to the Wharf, the Mission, etc. 
We had everything we needed and did not feel like this was a budget hotel at any point.

title: “my experience staying at the hotel”
text: I loved the hotel it was great. I have traveled a lot around the country with work and have stayed in many hotels and this one by far is the most family friendly hotel. Its on the river walk, police are patrolling the area around the hotel up until very late at night. The parking is great although you have to pay but its work it. The staff are great, the guy jonathon even remembers past guest. They really make you feel welcomed and safe. The rooms are great they are not the best I have been and the carpet could use a cleaning. The breakfast is great but could use a change in menu I have stayed there 3 times and have seen the same menu. The 5:30 kick back is awesome my kids love it and that is all that matters my kids feel welcomed at the Drury and if when you have kids anytime people treat your kids right you win the hearts of every parent. I have visited San Antonio 3 times this year and will be there again this weekend and I have stayed there and will continue staying there.

title: “Beautiful hotel, lousy service”
text:
When we first arrive, we were greeted by the valet people. They took the car, as we went in. After getting our hotel room, we decided to go out on the town. However, when we went to get our car they informed us that we have been charged $ 24. We weren't told of the charges before hand, so this had came as a surprise to us. Where we are from, it is unheard of to have parking fees that high. We were then told that we where going to be charged $24 for every day that we were there, and that we couldn't park anywhere else. Not wanting to spend an extra $100+ dollars just on parking, we decided to park at a near by parking lot and walk. When we asked to have the charges removed from our bill because we no longer needed the valet parking, they rudly ask us many questions, and after waiting 15 minutes, they finally took off all charges. Along with taking off the charges, they also closed our account so we could no longer buy items (like a pre-pay movie). We had also asked for directions to a place, but somehow they guided us the wrong way. We ended up in a mass confuesion trying to find our way to our destination. The hotel is also by a very "low" part of town. From many window views one could see homeless people laying about.
However, the hotel is very beautifully decorated, and the rest of the staff was happy to accomidate us. Personally, this hotel is great for business people, or any one that needs a hotel for a night. It isn't great for familys, espically people with young kids. Next time I go to Los Angeles, I will be staying at a different hotel, in a different side of the town. Hopefully this review is helpfull to anyone that is considering staying at the Biltmore.

title: “Strictly For Sports Fans”
text: I stayed at this hotel on June 24 of this year because of the close proximity to the airport. This hotel is in need of a rehab overall both in the rooms and the common areas. The room was large enough and clean but the bathroom showed age and the carpet was dirty. The property is fine if you are there to see the Phillies, Eagles, Flyers or 76ers, but there are no restaurants or bars in the immediate vicintiy. Close to South Philly but quite a distrance from the Central City. In the future I will stay in Central Philly and drive to any sporting events.

title: “does what it says on the box”
text: good location with parking, good transport links, not far from everything and a stonethrow from the gay area of Castro. Good choice of restaurants, coffee shops very close by.

title: “Convenient but ...”
text: I stayed at the Boston Marriot Copley Place in October for a conference. I loved that it was convenient, adjacent to the best shops/restaurants in the city and very accessible. However, the service leaves much to be desired. When I was checking in, it appeared that they had already checked in another person (whose surname was similar to mine, but who was obviously an entirely different person based on her address and other details) using my reservation and Marriott Rewards number. The mix-up was sorted out in a few minutes, but it was such a bother to have to explain that I had a reservation (made 2 months before) and that the mistake was theirs, not mine.

title: “OMG Housekeeping stole my birthday cookies!”
text: I live in Charlotte and my husband surprised me with a weekend Birthday stay at the Ritz. The staff became aware it was my Birthday and graciously sent up some sweets for us to enjoy however we were on our way out to dinner so planned to enjoy them later We returned to our room about 3 hours later to find that turn down service had been provided and noted that housekeeping must have been hungry because one of the cookies was missing from the plate.We had placed the plate right by the coffee bar before leaving so it was the first thing we saw upon reentering the room and as soon as it registered we both just looked at each other . We could not believe that a hotel of this kind would have staff of this caliber.So of course after this incident I went straight to where my jewelery was to make sure that it was still there. I never would have expected this to happen at 5 star hote. I let management know through phone call and they offered to replace the cookies but no thanks . On another note my husband and I also had Sunday breakfast in the restaurant and the waitress took 10 minutes to acknowledge us and take our drink order- and it was NOT busy by any means. She them proceeded to bring us our breakfast but not as ordered and just actually laughed it off saying that waht she brought us probably actually tasted better than what we had ordered.We left two small children at home in Charlotte with a babysitter and were actually looking forward to having a nice relaxing breakfast before going back home but such was not the case. This weekend is Food and Wine weekend in Charlotte and my husband just let me know that he had booked a night at the Ritz this Friday so that we would be able to enjoy the festivities. Thanks heavens he let me know before hand. I just cancelled the reservation. lI would much rather stay at the Ballantyne Hotel and pay the $45.00 car service fee. Their service is always impeccable.

title: “Nice Hotel”
text: I stayed here for a week in late June/July. I have stayed here previously so knew pretty much what to expect. The lobby is fantastic, restaurant, open for breakfast and dinner, is great. Also a free wine reception at 5 p.m. Hotel is contemporary and nicely decorated as such. Bed is great. Staff is very, very nice. My main complaint is the size of the rooms, very, very small. This time I had a king bed and there was very little maneuver room for anything else. Also, smaller things bugged me this time. No coffee pots in room; I don't like to get dressed and down to the lobby for it. I am ready to meet people AFTER coffee. The traffic outside was also noisy. Then there was a complicated docking station for an iPod, radio, and alarm clock all in one handy little box. The trouble was the alarm started going off way too early for me and try as I might, I could not figure out how to turn it off for good, other than the "snooze" feature. Unplugging was not an option as it had a back-up battery secured with a screw, and I don't travel with a screwdriver. A few little maintenance issues like a broken sink stopper were repaired promptly. All in all I would not choose this hotel again as a top 10 choice, but would stay here before big-box brands like Marriott, etc. My favorite is still Hotel Commonwealth or the new Revere, Boston Common, another independent.

title: “Great price/location but smelly linens & bad bed”
text: The Baldwin Hotel charges an incredibly low rate for SF near Union Square. But the linens and pillows smelled sweaty. The bed was very uncomfortable, squeaky, and caused my back to spasm. The internet speed was inconsistent and very slow (1 Mbyte) -- when it was working. The radiator could not be controlled. The pipes whistled while showering. The room was tiny and the bathroom had no counter space. No luggage rack.

title: “Toilet don't flush, motion sensor turns lights on all night, no refund”
text:
After walking thru the hookers in the lobby I get to my room which was deceptively labeled as an upgrade. In facts in the oldest building on the property, next to a busy road, with paper thin walls, and up 3 flights of stairs.
Rude gal at counter refuses to even say sorry about toilet or malfunctioning lights, refused to refund the big I cancelled.
Obviously crooks...

title: “You won't go wrong in booking a stay at the DIA Fairfield Inn”
text:
My wife and I have been staying at this Fairfield Inn for at least the last half dozen years and this is our preferred place when we fly either into or out of Denver International Airport (DIA), which we do multiple times each year. Prior to trying this Fairfield we had stayed at several other lodging facilities that are located in the same area, that being in close proximity to the airport terminal. Some of these were o.k. and one that I can remember was just a nightmare. But once we discovered this Fairfield Inn we decided that "this was it, this is where we'll stay from now on". And we've not once regretted that decision over these past several years.
We now know this place almost as well as we know our own home. So, I'll give you some details that will be helpful to those who have never been to DIA or to this Fairfield.
The motels location is roughly 4 miles from the airport terminal building. It, and many other motels, are actually located "on" the airport "premises", rather than being out on a highway or in the city of Denver. This Fairfield has a superb shuttle service that is owned and operated by this motel, for the exclusive use of its guests. The shuttle runs between the motel and the air terminal about every 15 minutes and operates 24 hours each day, so that when you arrive by air you get your bags and then exit the terminal building to the curb (the 3rd lane over from the terminal door) where you wait for the next "Fairfield Inn" van to arrive. They're painted white with blue and maroon trim so they're easy to spot. The driver will load your luggage and within about 10 minutes you'll be at the entrance door to the motel, where the driver will offload your luggage for you. There are about 6 van drivers and each one is a very nice person. We've gotten to know them by name as well as what they enjoy about Colorado; Kevin, for example, is an ardent fly fisherman. If arriving late at night by air, call the motel when you have your luggage and they will send the van to pick you up.
When arriving by air, if you're picking up a rental vehicle the van will take you to that location after they pick you up at the terminal. We prefer to spend the night at the motel and then the next morning the van driver wil take us back to the rental cars location, where we then pick up a car and head for the mountains, after a good nights sleep and some hours acclimation to the 5,200 ft elevation of Denver. This van shuttle is entirely free as a courtesy of The Fairfield; but we always tip the driver about $5. for each trip as that constitutes a significant part of their earnings and because they are so very nice.
The Fairfield "DIA", as we call it is new, less than 10 years old, attractive, very clean and is well run. Both the exterior and interior appearance is impressive. They have a room, just off the lobby, with a couple of computers for the use of their guests, so you can check reservations or print out a boarding pass while at the Fairfield. They also serve an very nice breakfast each morning, again as a courtesy to their guests. The motel has three stories and all corridors are interior corridors. There are 2 elevators for the upper floors. There is very adequate parking and the premises is quite safe for both people and cars which is something we consider quite important.
During the several years that we've stayed here we've never had a bad room or a bad stay. And all the people who work here have treated us with consideration and in a friendly manner.
This Fairfield is about 7 miles north of "I-70", which is the East/West highway that runs up into the Rocky Mountains (if you're heading West). When going into Denver it is about 15+ miles into downtown Denver once you arrive at the junction of "I-70" (and "Pena Boulevard", which is the North/South road that connects the air terminal building to I-70.
You can see the Fairfield Inn from Pena Boulevard when you've driving from I-70 toward the air terminal. It will be off to your right, about a half mile east of Pena Boulevard as you're heading toward the terminal. 
There are several places to eat which are within a half mile of the Fairfield Inn, one being just across the street, about a 100 yard walk from the Fairfield's front entrance.
Hope you like it. We Do.

title: “Not Bad”
text: Great Location! I loved the visual of the Wellington Sign- it helped as we walked back to see how much more we had to walk. This hotel was alright. The beds seemed clean. Beds were rather hard- but I was exhausted so it didn't matter! The carpet was very dirty. The bathroom was old and small but clean. The room had a hard time staying cool- with a loud A/C. We were on the 25th floor. The elevator was small, crowded,hot and not very smooth. It took them about an hour to get our car out of valet parking- we just sat in the lobby watching people come and go. Over all it wasn't BAD but it wouldn't be at the top of my list of hotel choices.

title: “Great stay!”
text:
We recently stayed in this hotel for one night only. We experienced great service from Varzan in the reception. We used points from Carlson Club, and we even got a upgrated room + free wifi :-)
The room was clean and the bed comfortable. Good breakfast in the restaurant! 
We will definently consider staying at Radisson Lexington next time we visit New York.

title: “Great downtown hotel”
text:
Stayed here for 2 nights in August 2008.
Room/suite on 9th floor was big and with a small kitchenette (nice with the fridge). The room was facing the habour and the downtown streets which gave a bit of noise friday and saturday night. But this was not a problem for us. 
Otherwise just a wonderful view.
Bathroom with tub was ok. Nothing fancy but just as needed. 
Breakfast was served at the roof teraace which is absolutely wonderful! Great view of the city- escpeically during the evening. Fantastic.
Breakfast was nothing specialt (maybe a bit too many cakes:)) but we managed fine.
Location is wonderful.
Everything is just outside and the hotel offered parkering (charged) which we used. Lots of restaurants, bars, a mall etc is just around the corner.
Great hotel!

title: “Awesome location with great service in a contemporary boutique hotel!”
text:
The staff at every level was accommodating, from the doorman to the manager! Chris, Claudia, Christina and Michael to name a few. They are so attentive that within a day we were on name basis! We had two rooms for 3 nights on the 14th floor with amazing views! We traveled with 2 teens and an 11 uear old. The neighborhood is teeming with restaurants and shops. The subway is close by and taxis are easy! The rooms are compact and no problem
For us. It is a new and clean place to stay with trendy style and comfy beds!

title: “I would think twice before coming again......”
text:
I was so excited to book this hotel for our family vacation. We have 2 kids ages 7 and 4 and the 3 waterslides at this hotel was the SOLE reason for me booking. 
Unfortunately we were so disappointed when we arrived around 1pm and found there were no chairs ANYWHERE around the pool to put our towels on. The staff feels the pain too. I mentioned to the lifeguard the problem, and she said, "believe me you are NOT the first to bring up this problem." There is room to add more chairs, it baffles me why they don't add more. 
The staff was the saving grace at this hotel. ALL of them were so helpful, nice and great!! 
We originally had a room in the Bayside tower, so HORRIBLE. I am not exaggerating. We were right next to the elevator and heard it all night. There were only 2 drawers to put clothes into, the nightstand table and a very small closet. The next morning we kindly asked to be moved. They were very accomodating. The tower rooms are MUCH bigger and have more drawer and closet space. Plus all the rooms have an inside hallway.
If you plan on staying here and your kids love to swim, you HAVE to stake out a lounge chair by 8am or they are all GONE! The hotel restaurant was good, but very spendy. I think the fish plate I got was 29$. Ask the hotel staff where to go locally for seafood, and it is much cheaper.
I agree with many other reviews that this hotel doesn't seem to live up to the Hyatt standards that I have had at many of their other properties. I will definitely send Hyatt a letter letting them know of my disappointments.

title: “Excellent...ands keeps getting better!”
text: I usually stay at this property about 6-8 times a year. Have always enjoyed my stays. Staff is exceptionally responsive and pleasant. Rooms are always clean with great amenities. My most recent trip I was blown away. The room seemed so clean it looked ready for a photo shoot. Plus I was blown away. Bathroom had heated floors and tv monitors in the bathroom mirrors. Needed new batteries for my remote. They were delivered in less than 5 minutes. My home away from home couldn't be better...

title: “Nice Conference Hotel”
text:
My daughter and I attended the SWACDA conference in March 2012. We were treated very well at the front desk. The room was very clean, great view, comfy mattresses and pillows. Accidentally left valuables in room during cleaning. The valuables were left untouched and the room cleaning was immaculate! Food at the Kitchen Table restaurant and the bar was delicious with beautiful presentation. The buffet was a great value, including drinks and dessert in the price. 12.95 breakfast, 16.95 dinner. Waiters were stellar!! This hotel has a huge computer access station area in the lobby. Hundreds of well-behaved teenagers/college students from the honor choirs had a great place to hang out. I loved that there was a full service business center where I could have Fedex packages boxed and sent. Cab to airport was about 23 dollars. Cabs were ready and waiting and hailed by the doorman. Valet and doormen were wonderful. 
The public bathrooms in the hotel and conference center were stylish, adequate number of stalls, well kept and fully functional. THANK YOU for this!!! We never had to wait for a stall, even with the large number of people at the conference. 
The Conference center is right across the street and there's a 2nd floor walkway to it...or you can cross the street. There are great local inexpensive places to eat within walking distance. It's located in walking distance from the artistic locations of the city including the Dallas Symphony Hall, the Art Museum and I'm sure many other places. We felt very safe out walking at night in this area. 
Conference rate was 159 per night which was a bit higher than the Marriott nearby (139). But the room and the general climate of the hotel, plus the convenience to our conference, great food and great rooms made it a value. The staff deserves kudos and compensation for making this a great experience. 
Only negative was overworked elevators during certain periods. But we learned to time our elevator rides to non busy times. We were on the 24th floor, so stairs were not an option.

title: “Good but not great”
text:
I had somewhat high expections and while the hotel was very good it was not "great". 
On the plus side:
This was our first time in NYC and the locations was really good. We did a lot of walking but the close proximity to bus stops and the subway station on 33rd street was also a plus. 
The staff were friendly and really helpful.
The gym was very nice as well and I liked that it was open 24/7 - great when you're jetlagged and up early.
On the downside
The e-concierge requests didn't work out at all even though I followed up with an e-mail. The staff did it's best to fix it but in the end we got only 3 out of 5 requests after a couple of reminders.
The room seemed clean but then we discovered a forgotten shoe next to the bed.
We unfortunately ended up whith noisy neighbours during the labor day weekend but we can't really blame the hotel for that. We thought about complanining but we were so tired after a long days of sighseeing so in the end we just used our earplugs. 
All in all I would come back but perhaps with lower expectations. I liked the neigborhood. We had breakfast at Murrray Hill Diner one morning and Chinese takout from Grand Sichuan one night.

title: “Wonderful Location!”
text: Hotel 41 at Times Square could not be in a more perfect location!! RIGHT next to "Rent". If you are going to see this show, book here. A short walk to everything. A very "trendy" type New York hotel...not like a hotel chain...more intimate. Great front desk personnel, all questions or issues were answered promptly. One night the hot water wasn't working, but was fixed in a few hours. Rooms are small, but if you get the superior room, you'll be fine. But be aware, even with this, no more than two people can fit comfortably in these rooms. Not much time spent in the room though, so it won't really matter. Bed is comfortable and linens were nice. Had trouble keeping the room cool at night...for some reason, the AC didn't always automatically kick on and it would get hot. Free coffee, danish and juice in the morning at the little hotel bar was nice...don't eat dinner there..the food was not very good. easy to get the Subway as well. I'd rate it as above average...about 4 stars. You really can't go wrong here and the price was resonable.

title: “Location, Price and Service”
text: What more can I say. Location was great if you wanted to be in amongst the cool and diverse surrounding neighbourhoods such as the Castro, Mission, Hayes. Close to transport. The room had all the necessities and was certinly big enough. Price was great value with the continetal breakfast and free Wifi and the service from Roy and his wife with friendly and accommodating.

title: “Room well, breakfast awful”
