text: My boyfriend and I went to Washington DC for a trip in my schoolbreak. He chose this hotel via Blackberry travel. The clerk didn't know that we had the breakfast included and we had to show him on the phone. Those 3 breakfasts weren't good at all. There's not a lot of choice. We can't eat apples or bananas which is sad because I don't like any kind of melon! The bread is dry and there is only apple jam no strawberry or raspberry! For the room, it was okay, ours was a bit smaller because it was near the elevator. The location is not bad if you like to walk like us. Capitol is about 20-25 minutes if you walk fast. The neighborhood is okay. I don,t think that we'll come back here again.

title: “Service and quality "as advertised"”
text: The reviews we read were good and the hotel exceeded our expectations. Except for the dumpsters being emptied at 0500 everything was perfect.

title: “Staff is very helpful/convenient location”
text: We stayed at the Holiday Inn Stadium after attending a Phillies game. This hotel is located within walking distance of the stadium and is very convenient. Just wanted to thank Adam and Demotus from guest services for making our stay more enjoyable. They went out of their way to accomodate us and make sure our stay was very pleasant.

title: “Perfect Location and COMFORTABLE”
text: We had a group of 3 and only stayed one night but it was the perfect location and very comfortable. Lobby is beautiful with mediterranean tile and black iron accents. Customer Service was wonderful. Gift shop is well stocked and has a lot of variety. We visited Sandra Bullock's restaurant (she wasn't there), Bess Bistro @ 500 W. Sixth, food was excellent. Also visited Hill Country Bible Church NW Sunday morning and enjoyed a great service. Both the restaurant and church were about 15 minutes from the hotel. Will definitely be back!

title: “Very nice for the price.”
text: This is not a 5 star hotel, but it IS a very solid 3.5 star hotel just as advertised. My only complaint was that we were not aware of the extra fee for parking until after we had booked the room. Then after paying the parking fee, we would not have known there was no charge for handicap parking if the elevator had not been out of order on our second night. Since my daughter was using a "knee walker" and we were carrying her crutches, you would think the desk clerk would have asked if we had a handicap placard. But all was well since they did credit the $16 parking fee that had been charged.

title: “Not truly a four star hotel.”
text:
We stayed at the hotel for 5 nights. The night we got in, we were led to our Premiere Suite only to find that it reeked of cigarette and/or cigar smoke.
My fiance is HIGHLY allergic to smoke. Called the front desk only to hear, " Sorry, it's the only suite we have left." They said they could send up an ozone(?) machine to get the smell out, but by then we were both coughing, and it appears the scent probably was imbedded in not only the air, but the drapes and upholstery. I asked for the manager, who was the ONE person ONLY who was pleasant and helpful the entire trip. Jeff said that he would give us two adjoining rooms for that night, and then tomorrow offered to set us up in not only a Premier Suite, but one that also adjoined to an Executive suite. WE actually had an "apartment," for LESS than the price we were going to pay for only ONE suite!
That was great. (However, there was a lot of honking horns where we were in a corner room, not to mention outside jackhammering at night. We were on the 11th fl. so it was not TOO bad. It did get on my nerves after 4 days.) But MY bathroom was so small, it was the size of a closet- and a small one at that. I had to put my makeup on, by placing all of my stuff in the SINK, just to get to it without dropping everything all over the floor. And to blow dry your hair???? Forget it. Nothing else need be said. 
 It is true I am a pretty picky person about rooms, because I travel alot and stay only in 4 star - or 5 star--hotels. Furnishings were very nice, but I noticed a few small places of mold in the shower. Not great.
I called housekeeping for turndown service and they never came that night, and at least one other night. We are members of the Omni Select program, and were supposed to get a daily newspaper. Had to ask for it TWICE. The concierge people knew absolutely NOTHING about directions to anything. Got us so lost that we finally gave up even asking. We did not eat a lot at the hotel, but the salad we ordered was surprisingly good... one of the best during our Boston stay. Nobody was friendly at all-- but that might just be Boston. It was my first time there.
This was actually a 3 and 1/2 star hotel, based on the poor service, unfriendliness, etc.
Jeff, the manager, however was great---helped us out a lot with the room problem.

title: “Lots of space in a good location”
text: For anyone used to European hotels, the first thing to strike you is how huge the room is. We had a 2 queen bedroom , which was amazingly spacious. The kitchenette was well equipped and had a bigger fridge/freezer than ours at home. It was useful to have kitchen facilities, particularly when travelling with a young child. The décor could, perhaps do with an update, but the beds with genuinely comfortable and the staff friendly. The location on E 50th was very convenient: the subway was very close, and there was a supermarket, efficient laundrette and plenty of great restaurants in the immediate neighbourhood. The hotel put us in touch with the Babysitters Guild of New York, who provided a babysitter for $25 per hour. We felt very comfortable leaving our son with her. I would be very happy to recommend the Affinia 50 or to stay here again.

title: “Sheraton Phoenix Downtown Rocks”
text: What a pleasant surprise! There is a lot to like about this hotel, but the best part is the service by all members of the hotel team. Check-in (Jenny) was very accommodating despite a little glitch on a second room reservation (perhaps on my part), the well appointed room on the concierge level overlooked the new strikingly beautiful Phoenix Convention Center, our lunch of heirloom tomato soup and salmon wraps was excellent, front drive management was friendly and eager to assist, housekeeping was quiet and effective, and Tom at check-out recommended a Trip Advisor critique. The only downside about this trip was we didn't have any time to enjoy the family friendly pool facilities and spa. GM Leo Percopa has assembled a quality team who are there to please.

title: “Nice place to stay”
text:
Whether on business or pleasure, the Embassy Suites is a nice place to stay - good location, pleasant rooms.
It can get noisy - hey, it is a family hotel, but the front desk staff is very nice. Ask to get upgraded to the penthouse loft suites - very pretty, and TWO bathrooms!

title: “on the beachbeach”
text: what a location right on the beach with a pool.rooms areany time ok . would stay ther again .

title: “FANTASTIC”
text:
My sister, daughter and myself have just returned from a short stay at the Hilton. We were very lucky and had an upgrade of room - thanks to Kellie Ann Cahill - which was fantastic !! The staff at the hotel were very very helpful - especially Caroline at the concierge desk. We also received lovely chocolate covered strawberrys - they were delicious. I would highly recommend this hotel and the staff - a perfect hotel/staff combination
The location of this hotel is an ideal location

title: “Great deal!”
text: This hotel was fantastic. The entire hotel was super clean and decorated really nicely for the holidays. The whole lobby smelled of cinnamon! The room was nice, modern and very comfortable. The staff was excellent and it is in a great location. Room service food was yummy with fantastic home fries. You can't get a better deal for the price.

title: “Location, Location, Location”
text: My 9 year old and i stayed here for 6 days at the end of August. It was clean, very pretty, safe neighborhood, great location (2 blocks from white house and mcpherson metro station), great breakfast buffet, nice staff. We paid $99 per night through priceline but probably would have done better through AAA ($170 including parking and breakfast) since parking was $35 per night and breakfast buffet ran about $40 for the both of us. We could walk to almost anything. I would recommend this hotel except for the following disappointments: room was very small and there was no refrigerator. There was a charge for internet service in the hotel's business center and there was a charge for fitness facility.

title: “my retiral trip to Boston.”
text: this was 5 star all the way, beautiful hotel service was great and despite a hurricane the entire holiday was superb.

title: “Affordable but noisy”
text: Noises from the rooms next door were troublesome. The breakfast room was very small and crowded. Staff were slow to replenish items.

title: “Excellent location”
text: Super value for money, great location, room were fine but dated, cleaned everyday, friendly staff, definitely stay there again.

title: “Excellent Stay”
text:
This was our first stay at this hotel and it will definitely be our preferred hotel for future overnight stays in Jacksonville. From the moment we arrived, we received excellent service. The room was nice, spacious and smelled great! The bed was comfortable. The towels were large and plush.
We had dinner and breakfast the following morning in the hotel restaurant. It, too, was excellent with great service. 
The hotel is located right across the street from the Moran Theatre. Attending an evening symphony concert was the reason for our stay and it couldn't have been more convenient.
The property is not new and there were just a few items that should have been updated. The tub in our room was in serious need of a make-over, and the make-up mirror needed to be replaced. Outside of that, everything was in very good condition. 
The Omni rewards program, which we joined when making this reservation, has some very nice perks. We enjoyed several during our stay. 
Great job, Omni, Jacksonville!

title: “I had a very good stay”
text: This place was super clean. Also, it was close to down town and most tourist attractions. Most importantly, this place had very good price for travelers who are try to save money on motel.

title: “Great Hotel and Great Staff”
text:
This hotel is the best in New York City. Best accomonindation, best staff and best food.
Mrs. Annmara Gayle, one of the excellent Guest Relations Offices, is one of the best in the business. She always helps, is pleasant and makes you feel like family. She helps make this hotel a home away from home.

title: “Starwood's attempt at being "hip"”
text:
I have never stayed at an Aloft before but was familiar with their attempt to serve a younger clientele. I am in my early 30s and travel semi-regularly for work so I know my way around a chain hotel. The decor is modern and looks like it was inspired by Ikea. It is a nice break from floral patterns and tired wall art. The room is kind of weird. It has a glass wall of the shower facing the outside of the room. It is totally frosted and private but still weird. Also, the glass shower stall doesn't seal and has no gaskets around the edge, leaving puddles of water in the adjacent water closet (aka small room where the toilet is). Said water closet is accessed by a sliding pocket door that is a bit teetering and unstable. You can easily rip it off its hinges if you aren't gentle. Also, said sliding door never fully closes 100%, making it awkward if you are bunking with someone you aren't very close with. The shower has Bliss products, which are in environmentally friendly pumps in the shower. I rely on hotel shampoos for ease of flying with liquids. I was greatly annoyed as a long haired female to discover an all in one combo shampoo/conditioner. Anyone with hair longer than 5 inches knows that stuff doesn't work well and I was left wrangling lots of tangles until I could hightail it down to the nearest drugstore to buy proper shampoo/conditioner.
Now to the lobby- some slacker parents were letting their obnoxious kids run around the lobby, as they were apparently elated by the single pool table available. Not that bad parenting reflects poorly upon the hotel, but it certainly kills the vibe that Aloft is trying to create in their lobby/bar. By the way, the bar, as with all hotels, is overpriced ($18 for one shot of a $40 bottle of tequila? Really, Aloft?). The bar has a door leading to a courtyard with seats, though it was way too hot for that the day I visited. The other side of the courtyard is the indoor pool. Unfortunately I witnessed a couple getting their, um, romance on, in that area so I declined to use it after that. The pool area is completely on display to the courtyard if you have problems with being on display. The fitness center was nice and clean with modern equipment and even had little ear buds available if you forgot yours.
Their cafe area is also overpriced ($2.50 for Powerade, $8 for a frozen Amy's meal, $8 for a pint of Ben & Jerry's, etc.) but a fridge is provided in each room so do yourself a favor and hit the grocery store instead.
All in all, a decent hotel with costly extras. It is right across from the airport and I heard zero noise, which is always nice!

title: “Great for business - very attentive staff”
text:
This hotel is not in the downtown area and doesn't have much of a bar scene but the staff are really nice. I got in late and needed food and the van driver volunteered to drive me to get sushi. He also picked me up there when i was done eating free of charge. Not having a rental car in houston made life difficult but the staff at this hotel really helped me get around that.
They also drove me to my business meeting the next day which was a 5 min drive from the hotel but a VERY far walk. Overall this is a great hotel for business travelers who need to be in the area. If you are visiting for pleasure, it is still a good hotel but perhaps you would want to be closer to the downtown area where there is more going on.

title: “Great hotel, bad location”
text: This was a great hotel. I stayed here as part of a Contiki vacation group over the 2011-12 new year holiday. Check-in was simple since I arrived before the group I had to check in alone, but it was very simple. They have a nice lobby, very historic style, and the elevators were quick to my floor and from the lobby. The room was nice, nothing too fancy but wasn't run down at all. the lighting in the hallways was a little dim but i think it added to the historic value of the hotel. They have free wifi internet in the rooms so that was a plus. the hotel is just across the street from a BART station so it is very convienent to the airport and in the middle of the street in front of the hotel is a muni stop for market street. so getting around is very easy. the only downfall was the location. i walked across the street to get some food on the first night only to find out the area was very shady. there were a lot of bums around the hotel. if you must venture out at night, i would get a cab or go as a part of a group, i wouldn't go alone.

title: “Wonderful Hotel ! Hope to come back soon.”
text: The Hotel is really nice. The people that work there were very friendly and helpful. Excellent ubication. We loved it.

title: “Pay a little more, this place sucks”
text: First of all, we got on at 1:30 am and have to leave at 6 am. When we got in the room there were only 3 towels. We had four in our party. I went back to ask for an extra towel, the person said " sorry no towels". I asked if they could give a liitle continental breakfast at 5:30am. He said " no" it's from 6-9am. Then when I went back there to use the lobby computer at 5 am. He wouldn't let me in. He came out the back room, hair messy, eyes red, like he was sleeping in the back. I asked what time the manager comes in. He said" I'm the manager". That was the end of it. Will never stay here again. For those of you looking just for a cheap stay, this is not one of them.

title: “Comfortable and Sofisticated”
text:
Superb Hotel!! As a business traveler the hotel is in a great loaction convenient to Madison Sq Garden, Macys and Times Sq, The redesign and transformation into an inviting grand entry and check-in was a relaxed and comfortable experience.The staff was very friendly, efficient and made sure that I knew about the internet access and gym and available transportation. The new rooms are spacious, well appointed and very soothing with a large desk, outlets for my electonics, big bathrooms (great showers,with room for toiletries/however: I couldnt find the shower matt and had to use a towel to step onto) and a nice size closet to put away clothes without having them all around the room folded in little corners like so many NYC hotels. Unlike so many New Hotels in NYC the TRYP seems to know how to make a guest feel comfortable right out of the gate. 
I thoroughly enjoyed my stay, and felt refreshed and relaxed in the morning when I went off to start my day.

title: “Bring Long Johns”
text:
After arriving to an unheated room I was told by the front desk that for energy conservation purposes rooms were not heated until the guests turned the heater on. With a snow storm outside, the room was actually pretty cold. After some "negotiations" the maintenance did check the heater, which was in order, and the room was also warm in the morning when I left.
One should value new experiences, I guess, and sleeping with the overcoat on was new to me.

title: “Classy but friendly”
text: A girlfriend and I book a room through the Northwest Flower and Garden Show, and we weren't sure about the fact that our room would have two twin beds, which seemed to be the only room offered with two beds. I'm happy to say that the room was still spacious and comfortable, with nice furnishings, and the beds were comfortable with plush linens. Hotel staff were friendly and professional, and we were guided by them to local sights, shopping and restaurants. This is a first class hotel built in the 1920s, but seemed up to date in terms of furnishings. The hotel is located very central to Seattle's major attractions, with Pike Place Market and the Convention Center, as well as all the major shopping within walking distance. We walked everywhere, but were delighted to have free valet parking because of our hybrid vehicle. I requested a quiet room location, so we were facing the courtyard and it was very quiet given its downtown location.

title: “Great location for the money we paid”
text:
My husband and I just got back from a weeklong trip to Chicago.I was adamant to stay in the downtown or Mag Mile areas despite the high room rates because I wanted us to be in the middle of everything. But we were on a budget.
The pros: 
Rates about half of those for hotels just across the street. 
Clean rooms and quiet, considering the location of downtown. 
We had the choice of several king size rooms on different floors - getting a 5th floor room was ideal as it kept noise to a minimum.
Location - just a short walk to Water Tower and Hancock. Michigan one block over.
A great breakfast place just down the street - the West Egg Cafe.
Free coffee, hot water for tea and hot chocolate available at all times
A 24 hour Dunkin Donuts/Baskin Robbins is across the street
Patient staff who answers questions of first time visitors instead of brushing them off
We will definitely recommend them for anyone on a budget who wants to stay in downtown/Mag Mile Chicago.

title: “Excellent”
text: Great building with excellent old style service and excellent location. The Daily Grill had excellent food and friendly attentive service. The desk staff and bell staff were friendly, helpful and very responsive. The price is extremely reasonable and quite a value.

title: “top spot in New York”
text: the novotel in NY is in a great location and the staff are very good and helpful.The only problem we had was not knowing that the normal 50% off dinning does not apply and the breakfast service was slow and almost took the amount of time to have breakfast before coffee or tea was offered. Eggs did not appear until we were leaving. But overall this is a great place to stay just avoid breakfast and being Times square there are better offers anyway. Will stay again.

title: “Wow, what a beautiful place.”
text: Me and the missus stayed here for two nights in December 2008. Very nice property. Big, clean, comfortable room. Very nice on site restaurants (also quite pricey). Do not play golf and we did not use the swimming pools, but everything we saw looked first rate. I might choose something closer to downtown on my next stay in Austin, but this resort had nothing wrong with it.

title: “Awesome stay, wonderful service”
text: I booked a night for my wife's 40th Birthday as well as our 20 year wedding anniversary. She spent the day at Zaspa which she said was wonderful and upon check in the desk told me they had upgraded us from a suite to the SOHO Loft room because of the occasion! This was a wonderful surprise that I truly appreciate as I was hoping to make the evening extra special. We can't thank the hotel enough for the kind gesture not to mention the bottle of champagne. It truly made our special occasion very memorable. We decided to do this every year for our anniversary from now on, along with a few summer getaways in between. Special Thanks to Hotel Zaza for a wonderful weekend, we'll be back soon!

title: “Noise, etc!”
text:
The hotel is next to I5 highway and the traffic noise was terrible...non stop all night. I used ear plugs and still had trouble sleeping. My spouse had no ear plugs and could hardly sleep at all. The door to the room did not fit the door sill properly and there were openings around the door, allowing more noise to enter the room. The bathroom had been upgraded and was fine, but the room , furniture ,tv, were dated and run down looking.For our purpose of staying one night before we flew out, it was barely tolerable,although the room rate was reasonable.
There are no restaurants any where nearby, although we finally found a pub, after driving around for awhile, and had a great pizza.
On our return one week later to pick up our car, as it was a stay and park arrangement, we discovered that the location they use for long term parking is directly under a row of trees, which deposited their needles and leaves all over our car. It took us 30 minutes to clean the car so we could drive home. We had to go to a nearby gas station to hose it off before we could proceed. We were not happy about this.
All in all, not a pleasant stay at his hotel, and we will not return. Robert Wood
 O

title: “Excellent Suites Hotel in Hillcrest”
text:
My wife , 17 year old daughter, and I had an extremely pleasent seven night stay in one of the hotels one bedroom suites.
After checking the usual hotel booking sites we actually got the best deal on the hotels own website.
The room/suite was surprisingly large, (we have actually rented smaller apartments), and extremely well apointed.
The separate bedroom contained the onsuite bathroom, a large walk-in cupboard/closet, kingsize bed and large LCD TV, with a window overlooking the balcony.
The lounge area again was very well appointed, containing the sofa/bed, (acceptably comfortable) according to daughter, and very easy to set up/ put away.
The kitchen area had everything you would need from large fridge to full size electric cooker.
Worthy of a mention are the domestic staff, who were always pleasent and willing to help.
This hotel will be the first one we check on our next trip to San Diego.

title: “AN EXPERIENCE TO REMEMBER”
text:
The entry to the hotel was stunning, and so were the staff, polite, friendly and welcoming.
Each part of the hotel from dinning, to relaxing, to the rooms, is an experience once has to feel, to have fond memories of.
The food, and wines, were excellent, and an experience.
Above all the stunning interiors, and the open air dinning.

title: “The Plaza in Philadelphia”
text:
Looking for a stately old hotel that has been totally updated? The Bellevue is your place.
The service was impectable, the rooms beautiful with all modern conviences and views of the city and the food at each venue was amazing. We were attending a wedding and the Ballroom was just spectacular as was the top floor room where the brunch was the next day. If your not going for an event The Palm Resturant is in the lobby of the hotel and The Philadelphia Museum is a short drive from this centrally located hotel. Check it out you won't be sorry.

title: “Comfy, cozy gem in a surprisingly quiet hotel in downtown Dallas!”
text: I LoVE this hotel and my group stays here each summer for a business conference. The free breakfast is wonderful...eggs, meats, potatoes, pastries, cereal, fruit...all delicious. This hotel blocks out the bustle of downtown activity, but is an easy walk to the convention center. Rooms are great, and I especially love the suites with full kitchens. A gem!

title: “Lovely hotel in Dupont Circle neighborhood in DC”
text: We are often in Washington DC, but this was our first stay at Hotel Madera near Dupont Circle. We will definitely stay there on our next visit. The hotel is a small boutique hotel in a fantastic area. Our reception in the small lobby was very warm and welcoming and Fernando, the bellman, was very cheerful and helpful. Our room, a king with a balcony, was spacious, nicely decorated and clean. The toilet and shower room are quite small but the sink area is separate, so the arrangement worked well. The balcony overlooked the entrance street, New Hampshire Ave, and it was really nice to watch the world go by. We were on the third floor and with the patio doors closed we heard little street noise. It would have been nice to have had a table and a couple of chairs on the balcony where we could have had morning coffee or an afternoon drink. There was a problem with the condition of the sheer drapes and I noted it in the review that the hotel sent to my e-mail after our departure. The very next day I received an e-mail from the General Manager apologizing and saying that the drapes had been replaced. During our stay we asked for extra towels and they arrived promptly. The Dupont Circle area is a neighborhood where people actually live, walk their dogs, go out to eat, shop and walk to work . We felt safe at all hours when on the street. The Metro is 3 blocks from Hotel Madera and there are many restaurants nearby, as well as bookstores, drug stores, food shops etc. On the morning of our departure we had breakfast in the Firefly, the restaurant that is connected to the hotel. The food was very good and service was very attentive and pleasant. Every evening the restaurant was busy. Even though our business is rarely in the Dupont Circle area we feel that because of availability of taxis and proximity to the Metro, Hotel Madera is where we prefer to spend our evenings and nights.

title: “Perfect Mother & Son weekend”
text:
Having been to NYC a handful of times and stayed at more botique hotels, this hotel was great for being a large chain. I booked a weekend trip with my Mother to New York and elected to stay at the InterContinental Barclay. I didn't see a need to get two rooms but we did need 2 beds and this can be a premium in Manhattan. The hotel was great from the second we entered and loved the location. We had multiple places to go, and being close to Grand Central Terminal made it very easy to get where we wanted to (I'm not a huge fan of public transit but it beats traffic and the horrible NYC cab drives). It was a short walk to Times Square, or a quick cab ($7) for when we didn't want to walk. 
Most restaurants we wanted to try were about 20 Blocks south, but overall this hotel is very centrally located if you're looking to spend time a little time everywhere in the City, this is the spot. It was raining lightly on Sunday, and they provided us with umbrellas (no charge, if returned) The Room was nice with a good/great bed and great linens. Bathroom was a little small but you don't go to NYC to be in your bedroom. Also, we were on the top floor and there was not a problem with road noise.

title: “TERRIBLE HOTEL, TERRIBLE SERVICE”
text: I cannot express to you how much I DO NOT like this hotel. I DON'T suggest staying here! The manager, Monica, was EXTREMELY rude and very disrespectful to me. She made multiple mistakes on our reservation. When I called to cancel our reservations, she gave me a cancellation number and I was told me my credit card would be reimbursed, so I thought everything was fine. It wasn't until a few weeks later that I learned she had only canceled one of the four rooms and charged the other three to my credit card. When I called to tell them there was a mistake, she told me that it was my fault and that the hotel was still going to charge my card (three rooms for two nights). The entire experience was terrible and the manager was extremely unprofessional.

title: “Great staff”
text: Hotel is older so rooms are a bit small, but liked the historic feel. Staff was wonderful and went above and beyond. Our original room had a bit of an odor and we were promptly moved and upgraded, plus given complimentary breakfast. A friend moved into our original room so we could tell it had been thoroughly cleaned to address the odor. Staff was responsive and great. Location was wonderful for walking to Riverwalk, Alamo, shopping, etc. Would definitely stay here again and room rate was extremely affordable.

title: “Beautiful hotel”
text:
The Omni is in a beautiful building the the financial district. The hotel completely eschews trendiness in favor of traditional decor and design, fitting the building in which it resides. The service is very professional yet friendly. The rooms are nicely appointed and very comfortable. The hotel is frequented by both business-trip types and well-heeled vacationers. 
If you want to stay in the heart of SF, want a quiet night's sleep, and want to avoid tourist kitsch in favor of traditional charm, stay at the Omni.

title: “wouldn't recommend”
text: Free parking, wifi, helpful people are the positives. The room was small and run down. Very expensive for what we got. There are plenty of other options and we stayed somewhere else the other nights we were in the city.

title: “Great hotel, even better service!”
text:
I really love this hotel. It was my second time to stay here for a business function and this time I stayed for 5 nights. I love the rooms and the decor, but the main reason I am writing this review is to brag on the impeccable service. 
The staff bent over backwards to make sure my colleagues and I had a wonderful stay. They charged my cell phone for me and brought it back to me the next morning...exactly at the time the night manager said they would. They brought a gift I left in my car to the reception I was attending. They also brought me toothpaste and then followed up to make sure housekeeping brought it to me! 
It was an excellent stay and I would highly recommend this hotel for business or pleasure.

title: “Just say NO!”
text: *takes a deep breath* Where.....do I......begin?? When I first checked in, I asked to see the room before it was assigned to me. I head to the room, located on the 2nd floor. Opened the door and almost fainted from the stench. Whatever it was, it was awful and I knew I would never want to smell that smell again. I head back and request for another room. I was told there weren't any available til Wed (it was Monday), and that most likely the smell was from smoke. However, I know what smoke smells like and that wasn't it. But it already was supposed to be a non-smoking room??? He tells me that all of their non-smoking rooms are on the 1st flr (for an extra fee). How convenient! So I change to the 1st flr one, which is better b/c there are no elevators at this facility. So was I satisfied??? Of course not....roach infested city!!! I spent the majority of my night killing roaches. On the bed, on the walls, paintings, in the tv (yes, they were crawling from out of the tv), fridge, behind bathroom mirrors, shower wall. It was ridiculous. I took pictures and complained. They sprayed and then MORE CAME. By that time, I was crying and the manager switched my reservations to a location on Horizon Lake Dr (5 stars). Overall I guess the staff was helpful. I mean, how could you be rude to me at this point. If the room was habitable, I'm sure I would be able to tell if the staff is generally nice. The location is convenient but the area doesn't scream creme de la creme either. Signs posted all around, "Park at your own risk", literally. Even when it was sunny out, the room was still gloomy with shades open. Its definitely not a vacation spot. More so for ppl (probably the ones who keep saying this is an excellent spot) who really need to crash till whenever. And I get that, but if I knew I would be sharing my room with "pets", I would've booked accordingly. Beware!

title: “Enjoyed our Labor Day weekend stay at the SD Hilton Gaslamp Hotel”
text:
Just returned from a great Labor Day weekend stay at the San Diego Hilton Gaslamp Hotel. Because I’m a gold Hilton Honors member, I was upgraded to a top floor room on the 12th floor. Check in was a breeze and the staff was professional. Parking was valet only and at $35, kind of expensive, but that is comparable for the area. The valet however was convenient and efficient. The room was spacious and clean. It was nicely decorated. The beds were nice and the large LCD TV was a plus.
From my side of the building, I had a great view of the HardRock Hotel pool and lounge area. The music was kind of loud, but it was turned off at night. I did not hear any trolley or train noises from my room. I however heard the aftermath of the partying from everyone walking from the elevators to their rooms. Ironically, I did not hear any noises from the rooms next door, however the noise from the hallway was loud and clear. (they should put some insulation tape underneath the doors to muffle the noise) 
The gym was functional and it worked out great for my wife. There are headsets at the treadmill for watching TV. The heated pool area was kind of small, but it was good for the kids. The Jacuzzi only seats 4, however the temperature was just right. It was great to come back after a day of sightseeing and going to the pool. 
For the gold Hilton Honor members, there are no executive floor lounges, however they do provide you with breakfast coupons to be used in the in-house restaurant. The service staff was great. They were friendly and efficient. It is a standard breakfast buffet with an omelet station. The food quality was good and fresh. I’m a starbucks drinker and the coffee wasn’t bad. It was freshly brewed. The fresh squeezed orange juice was also very good. I think the normal price for the breakfast buffet is $12.95. 
Overall, I’m very happy with my stay at the Hilton. The location was perfect. It is within walking distance to most of downtown. The staff was courteous and professional. We will definite come back to this hotel in San Diego.

title: “Good business hotel”
text:
I was at the Marriott for a meeting of my professional society. Overall, I liked it. The room was clean and well-equipped but a bit small. There are plenty of grocery stores and restaurants within easy walkting distance so you're not stuck with paying hotel food and restaurant prices.
Business services were decent with one “miss”. I was moderating 2 panels, so I really appreciated the fact that they had A/V people walking in before sessions and asking if everything was OK- technical issues with the equipment could be resolved quickly and easily. They also had a single in-house number to call for support if you needed them at other times. The “miss”- one of my panelists was stuck in traffic and called the hotel trying to reach me. They told him I wasn’t registered there. I’d been there for 4 days at that point. We also found the elevators very slow when sessions finished up; sometimes we waited forever and then 3 showed up on the same floor at once.
The high-speed Internet was consistently reliable, which I can’t always say for many hotels I’ve used. You have to sign on daily unless you get the “wired for business” package ($9.95/day) when you check in. Oddly, every time I signed in it gave me a choice of a $14.95 rate or a $9.95 rate and I always chose the $9.95 one even though I hadn’t bought “wired for business” and $9.95 is what I was charged. Note there’s a 15% “Internet tax” on top of that. Nasty.
The hotel offers shuttle services to and from Midway and O’Hare every 15 minutes. It’s cheaper than a cab- for the 2 of us it was $38 one way. An alternative is the subway/train system (Grand is the nearest stop) from the airport for $2 but it involves a change of train, which is even worse if you have bags. Two warnings about the shuttle bus: first, we were waiting in the lobby and one came and went without anyone announcing it. So keep an eye out the door. Fortunately, we weren’t in a hurry and got the next one. It’s also “first-come, first-serve” and they don’t take reservations. Ours stopped at a second hotel and couldn’t pick up all the people who were waiting for it due to lack of space. We were skeptical about the one-hour estimate for transit time to the airport when we got into a traffic jam (this was a noon departure from the hotel) but it was almost exactly an hour door to door. You can get tickets for the shuttle at the Concierge desk and they can add it to your room charges.
The pool was decent- a nice length but narrow enough that when there were 3 of us swimming laps we had to duck out of each others’ ways as we passed. The Fitness Center had enough equipment that I noted treadmills available at 7 AM.
Overall, I liked this hotel and would return if the price is right.

title: “Don't be put off by the neighbors!”
text:
After doing a little research looking for a 2 bedroom for 4 adults, I choose the Moore Hotel. I was given a rate of $135 a night (plus $10 for the extra 2) for a total of $150 a night. 
What we recived for our $150 a night was the biggest 3 bedroom you've ever seen! The 1st room had a full size bed, the 2nd room had 2 twin size beds, and the 3rd room had a queen. Each of the 3 rooms had a sink, and we did have to share a bathroom. Yes, we had no air conditioning, but we got 2 fans from the front desk, and left our windows (that open completly) cracked to get a nice cool breeze.
I was worried at first when we arrived, as the lobby was very old and had not been updated in a long time, and there were a few "characters" hanging out right outside the entrance. However, the desk staff was very friendly and helpful, and assured us not to worry about the people outside. 
We took the (tiny) elevator to our room, where we were very impressed with the cleaning job and the size of the room. Being on the 4th floor, we wern't blessed with the greatest view in the world, but that was just fine. 
Yes the parking situation -----, but there are plenty of lots across the street, and if you park at night on the street, it is free, and very safe. 
Check out the Night Lite lounge next door for the best cheap strong drinks in the city. A funky little dive, where we were made to feel right at home.

title: “Not my cup of tea”
text: Centerfolds is a strip bar in the red light district. Boston abounds with many venues around and near this hotel. Fenuil Hall, Quincy Market, the Freedom Trail, Parks, and other venus worth seeing and doing. I disagree with your assesment of this hotel. If it took 1 hour for you luggage to arrive, did you take the time and call anyone after 15 minutes had elapsed. I have stayed at many Hyatt hotels, I find this assesment to be completly out of focus. Having stayed overinght many times at this location, I have never been woken up by food service carts rolling by, nor the 'thin walls" as the author stated. Perhaps a pair of earplugs would be helpful. On the contrary, I have found the rooms to be clean, beds were comfortable, and the only noise that I head was fire trucks going by one time. As for the location, sure its downtown, but it is central to most places to go. I and my wife have attended concerts in the park until 11PM and have never had a problem walking back, or for that matter, walking to chinatown late at nite for a bite to eat. For the $12 USD you have to pay tor a movie, nextime watch HBO for free or go to the Lowe's Cinima around the corner and pay more.

title: “Great experience.”
text: What a great Experience. The front dest was very helpful and nice, shuttle was great and on time, room was very nice, and the service on my return trip to the hotel to pick up my car was excellent. They had my car parked right at the valet, hatch open to put my bags in and I was ready to go the second I stepped off the shuttle. I will definately stay there again if I need to take another flight out of Seattle.

title: “Nice but not great”
text:
Booked a club level room for three nights for the price of two through a deal on the Starwoods website. 
I checked in on the weekend so obviously the lobby was very busy but service was fast & efficient, checking out during the week had no waits. The lobby has free wireless internet available & comfortable sofas/chairs.
Had a room on the 33rd floor which included complimentary high speed internet; club lounge has complimentary continental breakfast of lots of varied fresh fruit, cereals, coffee & pastries; hors d'oeuvres of veggies, cheeses, small desserts & drinks in the evening. 
The only disappointing things were that there was bird defecation on the window & the ice bucket still had a bag of water in it. I didn't use/touch it & neither did housekeeping for 2 days. The bed of course was the best part with a great mattress & sound sleep. Otherwise it was fairly standard: hairdryer, coffeemaker with Starbucks coffee & tea, iron & ironing board, large safe that you could fit a laptop inside of, good shower.
Health club/pool/hot tub: I never went in the pool or hot tub because it was always busy morning/evening & as well, lots of children/families. I did use the health club every day which consists of 4 treadmills with views of Seattle, one crosstrainer, a few bikes. My only complaint was that the room was too warm with the sun shining in & just being in a small area with a lot of people working out.
You can't beat the location: a block or two away from the main shopping street (Nordstroms, Barnes & Noble, Sephora, etc), coffee places, restaurants. Also a 5 block or so quick, easy walk to Pike Market & the new Seattle Art Museum on First Ave.

title: “Marriott Essex House on Central Park South”
text:
Stayed at Essex House early October and found the luxury hotel typical of Marriott higher end properties. Great linens, pleasant and accommodating personnel but still in the midst of their transition. Being Platinum, I was looking forward to being on the Concierge level with comparable service. As of October, 2012, they had no Concierge level. As a result, they credited some points to our account which were insignificant but it was their way of placating loyal guests. 
The normal price point of the Essex House is right up there with higher end New York city hotels and essentially more for business and international travelers. The area of the hotel where we were had no wireless connection in the suite. Not good! I found out if I went out into the hallway where there was a bench next to the elevator, I was able to get reception. Still not sure what the problem was after several days of trouble shooting. But it made it difficult to communicate. 
I would recommend this hotel for business travelers or luxury travelers who don't mind paying for location, location and fairly good staff. I did not eat there thus I cannot remark on restaurants. There are too many good restaurants in New York City to sit in a hotel and eat. Bottom line, I loved the location. Good hotels in New York are pricey and you must realize that from the start. I am a loyal Marriott Rewards customer thus I try to stay at their properties to garner more points and bennies. But I am finding more and more that Platinum really doesn't mean that much any more. It all depends on the property. It seems they can make up their own rules.

title: “Fabulous”
text:
I stayed here for 4 nights with my fiance + we thoroughly enjoyed our stay here. The staff were very friendly + professional, the room was spotlessly clean + it was nice + big! The bed was one of the comfiest beds I've ever slept in!
The room is very well double glazed - it's hard to believe that Times Square is just outside the window when it's so quiet inside! We didn't have any meals at the hotel but the rom service menu looked appetizing + it wasn't too expensive. We had no problems with the lifts - we didn't have to wait too long - to be honest though, I wouldn't let a lift ruin my holiday!!!
I would have no hesitation at all in staying here again + I would highly recommend it. Enjoy!

title: “What you would expect from a Hyatt Regency, but could have been better”
text:
I got a great deal on Priceline and stayed at the Hyatt Regency over the weekend. The front office staff were helpful and friendly. Upon my departure at 5am the valet attendant on duty was notably courteous as well and helpful and provided excellent customer service even though we didn't part at the valet. He offered to help with bags, gave directions to the airport, and genuinely considerate. If I were scoring the stay based only on him I would have given a 10 star. 
The room could hae been cleaner. There were hairs in the tub and spots on the carpet. For a Hyatt Regency this was below standard. 
Free internet at the bar was a plus!

title: “This hotel is Clean! Dated a bit, and much more like a Motel.”
text: My sister and I stayed at this hotel for 5 nights the end of February because we had come to town for the Oprah after Oscar Party show...Having never been to Hollywood before and not knowing where to stay and not having a huge budget, we chose this hotel...When we arrived the front desk clerk was terrific and helpful. We were surprised that it is clearly more motel style than hotel style. We were a bit skeptical when we got inside the room...but if you can get past how dated this motel is, I will tell you we found it to be really very clean and well kept inside and out. The front desk staff was helpful during our entire, the Hollywood bus tour they suggested was fantastic we took that the second day in town and they picked us up right at the hotel and dropped us back off at the end of the day at the hotel..We ate at the hotel restaurant several times and each time the food was fine and good priced and the staff was just as fantastic. The location to all the sights is within walking distance which was great...It was a little sketchy walking late one night but other than that it is just fine...The parking is tough at night but as someone else said FREE parking in Hollywood is very few and far between...if I were to go back to Hollywood I would stay here again...

title: “It's in the details - loved the elevator system”
text: The Marquis is in the heart of the theater district. I traveled alone so it was a perfect spot for me. I went to several Broadway shows. I could walk back with the crowds and never felt anxious because I was single woman. The room was very comfortable. The staff were always polite - especially the "maid" service. They greeted me with a smile and hello no matter what time of day or night I came and went from my room. The detail I loved was the elevator system. There's a panel where you select your floor and then you are assigned an elevator. Wonderful. No pushing or shoving or jockeying for position. It seems small but i loved it. I hate trying to play the "which elevator is next game" and having rude people cut me off.

title: “Very nice room, great service and location”
text:
The good things: beautiful lobby, excellent service, very well equipped room (lovely linens, flat screen TV, refrigerator, robes, coffeemaker, easy to set alarm clock/MP3 player), central location.
The bad things: no wi-fi, tiny room.
Make sure you check the hotel's website for special rates (we got 3 nights for the price of 2) and DEFINITELY sign up for the Select Guest program (free drinks and newspaper delivered to your room in the morning, free internet, free bottled water).
Would definitely stay here again!

title: “great location”
text: we stayed here in October. the reception staff where friendly and let us into our rooms early with no extra charge. the room was clean and comfortable, the only downside was the view onto another building. the hotel is so well located, walking distance of grand central station and times square. it is also local for subway 6 that takes you to battery park for the satutue of liberty etc. we would recommend this hotel to all.

title: “Very Pleasant Stay”
text:
My wife and 2 children stayed here on our way back home from a road trip. I called from a few hours north to confirm our late arrival and the front desk staff was very prompt & helpful. The room was very clean and nicely appointed. Tub/shower was large.
We went for a late night swim and enjoyed the outdoor pool and indoor hot tub. 
We had breakfast at the hotel restaurant the morning we checked out and the staff was all attentive & pleasant. The food quality was good, selection was OK.
We are frequent Marriott guests, and were pleasantly surprised by this hotel. I can see why it is so highly ranked on TripAdvisor. I can't think of anything truly negative to report.

title: “Standard/Average Hotel in Center City Phili”
text: Good, moderate quality hotel in Philadelphia. Nothing special - but iit's a good three star hotel in the center of Philadelphia. The staff is very pleasant and helpful, The rooms are fairly standard.

title: “Great location, nice rooms”
text: This is a corporate hotel with conferences and meetings, but it's perfectly located in downtown SF. We've stayed here twice, and probably will come back again. We walked to several museums, it's right next to the cable car line, and surrounded by shopping malls and dozens of restaurants. Prices are reasonable for the area and there are often special rates online. Upper floors have spectacular views of the city or the bay, if you get lucky and snag a good view room. Rooms are clean and updated, the beds are fine, and the bathrooms are small but okay.

title: “Romantic, posh, funky, amazing!”
text:
Stayed in the W Victory for a Coldplay concert at American Airlines Center. We had a large corner room with a balcony that was amazing! The accomodations were top notch; modern with a big city flare. The balcony had a large round snuggle chair! Large tile shower and seperate jetted tub.
This was a pricey room but it was worth it for our weekend away. We loved it so much we stayed an extra night! They have an infinity pool on a high floor to overlook the city, a spa, a great workout space (huge!) and an amazing restaurant and bar. Will go there again for sure!

title: “Terrific Place to Stay”
text:
I am a former NY'er who goes home for visits frequently for at least a week at time. I hate hotels so I look for apartments or apartment-like accommodations. I got this through a travel deal on Orbitz and I could not have been happier. Much better than the place I have been staying in previously, which I will not name but which I will never go back to again now that I have found the Murray Hill!!
We had a one bedroom suite - huge, this place obviously used to be an apartment building and I sure wouldn't mind living in an apartment like this! I love the bathroom (it's bigger than the one in my home)and has nifty art deco lights. The bathroom was white and green and the green theme continued throughout the apartment. Dark green carpet and the bed linens were also in the green hue. 
If you are looking for shiny new modern, then this is not the place for you. BUT if you are looking for large, comfortable, CLEAN, convenient accommodations, you can't beat this place.
The kitchen has a dishwasher, some very basic pots and pans (not new but clean and they did the job). No toaster or microwave. The coffee pot is small and since we were there for a week and my husband drinks a lot of coffee we bought a larger coffee pot and 2 large mugs. No big deal to us. We had brought our own coffee and coffee pot filters.
We never had any reason to call the front desk for anything and checking in and out was a breeze. The doormen were all charming, the housekeeping staff pleasant.
Since I'm from NYC, I was very familiar with the neighborhood (having worked in the area for many years)tons of stores, a short walk to Grand Central,
All in all, I'm loving it!
We WILL be back!!!

title: “OK hotel. Location is its best asset”
text:
This hotel is in an excellent location, more or less across the road from Penn Station. On arrival, we were greeted by very friendly, helpful staff, especially the porter who lugged in our bags in the pouring rain.
We arrved at our room, which I had expected to be small, but turned out to be reasonably-sized. The bathroom, on the other hand is about as pokey as it could be, to the extent that if you sit on the toilet, your thigh is pressed against the toilet roll holder!
The hotel is being renovated at present, which makes wheelchair access a pain, depending on the time of day. 
One problem we encountered was with the concierge. We needed to get a wheelchair-accessible cab, which should be available from any yellow cab dispatch operator. I asked the concierge to call one for us, who responded that there was no longer an obligation on taxi companies to provide ramp cabs! She then offered no further assistance to us! (We went across to the taxi stand at Madison Square Garden and got a ramp cab within 15 minutes) I would really expect better from a concierge in Manhattan.
We had some food in Niles one night which was decidedly average, but it is a very pleasant place for a few cocktails and the bar staff (the guys behind the counter, not the table staff) are top notch. The doorman will hail a cab for you, but will try his utmost to get you into a Town Car waiting outside the door, usually at a higher fare. The Town Car drivers must tip better than the Yellow Cab drivers!

title: “Nice place for families”
text:
This is a family resort. Don’t assume that because it is a Hilton that it will be a classy crowd staying there. If kids having fun bother you then this may not be the place for you. My wife and I went here, just the two of us and we had a great time. The water park isn’t that large, but the lazy river and the main pool were nice. It was 115 degrees while we were there so the lazy river and the hotel pools were really warm, but the main pool at the River Ranch was cooled.
Like some other reviews said, the water park was seriously lacking when it came to daily upkeep. Cups and towels left all over weren’t picked up until the end of the day, some not even then. Rules weren’t enforced as far as, “No swimming in the lazy river. Stay in your tube”. If you wanted to float around in your tube, you were constantly being blocked or pushed out of the way by people not in tubes, but just playing around in the river. Nothing was ever said to anyone about it, and it was slightly annoying at first, but seeing how they didn’t enforce that rule, I didn’t feel bad breaking the rule about bringing in your own food and drinks. Food and drinks at the poolside restaurants and bar were way too pricey.
The rest of the hotel was fine, clean rooms and nice staff. The refrigerator froze everything and we couldn’t find an adjustment to lower the temp., and didn’t bother to ask anyone how to do it.
We never ate at any of the hotel restaurants. There are tons of places to eat close by. If you like sushi, try Moto Sushi about a mile up the road. During the week get there between 3 and 5 for happy hour. The only down side of Moto’s was loud angry music. There is a McDonald’s up the road for a cheap breakfast, and a grocery store to stock up on stuff for your stay.
The WIFI is $12 per day, but we were able to find a signal and hook up without having to pay for subscribing. It was a weak signal and was hit and miss, but we used it to find some restaurants that we wanted to try. If you absolutely need to have internet, you may want to pay, but try it first and see what kind of signal you get.
All in all, not a bad place to stay in Phoenix especially if you have kids. Maybe Hilton will work on maintaining the water park a little better. While we were there it looked like it was all kids working in there and they didn’t really care enough to work hard. After school starts an older group may come in and things may improve.

title: “Good Value, Excellent Location”
text: I was attending a conference being held at the Grand Hyatt. I was unable to get into the Grand Hyatt unless I paid $269/day. I went on line and found the Paramoount directly across the stree at $129/day. It is an older renovated hotel but it was clean and comfortable. There are a number of excellent resturants within walking distance. The staff was very friendly and helpful. If you need or want to stay in downtown Seattle, I recommend this hotel.

title: “Great place!!”
text: Me and boyfriend stayed here for 5 days, and we really loved it! Friendly staff, nice rooms and we loved the swimming pool. 'Till we meet again!

title: “Disappointed”
text: I sent my wife to this hotel for a Christmas present "getaway". I researched this hotel and thought I made a great choice, but I was wrong. AC did not work both nights, and it was in the 80's in Houston in Dec. So humidity in room was awful. Other than that room was ok. I was most disappointed that the only comp for the room was not having to pay the ridiculous valet parking fee. We were also told that a MGR would call us, and have yet to hear from anyone. In my line of business, I am sure to return, even the "tough" phone calls! We are not ones to complain but this was a big Christmas disappointment. I could of sent her to a much less expensive hotel and had better customer service. We will not be staying at any Magnolia Hotel again.

title: “An unexpected gem”
text: Located near the airport, it is a gem of beauty and serenity. Great service, great food and the facilities are terrific. Don't miss it if you need to stay near the airport.

title: “Hotel is pretty . Noise all night..couldn't sleep strong smell of industrial cleaner”
text: The hotel is close to the Pacer's stadium. The hotel is pretty ,decorated nicely, breakfast decent, usual free brkfast. fare. The hall and room had a terrible strong smell of cleaner. The room was noisy. Dumpster pickup started at 2am and went until early morning. Im not a light sleeper and could not sleep through this. I guess because there are several bars and lots of restaurants nearby they have lots of trash. Mentioned it to the girl at checkout and she said yeah we get that all the time. So we will not stay here ever again. If it was quiet then we would reconsider

title: “Modern Flair...”
text:
The hotel's location was excellent in respect to getting around to all the stops on our itinerary. The check-in process did leave something to be desired which is the only drawback for us. There was a 30 min. wait just to get onto their parking lot so the valet would take our car.
The room itself was modern, and had a decent size closet in the bedroom. I thought the bed was super comfy but for my boyfriend it was too soft. It would have been nice of them to also provide a lighter blanket, as the one that's on the bed is too warm for the summer. The bathroom amenities provided were all more than sufficient. Overall, I definitely recommend the hotel, but might try a B&B next time.

title: “Repeat stay - great location and people”
text: I stayed here a few years ago and liked the Chancellor. Came back in an updated room, room 1005, and it was a great stay. This room is an inside room, its window has limited view of Union square and a fire escape ladder crosses right outside the window. If good view is what you need, this room may not be it. But it is a quiet room. It only borders, I think, with one other room. It's a good size room, with a walk in closet. Bathroom is good size, with a bathtub. Great and very comfortable bed with hypoallergenic pillows and linens. No coffee machine in room, but great coffee at the lobby and cookies. If you don't mind going down for a coffee, it's an option I prefer - the quality of the coffee downstairs was great, unlike most in-room coffees. Here for a business trip and I would stay again. The main cable car line passes right outside and shopping is right there as well! Walking to the conference center takes maybe 10 minutes.

title: “Was as expected!”
text:
This location was what one would expect from a Homewood Suites.
Some observations: 1) The dinner food was better than expected - esp, the bbq night. 2) The king bed suites are much small than expected - I recommend getting a room with two queen beds. They are much more spacious. 3) The breakfast had alot of selections and was served at 6:30 am - however the food was just ordinary. 4) The blue collar employees seemed to work harder and cared more about guests than the white collar employees. I was somewhat suprised at the lack of general knowledge of the area and the operations of the hotel displayed by the folks working behind the check in counter. When I asked one employee a question about how the van service worked - she said that she couldn't work and think at the same time and I would have to wait until she finished what she was doing to be able to answer my queston. I also told her that the location I needed a van ride to was 4.8 miles away according to mapquest and she said they couldn't help me because the van didn't deliver anyone to a location over five miles away. Guess she was a product of the public school system ;-)
I would stay there again but I wouldn't expect much help from the staff. 5) The mattress in my room needed turned - there was a definite sag.

title: “Good, friendly service”
text: I quite liked this hotel as it is extremely convenient to the airport without the aircraft or traffic noise, and all the staff I encountered, whether at the reception desk, in the restaurant, room service and the like were friendly and courteous. The rooms are clean and I really liked the relaxation/jet lag CD they provided. My only complaint was that reception staff would often give preference at check-in to airline staff, whilst ignoring other guests who were also waiting to check in. Otherwise, I cannot fault this fine hotel.

title: “A real gem”
text: Wonderful hotel in a great part of Chicago - very quiet street and a short walk from some great bars and restaurants and it is only a 5/10 minute drive to downdown Chicago. The restuarants are also much better value in this neighbourhood than downtown. The staff were wonderul and always willing to help. The rooms of very high standard and extremely comfortable. They do a very simple buffet breakfast - nothing special but was included in the price. You can take your breakfast up to your room - which is quite helpful as the space and seating in reception is not really geared up for eating breakfast. They also have tea and coffee on tap 24/7. This is a great hotel and really is home from home. I will certainly stay here again.

title: “Nice views of the Baltimore Inner Harbor surrounded by excellent resteraunts.”
text:
This is a busy place on summer weekends. The Baltimore Inner a harbor is a fun place to walk around, eat and shop. This hotel is at one end of the whole affair, connected by a set of bridges. 
The service was good but our room wasn't ready on arrival at 4:00. They seemed to have big weddings going on. The brunch on Sunday morning was extensive and delicious, and the harbor view room was lovely. I suggest NOT using valet parking for $40 per night, unless that price doesn't bother you. I found them a bit slow for the cost. The lot is just around the corner.

title: “Beautiful Hotel! poor service!”
text:
The hotel and its location are fantastic !! Breakfast we ate once which was disgusting and expensive and left my wife feeling ill all day so did'nt eat there again. Found the staff very abrupt and was once asked for my room key to even borrow an umbrella when the three guys in suits in front of me were handed too without question remember don't always judge a book by its cover.
To "Summarize" the hotel is stunning except for the damp smelling bathroom but the staff and food let it down so wouldnt stay there again plenty of choice in New York!!

title: “Very nice experience!”
text: Very nice hotel and great location. Subway, tours, etc are near the hotel. Nice staff and clean rooms. I will come back to this hotel if ever in Boston again.

title: “Great service, great location”
text:
I have been to this hotel a number of times now. I have gone for both business trips and getaway weekends.
Each visit exceeded my expectations. The staff and facilities are fantastic.
The location can't be beat.
I guarantee if you go you will go back!!

title: “Not my favorite Hampton Inn”
text:
Stayed at this Hampton Inn a couple of days before Christmas. Great location, close to Times Square. Pretty much close to everything. Hotel and room were clean. Stayed on the like 27th floor and got the "City View" room. View from the room was amazing. Only problem was the room was so small that you literally couldn't get to the window to see the view because the bed was right up against the window. I expected the room to be small because of the location and I was fine with that but I had to open the window and stick my head out to actually be able to view the skyline and Empire State building. 
Typical Hampton Inn breakfast. They did a good job keeping the dining area clean. Wasn't overcrowded like I thought it would be which was nice. 
My issue with this Hampton Inn was the service when I went to check in. There were two people at the desk waiting on one gentleman. I waited at the desk not knowing what the situation with this other gentleman was. Had no problem with that. Stood around a bit longer. Was never even acknowledged as being there or told they would be right with me. The guy at the desk kept talking to the other girl even after the gentleman they were helping left. I was the only one there left to check in. They both started doing other things and still didn't acknowledge I was standing there, they just kept talking and laughing with each other. Finally after standing there a while the guy asked for my name and told the girl to print my paperwork up. Good thing I checked the price because I guess they were so distracted that they gave me someone elses paperwork to sign with a room costing over $100 more than I was supposed to pay. When I made him aware he didn't really seem to care, just kind of nonchalantly told her it wasn't my paperwork , to which she didn't really seem to care either. No apologies for the wait or mistake and not very welcoming. I would have fully understood if it was chaotic and busy but I was the only one there! I am pretty big on customer service and this was the only thing I really found wrong with this Hampton Inn. It is unfortunate, since this is really unlike Hampton Inn. All my experiences with them have been pretty great. I think as long as you don't get these two when you check in you should be fine.

title: “More Than We Ever Expected”
text: We went because we wanted to see the famous "Duck Walk" in the hotel lobby. The Ducks walk in and enter the hotel lobby pool from the elevator in the am and return in the pm. Great show, fun for all ages. The hotel was beautiful. The lobby is a must see. Great shops surround with all amenities. The exercise room, pool and spa is just wonderful. The hotel staff was superior in every way. Hope to do it again soon. Don't miss a stop at the Peabody.

title: “Avoid - Felt Like an old Motel Room- paint peeling"”
text: My wife and I travel extensively worldwide, and enjoy a variety of experiences...We checked into the Hyatt for a 4 night stay, and upon check in decided to upgrade to a view room with a deck - we recieved a room three floors from the top - so far so good!, when we entered the room, we were transported back to 1990 - the room felt, old, out of date, and much more like a Motel - (they comicallly had a coffee and tea setup without any plug nearby - I guess we were supposed to haul it around the room..). We were tired from travel so we did not say anything and figured we would just laugh and have fun in the city... but then we saw the bathroom - enamal paint peeling off the tub! mold and dust covering the air vent - this for a $350+ a night room? We ordered room service, and asked if we should call to have the tray picked up - no we were told, the halls are regularly monitered - needless to say, the tray was still outside our door the next day. We checked out the following morning, and not only was the receptionist not interested in the room problems, but she did not even make a note - obviously they were used to this (please know, that we did not ask for any money off our bill or any other form of compensation, we simply wanted to get the heck out of there). We found a nearby hotel which was perfect. Shame on Hyatt. We even completed an online survey documenting the problems upon our return home which Hyatt sent - never heard a word from them.

title: “Excellent hotel”
text:
This is a great hotel. Lovely spacious, modern rooms, with great bathrooms. All modern amenities, and bed was very comfortable. Best thing about the hotel was it's location to Fisherman's Wharf and lots of lovely local restaurants. 
The only downside I could see was the hotels location to Downtown San Fran, if this is important to you this could be a problem. It is a bit of a walk to the cable car and then a 15-20 min ride, or about a 40 minute walk up some very steep hills!.

title: “Nice hotel at a great price.”
text: This Econo Lodge has better than average rooms and an air conditioner that easily keeps up with sweltering Phoenix heat. The reception building is spacious and breakfast is very basic. These are basic but clean accomodations close to downtown but in a slightly seedy neighborhood. If you're looking for inexpensive and don't need any frills then this is your place.

title: “Perfect location. Great rooms. Courteous staff. Excellent Buffett breakfast”
text: I could not have been more pleased. Across from the pier. Trollys across the street to Fishermans wharf. A short walk to Chinatown. Excellent restaurants just outside the hotel doors. If you get a chance to stay here, jump at the chance. I really could not be happier. It will be my first choice in San Frncisco hotels

title: “Highly Recommended”
text: We stayed at The Bryant Park Hotel for our honeymoon and they were brilliant, providing an upgraded room for our five night stay and a bottle of complimentary bubbly. The location is perfect for sightseeing, within view of Times Square without the crowds. Want to come back one day!

title: “Expensive but good.”
text: We stayed with two couples in one room, during a city trip to New York in december 2011. Everything was perfect, except that it took some time before the room was set up for 4 people. For sight-seeing this hotel has a perfect location. Close to Time Square, but without the hassle of Times Square. Breakfast is expensive, and do not think to save money by not taking the full breakfast because then you pay for every item and easily end up paying more. But a few steps from the hotel there are cheaper alternatives. After a day of sightseeing it is great to relax around the fireplace in the lounge. The bathroom was very stylish and convenient. The view from the room was wonderful.

title: “Will never stay at this chain again”
text: Please beware of what you are told before you stay at this hotel. Every year I meet my family in this area for a three day weekend and the race. This year I came across this hotel on the internet. The pictures were amazing. The full kitchen really looked great. The price was a little high for a two bedroom suite. But I thought it might be a nice treat. I called to get more details. I was sure to have a long talk with the reservation clerk as I need to ensure we were getting one room with two double or queen beds as I have a 71 year old father and a handycapped sister. They require their own beds. I also travel with my husband and two young children so they could stay on the pull out if needed the other room really didn't matter. I was very excited after talking to the clerk that they had a two bedroom suite one room with two queen beds and another with a king as well as a full kitchen. We arrived three hours early and obviously the rooms were not available. When the room was ready we were very excited to see how it looked. What we found was a a two bedroom suite with two king beds and a kitchen that really should not be called a kitchen. It did have a small fridge and mini stove top but looked nothing like the picture. It actually looked other places we had stayed that called it a mini kitchen area. Basically a one bedroom suite with a door left open to another room. I called downstairs as there was no way father and daughter could sleep together and at this point we didn't have enough beds. I was told that I must have made the reservations wrong as it was coded two kings. I explained I had a detailed conversation with the clerk and was told that is not what we have here. So first I was insulted and made to look like I lied. I explained we cannot take this room we didn't have enough beds. After some back and forth I was told we will give you a room across the hall as that is all we have and will take 50.00 off the room for your trouble. Although I was still a unhappy with the situation and being separated from my 71 year old father he felt he would be fine alone and we were getting a discount price which would save him money so we decided to go ahead and agree. The only other complaint I have is the "movie room" this is really just a TV and you have to bring your own movie to watch. I was under the impression from the site that they played disney movies. When I got home I found a 868.00 room charge and a 197.00 room charge. I would like to know who would ever consider paying that much for three nights! Anyway, I called to complain and was told that again I can't hear well and that the front desk clerk did a great job by giving me a 50.00 credit for the second room. If you are reading this I hope you are also reading the review where a plane was late and someone lost their room ever after calling to let them know. You might want to get a noterized document prior to staying here!

title: “Great Location, Solid Hotel”
text:
I stayed at the New Yorker in mid July, primarily due to its vacinity to Penn Station (I took the Amtrak Maple Leaf from TO) and for its reasonable price quotes on-line. Overall I was very impressed with this hotel.
First off, due to weather issues, I was unable to check-in until about 1130pm...no worries, the hotel staff was great and I was checked-in within minutes. The location to Penn Station is unreal, it's a block north of the Northwest entrance. 
Now for those who are expecting a huge room, well for a single bed, it's not big at all, but since you will likely spend about 80-85% of your time in the city, it's fine. The room was really clean and the cleaning staff addressed all of my questions/problems I had (btw I only had on problem with a tap that was leaking the first night and that was addressed the next morning).
Since this hotel is on top of the A,C and E subway and down the street from the 1,2 and 3 lines you can get anywhere at anytime. I was able to get to all the sites and attractions I wanted to in relatively quick times. 
My primary reason for the trip was to see Yankee and Shea stadiums and both aren't too bad to get to from the hotel via the subway. 
To be honest I really just slept at the hotel and was all over the city the rest of the time (MSG, Yankee and Shea Stadium, St Patrick's Cathedral, WTC site, etc.). 
Here are the main pros and cons from the stay:
Pros:
Location- see above
Security- you have to show you pass to get to the elevators all the time
Cleanliness- very clean and comfortable room
Access to the subway- See above, it's right below
Access to attractions- down the street from MSG and the Empire State Building. Also for those shoppers, Macy's is about 2 blocks west
Value- For what I paid+location, it was excellent
Cons:
Room size- again this is a minor con, but I'm sure some people need a large room....this place might not do that for you
Air conditioner- It was a bit noisy and it was really, really cold (even on a low fan)
Bathroom- although it was clean and a fair size, it was outdated (green tiles and what looked like a sink from the 40's)
Cable TV- Hardly an channels, but again NYC is the city that never sleeps, so who needs TV,
Overall the cons were very minimal and the pros far outweigh them. I would definately recommend this hotel to anyone and already have to my parents.

title: “Great place, very comfortable, though could be pricey if you book late”
text:
Nice and clean twin room with bunk bed. 
The rooftop is open for guests and presents a good city view. 
Bathrooms were shared on the floor, but there were enough of them and they were clean and comfortable. 
Room had a music station to listen iPod. 
Free wireless internet.
No breakfast included, but there is a good american-style cafe around the corner.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: I was not sure at first as somebody told me that the walls were super thin and noise would be a problem. That was not our experience. The beds were VERY comfortable and the service very friendly. We walked around quite a bit and just discovered Boston on foot. I would stay here again.

title: “All Depends on what you want”
text:
Location is key, but if you are expecting great amenities, go somewhere else. Not a horrible place, but you definitely get what you pay for and I do not know if I would stay again.
The clerk on check in was a little bit rude and the shower could not make up its mind if it wanted to give you scalding hot water or freezing cold. This being said, we walked nearly everywhere and there were decent restaurants near by. (Not the ones attached to the hotel... I never got a cold beer from Harrys although the food was not bad. ). Because of its location, we were able to sleep in a little bit longer and still see all of the sites. You were never too far away from the METRO, the Capitol or the museums. 
So it all depends on what you want more...location or amenities

title: “Great Hotel - A real Home Away from Home”
text: I recently travelled to San Diego with a friend and we chose to stay at The Westgate Hotel. Would I stay there again or recommend it to others? Absolutely!!. It reminded me of a Paris hotel I stayed in with its many heritage pieces of furniture and decoration throughout. The real bonus of this hotel is the Chief Concierge. She made us feel very welcome both to the hotel and to the city. She gave great advice for restaurants and for tours, booked and made reservations where required and overall made this trip more memorable that we thought possible.
