The Chief Concierge in this hotel would make me choose it over larger hotels overlooking the water. It is in a good location, right downtown within walking distance of a shopping mall and the water front. There is a transit stop directly outside the front door and we were able to ride all public transit for a daily rate of five dollars. I hope to return some day.

title: “EASY TO GET TO FROM O'HARE”
text: I stayed in this hotel for a conference. It was easy to get to from O'hare. Just go to the CTA train station in O'Hare. Please bring exact change of $2.25 for ticket since the machines do not give change. Get a ticket and go on the blue route and get down at the Monroe station in downtown, walk three minutes and you are at the hotel. The hotel is in an excellent location and is really beauftiful!! Internet at this place is $14.95 a day which I do not understand. Why not provide free wifi especially in this connected age!!! This was the only downside... Hotel room was nice, nice comfy bed and nice bathroom.

title: “Great Location, great staff, good breakfast, small rooms”
text: Easy to get around Chicago from here, close to the L, lots of restaurants/Bars. Can walk to Michigan Ave/Navy Pier/etc. L to ballparks. Staff very helpful, TV in room limited (some channels not available/could never access pay channels). Room is small but okay considering you are out in Chicago most of the time.

title: “Where the heck did we end up?”
text:
This was our last stop on a mini-roadtrip through parts of the east coast. We booked this place in advance, but didn't arrive until almost 3AM in the morning due to spending time with friends. We walk in and the first thing we see are bunk beds and wondered why we were given this room; we realized it was a family suite. This is fine and we came to appreciate the funky decor, but then it was all downhill after that.
Pubic hairs on the towels, for one thing; a toilet that didn't flush; a broken light fixture in the bathroom; oh, and a half-working AC unit on one of the hottest days in the summer (approximately 105°F during the day, but feels like 111°F). I woke up the next morning and had a scratchy throat because of how muggy the room was from the barely functioning AC and the moldy smell of the room. We complained about the last three (didn't bother with the towel, which is absolutely disgusting and I feel I should have); we get back from being out and about twelve hours later... and surprise! The toilet still contained waste, light's still broken, and AC still sucks. We complained again, but at this point it was so late that they had no one available to fix it; they upgraded our room to suite, which was also nice but it was almost midnight and the only thing I can remember is the spider crawling on the ceiling above the bed before running from the room to sleep in the living room of the suite. The next day, we realized we had a tub that didn't drain water either, but we didn't care at that point since we were leaving.
The appearance of the two rooms were very worn with wallpaper peeling, old makeup stains and smudges on the walls and for some reason on the edge of the tub, and did I mention spiders? Because, yeah - - spiders. One star for the artsy decor and funky style, another star for trying to resolve an issue that should have been resolved during the day to begin with. I really wanted to like this place, but the spider was the last straw (though someone else's pubic hair in our 'clean' towels should have been it). PS. The AC worked great, but it was a moist kind-of-great that I was definitely sick the day we left, currently still sick NOW.

title: “Convenience, Nice Rooms”
text: Easton Town Center had been one of my main destinations during my first six visits to Columbus, although I had never stayed near the Easton property until this hotel opened, as most of the older Easton hotels are on the expensive side. Easton Town Center is only a few minutes away by vehicle (walking is possible but not all that convenient) and a courtesy shuttle is also offered both to the shopping/entertainment complex and to the airport. It's convenient to both I-270 (the beltway around Columbus) and some of the city's major arteries, making city travel easy no matter the destination. The rooms are clean, modern, quiet, and spacious--nothing overly fancy, but up-to-date and practical--exactly what a good Hampton Inn should be. The staff was friendly as well. There is a very nice indoor pool at this hotel plus a fitness center and business center. The continental breakfast offers a decent selection of good food. There aren't any real drawbacks to this hotel at all--it's probably the best overall package for the money for those who are coming to Columbus for a night or two and want to spend some time at the incredible Easton Town Center.

title: “Please read the Review before using this Rating.”
text:
When you book at a Hampton, you come to expect updated fixtures, nice beds, fashionable décor and great service. This hotel has all of those things. My only suggestion to the management would be for them to review the practices of those who perform the cleaning of these rooms. We had spent 8 days prior to our arrival here in a dated and very old hotel in Amish country that was sandwiched between stays at two Hampton Inns. We were shocked at how well the older hotel cleaned their rooms and how spotless they kept them for 8 days.
When we checked in at this hotel, I immediately noticed that someone had sneezed in the bathroom and left a bloody nasal discharge on the wall just below the sink counter top. This would be an easy oversight as you could only see it when you sat in the bathroom as the counter blocked the view while standing. While this was a disgusting find, we both felt that anyone could miss something this minor. 
The next morning, one of the kids pulled the newspaper off the end of the bed and scattered it across the floor next to the bed. We were in a rush and both ignored this. When we returned, the paper remained scattered around the bed. 
This review was not written to dicourage anyone from staying at this establishment. I would stay here again and am certain the room would be cleaned to normal Hampton standards. 
The good points are the location, which is conveniently located if you are seeing the great zoo and there are a number of really good restaurants a short drive away. The complimentary breakfast is excellent and the pool is great and open later than some hotels, which gives the kids more time to exhaust themselves before bedtime. 
If the cleaning staff had paid more attention to details, or if I had drawn a different room number, this hotel would have received a 5 for this review.

title: “Poorly Managed”
text:
My family had a reservation at this hotel for a non-smoking room. When my husband made the reservation he made it clear that we would be arriving after midnight after flying into Phoenix. When we arrived at 1:30am we were told that our room was a smoking room and was the only room left in the hotel. It smelled like a casino and there was no way we could stay with my husband and daughter having a headache from traveling all day, me being very sensitive to smells and my other daughter had a cold. The front desk clerk had offered to spray something in the room but had no idea of how long it would take to work. We inquired about other hotels in the area but she said they were all full. We decided to leave and drive the 2 hour trip home in the middle of the night. What an inconvenience!
My family was in the hotel business for forty years, and I have a feeling I know what happened. Someone else checked into the smoking room that did not have a non-smoking room reserved. After they complained, the front desk staff decided to rent our room to them and let the night auditor deal with us when we arrived much later. Why didn't the housekeeping staff try to get the room smelling better during the day or anyone else once they realized they would have to place a non-smoking reservation in a smoking room? I left my contact information and asked for the general manager to call us but never heard from her.
I think this property is poorly managed. Before leaving I used the restroom off the lobby. It was a mess. I do not recommend this property and will not try staying here again.

title: “Excellent place to stay in Memphis”
text: My wife and I stayed at the River Inn for two nights over thanksgiving and we were very happy with our choice. Before we arrived we were a bit concerned about how safe it was in Memphis but we need not have worried about the location of this hotel because it is in a very nice new residential area opposite a park that runs alongside the Missippi and just 5 minutes by taxi into town. The hotel itself is built in mock New England style and our room was perfectly ok with a fairly large bathroom and although there was no separate shower cubicle the shower itself was excellent. We spent thanksgiving night in the hotel restaurant Paulettes in all honesty because nowhere else was open. There wasn't much atmosphere but the food itself was fine. Special mention must be made of Caprice in reception who was lovely and Patrick who served breakfast who was just charming. Would we stay here again when in Memphis - yes definitely. During our brief stay we managed to visit Graceland, Sun Studios, Stax Museum and the National Civil Rights Museum all in one day (just!) with a very quick stop for lunch at the Rendezvous Cafe and I would recommend all of these places except perhaps the Rendezvous which is an experience though we thought their famous ribs were nothing special. We particularly enjoyed our trip to Graceland even if it was bit like Disney for Elvis fans and the Sun Studio tour was also great though the the other two places mentioned above were also definitely worth visiting.

title: “good location”
text: right next door to grand central station ,great location.,nice room .the lobby is spectacular ,ice machines on each floor.shampoo n soap changed daily.walking distance to times square .and broadway ,very enjoyable stay

title: “Funky, contemporary, super staff and excellent location”
text: Very funky and contemporary accommodation, the best I have had in NY on a budget. From checking in via machine on the ground floor, seeing the infamous YOBOT in action, it was a most pleasant stay from start to finish. Staff were very friendly and could not do enough for the group of us that stayed in the hotel. Any queries were swiftly dealt with by MIssion Control (4th Floor). If you are there for work, the food is supplied separately by an outsourced company from the hotel. The room was akin to an airline cabin, the bed was in a lounge like position and could be lowered for bedtime. All very clean, comfortable with room service daily. The galley at the end of the corridoor was available to all for hot drinks/fridge/water and ice - no facilitied in the room. All other conveniences were provided in addition with the amazing view day/night of the river and of NY from 22nd floor. It was only 10 min walk to Times Sq and taxis were always available to your destination. The subway is just before Times Sq and we were able to get the bus to Woodbury Common, only 5 mins around the corner. Highly recommed YOTEL for your NY accommodation and will definitely making reservations on our next trip to NY.

title: “Great facility for a conference!”
text: Wonderful facility, great location on the harbor with many, many local activities and eateries. Baltimore is a great tourist location that is a well hidden secret and the Marriott is the centerpiece.

title: “A nice property offering good value BUT NO CNBC!”
text: This hotel has been nicely amenitized over the years, and the lobby is open and inviting, and food is decent to good. My one complaint, and it may not be relevant to you, but as a business traveler, I was SHOCKED to discover the hotel offered no access to either CNBC or Bloomberg. As a business traveler who relies on market data I find it unacceptable that a property in the US would not make available through their their cable or satellite provider access to at the very least CNBC. I have NEVER stayed at ANY property in the WORLD where this channel was not offered, except in some South American countries where at least Bloomberg was provided. Easily 4 star hotel with this one simple change.

title: “Dim hallways, great service”
text:
Rooms are great, service is very good (with the exception of some waiting for service at the front desk....). Restaurant is very good as is the rooftop pool area and bar (on the downside, they close too early).....
Hairdryers in the rooms are not very good....small detail but one of the only areas where attention to detail is lacking. Hallways are very dark, almost shabby. Doors of the rooms slam shut which makes for noisy neighbors. Rooms on the Huntingdon avenue side (odd numbers) are larger but noisier.....
Finally the AC is not great in some of hte rooms and they need to work on the bathroom fans.
Would stay there again for price, location and the rooftop pool. A nice boutique style hotel, well located.....

title: “The first new technology I’ve seen in a long time!”
text:
I am a frequent traveler and stay in hotels a lot, very often in Hilton properties. I must say I was really impressed with the computer Hilton provided in the room. A great big touchscreen, welcomed me by name, and I was able to explore the hotel, surf the internet, and explore the city with a great directory of everything around the hotel. 
I must say this was a great convenience and I really wonder why more hotels don't offer this!

title: “Wonderful Stay”
text:
The room was wonderful and new; the customer service folks were among the best any where. The lobby is a typical Embassy Suites, only a little bit larger than normal. 
This hotel is less than 20 minutes from the airport; less than 30 minutes from downtown and Graceland; and less than an hour from the casinos in Mississippi. There is a Target, Ruth Chris Steakhouse and a boatload of shopping and other dining options within a 10 minute drive along Shady Grove Road. To the left of the hotel along Shady Grove is upscale, and to the right of Shady Grove is old Memphis, which offers a movie theater and orginal BBQ.
My meeting were at the airport, and I found this property ideally located. The property is VERY SAFE and VERY CLEAN and offered very reasonable rates. 
By the way, the Hampton Inn next door looked really cool too!

title: “Great hotel -- perfect for families or corporate events”
text: My company hosted a meeting at the JW Marriott Hill Country in Sept 2011 -- overall, it was an excellent venue. The layout of the hotel makes it the perfect venue for both business events and family outings. The meals and catering provided by the facility were excellent and the staff was courteous and helpful. The facility is nice but not overly pretentious – the meeting rooms and facilities were very functional for business – the guest rooms were very comfortable – and the waterpark area / lazy river would be fun for families of all ages. I’ll be back to the JW Marriott Hill Country – but next time with my family. Excellent hotel!

title: “"Disappointed"”
text:
We decided to stay here because we love history, old stuff, and it was rated 3-4 stars. It was not a 3-4 star experience.
Let me start with the pro's! Panama Hotel did warn us that it was old (100 years-ish) and had a lot of charm. Which was great! It was oozling with charm and historical significance. Our room was spotless; very clean, the linens were crisp & white (no stains!). The room had no TV, but it was very authentic. The tea house on the main level was charming and we could have hung out there all day. The drinks were a bit overpriced ($5 for tea? Really?) but the continental breakfast included there was fantastic. We were prepared to share bathrooms with others and I have to say I was amazed at how clean they were...all the time! And the price was decent for it's location, era, and weekend rate. 
The location was decent, in terms of being close to the main sports arenas, but it is a bit of a trek to Pike Place, Key Arena, etc. The staff were very genuine and friendly, although awkward. 
Prepare for a pretty rinky-dink operation. When I arrived there was no Visa machine and everything was signed at a table in a main room. They lot our reservation. They literally copied our ID on a printer on the table and then were unable to give me a receipt. Parking was awful, but I think that's just a Seattle thing (sorry Seattle!). Our room was very "cozy" (read: SMALL; so small you have to dance around your spouse to get anywhere, and climb over them when you want to get out of bed). Our bed was incredibly uncomfortable; I kept almost falling off the bed because our mattress was so worn. The bed was super creaky and we could hear every word that came from the room next to us (so if privacy is your thing...check elsewhere). I did not get hot water once, so bathing was a no go (luckily we only stayed one night!). We did not realize it was pet-friendly, which combined with the age of the furniture/carpets/building made my allergies flare up. We were out all evening and came back to our room which was so hot it was unbearable; there was no way to adjust heat or turn on A/C and the window was impossible to open. 
They are trying to make it authentic, and it's hard to keep things authentic and meet modern expectations, however, it was not a 3-4 star experience, and we will not be returning. It was very charming though; if that's your thing, go look at a room, take a tour, then decide if it's right for you.

title: “Excellent stay & great location for our requirements”
text:
We had cause to use this great hotel twice in our recent holiday, we were first introduced to this hotel by our airline after an uncheduled delay in our ininerary and subsequently needed a complimentary overnight stopover. We were not happy about the situation but on arrival at the Hilton in our aggitated state we were immediately put at ease with the swift checkin and cleanliness of our room. The use of the swimming pool was an added bonus and the 'hot-tub' was relaxing. Our evening meal & breakfast had a great choice and all looked freshly prepared.
The courtesy shuttle bus to the airport runs continuously 24/7 and if you just miss it a 15 minute wait is very acceptable. Towards the end of our vacation we altered our plans to spend time in Mexico & immediately decided to book ourselves in the Hilton for our required overnight stay between flight connections.
Our second room was larger than the first and all amenities were in place, again we were very impressed with the overall whole experience & would not hesitate to book this Hilton again if we return to L.A.
We booked direct online and chose the 'cheap' option of 'any available room' on arrival and it all worked perfectly.

title: “Weekend Getaway”
text: Planning a weekend getaway at Christmas time, we decided to book a room at the historic Menger Hotel. My wife and I were not disappointed. The room was a plaza suite. The room was spacious, the bed very comfortable, and we had access to a balcony. Each and every night, we heard Christmas songs sung by carolers in the plaza below. My wife treated herself to a "Heal Thyself" foot massage at the spa and loved it. Looks like this might be the start of a Christmas tradition.

title: “Affordable with great location”
text:
A bit worn down, but in a charming way. The elevator was not working when we stayed there, but Im sure they would have helped us carry our bags had we asked for it.
Close to The White House, and Dupont Circle with its bars and resturants.
Breakfast was the usual continental stuff, but with varm waffels.
Recommended for an affordable stay in DC

title: “Cannot Recommend the Hawthorn”
text:
I recently attended a conference for work and had the misfortune to stay at the Hawthorn Suites Hotel in El Paso, TX. As an overall recommendation - I think the Hawthorn Suites tries hard, they list amenities similiar to what one would get at other suite hotels - such as Residence Inn - but the facade wears out pretty quickly - so I would have to recommend not staying at this location.
When I travel I make a list of good points and bad to help me remember the details and so here they are for the Hawthorn:
Good Points:
- It is located near the airport but is pretty quiet - I don't recall being woken up at night due to airplane noise
-Has a data port in the room - although - I did not use so I don't know how much they charged for using it.
- They have a pool and jacuzzi - although I found the jacuzzi to be a bit strange - the benches were too low in the water to sit and the steps leading into it were too high....NEver saw anyone elese ever use the pool or jacuzzi.
- Free Parking
- Close to Applebees and a steakhouse - but not much else around.
- They offer a hot breakfast with ham or bacon & eggs, not just cold muffins and cereal.
- They offer a manager's cocktail with beer, wine and soda. However, no matter which night we went to this & despite repreatedly mentioning it to the staff, the beer was flat & the wine was chilled - including the reds....
- They had a small gym - although several people commmented that it was too small, too limited and did not offer good working equipment.
- Price - Not sure if it was due to Katrina folks or what but this hotel beat the other hotels close to the airport by a significant amount.
Well, afraid thats all the good points - here are my list of negatives:
-The room was too small. They advertise as being spacious - but there was the just no room to maneuver in the room. There was one uncomfotable easy chair to sit in wedged in the corner by the window but that was it. The room was so small the stand for the suitcase/closet was in the bathroom...
- Gum in the carpet beneath the bathroom vanity - I had to ask specifically for it to be removed as the cleaing crew never saw it...
- No sheer drapes inthe room - so you were on display or it was very dark.
- Terrible smoke smell in a non-smoking room. Why hotels never enforce the no smoking policy is a real irritant.
-Check in time was listed as 3:00 pm, yet they could not offer me a room until 3:20 and no one at the front desk seemed to care of apologize for the inconvience.
- Glassware in bathroom was not clean - with some sort of white substance in the bottom.
- Poor, small, scratchy towels in the bathroom.
- A $.35 charge for local calls
- USA Today offered only in the lobby, not to rooms and no local newspapers offered.
- TV Remote was very small and did not offer numbered buttons to change channels - to go to a specific channel you had to scroll all the way up or down to the end.
- No do not disturb sign or placard in the room.
Thats it for the negatives. To be fair I offered to discuss my comments with management before I left but no manager was on duty who was available to hear them.
A very dissapointing stay and this hotel is not reflective of a Hyatt Hotel property. Recommend you look elsewhere to stay in El Paso.

title: “A great family or business hotel”
text:
As a Hilton diamond member, I see a lot of hotels around the world. This hotel
is one of the best hotel stays in my 16 years of traveling. Sure, it is not to be compared to other Hilton hotel brands since "Homewood" suites are designed for long-term stays. The breakfast and more importantly, the dinners (buffet style) are very good. The outdoor area is very inviting as well as functional. The rooms are spacious and well appointed. The ease of parking and access to the San Diego area make this hotel a winner

title: “For Business travellers maybe?”
text:
We would really love to rate this Hotel higher as all the staff were fantastic, but for Tourists we really felt it was a more a business Hotel.
First the good points. The Staff were extremely helpful, friendly and efficient. There is also a courtesy bus which we used to go to Sea World. They can also get you discounted tickets to various attractions.That's about it.
The Hotel is miles away from anywhere. A ten minute walk will take you to the Trolley stop but other than that you will need a car.
Our air conditioner cluncked so bad through the night that we had to turn it off. We had stayed in seven Hotels/Resorts on our month long trip and this was the only one that charged for Wi Fi, Internet, printing and even the bottle of water left daily in the room.
The rooms are basic and there are no in Room safes.
We would've rated it a two, only that the staff were so good. 
If you have a few days to Tour, stay Downtown.

title: “Ok if you get a priceline rate”
text: I booked this hotel through priceline for $70 on a Friday night. I didn't expected high quality for the price I paid so I wasn't disappointed. Check in was quick and easy. Elevators are plentiful and fast. Hallways are a little dingy. Door to room was falling off its hinge. Had to give it a push with my shoulder to open and close it. Room was clean but well worn. Looks like they upgraded at some point but the upgrade was done on the cheap. Some mildew in the shower. Wallpaper peeling in places. Sleep number beds are not the best for me. Felt more like a camping air mattress. We parked on the street and fed the meter for a few hours Friday afternoon and Saturday morning (spent $8 doing that). We didn't eat/drink at the hotel. I would go back if I could get a good priceline rate. good luck!

title: “excellent location , beautiful interiors .. pricey though.”
text:
I stayed in nikko hotel for 3 days. It was an excellent location for shopping, just walking distance, ranging from the high street shops to some of the moderate priced outlet malls. A lot of good restaurants to choose from aswell, just walking distance. The service was very friendly, i had a single room which was very spacious, including the bathroom. If i was to be very critical ... the day i checked in the towels weren't very clean, my fridge didn't open but no fret ... that could be replaced easily. The breakfast menu was expensive. There is a sunflower cafe right infront of the hotel which does very economical , and delicous breakfast menu's. And you have starbucks right below the hotel, very convenient. 
The lobby was very nice aswell . They have a business center but you have to pay even for making a copy which wasn't very nice. I haven't had to pay in other hotels. So, overall this is an expensive hotel... if you have no problem paying ... you can choose this one for. 
Dine out !!!!!

title: “The worst! Forced to sleep in a closet (no beds and windows)”
text:
My wife and I recently stayed here for a half business/leisure trip to Jacksonville. What was supposed to be a pleasant visit ended up becoming a catastrophe. We would NEVER recommend this hotel after our horrible experience of being mistreated. We left extremely disappointed with hotel management and will never return. Do NOT go.
Pre-trip:
My wife and I are over 60 years old and frequently travel, and this is by far the worst experience ever! We usually don't leave online reviews, but this is the first time that I have to ask my son to post this review using his TripAdvisor account. 
Hyatt offers online check in 24 hours prior to arrival. We took advantage of this online tool and confirmed our room.
On-arrival:
We arrived at 11 pm and tried to pick up our keys, but the front desk informed us that there has been a change in our room, and our online check-in has been voided. Our new room was basically a closet with NO BED, NO WINDOWS, and it turns out that the kitchen/toilet was malfunctioning. 
Assistant manager to the front desk, Mr. Matt Palmer, came out to inform us that this was our ONLY OPTION. We were told that this was due to our late arrival (so...online check-in and specifying our arrival time was not enough?) We were told that this will only be for our first night, but the room rate of $175 remains unchanged. As compensation for this ridiculous closet, we were given breakfast for ONLY the next morning and a one-class upgraded room for the remaining two nights (a lofty $35 value - wow, lucky us...). This is completely unacceptable!
We tried to argue and demanded alternatives, but unfortunately, English is not our first language. Mr. Palmer took advantage of the situation and brushed us off. We were left feeling helpless, mistreated with his service, attitude, and inability to deal with the situation. It wasn't until after repeatedly asking "why" did he finally tell us that the hotel was overbooked. Apparently, ONLINE CHECK IN is useless. We just want our original room and will pay the rate that we booked, but this is too much to ask at Hyatt Jacksonville Riverfront.
We had to call our son and ask him for help. After numerous calls to get in touch with Mr. Palmer and what I'm sure was a very frustrating conversation, the best that he could do was to take $75 off the FIRST NIGHT ONLY - that's $100 for a room with no windows and no bed (see pictures). It is clear that Mr. Palmer is grossly incompetent, unable to manage his staff and customers, does not understand basic customer service and hotel management, and cannot deal with situations outside normal/standard business operations. He took advantage of our old age and inability to speak English fluently. Hyatt Jacksonville has the potential to be better without this employee. 
No bed, no window, closet room:
We had slept (or didn't/couldn't really) on a sofa bed. The sofa bed is extremely uncomfortable, and at our age, we woke up suffering from BACK PAINS. That terrible evening weakened our immune system, and we got so sick that we COULD NOT WALK downstairs for the only free morning of breakfast that was offered to us. 
We feel relieved to have returned from Hyatt hell and to have escaped from the unjust treatment and customer disservice. Unfortunately, we are still physically ill and recovering from the emotional trauma. We recommend that you avoid this property at all costs. There are plenty of other wonderful places in the area to stay.

title: “Great place - highly recommend”
text:
We stayed at the Hotel Drisco for two nights in September. The location is fantastic in Pacific Heights. The staff were very attentive and helpful - a special thank you to Marti and Bob for helping us with everything from maps, taxis and a car service pick-up to the airport. We'd come back from an evening out and tell them all about our experience. They really made us feel at home!
The room was nice, but a little noisy. I think that is because our room wall was against the staircase so we would hear people using the stairs. That's the only reason I wouldn't give this hotel 5 stars. I think if we stayed in an outer room we wouldn't have had the noise issue. But it is an older hotel so I guess you have to expect that. 
Service was great. Location was great. We'd stay here again and would recommend.

title: “Perfect stay in Times Square”
text: My daughter and I went up to New York for a concert at a theater in Times Square--found Yotel on Priceline and read the reviews on Tripadvisor. It was perfect--ultramodern facility. Safe, clean, beautiful use of space, friendly staff. Bonus--we were able to leave our luggage with the "yobot" for the day we spent in the City before heading home that evening.

title: “OMG.. this was actually the most awful experience!”
text:
I have never been to a hotel where when you call the operator, guest services or housekeeping you either get NO ANSWER... or the actually disconnect the line when they answer.
AWFUL AWFUL CUSTOMER SERVICE ! ! ! !
Being a Crowne Plaza you would expect better.... 
AWFUL.
Also very VERY LOUD HALLWAYS>.. VERY NOISEY...SLAMMING DOORS...

title: “near road and airport very noisy”
text: The hotel itself was very good, however it is very noisy as there is an airpot very close and the planes fly all night long, it is also on a main road with ver heavy vehicles passing.

title: “This is not a four star hotel.”
text: Do not Priceline this hotel if you are expecting a four star hotel, it is a three star at best. My husband and I took a chance with Priceline requesting four star or better and were so disapointed with this hotel that we gave up our room and checked into the Marriott, a true four star hotel. Of course, we gave up the money we paid for Hotel Felix as Priceline is non refundable, but the Marriott completely understood our disapointment and at no extra cost, upgraded us to a suite on the 46th floor with a stunning view of the city.

title: “thanks”
text: was in NYC last weekend shopping for our daughter's wedding dress and stayed for our first time at the Andaz. So happy with this choice! This was an emotional and busy weekend and the Andaz was a great place to relax after the day. Best features were the terrific staff and wonderful shower. Convenient to all, quiet at night, comfy bed, coffee water and wine when needed and never a wait for anything including elevators or car as previous review stated. We did not try the restaurants as we were off with family all day but they seemed to be continually busy. Will definitely return, probably for the fittings- we found the dress!

title: “Great location near Hollywood Blvd”
text: Terrific hotel just a block away from Hollywood Blvd. It's not cheap ($180 AUD) per night, but worthwhile if you want to check out the local area for all the famous sights. A nice choice at breakfast too. Big bonus - free snacks for the duration of your visit!

title: “Rock-tastic experience!”
text:
We loved the location, decor and the room. Clubs downstairs seemed to attract an interesting crowd, that was rocking the streets until wee hours. But we were on vacation and did not mind.
Hotel's pool was good too, with a bar close by.
Absolutely loved the complimentary Gibson guitar. 
I kept her close to my side of the bed (i think my partner was jealous). We managed to learn some 'Iron Man' cords on it and rocked the room :)
Seriously - awesome!!!

title: “A quiet cozy treasure in Back Bay”
text: I use to live in Boston and recently have stayed here three times and each time have absolutely found this hotel to be a treasure; small, quiet, cozy, and a fantastic location to my favorite Newbury street shops (Cotelac) and restaurants (Sonsie). The staff is beyond gracious, welcoming, accommodating and knowledgeable. Not fancy, but updated, clean, convenient, and comfortable. A five Star value!!!

title: “They should have better cleaning and some one to pick up your luggage”
text: It very modern style. It is located near to the White House. The rooms, kitchen, dinning area are perfect for families. The only thing that they should improve is to clean rooms. They forgot to clean up our room. And have in mind nobody helps you with your luggage.

title: “not a bad place”
text: hotel stay was mar,24-27 2007 let us check in early.here for nascar race in fontana,,.suite was nice for the days that we were here but the fridge was not as cold as it should be. called downstairs and was told that i could bring my drinks downstairs [pop,water,juice] and put in their fridge.i declined and said thank you for the offer.came back from the race late on sunday 10pm,and the front door was not completely shut [locked].i went downstairs and told them and they said they would send security with me and check the room out.my wife and myself checked it out before i went down to the front desk.they said that they were very sorry and it would not happen again,she said she would notify housekeeping of what had happened.she called my room about an hour later and said how sorry she was about what had happened. i thought that that was very awesome of her too call back at a later time a say she was sorry for what had happened.i told her that i will be back in sept. and said thank you. thumbs up too her

title: “Would repeat with a few changes”
text:
I recently stayed at the O'brien while attending the Women of Faith conference, held at the Alamodome.
The room was comfortable, once we figured out the ceiling fan, and room fan.
Continental breakfast was sufficient.
Alamodome was a short walk away, cutting through Hemisphere Park, which allowed us to leave the car parked the whole weekend.
Riverwalk was 2 short blocks away, and we felt safe all evenings walking after dark.
My only 2 complaints were the $10/night parking fee (just include it in the room rate, and I would feel less raped, and I would request a room on the back side of the hotel, as the traffic noise was a bit intrusive.
Otherwise, a pleasant stay, with affordable rates. ($116 internet rate)

title: “An Amazing Experience - Fantastic Upgrade!”
text:
We stayed at The Waldorf in August as part of a trip to The US and Canada before returning to the UK on the QM2. We stayed for four nights. Our party consisted of my husband and I and our 2 boys aged 12 and 9. On checking in we waited a few minutes and another desk was opened and we were served by the Night Manager "Yon". He went to check us in and commented that he thought the room that we had booked would not be comfortable for as my husband is 6ft 10" tall and we had booked a double-double. We assured him that we were used to it but he offered us a suite albeit on the smoking floor. We gratefully accepted and excited went up to "17H". The suite of rooms was absolutely beautiful. We had a marble lobby area with butler area, a massive sitting room with windows over Park Avenue and a view of the Empire State Building from 49th Street window. There was a massive master bedroom with huge flat screen TV, DVD player and Bose radio. There was a large dressing room and a huge marble bathroom with separate toilet and shower and bath with 2 vanity areas. The rooms were spotlessly clean and richly furnished. There was bottled water and bowls of fruit that arrived at intervals. The suite smelt beautiful - not of smoke that you might have expected. The hotel delivered 2 rollaway beds for the boys and they set up camp in the sitting room. We are delighted to have a few nights in our own room after many days travelling altogether!
The Concierge were very helpful in recommeding restaurants that the children would also like and all staff that we encountered were friendly and efficient.
The hotel itself was like walking back in time. The displays and photos all around I found very interesting and we looked around the hotel and the various function rooms and you can begin to imagine what life for the guilded few was like 80 odd years ago. The hotel trades on it's past and why not - I really enjoyed it - and the people watching! It tied in nicely with the final part of our holiday - travelling home on the last ocean liner. For that our cabin was smaller than the walk in wardrobe in the Waldorf! We had a fantastic time in New York and the Waldorf is ideally placed for a trip to NYC and to to stay in the style we were given made it all the more special - Thank you so much. I very much doubt we would ever get an opportunity like that again.

title: “Good place, but no in-room coffee”
text:
I liked the location, clean room, good reading light/chair, free, no-hassle WiFi and LAN cable, functional desk with power strip, friendly, helpful staff.
Did not like: No in-room coffee (made do with hot water and instant coffee from nearby CSV). Breakfast only at 7 am ("Broken Yolk" next door opens at 6 am).

title: “Bed bugs and unfriendly receptionist”
text: I stayed in this hotel for two nights over Thanksgiving weekend with two friends. Our first impression of the hotel was very good: great rates, great location, nice decor. After our first night, however, we discovered that we had bed bugs in one of our beds, had been bitten and started to have allergic reactions to it. After we requested it, we were given a new room, but nothing was said about compensation for our inconvenience. In the evening our physical condition became worse so that we had to cut our planned night out in San Diego short in order to rest in the hotel. We asked for compensation for our inconvenience but came across Scott, a very rude and unfriendly concierge who pretended he couldn't do anything for us until his managers were back on Monday. On Sunday morning we had to call an emergency doctor in order to treat our allergic reactions. This time we were helped by two very friendly ladies at the reception who, surprisingly, had phone numbers of several managers and were able to put us through to one. This lady at least agreed to put our charges on hold until we could speak to the general manger about compensation on Monday. In the end he waived the accommodation charges, but said they couldn't cover for the medical bills (more than 600$ in total). We were still very upset about the fact that we had to find bed bugs in a hotel like the Bristol and that some members of the staff weren't understanding of our medical conditions and our distress about the situation. I would not stay at this hotel ever again.

title: “Nice, updated Marriott in a great location”
text: My family of 4 spent two nights here on a last minute whim to escape the wrath of Hurricane Sandy back home in New York. The rooms and hotel seems updated and/ or very well kept. the carpets in the hallways and rooms looked brand new and the furnishings were nice and in excellent condition. Comfy bed too! Marriott tends to be our go to mass market hotel chain and we are usually very satisfied. The breakfast buffet was very good in terms of variety and quality also. The location was perfect for touring Boston and shopping and dining at the adjacent mall. We had planned to stay a third night but headed home a day early when we learned our electricity at home was back on. Canceling our last night was no problem, with no penalty. Staff was courteous and efficient. Would definitely return.

title: “Horrid experience”
text:
We paid about $100 a night for this horrid place and won't go back next time. (I accidentally booked it without checking reviews.) I had to inquire about our reservation beforehand and when I called before arrival, I couldn't understand a word the lady at the front desk said. Foreign accent. Maybe English, but I couldn't tell. There's only enough parking for about half the units. All this I could live with, but the NOISE was unacceptable. The walls were thin and a small child cried all night the first night. Garbage trucks were outside our window in the middle of the night to pick up trash. In the a.m. we woke up to a jack hammer outside. The next night someone next door came in at 3 am and talked for hours non-stop. We also had problems opening the door with the card keys that were issued. We had to have them re-issued 3 times, but it didn't get better. One outlet was dead and, of course, it was the one I plugged my phone in for recharging at night. The complimentary breakfast was OJ, coffee, tea and pre-packaged coffee cakes. On the good side, the room was clean (but outdated) and the TV and microwave worked. 
What else would we want from a hotel? Other than parking, access to our room, quiet, free breakfast as advertised, I guess nothing more.

title: “Nice hotel”
text: My mother and I enjoyed our 2 night stay at the White Swan. I'd give it a good, not great. The rooms are larger than I am accustomed to seeing in San Francisco which was nice. The hotel is about 4 blocks from Union Square, however the walk requires a steep uphill return of several blocks, beyond the ability of my 78 year old mother. The elevator is old, and quaint or annoying depending on your attitude. While were there almost all of the people we saw at the wine happy hour and breakfast were AARP'ers.

title: “A Shabby Cave”
text: Imagine a grim, dark cave of many rooms and long, bleak hallways. Now add old carpets in dismal patterns. Remove almost all electric lights, and install low-wattage bulbs in the few remaining fixtures. Welcome to the Best Western Center City Philadelphia! I'd be hard pressed to think of an uglier, shabbier, more depressing hotel. It would cost too much even if it were free.

title: “Recent renovation but not near union station”
text:
I checked on google maps before staying at the hotel so knew it was about 2km from union station.
The hotel has a shuttle which was running every 20 minutes or so until 11pm.
The area around the hotel is not nice but with the shuttle I did not see it as a problem as the trade off is much better deals than the central hotels.
I was told by the taxi driver that the hotel had been recently renovated an you could tell, the shell was still the same but the bed, fridge, microwave etc were all new looking.
The staff were helpful on the few occasions I had questions.

title: “Clean, affordable”
text:
The staff were very nice to us and when their shuttle was down, they reimbursed us the cost of a taxi. The room was clean and the breakfast was pretty big.
In this day and age, when most hotels in Texas are being bought up by people who don't care about how clean they are, this one was a clean, decent place. We will stay here again.

title: “PENN INN THE HILTON AS ONE PHILLY'S BEST”
text:
What a pleasant surprise. I was welcomed from the entrance to the elevator and the front desk. Even a nice VM and a message from the Manage on the iPad in the room. The Inn at Penn has the most professional and friendly staff for any hotel I have ever stayed in. They certainly have a customer’s first attitude.
The room and bath was sparkling clean with a wonderfully designed interior. Most impressive was the bedside iPad with a hotel page where you can do anything from order room service to getting a light bulb changed from maintenance. It has links to the menus and to maps of points of interest in the city. A dreamy comfortable bed with tons of pillows that put me instantly to sleep. A large flat screen TV with the most channels I have ever seen in a hotel including free HBO and Cinemax. Complimentary wireless internet was provided which I am not accustomed to at other Hilton hotels who often charge a fee unless you are Gold member. 
A great location even though it is not in the hub bub of the city center. A Septa trolley station right next to the hotel, a Metro station a couple of blocks away and the 30th Street Amtrak station just six blocks away and accessible by the trolley. 
It a great area to explore with lots of tavern/cafe/bars/restaurants nearby but don't forget to explore the campus of Penn University. The building blends in so well, it is just a little hard to locate if you are not paying attention but I did not let that detract from a wonderful stay which I will repeat soon.
I highly recommend this hotel for those looking to relax after a hustle bustle trip into town.

title: “Thumbs up for the St Francis”
text: I have just returned from San Francisco, where we stayed at the Westin St. Francis Hotel. This was absolutely and undoubtedly one of the most exquisite hotels in San Francisco. The public rooms of the hotel are beautiful, the services are prompt, the staff is friendly and helpful and the food in the restaurants is very good. As for our guestroom--it was immaculate ,very tastefully decorated and enormous. The "heavenly bed" was just that -heavenly -- the bathrooms were a very good size and our view of Union Square was wonderful. Yes, there were people in the streets asking for money, but you will see this in all major cities--who cares --give if you want or can --and keep walking if not. This hotel is great and I will definitely stay here again!

title: “loved it”
text: Second year in a row that we were there in October and loved it. The grounds are beautiful as are the rooms. We had a studio suite which was perfect for two. Employees of the resort were very helpful and delightful to talk with. Recommend for couples or a family. Oh, golf course is very nice and somewhat user friendly.

title: “Best Stay”
text:
Its been great stay. the rooms are nice and staff was very helpful.
always come back

title: “Won't be returning back: feels like you're sleeping on the highway and the service is poor.”
text: I was looking forward to spending 5 nights at the Angeleno but was utterly disappointed for the following reasons: 1. Noisy rooms due to proximity of highway and non-double glazed windows 2. Without prior notice or knocking, someone came into our room and abruptly exited when they discovered we were in the room. I flagged it 3 times with front desk but eventhough they said they will check and revert, no one did 3. Front desk could not answer any of our queries and kept transferring us to someone else who also failed to answer our queries - specifically Internet problems we were having

title: “I will come back.”
text: After a good nights sleep i went to the morning buffet to discover the freshest selection of food that i have seen in over 30 years on the road keep it up.Ask for Anna she made the start of my day fantastic.If you are in Phoenix check this hotel out JD.

title: “Two Bedroomed Apartment with Fantastic View of Chrysler Building!”
text: We stayed in one of their two-bed, two-bath apartments and it was fantastic. Bathrooms were great, beds comfortable, and good linen. The kitchen area was small but perfect for us. The lounge area furniture could do with updating/replacement. Our apartment had a fantastic view of the Chrysler Building and was very special. Excellent location, and would definitely stay here again on our next trip to NYC!

title: “Excellent Place”
text: The Kimpton chain knows how to treat its guests right at whatever location you visit them; hotel Solamar is no exception. From the moment you arrive you feel welcome. The staff is friendly and goes out of their was to help. The hotel is in a good location near Petco Park and the Gaslamp District. It is ecco friendly which is always a plus. They have free coffee and tea in the morning, lemonade at 2:00pm and complimentary wine with hors d'oeuvres at 5:00pm. If you belong to their In Touch Program you get to raid the mini-bar for $10 worth of goodies, and also free internet. The only down side is the parking as it is $36 per night. I have a hybrid car so parking is half price. I highly recommend Hotel Solamar when visiting San Diego.

title: “Truly Palatial”
text:
Our first time in NYC, but hopefully not our last. The Palace is exactly that, a palace. The rooms are huge and wonderfully clean, the marble bathroom was bigger than we have at home, so no problems there. As for the bed, I didn't think there could possibly be a bed as comfortable as ours at home, but I admit I was wrong....lying on the bed was like sinking into marshmallows, simply wonderful! 
We had a view of St. Patrick's Cathedral and over that to the Rockefeller Centre, looking at that scene is a wonderful way to start your day!
The staff are all superb, and special mention must go to Juliana Esteban of Istana, she's extremely good at her job, but also genuinely friendly!
My husband contacted the Hotel before we went to inform them of my approaching birthday (51) and when we returned to our room on the first evening there was a delicious chocolate cake, bottled water and card waiting for me! 
Turn down service is faultless, chocolates by the pillows, and the ice bucket filled, very handy to chill the bottles of Snapple which we brought in with us!
We had breakfast in Istana every morning, and can recommend it, everyone should start their day drinking fresh orange juice whilst sitting beside a marble pillar! 
Yes it's fairly expensive to stay at the Palace, but worth every penny. Would we stay there again? In a heartbeat!!!

title: “Good hotel close to prime shopping Mall”
text:
I did not select this hotel as it is close to a shopping Mall, but it helps if you go Houston for work with your wife! The hotel is nice, has a good parking area, a good reception area and attentive valet service. I was give room 2612, which is a suite room. It was very large and even with a kitchen (something I do not use very often...). I found the pillows not to be exceptional, but everything else was in good working order. The Club lounge is a bit small but the buffet was good, even if they charged for wine and beer (again, US hotels should learn something by looking at their Asian counterparts....).
Gym is small but well equipped, only item missing is a crunch bench but that's ok. It is also quite pleasurable to go around by foot for a walk or run. The area around the hotel is full of good restaurants which can be reached by foot, so the location is quite good.
In all, a hotel I will come back to.

title: “Satisfactory base - no frills but adequate”
text: We were only in the rooms to sleep in and the beds were clean and comfortable. The service was pleasant too at both reception and concierge. Had we stayed longer, or wanted 'down time' in the hotel this might have dampened our satisfaction - the noise is unrelenting in NYC and this didn't feel too different in rooms - from the streets, the room next door, the corridor etc. The bathrooms were disappointing, being very tired and the with fixtures and fittings the worse for wear. Overall though - we wanted to pay a low price for the City and the Milford Plaza is reasonable and the location is perfect. As long as your expectations are appropriate this is fine.

title: “Nice hotel at a good price, book the room class you actually need there aren't roll away beds.”
text: Stayed her with some friends for a weekend of eating and drinking. Got a very good price on priceline. Hotel is modern and clean. The bar downstairs is hip but not open super late so across the street at Harry's is a good bet for quick food and late night drinks. Overall a good experience. If you are looking to walk to NYC attractions this may not be your best bet (as it is in the financial district) but the subway is very close and easy to use to get to most spots.

title: “Beautiful hotel”
text: The hotel is very nice and the location is perfect! It is attached to the Galleria Mall in Houston with lots of upscale stores.

title: “Rodeway inn”
text: Stumbled across this motel during my road trip. great location only 5 min walk from Hollywood blvd. the room was quite a good size and very clean. big bed and flat screen tv. air con was excellent. on site parking. breakfast was suprisingly good. would stay here again.

title: “Great place”
text: This is the second time we have stayed here, the last a year ago and went back as the location for us is great, really close to Pike Place Market and down the hill to downtown - walking back up is not so good but walking in Seattle just involves hills! Close to bus stops (free bus system in central areas). The rooms we have had have all been clean with comfy beds and nice bathrooms. The staff are really helpful and very knowledgeable about eating, drinking and sight seeing places. The wifi wasn't very good in the room but fine in the lobby and free.

title: “OK, but not more”
text:
We stayed three nights and thought Harrington was OK. Location is great for going to the museums, but a little bit boring for eating out. Hotel is in need of renovation. The tiles in our bathroom was broken, the room was smelly and small, TV didn't function properly. Next time in wonderful Washington DC we will go back to Hotel Rouge, where we stayed last time. 
Single Mum on Amtrak

title: “Consistently Good”
text: I have stayed here a dozen times in the last two years, most recently on July 9. The hotel sits next to the old World Trade Center site and was completely renovated after 9/11. The hotel is sleek, modern and comfortable. The standard rooms are small, but very comfortable. The room decor is also modern and minimalist in a good way. Light wood furniture; glass tops on the dresser and desk; large flat screen televisions. I've eaten in the restaurant many times and have been happy with the food. The continental breakfast used to be better and has been scaled back a little of late, but it's ok. It's several years out now since the renovation, but everything is still in very nice shape. Noise has sometimes been a problem with the continuous day/evening work on the World Trade Center site, and most of the rooms face that direction. There are rooms on each end of the hotel that face the opposite direction and they are quieter (although the view isn't nearly as interesting). These rooms are also significantly bigger than the typical rooms facing the WTC site. I've stayed in four of these end rooms, and it seems to be hit or miss if you get one. I've attached some pictures of one of these bigger rooms, so for the standard room, imagine something much narrower. The staff is courteous and professional. One extra bonus of the hotel is that it is also right next to the Century 21 department store. I definitely recommend this hotel.

title: “Great location and local feel”
text:
I've been looking at this hotel for a few years and finally found a great deal though my travel agent. My wife and I do not like staying in Mid Town or Times Square for several reasons mainly due to tourists and the crowds. We like to stay in neighborhoods that feel like you can become a part of time while traveling.
We pulled up the hotel at 4:30pm on Thursday and their was no one to help us with our bags or point us to check in. Not the end of the world, but not what I was expecting. Check in was pretty simple, my request for a high floor was granted and then some computers issues we where put on the 3rd floor. I would suggest a high floor like other reviewers have mentioned to get a way from the street noise and get a better view.
The room was decent size for NYC standards. Great black out blinds, good size bathroom and the AC was really good.
Our room 305 looked worn in places, not what you would expect from a hotel of this nature.
I took a shower and immediately noticed that the shower head was spitting water and really dripping on my head. Again, not would I would expect from this hotel.
We did try Maialino for drinks and snacks. It was very good. You can go grab coffee which is very good at the bar anytime. It's Coffee Culture which is fantastic if you have not had it.
The food was solid, we only had snacks. Service top notch.
Room service was really a downer. We had complementary continental breakfast each day. This was nice to be able to grab coffee and OJ while getting ready. The baked goods where bland. 
The concierge was super easy to work with and made every effort to book reservations and provide suggestions when asked. If you are not familiar with NYC, I would ask then for help and ideas.
Overall, I loved the convenience to lower Manhattan. We really did enjoy the hotel and if it had not been sold out, we would have switched rooms. Each hotel has a few rooms with some problems, I felt 305 was that room. Both my wife and I agree we would stay here again.

title: “Throughly mediocre”
text: I travel a great deal for my work, and as a consequence have stayed in a large number of hotels worldwide, including the Sofitel in Bangkok, Hanoi ( the Metropole) and Paris (Dokhan's). The Sofitel New York was in every respect a clear underperformer in both absolute and comparative terms, from what is, normally quite a dependable chain. The room was okay (just), but it didn't require close inspection to see that it was grubby (heavily stained curtains for example), an ugly emply raw plug left in the wall, a flat screen TV thoughtlessly dumped on the desk, and little attention to detail or style overall. The corridors were frequently littered with the aftermath of room service dinners and there were disturbing building works going on from early in the morning, (a fact the hotel didn't seem to see the need to trouble me with when making the reservation), and which the front desk seemed to regard as par for the course. All this may just about be okay if if you are paying for a three star, but this holds itself out as a stylish top of the range choice, and it's simply not up to the mark. It has a reasonable bar, and in fairness the bed was comfortable. Its principal redeeming feature, however, is its location in midtown, but the hotel itself is second rate. Avoid.

title: “Not at all what a W should be!!”
text: Being an Starwood member since 1997 and having stayed at other W hotels including the one in Barcelona, my wife and I were very disappointed with our stay. Bad service, Louder than average music and smaller rooms being some of the examples. will certainly not return to W San Diego.

title: “Recent stay at Parker Meridien”
text: We recently stayed at the Parker Meridien after having not stayed there since it became part of the Westin chain. The hotel has really been upgraded and the accomodations were excellent, much better than when it was an independent hotel. We would heartily recommend this hotel.

title: “Expected better from a Hilton”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for business in late October. 
Before I arrived, I called to ask what transportation options were from BWI. My call was transferred and dropped several times by the hotel before I spoke to a representative, who seemed incredulous that I did not possess deep knowledge of Baltimore's transportation options. Short story: I told her I was arriving at BWI after 9pm on a Sunday, and she said I should take the light rail. Which stops running at 9pm on Sunday. 
Terrible sign, and things got worse from there! The front desk staff was rude. There was a pair of underwear in my room when I arrived, and the staff seemed to think this wasn't a problem of any kind ("Did you want us to send someone up to retrieve the underwear?"). 
I spent $1000 to stay here for several nights and found the whole stay deeply impersonal and, really, unkind. The room was average. One major pro: the fitness room has an unbelievable view into Camden Yards.

title: “Fantastic W Experience”
text: The W Chicago Lakeshore aims to Wow and that is exactly what they did. The service was Fantastic. The view from the hotel lobby bar that looks out on to Lake Michigan and at the Navy Pier is breathtaking. It is a great scene for those who are looking to meet people but also offers a quiet room to sleep when the party out last you. I highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Not a 4 star hotel by any stretch!”
text: I just got back from New York yesterday. No coffee pots in the room, yes you have to get dressed and go to the lobby to get coffee to read with the free Wall Street Journal! Cigarette smoke coming in through the vent, 1 set of towels for 2 people and don't bother listening to the time share presentation unless you are uber rich!! I won't stay there again.

title: “Great Location - mediocre everything else”
text:
We're San Diego locals and stayed over the weekend for a second honeymoon. This is a huge Super Walmart of a hotel...Made the reservations online and requested a room with a king bed with the option of upgrading to a suite at check-in time. Did the kiosk check-in, got upgraded and everything appeared to go smoothly. Walked into our "suite" and found it to be more like a conference room - with a small murphy bed - WTH? After several phone calls to the front desk, somebody finally came up with keys to an adjoining room...two twin beds. Of course, nothing else was available. 
The hotel is badly in need of remodeling and a deep cleaning. Our rooms had many, many stains in the carpet and almost all the furniture was stained and dingy. The breakfast buffet was OK, nothing you couldn't find at and Embassy Suites or Comfort Inn. The top of the Hyatt lounge has excellent views of the city and the bay from the 40th floor . Great desserts too. Worth a quick stop even if you don't stay at the Hyatt.

title: “What an amazing hotel!”
text: This is an excellent hotel for someone looking to enjoy the nightlife in San Diego. The staff is attentive to every need and my upgraded room was absolutely beautiful--a spacious one bedroom loft suite with an amazing bathroom. Yes, there are three nightclubs in the hotel so if you don't want to be part of the party--stay somewhere else. I can't say enough about the professionalism of everyone who works there--from the valet to the security men at the clubs. I can't wait to go back! And, by the way, if you think I'm a young hipster, think again--I'm a retired 62-year old professional who still knows how to enjoy a weekend in the city.

title: “I would return here”
text:
I am not a huge fan of LA in general, but the Intercontinental was a nice surprize. It had a fantastic location for the meetings that I had and I also used the hotel's Mercedes Limo service which really came in handy. Very courteous staff at check in and through out the hotel. With most arriving at all times from the east coast, the restaurant was utilized by most of our group and was very good. Very diverse menu and maitr'd and wait staff were very good. Breakfast buffet also a hit. Had a super room with balcony and workout facility was very adequate. 
PS: do not miss Parmesan Fries in restaurant.

title: “I loved this hotel”
text:
We were attending an event at the convention center, and did not want to pay downtown prices, so we looked for a hotel that was a bit further out. The Le Meridien was just fantastic. It took only 10-15 minutes to get to downtown and is directly across from the mall and several restaurants. It is also within walking distance to a movie theater. 
Our check in process was perfect. There is a constant "clean" smell as you walk into the hotel, and everything looks just very "crisp". Tony at the front desk made sure to take very good care of us. Our room was ready right away. When we went to our rooms, they were both just wonderful. There is nothing that I can think of to make them any better. They too were very "crisp and clean". While staying at the hotel. The handle on my shower needed to be repaired. It was done within five minutes of me informing the front desk. The hotel is very modern, and it seems that there is nothing that has been overlooked. There is free wi-fi throughout the hotel, and free computers in the lobby to use.
The staff made the stay. The would totally bend over backwards for the guests. We will stay here again for sure!!!!

title: “Would stay again”
text:
Just returned after a week in San Francisco for holidays, staying at the Donatello. Arrived early from Australia and given room very quickly, no questions asked. Evita at the front desk is fantastic. We had a corner room on the 9th floor (although appears to be no level 2/3/4, so not sure it really was 9th). Very spacious, well equipped. Fridge, microwave, wifi
Breakfast served in room, no onsite, so we ate at Pinecrest, Cafe Mason, David's Deli (including dinner at the last 2), all within a block. Good value for money, and very happy with the quality of food. American breakfast coffee is appalling - always filter coffee, topped up constantly, and just awful. We could not find anywhere that did genuine cappucino or latte with breakfast. Evita steered us to Encore cafe, diagonally opposite the Donatello, which did very good coffee, with a range of beans including Yergacheffe, Sumatran, Ethiopian, etc. Best coffee (and pastries) is in North Beach (Little Italy) at Stella Pastries on Columbus Avenue, where you can also access the wifi from Hotel Boheme next door.
Very easy access to and from SFO via BART to Powell and easy walk to Donatello. Everyone helpful, never any concerns for safety. We took buses everywhere - Haight Ashbury, Golden Gate, Golden Gate Park, Legion of Honour. These and the Cable Car just minutes away.
Biggest downside to this hotel - which I suspect would be the same everywhere near Union Square - is the street noise. We were then on Black Friday, and so a holiday weekend. Everyone seems to drive with one hand on their horn, and late night revelers seem happy to give a character reference to their friends at the top of their voice at 2am. Take ear plugs if you are a light sleeper. Otherwise just accept this is life in a big city and you will go back to sleep in the enormous comfy bed.

title: “Not great for biz travelers”
text: I arrived a little after 4 in afternoon and called the front dress to get my suit pressed for a meeting the next morning at 8. They told me that the hotel could not guarantee that the pressing would be done by then and told me to look for a dry cleaner in the neighborhood. Very disappointed in the hotel's inability to perform what seems like a basic service. Will stay elsewhere on my next trip to NYC.

title: “Parking was a nightmare!”
text:
We stayed at the La Quinta in Seattle for three nights. One of the reasons we booked this hotel was because it offered free parking in a secure garage with surveillance cameras... but that turned out to be a total nightmare!
On the second night of our stay, someone hit our rental car which was parked in the hotel's garage and left a huge dent. When we asked the front desk to see the footage from the surveillance cameras, we were told that the cameras only face the entrance, exit, and elevator, NOT THE CARS, so we were not able to identify the person who damaged our car.
On the third night, we weren't even able to park in the garage because it was completely full (they have very limited parking spaces, a whole lot less than they have rooms), so the front desk told us to park on the street until 10PM then move to the garage that belonged to the restaurant across the street from the hotel. This ended up ruining our plans for the night since we wanted to leave our car at the hotel and take a cab downtown.
In addition, on New Years Eve night people were throwing confetti canisters down from their balconies and hitting the cars parked in the handicap spaces below, right in front of the entrance to the hotel. They made loud thumping noises as they hit the cars and one of the canisters almost hit me. We told the front desk about it, and they said, "Yeah, we know. We just got a call about it." I doubt the hotel did anything about it cause those same people continued doing it all night long.

title: “Amazing location”
text: Location, location, location....We have been staying at the OB Hotel for the past 10 years and enjoy each stay. The staff is available to respond to any request and the accomodations are perfect for being 20 steps from having your toes in the sand.We just stayed there last weekend and I can't wait to go back with our dogs.

title: “Amazing service”
text: We had a long week of meetings and had looked forward to some relaxing time at the hotel. When we returned to the hotel we were first approached by so so service, but shortly after had a waitress that could not have been more accommodating. It is the simple things that make your stay worth returning for and this waitress went way above and beyond to our group. Her name was Daley P. Thank you Daley and we look forward to seeing you on our next visit...

title: “Great Location, Acceptable Accommodations”
text: The Millennium Hotel Broadway is in an ideal location for tourists. It is in the heart of the Times Square area and within easy walking distance of many attractions. Access to the NYC subway is just a block away. The accommodations are acceptable, but marginal for a 3 1/2 star rating. The hallways and rooms are a bit run down looking. The room was clean and everything was in working order. I would recommend Johns Pizzeria (44th st between 7th Ave and Broadway) for excellent pizza. There are a few inexpensive cafes on 45th street directly across from the hotel that are good for breakfast and lunch. Overall, if you plan to spend minimal time in the hotel this is a good choice simply for its location.

title: “Basic Clean Hotel - Well at least our stay was!”
text: Stayed here during the first week of December. Got a room for 3 people on the 14th floor, it had been renovated, with 3 single beds. It was clean and the cleaning staff were very nice. Location is just great. Room did get a bit cold though during the night, but we had a great view of The Empire State Building. This was our 6th time to stay at this hotel and lucky for us we have always got good rooms, sometimes the decor leaves a lot to be desired, but as long as its clean and lots of hot water in the shower, then its grand.

title: “Great Hotel with Great Service”
text: Stayed one night on business. Very welcoming staff checked me into a well appointed, very clean room. Staff was knowledgable about the area and recommended a great place close by for a Philly Cheese Steak. Wake up call was right on time the next morning so I was ready to get to my meeting. The hotel has a great location and I can't say enough good things about the staff. Everyone had a smile on their face and that's not the norm these days.

title: “Recommended”
text: Nice hotel, great location, friendly staff. The feature that is unusual is the free wine and beer from 5-7pm each night in their very cool lounge on 5th floor. We also had the Chef's Tasting Menu one night and that was very good.

title: “No thanks”
text: Stayed here for 4 nights, 3 of which were on points, and if this is how Hyatt rewards its frequent customers, the corporation is in trouble. My room was a cave, looking out at a large gray concrete wall. Very small. Hotel has a card on the desk stating they are "environmentally friendly" and if you want your towels and linens changed, to call the hotel operator. I did so immediately, and was transferred from one person to another and finally to the front desk, who noted my request. My linens were never changed during my stay. Room service breakfast trays were still on the floor in the hallway when I returned to my room in the evening. I was there for a meeting, so the location was convenient, but there is really nothing around for dining out without having a car. A really disappointing Hyatt.

title: “Great location, tiny room”
text:
The central location of this hotel made it ideal for this short trip with my Mom who has some physical limitations. Hence, the taxi rides from the hotel to all the major tourist sites were affordable and of short duration. 
The service provided by the hotel staff was good to excellent and we were happy about the daily breakfast buffet (included with room rate). Actually, 95% of the staff was very polite and helpful. The decoration of the hotel is very tasteful -- modern with an Asian flair. It has been recently renovated and everything looks new and up-to-date.
The only negative about our experience at the Sanctuary is the size, lighting, and thin walls of the room. This was my 4th trip to Manhattan, so no palatial hotel room was expected, but this was definitely the smallest hotel room I've ever stayed in (smaller than any European and/or American hotel room). The window looked out to a wall of the next building, giving the room a bit of a gloom and one could easily hear any guest passing by the room in the hallways.
I would probably not come back to the Sanctuary, since I've stayed in equally well located hotels, that offer more spacious rooms.

title: “Caveat Emptor: Cancellation policy is ironclad rip off.”
text: I had planned a trip to Indianapolis but it was cancelled. I notified this hotel (Candlewood) 3 weeks in advance and expected to be billed for the first day or for half the reservation. Instead, despite 3 weeks notice I have been told I will be billed for the entire reservation (almost $1,000.00). Then they can rent the same room to someone else for the full fee. Any alleged "discount" applied to the reservation was a total rip-off as far as I am concerned.

title: “Met all expectaions, and then some”
text:
I traveled Oct. 16-19 with 7 other friends/coworkers to New York City. I had checked prices on hotels for 6 months prior to the trip and found that this was the best deal, and the pictures looked great. We were very pleased to find that the pictures were acurate, The rooms were clean and beautifully decorated. There were no complaints on the hotel what so ever.
What stood out the most with the Four Point/Soho is the incredible staff. They were friendly and helpful and went out of thier way to make our stay more enjoyable. During the 4 days we were there we met many different employees, and they all were wonderful.
I will stay here again when i go back and I recommend it for anyone else.

title: “Overbooked and Banished to Katy”
text: Having booked and prepaid my three night stay at the Bradford-Galleria through one of the major internet services, I arrived at 8:30 PM in the evening after a four hour flight to be told that the hotel was overbooked (for which they blamed the internet service for confirming my reservation) and they claimed they had called around and the only room they could find was at their facility in Katy which was 22 miles away. I explained that I needed to be in the Galleria area for business over the next three days and I was not going to Katy. While I politely stated my case at least two other parties arrived and were checked in and not told the hotel was overbooked. Finally after 15 minutes of insistance on my part they told me I could go for one night to a neighboring hotel at a fair rate. When I arrived at the neighboring hotel I was booked into a room pre-reserved by the Bradford which told me that they were holding a number of reservations at the other hotel and had only told me that the only room they could find was in Katy TX to try to gain the benefit of my pre-paid reservation. I judge the entire incident to be extremely unprofessional and advise readers to keep my experience in mind when making reservations in the Houston Galleria area.

title: “Basic room, outstanding service”
text: I stayed here for one night on a business trip. The front desk agent, Henry Strait, who checked us in was great. Very professional and efficient. He even went so far as to adjust my hotel room rate so my business associate and I were paying the same rate. The rooms were older--a basic place to shower and sleep. The room was clean and so were the sheets. What stood out for me during this trip was the fact that the front desk manager (Ronzi?) noticed that the line for the women's restroom was long during our conference breaks and opened up an empty hotel room so there was a 3rd restroom available for our use. This hotel's service compared (even exceeded) some of the 5 star hotels I have stayed at. Great job!

title: “A new Marriott on San Diego Bay”
text: We had spent 3 nights with my 3 kids to visit Zoo, Sea World etc ..Rooms are big and quite newly decorated..Very quite ..Very much delighted to stay there

title: “Average, dirty, noisy, dated, still good value for location, but must be better out there”
text:
Stayed in this hotel in LA when we arrived in Hollywood hills with no plans. The service is ok, the reception alright. The rooms are a good size, but they are dated, furniture are ugly, a bit dirty, seriously noisy and the aircon sucked. But it was for one night only and it was cheap, so we sucked it up, and got on with it. It is in a good location for the walk of fame, Kodak theatre etc, which is highly overrated anyway, and also for Universal studios, so thumbs up for location. And free parking, thumbs up. 
This is a very average hotel that is what you expect when traveling cheap.

title: “Great Room, noisy & not the best location”
text:
The Hampton Inn in the Financial District is a newer property and features very comfortable rooms, nice bedding/linens, flat screen TV's mounted on the wall, and nice bathrooms. As far as Hampton Inn's go, this is a very nice property.
