The Service was excellent. There is a doorman, whose name escapes me, who was very helpful and had very good local insight. He gave us detailed directions to everywhere we wanted to go. The front desk staff and everyone else was very nice. 
The only negative was that the way the rooms were situated was such that all room doors on a floor opened into a common area - there was no hallway. So, if people are going out for a nightcap at 1,2,3am, you can easily hear slamming doors, cell phone conversations, etc...this is more of a "heads up" not a reason not to stay here at all. 
Also, the location was good for history buffs (wall St., financial area, 9/11 memorial area, south street seaport) but we didn't really find a whole lot to do within a short walk from the hotel. There were 2 subway stops close by, and both were easy to get to and made transport into mid/upper Manhattan easy. Just know that you're going to have to ride the subway or take a cab to get anywhere other than the few blocks around your hotel (chinatown/little Italy is about a mile walk - not TOO bad...) If you're OK with that, this hotel is an excellent and affordable choice (we paid $179/night over Thanksgiving weekend!) 
I fully recommend this hotel!

title: “great location”
text:
spent 5 days at this hotel wonderful location in the heart of Manhattan.the hotel it self is rather old and the rooms very small but it did not matter.the hotel is very busy the foyer a hive of activity.
the diner attached to the hotel is excellent for all meals and open 24/7. my only problem was that they do not supply any tea or coffee in the rooms but the Starbucks across the road is excellent with great service
The staff most helpful and and arranged for us a car to the port for our cruise

title: “Perfect hotel to enjoy downtown Denver”
text: Great hotel to walk to local sites, restaurant/bars, Denver Musuem of Art etc. Staff is very helpful. Our room was as if we had our own downtown condo, great to relax in and easy walk to anything. Perfect stay.

title: “Quite an enjoyable stay.”
text:
I arrived at The Holiday Inn-Fisherman's Wharf after a coach journey from Yosemite National Park.The hotel consists of two buildings,the Beach Street building and the Columbus Avenue building.I was allocated a room on the 2nd floor of the Beach Street building.The room was large and spacious with two double beds,wide-screen T.V,coffee/tea maker,iron/board and a safe deposit box.The en-suite was a good size with a plentiful supply of clean,fresh towels.
The rooms have complimentary Wi-Fi and there is a computer for guests use on the 4th floor,which during my stay ran very,very slow.There are two lifts in the Beach Street building and during my stay only one was working and it was,just like the computer on the 4th floor,very,very slow.
There is a coin operated laundry for guests use on the 2nd floor with two washing machines and two tumble dryers.There are also ice-making machines.The hotel has a 24 hour diner called 'Denny's'.I had breakfast on one occasion in 'Denny's' and it was a basic breakfast,just a bit expensive considering what was served up.I went elsewhere for breakfast for the remaining days of my stay.
As the hotel is situated in the heart of a very busy Fisherman's Wharf,many attractions are only a short walk away.All in all,I quite enjoyed my stay at The Holiday Inn-Fisherman's Wharf and would probably use again in the future.

title: “Nice hotel in bad location.”
text:
Not at all impressed with Jacksonville. The city is dirty and run down and all the restaurants smell like a sewer.
The hotel was friendly, nice, clean and comfortable and did a very nice job with the convention.
The pool on the roof was clean and comfortable. We were quite puzzled when the pool bar closed at 5pm when there were more people there than had been there all day.
All in all a nice hotel. Too bad it's in Jacksonville!

title: “Great hotel, great service, especially for readers”
text: I shared a junior suite with my 20-year-old niece. The room had a perfect view of the NYC public library in one window and another window offered a view of Madison Ave. Everything in the hotel was clean and well cared for. The hotel staff were friendly and helpful. Each room has a library theme (ours was "mystery" and our friends had "paranormal psychology"). I settled on a biography of the turn-of-the-century sculptur Jacob Epstein, which I found in the 2nd floor lounge/breakfast room. Other "pluses" for jet-laggers are 24-hour refreshments in the 2nd floor lounge and the roof-top lounge. The hotel also offered as a courtesy wine-and-cheese etc., from 5 to 8. We all liked this hotel very much, and the location was perfect with regard to visiting the major attractions and getting around town (just minutes away from the underground station at Grand Central).

title: “A perfect stay.”
text:
From arrival to departure everything was superb. 
The room was clean and spacious and the staff were just wonderful throughout.
There is a guided tour of the hotel, which was actually a really great experience. We learned a lot about the history of the hotel and got to see parts of the hotel you would not normally see as a guest, including the kitchen. 
I would happily recommend it and I would happily stay again.

title: “Did not seem like an "airport hotel"”
text: This hotel has been often reviewed -- accurately. I spent two nights with my daughter. It was her choice to stay at the airport because she had 2 huge suitcases + pillow, etc. (for summer school in VT) and did not want to haul her stuff into the City. It was a good choice. Getting into the City is (as others have written) easy enough: hotel shuttle to T stop and a short T ride to (wherever). We never waited more than a few minutes for the shuttle. We had a room with a great view of the City. The room was very comfortable (although lacking in cushy beds). The hotel bar/restaurant has (I suspect) recently been remodeled (the photo in the elevator is different from the actual place). If I were a solo business traveler, I would give it very high marks -- lots of space at the bar and then a second laptop friendly bar running the length of the bar. Starbuck is available in the lobby. One caveat: it is a long walk (almost, but not quite, a mile, I would guess) from Terminal E to the hotel.

title: “Good location and good service”
text: We chose the Castle Inn because of the location, the front desk upon check in where really really good, advising us of places to go, places not to go and tickets if we needed them. The hotel included parking and breakfast with coffee at reception throughout the day. Considering the price this hotel is above average in everthing!! The hairdryer did not work and I reported this to reception, this was fixed within the hour.

title: “Excellent location in downtown Seattle, service uneven”
text:
I just returned from a weekend away at the Grand Hyatt-Seattle. Here is my breakdown of the hotel.
Pro's-
1) Able to check in early, arrived at 12 pm and the front desk graciously let us check-in. She even had a smile on her face and was very professional
2) Ruth's Chris has a tremendous happy hour menu and is attached to the lobby of the Hyatt. Great place and SO much better than the usual hotel restaurants
3) The bathrooms are incredible. My room on the 20th floor had both a bathtub and walk in shower. 
4) The 32 inch LG LCD tv was a plus
5) The beds are very comfortable. (but not as great as the Marriot beds)
6) The concierge Scott was a good guy and very helpful 
Con's
1) Upon check-out, my friend asked the bell-hop to bring the bags out of the temporary storage to him. He brought the 3 bags to him while I was at the Concierge and it looked as if the bags were just dropped down in a reckless manner. Also, the porter didn't offer to help us with our bags to the cab and just went back to 'stand at attention'. The experience only affirms my belief that it's best to always handle your own bags at all times.
2) There were two staff members 'standing at attention' in the lobby, but NOT opening doors or offering to help you with your bags in a gracious way. I was reminded of the Vegas 'tip for everything' mentality rather than feeling that the staff was genuinely eager to help. I tend to appreciate when people are a bit more pro-active.

title: “Convenient Location but rooms not up to standard”
text:
It is a grest location for the city, a couple of minutes from Union square and the trams. Our room was a double standard room, but we found that the air con didnt work, the wall lights didnt work, the room was scruffy and poorly decorated, and dated.
The staff were ok, a smile would have been nice! 
The cafe and bar attached to the hotel, Joe's Bar, was great. I can recommend a good meal in there and reasonable cost.
If you want a hotel that is reasonably priced and in the city, but dont mind the chance that the room is not up to scratch, stay here.
Also, we were charged $32 a day to park there!!

title: “ideal for short stay”
text: staff were all very pleasant and helpful ...location is excellent this was my first time in New York so can't compare to other hotels etc.... after reading other reviews I was expecting a cramped room but was pleasantly surprised ... your holiday is what you make it will definately be staying here next time I visit

title: “Not So Great”
text: Weekend stay in Dec after Christmas was not so great. At reservation time was guaranteed connecting rooms w/ 2 queen bds per room. At check-in was told those rooms did not exist connecting - which was a problem since we had teens in the next room. We ended up on roll away beds. Not comfortable at all. Desk clerk was no help and basically did not care at all. The renovations are a joke. The furniture looked like the kind you screw together - very cheap. The bathroom door is a frosted glass door that does not lock so when you go in and turn the light on, your shadow can be seen by anyone that walks by - very uncomfortable feeling for my wife and sister. Basically, they tried, but missed by a mile. Used to love to stay there, but won't in the future!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

title: “Love the club”
text: When you visit SF, the Donatello is a place away from it all. Balcony club house, wine Fridays, superb concierge. Leopoldine is a person I trust as she's in the know. And staff in general here are great with impeccable service standards. Their restaurant has a night cap and live music as well.

title: “The best place to stay in San Jose”
text: My husband and I stayed here for a short getaway on our anniversary. THe location was accessible to the local wineries, and we couldn't have been happier with the accomodations. The hotel is right next to a park, which was a nice place to take a morning stroll. The hotel also provides tennis equipment if you want to play tennis on the park courts. The hotel has a nice restaurant, and provides coffee in the mornings. We got a great deal through the hotel with a weekend getaway package, but we would have paid more for such great accomodations.

title: “San Diego Family Getaway”
text:
We read some reviews before booking our stay at the
Pacific Terrace and found that it was probably one of
our better choices. It was one of the BEST Hotels that my family has ever stayed at...really, the BEST!
The staff was very friendly, professional and always 
ready with a smile. The room was clean and most 
comfortable to sleep in. The breakfast buffet had a 
variety of everything you need to fill a hungry tummy.
Having the Hotel on the beach was wonderful for our kids who loved going down to the water everyday. Thanks to the staff and we look forward to coming back
again.

title: “Great location for San Diego Gas Lamp Qtr”
text:
Spent 3 days at Hard Rock Hotel San Deigo on our last leg of our Californian vacation. The Gas Lamp Qtr is perfect if your into partying, pubs, clubs, restaurants and night life - Hard Rock Hotel is on The Gas Lamp qtrs doorstep. 
The hotels Roof Top bar on Level 4 is awesome. Definitely worth checking out. Try the Raspberry Mojitos. Delicious! 
MaryJanes restaurant and cafe is a great place for a breakfast, especially when you're hung over. pink Berry frozen yoghurt is just outside the hotel. This is yum!
The rooms were spacious and clean but very noisy. You could hear everyone in the corridors and whenever doors slammed shut. Our room looked down onto a court yard where weddings, functions and concerts were held. 
In all check in and check out was a breeze, valet staff were helpful and in all a pleasant stay. Would recommend and stay again.

title: “Stay away from here.”
text:
Inside of the room was okay, especially considering the price. However, the place looks like a ghost town. I think I may have been the only overnight guest of 105 rooms. The outside of the property is in disrepair. The building next to me had a constant pattern of different vehicles pulling up to one of two rooms, knocking at the door, going inside, and coming out in less than two minutes and leaving. Supicious to say the least. Also, a lot of people just walking through the property...past my door.
I left and found another hotel. I simply did not feel safe.

title: “Great location”
text: Visited NYC at end Nov04/beginning Dec04. Booked quite late so was limited re: hotel availability. Paid approx £950 for 5 nights in a double double on room only basis. Location was great: 1.5 blocks to NY Public Library & 5th Ave, 0.5 blocks to Grand Central Station, and within easy walking distance of both Time Square/Broadway and the Rockefeller Center. Room itself was large enough (suggest a double double room as min.), extremely clean and well decorated in a contemporary style. Hotel staff were extremely helpful. NB: the hotel has standard glazing and is only 2 doors away from a VERY busy freight entrance which has deliveries between 1am - 7am most mornings(!) so would recommend a room as high up the hotel's 16 floors as possible in order to avoid the noise and get a decent night's sleep. Would definitely recommend this hotel and stay there again particularly if rate was cheaper.

title: “disgusting”
text:
we booked an none smoking room, the reception agreed with that "unfortunately", there weren't any available. So I had to sleep two nights in a smoking room, wich was really disgusting. I asked 2 times at the reception if there really wasn't a non smoking room availeble but he sad there wasn't. 
The hotel is located in a scary enviroment, there are a lot of homeless people hanging around and sleeping on the streets next to the hotel.
I would definitely not recommed this hotel to anyone.

title: “SAD TO LEAVE”
text: Having never been to Texas, was not sure what to book. Of course, any time there is a JW,you know it will be fantastic. Having said that, this is far superior. From the minute you drive onto their property, you are impressed. To see the hotel on top of the hill is very inviting. The doorman, bellman, front desk people, concierge, all greet you with a smile. Our room was on the 4th floor, overlooking the golf course. It was amazing. The hotel has wonderful art work all over the lobby area. No detail was not addressed....can't say enough about it. HIGH VELOCITY (sports bar) is really something to see. The BIGGEST tv's you will ever see. Let's not forget the water park......it was not really busy when we were there, so finding a shaded seat was never a problem. All the lifeguards and people working the pool area are all very nice also. All in all, a great time.

title: “Great Location close to Times Square”
text:
We booked this hotel online. They had a special offer with 10% discount until end of February. Our stay was in the week were February ended. Through the website it was not possible to book further than February with the discount - I therefore had to "make up" our stay of two seperate bookings. To make sure that we wouldn't have to change the room in the middle of the week I emailed the hotel: no problem...
When we arrived our booking was recognised, but when I wanted to have confirmed the we wouldn't have to change the room during the week I was told that we would have to. I got a little annoyed and referred to my email, but they didn't have that anymore. After a few minuttes where we got more and more upset suddenly it was possible to change to another room category (upgrade) at no costs and the all was fine. Not the best start when you arrive (after an 8 hour flight). Nevertheless, the room was ok, spacious and very clean. The room was facing the street (3rd floor), but we rarely heard any noise.
The breakfast is a complete joke in this hotel. Other reviewers had noticed that as well. It would be better if they would reduce the room price with $5 or $10 and leave out the breakfast. We tried it a few times and had breakfast somewhere else most of the days.
Location if very good - less than 5 min walk from times square and many theatres. The hotel was ok - served our purpose. Please note that there isn't much infrastructure attached to the hotel (small fitness room - looked ok) - not much else.
If you're looking for a good central location and you find the rice ok, it's worth going for. However, I don't think we'll return...

title: “Handy to LAX, clean, dated”
text:
We've all been there - hours of travelling, delayed links, frayed nerves, and the last flight (in my case last Qantas to Syd) missed. It's 12.30am, I'm tired, airline staff are arguing about a hotel voucher, I am starting to sway on my feet and am most decidely over it. 
A quick call to the Hilton LAX and $120 later I leave them arguing, shuttle bus picks me up and soon I'm showered and sleeping and ready to tackle everything fresh the next day. 
For what I needed Hilton LAX gets v good marks - quick, efficient, easy to get to from a deserted LAX. Other positives: the lobby area is nice, there is obvious and friendly security at entrances, 24 hr room service and the L1 cafe is open 24 hours. 
The bed was comfy, extra blanket and pillow in the (very small) closet, room service quick and pleasant (note - gratuities already added), a 5pm check out for no extra charge, internet fast and staff were helpful and generally friendly esp reception staff.
The rooms however are very tired. No minibar, the drink machines only take $1 bills . Bathrooms small and plastic feel. No safe in room. TVs are old and not flat screen. Air con seemed a bit hit and miss with the temperature. No extra deadbolt on the door. 
About a $40 cab ride downtown, shuttle to LAX runs every 15 mins or so and both my drivers were lovely - helped other people with bags etc (of course, I had no bags). 
So thank you Hilton LAX for being there, for being reliable and for your check in staff and security who welcomed me late at night when I wasn't feeling the best. 
That said, I reckon a refurb is quite overdue. For the rooms, at least upgrade the TVs, see if you can compensate for the poor bathrooms with some other toiletries or more towels or some other touches, add a keyed minibar (even if just soda or one of those cheap move it and you've bought it models), update the room aircon controls to digital and a safe would be good places to start.

title: “Staff was not friendly”
text: Called to make reservation Person that answered the phone was rude asked for the manager was on hold for five min hung up and called the Hampton, this would have been my fourth stay will not be back

title: “I thought that it was just old”
text:
When I first walked into the lobby, it was dark and old. The carpets were old, the style was old, the reception area unassuming and nondescript. Then I found out that it was a landmark building built over 100 years ago. So, what do you get with a landmark building. The rooms were huge by any metro standard. The room's ceilings were high. The place is built like a fortress and you don't hear anything above you. I love that.
The hotel is not in the downtown area, about a mile south from all the action, but only a 1/2 mile south of the Inst. of Fine Arts. There is a nice tapas style restaurant on site. Service is a bit rushed, but food was better than most hotel restaurants. I didn't try the room service. There is a small Starbucks on site. There is a breakfast place 4 blocks further south (Yolks).

title: “Nice Hotel........but not up to SPG standards.”
text:
Booked this hotel on a discount website and was excited to experience a change from the Westin. Upon arrival we had to wait 10 minutes for a spot to park our car and unload luggage. There is no drive in/ pull in spot in front of this hotel, so if 4 cars are on the curb, you have to double park. A policeman pulled up behind me while I was unloading and told me to move my vehicle. Nice forward thinking Le Meridien!
The hotel was Ikea style Euro decore with a very friendly and chatty staff. (Noticed not one employee over the age of 30 our whole stay)
Check in was fast and easy and our room was located on a very scenic 9th floor overlooking the city / Love Park / Comcast Building. Great views.
Bed was comfortable but my wife and I noticed the absence of a featherbed or pillowtop mattress which proved to be very hard and firm. The pillows/ comforter was very comfortable though. Service staff were attentive and caring. We ordered breakfast room service 2 mornings and found the food to be well prepared and fresh. The rooms were very quiet and we noticed very little noise on our floor. (Possibly due to vacancies)
Biggest problem with this hotel is the location! Be careful walking around in this area at night especially through the park adjacent to the hotel. We were literally asked to give money from panhandlers and bums every 10 ft. I would never recommend walking this area alone if you are a female. 
Also to note..........cabs were noticeably hard to come by in front of the hotel. I don't know if this was due to the fact that the hotel had just opened 3 weeks prior to our stay or not. We did have a cabdriver comment to us that there was no pull in for cabs and that double parking made it difficult to pick up / drop off customers. Overall this is a 3 star hotel at best with a modern look and feel of an Ikea store that opened in an older brick building. Not Starwoods best foot forward.

title: “Great nights sleep, wonderful views...”
text:
We stayed here on the first night of our 6 night New England trip after arriving in on a 7pm flight, before collecting our hire car the next morning; and also on our last night in Boston prior to an 8.15am flight home.
The last time we stayed here was a few years ago, and knowing how practical the location is for sightseeing and also for flights, we did not hesitate in booking it again for this trip.
We did advance purchases on our room and got it for a great rate, and was upgraded to a Harbor View Room on our second night.
The terrace serves food, which is OK but not great. Th lobster Mac was a bit bland in taste and my linguini with shrimp was a bit overcooked. BUT the breakfast the next morning from the a la carte menu was superb. I had the Lobster Eggs Benedict, and hubby had the Lobster Omelette. Both were very tasty and beautifully presented and service on both dinner and breakfast was excellent. To be honest, we wished we had gone for something a little more simpler for dinner such as the Fish & Chips, but this was our first night in town and we wanted to try something special.
The breakfast buffet was $25pp, and our single dishes were $17 each, plus $4 for juice and $4 for coffee - not cheap, but the breakfast was the best of the trip!
The views from rthe terrace (and the Harbor View rooms) of the Boston Skyline are superb and we slept with our curtains open!
Staff throughout the hotel from the front desk to the concierge and his staff and the shuttle drivers are extremely friendly and helpful, with the front desk staff remembering me from our stay a few days earlier.
To get into town, you can catch the complementary shuttle bus to the T Station, or take the water taxi across to Rowes Wharf (adjacent to the New England Aquarium / 2 blocks from Faneuil Hall). It costs $10pp one way or $17 return.
We also went to Antony's Restaurant on Pier 4 on our last night, and a taxi from there cost us $17 via the undeground tunnel.
Rooms are comfortable and very quiet - you would not know you were staying at an airport location. The only small niggle is that they do not contain a fridge, but there is an ice-machine in every level.
We would not hesitate in staying here again!

title: “It was fine”
text:
Stayed a couple of nights for a convention in April. Convention rate of $219 per night + tax. The tax adds up to a total of 15.2% on top of the rate.Room was fine. 
Eat at the bar in the SoleFood 'lounge/dinner' on the first night. Overpriced in my opinion. The 'fish and chips' was small and poor. Not recommended. However, it's right in the center of Philly so you don't need to use the hotel facilities at all.
Convention went well and decent food in the convention. The gym was decent.

title: “Perfect for visiting OSU”
text: Yes, there are less expensive hotels in Columbus but none come close to the convenience of the Blackwell if you are visiting Ohio State University. The Blackwell is right on campus, near the stadium! This is the 2nd time I've stayed here with a child attending freshman orientation and nothing compares. For example, when there were no longer parent sessions, I walked back to my room and my son came and went based on the schedule for students. He's meeting with an advisor now while I relax with my laptop in my room. Even if you are not visiting OSU, the hotel stands on its own as a great place to stay. The room is spacious, with windows that partially open. Two large work areas, with a live plant that warmed the feel of the room, included convenient outlets for charging laptops, cellphones, etc. (No need to unplug lamps to use electronics like at some hotels.) A bedside iPod/mp3 player. Cordless phone. "Turndown" service that skipped the needless moving of pillows and went directly to providing chocolate and bringing ice without having to ask. High quality restaurant which I considered very reasonably priced for what I recieved. Breakfast buffet. No hassle extended checkout time. Some young staff have limited experience but compensate with a customer-service attitude that contributed to a very enjoyable stay.

title: “Outstanding overall with one glitch”
text:
This is one of the better urban Ritz-Carltons as far as public areas, rooms, and service, all of which were top-notch. The location is also wonderful for business travelers.
The gym, however, is unacceptable. As other reviewers have noted, it is cramped and surprisingly dark, and the equipment is fairly old. The size cannot be easily remedied, but the solution to the dreary darkness is, well, more lights. It shouldn't take years of study to figure this one out.
As an extremely frequent Four Seasons and Ritz guest, I would also note to the manager that, although responding to these reviews is admirable, he should avoid PR spin along the lines of "We think the city of San Francisco provides enough of a gym." If someone complained about your 5-star restaurant, would you respond that the city of San Francisco provides plenty of renowned restaurants?
Keep in mind that many of your guests are likely traveling West, which means they wake up earlier than they want. Going to your gym is one of the only things to do, so you should really ratchet up the quality.
That said, I would consider staying at this property again.

title: “Perfect Choice”
text: It was worth every $$$....Book Online you get a better rate. We stayed in the presidential suite on the 3rd floor, beautiful views. If you are going to do it...do it RIGHT! We picked the right hotel for our family. Walking distance to some GOOD food and shops. The staff was very friendly and my kids fav was the free cookies at 5:00.

title: “Mixed review after renovations”
text:
Nice style to the new rooms. Clean, comfortable and very modern. But as sometimes happens with this kind of refurbishment, form can win out over function. Drawer space is limited, the switches for the lights and shades are puzzling at best, and the time on the alarm clock was visible only when the lights were off (?!). Elevators continue to be a bit of an issue during busy times -- they are small and move slowly, and it's not unusual to have to wait, especially if you're on one of the lower floors served by that bank of elevators and it's the morning rush hour.
Overall, though, a perfectly fine hotel, with efficient service.

title: “Amazing Resort”
text: Had the pleasure of staying at this resort in September this year for business for 5 days. This place is big and can cater for up to 5 weddings at a time so can get very busy but there is plenty of space. The service is great and dining options very good. A championship golf course is attached which is in very good condition. The conference facilities are first class. Little attention to detail like hand towels, ear phones & mints in the Gym shows the quality of the place. They are about 30mins from SanDiego which is an $80 Cab ride so a resort bus would be useful to take guest into town a couple of times a day. All in all a great place to stay to relax, have a function/wedding .

title: “Super Small Rooms -- Great Location”
text:
I had stayed at W-The Court previously and loved it. So when my wife wanted us to return to New York but stay near Fifth Avenue, I -- without thinking -- booked a room at the W-New York. 
Without question, it's a **great** location.
But Be Warned: The rooms are SMALL. As in, when we opened the door to our room, my wife said, "You have got to be kidding me." It was (much) smaller than my dorm room at USC.
The Good: Service was good. Lobby was gorgeous. Bar had that cool W vibe.
Spa was only OK. I asked for a male therapist, and I wasn't very impressed. Plus, the decor was rather bizarre -- hard to explain...felt like I had done some really hard drugs or something. Or like I had entered The Twilight Zone. 
Gotta say, though: Location was terrific!

title: “Favorite DC hotel”
text:
My most recent stay was in April, but I've stayed at the Topaz several times before. This is my favorite of several hotels I've stayed at in DC.
The neighborhood is beautiful, a nice mix of leafy residential streets and quirky, unique shops and restaurants. I felt safe walking alone at night. Convenient to the red line Metro or a slightly longer walk to the blue/orange lines at Farragut West.
The rooms I've had have been generally spacious, with a sofa or chaise in addition to the usual bed, desk, desk chair, etc. The beds are plush and comfortable. Great Aveda toiletries and Mighty Leaf tea in the room (there is an electric teakettle instead of a coffee maker). The TVs have been old tube TVs, not new flat panels like some of the other places I've stayed, but oh well - there's HBO, at least.
Front desk staff has always been pleasant and helpful. (However, I'm a rather independent hotel guest, I haven't asked for any special assistance with making arrangements for transportation, etc., so can't comment on their capabilities there.)
I appreciate the quirky spirit and uniqueness of the Kimpton hotels in general, but especially the Topaz.

title: “Nice little hotel in a great location”
text:
I stayed at the Moderne during 19 November - 24 November 2003. For its price, it really cannot be beaten. It's in a great location - 10 minutes walk away from Times Square and 2 blocks from Central Park.
The hotel itself is clean and has some great decor - the bathroom is large and spacious and there is always hot water. A complimentary breakfast of bagels and coffee is provided, but there are plenty of diners nearby if this doesn't appeal.
The staff are friendly and helpful - the only problem I experienced was my key often didn't work, but this was quickly sorted with a quick trip down to reception.
McGee's is a great Irish pub just over the road.

title: “Great stay”
text:
My wife,daughter and two granddaughters enjoyed a two day stay while the granddaughters partipated in an Irish Feis. Our rooms were very clean and the beds were extremely comfortable. Our limited contact with staff, we were impressed with their friendliness.
We did not eat in the hotel but there appeared ample space for eating.
Our only suggestion would be to a microwave oven in the rooms, but that is because our granddaughters like to warm up food.
I would certainly recommend this place especially if you are flying in or out of Seattle.

title: “NEVER Again - 2 Star at Best”
text: What can I say??? The hotel room is dated. Feels like I'm in my grandmother's house that she doesn't tend to very often. Furniture and wallpaper looks right out of a 1970's. Popcorn ceiling. Feels so dirty. Carpet definitely is. Mad I didn't bring house shoes. TV Remote Control is even dirty & dusty. The bathroom fixtures are silver and gold and the original color was only one - and that's even hard to figure out which one was the original. Want to wash my hands after washing my hands. I have free wi-fi with my room and you would think when you check in that they will tell you what you need to do to connect - nada. I thought since it wasn't mentioned that perhaps they had instructions in the room - nada. Had to call down to the front desk when this basic information should have just been told to me upfront. Don't let the hotel lobby fool you (as it is nice (not fancy, but nice) - spend your nights somewhere else. The ONLY perk to this hotel is the fact that it's on the Metro line but there are zillions of hotels in DC - don't be fooled - stay somewhere else.

title: “A super clean, friendly hotel with great service and location!”
text:
We visited the Sofia in june-july of 2008 and we just loved it! The rooms are really nice, a higher standard than what we expected. It´s true that they are a bit small, but not too small either. The service was exceptional, the valet´s and the concierge was really helpful! We ended up renting and delivering a new car every day, that way we saved the overnight parking fees. The car rental (Rent4Less) picked us up every morning and dropped us off every night, perfect! The location is perfect, walking distance from the Horton Plaza Mall and the gaslamp district, but a bit too far from the beach. The Greyhound bus stop right next to the hotel has some shady people hanging around, but it was no problems for us.
Liked: Excellent service, good value, great rooms and amenities, free internet (business center).
Liked not so much: A bit far from the beach (which was our purpose of the trip).

title: “Great for Fun, Function is another story”
text:
The newly-rebranded Andaz San Diego is in the heart of San Diego's Gaslamp Quarter nightlife district, and is a destination for the cool and the hip. While the Hyatt-owned nameplate cometes with the established W brand, it does not feel like a copycat.
If you're on business or traveling with family, there may be better options in downtown, but if you are single or a couple, it is definitely worth a visit. The rooftop pool turns into a rocking bar at night, making the hotel lobby feel more nightclub than hotel, and there can be noise from other bars and clubs in the neighborhood.
A warning to anyone traveling with non-romantic interests: the Andaz has showers are all-class boxes that open into the bedroom, so there is no privacy.
On the positive side, soft drinks, snacks and wifi are complimentary, and they do put the hotel guests first.

title: “Fantastic Place, Fantastic Location, Fantastic Staff”
text:
We stayed at the Affinia Dumont from 15th to 18th May in Room 3103. After requesting a view of the Chrysler Building from a high floor, we were not to be disappointed and had spectacular views of the building. We could also see the Hudson River which was a bonus. If it hadn't been for previous reviews on Trip Advisor we wouldn't have requested this room and would have missed out on a treat. We were also left a complimentary bottle of wine which I presume was down to us celebrating Birthdays / Wedding Anniversary while we were there.
From a location point of view, it couldn't have been better. 10 mins walk and you could be at Grand Central Station in one direction or virtually Times Square in another. The Empire State Building was only a 5 minute walk along 34th Street. We didn't go up the Empire State and elected to go for the Top of the Rock - this was only a 10-15 minute walk away and didn't have the horrendous lines the EPS had - it also gave a fantastic view of the empire state itself and great views of Central Park.
Everything within the Hotel was great and the front desk staff were genuinely friendly and made you feel wanted from the moment you stepped foot in the place (larger chains should take note)
This was our first stay in NYC and we loved the place. We do want to return next year and on the basis of this visit would only consider booking the Dumont.

title: “It would be a crime to stay anywhere else!”
text: My company suggested I stay at Jurys on a recent trip to Boston. What a surprise. For an Irish Hotel, I was picturing shamrocks and Leprechauns. What I got was a funky, upscale, fantastic experience. The colors and textures they used throughout the hotel were quite impressive. Love the staircase! My bed was very comfortable and loved the mattress and sheets. Stanhope Grill was great and I was glad they have outdoor seating. Would definitely go back again as I find other hotels in the Back Bay either really too big or quite stuffy. It’s located in the old Police Station. Definitely a crime to stay anywhere else!

title: “Great for a drink, Terrible for a workout!”
text:
A typical Marriott, bland and typical of corporate America.
Check in superb.
Staff wonderful and very helpful.
Food at breakfast was good although service was poor for a USA hotel and we were not offered water or juice until we asked.
The gym or fitness room was exactly that! A room where you could do fitness but the equipment was old and the room drab.
Go for a run by the bay rather than waste your time potentially injuring yourself on old potentially dangerous gym equipment.

title: “Great Location”
text: My sister and I went to New York City right before Christmas and stayed in this hotel. The location was great and close to major attractions like central park and times square. Its a good value and great location for your typical average hotel.

title: “Near San Francisco Airport Best Stay”
text: we were looking for an close, easy and not compromise quality on our trip, the Hyatt Regency was a very good choice, the location, service, quality and courtesy met our expectations (although avoid memorial day week-end - they have a game convention there and is "busy") but not disturbing

title: “Excellent customer service”
text: I have traveled to the Dallas area several times over the years for business and the southern hospitality is generally okay. However, I was first greeted by Leshawn who was the customer service agent at the front desk. She was really nice and very helpful. She gave me really good ideas that helped me to explore the culture of Dallas. She provided great restaurant referrals, tourist sites, etc. I love it when the first person at any establishment is pleasant and helpful. By appearance only, this wasnt the best Sheraton that I've experienced, but, since customer service is so important to me, the four star rating is well deserved. I look forward to returning.

title: “Horrible,Stinky,Worst hotel ever”
text: This is really the worst hotel i stayed in ever when i entered the room it smelled so bad,bath room was the worst part very dirty, carpet was sticky bed sheets had spots on them and the mattress box had holes in them and were open there was no sheet or bed skirt on them i did'nt sleep almost all night because i was scared that any bug might come out of the holes ,there is a train crossing so you can hear honkings of the train at almost 2 o clock and again at 4 or 5 o clock,i wo'nt recommend this hotel to any one because it was the last day of my vacation and we did'nt plan to book this hotel they also charged a lot of that stinky room ,and our last day was ruined and it is not even close to river walk.Believe me book anther hotel if you want to enjoy and sleep well.

title: “Great value convenient for work location”
text:
Great nightly rate. Stayed 2 nights for work. Free Internet since I'm a Gold member, saw that was a previous complaint. Got warm cookies upon check in and it was a quick process. The food at the restaurant was average and average price. 
Only complaint is that there are not nearly enough channels on the TV, that was a major disappointment.

title: “Elegant airport stay”
text: The hotel, restaurant and bar were modern yet comfortable. The beds were soft and each had a variety of pillows for varied firmness. The bathrooms had showers and soaking tubs. The biggest downfall was no ear plugs in the room. My second night I heard planes quite frequently and could have used something to block the sound. This was a great hotel for business travelers needing to access the outskirts of town. The biggest downfall is having to valet your car as the only other option is to park and take the shuttle in from short-term parking.

title: “stayed for a business trip and plan to go back!”
text: I stayed at this hotel during a business trip. While I did not stay for long, just 2 nights, I really enjoyed my experience. The rooms were spacious and extremely clean! I encountered Brady Guerrero who helped me out with finding a nice place for me to go eat. I traveled alone and wanted to go some place quiet. Definitely one of the best hotels I've stayed at.

title: “An amazing staff...”
text: My husband and I stayed at Casablanca Hotel during our last trip to New York. We usually do not stay in Times Square but decided to give it a try. We booked one night at Casablanca and I wish we could have stayed longer. From the moment we arrived, the staff was friendly, helpful and professional. They have a wine and cheese event between 5 and 8 that was really impressive. In addition, they have a wonderful continental breakfast that would have run us over $40 if we had gone out. I was impressed by the size of the bathrooms and found the beds (and sheets) to be so cozy. The whole vibe was so laid back even with the craziness of Times Square out the door. We would definitely recommend and will stay again!

title: “Great Hotel, Recommend to anyone”
text: Check in was quick and easy, valet parking was painless. Had a 2 room suite and the room was clean and pretty big. 2 flat screen tv's in suite. Staff was friendly and always willing to help answer any questions. Location was not the best because there is not much around it but they do have a shuttle to shuttle you back and forth if needed and it seemed to be always readily available. Would recommend this hotel to anyone staying in the detroit area.

title: “I would not reccomend this hotel ever!!!!”
text: This is not a friendly place to stay. After making reservations months in advance,my husband and I enter our room only to discover that they gave us a queen size bed when I had requested a king. So we hauled our lugage back down to the front desk. I told the employee about the mistake and he told me that there were no more king size rooms avalible. I told him that I wanted the room I had made reserations for(I had a confirmation #) or a discount on the room that was given to us. After talking with a manager(via phone)I was given a key to a king size room(I thought that they were none left). No one apologized to me. The room itself was clean but small. I would not stay at this or any other Red Roof Inn again.

title: “Fantastic stay in downtown Memphis”
text: We visited memphis last September with our Two Children ( age 10 + 13) and wanted to start the holiday in comfort, so after looking at various hotels decided to book the Peabody as they had a special offer for the days we were staying. We booked a family room ( Two double beds) with a Peabody Club package. The room was quite large with plenty of room for a family with two older kids sharing - and had a sofa and sitting area at one end. The beds were so comfy ! The bathroom was great and even had TV in the bath with little duck shaped soaps and duck chocolates, Peabody Water, dressing gowns in fact everything your wanted and more. The views from the room were great overlooking downtown memphis and the Mississipi. We had exclusive, private-access on the concierge level. We had valet parking inclued and comlimentary drinks and evening snacks and breakfast included in the morning with tea, coffee anc cold drinks. The atmosphere in the hotel is great and of course the duck parade was special, the shops in the hotel are excellent and the piano bar area had great atmosphere.. The kids said this was one of the best hotels they had been to and wanted to stay longer. The trams stopped just outside and we enjoyed a tram ride quite late at night to see the sights, it felt really safe. It is within easy walking distance to Beale Street. The kids also had sole use of the indoor pool and jacuzzi whilst we used the gym ( you can watch them while you jog!) Although I would not say it is cheap at $280.00 per night ( and this was a special offer) we thought it was worth every penny and I would have no hesitation in recomending this hotel to my friends and family as a must.

title: “It'll do for a backup”
text:
I stayed for 5 nights on a business trip at the end of October. For a Marriott brand, the hotel just delivers enough. The lobby is newly remodeled and is pretty. There is no Marriott Rewards concierge level or members' lounge. The standard king bedroom is fine. It's a bit dated with the usual corporate Marriott touch. So it's not going to be a turn-on or turn-off to many people. The bed was comfortable. There was plenty of space in the room. The bathroom was not very large but had just enough space. I just hate the Marriott basic toiletries and am openly begging them to change to something that is not orange smelling. The WiFi speed was very good.
The #30 bus stops right outside the hotel which is a big plus since you can never count on having taxis at the ready outside the hotel. The In-n-Out burgers is a short walk away too!
This Marriott falls behind the nearby Sheraton hotel. That Sheraton would be my preference when staying in Fisherman's Wharf.

title: “Good Convention Stay, Excellent Management”
text:
Hotel is two blocks from Convention Center and only a $5 - $10 cab ride from most major institutions and attractions. Room was totally clean and comfortable and well stocked with towels and toiletries. The breakfast in the morning is the best I've seen when it comes "free" meals. Dining area was clean and cared for by a very nice young lady who was very attentive.
The General Manager of this hotel deserves special mention. S/he has clearly trained staff to understand the importance of guest care and they are a great leader because all of the staff were just terrific! I did not inquire who this person was but I hope someone at Hilton sees this note and promotes them.
The air conditioner made a little noise but boy did it work. Nice and cool in a very hot city.
Will gladly stay here again, a very well run property.

title: “Go with a Suite or dont go at all”
text: Terrible value. Initially reserved a harbour view room. Arrived in room and it smelled terrible, bathroom was disgusting and staff was slow to respond. Changed to a junior suite and what a difference. Furniture is dated but the bathroom was bigger than the prior room. Wonderful amenities and great space. Still overpriced, but the stay was pleasant and the location was excellent.

title: “Simply perfect”
text: I spent a week in this hotel with my wife in September 09, and we loved every moment of our stay. Staff was extremely helpful. Our room was excellent, very spacious, well equipped and everything was brand new. Also, location was great, close to cable cars, department stores, bus stops and lots of restaurants and shops. I would definitely come back to Donatello in my next trip to San Francisco.

title: “A Solid value in the Hilton Lineup”
text: This was my first time at an Embassy suite and overall I was impressed. This hotel brand seems nicer than Hampton Inns but not as fancy or service oriented as Hilton so it is sort of the middle of the Hilton lineup. With that said, this equates to a solid stay at a good value but not as fancy or expensive as Hilton or Hilton garden. Free parking is great and fairly close to the back entrance. Covered parking is a real plus especially in winter and bad weather. Valet is available but not pushed on you like at Hilton/Hyatt. Bell service is also available but most everyone just uses a cart. Again, nice because it is there but I did not feel forced to use it or to have to tip three people before getting to my room. Front desk is small but not busy during checkin, though I wonder if they get slammed sometimes with only two terminals. Front desk agent was average. She was quick, but was not overly friendly and was inaccurate on two questions asked about the hotel. I like agents that engage me about my trip, present info about the hotel and offer to help, which was all lacking. Not a deal breaker but not as polished as Hyatt/Hilton. Hotel is laid out well on the lobby level with breakfast, manager's reception and pool/fitness all on one floor. Manager's reception is great, Nice selection of beer and wine and great nacho's/salsa and eggrolls. Bartender was very quick to get more wine when she ran out and white zen hit the spot. The reception was a great way to relax after a long ride and now I expect this of all hotels. The room on the 10th floor was away from elevator as requested however the hall was very noisy all the time with one room having like 8 people. I am not sure how they enforce room occupancy, but it seems easy to sneak in tons of people, a real weakness of the suite only format. As a silver VIP, I expect my quiet room request to be taken seriously even if it does inconvience housekeeping by moving me to an emptier floor. The suite/living room was a nice size. New furniture and two flat screens were all appreciated. Desk with four chairs is also great and makes it easy to eat and watch TV. The bed I ordered was supposed to be a king, however it was a queen?? Do I have to upgrade for $9 per night to get a king bed?? This was a bit surprising as a VIP member but for one night I managed. As far as cleaniness, the hotel is pretty new so no signs of wear, however in the bedroom behind the nightstands were trash and food particles. The noise from the hallway was loud all night and when watching TV in the living room, it was distracting, however the bedroom has a separate heavy door and it really helps eliminate all noise from the hallway, which is super important to light sleepers. Room service was pretty quick and I had a "wedge" salad which was awesome and a good value and a club sandwich which was average but prepared fresh. It could have used pickles. Fruit cup was also very tasty and healthier than the usual side of fries. Bathroom was average with small tub and shower, no curved shower bar and just a few basic amenities, not the deluxe spa stuff and toothpaste like at Hyatt/Hilton. Also just one sink, not two sinks or a vanity mirror or special lighting like at the higher end brands. In the morning, the breakfast buffet was awesome. Omelet station and a huge selection of items much like golden corral and free to boot, can't beat that anywhere. It is probably the best breakfast I've had outside of a hotel room package which we all know are not free but included in the price. I also got a gas card at checkout. This is a valero gas card so you have to use it at those stations so if you are from a different state this might not be worth it. Overall, it is a solid hotel at a great value price in the $100 range Lastly, the heated pool was nice, though a little small. It can handle about ten people at a time max, but it was not crowded when I went down there. The hot tub holds about five people and it also was not crowded. The business center is also stocked pretty well, though I am not sure about the rates or if there is anyone there to help you. Yes, there are plenty of $50-85 hotel rooms in Houston, some of those suites, but for a few dollars more you get a new hotel, good service that is not overbearing and a good location. I researched a lot of hotels before choosing this one and I agree with most of the other reviews. If you are more of a business traveler the Hilton garden or Hilton may suit you more, but as a leisure guest this was a chance to relax while in the heart of a huge city. There are fancier hotels but not at this price level. Hilton is $20-25 more per night at least. I will probably return as this is a safe solid bet, and I don't think I want to stay at another hotel that doesn't have a manager's reception and a great breakfast. Are you listening Sheraton?? If you want a lot of service and polish and demand excellence, skip this one and pay up for Hyatt or Hilton.

title: “Great Stay”
text: Loved this hotel. Very close to the Broadway and all the action. Hotel was clean and quiet. Bedding was great. We especially enjoyed our "corner room" with five huge windows looking out across Manhattan. Staff was pleasant and helpful. We highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Marvelous stay, within a budget, Great Service recieved”
text:
I stayed in Edwardians San Francisco for two nights. The location is really great, withing a trolley (city car, called in SF) you will be to reach almost attractions in Sand Francisco bay area, it is located on Market street, which the name is representing the location.
The hotel itself is in an old European style, which I always dreams to stay. The service is great, even after check out time the hotel has provide service. Clean rooms and old fashion decoration of them are memorable.
Two guys working there, Ami, and David are quite nice to me, so I will advise all those visitors on Sand Francisco if they like to stay on Budget and receive a quality service, do not miss Edwardians.
Next time visiting SF, I will choose Edwardians, for their nice hospitality and friendly environemnt.

title: “Nice, but confusing Hotel”
text:
Stayed at W Time square for work back in end of Jan. It's a very nice hotel and the best of it is, Location, location, location. Hotel is new, very nice service.
Price: Can't really complain about price since it is business trip. But for W at a centralize area like this it's not bad.
Hotel: The lobby is confusing!!! There are 3 elevators from Ground to Lobby, then another 4 elevators from lobby to rooms. Honest one thing that I can complain is you don't need your room key to get into the elevator, which is kinda, Ahm.. not safe? This security feature kicks in after 10 PM I think.
No gym, free internet, etc and bottle of water there cost you 8 bucks. Watch out on your bill since my colleague didn't drink the water but she got charged somehow. She had to call the hotel to get that fixed.
No complain what so ever with this hotel; in fact I am going back tonight. Room is chic, location is great...I am looking forward to it.

title: “Small rooms, smaller bathrooms”
text:
I booked this room via Hotwire as a 4 star hotel. It was anything but.
The staff was very friendly and the location is amazing, but there is no way that this is a 4 star hotel. The room was tiny and the bathroom was so small that if you sit on the toilet your knees are in big trouble if someone opens the door. It is far and away the smallest bathroom I have seen in a hotel that claims to be 4 star.
If you need a good location and can book the room at a low enough price go for it. Otherwise check out a better downtown hotel with an equally great location... There are a lot of them that won't break the bank. Like The Magnolia or The Hyatt.

title: “Westin Galleria updated modern design comfortable and clean 4 star”
text: We stayed at the Westin Galleria over Valentine's weekend for my 5 year old daughter's birthday. The Westin Galleria is conveniently attached to the Dallas Galleria (shopping mall) which has an indoor skating rink and lots of places to eat and shop. Across from the front of the hotel, just through the parking lot, is the almighty and coveted American Girl Place...yes, the epicenter of many little girls dreams of overpriced historical doll characters with marketing that has been so successfully accomplished that even we own several of them. Since this review is of the Westin, however, I will stick to the hotel features. The front desk check- in was fabulous. Our room was on the tenth floor, with a large window seat that is 5 foot in length, it overlooked the highway system with cars and city lights. The noise level was zero-we were up high enough so there was no street noise. The kids LOVED that view. My son loved those cars. Even though our room was right near the elevator "lobby" of the 10th floor, there was no annoying "beeping" sound (I am very sensitive to noise). The room looked like it had just been updated. Modern lines, of course the two queen heavenly beds, granite bath counter, new shower/bath stall. Very clean and well done. There was lots of activity at the hotel this weekend (Valentine's)-the lounge and restaurant were hopping. The pool was under construction-we looked at it-it is on an outdoor patio on the roof of the fourth floor. A large rectangular shaped pool-suppose to be open "this spring". My son bout a Reeses peanut butter cup at the hotel store and he paid $3.00 for it (yikes). There are refrigerators in each room (stocked at a price). We also visited the Dallas children's museum and history museum at this visit-they are mediocre. We frequently stay at Westin hotels and this is definately one of the nicer ones. It was very well done, clean and modern lines, friendly staff, comfortable room, great view and location, I would stay here again. Reasonable price for a four star in Dallas.

title: “LOVE IT!”
text:
First off we had a double. They are spacious, TV's in each room and clean. The STAFF was OUT of this WORLD! I was there 31 days and the staff and management were so helpful and friendly, I felt like I had the greatest neighbors ever. I almost did not want to go back home. 
As for person who wrote NOT to say here because of CostCo. I had a room on that side. I never heard any sleep distractions whatsoever. Who knows? Maybe he had his window open and he's a very light sleeper. I am sure if he/she asked they would gladly have given him another room. 
I HIGHLY recommend the Marriott Stone Oak.
Di Haman

title: “A classic in Seattle”
text: 3rd year in a row staying here, nice size room good amenities and excellent staff from valets to concierge to lounge staff. Buffet at the hotel was outstanding maybe a bit pricey but selection and quality of food was excellent, great service in there as well. Hotel is in a very good location with everything you need within an easy walk. Would definitely recommend it to anyone staying in Seattle.

title: “Just Okay...”
text:
First off, got a great rate through Priceline, so I can't complain too much. But, next time I come, I will definitely find somewhere else to stay. Too many choices in New York to stay here again.
Service was excellent! The lady at the front desk was very helpful and polite, and there were more than enough people around to help with bags and such. Service is defintiely their strong point from my perspective.
However, the room I had on the 19th floor was not a gem. It seemed much more like and old dorm room wiht a view modern touches than a hotel room. The woodwork and bathroom was very nice and looked updated, but otherwise the paint looked old and dingy, the carpet was in poor repair, and the beds were not very good. It seemed like they tried to toss a few new items into an otherwise old room and call it good. I was left thoroughly uninpressed.
I moved to The Benjamin later in the trip and feel that it far surpassed the Le Parker.

title: “Great Place! Concierge was fantastic, great suggestions!”
text: We enjoyed our stay here. Room was excellent. Eric Hanson at the concierge desk had fantastic meal suggestions for the area A1- Job!

title: “Use only if you are on the tightest budget”
text:
I booked two rooms at this property very last minute due to a family emergency. I will never use again. My family stayed in one room, and my brother's family stayed in the other room. The rooms were dank and dreary, desperately needing a paint job. I understand that Motel 6's are barebones, no frills accommodations, but this failed to meet even that expectation. "No frills" should include, at the minimum, cleanliness.
In the middle of the night, I heard a loud thud come from my brother's room. In the morning, I come to find out that the supports underneath his box spring had collapsed, leaving the bed at an unusable angle. At that time, they were fast asleep, so it was a very startling way to wake up. His wife is sight impaired, and didn't want people in her room in the middle of the night, so they decided it was easier just to finish their night's sleep on the floor. 
In the morning, my brother asked me to go to the front desk with him so that he could report the bed. When he told them the problem, the clerk thanked him, called the maintenance man, and proceeded to charge him the full rate. My brother reminded him that the charged rate should include a functional bed, but the clerk said he had no way of adjusting the rate or compensating him. We left somewhat frustrated, concerned that a large company like Motel 6 did not afford its employees flexibility to make their customers happy.
Consequently, in the future, I will only stay at the newest Motel 6 properties.

title: “Outstanding Experience”
text:
We recently booked a city-view room for our vacation. We were extremely pleased with our stay. The staff were courteous, helpful and warm beginning with check-in. Our room was very large, updated, clean, and bright. The decor was inviting, having both modern and traditional touches. Views of the city were nice but not facing any particular SF landmarks. Our bed was extremely comfortable. Water pressure in the shower was excellent. The only downside with the room was the lack of soundproofing around the door to the adjacent room. While we could only hear muffled conversation, it still felt slightly awkward. The pool and hot tub were both small, but clean. 
We loved being located on Nob Hill. A beautiful park was directly across the street, as was Grace Cathedral. The hotel is centrally located and several neighborhoods are easily walkable. We generally took a taxi back in the evening after long days and filling dinners, although those more athletic travelers might prefer navigating uphill to return home. 
We would definitely choose The Huntington Hotel for a return trip to San Francisco. 
FYI we are told the repairs to the California St. line will be done by the summer. Seeing cable cars go by the hotel would have been icing on the cake, although this should not at all affect your decision to stay here.

title: “good location for 1st NYC trip”
text:
biz travelers will be disappointed by sub-standard decor and outdated rooms, tourists won't care because they're exhausted from their days of exploring the city
Pros:
- Location: walking distance to Times Square, Broadway shows, Top of the Rock, 5th Ave shopping, Central Park, etc proximity to 3 subway lines
- price: since most agree the hotel's rooms and decor is outdated, one should have paid less than other comparably located hotels
Cons:
- no major complaints, did not spend much time in the hotel
- this should go without saying, but don't eat anywhere near the hotel (unless it's from a food cart or pizza by the slice), you're overpaying for crap tourist food

title: “Small footprint, Big impression”
text:
We stayed at the Distrikt for a week long tour of NYC. Trip Advisor reviews were spot on. This is a great property tucked into the heart of Manhattan amidst the hustle and bustle of real urban daily life. Growing up in a city and living in the country for the last many years, walking out the lobby door on the first morning was a rush of excitement. If you can swing it, stay on an upper floor where the views and panorama will make you forget about turning the TV on. Reviews of the quality of rooms is correct. Coffee is pretty good and you can't beat the free WIFI. Tube station is a short walk up the street. There is a Dean &Deluca coffee shop a block away for a quick bite. 
There are plenty of nice hotels in NYC. The Distrikt won't give you the sidewalk glitz and superficial glamour many NYC hotels show. The Distrikt lobby is tiny. But, the Distrikt is special.

title: “Great hotel, excellent value for money, would definitely recommend it!”
text: We booked the Strand for a special celebratory 60th birthday visit to New York and were very impressed. It's ideally situated - very close to Empire State Building etc. Rooms were small but very clean, comfortable and well furnished - the most comfortable hotel bed I think I've ever slept in! Breakfast being included was a bonus and it was very good. Some Trip Advisor reviews complained about polystyrene cups but this was a very minor issue - lids were supplied for take-out too if required! The rooftop bar on the 21st floor was very expensive but well worth a visit at least once for the spectacular views of the Empire State Building lit up at night. All in all, a fantastic trip and we would recommend the Strand Hotel to anyone visiting New York.

title: “Great hotel next to White House and Smithsonian!”
text: Just came back from D.C. where we had a wonderful Thansgiving holiday at this very comfortable hotel, steps away from the White House and from the Smithsonian. Very nice room on 8th floor with a view of Washington monument! Wonderful bed, firm yet very cushiony...A real delight! Ask for a room far from elevators as you can hear everyone chatting loudly as they walk past your room ( the door is not noise proof ). Paid only $150 for the room by calling directly the hotel. A true bargain! The gym room is great, as well as the sauna, and they are opened till 11pm. The pool is nice for families only, as there are many kids playing and jumping in it. Breakfast buffet at the JW Marriott is $25 but quite good. Breakfast at the Willard hotel across the street is just fabulous! The Corner Bakery next door is much cheaper ($7 for scrambled eggs, but do go there only if you like your scrambled eggs cold, or warmed in a microwave!!!)

title: “My favorite NYC hotel”
text: I've stayed in Radisson three times and plan to come back again. The location is within a reasonable walk from Central Park and the Times Square. Bloomingdales is within a 10 min walk up the Lexington Ave. I stayed in standard and superior rooms (got an upgrade!) and there was more than enough place for me (ask for the top floors, almost no street noise is heard there). The bathrooms are clean and there you will find shampoo, soap, body lotion, hair dyer, etc. I was also lucky to get a good view from my windows. Internet access is a bit pricey (app.USD15 for 24h), but there is free wi-fi in the lobby. Personnel is friendly and professional and make you feel welcomed right after you step out of the taxi in front of the hotel. Also, when planning your budget keep in mind that the hotel reserves a deposit (app. the cost of a two nights stay) on your credit card when you check in. The money is released from hold when you check out or within app. 2 weeks if you have an international credit card (it depends on your bank though). From JFK to hotel expect to pay app.55USD and 30USD from La Guardia.

title: “OK dated hotel nothing offensive but probably won’t return”
text:
I had always intended to stay at 3 hotels either side of a conference at Microsoft in Bellevue so I could see which one I wanted to stay at on my next visit. I booked my first night at the Mayflower Park as I needed an address for the visa waiver form, however I had to move rooms as soon as I arrived due to noise, despite requesting a quiet room on the booking and again during the check in. The second room was adequate however it faced the street so there was some noise and the room was fairly small, dingy and rather dated in a shabby kind of way rather than quaint. The TV was very small and looked about 20 years old with poor fuzzy reception and poor range of channels. I did not try the restaurant so cannot comment on this. On a positive note the hotel is in a great location which would be difficult to beat.
In short the hotel is ok however it was not a tough decision to try another hotel and I would not stay at the Mayflower again unless my first choice (The Vintage Park) was not available.

title: “what a view - great staff - great hotel”
text: Ok - it is an older hotel but we were given a renovated room on the 22nd floor. The hotel does have that old smell to it...they should see about that. The room was lovely and all upgraded bath items. The view from the room and from the bar on the upper floor was fantastic. A nice walk to the downtown area and we had no trouble finding our way around. Parking is $28 a night and the drinks at the bar a bit pricey, but the view at night is wonderful. Staff were very friendly and helpful. I would definitely recommend this hotel for adults who want to see downtown Seattle.

title: “Old school Boston charm, great location with limited downside”
text:
Stayed here for a graduation weekend in Boston. Was a little concerned because the room rate was so good, reviews on this site weren't stellar, and my brother (who lives nearby in the Back Bay) had heard nothing about this place. We ended up having a nice stay, the room was not huge or especially modern, but certainly clean/pleasant. All of Boston was basically at out disposal, most of the major sites being within walking distance. 
The service we had at the hotel bar/front desk/valet service was good. I definitely enjoyed the old world look/feel of the building and lobby. We would definitely go back.

title: “Wonderful Wonderful Wonderful!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!”
text: My daughter & I spent 5 nights in August at the Sofitel New York. It was our 1st trip to NYC and I can’t imagine it being any better at any other hotel. We hope to return next year and I will stay at the Sofitel New York again. I can’t say enough about the staff, the location and the city. I want to go back ASAP.

title: “The wrost hotel, ever!”
text:
They have five elevator shafts, and it seems only two of them are working at any given time. You are waiting for at least 5 minutes for every elevator ride. And they are small - seven adults max. After 5 minutes of wait, you often have to pass and wait for the next one because it's full.
If you are on the 22nd floor like I was, expect to spend at least 10 minutes to get to the ground floor. Taking the stairs actually was faster!
They have a treadmill and a bike machine in the "fitness center," which is about the size of your standard room (very small), and NEITHER OF THE MACHINE works. The bike machine didn't even turn on. What was worse was the treadmill! It started working, and the belt sticks and stops abruptly. I almost hurt myself from tripping over a treadmill!
"Free wireless," which is only available in the lobby area, didn't work. After spending 30 minutes on the phone with an outside-vendor tech guy from India, they couldn't figure out why it wasn't working.
My room smelled like somebody had smoked, and the $9.95/day DSL didn't even work. When I had my room changed, the DSL I was finally able to connect was as slow as dial-up.
The worst, absolutely worst, hotel, ever! Avoid this one, folks. A $55/night Motel 6 would be much, much better than this one.

title: “Quiet and restful”
text:
We (my husband and I) chose this hotel because it was close to the airport and there was free shuttle service to the airport. We stayed at the hotel on a Saturday night and had an early Sunday morning flight to catch. The reason that we were in Phoenix was to spend the Thanksgiving holiday with family.
I booked directly with the hotel and received a better rate than what was offered on various websites. When I asked the reservation person for an AARP discount, she said they didn't have one, but she would extend the AAA discount. A bargain!
The shuttle picked us up at the airport after we returned our rental car. The wait for the shuttle was short, and the driver was courteous and friendly. 
Check-in was fast. Our room was clean and modern. There was adequate space for our suitcases and we even had a little mini fridge. There was plenty of room to spread out. The room was on the first floor and was very quiet. 
The hotel has a guest laundry room. We had a bunch of dirty clothes so I ran a load. The machines were coin operated, but the price was reasonable and the hotel provided the laundry soap and dryer sheets. The laundry room was clean too.
I stopped by the front desk several times for little things like a stapler, change for the laundry, some tape, drop off some letters for mailing, ask about location of a drug store, ask for an envelope to put all of my receipts in. I always received a smile and a helpful response.
We stopped by the front desk and inquired about dining options. The desk clerk gave us a list of recommended restaurants and let us know that the shuttle driver could drop us off on Mill Street in Tempe so we could eat at one of the restaurants in that area.
We took her advice and had a great dinner at a Greek restaurant. We called the driver when we finished dinner and she arrived in five minutes at a prearranged pickup area.
We asked for a wake up call and received it. We were up too early to take advantage of the complimentary breakfast so we do not know what we missed. We rode the shuttle to the airport for our early flight. Everything was smooth and everyone was great.
All in all this was a good experience. We would stay here again and would recommend this hotel to everyone.
Oh, yeah - cookies. They make cookies every evening. Mmmm. They were good too.
My husband says that this place is first class.

title: “We got exactly what we paid for.”
text:
We booked a trip trough Expedia. We were looking for a buget motel and got exactly that. 
The rooms were clean, but old. They are in need of a remodel.
Our room was on the ground facing the parking lot. There were loud people coming and going all night. The second night there I used the ear plugs I brought with me. 
The rooms facing the pool were probably more quiet. 
We had a small kitchen with a fridge, micowave & coffee pot. We didn't know that before we got there. It was a nice suprise. And we used it.
The pool area was nice. There were chairs and loungers. 
The motel is near a McDonald's, Denny's, Arby's & Jack in the Box. Other wise not much else in the area. 
It was difficult getting across the street to get to the I-17 South exit. Traffic was backed up there frequently. Getting North was not a problem.
There is a continential breakfast. There is very little food here. If your hungry go across the street to Denny's otherwise you'll starve. The coffee was good though.
For the amount of time we actually spent it the motel it was fine with us.

title: “Great staff, great hotel”
text:
After arriving hot and tired from our long ride to Philadelphia, we found the hotel staff to
be extremely courteous and welcoming. They always provided us with good directions and went our of their way to help in any way they could.

title: “Hotel on the Skids”
text:
Sadly, this hotel has hit the skids. We had our wedding reception here 10 years ago so I hate to see this happening. For our wedding night, they gave us the Kabuki Suite, a two-story suite with a large living room upstairs. So for our 10th Anniversary in July, I called to ask for the Kabuki Suite again. She didn't see one with that name so she suggested I call the hotel directly to make sure we got exactly what we wanted on our special day. Unfortunately, the local person acted like they didn't know what I was talking about so I described it in detail. She gave some vague reassurance that we'd get what we wanted. When we got to the suite, it was tiny and absolutely not right. There were several stories at the front desk - that suite was being renovated, that suite was available for $1K per night (it cost $500 10 years ago and we've rented it since for $450) - none of which rang true. We cancelled our reservation immediately.
They nearly ruined a very important day for us but we re-grouped and went to the Ritz Carlton, a much better hotel with exceptional service. Save yourself the disappointment with the Intercontinental.

title: “Great location and good value”
text: We spent three nights at the Sheraton in a poolside room and were throroughly satisfied with the stay. It's a stone's thrown, with a regular shuttle, from Universal and meant that you can dip in and out of the theme park and then take some and R and R by the pool. The breakfast was good and staff all friendly and helpful. My sole complaint was that the the room service was only average but overall I wouldn't hesitate to recommend staying here.

title: “Very poor for that price!”
text: We booked a renovated room because we saw on tripadvisor.com that the old rooms are terrible. At the check-in desk, we waited about half an hour. The staff was very unfriendly, we didn't feel welcome at all. As we got into our room, we found it very small and the first thing we noticed was that it was about 85 degrees (30 Celsius) in there. We complained at the check-in, and they've sent an engineer. He told us that we had "one of the good A/Cs, because it still heats the room, other guests are freezing". We were surprised that he couldn't do anything about the temperature. So we opened the window to the max (about 5cm) and went for dinner. After returning (about 1 hour later), the room was still way too hot! So we complained again and they sent the engineer again to our room. Meanwhile, we found out that the heat was coming from the bathroom floor, he told us that we (obviously) cannot turn it off. Best thing he told us: They had problems with the A/C for months, but cannot solve it. So we went to the check-in again to complain, but they didn't care at all. To make matters worse, she mocked us because it was freezing outside and we were complaining about a room that was too hot. But it was not just that, the room is simply not renovated. The bathroom door cannot be closed properly (and I don't mean locked, the door cannot be CLOSED). The room smelled weird and we couldn't get rid of the feeling that we paid way too much for that and that we are just getting ripped of. Last but not least, you wait forever for the elevators. They couldn't offer us ANY alternative, so we booked another hotel (the Belvedere) for about the same price. That hotel was great, we were so relieved and confirmed that our feeling about this hotel being to expensive was just right! We spent one night at the Milford (didn't sleep well though because of the heat and open window) and changed the hotel right on the next morning. Don't book this hotel and if you booked, cancel! It is really not worth it, you will just be disappointed. As I saw on tripadvisor.com, Diane Devine, Manager at Milford Plaza Hotel is answering all the bad reviews with a standard text.
