I have news for you: In a city like NYC, where there are hundreds if not thousands of hotels, nobody will give you a second chance. You act in a very short-term oriented manner, not realizing that you will loose a lot of customers like that in the future. The prominent place will not guarantee you guests forever. It is simply not a coincidence that every time I went to the front desk there were other guests complaining about diverse things too. I understand that this hotel is under renovation, BUT selling rooms as renovated while they are simply not finished is not just wrong but also illegal in my understanding. I will never stay there again.

title: “Great experience”
text: This is a wonderful hotel, reasonably priced given its location a stone's throw from the Capitol. The rooms, for Washington, were large, comfortable, and well-appointed. My room was right above the bar, but the thumping dance music stopped every night by the time I bedded down. Staff was helpful. No complaints.

title: “Friendly staff & clean, but dated interior with billing issues”
text: Like the title says, the staff was good and the hotel was clean, but the interior/rooms need some pretty serious updating. We'd never stayed at this particular hotel on the Riverwalk, but our regular hotel (The Westin) was full. The Crowne Plaza's rate was pretty good and we needed a pet friendly hotel so we decided to give them a shot. First of all, we were told by their reservations line that there would be ZERO charge for a pet and my email confirmation shows no pet charge either. We check in, the folks at the front desk see our dog and there is no mention of a pet charge here either. We check out and whaddya know... a $75 pet charge was added to our bill with no help by the front desk after I explain the issue. We were also told by Reservations that a roll-away would be available for our 10 year old son for a $25 additional fee. We said no problem, but were then told they could not do so because it was a fire hazard. Finally, the breakfast buffet was so-so at best. Our waiter was great, but half of the buffet options were only luke warm + the touted omlette bar was closed. If you have other options, take it. As far as location goes, it IS on the Riverwalk, but it's a good 10 minute walk from the hotel to where "the heart" of the Riverwalk is actually located. It's well lit and nice, but we would have preferred a closer location.

title: “great center of city hotel”
text: This is a great get away hotel if you live in the city. I'm sure it would be great for tourists too but for myself already living in NYC, I love it. My husband & I stay here sometimes just becauase it's convienent to be able to do a lot of stuff in that area without having to travel. We like it because we can go see a show, go to dinner, go shopping and have drinks in the great rotating lounge on the top floor. You can walk to lots of stuff in the area so you save time & $$ on taxis. We live only 25 mins away from this hotel but we still love staying here. Rooms are comfortable & very clean. Stay during the week and the price of a room is significantly lower.

title: “A special treat in New York - worth every cent”
text:
I treated myself to an extended stay at this lovely hotel in November-December 2009. I stayed in the Poetry room which was small but perfect for a solo traveller. The staff were very friendly and couldn't have been more helpful: if they didn't know the answers to my questions they looked them up on the internet and when the wireless in my room played up, they provided me with a cable and arranged for someone to look into the issue.
The breakfast was extensive and included everything you could ask for in a continental breakfast and the staff on duty were attentive and always willing to help On the rare occasion that all of the tables were full, the staff offered to provide you wtih a tray to take to your room or to the upstairs lounge.
The complementary wine and cheese evenings were a wonderful way to wind down before dinner after a busy day experiencing the city and the free drinks and pastries available during the day were a lovely touch.
The free DVD library was also great for the night I just want to stay in and relax.
The hotel isn't cheap but it is a lovely treat and completely worth every cent, paricularly if you get a discount by booking early and prepaying. I would definitely recommend it to a friend and would love the opportunity to stay again.

title: “Location Location”
text: The hotel is in a great location right next to the tram line and walking distance to all the shopping in downtown San Francisco. The room was small and the bathroom very small. Parking is very expensive an add on cost that we didn't need. Every other hotel even 'budget' hotels have provided free parking. So it would only be worth staying here if you don't have a car.

title: “Great place to stay”
text: Our company was traveling here for business. Stayed here for a week. Great Location, it ended up only a few miles from where we were working. The hotel staff were friendly and helpful. The rooms were clean and nice. Only comment was they wished the pool was inside.

title: “Nice Surprise!”
text: Having never stayed at a Fairfield Hotel was unsure of what to expect, but being a frequent Marriott customer I thought it would be okay. What a nice surprise the Fairfield Inn in downtown Chicago was! From the moment we checked in we were greeted by friendly and helpful staff and were very happy with the accommodations. Very Clean and comfortable. Great 24 hour coffee bar was a nice convenience. Hotel location was perfect. I would not hesitate to stay again. In fact look forward to doing so in the near future. Great bang for your buck.

title: “I had a very pleasant experience at this hotel. They were very helpful when I told them I had forgotten my toiletries.”
text: I found the hotel to be very clean and the receptionist was very helpful in providing me a toothbrush and other toiletries I had forgotten. The atmosphere was also quiet; unlike other hotels I've stayed at where there seemed to have been a lot of doors slamming. Overall, it was a great value for the price.

title: “Exceptional Service”
text: We have stayed twice at this hotel when we travel to Seattle Mariners games. The rooms are small but the location and cost are great. You can walk to the Amtrak, both stadiums, Metro, Pikes Market, and downtown. The rooms are small but ours have always been clean and the beds are very comfortable. The staff is very courteous and friendly. This past visit we forgot some expensive items in the safe both Gabriel and Roberto were so helpful in getting our stuff found and back to us. We would highly recommend this hotel to others.

title: “What a TOTAL Disappointment”
text:
We came here on Friday, October 9, 2009 for a three night stay. It has been nothing but a comedy of errors and poor customer service.
When "security" was roaming the halls with their Walkie-talkies on volume 10 at 7:15 AM and woke us up on our first day of vacation, I called to the front desk. They transferred me to the voicemail for the hotel's general manager. He never called back. 
Then, 36 hours later, after leaving at 8:30 am and being out and about until 5:25 PM, we returned to a room that was not made up. I called over a porter in the hallway to bring his attention to this. All he said was that he was sorry but that they were "going to get to it." We called the front desk and they transferred us to the voicemail for the same general manager who still hasn't called back. Then, there was a knock at the door. A woman identified herself as the maid. I asked her why our room was still unmade and she said, "I've had a busy day. I had 15 rooms to clean." REALLY??!?!?!? Are you [--] kidding me???!? THIS IS YOUR JOB. The hotel (and our floor) isn't even full. How could you handle this if it were at capacity? 
Bottom line: Excuses don't explain and explanations don't excuse. For a "luxury" hotel, go to any of the adjacent properties here-- the rooms are just a nice but the rates are 50% less and the service is better. The Hilton and Marriott are great. This place sucks.
BIG disappointment for us, as we were "splurging" for an extra nice "luxury" weekend.

title: “Good Location but staff could do better.”
text:
Spent 5 nights here with my wife and adult son and found the location to be excellent for walking to Central Park, Times Square, Rockefeller Centre and subway stations. We were on the 14th floor and were surprised by how quiet it was at night for a New York city centre hotel. When we visited the hotel seemed to be very busy with numerous tour groups and school trippers milling about the lobby area. We had to wait some time to be attended to on arrival and what made it more annoying was that there were several staff standing about chatting behind the reception desk whilst we waited. The hotel shop was not what we expected from such a large hotel and staffed by a surly uncommunicative male who did not even acknowledge our presence. We had cocktails in the bar before heading out to see a Broadway show and again found the barman grumpy and unwelcoming plus the cocktails were unimpressive, poorly presented and quite expensive. 
So although we thought the hotel itself was very good our overall opinion was diminished by our contact with some staff.

title: “1982 meets 2012”
text:
I am a frequent business traveler so my review will be fair given what I have seen. This hotel appears to have been partially updated over the years, but the furniture, fixtures, lighting, and general feel of the hotel still feels like 1982. My overall rating is average.
Pros:
The rooms are large
Climate control is relatively quiet
Fair to good decor in the halls and rooms
Good location
Good parking
Cons:
Housekeeping falls short on every level (Carpet stains, dirty curtains, shortage of towels)
Front desk service is average
Furniture and fixtures are old
Other hotel chain beds are more comfortable
I would stay here again if other hotels are booked, but this hotel is not a favorite.

title: “Worth the two trips around the block!!”
text:
I adored this little hotel. Although, my girlfriends and I joked about the hotel sign being in braille! We circled the block twice looking for it, and there it was--the tiny little CLIFT sign; hiding in plain site. The two Justin's out front were very nice, the checkin gal very helpful and the general vibe inside the whole place felt uber cool. Loved the funky chairs and eclectic decor. Never met an unfriendly hotel worker our entire stay. But we are friendly folks too!!
We had a room on the 7th floor, far away from street noices, and as long as you didn't look down (unless you like looking at HVACs) it wasn't bad. I liked being able to open the widow for a bit of cool night air. 
The room was big enough for three small town girls to get ready to be fancy girls for a night at the theater. After walking to the Daily Grill for a great Happy Hour menu, we had plenty of time and room to get ready for Wicked, the play. After the play, we just knew we had to finish our big night off in the Redwood Room. Fun place to people watch!! Conversations are difficult, however. The music is a bit loud. Never thought I'd get old enough to hear myself say that!!
Meanwhile, up stairs, we found beds that were comfortable enough. There is a Starbucks across the street, and in the morning, it's an easy trip over and back for coffee and scones in the room. The location is safe, and within walking distance to Union Square, Market Street, cable cars and lots and lots of fun shopping and eating and exploring. Oh the SHOPPING!!
I would stay here again, I would recommend it to my friends, and except for the pricey drinks in the Redwood Room and $50 valet parking, I have no complaints. But, hey, it's San Francisco!! We may not like it, but we have come to expect it! You only live once!After many, many, many stays in this crazy city, The Clift stands out in my mind as one of the most unsual, eclectic, but clean and comfortable places I've been. Would be interested to know if there is a "park and shop" special.
Pros: Safe location, close to many attractions, clean, cool, quiet and eclectic. The staff we encountered were all nice. Good price thru Hotwire.
Cons: Not really "cons" so much as comments: Parking is expensive (It's like that everywhere in SF) The hotel sign is hard to see, you really have to look for it, which is not easy to do when you're driving in SF. Hint: It's on the left side of the street, and located almost at the corner. Not much of a view from our room, but we weren't there for the "view."

title: “Very Accommodating!”
text: Not too fancy, but definitely great value for your money. The continental breakfast was very good! They provided eggs, cheese and ham to make hot sandwiches and a waffle maker! There is one big jacuzzi! Very clean! The gym had 3 pieces of cardio equipment. We did experience ONE problem, however, the hotel was able to remedy it! When I called to make the reservation and asked about transportation from the airport, the man on the phone said they use a town car service and the trip for 4 adults would cost $40 total ($10 per person). We arrived at the airport at midnight and the driver was a little late, which was no big deal. Then, the driver proceeded to let us load all of our luggage, not helping himself. Then on the way to the hotel, he started falling asleep at the wheel! My husband had to make conversation to keep him awake! He was swerving everywhere! When we arrived at the hotel, he charged us $65 after letting us unload all our own bags! We were PISSED! We told the hotel manager, and he arranged for us to get a complimentary ride back to the airport. The hotel staff was very understanding about that. So, maybe arrange your own transportation!

title: “Wow! This is my place in San Diego.”
text:
Well this place was a total surprise! The Staff A+, the Cleanliness A+, and the facilities(Pool, Jacuzzi, and Ground Top Notch.), the rooms were inviting and ergonomic, the bed and feather pillows(6) were inviting. Don in the Bar couldn't had treated us any better, his attention was beyond beyond. The front desk personnel Emroy & Latoya remembered my Last name after I hadn't seen them for a couple of days. I forget I'm not at the Beverly Hills Hilton. If you want 5 star service at 3.5 star price, then this is your place.
My name is Dave Deninger and I'm very happy and satisfied. I'm business and vacations are here. Sounds like I like it a little.

title: “Excellent Location! Huge rooms!”
text:
Pros: 
- excellent location in the theatre district close to Central Park, Times Sqr, subway stations and bus stops
- very large rooms, I had a room on the 16th floor with a small kitchen, separate toilet and showers
- pretty quiet
- I booked the room through Quikbook for 149 USD plus taxes etc. pretty good rate I thought
Cons:
- the air-con unit was extremely loud, but all's ok with ear plugs!
- TV's a bit old but that's ok
- gym's on the roof, can get pretty hot, it's pretty small and the machines are pretty old

title: “Excellent Choice”
text: This was by far the best decision when planning our trip to New York. My criteria for a hotel..2 queen beds..clean..continental breakfast..location..price and self laundry. This hotel had all that I was looking for. We were traveling as a family of 3 adults and 1 teenager. The room was "just right" considering all the reviews I had read of how small rooms can be in Manhattan. I wasn't expecting much but hoping for the best and it turned out that we were pleasantly surprised. The room was clean and having continental breakfast was a great bonus. The location..awesome and surprisingly quiet. Walking distance to many sites. The metro was so close and convenient and it felt safe too. The area in general felt safe..big, big plus. The price...excellent. The staff..very helpful. Laundry..a block away. I would definitely stay here again. I've recommended this place to friends and family. That in itself says a lot. It's difficult to please people but I believe from my experience that they will like everything that I liked about this place. I wish I had wrote this review sooner but LIFE..well it gets pretty busy. Try this place. I know you'd like it.

title: “FANTASTIC SERVICE/LOCATION/ROOM - GREAT HOTEL!!”
text:
We stayed at the Hilton Garden Inn in Chelsea at Easter 2010 and had a wonderful time. The staff were very friendly and eager to not keep you waiting. The room was great, cleaned well and even though the front of the Hotel is scaffolded at present it did not spoil the experience. The best thing about this hotel is the location - you go right your at Madison Square Gardens and Penn Station and go right and your 10 mins from Times Square. Fanstastic. New York does not have many great bars but i would recommend 'Harringtons' next to Madison square near the hotel, my friends and i had a meal and quiet drinks after a show, so really the hotel was perfect. 
I also realised after checking out that i had left a top in the wardrobe and (due to the volcano extending our stay!) we went back the next day and the receptionist searched the whole hotel and found it for me. I would tell anyone to stay at this hotel for a great NYC trip!!

title: “Overnight Stay”
text:
I stayed at Affinia Manhattan on Tuesday. I arrived early in the day and was hoping they could store my bags while I went out. Instead, they had a room ready for me at 10 am! 
The room was spacious with a huge comfortable bed. There was also an alcove with a chair and side table - enough space to stretch out and watch TV.
The room was on the 3rd floor. I was afraid the street sounds would be overbearing. Actually not. Only downside was the sound coming from the pipes. It was more bothersome than anything coming from the street. Also, no view - the window was too tiny.
Location was great, right across from Madison Square Garden. I will stay here next time, just on a higher floor.

author.location: Washington, District of Columbia, United States

title: “Hotel was nice”
text: Nice comfortable rooms where we spent 6 nights. Nice landscaped gardens but a little noisy from the Motorway near by. However, rooms were reasonably sound proofed so had no problems with sleeping. Plenty of parking, but found $9 a day charge, somewhat steep. Would recommend asking for a room overlooking Ventura Blvd as I'm sure this would be quieter (something I did not do). Would stay there again.

title: “Pleasantly surprised”
text: After reading some of the negative reviews, I bit my nails when Club Quarters popped up my screen after a Hotwire purchase. On our recent visit (9/10 and 11) we were pleasantly surprised when we arrived to find modern accommodations, free wireless internet access, helpful staff, and ample street parking if we did not feel like being robbed by the parking garages. The location was great; in the heart of the financial district, close to Chinatown and the Ferry Building (excellent outdoor farmer's market on Saturdays). The only downside is that the walls are a bit thin, so if you have a noisy neighbor I can see how sleep may be a problem. Perfect for a business trip or short stay. I'll definitely stay there again.

title: “Good Hotel in a Very Busy Location”
text:
We originally had no intention of staying here, but our favorite San Francisco hotel was booked and we were able to secure a very good room rate, so decided to give this SOMA hotel a try. Overall, we were pleased with our visit, with a few reservations.
This is an extremely large hotel, near the Moscone Center, so it is heavily utilized by conventioneers and tour groups. Located less than a block from Market Street, the Westfield Mall and near Union Square, the area is extremely crowded and busy with traffic, pedestrians and the inevitable San Francisco street people. The hotel elevators and hallways are like a maze and rather confusing until you get your bearings.
However, our room was good sized, clean and quiet, despite the many guests staying over the weekend we were there. The maids were very helpful and accommodating to us. The front desk personnel were also helpful and attentive to all the guests, even when the lobby was packed with people coming and going. Our concierge, Dave, was fantastic, friendly and helpful, full of great, local dining information which we made excellent use of. I also noticed when the concierge line backed up, other staff members immediately came up to offer help to the waiting guests.
So despite the large size of the property, crowded with guests in an extremely busy location, the staff helped to make our stay very enjoyable. I would definitely consider the Marriott Marquis again, if our preferred hotel is unavailable.

title: “GREAT CUSTOMER SERVICE - GREAT VACATION”
text:
My husband and I booked in here after an awful first night experience in another hotel in San Francisco!
We arrived just after 9am and were greeted at reception by Erikka. We explained that we were on our 'trip of a lifetime' to celebrate our 25th Wedding Anniversary. We arrived in SF late the previous evening, and had the worst hotel experience ever!
On hearing this, Erikka was absolutely brilliant. She checked availability of rooms and appointed us a fabulous Bay View room on the 26th floor.The room was spacious, spotlessly clean and had everything required to make our stay memorable. We were really impressed with the level of customer service given to us. Erikka was an absolute gem and she is a credit to the hotel.
During our stay in the city we took a ferry to Sausilito. Beautiful little place. Spotlessly clean with lots of good restaurants etc.
We visited Fishermans Wharf and tried the famous Clam Chowder - delicious! We then queued for 2 hours for a cable car - boarded it and then had to jump off quickly as the clutch had snapped! It took quite a while to have it repaired so we decided to walk back to the hotel. Bad idea - we obviously looked as if we were lost (we were) and a lovely lady stopped to give us directions. Great to know that people will take the time out to help strangers to the city!
We found eating out to be quite expensive but it no different to any other city.
I would love to return to San Francisco one day and I would definately stay at Parc 55 @ Wyndham without a doubt.

title: “Great Place to Stay for Business”
text: I stayed at the Westin In Charlotte one night for business in May 2012. I found the hotel very warm and the front desk very friendly and helpfull. The room I had was nice, two double beds with plenty of pillows and very comfortable bed. There are two reasons I am not giving this a 5 star rating instead - 1. the safety latch on the inside of the door was missing so I was not able to latch the door for securely. 2. there was no exhaust fan in the bathroom. I know this is a minor thing but I list it as a disadvantage because you can not get the steam out after a shower to get ready for work very easy. However, the shower was awesome with the Heavenly Shower Head. Overall my stay was great and I would defidently stay again with a room that had a latch on the door that worked properly. If you have any questions about the hotel please feel free to contact me.

title: “Good location, lovely & spacious room, OK service”
text:
I stayed at the Hotel Madera for one night during the week on a business trip in March 2006. 
Upon arrival, I was slightly confused because there was no valet to be seen outside and I had to parallel park my car in a tiny spot on the street in front of the hotel. Also, I had to carry my own bags inside. This is not typical for me on a business trip, but I had booked the Hotel Madera knowing that it is a small, boutique hotel and that reviews of it on this board had said that service was lacking.
However, once I got inside to the front desk I had very good service from the woman staffing it. She immediately radioed down for a valet to move my car. While my room wasn't immediately ready, she had the valet also store my bags. While I camped out on the lobby sofa across from the front desk to check my email and voicemails, my room became ready and she sent me upstairs. My bags arrived about five minutes later. 
As I am a Kimpton in touch member, I did enjoy the bottled water and fruit basket, along with handwritten welcome note in my room. The room was incredibly spacious for the city, with a full size sofa in front of floor to ceiling windows that opened out onto a small balcony with great views of New Hampshire ave. The bed was comfortable and they let me select pillows from the pillow menu. I was disappointed that the high speed internet connection was not wireless, however. 
All in all, I had a nice time at this hotel and would stay again for business. However, if you have a car that needs to be parked, be prepared for slow service from the valet. Next time I am in DC for business I will probably just take a cab from the airport. There were almost always cabs out front and the metro is just two blocks away in Dupont Circle.

title: “Great deal on a great hotel”
text:
I decided to try Hotwire for the first time and ended up with the Westin at under $70 a night for a weekend. This is a fantastic ,old style hotel that makes you think you are staying in New York City. Huge grand lobby, all in marble, with the staff mostly in black dress uniforms. The staff service was fantastic. We stopped at the front desk to ask for some directions for a walk down through German Village - they got us a map and made us take a complimentary umbrella since there was a chance of rain. The bar was very nice with good service, and the hotel restaurant (we didnt eat there) but it looked nice and appeared pretty busy. One evening they were serving complimentary champagne in the lobby. We used the $20 valet parking (great since it rained) but they had $5 self parking behind the hotel. The room was nicely decorated, well kept, and clean. They have the special slumber beds - very comfortable.
While there are really no cons, the rooms are smaller than contemporary hotels but unless you plan to entertain, you won't need the larger space. We could hear some street noise (our room was at the front of the building) but it didn' bother us. I would certainly stay there again.

title: “Great stay at the Omni”
text: Stayed at the Omni LA at California Plaza for the second time in 2 months. The location was very convenient to USC. We've now stayed at four different hotels in downtown LA, and the courtesy and efficiency of the hotel staff has far exceeded the other three. We were looking for a nice hotel to return to for our frequent visits to the area and have found it at the Omni!

title: “Great Exoerience”
text: We enjoyed our stay at The Willows! Thier pillows are delightful. Clean and very confortable. Pretty too!

title: “A fab slice of the big apple”
text:
I recently returned from New York City where I stayed at the Gansevoort, Park Avenue for five days. What a great experience it was. This is a hip, funky hotel attractive to the younger visitor but also making older folk, like myself, feel comfortable, welcome and special. 
My room was spacious and clean, well appointed with contemporary furniture and tastefully decorated. The bed was the most comfortable I had ever slept in and the pillows were like lying on a cloud. The king size bed was a rare treat and I felt completely relaxed. The bathroom had one of the biggest baths I have ever seen and the daily service kept the bathroom spotless and provided me with fluffy white towels every day. Turn down service was unobtrusive and appreciated. 
The Gansevoort provides everything a traveller needs including the use of luxury robes and the slippers which are provided for the guest to keep (the slippers not the robes) just give that extra special nurturing that other hotels miss out on. Attention to detail is the key here to a first class experience from the luxury bath products to the mini bar which was undoubtedly one of the best stocked bars I have ever seen in a hotel room. The only thing missing was coffee and tea making facilities in the rooms themselves!
The service was outstanding and I was always able to get help with anything I needed, even at 1am in the morning! When I found out my room did not have a safe as promised (being replaced) and a faulty iron, I was given another room with everything I needed and although I did not want to move luggage again, this was done with a minimum of fuss and I had no issue with the way it was resolved.
 I always felt I came first with the team, from front desk to housekeeping and I appreciated the attention given to every small detail. My concierge, 'M' was simply amazing and took care of my every wish from premium theatre tickets to transport needs and it was all done with a smile. The roof top bar is a happening place for the young and young at heart and has views of New York City which are breathtaking. Although I know some patrons find the pulsation of the music and conversation loud in their rooms as the night goes on, I found this was no issue when I returned to my room and would not see this as a negative factor.
Food was first class at the adjoining restaurant to the hotel and we spent several nights in good conversation beside the gas fire feature in the bar lounge served by attentive waitors who always seemed to be there when a drink or finger food was needed. The location is also excellent, close to a number of restaurants and brasseries and a 'Starbucks' if you need a coffee fix. 
This was a great experience and I thank the hotel staff for making me feel really special on my first trip to New York city. Good value hotel - worth a serious look from anyone wanting a really top notch hotel experience in the city that never sleeps!

title: “Great Little Place.. Excellent Location!”
text:
First off if you are expecting the Hilton - the Queen Anne is not that. If the Hilton is what you are expecting find a Hilton and pay the price otherwise do not complain about this nice little quaint hotel!
Pros: Very Comfy - everything worked in the room. Rooms were small, but I like to think of it as cozy instead of small. The closets are real large so therefore much of your traveling items can be stored out of arms way. I believe all the units have a small kitchenette which consists of a (2) burner stove, microwave, sink, cupboards, small fridg and enough dishes and silverware to accomedate 2 just fine. 
The staff was very friendly and helpful. There is a continental breakfast offered with coffee, OJ, and rolls - there may be more I was not sure as my husband just went down one morning to get me some OJ and a roll. I can say the roll and OJ was tasty and fresh.
The maid server was very nice and did a good job on cleaning daily.
There is high speed internet available in the rooms, which is a plus if you are like me and have a traveling office which requires you to work while out of town.
Location is absolutely wonderful. Walking distance to space needle and Key arena activities, many restaurants close by and the metro bus lines are right there to take you where ever you little heart desires at a very reasonable small fee. PLUS a grocery store right across the street, drug store about 1 block away some smaller businesses like office supplies etc! How wonderful is this. 
The staff pointed out that is is about the same price to take a Towncar from the Sea-Tac then a taxi. And they have one that they recommend. I mean why not we did ~ hmmm Taxi or Towncar.. not really to hard of a decision there for the same price. I am sure the shuttle may of been a few dollars cheaper, so if you don't mind a 1 1/2 hour shuttle ride to save nothing more then a couple bucks then take the shuttle, otherwise the towncar is the way to go between airport and the Inn At Queen Anne.
Cons: The pillows could be a little fluffier. We solved that by asking for a couple more pillows which the staff supplied without hesitation. There is not that much hot water or pressure. We stayed there for 6 nights and found that if at all possible take your shower around noon or a little after. There is really no need to turn on the cold water knob when taking a shower and the shower head can be rotated to help with the pressure aspect. 
Other then them two small issues really just one the water pressure (the pillows can be solved by asking for more pillows) - I cannot say anything negative about the Inn At Queen Anne"
Again this is not the Hilton or even the Radisson it is a small 1930's quaint Inn located in a nice area and for the age still holds her head fairly high. It shows and feels charactor. You can almost feel the history within the walls. And the price cannot be beat!
We will stay there again if we have a need to go to Seattle again!

title: “Great value, great location, though basic”
text:
This hotel is a lot better than I thought! I would call it a hidden jewel among Houston hotels in terms of value and convenience. 
I normally stay at other hotels when I visited Houston. Last week, I had a hard time booking a hotel because of a huge convention in Houston. My company finally booked me a room in this hotel.
For the price we paid, I was happily surprise that it is probably the best value among all the hotels I have stayed in Houston. If you are looking for a long-term stay place that is reasonbly clean and at a low cost, this can be a top choice. 
This hotel is next to Loop 610 and only one block from the gigantic shopping mall: Galleria. With all the shops and restaurants on Westheimer Road nearby, this is a very nice and convenient location. 
They only charge $5 for internet hookup. This is all you have to pay even if you stay here for months. That is right, the $5 is just a setup fee. After that, you can logon with your computer wireless in your room and use a much as you want, as long as you want. 
The room is good size, with small kitchen, and refrigerator. There are pot and pans, microwave, dishes and eating utensils, Sound proofing is very good! 
However, you do have to somewhat lower your expectation, as this hotel is very basic in term of services and aminities. The bed is average in comfort, there is only a bar of soap in the bathroom; and they clean room only once a week. 
The staff was very friendly and helpful! If someday I have to stay in Houston for a long visit on my own money, I would not hesitate to book into this hotel.

title: “Great hotel perfect as home base for San Diego County attractions”
text: We really enjoyed our stay at Homewood suites in Del Mar. I was travelling with a pregnant wife and 18 month kid, so my needs were somewhat demanding, and Homewood delivered. The suites provided all the amenities that we wanted and served as a good focal point for all the san diego attractions. Shops are nearby and the neighborhood is upscale.

title: “Great Location & Wonderful Staff”
text: Checked into the hotel, the staff was very friendly and efficient. The beds were extremely comfortable, the food was great at the restaurant. The pool and jacuzzi were my favorite part of the hotel. Parking was easy, and getting to and from the freeway was easy as well. I would reccomend this to anyone traveling in the area.

title: “Very good hotel, great location at an excellent price”
text:
The Radisson Airport is a very good hotel. Rooms are big with wireless Internet and a separate work area. While it is not a luxury hotel it has all the conveniences and amenities of a very good three-star. No downsides. Staff was friendly. Check-in and check-out processes efficient and there is free parking.
I was in room 214 and well, it has the worst view ever (directly into the satellite dishes, but no biggie). You may want to request a higher floor.
Got the hotel at $55 on Priceline (on a weekend) and was very satisfied. Also, you do not have the noise problems of other airport hotels. Actually, you can't hear a thing while in your room.
A few weeks ago I stared at the Park Plaza Phoenix North for a few bucks less. The Radisson PHX airport is better appointed, so if your plans are around the area stay here. If your plans are in North Phoenix you'll probably better off at the Park Plaza and save the few bicks.

title: “Location Good, but that's it”
text: We did not have a good time at the Helmsley Park Lane Hotel. The location was great, but that is about it. Checkout time was listed on the door as 1:00, but when I called to ask if we could checkout at 2:00 the front desk said checkout was now 12:00 (even though we were never told). Our 23rd floor "city view" was the roof of a building next door. There are no ice machines so we had to call room service each night for ice. The tiny refrigerator was in the bathroom and covered over with ice. The cords on the lighting fixtures were scarey. We were right next to the room service door which was continously slamming shut, and the elevador. The decor was cheap and the bellman was piling people's bags in the lobby with cable locks around them because they ran out of room in storage. Our friend's parents stayed at the Woldorf for $159 a night that their place was much better.

title: “Some Opening Night Hiccups”
text:
First, let me say that I am a big fan of the Kimpton chain, so I was thrilled to be in town the day the new Monaco opened in Baltimore (July 30th). The location is not as good as the other true Inner Harbor hotels, although it is definitely walkable. The building itself is beautiful as the former headquarters of the B & O railroad. Even if you aren't staying here, if you happen to be walking by you owe it to yourself to stop in the lobby to see the magnificent Tiffany stained glass ceiling. 
As with any opening, there are bound to be a few glitches, and the Hotel Monaco was no different. I was greeted by several doormen, who all seemed excited to have guests and eager to help. I dropped off my bags and took the rental car two blocks north to a garage that charges $6 /day weekend rate (222 N Charles I believe). Valet is steep at $36 per day, so check out the other options. The receptionist was still learning the system and it took a few minutes to apply my Kimpton InTouch membership to my stay. Understandable. I was then escorted to my room by one of the bellmen who took my bags. I was assigned room 1406, on the top floor as I requested. We got off the elevator and the bellman took me to the wrong end of the hallway before realizing he had gone the wrong way. Honest mistake as he was still learning his way around I guess. We went back the other way and found the room. He then came in and began explaining the features of the room as one would expect. After he was done explaining the finer points of the bathroom, he then pointed me to the FOURTEEN inch flat screen TV (no, I didn't mishear him as he said it twice). In actuality, it was a nice LG 40"+ LCD. This was clearly a direct result of the training this gentleman received, and I hope they had this straightened out soon thereafter. 
The room was very nice....typical Kimpton style and very large (my queen queen room was over 400 sqft!). I particularly fancied the leather wallpaper in the bathroom. 
I have only two other minor quibbles, the first being that my rate included a nightly cocktail in B&O, the hotel restaurant, but the hotel had not received the vouchers from corporate yet, so I did not receive my cocktail. When I checked in, I mentioned this and they offered to escort me to the bar right then, but I was late to a dinner reservation so I declined. The only other comment I have is I did not receive my InTouch welcome amenity $10 minibar coupon, which I assume is also attributable to opening night kinks.
I understand one cannot accurately judge a hotel by it's performance on opening night, and I will be back next week to see how much the staff has grown in 5 short months.

title: “Great Service but missing some fine touches”
text:
Visited Chicago on a recent birthday get away to Chicago - 3 night stay. 
Staff and service are thoughtful, attentive and very professional - worthy of a 5 star rating. Special attention should be mentioned to the exceptional concierge Shannon Boland. Shannon put together some great recommendations for places to see and a few spectacular restaurants. She took the little homework that we did and built on it; using her personal experience and critical acclaim. All of the other staff were great as well - front desk, door and bell hops. They sent up a little something for me for my birthday - nice touch. 
The hotel is in a nice location - very close to Millennium Park and south of the Magnificent Mile. The hotel is historic and built on the Blackstone mansion. It has a great mix of classical charm and really stylized, modern touches. Very nice in a city that is all about the mix of old and new. 
Rooms carry the classical and modern touches from the rest of the hotel. The rooms are missing some of the finer touches the prevent me from classifying this hotel as excellent. The bed is very soft, with lots of very soft pillows and great linens. While this is comfortable for a short time, we both woke up with sore backs each morning. We discussed this with the staff but were told that all the beds were the same - no resolution offered. The room did not have a sheer set of blinds, blackout shades were the only option. Since we were in a south facing room, our room was very bright and looked at the Hilton across the road - so we could only have the blackouts closed. It prevented us from enjoying the natural light in the morning while getting ready. Hotel did not have slippers for guests and only one robe was provided. 
Went to the hotel's restaurant, Mercat a la Planxa - wasn't impressed but I will mention that in a separate review. 
All in all a nice stay in a great hotel but a few small tweaks are required.

title: “Not what I expected from a 4 star.”
text: Really small rooms with alot of excess furniture in them. Ruby Restaurant is a joke and the Bartender is horrible. I will definitely not stay here again.

title: “AMAZING PLACE !!!!!”
text:
This is a long review but worth the read!! I skipped my lunch t write this because people need to know abut this place!!
This place is hands down the best hotel I have ever been to in NYC. I read the wonderful reviews and contacted Patrick, (Whatever/Whenever Talent Coach) and explained that my best friend and I lost touch and were meeting up again after 4 years, and right away he and Jamila (Whatever/Whenever Agent) jumped right into asking me questions about my stay and made me feel soo important! When my friend (Sarah) and I arrived we were blown away by this place. It’s very stylish and I love the house type music they have playing throughout the place. Makes you want to dance! When we went up to the desk our room was already ready and we were upgraded to the cool corner room! AMAZING view! I highly recommend getting the cool corner room, you can see everything! We walked in and had two really cute gift bags waiting for us with all kinds of goodies, including this lovely vase (that I have at my desk as I type) we literally started jumping up and down like two little kids! We are 32! We even got a cute letter with our names on it welcoming us. My friend was so touched, she has never been to NYC and felt so important. The amenities are awesome. The king bed, my friend said was like (sleeping with GOD!) hahaha. She literally said that. We didn’t want to get out of it…soo comfy!! The room was a perfect size, and bathroom was clean and soo modern, we fell in love with the cool sink! The shower is big and perfect. The closet is nice and they give you a cute robe. When we checked in we were politely warned that there could be some noise outside in the morning because of some scaffolding work which was fine, but Saturday morning came and it was quiet! I’m a light sleeper and I slept just fine. The windows were clean and I got some great pictures! 
We loved the room so much we hung out a while and took in the view and had a chance to catch up. When we came back to the room later that night; we had a cute tray of pistachio nuts and yummy treats on our desk,. We were starved and devoured the whole thing! We forgot our toothpaste and called the desk and they quickly brought us some in a cute little black bag. When we left late Saturday night, I wasn’t feeling so well so I sat at the lounge, bags and all, a bit worried maybe I wouldn’t be able to hang out because I wasn’t drinking & taking up space…, but the gentleman was very kind and told me to stay as long as I liked and asked me if I needed anything. How nice! I must say too, there are some pretty good looking guys working here!! Hahaha, one in particular working outside opening the car doors for people..oh my..hehehe sorry I had to add that! I’m a single gals what can I say!?? 
I just joined their SPG membership. I NEVER join those things! I will never ever stay anywhere else and I cant wait to come back! You made our reunion soo special!! 
Thanks again Jamila and Patrick! I won’t forget it!

title: “Excellent resort ,has it all”
text: Have used the Houstonian for business travels many times, makes the time away from home a little bit better. The resort has it all, good meeting facilities, clean rooms, friendly and helpful staff, spa, excellent facilities for a good work out and a decent restaurant with excellent fruit for breakfast. The gym is probably the best in Houston and the tracks around the hotel is fantastic for a morning jog. The staff is helpful when it comes to arranging transportation. The hotel is also perfect for a weekend with your spouse, just relax or take a short ride to the mall at the Galleria :)

title: “Another excellent stay at the Hyatt”
text:
I was fortunate to get a good deal on Priceline for our 10th anniversary weekend. I let the Hyatt know it was a special occasion and they treated us like royalty. We were given a corner king room on the 17th floor with a great view looking up and down the Delaware River. Many thanks to Mike Costello for providing us with a bottle of wine and a chocolate covered strawberries upon arrival.
We could not of had a nicer room. There was water in every direction. The room had a comfortable king bed, mini fridge, LG TV and a large bathroom that also included a window looking over the river. It was quiet sleeping at night. I paid $12.95 for very efficient internet for a 24 hour period. We ordered breakfast to our room and it was delivered promptly and was satisfying.
The staff was helpful and friendly throughout our stay. We did use the fitness center and it had all modern equipment. The cardio machines had TV’s and plugs for I-Pods. There was a sauna and all the extras one would expect from a quality gym. The pool area was plenty big enough and connected to the fitness center. We did not eat at Keating’s, but stopped at the bar for a nightcap and found it to be welcoming and relaxing.
The only negative I see is the Hyatt is not close to downtown. Being January we did walk downtown but took a taxi back to the hotel. Society Hill is close and we ate at Bistro Romano one night and it was fantastic. We would have no problem returning here in the future.

title: “Good Value for Budget Conscious”
text: We are young newlyweds and my husband is a Marine based at Fort Bliss. As he had some leave time I flew down to join him for a few days. We don't have a lot of money to spend on expensive hotels so when we found the Best Value Inn Extended Stay online, decided to take a chance. The check in and check out was fast and efficient, totally problem free. Our room was very, very basic but clean. The housekeeping staff very friendly, fast, and hospitable. We stayed 5 days and found restaurants and hotels closeby and convenient. Although it was 107 degrees outside, our air conditioning was up to the job and we stayed cool. If we had any criticism at all it was that the pool was sparkling clean the first 2 days we were there but too murky to use the last 3 days. Anyone just looking for a good price for a clean, friendly,basic motel should be happy with their stay here.

title: “Nice hotel, good location, GREAT staff, but NOISY rooms”
text: Nice hotel, good location, GREAT staff, but NOISY rooms – that about sums up this decent 3* hotel in San Antonio. I was treated to the “beep – beep – beep” noises of trucks backing into the loading dock below – all night long. The greatest hotel in the world with rooms this noisy would not warrant a return visit. Instead, I recommend the Marriott Rivercenter across the street – it’s a newer property with QUIET rooms in which one can actually fall asleep. Avoid the Marriott Riverwalk due to NOISE. However, the staff – front desk, room service, valets – were all top notch.

title: “Cute hotel in a great area”
text: We chose this hotel for its convenient location to the Gaslamp quarter, but then we didn't even end up spending most of our time in that area. Oh well. The hotel itself was nice and cute - like most Kimpton hotels. We had a comfortable stay, and the staff was very nice.

title: “Interesting hotel...”
text:
I recently stayed at the Wardman Park hotel for a family vacation. Coming from California, I arrived at Ronald Regan Airport. I took the Blue Metroline to the hotel, which only costs 1.10 per person (one way.) If your coming to Washington during the off-peak hours, the metro is definitly the best way to get to the Wardman, because the Woodley Park metro station is on location. While the hotel raves this "on-site" metro station, the station is down a LONG hill, and those with physical disabilities may have difficulty accessing it. Also, the metro station is only serviced by the "red" train, which has stops at more residential areas, and not really the line for tourists. Most tourists who stay at the Wardman have to transfer to the Blue Line, which goes to stops such as Arlington Cemetary, Smithsonian, Federal Triangle (White House,) George Washington/ Georgetown U, and Regan Airport, and the Pentagon and Petagon City mall. 
This hotel is probably the largest hotels that I have ever stayed in and is more designed for the business traveler in mind. There were three conventions going on during my stay. While I saw a few kids there, most of them swarm the pools like bees. Notice how I said "pools" (pluraly) On the last night, I had been rummaging through the green guest services mannuel that all Marriotts have, and I found out they have TWO pools (which came as a surprise, as I thought they only had one.) Businessmen were running though the lobby, which took me a while to find. 
As for the concierege, I thought that they had some idea of where they were, but they mostly relied on paper maps and handouts, and didn't really give that "personal" advice and insight...
The resturaunts were very stuffy and snobby. If your traveling with children, I would definitly recommend the sports bar, which had your basic hamberger and chicken fingers. It seems like every resturuant in the Wardman has its price. There was a stakehouse "Perri's" or something, which was probably the snobbiest and stuffiest place I have ever been. A dinner with four costs $140+, and the waiter we had wasn't good at all. The waiter had the attitude of "well, I'm too good to be working here." I ordered a stake, which was basically just that, a stake; there were no seasonings or side dishes. I'm not a conussoueur of food or anything, I just like to get my money's worth, and 39 dollars for an unseasoned steak is too much. Don't make the same mistake I did, if your hungry, go to the sports bar and get a simple burger; but nothing on site is cheap.

title: “disappointing”
text:
My daughter and I satyed here for 4 nights. We knew it would be basic but were still a little disappointed. It is good to be close to Soho, Greenwich Village etc but the area directly around the hotel is not good for walking at night. The first night we arrived around 8pm and were hungry - we wandered around the corner to find ourselves amongst a queue of men waiting to get into a mission for the homeless, and as two women we felt pretty vulnerable. In the day it's not far to walk to the subway or to nicer areas, but bear this in mind if you are women travelling alone.
Also the beds were not great , the sofa very uncomfortable and the kitchen did not have the basics like a plug in the sink to wash any dishes. The hairdryer cuts out after 30 seconds of use!Don't be misled by their video - this is very basic accommodation and a bill of $1200 for a 4 night stay seems very high to me. I guess it is NY but I am sure there would be rooms of equal standard in slightly nicer areas for a similar price.

title: “Pleasant Hotel, great location”
text: My husband and I spent the weekend at the Michelangelo in mid April, 2005. I booked a standard room through Travelocity and the front desk upgraded us to a Jr. Suite which was like a good sized bedroom (we had to wonder what the standard room was like). Unfortunately our room was near the elevator (and you could hear the "ding" everytime it arrived). There was also a VERY loud birthday party in the room next to us and the whole floor smelled like smoke. When I called the management, someone promptly asked them to tone it down and kept going back until 4am (which is when the party finally ended). We asked for a different room but were told the hotel was sold out. I told the management about the 4am party when I checked out but wasn't offered anything for compensation (didn't really expect to be anyway). The free breakfast was a few different types of muffins, coffee, and juice, very basic. The best part about the hotel is the location. Easy walk to Times Square and Central Park. All in all, my husband didn't think it was worth $225/night - but then we are from San Francisco where $225 would get you a very nice room, so it's hard to judge. All in all not a bad experience.

title: “Can't wait to stay here again”
text:
Everything about my experience was perfect. I stayed here during the upfronts while I was in NYC casting a feature film. My reservation was made via HBO and I was weary since I didn't take care of it myself. My room, while NYC small, was top notch. It was beautiful. The bed was HUGE and incredibly comfortable. The pillows were actually good enough to want to take them home. The bathroom was gorgeous: marble floors and counter with first class soaps and other products. The shower was great, the carpet was even pretty. Everything worked.....the tv, the internet, etc. I even had a view, which is rare in NYC. 
The room service, while VERY expensive was so good I wanted to eat 24/7 (and I kinda did). There were multiple restaurants in the hotel and they were all amazing. I did not interact with one employee who wasn't 100% professional. 
I had a great time and can't wait to go back.
Oh yeah, the neighborhood was central and easy....and there is a really good French restaurant next door.

title: “Average Hotel”
text: My husband surprised me with trip to New York City, so I didn't know where we were staying until arrival. The hotel was in process of renovations, which it is due. Rooms were average,but very small. definitely wouldn't have wanted more than two people in the room. Location was fine; walked alot to TImes Square, which is about 7-8 blocks. My biggest gripe was the remodeling noise. We were on the 14th floor and the noise above us was very loud, We were fortunate enough that the noise started on the morning we were leaving, so we only had to put up with it for one day; However, it was not revealed to my husband that they were in this process; We discovered it upon arrival. Overall average hotel.

title: “Good if you have business in downtown Ft. Worth”
text: I stayed at the hotel for one night while attending a meeting at the hotel in October 2004. My room was very large, comfortable, and quiet. The decor is a bit dated, and the food in the hotel restaurants was just average in my opinion (service was good). The hotel staff was friendly and helpful. This is a good choice if you have business in downtown Ft. Worth, and can pick up a discounted rate.

title: “Beautiful views from the tower”
text: We stayed here for the views from the tower and they did not disappoint - breathtaking. The hotel itself seemed overpriced, though. The hotel seemed a bit stretched thin, a little ragged around the edges. The staff was friendly and the room was clean and comfortable, no complaints there.

title: “Excellent Location!”
text:
We stayed at the Capital Hilton for 5 days and 4 evenings over the Easter weekend. This was the first time we visited DC with all 4 of our kids - ages 13, 11, 7 and 4. For us, the Capital Hilton was centrally located, especially for our tour of the White House. Thus, we were close to everything we had planned to visit, including the Lincoln Memorial, WW II Memorial, Vietnam Memorial, Washington Monument, etc. We walked to Ford's Theater too. We took the Metro to the Capitol and the Supreme Court. 
We stayed in a very large and beautiful junior suite - our family fit comfortably, thanks to the two beds and a pull-out sofa couch. The room was clean, quiet, spacious and well appointed. The bathroom was exceptionally large. There were 2 flat screen TVs in the room too. We ate breakfast 3 mornings in the Executive Lounge - good selection of bagels, muffins, juices and fruit for our kids. We also grabbed a few late night pizzas/flatbreads at the lobby bar one evening after a very long day of sightseeing - excellent food and relaxing setting! The staff at the hotel was exceedingly accommodating and responsive to our needs, including securing us great dinner reservations and a wonderful Sunday brunch reservation in Georgetown. The kids could buy snacks in the gift shop or have beverages in the Executive Lounge - they were happy. We intentionally chose this hotel b/c it did not have a pool - we didn't want the younger kids requesting to spend the day swimming. Instead, we were out very early every morning and did not return back until late in the evening each day. There is a very good ice cream shop close to the hotel, as well as several good places to eat dinner, including, P.J. Clarke's (just across the street) - AWESOME burgers!!! The hotel has an ATM machine in the lobby. The valet parking is expensive - we paid about $160.00 for parking during our stay. Otherwise, our stay was exceptional. I recommend this hotel b/c of it's location, friendly/accommodating staff and quality of their rooms.

title: “Not a good experience for a Hilton Diamond Member”
text:
I just finished staying 2 nights at this property and I'm a Hilton Diamond member. I was "upgraded" to their 4th floor "executive level". Upon entering my room, I find the previous guests' hairs all over the bathroom floor, inside the bath tub and on the shower walls. Urine and cleaning chemical stains were all over the toilet and heavy dust on all the air vents and furniture. Housekeeping didn't leave a "do not disturb sign" when they finished the room, so a housekeeper tried opening my door without knocking at 8:00am on my 2nd day there. I had to tell her my room was occupied as I was staying 2 nights. 
I'm just appalled that Hilton hasn't provied adequate training for their staff, especially in this situation with regards to housekeeping. The restaurant had good food and great service, but the rooms are in desperate need ot help. I won't be returning to this property at all anytime soon.

title: “Nice hotel, great restaurant”
text:
Service was excellent, however, we were given a disabled room, which honestly, was just a little weird to stay in, as there were bars everywhere. The up side was that there was a lot of space. I think they should have notified us about this first however, and I am disappointed about this.
We had the opportunity to have coffee and snacks in the bar downstairs - which has a nice, casual atmosphere. 
The restaurant in the lobby is great. We were very lucky to have this calibre of restaurant at the base of our hotel! Great food and great service.
The hotel is in a nice location, though not much of a night life around us. Walking distance to major sightseeing attractions though.

title: “Fantastic pre cruise hotel.”
text: This hotel is perfectly located for a stay in Seattle. They offer free shuttle anywhere within 1 mile of the hotel. This gets you pretty much anywhere you want to go. The breakfast included is quite nice. Employees were very helpful and pleasant. Highly recommend.

title: “This place is great!!”
text: I was in Jacksonville with my wife, daughter and grandson and we stayed at this hotel. This is a really cool hotel. It's new, very clean and in a great location. I've stayed in several nice hotels (the Ritz Carlton in Cancun, the Peabody in Memphis, the Grove Park Inn in Ashville), but the staff at this hotel was the best of any hotel at which I've stayed. I would like to stay here again and would definitely reccommend it.

title: “Worst Stay in San Francisco”
text: I usually search well before book anywhere to stay but this time, because of it was a last minuite decition to go getaway, I booked it over the phone. Im actually mad at the representitive because he didnt give me coorect infor about this hotel. first of all, I asked for a hotel with 3 star above and this one is 2 star. Second, I requested a fridge in the room and they said that the room has a fridge and a microwave but non of them were there, not only that but awful smell, super small room with a super old TV with 3 channels you can watch, staff were very rude, bad location ( adlut theather is right in front of this hotel) plus homeless people, hookers are almost every corner. DO NOT BOOK with this hotel.

title: “Reasonable, clean and great location. What more can you ask for!”
text:
I was reading reviews of Queen Ann because I will be back in Seattle for my second visit. Last time, about 6 yrs ago, I found this hotel to be just as it is being described now. That means I'll be going back for another stay.
Thanks to all those who take the time to contribute to these forums and make travel easier for the rest of us.

title: “Close to Airport”
text: We stayed here the night before an early morning flight out of the airport, mainly based on Trip Advisor reviews and proximity to the airport. It was very clean and comfy. The room was huge. We got a good night's sleep. It is in a very busy area, and being from VA, I find the TX frontage road/loop business hard to get a handle on, so finding dinner after checking in was a bit of a challenge for me. There is a restaurant within walking distance, but it s a New Orleans-style place with mostly seafood and my husband wasn't up for that. The main complaint I have is that our flight was so early that we had to check out of the hotel before 6am, which is when the continental breakfast began. The do have coffee in the rooms and there is coffee in the lobby 24-7. When we checked in we asked if there would be any food out for folks checking out early, and the woman who check us out said the breakfast wouldn't be out, but that there would be a few things we "could grab and go" with. However there was nothing when we left. We ended up flying out on empty stomachs (no time to grab food in the airport, and no food on the plane). We had our first meal of the day at the Atlanta airport during our 45min layover. I would expect that a hotel situated so close to the airport would start their breakfast early enough to accommodate the people leaving to catch early-morning flights, or that they really would at least start putting out grab-and go foods at 5am. If we had not been assured at check-in that there would be something to grab, we would have purchased breakfast foods the night before to prepare in our room.

title: “Lay off the Vintage Court!!”
text:
I booked a 10 day stay at the Vintage Court through the internet and after reviewing the reviews we went there with some trepidation - we needn't have bothered - 
the staff were friendly and helpful - the room was clean but on the small(ish) side, as was the bathroom - but neither were intended to be used as a dance hall - we found them quite adequate - the continental breakfast of coffee and a muffin was exactly what I expected from a continental breakfast - the evening wine tasting was fun and we met a number of very nice people there - we discussed the hotel with a number of them and none had any complaints - my only adverse comment is that if you book an early call - and there is an alarm clock in the rooms - ensure that the details are entered in the diary and not just on a piece of paper - all in all we had a great time - the location is great unless you are adverse to walking a couple of blocks - and if we were returning to San Francisco for we would certainly stay there again -- For those who want the Hilton type of accommodation and service - book at the Hilton and pay the Hilton prices!!

title: “What a pleasant surprise”
text: Older hotel, redone, clean, great 2 bedroom suite for a reasonable amount of money. If you want to be on the riverwalk. The service and attitude of staff would be hard to beat. It has been a long time since I have seen such consistently nice hotel employees. Free breakfast...I think happy hour too, however, not there t that time of day.

title: “Oustanding, thoughtful service...”
text: Concierge Michael and front desk staff go out of their way to anticipate your needs providing personalized suggestions, solutions and amenities ensuring your comfort.

title: “First Time Staying, Certainly Not the Last!”
text: Stayed at the Crowne Plaze Times Square for the first time after many trips to NYC! Sorry we didn't find this hotel sooner. Very spacious, clean rooms with excellent service and staff. Location couldn't be better for theatre, shopping and dining. Highly recommend this hotel!!

title: “Very nice for an overnight stay”
text: I stayed here overnight when I had a flight cancelled, the transfer from the airport was very convenient via the airport shuttle. The rooms were spacious, comfortable and clean. The bar downstairs was open late with decent food options and good service. Hopefully you don't get stuck at O'Hare for a flight delay, ever, but if you do this is a very pleasant place to spend the evening.

title: “Highly recommended”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for about ten days in November 2009. It's nearly a year later and I've been intending to write this review ever since. Of all the hotel experience I've had, this was probably the most positive. The first few days I was on my own and after an incident, the hotel staff were incredibly supportive and helpful, the manager even stepping in to make sure everything was ok, then checking up on me subsequently. I couldn't have asked for a better response.
Staff were friendly, breakfast was plentiful, location is incomparable, rates were reasonable, rooms were spacious and clean. I'd stay here again in a heartbeat.

title: “Excellent hotel, superb staff and great location”
text: We travelled to NYC last year and were very fortunate to stay at the Park South Hotel, I always assumed that for the price we paid it would be very econolodge/travel lodge style - however we were surprised by the helpfulness of the staff from the moment we arrived. The room was well sized for a New York hotel, the bathroom was gorgeous and the hotel had a lovely vibe; I also enjoyed my newspaper each morning. Breakfast was good, and the Black Duck restaurant was worth every penny.

title: “The Bahia is just ok”
text: We stayed at the Bahia on 2-13-06 to 2-17-06.It was just ok, the room we had was 136 on the private beach side, I was not that impressed.The room smelled old the fan in the batroom made alot of noise the sliding glass door was hard to shut. we told them a couple times but it was never fixed.The rooms need to be updated big time.The pool and the hot tub are nice.The Bahia would not be my first choice.I would stay some where else.

title: “Stay away.”
text: I stay at roughly 6 different hamPton inns per year. This one is not good! Lots of problems, too many to list but the icing on the cake was they forgot to clean our room on our last night stay. Us we got in at 9pm and were beat with 2 young kids. Stay away!

title: “Nice place, good value, convenient location.”
text: I wanted a hotel that was reasonable in price, located in downtown, clean, and offered self parking at a reasonable rate rather than valet parking which I refuse to use primarely because I don't want some stranger driving my vehicle and I'm not lazy enough to require someone else to park my car for me. I got all of those things at the Executive Hotel Pacific. The room was small but comfortable. We were upgraded to a king room when I had reserved a queen which was a nice surprise and I'm guessing doesn't happen everytime. Parking was nearby, easy in and out, and cheap compared to other hotels I had called. I'll stay there again if I ever need to go to the city.

title: “Commercial Real Estate Broker - Great for business meetings”
text: Over 1,600 meet at the Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers for a National Summit and was greeted by a very friendly and helpful registration clerk. She told me about some of the features of the hotel that I was not expecting, upgraded me to a nicer room and took time to answer some basic questions that I had. I don't typically get that kind of service at other hotels. The hotel was neat and clean, service was very good and not once in the two days I stayed there, did I have a negative experience. One more very important thing for me is to have a quiet room for sleeping. In some hotels, you can even hear people walking down the hallway. Not here!!! I know that the hotel business is a "People Business", and the Sheraton has their service and program down very well. I would encourage anyone to consider the Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers. I know I will be back.

title: “Nice hotel, but stay away from the rooms close to reception!!”
text: Had a fair stay, although beds need replacement. However, if you end up in a room close to the main building, forget a good night of sleep due to the unbearable sound of the (I guess) airconditioning units next to the building. Really loud and even got the room trembling...Very friendly staff!

title: “Beautiful Place that Smells Like an Old Lady”
text:
The Henley Park may be the grand dame of hotels near the convention center - unfortunately my room smells like a grand dame as well. To be clear, this isn't the musty grandma smell, this is the 'my nose is going so I bathe in perfume' smell. I'm not even sure from where it is emanating as it wasn't in the halls, but I think it may be over-use of heavily scented cleaners (the room is spotless!), or perhaps misguided spritzing with an avalanche of air freshener.
Upon check in the staff were wonderful, the room is comfortable, and the bed is great. Got to love 6 fluffy pillows on my king bed with a lovely white fluffy duvet. I don't even mind the view of the construction - I'm an early riser and I didn't come for the view. The complimentary internet is working well, and, although not my personal style, the colonial style furnishing are nicely done. The room is pleasant, large for an historic venue, and the windows actually open, a feature for which I am eternally grateful or else I would have to change rooms.
Weather.com says it is 34 degrees out with wind chills bringing it down into the low 20s. With all of the windows open, I'm airing out the place and it is getting more pleasant by the minute, although I now have to wear my coat to type.
So, overall the place is lovely, but smelly. If you are sensitive to smells (and I admit that I am, but I also spend 60 days a year in hotels and have never run into one quite this pungent), then this may not be a good match for you. Especially in winter. Thank goodness it isn't snowing.

title: “Good location, and average + value”
text:
Traveled from Paris and stayed in SF at La Villa Florence. Planned 3 days and finally stayed 4. Which does not mean everything is great. I would rate this hotel 3.5 /5 for the location, quick and effective check in. I choose a King Size Room. 
My spouse and I were given a 7th floor room, not on Powell street, which is good for a nice sleeping without any noise. Room are a bit small. Super clean, well decorated. beware of bathroom size : not an American, neither European size. They are SMALL. 
3.5 /5 instead of 4 is due to
* size of bathroom
* quality of bed that is very correct but not the best I have deal with
* I have been charged 45 usd for parking but had no car! If i did not realize it 24hours later and give a call, I would probably have been charged for this!! First time ever it happens to me in the US
Overall a good quality/price ratio, with ideal location

title: “Magnificent Monticello”
text: I booked the Monticello Inn for my family, after reading the positive reviews written here, and was very glad I did. Our suite was huge with two TV's & even bath robes. The concierge went out of his way to get us on our city tour, as we were running a bit late. The location is superb with tram stops & shopping right there. Everything was clean and lovely and I couldn't recommend it enough. Also the best coffee can be found around the corner in the Westfield Centre at Peet's Coffee....

title: “Affordable and well located”
text: Got a great $90/night deal through Hotwire. Easy $30 ride from IAD on SuperShuttle. The hotel lobby is being renovated, so a bit of a mess, but check-in was easy and I found the room clean and comfortable. Needed late dining and their lobby bar was a fine option. Internet was free with HHonors. Great location for US Chamber of Commerce and White House.

title: “Best Place To Stay In Memphis”
text:
I have stayed in Hotels in Memphis 4 - 5 nights every week for the last 4 months. I have stayed at several Hotels, such as Hyatt Place, Holiday Inn Select, Courtyard by Marriot, and several others. When I found the Double Tree I found MY HOTEL. It is very possible that I will be staying in Memphis every week for then next Year. This is the only place that I will stay.
 I have traveled extensively for the last 37 years. I have to say, all things considered, out of ever place I have ever stayed, this is my favorite Hotel to stay in. My wife was able to stay with me a few days this week. When she saw the awesome Hospitality in the Hotel and also the Restaurant, she said, “the way they treat you here, it is a wonder you even want to come home.”
The location is great. Anything that you need from Restaurants to Mall’s are within 5 minutes. The Lynchburg Restaurant in the Hotel is great for Breakfast or Dinner. The Hostess and waitresses are first class. If you have not figured it out yet, this is my kind of place.
Rating A +++++++++++++
Hotel Appearance: 10
Hotel Location: 10
Cleanliness of Rooms: 10
Front Desk Employees: 10
Hotel Management: 10 ++++++++++

title: “WORST PLACE EVER STAYED”
text:
If you want a truck stop this is your place but as accommodation close to beaches and restaurants this is not your place we book 3 nights with this place and when we checked into it, it was not what it was made out to be, The room was basic which is fine but not closed to anything at all and after a $70 cab fare checked straight back out and went and stayed in Santa Monica which was the best decision ever made. 
Do not stay here unless you want a basic stay not near anything or central to anything it's not a tourist area.

title: “A modern contemporary outstanding hotel with great service and amenities.”
text:
A hidden gem in downtown Dallas. The service was impeccable, the rooms very trendy and probably the most comfortable bed I have ever slept in.
The Aloft is walking distance to most restaurants and convenient to most downtown destinations.
The only negative was the heating/air conditioning system in the rooms that was difficult to control. All employees were very responsive to all our needs.
I would highly recommend this hotel for business or pleasure.

title: “It is a Sheraton...with lots of quirkiness!”
text: So many odd things happened during our stay that it is hard to explain. The front desk staff is nice enough, and they have the 'smile and nod' response down pat, but only when pressed do rooms appear that somehow were a minute ago booked!! On the other hand, the front desk manager didn't hesitate a moment to give me his direct cell phone number so I could contact him with any further problems. Unfortunately, I had to call him at least twice more during my 4 day stay. One evening the meal in the District restaurant was fantastic! Really really good. The next time we dined there, the service was non-existent and the restaurant manager was defensive and had a terrible attitude. The gym is fabulous! One of the best around, but there is no spa at all and the pool, even though advertised as heated, is cold and small (although the hot tub is nice). The view from my room was amazing and the bed and bedding were great, but I think that housekeeping is the real weak link in this hotel. When I first entered my room there was a used towel and robe hanging on the back of the bathroom door! Disgusting. It took several calls to get extra hangers and they were very stingey with their toiletries. The bathroom was great, very spacious, and the complementary bottled water was a nice touch. But paying for wifi is an insult, particularly since you can use computers in their 'connect lounge' for free and the wifi in the Club Lounge on the 28th floor is free. A hotel should be ashamed of itself to nickel and dime a traveler like that, especially when they look you in the eye and tell you how much they care about your comfort. The location was very convenient for us next to the convention center. The hotel does not have a complementary airport shuttle, which is outrageous since the airport is only about 3 miles away. The private van costs $12 one way and leaves the hotel every half hour. Overall, the service was sub-par, the gym was great and the lack of value was hard to take.

title: “Homewood Suites fan now!”
text: I had booked a reservation for one night for my husband and I while visiting family for the Christmas vacation. I had used TripAdvisor for the background info and was not disappointed. It was our last night in FL and we were exhausted. We checked in around 6:oopm with the nice front desk staff and there was an excellent dinner buffet with beer and wine waiting for us. What a relief! We ate until we were full and then went to our room which was a stone's throw from the main lobby, so my husband kept walking back to get another glass of beer or wine for us while we just chilled and watched TV! The suite was spacious, clean and there was even a bag of popcorn for us to pop! The room was also very quiet and the little store was open all night when I had to run over for some aspirin (too much wine, perhaps?) ;) The next morning, the paper was on the front step and the breakfast buffet was served in the lobby--it was awesome. They even had waffle batter premixed and in little cups so you could make your own waffles! The whole thing only cost $70 for the night--what a deal! The only thing I think I thought could be better was having some conditioner (instead of just shampoo) offered and maybe some better coffee in the lobby...but that's just me, I'm a coffee snob. We are sold now..before we go anywhere anymore we will check to see if they have a Homewood Suites around!

title: “Really great Stay”
text:
