I stayed at the Hotel Monaco, Washington D.C. with 3 of my sisters for one evening. We chose this hotel at the recommendation of my sister who lives in Arlington, works in D.C. and was celebrating a very special birthday. When I booked the hotel, I asked the reservationist if 2 rooms could be adjoined and mentioned that the birthday was a special one. I was assured that this could be done. I called back about a month later, 3 weeks before arrival to make sure the reservations were confirmed and that rooms could be adjoined. I emphasized the significance of the day but I did not ask the hotel to do anything special.
When we arrived, we found the hotel to be beautiful and the staff very friendly. The gentleman that checked us was very professional and told us a bit of the history about the hotel. He briefly noted that we would have a surprise. Thinking nothing more about this we entered our rooms which were fabulous! After about 30 minutes champagne, balloons, a small cheese plate and 2 cup cakes were sent to the room along with a Happy Birthday note to my sister!!. Can I tell you that we were so surprised and happy; it was completely unexpected. All 4 of us travel quite a bit so we are used to hotels and very little surprises us. To whomever took it upon themselves to send the "surprise" ..thank you! My sister was so happy. It made our visit all the more special.
We had a great time in Washington D.C. and really great visit at the hotel. The rooms are beautiful and very well appointed. I had not heard of Klimpton Hotels before this visit nor of the Hotel Monaco...but I was certainly pleased.

title: “Great hotel for my purposes”
text: I always stay in Holiday Inn Express Sorrento Valley when I'm in San Diego, they always welcome me with a bag of goodies that at least make me feel good... All personnel is always very nice and I would like to give a special thank to Elisa Santos for all her help and as always she is very helpful, I really appreciate it.

title: “Beautiful hotel in beautiful spot”
text: We stayed in this hotel in 2002 and was close in price to the Holiday Inn at Fisherman's wharf. The hotel is beautiful inside and out and the rooms are a great size especially for San Fran.

title: “Good Rates, Average Hotel”
text: Well located for a visit to Baltimore, very near the sports stadia, convention hall, the light rail from the airport, and the University of Maryland professional schools. A short walk to the inner harbor. Lobby is ok, but not large. Since the location is in the inner city, in addition to being near the aforementioned sights, one is also, if one walks the wrong way, near some inner city street life. Restaurant and parking on premises (for a fee). Business center is available but computers, for some reason, don't have Microsoft Office Suite making it difficult to do more than browse the internet for local information. Hallways are ok and rooms are on the small side. Beds were not particularly comfortable, but not uncomfortable either. Staff was very nice and helpful to us when one of our party broke a foot and needed to borrow a wheelchair during our 5-day stay. Hotel rates were on the reasonable side given the location. For a bit more cost one can stay at the nearby (and nicer) Holiday Inn or the even more expensive Hilton. Days Inn is a budget choice, not a bad choice but not the best choice.

title: “What a great place to stay!”
text: We stayed here for one night and arrived after a long flight and were so happy with this place! The rooms were huge and the beds were so big that I felt like a little princess in there. Everything was very clean and the room was conveniently equipped with a microwave and fridge. I slept really good but we definitely needed the AC since it was a warm night outside. The breakfast was also very good, I enjoyed the Cheerios, the Mexican omlette and the sausage. Unfortunately the juice machine was not working but other than that it was great. I also loved the location of it since there was a Denny's and a Mexican place close to it and the next day it only took us 2 mins with the car to get the the Outlet Center. If I ever come to Anthem again, I will for sure stay here again!

title: “Best Holiday Inn Express in Houston”
text:
From the street the Holiday Inn Reliant/Medical Center looks like any good hotel. The interior is very modern and warm and the rooms are large with all the amenities. Plenty of great shopping and restaurants close by with perfect central location.
This Holiday Inn is much better than my previous favorite Hampton Inn Galleria and about $30.00 less per night.

title: “Clean room, large bathroom, quiet hotel”
text: Two friends and I decided to share a room in Dallas while we attended a conference at American Airlines Center! The room was perfect! Comfortable beds! Large bathroom! Large shower! Vanity big enough for two women to primp and preen together! Which is wonderful when three women are sharing a room! Also, the hotel was very quiet!

title: “Hip,fun,and stylish... the staff have a way of making your day!”
text:
The Hotel Deca will not ever try to outshine its competition with fancy meeting rooms and swanky chairs around a roaring fire... Although, it could!!! The rooms are just stylish enough, all with a view. The adjacent coffee shop screams "Welcome to Seattle"...
No, The Hotel Deca makes its mark with its staff. I could go over every small experience and relate to you the smile here or the helpful gesture there. I encountered those types of things at every turn. Two staff members went above and beyond making my trip and enjoyable one. Firstly, Colin,.... you are the man. Thanks again for the help setting up my week stay with you, your patience set the tone that my long week was going to be made most comfortable, once i made it home to Hotel Deca. Thanks again Colin. Once at Hotel Deca, walk downstairs to "The District" this place is very nice, food and drinks all very good and affordable. The staff all great, but special thanks to Robyn. Great bartender, let me talk her ear off. Without people like this its all just brick and mortar.... thanks guys. 
-e

title: “Its Ok - Rooms are small”
text: The staff is friendly and very helpful.. Rooms are very small. 8ft x 8ft is my guess, not including the bathroom and doorway. If all you are doing is sleeping, it is ok. If you plan on doing business work in this room.. it is not comfortable. Internet access is $13 /per 24hours. Only 3 hangers and 3 hooks to hang up your clothes and very little drawer space. We were at this hotel for 6 nights. Two people, large luggage and no place to really put your luggage or clothes. Bathroom is very small. I am not a big person and my elbows hit the wall and the vanity when sitting down on the toilet. :-) There is no shower door, but a half wall. The shower is a rain shower, which I like, but also has a shower wand - which was on, facing toward me when I turned the shower on. - sprayed right out the shower opening and into the room.. Awesome... things got a little we and had to figure out how to turn that shower wand off.. it was comical. View of our room is the other part of this building.. can see other rooms. Shades and curtains truly black out the room.. At 11:30 in the morning, you could not tell what time it was.. There is not coffee maker (no room for one). I did ask for a iron and board - which they brought to me. There is a hair dryer, small box fridge that is full of their expensive stuff, Had to take out some of their drinks to put in a few individual bottles of soda that we bought elsewhere. I marked the Spa as terrible - only because there isnt one. Work out facility is two rooms converted - just cardio - elliptical, treadmill and a ski machine - no weights, exercise balls, or mats... It is just a block from Central Park - nice. and walking distance to Times Square - also nice. So, over all - so so experience at the hotel.

title: “Disgraceful and misleading”
text:
This was one of the absolute worst hotel experiences of my life and this comes from someone that spends 150 nights a year in hotels! Not only was my quoted rate (I showed my itinerary upon check-in) not honored (upcharged $90 on second night of stay), the desk clerk upon check-in was disinterested and really embraced the "tough-crap" attitude ("Hey, I can't change what the computer says!") I'm sure you are looking for in employees. The room was a disgrace, a closet really, housekeeping was poor, air conditioner never satisfactorily cooled the room (plus it was noisy and since the room was 8'x10', it hung over the bed-the only place to set my suticase was in the shower; HONESTLY) and the t.v. barely functioned. I desperately tried to move after the first night but couldn't find a vacancy. Utell should be ashamed of this hotel bearing it's corporate name. A disgrace.
The photos are misleading, even the poor ones by the secret traveler make it apear better than it really was.

title: “Best Hotel Ever!”
text: We stayed at the Hotel Contessa while attending the APIC convention. We have stayed at other hotels on the riverwalk, but NONE even came close to the Hotel Contessa. The rooms were beautiful, the beds were comfortable, and breakfast at the restaurant was exceptional. Above all, the hotel staff was friendly and helpful - especially Eddie G. who greeted us each time he saw us and made us feel so welcome. From now on, the Hotel Contessa will be our hotel of choice each time we visit San Antonio.

title: “MAXWELL HOTEL SEATTLE”
text: Loved the hotel, the staff and the location. The rooms were excellent and the bed was extremely comfortable. The room amenities were just right. They have all you would need for a few nights. The hotel is located perfectly so you can visit the Seattle Center and all the activities there, plus you can catch the monorail down to Pike's Mkt. We had a lovely time. My only complaint is that we came early 10 am and checked to make sure that our reservation was right before we took off and did our days activities. Check in was at 3pm. We came back at 5pm expecting to be able to go straight to our room. It was not ready yet. I understand that they had a full house, but then I think you need to have more people available to make sure the rooms are done in time for the next group coming in. I really wanted to freshen up before dinner and that wasn't possible. I felt bad for the staff on the front desk, as you could see they had had a difficult day, but they were still nice to us and visa versa.They gave us a good recommendation for dinner Petit Toulouse (a little pricey for a family, but happy hour worked perfectly). We went to dinner and when we came back our room was ready. I really appreciated their locked private garage and would be willing to try them again. Hopefully soon :)

title: “Our favourite hotel in Boston”
text: If you are planning a stay in Boston, the Four Seasons is the place to stay. We have stayed here in several times and never disappointed. Service, location and staff are just great. We will be back in March.

title: “WOW! The rooms!!!!!”
text:
Well we tried yet another Seattle hotel.
Gotta say I loved the lobby. Yes it's the 80's but who cares.
We booked the 2 bedroom suite.
King in one and 2 doubles in the 2nd.
Each room has it's own bathroom. Perfect for the 5 of us.
My kids loved having their own room. So did we.
The living area was fantastic, nice living room, full kitchen and a dining table for 4. Plus a small balcony.
3 TV's total as well.
The room was very clean and also seems to have been updated for the age of the property.
We were also on a nice quiet side street.
Check in was fast, and free coffee and snax in the lobby.
Nice work out room. 
1 small pool for little ones, 2nd larger (not by much) pool for the bigger people and a hot tub.
I still dislike when a hotel charges for parking, I think it's gouging.
We want to stay next September for 3 or 4 nights, but I hesitate having to pay up to $100 dollars for parking.
It is a good 20 minute walk to the Needle, but very doable.
No need to take your car once here. Rail to Downtown right outside the hotel as well.
Yes there is construction but it's only during the day. It did make it a challenge to get to the Hotel, but I just used my Spidey senses. 
Very good chance we may book this next September for our annual trip to Seattle, but the parking charge may deter me.
It would have scored a 5 but parking......... 
Hope this helps.

title: “Stay in the main building - newer, larger rooms.”
text:
This hotel is my go-to when visiting San Francisco.
Positives:
- It has a pretty convenient location that is accessible by taxi or cable car if you want. (Parking your car is $ as with all other hotels in the area). 
- Accommodations are excellent. The rooms are clean, the beds are really quite heavenly, and the rooms in the main tower are spacious. (The smaller, more dated rooms in the other locations of the hotel have equally nice beds and appointments but the bathrooms are much older and the rooms are significantly smaller. Not a big problem if you're going to be out and about most of the time or if you are only here a night, but paying full price, I'd try to stay in the newer rooms.)
- The concierge is very helpful and friendly. 
- The city views are beautiful. 
Negatives: 
- Food here is pricey, but it's a Fairmont and it's San Francisco. I didn't eat at the hotel except for a breakfast that was included anyway. The buffet was quite nice quality food, but I wouldn't pay full price for it. There are better places to eat in the city. 
- Parking, as stated above if you're driving. 
- Room size if you're staying in the older rooms (specifically the bathroom)
Bottom line: If you need just a place to crash don't spend the money. If you are going to enjoy your time, like the finer things but don't want to pay exorbitantly, and prefer a bed that isn't a concrete slab, this is your place.

title: “Great Place for Drinks”
text: We followed the advice of folks and went up to the rotating bar for drinks. It's a cover of $8 per person if you are not staying there, $8 for beer, $16 for a margarita but the view was fabulous. We used a Marriott rewards point gift card and it was basically free. I thought the dessert bar was overpriced...a la carte items can be purchased at the bar on a lower floor (6th or maybe 8th floor) and that overlooks Times Square (we didn't go there, though)

title: “Great location”
text: This hotel was in the best location for getting around, right outside is the cable car stop. The hotel was very clean and the rooms were a good sizes with a fair size bathroom.

title: “Great Hotel-Cheap rates”
text: My husband and adult children recently visited LA to check out the tourist attractions. We were very impressed with this hotel but were initially skeptical as the prices were low. However, we were pleasantly surprised. The rooms were modernly decorated and very clean. Each of our rooms had a microwave and mini fridge which is always nice for leftovers and water. Our continental breakfast was perfect and much appreciated-my husband enjoyed fresh waffles every morning while I enjoyed cerial and toast. My boys all enjoyed the selection of pastries as well as some scrambled eggs and juice. We were extremely happy with the helpful desk staff. Every time we asked for directions or suggestions of places to eat and shop, they were quick to help and even printed off directions for us. The location of this hotel was also great as was pretty central to where we needed to go. Definately recommend this hotel to anyone who is visiting LA.

title: “Oct 2012”
text: Room initially had smoke odor. We left door open & staff offered air freshner. Shower spout came flying off the first time we used the shower. The next day it was recaulked - did not fix problem, continued to creep off why you were taking a shower. Light did not work. The second room had a toilet that ran continuously all night. If you needed to flush toilet you had to take off tank lid & adjust the flapper each time. Asked for a credit on the second room - was refused

title: “Sweet Stay”
text:
My husband, toddler, and I recently stayed here and it was a great place. We had a million dollar view of Boston from our Harbor side room, at an AWESOME family rate. (You have to request it). The room was very posh and comfortable. Our daughter could not get enough of the glass elevator rides with views of the airport. Outside the back of the hotel is a great Harbor walk that leads you to a wonderful outdoor public park, or you can catch a water taxi into the city.
The only thing to note is that there are NO amenities nearby. So, unless you want to eat in the hotel's restaurant (which is pretty good but pricey) there are no other options for food, drink, snacks...
We would definitely stay here again and spend more time on their back porch in front of their gas fireplaces with a drink from their well stocked bar, looking at the great view of Boston.

title: “The best thing about this airport”
text: I actually look forward to travel delays just so I can stay here. After a long day of traveling, the beds shower and food are the best!. This is by far my favorite weston property in the US. it is so soothing to walk inside and feel like you are in a posh lodge retreat somewhere. It is amazing to just be able to wake up at your leisure and just walk out of the hotel to your terminal. Although the security line to get out of the hotel is fast, you will still have to deal with people that dont regularly travel and have no idea how to go through security so they hold up the line... but its all ok when you're standing there with your cup of starbucks and the WSJ journal after a good nights sleep.

title: “Shame about the View”
text:
Booked 3 nights in Boston through Virgin Holidays as part of a week's stay in USA.
Got room 315 at the Lenox. It is small by American standards and the bathroom was tiny. There was mould all around the bath and everytime we used the shower, there was water on the floor afterwards, so we had to put towels on the floor.
The view was of some sort of heating ventilation on a flat roof. we couldn't even tell what the weather was like so just kept the curtains closed all the time.
When we asked if we could move to a room with a better view, we were told that we would have to pay a charge of $60. The guy on the desk was totally disinterested, although the person who took our bags to and from the room was very helpful.
There are no tea/coffee making facilities in the room so you have to order room service if you want anything. 
The lobby was recently renovated, but how often do you use that apart from when you are waiting to leave?
The only good thing for us was the central location.

title: “Perfect location, great hotel”
text: First time in NY so didn't know what to expect but this hotel was brilliant. Very friendly and helpful staff (though they could do with stools instead of having to stand all the time). Clean and cool room and free wifi. Amazing location - 5 or 10 minutes walk to Times Square and near 5th avenue. Will definitely come back.

title: “Great Service”
text:
This was probably between a three and a half star to a four star hotel. Guest services were outstanding, we had two employees ask if we needed help between walking in and getting to the hotel desk.
 We ate at the hotel's cafe on the 2nd floor for a quick bite after checking in and found the steak sandwich to be the most tender we've ever tasted.
 Hot water in the bathroom was almost instant and the towels were nice and thick. 
We paid about 100 a night through priceline and I think parking at the hotel was 21 dollars a night.
Feel free to ask any questions.

title: “Great stay, very helpful and friendly staff!”
text: We had an amazing experience at this hotel. It was in a prime location, close to major shopping area and gino's pizza east. Hotel room had really great view and was clean. The only thing that I did not like was finding a spider near the bed.

title: “Good stay”
text:
My wife and I blended a business trip with a great weekend in NYC. Although the hotel is very pricey - we stayed in one of the mid-floor suites. 
The best thing about this hotel is the view. It is incredible. Floor to ceiling glass. The shower has a crank window to enjoy the outdoor air while showering. The beds are very nice, large and comfortable. Room was very clean but somewhat small.
Service was good and staff very friendly. Elevators very slow and busy on Sunday morning trying to checkout.
Neighborhood is great if you enjoy the locals and don't like hanging out with tourists. One of the best restaurants is on the corner, great wine list and unbelievable staff....I believe the name is Enotech, nevertheless it is excellent.
I will definitely stay here again especially if I can book at the right price.

title: “Not a Hotel - A Crummy Hostel”
text:
Some of the other reviews here say they paid $20. Well, for that price, I'd stay almost anywhere. And, if you're down with staying at a hostel, at least they give you a private room, which is a definite step up from most hostels.
But, as a hotel, this place fails, hard. It's pretty clean, I guess, but I fell hard for the deceptions presented in the website. I guess when people say that "historic building" is code for "falling apart old structure," I should listen. My naive reading of the website gave me the impression it was going to be some kind of quaint red-brick B&B sort of place, but miraculously at a much more affordable price. Instead, I get a full-on, no doubt about it, youth hostel. The website says they've repainted the walls and recarpeted the floors - whoop-de-doo. The place still looks, and feels, in sore need of being torn down altogether and replaced with a newer, shinier, sleeker, nicer building.
They fail to mention that the wi-fi is only available in the lobby, that the rooms don't have private bath/shower or toilet, that no shampoo or soap or amenities of that sort are provided at all... I know $65 is pretty cheap as hotels go, but I paid that last week for a stupid corporate-chain airport hotel, and got a proper hotel experience - wifi in the room, private bath/shower with all the tiny bottles and other basic hotel amenities, a spotlessly clean room, a huge, super comfy hotel bed... I am checking out of the Allen Lee as soon as I can, and going somewhere else.

title: “Great place to stay!”
text:
This hotel is great - everything LP suggests - great location with excellent public transport links to everywhere (Cable car, BART, Muni buses and taxi rank all within a block), sparklingly clean rooms, friendly helpful staff, and great prices for central SF. Other reviews have mentioned the lift, the breakfast and the room size. The breakfast is toast, muesli and good coffee - a great choice when you are staying in a foodie city and are likely to be eating large quantities of great food at all other meals. The room is certainly smaller than a suite at the Ritz (although larger than my own bedroom at home [I live in England]), but there is so much to do in SF I was not there much so it was more than adquate. Now the lift - I was staying on the top floor of the hotel (8), and timed how long it took in the lift to get from the lobby to my floor. 46 seconds. Not so long I think you will agree. I must say though that at busy times (breakfast, and when the staff are servicing the rooms - there is not a service lift) it can take ages for the lift to actually arrive at your floor..... still though if you are that impatient there are stairs...
Overall I loved the Stratford - I recommend it highly and will certainly be back!!

title: “Just Typical”
text:
I stayed recently at this Hampton Inn in Indianapolis, IN for a volleyball tournament with my family and our teams. Overall my impression of the hotel was that it is a typical Hampton property. Nothing bad, nothing good. Just average. The inside looked as though it had been refreshed recently and there were nice touches.....dark woods in the rooms, large dressing closet in the room and generally clean and functional. 
On the other hand the rooms we had and that our daughter had were somewhat small. If you are alone in a king room this room was ideal. We had me, my wife and my son and it was very crowded. One of the smallest hotel rooms I have every had. Not that it was a deal breaker but it was noticable. Breakfast was fine. Enough to eat (even with the 30 volleyball girls attacking the breakfast bar all at once) but probably not for those other visiting guests. The staff kept it stocked as best they could. The hotel was clean and we had no issues.
The only negative I could find was the staff at the front desk seemed stiff, less than interested and somewhat difficult to deal with. Again, not a deal breaker but would have been nice to have been felling more welcomed....especially in light of the fact that we brought in over 30 teenage (17-19 year old) girls who will soon be consumers of hotel rooms when they grow up and their families so we had many rooms and keep the hotel hopping. 
Overall.....a servicable stay!

title: “Great location, great service!”
text: I would like to commend the W Chicago City Center's concierge service overall, particularly that of concierge Eden. The service we received from Eden was truly first class, from contacting us to set up sightseeing and reservations prior to our trip, to checking in on every last event we had booked during and following our trip. The service was really outstanding and made our visit to Chicago easy and fun!

title: “A great place to stay”
text: Our stay at the Hotel Chandler could not have been better. At arrival, we were met by a staff that was extremely courteous and helpful. From the doorman to the people at the front desk, they went out of their way to help us with transporation and recommendations for dining and entertainment, Our room was very clean and was as spacious as any that you will get in the City. The location on 31st and 5th was centrally located to the 4/6 subway and walking distance to Times Square. We would love to stay there again.

title: “Excellent”
text:
On the Ave was definitely one of the best things of my stay in NY. The hotel was really well located. The zone is pretty with diners, markets, bakeries and practically anything you would need around. Best thing, two blocks away from the subway and it gets you to time square in 5 minutes, to the financial district in 15. 
The service was amazing. People were great, attentive and very accommodating. The rooms are small but they have everything you need and if they don't, be sure that the staff will do their best to get it for you. 
I definitely recommend it.

title: “very good location”
text:
We stayed there for two nights and really enjoyed our stay.
The room was big, clean and quiet despite overlooking the street.
The breakfast served in the hotel bar was good but we didn't have as much choice as we had in other hotels during our trip.
We were also disappointed not to be able to get boiling water for tea on a sunday evening.

title: “Back Bay Charm”
text:
My wife and l spent one week at this Hotel. From the moment we arrived at midnight without any luggage, which had been misplaced ex Australia, the staff could not of been more helpful.
They provided us with the necesities of life and a late night upgrade.
Breakfast was first class, as was the room.
Whilst the views are tainted by the location, the location from a tourist point of view was awesome.
 Will gladly return next year.

title: “average NY hotel with great location”
text:
For sure this hotel needs updating, but our room although small, was clean, sheets clean, no bedbugs (I checked - paranoid about hotel bedbugs), King bed very comfortable, bathroom very clean, front desk courteous, not warm. Room was noisy (9th floor, corner of Madison and 38th) but used the AC to mask the noise and slept fine. White curtains could have used a good wash. 
 Let's face it - you're not in NY to stay in a hotel room, you just sleep there. This hotel is all about location - excellent! Starbucks was two blocks away on Madison for our morning coffee, and we had a nice dinner at the Park Avenue Tavern two blocks away (Park Ave near 39th or 40th) when we were too tired to walk any further.

title: “A unique experience”
text:
When I found out that I was staying at the Hotel Figueroa to attend a conference, I started looking at these reviews. Based on what is written here, I was truly not looking forward to my stay there. 
I was attending the NBTA (National Business Travel Assocation Conference) in LAX. I know travel and have seen many different types of hotels in different cities around the world. 
This is the most unique hotel that I have ever seen. I was very skeptical when I arrived and saw the decor, the darkness, the hallways and then most of all the door knob with no deadbolt, the simple key that unlocked the door, and chain lock on the door. 
This hotel takes some getting used to, but I found that by the second night, the place had grown on me. I wanted it to be clean, not have bugs, and to feel safe. I got all of this from the Figueroa. 
The concrete floors in your room are very unusual. I naturally expected them to be dirty but they were not. Neither the concrete floor or the area rugs felt dirty under foot. 
There is no room service, no coffemaker in room, no ice machine (but there is a small fridge with ice tray in it in the room), no business center, no free internet (that I could see). 
The staff was friendly and very helpful. The breakfast served in the lobby was good and adequate - not overpriced. The accommodations are unique and sparse, but all-in-all, my stay there was not so bad. 
The hotel was busy with tourists. Everyone was quiet and friendly. 
It was a unique experience to stay there. I don't know that I'd go out of my way to stay there again, and I'd be careful to whom I recommended this hotel. It's not for everyone.

title: “Right in Downtown, but needs some updating”
text: Rooms were a bit dated, but they were large. Free breakfast was available, and the staff were very friendly and helpful. There is also a security guard on duty at this hotel. Parking is available on site, but it is not free. This hotel is right in downtown and you can walk to almost anywhere. Besides needing a bit of a renovation, the hotel is a good place to stay when visiting Memphis at an affordable price.

title: “NY Palace is my first choice”
text:
Whenever I go to NYC on business NY Palace is my first choice. This time around I stayed there for 10 nights. Even though the hotel was packed, due to Christmas season, service was as always outstanding. Rooms are spacious with comfortable beds. Great bathroom with tub and nice shower pressure. Even though it’s located in Madison with 50th is amazingly silent (upper floors at least). There is a great gym too and staff is always helpful. If you have an upper floor room you will have a great view, especially if faced to St. Patrick's Cathedral. 
If you want to be in mid-town this is a great hotel to stay. Walking distance from Apple Store , Rockefeller center, all main 5th Av stores , Central Park, Times Square, Grand Central, etc.
Unfortunately I was told that the private breakfast room at the Tower (more upscale rooms in NY Palace) was turned into guest rooms. This was one of NY Palace´s great assets.
Down side: free Wi-Fi only at the lobby. A friend observed this and it’s true: room temperature seems to vary more than it should. Breakfast is outstanding but overpriced.

title: “Didn't Want to Leave Hotel Teatro”
text:
I stayed at the Hotel Teatro for 5d/4n for a professional conference in early November. What an amazing treat. I started my stay with an embarrassing case of altitude sickness. The staff (Torie and Stephen) were so empathetic and sweet in their care of me that I can barely describe how grateful I am. They brought me a nail file when I was too sick to leave my room, brought me water and checked on me periodically through the evening and next morning.
The Hotel is well above average in their service, cleanliness, amenities, location, and decor. Everyone was pleasant and extremely service-oriented. I felt spoiled by Jim and Torie each day that I ordered my wake up call, and more so when they offered to drive me to a conference hotel down the street, complimentary of course. Touches like turn down service with chocolates, the lovely Aveda bath products, the chauffeured Escalade, and complimentary shoe shines were the small things that complimented the personal service and made my stay a very comfortable and memorable one.
I knew Teatro was excellent in every way, but did not fully appreciate it until I attended meetings in another local hotel. Upon entering the other hotel, which will remain nameless to protect the guilty, I was hit with the overwhelming smell of bleach and harsh cleaning products. I was immediately wistful for the pleasantry of Teatro's aromatherapy ambiance. 
The bed was divine, the linens exceptional and cozy, the wireless service reliable, the robe and towels fluffy, and the bathtub was something I would have liked to smuggle home in my suitcase. I literally did not want to leave this hotel!
I would highly recommend the Hotel Teatro to anyone: from the quick romantic weekend getaway to the extended (no choice but to attend a conference/meeting./consulting gig) stay. Teatro's staff and amenities will make being away from home special and comfortable.

title: “Loved our stay”
text: Had a very spacious corner room. Wonderful to come back to and relax a little before heading out again for more sightseeing. Noise from the street was NOT a problem, and my wife is a light sleeper. Staff very friendly and helpful. Enjoyed breakfast at Pigalle each morning. Location was great. Easy walk to Broadway shows, great restaurants, and transportation.

title: “Graet Budget Hotel for good price”
text:
Arrived mid-late August for 2 night stay. Reception were really friendly and lobby clean and presentable. Check in and Check out really simple and easy.
Room was okay - in need of a little make over but was clean and comfortable. Fridge was an assett. No air-con but didn't really need it as it wasn't 100 degrees heat! Good shower!
Great location, 5-10 mins walk from Union Square, cable cars, muni stations etc. Our room faced main street (it is on Taylor Street) and with windows open could get very noisy!
My husband and I thought it was a great price for just somewhere central to sleep and wake up. We stayed at Fishermans Wharfe after, and although hotle there was more 'plush', we didn't feel it was worth double what this cost!! Depends what you want really.... but I would definitley reccommend it for a budget, great location hotel.

title: “Good west side hotel”
text: Stayed for 2 nights in February for business. Nice lobby with lots of seating so it was easy for business meetings. Plus there is a bar that definitely gets a happy hour crowd. Ate 2 lunches and a breakfast at the restaurant on the 2nd floor which is really nice and bright and sunny. The breakfast buffet was $26 so not cheap but typical for a nice NYC hotel breakfast buffet I guess. Room was small (not the smallest ever in NYC) but totally fine for a couple nights and was nice and modern. Bathroom was nice too. No complaints whatsoever. Free wifi in the lobby but you have to pay to use Internet in your room.

title: “St Giles is always a good choice”
text: St giles is a convenient place to stay in the City. # blocks from Grand Central and within easy walking distances from many attractions. It is always very clean, the staff is extremely helpful and friendly. It is a great value.

title: “Amazing hotel in every respect!!”
text:
In June of 2004, we held our client conference at this amazing property. Being the one that coordinates everything for these conferences, I was invested in this property before I even laid eyes on it and hoped for the best. I was hardly disappointed! From the moment we arrived (chocolate chip cookies and all) everything was perfect! The staff is energetic and extremely helpful. The rooms are amazing, the decor is top notch and the meeting facilities are superb! From my pre-conference planning up through the post-conference follow-up, this could not have been a better experience.
The rooms are extremely comfortable and all the ammenities are top shelf. Aveda products in the bathrooms, window seats with spectacular view (I had one of the Suites) of the river, amazing beds and linens and a very functional workspace (with highspeed wireless internet to boot)...I couldn't have asked for more!
I'll be back next time for a vacation and I'll bring my family.

title: “Luxury with Amazing Views.”
text:
The view from the one bedroom suite was AMAZING! I spent 10 days in a suite while a family member was being treated at John Hopkins. The hotel gave us a great rate and was very understanding about an uncertain departure date. 
My 7 yo son came in over the weekend and the location couldn't have been better. We were easily walkable to the Inner Harbor, w/o being in the middle of the crowds, and also close to great restuarants in Fells Point.
The hotel has a beautiful pool the overlooks the Chesapeake Bay. A nice, modern 24/day workout room and spa. I was not able to get any treatments as they were booked for short notice appointments. As a hotel guest I was able to use the other spa features at no cost.

title: “One disappointment after another”
text: The door to my room was open/unlatched when I first arrived. While I was unpacking I pulled a drawer out that had crumbs and old papers in it from a previous occupant. The next morning I was looking for a shoe and pulled up the bedskirt to find a used tampon wrapper/applicator. When I complained on my way to work (7am) they promised they would have the manager inspect the room after it was cleaned. After work (7pm) the items were still there. I complained again and asked for a call from the manager and for it to be cleaned immediately. I went to dinner and items were cleaned when I returned however still no call 2 days later... I will not be using this property again.

title: “Chilled out, comfortable hotel in great location”
text:
We arrived at the hotel late Friday afternoon to be greeted by friendly welcoming staff who were quick to deal with our check in. As it was our 1st Wedding Anniversary my husband asked if there would be a chance of a room upgrade, the lady on reception found us another room for the weekend with a small charge.
The hotel lobby was very chilled with dimmed lighting, comfy sofa's and funky but soft 'wine bar' music.
The room itself was very modern and just the right size. We had read reviews previous to travelling saying the rooms were very small but ours was perfect. The bed was soooo comfy and just what you needed after a long days sightseeing. The only downside of the room was that it smelt a little bit like sweaty feet when we walked in and we couldnt open the windows and that the air conditioning unit was quite loud, this wasnt a huge problem as we didnt need it on through the night.
The consigerge were brilliant, very helpful and knowledgable. We enquired on a few occasions for directions, ect. 
The hotel was litterly just off Times Square, i thought it would be very noisy but it wasnt. So location was fantastic, perfect for shops, sights, Broadway shows(We saw Lion King, WOW! what a show!) and close to one of the main subway stations 42nd street. 
The hotel had a bar downstairs on the street level, which we also visited, this again was very relaxed, although quite expensive and the waitress was lovely. Definatley a good way to end your busy day.
Also there is a coffee shop attatched called Dean and Deluca that did coffee and cakes.
The only downside of the hotel is that there are no stairs only lifts which in a morning is terrible as everyone is on their way out and although there are 4 lifts, been on the 3rd floor, each lift was packed as they always went to the top. We found the trick was to press the button to go up, get in an empty lift and go up first! it was quicker than waiting for a lift you can squeeze into, one day it took us 15 mins to get a lift! Not Good!
Overall our experience of the Paramount was brilliant and as for New York, what a place! We would definatly stay at this hotel again.

title: “"A Beach Zoo Hotel"at Catamaran Resort Hotel”
text: The Catamaran is a beach with Eden Gardens around. Beautiful fish and parrots with streams and ponds around the resort on the beach. Rare Palms and plants from all over the world. I loved the parrots. I wish I can take one with me. But these birds belong at the garden. There is a magnificent waterfall in the lobby as we entered from outside. It's a "San Diego Zoo Hotel on the Beach" at the best location. The hotel offers water sports to rent kayaks or jet ski or windsurf at the bay. Even the food is good to eat at Atoll restaurant or Cannibal bar on the beach. I'll love to come back again soon with my finance.

title: “Friendly Hotel in the heart of mid town”
text:
Stayed 7 nights at the Hotel Elysee and had a great vacation. We had never been to New York before, so was unsure what to expect but was glad to be welcomed by a very friendly and accommodating staff. Our room was larger then we expected, not much of a view, but we didn't come to New York to look out our window. Room was clean, but maybe a little tired, but was obviously attended too regularly. In fact the hair dryer in the bathroom was broken when we arrived, and although we never complained about it, it was fixed a day later (Obviously one of the cleaning staff noticed it and made sure it was taken care of).
The only thing that was a bit of an annoyance was the elevator; it was very slow, especially during busy times, and the stairs where not accessible as another option (security reasons).
The Hotel is in a great location. 10 min walk to Central park, Rockefeller Centre and Times Square, also easy access to the Subway. The hotel was also close to some great restaurants and shopping.
The Hotel also had a great lounge area, which was a nice and quiet place to relax after a long day touring.
We would gladly stay here again and recommend it to any of our friends.

title: “Great staff and frill free hotel”
text:
We stayed here the evening before our international flight to Japan. The staff were wonderful. I had a 2:30 am shuttle to the airport with a lot of luggage and a crated cat. The driver was super helpful with our bags. The front desk let us store our excess luggage in a closet off of the lobby so that we didn't need to haul it up to our room, which was really nice. 
The room was very basic, but clean and comfortable. For the price, it is perfect. They have upgraded rooms with microwaves and fridges, too.

title: “My P.O.V. Experience @ the W Hotel”
text:
So I like the W Hotel and the atmosphere that it creates, business sexy, but what makes me go to the W when I don’t have a room reservation is the Happy Hour. So I have experience plenty of W Hotels across the United States, and 3 come to mind that I like, Chicago, NY Manhattan & DC. Chicago, awesome-love the lobby club and the after hours lounge way up there fantastic. NY, beautiful, the lounge area and staff awesome. DC, just to die for, (THE BEST *****) the lobby bar, amazing, staff crazy kool, but P.OV. OMG... Yes --- it’s the best thing happening Friday in DC for Happy Hour, with or w/o reservation I love it, the most beautiful arrangement of women whom serve with professionalism, style and sexiness. My P.O.V service award goes to Krystle, (Reminds me of Lisa from Save by the Bell), I have been blessed to have her as my server twice and I’ am highly awed with her meticulous professionalism and attention to detail, and she is sexy too! (LOL)…. So when I make my reservations from now on, I want my service to come from Krystle.
To say it in a hip hop statement “She is Fancy & a 5 Star Chick” in my book. 
M Jay Spearman

title: “Nice place”
text: Sitting on 5 acres of land over Old Town, San Diego this hotel is a short walk into town and very convenient. The hotel sits on several layers on a hill and the rooms are large, with heavy tile floors, microwave, refrigerator, TV, etc. We found the rooms were clean. One disappointment was that wireless internet was only in certain designated outdoor areas and lobby which meant that you had to sit outside to get on the internet. Not bad usually, but could be a problem in bad weather. The grounds are lovely, landscaped and with flowers, but we were more impressed with our ability to walk into town which has a lively nightlife. The pool is ok and there is a heated spa pool. Parking is free and in a gated garage. We found the place charming and a ten minute drive into downtown.

title: “Beautiful Hotel, Great Location!”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for three nights in June. 
You couldn't ask for a better location. We left the car with the valet and didn't need it again until we left town. The neighborhood felt safe, and we walked or took (reasonably priced!) taxis everywhere we went. 
The staff was friendly and helpful. The doormen had plenty of suggestions for places to eat and were always ready to give directions or point you the right way. Even the housekeeping staff greeted us and asked if we needed anything.
The rooms and the facilities were charming. Yes, the furniture looks older, but it's a historic hotel. It's supposed to have an older/antique feel to it. That's part of the appeal. The bedroom and bathroom were clean, and I had no complaints. There were only two sets of towels, so we had to request more; they were waiting for us in the room when we returned from dinner.
There's not a restaurant in the hotel, but I don't usually frequent those anyway. There are lots of good, local restaurants in walking distance. Ask the doorman. :-) 
My only word of caution is to check the rate; when we called to book, we were told there was no AAA discount, but when we asked again on arriving, they lowered the rate for us.

title: “Better then I expected, BY FAR.”
text: All the staff were really with it -- good attitude and competent. I left items in room and they put them in my car -- all waiting safely after 9 days. GREAT breakfast and easy access to T-station on the day before flying.

title: “Great price, great Hotel, great location !!!!”
text: The rooms are very clean and so confortable. The breakfast is pretty good with some choice. The location of this Hotel is correct, situated beside of outlets. 5min by foot from subway or 5min of city center by car. Even if located near the highway we hear nothing, the hotel is well soundproofed. I will certainly retake this Hotel for my next trip at Boston.

title: “Top hotel top location”
text: Top hotel that has it all, location, restaurant, rooftopbar and pool

title: “Excellent Hotel, great location, amazing value”
text: Stayed here for 5 nights and were impressed by this well managed hotel; great (if not huge) rooms, clean, quiet (at 18th fl) and well appointed. perfect location just round the corner from Moma, 5th Av, Rockefeller Center etc. And absolutely amazing value with a $140 rate found online. This hotel is at the top of the list for next NYC visits, business or leasure.

title: “Great location; excellent staff.”
text: We stay mainly at Comfort Inns and this one was excellent for our needs. We are from a rural area, and being in downtown D.C. made us a little nervous. The staff helped greatly, allowing us to check our bags and leave our car before check in time. We WALKED to the white house, then on to the mall and museums, and it was more accessible than we thought. The breakfast room was big and set up well -- one of the best we've seen. We would definitely stay again.

title: “Great Stay”
text:
I will admit, that after seeing so many poor reviews recently, I was nervous to stay here, but I had a great stay, and found everyone extremely helpful. Emily checked me in, and was as pleasant as could be, and was also helpful in providing dinner recommendations. It seems to me that one or two people are posting multiple negative reviews (see the two that are both from Marietta...), but that's on them how they want to spend their free time.
I found the rooms to be clean and comfortable, and the breakfast was excellent. I will definitely stay here again.

title: “The Maritime Hotel is the PERFECT place to stay in New York City!”
text: Our family of 7 came to the Maritime for a weekend in the city and they were able to more than accommodate us! The staff was amazing! They greeted us right away and were friendly and attended to any need very quickly! The rooms were gorgeous and absolutely clean. The girls and I loved the Bigelow toiletries! We will stay here again and again! Thank you!

title: “It's nice hotel, nice breakfast compared with 3 stars hotel”
text: The room is standard for 2 stars hotel (with noisy A/C). It's clean and roomy. The staffs are friendly and the breakfast is a lot better than 3 stars hotel. It includes make-yourself pancakes, banana, apples, milk, cereal, variety of muffins, juice and etc. At first, I was so reluctant to stay in this hotel based on reviews in this website but later I found this hotel is really a good deal package for $40 plus tax per night.

title: “Southern Hospitality At Its Finest”
text:
My pleasure is the popular phrase at this hotel. Celebrating a girfriend's 40th birthday in Memphis we selected the Madison. The rooms were spacious and clean and the service unbelievable. This hotel is in the heart of downtown Memphis and great for a weekend getaway! 
Loved it.

title: “Fair warning: Don't stay at the Allerton!!!”
text:
This hotel does care the slightest for the guests satisfaction. Upon check-in I requested two beds in the room as was told I would have to pay an upgrade fee, not for a nicer room, just for the extra bed, this was just the beginning, don't get me started. 
I strongly causion you against staying at the Allerton, plenty of other guest friendly hotels to choose from. Learn from my mistake!!!

title: “Great location, need better doors in the rooms”
text:
Location is perfect, check in was quick until we realized that they didnt activate our cards correctly so the parking ramp would not take our card. We had to back out of the parking structure and go back to the hotel to get them properly activated, attention to detail by the front desk clerk is all that would have been needed the first time. 
Room was nice but at night there are HUGE cracks around the door jam that let light and NOISE in. twice a group of drunk people walked by our room and woke us up. 
Also I will NEVER understand how crappy little hotels can offer free wifi and places like this will try to charge you for it. Not to mention the 4 dollar bottle of water in the room. 
I can buy a case of bottled water for 8 bucks ,, does the hotel really need to nickel dime you on everything? 
Overall a nice stay.

title: “fabulous position ,”
text: Me and a girlfriend had fab 5 nights location was walking distance from Times Sq, and only 3 blocks from Empire State building, it is an old building but location cantbe faulted

title: “Great location”
text: Located one block from the Magnificent Mile, this newly renovated RRI is a great option for first-time visitors to Chicago. Walking distance to Hancock Observatory, many stores, and Millenium Park. Only downsides are the non-stop sirens, which they can't control; must be located close to a hospital? Try to taxi, CTA, or L train to hotel since overall parking in downtown Chicago often will total more than your hotel!! Also, just 4-5 blocks from Lake Michigan. Staff very friendly; offered discount coupons.

title: “Great experience”
text: Excellent service, and all the amenities without feeling too big. Very clean rooms, gorgeous bathroom, french press and electric hot water pot in the room -- a nice touch. We've stayed in several hotels in downtown Seattle, and this was our favorite. Just two blocks from the water, a short walk to Pikes Market. Thanks to the great staff for a wonderful weekend.

title: “Traveling Home Stop Over”
text: Room was spacious, clean, had a small refrigerator and microwave, and beds were comfortable. Location offered selection of restaurants and shops (e.g. Walmart, et.) nearby. Staff was friendly and efficient. Breakfast offered hot and cold cereals, toast, bagels, danish rolls, yogurt, small sausage -biscuit sandwiches, and Belgium waffles.

title: “Very average”
text: My husband and I stayed at this hotel during a 4 day trip to NYC to see some shows and eat good food. Everything about this hotel was average- nothing special, blah. We ate sliders and pizza at the hotel bar. The food was ok for bar food but the service was nothing special. Our waiter was obviously upset at his coworkers for some reason or other and took it out on us. We were constantly asked if we wanted to attend a time share presentation. There was no in-room coffee available in our room (so that you can make your own coffee as soon as you wake up). The lobby was bland and unattractive. The best thing I could say about the hotel was that it was in a great location and that's probably why it is so popular. If you are looking for a special place try the Sofitel or any of a number of small, boutique hotels that strive to make your stay memorable. You can find deals that make the room rates comparable.

title: “Terrific staff & location”
text: The room was small; the heating system was noisy but the location and the concierge were superb. Just one quick overnight so location in the Back Bay area was so helpful. Walking distance to the Boston Symphony. Just a couple of blocks from Copley Square.

title: “Great location”
text:
We (family of four) stayed in this hotel for 6 nights and could not fault it. The location was excellent with its own private access to fisherman's wharf, close tro thecable cars and lots of excellent family restaurants and cafes. The room was large enough and the staff very friendly and helpful. Following the previous comments about the rooms we emailed several days before and asked for a room overlooking the pool and this was provided - it is the best option as you do get views of the bay and Acatrax from a balcony. Some of the other rooms do overlook the street at the back and that could get noisy.
Happy to recommend it.

title: “Just like home atmosphere!”
text: Oustanding staff service - went out of their way to help us find hotel in Cocoa Beach. Convenient location to highways without all the noise. Exceeded our expectations!

title: “Exquisite”
text: High tech, gorgeously modern room. Very friendly and helpful staff. Enjoyed our 8 year anniversary weekend here and will happily return for another special occasion. I would highly recommend it. Being right next door to MOMA was a bonus.

title: “Awful!”
text: While staying here my hotel room floor had hair all over it. It looked as if it hadn't been swept in weeks, lots of different types of hair. As I complained to the front desk, I could tell the floor had been mopped but was not cleaner than it was before. Hair and dirt also went down the drain as I turned on my shower. My floor had not been very well vacuumed. Outlets are hard to come by. Beds are uncomfortable. They charged me for a night TWO weeks before I stayed there! To top it off as I've been trying to call mangement, they've yet to answer my calls or return my voicemail. I've stayed at lots of La Quinta's as I travel a lot for my job, but I have NEVER been so disgusted or ticked off by any other location. Personally, I would not recommend this location to anyone.

title: “Very good stay for Verizon Center Event”
text: I stayed this past weekend at the Hampton Inn in Washington, DC (near the Verizon Center - about 2 blocks). I had initially booked it because of the location before looking on tripadvisor, but then found out it was ranked in the top 10, so I kept the reservation. Really glad I did. The event was at 2, and I had a pre-game lunch to attend at 12 at a local sports tavern with other UConn Alumni, also close to the Verizon Center & Hotel. With check-in at 4, I was able to check my car into the valet service & my bags at the hotel around 11:30 am until after the event when my room would be available. After the game, went back to the hotel, got our bags and got into our room. We later walked to the Hard Rock for dinner (maybe 6 blocks - by Ford's Theater). The next morning we ate the complimentary breakfast, also a plus, and checked out of the room. But, since we were going to visit the Air & Space Museum we checked our bags with the concierge again since we knew we wouldn't be back until after check-out time. After the museum, walked back to hotel (Air & Space about a mile away), got our bags & our car & went home. Definitely will consider staying here again next time in DC. The price was right too.

title: “Budget Best!”
text: Spent one night in LA and this was perfect! Right next to an In-and-Out Burger and about 1.5 block walk from Hollywood & Highland for Mann's Theatre and Walk of Fame (we were lucky enough to see a movie premiere!). Traveling with my teenage sisters and felt safe at this hotel. Parking is free!! You are on Sunset Blvd so if you just keep driving past the hotel you see all the cool clubs and celeb spots. Will stay here again.

title: “My home away from home!”
text: I attend University of Phoenix in San Diego, but I live in Riverside County. Each Thursday I rent a room at the Mission Valley Resort. Brad and his staff always ensure that I have one of the best rooms, they also greet me as Mr. Beller, which makes me feel more like a business man than a student, even though I feel like I am staying with friends because I engage in a conversation with the staff while checking in and I must say that they are very nice. The staff are very friendly as well as professional to everyone. My wake up calls are always prompt, room is very neat, and the view overlooking the pool is exquisite. I enjoy each night that I reside at the Mission Valley Resort in San Diego, California. Keep up the great job Brad and staff!!!

title: “Nice room, Peoria Grill a little weird”
text:
We stayed here for only one night after hiking through the Colorado Rockies. Almost every other hotel downtown was booked, so we ended up at Timbers Denver. We were pleasantly surprised.
We booked a studio suite with a king size bed on the 2nd floor. The cathedral ceilings made the place feel huge! The decor was modern/art deco, and the place felt relatively new. Bed was unbelievably comfortable. The bathroom was modern and while it did not have a shower, it had a modern looking shower. We had a very comfortable stay, even though the place was overrun with convention attendees.
My only complaint was the Peoria Grill. With our stay came a free buffet breakfast. When we got there, none of the tables had been bussed, it appeared only one flustered, overworked server was working, and there were no clean plates or utensils to be found anywhere. Most of the food had been picked over or was cold. Even the coffee was out. It was very odd. We ended up eating cold scrambled eggs and an apple, and some lukewarm coffee. We left a very small tip for the poor single server who was very harried, but we noticed nobody else left a tip. For a Friday, I thought this was a poorly managed restaurant with very bad service.
Other than that, I thought this was a nice hotel. It's not really downtown, but there are tons of shopping malls and things to do in the area. We weren't far from the movie theater.

title: “Wonderful stay at historic hotel”
text:
Boston is a small city with very expensive older hotels with small rooms. With that in mind, I was pleasantly surprised and extremely satisfied with my stay at the Omni Parker House. I am an Omni Select member, and they upgraded me to a deluxe room, which was larger than I expected (after reading reviews saying the rooms are extremely small). Omni select members get free internet access. The room wasn't as large as rooms in similar hotels in Orlando or Las Vegas, but it was much larger than my room at the W in east Midtown Manhattan. Plasma/lcd TV, wonderful bed, and very clean. The lobby is amazing--it really has a historical and colonial feel to it. The people there are super nice and the service is great.
The location is about the best you could ask for. It is one block from the government center T stop, which has the blue line to the airport, and the green line to Fenway or Copley. It is also about a block from the Park Street T stop, which has the red line to Harvard or South Boston. It is on the historic Freedom Trail, and right down the street from Boston Common and the Public Garden. It took me no more than 25 minutes from when I walked outside the airport until I arrived at the hotel, using the continuous free bus from the airport to the Airport T stop on the blue line, which I took to government center. The T is great in Boston. The price from the airport to my hotel was $2!
Overall, I loved my stay here and I would definitely stay here again if visiting Boston.

title: “Convenient, clean, very pleasant customer service”
text: Our room was on the small side, but comfortable, well-appointed, and very clean. Since it's on Geary Blvd it is not surprising that there is a fair amount of traffic noise, even late into the night (at least on Saturday). There is free off-street parking, although I don't think there are quite as many parking places as rooms (we did get a spot). The breakfast is minimal, but for the price it's nice that they have it at all. Henry, at the front desk, was exceptionally friendly, polite, and helpful.

title: “Nothing special past the lobby”
text: We stayed at the Peabody over Labor Day weekend. We chose the Peabody simply because it is considered a Memphis "must do" and because we could take the pooch. There is nothing MAJOR to complain about (elevator noise, noisy guests, unemptied trash from the previous guest), but there is nothing to brag about either. I think the Peabody is resting on past laurels, ducks that swim in the fountain, and a beautiful lobby. The room was small, the bathroom smaller, and just "OK" amenities. There was no coffee service and no refrigerator in the room. Oh, did I mention the parking is ridiculously situated about 1/4 mile away and pricey! I'm glad we had the experience but I wouldn't do it again.

title: “5 star service location and decor will bring me back here!”
text: This hotel has been so accomodating and service oriented. Here on business for 4 days and they allowed early check in, late housekeeping service and even charged my I phone. I seek out boutique properties whenever I travel and the Affinia is simply delightful. I will certainly be back with my husband. only flaw is that they did not deliver the requested pillow and walking tour I requested on line.....

title: “Las Vegas prices and Motel 6 rooms”
text: Do not stay at the Riverwalk. $259/night and they didn't even clean our room before the second night. It was loud, busy and very run down. We expected a top notch hotel with excellent amenities, but got a very low class hotel.

title: “Room not fully cleaned”
text:
The staff is very nice and proactive! Always ready to help. 
Breakfast is very limited but is okay!
My room was not fully cleaned as i found crackers/ships under the window! I stayed 2 nts an my room as not been cleaned at all during my stay.

title: “Not as nice as before”
text:
Have stayed here many times and previously wrote a laudatory review in 2004. This recent stay, however, was lacking. 
First off, the price was high - $300 for a Deluxe room. More than I have ever paid for a hotel room outside of NYC. 
When we arrived, we noticed that our room was right next to the OLD elevators. Having stayed next to the elevators before, we weren't worried. However, the bed was against the shared elevator shaft wall and that was new...and noisy. Also, the headboard was such that every time we shifted in bed, it slammed against the wall.
Add the loud people in the adjoing room--from whom we were separated only by a thin door--and unlike previous stays, it definitely did not seem like we were the only people in the hotel.

title: “Great location/super hotel”
text: Nice hotel in a super location, near China Town and at the bottom of Nob Hill, cable car right outside the door and close to everywhere you want to be, very comfortable and upsacale but relaxed.

title: “Solitude, serenity, and sophistication along the Boston waterfront.”
text: Great price through Travelzoo and hotel's own price-matching. Professional, customer-oriented, courteous and helpful hospitality management at every juncture. Overall very modern, well-constructed, well-maintained with nice art touches; compact but adequately-sized rooms with great layout and amenities, including water view. Very soundproof, good clean bathroom, good clothing storage, free wireless, iPod, etc. Bose plug-in. Convenient integrated parking ($31 per; barter for free or reduced, we did and got it). Quieter, less-developed Boston Seaport area is moderately developed and appealing in separation from the ruckus and waterside tranquility. Enough quality local restaurants or just minutes to Chinatown, Back Bay, et al (Boston metro is not that big and at off traffic hours easily navigable). Fairly large scale, but boutique in feel and function. My Boston choice going forward.

title: “Great hotel in SF”
text: The Baldwin Hotel is an excellent choice of lodging in San Francisco. We could see the gate to ChinaTown from our window. You can walk anywhere from this location. It is a few minutes walk to the BART, cable cars, buses and many wonderful restaurants. We couldn't have picked a more perfect location at a reasonable price!!! Our room was spacious, very comfortable and clean. Though our room faced the street the noise of traffic, garbage trucks, etc.... was not enough to bother us or keep us awake. The people at the front desk were always very helpful in answering any questions. I highly recommend this hotel and would stay here again.

title: “Weekend Getaway”
text: My husband and I stayed for the weekend at the Staybridge and although it not exactly in Times Square as advertised it is close. We were surprised at how small the room was as it was a "suite" but on a good note it is a very clean hotel. The room did have a kitchen area with a full size fridge, stove, microwave and even a dishwasher. The free breakfast was average at best. The area was a little sketchy with a 24hr adult store and a liquor store as well as the New York parole board on the same street but turned out to be fine. The front desk staff was not overly friendly but doorman Sunny more than made up for them.

title: “Loved this hotel!!”
text: I really liked this hotel, I was plesantly surprised. It was cute, clean, charming, and a great surprise-- very spacious for such a great price, $69.00 (I found from Expedia). The location was excellent too for those wanting to get a nice D.C. experience.

title: “Great Hotel, but not for children!”
text:
The rooms are nice and clean, and they have great amenities. They are in walking distance of Pier 39 and many great things to do. The staff is courteous and helpful. But this place is not great for young children, especially those who like to watch a few cartoons in the morning. They only have a few TV channels and 1 cartoon channel, but it has shows for older children. We didn't spend much time in our room, but when children are up at 7 am and we nothing opens until 10 am, you run into a little problem entertaining them. The hotel wants you to purchase TV packages to watch shows, so unless you want to spend money on good TV, you have to try and find something on the local channels, which during the week is manly morning show.
Over all the hotel was great, I just don't recommend it for families with young children.

title: “Fine hotel, good price”
text: We stayed in the Hotel Monaco for four nights in early September. We were very pleased. The staff is friendly. The room, while not large, was nicely done. We had a room overlooking the river and could sit in the large, cushioned window seat and watch the world go by. The hotel is within a block or so of the Els on the loop so tranportation is easy,, but far enough from the trains so that there is no noise. It is also only a block from Michigan Avenue, and thus close to the parks and the best shopping. Jewlers Row and Marshall Fields are also near by.

title: “Location location location”
text:
I read alot of viewer reviews about the location. It is awesome. I liked the simple rooms. They were well maintaned and very clean. The rooms are very simple but had everything I needed. 
Most impressive part of the hotel was the free breakfast. They have something for everyone.

title: “Great experience at Holiday Inn-Bayside”
text:
I stayed here for a week in October. The staff was very nice and helpful. The location is close to the bus line (if needed). Stayed in a poolside room overlooking the golf course with a nice landscaped view. Laundry facility is on the premises 
The restaurant has excellent food with friendly service.
Had a great time in San Diego.

title: “Great place to stay!”
text: Great place to stay when in Boston. Smaller feel, great restaurants, clean rooms, and excellent staff!

title: “Stay for location & price, not luxury”
text:
We knew based on other reviews and photos that this was not going to be a luxury hotel, so were realistic in our expectations going in. The room interiors are very basic--we stayed in a double room for a family of five, and could tell the bathroom had just been refreshed and painted, but tile dates from the 20's. Beds were rather hard, but the double room was huge and we had a wall bank of windows overlooking the street, which was fun. The kids loved it. Our room was also very clean, and I am one to go looking for dirt when entering a hotel room:)
I would recommend this hotel for the location and price. We were on an Eastern trip for which DC was a three-day stop. We knew we would not be spending much time in the room--we came to sightsee. The only other hotels that had this excellent a location cost more than double this one. We splurged on stays in other cities where we spent more time in the room/facility. If you are like us and want a location in D.C. from which you can walk everywhere you need to go (or take the convenient metro, for which the main station was two blocks north), then stay here. If you are looking for a pool, luxe beds, and other amenities, be prepared to spend quite a bit more and walk farther or (God forbid in DC) drive!

title: “Needs cleaning”
text: While the Hotel still does have a faded glory charm, there is absolutely no excuse for poor standards of cleanliness in any hotel, certainly not a premier priced hotel such as the Fairmont. The amount of dust on the baseboards is spectacular (do not look behind the beds, it is too scary), the soap scum collected in the sink moulding was impressive as was the interesting collection of life under the rim in the sink. This is not acceptable in any hotel.

title: “Will return”
text: My husband and I stayed for 2 nights with our teenage daughter on a short trip away. The hotel surpassed my expectations. The complimentary dinner was quite sufficient for our needs although there is only one choice (on this night it was Totellini with an option of 2 sauces), but the salad bar was plentiful and the complimentary beer/wine certainly hit the spot. The room was located close to the street and although we could hear some outside noise it was not disturbing; it was comfortable,clean and service was very friendly. The location is ideal for sightseeing as we walked to Pike place and the art gallery, also to the Science centre. We shall definitely select this hotel for a return visit.

title: “so run-down”
text: I stayed here because the Sheraton Tower across the street didn't have the room type I needed. The lobby is decent. Otherwise everything here is just sooooo old. The mattress, elevator, sheets, bathroom, wallpaper, carpet, blanket are dirty, stained, and dated. The room here is no better than one of those independently-owed no-name roadside motel. The staffs are kind of unhelpful, too. Calls to the frontdesk, housekeeping, concierge, engineering, are put on hold, transferred, disconnected, or never picked up. If I hadn't stayed here for free, I be really p!ssed paying $300 buck a night for this crap. On the plus side, the hotel is very centrally located. There is free internet lounge in the lobby which I am using to write this. Do yourself a favor and stay at the Sheraton Tower across the street or stay elsewhere.

title: “Nice location”
text: Once we navigated successfully to the hotel, it was a delightful stay. Road construction had my vehicle nav system rendered; useless. Very nice room with a wonderful view to the west, over the water. Easy walks to many nice resturants.

title: “Indeed It Is!”
text:
First time staying here, but will not be the last - as long as the prices hold out.
Great location, very nice staff all around, and pretty nice room!
The room was perfectly appointed. Nice work desk. I notmally don't use them as they typically seem to be an afterthought. This one can view the TV and had a lot of power outlets and even a USB charging plug!
Bed seemed short as the room was narrow, and I am not that tall.
I only wonder why they don't give the reception folks a chair or stool to sit on??
Other than that - it was great.

title: “Great stay, will be coming back!”
text: I was in town for the night visiting my daughter Brianna, who works at the Town & Country. I never stay in town longer than one day when I come to visit due to not having any place to stay. I checked in on a Saturday and was surprised to see that it wasn't horribly busy. I was greeted by friendly smiles from Donna and Trina and was checked in right away. I got a renovated room in the tower, which was absolutely beautiful. The beds were so comfortable, my "quick nap" turned into 2 hours (oops!). The view was amazing from both sides of the building! I had my daughter take me on a walking tour of the property and the grounds are spectacular, hats off to the groundskeepers! I had the breakfast buffet at The Terrace Cafe, which was good. The service was excellent, our server Maria was very attentive and made sure to keep topping off my coffee. Overall, I had a great experience and can't wait to come back and maybe stay a few more days next time!

title: “Worth the extra $”
text:
This was a very comfortable and clean room, helpful & easy going staff and lots of onsite amenities. Chris was very helpful at front desk when I asked how to find a Starbucks. I would definitely recommend this hotel.
Thanks!

title: “Too expensive for what it is”
text: The location is amazing, but the price ($310 per night for 4 nights' stay WITH Military discount!) was way too much for the tiny bathroom, tepid & weak shower and grim aspect of the front desk.

title: “Sights versus Cleanliness”
text: If you are wanting to sightsee and be in walking distance from historic attractions this hotel is great. But, if you are more concerned with cleanliness and accessibility this is not their forte. The old fashion look of the hotel was neat, but the bathroom floor was not clean, the carpet was not clean and the blanket laid across the bed had stains. Yuck! The Internet accessibility was horrible. Not a fantastic experiment for me. The fitness center was cleaner than my room.

title: “Event Hotel: ho-hum but in good location!”
text: Most of my business travel has me booked into "event hotels." I call them "un-eventful" hotels. These are usually hotels geared for the business event attendee. They don't have spas or hair salons or shopping inside to any great degree. This one is no different. The Gift shop sells mostly "I love Philadelphia" stuff, the room service is basic and ends late night. The restaurant known as "13" is where they get the room service menu and it is also basic. The rooms are ok and very clean. The saving grace of this hotel is its location. Smack dab in the center of downtown Philadelphia. There is a Macy's 1 block away and plenty of restaurants. I would stay here again for a business trip.

title: “Huge Hotel; Great Location”
text: We ended up in Chicago during the Air & Water Show, and this hotel was hopping busy! Even so, check-in was easy, and service was excellent. We drove in from Milwaukee, so we had to pay $50/night for parking (yikes!) We got there a little early, but our room was ready, and the bell service quickly removed our bags from the car and brought them right up to the room. We stayed on an upper floor in the west tower. The room had a partial view of the river and the Wrigley buildings, and the room was quiet. The hotel is a short walk to Millenium Park, The Art Institute of Chicago, and Willis (Sears) Tower. We did not eat in the hotel, as there are far too many great places to eat within walking distance. Hotel staff are very helpful and polite. Security was especially helpful and securely stored our laptops for us while we were out sightseeing during the day. The hotel concierge assisted us with finding a good breakfast spot close to Millenium Park, and the parking garage allowed us to pre-load our luggage and keep our vehicle in the parking garage until 6 p.m. after check-out. We got a good deal on this hotel on Priceline, so other than the $50/day parking fee, (which is not unusual for Chicago) we paid a fair price for our stay. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Great Stay”
text: II was a little worried about the hotel when I saw some of the previous reviews. I think the hotel was wonderful! The staff was friendly and helpful. The room was very clean and I just loved the cookies! My only complaint would be that I arrived at 4:30 PM and my room was not ready. The staff was very apologetic and after 20 minutes...the room was ready. The staff made me forget about the room not being ready because they were so helpful. The restaurant was awesome also! I would definitely stay there again and recommend it to a friend!

title: “Excellent price for the location”
text: Visited SF on a pleasure trip and the location to the downtown is outstanding. The rooms are a bit small but sufficient. The daily wine tasting is a bonus feature and well enjoyed. Lots of things to do being so close to Union Square, Chinatown and the shopping. Easy to travel around as the BART, cable car and bus system are all minutes away. Found some very quaint resaurants with live jazz music nightly. Would definitely stay there again.

title: “VERY BAD CUSTOMER SERVICE”
text: VERY BAD CUSTOMER SERVICE . . . We reserved 4 hotel suites for the Women of Faith Conference at the American Airlines Center back in May 2011. The conference was in August 2011, and we called the week before to confirm everything about our rooms. When we got there the lobby was crowded with women from around the US trying to get checked into their rooms. When it was our group leader's turn, the front desk manager informed her that they had doubled booked our rooms, and the other guests had already arrived. We found out that this had happened to several other women too. The hotel ended up booking us another hotel and they paid for it which was nice, and they really had no choice because our group leader was furious!
