We ended up 30 minutes from where we needed to be with no restaurants near us within walking distance. We had to depend on the shuttle service from the hotel that messed up the reservations instead of the one they took us to. It really made it hard getting back and forth to where we needed to be all weekend. The hotel General Manager, Jeff Jones gave us each a gift certificate for a two day stay at another time for up to a year. We have to call and book the room and mention the gift certificate and give the voucher number when we make the reservation. The certificate isn't good for holidays or black out days, standard policy, no problem; right! I call for the weekend of September 10th-11th to use my two days for my daughter and her husband for my daughter's 25th birthday. I tell the front desk who I am, and the lady says that I have to talk to Mr. Jones myself. She puts me through, and I get his voice mail. I leave a message and five hours later the front desk lady that I talked to earlier calls me back. She states that the GM is busy and asked her to relay a message to me that they are all booked up and that weekend is a "blackout" date. I asked her about another weekend, and she says that they are booked for the next few weeks. They have one night available on September 24th. I told her that wasn't a good weekend for us. She said that I could call back in October and try to book another date and time. But I would have to call and see when the black out dates are because they change every month. She stated that they are really busy during the holidays and that I would need to call as soon as possible in order to see if I can use my certificate then. Needless to say, I was upset again, some hotel this is turning out to be! I looked up the hotel reservation line's number and called. I told the lady that I was looking for a suite for this weekend, the 10th - 11th. She said no problem we have several different suites to choose from. She asked if I had a preference, and I told her no. I also asked her that I had some friends that were looking for rooms as well, and that I would need to book four more rooms. She said that isn't a problem, but they might not be side by side. I said that was fine, and asked her again that you have several rooms available, and she said yes. Then I told the lady that I had called the hotel itself and asked about making a reservation, and that I was told the hotel was completely sold out. The lady said well, I don't understand, there must have been a cancellation since you called. I told her that I would get back to her about the reservation and hung up. It makes me wonder if I will ever use this voucher, and I wonder why the GM was lying to me. He didn't even have the courtesy to call me himself. I don't know why I would even want to stay here, much less recommend it to a friend or family member.

title: “Great time”
text: We stayed for five days at the Desert Ridge over Thanksgiving for a friend's wedding. The property is beautiful. I can not give a helpful review of the rooms because we somehow were upgraded to the Presidential Suite which was UNBELIEVABLE! Although if you have thousands of dollars to spend on a room, I recommend this one. I thought the staff was very helpful. I went to the spa which was wonderful. The waiting room upstairs is very relaxing and the treatments were very good. The only complaint is that they charge for wi-fi. Who does that any more these days?! We would go back.

title: “Great place for a family!”
text: We were told never to stay in Hollywood and we did not know the area at all. We relied on the positive reviews from this site, and everything worked out great! This hotel is perfectly situated near the major attractions and it is in a very safe location. It was the perfect amount of space for our family of 6! Full breakfast was included every morning, and the staff was very informative and helpful. Hollywood walk of fame and major attractions are in walking distance. Parking is in the building and it is easy in and easy out. It is a perfect place to stay if you are coming in to tour with a family.

title: “aahhh it was OK”
text:
Stayed 2 days, Checked in Monday the NON SMOKING room we we're given stank, the front desk was almost no help stating they would send up housekeeping to "spray" some air freshener... it stank of smoke and mildew, I asked for a refund and was greeted with an "you'll have to take that up with Hotel, COM attitude. Finally got in touch with the night desk manager Steve and insisted he come smell the room.
The word he gave it" Pretty Narley" and gave us another room I feel sorry for whom ever got that one, as they stated they were completely booked. I also believe from the attitude there is some prejudice against those who book outside of Best Western proper.
The rooms are small but the beds were comfortable and if not for Steve the night manager changing our room at the last minute the stay would have been intolerable. We paid 97.00 per night and felt it was overpriced. Told you Steve you never know who writes reviews....

title: “One of my Favorites”
text:
The Mayflower Park in Seattle is one of my favorites while in that city. It is one of those charming old pre-depression area downtown hotels. My experience is that service is consistently superb. The restaurant and lounge are also very good. You have to try the cornmeal hot cakes with homemade sausage. The hotel is clean and in great repair. Comfortable, safe and convenient, it is also very beautiful. Valet parking and concierge are available.
The location is within easy walking distance of many downtown activities, including Pike Place Market, shopping and restaurants. The Seattle Center Monorail departs from Westlake Center, which is connected to the hotel via interior breezeway. Seattle Center, site of the 1962 Worlds Fair, is now home to the Space Needle, Key Arena, Theatres and other fun venues.
I highly recommend this historic hotel.

title: “Thin walls, but otherwise excellent”
text:
The Downtown Sheraton is what one would expect from a large convention hotel in a downtown area. Check in with friendly staff and easy check out. Friendly staff all around. A true green program that rewards you. Many hotels tell you to hang up your towels to reuse them and when you come back, fresh towels. Not here. You hang a hanger on your door that says "green" and you are rewarded with a $5 voucher or more Starwood points. It was wonderful. Convenient location to restaurants and stores. 
The down sides of the Sheraton really are thin walls or sound just travels well through the ducts. I was in bed and thought my toilet had flushed, but no, it must have been the room next door. Also, heard radio music that had to be coming from next door. Didn't hear voices and such, just toilet and music. Odd! The hotel and convention center are rather confusing - go up to 2 or down to C to get to the convention center.

title: “Good value in San Francisco for the location”
text:
We found this inn after quite a long time searching on the internet for a reasonably priced motel in San Francisco. We also chose somewhere with parking as friends had said that they had paid a fortune to park in San Francisco. The Redwood Inn was nice enough. You could walk to Fisherman's wharf and the crooked part of Lombard st or take a bus or cable car nearby. The man in reception gave us a map and useful information about places to go and transport links.
We were a bit annoyed that we only found out about the 'breakfast' (doughnuts) on our last morning whilst checking out, so they could do with improving their information/communication. Room was a little dated and blanket had some small holes in. Also, when we arrived at the allocated check in time and given our key we found that our room had not been cleaned or emptied since the last occupants which was poor, considering that we had phoned ahead informing them of our arrival time.
As our room faced the main road it was a bit noisy. We had to keep the window shut and even then it was still noisy. I would ask for a room at the back if staying again.
Having said this it was a perfectly reasonable place to stay and a reasonable price compared to others in the area. There are restaurants within walking distance.

title: “Single Females Do Not Book”
text:
On May 28,2011, I had a room at this Motel 6. I was there a couple of hours and the adjoining room door opened and closed. I went to the lobby to tell the front desk what happened and the guy with tattoo on his neck told "Me" the guest to knock on the door and tell two male hispanics to stop. I went back to my room and they did it again. I went back to front desk and basically he told me to bad . I asked him to call his manager and I got the same response. I went back to my room 108 and left
My safety was not a concern

title: “sf weekend”
text:
Everything about this hotel was tops--from the time we entered the hotel, very
welcoming and friendly. The rooms were nice and the requests we had were taken care of
promptly. The location was good, close to shopping and activities we had planned.
The staff even remembered our last stay there.

title: “Motel 6 would have been an upgrade”
text: Do not stay at this hotel! I wanted to stay at the beach so I chose one across the street from Ocean beach. This was a mistake. I had a patio room and the entrance door had rust around it. I opened the door and the smell in side was so overwhelming I couldn't fall asleep so I had to buy a scented candle that I burned the entire time I was there. The bathroom was very tiny and didn't look anything like the photos I have seen online. The old tile shower stall made me feel as if I would catch some sort of disease by stepping into it. The paint behind the sink (a good 4 inches thick). The toilet is partially under the sink so you have to sit sideways. There is no electrical outlet in the bathroom and no hair dryer. The telephone didn't work and neither did the remote control for the tv. The wooden blinds had been broken off about a 1/3 of the way down so I had to put a wash cloth over the area where the missing slat was. The bed was extremely uncomfortable. I left really early on my check out day so I wouldn't have to be there anymore. I went to San Diego to have a relaxing weekend and to pamper my self so I decided I would have a nice relaxing time at the beach but that was spoiled by this hotel. Oh yeah, I could hear the conversations easily through the wall of my neighbors and I actually was woken up by hearing my neighbor snoring. That is how thin the walls were. Lots of transients in this area so I was nervous the whole time thinking my car was going to get broken into. Seriously, save yourself some money and stay at Motel 6.

title: “A Wonderful Hotel with a Caring Staff”
text:
My husband and I had to go to Boston on very short notice to see my elderly aunt who had fallen and broken her hip. We had to book our flight and hotel in a panic.
Joseph Herrin who is the Guest Services Coordinator of the Sheraton did everything he could to make our stay more comfortable. He booked us a room with a wonderful view and that was very quiet. We even had access to breakfast everyday.
We were able to take the orange line subway, which is about a ten minute walk from the hotel to Malden to see my aunt. When we returned to the hotel, Joseph had arranged a little dessert tray in our room with a lovely kind note for us.
We stay at the Starwood hotels when ever we can, but this time was so different from being on vacation. Sheraton, you really came through for us during this difficult time and we are so grateful.
Joey and Mem you are real stars!

title: “actually very nice place, but not all hotel facilities”
text:
Stayed here on a return deal after going on one of the timeshare visits. Had a 1 bedroom suite all to myself. I have to say, I really like the rooms and the facilities and the location is about as good as you can get. 
I will seriously consider using this as a hotel in future on stays to new york.

title: “Don't stay here if you want to be in the 21st century!!”
text:
Rooms are not very clean...though they have worked on "some" remodeling. If you expect HDTV and/or ESPN (for Monday Night Football) forget it!!! They seem to not to want to pay the price for the customer....also Some of the TV channels are doubled or so snowy they are not watchable!!! I've not yet eaten any food served at this hotel but if you like dinning with a "Herb-A-Life" meeting, then by all means check in during the week and you'll get a front row seat. 
All in all....this is a get a little less than you pay for kind of Hotel. But if you're really on a budget...it will serve you well...plenty of fast food in the area and the taco truck across the street is very good.
BTW....I've live in this hotel for over 2 years and changes are very hard coming.

title: “A perfect New York hotel...”
text: After several recent bad experiences at New York city hotels, I was starting to think there are no good hotels in the city, but thankfully, the Roosevelt proved I was wrong. This hotel is big, but both the rooms and the public areas are well decorated, comfortable and have great beds. The closet was large and there was plenty of storage space. The room and bathroom were immaculately clean. The breakfast buffet, although pricey, was worth every penny because it included thing like fresh berries, smoked salmon, omelets made to order, etc. The service was excellent and the staff universally friendly. The location is also very convenient since it is right in the middle of midtown, near the subway, shopping, the theater district and many attractions. This hotel is worth the money and many of the hotels I have stayed at in NY charge more and provide less value. I thoroughly enjoyed my stay and will return again.

title: “Expected more. No attention to detail and more bed bug comments”
text:
I have stayed in other holiday inn's before so I was concerned about the reviews posted. 
The bed bug comments are all true. A group of us had 3 to 4 rooms where we found bed bugs. After discussions with the hotel, they offered to wash the clothes and luggage and offered other rooms. However if we would have stayed quiet, nothing would have happened. No initiative from the hotel regarding bed bugs. Time for a deep cleaning of all rooms. My room was fairly cleaned everyday, but for some reason the bathroom was never "detailed" cleaned. If the bathtub was cleaned. Then then soap dish was not or the uses bottles of shampoo were left where I left them. Sometimes I only had two shampoos and one conditioner. The front desk staff was completely average. No smiles or worked at their own pace. The shuttle service was slow. They needed more drivers or altered their schedules to accommodate the high demanded hours and service, especially to the airport. I don't know I think I was expecting more.
The location and sizes of the room were good. The complimentary service to the mall and Walmart were greatly appreciated. Coin laundry was great. The restaurant "good eats" had better staff service. The housekeeping dept always greeted guests in the hallway ( that is nice). 
If I had to come back again, it will have to be because my company is paying for it. I am concerned of the bed bug situation and by the multiple comments, it probably won't stop until the hotel takes care of it

title: “CHOOSE ANOTHER HOTEL”
text:
We stayed at the hotel 6/27/2009 and were supposed to have two rrroms but the staff failed to have one of the rooms ready. After waiting until 6:30pm we were forced to cancel the room. We were not going to wait around all night. 
While UNSYMPATHETIC, the hotel manager indicated we would not be charged for the second room. UPON CHECK OUT THE CLERK CONFIRMED SAME. HOWEVER, CHECKING MY AMERICAN EXPRESS REVEALS WE WERE CHARGED FOR THE EXTRA ROOM AND TO DATE HAVE NOT SEEN A CREDIT. 
Calls for extra towels and room servive were handled by rude employees. THIS IS A COMMON THEME HERE. UNLESS YOU ARE TIPPING THE STAFF DONT EXPECT ANY SERVICE. 
WE TIP VERY WELL AND FOUND THE BELL AND WAIT STAFF PROVIDED TOP NOTCH SERVICE. 
WE WERE SUPPOSED TO HAVE A VIEW OF NAVY PIER AND CONFIRMED SAME AT CHECK IN. 
The rooms are cruise ship small. 
Beds were sagging to the middle. 
Pool smelled of Amonia. 
Dont bother with the fitness center. 
Outdoor restaurant was way understaffed we noticed people leaving after waiting to place their drink orders. not the servers fault. they were trying their best.

title: “The More I Travel, The More I Appreciate This Hotel”
text: This hotel is just a consistently good choice for my business travel needs. I stay here a lot, pursuant to a contract an employer has with the hotel. I have to say, I have few, if any, complaints. The rooms are always clean, they are large, the wireless Internet always works, and with a quick connection. The staff is very professional and competent. It is easy to catch a cab, catch a train, or even valet your car. I suppose the inside, with a completely open atrium from the top to the bottom floor, looks cool, too. This is not a luxury hotel, per se, but it is a solid four stars and is a great consistent choice for those in San Francisco on business or pleasure.

title: “Great way to spend a weekend”
text: Love the extras. They have every thing you need to relax. The spa treatments are great, the staff is super helpful. We stayed here for our anniversary. We didn't even ask but they upgraded us to a loft. The summer salt bar and pool are a must also.

title: “Wonderful Stay”
text:
What a great little hotel! Within walking distance to my favourite parts of Manhattan also! The staff were extremely friendly and helpful, especially Shane who always managed to find us chocolate muffins for our coffee when we thought there were none left! The rooms were ideal, not luxury obviously, but clean and perfectly adequate with flat screen TV’s and ample space (definitely not as small as other NYC hotel rooms I have stayed in). The breakfasts were great – when they don’t charge you any extra for them, you don't expect everything to be perfect, but I was pleasantly surprised. There was an abundance of food to keep you going. As for getting taxis we had no issue. Even if we had to walk to 6th Ave – it’s a 1 min walk, really not a big deal!!!!!!
In summary the service, the location and the breakfast all made this hotel a great base for our long weekend in the city. I would definitely return!

title: “Fantastic! great staff and lovely room.”
text:
We went to New York in June on our honeymoon and trawled through hotel and hotel on this site to find one which didnt have bad feedback which I have to say was a hard task... this was the only one with no bad feedback so we booked it. We were not disappointed. On arrival the room was not ready and there was a little mix up with rooms but it was ok, sorted and they were professional and put it right. The room was lovely (we had a penthouse suite top floor with balcony) I can highly recomend one of these rooms, the bed was huge, the aircon whilst noisy in the day time was suprisingly quiet at night. The location is perfect for the first time New York visit as its round the corner from Macy's and the Empire State.
All in all a fantastic hotel, no restaurant but hey its New York! and if you want to stay in the hotel they have a fantastic array of take out menus to choose from who will deliver to the hotel for you and the staff are happy for you to bring food in at any time.
A great hotel and a trip of our lifetime.

title: “The best hotel I have been to.”
text:
The best hotel I have been to so far and I travel a lot. Rooms are modern and designed with details in mind. Loved the TV within the bathroom mirror. Beds are comfy. Staff is very friendly and would never miss to greet you or open the door for you. Valet desk always ask if you need water or directions.
The food (catered for event) was good. 
Would be glad to visit again :)

title: “not worth it”
text: This hotel bills itself as a 3.5 star, but really it should be 2 stars. I've had better service at motels. When I checked in 1 hour before the official check in time, they refused to find a room that was ready, and flatly told me to check my bags with a porter. If it had been really busy, I could understand. As it was, the hotel was only half full. Then when we checked into our hotel, there were not one piece of towel in the room! They made us wait to check in because the "room was not ready", and no towels when we did check in? I'm sure it was an oversight, but why make us wait an hour to check in when it still wasn't ready in the end? The bathroom door was uneven, so we could not close it. And the room reeked of smoke, even though it was supposed to be non-smoking. At almost $200 per night, I would advise all to avoid this hotel. You're better off with a 2 star for less price with the same service, if not better, or to spend a little more and get better service and quality.

title: “greatly enjoyed our stay”
text:
A friend and I stayed here for 3 nights while on a short vacation in the city. Our room (double double) had sufficient space for the 2 of us. It is NY after all, where hotels rooms are small. The beds were very comfortable w/ quality linens. Bathroom was small. If you are a very large person, this could be a bit of a challenge.
Nightly wine reception in the lobby was great to come home to each day. Apples, lemonade, ice tea and water w/ lemon or lime available all day. It was hot during our visit and these were appreciated. The happy hour in the attached Silver Leaf Tavern was a very good deal.
Moonstruck Diner around the corner was a good deal for breakfast. Ask the concierge for suggestions about where the locals eat dinner.

title: “great value for money”
text: Booked the cheapest hotel we could find online and were very pleasantly surprised with what we got. Staff, though busy, were helpful and friendly. Room clean, quiet and well equipped. Lobby breakfast perfectly adequate. Good location. All-in-all this hotel was great value for money and anyone who requires more than this needs to be prepared to fork out a lot more.

title: “We wouldn't stay anywhere else!”
text: This was 'hands down' our favourite hotel during our honeymoon in the USA. It is in a great spot and very close to Times Square. The room was larger than we had expected and the bathroom was decadent with a gorgeously large shower and bath... much needed after pounding the pavement day after day! Brilliant service and the house keeping staff came to make up our room a few times a day and brought us small bottles of water in the evening (a lovely touch). There were three computers with free internet available for guests in the lobby which was handy for keeping in touch with family and friends back home. We wouldn't stay anywhere else!

title: “Still a great choice”
text:
We stayed here again in January 2011 for three nights in an executive king.
We were again kindly upgraded to the top floor bay view with balcony. The viesws from this floor are spectacular. The staff again were all very helpful and friendly, special note to Andrew on the front desk checked us in. We had no problem with the small amount of noise we could hear from the building construction next door, but you do hear it. Housekeeping were exceptional, room was alweays clean and fresh. I much prefer this area being close to North Beach, Chinatown, Telegraph Hilland Nob Hill. the only disappointment was that the Executive Lounge has not re-opened. 
Would recommend booking a luxury floor room and emailing ahead to see if you can get a top floor balcony room, they are well worth the money.

title: “good value at Fishermans Wharf”
text: we have stayed many times, always clean good value and happy to see you also free bonus of free parking which at around Fishermans Wharf area is not to be found all hotels charge at least $15 a day.very good value.

title: “The Best”
text: Have stayed at this hotel several times and will be staying again in a couple of weeks. ALWAYS THE BEST, room, view, food, service. Don't listen to the cry babys about this hotel. I think they may be surferring from unfullfilled romantic expectations of NY out of a 40s black and white film. Hotel is terrific.

title: “Take a peg for your nose and wear gloves at this hotel”
text:
We stayed here a night before a cruise as we wanted to check out Hollywood Boulevard and surrounding areas. We checked in and were allocated a room on the second floor and upon entering the room the smell hit us! It was terrible, like a musty, damp smell with disinfectant mixed in. We coul hardly breathe it was so thick. 
We requested another room and this was no a problem. We were allocated a room on the ground floor. Now, this room didnt smell but the noise from upstairs was out of this world. We could hear the people in the room above walking aroud and the creaking was that bad we actually wondered if we were safe laying under the ceiling. The whole hotel had a very unclean feel about it, like you didnt want to touch anything, doorknobs, stair rails, eeeew. If you want to be close to Hollywood Bvd on a budget then this place is ok for one night. But saying that, we payed $100 for our room (Fri night) and you can get a really nice hotel at LAX (15 mins away) for a lot less. If you have a hire car I woud stay at LAX. We did this and had easy acess to Santa Monica and Venice beach and stayed at the Sheraton Gateway for 65.00- lovely hotel with everything you need.

title: “Smart & refurbished - smart choice”
text:
I stayed here for 4 nights while on trip to San Diego arriving on a wet Thursday. Check in was quick & rate was good at $89 plus tax for the 4 nights. Car parking however was $6.95 a night which seems to be the norm in Hotel Circle now, it was free when I was last here in 2005, where else do you park ?
I seem to have booked an accessible/disabled room which was huge and at the end of the building but the front desk was easily able to change it to a normal room with a tub, not a problem. New room on the 4th floor was clean, good sized. Fridge & coffee maker , wardrobe & drawers, I believe it has been refurbished as all the furniture & decor seemed new. The a/c had a slight odour but nothing too bad. Bed was big & firm & slept very well on it. 
Breakfast which is included & free is just your pastries & cereal & fruit ( not too many bananas) & beverages . There are also waffle makers which seems like a good idea but the lines can sometimes be long for them. They seem to close the breakfast room at 9.30 sharp so don't oversleep if you want the breakfast.
Next time I think I will stay down town or Bayside as it is just a little too far from downtown & if you miss the freeway exits for the hotel, it is no fun !!!
Do try & eat at Top of the Market near the USS MIdway for a fancy fish meal or go for a happy hour meal after 9 at the Currant Brasserie & Bar in the Sofia Hotel on Broadway, great cocktail barman & fab onion soup for $3.75.

title: “worst club lounge”
text: Their club lounge is absolutely the worst I have ever been at any hotel and in any country. The lounge is very small. There is no staff on site. I was doing interviews in the lounge when one of the hotel janitors came in and sat down in a massage chair, which is very close to us. He turned on the massager, closed his eyes, and was really enjoying himself. I have never seen a hotel staff taking advantage of the hotel amenities while on duty and in front of hotel guests. I asked him to come back in an hour and he left to vaccum the floor. It was 11am and I had to do the rest of my work elsewhere because of the noise. The hotel location is convenient being adjacent to a mall. I have stayed there 6 or 7 times in the past few years. I think I'll still come back to the hotel but definitely not the club lounge.

title: “Lovely hotel, lovely staff”
text: We stayed here overnight on our way to Fort Lauderdale and will stay again next April when we visit again. The hotel is lovely and clean and the staff extemely friendly. The mushroom brie soup is worth the visit!

title: “The Worst”
text:
Stayed at Town and Country for a conference for 3 nights. Paid $159 a night and had
Tiny room of Motel 6 quality
Furniture and decor out of the 1970s
19 inch tv
broken remote
shower did not work
$1 fee for local calls
$10 for internet
$35 for 30 minute late check out
Surly staff (can't blame them as they must recieve hundreds of complaints a day.
$16 breakfast buffet that had moldy fruit
$15 to use on site gym
I spooke with dozens of others staying here and all (100%) had similar complaints, including:
broken window
no heat or air
musty odor
The most frustrating part was the are Best Western, Days Inn, Marriott, and others acrss the highway for $70 a night. Friends staying at those places bragged about free internet and breakfast, flat screen tvs, etc.
Save money, avoid a horrible experience. Stay elsewhere.

title: “Love this hotel”
text: What you lack in amenities, you make up for in customer service, location and cleanliness. Rooms are decent size for nyc, it's always clean and friendly, awesome location.

title: “Tiny and extremely hot rooms, very noisy but to a probably fair price.”
text:
First of all: You could get hotels in another area with an own bathroom and double sized for easily half price. It's the location you are paying for. 
I don't really know if i should recommend The Mosser to other people - some things were really nice, some were very annoying. FYI: This is a review about a room with shared bath. I will give you pros and cons:
+: Location - the Hotel is Downtown - Market and 4th. If you wanna be around that area, you are everywhere in a couple of minutes if you prefer to walk, plus there are all kinds of public transportation (Bus, Tram, Cable Car) in the vicinity. You shouldn't be afraid of very weird people - but the whole area is full of them, so even the most expensive Hotel wouldn't help you with that.
Value. At least I couldn't find any acceptable Hotel to a comparable price in this area. But: That's still a lot for what you get.
Good shape. The rooms were fine, the shared bathrooms too - even the restrooms were very clean.
-: Size. The rooms are simply tiny. It's not even possible to open two bags. So be careful if you have a lot of luggage, it won't be nice. The beds are very short.
Temperature and noise. You have two choices - either you sweat like an idiot - you almost couldn't stand the heat, even with a slightly open window. If you open the window completely it might be better - but then you couldn't stand the noise - it was horribly loud. And we had a room with view to the side street - I don't want to imagine the noise with open window if i'd have had a room with view to 4th street.
And remember, my review is based on a room with shared bathroom - if you choose to have a room with your own bathroom, the value of the hotel can be different.

title: “Convenience, Quiet, and Calm”
text:
Was lucky enough to get a room at the Westin. The check-in was good (although I still hate how you have to pay for wi-fi when the other properties in the various chains offer it for free). The room was wonderful! I love the Heavenly beds and had the best night's sleep I've had in months. The view over the tarmac was kind of cool and, although there were airplanes galore just outside the window, it was so quiet in the room. The bathroom was good and the shower had a double showerhead!
I didn't use any of the facilities at the hotel.
LOVED the security lane into the McNamara Terminal! Sweet!

title: “Great rooms, everything else was average”
text: I thought this was an okay stay. We stayed for two nights, and for the most part enjoyed it. The beds were comfortable, the rooms were clean. The showers were nice, as was the rest of the bathroom. The hallways and rest of hotel could use an deep cleaning or some renovation. The buffet was good but a bit pricey and the food was not the greatest nor was the breakfast selection. The inner pool closes around 10 or 11pm but remained noisy beyond that with kids yelling around the game areas. We were also awakened both mornings with loud music coming from the pool area again, and many staff members were joining in the dancing and encouraging the loud music, perhaps it was a scheduled event. The water park area was the best part. The kids enjoyed it, the staff was helpful and did their best with what seemed to be limited resources. I think with some good management and maybe some upgrades this could be a better hotel, but it is not too bad as it is now.

title: “Great Location for Fishermans Wharf”
text:
My wife and I stayed here for a week while in San Francisco, it is a pleasant clean reasonably priced hotel. The room was a little dark but was clean and well maintained with all the usual amenities. The staff are friendly and helpful, there is free coffee in the mornings and wine every night between 5 and 6, Ed was especially welcoming to this event. You could not hope for a better location the wharf is 5 minutes walk a way and Pier 39 ony 10 minutes. It is ideally placed for the cable car stop at Mason will will take you to to the centre of the city. You must visit the attached restaurant called Cafe Pescatore, the manager Nick is charming and the barman Sean a complete character and the food superb, we went 2 nights out of the 7, and is a little cheaper than eating at an equivilant on the wharf.
We both thoroughly enjoyed our stay and would recommend it, the only drawback is that if you have a car it will cost you $44 a night to park there. We arranged with the hire company to return it to them every night which was only a few minutes walk away.

title: “Wonderful and Clean!”
text: I stayed at the La Quinta San Antonio Vance Jackson and was so impressed. I was very comfortable and surprised at the cleanliness of this hotel. The front desk service was friendly and professional and very efficient during my check-in process. I confess to be borderline germ-o-phobic and let me tell you after my ritual check of all linens and surfaces I found absolutely nothing wrong with this room. I slept soundly in the comfortable bed with the surety I was safe and in a fresh, clean bed. I also must comment on how pet-friendly this hotel is. My pet and I were welcomed and informed of their pet-friendliness and policy. The grounds were well kept and other owners with their pets were all respectful and leashed, respectfully.

title: “Great Location”
text: I stayed here for a convention in San Antonio. As far as location, this was perfect. It was right across from the Henry B Gonzalez Center, which is where the convention is held. It overlooks the Riverwalk and is across the street from the Rivercenter where there are a number of shops and restaurants. It is an older hotel. We had an odd number room, so our view was overlooking the parking lot. It appeared that even numbered rooms had balconies that overlooked the riverwalk. I feel sure the view from those rooms was amazing! The walls were thin. A baby was in the room next to us, and I could hear it crying all night. Not that big of a deal for me since I'm a heavy sleeper. We took a cab from the airport which took about 20 minutes. Internet access in NOT free, which was a bummer! But overall, it was an enjoyable stay!

title: “I am DEFINITELY staying there again!”
text:
From guest services at sign-in to the morning breakfast and the evening night-cap or dinner this hotel is a real find. The front desk personnel are very helpful, maintenance is quick, services are well beyond what I expected. I was there for business for nearly a month.
There were limited exceptions to the superlative experience I had at the hotel - insignificant enough to not merit mention. In fact there are not enough good things I can say about the staff and the facility.
I have recommended this hotel to my co-workers, clients, and directors alike.

title: “Not my scene!”
text: Just want to say a huge thankyou to staff Amanda and Jeff who are great assets to the Handlery Hotel. Our stay was cut short but we could not speak highly enough of Amanda's professionalism and kindness.

title: “Couples' MUST STAY - Unique Romantic Atmosphere”
text:
Well, where to start...I guess I should start by pointing out the door keeper waiting for my girlfriend and I as we walked down the street looking for the hotel; it's like he knew us for a long time! He greeted us cheerfully and quickly brought us to the front desk for an expedited check-in (They let us check-in early, very nice).
I quickly noticed that the hotel was in fact really modern looking. It has a dark, romantic feel to it; very different from anything I have seen before. Thumbs up for interior designing.
The room was very clean and neat; just like previous reviews had mentioned. I could say that the room size is small/compact; but then again, it is NYC. I would not really recommend the Deluxe Queen room for a business traveler, for there is no enough room to work. The shower was really spacious and practical; not a problem for tall guys (I'm 6'5"). Bed comforter and sheets were nice and crisp, really cozy! The view from the seventh floor was not bad at all; I was expecting just a wall in front of me, but in fact, I was able to see many different buildings and get a glimpse of the city lights.
Overall, I had a great experience. The concierge gave us some nice restaurant suggestions, and boy am I glad I took his advice!
A few things to point out:
TV: Remote control was not accessing the menu/pay-per-view. I swapped remotes at the front desk. Still did not work. I'm not a big TV watcher, so I didn't really mind.
WIFI: Did not work 90% of the time using my iPhone. When it did, it was really slow. Again, I didn't really mind because I had 3G and did not have to do any work while in the hotel.
Breakfast: The hotel currently does not have a kitchen, so there are limitations to your meal (No eggs, bacon, pancakes and that stuff). Other than that, fresh fruits, awesome OJ, tasty bread, and some other goodies. 
Mini Bar: Awesome selection (wine, beer, FIJI water, and more). But very expensive, like most mini bars.
I Rated a 4 for Condition/Maintenance due to the WIFI and TV.
A+ Service, great location, friendly staff, hip atmosphere, and the coolest bartender (Tom).

title: “A gem (no pun intended) in Washington DC”
text:
I really like Kimpton Hotels. They are top-tier hotels, and while a chain they feel like much smaller and more intimate places to stay. As others have noted, the decorating is non-traditional and a bit off-beat, but still very tasteful. My room was large and obviously not a standard box in a large hotel. The location was near Dupont Circle and an easy walk to the offices along Connecticut Avenue.
What made this trip especially nice was the outstanding service. Everyone I met from the desk to the lounge restaurant was incredibly nice and friendly. The light meal I had in the lounge was delicious and the service pleasant without being overbearing. I had a problem with my computer printer and the front desk staff went out of the way to get me what I needed. Staying here was a very pleasant experience

title: “Great Vacation except for the bee's”
text:
My family and I had a good time. We loved the suites, they are comfortable and clean. The pools were wonderful, also clean!!!
The trouble we had is when we checked in we noticed on the balcony above was a bee's nest, and swarming bee's. We called 3 times for someone to take cake of it. No one responded in over 2 hours. We were finally moved.
I also don't recommend the Mexican resteraunt. We waited over an hour for our meal, no one seemed to care. And when the food came it was cold.
Overall we had a GREAT time. And I'll go back again.

title: “Nice upscale place.”
text:
Hotel & service was great. 
Down side: 
1) no mini refrig. in the room we were staying in
2) No 'free' internet
Otherwise hotel, hotel associates & location is great! Plenty of room for luggage's. Skip the restaurant in the hotel, no worth the time & especially not worth the money. There are better pizza joints then the restaurant.

title: “Lovely hotel”
text: We stayed here for 6 nights in a View Suite. We had been touring round California for the last 2 weeks and were exhausted (we are from England). We were really looking forward to San Diego and it didnt disappoint. Infact we felt it was our best place in CA. We were given an upgrade and so faced the marina. This was lovely, we had a little patio with table and chairs. The ducks came every day and my daughter just loved feeding them. We loved the pool and enjoyed listening to all the concerts, especially Olivia Newton John. We felt very privaledged to be able to hear this lovely music with our glass of wine. You could sit in the huge spa and listen to the concerts, bliss! Our suite was very big and had a lovely big bathroom and dressing area, nice big kitchen and 2 TV's. It was a bit drab and brown, and could have done with a little bit of colour, but otherwise was very nice. I would definately recommend this hotel and would love to come again. We left with heavy heart and could easily have stayed atleast another week. A great place!!

title: “Good experience”
text: The Hilton offers a comfortable room in Midtown, close to major tourist attractions. We stayed for two nights during the Christmas season. The room was $125 from Priceline. Comfortable, good service, safe--they ask everyone entering after 10 pm to show their room key.

title: “this is a dump”
text: This message is coming out of Greenville N.C. Istayed at this hotel on March 5th. It was very nasty. The blankets and sheets were discusting. We had to call and ask them to give us some heat in 20 degree weather. We had no way of cutting the heat on ourselves. The shower curtain had mildew stains all over it. You could have died from the thick dust on the furniture. This hotel needs to be shut down. Hotel needs to take this off their list.

title: “One of the best”
text:
Ottawa, Ontario, Canada
Our group travels to San Diego many times every year for business. We always stay at the Best Western Blue Sea Lodge.
The staff are very nice. Rooms are always very clean. The location by the board walk is great. Access to bars and good restaurants within walking distance. I give this hotel a 5 start rating. I firmly believe it is well diserved.
Should you be travelling to San Diego, I highly recommend the Blue Sea Lodge.

title: “I love this hotel and will be back”
text:
The great hotel stay at the Hilton Garden Inn started even before I arrived at the hotel. Via email, I received an email from Nicole Cermele, the Guest Experience Manager of the hotel. It provided some general, but valuable information about the hotel.
The experience continued to exceed expectations... from the warm reception I received at check-in from Rachel, the swift, efficient check-in, was handled in a few minutes. The room was spotless and comfortable each day of the five night stay. I commend the housecleaning staff for their quick, complete cleaning of the room each day. 
I can think of nothing that could improve the either the hotel or services provided by the entire team at the Hilton Garden Inn Times Square.
I look forward to returning to this hotel in the very near future.

title: “I was more than satisfied with this hotel.”
text: I found this to be a great hotel especially for the price. The staff was nice from the time we checked in and even helped us with directions. I also liked the design of the room. It felt upscale and comfortable. I really had no complaints during my stay here.

title: “Did not live up to the rave reviews”
text:
I was really looking forward to my stay at the Valencia. At my $500 a night AAA discounted room rate I was expecting something really special. The checkin staff were great and I could not wait to get to my room. When I opened the room it was pitch black. I need to use my phone light in roder to switch on the entrance light and then needed to use it multpiple times again to find the different switches on all the lights in the lounge and the bedroom. I also found that the desk did not have adequate power supplies with a work chair less than adequate. We neded to conduct multiple business meetings in the lounge yet the light in the room was totally inadequate and the meetings were conducted in semi darkness... I will say the bathroom was large abd brightly lit and very very nice
The breakfast was very average and while included in the price did not wow me with the selection or taste. Staff though were very very nice.
Internet service while free was very very slow
Overall this hotel did not at all wow me and was certainly not worth the "discounted price" I needed to pay. There are much better and cheaper places to stay in the valley

title: “I Like this Place”
text: My wife and I have stayed at this hotel many times for two primary reasons: availability of good rates and swimming pool. We were able to get an excellent rate Christmas week by using the travelzoo/ticker code. The corner rooms in the east tower have a magnificent view of the East River and UN on one side and the Chrysler and Empire State Buildings on the other. The corner room is quite spacious by NYC standards. The pool is on the 27th floor and also commands the river view. Although the hotel is very comfortable, it is several steps below luxurious. We had a few maintenance issues in our room and the carpets in the 33rd floor hallways are taped in multiple places and present a shabby appearance. This hotel would be truly spectacular with an injection of cash for some necessary updating.

title: “Better than the TripAdvisor rating suggests”
text: I was worried when I "won" a room at this hotel on Hotwire; however, the hotel surpassed my expectations. I stayed on the 9th floor and my room was clean, quiet and updated. As others have attested, the location is great. You can easily walk to Beacon Hill, the North End, Faneuil Hall, the Public Gardens, the Esplanade at the Charles River and many other places. The MBTA (red line) is also close by, which will take you almost anywhere in Boston. For the price I paid, I was satisfied. The hotel really deserves a higher rating on Trip Advisor. It is not on par with The Liberty by any means but it is a solid 3 star hotel.

title: “Terrific Stay”
text:
Very impressed with the Coral Sands Motel in Los Angeles. The hotel staff were very friendly and very helpful from the second I arrived at the hotel. The gent who works the front desk in the morning was simply the best, wherever I needed to go he made sure I had the best way to get there! Also, the hotel is very gay friendly, so that made me feel right at home. Also the motel is located at Hollywood and Western, kind of out of the way of everything but it is a 2 minute walk to the Metro station and 2 stops away from everything one could do in LA. 
The pool and hot tub were the best! That is how I started and ended my day. Thanks for a great stay, will be back to stay here everytime I visit LA.
Justin, from Canada.

title: “Good Location. Mediocre, Tiny Rooms.”
text:
We stayed at the Stanford because we were seeing Paul McCartney at Madison Square Garden on 09/30 and chose the hotel because of its location to MSG, and because of the reviews on Trip Advisor were pretty good, compared to others in the same price range.
Our check-in was smooth, however, the person at the front desk neglected to inform us that the following morning there was a Korean Festival taking place and if you parked on 32nd Street (which we did directly across the street from the hotel), that you would have to have your car out before 8:00am or you would be stuck there until 6:00pm when the festival ended and 32nd Street reopened.
It wasn't until 12:30am after the concert, when we headed up to our room did we notice the plain white flyer posted on the wall stating that the street would be closed off. Not being early morning people, and had not yet unwound from the concert, we had no desire to be leaving prior to 8:00am so we ended up driving home at 1:00am that night . So we weren't real happy with the lack of information. We understand the hotel does not control street closures, however, the staff could have been more informative so we could have parked elsewhere and saved us alot of hassle. Needless to say, we paid $200 for a hotel room we basically only used to change clothes.
As for the room itself, it is very small and not kept very clean. The bed was uncomfortable, the tv old and the fridge kept things luke warm at best. The towels in the bathroom were clean, however, the bathroom itsself was not and the tub was disgusting.
The pictures of the room and bathroom are greatly enhanced on their website.
If you are looking for a reasonably priced hotel with a great location and are only staying 1 night this hotel will do. For anything more than that, pay extra and get a nicer place.
Lastly, I was a bit apprehensive about it being in Koreatown, however, there is a ton of activity going on and great restaurants at your doorstep. I never once felt unsafe. And MSG was literally 2 blocks down the street.

title: “Mixed Review”
text: The Grand Hyatt is a beautiful hotel in an excellent central location for touring Washington, DC. As another reviewer mentioned, there is a Metro station in the building, and the hotel is close to Chinatown and several restaurants. The service in the hotel, however, is not the best. Guests are required to call the front desk if they want their towels and linens changed daily. We asked for recommendations for a casual restaurant near the hotel, and the concierage recommended a chain burger restaurant. The hotel tends to have great rates on the weekends because it caters to business people during the week. There is a Starbucks and deli in the lobby, which is also very convenient. Overall, the good outweighs the bad. We have stayed there twice and plan on staying there the next time we go to D.C.

title: “I will stay at the Indepedent everytime I travel to Phily”
text: What a hidden gem in the heart of it all. The rooms are amazing and my clients raved about this hotel. I'm in the hospitality industry and travel significantly for work. I would recommend this property to anyone.

title: “Great location, friendly staff and great room!”
text:
We got at the hotel at 10.30PM after flying for 10 hours to get there. We booked for 4 nights. When we arrived and wanted to check in, the lady at the reception said they had a little problem and asked if we wanted to wait in the lobby (which is very close to the reception). We heard her and a male staff member calling other hotels and asking if they had a room. After 5 minutes she said 'we are looking for a room, sorry for the inconvenience, it will take a few minutes more'. After about 10 minutes they found the Flatotel on 52th Street for us. We would stay here one night and check in again the next they. They assured us we would really have a room the next day and we left by taxi to the Flatotel. The lady at the front desk said we should save the cab tickets so they could return the fare. Next day we went from the Flatotel back to Salisbury, again with a yellow cab and we saved the tickets. They returned the money and we could leave our bags in the storage room at the concierge. We went to see the city and returned at about 8PM. We asked the reception for the key, we got a room at the 7th floor. We asked the concierge for our bags and he would bring them to our room.
We went up with the elevator and saw we got a really big, nice room. It was a room with seperate bedroom with TV, little kitchen (well only microwave, coffeemaker, sink, refrigerator with freeze compartiment) and off course the living room with an TV about 42" big. We wondered if the hotel gave us this room cause they couldn't give us a room the first night. The concierge came with our bags about 5-10 minutes after we asked him to. Oh, and the lady of the reception explaned to us (after we asked) that they had a problem with piping on one floor. So we think, because we arrived so late the first day, they had just gave away all of the rooms and had some guests send over to an other hotel (like us).
Each day you get a paper which says you can go to the 3th floor for breakfast, I think they charge about $6 per person, I'm not sure of the price. We didn't used this option as we went to the Green Cafe which is 3 doors away from the hotel. I can imagine some people think the breakfast is included, but if you read the paper well you can see it isn't.
Cleaning is fine, didn't find hairs or anything. One remote controle didn't work very good, it couldn't switch on the tv. But if the tv was on, it was working okay. 
The location of the hotel is okay, although the location Flatotel (52th Street) was better in case of seeing Times Square, Rockefeller Center etc. But just walk and it's fine. The hotel is only 2 blocks away from Central Park, wauw! 
Pros:
- Location
- Friendly staff
- Clean, comfy and spacy room
- Didn't hear neighbour sounds
Cons:
- Piping problem, so we were send to an other hotel. Problem quickly solved and to our satisfaction. This is only a little con.
- No free WIFI

title: “Quick, but fantastic Chicago trip”
text:
We arrived about 3 hours earlier than check-in to the Springhill Suites, which didn't seem to be a problem at all. Every employee we saw was friendly and welcoming. The giant bowl of lollipops at the front desk was a bonus.
We had a 4th floor handicapped room (it was the only one ready due to our early arrival). Although the handicapped room was smaller than a typical suite there, it was very comfortable and the restroom was huge. Our group of 4 twenty-somethings had no complaints about the space in our room. And the mini-fridge and microwave were so handy to have. Also, the wireless internet was free and worked wonderfully.
The hotel is in an excellent location. Quick walks to shopping and amazing dining. And just steps from the dueling piano bar Howl at the Moon (which is a must-do for tourists!).
A couple other great things about the Springhill Suites- the amazing free breakfast (it was delicious, had tons of variety and the employees were so friendly and quick to help with anything) and the pool and hot tub (although the pool is kind of small, it was rarely crowded, the view is amazing and a soak in the hot tub really hit the spot after a day of shopping and sightseeing). 
I would return to this hotel in a minute. I have zero complaints and our group can't stop talking about going back again.

title: “Quality San Francisco Stay”
text: Aside from the centralized location of the Hotel Kabuki, the quality of the rooms and customer service make this hotel always a pleasant stay for me. The access to great food and entertainment is ideal for this 7x7 city. I would highly recommend to anyone looking for quality lodging in San Francisco.

title: “Great Memorial Day Weekend”
text:
We spent one night over Memorial Day weekend. This was our second stay at Marriott Marquis. This time we had access to the concierge lounge which we took a full advantage of. We enjoyed our stay and will definitely return. 
LOCATION: The hotel is right by Time Square which is great for seeing a Broadway show. We walked to the Rockefeller Center, the Central Park and also down to Macy's. The disadvantage of this location is that the streets are always crowded. Because we were staying over Sunday night, we could find free street parking not too far away from the hotel from Sunday morning till Monday morning. I always use http://nyc.bestparking.com to look for the best parking rate and free street parking when visiting NYC.
ROOM: Clean and spacious for a NYC hotel room. We had two double beds - very comfortable after walking around all day.
CONCIERGE LOUNGE: The evening Hors d'oeuvre were average, but the breakfast was good with eggs, sausages, croissant, muffins, fresh fruit, yogurt, cereal, etc. The place was really crowded during breakfast, and it was hard to find a table. But we thoroughly enjoyed our breakfast and took water bottles for the rest of the day. 
I recommend going to the revolving View Restaurant at the top of the hotel. We were there at 11pm for cocktails, and the place was packed. I thought the dessert buffet was overpriced for what they were offering, but if you are in a splurging mood, both calories and money, enjoy yourselves!

title: “Very disappointing!”
text: The Westin Columbus looks nice on the outside and their lobby is beautiful, but their guest room was so disappointing. it was the size of a closet, with only a full bed for two people to share. The view was laughable, of the air conditioning units and roof and looked right into other rooms. The worst part of it was the parking though! There is a tiny lot that you're expected to park in for $20/night/car, and you can barely pull in and out. It is a total nightmare when it's busy! They inspect your car beforehand, and I later understood it was probably because they have a lot of accidents and bumps in that lot. The new Hilton is opening downtown, it might be worth a try instead.

title: “Amazing place for the price!!!”
text:
My husband and I chose this hotel for a vacation to Dallas. We wanted a pet-friendly, NON-highrise hotel in an upscale area that was pleasant to walk in. This is directly across the street from SMU and adjacent to beautiful residential neighborhoods full of $700K+ homes. We weren't sure what to expect as they had JUST opened shortly before our arrival and the price we paid per night was $134.
Everything certainly exceeded our expectations. The rooms are beautifully appointed, and the staff was very attentive and helpful. I loved the modern, clean, but warm and earthy decor - MUCH more chic and aesthetically pleasing than your typical sterile, corporate Hilton, IMO. 
The shower was wonderful - love the body jets and the fact that it's big enough for two. Of course, sometimes it was hard to get in the shower without getting the floor wet. I also liked the shampoo, conditioner and soap they provide - reminded me of Aveda or other natural products.
They were WONDERFUL to our dog. We have a 40lb well-behaved dog, and they were extremely accomodating, even providing a large, high quality dog bed, a stainless water bowl and a pig ear! They allowed us to leave her crated in the room when we went out, which was nice - some hotels don't allow that. 
We went to their restaurant the night it opened for the very first time. I'm glad we got to try it - it was good. The Mac n Cheese was the most unique item on the menu - sounds low brow but it was quite good, if a little salty. They hadn't worked out the kinks enough for a full-on room service menu, but they would have given us whatever we wanted. It was that type of hotel - small enough to really accomodate individual requests. 
We LOVED our stay there - an extremely comfortable place, ESPECIALLY if you have a dog. The neighborhood could not be more perfect for dog owners. We run with ours a lot every day, and we could easily take a short, scenic run through the neighborhood, past the countryclub, to Highland Park Village (where they have Chanel, Hermes and Jimmy Choo boutiques)and have Starbucks in the morning. 
I highly recommend this boutique hotel, ESPECIALLY if you can get a rate like $135/night - far and above simliarly priced hotels we've stayed at in the past!!!

title: “perfect”
text:
We were in San Diego for a convention and real happy to stay here. Nice room on 7th floor with view of the Star of India and the bay. Easy to walk to the convention center. Good breakfast, near Little Italy and Gaslamp, free wifi. People at the front desk were real helpful.
We enjoyed our stay. The noise of the train is not so bad when we close the door and use the climatisation. Free shuttle to the airport.

title: “Just Okay”
text:
When in need of a place to simply stop for a night, we often choose Hampton Inns. They are never luxurious, but you almost always get a well-maintained facility with clean rooms and the basic amenities you need for a short stay, at a reasonable price. We were flying out of Love Field early in the morning, so chose this Hampton because it is fairly close to the airport, and just off I-35E. With the road construction on and around I-35E, and the proximity to the airport, this location was somewhat disappointing, and it's still a few miles from the airport, so not quite as convenient as you might think. Even though it wasn't all that close to the airport, we chose it anyway, relying upon the fact that Hamptons are a reliably-good option. The location was somewhat noisy, and just generally unattractive.
The exterior, common areas, lobby, hallways, etc were all somewhat shabby-looking and in need of some updating, which is unusual for a Hampton Inn. It appeared that there was some renovation/updating going on, as almost all the doors to the rooms had some sort of spackling smeared on them in places. One of the two elevators was not working. On the positive side (and the reason I gave them an overall "average" rating, instead of something lower) the interior of our room was just what we've come to expect from a Hampton Inn. It was clean, well-maintained and appeared to be relatively new. 
So, perhaps this hotel is in the process of an upgrade/remodel, in which case, in a few months, it may be deserving of a higher rating, but until then, "average" is about the best I can offer, although, I doubt the quality of the location is going to improve much any time soon.

title: “Lives up to Westin name”
text: I've never had a problem with Westin hotels and this one was no different. Got a great deal for $89. I like the round towers which gives the room a cool layout. There was a great view of the city. Room service was expensive but good. Westin beds are always the best. I felt very comfortable in this hotel. The bellman was very helpful and told me about the Airporter bus which saved me a lot instead of taking a cab to the airport.

title: “Relaxing stay in the beautiful Magnolia Denver”
text:
Desired a night out in downtown Denver and chose the Magnolia based on TripAdvisor reviews. Nearly everything of what you'll read on here about the Magnolia is true; it's in a great location in downtown Denver (lodo), is a beautiful hotel made from an old bank building (even has original elevators), and the staff is great. We had a King Suite and it was a spacious, multi room suite with a king bed. The furniture nor television sets didn't blow me away as being super modern, but the room was clean, well designed and spacious.
They have a bunch of free perks you will not find elsewhere in downtown Denver. Just check their site for that information. We didn't have a chance to enjoy the breakfast, but it looked pretty solid. We did use the free shuttle service; made a 7:15PM reservation for a ride downtown and they were easily 20 minutes late for that. They were apologetic and this was the only slip up we experienced.
Overall we were very happy with the experience and would stay at the Magnolia again without hesitation.

title: “We loved it and we'll be back!”
text: When my husband and I were booking a hotel for our recent trip to Seattle, we tried to book the Grand Hyatt and Hyatt Olive 8 because we've stayed at both before and found them to be exceptional. We were very disappointed to find that both hotels were full for the nights we wanted. My husband suggested that we try the Hilton, reminding me that it was closer to much of the "action" - Pike's Market, shopping, Safeco Field (well, that is about a half hour walk away), We booked our two night stay online. One of the options was to book a room which gave us access to the Executive Lounge (room price was around $210 Canadian - internet and parking extra). When we arrived, we went for a drink to unwind after our day of travel. The Executive Lounge had a great selection of appetizers (free of charge) and reasonably priced drinks. Unfortunately, we had other plans for our second day and we didn't get back to the lounge. The room also included breakfast both days. We were given the choice of ordering from the menu or going to the buffet. The buffet had a good selection of breakfast food (eggs, sausage, bacon, breads of all varieties, cereal, etc.) but also had cold meats, fruit and some fantastic lox to go with your bagels and cream cheese. The service was fantastic - they were quick to bring us our own coffee pot and the staff was extremely polite and helpful. The hotel is undergoing some renovations (most seem complete) but they didn't interfere with our pleasant stay. Our only concern was that parking was at a premium. The first day we had no trouble finding space, but after arriving back at the hotel around 7:30 on the second day, it was so busy that the hotel manager was directing parking and we were directed to go to the 9th (and top) floor to find a spot. This was likely because it was a Saturday night and there was at least one wedding reception being held in the hotel. All in all, it was a wonderful stay and I wouldn't hesitate to stay there again, or to recommend this hotel to anyone!

title: “Great Employee: Juan Verduzco Jr.”
text: Thanks so much to Juan for making my solo trips to the hotel restaurant for breakfast such a delight. He was attentive and engaging and I enjoyed hearing about how he was planning to enjoy his family for the July 4th weekend.

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
We had a great time here while in Denver. I let them know that it was our son's 9th birthday before our stay and when we got to our room there were balloons, Izze juice, snacks and some small gifts waiting for him. It was such a great surprise and our son was so happy. It was so great of the staff to make him feel so special.
The room was spacious. The colors were strange but it really works. The bed was very comfortable. The hotel was very close to the 16th Street Mall so it was easy to walk to restuarants and shops.

title: “Great for business travel.”
text: This hotel is great for business travel. The rates are good and the staff is very helpful. The Manager Aurelia Gaskin is always ready to help. Check in and checkout is always fast and easy.

title: “Fantastic hotel”
text: Hotel is in a great location. Bagel and crepe shop across the street. Pizza one block down and French bakery on the corner. Very close to the Metro with Krispy Kreme at the entrance. What could be better! The staff is wonderful. This includes front desk, bell boys, valet guys. Our room was a King suite with a roll away which was perfect for us three. VERY large room. If I had a negative it would be the congestion in front of the hotel. The valet guys grab your car very quickly, but you have to watch the traffic. We did pay $40 per day for parking in the final bill. I think the staff, hotel decor and cleanliness is great enough to balance out the parking issues.

title: “Beautiful Stay in San Diego”
text: The hotel is conveniently located across from the Gas Lamp area and trolley line. Very easy to get around San Diego. Exercise facilities in hotel were great! Hot tub and pool - beautiful. Staff was very attentive - great stay!

title: “Very good”
text: I lived in new york for a while, so i know the city pretty well. I was looking for something for few days, and this hotel was the solution. Even if it was not really cheap, the accomodation and the location were excellent. It worth the money we spent. And I appreciated the included breakfast. The room is new, clean, with lcd tv, and the staff is very gentle, available, and polite.

title: “Hit and Miss Service”
text: I stayed at the Sofitel in January and had a very good experience: a nice room, very clean, good service, no problems. So when I stayed there again recently, I was extremely disappointed in the service. Both times we stayed in a Junior Suite. The room was on the top floor, very large, clean and nicely furnished. The problem with my second stay was the service. I left out a breakfast order on the door and called down to reception to let them know that it was there, but the next morning there was no breakfast. The next morning when I called down, they scrambled to get something up to us as quickly as possible, but they only brought up breakfast for one, not two, so they had to go back down and get the second breakfast. I had to call down as well to get bathrobes, which housekeeping had tucked away on the top shelf of the closet as opposed to having them hanging somewhere that we might find them. We ordered a bottle of wine to be sent to the room, which they brought up with wine glasses and a corkscrew. However, we didn’t open the wine on the first night so we had to call down on the second night to get them to redeliver the wine glasses and the corkscrew which arrived half an hour later. So we ended up spending much of the weekend waiting in the room for room service and housekeeping to take care of many of the small requests that had been overlooked in the first place. I wasn’t impressed.

title: “Great Value”
text: I had booked this hotel last November but did not realize I had made a mistake with the dates until I arrived in Pheonix. The manager was very accomodating in finding us a room. This is probably the cleanest hotel I have ever stayed in. You could tell as soon as you walked into the room that they take pride in having a clean hotel. The place is not fancy by any means but well worth the value.

title: “Perfect for business travel”
text:
The single room was perfect for me: desk, wi-fi, bed, hangers, and an iron on request. There's room under the bed for a suitcase. Everything was clean, good shower water pressure. And central to the newark express bus and grand central. I've stayed in bigger rooms with less usability. 
I slept well and worked well.
The one thing I would add is some sort of breakfast-in-box option. If they had a bagel, yogurt, and coffee to go, I would definitely have taken advantage of that.

title: “Fabulous Location”
text: Myself my husband and our two children recently stayed at this hotel. I was a little nervous being unfamiliar with the area. Everything was perfect, we had the room with the kitchenette there was plenty of space for us. The location however is what will keep me going back, just amazing we were there during winter break and we went to see the Rockettes. Radio City was a 2 minute walk and skating at Rockefeller 2 minute walk. We did not have to take a taxi once we walked everywhere and to the subway once. I have recommended this hotel to my friends and family.

title: “Parking problem / Horrible response”
text: Beware! Hotel lot fills up weekends and if you park slightly off the property your car will be towed and you will have a $300 fee to retreive your car. I was hit by this. Management was NO help. Worse, no signs indicate where exactly the boundary is between Sleep Inn and defunct Comfort Inn next door. They also state that if you park at curb, they will tow car because that is the fire lane. Lot is not sufficient for the number of guests. Also agree that general maintenance in many areas was poor, hotel is "beat up" and needs work. Furniture and carpets were dirty.

title: “small but happy at park savoy”
text:
After traveling 11 hrs on a bus ANY hotel would look good but I did find a great suprise when our taxi pulled in front of the Park Savoy Hotel. For once a hotel looked JUST like it did in their pictures!! From the entrance, to the stairs, and the rooms all appeared to have no hidden suprises! The price also upheld what I was told. I ended up paying on 99 dollars a night which included tax and breakfast for four people for 5 nights!!! Great price huh?!?! There was only two things I did not care for that much. The first being the beds. They ae NOT beds for someone with a bad back! They tend to be hard (but after walking the NYC streets you really don't care to much were you sleep as long as your not on your feet!!!) And the second being the bathroom. Along with the size (pretty small) it got EXTREMELY hot when taking a shower. About half way through each shower I had to open the door to the bathroom to get some air!
Aside from these two things you will not find a better hotel in NYC for a person on a budget. It sits across from some of the "big expensive" hotels and it only a few blocks from places such as the Plazza Hotel, 5th Ave shopping, Tavern on the Greens, and the Russian Tea room. 
My second surpise is when I found I was ni WALKING distance to Times Square!!! Only about 6 blocks!!!!! Also, you can't forget Central Park is only ONE block, and the same goes for the subway station. 
If you tried to find a hotel that offered this convenience, price, and location in NYC it would be around 400 to 600 a night!! I would recommend this hotel for anyone who comes to NYC to have some fun and not pay to much!

title: “Brand New DoubleTree in Midtown - Perfect”
text: A brand new DoubleTree right in the heart of midtown - what more can I ask for! I booked this room for a leisure trip at a fantastic rate and was happy with everything. Rooms were all brand new with major new amenities. The only downside were that the rooms were small, but that is to be expected in NY and I didn't really mind the size of the room.

title: “Crap”
text: Paint fallng off,hole in bathroom wall,dirty,bed was broke and they never came to fix,over all VERY bad visit,oh did i forget to mention mold in shower and pool has not been open yet i was told

title: “Very nice hotel”
text:
I was really looking forward to staying here and seeing SF again after 11 years - back then I was 20 now I'm with my kids. 
This hotel was fantastic, the friendliest most helpful and kid friendly I have ever encountered in such a nice hotel. The rooms are nice, food in the resturant was great- especially the steak. Hot apple cider daily in the lobby with gingerbread and apples was enjoyed by my kids 3 & 4 and us parents also. 
Milk and cookies every night when we got back to our room was such a nice touch.

title: “Unnecessary Roughness”
text:
I love Chicago and have always had a great time there. I stayed at this hotel as the friend I was traveling with had loyalty points. My friend requested a nice view when she made the reservation and it was so noted. When we arrived she asked again about a nice view and was told there was no such thing in this midrise hotel in uptown Chicago. He was right, there was no nice view....there was a view directly into the room around the corner. It felt like you could climb right into the bed in the room next door. So obviously it was necessary to use care to keep the curtains closed......so quite correct, no view at all. In fact, I would suggest black-out windows. Note the picture of our view, taken with an iphone from our window with no zoom whatsoever......see what I mean?
The main entry lobby is gross. Like an attempt to make a too small area into some funky Euro-decor complete with neon lights, ala Moulin Rouge. No refrigerator or micro in the room, no safe in the room, no nothing.
We arrived in the evening and checked out next morning, so we closed the drapes and stayed out of the room except for sleeping. Checked the bags and shopped North Michigan Avenue for the day, came back to pick up our bags late in the afternoon, valet brought up the car and we loaded up and headed out without incident. It should be noted that a gentleman by the name of Charles helped us with our bags and was very friendly and hospitable. 
After returning from our trip my travel partner informed me that her card had been charged $250 for a "smoking fee." The hotel provided digital pictures of cigarette butts floating in the toilet and ashes on the desk along with a photo of our room number. Problem is, not only are we non-smokers but we could be categorized as militant non-smokers. After about ten days of back and forth with the AGM "investigating officer anti-smoking Nazi" (actually that's kind of a compliment coming from me, a fellow anti-smoking Nazi) and finally a call to the Corporate office they finally took the word of their non-smoking guests and removed the charge. Not a very nice memory for either of us, and a crazy thing to do to a regular guest over many years with nary an issue regarding smoking.
My suggestion is that you cough up an extra $100 per night and stay at the Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers, where I have had many delightful stays and where I will stay when I return to Chi-town. I promise it will be well worth it!

title: “Beautiful hotel! But lots of noise in room”
text: There is little sound proofing in the rooms for outside noise! Other then that what a beautiful hotel! Great staff, very helpful, great location close to the stadiums for the sports fan made to feel secure in the hotel, made to look the age of the hotel but brand new furniture in the room!!!!

title: “Impressive Hotel”
text:
Impressive Hotel but not a lot to do in downtown Houston.
Lovely room, very comfortable bed, and staff were very helpful too. There is a shuttle from the hotel to the Galleria shopping centre but other than that nothing!!

title: “Best concierge”
text: While the hotel itself was good and had all the amenities that one would expect from Marriott in a big city, what really stood out was the outstanding concierge at this hotel. I was in town for a conference with a large group and each time I called the concierge, I was given the best customer service that went above and beyond the call of duty. Not only was I given help in making reservations, Franco and all the other guys at the concierge desk would make sure that the places I took my group to met the "seal of locals approval." The service was professional, thorough and very personalized - thanks guys for making our trip a great one!

title: “You have got to be joking”
text:
The marketing department for this hotel needs to be hired by the US government, they could make the current debit situation seem like the best thing since slice bread was invented. 
Please take note their web site view of the lobby is an artist rendering only the real lobby is very cold, like you are walking into a meat chill room. There are so many things wrong with this place I don't know where to begin. Let's go with small rooms, how small, yes I'm going to say it. It was so small I had to leave the room to change my mind. The tv was wider than the bed, no tub only a shower with one towel. Not to mention the 3ft ironing board, thank goodness we were only there for two nights. This is not a four star property, it is a hostel with bellmen.

title: “Extremely Rude Staff”
text: Had called to verify my room type after booking and then arrived to check in and was given a different room type, after a 30minute wait to check in and the front desk clerk answered a call while checking me in, I returned to the front desk to inform them of the error she proceeded to tell me there was an upgrade charge and I informed her I had called and was told I was in that room type already. She was beyond extremely rude, called security over, I'm not sure what his purpose was, she then proceeded to continue to be super rude and basically called me a liar. Super unimpressed, 4 star this is not what you expect

title: “Great business stay in LA”
text:
I had a great stay in the Westin. The hotel bar is in a central location right by reception and is easy for meeting collegues.
