The rooms are standard, and the bed is worthy of praise as it was large and comfy. The shower was 2 headed and really woke me up in the morning! Scenes from "True Lies" and "In the line of fire" were filmed here and the elevators are instantly recognizable for fans of those films.
There is a revolving restaurant and cocktail bar on the top floors which is well worth a visit, particularly if you like steak with great city views!
If you are in downtown LA for a conference then this hotel is a 5 minute cab ride or 20-25 minute walk from the conference center.

title: “Friendly Staff and Best Value Hotel in San Francisco”
text:
The Hotel California is clean, its staff are friendly, and its location is just about perfect.
Upon arrival, Duane at The Hotel California gave us a bunch of tips on how to make the best use of our time in the city, from transportation tips to where to eat and what to see. Without his tips, we would have spent twice as much and seen half as much. Thank you, Duane. We will come back to see the city soon.

title: “Great base for sightseeing and shopping due to location and very knowledgeable staff.”
text: Clean and well equipped rooms. General manger makes himself known to guests and is very helpful. All staff are courteous, friendly and extremely knowledgeable. They ensured we enjoyed our visit by their help and advice.

title: “What a find.”
text: Thank you to the contributors of this site for recommending this lovely hotel. My elderly mother and I stayed two nights at the beginning of June and couldn't have been more pleased, especially given the bargain price of $149 a night. My mother took the queen size bed and I slept on the pull-out sleeper couch, which to my surprise was very comfortable. The room was large and as mentioned by others there was a well-equipped full kitchen, a nicely decorated dressing area and comfortable bathroom. Great location! Close to Metro, restaurants, and sights and walking in the neighborhood is very pleasant. There is also a Safeway located in the lower level of the Watergate complex that is only two blocks away. I would stay there again and highly recommend it.

title: “Great history...tired Grand Dame”
text: Was a bit disappointed in the St.Francis. The location was terrific, the staff top notch...and the hotel is storied. However, I expected much more from a hotel of this caliber. The rooms are spotless...yet worn. I consider myself an adept traveler, not that picky. This Gran Dame needs some Botox!

title: “Fine Hotel in a Great Location”
text:
Stayed here for 4 nights in September 2010. The location, just off Union Square, is excellent with Market Street just a few minutes away for access to the MUNI and BART transport systems. For shopaholics, loads of fine shops around. Plenty of restaurants in the immediate vicinity and Chinatown is barely a 5 minute walk away. 
The rooms were surprisingly large, with a fine, large comfortable bed. The standard of cleanliness and housekeeping was also good. We heard no street noise on the 26th floor, excepting occasional emergency vehicle sirens. The only negative comment I have of the hotel as a whole is that we felt the rooms themselves could do with a makeover – seemed a bit on the tired and dowdy side. I was especially surprised to see an old fashioned CRT TV – we’re more used to LCD TVs these days. 
We enjoyed the very excellent bar on the top floor (36th floor) where the views were quite stunning. A good drinks menu, but we never had a full meal in the restaurant, preferring to eat out although we did enjoy a pizza on our first evening after an 11 hour flight as we were tired but not especially hungry; it was fine. Bar prices were not too expensive considering the status of the hotel and the location, so we used it quite a lot. 
We always found the staff to be very helpful and attentive. In all, an excellent stay and would definitely stay again.

title: “Nice rooms, although small, in good location”
text: We enjoyed our stay at The River Hotel. It is a great location easily accessible to public transit. Our room was small, but it had a European type of feel, and it seemed many guests were European. We had both a small fridge and a microwave which was helpful. The free wireless is a nice feature with ability to print downstairs. I did not use the fitness center since we do so much walking, but would have had they had a pool. My bad for not checking that. The water bottle filling stations on each floor is also another great feature. We did not eat at the restaurant, but there are many nearby, including Dunkin' Donuts and Starbucks for coffee and breakfast. Filming of Transformers 3 was taking place during our visit which made it very interesting.

title: “Clean, Extremely Friendly Staff, and Great Location”
text:
We came into town to watch a Yankees game and eat a wonderful steak house. Were able to do both and this hotel was perfect. Central location to other friends who lived in the city and we'd go back to this hotel in a heartbeat. 
Andrew at the front counter was terrific. Understands hospitality and was extremely professional.

title: “Motel 6 on Military Rd., S. Seattle, WA”
text: The Sea-tac Airport location has had security theft problems involving vehicles and is not a quiet place to stay. This location on Military Rd. is just off the I5N and after exiting there is another right exit. Our room was large, the heater worked quietly and efficiently set on low. We did not need to run the heater the entire night. The carpet was freshly shampood. Nearby gas and coffee and pastry shop also. This location allowed for the parking of our vehicle in front of the room. This location is also a very quiet place to stay with a moderate price.

title: “Very high standard in a great location”
text:
Stayed here for three nights during September 2008 and thoroughly enjoyed it. The rooms were large, clean, comfortable and very well appointed - I especially enjoyed the huge HD flatscreen TV and the Bose Waveradio. The furnishings are to a high standard, lots of toiletries, bathrobes, towels - really everything you need
There are the usual facilities - we ate breakfast in the hotel only once and whilst it was of a very high quality and, again, superb service, it felt a little pretentious. So we walked 200 yds up Rush for something a little more Chicago.
The hotel staff were to a fault courteous and helpful, nothing was really too much trouble. It's also a very attractive building located around 200m from the John Hancock centre on Michigan Avenue. Perfect for shopping, and only 250m from the Chicago CTA Red Line station so very easy access from O'Hare.
Very highly recommended.

title: “Safe, clean, great location”
text: This was a really good choice for the price in Manhattan. Secure, clean, modern and newly furnished rooms, friendly and informed staff, comfortable beds and in a great location for all the varying downtown neibourhoods. Greenwich Village, West and East Villages and even Chelsea and midtown are also walkable. You are also very neat the Williamsburg Bridge so the multitude of bars, restaurants and galleries of hipster Brooklyn are about $12 cab ride away. Yes the breakfast is busy and functional but we stayed hear for seven nights and didn't have a problem getting a table on any day. One proviso in terms of noise: the Queen doubles are at the back of the building. This has pros and cons noise wise. Whilst you're away from the 24 hour street noise of the Bowery and Grand Street there is a constant hum from the aircon fans. Even though we were on the ninth flour and the fans are on the ground I could still hear them. Some earplugs might be recommended if you're a light sleeper. Having said this, it is New York and you should expect noise and overall we had a great stay at the Hanbee.

title: “One of the best hotels I have ever stayed at.”
text: It was such a wonderful hotel. It had very friendly staff. Rooms were huge. When my sister, my son and I were ready for bed we have never had such a wonderful nights sleep. The beds were amazing. It was so great we didnt want to leave.

title: “beri nice hotel”
text:
location is simply great, it's just behind Times Square and near 42 street Port Authority bus terminal. A short walk from Macy's, Grand Central Terminal and Rockefeller Center. Shake Shack is just diagonally across the street, Junior's is behind the hotel, MacDonald and Starbucks are next block. 
Lobby is on the 2nd floor, there is a lift at the back if you are having big luggages, otherwise there is a escalator in front. There are inter-connecting room as well. Room is rather small but its more than sufficient for twin sharing.

title: “Tranquility at the edge of downtown LA”
text:
After being intrigued by this gem of a hotel back when it was known as the New Otani, I was glad to wind up there recently with a successful Priceline bid.
The room was what I expected for a 3-star hotel: perfectly adequate, nothing to go wild over. At registration the desk clerk handed me a cup of iced tea and a warm towel while I was signing in--a nice touch, and a sign of the thoughtful service that was to mark my stay throughout.
The lobby's great, and the third-floor garden is a haven. The restaurant A Thousand Cranes is worth checking out. It's pricey, but the Sunday buffet is one of the best meals (and high-end bargains!) I've had in Los Angeles.
The location, with a bail bond place practically next door, may be off-putting, but that's because a city detention center is nearby, as is City Hall. Thanks to one or two restaurants open as late as 3 a.m. I've wandered the streets in the area late at night without incident for more than 25 years. 
If you use public transit, there are many bus lines that go past it. The Civic Center Metro stop is a third of a mile away, and Union Station is just over half a mile away.
It's not Beverly Hills, but it's not Blade Runner territory either.

title: “Enjoyed Howard Johnson-Fenway, great proximity to the ballpark, and downtown.”
text: Enjoyed our recent trip to Boston and our stay at the Howard Johnson-Fenway. It was great to be close to all the wonderful place to visit at within walking distance to Fenway Park. We will stay there again.

title: “What a bargin”
text: Hotel was older and not glamorous but was clean and an excellent bargain. Couldn't ask for a better place to stay for the price with such a great location.

title: “Good Staff and Good Location, A few room issues”
text:
The free breakfast is still one of their best selling features. Breakfast at a reasonable price in Washington can be hard to come by, and Embassy Suites helps you get started with hot food and hot coffee. 
One of the big advantages of this hotel is that you can walk down to the Metro (the "Friendship Heights" stop on the Red line) without having to go outside. 
The other advantage is the staff. Their staff is well-trained and friendly. There were some minor problems with the room, but the staff fixed it quickly and professionally. 
The only problems were with the room itself. The toilet made "filling" noises at random throughout the night, the two rooms within the suite were at vastly different temperatures, and one of the other guests passed out right outside my door. I am not sure any of this is the fault of the motel staff, but it is enough to keep them from getting five out of five.
My son loved the elevators and rode them endlessly. They made a good move by putting end tables beneath all the elevator buttons. It keeps 3-year-olds away from the buttons.

title: “Nice hotel with good parking garage”
text: Great hotel. Staff was very friendly and provided fast/excellent service when additional towels and sheets were needed. Shuttle to airport every 15-20 minutes. There is a coffee/breakfast cafe in lounge are and a bar.

title: “stay away. stay far far far away”
text:
Why you should stay away..... 
bugs on the walls & ceilings in the rooms. 
what appeared to be menstrual stains on the beds.... either that or trace evidence left over from some horrific crime scene
housekeeping (if they actually exist, but I dont think they do) forgot to put sheets on one of the beds and when we called the front desk to try to remedy this, they didn't speak english

title: “A wonderful choice, especially if you can snag a good deal on the price”
text: My first choice for a place to stay in NYC is the Affinia Manhattan. Sometimes you can get a really deals through Hotels.com or directly through the Affinia booking site (which has a best deal guarantee). For the same price or less than a regular room at many other 4-star hotels, you can get a studio suite or a one bedroom suite. The hotel is perfectly located if you are coming in and out from Penn Station (it's across the street) easy to get to other parts of NYC by subway. It's not so long a walk to the theater district, about a half mile. The hotel staff is competent and housekeeping was pretty swift with requests for extra towels. The only reason I don't stay here every time I go to NYC is that sometimes the good deals are not available, and it can be pricey during a heavy demand time of year. (Or sold out when the price is most attractive). There is a charge to use the internet, though. If I could change one thing about the hotel, it would be to offer free wifi.

title: “You'll love Washington Square Hotel”
text:
Washington Square Hotel is a fantastic hotel. Great location in Greenwich Village - very close to George Washington Square, Little Italy, Soho and the 9/11 Memorial. We used the hop on/hop off bus and the bus stop was near to the hotel so we could get on and go virtually anywhere in Manhattan.
The room was lovely - We requested a 'high' floor and got a 7th floor room with side view of the park. Not large but very clean and adequate. 
The staff were fantastic and the bonus of a continental breakfast every morning was great.
There is also a bar/restaurant in the basement which is great.
Our stay was fantastic and I would definitely return to this hotel.

title: “A nice getaway”
text:
We stayed here for one night as a getaway for my wife's birthday. It's very close to Dupont Circle, and Komi Restaurant, where we went for dinner.
The rooms are very nice, and it was good and quiet, which was important to us. The bathrooms are small and could use some upgrading, but didn't put too much of a damper on our stay.
The staff was very friendly and helpful, and the bar is a great place to have a drink before dinner.

title: “The Nicest Staff”
text:
Fro the moment we walked into the lobby till the moment we checked out the entire staff could not do enough for us. No matter what we wanted or asked for, they were incredibly sweet, kind, helpful & delightful.
Great location in SoHo. Right around the corner from Jacques Torres chocolate shop. The Vandamn diner 5 minute walk away. I had an incredible Monte Cristo sandwich made on french toast with maple syrup on the side to dip. 
Everything was so close, Little Italy, Greenwich Village, Chelsea. Great local, great people, close to subway, extremely reasonable rates.

title: “Great employees”
text: I checked in after attending a funeral for a Seal Beach victim. The gentlemen who checked me in knew I was upset. He was kind and helpe put a smil on my face. Wish I remembered his name. Liked the location and the food at the Barefoot resturant was excellent. We had a suite bunglaw was very nice.

title: “Horrific Night”
text: Out of thousands of hotel room nights in my lifetime, this was one of the two three worse. Not just because because the room was very small, or faced onto a junky interior wellway-- for low rates in Midtown, what should expect? BUT-- First problem - very dingy lighting (expect in the bathroom) -- one weak ceiling light, one anemic light on bedstand, and none on the desk. Second a VERY HARD BED, so that I was tossing & turning most of the night-- result true soreness! (And I normally like rather hard beds-- this one was hard over the top). Third, an air conditioning unit that made such a racket, especially when cycling on, that I was awakened each time it started up. I left exhausted.

title: “Nice place to stay!”
text: My wife and I needed to get to the city to recharge our batteries. I was born and raised there but now live in Central California. The area is not like I remember it. It still has it's share of problems but for the most part the changes that the city has made are fantastic. The Hotel is charming, with a very comfortable "lived in feel". The lobby is grand yet not too over the top. Just right for San Francisco. We were close to everything, either by BART, bus or even on foot. The best food and shopping in the area is about 5 blocks away at the San Francisco center. The service was great, but the beds were a little too firm. We will be back, but next time we will upgrade to one of the Suites.

title: “Fantastic Place”
text:
This was one of the best hotel experiences I've ever had. I was there on business for three days and from the moment I stepped out of my car until the moment I regretfully had to leave, every staff member was friendly, professional and helpful. I was using Marriott Rewards for the first time and had my room upgraded to a bay view in the South Tower. The beds and the pillows were amazing--the most comfortable I've ever had! (Too bad I didn't take an empty suitcase!). The bed was like sleeping on a dozen quilts and there were about 7 stay fluffy pillows. I'm sorry I didn't bring a bathing suit because the sparkling pool looked so inviting, very large with waterfalls and a hydrospa. 
It was a bit pricey in the restaurants, but there were many to chose from. Plus being in the downtown area you can walk to the Seaport Village and Gaslamp quarter in only a few minutes.
A lot of hotels are nice and accommodating, but like I said in the beginning, it was the staff that really made a difference. Always smiling, anticipating your every need, just plain out friendly. Quite a change from other "fancy" hotels I've stayed at. Room rate was $131 a night for one king size bed or two queen beds.

title: “Fantastic stay”
text: The River Inn is a fantastic hotel. Found it through a search engine and it offered great value for money. When we got there the room was more than we could have hoped for, spacious, comfortable, clean, superb shower, space for my wife to get ready in the eveing. For the value for money and nice design of the hotel this is the best I have stayed at in a long time. The staff are friendly and this is in a great area of Washington. Can't wait to go back!!

title: “Greate Place to stay to see new york”
text: Stayed with my family over Christmas. Chose the hotel based on good reviews on this site and was not disappointed. The hotel is just a few feet away from Times Square. You cannot beat the access. The hotel rooms were small but well done. Staff were very friendly. Perfect place for a NY visit. You are paying for the location.

title: “great facilities...poor service”
text: The location couldn't have been better. The rooms were spacious. This hotel was supposed to be one of the top 50 hotels in the world according to a well-known national review. Although the staff was friendly, for a luxury hotel, there just weren't enough of them. For example, we had to get our own drinks from the bar while sitting on the patio or wait 45 minutes for the one lone waitress to get around to our table. We had to finally call at 3 pm to get our room cleaned. An errand from the desk took 30 minutes. There were no robes, no turn down service, no "extras" to make us feel like we were staying any place special. Plus, the traffic noise was almost intolerable. Apparently, a bus station is close by and the noise from the buses created a rumbling all night long. It's way too expensive. We felt like we had gotten better service at a La Quinta and for a fraction of the cost.

title: “Nice hotel in a good area for shopping and dining”
text:
This was my 2nd stay at the Austin Renaissance, Arboretum. The staff are friendly, the rooms clean and comfortable, the fitness center is well equipped and maintained, and the hotel is in a nice location.
In the Arboretum area, the Renaissance is comfortable walking distance to Z'Tejas and Eddie V's and the Arboretum shops, and only a few minutes drive from the Domain shopping area which boasts a number of nice restaurants and plenty of additional shopping. In addition, it's only a few minutes drive from some of Austin's finest barbecue at Rudy's.
The hotel is an open style with all rooms opening onto the walkway which is open to the atrium. It can be a little loud during the day as it has some meeting/convention rooms and sees a good bit of traffic through the Atrium, but I haven't had any issues with excess noise at night.
Overall this is a very nice property and I will definetly stay here in the future when convenient to my needs.

title: “It's Nice to be Welcomed Back!”
text:
It was a pleasure to check in and be told, "Welcome Back!" I arrived at 8 a.m., had my luggage stored and checked in at the Starwood Member desk. I hadn't expected my room to be ready...and it wasn't, but I was given a "key" to the Atrium Club Room, so I could have a free continental breakfast. I appreciated the touch. 
My room was on the 12th floor in the Atrium Tower, looking down on 8th and 42nd. The room is huge and is very nicely decorated. The bathroom is modern and well appointment with robes and Occitane bath products. I feel like royalty! Best of all there's an enormous HD flatscreen TV and an Apple Mac with free Wi-Fi in the room.
The main entrance is at 43rd and 8th, a long block from the heart of Times Square. There are two multiplex movie theaters on 42nd, one which can be accessed by walking through the hotel lobby. Although the Westin Times Square has a restaurant and wine bar, visitors may enjoy wandering. There is every type of restaurant you can imagine in a three block radius from this hotel. I highly recommend the Shake Shack on 8th between 43rd and 44th, about half a block from the front of the Westin. They serve simple and delicious burgers and fries and the most delicious, thickest shakes anywhere. It's fun to get "take out" and bring it back to the room. Keeps your budget in line.
I'm a fan of Westin hotels, but they are pricey. However, if you're a good shopper you will eventually get a better deal on the room of your choice. You must join Starwood to accumulate "points." They really do add up to free stays, which is quite a nice loyalty reward.

title: “Clean & Affordable in Georgetown”
text: I stayed here for one night on business. I was pleasantly surprised at the great location and charm of The Latham. Room was very clean. Small but for one night it was fine. Would have given it 5 stars if not for the stiff bed and flat pillows. But i still had a good night sleep.

title: “Great Stay, but the Neighbors had a Better Stay”
text:
I travel to Indy on a semi-regular basis, so I have stayed at many of the downtown hotels. The Hilton ranks near the top. My room was really more of a suite; it had both a bedroom and living room, separated by french doors. Everything in the room was comfortable, from the sofa to the chairs to the beds. When you consider the fact that I only paid $60 for the room (look for a 3 1/2 star downtown hotel on hotwire), I really could not have asked for any more.
However, the room is not the only thing to like about the Hilton. There are two restaurants attached to the hotel. In addition, the hotel is centrally located, and within walking distance of nearly any downtown attraction. The staff was friendly and efficient; check-in and check-out took no more than two minutes. Parking is a bit spicy ($22 per night), but I suppose that is to be expected in a downtown hotel.
The only issue I had was that the neighbors seemed to REALLY enjoy their room. Their amorous outbursts could be heard throughout the halls and into my room until the wee hours of the morning. Headboard knocking, skin slapping, the whole nine yards. I don't know if any amount of sound insulation could have muffled their good time, but I was wishing for something at about 2:30 a.m.

title: “Good location, thats about it”
text:
This hotel has a good location, that is the main appeal of it. 
We didn't spend much time in the hotel, theres much to do in New York. 
I thought it was pricey for what we paid, but the location of the hotel made up the out dated decoration and small room.

title: “Good Location, Comfortable.”
text:
Stayed for a two night NYC getaway. Location was an easy 7 block walk from Penn Station down 7th Ave. to 24th street. Our 10th floor room with King bed was a little small, but the bed was very comfortable and it was very quiet. 
Breakfast in the morning included muffins, make your own waffles, pre-made omelets, sausage patties, fruit, juice, and coffee. Coffee was also available in the lobby and warm cider was out when we arrived. Desk staff were friendly and helpful. Guests included families, couples, singles. Neighborhood had a Whole Foods grocery, coffee shops, and restaurants.
Overall for the price we paid, it was a very good option.

title: “Great value in NYC financial district!”
text:
We arrived, were seated, and provided a lovely glass of wine while they came to us to check us in. The morning lattes were another nice touch! Its a great location if you are doing business on Wall Street, Beaver Street or lower Broadway.
The beds are extremely comfortable, crisp white linens and soft towels in the bathroom. If I could change anything, I would have better lighting in the bathroom or a well lit makeup mirror!
Thank you Andaz Wall Street for a truly pleasurable stay!

title: “Pleasantly surprised...”
text: First time to stay here and we were pleasantly surprised upon arrival. Well manicured property - very pretty - lots of trees. Nice lobby area and laundry facility. Average breakfast but would run out of things if you didn't go fairly early in the morning and they also started putting breakfast up before the time they advise breakfast ends on all four days we were there. The early evening reception at the cabana was nice - the kids loved the nachos and pop! Nice big pool although the water had a salty taste to it. We saw a man cleaning it every morning but not sure about the saltiness. Several people in the pool commented on that as well. BBQ pits were neat to have and lots of people used them and there were plenty of them. The playground was a nice 'extra' that you don't get at other places. The separate living room area with the extra TV was really nice - the kids watched one and the parents watched the other. The spa area was really nice and landscaped - nice tropical feel. We saw security walking the property frequently so that gave us a 'safe' feeling. Got a great rate through Orbitz. Would definitely stay there again.

title: “PERFECT for family”
text:
Took the family (wife and 5-year-old) to D.C. for a three-day trip. Couldn't have asked for more.
Checked in at 2:00 PM after 12-hour flight. Ordered food from a service advertised that stops at any of several different restaurants, and settled into our comfy room. Put leftovers in full-size refrig, and munched on them as we dozed in and out of sleep (jetlag). Staff was attentive, and amenities exceptional. Breakfast was very good all three days, and the only weeknight we were there (dinner only served on weeknights) found stuffed bellpeppers, green beans and a salad bar. 
 If I could change one thing, it would be the doors that separate the living room from the bedroom - they don't have regular handles. They snap shut like cabinet doors and thus, are very noisy. If we went out to the front room at night to get food/beverage, the noise would wake up our son sleeping on the sofabed. 
Housekeeping staff was OUTSTANDING. Not only efficient, but friendly as well. 
I would definitely return.

title: “Central location, but sketchy neighbourhood”
text:
I stayed at the Hotel Whitcomb for 5 days in July. The hotel boasts as historic, and the lobby was - it was gorgeous, but the only thing that's historic about the rest of the hotel is in the structure, high ceilings, elevators... the rest is just old. the origional features have been done over and now look disappointing. There aren't many ammenities, but it did the job. 
Cons: I was very close to the elevators and ice machine and could hear everything.. very loudly. not just a little noise - a lot of noise. Wifi in the room - forget about it. You're better off going down to starbucks or using your phone. It is so slow that most pages time out before they can finish loading. Completely unusable. The room had a musty smell, but I found if I had the a/c fan on it cleared up a bit.
Pros: The bed and pillows were comfy, which really if you're going to be doing a lot of sightseeing that's all you need in a room. I did a complete bed bug check and didn't find a single one. They have covers around the mattress too so that probably helps.
For the neighbourhood.. well if you're from a big city you will probably be alright. This is in one of the worst areas of the city, you can't go more than 20 feet without passing homeless people. The streets almost perpetually smell like booze and urine. There is nothing right there, but you can walk 5 minutes in any way and find something. Easy transit too - bus, subway, BART are all right there and the touristy buses pick up about 5 minutes walking. There are 2 diners (the one across the street and to the left has a good breakfast. cheap too), 3 fast food (subway, hot dog place, burger king) and the hotel has a restaurant and starbucks. there's a few convience and liquor stores close too, so everything you need is there.
I was travelling alone and never felt unsafe during the day (I'm a woman), but I wouldn't have gone out at night on my own. 
I chose this hotel because I booked my trip so late it was the least expensive in centre of San Fran that was still available. It's not that I wouldn't stay again, but I would look elsewhere first - and definitly get a room as far from the elevators and ice machine as possible!

title: “A savory "iconic" experience.”
text: My husband and I stayed at Hotel Icon in downtown Houston last weekend and really enjoyed it. The hotel has a 20s-30s luxury to it, which I found quite charming. We ordinarily prefer more contemporary hotels, but this was a refreshing escape. It felt like we were guests at the Hearst mansion. The service was attentive, room details and amenities were well appointed, and the king bed was very comfortable. I did call to confirm everything since I had purchased the room through a travel site and was glad I did. The standard was a double, which my husband and I had not slept on in 20+ years. Even with the upgrades though, king, then superior, the cost was still below the published standard. If you're in Houston, try this one on, you'll be glad you did.

title: “our trip to San Antonio”
text: Everything about the hotel was FIRST class. They upgraded our room to a river view. The breakfasts were tasty and service was great. Last but not least David Swift in conciege was fantastic. He made all our dinner reservation recommending fine restaurants. He went above and beyond with little things that madeour trip memorable.

title: “Clean and Pleasant”
text: If you want to stay in a luxurious hotel, this is not it. HOWEVER, if you are looking for a clean and friendly place to stay with access to the city and shopping, then you have found your match! I think the radisson employs the friendliest and kindest bunch! George, the check in person called up to the room after we settled in to make sure it was to our liking. There was plenty of room and it was clean, what more can you ask for. The room service was good, i recommend the chocolate mousse. You are near tons of great shopping and some great places to eat. Had a lovely dinner just around the corner on Walnut (b/w 17th and 18th) called Pietro's. That is if you have an inkling for some italian. If your on a budget, and location and cleanliness is important, the Radisson should be high on your list!

title: “Great Stay!!!!”
text:
Nice hotel, friendly and helpful staff, VERY CLEAN ROOMS!!!! Mission accomplished!
Location was good. Will definitely go back if we are in Denver in the future.
Thank you!!

title: “Outstanding”
text:
Room Rate was great, room was fantastic view of bay to the west, saw a spectacular sunset over the mountains& bay. Both rooms had a TV, Bathroom real small but functional.Great location short walk to Pike Place Market and all the stores.
Was told not to eat at hotel. Many places close for coffee and meals.
Would recommend to solo traveler, small for a couple for more than 2 days.

title: “Long life”
text:
Dear Team of Airtel Van Nuys, 
the first Night I slept in the Great USA was in your Room # 222 , 
so I will talk about your Wonderful hospitality whole life ,, I have never seen such a team with 24 h smiling faces :-) 
thank you for Team of the Magnificence Hotel . A Special thanks and gratitude to Cristina C for her Outstanding performance at The Breakfast Time and her Team .
Thank you very much lovely Team of Airtel Van Nuys 
Good Bless you & Bless America

Vielen Herzlichen Dank

title: “Not thtat good”
text: Clift Hotel very stark with little warmth or ambiance. Rooms are small. Staff friendly and helpfull. Would not go back

title: “The Milburn did nicely!”
text: Myself and two daughters, aged 17 and 20, were at the Milburn November 9 to 14 and enjoyed our stay. Did not see any roaches, and while a touch shabby, our one bedroom suite was comfortable. Lots of clean towels and the bathroom was a decent size, lots of mirror space. Little things could be improved, such as replacing mattresses on the twin beds (the girls said they sagged a bit); better heat regulation (too hot for us most of the time); and a more consistent water temperature (all of us found the water suddenly went cold or suddenly went too hot. For us, the location was ideal and we stopped at Fairway Grocery nearly every day to stock up on snacks and ready to heat meals. Fairway is two blocks away on Broadway with a tremendous selection including organic and health food floor. The famed Zabars is just another few blocks north on Broadway -- yummy blintz! Great shopping closeby, and we highly recommend the lemon tart at the Columbus Bakery, Columbus and 82nd. 30 minute walk across Central Park to the Metropolitan Museum of Art or the Guggenheim. A great place to stay if you want quiet while you save money for other things that matter more than luxury accommodation.

title: “Great place to stay,and great location!”
text: Comfortable beds,clean rooms,and friendly front desk.Also close to a Wendy's! So,infact you could just walk over to Wendy's and grab lunch,dinner,or just a drink! They also had complimentary printing.So,friendly,clean,comfortable,and in a great location.

title: “Save money”
text: Hotel was fine thought we would try a step up from Hampton but found no advantage for the extra $. Stay at the Hampton instead and buy yourself a nice dinner.

title: “Love The Ritz!!!!”
text: We stayed at the Ritz over Labor Day Weekend as we moved our baby into the George Washington University. The service and comfort provided by the Ritz was a perfect. I shipped NINE boxes, suitcases, etc. to the Ritz via FEDEX to coincide w/ our arrival and not only did they receive the packages, but they held them for us in a secure location until we were ready to take them to the dorm. Our package included breakfast and valet parking and we were also surprised to receive two VIP tickets to the Spy Museum. Breakfast was excellent, with fresh squeezed orange juice and made to order eggs, toast, potatoes and breakfast meats. The wait staff couldn't have been more gracious or accommodating. The room was extremely comfortable. We had a big bathroom, wireless internet, and twice daily maid service. The fresh flowers in the lobby and everywhere else were gorgeous. It's location is very convenient to the school. All of the staff were extremely attentive, from the front desk to the valets. It's a very well run property-I can't wait to return for Parent's Weekend in October.

title: “Willing to do whatever it takes”
text:
I stayed at the "St. Gregory Luxury Hotel & Suites" on L St NW last month while in DC for a business meeting. Oh yes, the staff was helpful and friendly. The room was large, quiet and comfortable. Food from room service was excellent. I would expect all of that from a "luxury" hotel - but wait, there's more.
I had driven up to Middleburg with a horse. I dropped the horse and trailer off, but still had to find something to do with a 3/4 ton diesel truck in the middle of DC. With a little advance warning, the staff at the St. Gregory made it happen. I don't know where they put it, but they made it disappear and produced it again the next day, unharmed. Kudos to the manager, Steve, and his staff!

title: “Very nice Sleep Inn!”
text: I stay in many Choice Hotels during the year. This is one of the nicest and the best Sleep Inn I've been Inn. The larger shower is nice. Spacious suite. Friendly and helpful staff. Clean and new. A nice night.

title: “Terrible hotel...”
text:
I stayed at this hotel for 6 nights at the end of December 2006 and had one of the worst hotel experiences in my life!
Would not recommend this hotel for anything but its location (which is convenient).
I had a single tiny room, with old furniture (partly) falling apart. It had a horrible cigarette smell which would not go away.
Most importantly, the first day I was there, didn't have any hot water in my room! Also, the heating wasn't working and believe me, the outside temperature was really low... Despite mentionning this problem several times to the hotel manager, it was not fixed before the 4th day of my stay, which made it totally unpleasant and uncomfortable.
Also, one day, my room was not tidied up. And another day, the elevator did not work (I stayed on the 4th floor).
Everytime I (rightfully) complained about problems to the manager, he looked really annoyed... So my advice: don't go there, it's certainly not worse the price you will pay. And don't believe the positive reviews you may find here, which I believe are all complete lie... This hotel is not even worse a 1 star hotel...

title: “Ok Stay, Depending Upon Your Room”
text:
We were happy to get this hotel off of Priceline for $360 + tax for the first weekend of December, as this is a very busy holiday season. 
Sure, the entrance to the hotel isn't grand, but it serves its purpose. Our first room we received had a nice view. I noticed immediately that the floor was wet by the heater and the heater was very noisy. It was extremely outdated too. I informed the staff and it was "fixed". This really meant that a towel was placed on the floor. After requesting a new room, we were placed in a freezing room with the smallest bathroom that I've ever seen. Immediately requesting a new room, we were placed next door. The bathroom was slightly bigger and the heater was working. 
We ate breakfast several times at their restaurant. We choose the buffet option for the kids; it was a good deal at $10 too.
Staff tried to be helpful, but sent me in the wrong direction to locate the subway. Sigh...
Overall, I was hoping was more than the Warwick could provide. For the price, I wanted more. I've stayed in less expensive hotels, at this time, and received nicer rooms and service. If you get an awesome deal, it might be worth staying here. Maybe...
Not sure, but it seems that we often get the less desirable rooms after making a reservation with Priceline for the hotels. Just an observation.

title: “Noisy nights at the Hampton”
text: Located near the entrance to the tunnel, and staying in a room facing the street, I listened to all manner of city noises the entire night. The rooms are small - surprise! - but the Hilton beds are very comfortable. Front desk staff was great. The small bar is run by a young transplanted Californian but with a bad attitude. This is a hotel I have stayed before because my company searches the best rates in the area. Just ask for a room away from the street.

title: “Seriously – we loved our stay here.”
text:
We stayed at Topaz this weekend and what a great experience! The location is great. A quick and lovely walk to all the major tourist sites. The hotel is on a very quiet block that is only a one block walk to great restaurants and at night lively bars and nightclubs. The best of both worlds. 
The staff is so friendly and welcoming. Even housekeeping stopped us to say hello and let us know if we needed anything just call! While we didn’t have a pet, the was a wide friendly assortment of pups in the hotel. 
This is not a typical Kimpton. Its definitely more basic but still has that funky vibe. We just could not have gotten a better deal for the price anywhere. For a 3.5 star, you get an amazing experience and 5 star service. 
As a Kimpton frequent guest, we got a $10 credit to raid the mini bar and the NY Times on Sunday! Plus the wine reception and continental breakfast! Seriously – we loved our stay here.

title: “Great hotel, location remote”
text: Stayed here for a convention. The hotel was very nice with good employees, but if I was on a non-business trip, I wouldn't stay here because of the distance from the city. There are quite a few nice restaurants nearby and you can walk easily to the Silver T line (which will take you to the airport for $2).

title: “Great new hotel”
text: The simple decor and little treats in the room were nice additions. The room was a little smaller than i am use to but the excellent bathroom and deep soak tub made up for that. I always enjoy having a nespresso machine in the room. Unfortunately the capsules were not restocked on a daily basis. Housekeeping was clearly an issue as I had to call on a daily basis to have my room serviced.

title: “Pleasant Stay”
text: Stayed here for 4 nights, good location in the heart of times square. We were originally allocated a room on the 32nd floor. On inspection was it not only too high, but the room we felt was in desperate need of a refurb, the wardrobe door was shattered and broken. We asked to be moved to a lower floor and luckily we were placed on the 9th floor - room 908, the room was so much better, modern, clean and comfortable it was like being a different hotel we were relieved that we asked to move and to be fair the receptionist arranged this very quickly for us and in a friendly manner. The bar was really nice, service excellent, we had a snack in the restaurant which was very nice. I would stay again but only in one of the refurb rooms.

title: “Great Location”
text: My wife and I spent 3 nights the first week of October. Hotel was a great "base of operations"...close to Central Park, Times Square, Theater District, St. Patrick's, and 5th Avenue. Service was above average. Room was large, no problem with street noise. We would probably stay there again without second thoughts.

title: “All Around Quality”
text:
Excellent experience over all. Spotless, comfortable rooms. Great location. Terrific service.
I particularly enjoyed the fitness center. I am something of a connoisseur of hotel fitness centers, and this was one of the best around (slightly larger and more modern than Boston Harbor Hotel).

title: “I love Aloft hotels”
text:
Since I stayed at the Aloft Denver Airport whenever I can try to sleep in this hotel chain ... The rooms are the same in all hotels and I love ... spacious, modern, amazing shower, toiletries formidable, the excellent treatment.
I stayed one night to be near the airport and I had to take a flight to MEX.
The recommended hotel bar and fast food they have. Certainly, provided you have the opportunity, stay at Aloft Hotel

title: “christmas”
text: It was a very good stay. All the acomodation were in perfect shape and no had no issues with the service

title: “Live Like a Tycoon Amidst Stunning Pacific Heights Mansions!”
text: Love Period Buildings, Pacific Heights Mansions, and top of the world views? Want to have excellent, comfortable, friendly service that will make you feel as well cared for as Lord & Lady Grantham of Downton Abbey? Then Hotel Drisco is an excellent choice! Both the building and the staff are wonderful and give you that stepping-back-in-time-to-a-better-time feeling. From the moment you arrive you will be impressed with how friendly, pleasant, and helpful the whole staff is (true career professionals- no disgruntled staff here!) The neighborhood is wonderful - it's worth staying here just so you can step out for a stroll around the very peaceful neighborhood and take in views from all directions, all the while admiring the many beautiful mansions and how fabulous it would be to live in any one of them! The room is perfect: solid and comfortable, and very appealing in the traditional white trim wood kind of way, but with all the modern conveniences you'll want, like large flat screen TV. The bed and bedding are really wonderful too. Love staying in an ultra-modern space with lots of metallic decor and floor to ceiling glass windows? Then go somewhere else, because at the Drisco you get the real, traditional, white wood framed, "hoist it open by hand" windows, which all add to the back in time feeling I love so much. (If you are the type of person that likes modern Vegas hotels and demand everything to be sleek and slick, then you aren't going to understand the true beauty of the Drisco, and fellow Drisco lovers certainly won't understand you either :) The icing on the cake is the complimentary wine reception at 5pm (the Merlot served was a really great choice to compliment the gourmet assortment of cheeses and hors duerves which were so tasty, it was almost a dinner, and some of the best food I had all trip), as well as the wonderful breakfast downstairs, again with really nice fruit, breads, cream cheese, and to-die-for Salmon Lox, etc, in such a pleasant little room with many tables, and more great staff, all which add perfectly to the Pacific Heights feeling of your stay. One other thing I really appreciate, is that, although it’s not the cheapest place to stay, once you’ve paid for the room, you’ll find that they’ve included so many other wonderful things which are either free (such as the Wine Reception, and Breakfast) or very reasonable, such as the $10 panini’s and sandwiches which can be delivered to your room (in contrast to so many other hotels which seem to gouge you at every turn once they’ve got you captive ) Can you tell I give the Drisco a major thumbs up? :) To be fair, the only things to watch out for are: Know what you are looking for - if you want location near all the cheap touristy attractions, or if you insist on a new & modern kind of thing, then this is not the place for you. This place is for people who want to experience a prestigious bit of old SF, in a prestigious old SF neighborhood. Also, since it is an older building, I suppose you may hear a bit of room to room noise occasionally (although we did not) however the Drisco even provides each room a really nice sound & clock radio which allows you to drift off to ocean waves or many other nice sounds - just another example of how well they will take care of your every need to give you the perfect Pacific Heights experience at the Hotel Drisco!

title: “Disappointed the second time around”
text: I visited two years ago with my daughter and was pleased with the accomodations...they were cramped but neat/clean/ and safe. This time with my spouse the initial room reaked of cleaner and the window faced a wall. Another room was offered but that was also claustrophobic with a window opening up to another building. When I asked for a room with a view or some air I was on the corner of Lombard and Octavia. It was very noisy but the room was pleasant with two bay windows. Room was clean and breakfast consists of bagels, muffins, coffee, juice and hard boiled egss. Parking was awful and we did get a ticket for not removing our vehicle off the street after exceeding the 11AM limit by ten minutes. I still love SF, but maybe I'll stay elsewhere next time. Parking is ten dollars at an adjacent hotel, take it as parking is horrible.

title: “Pleasantly Surprised”
text: We booked this hotel with mixed expectations knowing that the location was going to be good but that it might be a bit tired and old fashioned and possibly even a bit grubby. Well, how surprised were we! You've got to stay in this place - the 1920/30s decor is unbelievable and the lobby is just superb. We were with our two teenage girls and booked a room with two double beds and I must say that the room was a fairly decent size with good quality fittings, lots of crisp clean bedding and pillows and really comfortable beds. The bathroom was small but adequate and although the basin was a bit scratched and discoloured, it was spotlessly clean, Not once in our four night stay were we disturbed by people coming and going in the corridors (they are amazingly wide for a hotel and thickly carpeted which probably helped) and in the mornings there was always an army of very polite and friendly cleaning staff attending to to the rooms. My husband said it was the best night's sleep he'd had in a hotel for years. We were on the 12th floor and the street noise was apparent but really not a problem, The down sizw for us was that there was no tea and coffee facilities in the room and if I had to be picky, I would say that the staff on the desk were a bit unfriendly and could have made more of an effort. The doorman, however, was a great guy - really helpful with restaurant directions (there is a great diner down the street for breakfast called The Comfort Diner and lots of other near by restaurants for an evening meal) and he organised a hotel car for us rather than a taxi to take us back to La Guardia airport which worked out much cheaper. I spent a lot of time looking for a reasonably priced and well positioned NY hotel and would definitely recommend this one and will stay there again if ever we are in NY - don't be put off by the negative reviews.

title: “Fabulous Location!”
text:
The location of this hotel is amazing, you are less than a five minute walk away from pier 39 and it is situated right in the middle of Fisherman's Wharf.
I'd booked a room with two queen beds as there were four of us. The rooms are nicely decorated and very clean. The only downside is the lack of space, I think the room we had was too small for 4 adults with 4 suitcases as there wasn't really any spare space. The wardrobe is right by the sink and was too small to accommodate all our clothes so we had to leave them in our suitcase, but this wasn't a massive problem as the hotel supplies you with a iron and ironing board.
Housekeeping were also very quick to respond to our requests for more towels, as they had only left us with two. I know people have mentioned about the rooms being noisy - our room was on the 1st floor near the swimming pool and it was nice and quiet.
The firepits outside the hotel are a lovely touch if you want to sit outside as it can get a bit chilly in the evening, so make sure you take a jumper!

title: “A real find”
text:
After reading all the positive reviews of this property, and knowing we would be centrally located with extraordinary space for the price, we were primed for disappointment - which did NOT happen! If you are looking for spacious rooms, great location, and excellent service - and, who isn't - this hotel is for you. 
Our 'junior suite' was easily twice the size of an ordinary hotel room, especially in expensive NYC, yet at half the cost you would expect. Our two daugters shared an ordinary hotel room here as well, with a tariff only somewhat below expected for the size and location, but were also very happy.
The managers put us into a street-side room at first, which has the advantage of the view but the disadvantage of noise. I called downstairs at near midnight (when a bus pulled up and sounded his air horn!) to ask for an inside room change. They responded immediately, found a room on the same floor (but even larger!), and offered to help us move! 
The elevators, often an Achilles heel of hotels, especially smaller ones, worked remarkably well - fast and efficient. The exercise room appears to be new, with 2 new Life Cycles (both with heart rate monitors) - one upright, one recumbant - both with toe straps, a real rarity. You will be hard-pressed to find this anywhere else in the City. 
The breakfast facility is very nicely furnished, but serves only a continental for $15. When we wanted full breakfasts, the hotel staff itself directed us to the 'luncheonette', 50 meters up the block, which was about $10. But, the kichenettes, equipped with service for 4, make it easily possible for you to provide your own, for a lot less. And, despite the very friendly and helpful staff, there was none of the usual discomfort found in larger hotels, I mean the shilling for tips. At no point did we feel under this distasteful pressure.
Be aware that the internet will cost you about $10/day, but, at their room rates, you can hardly complain. You will not find here the luxurious, and often useless, amenities, such as terricloth bathrobes and slippers. And, if you are looking for a large lobby, or a grand atrium, look elsewhere (and expect to hear your wallet complain).
No property is perfect in every respect, of course. My two criticisms, though, are very minor: The hot water took a very long time to become hot from the sink faucet (something amiss with their recirculation system). And, the A/C was too noisy until I 'adjusted' the knobless fan speed with my faithful Leatherman toolkit, whereupon it was close to perfect. 
Overall, though, this is a definite winner, and one I will use whenever i find myself in this city.

title: “I would not stay here again.”
text: Both the hotel and the service were a disappointment. My room fan was stuck ON and the temperature never got below 85 degrees, leaving me wanting to open my window (which of course did not open) even in the coldest days of the year. When I asked for a cab the first day, I was told to walk down the street a few blocks and I could probably find one. When I asked if there were shuttles to the airport, I was told NO, although there were several available. I could go on with more examples of why I would not stay here again, but I am sure you have the idea already.

title: “Overpriced and in the middle of no where”
text: Made the mistake of booking a room here... Nightly drug deals outside the window as well as a sense of dread as you walk to wherever you need to go in Chicago. Across the street is a wonderful building that looks like it belongs on the Walking Dead, tv show. The rooms where as if I had traveled back in time to 1970... Although I fear they hadn't actually been updated since. Lastly and for heavens sake, do not eat at the adjoined restaurant... The staff are actually zombies and I was sick as one after eating there...

title: “we loved it”
text: we stayed at heartbreak hotel all the staff were helpful and friendly our room was clean the maids come in every day including weekends, we went to graceland on vip package it was really nice to see everything in graceland including gold discs boots its well worth going to graceland memphis zoo is also a nice day out and cheap to get in beale street is also good with all the live bands the gibson factory is good

title: “Ideal location, great price!”
text: I had read reviews on TripAdvisor before my holiday and we managed to find our way there ok. The location was ideal, 2 blocks from Cable Cars, five minutes by bus to Fishermans Wharf. The owners we really helpful when we arrived giving us a great map with lots of do's and don't bothers. Our room was big, clean and quiet, we could even see the top of the Golden Gate from our room. Perfect for the price!

title: “Excellent hotel, had a great experience there”
text: This was the last stop on a road trip from LA to SF and it was the joint best hotel I stayed along the way (the other being San Ysidro Ranch in Santa Barbara was incredible also). Stayed for 3 nights in the Astor Suite on a great package deal (3 nights for price of 2) and was very happy with my choice of this hotel over the other options (Four Seasons, Clift, Fairmont). The suite was wonderful, great views and totally relaxing. It was very big and felt like a private apartment more than a regular hotel suite. The staff at this hotel are what sets it apart though, they are so friendly and seem genuniely so, it's not forced like it is in a lot of places. The concierge was incredible (got us into 2 "fully booked" trendy restaurants) and also the Mojito's at the hotel bar were the best i've tasted. This was my first experience of a St Regis property and i'm impressed.

title: “What a great hotel!”
text: Paid for this with air miles, stayed two nights and was delighted....a real hotel, built in the 1920s, chandeliers, grandeur, great food, friendly and knowledgable stagff, right across from the public park which was great for the kids. Rooms were comfortable and clean, cant fault the place on anything. Felt like total luxury to stay here.

title: “Always love a Hyatt Place hotel”
text: Stsyed here one night before leaving for Seattle. Had an early flighdodo we chose the Hyatt Place closest to the airport. Was extremely easy getting to airport with very little traffic. The staff was friendly, rooms were large and very clean. Bathroom had shower only but it was spacious. Heard no airport traffic which had been an initial concern. Great stay.

title: “Happily Surprised”
text:
Got this on Priceline for $42. They had it listed as a 3* and it certainly is at least a 3.5*. Hilton staff seemed surprised when I mentioned to them that I had been told this was a 3*. This property appears to be an older renovated hotel. Parking at the Hilton is $20 per night which is steep considering EVERY property around there advertises for less. Best choice is the Clarion for $9.50 a night and is directly northwest of the Hilton.
I didn't spend much time exploring but the staff I encountered were extremely friendly and went out of their way to assist. The restaurant sold chops and steaks ($30-50) and had a dress code. I spoke to the locals and found a great, little restaurant at the old, run-down Jet hotel 10 minutes north called the Happy Teriyaki. Price was low for entrees and drinks. 
Considering that the Hilton is directly across from the light rail, a major throughfare and the airport - I hardly heard a thing with the window closed. Free wireless compliments of the Holiday Inn!
Located directly across from the hotel, the new light rail service to the city was enjoyable and cost efficient at $5 return. We took in two ball games, shopped/ate in the city. We checked out the fish market which was great.
The only possible downside to this hotel (and I am really stretching this) is perhaps feeling a little under-dressed, CRT TVs (no flat screens) and parking.
I was very happy to stay there and will return in greater numbers!

title: “One of My Favorite Hotels”
text:
I splurged a bit on this hotel (though got a AAA rate), but it was worth it due to its proximity to Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport, Arizona Mills Outlets, Desert Botanical Garden, as well as its 24-hour airport shuttle, comfortable bar and friendly wait staff. One of the stops along the Metro Light Rail is also right in front of the hotel, so if you don't have a car, it's quite convenient as a means of getting into town to visit the Phoenix Art Museum or Heard Museum, as well as various shops and restaurants.
Check in was quite fast and the staff friendly as I asked questions about the marathon that was to take place the next day. Really appreciated my spacious king bed room with its sleeper sofa, coffee table, work desk, free wi fi, wardrobe with TV, microwave, small fridge and spacious granite bathroom vanity. Most of all, the bed was incredibly comfortable with lots of pillows and soft comforter.
Upon check in, I had signed up for the Priority Club Rewards and from what I understand, this enabled me to get a better room. Another nice perk is that the room welcomed me with lights on, music playing on the clock radio and a nice snack bag of chips, apple, a fortune cookie and bottle of water. Not bad for just signing up!
Being alone, I also enjoyed topping off both nights at their friendly Cafe Sha bar; the Citrus Salad was delicious! Happened to meet a few people and had great conversation to boot.
Loved: the oh-so comfortable bed, convenience of location.
Not so much: $4 daily parking fee.

title: “Over All Very Good......But”
text: Just spent 6 nights at the Barclay. Like other reviews the location was very good. Nice walks to all the major stuff in New York and if you want to catch a subway train then the options are also very good. The room was a lot nicer than i had expected. We had the deluxe and that came with a king bed. Room great size for two people. The house keeping each day was very good and the room was clean when we arrived. The only concerns i had was just the slow service. We called down 4 times to get a travel adapter and 2 times for flatter pillow. We were always waiting at the bell desk to get help with our bags and also our room key card failed on us 3 times. (More waiting to get those fixed each time) Lastly, not one staff member in 6 days offered to open the door for us even when there were a few staff members standing there not doing anything. This is just something I expect if I was staying at an intercontinental property. Saying that I think I would return just because it was much cheaper than my other hotel options I had and also because of the location

title: “Great service”
text:
We were warmly welcomed and even offered complimentary glasses of champagne while we checked in. The room was nice and the bathroom was extremely spacious however, the sheets were kind of scratchy and not as soft as those found in a five star hotel.
When we left, we wanted to grab breakfast and the concierge promptly printed out a map to a great local breakfast restaurant that was fantastic.
I have to agree with the others; parking is an issue. When we arrived we parked in the nearest garage and were surprised to see there was a charge. However, when we left the gates were opened and we weren't charged. It seemed there was a wedding going on and that may be why we weren't charged for parking.

title: “Great Location”
text:
Located in a great part of the city near Union Square, new Westfield and major transport hubs. Service was ok, condition of the room was good and Westin always delivers a very comfortable bed. 
Positives: Short walk to Union Square (shops/restaurants) and key transport services (trolleys, trams and trains). I have not attached a photo to this review because the photo on the Westin website is actually correct.
Negatives: Not enough staff.
Cheaper than the Westin St Francis (best rate was direct thru Westin on Market) but further from Union Square. Good value for the rate.

title: “VIP Treatment without the VIP Prices”
text:
As a former customer service trainer, I'm always observing customer experiences. The Downtown Chicago Red Roof definitely earns an A+! 
Since I started my current job a year ago, I'm back and forth to Chicago often. We stay at the Downtown Red Roof for the value and the proximity to our office. The staff has always been extremely friendly and accommodating, and they always knew my boss by name, which was nice, but expected seeing that she stays there sometimes 3 weeks out if a month or more. The rooms are always clean, the beds always comfy.
It was my last visit which blew me away. I had not been to Chicago for probably 3 months. Even when I came regularly, unlike my boss, I was only there maybe once a month. When I checked in, I wasn't surprised that they greeted me as if they were really happy to see me. I wasn't even surprised that despite the hundreds and hundreds of people who are in and out of the busy hotel, they recognized my face. What shocked me was as I reached in my purse to get my ID, the clerk addressed me by name. She knew what kind of room I liked. She even knew to use my Redi Card and corporate code to get me the best rate...all without me saying a word. I felt like a celebrity.
In addition to the five-star customer service, the hotel provides the most affordable and covenient valet parking in downtown Chicago. They offer free bag checking for those who arrive before check-in or business travellers like me who need a place to stash their luggage after check-out while they conduct their business in the city. There are great restaurants just steps away, and the hotel is just a block from the Magnificent Mile.
When I'm at the Red Roof in Downtown Chicago, I feel like I'm in a home away from home.

title: “Really, I have to pay for internet access on EACH of my devices?”
text:
Location: Pro - near a redline Metro stop. Cons - too far from downtown so you'll need to use the metro or cab often. You cannot walk to the monuments from here.
Service: Pro: the maids are very nice and most everyone tries to be helpful. They are well trained staff. Cons (2): Internet is$12.95 + tax per day for the SLOWer internet and $16.95 per day for the fast internet and that is PER DEVICE. So they really want me to pay $155 plus tax for all my devices to be connected during my stay. This was not apparent when I purchased the access. I thought I was getting generally wireless access code. Also when I asked the front desk for tea instead of coffee for my room (and handed them the 4 packets of coffee from my room) they sent up tea packages that were for the coffee machines on a different floor meaning they were completely useless to me unless I wanted to strain tea leaves through my teeth.
Rooms: Pro - Good temperature control and very clean with nice TV and comfortable bed and possibly a good view. Cons - I can literally hear through the walls. This seems to be well known to the hotel because after 9pm or so they put up signs near the elevators on every floor that direct that all conversations (including in room) should be at a whisper level. Whisper level in MY room? Maybe the least sound proofing of any hotel I've ever been in or at least close to it. In addition the hallways could use an update. 
Fitness Center - Pros - excellent. Cons - None.
Nearby food: Pros: Lots nearby. Cons: it's all of the tourist quality. For good restaurants you'll need to take the metro or get a cab to downtown. (refer to my comment above on location)
Room Service Food: Hit and Miss. About 50/50 on whether I liked what I ordered. I suggest going downtown to eat. Con: 22% tip (service charge) plus a delivery charge ($4.00). That's cab far to go get a better meal downtown. My dinner for one without alcohol came to $79.05 because the high price of the meal, and tack on top of that the service and delivery charge.

title: “Good Upper West Side Location”
text: If your visit to NYC calls for any time to be spent on the upper West Side, consider the Excelsior Hotel on W. 81st Street just off Central Park West. It is a small hotel, tastefully decorated and features an attentive staff. Local transportation is nearby while the Museum of Natural History and Haydn Planetarium are just across the street. Local restaurants cater to any culinary whim while other shops transform a walk into a delightful experience.

title: “I found a very good hotel in Indy”
text: Just to say I stayed there on June 1st for 3 nights. The staff very freindly. Rooms large and clean. The towels are not the largest. The continental breakfast was good. Very good location if you need to be by the airport and a major highway to get around the city.

title: “Quiet Stay at the Seattle Westin”
text: The Westin Seattle is a unique hotel, with its two distinctive, circular towers that can be picked out in any downtown Seattle photo. The hotel is a bustle of activity with a nice mix of business and personal travelers. The hotel does a great job of customer service and getting people where they need to be. Even though I was a Priceline customer, I was offered a higher floor room when I requested one. The hotel common areas, while busy, were not loud or boisterous. I found the service at the lobby level lounge to be quick and efficient. My room was on the 26th floor of North Tower (which I recommend if you have a choice). It was extremely quiet and relaxing. The room was comfortable and nicely appointed. The bathroom was not large, but did not feel cramped. I enjoyed my one night stay at the Seattle Westin. A couple words of caution. The hotel is starting to show a little wear and tear; small things like scuff marks on the walls, dings on the wood trim around the doors, tears in the carpeting, etc. These may be small deals or big ones depending on your expectations. Also, the elevators are quite slow, especially if you are waiting for one or on one during peak usage. The Westin is located on the northern edge of downtown Seattle proper. A couple of the surrounding areas can get a little sketchy the later into the night it gets; mainly the area north of the hotel.

title: “Cozy and quiet”
text: Located on Lombard Street, near the Exploratorium and the Marina, this quaint and slightly old fashion motel features a garden courtyard and rooms individually decorated. Family owned for generations, this place seems immune to the busy street just yards away, provided you get an interior room. The room prices are reasonable and the staff is friendly and helpful. They also give you a two for one coupon at Judy's, a great place to have breakfast, just two blocks away.

title: “Fab hotel!!”
text: I loved the Boston Langham Hotel in every way - the decor, service, peace and quiet, and discreet luxury, all of it was just right. It was a joy to have everything run so smoothly e.g. the hairdryer's fuse had blown, and a call brought the engineer up to fix it in less than 2 minutes! The Broadband access in the room meant I could use my laptop to keep in touch with home and office - it is the perfect place for business. It is also ideal for shopping, with all the great shops within 5 mins walking distance. But it was not cheap, specially breakfast and room service!! However if someone else is paying, or you want to splash out and feel pampered, go spoil yourself..... you will without a doubt have wonderful memories :)

title: “More Motel than Hotel”
text: A co-worker and I stayed at the Magic Castle hotel on business last month. Not quite the "boutique hotel" I was expecting. Felt much more like a budget travel motel with the window unit air conditioners and iron burns on the carpet. Wireless internet did not work well at all. If you're trying to locate a cheap room near the Walk of Fame - ok. If you're needing a business class hotel because all others in the area are full - keep looking.

title: “Funky, clean, great location”
text: The rooms are small but this is normal in New York. This hotel was the best rate that we could find where the reviews were positive and the rooms clean (£189 per night). Prices and availability came down the week before. We were very impressed. The room is funky like somehting out of Ikea but very practical and uses the small space brilliantly with all the personal touches and plenty of storage room. The bed was really comfy and the air con worked well. Although the street was noisy in the daytime i had no trouble sleeping at night. The hotel also has a roof terrace which is great at night. The Pod is in a great location in Midtown, it is a great base for exploring New York., 2 blocks from the subway and one day we even walked to Fifth Avenue, Central Park and back no problem. There are plenty of cafes around to get breakfast from. There is a brilliant french restaurant attached to the hotel, quite pricey but worth it. Head right out of the hotel and there are also several restaurants and bars really close. Our room had its own toilet/shower which i preferred but some rooms have shared bathrooms which seemed clean enough (check before you book if you're bothered).

title: “Great Location - Room was only ok”
text: Spent travel time here during the last week in August. The location was great but the room was outdated, fortunately though it was clean. Still at $289 per night plus $40 to park your car it was a little steep, however, I don't think you will find anything less expensive in this location.

title: “Almost 5 stars”
text: We stayed here on a "Park and Fly" package. The rate was only $10 more than a regular room and included 7 nights parking which would've cost at least $40 at the airport. The room was very clean and spacious. My check-in experience is where they lost a star. It took the clerk a long time to find the reservation and then when I mentioned the "Park and Fly" he proceeded to tell me that it would be an additional $5/night for parking. When I mentioned the fact that the woman who took my reservation for the package had informed me that parking was part of the deal, he said "oh, well if they didn't charge you then it's probably ok". I also asked about the shuttle and he wrote down what time we needed to leave for the airport and said he would schedule it later. Needless to say I was a bit concerned at this point so I got up extra early the next morning and asked the morning clerk to please verify that we had a shuttle reservation. She said "No". I proceeded to tell her about the check-in confusion and she didn't seem too surprised so maybe this guy has problems. Anyway, she went out of her way to be helpful and could not have been more kind. We got the shuttle arranged, she told us about the return arrangements, and she was on duty when we did return and she set us up with coffee and granola bars for our late drive home (10pm). What could have been a nightmare experience was saved by the grace and charm of this helpful lady. If you do the "Park and Fly", you may want to confirm more than once. I am rating "Service" as average but really I had both a "1 star" and a "5 star" experience here.

title: “Perfect location”
text:
Location could not be better - the real bonus of this hotel. A few blocks to subway, walking distance of 5th Ave, Central park, Macys etc. 
Refurbished rooms very nice, although the view from ours was not great. 
Staff very attentive and polite though the lady who checked us out Saturday let the side down. She was snotty, rude and mannerless. All the other staff though made up for her, particularly the doormen and concierge who could not have been more accommodating.
All in all a great hotel. Will return.

title: “Great Location and Amazing Beds!!”
text: My husband and I spent 3 nights here while visiting Boston. The hotel is right downtown with a great central location. Boston is truly a walking city, and The Omni Parker is right in the middle of it all. It's right along the Freedom Trail. Staff was very friendly and helpful, upgrading our room upon request. The conceirge suggested fabulous places to eat. Parker's Bar within the hotel was great for dinner and open late. Our room was spacious and clean with a view of the city. The bed was amazing!! Made it very hard to get up early and walk around town! The Omni Parker is a great place to stay in Boston!

title: “Great hotel unless you expect to actually sleep”
text:
First- the positives. It's beautiful, and the location is amazing, and contrary to what I've read, I received great service from everyone from the front desk to the concierge (who we utilized several times) to the bellman.
We were able to get into Drai's after a bit of a wait on Thursday, we found it nice enough but not someplace we HAD to return to. When I requested a song of the DJ I was very rudly shot down. As I work as a DJ myself I never would have said what he said to a patron. The songs I requested were right in line with what he was actually playing, so Drai's did not really impress us. We actually turned down an invitation to return on Fri evening.
The room was very nice and ultra modern although I kept banging my right shin on the edge of the platform bed, I still have the bruises.
But the reason why I don't see myself returning was the noise at night. You hear EVERYTHING from doors closing to regular conversations from all directions. 
After a rather sleepless Thursday I asked the front desk for earplugs which I was shocked to see she had right onhand, prepackaged and ready to go!
However Sat night the earplugs did nothing to mask the people who decied that the hallway outside our room was the place to party at 3am. At first I politely poked my head outside to the couple who sat on the floor in bathrobes with food and drinks laid out picnic style in front of them and asked if they would mind taking it inside as we were trying to sleep. They apoligized, then moved maybe 5 feet away and keep on their conversation. After that I called the front desk and explained the situation. Their reply was not an apology but to ask if I had earplugs. After I explained they weren't making a dent they sent up security. 
I was prepared for a party hotel, as I've stayed in several other W's including Mahatten but nothing prepared me for the noice level at night. We were on the 10th floor and could hear the nighclub two floors up quite well.
Of the 3 nights I was there, I didn't sleep for two of them. 
At checkout when they asked how my stay was I relayed the above. They took my info and promised a manager would be in touch right away but so far I have not heard anything. 
I'm in the industry and know what is normal and what is not. Unless you are in a drunken stupor, I can't see how anyone gets a decent night's rest at the W.

title: “Amazing Stay, great hotel”
text:
The rooms are very new and well kept.
The staff was very friendly at the front desk and eating area. (even the general manager took out time to stop and visit while we were enjoying a free evening BBQ in the outdoor eating area)
We stayed here with 4 little children for a week while we visited San Diego. It's 11 miles from the major beaches (very reasonable). It's also 14 miles from the outlet stores.
This hotel is PERFECT for families visiting from out of town.

title: “Nice Hotel, Convenient Location”
text:
My fiance and I stayed at The Hotel George Memorial Day weekend from 5/22 to 5/24. We took the Greyhound Bus from NYC to DC and from the bus station it was about a 15 minute walk to the hotel which was very convenient. We arrived at the hotel at about 5:30pm and at check-in, the guy at the front desk was pleasant and check-in was quick. We had reserved a King Deluxe room and were given a room on the fourth floor. The room was very clean and the bathroom was laid out nicely with a shower and granite countertops. Honestly we felt that the room was nice but on the small side. We didn't have much of a view from our window, which was nothing more than a view of the other rooms on the other side of the hotel. We all had to have our blinds drawn all the time or else we'd be watching each other. We had to admit though, it was quiet on this side of the hotel since we didn't face street traffic. 
The hotel was about a 15 minute walk to Chinatown and to museums. On our first night, we walked to Chinatown and ate at The Wok N Roll which we ate at the last time we were in DC and it was just as good as we remembered and it was busy.
