The walk back to the hotel at night was okay. It was a very quiet stretch of road except for the occasional homeless person, passing car and random tourist. It seemed pretty safe though and no one bothered us. Our second day we walked to have lunch at Ella's Wood Fired Pizza. It was just okay for me. I ordered the marinara pizza and found it to be pretty bland and tasteless. My fiance ordered the pepperoni pizza which I tasted and it was much better than my marinara. They really need to do something about the tomato sauce they use. This once again proved that there is nothing like a good slice of NYC pizza. 
The Hirshhorn Museum and Sculpture Garden was fantastic and we had a good time there. The giant spider sculpture in front was creepy and yet really cool. The NSA Sculpture Garden was also fun. Our last museum visit was to the National Musum of Natural History which was crowded but great. The dinosaur, underwater and mammal exhibits were really fun and informative. 
The Hotel George was a nice little hotel located close to all the sights. The staff were friendly and helpful and even though our room was small, it was comfortable. The shower was great (thought the water pressure could have been stronger) and there was never a problem with hot water. The plasma tv was also nice and there was plenty of storage space for clothes in the dresser. The bed was very comfortable and there was plenty of light/lamps in the room. Usually we find that hotel rooms don't provide enough lights which make rooms appear very dark but this wasn't a problem here at all. The free wifi was also a nice touch.

title: “Kudos for excellent customer service, hotel is dated”
text:
First the positives:
-Let me rate the customer service. The front desk staff is very friendly and helpful, although there is no dedicated line for GoldPassport Elite members. Either way there are plenty of staff on hand and the wait is not long. Once you are at the desk, the staff takes the time to make sure all your questions are answered.
-What really impressed me was the hotels reaction to an unexpected event. I was there for a donwtown festival that got cancelled due to an impending tropical storm in the area. The hotel, recognizing that a lot of guests were there for that event and would want to leave to avoid the storm, made the decision to allow guests to leave withouth an early departure penalty. This clearly cost the hotel revenue, but they placed guest satisfaction before profit, major kudos for that.
-The restaurant provided good food for both breakfast and dinner, with a creative pasta buffett option for dinner which was a nice touch. 
-The location of the hotel is great, one easy walking block from the Jacksonville Landing and a bridge if you like to walk accross bridges for a view. Dowtown Jacksonville however is downright scary on weekends, and nothing is open, so unless there is an event going on, don't pick this location for a weekend escape.
-The river view rooms have great views of the sunset, river, and bridges, and the all glass doors that actually open to a balcony are a plus when most hotels this day an age are sealed.
Now the negatives: 
-The hotel is clearly dated and carpets and furniture are worn out. To be up to current Hyatt Regency standards, it needs a major facelift.
-The workout facility is clearly undersized for the number of rooms in the hotel, so depending on what is going on, expect to wait for equipment.
-Of the 8 or so elevators, only 2 or 3 seem to be working and the wait was always long
-The pool area seemed like a war zone, but I think this may be due to the type of people staying at the hotel on this particular ocassion. The pool on the rooftop is actually quite nice.
-Parking is $15 per day, which seems a little much given plenty of other parking available in the surrounding area.
-No refrigerator in the room, and a new trend I noticed at Hyatt's, no safe deposit box in the room. And given that this is a very large convetion hotel, with all kinds of different guests, this should be a priority.
Given the very slim choice of hotels in downtown Jacksonville, this seems to be the best choice, but by Hyatt standards, this is on the low end.

title: “Wonderful service and excellent accomodations for a great price”
text: The staff at On The Ave Hotel were extremely welcoming and accomodating to all of my requests. The friendly bellhop staff greet you at the door and the front desk staff are pleasant and willing to help you with any questions you have or requests you make. The room was clean and the bed comfortable. On The Ave Hotel made my brief stay for a very hectic and stressful business trip enjoyable!

title: “especially nice lobby, everything else fine but not very exciting”
text: stayed here on business, so i cannot comment on value for money because i did not shop around. gorgeous lobby. nice breakfast in the restaurant. nice staff. standard hotel room, all clean modern, full working order. good location for downtown, plenty of restaurants etc nearby

title: “Very Average”
text: The best thing I have to say about this hotel is the location. You are walking distance to the touristy Fisherman's Wharf, transportation and tourist shops. The hotel itself looked very unkept. In the lobby there was a huge water stain on carpet. Rooms just not very nice looking at all. The staff was very friendly and helpful though. If you like quality rooms I would say keep looking.

title: “Historic hotel - great location”
text: I went for a "staycation" in the Seattle area and ended up at this hotel with my son. It was great! The location is perfect - we walked to Pike Place Market and the waterfront (had dinner at Ivar's and rode the ferris wheel!). You could also walk to Pioneer Square in about 5 minutes or so. It is a historic hotel built in 1917 and had a lot of interesting history and architecture. If you are more into sleek and modern, this hotel might not be for you. The attached restaurant, Juno's, was extremely expensive ($20 for french toast, $6 for coffee in the morning). With a child, we chose to go to another local restaurant within walking distance. The only negative were that parking was $40 a night (typical for that area, though) and internet was $9.95 a night. We could hear some traffic outside, but that is the price you pay for being in the center of a city. Staff were extremely helpful. I paid $220 a night and got a deal from hotwire.com.

title: “Great Place and Location”
text: I have stayed at Sofitel a couple of times and they have been great. Service is wonderful and the hotel is located right in center city in the Rittenhouse area (17th St. between Chestnut and Walnut where there is lots of shopping and restaurants - overall a nice area). There's a restaurant and lounge in the lobby which always seems to be well populated, and the elevators are keycard activated so it's all pretty safe. The rooms are spacious with WONDERFUL beds and the bathrooms are clean and upscale. Definitely a nice, comfortable stay in center city Philly.

title: “Pioneer Square Hotel”
text: Recently stayed at the Pioneer Square Hotel. This boutique hotel is in a great location - close to the wharf, historic Chinatown and "old Seattle". The rooms are comfortable and reasonably priced. Great value for the money with in-room coffee and continental breakfast. Also close to all public transportation. Took the bus to Pike's Market - walked to the Space Needle - took the tram to downtown and then the bus back to the hotel. Dinner along the wharf with a fun trolley ride to get there.

title: “Greatest Hotel in D.C!”
text:
This hotel had great family service. Had a cookie jar in the front lobby filled with differnet kinds of cookies....my daughter loved it. Views are excellent. Service was outstanding, and very helpful. They let us go on the roof deck of the hotel...beautiful views of D.C., great camera place!! Also, really nice small containers of Evian mist provided for no change. A great place right in the middle of D.C.! Who could want better than that?
Hint- In April, they have the White House Garden tours. We were lucky enough to get tickets.

title: “Excellent hotel, only place I will stay in DC from now on”
text: Everything about my stay was great, the hotel was beautiful and kept well. The room I stayed in was huge and comfortable and the hotel is in a great location with easy access to great restaurants, stores and the metro. Room service was good as well. What really set this hotel apart was the staff, everyone there was great and went above and beyond to make sure I had whatever I needed during my stay. Since this is part of the Kimpton chain if you join the rewards program it is easier to get an upgrade and the wireless is free during your stay.

title: “Awesome”
text: Loved this hotel! Location is in the middle of everything downtown. Walked everywhere. Rooms were very modern and the beds were so comfy. Everyone who worked at the hotel was so nice and helpful. We even hit a round of golf at the virtual golf located at the hotel. We loved it here and will definitely stay here again when we travel to Seattle.

title: “Beautiful Hotel---Will return”
text:
Hotel was perfect. Recent remodel last year, rooms great, very, very clean bathrooms, glass showers, big vanities. University was closed, so ate in the ground floor restaurant. The french fries alone are worth a trip back. $15 cab ride from Hobby Airport.
Had a single room for my niece who was starting school, suite for my wife and me. Stay here....you'll like it.

title: “Stay at the Westin!”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for one night and we were not impressed. 
When we got there, the garage across the street was full and that was the inexpensive option for parking but the valet at the hotel let us know (without us even asking) that there was another cheap garage two blocks away so that was nice.
When we went to check in, they already had our room picked out which I didn't love because there is no chance of upgrading or asking for anything specific. Could be that there was nothing else available. Check in took about 1 minute. 
To get to our room, you need to leave the lobby, go across the valet/garage entrance to get to the other section. I thought this was crappy. Dragging all of your stuff across a garage while waiting for cars to go in and out is annoying. 
Our room was on the second floor and the elevator took forever!!! Literally, it could take 5 minutes for the elevator to come-even if it was empty!
Our room was interesting. There are no windows in these rooms but when I called to book the room, the booking agent was really helpful and booked us into a room overlooking the terrace. This way our doors were our windows. This was also strange because if you are out of your room, you need to have all of your lights off so no one can see you aren't in there and see all of your stuff lying around. You also have to have your shades drawn when you are in the room if you want privacy.
There were two double beds which were tiny! My husband and I would have preferred a queen or king but none were available I guess. The bedspreads on BOTH beds had stains on them and our bathroom had a dirty towel hanging up. I called the front desk and let them know the problems. Then when I went to use the mini-bar, I found that it was not on so all of the drinks and foods in there were hot and it smelled! I called again and asked if they could do something about that as well. They sent housekeeping after we left to sightsee and they changed the towel and bedspreads and turned on the mini-bar.
It was a pretty small room and tiny bathroom. 
The room was next to the road and it was very noisy. The room shook whenever a truck stopped at the light which was all of the time. 
When we laid down in the bed, there was writing on the ceiling and beams.
The remote control to the tv did not work and that was a big challenge. It was incredibly loud when it was turned on and it would not turn the volume down. The buttons basically worked after 5th or 6th time you pressed it (but it was random). You couldn't really turn the channels at all.
We went to the pool in the afternoon and they had a nice outdoor bar where you could get alcohol and juices. You could also charge to the room which was nice. Of course, we just told them the room number and they didn't ask for anything so we could have charged it to any room. 
The pool was a problem because although the pool itself was nice, there was NO seating. Every seat was full and there were not that many. There was oodles of room to put more chairs. 
The wall was high next to the pool so the sun was off of the pool pretty quickly and the water got cold fast. 
The location of the hotel was wonderful. It was right on the Riverwalk (which you will pay out of the nose for that view). It was close to the restaurants and bars and where you pick up the boat tour. 
We are Omni Select Guests so we got free drinks in the morning and although they were large bottles of Evian, they were warm. Not even slightly chilled. 
All in all, it wasn't horrible but there were a lot of problems for the cost and rating of this hotel. I would absolutely stay at the Westin next time I am there. 
Tips-The Riverwalk was great. Lots of fun and very touristy. The boat tour was the best part.

title: “good hotel for the money..not elegant at all but comfortably meets need”
text: stayed at this hotel for two nights while in city for taping of tv show at columbus circle..very convenient to that area as well as times square and theater which are generally ten blocks away...the staff was friendly and helpful at front desk, bell service,restaurant and housekeeping...this is an older hotel at which i stayed years ago...it is not the mandarin oriental so adjust your expectations but it is a good stay for the money...the room (733 south tower) was large and clean..the tv is the old type and needs updating badly..bathroom was clean with usual amenities..i am priority club member and was given continental brkfst each day and coupon for free drink in lounge as well as easy late check out...these benefits were a pleasant surprise...was told the hotel had been renovated two years ago but could use some sprucing up again...things look worn but not outrageously so....i wouild stay here again and feel safe in doing so...subway stop is block and half away towards 8th ave...

title: “Nice Chicago Hotel”
text:
We stayed at the Amalfi hotel for one night in October. We were greeted warmly at check-in and we immediately went to the happy hour on the sixth floor. They had all kinds of drinks including beer (some Italian), wine (American), and mixed drinks. I had the signature martini which had a nice story to it. There was also a buffet of meats, cheese, veggies, dips, and other snacks. There were a lot of people in the room and everyone seemed to have a nice time. The bartenders were friendly and helpful. 
The Amalfi is located in the River North neighborhood. There were plenty of restaurants and bars in the area. It is right around the corner from the House of Blues. We felt safe walking at night because there were so many others out having a good time. 
The room was relatively large for a city hotel. We were on the 5th floor, so we had a nice city view. I can see that if you were lower than we were that you would have a view of a brick wall. Everything was clean and well-kept. The mattress was a little soft in the middle, but was OK. There is a coffee maker in the cabinet. We did not realize this until we came back from getting coffee.
Breakfast was different. They serve it out in the hallway on each floor by the elevators. It was super convenient, but the only place to eat is in your room. I did not know if there is seating on another floor. If you have to grab breakfast to go, this was a nice way to serve. Breakfast consisted of juice, yogurt, coffee, tea, toast, donuts, cereal, sweet rolls, and bagels. I can’t complain about this, because it was free.
We decided to splurge on the parking package. However, I am not sure it is any cheaper to pay for it this way. I wonder if it is more expensive with the tax. I would call the hotel next time to be sure.
All in all, we had a very pleasant stay. I would probably give this hotel a 4.5, but I will round the points up since you can tell they are trying hard to give their customers a good experience.

title: “Good price, good hotel”
text:
We picked up a room at the Wall Street Inn for a pretty good price and were impressed with the hotel. We found the hotels location to be good - It's in a quiet lane a few blocks from the stock exchange and is close to subway stations, so easy enough to get around Manhattan. It's also right next to stone street where there are a bunch of good restaurants and pubs.
Room came with a continental breakfast which was good and very convenient.
Would recommend this hotel if you don't mind a subway ride to get back from midtown.

title: “Feels like your own Pied a Terre”
text: The hotel is divine – feels just like your own NYC Pied a Terre. The professional, courteous staff are well informed and cater to all your needs, especially attentive at breakfast. Rooms are architecturally intelligent and have everything you need for a great city stay. The hotel is well situated, not to mention the fabulous view of Empire State bldg from our front room on the 29th floor. Everything was spotless including the health club, which we enjoyed to start the day. We can’t wait to return.

title: “New, clean and quiet....an oasis.”
text: My husband and I just returned from a three night stay here. Check in and check out were very easy. Our room was clean and spacious, with a great view of Times Square. The bed was very comfortable and we slept well as the room was quiet. The only reason I did not give a perfect rating for service is having to ask three times for more coffee in our room, all we had was decaf when we arrived. We ended up at the Starbucks right across the street. I also had to ask for shampoo on the second day. The convience and ambience cannot be beat.

title: “A great hotel”
text:
From the moment we arrived at the Luxe at the end of a two week fly drive down the West Coast of the USA, we could not have been more impressed. Every member of staff was courteous and helpful and went out of their way to make us feel welcome, none more so than Debbie, the concierge, who was full of helpful ideas on what we might do during our stay . 
Our room (two queen beds) was large and very well-equipped, and during our stay we made full use of the pool area, which was never too busy and also the gym, which while pretty basic met all of our holiday needs. On our last night we also enjoyed a very good meal in the hotel restaurant, again with excellent service.
True the valet parking charge of $24 per day is a bit of a pain, but that service was provided with such efficiency and courtesy that that's really only a minor gripe far outweighed by all the other positives.
Located just off the I-405 in Bel Air/Brentwood, the Luxe provided an excellent base for exploring Santa Monica, Malibu and the rest of the greater LA area. 
It could not come with a higher recommendation.

title: “Bulfinch only if you get a great rate”
text: The price was right; the T, handy; the bed, comfortable. However, the extremely tiny room's lighting was so minimal that we could not see inside our suitcases nor read a book once dusk descended. The staff was insolent, hostile, if one had to address us. For example, upon arrival, the woman at the desk, never making eye contact, said, "Give me a photo ID and your credit card." There was not even a "Hello". The "laundry men" seemed to do little but ride the small elevator, leaning against their large laundry carts, discussing their private lives, making no acknowledgement or accommodation for guests. The bartender in the adjacent "lounge" leans on the counter or sits on a stool, conversing with her friends.

title: “Great staff, clean, and slept like a baby!!!”
text: This hotel is really nice. It is modern and clean. The staff was very helpful and friendly. Breakfast was good. I have no complaints. I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: “So-so hotel”
text: I stayed at the Mandarin Oriental New York for five nights. Yes, it's a pretty hotel with a nice location. The spa is good but terribly expensive. I was disappointed with the service. Every morning room service got my breakfast order wrong. And it was a new mistake every morning. Quite annoying having to wait for them to get the order right - every day! At least they got my dinners right. Several times when I called housekeeping to ask for something to be delivered or done in the room, they forget or made a mistake and brought the wrong things. On several occasions the concierge forgot to call me back or to find out things for me. They also provided me with addresses to several shops, but did not provide a map, or the side street, or the opening hours. And I had to help them find out several things which should have been easy. All in all, the hotel does not provide the type of service one would and should expect from a five-star and very expensive hotel.

title: “very good”
text: it is in a nice area. We had a room on the tenth floor with nice view all over the city. They had a really friendly stuff that helped us a lot because we extended our stay several times. They gave us tips on where to go and how and they bought us train tickets to New York. It was not expensive and the rooms were nice.

title: “Great midtown location and attentive staff”
text:
Convenient at Park Ave & 38th St., taxis easily available, staff attentive to any request, and room rate very reasonable. Having lived in NYC until 2003, it was a pleasure to stay here on a visit. 
The room could have had a better reading light. Hotel staff was friendly and helpful.

title: “Old School Service, Posh Place”
text: I had heard great things about the W hotel chain, but the D.C. location is amazing. It was exactly the stylish and unique place my wife was expecting. And the service...I felt like Jeff made our trip that more amazing!!! He was so helpful and attentive, and even arranged our dinner plans for us. By the end of the trip, I did not want to leave. I speak for my wife, too, when I say we can really get used to service like that. Thanks Jeff! We don't meet people like you too often, and we travel frequently. When in DC, we'll be staying at the W because of you.

title: “First visit to chicago!”
text: I really dont get much time to write a review on anything but my experience at this hotel was amazing! Having never been to Chicago i got great advice on things to do from your Concierge Brad, he recommended i do the architectural tour of the city and i loved it...great pictures! i also wanted to thank Eran from your bell staff he was super helful and even suggested a great park so i could enjoy a jog. I will definitely return and next time with my family!!!

title: “Great Hotel!!”
text: I would recommend this hotel, great location and a great price. The staff were very friendly and helpful. The rooms very comfortable and clean. If I visited San Francisco again I would stay here. The airport shuttle bus drops you off and picks you up right outside the hotel.

title: “THE WORST HOTEL!! I HAVE EVER BEEN IN MY LIFE”
text:
HORIBLE,
The pictures on the internet is not representing the hotel running by some Indian people which are so rude unhelpfull1- no telephone in the rooms 2- rooms are smaller than you can imagine I had to switch to a handy cap room so i would get some extra space, the internet had problem they did not help me at all and they didn't have any technician, no amenities NOTHING!!!! for one extra night they double charched me even the Expedi agent was shocked

author.location: White Plains, New York, United States

title: “Good stay in downtown Indy”
text: Overall a good stay. You have to pay for parking on top of the room. The desk staff wasn't really on top of things and the hotel is showing it's age. Overall a nice stay and very close the everything downtown.

title: “Decent for families”
text: My family of four stayed here in April of 2005. We have two small kids, ages 2 and 4 at the time. We had a room with two queen beds, a kitchenette, and a pretty nice bathroom with separate vanity area. My husband bid on Priceline and got if for 90 dollars. The room was dated but clean. We had a view of a brick building. The kitchenette came in handy to store milk and juice for the kids, snacks, etc. There is a CVS drug store right next to the hotel. I liked the bathroom. Although it was old, it was clean. The water is extremely hot, especially in the kitchen. The vanity area was nice to sit down and get dressed and do your hair, etc. We didn't eat the complimentary breakfast. We heard it was served in a smaller room and decided to go out instead. There is a nice cafeteria down the road next to the Red Cross building. I think it's called Java City Café. There is a café and a huge cafeteria with all sorts of delicious breakfast items. I mainly saw workers, but it is open to the public. I can't comment on the front desk, since my husband went in and I stayed in the car. The parking garage was crammed full, but wasn't a problem. There were employees there to move vehicles if need be. Overall the hotel was fine and met our needs. It was clean and comfortable. I wouldn't pay much over a hundred dollars per night though. The location was excellent.

title: “Bad customer service w/ broken facilities & thin walls.”
text: Great reasonably priced space. Bathroom facilities that do not work. Plumbing is very loud, every flush or shower your neighbor makes echos through your room. You can also hear, thanks to very thin walls, your neighbors going to the bathroom. You will have to be an early riser or a hard sleeper to stay here. Also parking is another $16/day. Stiff bed with overly stuffed pillows resulting in waking up with a stiff back & crick in the neck. Bed so stiff that when your partner rolls over every movement is transferred to shake you awake while sleeping. Do yourself a favor, spend a little more and stay somewhere else or stay home.

title: “Stay within your budget at Stay”
text:
I do a fair amount of business travel for a company that is exceptionally cost-conscious. It is difficult to find decent lodging in NYC while staying within the travel budget allocated me, but i managed to do it, (and even with a dash of style!) at Stay.
Upon entry, I found the lobby decor to be updated and very pleasing -- i like the aquariums in the seating area, which were a calming sight after the ruckus of the NY streets! The staff was limited and overworked when I arrived, but they were still gracious and accomodating, though obviously tired. I was able to get into my room at the unheard of hour of 11am, which was a huge bonus, as any business traveler knows.
There are only 2 elevators at Stay, and both are quite small. It didn't prove to be an issue, but you will spend some time waiting for them.
I liked the color scheme of the room (orange is a favorite!), and though the quarters were tight even in my "Large" room with a king-size bed (which is typical for NYC), the rate was just $220, which is exceptionally reasonable for the Times Square area of Manhattan. I found the bed to be very comfortable, with nice sheets and a fluffy duvet. It was great that there was an actual closet in the room, a large flat-screen tv on the wall, and the blackout shades on the windows were awesome. The hotel's updated phone system was also really nice because a digital touchscreen allowed you to set your own wakeup calls & such, and the tone of the alarm was actually pleasant to wake to.
The bathroom isn't as tiny as in some hotels of this level I've stayed at, but it isn't grand by any stretch. There was only a shower, no tub, but the shower itself was spacious enough & its interior was updated with tiled walls and a slate floor that ran thru the entire bathroom. The hotel features L'Occitane products, which was also a nice little surprise. The issue i had with the bathroom is that there is a pedestal sink with no counter space, only a very tiny glass ledge beneath the mirror for your toiletries & "stuff" -- the sloped forward tank lid on the toilet didn't afford any more surface-area for toiletry items! However, everything was very clean, and there were extra towels in the bathroom, always a plus!
Do note that if noise bothers you, you should definitely request a room on a higher floor -- Aspen is the very cool bar on the ground floor of the hotel that was surprisingly busy until at least 4am....and was also surprisingly loud in my 3rd floor room on my first night there! With earplugs in and the room's fan turned on high, i could still clearly hear a very methodical thump of bass and the music from the bar most of the night, which didn't bode well for getting any sleep. I requested a move the next day, which was very politely acommodated (i'm sure they get that a LOT...) and i then had no problems with noise in my new room on the 8th floor.
All in all, I'd definitely stay at Stay again...it fit my budget yet didn't feel bare bones, old or dirty like many of the other hotels within this price range that I've stayed at in this area.

title: “Perfect location, funky hotel”
text: If you want to be based in the heart of everything, you couldn't choose a better hotel! Views from the rooms are stunning. Rooms are designed well, with only annoyance being the extra charge for internet access that's still typical of too many high-end places. Lovely reception staff kindly gave free drinks vouchers on check-in, and we took advantage of the Acura transport offer thanks to the great door staff. You really feel like a star here, and with so much on your doorstep, don't spend the bulk of your time in your room - get out there and enjoy the city!

title: “Great Boutique Hotel Near Union Square”
text:
Stayed at Prescott in Club Level every time we come to SF for last 10 yrs as our daughter lives in SF. Some rooms are not large, but had a large room this time on 4th floor. Service was excellent, as always, even though hotel was fully booked due to baseball all-star game taking place during the time that we stayed there.. There is a separate concierge on the Club Level in addition to concierge in main lobby. Both were very helpful with dinner & theatre reservations. Wolfgang Puck's excellent Postrio Restaurant is located in the hotel & hotel guests have inside track on getting reservations. Free continental breakfast & full happy hour with Wolfgang Puck pizza in the afternoon & full complimentary bar. It is a short walk to Union Square, MOMA & art galleries, theatres. 
We arrived early before rooms were ready & checked bags. When we came back later in day the bags were already in the room, rather than in the storage area. Could use upgrade to flat screen TVs.

title: “Excellent value, service and location”
text: Stayed for 5 nights recently. It's excellent value with modern, renovated rooms, good solid service and wonderfully clean. The rooms are very comfortable and well equipped and serviced very well. Location is great, round the corner from the subway, safe and walking distance to so much. The hotel management obviously knows something about customer service and this shows in the staff dealings with guests. They respond quickly and appropriately to any issues. The breakfast buffet is more than adequate with a nice variety of food, continental style. The only criticism I have is that there are only styrofoam and plastic plates and utensils available and nothing seems to be recycled. I know there's no kitchen at the hotel, so they can't provide reusable dishware, but can't they find a way to recycle? This is just a personal beef. I'm already planning a return trip to NY and will definitely stay here again.

title: “Nice but no heated pool as stated”
text: I stayed at this hotel primarily because it advertised as having a heated swimming pool. I was very disappointed to find it was so cold that it wasnt bareable even for a minute. no-one used it im presuming because of this and it was left empty with a service man cleaning it so it looked good. This is typical Sheraton Hotel 'all about the looks', i asked if it could be heated up but was told that the engineers have to be called and that wasnt possible. The rooms were nice, well serviced and the breakfast very good. I loved the flames outside!

title: “hotel from h****”
text: was put in a non smoking room that reaked of smoke. i was then put in another room that did not smell of smoke but had burn marks on the furniture and the bed linens. i was very disappointed in this hotel, considering it is associated with the wyndham hotel chain

title: “Overpriced and not enough bang for your buck”
text:
I stayed here for the first time earlier this week with my Mom for a Women of Faith conference at the American Airlines Center across the street from the hotel. The convenient location is the only thing I really enjoyed during our stay. 
We had no idea until we got to the room that there is barely any privacy in the bathroom. The tub/shower is not separated by a door. So you have to pull a curtain all the way across the room to separate the bath from the bedroom. Also, the only wall outlet in the bath area was very low on a wall between the tub and sink- not very safe with lots of water around. 
The first night we were there, I barely slept at all as I could not sleep under their very thick down comforter. This was the middle of August- too hot for down comforters. There were no other options for bedding in the room. The second day, I called and asked for a different blanket and that one was much better. 
Finally, three days after staying here, I noticed that I was charged the full amount on my credit card even though we asked the man at the front desk to put half on my mother's card and half on mine. Not sure why that was not done.

title: “an perfectly fine not outstanding hotel”
text:
I was expecting a lot when I heard I was going to be staying at the New York Palace hotel and found out it was part of the Dorchester Collection, which includes the famous hotel on Park Lane in London.
So I guess I was always going to be disappointed. The best I can say is that the hotel overall is fine. Nothing special but not too bad for New York hotels.
The hotel is busy and like so many New York hotels the reception staff seem off hand and disinterested, reeling off their patter with little real honesty or believability.
The rooms are large for New York and quiet. The bed is large and very comfortable, and there is a gigantic flat screen TV with large range of channels. A good sized desk and fast internet access.
The overall decor of the rooms, and the hotel for that matter, is beige, bland and unmemorable. The bathroom is a big disappointment as is a cookie cutter New York hotel look. They do have Molton Brown toiletries which is a plus.
Room service is cheerful and efficient, but the food is very average.
The location on Madison and 50th is good for Fifth Avenue shops.
The fitness centre on the 8th floor is large and well equipped and a plus.
There is a lack of attention to detail overall, so things like the battery in the scales was run down, the toilet needed some manual help to shut off after flushing and the limo I booked was booked for 615pm and not 615am as asked for.
The hotel rides on the brand name of Dorchester, but is not giving the service, attention and the overall experience it should.
It is one of those bland but fine places you end up staying for when away for work. Not bad enough to complain, but not good enough to really look forward to going back to.

title: “ok”
text: Nothing nice but ok if you are just passing though and need a place to sleep. Nice shopping across the street. Parking is cramped.

title: “Great Hotel, would definitely book again and recommend to all!”
text:
A very positive experience at Yotel Times Square New York. We arrived 2 days after it opened and was definitely pleased with the results. It looks just as good as it is advertised, staff are extremely helpful.
Facilities are top notch, instead of having a kettle and hot drinks facilities in your room, they have a galley (mini kitchen) on each floor that includes a fridge, microwave, sink and a posh hot drinks machine. The drinks tasted amazing, none of the cheap sickly stuff offered in some places. Rooms are kept clean on a daily basis ensuring you leave your card outside the door, instructing them to clean your room. The hotel has an amazing terrace area where there is a large seating area accomodating all weather conditions, looks extremely nice when the sun is out. We did not try the restaurant or bar food so we can comment however the menu did look appetising. Free Continental breakfast consisted of fresh fruit, muffins and pastries, with a seperate menu for items to order inc hot and cold.
The location of the hotel is not exactly Times Square yet a ten minute walk, it is a very good location from the centre. Hells Kitchen is literally a few steps away, with an array of different restaurants and bars to choose from.
Staff were happy to help on all occasions, we forgot to bring a travel adaptor with us from the UK and were offered a new one free of charge. You are able to store left luggage in the hotel lobby if you want to explore the city on check out at no extra charge. Concierge were always at hand day or night, great guys.
Would definitely recommend this hotel to all and will definitely book again. Thanks Yotel New York for an excellent stay.

title: “A nice hotel at a ridiculous price.”
text: Thank goodness for discount booking sites! We enjoyed our overnight stay at the Hilton at a price tag of $100, but had we paid the full rate of $200+, we'd have been sorely disappointed. Valet parking is the only option, and at $30 per night, it's highway robbery. The room was pleasant but small (and the decor a little garish for my tastes, but your mileage may vary!). The desk staff was delightful, but housekeeping didn't seem to know we were checking out, so they knocked on our door while we were trying to sleep in. The faucet fell apart in my hands and the bathroom fan didn't work. There was no minibar, which we didn't mind, but there WERE two small bottles of water in the room.....at a cost of $5.00 each. Seriously, when you're paying $250 for a hotel room and parking, should you really have to get stiffed for bottled water too? If you stay here, understand that you're paying for the great location, not for a luxury hotel experience.

title: “Better than average but not top quality”
text: We wanted to spend a relaxing weekend in S.A. and found a special deal at the hotel's website. We choose Westin because we knew they had quality properties so we were surprised when we found the room and amenities at this hotel just average. The Heavenly Bed was very good, but that was it. The room had no robes, no slippers, only two worn out bath towels, a burned out light, non-locking balcony doors, no stationery or pens, a broken makeup mirror, and worn carpet. We couldn't find any complimentary water anywhere on the property .Everything in the miniibar was outrageously expensive, like $5 for a coke or bag of peanuts! They did replace the broken stuff, however we should not have had to tell them about this sort of thing. We had a couples massage at the Spa which was excellent, however the location by the pool made for a less than relaxing experience. Also, the 'Spa' had no locker room or lounge so we waited in robes in the reception area, not my ideal of luxury. Before we made reservations no one advised us the main restaurant was ungoing renovations, so the hotel had only a single place to eat. We had breakfast there and the buffet was very good, but it was crowded with only the one venue. Staff was very nice and friendly. Parking, like other hotels in downtown S.A., was very expensive at $25 per day. All in all, it was a nice hotel, but not up to Westin quality or our expectations.

title: “Pleasant hotel and staff”
text: The hotel is near the 16th St Mall. But that should not deter you. Good service, pleasant accommodations. Good selection for breakfast. Forget the mall. It's depressing and not worth the walk.

title: “nice but not as nice as NYC Kimpton”
text: The hotel was very nice but does not compare to the New York City Kimptons. Much different service and attitude for families

title: “Clean and quiet!! Perfect location!!”
text: Woud stay here again anytime! Right in the middle of all the Boston attractions! Clean, quiet and helpful, friendly staff! Thanks Hotel 140!

title: “First-class hotel”
text: I stayed here on my most recent trip to Chicago and was very pleased in all respects. The front desk staff upgraded my room without any special pleading on my part, they switched the duvet for a blanket without asking, etc. Probably the best, most consistently attentive service staff I've encountered for a year. My room was good, as usual. The location is excellent, the facility is very attractive and all around the Sofitel Chicago gets my highest recommendation.

title: “Very nice hotel”
text:
Hiltons are always great hotels, and this one is no exception.
Although Hilton has a weird policy of paid wifi in guestrooms, at least they offer free wifi in the lobby - and this hotel finally has tables and stools with outlets, so you can plug in a surf the net.
Comfy, clean, and very nice staff.

title: “It Doesn't Get Any Better !!”
text: I stayed at his hotel while on business. My room was HUGE and had a corner balcony that had a great view of the city. This is an older hotel with a lot of history. But, unlike most older hotels, this one was classy old. The staff was super friendly and was asking to help you everytime that you saw one of them. Unlike most expensive hotels, the hotel bar was reasonably priced and the food was excellent. As I am typing, I am trying to think of something negative but I can't think of anything. WAIT - Avoid the 19th FLOOR ! The hotel is supposedly haunted and the 19th floor is the center of the activity. Some of my coworkers on the 19th floor had odd things happen but my room was actually too quiet. I personally like a little noise from a fan or traffic but there was dead silence in my room. There is some irony in that my room was so quiet and my co-workers heard big band music on the 19th floor. :)

title: “Quietest Room In Town”
text:
I've stayed here before and came back by choice. It's a new from the ground up hotel right in the center of things on 31st between Broadway and Fifth. Short walk to Times Square, Empire State Building and Macys -- and lots of other attractions. 
But what really sets this hotel off for me is how quiet the rooms are. New York is known for noise from the streets that echos up between the buildings and into your space all night long. The building is new and has double pained glass windows that seal tight. Pull the window shut and it is just like putting on a pair of Bose Noise Cancelling headphones. In addition, there are only eight rooms per floor so much less traffic and noise outside your door as other guests come and go.
Staff is most accomodating, friendly and attentative to everyone coming into the building. I suspect security is good since anyone coming in through the front door has to pass within ten feet or so of the front desk personnel - and they seem to be watching in a friendly, non threatening way.
I'll be back again when business brings me back to Manhattan.
Staff is

title: “clean and quite spacious room”
text:
we spent there 4 nights just after arrival to LA. 
Easy check-in, room was clean, with new carpet, bed was comfortable. 
Good location as it's just about 10-15 min drive from Venice Beach, Marina del Rey, Santa Monica. But if you are looking for any entertainment in hotel nearby u will be disapointed.

title: “just for stay”
text: perfect location, in the hearth of Old Town. easy access to every location safe place. free parking lot and free internet at all location. poor breakfast desk, they would improve the breakfast desk. the bathrooms need to renew.

title: “One of the best hotels EVER”
text:
I stayed at the Grand Hyatt Seattle while attending a conference and could not have been more pleased. It was one of the best hotel stays I have ever had. 
The room was absolutely gorgeous ... I honestly don't think I've ever seen a more attractive hotel room. It was like something out of Architectural Digest. Beautiful furniture, wall coverings, window treatments, everything. I loved the automatic blackout blinds over the gigantic windows (I could see the top of the Space Needle from mine) -- you can raise or lower the shade without getting out of the very comfy bed. Lots of nice little touches; I liked having a little "do not disturb" light you can turn on rather than hanging a sign on the doorknob -- very convenient and classy.
The bathroom was ENORMOUS, and stunning. Marble, brass, huge glass shower, beautiful fixtures. The tub was so large and inviting that I couldn't resist taking a bath, and I'm not even a bath person.
The location was wonderful -- about a block from the convention center, and tons of dining and shopping options within easy walking distance. Loved the Barnes & Noble across the street and the Starbucks you can get to directly off the hotel lobby.
The desk staff was friendly, professional, and helpful; I never had to wait in line to be helped. The lobby has lots of comfy seating and is a great place to meet friends and chat. This feels like a boutique hotel -- you never feel like you're in some huge monolith. The hotel is actually quite compact, so you're never too far from the elevator (though I never heard it, or much of anything else, from my very quiet room). 
I can't recommend this hotel enough, and hope I'll get to return to Seattle soon just so I can stay there again!

title: “Too Stylized to Be Comfortable”
text: The Standard New York is a hip, very trendy and fantastically located hotel. My room had beautiful views, and the hotel is close to great restaurants and trendy fashion boutiques. Overall, I felt the rooms were too stylized to be comfortable. My shower was small and awkwardly shaped - plus, it was open, which made it a bit cold and obviously not private. The bed was comfortable and my room had this great wrap around couch and coffee table. That was my favorite part of the room. The service weas pretty good, but I certainly wouldn't describe it as friendly. The flooring in the lobby is very slippery, so if you are wearing heels - watch your step! I almost slipped and someone on the staff caught my fall, remarking that I'm not the first for it to happen to. It's a nice hotel, and if other Standard properties are to your liking, then I'm sure you would love this one.

title: “Will Never Visit Again”
text: Before I write this, I just wanted to say I am not one of those people that have high expectations. I stayed at this hotel the day before my cruise was to depart. I was not aware of the $15 parking fee until I got the bill. If I known I there was going to be a parking fee, I would have never invited my friend down the the hotel. I went to the bar and never got waited on, so I walked down the street and got some Chinese food. My sleep number bed didn't work. Very disappointing. The desk chair was broke. The vanity lights were on a very bad slant. The tub had black scuffs in it. The hallway reeked of marijuana. The hallway of my floor, the walls were badly scuffed. The place just needs some major remodeling or something.

title: “Great deal in a great location”
text: We stayed two nights in December. The location, amenities and price were perfect for us as we spent very little time in the room and do not mind being "close" together. The rooms are small, the elevator is slow, and it is an old hotel. However, the rooms are comfortable and clean, the bathroom is roomy enough and has nice towels, and the location is great -- right next to Union Square and on the trolley line. You can eat breakfast (included) in the Tea Room on the second floor and enjoy watching the trolley and people through the street side windows. Wifi is also included and the staff is very friendly. Our room was quiet and the bed was comfortable. Not sure if there is air conditioning but our room had a ceiling fan and windows that open. I would definitely stay there again. You can't beat the price.

title: “Simply awesome!”
text: We visited this hotel for a short break just before Christmas 2010 and were very pleased with it. The location is perfect, being 100m away from times square. The rooms are small as it is a boutique hotel, but they are very very clean and have every thing you could want. The hotel has not long been refurbished and it has been done to a very good standard. The staff in the hotel are very friendly and helpful. We booked excursions through the concierge, we printed flight boarding cards off on the printer in reception to avoid business centre costs. One girl even stood outside at 4am to hail us a cab. Our flight got cancelled and we thought were going to have to stay longer so the hotel agreed to extend our stay at rock bottom prices. We will definitely be visiting NYC again, and will definately use this hotel next time.

title: “Great location and clean”
text: Check in was fast and friendly and informative of surrounding area. I will diffidently stay again in future trips. The manager reception was a perfect ending to a long day ;)

title: “I so love this hotel and the guys that work there!!!”
text: Sleep Inn hotel is located downtown Inner Harbor which is a great location. You have all your favorite restaurants and more. Great hotel for you and your family. Sleep Inn have great service and the people that work there are amazing (Abraham and John :)). Parking is only $15 which is a low rate compared to the other garages and parking lots downtown Baltimore. I rather stay at this hotel any day!!

title: “Interiour room - not insanely bad, but...”
text:
We were gifted enough to receive interiour rooms. Which, at first I thought I would hate, but then again, we were only there to sleep a few hours anyways.
However, since the room was at the start of a hallway, next to the elevator, it got a little bit to noisy for my liking, and I didnt get the best sleep of my life.
Could maybe stay again, but would be 100% sure to get a room with a window, and also a bit further away from the elevators. The area was a little bit sketchy, it might be better when the construction across the street is done, what do I know :)

title: “THE Place to stay in San Francisco”
text:
Spent 3 nights at the Argonaut and found the whole experience fautless. The doormen were very helpful and knowledgable on local attractions and places to eat - try Joanies in the square behind the hotel for great breakfasts!
Rooms very comfortable with all you need and a great power shower, though neighbours can sometimes be heard if particularly noisy.
Location within Fishermans wharf is superb. There is the cable car terminal literally next door and Pier 39 is only a 5 minute walk away. Getting into the city centre is easy and if you are lucky enough you even get a view of the Golden Gate bridge and/or Alcatraz from your room!
Reccomend Tower Tours for a 3 hour coach tour of all the city's sights (Golden Gate/Twin Peaks/City centre etc) followed by the Alcatraz tour - A MUST!!!!!
Go stay at the Argonaut - you will not be disappointed.

title: “Great Hospitality, Very welcoming, Excellent Staff”
text:
Luke Profancik, Front Desk Manager is an excellent representative for The Westin San Diego Hotel. He exceeded our expectations in handling Guests and any problem they may encounter. (Parking Garage Door would not open) He got us to where we needed to be.
Reham Attya, Front Desk person registered us. She was very personable. Her conversation with us made us feel very welcome. 
Jesse was our Bellman and was exceptional in making sure we were very satisfied with his service. The other Bellman were wonderful, too. I can't remember their names.
My husband and I have been in the Hotel business for 35 Years. THe Westin San Diego truly knows how to hire a great staff .

title: “Got tired of asking”
text:
Firstly it's not on the Magnificent Mile, though the location is fine with plenty of nice places to eat and many places within a short walk. It's a big, busy, bustling place - not really what we like but as we were just having a brief stopover that was ok. 
Maybe it's me being not used to the US hotels but I found paper cups for coffee in the room a bit incongruous. You have all this 'flash' glassware and bottled water but the cups seem out of place.
Our problems were as follows:
Internet access in rooms - yes, no problem - except it costs and we had to ask how much. Then we have two iPhones and two iPads and that meant according to the concierge a x4 charge.... Almost $40 a day...... Hmmm, ok sits in lobby and it's free- provided you - you guessed it - asked for a code.
Ok, coffee in a double room - 3 coffee sachets..... You guessed it, asked and we were given some more, and some milk as well.
Ok, toilet tissue, no spare..... Ok let's go and ask for some......
Ok no facial tissues, had to go and.......
It's the little details that make life a hassle or not.... Being on a trans USA trip it would have been nice to just 'have things' to hand. 
Ok let hope the next Doubletree is not on an economy drive.

title: “OK hotel, location a bit far form attractions”
text:
Stayed here on Sunday 25th March for 1 night with my partner on our 1st visit to DC.
We were greeted by a lovely member of staff on reception who took our bags and stored them for the day so we could head off sightseeing.
Came back to the hotel around 6/7pm to check in. Smooth check in made. I didn't like the fact they charge $40 "holding fee" as we are UK travellers and using a cash passport that was $40 of my spending money gone. I didn't get the money back onto my card until about 2 days later which luckily we were still in America to use, otherwise if I had to change it back to sterling in the UK I would have lost out on with the exchange rate.
ROOM - Room was vast. Not enough furniture in the room to fill the space. TV temperamental. Felt very bare and echoed. Room overlooked the road which was quite. We didn't hear any road noise only noise from the room next door. Walls seemed a bit thin as we would hear their TV and child screaming. The bed was very uncomfortable even after changing the firmness/softness. We didn't sleep very well. Room was spotlessly clean though.
LOCATION - Location was OK. About a 10/.15 min walk from Union Station. We joined a sightseeing tour bus at Union Station and used this pass to get around a see the sights of Washington. There were a few places to eat around the hotel but not many. I would book a more centrally located hotel next time.
OVERALL - It was an OK stay. Staff lovely, hotel immaculately clean and location so-so.
Would I stay there again? For a cheap price but not for what I paid.

title: “Good Hotel”
text:
I recently stayed and the travelodge central and my expierence was very good. The Manangement staff was very accomendating and friendly. I had to extend my staff for work and the made the process very smooth and easy. 
It is a good value for San Francisco and I would redommend this hotel.
L. Green

title: “Superb”
text: Beautifully maintained both public areas and room. Fine interior design and decor. Two short blocks from Times Square, but completely quiet. Reasonable accessibility to non-tourist coffee shops and deli-type food, but a but a few blocks from decent restaurants. Very comfortable beds.

title: “Great neighborhood feel”
text:
A gem of a hotel! Classic in styling with superior room amenities- you'll love the mini bar and bath products. We love this neighborhood and have stayed at several nearby hotels- this one is best for luxury hotels as far as comfort, quiet rooms, and private Gramercy Park access- a nice treat after an exhausting day of touring the city. Concierge was helpful with business transactions adn the Maialano Restaurant is a must do for Sunday brunch.
Lighting is a little dark for reading in bed but otherwise- awesome!

title: “overrated”
text:
I stayed here based on the TA reviews as my usual NY hotel was full. Whilst the hotel was perfectly adequate, the service was terrible, especially on the roof top bar, and the breakfast, whilst complementary, had a poor choice.
Not quite as perfect as described in many of the reviews!

title: “Couldn't ask for better”
text: We arrived and promptly found a parking space. we had driven from LA to SF stopping on the way at Best Western Hotels on the way. The holtel is in a fantastic location and was accessibe for shops and local buses. We must recomend the burger restaurant nearby Barneys Gourmet Handburgers. ( i'm a veggie and the range of options was fantastic)

title: “What a wonderful place!”
text: We enjoyed our week stay at the Majestic, the staff were all friendly and made us feel as if we were at home. The place is beautiful, very quiet at night and the bed is just so comfy, we slept like babies. The complementary breakfast is great for light breakfast eaters. The elevator is small, two people plus luggage is comfortable but we took the stairs most of the time. The linens and bath robes were very plush. Chicago will always be a special city for us and with the memories of staying at the Majestic makes it a slice of heaven. Go Cubs!!

title: “Good experience despite ongoing renovation work at hotel”
text: Spent one night there for business. They are currently going through a renovation the hotel. However, I had a very good experience. The staff were friendly and helpful. They helped with finding a place nearby to eat. The hotel workout room was unavailable due to construction. However the hotel offered free passes to gym just a couple blocks away that was fabulous. The morning breakfast was good. One minor issue: Wanted to take some conference calls from the room using speakerphone but the phone didn't have the option and the sound quality overall was poor with the phone. Perhaps that is getting fixed with their renovation. Other than that, it was a very good experience I look forward to coming back next when the renovation is done.

title: “Great hotel!”
text: I recently stayed at the Westin as a business trip that we turned into a mini-vacation. We stayed 4 nights with my 5-year-old, a babysitter and my husband. We got a junior suite to have a bit more space. We travel a lot and are pretty picky about service and amenties. The Westin was one of the best we have expereinced. Great location, new and updated (especially compared to the other hotels on the riverwalk) and friendly and accomodating staff. Room service was quick and easy but we all ordered the Salmon which was just OK. Otherwise all was exceptional. Will be my first pick if we come back to San Antonio!

title: “Such good value for money”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for the second time and once again were not disappointed. The service was very good. Our room although small was comfortable and very clean. The complimentary breakfast( very unusual for New York hotels) was limited but very welcome and sets you up for the day. The hotel has a bar which is very lively early evening with homeward bound office workers. It also has a restaurant which we didn't use but if you are staying at the hotel you get 15% off the bill which you also get at the Irish bar opposite. The menu looked good but we preferred to go out and about in the evening. The location is spot on, if you turn left out of the hotel you are at Macys, if you turn right you are on 5th Avenue and the Empire State Building. It is a short walk to Times Square and a slightly longer but reachable walk to Central Park.
The best things about this hotel were the location, the price and the friendliness of the staff. The worst things were the temperamental hot water system which sometimes took 5 minutes(yes really!) to reach our 12th floor room. However we think this hotel has much more going for it than against it and would not hesitate to stay there for the 3rd time.

title: “Very clean, useful, straight-forward and great location!”
text:
I booked 2 nights at the Hilton Garden Inn in Chelsea for my NYC holiday, and was very happy about it. It was a bargain I grabbed and I was welcomed very friendly and politely, and given a couple of bottles of water.
The room is spacious with 2 double beds and a nice spacious bathroom. I liked that there was an empty mini fridge and a microwave in the room so you could buy your own food and keep it there, which is a big money saver! The bed has some sort of sleeping system which is a dial on the side of the mattress but I didn't really feel the difference. The AC worked well and kept the room at a nice temperature. Great views of the Midtown skyline as well. Plus - there is FAST, FREE WiFi. 
There is a small fitness room in the basement which is good enough for a bit of cardio and some basic weights, plus a complimentary bottle of water. There is also a small shop where you can buy snacks and a restaurant/bar, but I didn't use any of that.
The staff was overall very friendly, smiley, welcoming and polite and really made me feel good about staying there. The only nag was when I called Room Service to ask for a spoon and I was told "ring reception." 
It is really well located on 28th street so you have the subway on 8th avenue (3 mins walk) or the one on Broadway (3 mins too), but you can walk to Macy's on Herald Square/34th Street and you have other lines there. There are lots of very comfy, cool buses that are cheap, safe, quick and not as hot as the subway, plus you see the streets and not a tunnel.
I was so happy staying there that I stayed a third night! The one thing I didn't like (but I don't know if it's hotels in general) was that I was going to the Hamptons the day I checked out and back the day after so I asked if I could leave my luggage overnight and I was told "they don't have the space" (??), so I was given a photocopy of a luggage storage service up on 36th Street between 8th & 9th Aves. While they were happy to have my bags for the day, they didn't help with keeping one single bag overnight, which I wasn't thrilled about. 
Overall, it was VERY clean, comfortable, spacious and a good service. For what I paid, it certainly was a bargain and very, very well located. I'd definitely recommend staying there - I will certainly go back.

title: “♥♥♥”
text: Loved this place. I was at the Eventi for four nights and had amazing time. My room was on 9th floor and the windows were facing the Empire state building <Amazing View>. Room was clean, modern and very roomy. Bed was very comfy and i needed it that way as i was in the plane for like 18 hours or so. The staff was amazing and that was the highlight for me throughout my stay. Front Desk guys greeted me with my name when i just entered the hotel. I was kind of bit shocked that how they know my name but was impressed. 24 hour room service was great too and had some good desserts in the menu!! This place is on 6th avenue and 30th street which is very very close to everything. Time sq., MOMA, shopping at 5th Avenue, Madison Avenue, Fashion Avenue are just short walk away from the hotel. This was my first ever time to NYC and i think i did make the right decision to book this place... Overall very happy with my stay. But the only point i would like to raise is that why less than half a glass of milk costs 5 dollars? i know its NYC and we are talking about Manhattan but seriously 5 bucks... hahaha anyways i was even happy to pay 5 bucks for that cuz this place was amazing. Thank you so much for making my stay very pleasant!!

title: “Great stay!”
text:
This hotel is a great value in Seattle. My husband and I were there for a wedding in June of 2007. We had original plans to stay at the Warwick. We were meeting my in laws and they had already checked into the Warwick and hated it. They found the Silver Cloud in Capital Hill. The public transportation (bus stop) is right at the corner of the hotel so it was really easy to get to shopping and Pike Place. When we checked in, the hotel did not have a standard room with a king bed so they upgraded us at no charge to the corner suite. It had a jacuzzi tub with a fireplace! Wonderful! The staff was very nice and helpful. They even called to place our dinner reservations. There is a complimentary breakfast every morning in the restaurant- delicious! 
Highly recommend this hotel and would stay there again in the future.

title: “The best hotel in New York - and I've stayed in quite a few.”
text:
Over the past 15-20 years I've frequently travelled to New York for work, usually at short notice and for brief trips (most of them no more than two nights). It's also one of my favourite cities in the world and I've been there for holiday too, though much less often. I've stayed in a wide range of hotels, from hostels with shared bathrooms up to deluxe five-star palaces, but my favourite hotel among the many is definitely the Royalton. The location is absolutely perfect, but despite being in the heart of the city the rooms are quiet and you can get a good night's sleep. The service is first class and on several occasions I've had individual members of staff do little things, probably not that big a deal to them, but that make all the difference - leaving a little hand-written note to welcome you back, making sure a room is readied for early check-in, or whatever. Every stay there has been perfect, and I can think of no higher praise than to state that it's the place I stay when I'm paying for my accommodation myself. Granted, it's not the cheapest option, but you definitely do get what you pay for. 
I should also add that I'm by no means a huge fan of the other hotels in the group. I've stayed in the Hudson, Morgan's and, when the Schrager people ran it, the Paramount, and found all of them pretty frustrating, for various reasons. The rooms at the Paramount and Morgan's are incredibly small - sometimes you can't even walk around the side of the bed and have to sort of launch yourself onto it from the foot, which suggests the hotel has been carved up into too many rooms to maximise returns at the expense of guest comfort. The rooms in the Hudson are good but the hotel didn't seem to be able to make up its mind whether it wanted to be a trendy night club or a place for people to stay, it was noisy and preeningly self-conscious, and, worst of all (and it was a few years ago so I've no idea if this has been changed now, but it put me off so much I would never stay there again) the en-suite bathroom is separated from the bedroom by *a sheet of glass*!!! OK if you've got sole occupancy, but a serious issue if not (no matter how intimate you might be with whoever's in the room with you). I've also stayed in the Mondrian in LA and that has similar problems of pretentiousness. But the Royalton has never succumbed to any of that stuff - it's stylish, yes, and it takes itself a bit seriously, but not in a show-offy way; and never to the detriment of the guest. They remember that what they're there to do is provide a refined, relaxing, high-quality place to stay in one of the greatest cities in the world. You'd think it wouldn't be difficult, yet very few people get close, and only one hotel does it this well.

title: “Won't return”
text: We had two rooms: one "upgraded" to a suite and the other not. The "upgrade" had no air conditioning in one of the suite rooms for two of the four nights we were there. Repeated phone calls were required before we could get a response. The wrong size sheets were used on one of the beds ie twin on a queen-size bed so the bed came unmade during the night. Pest traps for roaches were left on a nightstand. Towels in complete sets were never delivered even with daily phone calls. The "queensize" sofa beds are barely fullsize. We measured this and checked several online sites. This was not a good value.

title: “Avoid at all costs”
text: Stayed here and want to save you the trouble of a terrible stay. Once they screwed up our reservation, they choose to save face and blame us for the mistake. As a result, I had to sleep on the floor. Stay away from this place. There is no customer service. Unless you get lucky, you will hate your stay here. I won't even get into the uncleanliness and discusting bathrooms.

title: “great place to stay in the city!”
text:
We stayed here for a weekend get away. I was pleasantly surprised the hotel was right in the middle of everything! The location is awesome but parking was rediculously high (24/night). I actually just parked a block away at a meter (free after six and six dollars for four hours (starting at 9am mon-sat), enough time to walk and shop around downtown). 
The room was a good size for two people. Had a comfortable queen size bed w/lots of down-filled pillows. The only downside was the semi-clogged drain in the shower. Didn't call to complain, just took quick showers. 
We would definitely come back again!

title: “Greatest hotel in the World”
text: The Chelsea is obviously very famous for those who have stayed here and those who have died there. As other reviews testify its not renowned for being a great hotel. Don't stay here of you don't want to meet eccentric people, don't stay if clanking heating annoys you and don't stay if you want a hermetically sealed, hypoallergeinc Philippe Starck experience. This place reeks of atmosphere (amongst other things) which is worth the room rate 3 times over. In reality the room I stayed in was quite perfect, restored but not stripped of all heritage. Stay and enjoy it for being the best hotel in the world, if not go to a Marriott and knock yourself out.

title: “Very Good in many ways - but oh! - the noise”
text: The noise of jack hammers and drills from the World Trade Centre building site at the front and the grinding noise from air conditioning fans on a nearby building at the rear spoils the visit. Very helpful staff. The superior rooms with kitchenettes are well equipped but a little odd as they are 35ft x an average of circa 12 ft. To get to the hotel you have to negotiate blocked off streets because of the building work. Good price if booked in advance but take ear plugs.

title: “Good location, clean, helpful, good value compared to others in the area.”
text: We got a good deal on this hotel through Priceline and I wouldn't hesitate to stay here again. The front desk was efficient and helpful. We didn't use any of the amenities so I can't rate those but the room was spacious and clean. The bed was comfortable. The street noise didn't bother us, we could barely hear it.

title: “wonderfully accommodating”
text: This was the last night of our 12-day trip, and this was a great place to stay! The staff was exceptional accommodating. They had a complimentary dinner the night we were there, and the breakfast was great also. Though we didn't use the airport shuttle, it was apparent the man driving the shuttle was very familiar with other guests; it was a nice touch to see such personalizaton. I would recommend this absolutely. The room was very clean, full of kitchen amenities, and divided into two rooms to afford some privacy among the family.

title: “Quiet Location with Sophisticated Atmospehere”
text: As soon as I checked in the staff was really friendly. I asked about finding a restaurant and they knew just where to send me. Theres a small town nearby that has a strip of local restaurants; it was nice to find places that you can't find anywhere else. The hotel looked brand new and my entire stay ended up being really pleasant. Thanks for making my visit more comfortable!

title: “A perfect vacation and hotel!”
text: During our stay at the Hampton Inn during Memorial Day weekend, we encountered some of the best hotel staff, Especially Alonzo Jones and Eugene Harris. They were willing to go the extra mile for us and make sure we were happy. We enjoyed their hospitality and professionalism and we look forward to a return visit!

title: “Good room at a great value!”
text:
Stayed here one night while on a spur of the moment weekend trip to St Augustine and Jacksonville. Since moving to Florida from the midwest last year I have enjoyed taking my fiancee around the state to show her things I have seen on previous trips and exploring new things for both of us. After a long day exploring the Old Town in St Augustine and then zipping up US 1 to Jacksonville to get a little bit of the ocean and a dinner at The Jacksonville Landing, I decided the 2 hour drive back to Orlando could wait til the following day. I decided to head to the Baymeadows section of Jacksonville to find a place to spend the night. I was familiar with that area of town and knew there would be lots to choose from. 
I was able to get a queen bed suite with a full kitchen (not that I really needed the kitchen) for $65 including tax. I was expecting to pay more with tax but was pleasantly surprised to discover the rate. 
The room was clean. The room showed a bit of age but it was still a perfectly fine room. The fridge and microwave looked like they were cleaned after the previous person who stayed in the room left. The television was fully functional, but the cable signal was a bit weak. It may be time for the television to be upgraded as well. The bed was comfortable. My only complaint was they should stow an extra pillow or two in a dresser drawer for those guests that arrive after the front desk closes at 10 and there is really no way to get an extra pillow. 
Overall, a good nights sleep in a clean, comfortable room... I would stay here again in the future. It is a much better choice than the Motel 6 on the other side of I-95 or the somewhat seedy looking La Quinta over there as well.

title: “A great hotel”
text: Stayed here for 6 days in March and found it to be a very good hotel, the location is second to none as you are right in the heart of Broadway, rooms are very clean and the maid looks after the room very well. The Bistro bar attached to the hotel is very good and a great place to people watch, especially when the theatre across the road comes out

title: “Great View and Staff”
text: Stayed for a Business Conference with 400 attendees. Room on 9th floor was jst fine -- had trouble getting into the minibar for snacks and they sent the building engineer right up to fix it! Atrium is a great plus for business conference - keeps you from feeling cooped up all day. Good layout for meetings and reception. Faaaast elevators with a view! Good Parking within the hotel complex - easy access. Truly enjoyed my time at the Hyatt Baltimore -- did not feel like a huge hotel - felt like it was just our conference. Heard one of our guests rode in the elevator with RAVENS Quaterback Joe Flacco!

title: “Not Enough Room to Swing a Cat!”
text:
After a wonderful week in the sister property, Suites at Fisherman's Wharf, Hurricane Irene cancelled my return flight to NJ and the wonderful staff at SFW went out of their way to arrange a room at the Inn at the Opera at a discounted rate of $129 per night. I was clear that I was traveling with a friend, and we definitely needed two beds, or a bed with sleep sofa. Miguel, the manager at SFW, told me he'd spoken to the Inn management and they could provide a rollaway bed. I had been told we had a "Studio" room reserved, with mini-fridge,microwave, and coffeepot. So off we went, excited to be spending 2 days in a new part of town and in a property I'd not seen before.
When we arrived, the staff at Inn at the Opera stored our bags until the room was ready. They told me they did not have an available room with a sleep sofa, or with 2 double beds, but did have rollaway beds, and once again, I stressed to them that we definitely needed 2 beds. My friend and I went off to find lunch and adventure, and came back shortly after three PM to check into our room.
At the desk, I asked about the rollaway bed. The desk clerk told me that, sadly, they had given out the last one, but that the bed would be comfortable for both of us. When I asked why a rollaway wasn't held for us, as the reservation had been made on Thursday, 2 days before, he told us that no matter when it's reserved, it's on a first come, first served basis. After a hurried consultation at the desk, my friend and I went to look at the room, to see if we could survive the next 2 days comfortably.
What a shock when we walked into the room. The bellman who brought our luggage up could barely get all 4 suitcases in the room. The overall room size, including the bathroom, narrow entrance hall, and "kitchenette"(a microwave and coffeeepot on a shelf over a mini-frig, no counter or work space), was barely 160 s.f. There was a full-size bed (measured it...certainly wasn't a queen) and one small 24" round table jammed into a corner with a big lamp sitting on it and a chair in front of it. Other than that and the bed, no place to sit, no room to swing a cat! And even a mid-afternoon on a sunny day, with all the lights on, the room was distressingly dark. Even if I were traveling alone, I would not have stayed in that room. While I've traveled throughout Europe and understand the concept (and size and scale)of a European style hotel, that room was just...sad.
Twenty minutes later I had booted up my laptop, logged onto priceline, and found a four-star (The Omni Hotel, on California St in the Financial District) for $130 per night. I called downstairs for the bellman again, and when I checked out, I asked the front desk clerk where he was planning on putting the rollaway bed if one had been available, and he admitted that they knew there was no place in that room to put one. I think that was the most infuriating part of the whole situation for me. Not only had they misled and outright lied to me, but they also jeopardized the reputation of Miguel at SFW by allowing him to promise something they had never any intention of delivering.
Away we went. Twenty minutes later we were ensconced in a very beautiful and spacious room at the Omni with two queen size beds, a large desk, a table and easy chair, and plenty of light. Heaven, while we waited out Irene.

title: “Small, clean, cheap good location. OK for fun but not for work.”
text:
I stayed at this property for 1 night while visiting Camp Pendleton and needed a hotel near the airport for the outbound flight in the morning. It is 10 minutes from the airport. They do not have their own shuttle. Shuttle service is coordinated through Super Shuttle and/or taxis which are paid for by the property.
 This is a Choice Hotels property, so I didn’t expect much. I stayed in room 409 which is a standard King. The room is small but well kept. From an entertainment prospective, it seemed fine. Good location near many restaurants and bars. Only two short blocks to Fifth Street. 
The room had it’s own, window mounted A/C unit which was noisy, as was the overhead fan which hummed constantly. I shut both of them off during my stay. There was moderate street noise in the room, with an occasional police or fire truck going by. Typical large city noises.
The room has a micro/fridge combo with coffee maker and small sink in the sleeping area. The bathroom is the size of a Chicklet , but was clean. It has a 32” flat screen TV.
