If you’re here for work, like me, this room falls short. The work desk is small and has a horrible chair. There is only ONE outlet for use with laptops, etc. The bed was good but the pillows were cheap and lumpy. The staff was cordial, but not overly friendly. Parking was $16.00 for a surface lot behind the hotel which is not monitored. 
Overall I would give the property a 78/100 and 90/100 for value. 
I would consider staying again, but would also see what else was available nearby.
PROS: Price, location, good value for price bad
CONS: Small rooms, horrible work area, street noise at night

title: “Inexpensive for Downtown Seattle”
text: Very basic but clean room. There is no air conditioning so the window had to be open to cool of the room. Fortunately the room was not on the main street. The location is perfect for downtown Seattle. All attractions are within a few blocks. The monorail is 3 blocks. The staff are helpful.

title: “Great hollywood feeling”
text: Stayed there in November 2011. My first time in Hollywood (which itself is quite dissappointing and nto as glamorous as we are made to believe it is) and it has the perfect location and ambience for what you expect Hollywood to be. Got the room at a discount so worth its money. Restaurants and bars are not cheap but not as expensive as other places in LA and the quality and experience ar top notch. ou might see soem strange things there like Kelly Osbourne throwing a party, male cheerleaders practising by the pool, midgit performers smoking outside, etc. It's all part of the experience. Swimming pool is great, gym well equipped, staff are very helpful and friendly. Had bigger rooms in the States but no complain really, bed was super comfortable. I'd love to be back. A couple of negatives: expensive valet parking but Ithink there is a parking place just across the street

title: “Was given a choice, not sure I made the right one...”
text:
My new employer brought me down for business and I was given a choice of 3 hotels in the area. I chose this one, but I'm starting to regret it. First of all, despite my room being prepaid, they did an additional authorization on my card, and a third card. This has greatly inconvenienced me, and even though the girl looking into it was very nice at the front desk, she never got back to me to let me know if that was resolved. Then, for two days straight I got no replacement coffee in my room, despite calling the first day and letting them know. Finally today I called again and it was brought to me. Tonight, because my room has a kitchen, I bought a bottle of wine. I called down to get a wine opener, and was informed they had "one", but the guy never brought it back". A hotel has ONE wine opener? Really? The dirty coffee mug in the cupboard was just icing on a bad, stale cake.
I'm here for 9 days, and come back regularly. You can bet I will reconsider my decision next time. Very disappointed.

title: “Good value.”
text: Arrive about 8pm, after a long drive from CT, we found this hotel in downtown Philadelphia. Good value, clean and we got a room with a view to the Benjamin Franklin Bridge. Elevators have a lot of space, fast Wi-FI, flat LCD. They also offer continental breakfast but didn't stop by. Overall is a excellent hotel, good value near downtown and in front of the Delaware River, lots of attractions. Free parking.

title: “Checked me out before I even checked in”
text:
I booked this hotel over the phone and one week later, I received a cancellation notice without my approval for the reservation. When I inquired with the hotel, the receptionist told me that their computers were down but that she would re-reserve my room. She didn't seem too concerned though which led me to book another hotel altogether.
An odd occurence but certainly important enough to mention. It would have been awful to arrive at the hotel only to learn that my reservation had been cancelled.

title: “Clean and great location”
text: Room was clean and quiet. No "bells and whistles" but comfortable and convenient to major highways to get to all parts of Jacksonville easily. The hotel is in an area of other high end hotels which adds a lot of security to the entire area. Good for business trip, Mayo Clinic. Not close to beaches.

title: “Nice hotel in good proximity to AU”
text: Nice hotel, reasonably priced, clean, free parking is a major plus. AC in rooms can be a challenge as it is either very cold or stuffy. Wifi while free is inconsistent and generally slow. Overall, more positives than negatives, a good spot to stay in the embassy area, would stay here again.

title: “Location and comfortable room”
text:
This is a very nice hotel with a great location. It is located at the south end of the Magnificent Mile which makes everything in the Downtown Chicago area within walking distance. You can easily shop the Magnificent Mile, walk down to Millenium Park or down to the Loop area. 
The rooms are very comfortable although the sink space in the bathroom is small. There is a nice "Big Bar" area in the lobby where you can get a drink after a day of shopping or meet friends.
We didn't use any of the services but I received a thank you note from housekeeping for my tip. That was a first!

title: “Nice...unassuming.”
text: The Hotel Lombardy is nice place to stay. A different sort of feel. If you like old houses (we do) that have been modernized a bit this place is for you. The kitchen in the suite isn't really a kitchen. A fridge and a sink do not make a kitchen. But the suite was very clean and comfortable. The bar closed at 10pm, which was a bit surprising and disappointing. The location is great. We walked to almost overything.

title: “Wonderful beds!”
text: We stayed here for 3 nights in Oct 09 and were extremely pleased. We had a junior suite on the 14th floor at a good price and were very pleased with the level of comfort, decor, L'Occitane toiletries, bottled Evian each night and the fabulous comfortable King sized bed. The corridors need brightening up but we weren't in them for too long. The staff were very helpful, friendly and polite. We didn't try the breakfast - rather expensive (as was the parking and wi-fi), but went instead to Little Pete's just 100 yards up the street where you can get eggs, potatoes, toast and coffee for about $3. If you need wi-fi you can get it free in the lobby area. A lovely stay, a fantastic city - we'll be back!

title: “Such a wonderful place to stay!”
text: I just love this hotel, very clean and the decor is beautiful! I just love this hotel!

title: “Improved!”
text:
Originally booked a room on the conceirge level, but was later notified by the Taj, that on those future dates, the conceirge level would no longer be open. I was disappointed, but they graciously upgraded our room and provided a $100 a day food and beverage allowance. All staff encountered were excellent! The restaurant and bar/lounge offerings were delicious, and I'm picky....especially when having a lobster cobb salad!
Of course the location is outstanding...the best in the city! So glad we gave it another chance. Won't stay elsewhere, when in Boston.

title: “What a Great Hotel!!!”
text:
My girlfriend and I stayed for a week, at the Barclay. It was our first time in NY and we had a great time. The room was nice and big, great entertainment system, wonderful large bed and fabulous roomservice. 
There is no dobt we'll stay at the Barclay the next time we come to NY.

title: “Lovely Hotel - would stay again”
text:
The hotel was lovely, staff were great, and the roof top view is amazing. Would certainly recommend that people stay here. Bathroom was clean and in working order and decor was fine. Only issue is that it is approx 5 blocks away from the main strip (Lexington Ave) so its a good 5-10 mins walk.
Would look to stay here again in future and highly recommend it.

title: “Perfect Experience at The Time!”
text: We stayed at The Time September 1-4, 2006. When we first arrived our room was not yet available so they took our bags and we went and had lunch. When we returned our room was available and they had upgraded us to a King Superior room from the Queen. Our room was just what we needed. The beds were comfortable, the shower was great and the decor was very fun! The plasma TV was a plus. The overall look of the hotel is very chic. The location can't be beat. You are literally one block from the heart of Times Square. And there are subway stops right there. It is also directly across from the theater that "Chicago" is showing and right next door to another popular theater. If you want tickets to either just talk to the concierge and they will arrange. We even spotted a celeb getting off the elevator! We would highly recommend this hotel to anyone wanting to be in the midtown area. The only complaint is that the 2nd floor lounge was closed at 9pm on Saturday night, which was very odd to us.

title: “Good Location and Friendly Staff”
text: The location of this hotel is good, situated a short walk from Time Square and other main attractions. Whilst the room was small, it was comfortable, clean and of a good standard. The staff were very helpful and friendly. This is an ideal hotel for a short visit to New York.

title: “Exceeded all our expectations!”
text:
Stay at The James! 
The hotel was in a fantastic area - right in the heart of Soho but on a quiet corner, with great convenience to all the best shopping, restaurants, bars, etc. Every single person that works at the James is committed to making you feel at home! We were only there for one night, but they were so accommodating and friendly! The customer service was just great - top notch - I can't say enough about it! And the room was pretty big (we were in a corner suite), and had a fantastic view of the city. We loved the modern, sleek, minimalist decor. The bed was one of the most comfortable beds I have ever slept in! And the rooftop bar, Jimmy - you HAVE to check it out! Drinks are pricey but VERY unique, and the view at sunset is unbelievable! 
We cannot wait to go back - The James has become our go-to hotel in NYC!

title: “Very nice hotel in a good location and fantastic breakfast”
text:
We went to New York for Easter, I was looking at lots of hotels as I wanted to stay somewhere nice and to have a good time. I came across this hotel, they had a special offer at the time, so we had a Club level room with breakfast included. We stayed there for 4 nights and paid about £500 for the whole stay. i believe it was very good price for New York and for such a spacious room.
we liked everything about this hotel except the room was not ready then we arrived at about 11.30 pm, but the receptionist offered us free drinks at the bar while we waited. during weekend room has not been cleaned twice so we had to ask for it which was not really pleasant but i have asked for late check out, so they kindly agreed us stay in the room till 5pm as an opology for the late cleaning.
As I mentioned the breakfast was excepcionally good and pancakes just fantastic!
we had a dinned twice a pasta dished were just lovely.
Overall we had enjoyed the stay there and definitely would go back.

title: “Weekend in NYC”
text: My fiancee' & I came to NYC to celebrate my birthday, and stayed at the Doubletree Metropolitan. The hotel was nice (nothing special about the common areas, rooms, bathrooms) but it was a good price (comparable to other NYC hotels) and had a great location - within walking distance to most mid-town areas of interest. Located right near a subway station, but be aware the subway access is limited on weekends - especially if you are traveling uptown. We had a upper level room so there was no road noise. The room was a decent size (for NYC), the bathroom floor could have been cleaned a little better. But overall it was a good place to stay.

title: “Beautiful, clean, BEAUTIFUL”
text:
My girlfriends from college and I get together for a trip every year, and this year Chicago won out as the city that would be graced with our presence =) We spent a week at the Palmer House and everything, absolutely everything, from beginning to end, was fantastic.
I am a Hilton Honors member and booked this hotel on points (though none of the others did, so this review shouldn't be read as a raving review by someone who gets perks or anything). I arrived early, and upon stepping into the lobby it quite literally took my breath away. It's STUNNING. Check in was very fast, I was able to get into my room at 10:30 am (regular check in is at 3pm) and I was just in awe the whole time. I made it to my floor and eventually found my room (word to the wise...this place can be a little maze-like in the hallways, but with 1639 rooms that's understandable!) the room was impeccable (albeit a little warm) and decorated beautifully. There were some things that seemed outdated though, such as the small-ish (for the size of the room) tube tv and the extremely small bathroom (read: door could not open the whole way or it would hit the tub) the bathroom size may bother people who are a bit larger, as there really is no room to turn around in there or anything, but I am understanding the hotel is also in the works of renovating a lot of their rooms, so I may have been in one that has not been completed yet. 
As part of the Hilton Honors program I had access to the executive level concierge and 'happy hours' if you have access to these do go, it was a great break in the day to enjoy some snacks and drinks in the middle of being touristy =)
Check out was speedy as well, just dial a number and input your departure time and that's it. Nothing to sign or fill out, pretty convenient. 
Room service was very fast, and the food was good, however they do stop service at 10pm. We did request a bottle opener and plates/forks/knives a couple times and they were sent up within 5 minutes even after hours.
I do know they have an AMAZING spa, but I unfortunately didn't get a chance to go =( The fitness center is pretty amazing too, however I don't believe it's free (which can be a turnoff, there are, however, trainers available all the time to help you with your workout, which can be a turn on)
Overall I would recommend this hotel to just about anyone. If you're in CHicago on business it's definitely an amazing place to bring clients, very impressive. The downstairs bar and lounge always had well dressed people having drinks/apps. For families, it's very spacious (well except for the bathroom in my case) and the desk attendants were more than willing to help us find tours, book dinners, etc. Couples will enjoy the romantic ambiance and everyone should enjoy the central location. Both the red and blue line trains have stops within a block of the hotel and with entrances to all four streets surrounding there was NEVER a time where we couldnt catch a bus or train or cab. Loved the Palmer House!

title: “Don't be scared by earlier horror stories”
text:
I very nearly was.
The Allen Lee was perfect for my wife and I. As a poverty line-skirting graduate student in town for a conference, it fit the bill. It's definitely rough around the edges, by which I mean some chipped tiles in the bathrooms and rather threadbare carpeting. However, I didn't see any pests throughout our entire stay. The bathrooms were cleaned daily, and although I was apprehensive about sharing, it wasn't an issue in the least.
After initially booking our stay, I came across the horrendous reviews here on TripAdvisor and nearly canceled. However, like another reviewer recently mentioned, the reviews on hostelsworld are not as harsh, and for the most part a lot more recent. The Allen Lee's website states it recently came under new management, so I'm hoping it has turned things around. We had a great stay. The location is truly unbeatable. If you're on a budget and want to actually stay in DC, the Allen Lee would be a great choice.

title: “My First Trip to Boston”
text: This was my first time in Boston, so I wanted to stay in a conveniently situated place, close to everything...Boston Park Plaza was the best choice. At arrival, the staff were helpful and friendly (most important). When we checked in, we were immediately informed that we were being upgraded to a King size bed on the top floor, which also included free continental b'fast and PM hors d'oeuvre. The room was warm and the bed, extremely comfortable. As well, the bathroom was clean. I would recommend anyone going to Boston, to stay here...

title: “Excellent stay”
text:
Stayed at the Hard Rock ona Friday/Saturday. Room was a Hard Rock King suite, approx $200 night plus $15/night. Overall very happy with the great room, very spacious, 2 large flat screen TVs, great check-in process, quick. Great bar in the room with all sorts of drinks available, and chips and cookies (obviously for $). This is not your average hotel and I am not sure if I can recommend it for regular tourists or older people. Especially weekends, it seems like a party place and even in the rooms there were people partying. Did not get back to the room until 2am and there was actually a fight right outside our door... Called security and they were there in seconds (still not sure where they came from, because they appeared in no time!). 
Great bed. Great bathroom. Great room service. Always addressed in a very polite way by all staff and very often by last name.
Valet parking was $30/day. When the car was brought to us the driver addressed me by name and there was a small bottled water placed in there for me!

title: “In the heart of Japantown! Japanese themed hotel, cheaper than the Best Western Anime on the other street.”
text: Any time I go to Japantown i stay at Hotel Kabuki! The staff is always friendly and have a smile on their face. When it comes to going to the Cherry Blossom Festival, this is THE place to stay! it's in the heart of Japantown, linked to the mall and in a walking distance there's a lovely karaoke bar that we always go to DoReMii!! I've stayed in different rooms here and each one was unique, if you want to go full on japanese style, then stay in the japanese suite, the floor has tatami mats and the bed is the traditional mat on the floor. I love it!

title: “No frills - meets all my needs - amazing staff”
text:
-Staff were friendly.
-Clean, big room with desk, bed, room for clothes.
-Great location.
-Free breakfast.
-VERY inexpensive.
-Quick walk from Amtrak.

title: “Classy and friendly. Great Location.”
text: Stayed here using points. The property was recently renovated and it is a real class act. Impressive building, lovely interior areas and the room was modern, roomy and comfortable. Best of all was the friendliness of the staff. We got the most attentive and appropriate recommendations from the concierge. He was sympathetic to this suburban mom whose daughter wanted to go out clubbing. After making several great suggestions, he could appreciate that a "mom and 18yr old" demographic was possibly not one that would make it past the bouncer. Given that constraint, the concierge still got us to a fab clubbing experience that totally made our stay in NY memorable! Thanks Mr. Concierge (sorry I didn't get your name) and thanks to all the staff at the Marriott East Side. Great Property!

title: “Location, location!”
text:
We spent a week at the Beacon on Broadway at 75th St West, and were surprisingly pleased. The room wasn't big (but you don't spend your holiday in your room), but it was clean, comfortable, had all mod cons, a good view to the west (we were on the 21st floor) and a little kitchenette with microwave, oven, toaster etc so we could save money by getting our own breakfasts.
But the location was the thing. A three-minute walk to the 72nd St subway (the 1 Train to Times Square, one stop to the Lincoln Center), a five-minute walk to Central Park, and good shops and restaurants and cafes all round.
Staff under pressure (are they short-staffed or is the reception desk too small?) but friendly and helpful.
We will definitely stay there again.

title: “Very Deceptive.....Not as advertised!!”
text:
My husband and I booked a weekend away through hotwire and received a room at Dana on MIssion Bay. Once booked, we called the hotel to see about our reservation and found out that we were booked in the old part of the hotel. Apparently, all hotwire customers are booked in the old part. After reading reviews on the old part, we called the hotel and tried to cancel our reservation. We were unsuccessful. Then we decided to give it a chance. Big mistake. Upon checking in, we were coldly greeted by a very unpersonable front desk worker. We asked to see a room before securing the reservation and our request was ignored. We were told that there were no rooms available in the new part. We were stuck. The room was awful. It was small, dingy, and smelled musty. There was no closet but there was an oversized armoire that when opened, allowed no room to walk. The bathroom was dirty (a stain on the toilet) and had exposed plumbing under the sink and bad patchwork over holes in the door. The door frame missing from the bathroom door and the room carpet was dirty. 
Many of the advertisements of this "resort" are likely of the new part of the hotel. We would not know though, because we were stuck in the old part. The night we arrived, we checked in at 8pm. We checked out two hours later at 10pm and again exchanged very few words with the same front desk worker. We received no common courtesies from her like, "Sorry for the inconvenience" or "Is there something we can do?" Oh and by the way, this hotel has no amenities like free WiFi, free parking, or free contential breakfast. In fact, the hotel charging $18/night to park there. Rip off!
So....now it's 10pm on a Friday night and we have no place to stay. We spent 45 minutes calling around trying to find a hotel that had a decent room at an affordable price. We lucked out and found a room in the Old Town area and will be writing a pleasant review for them.

title: “Customer Service Above and Beyond”
text: I have to write that the doormen Felix and Mike were an amazing help today when no cabs would actually agree to take me to a Newark Hotel near the airport. God bless the doormen as they kept trying to help me! I even got into two cabs who kicked me out, one of which took me, thought I was going to the Newark airport and 5 blocks into the trip when he found out I was going to an airport hotel instead, turned me around and dropped me back at The James. Mike was just getting off shift when he went above and beyond by offering the option of commuting with him home to Jersey on the subway/bus and his wife would pick us up at the other side and personally drive me to my destination. Amazing. But it gets better - a colleague named Mimi, graciously gave Mike her car so that he could drive us to Newark instead. Now that's going above and beyond for your clientele. Thank you so much Mike, Felix and Mimi for leaving a very positive impression and actually caring about my predicament :) Much appreciated! It's nice to know there are genuinely good people out there!

title: “I quite liked my stay here”
text:
I stayed here on a recent trip to Philadelphia for family business. 
The hotel is very centrally located and close to most attractions.
The property is old and the ongoing makeover a welcome event indeed. In particular, the carpets and decor are jaded and the room airconditioner noisy and archaic. With a host of business events going on, the lobby and lifts are crowded over most of the day and certainly not the place for a lover of solitude.
That said, I found the staff warm and quite responsive. I got the legendry warm cookie on arrival as expected and was pleasantly surprised to receive one on my departure as well. My son, who had come to see me off, got one too! In spite of heavy occupancy, my request for an extra two hours to checkout was not turned down by the front office manager,Mildred Unger.
There were maintenence issues in the bathroom- a difficult shower handle, a fused bulb and a damaged toilet seat, but these were attended to on each occassion within minutes of my phone call by cheerful engineers and later followed up by a call from housekeeping asking if the job had been done to my satisfaction. My request for a safe deposit box was attended to promptly by Mildred whenever I needed access.
The hotel restaurants were quite dissapointing, the business centre adequate, the concierge helpful and the beds very comfortable.
In this day and age, internet access should be more reasonably priced than the 10 dollars charged.

title: “Was very relieved with our experience”
text:
I feel that I have to stick up for this hotel since our experience was better than expected. I got this hotel through a bid on Priceline before I read the reviews here and I was very nervous about it as a result. I believe what others wrote but I think that the hotel's worst crime is to be inconsistent. My experience was good because I was given a large corner room on a high floor whereas other were given smaller rooms that have still to be renovated (someone has to stay in those rooms if the hotel is full, I suppose). I had very little trouble with the linen service. We had sufficient towels, although washcloths seemed to be in short supply since ours were sometimes taken away without being replaced. We found an offensive looking stain on the down comforter that was between the topsheet and the coverlet. We left a note with the housekeeping about it and it was removed but not replaced by a clean one. That was alright, because we were glad to be rid of it and we just cranked up the heat. We didn't use any of the services mainly because we didn't require it and also to avoid ruining our experience if anything were to go wrong. We did pay $9 to store 3 bags, but that was after a cost/benefit analysis that found it worthwhile for us to pay to store them rather than lugging them around with us on our last afternoon in NYC. Lord knows $9 was nothing after all the expenses we racked up that week. All in all, it was a decent experience. I probably won't stay there again only because I would want to try a different hotel.
For those of you who are thinking of booking here, you might want to assess whether the price you are paying is worth the risk of getting a bad room. I'd say that anything less than $175 is a fair value. For those that have already booked and are now spooked about staying here, I say that you should prepare to be disappointed but you may be pleasantly surprised. Also, it helps to be polite and friendly to the check-in clerk, they're the ones that assign the room. :)
I made sure to take pictures of the entire room. I found none of the things in my room that people have complained about, although I may have just lucked out.

title: “Old world charm and a bargain in New York City”
text: I have been staying at the Belvedere Hitel for the past five years as part of an annual convention that I attend during the Holiday season. The rooms have all the amenities I've come to expect as a business traveller. A little off the beaten path but still close enough to great restaurants and the downtown experience.

title: “Perfect for a theater/dining blitz”
text: Clean, quiet and safe,with outstanding housekeeping and front desk service. 1/2 block off 8th Avenue in a pefectly nice neighborhood. Booked through Traveolcity for a very reasonable price. If you like to lounge around a hotel, this is probably not your place. If you use your hotel as base from which to enjoy the city, the Belvedere is perfect.

title: “Moldy ceiling in bathroom...Hair on towels. GROSS.”
text: The rooms are very outdated and need to be cleaned. There was mold on the ceiling above the shower, little black hairs on all of the towels and in the bathtub. I would never stay here again. I moved to a Holiday Inn Express after my first night. For the same price I get a huge, CLEAN suite.

title: “Accessible, Affordable and Enjoyable”
text: Very nice hotel in convenient location for downtown, old town and airport. Rooms clean, well serviced and above average size. The pool area was a great sun trap with a fantastic view of the bay. Well stocked bar and nice food with mostly good service. The $20 self-park seems steep but that seems to be the average wherever you go in SD! It's realistically a 15-20 minute stroll to 5th (Gaslamp) but its a nice walk and only around $5 in a cab.

title: “Excellent customer service”
text: I went to a conference hosted by the San Diego Marriott so it was very convenient, but I was especially impressed by the great service provided by the staff. Front desk tried very hard to let us check in earlier, the concierge was very helpful in directing us to restaurants, and housekeeping provided prompt delivery of a rollaway bed and pillows. Room was a little small compared to hotels of equal caliber but the view was incredible (I was on the 8th floor) with a small balcony.

title: “Not the best choice while staying in San Francisco”
text:
While the room rate is moderate, not cheap, the Metropolis hotel is not a viable choice when staying in San Francsico. The hotel is worn, desperate need of updating, much like the neighborhood it reside within. The hotel staff is pleasant, but I found the rooms to be in need of a deep cleaning, meaning shampoo the carpeting, dry cleaning the comforter, and addin screens into the windows (who ever heard of a hotel with windows that completely open so that children or anyone could jump out of? Weird!). The hotel has one elevator that can accomomdate three persons comfortably, you can imagine if someone has several bags with you when you get on the elevator, very cramped. Sometime you wait for 4 -5 minutes to get out the hotel, depending on which floor you reside.
Then there's the neighborhood...I grew up in Detroit, Michigan, so I know what inner city life can be like. Frankly, I was shocked that I was harassed by small gangs that hung out near the hotel. More over, it's the climate of San Francisco that attracts homeless and wandering youths, not the hotel fault, but why not have someone at the door on the street to watch out for their guests? Simple solution to help the guests feel safe. But apparently, common sense is not a forte of this property.
Also, I was really shocked that when I booked my room, the hotel charged me for the entire stay on my card, normally, I would expect one day charge to hold the room and charge the balance of the stay upon CHECKOUT. But this was not the case.
Bottom line, there are many alternatives to this property, you owe it to yourself to investigate all of the alternatives in the area before booking at the Metropolis.

title: “Romantic Resort”
text: My husband and I stayed at the resort just for one night and wished we were there longer. The grounds are beautiful with the mountain view. The staff was great. Dining at T Cook was romantic and the food was great. If you want to be catered to, this is the place to stay. I cannot imagine anyone going here and having a bad stay, even if you do not interact with the staff the property is so romantic, beautiful and clean.

title: “Amazing!”
text:
I stayed here for 1 night over the weekend for a friend's birthday and was blown away by how nice the hotel was! 
My stay at the Hotel was great. The staff was very attentive to our party as we all flew in for my girlfriend's birthday. For me this is still the IT HOTEL where all the young and on trend people hung out, specially in LA where the competition is stiff. 
Breakfast was fantastic....I enjoyed the hotel; overall it is a nice place to stay. Rooms are so cool!!! And what woman would object to their room being stocked with amenities?? 
I recommend this hotel!!!

title: “Fantastic Hotel!”
text:
My husband and I chose this hotel after lots of internet research, since this was our first trip to L.A. This was just a great place to stay for several reasons:
First off... LOCATION LOCATION LOCATION!! The location was ideal, because we planned on visiting Universal Studios, and we were also attending a taping of a sitcom at Warner Brothers Studios in Burbank... the hotel was a very short drive from both of these. In addition, it took us less than 10 minutes to get to Hollywood from there too, and the freeway access was quick and convienent! LAX was about 45 minutes in good traffic, same with Santa Monica pier.
The staff were amazing! When we checked in, I mentioned that the reason for the trip was to celebrate my hubby's recent 40th birthday, and we received an immediate room upgrade. We also weren't charged for parking for our entire 4 day stay, but to be honest, I'm not sure if his birthday was the reason for that... during the massive storms in L.A that started half way through our trip, the power went out in the hotel one day (not for very long), so perhaps we received free parking because of that inconvience... but regardless, it was a $14 per day savings, so we weren't asking questions!
The pool was open and very well heated, and the surroundings were lovely.. well treed. The rooms were spotless. The only "negative" I noticed others pointed out was that the rooms don't have in room safe's but we had no issue with this, we simply locked our belongings in our suitcase. 
Would I stay again... without hesitation!!

title: “Just like home”
text: Our first time in SF and were recommended this hotel. Fantastic location. Friendly staff. Breakfast sets you up for the day and complimentary hors d'oeuvres and wine went down a treat. Decor like old English. Large room with lots of facilities. Quaint elevator.

title: “Location, Location, Location!!!!!!!!!”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Boston Harborside Inn for three nights in December 2005.
If you are taking the "T" in from Logan International, you can't beat the convience! You just take the blue line from the airport and get off at the
aquarium stop. As soon as you leave the "T" station, you are standing right outside the Harborside's door!!
I had read in Trip Advisor that the rooms facing the street could be noisy because of the bar next door.
Because of those reviews we booked a room in the 
atrium instead. It was very quiet and comfortable.
The furniture are Early American reproductions, and combined with the original brick walls, gives a very unique, historical effect to the room.
The only negative aspect about the room is the back of the bathroom door had a large hole in it, as if someone had slammed their fist into the door. However, there were notices in the hotel that they were remodeling and perhaps they hadn't gotten to replacing the door yet.
The desk staff were not overly friendly, but were helpful if you asked direct questions.
Quincy Market is only a few minutes walk away, and the hotel is also a very close walk to the court house and finacial area.
For the price and convience, I heartily recommend the 
Boston Harborside Inn.

title: “Excellent hotel at an excellent location”
text: The best hotel you can get in Seattle at an excellent price. Premium location with premium room facilities. Very friendly and helpful staff. Get the panorama view rooms on the corner and you will enjoy seattle at its best. Not a cheap hotel but worth every penny for those who want to relax and have a nice stay in seattle after a long shopping day.

title: “Good and Clean Hotel, Perfect Location”
text:
The Novotel NY Times Square is centrally located in Midtown Manhattan. That makes it very convenient to many attractions and shops.
The staff is helpful. I never had to wait for an elevator. The view from the 29th floor is great. I could see the space shuttle pavilion on the USS Intrepid Museum ship. The room was very quiet and the bed of excellent quality.
I didn’t use the restaurant because there are plenty of possibilities on that position which help you learn the local “eating culture(s)”.
Four subway locations serving different metro lines are very close (1 or 2 blocks walking). That will help you travel to every place in New York in a short time (for example to Penn station to make a one day trip to Washington DC). And Grand Central railway station, it’s a 15-20 min walk from the Novotel. 
I got what I expected

title: “Business hotel in a good location, but no frills”
text: If you're looking for a small, intimate boutique hotel for your trip to New York, this is definitely not for you. It's a very large hotel with two bars on the ground floor and a cafe. I'd recommend eating at the deli across the road on 53rd if breakfast is not included in your deal -a simple coffee and pastries costs $19 plus tip in the hotel's cafe. The hotel as a whole looks like it needs refreshing - the rooms are a good size, and kept clean by the housekeeping staff, but they're dated and basic. The minibars have been taken out, and there are no coffee machines. It will cost you upwards of $14.99 a day to use the internet in your room, and it was disappointing that the staff didn't tell me that I could use the wifi for free in the lobby. The hotel is in a great location - one block to 5th Avenue, six to Central Park and three to the subway. I didn't love this hotel, but it was clean and in a great location, and when asked for advice, the staff were helpful.

title: “Hotwire rates this a 3.5 star - No way!”
text: We booked this hotel through Hotwire. My mistake and it won't be repeated. In hindsight it seems reasonable that only the bad hotels use Hotwire. A good one wouldn't need too. If you aren't booked or can cancel go to the Handelry. Similar price but much better facility. If you are booked and can't cancel then bring your ear plugs. It isn't that this hotel has no redeeming value, it provides free robe and slippers, a nice mini-bar and nice hotel staff Although I think they were tired of all the complaints they get. As I was checking in folks were complaining and when I stopped by to see if they had closed the window in my room that was stuck open they were complaining. When I checked in I called to see if I could get a quieter room and was told it was the nature of their hotel to be noise, which since it clearly was I said thank you, put my ear plugs in and went to bed. There are two main problems with this hotel. The old (and cracked in my room) single pane windows do not cut down on the noise from outside. I book a hotel for a good nights sleep so am not too concerned with room size. The other main problem I discovered when I wanted to take the stairs for exercise. The old fire escape stairs are a death trap in an emergency. They are narrow enough that only one person could go down them at a time with no room to pass or get around someone who has fallen without stepping on them. I never thought of checking this type of thing at an old hotel before as I often take the stairs for exercise and have never seen anything that looked as potentially dangerous as this. Other random comments. The room was reasonably clean but clearly to a one or two star standard (plenty of dust and dirt for those who looked for it). Sears fine food across the street is over rated.

title: “Rude Staff, Ugly Rooms”
text: Yes, the location is great, but the staff is terrible. They are very rude and treat you like you are an idiot if you ask a question or don't know something. This was my first time to chicago... and just a head up if you have never been parking is 41 PER night t.... The furniture is very chipped and in rough condition, looks like something that can be found at Goodwill for $20. Wifi is 10 PER computer in your room which was frustrating to me because we stayed two nights so they managed to take another 40 dollars just for me and my boyfriend to be able to use our computers. There is no breakfast and of course, when I asked the lady at the desk looked at me like I was a complete idiot and told me to go to a cafe. WOULD NOT RECOMMEND. I stay at hotels often and this one is at the BOTTOM of my list.

title: “Everything you can expect from a budget hotel”
text:
My dad and I had visited New York in 2006 and because we both loved it so much, we decided to go again. We were looking for a simple hotel with low prices and chose Hotel Newton.
The hotel was everything you can expect from a budget hotel, nothing more, nothing less. The room was simple, but clean and tidy. The bathroom looked good (renovated?) and the bath/shower combination was excellent. We slept well and since we only stayed a few days and wanted to spend as much time as possible walking the streets of NYC we really didn't need a luxurious hotel.
The only possible downside of this hotel is it's location. It's located at 96th street and this is quite a bit outside the heart of New York. With the excellent public transport however, I did not feel this was a significant problem.
Overall I enjoyed may stay in Hotel Newton. It wasn't special, but considering the low costs I was very content.

title: “AWFUL! STAY AWAY!”
text: Horrible and rude service. We booked a non-smoking room and when we got there the room had clearly been smoked in for years. When we tried to discuss this, the office denied anyone had ever smoked in there and told us there was nothing they could do. They also accused us of smoking marijuana in the room. (Do you find it a little ironic that we had issue with a smoke smell and their response to it is to accuse us of a smoke smell?). Very difficult to deal with, the place was extremely dirty as well. Don't even get me started on the stains on the towels, walls, and doors. Ugh.

title: “above my expectations, too good to be true!!!!”
text: Everything was excellent, When every I have to go to LA again, I know where to stay. I super loved it!!!!! service, location, price value is excellent!!!!!

title: “Rooms need a renovation (from top to bottom)”
text: Staff are great. Lobby area has been renovated and is fine. Has a nice small gym with new equipment. I have stayed here several times in several different rooms and there is no other way to put but say the rooms are subpar and need to be totally renovated. I will say it is primarily because of the bathrooms and closet but the rest of the room is in a "old' condition as well. You can expect shower curtains not only in the bathroom but also to cover your closet door?? (give me a break). If you don't get a suite the room will be tiny. There is no suana or steam room or pool. The owners are going to have to up the ante and spend a lot of $$$ if they are going to keep up with the near by competition. But then again, this is a Holiday Inn brand property which always pales in comparison to Marriott or Hilton and there are other boutique hotels in the area which are far superior.

title: “Home Away From Home”
text: I lived in Fort Worth for 15 years (now in Pennsylvania), so my wife and I come back often to visit friends. Staybridge is like our mini-apartment...but even better, because they provide breakfast everyday, dinner (with beer and wine!) on Tuesdays through Thursdays, our room cleaned daily and a paper on our doopstep. The hotel is very "new" feeling, close to everything, and attended by friendly staff. Once we retire, my wife and I may just stay here for a couple of months to get away from the Northeastern winters! Great place!

title: “A good, typical Holiday Inn”
text:
We stayed in this Hotel for what turned out to be six nights in July 2012. It was pretty much what you would expect from a Holiday Inn. Average, no frills, ok quality.
Our room was clean and comfortable. All the Staff we came in contact with were very helpful and cheerful. Especially the Reception and Bar Staff. The Reception Staff helped us out when we asked for a different room (no reason other than we decided we preferred a King bed rather than two doubles as was previously given to us). We also asked for a higher floor and they obliged. The Bar Staff were chatty and friendly and we felt welcomed into the Bar. The Bar itself, we found was a little odd. We couldn't put our finger on why, but decided that it looked a little like a play area rather than a bar because of the decor, but that was a minor thing and we enjoyed a drink or two in there after a long day sight-seeing. The food in the bar (we ate one evening) was very good. The breakfast buffet was average and ok.
The Hotel had a bit of a Business feel about it. There was a conference on, so it may have been because of that. The pool (which we didn't use) looked a bit scruffy but was better than nothing.
The Hotel is close to Bus stops, so getting about is cheap and easy. 
There are a couple of reasonable Restaurants and a Supermarket within walking distance, but that is about it. Everything is a bus/taxi ride away even down to the main part of Georgetown, but we didn't find that a problem as the buses were cheap and we also discovered the circular bus and the open top bus both dropped us in the vicinity we needed to be to get back to the Hotel. 
Overall, I would recommend this Hotel for a basic, reasonably priced, friendly, no frills stay.

title: “Very nice time here at the Sheraton Crescent”
text: We came for an urban resort getaway. This hotel has nice facilities and a wonderful staff. Margarita in the lobby Starbucks makes a mean cappacino. We were pleasantly surprised by the facilities and access to equipment. Racquet ball, tennis and basketball plus a slide for the kids at the pool. The only negative is that the immediate area the hotel is located is unfortunately very boring.

title: “A fantastic boutique hotel in the heart of Midtown Manhattan”
text: I stay at the Muse on a regular basis for business. I LOVE this hotel. The location is fantastic. Close to Times Square, Central Park, Rockefeller Center, Bryant Park, Broadway theatres and all of midtown Manhattan. The rooms are a really nice size by NYC standards and the beds and beyond comfortable!! As with all Kimpton Hotels, there is a complimentary wine reception in the lobby every evening. The staff at the Muse are extremely friendly and helpful and the bar/restaurant in the lobby is great. The hotel is very modern, hip and stylish. I cannot recommend the Muse enough.

title: “Excellent location”
text:
Comparing this hotel to the White Swan, where we usually stay, this hotel has the better location. It fails in other comparisons, leading to its lower overall ranking. The breakfast here is quite adequate, but you may find nowhere to sit in the small parlors at each end of the third and fifth floor, where the breakfast is served. Trays are provided so that you can take it to your room.
The room itself is small but adequate. It lacks the finer ammenities such as a refrigerator and fireplace, but otherwise is clean and comfortable. Our room at the back was exceptionally quiet, while the front of the hotel faces busy Post street. One peculiarity is that the bathroom in our room was up two steps, a hazard in negotiating trips to and from the bathroom in the dark of the night.
Internet is free and fast. It does have the annoying feature of requiring a sign in on a very regular basis.
Overall, a very nice boutique hotel, less expensive than, but having fewer ammenities than the White Swan. The location right off of Union Square, not far from the BART, makes up for most of the differences, and this is a good choice for where to stay in the city.

title: “Great, great choice!!”
text:
We booked on-line,so sight unseen when we booked. The staff were helpful and friendly, the location could not have been better.Rooms were funky and very comfy. We were walking distance to Union Square, tour busses, cable cars, lots of restaurants. Lots of little stores for emergency supplies,like Gin and Tonic!! Altogether a fabulous trip, we would go there again in a heartbeat, thanks
Joanne and David Parkinson
 Richmond, B.C.

title: “Great Stay”
text: This hotel is perfect! Great location, beautiful room, fun restaurant and friendly, helpful staff. I can't wait to go back and stay here again. The pedway is under the building with shops and restaurants so even if the weather is bad, you can go "out" and stay comfortable. The building has a beautiful gym, pool, business center and a lovely park. I can't wait to stay at the Blu Agua again.

title: “Pretty good but not perfect”
text:
I have stayed at the Westin a couple times of the past couple year it also was the site of my companies holiday party the past 2 years. It is generally what you would expect from a Westin; great quality, up to date and clean. Two complaints: First the Westin Georgetown is NOT in Georgetown, near but not in so the name maybe a bit misleading . Expect a decent walk or a short cab ride to visit destinations in Georgetown. 
The second complaint stems from one bartender working my companies Holiday party at the Westin. Generally the service is phenomenal at Westins, this one bartender in particular was the antithesis of that (I wish I got the guys name, I would have filed a complaint against this guy), he was very rude to everyone his rudeness came up in party conversation it was so bad, him poring you a drink was like he was doing a favor for you.

title: “Great place to stay for a weekend downtown!”
text: We were in Houston to see a play and wanted to stay downtown. The hotel was located about five blocks from the theaters and the streets were well-lit. The hotel offered a free shuttle but we wanted to walk. Just down Texas Street are several excellent restaurants, and the downtown train is about a block away to take you to many more very good restaurants. Don't miss the pool and hot tub on the roof. Both are small but it is very unique to be at the pool and be part of the Houston skyline!

title: “After Much Anticipation...Just Satisfactory”
text:
I'd been wanting to visit D.C. for a while, and had been eyeing staying at the Hotel Monaco for sometime. So when my husband was asked to attened a convention in DC, I of course had to tag along, and was happy that the Hotel Monaco was on the approved lodging list. 
The hotel is very hip and stylishly decorated, so I really loved the decor. We rarely saw any other guests, nor were the staff in the lobby overly friendly, so most of the time it felt like we were the only guests at the hotel.
Upon check-in my husband was told that we had been upgraded to a larger room, but strangely enough it was located in the lower level/basement of the hotel. Walking through the hallway I did notice that the other rooms were smaller, though a few doors that I saw open (cleaning time), but still. Being in the basement was a little strange. We didn't want to risk being moved to a smaller room, so we didn't complain. Fortunately for us, it wasn't too bad. There were four windows in the room (two were frosted for privacy) and we just had to make sure that we kept the curtains open to let the natural light in.
The bathoom was huge, and you could probably fit six people into the shower! We loved that the showers had two huge showerheads, and that we were able to use the animal print robes in the room wardrobe. The toiletries were also amazing, and there were ample towels.
Wi-Fi was free because we joined the Kimpton club, so that was not a problem. But parking was horribly expensive at $38 a night! Other than that, I only really had two issues. One, since the basement is enclosed, the air in the hallway doesn't circulate. I know the hotel is pet friendly, and so at times it did smell like wet dog. There were large plug-in type air fresheners located throughout, but they were still not enough. Two, the first day our maid serviced our room, it was pristine. But the cleaning services seemed to deteriorate as the days went on (we were there a week). Nothing was filthy, but the lack of attention was noticed.
The Penn Quarter neighborhood is amazing. There are several shops and restaurants within walking distance, and it is a busy area, so we never felt unsafe. Several tourist attractions are close as well, and we never needed to take a bus, cab, or metro anywhere, even though stops for all were nearby. So while I wasn't 100% happy with the hotel, the location more than made up for the hotel's shortcomings.
I would go back or recommend to a friend, but only if they were going for business and being reimbursed, or found a really good deal, because again, it's pricey.

title: “Not so hot. Disapointing service. Little long in the tooth.”
text:
The two young men running the desk when I checked in at night were too busy being goofs to take care of the customer. They had no interest in providing service. The second evening I was there, I stood at the check in desk for 10 minutes to buy a bottled water. The two same young men were having such a good time together in the back room that I had no one to pay and finally gave up. 
The rooms are a little long in the tooth. They are okay but not what you would expect from a Marriott property.
The young woman running the desk in the morning was attentive. She went out of her way to be nice to the guests. What a difference between the day shift and the night shift. 
My advice; if you must stay here, check in early and check out early and avoid the two BOZOs!!!

title: “Disturbingly filthy and outdated”
text: This is by far the worst hotel I have ever stayed in. Ive traveled plenty for business and leisure and have not encountered such a disgrace. I chose Crown Plaza because it was on my comany's recommended list for hotels near LAX. Ill be sure it is removed ASAP. Not sure how they get away with the stained carpets, peeling wall paper, stained bedding, broken TVs and layers of dust. (see pictures) Im also unsure of the integrity of the good reviews on this site. My coworker and I booked 2 rooms at full price, direct on the website, not on priceline for $60 like many other unhappy guests who commented on TripAdvisor. Apparently there are some remodeled rooms that they offered to priceline customers for a higher fee according to some reviews. Even though I paid full price for my room I was not offered that option when I spoke to a manager about the condition of my room. I was offered free drink tickets and free breakfast but that doesnt make me any less freaked out about sleeping in filth. Out of desparation we ate in the restaurant of the hotel which was also poor. Our food was cold and tasteless. On top of that, they didnt even honor the drink coupon I had because it wasnt beer or wine that I ordered. (in fine print of course). It was too late in the evening to find another hotel and we were flying out early in the morning. I barely slept and stayed fully clothed until it was time to check out. It would have been tough to sleep with all the teenagers running up and down the hallways anyway. As I left my room at dawn, I saw the lovely room service tray of half eaten food in the hallway that had been sitting there when I checked in the day before...as old and crusty as it was when I arrived. A perfect ending for this nighmare of a stay.

title: “Great location for a fun night on the town”
text:
Ideal location, courteous staff (ask for Innocent- he knows EVERYTHING there is to know and do in the DC area) and clean rooms. Just know that parking is impossible
In this area! The hotel provides valet though

title: “Great stay! Fairfield Inn shows they are improving!”
text: In Charlotte for the weekend to visit family and we choose the Fairfield Inn based solely on reviews posted here. The rate helped make the decision easy. If all Fairfields were as nice ad this one I would stay more often at this Marriott brand. The staff was great, hotel was very clean and you could walk to a few choices of restaurants. Overall great weekend stay.

title: “Absolutely wonderful hotel”
text: This was our first time staying at the Silversmith. What an absolutely wonderful experience! The staff could NOT have been any nicer. And 'real' nice, not 'business' nice. The rooms were so clean I was absolutely comfortable walking barefoot (how many hotels can you say that about?). The high ceilings gave the comfortable rooms an even more spacious feel. The decor was classy and sophisticated, yet still comfortable. My husband and I stayed there for a week along with our two small children (2 & 4) and it was such a great experience that we were all sad to leave. The only thing that wasn't absolutely perfect was the view from the room. We looked out on a very nearby building's fire escapes. But that really is a minor detail. We will definitely be staying at the Silversmith again. I would highly recommend this hotel to absolutely anyone and feel completely confident that they would enjoy it as much as we did.

title: “Good place to stay”
text: My wife and I dropped in on the Tuesday night before Thanksgiving. We got a great rate and package by asking at the front desk. Location was great because it is so close to the 16th Street Mall. Room was solid nothing amazing. Great View.

title: “WOW! Great people, great service, great view, great experience!”
text: The people rock! The bellman who greet you are so very, very friendly and helpful! The concierges helped us tremendously...we loved Christopher! We had issues with getting Sears tower tickets from the Sears tower group and he was "on it" from the start. He was relentless in his pursuit of our happiness and kept following the issue until even after we checked out. The people taking reservations were very personable, the waiter in the restaurant was right on top of it and even the housekeeper was very nice, very professional and very pleasant. Alls I can say was WOW...great job!!

title: “What you expect from Marriott”
text: We stayed here for NYE. It was about $300 after all the taxes. This was one of the better rates for the night. Room was great. No fridge in the room, a big negative. Could not keep our leftovers from dinner cooled. Service was great. Parking very convenient. Great location

title: “Nice trip, but be forewarned....”
text:
My husband, two small children, and I stayed at the Pier V recently as part of the Harbor Magic, Spring Break Getaway package. The package included 2-3 night stay, 8 breakfast passes to the hotel restaurant, and 3 tickets to the Port Discovery Childrens Museum. Here are my thoughts.... 
Hotel--
First, the hotel was clean and comfortable and has a evry interesting look, and the staff was very helpful and accomodating. They had a nice crabby hour where you can sample a nice crab dip and have wine, beer or soda. My complaints were 1) that our tv remote didnt work,and we called 3 times to ask that someone fix it, but it was not addressed until the last night of our stay. 2) the cleaning service was not good, ie we would see wrappers/debris still scattered on the floor after the room was "cleaned"., 3) the room we were given only had one bed, EVEN THOUGH WE TOLD THEM WE WERE A FAMILY OF FOUR AND WANTED TWO DOUBLES. (After complaining at the front desk, they bought in an air mattress but I was still kind of irritated by this. The kids were fine with it though). BE FOREWARNED: there are big $$$ tax and occumpacy fees. We payed nearly $60 on tax and fees PER NIGHT..Ask about the costs of these to avoid any unpleasnt surprises...Plus PARKING IS $21 PER DAY. No free parking options available. Factor this into your budget.
Hotel Breakfast passes --
The food was good, the service, not so good. On day one, there was s a long wait because the place seems understaffed. The next day, it was better, no doubt because of complaints. BE FOREWARNED: Go early (before 9) or expect a good wait.
Activities--
The package came with 3 museum tickets. Ypu can buy extra tix in advance. The kids had a nice time (they are 8 and 5), but they were only entertained for about 2 hours. They loved the jungle gym - that's the main attraction.The rest was not that interesting too them....
We also purchased (in advance) tickets to the Acquarium. This was a bit of a disappointment. BE FOREWARNED: The 3D showed scared my children. If you have small children, SIT NEAR THE AISLE SO YOU CAN LEAVE EARLY IF NEEDED. The dolphin show was nice but over so fast you hardly felt you saw any tricks. GET THERE AT LEAST 15 minutes early if you want a good seat. Also, if you go to the acquarium on a Saturday, there is a long line, so if you are sure you want to go, buy tix in advance to avoid the line.).
Lastly, we also purchased (in advance) ESPN zone tickets. This was okay as well, but really the games are geared to older kids than mine so we didnt get much benefit out of it. BE FOREWARNED: DONT buy tix in advance because they are pretty easy to get once you are there, and if you dont use them they are NOT refundable.
Overall, nice trip, but much more pricey than the benefits we received. I can say Ive been to the Harbor, but not likely to go back anytime soon.

title: “A very comfortable stay!”
text: The Langham is a very nice hotel to stay at if included in your tour but over priced I feel if you have to pay! Arrivd in about 10pm and could not get anything to eat other than room service which was disappointing. had to go out and pay $98 elsewhere to have some dinner. Breakfast was excellent! Location Ok ..near Macys but not near the best shopping like the Prudential Centre. Close to the harbour and Legal Seafoods which was a good restaurant.One of the few hotels I stayed in in a month without free wi fi.

title: “Much better than anticipated.”
text: We ended up here as a result of "pricelining". read the reviews at trip advisor and thought this didn't sound much like a four star (what we had put in for our priceline bid). we were particularly concerned because, at the moment because of physical limitations, we need a walk-in shower, and priceline is pretty minimalist about what needs you might expect to be met (you pretty much get a basic double and take your chances). I called and spoke with the desk clerk: I'm so sad I didn't get her name because she was a doll. I explained my need and that the reservation had been made via Priceline so I knew she might not be able to help. Instead, she said she'd find me an ADA accessible room at no additional cost. When we arrived we found she had put us in a deluxe double queen size bed room with a marvelous walk-in shower, far more luxurious than we anticipated. I know this hotel is on the strange side (no id on the outside, weird dark halls offset by a gorgeous inviting atrium) but the staff couldn't have been nicer and I am grateful.

title: “Good location”
text: Across from the street cars and a bunch of restaurants. Only a 5 min street car ride to the heart o downtown. Free breakfast was ok. Some hot food.

title: “Great Location”
text: Excellent location, subway very handy. Staff helpful. Room and bathroom good size. Only issue we had was the cost of breakfast in the dinner. Be warned, very expensive, didn't make the same mistake twice! Luckily there is a Starbucks in the hotel also which was great. Would stay here again but elsewhere for breakfast.

title: “Brilliant stay, good hotel!”
text:
Our first trip to New York and it took us forever to pick a hotel, we chose this one because of its good reviews on trip adviser. Needless to say we were not disapointed! 
The hotel is in a brilliant central loaction a stones throw from Macys, a couple of minutes around the block to the Empire State building (we opted for a city view room which was on the 28th floor and had a fantastic view of this building), and a comfortable short walk to NY Pen station numerouse metro stations and many other atractions are just a short stroll away. Close to a number of good restaurants, bars, cafes and shops. Perfect base to explore the city.
We chose a City View King room, the bed was comfortable, the bathroom and shower were a good size. All the usual amenities were provided and worked well, hair dryer, iron, tv radio alarm, lamps, fridge, microwave, intenet, coffee maker with quality coffee (regular and decaff). The air con could be a bit noisy but as we went in February we didn't really need it on but bet it would be a god send in the humid summer and you would get used to its dull hum. Most importantly it was all clean!
The staff seemed helpful and polite, we were able to check in a little earlier than their website showed without any hassle. I was made up that they allowed us to store our luggage free of charge on the day we checked out as we had a late flight.
We can't comment on the restaurant at the hotel as we ate out or brought take-away back to the hotel, it looked nice but was a little on the pricey side for us.
All in all we had a brilliant honeymoon and would recomend this hotel to anyone!

title: “Hotel Awesome”
text: I normally do not respond with a review; however, I had a total of 4 rooms booked for my family and I for 6 nights. What a wonderful experience we had at this hotel. I have stayed at many Starwood Hotels and this is one of the best hotels that I have stayed at to give you EXCELLENT customer service. The staff was just absolutely wonderful. They made our stay away from home like we were home. You all rock!!!. Hotel and location was perfect. When we come back to NYC we will be staying at this location. Definitely a thumbs up!!!!

title: “Very clean and convenient”
text:
We stayed over five nights at the beginning of July. It was very hot but the room had a window airconditioner that kept us cool. The room and bathroom were immaculate. The hotel was very convenient to transit and was a little out of the way of the major traffic corridors so it was quiet at night. Construction on W. Broadway started promptly each morning at 6:45 a.m. 
Lots of places to grab a quick snack or a good meal in the neighborhood. The staff was very polite.
Would stay again!

title: “Great Location!”
text:
I was not very familiar with the area, so I didn't know what to expect. My husband and I were going to a concert at the Hollywood Bowl and decided to take one of the bus shuttles from the Chatsworth Metro Link Station. (Which, by the way, is an absolutely great way to go the concert!) The hotel is less than a mile from the Metro-Link Station. The room was very up to date and spacious. Check in was very fast. We ordered breakfast from room service the next morning. It came on time and was very good. 
If you're ever going the the Hollywood Bowl or anywhere in Chatsworth, I definately recommend this hotel.

title: “Sleepless nights but perfect management”
text: We were alerted to the fact that the hotel was right over a bar, but were assured by the desk clerk that no one could access the hotel floors from the bar stairs or elevator. However, the first night, we were awakened twice by drunken patrons screaming (once at 1:30AM and again at 3:30AM) and the second night, we were awakened at 7AM by the bar staff dragging patio furniture around in order to put up Christmas decorations. We were incensed, and each morning, told the front desk that they needed to rectify the problem. I was assured that the manager would call me when we returned home and take something off the price. When I didn't hear from him, I wrote an impassioned email, outlining the problems, and he responded immediately by phone, offering to reimburse our stay in full. He also invited us to come back in future for a night as his guests. Although the hotel really needs to do something about their relationship with the bar, they are clearly aware of the problems and are trying to fix them. I applaud the management for their generosity and sense of duty.

title: “Very good place for solo traveler, clean and pleasant”
text: Good place to stay, clean room, stayed there in single room and got much more that expected. The room is not so small and very comfortable. Very close to time square and in good location that close to everything. Very recommended.

title: “Just mediocre”
text:
My best friend and I had never been on a road trip together. We decided to do something within driving distance from home. She had her mind made up to stay at another hotel that was not as close to downtown. In some ways, I wish we would have. The only reason I was glad she changed it, it was close to Beale Street! The pictures online are NOTHING like the rooms. The pictures show green bushes in front and there are flowers there now so this tells me that the pics are when the hotel was much newer and nicer. She noticed there were four lounge chairs in the pictures online so she called and asked if there were more LOUNGE chairs and they said yes. Well, that was a lie because there are FOUR and one was broken. She called back after making the reservation to ask for a refrigerator and microwave and they told her she could do that at check in; we arrived to check in and she asked for the fridge and microwave or if our room had it and the girl said I will have to see if we have one. She never gave us an answer as to whether she did or not. We got to our room to find the carpet ancient and looked like it was shredding and had been stretched a million times.very dark blue and nasty. The beds were not as they were described or looked in the online pics but not too bad in the way of comfort. We noticed rooms with the doors open when being cleaned and they were a lot nicer than ours. They did not have a lot of people staying there so why they chose to give us the crappiest room, I will never know. The cleaning people are very noisy in the hallway talking loud amongst themselves and take a long time to complete the rooms on the floor. Most cleaning people I have seen are quiet, clean the rooms and figure they can go home when they are finished. These people must get paid by the hour because they are so busy talking, they are there until four in the afternoon. We did a hear TV up full blast early one morning and people at the pool at times. The filters in the pool were not on and my friend cleaned it herself. There was hair and crap in the pool and no one ever came out to clean the actual pool itself. There was a guy coming around sweeping and checking the pool deck but not the pool. We never saw anyone put chemicals in and it didn't smell like they had any chlorine in it.
The pluses are the hotel is close to Beale, some of the staff are very friendly, the price is great, there is a parking attendant but two nights out of three, the guy was literally asleep in the booth! That would have made a great pic-Kodak moment.lol
If you don't mind an old hotel and you are just looking for an economical way to go to Memphis, this would be fine. The breakfast they talk about is bagels and danishes with juice according to what we were told by the front desk. There is NO cereal. We asked. Also, there is an iron and ironing board in the room. If you want a hair dryer, you have to ask at the front desk and they do have them.

title: “Great hotel great location”
text: Stayed weekend recently at this hotel. Very clean rooms. Great beds. Super club floor lounge. I had 3 kids under 8 with me and they loved the n/c breakfast and snacks in the lounge. Well located hotel close to times square and many attractions. Efficient friendly check in. Reasonable priced hotel. Will stay here again.

title: “I won't be coming back”
text:
I stayed longer than a week at the TG over the summer, and I won't be going back. If you're in town for business and you need your full eight hours, don't stay here, particularly over the weekend. The noise was so loud on thurs, Fri and Sat nights, we had to ask to be moved from the 5th to the 8th floor. And STILL it was too loud!
We ate in the restaurant and drank at the bar. Staff in both places had serious attitude, as though they were way too cool to be working there, really. A bottle of wine was bought was corked and tasted awful. I asked for it to be replaced and the barman looked at me as though I had two heads!
The door/bell staff are nice, except at the weekends in the evening: because the bar is quite popular, they have a bouncer on the, and if you're not dressed head to toe in black, or maybe look as though you might be under 21, he is very rude and aggressive 
MY big issue was attention to detail. Given the prices paid in that hotel it should be paramount, but small things happened: no replacement of toiletries in the room; gym equipment was broken; gym water cooler wasn't filled; no towels in the gym; bedroom furniture was chipped and battered; a cupboard door was broken; a drawer was stuck and wouldn'y open; TV VCR doesn't record (and the TV is way too small, by the way).
That said, the management was very responsive to my complaints. The assistant manager I spoke to was very solicitous and concerned, and he did his best to make up for it. Still, I'm not going back.

title: “Great location”
text:
We have just had a great four night stay at the Library Hotel. The hotel staff were superb and had great recommendations for places to eat. The hotel has a library of DVDs which you can borrow. 
The room was well presented and maintained. However, it is noisy at around 3am when the bin men are in the street. We would therefore strongly recommend ear plugs for a good night's sleep. 
We found the hotel to be very well situated for both shopping and sightseeing.

title: “I liked the location”
text:
Many hotels in mid-May 2007 were full due to conventions and graduation ceremonies. The result was that I experienced 3 different hotels during my 6 day visit to Washington DC. I stayed in the Carlye Suites Hotel, The Washington Court Hotel and the Washington Suites Hotel Georgetown. Each had advantages and disadvantages.
The Carlyle Suites Hotel.
Of the three hotels I preferred the location of the Carlyle Suites, situated in New Hampshire Avenue, a pleasant tree-lined area comprising good quality residential properties and second tier embassies, but only 5 minutes walk from the Dupont Circle metro.
Room 306 was clean and adequate in every way, whilst lacking the luxury of the Washington Court’s furnishings. But Carlyle offered a better range of TV channels.
Pillow was extremely comfortable whilst bed verged on hard. I was disappointed to find that the well-furnished kitchen did not provide the basics of coffee, tea bags or creamers. Bathroom on the other hand, consisting of shower but no bath, had a reasonable selection of soaps, shampoos and towels. The supplied ironing board was so small as to be virtually useless.
Staff were correct, but matter-of-fact and not overtly warm. Their knowledge of how to reach Adams Morgan was vague. Its not complicated. Cross the road into Riggs Place, take first right onto 18th Street and keeping walking for 10 minutes. 
A good buffet breakfast was served in the hotels very attractively decorated restaurant. Buffet breakfast was only marginally less varied than that provided in the Washington Court but the sausages were tastier. The restaurant appeared deserted in the evening.
A good choice of restaurants is available 5 minutes walk away in the (overrated?) Dupont Circle, and 10 minutes away in the much livelier and more varied Adams Morgan area.
Free of charge, unsecured wireless internet worked well from the room
In all three DC hotels I found the bedside lights to be user-unfriendly. If you wake up in the middle of the night one does not want to fiddle around searching for the switch with risk of damaging or knocking over the lamp. Hotel interior designers – please note. 
Would I stay again at Carlyle Suites? At equal prices I would chose the Washington Court Hotel. At 30% discount to Washington Court I would go for the Carlyle.

title: “Wonderful experience”
text:
On August 22, 2010 we checked in to the Westin Philadelphia for the American Assoc. of Zoo Keepers annual meeting. Upon driving up to the enterance Adrian Johnson politely greated us and after check in he delivered our things to the room, answered all questions and we thought that was it. Not so, later Adrian gave us great restuarant recomendations. And on a passing in the lower lobby valet area my wife indicated that a few extra towels etc. would be nice. He said house keeping would bring them right up. Five minutes later in the room a knock at the door and it was Adrian with the requested items. He said house keeping was too busy to get them to us promptly, so he delivered the goods. Adrian Johnson did truly go out of his way to make our stay at the Westin a great visit. Our room attendant Lisa was also great.
I have traveled to zoological conferences for the past 34 years and never had such great service and friendly treatment.
Rich Freitag
Dir. Marketing and Sales
Central Nebraska Packing, Inc.

title: “Comfortable and a great location”
text:
Great location if you're staying in mid town and want to be near Central Park and Fifth Avenue. Small, intimate - definitely no "chain hotel" feel
I've been coming here for a number of years now and always find the staff here friendly and helpful - check in always goes smoothly and you're in your room in next to no time.
The standard rooms are more than big enough (and I usually bring my bicycle!) and have great beds / linen and curtains that really shut out the light. Comfy armchair, large workdesk and free wifi complete the picture
Bathroom only has shower but its a great rainforest-type shower. Noted that its an industrial design but nice amenities and towels along with the shower are what's important.
Had breakfast for the first time since the restaurant changed hands - definitely worth trying! Small but good menu (good breads) at decent prices
Had to stay elsewhere when full but if there's room, I always stay at Chambers!

title: “Pre visit customer service”
text: Okay so I have to confess that I have not stayed at the hotel yet, however I thought I would add this as it is useful for those considering staying here. Given allofo the negative vies here I contacted the hotel to explain that I was worried about my stay, I have to say that the hotel called me back and eased all of my fears. Not only did the lady update me on the state of NYC as we speak but she was also willing to listen to my reservations about staying and promised a face to face encounter when I arrive, at which poitn she will taje care of my stay. To be honest I dont think that you can say fairer than this and I am now looking forward to my stay at the hotel and hope to be able to come back here in a couple of weeks and tell you all just hopw great it is!

title: “Enjoyed a Wedding and Reception at the Magnolia”
text: What an excellent value and choice in Downtown Denver, with breakfast buffet, Happy Hour and late evening ice cream and cookies. Clean, well appointed room, great location, close to all the Downtown sites.

title: “Great Value”
text:
The Hudson is a great value. The rooms are small, but the location is great. The hotel is clearly for the young hip single crowd but my family had a blast at the 
Hudson. We were able to walk to several locations spend the day sight seeing come back refresh and hit the exciting streets of NY again. I booked on priceline and was worried after reading the reviews of the small rooms. It worked out great, the rooms are clean, the staff is outstanding. All in all I just wanted to stay in a location close to Time Squartes, near the broadway shows we were going to see and the Met. The Hudson was perfect.

title: “Adequate”
text: This is a grand old hotel with prices to match. I have status with Hilton so between that and the cost/overall vibe of the hotel, I was expecting a pretty great experience. The service and room were fine, neither exceptional or poor. We probably could have gotten a better deal through a 3rd party booking site, but then you lose your reward points. Also we were able to get tickets to the Shedd Aquarium (less than 10 minute walk) by booking with Hilton, and those normally retail at $35.
