I guess what you want to pay depends on your reason for travel. I'd be inclined to try a different Hilton next time though.

title: “Upper class”
text: The name itself tells you that you are visiting a piece of history. Elegant, sophisticated and one of the best locations in Manhattan. You are right in the center of things, both for business and pleasure. Old world charm, mixed with modern facilities. We rented a suite and had a fantastic living room with fire place and a separate bedroom and bathroom. Ample, comfortable and elegant. Service is 5 stars and the facilities are excellent. The only thing that bothers me a little is the amount of people in the lobby as it is full o visitors and onlookers, but this is the price you pay for being a New York visitors attraction on its own right. This is one of the 5 hotels I would recommend to stay in New York if price is not a real consideration :)

title: “Wonderfull W”
text:
We were in a wonderfull room with a city view,it was spacious and much like the pictures already available in other reviews here.
Because it was november,there seemed to be no activity in the pool area but it's as nice in real life as it looks in the pictures.
Theres a night club right up at roof level that was very busy when we were there as was the bar down at the ground level.
Service was very good and with a smile all the time.
I liked breakfast in the main restaurant downstairs.Very tasty! It doesn't look like a W there but other parts like the lobby and main bar are very W in style as is the welcome you get when you check in.."So what is going on in Dallas this evening?" That seems to be the question everyone was asked.
The hotel is near enough to many bars and nice restaurants such that you would be able to walk to them.
Incidently whilst there was a hip and party like athmosphere and a young feel to the clientelle at the hotel when we were there.We did not experience any hassle with people going wild in the hallways or general rowdyism at all.Everything was very pleasant and a good nights sleep was had.

title: “Beautiful but not hospitable!”
text:
My whole family came in on a Sunday around 3:30 and we had to wait until 6:30 for our room to be ready when check in time is 4:00. Nothing to say but, "sorry". Finally, when we were able to get into our 10th floor room, it was hot. The a/c was on, but the room stayed hot. At 12:30am in the morning my husband went down to the lobby desk to complain. They gave him a box fan! It did help, but again, nothing but "sorry". The pool was very dirty and unclear. I hated my kids swimmimg in it, but how do you keep 12 and 13 year olds out of a pool on vacation. Again, we got "sorry". 
Our last morning there we checked out and the parking bill was horrible!! 26.00 PER NIGHT!! We stayed 3 nights. You would think that with the 3 hour wait for the room, 80+ degree room, and dirty pool, we would have gotten a little break on parking or breakfast.
FInally, I must say the hotel lobby is beautiful and classy. We were hoping to have seen the famous ghosts, but nothing was seen or felt. Also, the BEST part of the hotel was meeting Marc the bellman. He was a true gentleman and a pleasure to meet.

title: “Classic Art Deco in the Heart of the Theater District!”
text:
I love this hotel. This was the second time we'd stayed there and it is a favorite, to be sure! A small lobby for check in, wonderful staff. The lounge upstairs is a great place for people watching after working hours or late night. Their restaurant downstairs is quite excellent, although I think if you're in New York you should get out of your hotel for dinner.
You are in the heart of all things theater and only a block or so from Times Square.
The rooms are VERY spacious for downtown NYC and have every amenity you need and don't. Perfect little wardrobes, mini bars, full length mirrors, it's all very high end. The bathrooms are extremely luxurious and, I know this sounds weird, but the toilets are rather decadent. That's all I have to say about that, you'll see what I mean when you stay.
The spa and pool are beautiful and I thought the masseuse that I had was world class. This hotel combines a retro New York City feel in a charming and warm atmosphere, all while letting you know that this is a full service, luxury property and whatever you need will be delivered.
Love it.

title: “I stand loyal to the La Quinta hotel chain”
text: My family and I have a small dog. We love to travel with him and La Quinta is one of those hotel chains that offer a great price and do not charge for bringing your pet. It's not a luxury hotel, but it's clean, the staff is friendly, and there's free breakfast. This time we stayed in the Deluxe Suite. It exceeded our expectations. There was separate living area which allowed my kids to watch tv and hang out. We have been here many times and we will definitely return again!

title: “Excellent Customer Service”
text: I've been staying at the Adophus Hotel in Dallas, Texas, every summer for the past 10 years. Beautiful hotel with excellent customer service!!!

title: “First Class All the Way!”
text:
The Orchard Hotel is a first-class surprise! Located in the busy Union Square district of San Francisco, it's close to cable cars, shopping and lots more. A special tip of the hat to Cornell the doorman, who smoothed out a small problem with car parking with ease and aplomb! 
I've stayed in pricier hotels on Bush Street and elsewhere in SF ... 
but the Orchard beats them all! Nice breakfast buffet ... and as a sign of an active hotel ... lots of people in the bar area on a Saturday night! The rooms are spacious - I had a room on the top floor ... and a great San Francisco touch .. I could hear the clinging of the cable car as it went by! Just a friendly place all around!

title: “EXCELLENT SHORT STAY”
text: Stayed 1 night pre cruise last month and had a great stay. Caught the BART from SFO, walked out at Powell St, turned left, walked 1 block and there it was.....very handy for our weary bodies! Room large with good view, 2 king size beds, very clean and lovely reception. Very handy for both the Union Sq shopping and the tram....always a must for the SF traveller! Would definately stay again.

title: “Park the car and put on your touring shoes!”
text:
We stayed here for three main reasons. One, the location doesn't get any better. You are right next to Ben Franklin's grave site and Independence Hall etc. is a three minute walk. Two, my son learned about Ben Franklin in school and really admires his accomplishments. Three, the rooftop pool is really cool. The views are beautiful and the pool was clean and sparkling. My boys loved it!
The hotel room was clean and inviting. The bath and beds made my wife very happy. The breakfast was a little pricey, so after one day we hiked on over to a great little coffee shop for the first meal of the day.
Old Town has many amazing restaurants, so be adventurous. A neat place we went to was called Raddichio ( about three blocks away ). It's a bring your own bottle place that doesn't charge you a corkage fee. Great homemade Italian. Campo's has the best philly cheese steaks!
Don't miss the Duck Tour either.
We stayed for three nights and we still didn't see all that Philly had to offer.

title: “A let down”
text:
I am just going to be honest here; I just do not get all of the positive reviews. I think the only "five" I could give this hotel has to do with service. This is not a bad hotel, but there is nothing great about it. It is probably my least favorite hotel in the immediate downtown Indianapolis-area.
Yes, I understand that this hotel is a historic building. My issue is that “historic” is not an excuse to allow a hotel to look worn and shabby. Both the Omni Severin and Canterbury nearby are old, yet (even with actual small rooms) the places have been recently remodeled. With Indianapolis hosting the Super Bowl one would think all of the hotels would step it up a notch, not the Crowne Plaza!
The staff at this hotel is great. The valets, front desk staff, and the older man offering assistance from a podium by the front door could not have been friendlier or more helpful.
Location wise, while this hotel is a bit further south than some others, it is convenient coming from the south. Since the hotel is located as far south as it is, you do not really deal with the congestion and one-way street issues encountered at other hotels. (Just drive up Illinois and take a left immediately after you emerge from under the viaduct.) I liked the location because of the proximity to Circle Centre Mall, Pan Am Plaza, restaurants, and the highway. It was easy enough to walk to Monument Circle from this hotel for our group. Sure, there are hotels closer to everything, but there are worse “downtown” locations, too (by the canal, up by IUPUI, way east- all of these are considered downtown but are not as close to the action). We used the valet service to park our car, but self-parking at Pan Am Plaza was just north of the hotel. (I was not really fond of the hotel not having its own self-parking, but since the location is what/where it is, that is how it works. The cost at Pan Am plaza varies based on events happening downtown, which is not necessarily at issue at hotels with their own parking.)
We stayed in a “normal” room (#277), not a train car room. The room itself is the usual size and overlooks the pool. It has a normal-sized bathroom, two double beds (no way queens would fit unfortunately), a small table to hold a suitcase, dresser with a stone top & a flat screen TV, and a small table with two chairs. I would say that our room was on par with your typical Crowne Plaza/Holiday Inn room size, amenity, and set-up wise. You can tell this is not an older hotel, just an old building converted into a hotel (no tiny bathroom, tiny rooms, etc.; as you will find nearby). I thought the bed was comfortable. I also appreciated that it was double sheeted.
The reason I give this hotel poor marks is because of obvious issues:
First: This hotel needs to be remodeled. If the owners/management company is not prepared to do that, then it at least needs a good cleaning and sprucing up. Sorry but I find caving in tub surround tiles, rusty drips, peeling wallpaper, gunk around the bathroom door stop, dirty windows, stained dust ruffles, broken switch plate covers, etc. unacceptable. It just tells me that with some TLC this hotel could be great. Instead, it’s not. I would not put this on a level with hotels that are dirty, but it is not really that clean either.
Second: This hotel needs some soundproof windows. I needed to keep the fan to the climate control system running to drown out some of the sounds around the pool. I can not imagine what rooms on the first floor are like. On the second floor, we constantly heard people around the pool. There are things that can be done with windows to lessen the sound transmission. Unless you stay up late and wake up early, I guess try to avoid any of the rooms that overlook the pool.
Third: I could hear everything in the rooms above and next to ours (on the bed side of the room). All morning I heard the people upstairs talking, their kid running around, toys pushed across the floor, laughing, etc. At night and the next morning, I could hear the people next door. In the bed closest to the bathroom, I could hear our neighbor in the bathroom. Not cool. The problem is, I do not think that thin walls & floors/ceilings are fixable in a remodel.
Fourth: The bathroom is at the level of an old Holiday Inn. Peeling and ill-fitting wallpaper, plastic counter top, tile walls around the tub caving in, etc. Totally fixable. Actually, with some serious cleaning, tolerable. Instead, barely clean but not competitive with other hotels downtown.
IF this hotel is remodeled I MIGHT stay here again. Otherwise, I will probably avoid it. For $25/night more, we could/should have stayed at the Marriott. It is a bit further west, but it is a much nicer hotel. If I could get this hotel really cheap after a remodel, I might just bring earplugs and try to deal with it. Nevertheless, probably not. If this hotel was not priced similarly to other, nicer, more recently remodeled hotels, I might say the value is better. There is not enough that is redeeming about this hotel to make me want to stay there again. I would not recommend this hotel to friends staying downtown either; I would direct them just about anywhere else.

title: “Great Hotel-Great Price- Great Location”
text: The hotel in right in times square. You can walk to all the major attractions within minutes. My husband and I stayed at this hotel for our anniversary, and we loved it. I will say that I am a verrrrry picky traveler. If I arrive at a hotel and its not up to par, I demand a refund. I read thousands of posts on hotels before I visted New York, so I was prepared for the small rooms. Although the rooms were small we still got a great bang for our buck. The hotel was clean. And it was nice to come to a warm room because its freezing in New York in December, we just basically left the heat off most of the time and turned on the air when it got too hot in the room. I will say one minor negative thing, some of the hotel staff at the front desk are pleasant, but are NOT very helpful in explaining things. I believe they need to realize that not everyone who vists the New City is from another major city, so a little extra detail in giving directions and when recommending things to do they could do a better job at.

title: “Great Hotel !!”
text: We didn't have a reservation, but they had rooms for us. To my surprise, the rate was reasonably great due to the fact that this hotel is fairly new. Very modern with internet access. The rooms were better than expected. Besides the bed being very comfortable and a nice flat screen tv, they also had a lounge area with an L-shape sofa, nice desk area, microwave, fridge, coffe maker, separate toilet room from shower. Nice breakfast! Friendly employees. I would recommend this hotel to all my family and friends. Also nice area with a walmart next to the hotel and a target a block away. Very close to Sea World is a plus!!

title: “VFM and great location!”
text:
My wife and I spent eight nights here in April, 2007 and thoroughly enjoyed ourselves. The hotel is very conveniently located for the many attractions of Fisherman's Wharf and only a five minute walk to the cable car terminus. The cable car (which is a San Fran "must") takes you right into the heart of the shopping area centred on Union Square. Indeed the cab fare to the Square was only $8 so for four people (we were joined by our daughter and son-in-law on day 3) this is the better deal.
The hotel is all that you could wish for - spacious room, queen-size bed, cable TV, ironing board/iron, complimentary tea/coffee etc. Add to that the inclusive continental breakfast and you have a bargain. The hotel's warm cinnamon buns are to die for! 
Built-in ramps for those with wheelchairs etc figure in the lobbies on each upper floor and I cannot honestly think of any negatives. We would certainly stay here again if visiting San Fran once more.
Do visit Alcatraz (but book in advance), Ghiradelli Square and Pier 39. We also enjoyed the open-top double decker bus tours and our tour in a World War II DUKW.

title: “Old world elegance with modern conveniences”
text:
I travel to New York frequently on business and stay at the Waldorf as often as possible. The rooms are quite spacious (especially by New York standards!), well decorated, and comfortable. I adore the food---the cheesecake is not to be missed--and the service is top notch. A few months back, room service somehow lost my order; within minutes of realizing their mistake, the Waldorf had sent up the kitchen manager to personally apologize and our entire meal was comped (with extras thrown in). 
Overall, one of my favorites in New York.

title: “Nice, clean and friendly”
text: My husband and I booked a weekend at the Hampton Inn Arrowood so we could go to Carowinds (without the kids!). We were also looking for a romantic getaway so we booked the King Jacuzzi suite. Overall, the hotel was very nice. It was situated in a quiet business park area, with trees and nice landscaping. It was just a few exits from Carowinds; very convenient. There was a Ruby Tuesday's restaurant across the street. The front desk staff was friendly and helpful. The lobby has a seating area with leather sofas, decorated in a wild animal theme - which was the decor theme throughout the hotel. Beyond this was a large room which overlooked the pool area with tables and chairs for eating breakfast. Our suite was very large! It was essentially an apartment. The room was clean and the beds were very comfortable. The pillows had a down feel. The bathroom was enormous! We were disapointed with the jacuzzi tub, though, it was not as large as we had hoped. It was essentially a large bathtub with jets, not meant to accomodate more than one adult comfortably. Not like a "hot tub". The shower had good water pressure and a massaging showerhead, which we appreciated after being jostled about on roller coasters earlier in the day. The breakfast was your standard help-yourself "continental" with bagels, muffins, juice, etc., and they did have some microwavable omlettes and stuffed biscuits (think Hot Pockets). The whole breakfast area was very clean, and the staff was busy making sure nothing ran out. Overall we thought it was a good value, and we would stay again.

title: “Good quality, comfortable hotel”
text: My partner and I stayed here two nights recently on a business trip to LA. The staff were helpful and friendly and our room was very clean and functional, albeit on the small side. The room was well appointed, good quality furnishings and excellent wi-fi connectivity. A bath tub would have been nice but the rain shower was a nice touch of luxury. I would recommend this hotel to anyone wanting to do business in West Holllywood area.

title: “Filthy bathroom/entryway floors.”
text:
My stay at this hotel started with great promise. The checkin was extremely friendly, the location is better than I expected for the price. And, if the room were hygenic - it would have been a good value, with the free breakfast and all.
Unfortunately, the entryway and bathroom are done in white tile. And it looked like they hadn't mopped in weeks.
I called down that morning to ask them to mop the floor. Okay - perhaps a maid made a mistake, and the last folks in the room were messy. That would be forgivable. At that point, I would have been happy with a cleaned floor.
Came back after an afternoon of museum-going and shopping - and the floor looked exactly the same. I called the manager, who said "We've got new floor tiles - I've got 3 complaints about this so far today. It's part of the tile pattern, it's not dirty." (Do most people buy white tile that LOOKS dirty? Or skillfully installs so that bootprints line up on multiple tiles?) I asked her to come up. She wiped her dry finger against some of the stains, and pointed out that no dirt was on her finger - and that was "proof" to her. They told me that they'd try to mop it again - even though they kept saying that the floor was not filthy-dirty.
I waited for a half hour, just to see what they did when they mopped the floor - but I had to leave. I never saw the maid again. She may have come when I was away - I don't know. But the floor looked the same when I returned.
My first call to Hilton to complain was met with a telephone operator who insisted that, if the manager wouldn't help me, there's nothing she could do, and refused to register my complaint. I called the special "Silver member" line (which I am), who at least took my complaint seriously - but would not offer anything other than to email management.
I really didn't feel like I could take a shower in the morning and touch that tile floor. So much for my weekend trip. I cut my weekend trip short and drove home that night.
The funny thing? This was a "rewards" stay. Intended as a special gift for loyal frequent business clients. This is a reward that I would rather not have had.

title: “Good quality but over priced”
text: I really enjoyed the lobby but hey it's the bed you there for. And the bed are great with really nice pillows. Staff was great, ambiance was wonderful especially around the duck marching time. The lobby was crowd most nights we where there with a nice bar in the center. Hotel is In the heart of downtown so you can walk to most places with Beale street being our primary destination. Lots of good music and okay Bar BQ.

title: “My go to accommodation in San Francisco”
text: My first stay at The Phoenix was in the summer of 1992, and have since continued to make it my first call when I am in town. As always, from reservation to close out my experience was delightful due to the professional staff maintaining a high standard of the property. I have recommended The Phoenix to all my friends visiting from abroad and have heard positive comments about their stay. Keep up the good management and I will see you on the next trip.

title: “Holy Crap!!! Don't stay here!”
text:
We travel quite a bit in the summer with a softball team, and I will admit that I have had to tolerate some cruddy hotels because there was no where else to stay - this hotel far surpassed anything that I have ever seen in my life!!!
A group of 16 of us traveled to Detroit for the OSU v. Michigan game. We chose the hotel because we thought it would be nice to go to MGM Grand Casino (MGM actually told us about the Ramada!) on Friday evening. 
The rooms were very old and needed upgraded terribly. One room was missing it's TV. One room had broken windows, and when we told the front desk they asked if we would like more blankets!!! Are you kidding? It was 24 degrees outside that night. You have no control of the temperature of your room, the drains don't actually drain properly, and there were bugs. Maybe some of this doesn't sound all that scary to some, but the elevators aren't exactly quick to come to your floor, but for God's sake DO NOT ENTER THE STAIRWELLS. They were dark, smelled of urine, and had graffti all over them. We ran for our lives down those stairs!! (I wish I had my pictures developed to share!)
Drugs seems to run rampant in this hotel. A man that was clearly a junkie jumped on the elevator with us gnawing on some cold leftovers that looked like he found them in the trash - this was at 6:00 a.m.! There was a vacant room next to ours that had no door handle and wide open that was obviously a place that squatters frequent all the time. 
I could go on and on about the horrible things that we saw, but figured I would just give the highlights. 
I am very disappointed in the Ramada chain, they should tear their names from this building!!!!

title: “Wonderful.”
text: My experience at this hotel was nothing short of first-class. The room was clean and well tended to, the location was prime, and other guests were respectful and courteous. What made my stay excellent, though, was the service the employees provided. Tyler, a front desk manager, was kind and such a delight to speak with. He exhibited customer service skills that you rarely see in this day and age. He made me feel welcome, and was always more than happy to help when I had a question. I will be returning next time I am in town in hopes to see him again!

title: “Good value”
text: Nice atmospheric place. Rooms do not have a sink/bathroom so one should be aware of that, but the shared facilities are quite clean. Check-in only possible in the afternoon, after 2.30, which is quite late. However, there is a luggage room to store luggage.

title: “Arrogant staff and rip off”
text:
The moment my wife and I walked in with our backpacks we were given the once over look by the staff at reception as if we weren't good enough for their hotel. And no we were not poorly dressed.
Perhaps I should have reminded them they are a mid range hotel at $140 a night and not anything above.
The room we had was a dogbox and the smallest I have ever stayed in. Breakfast???? So they call serving a few muffins, pastries and fruit breakfast?? I don't think so.
Then to top it off our room rate jumped from 140 to $389 per night for the same room all because there was some stupid conference on in town. The hotel thought it was a great opportunity to rip us off obviously and did so.
A few weeks later I returned to San Francisco and needless to say I stayed elsewhere.
I passed on the thought a dogbox room, snobby staff and being ripped off again.
They think they are better than they actually are.

title: “Stay away!”
text:
The room smelled of mould and urine. The smell seemed to come fron the A/C-unit The bed was awful and gave both of us back pain. The wall paper had come off the wall and there were cracks in the walls. 
When we complained about the nasty small, they did not at all seem suprised, but gave us a room on the 3rd floor. That room was a lot better, even acceptable.
Staff was not very friendly.

title: “Not business friendly”
text:
The hotel wifi is virtually non existent in the room, my wifi hot spot barely works in the room, and the ethernet cord for wired access is not accessible from the desk. All of which makes its difficult to work from the room.
There was no room service menu in the room, and the Wall Street Journl was not available from Room Service.
I have to think the majority of the Hotel's traffic would be business travelers, but they don't seem tuned into to making it easy to work on business at the hotel.

title: “Excellent location , fancy lobby, good security”
text:
We stayed in this hotel during April. There are two entrances for the hotel , the smaller one is next to the Hershey's candy store. The other one is on the back and it's the car entrance.
Once in you take electric stairs up to the lobby. About five people will help you through reservations in peak hour. The bar is just in front of the desk and it's got nice atmosphere. It gets crowded at nights.
We stayed on the 25th floor, side views (not to Times Square but to the side of the buildings) so nothing fancy to comment. The room was clean and the beds were quite good. There was no free internet so thats a downer. 42inch LCD screen but no connection panel (you couldn't connect the laptop to the TV).
Location is great , at least three subway stations nearby, close to the tickets booth for Broadway shows and excellent security, they required keys at night to let you through the lobby.
There are several diners nearby , the one to the left (an italian) is a little bit expensive, but other than that , it's fine.

title: “Great T ime”
text: I found this site after I had booked a week long stay at the Time Hotel and with a disabled husband I was very worried, but I have nothing but praise for the hotel and its staff everyone from the doorman up was kind, friendly and very helpful, the room was clean and cleaned every day, we arrived at 1pm and where informed that our room was ready and we checked in. As to the last comment about a $a a bag at the last hotel we stayed in New York we were charged $5 per bag. We plan to go back to NY next year and will stay at the Time

title: “The most bare bones of the bare bones but no bare bone price - props for cleanliness”
text:
This hotel is perfect if all you're looking for is: 1. location 
2. a place to stash your bags while you do whatever it is people do when they have business between the hours of midnight and breakfast.
3. Require no more than a short catnap between "assignments".
4. Have traveled enough to know how to handle aggressive panhandling.
Bottomline: If forced at gunpoint to stay in this area (hopefully not as likely to occur as a glance out the window in this neighborhood would suggest)- then this place looks by far to be the best option for lowering your chances of various bedbug, roach, and other inner city nuicances. Still quite overpriced for what you get, i liked the parking options and it seemed clean enough..especially when in contrast with the surrounding couple of blocks. The staff was also pretty friendly and if it were a good $40 cheaper I would have given it 5* for value for money (granted I was here during peak summer season so i may have to take another look during lower season).

title: “Fun place to stay”
text:
The Indigo had a very cool vibe, everything was bright & beachy. We stayed in a regular 2 bed room & it was a weird layout with the beds facing each other, but I can appreciate odd things like that after staying in a million hotels that all look the same. 
The room had a fridge & a microwave which came in handy. Also loved the Aveda products they have. 
The front desk ladies were very nice and helpful with recommendations. One of them even printed out a bunch of restaraunt menus & coupons for us! 
The hotel taxi will take you anywhere within 3 miles for free which worked out great for us. We found out taxis in the Dallas area cost double what they do in New Orleans.. kinda crazy. Maybe because Dallas is a lot more spread out. 
We did not use the valet as there was a parking lot a block down that cost $4 for 12 hours. We could see the car from our room, it is a safe lot. 
Only downside was with the 106 degree heat & the wind that we felt was more like a hot blow dryer... we wanted to jump in a pool asap... which the hotel didn't have. 
Overall, I would stay here again- no extra charges, staff was nice & helpful, within walking distance to food, bars & art museums- Sounds good to me!

title: “Nice Hotel, Disappointed in Room”
text: We booked same day for a Saturday night out in Houston. Booked a Queen Bed. Got the "Crews Quarters" room on 2nd floor overlooking pool. Everything was nice but room was very small. Had a small full size bed. Talked to front desk. No other rooms available. Manager called me and said we must not be used to their custom queen size beds. Back at room looked at mattress dimensions on tag (53" x 74.5"). Don't appreciate being lied too or misled. Could have ruined our trip but night out in Houston was fantastic and pool watching was great.

title: “Old Elegance”
text:
First, my suggestion is to get a cab or bus to the hotel. It's a walk uphill from the Dupont Circle station, and it's longer than it appears.
The hotel itself is pleasant enough. The lobby is smaller than a standard hotel lobby, so if there's a lot of people checking in, things go slowly. 
I have to echo another traveler's point: the elevators are SLOW and SMALL (think European style). However, there are two of them.
The room itself I got (single king size bed) was larger than a standard hotel room. There's a table against the wall that can serve as the desk, though I should note that the chair is slightly too low which makes long working uncomfortable. There was a small alcove at the other side of the room where a mini-fridge and buffet sat. The TV is a large, flat panel and is very new - nice.
The bathrooms are another story. Mine was about 6 ft by 10 ft and the door didn't completely open - it was blocked by the toilet, which sat directly next to the sink. The shower/tub was okay, but the tiles and grout looks as though they needed to be replaced. Be prepared for a very small bathroom.
One other thing I noticed was that I couldn't set the Thermostat to "Auto On" - either it was on, blowing cool air, or off.
Positives: Great bed, larger than normal room
Negatives: Small bathroom, noises from the hall (LOTS of noises), desk/chair not good for long periods of working, vending/ice machines alternate floors
- Airline executive staying on business

title: “Relatively Affordable, Modern and Clean, Accommodations in Boston”
text:
This is a very nice place to stay in Boston. Get your walking legs and your Charlie Card ready though, because it's a few long blocks to the start of the Freedom Trail from the Newbury Guest House, but that just gives you something to look forward to at the end of a long day when you want some peace and quiet. The Newbury Guest House was extremely quiet. We could barely hear any room to room noise and little street noise.
The rooms are very well decorated, with modern tones (think Ikea), nice lighting, very nice bathroom fixtures and equipment, a safe and mini frig in the room, and all very clean.
The breakfast included with the room was first of all unexpected, but perfect. It's not continental but buffet with eggs and bacon, some toast, cereals, teas, coffee and juices, and all with real plates and utensils, no Styrofoam waste.
My only comment to folks is to not expect a bellhop to whisk your luggage up the entrance stairs and to your room. This is a very low frills hotel from those kinds of services, but perfectly acceptable if that's not your expectation.

title: “Great Theater Hotel”
text:
I was in NY for work and this is a convenient hotel to my office, but is great for going to the theater in the evening, heading over to 9th Ave for some nice restaurants, or people watching in Times Square. (A plus is the half-price ticket booth is just 50 years away.) I took a cab into town from LGA so I don't know how much parking is at the hotel, but the cab is about $30-$35. The lobby is on the 8th floor, and they handle a huge volume of people and do so fairly efficiently. Times Square is a noisy place, but the room start I think on the 11th floor, and you don't hear much of the noise from the street. (They may also have additional sound proofing.) The room is a decent size for NYC, and the bed was very comfortable with a nice bathroom (including a tub). 
If you don't like big crowds, this is NOT your hotel. If you want to be in the middle to things and a lot of action and excitement, it is a fun hotel and a nice oasis in the middle of Times Square to escape.

title: “Great hotel but eat elsewhere”
text:
Terrific location, adjacent to Logan. One side of rooms looks out over the water to downtown Boston, the other side overlooks the airport; you can spend a lot of time just gazing out the window on either side! Despite being close to the airport, the rooms are fabulously quiet. Clean and modern, though some puzzling things missing (example: no towel racks in the bathroom). Excellent beds.
The dining option, though, was a big disappointment. Dinner was slow to arrive, food was cold, some items were forgotten on a special salad, and the meal was pricey. Breakfast was good, but VERY expensive. It's a great view, but I'd eat somewhere else.

title: “Not What We Expected”
text:
This being our first time to NYC, my boyfriend and I really wanted to stay at a nice place. We were there from July 5th to July 10th. This hotel being in an "ideal" location and looked very nice, we were sold. Upon arriving we were pretty impressed. Our room looked nice, the service was great, I even boasted to my boyfriend how great of taste I had. Unfortunately later on he would have the uper hand. The first night we found out how noisy it was. You heard perfectly the people showering above us. We can't really complain about the noise outside as it IS NYC, but I do not recommend staying on the Lexington St. side. Going through our room and walking down the hall, we were really let down. The wall paper in the halls were peeling, and the siding was falling off of the wall. Our room had water damage and beside the sink vanity looked like it was never cleaned. *we got that taken care of after 3 calls*. Our large lamp also did not work, and even after the housekeeping lady tried it infront of us, it was never fixed. Also, the ice machine and "vending machines" which was a single pop machine was the scariest site we both saw. Located in a dark, dirty room by the service elevators and janitors closet, there was garbage, old mops and broken equiptment everywhere. I definately did not go back and made my poor boyfriend make that "lovely" trip. Our "anti-slip" tub was anything but after my boyfriend took a nasty spill and still has the lump to prove it. Please get the bathmat offered if you call. Though the room service was friendly, the food was HORRIBLE. We had breakfast one morning, and then went to the restaurant the next, and both were very bad experiences. 
We left our room on the 3rd day by 11am and when we returned at 6pm that evening, our room was not cleaned. If we didn't have a broadway to go to that night, we would have to wait outside the room while it was cleaned or wait until the next day. Our "stocked" mini bar was never stocked even when we called 3 times. 
Unfortunately the only real "plus" we could think of for this hotel was the cookies. They are delicious! haha but other than that, we left unsatisfied. 
The hotel looks wonderful and the rooms amazing, until you really look at what you're paying for. Perhaps if we coughed up the money to stay in a guest suite or one of the larger rooms *we had a queen, non-smoking*, but I wouldn't risk the money. 
I only wish I took photos to back up my experience. The photos already taken though give a good impression on what it is like. The rooms are nice looking, but falling apart.

title: “Great location - wonderful beds!”
text:
I've just come back from a 4 night stay in the Herald Square Hotel. I was very impressed with everything about this hotel. The location is superb - located on west 31st Street between 5th and Broadway, the Empire State Building is literally around the corner as is Macy's. Walking distance to so many of the main sights. I walked to MOMA, Times Square, St Patrick's Cathedral etc. 
The staff were very friendly (thanks especially to Augusta and Karl), the room was immaculately kept and the bed was wonderful - I had 4 fantastic night's sleep. The free tea, coffee, hot chocolate etc in the lobby is a great idea. I will definitely stay at this hotel again as would the friends I travelled with. Well done Herald Square Hotel!!

title: “These Guys Are Amazing”
text:
We spent two days with these folks, and it was delightful.
 Their front office manager Riz Marfani acts like a good will ambassador. He will do anything possible to make your stay enjoyable.
 I had read about Riz in other TA reviews. He was
complimented consistently. These reviews did not do him justice.
 He helped us select a restaurant among a list of about 40 on the hotels list. The place was ultimately outstanding.
 The room were nice, bright, clean, and comfortable. The bed had a nice pillow-top mattress.
We slept like logs. The window insulation is great.
The dining room service was superior at breakfast,
and the food was tasty.
 This property is at least 30 years old, but appears much newer inside.
 There's lots a space for convention business here.

title: “Beautiful hotel”
text: We only stayed for a couple nights, but the rooms was clean and classy, the location was convenient (we raced from the train to the hotel in the pouring rain), and the staff was friendly. Having to pay extra to use the amenities is a bit overkill.

title: “Terrible Management/General Manager”
text: Stayed at this property for a two bank event April 24-26 (two nights). Upon returning home I noticed my bank account was charged for a third night. Called and no management available. Wrote letter to property May 7 disputing charge and asked fro a written repsonse. Disputed charge with my bank June 14. July 2 my bank upheld the fraudulent charge (I assume because the hotel indicated it was a valid charge). July 2 spoke with the Controller. He apologized for error and assured me I would receive credit that evening. July 3 received voicemail from Scott (General Manager). July 5 called back and no manager on duty and Scott (GM) is off until July 9. The Controller acknowledged the error. The charged me for a no show on April 24. I was there. The clerk that checked me in spelled my name wrong (even though they were looking at my drivers license), thus triggering the no show charge. No big deal. Just fix it! Never, ever had a problem at an Embassy Suites property. What a nightmare.

title: “fantastic staff”
text:
bottleof wine awaited us in our room
staff was super friendly
hotel was clean
daily happy hour for customers
great great great!

title: “uninteresting location”
text: While the hotel was pleasant enough, the location leaves little in the way of restaurants, especially on the weekend when the financial district shuts up tight as a drum.

title: “Funky little hotel”
text:
This is a modern hotel with funky decor (but not too funky, like some hotels that get carried away). The staff are very friendly.
The rooms are small and we did not have a proper desk in our room (only the table/desk on which the TV stood, which was accompanied by a single "bar-stool"-type chair). So it was totally inappropriate for doing any work in the room. If traveling on business and/or you need to be able to do work, enquire in advance about your room setup.

title: “Pet Peeve - paying for internet”
text: We stayed about 10 hours in this hotel on points. We arrived around 11pm and the security guard (not a Sheraton employee) standing right next to the check in made me wonder if the neighborhood was not as safe as I thought. We didn't try anything except the shower and the bed which were both great. I only gave 4 stars for charging for internet on an award room - it seems really petty. Hotel is in a mall location. Granted, the stores are high quality but it's still just mall shopping and dining.

title: “Typical Westin, great location in the heart of Denver”
text: This Westin is very much in line with other Westins. It is nice and clean, albeit predictable. The front desk staff was extremely helpful, and helped us book a rental car. It is located right on "The Mall", and the free shuttle stop is right outside the door. There is a Starbucks in the lower level, and it is within walking distance of dozens of really good restaurants. We booked through Hotwire (it is listed as a downtown 4-star), and got a phenomenal price.

title: “Adequate but nothing more.”
text: We had trouble with room keys until they replaced the battery to the card reader on our door. Room was on the small side with two double beds--no room for a roll-away. Volume on tv didn't work on several stations. They started construction during our stay and moved the balcony furniture inside and screwed the balcony door closed which further cramped our room. The computer available to guests was INCREDIBLY slow and the printer didn't work at all. No guest laundry facilities. Pool and hot tub were clean and my kids enjoyed swimming, but the area wasn't pretty. On a brighter note, the housekeeping staff was nice and the location was FANTASTIC. 3-minute walk to the Riverwalk, which was a great place for adults and older teens. $18-a-day parking fee for self parking. All in all, we would probably choose a different hotel next time.

title: “Massive, impersonal hotel, in a relatively convenient location”
text:
I've stayed here 4-5 times this year alone. First, the good. It's relatively convenient if you want to be in central San Fran. To one side you are only 2 blocks from Union Square, though they other side is the tenderloin district, which is sketchy.
Now the bad. First, if you happen to be in the wrong tower, the rooms are older and stale. and the hallways leave you feeling like you are in an endless, narrow labrynth of some soulless 1990's hotel. Try to get into the main tower (the one with the elevator closer to O'Farrell St. They've updated that tower more recently.
The lobby is absolutely massive, noisy and busy. The line for checking in - if you aren't a HHonors member - can be 20 minutes long. It's everything bad you fear from a gigantic hotel.
The staff is competent, even if a bit curt due to the massive volume of people. My last visit I got the real impression (from more than one person at the front desk) that they were overwhelmed and tired.
I'm a HHonors Diamond member, so they give you some drinks and coupon for continental breakfast for free.
I only stay there because I want to be in a Hilton property and I need something close to Market St. But I know what to expect. A huge impersonal hotel, clean rooms, even if they are a bit small and, depending on the tower you are in, older and a bit dated.

title: “Good Choice - great location to be near all the gay bars and restaurant”
text:
The hotel is in a perfect location, as it is convenient to many train and bus lines. 
The hotel is very clean and the staff very friendly. It's the perfect hotel if you are looking to be in the heart of gay New York as well. Many gay bars and restaurants are very nearby...like Splash, The Gym Bar, etc.

title: “Hospitable Hosts”
text: I've never been to D.C before and was pleasantly surprised by the friendliness of the staff. Stacy assisted me at the front desk during check in and was very helpful with information concerning the surrouding area. Though I can't say much for the REST of D.C's service industry, the Doubletree Suites is awesome! Thanks for the great stay!

title: “Great hotel and location”
text: We stayed at this hotel during the spring break period after Easter. There was construction next door and the staff offered to move our room to a quieter area of the hotel. We liked our second floor room and decided to stay hoping that the construction would be quiet over the weekend and it was. Our room was not large but well appointed and very comfortable. The staff was very friendly and helpful, especially the concierge who had great recommendations.

title: “Good hotel, but not spectacular (and slow Internet)”
text:
I was debating whether to give this 3 or 4 stars, but I pushed it towards 4 given it was near to the Space Needle.
The rooms were clean and comfortable. The shower was a little basic but reasonable pressure. The TV was an old CRT one. The breakfast was slightly better than average for this type of hotel but nothing spectacular.
The worst thing was the Internet. Although not the slowest I experienced during my trip to the US, it took me 20 hours to upload a 400MB clip to YouTube, It was not possible to video skype on the connection, only audio skype (multiple devices tried)
The hotel did sell stamps (although it only had 4 International stamps left so they had to direct us to a nearby post office to buy the rest) which was useful and gains points for as this is a useful service to International travellers.

title: “Outstanding Service”
text: I am writting this review to commend John the front desk associate at the hotel. Due to a winter storm me, my wife and teenager daughter were forced to extend our stay one more night after a Cheerleading event (12 Dec). John was a savior finding us a room in record time and helping us in every way possible. What a wonderful experience under stressful conditions . Please commend this fine individual for a job well done!

title: “LOVED LOVED LOVED HOTEL!”
text: Perfect location for Ohio State football game away from the OSU madness. Max and Ermas was great, and arena district was so much fun for our kids. Room was very clean, fridge was great to have. Lobby beautiful, hotel seems to connect with THE LOFTS, seems just as nice at a MUCH MUCH more reasonable price. One issue was not getting a wake up call when we requested one. It was a big inconvenience, because I ended up having to meet friends for breakfast with literally 2 minutes to spare. i mentioned this to the check out desk, not for any special treatment, but just to let them know there was a mix-up. Cindy, the director of guest services was wonderful! She offered compensation which more than made up for the getting late to breakfast. She was very apologetic and welcoming. I truly believed she felt badly for my situation and wasn't just doing her job. Am looking forward to returning when I can fit in another buckeye game. Parking was expensive, but probably normal for area.

title: “Great value!”
text: Great location and value. San Diego is a great family destination! Close to Sea World and a short drive to anything in San Diego including the Zoo or beach.

title: “Great Hotel!”
text: This is one of the best experiences I have had at a hotel. The service levels were excellent. I enjoyed the different themes that are displayed on each floor. Great hotel you can not go wrong.

title: “Perfect location and hotel”
text:
We stayed at the Marriott Marquis on a recent girls trip. Great location, easy to get to everything and perfect room. We stayed on 36th floor and it was very quiet and had a great view. Staff was very helpful when we had questions on places to go and how to get around NY. We did not have enough time to visit the restaurants in the hotel, but definitely planning on staying here again. I don't think the trip would have been as convenient if we weren't staying in Times Square. 
This was a very busy hotel on Saturday night so the elevator waiting line got a little long. That would be the only thing I would say negative. Also, the check in and concierge is on the 8th floor. Not that it is bad, just different. 
Great place, lots of fun and right in the middle of the action! Will stay there again!

title: “Exceptional service and great location for work and seeing the sites”
text: We traveled to DC for work and my family came too for a "DC experience." Our stay at the Sofitel was off to a great start when Jamieson helped check our family in, orient us to the City with maps and good advice; he was exceptionally friendly, helpful and professional. Their service remained top-notch through the duration of our stay. The location was convenient to the Metro (which helped for my meetings around town) and within walking distance to the Mall and White House, which was great for site seeing. We would definitely stay again.

title: “Great Lobby and Desk Clerks”
text: Really good staff, close to the airport and one of the best shuttle service I have seen. Parking is a bit steap, as well as internet now a days, should be in the cost of the room not an add on.Nice size rooms.

title: “Great Hotel, wish I was there longer”
text: I loved this hotel and location. Theme of hotel is fun. Close to National Mall (I ran there every morning with my dog). Customer service was great. Everyone was friendly and helpful. Pet Friendly (pets stay free). Free drinks from 5-6pm. Cool bar. Room very comfortable. Only bad thing is parking is very expensive, 33 a night. But, street parking is free on weekends. Would recommend and stay here again. Thanks Hotel Helix.

title: “Excellent service, excellent food, excellent location”
text:
I travel often for business and have stayed in countless hotels that I can barely recall they are so mediocre. the Palomar is a standout Hotel. The location and amenities were great but the service and the food were excellent. I can't remember a time when I received this kind of service - so consistent regardless of time of day or position. Everyone was friendly and attentive. The only down side I have to mention is that it is near a fire station and that interrupted more than one night's sleep with repeated sirens. 
It also has a great fitness facility and indoor pool and a 5pm wine reception every evening. The bartenders are great too and there are some really interesting and unique drinks on the menu...I would definitely go back and stay here and would revommend this to anyone as a great place to stay.

title: “Lovely hotel, terrific staff, terrible restaurant (but don't let that deter you)”
text: We stayed at the Copley Square Hotel from Feb. 20-23, 2012. We stay in Boston 3-4 times a year and this was our first time trying the Copley since its renovation. The staff are very welcoming and we particularly liked the valets, especially the musician who works in the afternoons. The rooms are decorated very nicely and we liked our bathroom. The housekeepers come by around 4 pm every day to ask if you would like complimentary water bottles or if there is anything else you require for the room. The Wine Down at 5 pm is a lovely start to the evening. The *only* complaint we had was the restaurant, Xhale. What a disappointment. When we go away for romantic weekends, we often like to just hole up in the hotel and eat breakfast lunch and dinner at the hotel, drinks and books at the bar, and movies in the bedroom. That wasn't possible here. The dinner at Xhale our first night was just dreadful. Breakfast is better but the restaurant lacks warmth and charm. Fortunately, there are loads of restaurants near by. We would absolutely stay here again based on the staff alone. But we really do hope they find a way to improve the restaurant.

title: “Cool Hotel!”
text: We were pleasantly surprised with this older but charming hotel. Very reasonably priced - complimentary continental breakfast and a simple but adequate wine & cheese hour. Only 3 blocks from Union Square. The hotel has a spacious lobby area with an old world feel. International guests outnumbered Americans during our stay - great conversations during breakfast. Similar to a bed and breakfast but on a larger scale. The rooms were large and clean. The bathroom was a bit dated but roomy. Take your hair dryer though- the hotel "loaners" were not very good. All in all we were very pleased with the Beresford.

title: “Mayflower is still a good bet for a good price”
text: Spent 2 nights at the Mayflower in late May, 2010. I chose this hotel because I like old hotels, it good pretty good reviews, has a good location in DC and the price was right. No complaints. The rooms are nice, the beds are good and it still has old world charm. The only down sides were the price of breakfast in house - very pricey; and a bar waitress that went on retirement some time ago. We found the Luna Grill for a great breakfast just 2 1/2 blocks away.

title: “Horrible Beyond Belief”
text: After traveling four hours to an area we were unfamiliar with, we called the hotel for directions. They told us to get out of the area we were in but were unable to give us directions to do that...."just get out at a gas station and ask." was the response. Hello, two women and two children in an area where there are bars on every window. Sorry I'm familiar with what happens in Detroit if you get out. When we finally did manage to get to the hotel, we learned that valet parking was extra and that's all that was offered. The heat from the room blew us across the hall. What idiot in their right mind sleeps in a room that is 67 degrees unless it is summer time? Did I mention that the people in the next room tried to come through the adjoining door after we got settled into bed? Then there was the room, it was hardly bigger than a closet and there was no room to move around. And if there was a restaurant, it sure didn't open early enough for us to get any breakfast. Where are the luggage carriers? it sure would have helped with check out. NEVER again.

title: “Beautiful hotel but....No pool!”
text: First time staying in the financial district area and it was a little out of the way from most of the places we visited. Overall the stay was nice, rooms were a good size, very clean and comfortable. Customer service was okay- not the best nor the worst.

title: “A perfect wedding!”
text: We had an great stay at the Hampton Inn while traveling to Manhattan for our wedding. My (now) husband and I stayed at the hotel, along with a couple of friends that stayed on the same floor. Rooms were small (as are all rooms in the city), but were a great price, very clean, and surprisingly able to accommodate a lot of luggage! Bathroom was updated/modern, but had some problems with the shower fixture (the different shower head options didn't work, and when I tried adjusting the dial, the shower head fell off and had to be screwed back on). Continental breakfast had a nice selection of fruits, breads, hot food, yogurts, and cereals. Front desk staff were exceptional, and Jose was incredibly helpful with all our transportation needs! He arranged for transportation for our entire wedding party (which included some family/friends staying at neighboring hotels) from our hotel to Central Park for the ceremony. That was one less thing we had to worry about on our wedding day, and it made a world of difference (especially since we were "out-of-towners" and traveling with aging parents, one of whom had a physical disability). Location was great -- within walking distance to Times Square and all the restaurants in Hell's Kitchen. Also very easily accessible by cab, since its near the corner of 9th. We will definitely stay there again when we return to Manhattan!

title: “outdated and old as dirt”
text: the lobby is nice and the service is wonderful, however, once you take the elevator up to your room you see how outdated this hotel is. I like trendy, modern, and updated. The rooms and hotel floors are old as dirt and hot as hell in the middle of summer. I would never stay here again. The location is good, but there are several other hotels in this area to stay at, like the palomar and the sofitel at the same price.

title: “A little gem”
text:
Love this hotel. It is old, some of the rooms are small. But it is reasonably priced, FREE parking, and within walking distance / bus to almost anything in Chicago. 
When I come to Chicago with my son, I come here.

title: “Still liked it second year in a row”
text: We stayed at the Palmer House over Thanksgiving for two nights, same as last year. We reserved a 2 bath room for $119/night through the HHonors web site (Hilton Honors members) then later sent an e-mail basically asking for any upgrades possible. We were upgraded to the Executive level (the one with a private elevator) and actually a view! Of course there were office buildings in the view but we could also see the lake, the top of the Millenium Park bandshell (lit at night) and a sliver of the Navy Pier ferris wheel. So it is possible! The spacious room was lovely, both bathrooms although small were nicely appointed with a really cool flip up shower head, and we had turn down service every night. A free continental breakfast was included. The location was ideal for our purposes of theater, dinner, and seeing the decorations. For a Loop hotel, in-and-out parking for $25/day was quite reasonable even though it was across the street. There couldn't be a better place to see the Thanksgiving Parade. The lobby was stunning but very smoky this year (didn't notice the problem last year). From the sound of the reviews it seems to be the room itself that makes all the difference - apparently people buying a discount room through Priceline or some other third party do not get the same service as hotel program members. Duh, as my teenage son would say!

title: “Quirky but nice”
text: Lovely hotel in an excellent location, close to shops, BART and cable car. Took advantage of the complementary continental breakfast, so can't vouch for the food, but bar was always full of early evening diners downing seafood and cocktails etc. Kimpton Hotel, so signing on to the newsletter gets you free WiFi in your room - a nice touch.

title: “A very bad surprise”
text:
My wife & me choose this hotel for the good comments we saw on internet
We booked a double room with private bathroom (strongly specified at the moment of the reservation).
Once we arrived for the check-in (very late in the night), we were told that our room was with shared bathroom; anyway the assured me to solve the problem within the following morning, so we decided to stay
The following morning the guy in charge told me that no room with private bathroom was not available for few days
I made my complaint, very strongly: they accepted ON PURPOSE a reservation they already knew they could not honour. They really didn't care about my protest, telling me that NYC was very big and I could find another hotel (unbelievable!!!)
So we left the hotel very angry, fortunately the vacation came back to the normality when we found a respectablaeBest Western near Times Square

title: “Great hotel!”
text:
Stayed here for a 4-day girl's weekend and had a great time. Rooms are clean and decor is great - very LA! The rooms and bathrooms are also a decent size so there is room for two girl's suitcases, shopping, etc. while still allowing room to move.
The lobby has a nice sophisticated-but-comfortable vibe and there are all types who stay here - couples, families, business travellers, and those on trips with friends. And there are also pets - we were startled by a beautiful golden retriever when we got off the elevator one morning! 
Service is very good overall - attentive, friendly and very helpful. The concierge, Paul, made some great recommendations for a Saturday night out including AOC, which we didn't realize until afterwards was such a highly-regarded restaurant. He also gave tips on when to arrive at Bar Marmont so that we could be sure to enjoy the Saturday night vibe and miss the line! 
A few small things. Room service, although 24 hour, is expensive and the restaurant closes around 10 or 11, so come prepared if you get in on a late flight! There is also a very limited night menu (from 11 PM or 12 to 6 AM).
Also seems that there are a fair number of new staff right now. They are all trying hard and doing a great job but some of them don't yet have a good knowledge of the area/sights and some processes - like an early morning check-out - were a little slow. But everyone is keen and friendly - the most important thing.
This hotel is in a nice area but you do have to walk a bit to get to shopping, etc. But it's LA so to be expected - just about anyone visiting the city should be prepared to rent a car. Valet parking is $30/day. A little pricey but definitely cheaper than the downtown areas of a lot of major cities - San Fran, NY. We didn't look into other parking options so don't know if self-park is available.
Overall a great stay for two girls looking for a fun weekend!

title: “A honeymoon highlight”
text: We stayed at the Palomar as part of our honeymoon tour of the East coast. We were absolutely delighted with this hotel and it was certainly one of our favourites. The hotel is boutique, well-maintained and boasts a number of guest luxuries such as happy hour from 5pm - 6pm during which you can enjoy a free glass of wine. The rooms are artistically decorated and the beds are luxurious. All the hotel staff are friendly and make uou feel genuinely welcome. We loved our stay and would have liked to stay longer.

title: “A good place to stay on vacation”
text:
We stayed here for three nights on our way to Hawai'i. It is a great place to stay, clean, comfortable, great free breakfast, etc. Make sure that you get a view of the Space Needle because, if you don't, you probably have a view of the hotel 5 feet behind this one!!! We are both runners and we also love to walk to places, so this hotel is right for people like us. If you don't like to walk more than a few blocks, you need to spend the big $$$ and stay closer to your places you want to visit. We easily walked to the Space Needle in about 10 minutes, downtown to the Pike Place area in about 30. One thing that is nice is if you walk to either area, the monorail that was built for the World's Fair in 1960 (?) still shuttles back and forth between the two areas for two bucks. It drops you off right at the very nice, downtown shopping district, only a few blocks from the Pike Place Market. Also, there are tours that will pick you up right here and take you to places like Boeing, etc.
We paid about $160 per night, which includes all taxes, etc. For the money, a very good place to stay.

title: “Delightful, charming ambience but tiny cramped rooms”
text: The hotel is attractive; the personnel helpful, attentive and pleasant. The hotel hosts a morning breakfast and an early evening cheese and wine buffet which are pleasant and reminiscent of B and B's rather than large city hotels.Another unusual feature is that the coffee, rolls and cookies are avaulable in the common room throughout the day. While the lobby is small, but waiting time is spent in the second floor common room which is tastefully decorated in a North African motif. The only shortcomming is the size of the rooms. My interior room was small and cramped; our luggage had to be placed on chairs as there was no room on the floor for luggage and room to walk; the bathroom was similarly tiny and could not accomodate the personal items of two adults. While the corner exterior rooms were larger, management advised that our interior room was the standard in the hotel. If you are not planning to spend much tiome in your individual room, but rather in the large comfortable common room , this is the ideal place.

title: “Great location, Not-so-great establishment”
text:
I wanted a romantic getaway for my boyfriend and I and we thought a lovely B&B on Boston's Newbury Street would be perfect. The only two good things I can say are that the room was clean and the location is excellent. Other than that, the staff was very uninterested and I never was introduced to an owner or manager and never got anyone's name upon check in. Also upon arrival there were signs up speaking of renovation....we soon found out during breakfast what this meant when people were literally renovating in the breakfast room while we ate! I am talking about chainsaws being run 10 to 15 feet from breakfast tables! Being a B&B manager myself, I was appalled by this and went to speak to the one woman they had on breakfast (yes one woman for the ENTIRE 30 some-odd rooms they have). She pointed towards the workers which I had to ask myself to pipe it down, as my boyfriend and I had to yell to one another to have a conversation. The chainsawing stopped briefly then started up again. Thoroughly disgusted, we left our breakfasts and went up to the front desk where I complained to the man sitting up there. He told me that they tell the workers to start after breakfast but the workers don't listen. I found this to be a ridiculous excuse, as the sawing and hammering is DEFINITELY within earshot of the front desk. He most definitely heard them going at it during breakfast. I didn't appreciate the terrible excuse and it frankly ruined my experience there.
I would never stay at the Newbury Guest House again, and judging from some other reviews talking about renovation nightmares, this establishment definitely has no regard for their guests' comfort or pleasure.

title: “Good Business Hotel”
text: This is a hotel well suited for business travel. Very close to the galleria and businesses on the west side of Houston.

title: “Our family was blown away by this amazing resort!”
text:
All I can say is WOW! We booked a suite at this resort to celebrate my son and father's birthday. We were interested in this resort because we heard they had a great water park and in this desert heat, that's exactly what we were looking for. We arrived at the resort 3 hours before check-in, so that we could play in the Oasis Water Park all day. When we got there, our room was already ready! The staff was so friendly and so helpful, we were already beyond impressed within 5 minutes of arrival. Then, we were taken to our suite and we were even more blown away! We did not expect to be staying in such a beautiful, spacious room! The bedroom was HUGE with a comfy king bed and an entrance to the balcony that overlooked a rolling green golf course and a gorgeous waterfall! The bathroom was gigantic, with a large garden tub and a seperate all-glass shower that was the size of a large elevator! Very romantic :) This suite had a full size kitchen (full size fridge, oven/stove, microwave, etc..) and the dining and living area was very spacious as well. The couch folded out to a queen size bed, where the kids ended up sleeping. Flat screen TVs, beautiful decor and very very CLEAN. 
The Oasis Water Park was a BLAST! The kids ran around all day, playing in the wave pool, flying down the huge waterslides and floating down the lazy river. My husband and I enjoyed laying out in the sun with yummy frozen drinks and even floated around the lazy river ourselves. We ordered food while we were out there (nachos, wings, chicken sandwich) and it was top notch. I can't say enough great things about this resort. I am DEFINATELY going to plan another weekend getaway here! We even played at the water park all day on Sunday after check-out. 
This resort is only 30 mins away from our home and it felt like we were on a distant vacation. We didn't feel like we were anywhere near home!

title: “Great value provided by a reputable hotel.”
text:
I can always expect wonderful accommodations from Four Points and this last overnight stay at the LAX location was extremely an enjoyable event.
The value provided from such a major hotel chain was beyond my expectation.
Adding to the value was a warm and friendly staff that saw to my comfort and that includes a courteous and timely shuttle to the airport.

title: “thanks rolando!”
text: had a lovely finish to a great tour of california and the southwest. special thanks to rolando at the front desk, who went above and beyond to help me recover my wedding band at furnace creek ranch in death valley. i will definitely be back

title: “Great Location”
text:
We picked the Courtyard by Marriott New York Manhattan / Times Square South because of it's location only half a block from Broadway and 2 blocks from Times Square. We were also pleasantly surprised that we could also easily walk to the follow places as well; Central Park, the United Nations, Empire State Building, Macys, Madison Square Gardens, Rockefeller Center, Grand Central Station, restaurants, and of course the Theater District. We went to three shows while in New York for 9 days, walked there and back and never once felt unsafe. Lots of people on the streets at all times of the day.
Our room was expensive, as we stayed there during Fashion Week (our choice), so every room in the area was booked and this hotel was the closest to Bryant Park where the show was being put on. The room was clean and had all the necessities we needed. We didn't eat in the hotel but there was a restaurant there. Coffee was available free of charge in the lobby every morning. As suggested by another Trip Advisor we brought our own alcohol as it was expensive to buy there.
Get a map and directions from the Concierge to make your way around New York Manhattan a lot easier. After talking with the Concierge we took the subway from Grand Central Station to Battery Park and took the Staten Island Ferry (free) to Staten Island and back ( 25 minutes each way), going past the Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island. Walked through the Financial District before walking over the Brooklyn Bridge (3.5 miles each way). We also took the subway from Grand Central Station to Yankee Stadium. 
Security in the hotel was first class, always someone around, and you have to use your room key in the elevator before it will move.
If and when we go to New York Manhattan again we will definitely stay at this hotel.

title: “Wonderful trip ruined by parasite infestation”
text:
My wife & I were enjoying a trip to the Austin Hill Country, and were looking forward to our stay at Barton Creek Resort while attending a charity golf tournament. 
Certainly the course was beautiful and the resort appeared to be well run, clean & well organized. However, upon waking up one morning in our room with a very swollen eyelid & red eye, I became quite concerned, to say the least. 
I assumed I had sunburn from being out on the golf course all day, but after arriving home with continued swelling, I visited my Ophthalmologist. He immediately diagnosed a parasite infection. The doctor said it was probably contracted through unclean pillows, linens/towels, etc. He prescribed medication & cleaning materials designed to eliminate this problem. 
I contacted BCR right away to notify them of this issue. I expected a thank you, a quick apology & offer of assistance. I got none of these things. Instead the manager simply stated that they were not going to take any responsibility for my problem at all. I was dumbfounded-- this is the type of response I would have expected from a cheap roadside motel-- certainly not from a renowned golf resort. 
I have reported this parasite issue to the BBB of Austin, and the Texas Department of State Health Services.

title: “Excelent...”
text:
Wonderful Hotel,with clean and spacious rooms.
 Great Airport location.Great stay.

title: “Great Stay”
text: We enjoyed very much our stay here. The daily breakfast buffet (included) was plentiful and very good. Staff was friendly and helpful, the rooms clean and well-maintained. The location was easy to get to by car and being close to the 16th Street Shuttle made getting to sites in the city by foot a breeze. We especially enjoyed the light dinner and happy hour during the weekdays (Included).

title: “Perfect location to stay in NYC”
text: Thank you to all the friendly and helpful staff at Seaport Inn especially Frank & Dion for making our 7 night stay in NYC so enjoyable. Our room was on the 7th floor with a terrace overlooking the Brooklyn Bridge so much more than just a hotel it was like having your own apartment..A big thank you also to the cleaning & kitchen staff who were also very efficient and friendly..We found the downtown location perfect for accessing all the city and its attractions we used the subway at Fulton St only 5 mins from the hotel to go uptown and found the area safe day and night also within walking distance to all the ferry and river taxis services,restaurants and shops on Pier17...Overall we had a fabulous holiday and would not hesitate in recommending to anyone to stay here....

title: “Nice view”
text:
Some additional info: For a real view of Lake Union, try to get as high as possible as there are trees and waterfront restaurants blocking some of the lower views. The 3rd floor actually is the lowest floor with rooms. See my photo of the hotel room map. The best views are at the right side (rooms 07-11) or looking out to the right. The hotel is shaped like a pyramid so the end units on each level have large outside patios with the best views and are also larger (e.g., room 11 on the map). (In the room map, the hotel is shaped like an arrow pointing away from the Lake. Each floor going up will be somewhat smaller since the hotel is pyramid-shaped.) The lake view is wonderful as there are float planes that land on the lake in the morning. The back of the hotel has no view.
Parking under the hotel is $19/night. There are no spaces on the busy street in front of the hotel but free street parking always is available in the evenings behind the hotel or on the next block up. 
For breakfast in the morning in addition to scrambled eggs with some kind of meat and the do-it-yourself waffle makers, there are bagels, yogurt, berries or cut-up fruit to go with the yogurt, oatmeal, apples and bananas and cereals. Get your banana early as they tend to go fast. Coffee is decent (this is Seattle!) and served in carafes. Staff is very efficient at replenishing food and cleaning tables. The lobby has carafes of coffee, decaff and hot water with selection of regular and herbal teas and packets of hot chocolate mix. This is available 24 hours/day and never ran out during our stay. There are also refrigerated displays with microwaveable foods and cold drinks (e.g., Gatorade for $1.50) you can charge to your room
High speed internet is by hard-wire LAN connection. It worked flawlessly and was free. There is no in-room safe for your laptop. 
The bed was updated to the more plush kind that are becoming common in up-scale hotels, with high-quality sheets (see photo). The bathroom had a roomy counter with real drawers for your toiletries, and a separate door for the toilet/bath room.

title: “Renovations Cater to Freeloaders at Expense of Paying Guests”
text:
From the moment I first saw pizza being eaten from cardboard boxes and fries being doused with ketchup from packets spilling on the tables, I realized the lobby renovations at the Marriott Marquis were intended to cater to this group, and not to guests like me who were footing the bill to clean up this space after these visitors left. I knew this because the renovated public space now looks more like a food court at a local mall than a place for tired guests to escape the crowds and grab a drink before heading up to their rooms. This lobby now WAS the crowd off the street, clogging the restrooms and trashing the tables as they waited for their show, or their friends, or something else. 
Similarly, the new restaurant space looks and feels like a diner in a bus station, crowds pushing past your table to get somewhere else and servers rushing you to seat yet another guest in an extension of the conveyor-belt madness throughout the lobby. The new Broadway lounge sports high white tables and straight back chairs whose design is meant to get you up quickly, with no time to linger over a drink or conversation. In every respect, this lobby says "come on in" to the streetgoing public and "move along" to the paying guest. My family resented that ambience, it colored our whole stay here, and we left New York earlier than planned to escape it.
We have stayed at the Marquis several times a year for over 10 years, always returning for the location and the friendly staff whose lives had become familiar to us after so many visits. Now we may never return, and the lobby renovations are the primary reason. We used to spend a lot of our down-time in this lobby, reading, looking out over Times Square, grabbing a quick snack, even playing board games and catching up on schoolwork. None of that is possible now, even as room rates have skyrocketed and harried servers specialize more in crowd control than serving guests. 
Don't even get me started on the Concierge Lounge. Used to be this haven for elite rewards members could bring peace and quiet mid-day and a light snack before dinner, with friendly staff asking about family and plans in the city. On this trip, the Concierge Lounge had become nothing more than a frenzied extrnsion of the lobby, everyone grabbing excitedly for free food while leaving their tables dirty and chairs askew. So intense were these crowds that at 7:30 one evening we found not one of the 40 or so tables clean enough to use. The music was blaring so loud we could have been in Johnny Rockets, overwhelmed and understaffed with apathetic employees barely meeting your gaze. Marriott must be selling access to this space as a room perk, because there simply cannot be this many elite members in 2000 rooms. To paraphrase the charcter Syndrome from Disney's The Incredibles, "when everyone becomes elite, then no one will be." Sadly, Marriott accepts this result, having done everything possible to this property to ensure it.
Listen, we know this property faces unique demands for its location and popularity, and our visit came during the rush of the holidays, as it often has in the past. We also know that Marriott tries to keep this property current by renovating to meet expecations. This time, when Marriott obviously had to choose between the freeloading public and its paying guests, it chose the former. Not only does this seem to be a bad business decision, for all the patrons bringing in food and taking up space while placing additional demands on cleaning and security crews, it was unquestionably a huge blow to customer loyalty. We will be taking our elite status elsewhere in the future, satisfied to occupy a smaller and less convenient property where paying guests are actually invited to enjoy what they pay for.

title: “Not worthy of the Westin name”
