text:
Overall an ok hotel if you don't compare it to other Westin locations, or other Starwood hotels when staying with Platinum status.
The hotel location is great, but really that's about it.
As for the Westin name...this location is a little run down and lacks many amenities. There's no lounge (sorry Platinum folks), the hot tub wasn't hot (in January!) and looked like it hadn't been cleaned in about a week, the gym is slightly below par for this level hotel, and even a "deluxe" room is nothing to brag about.
The Hyatt, which can be had for the same price much of the year, is MUCH better. I really messed up this time.

title: “Simply the best !”
text: Hotel is extremely clean and well kept. Bathroom fixtures are state of the art, and beautiful. Very large rooms, high ceilings. (Room 205). Great hotel staff - very friendly and helpful. Has an ice cream parlor, and cafe resturant, both excellent. Very close to subway entrance, (right outside the side door) and bus stops.

title: “Perfect location and ammenities for a family”
text: We spent 4 wonderful nights and 5 days in Chicago. The hotel was clean, the staff very courteous and knowledgeable. With all the attractions and activities in town, we didn"t even miss a pool! We would stay at this location again without hesitation.

title: “NEVER AGAIN!!”
text: Where do I start... We were traveling with a rather large group. Check in was SLOOOWWW. In our 1st room, it had no bathroom door. So we get moved to our 2nd room. Where our A/C isn't cooling the room down at all. So, we get our 3rd attemp to our room. Finally a door to the bathroom and the A/C worked, but the mattress to this hotel seems like something you would pick up at the flea market. SO UNCOMFORTABLE!! My family was tired of moving so I decide not to say anything. I also mention to the clerk that our hall way is extremely hot, doesn't seem like the A/C is working. She said she would have someone check on it. The hall way never got cooler. On our way to the pool I ask the front clerk for towels for my kids and the kids in our group. About 10 kids, he says he can only give me 3 towels total. He says, that once those get soaked to go and take them back to him so he can give us 3 more towels. WHAT???!! Never heard of such a thing!!! 2 other couples from our group had to change rooms becuase their beds were BROKEN! One of those couples with the broken bed were switched into a room where the toilet would not flush. We finally settle for the night, I get up in the morning and there on the wall is a huge ROACH the size of a ketchup packet!! Disguesting!! I get the kids up and tell the to start getting ready so we can check out and leave. My daughter pulls out their iron to iron, doesn't work and had GUNK all on the bottom of it. Then I realize that the clothing rod in the closet isn't even hung up! Also, don't be fooled by the amenities, the rooms do not have microwaves or mini fridges. Seems like this place doesn't get many guest. Our group felt like they were running around the last minute trying to make these room appear presentable. This is a trip our group takes once a year to the same location in Dallas. We will never return to this hotel. An aweful experiance.

title: “Nice stay with comfortable bed.”
text:
Having been tired from a long day of work, it was great to come to a hotel with such a comfortable king-size bed. This night's sleep was one of the soundest I have had in a long time.
The hotel is in central city near shopping and entertainment. There was free and fast wifi in the rooms. The television was small and could use an upgrade. 
I would stay here again.

title: “Great location but average hotel for a marriott”
text: The exterior of the hotel and hallways were a bit dated and worn, however, the rooms and common areas were clean and upgraded. The elevators were broken the day we checked in so we had to carry our luggage up the stairs. The front desk and conceirge staff were very friendly and helpful! The location is just steps from Fisherman's Wharf! The onsite parking was expensive ($36/d), however, there is a public garage next door that is $32/d. We opted for the hotel parking because it was unlimited in/out whereas the garage was pay each in/out. The cafe had minimal choices and was overpriced. Don't bank on having a rollaway bed!

title: “2nd visit and still very very good value”
text:
I'm staying here for a second time and I still think it is good value for NY. The room is very large, not beautiful by European standards, but clean, in good condition, dark wood furniture and light walls, etc. The bathroom is also in good condition and clean with no signs of wear or tear. The room comes equipped with microwave, coffeemaker and fridge! All in very good condition. The hotel is quiet, apart from the occasional excited teenagers in the hallway!
The location is also good - there are lots of pleasant bars and restaurants on 8th and 9th avenues, and you can get away from too many tourists!
I agree with a previous reviewer that the Internet connection is rubbish in the hotel - they should do something about it! Otherwise, though, a very pleasant place to be!

title: “close to the main touristy area”
text: the rooms were fine, not so big and not so luxury and little dark. but clean and close to everything. price could be a little bit less by 20% for that room. service was average not excellent but they were also very busy. no restaurant, but you can easily walk to any good restaurant in town. walking distance to most of the ocean view attractions.

title: “Another great stay”
text: The Jacksonville Airport Springhill Suites provided excellent accomidations and amenities to the staff of Ride for Kids. They provided us with excellent rooms, training facilities and service. We will continue to use the Springhill Suites for our events in the JAcksonville area. There are excellent restaurants within a block of the hotel and a shopping center within a half mile. Even though the Hotel is very near the airport, I did not hear plane traffic. Overall an excellent facility.

title: “Great staff and location!”
text: We stayed for 5 nights. The free bike usage, the half price breakfasts, the promptness of staff and service and the location as well as a nice, large room, including large private patio made it worth it's price. Pool and hot tub are nice! They have pool service for drinks, etc but also have free ice tea, lemonade. Free warm cookies in the evening, turn down service in the evening with chocolates on pillow. Nice robes. All the little touches added up to a very nice stay. We rode bikes everyday, keeping the bikes all day one day. Very prompt valet with both the car and the bikes! Our room was very quiet as I requested and even though they said we had a non- view room, we actually had a peek of the ocean! We didn't have to look at a parking lot or wall!

title: “Not very good value for your $$$”
text: We stayed there one night, hence we did not need to use the kitchen. The sleeping area had looked new or renovated; the two queen beds were very comfortable. The kitchen was a different game, because apart of the refrigerator and microwave, that looked new, the rest of the furniture looked cheap and aged, as well as the bathroom, that shown its age. The tap of the tub was broken – we could not cut the water; we called the front desk and the tap was immediately repaired. Other problem with the TV set; the volume could not go down to a night level, so at an hour we shut it down not to annoy the neighbour rooms. The wi-fi was available only at a fee (5$) when the motel near offered it for free, as many other around. Considering that we paid 71$ plus taxes, we believe it is overpriced for what it offers.

title: “A wonderful splurge”
text:
We started the first 3 nights of our Northern California honeymoon here. With the exception of a small mix up upon checking in (there was someone else with the same name checking in the same day, and we were getting quoted their deal... much better than ours!) everything was flawless. Because it was our honeymoon, we got an excellent room, complimentary chocolates and a pot of honey, with a story of the history of the "honey moon", and rose petals on our bed. 
We happened to be staying here during the premiere of the new movie "Milk", and many of the celebrities were staying on site, so there was a lot of commotion and security around, but even they managed to seem very normal with the abundance of attention guests were receiving. 
We'd booked the hotel with hesitation (do we really want to spend that much money on a hotel??), and all hesitation melted away within 5 minutes at the property. It was precisely the luxurious splurge that defined our honeymoon!

title: “Excellent Stay”
text:
Thoroughly enjoyed my recent stay at the Affinia Gardens. Spacious, comfortable room which was elegantly furnished, and with modern comforts. Most importantly, room was quiet, with no street noise. Hotel reception and tea bar were excellent.
Staff were at all times attentive, courteous and well-informed, and focused on the well-being of guests.
Would strongly recommend hotel.

title: “Good...but not great”
text: This was my first "grown-up" stay at a high-end hotel chain. I travel most of the year and stay in a lot of average hotels, like La Quinta or Comfort Inn-like hotel/motels. I wanted to stay here because it is where I have booked for my wedding night hotel. The room was small/average at best. The bed was awesome!! I had emailed ahead of time and requested a robe and extra pillows and there were neither in the room. Really, I am glad I paid only around $100 + taxes. The only reason I am still staying there for my wedding night is I have enough points to stay for free.

title: “Work in progress”
text: Got a good deal at the Artisan Hotel in Phoenix via Hotwire, but had no idea what to expect. The room itself was fine: clean, large, everything worked. Aside from that, there are zero extras: there's a pool outside and a computer in the lobby, but otherwise, nothing. The website I had visited claimed there was a restaurant (in construction), a workout facility (none), etc etc. I couldn't even find a vending machine. The overall concept of the boutique hotel is that of some sort of art history class. There's great works of art all over the walls, ceiling, etc. Unfortunately, everything else is black and dark dark dark. The lobby is not exactly inviting, in fact, it's darn-well creep-crawly. Not what an exhausted traveler wants to see upon first inspection. Would I stay there again? Not really.

title: “Brand new hotel with great staff!”
text: There are two Hilton Garden Inn's in Washington DC, please choose this one as your destination. Firstly upon check in we were upgraded as we are on our honeymoon, when we entered the room we had wine and chocs on our bed. Checking in was a breeze and Latoya at the front desk was awesome. The rooms are so clean and new..unlike other Hilton properties, the bar staff great and a great restaurant the watershed located within the hotel. This hotel and staff well exceeded our expectations, the food and facilities are ten out of ten. I cannot find a fault with our stay and so far, maybe because of the hotel and staff, Washington DC has been our favourite destination throughout our honeymoon. Thank you Latoya and the other staff that made our 2 night stay a vacation to remember.

title: “Best hotel ever!”
text:
The location is perfect, the crew is great and the hotel is AMAZING!! Loved it! Will never stay at another hotel in NY, this is the one!
It is a brand new hotel, very modern and practical. There was a kitchen at my floor that can be used 24/7 with free water, espresso, tea, etc.
The breakfast had a nice selection of muffins, coffee and tea (included in stay).

title: “Just Wonderfull”
text: We had an amazing stay at the night hotel. Everything is so cozy, dark and quiet. Location is perfect, employees nice and helpfull.

title: “A BEACON OF LIGHT IN NEW YORK CITY”
text:
My husband and I celebrated my birthday by spending the weekend in NYC. Even though we live in Brooklyn, what a treat it was to walk home after a show and not have to schlepp on the subway!
We stayed at the Hotel Beacon on the Upper West Side, a neighborhood we had both lived in.
I had requested a quiet room. What we got was a little piece of heaven! We were on the 25th floor with views of Central Park! How lucky were we?
The room even had a small little kitchen we were could store our waters and juices.
The bed was extremely comfortable with extra pillows.
The staff was really nice and friendly. 
We couldn't have asked for anything more for a fantastic birthday celebration.
And the neighborhood~~right across from Fairways, a few blocks from Zabar's and a block from Central Park. Perfect!!!

title: “Just what we needed”
text:
As a first time visitor to NYC, I did a lot of research into where to stay and am very glad that we ended up in this hotel in Tribeca. If you want to get a feel for the real New York then downtown is definitely the place to be, and the Garden Inn is ideally situated. With easy access to the subway, plus in an area that deserves exploring on its own, we had no complaints.
Great size rooms, and the beds were everything that other reviewers have said they are - you just sank into them at the end of day's hard work being a 'tourist'. Also very handy to have wi-fi in the rooms plus free accesss to PCs and a printer in the business suite. Didn't use the hotel restaurant, but did enjoy wonderful breakfasts at the Square Diner at 33 Leonard Street.
The rest of the family stayed in a more expensive hotel just 2mins walk away, yet they certainly didn't have complimentary coffee or cookies available to them all day! Would stay at the Garden Inn again.

title: “Too many add on charges”
text:
The room was OK. The view was terrific and the location was good. The beds were too hard and uncomfortable. The real problem, however, was the add on charges that just kept piling up. $22 a day to park is ridiculous. $11 a day for internet is even more ridiculous, especially considering it isn't wireless or high speed. There are no vending machines, or if there are they make them impossible to find, and the prices for the in room refrigerator are unbelievable. And room service-$16 for pancakes. Come on! You people need to go out in the real world.
Even Super 8 has free high speed wireless internet. 
This hotel is really about a two star that is trying to act like(and charge like) its a five star.

title: “Updated historic hotel with great location 1 block off Sundance Square”
text:
The Ashton is an updated historic hotel in downtown Fort Worth. 
I will start with the couple small negatives. One, downtown Fort Worth was louder at night than I would have expected. The street noise that you could hear in the middle of the night reminded me significantly more of New York City than I ever would have expected. Two, it is a smaller more boutique-y type hotel so they seem to run somewhat fewer staff. The staff is very helpful when available but if they get a little rush such as at check in, you just have to wait your turn.
The biggest advantage of the hotel is the location. If you are doing anything in the heart of downtown, it is perfect. It is located a block from Sundance Square, a block or so from Bass Performance Hall and right next to the DR Horton office buildings. Very convenient.
The hotel was very clean and surprisingly spacious for an updated historic hotel. They did a really good job with the update adn the bathrooms were especially well done, new, clean and modern feeling.

title: “Home away from home”
text:
When we come to New York we always stay at the Barclay (Intercontinental) hotel,it's really home away from home. We don't look for anywhere else.They never let us down.You always get whatever you need. The staff is excellent, they help you with everything. Guest Relation is there for you taking care of evrything you need, always with patience. Concierge gives you the best information about the city.
Breakfast is great to start the day with.The waiters are so nice, you get instent service and testy food.
Rooms are big, well equiped and very clean.
Fitness center is open for you 24 hours,is big enough, well equiped
Best location in town.
For us it is the best hotel in town.

title: “Nice Surprise”
text: I do not normall stay at Holiday Innss. Was in Fl for a wedding and was too tired to drive back to SC so we just stopped because it looked new and it was. Since it was very new there were no issues with the physical building but the Staff's kindness and friendliness was exceptional and very appreciated. We check it about 9:00 they gave us excellent written directions to a mall with plenty of food choices and the list of extras kindness goes on. Even at breakfast when serving their complimentary items. Again you have trained this staff well. They were much nicer than some persons I have encounter in much pricer hotels.

title: “Wish I had remembered I had stayed here before”
text:
This is a conference hotel and I had stayed there ten years ago and found it bland and lacking in friendliness. All the facilities are there and work but I did not feel like a guest rather a source of revenue. I should not really be surprised as a lot of conference hotels are similar.
One thing that would really improve the feel of the lobby in the evening is to get a quieter piano player or close the lid. The choice of tunes and volume must reduce the bar income.
Maybe I will forget again on my next visit in 10 years and get a great surprise

title: “Classic Style”
text: Second stay here. Close (too close?) to Pioneer Square, and a good long daytime walk to downtown shopping. Prefer the short cab ride to restaurants in the evening. The rooms are very comfortable, though a little dark. Take time to explore the lobby, as the hotel has an interesting history.

title: “Overpriced!”
text:
I must first preface this review with the fact that my husband's employer paid for our stay in this hotel. That said, even with the corporate discount, our standard room was terribly overpriced. Granted, the hotel itself is quite stately, complete with ball rooms, corporate facilities, a pool and fitness center, several restaurants and a concierge service, not to mention immaculate grounds; but, there was certainly a disconnect between these amenities and our small room with its two double beds. 
With respect to cleanliness and service, the hotel was impeccable, and we definitely slept well each night. We also appreciated the fact that the Woodley Park - Zoo/Adams Morgan Metro station is directly across the street from the hotel. That was VERY convenient. Still, unless price is not an issue for you, or you are specifically looking for a hotel in this area, I would suggest looking elsewhere.

title: “Hotel Room takes a back seat to Lobby”
text: While room #225 was average at best in size, maintenace, ammenities and retro design, the real show stopper is the 8 story open atrium with clubby atmosphere and industrial chic decor. Rhythmic lounge music prevails on the weekends into late hours with all the partying hipsters. The noise-dulling device in the room is effective. Friendly and welcoming staff. Puny gym. Pet friendly. Excellent and popular Sunday Brunch in the atrium. Movie viewing room on lower floor. Soho shopping and dining is 5-7 blocks north. Midtown and theater district is a 20-30 minute cab ride away in traffic. Hotel is a good choice to be away from congestion further north, edgey neighborhood and trendy design.

title: “Deserves an A- rating”
text:
A very good hotel, conveniently located right beside the Metro Center subway line in Washington DC. All the major monuments around the National Mall are close. The White house is about a mile away. 
The rooms are good. There is a Starbucks in the lobby and a good restaurants in the area. There is a Macy's and some other stores right across the hotel. 
NB:
Watch out if you are driving to DC ... parking is very expensive! It's about $40 for valet parking and self parking in not available. Overnight parking at other parking lots is not available. You can park on the street after 10:00pm, but then you will have to remove the car at 7:00 am the next morning. Good luck with that!

title: “Fell short of a good stay.”
text: Disappointed. We expected great things from the description given by the front desk when we booked and had to accept the only availability in a suite. Very pricey for what we ended up getting. The sofa bed was all but unusable for any human body to sleep, even the kids balked after the first night. The promised WiFi only worked in the lobby near the desk, never in our rooms. The maid service was SLOW, as we left for 6 hours in the middle of the day and came back to find her still cleaning at 4:30pm. So we couldn't come back and enjoy a clean "upgrade" room when we needed it most. Great location, we appreciated that as we rode the trolley to the Padres game. And I must applaud the young woman at the desk who acted as our concierge.

title: “ABSOLUTELY WONDERFUL EXPERIENCE”
text:
SUPERB IN EVERY WAY! Crosby Street is our new favorite hotel in NYC. Brand new; absolutely gorgeous, chic, funky decor; top-notch friendly service; well-located on a quiet street in the middle of Soho.
Owned and operated by London's premier Firmdale Hotels group (ever heard of the fab Number Sixteen???), Crosby Street is their first outpost in the United States. We were told that a second New York hotel is due to open in midtown later this year.
We had one of the premier, corner rooms and were delighted. Good-sized by NYC standards, sparkling clean, floor to ceiling windows, finest quality furnishings and hardware - all from the U.K. Even the smallest touches were appreciated: padded hangers, bathrobes, heated towel rack, and a shoe horn! The bathroom and shower were to die for. When was the last time you had good water pressure from a shower head in a hotel!
Public spaces were awe-inspiring and hats off to the decorator. Feng shui to the max. If you stay here, make sure to get downstairs to see the film screening theater, function rooms, and bar. I'd have a meeting in that conference room any day.
Every member of the staff was lovely, and we were treated with warmth and respect from the moment we arrived. They are genuinely service-oriented without a hint of snootiness. No faux sycophancy here. They went out of their way to be helpful, including getting us out of a restaurant snafu on a Saturday night (thanks again, George!).
Coincidentally, a few days after our return to Boston, we noticed that the weekend Financial Times had a feature about hip NYC boutique hotels. A full two-spread photo of Crosby Street's art gallery, um lobby. Well deserved, and wow did we feel on the cutting edge.
The only gripe over our two-day stay had to do with the bar within the hotel's restaurant. Living in New England and frequenting Boston and New York, we are more than familiar with high prices and rarely blink an eye. BUT -- $18.00 for a cocktail is simply over the top. We each had one drink and a tiny bowl of peanuts and the tab plus tip came to $50.00!!! As good as the ambience and drinks were, it felt like a rip-off and we would not visit the bar again. Our recommendation? Lower the prices to within striking range and attract more customers. 
That being said, we adore the hotel and can't wait for an excuse to go back.

title: “A Real Disappointment”
text: We stayed three nights, had a double room on the 7th floor. Upon check in the staff was not really welcoming. Bed linens are low quality, torn blankets, thin and worn flat sheet thrown over a thin, felt like pad on bottom mattress. We were there Thursday through Sunday, by the time we left Sunday, our trash container was stacked about 2 feet tall with trash that had not been removed from the room since the first day (newspapers, pizza boxes, plastic bags, paper cups). I kept pulling it further into the room each day, thinking they couldn't possibly miss it again. They did. Even though the hotel went through a renovation not too long ago, the rooms are pretty dated. Parking was expensive, $21 per day, plus wifi at $9 per day. with sales tax over 15% added on, it was not an inexpensive hotel. I remember seeing it rated as 4 star. I'd probably say more like 2.5 star. Parking for guests is on levels 4 and above. Yet, there is no elevator in the garage. Location of the hotel is very good, and although we did not try them, the bar/restaurant seemed pretty busy. Bottom line....we were not impressed with either the service or the hotel itself, and will definitely stay elsewhere next time we are in Seattle.

title: “Dont frequent the restaurant/bar at this hotel.”
text:
Variable pricing at the restaurant made me disgusted this evening, when prices I've paid in the past three days increased by %50 due to the late hour (11PM). 
Really!!!.do you need to screw your customers who happen to come back a little late from dinner/dancing with 50 % increase in drinks and food??
Try the Marriott across the street or La Quinta a block away for a better bet.

title: “Perfect!”
text:
We stayed there one night on June 6. loved it, loved it... Everything was perfect. Friendly staff, especially bellman Brian. He was very knowlegable and helpful. 
The hotel itself was beautiful. We really enjoyed sitting in the courtyard. The lobby was elegent too.
The location was convenient. Easy to walk to restaurants and shops.
Liked everything about the New York Palace. Will definately come back.

title: “Excellent service! Great breakfast!”
text: Stayed here 1 night. Decent room, clean and comfortable bed. Kids enjoyed the pool - looked like a great fitness area - nice machines. Breakfast buffet was excellent! Everyone from the front desk, valet, baggage guy, to the waiters was really nice and helpful. Would stay here again and it's an easy walk to the Capitol.

title: “Location Location Location”
text: I really couldn't tell you what amenities were offered at this hotel because I was out exploring during the day and only returned to my room to freshen up for dinner and of course, sleep. My boyfriend and I spent 3 nights at this hotel and we had no problems at all. Of course, we LOVED the location. We took the subways everywhere...and the hotel is within walking distance to Macy's and Times Square. Rooms were clean and smelled a little musty...but that was only noticeable the first day. We booked the room on hotels.com for about $160/night. Excellent price for this location!

title: “$680.00 per night - bad value”
text:
I was at this hotel on a one night business stay. I could not find a decent hotel any where in New York at a cheaper rate at this time of the year. I booked the Hilton thinking that I would get what my money was worth, but how wrong could I have been.
My company paid $680.00 per night for an executive room, the room was big but it was very dated and in need of modernisation.
The furniture was old and needed to be replaced.
The morning of my meeting I woke up to find my shower was not working. My husband had to call twice before anyone came up.
This hotel is very busy; the reception area is full of business travellers. There are also lots of conferences going on at this hotel.
I missed the complimentary breakfast in the executive lounge but my husband said that is was pretty bad and not even worth eating.
The hotel is in a very good location and that about the only good thing.
Overall the stay was ok but I would have expected more for the money my company paid!

title: “Best location and cozy hotel”
text: Very clean hotel, staff is really nice and happy to help. Located in the heart of Time Square, great restaurents and night live around the corner.

title: “An odd mix”
text: This Embassy Suites, in so many ways, is a typical ES. They have a nice lobby, good business center to print boarding passes for free, good airport shuttle, and good breakfast/manager's reception. The rooms are largely the same as other ES, though the rooms seem a little older, especially the bathrooms. But, the outside feels so much like a motel it was almost disconcerting. We first went to the wrong address, as they have clearly moved since our GPS was updated, and thought we must be going to a nifty new hotel as many on 24th street appear to be. However, the outside made me feel a bit down. I could not complain about anything inside, pool, food, etc., we even used the shuttle twice (once at night to return the car and be done with that drama--ES picked us up at the rental car return building), but outside it just felt weird. Very silly I guess as we got a good rate for near the airport, and I guess I would stay there again, but i would probably request a room on the 3rd or 4th floors.

title: “Good Service and Wonderful Location”
text:
Located on Wilshire Boulevard the Palomar is near UCLA and close to the dining options of Westwood Village. Booked through a very special offer on their website and got some extra benefits by applying as a Kimpton member (free wi-fi, mini bar bonus). No other hotel came close to the rate.
Got an upgrade and stayed in a wonderful room on a high floor, with a nice view. The room is very modern and updated with a comfortable double bed, a sitting sofa and working desk. It was large enough for us and our suitcases.
It is a very short drive to Rodeo Drive and Hollywood as well as on the way to Santa Monica, so it is on a central location to explore LA, on a quiet part of the busy Wilshire Boulevard. Many options for breakfast in Westwood.
Staff were very nice, especially the Concierge - Josue Ticas - who before arrival asked if we nedded anything special and so on and when we got to the room there was a complimentary bottle of wine. Very nice man !

title: “Really enjoyed the Standard”
text:
We stayed 3 nights at the Standard in Downtown for our honeymoon and to catch an NBA game and go shopping in Santee Alley.
Overall the experience was great. Was worried about the noise factor considering the other reviews, but didn't have any problems except a dog (terrier?) barking next door at 3am on our last night. The dog shut up after a verbal assault from my wife! 
I think it may have helped that we chose a non-smoking floor as smokers tend to party and drink more I believe. This meant we rarely heard other people while we were in our room.
Bed was nice and big with new sheets and comforter. Was surprised to find some shampoo, conditioner and soap provided as well as bathrobes! Massive TV and Nichiguchi stereo was also nice. 
Didn't have much to do with the staff, but they were courteous.
We checked out at 4-30am during which their computer system was down, so we weren't issued with a reciept or charge list. Hopefully nothing scary will be billed to my credit card.

title: “Trendy Luxury Hotel in a Great Location”
text:
I stayed here in early June when I went to LA for business and attended the MTV Movie Awards. This was exactly as billed: a luxury high end hotel set in the LA nightlife scene. This is not a family hotel --- but does anyone expect it to be?
By day, guests are spotted enjoying bloody mary's by the pool and, by night, cocktails in downstairs lobby. The room was comfortable and modern. Room service was prompt. Restaurants and bars were pricey but excellent.

title: “Central Location but terrible service”
text: This hotel is centrally located in Manhattan but I would advise avoiding it. They increased the price of our stay by 20% and charged it to my credit card without authorisation. The cleaners woke us every morning, despite the do not disturb sign on the door. The reception staff were very unhelpful. The rooms are tiny, even by New York standards. Certainly not worth $250 per night!!

title: “Convenient, Clean, and Cozy”
text: This hotel was very professional during a very busy time: weddings, the hottest weekend of the year with slow elevators due to the heat, and a busy and eager baseball crowd. Our room was spotless and comfy with a nice view. The fitness center is very new and spacious. The pool isn't great; but it did seem like the kids in there enjoyed it. Everyone who worked there was very kind. The parking was a pretty good deal, too (considering the other rates we paid in Mid-Atlantic cities). Also, the Sheraton is a stone's throw to both Camden Yards and the Inner Harbor. I love to see great cities come back, as Baltimore has! It's a testament to the city, the people, and nice hotels like the Sheraton.

title: “Great location and really helpful staff”
text: Ideally placed , 10 minutes from Union square. I am so glad we chose this location for our city break rather than the very commercial and down market Fishermans wharf. Go for the signature rooms as you get free WiFi. We had a package that included valet parking which was great and the parking guys were really obliging. Rooms were good size , we were a family of four and had two double beds on the 15th floor. Concierge was good fun and again full of great tips and info. We ate dinner in Bobs Steak house which was good but expensive . Ate breakfast out so can't comment. Definately a great place to stay plus opposite 555 California st which will mean something to Clint Eastwood fans.

title: “Best stay in NYC ever!”
text:
I can not say enough good things about this hotel. My fiance' and I stayed here from Oct 14th to Oct 16th. I can honestly say that I have never experienced better service from a hotel in my life. It all started with Gary helping us withour bags. We arrived at 12:30 Pm and our room was not ready yet (not exactly a surprise it was early) Our The front desk took our cell phone numbers, Gary, placed our lugage in storage and we went to go get lunch. The room was ready in less then an hour as promised. 
Also Mohammed was so helpful throughout the trip as well. I never felt like someone cared so much about my self and my fiance even though all he was doing was getting a cab for us. 
My fiance' can only eat brown rice. When we wanted to find a good sushi place that served brown rice the concierge was so helpful. She called around until we found the right place for our needs. I wish I took her name. 
The also served a very nice continental breakfast in the lobby as well. My fiance and I really felt like we were being treated as if we were the two most important people in the world the entire time we stayed here.

title: “Great hotel, Excellent Staff”
text: My husband and I spent three nights at the Brentwood Inn recently while we were in town for a wedding. We were looking for a reasonably priced hotel, and a family member recommended the Brentwood. We were thrilled with the hotel's location (minutes from Santa Monica and a beautiful drive up highway 1 to Malibu), clean (though slighly small) rooms, and a fantastically helpful and welcoming staff. We highly recommend it, and will certainly be back ourselves!

title: “Hotel Metro a real find”
text: A lovely stay. Kind people at the desk. A surprisingly nice continental breakfast. My room was quite large. As a single traveler I'm often given a closet. Small bathroom but perfectly nice. I'd stay here in a minute. As there was a lot of snow on the roof and repairs were underway, the amazing roof deck was closed. I peeked out and wasn't prepared for the stunning view of the Empire State Building! For the on-line price you can't beat it.

title: “Clean, quiet room, great staff!”
text: Quiet neighborhood. Extremely helpful staff. Clean room. The city was foggy during our stay. Raymond helped us figure out when's the best time to see the Golden Gate Bridge by logging on to a live webcam on his computer. He is just amazing!

title: “Small Clean Room”
text: We stayed at the Grand Hyatt October 7-9. Our room was small but clean and comfortable. The bathroom has poor lighting and is very small but that is my only complaint. The hotel lobby is under renovation but it did not disrupt our time at the hotel. The market store in the hotel is very convenient for coffee on your way out in the morning and late night snacks. The location and access to public transportation is excellent.

title: “"My business trip stay from now on"”
text: A few weeks ago I was in on business. There have been a couple of different hotels I have stayed in when down in DC on business, but this was my first time at The Normandy. Let's just say it will now be my regular stay in DC. This wi-fi was great, the rooms gorgeous, decor beautiful, the bed extremely comfortable, the hotel quiet, all of my business stops were easily accessible, and the staff was exceptional. Great job on this property Doyle Collection.

title: “Dirty!!!! and out dated”
text: A co-worker and I stayed at this location on december 7th for one night.Upon arriving at 7:00 pm my co-worker checked into his room first and once in room found that room was not cleaned from previous guest. The staff did upgrade him to a suite but it was not all that clean either. As i entered my room I wanted to take a shower after a long drive...went to get in and my tub looked like someone had shaved in it...hair everywhere and also all around bathroom....the heating unit in room did not work right and was very loud...louder than anyone i have ever heard before....I would suggest staying at the HIE a couple miles away (holiday inn express southeast indianapolis)

title: “Great Hotel. Clean and Quiet”
text:
Are a very nice hotel. Quiet rooms, very clean and in a decent location that allowed us to walk all the best attractions within 10 to 15 min. The staff are also particularly nice. the bedding is fantastic! 
While the breakfast was decent, our one complaint is their use of those environmentally unfriendly disposable Styrofoam and plastic plateware and knives and forks. Every morning there filling up bags and bags of these be hauled off to the local dump. We assume. With that sort of volume we would've preferred to see them use normal plate where I just wash it.
Still, we would recommend this hotel as it was very nice

title: “A Saved Vacation”
text: We just came back from a 3 day vacation and here is our story. We sadly could not stay with you guys at the beginning because you guys were all booked up so we had to go elsewhere. Well, our elsewhere was horrible and they treated us very poorly and just when I thought our vacation was over, my husband said let me check with Paradise again maybe there might be an opening and so he called and you guys were able to save our vacation! You guys were able to get us in without any hassles and you made one little 2 year old very happy along with her parents! We can't thank you guys enough and I already have told all our friends and family to go down and check you guys out whenever they get the chance cause I know they will have a fantastic time, just as we did:) I will recommend you guys to everyone:) thanks again:) Danielle

title: “Great staff at Amalfi”
text: I stayed with a group of 7 and had a great stay. Although we did not initially get the adjacent room I'd requested, they were able to make it happen and we had a rollaway bed there in minutes. Room was clean and well kept up. The complimentary breakfast on each floor was a nice touch! I would definitely recommend this hotel in downtown Chicago, but search around the bargain websites as the hotels website/list prices are much more expensive.

title: “Best Service in Chicago”
text: This might not be the newest, swankiest hotel in Chicago, but you cannot beat the Peninsula service. From the doorman to the servers in the restaurant, concierge, room service staff, and housekeeping, the service just shines here. The location of the hotel is perfect for shopping and restaurants. We had afternoon tea at the Lobby, which was just divine. The rooms were not exactly modern, but spatious and decorated with warm tones. TV in the bathroom made a lot of sense as we caught up on morning news while getting ready. I would definitely come back here when I return to Chicago.

title: “Incredible Staff !”
text: During our Annual Seminar I had the pleasure of staying here. I had not been back since the renovations and was impressed with what they have done with the place. The dek staff there is fantastic - I stayed in a room in the tower across the driveway from the lobby. It had a great feel with nice amenities. I would definately stay here again.

title: “Very nice hotel, but...”
text:
We stayed for 1 night - the hotel is very well maintained, staff was very nice, location is great!
But, our room (702) was facing the Boston Library, and there was an engin noise coming out of that building all night long.
I would stay again in his hote, buy stay away from room facing the library.

title: “Historic and Wonderful”
text:
My husband and I travelled to San Francisco in May 2008 to visit family and planned 3 nights alone together at the St. Francis to celebrate our upcoming 15th wedding anniversary. The first two nights we paid for and we cashed in our Starwood points for the 3rd night. 
We had heard the older tower was small and not as modern, so we opted for a grand deluxe room in the newer tower and it was WONDERFUL. The Westin heavenly bed (exquisite bedlinens) and heavenly bath (large marble bath with 2 shower heads) were romantic and everything we could have dreamed of. Our room was quite large and had a breath-taking view of the city and the golden gate bridge. It also had a flatscreen tv, desk, leather chairs and a soft chaise lounge. It was all very clean, comfortable and perfect.
The history of the hotel really appealed to me. As a classic movie fan, it was really cool to sleep where Ingrid Bergman, Charlie Chaplin and Ernest Hemingway once stayed. The lobby has several columned display cases with artifacts from each decade and we also purchased the book in the gift shop which had all of these items scanned and all the amazing stories of this hotel's rich history. 
The staff we met in the halls and in elevators were friendly and for the most part, every need we had was met very well. I especially appreciated being able to print boarding passes and check-in to our flight in a secluded corner of the lobby. 
We ate outside the hotel except for anniversary martini's at Caruso's - -$14 each was a little steeper than I would have expected, but it was a classy place, the service was excellent (despite being a busy Sat night), we were served pretzels and water as well and the drinks tasted delicious.
My only beef with our stay at the St. Francis was the "nickel and diming" that seems to be a staple of the Sheraton hotel chain. We bought some food from Whole foods and removed some items from the minibar to refrigerate them - they were scanned from our fridge and we were charged $89.00. When we realized this was the case, we looked at the card in the room and it stated there was also a $25.00 re-stock and cleaning fee. But I calmly phoned the desk, and all of those charges were all removed without delay. The gentleman I talked to was polite, respectful and I was very pleased with his response. 
We also had some minor service issues. For one, we were told at check-in that our 3rd night was our starwood night and we could keep our same room and not have to report to the desk at all after night #2. But our 2nd morning, we were informed by the desk clerk that we needed to have our keys re-programmed. It was only a couple of minutes, and again everything was friendly and professional, but were given differing information by different staff which was frustrating.
Also, when I called to inquire about internet fees, we were told by 2 different staff members that it was included no charge with our room. When our last, gratis night was complete we got a bill for all of our internet usage. When I took that bill to the front desk at check-out, I encountered my first rude staff member. The gentleman at the desk was quite abrupt that I was misinformed. Eventually he admitted "30 dollars isn't a big deal and we'll remove it from your bill. But it is not free". His snarky implication that I was just being cheap frustrated me since 2 other staff had told us this. There seems to be a lapse in communicating policies among staff and while it certainly didn't ruin the experience, it was frustrating.
Another reviewer mentioned the tower elevator. I agree it was swift but despite being easily car sick, the rise was usually over fast and the awesome view made up for it. We probably caught the elevator 15 times during our stay and only once were we waiting more than a couple of minutes for an elevator car during the peak check-in time in the afternoon.
I LOVED this hotel. It was close to shopping and restaurants, beautiful, quiet, felt quite safe, classy and most of the staff really went the extra mile. We plan to return since we have family in the area, and I wouldn't hesitate to stay at the St. Francis again.

title: “Try a different hotel for now.”
text: This hotel offers little and charges much. It has no amenities, ie., no restaurant, no fitness center, no business center, no parking, and no airport shuttles. The elevator broke twice during a weekend stay. The rooms are cubicle sized. My room had neither a full-length mirror nor a bathtub, just a shower. Good points: location, I guess. And the bed was comfortable. Ostensibly, they are going to add a restaurant, fitness center, etc, but right now, their advertising boasts about how much they offer when the reality is otherwise. For me, paying $199 nightly for something barely better than a dorm room hurts.

title: “Location is awesome!”
text: This hotel had a great location, the center of San Francisco! The price was great considering the location. The only downfall was the size of the rooms. The rooms were very small but clean. The location makes it great!

title: “felt like home”
text: From ythe moment we arrived for the weekend until we left 3 days later, the service and staff weere great. I forgot some toiletries and they were delivered in less that 5 minutes by housekeeping. Great bed!

title: “Great stay at the Fairmont”
text:
Stayed 5 nights last week with my 75 yr old parents. Service was great. All the staff were so friendly especially Lasheema the receptionist. Room was nice and quiet. Beds were so comfy. Agree with previous reviews that tv was quite small but it didn't spoil anything for us....would have liked USA today though each morning as opposed to the New York times. We were in a deluxe room which had a lovely view over the courtyard.
15 minute walk to Georgetown (very lively with so many restaurants and shops)but we tended to get the bus or a cab when our feet were aching at the end of the day. Just bit too far to waste time walking to the mall but foggy bottom metro stop is only 5 minutes away.
Had the breakfast in the hotel once which was lovely but $26 each. Most mornings we went to the uptowner cafe nearby. 
Really enjoyed Washington. So much to see and do.

title: “Great visit”
text:
We spent two nighs recently.
Great location next to Little Italy.
Walking distance to Inner Harbor and Fells Point. The free city shuttle bus, the Charm City Circulator stops near the hotel though we chose to walk to all attractions. 
The hotel was very nice and offered a full breakfast everyday. The room was large with a nice view towards the Inner Harbor. There is a great Latin American 
restaurant, Talara, next to the hotel.
I would definitely stay there again.

title: “LOVED IT - A MUST-STAY!”
text:
My husband and I came to Penn's View for our little getaway from the suburbs. We love the Old City so the location was perfect. The hotel prices were really affordable - cheaper than at the big skyscraper chains in the area. 
The place is charming, the rooms are big and beautiful. We had a jacuzzi suite, which was great. Our window faced the back street, so it was nice and quiet. We loved everything about our stay! The staff was very nice and friendly and our host - Antonio - extremely helpful. 
During our stay we had lunch at the Restorante Panorama and their homemade pasta dishes were amazing! The wines are incredible and the wine bar is pretty cool to see as well.
We loved it and will be back!!!

title: “Good Hotel and Great, though touristy Area”
text:
Just got back from San Fran.
This is a fairly good hotel. I booked with the Friends and Family Rate and so I saved a bundle. Got the 4th floor.
The front lobby area and common hallways/areas are actually very nice and modern.I found the front desk clerk quite friendly.
The rooms looked average though, with old box style TVs, No Wireless Internet (had wired though) and furniture that is a bit worn.
The rooms and hotel in general were kept quite clean and organized. Breakfast was chaotic. It would open at 6:30am and would be packed. It was standard HIE breakfast and suited myself and my family just fine.
Watch out for parking. 43/night! 
If I visit San Fran again, I'd probably stay again thanks to consistent service, standards and location.

title: “Really accommodating Staff; typical excellent Marriott”
text:
This Marriott had the expected great customer service from check-in, through your stay, to check-out. Rooms were clean, comfortable and quiet. Fluffy towels, soft pillows, quality beds and bedding, all as we have come to expect from Marriott. 
Bar on second floor was nice. Loved the Starbucks in the lobby. This hotel is directly across Fannin Street from the entrance to Methodist Hospital and is convenient for that whole medical and academic area.

title: “boutique motel”
text: Farmer's Daughter has an odd mix of attributes. It definitely has the feel of an old motel, but some stylish updating, lively public spaces, and a good location make it a pleasant choice. My room had a good radio with iPod dock and a small fridge. Nice towels, but no robe.

title: “Wonderful Stay At The Affinia Dumont”
text: I come to New York every summer with my teenage daughter. Usually we stay in Times Square which she loves & I hate. This year we stayed at the Affinia Dumont in Murrey Hill. I can not say enough about this hotel! Wonderfully helpful staff! We stayed for two weeks & they upgraded us to a bigger corner room with 2 beds. Quiet neighborhood, with a corner market. The subway is right around the corner. I'll be staying again next year.

title: “Love this place!”
text: I stay here almost weekly and love it. It's new, clean, staff are always courteous, and it's very close to work. Fitness center has all sorts of gear (even if it is a little cramped), and it's only about a mile to good eating, shopping, etc. One of the best hotels I use!

title: “Never again”
text:
This was a depressing hotel. The room was barely adequate, I wondered if I was going to come down with something just staying there one night.
I was booked for three nights, made it through the first night, decided life was too short to be miserable.
Parking is odd, the people staying there were out of a Fellini film, the staff was not helpful, the room was dark and dank.
Never again.

title: “Best Western”
text: The Best Western Seaport is a nice, clean hotellocated "downtown," meaning it's a quite far from mid-town(Times Square, theaters, central park). It is within walking distanceof the Statue of Liberty ferry, the WTC, the Seaport (which is a nice,touristy area with ships, shops, and restaurants). The Brooklyn bridgeis right next to the hotel (you can't hear it, though). Interestingly,the hotel basically shares the parking lot with the famous"Fulton Fish Market," which is something you should considerbefore going here. For starters, there is often a "fishy"smell in the air (though not in the hotel), which may or may notbother you (I didn't mind at all). Another drawback is that, fromabout 11:00 PM until 9:00 AM Sunday through Monday, the hectic marketis within earshot. The first night, there were car alarms going off,trucks driving by, people yelling -- all night long. On the weekends,the whole area is pretty quiet. We got used to it real quick, but,again, it's something to consider. One last thing to consider aboutthe location is that it is a nice little walk to the nearest subwaystation (I'd say 5-10 minutes), but you can catch either of the twosubway lines (A or C) that go to mid-town Manhattan (either West ofcentral park [the A] or East [the C]. The hotel has a deal with alocal driving company; they called a "cab" for me and aMercedes pulled up, which charged a couple bucks more than a yellowcab. To get a yellow cab, you'd have to walk up about one shortblock.About the hotel...the rooms we saw were very clean and spacious(for NY standards). The 6th floor has some cool terraces overlookingthe river towards Brooklyn. Each room has a tiny refrigerator, iron,tv, and desk. In the lobby, there's a handy "businessoffice" with free internet access, which was nice. There iscontinental breakfast each morning which included bagels, fruit,cereal, oj, danishes, and croissants. There is also a nice deli nextdoor which is pretty much open all the time because it serves the fishmarket. They have full breakfasts there. There are four bars /restaurants right by the hotel. The staff there seemed excellent andvery helpful towards tourists. We had no problems and greatly enjoyedour stay. Suggestions from a first-timer......if you do the Statue ofLiberty, go early as the crowds are obnoxiously large. You can takethe ferry at Battery Park (which starts 8:30 or 9:00, depending on theseason). The ferry runs from the Statue to Ellis Island, to BatteryPark and back. If I went again, I'd take the first ferry and get offat Ellis Island (which is nice) before the crowds got there. You can'tclimb the statue anymore, so there's no point rushing that....TheCloisters (part of the Metropolitan Museum of Art) is worth the tripway uptown, provided you don't take a cab (which would be $$$). Asubway will get you pretty close (ask around; everyone knows everysubway route it seems), and a bus actually will get you to thedoor. The Metropolitan is nice, too. Personally, I would skip theMuseum of Natural History because it's basically like any big-cityMuseum (dummies wearing costumes, stuffed animals, paintedbackdrops)....Chinatown is within walking distance of Best Western andis worth the trip. It's basically like visiting China, and is verylarge. There are tons of shops and restaurants....Central Park is coolfor people watching, but very confusing if you're actually trying tofind places within it like "the castle," the carousel, orthe Alice in Wonderland section. Walking from one side to another isless than a mile, I'd guess....To get around, you can currently buy a"Fun Pass" (you can use credit cards at vending machines inlarger subway terminals) for $7 which will let you ride the subways orbuses all day. You just scan each time. This is nice if you're tryingto pack in a lot of stuff in one day without paying cab fare. To giveyou an idea, a cab ride from Times Square to the Statue of Libertywill run you about $14ish before tip....Ray's Pizza near Times Squareis highly recommended.Have fun!

title: “Fine”
text: I stayed at this hotel for a conference. The hotel and rooms were clean and tidy. I was very happy with the fitness center. The staff were very helpful. The hotel was, shall we say, a bit "retro".. it could use a workover. Overall the hotel was fine. The one big disappointment was that there was no breakfast included in the price, which, for the price (~$135 per night) is not great. The internet access wasn't cheap either, though the wireless internet in the lobby was free. My work paid for the hotel, so I won't complain too much, but if you are paying yourself, or looking for "good value", then I would look for somewhere else to stay.

title: “Excellent hotel”
text:
Stayed here for three nights and loved it!
The whole hotel was spotlessly clean and treally quiet. The bed was so comfortable so we got a great nights sleep! Every morning we got a complimentary newspaper delivered to our room, which was a really nice touch.
The staff are lovely and gave us some great advice about shopping, sightseeing and transport. 
The hotel is in a perfect location for seeing Boston
I would absolutely stay here again!

title: “Clean, reasonably priced, best for travelers with a car”
text:
I stayed here for a work trip and found the hotel to be mostly fine, but there were a few issues. It was clean, the staff was friendly, and it is very reasonably priced. The breakfast buffet was kind of expensive for fruit, yogurt, some pastries and coffee, but whatever. The room was mostly fine, but there is an air vent that is constantly blowing cold air on you when you first enter the room, and it can't be shut off. Some folks might not mind that, but I didn't like it as I get cold easily.
The big issue with this hotel is that the location is not all that great if you don't have a car. The hotel offers a free shuttle to Union Station (and a few other stops) and back, but in the early evenings it is VERY sporadic, and calling a cab in DC is a futile effort - they take at least 45 minutes to get there. There is a metro station near the campus, but that is a considerable walk if you have luggage as the hotel is located inside the campus.
I would stay here again, but probably only if I had a car or didn't need to go anywhere in the evening.

title: “Perfect location.... decent room. Great bars, restaurants!!”
text: Just got to stay one night for business... but will definetly be staying again. This is the perfect location for restaurants, bars and all downtown attractions. The zoo is a cheap cabfare ride away.

title: “Over It”
text:
I stayed at the W Hotel three years and enjoyed it, but this visit was extremely disappointing. Instead of cool and cutting-edge, it now feels dated and in need of refreshing. 
To start with the positive, all of the staff have been courteous and professional. It's unfortunate that their politeness is not enough to make this hotel a worthwhile place to stay.
The hotel did not honor my request of a high-floor room far from the elevator (even though it was made both through my travel agent at the time of booking and AGAIN with a same-day call the morning of check-in). Instead, I was placed on the fourth floor in the room ADJACENT to the elevator, low enough that I could hear the constant music playing in the lobby. When I complained, I was told the only other available room in the whole hotel was a smoking room. Normally, this wouldn't bother me, but when I was dispatched to this room, I was appalled. The room smelled as though 50 people had been chain-smoking in their all night long. There were burns on the carpet and duvet, in addition to chipped paint on the desk and black scuff marks all over the wall. The room was so filthy I wouldn't have taken off my shoes, never mind slept in the bed. Another call, this time to the manager. Finally, I was place in a room on a high floor, and while it's fine, it's absolutely NOT worth the price.
The music that blasts from the lobby 24/7, the pitch-black elevators that are reminiscent of an 80's strip club, and the trying-too-hard-to-be-trendy-but-not-trying-at-all-to-comfortable rooms make this a hotel best enjoyed by those under 25. Which, by the looks of it, is exactly who stays there. If you're traveling for business (or just like your peace and quiet), stay elsewhere. Stop by the Beach Bar with the fire pit for a drink, but don't consider sleeping at this place....you won't actually sleep at all.

title: “Excellent for Family Vacation”
text:
We chose the Hampton Inn for our 5 day family vacation. The location is excellent, within walking distance to the Verizon Center, Metro, Shops, Museums, Tourist attractions and Restaurants. 
The free breakfast is any thing but your ordinary continental breakfast. Every day they had a new egg based item (omelet, scrambled eggs) and a new meat (pork sausage, bacon, ham). They always had fresh mixed fruit, apples, bananas, oatmeal, packaged cereal, 6-7 different yogurts and a wide assortment of baked goods. 
On our second day our bathtub began to leak and they quickly swapped our room and gave us a price break for the inconvenience. 
The staff was always courteous, especially Simon the concierge. He helped us book tours, catch cabs and made sure we saw everything we wanted to see. 
We would definitely recommend this hotel again. 
I took one spot off for cleanliness due to the room swap and one off for sleep quality. The beds were very comfortable but didn't have the extreme lush feel as the Hilton Heavenly so I took one mark away. 
Only slight issue was heavy use of the elevator and a sometimes long wait.

title: “Great value for the money...”
text:
I was a bit skeptical about heading to San Francisco... I wanted to be near my conference, but didn't want to spend that much to stay AT that hotel... Plus, I'm a smoker. San Francisco is pretty much a non-smoking city, including most of the hotels. Bummer.
Fortunately, my request was honored - the hotel has ONE last floor that is smoking (which one of the front desk guys mentioned they were considering getting rid of it), but I can't tell you how stoked I was to be able to smoke in my room (advice to mgmt of SFD - there is a market for allowing smokers to honestly smoke in their rooms. 99% of the hotels in your city won't let it happen, but personally I will pay more for the privelege. Just a thought).
My room was two double beds- I would have prefered a king, but oh well. The bathroom was a bit small but not a big deal. Good use of the space, at least. Large closet, free wifi, free coffee until 6:30am (after which I could buy coffee in the cafe), all-in-all I was very impressed with the hotel, the location and how nice all the staff was. 
I can't say that I've had any other experiences at all with hotels in this city, but unless they eliminate the smoking floor, I'm certain I'll be back.

title: “SAVED OUR TRIP!”
text:
We originally stayed at a Hampton further north that was closer to our friends we were visiting. It was a disaster as the air never worked and it was over 90 the whole weekend. After the second night of them not fixing the air, we gave up and moved down to the Cambria Suites. Our kids loved the room and we were all wishing we'd spent the entire time there. We are actually spending another long weekend here in August, just because the last stay was so great. There is a ton of good food (fantastic Indian restaurant!) all near the close Polaris Mall. It's easy to get around Columbus from here, and well worth the price. Oh yeah, and the staff was wonderfull!
STAY HERE!!!

title: “BYOP (Bring your own pillow!)”
text:
Pros: Cheapest hotel within walking distance of Riverwalk that allows pets for no extra charge. The room has just the bare minimum that most hotels get by with, but it was clean. The staff was friendly, though they very busy. 
Cons: Very busy on the weekend, lots of kids and large families going to Sea World and lot of rowdy kids running and screaming in the hallway. You can hear everything going on in the hallway. I woke up every time someone slammed their door. My biggest problem with this hotel was the bed and pillows. We had the king suite, and the mattress was so old and hard, and it sloped towards the center of the bed. My husband and I were sliding towards the center all night. At one point I made a pallet on the floor and tried to sleep that way. The pillows were rock hard and overstuffed, so our necks were killing us for 2 days. 
Overall, it's a mediocre hotel that is plenty sufficient for those who want to be close to riverwalk or who have a dog as long as you are just planning to stay for a night or 2 (max). It's economy over comfort. Just bring your own pillows, and you'll probably be fine.

title: “Good value for $”
text:
Nice little place. Building old but well maintained and clean. Our room was quite spacious and had a kitchen and small living room as well as adequate closet space.
Breakfast was adequate, not huge. The balcony and its furnishings looked old but serviceable. It was very clean up there and comfortable place to enjoy the evening cool.
The location for the Balboa park is great. A 10 to 15 min walk to the zoo a major bonus. The downside is that there are no stores or restaurants nearby. There is a bus stop very nearby (the #7 bus) that goes downtown and that solved most of our shopping/dining requirements during our 3 day - 2 night stay at Balboa Park inn. 
Staff were friendly and advice they gave was helpful.

title: “Perfect stay”
text:
Loved it!
There was a LONG line to check in on Sunday at 1pm. Fortunately, the hotel had 4 or 5 people checking guests in so it only took 10-15 minutes. An hour later I came down to the lobby and there was nobody in line. 
Our room was on the top floor (40) of the south tower and it was AWESOME! It was very clean and stylish with a terrific water view.
We got assistance from the concierge desk for a dinner spot (Some Pie - Pizza) which was fantastic. 
The hotel was very centrally located about two blocks from the airport light rail line. There was also a monorail that ran from the space needle to the west lake shopping center which was across the street. Pikes Place Market is about 5 blocks straight towards the water. 
Honestly, I have no idea why this hotel is not rated higher on trip advisor. Although it is pricey, we thought it was fabulous.

title: “Great hotel”
text: The rooms are pretty clean and comfortable and the price worth it. The service is very friendly and helpful. It's not an expensive hotel considering that it's located in one of the best areas, in downtown Phoenix, you have a lot of places near and also the metro.

title: “Great Location, Great with kids too”
text:
After a bad start to our arrival in NYC, it was such a joy to find a wonderful place stay! My poor daughter lost her special toy in a cab on the way there from the airport and the staff were as helpful as they could be in ringing the cab company and telling us what else we could do (unfortunately with no luck!)
So with 2 small kids we loved this place, the rooms were great and loved the convenience of the subway to the hotel and of course Fairways supermarket across the road to stock up on snacks and supplies for breakfast etc. The rooms were large and very confortable and clean...the house keepers were super friendly too. We used the guest laundry, which was handy for a family that had been travelling for a few weeks to clean and wash our clothes. You could also make an easy walk to the red tourist bus route as well.
We are all desperate to come back to NYC one day and I would stay here again.

title: “Not quite what I expected”
text: We were in San Francisco for 6 days, and we stayed at the Monarch.They were nice enough to check us in early,but the room had a slight smell and a view of the apartment that was 10 feet away. The bed was clean,but the pillows really really flat,and I am not a pillow person.It was cold in the room so bring warm socks(this was in Aug), warm pajamas and a pillow.The washrooms were clean and the bathtub deep.The safe did not work and if the temp.outside was hot,we would be in trouble,because it the AC was missing knobs.The tv had 15 channels and HBO( a few great movies).The Wi-Fi worked and the morning coffee was good. The biggest problem was that the area was loud at night with the homeless and druggies talking/yelling until 1am.In the morning the homeless were very visable and at night,I would not want to be coming in late if you are on your own. SO the hotel it self is worth the savings,but the area I something to really really consider and I am a city girl.Stay in little Italy or near the Warf,these are the cleaner and safer areas. Enjoy your time in San Francisco!

title: “Excellent Hotel, Lousy Location”
text:
My wife and I stayed here for two nights in December. We booked this on Priceline, we bid $55.00 and would up paying about $72. per night with taxes.
First the positives.
-The room was very large and clean.
-It had a full kitchen that had a microwave, a two burner electric stovetop and a full size refrigerator. The kitchen also had very nice selection of utensils, dishes, pots and other cooking implements.
-The breakfast buffet is one of the nicest that I have seen. People who are on Atkins or other diets should have no problems here.
-Parking (valet) was $20.00 per night, which is about $10.00 cheaper than other locations in DC.
Now the negatives
-Noise.The hotel is on a triangular piece of land and there is a lot of traffic on the streets. We were on the 9th floor (which was great considering that we booked the room on Priceline) and I still heard traffic noise. One morning garbage trucks came at 5:30 and woke me up. Their noise continued for about a half an hour.
-Homeless people. When we came back to the hotel at night, there were homeless people in front of the hotel begging. I don't expect this at a hotel that bills itself as a 3 or 3 1/2 start hotel.
-Safety. My wife and I went to dinner Sunday night at Georiga Browns several blocks away. We walked back to the hotel, which is only about 3 blocks away from the restaurant and I thought we were going to get mugged. The streets were deserted and what few people who were on the street looked like they were sizing us up. The next night when we went out to dinner, we took a cab back and forth. I have walked in many cities at night, but this was the most uncomfortable I have felt at night in a long time.
I can excuse the noise, but because of the safety issues, I cannot give this hotel a higher rating. I hate to rate this hotel as "okay". We got a great rate and their staff is terriffic, but because of the safety issue, I cannot recommend this hotel.

title: “Great location and service”
text:
We stayed in this hotel for Christmas, and it is in the middle of everything. Times Squere is 5 min. Lots of restaurant next to hotel, try the Turkish Antalia across the street. 
The staff in the hotel is very friendly and helpfull, rooms are on the small side, but anyway you will spend most of the time outside and enyoj the action and the vibe of NYC!

title: “Great stay at Courtyard”
text:
This hotel is a fantastic find in midtown. The rooms are at least 50% larger than are the ones at the Marriott Eastside located only minutes away - and they are much cheaper, including free internet access. Staff was very friendly. Ask for a high room if possible - the views are wonderful. 
Although the restaurant onsite does not offer room service, Courtyard has a deal worked out with the nearby Outback Steakhouse for delivery at a very reasonable charge. 
All rooms have been recently renovated, and have the most comfortable hotel beds I've experienced in a long, long time. Overall, this is a nice find in a great location. I would stay here again in a heartbeat.

title: “I like it !! The room is cute and i love it”
text:
I love the room and the staff was nice 
I saw a lot of people write bad review but i think this is kinda good room

title: “Hyatt Wild Oak review”
text:
We just returned from the Wild Oak for a 3-day mid week trip, & felt compelled to write a review since we read others here that were very helpful. 
It's a very nice place - it almost feels like a new apartment complex as opposed to a hotel, with separate 3-story buildings. More units planned but they're at least 1 year away from doing it - ground not even broken yet on them. Excellent resort for families/kids - the lazy river is long & clean, good little beach area, and there are approx 8 bungalow type spots with hammocks and chairs that are quite relaxing. Then another pool area with tall waterslide, and an indoor pool area with another waterslide, bball hoop, and sauna/steam room and a hottub outside. Also in this rec bldg is a gameroom with avg games(some broken) and decent workout facility. 
The pitch - like many we got the Hyatt flier in the mail numerous times, but finally decided to try it out since the price ($49) was so good. That price is for a "studio" which is 1 big room, & we upgraded to a 1 bedroom for $79 per that gave separate rooms.
Here's how it plays out - you go to a "reception room" and there's lots of salespeople (mostly younger college types) and they assign one to you - we were one of approx 10 different families/couples there at 8:30 am. The "rep" asks you some questions about your vacation habits - where, how often, how much budget yearly, etc - bascially to gather info to see if/how you may fit into their program. Then a quick video and "property tour" with a markup/model, and a golf cart ride to see a 2 bdr/2 bath unit. Then it's back to the reception area for a sitdown, where they finally get to the price - they started off at $30k with a certain down payment and this gets you approx 3 weeks per year to be used at any of their locations/partner hotels. Then if you object or laugh out loud they'll scale back and say how about 2 weeks or 1 week - does this fit your budget, is that better, etc? 
We said thanks but no thanks it's not for us, and it ended pretty quickly from there. Our guy did bring in his 3rd baseman manager to try to overcome our objections but we just said thanks but no thanks and that was that. You get your "gift" on the way out, which equates to $150 of credit/tickets/food comp, which was worth it for the 90 minute spiel. And it was 90 minutes on the button - if you ask a lot of questions or hem/haw during the final "here's what we can do for you phase", then I could see it lasting longer, but if you stay quiet but polite it goes by quick, and admittedly the idea/pitch makes some bit of sense. 
Biggest room for improvement would be the food - JBs is the only offering, and it has standard bar type fare that's very average, but nothing on the menu is over $10 so it's a decent option. And since it is geared toward families, after 9-10 pm there's nothing going on, so expect peace & quiet thereafter, not a party. 
All in all a very positive experience that my family loved, and we would return without hesitation.

title: “Don't do it!”
text: We were not given the room we paid for and staff was very rude switching us to what we had reserved. Someone had defecated beside the pool. Drains in bathroom would not drain. Sink stopper had gray slimy mass of hair, toothpaste and soap scum. No forks for breakfast. Mold in ice container, phone had a short in it. No alarm clock in bedroom.

title: “5 Star treatment with gorgeous rooms, lobby and lounge!!!”
text:
I can't believe that I waited so long to give this jewel of a property a try. I stay in Dallas about 4 to 8 nights a month and have stayed at all of the so called "4 and 5 diamond" properties. None of them in this area (Dallas/Ft. Worth) can touch the service, the ambience or the location of this property. Trust me when I say to all that this is a must try. Once you stay there, I believe you will be hooked. Not only did I feel like a star when I entered the lobby, but I actually saw several current movie and TV stars having a drink in their wonderful lounge. 
The Melrose Hotel has given me a bunch more reasons to stay in Dallas as much as I can. 
Thank you, Thank you, Thank you for the wonderful experience!!!!!!!

title: “Extremely Nice Medical Center Area Hotel”
text:
The Hilton was our choice for a business stay, and we were extremely pleased with the choice. The hotel was about 1 block away from the conference location. 
We arrived and were warmly greeted by staff in the parking area as well as the front desk. At 18th floor room had an awesome view of the Houston area, Rice University etc. out your window. The room was spacious, very modern, and the bed appeared brand new. 
Large bath with shower head that made a 6 foot 3 inch person comfortable. 
We didn't have time to check the restaurant, bar, or workout facilities, but I would stay here again any time. 
If you need to stay in the area of all the Houston hospitals, this is certainly an excellent option.

title: “Careful it's more than one hotel”
text:
This place used to be a dump so thumbs up for the remodeling or better said - restoration .. 
we arrived around 5 paying close to rack rate $290 and were assigned a room on 5th floor .. when asked about a room on higher floor were told the hotel was full and this was it .. everything on north side of hotel faces huge air conditioning fans .. not noisy but the vew encourages you to keep drapes closed .. Make sure you face west toward Congress Ave or get waaaay up high .. rooms are what you would expect but oddly configured .. impossible to see TV from the bed! 
The rates should be about $200 because there are better hotels in Austin at that rate.
don.brown@brownchild.com

title: “Great value.. mixed review”
text:
This is a great hotel to stay at in the hollywood area - not that you need that much time to visit! Hollywood & Highland is close (shopping). I would suggest anyone with perceptions of Hollywood Bld, walk of fame, etc all shiny - this is not so, it has a thin layer of glitz - but the vast number of homeless is sad to see!
The hotel offers a great free breakfast, and WIFI. Parking is $22 per night. The rooms are clean, modern - however I was placed in a very dark room, with a view of a wall under the hillside - very strange. Overall it's a great hotel - just don't ask for a quiet room :)

title: “Great Place...Great staff. Have to stay there”
text: Stayed there recently. Rooms were very nice, clean and well appointed. Staff was curious and knowledgeable. Highly recommend The French Quarters to my friends and colleagues.

title: “Great New Hotel”
text: Brand new hotel (effectively, it was stripped down to a shell and rebuilt) with very nice rooms - granite counters, big flat screen televisions, plush linens. Friendly staff and easy parking. We had a good breakfast and dinner in the restaurant - I just wish they were on the top floor which has a great view of the mountains. This hotel is a great alternative to the Camino Real for a downtown stay - both the public spaces and the rooms are a big step up.

title: “Very Close to the Space Needle...”
text:
Basically we wanted the closest budget hotel/motel to Seattle Center that had free parking AND a free breakfast; these two features are worth probably $30/day alone (for a family of 4).
Parking was not a problem and there were a limited number of covered spaces as well. The breakfast is a full buffet and tends to get very busy about 45 minutes before closing (0930). Coffee is good, and bacon, eggs, hashbrowns, etc. make it worth the 5-10 minute wait.
The indoor pool/hot tub is nice, especially with kids, and is open 24/7.
The rooms are a little tired but include a fridge and microwave.
Location is great - maybe 5 minutes to the Space Needle. You can walk to the Pike Place Market as well in 20-25 minutes or so.
The only real downside to this property is its age, though they were renovating while we were there. The pool area and halls didn't seem particularly clean but it wasn't really a problem. 
I have seen comments about no restaurants close by but there is a full food court near the Space Needle that was open until 7 p.m. while we were there. We also walked downtown to numerous restaurants (20 minutes) but could have taken the free bus if the weather was bad. McDonald's is only a couple blocks away as well...
All in all, not a bad deal for the location. Honestly, if you are a tourist on a budget then why would you want to spend 2 or 3 times as much for a fancy property? Spend the money on a nice restaurant, the local attractions or whatever!

title: “Good Hotel for a Good Price”
text:
