It's hard to find a good hotel in San Francisco at a decent price. I think I got this hotel for around $130 a night, which is a good price and the hotel was good. The staff are very nice, the rooms are clean. The location is great. It was very easy to get cabs everywhere. The walk to public transportation is a bit long, but when I'm on vacation, I tend to use cabs anyway so this didn't really bother me. 
As a bonus, the hotel also saved my life by offering same day dry cleaning service which I needed in an emergency. This accidentally got charged twice to the room, but as soon as I pointed it out to the front desk, they promptly fixed the problem so no harm done there - just good thing I checked the bill.

title: “Great Location and value for money”
text: When searching for Washington Hotels we were a bit dismayed as they seemed very expensive for anything within a reasonable distance of the major sights. After some persistence we found the GWU Inn that seemed to be a good price and had good reviews. We stayed 3 nights and were very pleased with the service and rooms provided by the hotel. We found that we had been upgraded to a one bedroom suite which was very spacious with a large living area, kitchenette and a separate bedroom with king bed. Our room looked out toward Georgetown and the Potomac and over the residential neighbourhood. We also looked at the Watergate Hotel we discovered where we found a Safeway grocery store with good supplies for breakfast and a couple of meals when we were too tired from all the museums and monuments). The exterior of the hotel and the lobby are plain and modest but the room was clean, well appointed and well equipped. It was an easy walk to Georgetown to all the boutiques and bars as well as the metro which took us in no time to the mall and the major attractions. At night it was quiet and the area surrounding the hotel was very safe. On top of all this it was good value for money. We thoroughly enjoyed our stay in Washington and at the GWU Inn and will be recommending this to other Australian friends.

title: “Don't stay here!”
text: We are a family of 5 with 3 kids under 10 who travels a couple of times a year. This is the first hotel in 20 years that I didn't leave a tip for room service. This hotel is filthy and was a complete disappointment. We had two king suites on the bay beach and stayed for 3 days. The only reason we continued our stay is because we were gone all day at the SD zoo and SeaWorld - otherwise we would have changed hotels. I can't believe American Express recommended this place. The furnishings look like the pictures but the rooms we stayed in smelled of mold and animal urine, the carpets were filthy and the travertine tile in both our suites had not been mopped and had hair throughout the suite. The rooms we stayed in had stains on the walls that could have been easily wiped up. The rooms has very poor ventilation and moisture builds up at night which intensifies the poor smell. You won't find a telephone book or a clock in these rooms or any kind of utensils other than the two tiny dirty glasses in the bathroom. So if you want to drink a glass of California wine - good luck. If our housekeeping was indicative of everyone else's experience, the entire department should be fired. They were very inconsistent. One day they brought coffee and one day they didn't. One day they forgot soap and then gave 2 soaps the next day. They made the bed and gave new towels but didn't clean the floors or vacuum the rug. Also - the beach on the side we stayed on is sad. The bay is not the ocean. Right outside our suite was some kind of concrete runoff gone amuck. It was a danger enough that I didn't feel comfortable having my 7 and 10 yr old play football in that area. To top it off, my 3 year old with sensitive skin got a rash all over his face the one night he slept on the hotel pillow rather than his pillow pet. I mentioned the cleanliness issue to the front desk as I checked out. She responded that it was an issue the hotel was addressing and took off my parking and internet charges. You won't see us back here. Stay at the Grand Pacific Palisades up in Carlsbad and you will have a much better experience!

title: “Great place to inflict your yappy dogs on strangers!”
text:
Great place to stay if you have a yappy barking dog you wish to inflict on others! Because the staff can't care less about it's barking annoying the other guests! Not so great if you want to sleep or work or think or NOT be serenaded by yapping dogs, sadly. 
The rooms are small, and have poor cell service, like ALL SF hotels. So no complaints about that. Decent amenities, decent decor, though not all rooms are as stylish as depicted (yet still have the failings of form-over-function design flaws-- in this case, very sharp toilet paper dispensers that look cool but in the middle of the night inflict wounds; non-functional heating requiring a call to the desk and 15 minute wait for ancient possibly dangerous space heater to be brought to your room, lack of trash can in room). 
Great location, and not bad price for the location. Some of the rooms and hallways smell like the thai restaurant located below the hotel, even on the top floor (at least this as true for 628). 
Staff are nice but ineffectual. I complained twice about the yapping squealing dog, was given earplugs when requested, but no real concern was exhibited. Rooms ought to come with white noise machines and proper, safe heating systems. 
For 200/night in SF, I don't expect a big room, but how hard is it to provide basic comforts, like safe heating when the temp is in the low 40's and some sort of noise guard? 
Also, possibly related to the Thai restaurant below, there were occasional fruit flies. That, the lack of a trash can, and the odd lipstick stain on the curtains led me to give a score of "poor" for cleanliness.

title: “Very Nice Hotel, Great Location”
text:
My wife and I went to Chicago for a weeding and stayed at the Crown Plaza two nights. We arrived at the hotel before it was time to check in and were told we would have to wait while a room was prepared. We went to the restaurant in the hotel for lunch and we both ordered the chicken wraps, they where "Horrible"... soggy, wilted lettuce doesn't taste good. After lunch we waited in the lobby for about 20mins and was told that our room was ready by the friendly staff. We where given a upgrade to a suite, as they said for being so patient.
The room had a great view of the city and the sitting area was very comfortable with the signature zebra chair.
Pros: Great location; easily walk to all of the great shopping; responsive and professional staff; comfortable room, great view.
Cons: $20.00 for the use of a microwave but brought up promptly and set up by maintenance. Not the greatest signal on the TV, but who is watching TV in such a great American city! Not the freshest smelling bathroom upon walking in for the first time.
Overall great hotel and would stay again!
.

title: “It was Okay...”
text: This hotel was okay. The staff is incredibly slow at checking in, but that's fine. The room was huge - it had TWO bathrooms! However, the bathrooms were so dirty that I wouldn't even touch the shower. It was old and kind of run down, but that was kind of expected. Not bad, but I probably wouldn't stay there again.

title: “great location, good price!”
text:
We stayed here for 4 nights in August, after looking at a bunch of different hotels on tripadvisor. We selected this one based on the positive reviews, the price and most of all the location!
We had a double room, with bridge view. The Golden Gate bridge isn't exactly very nearby, but it was clearly visible from our window. Very nice. The street below was a bit noisy, but not in a disturbing way. We slept very well all nights.
The hotel is within walking distance (downhill) of the Fisherman's Wharf area. If you're not too tired and in ok shape, it takes about 15 minutes to get there. There is also a busstop not far from the hotel, and with the excellent public transportation (get a MUNI passport!), you could anywhere easily.
Breakfast is cool - you make your own waffles! Additionally there's hot or cold cereal, bagels, muffins, juices, fruit, coffee/tea/cocoa. Nothing incredibly fancy, and not everything is very healthy perse, but it fills the stomach! 
Parking is a bit expensive - $26 + tax per night, however, it is in a sealed, secure parking garage underneath the hotel. You're not guaranteed a spot though. I'm not sure if it makes a difference, but we arrived on a monday, and had no trouble finding an empty spot. Once in, leave your car there for the whole stay, and use public transportation. It prevents frustration :)
All in all, we'd definitely come back again!

title: “Excellent value”
text: This hotel was great for the money. Great service, attentive. Left our car for 10 days, shuttle to airport. Snacks and any drink you wanted on Wed. evenings. Everything about this hotel, especially their staff, was great. uncovered parking, but safe, with restaurant next door and right off freeway. I would stay here again. Breakfast was nice, ample.

title: “A decent clean stop over hotel”
text:
This hotel provides, clean basic, no frills accommodation.
 The twin room was at the rear of the building and had two comfortable double beds and a clean, though spartan, bathroom.
Reception staff were polite, recommending transport and dining options which proved really accurate and helpful to first timers in Boston.
Other reviews, I note complain about the lack of free parking.....no one parks for free in a big city...The nearest breakfast restaurant is 2 minutes walk away and is excellent....Symphony and Prudential T stops are easily accessible and the Trolley buses stop directly opposite the hotel.
Yes its a bit old fashioned. Yes there is only one elevator but it is a budget hotel.
We liked it.

title: “Always Friendly”
text: My husband and I frequent this hotel because of the friendly staff and great service. There is a wide variety of quality breakfast items included in the free breakfast and the hotel is convenietnly located for easy shopping and dinning.

title: “Great stay”
text:
We stayed here with a group of friends to see the World's Largest Block Party concert in July. Hotel was very nice - quiet, but still plenty of young people and an energetic vibe. It's in a good location - actually close to Michigan Ave (the previous person obviously did not know that you can walk a different way and be there in five mins), yet still within the Rush St. area that has good bars and restaurants. Don't miss the burgers at Harry Caray's. Also, the Weber Steakhouse was very good. Best place of all was the Billy Goat Tavern. Anyone who appreciates SNL ("cheezborger, cheezborger") will love it - it has not changed in the seventy years it has been sitting there. Very cool place and great burgers.
Amalfi was just what we needed. Nice, clean, professional...

title: “The suite was quite small and pricey, but hotel was nice.”
text: I thought I would get more for $300 per night, but all I received for my "junior suite" was a corner room about the size of a standard room in newer hotels. Room was nice though, minibar was restocked daily, and the bed linens were the best I've ever slept on. I definitely recommend this hotel, just don't pay extra for the suite.

title: “Absolutely Fabulous... can't wait to go again”
text:
Me and my other half stayed at the Comfort Inn Manhattan between 3rd and 7th Dec 04 to celebrate my 21st Birthday on the 5th. We arrived a couple of hours before check in and were really pleased that we were able to check in early so we could have a good walk around everywhere as this was our fist time in NY.
Alex at the front desk was an angel throughout our trip and he really helped us with many things, from where to go to eat and directions and sightseeing. He is truly a tree of knowledge.
Now a little bit about the hotel and room. I was worried about the size of the bathroom after reading a few reviews from this site, however i found it was not only ample, but larger than my bathroom at home. (and we ALWAYS had hot water). Regarding the radiators, they do make a wierd noise throughout the night and i suppose it was a little annoying, however, as we were that busy during the day shopping and seeing the sites, when our head hit the pillow we were out for the count and it didn't affect our sleep at all. The breakfast was basic, bread, toast, donuts, tea, coffee etc but it's so cheap to eat out and everything is in close proximity. The lifts were amusing- not slow (we never really waited more than a minute of so and the hotel was full) but the one nearest the desk has a tendency to bounce slightly on ground floor!
Macys is at the end of the street and the Empire State Builidng around the corner, and there is a subway stop at the end of the street, only a couple of minutes walk. We used the subway for the first time ever on the second day and and then constantly after that. Of course you have to be careful but it is so easy to use and cheap and really worthwhile considering, as most of the major tourist sights are on the same line. Times Sq is only one stop on the Subway heading Uptown and amazing.
All in all the hotel was great, the staff ever helpful and Alex a gem, and we will DEFINATELY be back again soon.
Another thing to note, however not relating to the hotel; we took a tour whilst we were there which we booked in advance called a Phototrek Tour. Marc , our photographer and guide was fantastic, he took loads and loads of photo's, delivered the CD-ROM within a couple of hours, and they turned out great. I would suggest visiting his site to have a look as this was one of the best experiences we had whilst we were there. W also now have loads of photo's of use TOGETHER in and around what we thought were the most important tourist sites to us. 
Go to : ---------------------------------------------------------
and mention Jennie and Ian Francis reccommended him.
Hope this has been helpful and have a safe a fun trip.

title: “Started renovations the day I checked in.”
text: Great location. The hotel started major renovations the day I checked in and was never warned about this when I made the reservation. The hotel sounded like a construction site from 8am to 5pm. One night the work crews stayed late and were pounding away in the room above mine until almost 9pm. The lobby was boarded up and they had created a temporary one in a spare room/hallway. The hotel will be nice when completed but I would not recommend staying here until they have completed renovations, which the manager said should be the end of March.

title: “Great Value! Huge suite in the perfect location for the right price!”
text: We travel to Chicago often always staying in a suite to accomodate our group size that at different times includes our kids, friends, or other family members. We've stayed in the Embassy Suites (both locations), The Omni, Homewood Suites, Marriott Springhill Suites and others that are not as easily coming to mind. The Comfort Suites on Michigan Avenue ranks among the best of any of these all suite properties mentioned. The location is perfect - right in the middle of Mich Ave and State St shopping, a short walk to amazing restaurants and bars - we spend most of our time in River North but you can walk anywhere from here. Our room had a balcony with beautiful views of the river and Wrigley Building. And as an added bonus breakfast is free - We will stay at the Comfort Suites on our next trip to Chicago!

title: “A totally different hotel.”
text:
This has to be one of the best hotels for the dollar. The entire hotel is very modern and fresh. I felt like I was transported to Scandanvaia. All of the furnishings, appliances (there's a full kitchen in the room), and decor in the hotel are very contemporary. The gym is equipped with up to date treadmills, ellipticals, and Lifestlye weight machines. The free breakfast was good and the eating area was kept clean all morning. 
I would stay defintely stay here again.

title: “Best Westin Ever”
text:
I arrived at the hotel and was immediately impressed with the kind young woman who helped me check into the hotel. She was pleasant in all pleasantries... and I soon found out that every single person employed at this hotel is the same. Without exception, I found everyone to be helpful, forthcoming, and thinking outside the box. The staff is just superb.
Other than the employees, though, it is really a great hotel. I stay at Starwood hotels often and this one was above par. Their foyer/atrium rose to multiple floors and the glass elevators literally went through the ceiling, creating stunning views. The business center, fitness area, and all common areas were just at the standard you would expect from a Westin, which is to say, were great. They were all modern, well-maintained, and easy to access. 
The rooms themselves were also highly comfortable. There was adequate space, abundant resources of utilities and necessities, and are again very modern. The entire experience was just as comfortable as could be.
I was upgraded to a bay-view room, affording me nice sights. I enjoyed watching the boats and the sunsets. 
The location was also better than I expected. On my last trip to San Diego, I stayed at the Westin in the Gas Lamp quarter, so this time I was expecting a bit of a walk to get to that area. However, the city blocks are small and this hotel is only about 10 minutes' walk from the same Gas Lamp area. It was a pleasant walk, too, and in a very safe area, well-lit, and easily navigated. There were multiple restaurants and convenience stores nearby, as well as a trolley station, so everything was easily accessed. There is even a micro brewery located one block away. The airport, too, was only about 10 minutes away by car, but I was never even awoken by noise! 
All-in-all, this is a fabulous hotel. I liked it better than the other Westin I mentioned, too.

title: “Great Bed Pitful Service”
text: Great bed, nice room. No wake up call as promised, billed for Valet parking when a friend dropped me off at hotel. Then my credit card was charged for the entire room when it was a direct bill to Harris County Metro Transit Authority. Tried for seven days to correct problem without proper action or a call from this establishment. They are collectively incompetent on Customer Service. I strongly suggest you select another hotel when in downtown Houston.

title: “True Service”
text: I stay with Kimpton as often as possible. The George is another shining example of what good service looks like. We were not happy with our first room and were changed into a great room without any hassle.

title: “It's all in the details...”
text: I travel a lot for business and have stayed in every type of hotel from luxury boutiques to chains... and I have yet to ever find such a great mix of service and ammenities as I have consistently seen here at the Homewood. As everyone mentions, this place is in a fantastic location. Anything you could want to do or see is either within walking distance or by nearby public transportation. But what really sets this place apart is in the details. The people that work here do their jobs well- but with the added detail of actually enjoying it. Everyone was so helpful but most importantly - sincere. The suites are fantastic with the added details of soft linens (I have never in my life felt such a soft towel) and thoughtful ammenities. The free food at breakfast and cocktail hour is a great value add with the added detail of take away containers for those that want to eat in their rooms. Everything about this place is perfect. Also - it is great for families - my daughter adores swimming in the very nice indoor pool (with an awesome view of the city) and the food and location make it just perfect for fun family time. We ate at Rainforest Cafe and the Melting Pot which are both a few blocks away. We had a total blast. Can't wait for my next visit!

title: “Bit of a dive”
text:
I paid standard rate on Priceline for this hotel, about 102 USD per night. I got 10 bucks off for each roach I found, which was a total of 4. I read other reviews, people said they liked this hotel, but it is very worn out. Great location, other hotels nearby, the Liberty Hotel or Orchid Suites maybe be cleaner/better shape.
Overall, I would not stay here again, even though it is in a safe area, right by the metro and the H&H mall, Hollywood Blvd has been elevated in status these last few years, it is quite safe. The hotel manager is not so friendly, other staff are. He does not know LA very well...so beware his directions, he would not call me a cab saying FedEx was 3 minutes walk away. It was 45 minutes walk. That pissed me off more than the roaches. Oh, the other thing in this hotel is noise. You can hear everyone around you as clear as day, the stomping on the ceiling, their going to the toilet and the room next door's TV. It makes you feel as though you're in some run down doss house with it's worn out 1920's decor - which with the roaches and stuff I am thinking you possibly are. Great location, needs a lot of work.

title: “BUGS! BUGS! BUGS!”
text:
I was looking for an economical hotel for a week while I relocate to the area. Seemed like a good hotel for a reasonable price. The froint desk staff seemed polite and accomodating.
Little did I know that when I woke up after the first night, there was blood on my sheets and two bed bugs were crawing around. 
Now, a couple of days later, I have welps on my arms, neck, and ankles.
They did refund the unsed portion of my reservation, but I still had to pay for the night that I was a feast to these critters.
This is GROSS!
I will never stay here again.

title: “Fire hazard-not kid friendly!!”
text: Do not stay here if you have kids. I wouldn't expect a hotel to offer cribs for babies if the rooms were not large enough to accomadate the crib. The only logical space for the crib leaves appx. 6" of space to exit the room... Total fire hazard. When I called the front desk to see if there was a larger room option, I was told all the rooms were the same size. This is a total falsehood because our aunt stayed on the same floor with a much larger room. I then went to the front desk and was told there was no other option. Very dissapointed. Don't waste your money!

title: “Nice hotel, near lightrail”
text:
I stayed at the Hampton Inn near the Medical Center and Reliant Park because I was looking for an affordable hotel near the lightrail in Houston. Overall, the hotel exceeded my expectations. The front desk staff was courteous and helpful. The hotel itself was very new, clean, and comfortable. The free continental breakfast was much better than average, with a good selection of food, a comfortable seating area, & pleasant hostess who would go out of her way to make people comfortable. The high speed internet was free and easy to use. The room was nice with a very comfortable bed, a good tv, and a small refrigerator. I also got a complimentary water bottle and a box of cookies. All this for under $150/ night average (slightly different prices on different nights). I came away with absolutely no complaint about the hotel.
One of the biggest unadvertised perks of this place is its proximity (2 blocks) to the lightrail station. I found this a convenient way to go downtown & to connect to the airport bus. Another random hint (not really related to the hotel) was that the airport direct Metrobus was a really better way to go than the super shuttle, took much less time and money + was more comfortable (Metrobus takes you to the lightrail which takes you to the hotel- I did all of that in much less time than a colleague took to super shuttle to her hotel downtown). The hotel is next to a chain restaurant (don't remember which) on one side and some upscale condos on the other side. Overall, the area is full of newer condo developments and hospital complexes, not the most stimulating area to hang out, but safe and ok.
If I was forced to go to Houston, I would stay here again!

title: “Best by far!!!”
text:
My fiance and I got engaged in New York last September and stayed at a different hotel over in Murray Hill which was great if a little old. However, we were coming back to the city (to buy wedding rings this time!) and we wanted to stay somewhere different, so I checked out the Sofitel, was very impressed with the reviews on this site and booked it.
We stayed there from 5-8th March and it was simply the best hotel that either myself or my fiance had ever stayed in (and we've stayed in A LOT of hotels!). There is no way that this is a 4 star hotel - its 5 star all the way, from the impressive lobby, to the courteous staff, to the fantastic bedrooms.
I was totally thrilled from the minute we walked in, we requested a room with a view and were given a room on 21st floor - no problem, the bathroom was absolutely fabulous, the room spacious and spotless. We even had the maid come in again at night to turn down our bed, and leave a bottle of mineral water with the weather forecast for the next day!
I can't rate this hotel enough, its in a great location between 5th and 6th Avenues, 2 blocks from Times Square and close to many great attractions and stores. Definitely sign up for the Sofitel Privelege card, worth it for the late check out alone. Also the restaurant in the hotel (Gaby's) is top class and well worth a visit.
We would not stay anyway else in New York now!

title: “Great location, no real life about the place, have to pay for wifi, ideal for short break”
text: Old hotel in great location, staff are friendly, its just a big hotel lacking a bit of life, have to pay to much for wi-fi , rooms are adequate, lifts were dodgy if not working at all. Overall it was fine

title: “It's still the best...”
text: I returned to the Sofitel in DC and still find it outstanding. So many personal touches from the minute you walk onto the property greeted by the doormen to the pleasant check in process to housekeeping coming to ask if everything is "satisfactory"... Ivette had a charming and pleasant demeanor and immediately worked to remove feathers from our room. The room was immaculate and comfortable and up to my high standards. This is my home away from home in DC...nice job and kudos to the staff at the DC Soffitel!

title: “Loved the Hyatt!”
text:
My husband and I travelled to California last May and our 2-night stay at the Hyatt was a highlight of our trip. The hotel is centrally located on the Fisherman`s Wharf and close to sights and restaurants. The hotel is very modern and both the rooms and the lobby were renovated recently boutique-style.
Would certainly go back to that hotel.

title: “good value, but you have to be careful”
text:
I stayed here twice on business, 3 nights each. Location is fantastic, just walk to Times Square in 10 mins in the middle of all the action. Although my work took me to distant places, the feeling of returning back almost to the heart of the city was unbeatable. The hotel itself is a bit tired, they try hard to be modern, but one can discern that the fittings are well worn. I was given a room right next to the lift and boy, was that a nightmare! The old lifts create a huge clamour, esp when they come to a stop and the doors bang shut. I could hardly sleep the whole night. 
Next day I demanded a room far away from the lift, and because they didn't have one on the lower floors, they had to upgrade me to the higher floor with a better room. The next time I checked in, I made sure they were not sneaky and allot me a room next to the lift. The staff exchanged a knowing look, realising I was an old hand. If you are not choosy and careful, they'll palm off noisy and dingy rooms on you. 
The Penn station is close by and connections are excellent.

title: “Exceeded expectations!”
text:
This is my 3rd 'budget' hotel experience in NYC (look for my other 2-Mount Royal Hotel and Belnord Hotel). I'd say this is by far better in terms of space area. The room we stayed at has a double bed, airconditioner, a lounge chair, a desk with chair(!), a closet, a small storage area for suitcases and stuff, and a TV encased in a cabinet with drawers to put in more stuff. We stayed for 4nights/5days and locked in a great price! The staff are quite easy to talk with. They make the bed if you say so, give extra towels if you ask. Checking in and out was a breeze! The bathroom is basic but new and clean. They give hotel soap and shampoo which are puny but so is the toiletries at a 5-star hotel!! NOW for the NEGATIVES: The internet connection to your room is about $11 a day plus you gotta have your own cable wire to plug to your notebook (they don't have it and buying it at compUSA cost us $20!!). The shared bathroom has a short wait time between 8am-9am when most people start their day. The towels are more like handtowels in size! We brought our own towels, robes, flipflops, beddings/pillowcases and AIR FRESHENER!! The carpet is soooo old that it's musty and stinks a lil bit at night!
If you're only staying overnight, you'd probably NOT notice and care about the negatives. I did because I stayed longer and I'd rather have my own clean towels and sheets... The hotel is only two blocks from Broadway on 94th, get a cab there to Times square and pay an average of $10 including tip. From times square just walk your way around. Because everything else is expenisve in New York, this is STILL the smart choice for a place to just sleep in. I'd definitely go back and recommend it to others.

title: “Not Good”
text: The Cafe closed at 9:00, which was very inconvenient. So we had to walk down the street to a restaurant connected to another hotel. When we inquired about shuttle to MCRD, we were told, because we booked through Hotels.com we had to wait to make sure everyone else got on the shuttle first. The shuttle driver was very rude that picked us up on Graduation Day at MCRD. He told us we all could get off. What do we expect out of him when he makes minimum wage and after all it is a FREE shuttle. He told the newly graduated Marines, he'd go get the General and they could go back to boot camp and learn something. The Marines didn't do a thing. We all put our names on a list and he didn't even go by that. He was just RUDE. The other shuttle driver we had that picked us up from the airport and picked us up from MCRD the day before was so nice. I didn't think the rooms were as nice as the website stated. I was told we could get discounted tickets at the front desk for Sea World. We get there and they are full price. I was told late check out wouldn't be a problem and yet they put us through a waiting period, which we didn't need being graduation day for our Marine. So all in all I believe they didn't make my visit very comfortable. I will not stay there again.

title: “Darling inn!”
text: I am a frequent contributor to TripAdvisor, and I often review the hotels where I have stayed. I chose Inn at the Market because of the great reviews on TripAdvisor, and I was very pleased! Staying at Inn at the Market was a great experience. The valet and front-desk staff were extremely friendly, welcoming, punctual, and helpful. My room was comfortable. I often feel in hotels like I don't really want to let my bare feet touch the floor, but my room felt like a comfortable home-away-from-home. I had not slept on a Tempurpedic bed before, and it was very comfortable. The bathrom was spacious, toiletries were lovely, and shower was well-designed. The Seattle Athletic Club down the street was terrific. It is $15/day to use the facilities there, but really worth it if you're someone who needs to work out while you're traveling. It was wonderful to be right in the heart of things in Seattle, too. I enjoyed walking around the fish market, stopping at the original Starbucks for tea in the mornings, and eating at nearby restaurant The Pink Door. The one disappointment for me was the lack of breakfast, not a huge deal since there is a restaurant attached to the inn where you can order breakfast (though it is sit-down, not quick take-out) and many other restaurants nearby, but a slight inconvenience. As long as you're prepared for that, and leave time to find breakfast elsewhere, this won't be an issue. The rooftop deck offered a lovely view of the Puget Sound. Turndown service each night with chocolate was a nice touch. I would definitely stay again for business or pleasure.

title: “SF Gem!!”
text: From the morning coffee/tea/juice in your room to the apples in the lobby in the mid-afternoon it is all of the extras at make this hotel a true joy and respite in the middle of a bustling city. Excellent walkable and safe location in SF. I will stay nowhere else if possible next time in San Francisco.

title: “Great Location”
text: Well for starters I showed up at the wrong time to check in it was right at 4pm and I think everyone was checking in at that time. Even had lines for the self check in computers. No big deal was not in a big hurry. Very nice lobby which is always a good thing when you walk in to somewhere in NY. When I got to my room I did not know whether I checked into a match box or a hotel room. But come to find out I got stuck in a smaller room (could have been because of the stairs right beside my room). Other then that it was ok. Internet in the room was $11/per day. Bed was soft pillows were ok. Crappy view of the condos right next to the hotel. I do not recommend buying a drink down in the hotel bar/lounge unless you are ready to pay for it (beer $8 / mixed drink $12) maybe I just got the wrong bartender. Of course it is Manhattan. But in all the hotel is nice!

title: “Excellent location, very good service - but not quite a five stars”
text:
Stayed here for a business meeting hosted at the hotel.
Very many positives: catered food during meeting, fantastic location at central park south, mostly very pleasant staff, and clearly one of the better products in Manhattan overall and in this area. The rooms are pleasantly furnished. Elaborate light arrangements. Unfortunately, no coffee maker or water boiler and no sparkling water in the minibar. Nice bathroom shower gel and shampoo amenities. However, the shower being good isn't great. Just an in tub standard deal, no rain shower, no massage jets or anything fancy. The meeting room floor is pleasant, but the windows are not well insulated with a lot of central park south commotion imposing noise on your meeting. Front desk usually has long lines and "the rest of us" package customers get a different level of attention than "the upper floor" crowd. Also, this place has a lot of permanent residents, a clientele who doesn't mix very well with the commoners, bearing annoyance visibly on their expressions.
For exercise, there obviously is central park. The in house gym, however, is rather smallish and basic...

title: “Great time at W Hotel Washington DC”
text: Had a great time at the W Hotel in Washington DC! We had a bit of a mix up on our end, and the hotel staff cleared it up with no problem! Rooms were on the small side, but that is typical for a W Hotel. I've stayed at many W Hotels and this compares to the rest of them. Great modern room, nice amenities, polite staff, etc. Great view from the rooftop bar! Definitely a place to go for drinks, but not to eat. Hotel room was really quite and didn't have any noise at all. Great location for sight seeing (White House, Smithsonian museums, etc). Wouldn't recommend a family to stay here, but a great place for couples. Would definitely return here when I'm back in DC! PS. Try the Cara Car water during the day in the hotel lobby. It's amazing!

title: “A Little Mixed, But Mostly Good”
text:
The Pan Pacific Seattle is quite a beautiful hotel and the level of service was first-rate. The views from the wall of windows were outstanding, and the bathroom is one of the best: the tub is very deep and there is a separate shower room. 
The location is OK - Whole Foods and Starbucks couldn't be more convenient, but it was maybe a 10 minute walk to the main shopping and 15 minutes to Pike Place. Neighborhood felt safe. Hotel parking is expensive, but that is the case anywhere in Seattle. And their friendly valet service includes in-and-out privileges, which is nice. 
The main disappointment for us was the condition of the room. While generally clean and stylish, it didn't quite live up to the standard of the rest of the hotel. There were some small stains in the carpet here and there, black smudges on the cabinets, and the loveseat was the most uncomfortable piece of furniture I've encountered in a hotel! The cushion squishes down, leaving your legs hanging over the hard frame in the front. Another disappointment was the minibar policy - even in the Executive Suite there is only an area for about 4 pop cans left for personal use. The rest is electronically monitored, so that if you move one of their bottles, you pay! A note said they will remove all the drinks on request - for a fee of $35! Ridiculous. And finally, the fitness center is located in a separate building across a small courtyard. It's not far at all, but it would be a lot more convenient right inside the hotel.
Bottom line: we had a good stay, but there are other hotels in Seattle in the same price range that are better.

title: “The Management of this hotel gets a failing grade”
text:
I am presently a guest at the hotel originally booked to stay 3 nights. I will be checking out tomorrow April 15th due to my almost complete dissatisfaction with the management of the hotel.
I am from overseas and had a difficulty checking in due to the fact that my office misunderstood the process of completing the credit card booking. The first front desk clerk was indifferent and it was another clerk Mr. Amado Sosa who intervened and resolved the matter. He is indeed a credit to the establishment. The bell man was also polite.
I was booked into a room on the 12th floor which is almost directly across from a room marked "Vending Area". The room is not functional however as construction is taking place. The door is left open and garbage is visible. I have had to repeatedly close the door.
Yeterday evening when I returned to the room I was met with the noise of drilling and hammering. I had to call the front desk to ask that the workmen be instructed to stop. This was done.
Today, I spoke to the Ms A. Butler, Director Front Office about the matter and could not understand my point that I should not have been booked into a room on a floor on which construction is taking place. I informed Ms Butler that under the circumstance I would be checking out of the hotel tomorrow.
I also asked that the room be cleaned. I returned to the room after 7pm and it has not been cleaned.
J Douglas, Jamaica W.I.

title: “Beautiful hotel. Excellent service”
text: We stayed here as Shell Vacation members. Their customer service is excellent. The front desk and bell caption service was very helpful. Room service was great with very good prices. Dinner at the Italian Restaurant at the hotel was 1st class. We will definitely stay here again. Location was perfect to take public transportation anywhere.

title: “Another wonderful stay at Westin San Francisco Market Street”
text:
Given Hurricane Sandy, we had to quickly change our holiday from New York to San Francisco less than 24 hours before we flew out of Australia.
Having changed our flight, we looked at San Fran accommodation, and having stayed at the Westin last year, it was always going to be our choice this time round.
The price for 5 nights was great, and upon check-in we were greeted with warmth and empathy, and we were placed in a Stargate preferred room on the 17th floor. The room was smaller than the one we had last year on the 8th floor but it had wonderful views.
The property is very well located, and it was our home away from home. It is a true 4 star property with a wonderful bed (though the cushions were very soft - that is the only thing we would fault).
I recommend this property to anyone looking for good accommodation in San Fran.

title: “My Favorite Hotel in NYC”
text: Since October 2008 I have spent 33 nights in this hotel. The staff are welcoming, courteous and genuinely kind. Rooms are lovely with marble bathrooms and luxury amenities. In addition the location is fantastic! I can't say enough good things about this hotel so I show it with my loyalty: since October 2008, I've stayed in NYC 35 nights, 33 of them at the Omni Bershire - the 2 night difference was only because the hotel was booked solid.

title: “Urban and beach atmosphere combined”
text: This hotel offers an escape into another world, due to its unusual accents from every angle. It features a sand-filled, beachy upper-level terrace surrounded by downtown glitz. Rooms are bright white, combining high-tech with Cape Cod warmth like inviting soft window benches. The room furniture is holding up well, but will be due for replacement soon. My bath featured only a high-tech shower, perfect for me but not for those who prefer a soak in the tub (not sure what is available on request). Public areas are filled with pop art and small pillow corners for hanging out. Part of the vibe is a lobby, partly a living room, that includes a sophisticated collection of books on art and architecture. I did not arrive by auto, but it appears there is no dedicated parking garage, only valet service to nearby garages.

title: “Excellent for a quick stay!”
text: Had a late concert at Constitution Hall. Excellent spot to stay to avoid the travel back home. Very small room, but it was clean and worked well for the short stay. We were totally able to walk to the venue. Good times.

title: “The Best”
text: My wife and I had a wonderful stay. Our room faced the ocean. Two sets of double doors open onto the ocean. It was romantic and peaceful. We saw the most beautiful sunsets though the glass window above the spa tub. The staff were cheerful and nice. We will stay at this hotel again when we visit OB in San Diego.

title: “The hotel is beautiful, cultured and inspiring to look upon with nice people and things.”
text: The hotel is gorgeous. The room is spacious and well decorated. The hotel staff which I interacted with (Erica and a few others like the vallet guy) were warm and welcoming. I only wish the view was a little better and that it was easier to find. The hotel is connected to a restaurant which is on the face which the address is for. So it was confusing getting there. (The drive in entrance for vallet is on Congress.)

title: “Beyond impressed”
text: When I was looking for a place to stay in Memphis on my way to Houston Texas. I looked on Twitter for hotels in the area. I found wonderful comments on The Peabody. How true. We had a wonderful time. They have great old world customer service. Make sure if you go to take a walk around the hotel and view the roof top and all of the conference rooms. Loving staying at old hotels.

title: “Great value for a very expensive city”
text:
For what you pay at the Monarch you are getting a great deal. I have stayed at many hotels in San Francisco and found the Monarch much cleaner than rooms where I have paid 140 a night. The area isn't the best but you really don't spend a lot of time hanging around the outside of the hotel.
I only ate breakfast in the little cafe but it was good food at reasonable prices.
The room I was in didn't have a clock, which was kind of a pain but I worked around it.
I didn't have a car to park which was good because I don't think it would be the safest location to leave a car outside.
All in all a nice place.

title: “Getaway Central”
text: The best things about the Ohio House Motel are its location and its price. It was easy to get anywhere from there and the parking was included in the very low rate.

title: “Loved the Lodging”
text:
We stayed one night at the Hilton CityLine for an event at the hotel. Friends of ours had blocked a group of rooms for a reduced rate, $149 from $164 for a kingsize bed double occupancy. We would surely stay there again. 
The driveup was well staffed by friendly valet who even remembered how we had packed the car the next day on check out; the reception was most helpful and welcoming; less than 3 minutes later we were in our room with our luggage delivered. There is a warm gas fireplace and fresh fruit, plus an oak bar in the lobby. It was a relaxed feeling. 
The hotel has undergone a major internal renovation. We had asked for a "new" room just to be sure and indeed it was new. The bed was excellent, with the soft thick down blanket; the bathroom was well stocked with double sinks, a classic desk was in the corner adjacent to the large window looking west; cheap wifi internet access, flat screen lcd tv, modern double cup european coffeemaker, ottoman with leather easy chair was a nice touch, and the blinds were durable to keep out sunlight if we wanted. No one rushed us out in the am and there was a nice looking buffet available which we passed on since we had a brunch event with the party group in a lovely conference room.
There is a pool and exercise room, we did not check either out. 
There is a small mini shop in the lobby, and plenty of local options within a half minute drive either direction, and the major highways are close as well, Rt 23 and 76. This is a busy strip, most of Cityline is, but our room was extremely quiet, so we could have been anywhere... You can see the Philly skyline from the parking lot. 
Considering the reviews below, positive and negative, I would say that the refurbished hotel deserves a 2nd look by any who missed it, since at this price, you cannot really do better in the area. This place deserves a solid 4 of 5 stars.

title: “The Magnolia in Houston is outstanding!”
text: The Magnolia Hotel in Houston is outstanding! I stayed there for a conference and business meetings. The hotel is in the old Houston Post-Dispatch building that has been renovated. It seems kind of small in the lobby but the second and third floors contain the lounge, sitting areas etc. The staff was terrific when I was there. And the cost was unbelieveable! I will definately stay there again. And any other Magnolia Hotel that is at a destination

title: “Beautiful hotel - great service”
text: Hotel was very clean and one of the most quiet I have stayed in... The staff was very nice and attentive. Bistro Alex has excellent service. There are nice shops around to browse and many restaurants to choose from. I even took in a movie at the Movie Studio Grill which was within walking distance.

title: “Your basic 2-tier hotel that looks more like an apartment complex than a hotel”
text:
I stayed here for 3 nights in mid-May of 2010. I requested a quiet room and the front desk staff were good enough to get me a room away from the freeway and the hot-tub. The rooms to the back of the property face a hill side and that kept things quiet and also not having noisy neighbors worked in my favor for some solitude.
Location- the hotel is located right along the 8 Freeway so getting on and off the freeway is very convenient. The Fashion Mall is about 2 miles away and is easily accesible via surface streets.
Room- the room is basic with a full size bed. No frills. Your basic 70's furniture and art decor. I appreciated having a small fridge, hair-dryer and cofee-maker. The TV had cable but with very limited channels, the good stuff (i.e movies and recent episodes of your favorite shows) cost money. There is a computer desk in the room that served adequately for my lap top. However, I had to use the outlet behind the TV, that luckily had a 6-prong outlet to plu in my laptop and blue-tooth for the night.
Service- The like to change your sheets every other day unless you specifically request that it be changed daily. They did not leave any plastic bags in the trash bins but luckily I brought some plastic grocery bags that I implemented as trash bags.
The Bed- I got a full size bed that needed replacing and only 2 standard synthetic-fill pillows.
Food- There is a restaurant next to the front desk that is decent. There is NO complimentary breakfast and NO complimentary afternoon snacks or drinks at this hotel.
Parking- Parking is abundant but the spaces are very compact and perhaps parking away from your room might be a better idea especially if you need space to get things in and out of your car. And, also, there is no elevator to the second floor and some of the stairwells to the second-floor looked as though it was ready to collapse. So be careful.
Amenities- I saw a pool but it was closed for some type of work, I know this hotel had a gym but I never saw it, and they had about 2 hot-tubs.

title: “Last Minute Sight Seeing Trip”
text: Great Room... Great Staff... Wonderful bar and restaurant... Close to Sights and Subway.

title: “Literary Gem”
text: We just returned home from a stay at the Hotel Rex. The experience was terrific. The staff was one of the most professional and attentive that I have ever experienced. The hotel itself has a European, literary feel to to it and is in a great location--just a block and a half from Union Square, yet removed from the hubbub of Powell Street. My wife and I plan to make the Hotel Rex our base in future trips to San Francisco.

title: “Absolutely Terrible”
text:
This was without a doubt the worst motel I've ever been to - and it has made me lose faith in the Days Inn chain. Sadly, the only part of this apparently independently owned hotel that is like a typical Days Inn, is that they use the plastic cups with the logo on it. My wife and I booked this hotel online through the Days Inn website for a one-night stopover on a trip, and it was just awful. The service at the front desk was rude, and the room was incredibly dirty. The sheets were stained, the tub was filthy, the refridgerator was unplugged and leaking melted water all over the floor. Further, the sliding chain lock on the inside of the door was just barely attached to the frame, and I'm sure it could have been easily pulled out of the wall should someone have tried to force their way in. 
The layout of the motel is that there is 5 or 7 separate one story buildings, and they put us in a room that was two buildings back on the edge. Now this wouldn't be terrible at other hotels, but here, there was no external lighting by our room, the edge of our building was about 20 or 30 yards from the Interstate, separated only by some dark shrubbery, and there was a family of feral cats running around that hissed at us as we tried to get into our room. Worse yet, for some reason they stuck us down at the end of the building when there were no other cars parked anywhere near us. I can honestly say that I have never felt more unsafe in any particular situation than I did at that time. 
After inspecting the room, and realizing that it just wasn't safe to stay there, we went back to the front desk to leave. It had been less than 10 minutes since we checked in, and the clerks refused to give us our money back - however, we turned in the keys and left anyway. 
Please avoid this hotel at all costs. For about $20 more you can stay at the Days Inn Suites Columbus West, which is maybe about 10 minutes away down the interstate. This is where we ended up that night, and the room and service exceeded what I normally expect from a Days Inn. 
Bottom line: Don't stay this motel.

title: “great staff”
text: The hotel is situated in a save, central, but not so attractive area of the city. The rooms - we were on the 9th floor - are small and oldfashioned, and the walls are thin so we could listen in on both neighbours conversations !! The staff made up for it, though, they were helpfull, friendly and above all really funny. Would we go back? It was value for the money, but if I had more of the latter, i would go to a hotel in Fishermans Warf.

title: “Stay there!”
text: Hotel is downtown so u get some of the usual "interesting characters" outside, and of course u have to pay for parking. The rooms were very clean and the staff was great. They made me feel like they cared about me. Way to go Crown!!

title: “Not ideal for business trips”
text:
Room was OK, specially because the bathroom was quite new, refurbished very recently. The street was quite noise at night and you could heard some trucks playing the horn!
The worst was breakfast. Poor sitting tables, plastic clutery and a bit busy.
The best, WIFI available throughout the hotel

title: “Great Staff Nice Hotel”
text: The staff was friendly and it is in a great location. They recommended a Spa across the way I am so thankful they did. I tried the breakfast it was delivered right at the time I requested. I ordered the continental breakfast I have had this at several hotels and this was by far the best including several 4-5* hotels. Self parking was free and you can park in the garage which I thought was very nice. They had a shuttle I didn’t use it but I saw others coming and going. Overall it was a very nice hotel. I think it needs a little renovation or refresher but all in all a great hotel.

title: “Wonderful atmosphere and great location!”
text: The Surrey has it all. We loved it; the location fabulous on the upper east side. The service was excellent and the rooms wonderful. I loved that we had the choice of walking down Madison or Fifth avenues and finding everything we needed. The lounge is very active in the evening. Will definitely stay again when in the city.

title: “Very accommodating”
text: I really like this property although the parking can be difficult and it's a little off the beaten path. However it's quiet and nice, and the staff are out of this world. In the winter you can burn logs in the fireplace, which given the right companion would be lovely.

title: “Great location but average hotel”
text: Stayed here one night for business. The location can't be beat, and the sky walk access to the Prudential Center and the shopping mall is great (especially when it's cold outside). That said the hotel needs a little sprucing up. There were signs of wear and tear in my room. The bed was quite heavenly, but the shower was nothing special. The bathroom was small but functional. The room could have been cleaned better too -- I found random hairs in the very white tub and mildew on the shower curtain. The gym is adequate, and there is an indoor pool, which I didn't use. Overall, the Westin is okay, but certainly not outstanding. I would consider another hotel the next time I'm in Boston.

title: “Comfortable stay”
text: Centrally located, convenient to tourism hotspots.Comfy beds and furniture. Good lightinng and friendly service. Reasonable rates. I would definately stay here again in New York.

title: “Uncomfortable; not worth the hype”
text:
Booked a spontaneous visit for our anniversary, partly on recommendations from friends. Nice area and neat old building, but otherwise a huge disappointment--and this is normally just my kind of place: quirky and unique.
Problems:
We noticed a few days after booking that they were running a fall special. However, they insist that we have to keep the rate as it was when booked--about $50 a night more. Bummer!
After reading reviews about noise downstairs, I requested by phone when booking a 2nd or 3rd floor room, and was told I was booking a 2nd floor room. We arrive, and guess what? First floor close to the entry, and all other rooms booked.
The bed: AWFUL! I have a 12 year old cheap mattress at home--this thing is like sleeping in a hammock. Super saggy. 
I also find the decor really lacking in charm and warmth, bur that's just personal taste. However, don't bother with a suite--the furniture and lighting are such that I have a hard time imagining anyone using it... ?
Seriously considering moving to another hotel for our 2nd night. Big disappointment!

title: “Wonderful view.....great stay”
text: The St. Regis is located in the lively SOMA area of San Francisco. It is next door to the SF Museum of Modern Art which is great for the art, restaurant and gift shop. Also, it is walking distance to Union Square. The lobby is inviting with comfortable seating for drinks and light food. The rooms are spacious and well appointed with large glass windows that provide lots of natural light. We had a wonderful view of Yerba Buena Gardens. There is a central system to control temperature, lighting, shades and black out shades that is easy to use and conveniently located. The bathrooms are also large and beautiful. We had breakfast in the hotel's restaurant, called Vitrine's, our meal was not memorable but the service was excellent. The staff were professional, helpful and friendly. The only thing annoying about our stay was the charge for internet connection in the room. Other than that complaint, it is my new favorite hotel in San Francisco. It was heaven!

title: “This is a wonderful place to stay!”
text: We were in town just for 2 days to attend a Denver Broncos football game and stayed here. It's within walking distance to Mile-High Stadium and the path from the hotel to the stadium is well lit. The front desk staff was very helpful with questions regarding recommendations and directions as well. They seemed very pleased to have us there! The room was clean and comfortable and quiet. They had a complimentary breakfast that offered choices from omelettes to waffles to different cereals. The breakfast area was clean, and well-attended by a hostess who was very friendly. Will definitely stay here again when in town for a Broncos game!!!

title: “Cool”
text: I stayed at this hotel for 3 days and It was such a great experience. The breakfast was very thoughtful with healthy choices. Newspaper awaited me every morning, the folks that worked down stairs were very friendly and helpful. They wear these cool hats that make the hotel a place you can't forget. If you do decide to stay at this hotel look for a guy name Greg he was great a ton of help to me and my girlfriend.

title: “A cocoon in decadence”
text:
This is the hotel to fulfill our dreams.
From arrival to departure we were immersed in luxury. Staff, food, decor , bed linen, we could go on forever, this is worthy of 6 star rating. We will be back-)

title: “Don't bother”
text: Stayed for 5 nights (24th July - 29th July) as part of our honeymoon and we were left very dissapointed. The lobby and exterior view were very impressive, but thats about as good as it gets. Our first room (6th floor of older part) smelt of urine as the cupboard sized bathroom door had been left open. The two windows both overlooked a brick wall. We changed rooms and were given an 8th floor room in the back tower. When we stepped out of the lift we knew this room would not be much better. The corridor was completely deserted and we did not see or hear another person for almost our entire stay. The room overlooked the street and was a very dated green/brown combo. There was a problem with the shower which made a very loud clanking when the water pressure was too high - this was also set off by any one else in the area using their shower (which woke us up on our first morning at 7.30). We ate in the Oak Room on our first evening, the staff were mostly polite except Max who demanded to see our id when we ordered from the wine list - we are both nearly 30 and he loudly asked us to confirm our year of birth as if the id's were fake and then threw them both down onto our side plates without a thank you. The maids knocked on our door at 8.30 on our second morning and seemed to sigh and tut when we were not ready for them to change our room. Room service was stupidly expensive and we had two double beds that were too small to share, so for the last 5 nights of our honeymoon we slept in separate beds!! Having seen some of the other rooms we did not want to risk changing rooms again to get something worse. We were not offered an upgrade or queen bed when we complained the first time. The lady at the hertz counter was also unhelpful when we asked for information on the tours and lets not forget the homeless people outside. We counted 6 on the way from macy's to the front of the hotel which is just accross Union Square. Nobody made us feel welcome or made any effort at all - I would not stay there, or even go to San Francisco again as this hotel was supposed to be the best one in the area...

title: “Dreaful Service”
text: Wanted to advise other travellers NOT to book this hotel, staff were incompetent and lacked training and it was not just my husband and myself who had problems three other couples were unhappy also. We had to wait an hour before check in after being advised it would be 5 mins, they double booked our room we had a famiy enter the room 5 mins after we had - mini bar not replenished with water after asking them for 3 days straight to do this, no one seemed to understand the concept of bottled water. I could go on and on but would take up too many pages, please do not go there !

title: “Excellent”
text: We were given an upgrade upon arrival, and I couldn't even begin to say how wonderful the staff and the hotel were. The hotel is immaculate, and you really do feel like you have stepped back to a time of luxury, class, and excitement. Just the history of the hotel is enough to make anyone who loves literature content. It was so wonderful to be greeted with Belgian chocolates, the beautiful lounge which provided an excellent breakfast, and the friendly and super efficient staff. We even enjoyed a drink at the Monkey Bar. So much fun. We have stayed in several hotels in New York over the years, but the Hotel Elysee provided so much more. Thank you for making our time and my birthday celebration something we'll never forget!

title: “Very Friendly & Comfortable”
text: ...staff could not have been nicer or more accommodating. Hotel was very clean. Turn-down service was nice to come back to every evening. Would definitely recommend, especially if wanting to tour the heart of San Fran.

title: “Brilliant”
text: Stayed here last summer but have only taken the time to review it now. This hotel was truely fantastic. It had only been open a couple of months prior to our stay and the whole hotel concept was great. The rooms, although small, were modern and exceptionally clean. Location wise it was brilliant being only between a 5 and 10 minute walk to times square. staff were very nice and always there to assist you with any problems. The roof terrace was great and the bar did some lovely cocktails although costly. Will definitly come back here on my next visit to New York!

title: “Expensive All Around”
text:
My daughter and I stayed at the Mandarin Oriental 2 nites in March 2008 and were expecting the world considering its high price and five diamond rating.
 When you first arrive you are greeted by the doorman who will willingly help you with your baggage (for a tip of course) From the moment we walked in we were greeted and acknowledged several times, though through the door and to the check in desk is not very far. The lobby was modeled after the Jefferson Memorial. The hotel only offers valet parking which is very expensive 38 dollars a nite plus 14.5 % tax ! Check in was fast, you just sign a paper stating the price and nites which you are staying then the person who checks you in walks you over to the elevator, pointing out things along the way, pushes the elevator button hands you your key card and away you go to your room
 Our room was a city view, not such a great view, but for the price we paid (235.00) it was fine by us, not one noise did we hear from traffic, trains or planes in that room. The room was a little disappointing though, not quite as big as I would expect considering the ratings for this hotel. The room was tastefully done, bed was comfortable room had darkening curtains which worked amazing. Shut those curtains and that room was extremely dark (while it was still bright outside)
 Had to call housekeeping to change bedding because I am allergic to feathers- the bed had a feather bedspread and pillows . They arrived quickly within 5-8 min I would say. Turned down service is also offered, which is when you get water and ice if you like (there is no ice machine anywhere in the hotel) Apparently too tacky for such a resort. They will also turn down your sheets for you, but I can manage that all on my own.
 Bathroom, as others had mentioned is beautiful.. Boy oh boy, the water pressure in the shower was powerful. Very relaxing after walking all day.
 The hotel is located by the basin which is a little off the beaten path (it's so new and huge where else would they build it) so I course I was worried being there alone with my daughter. Don't be. It's a easy 3 walk block to the Smithsonian station, walking distance to the Engraving & Holocaust. I can't even count how many police we saw. We felt safe the entire, but we were back at the hotel by 7 both nights. If you are concerned about getting there after dark, take a cab, shouldn't cost more that a few bucks considering how close everything is. 
 Front desk clerk helped in pointing which metro to take, (get a day pass much cheaper than single trips- day passes are 7.45 a day and that metro is super fast, clean and EASY to naviagate--only took the metro train, didn't do the bus at all) where everything was located, any questions I had he was very pleasant and accomodating. Did alot of research before I went but still nervous about the area and he rest assured me. Did ask the concierge to call me regarding how to get to the National Cathedral ,, but no call EVER CAME. Was very disappointed about that.
 Prices to eat there very expensive, we just brought food back to the hotel with us. (subway worked well- $5.00 for a footlong, Mcdonalds was also an option, as long as you don't mind it cold )
 Pool was a lap pool--4 ft deep but long. Chairs set up nicely calming feel to it. Bonus for us nobody was in the pool the two nights we used it. Daughter considered it her own personal pool for the night.
 They also offer a good size gym room, but will not let anyone under 16 in which had my daughter a little upset, me-- happy! With all that walking and sightseeing during the day, the last thing I wanted to do was workout!!!
 Didn't do the spa due to the daughter being with me, though I don't think I would've anyway.. Did Hershey Spa before and these prices were way over what they charged. Very expensive
 So overall, was this hotel worth staying in while in Washington D.C.? For the price which I paid 235.00 yes!! But at their rack rates, I would seriously have to rethink staying there. Don't get me wrong, it's a beautiful hotel, location is fine (after all, no matter what hotel you pick, it will be away from someting) but I think for that kind of price the rooms should be bigger. Staff was friendly and spoke to you whenever you meet up with one. When asked where somehting was, not one time did we get a finger point and go that way, we were escorted to the area we were seeking. The rooms with a monument views are gorgeous and might considering the higher price for those. Whatever price you get don't forget that D.C. charges 14.5% hotel tax on top of that. That tax is also added to valet parking. My only complaint with this hotel is the valet parking fee. Higher than any other hotel in the area, and you should be able to just pay that price for your whole hotel stay.
 Enjoy!!

title: “Great! exactly what it says on the label”
text: This hotel is a gem. Yes it is an old original New York hotel but that is the charm of it. Location,staff and cleanliness can not be faulted. We have stayed and both W and Crown Plaza and although these hotels are modern and more trendy, on a New York trip your there for the sites and shopping not to spend the time in your room. We had a junior suite which was ample for 3 and the Times Sq view was perfect especially to watch the parade go by on Thursday morning . We got a good deal with this hotel and the same trip at a higher star hotel would was considerable more. Hat's off to the Edison see ya next year.

title: “What more can you get in San Diego for < $100?”
text: This place provided all that was needed for a < $100/night stay. The b'fast was tasty and plentiful, the room had a fridge and a micro, and the location was second to none. I'm going back to SD in 8 weeks and will be staying there again. Besides, I'd rather spend the money I saved on the nightlife and activities versus a room in which I'm really only going to sleep, shower, and shave.

title: “Convenient location, BUT not very clean”
text:
Great location, close to subway. There are no signs for hotel either in subway or when you get out of subway to help you find your way. The hotel is truly above the subway stop but good luck finding it without get good directions.
The hotel was NOT clean. The bathroom was dirty. The towels, sheets, and carpet had many stains.

title: “Lovely Hotel and great location in downtown Denver”
text:
We stayed 2 weeks in this hotel, we were on vacation from the UK and wanted a central base for sightseeing. After reading some reviews I was a little worried however i need not have been. People have commented on the tower rooms, when we were allocated this wing i was worried, our room is very large and on the 21st floor with views of the city and the mountains exactly what we asked for! I am a platinum member and this usually gives us the best rooms when we travel so perhaps the lower floors have smaller rooms. 
The Sheraton service is always excellent and this hotel is no exception, yes its large and therefore you may have to walk a little more to reception but it is a city hotel. We had no line of people when we arrived and no problem booking in, I get free WiFi and fridge and cannot comment on the costs.
The room is cleaned every day and the club floor is open 24hours a day which is unusual. This hotel is a great base for both Denver and sightseeing in Colorado as you can get out on the buses, trains and tours and see Colorado.
It has snowed twice for us which is wonderful as the mountains are covered in snow and seeing it is amazing. I would recommend the gray line trips into the mountains they are really good and the Amtrax to Glenwood Springs the 6 hour journey takes you through the mountains and you cross the continental divide. We saw deer, wild horses, buffalo, coyote and lots of eagles along the Colorado river and amazing trip.
Love Denver and Colorado and we will definately recommend the Sheraton.

title: “Pleasant”
text: I stay In El Paso once a month. I had never stayed at this days inn. I was pleasantly surprised with service and cleanliness of the room. Thanks James

title: “Wonderful”
text: Our family of 5 stayed at the Magic Castle in September. What a wonderful hotel!! We had a two bedroom room with loads of space, a queen in one room, double in another and a fold out in the lounge. We found the staff amazing, helpful and polite!! Our kids enjoyed the free snacks & drinks from reception and the pool was great. Only issue we had was they purchased tickets for us for a Dodgers game through a third party and as we had not had time to research, found out that we paid over $180 extra for the tickets when we got to the game, BUT as soon as we disscused the issue with the manager he was very apologetic and refunded the differance off our final bill!! They also provided Vegimite with breakfast. We would higly reccomand this hotel for families.

title: “Great bargain”
text: I stayed here with my daughter in Nov 2003 when she was visiting NYU. The hotel has a great location and price. The staff were pleasant. The room was clean and small with 2 twin beds, but it was not a problem for us. The restaurant downstairs was fantastic. I would definitely plan on staying here again.

title: “Excellent Location; Wonderful Staff”
text: The Alexander is a charming hotel, up-to-date but with a lot of atmosphere. Our room was well appointed and the floor was quiet (even though our room was next to the elevator). The breakfast buffet was generous and, as others have noted, some fruit and pastries were available throughout the day. The staff is very engaging -- friendly and helpful without being overwhelming. The hotel's location is just about perfect. We were about 10 minutes walk from the historical sights to the east, five minutes from Market Street to the north, and five minutes from the theater district to the west. We walked everywhere -- there was no need to take a cab anywhere. There are many restaurants close by -- an excellent one across the street. One surprising, and charming, touch was when we checked in and were given a pack of five calling cards with my name on them "In Residence" at the Alexander Inn. I didn't have occasion to use them, but I imagine that Thomas Jefferson or Benjamin Franklin might have had they stayed here. All-in-all, a very delightful and pleasant stay.

title: “good location”
text: Brilliant location for a NY hotel. rooms were small but were comfortable. Flat screen tv and modern decor and bathrooms were beautiful. We paid €2,000 for one week for the two of us. this was considerably pricey considering breakfast was not included. We went to the restaurant on the middle floor for lunch on the first day. it came to $36 and we gave $50 and the waiter took the pleasure of tipping himself the $14 himself. We didnt eat there again. i have no problem with tipping, just i would like to do it myself. Breakfast was an additional $18. The location is fantastic and we had a fabulous holiday but breakfast should have been included for the price. there was vending machines and free bottoled water as well as room service on demand including every takeaway ou would wish. the hotel was fantastic and i would stay there again but would not eat in the restaurant out of principal.

title: “Do not stay here. Terrible service. Rude staff.”
text:
Please do not stay here. I had a very bad time.
The staff will take $100 off your credit card as a room "deposit". This was a very dodgy practice and was never properly explained.
- I had to change rooms halfway through my stay. The reason for this was never explained.
- The breakfast is terrible. No cereal. No milk. 
- The staff didn't seem to care. They could not give directions.
- You have to pay for internet in the lobby (It is NOT free)
- The elevator broke down, and had to walk up 7 floors to my room.
There is a Best Western down the road. Stay there instead.

title: “Happy Hotel Stay”
text: I could not have been more pleased with my recent stay at this hotel. The staff was wonderful, the food (room service) was very good, and the price was great (we "pricelined"). Our room was not one that fronted 44th, but it really didn't matter, as our 7th floor view was beautiful. I've stayed at several nearby hotels, and this was by far the best deal. The room large, the bathroom was among the coolest hotel bathrooms I've ever seen, and the beds were SUPER comfy!! Stay here if you have a choice.

title: “Dirty...small rooms”
text: I read the reviews here and thought we would be safe staying here. The room was very very small and was not clean. We found stains on the bedding and wallpaper peeling off walls. The only positive thing was location but there are so many hotels in the general vicinity, we won't be coming back. My 8 year old even commented how icky it was.

title: “LOVED IT!”
text: The Alexander Inn was everything I had hoped to find in a boutique inn. It's a little piece of history that one can be a part of when visiting Philadelphia. The staff was helpful and very personable. I loved our room. It was very clean and just the right size for what we needed. I adored the Art Deco furniture! The complimentary breakfast was better than most chain motels offer. I WILL BE BACK!

title: “Mixed feelings on Andaz San Diego”
text:
The good:
-very nice lobby and checkin area. Complimentary drinks while you are checking in. 
-nice rooms with cool decor, good shower with great bath products
-great rooftop bar with an even better happy hour
-room service dinner food is really good (I haven't been too impressed with breakfast room service though)
-fully stocked mini bar with several complimentary selections
-friendly and good customer service
The bad:
-very noisy...and I'm not even talking about the nights it turns into a night club. I have been on high floors (they only have six) but the noise from the streets down below is obnoxious. Loud, drunk people at night. Trash trucks early in the morning. 
-I find the bed and pillows to be very uncomfortable...mixed with the noise factor, it's a horrible nights sleep. 
-I'm a Diamond member with Hyatt and the rooms they "upgrade" you to don't really feel like an upgrade. They have suites (based on their website pics) and I've never been offered one even once (and I've stayed here at least 10+ times over the last year) even when using a guaranteed suite upgrade. 
-pool is very small and I wish they had a jacuzzi.

title: “Fantastic customer service, wonderful location, perfection!”
text:
I cannot rave enough about my stay at this hotel! Amazing customer service, everyone went out of their way to do anything they could for you! 
Very spacious, very clean rooms. Amazingly comfortable bed and furniture. Nintendo controller with the option to order games to play through the TV -- HDTV I might add w/ free HD HBO.
They also offer valet parking in an adjacent garage--24 hours, and very safe feeling. 
Highly recommend this hotel, Subway stops also just around the corner from the hotel.

title: “Great Value”
text: I stayed have stayed at every Marriott in Philadelphia. This location is my favorite. The rooms are very nice... The views are fantastic..Good central location close to bus terminal and walking distance to historic sites (all Marriott hotels downtown are within a few blocks radius)..There is an indoor pool and Jacuzzi on the location. Also never pay full price bid for a room on Priceline.

title: “Perfect location for Wedding at the State Room”
text:
We had a suite. It was quite large, high ceilings,plenty of windows, and comfortable furniture and bedding. The rooms did not have a flat screen TV. The staff was friendly and helpful. It was well located for the wedding we attended at 60 State Street. The breakfast was very good with excellent muffins.
We would gladly stay here again.

title: “Just what you'd expect from a Fairmont.”
text: I have travelled to Washington and stayed at the Fairmont for two nights. The room was just as booked, on a quiet floor with a balcony and a view of the beautiful garden below. All amenities and more were waiting for me. The concierge was excellent and extremely helpful with all my requests, just as you would expect of the legendary Fairmont brand. I had several shipments arrive during my stay and the Fairmont staff was most helpful in taking care of them. I would recommend using the valet, saves time and is very professional. The garden in the courtyard is beautiful, even at night and the restaurant within it serves wonderful local meals. The waiters are very knowledgeable and helpful. What can I say, you can't go wrong with this one just as with any other Fairmont. Highly recommended. Please check some of my pictures.

title: “Enjoyable, but not everything was in working order - spa and steam room not working.”
text: Enjoyed my stay. Location is perfect to the downtown nightlife. We stayed in a suite and it was nice but air conditioning in the bedroom seemed not to be in working order.
