Also, I was over charged on my card almost over 200.00 dollars. I did discuss with front desk and they fixed it there but my card has yet to changed so we will see. Spa and Steam room were not in working order when we came for the weekend. Room was nice, bed was comfortable and suite is nice for a long stay with a full kitchen and living area. Shower/bath was nice as well. Water pressure nice and strong and the view from our room was amazing. Also, parking is not free, it is 22.00 dollars a day to park valet. From my knowledge, parking was only available on the street, if you could find a spot.

title: “Good value and well located”
text: I stayed at this hotel last night because it was within walking distance to a concert I was attending at Irving Plaza. I would describe it as IKEA-like. It was stylish and contemporary in a low-cost way with minimalist touches all around. For instance, instead of a coffee maker in the room, there was free coffee in the lobby at breakfast. Ditto newspapers and city magazines- they were available in the lobby. The rooms and bathrooms were functional and tastefully done. The front desk staff was competent and pleasant. The lobby is chic and I thought it was just fine for a short visit. The only issue I had with the hotel was that there were not individual thermostats in the rooms. They keep the whole hotel at a constant temperature which cannot be changed based on personal preference. Very close to Union Square and metro.

title: “Great location! Wonderful motel!”
text:
My husband and I vacationed in San Francisco in Oct/06 for the first time and after reading such great reviews about Nob Hill Motor Inn, we decided to stay there. Everything was exactly as described. The owners were extremely nice and helpful. The hotel was conveniently located. Parking spots were a little tight, but hey, they were free! Our room was clean and beds very comfy. The light breakfast in the am
was good too! Would stay here again!

title: “Short stay, but nice.”
text: We checked in around 11:30P. We found the overnight desk clerk Cheryl to be incredibly nice. The room was very clean and spacious. We checked out the next morning with Cheryl still at the front desk. We didn't get a chance to check out the pool or exercise room because of our short stay. The breakfast was very nice, but there was no bacon or sausage available the morning we were there. The breakfast hostess was nice enough to make my meat loving son some sausage.

title: “Perfect Hotel for Everything in Baltimore”
text:
Although my usual favorite place to stay in Baltimore is the Marriot Waterfront, we managed to get an unbelievable deal on a room at the Hyatt Regency Baltimore Inner Harbor on Labor Day weekend for under $100 through an online discounter.
We asked for a waterview room and got Room 746 (a corner room) that had two entire walls of glass facing Inner Harbor and also overlooking the 6th floor rooftop pool, poolside bar and tennis courts. The room was cozy and ample sized, with a small sitting area and desk/office space. Comfortable beds, plenty of storage space, nice size bathroom, many sundries/mini-bar/coffee and toiletries.
The housekeeping staff and front desk staff were extremely friendly. The bellman and doorman were functional. The parking staff was even very accomodating. About parking.......If you drive to this hotel you have two options: Valet parking at $36 a day or self-park at $27. "Make sure you get your parking card as soon a you check in for self-parking" so you don't pay more than the daily rate if you are going in and out of the lot in the same day. Your parking charge covers you until 5 pm on your check out day, in case you want to do more sightseeing or have a late flight.
Unless you have to drive somewhere, the hotel is very convenient to all Baltimore attractions without using your car. You can safely cross the boulevard to the Inner Harbor shops and restaurants by an elevated walkway. Once there, you can use the water taxi system to get to other areas like Fells Point. The hotel is also linked by elevated walkways to the Convention Center. The pool was a nice outdoor oasis and is open Memorial Day to Labor Day each year.
Great stay, excellent staff and perfect location!

title: “First impressions count”
text: Waited in line to check in over one hour, most of that time only one clerk available. So far, customer service is dismal, room is old, aiur conditioner doesn't work effectively ... I've been here less than an hour and I already know I will never stay hjere again.

title: “Great Hotel and Nice Location”
text:
I have stayed at the hotel several times. I enjoy the hotel and the staff is always helpful. They treat you really well at this place. The rooms are very clean and comfortable. As a Royal Platinum they upgrade me to a 2 floor suite. It is fabulous! The room is comfortable and great to do business in the day and sleep at night. They have just about everything you need at the hotel and you are a short distance from nice malls and shops. 
My only complaint would be the breakfast. It is pretty lame. Well, more than pretty name. The VIP lounge is not really a lounge and the breakfast is not really a breakfast. It is more of a muffin meal with coffee. 
Other than that, the hotel is great. The reception desk is helpful and knowledgeable. I have to stay at this hotel several times a year as I have family in Texas and I use the DFW airport. It is a very short and fast commute to the airport. 
Overall, it is always a nice experience.

title: “Very Nice Experience in Japantown”
text:
Hotels in downtown San Francisco aren't cheap, but Tomo is definitely a bargain. Nice property, cute decor, friendly staff. Room service was very friendly and courteous, as well as the front desk. My only complaint about the property is that our room had no accessible electrical outlets. Zero. Nada. This explains why some of the furniture in the room was moved at odd angles away from the walls - so that the hidden electrical outlets behind the desk and nightstand could be found. There was a very nice and spacious computer desk, for example - but NO electrical outlets to use!! We had to pull the desk out further so that we could reach around to plug in our laptops. Same for charging the phone on the nightstand. This is a very easy issue to resolve - they need to install mounted power strips for easy access. This is obvious, but but I guess that doesn't keep people from ignoring it. At any rate - bring a power strip.
More about the area: Japantown is a surprisingly nice and quiet area to stay, with an authentic Japanese urban feel. Unlike Chinatown, Japantown is an actual established Japanese community in the Pacific Heights area of the city. Lots of Japanese-Americans live in and work in this area - but there seemed to be very little tourist traffic overall. No crowds whatsoever... just a lot of "local" Japanese - it was a great place to start and end the day during our visit.

title: “This would be a really great hotel - except for the noise!”
text:
When I checked in, I was greeted by a really friendly front desk staffer who gave me a room "further back, away from the freeway." I did not realize the significance of this until later.
The location is directly on I-35W about 5 miles north of downtown Ft. Worth. It is in an industrial/office area and there is not much nearby for dining options. There is a cafe in the hotel that was fine for breakfast and adequate for a light meal in the evenings.
The room (a king) was great. It was fairly roomy, clean and had that really comfortable adjustable mattress used at Hilton Garden's. The speed of the complimentary Internet was excellent. The TV was a flat screen but only had 20 or so channels and none of them were in hi-def.
The big flaw with this property is the proximity to the freeway and a rail yard and, despite my room being further away, had an incredible amount of noise 24-hours a day. The windows are double-paned (I checked) and appeared to be closed tightly but there was still a lot of noise egress. My usual solution in these circumstances is to run the HVAC fan continuously to drown it out but it turned out this fan was one of the quietest I've ever (not) heard!
Sadly, despite the otherwise nice features of this property, due to the noise issue I will have to look elsewhere when I return to the area.

title: “Friendliest staff ever!”
text: We loved this hotel. We came as a large group, so things could have been very complicated. But the staff were so friendly and flexible- they made it all easy! The breakfast in the morning was great, and the location was convenient if you had a light rail pass. There's a station just outside the front door! I recommend this to anyone looking for a great hotel at a great price.

title: “Great hotel! Great location! a SaTiSFiEd Vacationer!!!”
text:
LOVED staying here. I have a lot of positive opinions but like other hotels, there were a few downsides. Overall, we (my sig other and I) had a great experience in this hotel and Washington DC…
Lobby, Concierge & Check-In
Great location; only took 15 minutes from Ronald Reagen airport. The front of the hotel is very nice and there are 3-5 suited men who are very willing to help you with luggage or just to open the doors. The lobby is pretty impressive with marbled floors and walls. There are a ton of leather seating areas. Check-in was a breeze and we had no problems getting our room assignment and keys. The front desk also gave out maps and a list of nearby restaurants that were very useful for first time visitors.
Room (Pull-Out Sofa Parlor)
The elevator and hallway were very clean. The room itself was very nice and was surprisingly SPACIOUS (I half expected a room with just enough space for a couch). The room is the same size as a regular hotel room but with a pull-out couch. Besides the couch, there were lots of additional seating available (1 ottoman, 3 chairs). Our view was amazing! On the 9th floor, we had a view of the city and the Capitol building.
!!!THE NOISE!!!
Despite all my positive remarks about this hotel, IT IS RIGHT NEXT DOOR TO A FIRE STATION!!! (no lie). Washington DC, although it’s a very small area of land, their emergency response system services 3.5 million people a day. So there are fire trucks going in and out of the fire stations with their damn SIRENS on ALL DAY and ALL NIGHT.
Downside: the pull-out mattress was very THIN and UNCOMFORTABLE. With two people sleeping on it, we were able to feel the metal bars underneath us. We ended up using the extra blankets that were provided for a bit more cushioning. The mattress was very poor quality and need to be replaced. I have slept on pull-out mattresses during my college days and this hotel’s mattress was by far the worst (which says a lot).
Downside: the heater was more of an AC. We set the temperature to 73degrees and it did not get any warmer than 60degrees. I have no problem sleeping in a cooler room but I can only imagine others who would be very uncomfortable and unhappy with that type of climate at nighttime.
Downside: TV SUCKS. It’s nice to watch the news in the morning. After a long day’s worth of walking a few miles, it’s nice to come home and watch a movie. This hotel does not have a full list of cable channels but they do subscribe to 20 of the more popular channels (ie: all the news channels, TNT, TBS, HBO). The sucky part is that the signal was really bad that we were only able to watch about 30 minutes out of a 2 hour movie. Whether we were watching the news or a movie, we consistently saw static (black and white, rainy-grainy) and we were unable to hear anything.
Downside: Internet or no internet access? NO internet access!! The hotel advertised complimentary internet access and indeed, there were 3-4 networks to connect to. Of all those networks that I tried connecting to, my signal was very poor and could not load a single website (yes, my firewall was down). It’s definitely not my computer – maybe it was the location of my room. But despite the location of my room, there were 3-4 networks too many that I could not connect to. BUT… when we called tech service to complain about our difficulty connecting, they were able to provide us access that costed $10/day and WAIVED our fees. That particular network was a bit better but was still as slow as dial-up.
Downside: No minibar 
Marbled Bathroom
The bathroom was very nice. It was all marble, very clean and even had a retractable clothes line in the shower. They provided more than enough fresh linens, had a coffee maker and its condiments, toiletries, a small tv (ladies, very convenient while you’re getting ready), and many more. We were very pleased with the presentation of the bathroom. The water pressure of the toilet and the shower was really light but they had a note stating that they were making efforts of saving water.
Because I brought my own toiletries, my sig other wanted me to add that he was very impressed with the shower products in the bathroom that were Neutrogena brand and NOT the generic, yucky-smelling hotel brands that make your scalp and your skin dry. Good for those who do not bring their own products.
Housing Keeping
Due to privacy and security reasons, I usually do not like when housekeeping comes in to my room. But we forgot to put the “no service” sign on our door one day so housekeeping came in and cleaned our room very thoroughly (needless to say, nothing was missing). Because they were unaware of the fact that we did not want our room cleaned, they left us at least once voicemail a day, assuring us that their service is just a phone call away (which was really nice of them). FYI, for environmental reasons, they only replace the towels that you place on the floor (not all because some are usually unused) and they only change your bed linens every 3rd day of your stay (which I feel are all reasonable). Their efforts of preserving water and natural resources were pretty impressive. “This may seem very little but it means the world” –the note in the bathroom regarding their efforts of being environmentally friendly.
Location
DO NOT RENT A CAR!!! Parking is very scarce and expensive. The Union Station is only one block away. FYI, they tell you to make a left when you step out of the hotel to go to the Union Station but if you make a RIGHT, it saves you a block of walking. This hotel is walking distance to a lot of landmarks (the Union Station, the Postal Museum, Capitol Hill and all its glory) but is also in the midst of businesses (so you will be walking with people who work in that area too). Starbucks is RIGHT ACROSS THE STREET for us coffee lovers (FYI: there are 385 Starbucks locations in Washington DC). Billy Goat Tavern and Grill Restaurant (well known for their “cheezboigerz”, founded in Chicago) is right across the street, next door to Starbucks. The breakfast menu and their burgers are average on taste and quality but for an affordable price and great location.
Downside: at nighttime, there are a lot of homeless people who sleep in the nook and crannies of the hotel’s building. Please be advised to never walk alone.
Overall, we had a GREAT stay, I would definitely stay here again (in fact, planning on it within the next 4 months) and worth every penny! We saved a lot of money but worth a million dollars for a great experience.

title: “Okay, but overpriced”
text:
We stayed here for 2 nights while visiting TCU. It is very close to campus and there is a nice walking path right across the street. However, it was very pricey compared to most other hotels in town. Also, there was no elevator and it is a 2-story hotel. We had quite a few bags and they said there was no one to help us with our bags. 
The room was okay, nothing special. The internet was free. The front desk wasn't super helpful, but we didn't need too many services.
Next trip, we will look for another hotel. Ft. Worth isn't that big of a town and even staying downtown doesn't add much time to a commute to campus.

title: “Wow!!!!!”
text: I have read the reviews on here and I'm really shocked that people are moaning about this hotel!! I booked this hotel for our honeymoon despite what I have read on trip advisor i loved the website and when i arrived i wasn't disappointed. This hotel is amazing from the moment you set foot in the door the fluorescent escalators are sooooo funky!! I could go on forever about what I love but I'll give y'all a tip....... If you are young and appreciate something that is very different from the norm DON'T let these reviews put you off, yes the rooms are small but you shouldn't go to New York if you are going to stay in your room!! Please don't miss out on this hotel it really is a little gem and when your in the city that never sleeps why bother about the bedrooms!!!!!

title: “we loved it”
text: The staff at the hotel were great. Very friendly and courteous. Always quick to give us directions when we needed them the rooms were clean and all in all it was pleasure to stay there. i beleive that we have made some new friends and welcome them to come visit us one day.

title: “location is excellant BUT..........”
text: Stayed at the Drake for 2 night s in mid January. While the location is excellent be aware of certain issues. First, we got a great rate on a hotel website, only $89 a night, what a deal! BUT parking $90!!!! $45 a night...! I expected the parking to be expensive, maybe $20 a night. $45 is just way too much.. The check in was easy and the front desk staff friendly. Our room... VERY TINY, especially the bathroom.. seriously, there is barely room to turn around... but the room we thought was very nice and classic looking. Another plus, the bar/restaurant on the top floor (oops forgot the name)... its very very romantic and the views are beautiful.

title: “Typifies what I have come to expect from Kimpton hotels”
text: A block from Rittenhouse Sq in central Philadelphia and walking distance to most attractions, restaurants and shops, the Palomar and it's staff are friendly and accommodating, from the cleaning staff to the bar staff with a special (Pork-pie) "Hats-Off" to the guys on the door. Clean lines for the furnishings and quality linens and bathroom "Etro" products. Worth joining In Touch for the free Wi-Fi, "raid the mini-bar" and other specials. The Kimpton folks really have put together a team of people in their hotels that in my experience do go out of their way to make your experience a positive and leave you, the guest, feeling special.

title: “Great Stay at Staybridge Suites”
text:
We stayed here for 6 nights and really enjoyed the hotel. Our rooms were on the 23rd floor and had a great view of the Empire State Building. The room was spacious and designed with functionality in mind. The bed was comfortable and was great to relax on after long days touring around the city. The bathroom was very nice and spotlessly clean. We're not used to such small showers, though, but we were able to adapt pretty quickly. The hotel's free Wifi worked better than at any other hotel we've ever stayed at and did not crash or slowdown at any time during our visit. They also have the most extensive cable TV package we've ever seen. It was like watching our TV at home. Our only issue with our room was minor and was just that the AC unit was a bit loud during the night. The family members we traveled with that stayed in a room down the hall also said they also experienced the same thing at times.
The staff at the hotel was phenomenal. Everyone we interacted with was friendly, helpful, and seemed to genuinely be enjoying their jobs. The bellmen were especially great and did a great job arranging transportation to and from the airport, securing our luggage before and after we checked out, and giving us some good recommendations on where we might enjoying visiting in the city. One of the engineering team members came up one evening to help us with a TV/remote issue and she was fantastic, even though it was 10:45pm. We really appreciated that.
One of the biggest perks we enjoyed was the free breakfast that was included each morning. Each day it was very busy, but the staff did a great job of keeping everything stocked and making sure there were clean tables between the dining area and the bar so everyone could get a chance to eat. The food was above average for a free hotel breakfast and certain items rotated in and out over the days we were there, which kept it from being too repetitive. It's great that they provide breakfast and probably saved us several hundred dollars between the four of us who would have otherwise had to eat out each morning.
The location of the hotel was also great. It is literally one block away from the 40th St. and 8th Ave entrance to the 42nd and Port Authority subway station, which has an underground connection to 42nd and Times Square station. Between those two stations, you basically have access to any train you will need to get around the city. There are also several bus stops nearby with routes that cover many of the areas that are not as easy to get to via the train. There are several restaurants within a few blocks walk to choose from and a Duane Reade pharmacy right across the street inside the Port Authority Bus Terminal. This made it very easy for us to pickup anything we needed or get food when we didn't want to venture more than a few blocks away.
If you are looking for a good Times Square hotel, we would definitely recommend staying at the Staybridge Suites Times Square!

title: “OK room, great location”
text:
The big plus for this hotel is its location - you're right across from the waterfront walk, and within walking distance of the trolley, Amtrak, restaurants in Little Italy and the fabulous Extraordinary Desserts cafe. You're also about a 10-15 minute walk from the Westfield Shopping Center, Gaslamp Quarter and a Ralph's/Kroger supermarket. You could almost walk to airport, it's that close. Front desk staff and housekeeping staff were all exceptionally pleasant. Parking is expensive, at $22 day, but if you're lucky, there's half a block of unrestricted free street parking on the north side of the hotel. 
Of course, the downside to being close to the Amtrak station is that you will hear the train horns. The first night we stayed, our room faced the back of the hotel (overlooking Pacific Highway) and we heard trains all night; we switched rooms for the remaining 3 nights of our stay. If you request a room that faces Harbor Drive, or overlooks the pool, then you should be fine.
Pool is big enough to do laps; we never saw anyone in it the whole time we were there, but I imagine it is well-used by kids in the summer. The exercise room is well-equipped. Complimentary PC to quickly check email or print a boarding pass in the lobby. 
Rooms are OK - clean, reasonably sized with 2 full/double (not queen) beds, nice balcony with chairs, but starting to look a little scuffed and tired in places. Mattress was comfortable and there was an adequate array of soft and firm pillows on each bed. Thermostat was easy to use and worked fine. As other reviewers have noted, there's a sliding, frosted glass panel to the bathroom that doesn't lock. If you're travelling with someone, such as a work colleague, who you don't know well (or who you don't want to know well), you will probably find this room uncomfortable. It would be fine though for families, or those who need assistance with using the bathroom. No tub, but a large walk-in shower, with a great shower head.
I got the room through priceline and was reasonably satisfied with the price I paid for the room quality.

title: “Excellent!”
text: We thoroughly enjoyed our stay at the Metro. We'd let them know in advance that it was our wedding anniversary while we were there and they upgraded our room and laid on champagne for us! The hotel is really lovely and friendly. special thanks to Matthew the doorman...our taxi was waiting at 5am as promised! Also, Jeff the concierge who was so friendly and helpful. The breakfast was great, especially the huge muffins which did my waistline no good but were worth it!!! The view of The Empire State Building from the roof terrace is jaw-dropping. The Metro is in a perfect location for sight-seeing though we didn't even scratch the surface of New York...so we're definitely going back to this hotel! Be aware that this really is the city that never sleeps and you will hear traffic during the night but who cares? It was amazing!

title: “Great staff makes up for a hotel that is getting to be "too historic."”
text:
This was my second stay at the Westgate. The staff was very warm and welcoming and helpful at every step. Bed comfort, shower, towels, water pressure were all top notch. Great location as well. 
Where the property most falls short is the older furnishings, an old and small TV and the anitque desk area that lacked modern amentiies such as easy desktop electrical plugs and an adjustable desk chair.
If you like historic properties this may be for you, but in some ways the property is on the verge of just feeling old versus historic.

title: “Great Birthday stay!”
text: This was a great stay for my birthday last February! The service was good, the wine service each evening was very nice (though somewhat crowded with not a lot of sitting space) next to the fireplace, and the location was awesome! The room was small, but big enough for 2 adults and 1 child, and the yoga supplies were a nice touch. I'd definitely stay there again.

title: “Spacious and regal, you are special when you stay here”
text: Although we booked with expedia and the "breakfast buffet" was listed as included; the hotel was not informed of this and still honored our reservation with the buffet. Everyone was set to please us; the patron. Very refreshing. Rooms, service and hotel was top of the line even if the pool was not open. The workout room was bright and fresh. We would return. The restaurant was 5 stars!

title: “Location and Value”
text:
Stayed here New Year's Eve and the night before. 
First some orientation - hotel is located at the "intersection" of St Marys and the riverwalk. Front of hotel faces east along St Marys. Left side of hotel faces south along the riverwalk. 
We checked into a one bedroom suite (632) Nice enough but somewhat dark even with the small terrace facing north (limited view). Asked to see another room and was showed suite 300. It had larger rooms and TEN tall windows. The room wrapped the NE corner - overlooking St Mary's Street and to the north. No terrace. I don't think any riverwalk hotel offers a room with an unobstructed riverwalk view. This is because of the proximity of the adjacent buildings and trees.
There are other rooms with an extended living area but they are still one room. The suites actually have a door separating the bdrm and living room.
We enjoyed the windows because you can open them up about a foot and hear the sounds from the riverwalk and catch a cool breeze during a mild January (upper 70's)
Microwave, frige, and two TVs. Disappointed to find they did not have pay-per-view movies. (Odd considering this is a family hotel.) Bed was comfortable and the living room has a sleeper sofa, recliner, upholstered chairs, and a desk.
All staff very personable and helpful from the front desk to housekeeping, including the waitstaff in the on-site resturant (not operated by the hotel)
Having the garage adjacent was a definite plus. Parking $10/day which is a relative bargin. 
Although located along a quiet section of riverwalk, you are no more than a 5-7 minute walk to riverwalk ground zero (Hyatt,Dicks,Joe's Crabshack) and 10-15 minutes to RiverCentre Mall. Goes by quickly because of the scenery and people. Walking is quicker if you stick to the streets above the riverwalk - less crowded.
Breakfast was free so I can't complain about quality but most of all it was convenient. Didn't stand in the long line for the 2 free drinks at happy hour. 
Only complaint is the noise from outside the building. Despite the heavy curtains over the windows, we were disturbed each morning at 4AM by the garbage truck which stopped right outside the building. It was loud enough and long enough to wake us each time. The situation is probably better for the rooms farther from the street. You are downtown and close to the street so sirens and traffic noise are common.
We recommed this hotel and would stay here again.

title: “Ew, thin walls!”
text:
Great location (for Seattle Center), clean rooms, comfy beds, large bathroom. But the walls were paper thin!!
First night we heard the cleaning people at 6 am (woke us up)! Vacuuming, moving dishes around etc. The second night around midnight--for 2 hours--we had to listen to the people next to us having s*x. No matter how loud we turned up the Tele, we could still hear this women's voice. Not a pleasant experience, I can still hear her voice in my head 2 days later!!
If you stay here, get a room that will be isolated or else expect to get little to no sleep!!

title: “Disappointed”
text: On arrival at the Diva quickly checked in by a really friendly receptionist Charles but it must have been his last shift and a complete arrogant "diva" had taken over, he seemed to be a night receptionist although on our last day he was there in the morning as well maybe this was why he was so unfriendly and unhelpful. The room had an awful sewage-like smell which I reported to reception, when we returned in the evening the smell had gone but only because the window had been opened it soon returned when closed. Hotel was in a great location but we were glad to leave.

title: “Great Value”
text: Convenient, close to restaurants, Universal Studios, great service & staff, great value, nicely maintained and staffed pool...would stay again in a heartbeat.

author.location: New York, New York, United States

title: “Very,nice ,convenient friendly and gem of the area!”
text: I am staying here on business and couldn't be happier! Beds are super comfy , staff if friendly, breakfast is free, location is great and a free bus to pick us up and drop us off at night!!! I think recently renovated because everything looks brand new! Fantastic for the business traveler!

title: “fantastic location”
text: fantastic location - the hotel is one block from Madison Avenue, two blocks from mid 5th Avenue and 15 minutes walk from Times Square. The rooms are not the biggest but the beds are!!!. everything is clean and in good condition with a safe in the room. Everyone is friendly and Starbucks operates from the bar every morning. The foyer is a tourist location in itself with it's traditional features. Price - cheap compared to other hotels in the same location and we found it well worth the money and would stay again

title: “I will return...”
text:
I stayed at Studio 6 for 35 days. I did have some problems at first. The internet did not work and I was moved to another room. Then the telephone did not work and I was moved again.
This may sound like a negative review. Overall, this is not the case.
The staff did everything they could to correct the problems, even offering to help move my possessions. Once things got settled, the room was clean, the bathtub was huge, and the swimming pool was outstanding. The laundramat is outstanding and cheaper than a public one. I found the bed to be very comfortable with soft sheets, blanket, and bedspread. The location is excellent, and I felt very safe the entire time I was there. 
ALso, unlike many long-term stay motels in Jacksonville, it is possible to check in on a Sunday, There is a nice road across from the hotel with broad sidewalks for exercise walking. Grocery stores, ATMs, convenience stores, and restaurants of all kinds are nearby.
Also, there is a monthly rate there, but you have to ask for it up front. It makes the stay there much cheaper than paying a weekly rate. 
If I am invited for my summer job in Jacksonville next year, I will return.

title: “8/31-9/6/2009 North Eastern University - Daughter's College Trip”
text:
We just returned from a stay at the Hilton Boston Back Bay Hotel over the dates of August 31 through September 6, 2009 as our daughter was starting her freshman year of college at NEU. This hotel is centrally located to the "T" Green Line between the Prudential and Hynes stations, two blocks from the shopping and restaurant district on Newberry Street, three blocks from the NEU and BU campus' and about four or five blocks from Fenway Park. There is also a great wine store about a block away from the Hilton on Massachusetts Avenue!
 I made our hotel reservation at priceline.com with a bid of $71.00 for a three and a half star hotel in the Back Bay area of Boston (we were in Boston in April 2009 and we got the Marriott Copley for $71.00 on priceline). I checked another site, www.betterbidding.com and found another person that stayed over the same dates that we did at the Hilton paid just $64.00 on priceline. Unfortunately the Marriott Copley was at something like $120.00 per night over our dates.
I called ahead to the Hilton and requested a high floor, corner room because the community on Trip Advisor advised that these rooms were a little larger and they were located away from the elevators and ice maker noise. The only problems we experienced were:
1. The carpet in the room didn't look dirty but when you walked barefoot or with socks on, your feet tuned black almost immediately. I called housekeeping and requested them to shampoo the main areas of the room and they complied the next morning! Make sure you leave a $2.00 tip for the housekeeper each morning and they will make certain you have plenty of bottled water, clean towels and extra bath amenities daily!
2. The thermostat in the guest rooms can't be adjusted by you (even though it looks like you can adjust the temperature from the thermostat), it can actually only be adjusted by the hotel maintenance manager from his computer. The first four nights, we felt like we were sleeping in a refrigerator. I let the front desk know about the problem each morning for the first four days in a row and the problem finally got taken care of on September 3rd. I was a little upset that we froze our butts off for the first four nights, but the front desk staff shut me up by giving me three coupons for a full American breakfast for the next two mornings.
Some tips for you:
1. Wireless Internet access is $14.95 for each 24 hour period in your guest room but it is free in the lobby area. I went down to the lobby the first day to connect my laptop to the Hilton's free wireless service, I then left my laptop connected and took the elevator back up to my room. The WIFI service stayed connected for free! It will automatically disconnect every 24 hours, so you have to repeat this process daily. This saved me almost $90.00 over our 6 night stay!
2. Hilton Honors members (Gold or better) have access to a complimentary continental breakfast in the lobby restaurant. We called the waiter The breakfast Nazi because he seemed to be mad every day, but all in all, the breakfast was sufficient as it consisted of eggs of the day, fresh fruit, oatmeal, bagels, juice and coffee.
3. Parking is something like $37.00 per night. That's more than half of the cost that we paid for the guest room, so you are better off using public transportation if at all possible!
4. We purchased three, 7 day Charlie Cards for $15.00 each upon arrival at Logan Airport (ticket machines are at the baggage claim area). I read on Trip Advisor about how easy it was to take the "T" from the airport to the Hilton (take the free airport shuttle bus from the curb at baggage claim to the Blue Line inbound, Transfer to the Green Line at Government Center and then catch any Green Line B, C or D outbound to to the Hynes station and walk two blocks to the Hilton or take the Green Line E outbound and exit at Prudential station and walk through the mall to the Sheraton hotel, the Hilton is across the street from the Sheraton). We saved $40.00 to $45.00 on taxi fare from the airport and another $30.00 back to Logan when we departed and we used the "T" and the bus system to get around Boston for the entire week to shop and get to the North End. We also went to the New England Patriots game on Thursday night and we found (on Trip Advisor) that there is a special MBTA commuter train that will take you from the Back Bay station in Boston directly to Foxboro Stadium for just $12.00 per person, round trip. This is a great deal as the train only makes three other stops along the way and it only takes about 45 minutes to get from Boston to Foxboro Stadium. The train leaves the stadium for the return trip to Boston about 30 minutes after the conclusion of the game (you don't want to miss this return train as the stadium is in the middle of nowhere).
5. The North End area of Boston is full of great but over priced Italian restaurants. We found on our last trip to Boston that La Famiglia Giorgio's ([--] or www.lafamigliagiorgio.com) one block off of Hanover Street to be a great "family style" restaurant. The three of us shared a large Caesar salad, an order of steamed mussels, the daily special lasagna, my wife had a glass of wine and I had an Italian beer (this was enough to feed the three of us and have leftovers to take with us) and the check was under $70.00 including a 17% tip for the wait staff! We then walked over to Modern Pastry Shop on Hanover Street to pick up a few chocolate dipped, ricotta cheese filled cannolis for dessert. These are to die for and they are only about $3.50 or so each. Just remember that the cannolis at Modern are much better than Mike's Pastry Shop!
6. I went to restaurant.com and purchased a $50 restaurant certificate for Kingston Station located at 25 Kingston Street or call [--] (another Trip Advisor suggestion) for just $20.00. The stipulation is that you have to purchase at least $100 at the restaurant which is no problem if you have a glass of wine, share appetisers and an entree each. It worked out to be about a 30% discount once you added in the gratuity and the food and service were great! Make sure you try the truffle fries, They are awesome! You can take the Green Line and walk three blocks to the restaurant (sorry, I forgot the stop).
Hope these tips help you to enjoy Boston on the cheap as much as we did... I'd also like to thank the entire Trip Advisor community for pointing us in the right direction and suggesting such great things to see and do while we were there. My only complaint is that we didn't have enough time to do everything we wanted!

title: “A traditional oasis”
text:
I enjoyed my two night stay in the Topaz (I was on business in DC). It’s well located (although a little walk from the subway) in an old style street. The hotel itself is tastefully decorated. The rooms are spacious and sympathetically laid out. Don't be put off by the somewhat small reception area which can get a busy at times. I really liked the complimentary wine / wine tasting in the early evening and bar has real atmosphere (unusual for a hotel!). Price wise it’s not cheap, but this is DC and, in my view, the Topaz is fairly good value. I stayed in a rear facing room which was quite – it’s on a quiet street, so my guess is that the front rooms would equally allow for a relaxing stay. Service was first class.
In summary - recommended if you like boutique hotels (as I do) and are in the neighbourhood.

title: “Good service”
text: We stayed here from July 5-9, 2012 and were not disappointed. Steep walk to hotel but burned up dinner calories this way! Booked through a third party Internet company and was sold two double beds. Upon arrival, was told only had kings left. Since we were travelling with our 9-year-old I refused. Front desk agent went to get a manager who first said we had to keep the king and pay 30$ a night for a roll-way. I again declined and held fast to what I had prepaid with Hotel.com. After about 5 minutes of going back and forth, the hotel manager agreed to providing the roll-away bed at no cost. He was a dapper young bespectacled gentleman with a charming accent. Once this matter was sorted out our stay was amazing. Beautiful large room. Kurig coffee-maker. Our housekeeper was friendly and did an excellent job. The concierge made good dinner suggestions for a family. We enjoyed cocktails at the Top of the Mark. Views stunning. Drinks over-priced and small food portions but we watched the sunset and the views were priceless.We would stay here again.

title: “Charming Hotel, Super Staff, Great Location”
text: The purpose of our trip was to do some Holiday shopping in a real city and have some fun in the process. The hotel is easy to find and just a couple of blocks from Union Square, great stores and the Cable cars. For the first time since we left Chicago I actually enjoyed shopping. We had a Duluxe Queen room which was clean, quiet and comfortable. The bed was great and the shower was sweet. The rooms are a bit on the small side but to us that was part of the charm. It's an old school hotel with its own personality but I understand that some people might prefer more space and less character. Everyone we encountered on the Staff from check-in to check-out was very friendly and efficient and gave excellent directions and suggestions. We've already decided to make Holiday shopping in San Francisco a tradition and the Warwick will definitely be a major part of the plan.

title: “Great location, good service"”
text: I am a picky guest, working in the hotel industry for a competitor. The Sheraton Chicago hotel staff was terriffic. Despite the heavy bookings and turnover during our stay, the staff blocked us an additional room on the same floor when our son joined us for the second night of our stay. The hotel allowed us a late checkout for the larger room on the day of departure, which was nice for us as a family since our planes did not depart until late afternoon. All of us agreed the beds were very comfortable. The hotel was very busy the entire period of our stay, but we nevertheless received excellent and cheerful service, from the front desk to the housekeepers to the bell staff. Beautiful lakefront views from the rooms, and the location is ideal--just a block east of the congestion of Michigan Avenue and close to the Loop. The hotel is less than a ten minute walk to Millennium Park and the Art Institute...make sure you find an hour or two to visit. We booked as part of a wedding group, and the rate was very good. We did not use most of the hotel facilities because I am a former Chicagoan familiar with the city; this hotel was well located to get to all our destinations (restaurants, Navy Pier, Lincoln Park, Grant Park, museums, theater, North Side, Hyde Park), and, unlike many of the downtown hotels, it has very convenient access by car/taxi with none of the Loop or Michigan Avenue congestion.

title: “Absolutely Fantastic!”
text: I booked my room and received a discounted rate which actually cost less than the Hilton where I usually stay while in Austin (I have been a Hilton Honors member for many years). The hotel was immaculate, all of the personnel were very friendly and helpful and Mr. Chen was a very accommodating host. My room was fabulous-the bathroom was awesome, my balcony allowed me to enjoy the sunrise while laying in bed and the breakfast was delicious. I will certainly return and will recommend this hotel to everyone I know that travels to Austin.

title: “A diamond in the rough!”
text:
OMG! Just what the doctor ordered, elegant, reasonably priced, close to IIT, and free parking! We stayed there when my husband took a weekend accelerated class at IIT. He had class from 9-5 and I wanted to have a mini “get- away.” This place is just what the doctor ordered and included free parking! A good sized room, with a flat screen TV and a 6 ft. soaking tub and soft fluffy towels! The only negative comment is that the room had plastic glasses. It would seem more upscale if there was real glassware or better quality plastic. There’s a great business center and workout room. The housekeeping staff was very accommodating and The Pearl Café offered yummy homemade food! 
The manager, Todd Solidy, gave us and extended late check out so that I would not have to wait for my husband in the lobby. This REALLY helped as I was able to have enough time to take another bath in that awesome tub! My husband came home a bit smarter and I came home pleasantly “prune-y!” All in all a great place to stay and we will definitely stay there again!

title: “Clean Modern Hotel”
text: We enjoyed this clean, modern hotel. The breakfast service was a bit scattered as all wait staff seemed to wait on all tables. One morning they ran out of coffee, another they forgot about us as we sat, at the host's suggestion, in a slightly removed location. The food was delicious once it was delivered. Much better than the typical breakfast buffets and worth the extra $10 each day.

title: “Downtown Dallas Gem”
text: We received a corner suite upgrade for just a few dollars more - what views of the old Mercantile Bank bldg/Comerica Bank Bldg and more! Not to mention the fact that this is the "Pegasus" building itself! Located in the heart of the historic district puts you just steps from great shopping, restaurants, bars and Thanksgiving Square - a MUST for every visitor to downtown Dallas. The free drinks for cocktail hour, the evening cookies and the breakfast buffet were all outstanding and not to be found anywhere else in the area (for the price). What a great find!

title: “Lovely hotel in a terrific location”
text: This is a great hotel in New York City and only a few blocks from Grand Central Terminal. The staff was very friendly and the rooms are great. The banquet staff is very energetic and makes sure a meeting room is set up right.

title: “Don't be fooled by Hilton name”
text:
Amazing decor, nice historic hotel. It could be a great hotel if managed properly...
The main problem is the attitude of the staff. They are unfriendly, obnoxious, indifferent. I am not talking about housekeeping (who were relatively friendly) but about reception, concerge, and business center staff who behaved like doing a big favor by paying attention to you. 
As HHonors diamond VIP (which is Hilton highest tier - so I obviously stay quite a bit in Hiltons ) I just cannot recall being treated with such attitude anywhere in the world. I don't know whether the problem is due to the lack of training, or hotel hirig polices, or due to racial tensions in Chicago (I am coming from Canada where these are virtually non-existent). 
Hotel doesn't have adequate security, with easy access from the street arcade everyone can enter the elevators unnoticed. Coming back from dinner, I ended up riding the elevator with vomit smelling street drunk who was sporadically pressing all buttons . When raised this issue with reception, I received an answer that they cannot put steel barriers to prevent people from entering the building...?
And speaking of elevators, be prepared to wait for an elevator for about 10 min in the morning and about 5 min the rest of the day. I guess it's the price of staying in historic building :-)
Yet, the hotel lobby is fantastic and room decoration is really good. I don't regret staying in this hotel (apparently, it is longest running hotel in North America) but the service is certainly not up to Hilton standards.
And BTW, be aware that health club is only free if you are diamond VIP member.

title: “Comfort in the East Side”
text:
My family and I stayed for five days at the Lowell in April of 2012. We organized a two-bedroom suite for everyone, and I must say it was very, very comfortable. I thought the rooms were wonderful, with every amenity you can think of included - and I was happy to have a tiny kitchen as well. Beds were comfortable, and weirdly enough, the hotel was really quiet - which was a new experience for me in New York!
As other reviewers have suggested, it really was like being at home in New York.
The best thing about the Lowell are the concierge team, hands down. They were courteous, they were able to organize anything, they didn't kill you with crazy charges and if things were expensive, they were also able to offer alternatives if you wanted them. Our family usually uses the concierge service a lot, so this was perfect for us. I really appreciated both John Mark and Philip and I would go back just for them.
I was sad that we didn't have a view, but I think that is because I had asked for rooms with fireplaces; I wouldn't do this again because the fireplaces looked a bit shallow and I would have been afraid to have a fire in them, so when we go back I will try to book a suite if I can that has the outdoor area (I think it is a large covered balcony or something). Since we used to stay at the Ritz at Central Park, we really love a great view, and I feel that we missed this. But this isn't something that the Lowell can be faulted with.
I didn't really love the restaurant/bar that is next door to the hotel and is attached to it with a door. I felt that, on the one hand, it did have the feel of "old New York". On the other hand, the bar is just a line bar that is set in the walkway to the restaurant, and it didn't look comfortable or inviting. Surely there must be a way to make this place more like a place people want to have a drink before dinner?
The restaurant, in my opinion, could also use some sprucing up. We had a better experience (thanks again to the concierge) at Le Billbouquet across the street.
Finally, the hotel breakfast room/small restaurant on the second floor was really weird. I thought it was creepy the first time we were there because it is low and dark and furnished in an old-fashioned way. Later, I went down and had breakfast there, and it didn't seem so strange. It was kind of cozy. It is, again, more like a home than a hotel - which is a good thing.
All in all, I would go back. I loved the neighborhood setting as well. You don't always have to be in the middle of everything all the time, and Lowell Hotel is a nice place to kick back and relax, knowing that you are steps away from anything you want or need at any time.

title: “Tiny Rooms, Horrible Arrival Process”
text:
Great location, impressive aesthetics, friendly front desk staff, and attentive valet parking staff. Unfortunately, that's where the positives end.
The negatives started upon our arrival on a Friday afternoon. Only the doorman was working along Flower entrance, and there was absolutely no help with unloading our car full of luggage. There were no bell carts available nor were there any bellhops. The luggage was unattended along a high pedestrian traffic area, that my father felt compelled to watch them like a hawk because the solo staffer working was distracted managing other guests. After check-in, with still no sight of the bellhops, we decided to take our luggage up ourselves. We passed two bellhops on the way to the elevators, and we were denied the use of the bell carts. Fine. What exacerbated our concern that our luggage would've been mishandled was when those same bellhops tied to deliver us other people's luggage after we've been in the room for awhile. Very poor process-- totally left a bad taste in the mouth from the get go.
The rooms were TINY. Perhaps we were give the tiny rooms as we booked through Priceline, who knows? I don't even want to know how much it would've been at full price. And where are the electrical outlets to accommodate the chargers for the various electronic equipment your customers travel with? And I can't believe you still charge for wifi. 
We opted to stay at a different hotel for the second evening, which offered exponentially better amenities, larger rooms, and just as great a location. I would definitely choose them or any other hotel the next time I stay in L.A.

title: “Great Stay”
text: Our stay for 1 night was wonderful. We loved the short walk to Old Town, and the breakfast and welcome bag that was given. Would recommend to all!

title: “Homewood Suites: A terrific value!”
text: The Homewood Suites was very conveniently located, so we did not have to drive and pay parking. Enjoyed the kitchenette with full-sized fridge! Complimentary breakfast was first-rate! Even a small fire that emptied the hotel on Saturday night did not dampen our enjoyment of our stay! We will go back!

title: “Not for Sleeping or Eating”
text:
This is an older property that has been updated, but lets put it nicely the soundproofing is woefully lacking. Be forewarned, if they tell you that you have been given a room with a view of the city...ask for another. What they are not telling you is that you are also facing the train tracks! Freight trains pull thru at all hours of the night, besides the commuter system in the morning and even on the 15th floor I could hear them. Also being on the Atrium side I heard the elevators go up and down continuously. Apparently one of them needs lubrication.
The common areas are nice, the gift shop is well equipped and the snack bar is adequate. The Cafe is to be avoided. Both times I ate there the service was abysmal and the selection of food minimal (the dinner selection is worse but they have a passable buffet). I ordered the Bison Burger but was told that would take at least 15minutes....meaning the burger is so frozen the word fresh is not to be mentioned. So I opted for the Grilled Chicken Sandwich and my friend ordered the Chicken Quesidilla. After almost 20min, we inquired as to our order, it came out...mine was cold and dry, hers was more like a taco and had very little to no cheese on it. I complained and got mine comped, but still, I recognize it was a busy time, but this IS a convention hotel.....they knew this when they got into this business.
Also the location, not walking friendly, dark at night and the main walking route to the West End takes you thru a dark roadway underpass. On the good side it is connected to the Union Station via a tunnel...just don't linger too long, the tunnel is musty and smells of mold.
All in all it is a surprisingly lower than average Hyatt experience. Adequate but in no way can be considered anything but that.

title: “The best sleep I ever had!”
text: This hotel has such a great bed that you could fall sleep right away. I love the decor. The food was very good. Great customer service. It's very close to all the museum. I have nothing bad to say about it. I would definitely stay there again.

title: “Nice but not my favorite Kimpton property”
text: Have stayed in Kimptons in NYC, DC, and San Fran ( last Nov. @ Tuscan Inn). My only complaint is about the shower. We were at the Monaco for two nights earlier this month and after the first night I voiced concern/dismay that the shower had quite a bit of mold in the grout. A $3.79 bottle of Tilex could take care of the situation. I was told by a member of the front desk staff the next morning that it would be taken care of by housekeeping. It wasn't. For the price/status of the hotel I expect a clean shower. If I can see mold, what can't I see that hasn't been cleaned in the room/bathroom?

title: “A little disappointed...”
text:
Not that there was anything wrong with the hotel per se but was expecting more after reading the super awesome reviews on Trip Advisor.
Stayed there during the President's Day weekend. Location of the hotel is brilliant, less than 5 minutes walk from the union station and US Capitol. The room was spotless clean and the front desk staff was very helpful. What ticked me off was the super expensive parking - will recommend travellers to use Union Station Parking, its a 5 minutes walk till there and it is half as expensive and lack of food options in the neighbourhood except in the Union Station. Though Bistro Bis, attached to the hotel, has great reviews, options are limited and non existant for vegetarians. Overall a good experience but not a great experience

title: “Great Location, Nice Hotel”
text: Just got back from two nights at The Roosevelt Hotel with my two young kids and husband. We got a great rate and breakfast included. The hotel was a good find in a great location. Close to subway, walk to most mid-town tourist attractions. The room was a decent size, especially for NYC. The lobby was very lively and a beautiful space. Hard to go wrong with this moderatly priced hotel.

title: “Best deal in NY”
text:
My mom and I stayed at this hotel in Nov/Dec. We selected the hotel because 1) we could redeem points there and 2) it was centrally located. We didn't so much research and were pleasantly surprised at what a great hotel it is. I usually stay outside the city so I thought the room was more of an average size, but my mom said it was huge for NY. 
The hotel is fairly new and I loved the decor and feel of the lobby, rooms, and 3rd floor lounge. The staff was extremely helpful. The food (breakfast and h'orsdevoures- which could be dinner) was very good. The walk to Times Square was much quicker than we expected and there is a subway stop just a block up the street. 
The internet didn't always work. When the I.T. guy on staff wasn't able to fix the internet one night I received a call from someone at the front desk who looked up everything I wanted to know and gave me tips on restaurants and things to do. (there are also computers you can use in the lobby but I was already in my pj's). 
We will definitely stay here next time we're in NY- even if we're paying instead of redeeming points!

title: “Good location”
text: Good for 1 night stay, close to Boston commons, State House, Legal Seafood, downtown etc. Great Staff, if you need to use a computer bring your own bc they only have 3 which are always occupied. Only received one sheet and a very thin blanket, maid must of forgot to put on comforter. Excellent staff. Must eat at Legal seafood for best Lobster you will EVER have in your life.

title: “Worst customer service and unsafe”
text: My wife and I stayed here on our way to honeymoon. We arrived at 10 pm and had a couple Of drunks staring us down. I asked where the bell boy was and the response was he would be out in ten minutes. Feeling unsafe already we picked up our lugggage and went inside. The person at the front desk did very little to help when I asked her for help moving our luggage up to the room. Overall this was a very unpleasant experience.

title: “Comfortable Stay”
text:
A second stay for my wife and I. After a nice train ride to MSG, a two-block walk down 32nd st. to the hotel was easy. We were greeted by Tom at the desk who was friendly and informative. He briefly explained all the amenities and gave a map of Manhattan marking the hotel's location, which was very helpful. Our room was on the 5th floor with a nice view of 32nd street below. It was fun to people -watch from there. Rooms are small with a king bed but still had room to move about. Very clean. Bathroom was small but manageable. Shower had decent pressure. Nice picture on the flat-screen with a game control (we're not gamers). .The clock radio had an MP3 hookup and a iPod dock with great sound. 
The only negatives about the room was the A/C and the toilet. If you're going to stay here in the summer make sure the A/C works. We had maintenance fix it once but it never worked that good. We like our room cool , especially for sleeping. We managed though. The toilet tank had overflowed and flooded the bathroom. Maintenance came up promptly and fixed it. Both the toilet and the A/C were older units and could be why there were issues. But they were attended to by friendly staff members and really did not hinder our stay. The best part of our stay? The bed. It was so very, very comfortable. We walked all over lower Manhattan so at the end of the day, that bed was therapeutic. 
We had the continental breakfast one morning. It had the usual fare. The doughnuts were great. On the 14th floor is a roof-top bar that's open till midnight. Couldn't see much but had a great view of the Empire State Building which is only a block away. It's a small area but comfortable.
While all hotel pricing is high in Manhattan, the price for La Quinta was low considering the location. Two blocks from Penn Station/ MSG; one block from The Empire State Building; walking distance to Time Square, Broadway, theaters, various subway stations and food on every corner. And it,s in a safe well-lit area. Great for families. We're looking forward to staying here again.

title: “Location is AWESOME!”
text: Company had a meeting there, and it couldn't have gone better. Took the train into Penn Station directly across the street, and shuttle to the airport picked up a block away. The renovated guest rooms were very spacious....especially for New York. But the best part of the entire experience was the overall service and how genuinely nice the staff was. Everyone from the front desk to the servers were extremely nice and very helpful throughout my stay. Definitely found a new home when going back to New York.

title: “charlotte airport”
text: Excellent evening counter help, Young lady had a great smile, wonderful attitude and willing to assist... a great person to have at counter serving customer...Your Charlotte Hotel did a great job with this hire...Drivers were very pleasant as well...

title: “nice hotel in the heart of downtown”
text: The bed was super comfy as we stayed 2 nights here in Oct. I arrived a bit earlier than my friend so I had a snack and a drink at the bar. The hummus plate was pretty good and the margarita was delicious. Restaurants were all walking distance so was the concert hall (we saw Eddie Vedder play). I would stay there again.

title: “Loved it - Highly Recommended”
text:
I absolutely loved this place. It's the best value for a great price!
The design is so unique. It's exciting to explore the hotel - all the freebies - free coffee (ie, nice tea, iced coffee, hot coffee, milk, soymilk, etc.), summer drinks in the afternoon, cocktail hour every day are wonderful!
The room itself is a little small, but the bed is wonderful, everyone is extremely helpful, you're right in the middle of the city, and you get a lot of other freebies!
Tip - join the kimpton list to get free wifi and 2 free cocktails and an appetizer, and $10 off the minibar!

title: “A solid option in San Francisco”
text:
We stayed at the W Hotel in San Francisco in May 2010. At check-in, we were told that our room had been upgraded, which was not the case. This is not a big deal, given that we had reserved a large corner room, but it was strange.
The W hotel concept seems slightly out of place in a hotel this large. At three times the size, the personal touch and some of the services that we take for granted at W in Montreal are either lost or fully booked at W in San Francisco. The guide books list this as a “boutique”hotel, but despite the funky décor in the lobby, the elevators, and the guestrooms, it seemed more generic and anonymous. 
All of that aside, it is a very nice, comfortable hotel. There are very nice views, and it is convenient for public transportation and walking. The pool, deck, and fitness facilities seemed nice,though the deck was closed and covered in a tent. It is a very solid option among four-star hotels.
Overall, we would stay here again, but we would look around at other options as well.

title: “Not as nice as it looks from the outside!”
text:
I live about 2 blocks away from the Beach Haven Inn, so when my dad came down to visit, I tried to find him a cheap room nearby. From the street (and if you don't look closely), the Beach Haven Inn looks like a cute little hotel, and it always is busy in the summers. It also was less thatn $100/night, which is unusual in San Diego. 
Well, it's not as cute/nice as it looks from the street. The building/rooms are in desparate need of a new coat of paint, as well as new furniture. The room was a decent size, and clean (I actually talked to the housekeeping two different days, and I think they were really making an effort to keep it clean). But man, does this place need renovating. The bathroom was tiny, and flooded every day. The ceiling had major water damage, and the sink/cabinet was so old the door kept falling off, and also leaked. 
If this place was better maintained, it would be a nice little hotel in a great location...unfortunately, it isn't!

title: “Great Place To Stay By The Beach”
text: The hotel is situatated adjacent to the beach. Many of the rooms have a wonderful view of the ocean, which is extremely easy to hear from the hotel, is relaxing to listen to in the evening. The staff was wonderful and we will be lodging here the next time we decide to stay in San Diego. I would definately recommend this hotel to any family wanting a clean, quiet, and friendly place to stay near the beach.

title: “Spend most of your time out of the room !”
text: This hotel has a great location, it's so easy to get to the Powell cable car line and Market street for the BART and Muni. We felt safe walking around at night not too many beggars, but if you go towards Japantown or the Civic centre that all changes. The room was old, hot & a little smelly but not unbearable considering we didn't spend much time in the room. Poor water pressure in the shower, small towels and the hair dryer was a waste of time. The first night we stayed on the Geary st side of the hotel, which was a bigger room with a wardrobe but the street noise was too much to get a good night rest so we moved to the other side of the building. This was much quieter, but a smaller room with only a view of the alley. The staff were OK, they didn't go out of their way, but did all that was required of them. We overheard a couple of the front desk staff rubishing the hotel one night and calling it a dive, so that doesn't give you a lot of confidence in the place. For a cheap place to crash in a great location this would be fine, but we will be spending the extra $$ next time for somewhere else.

title: “Best bet for conference travel to Denver”
text: The closest hotel to the convention center in Denver, the Hyatt Regency is nicely styled, has excellent customer service (friendly employees everywhere), and reasonable conference rates. It is at the high end of other Hyatts I have visited in styling. The Altitude had a decent breakfast buffet with pricing typical for hotels of this sort.

title: “A relaxing retreat in bustling Boston.”
text: My husband and I had a wonderful stay at 15 Beacon in historic Boston. This quiet, boutique hotel offers a wonderful combination of old world charm with modern amenities. The gorgeous studio we stayed in was tastefully decorated in neutral colors and furnished with a contemporary flair. Loved the ease of working the gas fireplace and stereo from the bed. Loved the shower! Enjoyed wrapping up in the terry robe after pampering myself with the soy shampoo, pomegranate conditioner and lemon sugar lotion. Fitness center was bright, clean and stocked with waters. In our opinion, the rooftop garden patio with comfortable teak furniture is the hotel's best kept secret! A great place to enjoy a drink and some North-End bought appetizers. We had a great stay!

title: “Large, clean, comfortable room with excellent coffee”
text: Convenient parking at reasonable rates, friendly and helpful front desk staff, interesting mural in a very spacious and clean room, excellent complimentary coffee service, comfortable working chair and desk and a nice round table alongside a bay window with a street view, good quality toiletries, good selection of cable channels, located just across japantown - if you manage to get there on time, you might even be able to get the best coffee cake in the japanese store across the street. A healthy uphill walk will either take you to streets lined with nice homes where locals live, or take you to Fillmore where you can meander into-and-out of one-of-a-kind retail outlets and restaurants. I would recommend this, and would return when there is an opportunity.

title: “The perfect place to wait for your next flight”
text:
Right at the Airport, this hotel has everything you need while waiting for your next flight. Rooms are big and clean with excellent beds and pillows. The hotel has a good pool and 2 restaurants one of them the typical sports Bar where you can have a cold beer and appetizers.
The staff is excellent

title: “Old Westin, but enjoyable”
text:
We had a day in San Francisco and the Westin St. Francis was not planned. Due to a bad experience at another hotel, we ended up here. We got a room on the 26th floor of the tower building. It had a city view but nothing to elaborate about. We just wanted to come back to the "heavenly beds" after a day in the city. 
The hotel is close to everything and we walked a lot!! We never even saw the car until it was time to check out. There were few issues with this room, but this is an older (historic) Westin. I was credited upon checkout when I mentioned it to the front desk. 
The hotel was good for what we wanted, a great bed, and a central location. Although it can get noisy outside, but it's a city. Being on higher floors we were still able to hear a lot. 
The concierge was very helpful. I don't think I would stay here again though.

title: “One of the best hotels I have ever stayed at”
text: I was very impressed with the staff from the Valet parking to the service staff. I was treated with the utmost of respect. The room was very clean and the bed very comfortable. The location is just a block up from the harbor so it is an easy walk to get there. The entrance was just off the street but with the valet service that was fine also.

title: “Perfect spot!”
text: We stayed at the Wyndham Blake for two nights and had a great stay. Nicely central. Only a 10 minute can ride from anything and everything (Museum Campus, Navy Pier, Millenium park, Union Station, etc). The staff is wonderful and the rooms are very well appointed with lovely high ceilings. Would definitely stay there again.

title: “Personal and Business perspective review”
text:
I have stayed at this hotel over 15 times for business and once, my last trip for a personal trip. 
My fiancee is from Kansas and his best friend and wife flew in to celebrate his birthday. They had never seen NY so I used Marriot points to book us a weekend at the Marquis. The main plus of this hotel is location. It sits in the heart of Time Square and most rooms have a fabulous view. For those not familiar with Manhattan it is in Midtown meaning it is centrally located on the island.
The bad: The parking attendants are clearly not trained in the "Marriot way" and you can expect to find a "lot full" sign posted if you are checking in on a Friday or Sat. They are experts in the NY way, which means be prepared to pay. Tip $20 bucks and a parking spot magically appears. Marriot really has to fix this as it's hurting their reputation. Full should really mean full especially when it costs $50 bucks a night already to park your beloved vehicle. I saw the parking attendants turn away an elderly couple who had driven from Canada telling them the lot was full and that they had to find another lot. It was shameful. Sending these elderly people out into a city they clearly did not know to find a garage that was 10 blocks away. They didn't even take their baggage and hold it for them.
My other gripe is the Japanese restaurant in the lobby (8th floor). It is just awful if you want sushi. I took our friends from Kansas there our first night and the fish was not tasteful and the avocado was brown....ugh. If you must eat there order the steak. The waitstaff is pretty bad too. There are a million fabulous places to eat in NY, go find em!
Marriot classifies this as a category 7 hotel but I really think only the location makes it a 7. The carpet is just hideous and the rooms could use redecorating. 
The good: Especially if you have friends or clients from out of town go sit in the lobby bar and you will find the whole side of the bar is a glass wall that overlooks times square. The drinks are pricey but worth it for the view. Also, if money is not a concern eat in the restaurant on the top floor that rotates. It's excellent and worth it. 
The check in staff have always been helpful and will generally give you times square view for no extra charge if you ask nicely. The maid service is always good and the concierge is not terribly friendly but then again you are in NY. She does her job but does not go above and beyond. Do you your own research and get the maps from her. 
The gym is good for those weary business folks that need a work out. Keep in mind there is no pool though. 
The business center is well run and efficient. 
**One tip for everyone about the elevators**
When you walk in on the first floor you will see a bank of elevators labeled alphabetically A,B,C and so on. You will also see a key pad mounted to the wall at the front of the bank of elevators. You must type in what floor you want to go to before you board an elevator. The keypad will tell you which elevator is going to your floor. For instance you need to check in so you need the 8th floor. Type in 8 and the keypad will blink a letter like "J". Board the elevator labeled J and it will automatically go to the 8th floor. There are no buttons on the inside of any of the elevators. It all runs off the keypad by computer. If board any old elevator you will have the pleasure of going where everyone else needs to go. Just a tip! I can't tell you how many people I have seen dash for an elevator only to get inside and look dumbfounded when there are no buttons to push. 
Enjoy!

title: “A great old hotel with a lot of charm...but even better Staff!”
text:
I have read through a lot of the posted reviews and have to agree with a lot of what has been said - sure some things could be upgraded, and for the prices they charge, there should never be the smell of mold in the carpeting. However, there are some outstanding things about this hotel - but you need to do a little work to be able to access all that this place has to offer. 
1st - join the Fairmont President Club - it's FREE and then the internet service will also be FREE! (otherwise they charge $14.00/day) in addition to a whole bunch of other perks - so why don't more people do it? I have no idea, but I see that many people like to complain about things that they could have changed themselves (and for the person who complained about lack of newspapers - they do come FREE when you join up).
2nd - you can get a great French Press coffee maker with a European style water heater pot delivered to your room with plenty of Wolfgang Puck coffee - delivered FREE to your room - you just have to ask for it (same goes with a refrigerator!) 
With out a doubt - have the hotel house dog in the lobby for guests to play with is a really sweet thing about the hotel (and if you don't like dogs...you can just ignore her - she doesn't seem to mind).
What really stood out about the hotel was the people working here though - from the front desk (a very very patient woman walked me through getting onto the wireless system when I called up for help) to the room service (so one of the spoons in the coffee set was dirty, and they seem to only serve half and half with the coffee - no skim milk or low fat alternatives - BUT they came quickly with new dishes and an unopened box of Soy milk - which was great!). The guy cleaning the room was super friendly and offered plenty of extra towels (I did notice our bath mat had some sort of stains on it and probably should be taken out of rotation for what they charge here - but I just turned it over and moved on to more important things). When I went out for a run, the wonderful woman at the Concierge Desk gave me a small map/fold up card with a 2 1/2 mile - 5 mile path on it, and she also gave me her card - in case I got lost and wanted to call, which I felt was really nice.
About the intermittent web connection - although I was connected during the day - at some point the wireless connection just shut down in the evening. Again I called the front desk but this time they transferred me to their help desk (somewhere far away overseas not in the buiiding) where I got an extremely helpful person who had to walk me through connecting in a much more complicated way then when I first signed on - for reasons he didn't explain - but when it was all done and working - he said he could make sure that my room would stay completely connected until the time I checked out - and so far this morning - it's still working. He also gave me his number and a ticket # in case something went wrong and I could call back and the next person helping would have seen what had already been done to my account to get me up and connected.
I'll admit - my husband and I couldn't normally afford to stay here at these prices but we are here for his business meeting and the room rates were heavily discounted. Now that we are members of the hotel's President Club - we've got nothing to loose - and a lot to gain by checking them out first when booking our next trip.
I see that the comments left by the hotel in response to the complaints is that they are upgrading for their 2012 anniversary. As someone that tends to like "old/original" over "new and shiny" I'm hoping the charm of the somewhat dark hallways (think of the movie "The Shining" - before it gets to the creepy parts) with great pieces of old ephemera framed on the wall - and the unusual things like the large walk in closets with the old fashioned hooks on the wall (as well as regular hangers, iron and ironing board), lots of wood molding around the doors, windows etc....and most unusual in these times, and important to some of us - windows that you can open to let the fresh air in! (and as people have mentioned - the beds are very comfortable).
If you have to pay full price for the room - then honestly, for the people who are used to paying these prices, I gather this place may not fit their expectations (i.e. like the small gym and some older wooden - not sleek - furniture). However, if you like things just a little off the beaten path (but in a great location) and want to feel some old world charm and luxury - then I believe you would really enjoy it here.

title: “Does what it says on the tin!!!”
text:
The Layne Hotel is a great base for a city break in san Fransisco.
 It has a great location just outside the main shopping centre of Union Square. 
 The rooms are fine/clean and you have everything you need..
 Randy and his family who own the layne are very helpful and will help you out whenever they can... 
 if i were going to stay in san fransisco for a shopping or sight seeing hols then this is where i would stay again.. great budget hotel with great location...

title: “Belle Auberge!”
text: We thoroughly enjoyed our stay at Petite Auberge after a flight and two train rides in coach class spanning 3 days from NYC via Chicago and L.A. On arrival we were fatigued but delighted by a warm welcome, a comfortable and clean room with a luxurious bed. The breakfast buffet was excellent and varied on each of the three mornings. Tasteful decor with a different helping of biscuits/ cake in the foyer each evening after a days walking round the city. We were able to store our luggage after check out until our evening flight. The hotel is ideally situated, the staff are helpful and we would gladly return on our next trip to San Francisco. Fantastic! ****

title: “horrible bathroom”
