text: My husband and I stayed at this hotel July 4th weekend. The hotel is in a very nice area with tons of restaurants as soon as you step outside. Our room was very clean; we thought the staffs were friendly and helpful. The shower was horrible, trying to close the curtain for a shower was a job itself. The showerhead keeps falling. Overall, it was okay for us. We would not recommend this hotel for first timer to Chicago.

title: “Luxurious Hotel”
text: This hotel was excellent in all aspects of the word. The room was very spacious and the decor was classy. My favorite was the large bathroom with marble countertops and floors. The beds were very comfy to cuddle up in at night with very soft sheets. We had a great view of Michigan Avenue. Due to our early arrival, the staff was very friendly and helpful to stow our luggage while we hit the town. The only down side was the mediocre room service, but other than that, no other complaints. It's a great place to stay and in a great location in the heart of the city.

title: “Exceeded My Expectations”
text:
I stayed here as part of a business trip and professional group meetings. The view and location are first rate. It is five minutes from Boston Logan airport by taxi (also there is a convenient train/subway). The hotel has waterfront views and is right on the harbor. The Seaport area is a nice upscale clean, scenic, safe area with lots of bars, dining, and amenities. 
The rooms were clean, new and well appointed. I had a group rate which was $209 / night plus a $3 ‘inclusive facility’ charge which allows access to the exercise facility and internet. That is much less than the going rate at a lot of the nicer hotels in downtown Boston. 
They have outstanding fitness facility that is clean, new and well stocked with, weights, elliptical, treadmills, stationary bikes; everything was in good running order. And they have a great swimming pool. 
The also have a variety of eateries, bar, coffee shop, onsite. 
I would highly recommend this for anyone visiting Boston. It’s great for a business trip or even better if you have a few days to stay and enjoy the scenery, history and nightlife of Boston.

title: “Hotel Max....stay in Seattle with a rockstar!”
text: Very cool, sleek Seattle hotel. This hotel was easy to find after exiting I-5. When you arrive plan to be well taken care of. The doorman was there waiting for us and the lovely staff at the front desk had us checked in and on our way to our room. We stayed in a suite which was quite spacious, had a very comfortable king bed with great linens, a deep bath tub and was decorated with cool art. Make sure to check out all of the rockstars on the 5th floor doors (each floor has a different theme). The staff is very attentive and really knew the area well for suggestions. The sushi was great at the hotel's Red Fin Restaurant. I would recommend this hotel for business or leisure, it is in a great location to walk to Pikes Place.

title: “Amazing Service, Great Experience”
text: My company has had two training session at this hotel and both have nothing less than outstaning. The employees are helpful and pleasant to deal with. The management staff is willing to do anything to make you and the other guest happy. Its a great hotel.!!!!!

title: “Predictably good - like always”
text:
We've been staying here for about 2 years now when making quarterly trips to Chgo. While it's just south of Chicago's main Downtown (The Loop) the location is good. Right near public transit and the self-parking is free.
The rooms are spacious, with a European soaking tub. Our room had a fridge, too. We enjoyed the view. Only two things were lacking: restaurants within walking distance and they couldn't clean the room until afternoon because of being at 100% occupancy.

title: “They had me, then they lost me...literally. But still lots of good amenities and terrific location.”
text:
My first business trip in a long while, went to Chicago to spend two days working on a project, and chose this from several in the area that my company offered because we had a great corporate rate and location was good. Initially was very impressed. We checked in mid-day and both my colleague and I immediately were able to go to our rooms (early). Trendy vibe the moment you walk through the door. Through some promotion I don't recall, I'm currently Starwood Gold, so was upgraded to a spectacular view of Lake Michigan and Navy Pier on the 24th floor and given 4pm checkout on the day of departure, which was nice with a late flight. 
Room had flat-screen TV, two double beds, well-equipped bathroom with nifty Bliss amenities (and there's a Bliss spa on premises). There is an odd window in the bathroom with shutters that can open and close. I didn't mind it, but can see where it might freak out traditionalists. iPod docking station on the nightstand has become an expected but welcome amenity in this class of hotel. Weird traditional analog bedside clock was very hard to see if you woke up in the middle of the night. Closet space is strange because clothing storage is in drawers undeneath the closet so you have to awkwardly bend down to get your clothes. Not a deal breaker but if I had a bad back, would be annoyed. I missed some small amenities like an in-room coffeemaker and a stand for my suitcase for packing/unpacking. 
Everything's very design-y and trendy and theme-y. The extra roll of toilet paper in the bathroom had a cover titled "Backup Plan," the newspaper was presented every day in a grey bag titled "News" that hung on the doorknob,even the bathmat had the word "Step" inscribed on it. Little details were fun; guess these are a W signature but I don't stay at a lot of them.
Had best intentions of working out so I did visit the pool and gym area, which seemed well equipped. The pool is indoors but there is an outdoor deck which would be fun in the summer months. Loved the treadmills facing the lake. Sadly, business and sleep took priority and I never made it there to actually work out. 
Had a great ahi tuna sandwich for lunch at the lobby bar and our group even briefly checked out Whiskey Sky, the rooftop bar, which wasn't as exciting as we'd hoped - very small and the view was better from my room.
We had the chance to try their Acura "Wherever Whenever" service where their driver will take you anywhere you need to go within 5 miles of the hotel - much more pleasant and fun than a regular taxi cab. Service starts at noon so not great for early morning business meetings, but a really fun perk. 
So I was feeling great about the place initially, but the love affair ended abruptly when after a grueling 12 hour work day, I came back to my room to find that they'd checked me out. All my things were still there, untouched, but a friend came to visit and texted me to tell me the front desk told her I'd checked out. A half-hour ordeal ensued with a manager (Sasha) who insisted my reservation was only for one night (though I had an itinerary and materials given me at check-in that clearly stated two nights) and suggested that somehow I had made the mistake. "No, there's nothing noted here in the change log, it always was for just one night..." she kept saying over and over again. Wish she'd spent less energy insisting I was wrong and more energy trying to fix it. I was finally checked in again, but the next day the bill slipped under my door was wrong on so many counts that I had to go to the front desk again to fix it. Wound up with two separate bills, one for each night, which should be fun for submitting expenses.
Parking was a breathtaking $48, so I was glad I didn't have a rental car, internet access was $40 for 3 days, and they charged me $2.29 access for calling the airline's 800 number. Be aware. 
Would I stay there again? Sure. But I'd make them print out proof of my check-out date and rate the moment I checked in. I would skip the internet access and stick to the cell phone for all my calls, even 800 numbers.
The hotel is a block away from West Egg Cafe, a favorite breakfast spot, and another restaurant recommendation is Graham Elliot (not in the neighborhood but worth seeking out). Pumpernickel crusted sturgeon was amazing.

title: “Fabulous Hotel”
text:
I LOVE this Hotel!! I have bee nwith my husband for a romantic getaway, the family for vacation and with friends for fun. Always a wonderful stay at this Hotel. Excellent service, location, clean, good views & everything you need is close enough to walk too! I will be back many times. 
~ Sandra Nelson

title: “Excellent hotel and staff”
text:
We had to stay here for almost 4 weeks while my wife recovered from surgey at a nearby hospital. The sales manager worked with me on a long stay rate and I can say that I am very satisfied with the hotel property and the staff. All of the staff was friendly and accomodating. The shuttle ride from the airport had complimentary water. The hotel has free cookies and newspaper every day. I liked the library in the lobby that allows you to check out and read books. Every morning there was a hot breakfast with eggs bacon or sausage and fruits.
There was an evening reception Mon-Thursday with free beer wine and hot snacks.
There is really not much more you can ask for.
You easily walk to a Pizza place, Thai, Outback, Liquor store and a Mexican restraunt
Excellent stay and the pool and hottub was nice for my daughter.

title: “Gotta love the staff!”
text: Our first impression was from Sheila our shuttle driver. what a great gal...went out of her way to take care of us! Could not ask for better service than from Lauren at the front desk....she made us feel like family! The room is comfortable and clean. Happy with our choice to stay here the night before our cruise.

title: “Got a great price on Priceline, but had some issues”
text:
Overall, we enjoyed our stay. The room was very clean with a microwave, fridge and coffee maker. Very modern designs and the bathroom was very spacious. The tub had a place to sit down which my son loved. Wifi worked great both night we were there and its about 10 min to the zoo, park and the museum campus. Close to Reliant Stadium and there was a grocery store within walking distance. The Residence Inn is next door.
The issue we had was as Priceline customers, we were forced to pay a 100 buck deposit at checkin. We chose the pay in in cash because they said they would put a hold on our credit card for up to 10 days and since we were in transit to other cities, we didn't want that much of a hold put on our card. The checkin process was rude and I felt that we were being treated differently because we were priceline customers. As a Marriott Rewards member, I find this type of behavior offensive. If they don't want the business then they should get out of priceline's system.
At checkout, we couldn't get our deposit back until someonewent into visually inspect the room to make sure nothing was broken or missing. Again, offensive to the guest and this practice needs to stop. It took about 15 min to get our deposit back because they couldn't find someone to go inspect the room. Mangement didn't even offer any sort of apology. Their explaination was "its our policy and that's how it is"
My other issue was the fridge, It just would not cool no matter what. My son is on a special diet so we always have to travel with food. But this time we need the fridge for medicine as well. Someone looked at the the first day and it worked for about 2 hrs then it wouldn't cool at all. I complained again and was told I was not eligible for compensation. I don't want anything, I just want it fixed I told the woman at the desk. She offered free breakfast coupons, which I accepted, but it still didn't fix the problem. The food had to be thrown out because it spoiled and I had to refill the Rx. She did offer the reimburse the food costs, but I had brought everything at home so I didn't have the receipt.
The breakfast was very good and we were able to get an entree with a meat and a drink with the coupons. The lady at the cafe even gave my son an extra juice and she gave my husband a free coffee as well.
There is a business center as well but the internet seems to work when it feels like it. It logs out after a few min for whatever reason and then you have to log in all over again. I had problems with the printers on several occassions and the front desk staff didn't seem to care. One man did go out of his way to help me print our tickets for NASA and I appreciated that.
I would probably stay here again but as a full paying guest. I didn't appreciate being treated differently as a priceline guest and they need to do a full disclosure to priceline so that priceline can inform their customers of the additional costs.

title: “A great stay!”
text: Superb customer service, excellent food, well appointed room, great view of CIty Centre, did I say superb customer service? Worth repeating. I will happily stay here monthly on business travel, and hope to enjoy this fantastic property for pleasure travel also.

title: “Exceptional Guest Service”
text: I was recently in San Antonio for business and extended the stay with my family for my mother's birthday. The only other hotel I have seen this level of attention, is in the Ritz and 4 Seasons. And even in those hotels due to there larger size it was not as consistantly wonderful as it was here. They have made an art out of focusing on the little things that are important to the guest. The staff in every part of the hotel are friendly and willing to provide anything to make the stay great. We had several meals in Ostra (the main resturant in the hotel) and the food was well prepared and the wait staff bend over backwards to give you a great meal. I will be back in San Antonio often and I think I have found where I will be staying on a regualr basis.

title: “Perfect for the business trip”
text: This hotel has all the qualities I want in a business hotel. Clean, comfortable, quiet, nice bathroom, spacious, friendly staff. Since I wouldn't be in this part of Florida for fun, I just want the basics done right when I come here. And they do this really well.

title: “Loved, loved, loved Nine Zero!”
text: Nine Zero was our favorite hotel on our New England vacation. We stayed 3 nights. Great room size for our family which includes 2 teens. We had 2 queen beds and a cot and still had room to walk! The beds were very comfortable. Great location - right on the Freedom trail! We walked everywhere - we didn't even need to use a taxi. Restaurants, sightseeing, Long Wharf - it's all right there! Staying at the Nine Zero really added to the wonderful time we had visiting Boston! Love Kimptons!

title: “Great stay”
text: We had to spend an unplanned night at BWI recently and stayed at the Sheraton by random choice. We called from the airport and they quickly answered and confirmed a room. The shuttle was there in minutes (the hotel is right next to the airport so you do hear planes). The front desk people were so welcoming and friendly. It was so nice after a rough day at the airport. The room was great and we ate dinner in the pub. If we ever get stuck in Baltimore again - we will definitely stay at this hotel.

title: “Not bad for the Money”
text: This hotel is not in the best neighborhood and there is a lot of road construction going on, but they are making the best of it with friendly service and clean rooms. The beds were clean and comfortable, the free breakfast was good, plenty of clean towels and a nice swimming pool. I couldn't believe the price and the fact that parking was free this close to downtown. I'm in San Antonio a few times a month and will stay here again.

title: “Good Mid Manhattan hotel choice”
text: Value and location makes this Marriott Courtyard property a great choice for theater and sightseeing visits to Manhattan. I stayed here five days while attending a business meeting nearby. After price shopping on line, I found this matched my needs and location. Easy walk to the Browadway theaters, so no cab rides required! Friendly reception staff were helpful with directions and suggestions. Room was perfectly clean, great bed, adequate bathroom. Housekeeping tends to arrive late afternoon, but did a fine job. Flat screen TV is nice but remote control did not work well. There are good casual dining options within the block, including a great bar and grill directly across the street. The "Times Square" name is slightly misleading, since it's a three block walk to actual Times Square--not a problem, but don't expect to see the neon glow from your room. My room view was a brick wall. There is another Courtyard a few blocks farther from Times Square, so check exact address.

title: “Good location but the air conditioners.....”
text: This hotel is very very good for the location (5min walk from Grand Central, 7th Avenue); it's one of the few hotel still having breakfast included into the room rate (maybe because this is a former italian chain hotel) and the bathroom is all decorated with marbles and very clean; the real "negative" point is due to the air conditioner: we stayed there 4 days in Aug 2012 and NY was like a oven and the air conditioner in the room, an old type, was very VERY noisy; apart from this, maybe the fornitures could be renewed cos they clearly are directly from 80's, but at the end this is not a real problem.

title: “Door Broken, Apathetic Employees Acted Bothered”
text: Was originally checked into a room with a broken door that wouldn't close and had to move. Second room didn't have hot water. Room wasn't cleaned the next day and the third night the noise coming from adjoining room was unacceptable. Called front desk and got major attitude from Vanessa. Also, housekeeper and front desk clerk sat in the guest breakfast area each morning and ate in front of guests. Carpet also turned our white socks brown.

title: “Loved my stay....”
text:
Had a wonderful stay at the Charlesmarks hotel. The price was reasonable and I was close to where I had to go.
The Hotel is small but I loved it. Very reasonable in price and the staff was nice. I did not have any problems. I had a queen size bed, which was on the second floor. It was a nice size for me. I was not planning to live in the room, it fit what I had come to Boston to do. Go visit friends. 
A great place to stay if you dont plan on staying in the room all day and night. I love the sound system in the room. The music was also heard in the bathroom during a nice hot shower. 
The hotel is directly across from the "Boston Public Library". The bar is really small downstairs; however really nice.

title: “very good -remember you are in NY”
text: I liked in stay here. The room is really short but remember: you are at ny!! The price is good, you have a free continental breakfast and you are so close to Macys, Empire state and others attractions! I payed U$140 dollars for 4 people with breakfast! Its amazing..

title: “Excellent value!”
text: We stayed a few nights in this hotel and found it to be a great value. We booked through hotels.com and I thought we were getting a king suite, but we had a king bed and a pull-out sofa (with very little room between). The room and the bathroom were very clean. I found it strange that we didn't have a microwave or a refridgerator in our room. The location was a little challenging to get to when we used our GPS because it didn't recognize that there's a "back way" in because you can't turn left off of El Camino Real when you're going under the interstate.

title: “Fair priced for its location; breakfast pales compared to other Residence Inns”
text:
Good location (5 mins to harbour); room seemed new and very comfortable. 
Breakfast selection is average...closer to a Hampton Inn & Suites than the full breakfast buffet i've seen at a different Residence Inn
Valet parking is pretty pricey ($28)...that's the price to pay for this location!

title: “Great Location and Service”
text:
My family went there for a birthday long weekend and had a great experience. we have 3 babies (all under the age of 2) and let me tell you, we were pleased. (aside from the NOISY neighbors that we had in the adjoining room next door - they were clearly drunk and didn't get that there were infants in the room next door). 
the rooms were spacious enough for us to fit 2 cribs and still have walking room. the location was great - right in the middle of what we needed just steps away from reading terminal. the staff was great as well - like i mentioned before about the noisy neighbors, i called the front desk and minutes later it was quiet.

title: “Great Christmas vacation!”
text:
Based mainly on the reviews we read here, we selected the White Swan to visit the Bay Area over Christmas. The property was charming, the breakfasts were both satisfying and varied from day to day, and the location was convenient. I expected small rooms but the rooms were more than adequate in size. The staff was extremely helpful, taking time to fill us in on not just local attractions but discussing local culture and news. It was a perfect location for a family Christmas gathering, with the fireplaces (we brought our own stockings). The walk to Union Square was easy. We stayed there with our children 15 & 23, and they liked it as well. We checked out at noon and they graciously let us store our luggage until late that evening.
If I had to stretch to pick negatives, I would mention that the bathroom fan sounded like an airplane engine, but that was the only negative.
Overall a very nice experience in the heart of the city.

title: “Washington 2011”
text: Wonderful hotel. I am now hooked on Hampton Inn. The breakfast is amazing and had something for all of our ten guests even those with picky pallets. The staff was very friendly and welcoming. They took care of all of our needs, even seemed to know what we needed before we did. Downsides to this hotel: Parking for checking in. We were a little confused when we arrived and found the two spaces out front to be taken by a limo and a repair van. We ended up parking our two cars in the road to unload which made for a stressful check-in and paying to have our cars parked overnight was pricey also. Also, we reserved three double queen rooms and found that they were not available when we arrived even though we arrived on time. Two of our rooms had been switched to king sized beds with pull out sofas, this was frustrating. The pool was a huge hit with the kids but the hot tub was undergoing repair. Other than that, our stay was perfect.

title: “Beautiful”
text: Well, there is not much to say about this one. All you can expect from a beautiful hotel like this came true. Great service, outstanding food ( had the breakfast and was at The Bazaar ). Everybody is very friendly and I will come back for sure ;-)

title: “Girls Trip 2011”
text: The whole property was amazing. The staff made us feel so welcome and our rooms fantastic. The restaurant was wonderful and our server (Angel) was very delightful. The patio lounge (bar) was a nice place to sit out and visit after our long days of exploring the City. Over all our experience was fantastic.

title: “Love, Love, Love this Hotel.”
text: This hotel is in a great location. Parking garage is right next door and they are reasonable in price compared to being right in Times Square. You are about 2 blocks from the center of Times Square. Plenty of restaurants just around the corner. Breakfast & WiFi is included. Staff is extremely friendly and helpful. Our room had 2 double beds. My only wish for this hotel would be to offer two queen beds or a king bedroom with a pullout sofa. If I was to bring my family of 4 back, 2 double beds would be a bit cramped. But that is just my personal preference. I will be back to this hotel.

title: “7 Good Nights”
text:
Having just returned from a week at the Boston Park Plaza the only let down was the room to room noise. As far as my wife and I were concerned the sound proofing could be better.
The bathroom was small by US standers but did it's job, good shower and clean. Good bed and clean room. Lots to do and see, we walked most places, Coply shops, the harbour ,Park ,and part of the Freedom Trail.
If you do not have time for a sit down breakfast there is coffee and patries etc to go by the bar area.
Bonfire the onsite restaurant is very good, great steak (but closed Sunday's)
Would I recommend it to a friend, Yes, but would have to mention the room to room noise.

title: “Great place to stay”
text:
We spent 4 nights at the Comfort Inn in Aug 2003. It was a really nice place to stay. The staff were lovely - very helpful and when we arrived at 11pm, were only too pleased to recommend a safe place for us to eat. 
The free breakfast buffet is great - loads of bagels, muffins, coffee, cereal... We loaded up for the day! The rooms were small but clean with a nice bathroom. It's very central too - 10 mins to Fisherman's Wharf, 10 mins to the Cable Cars... plus, the buses stop right outside the hotel. Only one tiny thing - on our last night, we had a cockroach in our bathroom. I have had that before in lots of US hotels so it didn't put me off. So stay there!

title: “excellent location!”
text: This was my family's first trip to Chicago, and we loved the city. The location of the Hyatt was perfect, steps away from many restaurants, the Magnificent Mile, and the double decker bus tour that we enjoyed. The front foyer of this hotel is beautiful, The room was clean, spacious, and a bit dated. This didn't bother us, as we didn't spend too much time here. The workout room is great, with lots to do. The pool was clean, but very small. I would stay here again, if I got the same hotwire deal. I think my feelings about this hotel may be different if I paid full price. The biggest downfall was the cost of parking, $55 a night. The valet service is a great idea, but since the location was so great, we didn't use our car once while in the city.

title: “Pleasant front desk staff, wonderful breakfest and waitstaff!”
text: On labor day, not very busy, was allowed to check in early, thank you. Though the staff was few, they were pleasant and helpful. Hotel lobby was clean and orderly, Breakfest staff was warm, sincere, and pleasant. Her name was cecila, warm smile, sincere appreaciation for the business. We related stories of mutual Interests, and the whole morning started off well, even though it was raining. I have been told there is new management for the hotel, Shae (female) was helpful with my reservation. This hotel is in the middle of everywhere, so you will not go hungry, within minutes of nightlife in the area. If you get a chance to visit the hotel, ask for Brandon, one of the agents at the front desk. He will make you feel at home, and provide suggestions on what to do in the area, you cannot go wrong with him. Thank you for an enjoyable stay.

title: “What a treat!”
text: I stay at the Four Points often for business. This last trip I arrived in the middle of the night due to delayed flights and a nasty cab ride into town. The manager on duty took especially great care of me - upgraded my room on arrival and made sure that my stay was pleasant. He even offered to help me by booking a car service for my ride back to the airport, to make my trip home much nicer. On top of being a clean, quite and safe hotel, I really appreciate a hotel that makes me feel welcomed, cared for and tended to during my stay. The Four Points delivers - every time.

title: “Perfect location”
text:
We were totally satisfied with this hotel, perfect location and renovated rooms with nice view!
A very nice hotel to stay at !

title: “Perfect”
text: My company reserved the meeting room and sleeping rooms and everything was great!! T.J. at the front desk was awesome!! Victor at the Happy Hour was very professional and accommodating!! The Director of Sales, Patti Timblin is always remarkable, professional and always takes care of all our needs. The rooms are always clean as well as the hotel. The breakfast and happy hour is good and if you are trying to get the most for your dollar then Homewood Suites North @ Stone Oak is the place to stay. It's also a great and safe location!!! Thank you HWS North @ Stone Oak for being our #1 hotel in San Antonio for business and leisure purposes!!!

title: “Good Location, Not Worth Your Money”
text: We stayed at the Marquis in March, 2004. We were amazed at the great location of the hotel- we walked out and we were on Times Square. Plus we got there and there were no standard rooms left, so they upgraded us for free to a Times Square view. But overall, the hotel is not worth your money. You are paying for the location and that's pretty much it. The rooms are nothing special, they're just average, standard sized rooms. We were on the 42nd floor, but we could still hear the street sounds which was annoying when we were trying to fall asleep. The elevators take forever to get, so plan on allowing 15-20 minutes extra just to catch one. The staff was very unhelpful and not incredibly friendly. We asked the concierge about how to get to Ground Zero and it took her 20 minutes to first of all find the map and then figure out herself how to explain to us how to get there. You'd think that was a pretty common question! But it did have a great fitness room with floor to ceiling windows overlooking Times Square and it had a great restaurant/lounge at the top of the hotel that overlooked all of New York's skyline. I would probably stay there again if I got a good deal, but I definately would not pay $300 a night again.

title: “Alexander Hotel NY, value for money”
text: I read mixed reviews on this hotel but was looking for somewhere on a budget, so decided to give it a go. Rooms are kept very clean on a daily basis, we had our own bathroom which was spotless. Beds a little on the hard side but if you can live with that (we could) then it is fine. Neighbourhood (Upper West Side) feels really safe and there are enough eateries, diners around. Single lift is really slow, but staff were very friendly/helpful. If you are looking for a place to stay where you will only be coming back in the evening to sleep and be out all day, then this hotel is fine and inexpensive - leaving you more bucks for shopping :-)

title: “Good hotel, great value and location”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the Washington Court Hotel with our 5 month old son. It was our first family vacation, and we couldn't have been happier with the hotel. It's certainly not a high end destination - everything feels slightly aged - and the service is good but not exceptional. But the price, $139 a night for a Deluxe King, was the best we could find, and the location was ideal for two new parents to walk around town. The staff was always helpful and friendly, and the room was large and comfortable. We felt safe in the neighborhood (yes, the homeless gather around Union Station, but we never felt threatened), and happily wandered to Union Station a number of evenings for dinner.
We'd highly recommend the hotel to friends and family, and will stay there again for our next trip to DC.

title: “Very nice room”
text: Stayed here using points so price wasn't a factor. Comfortable bed, quiet. We stayed on the first floor so you never know about what you may get on the upper floor as far as noise is concerned. There was a complete kitchen. Including a full size oven. Everything was stocked, plates, glasses, utensils, a toaster. What we didn't see were pots or pans. So I don't know how you would use the oven. And the refrigerator was not flush with the wall so the oven door wouldn't open all the way. May that's why there were no pots and pans. Included was a nice full complimentary breakfast. I would stay ther again.

title: “The Washington Plaza Stay!!”
text: If anyone has anything bad to say about this place...IGNORE IT! I am 55 years old and have stayed in many hotels but this is the first one that left me with a totally satisfied experience. From the service and wonderful room to the location with ease to everything we wanted to see and do (and we saw alot by walking to it) to the great food we had in the restaurant. I don't ususally write reviews but could not wait to get home and write this one.My wife and I had so much more to say to the management about our stay but I will just sum it up here by saying, when we go back to Washington we will definately be staying at The Washington Plaza.

title: “Keep this gem to yourself”
text:
What a gem find! Huge appartment in the centre of Manhatten ? dont tell anyone else about this hotel or you will never get booked in again.
Fantastic large two bedrooms, large sitting room/ dining room. Kitchen with all required equipment for self catering if needed, everything spotless.
Desk staff really helpful, as was the guy looking after the breakfast room.
Complimentry beakfast really a surprise, not just the normal continental, hot bacon/sausage and egg avaliable plus cereal, make your own waffels, toaster, everything you could think of, brilliant !
Although the breakfast room small, there is a outside area, when weather is ok, not good views though. Suggest taking the trays from the appartments and taking back to eat in comfort. 
If you are going to NYC with a family or two couples, you must try this fantastic hotel.
The only downside was city noise, but it's NY what would you expect, wear yourself out walking about sightseeing, then sleep well !

title: “Not entirely convinced!”
text:
I stayed here with a friend during a visit in December 2011. There's no doubt the hotel is well located, it's a short distance from Michigan Avenue, the main Chicago shopping street.
When we arrived, we spent around 15 minutes just chatting to the chap on reception and the bell boy about various things, mainly sport! All the staff are very friendly and helpful, our room safe broke at one point and they couldn't do enough to help fix it straight away.
However the standard of the rooms could be slightly better, they just look a little tired.
The walls & furniture look like they need updating to keep up with the competition and the bathroom was freezing. There was no source of heat to it that we could find and the window just let the icy draught right in even when shut (it wouldn't open).
So you had to be very quick when using the bathroom!
I'd say if Travelodge spent a bit of money updating this hotel and making the bathrooms a bit more 'user friendly' it would be a 4 or 5 star rating for sure.

title: “Small rooms with old carpets that smell!!”
text: We had to change hotels because the carpet in our room smelled old from the humidity. We had to leave after one night due to smell.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: We have stayed here on several occasions. Each time we are pleased with the service we receive. At check-in, the desk clerk informed us that it was a full house due to a marching band/step team competition. She made sure we were placed away from the noise. The hot breakfast is tasty and even with the crowd, the staff made sure nothing ran out. It was the same with hot snacks at night. You can make a meal of it to save money. Adults receive 3 free grown up drinks each night. We always check to see if there is a Drury Inn when traveling. We recommend this hotel to friends and family traveling to the area.

title: “Outstanding hotel”
text: Fantastic service, gorgeous rooms and an unbeatable location smack bang in the middle of San Diego. The only thing that's missing is a pool. Would thoroughly recommend it, though.

title: “Almost Perfect”
text: The location is perfect, the rooms are wonderful and the bathrooms are down right exceptional. The bed is like a big pillow and the view was outstanding. Room service was prompt. The overall feel is very good and everything is new. In the category of "almost" the elevator was on the fritz, the in room controls are difficult ( for the life of me I could not turn on the bedside lamp), they charged me for the previous occupants mini bar bill ( also removed) and they messed up the breakfast room service order. I will chalk this up to new hotel and will return so I hope they clear this issues up. Overall I would recommend especially for the area.

title: “No Mere Tweener”
text:
Is the hotel in the Back Bay or the Fenway? Doesn't matter. Both are accessible, and this boutique hotel is no mere tweener. 
The staff is friendly, extremely professional and helpful. The rooms are well appointed, and everything works. Complimentary newspapers at your door (upon request) are delivered while you sleep.
Our stay spanned a weekend, and the jump in rates reflects that weekends are more in demand. The weekday business traveler will nonetheless find this a very accommodating establishment, and a bargain in the area. For family and couples, it is a warm and welcoming perch for sampling the delights of Boston.
We did order from room service at what I consider reasonable prices, and the food comes from the kitchen of Eastern Standard, a very nice and capacious restaurant on the premises. The Island Creek Oyster Bar (a top rated Trip Advisor restaurant) is located just off the lobby.
Couldn't have chosen better.

title: “Has It All..Views, Value, Comfort & Service!”
text: First time in San Diego, stayed 4 nights before a cruise. Called several hotels, and after hearing that this one was just renovated (brand-new mattresses!) decided to give it a try. We couldn't have been happier with our decision. Our king room had a great view of the harbor, and was spotless, with new carpets & window treatments (the furniture seemed a little dated, and probably should be updated to match the rest of the hotel). The bed was super comfortable, and the room amenities (microwave, coffee, fridge, ironing board & iron) made our stay very comfortable. The pool and hot tub where a great place to relax after a day of sightseeing, and they have an exercise room also, if you are so inclined (not while on vacation, please). The location was excellent. We walked 2 blocks to a bus stop, for a direct bus to Old Town, then took off from there on our adventures. Also, can walk along the water to a great park. The front desk was very helpful with all our questions, and the internet access came in handy. Overall, I think this is a great hotel for the price, with friendly, efficient staff & a can't-beat location. Can't wait to come back to San Diego.

title: “I Liked It”
text: I named my price on priceline and ended up at the Tremont. After reading all the reviews here I was really nervous about staying there, but I found it very pleasant. The staff was very friendly for the most part. There was a desk lady when we checked in who was helpful, but not overly friendly. Everyone else was very nice. It was fine for us as we were vacationing and not spending a lot of time in the hotel. We basically were there to sleep and shower and on one day nap. If we had to spend a lot of time there I wouldn't have cared for it as much since there was no cable in our room and we only got a few fuzzy channels. I did hear the desk lady tell other guests though that if the sattelite in their room isn't working they can call the front desk and watch movies and they'll take it off the bill. I was travelling with two small children and they were very nice to the kids as well. I'm going to not recommend it for people travelling with small children only because there is no pool and basically no tv, even though it was fine for us.

title: “Blah stay near airport”
text:
We were not expecting anything special given that our purpose was to stay near the airport after an evening arrival at the airport. Arrival...the lobby was so hot and stuffy we could not wait to get checked in. The clerk was very friendly and helpful. Room was basic with laminate furniture and loud wall mounted AC unit. There was no airport noise but we could hear doors opening and closing throughout the night as well as showers and toilets in other rooms. Breakfast was below par even for the free breakfasts offered by the chain hotels...the coffee was gross. We tried to fill our water bottle in the pool but the water fountain did not work at all.
As I said we did not expect a lot since it was a hotel near the airport and we used points fr a free stay but thus was below average.
If this was a Best Western Plus, I cannot imagine a basic Best Western.

title: “Excellent Hotel and location for Special Occasions”
text:
We stayed at the Austin Airport Marriott South while we attended our son's wedding which was also held at the hotel. The accomodations and event support was all outstanding! The room was super clean and completely re-stocked (coffee, shampoo, etc.) every day. The bed was very comfortable with plenty of pillows. The entire staff, from desk staff to the cleaning crew, were always polite and friendly. Best of all, the special room rate arranged for event attendees made it one of the best hotel bargains I've ever heard of. Oh, and the food on the breakfast buffet (not free) was also very, very good with equally polite staff. About the only downside is that the wireless Interent (also not free) did not work properly.
Our son's wedding and reception (hosted by the bride's parents) was excellent to include the attention given by the hotel staff. They hosts seemed very pleased with the support given by the staff.
I would wholeheartedly recommend this hotel for accomodations and special events.

title: “Very pleased”
text: We booked this last minute on a third party website so got it at a rock-bottom price. We didn't know what the hotel was until we had paid, but we couldn't afford it if it were full price. We were very happy with our choice! The service was outstanding. They went out of their way to accomodate us, even though we paid a pittance of the full rate. Our room wasn't ready so they gave us a suite with a view of the water! They made up two extra beds for the kids, looked after our stuff when we checked out, marking our daughter's violin as fragile, and all the staff were helpful and polite. The room was nicely decorated, the lobby and bar were humming, and it is in a fairly central location. The concierge was very informative and gave us maps and all kinds of information about the subway and the Freedom Trail, as well as restaurant tips, etc... A great Boston choice, I highly recommend it.

title: “Friendly, informal relaxing hotel with harbor view”
text:
Had an excellent experience at the hotel. Had two unfortunate clumsy accidents in the bedroom and rang Reception and they came up straight away (literally within minutes). The hotel reception staff were very friendly and helpful, which really counts. The hotel is a little bit outside the main city and you need to walk across the bridge to get there. However I wouldn't say the walk was much of a problem. We got the hop-on-hop-off bus that goes from Stop 3 at USS Naval Yard, if you want to save your legs for the odd day.
I liked that the hotel had a spa tub and swimming pool, so you can relax after a hard days sightseeing around the city.

title: “Comfortable, but not very well run”
text:
First Westin I've used in the US. We had a few Starwood points to use but not enough for our whole stay, so had to make 2 bookings for consecutive periods; we emailed the hotel to tell them we were combining them to make a continuous stay. All a waste of effort: they had not linked the reservations, and we had to change keys at the change-over point after 3 days, and we also got an unwanted bill under the door on that day. Receptionists were friendly whereas I would have preferred competent.
Room was fairly good, but maintenance poor: basin waste annoyingly slow to empty, one room light not working throughout our stay. Phone calls ridiculously expensive, even $2 for each call to a 1-800 number. Wifi worked, but not free. TV remote had terrible user interface, designed to make free TV channels extremely hard to find. Obviously designed for those on an expense account, not ideal for tourists.
On the other hand, good location, 2 blocks from elevated railway and underground trains. Bin36 restaurant across the street is good, we didn't try meals in the Westin except for breakfasts, which were fairly good and reasonable value at $13 for continental buffet.

title: “The Cosmopolitan NY was much more than expected and great value.”
text:
My wife and I stayed late November 2005 for 4days.
We found the hotel as a whole very clean. This includes the rooms which are quite small but more than adequate as a base. 
The rooms are very warm but have air con if required. 
The bathrooms are very small but have an excellent shower (and how big does a bathroom need to be for crying out loud!).
The bed was very comfortable (though your feet may hang out if over 6foot tall).
Getting around is easy from here with a subway station on the corner.
We had a late evening flight so were pleased to discover the Cosmopolitan will hold on to luggage free of charge after checking out at 11am.
We found the staff very helpful.

title: “Elegant, Great location and not bank-account busting”
text: this is a beautiful hotel with classy rooms. the views over Bryant Park are just fab. we didnt eat in the hotel as there are just too many other great places, but the cellar bar has great atmosphere for drinks. the place has a wonderful 'unique' feel to it, that makes it stand out from the big chains. Although its certainly not the cheapest, it was a lot less expensive over the holiday season than a number of others we looked at. we loved it.

title: “Nice stay, but not overly impressed”
text: I stayed at the JW. Marriott L.A. Live for a conference in late May. The hotel is very nice looking and the rooms were spacious, however, I've seen nicer hotels that are less expensive (and I had a group conference rate). The breakfast buffet was still affordable at 24$, but the choices were limited. There are lots of nice restaurants in the L.A. Live complex which were very good.

title: “Another Great Stay!”
text:
There is a reason this is one of the top rated hotels in downtown Denver. It is that good. Free made to order breakfast, evening manager's reception and perfectly cleaned rooms (I mean suites) are just the beginning. How about free internet access when affiliated with specific groups or the valet parking that knows you by name...Did I mention location? Directly across from the convention center and two blocks away from restaurants and other attractions makes this one of my favorite yearly destinations...thanks to work of course.
Staff makes you feel like you are the only guest. They all seem to truly want to be there!
Indoor pool with associated services and a gym round out this property to make it my favorite so far for business or pleasure.

title: “Nice hotel, lousy area.”
text:
I stayed here on a recent business trip to Silicon Valley. They hotel itself is nice (recently renovated) and it is close to the airport. The staff was very friendly at all times. Upon my arrival, the elevator was out of service so I had to schlep my bags to the 3rd floor via the stairs (which I might add are not a direct trip).
 The area around the hotel leaves a lot to be desired. There are bail bonds stores on just about every corner for a few blocks around the hotel. The commuter train runs directly in front of the hotel. This is good if you take the train, but bad if you drive, as the road is divided and you need to go down a block or two to turn around if you are coming in from the north.
 The location is between downtown and the start of the high tech business area, but I wouldn't advise walking to town from the hotel. I wouldn't advise walking ANYWHERE around the hotel for that matter.
 The room itself was nicer than I had expected for the price ($90). I had free high speed internet in the room and a small wetbar and fridge. The room was relatively quiet except for the banging doors in adjacent rooms when the guests left for the day/night.
 There are no restaurants within walking distance, just a small convenience store about 1 block south. The nearest food is either downtown or north by the mall area (about 5 miles). The hotel is pretty much in no mans land.
 If you are planning to stay in this area, I would advise checking out the hotels in the McCarthy blvd, 880, 237 area near the mall. There are many shops and restaurants withing a stones throw from this area.

title: “Nothing great”
text:
I thought that this place was ok but nothing great. It has lots of character. Room was fairly large but in desperate need of updating;especially the bathroom. Bed was very comfortable. My biggest complaint was the noise factor from both inside and out. I was in an exterior room on the second floor so there was lots of traffic noise. I also wasn't that happy about hearing the room above me being vacuumed at 8 am. The staff was great - very friendly and helpful.
Overall - I would try somewhere else next time.

title: “One of the BEST hotels we stayed at...”
text: We arrived in LA with no hotel reservation. When we went to visit a friend in Hollywood, he suggested several hotels in the area. We booked this hotel for 2 nights at hotels.com. It recently opened in 2011, and the carpet smelled very fresh. The room was dimly lit (which added to the great ambiance), and it smelled like fresh linen. The King bed was one of the most comfortable beds in which we ever slept. Overall, the room was great, the property was beautiful, and the staff were very friendly. We will definitely book this hotel again when we return to LA. A+

title: “Not what it used to be...”
text:
This was my second time staying at the Gansevoort Park hotel and perhaps they set the bar very high the first time around, but this stay was mediocre at best. It started when I checked in and they didn’t have me listed as having a King bed (which was on my reservation) and the only room they had available was on a smoking floor.
The room itself has definitely been worn-down. It may have been that I was in a smoking room, but it definitely wasn’t as clean and pristine as my first stay. I also found that the air conditioning in my room was broken and after multiple calls and 1.5 hours, they finally sent up a technician. After about 30 minutes of work, he fixed the blockage in the pipes. Not an ideal situation when you are traveling for business.
They were also out of “G-Cards” when I checked in which are what you use to pay for things at the hotel. I was up at the rooftop bar with colleagues and wanted to pay for our drinks on our room but they wouldn’t allow me too since I didn’t have the card. I went downstairs and explained the situation and, to their credit, they gave me two cards for a free drink, but still no G-Card and they said that the bar was informed. Either way, the miscommunications were an annoyance having to go up-and-down trying to just pay for drinks.
I will say that the staff is very friendly and helpful. Unfortunately, I’m not sure it’s enough to get me back to the hotel.

title: “Good Business Hotel”
text: All hotel facilities at your service. From a good reception to shop and restaurants in the same building. The Hotel in a perfect part of Boston close to the Boston Common & Public Garden and the old part of town around Boylston Street.

title: “POD HOTEL NY”
text:
Hi, 
I travel allot as part of my business, and I got stuck without a hotel in new york, and booked online (easyclicktravel). The hotel was very very simple, but the location was AMAZING, and the rooms were really comfy. Staff also good, they helped me get around. 
I would say I recommend.

title: “An outstanding way to visit Chicago”
text: Excellent accomodations, outstanding restaurant, helpful concierge, and perfectly located for all travel desires. A touch of Europe in the USA. We will always return to the Sofitel Chicago Water Tower.

title: “Foul front desk personnel !”
text: This hotel has clean modern rooms and is in a great location. However I will never stay there again... The front desk people are incredibly rude ! Was snapped at on 3 different occasions... Don't think they understand that the guests are the reason they have a job... Too bad , because other than the horrible front desk service , this is actually quite a nice place to stay.

title: “Unbelievable stay”
text:
We stayed in a one bedroom suite over looking the Hudson and manhattan. The view amazing. . The room was huge for ny standards. The bathroom was unbelievable.
Staff were professional and helpful. They made myself and children feel very welcome.
I can't recommend the hotel enough. Read all the reviews as they are accurate.
The only critiscm which I know other reviewers share, is charging for internet is very poor. We stayed ten nights in a suite and charged for Internet use. Yes I know you could use the lobby. We are touring thru the USA and the trump is the only property that didn't offer complimentary wifi.
The trump is a must for anyone planning at trip to NYC

title: “Great Hotel - but extras can add up”
text:
Great hotel, modern, stylish, clean and very spacious. We have just returned from a 6 night stay and thoroughly enjoyed it. Ideally located, within easy walking distance of the Gaslamp Quarter with its many lively bars and restaurants, as well as many shops.
We had 3 nights in a room facing the Coronada Bridge and 3 nights facing the Bay/City - the latter was best for views, but both rooms were excellent in terms of comfort and space.
The hotel is also in easy driving distance of all of San Diego's attractions i.e. Beaches, Zoo, Balboa Park, Coronada Island etc.
Just one word of warning - look out for the additional charges which you may encounter i.e Car Parking $21/day, Internet Access $19/day (its free downstairs in the Fox Grill), Gym $15/day, Breakfast $24/day

title: “Loved the location and the experience”
text: Great location, just a few blocks to Times Square, easy access to subways, and walking distance to several theaters. Rooms were very clean, and extremely comfortable bed. This helped to get a good nights sleep, even with the sirens going all hours of the night. The front desk staff were friendly and helpful. Rooms tend to be on small side, so recommend staying in a queen suite. Had plenty of room...Room lacked a full length mirror which would have been nice; bathroom clean but small, especially not much shelf space for toiletries. Thoroughly enjoyed oour stay.

title: “Fantastic Stay in SF”
text:
The Kennsington Hotel in SF is a great place to stay. Here is my list of pro's and con's, but as you can see, there is not much to complain about
Pros
Great location, close to BART station (the train that will get you to the city from airport, which I highly recommend as it costs a fraction of the price of a taxi, very clean as well, and takes about 30 minutes of travel time, get off on Powell Street), the best shopping in the city, tons of dining options, small boutique hotel (which means you get personalized service as opposed to the big hotel chains where nobody recognizes you from day to day), service/cleaning of the rooms was fantastic, Chinatown is very close, right by Union Square (which often has music and/or events going on) and if you like to walk you are in a good location to walk to most of the major attractions within 20-30 minute walk. The walking can be complicated if you are not in decent shape due to the steep hills, but I enjoyed walking almost everywhere.
Cons
Small room, but pretty much what you can expect in a big city like SF. 
Overall, I would stay here again with no questions asked. The value for what you get is unbeatable in this city and trust me I did my research prior to the trip. I have been to SF on many occasions and all of the other hotels I stayed in were a higher nightly rate, but would choose this one over the others given all of the factors involved.

title: “nice hotel”
text: Nice hotel for being around for awhile,comfortable beds,a little pricey.

title: “Solid Bang for the Buck”
text: The staff - check-in, maintenance, breakfast room and bell hop - were all friendly and engaging. Although the room is on the small side, it was pretty standard for NYC. The hotel is probably not more than 2 years old and was in fine shape. Although we had a slight problem closing our window, maitenance was on it within minutes of being notified. The location was within a few blocks of several subway lines and the complimentary breakfast was even more of a treat considering what it would have cost us in that city to get equal fare in a restaurant. The only negative to be had was the sounds of hallway activity were quite noticable. Regardless, I would definitely recommend staying here.

title: “Noticeable improvement, and great pillows!”
text:
I've stayed at the Park Plaza twice in the past two weeks on business, and since I wrote a fairly critical review a couple of years ago I wanted to give the place some props for the improvements they've made in the meantime. 
I gather from other recent reviews that there's quite a lot of variation in the rooms, with some newly renovated and some less so. I was given a complimentary upgrade to a Tower room last week, which was a little cramped but had a great view and came with a good and varied free breakfast that I appreciated before I raced off to a morning meeting. Last night I had an even nicer non-Tower room, spacious and spotless and very, very quiet. 
And I am thrilled to report that for the past year every room I've stayed in at this hotel has included a toiletries set with conditioner (thank heavens!)--which for a while was an amenity this place skipped. I'm relieved that they've come to their senses.
My colleague and I compared notes this morning on our way out and agreed that the Park Plaza has excellent pillows. All in all, a very comfortable night's sleep.And of course it's still a great location (duh--it's not as if they've moved!).
I still feel just a little irritated that wireless isn't included in the not-cheap rate, but on the whole, they're getting better. Since this is the hotel across the street from my company office, I am grateful that they're on the upswing instead of the other way around.

title: “Great value!”
text:
This is a very pleasant hotel which is unbeatable for the money. The rooms were very clean and nicely furnished. The indoor pool is nice and was not busy. The staff are nice enough.
The only downsides were the location - as a general tourist we found it a long walk to some of SF attractions, and also, there are hardly any nice restaurants or bars nearby and the hotel bar was nice enough but lacked that certain 'atmosphere'.

title: “Nice”
text: Nice new hotel. A little disorganized two weeks after the opening but staff seemed intent on serving guests. Good points: nice new rooms with good views, great pool, close to gaslamp & downtown. No so good points: pricey, bathrooms are semi-private (louvers on doors & internal "windows"), hotel located right next to the baseball stadium so area gets overrun on game nights -- but I'd probably stay again.

title: “Great place to stay!”
text: Staff cannot do enough to help you. Serivice is top notch from top management to housekeeping. This is our hotel of choice if we are to do LA again. Walking distance to the Cathedral. Parking is steep but you can find a lot across the hotel for much less.

title: “Never Ever Again”
text:
What can I say !!!!
As we were travelling from Australia [17 hour flight ] we e mailed the hotel and explained that as we would be travelling for many hours could we please have a quite room away from the noise of the street 
Well after arriving and getting a cab to the hotel we were told that check in was 4 pm NO EARLIER by a VERY rude lady so we had to walk the streets for 3 hours and then we did eventually get into our room it was right on the street and the noise was terrible ALL night rubbish trucks and delivery trucks all night the air conditioner made more noise than the Plane we flew to the States in.
To say the rooms were poor would be VERY kind they were filthy and I feel the Y would be a better standard 
I do understand it is a budget hotel bit for your own sake spend an extra $20 a night and stay elsewhere DONT EVER STAY HERE I won't ever again 
As for San Francisco FANTASTIC loverly place to visit and would go back again and again dont miss Alcatraz [ book before you go as you would get there otherwise] and pier 39 is great

title: “Amazing service! Amazing experience! Thank you!”
text: I can't believe that people have bad things to say about the W Times Square staff and hotel. My wife and I had one of the best stays ever at a hotel...just as good as our last stay at the Park Hyatt Vendôme in Paris. The staff went above and beyond to make sure we had an amazing stay and really helped to make our four days in NYC incredible. Room service was wonderful. The room was in great shape. Elevator always worked. Housekeeping was friendly. Staff was professional and friendly. I felt like they genuinely cared about us and didn't have any attitude. Big, big, big thank you to Patrick and Paola!

title: “Beautiful hotel and grounds in a great location”
text: We loved the hotel property, the views from the tower room and the pool. It was a great vacation spot to be with my family. We also loved taking the water taxi to Sea World. The kids loved the water slides.

title: “The price is alright”
text: I stayed at the Travelodge for 3 nights during spring break with my boyfriend, and his siblings. We were all on a budget but we still wanted to stay close to downtown. The hotel itself was fine, it was pretty clean, and it was close to the BART (Bay area rapid transit) which we used often. The walk to Union Square was lenghty but manageable however it is through a rougher neighborhood. We instead often opted for the bus or subway which ran almost every other minute. It was also close to the Haight area which was great for dining. The biggest problems we had with the hotel were:the water heater sounded like a jackhammer everytime the water was used, the continental breakfast was orange juice, coffee, and pre-packaged sara lee style sticky buns, lastly, some of us ended up having bug bites on our arms and such, but we have no way of telling what it was from. For a budget hotel, this is what we expected, but it does not exeed any expectations.

title: “can't beat this hotel”
text: Center city for a reasonable price. Super and welcoming service, excellent rooms nicely designed, comfortable beds, bath area well designed. Loft-like design provides space and electronic amenities, including TV's, are up-to-date. This hotel is at least $100 less than comparable hotels in uptown Charlotte and it is close to all major attractions in the uptown. It is favored by a younger crowd and overlooks a busy nightlife. If you want a quieter experience they will provide rooms on the uptown side. Belk theatre, Bechler Museum, etc. are all within four blocks. Parking is reasonable in the garage underneath the hotel.

title: “Great staff”
text: A last minute reservation didn't get me the best room but I did get a room which was great considering there were three adults and 4 grandkids in the group. The room was a bit dated compared to the new Embassy Suites in Louisville we stayed in over the summer but it was servicable and clean. One 4 year old was awake at 5:30 a.m. so we headed to the lobby to walk around. The staff prepping for breakfast were pleasant and let us wander around as they worked. Another big plus is the deli/ restaraunt that is just across the parking lot. GREAT "food to go" for kids and adults.

title: “Very relaxing weekend”
text: Ok, our room had some paint peeling off the wall, the carpet is a bit warn, and some tile is buckling. SO WHAT! The room and hotel are clean, the staff was great, the grounds are very nice, and the pool area was terrific. Our bed was comfortable and even with a full house on the second night our room was quiet. Room service delivered our burgers in less than 15 minutes. They were hot and cooked just right. All that being said the real reason to stay is the location. A large balcony on the water made for a very relaxing weekend. We will definitely return to this hotel.

title: “Nice location, creepy area, terrible staff”
text: I booked 3 rooms at this hotel for 2 nights in August. The rooms were ok, with a kitsch accent from the seventies, but clean. Could hear what was happening in every room around us, so it's a bit noisy! Most of the time you'll get the valet parking included in the price of the room. The area is kinda creepy and dirty, but it's close to everything. You'll have to move your car at noon the day you check out, otherwise you'll have to pay $10.00 for the rest of the day. That's the fun part, we paid $10.00... + tax for the parking! First time ever pay extra taxes for a parking (not mentioned on the invoice), not a big deal, but c'm on...! The lady at the desk was absolutely terrible, and I must say ridiculous. She had some short term memory loss issue and is horribly arrogant. She alone ruined everything.

title: “Great location, but expensive for what it is.”
text: Booked based on other reviews. The location is hard to beat. Admitted, I have not stayed in nyc for a few years now, but it seemed very expensive for a very basic hotel. Clean and quiet, yes. Excellent location. Would shop around a little more next time for a better rate somewhere nearby.

title: “Can't please everyone.”
text: If I were an animal lover, I would probably appreciate the fact that this is a pet friendly hotel but I'm not. I dont mind if people bring their pets; I just dont want to listen to barking most of the night. I took my family the Saturday after Thanksgiving; which BTW is an extremely busy weekend. I was checked in fast and was given 2 upgrades with Riverwalk balcony rooms. I thought that was very nice and I really appreciated it. The problem was the doberman next door. Fortunately, I had been up late for the past 4 nights and even though the dog was barking because his owner wasnt in the room and I could hear when "Daddy" came home; I pretty much was passed out that night. If that hadnt been the case, I would have called down and changed rooms. Other than that I thought the room was nice and the location was good as well. The property is very well maintained and is really beautiful. I would probably not stay there again unless I was guaranteed a room that wasnt next to any pets.

title: “A little piece of paradise.”
text:
This is a great place to bring a family or a couple's getaway. The rooms are nice and clean. It is a bungalow style type of room with modern furnishings. The staff are super nice and accommodating. My top favorite things here are the following:
1. The spa is just fantastic. I went on a Thursday and I had the whole place to myself. I selected the loma spa treatment and I have to say it was 2 hours of heaven. Well worth the price.
2. The facilities. There are several pools located throughout the resort as well as the beach area where you can lay on the beach or relax at night in front of the fire pits. They also have a wonderful pond area with birds and fish. you can sit with your book or iPad and just relax for hours! They also include free wi-fi, another added bonus.
3. The location. The resort is only minutes from Sea World and other destinations. A really convenient place yet you still feel separated from the city.

title: “A great location for the Inner Harbor experience”
text:
We stayed here for Labor Day weekend/Baltimore Grand Prix. We had a room overlooking Pratt Street and hence Turn 1, so that in of itself was worth five stars. I'm not much of a hotel aficionado, but I do know what I like. I like decent televisions with digital reception...check. I like comfortable beds....check. I like big pillows....check. There is some noise to deal with, but that's at nearly any hotel. If you could get a 'drunk idiot free' floor at check in it would be great, but you're not going to get that here or anywhere else for that matter. Do what I do and pack a white noise machine with earplugs with Benadryl for backup and you should be good to go. We were up on the 9th floor so the street noise was not that much of an issue...I can see how lower down it could be a problem. 
The bathroom was very nice, clean, more than enough towels and toiletries. Small fridge in the room was perfect for leftovers from dinner and the occasional six pack. Staff was friendly and attentive. They seem to have a nice bar downstairs with seating out on the sidewalk, Starbucks in house. The guy managing the elevators was a trifle annoying (I know when to get on and off, thanks very much...don't need some guy hustling me along) but all in all the staff was friendly and more than willing to answer questions. Internet is free for platinum members, as is the 12th floor breakfast room (which is kick tail, by the way)/lounge. In room movie rentals were outrageously expensive, but we never were in the room long enough to watch a movie anyway. Besides, what's why God made iPads and portable DVD players :). 
Parking was fairly hefty at 28 bucks a night, but I don't know how this compares to other hotels in the area. The pool has a shallow and deep end, indoors, nothing too extravagant, towels available at poolside. Nice little hot tub that you can turn on for 15-20 minutes. 
We'll stay there again for our foray to see the Grand Prix next year.

title: “Okay for Budget”
text: I stayed here while touring through California. The rooms were dated, the skirtings looked like the dust had been painted over. Bedding & towels were relatively clean and the bed was comfortable. Bathroom could have been cleaner. Stayed at the back of the hotel. The police or ambulance cars are noisy and they could be heard frequently through out the night. The hotel borders the Tenderloin district which isn't a safe place to walk at night. The staff were friendly and helpfull. The free Wi-Fi was good. The restaurant was excellent and was very busy on the night we dined. Some of the rooms were being upgraded, new carpets were being laid. I think mine had already been done!

title: “Great hotel and prime location”
text: We booked thru my travel agent and were wary based on mixed reviews. The front desk staff was warm and welcoming, offered us late check out and the doormen very helpful. The rooms were clean, comfortable beds, bathroom small but hey, it is Manhattan. Very nice location with subway and plentiful cabs. The only negative was that the walls are pretty thin- toddler next door could be heard- and the shampoo terrible.

title: “Oops, room given away, hotel made it right.”
text: Booked hotel room two months ahead of time for the ARCSI Convention. Arrived first night to find that they overbooked (computer glitch) and gave my room away. Bummer. Manager did everything she could to resolve issue. Despite having to take taxi 45 mins away (all nearby hotels booked out), hotel went above and beyond to make things right for me and the remaining week stay back at the hotel the next day was fantastic. Great rooms, however they could use more lighting. Some areas are very dark, especially closets. Also, would like the refrigerator to not be so full of their stuff to sell. Would have liked to put my own drink/food in there. Breakfast buffet was really good and fast. They even let me take to-go box so I could eat it on the bus to the convention center. Saved me time and money not having to wait in lines at convention center. Valet parking was $50/night, not so great. Meeting rooms were really nice. Elevators were confusing though. Some didn't go to certain floors and I was constantly checking to see if I was on right elevator. Overall, great stay.

title: “Would go back for sure”
text: Exceeded expectations for a big city hotel in every way.

title: “Its the little extras that count”
text:
The Casablanca Hotel, Times Square, New York.
Trip Advisor member - Staffordshire, U.K.
04-June-2007
We have just returned from the Casablanca and really must thank all of the staff for ensuring that we had a good holiday. Everyone of them went out of their way to help us, and provided a professional and courteous service. The hotel is situated next to Times Square which is the busiest part of New York. After a day spent trekking around the city it was a pleasure to return in the evening to the complimentary cheese and wine buffet in Ricks cafe (between 5.30 and 8.00). Ricks cafe also provides free computer / internet use and free coffee from the vending machine 24/7. The buffet breakfast is adequate to start the day with a choice of cereals, croissants and fresh fruit etc. We booked a Queen room but were upgraded to a King room on the 5th floor. The room was a reasonable size for New York with a nice bathroom, however, ask for a rear room if you are a light sleeper. The air conditioning units are fitted into the windows and if being used you can hear the outside hubble (it seemed like an emergency vehicle passed by every time we dropped off to sleep. We eventually turned the unit off and shut the window which made it a lot quieter, sleep or be cool, its your choice.
Overall an excellent hotel in the centre of Manhattan. One word of warning! We could not get a taxi to JFK airport on Friday afternoon. Taxis stopped but refused to do the trip. After an hour we ended up takeing the bus from the Port Authority Depot 2 blocks away. Due to congestion (probably why the taxis wont go) the journey took nearly 2 hours and we only just made the flight.

title: “Rude and Disorganized”
text:
I booked the room through Hotwire. We got a great deal at $129.00 a night! That's where the deal ended....
The people working at the front desk looked as if they were upset we had disturbed them when all three rooms in my party showed up at the same time. Only one room was ready so we all had to squeeze into one room for the time being - boy did we have to squeeze! The room barely left a path around the oversized bed. There were no drawers so we were forced to leave our suitcases on the ground open, leaving even less space. 
When my group returned from our evening, the rest of the party were given there rooms....let's just say that one of the rooms was already occupied when they arrived. How does something like that happen! 
We woke up in the morning to go down for the free breakfast we were given because of the "mix-up" but it wasn't much of a deal after waitng in line for half an hour watching the girl behind the counter funmble around as if she had never heard of coffee. 
When we finally left Hotel Indigo no one said goodbye, wished us a safe journey home or even asked how we enjoyed our stay. 
Overall if you are looking for a clean hotel, that it is. If you are looking for a place to compliment such a beautiful and freindly city, you are better off booking another hotel. 
I won't use hotwire again to book in case I end up at Hotel Indigo again.

title: “Clean room, good value”
text: Other reviewers raved about this place especially for the value so I booked 4 nights here. It is a good value I must admit, but I also wasn't in my hotel room a whole lot. My room looked like it was just recently renovated. It was nice and clean. Like the previous reviewer, it was very damp. The owners told me they had some water damage and they actually had to re-carpet my room while I was there. It proved to be a minor inconvenience. Also, the place is fairly noisy. There is free parking, but the all the cars park below the rooms. So, you can hear families, kids, doors slamming, and even cars starting in your room. The walls proved to be pretty thin too. The free wireless internet worked well and the room has all major amenities. Management was nice and pleasant. The location is good. Close to California 1 bus-line and the Cable Car. Close to Polk St. shops and restaraunts. If you're looking for basically a clean room and a bed to crash while travelling in SF this a decent choice. I'd probably stay here again.

title: “Great stay, perfect for a family”
text: We chose this hotel after a great deal fo research due to having a two bedroom suite. We had never stayed in Soho before but we have a ten month old so we wanted to stay in a little bit more of a neighborhood environment. It was a great find. The rooms were perfect for our needs. We were able to put a crib in one room and hang out in the other after baby bedtime. The location was great. We used a stroller to go everywhere because we have a baby so we did all of our commuting by subway which was extremely simple. The E train is almost right out the front door of the hotel. We used it to go to Flushing Meadows for the US Open, Yankee Stadium, the Financial District and everywhere in between. The staff was excellent. Cullen was a great concierge, Rashawd was an excellent bellman and the rest of the staff was very courteous. They arranged our airport transportation seamlessly. We used the swimming pool in the afternoon on the 7th floor and it was very refreshing. We had a corner room on the 22nd floor that faced NW as one the bedrooms and the view was the best I have ever seen in NYC. We could see the Empire State building, the skyline and Central Park all the way up 6th avenue. The view out the other window was across the Hudson and was gorgeous also. The room has computer controlled curtains, lights and a/c which were great. The television channels had great choices also. The bathrooms were roomy with seperate shower and tub. I cannot imagine that another hotel in NYC is as spacious as the Trump Soho. I didn't use the workout facility but I visited the area and it was a nice room with the cardiovascular equipment facing out for great views. We were not so high that we could not hear street noise but it was not too bad. Within 4 blocks each direction there were restaurants and shopping. A Whole Foods Market was also within walking distance. With a baby, we were close enough to walk to the World Trade Center and Union Square. We made several trios down Spring street to Viva la Crepe which had fantastic crepes and we enjoyed nearby restaurants such as Hundred Acres, Amelias, and Wolfgang puck steakhouse. The hotel rooms and location far exceeded everything we were looking for in our stay. The two bedrooms adjoined through keyed entry way with one room having the living area attached directly. The rooms did have a microwave but only had a mini bar refrigerator that was not exactly designed for storing things and did not have a freezer component for freezing our dry ice packs.

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text: I made the reservation on hotwire.com. As people know,unless people confirmed the reservation, otherwise there will be no way of knowing which hotel I will be staying at. After confirmed, it shows me Chicago South Loop Hotel. I went on their website right away, and it looks kind of nice. Then i started to read people's reviews. There were some bad reviews which made me kind of worried. When i arrived at the hotel, I had to wait. They wont let people check-in until 3 o'clock on the dot. After checking in, my husband and I went to our room, it was on the 2nd floor. The room was very nice and clean. The windows faces the parking lot. I saw some people mentioned the noise from the bar. We had the same problem too, but it was quiet after11pm. The next day I mentioned to the staff about the noise. The staff was very helpful, and said we could switch for me if i want to. Since it wasnt that bad, i stayed in the same room. The location of the hotel is great. The bus stop is less than a minute away from the hotel.
