Taking bus 29, it will take you to navy pier and some other places in downtown. Free parking is another good thing. Overall, it was a great experience. I will definitely stay there again in the future.

title: “Good price, but...”
text:
The room was in decent shape. Not a high end hotel, but the price point was what attracted us. The location is next to a busy interstate, but the room was quiet. We had a few small inconveniences with the room, but the room was overall worth the price we paid. 
The big negative we had was to have a pair of sunglasses go missing from our room while we were out. I was shocked at this and still have a hard time believing it wasn't some kind of accident. La Quinta Inns usually have great service. With this being said the price was very good for the room. There is a safe in the room so use it!

title: “Had a Wonderful Stay !!!”
text: This place is not like your regular Super 8. They have a 27inch flat screen TV (few of the rooms have even a 72 inch) ,DVD player, VCR , all in their standard room. They have a complimentary business center and fitness center all free !!!! For about 70-80 bucks/day this place is really awesome. They have a complimentary breakfast and evening snacks served daily. They even have DVD rentals in the lobby. All together I think this is a great place to stay in Austin when on a budget. Would definitely stay here again.

title: “Travelodge market street, San Francisco”
text:
The only good thing about this hotel is its well lit parking in the middle of the hotel compound, because it's quite rare in San Francisco downtown, although that costs 11$ per night. 
The hotel is located at a junction of busy streets (Valencia and Market) Very noisy and the rooms are not soundproof. You hear traffic and neighbors all night.
The adress is given mainly on Market Street. Be careful, it is on the other end of this famous street you find more homeless people, junkies and cheap cafes than elegant shops and hotels on the other end.
My room was dark and old with very old furniture. I had to turn the mattress upside down and inspect if there were roaches somewhere. Thank god there was not.
Well, it's 100$ a night, so what more to expect, especially in San Francisco!

title: “No complaints!”
text: This charming hotel is conveniently located between Union Square and the financial district. Nice, clean rooms; good customer service; noon checkout; great location; comfy bed; old San Francisco charm; great terrace.

title: “Overall a great stay”
text:
Our stay started badly as the first room we were sent to hadn't been cleaned or made up!
After this false start I was a little concerned but things improved. We did arrive early and so it was great to be able to check in before 11am. 
The room was comfortable. We opened and closed the pointless dishwasher... really who uses a dishwasher to wash wine glasses in a hotel? 
The best part of this hotel was the lounge. Great coffee machine! Pastries in the morning were fresh and plentiful and we really enjoyed the coffee but they did run out of 'to go' cups. It didn't really bother us as we were in no rush and spent an extra half hour drinking coffee before venturing out into the city.
The restaurant within the hotel (Lexington Brass) was also very good. Excellent service and we were given a complimentary appetizer.

title: “Cedarbrook Lodge is great!!!!!”
text: We stayed at Cedarbrook Lodge two nights when flying in and out of SEA/TAC. I wanted to stay our entire trip. The landscape was lush and beautiful. The decor was contemporary and everything was very clean. The free continental breakfast included salmon and capers (excellent). My kids loved the free ice cream and snacks in the common lounge. Shuttle to/from the airport was very convenient. The atmosphere was calm and relaxing. I'd go back and recommend this place in a heartbeat. Kudos to Cedarbrook Lodge. I never write reviews but this place is worthy of an excellent review.

title: “A Classic New York Experience”
text: As a Manhattanite, one rarely gets to spend any time at New York City hotels. Was at the New York Palace Hotel during the Republican convention for three nights for work-related reasons. Security was tight given the circumstances. However, appreciated the beautiful hotel lobby, with gorgeous courtyard views and the famous Le Cirque restaurant next door. View was really nice from my 31st floor room. Room looked east, with the Citicorp building in the distance. Staff was courteous and quick. Turn down service was provided every night. Nice amenities, robes, complimentary slippers, fitness facilities. Skip the room service, which can be pricey -- averaging $35/person for breakfast. Instead, go across the street to the Starbucks's for a cup of joe and breakfast pastries and check out the multitude of restaurants in the area. Conveniently situated near Rockefeller Center. Will definitely recommend to out of towners, who are looking for a nice treat.

title: “Amazing Location - amazing room”
text: We were in town for the Rock n Roll Half Marathon so the location of our hotel was extremely important. We wanted to be within walking distance of everything to maximize what we could do and see in our 4 short days in Seattle. The W Hotel has an incredible location that will put you close to everything. The rooms are absolutely amazing with everything that is first class and all the comforts you would want and need. I do have a few issues with the front desk staff - just not very friendly at all - and the fact that there is no business center available on the weekend at all. And it doesn't open until 9 a.m. on Monday morning. I would highly recommend that you bring your own laptop if you need to stay in touch with the office or family over the weekend.

title: “Disappointed.”
text:
We booked a room for one night to stay in after our trip to Sea World. We arrived around 8pm and checked in. The neighborhood is a bad one. It is mostly industrial buildings surrounding the hotel. Make sure to park as close to the front doors as possible as it is the most lit area of the parking lot.
Right away we could hear a lot of loud music and party noise coming from the pool area. Initially our room appeared okay. When we pulled the sofa sleeper out for our kids there were no sheets. So we checked to closet and no linen there either. I called the front desk and explained there were no linens or pillows for the sofa sleeper. I then sent my kids up to the front desk to get them. they came back with a set of sheets. No blankets, no pillows. So I send them back and they return with pillows. No pillows cases on them and no pillow cases with the linen they picked up prior. So I went up and specifically asked for each item needed. We could hear the noise from the pool even though our room was on the other side, but I was so tired I didn't feel like dealing with it as the front desk person was clueless to begin with.
The next morning we go to the complimentary breakfast at 8am, with breakfast closing up at 9 or10. The was not much food there. They had a waffle machine, but no batter. They had run our of cinnamon rolls. They had run out of yogurt too. What we were left with was cereal and milk! I went to the front desk to ask about bringing out some food and was told that they had run out for the weekend and that was all they had left! Unreal! I almost exclusively stay at Holiday Inn Express hotels and have NEVER run across this before or since. So we checked out and had breakfast at McDonaldson the way out of town.

title: “Wonderful hotel!”
text: I have been in this hotel at the beginning of August. I had a little problem at the check-in that has been solved. The room was amazing, overlooking Chicago skyline, well furnished and spacious bathroom and bedroom. I will definitely go back!

title: “Excellent customer service!”
text:
I read some of the reviewers that rated this hotel poor or terrible. You know, some people just have to be unhappy to be happy. This hotel is an historic building. It's a former bank building complete the teller cage for checking in. The lobby is beautiful and the location is downtown people! There's sometimes "undesirables" who hang out at bus stops and in the parks. The hotel has nothing to do with that. The building is secured after dark and you must slide your room key in the slot in order for the elevator door to open. 
Esmeralda was very nice at check in. She found out we were there to celebrate our 30th anniversary and to our surprise, she arranged for a bottle of nice red wine and a box of dark chocolate covered almonds (my husband's fave) to be delivered to our room. You will not encounter an employee who doesn't speak to you. 
They offer hot breakfast with all the usual items including biscuits and gravy, fruit, yogurt, etc. It does get crowded because weekends tend to get busy. The 5:30 snack time was generously stocked with baked potatoes, Mac and cheese, hot dogs, popcorn, adult beverages and fountain drinks, just to name a few. 
It's s non smoking hotel however people smoke on the balconies and unfortunately it stinks up your outdoor enjoyment but oh well. Until San Antonio becomes smoke free you have to take the good with the bad. 
I would not hesitate to recommend this hotel to anyone!

title: “Great find!”
text: We stayed 2 nights and could not have been more pleased with the location, room and service of the staff. The breakfast was yummy and well located for the 2nd floor of the main house. We would definitely return.

title: “Great Location!”
text: We booked our stay through Orbitz and it included parking, which worked great! We were able to come and go as we pleased. This hotel is in a great location! We walked to Shedd Aquarium no problem. The only down side was the room was kind of small. Our daughter was only 11months at the time, so we took her pack n play for her to sleep in. There was barely enough room to set it up and still be able to walk by. However, all of the staff was friendly and helpful and the room was clean.

title: “GREAT UPDATES!”
text: I stayed at this hotel a few times prior to the updates, and last week stayed at this hotel after the room renovations--what a huge improvement! The Milford is in THE PERFECT location in Midtown Manhattan and it's so nice to see that they have made those rooms new again. Don't be fooled when you get off the elevator by the very dark hallways...the rooms are wonderful. They did a good job at making it updated, yet keeping it affordable to average folks. The entire staff was amazing and went out of their way to be helpful and friendly. We interacted with the front desk a few times, housekeeping twice, two managers, the doorman, etc. and everyone made us feel welcome. I would highly recommend this to someone looking for a clean hotel room, in a great location at an affordable price.

title: “OK hotel”
text: We visited family in San Diego and the hotel was fine for that, it certainly isn't a destination, but they don't advertise it as an destination. It is clean, good breakfast, typical Residence Inn room. The only really negative is that they charged us $13 for parking. That is NOT obvious on the web site and it should be. We would never have found it if not for our GPS. You literally go round and round to get to it if you are coming from the east. It may not be as difficult if you are coming from the west. It's set back from the freeway so we didn't have any road noise. The breakfast is great, hot food (eggs, waffles, sausage, etc) and lots of fruits and breads.

title: “A Unique Lil' Hotel For a Smaller Budget”
text:
I was a little leery about visiting the hotel after reading some of these reviews. I called a day prior to arriving to verify that my reservation was still valid - and when I showed up the next day, they explained that they had upgraded my room from a theme to "superior" (we had to wait an extra hour and half though) - It has a private bath
After we were able to get to the room - I found it to be quite refreshing. It was a tad small - but very clean and well kept. The only major complaints that I had was that the walls were thin (you could definitely hear your neighbor), the TV (which had a DVD player built in) didn't get some channels really well, and the A/C wasn't very good, Lucky for us - we went in November. Since there was no vending machine's or cups for water and such - the Subway Restaurant right below the hotel came in handy
On the other hand, the front desk was very helpful - offered us advise on things to do and ways to get around. The location was fantastic - about 2 blocks away from Madison Sq Garden / Penn Station, lots of nifty diner's and food joint's around. There's a quaint little patio for smoking and socializing and there is pay Internet terminal downstairs. 
I didn't get a chance to see what the Theme rooms looked like - but I did get a chance to see the shared bathroom. On each floor (there are 3) - about 8 rooms share one bathroom (which always looked spotless when I checked).
For the price and location, I don't think that this could be beat. And, if you are going to NYC as a tourist, how much time will you spend in the room anyway?

title: “Never Again”
text:
Room preparation was bad, alarm clock was set by cleaning staff at 5 am, at trying to unplug the alarm clock I hurt my elbow.
Breakfast was bad, even if it is complimentary, it should have had water, a fruit, a piece of whole wheat bread, and honey. Those basic things were not available.
Wifi internet did not work...funny, I can connect everywhere instantly with smartphone and laptop, except for the Ramada wifi.

title: “Excellent Location, clean, great decor and very friendly staff!!”
text: My sister and I spend 2 nights at the Moderne 6-8th July 2011, and absolutely loved it. Location is just fantastic, 5-10 min walk from the middle of Time square, same distance the opposite way to Central park. well located for the Metro for 3 different lines, and there is a pub opposite which is very handy for stumbling back! The hotel has just recently been refurbished, and has only been open a couple of months since. So all the decor is very fresh, retro style, and the staff, seriously they were so helpful, advice on the metro, booking us a car for the trip back to the airport, checking us into our flight etc. There was always a very cheery hello, good morning, good night everytime you were in the lobby. The rooms were of reasonable size, but why would you need anything bigger, New york is all about spending the minimal amount of time in the room, max time out and about! This has to be the nicest hotel i have stayed in in New York. I'd say its excellent value for money too.

title: “Awesome hotel for couples and a ball game!!”
text: Great hotel. Short walk to Petco, good bars, and restaurants. Walking distance to seaport village. The hotel staff is very friendly and bar is great in the lobby. I will stay here again.

title: “The best hotel staff in the world”
text:
I am a regular at this hotel for some years now, I belong to India but whenever I or anyone from my company goes to Charlotte I recommend them to stay here, their feedback about this hotel is about the same as mine when they come back which is 'fantastic'.
On Arrival you are greeted with a smile, the check in is so easy, it takes a max of 2-3 minutes to check in if you have a confirmation. The staff ensures (try their best) that you get the room of your choice i.e. you want a room away from the lifts, one which is quiet or with a good view, not too high, too low et al.
Room Service is quick, at times the chef would deliver food to your room (Multi-Tasking :-)).. The prices on the menu are reasonable & the food is of great quality & taste, My personal favorite - Hot Spicy Buffalo Wings with Ranch. Complimantary Breakfast is sumptuous & has all the necessary items that you would like to have for a good breakfast..
Mondays to Thursdays, the hotel provides complimentary drinks & snacks at the dining hall on the ground floor, the place is just full of energy with people having good fun, great food & drinks and wonderful service, the bartenders are not just polite, prompt but also generous in serving you drinks as many times as you want, If you're a shy kind - the bartenders would usually walk up to you & ask you for another drink if you need it, For us every bartender knew what we drink (and how many) so we didn't have to do the hard work.
I would personally want to recommend the entire staff especially Stacey, Liz, Paulette for their customer centricity. One of my colleagues traveling with me got ill & unfortunately didn't have medicines late at night, Stacey from front desk offered him her Advil (Over the counter medicine) pills so that he feels better, he got better after taking them & the next day we took him to a doctor suggested by Stacey after which he got perfectly fine - she was okay with my friend keeping the pills with him just in case he needs them at any time during his stay, Now this is something I've never seen with any 'hotel staff' in over 50 hotels I must have stayed at, Stacey isn't just a great employee but a great human being.
The complimentary shuttle service takes you to most places nearby i.e. your office, places of interest, Bus/Train Station. The shuttle drivers are friendly & try their best not to make you wait.. But, as it's just one shuttle so we had to be patient & wait as we knew that there are others also he needs to take care off!
At the end I'd just like to say that when someone gets such a great place to stay, he/she would also try to be more polite & friendly with the staff and that's exactly what happened with us & other guests, you give your guests great service, they'll give you good business & would be friendly with you..
Stay at Residence Inn for a stay that you're gonna remember for a long long time.. 
Cheers & Peace - VK

title: “excellent location for stopping in Philadelphia”
text:
stopped with three friends (in two rooms) for 2 nights early May. Both rooms were twin rooms with ample space and ensuite bathroom.
We basically used this as a base, as we were out all day and night (at night watching baseball).
Excellent location, right in the middle of town, handy for the underground. There is an underground parking lot opposite underneath a shopping complex, the hotel will give a discount on the parking.
For the limited time we were there, we had no problems with anything in the hotel.

title: “Great overnight find!”
text: This was our second stay up in the Baltimore area, staying previously in the Inner Harbour. Thought we would try a different hotel to get a better feel for the area and was pleasantly surprised at our find. We found the hotel to be very clean and comfortable and pleased with the accommodating staff. Our room was spotless. The bed was slightly lumpy, but not bad. Breakfast was included which provided a large selection of breakfast foods. Very nice! Although we did not use, we also understand the hotel allows parking, while you cruise! That would be very nice as we paid a ton to park at the port. Best Western provides a free shuttle to the Inner Harbour area, which was another great perk. Overall, we saved a ton of money by not staying directly in the Inner Harbour area and we were perfectly comfortable.

title: “Great hotel, location and excellent customer service”
text: As other reviewers have mentioned, the customer service here is fantastic. The chef made complimentary mickey mouse shaped pancakes for my kids one morning, the front desk staff was very helpful with recommendations and upgraded us to a very large and comfortable room for a family of 4.The furnishings and carpeting are a bit outdated but nonetheless everything was clean. I will stay here again !! Thanks St.Giles for making our stay wonderful!

title: “SO Impressed! Definitely will be back!”
text: I found a great rate for this hotel via hotels.com & I was SO surprisingly impressed! It was only 9 miles to Mayo where I had appts for two days. The hotel was kept spotless inside & out. The first person I see at the front desk greeted me so warmly. She welcomed me as if we were old friends. Being nervous with personal reasons b/c of a health issue I was in town for to deal with I was immediately put at ease from this employee's attutude & treatment towards me. I found my room to be very clean & even the housekeeping staff was very friendly. All I wanted in my stay was WiFi hookup, TV, & smoking room. I got all that & more! The hotel sits right next to two affordable restaurants & is located conveniently just down from the interstate, I-95. What topped it off & made it all worth while was one employee imparticular. She was aware that I was going thru testing all day at the hospital & had to go back the next day for more appts. I came back to the room after my 6pm MRI-(by then it was 9pm) & there were a pot of fresh flowers left for me. I called down to the desk & this woman admitted to leaving them for me. She knew how sick I have been now for 1 1/2 years & just wanted to make me smile. She didnt have to do this but took it upon herself to personally & privately (separate from the hotel) just to nring a smile to my face. What an angel! There really are some good people out there! Then, I found out she is the general manager! Some places the gen. mng act "too good" to talk to the customers. Not her! She paid out of her own pocket to buy flowers just to make them feel better! LOVE THAT! My folks came into town to visit me in the hospital as I was admitted immediately and stayed at this hotel as well. They, too were very pleased! Also, it is pet friendly which helped my folks a lot! I could go on & on but hopefully you can get the picture. I absolutely recommend this hotel!

title: “Will never return again!”
text:
My husband and I stayed here at RBI because we have stayed at other JC Resort Properties and we loved the service and atmosphere of the resorts and thought since this one was close to home we would give it a try. This place, compared to other similarly rated properties was very disappointing. We wanted to check out as soon as we arrived. There was a long and confusing hike to find our hotel room. Prior to arriving Arlene in the spa bent over backwards to accommodate our last minute requests at the spa. Because of all of her hard work and professionalism we decided to give RBI another chance. Arlene in the spa was so accommodating and welcoming we decided to tolerate a lot more than we normally would have. When we arrived in the room it was nice and clean with what appeared to be a lowly budgeted recent remodel. When we sat on the bed, the mattress slid across the frame mounting about 6 inches. The frame of the bed was too big for the mattress! The bed was extremely uncomfortable. You could hear springs in the mattress all night and neither my husband or I got a good night sleep! I ended up with bruises on my legs from banging them on the frame every time I got out of bed. 
The only nice thing I can say about this place is the spa was a wonderful experience and the atmosphere of the grounds is beautiful. Our hotel rate included 2 spa treatments with each night stay for $268. Which is a great deal if the room had not been so miserable. I have been to better spas, but everyone was quite professional and caring. My husband chose to have the signature massage and I chose the aroma therapy facial. We also opt'd for the spa pedicure, which in my opinion was a waste of money. The environment for the pedicure was not in the spa area and the bench seat was very uncomfortable. The room was attached to the fitness area and was very loud and non-relaxing. The spa has a nice dressing room area with all of the amenities, 3 showers and plenty of lockers. While waiting for your treatment you can enjoy a private men or women only steam room and jacuzzi, the saline pool or co-gender jacuzzi, or relax in the cabanas that are included for spa members only. 
Needless to say the night only got worse when we went to the Veranda Dining area and were highly disappointed by the very low quality of the food offered there. The ambiance was amazing as it sits outside overlooking the golf course but we could have gotten better food from Denny's down the road! 
Overall it was nice to have a weekend away with my husband but I would highly recommend that you consider another place unless you are used to the Holiday Inn level or lower of accommodations. The grounds are beautiful. If you live locally, I would recommend a visit to the spa!

title: “Amazing”
text: The Claredon is extremely beautiful. All the staff members are so kind and generous. I am happy that my family decided to spend part of the holidays there this past year. The rooms were spacious, comfortable and extremely clean. My family LOVES pools, and the Claredon's definately passed the test. I would highly recommend the Claredon to anyone coming to the Phoenix area.

title: “review of stay”
text:
room was in generally good to better condition as far as the cleaniness, There was not much noise so good sleep quality, The price was just a little higher than should be. $45-50 would be a better value based on the condiition of room, I didn't like the bed. It was too soft.
Overall it was a pleasant stay.

title: “A Gem In Hollywood!”
text:
After searching through seedy motels and low end budget hotels in Hollywood and being scared off, it was a relief to find a good value clean hotel just one block away from the Hollywood & Highland area!
The Hotel is situated on Franklin Ave, just a 5 min walk to Hollywood Blvd which contains the Chinese Theatre and Walk of Fame etc
The Hotel (A converted apartment complex) features a swimming pool, patio area and rooms overlooking the pool. The rooms were spacious and functional and the staff were possibly the most polite and helpful people in Hollywood! Nothing was too much trouble!
The complimentary breakfast and mini bar (free soft drinks and snacks) was amazing! Didnt need to spend a penny!
The price is outstanding value for the area and I highly reccomend this hotel to families or couples.
Don't forget to book any tours from the front desk! The staff will also book reservations for restaurants if you ask!

title: “Great Staycation!”
text: It was July in Phoenix and it was hot!!! The family wanted to get away but didn't want to go on a long road trip. So we drove about ten minutes to this Embassy suites for the 4th of July weekend and had a blast. The hotel has a very large circular pool that very comfortably accomodated all of its guests over that busy holiday weekend. My kids loved it! The room was clean and comfortable. Not quite as shiny and new looking as you would expect Embassy Suites to be, but it was okay. The best part is the cook to order breakfast. What a money saver, especially when traveling with the family, and the food was delicious. They will make you an omelet with your choice of ingredients. They also have all the potatoes, sausage, fruit, danishes or just scrambled eggs that you can eat. Plus they have a variety of fruit juices and coffee. It was great! My family and I had a great time, it was an affordable get away from the heat "staycation".

title: “Great value and friendly staff”
text: I have stayed at this Hampton Inn several times in the last few months while dealing with a family matter. The rooms are comfortably furnished and well maintained. The lobby and breakfast area are pleasant, with a "homey" feel. The property has a very nice fitness room and a lovely outdoor pool. A guest laundry is available at the Homewood Suites across the parking lot, a real convenience when on an extended stay. The staff has been friendly and unfailingly helpful on my repeated visits, making me feel like a welcome and valued guest. As a woman traveling alone, this level of personal recognition and attention was much appreciated.

title: “great Location, nice room”
text: This hotel is in a great spot about 2-3 blocks from two Metro stations. The staff was friendly and checked me in quickly. The room was spacious and the beds were comfortable. The hotel is about a 15 minute walk from the mall. Only a few negatives: parking is overpriced. I found two lots down the street for $15 less. Also i can understand a charge for wireless internet in your room, but guests needed to pay to use internet in business center. Overall, if you can get a good deal, this is a good place for all types of travelers to stay.

title: “loved it”
text:
stayed at the chancellor for 5 nights during November. The hotel location is perfect, the beds very comfortable , the staff very helpful...thank you Rory...and the cookies delicious.
All in all excellent value for money. I would highly recommend this hotel

title: “Best Hotel in Chicago”
text: Great way to visit the City and take in some of it's sites; museum, architectural tour and Navy pier. My wife had one of her best birthday celebrations ever. Had dinner in the cafe on the twelfth floor and the food was outstanding. Breakfast in the room rounded out a complete trip. Best coffee in town! Unbelievable service all around.

title: “Great airport location, typical Hilton quality”
text:
The great thing about staying at Hilton hotels is that you always know what you're going to get; consistently high quality rooms, outstanding customer service, and all the amenities that a business traveler needs. 
I stay at this hotel often when I'm in Los Angeles for work, as my meetings are always in the building adjacent to this hotel, so it's very conveniently located. However, the hotel is only about half a mile outside of the entrance of the LAX airport, so it's also ideally situated for anyone who has an early or late flight out of LAX and wants to be nearby the airport. The hotel has a complimentary airport shuttle, which is very convenient. 
The rooms are large and comfortable, with many amenities that travelers value, such as wired internet (for a fee), power outlets, coffee/tea maker in room, hairdryer, and name brand toiletries in the bathroom. The bathroom towels were soft, the bed linens were soft and high quality, the pillows were cushy, and the bed was amazingly comfortable (all very typical of Hilton linens/beds). The room I was in had an old tube-style TV rather than a flat screen, and wired internet instead of wireless -- so a few updates to the amenities in the rooms might be nice. 
This hotel also has many other amenities that guests may value -- multiple onsite restaurants, a business center, fitness center, convention center, gift shop, room service, concierge desk, swimming pool and more. 
The only downside to this hotel is the noise from the airplanes taking off and landing, as the hotel is literally across the street from the LAX runway. As LAX never really shuts down (the cargo planes and flights departing for Asia/Australia depart late at night/very early morning), the noise from the planes can be bothersome when trying to sleep. Although this is something that the traveler would just have to expect when staying at a hotel located across from a major airport, you might want to bring ear plugs to help you sleep.
All in all, a great location and a comfortable hotel with all of the amenities and standards you would expect from the Hilton brand.

title: “Just so-so....except the doughnuts!”
text:
We stayed at the Hotel Andra for 2 nights before heading to Vancouver. The hotel looks like a great European Boutique hotel, which we liked. The area seems to be quiet and sweet…just watch which way you walk. There are many vagrants wandering the streets as you get closer to Pike Place Market. The hotel itself is nice. The staff could just use a bit of a pep talk. When we checked in, the front desk attendant tried to change the price of one of the 2 nights of our original reservation. Then when my husband asked for an itemized receipt to verify upon checkout, another clerk seemed as if he couldn’t be bothered.
The room was comfortable, two cozy Queen beds, a sofa and table, desk, large marble-top bar area, and a huge walk in closet that was great for storing luggage. The bathroom was a little small. My biggest complaint about the room is the lighting. All light in the room comes from small lamps except for the light over the bar. The hotel is romantic, but not the best for family…also there is no pool. Internet access is not free, and there was no water in the fitness center just FYI.
The restaurant LOLA was good for brunch. The food and service were great, but it’s a bit expensive ($200 for 3 of us). Make sure, though, that you have the “made to order doughnuts” as an appetizer for your table! YUM!!! 
Hotel Andra is located close to the monorail that takes you to the Space Needle, as well as to buses and trains that get to other points of interest in Seattle. 
SIde note: I would totally recommend a few hours at the Museum of Flight.

title: “POD PERFECTION!”
text:
Returned to dreary Britain today after an incredible Thanksgiving week in New York City with friends.
This was my 5th visit to the city and I have previously stayed in some of the more 'historic' hotels that line the streets of Broadway and 7th Avenue, so for a change I decided to go for a slightly more modern and upbeat hotel. That is exactly what I got with the Pod 39.
Situated in the Upper East Side in the Murray Hill district, the Pod 39 is within walking distance to Grand Central Station (about 10 mintues), you can then hop onto the S train which runs backwards and forwards to Times Square, walking distance to 5th, 6th and Lexington Ave, which is fantastic as we where mainly there for the Black Friday sales and there are some fantastic diners and bars in the area, too. Not to mention the roof top terrace of the Pod itself. The bar wasn't open, but the terrace was lit up at night so it was nice to chill out at the end of a long day with a bottle of beer and watch the city. Views of the Empire State Building, Chrysler, East River and the rising Freedom Tower dominate the views.
I was in a party of 4 and we had two bunk rooms. One was slightly bigger than the other, but not by much. Alot of the reviews here state that the rooms are almost two small, I shared with a male friend and we're not the most tidy of people, but we still had space to move around (even with all of our shopping!).
The bathroom wasn't a problem, either. A glass sliding door with frosted glass in the middle, but dim the lights (using the dimmer) and you can't see a thing! It steamed up when the shower was on, anyway.
Bunk beds where comfy, had a great night sleep and each bed had it's own TV. There was also a unit with various input/outputs for AVI, USB, HDMI ect. I only made use of the USB to charge my camera/phone. There is also an electric safe in the room to store your important posessions.
Staff and house keeping where really friendly as was the entire concerige team. They booked us a car back to EWR at a cost of $77 which is cheaper than using the town car service provided by groundlink or the NYC Taxi service.
There's some slight building work going on downstairs, but it's out of the lobby and behind doors, so it wasn't a problem. Also a bar in the hotel, which I didn't make use of, but it looked really good. They also served breakfast, but we chose to dine at Scotty's Diner on Lexington which was one block away. If you eat here, get the French Toast, eggs, bacon and sausage. The enitre meal isn't on the menu, but ask for it. It's some of the best I've had during my time in NYC.
Overall, if you plan on travelling with friends or as a couple/solo, this hotel is perfect. I don't know if they have family rooms, I'd guess not, but don't be put off by what others are saying about room size/privacy ect. We had no problems at all. It's worth booking this hotel for the views from the top to be honest. Give it a go, you'll be back!

title: “Better for a business traveler”
text: I chose to stay here for a conference because I grew up in Philly and thought it would be fun to stay in the old PSFS building. There is hardly a lobby, which is dissapointing. The front desk is run by teenagers who act like they are doing you a favor by speaking to you. The girl that helped me had wet hair and kept yawning while she checked me in. The room itself was large and quiet, with a fantastic panoramic view, though the peach/plum color scheme was puzzling, and the TV was at an odd angle to the bed. Very, very convenient to the convention center. It was OK, though once was probably enough for me.

title: “Good location for convention center, but very noisy and misleading”
text: Good location for convention center business, but hotel walls were paper thin as I could hear everything and am normally not bothered by hotel noise. Ice maker ran like a waterfall 6 nights I was there. "Chic"-ness was only in lobby and hallways - rooms were standard fair. If you need anything, be prepared to walk to 7-11 around the corner - bottled water and 3 lb boxes of Jr Mints are about all they have.

title: “Good value, clean, comfortable and good amenities”
text:
We stayed here for 4 nights at the end of May 2012 & liked the hotel very much - the room was very big, with two kingsize beds, a spacious bathroom and enormous tv! 
The bed was very comfortable and we also appreciated the coffee maker in the bedroom. 
Breakfast was great - cereal, bagels, toast, danish pastries, muffin, fruit, yoghurt and waffles with maple syrup. We enjoyed the coffee/tea/hot chocolate available in the lobby 24hours and the warm chocolate chip cookies at 5pm were great too! The breakfast room did get busy if you were there later in the morning but we generally ate at around 8-8.30 and had no trouble getting a table. 
Parking was easy - and most important free (I had considered some downtown hotels where parking was up to $30 per day on top of the room cost!). We had rented a car and wanted to drive to various places in San Diego and the hotel was very well placed to do this with quick, easy access to all the main sites. We also enjoyed the pool and jacuzzi in the evenings. 
We had no trouble with traffic or airport noise as some others have reported and driving to the airport for our ongoing flight only took about 5 minutes!
I wouldnt hesitate to recommend this hotel to others and it was one of the best value stays on our whole road trip around California.

title: “Noisy and old!”
text:
This hotel should not be rated at 3 stars --- it should be 2 stars.
Pros: The hotel is very environmentally conscious, which is great. The staff was pretty nice and accommodating and they like to have fun and joke around.
Cons: The hotel is very old and needs some major up-keeping. The plaster on the walls are cracking and the paint on the walls and around the windows are chipping off. The room was really, really small but we were told that we had one of the bigger ones --- a more deluxe room. The walls have absolutely no sound proofing. We heard our neighbors all night long --- not just the room next to us but even the room across the way from us. We had to turn our TV up to drown out the voices and other noises we constantly heard. We even called down to front desk and asked to have our room changed because our neighbors were so noisy, and they gladly did that for us but when we took a peek at the room we were going to be switching to, we decided that we would stay in the room we had because the room that they wanted to give us was even smaller, the TV was old, and there was a horrible view of an apartment building next door which was so close that we could see into a person's apartment. There was also some mildew/mold around the shower/tub area, and no thermostat in the rooms. The temperature in the rooms are centrally controlled which was not good for me because I get cold easily. I was freezing in my room so they sent up a portable space heater for me, which helped, but it didn't warm the room up enough for me. Also the space heater ended up being an inconvenience because I couldn't blow dry my hair or iron anything while it was on. I tripped the breaker once because of that and all the lights went off and I had to call down to have maintenance turn the lights back on. 
Overall, our stay was bearable, but we will not be staying at this hotel again.

title: “Fantastic renovation”
text: We stayed at the Grand Hyatt in San Francisco off Union Square just after Christmas. We stayed here about 4 years ago and at least the room we stayed in had been tansformed since the last visit. We enjoyed the hotel before but the new room was beautiful. the full length windows give you an amazing view, Ask for a room as high as possible. If you can upgrade to a club room those are on the higher floors. I used Hyatt points.The after holiday shopping was great and there were sales at all the stores around Union Square.

title: “Welcome Surprise in an Emergency”
text: When our electricity failed in a 104 degree heat wave, we called Days Hotel. They gave us a spacious two rooms that were cool and quiet. What a relief to find something so practiclal, inexpensive, and professional in a nearby neighborhood. The staff was helpful. The room was very clean. I'd recommend this to anyone who needed a safe place for a day or two.

title: “Good Alternative to Downtown; Gym review in summary”
text:
I travel to Denver for business for 3-4 nights a month and frequently choose this Hotel. The executive suites are very comfortable and newly refurnished. There are restraunts of every kind and every price range including a Safeway and whole foods within 1.5 miles of the hotel. 
As a runner, the suburbs to the west of the Hotel lead to U. of Colorado Campus which is a good urban run. 
 If you are visiting Denver as tourist the downtown hotels are better bet, but as a business traveler who has gotten over eating at Cheese Cake Factorys this is an easier stay.
Pool: don't waste your time
Gym: nice treadmill, ok eliptical machine, free weights up to 40lbs; low end universal machine
Bus. Office: standard
Complaints: The in-room coffee and continental breaskfast coffee are way sub-par, plan on hitting starbucks down the road.

title: “best hotel stay I have had in years”
text: I have been in the travel business for over 30 years and have stayed in more hotels than the happy hooker, but for hospitality and comfortable accomodations, I was so impressed with this hotel. I felt the most genuine welcome and the staff was so professional and anticipated all of my needs in the most gracious manner. I felt like I was visiting family. My room was so comfortable and the sleep number bed was fabulous. Room service was fast and great, and the shuttle at 440 am was right on time. I will become a regular client.

title: “Wonderful Experience”
text: My daughter and I stayed one weekend night to attend "Cinderella" at the Fifth Avenue. The hotel is beautifully maintained; lovely artwork and furnishings in the lobby. The entire staff is professional, helpful, and friendly. Loved the rooms. Very, very, comfortable beds and tastefully furnished. Next door is an outdoor elevator that takes you up the hill to Pike Place market. Walking distance to all the waterfront shops and Westlake center. Will definitely stay here again.

title: “Impressive”
text: At Omni October 15-17, 2012 for a conference. The structure itself is impressive and expansive - self parking is below street. Well maintained as I noted no lamps out or issues throughout the building. Room was in great order and bed/bedding was outstanding. The set-ups for the conference were great and the food was better than average. Front desk staff were very helpful. The concierege floor 14 required room card access for the floor and the waitstaff in the service area on the floor were friendly and excellent. Price was a bit high.

title: “beyond satisfactory. service was great, and had a great stay.”
text: I would absolutely recommend this hotel. location is great. convinient short distance south of downtown austin, without the noise. when I arrived drew assisted me at the front desk, check in was very quick, and I was able to get to my room after a long flight. downtown shuttle was available every 30 minutes, ching, the shuttle driver, was very friendly. service and food in restaraunt/bar was supurb.

title: “Impressive boutique hotel with literary ambience within sight of New York Public Library.”
text: Great location & wonderfully worked literary theme. A quiet restful ambience conducive to reading, writing and reflection. Well done to all invalid for the welcoming service.

title: “Love the hotel but a little far if you don't have a car.”
text:
The hotel itself is nice and pretty W style, though we got the room facing the Residency so pretty much facing the wall. The staff found us another room when we asked to move just a little further to the front. Some staffs are nice (my waiter in a lobby) as she asked for a discount from her manager when I showed her SPG card ( got no point from this stay since I hotwire it). The bar can be noisy during the night and I was aware of this so I booked it during the weekday, though the bar was pretty full during our stays. 
There's a subway station right in front of the hotel and there were homeless people sleeping in the front sometimes. It's quite a walk from the center of the Hollywood. There one great thing about W though that they have a drop off service with a ....brand (sorry don't remember the name). The driver was really nice and good looking and we always got him a couple times we used this service which I must admit it's lovely for some people who don't drive. My bf license expired so we couldn't rent a car. 
Overall it was a nice stay but some staffs can be a little snobbish. It's roomy and if you love W, you'll love this one.

title: “great location, good buy”
text:
i just spent a week working at the Farmer's Daughter for business and I'd definitely recommend it. The staff are friendly and helpful, the rooms, lobby, and courtyard are well-designed and decorated, and the location is amazing -- right across the street from the Farmer's Market and the Grove, near a drugstore and a Whole Foods. It's great if you're there on business and don't want to go to a restaurant every day.
The only issue I had is that Internet access is not free - $10 for 24 hours or $4 for one hour.

title: “Great location, but outdated product and service.”
text:
Not recognized as a platnium member of PC. No water, not much benefit of being a platnium member. 
Candy and snack Vending locations aren't ideal. 
Unable to obtain change for vending quickly. Ordered room service and it was incorrect. Would not offer a refund unless I waited another 30 min for a sandwich.
Join the times with flat screen tvs please.

title: “Underwhelmed”
text:
I was so ridiculously excited to stay here until I started reading the reviews here on Trip Advisor and started to worry a bit. I hoped that my stay wouldn't be like the others and kept my chin up. That was my mistake. 
We arrived a bit before our check in time and used the valet. I've used valet at other NYC hotels and it's never been an issue but here it was a [--]. They really didn't help point you as to how the heck to get to the lobby and were really rude. We had no idea where we were going and after a few tries we found it but it wasn't for the help in the valet area. Our room wasn't ready yet so they told us it'd only be about 30 minutes at most and we decided to wait. 45 minutes later our room STILL wasn't ready so we decided to hit the bar (their own brand of champagne is pretty decent I must say). After about 2 hours total of waiting our room was ready and I was informed we'd been upgraded from our Junior Suite. 
We got to the room and I was pretty excited as I was told this was a suite, yay! We opened the door and almost were physically knocked over by the stench of cigarettes and cigars. It was horrid!! What made it even worse was that my husband had just quit smoking days before the trip so that made things a lot more difficult. After all of that waiting, we didn't want to sit and wait MORE so decided to hope it dissipated and headed off into the city. I will note that our suite WAS very nice, 2 full bathrooms, a bedroom and a living room. The decor was a bit dated but it was still a nice space. I also have seen others complain about the lack of hair dryer and neither of our rooms had one. 
The next day we got a phone call asking how our stay was and I told them about the rancid smoke smell (mind you this was a non smoking room). They said they'd bring an air purifier in the room while we were out to hopefully make it better. I don't think they ever did that because the smell never got better. 
That night while sleeping I woke up when I was bit on the foot by a spider. In the bed. I know this could happen anywhere but this is the last place I ever expected this to happen at. My foot swelled up and it was pretty painful for a couple days. Again, it could happen anywhere but happening at a hotel of this caliber is kind of surprising. 
Finally upon leaving we were told to call 30-45 minutes before we needed our car which we did. When we got to the valet though we had to wait ANOTHER 45 minutes for our car, which had I not planned for delays, would have made us late for our flight. 
After seeing my complaint about the spider bite on Twitter the Waldorf did email me and ask what happened. However when I told them what happened, I never heard a response. 
It was an OK stay but I don't think I'd do it again. The hotel definitely has seen better days, the service wasn't nearly what I was expecting and the rooms (although big) were ho-hum. Bummer.

title: “great location and absolutely adequate”
text: one half block from tkts booth on times square, old rooms and hardware but sufficiently sized, everything works, housekeeping and front desk excellent, reasonably priced and good food at cafe on street level, clean and attractive

title: “Nice, good value”
text:
Old hotel which is changed to a funky stile. 
Room was nice and AC worked fine. Wireless also worked fine and the staff was nice. 
Location is nice and there is a bus just outside the door taking you downtown. 
Never tried to eat at the hotel since out rate did not included breakfast. 
All in all, good value for money.

title: “THE GRAND OLD LADYReally needs upgrade”
text: Stayed at hotel great service and staff but the room was terrible. I saved all year for this holiday as a treat for my wife birthday but was really let down because of the room. There are better 2* hotel rooms .carpet dosent fit chipped cabnets really old decor really poor state and its a shame because food good. And staff great would I stay here again no. But if they re decorate the rooms I would return real shame the grand old lady has been run into the ground

title: “Exactly what you need that night!”
text: This hotel is perfect if you have to fly in late to Boston and don't want to get going on the rest of your trip until the next morning. You just follow the signs from baggage claim through the airport -- not a long distance, and not outside -- into the Hilton. The rooms are comfortable ~ There is food available (I was able to order as late as 11 pm when I checked in) ~ and the rooms are comfortable. There's a shuttle to the rental car places for when you get going the next morning. The Hilton makes late-night travel into Boston as easy as it can possibly be.

title: “Wonderful hotel right behind Port...”
text: Wonderful hotel right behind Port Authority with plenty of shopping nearby. My husband can be very picky and he loved this hotel. Everything is new and it still has that new carpet smell. We were on the 14 floor and did not have much of a view but for the price it well worth it. I highly recommend the Distrikt!.

title: “Dated Embassy”
text: The property overall is a good, standard Embassy Suites, but does need an update. Everything from the lobby to the rooms is dated, but is clean. No complaints about the staff, everyone was very helpful. The breakfast was a good and hot breakfast with all of your standard choices.

title: “Liked the hotel, disliked the restaurant.”
text:
Overall the restaurant is the downfall of the entire hotel. The hotel, hotel staff, rooms etc are great. However, the restaurant leaves much to be desired.
The female restaurant manager was less than helpful when resolving our seating issues. We had a party of 8 and I can understand having to wait for a large party but the restaurant was completely empty and the manager had the audacity to tell me she couldnt seat us...not even at separate tables and THE RESTAURANT WAS EMPTY (there were 2 tables seated and a couple at the bar). She was slightly rude and extremely unaccommodating. Later when her behavior was brought to her attention she apologized but it was too late.
The restaurant also got one of my family's orders wrong on a separate occasion, we had to wait over an hour for our food and it was wrong...you can imagine my disappointment. Then the manager assured me the order would be corrected, which it was and he also assured me that the bill would be taken care of, which it was not. The charges for the lackluster and incorrect meal showed up at checkout to my disappointment. Finally and thankfully the hotel manager took care of that charge.

title: “suprisingly elegant”
text:
I spent 1 night at the JW Marriott Union Square. For Christmas shopping in San Francisco, I would recommend this hotel highly. The service and facility is equal to the JW brand around the world.
I would recommend to get a room with executive lounge access, compare to the Hyatt Union Square, it's about 5 time bigger space and you are waiting for seats. 
The breakfast at the lounge was very good with plenty of choices for a full breakfast buffet. During the day and at evening, lounge is open,and there are plenty of drinks and water bottle.
I like to location because it's 1 block from union square,and is surprisingly quiet for downtown hotel.

title: “Dirty, small”
text: I went here for 5 days with my girlfriend, it was horrable. The room was not clean (even the bed was not clean and beneeth the bed... don't look!), it just fits one queen bed, and the room was full. we could not place our suitecases in the room so small. Location was ok.

title: “Would not recommend. Hard to tell what the hotel will be like after the renovation but it was just ok.”
text: Beds were comfortable but with an address boasting Beverly Hills that is what you would expect. It was close to Rodeo Drive.

title: “Nice business hotel - great location”
text:
Just stayed at the Orchard Garden for two nights and had a nice stay. I requested a quiet room and was given a top floor room at the back - very quiet. Nice, spacious room and bathroom. There was a distinctive slight patchouli smell but it either went away or I got used to it. My only complaint is that the doors slam so whenever someone goes into or out of their room, there is a loud banging in the hall. 
They don't include a breakfast in the rate so I took a walk to Lori's Diner (short, eight-minute walk) because the french cafe across the street doesn't open until 7:30 a.m. There's a Starbucks nearby (actually several) and a Posh Bagel.
There is a small fitness room with a treadmill, bike and elliptical. Not much else, but it does the job. 
The location is good - easy to walk to Union Square. Valet parking was expensive, but comparable to other SF hotels I've stayed in. We were here on business and the hotel suited us perfectly.

title: “NOISY aircon and unwashed sheets!”
text:
LOUD aircon unit is "standard" in Aloft design, according to staff. Auto setting whined, so we left it "on" (LOUD) as the lesser of two evil sounds. Mini fridge did not work either, but maintenance and desk were friendly and tried to help. After dinner, we turned back the bed to find sheets were not clean. Again, helpful and mortified staff acted quickly to try to help, moving us to a different room, unfortunately with communicating door. Good news: bed clean, aircon "auto" setting was quiet, and fridge worked. Bad news: without the LOUD aircon, paper-thin walls allow neighboring sounds to be very clear, and communicating door especially helped us to hear the crying baby on the other side. 
Pros: very nice and helpful reception and maintenance staff. Flat screen TVs are on exterior wall, so no danger of having the neighbor's playing loudly behind your headboard. BUT those loud aircons make guests turn up the volume on their TVs. Cons: Loud aircon, cleaning staff took a chance that sheets looked clean enough for next guest?

title: “100 Degrees in Denver and gave me a room with No Air Conditioning”
text:
Is One Dot the LOWEST I can give this Comfort Inn? I made this reservation a month ago, Went to check in around 5:45 after a long day in downtown Denver, the temperature was 100 degrees / 25 June 2012 / and they gave me a room with NO Air Conditioning. It was at least 90 Degrees in the room. I went to the front desk to as for another room and was told there were not Empty rooms they could give me, I asked for the manager and was told the manager was not on site. I asked if the Maintenance man could Fix the Broken Air Conditioner and was told there was NO Maintenance Man for repairing Anything. 
 After raising a fit and demanding another room with a Working Air Conditioner ( as Advertised and Promised ) the manager magically appeared walking down the hallway only to tell me the same room, they cannot give me another room because they were all full. I got on the phone with the corporate office and witnessed at least 4 people checking in to the empty rooms they said they did not have. The managers solution? Was to check me out , refund my credit card - and Asked Me to Leave the Property. Let me repeat that - Checked me out of my Room and Asked me to Leave the property. Do NOT USE THIS COMFORT INN. The did not try to help me in any way - look for other accommodations, NOTHING - I got in my car and drove 2 hours home not believing what just happened. I filed a Complaint with the Corporate office but I'm sure they will turn around and try to give the room to some other poor soul.

title: “The best!”
text: Ease of travel access accompanied by wonderful accommodations made for an extremely comfortable and personal experience.

title: “Corrupt front desk and thugs knocking on my door at 4am!!”
text:
I should have bailed during the check-in. When I arrived I was told by the front desk that they had oversold my room and instead of upgrading me they were putting me in a lower class accommodation. This was after they had me sign the invoice stating the nightly rate at the higher class room. When I said that I expected the price to be adjusted to reflect a cheaper rate given the lower class accommodation the person at the desk looked at me blankly and then shrugged his shoulders. It was only when I asked him to speak to his manager did he adjust my rate. 
Later that evening I was having a hard time sleeping due to all the noise from the street. The outer walls are PAPER thin and drafty! When I finally dozed off to sleep I was awoken with a loud knocking at my door. I answered the door to find this thug/crackhead asking me if Maria was there? WTF?!? He was obviously trying to find open doors or find someone he could rob! It was a good thing that I am young and at 6'5" I towered over him. 
When I called to complain in the morning and tell them that I was shocked that someone looking like that could gain entrance to the elevators through the lobby and go up to the 5th floor I was told that there had been several thugs in the building last night and they were going door to door on floors 5 and 13. The cops were there and they were investigating. I was told that a manager would contact me. That NEVER happened.
This place sucks and is not safe. Avoid at all costs!! There are MUCH better hotels for cheaper in Manhattan.

title: “Best Hotel I've Stayed in”
text:
Hyatt Place Charlotte - City Park
(Please note this is different than Hyatt Place Airport Tyvola Rd)
From the moment I called the front desk from the airport, they sounded sincere and helpful about giving me clear concise directions about how to catch the shuttle. 
Once arriving, it was just extremely pleasant checking in. They treated me like a special guest even though I was wearing shorts and T-shirt and looked pretty hammered from a long flight. I liked their laid back attitude and the informal attire the front desk personnel wore- it made check-in feel comfortable and personable.
The room was just really nice. The office area, with wet bar, fridge and long sofas gave a feeling of elegance. I like that the bed and vanity/wash basin area was separated by small dividers from the office area, the marbel counter tops and décor were beautiful. The room was very quiet, the bed, headboards and night stands were nicely done and comfortable. The 42" LCD TV had lots of easy to reach inputs for computers or other peripherals and was impressive (although I don't watch TV). I appreciated the tube of toothpaste that was waiting. This is the nicest room I have ever stayed in for the price (about $90). It was also great to be able to purchase a sandwich before leaving for the airport, it seemed fresher than airport food. It was also great that there was a sports bar/restaurant (Jocks & Jills) in the adjacent parking lot with good margaritas and good wings, the ribs were just okay. I have stayed at other airport hotels in Charlotte that are less expensive, but they are isolated, not close restaurants, and not near as nice as this one. I have to stay o/n frequently near the Charlotte airport and I will always now stay at this hotel. I did not use the pool or exercise facilities and didn't eat breakfast. The web site has photos that accurately portray the rooms.
If I could make one suggestion: the morning is very busy and the front clerk was making coffee, selling food, answering phone calls, and checking out guests. This is way too much work for one person. They did it well but I felt sorry for them.

title: “Nice respite from the noise and bustle”
text: I stayed at the Westin last week while up there on business. Check in line for Starwood members was longer than the line for "regular folks" (15 min wait) and I almost switched places, but someone kept beating me to it. Staff was very gracious. Room on 26th floor was very nice and spacious although I was surprised to hear how loud the noise was from doors shutting in the hallway, folks walking around, etc. Was charged $6 as a "handling fee" for having the Business Center send out a package via Federal Express. Room service was excellent (nice service, yummy), but equally expensive. I find it somewhat odd that one can only get a bathrobe upon request and the newspaper is not left at your door, but instead is left in a stack by the elevators. The combo of the two could result in some weird moments if folks caught you grabbing your paper first thing! :) I did hear other business folks talking to each other about how they prefer this hotel over others as well...one benefit to standing in the check-in line for so long. Overall, I agree and I'd stay here again because the bed is deliciously comfortable and the folks were so nice, but there are some rough edges that could be corrected.

title: “Probably the best located hotel in the world”
text:
This is a massive hotel. They have 2000 rooms and if you have ever been on a cruiseliner then its certainly the feeling u have when u are rushing up the elevators to your rooms.
The lobby is on the 8th floor and below is a vast ammount of convention space. The hotel was fully booked when i was there. 
The elevator system is amazing. You have to dial in the desired floor on a keypad and the system will tell you which elevator to take. Probably the fastest elevator I have ever been in.
The exec lounge is on the 30th floor. Grabbing breakfast there is no easy task when the hotel is full. It was very crowded. Breakfast downstairs would have set me back by 30USD.
The hotel is good. Ridiculously over priced. But then again you can expect nothing less at Times Square.

title: “Simply The Best!!!!”
text:
I booked this hotel as a surprise for my husband to celebrate his 40th birthday and quite frankly I don't think I could possibly have found a better place to stay in New York! 
From start to finish the staff were fantastic. I had a conversation with the head housekeeper (I think it was Maria) and it was refreshing to see how much pride she genuinely took in making sure everyone was happy with their stay. Our room (410) was spacious, comfortable and spotlessly clean, as was the lounge/breakfast area.
From the young ladies who served breakfast and the cheese & wine in the evenings, to the reception and door staff (Hassan was exceptionally pleasant and ran around for us no end!) there is simply nothing negative I can say about these people.
We had an absolutely amazing time in New York, and if we are ever lucky enough to return, I would not consider staying anywhere other than the Casablanca.

title: “Thanks to the Fantastic Staff”
text: The staff was fantastic before and during our stay 2/21-2/23 and again 3/2/08. The hotel staff was great with reservations and answering all of our questions. They took their time and were very friendly. The shuttle was also perfect, we were able to take the shuttle to and from the cruise ship terminal, Sea World, the Zoo and the Mall. The mall was a 15 min walk after shuttle hours. The property is a little dated and second floor room are a little difficult if you have lots of bags. I would stay again. The room rates are good and the staff really goes above and beyond. From from desk, to reservations to the shuttle drivers. Thanks Dirk.

title: “Pretty Darn Impressed”
text: Booked this hotel through Priceline and got a heck of a deal. After booking, I emailed the property to request a non-smoking king, and they had no problems accomodating us. They gave us a large corner room with many windows overlooking Town Lake and the Congress Street Bridge. We fully expected to be in the basement after our Priceline bid. We have never stayed at a Raddison, but were very impressed with this property. TGI Friday's and a Starbucks on site. Six street is a little too far to walk, but there are cabs and pedi-cabs (bicycle shuttles for two) available. Rooms were very clean, but a little "lived in". Carpet in the hallways needs to be replaced, and the parking garage elevator is a little slow. Be advised that self parking is $15 per night (valet $22) and internet service is $10 per night. Very friendly staff. Front desk and reservations were more than accomodating. Excellent room service and maid service. Newspaper at your door in the morning, and turn down service at night. We'll be back. Austin is such a fun town.

title: “WOW”
text: I have never in life felt so low but treated so kind. My house burned down and I had nothing and looked like nothing but the staff treated me like royalty. Waking up to Ms. Carolyn's warm smile every morning made me feel so at home and she was so encouraging and the staff just made me feel like everything was gonna be alright. they took out time to handle my situation with so much love and care. Also the rooms were sooo clean and the breakfast was wonderful too. Thank you Hampton Inn for this wonderful, touching experience.

title: “Value and Luxury and Great for Families”
text: We had a family reunion in New York, and we had 3 rooms, with a total of 12 people (3 couples and 6 kids). The reservations were easy to do online, and the price was amazing. I was skeptical that somewhere so reasonable could be nice, but I had a few friends personally recommend the Affinia, so I gave it a shot. I was blown away. I couldn't believe the HUGE rooms! We had a beautiful, large living room, with large desk in the office area, a full kitchen, and a separate large bedroom with 2 queens. It was the perfect place for a family of 5. My 3, 6, and 7 year old kids had a great time, and the service was perfect. When you travel with young kids, the full kitchen is a godsend! They could have healthy, inexpensive meals instead of eating out all the time. I would recommend this hotel to anyone. We will definitely stay here whenever we travel to New York.

title: “Very good hotel in excellent midtown location”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the Hilton NY over Christmas weekend. The Hilton is a very large and crowded hotel, but since we arrived very late in the evening there was no problem checking in. In fact, the front desk was nice enough to upgrade us to the 41st floor which allows you complimentary access to a very good continental breakfast and afternoon hors d'oeuvres on the 44th floor. 
The room was cozy, maybe a bit small, but very comfortable; excellent Queen-size bed with comfy linens and comforter, nice view of the City, and plenty of hot water. Some others on this site complained of thin walls, but we couldn't hear anything from the room next door or the hallways. But thankfully our room didn't have a pass-thru to the next room which can allow noise to filter through.
Only glitch was that the free breakfast can get very crowded and the line was so long the first day, that we had breakfast across the street at the coffee shop. It seemed that people from the non-executive floors were also taking advantage of the free breakfast. The second at third mornings were much better and they were checking the room numbers of guests more carefully.
The location of the Hilton can't be beat! Near pretty much everything, especially during the holidays! 5th Ave., Rockefeller Center, Times Sq., Central Park, MOMA, etc. 
I would definitely stay here again!

title: “Terrific Atmosphere”
text: Me and the Wifey had a great time visiting Venice, CA. Staying at the Cadillac was a terrific choice. The convenience of having whatever your needs may be just minutes away..

title: “Amazing view: book top floor!”
text: Spectacular top floor view of Golden Gate Bridge and the Bay. Great central location. We had family room no car. Breakfast was satisfactory. Not cheap but San Fransisco is expensive.

title: “Nice Ritz”
text: Nice, but not great. But the marble and friendly staff made up for it!

title: “very modern, new hotel with great location”
text:
Stayed here for 5 nights. Had a room 1907 which was a corner room with 2 double beds. There was 2 adults and 1 child in the room. THe beds were very comfortable with luxurious bed linen and a choice of soft or hard pillows. It was a regular size for NYC, the two beds in the room, a desk, a small closet with iron and board. You had to clean up after you as it was easy for the room to seem like it was a tip due to the size.
There was a flat screen tv, air conditioning which was lovely as the weather outside was in the 90's. Our room looked south and you could see other buildings. However, some of the rooms did overlook the Empire State building. The hotel is 26th st and 6th ave end. It was 5 mins walk to Penn Station and the nearest subway was 7th ave and 28th st. or broadway and 28th st. There were plenty of deli's nearby so dont worry about the lack of mini bar in the room. There were also ice machines and vending machines on 3 separate floors These had soda, water(2usd) and crisps and sweets. There was also an Olive Garden and McDonalds and Starbucks on 6th Ave. All within 5 mins walk. There was also a nice bar called Rogue where you could sit outside on 6th Ave. This had a nice seating area outside. There was also a bar next door to the hotel that looked nice.
The bathroom had a small bath with adequate shower and small sink with hairdryer and basic toiletries. The towels were fluffy and replaced when required. 
The maids need to look at the rear of the bed though as we found a pair of mans underpants (yes a bit disgusting) and a mens deodrant. I wouldnt let this put you off though as obviously the staff are very new in the hotel. The staff were friendly and they stored our bags for us and sourced us a taxi with enthusiasm.
The reception staff were very friendly and welcoming and tried very hard to keep you happy.The reception was small but hey alls its for is passing through. There was a bar next to reception with comfy sofas and bar stools. They were friendly and offered us lunch or evening menu on the night we ate there. The evening menu was a bit expensive but normal for a hotel in NYC. It was 8usd for a large glass of wine. The food was good and kids ate free and got a free soda. Next to this area was the restaurant which was part of the bar area. I gather this is where breakfast was served.
I used my hubbys priority points for the trip and it was only 15000 a night this is very good for NYC as normally you would need 25000-40000 per night.
There were no safes in the room. However, there were free safety deposit boxes at reception. If you lose the key they charge you 350usd.
On the basement level there was a small gym area and a business centre. There were 2 computers with free internet. This closed at midnight. There was also free wifi in the hotel room if you had your laptop.
Would I stay here again. It would have to be a yes. I would only pay 250 a night max though as i think there is other NYC hotels that have slightly larger rooms,.

title: “High Average is our rating”
text: High average is our rating. It is on the high end of the price scale but location, location, location! You are right there close to it all. It was very, very, very hot - upper 90s all three days but close enough to attractions that at a slower pace we all made it . We did like that Union Station was right there - use it. The room was small but clean and comfortable. Now on to the staff. They were all for the most part nice and very helpul. Then there was one man the best, most helpful and just a very, very, nice human being. WADE, the bellman, is who and what made my stay super good! So if you see WADE, shake his hand and give him a pat on the back and a $5 or $10 in his hand.

title: “I wouldn't consider this place a hotel”
text:
First off.... I AM STAYING IN THIS HOTEL RIGHT NOW.... and I absolutely had to write a review. To be honest, this is the first review I have EVER written on trip advisor.
Let me just say that the word "hotel" has new meaning here. There is a few things you expect at a hotel.
1. Maid service.
2. Clean sheets/towels
3. TOILET PAPER 
4. People at the front desk.
5. Internet that works.
6. Trash bags
7. Soap/shampoo
EVEN MOTEL 6 has this stuff !!!!!! 
You do not get ANY of this at this place. Internet is so spotty that each page thats FOREVER to load. I think they are using some type of cheap DSL wireless router for the whole hotel.
This place really is just.... You pay for the room..and you are on your own after that.
Front desk closes at night. God forbid you want to check in late, you will be sleeping in the parking lot. 
At the bare minimum you should at least get toilet paper and trash bags... NOPE... buy your own...and walk your trash to the dumpster people !
Oh and if you decide to wash your own sheets (you have to because they dont ! ) you need to get tokens for the washing machine. But guess what, if you go downstairs and no one is at the front desk....your out of luck... wait until the next day when they come back to the work...... this includes if you run out of tokens in the middle of doing laundry. 
There is a kitchenette with 2 burners...but guess what... no utensils/plates or pots/pans. Most hotels I have been to have those in the room if you have a kitchen. How do they expect you to cook anything? 
I had to go and purchase it myself. 
Basically this place is exactly what I said earlier in this review. You get a Room to sleep in..... and you are on your own at that point..... Might as well go on craigslist....and find someone's basement.... 
I've been here 2 days... I'm gone tommorrow...can't stand it...
But guess what... you have to pay for the whole week regardless... 
At this point... I don't even care.....
.

title: “Love this Hotel”
text: I really enjoyed my stay at the Warwick, the hotel was beutiful and the staff was terrific. I only wish I could have stayed there longer than the one night.

title: “Great home base for first time in the city”
text:
My husband and I came to New York City for our anniversary weekend. The location is so convenient due to being literally just a few steps from the subway station (34th Herald Square) which will take you anywhere in the city. It is also about a 10-15 min leisurely walk to Times Square or one subway station away. 
We booked directly through the hotel website for a premier queen vs. hotels.com for the same price only for a standard room. If you can get a premier room, I highly reccommend it! We had a large room on 11th floor with high ceilings, a sitting area, desk and fridge. My absolute favorite part of our room was the bathroom, newly rennovated in a European style with high ceilings, walk in shower with 3 shower heads, including a rainfall shower head. The toiletries were from London with a refreshing scent. I had mentioned our anniversary in booking the room, and we were greeted with a botte of champagne and a handwritten note - such a nice touch!
Continental breakast was included in the hotel price in a cozy dining room with fresh bagels, toast, muffiins, yogurt, fresh fruit, coffee, juice, and milk - just enough to get your day started in the city. Free wi-fi was also included in the hotel price. We were invited to a weekly Tuesday wine tasting in the hotel, but didn't get to make it. The bar on the top floor had views of the Empire State building. It was a bit pricey so we didn't stay for a drink, but it is a nice place to stop before your night out. Hotel staff was friendly. For less than $250/night, with all that is included, I think this hotel is a great value for the money in Midtown Manhattan. 
The only cons would be small counter space in the bathroom, and construction heard in the morning. My husband and I are pretty deep sleepers so it didn't bother us. I definitely would reccommend this hotel for another future stay!

title: “Great Experience”
text: We recently stayed at the Hyatt Regency in San Francisco near the Ferry building. Great location if you are interested in the activities at the ferry building or along the piers. Very nice atrium like setting with class you would expect from a Hyatt. The rooms are comfortable and as many times as we have stayed in San Francisco this was one of the quietiest hotels we have stayed at in the city. The noise from the streets i.e. traffic and sirens usually are an issue in San Francisco but we stayed two nights and did not hear any outside noise at night. The hotel also a nice work out room.

title: “Great hotel, near Mag Mile...Loved it!”
text: I was skeptical about this hotel at first, since I'm use to staying right on Mag Mile and since I got such a good rate on Priceline. I'm happy to say that I was proven wrong! This hotel was beautiful and the staff were nice and accommodating. The location was great! We were in the Gold Coast area which is very close to Mag Mile. However, there was a more neighborhood feel. We went to the breakfast place across the street and a place called Tempos a few blocks away. Both places were great! It's a good thing that we are early risers, because there was a line for breakfast every day when we were finished! We went to Tavern on Rush, also across the street, for lunch.
