Great place to people watch! The El station is only a few blocks away, so we could easily get to Wrigley. (Go cubs!) This was also a beautiful area to walk around and there was LOTS of shopping! I will definitely stay here again on my next Chicago trip!

title: “Very nice & brand new accomodation!!!”
text:
Every year I attend to a convention during March/April in San Antonio and my base hotel has been La Quinta Inn San Antonio Convention Center due to its location and price. During March 2011, I saw this new hotel was under construction and having it open already I decided to give it a try.
What I liked the most is the feeling and smell of a brand new hotel. Everything looks perfect and fresh. It's really nice to get to your hotel room and find trendy and modern ammenities, from I-dock for your I-phone to LED light for night reading and USB ports.
Location is perfect, really!. Eventhough you might think is quite far from atracctions (Alamo & Riverwalk) is just 5-8 min walk to the Alamo. As soon as you get off from the hotel, turn to your right and at the corner you will see tha back part of the Alamo, that close is this hotel to the top attraction in SAT!. Then, head to Riverwalk crossing the street and walk down thorugh a nice stairs corridor throughout the Hyatt and then you'll be there at the Riverwalk, a really nice short walk!.
Only downside is that hotel's sole option for parking is by valet, and cost $21.00 USD. I believe is a little pricey (at La Quinta there is an option of selfparking at $18.00 USD). We arrived by late afternoon and we parked our car just in front of the hotel (you just have to be lucky to find a spot!). from 6pm to 8am is free, after you just have to pay $0.25 per hour!!!. We stayed two nights paying roughly $3.00 USD per day!!! just put enough for 10 hours (from 8am to 6pm), nevertheless you wont need your car for sightseeing downtown, everything is walking distance. If you don't find a place to park in front of the hotel, go to the park just meters away and there will be for sure space.
Breakfast is good, with scrambbled eggs and bacon as hot dishes. Lobby and breakfast areas are very nice and relaxing. Check in and Check out was very smooth. Price was also good ($116.00 USD per night plus tax). Room was fair enough in space. I thought it will be bigger, but is comfortable. Mini-living room, work desk and tiny-kitchen are nice. Space where bed is located is limited. Bathroom is big enough. I liked that vanity area is separated from shower, that gives you more flexibility.
In general we were happy tro try this new option in Downtown SA, and we will consider to stay here again next year for sure!.
Bon voyage!

title: “Wonderful!”
text:
I was leery of what I was going to get considering that the arrangement was very last minute (the day before?), but this was the hotel that had the best price for a 3 person room that was available on such short notice. 
I was impressed! The room was clean and very big, the bathroom was wonderfully stocked and the service at the front desk and throughout the hotel was very friendly and willing to assist us.
They have a wireless connection, but if your computer can't pick it up (like mine, haha) they have a courtesy computer in the lobby.
The location is also nice -- you're right next to quite a few karaoke bars and the shopping area on 34th street.
I was moving out of my dorm and used the place to keep my stuff and they were very helpful in getting my things upstairs -- without them, I'm pretty sure the majority of my things would have stayed in the lobby!
I definitely recommend it, and while it may not be the least expensive, you're definitely getting your money's worth!

title: “The free breakfast included is AWESOME!”
text: This hotel is a wonderful choice if you don't want to pay "tourist" prices! It is just far enough away from the city center, yet not too far. Lots of restaurants and shopping close. Good location for jaunts downtown or to Fiesta Texas/Sea World too! I still say the breakfast buffet/made to order omelets are what MAKE this place THE place to stay! There is also a manager's reception at night with appetizers and drinks, but we didn't get to take advantage of that. :( Clean and quiet and have recommended it to anyone who will listen!!!

title: “second time just as great”
text:
This was our second stay at Indigo (the first time this past winter) and it was even better than the first. The suites weren't available this time but the staff was sensitive to our request for that kind of room and put us in an "over sized" queen room. Wonderful! 
I love the hardwood floors at Indigo. The "funky"--used in the best possible way--atmosphere is wonderful, too. 
Everyone is friendly--and you get the sense they mean it too.
Indigo is close to Michigan Ave and lots of restaurants and bars of course. And we had no trouble getting cabs (or there's parking immediately next door).
I can't say enough nice things about Angela and Rhonda (at the front desk) or Scott (the manager)..it's nice to be pampered and they all went to the next level of pampering.
Thanks and we'll be back!

title: “Family”
text: Room was very stuffy when we first arrived. Heater/AC needed work for setting the temperature right. Mold? around fire alarm in bathroom. Baseboard trim in bathroom was a bad job and needs to be redone properly. Pillow too short.

title: “The Standard in NYC”
text: A great hotel- excellent rooms with great amenities and good views...spacious enough considering NYC hotel rooms. Superior, friendly service and the hotel boasts excellent bars for amazing people watching in a cool, trendy neighbourhood. Pillows and sheets were so good - I asked brand names!

title: “Trump knows his stuff!”
text: Went to Chi town for a business meeting, and felt like we had won the lottery in this hotel. Stayed on the spa floor- had the best view of downtown, the river to the lake from this tower room, It was on the curve of the hotwl, so we had a complete wall of glass - ridiculously large room, even had a TV in the mirror in the bathroom so hubby could catch sports while he shaved. You can walk anywhere from here too, but the best was the terrace cafe with music, drinks and a whole lotta view of the entire city,

title: “Holy Cow! Great Hotel!”
text: Wow! The Max lived up to the reviews I read. Cool and Hip; Funky. Truly a wonderful art hotel! How can you not love a hotel playing Niko Case on the background soundtrack??? Excellent front desk service too. We used public transit and the front desk was ever so helpful in pulling up schedules and printing itineraries for us, numerous times. The bar rocked on happy hour and late night beverages and service. Shout out to Craig! Waiter of the year! Downside... Small rooms.... two people cannot pass one another in a typical room; also dark showers after you step UP into the bath rooms. No light above the shower/bath. Could we at least get a candelabra in keeping with the atmosphere? I keed I keed! Overall, most enjoyable and I wouldn't think twice about staying here again.

title: “Perfect!!!”
text: Ive stayed in a lot of hotels in the states and I must say this has been my favourite, its clean, classy and staff very helpful. Location couldnt be better , would definitely stay here again. we only had breakfast in the restaurant but that was excellent I honestly cant recommend this enough , enjoy.

title: “Hate to leave”
text: The only bad thing to say is that at some time yoni have to go home. The service was as good as I have had anywhere, the staff was professional yet not at all stuffy. My wife and I were treated like roylity. It was like a zin oasis in NYC

title: “So close... but the small misses add up”
text:
First, I do want to say that overall our experience at the Yotel was positive. It is a fantastic value with some very nice touches. But there were just enough little problems that prevent me from giving 5 stars.
On the positive:
- Rooms are nicely laid out. Good space for the price.
- The galleys have free filtered water and a free Lavazza machine for coffee and espresso drinks on demand
- Rooms were clean, and housekeeping was efficient
- Every staff member we interacted with were very friendly and helpful
Neutral:
- White decor showed dirt and scuff marks. It is hard to overlook the suitcase scrapes or wear in the spot where the door handles touch the wall.
- Beds are firm. YMMV. We were OK with it, but I can see where others would hate it.
On the negative:
- We had an odor coming from the bathroom - sort of methane odor. While the staff tried to solve it by leaving an ozone machine in the room, that just covered the odor and didn't eliminate it. This was a huge turn off.
- Breakfast service for the non-self-serve sucked. Every thing from messed up orders to 5 of us getting our meals randomly over a span of about 25 minutes. 
- Reading light in the room had a short and would flash. 
- Coffee machine's "spent capsule" bin was often full, meaning you couldn't use the coffee machine.
In the end, what bugged me was that the negatives were really "attention to detail" type problems that are easy to fix. The sheer number of them detracted from the overall experience, which had the potential to be very good.
In the end, I'd still recommend them.

title: “Restaurant closed and no afternoon tea”
text: A gorgeous hotel in every way, close to most sights, incredible beds, very large room with beautiful furniture. The only complaints I have are the fact that there is no hot water or cold water, just lukewarm and marginal water pressure. It may have something to do with the age of the hotel but they should fix the problem. During our three night stay the first week of August, the Willard Room restaurant was closed as well as there being no Afternoon Tea in Peacock Alley. Very disappointing. The heat was unbearable in the city so the hotel was a welcome reprieve. Turn down bed service in the evening with classical music turned on and mints on the bed along with fresh towels and tidying up was lovely. Beautiful flat screen TV. The bathroom could have more useable counter space but that was minor. Would recommend to others.

title: “Good price, excelent location, friendly people!”
text:
The location is great, few blocks from Union square, china town, and also few blocks from Montomery station (wich is great if you want to get there from the airport by BART)
If you don´t want to sepnd a lot of money in your hotel, but you want a clean, safe and freindly place, this is the hotel.

title: “Very well located – not very comfortable”
text: The location of the hotel - just a couple of minutes’ walk from Times Square - is what you pay for when you book it. The design of the lobby is quite interesting but that’s about all. Tiny rooms, walls that are not soundproof, noise from the airconditioning unit outside (bring some earplugs) – those are the main cons I think. Paying for the hotel breakfast is not really worth it as you can eat cheaper and better at one of the many cafes in the area. Free wi-fi is a bonus of course. If comfort is not a priority and you need a hotel just as a starting point to explore NYC and as a place to sleep – then go for it.

title: “Helpful staff, enjoyable stay”
text:
We only stayed one night, arriving early Hotel our room was not ready.I did not expect it to be ready but the staff took our cases and directed us to the lounhge for drinks etc. They even offered us breakfast.We went out shopping and returned later. The room was smaller than expected and did not have a bath. 
That said the room was comfortable and it was only for one night.The free buffet breakfast was great and as we were flying out later that day the staff looked after our luggage and we were allowed to us the lounge through out the day.
All the staff were pleasant and helpful. Would I stay there again? yes I would.

title: “Great, friendly staff”
text: We stayed here for Fiesta week. What a nice surprise to find such a charming and wonderful property. We enjoyed the easy walk to the Riverwalk even more than the free breakfast waffles. Our housekeeper offered great suggestions on things to visit and tour. I think the best part of the property was the rooftop pool and spa. Beautiful views.

title: “A Phoenix Gem”
text: If you have cause to stay in the Avondale area of Phoenix this would be an excellent choice. The property seemed like new condition and the staff is absolutely fabulous, Particularly the breakfast staff. You could not wake to brighter smiles or more pleasant people. The lounge area is quite nice as well with reasonable prices. I have stayed in several Marriott properties and this is one of the best. I am certainly fondest of the Courtyard and Townhome suites properties.

title: “Great Location and Staff”
text: I'm on the road quite a bit for work, and have stayed in plenty of hotels in NYC including the Waldorf, Marriott Marquis, Sharaton, Double Tree etc. The Hilton Garden Inn TImes Square is my favorite. The staff is so friendly and helpful, especially Larry the concierge. Very clean room, and nice touches like hand sanitizer by the elevators, cookies in the lobby and Starbucks coffee in the morning. The location can't be beat, super close to TImes Square, Hell's Kitchen, and most theaters, but you aren't fighting the Times Square foot traffic as soon as you step out of the hotel, only a block from the Subway. I have found my favorite NYC hotel, and will be back!

title: “Perfect!”
text: From the warm personal greeting to the amazingly comfortable bed, our stay could not have been better. They did a great job with the renovation and an even better job with the staff. Everyone was very warm and accommodating.

title: “Good location near Old Town”
text:
We stayed at this hotel after comparing reviews by other travelers and overall were pleased with the hotel. The staff was friendly, and maid service was good. Our room was in the newer section of the hotel, non smoking and on the second floor. Breakfast was fair, consisting of fresh fruit, make your own waffles, cereal, OJ , milk, coffee. Pretty much standard American continental breakfast. Upon check out I was asked if I had a good stay, I agreed, at which time the clerk had rubber stamped the receipt with a notation to leave a comment on TripAdvisor. Just as a previous reviewer noted, I also found it interesting the combination of the three flags outside, Mexican, Californian & US Marine. It would have been nice to see Old Glory flying.
Pros: Nice location close to Old Town, which had some great Mexican food and trinket shops. Staff was courteous, check in was quick and efficient. The pool was small and surrounded by nice vegetation and palms trees, not to deep. Our kids enjoyed the soak. 
Cons: Our biggest complaint would be that the beds in our room felt like you would roll into the center, almost like too many kids had been jumping in the middle. Both beds in the room had this issue. If we had to stay another night I would have looked at another room for better beds, or another hotel. It also would have been nice to have had a small fridge in the room to keep food & drinks cold.

title: “Nice stay for a nice price”
text: We stayed at the Hilton Back Back for 3 nights. I thought the room and bathroom were both clean. We had an issue with the shower on our second night. A quick call to the front desk and someone was at our door within 10 minutes to fix the problem. Afterwards, the front desk called our room to make sure that we were satisified with the repair and if we needed anything else. The staff was very friendly and accomodating. It was a great perk that they offer complimentary luggage storage after check out time as we had approximately 5 hours before leaving for the airport. The front desk staff was helpful with directions and recommendations for dinning and local attractions. It's within a 5 minute walk to Boylston Street and Newberry Street - both are great for dining and shopping. I thought the price was reasonable based on the location. I would stay there again.

title: “Good location and attentive staff and service”
text:
Stayed here for business in April. The hotel is near all of the restaurants in the harbor and about a mile from University of Maryland Medical Center. Check in was quick and painless although once I went upstairs and dropped my bags and came right back down there was a huge line and one front desk attendant. She was good, however, and quickly got things under control.
Breakfast in the morning is free and GREAT. They have ample supply of breakfast sandwiches, waffle maker, and assorted cold and hot cereal. There is also an evening reception. One morning I was running behind schedule and they were closing the breakfast room but the girl allowed me to come in anyway and grab something to go. She was really busy trying to get everything put away so I really appreciated her allowing me in.
I did have a housekeeping issue with my room. Something that looked like blood was on the sheer curtains in my room and in the grout on the bathroom floor. I could sort of see how housekeeping could miss the curtains (I only noticed because I went to close them since my room faced the front of the building and I was on a low floor and needed to change) but I think the reason why it was missed in the bathroom is because housekeeping simply didn't mop it between guests, which I would assume should be policy. I mentioned this to the front desk on my way to work the next morning and upon my return they were EXTREMELY apologetic and offered me a little snack basket for my inconvenience. We all know things happen and their prompt attention to the matter is what most travelers are looking for when choosing a hotel.
I noticed another traveler mentioned the $30/day to park. Perhaps since I'm from Chicago I'm used to exorbitant parking rates although that doesn't make them easier to swallow. Fortunately, I don't need a car when I'm in B'more (my job and favorite restaurants are all within walking distance from the Fairfield in the Harbor)
Due to the attentive staff and great location, I would definitely stay here again when business brings me back to Baltimore.

title: “Excellent Location”
text:
Walking distance to most attractions - Elevator opens up to door on the Riverwalk - 
When in San Antonio try and eat at Schilos (She-lows) - One and one-half blocks from the front door of Hotel Palacio and priced very reasonable.
Pat O'Briens - Appetizers one-half price after 4:00 p.m. Gator Bites are "Great"

title: “Mixed feelings”
text:
On arrival at the hotel the exterior was covered in scaffolding so it's not very easy to see or appealing to the eye at the moment. We arrived only about one hour before check in time after an incredibly long day of travelling and fighting our way up about 20 blocks through the crowds of Times Square with heavy suitcases desperate to get into our room. There was one member of staff on check in and a huge queue. We were told quite simply and abruputly by a member of staff that the room wasn't ready. We quickly got used to the extremely rude and abrupt attitudes by most new york service staff we encountered.. Manners and a friendly smile cost nothing. The locals were always very friendly and helpful though.
When we eventually got into the room on the 15th floor there was no sofa bed made up (there were 3 of us). The last thing you want to do after a long day of travelling is make up a bed. We couldn't find any bedding and had to phone down and ask where it was. Be warned -the "mattress" on the sofa bed is awful - you can't even call it a mattress. It is bare springs. I would not expect this from a 4 star Hilton never mind a hostel. We asked for a room with 2 beds instead and were told there were none and were offered a mattress topper which we had to accept. We also encountered quite a rude guy working at the bell desk who couldn't ask for a tip fast enough before we had even given over our cases - we would have given a tip when picking the cases up and this was really offputting.
The hotel is right in the thick of Times Square like others say - it's always incredibly busy. It's an interesting experience but if I went back I'd definitely stay in a different area. Maybe in a smaller hotel with a more friendly and welcoming feel. The plus side is definitely the extra room especially if there are more than 2 of you in a room. It also has quite a few subway stations surrounding it so it is easy to get back to after days of sightseeing.

title: “Good base for sightseeing”
text:
We were happy with a king suite on the 4th floor of the 30th street building. The room was large and well kept. The staff was helpful and friendly.
A lot of walking is unavoidable for seeing the museums and monuments. The Metro is close, but does add a 10 minute walk. The Circulator bus is 2-1/2 blocks from the hotel and goes within walking distance of the National Portrait Gallery. 
The free breakfast downstairs takes less time than eating out, leaving more time for sightseeing. The neighborhood has a many restaurants. We only saw one chain restaurant.

title: “Best Valentines Day at your beautiful, historic hotel.”
text: We stayed 3 nights on the 17th floor and everything was perfect. While the room was a bit small it was very clean and comfortable. Used the concierge service at least 3 times for directions, restaurant recommendations and they were always very helpful and accurate. We had a wonderful and memorable wknd and I highly recommend your hotel. Thank you for everything, we will be back!

title: “Great value, and conveniently located near everything”
text:
Stayed here for a week for business.
1) Located right next to the arena and bus station
2) Friendly staff and cleaning crew
3) Modern decor and decent layout
4) Wifi was above avg in speed
5) CVS and other food/restaurants nearby
6) Decent selection of food from the bar/room service
7) Great free breakfast (omelet station, continental breakfast, etc)

title: “Just okay”
text:
Was here for business - not my first time at the hotel - and was surprised to see the property was a little, well, ragged and worn. (personally, I wondered if the newer Hilton down the road is getting all the love...) 
Room service food was marginal, and even though I have gold status with Hilton, I was uncertain what benefit I should have been receiving for it. And not to be too picky, but the fact that there's no wi-fi in the rooms (common area in lobby only) makes it unlike most properties, new OR older. 
Oh, and when the concierge isn't there (and they keep limited hours), nobody seems to know anything. 
The noise from the train - which I faced - wasn't too much of an issue as I've stayed in this area many times and have grown used to it. BUT - the thumping loud music from the Hard Rock hotel, which I was told can go on until 1:30 a.m.? Not cool.

title: “LOVED this hotel! Can't wait to come back!!”
text: Beautiful lobby, great location, gorgeous room!! Can not say enough good things!! I WILL be back!

title: “So-So”
text:
When I stayed here I chatted with an employee and got some inside info....The vending machines were all removed so you have to go to the gift shop and pay $2.50 for a soda or even more for room service. The restaurant (awful) does not use their a/c and always pretend that it "just went out". They do not let you into your rooms even a minute before 4:00 because it is financially better for them (no electricity used ahead of time, you spend $ at the gift shop or restaurant- where they tell you to go while you wait for your room). I would not stay in the bungalows even if they were free of charge. Absolutely motel 6 and everything that implies. The non-tower rooms seem to belong to a different hotel. When my a/c would not work after 2 hours of trying the maintenance guy said he would just bring us a fan because the a/c s were old and didn't work all that well. Oh no he DIDN'T think I'd be paying big $$$ to use a house fan. We got a quick and free upgrade to a tower room and many apologies from a very helpful, friendly front desk person (Amanda).
The ugly :The fridges in both rooms barely worked, the carpets were stained, room service was totally inept both meals. You need to put personal items on a lounge chair by the pool at 6 or 7 or you will be sitting on the cement next to someone's chair. The cushions on the chairs are disgusting- sweaty, oily, bird poopy. $23 for parking is unreal in this area. Smokers paradise- people smoking all around pool and landscaped sitting areas.
The good: Best front desk service I have ever had, good valets, view of Sea World fireworks every night, kid's slide in pool (although many oiled up sun tanning adults liked to use it, I wish it was for kids only), view of marina from tower room, awesome landscaping outdoors. Great discounts when booking through the zoo or Sea World websites.

title: “Great hotel for everyone.”
text: What a great hotel. Great location, right in the center of the city for shopping and across the street from a beautiful park for the kids. We stayed here for a week and the concierge was amazing. Everything from food delievery from specialty restaurants(sometimes we just wanted to eat in and watch t.v.) to lending us a baby carriage and helping to locate shops and sight seeing recommendation. Always with a smile. Gave us water for the drive down to Carmel. Would recommend it anytime.

title: “Outstanding Hotel!”
text:
I can't say enough for this hotel. My friends and I were treated like Kings and Queens. I've never stayed at a hotel where the goal of the staff is to make every one of your desires and whims come true.
My girlfriends and I, shared a two bedroom suite. We had 6 of us ladies sharing this suite and we had room to spare. Two good size bedrooms with very comfortable queen size beds and a living room with a sofa bed. We also had two full bathrooms and a wonderful apartment size kitchen with the works.
We had traveled from all over the states to see a concert and the Hollywood Bowl, and they knew about this and welcomed us with a special card and some nice little treats and candies. They also provided us with a 6-pack of Coca Cola.
After the concert, we were all very hungry, the young man working the front desk ordered pizza for us to be delivered on the patio by the pool. It was a perfect way to end the day.
If I am ever in Hollywood again, this will be my choice from now on for a hotel.
Gretchen and staff are incredible! 5 Star treatment with a 3 Star price. Doesn't get much better than that.

title: “Nice staff but not clean”
text: We stayed at the Clarendon for three nights this past week (March 7, 8, and 9th) and overall, we were disappointed. The desk staff were nice and provided free munchies and drinks after 10:00 pm and the restaurant had fairly good food. The restaurant also provided some entertainment, fantastic Flamenco dancers one evening. The room was average, with a tub that needed repairs, but what was most disappointing was the cleanliness. We stayed there three nights and the sheets were never changed. I actually put a note on the bed the third day, asking for the sheets to be changed and the housekeeper ignored the note. Later that night I called the desk and explained that our note was ignored and that we would like our sheets changed and that request was also ignored. When we checked out yesterday, I shared my concern again and we were told that it was their policy to change sheets daily, but as we left, it seemed like the desk clerk was not going to make any attempt to rectify the situation. We will not go back.

title: “great service”
text: we just completed a weekend stay at the Fairfax. clean rooms, good location near dupont and great service from the manager kent. thanks!

title: “Hidden Gem”
text: I visit Philadelphia for work and stumbled upon this place by chance. The staff was very friendly and my hotel room was absolutely perfect! I found myself speaking to one of the managers during their breakfast and she told me how it was a restorerd historic landmark with tons of history. They have gorgeously warm common areas and a very charming courtyard to sit and enjoy. That evening I asked for dinner recommondations and they pointed out one of there three buildings was a restaurant which I tried and loved! By far best experience I have ever had in Philadelphia. I consider myself a foodie but they really opened my eyes to how much fun food can be! Very excited to visit again.

title: “Completely Enjoyable”
text: Great service. A block from Union Station allowing for an easy walk for train riders. They allowed us to check in early and held our bags after checkout so we could walk around until our train departed. Great food. Highly recommend.

title: “#1 Experience in service”
text: From top notch staff that rarely changes - like Kolby who is a service genius- to perks like the wine hour set the Eventi apart. The vibe is cool w/o being pretentious - I only stay here when in NYC

title: “Jury's was good”
text: Stayed here with my teenage son from 20th October for 5 days during some unexpectedly warm weather. Really enjoyed our stay. Comfortable rooms, friendly staff, good location. Had 3 breakfasts which added to our costs but very enjoyable. Good restaurant called "Laurel" just next door in Berkley St. Would stay again.

title: “This is the best hotel in Denver”
text:
I have been meaning to write a review of the Hotel Teatro for a number of months. I travel to Denver fairly frequently and I always stay at the Hotel Teatro. From the welcome at the front door, to the wonderful front desk team, to the amazing rooms there is no better place to stay. The service in a hotel like this is everything. Just before Christmas this year I had a car accident while driving to Denver. When I finally made it to the hotel I mentioned what a horrible day I had had. I left the hotel to head to an event, but when I returned to the hotel later that evening the hotel staff sent a bath butler to my room to run me a hot bath to help with my whip lash. That is 5 star service. They remember me every time I check in and are always so kind. I have offtern recommended the hotel to friends and everyone who stays there loves it. 
Thank you to all the staff at the Teatro who always make my trips to Denver wonderful. You are the best.
P.S. They have the best beds and linens!!

title: “Long weekend stay for MCM”
text:
The good points:
1 Great Location
2 Quiet AT Night
3 Suite was huge and well equipped 
The bad
Room service breakfast never appeared.
Downstairs restaurant was too expensive for the amount and quality of food (breakfast) eat out!!
 Coffee grinder would not work and complimentary creamer/sugar was lacking
Shower was tired and needed refitting.
The place was great for a base. The quality of the sleep, brilliant!!
If you're coming in via Dulles, get the 5A bus from the far right of the upper level. It costs exactly $6 (no change given) to Rosslyn Metro station, then literally one stop on the Metro to Foggy Bottom.
Coming out of the Metro, turn right and right again (back on yourself) through a short pedestrian area and keep walking to 25th Street, turn right, and it's on your left.
From Ronald Reagan, Blue and Orange line take you to Foggy Bottom.
The better amenities are found by walking back up to the Metro, but keep going past it 
Would I stay there again? Yes.....

title: “Location is key”
text: While taking my daughter to visit colleges in DC we booked a room using Priceline. We named our price $200 and were booked at this hotel. When we checked in we asked to extend the stay by another night and were able to negotiate a price for $239. This is a classy hotel in a great location, but I call these hotels the nickel and dime hotels. No free internet, $12.95 for 24 hours. No wi fi lobby even. No breakfast. The Starbucks is fine, unless you like spending $40 for two for breakfast. Since we had driven from Chicago we had to park our car while at the hotel. The parking is $38 per night, includes tax. Fairly normal for parking in the city. The concierge at thehotel was very well informed regarding colleges as he is doing a PhD at Georgetown. He was also helpful regarding restaurants. Try DC Coast across the street and Old Ebbits Grill a few blocks away. When we left the parking valet took 50 minutes to retrieve my car. I had an appointment 3 hours away and lost valuable time waiting for the car. The doorman, Pierre, took his own initiative to call the manager over and she credited my account for the two nights of parking. Mistakes happen, but it is the right thing to do to immediately correct them. I appreciated the way this was handled and will stay there again. The ceiling in the bathroom was patched and peeling and it should have been repaired a bit better, otherwise the room was fine.

title: “Really comfortable hotel”
text: Good location. Good sized rooms for New York. Helpful staff.

title: “Great Value”
text:
Plus: very large rooms, light breakfast is included, good location on Broadway, prices are great.
Minus: not a five-star hotel, it's a bit faded and chipped around the edges; the free wifi in the rooms is unreliable.
I liked the Milburn and would stay there again. NYC hotels in this price range generally do not offer breakfast or have such large rooms. I would like to see some of the old furnishings get updated and the wifi system is terrible, it often goes off at night, so if you plan to work from your room, it's a gamble whether you can get online.

title: “Excellent hotel”
text:
Stayed at this hotel for 2 nights. Booked it because of its great reviews on trip advisor, location, price, and good reputation of Shell properties. Parking rates were significantly lower than most of the hotels in the area, and it also offered free wi-fi (most of the 5 star hotels charge a fee for internet access) . (The only disappointment was the internet as it was dreadfully slow and frustrating to use. There was a computer for guest's use in the lobby area, and this seemed to be faster than the wi-fi in the room.)
Overall we were very satisfied, and the hotel met all of our expectations. The room was very spacious, bed was especially comfortable, and location was fantastic. There was free tea, coffee, and hot chocolate available on the 10th floor, with a lounge . The concierge was available to assist with any sightseeing and booking of restaurants and entertainment, but we didn't require any of these services. We enjoyed the welcome wine and cheese reception on Friday late afternoon, and we were very pleased that there were no sales pitches for the Shell time share properties, which is a common feature when we have stayed at timeshare resorts.
It was noisy at night from the street below, but this seemed to be an issue from the reviews for any downtown hotel .
It would definitely be our first choice of hotels when we return to San Francisco.

title: “attemped to use groupon and received terrible customer service.”
text:
I had a horrible experience attempting to use a groupon at the Brookshire Suites. The blackout dates listed on the groupon are only the beginning of the restrictions. Once the Brookshire Suites has sold an unspecified amount of rooms for any given day they will prohibit customers from using a groupon on that day, even though rooms are still available. 
Long story short, I now have paid for a night at this hotel via groupon that I can't use, even though they have availability. When I spoke to reservations about my situation, they said they couldn't help me, and referred me to Andrea at guest services. Andrea is apparently the assistant manager at the hotel, but she insisted she could not do anything to accommodate me, even though I was coming from out of town, and even though I had previously made a reservation online at the full price. She recognized that they were not sold out, but "likely would be" and refused to make any exception. She explained that the "Revenue Manager" sets the prices and blackouts, and he adds blackouts as he sees fit. 
As someone who has traveled extensively, I was appalled at the lack of customer service I received during this entire experience. I will not stay at the Brookshire Suites knowing how little they value their customers.

title: “Great stay at the Rivercenter”
text: We had an excellent stay at the Marriott rivercenter! Luxurious down Feather bedding and a very spacious king bedroom! I had only one complaint the intire time, there was an odor comming from the sink drain, which happens from time to time, I asked them to put bleach or some other disinfectant down the drain to get the odor out and they did, No more odor!! It was great! A+++++

title: “Great location and value”
text:
My husband and I stayed here for a long weekend. It was great! We booked for 
79/night on priceline, but upgraded to a king bed room. We were on the 16th floor, with views over union square area. It was quiet, clean,beds were super comfortable, and service was great. They have great room service coffee! I would definately stay here again.

title: “Sometimes someting goes right...”
text:
The hot and cold reviews for the Sir Francis Drake are amazing. They scared us a bit. We had stayed there in several of its configurations. Generally the experience was good.
This time I asked for some special arrangements for a welcome in the room as we were arriving the afternoon of the Thursday of the Thanksgiving weekend. Every detail that had been confirmed by e-mail had been looked after beautifully.
True, the hotel is a landmark. That means lots of “quirky” things can be expected. Like a room that could not accommodate bedside tables, and limited space in the bathroom so room robes were available only upon request. Lots of coats of paint on old doors. Definitely not glossy and new – but clean, very well appointed, and with great views and location. Our Expedia price was $131Canadian for a king deluxe on a higher floor. That included all entertainment and WIFI. 
When we phoned for robes- we were expecting the standard issue white. However some wilder designer seemed to have taken over with terry cloth animal prints. Definitely quirky. But in an oddly nice and offbeat way
 This accommodation, combined with a transportation pass that allowed for hopping on and off all cable cars and buses as much as we wanted for a daily rate, made for a memorable stay.
Bottom line – we would go back

title: “Bad sign when they have earplugs on the night stand.”
text:
We stayed here for one night after a 40+ hr trip from Australia. The hotel is next door to a train track and the trains blow whistles all night. We were exhausted so it didn't bother us but if we were vacationing the location would be unacceptable. 
The AC in the room was off when we arrived so it was very stuffy and it took a long time to cool off. Halls are very stuffy.
This is an older hotel, not as nice as a usual Hampton.

title: “Nice but overrated”
text:
We travel a good bit and usually choose to stay at boutique hotels when we do, so have a wide variety of similarly-styled hotels to compare this one to. The hotel was beautifully appointed, in a fabulous location in downtown Memphis, and had all the infrastructure one would expect in this type of hotel. The staff was very pleasant and quick with a greeting in all areas of the hotel. The martini bar is a must-stop if you are in Memphis, but you don't have to stay there to do it. Where we felt things fell short was in the extra service that you expect in a hotel of this type and in this price range.
We attempted to make arrangements with the concierge to have some extra items placed in the room to celebrate a birthday and had difficulty getting a response leading up to our stay. After some complaint she corrected that by being very responsive, but in the end our request was not met even though we had complained. (We had to call again after arrival, which eliminated the whole point of the surprise). The service at the breakfast was abysmal - we waited for some time to be seated, and then it was over 20 minutes before someone returned to the table to even offer us a menu or coffee. Another 30 minutes later the food came - for a continental breakfast. Checkout was slow and chaotic and the valet brought the wrong car down.
This hotel has everything it would take for it to be on the level with, say, W Hotels or other Leading Small Hotels we've stayed at in the chain, but if you're looking for specialized service for the price, look elsewhere.

title: “Very nice, quaint get away spot”
text:
I took my wife to San Diego for Valentines day. We stayed in a newly renovated suite. It was spacious, clean, attactive and relatively inexpensive. 
As it was part of a timeshare chain, we were unfortunalely solicited for a unit. Other than that service was good.
Located close to bars, restaurants and otehr attractions.

title: “not bad”
text: stayed here solo for a business trip and all i can say is that this hotel is average, pretty good service and value. but sorry don't think i'm coming back again, unless there's promotions or something.

title: “San Francisco vacation”
text: Excellent hotel, perfect location, close to union square, big mall, groceries stores, restaurants and market street. Close to the hotel you can take the bus or cable car to pier 39 and to the golden gate. the staff is profesional and friendly. the room was perfect, beatifull,clean and quiet. The fitness room has everything you need.

title: “Best deal in Manhattan”
text: Typically we opt for 4 star, boutique hotels, but we were travelling with our two children (ages 9 & 8), and we wanted to cut on expenses. This was a great deal for families. The location was great, close enough to Times Square and theaters that our kids walked to w/o complaints. The rooms are clean and redone. Bathroom, however is small. The free breakfast was a plus, very simple eggs, toast, cereal, fruit, pastries... But a good savings to get you started for the day. U can even get a bagged bkfst-to-go, for example, if you are venturing out to a tour for the day. Although I lived in NYC for 1 year, we opted for a double decker tour for the kids. The pick up point is a few blocks from the hotel, so that was perfect. The hotel offers free use of a desktop and printer for online ticket printouts, etc. they also offer free coffee and hot chocolate throughout the day, and cookies. I was skeptical but very happy with the hotel. Our room was on the 2nd floor, street side, but relatively quiet. Would stay there again.

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text: The hotel was beautiful. The beds were very comfortable. The location was great. Lots of eating places near the hotel. The fitness room was very clean and had new equipment. The hotel staff was very professional, courteous and helpful. I definitely would rate this as a 4-5 star hotel. We really enjoyed our stay there and would not hesitate to go back. Would definitely recommend this hotel.

title: “Bad management! Shame to Hilton Hotel”
text: NO AIRCONDiTION on my room! And supposedly it is not. Enough reason for them to transfer me! So what, if you dont have available room? You have to compensate better for your flaw! The rate i paid is for a room with A/C not with a fan. Since you are not meeting the expectation, you should do something abt it! I was sweating!!!in a Hilton Hotel! My car is even cooler than the room! Very bad management! I didnt come here for the food so no need to offer the breakfast! I paid for a nice room not a room with MAlFUnCtIon aircondition and a NOISY electric fan! So demeaning!!!

title: “Very Good Hotel”
text:
Check-in: Hotel has a nice and welcoming staff at checkin desk. I arrived to hotel at 9:00 am and requested an early check-in if possible. There was no empty room for booked room-type so I accepted to wait till afternoon. But then the lady at the front desk checked again for other room times and complementarily upgraded my room with an early check-in.
Room: With the upgrade my room was the way larger than I need. It was a 2 bedroom suit with a sitting area and kitchenette. I only use a bedroom and it was super-clean. The bed was comfortable and I definitely had a good sleep quality. Rooms don't have free wireless internet but hotel lobby has. So if you'd like to work from your room, you need to pay extra for internet.
Check-out: It was quick and easy with no problem.
Location: If you're here for business trip it is great, close to everything in Manhattan. If your destination is Grand Terminal, it is very close to hotel. As you're in Manhattan, you have good choices for food.

title: “Beautiful Vacation, awesome hotel”
text: My new bride and I stayed here for our honey moon and the hotel certainly helped make it a special and memorable occasion. From the ocean front room, the friendly staff, and the comfortable rooms—our stay was amazing and truly helped make our honeymoon special. The location is also great as there are plenty of restaurants and outlet stores within walking distance. The staff went above and beyond to make us feel welcome and appreciated.

title: “Basic, No-frills, Great location”
text: We got a great deal for The Manhattan at Times Square through Priceline. Location and price were the most important criteria for us for this Thanksgiving trip. After reading mixed reviews, we didn't have high expectations. The location was perfect...2-3 blocks from the center of Times Square, and the Thanksgiving parade passes directly in front of the hotel. The bidding process got us in at the price we were looking for...but as with most NYC properties, parking was not included and it is expensive, although convenient (right under the hotel). The hotel is rated 3-stars on Priceline and I generally agree with that rating. The hotel is outdated, but clean. Small rooms - typical for NYC. Comfortable beds, clean linens (we did not see any bedbugs). The only amenity worth mentioning is the pool which was a treat for the kids. Overall it was fine and considering what we paid, a bargain for the location at the time of year we traveled.

title: “Not as nice as pre-Sandy”
text: I have stayed at this hotel several times in the past and had excellent service and enjoyed the extras the hotel provided. However, this visit was disappointing. Although the lobby does not appear damaged, they no longer offer free wine from 6 to 8 pm in the lobby although you can purchase it in the restaurant for $14 a glass. There is no longer coffee or tea or snacks in the lobby area. When I inquired, the hotel staff said that I could get one upstairs in the restaurant. I did but then found out that there was a $3.50 charge to take out a coffee/tea. I might as well go to Starbucks. I did not get my wakeup call one morning and the one service call I made wasn't fulfilled. I am a platinum Hyatt member, so I used to be offered turn down service each night but not once was it offered on this trip. I did receive a room upgrade as a platinum member but a coworker received a room downgrade. The gym is unavailable but you can use the gym next door. It is fine but you need to bring picture ID with you and sign in. I complained to the hotel manager about the service issues when I left. She promised my some additional points to make up for this but they never were added to my account. I think that I will go to another hotel on my next visit.

title: “Everything you need!”
text:
This was our second and third stay in this great motel. We found this place 2 years ago and liked it for its great value and clean rooms. This year we came back for 2+2 nights at the beginning and ending of our CA roundtrip. Conclusion: we liked the place even more. The whole dolphin team including the owners gave us a lot of advice for San Diego and were very friendly, the rooms were as clean and well-equipped as we remembered them and we got to know the area around the hotel better. We found a really nice restaurant "Pomodore" at Avenida del Portugal and a very nice bar "the pearl" just around the corner. You can walk there!
Overall, we will be back next time and are already looking forward.

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
Fantastic hotel. Superb location, right on the Riverwalk. Old style, yet modern. It is located at the very beginning of the string of fantastic restaurant's on the Riverwalk.
Room was very clean, tastefully done, comfortable with an LCD TV. 
Valet parking is very expensive at $28/day, but right across the street is a parking lot that goes for $7/day.
The Majestic Theater is one block away. Riverwalk is right out the back door. This hotel shares an exercise facility with the Watermark hotel right across the Riverwalk and it's fantastic, on the 8th floor, with pool and hot tub up there as well. Most downtown attractions are within walking distance from La Mansion.
I recommend using Priceline, as we got the room for $100/night com[pared to Expedia's $234/night.

title: “A Good Place For San Francisco Newbies”
text:
Just back from four pleasant nights at the Tuscan Inn. Some folks might be put off by this hotel's Best Western affiliation. Don't be. This is a real hotel, not some plastic motel at an interstate exit. 
I'd recommend this property, especially to first-time San Francisco visitors. It's modern, clean, efficient, comfortable, and professionally run with courteous staff. On your second visit you might opt to stay a greater distance away from the tourist schlock of Fisherman's Wharf. (The hotel is about 2 blocks south of all the buzz on the Wharf, so don't worry about hordes of tourists lurking about.) Or, like me, if you've been to the city several times, you might choose to stay here because it is so close to transportation: A bus stop is right across the street; one cable car turnaround is literally around the corner and another is a few blocks away, and the Pier 41 ferries are a 5-minute walk away, as is a streetcar line. (You know all those warnings not to drive in SF? Pay attention! Don't Drive. You'll be having fun while some other poor sod is looking for a parking space that isn't there.)
Although I didn't notice much of an authentic Tuscan note, my queen bed room was Europeanly small. Not cramped or inaccessible, just compact. (I had a glimpse at a king room, which was larger. More later.) The bed was comfortable, the closet and storage space was sufficient for one or two people traveling light, and the bath was not cramped. If there are two of you and several bags, plan on stacking most of the bags in a corner of the room.
The room had a few annoying decorative items -- like a four-foot long round pillow carefully placed at the same location on the bed by the maid every day -- that seemed spawned by a marketing maven. Apparently, all the rooms are similarly afflicted. Oh yeah, if you don't like mirrors, go elsewhere. One entire wall is covered with mirrors.
The restaurant on the premises is the Cafe Pescatore. Breakfast there was fine, but I ate elsewhere for lunch and dinner. The cafe is comfortable and service was attentive and polite. Plan on spending $15-$20 on breakfast.
Room service at the hotel is limited: Breakfast items from the Cafe and lunch or dinner from a neighboring pizza joint, But, hey, this is San Francisco. Why are you eating in your room?
The hotel provides complementary coffee and biscotti in the morning and hosts a winetasting in the late afternoon, 
If you forget something, a Walgreen's, a Safeway and a Trader Joe's are each about a block away. A large Barnes and Noble bookstore is even closer, if you're in need of caffeine and a book to read on the flight home. The rest of the immediate neighborhood seemed safe and nondescript, and largely free of the homeless and the street people that are in evidence elsewhere in this costly city.
Other's have urged requesting an interior room overlooking the courtyard. They're right. Streets in the neighborhood carry a lot of traffic, and rooms on the streetside might be too noisy for your tastes. (This isn't unique. Traffic is heavy almost everywhere in SF.) I'd booked an interior courtyard room with a king bed, calling the day before I arrived to reiterate the request. However, I was given a streetside room and I could hear the noise before I unlocked the door. After complaining back at the desk, I was switched to a quiet queen room overlooking the courtyard.

title: “All what you get is the location”
text: Rooms are very small. Staff not helpful at all. My shower was broken. I asked for a fix, they use tape to tie the shower head to the wall, really?

title: “Nice Hotel”
text:
We stayed at this hotel pre and post a Mexican riviera cruise. It was great as it is right across the street from the cruise dock. However as we are elderly and had a lot of luggage we asked for a shuttle ride to the ship and were accommodated. We had a bay front room and it was great looking across the harbor and we could see the airplanes coming and going from the airport. 
Staff were all friendly and helpful. 
Someone mentioned the trains. They are nearby, however they did not wake us up during the night. Maybe we are heavy sleepers. We did hear them early in the morning. We did hear a couple of dogs but they didn't wake us either... i mention this if you are adverse to pets in hotels.

title: “Friendly and Comfy”
text:
I had booked this room for one night Sunday May 20th through Monday May 21st. I had done alot of research for our post-cruise stay and The Pearl seemed in a good central area and price wasnt bad. I made a reservation on booking.com for $200 before tax for a Deluxe Queen Room about a month before we came out. I kept checking prices but this was the best price for the 4 stars it gets
Check-in is usually 4 pm, but when we arrive at 10:30 am, they upgraded us, for free, to a Deluxe King on the ninth floor. The reception was friendly and they let us know about the included breakfast and the wine hour at 4-5. We had to sign a contract saying NO SMOKING or they will fine you $300. Total with tax was $237.
After staying in a tiny interior cabin on our cruise, this room seemed enormous. You walk into the living room, which has a couch, chair, table with phone and TV, look straight back and there is a kitchen area with Keurig machine, microwave, sink and mini-fridge. There are 2 closets, with a free safe and 2 robes
The bathroom has a TV, bathtub, separate shower with detachable shower head and rain forest faucet on the ceiling. The bed was super soft with three pillows. The window was huge and the curtains blocked out the sun very well. There was a TV, a desk, an alarm clock, a cordless phone and another closet.
They had alot of pay-per-view and the normal news channels but they also had some good channels like TNT CW etc We went to the wine hour, where they have someone serving either red or white wine. There was a counter with cheese, crackers, fresh fruit (perfectly ripe strawberries, bananas, oranges and blueberries) cookies and apple juice. It was on the second floor, overlooking the reception area, with lots of couches chairs and tables for socializing, as well as fast, FREE Wi-Fi through-out the hotel.
When we checked out at 12:05, they gave us the list of charges, which was the same as check-in. They asked if we wanted to store our bags, which we did. Its free, but we tipped when we picked them up. Alot of the time we would stop by and hang out in reception using the Wi-Fi to find coupons or directions. They never gave us dirty looks or anything, even after we checked out. 
It was right by the Subway and close enough to Time Square to walk, but not be disturbed by the noise. The fire house is kinda close by, but I wasnt too disturbed at night

title: “Good location & value, poor housekeeping”
text:
We needed a hotel for 7-10 days in the Madison Square Park area (23rd/5th) and, having stayed at a Wyndham before, thought that this one would be good, particularly at less than $150 per night in NYC. The room (on the 6th floor) is a fairly-typical example of what you'll find in the price range - quite small, but with a decently-outfitted bathroom.
Upsides - location, morning paper (get there early, or they're gone!), access to concierge, comfortable beds/pillows, nice restaurant attached.
Downsides - paper-thin walls (easy to hear neighbors conversation and elevator noises), very loud heating/AC unit (very loud on/off sounds), one small wardrobe that was not deep enough to accept a hanger (cabinet doors won't close with items on hangers in place), bathroom fan did not function (no apparent switch), and little things like no coat hooks and only one towel bar in the bathroom (where do you put towels after use?).
Biggest downside was that the room was not properly cleaned - specifically, vacuumed - during our entire stay. After 4 nights, we told the management that this was the case. For the next 2 days following this (and after being told that this would be taken care of), we came back each evening to find that nothing was done. I then asked for a vacuum cleaner to be delivered to the room so that I could vacuum it myself. After the cleaner arrived, I found out that the problem was in the cleaner itself - it would only pick up dirt if held at a particular angle, and there were no attachments to get into areas such as the area between the nightstands and the bed, so these areas were filthy and I could not get to them myself. Why the cleaning staff did not tell this to the management, I can't say, but so much for pride in your workplace...
Anyway, we won't be staying here again. I can't say that this is the case with every room and every floor, but since we come on extended stays, we don't want to take the chance again.

title: “Wonderful and unique hotel with great service and style.”
text: I was concerned before my visit by some of the negative reviews on the Hudson Hotel, but was immediately put at ease by the wonderful staff. Each employee I had contact with was professional and courteous. The vibe of the entire lobby and bar area was cool, urban, and very much what one would want in midtown Manhattan. The rooms had a more European feel, which was a relief from typical American chains. I slept comfortably and heard no sounds from the hallway or neighboring rooms. The location was great, with many restaurants and bars within walking distance. I will absolutely being staying at the Hudson on my next trip to New York.

title: “Worst Hotel Experience Ever”
text: Absolutely one of the worst hotels I have ever stayed at. Stayed in room 210 and noticed the first cockroach in the bathroom within the first 10 minutes of being there. That should have been my cue to leave but decided one bug wasn't bad. Boy was I wrong. There were several cockroaches throughout the entire room including the area by the sink, in the refrigerator, and crawling along the floor. Owner/manager could care less about the complaints about it. Do yourself a favor and staty elsewhere!

title: “Excellent location!!!!! Near TSQ, Central Park, Meatpacking.... 110% recomendable!!! From Argentina.-”
text:
We didn´t need to take to many subways because of the location despite we were a family with two kids... The self-landry was a good point...the breakfast...all... One of my kids loved the chocolate muffins and the staff when i asked, try to find me one because it was so hard to caught one during the breakfast....So delicius!!!!!!!
We love NYC....we were in differents hotels before...but we would definitly will try to come back to The Staybridge!!!!!
From Argentina.-

title: “Especially good for city walkers!”
text: For people interested in more than Sea World who like to explore on foot, this hotel is centrally located and offers great value. It is situated at the start of the bars, restaurants, and entertainment on gentrified 5th Ave., a stone’s throw from the Westfield Horton Shopping Plaza where tour buses stop. Walking a bit further brings you to the convention center and touristy waterfront. Taxis to must-visit Balboa Park are around $10. We were able to book a very large top floor suite for a weekday rate of less than $200 per night. The small staff who rotate through the front desk were friendly and in our case exceptionally helpful. The hotel’s self-serve breakfast is modest but provided on the roof top (part of which is under cover) where the view more than compensates. We found this historic property to be clean and well maintained… very easy to recommend.

title: “Great hotel”
text: Stayed here for 8 days in July and loved it! Everything is clean and new. The best beds in the world! Staff is superfriendly and helpful. Our room was in 3rd floor but couldn't hear anything from the street or from the restaurant above. I highly recommend this hotel!!!!

title: “Very nice place!”
text: We stayed at the Parc55 for 3 nights. HUGE benefits to this hotel is that the BART train is only a couple hundred feet from the hotel and the Trolly is only about half a block. The Hertz only being about 2 blocks away is also very convenient. The hotel itself was very nice. There's a ton of elevators to waiting for one isn't a big issue. The Fitness Room is well stocked with treadmills. ellipticals, free weights and pretty much every type of weight lifting machine there is. Overall it is a very nice place!

title: “Great value unbeatable location friendly staff”
text:
Triple A rate 102/night nicely furnished rooms with friendly staff and a huge star bucks in lobby You will not get a better value on mchigan avenue. The walls were a little thin and some women were fighting @230 am but no other problems. We would go back and stay a couple of nights for a Chicago getaway.
Cannot beat this hotel's location!

title: “Great Place, Perfect Location”
text: Totally happy with my stay here. Cool, kitchy decor (yes other reviewer, it's meant to be!) and the place has a pulse. Walking distance to most of the parts of DC that I wanted to be near. My dog loved it too. :)

title: “Great experience”
text: I stayed at Affinia 50 for work, then spent two additional days there as a tourist. It was a great experience. The location was excellent for getting around. The staff were friendly, with good recommendations and always very polite and helpful. It was noisy due to the location (midtown), but my room was nice and it was enjoyable to hang out in the "club" area which is a sort of living room area with a big tv, free coffee and tea, and free wireless internet. There is also a pillow menu, which is fantastic - you can choose the type and number of pillows that you want for your bed. The toiletries are great - they are "philosophy" brand - and they give you any toiletries that you forgot for free (deodorant, contact solution, toothpaste, etc). And the hairdryer is a good (strong) one. They really took care of me, and I would recommend this hotel, which is also good value for money. The only thing is don't order the room service - it's really overpriced. And from what I understood some of the rooms at the back of the hotel are fairly dark since they face another building (although they are probably more quiet).

title: “the bathroom is a joke!”
text: Beautiful lobby, the room is okay, the bed is comfy, the bathroom is very small and old, no coffee maker, I will not stay here again, there are plenty of hotels in NYC with better price and more updated, people in the front desk are not too friendly, arrogant!!

title: “Great Place to Stay!”
text: We stayed here for our anniversary, and were given very special treatment with a wonderful welcome package and even a personally signed anniversary card! The hotel staff are thoughtful, friendly and responsive. We had a lovely, spacious & modern room and the fantastic location of the hotel, right outside the Chinatown Gate, made our time in San Francisco perfect. We were thrilled with Hotel Triton and are big fans of Kimpton, they treat their customers well. Rooms are always very clean and the service is not only reliable but in this case exceeded expectations. The flavoured water or iced tea in the lobby is always a welcome treat after a day of sightseeing or shopping! We will be returning!! Thank you to the hotel staff.

title: “A truly wonderful experience”
text: A truly wonderful experience is exactly what it means! After seein the sights,shopping etc..i could'nt wait to get back to the hotel! All of the hotel was so relaxin,the lobby,the reception area,i highly recommend the Bull n Bear restaurant located in the hotel,excellent !! I would definaltely go again!!

title: “Great View”
text: Despite the expensive breakfast and internet access, this hotel is perfect: great location, since it is near of many interesting places; amazing views, mainly from the restaurant on 36th floor; and friendly staff.

title: “Delightful”
text: I booked this hotel through Travelocity and was quite hesitant after reading some of the comments left by others. I have to say that my stay was delightful. There was a group of 4 of us and the room was nice and big and we didn't feel cramped at all (and that is a lot due to the amount of luggage we all brought for our cruise the next day). The decor was very nice and the beds were very comfortable. We had a room that opened to a lake (I think it was called a lagoon room) . We opened our patio doors in the morning to enjoy the fresh air and to our delight we had a family of ducks join us in our room for the morning. They were very friendly and just came and went as they pleased (where else can you have that happen), We ate breakfast at the restaurant overlooking the ocean and both the food and the service were up to our standards. Overall we enjoyed our stay and I hope to return soon with my kids.

title: “Beautiful hotel on superb location - real recommendation!”
text:
After many hours of comparison on trip advisor we selected the Pearl for our 7 night stay in NYC and boy, what a great choice it turned out to be. Executive summary: I recommend to book it if you are looking for a spacious room at a very competitive price in a central location. 
Location: The hotel is situated at 100m from Broadway / Time Square and to two of the main subway lines. We like to walk a lot during our city trips and the central location gave us a great start each morning in either direction. Central park is on 20 mins walking, 5th Avenue is on 15 mins, Madison Park is on 30 mins. Broadway is literally on your doorstep and although Time Square obviously is busy, we were not bothered at night by outside noise. The location is very safe, there are always people around in the street. 
Price: average price for 7 nights was around 220$ per night, which we considered a great deal, especially when comparing to the alternative hotels in this area. Breakfast is simple, but sufficient and for free! Initially we planned to have breakfast outside the hotel anyway, but we changed our mind after the first breakfast experience. Although limited in choice compared to big hotels (no scrambled eggs, no coffee service, no cheese selections etc), the toast, bagels, muffins and pastry were more than enough to have a good start of the day. Yoghurts, serials, juice, coffee/tea, all the basics are present. It is constantly being stocked as well, we never ran out of anything. Considering the fact that is all for free, we have no issue with the fact that it is served on plastic plates. 
Room: the room was the biggest surprise. It was as spacious as the rooms we have encountered in most big hotel chains outside New York. The inventory was very complete and offered far more than we needed, the design was very contemporary and the bed was comfortable. Although we did not spend much time in the room (basically only the nights), it was a pleasure to return each day. A suggestion for improvement is that the aircon system cannot be turned off, which we actually prefer to do at night. There is some minor street noice during the night, but that is acceptable considering the prime location and the fact that you are in NYC and it did not bother us at all. 
Staff: in short - very friendly and very helpful. 
The Pearl really has over delivered on our expectations and we will definitely book it again next time we are in NYC.

title: “One of the best hotels I've been to”
text: I booked a room for 2 nights at the Omni last August for my boyfriends birthday, even though we live in Austin I wanted to take him somewhere upscale and relaxing, we were not disappointed. Upon arrival we were met with cupcakes and a signed card for him in our room. The room itself was very large and comfortable with a nice view of downtown. The service was excellant all of the staff we came arcoss were helpful and polite. I've read many reviews regarding the noise but we never heard anything at night and if you know Austin you know that people here love to party. I don't understand why this hotel is rated so low on tripadvisor, we had a wonderful stay and are for sure coming back for another special occasion. Thank you Omni for a great weekend.

title: “The best hotel I ever!!”
text:
I had no idea what to expect when I booked a room at this hotel. I wasn't familiar with it, and the rates were so reasonable considering the location that I didn't expect much. It was only for one night, so It didn't matter.
The staff were exceptionally courteous and friendly from the minute we walked in. It was 11:20 am and we wanted to leave our backpacks. The gentleman in the main lobby suggested we see if our room was ready (I was sure it wouldn't be) and led us to the reception desk, and asked for us. It WAS ready. The young lady behind the counter was also courteous and friendly.
We got to the room and found it about 4 times larger than we expected. It had a kitchen and a very large area with a desk and dresser. I wished we were staying longer.

title: “A boutique Marriott with pros and cons”
text:
Arrival experience: Arrived around 9:00 p.m. Efficient check-in. 
Room (general): Spacious room with many architectural details such as excellent crown molding and trim, nice tucked away mini-bar, and more. The quality of materials in the room exceeds your typical Marriott room. Large LG flat screen TV, good carpets, good drapes, fixtures, etc. all of nice quality. Great 4 cup coffee maker.
Bathroom: Good size, nice granite counters, huge Jacuzzi tub, huge shower with the best water pressure I have ever experienced. Tub and shower were clean, but Jacuzzi was very hard to activate; a maintenance man showed us how to turn it on by repeatedly using shallow pushes to the start button. Also, several jets came off while using the tub. It’s a nice feature but was not maintained. 
Bed: Very good bed. 
Houskeeping: Average. We left a tip requested extra bath towels. Housekeeping took the tip but did not leave towels. 
Restaurants: We cannot recommend the hotel restaurant. We had the full breakfast buffet on Thanksgiving morning. Both the food and staff were sub-par. The buffet was not restocked, and we had to scavenge the dregs of what remained. Several core items were out of stock on the buffet including jam and fruit. The bacon was swimming in grease. We finally asked the staff to bring us fruit, and they did. However, the staff’s attitude was lackadaisical at best. We even had to get up to get our own water after waiting an extended period of time. This was probably our worst dining experience at any Marriott owned hotel. 
Bar: The bar in the lobby looked very nice, but we did not patronize it. 
Grounds: This is a downtown hotel. So there are no real “grounds.” Great gym in the basement. 
Pool: we didn’t see one
Staff attitude/service: The front desk was good, but the restaurant staff was bad. 
Perks for status: Platinum gift/points offered at check-in. Upgraded room also provided. 
Parking: Valet only. The valets were very efficient and helpful. 
Misc: This is a quaint, historic hotel. We loved the lobby. And the valets were very knowledgeable about downtown and restaurants. Use caution at night downtown. There are many bums in this part of downtown. I worked nearby at Pennzoil Place (about 5 blocks away) in the late 90s, and never noticed bums during the day. But they are everywhere at night, even urinating in public. Although the Houston Police Department is also downtown, we saw no police patrolling this part of downtown at night. 
Photos are of room 1108.

title: “My Mini Trip To Houston”
text:
'Although i did'nt have enough time to stay in Houston for long , staying at the Laquinta made my visit worth traveling for. I have never felt so revived and rested in my whole life. Thanks for making my short stay one incredible unforgetable moment.'
 - Braxton, Tx

title: “Sleep at the airport on the floor before staying at this hotel”
text: We arrived from the UK for an overnight before heading off the next day to Austin. The joy of booking a hotel overnight is that you can shower for the next day. We arrived at the hotel very late in the evening to find out they are refurbishing the hotel. When we went to the room we literally were heading straight to bed. We could not even brush our teeth as they had been doing some work with the water tank that day and to say the water from the River Thames was cleaner should give you an idea. It was disgusting. We could not brush our teeth or shower. When I complained to the hotel upon check out was told the Management would contact me. 6 weeks later nothing. That should sum up the hotel. No refund of any kind, no apology, basically the attitude was "its not our fault". The fact they took bookings when the accommodation was unfit to stay overnight is the point that disappoints me the most.

title: “Nothing special but good location”
text: Stayed here for 4 nights with husband, 17 and 15 year old, 2 double beds. Rooms slightly small for a family but adequate. Bedding clean and beds very comfortable.Location superb, couple blocks to Fishermans Wharf, where you could find a Walgreens to buy water for room, none provided at hotel, not even in the lobby. Also at Walgreens you can purchase travel cards and catch transport outside.From hotel we were able to walk to beach area to see Golden Gate Bridge, Tram turnaround and Pier 33 for Alcatraz. Plenty of restaurants at Fishermans Wharf to eat in. Most staff in hotel friendly but did not seem very aware of the local area, when asked questions they gave very vague answers or unsure what we were trying to find out. They told us to talk to concierge at the holiday Inn a couple of blocks away. Took a stroll down to him but found him very unhelpful. If staying here make sure you do lots of research on the area as we found they provided us with none. Other downside was breakfast, it did not matter if you went very early or later it was a mad scramble with not enough tables to sit and eat at. I think if it was set up different the queuing system may have been easier. Food basic and boring after a few mornings as no real varients, but ok to fill up on. Once breakfast finished no other drinks or food to be found in the hotel. Would I stay here again? probably not unless it was too good an offer compared to other hotels in the same area.

title: “Ask for an inside room..”
text: A popular business hotel in downtown Denver, ½ block from the 16th street pedestrian mall. With reservation we had asked for an inside room and received it. There is a light rail line in front of the hotel so be sure you ask for an inside room. Room was clean, quiet, and comfortable. Location is very convenient. Room rate included breakfast which was more extensive that we expected - they advertise a "continental breakfast" - this is a full breakfast.. A Big Negative is parking. Adjoining ramp charges $23 a day for self park – no in/out available – you pay each time a minimum of $8. On the positive, you are right on the 16th street mall with free rail lines – no need to move your car. Recommended.

title: “Excellent hotel, some of the front desk staff should be politer”
text:
We booked our room for six nights. Upon our arrival, we were told the hotel was booked out, and were assigned a higher category room (355) with no charge. The following day, we were put up in an excellent one (2512). However, due to the heavy rain in NYC three days after, we had two leaks in the room, which prevented us from sleeping there and we were relocated. On that occasion, in room 1833.
Staff was very sympathetic and helped us a lot. 
The biggest and most outrageous situation, after all this ordeal was the moment we checked out. I literally strove to explain to the receptionist (code number '17') what happened over our stay with a view at making sure that no extra charges would be made to us. To our surprise, she told me she did not want to hear about it, handed me the bill for revision. No thanks, no nothing after paying almost $2000.
I know this is just a bad attitude from one person, but needless to say that, sometimes, the last impression is what counts and this, unfortunately, may make all the hotel good souvenirs fade away.
I leave up to the readers to judge by themselves what happened to us.

title: “Hospitality Perfection!”
text:
This property has become, for me, the benchmark to judge other hotels with.
From the moment you step into the lobby to check-in and until you leave, the service levels, the warm smiles and the eagerness to please will leave you breathless. Compares well with any Four Seasons anywhere. I rate this property higher than the George V in Paris in terms of service.
The room service standards are difficult to match for any other hotel. In a longish stay, not a single error, never a minute's delay and when you want your tray/table cleared, someone's at the door within a couple of minutes. Similar with laundry pick-up and bellman services. Astonishing speed and efficiency all around. 
The smallish rooftop pool and health center are very nice, the concierge services are top-class, the breakfast and other meals at Bristol Grill are also very very nice. Spa treatments are among the best you will experience anywhere.
The room itself is very large, the bathroom is also oversized, wifi upto two devices is free, the toiletries are L'Occitane. No coffeemaker, although complimentary tea/coffee and muffins are served in the lobby in the morning.
The hotel offers a complimentary car for drops within a couple of miles and with the small size of Central Boston, it is a service you do get to use often.
Like the title says, this is hospitality which has achieved perfection! Flawless! Four Seasons at its very best.

title: “Very Convenient Hotel”
text: I go to NYC 3 times a year just for fun, and always stay at different hotels. I usually stay in hotels anywhere from 20th Street to 30th Street locations at boutique hotels, but this time I opted for this 51st Street location. I've never stayed at a Hilton property before, and I was pleasantly surprised at the excellent service this hotel had. I arrived at 10:00 a.m., but was not able to check in, so I took my luggage to the ladies' room, and changed clothes as I was going to a show at 2:00 pm. I asked if I could check in, just to give me a call, but was not expecting to receive a call until 3:00 pm. At 11:30 am, I received a call that my room was ready. So I ran back to the hotel, got to the room, unpacked, and changed clothes again. I walked over to the St. James Theatre at 44th Street and saw Hair. Came back, and the hotel was really busy. There is a very convenient little coffee shop next door, and I went there the next morning and picked up a coffee and a chocolate crossaint. The subway is right beside the hotel, and I took the #6 train down to NOLITA and went shopping.
