I also took the subway down to 42nd Street, and changed to another line and went over to the west side to Chelsea Market. The location of the Doubletree is excellent, as you can either take the subway, or you can walk to most of the sites. I checked out 2 days later, and they held my luggage, so I walked over to MOMA for the afternoon. The hotel has a lot of services, and the service people are very well trained. I asked for an ice bucket and received it within 1 minute. My shower could not turn on, and the engineer came within 2 minutes, and fixed it. They have a large HD television, and it has HBO. The cleaning ladies are quick and efficient. They start cleaning up the rooms around 9:00 am. I asked for some more towels and they gave them to me. This room was larger than what I have had in the boutique hotels. They have a business center so you can print your boarding pass. They have a nice bar, and a very large lobby where most people were on their laptops. I really liked this hotel, I felt safe here, I liked the coffee shop next door, and I liked that the subway was right at the door. There's a great place to buy wine, its called Graybar, and its south on Lexington about 5 blocks down. When I picked up my luggage, the bellman offered me a limo ride to LGA for only $35. What a steal. Its costs $75-$90 in Chicago to take a limo to O'Hare airport. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “My 2nd time there - great location and service”
text:
I have been to the Park central twice, last and this year. This time I was overwhelmed by the service at the check-in. My special thanks go to Ellen, she made our stay an amazing time to remember on. Thanks for your great service attitude. 
The Hotel has a great location, just a few steps away from Times Square. A subway station is just around the corner. I would highly recommend the hotel.

title: “Do not recommend”
text: I would not recommend this hotel. When we checked in the lady behind the counter was not friendly-we were excited because it was for my daughters b-day. The rooms are SO small-I noticed a $75 charge on my credit card when I called the Hotel 4 times the front desk lady kept transferring me to the Manager who NEVER got back to me. The 5th time I called I was told that the $75 was a deposit for incidentals and that I shouldn't be charged. I wish they would've explained this on checking in to the hotel.

title: “Fantastic place to stay”
text:
One block walk to Camden/bars outside left field & 5 min walk to Inner Harbor.
Rooms were clean as could be and food/sports bar was great meeting place before heading out. The place was busy but Marriott had everything under control.
Strip club(Godess) across the street was so bad it was funny.

title: “Family Visit”
text: My husband and I have stayed at this hotel several times and have never had any problems. The owner goes out of his way to make our stay as pleasant as possible. And the people that he has working for him at the front desk and the housekeepers are all wonderful. No matter what we ask for, they were very helpful. The 2 girls upstairs, Tina and Jackie couldn't have been nicer. And the front desk people, male and female were great. We will continue to use this hotel for any stay any time we are in this area.

title: “We Loved the Service”
text:
Nice clean Hotel even seen.
Very good Breakfast.
We try this hotel in July 1st and stayed for 2 nights we loved the stay.
Kids enjoyed the Indoor Pool
We will stay here again

title: “Best hotel experience in New York”
text: I stayed at the Empire Hotel for 8 nights during New York Fashion Week and had the best stay I've ever had in a long time. I had stayed at the Hudson Hotel before and had a horrible experience, so I was little apprehensive at first staying at a hotel I had never stayed before, but I was greeted by a very friendly and professional employee named Mariana as I checked-in who immediately put me at ease and made sure I was happy with my room. Everything was perfect (and I don't use that word often); Friendly and helpful staff, great continental breakfast (more food and variety than I was expecting), my room was always clean and fast check-in and check-out.

title: “Only good for airport related stay”
text: I stayed at this hotel for a business trip. I was not using the airport so I am not sure why my company recommended this hotel. It is a little hard to get to because the roadway is confusing and it sits in parking lot in a row of other hotels. The staff were OK but I almost complained to somebody in the Hampton Inn organization because none of the staff had any kind of Hampton Inn related clothing on. I felt like I was checking into a family owned motel. When I checked in there were two men at the counter and then a woman sitting to the side eating her dinner on her lap. In the morning there were people who I assumed were guests but then I would see them carrying out trash from breakfast so I realized they were actually staff. The room was OK but the bathroom seemed kind of old. The breakfast was not very good. There were no eggs and nothing that I had tasted very good, not even the bagels. I took a walk around the area and the Hilton Garden Inn next door looked way better. Also, there is only a pool outside that wasn't open. I went into the business center and the internet was very slow. In fact, a few sites I could not access.

title: “Amazing Service”
text:
After a long trip from London we were not disappointed by the Hilton. We had read about how amazing the staff were, and it was all true! They were SO polite and helpful. Our rooms were great and it was extremely convenient for Universal Studios and CIty Walk (easy 5 min walk). Only slight gripe, was the level of air conditioning in the public areas - it was freezing!!
The whole family had a great stay (including 2 teenage boys).

title: “Excellent Experience”
text: We booked the Mokara as it appeared to be highly rated and now I understand why. It ranks in an entirely different class than other hotels we have stayed in. Best memories are: lunch and margaritas at the roof top pool, the robe and slippers they provide, morning coffee on our balcony overlooking the riverwalk, the free morning paper of your choice, the free access to the spa amenities (steam room, hot tub, etc), the spot on recommendations of the concierge, and the amazingly quite rooms - the riverwalk tends to be noisy but once the balcony door was shut it was perfectly quiet.

title: “I would stay here again.”
text: Clean hotel with very helpful staff. The bell staff were very helpful and the valet parking was a breeze. The room was very comfortable. Old building charm with lots of antiques. We enjoyed the drinks and atmosphere in the bar and breakfast was great in the cafe. Quick walking distance from the White House and an enjoyable stroll to the mall and monuments. The AC did not kick on as frequently at night, but I prefer my hotel rooms arctic cold. The elevator is small and once I did have to wait for it, so I just took the steps down. This happended during the hotels buisiest time (i.e., 8:30 AM). I did not try and use the internet while I was there.

title: “Excellent location and business friendly”
text:
Stayed here for a conference. We nornammlt stay at the Westin but this year the conference was at the Marriott. Nice rooms that were recently updated.
Ask for a room with a vew of the Charles River.
Also walk down to Newbury street for excellent shopping and places to eat.

title: “Good value, good NY location”
text:
Arrived at hotel 8pm long check in line, probably 20 min wait. Looks like all rooms weren't ready and had to check what was available.
Saw reviews prior and expected small room- yes is small but clean and great bath products.
Restaurant is great I ate there several times- it's buffet but dishes are cooked fresh in single serves.
Concierge always helpful but were always so busy had to wait a bit but ok
Location close to central park and can walk to 5th ave, times square, subway nearby also
Would recommend to anyone staying in NY

title: “DON'T stay in an outer East side room!!”
text: Nice hotel, but do not stay in one of the outer East side rooms as you will hear planes coming and going all night long. I thought it would end after midnight, but I forgot it is a FedEx hub so it NEVER stopped! Sounded like they were going to come straight through the windows.

title: “Great place to stay”
text: My husband and I stayed one night here and the management was so nice. They answered all of our questions, provided us with great information and made our stay pleasant. The hotel is older but in decent shape. When we got there, our room was upgraded to a suite, which was nice. It is very close to all of the attractions. Would recommend it!!

title: “Location, location, location”
text:
Stayed for four nights as part of our honeymoon.
The location is fantastic. Metro stop on the hotel's doorstep and just a five mins walk to Times Sq and 10min walk to Central Park.
Our room was tiny and we approached reception to see if we could be moved. Apparently there were smaller rooms than ours which I couldn't believe. They did try and upgrade us / move us when we told them we were on honeymoon, but the hotel was fully booked. Found that the hotel rooms needed redecorating as it was very dated.
Useful internet provision for a small fee avaiable in the lobby.
However, we would look for a different hotel if we stayed again, but the great location of the hotel scores very highly if you want everything on your doorstep/

title: “The Only Good Thing This Stay Was the Happy Hour”
text: We have stayed at this hotel many times before since our children were little. This was our last time at this location. If we stick with Hilton Properties next time we will stay at the Embassy in Center City - It was much better. We were unfortunate enough to have my teenage son wake up with bites and sure enough we found bed bugs. Management handled it well, but housekeeping should have noticed them. My son also left his ipod in the room plugged in being charged. We got 20 mins down the road and he realized he had left it. I called the hotel and they could find no trace of it. In other words they have thieves that work in this hotel and I think management should have done more about finding out what happened to it instead of taking a sorry we can't find it attitude. Our first and second room had a moldy smelling room that was not cleaned to our expectations, the pool was filthy and breakfast was not as good this stay. the only positive point was happy hour. They did let us check out early and we moved to Homewood Suites and had a much better experience.

title: “Clean rooms, good location, but a few issues...”
text:
The location of this hotel is wonderful, as it is centrally located to many points of interest in the city. The rooms are clean and spacious, however although the entire hotel is now non-smoking (by Boston law) our room REEKED of smoke. It was really quite horrible. All of our clothes smelled like smoke and my husband's asthma was acting up as a result. We were told our room was always a non-smoking room and clearly this was untrue. We booked on Orbitz, and my assumption is they give the rooms booked at a lower rate through third party sites the "previous smoking" rooms. 
Softness/firmness of beds is a matter of personal preference, however my husband and I found the mattresses and the pillows to be extremely soft and unsupportive, resulting in two bad nights of sleep.
The front desk representatives where somewhat clueless about parking in the attached hotel garage and the hotel in general (note: park across the street in the lot for $10 cheaper a night instead of Hilton's attached garage) but managed to check us in and any other interaction with hotel staff was limited. 
We found it somewhat unbelievable that the hotel did not have complimentary Wifi in the rooms. It's 2010, and having to huddle in their small and crowded lobby to take advantage of free internet seemed a bit dated, and frankly disapointing. 
All in all it was an adequate hotel for a short stay, but if I would think twice before making a reservation here for a longer trip.

title: “Felt like Europe, only more convenient”
text: The hotel very much felt like being in Europe. The room was a bit on the small side but the high ceilings & well appointed room made up for that. Our quiet room was actually quiet, the staff was very friendly, the lobby was beautiful, it was in a bustling location, plus their recycling program was very admirable. The only draw backs were an odd & consistent smell on the 4th floor & a little mold in the bathroom (not in the shower though). We got a good rate through hotels.com so it was well worth the money. Highly recommend it.

title: “Very Good Experience”
text:
Many reviews speak about the construction taking place, and after I learned from Hotwire.com that this would be the hotel I booked, I was a bit concerned. I was pleasantly surprised at what I experienced. 
The front desk clerk was very cordial and checked us in early.
The concierge was very helpful in helping me to learn my way around the metro system.
The rooms were new, and as a result, very clean. 
The beds were comfortable, as were the standard pillows.
The bathroom was fine...a bit small, but everything was new and clean.
A message from management awaited me when I returned to the room later in the evening; a call to make sure I was happy with my accommodations. Nice touch.
The only negatives I discovered are as follows:
Noise from the outside was a bit loud, but it's beyond the hotel's ability to change what's happening outside.
The parking garage is expensive and very small! I drive a full size pickup with a crew cab and found it to be a tight squeeze and many places there.
I stayed on the 8th floor. Construction was taking place on the 2nd and 3rd floors. I never heard a sound from the construction crews, nor did I ever have to wait an extended period of time for the elevators. 
I was very pleased with my stay. Should I visit the city again, and need a place in the Capitol Hill area, I will look to the Liaison for my accommodations...especially if they reduce the cost of parking!

title: “Loved the St. Gregory”
text:
Our family of 4 (2 adults, 2 childen) stayed at the St. Gregory Hotel for a long weekend during Presidents' Week. We basically booked this hotel so we could have more space by reserving a one-bedroom suite. We were so happy with the accommodations - the suite was lovely, roomy and clean, with a separate bedroom, full kitchen and large bathroom. Our kids loved the flat screen tv! The location is in a nice area- with lots of restaurants close by. It is a bit of a walk to the major sites, but the Metro is not too far. 
The hotel itself is very secure - you need a room key to operate the elevator. The St. Gregory is small and intimate - more like an apartment building than a hotel. We would not hesitate to recommend staying here!

title: “Definitely the best hotel in New York”
text:
I travel to NYC for business or leisure very often.
Over the last 5 years, I stayed in many luxury hotels such as Waldorf Astoria, the Plaza, the Parker Meridien or the Peninsula.
The Four Seasons New york is the best hotel in town. Rooms and suites are wide and beautifully decorated, the service is fast and sophisticated.
The staff always takes care of guests. For example, security guards know your name and wish you a good day when you get in or out of the elevators...
Its restaurant is really a gourmet one that can easily be compared with the best NYC restaurants (Daniel...).
Even if rates are slightly higher that its competitors, this hotel is a great value.

title: “Nice Hotel with small comforts”
text: I came here for a birthday weekend. I stayed in a Junior Suite which was small by my standards but comfortable. A sleep number bed made the sleep relaxing. The down part is the price of food in the hotel and the adjacent restaurant called Razzle. This place gouge you for the food so I suggest you go across the street to the Deli which has the best food I tasted in a while. The selection is vast and the value is good plus it is open 24 hours. The fitness center is well equipped but a little small. I did get a good 45 minute work out though. Very good location, around the corner from the Rockafella center and other attractions. We had a wonderful time shopping on Maddison Ave and was 10 minutes driving to Broadway when we went to see the play Fela.... Which I give 5 Stars to see......

title: “Pretty fancy”
text:
We got an excellent rate here through a last-minute package on Northwest Airlines. I probably would not have been willing to pay the rack rate at this hotel, but if you can get a deal it is definitely worth it.
Pros:
1. LOCATION was fantastic. Right across the street from Copley Place (shopping mall), Trinity Church, and Boston Library. About a block or two from Newberry Street and Boylston Street, where you can find great shopping and restaurants. Also a T stop was a block away, literally a 3-minute walk.
2. HOTEL staff was very friendly, lobby was beautiful, rooms were clean and nicely decorated.
Cons:
1. AGE of the hotel was a con for me, although I'm sure a lot of people would find it charming. It is very nicely kept up, however the Fairmont rooms are small (reminded me of European hotel rooms) and there were some things, like a fan in the bathroom, that I missed. Also our view was non-existent, although I'm sure there are rooms with really nice views. Also, I find feather pillows extremely uncomfortable, but I know others love them, so it's a matter of taste. 
2. One thing that happened to us- upon turning down the bed our first night to sleep, I found this strange stuff on the inside of the sheet. I looked like dark cracks, but when I looked closer, it seemed like little clumps of hair. I called the front desk and even though it was late, they sent someone right up to change the sheets. The guy who came up said that was from ironing. I didn't really buy that, but I really didn't know, so I let it go. The important thing was that they tended to my problem immediately without question.

title: “Would do it again!”
text: After reading the reviews we decided to give this hotel a try. Not dissapointed. The hotel check-in was easy, room was a good size and the room service arrived quick and hot. The pool area is small, but the full size beds make it comfortable and cozy. The location is great, we didn't have to use our car once. Great restaurants and transportation. The concierge helped us get tix to the SDSU game and suggested we take the train, which was a great idea (if you decide to go to a game watch out for broker fees). The concierge also recommended a great breakfast spot Cafe 222, great idea, a ling wait, but worth it.

title: “Nice Clean Hotel, Friendly Staff and Convienient Location”
text:
La Luna Inn was the last stay on our California road trip last year. It was a nice hotel to stay in if your not fussy on the extras. 
Rooms are clean and spacious with a big TV with good selection of channels, a decent sized en-suite bathroom and a desk.
No complainents on noise and the staff were friendly. Convienient to all of the major tourist attractions and city.

title: “Great location and service”
text:
I met a college friend in the city for some time away. The Benjamin staff was great and very helpful. As most of you know, NYC hotel rooms are typically very small. Ours was not small at all. We had a kitchenette, nice closet space, a writing desk and comfortable chairs.
It was so nice to have my choice of pillows.
The concierge secured airport travel and printed boarding passes along with great local recommendations for a late dinner after the theatre.
We had a late night cocktail at the bar and the staff was so much friendlier that the waitresses at the W (just down the street). We were ignored there and left without ordering anything.
A friend's daughter works at The Benjamin and gave us some great local advice and made sure that everything was perfect. Even without her assistance, the stay would have still been great. The other staff at The Benjamin didn't know we knew her, and we were treated with professionalism and kindness.

title: “NEWELY REMODELED ROOMS...loved it!”
text:
I'm a self proclaimed GERM-A-PHOBE. I bring my own cleaning supplies on every excursion. I needed a room for 1-night in San Diego. As I drove up from the airport at approx 10PM to check-in, the exterior of the hotel was a little disappointing -puts you in the mind of an old Vegas style Motel 6!
Front desk 10+++. Awesome service! As I crossed the threshold of my single, non-smoking, king sized bed room I was floored! I stepped out of Motel 6, into a really nice HYATT! New paint, new carpet, new furnishing, refrigerator and stainless steel microwave. No mold or chipping pain in the shower. New replacement windows.
I immediately snapped into "Operation Germs" and performed a thorough inspection of every crevice from behind the toilet to smudges on the drawer handles. I was impressed! Nice little jewel of a hotel... Clean and comfortable...
Nice continental breakfast and one computer

title: “Convention hotel on the wrong side of the river”
text: Big convention hotel. Clean and well maintained, but isolated. Few restaurant choices nearby or in the hotel. The casual restaurant was only opened for breakfast and lunch. I had a upgraded corner room with a great few, but a in-room safe was barely big enough to get my iPad in it. Honor bar was the "lift it and you bought it" model. Room service was quick, efficient and good. Navy Pier is six blocks as are restaurants and other activities, but mostly on the other side of the river. Just remember, six walking blocks in Chicago in April is six Taxi blocks in Chicago in January.

title: “Not what reviews said...”
text:
As a weekly traveler, I have stayed at many Crowne Plaza hotels - this by far was the dingiest. 
Bathroom floor and tub dirty, hair still hanging around. 
Bed is way past expiration date. 
Rooms so small (for US hotels)
There are many newer, cleaner and more affordable hotels in the area. This ain't one of them.

title: “Very reasonable price, undergoing improvement”
text: Stayed at this hotel for two nights in late June 2010. At that time the place didn’t feel finished. The room was huge and clean, but it was hardly furnished apart from the bed. The air con worked fine and the room was clean and quiet. The hotel is in a residential area. Maybe I missed something but there wasn’t much around the area. We drove to look at other places rather than staying close to the hotel. But for $100US a night, with parking inclusive, it was a more than reasonable place to stay. It will be really nice once they put the finishing touches on it.

title: “Best DC hotel that I've stayed at - by far”
text: If you are staying in the DC area on business, look no further than the Westin in Georgetown. Very convenient to the metro, a nice healthy walk to DC proper, and the rooms & service really are top notch. As someone who works out regularly, I was blown away by finally experiencing a hotel fitness club with NEW equipment. Will stay here for all my future DC business trips. TWO BIG THUMBS UP!!!

title: “Lovely hotel in great neighbourhood”
text:
Visited Chicago for the NRA exhibition, Hotel Indigo was perfect
Room was spacious New England decor and the hotel was perfect for our stay
The bar wasn't overly inviting but locally you have a top rate Italian within yards and many bars and restaurants within 5 minutes walk
Would definitely return

title: “Outdated hotel, needs lots of work”
text:
I want to start by saying that hands down this hotel has absolutely the best staff. Each and every staff member I came into contact with was absolutely fantastic, however their friendliness and enthusiasm just cant compensate for the state of this hotel. 
I stayed here multiple times for business trips, and each time I would be greeted by a number of broken items. The elevators are frequently out of order, but even when they were working, they were slow(10+ min wait) and frankly a bit scary! You also have the choice to ride the maintenance elevator with the trash, towels, room service...... The plumbing needs some major repairs as well, the rooms have drippy faucets, clogged drains, and just generally poorly maintained bathrooms. The gym is tiny, with only 1 elliptical and 2 treadmills; when I was staying there the TVs on the machines were broken too. The windows are insanely thin, if you're on the freeway side, you will hear traffic all night long. 
I stayed here frequently due to the fantastic location and proximity to where I need to be. I loved having all the shops and restaurants right there. The hotel itself leaves a lot to be desired, but works as a crash pad after a long day of work. If your room really really suck, well, you can at least count on the friendly staff to get you a slightly less sucky room and help you move your stuff. Thanks Emily! Really, it's not your fault this place is stuck in the 70s!

title: “filth everywhere!”
text:
How did this property get a 5 sunburst award from Days Inn? The room was filthy! The light was broken between the beds and I called the manager, he freferred me to the front desk and 8 hours later it was still not fixed. The telephone and alarm clock were not cleaned in months and coated with grime. The bathroom had numerous long black hairs on the floor and we both have shaved heads. The ice bucket still had water in it and was covered with mold. The floor of the room had beer bottle caps on it and pretzels and dust was every where! We called the manager to complain and he switched us to a so called suite and it was just as bad. I sent Days Inn two different emails asking for an ecplaination of why the rate this hotel with five sunbursts and they have still not answered me. 
I'm the former Director of Operations for Gray Line Tours Wisconsin/Milwaukee and I rely on ratings when making group reservations. Days Inn corporate should be ashamed of themselves for giving this property a 5 out of 5 rating as it is a disgusting property.

title: “Disappointing Stay.”
text:
During my stay, I stayed in both one of the smaller and medium rooms. The smaller room was tiny, but quite comfortable for just one person, the medium sized room was adequate for two people. 
The rooms were clean and nice however they were extremely noisy especially first thing in the morning when the house keeping staff were working. 
The hotel has two elevators, yet one was not working due to the construction going on in the hotel. The other elevator was incredibly slow and crowded - so we ended up taking the stairs the majority of the time. 
The main issue that I had with this hotel was the fact that they placed a charge on my card when I first arrived well in excess of the total cost of my stay. When I queried this, the staff member was slightly rude and told me this charge would be reversed when I checked out. I was incredibly disappointed to arrive home and this was not the case. 
I followed up with the hotel and they told me it could be 7 -10 days till the charge is reversed – very annoying.

title: “Sambie10”
text: Arrived at airport got train15 min ride to 8th street hotel right across the road was great. Checkin was quick. Booked a smoking room with balconey. On entering room it was disgusting very old and smelled musty the veiw looking at a wall. Returned to lobby was very busy returned at night told them not happy with the room. Was told u booked a smoking room. Said yes but dont smoke in the room just wanted balcony the man behind the desk was great upgrade us to the 12th floor had balcony with a great veiw very updated room. I think smoking room means you can smoke in the room I dont do. Thanks Holiday Inn. Getting round is easy you can get passport for 1, 2, ect days which lets u on the tram trains and cablecars Homless people around but felt safe would stay again.

title: “Excellent Hotel - Great Stay”
text:
We stayed at the Empire for 4 nights in July 2011. I was slightly apprehensive about what were going to find as a lot of reviews on here weren't great, but there was something about the Hotel that I still liked.
I have to say we had an amazing stay. Staff are friendly and efficient, decor is lovely although a bit dim, but I guess that is the effect. We had a room with 2 double beds, it was well furnished and we had plenty of room, We didn't have a view on NY but that didn't bother us. The bathroom is really small, but I can cope with small as it was spotlessly clean which is more important to me.
The pool deck is a lovely place to lie and have a well earned rest from all the sight seeing, The pool is tiny!! so much so we didn't bother to use it. The view from up there is also amazing!! I did witness long queues in the evening for the night club, as we had a younger daughter with us we didn't experience the club and didn't feel it bothered us, I did read on hear that they don't give guests priority which I do believe is something they need to change. If I went back without my daughter I would like the oppotunity to go up there in the evening and as a paying guest would like to think that give you some priority??
The location is excellent walking distance to two major subway stations and walking distance from lots of Resturants. We did eat in Pj Clarkes, I don't think it was over priced and my daughter enjoyed it :-).
Wi-Fi in the lobby is patchy - I don't understand why it isn't through the whole hotel and it was annoying to have to keep going to the lobby, Starbucks round the corner has a much better and more reliable free Wi-Fi service which we used to Skype home!
Would I go back to Empire - Absolutley, you don't go to NY to sit in a Hotel Room, your in an amazing city and you need to be out there enjoying it, this hotel is clean, with great decor and facilities, good staff and customer service and an excellent location - what more do you want??

title: “Favorite NYC Hotel”
text: The Chatwal exceeds expectations. The staff are extremely friendly and helpful. The maids do a wonderful job with their turndown service. After a night on the town, it is great to come back to slippers at your bedside and complimentary towelettes, as well as a bottle of water on each nightstand. The hotel is extremely clean. We used to stay at the New York Palace, but the Chatwal is where we stay now. I highly recommend this hotel to anyone that wants a truly great experience at a boutique hotel.

title: “Great Staff, Great Location, Great Views, OK Rooms”
text: Located right by the Pike Place Market, the Inn at the Market is a nice quiet boutique hotel. The staff is very helpful. The lobby is small but nice with a fireplace and lots of free newspapers, apples, and coffee in the morning. Great business center. FREE INTERNET. No gym. My room was HUGE but was a little sparsely furnished although the furniture was very nice and the bed extremely comfortable. The bathroom was huge and well appointed. Excellent towels and bath products. Water pressure was a little low in the shower. Lots of restaurants nearby. Great breakfast at the little coffee shop in the hotel. Ask for a room overlooking the water!

title: “A great home in New York - made by the staff”
text:
We stayed here for just under a week, and had a great time all round. Firstly, pro's - staff are fantastic, very helpful but non intrusive; a rare combo in hotel staff. If they didn't have any answer for something, they found out and followed up - exactly what a visitor to New York needs. Rooms were a fair size for NY (although not massive, no where is unless you are paying suite prices). Funky and clever design made it feel like a true holiday space as well. Finally, great water pressure - might sound an odd point, but I have been in some NY hotels where I'd have been better getting a tramp to spit at me. Hotel is very well placed for Times Square and getting to other tourist attractions is easy as well.
Some drawbacks - not suitable for families as only two lifts, so waiting around sometimes for the lift could be a pain for kids in a hurry to pee, etc. Location abuts what seems to be a sightly dodgy area, so wandering out at 2am to find fast food wouldn't be something I did in this hotel, but I would in some other parts of New York. That said, New York cops are all over the place and I felt much much safer here than in London, for example. No taxi rank nearby, which is usually not an issue as cab run up and down the street a lot, but if you were heading to catch a flight I'd book a limo
Overall, we will be using Distrikt again if we go to NY, and it's all down to the staff. Management should make sure they stay happy - as they are worth their weight in gold

title: “Soviet Westin: Not for Business Travelers”
text:
This hotel was a great disappointment for a business trip. First, the air conditioning was not adequate for a late September afternoon in Chicago. I arrived in the room at about 230pm and had to work. The AC had been off. I fired it up, but it took hours on a not very hot day to make the room tolerable. I was sweating through my business shirt --- something that wouldn't happen at the Days Inn or Embassy Suites -- chains not usually mentioned in the same breath as the Westin.
I was unable to get the Front Desk to answer or Conceirge, despite repeated calls. The hotel simply does not have enough staff to handle the crowds. Check-in was a 15 minute ordeal at an off hour.
My breakfast was botched. I asked for Special K, at Soviet Westin I got Total. I asked for Grapefruit, but at the Soviet Westin they do not have fresh grapefruit. Odd.
My telephone lacked its base, so it slid across the glass table constantly -- bad for business calls (manager: check it out - Room 1107).
The good points: 1) Gold Coast location is superb; 2) Heavenly Bed still good. The gym is B-plus; but completely full at 6AM -- Manager, it needs expansion.
This is a hotel with a great brand and location and very poor execution.

title: “LOVED this property, location, and service!”
text:
If all the Residence Inn rooms were this lovely and liveable I'd never stay anywhere else. In the heart of the Gaslamp Quarter - which I found to be wonderfully lively without being crazy. Mona at the Front Desk was so helpful on the phone and then we had the pleasure of meeting her when we checked in. 
DIdn't go to the pool, which was quite small. Just an FYI if that is what you are looking for.

title: “Get What You Pay For”
text: So the Salisbury Hotel doesn't have the newest decor, but for the money it is a great place to stay. The location is ideal - only one block from Central Park and a short walk to Times Square. The rooms were exceptionally clean and large enough for four girls to get ready comfortably. And so it was a little noisy...if you do New York the right way you will be so tired at the end of the day you will sleep soundly. The staff isn't overly friendly, but they are certainly efficient which is what is really important. One word of advice - skip the hotel breakfast and head down to Cafe Europa less than one block away for a wonderful selection at a great price. In summary, the Salisbury is a nice hotel for the money -- if you want fancy pay $400/night, but for us it was perfect. I would definitely stay there again!!!

title: “Was perfect for my stay”
text:
I had a great time staying at the Adolphus around New Year. It was in an ideal location for my stay and the staff were very friendly, particularly the bellmen and a technician who came to help with the dvd player in my room (there was a slight problem with it but nothing major.) The hotel was very helpful when the airline temporarily lost one of my cases and made sure it was returned to me safely. One bellman in particular, who I believe may be the one noted in other reviews, was especially sweet, chatting to me and helping me out a lot. 
I'm bemused by the comments that you could hear things through the walls/ceiling as I didn't find this to be the case at all. I was on around the 14th floor I think, definitely quite high, and I didn't experience this. There may have been some noise through the windows but as I live on a main road back home in England I'm so accustomed to the noise of traffic and people at night that I don't really notice. It was certainly not distracting and did not affect my sleep at all. 
Room service food was pricey but this is true of many hotels and I only needed to use it once during my week long stay. The food was warming and hearty, and the lady who brought it was very polite. We ate once in the dining room (not the French room or the Rodeo Bar) and the food was fine. 
Overall I had a lovely stay. My room did not have a musty smell, and was bright and clean. The only negative point I would say is that we did have some experience of the extra charge anomalies that some reviewers have mentioned - the hotel tried to charge again for valet parking when the final bill was settled but these charges had already been paid on a daily basis. However it took just a minute for me to explain, the situation to be rectified and the bill to be correct. 
I would definitely stay here again if was suitable for my circumstances. I splashed out on a stay there because the location etc were helpful to me as a lone traveller (I am returning to Dallas next month and staying in different hotel because of a different situation) but generally speaking there are probably hotels with better amenities (pool etc). Overall I would admit that although it is lovely it's perhaps not 'luxury' in the way that word might imply but I did not encounter the negatives others have cited and thoroughly enjoyed my stay.

title: “Our home away”
text: After many visits to Austin we found the Allandale about 5 years ago and it is now our home away from home whenever we visit. Great friendly ambiance, excellent accomodations in a condo-like setting. Wonderful staff. The location is terrific, in a semi residential setting takes you away from the hustle of the humdrum of 'commercial' areas. Highly recommended. Once you stay, you'll be back!

title: “Much better than expected!! Great Hotel!”
text: I was a bit concerned after reading some reviews and of the location, but to my surprise, it was a great 2 night experience!!! I would definitely stay here again!! Parking is secured and easy-even reserved spots for Priority Club Members-never have seen this before. The hotel is almost done with a renovation and it is very nice! The hotel is definitely an older property, but again, it is up to par with the "new" holiday inn look after this renovation. The rooms are large (except for bathroom) and spacious and come with all the modern Holiday Inn (IHG) amentities. Very Very Clean hotel!!! Great AC, very comfy beds, and VERY VERY good strong water pressure. The staff is very friendly and willing to help in any way they can. From the service stand point, it is that of a four star hotel. Finally, the breakfast buffet is better than average-a full buffet. If you are in the Valley, this is the perfect place as it is in the center of it all. Save your time from searching and stay here, even though it is a bit more than other properties in the area.

title: “Gorgeous Hotel”
text: I had to travel to Phoenix by myself on business for a week so I was a bit nervous with all of the bad things I heard on the news . When I arrived at the hotel to check-in I was greated very warmly by a gentleman at the front desk and given some tips to get around on my own. The young man that was the shuttle driver was very pleasant as well as the hotel offered a service to take you to the nearby supermarket and I was able to get some stuff for the fridge in the room. The rooms have a very modern look to them and the interior of the hotel is just absolutely amazing with waterfalls, bridges & fish ponds. There is a daily guest appreciation reception were you can get snacks and beverages. The Omaha steakhouse is conveniently loacted inside the hotel which is where I ended up eating most nights since I didn't have a car. There are transportations cars located right outside the hotel lobby daily so you dont have to bother yourself with pre-booking and/or waiting for a taxi. The mall is located right next door along with some other reputable dining establishments. The ladies at the front desk gossip a bit much for me..they should take some tips from the guys. This is the first hotel I've been to in years that does not offer free wireless Internet which would be a big detourant for business travelers on a budget but overall I had a good stay and would consider staying at an Embassy Suites Hotel again.

title: “Excellant service”
text:
I was going to Chicago to run the 2012 marathon and had reserved a room at a different hotel, but just a couple of days before the race I got a call from the other hotel to tell me the room I reserved wasn't actually available. Most of the hotels in Chicago were either sold out, or were charging $500/night. I had some friends staying at the W, so I called the hotel and they had a room for me, but were asking $600/night (before tax)! When I explained what had happened to me, and that I was scrambling to get a room, they gave me the room at the originally discounted price for marathon runners, even though that price had long expired, and from what I could tell when I got there they probably could have rented the room at full price to someone else. I did have to talk to about 4 different people before they gave me the room at the marathon price, but I didn't fell like the people I spoke to were punting, just trying to get me to the person who could make the decision for me. Everyone I spoke to was very helpful.
Also, when I got to the hotel the staff were very helpful, from a quick to check-in to some nice extra services like 5 am breakfast items for marathon runners overall the staff were fantastic.
As for the hotel itself, it isn't especially fancy and (like a lot W's) it has a little bit of a "club" vibe that I don't necessarily want/need in a hotel, like techno music in the elevators 24 hours a day and white and red color scheme in the lobby, but it was clean and the rooms were decent size and of course it had comfy beds.

title: “Fantastic Experience”
text:
After staying at a number of high end and boutique hotels, I have found one that I can now call "home." Electic but warm, comfortable and unassuming, the Andaz strikes the right chord of professionalism and relaxation. The rooms have a very clean, zen and peaceful feel to them with a bathroom that put any of the other hotels in town to shame. Perfect to sleep or work in. 
There is a whimsical, stylish English/Japanese feel to the lobby, the bar and the restaurant. The restaurant is top quality- fresh, organic and tasty. I loved it.
The location at 42nd and Fifth provides access to uptown/downtown, Grand Central and Times Square.
To me, this is a better version of the Peninsula or Four Seasons- smaller, more relaxed and just good energy overall.

title: “Great Location”
text:
I recently stayed at the Argonaut Hotel from 8/4-8/7. I chose the hotel based on the reviews here on Tripadvisor. I reserved the king size bed w/ a view of the Cannery. The room (#381) was the same size as any other hotel room. It was above average. The window opened out to the plaza next to the Cannery. There was a band/singer performing. I could clearly hear him, but it wasnt a nuisance. The room was $295/day after tax which is a lot for anywhere but San Francisco. I did see the suite w/ view of Bay and Alcatraz. Wow! Very nice room and large but i couldnt justify the extra cost. So all and all I was happy w/ the hotel. The front desk and concierge were NOT helpful at all. I agree w/ some other reviews in that it seemed the front desk wasnt happy w/ their jobs. The doormen and bellhops on the other hand were helpful and great. The best things about the hotel were its location at Fisherman's Wharf and cable car turn around and the fact a Starbucks was located in the same building in the back. That was a life saver. 
 Here a couple of suggestions/ideas/random thoughts: The cable cars are very cool and are a great way to get around town. U can buy a one day pass on the cabe car itself ($11) and you dont need exact change. The operators are very helpful and outgoing. it can get very busy at certain times but i waited no more then 15-20 minutes.
 Alcatraz is a yawner!! As a tourist, one is obligated to go to Alcatraz. So go so u can say "been there, done that". It's too crowded and uneventful. Buy tickets at least a week in advance and it will be windy and a bit chilly on the ferry ride.
 Fisherman's Wharf is a tourist trap nightmare. There are so many people milling about. Cheap t shirt shops and crowds are a huge detractor, but again as a tourist one has to go. I ate at Pier market and loved it. Neptunes restaurant was okay and it did have an awesome view. Bubba Gumps has the best menu but there was a 75-85 minutes wait on Sunday night so i skipped it.
 The highlight of my visit was Golden gate bridge. Beautiful!! nothing more to say.
 I took bridge over to Saulisito and ate a place called Burgers. It's a hole in the wall. Just look for the long line. Well worth it.

title: “Close to Times Square”
text:
Location:
This hotel was the perfect resting point for our weekend in NYC. While the room didn't face Times Square, we were only one block from the crossroads of the world.
Sleeping:
Luckily I like a firm mattress, my wife doesn't so she had trouble sleeping. However the room/hallway was very quiet.
Pool:
We were hoping to relax in the pool after a day walking around Manhattan. Although the pool was described as heated, it wasn't very warm.
Overall a nice hotel.

title: “Good midtown location, spotty service”
text:
When we booked through the spg program six months in advance we requested a king bed on a high level floor with a view. They granted part of that request, but unfortunately the view was not great. 
As you have undoubtedly read, the hotel is located a block from the garish Timesquare, which has its pluses and minuses. One downside is that there are few close local choices for dining; mostly chains instead. And there are crowds of people everywhere, which gets a bit old after a day or so. But transportation is never a problem and being close to most of the subway lines is a definite plus that should not be overlooked.
Our room was nice and standard Westin quality. The bathroom was too clinical looking for my taste and there was not adequate counter space. But there were other shelves in the bathroom to use for storage. Contrary to one previous reviewer, I appreciated the cardboard Starwood coffee cups, which made it easy to grab coffee to go. 
Upon return late one afternoon, we found our room door partly ajar. Housekeeping had apparently forgotten to close it. The room was also not cleaned, made obvious by the still unmade bed. It was as though housekeeping had come in and then left right away (after taking the tip money we left out). We did a quick inventory of personal belongings of value in the room and did not find anything missing.
Speaking of housekeeping, we would hang our towels up after using them, with the intention of using them one more time before changing them for fresh ones, and housekeeping would change them anyway. One day we left the dirty towels on the bathroom floor to indicate they needed changing, and we received no clean towels. Housekeeping overall seemed to be inconsistent, but minor inconveniences that were solved by a quick phone call to the service desk.
I didn’t understand why this hotel charged for use of the fitness center but I’ve stayed in other Westins that have not. This is a confusing policy. We ran in Central Park instead of using the treadmills, which was a must-do experience for any runner who visits NYC, but it would have been nice to have complimentary use of the fitness center.
Overall, the hotel was pleasant and a nice retreat from a long day of siteseeing and shopping. For a good rate I would probably stay again, but would hope for a view the next time around. However, there was nothing that made our stay spectacular, so if you’re looking for someplace really special, I would keep looking.

title: “Very small/tight but clean and comfortable bedding-3 1/2 stars”
text: I stayed here in a two bed double room (room 404) over the Thanksgiving weekend on a last minute trip with an adult family member and small child. The room was clean (no bed bugs) with modern appointments and the beds and bedding very comfortable but space extremely tight--as in we had to stand between the beds to pass each other. There was also no built in closet just a small wardrobe for us to share. I travel often and this was the smallest room I've ever stayed in except in Europe. I think the single king/queen rooms may be a smidge larger--but I was informed by the staff that all rooms are pretty cramped. We stayed on a smoking floor (none of us smokes) but not bothersome. The hotel however is in a convenient location (on a quiet street) for getting to main attractions--we took all modes of public transportation which were not more than a block or two from the hotel and we felt safe walking the neighborhood at all times of the day/night. I drove up and was also able to park for free on the street across from the hotel for the entire weekend (I arrived after 6 p.m. on a Fri) --it reverts back to commercial only parking at 8 am on Monday at which time I moved my car. I did not check out breakfast but it is at least there for $19.95, less for kids. There is a also a decent enough looking bar (did not use) that will give you ice for your icebucket. Staff was polite and professional. Hotel is also pet friendly for a reasonable fee. No views from my level but hotel has over 24 floors so ask if that is important to you. I thought it was a good value overall ( booked on Expedia) and I think I would stay again if I found a good deal--and could request a larger room. My review is really more like 3 1/2 stars.

title: “Beautiful landscape....dangerous couch”
text:
My fiancée and I arrived at the Squaw Peak Hilton on 9/24 for 2 nights. As a Hilton gold card member we were upgraded to a very nice and spacious room. It had 1 and a half bathrooms, 2 TVs, kitchen area, large couch and a boardroom table that could seat 8! The only minus was the sink outside the bathroom – I so hate that.
However, after getting settled in, I happened to notice a small shard of glass on the living room couch. This alarmed me as it is obviously dangerous if someone sat down or a child picked it up. Otherwise the room was very clean.
On Monday 9/26, we awoke to a loud racket at 6:30 a.m. only to find a very large crane right outside our bedroom balcony doing some sort of building work. Needless to say, it ruined any chance of a restful morning. It finished at 9:00 a.m. My question is why did the management need to disturb guests at such an early hour? Had the noise began at 9:00 a.m., fair enough, but 6:30? Why so early and directly outside occupied rooms?
The grounds were beautiful and the pool area was clean and well kept. The Hole in the Wall restaurant was good, but it was the only option for a restaurant as the other was being renovated. It was also the only bar available apart from the pool bar that had limited hours. I've never been in a Hilton hotel without an inside bar or at least a coffee shop. This had neither.

title: “lovely old fashioned hotel with service but, ...”
text: The rates are high but our company would definitely return; with their costs they should up the ante on maintenance and train their help - our suite was lovely but could not get air conditioning on nor lower the heat, the book was missing the page with directions; our tub drain did not work and my nails were broken ( normally I know this sounds quite absurd but we were in town for business and to shop for a wedding gown for our daughter ) when I attempted to drain the tub. I had just had them done as a gift from my daughter ! I hope we get a response from The Lenox as we did stay two nights , dined at the restaurant, Solas ( the Pub ) and had cocktails at the bar. Lovely cookies and lemonade were offered Sat night but not Sunday; we were told we would get the newspaper but none were delivered

title: “Just What We Were Looking For!”
text:
We chose this hotel on a recommendation from the bride and groom of the wedding we were in town for. They picked a central location to the rehearsal site, wedding, and the reception. We have never stayed at an Embassy Suites. We loved it!
We were immediately greeted by energetic staff. Before we even took our bags upstairs we were told about the Manager's 'Happy Hour.' Free appetizers, wine, liquor and beer every day from 5:30pm - 7:30pm! It was a nice treat to grab a drink before heading to our room or out to dinner.
Complimentary, cooked-to-order breakfast every morning too! Omelets, pancakes, bacon, sausage, hashbrowns, pastries, cereal, coffee, tea, etc. They even had a fountain drink machine...I've never had complimentary breakfast that served me my Diet Coke!!!
Large open atrium in the center of the hotel with the rooms circling around. I didn't think it was noisy like other reviews stated. Maybe you could request a higher level room. 
They have a 24 hours store in the lobby that sells snacks and toiletries. There is also a 24 CVS pharmacy practically in the same parking lot, which was very convenient. 
A few other notes: Courtesy shuttle will take you where you need to go; The Galleria is obviously very close; The lobby has a kiosk that allows you to check-in/check-out at the hotel and check-in for your flight; Rooms were spacious and clean; Room Service is available.
Everyone in our group really enjoyed our stay!

title: “Well equipped, friendly staff, good breakfast”
text:
Hotel is located next to Willowbrook Mall, and there are some restaurants in walking distance (walk under the bridge to the other side of 249). The hotel checkin was easy, even though they were overbooked (may have been due to Silver status). Bananas and apples were available 24h. Breakfast buffet with good selections. Did not attend their evening meal choices at managers reception. This hotel does not offer free airport shuttle. Yes, would come back here.
Room was quiet, was able to turn off the fridge over night. Complimentary Wifi Internet speed was good.

title: “Highly Recommend! Great Value, Service, and Location.”
text: Our family came in town for son's graduation from Air Force Basic training. The staff went above and beyond to make our stay comfortable and memorable. Excellent value and excellent location - adjacent to all downtown attractions including RiverWalk, Alamo, and Alamodome and easy to get to. The hotel was clean and tastefully decorated - rooms had queen beds (big plus for me!) and a nice sitting area with a pullout couch. They also offered a delicious hot breakfast as well as a social 'happy hour' during the week with complimentary beer/wine and hors d'oeuvres. I could go on and on..... My thanks to Sherry and her team for making this a fantastic stay - and thanks for cake!! If you're looking for a great place to stay in San Antonio, you don't have to look any further.

title: “Outstanding”
text: I booked this hotel for my husband and I as a weekend get-away in Fort Worth. Omni consistently proves to be one of, if not the, best hotel chain in the world.

title: “Great room, fantastic location”
text: Thoroughly enjoyed our stay at the Washington Court. Our room was ENORMOUS, however we were later told by the concierge that there was only one room of that size on each floor, so we got really lucky! Great location, only a few minutes walk away from the Capitol building. Also very close to Union Station, so if you don't have much luggage with you I would recommend walking, as taxis charged $2 for every bag placed in the trunk, making it over $10 for a ride that took less than 5 mins. Free wi-fi was only available in the hotel lobby, but otherwise, we have nothing negative to say about this hotel.

title: “Impressed”
text: I am more accustomed to full service hotels but there are none in el paso so I went with hyatt who I generally trust. Hyatt Place is an amazing concept. The room was huge the bathroom was surprisingly small though. I only stayed one night so I didn't really get to be in the hotel often but I was hungry very late and went down to the lobby where they had obviously a very limited menu but the sandwich was very good and it is very convenient. I just missed complimentary breakfast but they did still offer me coffee. One of the best hotels I have stayed in although it was limited service.

title: “Great staff, great accommodations.”
text: Good location if you need to be in Downtown Denver. Staff is very attentive to your needs. Facilities are neat, clean and comfortable. If you go to the restaurant, order the eggplant.

title: “Perfect for Chicago”
text:
I stayed here for 3 nights in August. I was alone and I had never been to Chicago before. I was there simply for tourist reasons. The hotel was perfect. 
The rooms were amazing. Any amenity I needed. I took a bubble bath in a beautiful tub overlooking Chicago and the lake. 
The location was perfect for everything I wanted to do. I was in walking/biking distance of Navy Pier, miles of walking and bike trails on the lake, the, Symphony park (where I enjoyed champaign and pate while listening to the symphony), boat tours and more. I don' think I got in a cab or on the L once. Though, I did have a bike at my disposal. 
The club on their roof is awesome if you are young and hip. I am not, but I did enjoy seeing it. Apparently, on Friday and Saturday nights, it is impossible to get in unless you are beautiful or a guest of the hotel. 
The Spa was a great way to end my trip after I had checked out of the hotel at Noon.
I asked the concierge for recommendations for theatre show, etc. and he gave me tickets to Chicago Live for that day.

title: “You Be the Judge...”
text:
You be the judge…According to their website, Club Quarters is a “private, full-service hotel for member organizations”. They also accept reservations from the general public. Since my sister and I planned to be in New York the weekend of the New York Marathon, we went online to a travel website, and prepaid for a standard room (queen bed) for two nights at the Club Quarters Midtown near Times Square. When we arrived, because hotel management claimed there was nothing else available, we were given a room with one twin bed. When we complained, it was politely implied that we would have to make the best of it! The desk clerk said he would try to move us to a standard room for the next night and (by the way) providing a roll-away bed “wasn’t allowed”. It was late and the ‘discussion’ was going nowhere – so that at least one of us would be comfortable, I let my sister sleep in the twin bed and I slept on the floor. The following day, the staff was unapologetic and evasive when we mentioned compensation, stating that they had the right to assign rooms according to the ‘run of the house’. (So that must include cramming two people into a room clearly designed for one?)
 It’s been over a month and we have yet to hear from either the Club Quarters Midtown or from corporate headquarters even though a registered letter was sent to both explaining our concerns. Since we are talking ethics (?), I will say that the travel website offered compensation after they got in touch with hotel management and also found them to be uncooperative. 
 Club Quarters Midtown is described online as part of a “new concept for the hotel industry.” …No thanks. It’s well-priced, in a good location, but there is no way I can recommend this hotel. For those fellow travelers who still want to take a chance – pack an air mattress and sleeping bag just in case.
 – L.V.

title: “Very average....”
text: Unfortunately another very average experience at a Starwood property (and yes, I am an SPG member.) I was booked into a North tower room that has a bathroom from the 60's, the ac was temperamental (ran hot air until I called, then no ac at all), the tub filled with water during a quick shower (ick!), the fitness facility was well equipped but stifling hot...the location was a plus, but next time I will pay more and stay somewhere else....

title: “What a tasteful,clean & well staffed hotel!”
text: My sister & I stayed a saturday Night here & enjoyed courteous service and quite clean & well appointed rooms. Cons are that we could clearly hear the toilet flushing in the room next door and the location is a bit out of the way. However... It was neat to spend some time in Chinatown / little Italy. And subway is not far.

title: “A-Mazing Stay! Hospitality at it's finest!”
text: From the moment I made my reservation I knew I was in for a great stay at the Mokara. The concierge called me the day before my arrival which was a special touch. At check in I was greeted by Philip Sanchez, Concierge, and he was very professional and fresh flowers were sent to my room and I also received a phone call after arriving to my room to make sure I was satisfied with my accommodations. My stay was now off to a great start and it only got better. The staff sure understands the customer and service, they made me feel special and pampered my entire stay. Everyone I ran into was polite and professional, from housekeeping to room service. I loved my room and the amenities, here are some of the highlights I enjoyed: A super clean room, fabulous comfortable mattress with luxurious sheets, oversized fluffy white towels, a bathrobe and slippers at the bedside along with nightly turndown service, a bottle of water, a bath butler, real water pressure in the shower, complimentary internet and coffee delivered daily and yes... fresh brewed, a bath butler and pressing service (ok I didn't use either but they were available by pressing a button) and a great patio. The gym was clean and well kept and that is where I met an amazing caring employee Caroline who works in housekeeping and really loves her job, she also offered me suntan lotion and cold water when I ran into her at the rooftop pool. The restaurant Ostra was right on the river walk, great for people watching and the manager Michael McClellan went out of his way to make me feel welcome at his restaurant and the chef prepared my scallops to perfection. I travel a lot and this was one of the best experiences I have ever had, this hotel so gets it and that is why I had to write my first trip advisor review. I encourage anyone coming to the San Antonio Area to select this hotel, you will not be disappointed, the only problem you will have is going home to reality after they pamper you, you will not want to check out! I already booked my room for Oct 2013 for a convention I have to attend!

title: “Probably Best to Go Elsewhere”
text: The hotel is right off the Interstate, but not in the best location. Homeless guys live under the bridge at the Interstate and the area is known for high crime (found out after the fact). Parking lot lacks adequate lighting for the area it is in. The staff was completely unconcerned about the air conditioning not working in the lobby/breakfast area which sweltered at times with the crowd. Hot breakfast consisted of one tex-mex egg dish and the usual continental bagels, etc. SLOW wireless. Sleeper sofa was very short and uncomfortable. Mattress was also uncomfortable.

title: “Beautiful hotel, service lacking”
text:
Great Modern & beautiful hotel and well appointed. Crabtree Evelyn Toilteteries,etc. 
Hotel has a screen that you can use to check out if your flight is on time.
It is connected to a terminal to the airport.
Free shuttle to terminals that are not within range.
The had awsome christmas decor, a train, santa, the whole nine yeards.
However, as with most Hilton hotels, the service was lacking. Ar my room I find a dirty sock from a prior guest.
This will never happend at a Marriot.

title: “Close to Galleria but pretty standard as a hotel”
text:
Went to a trade show and this was one of the selections. Had first a room close to elevator and seems that the noise of these travels more than expected through the cement walls. They moved me without any issues and had a pretty standard fair room for this type of hotel. All involved in any of the services were so forthcoming and so friendly; a pleasure from this aspect. 
Right across the street from the Galleria makes it pretty convenient for shopping but otherwise not much around.

title: “Five Star Experience”
text:
I read many reviews on this site and booked it with some reservation, but found it to be MUCH better than I anticipated. I was greeted by EVERYONE at the hotel. Doorman, bellman, maid, concierge at every corner. Staff was very helpful. The concierge staff is very connected and can get reservations for many places that are booked or don't even take reservations. I went with a room that was a bit smaller so we could have a view of the beautiful city hall. Bathroom was great and very comfortable bed. 
They must have gone through a staff change since the summer, as I see many bad reviews from that time, but I really felt a difference my stays at Omni's and Marriots. It really was a beautiful place, and definitely on a different level of quality from the 4-star hotels.

title: “Hotel Belvedere is a fine choice for location, price and comfort”
text:
We heard about the Hotel Belvedere from friends. The hotel is a clean, comfortable, centrally located establishment. They do their prime mission very well. We did not try to experience the restaurant or other amenities. My sense was that most of the guests were stopping in for a sleep while enjoying NYC. You can leave your bags after check out.
We did not ask much of the staff, but they were helpful and pleasant. The concierge is honest and helpful in his opinions.
The neighborhood has many good restaurants. Fun.
The Belvedere still charges for wireless internet.
Will return

title: “Disappointing”
text: Old world elegance, superior location, very friendly staff, fabulous view over the park and the Bay but... no mini bar, no tea/coffee making facilities ($20 to order a cup of tea and a coffee) and $10 per device per day for internet? Left a sour taste for a 5 star rated hotel.

title: “Above and Beyond”
text:
1 - Hotel rooms, while not huge, are a good size with lovely furnishings. Bathroom split between vanity and toilet/bath - very convenient. Beds are so so comfortable.
2- Nice outdoor heated pool.
3 - Nice restaurant, as well as bar. Monday nights they have bud-spud-steak for $12.95 - beer-potato-steak. Good deal.
4 - Location is the best. Close to all Wharf activity. Five minute walk to Trolley.
5 - Friendly staff, great concierge desk - and when Sheraton tell you "if it not right, just pick up the phone and dial 0, and we will make it right". And they actually mean it.

title: “Great Location”
text: We used this hotel as a base from which to explore DC and were not disappointed in our choice. Much of the old character of the building has been retained which gives the hotel a nice feel lacking in the larger chains. Our room was a perfectly adequate size, in good condition and very clean. Surprisingly the hotel has no pc facilities available for guests' use, which I would have thought was pretty much mandatory these days. Guests have to forward emails to the front desk to get any printing done; what a waste of their time! The White House area is within an easy walk as are good restaurants. We went into the bar a couple of times, pleasant enough but watch the $s fly away!

title: “A stay in the heart of San Francisco”
text: Stayed 7 days at the Suites second week in July. Third time in the last four years that we have stayed at the Suites and as always it was top notch. The location is the heart of San Francisco with a cable car stop in front of the hotel, fisherman's wharf two blocks south, and Geridalli Square one block west. The 1 bedroom suite was just remodel with a 50 inch flat screen in the living room and balcony with a view of Alcatraz island and the shores of Tiburon in the distance. Service is number 1 with staff very helpfull in providing restuarant recomendations and tourist information. Little Italy is a four block walk and Chinatown about a 20 minute walk. Parking in the city is difficult and expensive strongly recommend a multi-day metro pass that provides use of all buses and cable cars. Saving you much money and headaches. Also recomend going to the dinner theater of Treato ZinZannni at Pier 29.

title: “Very nice airport hotel.”
text: I've stayed at this hotel a half dozen times over last few years and have always found it to be a quality hotel. Rooms are clean and updated and include a safe in the closet. Very close to LAX airport makes it convenient for early morning departures. Quality windows keep traffic and aircraft noise to acceptable levels. Nice gym and pool area. Lobby area has this funky new age music playing that is to loud and annoying. The bath towels on this last trip seemed thin and worn.

title: “Great Hotel for family weekend in Houston”
text: World class hotel with impeccable service. I stayed 3 nights Friday thru Sunday with my wife and two young kids (age 6 and3). Vickie in reservations was great and even though I was booked on a SPG points stay she upgraded us (I'm SPG Platinum) to a jr. suite so we would have more room with the kids. Upon arrival late Friday night they upgraded us another level because the front desk agent was concerned that we would not "have enough room with the kids". Talk about looking out for their guests! Upon entering our suite with a huge living room and seperate bedroom we were greated by coloring books and a new monopoly game for the kids! As if that wasn't enough they had also brought us a Texas shaped chocolate box with chocolates and chocolate covered strawberries. My daughter thought this was awesome!!! All in all we had a very relaxing stay and will definately be back!

title: “One of the best locations for a hotel”
text: My husband, myself, our two children and our friends (who also have 2 kids) recently spent the weekend at the Sheraton Inner Harbor Hotel. The location of the hotel was perfect! We walked to the Inner Harbor, National Aquarium and restaurants. The hotel was very nice and the staff were helpful. It was great for a weekend getaway. I will say the only thing that was disappointing was the pool is extremely small and four children can get very loud and excited...which does not make for a relaxing atmosphere for other guests without kids. We also had a bit of a problem finding an affordable breakfast in the morning. Room service is pricey and the Orioles restaurant is not much better as far as price. I personally do not wish to spend 4.00 on a bowl of cereal for my children that I know they will not finish (that is just me). Other than that, it was a good stay for the weekend.

title: “Recommendation Depends on What You Are Looking For”
text:
First the pluses: The St. Regis is well located on Fifth Avenue near Tiffany's and other high end shops. It is a very short walk to Central Park and a five minute walk to Rockefeller Plaza. The beds are comfortable, the room size is quite good and it is a Grande Dame New York hotel property.
Now for the the mediocre to minuses:
Our two rooms looked out onto brick walls. One room had very little natural light and the other had virtually no natural light at any time of day. When booking the room, I noted to the St. Regis reservation clerk that I had seen an advisory on Trip Advisor that some rooms looked out on brick walls with no natural light. As this trip was a gift to my parents I told the agent that it was important to me that their room, at least, had some kind of view. I was assured that at $1,100.00 per night per room (and as a Starwood Preferred Guest) I was getting superior rooms with some sort of view. It was disappointing for me when that did not happen although some may not be concerned by that.
Also, the service was only "good" and not the "excellent" I would expect paying the rack rate of $1,100.00 per night. For example, The St. Regis prides themselves on providing butler service. Personally (and this is another case where personal judgement comes in), I did not find having a butler terribly useful. For me they really just became someone else to tip (and the expected tip, as a per cent of room rate, was high). Our butler was polite but essentially just showed us around the room as a bus boy normally would do. They did offer to serve coffee or tea in the morning as part of our wake up call which is a nice idea. However, as I was travelling with my young daughter I asked if she could have a hot chocolate instead. The butler advised that I would have to make that arrangement through room service at a charge of something in excess of $10.00. At $1,100.00 per night, I think the hotel could have been flexible enough to offer hot chocolate for the wake up call. However, I will leave that up to the reader to decide. For me it was a niggly item that at this price point should not happen. Also, our room rate included a bowl of fresh fruit but on arrival we only had an empty bowl. Not a big problem especially since the butler said the bowl would be filled right away. However, it ended up taking two reminder calls and, even at that, the fruit did not arrive until the next afternoon. Again, just a niggly but one I don't expect at that price point. Butlers will also do a complimentary shoe shine overnight, and will iron up to two garments per day gratis. We did not need those services so there was not advantage to us there, but I recognize others may find that service useful (although with or without butlers most hotels at this price point offer at least the complimentary shoe shine and the expected butler tip at the end of the trip would have more than covered the cost of having a garment or two ironed).
Finally, the food at the hotel is mediocre and, with the exception of the bar which has a beautiful mural that is worth taking a look at, the central restaurant suffers from poor lighting and an overall bland feel. To those choosing to stay at the hotel I would recommend eating meals elsewhere (even the highly touted afternoon tea was uninspired). Thanks to the great location there is a variety of very good restaurants and eateries including several that offer high tea.
So there you have it. I have nothing terrible to say, it was just below expectations. On my next visit to New York, I will seek a hotel in the same locale but will forego the butler in favour of a room with a view and natural light.

title: “Terrific staff, lovely hotel”
text: This hotel is a bit pricy for a basic room (US$240.00/night,) however Boston is an expensive city and the price was worth it for the quality of the service received. All staff I encountered here, from the bellhops and waiters to the front desk personnel and concierge were very competent, professional, and friendly. Also, I ate several meals in the hotel restaurant and must say the quality of food, especially for dinner, was outstanding. Room was very clean with some nice luxurious touches, like the linen and bath products. The location was also within walking distance of Boston Common and other attractions.

title: “Fab Location”
text: Excellent location, Cable Car stop at the end of the street which takes you to Fishermans Wharf. Shops in the same street, plus a Mall at the end and Macy's next street up. Rooms are a good size, plus the beds were amazing! Staff were very friendly and accommodating. Highly recommend staying here and will definitely return.

title: “Went in August... Enjoyed it!”
text:
I got a great deal on octopustravel.com (much better deal than my friend who stayed in a cramped hostel). My friends and I were shocked by how awesome the room was! It was very very nice, updated, and clean. 
The elevators sucked but hopefully they have improved on that. I had a good experience w/ the managment there, but I don't know about the higher ups. The location isn't bad. We were able to walk to the Empire State building, and for much more needed exercise, to Time Square. The metro station is about 2 blocks away. And there's a somewhat expensive deli nearby which was open late. All in all, I give this place 2 thumbs up!

title: “A beautiful hotel with excellent service”
text: We stayed at the Westin Boston for an anniversary weekend because the site of our wedding reception (the Seaport) was booked and we are so glad we did! Our weekend begin at check-in where we met guest services agent Nick Cintas who could not have been more kind and gracious. Upon hearing it was our anniversary he upgraded our room giving us an amazing view of the city! We had cocktails at MJ O'Connors (on site) and the staff there could not have been more attentive and fun. Upon returning to our room after dinner, there was a complimentary bottle of champagne waiting for us. Simply a wonderful weekend at a beautiful hotel where clearly service and attentiveness is their first priority. I highly recommend the Westin Boston.

title: “ICK!”
text: This place was horrible! i wrote several complaints to management explaining what happened to me during my stay (i wount go into the details here). All i have gotten in reasponse are condisending responses from whoever answers the mail and email there. I have no idea how this company can stay in business with such bad customer service. Do yourself the favor and spend 10 extra dollars to get a hotel that's door dosen't read "no refunds after 15 min."

title: “Great location!”
text: If you want to be central to everything stay here! Great location, great service and great staff. My boyfriend and I enjoyed our stay at the Orchard and will definitely be using them again for our future travels to SF. I want to thank the front desk especially for checking me in early :)

title: “This was the WORST place for a honeymoon!”
text: My husband & I spent our wedding night at this horrible place... it smelled raunchy... the furniture was tattered and had unknown stains; the bathtub had cigarette burn marks all across the top (this was supposed to be a non-smoking room); molding was detached from the wall; there were cobwebs; the sink was leaning... there certainly was NOTHING renovated about this hotel as the ad suggested! Had it not been so late at night, we certainly would have found another place to stay. We will NEVER stay in another Knghts Inn

title: “Amazing view!”
text: We had a night in the junior executive room overlooking Coit Tower and Alcatraz. I can honestly say, our jaws dropped as we walked into the room. The room was quite long with a window going from one end to the other that covered Nob Hill almost to the Ferry Building. Coit Tower looked like it was just a stone throw away. We did not want to leave. Because of the massive windows, it was a little noisy, but beside the sumptuous bed, there were earplugs. It was not bad enough that we used them however. We also indulged in the TRU spa and did a couples rainforest experience. The staff was amazing and we would most certainly do this again.

title: “BEWARE...THIS IS NO 3 STAR HOTEL!! (More like 1 and a quarter, if that)”
text: Got a great price on Hotwire for a 3 night stay at a 3 star hotel, which was the Red Lion Denver Central.
