First of all, the entrance is pretty tricky, we missed it twice and had to get back on the highway and turn around and figured it out on our third try. When you walk in, the lobby is very pretty and gives off a nice ambiance plus the front desk staff were very nice upon check in. THIS is where it all ends. The elevator, we determined was being hoisted up by a guy with a wooden wheel, a piece of rope and a sandbag, it was soooo slow, we eventually just used the stairs up to the fifth floor. There is a disgusting aroma that wafts the hallways that reminded us of filthy outhouses with the underlying notes of fresh urine...it was on all the floors (even in that elevator), gross. The room itself was okay, the bathroom was clean and the linens and towels were fresh, but the carpeting through out was so nasty that I wore my flipflops at all times, gives me the shivers thinking about how grimy they were. The ice machine on our floor never worked while we were there and no one resolved that issue until the day we checked out when a small bag of ice was delivered by maintenance. There is a train that goes by in the middle of the night, but it didn't bother me too much. I would never, ever stay at this property again...oh and I forgot to mention that a few doors down a woman was screaming bloody murder and making a huge disturbance for well over an hour while some members of the staff including housekeeping just stood around the hallway. Eventually the police, the ambulance and the fire department arrived (and brought the additional noise with them) and took the woman away. Worst hotel stay ever, except for the front desk staff. Don't do it!!!

title: “Four Seasons at its best”
text: We just had spent four great nights at The Four Seasons Chicago and to our great surprise, we rediscovered both the great Windy city and well run, cosy 4S Chicago. 4S offers both the privacy and clean, spacious rooms with attractive view (stayed on the 37th fl). Hotel offers proximity and great access for shopping on the Magnificient mile, museums and the University campus. And above all, the unforgattable Chicagoen hot dog served at their restaurant is unmatched. thanks to the entire team (bar, restaurant, CONCIERGE and entire room service) for great stay. A forever fan of the Four Seasons brand, Milan P.

title: “Terrific place to stay”
text: Great view of the river. Comfy bed and pillows. Luxurious terry cloth robes. Coffee on your floor starting at 6:00 each morning. Chocolate and port wine with turn down service. Nightlight in the bathroom -- I'm always forgetting to bring one. Our stay came with full breakfast each morning: my choices -- pancakes and bacon one morning, eggs Benedict the next; croissants so flaky they melt in your mouth. Menu is fairly extensive for breakfast. All of the staff were wonderful -- helpful and caring. Glass of wine upon arrival with live piano in the lobby in early evening. New amenities with old world charm. Highly recommend.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: great hotel.... great location.... nice and clean... wonderful staff

title: “Disappointing”
text:
Stayed here last week, very disappointing. 
Arrived at the Hotel to be told that we had been rebooked into a different hotel for 2 nights of our stay and would have to walk up to that hotel.
When asked why we were moved was simply told, it just says you were rebooked on the computer. I dont know why. 
Very frustrating. Had to walk up two blocks to a horrendous hotel with all our luggage and stay in a hotel with no elevator, tiny television, tiny bed and awful bathroom. 
As a result of being moved around for half the stay we obviously had to CHECKOUT of the other hotel by 10am and then check in was not until THREE PM at Broadway. 
Incredibly annoying wasting a day in New York relocating hotels, storing luggage etc etc.
Finally made it into our room and was okay. We had a private room with private bath. The only major complaint i had was the bed is quite small, no air con or heating and the light in the room was remote controlled, sounds amazing BUT it had a mind of its own and would switch on and off at all different times through the night! ~ One night in particular it turned on a 1am, then 3am and then repeatedly at at about 3.30am.
You can turn the remote control light off altogether at the wall BUT then you cannot operate the fan! Being on the fourth floor with no aircon the room gets incredibly hot even in fall. 
IF you can look beyond all these nuances the location is great and one block from a subway, wifi is free but in the lobby ONLY. Starbucks and MacDonalds a block away also have free wifi and plenty of drug stores and restaurants in the area. 
I personally wouldn't recommend staying at Broadway to any friends however the area is great to be based in for NY.

title: “Great Stay”
text: I had a wonderful time. I flew my husband out to see me as we had not been back to CA since getting married there.The staff took excellent care of my husband and during our stay!!! The location was central to any place we wanted to go. The amenities in the room were the best. This is the kind of greeting that we hope to have on our next holiday in San Diego.

title: “Can't get more noisy than this place”
text: Stayed at this hotel for two nights in October 2011. The property is a bit worn and is a typical HIE property. The noise from the freeway not 20 meters from our bedroom window was unbearable. We turned up the air conditioning to full thinking it might drown out the noise of the cars but it didn't even help. If traffic noise is a problem for you avoid this one!

title: “Good location - tytpical city hotel”
text: We spent three nights at the Parc 55. Very impersonal as most city hotels are but there was just something about it that did not endear you to this hotel. It was fine for what we needed - excellent location. Took the BART from the airport and it is nearly on the doorstep. Great location for all transport and seeing the sights. Room was fine however a little pokey for family of four and the double beds were very small. It was noisey and the people in the room next to us had the TV blaring until 4 a.m. - just what you need when you have completed a long haul flight and have been up for nearly 24 hours! There was no help getting through the door from the bell staff even thought we each had a case and rucksack - they just watched us. We picked up our hire car (dollar just round the corner from the hotel) when we were leaving San Francisco but heard that the parking was extremely expensive and a bit of a nightmare.

title: “Jordan Gandara, bellman extraordinaire, was helpful, friendly, and went out of his way to assist me/all guests.”
text: While staying at the Town & Country Resort Hotel, I needed medical attention and was concerned about getting to and from the hotel to an urgent care facility. Jordan Gandara was kind enough to help me locate the closest facility as well as drive me/pick me up so I didn't have to worry. He was kind, helpful, and compassionate to a traveler who was new to his city/hotel. I am very grateful for his kindness and help.

title: “Not as advertised”
text:
Though the staff were all really friendly, this was not a great experience. The website and post-booking confirmation promised Wifi in the lobby and in the individual rooms. I can tell you for a fact that there is NO Wifi in the rooms (as I am connected to the broken ethernet cable right now), and the Wifi in the lobby is inconsistent and weak at best. Even the connected internet is slow and weak.
It's great that the hotel offers free breakfast and, during the week, free dinner, and I certainly enjoyed the free wine and beer. However, the quality of the food wasn't great. Breakfast was so-so. The rooms are nice, large, and comfortable, with small kitchenette (including full-size refrigerator), which is great for families on vacation, but don't come here if you're on a business trip and need consistent internet. Also, don't come here if you want to avoid families with a lot of small children.
The bed was comfortable, but the wake-up call was late. The bathtub was slow to drain, as was the bathroom sink.
I am really shocked by the high ratings that other reviewers have provided. I can only imagine that they were here for casual family vacations that had no expectations beyond room and board. Admittedly, I didn't try the pool or gym, but I was here for work, and I would not come back again if I needed to have amenities for a business trip.

title: “Excellent Hotel. Great Fitness Center”
text: Had a great stay, The hotel was great. The only problem we had was the ice machine on the 2nd floor. It did not work our entire stay. We contacted the front desk and they told us they would have it fixed, but it never got fixed. We had to go to the 4th floor to get ice until that ice machine gave out. Other than that everything was great. We really liked the Fitness Center.

title: “Weekend in NYC”
text: My boyfriend and I stayed here for 2 evenings on a weekend in June. The hotel's location is excellent and is within walking distance to many local attractions. The staff will gladly hail a cab for you if need-be. They definitely go out of their way to make sure that you're enjoying your stay and have everything you need. One of the girls (Kelly I believe) even ordered our tickets for the 9/11 memorial and slipped them under our door! The complimentary bottled water and snacks are definitely a plus, especially after a long day of sightseeing. The room itself is nice--spacious and clean. The bed is very comfortable and the black-out shades are a nice touch. I have mixed emotions about the shower. It was really difficult for me to get a happy medium between warm water and a straight flow of water. I'd recommend just a standard rainfall showerhead. The only downer for me was that I had noted we were there celebrating a birthday and a room with a view of the Library would be great. Also, I am a Hyatt Gold member. Neither of these were noted nor acknowledged during our stay. Other than that, I'd definitely recommend! It is a bit pricey, but you're in NYC so that's to be expected!

title: “The Right location for exploring Fells Point”
text: Out of a possible ten, we give this hotel a five. Location is superb, right on the waterfront. Exterior architecture is period perfect - and this is a fun and historic part of Baltimore. Signage is a bit weak, but we found the right place to pull up in front of the hotel to visit the front desk. The lobby desk was easy to access, and desk personnel were attentive. Lobby sitting areas looked a bit jumbled in terms of decor. The upstairs has an interesting layout, with short ups and downs due to the combination of buildings that make up the hotel (not suitable for a disabled traveler). Our room with high ceiling was large enough to move around in, with hanging space for clothes and a little lobby of its own. Bed hangings were tastefully done but aging. The lightweight reproduction furniture was tired and worn, scuffed and chipped; the carpet was significantly stained. Bath was simple but adequate, mostly clean and the hairdryer worked. We arrived late and wanted a quick simple dinner, so asked for a bistro recommendation and were directed to a next door restaurant. It turned out to be a 'white tablecloth', full service restaurant associated with the hotel, which no one had mentioned. Our meals were fine but took forever, so the recommendation was not on point for us. On leaving we thought the Hotel might be a great base location for those who want to barhop and party, or those who like it quirky. We found it neglected and kind of sad.

title: “Great place to stay if you're visiting BU”
text: I came with my daughter to visit Boston University. This hotel couldn't have been in a more convenient location, just one block from campus. The staff was very friendly and welcoming. The rooms were clean, very accommodating and comfortable. I also felt very safe.

title: “Honeymoon..”
text:
I treated my wife to a 4 night stay at this amazing hotel as it was a once in a life time opportunity. I booked room only and was glad of that as on arriving at the hotel I enquired about adding breakfast, which would be an extra $40 per person per day. So decided against that at we had breakfast out everyday, much cheaper.
We had a king superior room on the 12th floor which had an amazing view of the Chrysler building. In all the hotel was everything we expected it to be, just a shame that we will probably never be able to stay there again.

title: “Outstanding”
text: Beautiful hotel with outstanding staff and services. Great location. They even upgraded our room at no extra charge after we had previously stayed 2 nights and booked another a few days later. Very courteous and friendly staff. Great restaurant and bar.

title: “Elegant room, beautiful Central Park view”
text: We stayed here the last weekend of January and loved it. Our room, although on the small side, was gorgeously decorated and had the best view of any NYC hotel I've stayed in. There was even a telescope on the windowsill, and Central Park in the snow is breathtaking, especially after dark. Room service was amazing -- cocktails were delivered within 10 minutes of our placing the order, and came with a rose in a bud vase on the tray. Granted, the lobby public areas are confined, but everything is beautiful and elegant.

title: “Eh”
text: I drove up and was really surprised. It really didn't look anywhere near as nice as the pictures made it out to be. There were a lot of people just hanging out infront of their rooms, kinda shady like. It is right on the highway and you can hear it. The wifi is pretty slow and you can only pay for it by going to the office. After two nights here I upgraded. It's clean but there isn't much to look at. The TV is like a 20" CRT, been a really long time since I've seen one. One weird thing was instead of exchanging the towels they just took them. Left me with just a hand towel after I had hung up the two I used. Prolly won't come back.

title: “Busy”
text:
Good place.
Busy.
Stayed here due to traffic and an early flight in the morning. $239 for a Wednesday night.
You can arrange to drop your Hertz rental car here at night and take the shuttle to the airport in the morning which is convenient and actually shorter / quicker than returning the car in the morning to the Hertz location.

title: “Nice hotel with horrible security”
text: Was attending an event at the conference center across the street. Hotel was very convenient, rooms were clean and very nice. Unfortunately the hotel is NOT secure! There are three dining places and continuous foot traffic. During the four day stay we were approached daily by 3 different beggars who were well dressed just "hanging" in and around the lobby and gift shop area. My coworkers purse was stolen in the lobby area and attendees from another conference had a bag of supplies taken. Wouldn't stay here again! We actually moved to a more secure hotel at the end of the week!

title: “A damn fine hotel.”
text:
Excellent rooms, excellent service and great location. It's close enough to all the places you want to go to in Manhattan, though cabs are usually waiting right outside the door if you want one -just ask the doorman as you step out.
My one and only issue is the change they made to the bar a few years ago, replacing a lot of wood with metal. Not my kind of thing at all and I wish they would change it back asap. The bar staff are friendly and professional.

title: “Great hotel”
text:
Loved the Palomar! Funky decor and comfortable rooms. The staff could not have been nicer. It's not often that my husband and I want to hang out in the lobby but that is exactly what we did during the free happy hour! They even gave us a free ride to the restaurant for dinner. Parking was expensive but the valet's were very efficient. Centrally located and right off the freeway. 
Only complaint was the barking dogs on my floor but they seems to calm down by the time we went to sleep. Maybe all the dogs should be on one designated floor?!

title: “Alternative Location”
text:
Stayed at this hotel for show at convention center, great alternative spot. Clean comfortable rooms with mini fridge and microwave. Fitness room in basement with tredmills, elipticle and bike. No weights of any sort. Free shuttle to and from convention center and train station. Mall is 5 minute walk behind hotel and has a few restaurants to eat at. $5 airport shuttle as well. 
If you want to escape the over priced rooms near convention center than I would reccomend this location and I would stay here again if need be.

title: “Don't pass this hotel up!”
text: We almost passed up this hotel due to the previous reviews here. Don't miss it, unless you are seeking the standard canned plastic typical American hotel chain experience. The Camino Real boasts countless historic touches including a magnificent Tiffany glass ceilinged bar. The staff were very warm, friendly and helpful with restaurant tips to local places. Yes, a few things are a bit out-dated decor-wise such as the bathroom. But the bathroom worked fine -and was huge. For $100 a night we had an enormous suite style room on the 11th floor, with incredible views of the mountains to the south and west. Acceptable pool, too. The Mexican food in the restaurant was really tasty and you can walk to what is left of the old downtown, including a nice grassy square with historic buildings. We also think $7.00 for parking in a downtown hotel is a perfectly reasonable charge. But if you want free parking and you want to be close to the Walmart and the malls, this is not the place for you.

title: “Good hotel for a large hotel”
text:
I stayed here for one night before heading to Martha's Vineyard. It is a large convention style hotel (not my typical choice) but I was pleased with the overall experience. Things did not start off well (waited in the SPG Preferred line for about 10 mins. to check in), but things got and stayed better after that. I was given a spacious corner room with most of the SPG amenities. (Why is it so had for Sheraton to put robes in all of their SPG rooms?) The room was clean and the bed up to usual Sheraton standards.
I did like the fact that there were express elevators to the SPG floors.
I was able to walk to Fenway and there are many shops and restaurants in the area.
Staff was friendly and knowledgeable. Concierge lounge was large and open on weekends.

title: “Beautiful Hotel”
text: We booked our rooms at half price through an internet discount and were not disappointed. Gorgeous hotel, valet area is very small. Got a free beer and free coffee at the bfast buffett. The breakfast buffett was ok, but we wanted a real breakfast so went down the street but enjoyed the free coffee. Room was great, clean and roomy (king suite). However, there was no fan in the room and the front desk was unable to provide one. The pillows were extremely firm so our necks kind of hurt the next day, but the beds were more comfortable than I thought they would be. Nice velvet curtains to drown out light as well. Great location, they stowed our bags the next morning after checkout so we could go roam around for a while, which was awesome.

title: “Very impressed!”
text: We were four friends visiting NYC for the Canadian Thanksgiving long weekend. We found our room to be well appointed, very clean and comfortable. Great location in midtown close to Times Square, Central Park, theatres, restaurants and shopping. The only thing we missed in the room was a mini fridge to keep our drinks cold but other than that the service was exceptional from the restaurant to the bellhops to the concierge and the front desk. We would definitely recommend this hotel and stay here again.

title: “More cons than pros”
text: Walked into impressive lobby and got checked in. Upgraded to a standard double which was an adequate size (cosy queen must be tiny!). Room is dated and in need of refurbishment. Bit smelly, but clean and tidy except for the odd exposed wire connecting the lamp into the wall and the bathroom door not closing properly. The air conditioning unit kept us awake for much of the first night. Tried switching it off and opening the window - but street noise was just as bad. Next morning requested that the air con unit was fixed. Had to complain again when we returned to the hotel later that afternoon as still not repaired. Engineer came up and replaced the unit within the hour. On last day checked out with no problem. Asked a member of staff if the hotel would look after the bags whilst we enjoyed our last day, he then proceeded to make 2 phone calls before passing us onto a colleague - rude. On returning to the hotel to collect the bags the doorman found one, but then I had to go into the room to find the other 2 as they had not been stowed together. All in all the hotel was not worth the money we paid. We have previously stayed at Club Quarters at The Rockafeller Center which put The Roosevelt to shame and was a fraction of the cost. Don't be fooled by the impressive pictures on the website - this needs to be refurbished!

title: “Great front desk...Noisy plumbing.”
text:
For a one night stay it was decent. The ambassador was as nice as can be. He was down to earth, kind, great smile. The front desk agent, Gabriel, was super pleasant. Got us checked in quickly and had a wonderful attitude. 
Two major cons: 1) $35 valet. 2) Thin walls. I could here the person upstairs urinating, that's how thin. Then the pipes knocked around for 15-20 min.

title: “Hospitality abounds”
text: All the members on the staff here I meet truly care about about what they do, how they do it and who they do it for...their guests!!! This is certainly a cut above the rest with a great location, service, food and atmosphere. Everyone seems to go beyond what's required to make their guest feel welcome with a warm greeting and a smile, followed by exceptional service. This hotel is consistent and persistent with their high standards of quality. Many thanks!!!

title: “Not the best place to stay.”
text:
I was really looking forward to staying at the Pearl. After reading most of the reviews on trip advisor being positive, I thought we were going to be staying at a really cool place. The restaurant food was ok. Movie night was cool. Our first night at the hotel was a Thursday night. After the movie we went back to our room. The room smelled good. But, there were many areas which could have used some attention. Dust along the edges of the walls, Nicks in the nice white furniture (would look better if touched up), Bathtub really gross and needing to be replaced (found out the next day that the drain could use attention too....standing water while showering), the caulking along the bathroom floor was so bad and the glaze on the tile was coming off. Under the sink the pipes are rusting out. Just needed much needed repair or replacement. There is a hairdryer, but it is very sticky with hairspray and tons of lint in the vent. 
The noise from the hotel is awful. The same retro music playing all night long. And a huge gap under the door to the room, which does not help at all! One last thing, the bedding is soiled. I woke up after the first night and was going to pull up the comforter, this is when I saw the stains! Gross!! So, I left a note asking to be replaced. The comforter must have been just turned around, as the stains were still there! I would not stay here again! Staff is super nice and cool, but attention to detail is lacking.

title: “Good location is as far as that goes.”
text: Carpet was filthy with dirt. Dead cockroaches in the bathroom. It was all about price, location and Albies Steakhouse Inn as the reason to stay there. I would stay there again to save money. But there are many other options in San Diego's Hotel Circle for similar prices.

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
The location of this hotel is great. Located a couple blocks away from miracle Mile and the Navy Pier, there is plenty of shopping and dining opportunities. 2 grocery stories are within a block and with refrigerators and microwaves in the room, you can save a little money.
The free breakfast is great but not very accessible for wheelchairs. Service staff didn't seem to care. But that was the only example of poor service. Everything else was great.
The lack of free Internet was disappointing for the price of the hotel. Rooms are spacious and well decorated. The sky lounge is several floors up, located over a bowling alley and movie theaters but you'd never know it.

title: “Not your average hotel.”
text:
Great location! Just a short walk to Michigan Ave. We had one of the more expensive rooms (the deluxe king). It was very spacious. The staff was pleasant for the most part. Easy check-in and helpful concierges. We didn't have any trouble with hearing people or TV's in other rooms which I have seen stated by many. 
The crowd to the Pump Room is a little obnoxious. We didn't bring "formal" wear, and apparently should have. Prices were a little steep, but expected. 
Our room was nice and spacious, but only because we upgraded. The beds are very low (basically 2 feet high) but we were comfortable. Honestly, we expected more from the room as far as cleanliness. The bathroom was decent, except for an already-used toilet paper roll upon arrival. Really? I think even Motel 8 changes their toilet paper for new guests. There were also "Chex Mix" on the floor against the mattress, so apparently their cleaning is subpar.
Other than that, it was nice, however, we will probably stay elsewhere for the price when we visit again this spring.

title: “Good business option for downtown Houston”
text:
I often stay here when I'm in Houston for business and think the only real reason to stay here is for business travel. It's in downtown and there is little to do here in the evening, so if you are on your own, there aren't many options for dining out or other ways to pass the time. Beyond that, the hotel is fine. The staff is friendly and professional, the rooms are comfortable and decent-sized, and the hotel has most amenities you'd expect in a hotel of this class. And the cookies at check in are a nice treat.
The downside: pricey breakfast, you have to pay for Internet access (they used to have a free internet station in the lobby but I think that is now gone), and breakfasts aren't that good. 
One other nice thing about the hotel are the corner rooms. I don't know if this is the case on all floors but sometimes I am assigned one, and they've turned out to be very large 2 room suites, the size of an urban apartment. They have expansive views and while not luxurious, it's nice to have all the space.

title: “Nice Hotel”
text: Very nice hotel, great staff, quick check in,. Loved my room which had windows all across the wall with a great Dallas Skyline view. Would have given a rating of 5, except that there is no free Wi-Fi in rooms, only on 1st floor. Other than that, would highl recommend!

title: “Pricey however nice.”
text: Hilton is proud of this property. Value for the dollar is a bit out of whack. The rooms and public areas were clean. The restaurants and price of cocktails were quite high. Internet access in room at $14.95 plus tax should be an amenity included for the price of your stay. Access to meeting rooms for our function was convenient. Value for dollars spent, fair. In room toilet tissue, "John Wayne" brand.......Roguh & Tough. Needs to be softer. Staff at check in and checkout was less than cheerful. Checkout was the worst. An error was found with the bill and I was made to feel as though it was my fault. If it were a personal visit with a choice, I would have searched for an alternative.

title: “Best hotel I have ever stayed in.”
text: Great location! Very friendly... Beautiful room...

title: “So Welcoming!”
text: We arrived in San Diego late at night after a horrible flight from New York. The staff at the front desk were so welcoming...we even were given warm chocolate chip cookies! We stayed a week. The room was spacious and clean. We worked out in the gym almost every morning. There were treadmills, bikes, elliptical machines, free weights, medicine balls, bosu, mats.etc. We never had to wait for a machine. Most times, we had the gym all to ourselves. We were given complimentary breakfast passes. Choices for breakfast were eggs, sausages, pancakes, fresh fruit, oatmeal, cereal, etc. The chefs actually came out from the kitchen and asked if there was anything in particular they could make for us! My husband requested an omelette and he loved it. One night, we got drinks from the bar and sat outside next to the fires. The hotel is located next to a shopping center which made everything very convenient. We ate lunch and I got a pedicure at the mall. We would definitely recommend the Doubletree Hilton Hotel in Mission Valley. We will definitely stay there the next time we travel to San Diego.

title: “Not bad”
text:
I liked my stay in this hotel. everything was ok.
the rooms was beautiful
the service was good.
and we were happy with the breakfast .
when we come back to Dallas we will want to stay there again.
God is good and will always provide for everyone to came and visit your hotel.

title: “Great location - not so great service”
text: Upon arrival we discovered that the hotel had booked us into a deluxe king room and not the corner king suite, we had reserved and paid for. They did not have a corner king suite availaable so we stayed in the reg room. It was ok but not what we booked. They offered a small credit. It will be a one time experience there.

title: “Stay could have been decent if it wasn't for bad wireless connection”
text: I knew that the hotel was old when I booked the room, so I was aware of what that means - lots of noise from other rooms, possible issues with warm water, elevators not working. All of that could have been ok, but the fact that you had to pay for your wireless connection in the room (different prices for different speeds), and that despite of that it was totally unreliable - made my stay frustrating. Had to go sit in the nearby Lavazza cafe for a good connection :| Other than that - the location of the hotel is excellent indeed.

title: “Simply ... the best!”
text: Flew into Newark. Hopped on Coach USA bus $25 return (includes a $5 discount on Grayline Hop on/off Bus on back of ticket). Got off at Bryant Park between 5th and 6th Ave. at 42nd St. and walked 12 short blocks with our rollerbags to The Warwick at 6th and 54th. Maybe took 10 mins or less. Airtrain from Newark stops at Penn Station 34th St. Need to take a cab or Subway to the Warwick. Front Desk staff and bellmen/doormen so friendly and welcoming. Stayed with my 18 year old daughter for her Grad present. Felt so safe and secure in the hotel and neighbourhood. We walked to everything - Herald Square Macy's, Lord and Taylor (for the Prom Dress), Times Square, Broadway theatres, 5th Ave shopping and Central Park. Never got in a cab once or needed the Subway. Location of the Warwick is the best. Hotel was very clean, great bed - no complaints about anything. If you are on a 'touristy' kind of visit - you can't beat the Warwick! Bring lots of money for food - Manhattan is more expensive than London!

title: “Great hotel. Clean, well appointed, and attentive staff”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the Doubletree Hotel at the beginning of our Alaska Cruisetour. Princess Cruises booked this hotel for us as part of the package. My wife and I found that the hotel was clean and well appointed. The room was more than comfortable and spacious. The bed was really comfortable. We slept very well. There was a small problem with the toilet. The flapper needed to be replaced. We reported the problem to the staff on checkout. Did not bother us at all.
Would definitely stay at this hotel again.

title: “Ahhh! Great service, great place.”
text: We traveled on business and ended up at another hotel. Blackstone rescued us, cheerfully. Clean, peaceful room, great welcoming staff. The bakery cafe downstairs has great breakfasts.

title: “Great Experience”
text:
We were looking for a decompression from dropping our son off at college in West Virginia so we thought of stopping at the inner harbor in Baltimore. We made reservations on our way there and arrived at the wrong Marriott (inner harbor/camden yards) We wanted to be on the Inner harbour
and the Marriott has many hotels in Baltimore. The consierge there was excellent he called the Waterfront Marriott and got us in with a Beautiful waterfront room on the 30th floor. The Hotel was great
the employees were great and we had a teriffic time. Just what we needed after dropping our son off at college.Thank You!

title: “Very Nice Stay”
text: I really enjoyed this hotel. The staff was very friendly and welcoming. I am looking forward to staying again.

title: “Good Points and Bad Points”
text: Let's start with the good news and work our way down. The hotel itself is gorgeous. Very Parisian with a nice comfortable lobby full of marble, art on the walls, velvet couches and glass tables each with a collection of coffee arty table books. Beautiful gardens. Awesome workout room. Great location, close to downtown and the American Airlines Center. The rooms we're classy and comfortbable, but nothing special for the $250-plus rates. Food at Beau Nash was okay. We tried both appetizers at the Beau Nash Bar and Beau Nash's Sunday brunch (no buffet just a a la carte menu). Now for the bad news. The lobby, although gorgeous, was hot and humid. Someone definitely needed to crank up the air. Overall, service was very hit or miss. Check-in crew and concierge were helpful, but the staff at the Beau Nash Bar was unfriendly and sometimes just plain rude. For Sunday brunch they "lost" our reservation so we ended up eating in the bar instead of the nicer restaurant area. The service was slow and they didn't have a high chair, so my 3-month old sat on the floor in his car seat the entire meal. (What kind of place doesn't have a high chair these days?) This is a bit nit-pickey but the shower in the room had a shampoo-conditioner combo. For the price you're paying they can spring for separate shampoo and conditioner don't you think? Overall, I expected more from a Rosewood Property - a company known for style, service and not cutting corners.

title: “Good Hotel”
text:
Close to the public transport. Room is clean and cozy. 
But the safty condition is not good around the hotel, especially at night.

title: “Clean hotel, great location, good price.”
text: This is a nice, small midtown hotel with good sized rooms for the price. Beds are new, bathroom had nice towels and toiletries. Cleaning staff were thorough and friendly. The breakfast buffet was basic, with convenient hours. Friendly front desk staff. Very short walk to subway or bus lines.

title: “Great hotel appalling customer servicev:(”
text:
We arrived the day prior to Hurricane Sandy after a nightmare cruise, room was ready at 3pm and was a lovely room with great view. On checking in, i discussed with the check in lady that it was likely that our flight due to depart the next day was likely to be cancelled, and if so could we keep the room on for a few days. No problem mam, we understand please let us know tomorrow if you need to keep it. At 7am we got notification our flight had been cancelled we immediately called the front desk to let them know and we told thats a shame you cant keep be room now be out by 12.00
We were stunned, by noon transportation had pretty much stopped in Manhattan and it was pouring with rain. We ended up walking with all our luggage in the pouring rain in a hurricane around Manhattan trying to find a new hotel. 
We have been loyal Hilton customers for many years including usuing two other Hiltons on this trip. Never again Hilton you let us down big time :(

title: “Hip and cool in downtown LA”
text:
Stayed last week for three nights with several colleages on a biz trip. As we were all staying solo the bathroom quirks were really non-issues. I found the staff totally pleasant and professional from the valet to the front desk to the wait staff in the restaurant. No complaints there and the food for breakfast and dinner was delicious. 
We spent an extended period of time over three days at the rooftop bar and it was a blast. Great views and happy hour prices for food made for a pleasant experience. 
I had no issue with noise in my room and experienced a restful sleep the entire time. The bed was comfortable although it was on a raised platform on the floor. Toiletries were refreshed each day.
Other than my room key becoming non-functioning each day ( I was warned by the front desk to keep it away from my wallet) I had no complaints. I also received a great recommendation for dinner from the hotel mgr to go to Drago Centro (directly across the street) and it was great as well.
Looking forward to coming back with my wife next time.

title: “A fine small hotel with a gracious air and great amenities”
text: This hotel, a short distance from the Amtrak station and Dupont Circle, has a lovely small restaurant, attentive staff, and well-appointed rooms. I would stay there again in a heartbeat.

title: “Nice room, great service, and the park and ride is a deal!”
text: We stayed here basically because it had the Park and Fly option, where you can stay, then leave your car and get a shuttle to and from the airport. The price was a good deal, but when you throw in the parking and shuttle it is a great deal! The room was very nice, and a good place to sleep. We weren't bothered by the airport noise at all. We didn't get a chance to try the complimentary breakfast because we had to leave at 5 AM. When we got back after a full day of traveling from Dublin, Ireland, we made a call and was quickly picked up by Jay, their van driver, who really was a great welcome back to North Carolina. Overall, this is a really nice place and run by people who you can tell care. It would be rated higher on here I have to believe if it was only rated based on their current owners, who according to the front desk took over about three years ago. Highly recommended.

title: “Most friendliest, warm and helpful staff you could wish for!”
text: Back in London after a trip to Memphis with my sister from saturday to thursday and had the most welcoming reception from ALL the staff there. The room was immaculate with the most comfortable beds, we had a double each which was a special treat! The staff were very accommodating and helpful when asking directions for the sights too - Gracelands left me speechless, wonderful place/Civil Rights Museum - very informative and deeply moving/Sun Studios - excellent/Rock & Soul - excellent and Stax Museum very good too. Beale Street is the place to be especially BB King's Blues Bar with Live Music every night..shame weather was a bit cloudy to do the Paddle Steamer trip but just travelling on the Trolley bus was a treat enough..Trolley bus drivers also very kind and friendly as well as the Blues City Tour bus drivers too..An unforgettable fantastic stay and left with wonderful memories... Well done Holiday Inn Select for having such professional, kind and warm staff that made me and my sister feel like we were properly looked after and feeling like home.

title: “Great location and very nice service”
text: I stayed there over Memorial Day weekend for the Cubs/Cardinals game. It very easy to get to just about all the major landmarks in the city. My friends and I had a great time.

title: “Bad Review before the Stay”
text:
This may be a first for me. I am writing a review for this Five Star Hotel because I did not stay there. 
I made a reservation in May for an August 3 night visit for $288 per night. The room came with a $200 resort credit. 
I asked for an email confimation when I made the reservation. I did not get it and called back July 28th and asked for it again. Did not come after an hour. Called back again and was told it might take an hour. I asked them to fax it to me. The fax (because of dark background on the print out) was unreadable. I called back again and finally got an email confirmation on my fourth request.
The email did not contain the $200 resort credit and included a $25 per day resort fee for such "extras" as "fitness center access, daily newspaper, wireless internet and twice daily housekkeeping service" - things which I would expect as a part of the $288 they were already charging per night to stay in a luxury hotel. The only thing listed on their extras that I would care about was a daily newspaper - and I am certainly not paying $25 a day for delivery. 
I cancelled the reservation and went to a better hotel, with no resort charges, for less money.

title: “Good value”
text: We enjoyed the spacious bedroom and separate living area. Bathroom was a small but adequate. The microwave and small fridge were convenient for preparing snacks or quick meals. We found the bed comfortable and room was very clean. The pool, whirlpool and patio were very nice and inviting. The location was near the airport and area attractions were easily accessible . Front desk was friendly and helpful. Overall we found this a good value, particularly for families on a budget. We would stay here again.

title: “First Rate experience”
text: A group of women friends met in Seattle for a mid-week shopping experience. We stayed 2 nights at the Crowne Plaza downtown. All of us remarked that we had never stayed anywhere with a friendlier, happy staff than this hotel. Each person who had any dealing with our experience there was genuinely charming...not in a fake or contrived or ingenuous way, but in such a way that made us feel part of a bigger, happier world. Truly remarkable.

title: “A GEM !”
text: Fantastic hotel!! Perfectly located at a walking distance from the Galleria. Surroundings are safe and beautifully maintained. Free parking is a definite plus. Rooms are very comfy and nicely decorated. Beautiful and clean bathroom. This place is a must! I highly recommend THE INDIGO to anyone! I wouldn't stay at any other impersonal chain hotel after staying at the Indigo.

title: “3 star hotel for a 5 star cost”
text: Although there was nothing obviously wrong with this hotel, I don't feel it was worth the $200+ price tag attached to it. Admittedly, the location was fantastic with almost everything easily accessible (restaurants, bars, shopping, etc). Rooms were very clean and spacious. For our needs it was fine, seeing as we were in the hotel to sleep only. It's the little extras all guests appreciate that would have made a big difference. There was no safe (very important for out of country visitors and pretty much a standard in most hotels), no coffee maker and a ridiculous charge of $12 per day for WiFi! No amenities to speak of, unless you count a tiny 2 person hot tub you have to fill and drain yourself. Upon checking in, I was surprised to not find the typical hotel booklet with services, amenities and important phone numbers until I realised that beyond a bed, the hotel really didn't have all that much to offer! Am I being picky? Probably, but I expected more for the price. Had I paid $50 less a night I would have expected what I got and would have been satisfied.

title: “Friendly service”
text:
We have never met a nicer staff. The hotel itself is also nice even if it is not in mint condition.
Suites are large (for an european) well equiped with full kitchen, chick bathroom and Tv-screens in bedroom and in livingroom. Breakfast with many alternatives. And the surrondings...we loved Georgetown.

title: “Hotel Palamor Dallas”
text:
Stayed for SMU Homecoming 2012. The hotel is a wonderful location if you are visiting SMU - only a few minute walk to campus. The hotel staff was very welcoming from the valet to the front desk staff. They served a very nice wine at the cocktail hour in the lobby. 
The only trouble we had was not being served at the bar (Saturday afternoon) when we stopped in to watch the K-State football game on tv. We were completely ignored and left after 10 minutes of no service.

title: “Old Hollywood Glamour”
text: I loved my stay at the Palmer House, the decor of the hotel screamed old hollywood glamour and the staff and service was also a treat. The rooms were decorated very tastefully and in the spirit of the old majestic hotel. As a Hilton Diamond member I was put on a Diamond floor with executive lounge access. I arrived too late to check out the lounge when I arrived but did attend for breakfast. The breakfast was a continental with some extra items and there were plenty of staff to clean tables and to help with whatever, unlike other executive lounges. I was on floor 20 and the foyer of the floor was relaxing and elegant at the same time and the room was spacious and comfortable. This hotel is an experience

title: “Brilliant!!!”
text:
Absolutely amazing,we stayed here in february 2010 for 4 nights,we stayed on the 11th floor and it really was beautiful,huge flat screen tv,also walk in shower all marble and glass,in the bathroom,you can play music from the t.v into the speakers in the bathroom!! Right in the centre of times square..
Definetly stay in this hotel when we go back again..

title: “The hotel is average.”
text:
We have never seen a bathroom this small in a hotel.
It is a busy hotel with lots of people in the lobby.Location is very good and there are many restaurants and shopping within walking distance.
As other reviewers have mentioned, you can hear loud sirens during the night.
The good thing is that you hardly hear your neighbors and also you do not hear loud door slammings as in alot of hotels.
We have also stayed at the Intercontinental which is located on the opposite side of the street.We will stay at the Intercontinental next time.

title: “Unprofessional, Complete Lack Of Security & Hospitality”
text: After a very disappointing series of phone calls, emails and letters to the President of the hotel chain, this matter is still unresolved. During a recent 5 day stay , my room was ransacked and my personal belongings were stuffed into paper bags and dirty boxes without my consent due to a clerical error from the housekeeping department. The staff claimed that I was scheduled to check out, but made an error on the day I was to leave, and cleaned out my room and locked me out. They did extend my stay the additional night, then had the audacity to over charge me at the current rack rate ! My reservation specifically stated a 5 day stay. I appealed to the manager, General Manager and finally had to contact the President to resolve the matter. It took 5 weeks to finally receive a letter of apology, but failed to do anything more than refund the difference of my reservation price and the rack rate. The lack of professionalism and customer service makes this hotel an embarrassment the the chain and the City of San Diego, DO NOT support or patronize this hotel. You will be immensely disappointed.

title: “Pretty Fabulous Despite Full House Environment”
text:
I attended a conference at this hotel in late March 2007. During my stay, there seemed to be five or six other events being held - this was a seriously busy place! I was mostly okay with that, but my traveling companion found it chaotic.
What Was Wonderful: the conference and exhibit area, my super-comfy room with a view of the river, ease of parking in connected garage, proximity to restaurants and free concerts at the nearby Jacksonville Landing, concierge service (they have these nice little pre-made slips of written directions to the beaches and other popular destinations), toiletries that smell like ginger
What Could Have Been Better: room cleaning service was slow and not that detail-oriented; one of the groups meeting at the hotel was some organization of older teenagers and they were unchaperoned - hotel staff just looked the other way at their disruptive and inappropriate (sometimes lewd) behaviors
Ended Up Really Annoyed That: wireless internet access is indeed free, but I arrived assuming that meant in my room. That's not the case! They have a cafe in the lobby where you can access the internet, but it is anything but quiet or private - everyone can see what you're working on, noise levels were high, and every 15 minutes or so a waiter stops by to ask if you'd like to order snacks or a drink. Ugh! Very hard to get work done in that environment. In-room access was pricey, so you have to decide which way you want to pay.

title: “Great location!”
text: very basic hotel standard, rooms were quite small! the location however was amazing!!! so close to the warf! not a bad place to stay. Not exactly 5 star luxury, but a decent place to stay for value! would consider coming back!

title: “Soccer tournament”
text: Limited service hotels are what they are. This one is no different. Small but comfortable room and of course no restaurant on site. Funky little pool but again, adequate. Location is great and close to other amenities.

title: “Very good stay !”
text:
We were in the hotel during "Irene". The housekeeping and reception staff were wonderful ! We had dinner in the restaurant and were happy that we didn't have to leave the hotel that night.
The room (a corner-room) was ok with a good bed.
The location is super.

title: “Very convenient location, Nice Amenities”
text:
We stayed in Club Quarters in Philly over Columbus Day weekend. This is a VERY conveniently-located hotel - pretty much right in the middle of most major attractions in Philly. The hotel itself has a very nice lobby, and what looked to be a fancy restaurant (we never ate there). Also, we LOVED the filtered water dispensers (with water bottles) on every floor - those were great. The rooms themselves were fine - a little small (especially the bathrooms, which is to be expected for a hotel in an urban setting), but the ceilings were very high, which was nice. The first room we found ourselves in smelled very strongly of mold and mildew, but after I asked for a switch, the second room was perfectly pleasant (and in fact slightly bigger, by coincidence). The beds were not very comfortable (and I'm not a picky sleeper) - the mattresses seem to be the cheaper, older kind where you move and everyone wakes up - but if you're not there for a long time, they're fine.
If you don't plan to have a car in Philly (which we didn't), this is a very good hotel - within walking distance (sometimes long walks, but still doable) from almost everything you would want to do.

title: “Most comfy hotel bed I've ever slept in!”
text: We stayed here for one night the last weekend in June to visit the zoo and catch a Phillies game. (Go Phillies!!!) The hotel was much better than expected after reading some previous reviews. The room and bathroom were very clean. The Jelly Belly jelly beans on the beds were a hit with my 2 yr old son! The beds were so comfortable!! Our room had 2 beds and each had 4 big, fluffy pillows. We would definitely stay here again.

title: “A suprising hotel in a great location”
text:
This was my second visit to New York and decided to stay a little further away from times square. The hotel is set a block from grand central and park ave so close to all transport.
I stayed in a suite on the 7th floor and even had a partial view of tje empire state building, which at night, was beautifully lit up. The room consisted of a small kitchenette, large bedroom, plus walk in wardrobe, and cupboard with safe. The main living room had 2 arm chairs, and sofa bed which was comfy enough to sleep on and always made up every day. The bathroom was clean and had a constant supply of towels, soap etc. It wasnt noisy at night at all. 
The staff were all friendly and helpful, reccomending resteraunts, and easiest routes to get to places.
All in all, a great hotel, with no complaints.

title: “A true gem! Give it a go!”
text:
We stayed at the Hampton inn for 9 nights. This hotel is an amazing find and focuses on the small details others miss. Very clean and ample sized rooms for two people with very comfy beds! Great added bonus is the inclusive breakfast- it isn't fine dining but is ample with plenty of
Choice from hot to continental breakfast. Free snack bags to go are available from reception as well as free water and warm
Fresh baked cookies for your return in the afternoon. Friendly and helpful reception staff and a very approachable manager. Times square is a short 8-10 minute walk and penn station just around the corner. The area feels safe and not once did I feel unsafe in NYC! Will definitely return to this hotel!

title: “A Great Place To Kick Back and Relax”
text:
My husband and I went here last month and enjoyed our time spent.
The rooms are gorgeous with beautiful amenities. Our favorite part was the BEAUTIFUL pool and lazy river. It was such a nice time to relax outside by the beautiful pool all day. The food was excellent and reasonably priced. THE SCALLOPS WERE TO DIE FOR!
They had a beautiful golf course, and the hotel is surrounded by beautiful trees and hills. Its a very nice secluded feeling away from the hustle of the city.
The only thing that was a suprize to us at check in was the 25 dollar per day resort fee on top of your room rate. But using the resort was worth every bit of the 25 dollars paid. 
The food, service, and hotel is BEAUTIFUL. Ive been to many Marriott’s around the world and by far this one is one of the best! We will be back!

title: “Excellent”
text: A fabulous stop. Clean, friendly, excellent location, fine amenities. The bedding was exceptional.

title: “Not great for business”
text: I stayed here two nights for a business conference. The room was very nice but the business facilities are not adequate. The business center is tiny, cramped, only one printer working and that one had an expired cartridge. Plus very expensive. Cell phone reception very bad throughout the confernece area; calls dropped or would not go through.

title: “Probably would not stay here again”
text: I was very excited to stay at this hotel and had even received a friends and family discount making the stay even more exciting. Upon entering the hotel there was an overwhelming sewage smell and housekeepers walking around with air freshener. Something I would not expect for a hotel like this. I had only once visited this hotel once before and it was on a previous stay to Austin last October. I simply walked through the lobby and looked around the bar area and knew right away I wanted to stay there sometime. The smell in the lobby sort of ruined the initial arrival. Aside from the smell there was nothing really wrong with the hotel. The room was on the small size but otherwise very nice. I ask for a room with a nice view and was told that wouldn't be possible so I overlooked a roof of an adjacent building, no big deal as someone who has worked in the hotel industry, I know not all requests can be met. The bar area is very nice and I would certainly go back and enjoy it during happy hour but I don't think I would stay at this hotel again overnight. It is in a great location but there are other hotels that are far better values that are close by as well.

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
I stayed at the Affinia Dumont at the start of October. 
I thought the overall standard of rooms, service and facilities were excellent. 
Check in was quick and easy, 4 lifts, all in order, all of the time. I was on the 32nd floor with views downtown.
The room was large with two double beds, a kitchen (with fridge freezer, oven, microwave plus pans, cutlery, plates etc), plus large desk and chair, plenty of wardrobe space and decent mirrors. The bathroom was smart with a powerful shower and Aveda toiletries (lovely!).
I never heard any of the other guests while there which made for a very peaceful stay. I didn't make use of the spa but would if I stayed again. There's also internet access in the lobby which was useful as I'd not brought a computer. 
The staff here were extremely helpful. They helped me work out which trains to get where and when I needed to see a doctor they put me in touch with one. 
Overall I would highly recommend this hotel and would definitely stay again. The only criticism I would have is that the phone calls made from the room were very dear (although I suppose that's true of most hotels).

title: “The Latham needs an overhaul!!!”
text:
The Latham has a few pluses: it's located in Georgetown, it has a rooftop pool, and one of the best restaurants in town - Citronelle - is housed under it's roof. And it's very reasonable for Washington, and Georgetown. The problem is, you quickly find out why!
The rooms, and the entire hotel, doesn't seem to have been refurbished or updated since the 1980's! The carpets are stained, and smell, as do the rooms. The air conditioning units barely work - and occasionally - not at all. During my stay, the first room I was given had a "window unit" as the AC in the room was broken. To use the window unit, you had to leave the curtains open! Realize that DC is usually around 100 degrees in August...
If you want a good location, and relatively cheap, you'll find it here. If you want good service, air conditioning, and a well-kept hotel, you won't find it here!

title: “Perfectly acceptable, good value, close to Memphis sights”
text: I recently stayed one night on a motorcycle trip. It was a good value, an older motel close to downtown attractions but clean and I felt safe enough walking in the area. i walked to Sun Records for the tour and also downtown to restaurants and to Beale Street in the evening. All in easy walking distance. I also rode my bike to Graceland for a morning tour and they were accommodating to allow me to leave my bags in the room after check-out until my return. I would definitely stay there again if I was just looking for a place to sleep while doing the tourist thing, not a destination hotel. Had a fridge and microwave although I didn't need them.

title: “Wonderful yet again!”
text: Stayed for another long weekend and once again it was superb. The location is unbeatable, the staff are excellent - couldn't be any more helpful, the 24 hour coffee and tea etc is wonderful (especially when you're on a different time body clock) and the rooms and en-suites still full of character. I was expecting the hotel to look a little tired and it didn't! One useful tip, take some earplugs for sleeping if you are in a road facing room - well hey, it is New York! Tony's Restaurant next door is fab - huge, tasty family size dishes. You may pay a little more for this hotel than some others, but in our view it is worth it!

title: “Space, lots of space!”
text: This was my fourth trip to Columbus in two months. Tried a few of the other nearby properties downtown and came out disappointed. Doubletree is not all that much better in looks or feel but at least you get 2 huge rooms with 2 huge 42" LCD TVs and a pretty decent breakfast brought by the friendliest staff that sure brightens your day. The place looks like an episode of an 80s prime time drama, but is it clean and everything, yes, everything works! Given the choice, I'd much rather stay at a foo-foo place but I don't think there's one of those in Columbus. Anyway, my only negative comment, would be that the 2 chocolate cookies I got from the friendliest front desk attendants, were burnt because they keep them in this warming drawer at the reception. Well, I was hungry and they didn't taste all that bad. And I just could not say no to the smiley faces. Checkout was super fast and by the time I made it to the street, the cab they called was right there at 5AM.

title: “Love the location and the price from priceline!”
text: This was the second time I was fortunate enough to get a great price from Priceline for this hotel. I asked for a "quiet" room and was given a room in the Seaport Tower Rm #1565 and it was a great room. With the A/C fan turned on automatic it was fine. No noise from the pool area at night but you could hear a bit of the trains. The room was great--typical business but clean. There was a nice ipod radio, safe big enough for 2 laptops, a small refrigerator, desk, easy chair, standard TV. The king size bed was reasonably comfortable. Yes, parking is $22 a night but for the price I got the hotel for the parking was no big deal. The best thing about it all is the very great location..it was so wonderful to walk to dinner, walk along the water before dinner, go to bed, get up and take a long walk on the harborfront, have breakfast, take another walk....just gorgeous. And yes, it is an easy walk to the Gaslamp District and all the excitement happening there...but this location was so much better. Not sure how it compares to the other hotels in the immediate area, but if you can a good price it is a fabulous place to stay.

title: “Mixed opinion”
text: We stayed here with our baby. The pluses are: good location (near the farmer's market, the Grove shopping) and the Swingers restaurant downstairs is terrific. Staff are friendly and our room (with a kitchenette was large). We dragged our chairs outside in the evening and would sip wine with a nice view of the pool. Downsides: the place felt dirty. Our daughter's feet were BLACK after crawling on the carpet. Some of the untensils in the kitchen had food crusted on them. The kitchenette was undersupplied: one wine glass, one bowl, a couple of spoons and pots and pans. Not even enough to have two bowls of cereal in the morning! Don't bother paying extra for a kitchen; you'll end up getting take-out anyway. The pool gets little sun and is not kid-friendly (i.e., almost no shallow area).

title: “Great location”
text: This hotel is at agreat location- 2 blocks from Fisherman's Wharf. It has a very attractive restaurant and comfortable rooms. My only complaint is the parking- I think it was about $50 a night, plus you have to use their valet every time you get your car out, and we felt we had to tip each time.

title: “Very, very nice”
text: My sons and I stayed here for one night and we liked it very much. Rooms were very clean,and all the staff were very friendly. The breakfast was very plentiful. A very nice stay, and would stay again.

title: “Good staff- coordination lacking in services”
text: We were here for a meeting at the Medical Center, so location was excellent. On check in staff placed us in a room that was not cleaned yet, so my husband had to trek downstrs for another room card. Very pleasant work out room had two eliptical trainers that did not have functioning displays, though they worked fine if you watched the clock. One person tried hard to fix this and a manager finally told me that a battery charger was missing and that they would try to get it fixed. Hotel very attractively decorated - had Mitchell Gold chairs in the very clean king bedded room in which we stayed.. On a Saturday, the lobby was taken over with special events in the am. Attached Peoria restaurant was fine and service was attentive. Transportation to nearby Macy's at Stapleton Mall was excellent. Major positive was staff who wanted to do a good job, but didn't seem coordinated. for some reason.

title: “great”
text: every employee was very friendly and helpful-never had to wait to get help-location is great for being in the heart of gaslight but not where all the party noise is. Turn the ice maker off in refrig or it will wake you up in night with the clicking of the ice moving. In my room the wall tv was located in an odd place in relation to the bed- my friends room was ok. The wifi worked great-the computer in lobby for all to use worked great. The common area in lobby was very comfortable. The bed was too hard for my liking. They use those super cheap plastic sacks for the waste baskets which slip down into the basket

title: “Great location and comfortable hotel.”
text: This hotel is located out of the noise, but within easy walk distance of Grand Central Station. It is an older hotel, but it has been well kept up. The staff was very friendly and helpful. I would definitely stay here again and would highly recommend it.

title: “Superb location, helpful staff, surprisingly nice rooms”
text: I stayed one night for business. The location is central to the Gaslamp District, with restaurants and bars three short blocks from the hotel. The staff treated me like royalty. With an upper-floor location and pool view, my room was large, quiet, and nicely-furnished. I would recommend this hotel to everyone, and stay here again in the future.

title: “Convenient Location near Times Square”
text:
We stayed here for four nights in July and found the location to be perfect. Close enough to Times Square/Broadway and other attractions & popular sites, yet away from the loud, busy streets. It's also close to several convenient shops on either side -- nice little grocery store with beverages and snacks a few doors down, French place next door has good coffee & pastries to-go in the morning, Irish pub a couple of doors down is excellent for a drink or dinner/lunch. Then of course, there are all the places a block or two away. Options are limitless. Subway is close in several directions.
We traveled with our 12 year old son and stayed in a King Executive room with a rollaway bed. There was enough room to put the bed at the end of our bed (by moving a small bench)...a little tight, but okay with walking room. Rooms were clean, bedding/linens were great. We stayed on the 7th floor (room 710), without a view -- our room looked onto a brick wall on all three sides. Sign up for the "Your Desires" program before going and you will get little perks. We had welcome treats ready in our room when we arrived (pretzels and bottled water, but you can chose from different options). 
We got into the city around 6pm on a Thursday and check-in was a breeze. Staff are friendly and knowledgeable. They helped us get a car service to Newark airport since it was the same price (maybe even cheaper) than a taxi and pick up time could be guaranteed. Check-out was just as quick and easy.

title: “Bad Times in NYC”
text: I booked this room 3 months in advance and when I arrived they had given my room away. I had reserved a superior king on an upper floor. I was given a queen in the front side of the hotel which is noisy with traffic. So I requested a quieter room and was given a small room in the back of the building. It seemed quiet at the time but it was not. It was next to the elevator and could here it going up and down all night. Next morning requested another room and was attended to by a very nice young man. I was told to go out for the day as planned and they would switch me when I got back. They lied. They had given my room away again and the only room I could now get was the smallest queen ever. I had to open my suitcase half way under the desk, after putting the desk chair on top of the club chair. What an awful stay in that hotel. I would not recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: “Great Boutique Hotel”
text: Hotel Vintage Park may be part of a large hotel group, but you are indeed treated in a very personal fashion from the valets, front desk personnel, to housekeeping, you are well taken care of. We were greeted by smiling & personable employees/representatives of the Kimpton Corp. Our room, 904, was spotless, well appointed, with upscale amenities. Join the Kimpton club for upgrades & specials! Our resvs were made online & all requests were effortlessly dealt with, including a special rate on an upgrade corner king room with a view of the Seattle Library at Spring & 5th, as well as a peak bay view. Dinner resvs were promptly handled for 'Tulio's', which is adjacent to the hotel. Value, convenience, hospitality, ambience - all at one very favorable price - highly recommended!

title: “Okay hotel see Asterick*”
text: Have you ever seen a trailer for a movie, see it and realize the best parts were in the trailer? That's how our experience was with our three night stay at Custom Hotel. It wasn't bad. In fact I gave it an "okay" over-all rating. It's just the hotel, in my opinion, was promoted as a chic, hip, trendy hotel not in Hollywood or Beverly Hills but by the airport. And it's true. The lobby is very cool, Macs abound everywhere. The pool, although small in stature, makes up with the "W Hotel-ess" gas fire, cabanas tiered seating area and the restaurant/bar, though we didn't partake in the food was everything billed in the Custom Hotel's website. What wasn't was our room. Maybe the hotel is a work in progress and I surely understand why management would rehab the outside first. Curb appeal is everything... Maybe we saw the prop queen before she put on makeup, what ever the reason, the room did not live up to expectation. What didn't do it for us? The bed... I like platform beds. But not ones that "V" in the middle. Our mini frig was on the fritz. Maintenance said the outlet was dead and moved the frig to the room's hallway, near another outlet. My wife's hair straightener worked fine in the old frig outlet, but maybe it's a voltage thing. My wife didn't like the dusk/dirt at the base where the walls met the floors. I know it's hard to to get but a Midwest girl notices such things. She also noticed that. Did not have a hair dryer and had to have one brought up. The hotel water took a while to get going, but it did... And the water pooled as I was talking a shower but still no biggie... Our biggest disappointment was that the wasn't a coffee maker in the rooms... Not that's my fault for two reasons, I show have notice the absent of a coffee maker in the room description and I should not have said to my wife as we packed to leave, "Naw... We don't need to bring the portable coffee maker, there'll be one in the room"... That's one me. Still, the only U.S. hotel we have stayed in that does not have a coffee maker in the room is in Vegas... And they want to get your butts out and into their casinos. What's the Custom's excuse? To make matters worse, there isn't a coffee pot in the lobby either. He only coffee offered at the hotel is when the lobby food area opens at 7:00am at the lovely price of I believe $6 bucks US for two large cups of coffee. When I asked the front desk about the coffee they said the Coffee, Bean, Tea and Leaf coffee shop a couple of doors down opens at 5am then a co-worker corrected him and said it opens at 6am. It opens at 5:30am. Trust me... I was their every day of our stay at 5:29am sharp! Please understand, it's a nice hotel, I do recommend staying there provided your expectations meet reality.

title: “Wouldn't Hesitate to Stay Again”
text:
We arrived very early after a looong trip on Amtrak, several hours before check in time and hoped to leave our bags in reception until check in time.
They could see how tired we were, and invited us to have breakfast in the breakfast room, and prepared a room for us as quickly as possible., While we waited we were able to snooze comfortably in the comfy armchairs of the lobby. The wait was just over an hour.
After all of the excessive charges in Phoenix, it was refreshing to have most of the extras for free at the Drury. Being on vacation it was a shame that the internet computer has blocked most of the social networking sites, but I guess the hotel caters more for the business clients.
The staff were very friendly and couldn't be more helpful. The free drinks were great. ;o)

title: “Cool, restful, unassuming hotel.”
text: We stayed here for 4 nights in April and found it a nice, cool haven from the heat (95 degrees) and bustle of San Antonio's Fiesta Week. We found the 'dark' decor and the space of the suite very relaxing and, as a light sleeper, surprisingly I found the road noise was not at all intrusive but quite soothing (!) as it's flowing traffic, not stop/start. The staff are pleasant and the housekeepers do an excllent job - spotlessly clean rooms - thank you. The soundproofing between rooms is also very good - we were not aware of other guests at all. We enjoyed the short walk to the centre of SA but also used the buses to get around and the yellow route which passes the door is very handy. Breakfast was better than you could expect for a free buffet - fresh, not packaged. For a 'budget' range hotel, it reaches way over that and this is an excellent place to stay in SA

title: “A Palacial Hotel”
text: Stayed at the Waldorf last year and it was truly a impeccable experience. Lobby was Grand and they have a old art piece of Clock right in the lobby. Room was spacious. Stairways, corridors, public areas were all Grand. They have a lot of boutique shops near the lobby. Infact in one of the boutiques, there was a set up made with fine pottery which was a mock up set up for a wedding set up done by the Waldorf... That was interesting. The lounge on the Ground Floor looked really grand with the Lavish use of Leather. Service was simply Great. If you walk around the hotel public areas, it is HUGE and sometimes you get lost if you are truly mesmerized with the Granduer. The history and grandeur of the Waldorf make it a wonderful and a memorable place to stay. It was indeed WORTH a STAY..

title: “Not a second time”
text: Upon entering the cascading water walls and ceiling on the ground level "lobby" (reception desk is on the 7th floor), I was excited to see the rest. I was very disappointed. The dark (LOTS of black and gray) lobby, hallways and rooms were gloomy, not "hip". The shower was terrible! To turn it on, you had to stick your arm in, getting wet before the temp was adjusted and water got all over the outside. Also, not a place to hang a washcloth or hang on when getting in and out (slippery floor). The desk area was non-functional (pencils for writing? why not a pen?) and the drape was very heavy to roll up (actually hurt my hand to do so). Extremely poor lighting. But maybe that was the idea! ? Design doesn't have to replace function; there is room for both. The W didn't combine both. The concierge needed a few lessons in better PR. This W is hung up on being hip..yawn.

title: “Great Hotel and location”
text: Just got back from a six night stay at this hotel. The hotel was very clean and the staff was very friendly. The free breakfast is amazing. More food than you could ever want. The hotel is in an almost residential area. It is close to two metro stops. The area around the hotel is very safe and quiet. I would recommend this hotel to anyone and would stay here again in the future.

title: “Worst NYC Hotel Experience”
text: Upon our initial arrival we had our bags brought up to the room and didn't get a chance to situate ourselves until after we had returned our rental vehicle (no need for one in the city) and ate dinner. On our return, we come to find that we're unable to contact any type of service from our phone - room service, housekeeping, concierge. I had gone down to the front desk and was advised to disregard the service buttons and to dial "0" for anything we're in need of [very well]. The carpet in our room was in pretty bad condition, our phone was missing a couple of buttons on it, the alarm clock was missing, our bathroom had no washclothes and our view was a street view lined with garbage dumpsters right in front of the hotel. You won't be able to miss it as it's right across the street, in front of the main entrance when you arrive. Mind you, the overall look of the room was presentable, but definitely not the "wow-factor" that you had seen online. The bathroom shelf over the sink stuck out so far that when you went to brush your teeth you had to tilt your head a little too far to the side to rinse your mouth out. I did complain to the front desk that evening and again the following morning to where they had accommodated us by changing our room that day while we went to a show. Upon our return, you would think they would've put us in a better location and a better room, but NO, and considering it was our last evening there, it wasn't even worth asking nor going through the frustration of being moved again. Our stay was only for two nights, and two nights of grief. Our second room was stuck back in a corner and our view, there was none. It was the walls of the hotel in the shape of an enclosed triangle with nothing but pigeons and bird poop. The bathroom was missing the fog-free shower mirror that our other bathroom had, and the towel bars over the rear of the bathtub were rusted in numerous spots. I took pictures of everything as we'll be writing to the hotel as well. My husband and I travel to NYC once or twice EVERY YEAR, and aside from the GREAT location, there are so many other great hotels that we've stayed at in the same vicinity. Our money was a waste for the price that we paid. We'd been on vacation for a number of weeks and what a way to end it here. Even though this is our home town, don't waste your money on this hotel! You don't get what you pay for. Want to see a "Dream"? Come to Vegas...I think we got you beat! Everything at the Dream hotel is nothing but SMALL! Best of luck to those who do give it a shot.

title: “Great room, problems with service and security”
text: I stayed at the Hotel Indigo for a recent business trip. I had stayed there several times in its previous incarnation (Claridge Hotel) and had enjoyed the great Gold Coast location; with the remodeling, it's an even better value. The "spa" theme is fun, with rooms and lobby in seaside blues and greens. I had a very spacious room with a lounge chair, big separate area with a coffeemaker, and lots of room to move around. Hardwood floors are a nice touch. However, the woman on duty the night I checked in did not know her job. I arrived late in the evening, so went immediately to bed -- and was awakened by another couple entering my room! They had been checked into the same room as I was. Sure, I should have locked the deadbolt, but this is still not what a woman traveling alone wants to happen. I complained to the manager the next day, and while he apologized, I was not offered any discount or even a coupon for a free drink or cup of coffee. Obviously they're still ironing out the kinks with the service staff at the Hotel Indigo.

title: “Great location, decent stay”
text:
Before booking our stay at this hotel, I too read a lot of reviews that left me nervous about what I would find once I arrived at the hotel. When we arrived at the hotel, maybe around 3ish, our room was not ready , but we were off to meet a friend so it didn't matter. Our room rate was a special that was a decent rate which included parking, so we could leave our luggage in the car. The front desk took our cell phone number and called us when the room was ready, which I thought was a nice touch. 
The room was ok..like others have said, could use new carpet, had thin walls and windows. The only "furniture" in the room besides beds and nightstand were the tv armoire, desk and chair, yet the room was large enough for there to have been a sitting area (maybe chair or two and coffee table). Just made it more annoying that we had to sit on the bed to watch tv, play games (travelling with a child), eat snakcs , etc. Also could have used another floor lamp, the room was rather dark. We were on the 2nd floor which seemed to be very noisy after dark, but this is also the level that comes in off the parking lot, so maybe that was why. The room was clean, the housekeeping staff was great and got us anything we needed. 
For us with a child, the location was great. Plenty to do on Pier 39, easy to walk to North Beach, as well as other areas.
