The heated pool was a lifesaver....our child swam in it everyday, it kept her entertained if we needed it. There is a Walgreens and a Trader Joe's a few blocks away, so it was nice to be able to pick up fresh fruit, etc., would have been nicer if there were a mini-fridge in the room. I didn't check into asking for one, just a little disappointed one is not standard.
We had trouble with the Wi-Fi after the first day or so, but after talking to the front desk they gave us a new code. If I understood correctly, they change the codes every few days or so, and this was not told to us initially and may be why other reviewers were having problems. 
Would I recommend this hotel to a friend? Only if they were travelling with kids as it was hard to find a hotel with a heated pool in the area. Would I stay here again? Not if it were just my husband and myself, I'd want something less noisy, more up to date.

title: “I didn't hate it”
text: I booked my reservations BEFORE reading the reviews and got really worried. But it really wasn't so bad! Yes, the hotel has seen its better days--dingy does describe the room decor. Beware also of MASSIVE construction in the lot next door to the hotel. It didn't bother us too much because we were gone during most of the days--you definitely can't sleep in. However, it is very close to all of the sights in D.C. The hotel staff was very friendly and helpful. Despite reviews to the contrary, the pool was just fine. Great after a long day of sightseeing. I traveled with two kids and it suited our needs just fine. It was clean and comfortable, a decent price, and convenient distance from EVERYTHING you'd want to see while there.

title: “I wonder...”
text: Sometimes I wonder who is really writing these things good and bad. I'll try to be as honest as I can here guys. We checked in pretty late on a Saturday night, and the gentleman at the front desk was very accommodating and the room we asked for was exactly what was given. The lobby is very nice, granite floors a sushi bar Krispy Kreme and Starbucks we took the elevator up to our room, the floor we were one was a little dingy for what I would expect for even a 2 1/2 star hotel let alone a 3 1/2. We got into the room and it didn't feel clean there was a permanent black mark on the toilet, fixtures were broken, carpet was very worn, in the corners of the room it looked like it had not been vacuumed in quite sometime, our pillow had something that looked like baby spit up on it and it looked like someone had exploded a can of soda all over the wall that never was cleaned off. Going into these type of situations, I try to keep my expectations low I in the past have regularly stayed at 2 and 2 1/2 hotels and the cleanliness is about what you would expect for a 1 1/2 or 1 star hotel. We were to tired to call down and get a room change and move all our things, that combined with the fact that after looking at the hallway I didn't have much confidence a new room would be any cleaner, so just turned the light off as quickly as possible to avoid seeing anything else that would disgust me. The hotel is ok, front desk ok, rooms not clean at all.

title: “definitely not worth $220+ / night”
text:
my boyfriend and i stayed here on a recent trip to philly. the location is great, the front desk staff is great, but the room was mehh... ok. the room itself is a good size, but the furnishings were nothing special. for some reason we had 2 double beds which made sleeping together not very comfortable. since we were in such a rush and were only there for the night, i didn't bother asking for a different room.
the biggest problem i had was the heating/cooling unit. it was set on COOL when we arrived... when it was barely over freezing and snowing outside!! sleeping without a thermostat was difficult; i woke up in the middle of the night to turn the damn thing off before i started sweating. and then of course this meant that in the morning when i woke up, it was freezing!! 
if there are other options available to you, i'd explore those... this hotel was not very ideal.

title: “Location, location, location”
text: This was our second time staying at this hotel. Our reason staying here is location, location, location. The lobby is nice and big but very misleading. Like our first stay our room was not very clean. The carpet was not clean. There was hair and mold all over the bathroom. One of our outlets did not work correctly, because my curling iron plug kept falling out. Our air filter was filthy. We did have a great view though. My parents room was in the same shape. Their toilet cover looked like a dog chewed on it. What could cause that? Our main reason staying here is for the location. This hotel is on top of the metro. It is very nic to just take the elevator down and hop on. There is a neat little sandwich shop under the hotel. We saw dozens of people stopping by to buy pastries and ec. After a certain time they halve their prices on the goodies. They are also open for breakfast on Sunday. It was much cheaper eating there instead of the hotel. We have never eaten at the hotel. We probably will stay here again only because of location, location, location....

title: “Best group party ever!!!”
text: I just wanted to thank not only our friend for inviting us to this resort but the managment and staff as well for one of the funnest trips we have had in a long time! We were invited along with 4 other rooms of friends to celebrate a birthday at the AZ Grand Resort. I was skeptical that this would be fun and relaxing but the staff at this resort was amazing along with the property itself. The grounds, pools and rooms were magnificent, clean and well appointed. The husbands were set up with golfing one day and all the kids and Mom's had a blast as well. The cake that was made for the birthday girl by the on site bakery was to die for! This hotel earns 5 stars from our family. We travel a lot and have stayed in many types of hotels but this one is the tops! Thanks so much! Can't wait to come back again. Think I'll have MY birthday party there!!!

title: “Beautiful lakeside setting”
text: Room was nice with a beatiful view of Lake Austin. Breakfast buffet (eggs, sausage, biscuits, fruit, grits, and more!) and menu service was great, with friendly and efficient staff. Close to downtown and the Sixth Street music scene. Bed was comfortable considering that I'm used to a water bed (not rock-hard like some hotels). Wireless internet worked fine with good speed. Access from I-35 northbound is a bit confusing the first time, but Google maps gives clear directions.

title: “Right in the Heart of Times Square buzz!”
text:
We spent four days in New York city and stayed at the Marriott Marquis hotel in Times Square. This hotel is right smack in the middle of Times Square and you can feel the buzz of the city here. It is a nice hotel, the most impressive feature of course is the glass lift in the atrium. We were on the 37th floor looking down on Times Square and the view alone kept my youngest son entertained. We found the room to be very adequate for our family of five, with a super king bed , pull out double couch and roll away bed. The room was big enough to accomodate us all quite easily. There were 3 or 4 restaurants in the hotel although we choose not to sample them. We were going to eat The View rest upstairs and went up to check it out first. The desserts looked lovely but forget ordering the dinner, it looked shocking so we decided to give it a skip. If you want to visit the View to look out over New York city at night , do yourself a favour and skip the dinner and just order the dessert option.
Hells Kitchen and New York are full of good restaurants , it just takes first timers a little while to find out where the best are, The Marriott Marquis is rated four star, I would say it is prob a 3.5 , given some of the four stars we have stayed at here in Ireland. It is a good hotel but not cheap as no city centre New York hotels are cheap anyhowl 
If you want to be smack right in the heart of Times square, don't mind paying a bit extra for convenince as you can walk everywhere from here in mins, enjoy a good standard of hotel then book here and ask for a high floor . We had no problems with noise although we were in the thick of it.This is a huge hotel and quite impersonal if you don't mind this, I found Marriott Druids Glen far superior for customer care. The Marquis is so huge, it lacks any personal customer charm but we didn't mind that as we were only there to sight see anyhow. I don't imagine it lives up the Marriott usual standards for customer care but I would still recommend it as anyone visitng this area won't be spending a lot of time in the hotel itself.

title: “It was like sleeping in a closet”
text: Rooms are small and beds are very uncomfortable.. People are nice and beakfast was great..

title: “Comfortable and well located”
text:
We stayed in the Belvedere for 6 nights ( we had to move to another hotel when delayed by the volcanic eruption as the Belvedere was full)
We found the rooms comfortable and fairly spacious (we had a standard 2 double bed room for myself, my wife and 2 children 11 and 12), and the equipment adequate for a short stay.
The hotel is very well located between Times Square and the restaurants in Hells kitchen along 9th Avenue.
The only downside was that when we couldn't get home as planned we needed the internet to find out what was happening, and it was expensive and unreliable in the hotel.
To be fair, the hotel refunded me the charges, but I had to go elsewhere to get a connection.

title: “Beware: Oversold led to an upsell”
text:
We stayed at the Loews Regency NYC from August 10-14, 2012, and used the Summer 4 Suites promotion. We have a 7 year old and a 1 year old and liked the idea of the Loews for Kids program. We booked a king one bedroom suite with an adjoining superior twin room. Upon check-in, the adjoining room wasn't ready. At 9pm, the adjoining room still wasn't available, so they open a second adjoining room. When we walked in the room, the carpet was wet and the entire room reeked of cleaning fluid. We were told that the carpet would need to be shampooed the following day and we'd have to leave. Obviously, this was unacceptable. We were told this room was the only one available and so I requested that the Loews walk us to another hotel. Instead, the Loews upsold us to a VIP suite. The Loews told us basically it was our problem that we weren't happy with a room with wet carpet. Housekeeping acknowledged that this room wasn't fit for occupancy, but the front desk offered us the ONLY other option - to move to a rarely used VIP suite (for an additional $1000) - a permanent resident lives on the floor and we were told doesn't like to be bothered, and this suite is the only other room on the floor. Not exactly VIP treatment to be asked to walk on egg shells.
Throughout all of the above, I was stranded in the airport 500 miles away (JFK had closed) while my wife and kids were in the hotel. It was 9pm when the room with wet carpet was opened and with two tired kids, the options were limited. I didn't get to the hotel until 2am.
The Loews didn't honor our original reservation and beyond that gave us a room that would never been given to a guest walking in off the street. They took the opportunity to upsell us when they should have either upgraded us or walked us to another hotel. It was insulting to be given a room in that condition with wet carpet and reeking of cleaning fluid and then be told it was our problem we weren't happy with it.
It's a shame too because it's a lovely hotel and a great location. But the problems with the adjoining room (and the room with the wet carpet was given to us instead of the room we originally reserved) and that the hotel chose to upsell instead of upgrade makes me not want to go back or recommend this property.

title: “Location, location, location (Safe)”
text: Stayed June '04 for 4 nights (2 Adults and 2 Teenagers). Never visited SF, LOCATION WAS THE KEY. AAA price $56 a night. We we able to park Free every night. Pool is being redone. Rooms clean, older but clean. Didn't spend much time in room, so this was ideal for a budget. Easy walk to Mel's Diner-A Must.

title: “Great overall hotel, location and service”
text: This was our first visit, and we were more than pleased. The location was fabulous. We could walk anywhere. The accomadations were great! The service was outstanding! I highly recommend this hotel. You feel totally safe here.

title: “Always a nice stay at the Vintage Court”
text: I have stayed here a few times already, and have enjoyed my stay. Vincent has taken my reservation over the phone several times, and has been very helpful with all the required details. The hotel's location in an excelent central location so you can do many activities while staying here. This stay involved going to a San Francisco Giants game. The walk to and from the stadium is not too bad, plus allowed for some trips to local establishments before and after the game. I missed the evening wine hour due to the game, but I recommend it for all those who stay here. The room was clean, and the bathroom was well stocked.

title: “great hotel and location, not so good staff”
text: So the hotel was great, great location especially for two 22 year old girls who want to shop, party and site see. Our room was great and although there was no view at all it was very comfortable. The only problem we had was the staff. Normally I would like to avoid using names but I feel that Rachel should be mentioned. She should NOT be in the service industry! When a couple in front of us asked for a statement folio she slammed down the phone in anger and was huffing and puffing, me and my friend were actually too scared to approach her at any point to ask any questions incase she exploded in the same way. She was always in the back office and never manning the front desk and i dont believe i seen her smile once her attitude was appalling. There was also another lady whos name I didnt get, she was also quite ignorant and abrupt. On the bright side the valet staff and another 2 front desk staff a young girl and boy were both very friendly so we were actually able to get in a few questions here and there. We also used the pool which was fun but very very shallow, nice and relaxin after a full days shopping though. I would recommend this hotel mainly for its location and certainly not for rachel!!

title: “Hollywood Roosevelt: Location, Location, Location”
text: The service staff, from valet to front desk are excellent. We were upgraded without even asking. But, although the room was nice and had an excellent view, the paint on the walls was old and chipped, the furniture was very old and there was virtually nothing decorating the walls. The main restaurant was expensive and nothing special but the biggest rip-off was having to pay $32/day for valet parking even if you never used your car!! If you read the reviews, this is the #1 complaint. But, if you want to be close to the action on Hollywood Blvd., this is the place to stay.

title: “Thanks for the great stay”
text: Wow, what a great gettaway weekend. My wife and I stayed in the hotel while attending my sisters 40th Birthday weekend getaway. The pool was great and the hotel staff was wonderful and made our trip even better. A special Thank you to Suzy and Xandra for making a great weekend even better.

title: “Great Experience”
text:
We have just returned from our first trip to NYC. While there we stayed at Dream Downtown Hotel. What a great location ! It was central to everything including walkable (minutes) to Times Square, Central Park, 5th Ave., etc. . Our accommodations were comfortable and clean and the staff very helpful. The hotel has a great restaurant, Pent House Bar with roof top patio that had great views. We would not hesitate to recommend this hotel to others.
We will be back to NYC in the future !
Charles and Irene Agius
Mississauga, Canada

title: “Staff is extremely friendly and helpful.”
text:
This was my first time to Los Angeles. I did have a very limited time to do research by myself on where to go and what to see, so I used help from hotel concierge. From the very beginning, Tatiana comes across as a very professional and courteous person. Tatiana is extremely friendly and helpful. 
She made me perfect plan for all my everyday activities. She always expressed her personal ideas on which options may be better, it was done tastefully, and I did not feel pressured to choose "her option". 
I highly recommend this concierge for any LA related travel assistance.

title: “Cheap Motel”
text: This is definatley a budget motel...there were cigarette burns in the comforter, an iron burn on the floor and worst of all there was a LARGE crack in the bath tub that had some kind of yellow texture on it. Needless to say I didn't take a shower that night and I wont be staying here again.

title: “We loved The Talbott”
text: We can't really say enough about the hotel. It is very nicely decorated and clean. The staff is very friendly and efficient. It is located in a great neighborhood. Ideally located for Chicago sights. The rooms are a nice size and the housekeeping staff does a great job. We loved The Talbott and would definately stay here again.

title: “Great if: you find dining ahead and pay for a good view”
text:
This is the only hotel I've gone to, so rather than giving general impressions, which are wasted without comparison points, I will give specifics.
The view from Water Premiere rooms is as good as I can imagine in D.C., looking at the Washignton Monument, the Jefferson Memorial, the tidal basin, and some skyline. Take another kind of room and you might not be so lucky. For instance, I once got a "District" room, which provided me with a beautiful view of the wall of the neighboring building, which was admittedly in the "District". If you like views, you gotta pay more.
The location is not great, as other reviews mention. To get to food, you have to go more than a ten minute walk, which urges people who are tired from touring the Mall all day to stay in room for dinner. (See paragraph on room service.) You can get a cab, but how do you know where you are headed, if you are like me and did not prepare eating options ahead of time? The Mandarin did not have a "local cuisine" kind of booklet in the room.
The walking time to the Mall is ten minutes or so, which is not so great in bad weather.
The tidal basin and Jefferson Memorial are right out back, but still take 5 and 10 minutes to walk to respectively. Another reviewer mentioned crossing highways to get there, which is true, but was no problem for me. But just as I was getting a excited about the slow walk on the waterside, with the grass and trees and white stone, I started to see the condition and appearance of the rusty-riveted bridges and industrial train tracks and cracking streets. So I had to settle for the more conceptual beauty of the contrast.
Room service was adequate. It took 20 minutes to get one meal and 30 to get another. If you like a bda joke, try the "Bento Boxes", which are "TV dinners". I put "TV dinners" in quotes because the menu did, which means they get the joke that these 31$, non-Asian trays of food are the same quality as 4$ TV dinners. The difference is you get less food in each of the six dollops that you get to choose. I ordered soup and got a 3X3X.5 inch (no exaggeration) saucer half full of tomato juice. I guess the Mandarin custom is to eat like a cat. My pizza was great, though hardly better than the Cal. Pizza Kitchen version. Oh, and get ready to pay 50 cents per ounce of bottled water, and to be unsure what you will be charged for.
My wife loved the appointment, from the embroidery on the pillows to the transparent shower stall, and I think she spent an hour in the bath for every hour I watched the good cable.
I paid 229$ per weekend night, and the rooms with good views were 375$.

title: “Very friendly, accomodating and professional”
text: We had a group of colleagues in town for a meeting and at last minute needed a conference room, AV capabilities and refreshments. The Doubletree staff was extremely accommodating and provided impeccable service. They made sure we had everything we needed and took the stress out of the meeting day. I would highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Convient to LAX-nice stay”
text: My family and I stayed at this property prior to our trip to the Caribbean in jUne of 09-I have stayed at many a Four Points and this one was outstanding.Very easy and painless check in-prompt bell staff got us to our room-a clean room no hassles-and surprisingly quiet for an airport hotel.They also have re modeled their GYM with all new cardio! They have their own dedicated shuttle to LAX which was also convient.All and all a nice stay.

title: “Disgusting.”
text: While writing this review, I realize there are thousands of people in this world who would just be happy to sleep with a roof over their heads... But as far as the hotel industry goes, this place is an epic failure. This hotel is filthy. From the airport van (with ripped up seats), to the lobby (with loads of shady characters hanging around), to the room.... Oh, the room!! General overall lack of cleanliness lead me to be apprehensive about pulling back the sheets. Unfortunately, my suspicions were confirmed when Bed #1 revealed a shoe print made out of dirt and Bed #2 had about 50 hairs (and very long extensions) scattered all over the sheets.  I only wish I were joking, as I had checked in at 11pm - and was not looking forward to finding a new hotel room in the middle of the night. Obviously, upon seeing the room, I decided to just take the loss ($90/night for this dump and no refunds within 24 hours), and sleep at either the Philadelphia Airport or find another hotel. Despite the general disgustingness of this establishment, I did find 2 positives - the van driver (who was very sweet and professional) and the free (although unsecured) wireless internet (which I used to book at a neighboring hotel). I am hardly a hotel snob - but this hotel clearly lacks the two essentials necessary for a decent nights stay - cleanliness and safety. Do yourself a favor and book elsewhere.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: We stayed at the US Grant for 1 night and it was wonderful. The staff was helpful and friendly. The hotel is beautifully decorated. It is also walking distance to the Gas Lamp District with plenty of restuarant. I would stay here again.

title: “Great Location!”
text:
Good Room, nice location. Kind of sterile furnishings.
I couldn't understand why they bothered putting HDTV in the rooms since the TV reception was the worst I have seen in a city. Any city.

title: “Good central located”
text: We managed to check in very early no problem and the older guy at the front desk was very helpful. The room was a good size, nice and clean but the walls are very thin and you can hear a lot of what goes on in the corridor. The elevator was broken the whole time we were there too. The hotel is in a really good location and cant be beat. Good value for money. recommended.

title: “Lovely pillows but noisy lobby!”
text: This is one of those hotels where you feel disorientated when you go in. Why do they do that?! We arrived from London feeling jet-lagged so to go into a dimly lit lobby with loud music, where we had to wheel our suitcases past the feet of those lounging on white leather sofas, wondering where the reception desk was, was not a great start. The room was fine - lovely pillows, good desk space, though not much space to spread out your stuff on in the bathroom. I think this is more about style than substance, so if you like the feel of a nightclub, go ahead, but I prefer the quiet life. The tripadvisor ratings make it apparent that views of this hotel diverge greatly. Oh, and my colleague said his room smelled of tobacco.

title: “5* experience!!!”
text: This was our first time in New York and we were really excited about our trip. We emailed the hotel in advance to enquire about getting the train from Newark airport. Steven, the General Manager of the hotel sent a swift response explaining our options and the train appealed to us as it was a lot cheaper and quicker than getting a taxi. The train from the aiport was easy and only cost $25 between us and took us to Penn station which was across the road from the Affinia. As we checked in we were automatically upgraded to a deluxe suite, which put a huge smile on our faces! The room was lovely, very spacious and clean. We were lucky enough to have a balcony which overlooked the city and as we were so high up the noise from the street was minimal. We were also pleasantly surprised to find we had been left a bottle of wine and some chocolates to welcome us to the hotel and the city. This was a fantastic start to our holiday! The room was modern and tastefully styled and the bed was very comfortable. The hotel staff were extremely friendly and helpful and in particular we were very grateful for the advice from Norva at reception when using the subway and getting out and about. She was very knowledgeable and provided us with a lot of information about the sights we wanted to see and bars and restaurants we should try. Overall, we had an amazing time and want to thank all the staff at the Affinia for our stay.

title: “Beautiful hotel, excellent service”
text: We are a couple that stayed over Thanksgiving weekend and we had a wonderful time at the hotel and in Washington (a beautiful, clean and classy city). Besides being a grand and elegant building, the hotel is also two short blocks from the White House. From the moment we arrived, the hotel staff was extremely proactive in ensuring that all our needs were met - specifically Lucas, the hotel manager. We are Starwood Platinum level and were treated royally. The rooms were beautiful (we were upgraded to a beautiful suite) and we thoroughly enjoyed every minute of our stay.

title: “Very average experience...”
text:
In short, our "respire" room was small, but clean. The WI-FI was useless on my phone and Kindle...I only got it to work on my Kindle at 9pm one evening. Parking is CRAZY at $50+/day. We asked for a fridge (because we had our infant daughter with us), and it was $25/stay. There were no soda machines, but there is a minibar fridge in the room, where you can drink soda for $4.50/can...typical. One really irritating thing was that the sheets came off the bed part way through each night...leaving you to wake up on the bare mattress pad, and the bed totally dishevelled -- this isn't a picky complaint...it was really irritating. 
This hotel was decently located, and we were able to walk anywhere we wanted. Millennium Park is an easy 5-minute walk, and so is the Randolph METRA station. We asked for a late check-out, and were able to check out one hour later for free. All in all, the hotel was fine, but certainly did not exceed our expectations.

title: “The perfect place to stay!”
text: The Pierre is a beautiful hotel which is ideally located for shopping and strolls in Central Park. All other attractions are easily accessed. The staff could not be more courteous or attentive. It was a weekend of truly gracious living.

title: “Great Stay.”
text: We stayed at the City Club Hotel with our 2 teenage boys in July and at the end of our holiday in Aug. The staff were very friendly and helpful, room was spotless and clean and smelled fresh. The location is great - a 2/3 blocks from Times Square - between Fifth Ave and Sixth Ave. We prefered this hotel to the big hotels on Times Square and would not hesitate to stay here again. Highly recommended if you like smaller boutique hotels.

title: “No Hot Water,Run Down, Dirty and Loud”
text: The first morning we were at this hotel there was no hot water for a shower. The hotel is run down, dirty and loud. The matresses are encased in hard plastic and are lumpy. The curtains do not close all the way, shower rod was bent, and there was no security lock on the door. The roar from I-35 is deafening so you can forget about sleeping. The room had a foul odor. I can't believe Choice Hotels allows this dump to be called a Comfort Suites.

title: “The Marines landed!”
text:
The only problem for us - and one for which we were not very inconvenienced - was that our visit to Columbus for a family wedding happened to coincide with the annual Marine Corps Ball. As a result, the hotel was overwhelmed at check in and valet parking with dozens of simultaneous arrivals of a large number of well-dressed, well-behaved young men and women.... and us.
We certainly don't begrudge the Marines their annual fete, we only wish the hotel had been better prepared for the concentration of activity. Other than that, the hotel and the Marines were terrific..

title: “A GREAT WAY TO TREAT YOURSELF :)”
text:
I found this location to be one of the best in reference to the Laquinta Inns and Suites chain. I came in to this location just for leisure for myself. The room type I had chosen to go with was the Executive King w/Panoramic View. Gorgeous!!! The view was excellent as well as all the amenities that came with it. 
I have to say, that if you are looking for a great room to treat either your significant other, family- or as I did, myself- then this is by far a great option.
The room was very organized and well decorated from the door all the way through.
The breakfast was decent. SN: If one may not want what the hotel serves during the morning hours, there are other eating locations right down the way. I am definitely going back within the next few weeks just to enjoy the great location!
-Jess

title: “Good hotel for Elvis fans!”
text:
After reading many reviews on this site we were concerned, but still excited, by the prospect of staying at Heartbreak Hotel only a couple of minutes stroll from Graceland.
We need not have worried. From our arrival at the airport and the free transfer to the hotel, to our free transfer back for our return flight there was little to worry about - other than enjoying the company of other Elvis fans, and watching and listening to Elvis in the hotel.
Upon checking in and getting our room we noticed a couple of minor issues - e.g no chain on the door and a couple of bulbs missing. We reported this at reception prior to us strolling over to see Graceland in the early evening light and by our return maintenance had sorted these issues for us.
We were staying with our 2 kids, aged 8 and 6, and we had a living room - complete with sofa bed, small hall/kitchen area, bedroom and bathroom. Suited us perfectly. We were there for 7 nights, and although the hotel is not central we wanted access to Graceland - and you cannot get a better location than this. We did spend a few days in downtown Memphis - but as it was only $20 or so for a taxi for the 4 of us the cost was not an issue. The hotel also offers free evening shuttle service to Beale Street and back - which we used on several occasions. Not sure whether this would be much use in peak season - as there were a couple of times we used it and the bus was full - it only seats 25 people.
Additionally there is a free shuttle to Sun studio - but this only seats 10 people - so even more restrictive - but it runs hourly during the day. This shuttle will then take you downtown after you have spent an hour at Sun studio. With returns to the hotel on the half-hour.
The complimentary breakfast was good - basic, but suited the needs to grab a bite to eat before or after the walk-up to the Meditation Garden each day. Unlimited amount of food - bread, biscuits, muffins, donuts, cereal, yoghurt, fruit, choice of juices and choice of spreads.
We only used the bar snack facility in the Jungle Room bar once - and the value for money was good, with decent service and quality.
Marlowe's BBQ restaurant offers a free pink stretch limo service which will pick you up from the hotel and take you to the restaurant five minutes away. The portions are large - the food is good - and all excellent value. The limo is usually then waiting outside to take you back. Great unique experience!
The hotel staff were friendly and helpful whenever we had a need to ask for assistance. The free internet access in the lobby was a great facility, which allowed us to check-in prior to our return journey.
The Elvis memorabilia shop is not big in the hotel - but it is open from early morning to late night - the staff taking short breaks throughout the day - great if you need a fresh fix of memorabilia.
One downside was that they decided to re-paint the bar area during breakfast on our last day - which meant eating with paint fumes all around! Not nice!
All in all I would stay here again - yes it is a 70s hotel, it is not 3 star as it suggests - but you cannot fault it for location or service.

title: “good”
text: Very good Westin experience. great location.. walking distance to tons of night life. Easy for everything. Good executive lounge. Service at the hotel was excellent. no complaints here. Would surely stay again.

title: “Perfect for short stays in NYC”
text:
We just stayed at the Milford and it was perfect! It is literally a minute walk in to the middle of Times Square and subway! 
Rooms are fresh and clean and was cleaned daily with fresh towels each day! The rooms aren't huge but why do you need a massive room your in NYC - hardly the place to spend time in the hotel room! 
Will be even better when renovation completes- I would definatley return!

title: “Wonderful boutique hotel”
text: My boyfriend and I visit NYC three to four times a year. We like to stay in smaller, contemporary, boutique hotels. Dream is in a great central location with Carnegie Deli just around the corner, and Times Square/theatre district in walking distance. The staff was wonderful and very accommodating. The room was rather warm when entered and we had to call the front desk to fix it. While we were out, they 'fixed' it. It never got really cool (which we prefer), but it was comfortable. The room size was larger than many other hotels in NYC, and the bed was very comfortable. The bathroom was small. The restaurant attached to the hotel had great food -- calamari was excellent. The lounge was great -- visually stimulating. We would stay there again.

title: “Couldn't have chosen a better place”
text: We live locally and were looking for a hotel to stay in while we had work done to our home. We thought it would be a treat to stay in Ballantyne but the cost was crazy and they added fees for internet. I had been to Stonecrest hundreds of times and had never noticed this jewel hiding behind the auto bell! The hotel was clean and very quiet, (ask for an inside room).... we took our dog along too. The staff are amazing and even made a special trip to get me british tea for breakfast (you know that we brits need our cuppa!) It made a stressful time almost like going to stay with friends. I would highly recommend this hotel if you plan on visiting Charlotte. It's 2 mins from major highways,very clean, opposite great shopping, restaurants and a cinema. On Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday they supply dinner for free! Free access to internet too.

title: “Horrible Stay!”
text: After a referral I booked 4 nights at the hotel and the rate seemed like a great deal. I had to call the hotel a couple times for information and the staff were always rude. Upon arrival the front desk person took phone calls instead of checking us in and was very unpleasant. When we got to the room, it was tiny! The bathroom has no counter space, a cramped/RV-like shower, and was painted dark green, and had one dingy light bulb by the shower so you can hardly see anything in the mirror. It felt like a cave. There is a tiny closet with no drawers to put your folded clothes. Worst of all, the room has NO air conditioning or fan. The window looked onto the courtyard and a painted wall. At least 12 other rooms also looked out onto the ugly courtyard. The room was well over 80 degrees. Everyone had their windows open so we could hear people talking, the street noise, TV's, etc all night. There were plenty of doors being slammed too. It was too hot to close the window though. We were awake all night long. In the early morning, we called the Hilton nearby and got a bay view room for $40 more/night so we booked it for the rest of our stay and it was incredible. We checked out of Hotel des Arts at 8:00am and luckily were only charged the one night. They didn't even ask why we were checking out so soon. If you like European style hotels, are okay with no a/c, a view of nothing, dark, cramped rooms, and want a hostel-like experience, have at it. It you want a traditional room with a quiet night, comfortable sleep, friendly staff and amenities, go elsewhere!

title: “Very good value and location”
text:
We stayed at the Park Hotel for 4 nights. Prior to the holiday I realised I had lost my reservation details so emailed the contact details on the website and received a prompt reply from the manager Rodel who was very helpful. Most of the staff were very friendly and helpful, eg when we asked about a taxi to the airport we were advised to get the nearby BART instead which was extremely convenient and much cheaper.
The best thing about the hotel is its value considering the location, it is right next to Union Square and about a half hour walk down to the bay. The French Quarter is also very close, which is a great place for dinner. There was some noise from the street but that didn't bother me as I live on a main road in London. The hotel had basic facilities which were everything we needed, except could have done with a hairdryer (which all our other California hotels provided). There was a fridge, basic toiletries and free wifi. Only bad point was the terrible smell in the corrider, but at least this didn't go into the room.

title: “Very nice”
text: Enjoyed our stay at the Magnolia. Very nice, clean, and friendly. Valets went out of their way to answer questions. Having a shuttle service to run you out to dinner , etc. is a nice touch since the only way to park your car is valet parking or the state garages across the street.

title: “The Benjamin”
text: Recently returned from weekend stay there. Fantastic hotel because its location, service, rooms and concierge help. First rate and very good value

title: “Exceeded Expectations”
text: My wife and I stayed at the Renaissance using priceline's "name your own price" and were rewarded with a room for $109. Upon arrival, the front desk upgraded us free after we told him it was our anniversary (which it was). We had a corner suite with incredible views and the room was gorgeous. The staff could not have been friendlier, we really enjoyed the lounge and we will certainly stay here again. All of my expectations were exceeded and my wife was blown away by the suite.

title: “Great for an overnight stay in the city.”
text:
My husband and I live in Queens, but wanted to stay in Manhattan for our one year anniversary. Since we live nearby, we didn't want to spend a ton of money, and staying too far away from midtown would defeat the purpose of staying at a hotel. We found a great deal--$109 for the Sunday of Memorial Day weekend. 
The receptionist who checked us in was not friendly, but was not cold either. The rooms are small, but neat and attractive. While my husband was looking for something behind the dresser, he found a pair of underwear belonging to a previous guest, which skeeved us out, but I could understand how maybe the housekeeper couldn't get back there.
The location was great, with many subway lines within a short walking distance. We walked to the theater district to see a Broadway show, and the next day we walked over to Chelsea Piers. The breakfast was on par with other hotel chains' free breakfast, although it was kind of a turnoff that it is only offered until 10 am.

title: “Great Stay in Seattle”
text: I checked rates all over and found "GReat Rates" on the hotel web page which included breakfast for $132 per night for Friday and Saturday night. The location is great, we could walk to anywhere and it was also 2 blocks from the Monterail. The buses are free all over town if you don't want to walk. The staff was helpful. Ask for a room with space needle view. Small but very clean room and beds. cute little balcony. The continental breakfast had fresh fruit and crusants with a small pot of great coffee. Take a taxi from the airport when you arrive. They are also everywhere around the hotel with no waiting around. I made the mistake and booked the downtown airporter shuttle. This is a bus that makes a bunch of stops and is full. have fun.

title: “Great place for the price”
text: I stayed here on recommendations from another online travel board. For the price I wasn't sure what to expect, but it was good. The bed was big, the pillows nice and fluffy and for being over an airport corridor it was quite.

title: “Great location - very noisey!”
text:
I read the reviews prior to booking about this hotel being noisey. I thought " how loud could it be?". Very very loud from 10 pm until 8 am in the morning. The loading dock for another business is across the door and you hear it. Not to mention garbage pick up at 5 am... We heard it twice in our four day stay. It is really awful - I would not recommend this hotel to anyone who needs a good nights sleep and especially those with young kids. Pillows were great but couldn't sleep so it sucked. Room was fairly modern/ clean. Bathroom was a pain. The sink area didn't have a door and that light switch turned on both the lights at the sink and in the closes door toilet/shower area. This sucked when my husband went to the bathroom in the midde of the night and lit up the whole room with the lights in the bathroom. Bathroom was small and toilet and tub were old and very tight in space. WARNING to parents with kids at thus hotel - the water is VERY hot. Dangerously hot. I like a hot shower - I have them everyday at home but myself and husband both burnt our backs- never been in a hotel where they didn't cap the temperature but this one doesn't - and it should.
Hotel was clean. Scott at the front desk was great ( helped save us money on a limo to the airport). When we checked in there wasn't any excitement (it was our honeymoon) there was no reaction at all the girl was quiet and not welcoming at all like I've experienced at other sheratons. 
Overall I would not recommend the hotel.

title: “Good Airport Hotel”
text: The Renaissance was very plush for the £65 per room per night we paid. The lobby and public spaces were very elaborate and the breakfast included in our price was second to none. A huge buffet and a made to order counter too. The staff were helpful and the pool was nice and particularly quiet while we were there. The rooms were clean & tidy and overall a 4* hotel. Excellent airport hotel.

title: “Loved it!”
text: We stayed here for 2 nights and absolutely loved it. The location was excellent, right on the boardwalk and close enough to Santa Monica to walk. The staff were brilliant, very helpful with regards to where to eat and what to do in LA and how to get about. Would definitely reccommend Venice Beach Suites and Hotel and we would stay here again!!

title: “Falling Apart”
text:
I had booked this room though Hyatt.com and had no problem with the booking process. Looking at the rooms online, everything seemed very modern, well-maintained, and spacious. Upon entering the room I noticed some deficiencies.
First, the closet was so small and awkward that it was almost impossible to hang clothes in. The clothes I did hang got snagged on the door and damaged due it being so small and jammed the clothes behind it. There was only a piece of cheap, poorly placed piece of drywall on the right side of the closet. Personally, I think if they were going to make it so small, they should have left it open with no doors or wall period.
In the bathroom, the tiles were coming up from the baseboard. The shower was cracking and paint peeling from above it, and had ugly mold in the grout. The toilet was stained and had mold growing on it also. Hair was in abundance throughout the bathroom (on the toilet, the floor, the shower, and wads of hair were folded up inside the towels).
In the living/desk area, the decorative divider panel was coming out from the wall (nails exposed) and one of the glass panels fell out while I was asleep making me think someone had came into the room and broke something in the middle of the night. The electrical outlet had a 6 outlet adapter on it that controlled the room lighting - when you turned out the light switch, the outlet turned off. (Very inconvenient when you tried to charge your phone/laptop at night with the lights off). The electrical outlet itself was loose and falling out of the wall, which seemed unsafe. The ice bucket had hair inside it, as did the drink cups that were placed in the cubby holes under the tv.
In the bed area, one of the beds seemed very wobbly and both were SQUEAKY! The air conditioning unit (which is the 'old school' under the window type) didn't work in the room efficiently. We had to place it down to 50 degrees just for it to come on.
I had came to Dallas because my sister had a doctor appointment with a specialist at Baylor Medical Center. We sneezed and felt sick the two days we were in the hotel. I am just hoping that it wasn't due to the mold or anything else in the room.
I travel quite frequently, and this was my first Hyatt experience. I do not believe I will return to Hyatt hotels in the future.

title: “Great staff”
text:
We recently stayed for six nights. We've stayed in Hampton's before, but never one like this.
It's hard to imagine this building was designed as an hotel. With the reception and concierge desks either side of the elevators, if the staff need to speak to each other, they have to speak over or through people going to and from, or waiting for, the elevators.
The route to the breakfast area, crosses the route that the kitchen staff have to take, to service the serving areas. The whole of the public areas seemed cramped and lacking in natural traffic flow. At times, it must be a nightmare for staff working there.
Thankfully, they have very special staff at this Hampton Inn. Nothing appears too much trouble and they go out of their way to make you feel that you are a valued guest. 
We had a room on the 17th floor. The same side as the entrance. But even that high up, the noise from the traffic was very loud from 5.00 am. A definite need for some 'Airline Hotel' style sound treatment in the rooms, on this side of the hotel. On the plus side, no need for an alarm clock. However, our friends had a room overlooking the Chrysler building side, which was very quiet.
Finally, there is an extractor grill in the conservatory/atrium, that blows cold air in, rather than extracting stale air. Not very comfortable in winter.
Even with the observations above, we would most definitely stay again. SoHo is a very interesting area explore, and the staff, really make this Hampton Inn special.

title: “Am I cool enough for this hotel?”
text:
This is one of the few hotels I've been to that I felt like I needed to be dressed in the latest fashions to fit in. But I understand that this is the vibe that W Hotels are going after and I love that they've picked their niche and are going for it.
My wife and I have stayed at the W Seattle 3 times through the years and enjoyed our stay every time. I don't think I'd recommend this hotel as a "family hotel" but I don't think that is what they're going for anyway. If they're trying to capture the 28-50 year old, that wears the latest trendy eye wear and whose wardrobe is at least 50% black clothing, they've nailed it. 
The lobby area has a very cool vibe with a large sitting area and books to relax after all the walking one invariably does in Seattle.
The rooms are very cozy and most offer a pretty good view. All the design throughout the property has a very clean and contempory look.
The location of this property is ideal and pricing for the rooms is quite reasonable for the location within a major city.
I would totally stay here again but just need to do a quick run to Nordstrom first so I feel like I fit in.
Shared more on our blog: www.worldfamilytravellers.blogspot.com

title: “sleepless at the nikko”
text: My husband and I arrived on a Wednesday. Rooms were clean but small. Hotel is near everything. Cable cars, Powell bart, shopping galore, wonderful restuarants. Returned to hotel for the evening around 9. We were awakened by loud fire alarm and intercom message that a fire alarm went off and they were looking into the situation. Then we heard fire trucks around the hotel. Since I fell asleep with wet hair I got up to dry my hair got dressed and got my belongings and waited for instructions. They never called. My husband called and they said every thing was okay. No apology, no nothing. Finally went back to sleep around 11. The next morning the front desk, concierge, all acted like it was no big deal. Contacted the director of operations. "Oh I'll look into it. " Checked out and charged $15 for internet service. Funny we don't have a computer. They looked us over to make sure we didn't before adjusting the charges. Stay at the Hilton across the street.

title: “Very surprised.....in all of the right ways!!”
text: My hubby named his own price on priceline and got this room for only fifty nine dollars. Then I read the reviews and was like OH MY GOD!! What have you done??? It sounded like we would be in a dump by some abandoned buildings, but I was very pleasantly surprised!! Our room was so clean...the sheets smelled fresh & bleached, and the king bed was the most comfortable that I have ever slept in. I'm online right now looking to buy the featherbed that was on the top of our mattress. I am VERY EXTREMELY picky and demand the best & i can tell you that I was very happy especially for the price. The hotel was overbooked and I did hear them say that priceline overbooked them & they turned some people away....not sure if those people had reservations but we did & we got our room in a hurry. Also, I heard them say that they were out of extra pillows & blankets but our king bed had FIVE luxurious pillows, so we were ok...PLUS they gave us 2 toothbrushes for free since i 4got mine!! No traffic noises but we stayed towards the back on the last row. Pretty close to all of the areas attractions, but the highway that takes you to the feeder that leads to the hotel is kind of tricky to get onto. OVERALL impressed & very comfortable!! Highly recommend & would stay again!! While you're here GO check out Chunky's burgers (the four horseman burger) as seen on Man vs. Food....crazy experience and Lou's Pizza for the 5ft pizza, but be ready to wait for a table for a LONG time.

title: “Good”
text: Excellent location right next to subway and Metro Deli. Nice staff, adequate room, good comfortable bed. Coffee maker in room would have been nice. The big negative was the bathroom - musty, moldy smell and cheap, thin plastic toilet seat. Evidently some attempt had been made to redo the bathroom areas because there was lovely tile which was in direct contrast to the peeling and chipped paint and a door that had obviously been recylcled. The sink area is separate, also new and 'trendy' - but with NO towel rail or hook and nowhere to set makeup, toiletries, toothbrush etc. Our room was on the 3rd floor on the corner and while street noise was obvious it didn't bother us. Some may find it too noisy.

title: “nice hotel but a few drawbacks”
text: Stayed at this hotel for a conference in april. I requested an accessible room with a roll in shower and loved how big the room was. The sports bar had great food, the Philly steak sandwich was my favorite. The staff working in the sports bar were very slow at taking your order and getting your food to you. Room service did not clean our room the 2nd day even though my husband had talked to the cleaning staff that morning. We checked out on the third day as the conference was over. Would I stay here again, yes. I liked the location to the metro but have never heard of them not cleaning your room each day.

title: “Feel luxuriously at home in NYC”
text: From the moment you step out of the taxi, one feels at home at the Trump Soho. From the doorman who takes care of your luggage to the reception staff and housekeeping, we were made to feel like regulars even though it was our first time there. We were greeted by name at the reception even though we were barely through the door. The excellent level of service and friendliness was consistent throughout our 7 day stay. Our corner suite was on the 31st floor with a fantastic, mesmerizing view of the Hudson and uptown Manhattan. The decor of the rooms was very stylish yet functional; bed and couch were very comfortable and the amenities left nothing to be desired. Housekeeping was topnotch. Clearly one expects excellent service and luxury at the price, but not many hotels live up to the expectations. The location and proximity to subways was an excellent point of departure for sightseeing and dining. And on a lighter note, one may not agree with Donald Trump's political views, but he sure knows how to run a hotel business.

title: “As good as it gets in Seattle”
text: We have stayed at this property many times and are never disappointed. They were training some new staff and we had some problems with the room key, but this is a very rare misstep for this property. Room was super, ate breakfast in the Georgian Room twice- love the corned beef hash, and in general just love sitting in the wonderful lobby. As always, the floral settings were awesome.

title: “What a great hotel”
text: I am a Marriott person but because this reservation was made by my business, it was the first time I had the opportunity to stay at a Intercontinental. What a great hotel! It was very clean and the rooms were made up perfectly each of the 4 days I stayed. The decor and design were up dated and serene. The bathroom was awesome. The views out the window of the Manhattan skyline were beautiful. The location was perfect, within walking distance to the theatres and restaurants. The thing that most impressed me was when I didn't answer my wake up call on my 4th day there, because I had awakened early and hopped in the shower, they sent someone to my door to make sure I was all right. Now that is service! The restaurant was excellent and the banquet personnel were top notch. I must say that I will probably stay there next time I am in NY for a personal trip because it was so enjoyable. It was the perfect size, never had to wait for an elevator or for someone to help me out at the front desk or bellstand.

title: “keep looking!”
text:
If you are doing case studies on the habits of nocturnal street people, by all means stay here. If you want safety, get far away from this dive. I wished I had read the previous reviews before staying there. Went to San Diego to attend a ballgame at Petco park and all I knew was that this place was within walking distance. When the game let out about 10:30 p.m. (10 innings) we started walking and got lost. I asked a Police officer for directions to the hotel and his response was "why are you staying there?" I felt embarrased for not doing the research before booking. In the middle of the night when the blood curdling screams around the corner woke me, I almost got dressed and left. I am a former deputy sheriff and this place scared me. SAVE YOUR MONEY!!! KEEP LOOKING!!!
A little p.s. the lobby smelled of urine when we walked in. yuk!!!

title: “Watch out for the windows!”
text:
Just a warning, we were surprised to find that the window opened up on our 22nd floor. Imagine if a kid managed to pry it open!!! That was not safe feature there at all.
No fan in the bathroon and no vent that worked for us. Room was an ok size but nothing special at all. Really old and basic. It was also noisy there. Parking was expensive too.
View was great and so was the breakfast buffet. 
Would not stay again.

title: “Great location, CHEAP parking, nice room. I'd stay again.”
text:
My husband, adult son & I stayed for four nights in June. I chose the hotel because of the good reviews I saw here. We wanted to drive into the city and leave our car at the hotel. This hotel is truly minutes away from the Lincoln Tunnel. If you time your drive to avoid rush hour traffic, you won't find an easier place to get to in Manhattan. And, if you stay at the hotel, parking is only $10 per night. Hard to believe in Manhattan. (I believe you have to leave the car in the garage. You don't have in/out privilieges for that price. But what tourist wants to drive in Manhattan, anyway? Take cabs or the subway!)
Our room was a nice size and the three of us never felt cramped. We had two queen beds with plenty of room on all sides to walk around. The room came with an ironing board, hair dryer and a mini refrigerator where you could store your own food. There was a gym, which my husband used most mornings. (I'd rather sleep, so I can't report on the quality of the gym!)
The hotel is in a GREAT location. We were in walking distance of both of our Broadway Shows, to the Colbert Report, Central Park, the High Line and an amazing number of fun ethnic restaurants in the Hell's Kitchen neighborhood. When we take another little vacation to the Big Apple, I'll definitely book at this hotel again.
The only downsides I'd mention would be:
* The place is not luxurious. If you're having a honeymoon in NYC and have a big enough budget, you might want to pick someplace fancier. The carpet, lamps and drapes look a little worn. (The bedding did NOT look at all worn.) But LUXURY costs a lot more in Manhattan and this wasn't a honeymoon/anniversary kind of trip where that mattered a lot to us. Everything was perfectly clean. If budget is a consideration, this is a great place to go.
* The concierge was NOT at all service oriented. I'd say she was condescending, bordering on hostile. (I nicknamed her "The Ice Queen." My son had a different name that I won't print here.) When we asked her about walking around Brooklyn and for bookstore recommendations, her responses clearly indicated that she thought we were a bunch of idiots. (My husband wasn't clear when he phrased the question about the neighborhoods near the Brooklyn Bridge and she told him that Brooklyn is three times larger than Manhattan – so where to go was obviously a stupid question. She told my son that all the bookstores in Manhattan are large and bookstores are going out of business.) After those interchanges, we decided to stick with our smart phones and look for TripAdvisor & Yelp reviews rather than asking her for any more assistance. I'm hoping management sees this because this young lady needs some retraining.

title: “Lucerne a fine hotel”
text:
My wife and I stayed here during a college reunion. The hotel is right at the corner of W. 79th and Madison Ave., one block from Broadway and subway (line 1). The area has many restaurants, and is not far from museums and Central Park. 
The deluxe king room was very large, clean, and well-appointed with a nice settee and two desk areas. It had two (functioning) air conditioners. The bathroom was new and clean, although hooks were a bit small for holding towels, we had no complaints whatsoever. A window (non-transparent!) in the tub-shower, opened for quick room clearing. The shower head rotated producing an interesting shower experience. We never had occasion to use it, but from what we heard, Room-Service was not 24-hours, as suggested in some of the literature, but ended at 11 p.m. However, there was a great restaurant just off the lobby, the Nice Matin (which the locals pronounce "niece matyne"), which compared favorably in both price and fare with another French restaurant we went to, and unlike the latter place, we were not asked to leave in an hour and a half when having dinner with friends and relatives. 
Other neat things: we were called by the concierge before we left home if there was anything that would make the stay better, and we asked for a fridge. Although it was not there when we arrived, it was soon delivered, and at no extra charge. In fact, every staff member we met was gracious and helpful, and this includes the restaurant people as well. A terrific experience, which enhanced out stay enormously.
And, by the way, the hotel has not been mentioned in the Bedbug registry, a main reason why we chose this one from several recommended hotels.

title: “Quite, comfy, safe”
text: This property in the financial district offers lovely views. The desk staff is friendly, the concierge well informed, and the room warm and cozy. Towels we nice, sheets were soft, the bed was like clouds, and the room maintained in good order. I was here on Christmas and enjoyed my stay. The TV is appropriately positioned to the bed so that I could watch TV until my eyes glazed! Give this property a consideration your next trip to SF.

title: “Nice Location, Needs Updating”
text: I stayed here for five nights while attending a conference. The hotel is in a good location, but does need some updating. The room appear in need of changes, but the sleep number bed was nice. Overall the stay was good, but could have been better.

title: “Easy recommendable.”
text:
Excellent hotel north on Manhattan, a close walk to Times Square. Parking as availible next door. Some have complained about waiting on elevators - we had no such problems at all. I dont expect the elevator to arrive 2 sec after I press the button. Breakfast area is small, with "standard american brekfast". But it works.... Free wifi and safety box in the room is a pluss. 
Would absolutely consider this hotel next time I am in NY.

title: “Close to Convention Center”
text: We have stayed here each year for the past 5 years and it is a consistently good stay. The hotel is not new by any means and is dated in its decor, but the convenience is what makes it an excellent stay for us when doing business at the convention center. The restaurant is good and saves us walking around on nights when we're too tired to hoof it to one of the many excellent restaurants in Baltimore.

title: “Yummy Breakfast & Yummy Rates”
text:
When we first arrived. We had two choices stay at the Civic Center Inn or at Alexis Park. Luckily we choosed Alexis Park. Rate were very budget friendly and front desk staff was insightfull with helping us get around with Public Transportation. The place seemed newley remodeled, they also have a flat screen TV w/ DVD player. And may I add Free Parking! 
Pros: Great Breakfast, Great Rates, Free Parking
Cons: No elevators

title: “Good quality for the price”
text: This was a good hotel for the night. We were traveling through and it fit our needs perfectly. We also got an extra sitting area (not sure if that was an upgrade or all rooms have it) but it was nice to have the extra space that we didn't get in other hotels during our cross-country traveling.

title: “Wonderful Place to Stay”
text: I stayed here January 14th through 17th, 2004. I thought the hotel was wonderful. The rooms were average, but the beds were super comfortable. The housekeeping crew was on the job! They came as early as 8:00 a.m. and always checked back if we said we weren't ready. Also, the front desk crew was extremely pleasant and helpful. They had directions to anywhere we could possibly want to go. The pool was clean. They had a sign asking guests to be patient while they went through renovations. I had to ask the front desk manager what was being renovated because it all looked wonderful to me. The only drawback was the fact that the whirlpool wasn't open.

title: “FRAUD”
text: We are unable to get a refund for hotel rooms that we had reserved for us. We are unable to reach the accounting department and they have avoided us for two months. Continually left messages. Rooms were reserved and paid by promoter but when we left card for incidentals they double charged our rooms! they are refusing to deal with this matter.........avoid like the plague

title: “Run For Your Lives”
text: WE HAD TO PAY UPFRONT FOR THIS NIGHTMARE!!! We were booked one night and we stayed 1 hour. Upon exiting the elevator the hallway smelled of bleach and cigarette smoke. It was dark, dingy and scarey. The curtains from outside were dirty and barely hanging on the rods. The windows were filthy. We entered the room and were greeted with a bigger smell of bleach!! I am allergic to bleach so this was not good. There was dried blood on the floor in the bathroom. The walls and woodwork were chipped and dirty. There was no front on the a/c unit. I went to the front desk to tell them about the bleach problem, was told...rudely...that there was nothing available. We checked out. It tooks us hours to find another hotel. It took us 2 weeks to get the credit back on our charge cards. ELVIS WOULD BE VERY UPSET!!!! The Graceland tour is tops!! If you have to choose between staying at this hotel and staying in your car...pack extra pillows and recline your drivers seat back.

title: “Hip! Cool! Convenient!”
text: If you have ever been to Austin, you know that there is alot going on on any given night. The W hotel is perfectly located in the heart of downtown within walking distance to all that fun! The staff is super friendly and accomodating! Eric Wilder was one employee that really stood out. He made sure my friends and I knew where to go and even set up rides in the sweet Acura! The pool vibe was relaxed but trendy. And you don't feel like leaving the hotel for fun, you don't have to! On the weekend the bar scene here is a blast! DJ, yummy drinks, and lots of different areas to hang out. My girlfriends and I had a great girls weekend and the W hotel was the perfect place to be!

title: “Great staff, great room, great stay”
text: Very friendly staff upon check-in. Lobby decor is dated, but well maintained. Rooms are large, very large. The decor of the rooms was a little dated and worn, but still more than adequate for our needs. We were on the 33rd floor on the East River side. We had no noise issues and great sunrises each morning. Duane Reed 1.5 blocks up 2nd Ave, Olympic Cafe served up a good variety of eats at reasonable prices on 2nd Ave and Sushi Time also on 2nd was our best meal. Easy walking access to much Midtown has to offer and about 5-10 minutes away from Grand Central Terminal should you want to head out elsewhere. We did not take advantage of any amenities except internet. We were able to get a strong signal with adequate bandwidth for $12.95 per 24hr. There is a business center down by the bar which is fee-based for services. However: there is a terminal down there dedicated to airline check-in and free boarding pass printing. We would be thrilled to find out we were staying there again.

title: “Not good”
text: Very dirty rooms. Workout rooms very hot and smelled like old towels. Manager reception only snacks old stale chips and tasteless salsa. Pets allowed and dog barked all night in room next door. Manager on duty was yelling at staff member in hallway, very rude. I will never stay here again.

title: “Really nice room, great staff”
text: Recently stayed here for business, using reward points. Booking the reservation on the web site was effortless. I was upgraded to a small corner suite on check-in, which was a nice gesture. It included a sofa, large work desk, and a minibar. The bedroom had great views from the large panel windows. The location is perfect for Mag Mile access. The property is nicer than the Allerton next door, where I've also stayed, and my guess is the rooms are more spacious. Staff were exceptionally helpful and friendly. I enjoyed breakfast in the Sky Lounge on the 40th floor one morning when it was pouring rain outside. Set up as a lounge rather than a restaurant, it's a casual and relaxing setting, (serving breakfast only), with nice views on 3 sides. The hot breakfast buffet is $18, a reasonable value and cheaper than a room service full breakfast. A full service restaurant/bar is also located at street level (it closes at 11pm weekdays though). Parking is valet only, $48 per night, which is pretty standard for the downtown Chicago hotels. My only complaint is that the TV was an older-CRT style unit that had a poor signal on some channels, and I couldn't enjoy one of my favorite shows. Otherwise a great stay and I look forward to returning in the future.

title: “Perfect for solo/couple travel - business or leisure”
text:
I travel to Seattle on business about once a quarter, typically by myself. As a mom of 2 young children, I appreciate amenities (small and large) that make my trip smooth sailing and enhance that "mini-vacation" feeling moms and dads get when we have a few nights to ourselves (don't pretend you don't know what I am talking about, parents). I chose the Arctic because it is one block from my company's office and had a very good rate compared to similar hotels. I also like boutique hotels - my stay was before the sale to Doubletree, I think, so I hope they have not changed anything about it. 
The Arctic has a strong sense of history, being located in a former gentleman's club. The hotel does a great job of maintaining that manly, clubby feel, without overdoing it. As a woman, I felt quite at home, but still a little like I was getting away with something sneaking into the boys' club (tee hee!)! 
Nice touches like speedy valet service, loaner umbrellas, french press coffee in the rooms, newspaper every morning, robes, nice in room office area, etc. I appreciated not getting charged for internet access. I sure hope the Doubletree hasn't come in and messed with that policy. Wireless has become such a standard amenity that it feels wrong to be charged for it - like if they charged extra for pillows on the beds! Staff was lovely, checkout a breeze. Rooms a bit tiny, but clean. 
I did not spend any time in the bar because I was too busy with work, but I really, really wanted to. It looks cozy and warm, and a great place to sink into a chair and enjoy a martini.
Never in a million years would I stay here with my kids, at least not until they are old enough to appreciate french press coffee and leather club chairs, but I will definitely be using this hotel for future business trips, and would recommend it for couples.
I thought the restaurant (JUNO) was a bit lackluster, but in downtown Seattle who cares - there are plenty of other choices.

title: “Great San Francisco Hotel”
text: We have stayed in many San Francisco hotels, so we have a good basis for comparison. The staff of the Omni is by far the most friendly, helpful, positive hospitality group in the area. We always stay at the Omni every time we have the opportunity to do so.

title: “good”
text: Good for price. Right off interstate and easy to get to everything in Jacksonville. Nice staff and very helpful. Good breakfast................................................................................................................................

title: “Great Hotel”
text: My wife and I stayed at the Westin Copley while I attended a conference for the weekend. The staff were extremely friendly and knowledgeable. The room was spacious and comfortable. We loved the lobby with it's fireplace and cozy seating in front. The dining was great with many fabulous restaraunts of all types either in the hotel or a short indoor walk through the mall. The location of the hotel to the mall was terrific. A short walk takes you to great shopping. The neighborhood is awsome. A short walk to fashionable Newbury St. great restaraunts and sightseeing. Copley Sq. is the perfect location to stay to enjoy the history and flavor of Boston. We will defenitely be staying here while we bring our daughters up to Boston to check out colleges next year, and will be planning a return trip soon to enjoy the great city of Boston

title: “Gorgeous - but a little pretentious”
text: Nice hotel - but I found it lacking in the usual wonderful Kimpton customer service. I usually get lots of bells and whistles, and I'm missing those here - and I have stayed here both as an InTouch and Inner Circle Member. That being said, beautiful hotel, nice rooms, good restaurant/bar. I loved the one time I got upgraded to a suite, the regular rooms are on the small size but fine. Views are nothing exciting, so don't worry about that option on the menu. It has a nice fitness center and the pool looks nice, although I haven't tried it. I did love the free fitness classes on demand on their TVs. If you want to be in Westwood, it's a great location, still seems random to me that this is the only Kimpton in the LA area, but it's convenient to my work travel. I'll keep staying here - but I just want it to be as great as some of the other hotels in this chain.

title: “Great value/location, some issues with reservation”
text: I booked 2 rooms 5 months in advance and got 2 different confirmation numbers. After 3 months I modified one of them (added 1 bed) and got confimed. The day I checked in I was told there was only one room with my name. The front desk made a big effort to find a second room, but this was too small and needed an additional rollaway, so the first night's stay was unconfortable. The next day a double-double was available and my friends moved there. Other than that, the hotel has great location and price. Bathrooms are very clean, housekeeping and maintenance are good. Rooms are VERY small but this is Manhattan. Interior corridors sometimes smelled bad. For our expectations, it was a good experience but make sure your reservation was kept.

title: “Awesome”
text: We only booked this hotel on chance because we decided to stay another night in DC and the place we were at was full. I have to say I am very glad we did. We will always be staying at the Carlyle from now on in DC. My favorite thing about this hotel wasn’t the big rooms with comfortable beds and a small kitchen or the well priced buffet in the morning, or the Dupont area it is located or even that the hotel staff went out of their way to help us find parking (For two vehicles). But that all of the front staff made the simple comment of “welcome home” every time we came back to the hotel from site seeing, shopping or eating. In my book six stars out of five, AWESOME costumer service!

title: “Great Location”
text: The hotel was nice, the room was clean and it was a good size compared to most nyc hotels. It def. met my expectations. The location was fantastic, close to everything! You can't go wrong with this hotel. The staff was well helpful, only bad thing is that the internet was not working and they charged my room for it, they did however refund me the fee they charged me.

title: “This hotel should be no. 1 on Trip Advisor!”
text:
Even before our trip began we were excited about staying at this hotel, it's not like stardard hotels!! Get on Facebook and like their page, keep an eye out for their updates!! 
All of the staff are lovely, we keep saying 'they are so 'real' here' refreshing change, not pretentious or unhelpful, but friendly and fun, stress free. 
Our room was a good size, 4 adults in doubles for 9 nights and we didn't fight at all. Clean, well serviced and fun details left in our room from time to time. Perfect location!!
We would all stay here again when we return to NYC

title: “what a dump”
text: This hotel is a total dump. Do not stay here!! Outside the hotel is very dangerous and people will mug you. Believe me, we have stayed in some seriously dodgy places but this takes the biscuit!

title: “Great location in San Francisco”
text: We stayed at the Chancellor for 3 nights in Marchl. It was everything that previous guests have stated. Great location - very central for shopping, eating and getting around. Front desk staff were helpful when asking for directions/bus or tram stops. There is a great diner next door where we had breakfast during our stay - sorry, we didn't eat in the hotel so can't comment. The rooms are small, but look exactly as the photo's posted on this site and are clean and comfortable. Bathroom is small, but clean. If you come to SF there is so much to do and see, you are not going to be in your room that much. It's a perfect place to crash, drop off your shopping, have a rest and then back out there! No, it's not a luxury hotel, but you are not paying luxury prices - go to the Four Seasons if that's what you want. I would highly recommend the Chancellor. I think it's great that the Manager takes such an active interest in the reviews.

title: “Great location - will stay here again”
text:
We recently stayed at this hotel and I can highly recommend it. Even though the rooms are quite small, the location is perfect- a 2 minute walk from the cable car station.
Staff is really friendly and helpful. Valet parking is offered for about 40 dollars/day. The bathroom is equipped with L'OCCITANE products and there is free wifi in every room. Previous reviews have mentioned the noise from outside. We had a room facing the street and the noise didn't bother us at all.
Great value for money!

title: “Customer Service”
text: Have only just made our reservation with the hotel front desk. Won't be staying until March, but the customer service I received on the phone with Alex was above average.(I'm tough to please and don't generally write reviews) Alex was amazingly patient with my list of questions about location and El Paso in general. We are looking forward to our stay and following up with another review. Thank you Alex.

title: “Good only if you can book it for $159 or less”
text:
We've stayed at the Parker Meridien about 6 times over the past 3 years. If you can get at rate of $159 or less it is worth staying here. At rates higher than that, stay somewhere else as it's value to price equation drops rapidly. 
On the plus side: good location, modern architecture, free internet (bring an ethernet cable), pool, pretty good gym (it's a bit gritty however), Norma's restaurant (great breakfast, big portions, big price), nice bathrooms.
Negatives: Any problem resolution, uncomfortable beds/pillows, doesn't participate in the LeMeridien Moments program, doesn't seem like a full-service hotel in many ways, won't guarantee a non-smoking room if you book anywhere but direct with them, bellhops pushing for tips
I generally like this hotel and the LeMeridien chain in general, but problems with reservations and subsequent price gouges in costly upgrades in order to get a non-smoking room leave a bad impression. I took the manager over 3 weeks to reply to a complaint email to him, with a lame response. If you don't like modern/contemporary decor, definitely don't stay here.

title: “A hidden sleeper”
text: Stayed here on a recent business trip in the LA area and found the property to be a pleasant surprise. I usually stay at full-service Marriotts, but found the Courtyard for a rate of $145 so figured I'd give it a shot. Glad I did. Hotel recently underwent a rennovation and it's this fancy, W-style modern and yet economical hotel. Highlights included a really nice TV in the room, a CD player. I think because of my Marriott gold status I was upgraded to an oversized king room, which basically meant it came with a couch. Freeway outside was a tad noisy -- even up on the 14th floor -- but didn't really bother me sleeping at all. Breakfast buffet was excellent.
