Fitness center I thought was phenomenal -- especially for a Courtyard. Treadmills, stair climbers, a brand new nautilis machine and free weights. Even a couple ab balls. Only negative was that my toilet had some trouble and it kept running and running, but maintenance came and fixed the problem quickly. Good place -- especially for the price.

title: “Not bad for the value”
text: The Mount Vernon hotel is a good place to stay if you are on a budget. After reading the other reviews, I was hesitant but the stay went smoothly. The only problem I had was how thin the walls were. You can hear every time someone knocks or a door closes anywhere on the floor. The breakfast was average, but like I said, it's nice if your on a budget.

title: “Loved this hotel”
text: The hotel is in a great location, so close to Bryant park, and times square area also. Beautiful lobby with a fireplace, very nice room, big for NYC hotels, also really nice size closet the bathroom had a great shower! Would definitely stay again!

title: “Shocked to see how worn down and out of date this property has become.”
text:
Had reservations to stay 3 nights at this property with my wife - she insisted we leave after one evening there.
Everything seemed worn out and dirty. They haven't maintained or updated this hotel in a long time. 
Our room was large but only had a bed , a small desk and a mirror in it. Therr was a lot of empty space - Felt like they didn't want to spend the money on an armchair or other furnishings. Room felt like a $80 per night hotel - but it was quite expensive. 
Location is very good and the staff seemed very nice - but can't make up for its shortcomings. 
We couldn't wait to get out of there. We won't go back until we hear the hotel has been fully renovated.

title: “Great Service”
text: Many stays in NYC but my first stay at the Times Square Hilton. The check in service was friendly Even though they were very busy. The staff went out of their way to get us in soon and surprised us with a great upgrade and view. The guest service agents, Peter and Raquel made us feel at home. I would highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Just like home”
text:
We arrived on Friday around noon but they said we could not check in until 3PM. They did let us in around 2:15. We purchased a "weekend special" so our car parking was included with day passes for the Metro. Check their web site for specials. 
The hotel is located in a neighborhood of town houses. Streets are very quiet. It is a 5 minute walk to the Metro, and around the corner from George Washington Unv. Trader Joe's grocery store is on the same street about 2 blocks away. There's a Catholic church a block away.
The room was very clean. We had a queen size bed with a fold out sofa so the room would sleep four. It had a kitchenette with full size refrigerator and freezer, microwave, coffee maker with beans and a grinder, 2 gas burners, even a garbage disposal. It's equipped with dishes, silverware, glasses and pots and pans. There were ice cube trays and a bowl of ice cubes in the freezer. It had a flat screen TV, internet, radio, table/desk and chairs. The kitchenette is why I mentioned Trader Joe's. We saved a lot of money not eating out. There are not a lot of restaurants within walking distance of the hotel. Geo Wash Hospital is beside the Metro. Parking in the street is free, however, you must move your car every 2 hours or get a ticket. A policeman makes the rounds noting the car and time it is there and writes a ticket if it's there when he returns. We saw one and spoke with him. We had parked while we were waiting to check in. The drawback with parking is that once you move, you've lost your space and may not find another. Friday after 6PM until Sunday you can park and stay. There is no charge or ticket. A ticket is $25. I highly recommend this hotel especially if you are looking to save $$ wherever you can. The hotel employees were very pleasant and courteous. During the week the rates are a little pricey, weekends are less expensive. It's comparable to hotels in the area. We felt the food savings made up for the price of the room.

title: “Great hotel; convenient location!”
text: Hotel Nikko is a modern and sophisticated hotel, located in the heart of the Union Square area. Public transportation is two short blocks away. Rooms are quiet and are very clean and comfortable with updated bathrooms and a flat panel TV mounted on the wall. The hotel restaurant, Anzu, serves great sushi! The workout facility is very good, and costs only $10 for the length of stay. There is an indoor, roof-top pool as well. The hotel gives a good AAA discount which includes free in-room internet. I highly recommend this hotel!

title: “Great New Years Eve hotel”
text: Stayed here using Marriott points for New Years Eve at the Kennedy Center. Easy access to subway and all lobby staff were very helpful and friendly. Room was fine-King size bed in business wing with a separate elevator for that wing. Cabs to Kennedy Center were readily available. Also easy walk to National Geographic Museum. We'll stay here again next year for New Years Eve.

title: “Lovely homely and clean hotel with excellent location”
text:
Stayed here with my wife, we loved the location of the hotel, Times Suare is just outside the door.
Yet despite this is, it is a very homely and quiet hotel. It is very clean and well looked after.
The breakfast was excellent and my wife who needs gluten free food was able to get gluten free bread.
We loved the wine and cheese available in the evening too which really was fantastic.
I definitely recommend this hotel to anyone considering a trip to New York.

title: “La Quinta Downtown, Chicago - clean, quiet, safe - a great place to stay”
text: We recently stayed @ the La Quinta Inn & Suites Chicago Downtown, Chicago, Illinois. The hotel is located about 4 short blocks from the Washington/Wells subway station. The hotel is centrally located in a safe area. A 15 minute walk to all the sightseeing areas on Micihgan Ave/ grant park area. The rooms are spacious, clean, and have LCD flat screen TV's, and a comfortable bed. Breakfast is included every morning. The staff is very professional and friendly. I would stay here again, an defiantly would recommend this hotel!

title: “Great hotel right in the middle of everything”
text:
Two moms, with two 14 y/o daughters in tow. We all loved this hotel. It was wonderful from the get-go. We were cheerfully greeted at checkin, were able to get into our room right away at 10:00 am. We were put on the 5th floor, facing 8th...a bit noisy at night, but otherwise a good view.
The location of this hotel is exceptional...there is a parking garage right next door, the subway is right at the corner. Good restaurants are a quick walk. And Times Sq is about a 2 min walk! Getting to any of the theaters is no problem at all. 
The folks at the Hampton Inn were wonderfully helpful when we needed to extend our stay due to weather last week..we had checked in on Thursday, the 21st, for one night only. However, the snow on Friday prevented our driving back to Mass, so we needed to stay another night. The front desk was wonderful about finding us a room. And they were able to honor our AAA rate as well...what a plus. Bell services was great moving our bags around whenever we needed.
The complimentary breakfast was good...everyone in our group was able to find something to eat. The always at hand beverage station off to the side of the lobby got a lot of use from us..lots of coffee and hot chocolate was consumed. And mid-afternoon cookies at the front desk..yummy.
We found the hotel to be very clean and nicely refurbished. The rooms were much larger than we had anticipated. The beds were incredibly comfortable. 
This hotel was everything we could have hoped for, and more. We all agreed that this was a hotel that we would all be happy about returning to.

title: “Not bad at all!”
text:
The hotel is dated and could do with modernising. The location is not too bad and it is very easy and safe to travel downtown at any time. There are many stores and retails outlets and other places to hang out in the area if you want to stay local. There is also a prity good cinema near 84th St.
Central park is walking distance around the corner and is handy if you want to go for a walk.
The hotel itself could do with a facelift and general cleanup.
The staff are friendly and helpful, our room was cleaned to a good standard everyday without failure. I wanted another room because my room was close to the main road and was offered one almost straight away. The lifts are slow and i had to go down 6 floors by the stairwell a few times.
The rooms are a good size and clean. The furniture needs to be updated as well as the decor. The only complaint i have is that my bed was very soft and awfull. I would stay here again if my budget was tight.

title: “Just Right!”
text: The room was clean and modern, the hotel was historic and cool. The location was perfect.- just south of the loop- walking distance to everything. Extra points for letting us check in at 8:00am after a red eye. We were VERY happy with the hotel.

title: “Great hotel for the price”
text:
Stayed here for 5 days or so. Would highly recommend. Easy location to find, right off the highway. Plenty of parking, and just a general great feeling about this Courtyard. Also, there is an Outback and a Mexican restaurant in the same parking area of the hotel, and just a few minute walk from your room. In terms of the price, this is one of the best valued hotels that I have ever stayed at. In all honesty, no real complaints at all.
Pros:
+Abram at front desk was great
+Great room, tv, cable
+Great mattress
+Tons of stuff around hotel (driving)
+Great coffee in the lobby
Cons:
-None, whatsoever.

title: “Wonderful birthday trip!”
text: My boyfriend and I stayed at the The Joule on a trip to Dallas for my 40th birthday. We wanted to be downtown near the Arts District and The Joule looked great online. We were so happy with our choice. Katy, the concierge, was very helpful in making reservations and recommendations. All of the staff were very friendly and helpful. We never used room service but we ate dinner at Charlie Palmers once and it was wonderful.

title: “Wonderful Hotel”
text: The hotel was in a perfect location for a night at the harbor. Everyone that worked there was very friendly and super helpful. The rooms were clean and even bigger than I expected. Parking is convenient if you don't mind paying for it, however the metro is only 3 blocks away. We had taken the metro and the hotel even held our bags for us while we shopped after we checked out. I will definatly come back here on my next trip to the harbor!

title: “Small rooms but great location”
text:
The Charlesmark is right in the middle of the Boston shopping and business district, and only a 30 mins walk to the university campuses at Longwood. Location-wise it couldn't be better.
While the rooms are rather small they have comfortable beds, free wifi and great showers. The free 24/7 coffee and tea, plus complimentary breakfast (bagels, pastries and OJ) are nice touches.

title: “Love it - again and again”
text: Although it may not be the newest hotel in town, there is a reason this on has stood the test of time. They really seem to have their business down to an art. Everything one would expect from a find hotel is in place. That is more than I can same for some other Boston hotels with pricier rooms. But beyond the hotel itself, its location also makes it ideal. Situated in the center of Copley Square and near the Prudential Center and Boylston Street, the location is perfect. It is one of the nicer areas of Boston and there is plenty to do without even needed to set foot outside!

title: “Okay”
text: We arrived in New York for a 3 night stay and had booked the Wellington online. The location was great. We were within walking distance to almost everything. It is at 7th Ave and 55th st so it right in the middle of everything. Our room was in the older section, we had to go by other elevators to get to ours, and you obviously were out of the nicer section of the hotel, and the halls in our section were not air conditioned. The halls looked like it was a run down hotel. The room was on the smaller side, but did seem clean. We saw no bugs, and the carpet, the bedding, and the bathroom definately seemed clean. We came in past midnight a couple of nights and there was a sign there that said that you must present a key to get in, but there was no one there checking, and none of the bellhops were even paying attention to the people walking in, one was reading a magazine and the other 2 were talking to each other. and with us having to go over to the back halls to get on the elevator, that was a little creepy at night. One was reading a magazine and the other 2 were talking to each other. On Sunday night there was someone there checking room cards. We came back in the middle of the day to drop off packages and to change and the maid service kept trying to open the door, would not knock but every 5 minutes would mess with the door. Next time we would pay a little more to get a nicer room and probably a little closer to times square.

title: “Westin is fab!!”
text:
We stayed at the Westin Times Square in February at the time when it snowed...and it was great!!
The hotel was really clean and very stylishly modern! The staff were really helpful, especially the concierge, and were always happy to help! Bar 10 was always welcomimg to go to for pre dinner drinks, despite being a little expensive. Shula's was great for an American breakfast...the pancakes are to die for!!!! However, we recommend you avoid room service as it is extremely costly! If you can, try and go for a club room as the rooms are ultra comfy and you get free access to the club lounge for breakfast (which was always nice) and pre dinner drinks. It's definitely worth the extra. The hotel in itself is in a great location ad is easily accesible!! We would definitely return here for our stay in New York City!

title: “Nice Rooms”
text: We stayed in the Marriott for three nights and arrived at 10.30pm. First impressions were 'ok' - the reception/public areas were a bit bland and the corridors looked a bit tired. Things got better when we went to our room. Our room at the front of the hotel was small but clean and perfectly comfortable. We just left our bags and went out for something quick to eat. As the bar was closed when we got back at around 11.45pm, we headed back to the room and the very comfortable beds. Unfortunately, as it was dark we didn't know about the construction site right across the road from our room. At 7am we were in no doubt of its existence. The following day was a Saturday and it was a 9 am start so if you were planning a lie-in - forget it! If we had been staying any longer I would have asked for a room at the back of the hotel in the hope that the noise might not have been so intrusive. Having said that, the location of the hotel is great - its 10 min walk to White House and about 20 mins from the National Mall. The staff were professional and had no problem booking return shuttle (SuperShuttle) to Dulles for us. All in all, there is no reason why I wouldn't stay in this hotel again if we got a good price, but I think i'd wait till the contruction work is finished!

title: “let me accentuate the positive”
text:
the personnel was helpful & friendly. towels were soft & plentiful.
beds (we had 2 rooms-and stayed 4 nights) were comfortable and the sheets & pillowcases were clean. shower was good, and the water was always hot. price was also great. location is PERFECT, near everything. adjoining deli--sandwiches were yummy. would I stay there again? ABSOLUTELY!! however, and this is a HUGE HOWEVER,
I highly recommend you bring a wash cloth or two, and slippers as I do not believe it was vacuumed in a very long, long, long, LONG TIME. and bring a plastic cup. also, even though toilet was forceful, it leaked every time we flushed, so we put a towel behind it. and, bring flip flops or water shoes for your shower, as the bathtub needs a cleaning. our bathtub wasn't too bad, but the other gals had mold along the wall, to which one gal said she was worried about Legionnaires disease. and our TV didn't work, but actually, we didn't seem to miss it. and the only electrical outlet that worked (besides the air-conditioner one) was the one in the bathroom, but that was a little loose, so we had to prop up some boxes of crackers on top of a suitcase to plug in our cell phone chargers. we found this to be very humorous. the outlets & TV worked in the other room. "they" even had a picture on their wall, ours was behind the dresser.
and my point to all of this is: great price, GREAT LOCATION, and if ever we go again, you can bet that we will stay at the Carter Hotel. we had a fantastic time, and at the end of the day, a comfortable bed to lay our heads, with no aching back in the morning. just needs some TLC and a REALLY GOOD CLEANING.

title: “Uncomfortable and old”
text: Once again, the bathrooms are old, poorly designed, the shower/tub drain is always clogged. There is mold and the grout is dirty. The rooms are outdated and uncomfortable. The beds are also uncomfortable I didn't sleep all night. Overly priced and the bright lights outside shine through the curtains.

title: “New Cool in the Meatpacking District”
text:
Though the hotel is still in 'soft' opening stage...if you are looking for a new cool place to stay, this is it! Forget the Gansevoort or Soho House...Andre's latest fits the bill. A purpose built stylish piece of architecture in its own right...you can't miss the 70's style over-the-highway design. Yellow doors on the corner with hip doormen mark your arrival. Plain entry hall with neat little bar off to the left...rooms are floor to ceiling windows with funky all in one bathrooms...stayed in two different types both were cool. The toiletries are plentiful and practical. The towels white and fluffy. The mini bar is built into a retro-new desk/bureau. Flat screen tv, free wireless and a free breakfast of coffee/pastry/juice brought to you by decidecly good looking staff any time from 6am..what's not to like. The location is perfect for the MP district. The concierge was really helpful and low key - never 'hyping or selling' the latest place - but rather, asking the right questions about what you want (noisy, dark, 'scene', etc). I loved the experience. A HUGE step above the all too knowing Gansevoort (long since sold out) or the dark and faux-hip 'W' experience (so cookie cutter!). 
When the rooftop bar opens it will be THE place...I just hope it doesnt lose the sense of understated cool. Restaurant wasn't open when I stayed in March, but should be an advantage for room service/dining. The view over the Hudson or the Empire State is incredible at night (and day)...so, if you want a cool NY place to stay, this is the new spot. 
Please Mr. B.... don't 'sell out' to the 'scene'.

title: “don't book it! it's a ripe off this place doesn't exist, Our family of four was sent to another location 73rd street 9th”
text: Very disappointing as this Central Park House doesn't exist, we were transferred to another site at 73rd street 9thWest. Nothing like the picture. Television didn't work, gave up. When arriving at the desk 2 other couples were complainning about hot water, heating. We were missing a blind in the lounge area to sleep in no heating on and off all night. Very disappointing next time will book through a travel agent.,

title: “Accomodated our early check in”
text: We flew in on the red-eye from San Diego and really needed to be in a room by 7:30am. They were so willing and helpful. Got our room ready and did not charge us extra! Loved the rooms, the location near Fenway and Newbury Street (shopping and amazing restaurants) and the T station just steps from the entrance. This was my first trip to Boston and not my last. I love this city! Will definitely stay here again.

title: “Highly Recommended!”
text: My daughter and I stayed at the newly opened Yotel for two nights last week and loved it. The staff is very friendly and the rooms are really cool. We knew they were small, but the size was fine for us. The decor is sleek and futuristic and the beds pull out, go up and down, etc. The beds are a little hard, but were fine for us b/c that's what we like. The breakfast was coffee and muffins and that was sufficient. Each floor has a galley with a coffee, latte, hot chocolate machine. The restaurant has amazing sushi. My daughter declared the miso coup to be the best. The outdoor space of the hotel is amazing! The location is only a few blocks from Times Square a little further to Rockefeller, which was awesome. We truly enjoyed our stay at Yotel. Whenever we needed assistance, the front desk staff provided what we needed, such as a map of NYC. (There was also a map in our room.) The towels were soft, but no bath mat was provided, so we used a hand towel. We enjoyed the rain shower head and the flat screen t.v. The housekeeping staff, bellmen, front desk personnel, waitresses, etc. couldn't have been nicer. My only caution is that the beds are not soft, but again, we like firm. it fit our needs. We would definitely stay there again. It was really clean, quiet and modern. My daughter who is eleven loved it and it was her first time to the big apple.

title: “Amazing Service - particularly by the Night Auditor”
text: I was in San Diego for a week on business, but had quite a bit of free time on my hand. Being jet-lagged I typically woke up around 4am so started planning for my days fairly early. Bernhard, the night auditor, proved to be an invaluable source of information and a great guy to talk to as well. I will DEFINITELY return to the W - and I do hope he will still be around. Staff make all the difference!

title: “Loved the Westin.”
text: My husband and I stayed at the Westin Copley Place December 29th for one night. We are Gold members and requested and received an early check in at 11:30am. We love the location,the rooms and the service. We also requested and received a late check out of 4pm which allowed us to relax in the morning, then shower and go out for brunch, do some shopping in the nearby Copley Place Mall then leave.

title: “Just ok, more 3 stars than 4”
text: Went to Chicago for a weekend with my two teenage children. Decided to go through hotwire and book a four star hotel, without knowing the name, but in certain locations. Ended with The Westin. The location was very good and convenient. The hotel was clean. That's about it. The room was surprisingly small. Two double beds in the room, and no room for a roll away. Yes, there literally was no room for a roll away. Bathroom was a bit dated, lobby was smaller. The hotel was ok, I expected more from a four star hotel.

title: “Great Hotel, Great Location”
text: After reading many of the previous reviews, my expectations of my one night stay here were quite low. However, the hotel was great, the staff very polite and helpful. Yes, the rooms are quite small - but very clean and comfortable. And yes, the hotel does have a trendy-type feel to it - but yeh, its New York. Stay, have fun and enjoy this great hotel in a great location.

title: “Comfortable, conveniently located”
text: The Hotel Commonwealth is the most comfortable hotel near Kenmore Square. While the view from all of the rooms isn't necessarily fantastic, you can't beat the location for access to Boston University, the Back Bay and the Museum of Fine Arts. It is also right on the T, so we were able to get all around town. The rooms were spotlessly clean, the beds were great, and it was very quiet at night. Champagne on arrival doesn't hurt, and the staff were outstanding when my daughter had to go back to the room post-check out to retrieve her ipod.

title: “Staff and room make this enjoyable”
text:
Clean room, great towels and bedding package. Not worn out. Staff was helpful and friendly.
Breakfast server does a nice job on the breakfast area. It is kept clean and full of food. Dining area can be used for small meetings and happy hour with friends.

title: “So so not in the league it's advertised at.”
text: We stayed five nts in the Clift. Ok so let's start with the positives. We did get a really nice big room and the room itself was high up so on the main it was quite. Its in a great location and just off union square so Macy's and cheesecake factory walgreens etc and a bus stop across the road and one of the main cable car lines round th corner. The beds are v comfortable and the toiletries are nice. Ok I do have a few negatives . Payin for Internet is crazy in this day and age when all the budget hotels it's free. The furnishings I felt were just for asthetic purposes and quite worn all the couches in the lobby area are impossible to get out of and the furnishings in the room were grotty. Also we had a room with adjoining room and while the Walls are very thin when u have an adjoining room it's not really what I would expect and. You can hear your neighbours.The other thing that really annoyed is that we got charged for toll free calls yes ihear u cry they are free no they are not in the Clift the only hotel we got charged for these calls. That's after spending four weeksvin the USA in lots of different hotels. The front off house staff were mainly helpful and the bar was very busy at the weekend.

title: “Pleasant, clean at the Clarion Fifth Avenue”
text: My daughter and I stayed at the Clarion Hotel in a standard room from July 23 to July 28. The room was clean, pleasant and quiet. One of the telephones was not working the first day, but the engineer came and replaced it within a half-hour. Housekeeping supplied a toothbrush and extra pillows at our request. The staff at the front desk was not overly friendly, but they did answer any questions we had. We did receive one call from the front desk at 6:30 AM asking if we had left any luggage at the airport. (We had not.) Our last night we received a phone call and a knock on the door from someone who had been given our room number by mistake. That suggested to me that the system for keeping track of guests and room numbers is flawed. We did have easy access to public transportation, and we felt walk safe walking in the neighborhood. There were many places to eat nearby. We liked the Chef Express for a quick breakfast, or lunch. There is no food available at the hotel after 9:30 PM except from vending machines. I felt that we had a good experience for the price of the room. (We had a combined airfare/hotel room package).

title: “RUN!!!!”
text: This place is a motel with all rooms located outside! The restroom in th lobby was filthy and the patrons staying at the motel looked scary. It is in a bad section of town until the motel hires Officers to patrol the lot. I am not a picky person but this motel is totally unacceptable and should not even be advertised as a Ramada. Pay the extra $$ and drive 15 miles for a better HOTEL!!

title: “Great experience - this Sheraton is underrated”
text:
Let me first start by saying I am not a frequenter of four star or luxury hotels. I am a frequent business traveler and value a clean, comfortable setting with great service that isn't hard on the dollar. I booked this hotel through Priceline because it seemed that by booking directly for even a low quality hotel in the Columbus area, the prices were relatively high. I ended up at the Sheraton on Capital Square for 57.00 per night and I was more than pleased with my stay. 
This hotel, which was originally a Hyatt, recently (August 29, 2011) changed management and became a Sheraton. I'm not certain if the management change was the reason for my viewing the hotel in a far better light or if it is the fact that I'm not overly "spoiled" when it comes to staying in hotels. 
I was delighted with my three day stay here from start to finish. I opted not to use the valet parking which was $23.00 and instead parked across the street for $5.00 overnight. The front desk was professional and welcoming and never even mentioned the fact that I was not paying full price as others have stated. The lobby was clean and spacious with a sports bar and a Starbucks coffee cart right there on the first floor. Saying that the room was clean would be an understatement, it was immaculate. The large bathroom was well appointed with an array of bath products, high quality towels and a brand new shower curtain. Admittedly, the armoir that the TV sat in was older but it wasn't offensive. My hotel room did still have an older TV, which was a huge complaint that many had but for 57.00 a night, I really can't complain about the model of television and, honestly, watching TV on a flatscreen isn't a top priority of mine. However, it was stated that they are in the process of installing LCD TVs in the rooms. The bed was heavenly with quality linens and there was a large desk that appeared to be either new or well cared for. My only negative remark would be that the internet was almost $10.00 for a 24 hour period, if I had paid full price for the hotel I would have been disgruntled (I realize that this is the way in many better hotels but if the Days Inn can offer free wifi, you would believe higher dollar hotels would follow suit). 
The fitness center was top notch with an array of cardio machines as well as weight and resistance equipment. It was situated on the 22nd floor with a great view of the city, which the hotel is right smack dab in. 
The location is wonderful and is very convenient to the airport.
I know that this is a long review but I feel this hotel is sorely underrated. I would not hesitate to stay again, even if paying the full price. Perhaps if you're a hotel connossieur that demands the absolute finest in every way, this isn't the hotel for you, but if you want a clean, exceptionally comfortable hotel with outstanding service and a large amount of convenient ammenities then I would recommend this Sheraton without any hesitation.

title: “World Class Hotel in Memphis”
text: The Madison is on a scale with any of the Luxury Boutique Hotels I have stayed in. I use the Kimpton Hotels on the west coast on a regular basis, and the Madison exceeded many of the Kimpton properties.

title: “Poor Customer Service”
text:
Our team booked this hotel because it was recommended by the KROC Center. When I walked in the front desk to check in the rep was really cold as if they are doing us a favor. Then, the night we checked in I called room service to place an order for the next morning and I was told that they can not deliver our food until 7:45 a.m. because they already have a lot of orders. I mentioned their hours of operation from 6:00 a.m. to 11:00 a.m. and the order taker just laughed it off and didn't care. I then called the front office and I was transfered to the manager and before I can say anything the manager said he can not help me and I have to talk to the restaurant manager. I said I was tired of waiting (on hold for 10 minutes) and didn't want to be transfered. I was really getting frustrated, the manager response was "OK have a good night" and hanged up. The same night I requested a wake up call for 5:30 a.m. so that we can have breakfast in one of the restaurant in the hotel, since they can not accomodate us with room service, unfortunately, I never got my wake-up call. I called the front desk and said I didn't get my wake up call and the receptionist response was "I don't know I just got here". 
I was so disappointed in this hotel. Never again shall I stay at the Town and Country Resort. The hotel is old and outdated, it probably would have been tolerable if the customer service was excellent to compensate for the lack of ammenities.

title: “Average hotel, annoyingly loud housekeepers in the morning”
text: Given the location, the hotel price was reasonable compared to others. Walking distance to Central Park and Times Square as well as many restaurants, etc. The only frustrating part of my experience was the door banging housekeepers first thing in the morning. It was ridiculous. The banging and slamming of doors was a constant all morning long!

title: “great stay”
text: We spent two nights at the Club Quarters in Sept to start our vacation in the northeast. After reading some reviews about the hotel, I was kind of anxious, but was happily surprised. We took the subway from the airport and it was an easy block and a half walk to the hotel from the subway station. Check in was simple, our room was small but entirely adequate, and the Elephant and Castle next door had good food and a wide selection of beers on tap and single malt scotches. The location was great (a few block walk to Fanieul Hall), and the price was right. There was a fitness room which looked nice, but we didn't use it due to all the walking we did in Boston.

title: “Marriott for a conference”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Marriott for a conference last week. It was a great conference property, large lobby, plenty of meeting space. Location was great for shopping- walk just a block or two and you will find a large selection of stores, ranging from Ross and Old Navy, to Macys and Nordstroms, up to Gucci and Armani. Short walk to cable car turnaround, about 8 blocks to Chinatown, 8 blocks to AT&T Park. You will have to either wait for the trolleys to get to Ghiradelli or Fishermans wharf, or take a cab- they are not within walking distance. 
Never a wait to get a taxi at the hotel, doormen and conceirge are a great help.

title: “Never Again, not clean at all!!!!!!!!!”
text: Well we went there for one night and rented 2 rooms. The pool was okay, but the breakfast was small, served late, and not very good. This was one of the worst hotels I have stayed at yet!! When my friend and I were getting ready to go to sleep, I found a used tampon in my bed!!! So when I went to the lobby to report this issue, and tell the worker I wanted a new room ASAP, he was very rude about the problem. He didn't even apologize or anything, so at 12 in the morning my friend and I had to pack up all are things and move to another room. Obviously the sheets had not been washed because the tampon was IN the sheets!!! Also, the coffee maker in the room was broken, and the toilet wouldn't flush. So I would tell anyone who was planning to stay here or is going to, to cancel their reservation, and find another hotel.

title: “One of the Best!”
text:
The W San Francisco is one of the best places to stay at in SF. I was upgraded to a room on the 26th floor and had an incredible view of the Moscone Center. SOMA is a great neighborhood and there were a few attractions within walking distance. Cabs were easily hailed out front, and the public transit was a short walk from the front door.
The staff were all incredibly friendly and helpful.
Loved the decor and the rooms, though small (and who cares cus you shouldn't be spending tons of time in them anyways) are incredibly well appointed with an eye for comfort and aesthetics.

title: “Holy thin windows, batman!”
text: Thin windows = cold rooms and loud street noise. One pilllow did not have pillowcase, which other pillowcases are questionable at that. Tiny rooms, but typical for SF. Boutique for sure, with prices to match, but not quality. Loved the bathroom.

title: “Great building, great location.”
text: Loved this hotel! Nice rooms. It has alot of great and quite funny history.. Very New York.

title: “Worth the 5 stars”
text: We stayed at the Trump for 3 nights in early March. There was an online special for rooms at 30% off. The hotel is worth its weight in gold. From start to finish with the front desk check in personel, the concierge advise and efficiency, the beautiful well appointed rooms, there is no doubt this hotel is a well oiled machine. The bed was the most comfortable bed I have ever slept in at any 5 star hotel. When we arrived home I noticed that I had left my iphone charger in the room. I called security, they located the charger and immediately sent it with no charge. This is why we will return to this hotel every time we visit Chicago

title: “great homebase”
text: Stayed in the family suite. Nothing fancy but room was clean and beds comfortable.When we are visiting NYC we spend very little time in our rooms, so it had everything we needed. Mini refridge as well.Staff was very friendly/ helpful. Location is great. Many choices to eat within walking distance and subway very close.Will stay there again!

title: “A Good Choice for Us”
text: For a last minute trip we scored with this hotel. Our rate was $79 a night for two doubles. The staff was very friendly and helpful. The room was clean and comfortable. The location was good, two blocks from the red line and right on bus route 29. We did a power tour of the museums, aquarium and zoo; and this was a good location for our "base camp". The pool and fitness center is shared with a neighboring condo complex. The fitness center is very good, the pool is average and needed cleaning, the hot tub was good. I would stay here again and certainly would have expected to pay a higher rate.

title: “Getaway with the wife”
text: Really after reading some reviews on tripadviser had me a little worried however I must admit I am far from wealthy and just looking to relax with a pool and in a historic part of town was kinda attractive! First the rooms are not amazing but they are neat as with the historic aspect. The swimming pool was the warmest pool I have ever been in. The staff were above helpfull and kind. I dont think it's a full five star location but well worth the stay :)

title: “Love It”
text: Wonderful hotel! This was my second stay there. The staff are great, the rooms are luxurious, and 24 hour room service can't be beat. Pricey but it's absolutely worth it.

title: “Good location, but night manager could use some help”
text:
Before I start, I have to say that during my stay at the DoubleTree (1515 hotel circle south, Oct 2011) I was on East coast time. Whenever possible, I stay at Hilton properties... for my meeting at the University of San Diego, the Doubletree seemed to meet my needs. 
They are not shy to brag about their service... just ask, blah, blah blah. Well, due to TSA regs, I never pack toothpaste, but always get it from the hotel. I called for it my first morning there and was told it would be sent up. 40 minutes later, I went down to the desk to ask to them to call a cab... and to retrieve my toothpaste. I was told... oops... we only have one packet left. 
Dinner that night was room service. soup and salad. I asked for bread and was actually charged for cold toast. ugh. 
Next morning @ 7am, i needed more toothpaste and while that did arrive, I had to call downstairs for a cab. The one young man working (seemed to be alone) and said he would be happy to call a cab. I went downstairs and waited. He was running around like crazy. 
Also, he was dressed in very casual pants and a polo... not what I expect from a front desk person.He really appeared to be overworked and needed help. I guess the next shift doesnt come on until after 7? 
Overall adequate hotel. nothing special... but fine. I would stay here again, but would probably spring for the Hilton Hotel if I could. 
Fast forward to day two...

title: “Great view & location”
text: I have had the opportunity to stay at the Hyatt at Penn's Landing in Philadelphia on 2 occasions. The view of the waterfront is always spectacular and you are very close to a lot of different attractions. Numerous great restaurants and historical areas are within walking distance. Accessibility is also easy from I95 and parking is ample due to the attached parking garage. Rooms are very nice and comfortable. If you are coming to Philadelphia and looking for a great place to stay this is the place.

title: “Not what I expected”
text:
My family visits downtown Fort Worth/Sundance Square several times a year. I was really excited when this hotel opened as Sundance Square was in need of more lodging options. If you are expecting this to be like other Embassy Suites....it's not. Don't get me wrong, there are some nice qualities to the hotel but overall I would not stay here again for the price per night ($189).
Upon arriving we were greeted at the door with 6 or 7 people in suits and uniforms welcoming us to the hotel although no one really offered to help with bags. They seemed to be cluttering up the already small lobby. Check in took longer than expected as well.
The hotel is well appointed, rooms are nice and comfortable. Most of the areas felt very clean and almost new. The lobby is very small as well as the hallways and elevetors. It was almost impossible to navigate a luggage cart from the front door to your room. There is no self parking and the valet parking is chaotic. There is no room to leave your car, so often you are blocking traffic while waiting for someone to get your car. It took between 10-20 minutes to get our car, even when calling to the lobby before going down.
The manager's reception in the afternoon was nice as well as having breakfast provided. The problem was that they kept running out of food and the cooked to order line took over 20 minutes to get through. We were there over a weekend and it was pretty crowded.
The elevators took an incredible amount of time to get to the lobby.
Again, the hotel was nice, but I would probably stay elsewhere next time in Fort Worth.

title: “Great Location”
text: We spent 6 nights here and our room was great. It was large and recently redecorated. Everyone at the hotel was friendly and helpful. The location is great with a subway station on the corner. Easy walking distance from many attractions and lots of cafes and restaurants on 2nd Avenue. We enjoyed our stay and would recommend this hotel to anyone visiting Manhattan.

title: “Perfect Location”
text:
We will rave about Redwood Inn for a long time.
The inn is perfectly located for walks to: Fishermans Wharf, Alcatraz pier, amazing food on Union & surrounding streets, to bike hire for the day, to the cable car & public transport options to the Mission District, Union Sq & all the cool San Fran hang outs.
The inn itself in terms of price is the cheapest in the area by far, it is spacious, comfortable, bright w a large window, small kitchenette in our room, a coffee pot that we used every single morning, the bed is large & comfy, the heater & all amenities work well.
We loved the inn keepers, they are helpful & very knowledgeable about the area & were always smiling when we walked in, asking for another nights stay ( we booked for two nights, then loved SF so much we stayed 6 )
Major plus: amazing donuts & muffins for breakfast every morning!

title: “Great location, Subpar hotel”
text:
CONS: I understand that most hotel rooms in NY are small, so I wasn't overly surprised to find a closet sized room. In most cases you don't spend much time in your hotel room in NYC anyway. However, I think the room could stand to be scrubbed and updated. It was dingy to say the least. A fresh coat of paint and a bottle of Clorox would make a world of difference! 
PROS: The bed was VERY COMFORTABLE! I overslept one day because I just didn't want to get out of bed. The location was more convenient than I possibly could have imagined. You walk out of the hotel and around the coner is Time Square, and every theatre imaginable. It was also conveniently located near the subway entrance that takes you directy to the Statue of Liberty.

title: “A little disappointed.”
text:
We stayed there for 3 nights recently. I had booked a double/double room as we required 2 beds and requested a high floor. We arrived at 3.30pm and were told our room was not ready as the previous guest was late checking out and the room would not be ready for at least another 40 minutes, if not longer. This threw all our plans into chaos as we were meeting friends at the Plaza for afternoon tea at 4.15 and wanted to change. The staff member checking us in was very apologetic but was a disappointing start.
When we did get to our room it was on the 8th floor, which was also disappointing, but we were just thankful to get a room. 
The room itself was clean, large and well appointed with lovely comfy beds. Plenty of towels and nice amenities in the bathroom and a lovely big tub. Great water pressure and plenty of hot water. Double glazing helps to dampen the traffic noise from 5th Avenue but you still do hear some. Perhaps on a higher floor it is less. Large windows give good light in the rooms. Good sound proofing of rooms - we didn't hear our neighbours or any noise from the corridor.
Position is great. Subway close by and great for shopping alomg 5th Avenue. 55th Street has a lot of restaurants in the block between 5th and 6th and we ate at a chinese one (can't remember the name) and the meal was good and inexpensive.
Staff were good but I would not say exceptional. We were always greeted and the staff were helpful but nothing that stood out. We had the feeling as those on a short stay were not really that important. Maybe I am being unfair but I stay at the Peninsula in Hong Kong and the staff there are exceptional.
All in all a good hotel well appointed but not exceptional and at the price would be among the most expensive in NYC. Would I stay there again? Well if there was a good rate, yes, but otherwise probably not.

title: “5 star service with the best staff they earn their number 1 spot in LA”
text: My husband and I stayed for 5 nights and also had other family members staying at the hotel. We stayed in a studio on the second floor and it was spacious enough for the 2 of us. The staff knew it was my husband's birthday and on the day of our arrival they had wine, chocolate cake and a card for him waiting in the room. I had also booked dinner at the Magic Castle to celebrate his birthday that evening. The Magic Castle is a private magician's club and you have to know a member to be admitted unless you stay at the Magic Castle hotel. It was a super great evening with lots of magic shows that are very fun and entertaining although I would not rave about the food. Back at the hotel the staff are so very accomodating helping with your travel , restaurants and sight seeing plans. The hotel is not luxurious but it is comfortable and clean. The continental breakfast is very nice and can be enjoyed poolside. The free snacks and DVD's are a great treat and parking is only 10.00 dollars a day. It is a quick and easy walk to the Hollywood walk of fame and the metro is nearby for a quick , cheap and easy way to get to Universal studios. On Thursday night the hotel staff recommended the farmers market up on the hill that had good views, delicious foods, the best gourmet ice cream sandwiches I have ever had and wine and beer was avaiable with live music. The observatory was another great free treat that was nearby. You have to allow for time to wait on line to see through their telescope. The night we went we got to view Saturn and there is no charge for your visit. This was our first trip to LA and we hope to go again and stay at this hotel. We highly recommend it

title: “Just OK”
text:
The hotel was over booked on my arrival date, and we were forsed to stay in a room with 2 double beds rather than the King that had been requested....We were able to move the next day as long as we would accept a room on a smoking floor. Not a perfect situation, but definitely not a reason I wouldn't come back again. Thanks very much to the staff for finding a solution to the problem. 
The hotel was clean (by my standards) but little things were always missing from the room after being cleaned. For example one day no towels, one day no coffe cups etc. 
The hotel is very close to Little Italy, but not much else going on in the neigborhoods around the place. Good Value, but not sure I would book here again??

title: “A good choice of elegance”
text:
The position is not really comfortable but there is a metro station nearby.
Staff is polite. Wi-fi connection is free and available in each room.
Breakfast is quite expensive, it's better to have it in the street.

title: “Great Rate and Location”
text: Finding a good rate for a weekend hotel in D.C. can be a challenge, especially during the summer tourist season, so anything under $100 can prove dicey...if the rate is good, the location is bad, or vice versa. The GW Inn, however, provides both and while you clearly are not staying a a five star hotel, our room was well appointed, clean and quiet. We've stayed several times here and found it to be a reliable choice.

title: “Was OK”
text:
Helpful staff but the rooms were a bit dated. Great location to Universal Studios and city. We hired a car which you'll need to get anywhere else. One of our rooms had a bad smokey smell.
Pool and whirlpool was basic but ok. Pool bar closes around 6 - 6.30.

title: “Couldn't stay - but would have loved to.”
text: After a long flight and BART ride with our 5 year old daughter, we finally arrived at Hotel Abri. Unfortunately, when we were checking in we discovered that my husband accidentally booked the Hotel Abri for July (2 weeks before we were supposed to arrive in San Francisco). They were fully booked for all the nights we were going to be in San Francisco, but the staff diligently worked to find us another hotel (not advised to arrive in San Francisco without a hotel reserved!). He also reimbursed us the $120 we were charged for not showing up on the first night. While we were not able to stay at this hotel, it looked beautiful and the staff were great. Location is great as we stayed a couple of blocks from here. Would highly recommend based on even our limited experience. Will plan another trip to San Francisco just to stay here!

title: “Pleasant stay”
text: Good location in Northeast Philly. Very clean hotel with friendly staff. Good mix of business and family travelers. Received good service in the restaurant/bar. I have to book all of my business travel through the discount sites these days so I never know what I'll end up with. Got a keeper here for a good price. Would definitely stay here again.

title: “Finding Nirvana at le Parker Meridien”
text: You will ask where you are, as the hotel is luxurious and with an european feel to it. There is a feeling of coziness not familiar to most hotels. The smiling faces and friendliness of staff make you feel right at home. The suite was comfortable, peaceful and well attended. Room service is the best and staff are very kind and friendly, and the food is well prepared, presented, and delicious. I consider Le Parker Meridien to be my home-away-from- home in New York City.

title: “Great Location, Beautiful Rooms, Nice Fitness Center”
text:
Next to the Williard, steps to the White House and the Smithsonian. If you walk around 2-3 blocks you will find a few places to eat, Corner Bakery, Cozi, Starbucks, up to 4 star dining. Great to walk all the monuments and get back to your comfy room. We where upgraded to a suite with dining table, living room, bedroom and incredible walk-in shower with tub. The roof top deck has amazing views and could be a nice place to have a drink if the bar staff wasn't so rude and they kept their beer cold and had more options to drink. Didn't try the restaurants. The gym was great for running, dumb-bells and some cable equipment. The front desk staff was very helpful. Will stay there again.
I would tone done the un-easy blue LED lighting in the lobby as it is unsettling. There are no coffee makers in the room so we picked one up for $15 at CVS. The lights are so dim in the bathroom that we had to put in a brighter wattage bulb; there are no well light mirrors period. The entertainment system went out twice while we where watching a movie. But nothing a little refinement can't solve.

title: “Wonderful location!”
text: Came to Boston for a long weekend. Hotel is situated in a wonderful location so that you can walk almost anywhere if you want. Very close to the T also. Clean room, decent exercise room and nice lounge. Would definitely stay again.

title: “Done right”
text: What can one say but our stay at the Brown was excellent. The staff from the doorman, bellhop, concierge and restaurant and bar staff do all the little things to make your stay the best. It was a welcome feeling to have service be important to those working to make our stay so pleasant. They truly do things right.

title: “Acceptable Hampton”
text:
I recently stayed a night while passing through Memphis at the Hampton Inn by Baptist Hospital. It was perfectly nice, and along the lines of all the other Hampton's I've stayed in. In addition to being adjacent to the Baptist Hospital, there's also a gas station, Wendy's and Quizno's within a short walk. 
The room was clean, just as advertised and checkin/checkout was a breeze. The high speed internet access worked fine, and the hot breakfast was just as expected. Plenty of choices: sausage, french toast sticks, oatmeal, and numerous breads, juices and cereals made for a great refresher before checking out. Definitely recommended!

title: “Major Disappointment”
text: “The Peabody Memphis” is an historical landmark and definitely a place that everyone should visit when in Memphis, but it is OVERRATED and OVERPRICED. Our room was not ready when we arrived, and the receptionist told us that she could not call our cell phone because we had an international number (we live in Europe)—we were shocked that a four-star hotel could not make a long-distance phone call for a paying customer! We also had a question regarding our bill when we checked out and the receptionist rolled her eyes and was very patronizing . . . we were just appalled by the blatant rudeness of the hotel staff. Memphis is a funky city and Beale Street was a LOT of fun, but stay somewhere else! “The Peabody Memphis” is a four-star hotel with one-star service (and that might even be too high).

title: “I will be going back!”
text:
I enjoyed my stay, my cousin and I went the 19th thru 23, .this was my treat to myself for my 50th birthday. If you friend the hotel on facebook, they have specials on there rooms. When I first registered my room, i started off with 4 nights at 20% off, so it was a $199 a night that went to $159 I belive. The hotel would run specials for certain dates, I ended up getting my room for $125 a night. Sounds good to me! If you coming to San Francisco, the Parc is the best hotel if you want to stay in Union Square where everything is. It's right at the Powell train station, up the stairs and you walk across the street you are at the hotel. You have to look carefully when booking rooms in expensive cities such as SF, especially if you feel you need to get a car. If you are coming for pleasure and are staying in Union Square, you don't need a car. The parking in the hotels garages are very expensive. You have the trolleys cars, the Muni, sightseeing tour buses, and if you like walking you don't need a rental car. 
I can go on and on, but overall, that was my first time in the city and third time to California. I love SF and Parc is my choice for when I go back. We had double beds, the beds are very comfortable. I loved the place! We were on the 13th floor, whether you were on the 32 floor of the first floor, you are going to hear the sirens regardless!

title: “Fore-Warned Is Fore-Armed”
text:
We booked through a UK online agent (Midas Hotels) and got quite a cheap price for three nights - therefore I suspected that we might be getting one of the small rooms that a few reviewers have mentioned. I'm very glad that I researced this hotel on TripAdvisor before we checked in because it would have been a big shock if we were expecting a spacious suite! 
We got - tiny room, next to service elevator, window that didn't open, no view, no kitchenette, deafening aircon unit.
However, the room and bathroom were spotlessly clean, the bed was clean and really comfy, we had the 'pillow menu', Aveda toiletries in bathroom, and because the room didn't face onto the street, we didn't experience any problems with noise. Sizewise, it was a bit like staying in a cabin onboard a boat - however, it was only for three nights and the first stage of our honeymoon so it didn't spoil our enjoyment of the city at all.
One other thing I would like to mention is that I thought the vicinity of the hotel was very run down, more so than other places in NYC. So I would not stay here again (even in one of the good rooms!)

title: “Great stay!”
text: After reading the reviews, I decided to stay here on a recent trip to Austin. I am glad I did, Everything was Great! I would highly recommend this property. It is better than some of the higher end chains that I have stayed at. Guest room was clean and the bed was comfortable. The breakfast was good, I liked the Texas shaped waffles. If you smoke, they have a covered smoker's area outside, which was nice. They have little extras that other places do not have.

title: “Great Location Great Hotel”
text: Located near the Galleria and some of the best restaurants in Houston. The hotel has a really great breakfast buffet, but the lounge has really uncomfortable seating with this really weird couch thing with pillows. Front desk staff loves to argue with you, (even if you show them their own web site) so make sure your reservation details are intact before you check in. Just because it says "free breakfast" doesn't mean they will give it to you!

title: “Modern hotel, excellent price, great location”
text:
My partner and I stayed at the Hilton Garden Inn over the Easter weekend. We got an excellent deal through one of the discount hotel websites, and used some credit card points. We ended up paying about $160 for a three night stay. The hotel is very clean. The room itself was spacious and comfortable. No issues at all. It is a newer hotel with excellent amenities. My partner and I used the gym which was fully outfitted with a weight machine, free weights, and great cardio machines. 
One morning we had breakfast in the hotel restaurant, it was about $14US per person - we were able to fill up on fresh omelets made to order, oatmeal, lots of fruit, an assortment of breads. There were also pastries and the standard sausage and bacon. Good value for the money and we managed to fill up on food before heading out for our long day sightseeing. The front desk staff was also very lovely and accomodating.
The location is a bit north of the main sightseeing area of DC, about 30 to 40 minute walk depending on your pace. My partner and I walked everywhere. For those interested in the metro, it is a 5 minute walk from the hotel. It was a very quiet area, it appears that they are building up the area with condos and businesses. We had no issues with noise during our stay.
We would definitely recommend this spot for future visitors to DC. Thanks for a great stay!

title: “Worst W I've Stayed At”
text:
The only reason why this hotel gets 2 dots is because it had a cool lobby, nice shower head and a heavenly bed. Other that this hotel sucked. First the room was so small that my husband I both barely fit in the room. The room is only big enough for the bed which was only a queen size. We had room service for breakfast and I had to sit sideways in the desk chair with my husband on the bed to eat. Simply absurd.
Also the rooms need to be remodeled. The bathroom had peeling wallpaper and the carpet was pretty thin and the heater was loud and old/dirty.
I will never stay at this W again. I'll try the Tuscany again while in NYC or go back to the Penisula which is an amazing hotel.

title: “Best stay ever at a Choice Hotels property!!”
text: Loved my stay at this hotel. Felt like I was staying in my own condo! It was very comfortable. The daily hot breakfast was great,. The ideal location was in walking distance of most of downtown Chicago's best sites. Will definently stay again! Hope you enjoy your stay as much as I did.

title: “Excellent Facility”
text: I have stayed at the Dana multiple times on business trips to Chicago. I am always greeted warmly and once they knew my name and recognized me on return trips I was often upgraded. The rooms are very efficient, modern, and comfortable. The small balcony is great for getting some fresh air. The room can be a bit dark due to the dark wood flooring. Bed is very plush and comfortable. The shower is FANTASTIC, although if traveling with someone else know that it is all glass and open to the room. Excellent breakfast served in the lobby restaurant.

title: “St. Antonio Texas....a little piece of Mexico”
text: If you haven't been to San Antonio yet, it should be on your list of to do attractions for sure. We stayed at a Marriott right across the street from the Marriott Rivercenter/I've been told that it is no longer there/renamed.....but a little research would definitely be easy to find the new name. The reason I liked this one better than the Marriott River Center is that it over looked the actual river walk, which is the main attraction. This destination is a must if traveling within the states. The River Walk is lined with beautiful trees, along the water, restaurants, cafes, shopping, outdoor concerts and outdoor eating venues. Delightful weekend get away. The Alamo is located in the area and there is a high concentration of a Mexican flare. The food, people and ambiance was magical. There is no need to rent a car, transfers from the airport are readily available. Gondolas go up and down the river.......loved everything about the area and it was a huge surprise. It's not far from Austin Texas which is a wonderful alternative as well. The Marriott River Center has a huge mall located on the ground floor and if staying in this section, you can get on and off the gondolas right by the hotel.

title: “Cozy and relaxing... Excellent experience!”
text: Hotel Rex is a very chic hotel. It was a very relaxing experience as our room was very cozy and comfortable. The staff was very friendly and the bar area with live jazz music was great. Overall it was a great experience and would definitely recommend!

title: “Four Points DisaPOINTing”
text:
My family and I had a dissapointing time at the Four Points Sheraton Washington D.C. downtown recently...We wouldn't recommend this hotel unless the better quality chains in the area are full or you can get a very sizable discount...
When we arrived there was a long wait at the front desk, because only one of the three front desk clerks was checking in guests, while the other two were engaged in a ferverent discussion (for 15 minutes!) that was clearly unrelated to their work and never even looked up or offered to check any of us in. That was a twenty minute wait before even getting our room key. The clerk was very unfriendly and unhelpful to boot. 
Our room was barely passable. They really have housekeeping issues at this place, at least when we were there. Entering our room, we were greeted with a very foul odor from one of the trash cans as they hadn't emptied it and their was some kind of old spoiled food in it. It took almost two hours for us to be moved to another room. We requested more pillows twice and were promised they were coming, but they never showed up with them so I finally had to go down to the desk to get them. Same bad attitude from the clerk - she grudgingly handed them over to me as if she was doing me some tremendous favor and like I was incoveniencing her greatly by asking!
They didn't vacuum the room or clean the bathrooms well initially so after a couple of days we got fed up and talked to the manager and it improved somewhat...The manager seemed completely frazzled by the way, and it makes you wonder about the whole operation when the manager is not at least somewhat poised and sharp...
Overall, much tooo many hassles and drama! Well go somewhere else next time! 
P.S. The business center is advertized as being open 24/7 but when I tried to use it at 11:00 p.m. on a weeknight, the computer was unavailable and the fax machine disfunctional.

title: “Loved the XV Beacon!”
text:
We arrived in the late evening to our studio suite to have a bottle of Champagne on water - must have been there all day. It was a sweet gesture though, as we were celebrating our 10th Anniversary.
Everyone was very friendly and always welcomed us back or expresssed interest in how our day was. There were a few men who worked the concierge desk, but all were fairly helpful with restaurant suggestions! The sedan service is definitely an added bonus, however I always felt guilty when asking for use of it. Like I was made to feel that I didn't deserve it, or that there were more important people to use it.
The location is fantastic.....so close to all the downtown attractions.....thus we sorta forgot about the waterfront, north end and such. Oh well, next time! 
I enjoyed the quaint feeling I got from the front door men in their fedoras, the lift, doorbells to the room and the flowers on the window ledge.
I loved the hotel....but I am a bit torn as I don't think that it was worth every penny I spent. We did have a great experience, but honestly I have stayed in a lot of swanky hotels, with a much smaller price tag.

title: “What a great hotel!!!”
text: From the moment we drove up the valet person gave us all their attention. At the front desk everyone used my last name and the checkin process was quick and eazy.. The whole staff was great, the room was amazingly clean and the view made me feel like i should be paying alot more. What i really liked was the complementary wine served at the lobby. I was really impressed with the service, you dont find a hotel like this very often.

title: “Another Red, White, and Boom”
text:
Another stay at the Courtyard for the July 3rd for the downtown fireworks. 
Again this hotel was a great location. The parade ended at the hotel, so we just walked outside to see it. Then we came back into the room and ate, then walked straight down Spring Street for the fireworks. 
The room didn't have the extra towels in like I asked but it did have a full size refrigerator. I would not stay in that room again (204). It was one floor above overlooking the interior courtyard where the smokers go. I was awakened at 3 a.m. by a rowdy bunch in the courtyard. After half an hour, I went down and asked the front desk to please have them quiet down, and the front desk clerk did just that. 
One thing I dislike are the stairs from the front desk area to the elevators. they seem to be a bit steep. I am so klutzy, I fell UP the stairs in the morning. From now on, I will ask to use the handicapped elevator. The valet is now $18, and the breakfast is now $8.95. Overall though, the hotel was still convenient and clean.

title: “great staff”
text: Me and my fiance stayed there for a business trip and the hotel is very clean which is my #1priority other than location. The reason I'm mainly writing this review is to say thank you to the staff because my fiance and I both forgot our coats in the closet of our hotel room. I realized this after we were already 2 hours driving back to New York so I called the hotel and they said they'd check to find out if our coats were still there. I got a phone call back right away saying they had them and they told me they would ship them free of charge back to us. I got the coats via UPS 3days later.!

title: “Nice place, great location”
text: First time guest of the Belvedere, and pleasantly surprised. Our visit was over the Martin Luther King holiday weekend -- $150/night on the internet. The room with double beds was more than adequately sized (for a NYC hotel), clean and tastefully decorated. Kitchenette with coffee maker, refrigerator, microwave and sink was a plus. Location, location, location for trips to the theater and elsewhere by subway. Frequented the quieter, more neighborhood-oriented restaurants and cafes on Ninth Avenue -- just as delicious and economical as the more tourist-oriented places on Eighth Avenue and east. Would definitely stay here again. Staff was helpful and pleasant. We experienced no trouble with the elevators.

title: “Short however nice stay!”
text: Met friends in Philadelphia and stayed the night at the Doubletree. Wonderful place with a great location. My room was clean and the folks on the front desk were very helpful. Did not use any of the hotels amenities but I had a good night sleep. The location is just right and around all of the restaurants.

title: “We enjoyed our stay”
text: We checked into this hotel about noon and left it at 5 a.m. the next day to get to the airport. The rooms were surprisingly lovely, brand new looking and very well appointed. The hotel has a van that will take you to dinner and pick you up and take you to/from the airport - all for free. The adjoining pool was nice, clean and fenced although in an industrial looking area near the ride. The hotel is in the middle of nowhere (which is why they must have the van service) but it is where all of the IND airport hotels are located since the IND airport and runway moved a few years ago leaving all of the hotels behind. However, it was only a 10 minute ride at 5 a.m. The staff was terrific and helpful. There's a bar in the lobby and an option to buy food at the hotel although they don't have a full service restaurant. We left too early to sample the breakfast.

title: “Club Quarters Standard: Great Location and Hotel”
text: First and foremost, the DC Club Quarters is in a great location: walking distance to Dupont Circle and Farragut North and Farragut West Metro Stations. It was also less than a mile from Whole Foods, which was helpful with self-catering. During our most recent stay, my husband and I actually had a fairly large room on the 11th floor, overlooking Farragut Square; we've had smaller rooms during previous stays. This hotel maintains the standard that I have come to expect from Club Quarters: it's clean, convenient, and efficient. The staff was kind and helpful, and Sherma in particular was a great help. She went above and beyond to make our stay special (storing our bags, having them delivered to our room prior to our arrival, etc.), and I wanted to be sure to mention her specifically. In short, an excellently priced, well-located DC option.

title: “Veneer of niceness, but slightly shabby.”
text:
My husband and I stayed at the Carlton the night of 8/17/12 because we had an abundance of Marriott points and it's a Marritott property and it's in a great location with proximity to Gramercy Park, Union Square and the Flatiron district. When we first walked in I initially thought it looked nice, but something seemed amiss. When I started to look around I noticed a little shabbiness that you wouldn't see in a top tier New York hotel. I did a double take when I saw the ceiling in the restaurant (named Millesime, which is balconied above and to the right of the lobby), it had an enormous, tacky, stained-glass grape and vine motif "window" (for lack of a better word) that was backlit with flourescent lighting. I think it was supposed to resemble a skylight, but it was straight out of my grandmother's kitchen circa 1988. Then we approached the front desk. The front desk agents didn't have the manners, the presence, or the knowledge of top tier employees. They were a little bumbling. I asked if they had coffee available for guests in the morning and they said they did. The next morning I approached the woman behind the concierge desk and asked where the coffee was and she said "Huh, that's a good question. I don't really know, let me see if I can find out" After asking 2 other front desk people they finally said it was set up in the "business center", which turned out to be a little room down a hallway with a fax machine. And it wasn't set up - it was just something automated that was akin to a Keurig - AND IT TURNED OUT TO BE DECAF ONLY!!!! No other coffee around.
The rooms looked nice enough when we walked in, but we had paid cash in addition to our points for an upgraded room that was 100 s.f. bigger than the others - the 100 s.f. amounted to an extra left twisting hallway that added no usable space to the room itself. In looking around the room we noticed things like burn marks from what looked like an iron on the bureau, chipped wood on the corners of the night table, pills and stains on the wool blend throw that lays over the foot of the bed, cheap lamps, a broken shade that could neither be pulled up or down to shut out the light in order to be able to sleep in, but worst was the cheap, louvered hard plastic pull shade in the bathroom that covered the window in the teensy shower/tub combo. It was the kind of yellowed plastic shade you would see in the Department of Motor Vehichles office or maybe the unemployment office. And it was the kind of shower curtain that blows in and sticks to you when you turn the shower on - gross. But the bed was quite comfortable and the pillows were too - they were down, so that was nice. But what we realized is that Marriott tried to renovate a very old, tired hotel, slapped up some paint and wallpaper in subdued, sophisticated gray tones, added some strange style elements in lighting and finishes that feel mismatched, and put in new carpet to try to get rid of that old, musty hotel smell. But sniff it out - it's still there!
Fast forward to the next morning at Millesime, where we ate breakfast. My husband and I ordered from the menu, nothing complicated. I ordered my omelet with the eggs cooked well done (I hate goopy whites - I know it's cool to like them, but I just don't). It came and the whites were jiggly and undercooked. I asked to send it back to be cooked longer, but the waiter tried to tell me that it was the Emmental cheese I was seeing. I told him I knew what melted cheese looked like and that it wasn't the cheese. Then he told me that it was the liquid from the mushrooms I was seeing, and again I said that it wasn't the mushrooms, but runny whites. He finally took it back (to the open air kitchen) where I heard the cook yell and curse about me and my omelet. Then the manager came over and tried to tell me that that's the way omelets are supposed to be. I stopped him and said "Look, I'm a chef myself and I own a catering company. I just want what I ordered, I don't need any explanations of what I'm seeing or how I should be ordering. Just please cook my omelet until the eggs are drier." Finally (after my husband had finished his eggs, which he ordered over medium, but they came over easy) I got my omelet. It was nicely cooked, just the way I like it, but probably with spit in it. But I was hungry enough to eat it, so hopefully my hot, dry eggs killed the spit germs! 
I know it's not really fair to include the Millesime info in the hotel review, but they are part of the same place, so for what it's worth. Would I go to either place again? No. I burned some Marritott points, but I'm certainly happy I didn't pay outright for it. It was better than a kick in the head, but only marginally so.

title: “Great Location and Pleasant First Stay in San Francisco”
text: It was my first time visiting San Francisco and I can't wait to go back. We knew the room would be on the small size but the beautiful spacious bathroom was a pleasant surprise! You couldn't beat the location. You had shopping close by and Chinatown was just down the street. We felt it was a great central location to walk to the many places. We walked to the Ferry building twice during our long weekend vacation so definitely visit the farmer's market!The cable cars were close by and we also were pleasantly surprised by the tour bus we took from Union Square that was just a block or two away. The beds were very comfortable and the turndown service in the evening was the best. The staff was very helpful in suggesting restaurants and the doorman (forgot his name...was always there during the day on our stay) was always putting a smile on your face. He stood out the most and part of the reason I would stay there again. It is hard not to fall in love with San Francisco and the Taj Campton definitely will be on our list of hotels to stay when we go back. We didn't actually try the restaurant given all the other great restaurants that fill the city but would definitely like to try it next time.

title: “A superb hotel in many respects!”
text:
A fantastic, better than expected stay.
The room was spacious, clean and had great views.
The service from all staff was fantastic and everyone concerned couldn't have been more helpful if they tried.
The location is in what most tourists would find to be a central, safe area.
Breakfast facilities were very good but our only criticism was that for simply cereals and fruit which we ate; the price was too high.
Cheap car parking is available round the block and this hotel is a very safe bet for value, cleanliness and location(Except for the breakfast prices).
Criticisms read previously seemed inaccurate as far as our stay was concerned- book with confidence.

title: “Great location, Helpful Friendly Staff”
text: Just finished up our stay at the London NYC and it is a wonderful place to stay. We got a good rate, especially for the location -- convenient enough to Central Park, Broadway & Times Square and Fifth Avenue that you can walk to almost everywhere you want to go. The staff from check-in, concierges, luggage personnel, etc were all exceptional and courteous and friendly -- couldn't have been better. Wasn't crazy about the decor of the rooms, but the rooms are spacious, especially by New York standards. We will definitely go back again.

title: “Very Convenient, Best View of Bay”
text: We stayed here for 3 days and 2 nights as part of our honeymoon in Sept. First off, upon checking in we were warmly greeted and instantly upgraded to this room for our honeymoon, what a treat!!! We got a bayview room w/ a balcony in the North tower on the 23rd floor overlooking the bay. What a great view. A few minutes after we checked in, the manager sent up a complimentary bottle of champagne for us. Now that was classy!!! We happened to be in town during the Red Bull Airshow and it was just amazing to see the show below us from our balcony. Great view of Coronado as well. This hotel room had a small sitting area and a fridge in it. It was very convenient to Seaport Village and to downtown and the Gaslamp District. All within easy walking distance. Plenty of stores, restaurants and bars close by. We even walked up to Little Itally one day and had an excellent meal at a nice little trattoria there. We did spend some time at the pool, which was nice as well. All in all, a nice hotel which was clean and convenient to many of the downtown attractions.

title: “love new york in christmas”
text: new york in christmas is like a dream. we had a wonderful time my daugther and I. our stay for the second time at the wellington hotel was very happy you can get every where in minutes theaters, THE CHRISTMAS TREE AT ROCKEFELLER CENTER waiting for nex year to go back love it margarita

title: “BEST STAFF EVER!!!”
text:
This is the 3rd time I spend a week at the W (room 1805 on the top floor) and I know I will come back next year.
the main reason is the staff working there : everybody is so friendly, helpful, available, smiling
I want to thank especially JESSY, LAMINE, MIRIAM, MARITZA, ANNA and Mickey (from housekeeping, whatever whenever etc): they ve all been AMAZING, so nice, they are smiling and friendly and make you feel at home
