of course the hotel, the rooms, the situation are great, but what makes it the best hotel in the area are the people working there and especially the ones listed above.
thank you again for your welcome and see you next year!

title: “One service problem after another on a short stay”
text:
On a brief stay for a business trip, I found that Ritz-Carlton Boston had one service problem after another. The check-in desk was completely understaffed at 9pm, and no bellman was promptly available to bring luggage up. There was a burned out lightbulb on the desk lamp, and no knob at all on the floor lamp. Setting the (very complicated) alarm clock required a visit from an engineer who needed 5 minutes to figure it out himself. A room service order was delivered incomplete, and shoes to be shined and returned at 7am were returned closer to 7:20 --- and then only after a phone call. Given the high rate charged, this stay was not a good value at all.
The Four Seasons is a much better hotel in Boston, although it has the big disadvantage of not having stall showers (which the Ritz does).

title: “Clean, no smells, great sleep!”
text: First off, this hotel isn't in a crummy neighborhood. The hotel is right off the freeway in a neighborhood that's typical for right off the freeway. There's a cast iron fence around the hotel and there's no reason for anyone to be worried about staying here.

title: “Location! Location!”
text:
You cannot get much closer to Hollywood Blvd, The Walk of Fame, Chinese Theatre than this!!! This is literally a two minutes walk to the walk of fame! The Service was fantastic, very helpful people even helped find where the resturant we were going to was, printed off maps, give us some good helpful tips for LA. The rooms were big, roomy and clean bit on the old side but for dollar value and location this place is well worth it. Also free internet on the second floor which is always handy.
Highly reccommended!

title: “Rooms very small”
text:
We stayed here for 4 days. It was on the Hotel Circle, where all the tourist hotels are. There is nothing on the road except hotels. You definitely need a car if you are staying here. The rooms were very small. The hotel has an outdoor launderette, which is good and also has an outdoor swimming pool.
The reception staff weren't very helpfull as the hotel offers a free shuttle into downtown san diego, but no-one in the hotel told us this, we just spotted the bus!
All the hotels have their own restaurant attached but s bit further down there is a shop where you can buy breakfast.
I wouldn't stay here again if i came to San Diego, would try and stay near the Seaport village as this was lovely, and more central.

title: “Location ,Location,Location”
text:
One of the best hotels i have been to,make sure you get a big room 
tho?Freedom trail just out the door,its not that long beleive me about 
a mileand a halve.Lot of good food ,a little pricey if you ask me. 
 People not all have that east coast mentality rude and dont ask for directions.A beautifull but small city with a lot of history.Take cab from airport,cheaper than shuttle 
 I had a great timebut forgot the boston cream pie at the omni suposed to be the best anywhere.

title: “Comfortable and convenient, with art”
text: We've stayed at the River Inn several times over that past few years. The rooms are large, and they have kitchens, so you can make your own coffee and store your leftovers from the wonderful Indian restaurant (Aroma) not far away, or the Peruvian restaurant or Founding Farmers. It's a short walk to the subway (and the new Whole Food Market) and not too far from the Corcoran and the Phillips Collection. While we usually skip the breakfast, the small restaurant in the hotel is very good and it has some really good William Wegman photographs on the walls. It took me a while to recognized that the photograph opposite the elevator is by the well-known Brazilian artist Vik Muniz, and there are a few other contemporary art works in the building. I find it quite a stylish place. Oh, yes, easy free wifi.

title: “Not Bad...”
text:
Room was nice, everything seemed pretty new. Room felt clean and fresh. Nice non-smoking room. Didn't get a chance to check out the courtyard and pool, but it looked very pretty. Our room had a view of the back of a car wash... most rooms don't overlook the Trinity River. Bed was very comfortable--on the firm side, but my girl and I both prefer it. The lights in the room were kind of annoying--every lamp was fitted with a VERY BRIGHT 150-watt equivalent compact fluorescent bulb. They were too bright; I couldn't leave one on to read while my girl slept. Nothing is free here. $2 to drink the bottle of water they leave in the room. Breakfast is an additional charge--and is revolting. Don't bother, hit the Old South Pancake house just down the street. They're open 24-7, and their food is infinitely better than anything you'll get at the hotel.
All in all, though, a good deal. Not a bad price for being that close to TCU and the rest of Fort Worth. You're close to some of the nicest attractions in town. I'd have no problem staying there again. I'd pass on the breakfast this time, though.

title: “A friendly hotel with staff happy to help”
text:
A friendly hotel with all the normal Residence Inn facilities. Its close to the 35 but never had any issues with noise other than the air con unit in ever room. As the aircon is just for your room you can turn it off. Breakfast is OK, nothing special being just the normal Residence Inn two hot and a selections of other dishes.
Its not in the best part of town so make sure you leave nothing in your car! Down town is 20-30 minutes away so if you want to same the Austin night life choose another hotel.

title: “Always Stay and always will when at LAX”
text: A very welcoming Hotel from the minute you step inside. Staff are extremely friendly and helpful. The rooms are always clean and functional and the beds are sooo comfortable. Great after a long flight. Great amenities especially the fitness centre. Best brekkie buffet going around. I can't fault this place and always enjoy my stay.

title: “Not what we were expecting. Very poor housekeeping”
text:
Check in was OK, but they forgot to give us our breakfast cards.
On first impressions the room looked ok, but then we realised that it was far from clean. There was massive clumps of dust clinging to the walls over the bed and in the bathroom, a sign that they hadn't been dusted for weeks. The windows were dirty, there were big greasy smears where someone had leant against them with a head full of hair gel or similar.
We informed reception who were very appologetic and informed us that all the housekeeping staff had gone home and nothing could be done until the following morning.
The following morning we went to breakfast which was an absolute joke, they refused to seat us as we hadn't been given our cards at check in so I had to make another trip to reception. When we did finally get to have breakfast we had to find our own table as we got ignored. There was very little left and asking for simple things like butter f or the toast or milk for the coffee either didn't arrive or took 10 minutes. In the end we gave up on breakfast, so another trip to reception to complain.
On returing to the room the housekeeping staff under the supervision of their supervisor were cleaning the room, however they had to be shown where the problems were as they couldn't see them!! You would have had to be blind not to, especially in the bathroom.
When having a shower I noticed that the soap dish had been snapped off the wall and just part remained. Again another trip to reception to notify them and complain, their answer was they didn't have any replacements.
They did try to compensate by leaving a bottle of wine and chocolates in the room which was a nice touch.
All in all not what you would expect from a four star hotel.
On the plus side, it's location was excellent

title: “Quick Stay - No Frills”
text: Overall the Washington Hilton was very nice. I stayed there for a quick 24-hour business trip. The hotel was incredibly crowded due to some big convention but it seemed to handle it well. The elevators handled the huge crowds as expected. No big delays. The beds were great and the personell were very nice. I recommend it for a quick business trip since it caters to the busines traveler more than a family on vacation.

title: “Good motel”
text: Good motel, the only one I have found with three queen beds - with 5 in our family, this made for comfortable sleeping (though you paid for it - $200/night for a motel quality room). Location was great - close to downtown (right behind the hotel), not too far from Ocean Beach, Corobnado Beach, La Jolla, Sea World, just about everything in San Diego. There is also a mini mart and a family restaurant right next to it. Heathed pool and hot tub were nice on chilly San Diego evenings, even in the middle of summer. It was clean and quiet, little road noise. The only cons would be the lack of an elevator, and the fact that there was no place to sit down and have breakfast in the lobby, you had to get it on a tray and take it up to your room. Quality of the breakfast was mediocre.

title: “BEST GET AWAY”
text:
my wife recently fractured her back and i thought it would do her good to getaway. i went through AAA and found this place, the staff was outstanding---dennis,sergio and joseph were way ahead of there game. meet all of our needs didnt pay nothing for parking. the room and the view was outsatnding. i would go back to this hotel again, and again
we are very happy the way the staff treated us and made us fill right at home.

title: “Better than expected”
text: I stayed here for one night in May 2012, with my mother & 2 daughters while visiting my cousin who is a college student at PAFA. I was pleasantly surprised. The staff from the valet parking attendant to the hotel reception were all very accomodating, helpful & pleasant. My kids enjoyed the all day hot chocolate set up. The room was a bit small, but the beds were comfortable & it was clean. We did use the pool in the evening after returning from sightseeing, my kids enjoyed it. I thought the pool area was a little steamy & the chlorine smell was very strong. The breakfast was good, it was a typical buffet hotel lobby breakfast, but it was edible & the staff kept it replenished. We happen to be there for Mothers day, and all staff greeted all the ladies with a Happy mothers day. We were only here for one night but it was a pleasurable experience, my cousin still has 2 years left in school, so Im sure if we come back to visit we would definetly stay here again. The location was key.

title: “Generally excellent”
text:
Loved the hotel - very comfy bed, great location, helpful concierge, spacious rooms (yes, even in NYC!), pillow menu is awesome, ability to use kitchen is great. Ability to use a bike is an awesome addition (although sadly we ran out of time to use it)! Don't expect luxury, but certainly you can expect a large decent clean comfortable fully equipped hotel. My girlfriend & I (we're from Australia) stayed in 5 hotels on our trip in the US and this was probably our favourite.
Few small things that could be improved:
- WiFi fees are extortion. Much cheaper to get a coffee at Starbucks down the road and use their WiFi.
- Our room was not serviced one night during our stay. This was really surprising given how much we loved everything else about the hotel. I was very disappointed by this. When we called front desk, we were not offered any explanation as to why they didn't come, said it was too late for a service and did not provide anything to apologize for the lack of servicing (particularly given the cost of a room). I really hope this was just a one-off mistake, but they could have handled it a lot better (e.g. small box of fruit or small rate concession to apologize).
- The lifts don't work properly. They sometimes take you to the wrong floor and you may have to press the up/down button several times before a lift actually arrives. I assume this was a small technical glitch that has probably been fixed now.

title: “smoke and mirrors”
text: hip? happening? no, not really- a real bridge and tunnel hangout. The hotel is going for uber trendy but frankly purple everything and boutiquified is so 2007- it is uninspired and poorly done. It already has a worn feeling of a project done on the cheap. The "scene" is sort of touristy and the hotel does nothing to insure that the guests of the hotel have a nice stay, you are just lucky to be able to hand with the trendy clubbers, even if that means that you don't get to sleep. As noted in EVERY review (damn, why didn't I listen!) service is terrible. Our $545 room was flanked by rooms rented to what must of been a Jersey cheerleading squad, I called the front desk a couple of times...nada. When I mentioned it at check out he said "Well, it is a happening place"

title: “Good location, but never again”
text: Just checked out today, and I'm so happy I only stayed 1 night. The positives are location and valet parking. However, the hotel is next to a fire station and the sirens sounded day and night. There is a club across the street, and the music and noise could be heard well into the early morning hours. The negatives are hotel reminds me of a college dorm, very small, with ano frills atmosphere. The bathroom was dirty- especially the tub which had blonde hair strands and other particles. The carpet was dirty with blonde hair strands. The windows were so dirty that you couldn't see out of them. The air conditioner had humid air. There is no refridgerator, no microwave, no free WiFi, and no tub mat. Hallway was dark and hot. Good things no bed bugs, nice TV, prompt elevators.

title: “Great value for the price & location”
text: It was in an ideal location for accessing restaurants, the subway lines, & many of the attractions such as Navy Pier, etc were within walking distance. The buffet breakfast & dinner Mon thru Thurs make it an ideal place for families or those on a limited budget. Having a kitchenette helped reduce expenses. The room was a nice size & the washroom was spacious. Enjoyed the pool. The decor is dated but who cares.

title: “One of the best choices for downtown Detroit”
text: This hotel is one of the best in Downtown Detroit. The rooms are tastefully appointed and the beds are very comfortable. Michael Symon's Roast restaurant is one of the highlights of this property.

title: “Ranked #324 of 430 for a reason”
text:
The staff is unfriendly and unprofessional. If you call with a question or complaint and request to speak to a manager you can plan on having to follow up to get anywhere. Even then all you get is the run around and no real answers.
I would not recommend staying here with all of the other choices out there.

title: “You have to see the picture!!!”
text:
A picture is worth a thousand words!!!
#1 I arrived at midnight. Had to use the courtesy phone and it took 15 minutes for someone to come and check me in even though I already had a reservation.
#2 I was so tired i just walked in and laid down on the bed without even unpacking.
#3 I dozed off but was awakened within 15 minutes. My back, my neck, my arms and legs below the knee where covered with fleas. I could see them jumping all over.
#4 I jumped into the shower, put all my clothes in a plastic bag and changed. By then even my suitcases had fleas. Called the front desk. The night lady was very courteous and did the best she could and she changed me from room 102 to another room. 
#5 In the am I asked to see the manager very politely and showed the reception lady the flea bites. She was RUDE and unpolite. They did not offer any type of apology. I had to ask them for a refund of one night.
VERY RUDE SHIFT MANAGER AND LADY DURING NOONTIME. 
Also, hotel is nextto the freeway and there are no restaurants within walking distance. 
Parking is an issue at night. You may end up parking far from your actual room.

title: “Glad I did it, but never again”
text:
My husband is a musician, need I say more? We stayed at the Chelsea Hotel, because he wanted the experience of staying where so many ledgens have lived and died. 
Alot of work has been put into the lobby and stair cases, but our room was not so lucky. It was small, which I can deal with- it is New York after all. The sheets were clean when we arrived, but they were not changed at all during our five nights there (towels were though). The carpet was what bugged me the most. In fact, an hour after we arrived I went and bought flip-flops to wear while in the room. It was strained, and was in desparate need of replacing. The bathroom was reasonably clean, but could have used a refresher.
Robert at the front desk was extremely friendly and helpful. A few of the other people at the desk were less so.
My husband could over look all the cleanliness issues, because he was so excited to be staying there. I suggest that if you aren't emotionally attached to the building already, do not stay there. I'm glad my husband's curiousity was satisfied, but I have already told him we are never staying there again!

title: “Fabulous hotel with great location”
text:
We stayed 3 nights and would surely go back to Hotel Athenee. Our room on 16th floor was beautiful, large, wonderful bedding and towels. Checkin - checkout was so easy. Bellman were all very helpful and friendly. The concierge desk was absolutely the best. Every recommendation was perfect and we couldn,t have been treated better. A special shout out to Anthony & Anabell for the late notice dinner reservations and show tickets. They really know New York and have terrific taste. Location in this Manhattan neighborhood is close to Central Park, Madison shopping area and many local eateries.
Thanks from Florida!

title: “Fabulous”
text: My boyfriend and I recently spent 3 nights at the QT for my birthday weekend. Having read the reviews I was expecting a very small dingy bedroom but was incredibly surprised when I opened the door to a large, bright, clean, modern room. Regarding the towels we had a rail in our room so this may be a new installment. We were on the 8th floor. There was space to hang our clothes and room under the bed to hide our suitcases. All in all extremely impressed and happy. I would recommend this to anyone. The comments about it being full of young, trendy model types should not put you off. When we went there was a range of people from late teens to early 60s. Something for everyone. One last thing - the breakfast! This was fantastic. You can eat as much or as little as you want. Fresh coffee, juice, bagels, muffins - wonderful. The hotel staff will also organise a car back to JFK at a fixed price which saves the hassle of a cab.

title: “Wonderful hotel with a real Italian Flavor”
text: My wife and I very much enjoyed our stay at the Michelangelo Hotel in NYC during the weekend of a ferocious snowstorm in late October. Everyone who worked at the hotel was exceptionally friendly and helpful. The location is perfect with only a few blocks to get to Central Park or Times Square. Our room-a studio king-was very well appointed with a marble tiled bathroom, handsome furniture and a Bose sound system in the corner--which was a big surprise. My wife, who fell in love with Italy during a prior trip, was extremely pleased with the Italian ambiance and style of the hotel. We will definitely return to the Michelangelo on our next trip to NYC.

title: “Heavenly beds, exceptional personel, well maintained”
text:
We had a very difficult situation and Crystal on the desk answered all of our questions and made great suggestions. We stayed for six days and everyone was very friendly and helpful. Anything we needed or were having trouble with was corrected immediately.
The breakfasts were delicious - made to order by Barbara who is wonderful. My favorite was the spinach omelet, but there was french toast, pancakes, hash browns, sausage links, plus juices, breads, bagels, yogurt, cereal, oatmeal, fruits...and on. Nathaniel at the door to the breakfast area was exceptional also. Very personable. 
We also had some sandwiches and dinners. Everything was very delicious. 
The facility is an older building, but very well maintained. There is an atrium filled with plants - all very healthy and vibrant. In the fitness center, all of the equipment worked and was in good shape. 
The business center had two computers and printers. They were a little slow, I just did basic email. One time I needed to print something out and couldn't get the printer to work. Crystal was a big help getting it printed and faxed out. 
The room was perfect for our needs. It was a quiet building (even New Year's Eve festivities did not penetrate the walls) and it was nice how one person could be sleeping and everyone else in the sitting area eating and watching TV or talking. The beds were heavenly and the pillows so soft!
The hotel is next to I-70, not far from the airport. I felt safe walking in the neighborhood which is businesses and warehouses. About a mile away is a great shopping area Northfield-Stapleton. It was originally part of the old Denver airport. Across 70 is another development of shopping, residential and office buildings. Very interesting.
They highly encouraged us to use their shuttle, so we took our rental car back the night before. Great service on picking us up. We had made reservations for the morning shuttle to the sirport, but they didn't have room for all of us and equipment. The hotel ended up getting a taxi for us. They paid the fare.

title: “Does the job for a one night stay”
text:
The good: comfortable beds, free parking; clean rooms, free wireless internet, free business center, good service (Thanks Joel), efficient Shuttle service to both Airport and T station (as well as local East Boston restaurants), easy to get via car, free coffee/tea around the clock, good location past Logan Airport. Starbucks nearby, but not much else within walking distance. 
The not exactly good: light sleepers will not like noise from busy highway, thin walls means you can hear the toilets flush a few rooms away, loud air conditioner fans; gym weight room broken, no pool.
This is a perfect place for a one night stay, but there are better options for extended stays.

title: “The Staff makes this hotel Fantastic”
text:
I just returned from a short stay at the Bryant Park Hotel.
I have to say, from the second I walked in, the staff at this hotel was phenominal. I arrived early, around 11 am, and the front desk team member was visibly upset that he didn't have a room for me yet. Really? I was not expecting one. A rush to store my bags for me (another gem of a staff member took them). Took my cell number and said they'd call when my room was ready. As I had a million errands to run, i was fine with it not being ready until the afternoon (after all, check in is 3 PM!).
When I did come back, around 4ish, I was given a key card and there was a small issue with my first room, apparantly the front desk knew about this because the phone was ringing, and when I went to the elevator one of the front desk members was already on his way to help!! I was given a new room (room was clean and stocked up with Molton Brown products) and within 30 minutes, the phone rang and I was told that room service was outside with a complimentary bottle or wine for my "inconvenience". Please keep in mind, my "inconvenience" lasted about 45 seconds!
Checkout was a breeze...I ordered room service in the morning, lightening fast!
All in all a great stay and I would definitely stay again.

title: “Excellent location and comfortable room with great view”
text: We spent 4 nights here and thoroughly enjoyed our stay. Excellent location as the hotel is right in Time Square which we enjoyed much. Easy walking to theatres and good restaurants (we also walked to 5th Ave area, Rockefeller Ctr, and Empire State Bldg). Easy access to subway which we also used daily (to/from Liberty/Ellis Islands cruise, Columbia, NYU, 911 Memorial, and Chinatown/Little Italy), Since many reviews have already discussed how great this location is, this review will go into more details on the hotel room. The rate was high, but the location couldn’t be beat. We were on the 35th floor with Time Square view. Our room was spacious even for a family of 4. The room with 2 beds also has a loveseat and chair and small coffee table by the window, looking down on Time Square. The layout of the room is good for our family, minimizing disruption to our kids’ sleep when we parents got up first to get ready each day. The bathroom, full length mirror, and closet are by the entrance to the room and this area is like a private dressing area separate from the beds and the sitting area.The room is modern and clean, and near the dressing area there is a little nook with in-room tea and coffee (the coffee maker uses single serving ground coffee in a disposable tray, so as long as you brew some water through to clean out the maker first, sanitary issue is somewhat eliminated). There are many electrical outlets to keep our cell phones, cameras, and other electronics charged at the same time each night. There are lots of good size drawers to put our stuff away to keep the room tidy even for a family of 4 with hectic agenda. We must point out that the beds, though very comfortable with lots of good pillows, are a little narrow and might be a problem for some (more like a full rather than a queen). It worked for us ok as we are all pretty thin folks. Check-in at the lobby (on the 8th floor) was quick, and check-out was easy. The lobby area is spacious and many spots to sit down to use free wi-fi (but in-room wi-fi at extra charge). The business center on the 8th floor is most helpful; we forgot to print our theatre tickets we bought on-line and the clerk there just said no problem to email to the business center and they would print them for us (no charge). We also went there to print our boarding passes for our flight home. Dislikes: 1) high room rate; 2) elevator system - we got stranded for several minutes twice during our stay (once because there was a…probably false since it didn’t disrupt our stay…fire alarm and we walked down 35 flights of stairs, and the second time we think it was just too busy to handle all the people using the elevators). Overall: Even with our dislikes, still have to say we love our stay.

title: “Excellent customer service in downtown Indianapolis”
text: I had the pleasure of staying at the Omni Severin in downtown Indianapolis. It's proximity to anything and everything downtown is unbeatable. I parked my car when I arrived and didn't use it again until I checked out. The rooms were very comfortable and the staff was amazing. Make sure you become a "Select Member" (it's free) for lovely extras like coffee and juice delivered to your room in the morning. The onsite restaurant is terrific! And Starbucks is just off the loby. I will definitely stay there again!

title: “Very dated!”
text: I have stayed at the Biltmore in the past and was looking forward to my stay this time. I was in the Garden building and was shocked at how dated the room was. Everything from the furniture to the small bathroom was worse that mediocre. The only concessions to modernizations were the tv and shower head! Thi hotel was not worth the price and I would suggest looking elsewhere as there are so many good choices in the Phoenix area.

title: “Wonderful Historic Hotel”
text: My family stayed here during our spring break and we loved it. This is a beautiful, historic hotel. It was very clean and the staff was super friendly. It is close to the Woodly Park metro, which was very convienent. It also has a trolley stop right across the street, which we utilized. There is a CVS and McDonald's across the street, as well as, several restaurants. We were able to book a AAA rate, which was a great deal. The only downside was the very loud air conditioner, which shut off and on all night, but we would not hesitate to stay here again!

title: “Just plain confusing....”
text:
I stayed here one night on a business trip. The hotel atrium is large and airy and contains the pool and the restaurant...a good first impression. Help at the desk was very pleasant. The carpet behind the desk was dirty and disgusting looking which seemed really strange considering the rest of the atrium space. No gift shop, just a window next to the registration desk that contained a few items. Per the front desk person, they only had some of the items in that window. Room was clean, but bed creaked a lot and seemed very old. I could hear everything in the hall and the adjoining room so sound was an issue. Stayed on the 8th floor and had access to the club. Elevators seemed really old and just felt dirty. Club space looked brand new and service there seemed to be good. 
Ordering room service for dinner was an experience. Tried to order a chicken quesadilla and was told that they don't have any chicken quesadilla available. Ordered burger with fries instead. Do I want chips or breakfast potatoes with that? I want fries like it says on the menu. We don't have any fries. Um, okay, chips. Would also like a bottle of water...we don't have any bottled water. I said it sounds like maybe someone needs to do some shopping, I was told that the chef is new. Co-workers that I traveled with said that they ate in the restaurant that night and that only 4 or 5 of the 20 or so offerings were available. When I went to the club to attempt to get some bottled water, the man working there said that they didn't have any. When I commented that they didn't seem to have any anywhere, he said that they usually ran out around the end of the month because that's when they do inventory and reorder stuff. Went down to visit the window at the front desk to get water, and they had none available there either. If it was earlier in the day, I probably would have walked over the nearby gas station to get some, but it was dark, so I just gave up and went to the ice machine instead (no vending).
Overall, the hotel was okay. I would probably not stay there again and was frustrated by the experience enough to post my first review on Trip Advisor.

title: “Nice place! great stay!”
text:
just spend a weekend at this hotel and it was very nice. the rooms are small but it's what you would expect from a hotel in NYC. it's dowtown, but i prefer that location over others simply because at night you can actually sleep without hearing hoards of tourists, cars, sirens... it's quiet and after a whole new york day, a bit of quiet is always good!
there is a subway within two steps of the hotel and whitin a few minutes you are midtown in the heart of the action. right around the corner there is a great breakfast and lunch place called Kozina. basically this hotel is really well surrounded with the things you need, not to mention it is right in front od a pharmacy, which can be quite helpful esp. for famillies with young children.
the staff was great and really very helpful and polite. there is a parking lot that gives you a discount if you stay at the hotel and it's really close by as well. (i think it was a bout 26$ a day to aprk the car after the discount)
little story about the staff: we had lost our parking ticket before leaving and we were pretty sure that the cleaning lady had thrown it out by mistake. When we asked the front desk what we could do about it and would the parking let us take out our car, she told us yes but that the parking would charge an extra 5$ for the lost ticket, since there was a chance it was the cleaning person that threw it out, the front desk person immideatly handed us a crisp 5$ bill! we hadn't even asked for anything from them and they just handed it to us. that small touch really made a difference, you don't get service like that in many places!
the rooms are clean and modern looking, yes the bathroom is small, but who cares? how much time do you really spend in a bathroom anyway??!
the free bottels of water on each floor is a great plus! and the guest closet where you can simply go into and get any extras you may need for no extra cost is a fantastic concept!
free internet in each room AND two PC's in the lounge area that are free to use really make this hotel stand out.
honestly this place is great and i definetely recomend it! it has everything you need in a hotel and a few extras you hadn't even thought of.

title: “Fantastic!”
text: Great service - hotel staff were so accommodating. Beds were the best I have ever slept in. We have absolutely NO complaints. Would definitely stay here again if we return. Location was perfect for sightseeing. Could walk to everything.

title: “Friendly staff, nice property, overall”
text: Stopped on our way through from a HHI trip. Had two youngs kids along this time around. The pull out couch was a nice touch as they couldn't manage to sleep in the same bed together. :) Check in was a breeze and the property is in good shape. The staff was friendly and about the only issue was the b-fast in the morning. It was so crowded it was hard to navigate. I think that's a good thing, though, as it was a really nice b-fast, so I can see why so many folks were down there. The only other thing was that the pool is outside. It's heated, but not protected from the elements. The night we were there, of course, there were storms so we couldn't use it. Finaly concern? If you head West under 77, it's a very different area. If you poke around, there are concerns with crime in that area. I didn't experience any, but I've read plenty about it. On the way down, we stayed at another property across the street who had the local police on premises when we arrived and checked out. I felt safe at both, but that did raise a red flag in my mind. I'd stay again coming through the area.

title: “A Very Pleasant Hotel”
text:
This was my first time in Dallas. At a conference and decided to stay at the Crowne Plaza Hotel. Check-in was online and very easy. The location is very nice especially if coming in through Love Field. Service at front desk was expeditious. The hotel is medium sized and lobby is lovely. The room was lovely and comfortable with a large LG flat screen TV. I had excellent WiFi as well. 
The amenities were nice with 24-hour fitness center (excellent treadmills) and business center. Elevator service was excellent with no long wait. 
The Thrive Bar was also convenient and nice.I would indeed stay here again and recommend it to others.

title: “Great location. Fine Westin, but missing the detail to be a great hotel”
text:
If you aren't a regular traveler or a Platinum SPG member or someone who expects hotels to do it right without asking, then you may be disappointed.
The folks who greet you when you drive up and handle the valet parking are lovely and welcoming. The rooms are fine. The Palm is great. The service is fine.
The location is wonderful...you don't need a car and can walk to great restaurants, nightlife, etc.
You can't get a drink in the bar at 11:15pm on a Saturday night? Really? 
That said, as a Platinum member, I shouldn't have to ask for an upgrade. I had one night paid & one night on cash & points, and they didn't know that. They didn't upgrade me because I was a "one-nighter" - or so the front desk check-in told me. Hmmm. Even as a one-nighter, I'm supposed to get an upgrade. After asking, I ended up in a lovely suite.
The bag for the laundry wasn't in the room. The papers to send them the laundry and dry cleaning were there, but the bag wasn't, so I had to call down for that.
There was a tag on the credenza telling me it held complimentary water. There was no such water. I had to call down for that.
When I checked out the bill was incorrect. I was charged for 2 full nights paid, not the 1 night paid and 1 night cash & points.
It is attention to detail and the little things that take a hotel from good to great, and they fall way short here.
Then there's the problem of no comment cards in the rooms, so you can't give them the feedback they need.

title: “Huuuuuge hotel”
text: Beautiful hotel, you could stay here forever. Food, relaxation, great staff.

title: “Good value”
text: Located right round the corner from the space needle but a bit of a hike to the city /pike place. Free breakfast awesome, staff mostly friendly, rooms clean but the pillows on the bed absolutely awful, lumpy!!! BYo pillow!!!

title: “Classic hotel”
text: The Palmer house is a beautiful hotel! I stayed in a two bed and two baths. The room was on the 21st floor and it was very clean. I would recommend this hotel. The location wasn't very good to me. I really didn't feel comfortable outside of the hotel. However I felt like I was the only one on the floor because it was very peaceful on the inside of the hotel.

title: “Nice hotel”
text:
I booked a room through Hotwire and stayed one night at this hotel in San Diego. It is conveniently located near the airport and offers a free shuttle from the airport to the hotel. My room was spacious and had a nice view of the bay. Overall it was a pleasant stay. 
The only negative I saw was the hotel has two separate towers, the Bay and Marina Towers. My room was located in the Bay tower which is not connected to the main hotel where most of the amenities are located. It was a 3-4 minute walk to the other tower where the pool, main restaurant, Starbucks and fitness room were located. This ended up working fine for me as I was only staying one night and just walked to the main area, however if I was booking a longer stay I would request a room in the main tower. The only other negative I saw was the bathroom was a bit on the small side and had peeling wallpaper. It really needed some refreshing.

title: “Mandarin Oriental - Absolutely Perfect!!!!!!”
text: What can I say?? Everything at the Mandarin Oriental Hotel in New York was perfect - the staff was so accommodating, helpful and courteous. The room was beautiful - the hotel lobby bar marvelous!!! I did not want to go home. I cannot wait to stay there again.

title: “Great value,decor and location small hotel”
text: Stayed here 2 nights. Fabulous location- if you like to walk,you can even walk to Georgetown, all the monuments,etc. great art deco decor in lobby. Nicely decorated,very clean rooms. Very comfortable beds and bedding. Had free parking in back of building( limited space there so not always available)Would definetely stay here again.

title: “Okay for a short trip”
text: The Hyatt Regency San Francisco is clearly a dated hotel, but renovations to the rooms have kept it up to par with other mid-level Hyatts (although it may be a bit overpriced). The location is great, right on the Embarcadero and across from the Ferry Terminal. There is also a cable car line right outside the door. We did go through 3 rooms before finding one that was nice, due to awkward window placement in the first rooms. The front desk staff was very kind as well as the concierge. Valet parking was $50/day and the valet threatened that other parking lots were far more expensive. I guess that comes with the territory in San Francisco.

title: “Disappointing”
text: The picture of the two-room suite on the internet certainly did not match the suite we booked and paid for. It was a miniscule sitting area and a small bedroom mostly filled with the king-sized bed. The carpet was brown, the couch was brown, and all in all it was dismal and depressing. The breakfast area was loud and crowded, the hotel was loud, the street noise distracting too. We shortened our stay and went to another Riverwalk hotel which was upscale and less money.

title: “Disappointed”
text: We just returned from the Hyatt Regency Islandia and I would have to agree with several other reviews that this hotel needs some major upgrades. The landscaping around the hotel was very nice. The room in which we stayed in was an average hotel room. The door to the hotel room had pry marks on it, which either someone was locked out of the room and tried to pry the door open or someone was trying to break into the room, either way it was an uncomfortable feeling. The grout in the shower also looked moldy in spots. I feel this hotel did not promote Hyatt's name very well. I feel this hotel was at best a 2.5-3.0 star hotel not 4.0.

title: “Good hotel”
text:
I stayed at the Sheraton Chicago for a business conference. The hotel is enormous although it does look a little dated. The room was very large, enormous bed, sofa, television, trouser press, iron etc. Great views of Chicago, although almost anywhere you can be in Chicago has great views of Chicago. There is a small gym and swimming pool which is just about large enough to swim in.
The bars are nice and sell some very nice microbrew beers. The location of the hotel is great. It is just north of the river and lots of Chicago and Navy pier etc are within easy walking distance.

title: “Average, Average, Average”
text: I stayed at the Mercer for a long weekend last month. I was completely underwhelmed by my experience. We had a room facing Spring St on one of the higher floors. The room had a tub and seperate shower in the bath. I found the staff to be very uneven. Some were arrogant and yet others very friendly. I find arrogance at front desks to be hilarious. All in all I think the hotel is pretty full of itself in total. The location cannot be beat, but value for dollars is upside down! We had decent service in the Mercer Kitchen and a couple of friendly bell men. I wouldn't stay there again. It would have been a value and acceptable at $350/night not $600!

title: “Excellent Hotel. Great for families.”
text: My family and I recently completed our 7th stay at this hotel. The average length of our 7 visits is 10 days, so we are very familiar with the hotel and its staff. The hotel completed renovations in August. The exterior was power-washed and painted, adding to its visual appeal upon arrival. There are new flat screen TVs in all rooms, new drapes, new furniture, etc. The rooms are clean, spacious and comfortable and provide many of the conveniences of home such as a refrigerator, toaster oven, microwave and coffee maker. There is a heated outdoor pool, a basketball court, a laundry room and an exercise room. The kitchen/dining area was thoroughly renovated. It is a very welcoming and inviting area of the hotel, adjacent to a Great Room which is a fun place to sit by yourself while enjoying coffee or tea, to meet friends or introduce yourself to a guest. There are abundant opportunities to meet and greet since a hot breakfast is provided seven mornings a week and a casual dinner is provided three evenings per week in midweek at the Sundowner Receptions. In addition, the location of the hotel is another positive feature. It is not located downtown among the hustle and bustle of businesses and tourists, offers ample parking, and has a variety of restaurants and many stores nearby. All of the customary destinations for visitors to San Diego are within a reasonable driving distance: Petco Park, Sea World, Balboa Park, Legoland, San Diego Zoo, Safari Park, Seaport Village, La Jolla, the Pacific Ocean, the maritime museum and Midway aircraft carrier. Lastly, my family and I always appreciate the helpful, friendly and courteous employees of this wonderful hotel. We are already planning to visit again.

title: “Excellent location, great rates”
text:
I recently traveled to Houston for a Conference at GRB, was pleasantly surprised at how close Athens was to the center!
The rooms were well-serviced and although we didn't utilize the kitchen it was a definite plus. 
The staff were overly accommodating, from the continental breakfast to stowing our luggage past checkout, even offering us a ride out to the bus stop on our way out of town!

title: “clean very helpful hotel”
text: outstanding shuttle to 4 places downtown; very helpful drivers; night staff took their time with us when checking in late; very accomodating

title: “Fabulous!”
text: We stayed at The Surrey for four nights last weekend. Everything was perfect from check -in to check-out. I could live here, it actually feels like coming home. When you leave the premises if you turn left, Central Park and the MET are a block away. Turn right and you are standing on Madison Avenue, great deli's and restaurants await you. Walk another two blocks and you can hop on the subway. I love this place. If you visit, be sure to say hello to Phillippe, the doorman, a true gentleman. We will be back.

title: “Disapointed HHonors member”
text: We arrived at 6 PM, most rooms were not cleaned yet, so the type of room that we had requested was not available. Very long check in process at the Honors check in desk. Clerk unable to find room that would accomodate seniors. Long hairs found in bath, sink and around trash can. Desk clerk next morning asked that I return later in the day to investigate potential room change. No drinking glasses or enough coffee cups where in room. Overall room is cramped and uncomfortable for three or four people.

title: “A magical hotel, with great location”
text:
A magical hotel, with great location
We spent 10 days at this magical hotel, and loved it!
I could go on and on about the service, location, and the hotel it self…
But ill just make it easy, and say it was a perfect accommodation.
We had a Executive King room, and it was absolutely lovely. Very clean (but then you get turndown service 2 times a day ;-) ) 
We will for sure live here next time in NYC!

title: “Nice place to stay”
text: if you are traveling with large luggage not easily walkable from the space needle.We had to ask directions twice.The map at the space needle is not accurate per a police officer who happened to be there when we were looking at it.The second time we asked for info we were informed a highway makes mapquest directions unwalkable.The hotel was O.K. but we had a view of the hotel next door outside our window.The staff were helpful with directions and calling a cab for us.It was clean and comfortable.

title: “Great Hotel...Mostly”
text: Our hotel stay had several problems from the start. Disappointingly, we did not receive our promised complimentary cookies upon check-in, which is not a big deal, but when we saw other guests receiving them, we felt as though we were being treated badly. We were treated rudely, and there was no effort made to make things easier for us. During our stay, the staff was of little help is numerous areas, and with many of them having strong accents, it was hard to understand what they were saying. The rooms are nice, and the hotel is in a somewhat unsafe area, but only at night must one be concerned. I was overall disappointed in our treatment and will not be recommending this hotel.

title: “What a bargain !”
text:
Short stay of 4 nights. First time in an Hampton hotel. Choice made upon high rated reviews on Tripadvisor.
We were located on the top floor as requested when we booked. Spacious room, king-size bed (based on European standard) newly refurbished (same in the corridors recently renovated) and spotless bathroom, lot of towels, changed every day. Big Flatscreen TV. Desk with business chair plus a lounge chair.
Great staff, efficient and very warmful for some of them. 
We did not expect to have breakfast included (indeed it's free for all the guests) so great surpris. Offer muffins and other american style dishes. Fruits. Dark side : Concentrated juices only (but not often free even in 4-star hotels). 
Free of charge internet access in the hotel (wi fi or landline) + computers freely available in the lobby.
Did not use the gym.
Great location in Midwest and quite quiet (we only suffered from the noise of big air conditioning machines from the roof of the next building but otherwise good soundproofing -- we were enough tired to have a good rest in the very conmfy bed) . Subway is very close to the hotel (red line : north to south - very convenient one). 
Check in and check out very fast. Luggage room appreciated on the day of our return flight.
Got the room in June for 140€ a-night, a real bargain for such hotel to us.
Definitely recommend.

title: “Very nice”
text: I needed to avoid the commute to and from Reseda for a conference. The stay was very nice. The room was beautiful and clean. The flat screen TV convenient. The staff was also very friendly and helpful.

title: “The absolute easiest option at Logan”
text: The hotel is really easy to reach because of the bridges connecting each terminal to the central parking garage and on to the hotel, which makes it easy to skip standing at the curb hoping a shuttle is coming soon. Yes, the shuttle does operate about every fifteen minutes, but the walk is totally enclosed while the shuttle stops are outdoors. The hotel is pretty standard for a Hilton and rather expensive so you are paying for the convenience more than for the comfort. If you're staying on the executive floor, be aware that the lounge closes midday Friday until Monday morning.

title: “NEVER!!! EVER STAY HERE!!!”
text: My husband and I planned on staying at this hotel for the reason that it states it has parking available, we got there at 3pm and checked in. The front desk clerk stated that we can park out front while we check in, I let him know that we are just dropping our things off and taking a quick shower and then hitting the town to do some shopping. I asked about the parking situation and he said that they have a lot in the back it would cost $20 I said fine just charge it to my account. We take the key card go to our room and the door was wide open and the room was trashed! We then went back to the front desk and asked for another room because that one wasnt ready, so he goes to check on another room on another floor, he comes back and gives a key for a room that he states is ready. We go up to the room, and behold the key card doesnt work, we cant take the elevator because it is slow and not stable so we walk down. He assures my husband that the key will work. Wrong! Finally get to our room and it was rough looking. The bed linens were frayed and ripped the shower smell moldy and someone was smoking marijuana in the next room blowing through our vent! Since we were just planning on sleeping there we went ahead and went shopping and dinner, came back at 11:30 and there was no parking. I was furious! Called the front desk and he said that there is no way to park in the lot, I let him know that I had paid for parking, his response was "Sorry". We ended up leaving and I let him know that I would be asking for a refund on my room that I didn't get to use, and he said that management would have no problem with that considering all our trouble. I called management for a week straight with no one to return my calls, and finally when they did thy were rude and only gave me half a refund because they stated that they couldnt rent the room out to anyone else! NEVER AGAIN!!!

title: “Try harder”
text:
Bottom Line Up Front: Poorly designed rooms with a severe lack of attention to detail mixed with a "per device" fee for internet leaves this hotel in the overprice and underdeliver category. Saving grace, location.
This was my second stay at this Hyatt and while the first was forgetable this one actually sank down on the totem pole to a place that will be memorable for unappreciated reasons. While hotels in NYC are expensive the Hyatt is tipping the scale a bit to charge at this price point. The lobby has a very cool vibe but is quite small and often seems to have events going on in half of the space, so if you want to just sit and enjoy the energy of New York in the lobby, you can forget about it, becuase you won't find space to enjoy the opportunity here. While I travel for business and often pay hefty sums for wifi, I was blown away at the "per device" fees that were charged. When I complained of the per device fee the charges were reversed, but honestly, getting me once at 12.95 per night should suffice even the most greedy appetites. While the hotel indicated it was a service provider issue, it is happening at this hotel, which makes it a Hyatt issue. Similar to others I found some of the managers etc. to be less that guest friendly in their understanding of my dissappointment and concern. It seems that apologizing is not a standard practice, which for these rates I would expect a much more refined and worry free experience. 
Moving onto the room, it was well appointed with some interesting furnishings and the standard enjoyable bed. However, it seems that this is the end of the experience. They have a nice "green" feature that turns off the AC/Heat whatever when you leave your room for an extended period of time so when I returned from working all day I came into a soggy room that still felt like the humidity from the shower I took in the morning was lingering. I am glad to be green, but I would prefer to be comfortable at these prices. Secondly the bathroom seemed to be created with short people in mind (I mean my mom short, at 4'11") The toilet abuts against the wall which has a shelf that I nearly knocked my head on several times. A taller person may find that this shelf gives them a nice bruise on their spinal cord, should they want to lean back. The angular furniture, while beautiful, is not functional it has sharp drawer handles that I cut my foot on and hit my shin against. I found cobwebs. The bed was poorly made. The bathroom never felt clean. Severe lack of convenient outlets. And finally, the lightswitches were designed by George Jetson, I really wish he could actually tell me how to use them!

title: “Clean and comfortable, and not too expensive.”
text: Was in New York on business for two days, where my activities were centred in the Chelsea area, so I was pleased to find this hotel just minutes away from where I had to be. Although the hotel is an older building, my room had obviously been renewed and was small but very pleasant. I had a very comfortable king-size bed, plus a desk, desk-chair, comfortable chair for reading, flat-screen television, free wi-fi, air conditioner, and the best lighting I have ever had in a hotel. The bathroom was small but clean. The room looked out into a courtyard and was very quiet. A free breakfast was provided in a bright and clean breakfast room and was billed as a "continental breakfast", although it included both hard-boiled and scrambled eggs, bacon, and waffles, as well as the standard dry cereal, toast, muffins, etc. The only problem, and a very minor one, was the slowness of the elevators. Staff was nice and helpful. I'd stay again if I had business in the are.

title: “Lacking service and silence”
text:
I joined the hotel's Select Guest program before arriving. That should have brought amenities like morning newspaper of choice, morning beverages of choice, extra housekeeping/turndown service, etc.
All was well on arrival. Room nice, desk helpful and courteous.
We never got the promised newspapers.
The beverage order was wrong (black tea instead of herbal tea).
And the extra, evening housekeeping? That was the ONLY housekeeping service on Saturday. We finished our conference (in that hotel) at 4:30, and the maids were only then getting to our room. Instead of having a couple of hours to unwind before we went out to dinner, we had to go find something else to do then.
Complaining to the desk, and to the manager, brought no response other than the excuse that they start maid service late on Saturday because the 6th street barhoppers like to sleep late on Saturday.
After coming in at 2:00 a.m. and making lots of noise. After lobby bar noise that ended at 11:00 p.m. that could be heard all the way up to the 12th floor. 
They assume that you know this. They assume that if you want housekeeping service before supper time you will think to ask for it.
Restaurant is not vegetarian friendly--strange for Austin. No meatless options available. But plenty in the neighborhood.

title: “Way upside surprise!”
text: Expected just another 'decent' chain hotel, but was happily surprised with the entire experience. Stayed on Monday and Tuesday nights when the Dallas Convention Center was quiet and got a great internet deal. Spectacular view from my bedroom windows. Hotel is under a year old. All facilities 'fresh' and in good order. Very helpful staff including chance meeting with Customer Service Director. In 'historic' part of Dallas. Nearby Founders' Park a treat to walk through with a couple dozen long horms (in bronze).

title: “great price for the location!!!!”
text:
First things first - people who give this hotel really bad reviews must have been expecting 5 star service at 1-2 star prices. I had no such illusions of this place and realized that I was getting what I paid for. Grant Plaza had the cheapest rates out of all the hotels I looked up in SF and it makes no pretenses of its service. Seriously, this is a no-frills hotel. Everything is very basic, the rooms are small, and there is no continental breakfast. However, the staff was great and it's a totally decent place for the budget traveler.
PROS:
-AWESOME LOCATION!!! Right in the heart of Chinatown!
-Within walking distance to Union Square, the Financial District, and all the cable cars/buses
-Safe area!!!! (My mother and I roamed the area at night and felt totally safe)
-Pleasant and helpful staff
-Clean and tidy rooms! A decent-sized vanity and plenty of closet space
-The upper floors with crappy views have a plus to them: no street noise
-Small bathroom but clean and enough space to maneuver for one person
-A coffee maker is available upon request
-Nice plasma tv on the wall
-A crickety but working elevator to get to the upper floors
CONS:
-Small room (bed is RIGHT THERE when you open the door). Not ideal if you're planning on spending a lot of time in the room, it can get stuffy.
-Tv had only 2 working channels (one of which was CNN so I wasn't complaining lol)
-Bare minimum amenities in the bathroom. Two small bars of soap - we had to ask for toothpaste and more towels. There is some generic shampoo but I'd suggest to bring your own shampoo/conditioner
-Can hear the creaking from upstairs and noise from the hallway (especially if you turn in early - it made it hard to go to sleep). But then I hear most SF small hotels are like that.
-No continental breakfast
-If you'd like a good view, request such a room. Otherwise you might get placed in one with the view of the backalleys. The good thing to a crappy view is no outside noise. The bad thing is there is NO sunlight during the morning hours.
CONCLUSION: I would definitely stay here again! Just remember, you get what you pay for at Grant Plaza.

title: “Terrible stay”
text:
I stayed at this hotel in June 2010 and I was highly disappointed. The lobby was very nice and attractive. 
But the room given to me was terrible. I was given room on 17'th floor. The room was very small, not clean and the the toilet flush was not working. I came to know about the flush when i used it late in the night, since i had early morning flight, i didn't change the room. I stayed in Sleep Inn in Niagara the previous night. I would say Sleep Inn experience was far better than my experience at this Marriot.

title: “One of the 1,000 places to see before you die.”
text:
With this trip being our 3rd trip to San Francisco in 3 years, we made it a point to stay here this time. The hotel is gorgeous. Especially in the older building. Historical artifacts throughout the hotel. Only drawback is there is no place to sit down in the lobby. There is a small restaurant set up in the lobby area, but you are expected to buy something if you sit in the chairs. The lobby area is a very busy place and there are people checking in all during the night. The standard room that we had was not small at all, and very comfortable with beautiful furnishings and a 37 inch HDTV. Giant walk in closet with safe and large marble bathroom. No view, but that was not an issue. You cannot beat the location of the St. Francis. Staff is accomodating. I requested a refrigerator at check in, housekeeping was at my door with it, in 5 minutes. ( Also came with 2 robes and slippers.) Everything was very nice during our four night stay. 
*****A word of caution to travelers who book with online travel sites: Beware of sketchy, too good to be true rates- on line. I was one of the unfortunate travelers who booked thru 1800hotels, paid in full, and was stunned upon arrival; the room was cancelled due to non-payment. I had to pay TWICE for this room. Even though I brought 2 confirmation letters from hotel, all they could see is that it was cancelled one week before our arrival. Now I am in line with 10,000 others in a class action lawsuit against 1800hotels. (An Irish travel company who will never operate again in the U.S.)*******

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text:
The JW Marriot is a great hotel. The staff were all very helpful and nice. The lobby is wonderful and it is a good place to stay. It is close to all the sights that most people want to see in D.C.
The only thing I can that is not positive is that the rooms are small but if you out and about a lot that will not matter.
Still it is a great place.

title: “good hotel”
text: This hotel was very comfortable, clean and had a great contemporary feel. It is in a great location in union square and across the street from Bart. The food in their restaurant was excellent as well!

title: “Good location only avg value for the money”
text:
I stayed here for a conference last week. I was in the hotel less than 24 hours and was decidedly underwhelmed. The rate was $400/night and with tax that came to $480. Room 2234 had a terrific view of TimesSq. so If you want a room for New Years Eve, this is the one. 
Otherwise, look for a deal elsewhere. This room had little annoying things. Unintellible wifi hook-up. Directions to connect that don't match computer terminologies. There is no water in the room, either for free or for purchase. The full length mirror is 12 inches wide and you can only stand back a few feet. It needs to be bigger.
Breakfast in the cafe was also poor value for the money. The 27-year veteran waitress had to have my wobbly table called to her attention. The food was OK. Someone else was picking up the tab but even there is a reasonable expectation of value. I would only stay on a special rate next time.

title: “Excellent hotel in a superb location”
text: We stayed at the Muse as part of our honeymoon and had a fantastic time! We booked the hotel through Magellan Vacations where Dana-Jo made the booking process so easy and her recommendations were spot on! The hotel is situated in a perfect position being less than a 2 minute walk from Times Square, but far enough away to be away from the hustle and bustle. The boutique hotel is very clean and professionally run. The bedroom was beautifully appointed with everything that you could want, and the bed was one of the most comfortable we have slept in! The evening receptionists Steve and Tony were really friendly and helpful and created a really nice atmosphere. The day receptionists were ok but not as friendly or helpful as the evening guys. The wine hour between 5pm and 6pm is a nice touch and the toilets by reception are definately worth a visit! We would stay here again and recommend it to anyone.

title: “Good budget hotel”
text:
Stayed at the Ramada from Apr 26 to May 4 2004. Advantages: The location. It's a hop, skip and jump from the Metro station, and just a few stops away from Universal Studios, Hollywood Boulevard and downtown LA. It's just down the road from Sunset Blvd and boho enclave Los Feliz and is handy for buses and banks. Staff are courteous, efficient and eager to help and the rooms are neat and clean. There's a good comedy night on Mondays in the bar, and it's got a nice swimming pool. 
Disadvantages: The juice in the breakfast room tastes like it's been watered down, and Metro trains are very infrequent in the evenings so can be a bit of a drag when you want to go out - get a taxi instead. Air con in the rooms is quite loud, but maybe this is normal.
I'd stay there again.

title: “Budget hotel about a mile from city”
text: If you are looking for a hotel on a budget that is quite far from the city centre this is for you. The Best Western is nothing like the UK version and looks tired and dated. From the outside, we'll you'd probably pass it by. Once inside the amenities are there but the best bit is probably the comfy queen size bed (if you ask for one). Mei's restaurant was really more if a cafe and breakfast was probably the best meal as it had more choice than any of the other meal times. If you arrive in the evening don't expect a full meal service it's rather more basic than that. However we didn't find anywhere else in the local vacinity to dine so had to stay there. Watch out for safe not working luckily we had to use a friends but the staff never managed to fix it before we left and there is no fridge either. Not a huge fan of Chicago but plenty to do just rather out the way in the hotel to what we are used to.

title: “Not a favorite”
text:
We stayed at this property for a brief overnight stay as the first stop on a 10-day leisure vacation. We stayed in a standard guest room and used the complimentary breakfast; we did not use the pool area or other amenities due to the briefness of our stay.
Parking: We arrived later in the evening (around 9 PM) on a weeknight and the parking lot was relatively crowded. We were able to find a spot, and there appears to be ample parking at the location.
Check-In: There was a very pleasant woman behind the desk who greeted me immediately upon check-in. I had used Hotwire to secure the reservation and my experience has been that some properties treat you differently when you use outside services, but they had my reservation all ready for us and she was quick and efficient in checking us in.
Public Areas: The public areas seemed to be, for the most part, well-kept, although I suspect some of the guests were massive smokers, since we smelled smoke in various locations as we went to our room. It wasn't obtrusive to us, however.
Guest Room: This is where most of my mark downs occurred. We stayed in 8 different hotels on this trip and this room was by far the most disappointing. It was outdated, which I could live with, but the degree of cleanliness was less than I like. Neither the main room nor the bathroom was particularly clean, although it wasn't as bad as it could have been. Worse to me was the fixtures in the bathroom. The shower head was old and not clean and the tub faucet leaked literally in a stream, not just drips. The water could not be turned off adequately. I can overlook dated decor, but there is no reason for the plumbing to have the kind of issues. We were only there to sleep, so I didn't call to try to have someone repair it b/c we were leaving early the next day and I chose not to spare the time it would have taken, but the fact is I shouldn't have had to. Also, the air conditioning system was extremely loud. Even my kids complained they couldn't talk over it. Because of these issues, I marked down below average.
Complimentary Breakfast: I travel for both business and leisure and have eaten many complimentary and not complimentary hotel breakfasts. Their breakfast area was crowded with guests, which is to be expected. We did find a place to sit. The selections at 7 AM were picked through, but we managed to find something for each our our party. You can't really mess up cereal. The sweet rolls were fine, but the scrambled eggs I had were very heavy and I left wishing I hadn't eaten them.
Overall, I received very good service from staff members. They were competent and friendly. The value was acceptable given how much I paid for the room, but if I had paid any more than what I did I would have been greatly disappointed based on the outdated and only fairly clean room as well as the plumbing issues and general quality of offered amenities. From the other reviews, it appears people may have had better rooms and experiences than I did, but I could recommend this only for a quick overnight stay and I doubt I would return to this location personally.

title: “Nice hotel...plus & minus”
text:
Stayed at This hotel last week. Hotel has good location, you can walk to union square and pick up easy transportation everywhere. Great shopping mall and stores everywhere near hotel. Hotel is nice looking, not too fancy. Service is excellent. Staff was super friendly. Room was on 31st floor, on the small side. Decoration was good. Bathroom was great except for the slide glass door. Was not a fan of the bathroom door but bathroom had a nice big tub and shower. Bed was horrible. not a good mattress. Views of the city where nice. Upgrade to club was worth it. Nice breakfast in a nice club room. did not try lunch or dinner but there are free drinks at night which made up for the upgrade price. Spa was small but massage was amazing. Again, very friendly staff. Room had a snack bar, a plus. 
Only two complain: no bottled water at the club level to take to your room ( there was plenty of sodas to take out) and our room was next to elevators and it was noisy. 
Overall: friendly staff, location, and good price, I would stay again.

title: “Modern Hotel, Great Location”
text: Overlooking ground zero, extremely convenient transportation with subway and Path train within 1 block. Clean modern decor. Quite room in spite of nearby construction. View of Hudson River. Nice lobby bar. Helpful staff. Restaurant onsite.

title: “OK hotel, good location”
text: My wife and I stayed in this hotel for a week while her mother was undergoing surgery in the hospital, which was right next door. Good location! The hotel itself was in pretty bad shape, the rooms were very small and the elevators were broken. The heat was broken during my visit and the lobby was over 100 degrees. Other than that, the staff there were friendly and helpful. We've stayed at 5 star hotels all over the country and we've never met anyone as spirited and professional as Denise at the front desk. She is very helpful and made our stay very accommodating, it was an absolute pleasure to chat with her everyday. If you ever stay at the Best Western, ask Denise about all the amazing places to visit in Boston. Although this hotel is mediocre at best, our experiences here were phenomenal. This hotel would have gotten a 5 star review if they gutted and renovated the whole building.

title: “Reception lady saved my life!”
text: My company should have booked a room for me before my arrival but they did not. I learned that when I arrived to the hotel after 11 hour flight. I was exhausted. The young lady at the reception saw my shape and decided to divide a large suit to 2 rooms. I never forget what she did for me.

title: “Horrible Place. But they have Indian TV channels (LOL)”
text: One of the worst hotels I've ever stayed. The room was filthy, the lobby had so much stuff behind the desk I thought it was a dollar store. Check in dude gave us free Advil packets... that expired last year! Unfortunately, we had to be in Indianapolis for l day.... the weekend of the Indy. Paid over $100 for their horrible room. Hallways smelled terrible. It should never be part of the Days Inn franchise network. We think they cater to those who have traveled from India or those of Indian descent. TV had 6 channels all speaking in their native tongues. Seedy people were hanging around outside smoking up a storm. Beds were dirty, carpet had stains of unknown origins. Someone else made the reservation and didn't check trip advisor. Please take my advice, from a seasoned traveler who has seen it all..... stay away at any cost.

title: “Manhattan at its best”
text: After decades of missing NYC at Christmas, we stayed at the Waldorf this past week. We had a king deluxe suite, and was so happy we took the plunge! A bit pricey, but the service, the cleanliness of the suite, friendliness of the staff (housekeepers, bell boys, front desk staff, room service attendants) was by far, outstanding. The Lobby decor really put you in a festive mood! From the cheese, crackers and *waldorf* champagne, to the eggs benedict the next day delivered promptly to our room, was extremely enjoyable. I would definately recommend the Waldorf Astoria to anyone visiting the city, especially during the Holidays. Once again this is Manhattan at its best!

title: “cool modern budget hotel, great location and price”
text: Great hotel, the rooms a clean, comfy and modern - great budget hotel. Shared bathrooms are clean and modern, cool light system in your room to show you when they are available/in use.

title: “Nice hotel, but incredibly rude and unorganized staff and amenities.”
text: When I checked in the person at the front desk sent me to two rooms which had not been cleaned and then the third room was still being cleaned when I entered. I was unable to connect to wifi on my mac laptop. When asked to use the phone in the lobby, since I was forced to go there to use my computer, the so called concierge yelled at me and refused to let me use the phone to make a dinner reservation. The staff was very rude and seemed like it was the entire staff's first day on the job. The hotel was very clean and nice and reasonably priced, but the rude staff and general incoveniences really put me off and no I would not recommend anyone to stay here with so many similar hotels in the city.

title: “Great place to stay in San Diego”
text:
Had a great girls weekend recently and the staff was great, from getting our rooms next to each other, to taking photos, and recommending great places to dine.
Rooms are great and the ambiance the best. Shout out to Nick, the concierge.

title: “Great Location”
text: Nice property, convenient to Union Square and cable cars.

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text: We stayed in a premium room, and it was very nice. Our room was huge for NYC and had a wet bar, desk space, living room, and even two large TVs. It was also impeccably clean and exceptionally quiet for being right downtown. The concierge was very helpful in getting tickets and giving advice. The hotel itself is within a close walk to Times Square and shopping, and the subway.

title: “Off-line at the Omni, but Still In-Line Service”
text:
I stayed at the Omni hotel for a conference and while I generally liked the hotel and the people there, there were a few annoyances. But first the good stuff, because I would definitely return to this hotel, despite the problems. Things do happen. This is a four star hotel and it is nicely, if not extravagantly appointed with pleasant, but sparsely decorated rooms that are big with large, airy windows. The hotel staff was very good and the facility is within walking distance of the Museum of Contemporary Art, the Frank Gehry-designed Walt Disney Concert Hall and, well, not much else. The high end hotel restaurant, Noe, is spectacular as was the service there. 
But there were a few rough edges you don't expect at a hotel like this. My wife and I got out of the shuttle with two large bags each and two carry-ons each, but no one came to take our bags. We dragged our luggage into the lobby ourselves. I thought a bellman would pick us up there and certainly once we checked in, but they never came. A surprise at a hotel of this rating. The Omn also needs to upgrade their TVs and cable reception, as both were substandard.
But the real, but unusual disappointment was the complete loss of internet service. Ironically, I was attending an internet convention and on the first day, the hotel internet went down and remained down for two of our three days there. The Omni was very accommodating, and ultimately comped me on a night's room, but again, in a major hotel in a major city, you don't expect this lapse of service. Upon leaving the hotel, Bell service was very prompt, stored my luggage for the hour or so I had to kill and checked me out quickly. I would definitely stay at the Omni again. Ditto any other good things you read here.

title: “Not too shabby ;-)”
text: Close to Six Flags and WalMart is literally down the street. Also, a Mexican restaurant called Jimador is next door and they are very good and reasonably priced! The Brightside breakfast was ok, the lady up front kept everything out til close to 10 (as opposed to shutting it down at 9) and waited for us to finish eating, she was very nice! All in all....I'd stay there again.

title: “Excellent service at this Doubletree”
text:
Mr Flippitti and I stayed here from Dec 10-16, 2007. Our suite was on the 39th floor with excellent views. 
Our daughter flew up from DC to join us halfway through our stay. She slept on the pull-out sofa and found it very comfortable. There were extra pillows for the sofabed but we had to call the front desk to get an extra blanket. They delivered it within 20 minutes. 
The two-room suite also had a small fridge, coffeemaker and supplies (with styrofoam cups - yuck!) , a microwave and safe. The bedroom and living rm each had a big flat screen TV and enough drawer space to store your clothes for a long stay. 
The bathroom was also large with upgraded Neutrogena amenities and big fluffy towels which housekeeping always replenished. 
Breakfast was included in the rate which was nice because we don't like having to go out and forage for breakfast every morning. Breakfast included made-to-order eggs or omelets but the line was often pretty long. They also had lots of fresh fruit, pancakes, cereal and breads. Service was excellent and the restaurant staff was always friendly. 
We also ordered room-service breakfast one morning. It was delivered within 30 minutes, warm and our omelet orders were perfect!
The concierge desk was very helpful, especially with restaurant recommendations and directions and helping us find our way around the subway system. 
Housekeeping cleaned our room every day, usually knocking at our door by 9AM. They always did an outstanding job replenishing our coffee supplies and making up the sofa bed. We also got turndown service (even the mints). 
We used the bellman downstairs to help us get a cab twice and both times, they delivered. The hotel entrance is on a corner and during the holidays, it's incredibly busy and congested so catching a cab out front is a lengthy process. 
We had a late night dinner at the hotel restaurant once when it was pouring rain and cold, our feet hurt from sightseeing and we just didn't want to go out and deal with the crowds. The dinner menu is limited and the food is pretty mediocre so I'd only eat there as a last resort.

title: “Modern boutique hotel, great rooms, breakfast, and service”
text:
We stayed here for one night during our company Christmas Party. We had an awesome room rate of $99/ night for a Friday night and had a wonderful stay at the Magnolia. 
We had a corner room which was large and included a separate walk in closet, kitchenette, separate bathroom. The bed was very comfortable.
Location of this hotel is in a prime downtown area, near Minute Maid Park, handful of clubs and restaurants, and the theater.
There is a nice complimentary hot breakfast on the weekends and a cute lounge/bar on the 2nd floor. 
I would definitely recommend this hotel if you are doing something in or near downtown Houston.
Note: $25 overnight parking fee, be ready for it.

title: “Very Friendly Staff”
