text: I would not hesitate to stay at the Comfort Inn in downtown Memphis as the staff were the most accommodating of any we have spent time at. When we needed directions, or advice on what attractions to see, they were always there to help. Thanks again for making our stay so enjoyable.

title: “absolutely...Perfect stay.”
text: I must say this place was perfect!! I and my son who is 10yrs.old ,and a close friend decided to stay here because we got an awesome room rate. I must say i was a little leery (i had no inside info on the place) but, it was everything we could have wanted. The staff was very accomodating (the bell boys even played with the kids) had a heated pool (clean) and every inch of the hotel was very clean...Our room was spotless! The hotel featured a free Shuttle to vistor "hot spots"..and the parking was relatively cheap..$27.00 a day (self park)not to mention the hotel itself is modern and upscale. We will be back!

title: “Fantastic location, quirky small hotel”
text:
I stayed at the Roger Smith Hotel with three friends for a "girls weekend." We were upgraded to a suite, which was wonderful. The living area was a comfortable place to lounge around, with plenty of room to fix drinks and snacks. The kitchenette has a small refrigerator and dishes ~ a nice bonus. The separate bedroom had comfortable beds, though they are small for double beds. The bathroom had a nice shower and plenty of room for getting ready to go out. The location of the hotel is outstanding for heading out for shopping or hitting the town at night. 
There are a few downsides to the Roger Smith ... First, the front desk staff, while friendly, are very slow. It took us a very long time to get checked in (though that's how we ended up with the upgraded room, so I'm not complaining!) and checked out. The air conditioner in our room would not work. Thankfully the windows do open a bit, so we were able to keep it from getting too hot. As I mentioned above, the beds are tiny. There was a queen-size sofa bed in our suite, which was a good addition. The hotel is older and it's a bit quirky (iron headboards, mismatched upholstery), but I personally found it to be a better option that the homogenous Hyatt or Marriott.
Overall, I would recommend the Roger Smith Hotel. If you're staying for more than a day, definitely look into getting a suite.

title: “All Shook Up!”
text: We loved it , the rooms were very affordable and clean, the staff could use a little more training , the dining room attendees were a little un-professional, but overall it was a great place to stay.

title: “Perfect hotel”
text: Great staff. Wonderful rooms that are very large. Good location in the downtown area. Very nice lobby with a great lobby bar. Highly recommended location.

title: “good business choice for downtown Philly”
text: I tend to prefer staying here for business vs other hotels in the downtown area since the rooms are updated, the hotel is well maintained and it is a better value for the money .

title: “Lovely old-fashioned quaint [refurbished] dite”
text: Wary at first as the lobby & elevators were a little, worn, but the room although small was modern & refurbished & had a great sized tv w/good channels, very comfortable bed. Staff were professional & responsive to queries. Hotel was situated near north Michigan Avenue, walkable to Navy Pier within a few minutes. Small bathroom but nice dark marble & timber decor, option of shower head or handheld nozzle. Apparently a fairly historical site w/old 'crystal ballroom' & celebrity guests including sorry can't remember!

title: “Wonderful and Great choice”
text: White Swan is in a great location. An easy walk to shopping and restaurants. The room was very clean and crozy. Loved the fireplace in the room. The breakfast in the morning is very tasty. Good options to choose from. The staff at the front desk was very helpful. Well worth price and would come back again.

title: “Selected This Hotel Three Times”
text:
We visit our daughters in Dallas every Christmas because they do not have enough room and allows us to not choose between them. Each time we stay multiple nights. I love the way they decorate at Christmas. 
THIS HOTEL IS A GREAT LOCATION. We can easily drive to our dining favorites and there is wonderful shopping areas nearby.
Booking a room on their site is easy and we have found the rates are pretty good.
BECOME a member of their "BY REQUEST" club and you will walk in to find refreshments of your choice.
We've had no problems so I cannot write about the management.
Next Christmas we'll be there again unless their rates become too high.

title: “Repeat customer”
text: This was my second stay at the Belleclaire, and it has only improved. The renovated rooms are beautiful and comfortable; loved the ipod docking station and flat screen TV. I had a room facing out onto the street and was able to get free wifi from somewhere in the neighborhood. The staff are outstanding and always very helpful with directions and advice. The location is excellent; only a short walk to the crosstown bus stop and to the subway and more great restaurants than one has time to sample. Consistently the best value on the Upper West Side.

title: “Good value and great service”
text: Great value for an airport hotel. Staff was efficient and check-in/check-out profess was very prompt.

title: “Nice hotel for business traveler”
text: Friendly staff and convenient location make the Hotel Blake a great choice for my business travels to Chicago.

title: “Incredible price/quality/location ratio!”
text:
I stayed two nights in this hotel in July 2012, travelling alone. I chose a single bed room with shared bathroom. Don't be afraid to choose this option! Bathrooms are very clean, you can lock yourself in there and shower in a total privacy :)
The hotel itself is very nice, modern, definitely suited for younger people. Rooms are very clean and you have a small basin with a faucer, a safe deposit and a TV.
What you get for your money is really great. And the location is not bad either! It's very close to a subway (either 51st St or Lexington/53St) and Central Park.
And don't forget to check out the rooftop!!! Probably the best feature of the hotel :)
Overall, definitely recommended.

title: “Loved my stay here”
text: There is a club next door, but its really not a problem, The area around the hotel is not great, but not that bad--car dealerships and officebuildings. Once you are on the hotel grounds, you feel secluded and safe and far away from anything else. The breakfast is fantastic, with healthy, sustainable options, and quite a few vegetarian options. I had my breakfast every morning under a tree by the pool outside. A lovely way to start the day. The staff was very friendly and accommodating. The rooms were quiet and pleasant. It felt like a home away from home. I will be going back!

title: “Perfect location!”
text: Thou window view can be not perfect, location is really Excellent!

title: “Do Not Trust The Hotel's Limousine Service”
text: I stayed at the Hotel Stanford for a weekend trip. The location is great. The staff is quick to accommodate any concerns. However, my only sour note was using the car service suggested by the hotel when leaving. The driver said it would be $40 plus toll ($5). The driver knew my mother and I would be dropped off at different locations at the airport. But only after he dropped me off as the last person did he add a $10 charge for the service. He never once mentioned it in the car or when he was dropping my mother off at the Delta Shuttle. Had I known, I would have gotten out with my mother and taken an airport shuttle to my airline check in. And then, he acted like he didn't have change for me. So, you can not trust the hotel's suggested car service AT ALL. It uses bait and switch tactics.

title: “Good value”
text: We have stayed at this hotel for several summers... we love it! All the rooms have been recently renovated...it's close to everything...it's not the Taj Mahal but is a good value for hanging at the beach for a week...you could pay more but why?

title: “Site Visit for Business”
text: I went to look at this hotel as a potential property for one of the conferences my company runs. After seeing 4 other properties in San Diego that day from the Downtown Gaslamp area to Carlsbad this was by far the most impressive. The grounds are beautifully kept, very green. The golf course is just lovely. It's a nice size property with a cozy, friendly feel. The staff was outstanding (even those who didn't know I was there to inspect the property) and they really made me feel that this was a very uniqie place. The spa is one of the best I've seen. The outdoor bungalows for the massages are very pretty and the Saline Spa pool is gorgeous, surrounded by lovely little cabanas. The food was delicious and fresh. The guestrooms were large, gorgeous and clean. And even though the area where the hotel is located looks secluded, there is apparently dining, wine/beer tastings and shopping just down the road.I'm hoping to return for a vacation!

title: “what a dump!”
text: I checked in at 4pm on a Friday and went up to my room. I looked around and saw DUST everywhere. The room smelled like some kind of fumigant powder. The wires on the TV were hanging. Half the lights worked. The bed looked like something was living in it. I did not take my coat off. I used my cel to call around for another hotel room. I made a reservation and left. By the time I got downstairs, it was twenty minutes later. The clerk insisted on charging me for the full day. I paid it because I was glad to be allowed out of there...

title: “Lovely hotel”
text: We stayed here for 4 nights in april 2012 and had a lovely stay. The location is perfect for seeing all the mail sights- walking distance to Rockafella and times square. Our room was clean and well decorated and comfortable. It was a good sized room for new york. Our stay included breakfast which was amazing - well worth opting for breakfast included.The hotel staff were very helpful and friendly and we would recommend this hotel - would love to go back.

title: “Great Location and Good Value”
text: Stayed here on a two night weekend stay in Manhattan. Awesome location with access to subways, and easy access to Penn Station, Macy's, Times Square, etc. Vibrant commericial district with plenty of shops, restaurants, etc. The hotel is well run, clean, no hassle. Rooms are a bit small. I happen to like HGIs for their ammenities -- there is a small business center with access to printing, an excercise room, free internet access in the rooms, and for me, the best part is sleeping on a matress that does not leave me with a backache the next AM.

title: “Great location for New Years party- if that is what you are there for!”
text: Stayed here many times. We got a very small room this time - but the view of Times Square was incredible. We looked right down to the stage. But, get ready. It is crazy - tons of security to get through to get pass baracades. After 5 pm you had to show a special badge to even get back to the hotel. Once you go out of the area you can't get back in if you are not staying within the cooridor. Many people had to stand for 6- 7 hours. Saw lots of them with little kids - which was crazy. - so if you are going to watch the ball drop - the Doubletree is a great hotel and good value considering the rates at that time in the city.

title: “Sueandthe girls”
text:
Great place to stay out of the hustle/bustle. 2 short blocks from metro line, lots restaurants, 2 1/2 bks frm Central Park. Clean, helpful service, water and snacks in room. Very nice rooms. Great family suites. Great singles rooms. Will hold luggage. Affordable rates. Nice neighborhood. Very accessible to all points in NYC, extremely convenient. I LOVE this place.
Currently under rennovation, hope rates don't go out of site! Very accomodating staff.

title: “Great value on the Lower East Side!”
text: Spent one evening at the hotel with my wife and two small children and was thoroughly impressed with the speed/ease of check-in. The room was small, but we were just looking for a spot to re-charge our batteries after a long day of shopping and site seeing. Wife and children loved the large flat screen television on the wall, free wireless internet connection in the room and free breakfast the next morning. Wife is a painter/photographer and absolutely loves the atmosphere in that part of the city. Will definitely consider staying again.

title: “Great location, standard hotel”
text:
My husband and I stayed here for one night on 4/17 because we redeemed our Marriott points so it was free. The location is great - right off of Michigan Avenue - if you are here for shopping it's a great place to be. The hotel is very large and very busy - tons of people in the lobby and we were told the hotel was at full capacity. Check-in was not a problem. Our room was a king size with a view of the city. The room itself was a good size but the interior was outdated and a little worn. The weirdest thing was that the bed wasn't the standard Marriott bed is always so comfortable - the mattress was hard and and there was no duvet, just a thin blanket over sheets. Kinda odd. 
I have stayed at a lot of Courtyards and it seems like a lot of times there is a trade-off between a great location and a great room. For instance not that long ago I stayed at a Courtyard in New Jersey for work and it was the best looking hotel - newly updated rooms, super clean, and the great beds. Sometimes I think consistency is a problem. 
Not sure we'd stay here again - there are so many hotels right there at the Mag Mile that I'm sure you could find better. But it was free for us and overall the hotel was fine - just nothing spectacular.

title: “great views of the chicago river”
text: Corner rooms on river side have great views. Hotel is well maintained and has a nice outdoor cafe bar. Convenient valet parking. Attentive staff.

title: “Comfortable Room”
text:
Everything about this hotel was great, except for the food.
Room wasn't large, but the bed was very comfortable and the shower was terrific. Bathroom is small but they've at least tried to make some counter space. Hotel was for quiet, except for the high pressure window spraying at 6:30 am. Lobby is beautiful. I checked in very late on a Sunday night, curb service was outstanding and front desk was efficient checking in (and out.)
Only problems were food related: no coffee in room. The service at Ponzu restaurant for breakfast was actually hostile, although we were able to go out into the lobby for the free coffee and bring it back into the Ponzu to drink. Bar is fine in the evening but closes early. However there are other excellent restaurants nearby, and the Hilton across the street has a top-floor bar with an awesome view.

title: “A great place to relax”
text: The Magic Castle is a wonderful, gem of a hotel. It's far enough away from Hollywood Boulevard that you don't get the noise, but is within a few blocks to make it easy walking. No need to move your car. The hotel was built as an apartment complex in the 40's and I could picture young starlets lounging by the pool. You actually stay in an apartment so you have a full kitchen, living room and balcony. The rooms are authentic with some updates, but they're still old. You have to appreciate ecclectic. However, the personnel are soooo friendly and the morning breakfast is a dream. Every morning, my husband would rise first, walk to the lobby and pick from fresh pastries from a local bakery. He would bring various goodies along with juice and coffee back to our room on the provided trays and we would enjoy all on our lovely balconey overlooking the pool and Hollywood. It was just wonderful. I highly recommend this hotel and you absolutely cannot beat the price in Hollywood.

title: “Very Comfortable\Excellent Location!”
text: Stayed at this hotel in July 2011. The Allerton is in a super location within walking distance of EVERYTHING! I was able to take the subway from the airport into downtown and walk a few blocks to the hotel. Great staff and comfortable, clean rooms for a great price. I would definitely stay here again.

title: “Don't smoke in the room, ok? Tough Love.”
text:
Drunk from a night of party with a C-list comedian, I have my luggage on my back as I meander down the sidewalk. It's 3AM and I need a place. Stopping on a street corner I notice the faint glow of a neon sign: Bay Bridge Inn. We have a winner.
I make my way to the back and open a door that reads 'Office'. In the florescent light, I stand before the attendant and imagine I have just entered the ringmaster's trailer, about to audition for a carnival act. 
"How much for a room?", my words come out slurred and lack a hint of emotion.
"Fifty-nine dollars, but you can't smoke!", he barks back.
"Anything cheaper?"
Of course fifty-nine dollars is pretty cheap so I opt to take the room. I have no other choice really. I pay the man, give him a cash deposit, and he hands over the keys, reminding me again not to smoke in the room.
My next recollection is waking up seven hours later. I am fully clothed, star-fished, face down on my queen size bed. It's 10 AM and I'd like a late check out. After a few white lies about flight departure times, the same attended sits on the other end of the phone agreeing to twelve noon as a good time to bid farewell. Again, he reminds me not to smoke in the room.
When I wake up, I am pleased with what I got for sixty bucks. The rooms are what you can expect for the price but do not feel overly dirty. I charged my blackberry and slept indoors. At this point, I am happy.
At noon, I make my way back to the familiar florescent lighting of the office. This time, I am greeted my a female attendant. I tell her my room number at that I'd like to check out. In an instant she turns to the left and barks something into the adjacent room; I can't begin to identify in what tongue she was speaking but it was startling and I liked it. A man emerged and exited the office in the direction of my room. I understood that he was checking for damages before they returned my deposit, though the attendant did not offer such an explanation.
As I wait in silence, again the woman startles me with a series of shouts. Who is she talking to? The man left. I saw him. A few more minutes of silence, then again, she shouts. Overcome with curiosity I begin to leaf through travel insurance pamphlets on the office counter... anything to get me a peek into the back and crack this case. Then the reveal: as I peer over the counter, I notice a toddler playing on the floor. My eyes light up, and I am smiling ear to ear. It was a baby she was speaking to all along though her tone suggested a hated mother-in-law confined to the hotel office in a wheel chair, slurping curry from a straw, and ruining the life of this hotel attendent. But it wasn't. It was a baby, and I loved it. This tone had been love. Tough love.
The man returned, and the attendant returned my deposit... two dollars short of what I expected. Normally I wouldn't even mention, but after all we'd been through how could I pass this up? I mustered up the courage, and without missing a beat, the ball of fire behind the desk informed me of my mistake. I am still smiling.

title: “Great location, but basic hotel”
text:
We recently stayed at the Hilton Midtown in Manhattan. We were very excited about our stay here as it was our first visit to New York. Although the location of the hotel is brilliant (between Times Square & Central Park) we were disappointed of the quality of the hotel. We thought that Hilton name stood for a little bit more quality than this. The hotel room we had was quite basic, clean & tidy but "tired". It is certainly due for a renovation. No coffee/tea making facilities and no minibar fridge. (Well, there was a minibar fridge there, but the cupboard door had been drilled shut, so it could not be used.). 
The gym could only be used for a rather hefty fee, the bar & restaurant was also pricey (although plenty of restaurants & bars nearby). We found a great little Italian restaurant just up the road (6th Ave) towards Central Park - Pazza Notte, great pasta & pizza. 
If you get a good deal it could be worth staying here due to its great location, I will probably book another hotel next time. Yeah, it will definitely be a next time.. New York is awesome!!

title: “A wonderful experience”
text: From being greeted on arrival,the bell boys, front of house ,and conceraige staff.where very professional Our stay was a very pleasant experience.We where lucky enough to get upgraded from our original booking. The suite and our room was amazing,full sized kitchen,not that we cooked!!,comfortable couches,and bedroom with views of the city.Bathrooms very spacious,with top quality towels & linen.Would definitely recommend if you enjoy a bit of luxury- and who doesn't.

title: “Great Combination of price, comfort, location, and food”
text: We stayed there while attending a demonstration at the Lincoln Memorial. Excellent location. Included Breakfast was excellent and made to order. The staff was efficient and courteous. Our room was clean and the bed was very, very comfortable. Very MINOR gripes that would not have affected my decision to stay: 1. I would like better lighting. Most hotels now use many energy efficient lights which never seem to be quite bright enough. 2. limited availability of accessible outlets on one side of the bed. Again, not uncommon. I admit that both of these are really petty in the grand scheme of things. This is a 4 star hotel in terms of atmosphere, but I must provide 5 stars because the over-all combination of qualities makes it an excellent value.

title: “Ballantyne is a relaxing oasis and memory maker”
text:
I have had the pleasure of being a guest at Ballantyne for over 10 years. My most recent stay was in December for pleasure and I've also hosted several business conferences there as well. I'll focus my review based on my personal stay but I have to address my business stays as well. 
All I'll say about hosting events there is TURN KEY. If you are looking for a staff to make you feel as the event planner that your job is done, sign the contract now. Carrie, Brian and Matt rock! Hopefully, you get to work with them. Spectacular!!!!
Now to focus on my personal stay. I planned a weekend with my 5 year old daughter and my mother. We were going to have Brunch with Santa on Sunday and decided to spend the whole weekend. We were close to so many activities and we enjoyed them but always looked forward to our return to the hotel.
The rooms are a dream. My daughter had never been there before and she was amazed by the bathrooms. Of course, the shower was her favorite part and I must agree with her. The indoor pool is second to none. She had such a great time as did we. I've been there in the summer as well and their outdoor pools are just as fantasic.
The hotel staff from housekeeping to the front desk are so kind. They seem truly happy to have you in their "home". You don't get that just everywhere. My daughter couldn't get over the hot towels we were given as we checked in. So cute to see her experience it for the first time. 
We ate breakfast, lunch and dinner at the hotel and YUMMY is the best way to describe it. Service is wonderful and the wait staff all made my daughter feel very important which makes me happy as well. She still has the chefs hat from there and loves to play with it. 
Because we were there at Christmas, we were also able to enjoy the Gingerbread House display. That was just a bonus. 
We didn't get to use the spa this time which was my only low point in the weekend. I knew what a treat I was missing. I've always had a great time and enjoyed the treatments. They are very open to my comments and truly customize my experience. On a business note, I am able to incorporate the spa into my conferences and let me say, that is the hit of the event. The educational aspect is great but let's be honest, it's the spa/golf that people talk about long after the PowerPoint presentations have been turned off. 
I mentioned golf and although I don't play, I've worked with the Noelene and the pro shop staff. They are so easy to work with and the courses are great.
To end my review I'd say, you can't go wrong with Ballantyne unless you don't like luxury, being pampered and escaping reality if only for a long weekend. I hope you enjoy your stay as much as I did.

title: “Best hotel experience in SF”
text: We were pleasantly surprised to get a room at the Hyatt through Priceline for a bid that was less than have the advertised rate. Then at check-in they offered to upgrade us to a bayside view for $35. Best money I've ever spent. We got a 15th floor king with a balcony and a gorgeous view of the Bay. The room was impeccable and the hotel staff was helpful and courteous almost to a fault. It was by far the best experience I've had at any hotel in San Francisco or elsewhere in many years.

title: “Great value and close to seattle center”
text:
Very convenient location near the Space Needle and EMP museum. Check-in was very quick.
Elevator is a bit rusty and after you got of on the floor the hallways to the rooms were very hot. Hopefully your keycard works the first time ;) The room itself was ok and the beds were comfortable for the night.
To bad that you are looking directly onto another hotel and have no view of the space needle.
This is the right hotel if you are checking out Seattle all day and stay there only to sleep.

title: “A beautuiful hotel in a great location”
text: I loved this hotel. The location was unbeatable. Walking distance to China Town and all the great shopping that San Francisco has to offer. We were upgraded to a beautiful suite that had great views of the city. The room was clean and the bed very comfortable. Parking was expensive, so take a taxi if possible.

title: “The place to stay in Chicago if you want an affordable, convenient, and comfortable option!”
text: I have stayed at Hampton Inn Majestic twice now and it is definitely my "home" when I'm in Chicago! The location is wonderful, very centrally located with both subway and bus stops steps away from the entrance. Also, my trips to Chicago have been with a small group of single girls so safety was a big concern and this location definitely helped to ease that concern. The staff there is very friendly and helpful. The free breakfast in the morning is a great way to start a day of adventure in the windy city. The beds are so comfortable you almost don't want to leave and the rooms are very well mantaned. I am a very light sleeper in general, but had no problems with noises keeping me awake here even though our window did overlook the street on both of my stays. And on top of all this the prices were the best I could find for the area. I don't even look for other options when travelling to Chicago anymore, Hampton Inn makes it way to easy and comfortable to go anywhere else!

title: “Great staff, rooms, and pool.”
text: Really enjoyed this hotel. The service can be summed up by when I called the front desk to ask if I could borrow a bottle opener. The man there said he had one on his personal key chain and would be right up to my room. He was there in 2 minutes! Rooms were nice and clean and we enjoyed the late night pool and hot tub. Could walk to 16th St in about 10 minutes for plenty to do!

title: “Girls weekend in Austin”
text: The location of this hotel was perfect for a girls get away. The service was top notch. The beds were incredible. Super comfortable.

title: “Pleasantly surprised by this property”
text:
I was very pleasantly surprised.....the hotel was a convenience choice being close to the office that I visited, but no regrets for that choice. I checked in at 8am with the expectation that they'd offer to store my bag, but instead they made a real effort to find an available room and upgraded me to an available Executive Room. Everything in my room and hallway seemed well maintained and working, traditional with some modern twists here and there.
My room was very quiet towards the back with windows at two walls, the bed was very comfortable and it's an absolute bonus that this property offer free wifi as standard amenity for all. I will certainly come back to this hotel and can recommend without hesitation!

title: “Christmas In New York”
text: The city is very busy during Christmas, but we had a very good time. The Mariott Marquis is the place to stay if you can afford it. You can walk to all of the popular shows and we felt safe on the streets. We were in a group of 8 and we all had a wonderful time.

title: “Great Location Right on the River”
text: We really liked that the hotel was connected to the River Center Mall. The location is great. The lobby bar was convenient if you want to spend one of your evenings quietly. The breakfast in the cafe was buffet style, expensive and just ok, not special. The staff was very friendly and helpful. The price of the hotel was not bad considering the location and quality of the property.

title: “Front Desk”
text: I felt that the front desk personnel were at best corporate robots. In fact, they were dishonest and mean. My company reserved my room with a credit card. When I arrived, I used my ATM card (as I have stopped using credit cards) for incidentals. Upon entering my hotel room, my cell phone alerted me to a $500 charge on my debit card. Whoa! I wish I had been told that the whole balance for the room was going on my card. The front desk after an hour of conversation said to come back the next day to complete a series of faxes and phone calls. I was in The City to work not deal with hotels and banks. So, I then checked out of my room but was still charged for staying the night. They said that there was a penalty for canceling a reservation within 24-hours. I asked them to charge the credit card that held the reservation and not my debit card. No deal. They were not going to help me beyond taking one night off my atm card.

title: “Great Value”
text: I booked several 1-Bedroom suites at the Shelburne for a family reunion weekend and it was a wonderful experience. I've stayed in many expensive New York hotels with very small rooms, so the spacious rooms at the Shelburne were a pleasant surprise. It was great having a kitchen and dining area in the room and there is a good-sized supermarket just a block away. Check in and out were fast and all the staff that we encountered were very pleasant. Considering the price of these rooms, I feel it's one of the best hotel values in New York and I give it the highest recommendation.

title: “Great location, very clean hotel”
text: I stayed here for 2 nights in June. This location is fantastic, it's just off Wall Street and great for shopping and sightseeing. It's easy to get the subway up to midtown for more sights. This is one of the cleanest and most comfortable hotels I've stayed in on a budget. Everything looks great, the room had a flat-screen TV and you can help yourself to anything you need from the closets they have on every floor. It gets very very quiet in the evenings and on weekends - we got back at 9pm and could not find a restaurant anywhere that was open. Had to go to a deli a few blocks away.

title: “FANTASTIC hotel!”
text:
I only wish I could have stayed longer, stayed for one night in July.
From the moment I arrived staff were extremely friendly and recommended restaurants in the area and offered maps and other suggestions.
The hotel has been completely renovated, some of the older photos are completely irrelevant now.
Rooms are very trendy and elegant. Although they are a little small, being from Europe these are the usual size hotel rooms that we have, so no complaints.
Large LCD TV with external adaptors (bring a cable!) in each room so you could plug in your MP3 player or play a DVD on the DVD player provided. 
Free fast wireless internet access also available which I used without any issues.
Large desk from which to work on also in the room.
Bathroom had a lovely walk in shower (good water pressure) which I could have stayed in all day and all the usual hotel condiments were provided.
The best thing about the room for me was the espresso machine, -yes-one espresso machine per room which was fantastic! 
The hotel is located 10 minutes walk from Dupont circle metro stop or 15 minutes flat walk from U street. 
Also, lots of comments mention the "uphill" walk from Dupont circle, the comments are a little OTT as far as I'm concerned. The hill consists of a slope which in most parts of the world would not be considered a hill at all! It's a pleasant walk, if you have a problem with the slope then U street is just a bit further away otherwise there are stacks of cabs available out on the main road.
If you are up for a drink you are just moments away from 18th Street / Adams Morgan area where there are plenty of bars and late night clubs.
However the hotel itself is located in an area around all the embassy buildings and is very quiet at night - I slept like a baby.
I only wish I had found this hotel sooner, I would have stayed here for my whole trip.

title: “Excellent hotel for business travelers at LAX”
text: This is the best hotel near LAX by far. Service is excellent, as is the food. Rooms are good size and well kept. The only downside is the parking. Self parking is a bit of a walk - and I did not feel comfortable walking that far alone at night. So I had to use valet parking, which was very prompt, but expensive.

title: “Great Value Good Location”
text: We've stayed in numerous hotels throughout Manhattan including the Michelangelo and the Drake, both nice, but for value the Warwick was a good find, averaging 170.00/night. I had requested two rooms side by side and that's what they gave us, but on a smoking floor. The sheets smelled of smoke. But the next day they moved us, and we were pleased with the size of our room. Since it has been recently refurbished, it's as nice as some higher rated hotels, nothing lavish, but good. For value I would recommend it.

title: “Excellent NYC hotel!”
text: Stayed at the San Carlos for 3 nights in a one bedroom suite this July. I chose this hotel after countless hours of Internet searches of NYC hotels and I have to say I am extremely happy that I did! The room that we had was clean and spacious with 1 1/2 baths plus a small kitchenette area. The hotel staff is helpful and friendly. Location is great for midtown. We were able to walk to Times Square, Central Park & Radio City! Plus, breakfast is included with your stay! My only problem was that I had to leave so soon!!!

title: “I happen to stumble upon this place from...”
text:
I happen to stumble upon this place from one of the app on my iPhone. The place is phenomenal with a 2nd floor lobby and check in. The staff is very friendly and informative about the city. The room I had was on the 5th floor that wrapped around the building allowing views from both sides. The area of bustling with
Restaurants and shops. The interesting thing is that I was given the same price as the ad on my iPhone. Then there was parking in a lot down the block This was great. I would definitely visit this hotel again.

title: “Not good enough for the area”
text: The hotel is down at heel. One of the elevators has a broken floor. The pillows leave you with neck ache. The breakfast is disgusting and waiting staff unfriendly. The service in Library Bar excruciatingly slow but the food is palatable. Most of the staff are unfriendly. Probably only somewhere to stay for the location-it is close to Georgetown and within easy walk of the White House.

title: “Horrible service”
text: This is a horrible place. The worst front desk I have ever seen. I gave them a credit card at check in and ordered a movie. At 7:30 AM I got woken up by someone telling me that I needed to come to the front desk and settle up my bill. I couldn't believe it. They then called me two more times before check out to make sure i would pay for the movie. I have never seen a more unprofessional staff. The next day, no apology. She seemed aggravated that I even found it strange that they were calling guests early in the morning. Stay elsewhere

title: “Excellent but some glitches remain”
text:
Stayed a week at the hotel with family. Lots of little issues to frustrate the week but otherwise excellent choice for a family visit to Baltimore Inner Harbor.
Pros:
Location (you can walk to most shopping, dining and entertainment in inner harbor). CCC. Room Size(better than average). Free Breakfast. Duty Manager. Great gym & Indoor Pools for adults.
Cons:
Expensive and very busy parking (can take you 20-30 minutes if you don't call valet in advance); Avg food quality (limited selection and not fully stocked - you'll have to wait for/ask the attendants frequently to stock up items & silverware - so if you are in hurry to go some place, arrive early); access to gym pools & hot tub limited for young (<16); no harbor views (the hotel is on the inside street and encased by taller buildings)
Minor:
Hot water went out for 3 days (Hotel offered transfer to nearby Courtyard and also made arrangements for shower use at the hotel) - probably a one of that was beyond the hotels control. 
Major Frustration:
Booked at Hilton on-line and pre-paid for the stay for a 1 bedroom suite. Hotel provided studio and also charged the current rack rate (much higher). Despite having confirmed the booking with the property before arriving, they gave us a different room.
Needless to stay there was a lot of distraction and angst at having to deal with Hilton customer service (who refused to refund the pre-pay) and property staff during and after the trip to finally resolve the billing and rate issue. Credit to the efficient Duty Manager for her prompt attention and stepping in but till she arrived, no other staff member paid any heed. It was a pain to have to do the go between the Hilton corporate staff and franchise Hotel (Hilton acted like they had nothing to do with the indep. business). Since another reviewer had similar frustration, there is an opportunity somewhere for Hilton to ensure pre-pays are communicated to the hotels and honored.
Tip:
Take free CCC (Charm City Connector) buses and water taxis. 45 minutes by car to National Mall in Washington DC

title: “Not worth it”
text:
Overall our stay was just okay. The room we reserved was not available so they offered an upgrade but honestly the upgraded room (small suite) was cramped and was definitely not as open as our double deluxe room would've been. 
I thought the bathroom was nice but that alone was not worth the $400+ room rate. I did have a couple of issues, the main issue being that the breakfast we ordered via room service was terrible. I actually had to send it back because the eggs were completely overcooked, the ham was rubbery from sitting in the warmer too long and the english muffin was completely cold and untoasted. 
Overall we were disappointed and have had much better experiences at 5 star hotels like The Ritz and 4 stars like Westin hotels.

title: “Classic Hotel”
text: Stayed at the Omni Parker for 3 nights last week. The first things that strikes you about this hotel as you walk in is its classic charm. The only hotel that I could compare it to in appearance would be the Waldorf Astoria in New York. Staff were extremely helpful, efficient and friendly. My friend and I had a deluxe room on the 7th floor with 2 double beds. The room was clean and the beds were comfy. Yes the rooms could probably do with a little updating but that is just nitpicking. When staying here you are left in no doubt that you are staying in a truly classy hotel with a rich history. I truly hope that this is something that does not get lost as time goes on and the hotel inevitably gets a facelift. Also for its location (pretty much 10 mins walk from everything) and the cost I would certainly not hesitate to stay at the Omni Parker during any future trips I take to Boston.

title: “Get a room at the back!”
text: We booked this room for a VERY reasonable rate and loved its central location to the Gaslamp quarter. The room had been recently renovated, and after flying in that night from the east coast, I was glad to fall into a clean and cozy bed. There was a sorority holding a formal in the hotel, but management made sure to put all hotel patrons who were not part of that party on separate floors away from them. It was a very wise decision, as I know those dances can get rowdy. However, it was not those revelers that woke me up that night, but the Greyhound station across the street announcing the departure and arrival of buses. I am not a light sleeper, but it woke both my family and me up. In the morning, we requested a room on the other side of the hotel (the backside), and it was much quieter. I was not awoken (neither was anyone else) all night. If you get a room in the front, I would rate this hotel poor. If you get a room at the back, I would rate it very good.

title: “Older, but beautiful and a fun place to stay with kids”
text: We spent 4 nights at the Bahia and it was great overall. I was a little nervous after reading the mixed reviews of the hotel but decided to stay due to the location. We were all disappointed to learn that the Bahia Belle only runs on Fridays and Saturdays in the winter time, and we stayed Sunday-Thursday. Our room looked quite scary from the outside, but inside it was fine. Roomy enough for us and our 5 kids. We had a few issues (the TV in the living room didn't work, and one lamp had no light bulbs) but maintenance took care of it right away. The kids loved being right on the beach and playing in the grassy areas all over the hotel. They have a small playground right on the beach with sailboats for renting, (they were hide and seek spots for us!) There is also a complimentary arcade which was a huge hit. I don't think I'd stay here for a nice business trip away, but it was a great beachy place to take the family!

title: “Excellent hotel well worth #4 status”
text: Stayed here 2 weeks ago and the hotel lives up to its reputation. Lovely big room with good room service each day and i loved the animal print robes. The staff are very attentive and gave good advice when asked. DuPont circle is an excellent base making Washington very walkable. Perhaps more choice for the continental breakfast and tea making facilities in the room without asking but otherwise no complaints. The evening session of wine and canapés was excellent for lone travellers. Would definitely stay again..... Enjoy

title: “Location, location, location + best bartender anywhere: YOUSEF”
text:
The only way this location could be any better is if it sat on top of a Metro station. And the bar, 21st Ammendment, has Yousef, the best bartender I have ever known. Our second night we walked into the bar and we had barely sat down at a table (the bar was full) and Yousef had brought us our drinks; I didn't even think he had seen us walk in. He is amazing: never flustered, never bothered, always cool.
We took the metro everywhere except to the Mall as it, theMall, was only a few blocks away. Besides location, a hotel is a hotel is a hotel. My wife and I have been in over a 100 hotels and motels in the last 5 years and believe me they all seem the same after a while...a little difference in size and cost, but these two are not related, and furnishings, but how much time are you spending in the room?

title: “Nice Place”
text: A one night stay in a nice hotel with a great view. The hotel is in the Gold Coast area, walking distance from Michigan Avenue.

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
This place has a great location to see all the sights of the city. Its also close to a subway stop which is a bonus.
The room was spacious at a reasonable price.
I would stay here if in NYC again.

title: “Yet another tired, lame Sheraton”
text: While I've had good experiences at many SPG properties, this is yet another low-tier, tired Sheraton, with a tired staff, tired rooms, tired service. Check-in was indifferent, halls are cave-dark, with bleach stains and crud on all the carpeting. I'm told this will property will be renovated in three years, which is about seven years too late. If the whole town wasn't booked solid, I'd move tonight.

title: “Dependable”
text:
This Fairfield Inn is located on a busy thoroughfare, but it is suprisingly quiet, and the position of the building relative to the street keeps traffic noise at a minimum. Some rooms facing Colorado Boulevard have a view of the Rocky Mountains, but there is some suburban clutter in the foreground, including a gas station immediately adjacent to the hotel and a strip mall on the other side of the boulevard. The location is convenient to most of south Denver, and it is a short but traffic-heavy drive to the Cherry Creek shopping district a few blocks to the north and west. Best of all, the hotel is located only about a block from the intersection of Colorado Boulevard and Interstate 25, making it easy to get on the freeway and go to other parts of the city from this location. However, if you're interested in the sights and venues of downtown and lower downtown Denver, there are far more convenient locations than this. There are a number of chain restaurants in the immediate vicinity to the north and south on Colorado Boulevard, and there is a major supermarket on the west side of the boulevard, just across from the hotel, if you are interested in fresh food or deli items. Don't try to walk there, though. The street is six or eight lanes wide and not pedestrian friendly.
Service was quite friendly and efficient, and check-in and check-out were hassle-free.
The exact amenities you'll find in the rooms are difficult to determine ahead of time. We have stayed at the hotel on three occasions. In the first case we were pleased to find a small refrigerator in the room. On our next visit we brought along a few things to keep chilled, only to find that this room had no refrigerator, although it was the same type and price as the one we had stayed in earlier. The third time we did not bring anything to keep cold, and sure enough, we had a refrigerator. If having a refrigerator is important, you had best make your reservation by phone and request one. Otherwise, it appears to be random luck.
The rooms are not spacious, but we did not feel cramped, and for a one-night stay I consider the size adequate. The bathroom is likewise small, but well-appointed. There was plenty of hot water in the tub-shower and good qualitiy towels. We had no complaints about the bed and slept well. The internet connection in the room worked well.
There is a small well-kept indoor swimming pool off the lobby, and one passes through the swimming pool area to reach the fitness center. It is equipped with a couple of treadmills and nautilus machines, and while modest in scope, the exercise room had everything I needed for a decent morning workout. 
Outside the fitness center and swimming pool area is a pleasant patio facing the side street, Mexico Avenue, where one can sit and have morning coffee. Breakfast is included in the price of the room and is served in a typical Fairfield Inn breakfast nook. Look for the line of hotel guests at the waffle iron. 
There is free underground parking beneath the hotel, with a very convenient pedestrian entry ramp directly from the parking garage into the lobby. The driveway from Mexico Avenue to the parking garage is very narrow, and there can be some brief congestion if two cars meet coming in and out.
The pluses definitely outweight the minuses at this hotel. It's a dependable place for its quality and price (our room was just over $100 a night), and we will likely return when the location proves convenient to our plans in Denver.

title: “Comfortable stay”
text:
Decent size hotel, located right in the middle of the Fisherman's Wharf. Great location! A lot of bus tours, bike tours are within a 2 block walk. Plenty of food and sights, all within walking distance. I do not recommend bringing a car, as you can walk everywhere and parking is pricey, $41 a day at this hotel.
We were a little disappointed when we checked in because we were not greeted as Priority club members. Usually at check in you are greeted and given water or cookies. Not the end of the world, but a little touch we have received at every other Holiday Inn Express, and we like it. Hotel staff was friendly and courteous.
The room was a little small but clean. No view, unless you like looking at the concrete walls and other peoples rooms. The bed and pillows were comfortable. The bathroom was clean. 
The breakfast was good. Eggs, bacon, cereal, bagels, toast, ect. They had their great cinnamon buns but they were luke warm at best. They stack the buns on top of each other so they don't have to refill so often but in doing that they never have a chance to heat up. They are still good but definitely not the same as when they are fresh and warm! It gets really busy! I noticed they stopped putting out fresh buns at around 8:30. Once they stop putting out fresh food your selection goes down FAST! I would suggest getting there before 8:30 if you want a good hearty breakfast. They provide a decent size seating area but it is always full, so search for a seat before you get your food and have another family member hold it.
Did not use the fitness room but it looked nice and big. We always use their computer as we would rather not bring our laptop. Their lobby is large. Overall, we had an average stay. Just thought it was kind of pricey for the size and quality of the room. Again, nothing fancy or special, but you will have a comfortable stay.

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text: I hosted my family reunion at this hotel, and the entire staff provided outstanding customer service and showed genuine interest in our family reunion being a success. They were very attentive, helpful, and hospitable the entire weekend. Compliments to the Chef, because the food in the hotel is absolutely delicious! Thank you for exceeding our expectations and making our family reunion all the more memorable.

title: “tropical paradise without going to the the bahamas”
text:
when I first walked into the lobby, the host greeted me immediately with great hospitality, i they were knowledgeable about 15 questions i had because this was a spontaneous 2 day getaway. 
 the Marina suite room was great mellow style. plasma tv's, little bar and kitchen, frig, hairdryer for lady's, great view outside the sliders onto the patio with two lounger chairs. the marina is a rocks throw with a little two-chair canvas covered lounger. 
 Bed was great in the separate room, but the only complaint about the whole trip is that the pull out bed in the sofa was a little rough sleep. My buddy told me, I was in the separate nicer room.hehehe.
 BRING BIKES!!! its 2 seconds away from the boardwalk get in the crowds people watch because there is plenty to look at.....A prodigious amount shops,restraunts, pubs/bars and so much more. us 4 rode our bikes farther then the girls wanted too without a doubt, but we found great eats everywhere shops to browse..
 i liked the fact you can have a great time with your friends and at the same time you can have a romantic time with your girlfriend or wife at the same place. 
 next time, im going to book in advance maybe get some package deals, and spend at least 2 nights if not a week...

title: “PERFECTION”
text: My wife and I have just returned from a wonderful seven night stay at the Casablanca.We first stayed at this gem of an hotel two years ago and could not wait to return.Everything was perfect from the check-in and the bottle of wine in our room as I was celebrating my birthday during my stay to every member of staff.Location is everything and you will not find a better one,just a few steps from the centre of Times Sq.It is very easy to read the reviews of the Casablanca and think no hotel could be this good,trust me it is.I have stayed in hotels all over the world and the Casablanca beats them all.But you do not have to believe me,just give it a try yourself.A big thanks to all the staff who made our stay so enjoyable.

title: “Looking forward to a return stay”
text: Excellent location, easy to get to museums, galleries, restaurants etc. Efficient and friendly staff, clean and comfortable rooms and generally quiet. We'll certainly try to stay at the Affinia when visiting NYC in the future.

title: “Where to begin?”
text:
A hotel can make or break a vacation or business trip. How you're treated by staff at a hotel can make or break a vacation or business trip. I stay in a lot of hotels, and wish that every hotel would send their staff to the Affinia 50 for training on how to treats guests. The Affinia staff treated me like royalty.
Planning a leisurely long weekend it NYC, I arrived at the Affinia 50 at about 11am, after an early flight. I approached the desk, stated I realized I was early, but wondered if I might store my luggage until check-in. Tamara--a true guest services professional--working at the front desk that morning would hear nothing of that, "Oh, no need for that, we have a room available right now." Totally unexpected.
She then offered an upgrade to a one bedroom suite. Mind you, I booked this hotel through Priceline, so didn't expect anything other than the most common room in the hotel. I told her I couldn't believe that as a Priceline customer, I was being given such wonderful treatment, or such a great room option. She dismissed that concern, too, making it clear to me by her actions that all guests were treated respectfully, without regard to how the room was booked, or what price (apparently) was paid. I don't use Priceline often, but this has not been my usual reception as a Priceline customer.
I was then given what was perhaps the most AWESOME hotel room in which I've ever stayed. A huge living room/dining area, lovely king bedded bedroom, and best of all, a corner location with a balcony that must have been 40 feet long. In New York City! It's hard to express how much I enjoyed sitting on the balcony, on sunny early summer mornings, overlooking the skyline of mid-town, sipping coffee in the morning while reading the New York Times.....a memory I'll have forever. 
For that room assignment, Tamara will long remain my favorite guest services representative ever, but she wasn't alone in making guests feel welcome throughout my stay, Smiles for every guest, coming and going. The doormen always made guests feel that they really WERE glad to have them back at the hotel upon arrival.
I realize that every hotel stay is a singular experience; a hotel that is a treasure to one person seems ordinary to the next. But for me, what defines a great stay is being treated kindly, having a room that exceeds expectations,and being made to feel truly welcome. The Affinia 50 did all that. I really can't remember, in nearly 30 years of travel, a hotel stay I enjoyed more.
I hope the Affinia 50 staff takes satisfaction in knowing that their efforts and attitude is truly appreciated by (I hope) most guests. Well done, and thanks.

title: “My easiest hotel experience EVER!!!!!!!!”
text:
Got off the plane in DFW in terminal D. Took about 100 yard walk to the security checkpoint. Walked out to my left up the escalator to the hotel. Put my credit card in the computer for check in, I was in my very well appointed room in about 5 minutes after I got off the plane. Went downstairs, ate incredible sushi, GREAT CHEF. Super quick service, back to the comfortable bedroom, very mild airplane noise, hardly realized I was in the airport. Next morning went to the same computer downstairs to check out. Down the escalator back thru security and on the plane.
Could not have been easier, great, convenient hotel.

title: “2 Year Wedding Anniversary Celebration”
text: My wife and I stayed at the Hudson Hotel for 2 nights this past August 06. We arrived at the hotel around 4 and were immediatley disapointed with the fact that our room was not ready. We are not ones to complain, but were told the room would be ready at 3 and were tired from the trip. However, the person behind the desk made amends by giving us two free drink coupons that we used at the sky terrace bar while they were getting our room ready. This bar was magnificent with stunning views of the Hudson and a wonderful ambiance. The only suggestion that I would make is the fact that they have one waitress trying to cover the entire area and the wait for drinks is substancial as a result(especially in the evenings). Otherwise, we were very happy with the room and its location to Central Park.

title: “A great location with comfy beds, but had some issues”
text:
First off, we were very happy to get a good deal on this property via priceline(PL). It was around 120 per night. The better news is that the buzz on betterbidding was that were were targets to be upsold on their travel club which would upgrade us from the old part of the hotel to the newer part where the rooms would be bigger. Well, we just got into the new part without an upsell attempt. This was good. The location was fantastic for shopping. Check-in was pretty quick and efficient.
Our room was small! When booking thru PL the hotel only has to provide one queen or king bed. Getting 2 beds is not guaranteed, but we ALWAYS luck out and this time was no exception. But the rooms were crowded and small. The bathroom was small and needed some upkeep in certain areas. We did not use the restaurant or bar but did use the concierge several times with good, helpful results. 
If I had paid $250-$350 for the room I would be upset, but I didn't. So, unless you get a deal via PL don't waste your dollars.

title: “Perfect Spot”
text: My husband and I recently spent a week in Seattle and stayed at teh Mayflower Park Hotel. We loved the hotel and the location. The staff was very helpful, the hotel accommodating and very clean. We would definitely recommend this setting to anyone visiting the area.

title: “Great location, reasonable value”
text: We went to Boston to tour the city and stayed here. Overall, this is a nice hotel with a great location. Very close to Quincy Market, NE Aquarium, the waterfront and the Italian section of Boston. Rooms were clean and the pool and gym are excellent. Only complaints are relatively minor...we expect that for the price you would get queen beds instead of twins. Also, service by the bartenders in the restaurant and one of the bellhops did not meet my expectations for a hotel of this calibre. Otherwise, would definitely stay there again due to location and cleanliness of the hotel.

title: “Best experience EVER!!!!!!!!!!”
text: My wife and I visted NY for the 1st time to celebrate our 20th anniversary. We stayed in the corner view suite. The room was incredible!!!!! Very spacious with 1st rate amenities. Our friends stayed in a deluxe room and other than it being a little smaller it too was great for the price. The staff are pleasant, professional, and bent over backwards to make our stay wonderful! We most definitely will be staying at Westins Hotel from now on

title: “Nice and Clean Hotel”
text: We stayed at this hotel over the Thanksgiving holiday. The staff was very friendly and helpful. I especially want to give kudos to the bell staff they were always smiling and greeted us everytime we left or arrived at the hotel. Even after we checked out they held our bags until we were picked up for the airport. The rooms were small but very clean and we used the fridge and microwave in the room. The hotel is close to the subway and many restaurants. My only disappointment was that breakfast was not included with our room, it has always been included in other Hilton Garden Inn's we have stayed at. I would definately stay here again on my next visit to NYC. :-)

title: “Couldn't better the location”
text:
Only just got around to writing this review. We stayed here in June for 4 nights after chosing it based on other tripadvisor reviews. We were not disappointed. 
Yes the rooms are small but then how long do you spend in your hotel room in a city such as San Francisco? And if want a quiet hotel why are you staying in heart of a major city? Our hotel overlooked Union Square but we didn't have any problems sleeping. The location of the hotel couldn't be better - right in heart of the city.
I really don't think you can fault this hotel for its facilities and location for the price - if you want 5 star luxury stay at Westin St Francis but if want a clean, friendly hotel that doesn't break the budget then stay at the Chancellor. If we ever return to San Francisco which I sincerely hope we will as I loved the city then this will be our first choice of hotel.
On another note we also bought a three day Muni pass which was excellent value - the city is too large to travel on foot and having this pass meant we could hop on and off transport without having to fiddle about for change - we must have had at least 3 times the value in journeys.

title: “Dont' Bother!”
text: We spent 4 days here and were without hot water for 3 hours the first night. I was treated very rudely by the night assistant and promised a comped night for my troubles, which I never received. The place was filled with barking animals and if your idea of a wine receptions, which is supplied with $2 Trader Joe's wines, than this place may be for you! I would never stay there again! The restaurant is also terrible!

title: “Super chic but staff need to wise up”
text: This hotel has all the style and a great bar but the staff could do with being lessons in politeness. The rooms are, as many others point out, on the small side but I have always found them perfectly adequate. The location is most convenient for all things in San Francisco but beware of the vagrants hanging around in the surrounding streets.

title: “weekend stay”
text: Pleasently surprised by the very friendly staff. Very helpful info for how to get around on foot. Great location for the must-sees. Go right out of the hotel and it is a 5 min. Walk to art museum. Starbucks and pub on premise, Potbellys next door. An overall great experience!

title: “(Not quite) Perfect”
text:
I was very impressed with Trump Soho. As a city hotel it scores very highly on key points:
- big room
- comfortable bed
- charming staff
- attractive architecture
- location.
So why not 5*:
- not enough lifts. There is a rush hour around 6pm when you can wait for over 10 minutes for a lift. Madness made worse by the hotel "privatising" some lifts for functions.
- our maid cleared cash off the desk (albeit having left a thank-you note!). Strange to assume that any cash in the room is a gratuity. Hotel handled it fine - but very embarassing/awkward for everyone. I had no idea how much I had left so had to report it.
- paid-for wifi. I know some hotels do it but my wife and I travel with 5 wifi devices between us (laptop, iPad, phone etc). Which means $15 per device per day - you can't alternate a log-in between them. So, of course, I just connect one which is then inconvenient. If the hotel wants paid-for access, it should be useable between different devices.
Would go back - really liked it.

title: “Recent 4 day business trip”
text: I was recently at this hotel for a 4 day business review. Overall the facility was great & the gym equipment was excellent & very clean. Food was good once we specified the types of cuisine. Estela Estrada was extremely attentive & made me a personal salad 2 days as I do not eat dairy. Her service was second to none. I was expecting a lot of aircraft noise & was pleasantly surprised that the building is very well insulated from noise pollution.

title: “Great place on a budget”
text: Stay here in Oct 2010 for 5 days great area room nice, clean, quite, breakfast nice added touch and filling. Balconies looked niced but were hardly opened to go out sit and relax. Had to returned and stayed in Dec 2010 for 4 days same exact service. Can get to everywhere in LA fast. Highly recommend the place AAA+++

title: “Great location!”
text: You can not beat this location - just walking in and out of the hotel was fun. Close to Rock Center, park and shows. Nice!

title: “Solid hotel though not quite in the right area”
text: We were looking for something in a funky part of town, and lower east side is not quite that area. The hotel is great, and the staff were fab, but it was super cold outside, and there didn't seem to be much of interest that was within close walking distance.

title: “Good for pre flight night”
text:
Stayed at the hotel one night before flying out of O'Hare on vacation. Very nice hotel but hard to find since it is set inside off of the main streets.
Rooms were very nice and large with good amenities. Ate at the hotel and food and service were very good. Manager immediately waited on us and spoke with us about how large the portions were. We were going to order too much food based on the huge size of portions, so he was very friendly and assisted us. Waitress was very helpful also.
I thought this hotel was very good value and location was good for flying out of O'Hare. Free shuttle service was good, departing every 30 minutes on the hour and 1/2 hour.

title: “Great location..decent price”
text: I stayed here a couple of nights after attending a conference. The hotel was right across the street from the conference hotel and right in the middle of a bunch of shopping and restauants. It was an easy walk to the market and Westlake station. (I rode in on the light rail.) The room was comfortable and modest. It was very clean I loved the soft bed. The flat screen tv was great. Downstairs in the lobby there are 2 computers with internet access you can use or bring your laptop down for free internet access. Staff was helpful with directions. I would definetely stay there again.

title: “Clean and Modern Hotel; Perfect Location; Priced Right!”
text:
The title says it all.
The hotel from the outside looks like an apartment building, BUT - inside makes up for it.
The rooms are well appointed, clean and affordable.
The location is INCREDIBLE with the Metro rail within 100 steps. PERFECT!
I did not eat in the downstairs restaurant.
The staff were very attentive and nice.
The gym was great and not busy.
THE CON: CAREFUL - If you do not book with them directly and you get 'a deal', they will play games with you. (There way of getting back to you) They will give you the same quality room, but if you ask for a single bed, they will give you a double bed. 
We put our foot down and got our way, seeing that they were only at 70 percent capacity.
Otherwise, THIS is the place to be. Starbucks is across the street too!

title: “loved it!”
text:
It was so nice to arrive at this place, after a 12 hour over night flight. We arrived very early, about 4/5 hours before check in, which i had notified them about when I made a booking. The guy at the desk was very surprised when I was expecting to check in so early but in fairness to him he had a room for us within 20 minutes. He was really nice to chat to too while we waited.
The room was gorgeous! Huge tv, fridge, lovely ensuite. Couldnt fault it in the slightest!
Location was ok, we were only there for two nights and spent most of our time in Hollywood. We walked alot (45mins to the chinese theater), but if i was going back to LA Id look abit more into public transport as distances are deceiving when walking! Theres also number of little supermarkets around the place, which was perfect for picking up snacks and breakfast.
Id definitely stay here again!!

title: “Pass it up!”
text: This hotel is tired. Though the staff was friendly but the hotel has seen it's better days and is in need of a major overhaul. The lighting was so bad you couldn't read anything unless you were directly under one of the 3 lamps, which was the only lighting. Should be enough you think? it was yellow and dim. There were only 2 electrical outlets in the room, not enough to charge electronics and plug in cpap machines. The sleep number beds were the cheapest ones made, they weren't comfortable (I should know as I have a much better one at home). The only plus side was the 24 hour diner across the street where you could get breakfast for half the price of the hotel restaurant.

title: “Excellent & Comfortable Hotel”
text: Spent 11 nights at on the ave. Staff were pleasant and very helpful. I checked in late and changed rooms and the staff could not have been more helpful. The room was a large room (even though it was "L" shaped) with everything promised and illustrated on the net. Transport links are very good with the Metro (Tube) 2 blocks away. Also Almo, National and Avis car rentals are very close (e.g across the street).There's room service available or there the Manhattan or Nicks Dinner (24hrs) opposite the hotel. There is also a Stand Up comedy club 1 block away (on 78th I think)

title: “This hotel is COOL!”
text: We stayed early July in the middle of the summer heatwave. We were pleasantly stunned by this place. The lobby and bar reminded me of an old library with lots of people milling around and surfing the web on their laptops. The vibe was definately hip and young but there was a mix of ages staying. Our room was the most basic they do. It was small but perfectly formed. The view of the Empire State Building was outstanding, especially at night. I loved the bathroom because to me (a scottish lass) it was typical NYC. The toiletries and robes were also lovely too. The bed was comfortable and the range of snacks and drinks available in the room were the most i saw on a months holiday. I managed to get a special deal on a website which made this hotel nearly on par cost wise with lesser hotels. It was worth the difference. The location was good - easy walking to Empire State, Flat Iron Building, Macy's, Time's Sqaure & Theatre's - even greenwich village if you like to stroll. There was however subway stations 1 block away for further a field trips. We definately would stay here again if rates were suitable.

title: “vewry good hotel !”
text:
i stayed 4 nights in this hotel . it was really nice. the bedroom is small.
you can share a bed only if you are two skinny girls. and that was our case.
if you are two big people book 2 beds or 1 king size.
the room was small, but really cute, i only have 2 carry on. so i was ok.
the room has no views at all. 
the staff speak Spanish, they charge u for using the computers. 
u can use the phone of the common area but u cant use the phone from your room.
the area is great to get far away for the craziness of new york for a little while. is close to everything. but is a lovely quite neighborhood witch i loved.
the subway is close and the central park is right away.

title: “Wonderful Beds!!”
text: While this was a very nice, clean, beautiful hotel. Upon checking in we received coupons for cookies that we're suppose to be available upon check-in. They were out of cookies. We had reserved our room well in advance, so it is not like we were an unexpected guest. Hotel was very quiet, 99% of staff was very friendly and helpful. However, when returning to the hotel one night after midnight we found the doors to be locked. Nobody had mentioned anything to us about how to get in. To make a long story short, the woman who was at the front desk on third shift on this night, was so EXTREMELY RUDE AND DISRESPECTFUL, that I will never, ever give my money to another Hilton hotel. Sad that one person can completely ruin an otherwise wonderful stay, I also think it is a shame that they would have someone with such nonexistent customer service skills to be working with the public.

title: “Great location & great service”
text: Very professional staff. Our room was comfortable with two double beds. It is just one short block from a Metro station. A great location to explore Boston from, just around the corner from the Theatre district. Would not hesitate in staying there again!

title: “BAD EXPERIENCE... I will explain..”
text:
Newer property as of August 2011. 
Caution. 
Really Soft water and slippery bathtubs. Ask for a non slip mat. I am not elderly by any stretch of the imagination. I fell 2 consecutive days in the shower. The second day I ended up on the floor. Non slip mats are not provided in the room. You have to ask for it at the front desk.
Pros: 
Close to Sea World. Pet friendly if that is your thing. Manager's Reception a few nights during the week. Complimentary breakfast. Okay Gym with free weights and treadmill. I ran outside though so I didn't use it. 
Cons: 
BIG CONS: The "do not disturb" sign on the door means absolutely nothing to everybody. I have been working nights for my business and therefore, sleeping during the day. My do not disturb sign was on the door for my entire 4 day stay. EVERYDAY I was awaken by someone pounding on my door. The last 2 nights i was wearing earplugs. I was still awaken by the pounding on the door to clean my room. Overall, I was really disappointed at the whole situation. This is such a simple thing.... you would think.

title: “Hotel room with a view”
text:
Had the opportunity to stay on the top floor Club room with very nice view over the sea. Upon check-in I was promised to have a free internet during my 7-day stay but when checking out the story was a bit different. Finally hotel decided to give the internet for free as promised. Otherwise there were no problems with anything. Service was good and attentive. Room was kept clean spotlessly and staff was serving with a smile. Since staying that long time I also got a cheese platter and wine on the 4th night from the hotel management and that was nice.
Had my breakfasts usually at the club lounge which offers smaller variety of foods than the restaurant but of the same quality. Club lounge also had free wifi, beverages during the stay and staff was there to help you with dinner reservations or any other matter you might had.

title: “DANGER Bed Bugs! Nasty, Disgusting, Obnoxious and a rip off!”
text: Worst hotel I have ever entered in many years of travel ! BED BUGS - need I say more. Management didn't really give a damn either and no refunds once you check in. Really thought I had entered the twilight zone and still fighting over credit card billing. Enter at risk of infestation and disease. This place should be condemned by Charlotte Health Department to whom I have written. Avoid like the plague!

title: “Staff very accomodating”
text:
There were several instances while staying at this hotel that we either needed something in addition to what they offer or we needed personal assistance. One each instance, the hotel staff went above and beyond to be accomodating. The rooms do not have microwaves or refrigerators. I asked if they could bring us a refrigerator and they did so free of charge. They said they do not run the shuttle to Magnificent Mile any longer and I expressed my concern with this b/c cab fare one way is around $7.00 w/o a tip. They allowed me to turn in my receipts for a cash refund from the cab company. This was because I planned my trip depending on the shuttle running to and from the Magnificent Mile several times a day.
The concegire was very helpful--giving us maps and other wonderful suggestions. Take advantage! 
The weekends at the hotel were very very crowded in the lobby area which makes dining in the restaurants downstairs less than peaceful. Staying during the week was nice.
The hotel is very close to the art museum which was nice!
I would recommend to any traveler to bring water to your hotel room b/c the bottles on site are $6 in the room and $4 in the hotel lobby. You need to plan for cash for a cab to the Magnificent Mile or bring sneakers to make the 1.5 mile walk, each way. The cab rides add up very quickly b/c you are paying to sit in traffic on the way there and back.
There are many Walgreens and other grocers to bring stuff back to your room which you may want to do b/c of the pricey hotel items.

title: “Double tree - San Diego Hazard Center”
text: I loved this hotel. It was at the Hazard Center. Beautiful rooms, beds, pool -- fire pits that are lit everynight near the pool, cocktail area. We did not have a car, and used the public transportation Trolley, and bus all weekend, and easily got from this hotel to Old Town for great Mexican atmosphere, , the Harbor for the Harbor tour and to visit the USS Midway floating museum, Gaslamp area, San Ysidro/Tijuana border ( I wanted to see the border-town), and a bus that traversed the whole Island of Cornado, and let us off by the beautiful del Coronado hotel. Total transportation costs for 2 days: $18.00 for 2 people!! We chose to take a cab to the airport, but a bus would have gotten us there too. From this hotels 2nd floor, you are just steps from Kinkos, Trophy sports restaurant, Joe's Crab shack, and Applebees., Starbucks, etc. and We got a wonderful buy on Hotwire to boot! My husband really enjoyed seeing all the Navy vessels in the harbor, the training center for the Navy Seals, etc. This is one great town. Got to see Petco park, and three more stopsy past our hotel would have gotten us to Qualcomm Stadium.

title: “Fantastic Cookies & Coffee - Great Stay.”
text:
My wife and I stayed at the doubletree for three nights in early August, part of a trip that took us from Washington DC to New York via Philadelphia. 
This is a really nice, clean, recently refurbished hotel in a good, quiet location. Only a 10 to 15 minute walk from the White House and the same to the nearest underground railway station.
Staff were really friendly, polite and helpful. The homemade cookies on arrival are a nice touch and so delicious you will be tempted to order more from the room service menu. 
The rooms are modern and tastefully re furbished with an extremely comfortable bed, flat screen TV and the Wolfgang Puck coffee machine and condiments which make for a sexy combination with the home made cookies.
The only thing I can criticise is the size of the bathroom. Although very nice it is small, however I personally would prefer a larger room and smaller bathroom.
We didn’t get chance to eat in the hotel restaurant however the food we ordered on room service was excellent.
The value for money was outstanding; we stayed Friday to Monday and got the Sunday night free, booked on Expedia.
If it’s a business trip or a city break, I would highly recommend this hotel.

title: “More comfortable than the Four Seasons”
text: I first came to this hotel about eight? years ago, right as it was opening, and we were floored! Push button blackout shades, unique photographs/art in each room, beautiful bathrooms. Then the FS Seattle opened and I'd been going there ever since. On our last trip, we needed a large room and the Hyatt and an "Emerald Suite" that was perfect for us and the kids. The fitness center and spa were great! It's a much larger hotel than the FS, so you won't have the same "everybody knows you here" vibe. But what you do get is a Ruth's Chris right on the property! It's the room service restaurant and they do a great breakfast. Free internet is always a huge thumbs up. Oh the softest sheets! Overall, wood has a maple,rosewood feel which is darker than FS's blond and earthtones mix. I'd go to FSS again if the staff hadn't all moved on to other things. It's almost like starting over in a new town, so might as wel go to the Hyatt. At least I get points!

title: “Good value, excellent service”
text:
