Clean, consistent and well priced, this small Hilton is a good option - I didn't hear any street noise despite being so close to Canal street. Good sized rooms with microwave, fridge and coffee - amazing.
Subway to go uptown is right in front of the hotel - the staff are just superb - they were informative, helpful and good humored. One night there was a false alarm that woke us at 3am - when I went down to buy some water and sodas from their small pantry/store, the woman at the front desk said it was on the house which was so kind. Good location with proximity to soho/tribeca area and lower manhattan. Would happily stay there again - the only drawback is getting cabs there but the subway is a better option overall. Carpetting in the hallways is somewhat worn and the restaurant downstairs (a pizza/burger bar) has uneven service but that's not reason to stay away. There is an amazing italian restaurant just across the street....

title: “delightful small boutique hotel perfectly located for foodies or anyone looking for a romantic intimate setting”
text: Upon arrival in the a.m. well prior to check in times, we were greeted by the valet who was pleasant and efficient. We left our car and bags with him , so that we could spend our day walking downtown and enjoying a fabulous lunch at Maximillans overlooking the Sound in Pike's place market. As parking in this area is a challenge, the valet convenience is something to take advantage. We enjoyed dinner at the hotel's more casual french cafe, Cafe Campagne, as the more formal Campagne is closed Mondays. We were very pleased with the service and our meal, both were in a relaxed french cafe tradition. After dinner we enjoyed a view of the city lights from the 5th floor balcony of the hotel...which is open only to guests. If it was a warmer night it would have been a perfect place for a glass of wine after dinner.

title: “Labour Day Weekend in the Park”
text:
Stayed at the Gramercy Park Hotel, over the Labour Day weekend. What a great hotel: convenient location, attentive service, well designed spaces.
I had a room that faced Lexington Avenue and was at first apprehensive -- noise. However, had a great night's sleep. There's a rooftop bar that gets busy, however, the staff was diligent in escorting you to a separate elevator.
The room was a bit too dark for my taste and there was a dearth of outlets. 
Ordered room service, my last day there and the meal arrived promptly -- definitely try the yoghurt and vin cot to with fruit. AMAZING.

title: “' Life Of Grime!!!!!!!!!!!!'”
text:
It may have been 3 years and 3 months since we stayed in 'THE WORST HOTEL IN THE WORLD!!!!'but the experience has been embeded in our brain,we still wake in the middle of the night 
sweating!!!!!A stay in the CARTER HOTEL is not an experience you are likely or ABLE to forget!Our room was like a science experiment.We believe the 9th floor is the point of origin for every bacteria known to man.The staff were ignorant and unhelpful,the bed sheets were dirty,the a/c unit at the foot of the bed measured 9 on the richter scale, there was mould on the bedroom walls,grime on the bathroom floor,sharp broken tiles,leaking pipes,taps that didnt shut off and the original 'prototype' tv that did not have a single channel you could watch.when we requested a hairdryer and iron we had to fill in an order form and were told there was a FIVE DAY WAITING LIST! 
Not only that but in two weeks(yes 2 weeks! everywhere else was fully booked because it was thanksgiving!) did anyone make our bed,change the linen,provide clean towels or toilet paperwe were told that the chamber maids were ALL ON STRIKE!!appartfrom the unsavoury staff on reception who we confronted hourly with a multitude of complaints, the only other employee we were unfortunate enough to meet was a porter when he knocked on our door to provide us with three packets of rat poison, instructing us to place them on the floor along the window walls as the guests in the rooms on the floor above made reports of vermin! if after reading about our absolutely honest account of the Carter Hotel you still desire to book a room, may we recommened you get yourself inocculated first! we would rather let the rats have the room and us sleep in the sewers than set foot in the Carter Hotel again, truthfully!! absolutely awfull, wouldnt recommened it to our worst enemy!

title: “The Perfect SF Getaway”
text:
Having lived in SF for 10 years, I tend to be pretty hard on the hotels there. On the whole, they are overpriced (tho often glamourous) and you always have to pay some exorbitant fee for parking when you arrive from out of town. The Orchard changes all my thinking.
Just off Union Square, this boutique property has all of the amenities (and then some) of the larger properties just up the hill (i.e. Fairmont, Mark Hopkins) without the price tag and snooty staff. The lobby is tiny but nice and upon check-in, the staff was phenomenally kind. While the room was a tad small, it's not much smaller than a standard SF room elsewhere and as there were only 2 of us, it's not like we needed a suite!
The bed and pillows were wonderful and the beds had DUVETS (which I'm an enormous fan of -- DOWN with those gross bacteria-filled coverlets!). There were spa robes in the closet for each of us (tho, one of them was starting to come apart a little at the belt loop) and the bathroom was extremely spacious and well-appointed with Aveda products and fluffy towels.
The hotel provides DVDs for in-room use and has a pretty expansive library of new releases and classics. The staff is so helpful that when my boyfriend and I rolled in at around 1 a.m. in NEED of some late-night food, we were directed immediately to a diner up the street which satisfied our cravings. The location is fantastic and you can walk to everything (Chinatown, shopping, restaurants, bars). North Beach was a minimal $5 cab ride away.
Despite having a view of another building (the standard view in a big city), the hotel was VERY VERY quiet. Our parking was taken care of by parking in the Sutter-Stockton garage merely 1 block away on Bush. The hotel only has valet and charges $34 overnite, but if you arrive on a Saturday after 6 and leave on Sunday any time after 7 a.m., the fee is only $15.
I am thrilled to have discovered this fantastic little hotel (thank you, TripAdvisor!) and I know we will return.

title: “GREAT LITTLE HOTEL”
text:
ok, 31st St, maybe 10 mins walk from biggest of attractions but very good location. The Hoetl Room we book into for 5 nights on a 3 week tour was too small and initially not hapy but were moved without fuss and room size perfect (for New York that is). 
Lovely decor with very friendly reception and bar staff. Met nice fellow guests too so and found hotel chic but not pretentious, intelligent but not obnoxious if that makes sense. In fact it was a lot of fun
Congrats to staff and rates are reasonable too. Any complaints delath with professionally, well and without fuss. Another 3-4 blocks closer to GSS of Times Square and it'd be a 5 rating but looking forward to re-visiting. (Great Cocktails too guys, hi from Ireland xx)

title: “Wonderful experience at Hotel Monaco”
text: My wife and I had an opportunity to visit Seattle for a few days on a corporate leisure trip. During our trip everyone at Hotel Monaco made every effort to make us feel warm, welcome, and satisfied. The hotel is centrally located in the CBD and we found everything within a few minutes walk. I'm not sure how they pulled it off, but they also arranged for perfect weather during our visit - many thanks. We look forward to seeing you again.

title: “Amazingly friendly staff”
text: We had a great stay here, it was refreshing to see how friendly all of the folks at the hotel were too. It was fairly priced and the breakfast was great too. The only cons I would mention about the hotel are minor: the water pressure was pretty weak (though we stayed on a high floor) and we could hear the bell from the elevator every time it stopped at our floor--but aside from those minor points, our room was great and very clean, and the location is superb.

title: “Highly recommend - the amenities are fantastic!”
text:
My husband & I stayed here for 5 nights, while in town for the Nike Marathon. At first glance, being used to the typical corporate chain hotels, we were both disappointed when we arrived to our room. However, the charm of this place becomes apparent rather quickly.
We too, had a corner room, just like a previous reviewer - room #51. It is immediately next to the elevator, and facing the street. The room is plenty big for 2 people with a fireplace, sofa, an upholstered chair and a desk with chair. I see no reason to avoid a room by the elevator - on the contrary, I found it quite convenient. The street noise is present, but either sleep with your windows shut or turn on the provided "noise machine" and you'll be fine. 
The amenities are such that I've never experienced at any other hotel before. They keep a refrigerator fully stocked with bottled water & sodas, for you to take whenever you'd like. There is always a bowl of apples available, coffee & tea. Starting in the afternoons, and going straight through to after dinner, there is a cookie jar kept stocked with fresh baked cookies. A different type of cookie appeared every day, and often times we were at the jar while the cookies were still warm! When dropping off your parcels or running in to change clothes, having a bottle of water and a small snack is a welcome find.
The breakfast is adequate. It's enough to get you started on your day. I agree that the set up is a bit of a disaster, having the coffee/tea immediately outside of the elevator doors. I enjoyed my daily cup of coffee and croissant with jam!
We did not take full advantage of the wine/cheese reception. We did stop in, grab a few glasses of wine to take up to our room while getting ready for dinner, but the people who were down there were social and it was a friendly atmosphere.
Overall, I recommend this hotel, and if staying in the Union Square area again, I would love to stay here again.

title: “The thinnest walls of any motel anywhere!”
text: I stayed here with my two children, ages 8 and 16. The walls were so thin, we could hear every word of every conversation from the people next to us -- and different people stayed in the room over three days. From the other side, we got to hear their TV at 11.30 at night, and every detail of their amorous activity at 1:30 a.m. THAT raised some questions from my 8 year old! The people upstairs sounded like their were bowling for dollars, although I think they were just walking. Possibly this was the worst motel we have ever stayed at. STAY AWAY!

title: “Overprice!!! Need some type of free parking”
text: It was good hotel. Very clean but pricey.. Make sure you bring alot of money

title: “Another great stay!”
text: This was my second stay at Affinia Shelburne, and as before the experience was wonderful! The staff was warm and welcoming, all of the requests I had made were honored (unexpected, considering I was staying the New Year's holiday weekend, a VERY busy time!), my room with a view of the Empire State Building was small but comfortable, the bed extremely so, and the bathroom larger than expected. The room conditions was A+ in terms of cleanliness, and despite the temperatures which were warmer than usual for December outside I slept very well. I love the location of this hotel - within easy walking distance of some of my favorite places in the city (the Morgan Library, Grand Central Terminal, Empire State and Chrysler buildings). Lastly, treated myself to room service with a delicious burger and fries. Also as before, the burger arrived piping hot, fries the same, and even with the usual upcharges the meal was worth every penny. You really can't do better than the Affinia Shelburne, not at the price offered and amenities.

title: “Good caring staff”
text: They took attention to all our needs and were careful about all our requirements.

title: “Sophisticated Hotel with 5 Star Service”
text:
This elegant hotel is literally just a stone's throw away from the White House and right across the street from Lafayette Park, which is a great location to view the White House, people watch or just sit on a park bench and read your favorite book.
Walking into the Hay Adams you are immediately struck by its intimate surroundings. The reservation and conceirge alcoves are immediately to your right and left and the elevator is just a few steps away. The rich surroundings in the small foyer gives you the distinct impression that you are walking into an luxurious private club.
We got to the hotel a few hours early; no problem. Our bags were stored and brought up to our room while we were out sightseeing. Dealing with the reservation desk was a delight (when was the last time you saw that term used to describe the front desk) whether it was getting change for a twenty, receiving a hard copy of our bill or snagging a tasty treat from the always filled cookie jar.
From our room we could directly looked across at St. John's Church, known as the "Church of Presidents". The room was average in size but was well appointed with beautiful prints of Washington monuments, a king size bed draped with fine European linens and a Bose stereo system. The bathroom was also modest in size but had beautifull brass fixtures and also had what a bathroom truly needs most: plenty of hot water.
This hotel is known for its service and it delivers it in every way. Houskeeping is truly spectacular. My wife and I have stayed at several five star hotels and she always at least finds one "dust bunny". Not here! The place was always immaculate and there was always plenty of fresh towels and top of the line lotions. Turn down service - with a little tray with chocolates and a card detailing the next several days forecast - was something to look forward to each night.
The concierge desk helped us planned our trips and gave us some great advice about where to eat. However, their best assistance was when I accidently left my credit card on the table of a restaurant the previous night and after several failed attempts by me to get a hold of someone, I told my plight to the concierge and he got on the phone to the establishment and within ten minutes I had my card. These guys are good!
We had breakfast each day in the hotel's restaurant, which overlooks Lafayette Park and depending where you sit, views of the White House. Service was first class and the food was terrific (try the oatmeal souffle with warm fruit sauce for something totally and deliciously different) Downstairs tucked away in the basement of the hotel is there bar "Off the Record" where you can grab a drink or a sandwich. The place is perfect for a nightcap.
This hotel is a great place if you want 5 star service in a beautifully sophisticated setting. The Hay Adams is not cheap to stay at, but here you get what you pay for, and that is a great stay.

title: “Better than a hotel for long term stays...”
text:
Overall, Oakwood Mission Valley is a nice place to stay. It is not extravagant or luxurious like you may be led to believe by reading the description given on their website, but it is comfortable and it did cost much less than a hotel with comparable amenities. Oakwood Mission Valley offers long-term stay prices as well as nightly rates for furnished or unfurnished apartments. The property looks very nice from the outside, as well as in the foyer. Upon entering the property, we were greeted by a friendly staff and offered a free refreshment. There is also complimentary self-serve coffee offered from the morning until evening hours. After working out a few problems that occurred with the pricing of our apartment, we were made three new keys to open the front door of our apartment, keys to gain access to the indoor corridors of the property, a mailbox key, and an electronic card to allow us to enter the underground parking garage. The entire property, including the garage is monitored 24-hours by security. Parking is free and not limited. However, the garage is extremely compact. 
We then set off to find out what we would be living in for the next month. By the way, all of the apartments are being switched over to electronic card keys. We learned this on the day before we checked out, when we were told that workers would be coming to our apartment to do work on our front door. We stayed in apartment 108 on the first floor of the property. It was in a nice location because there was actually parking just outside our apartment that we were able to take advantage of. Therefore, we really did not have to bother too much with the underground parking garage or the elevators. Additionally, it made bringing things in to our apartment, like groceries, very easy. The actual apartment was somewhat dated looking, and smelled very strongly of smoke. I don't believe that Oakwood offers non-smoking rooms, which is a shame, as we are not smokers, and don't enjoy smelling like we are. The apartments carpeting looked to be freshly cleaned and the walls looked to be newly painted.
We stayed in a 2 bedroom, 2 full bathroom (one bedroom was a master bedroom and included one of the bathrooms) fully furnished apartment. The apartment also included a full kitchen, living room with two sofas (not sofa beds), a very small dining table with two chairs, and a patio (a balcony if your apartment is on the second, third, or fourth floor. 
The kitchen was small, but it had pretty much everything we needed. It had a large fridge w/ freezer and two ice trays (no ice machine in the apartment or anywhere on the property), a very noisy dishwasher, 4-burner electric stove (one of the burners did not work and neither did the overhead light until we complained about it), a good sized oven, an older microwave that at times did not work, a cheap toaster, blender, eating and cooking utensils, glasses, mugs, cookware and bakeware, plastic storage containers, many cupboards for storing things, and a good sized pantry. I was actually quite impressed with the kitchen. I was expecting more of a kitchenette. The dining area was just a very small narrow table, seating two. So one of us always had to eat on the coffee table while sitting on one of the sofas. 
In the living room, the sofas looked nice and were comfortable, but were not of the best quality. The cushions on both of the sofas sunk in often leaving you sitting lopsided. There was one TV in the apartment located in the living room across from one of the sofas. The TV had Cox cable installed on it. There was also a VCR. To get a DVD player or an extra TV for one of the bedrooms you had to pay extra. There was also a cordless phone in the living room with free voicemail. The patio was located just off the living room. It was small, but nice. It had two patio chairs and a small table. 
The rooms were quite large and both had nice large windows in them, two nightstands, a dresser, an alarm clock, and an additional cordless telephone in the master bedroom. The beds were very comfortable. Each of our two rooms had king-size beds. We had a choice of two twins, or a king-size bed in each room. The furniture was stained in a cherry color and looked very rich. One room had control over the temperature of the two rooms for heat or air conditioning. There was also another heater/air conditioner in the living room behind one of the sofas. Unfortunately our apartment did not have a full-length mirror or mirrored closet doors, which was disappointing, but we made do. The closets were equipped with about a dozen hangers and a laundry basket. 
The bathrooms were just that, bathrooms, nothing too special about them. No hair dryer included, and nothing really fancy about them. Often times it was hard to get water to come out hot enough to take a bath (also hard to get hot water to hand wash dishes in the kitchen, they seemed to be having some water heating and plumbing problems while we were there as they were often leaving notes under our door letting us know that they would be working on them, sometimes leaving us without water between certain hours), but the attached shower heads worked fine. We learned the first day staying there that you can not run a blow dryer while running the heat lamp in the bathroom. The power went out in half of our apartment and we had to call for the repair man to help us out. It seemed like there was only one repair man for the whole property, as the same guy came out each time something went wrong in our apartment, and we usually had to wait quite a while for him to arrive. The bathrooms were of good size and the bath towels were nice, warm, and thick, not like at many hotels. We did have to buy our own toilet paper and kleenex, unlike at a hotel. They provided us with only one roll of toilet paper and one small box of kleenex when we first got there. 
The furnishings and decorations around the apartment were very pretty, and made the setting of the apartment much more comfortable. The property also had an outdoor pool and spa and many decorative fountains and flowers in the landscaping, an expensive hair salon, a conference room with a large screen TV, a fitness center, a couple of vending machines, and a newspaper machine all on the first floor. Additionally, a mailbox is assigned to each apartment and they are all located together on the first floor. There are pay laundry facilities which were a bit pricey on the second floor, and free high speed wireless internet in fully furnished apartments (a fee for all other apartments).
To sum up our whole experience at the Oakwood Mission Valley apartments, we got what we paid for. We enjoyed our stay there and would stay there again. We were most pleased with all the amenities that we received for the price. We paid just under $100 per night, for a 31-day stay. For short term stays (those less than a week), I wouldn't recommend staying here. However, for a stay for more than a few weeks and on a budget, I would definitely recommend one of their fully furnished apartments.

title: “Very friendly, but had a problem with the shower that was not resolved”
text:
The hotel staff were very friendly, but the issue we had with the shower was never resolved. The water poured out of the shower onto the the bathroom floor and soaked the floor and it even reached into the bedroom. We contacted the front desk and they said they'd send and engineer to fix the problem. They said that three days in a row and the problem was never resolved. It made the stay very uncomfortable. They attempted to address the issue by giving us free passes to the Sunday brunch. They apologized at check out but that was not satisfactory. 
On Friday and Saturday nights there is a party at the Church bar downstairs. The music was so loud that you could hear it in your room all evening. We were on the 5th floor.
We will not stay at the hotel again.

title: “The Bed Bugs Bite!”
text: First, it is not an "inn" as titled, it is a hotel. Second, the staff is not friendly nor helpful. And third, they have bed bugs! We noticed in the morning when one crawled across my mother's pillow. She then checked at the foot of her bed and found one dead and one alive (the live one burst full of blood when she killed it because apparently it had been biting her throughout the night). The small specks of blood in her bed and in mine and my daughter's as well confirmed that we had all been bitten as we slept. More importantly, it was denied by staff until shown photos (which I've included here), and no apology or compensation was offered. If you have seen any television programs on bed bugs you know that they cannot be eliminated so beware.

title: “Elegant hotel with great service”
text: My wife and I stayed at this hotel for business for three nights. The room was large and very comfortable, the furnishings in perfect condition, and totally quiet. The hotel staff could not have been better - always helpful. Highly recommended.

title: “Very nice Hotel”
text: We loved this hotel. Sheraton has great beds, so comfortable. The staff were very informative and helpful. The hotel was very clean.The only negative was the pool was extremely cold, we couldn't swim in it.

title: “Nice place, a bit overpriced”
text: This motel is as advertised. Great location, colorful decor, covered parking, pleasant rooms, cookies in the afternoon all good. We had no problem with the overflow parking -- actually preferred it to the tight spots in the courtyard. My only problem was the price -- Sunday night $160, Monday and Tuesday $120. It seemed about $20-$30 over priced for what you get... the breakfast is modest, courtyard can be noisy, no bathtubs in the rooms. We would consider going back because of the great location, easy walk to Union Street and Chestnut Street shopping.

title: “A pathetic hotel”
text: International traveler who's stayed here many times. Along with the single beds, small rooms, rude staff and no breakfast here's some stories for ya. I've been woken up by a jackhammer doing construction on my outside wall at 7am and no one cared. I've had a not working AC unit and 2 times the fire alarm has gone off after midnight or at dawn for 20 minutes and again. No one cared. The owner of this hotel should be ashamed to even call it a 3 star hotel. The only reason anyone is here is because of priceline.

title: “Great location, friendly staff”
text: Although the price of parking in DC is expensive, this hotel offers a lot. The breakfast and the evening cocktail reception were great. The hotel staff were all friendly and our room was clean. We were visiting our son and George Washington University so it was easy for him to walk over to us to visit or for us to go to his campus. One negative was the pillows, if you can you should bring your own from home.

title: “Great Customer Service..They must read our reviews”
text:
We stayed here September 26, 2011 My husband had to go to see the doctor in San Jose and we stayed one night. We were welcomed when we walked in and the service at the front desk was excellent. The location is very good for downtown and close to the freeways. The room was very clean and the bed very comfortable. We were on the 16th floor and asked for a wake up call so we could make a early morning appointment. Everything was right on time and friendly. Valet was expensive $26.00 a night. Close to SFO airport about 30 minute drive maybe longer depends on traffic. I am crazy for a clean room, comfortable bed and service. All was better than average, they do need to had extra mirror in bathroom for putting on makeup. 
We would stay there again and we are glad that they read our reviews:)

title: “Quick trip to France”
text: We love this hotel. We have stayed here several times. It is very much like actually being in Paris.The service is good, rooms are clean and the best part is the Jeanne d'Arc restaurant that is in the basement of the hotel. It is very cozy and the food is wonderful. We find our mouths watering when we just think about the Gran Marnier Souffle!

title: “Conviently & well priced”
text: Stayed at the Hotel Max for 2 days while in Seattle. My husband and I were looking for a place reasonably priced and close to attractions downtown. Hotel Max was a great find. Rooms & beds very comfortable. They even have a pillow menu if you are choosy about your pillows. Shower small but manageable. The hotel is only a few blocks from the space needle and Pike's Market with many fine restaurants nearby. We took the light rail to and from the airport and at $2.50 one-way, is a bargain. Ride the rail to the end of the line and the hotel is only 2 blocks away from the station. This is much better and cheaper way to the airport from downtown. We will stay at the Hotel Max again when we return to Seattle.

title: “Very nice, could be great”
text:
This hotel is very nice. From the moment you walk in, it is very appealing. Very bright, fun, looks modern. 
Very nice bar in the lobby has great charm and trendy vibe to it. The prices are expensive, $5 per beer.... But it is a very nice setting. Outside there is a nice looking pond, nice pool area(no indoor pool). There is a large convention center at this hotel as well. Bellman services too. 
The rooms were pretty nice. Modern bathroom, nicely decorated, nice toiletries provided too... Comfy bed, nice views, nice desk area for working.... Channel selection is good as well. 
Restaurant served a buffet breakfast that was good. Lots to choose from and taste was good, not great. Little pricey, but good. 
This hotel would be 5 star with a little updating. It is a huge high rise, but the elevators are scary. They have 25 year old carpet in them and creak and pop as you are in them. The floor doesn't feel solid either. I would hate to be on the 25th floor in these... The other upgrade is the room carpet. It truly seems like they upgraded everything in the room except the carpet. It seems clean and the rest of the room is modern, but carpet is worn and seems out of place. 
Nice hotel, and with a few upgrades could be very nice. I never had any service problems. Great location, easy to get places in the city. Lots of places around to shop and eat...

title: “One sister two dogs”
text: This is our third time at this hotel and we like it very much. Mr McCoy and his staff has always treated us very nice. I know that the hotel doesn't met a lot of peoples standards but it does ours. It is down the street from my sons home and they except out pets. It has a kitchenette so that we can fix our own meals and not have to always be at my sons home. The property is not to big. It is hard to find and some will think that it looks run down but the property is well maintained. The rooms are clean and if you need anything all you need to do is ask. We have always felt safe here night and day. They have a laundry room on site. A pool and basketball hoop. Everyone is very friendly who I have met staying there and the area is quiet which I like. Mr. McCoy and staff run a clean and well maintained property. We will be staying here next year. We generally stay about 3 weeks.

title: “Nice Stay on "Quiet Section" of San Antonio Riverwalk”
text: This was a pleasant experience at the Embassy Suites San Antonio Riverwalk. The rooms were clean and everything was as you would expect from this chain. There is a rooftop pool and hot tub with a nice view of the San Antonio skyline. One item of note, the building is not of the "typical" Embassy Suites design with the rooms overlooking a large open atrium. The building has been converted to an Embassy Suites fairly recently. The hotel itself is located directly on a "quiet section" of the Riverwalk and a short, scenic walk takes you to the restaurants and bars. Market Square, The Alamo, Hemisphere Park and The Tower of the Americas are all within walking distance. Otherwise, there is a shuttlebus stop right outside the front door of the hotel with an all-day bus pass at $4.

title: “Just okay”
text:
Pros: Good location near restaurants and stores, fridge & microwave in room, free water bottles, free wireless in rooms, free parking, nice shower/water pressure, recently renovated
Cons: The room seemed pretty awkward - all of the furniture seemed too big for the living room in the suite. Although recently renovated, still seems old. 
We stayed in a suite using our Starwood points and chose this hotel over the Sheraton Suites because of location and since it was recently renovated. However, I think next time I'd try the Sheraton. Even though this was remodeled, it still seems tired/old. Also, the other entrances to the hotel (away from the lobby) didn't seem secure - the doors were always propped open or unlocked.
We did like the fact that there was a small fridge and microwave. The fridge was actually cold and the freezer actually froze! Sometimes, that doesn't happen in hotel fridges.
The crib that was provided for our toddler was a mini-crib - much smaller than a regular sized crib. If she was over 2 years old, it would've been to small.
We didn't encounter many other guests so we didn't have problems with noise, although I could hear the elevator going up and down although we were down the hall from it.
There's a very tired, old golf course which I can't believe they actually advertise as an "executive golf course."
Can't say anything about service since our room was located near one of the other entrances so we only saw the staff during check-in and check-out. I only saw housekeeping in the hallways once or twice during our stay.

title: “Tired and expensive”
text: Apart from the location and the good to great food and service in Shula's I am not sure this hotel has much to recommend it. I usually love staying in a Westin hotel - the ones in Sydney and in Melbourne are a stand-outs. The Westin Times Square in NY is tired and expensive - or better said - I'd rather pay more if I had to and stay elsewhere. The rooms are depressing, with a sort of "grey" feeling with green walls for heaven's sake - the bathrooms are like those you might expect in a government institution and the shower anemic. As is usual in a Westin the beds are comfortable. Staff were ok - some abrupt and some not - guess that's NY. Not really a good business-class hotel and expensive for tourists. Not sure why it was full when I stayed.

title: “The way all hotels should be!”
text:
Just back from 17 days of staying at the Setai. Long Stay, got the avenue appartement suites, i HAVE to give top marks here. First off, the staff. I have travelled all over the world..never have I seen this. These people really do make all the difference. Courteous, super nice and very very good at their job. Never ever did they displease!! The rooms. Huge, brand new, great view, quiet, nice, the works. Fully equipped, like proper appartments. Decently priced as well in comparison to some of the other ones in NYC. Moving on, the food. Amazing consistently. Both the room service as well as the Ai Fiori restaurant. Limousine car service also very nice. The Spa is exquisite as well as the gym. The people there are great. Don't want to go on and on so I will end it here. After two and a half weeks living there I can only recommend it highly.
A home away from home. Better even. Thanks people. Room numbers 2501 & 2506.

title: “quite unusual - especially the glass enclosed shower”
text: I loved looking out at all the lights through the long glass windows in my corner room. the rooftop bar with the open pit fireplace was da bomb. I also liked the location and the hot trendy bar on the first floor. I would definitely go back and stay there and also because it is one block from MBurger which serves the best most juiciest burgers, fries and floats.

title: “water pools in the shower - a lot”
text:
The hotel was fine except that the shower in our room didn´t drain. At all. I called down, They didn´t offer a room change and didn´t seem very concerned. He also did not apologize. I got the impression they had heard the complaint a lot and were unable to fix the problem. 
Tub was a bit dirty from previous occupants (rings, etc.) due to the drain problem.
Sort of gross for a medium priced hotel.

title: “Good Location”
text: We spent with my family for Labour day holidays. Excellent location, but breakfast is very expensive for larger group. There are plenty of restaurants out side of the hotel. I got charged twice and annoyance for me call finance department to sort it out. However, good location saved me lots of time to see the core Downtown and surrounding.

title: “Okay Experience”
text:
I stayed at this hotel on business. The hotel could not combine my reservations into one (as a third party entity had paid for my stay for one night and I paid for the others) and I had to unfortunately check in and check out each and every day. The check in time was unusually late -- I was told that I could check in at 4PM (this was on the same day as the St. Patrick's Day parade). 
The hotel is located in Center City. In theory, it is very convenient and the Reading Terminal Market, drug store, Macy's, and other things are nearby. However, I made a point not to wander too far as crime is not unusual for this area.
The restaurant, Sole Food, has okay food. I did not find it very delicious, though. I also found that I had to tell them to apply the "Tasty Credits" (apparently, you have a discount on food if you eat in this restaurant which is inside the hotel).
I also ordered room service. They did a pretty nice job with the food and delivery. The room service people were very cordial.
The hotel is very big. Initially, I had a hotel room near the elevator and I had to change rooms because my neighbors next door were making a lot of noise and because of the noise from the elevator. The front desk had switched me to another room (and I requested that it should be away from the elevator). The new room was nice and quiet. The bed was also very comfortable. I had no problem getting a good night's sleep.
Taxis are generally available outside of the hotel. 
Maggiano's is located close to the restaurant (about a block away) and McCormick and Schmick's is a few blocks away too (albeit in the opposite direction).
The hotel is located across from the Pennsylvania Convention Center, which made it convenient in terms of attending my conference. There is a Fed Ex location across from the hotel and also within the Pennsylvania Convention Center itself.
The hotel has a computer which is near the front desk in the lobby. It also has a printer attached to it. Use of the computer and printer was free. (However, the front desk people told me that use of the business center's computer would cost a lot and therefore was not free.)

title: “Fell in love with this hotel....”
text: This hotel was not what I expected when it was booked by my co-worker. We attended Wild Days at Sea World and stayed for a couple of nights. This hotel was quiet and cozy. I already love Hyatt Restaurants and absolutely loved Springhouse that is across the street at their other property. The shop, restaurants and amenities within the timeshare portion of the property close pretty early, but they do let you travel to the sister Hyatt down the street and enjoy dinner there. The front desk staff were a bit unfriendly.....Overall experience was great...I'd sign up to hear a timeshare presentation just to go here again....

title: “Convenient and comfortable!”
text: We loved our stay at the Mayflower Hotel! The staff was extra helpful, answering our many questions and offering great suggestions. (Even provided a Muni-Pass for us!) Our room was fine (a little warm, but it was a near record-breaking temp. that day) and we loved the mini-kitchen/bar area. Our breakfast was a wonderful start to the day. Great restaurants nearby. Loved the free parking, but be sure you have a very small car!!!

title: “Loved the hotel, but bad personnel”
text:
We came in for the USGP.. We were staying in the modified train wagons. Very nice rooms. TERRIBLY annoying were the cleaners who actually knocked on the door at 0800 to ask if they could serve the room. Not once but several days in a row. Bad show, Holiday Inn.. 
Very thoughtful though was the package they gave us for the race day, with candy, water, etc.
Overall impression: Good hotel, good facilities, nicely located, but the cleaning personnel actually spoilt the experience. Sorry, no cigar..

title: “An okay hotel in a less-than-okay area”
text:
We made our reservations on the Holiday Inn Express site in July after getting tickets to an area concert. Our primary reason for selecting this hotel was because the jacuzzi suite showed available at the same price as a regular room... so we booked it! Once we arrived in the room, we quickly noticed it was not the room we had guaranteed on our reservation. I logged into the website to check the reservation to make sure I wasn't going crazy, and I noticed the email confirmation and the website reservation were COMPLETELY different. I called the front desk and they stated they changed the reservation because the jacuzzi suite should not have shown up for that price and if I wanted to pay another $50 per night, they could move me to the room I originally was guaranteed. Needless to say, we just stayed in this simple room instead since we had lots of activities going on over the weekend. The hotel was basic and nothing really special, but it was clean. Our bathroom door would not shut, but we had no problem throwing down a towel in front of the door to hold it closed for privacy. 
The area around the hotel completely changes after dark. There were cars continuously going around the hotel two or three at a time and would never get out of their cars. The hotel uses its shuttle van to block one of the entrances to keep unwanted people out. There is a Baby Dolls strip club right across the street. The night guy at the front desk was on his cell phone every time we came in and out of the hotel and the side entrance door was broken (so you have to walk all the way around the dark property at night).
Although the room was clean and the only actual problem we had was reservations, I would still not stay at this hotel again. The hotel staff, management, and their nationwide reservation number showed very little care for the situation and offered even less help.

title: “Very Good Hotel”
text: Extremely central, nice bar and restaurant with fantastic breakfast options. Only complaint I had was that I was charged 125 USD for an 8 min international phone call. But otherwise I would highly recommend this hotel

title: “Bring earplugs!”
text:
I was prepared early on to give this hotel a high rating. The lobby is absolutely gorgeous, the hallway leading to our room smelled fresh and fragrant, and our room itself, while small and a bit dark, was quite comfortable, very clean, and more than adequate for our needs. We had a lovely first day and an uneventful night. 
It wasn't until the next day that we discovered the one huge problem with this hotel--the paper-thin walls! We had no neighbors until the 2nd night of our stay, and when they checked into their room, they might as well have been staying with us, since we could hear every single thing they said, even their normal-voice conversations. It was just annoying at first, but it got worse as they had a young child that awoke at 7 a.m. every day, and therefore we were also awake at 7 a.m. every day. Every time their door closed, it rattled our entire wall and made our door shake very loudly. Needless to say, we got very little sleep after they arrived.
I would recommend this hotel due to its great location and affordability, but I would encourage anyone staying here to do yourself a favor and get earplugs!

title: “Decent hotel, terrible beds”
text:
We paid $171 on Priceline (rack rate was $219). The hotel is clean, the staff is pleasant and the breakfast buffet was pretty good. The hotel is five blocks from two metro stations and near both the White House and Dupont Circle. We found it reasonably easy to get around D.C. from there.
Our major complaint were the beds. My wife and I had a double (notwithstanding our request for a King) and both beds were brutal. I'd be tepid of staying here again notwithstanding the above.

title: “Unbeatable Location”
text: The Hilton New York's location is simply unbeatable because you're steps away from just about everything. It is a huge hotel, and very busy too I might add, so you don't get too much personalized attention but you do get the reliability that comes with the Hilton name. Lobby area was impressive enough for a business hotel and the rooms were very comfortable. The corridors to the rooms were a tad narrow but I guess this is New York! I did stay in a non-renovated room but I could not fault it. It did have a distinctly American feel to it. Breakfast at the Executive Lounge was OK - you really cannot go wrong with pastries and coffee.

title: “Nice hotel, bad location...”
text:
The area around the hotel is full of homeless people and although there are designer shops just down the road it's still not a nice place to be walking about. Otherwise, the location itself was handy for getting most places.
The room itself was nice but we had a few issues. I'm allergic to feather bedding, which isn't an uncommon complaint but although the hotel were able to offer polyester pillows they didn't have any duvets to replace the feather one so it was taken away and we were given a couple extra blankets which weren't as warm and we ended up having to sleep with the heating on which wasn't ideal. 
The toilet took forever to flush and you had to hold the push button down for a good ten seconds for it to kick in.
The door to the bathroom had no handle, just a recess in it to pull it forward and back to open. It wasn't the easiest to handle, especially for those with nicely manicured hands. I could also see this as a problem for those with dexterity problems. It's also easy to push it too far open and then it becomes stuck in the recess and is a nuisance to try and get back out.
The room was a little bit scruffy around the edges - some of the light fittings had bits hanging off which isn't what you expect from a hotel that advertises itself as a boutique hotel. The chest of drawers was also sitting unevenly, so everytime you opened one drawer another rolled out and you had to push umpteen drawers in until you hit the right combination to get them all to stay closed again which was annoying.
As far as noise was concerned, we were on the 8th floor and it wasn't an issue although we did sleep with the windows closed because of the duvet problem. Perhaps in warmer weather this might have been an issue.
On the plus side:
A store (walgreens, I think) right next door which was handy for any refreshments, toiletries etc.
Lovely big full length mirror with a plug point beside it to get ready in the main bedroom as well as a nice bathroom mirror with plugpoint as well. 
Super comfortable bed.
Spotlessly clean.
The towncar to the airport is a fab service and was a nice treat at the end of our honeymoon for not much more than what we would have paid for a cab, The driver was a lovely guy. 
All in all, a nice hotel that is slightly let down by the location and the failure to pay attention to detail.

title: “great location!”
text: wonderful hotel...conveniently located next to T station....clean and walking distance to food, shopping , museums, fenway park, and universities! Mobs of pedestrians on game days. Shop for combination flight and hotel deals...no car necessary to see the city.

title: “They don't make hotels like this anymore...”
text:
From reading all the reviews on TA, my expectations were quite high, and Elysian didn't disappoint. The hotel is just beautiful...lovely courtyard/driveway, sparkling lobby, dark and cozy bar, gorgeous guest rooms with fireplaces. I prepaid online $195 for a deluxe King room (600+ square feet), and we were offered an upgrade to an 1100 sq ft 1-bedroom suite with an extra half bath and balcony for an additional $55 per night. I had to pinch myself when I saw the suite we paid only $240 a night for. Peaks at the lake, balcony, tasteful and comfortable furnishings, soothing palette of taupes, grays, black, white and cream, working fireplace and gorgeous carrara marble bathroom with awesome soaking tub and Asprey bath products, a quite impressive B&W sound system, and some of the most beautiful linens I have seen anywhere.
Service was attentive and friendly. When we checked in, we asked if my husband's black driving moccasins with white top stitching could be polished. After half a winter in the mid-west, they looked like they had had a salt bath. (I had taken them to a local shoe repair place where we live, and they just couldn't do it without turning all the stitching black and "it would take at least 2 days to get the salt out"). Elysian returned his shoes within hours, looking almost brand new, top-stitching still white, and NO CHARGE. I kid you not!
We stopped by Bernard's, the hotel bar, for cocktails before a late dinner reservation, and it's a total departure from the rest of the hotel: very dimly lit; cozy and masculine. Exactly how a bar should be...I felt like I was in the men's bar of a country club that had been there forever. The bartender was very busy whipping up some pretty elaborate cocktails for diners in one of the restaurants, but he still made time to chat with us. Very pleasant, friendly guy. They serve wonderful homemade potato chips and mixed nuts too.
We didn't visit the spa or exercise area but we saw the spa lobby....also lovely. We also didn't visit the restaurants.
The only thing that fell just a bit short was in-room dining. The menu in the room has a limited dinner selection, but when we called we were told that we could order anything from Balsan's menu which we had to look up online. I'm sure they would have brought one to the room if we had asked, but it would have been nice if one was already there. Maybe it changes too often to put in each room. My starving husband ordered Pasta Bolognese and for $20, he received about 1 1/2 cups of penne with sauce. He complained, ordered a burger (awesome), and the hotel took the pasta off the tab. I had the chicken club which was also great. They sent a bread basket up that had some of the best bread I've had, ah divine!
I only have two very minor suggestions based on our stay: (1) I would increase the portion size or take the pasta off the menu; I've since seen other reviews that mention this. (2) I would have bath salts by the tub when guests arrive. (I asked for more conditioner and they brought salts as well.)
Our check-out experience was terrible...only because we had to leave. My husband and I live about 3 hours from Chicago and visit often. We've stayed in most of the hotels in the Gold Coast. Not one of them even comes close to the Elysian. I HIGHLY recommend you book your stay in Chicago here.

title: “Loved it!”
text: Our stay was great. The staff was extremely accommodating. Location was great also. My husband needed a refrigerator and microwave for medical issues and they were brought up quickly with no extra charge. Everything was great!

title: “Hotel on the beach and close to Sea World”
text: We stayed at the Blue Sea Lodge for two nights. I think this may be an older property that has been renovated in the last few of years. The hallway carpet was somewhat worn and the walls could use a fresh coat of paint. The room had a microwave, small fridge, coffee maker and a sink with a small breakfast bar. My daughter wanted to make hot chocolate in the microwave but could not get it to work. She used the coffee maker instead. One of the lights in the room did not work either. We had to carry our luggage up one flight of stairs to the elevator because we didn't park in the parking garage. To avoid the stairs you must park in the parking garage under your room's building. No other complaints. We stayed in a room on the second floor that had a balcony overlooking the pool and the beach. The only thing that separated the pool from the beach was a sidewalk/boardwalk. I loved the location. It was a five minute drive to Sea World. There were restaurants and stores within walking distance. We loved being so close to the beach. My daughter liked watching the surfers. One morning, from our balcony, we saw what looked like 5 or 6 dolphins or porpoises. Overall I liked this hotel.

title: “Loved the Lowes Hotel - Great location”
text:
I recently stayed at the Lowes Hotel and it was a great experience. It was in a beautiful old building. I was in town for business at the Wannamaker business which is right next door. 
When I checked in the hotel was not that busy so they upgraded us for free to the Business Level. You need to use a key access to get to the upper floors, stayed on the 30th floor. The room was art deco style but modern. There was a queen bed, with a chaise lounge in the corner of the bedroom. The view was spectacular and overlooked all of Philadelphia. Great continental breakfast on the 31st floor with a great view again of the city. Lox, bagels, fresh fruit, muffins and yogurt are served. A great staff person on the floor will even toast your bagels. Ask for bottled water. 
The bathroom was marble with nice Bloom toiletries in the bathroom, with shower gel which I like instead of soap especially in the winter. 
The gym was nice, treadmills, elliptical, and bikes. A weight room and a pool. They charge $10 a day, but my company had it included in the rate. There is also an on site spa, which I will try next time as I didn't have enough time. 
Ate at the hotel restaurant SoleFood which was excellent. I saw someone else recommended the sea bass with crab meat and I recommend it to. 
Overall excellent stay. I told my boss I would go back for business anytime and stay at the Lowes again!

title: “Four star might be a bit generous”
text: The room was TINY (it was a standard room) and the bed was a bit... tired. But it was a great location, the bathroom was nicely upgraded, and the linens were lovely and soft, as were the pillows. The elevator bank makes the adjacent rooms a funny shape, which means the bed is jammed in such that one person has to climb over the other to get in/out of bed. Plus the elevators make noise.

title: “Beautiful veiw!!”
text: This is our second time staying here. We love how economical the hotel is, however, very clean!! We walked to the wharf and it was not bad at all, maybe a mile. If you'd like to take a taxi, it will cost only 6 bucks. We also wanted a late night bite sent to our room and the staff helped make that happen, they sent up menus on places that were open late, very helpful! Another great thing about this hotel is that the parking is only 29-, other hotels are up in the 45-50 dollar range. Our room also had a great view and a refridgerator that we love to have. I definatley will stay again!

title: “Nice digs”
text:
Stayed here 3 nites for a conference. The hotel is a very trendy boutique hotel convenient located near the Magnificent Mile (Michigan Ave). The lobby is pretty small and 1/2 of it is overtaken by an extended bar from Prime, the hotel's steakhouse restaurant (heard some good things about the restaurant). 
The staff was efficient if not totally friendly. I noticed a tendency for staffers to congregate and felt as if I was intruding on their space when I went to check in/out so felt rather uncomfortable. 
The room itself is rather small but the clean lines of the decor made most of the room. The bed and the flat-screen TV was nice, and the corner room we stayed in was quiet throughout the night. The Kiehl's bath products were the best, and the housekeeping staff was really friendly with the bed turndown service and cookie(s).
Door staff was extremely helpful and friendly, and I went to them to ask questions rather than 'bother' the front desk staff. Was there a concierge there? Didn't notice.
Maybe my tastebuds were off but I would not order drinks at the bar. I ordered a G&T which tasted like soda instead of tonic; this could not be fixed so resorted to another drink.
Pro: convenient location. Starbucks and Trader Joe's right across. Good eats on the same block or right across. Friendly door staff. Decent mini bar.
Con: rooms were pricey and rather small (smaller than NYC hotel rooms). small elevators.

title: “Still a great place to stay”
text:
I returned to this hotel after 2-1/2 years and was pleased to find that it was still a good place. The interiors are stylish and the TVs are now of the large flat screen type. An evening service replaces any soiled towels and arranges the pillows for sleeping. A restaurant off the lobby provides good food for around $40 without drinks/desserts. The location is very convenient to Suburban Station and is near Rittenhouse Square. The area is gentrifying with new apartment buildings going up.
I wish that there was an alternative to the perfumed soap in the bathroom--I find it a bit overpowering. The bathroom (that comes with fresh orchids) has double doors that do not lock--a rather odd feature.
I do not stay overnight in Philadelphia very often, but would certainly choose this hotel again.

title: “Stay at The Sheraton Downtown in Denver-- GREAT location, GREAT POOL”
text:
This hotel is centrally located. We could not have picked a better place! If you forgo the room cleaning, you receive a $10 credit per day, at one of the hotel's eateries, and there are plenty to choose from. Parking is $25 per day, so it's better to pay the taxi fee from the airport.
Plus most places are within walking distance of the hotel anyway, so we did not miss having a car at all. The location is PERFECT... tons of places to see, shop, eat, explore. We even walked to the Denver Zoo one day, but shared a cab back to the hotel at the end of the day. The room was very nice, w. scenic views of the city, OH and THE POOL! One of the BEST hotel pools ever! Denver is a beautiful place and if we ever go back, we will stay at this hotel again!

title: “Great Location and Very Spacious accommodation”
text:
We recently stayed at the Magic Castle hotel with our two teenagers and had a 2 bedroom suite. The suite was apartment style newly remodelled, with large king bedrooms, bathroom, large lounge and full kitchen. Beds were very comfortable and bedding was good quality. The remodelling has definitely been done on a tight budget. New kitchen and beds but old carpet and living room furniture. Bathroom had new toilet and vanity but old bath with repainted rather than replaced tiling. Great to have a kitchen but only cooking utensil provided was a milk pan so couldnt really prepare a meal so still ate out every night.
Reception staff were very helpful and friendly. 
Even though the weather was cool and wet for April our boys used the heated pool every evening. 
Breakfast was OK but you have to eat outside or in your room. It was very wet during our stay and we had to carry trays of food through the rain and up many steps to our room.
If travelling with the family we would definitely stay here again for its good value, spacious and clean accommodation and its great location, but if we were without the kids we'd probably look for somewhere a little more upscale.

title: “What more could you want?”
text:
Never have i experienced so much attention to detail and courtesy at a hotel.
The food was obviously amazing, but the service is really just incomparable to other hotels.

title: “Patchy Experience”
text:
Decent rooms & restaurants; showing some wear and tear
Pool: Advertised on internet, but were told it was not working upon arrival; reluctantly agreed to free breakfast instead 
Front desk: Not very helpful
Rooms: They have air pump conditioners/heaters for each room; they are noisy
Internet Access: They charge $12 per night in room; it is free in all the holtels in the vicinity, even the Holiday Inn
Tip: 
1:Don't ask the bell captain for a taxi (you pay double); just walk across the street and get one!
2: Hilton just openend next door; overlooks Camden Yards, and has nicer facilities

title: “Ramada”
text: Lobby was blah food was blah priced way too high ...staff were friendly and the room was clean just could have had a bigger table or desk

title: “You Get What You Pay For”
text: THE PROS: Centrally located hotel, near good shopping and sights. The public areas were recently renovated in very traditional, psuedo-luxury style. There is a lively, young crowd gathered at the lobby bar on most nights. THE CONS: We got a special internet rate of $200 per night for a "deluxe" room. The rate seemed a little too good but we decided to take a chance. Our room was dark and dreary (one small window, two lamps), sparsely furnished, cheap materials, hard bed. Not our idea of deluxe. We switched to a mini-suite which was larger but just as ugly, and there were a number of stains and rips, damaged sink. I got a glimpse of a standard room and it was very tiny and old. BOTTOM LINE: There are far worse hotels at the same price, and the Roosevelt is safe and clean. Just keep your expectations low. If you can afford $50-$100 more, there are far better romantic and comfortable options.

title: “Cy Fair with pet”
text:
First time stay, with plans to go back in the very near future. Older style with doors that open to the outside. Our room was on the first floor facing the distant freeway but we never heard any noise once we were inside. Being on this side allowed us to have quick trips for our dog on nearby grass. The room was large enough for the crate without feeling cramped. In the area for dogs, it was not marked nor had signs reminding dog owners to pick up after their pet. No baggies (although we always bring our own) and NO near-by trash can - this would be nice if it were put in. 
The price was reasonable for room. The front desk staff at the time of check in seemed very unorganized. Breakfast was very simple. Overall the room was clean and that was the most important thing. We slept well in the king size bed.

title: “Location is EVERYTHING”
text: This is a wonderful hotel in the perfect part of D.C. for those who are traveling for sightseeing and fun. My husband and I stayed here on our honeymoon in April during the Cherry Blossom Festival and it was great. It is located within walking distance to all the major sites and the Metro. It has very nice amenities and a great concierge service. Because it was our honeymoon they sent us champagne and chocolate covered strawberries; it was pretty cute. It is an historical hotel so the rooms are smallish and a tad dated but very clean with comfy beds. It may be a little pricey but honestly you can't go wrong with this hotel. Also, if you decide to give it a go, try the Hamilton restaurant next door. They make an excellent drink called, what else, "the hamilton" and they have a really nice artesian cheese appetizer.

title: “Phenomenal Service & Location”
text: The first thing I noticed when arriving at 6 Columbus was the amazing location. Midtown Manhattan, right in the middle of Columbus circle and a minute walk to Central Park and the subway?! Score. Second, the service from the front desk, housekeeping, door/bell men, to the concierge was 110% Everyone always had a smile on their face and was ready and willing to help with anything you needed, reservations, directions, towels for your room, cab, whatever - you name it. They upgraded my room last minute, got us in before check in - this is just to name a couple things. The room was very clean, small yes, but its a boutique hotel and everything was comfortable. What a hotel experience should be like! Really pleased!!!

title: “Busy location, large rooms and comfy beds”
text: The Westin Times Square is located in the heart of Times Square. It's a bit touristy but it's not terrible. The rooms are very large for NY and the you can't beat the Heavenly beds. My first room had a terrible sweat smell in the bathroom and the front desk staff quickly and in a friendly manner moved me to a different room. Great views from the 33rd floor and it is relatively quiet with some, but not a ton, of hallway noise. Biggest issue with this hotel is the Wi-fi is so slow it is unusable. I eventually switched to the wired connection after paying for the Wi-fi and not being able to use it. For a business traveler this is a major problem.

title: “Quirky Hotel”
text:
I stayed at the Standard in June 2012, I was in LA for work and this hotel happens to be close to our offices. It has a very retro style going, I thought it was cool for one night. The rooftop bar was nice, I didn't try their food, but I had a drink and the crowd seemed very pleasant.
My room was pretty plain, just the essentials, which is all I needed. I thought it was odd that there was a glass separating the shower and the room itself. Since I was staying alone, it didn't matter because nobody could see me, but had I been there with my husband, I would have flashed him left and right while showering. So if you like a little privacy while you shower, ask for a room with some privacy in the shower.
I only ate breakfast in the hotel and it was VERY good. I asked for eggs whites (and rearranged the menu as I typically do) and they were very accomodating and the food was very good.
If I had to go back, I'd stay at the Standard, I liked it overall.

title: “Best Value you will find in Hollywood!!!!”
text:
Not sure why some folks have issues with this place? It's in a normal neighborhood (it's LA folks.), close to freeways, Hollywood Blvd, ralph's/walgreens/Food 4 Less (buy your alcohol here), and a ton of crazy nightclubs and Thai restaurants. There's free parking, free wifi in your room, and a swimming pool.
We were greeted with a clean, simple room. The bathroom looked newly renovated, tiles and everything. Be prepared to walk 300 ft to Walgreen's if you forgot your soap, they are lacking that here; the store is open 24 hours in case you arrive in the middle of the night and want to smell good. The room also comes with a mediocre tv, microwave, and fridge (store alcohol here).
A the best value if you don't mind listening to Frenchies sunbathe and smoke cigs all day :)

title: “March 2012 riverwalk trip”
text:
My family's recent trip to San Antonio was highlighted by our stay at the Westin Riverwalk.
San Antonio is not much of a city, older but still has its charms especially around the Riverwalk which lead me into the Westin.
So the positive things about the Westin are:
1) location
so central to the alamo, rivercenter mall, la vallita and of course it's right on the Riverwalk and only 20 min. from the airport or 10 min. from the alamo dome
2) clean hotel and friendly staff, nice restaurant facilities and decent breakfast buffet, la marienda is a nice special touch where they have an afternoon drinks and snacks for guests
An average part of the hotel:
1) you cannot access the fridge: if you have kids or have takeout you want to bring home to refrigerate, you have to pay for this service. only in the U.S. does it happen and it feels like they are nickel and diming guests. 
Overall i am a big fan of the Westin so enjoy your next stay

title: “Good Stay at the Holiday Inn-Express”
text: The Holiday Inn-Express is a nice hotel in a nice part of town. It is a couple blocks South of the Outerbelt and there are some eateries nearby. It is a little difficult to enter the property from Southbound East Street and you have to turn after the hotel and come back or work your way through other lots to get to it. The breakfast was excellent with the signature cinnamon rolls and biscuits and gravy, and more. It was clean in the room and in the breakfast area and seemed to be quiet as I slept well through the night both nights I was there. Check-in and checkout were a breeze and the clerks were pleasant and accommodating. It is good for a stopover or for a longer stay. I didn't get to try it, but the pool looked nice.

title: “Excellent - lovely lovely people”
text:
The staff were the nicest people I have met so far and could not do enough for you. Even offering to drive me inthe golf court to the back of my hotel so I didnt have to walk the 5 mins in the rain!! Also none of the staff would except any tips of any kind, so you know that the service being provided was just out of niceness. 
Location I thought was great less then a 10 min walk to Beale St. Some people may have concerns because it was a little of the beaten track and the area did go a little down hill. But as a single female I felt perfectly safe there. 
Room was large and clean and very comfortable. I think it the best bed in a hotel etc I have slept in.

title: “True Excellence”
text: If I had to rate this hotel and staff on a scale of 1 to 10, I'm giving it a 20. Excellence in EVERYTHING. Hoorah. It's worth every penny spent. I'll certainly be back.

title: “You get what you pay for”
text: Cheap price. No shampoo, soap, or iron & board in room. We got ate up with bug bites during the night. TV volume would increase in volume constantly. The front desk attendant was very nice. would not stay here again. YOU GET WHAT YOU PAY FOR!

title: “Thank goodness the location was great!”
text: The hotel was right on the Riverwalk. Close to all kinds of dining, bars and shops. Also, only a block or so from the Alamo! Plenty to do and see. The food at the hotel was mediocre. The afternoon bar tender did not know what she was doing. We ordered three drinks, which endedd up costing us over $40 and ended up leaving them as they were to bad too consume. But the evening bartender was fabulous, remembered our names from the night before along with our orders! The rooms were fine, but the bathrooms were tiny. We had a room on the 30th floor with a great view of the Riverwalk, but the only floor that didn't have a balconey.....what a shame! The elevators were HORRIBLE! One person in our party waited 17 minutes before there was an elevator he could squeeze into to get to his room, drop off his jacket and get another elevator to squeeze into to get down to the lobby. Everyone in the hotel seemed to complain about the elevators. I have to give kudos to the staff who were great. Next time I would stay at the Marriot across the street!

title: “Not a 4 star experience!”
text: This hotel is in a great location, however the room we stayed in was poorly equipped (one tea bag?!) & a little shabby - for example, black grouting around the bath tub & cracking plaster on one of the walls. Whilst the room was a good size, it was particularly cold - and the heating system was very noisy!

title: “location & price right”
text: The Roosevelt Hotel is an easy walk from Grand Central Station. It has a nice lobby, several eating establishments, boutiques. Our room was on the 18th floor. Small, but clean. Very low water pressure - hard to rinse long hair in shower. Hard pillows, but when I requested soft, feather pillows, they were brought to our room in timely fashion. Would stay here again.

title: “Clean and quiet, but neighborhood leaves something to be desired.”
text:
I needed a place to stay for a week while starting a new job. I have a Choice Hotel card and this location was nearest my job site in South Torrance on the edge of Lomita.
All I wanted was a clean and quiet motel room, and Rodeway did not disappoint. Despite being right on Pacific Coast Hwy, I did not hear a lot of traffic.
Amenities: No pool or laundry. Continental breakfast was juice, coffee, and danish and I did not partake. There was Wifi but it was sometimes flaky, requiring multiple attempts to get logged in.
What I liked least was the location, which is very near Lomita and Harbor City, which are not the safest places. I did not venture far from the motel at night.

title: “Great stay, would definitely return”
text:
This hotel really exceeded my expectations. The room was clean and updated (standard Courtyard decor). The parking garage took a little figuring out at first, but after that it was a snap, and the price seemed reasonable for downtown. The service was great, especially the front desk staff and Bistro staff. Speaking of which, the food quality was good, and they have great hours. There's also a Friday's next door which was also very good. Location was excellent, very close to the Canal Walk, which was great for running. 
All in all a great experience, and I will be back if/when I'm in the area again.

title: “Double Check your Bill”
text: This was the most amazing 5 star hotel, and probably the one I will compare all others for the rest of my days. The bed was so comfortable, my husband was reluctant to leave to go sight seeing around the city. After 'roughing it' for a week in another city, this was the perfect hotel for sheer luxury. However the experience was spoiled by some incredible charges on our bill. It seems far too many people linger around the hotel, and we found over $200 in meals charged back to our room that we did not eat. Turns out (after much investigation of receipts) that someone must have misheard our surname, and saw us going into our room (we were on the floor with the gym). Only the fact they misheard, and thus misspelled our names on the dockets made them suspicious. We certainly didn't eat 3 times at the same restaurant in the one night. Better yet, just tell the staff to not allow any charges back to the room, and this problem will go away. A great facility, however, and I would go back again (but with a bit more caution about the people loitering around). The concierge even arranged a stretch limo to the international airport as we left - a beautiful way to end a trip to the USA!

title: “I really enjoyed my stay and will be back”
text: I came to San Antonio just to get away from my busy and stressful life and that was exactly what I found here. I arrived past midnight and I was quickly checked in and direct to my room by the nice and professional front office receptionist which unfortunately don’t remember her name because I was tired & I am bad with names!. Arriving to my room was a haven; it was cool and clean the linen smelled clean. Everything was perfect for me. I was able to get a great night sleep. The next day I had full agenda so I was out the Hotel the whole day & I wasn’t able to see much there but the next morning I went to the restaurant for breakfast and I was greeted by the restaurant Manager name Luis, he was so nice & professional I was happy with the way he greeted & accommodated me. However what impressed me the most was to witness a situation where a guest had lost his iphone charger I didn’t hear all the details because; it seemed to have started before I arrived but, I heard how Luis was checking with the Housekeeping department lost & found and since they told him that they didn’t found the charger in that room I heard him call again & asked the Housekeeping department if they had any charger in their lost & found and he then went to the guest & asked if he would trust him to take his iphone to check & see if any of the charger they have would work with it. The guest allowed him to take his phone & just a few minutes later he arrived with his phone very happy that he found one that worked for it. I just couldn’t keep myself quiet and I told him that I was impressed with the way he had gone above & beyond to help the guest & save him from going to the store to buy another charger. The guest seemed pleased & I was happy to witness that there still people so customer service oriented going the extra mile doing so. After I finish my breakfast I walk around the Hotel & I felt in love with the pool! Very nice! And as I went back to my room to relax for a little bit and then finish getting ready to leave; I met one of the room attendants who was very nice & recommended me few places to go before I left. Overall I had a great stay and will stay here every time I come to San Antonio! I honestly recommended it.

title: “Fun, Sheek Hotel”
text:
The hotel is a fun and sheek party hotel. 
PROS: It's the hot spot with great clubs and music. If you want to see beautiful people this is the place to stay. The decor is amazing and if you want to lounge with your friends, this is the place. The staff was extremely helpful.
CONS: Unless you're staying in a suite, the regular rooms are tiny. The hallways and elevator are hot so for the hair straightening ladies, put it in a bun when you walk out your room until you exit the hotel. Do not stay in a room near the terrace or you will be up all night hearing music.
OVERALL: It's fun for a weekend stay.

title: “Ab Fab!”
text: Have just spent 4 nights here with my husband and 9yr old son. We have had a fantastic time, the staff could not have been more helpful and welcoming. We loved the decadence of the lobby (including the cat!) and the suite we had was small but immaculate. Great location for all the sights. The hotel was the icing on the cake for our first trip to New York

title: “Great location”
text: Easy check in and out. Very friendly. It is the perfect place to stay...especially for shopping at Market Square.

title: “perfect”
text: We stayed here on the night of our wedding. The views facing the riverfront were spectacular. Everything in the room was immaculate and perfectly coordinated. The colors were bright and bold, but overall the decor was soothing. Beyond appearances the amenities were neat and comfortable. The hot tub and window seats were our favorite.

title: “Trendy downstairs, tired upstairs”
text:
We stayed at the Royalton for a week in late November, 2012, based in part on the reviews on Tripadvisor.
First, the location is great; it is a few blocks from Times Square, the theatre district, and some pretty good restaurants.
The hotel itself has a very busy nightclub and restaurant in the 'lobby', the configuration of which could be more accurately described as a check-in desk in a nightclub. This is fine, just different. The music gets pretty loud later in the evening, but we couldn't hear it from our room.
We had booked a studio room, which has a fireplace, big soaker tub, king bed, and more space than a standard room. While broadly as described on the website, the room (although large) was pretty tired looking - worn carpet, missing grout between the tiles in the bathroom, ugly staining in the grout around the tub, shower curtain bar anchor pulled out of the ceiling at one end etc. No one thing terrible, but it didn't feel clean, and didn't feel like it had been well maintained. The fact that the paint and carpets were all a uniform grey-green color likely didn't help as it added to the dingy feel.
The mattress on the bed was pretty soft and did not isolate any movement, although the linens were fine. Sleep-wise, it would also be good to pick an upper floor, as the windows are not very sound-proof and New York is generally a noisy place at all hours. We were originally given a room on the 3rd floor facing W44th, and within a few minutes it was clear it would be pretty loud. We requested to be moved up and the hotel staff were very helpful in accommodating this request (note that this is the first time I have ever requested a room change in a hotel). Our new room on the 9th floor was much better, and faced W43rd instead, which is a quieter street.
We chose to have a fire one night in the fireplace (which requires that the outside temperature be below 40 f), and were surprised to learn that the fireplaces are not gas, but burn real wood. The building maintenance person came up promptly when we phoned and started a duraflame log in the fireplace for us, at which time we noticed the loud hum of an extractor fan starting up (it was maybe as loud as the microwave in your kitchen, or a hairdryer).
The fan continued to run for some time, shutting off at 3 or 4 in the morning (it was loud enough that the absence of the sound woke me up). The effect of the fan, apart from the noise, was that all heat from the fire was pulled up the chimney, so the value in having the fire was really lost (i.e. no 'cozy' factor). It should also be noted that the fan is common between rooms, so even when someone else has a fire, you are treated to the sound of the fan at the same volume.
While the hotel does provide an iPad in each room with web access, the implementation was a little clumsy and the browser was hard to find. There is WiFi in the hotel, but it is $10 a day.
