Overall, the service was pretty good, and the location was great, but the hotel did not live up to the $450/night it cost, even in New York (there are much better places like the Giraffe).

title: “Excellent example of an intimate small hotel!”
text:
Having just returned from a seven night stay at The Chancellor I wanted to share my experience with everyone here at Tripadvisor. The Chancellor Hotel was a wonderful find! It exceeded or expectations. It sounds too good to be true...BUT IT'S NOT!!!!
The Chancellor has an old world charm unlike the sterile chain hotels. It is charming with an intimate feeling, small enough to feel at home but right in the heart of The City, accessible to everything. The staff was friendly and welcoming, informative and efficient.
There are so many touches that make the hotel special. First, and foremost, it is clean and well cared for with much attention to detail. Ammenities such as comfortable beds, a pillow menu,ceiling fans, a walk in-closet with with a safe, a portable heater, iron and ironing board and an umbrella, plus ample room for hanging clothes as well as storing luggage . The bathroom had a soaking tub complete with bath salts and fine toiletries(as well a a rubber ducky!).There were sweets and coffee in the room as well as delicious Italian Roast coffee,cookies and apples in the lobby, along with free newspapers and WIFI computer access. All make it exceptional in my opinion.
I had the good fortune of communicating with Wes Tyler, the general manager, on the forum before our trip and he went out of his way to make our stay at The Chancellor VERY special.My biggest disappointment was that we were not able to meet him and thank him personally because he was away during our visit. Perhaps next time! And there WILL be a next time!
We may have been spoiled by the suite of rooms we were given on the 15th floor but we found no problem with the size of our accomodations. Given that is an older hotel we expected something smaller. And there wasn't much more you could ask for...all the ammeneties you could ask for were there. And add to all of that LOCATION, LOCATION,LOCATION! Being right on Union Square on The Powell Street Cable Car Line! We had great weather and had the windows open all week and were able to enjoy the sounds of The City that make it so unique. Even the local street musician playing the saxaphone put us to sleep at night.
There are so many things to say about San Francisco and The Chancellor in particular I could go on and on but I'll save some of that for other sections of the forum.
I do want to mention,however, that if you are staying in The City you will not have to rent a car. Just get a MUNI Passport (1,3 or7 days). It offers you unlimited accessto all Muni transportation ( buses, streetcars,trollies, AND also INCLUDES the Cable Cars!!!! )(Although we are afraid the MUNI might go broke considering we rode EVERYTHING and went EVERYWHERE for our 7 day $24.00 Passport !!!)
Kudos to The Chancellor, the staff and especially to Wes Tyler.

title: “Not what i expected”
text:
We went to the quality inn during august 2003. It was extrememly humid and hot and their air conditioning was broken. Elevators are so small that my closet in my hotel room was bigger. We had requested 1 bed, they gave us two. Room is EXTREMELY small, we barely had room to walk. 
It was difficult to get tv channels, bathroom leaked, hotel staff rude and discourteous. While this hotel may seem like a bargain, go somewhere else! It's not worth it, even if you are trying to pinch a few pennies!

title: “Okay hotel in a great location”
text: Most reviews are "on the mark", so to speak. Staff a little unfriendly and standoffish. Rooms clean and fairly modern. Great neighborhood, but at top of Nob Hill so anyone with walking issues be advised that you'll be taking taxis often (parking over $50 per day!!). Eat at charming Nob Hill Cafe. Only stay here if you get a decent rate (<$300 per night)....otherwise look elsewhere.

title: “Very nice hotel and good location”
text: Perfect location for what we wanted to do in Seattle without having to pay the expense of staying in a downtown location. On the other hand you don't get a view of the Puget Sound that you get from one of the downtown high rise units. However, this place is still very new, very nicely appointed though sparse to some extent since there's little activity in the main lobby area due, I think, to no on-site lounge/bar or restaurant. Staff engaging, friendly and helpful. Amenities were right up there, the bed restful and relaxing, wooden floors in the room were an interesting 'green' touch although it made sound bounce around a bit. A number of good restaurant choices within easy walking distance. And big plus was free parking (especially with what is charged downtown) although getting out to a bus stop (or the monorail) is equally as easy to do if its not raining too hard. We had beautiful fall weather and walked around a lot, over to the Seattle Center, etc. And glad to have found this very reasonably priced hotel. Well worth it and would stay there again.

title: “Luxury without the attitude! Loved it.”
text:
I recently stayed at the St. Regis with a friend of mine for a 4 day weekend. We found the hotel to be excellent across the board. 
Rooms are light and airy, well appointed with many conveniences and the blackout shades really do BLACK out completely as needed. I loved the configuration of the room with the double doors over the bath that open to the living area - made the room seem much larger. 
We used many of the hotels services - 
early checkin, and I mean really early. We arrived by 11am and were promptly given a room, no issues
Spa - pedi and massages, all were excellent
Pool/jacuzzi/sauna - all clean and uncrowded
Butler - Prompt and helpful
Concierge - got us reservations at my favorite restaurant which was 'booked solid' when I tried to call
Room service - great food delivered to the minute at 7am on the day of our departure. 
All in all - I loved the St. Regis - it was a perfect backdrop for a great weekend in SF. And did I mentioned it's located about 2 blocks from teh Powell BART/Trolley station? So easy to get around.

title: “Lovely hotel. Was worth the money. Good location for Union Square”
text: We really enjoyed our stay at this hotel. Very clean hotel with good facilities, including a gym, which altough isn't big, is perfect for keeping yourself fit whilst away. The staff were very helfpul and the location is perfect for restaurants and shopping. Only a €8 taxi ride from Fishermans Whalf. The only negative, is that it is at the top of a hill, which means a steep walk back from Union Square after dinner or shopping. We didn't find this a problem though as it only takes 5-10 minutes maximum and it keeps you fit.

title: “Rooms are like the W”
text:
nice building etc......the suites are set up the W so the toilet is right next to the bed.....shower on other side of room and sink in middle of room. So you will want to feel very comfortable with whom your traveling. 
The "nightclub" is fun, very young crowd, but has to close by 2 am like all bars in SD.

title: “We loved this place!”
text: Our family really loved this place. It was so close to Central Park and all the museums that my kids, ages 9 and 11 wanted to see. We ate breakfast at Zabar's just around the corner every morning and walked to the Natural History Museum and Children's Museum, and the Art Museum. We walked from the hotel to Central Park in only a few minutes. The concierge was so helpful in finding ticket information for us.

title: “what deceit”
text: friends from France were staying with us for 2 weeks apart from 2 days in Manhattan. They booked with hotels.com and prepaid well over $200 per night for a room for 4 [2 adults and 2 children] with breakfast. On arrival they were shown a room with 1 double bed. After protesting they were shown another with 2 beds. Breakfast was not initially available; they were told the hotel had run out. After insisting that breakfast was included, they were rudely told they would have to wait as someone was out purchasing more food. Finally, they were offered pastries. unfortunately they left with a poor impression of New York hospitality.

title: “Hilton Club on West 57th New York”
text: My friend and I stayed at the Hilton Club in October 2010. The location was excellent so we felt very safe walking and could reach any destinations in Midtown Manhatten with ease. The accommodations were excellent. The hotel was very new and modern unlike most hotels in New York City. We have already started to recommend this hotel to our family and friends.

title: “Ambassador Henry”
text:
After a meeting three of us attended, we visited the restaurant around 1 p.m. on 3/16/12. Met Ambassador Henry, who went above and beyond to make three of us very comfortable with our luncheon experience. We wanted to eat in the courtyard instead of the restaurant. Henry brought us china and flatware so we wouldn't have to eat using plastic flatware and Styrofoam boxes. We were told it wasn't his responsibility to assist us, but he brought our food out to us and provided plates, glassware and flatware. He even provided us with Tootsie Rolls for dessert. Henry truly went above and beyond to make our luncheon experience in the courtyard a memorable experience. Henry is truly an asset to the Marriott Indianapolis East. He always appeared at an appropriate time to assist us. His timing was impeccable.
Henry was always engaging and very helpful. It was a pleasure encountering Henry and relying on his expertise as hotel Ambassador.

title: “Good value, near ocean”
text:
We stayed at the Pacific Shores Inn on Mission Blvd. The room was clean, beds were comfortable. Found the flat foam pillows not great. Room was spacious for the 2 of us. We were on the top floor and away from the road so had no noise complaints.
Complaints we did have, were quickly dealt with: Initially we were in a room that had soaking wet towels neatly hung over the towel bar. When I called to request new towels, they whisked us to a new upgraded room! After 3 days of very cool showers, I talked to the front desk and the water temperature was quickly adjusted. 
The pool was closed when we were there so cannot comment on it.
The best part about the hotel was its proximity to the beach, just 1/2 block away. We had great walks along the ocean boardwalk.
We would not hesitate to stay there again.

title: “I expected more”
text: Don't get me wrong, the Westin is a nice hotel, in a good location. For the price I paid, I just feel like some things should have been better. For example, $12.95/day for wifi seems a bit extreme when already paying well over $100 a night for a room. The $18/day parking fee also seems excessive. The air conditioning worked, but not as well as you would expect. It took quite a while to cool the room off. The bathroom cleanliness was questionable, with a couple mystery hairs on the floor and a few drops of liquid of some sort on the toilet seat. We had a large window overlooking part of Charlotte, with a large soapy streak down the center. One thing in our room particularly confused me. In the credenza, there was what appeared to be a mini-fridge, however, on the front it says "this is not a refrigerator." Apparently, you can pay a fee for it to be stocked with beverages or snacks, etc, but it doesn't really get cold. Strangely, in all the hotel literature in the room, its referred to as a refrigerator - go figure. Upon checking in, I headed back to the car to start unloading, and my wife headed up to our room. Since I had the envelope, she only knew what floor the room was on, so she used the courtesy phone in the hallway to speak with the front desk. She told them who she was, and what floor we were on and just needed the room number. She was told to "hold on" for a moment, and then informed that they weren't allowed to tell her that info, despite it had been less than 2 minutes since we first checked in. I realize security is important, but what harm is it to remind a customer what room number is their's, especially so soon after being face to face with the front desk staff? In closing, once again, this is a nice hotel, but if they expect people to pay their prices, they should improve their service and performance and rethink some of their fees.

title: “Good location for the price”
text:
Before ending up at the Whitcomb I did a fair bit of research about the area and the facilities and I told my friend that it'd either be "a great deal or a horrible one". I'm glad to say that it is the former.
Most reviews I've read mentioned the homeless people around, I was only approached twice on Market Street and a short "sorry" was enough, I wasn't mobbed or anything. The hotel room itself was decent, I felt that there was enough space, and though the toilet was small, it seemed sufficient for what it's meant for (unless you were hoping for a bathtub, then you're in for a disappointment).
The Whitcomb is located just outside the Civic Centre BART station, which made it very convenient to get to from San Francisco International Airport ($8.10 as of writing). The trolley line is also just outside, and the staff were helpful in giving me directions to get around (F-line trolley to Fisherman's Wharf, $2). It is also across the road from the Orpheum Theatre, and a couple of blocks away from SF City Hall.
A real gem is how near it is to the Heart of the City Farmers' Market, which happens on Wednesdays and Sundays. I missed the market at the wharves on Saturday because I'd gone on the Angel Island/Alcatraz tour, so I was pleasantly surprised when my walkabout on Sunday morning led me to this place. Granted, as a tourist, I was limited to buying either small amount of edibles or stuff that could last a while longer, but it was still quite a sight to see.
Across the street from the hotel there are also a couple of places to eat (I didn't eat at the hotel restaurant during my stay so I can't comment on that), which is always a good thing.
I will mention that I didn't really venture out past 8pm, so I'm not qualified to say anything about that. The CRT TVs might feel ancient to some, but it hardly bothered me as most of the time I wasn't really in the hotel room watching TV (why would anyone go on vacation to watch TV anyway?). The wireless was a little off and on, though.
I arrived early for check-in so I don't really blame the hotel for only giving me towels and and toiletries the day after, and I brought my own so I didn't need to request for any. There was no kettle available to boil water, so I had to run across the street to the grocery store to pick up some bottled water, which to me was not a big deal since I'd intended on buying some for going around anyway.
For the price I got it at, it was definitely a great deal!

title: “Not impressed...”
text: We booked this hotel because of the free shuttle to the baseball stadium. We booked four rooms for 10 people. Before booking we made sure to ask if the shuttle would be available to take us to the game. Yes, yes the shuttle will be available. When we got to the dump and asked about the shuttle, it was no, no, only on the weekends. The couple that entered behind us also were told there would be a shuttle. The neighborhood was scary. Someone from our party went to the parking lot to smoke a cigarette before bed and mentioned that several people were going in and out of the front door. He thought it looked like drug deals were going on. The "excercise room" consists of an excercise bike and a treadmill in a room the size of a closet with no ventilation. We just opened the door and the smell of sweat and body odor was overwelming. I will some up this reveiw with one word. Ick!

title: “Great location - Okay hotel”
text: Stayed here Dec 18-20, 2005 based on the reviews on Tripadvisor. You absolutely cannot beat the location of the hotel, which is great because we didn't spend much time in the room. The room and hotel itself is average. For the price you could probably get a better room elsewhere, but you probably couldn't get the great location. For our next trip I would probably want to stay elsewhere in the same price range $400 - $500 a night to compare before giving the Sofitel the highest rating.

title: “Very pleasant stay”
text:
Just returned home after a three night stay at the Sofitel. I got a great rate on Hotwire and, especially for this price, the hotel was wonderful. I was on a low floor in queen bed room-- but I never mind a low floor in the rear of a building in New York because there was zero street noise. The room was completely silent except for the loud closing of other doors nearby (the one design flaw). The room was nicely furnished and all amenities were top notch-- frette linens, towels and robe. L'occitane shampoo, etc. Bed was supremely comfortable. And the bathroom was quite nice-- rain shower and separate bath. No coffee maker in the room, but I got one when I requested it. Small, but well-equipped gym.
The location was perfect for this business trip and I would definitely return. I've stayed at multiple hotels in midtown and this is one of my favorites (along with the Omni Berkshire).

title: “The Jane Hotel in New York”
text:
As we were desperately looking for a low budget hotel in New York for September 2009, a New York friend told us about The Jane. It sounded too good to be true; a fair price hotel in the West Village, recently opened and nice looking but small rooms. 
We were able to book a ‘cabin’ for two persons for 2 weeks.
Arriving at the hotel and seeing our home / cabin for the next two weeks we had the attitude of the positive, still. Okay, it was a very small room with a view on a blind wall and that airco outside was making a lot of noise, but, hey we were in New York.
The first night we were completely wasted from the flight from Amsterdam to New York and slept quite early. We woke up in the middle of the night because of the noise coming out of the bar of the hotel downstairs: music, base drums and people in the hallways making a lot of noise. 
A private party, said the man in the lobby. It was fashion week in New York and it had just begun. “Are there parties every night?”, we asked the next day. “Well, not every night,” was the answer, but we could be moved to a room with less noise coming in, on the other side of the hallway. So we did. A room with a view this time and no noisy airco outside. From then on things could only be better. 
Did it make any difference changing the rooms? Well maybe a little bit but even trying to sleep with earplugs in, didn’t stop the heavy base drums coming through. A few bad nights later we asked to be moved to a higher floor, further away from the noise. We ended up on the 5th floor.
The fashion week was about to come to an end, so that must have meant quiet nights and a good sleep finally.
Our new neighbour on the 5th floor thought different about this. As soon as he arrived in his cabin (at 5.30 pm) he put his music on and this would continue until 11.30 pm. We tried to talk with him and asked him to put his music down and especially to lower the noise of his base drums. In this way we could watch television and actually hear what was said. But he never even opened his door to talk with us. 
And what was going on on this 5th floor? We never figured it out. It seemed to us that most of the residents of this floor were residents in the true sense of the word; we thought they were living there permanently. 
A strange bunch they were, too. What was this man doing in the hallway every time I went to the bathroom, even at 3 o’clock in the morning? He sometimes looked to be in a catatonic freeze and stood there for hours on end.
Who was this fat guy making a mess of the bathroom and never saying a word even as he was spoken to? Who lived down our hallway in a cabin full of plastic bags? And where stayed the guy who was always smoking a joint? Coming from Amsterdam we sure do know the smell of it.
True, the people who are working in The Jane are very nice and sympathetic. The rooms, bathrooms and linen are cleaned regularly. 
We made the best of our stay in The Jane. New York is fantastic and we had a wonderful time there. But no way we’ll ever return to The Jane.

title: “Clean, Beautifully decorated and equipped rooms, friendly and attentive staff”
text:
I couldn't have been more pleased with my recent stay at the Cassa hotel. Granted, the common areas are still under construction - but that had little to no impact on the quality of my stay. The staff (from the front desk to the construction and maintenance workers) could not have been more friendly and helpful. My friend and I had a deluxe room with a king size bed. The room was small -- but so beautifully appointed it really didn't matter. The bed was exceedingly comfortable - the bathroom very european in style - with a wonderfully large shower. Loved the soft and luxiourous towels too. The room came with coupons for breakfast at a nearby restaurant. Clearly, this was included because the hotel's restaurant is not yet open. I enjoyed the fact that restaurant was not open and we had a lovely continental breakfast courtesy of the hotel.
In sum, I would definitely stay here again. The location is perfect. I just hope they keep the rates as low as we found them for our stay just 3 weeks after the opening of the hotel.

title: “Healthy Decadence”
text:
The spa is set along a chunk of Lake Austin, and even in February it was just gorgeous. We stayed for two nights. The whole place is built around their gardens of herbs and greens and flowers, which they use in their restaurants. When you check in, you receive a schedule of classes and events (all of which are included) and a pair of very comfy spa sandals. They tell you that everyone's welcome to just wear their huge, squishy terry robes everywhere, which I disdained the first day and then totally embraced by the second evening. The setting is very pretty, and the walk from the rooms to the spa is just gorgeous.
All your food is included, and is actually incredibly tasty and good - since they list all the calorie counts, you can be good if you want to, or if you're more interested in experimenting than calorie-counting (we, sadly, fell into this category) there's a wonderful variety and array of dishes. My favorite cut-and-paste dinner would have been the manchego cheese flan (60 calories-less than a mini-snickers - gorgeous and creamy anyway),a fennel, orange, and frisee salad, and perfectly cooked lamb chops with a wild honey-orange-rosemary glaze. Even dessert was amazing - we were so shameless we had a second one sent to our room later with room service - there's both a blueberry cobbler and a mocha-glazed chocolate cake that I'm remembering fondly. Breakfast and lunch were good, too - my favorite lunch was a smoked pulled-turkey bbq sandwich with peach chutney, coleslaw, and vinegary sauce, and followed by swirled peach and vanilla frozen yogurt (not TCBY - made with local peaches and vanilla beans, mmm). Hors d'oeuvres are served at 3, and drinks (coffee, several variations on iced tea, etc) are available self-serve all the time. You also have the option to do room service most of the day if you just can't be bothered to go out. 
There are tons and tons of exercise classes, with all kinds of styles - yoga and stretching all the way to hard-core marathon training, kickboxing, etc. They have kayaks and water-bikes for rent, and trips away from the site to hike or train. There are also a bunch of specialists around who will give you one-on-one training and workshops on other related topics, should you want to explore that option - or there's the option of doing nothing at all, which they also encourage: We failed to make our posture analysis session, for example, because we ended up falling asleep together in a double hammock by the river. And we took a great cooking class with the executive chef - the spa has published several cookbooks and we could see why.
There are reading rooms all over the place with a mix of "smart" and cheesy books, the best of which is in the spa itself, the "Blue Room". It's worth going an hour or two early for spa treatments just to hang out by the big fireplace in your robe on the various ridiculously comfortable chairs, chaises, and sofas. You need time to try out more than one... There are a couple of pools, two outdoor and one indoor, a hot tub, and lots of outdoor spa "rooms" where they can do any treatment if you ask ahead. The special treat is supposed to be the "Bamboo Room" designed for couples, but we missed that, sadly.
The staff is completely casual and friendly and anxious to please - they manage to convince you they'll do anything you ask without seeming sycophantic. And I appreciated that the fellow guests we were there with didn't seem to be overly concerned with "showing off" - everyone seemed to sincerely be there to relax, work out, and enjoy the pampering. We were there as a couple and never really talked to anyone else, but there was a "social table" for the people who were there on their own that seemed to be having a good time. 
At the spa, I had an "Olive My Love" treatment, crazy decadence - you start with a ground-olive-pit scrub over your entire body, neck to toe, then shower off in an in-room shower. Then you're doused in gobs of warmed, scented olive oil and wrapped up in warm towels so that it all soaks in - when they wrapped me up, I was dripping in sauce, and when I came back out there wasn't a drop on me, so it had to go somewhere! As you're absorbing, the masseuse massages your scalp with olive oil - totally satisfying, she kind of pulls the roots of your hair as well as rubs the scalp, so soothing - then moves on to a gentle face massage. Then she unwraps you to give you a full-body massage for 50 minutes, using more scented olive oil. By that point, you're basically liquid...and as silky as anyone's ever going to be, everywhere. And a deep-tissue massage on another day was equally amazing, if not even better. 
The one short spot was the room itself – the rooms are comfortable and the beds are great, there’s a shower as well as a deep tub with lots of their signature bath products to make you feel pampered, plenty of prep and closet space, but it’s a little dated and not as luxurious as I’d expected – kind of Texas shabby-chic, with handmade quilts on the wall and upholstered beds. We had a front porch area with chairs and a big soft ottoman (and an adopted cat, who liked our chairs as place to sleep at night). Big flat-screen TV (we watched the Oscars) but no wi-fi in the rooms, which stressed my husband out a little. And it was difficult to make the room really dark at night, due to the number of windows and use of venetian blinds (with wood slats, but still). Cute, but maybe not up to whatever the ridiculous price is for staying overnight. I’m a huge design critic, though, so don’t listen too much to me. The room functioned very well and the time we spent in the room, I wasn’t really critiquing…we were either dressing, sleeping, or being romantic, so obviously it couldn't have been too terrible! 
 I’ll give the spa six stars out of five, and the restaurant at least five out of five, and the rooms a 3.5 (though the beds were awesome, they’re a five, and I’m very picky). Would I spend $1500 a night for all of it, in-season? Not this week – but I don’t fault people who do. It was pretty amazing and soul-affirming. 
It's crazy expensive to stay overnight, so even though it's incredible, I might not do that again, at least not often; but luckily, I live in Austin, so the day spa is absolutely a must in my life, now. 
(Spa is $$$, about average spa cost for similar treatments but better value than most (and the treatments are more luxurious than most), resort is all-inclusive but still $$$$.

title: “Expensive - but a sure thing”
text: WE have stayed here a few times before and chose to pay the high rates to get a sure thing. There was something going on in town that made it challenging to find reasonable accommodations. In the end, we chose to pay about double the going rate to ensure a good night. We weren't disappointed.

title: “compact rooms but a brilliant hotel”
text: One of the best hotels I've ever stayed in. Not the fanciest, certainly not the roomiest, but a joy to go back to after a hard day's fun in New York. The library theme is entertaining, you get books in your room, and the famed complementary cheese and wine were a great, generous, start to each evening. The staff were welcoming and helpful. The breakfasts in the library/dining room overlooking the street were fairly basic but adequate and pleasant. The room was very clean and tastefully fitted, with free wifi and bottled water each evening. This hotel put me in a good mood each day. And I think it was incredible value for money. Midtown is not the most exciting location but so convenient if you want to explore Manhattan and beyond. We walked to most parts of the island from here. I was very sad to leave.

title: “Don't do it!!!”
text:
This hotel is a tip, could've cried when we got to our room after a hours wait in a queue to check in, the bathroom smelt of urine (had got under the flooring) there was a hole in the bath, the bath had been painted in what looked like gloss paint! The carpets were sticky and dirty, the paintwork was all peelong and had never been rubbed down just painted over and over, over the years, you could cup your hands and run along the skirting coming up with handfuls of accumulated filth. The Air-Con was hanging off the wall and made a banging sound 24/7 The furniture was from the 1970's the bed was as hard as nails, but overall the place was filthy, we changed rooms and the second one was just the same. we rung around other hotels but as it was 4th of July week everything was booked, so we were stuck!!
I always thought the Americans were picky, but they did not seem to mind the squalour of this place, although it is centrally located, close to all sightseeing and attractions I would not recommend it to anyone, I'm not posh by any means, but this place was squalid, you had to wear shoes in the rooms as the floors were sticky, don't even look under or behind the beds, you'd be sick, they smelt horrid damp and of urine, the bedlinnen had cigarette burns in it. 
Dont be fooled by the website pictures, the rooms are nothing like it shows, when we complaine dthey did not bat an eyelid and told us all the rooms were the same and if we wanted to check out we'd get a full refund off our holiday company, you could tell they dealt with these complaints all the time, I took 100's of photo's of New York but not one of the interior of this hotel as it was so disgusting and such a let down. I travelled there with my Niece as a surprise for her 16th Birthday and this place was absymal and such a let down to what was supposed to be a great week. I would never stay there again.

title: “Great service and nice location”
text: High end hotel, very clean rooms and people are the best of all!

title: “Best kept secret Chicago downtown”
text: We stayed at the Talbott for a business trade show visit, and I have to say it was the best hotel experience I've had in Chicago. We normally stay at the InterContinental or Palmer House, and the Talbott proved to be both less expensive and a better experience. Dwayne and the rest of the staff were extremely genuine and went out of their way to make sure we were comfortable. Very large double queen room, comfortable beds, great WIFI, Free TV access to internet, and fast valet service were all appreciated. Housekeeping did a fantastic job - very clean rooms. Location can't be beat - two blocks from Michican Avenue on a quiet tree-lined street. 24 hour diner, Walgreens and grocery store all within a block. Also, the cupcake shop (MORE) that is diagonally across the street is fantastic if you like sweets! HIghly recommend it.

title: “a great weekend!”
text: Arrived just in time for the hospitality hour. It was a great way to start an awesome weekend. We stayed in a tall room and everything was great. No problems with anything. We walked all over from the stores in the loop to Navy Pier. Nice location. Would definitly stay here again!

title: “GREAT DEAL IF YOUR TAKE BED&BREAKFAST PLAN”
text: Excellent choice! Great hotel and just a couple of blocks from Metro. Surrounding area is full of great restaurants & services.

title: “Fantastic Stay! The best ever :)”
text: I went to SD for a conference at another property but elected to stay here because it was a newer property. It was the best stay I think we have ever experienced. We were there for the 4th of July and all I can say is WOW. The fireworks could be seen from the grass and people come out in thousands to watch them. The hotel is a year old so it is clean. The staff is what really made the experience so great.. They were awesome. We had a room on the 4th floor that was overall quiet. The view was just fantastic. We could see the city, the water, the pool. The airport is close by so yes you do hear airplanes but that is one noise that has never bothered me too much. If you close the sliding glass door you don't hear much. The pool itself got pretty crowded but it is summer and that's the way it is in summer. The noise from the pool does tend to get kind of loud but it ends once the pool closes so it's not too bad. Housekeeping does tend to come later in the day but they clean your room every single day and they do a thorough job. The little deli downstairs is a nice added touch, the bar is small but sufficient, there are many seating areas outside; one with a fireplace and one with a firepit. There is a walking path by the water that will take you down to liberty station where there is a Starbucks, Panera bread that has some awesome pastries and sandwiches, a pizza place and a Von's to buy groceries. There is also a Subway, TCBY yogurt and a brewery within walking distance in the other direction. Parking was a challenge when the property was full but parking is free. I will def be back to this property. Point Loma seafood is close by and is one of the best sea food places I've ever eaten. Harbor Island and Shelter Island are close by and a must see just for the beauty and to sit and watch sailboats or take a walk or jog. Coronado is not too far...maybe 10 mins and Seaworld is not too far either. There is a free shuttle to the airport and the shuttle drivers are kind and courteous. We used the wireless internet in our room. That was a real plus. We ordered room service and the food was average hotel food and it took about an hour for our sandwich. Be sure to visit Cabrillo at Point Loma for awesome, breathtaking views of the ocean and the bay. It's $5 to get in.

title: “DO NOT BOOK!”
text: We booked this hotel yesterday for our trip to NYC next week after having our last hotel cancelled from storm damage to have our booking cancelled. Not only has it been cancelled but the hotel have now almost TREBLED the price we were quoted yesterday. It's an absolute disgrace and has really put a damp feeling on our trip next week. Avoid at all costs!

title: “Very Disappointed This Time”
text:
I stayed at this motel approximately 1.5 yrs ago and thought it was great. Maybe I was delusional at the time. However I think being a party of 1 and a party of 4 makes a huge difference at this motel. Also some things have not been kept up as they should have. The rooms at the motel are extremely small and compact, especially for a family of four. I have stayed at several comfort suites over the years but these are the smallest rooms at any of them. The rooms have 2 beds, a sleeper sofa, and a small area with a fridge and micro but they have all had that in the past with much more room. With the sleeper pulled out it is almost impossible to get into the room and the coffee table has to be moved but "to where"? A luggage cart barely gets into this space before it is stuck between the TV/drawer stand and the first bed. There is no closeable closet space. The closet area is an open area close to the bathroom sink and the clothes hang over the area where you can place a suitcase which is just a really think type of fiberboard, not real wood and it leans. The bathroom door barely clears the toilet so you have to stand between the toilet and tub to close it which is close. The bathroom sink is right outside that door and basically right in the room, just a few feet from the foot of the bed.
There was a musty smell in the room and there was water on the bathroom floor behind the toilet when we first got there. It took me about 10 minutes to figure out if the toilet was leaking or just water had not been cleaned up when the room was cleaned. The toilet was not leaking. They now have those rubber mats in the bottom of the tubs and there was mildew around the edge of it and when I lifted it up there was much mildew all under it so I quickly put it back down. The bathroom fan was extremely loud/noisy and the air unit was also quite noisy. Whenever these units were running you had to turn the TV way up and/or it was difficult to just have a conversation. The lighting in the room was not very good but over the bathroom sink area was awful. They also had put in a second mirror I guess in an attempt to help more than one person get ready at a time as the sink area was too small to share that mirror. However the extra mirror was stuck back in the open closet area behind the hanging clothes. Also a very dark corner so pretty much useless.
The beds and floor appeared to be clean but there was an issue with a pillow. One of our party continued to say they smelled something nasty when they would lay down on the bed. However it took us sometime to figure out what. They sniffed around the bed top and pillows to no avail. However upon sniffing the individual pillows one was found to be absolutely putrid. Obviously we banned that pillow from the area. We don't know if the smell was the pillow or the case but it was really bad.
The beds were comfy enough, the sleeper sofa was not. Was thin and worn out with a huge dip in the middle.
Breakfast was fine; cereals, yogurt, bread type items, waffle maker, sausage, egg patties(which were pretty good). Juice was not too good and was somewhat thick. However the lady in the breakfast area was very nice and accommodating. 
I definitely would not stay here again with more than two people in the room and would have to think about even then.

title: “Great location,great hotel”
text: We stayed at this hotel for 4 nights in August. We waited a while to check in even though there were quite a few desks open, this was a little annoying as the receptionists seemed to work in two's. Our room had a great view of Navy Pier and was a good size. The bed was very comfortable and the room was spotlessly clean. The location of the hotel is the best, we walked to Navy Pier and Michigan Ave. The breakfast buffet was great although a little pricey and the bar very relaxing for a nightcap or two. Would certainly recommend this hotel and would stay here again.

title: “Good Rates and very clean.”
text: Our service was very good the man at the front desk was very nice and friendly . The room was very nice and clean we really liked the fact that it has a microwave, refrigerator and other amenities that are very useful. Also loved that it has alot of places to go eat nearby. The best thing is that it has good rates the only bad thing was that there wasnt enough hot water and our view was the wall but other than that everything else was good and we would stay there again.

title: “Great value for money in Soho”
text:
Stayed here for 4 nights during New York Fashion week. This hotel might not not be trendy but the location in walking distance from fashionable Soho is a great deal for a long weekend. The rooms are in standard size with nice and comfy beds, it is quite and you can have a great view on Manhattan from the higher floors. Staff is friendly, nice breakfast for a very low price, small Starbucks in the lobby as well.
If you are looking for a good hotel in NY for a very affordable price, this is for sure a good pick.

title: “Nice hotel, convenient location”
text: Hotel is not a full service hotel. They do serve a buffet breakfast but do not have dinner service- only room service. Hotel was clean, housekeeping efficient, bar/lounge comfortable. Pool on the 4 floor clean and warm. Outside of the pool area there is an outdoor lounge/courtyard (we had our Easter egg hunt). Hotel is within walking distance to the harbor which we did 3x's a day. There are boutiques on Aliceanna - expensive but nice to walk around! The staff was extremely friendly and helpful on all levels! The courtyard is 3 blocks from Little Italy (not what little Italy in NYC is) there is one nice restaurant Della Note.

title: “A Good Stay”
text:
The hotel is located in an area close to transportation, supermarkets, shops, parks and restaurants. Being an old hotel completed in the first decade of the 20th Century it also has a certain amount charm. However billing themselves as luxury is I believe going a bit far. This hotel needs to upgrade its furnishings and appointments if it is to pass as a truly luxury hotel, while its current appointments are excellent for a four star hotel; luxury denotes a little something more.
I stayed in the hotel as part of a business trip, for 6 nights. After my first night the room had developed a fatal and deal breaking fault. However the helpful and professional staff was, within hours, able to rectify the fault and the rest of the stay was very pleasant. The room I was in was a Superior King. The bed was comfortable. The room had a flat screen television with a wide variety of channels to choose from, a dresser, a worktable a clerical chair and an easy chair. The room also had a walk in wardrobe. The view from the window, which looked along Boylston Street, was very nice and the room was well soundproofed. The hotel offers a turn down service, which was a nice touch. The hotel has a restaurant and two bars. One of the Bars offers a small terrace from which it is nice to watch the passing pedestrians. I particularly liked the way the stairwell was carpeted and presented as a genuine alternative to the elevators, rather than as a distant and forgettable alternative.
The are some minor issues one is the air-conditioning – it is very much like a jet engine at the start of the take off run. However it is effective and can be managed by simply turning it off when the desired temperature is reached. My only quibble here is that when I pointed this out I was told it is an old hotel. I have stayed in 300 year old hotels, they nevertheless manage to have 21st century air-conditioning. The other is that there is no tea or coffee making facilities in the room. There is an interesting aspect to this hotel, it was the refrigerator – it is simply placed in the room, by itself, ah well.
All in all this is a very pleasant and helpful hotel. It has a nice feel to it. In terms of luxury, it is not quite there but then I did not stay in any of the suites that are offered so maybe I am being a little harsh. If I had to stay in the hotel again I would not be unhappy, I would however want to stay in an outside room of King standard or above.

title: “Great place !”
text:
Booked here for one night to visit Seattle. Had read mixed reviews . Gave it a try and dont regret it.
The first and immediate impression was a positive one. We were welcomed by a man at the reception named Peter . He deserves a mention : Kind, extremely helpful and a very nice person . I travel extensively and doesnt happen often to bump into people like that.
Room was extremely well furnished, care for details, very comfortable bed, breathtaking view, spotless , silent and comfortable. Location , for our needs , was perfect. Close to everything and not more than a ( pleasant ) 8/10 minute walk to the Marina . I will definetely return to the Roosevelt

title: “Excellent Airport Hotel”
text: It is clear that the rooms here have been upgraded recently and they did a fabulous job - comfortable, high quality bed, new carpet, nice furnishings, updated bathroom, etc. All the staff were very helpful and took care of all our needs. Shuttle to the airport was quick and convenient. We got this room off priceline for about $80/nt and it was definitely a great deal. I would highly recommend this hotel!

title: “Oubliez-ça!”
text:
We were "relocated" at the Orlando by another hotel.
The Orlando turned out to be a big disappointment and a real downgrade.
First it was not that easy to find after a long 500 mile drive as the hotel does not have a sign, so had to go around the block twice before finding it. The welcome we got from the valet was “Ah! "that" hotel sent you?. The Orlando you’ll see is MUCH better. Well it turned out to be MUCH worse. The staff at the reception was pompous and a bit arrogant, told us they were booked out and that they were doing us a great favour to have us (maybe this is why they put us in a room with a bathroom for the disabled?). The bed was uncomfortable, the bathroom not too clean. When, at breakfast, we asked for an orange juice at the usual Latino waiter, he brought me the check ...... We told him the breakfast was included, but no way; we had to face the front desk again and were told the breakfast was complimentary for one guest only (??) It was hard for them to understand we were two of us…finally they said ok, they would make an exception…wow!. The only good feature of this hotel was its fast internet connection and maybe the location, but there are other hotels in the area with far better service and price. This is no way a 4 star hotel. This is essentially a pretentious little dark joint trying to be a boutique hotel as we have in Europe. It’s a pity to waste money on The Orlando.Oubliez-ça! (forget it!).

title: “Dirty Floors”
text:
Booked a 3-day stay at this hotel. I spend a lot of time in various hotels and have never written a review. I am compelled to write this review, however, because of the shocking condition of the floors of this hotel. I knew things were not looking good when the common area floors were such a mess when I arrived. I honestly have never seen floors so dirty in even a 2-star hotel (this is allegedly a 3-star). I have never requested a room to be cleaned, but when I saw the condition of my floors when I arrived in my room, I did not want to even take my shoes off until something was done. Housekeeping promptly responded to the request and took care of some of the more obvious debris on the floor. I also knew I had done the right thing when it sounded like sand being sucked into the vaccuum when she swept some of the carpet. 
If it had not been for the fact that, in addition to the disgusting floors, my keycard did not work and the TV in the bedroom didn't work after "maintenacne had left for the evening" I would not have brought these issues to the attention of the manager the following day. But I did. The manager was very kind and apologetic and had the tv fixed that day. She further informed me that the housekeeping supervisor would be in my room that day to make sure it was clean. The amazing thing is (which is why I now have decided to write this review) was that the floors were still filthy when I returned to my room late in the day. I would have thought that after using such superlatives that "the floors of this hotel have to be the filthiest floors I've ever experienced in a hotel" and that the "Doubletree brand (a Hilton brand nonetheless) would suffer with such inattention to cleanliness", that the manager would have insured the floors of my room were thoroughly cleaned...did not happen. 
If you decide to stay at this hotel (and there are plenty of other reasons to stay at this hotel as many of the reviews point out) and if you have the same experience, I would not hesitate to have housekeeping sweep your floors or request another room until you find one with clean floors (if that is even possible in this hotel). If enough guests complain, maybe management at this hotel will figure out that something needs to be done to improve this situation.
Bottom line: If Doubletree cannot keep the floors clean, where else are they cutting corners on cleanliness?

title: “Typical Hilton Excellence”
text:
This hotel are part of history, one of the original Conrad Hilton major purchases when he was creating his empire. 
Keep that mind if you are seeking an ultra sleek and modern hotel, because this is one of the more classic Hiltons you will come across. 
Check in was wonderful; I am an HHonors and considering the size of the hotel I was very impressed to be checked in within five minutes of getting into line, they even delivered the package waiting for me directly to my room which was handy.
The hotel is huge; so most rooms are going to be a bit of a trek from the lobby and the signage is a little lacking if you don't enter from the main lobby door to find the elevator but once you have that figured it its pretty straight forward. 
My room configuration was a little strange as it was a rectangle with a king sized bed in the middle with two full bathrooms on either side, however the room was very functional and the new touchscreen hotel directory was simple enough to use to find the room service menu. 
The room still allowed for me to work at a desk, and the bed like with most Hiltons was consistent. 
The Room Service was something that was noteworthy,
I had dinner and breakfast in the room once, and both times they were delivered within 15 minutes and was fantastic both times. 
In terms of location, you really can't beat you are basically right in the thick of downtown and within walking distance of any number of restaurants and sights. 
Internet was pretty good considering the size of the hotel; I was expecting some questionable connection speeds but it was pretty average but certainly functional.

title: “Nice stay!!”
text:
Stayed one night for next day early flight. friendly staff, nice shuttle service, convenient location
Room was clean and quiet, bed quailty was great. I didn't hear much noise from the planes.
i will definite stay here again!!

title: “New York Spring Break 2011”
text: great location. clean room. comfortable bed. very helpful staff. wifi Internet weak in our room, probably a good thing, gave me an excuse for not checking my work emails.

title: “Good location, between Times Square & Central park - no frills accomodation”
text:
I am a frequent visitor to New York, and usually go without my daughter (age 9). She wanted to come this time, and her favorite places to visit in Manhattan are the carousel in Central Park, the Museum of Natural History & American Girl & FAO Schwartz. But, she also likes the buzz of Times Square. So, I picked the Wellington as it is half way walking between both areas, and spending less on accomodations aloows more of a budget for other spending.
This is a no frills hotel. Nothing fancy, but clean and comfortable. I booked a room through Priceline, and although I booked a queen bed, if we wanted an early check in (we had early flights in), we could settle for a double. We did this because in all honesty, you really just need a bed to crash in after a long day of walking in new York. The bed was comfortable and the room was clean.
Washrooms have full sized bathtub for soaking your feet at the end of the day, and water presssure for the shower was good. Hairdryers are in the washroom as well.
Like others here, I would not reccomend the diner in the hotel - overpriced and not that good. LOTS of supermarkets and delis on every corner.
Right by Carnagie Hall & across the street from The London (Gordon Ransay). Walking distance to everything else you need, and subway is out front.
Only downfall is the 3 small elevators. Very slow, and being on the 15th floor, it was often a long wait to get downstairs in the morning due to every elevator going down being full.

title: “Two fabulous and memorable staff members”
text:
I travel all over the world on business as I'm sure many of you reading this do and we all have horror stories to tell. BUT - I stayed at the SLS 2 weeks ago and Danielle and Aaron at the front desk could not have been more helpful, polite, professional and more fabulous if they tried!!! And it wasn't just at check in - over my 3 day stay, they remembered my name, said hello every time I passed by and were "consistent in providing great service". Whenever I'm in LA from now on - this is my "GO TO" hotel. 
Margaret McMahon

title: “wonderful helpful staff”
text: this hotel is in a great location, right on the riverwalk in san antonio...but the reason it stands out is due to the wonderful staff, especially Eddie, a bellman at the hotel. he genuinely wants to help people, answer any questions, provide suggestions so that you can enjoy your time in san antonio...we will definitely visit again.

title: “Amazing staff helped the last leg of our trip”
text: We stayed at the Carlton for 3 nights in Nov 2012. We had driven from Yosemite and arrived earlier than expected in SF due to the snow arriving in Yosemite. The reception staff were so helpful, knowledgable (and funny) and we were able to get into our room even though it was 1.15, check in is usually after 3 pm I think. They offered great advice on where to go (and not) We had a room on the 5th floor at the back. No view but the room was big, clean, really comfy large King bed, huge walk in closet, safe, good shower over a bath, lots of hot water and large tv with plenty of channels (although we didn't use this much). Yes the rooms are a little dated but this adds to the charm of staying in SF. They are quite noisy, but we found them to be quiet at night and got a great night's sleep. cleaned daily the maids were really courteous and helpful. It's a short 10 min walk to Union Square and there are plenty of bars, coffee shops, supermarkets and restaurants nearby. We ate in the resident restaurant Saha our first night (our road trip had caught up with us) and the food and service were excellent. It's Arabic fusion, with meze options as well. Good beer and wine selection too. They do not belong to the hotel but you can put the meal on your room if you want. The free wine mixer from 5.30pm was a nice touch and we took up the hop on/off bus tour with them. They were really helpful at organising taxis for us and we were getting a taxi to the airport but they organised their car service instead which was $50 (about the same price) More expensive than Bart but so convenient and we had budgeted for this anyway, only 20 min journey. I would stay at the Carlton again and would like to thank the staff , especially Emelie, for making it a pleasant stay.

title: “This is where you need to stay...”
text: The Alexis is where you need to stay. A perfect mix of on-the-spot location, simpering relaxation, classic style, elegant romance and you-come-first customer service. You won't regret it.

title: “Great little hotel in the heart of Lakeview/Lincoln Park area”
text: This is an older hotel, but we thought it was great. The staff was always cordial and greeted us each time we returned. We had a nonsmoking room with 2 double beds (room 420), and we had 2 full bathrooms - unheard of in any hotel I've stayed in. The bathrooms were small, but having two is a luxury when traveling with a teen. We did not have a car, this hotel was a short walk from the Diversey Station El, from Midway. The continental breakfast was great (eggs, bagels, muffins, donuts, yogurt, fruit, hot and cold cereal, sausage and bacon). They had a nice lobby and a secure door that always required a key to access the hallway leading to the rooms. We chose this hotel because our daughter lives within 2 blocks. It is in a wonderful area surrounded by restaurants, shops and residential areas. I was pleasantly surprised and I would definitely stay there again.

title: “Great friendly service”
text:
We recently stayed at the crowne plaza Beverley hills for 5 nights and were very happy with our stay there. Don't always believe the bad reviews it was not like the reviews I read before we booked. The staff were so helpful and friendly and should be commended on that! It is no trouble for them to even tell you the buses to catch...
Close to rodeo dr a very short walk in fact. Buses run from around the corner to all the major sites to see.
The rooms were great too. Bed huge and comfortable. Yes the bathrooms may be a bit outdated but seriously who spends that much time in there? Even the cleaning staff greeted you daily!
The gym is also great with fantastic equipment.
My only advice would be to double check you get nonsmoking at the desk before you go to your room because even though we'd booked this ours was not and we ended up with smoking and I thought too late to change once unpacked?? I'm an avid nonsmoker so we had to air the room out daily!
But overall a great place to stay!

title: “Great location, snobby staff & lukewarm shower”
text:
Booked this hotel as part of a package deal with British Airways for a good price. The hotel is in a great location - 2 min walk to Times Square, in the Broadway area, amazing pizza place next door.
The hotel lobby is impressive - grand lights, flowers, seating areas, cool club style music playing. The staff are not very friendly (especially compared to all the other nice people we met in NYC) and come across as quite snobby and stand-off-ish. I had emailed the hotel a few weeks before to which I had no reply. They also didn't have our booking (despite presenting them with a British Airways Hotel voucher). In the end it turned out they had made a spelling mistake. I also had to provide them with a credit card even though we had paid for the room in full via BA and had provided them with passports.
The room was small, which we had expected. However there were 2 of us and we only had a queen bed i.e. inbetween a single size & double!! V small!! There was just about enough room to put our two cases down! The bathroom was small, but supplied with towels and toiletries. Big down point though was that the shower was in an alcove, which meant the bathroom light didn't shine through - i.e you had to shower in the dark! :/ Even with the dial onthe highest setting the shower was lukewarm - not enjoyable.
That said the room was designed very pleasantly and was trendy. Flat screen TV on the wall with lots of channels.
You could hear the taxis, people etc when in your room, even at night, but that's to be expected when you pick a hotel very close to Times Square.
We used the luggage room when we had checked out, which was only $2 per bag and the bellboy flagged us a yellow cab for our ride back to the airport. (BTW we hopped in a yellow cab on the way to the hotel with no effort or queue). We used the safe in the room (free use) which was good.
Overall, a good location but I wouldn't recommend this hotel - don't be fooled by the fancy lobby.

title: “Not even worth rating, -5”
text: My husband & I stayed here a couple of weeks ago & were severly disappointed. First....we arrived in a lifted 4x4, they suggested we park 3-4 blocks away (they're not prepared for that even though we were in Seattle, really?). Second....they went ahead & accepted the truck, the valet could barely drive. Third....they say wine reception HA, they had wine glasses & no wine. Fourth....our room was so small (even when they said it was the largest they had) there's no way we could both move around at the same time. Fifth....when I went into the restroom there was dried blood on the door, can you say Bio-Hazard (gross). Sixth....I went down to retrieve something out of our truck only to find it with the passenger window down & every door unlocked (we had 2 Co. laptops in the backseat along with other professional goods, no to mention the truck itself). Lastly....when I brought the truck issue to the clerks attention, the best they could do was offer a budget breakfast from the in house coffee house. The next morning upon checkout I informed the manager on duty of ALL the complaints, he replied that the regional manager would be calling me about our aweful experience at their facility, 2 1/2 weeks later I still haven't heard from anybody! Don't waste your time or money. The best thing about this place is it's an easy walk downhill to the pier & all the wonderful things it has to offer! Good luck walking back uphill!

title: “Pleasently Surprised”
text:
After a day of cancelled flights and hot weather it was nice to be in a clean, modern hotel. We were greeted warmly and asked of our choice of room. Happy when door was opened, nice layout, clean room, frig worked and TV nice size. Hot water in the shower, clean bathroom! Only drawback is I thought breakfast was included and the pool was not too clean given that high school baseball teams were also staying and their parents didn't keep tabs on them. There were plastic bags and broken, shredded swimming noodles in the pool, yuck!
I will stay again later this year if they can keep the pool clean.

title: “Quality on B'way”
text: I'm surprised to read negative comments about this place. When I visited (May 10) we were RELIEVED to be placed in this hotel, after being told upon check-in at the Comfort Inn Central Park West (one of its "sister properties") that something was amiss with our room and they were moving us here. In addition to getting a Quality Inn for Comfort Inn rates :) we were placed on an upper floor and had a very quiet night. The only things I could fault: 1) a tear in one of the curtain liners let in sunlight about dawn; 2) a remodeling project was underway, and a lot of furniture was in the hallway. The staff was very polite. The hotel offers to keep luggage under lock and key so you can check out, shop, and not have to lug the stuff around town. The man who handles this lobby service was wonderful. It isn't the newest place in town but it is fine by my standards.

title: “Enjoyable Downtown Chicago Hotel”
text: My husband and I recently stayed at the Embassy Suites Hotel in downtown Chicago for 1 night. Our daughter attended a conference in Chicago and stayed here for 4 nights. All of us really enjoyed our stay. The rooms were very clean, comfortable and affordable. The hotel staff were all very friendly and the location was convenient to both restaurants and shopping. A 2 hour happy hour was offered each day. The breakfast was exceptional. Everything you could want was offered from made to order omlettes, pancakes, fruits, yogurts, oatmeal, bacon, cereal, bakery items and much more. And all was complimentary! We will definitely return.

title: “Noisiest Hotel Ever, Terrible Beds!”
text: First of all, there are some good things about this hotel. The location is excellent. The recent renovation is lovely and modern. The staff was friendly and even waived the internet fee for us upon request. However, the design of the building makes floors 1-5 an acoustical nightmare. Every noise in the atrium/lobby/bar below the guest rooms is amplified by a million. It doesn't help that the management insists on playing terrible techno-lounge music throughout the common areas from approximately 7 AM until midnight. All of this noise is funneled right into your guest room and can even be heard over the TV! I don't know how the Mariott could do a renovation without addressing this issue. Floors 6 and 7 are completely sealed off from the atrium, but 7 is the concierge level and I assume floor 6 is similarly reserved for specific guests. In addition to the noise, the bed was the worst I've slept on from a major hotel chain. Also, the Mariott is trying to pass off their de-commissioned old mini-fridges as "silent coolers" for "keeping cold items cold"--HAHA! Yeah, right! I had to load a plastic bag full of ice and put our leftovers on top to keep them cold. One other annoyance is that Mariott puts a $30 charge on your credit card for incidentals that may be used, yet they don't announce this upon check-in. The charge is still pending on my account three days after I checked out, although I was reassured today that I should be credited for a refund soon. All in all, I can't recommend this hotel unless you are able to pay for a room on the special quiet floors and don't mind a crummy bed. I'm only giving three stars because I got an OK deal on Priceline and the internet charge was waived. If I'd had to pay the usual rates, I'd be extremely disappointed.

title: “Best Location & Best Price Hotel in Boston!”
text:
The CharlesMark Hotel, a charming boutique hotel, is located in the heart of the Back Bay and costs a fraction of the price of other hotels. Right out the CharlesMark front door brings you to some of the best shops and restaurants on Boylston and Newbury Streets; there's Copley Square, Trinity Church, and the park at Copley Square; and across the street is the Boston Public Library. The CharlesMark has a better location than both the Westin or Copley Marriott hotels and costs a fraction of the price. The rooms are cozy and incredibly well-organized and nicely designed.
The staff is very friendly and helpful, and they let you in on all the "secrets" of enjoying Boston like a Bostonian, rather than steering you to over-priced tourist traps like other hotels. Staying at the CharlesMark makes you feel like a Bostonian (even though you're stay is temporary). Be warned though, the CharlesMark makes Boston so inviting and wonderful you might be tempted to move there! Basically, the CharlesMark is just a whole heck of a lot friendlier and more personal than other hotels.
Did I mention there's a great lounge downstairs? Well, yes, there is! The street-level lounge is cheery and well-lighted during the day (and includes a wonderul little outdoor patio with tables and chairs). In the morning the lounge hosts a FREE help-yourself continental breakfast of bagels and cream cheese, muffins, toast, fresh fruit, coffee, juice, etc. and basically has the pleasant ambience of a European pensione. In the afternnon it's a perfect place to come back and have a cool drink on the patio before heading to your room. At night the lounge becomes a hip Back Bay neighborhood place to have a drink at night. It's the perfect combination --- hip, friendly, and not loud at all (the lounge was active the nights we stayed, but when we got to our room, we didn't hear a thing and it was as quiet as a cabin in Vermont!).
And are you interested in the Boston Marathon? The CharlesMark is is situated exactly at the Boston Marathon finish line! What could be more convenient to runners and their families and spectators than that?!
All in all, the CharlesMark is a unique blend of charm, friendliness, utility, convenience, great location, and cost effectiveness. My only hesitation in publishing my review is that I don't want the hotel to be booked the next time I call to stay there --- and believe me, the next time we go to Boston, we'll be staying at the CharlesMark!
Vive la CharlesMark!

title: “R +R= Rest & Relaxtion”
text:
Ahh!
Finally a hotel that is both affordable and clean. 
This hotel is right off a major highway, but you hear none of the highway noise maybe because it sits back a bit from the Dallas, hustle and bustle.
The decor was nice and contemporary. 
The beds where comfortable and the linen was user friendly. No Polyester. 
The windows were nice and big, giving you a nice view of location.
They have a wonderful menu for light eating. 
Business center a little small, but private. 
The fitness center was bright and inviting. 
This hotel had just about it all, except a shuttle on Sunday.
Oh, let me mention they had smart rooms, conserving energy, meaning the a/c unit is activated by movement, so when there is no one in the room, the a/c goes off, but when there is movement or when the room is occupied it reactivates.

title: “Lovely vacation - great hotel”
text: My husband and I recently stayed at the Dupont Circle Hotel. We booked our vacation on short notice to celebrate my husband's birthday and found this hotel through Hotwire. The hotel was very centrally located with a nice selection of bars and restaurants in the area. It was also very close to the Metro. We were given a room with two double beds the first night due to lack of available rooms and our third party booking but were switched to a King room the following morning. We did run into a snag partway through our trip but the hotel dealt with the issue very quickly and effectively. We had a problem with our room. While it was being looked after, we were offered drinks at the hotel bar and were later provided with dinner at the hotel restaurant where we had a lovely meal. Mistakes can sometimes happen but I think the mark of good service is in part how quickly and effectively a service provider deals with that mistake. In our case, the hotel staff, particularly the manager of guest relations, Ms. Cole Kelly, was cordial, gracious and made sure we were well looked after. Overall, I have nothing but good things to say about this hotel and would have no hesitation booking a further stay here if we return to DC.

title: “Fine, but don't expect too much”
text:
This is a very nice Victorian building in a very decent location. The staff is friendly and helpful. The hotel is in desperate need of a renovation. Most of the furniture is old and worn out (not antique, just old). There are extension cords running all over in order to power the lamps ect. (hardly any place to plug-in a computer or charger). Say a small prayer when you get in the elevator - fortunately walking up the stairs is a good option. The decor is "I love Victorian, especially when I can decorate my whole place by shopping in second hand stores and making it look charming-ish"
The real message comes across at "Breakfast". The cheapest most poorly presented "food" I've had in a long time. There is granola and the coffee is ok. Those are the high points. Peanut butter and grape jelly on Wonder Bread is the theme here.

title: “One of our all time favorites!”
text: What a find! We've stayed three times now and it's an amazing place to stay. Just outside your door is a ferry over to the Inner Harbor, so the location is ideal. The rooms are large and VERY comfortable. They gave us a bottle of wine when we checked in. The continental breakfast in the lobby is lovely. It's a romantic inn, more of a B & B than a hotel. The Harbour view room is worth the extra few dollars but a courtyard view is just as comfortable, and nice and dark (we are early risers and still slept till 10:00!). Can't say enough about it.

title: “Super-friendly”
text: Although the hotel lies on the edge of a dodgy district of San Francisco, we had no problems getting to and from the hotel during our stay. Even though we chose to avoid certain streets around the hotel, it was still easy walking distance to many parts of San Francisco, so the location was perfect for us.We found the Phoenix to be a bright, colourful, clean, cool place to stay, with a great newly-opened bar/restaurant, free parking (a bonus) and SUPER-friendly and helpful staff.

title: “Great location; great inclusions”
text:
Staybridge suites is located west 40th street between 8th and 9th. We picked the location because of its proximity, close to the Theatres, close to Times Square, walk or subway ride to other attractions and department stores.
It was clean and well appointed with two double beds, a kitchenette (a fridge was wonderful to have) included breakfast and a laundry. We were on the 31st floor so waiting for the lift wasn't an issue. We would highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Surprised they are voted #1 in area.”
text: We stayed two days for a work function. Our room was clean but the air didn't work which left the room hot and humid. TV didn't work In one room. The staff wasn't sure on the location of some of our functions. Overall I'm not impressed.

title: “upscale convention type hotel”
text: Hotel was very comfortable ith a great bed ,bathroom was marble with dual shower heads, we had a riverview room that was recommended to avoid street noise, room was still noisy from street traffic. one of my reasons for not giving a 5 star rating was because there was no free wi-fi in the guest rooms,the other is that they charge for everything, bottled water,business computer use , a cash bar inthe room i'm suprised they don't charge for tv, thats ok if you are there on business and charge everything to yur expense account,been there, done that ,now that I am retired I pay for everything. On the plus side the restaurant on the premises,ZOCCA, was excellent, the wait staff was great,they made us feel like special guests every time we went there, the food was also excellent.

title: “Great Hotel for a Business Trip to Dallas”
text: First and foremost, the staff at Aloft in Dallas is top notch. I stayed there for a week long business trip at the Dallas Convention Center (0.5 miles away) and I had nothing but the most exceptional customer service experience. My room was perfect. Everything is laid out exactly how I would have done it. The amenities were great. The atmosphere was superb. The WXYZ bar in the lobby was first-class. Their onsite parking was only $10.00/night which is far less than any of the other hotels around and the site is within walking distance of everything. I've stayed at a number of other Aloft hotels around the country and this one is by far the best. I will stay here again.

title: “Hello? 1985 called and wants their hotel back.”
text:
After I won a "3.5 star hotel" on Priceline and read the reviews I realized I was in a classic trap... Priceline rated this hotel much higher than is realistic and I couldn't cancel. So, I took it like a man and stayed there.
This property is a Crowne Plaza in name only. I got the hotel for $40 ($55 with taxes and fees), and I guess you get what you pay for. But never again.
Location: terrible. Tucked back in an industrial/office complex that's as outdated as the hotel. In an older part of town that's a little scary.
Staff: friendly. The night crew reminded me of the Ghostbusters but it was clear they were doing the best they could.
Rooms: Not good. Wall-to-wall worn and outdated. Not "dirty" per se, but cracked, peeling wallpaper, nasty doors, old furniture and drapery, damaged countertops, worn bathtubs, etc.

title: “Just an average hotel”
text:
The price was fair. 
The earliest check in time is 1:00pm. I arrived at the hotel around 4:00pm. At that time the room was not ready, so I had to wait there for about 20 minutes to let them get the room ready. 
Hotel website:
http://www.lq.com/lq/properties/propertyProfile.do?ident=LQ921&propId=921

title: “So so...”
text:
Can't make up my mind about this place. I booked through Priceline and got a 'good' rate for NYC. Good: location (within walking distance of what we needed to see), price good, pleasant staff (very responsive when we complained AC didn't work).
Bad: room location. 2nd floor facing 62nd St VERY busy/noisy, VERY well light street. I had tried to call for 3 days before arriving to see if we could get higher floor/facing river and no one answered the phone...ever. Told upon arrival that phone system was down, right before they interrupted our check in to answer the phone. No alarm clock, coffee pot in the room which we wouldn't have used anyway. Tub didn't drain all the way which meant tub looked dirty all the time, impossible to not flood the bathroom the way the shower was set up. I thought the bed was very uncomfortable (full size) but husband and daughter slept like logs. Jack hammering started at 7:30 on Sunday morning which i know the hotel has no control over but would have not been an issue if we had been on a higher floor. 
In a nutshell, really good location for our needs, price good but not sure if the rest makes up for it?

title: “Nice, affordable and clean with a friendly, accommodating staff. My third stay while moving my son in and out of his first year”
text: The staff is really friendly and courteous. The rooms have always been very clean and comfortable. Had an issue with noise from an adjoining room during this stay that was quickly resolved by the front desk. Well worth the affordable price.

title: “Great location but...”
text:
Nice hotel with very friendly staff. However, I did not receive my wakeup call (I always set my phone to wake up mode). Things like this happen but still in all...
Room was nice but a little cramped. They had just cleaned the carpets and the smell was a little strong. 
Good breakfast area and food the next morning. Price was I felt it was a little high $186 for one night but the location just two miles from the airport...well you make the choice.

title: “Great hotel that offers much!”
text: Our large group (79 high school students, 41 adults) stayed at the Embassy Suites LAX North at the tail end of a mission trip to Mexico. We wanted a place to meet, relax and have a little fun, and we were not disappointed. The rooms were so spacious and nice, the breakfast was fabulous (everyone loved the selection), and there was plenty of room for our large group to meet and hang out. When we didn't have enough chairs in our meetting room, the hotel staff very quickly fixed the problem. The only problem we encountered was when my poor husband was sick with a cold and had to stay back (the rest of the group went to the beach and dinner). He tried to call for room service, but nobody ever answered the phone! But, aside from that, we would stay there again.

title: “Great location”
text: Second visit to the Manhattan Club. Both times we went with concerns after reading reviews. We had no real problem. We asked for an outside room which we were given. Only problems were that room was a bit stuffy so we had to open the windows. Also, there was no bedside table with a reading lamp on one side of the bed. We requested a floor lamp, but they wee unable to find one. The elevators were not a problem and our interactions with the staff were all fine

title: “A great value hotel in the uber-expensive NYC”
text: It's not easy to find a safe and high quality hotel in NYC for an affordable price. Club Quarters Downtown is a great hotel if comfort, a convenient location and good value are what you're looking for. Located less than a minute away from a subway station, the hotel is in the financial district. Certainly, there's not a lot to do in the financial district as a tourist and you'll have to either walk or take the subway to the midtown area to see the sights, but armed with a subway pass, this hotel is perfectly located. The area is quiet at night, but very safe, so no worries there. The rooms are very clean, modern and aesthetically pleasing. The service is fine, and the hotel also has free internet on the ground floor. I would definitely recommend Club Quarters Downtown.

title: “Ruined honeymoon, left crying!”
text: We live in Denver and thought it would be neat to stay in the icon Brown Palace for our honeymoon, we were wrong. The room was really outdated, and for a suite compared to a discount chain. The air conditioning didn't work. So at this point we were just disappointed, then we ordered room service. They said it would be up in twenty minutes, twenty five minutes we called to ask where our food was, my husband was rudely treated, the lady snapped "I told you a half hour" and hung up on us.
