When the food finally came the waitress told us she heard both phone calls and we were told twenty minutes, not thirty and that we shouldn't be treated that way and the lady was rude and wrong. On top of that my eggs were overcooked. Some way for a "world class" hotel to treat its patrons. I left the hotel crying!

title: “Wonderful customer service, spacious jr. suite near everything!”
text: In the heart of Union Square, we always go to this hotel to experience wonderful customer service, spacious and lovely junior suite and the nearness of everything fun!

title: “Great location and that's about it”
text: Huge hotel, too much wait at the elevators, long hallways. Good breakfast though, ask for a room near the elevators.

title: “Charming hotel with excellent service!”
text: I can't say enough about how much I enjoyed my stay at the Dunhill. The staff really went out of their way to make us feel so welcome--it really reminded me of good southern hospitality at its best. My friends and I met in Charlotte for a girls weekend and also to celebrate my upcoming wedding. Upon our arrival to the hotel, there was a handwritten note to me from the staff at the Dunhill offering their congratulations and best wishes. I was so impressed by such personal service and attention to detail! Everyone we ran into at the hotel--from the waitstaff at the restaurant to the front desk staff to the housekeeping staff--was so friendly and accommodating (I forgot my toothbrush and one was brought up to me immediately.) And there was a lovely historic charm to this hotel that made it very special and unique. Our rooms were very clean and comfortable. I stayed in the penthouse suite and the views of the city from the TWO balconies were really quite magical. We found the Dunhill to be in a prime location in downtown Charlotte with lots to see and do just right around the corner from the hotel. And the breakfast was so delicious (they have the best home fries!). A sincere thank you to the staff at the Dunhill for making my stay so enjoyable! I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone planning a trip to Charlotte.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: I stayed Sept. 24-26, 2012. The hotel staff were very, very nice and the check-in process was quick and easy. The room was very beautiful, clean and very comfortable. The hotel is very, very close to the BWI airport. The hotel is little old. It could use a few new touches, a little updating. Otherwise I was very pleased.

title: “Hard Rock Anniversary”
text:
We went to Chicago for our 21st anniversary and had a wonderful stay at the Hard Rock Hotel. The beds are excellent! The room was clean and very well maintained throughout our stay. The atmosphere is very contemporary, which was the opposite of what we normally experience, but it was fun to try something new. The one drawback was the lobby turned lounge in the evenings. It is a hang out spot for yuppies and lots of partying and making out is going on. We avoided this by using the side entrance on Michigan Avenue when entering and exiting the hotel in the evenings. The staff was helpful and courteous. 
Located on the Magnificent Mile with access to some of Chicago's wonderful sights, we'd definitely stay there again.

title: “It's as good as the best reviews”
text:
I must have read all the reviews placed here for the last 6 months, and I can say that The Michelangelo Hotel in Midtown Manhattan is as good as the best reviews. Our room had a marble foyer, and an all-marble deepbathroom and dressing room. The shower/bathtub was deep...up to my knees, and I'm 5'9". 
Every night, they came in for turn-down service, and pulled-down BOTH sets of window shades, and emptied the trash. 
This felt like a 4 star hotel, but we paid like a 2 star hotel, considering that it was summer vacation in New York City. 
I would stay there again.

title: “Belvedere is Best”
text: I chose the Belvedere after reading all the comments posted, along with the great rating of 26/324 reviews! It met every need and expectation for me (and my sister and our daughters). Staff is friendly, and the rooms are beautiful, large, and clean. We had great water temperature and pressure. It included a fridge, microwave, hairdryer, iron and board, and air conditioning that worked well. We were in walking distance to the theatre distict, Today Show, Times Square, and had marvelous food all around us. The price was $190 on week days, $220 on the weekend. Taxes jack the price up, but I believe all hotels charge these. If we had had a AAA membership, rates would have been lower. I definitely would go back!

title: “Tired and dirty”
text: Common areas of hotel are tired, but room was both dirty and tired. Iron burn marks on the carpet. Missing parts in tub. Faucet in bathroom broken, sink would not drain. Water leak in room, called maintenance, not sure if they fixed. They placed a large fan in room to dry carpet. Fan was running when I came back to room prior to dinner. Called front desk and questioned them about it. They said they would have it fixed prior to me returning to the room for the evening. They did not remove the fan. It was still blowing when I returned, carpet still wet. No follow up from staff. They offered extra hhonors points, but shold have offered a new room when they were unable to remedy the situation in short order. Disappointed in this Hilton Hotel.

title: “Terrific Stay”
text: 5 block walk from Grand Central, hotel staff were very welcoming. Cleanliness, comfort, and amenities of room were all top notch. Though exercise room is temporarily closed, hotel renovations did not affect us. Some decent restaurants within 1-2 blocks; fashion district very near.

title: “Family and F1”
text:
Fabulous hotel in which me and my husband stayed on two different occasions during this 2 week trip.
The first room was great (9th floor) and the second (18th floor) was fantastic! Coffee maker in both rooms, good gym on the lobby level, a small swimming pool on the roof - just big enough to get some exercise.
We joined the Select guest program which gave us free WIFI and coffee in the morning, along with other perks we did not use this time.

title: “AWESOME value for NYC !!”
text: Always the choice for our money in NYC. LARGE rooms with kitchenettes, central location on 40th St. Friendly staff, etc-etc. Real nice homey vibe to property....if you want modern chain hotel chic & plushness go pay $400 / nite at the regular big names with their homogenized rooms, points, etc.

title: “Brand New Marriott - Awesome location”
text: Wow! What a great hotel. All the bells and whistles situated downtown. Steps from Lucas Oil stadium and so much more. But what really makes this hotel stand it is the staff. They go above and beyond - they are friendly, courteous, and always helpful. Food / Roomservice excellent. Museums, galleries and a great zoo all very close.

title: “Comfortable Stay”
text:
I stayed with a friend this past weekend (August 9th-11th) and had an enjoyable stay overall. Our suite was on the 4th floor and was appointed as noted on their website. Our room did have a chlorine smell of sorts, but it was tolerable. There were also red stains on the inside of one of the lampshades and stains on the door. The bathroom and bedding were spotless though and those are the most important things to me.
The staff that I dealt with were friendly, but the front desk employees were rather aloof on two seperate occassions. During checkout, the woman got distracted easily and started helping other guests while I stood there waiting for help with my bill. Also, I repeated my request numerous times. Again, not a big deal but we were in a hurry to leave and something that should've taken 2 or 3 minutes to do instead took 15.
I loved the in-room microwave and refrigerator. Very helpful! Also, two televisions were great. The pool area was very nice and we enjoyed the hot tub. We would have liked to use the outdoor pool but it was actually too cold! 
The location of the hotel was great. It only took us about 15 minutes to get to Easton and just a little bit longer to get into Columbus. Also, there were plenty of restaurants near the hotel and a movie theater right across the street.
When visiting Columbus I generally prefer to stay in downtown but if the city is sold out again (as it was this time) I wouldn't hesitate to stay at the Sheraton Suites again.

title: “Nice but need work”
text:
Our last stay at the Westin was a normal room on the 12 floor near the Executive lounge that offers free internet,coffee and tea. You can access the Lounge with your room key. Since they did not have a suite they gave us free breakfast as a platinum member. Our previous stay was a suite with a separate room for the bedroom. Both rooms have the same decor and I would expect a larger bathroom in the suite. The Westin needs an upgrade. There dinning area is nice, but nothing to write home about. I wish they had a hotel in the PV area or south bay. Reservation desk was friendly. Arriving at the hotel they do seem like they have something better to do then assist you with luggage or greeting you.
The separate check-in area for card members is nice when the main reservation desk is busy and it seem to be extremely busy when we are there.

title: “Room 936 is a dirty dump, a Sheraton in name only”
text:
I arrived at 2am and was exhausted so didn't do my usual room inspection before saying yes and moving my luggage in...what a mistake. Dirt on the bathroom floor, high miscellaneous hair count (not mine) mold and mildew all over show tiles, burns on carpet, left over hairpins on floor, desk chair was a refuge from banquet dept., easy chair had huge tears on both arms, and the carpet hasn't been properly vacuumed in some time. I called the manager's office and housekeeping sent a supervisor who called it "appalling" and moved me to another room. I asked, "who supervises the work the maids do?" Three people cover 600 rooms so they are too busy to deal with many problems. Nobody seems to care in this hotel and it is full of bus tour and airline staff guests who have no other choice so they can get away wit h calling this shabby shack at Sheraton. It's like a roadside motel stacked up 22 floors high.
Wisely the hotel did not charge me for my night in room 936. Stay elsewhere the Sheraton NY Towers across the street is a completely different experience. Will I consider Four Points by Sheraton for another stay, anywhere? Heck no.

title: “Warwick was fabulous”
text:
The Warwick was a great hotel...stayed there for business and pleasure. the location is fabulous--West 54th and 6th Ave. the hotel's front desk and bellmen (never saw an actual "conceirge") were tremendously helpful and very nice. The bar, Randolph's, was great. the staff there took care of us, were very friendly. good wine list. food was also scrumptuous. 
The room was wonderful: clean, and huge. Comfortable bed. Note, however, I ended up getting an upgrade (had originally booked "superiour room", the lowest end). My friend was given a room like that, and it was not up to par: it was clean, she said, but curtains were torn and it was quite small (to me, NYC rooms are expected to be small; but, worn furnishings for $300/night is not acceptable). Although they were pretty booked, they moved her to an executive room (like the one I had) with no hesitation.
Very friendly and accomodating staff, clean hotel, great location...i will definitely stay here again.

title: “Fantastic hotel close to everything”
text:
My Mom and i just got back from a wonderful 3 night stay at this very welcoming hotel. I have been to NYC many times but this stay was the best so far. We were sent a lovely email before we even arrived with the offer of assistance prior to our arrival, which was a very nice touch.
From the moment we arrived we felt very welcome and safe, which is very important when travelling with my Mom.
The hotel staff were wonderful, offering assistance during a very busy time of the year. The location is walking distance to everywhere. The hotel is very clean, quiet and modern.
I would definitely stay there again in the future and would not hesitate to recommend to anyone !! Great job Hilton Garden Inn Times Square family !!

title: “Incredibely helpful stuff!”
text:
The most friendly and helpful staff one could imagine in a hotel. Why? Our flight out of New York was at 6:00 am from La Guardia. Although we haven't booked a room for this last night, we could spend the night in the hotel, including the key to the gym where we could take a shower (towels provided by the staff) and resting for some hours in the hotel lobby. We did not expect this at all! Thanks!!!! 
Would chose no other hotel, great value for money!

title: “Fabulous location in Mid-town Manhattan”
text:
Beautiful hotel with impeccable service by “The Club” employees located in the heart of midtown. We tried to get a 1 br but could only get a studio and I was expecting the equivalent of a typical, small New York City hotel room. Boy was I surprised! Room 3805 was may have only been a studio but it was larger than the hotel rooms on the lower floors. It wasn’t huge, but by New York City standards it was quite large and we had plenty of room. 
Pros: King size bed- very comfortable
 Flat Screen TV
 Luxurious robes!!!
 Big spacious shower (no tub in studios) with 3 shower heads!
Cocktail hour – hot hors d'oeuvre, iced water, tea, coffee and lots of wine, cheese, crackers
Continental breakfast - great selection of cereals, coffee, tea and espresso, fruit, bagels, croissants, muffins, different types of bread for toast, butter, cream cheese, jams, yogurt, hard boiled eggs and I’m sure more I’m forgetting 
Free wi-fi – practically unheard of these days!
Excellent large (and largely unused) fitness center on the 5th floor free of charge
Close to all the subway lines
Walkable to theaters – we walked to some and took taxi ($6-7) to others. Also walkable to Central Park, MOMA, Radio City, Rockefeller Center 
The Hilton Club desk employees are very helpful
Cons:
 Mini refrigerator already stocked with their items which you must pay for
 Slow elevators – leave early and plan on waiting
 Bathroom counter space was very limited
 Both sink and shower drainage was very slow
 Parking is $51/night – OUCH! We had a car for 1 night.
Our little bar fridge was fully stocked with soda, water, beer and you will be charged if you remove something. There was a little room for us to put in a few bottled waters, but unfortunately you can’t put leftovers in. 
I will definitely stay here again. I have trade requests in for next May!

title: “Great Japantown location, good japanese food, but shabby, tired rooms”
text: 2 nights in 'deluxe' King. The only deluxe item appeared to be the bidet toilet. All Japanese hotels provide kimono & slippers - except this one! Paint peeling prolifically in the bathroom, no basin plug, bath faucet would not seal when showering - wasting precious LA water! Breakfast restaurant poor - 'hot' items were lukewarm, however evening restaurant was very good. Japantown has safe sidewalks, many good Japanese restaurants, supermarkets, shops and museums nearby. Staff were friendly, most speak Japanese. Would definitely return if rooms were refurbished.

title: “The Crowne need's a polish”
text: Had to stay here because everything in the core if uptown was sold out. Below average for location because it's not next door to the uptown offices and restaurants. If you want to eat at a decent restaurant it's a cab or free shuttle ride. Beds are clean and comfortable...but overall the place is in need of some TLC and deep cleaning. Black mold stains in the shower grout, soiled and rippled hall carpets, tired and dated room furniture, and elevators that are filthy are all indicators that the Crowne is tarnished. And when's the last time you stayed in a hotel room with a tube TV and not a high def flat panel? The on site restaurant is probably okay for a burger and fries...but dinner entrees must be food service concoctions that are about as tasty as frozen meals from the freezer section of the grocery store. Overall the place isn't horrifying ... But needs some scrubbing and polish.

title: “Great Hotel!”
text: I stayed at The Ballantyne Hotel for a 5 day business trip. The hotel is beautiful. The rooms are large, comfortable, very clean and very nicely appointed -especially the bathroom. There is also a roomy desk to work at. The turndown service at night was a nice touch- they put light classical music on, dim lighting and of course, chocolates on the pillow. The housekeeping was perfect. The restaurant has very good food and beverages. For a change, the amenities looked exactly like the website pictures! The staff is extremely friendly and helpful. The pool was lovely - clean, comfortable chaises, light cabana music playing and food & beverage service. The few negatives I could note would be that the hallways were very noisy, it seemed like housekeeping was cleaning rooms around the clock. If I were in my room at 4-6 pm working or resting it was very distracting, I was sure there was construction going on in a nearby room or something that's how loud it was. Also, late at night there was a lot of noise in the hallways, banging doors, etc. I brought earplugs so I was not disturbed but my coworker had a hard time sleeping. There is a spa, I did not indulge but my coworker went for a pedicure and a haircolor. The pedicure was very nice (and very expensive) but they were seriously limited in color choices from what she said. Also, she was extremely unsatisfied with her hair color (also very expensive) and felt the person who did it was not skilled at all so beware! The other thing to note is that aside from the lobby bar, there is only one restaurant in the hotel so we did dine out at a nearby southwestern grille and it was very good. The concierge was most helpful in making recommendations. All in all, it was a treat to stay at The Ballantyne Hotel and I would recommend it.

title: “Great Staff-- Great Stay!!!”
text: Our stay was delightful...we arrived a few days early for our family cruise...Lauren, at the main desk, went out of her way to make our stay the best. When our family arrived, Lauren again had all the details taken care of so that our stay and transportation to and from the cruise went very smoothly... There were 17 of us...including toddlers...I can't tell you how much we appreciated all the extra TLC...I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone....Those responsible for transporting us to the cruise ship were so helpful ...Truly this staff is one of the best...

title: “Park & Fly was a winner!”
text:
We stayed at this Holiday Inn one Friday night in July 2006. It was easy to find and conveniently located to I-10 and the PHX airport. It was in a safe area full of businesses and other hotels however (besides a Waffle House) there is not much to eat within walking distance. But a quick ride up the street or on the interstate and that problem is resolved. 
Our top floor room was nice and clean with comfy beds and pillows. The bathroom was above average as it was clean, adequately-sized, and stocked with higher-end sample products. The A/C pumped a lot of cool air to offset the Phoenix heat outside. 
We didn't have our laptop and we didn't need to use the internet while we were there so we don't know what they provide onsite.
The staff was very professional and kind. My wife dropped her full cup of coffee on the floor while they were setting up breakfast at 6:00 AM. The attendant on hand came over, cleaned things up, and did so with a smile. The breakfast was slightly above average for a continental given all of the choices - bagels, muffins, cereals, yogurt, bananas, choice of milk, brownies, etc. 
The biggest plus for this hotel is the park and fly program. We booked this room at a rate we were happy with and it included a roundtrip to the airport via the hotel's shuttle. This saves big bucks on parking of course as you can keep your car at the hotel in one of their (very tight) courtesy parking spots. Be nice and tip your driver - he can get you there within 10 minutes or so provided you are not flying during rush hour. The shuttle runs every 30 minutes from early AM to late PM. 
Our only complaint was that the hotel's complimentary happy hour couldn't be extended a little beyond 7:45 as we just missed out on a round of drinks. Oh well - can't have it all! 
Anyway, this hotel was a nice find and we will gladly stay there again in the future whenever we fly from PHX.

title: “Terrible Experience!”
text: Had a horrible experience--coming from a person who stays in hotels 6 times minimum a year. As soon as I walked in I smelled a combination of an old person and cigarettes. It was appalling. After forcing myself to sleep, I yet smell more smoke coming from the linens. I felt as if I was sleeping in a run down motel. It was disgusting. The carpet was dirty and stained. The tile in the bathroom was falling out and clearly was not put in correctly. There was hair on the floor in the bathroom. The faucets were old and dirty. The hotel needs serious renovating. To make matters worse, we waited for the shuttle that never came for over 25 minutes. We had to pay a cab $20 for a 1 minute drive to the hotel. Will NOT recommend this hotel to anyone. I was excited to leave in the morning and luckily it was an overnight stay as I connected to another flight in the airport. NOT worth the high amount of money paid. I ignorantly booked the room after reading some FALSE praises. GARBAGE!

title: “Good price and location”
text: As others have mentioned, we were worried about this hotel after reading some bad reviews. We were only staying one night after a concert and was looking for location and affordability; not a 5 star hotel as we would not be in the room for long. The room was not a renovated room but it was clean. The bathroom was clean and had plenty of towels. The only really bad problem we had that was worth complaining about were the pipes knocking in the morning when others in the building were running water. That was an unpleasant sound to wake up to at 6am. Other than that, it was an o.k. stay. Hotel is walking distance from practically everything in Times Square. Not bad for the price you pay. Don't go expecting a lot...go open minded and have fun in New York!

title: “Nice Place to Stay”
text:
My husband and I stayed for 2 nights at the Topaz hotel two weeks ago and really enjoyed our stay. The staff was friendly, the room was pretty big, and this was a great location for us. I certainly agree with everyone on the beds, they were so comfortable!
I did a lot of research before picking where to stay and I was happy that we picked such a great place.

title: “Fantastic boutique hotel!!”
text: We spent 4 nights in NYC, with our adult children and their spouses. Everyone loved the hotel. Their European breakfast was delicious. The staff was not only friendly, they were caring and made you feel that they were there just to help you and make you happy. We all would definitely stay at The Library again. We found the location very convenient.

title: “Worst Hotel in America”
text:
Recently my family and I had the worst stay of our lives at the Phoenix Radisson.
We arrived at the Radisson in Phoenix, AZ (3600 N 2nd Ave; Phoenix, AZ 85013) on February 13, 2011 and stayed until February 21, 2011. My husband and I travel for a living (on the road 24/7) so we fly our parents in to see us in different cities each year. This year, we booked our room at the Radisson (huge mistake) thinking that it would be a relaxing, upscale hotel. 
Online it states that every room is equipped with a coffee maker, mini fridge, and microwave along with other things. This is important because we bring our own food.
Upon arrival at the hotel, my parent's reservations were not found. It took about 30 minutes of phone calls to me and research for the front desk staff to find their reservations. Once in, their room had no washcloths, coffee maker (but the coffee was there), and no mini fridge. They called down to ask for replacement items but they said they were out and they had to stay in this room.
For the first few days of our stay we did not have washcloths and housekeeping was extremely rude--I would try to say hi and ask how their day was going and they would speak in Spanish to each other and completely ignore me; then they didn't even show up some days.
What topped the experience was two nights before I was scheduled to leave, housekeeping CLEARED MY ROOM! Imagine arriving "home" at 2 am to a completely empty room! My retainers, $100 toothbrush, supersized bottle of brand new mouthwash, underwear, bra, etc missing. My key still worked and my room was empty.
In conclusion, this was the WORST hotel that I have ever stayed in. I do not look forward to coming back to Phoenix for a week next year and will never stay at a Radisson hotel ever again since my experience with this hotel.

title: “Better than expected”
text:
Great experience from the beginning. People were very friendly and helpful from booking reservation to the valet car service leaving the hotel. New hotel and very clean and modern. Comfy feather beds and roomy bathrooms with all the amenities. Consierge was very helpful booking the dinner reservations. Great location just three blocks from the Magnificient Mile but without the congestion. Wonderful experience. 
I'll recommend it to all my friends traveling to Chicago.

title: “5 day visit”
text:
We always stay here when in DC; close to museums and metro. Although there is restaurant and lounge in the hotel, you will have to travel by metro, cab or walk to DC restaurants. 
 Staff is always friendly and professional.

title: “"Run Run Run away from this Place"”
text: This is not a hotel,just bar with rooms. The staff (with the exception of the busboy and maid service)at this hotel is the least attentive group of KIDS I have ever dealt with. Most of the time they just argue with you instead of providing service, that is if you could get their attention. During our stay we had a WOW room for $325 a night. Our TV did not work and it took 3 phone calls and a trip to the front desk to get it fixed. A strange thing happened...the water was brown for the first day. We had several friends with us in other rooms and they had the same. Also don't expect because you are a guest that you will get to use the facilites. The roof bar and pool as well as the outside bar was closed 2 of the 3 days because of private parties. Answer we got from the front desk when telling them of our disappointment was "You pay for the Room not the Facilities". All but one meal required that we sit for 20 minutes before anyone even acknowledged us. Service in the restaurant & bar (pool bar) was very slow and seemed unconcerned, even though the food was good. The decor is cool and fun, a nice change from most hotels. Otherwise nothing more than chic facades and a heavy dose of LA attitude. .

title: “Nice hotel on the west side - top service”
text:
Conveniently located near metro stop and Central Park. Next to Riverside Park this is a quiet area. Price for the location is very good and the staff were very friendly and helpful.
Nice hotel for families as well.

title: “SUPERB!”
text: My husband and I are fortunate enough to travel frequently and it has been a while since we have come across a hotel that ticks all the boxes. The hotel/rooms/facilities are lovely but the Staff are the jewels in the crown. Everyone we met were friendly, helpful, professional and not obsequious - very genuine. I would not like to single out anyone in particular , as Im sure it is a team effort. Fantastic.

title: “Good short stop-over hotel”
text: I chose this hotel for its convenience, also it is relatively affordable for SPG members. The hotel is overall very good, I can't complain and would definitely be back since I usually stay for a short business trip.

title: “Huge surprise - great hotel that exceeded our expectations”
text: Booked Hotel Del Sol for a family vacation based on mostly positive reviews on Tripadvisor.com. We spent 8 nights at the hotel and were very happy with our stay. The room was clean and maid service prompt every day. The Marina District location was excellent - walking distance to Fisherman's Wharf with a ton of restaurants within a 5 minute walk. The staff was attentive, friendly and helpful. I had read mixed reviews on the breakfast and the pool size but breakfast was fine - coffee, OJ, bagels, pastries and the pool was big and deep enough for us to swim lengths and it was salt water - no chlorine! Add in the complimentary parking, movies for our kids and hi speed internet and we found this hotel a great overall value - would absolutely stay there again.

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
My girlfriend and I (along with my brother and his girlfriend) stayed here a week ago for two nights before an Alaskan cruise (we are all in our mid-twenties). The Ace was perfect for our situation: great location, very reasonably priced and no unnecessary amenities. The room was small, but we did not care as we were only in the room to sleep. Also, the "shared" bathrooms were just fine, very clean with no wait (great shower products too!). Ed at the front desk (I believe that was his name) is an incredible person. Not only was he extremely courteous and friendly, but he also "went above and beyond." Next time I am in Seattle, I will most certainly return to the Ace. And the coffee was great!
Thanks Ed!
- David

title: “Simply Excellent!”
text: I travel all over the U.S. staying at top hotels. They're all pretty much the same. The Graduca is at the top of my list for Outstanding service and comfort. Excellent from curb, to Front Desk, to Housekeeping, to the resturant. It's quiet and "comforable" at all points. Great beds, smiling faces, and very clean. If you want to find some little point where they could be better, I am sure you could, but if your don't try to find something and just allow yourself to enjoy, this is a fine place to do it. TOP KUDO'S to the Concierge "Kelly". She was Excellent with a capital E. I totally recommend the Granduca, I will be back and I make it my personal FIVE STAR "Houston's Best".

title: “Excellent Custom House”
text:
Stayed here end of March early April for a week end with 2 children.
Very impressed with the hotel and the location.
Staying with children for a week end we did not worry about the lack of full blown restaurant facilities as we got what we needed for breakfast across the road and used the mini kitchen in the room. 
Next time in Boston I will be staying in this hotel.

title: “Great weekend stay”
text: I went here with a group of 10 for the weekend. We were in town to visit the city and attend the Browns vs. Cowboys game. The hotel location is good. It is just a short cab ride to many of the great spots to visit. The hotel restaurant and bar is very nice. The rooms are very spacious and clean. Definitly recommend the Renaissance.

title: “Nice Hotel”
text: Stayed here from 8th May - 12 May 2011. I was upgraded to a bay view room without even asking. The room is very spacious with a walk in closet. The staff are all friendly and helpful. The exterior is quite grand for San Francisco and the lobby is lovely. It is located in a nice part of town. Make sure you join Fairmont President's club as you get to use the gym and it's fitness classes (including zumba which was so much fun!). I enjoyed my stay here, however it is a shame they don't have a free computer in the lobby to check your emails. I don't travel with a laptop when on vacation, so it was annoying to have to pay to use the business centre. Otherwise I have no complaints.

title: “What you pay is what you get!”
text: I visited for my first time San Diego and my gf and I picked this hotel mainly for the location. Tower 23 has everything a modern hotel can offer. Nothing special or extraordinary but enough to make your stay enjoyable. Staff was very helpful, restaurant and bar were great as well. The view from our balcony is all the money. Finally the bed is one of the most comfortable I ve ever slept!

title: “A truly elegant and gracious stay”
text:
We had a delightful experience at The Mark hotel in NY. Although brief , we were treated with consideration and in high regard from start to finish. In addition , the fact that we had flown in from Europe and were jetlagged was given consideration by the very thoughtful and conscientous staff who upgraded us to a marvelous suite which we thoroughly enjoyed.
The hotel has been recently renovated and is in excellent condition. The personnel is very well trained and offers guests the best treatment from the doorman to the front desk.
We had room service which was served promptly and was very good.
We had the kind of stay we often wish we had had in several other 4 and 5 star hotels where we have stayed.
We hope to visit The Mark more often, thank you for a very unique experience.

title: “Good Starwood option for San Francisco business travel”
text:
The Palace is a grand old hotel with lovely common areas and small but comfortable rooms. The super high ceilings and windows that actually open keep you from feeling "boxed in" which is common in many city hotel rooms. The service was very good, food was solid and the location was perfect for the convention I attended at Moscone - far enough away from ground zero (about 6 blocks) that I could escape the constant networking happening in the lobbies and eateries at the closer hotels. It's very close to great shopping and is surrounded by many restaurant options.
In my opinion, the Palace is a much better choice overall than either Westin in the area or the W and the price point is far more reasonable than the St Regis. For SPG members (or non-members) the Palace is a great option.

title: “Great hotel, very convenient!”
text: My husband and I stayed here for 3 nights October 18th-21st. We were celebrating our 40th wedding anniversary and the staff couldn't have been more helpful. The Management had left us 2 beautifully decorated cup cakes with a note congratulating us on our special anniversary. We were delighted that they'd remarked on it. The room was lovely, very clean, comfortable and a shower to live in! Lovely toiletries too. The surrounding area was a little 'seedy' with a parole office nearby but we never felt threatened at all walking around. The location is very close to Times Square and Metros. We would certainly recommend the 'hop on, hop off' bus tour. We also would certainly recommend this hotel to anyone and wouldn't hesitate to stay again on another trip to New York!

title: “Fabulous, clean, convenient hotel”
text:
I had to stay over in Houston with an early morning flight out! I usually stay at the onsite airport property for convenience, but due to rates decided to find another airport hotel to stay in! I was very skeptical, but I had a great stay! 
I entered to be greeted by a friendly desk clerk! Went to my room and found a very modern, zen room! It had fabulous fixtures and the shower was awesome! Even checked out the faucets in the shower to consider for a home shower! They made great use of space and very clean and simplistic!
I had no vehicle and arrived before dinner, so figured it would be chips from a vending machine. To my pleasant surprise, they had a small restaurant/bar that offered some fresh cooked foods and great happy hour prices. I enjoyed this option.
I had an early am flight. They offered a free shuttle service and when I went to check out, I was greeted by a very pleasant man, Terry, who was so entertaining and made you feel uplifted! A very pleasant and surprising experience!

title: “The Perfect New York Hotel Experience”
text: This hotel embraces the needs of a tourist and makes their stay memorable. The staff was extremely helpful and made sure that we knew the best way to get to the attractions we wanted to experience. The hotel is located just far enough away from the mad rush of the key attactions to permit one to relax after a busy day. Quiet streets enabled evening strolls after diner at a fine local resturant. Two great ones are on either side of the hotel. The next time we leave Virginia to visit New York, this is the place for us!

title: “Rude staff, smelly rooms, charged for a night i did not stay.”
text:
The front desk staff was rude. The rooms smelled funny. They crammed as much stuff into that room, it was hard to move around. We never had enough towels. We were next to the pool, which was loud. I was charged for a night in that hotel that I did not stay, which has yet to be refunded to me.
DO NOT stay here. There are better hotels in the area.
Dallas is nice, though traffic sucks. BUt, thats true with any area.

title: “nice hotel”
text: This hotel has been completely been refurbished and is very modern for the price. Great staff and comfortable beds. My only complaint is that ice machine that charged .50 cents for ice.

title: “One of the worst Hilton hotels”
text: Stayed for 2 nights (January 12-13, 2005) and was very disappointed. Maybe my expectations were too high. Upon check in, I asked if the room had a king sized bed (which I had reserved on-line). No. Aksed if there were any rooms with a water view. No. I was given a 3rd floor room in the tower-like building overlooking valet parking. Listened to the valets yelling all night. The room temperature was very cold and could not easily be adjusted. When I turned on the shower each morning, I needed to wait for the brown water to clear first. There was a strange intermittent light buzzing noise that kept me awake. When I was leaving my first morning, the housekeeper asked if I wanted my room cleaned. Never knew I was supposed to specify that I wanted my room cleaned! The one good thing about this stay - they forgot to charge me the $14/day self-parking fee. I would have expected these accomodations from a La Quinta, but not a Hilton Resort!

title: “Great location, good bedside lights, windows that open-what else do you want?”
text:
I loved the location of this 4-star hotel obtained via Priceline last-minute bidding for an April 12, 2012 stay. My bid was $130, taxes and fees added $27.45 to total $157.45—a bargain in Boston. 
The room was small, very clean, with a European feel—double silk drapes in muted colors, etc. Its windows opened to a view of diners at the Westin Hotel opposite. The windows had awnings and a tiny balcony too small to use, but a nice extra barrier from the street. The extra-high quality sheets and duvet were just what I love at 4-star hotels, same for the excellent bedside reading lights. 
True, there were painters in the hallway outside, the lobby was dark for my taste and I found the wi-fi slow, but the location can’t be beat: A Shaw’s is around the corner, the Prudential center next door and it’s easy walking to any point in Boston. I would stay again in a heartbeat at that price.

title: “This Hotel Ciould Be A Real Jewel”
text:
This could be an extremely nice hotel if the management paid attention to the details of the way the place is maintained.
The inside guest elevator door looks as though something has spilled on it and was never cleaned off. The light bulbs in the lanterns outside of the front door were both burnt out during my stay. The flower box on the front lobby window had no plants or flowers-not even artificial flowers.
This is a tiny little hotel, with tiny little corridors and tiny little rooms. The room decor is a knock off of the early Schraeger-type boutique properties in the City.
The guest room was basic and met our sleeping needs. The coordinated Chinoise wall covering and matching bed covers aided in making the best of a room that had a double bed with no more than 24 inches of walking space around it. There are two phones in the room and a decent radio should you opt out of viewing television.
A word of caution, the thermostat on the wall does not control the room air conditioner. For that you must use a separate remote control.
The bathroom was large, when considering the size of the guest room. The lighting was functional and the water pressure in the shower was good. The mini shampoo bottles were made of such rigid plastic that it was nearly impossible to get any product out of them.
The hotel is conveniently located near multiple subway lines that can get you to virtually any area in the metropolitan area. The closest subway is west of the hotel at Eight Avenue (north bound for cars) and Broadway (south bound for cars); you can catch the 8th Avenue subway from either Penn Station or Port Authority should you be arriving by train, bus or airport connections. 
There is a parking garage right at 49th and 8th Avenue; but, I would be very afraid to guess how much the nightly charge may be. There is an intranet cafe next door and you can catch up on your emails should you not be traveling or being weighted down with a laptop.
And most interesting of all, the hotel is immediately adjacent to this year's Tony Award recipient of the Best Musical. If you are a theater junky, this place is your ground zero.

title: “I too found this place OKAY..but nothing beyond average for Ramada”
text:
was there on a Friday night for one night and they put me in a king room directly opposite the pool. The room was clean and well attended with toiletries and proper towns and linens.
The bed was a nice pillowtop that was very comfortable. I guess being really tired had a lot to do with the great sleep I had there.
The traffic in the area is extremely busy, but it is very accessable to I 95 but you have to watch the exits, its at 346B but going northbound you have to exit the Bowden Road exit to get to it. It can be confusing.
Overall, nothing special, but then again its not a five star

title: “An amazing experience!”
text:
This hotel near the Houston airport at Houston south is terrific. I didn't expect that such a modestly priced facility would look so attractive inside and out and be staffed by such friendly, efficient and generally professional staff. The reception desk employee went out of his way to be helpful, offer useful information, answer questions and even demonstrate the use of the waffle maker early in the morning before I was awake enough to figure it out. The bed was comfortable and the room clean and nicely decorated. The two different airport shuttle drivers were prompt, cheerful and friendly. The breakfast was quite complete and a great convenience before an early morning flight out of Houston. I really enjoyed my stay.
Claudia Jennings
a happy new customer

title: “a bargain, very comfortable, central”
text:
We stayed here for five days. It's very easy to dismiss this hotel because somne would consider the location sketchy.Indeed, I wouldn't want my wife wandering around at night. But it's right downtown, with bustling downtown on one side and run down on the other. Walkable to dozens of restaurants, Chinatown, Reading Termi al, City Hall. A long walk to Independence Hall area. Museums close but a long walk. Hotlel im/out parking $23.
Typical Hampton Inn breakfasts; inice staff, ndoor pool. I'll be back.

title: “THEY RESCUED MY LUGGAGE”
text: I was amazed by the consistency of the positive attitude and helpfulness of the whole staff. Whether it be the concierge, the housekeeper, or the front desk everybody had a positive attitude. I forgot my luggage in the hotel lobby. Within about an hour from my calling them the front desk had arranged my luggage be FedEx to Philadelphia. I didn't have to beg or plead or wait for the "change of shift". The rooms and especially the bathroom were clean. The heated swimming pool was great for my son and nephew to relax. The free hot breakfast in the morning was much better than any "Continental" breakfast I had at other restaurants. Just like at a fancy restaurant, one of the managers walked from table to table making sure everybody was satisfied with their breakfast. I'd surely go back.

title: “Perfect place to stay in great location”
text:
This is the kind of hotel that you want to come back to because everything about it made the rest of the trip that much better.
Pros:
Easy to find
Great Location
Fast Check-in
Very Clean room
Comfortable Breakfast
Friendly and helpful front desk staff
Cons:
Nothing I can think of. Breakfast was ok, not great, but certainly not bad. 
I will go back to this hotel and I would highly recommend it.

title: “Heavenly Weekend Escape”
text: A heavenly little oasis in a hellish environment. The temperatures in Phoenix are 110++ during July and August, but rooms are cheap and you can score a weekend at a five star resort like the Royal Palms for a fraction of the normal price. the Royal Palms is an elegant old world property with lots of beautiful little courtyards and gardens, a delightful restaurant and lounge, and a beautiful pool. It's quiet and secluded and luxurious and totally relaxing. The service is wonderful and everyone makes you feel welcome and completely pampered.

title: “Nice hotel in a great location but needs to improve/modernise decor”
text: Very good location & easy access to shops, subway, times square etc. The beds are extremely comfortable & rooms very clean. I rated the hotel 4 because there was no fridge or coffee maker in my room which was a standard room. The hotel needs to work on that & update amenities & decor.

title: “AMAZING!”
text: The Hudson hotel deserves a 10! The staff was extremely helpful! From the concierge, Matthew recommending the best restaurants to James, a bellboy always helping us get a cab! The Hall, has amazing food! Our rooms were nice and spacious!

title: “Just as expected”
text:
Stayed at this hotel during the last leg of a road trip in the US and Canada with my family.
Pro's:
1) super-friendly, professional and helpful staff (i.e., upgraded my room on arrival,...)
2) perfect location for exploring Manhattan (of course, being right in the midde of Times Square, if you don't like crowds at your hotel doorstep, than that'a another story)
3) good sized rooms - especially for NYC/Midtown standards
4) speedy check-in and out (plus they gave me a late check-out without any hesitation as soon as I asked)
5) great views from every room
Con's
1) the rooms are clean but not spotless
2) decor is decent but not exceptional and some refurbishment is needed
3) very expensive breakfast (I think, for that price, a basic continental breakfast could be included)
4) wii-fi: free in the lobby, high price in the rooms if you are not a premium Hilton Honors member (this I find hard to explain since a budget Hilton chain like Hampton Inn provides free wi-fi to everyone property-wide - the same applies to breakfast)
All in all, a very good experience and I would recommend this hotel to anyone wishing to explore Manhattan for a few days

title: “Nice hotel Great bed !”
text:
It's dc type of hotel . It's not high as the area will not allow it. We had a bit of a problem with the front desk girl on sat night the 7th of July . We were due to have free Internet . She was not nice and then when I show her , my confirmation she said "we will give it to you even if we don't give free Internet to 3rd party " well, didn't like her much. Smiling .
Great area ! 40 dollars for parking !!!watch it . Nice apple basket touch in the lobby .

title: “Perfect Philly weekend!”
text: We had several rooms for a girls' weekend. Greeted at the front desk with smiles and superb service. Rooms were *clean* and the beds & pillows very comfortable. Great Italian coffee in the lobby.

title: “Great business hotel with the essentials”
text:
Had a great stay at this hotel during a short business trip. 
The rooms were clean with great amenities. 
The staff was excellent and were able to anticipate the expectations and needs of my colleagues and I.

title: “Not bad experience, although communication”
text:
Pros
- great location
- comfortable bed
- Acura Experience car took dropped us off at a couple of places during our week-long stay (it was low-season so the car was often free)
- Doormen were very nice
- Nice room decor
Cons:
- bathroom with frosted glass walls. Not good if you don't want others in the room to see the silhouette of yourself while showering
- We called downstairs for someone to help take the luggage from our room to our car downstairs. Waited and waited. Called again. Apparently the message was not passed down. More waiting until someone finally came up. It was annoying.

title: “NEVER AGAIN!”
text: Room smelled of strong urine… called front desk and was told that all they could do was send someone to spray. Never made it in to spray. Horrible,Dirty, and Smelly… you decide…...

title: “No complaints”
text: My husband and I travel to Austin at least twice a year, and have been doing so for over five years. Up until our last visit we have stayed at the Homstead Suites Townlake and have always found it to be an excellent hotel. As an all suite hotel for extended stay guests it is perfect. The rooms are well appointed, clean and comfortable. The bedding was always in great condition, and the kitchenette well stocked with plates, cups, pots, etc. If you're in Austin for entertainment, as we always are, it's the perfect home base, as you can keep your Lonestar beer cold in the fridge while you're driving around South Lamar or checking out the shops on South Congress, and it's walking distance to some of our favourite clubs and restaurants (Gueros, Continental Club, Threadgills - which is right around the corner and has the best chicken fried steak in the city!). We've always booked on a weekly basis, so the rooms are only cleaned twice, but that's always been fine with us. It is not a five star hotel, it's a very comfortable middle of the road place, and I'd recommend it to anyone as a great place to stay.

title: “Great Stay!!”
text: We were extremely pleased with our stay at the Affinia; the folks at the front desk were very helpful and kind. We enjoyed visiting with the doormen everyday and pleased that they attempted to remember our names. We stayed for four nights in a lovely room that was spotless and so comfortable. If and when we come back to New York, we will certainly stay at the Affinia Dumont.

title: “Will never recommend to anyone”
text:
We travelled around US for 4 weeks and San Diego is one of the places we visited. By far this is the worst accommodation that we have stayed during our trip. The place is run down, the room and hallway smelled, the lady at the reception was unfriendly at all. Free breakfast consisted of cold, thinly sliced muffins, toast and tea/coffee. 
We were not informed of the free breakfast and found out through reading brochures. We later found out that there is a nearby hotel that looked much better that charge less than Harborview Inn, only one block away. 
Location itself was good, close to Little Italy and walking distance to trolley.
However, for what we paid, we will never go back there at all and will not recommend to any of our friends and family to stay there.

title: “a bit disappointing”
text: we booked this room based on tripadvisor reviews for weekend family getaway to Chicago to celebrate our 15 year old and 12 year old daughters' birthdays. the location is great and the hotel is nice but agree with an earlier review that this is closer to a Marriott in terms of service than a Four Seasons or other luxury hotel. An incident when we arrived was telling. Our train was late and we got in to Chicago at around 1 AM, we spilled out of the taxi tired and hopeful for a warm welcome. The staff on duty outside stood there staring into space as our taxi driver unloaded our suitcases himself and noone came to help with the bags. Finally out of sheer frustration, he shouted at the staff "these are your customers!! why aren't you helping them??" on check-in, despite 3 staff at the desk, it took way too long despite no other customers at that late hour. The room is nice but not overly luxurious and our view was of the corner of the building. Again, the overall stay was nice, but hardly worth the money we spent. I will say that our 7 year old son threw up in the middle of the night on our last night and the night staff that came up to help were kind and quick which we were grateful for.

title: “Great View & Room But Too many Panhandlers”
text:
This is a very nice property that is well kept and an excellent example of a 4 star hotel.
The bed was as comfortable as any I've ever slept in. The service was first rate in every way. The only place that I can give this hotel less than an excellent grade is the carpets in my room (6th floor). They weren't worn but were gummy to the touch and left your socks filthy and gummy. Obviously they are past due for a good cleaning.
My only other problem was the panhahdlers on Pratt street that hung out in a little park accress the street. They are very agressive. i recommend that you travel only by cab after dark. Marriott needs to pressure the Baltimore police to run these worthless people off!

title: “Business Hotel - needs upgrade”
text: Stayed here one week in October for business. Staff were friendly and helpful. Good restaurant for breakfast. Room was adequate. Concierge lounge was minimal. Passenger elevators did not work one afternoon and guests were forced to use the freight elevator. Hotel owner needs to spend some money to upgrade.

title: “Great midtown hotel”
text: Just spent four great days in New York at this wonderful hotel. On check-in, the front desk resolved a problem created by my travel agent. Had several occasions to use the concierge. . . An outstanding experience three different times. Would have enjoyed the entrance courtyard had renovations not been in progress. A great location at a reasonable price for NYC.

title: “Interesting”
text: My family and I thought it was a great place to stay. The bathroom did have a few repair issues(broken plastic on faucets, some mold on walls) other than that place very clean and unique.

title: “Suberb and consistent treatment at a cozy and fun NYC property”
text:
We've never been treated better by hotel staff and we've stayed at a lot of hotels from hostels to ultra-fancy resorts. The hotel is inviting in many ways. The people are consistently friendly from the front desk to the bell boys, bar tenders, servers, and housecleaning. The whole hotel feels warm and cozy. The renovation is tasteful but not opulent.
On our drive up to NYC our car overheated and had to be towed to a local dealer in Princeton. The whole debacle cost us 7-8 hours and our poor dog suffered through it with us. In desperation I called the hotel to cancel thinking we'd never make into the city. They obliged without penalty but said only this once. I later called back begging to reinstate the reservation as we found a rental car at Newark that would ultimately get us to the hotel. The Algonquin front desk said sure.
When we arrived we were greated with an envelope with 4 drink chits and breakfast coupons (I'm a Marriott Platinum). In addition, they had standard set of Platinum arrival amenities. New chose the split of Chardonnay and cheese plate. They also upgraded us to the Wollacott suite which was cute and a perfect place to relax after a stressful day on the road. I never expect huge rooms in NYC, but this had a nice separate living room. The decor is fun and the backlit photo of 1930s At the head of the bed is a nice touch.
The hotel is also dog friendly. We called ahead to be sure that our 75 lb 10 month-old golden retriever would be welcome. He was greater as a guest! They brought bowls and a mat for him. I signed a waiver but there was no security deposit or sanitation fee required.
We're big Marriott people but we had never stayed in an Autograph Collection Hotel. We love the concept. You feel the history....

title: “Best Service & Friendliest Staff in any New York hotel”
text: While this hotel is the epitome of contemporary in its design its service is old-fashion hospitality. The bellman literally ran to help my colleague and I with our luggage from the taxi upon our arrival. The front desk was genuine and warm in their friendly welcome, offering information about the area and was always gracious throughout our stay whenever engaged. The concierge was fun, friendly and certainly gave us a fabulous recommendation for dinner. Later when we saw him, he followed up and was genuinely pleased we enjoyed his recommendation. Once in my lovely room I had some technical challenges with getting on the wireless network - within five minutes someone came up to my room, helped me and got me connected - all with a smile! While the staff is what impressed me so much, I will add the hotel is lovely - room was immaculate and very comfortable. The tub was amazing, and the bed very comfortable. I highly recommend the Standard.

title: “Nice apartments and close to most things”
text: We stayed there for 9 days and it was a great home base. The apartment was clean and tidy but a little out of date. That was fine for us. We had a two bedrooom apartment which had one bedroom with a queen bed and one bedromm with two double beds. Two bathrooms, a small kitchen and nice sized lounge/dining area to relax. Perfect for a family of four

title: “Great location, excellent price, stay here to save money and see the Getty”
text:
We stayed 2 nights in this hotel, and were very satisfied with the hotel. The rooms were the cheapest in the area, yet this place was NO thin-walled flea bag hotel. 
The walls were quite thick, thank you very much, I never heard any noise at night. The air conditioner pretty much drowned out anything. Our rooms did face a courtyard, so that must have helped. We got a queen/queen room, and it had more square feet than the Paris in Las Vegas. In addition to the beds, there was a desk, a table with chairs and a kitchen. I got the impression this might have once been an apartment building. The place isn't sparkling new, so if you are looking for perfection, don't stay here. 
However, the beds were some of the most comfortable beds I have ever slept in. The bathroom was ok. 
The night manager, Chris, was very helpful and friendly. He gave excellent advice concerning how to get to the Getty: the bus! The bus stoped 2 blocks away and took a lovely route past Bel Air. He also gave us excellent advice about how to drive to several places in the area. 
The breakfast was danish, English muffins, toast, 4 kinds of dry cereal, coffee, tea and 2 kinds of juice. 
The parking wasn't a problem, you just had to leave them your keys if you blocked another car. 
Very safe, walkable neighborhood. There's lots of public transportation within blocks, including a bus to LAX. I loved the $18.50 burger at "The Garden." Also nearby is the Hammer museum, free on Thursdays. I can't wait for another excuse to visit LA again and stay at the Royal Palace.

title: “Best hotel in town (so far); go with a corner room (really!)”
text:
I spent about 3 weeks in Chicago this year, in many different hotels. I liked Dana a lot. Although quite expensive (only an online deal made it an affordable option for us, too), it was definitely worth the price. The rooms are beautifully designed, everything was taken care of. The windows are just huge; and it makes it even better if you get a corner (king) room. We loved the views; I think we have never ever spent so much time indoors; you almost don't want to leave. Internet is free (which is great), beverages in the fridge are nice (but too expensive, same to the candy prices; check out Whole Foods right around the hotel's corner instead).
The Gym comes with some fancy machines - but we missed simple (and effective) things like pilates mats or therabands. With almost no more money left, there was no way for us to check out the SPA (guess what, its not a bargain). Parking is about 40 bucks a night (outdoors, right next to the hotel).
When we asked for "the" manager (because of an IT issue), staff seemed a little bit confused (it looked like there are many different people responsible for only their own area and nobody overlooking everything?!). Anyway, staff was very friendly, professional and obliging.

title: “Great Location”
text: We stayed here for 3 nights at the end of June 2012. The hotel is located on Powell St and is a great location. The staff was friendly and the rooms small, but clean. This, of course, is a old bldg (as all the buildings in SF are) so all the rooms are small. We arrived before the 3 pm check in time and was told that our room was not yet ready. By signing up for the Starwood Reward program we were able to check in early, which was great. If you don't rent a car (which we didn't), I would suggest buying the double decker tour bus (Big Bus Tours) tickets...great way to get around. Parking is anywhere from $35-$50 per day. Also, if you are looking for a great place to eat breakfast, walk up Powell St and eat at Sears...you won't be disappointed!

title: “A wonderful hotel!”
text:
I traveled with my husband and two sons (ages 7 and 11) for a short family trip to Philadelphia. From the moment we arrived we encountered nothing but extraordinary service. The staff really went out of their way to make you feel welcome. Even though we arrived over an hour before "check-in", the hotel had a wonderful room ready for us. The room was large, clean and wonderfully appointed. After returning from a walk around the area, my children entered the room to find posters and a plate of cookies and milk waiting for them (a really nice touch!). The rooms were quiet and the hotel lobbies and hallways were nothing short of immaculate. After a long day of sightseeing my boys really enjoyed the indoor spa pool (again, immaculately kept). The concierge at the front desk was very informative and always happy to help us either find our way around the city or find a kid friendly place to eat. 
We loved our stay at the Rittenhouse Hotel and would gladly recommend it to anyone!

title: “Best Hotel in Texas”
text: This is easily the best hotel in Texas, if not the best hotel anywhere. Beautiful grounds on the north shore of Town Lake, perfectly located on the south edge of downtown, walking distance from the night life on 6th Street. Gorgeous, understated elegance in the architecture, lobby and Trio restaurant. Staff are flawlessly attentive without being intrusive. Rooms are immaculate, totally comfortable and relaxing. Yes, it's expensive, but well worth it.

title: “Clean Cheap Place to Stay”
text:
If all you want is a clean place to lay your head, this is a great one. If noise bothers you, don't bother. I had 3 good nights sleep.
I stayed by myself in the bunk bed room. There were 4 shower/toilets which all were cute and well kept, never more than one was occupied when I needed it. There was only one time that someone had been untidy....
They provide shower gel and shampoo, so all you really need is lotion and toothpaste.
Very close to trendy shopping, lots of food places that are open late. The housekeeping staff is fantastic.
When I checked out of a 3 night stay and the bill was under $600.00, that was my favorite part.
So, if hotel prices are the only thing keeping you from visiting NYC, go ahead and book!

title: “Nice but soulless”
text:
This was my first time staying at a W, and it was adequate, but not remarkable. The decor is fashionable and modern, but also bland and unimaginative. 
The service was great for the most part, except for Saturday night, when a doorman demanded to see our IDs or hotel keys before letting us enter. This seemed like a consequence of the W's burdensome and contrived hipness. 
On the practical side, the walls were too thin and and air conditioning unit was very noisy. But the beds were very comfortable, room service food was delicious, and the Bliss bath products were a nice surprise. And the location was wonderful.
It's not hard to stay at the W, but I will try the Hotel Burnham on my next trip to Chicago. It's in the same price range, and seems to have more character without being so desperately cool.

title: “Still a great place to stay Downtown In Philly”
text: Recently, I just stayed at the Mariott Downtown. It is a very large convention hotel conveniently located close to everything! The staff is extremely pleasant and the staff is very responsive. The rooms had been redone since my last visit. Across the street is the Flagship Macy's with decent shopping. In this location you are central to everything in Philly! Both bars had fast service and the food was above average for a Marriott. I would absolutley stay there again. It was a pleasant experience!

title: “Outstanding Service”
text: By far one of the best business retreats I've ever been on. The professional service extended to us by everyone working at the Renaissance Phoenix Downtown was exceptional. I would highly recommend this hotel for anyone scheduling a 'business outing'..if the conference room, hotel room and restaurant weren't enough, you're within walking distance to anything in the downtown Phoenix area. We are definitely going back next year!

title: “Good for families”
text:
Nice hotel in downtown Chicago. Great set up for families. Service was friendly and accommodating. Rooms were clean and spacious. Love that there is a separate area for tv watching and sleeping. The breakfast provided was way above your average continental breakfast. Great way to start the morning and save a few pennies from having to go out. Weekend breakfast is served a little later, but my early risers and I didn't know that so we went down about an hour early and Mike P. allowed my young kids to go ahead and get some hot breakfast. That was super nice of him. He didn't have to make that accommodation but he did and that won points for the hotel big time. Otherwise I would have had to take 2 hungry kids back up to the room and try to keep them quiet for another hour. Thanks Mike P.
The negatives for this hotel was the pool. yes they have one but it is small and seems to need maintained. The deepest part is 4ft. The chlorine is super strong, which I guess is a good thing for killing things, but it also turned my blond daughter's hair green. yuck! 
Overall a good hotel still pricey, but I guess that's what you get in Chicago.

title: “Perfect Accommodations”
text: We stayed two nights at Copley Square during the fourth of July. PERFECT location and extremely thoughtful and professional staff. We walked ALL over the City and to come back to relax in our lovely room made our stay a pleasure! Thank you !

title: “Fantastic Hotel!!!”
text:
I was spending 5 days in NYC which included 2 days of work and 3 days of vacation so I was looking for an affordable, clean, safe hotel which was convenient to get to both uptown and downtown. This hotel fit the bill perfectly! As a woman traveling alone, safety is always a concern and I felt very safe at this hotel and within the surrounding neighborhoods even at night. The hotel itself was tastefully decorated, comfortable, clean and very quiet (even by Minneapolis standards!). The front desk staff and the doormen were helpful, friendly and welcoming. The complimentary continental breakfast each morning was fantastic, delicious and filling. The morning paper (NY Times & USA Today) were also a nice extra. The price for my stay was right on the mark, too!
When I make my nect trip back to NYC, I will definitely include the South Park Hotel in my plans!

title: “Above average hotel”
text: Stayed there two nights in November and found it to be a good value factoring in free parking. The room we checked into had a bad smell coming from the restroom. We informed the front desk as we left for dinner and they had a new room ready for us when we returned. Since they quickly solved the problem we didn't think twice about it. The location isn't exactly ideal for restaurants or nightlife, but is only a couple of miles out of downtown. We highly recommend eating mexican at Pappasito's and beers at Humperdink's. Both of these places are just a few miles north of the hotel on Stemmons Freeway. Overall the hotel looked pretty new and the rooms were nice. We would consider staying here again if the price was right compared to downtown hotels.

title: “Great location and hotel!”
text: We really enjoyed are stay at the Sheraton. We got a great deal though. I don't know that I'd want to pay $200 a night, plus parking and internet though. We stayed in the Bay Tower. It is like another hotel, seperate from the Marina Tower, and has it's own check-in desk. There is quite a bit of distance between the 2 of them. The bay tower is smaller than the marina tower. There was plenty of parking at the Bay Tower, and it was $22 a day, or $28 for valet. The room was nice enough, and we had a great view of the bay, downtown, and Coronado Island. I would say this tower has a better view. The beds were comfy, and they had lots of comfy pillows too. The bathroom was small, but the shower worked well. Towels were not the best. The internet was $11.95 a day, and it was on the slow side. The mini-bar is expensive and if you move something in it, you will be charged, although they did take the charge off my bill, with no problem. Being close to the airport, I did not hear the airplanes at all.

title: “Value for Money but Location too far!”
text:
We were looking for a value for money place during our trip to PA and booked this hotel.
Hotel´s a bit too far from city center- by train - even though train service is regular and predictable. Station looks a bit deserted though the hotel is walking distance from the station - and there seemed to be no security concerns walking to the hotel from the station. They even sent a pickup when we requested for it.
Place is small and a bit cramped up. This also gets reflected in the room. 
But saving grace is staff - very courteous, nice, and helpful.
I thought they did their best, but i would not stay here again on my next visit. It´s too far from city center.

title: “Would definitely stay again”
text: Great location down by the pavilion and all the restaurant choices. Pleasant surprise to be upgraded to a suite without even asking. Beautiful interior of lobby and the room was clean, spacious and very well kept.

title: “Great hotel and location!”
text: We chose this hotel based on its proximity to the Blue Line, but it is also near some great stores for shopping. Our son lives in Bucktown, which has little or no hotel rooms, so the train was our best option. For Chicago, the Hampton Inn Majestic is an excellent value. The cost was reasonable, a hot breakfast was included, the room was large and recently updated, the beds were very comfortable, the bathroom was large, and the employees were all very helpful and friendly. They do a great job of keeping their breakfast area stocked and keep it open longer than a lot of other hotels that will remain nameless. I want to emphasize the friendliness of their employees, too. Many Chicago hotels have workers that don't care and are just putting in their time. The Majestic's employees are very helpful and outgoing. They really want to make you feel welcome, and they take pride in their hotel. We will definitely stay there again!

title: “Very enjoyable -- glad I ignored the bad reviews and stayed here”
text:
I had purchased a Groupon for 2 nights. ThenI started reading the reviews and was really worried that I had made a bad purchase and should just stay elsewhere. But there were enough good reviews that I decided to give it a try, and I'm glad I did. The front desk staff were VERY friendly and helpful. The room was decent, and the full living room and kitchen are nice to have, just from a "comforts of home" standpoint. The free hot breakfast was better than many I've had. And the free wi-fi was great too. Overall, an enjoyable stay, a very good value. 
On the minus side -- it is about a 15 minute drive to get downtown. But this is Texas. Things are spread out here! And if it matters to you, the housekeeping/maintenance staff don't speak much English -- but they do know how to do their jobs.

title: “Unclean Bathroom in Room”
text: Given room with unclean bathroom. Urine on wall. Unknown orange and yellow (probably urine) around base of toilet. Head of Housekeeping said the yellow stains on the wall was glue; however it wiped off so it was obviously urine and not glue stains from a recent remodeling. Said the stains around the toilet was cleaning solution, oh please! You still can wipe up cleaning solution. Hotel Mgr. offered us a free breakfast; however if they can't clean the bathrooms in the guest rooms then why would I eat there too? No telling what the kitchen looks like. Upon checking in to hotel, another guest was complaining because they checked her into a room that had not been cleaned; I guess uncleaniness is the norm at this hote. I'd suggest going elsewhere.

title: “outstanding service! & gorgeous hotel (:”
text: We came to this hotel after being at a dump, so we needed friendly people, & great service & this is exactly what we had! We called for a reservation the night before Fourth of July & we didn't think that there would be an opening, but there was & we got there & i absolutely fell in love with this hotel. I'm fifteen years old & it's just a very hip & retro hotel. i absolutely love it! Rick helped us, he was so friendly & great! then we got up to the rooms & the room we stayed it was awesome, everything they had was just great, very comfy, & cool. The outside deck was great. Everything was very colorful & chic. It's not even two minutes from Venice Beach, which is very nice! When we woke up the next morning we went to the Hash cafe, & it was very yummy, great service & food. I recommend this hotel to anyone staying in the Venice Beach area! FANTASTIC EVERYTHING :D

title: “Excellent location”
text: We stayed 4 nights for a family trip at this great hotel. We had originally booked 2 rooms through Expedia- one deluxe King for my husband and I and one room with 2 doubles for the kids. After it was discovered that the hotel had overbooked one of our room types, the manager upgraded that room and ensured that our two rooms were beside each other. We were very impressed with this plus the service once we arrived. The rooms are spacious, clean, bright and comfortable plus the bathrooms are beautiful with lots of storage! We found the location to be perfect- right in between the main downtown core of shops and restaurants and the Seattle Centre. We were able to walk everywhere we wanted to go!

title: “great location!! wonderful experience!!”
text: Took my daughter and 2 of her friends for start of their spring break. Very centrally located. next to a subway station. walking distance from shopping areas and other areas of interest. room nice sized considering we were 4 in there. Breakfast was also a good spread. Nice experience!!

title: “Phoenix Round Trip”
text:
We are from the Tucson area and fly to Michigan to visit our kids. We usually struggle with the cost and layovers of flying out of Tucson International. This time we decided to check out our options in Phoenix. This Best Western on 24th St was the answer to our need. We were able to find affordable round trip tickets from Phoenix to Detroit and back that fit our timetable.
We decided to spend the night at the Best Western and catch the 6:15am flight to Detroit. This worked out great since we could leave our vehicle at the hotel at no cost. This package made the whole financial part of the trip easy.
Staying at the Best Western was also a treat. Well organized at the front counter and gave us all the information we needed to make the trip a pleasure.

title: “Fantastic Hotel in a great area and friendly staff”
text: I stayed in this Hotel for one week with the family from 26June until 3rd July! we loved it! all the reception staff always spoke when we went out in the morning and came back in at night! they also helped out with a few request's.also i have to say the cleaner was fantastic! we left her a couple of note's with request's on and when we got back we got what we asked for! we loved this hotel was in a great location. just 2 mins walk to Broadway and so close to lot's of great shop's, bar's and restraunts. i would recommend you buy a pass for subway last's for 1 week and we went all over the place was only $27. i would recommend this hotel and have been saying to friend's it's the best hotel we have stayed in when we come to nyc. It was great to have the fridge and microwave in the room the coffeemaker was just bliss. i loved loved loved this hotel very comfortable room's amd very clean! i cant wait to go back.... :)

title: “Very nice hotel in a great location”
text:
I've had the opportunity to stay at the Talbott Hotel twice in the past 2 weeks and would recommend it as a well priced option in the Magnificent Mile area.
The Talbott is located on a reasonably, quiet block, two blocks west of Michigan Avenue and the hordes of shoppers at the Water Tower Mall. It's a relatively small hotel, at least compared to nearby options like the Sofitel and Four Seasons.
Check-in was easy and pleasant both times. I have seen both the standard and the parlor rooms. We like to watch TV in bed, so the smaller standard room was the better choice for us. We paid $145, including a $30 breakfast voucher for one of the best equipped rooms I've encountered. 
First of all, there's an overhead light, an almost unheard of convenience, as well as plenty of desk/table/floor lamps. The desk lamp has an outlet to plug in a portable power strip that is my must-have travel accessory. There's a refrigerator with minibar stuff in it but it's okay to put your own things in as well (there's a lovely little supermarket around the corner where you can buy pretty much anything you might need). There's a safe and an armchair (unusual for a small room).
The flat screen TV is large and Mac Mini computer-based, so the guide lists channels in alphabetical order and you can use it as a dvr as well. The lineup includes several HBO channels. There is also a wireless keyboard that allows you to use the Mac and TV as a computer with high speed Internet. This is a terrific feature. If you prefer a laptop, wifi is free and works fine. The only downside is that the tiny remote control forces you to do everything through a menu-based interface, which can be inconvenient. I couldn't find a mute button either.
The bathroom is fine and has huge bath towels. The two queen bed room has 2 sinks. There's a Keurig coffee maker with those convenient little K-cups that makes very decent coffee. The climate control is responsive and kept us cool on a record breaking hot day.
I did not try the nearby health club. The restaurant is kind of odd. We only had breakfast there, and if you do so I'd highly recommend avoiding the continental breakfast, which includes a "bakery basket" consisting of a piece of white toast, and a mini muffin and Danish like you get packaged at the supermarket, plus a tiny ramekin filled with maybe a third of a serving of cereal. There's a Starbucks across the street, one of a half dozen within 4 blocks.
The location is fantastic, convenient to almost anything. Valet parking is available for what the hotel refers to as the "nominal" charge of $51 a day. This is similar to the other hotels but at more than 1/3 of the room rate I'd say the word nominal should not appear anywhere on their web site.
Overall, I'd rate the Talbott a very good hotel and a terrific value for the neighborhood.

title: “Two stars at Best”
