text: Four star prices with a two star value. In town for college registration with my daughter - we were quite dissapointed in the room. TINY bathroom with black & green mold stained grout, 1/2 roll of TP, dated furnishings, carpet that verges on being indoor/outdoor and an odor that fluctuates between wet basement and care facility. The housekeepers appear to be adults but the results of 30min per room could easily be improved upon by any 12 year old with the ability to turn on a vaccum. Keep in mind, this hotel allows pets so that may explain a few things.... Good luck!

title: “Delightful stay”
text:
We were here during the heat wave in July and it was very delightful with a very nice a/c control system. 
Pros: stayed in the queen deluxe room. Very nice, 
very comfortable beds,
Cons: bathroom a little snug but that was the only drawback in this delightful stay.

title: “Perfect price, location, hospitality - you couldn't ask for more”
text: We stayed at Chelsea Pines Inn in March 2011 for 6 nights as part of our honeymoon tour of the US. The location was ideal, we could walk to some of the best restaurants in New York and we were able to explore the West Village, Meatpacking District and Soho on foot. It was right by the public transport system which meant uptown and Central Park felt like they were right on our doorstep. Chelsea Market was close by, as were great shops. The room was spacious, stylish, comfortable and clean. We were surprised at how quiet it was. The breakfasts were great - especially as they went so late! And last but not least, the staff were wonderful. Generous, friendly and helpful, they made us feel completely at home. Highly recommended, we will be back.

title: “Excellent location in Chicago”
text:
Chose this hotel because we had a couple free nights to use. Didn't regret it at all. This hotel is in a great location on Michigan avenue. The hotel is within the price range as most of the other hotels in this area. Its walking distance to attractions and shopping. Located within 2 blocks of the Metra and buses. 
The hotel itself is very nice, with courteous staff and great amenities including a pool and fitness center which we didn't use. The suite layout was perfect since we were staying with friends. It allows some privacy for those who want to stay up a bit later. The shower facilities were great with bath salts included. There was a small refrigerator in the room as well as a sink and electric kettle. Didn't eat at the hotel since there are so many great restaurants all around. 
The only inconvenience to this hotel was that you had to use two separate elevators to get to your room. After a long day on you feet this can seem a bit of a nuisance but other than that its a great hotel.Would definitely recommend it if staying in Chicago.

title: “Good central location, great rooftop pool”
text: Having spent a long time trying to choose which hotel to spend the first part of our holiday, we chose the Colonnade because of its rooftop pool, which was fabulous. However on two of the three evenings we were there it was closed or partially closed off for private functions - so if a pool is a priority, this could be really annoying. We booked through hotels.com and got a good bargain - I would have resented paying the full price though as it is not really that special. The concierge and door staff were lovely, the receptionists not so helpful. The bedroom, a double double, was really too small for four people, and the public areas are not cozy. But the location is great, and if you get a good price, I would recommend it.

title: “Location, location, location”
text: The hotel is off 5th av and between rockeffeller centre and Moma, amazing location, within walking distance to times sq, central park, empire state, macys etc. The rooms are basic, a bit outdated and noisy but clean. We were only spending nights there so we didn't mind.pay cash, just in case.

title: “Cheap good base”
text:
Stayed here last year. Just a base for us to explore Hollywood from.
Very basic, but does exactly what you would expect from this kind of accomadation. Only issue I had was the walls are thin and the deaf guy in the room next to us fell asleep with TV on loudly and kept me awake.
Alot of reviews have said they did not feel safe, but I stayed there with my kids and never felt in danger. One tip for fellow, not so bright brits like me. Google maps makes things look alot closer than they are. Its a long bloody walk too Hollywood Boulevard. And if you walk down Sunset you are likely to encounter alot of dodgey looking mexicans. lol

title: “Awesome park and cruise package at this hotel.”
text: Chose to do the Park and Cruise package that Fairfield Inn White Marsh offers. Man, I couldn't have done better if I'd designed the place myself. We were greeted at the front desk and "hurried along" by the smiling front desk clerk so that we could enjoy the complimentary burgers, dogs, beer and soda they were grilling for dinner. Fresh baked cookies for my nieces before they made their way to the front desk for new check ins. Beautiful room, comfortable beds, clean, and well kept. Free wi-fi and cable tv. Close by shopping, groceries, restaurants, Barnes & Noble, strip malls. Complimentary laundry. Hot tub and pool with on duty life guard as well as a small gym. Parked the car behind the hotel for the cruise (9 nights) in a lighted, secure area. Complimentary hot breakfast was quite good. Boarded the shuttle at our scheduled time and off to the pier we went. 10 days later, we boarded the bus to return to the hotel and packed the cars to head out. Synopsis, $15/day at the pier for 10 days is $150 just to park your car, credit card only. For $140, I got room for the night, dinner on arrival, swimming pool, hot tub, gym, wi-fi, breakfast, shuttle to and from the pier, and parked my car for 10 days. Gee, which is the better deal??

title: “Above average”
text: Room had full kitchen and hotel had FREE guest laundry with 4 machines. No breakfast. Paid $125 for Sunday night with AAA. Front desk seemed understaffed. About a one mile walk to the Galleria and a few other restaurants. We wound up at Paradise Cafe. Soups, salads, sandwiches. Hotel is freeway close. This worked well for our one night in Dallas.

title: “Nice hotel convenient to convention center and Larimar St”
text: Stayed here for 3 nights for a trade show in Jan 2012. First what I liked about the room: room was spacious, updated, clean with a flat screen tv, desk area, in-room complimentary coffee, complimentary daily newspaper, ionic hair dryer. I LOVED that I could open the window for fresh air although there is a trolley that passes by constantly with a damn trolley bell that rings which is quite annoying. What I disliked about the room: the cell phone coverage is terrible throughout the hotel, I had to text anyone I needed to speak with to call me in my hotel room, the towels were of motel quality - paper thin and very rough and I am a Hyatt gold member so I am accustomed to Hyatt Regency beds being much more luxurious. The blanket was not a down or down alternative it was 2 sheets with one of those nasty thermal blankets in between. Also the in room wireless Internet is EXPENSIVE - 48 hours cost me $30! The hotel has a couple of bars - the one on the 27 th floor is a must see, a 24 hour coffee shop/convenience store, and a decent restaurant on-site but it is in walking distance to Larimar St where there are some fabulous restaurants and bars.

title: “I love the swimming pool and jacuzzi there!”
text:
Before I arrived, I thought my stay would be very boring as it was just a hotel closed to LAX. Surprisingly, I was wrong, there are many hotels around LAX area and it was just like a tourist area!
There are many bus services and sightseeing tours to different places. I went to Hollywood, Beverly Hills, Universal Studio and also Manhattan beach. Manhattan beach is very closed to the hotel and it has a lovely view for Pacific Ocean! For the bus fare to Manhattan beach, they will also include a trip for you to visit the shopping area -Manhattan Village. It includes big supermarket, shopping mall and restaurants in there. 
I enjoyed my stay in LA, but I was so disappointed of the weather. I was told that LA weather is hot with lots of sunshine! However, during my stay in LA, it was very chilly as well as windy!
The swimming pool and jacuzzi in this hotel had just saved my days! The swimming pool and jacuzzi are both outdoor but heated. The temperature was perfect for you to indulge yourself there whole day!
The hotel was spacious with many nice staff! Delicious breakfast, lunch and dinner. 
I would recommend this hotel to people!

title: “great”
text: Went this weekend for an overnight stay, got a great price on priceline. The hotel is gorgeous, the rooms clean and modern, beds very comfortable. The people at the front desk could not be any nicer. The valet is alittle pricey but we didn't have to wait long to get our car and everyone was extremely nice. The location is great also. Overall was a fantastic stay.

title: “Location is great, breakfast is poor!”
text: This hotel is well located in the downtown district near the cable cars and the stores. Rooms vere OK but you get what you pay for. Breakfast was poor, no milk for the coffee so we had to go and buy some Starbuck coffees nearby. Service is OK but no smile there!!!!

title: “Staff better than advertised, location not.”
text:
My experience with the shuttle service and the staff in general was much better than described in other reviews. My wait for the shuttle at Logan was no more than 10 minutes and the return was right on time. The drivers were fine as were the front desk staff. Furthermore, I was able to get into my room at 10 am.
On the other hand, I concur with the other reviews regarding the hotel's location. Aside from the JFK T-stop being only a few minutes walk away, the is nothing else nearby. Furthermore the dining options at the hotel are extremely limited. 
Lastly, they charge for in-room wireless internet.

title: “Well located good value”
text: This hotel was well positioned for us considering we had a hire car. Free parking was one of the reasons we stayed here. Also the close proximity to Dodgers Stadium meant we could walk to the game. Reception area was nice and clean. Staff were friendly. Room was typical for a Super 8. Would stay there again

title: “Enjoyed this HOTEL”
text: the Conceirge were Extremely helpful. It is in the Financial district and it is quiet on the weekend. We did walk everywhere and only got lost once on the first day. It is close to the water but a little walk to Boston Common. Boston directions are strange and finally got our bearings. Love the BOND..High tea and Sunday Brunch very good. the BED was the BEST

title: “W - a good experience and great value, with some caveats”
text:
We had a small group of travellers that all stayed at the W hotel - the one downtown near wall street (123 Washington). It was a very pleasant stay - while we booked online through a third party website, they still honored my SPG gold status, which was nice and we received an upgraded room.
The upgrade came with the caveat that it was facing the World Trade Center construction site, so there might be some additional noise. We were open to it, however, because it sounded interesting, and while there was a constant stream of construction it was generally quiet in the evening. I think getting a birds-eye view of the site was one of the most interesting things about the stay, so unless you sleep during the day a lot, it's worth experiencing.
The check-in is on the 5th floor, so you have to take an elevator up to reach the proper lobby. The lobby has a bar, which is open in the afternoon/evenings, a good spot to catch a drink before heading out. The drinks aren't cheap, but the pours tended to be generous. 
The room itself was well appointed - the bed was comfortable, the bathroom had a nice shower, and my wife was quite happy with the bath products offered. As we did have a slightly larger room, I was disappointed that there was no sitting area or at least a lounger chair to relax in. It seems all the rooms have "sitting" areas on the window ledge, and part of the built in furniture, but they weren't really comfortable to sit on. To each their own.
The hotel restaurant was the BLT Bar and Grill - it was quite good, and a nice perk. We had the burgers and some other munchies and they were all excellent. It seems to have a great after work scene - bit crowded, but very lively. I'm a bit surprised by some of the negative reviews of the food and staff - we had a good experience and I like to think we're experienced diners.
The service at the hotel - in particular the doormen and the floaters - was excellent. Normally I wouldn't mention it, but in this case they did seem to go above and beyond, which really improved our stay. Some of our group members needed some additional assistance and the staff here did an exceptional job of assisting with cabs and arranging transport. 
I would recommend this hotel - it is good value for NYC and especially well located if ground zero is an important part of your trip. 
As a point of reference, we've recently stayed at the Hotel Andaz on Wall street and the Omni Berkshire around mid-town. This hotel compares well with those others - with a definite edge in service to the W if that is important to you. The rooms at the W appear to be slightly smaller. The Andaz has the free soft drinks and munchies, but the service was poorer. The Omni was the most traditional and anonymous of the three, but the room was very comfortable.

title: “Good all round midddle range hotel”
text: Walking distance to Upper Midtown attractions and Central Park. Good quality room, spacious and well-appointed. Good kitchenette, but no complimentary coffee/milk/sugar etc, so we couldn't have a drink on arrival and had to buy from shop - maybe this is normal for NY, but this was our first visit. Excellent service (doorman, concierge, bell boy etc). Simple continental breakfast included. No restaurant, lounge or even a decent bar (just a small bar where breakfast was served), but who needs these when Manahattan is on your doorstep. Good value-for money. Our room was at the back so no noise except the slightly irritating air conditioning of the blocks behind us.

title: “Great location!”
text:
The hotel is within walking distance of the subway and that made it so convenient to see all the attractions in NY. Because of religious reasons, we needed to find halal food and there was a halal food cart just steps from the hotel... perfect! 
We booked a room for 4 pple and it was spacious enough for us to move around when we put our bags against the wall. The breakfast provided was a plus and we ate our fill before we ventured out for the day. However, the coffee machine in the room smelled of plastic when it was switched on to make coffee. We didn't use it again after the first time.
I would definitely return to this hotel because of the great location. We walked to Times Sq and there were plenty of shops around so everything we needed were within reach.

title: “Good hotel perfect position”
text: Perfect position, poor breakfast, nice room but small. Perfect quality/price

title: “Excellent Hotel!”
text: We stayed over the July 4th holiday[5days]--- terrific hotel for the holiday!-- near everything----we are Marriott Platinum and was upgraded--the newly renovated Club lounge is a "big" plus--- excellent food and service---the Marriott people were really great--check in was easy and fast hats "off" to Ms.Julia D. Blade

title: “3 bedroom penthouse suite”
text: We thoroughly enjoyed our stay in the beautiful 3 bedroom, 3 1/2 bath penthouse suite. We travel quite a bit and the ultra modern style is my favorite. With outstanding downtown views and spacious floor plan (2,700+ sq ft), we were quite happy. The designers obviously got everything right. The service was outstanding. The management team truly cares. We look forward to returning to the beautiful penthouse suite in San Diego at a future date. One thing that you should know is that the 3rd bedroom is an open loft. It lacks privacy when going up the stairs to the master bedroom but does have it's own private bathroom.

title: “Comfortable and reasonably priced”
text: This is a nice hotel that's very reasonably prices. Rooms have recently been refurbished and the needs are so comfortable. Also, the staff was friendly and the location is great!

title: “If you have kids - stay here!”
text: From the moment that we met Steve at the front door, it was a family-friendly experience. He had my son help him with the luggage, showed him where the toy chest was, told him of a spy shop around the corner, and made us feel very welcome. Then we met Ernie who was awesome as well - playing versions of rock paper scissors every time he saw my son. Rooms were clean and cute. Not a 5 star fancy property, but 5 star for service and location!

title: “Great location and hotel”
text:
Located next to Times Square, this is a great hotel for a romantic stay. Ideal place to retract yourself to to have a quick break, or have a (free) drink before heading out for diner. Rooms are small, but not too small. 
Breakfast didnt have that many choices, but good enough. 
Staff was friendly and helpful.
Would return without hesitation, one of the best hotels I stayed in (not for business). We loved it for its atmosphere (totaly not my style of choice, but here it worked) and location.
Minor issue:
Our Queens room was in the back on floor 4. So no sound issues, but: a bit too warm, no view and a smell of the kitchen next door when you opened the windows (to get fresh air). Which was unfortunate, as it's about the only complaint we had, but very noticeable.
Would also not recommend this hotel for business though: it has no inhouse bar, no desks (guess the suites have), and it breathes 'family' a bit too much.

title: “A Good Starting and Ending Location for a Trip to Colorado”
text:
We stayed 2 nights upon our arrival in Denver and then the night before our departure about a week and a half later. I chose this establishment because I was able to use Hilton Honors points for the 3 nights, and I do like the Embassy suites hotels. I enjoy their Manager's Receptions, free made-to-order breakfast, free shuttles to airports, and the good night's sleep in their comfortable suites. I don't really know if this Emabassy is more economical, for what you get, then the many other establishments near the airport.
This Embassy met my normal expectations for this brand. My only minor complaint regards the appetizers at the Manager's Reception. Carrots & celery sticks, a few cheese spreads with crackers, and a rather bland salsa type dip was about it, and it was the same for all 3 nights. I've stayed at other Embassys where there is at least one food nibbly, like wings or shrimp.
I want to pass on that they did shuttle us to the off-site car rental company (we used Avis) as well as the airport. We found this quite handy because we didn't get the car until the morning of the 2nd day (getting in late at night why pay for a partial day's rental just to drive it to the hotel?) and dropped it off the evening before our departure flight. They brought us to the Avis location to pick up the car on that 2nd morning and then picked us up at Avis after we had turned the car in. Avis has 2 waiting areas - one to shuttle you to the airport and the other for hotel shuttles. You may want to check this option out with the front desk.

title: “A disappointing Marriott experience”
text:
I've been an elite level marriott rewards member for many of the past 8 years. That didn't seem to matter a lot to this hotel. This was also the first time I brought my entire family to a full Marriott. 
We had a little trouble finding the hotel because the national reservation hotline gave us the wrong street name, and it didn't show up in our gps. 
They gave us a room that backed up to the elevator, even though there were other rooms available. By the time I realized this was done, my kids had already messed up the beds and bathroom area so I felt we should stay in the room. It was like sleeping near a subway- I know because I've tried to do that before. Later the manager said this was an accident. 
We booked a 'stay and eat' deal and should have received breakfast tickets at check-in but we did not. Instead we waited in the restaurant while the staff whispered back and forth and eventually validated our story with the front desk that in fact we had paid for the breakfast deal. They apologized for that inconvenience also. 
There was a used coffee straw in the closet, the printer in the business center was out of order and the internet access in the business center was very slow. 
Beyond all that, breakfast was very good, the pool was excellent, the hotel staff friendly and the facilities were very impressive. 
This hotel has the presence of a nice hotel but left too many details out for me to believe it has the service class of one. For the money, you'll probably be happier elsewhere. If you decide to stay, don't count on them to take care of all the details.

title: “nickle and dime”
text: Quite simply my biggest complaint was how they charge for every extra amenity that I have gotten free at even the dumpiest hotels. OK I did get my room thru Priceline so I guess in their minds it's OK to treat me like a second class citizen. First it was the $35 parking fee per day to use the garage ! $35!!! I know this is Boston but it's not like it's in the North End. Like many guests I just went 3 blocks down on some dark and empty side street - for free at the risk of a break in. Then it was the wireless. Fine doesn't need to be free in my room but no Hotspot in the building left me a captive unless I paid $15/hr. $5 for bottled water in the room? OK all that just left be bitter.. but $2. for coffee in the morning !!! REALLY. You can't throw down some free coffee ?? Is Hyatt going under? Because all this terribly cheapness makes it feel low budget.. I left the hotel soap and shampoo... maybe they'll start changing for toilet paper next. Probably going to go somewhere with out the Hyatt name that feels less like staying with a cheap relative.

title: “Get your money's worth”
text: Everything in Chicago being pricey, we selected Embassy Suites for it's family-friendly rooms and the breakfast. But WHAT a breakfast!! WOW, very fresh, a great start to the day! And Happy Hour in the evening was a joy. The accomodations were also very clean and the staff friendly but not intrusive. The night manager brought the luggage cart to our car at valet parking when we checked in and he was very "real" and personable. That was also a great start. The location was great and our Embassy Suites room was the perfect oasis of comfort in between being out-and-about in Chicago. I will be staying here again and would highly recommend it to others.

title: “Convenient and clean”
text: Hotel staff was professional, accomodating and efficient. Being connected to Macy's, a food court and other small shops provides options- especially for the single traveler. I usually attend a sporting event at Staples Center and eat and maybe see a movie at LA Live, and they're only a five-ten minute drive from the hotel. My room and the common areas were clean, the bed was very comfortable.

title: “Great - But Cramped!”
text: I have stayed at Paramount many times over the years, but this was the first time back in a few years. Even though it was never bad, the customer service is 1000% better than it was a few years back and the staff is outgoing and friendly (evidently the cool and aloof persona from years back wasn't doing it). The food was great, the room was great (but yes it is small) but the bed is very comfortable and everything is so clean and crisp - love it. My only 2 criticisms is 1) the toilet is so close to the wall it makes the morning ritual both adventurous and challenging and 2) the drawers in my clothes wardrobe didn't open because the hinges from the wardrobe door stop them. I usually don't mention people, but I have to say, Leonardo and ESPECIALLY Nathalie went out of their way to help me. She checked me in and took a personal interest in my stay and my comfort for all four days I was there. At checkout there was a mistake on my bill (charged several times for internet). BEFORE I could catch it, Nathalie called up to my room and said she noticed it and was making an adjustment. That has NEVER happened to me before. Leonardo seemed to always be there with a quick hand if I needed help with luggage or maneuvering around the lobby, etc. But not just those two, everyone on the staff was friendly, helpful and took a personal interest in my happiness. What a refreshing change from the usual sullen staff I have had to deal with in my travels. It was so nice, that I don't care if I have a hole instead of a toilet in the bathroom, I will stay at Paramount again. Also, location can't be beat.

title: “Book now - AWESOME hotel!”
text: The Hotel Solamar is the best hotel I have ever stayed in – and you need to book there as soon as you can! The property is beautiful, extremely clean and comfortable! The best part – hand down – is the staff! From my new friends at the front desk, to the basketball-playing-knowledge-dispensing bell staff, I could not have had more fun! I even had the privilege of spending some time with Mark, the General Manager who secretly wants to be a cabana boy at the pool on the fourth floor! The wine reception was excellent and gave my group the chance to relax and meet other folks staying at the hotel. The location was excellent – close to everything including the convention center. Bottom line is that the people make the experience and the Hotel Solamar is full of people who are there to meet your every need and want you to enjoy your stay. I will be back for sure!!!

title: “Good but not fantastic option for downtown Austin”
text: We stayed at this property for a getaway weekend and were pleased, but not blown away. Great: front desk service (professional, efficient, very pleasant), fantastic hot breakfast (although pricey!), clean and comfortable room (the bed was great). Not as great: property needs to be updated (needs updated wall coverings, media, bathroom), overpriced valet parking (your only option), location is a little far from the center of downtown. Still, overall this is a good option for a long weekend getaway,and we would happily return.

title: “Close to CHOP”
text: I chose this hotel solely on location. I needed to be near CHOP for my grandson's surgery, and I did not want to rent a car. Even in 20 degree weather, the walk from the hotel to CHOP was fine. The staff was outstanding. I would stay here again if I needed to be near CHOP. Pricey but the location was key.

title: “Great Hotel”
text:
We have stayed at this Courtyard before and were just as pleased with our room and staff as the previous times. We had a large corner room on the 22nd fl, very clean, quiet , the comfortable Marriott bed. The entire staff was pleasant and hospitable, from front desk to concierge, housekeeping to restaurant waitresses. 
The AAA rate was a good bargain, especially for NYC standards. Conveniently located to subway, and easy walks to many attractions, restaurants and parks. 
Highly recommend this property.

title: “Best Hotel On Our Trip”
text:
We only stayed two nights here and we wished we had stayed more. This was the best value hotel we had all trip. From the warm cookie's on arrival, which were needed given the freezing temperature outside.
We stayed in a King Spa Suite and it was great value. The room was huge, modern, comfortable and had an amazing view in three directions from Millennium Park, State St and the river.
The service we had was spot on as we had to call maintenance once and they were there is a minute. Also we would highly recommend the restaurant given the fact we were provided with a free bottle of wine for each room we had, and given we had four of us was a great night for the family. The food was amazing and though more expensive than most food places it is definitely worth it. Also the rooftop bar is a great place for a quick drink before dinner.
The hotel is also really close to everything in central Chicago from shopping, sight seeing, theatres and eating. This is the place to stay and hopefully they stay at the same price as they were in December as it was great value.

title: “A quiet oasis in a bustling city!”
text: Everything about this classy hotel adds to the NYC experience. After running around the City all day there is nothing better than coming back to the hotel and having a cold beverage in the contemporary, cozy roof top garden, or a cup of cappuccino and a bit of chocolate in the peaceful, elegant lobby. I have never met a more pleasant and accomodating staff; everyone wore a smile, asked about our day and engaged in conversation. They could not have been more helpful, from the concierge, Jose, to the ladies serving drinks on the roof. The rooms are clean, crisp and comfortable. The color scheme is as restful as the bed and pillows. The location was perfect for all of our sightseeing needs and we had easy access to the subway. We will definitely be using this hotel again and again!!

title: “Clean affordable hotel in the middle of downtown”
text: Went for an anniversary trip. Couldn't have been a better deal. Clean rooms and huge. Nice service as well.

title: “Friendliest Hotel Staff in Downtown Indy”
text: I stay in Indianapolis quite often and I have stayed in just about every hotel downtown. My favorite by far is the Marriott. The staff is very friendly and helpful. Rooms are great. Location is great.

title: “Great Service Excellent Hotel”
text: My review of the Hotel itself is excellent. Great Food, Great Rooms, Comfortable Beds, Great Service. If you are planning on doing Business in Lower Manhattan than the location is excellent as well. If you are coming for a Vacation I think you would prefer something in midtown or uptown. I think the best area to stay is around the park check out the Ritz Carlton Central Park. But this hotel is nice if you are going to be around lower manhattan.

title: “Nice place to stay”
text: The hotel room was nice and comfortable. A bit cramped but fine for a single person on a business trip. The bathroom was small and walk around space in the room was limited. However, the room was sufficient for my needs. The wireless service was easy to access. Fitness room is well equiped. The Dubliner restaurant is accessible from the hotel lobby. It is a fun place to eat. Location of the hotel is good with easy access to Union Station.

title: “perfect stay!”
text: my husband & i chose the inn for its location & it had great reviews, well i want to add to it! we arrived after dealing w/ friday night traffic from palo alto! the front desk man was gracious & smiling! the inn was quaint! we loved the room, it was a little small, but comfy beds & all the amenities you need! they had evening wine & breakfast was great too! we met people there who said they have been coming there for years! our day time desk clerk was helpful & even the housekeeping were friendly!

title: “Great Hotel! Great Service!”
text:
Very nice hotel. Service is great (outside the bar area). They are there for whatever you need. The manager walked me to the elevator on my first stay here, to be sure that I knew all about what the hotel had to offer.
Hotel has a modern feel to it. 
Bathrooms are very nice. Huge soaking tub which is great after a long day. Beds are super comfy. 
One semi negative comment for the hotel - restaurant and bar configuration is very odd. I was supposed to meet a colleague in the bar/restaurant area. There is no straight forward entrance to either. Multiple glass walls with multiple entrances. The entrance to the restaurant looked like it was through a kitchen prep area. Once I was seated in the bar area, the bar wait staff was kind of snotty and rude.

title: “good value for the money”
text: this hotel is near the market place. the area around it is commercial. the room was a good size. the bathroom was a little musty, and the carpet was a little tired. the bed was great big and firm. the breakfeat was amazing! waffles, sausage, eggs good coffee. the pool was indoors which was good because it was overcast and too cool to be outside. this hotel could use some updates but overall not a bad deal for the price.

title: “Not much redeeming about this Dope House”
text: I stay 3 nights with my toddler and everynight the action never stopped. I worried about my car. I worried about our safety. Management was attentive and did attempt to address my concerns. The housekeepers were thourough. Rosa was always smiling and got me exactly what I needed. I appreciate people who make an honest living, but belive the more people who "work the night shift" are given rooms, the more of that element you will attract. I am now staying out my remaing 2 weeks here at another, safer hotel.

title: “Ups and downs (2011)”
text:
New Yorker was a mixed bag-the pros- Its location was perfect, if you're up for walking in the big apple it's a quick walk to Times Square, 5th avenue and Empire State building along with Penn station and main subway routes very nearby. Room was comfortable enough, clean tidy and spacious enough for 2 adults and child but a visit to new York doesn't really involve spending much time in a hotel room. Was lucky enough to have an excellent view from room facing to the east which was a bonus. Breakfast at the tick tock diner attached to the hotel was again ok, not terrible but didn't blow my skirt up either but was decent enough place to start each day. Did also like that there is a ticket outlet for shows around the city.
The cons-Staff in hotel very variable, having worked in the hotel trade I realise how important a consistent front house staff is but it really was dependent on your luck, some staff very pleasant and helpful whereas others were dismissive, short and on occasion quite rude. The biggest shock was that the rooms do not have safes and you have to use safety deposit boxes in reception for valuables so this meant daily treks down to reception in the morning to wait in line to get access to your stuff while also carrying round a box key for your holiday.
In summation-was a decent enough hotel which was clean and tidy but some little things just stopped it from being great. I am planning to visit New Yorker again in 2013 because its location was excellent for event I was in town for.

title: “Does't live up to the hype of the W Hotels”
text: At first I was really excited when I saw that I had gottten the W Hotel on Hotwire, but then I discovered that it wasn't the W in Union Square which is the really nice one, but this one in Midtown. Yes, the location is very convenient to Grand Central and so you can get anywhere in the city and it's full of cool Europeans and other non-Americans, but the room couldn't be any smaller. It basically fits a queen size bed, a teeny tiny table and a teeny tiny upright closet that doesn't hardly fit any clothes with a teeny tiny bathroom. It definitely encourages you to stay out and be in the city. It is nice that there is complimentary lemongrass water in the afternoon and cider in the evenings, but it runs out quickly. The concierge was quite helpful. I would definitely not stay in this hotel had I not gotten it off Hotwire. It certainly is not worth the rack/internet rate.

title: “Not what you would expect from a Red Roof Inn”
text: My friend made the reservation so I definitely was surprised when I arrived at this wonderful hotel. JJ and Haley could not have been more helpful. The hotel was clean and the room was very large and beautifully decorated. The location could not have been better. The Continental breakfast was more than I expected. I will certainly make this my place to stay when I'm in Columbus.

title: “"Deluxe" makes all the difference...”
text:
We spent 5 nights here in July, and it was excellent. We had a deluxe, and our 2 sons (20+) were in a superior. BIG difference. Pay the few extra dollars and the better room is wonderful. Service was good, and the location was great. Easy access to the subway, and easy walking to the village, SOHO, etc. Our room was quiet, good bed, and small but very nice bathroom. The hallways are a maze, and the building was old.... but so what? Our experience was excellent. 
Frequent travelers from Dallas, Texas.

title: “Above and beyond best experience!”
text: Superior quality, comfortable, great lounge and breakfast, most friendly and helpful staff and such a perfect centralized location. Could not have been happier!

title: “Poop does happen”
text: While my family were staying there the toilet stopped up. try as we may to plunge it, nothing worked. this went on for a week. they would send someone to plunge it. finially they moved us to a different room. plus the prostitutes from the truck stop knock on your door at all times of the night.

title: “Wall Street Banker”
text:
This was the first stop we had for our 25th Wedding Anniversary trip of a life time and we could not have started in a better place - first off we were met by one of the hosts, we talked to most of them by the time we left and they were all without exception very helpful - first off they wished us a happy 25th anniversary and upgraded our room - the room was a very high standard even if I made an effort I could not fault the room - as I am not a drinker having the free mini bar ( every thing was free but the booze ) was great to be able to twist open a nice cold water at the end of a day or juice in the morning brilliant.
The fact that its a short cab or tube ride away from the hustle and bustle of the City is a very good thing - if you asked me if I would ever stay there again its 100% yes.
Why a Wall Street Banker because you can always bank on getting the best service a great bed and the finest shower in New York City at the Andaz Wall Street.
room 1012

title: “Location and price-wonderful duo!”
text: I really enjoyed my stay at Club Quarters.It is relatively cheap,close to the city center and to anywhere you'd like to see in the city.Cleanliness is another good point of the hotel.Wifi is great and there are many TV channels that you can choose from.It's a good thing that the train station where you can catch the train to/from the airport is ten or fifteen-minute walk from the hotel.Loved it.

title: “Very good, after initial difficulty”
text:
The first room they gave us smelled strongly of mold. I asked for another room and opted to pay a little extra for a suite. It was only 2:00pm and it was not ready yet. We left for a while, came back and it was still not ready. We wasted even more time in the lobby and the room that smelled like mold. It was finally ready around 6:30pm. The prior guest checked out late and the hotel was very busy that weekend. It was an issue beyond their control, but still frustrating. We ended up canceling our plans for the day after all the aggravation. The person at the Ambassador desk said that they would make some room in the minibar refrigerator for insulin and the carrying case that needs to be refrigerated. I asked the front desk person about it when I was finally given key cards to the new room, he said there would be a $35 charge for removing the items from the minibar. ?!?!? There was a second refrigerator in the suite, so it wasn't an issue. It would have been nice if he told me that. 
The junior suite was very nice. The room was large, as was the closet. It was very clean! I was a little surprised to see a tube TV, but we didn't travel to NYC to watch television. Bed bugs are always a concern when traveling to NYC. I checked thoroughly, but found none. And, more importantly, I know we didn't bring any home. We stayed for 2 nights. 
My daughter was very pleased with the "check-in" process for her American Girl doll. It was just a doll on a desk and a little slip to be filled out and put into a box. The woman at the Ambassador desk was kind and sent some cookies and juice to the room for my daughter. 
The location was great. It was far enough from Times Square to be less crowded and quieter (NYC quiet, not rural quiet), yet close enough to walk to all the attractions and shopping in and around Times Square. It was an easy walk to the American Girl Place. 
The bellmen were so helpful with directions, taxis, even a recommendation where I could buy a good pair of tennis shoes. The concierge was helpful, but there was almost always a line to speak to one of them. 
I will probably stay here again, but hope that the check-in experience and service are a little better next time. The service after the initial frustrations was fabulous!

title: “Preparedness is everything to a tired traveler”
text: Arrived at the hotel right at check in time only to be told to take a number behind some other (better customers?) guests. The Stanley Cup playlets were fullon, with a game right across the street being played the next afternoon. We had reserved a suite and it would not be ready for another two hours, we were told. We headed to the restaurant , two children in tow, only to be glared at by waitstaff when meals were taking so long and kids were restless. Great food, great waiter, hosts were not friendly and couldn't accommodate kids in the open dining/bar atmosphere with a booth, or something, say-family friendly. Whatever-restaurant did have a great atmosphere and food was delicious. Room was ready in two hours, bags were not in room along with the little goldfish promised. They were fine with it, though, as exhaustion set in. Bed linens were perfection, as was bed! Room was clean and roomy. Surroundings were surprisingly quiet. I love Kimpton Hotels, but believe this stay was not impressive because staff couldn't handle the volume or demand of it's guests this particular super busy Easter weekend.

title: “Well located cozy and grand hotel”
text: We stayed there from 5th september 2012 to 9 th september 2012. This is nice and smallish hotel and pretty classy inside. Had the club room and it was very clean and comfortable. The bathroom was compact. Great service. My husband celebrated his birthday there and they gave him some amenities of chocolate when we checked in. We had good glass bottled water throughout our stay and not just plastic bottled water like most hotels provide. The hotel faces the road and its not very high like the Hilton where we were on the 40 th floor. So if you want to sleep in its almost impossible as there is certain amount of honking you can hear in the rooms. We were on the 9th floor. Think this hotel has only about 10 or 13 floors.

title: “Satisfied with Paramount”
text: My daughters and I just returned from a week at the Paramount in NYC. The room, while small, was very clean. The bed was extremely comfortable. The staff were very friendly. In particular, thanks to the concierge for all of her advice. The lobby is under construction but that did not impact our stay at all.

title: “Very nice hotel”
text:
This hotel is very nice if you want to explore the city of Hollywood. the hotel is 2 min. walk from walk of fame and the highland center. The staff is fab! So nice and helpfull. The breakfast is fine. - the lady in the restaurant are so sweet and really enjoy talking to the guests. Poolarea a little small, but fine. When we where there, not many people where staying at the hotel, so there was plenty of sunbeds and space in the pool. The security in this hotel is very good. outside our room there was lines that would glove in case of all fire, etc. Another fine detail is the parking lot. on the walls in the parking, there are paintings of celebritys like Michael Jackson, Marilyn Monroe and Johnny Depp.
All in all very good hotel with a great location and great staff :)

title: “A LONG walk”
text: Overall the hotel was pretty nice. It had obviously been redecorated recently. The beds and pillow were VERY comfortable and seemed new. Our room was clean, although several people I was staying with had complaints (they were moved to different rooms immediately). My main complaint is just how far it is from anything on the riverwalk. It was also kind of shady walking especially early in the morning or late at night. Basically, the hotel itself was pretty nice, if you're looking for a good location, look elsewhere.

title: “Oldie Moldy”
text: This hotel is a mold factory. The carpets are filthy with stains and I had to call 3 times to get the heater/air to work. There is black mold around the shower. It may have been a good hotel at one time but not any more. And they hit you up for $8 to park per night. Just add the parking to the hotel cost and don't bother me with it - PLEASE. It does have laundry facilities and free internet. I say knock it down and build another.

title: “Big Spacious Room”
text: This hotel is very elegant -- beautiful lobby and rooms are gorgeous. Location is superb. We walked to all the main Boston spots.

title: “A pretty building and pretty high prices.”
text: My stay here was during a week long convention. My assessment is that, although the property is very attractive, the service was adequate, rather than superior and the prices were well above the norm. When our organization holds a convention, we always arrange for complimentary internet access for our members in their rooms. Not so here, as the hotel was unwilling to budge from the $13 per day charge per room. They nickeled and dimed us at every turn for the convention and banquet services throughout our stay. The house restaurant is very proud of their food, charging very steep prices for small portions of average fare. My feeling, and that of most of the other folks in our group is, this is a place to which we should not return. If we hold our convention in this city again, I'll certainly recommend we look for a different venue.

title: “Great Hotel in Boston!”
text: This is a newly constructed hotel with excellent rooms and a great location. The staff is very friendly and the rooms have to be seen to be believed. This is one of the best Courtyard properties. Lighting and decor are incredible. Parking can be a bit of a bother, but that's really the only negative. You can often find great rates on this hotel, but it can also be very expensive. It's my choice when traveling to boston

title: “Look no further...”
text: Having had a bad experience staying in a similarly priced hotel in New York before I was cautious in my expectations of this one (booked as part of a group booking). I needn't have worried. Hampton Inn Madison Square is a great hotel to stay in if you want a central base for your New York trip. The rooms are a little small if more than two folks are in them, but they are clean and comfortable. The staff are what really make this hotel a pleasure to stay in. They are fabulous to a man clearly taking their lead from the excellent manager.

title: “Pleasant Stay”
text: This is a very pleasant old hotel with a lot of history, helpful friendly staff, the rooms are a little dated but clean and tidy and everything worked. Sadly the restaurant only did breakfast and there's not much else nearby but we caught a bus to Santa Monica for next to nothing. Area a little run down but felt perfectly safe outside. Plenty of people staying so can't be as bad as some reviews say. Didn't hear any complaints or see any problems while we were there. If you want luxury and nice surroundings head for the beach area and pay a lot more money.

title: “Unparalleled service”
text: The moment we walked in the door we were cheerfully met by Elrick Mims who went above and beyond to make sure our stay was perfect for our anniversary. We had an issue with the phone in our room which turned out to be our fault - it only needed to be turned on. But still they sent the engineer, Bryan, who was gracious and very helpful when we asked his advice about the area and where we could go out to eat. Upon our return we found chocolate covered strawberries and champagne in our room. What a nice surprise. The hotel was the cleanest we have ever stayed in with the most comfortable beds. Breakfast the next morning was also wonderful. We are so happy with our stay and our service. Thank you Elrick and Bryan for helping to make our stay more than pleasant. We will definitely be going back soon.

title: “The London is an excellent hotel.”
text: The London is an excellent hotel. Great location, wonderful rooms and quite beautiful. The bar was also a good experience. The check in and check process was efficent and quick. The staff is very accomodating. This is an excellent hotel to experience New York.

title: “Excellent venue, service & location”
text: We stayed in this hotel for 3 days and for a family of 3 this was a brilliant choice, we arrived late and the check in staff on Monday were absolutely grand as they served us very professionally and very friendly.........the rooms were very clean, spacious and for 2 rooms brilliant. I will definitely recommend this hotel for families and all.....location is just around the corner of the white house which are all walking distance........a good shout goes to the barmaid for her great attitude and help especially when Miles came to assist for a night out location.........and U Street was the location to go to if you all fancy going out........top scores for this brilliant hotel, thank you all for making our stay worthwhile and mostly memorable......

title: “Excellent stay/Worth every penny”
text:
The Wingate Inn Jacksonville Airport is excellent! The front desk people were helpful, very informative, and knew what they were doing.
The rooms were huge, the queen beds were comfortable, the bathrooms well stocked, and the rooms were very, very clean. 
The indoor/outdoor pool is very nice as well as the hot tub. Best of all, the breakfast is free. Breakfast consisted of a hotbar as well as pastries and other various breakfast items.
Overall, this is a very nice hotel. Thanks Wingate Inn.

title: “Amore! The Amalfi !”
text: Our family of 4 travels quite a bit so we've had lots of hotel "experiences". The Amalfi was one of our most pleasant stays. The staff was friendly and helpful, the hotel clean, and the afternoon happy hour was divine! Each staff person we encountered seemed to enjoy their work and performed in top form. I believe this also reflects on the management - happy work environments create happy workers! Cudos to the trustworthy housekeeping staff who returned my forgotten "stuff". Some of these things were vacation purchases that still had tags on. They were returned in a timely manner intact. We will see you on our next visit to your beautiful city. The Blake Family from Winter Park, Florida

title: “Very nice and affordable but a bit noisy”
text:
The Microtel is just inside the loop on Rockville road just a couple of miles from the airport. The rooms are spacious and pillow-top beds are comfortable. They own the Kazablanka restaurant next door and the one time we ate there the food was good and plentiful. Prices and menu similar to an Outback. They serve drinks and nobody under 21 allowed but they have free delivery to your room. Service is friendly and rooms very clean. Free continental breakfast as well. 
 Only one person on the desk which can make service a bit slow. Parking is well lit and windows leak enough light that you won't need a night light. Biggest problem is noise from aircraft on nearby flight path. When the air conditioning fan is running it masks the sound pretty well but an amazing number of planes seem to come in at five a.m. What's up with that?
 For a price under sixty bucks this is a bargain. Especially if the plane noise is not a problem for you.

title: “Good place to stay in Washington”
text:
We found the service to be very good and helpful during our stay in Washington.
The location was Ok, walkable to the whitehouse or to the Dupont circle underground. 
We found the room to be larger than normal which was a nice suprise and like other guests have mentioned we liked the wine hour of 5 - 6 - a good end to a day sightseeing!
Also there are lots of cafes and restaurants just one block over on 17th street to make a lovely location for the evenings.
We would defnintely stay here again.

title: “very good - this place is as advertized”
text: Location was perfect for us. The rooms are small, but then they didn't promise big rooms. They do promise a free and filling breakfast, and they delivered that 100% every morning! There were at least two staff people constantly refilling everything, everything worked, just enough seating for everyone in the breakfast area.

title: “Unhappy with this hotel”
text: Older property that feels run down and dated. The eleavators are so slow! The staff is hit and miss on service. The only thing I liked was the location which is that the hotel is located on the outskirts of downtown and only a few minutes walk from most things.

title: “Affordable luxury and great in room dining”
text:
My partner and I stayed here for a 3 day 2 night holiday to celebrate my Birthday in January 2010. 
The Crowne Plaza Times Square is an affordable, modern hotel located in midtown right at Times Square in a fantastic location. The bed was like sleeping on a cloud and the staff were very helpful. I find NYC service staff to be the best in the world, I alway's leave wanting to come back and the staff at the Crowne Plaza were no exception.

title: “Great staff.”
text: This was a comfortable stay, with staff who went out of their way to help. Plenty of breakfast, large breakfast room, convenient to freeway, clean. Nice landscaping, nice pool area. We'll be back.

title: “Okay if you get a good price”
text: If you're okay with older, not-so-clean halls & rooms, and you get a good price, this is a decent location for proximity to SeaTac airport. Be aware that they are now tacking on an extra $7+ tax for parking. The halls & elevator are pretty run-down, and there's a vague scent in the rooms and halls of a something (old furnishings, pets, too many visitors over the years without a remodel?), I know not what. Not terrible, but definitely there. The room on the back side of the hotel was quiet, although the not-so-clean fan woke us each time it went on through the night. It was quite stuffy when we arrived in the room. So I guess I'd recommend this hotel if you are traveling cheaply, get a great rate, and don't mind some uncleanliness (as many budget travelers may be okay with). Positive: The staff was very pleasant and helpful in our limited interactions.

title: “Definetly not the hotel represented by the pictures”
text: Well to get right to the point, I wouldnt stay here again.

title: “A good budget hotel”
text:
Im a brazilian guy who travelled to NYC this last april, 2010. Id like to say I was a bit scared about reading all the reviews about Carter. I usually stay at good hotels, but as this time I was travelling to NYC just to shop and I wouldnt stay at the room for so long, I decided to book this hotel.
I read all the reviews and Carter Hotel is an old hotel, but its well located, good service and when I arrived I asked for the new rooms. They gave me the key of room 802 and to my surprise, the room was so nice. It has a good queen bed, a new carpet, my bathroom was so clean, new curtains and 4 big mirrors on it. My room was cleaned everyday and the heating was working perfect. My tv was nice too and all the 10 channels were working fine. I dont have any complain about it. I was really, really surprised about it. The shower was very hot. U just need to let it warm for 10 minutes and the front desk at the hotel were very nice too. I would stay there again...Just ask for the new rooms and u wont regret.

title: “fantastic in NY”
text: i stayed at the Sofitel due to the reviews i read on this site and i wasn't dissapointed. Iit has a great location, one block from Time Square and one block from fifth avenue, and like everybody else the beds are the most comfortable ones i have ever slept in, the rooms are huge for NY and are very well presented, i would recommend this hotel to anyone and i will stay there again next time.

title: “Great view; not ready for prime time”
text:
First off, I'd like to compliment the staff. To a person, they were all very accommodating and attentive and really helped to (mostly) turn around what was for us, initially, a horrible experience. I understand the pressure they must be under in dealing with the Hollywood Hills Hotel.
In December, we got the news that my partner had been nominated for a Grammy award. I went to look for a hotel and quickly found the Hollywood Hills Hotel and the Magic Castle Hotel. Armed with the knowledge I gleaned from their website, I thought the HHH would be a good choice, particularly because of the view and what we perceived was the style of the hotel based on the website presentation. I called the reservations line and explained we were coming out for the Grammys and were looking forward a great experience.
After a long flight across the country (and, I might add, a ferry trip from the island where we live and lots of connections), we arrived on Friday night, Feb 8. After a somewhat bewildering front desk experience (the front desk for the HHH is actually at the Magic Castle Hotel down the hill - yes, there is a pool, but use the one down here. Yes there is wifi, but it's down here, yes, there is breakfast but it's down here, etc. No mention of the Grammy nomination, something I mentioned at the reservation time. It would have been a nice touch to wish us well) off we went up at the hill (no offer of assistance with bags, finding our way in the dark, etc).
Imagine our disappointment when we saw the corridor where the room door for 203 is. The pile of US Mail buckets in the hall, the darkness, everything. Once in the room, the cracked paint, the stained rug, a dresser with a drawer missing and the rest of the drawers stuck and on the way to broken. The bed was okay, but all night there seemed to be a parade of odd smells. With all the comings and going of the neighbors outside - many of the hotel units are long term rentals - we joked, but crack house did come to mind. It was pretty bad.
The next day, we had errands to do: get our tuxes for the awards ceremony, get the tickets for the events, etc, so we were out of the room for several hours. Imagine our disappointment when we came back at almost 4 pm and the room hadn't been serviced. It was the last straw and it was at this point we reached out for a room change down the hill at the Magic Castle Hotel. I'm grateful we could be accommodated and I'll be typing up a good review next.

title: “You can do better”
text: I guess we should have known better, but the W is too hip by a factor of 100. I will blame the youth and inexperience of the staff for their lack of finesse and seeming robot like service. Check in was chaotic and uncomfortable. The rooms are fine. We stayed in a 'cool corner suite'. Our view of the water, was more a glimpse of the water. I was at war with the bed linens all night. The sheets refused to stay tucked and the duvet preferred to spend the night on the floor. We were provided with every gadget in the world...BUT NO COFFEE MAKER IN THE ROOM!! I am baffled by that oversight. There is a charge for wi-fi, which we knew, but in the 21st century that's like having pay telephones in the room. Breakfast was fine, but a deep fried poached egg is just a little too contrived for my taste. All in all, I am confident you can do better in downtown Seattle.

title: “Not at all bad for the price”
text:
Finding inexpensive hotels in the center of SFO is a challenge! The Grant Plaza is in a fairly central location (Chinatown, near Union Square) and close to Market Street. Efficiently run, the rooms are small to medium sized, reasonably well equipped, with a small desk area, and working WiFi (with access code). The carpets look a bit suspect, but overall, it seems fairly clean. It serves well to all those who wish to have economy + accommodation without spending too much time in the room.
Mattresses were a bit on the worn side.
A bit strange (at first) are the shutters (with a sign: do not open) in lieu of net curtains or curtains, but I suspect one gets used to them after a while.

title: “Unsafe, worst hotel stay ever.”
text: I requested a quite room for my family in checking in. My parents were put next to a room of 8 guys (in single room) who partied non-stop for 3 days (until on average 7am). There are also a number of prostitutes working out of the hotel, so they were awake all night as multiple men knocked/pounded on the doors down the hall, shouted out passwords, this woman's name etc. Key card access isn't required for the elevators so anyone can walk in off the street (and they do). My parents didn't feel safe at all. We've stayed at holiday inns in the past and they are usually OK. This place really needs to make the elevator key card access only and get better security.

title: “excellent hotel, staff and location!”
text:
i have stayed in this hotel numerous times. both professionally and for personal holiday! 
i recently help a conferences of more than 300+ people. the hotel was excellent on every occasional. staff is kind and helpful. hotel is clean. 
ive met with the GM Mr Paul Schwartz- the hotel is lucky to have him!
The concierge Eric got me great tickets to some sport events too!
i highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Very convenient and great location”
text:
We were very concerned about booking here but we are so happy that we did, the Hotel is very old but it was clean and neat, after getting off an 18 hour flight we were so pleased that our room was ready so we could freshen up and go sight seeing the same afternoon.
Greetings From South Africa

title: “Great hotel for business travelers”
text: The hotel is top notch. The rooms are spacious and works well for working on the road. I am especially impressed by their friendly and always great customer service.

title: “good room for handicapped person”
text: My mother who is 90 and I stayed one night on our way to Virginia Beach, VA. While she can walk-she can't walk far and also needs a bathroom made for handicapped people. We stayed in one of those rooms on the first floor. It was very helpful for my mom. We also had the breakfast buffet. It was very reasonably priced and very delicious. My brother-in-law who lives in Baltimore recommended this hotel and I will too! Great Place!

title: “Nice, but...”
text: The hotel is in an ideal location for shopping, shopping, and more shopping. Everything from discount (Ross next door) to high end (Bloomies, Nordstrom's, N-M all very close) and even a few quirky places (Xanadu Gallery in a Frank Lloyd Wright building). The staff is nice if not too effective. We were never able to connect to wi-fi and no one seemed to be able to help. Since we had not preplanned our visit it was a huge detriment as we were unable to use the internet to plan our our day. The lobby is impersonal and not particularly comfortable but the rooms are typcial of Marriott, which is a good thing. Street noise was very present even on the 22nd floor, but then San Fran is a big, bustling city.

title: “As bad as they all say...”
text: So you're thinking about staying at the Hotel Carter...Well DON'T! My girlfriend and I have stayed here twice because of the budget price that comes along with the hotel. There's a reason for it. Everything you've read about is true...and then some. I, for one, have never noticed any bugs or rats, and am grateful for that. But seeing all of the other reviews, and having stayed here twice, I can honestly believe the other reviewers. For one, the front desk people can barely understand English. I understand maybe having a little trouble speaking English or whatever, but when you are in the hotel business and over 90% of the clientele will be speaking English, it should come into consideration when hiring front desk people. However, at the same token, check in is fast, but bring reservation confirmation! The lobby is something straight out of a dance club, with blacklights and the such in the lobby itself. There are unused carpets stacked high in the right corner of the lobby as well. Very unappealing. The elevators take forever to come down, but are realtively quick once you are on them. Now to the rooms. The hallways are very dark and creepy looking, as if you are about to enter your own horror movie. Upon entering our room, there was a very musty smell. The TV barely worked, only getting maybe 3-4 channels that worked properly. We can hear some other channels, but the picture didn't come in at all. I had to physically move the TV around the room to try and get better reception, mind you this is cable reception, NOT rabbit ear antennas! As for the cleanniness of the room, it wasn't too bad, but did notice alot of dust in corners, and some fallen debris from the ceiling. The bathroom door does NOT shut. I've stayed here twice, and neither door has been able to close properly. Unbelieveable. Next, the lack of maid service. We stayed for 2 days and never once did I see or at least HEAR a maid cleaning the room. We had to get more towels from the front desk, and make our own bed. Probably a good thing, seeing as how I wouldn't want any of the people that worked there in my room to begin with. The only good thing I can report about this hotel is the Lucky Star Cafe, which is next door, adjacent to the hotel. Good food, open 24hrs a day, and relatively cheap for New York. Last but not least, a murder has recently occurred there, so now the police have stepped up their presence. This place should be condemned. I've read it used to be a homeless shelter in the 80's, and after seeing some guests in there, as well as in the elevators with me, I believe this place is still used for such activities. Please...Anyone wanting to stay here, take heed and follow everyone else's advice. It's not worth the money (even if it is cheap), as the risk to your health is overwhelming in comparison to the price.

title: “QUIET ZONE”
text:
Executive level offers serenity! No kids, no slamming doors, peaceful and quiet. Quiet is mandatory on the E.L. E.L. offers evening reception and a very upscale continental breakfast with hot items. Key access only to executive level guests. It is similar to airline private hospitality rooms. The lobby is very pretty, but don't think your room will look as nice. Never does! Charge for parking, located directly next door. We felt the vehicle would be secure, no worries there. Customer service is superb.
Rooms are nice but not Luxurious. I would upgrade to this level but not if it cost more than 40.00. I have only stayed on this level so cannot comment on standard rooms. There have been times they upgrade us at no charge. Have stayed there 4-5 times and would continue to stay there. Complimentary shuttles to LAX are clean, on time and reliable. I search for the least expensive rate and most of the time crowneplaza.com will have the same price. I believe staff must maintain the E.L to a higher standard as I do not experience stained carpets, or run down. The bathrooms could use re-tiling on the floor. No balcony. Food is expensive and I have not eaten there. Join Crown Plaza Rewards and they treat you even better. Late check out is automatic unless they are booked solid. I have always received a 2pm check out. Love the E.L. amenitity kit, including a few things like linen spray and eye mask. Linens are much nicer as well. Staff has always been very attentive and helpful

title: “Very nice, great location.”
text: I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone who has plans at the Staples Center or Nokia Theater. The staff was friendly and helpful, the rooms were clean, and there was plenty of entertainment and dining options within walking distance. They provide robes, slippers, and wonderful toiletries! The shower was beautiful but the head was not working properly and we requested a non smoking room but there weren't any available. The smell of stinky cigarettes really disgusted me but if they had a non smoking room available I honestly would not have any complaints. I recommend taking a car to and from the airport. I would stay at this hotel again for sure.

title: “OK property, decent rooms, not much more...”
text: I was a conference attendee at this hotel, located a short ride from IAH. As a Diamond Honors member, I was not upgraded to the exec level, but had access. The room is nice sized, large flat panel tv, desk area, small amount of ac plugs. Wifi was comp'd as diamond and signal was good. The bath was good sized, too. Each night there was turndown service and the ice bucket was filled, but no bottled water (made little sense). Housekeeping mediocre. I was disappointed this year (vs. last) in the exec lounge. Morning offerings were slim, nothing hot except for coffee. Evening offerings were also slim, as well. Guessing maybe cost reductions because other full-service Hiltons are better. All in all, I would rate average to slightly better.

title: “A taste of Old Europe”
text:
Mandatory hotel fee: $15/ day (to pay for bottled water and wifi), Two Double Bed fee: $20/ day, Parking fee $32/ day. Plus, taxes on aforementioned fees. For a 2 night stay, expect to pay an extra $100 in fees. 
The manager reports this is one of Travel and Leisure's World's Top 500 Hotels. Unfortunately, the hotel does not even make it into Trip Advisor San Diego's Top 40. 
Westgate actually is a nice hotel, but just not as luxurious and opulent as the website and pictures would suggest. The rooms are on the larger size. The mattresses are average. The rooms have a mini fridge and small LCD TV. Best of all, there are "free" chocolates. Overall, I think you'll have a better stay if you expect in advance to pay an extra $100 in fees and if you don't come with high expectations.

title: “Best night's sleep in years!!”
text:
Stayed here in Summer 2010 with my teenage sister.
The staff are impeccible, very polite and too eager to help.
The trip was a treat celebrating finishing our recent exams, so we asked at reception if there was a chance of an upgrade, which there was - and WHAT a view! 
The location is top notch - just a ten minute walk from Times Square.
We originally had a twin room, but we both got double beds, with the most wonderful plush duvets and pillows. We even emailed the hotel afterwards and asked where they got them from!
I'm a bit of an insomniac, especially on holiday, and I had the best sleep in years - out like a light within minutes!
We ate breakfast every morning at the Tick Tock diner next door, which was always lovely. We recommend the french toast! (The waiters are also very sweet, and since it was during the world cup, they had good banter!)
Security is tight, which is very reassuring to two young girls travelling alone. You're asked to show your keycard to get to your room - but they're still very warm and kind.
The only staff I found to be a bit rude was the concierge. She's good at her job, but was a bit impatient and huffy to some visitors whose first language was not English.
If I ever get back to New York, my first stop will be The New Yorker! :)

title: “Comfy”
text:
I had a layover in NYC for one night and got a double room.
The beds were great, and super comfy..in the middle of it all
times square..what else..for the money the best hotel
in that area,,

title: “Hyatt Place Downtown, great value”
text: Stayed just one night, while near the Key Arena (walking distance) for a concert. Also walked to a great waterside restaurant on Union Bay. Quiet, good free breakfast, and a great little studio room with desk, etc. Couldn't have been more happy.

title: “Best place to stay in Seattle!”
text: My husband and I have stayed here twice in the past couple of years. The staff is always courteous and professional. I always feel like everyone goes out of their way to make us feel comfortable! The rooms are clean, quiet, spacious and inclusive of modern immenites. The on-site restaurant is wonderful as well. We only stay here when we travel to Seattle and have come to expect great things from this hotel...in fact, we've reserved a room for 12/23 and are so excited!

title: “Pleasantly surprised.”
text: After two nights staying in the heart of Times Square, I was ready for a breather. Got a last minute great deal on this hotel so we tried it out for our last night in the city. The hotel has been remodeled recently and it looks great. The staff was friendly and helpful. Our room was immaculate and beautifully decorated. It was reasonably sized by NYC standards. The bathroom was beautiful, but tiny, with no counter space to leave toiletries. Didn't matter much for us, but multiple girls in this room might have a rough time. There was a shower, no tub. Parking was only $20 overnight, the best I've found in the city. I really enjoyed this location. It's about 4 short blocks to the subway and Central Park. It would be a great location if you're going to the city to see Broadway shows, but don't want to spend the money to stay in Times Square, or don't want to spend every waking minute in the Times Square chaos. I loved it, and will be back.

title: “this was a pleasant hotel stay”
text: staff efficient and friendly. breakfast a little lacking, but was nourishing. room temperature was difficult to control was too warm or too cold. hotel was quiet, convenient and as i said staff was very friendly and accommodating. a good stay.

title: “outstanding Hotel & Service”
text: We recently spent a few days in Austin. The initial hotel that we chose, did not meet our expectations and after spending a night, we checked out. We then inquired at the Driskill for room availability. The front desk staff was very helpful and checked us into a room at 9am and our vacation continued without a hitch. The rooms are very clean, the service impeccable, and the 1886 Café serves an outstanding breakfast. The bar is quite busy on Friday night with live music which provides an interesting people watching venue. The valet service was also very good. We will be back to this hotel.

title: “One of the Few Hotels I Can Highly Recommended”
text:
What a great stay we had at the Palomar.
The rooms were great, so good that my daughters didn't want to leave their room for the first hour or so and see the sites. They had the 2 queen room which was huge and big enough so they could spread out. Our room was the King Suite with the spa tub and it was really great. 
It's the small things that made it a great experience. The girls could order up milk and cookies in to their room for free (and they did every night). There was always hot chocolate waiting after a cold day sight seeing and fresh coffee in the morning.
The staff were excellent. Always pleasant.
We had a bit of a bump when we came in as I had booked two promotions for our two rooms which did not get caught (heads up, it appears if you punch the AAA/CAA tab on the Kimpton website it over rides all other promo coes) but the Manager, Stephane, was great and made everything just right.
The only thing where they could improve is to get some new movies for the kids to borrow at the front desk, most were old, really old. But again, they were so tired after a long day it wasn't really important.
The hotel itself is a bit far away from the Mall (where all the attractions are) for walking but the Metro is 2 blocks away and makes it really easy, faster and much more affordable than taxis to get downtown.
Based on my experience at the Palomar I am much more likely to stay at a Kimpton hotel in the future.

title: “Poor service & broadband access”
text:
The offerings are basically what one expects from the Marriott chain. Surprisingly, the broadband provision is very dated for a business hotel. The modem that was provided had a missing cable, and the customer service desk had consistently denied that the cable was missing and sent a technician to take a look only 1.5 hours later. By the time the service was available at 11.30 pm, I did not have much time to work online. What was more appalling was that the operations manager that I was referred to became frustrated and raised his voices at the situation. 
Overall, it has been a highly negative experience, and I urged the hotel to improve on its broadband access and its customer service.

title: “Great service and Garden to relax in!”
text: Very comfortable. Enjoyed the rooftop garden and the Little Tokyo restaurants attached to the hotel!

title: “Good place to rest your weary head”
text:
We stayed at SpringHill Suites in El Paso on our way to Colorado. It was very nice. I was afraid after we checked in and could hear the trains in the distance that we would have trouble with noise, but that wasn't the case. I slept like a baby. The room was clean and comfortable. Free Wi-fi which was faster than we expected from prior reviews. Walked next door for Mexican food.
We recommend this hotel.

title: “fabulous hotel !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!”
text: This was our first trip to NY and we loved it. The hotel was centrally located to many tourist spots. Front desk was very helpful and our room very spacious. We walked to alot of places, everyone was very nice. The subway is nearby and we took it several times to different parts of the city. Will return again !

title: “Enjoyed our night at the Marriott”
text: We stayed here one night because it was close to the Joe Louis Arena and we really enjoyed it. The complex is huge but there are alot of staff around to help if you are lost. We found the staff to be very helpful, friendly and professional. All you have to do is ask. The people mover was a big help to be right there in the building. We had a breakfast included in our price of the room and the breakfast is great. There are alot of choices in the buffet and very courteous staff attending to the breakfast. We would definately stay here again in the future.

title: “Westgate hotel San Diego, very quiet rooms”
text:
When I look for a hotel, one of my most important requirements is: no noise, because I'm a light sleeper. I was not disappointed by the Westgate hotel: no streetnoise at all. The rooms have a common entree with the adjacent room, which might cause inconvenience; I was lucky to have a quiet guest in that room.
The hotel is very clean, friendly people at the desk. Near the entrance a room with 2 computers with free internet-access. Very close to the Gaslamp quarter. I can highly recommend this hotel.

title: “In a great location”
text:
We ended up at this hotel after a home stay with a friend didn't turn out. 
Anyhow, the hotel is perfectly located for people wanting to look around Hollywood. The room was a good size and very clean. The beds were super comfortable. Staff were friendly and helpful. 
Tip...get to breakfast early as seats are limited (we managed to share with other people though)
Only two slight negatives 1) the wifi connection was free but a little unreliable in our room. 2) our room was non-smoking but it smelled somewhat like it was a smoking room in a former life. Neither of these issues were deal breakers (despite my aversion to cigarette smells) we enjoyed our stay and would recommend the hotel.

title: “Close to many attractions including S.D. airport”
text:
