We just wanted to be close to the airport and Howard Johnson has a great location plus a shuttle.
Staff was very nice and best of all, Howard Johnson provides free parking!!!

title: “Lovely Little Hotel in a Fantastic Location”
text: I just returned after a great one night stay at The Pearl. The hotel lobby was under construction, so the doorman ushered us up the stairwell and to a makeshift check-in desk. We knew the hotel was under construction and this was the only evidence. The staff was friendly and helpful. The doormen called us taxis and eagerly helped with the luggage and the front desk greeted us each and every time we passed. We requested a bucket of ice and it was promptly sent to our room. Snacks and drinks were available on the mezzanine all day. This was a plus for me, as I was traveling with two small children and it was great to grab a quick glass of iced tea between sightseeing. The complimentary breakfast was simple and convenient. We missed the complimentary wine hour, but when we returned in the evening, a staff member offered me a glass of red wine before we retired to our room. The location is fabulous. The street was quiet yet we were only a block away from Broadway. We walked to Times Square, Rockefeller Center, American Girl, Bryant Park, and Grand Central Terminal. The rooms were sleek and modern...The bed was very comfortable. Little perks like Aveda bath products and a Keurig coffed pot were nice touch. Excellent restaurants and bars are right around the corner so you don't need one directly in the hotel. They don't offer room servicel, but you can order from 3 local restaurants for a very small fee....I prefer this to tired room service any day.... Great little hotel....The price was a bit steep, but I guess you get what you pay for: A Lovely, Clean, New, Modern Hotel in a Fantastic Location....

title: “GREAT hotel and conference space”
text:
I recently attended a conference at the Baltimore Hilton and was very impressed. You can tell the rooms were updated recently. The rooms were spacious and mine even had a new car smell! 
I do have to comment on the conference aspect of the trip. We had over 550 conference attendees and I do not know if the dining staff was prepared to handle us! We had to wait on lines for our drinks (cash bar) and it really irritated me that I had to wait online for 15 minutes just to get one drink. I missed the beginning of my dinner with my colleagues and had to sit with strangers because of these ridiculously long lines. I would seriously attempt to work on the flow of these practices. 
Parking cost was a little high (this was the off season..no game in town and we still had to pay $14.00 for parking).

title: “Easy access to convention center; Business appropriate”
text:
I did a Hotwire deal: $238 for (3) nights. 
Staff was really personable. When I travel for business I really don't "challenge" the staff with any special requests or demands. Clean room, decent internet, free parking, meal choices nearby: That's about all I need. 
Room was clean. This was remarkable: NO SMELL! Nothing! No chemicals, deodorizers, carpet shampoo. Lots of dogs and I saw a cat being taken to the car. No animal smell!
King bed was fine. Shower was decent. Breakfast in lobby was OK. Go here for a great breakfast: Carolina Prime Steakhouse. Close-by & cheap, fabulous, hot!
I would stay here again if it were appropriate and it was deal! I haven't stayed at a La Quinta in years.

title: “Best concierge”
text: David Bach was a font of information for our visit to NYC. He recommended neighborhoods to see based on what we were interested in seeing. He gave us directions to get from one place to the next and wrote it all out on our map. He's dining recommendations were fantastic - beautiful places with excellent food at decent prices. He gave us options for places we could walk to around the hotel but also got us into places that are very well known outside of NYC. He really made our experience great and made us want to come back to continue the adventure.

title: “The room was very small, hotel employees were very accommodating and friendly.”
text:
I met my husband at the Microtel Inn and Suites for the weekend (January 28-31, 2011) as he was laying over there in between job assignments. We stayed in a regular room. The room was VERY small, not sure what the suites are like. I'm not sure what size the bed was, it seemed between full and queen. It didn't seem as big as my queen bed at home. The room was clean and the bed linens were clean (we asked them to change everything out). However, the sheets on the bed looked very worn (thin) and old. There was free wireless internet in the room and also a computer with internet access and printer in the lobby area for guest use. The room was very brown. (dark brown carpet in a print, dark brown drapes with a different print). The t.v. is up on top of the closet /cabinet so you have to either sit in the chair and look up at it or lay in the bed to watch it. This hotel is very convenient to the aiport, resonably priced, and okay just for a brief layover. It was hard to be cooped up in that little room for too long. I wouldn't suggest it for a romantic getaway. 
The hotel staff was very accommodating and friendly. (One of the desk clerks even helped me spring my surprise arrival on my husband when I got there which was funny.) They provided free shuttle service around the area and if only one person was on duty at the desk, shuttle service was provided by the Wyndham Hotel next door. Room service is also provided by the Wyndham Hotel and could be charged to your room. The Wyndham shuttled us to a restaurant about 10 miles in to town for dinner one night and returned to pick us up when we finished dinner and called them. (We didn't want to venture out too far because of El Paso's close proximity to the Mexican border town of Juarez and all the violence there.) There is no guest laundry facility at the Microtel but, we were allowed to use the laundry facility at the Wyndham hotel. 
The Microtel provided a nice complimentary buffet style breakfast./snack (waffles, muffins, pastries, boiled eggs, fruit, juice, milk, and coffee). We also had a couple of meals at the Wyndham while we were there which were pretty good.
I think that this hotel is owned by the Wyndham Hotels now. If so, The Wyndham should update the rooms a little and invest in better sheets for the beds. A laundry facility on site would be a great convenience also. I know that the Microtel isn't meant to be as luxurious as the Wyndham Hotel for the price that you pay but, a few changes would make it much more appealing.
The friendly and accommodating staff was the highlight of my weekend stay at The Microtel Inn and Suites, El Paso Airport. Thanks for the great friendly service.

title: “A very nice stay at Drury Charlotte North”
text: We thought we would try this Drury after an excellent experience in San Antonio earlier this year. This Drury is in an easy to reach location right off the interstate. We had no trouble finding it after a day at Carowinds. The lobby is clean and we were promptly greeted by friendly desk personnel. The air-conditioned hallways were quite welcome from the summer heat. The room was clean and had a large screen LG televsion with free HBO which we enjoyed that evening. The carpets were clean, The bathroom and shower area were very clean with everything functioning properly. I though tthe bed was too soft but my wife loved it. Individual preferences. The wall controlled thermostat worked fine and controlled the a/c to our liking. The small microwave did it's job and the small fridge kept drinks cool but was not up to freezing ice cubes in the compartment provided (too weak or worn out). It was also a bit noisy in the quiet of the night at bedtime. The evening snacks in the lobby (5:30 - 7:00) were fun and typically cheap but we don't rate motels on food quality. It is just a perk. The same with the breakfast. If you don't want to drive anymore after arrival there is a TGIF restaurant within 200' of the parking area. No streets to cross, just walk over. There is also a steakhouse but across the street. The pool area is different as it is both an indoor/outdoor pool. Not particularly inviting but it is there for those that want to enjoy a swim. For those that arrive in nice cars or bring show cars to the nearby Charlotte Speedway the parking area was safe and protected by shrubbery and decorative iron fencing. No issues on the night we stayed. We would definitely recommend this Drury and we will be back.

title: “No Bedbugs at this Hotel”
text: Stayed for a weekend for the US Open and the rooms were very clean and none of us experienced any bugs whatsoever. Check out this hotel as one you can rely on for a comfortable, quiet stay. The staff was great and although the rooms are smaller than some I've stayed in, it had all the amenities.

title: “Beautiful Hotel”
text:
Stayed for a conference at McCormick Place. Hotel eludes classic elegance. The hotel was very nice and the rooms were clean. 
My room was on the 8th floor with a view of the other rooms in a u-shape. Had to keep my windows closed at all times. The room was spacious with 2 double beds,2 full bathrooms, flat screen tv and nice pc with flat monitor. Internet was not free and I did not find a safe in the room. Be sure to request a view when you check in. 
The only positive about my room location is that it was on the same floor as the health club. There were several elevators and the layout of the hotel was easy to navigate even though it takes up a city block.
I found the location of the hotel to be great. You can walk to the restaurants by the river, it is within a 1 mile radius and it has the lovely park right across the street.
The hotel is undergoing renovations so there weren't many dining options except the pub. I didn't try any of the restaurants nor room service but the bartender in the lobby bar was excellent. She was quick and mixed great drinks.
The front desk and bell service reps were very nice and both individuals at the concierge desk were extremely helpful and friendly. 
I would stay here again mainly for the location.

title: “A solid 4-star hotel in Manhattan”
“Excellent Hotel!!!”
text: I have been residing at Extended Stay Northridge for over 2 years. I love the staff, Ashe, Annjannett, Nahid, and Gen, are all so very nice. The hotel is kept very nice and clean and Housekeeping Staff is very courteous and helpful. The staff, especially Ashe, is very accommodating, understanding and easy to communicate with and very good at problem solving. Because this has been my home for the past 2 1/2 years, I have always felt comfortable and safe. Any and all complaints are immediately addressed and the entire staff's aim is to make sure their clients are satisfied. I would definitely recommend ESAN as it is strategically and conviently located and a great place to stay.

title: “Great location. Can't wait for renovations!”
text:
This is a nice boutique hotel that is a short walk to just about everything. The room we had was a bit small but I'm not in Boston to sit in the room. The staff was very polite and helpful and the bar is nice. The rooms just need some tweaking. There was still spackle on the bathroom wall where they had moved a towel bar. The bathroom light was mounted off to one side of the mirror and only lighted half the mirror. The caulk around the toilet and sink was sloppy or missing. The beds were spotless and nicely covered. Unfortunately the shower had mold around the tiles and really wasn't cleaned very well. There was no noise at night though.
The parking is rediculously expensive considering the hotel size. $44 per night is crazy. I stayed at a similar hotel on the other side on Quincy market and only paid $23.
This hotel has good prices and great potential. They just need to retrain the maintenance and housecleaning staff to be more detail oriented. I was told that they will be undergoing a complete renovation starting in November and ending in April. We'll be back to see how they did.

title: “Great location”
text: This hotel is centrally located in mid-town Manhattan, and right above Grand Central Station. In terms of being in the center of the action, and easy to get around from, it is excellent. Rooms are OK.

title: “Almost didn't book”
text: PLEASE don't look at the pictures that are on the tripadvisor website for this hotel. I saw them when we were told we were staying there for my son's football tournament. They are super old and look NOTHING like this hotel really was. The rooms are newly renovated and gorgeous!! New carpeting, granite in the bathroom with central air. Definitely would go back to this hotel again if in the area. I should have taken new pictures to post to do it justice.

title: “location location”
text:
March 9-12 2012:
Our group was six, four adults and our grandchildren (5 and 2). 
First thing to say is that in my opinion this is not a business hotel, and cannot be judged on those criteria. 
You have to choose carefully in New York. That said, I think this is an excellent tourist choice, particularly for families. 
There were several student parties and coach tourists. 
As the title says, location is everything. On 7th Ave and 55th St, it is a few blocks easy walking distance to Central Park (going north) and Fifth Ave (east). Rockerfeller Centre five blocks south-east. Going due south gets you to Times Square in about twenty mins-that is with a buggy/stroller. Carnegie Hall is a few yards away.
There is a Subway on the doorstep.
The M7 bus gets you to Broadway and down to Macy's/Empire State Building easily.
The M5 goes from Fifth Ave right down to Battery Park and the ferries. Coming back it stops by the hotel.
Anyway,the hotel.
I was aware of differing reports but, like most things, you need to trust your nose and try it for yourself. I liked the "olde worlde" mature look of the place. As my grandson observed when we drew up, "wow this is a fancy hotel!". It does have charm.
Check-in was easy, and we were allocated two rooms on the 12th(top) Floor of the East Wing. I would guess this is the older wing, and definitely not as high as the main wing.
The basic double room for my wife and I was very clean, well decorated, with good quality bedlinen. It was definitely "New York size", which we found perfectly adequate. The shower was spotless and worked well.
My son, his wife and their two children thoughtfully were given a suite right next door.This was huge, with a fridge and microwave.
No good views, but facing way from the 7th Ave traffic meant minimal external noise. 
The internal walls let through some noise. 
I am struggling to find any downsides. The only potential irritant I can think of is that the two East Wing elevators are quite slow, and not that big. This was not a problem for us, but if you get stuck behind a school party...
We did not use the diner on the ground floor, so unable to comment, but it did seem pretty full up. Prices not bad compared to what I have paid on other NYC hotels. 
No free wi-fi, unfortunately. USD 5.00 for half an hour using your own machine, or there are five desktops down near reception, not sure of the rates.
Check out was again seamless, and storing your cases between check out and pick up was a well oiled operation.
Overall I was extremely pleased with our stay, and would consider this my obvious choice for a base if/when we vacation again in NYC.

title: “Quirky hotel, a little tired.”
text:
Stayed here with my husband whilst on holiday. Location is handy for all the sites of San Francisco.
Our room was on the top floor and quite big. Felt very stuffy. As soon as breakfast was being cooked the smell permeated all the way up to our room. Nice fireplace. Bathroom was average, although had nice toiletries. Main problem was outside noise as the windows are single glazed. 
Breakfast is included in the price and was ok. Hot food was very greasy, croissants a bit stale. 
In all a pleasant hotel and v good value for money. I wouldn't stay here again because of the noise and stuffiness.

title: “Cozy and great location”
text: We stayed at the Good Night Inn for 4 nights the staff was very helpful with any questions we had about the area and gave us some good advice on place to eat. It was close to the beach and sea world were we spend most of our time and overall our experiance was wonderful.

title: “Budget hotel...not bad.”
text:
First of all, there is nothing WRONG with Hotel 17. The place is very clean, the check in was fine, the bathrooms in good shape. Rooms are a bit worn, but clean and the bed was comfortable. But...for the price I paid, I could have gotten more bang for my buck.
I booked a double room, thinking my daughter might be coming. I ended up by myself, but figured it would be nice to have the extra space. However, my room was obviously a single into which they had crammed a double bed. Very cramped. To be fair, the next day, they did offer to switch my room, but I was on my way out and did not have the time. I asked for a reduction in price, but they would not do this. So it seems that a (VERY) "small double" is the same price as a standard room. 
There is no lounge, no bedside light, no bedside table, no facilities for making coffee/tea, no refrigerator, no breakfast. Basically a room. They do have free WiFi and there was a small TV in the room.
I paid about 50% LESS at the Larchmont (just on the other side on Union Square) for the same size room which included bathrobe, slippers, a lounge with free computer, a bedside light and table, flatscreen TV and breakfast. I have also stayed up at the Chelsea Lodge in a double room which included a private shower and was cheaper by about 25%.
So, in my opinion, the Hotel 17 needs to add a few more niceties or reduce their price to get more than 3 stars as a budget hotel in NYC.

title: “Tired, In Need of a Total Rehab, but Friendly and Helpful Staff”
text: I must admit paying 55.00 for this hotel through priceline, for one night following a business trip (couldn't see spending 200+ at the Hilton for one more night; way over-priced there). This hotel, the former "Lord Baltimore" is a "grand" hotel. But it is simply tired. Carpets are worn; paint shows many coats and chips and re-painting. Elevators are ancient. But I must say that from the moment I walked into the lobby, the staff could not have been friendlier and more helpful; actually outstanding. My room was OK. Bed was one of those sleep number deals; the last thing I want to think about in a hotel is what my sleep number is. The bathroom was in need of updating; bad and dirty grout in the shower/tub surround. And under the bathroom sink was one of those stainless steel mini-trashcans with the pedal to open it. Really? It was old and filthy. It would be SO MUCH BETTER if this fine staff had a building of which they could be proud. Radisson, it would be worth the money to renovate this aging edifice. Kudos to the great staff. The heart "Good morning, sir!" when I walked into the lobby in the morning was much appreciated. I would not consider paying more than 55.00 per night here.

title: “Stay away from this place!”
text: This place is awful. I am in my room right now, it is after midnight, and the music from the club in the lobby is so loud that items in the room are literally VIBRATING. I spoke to the person at the desk and then the manager and they both told me that's how it always is and that the music goes until 2 AM. I was told that they do keep ear plugs on hand to help the guests deal with the music. He was serious. He then said that the music is usually even louder. So I am paying 500 dollars to sleep in a hotel that I can't sleep in. I wish I could record how loud this music is. I can't believe they aren't up front and honest about it. And my room is stifling hot without any AC. This place has ruined my trip to NYC.

title: “Underwhelming but not a bad choice”
text: My husband and I stayed 3 nights at the Mayflower Park in July 2006. I chose it for the very central location -- walking distance to the Pikes Market, Space Needle, ferry terminal, monorail, etc.; the price-point -- about $215/night plus tax; and the good reviews here and elsewhere. The biggest problem was that our room's air conditioning was not working. It was close to 80 degrees in the room. An engineer came up twice, but the problem was never fixed. Ultimately, the engineer admitted to us our room had a problem as did another room on our floor. We had to ask to be moved to another room -- no offer was made. The substitute room looked out at a brick wall. It appeared to be a single -- full bed, not queen; one nightstand; no table by the reading chair as in our first room. The room rate was adjusted down, but it was a lesser room, so it just ended up feeling like the hotel didn't care more than the minimum necessary. On Sunday, our room was not made up until 4:30 in the afternoon, after we had been out all day and returned hoping to relax for a while. When our bill was prepared, we were incorrectly double-charged. The hotel provides one computer for free internet access, but it is not easily found and no one told us about it. Not awful problems, just annoying. The Mayflower is a place with lots of brass trim, big flower arrangements in the lobby, and you have to call room service if you want ice. If that's your style, and if the air conditioning in your room is working, I think you'll find the Mayflower to be a fair choice. If you're like me, and favor modern accommodations, no opulent frllls, consistent quality, and a feeling you are a valued customer. . . you may end up deciding the Mayflower Park is a bit underwhelming.

title: “DON'T EVER VALET your Car Here!”
text: The WORST part of our experience was the valet. We were told that it was $48 to valet our car! We were handed our valet ticket and a confirmed price of $48. When we checked out the price increased to $54 due to some 25% service tax on top of that. This is very misleading. When we got into our vehicle all of the mirrors and seats (both driver and passenger) were significantly changed. Again, the passenger seat which should not have been occupied had been moved and there was women's hair in the vehicle. To our knowledge there were no women on the valet staff. We decided to look over the car and we discovered that our bumper had been SIGNIFICANTLY DAMAGED. Many DEEP SCRATCHES, GOUGES, AND MISSING PAINT. We notified the Valet Manager and he pulled out this claim ticket with the outline of a vehicle pointing out that someone had marked scratches on the bumper. We were NEVER showed this ticket prior to leaving the car with valet and we did not sign any such paperwork because it was completely FALSIFIED. My bumper DID NOT have any such scratches all over it prior to my arrival at this hotel. For a price of $54 to park my vehicle I would expect the car be returned in better condition then when we left it. This hotel is deceitful and has horrible customer service and a valet department that should be trained and held accountable for their actions instead of LYING ABOUT DAMAGING a vehicle. I hope that at the VERY LEAST they pay for the damage they caused to my car.

title: “Great Experience at the Ocean Villa Inn”
text: I stayed at the Ocean Villa Inn at the end of May 2012. My experience was extremely enjoyable. My husband and I were traveling with our two dogs. The first floor rooms have direct access to a fenced-in grassy area, where friendly dogs are allowed off leash. The location has direct access to Dog Beach. The hotels location within the Ocean Beach area is also convenient to numerous local restaurants, coffee shops, and small grocers - all within easy walking distance. The hotel's dog wash area provides dog towels and shampoo. This is a great feature, when your dogs have been playing on the beach all day. Ocean Villa makes traveling with you pet even easier. All the staff were very friendly and accommodating. The room itself is very basic, but perfect if your traveling with dogs. The room and bathroom were very clean. The in-room refrigerator was very convenient as well. If you are traveling with your dogs, this is the place to stay!

title: “it's worth the peace of mind and convenience”
text:
If you are with a family member or friend undergoing surgery or hospital stay at the Mayo Clinic, I highly recommend this inn. We were a little hesitant at the price, given that we could get much cheaper elsewhere in Jacksonville, even places that were relatively close, but there is nothing like being able to walk down the corridor to the Clinic from your room to visit your loved one. We would be able to visit multiple times per day, including a quick stop in after we had returned from dinner, and it was no big deal if my father-in-law was at therapy or tests, or asleep. We also didn't all need to go at once; one of us could go upstairs, and others follow as worked for them as we all juggled doing work on our computers with the free wifi (or cabled access from the desk). 
There were three of us, so my sister-in-law slept in the living room, which has a full-size kitchen and fridge with plates, utensils, etc., for your use. We didn't go grocery shopping, but it was nice to have the fridge for beverages and leftovers, and snacks. If you were staying longer, it could save you money in the long run to be able to stock the fridge for your stay. 
Breakfast was fine - Holiday Inn Express or Hampton Inn level free breakfast - waffle iron, bagel,s fruit, cereal, sausage patties, boiled eggs, etc. 
There is no pool on the property - but it does have a small exercise room with two treadmills and a stationary bike. 
It's also very convenient to the beach area for dinner choices to get off the property for a bit. 
The only bad thing about the arrangement was that the bathroom is off the bedroom, so my sister in law would need to come in through the bedroom to go to the bathroom in the middle of the night. That's it. the only complaint. 
So - spring for the extra and enjoy the convenience and ease of being close to your loved one.

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text:
Very nice, classy hotel. All of the staff is friendly and helpful.
The rooms are clean, large and comfortable. Nice location.
You must eat at Sullivan's when here - it is only a block away.
I would stay here again in an instant.

title: “Convenience & reliability”
text:
Perfectly clean & beautiful rooms, lovely staff who were always ready to help or give us advice. 
Came over from New Zealand to spend a few days in Venice Beach & LA before flying over to the Arnold's in Columbus, Ohio. Then stayed an extra night here on way back to fly out again to NZ.
Food pretty average in restaurant but plenty of fast food & restaurants within walking distance. Gym great for morning sessions of cardio. Chilled water. Money machine in lobby for $ extractions!
Used laundry, not a problem. Microwave available in laundry.
McDonalds right outside for our morning oatmeal to mix with protein powder post gym session!
Happy Campers!
Loved location as also close to LAX & bus stops to explore the coast & city.
Loved the city & the weather! Would definitely consider staying here again when I return one day;)

title: “Stylish and perfectly located”
text: Very nice hotel, modern, stylish, clean and friendly. The best is the location: from our room we could look down Broadway to Times Square. There is a small wellness area and a cool bar on the top floor with a great view!

title: “Pennsylvania Six Five Sucked Sucked Sucked”
text:
This hotel may be immortalized in song, but its 21st century incarnation is AWFUL. The lobby is clean, but the hallways and rooms are utterly filthy. Once you step off the elevators, you may as well be visiting a fleabag motel off I-90 in the midwest somewhere.
A complete ripoff...and I don't care about the ideal location or the storied history -- this hotel is being marketed as a great value and safe place to stay in NYC. FUGGEDABOUTIT. This place is a complete dive.

title: “Palace with closets optional”
text:
Recently we stayed at The Palace Hotel for 3 nights. At check in, we asked for an upgrade since we are Starwood Preferred Guests. We were informed that the hotel was crowded and there were no upgrades available. The woman at the front desk told us that she was giving us a very nice room with a courtyard view. The very nice room was a cramped small room with no table next to the bed and a large piece of furniture that was the room closet positioned on the side of the bed. The courtyard view was a view of a roof with no greenery. After a long day of travel, we did not feel like changing rooms, but the room we were given was not satisfactory. The man at the front desk was very understanding and located a room that was a similar size with a built in closet. The second room was on the small side, but the built in closet made the room acceptable. The hotel is large and did not seem crowded. We did not want to pay for the hotel parking which was over $50/night. We were informed that there was a self park garage a block from the hotel that was $25/night. The garage was fine and the cost was as advertised. My wife was not happy that the route to the garage which was behind the hotel was frequented by homeless people and drug dealers. We had no issues.
The location of the hotel near Union Square is very convenient. We would consider staying at the Palace Hotel again if the room rate is below $200/night.

title: “Christmas in June”
text: The warm welcome we received from the valet continued during our check-in when we were surprised with the news that we had been given a complimentary upgrade to the Elizabeth Taylor suite. We indeed felt like stars during our short stay. The suite is decorated in a minimilist, white, modern aesthetic that encourages an appreciation of the awesome views of the Chicago skyline and Lake Michigan. The mattress and linens are of the finest quality and the large balcony includes loungers and a wrought-iron table and chairs. The public areas of the hotel are also lovely & include areas to relax with a drink or use your computer. We enjoyed brunch at the Pump Room & while the Croque Madame was too heavy on the cheese, the Eggs Benedict with salmon was wonderful. The service was polite and welcoming. If you are looking for a smaller, boutique hotel in a quiet location, book a room at the Public.

title: “Not so hot”
text: We did get an okay price for this hotel ($100/nt.) on Priceline. Parking was $30 a night, and the staff always had their hands out for tips. When we arrived in our room (the only "update" was a flat screen TV), there was a fridge still full of someone else's food, and items remained in the drawers. When we called staff, they did take care of it right away, but with zero apologies or compensation (drink coupon???/coffee coupon???). The mirrored wall in the bathroom had a large crack in it. The lobby was very nice with an open bar area and lots of seating. We didn't use the pool area at all. The view was excellent, and it was very quiet. The beds were very comfy. Upon check-out, the desk attendant didn't inquire about our stay, say thank you or good-bye (and I had a pleasant enough look on my face). I'd sooner stay someplace with a bit more personality and not so much stuffiness.

title: “Hyatt Regency Chicago- Somewhere between a strong 3.5 and a weak 4.0 stars”
text: I stayed three nights at the Hyatt Regency Chicago to attend a conference. I will start this review with what I liked least about the hotel. The hotel is divided into the east and west tower, which would normally be a non-issue for me. However, attending conference sessions was somewhat cumbersome and a tad bit confusing. By the time most attendees had a good handle on where the various ballrooms and conference rooms were the conference was over. Though the bed was comfortable and I had a great view of the river and downtown Chicago, the room was somewhat basic. Other than these two minor things, the hotel was very satisfactory. The hotel staff was courteous and went out of their way to ensure guests’ needs were met. Also, the atrium was beautiful and the Big Bar has a great view of the city and good cocktails. All in all, my stay at the Hyatt Regency Chicago was a good one. I would return to this hotel again.

title: “First time in Boston”
text: Thank you Four Seasons for making my visit to Boston so special. From the moment I arrived I knew that I was in for a wonderful experience. I cannot fault the service, the room and facilities - first class without being pretentious. I recommend the Belgian waffles with mixed berries and warm maple syrup for breakfast - to die for! I loved Boston and the Four Seasons and look forward to next time.

title: “If you like walking its a good hotel”
text: its between airport ($16-20 ride) and downtown. The green bus tour stops at this hotel and you can buy the $36 two day pass in the lobby. It makes 24 stops around the city. Get off/on, bus every 15-20min. Parking at hotel is over $40/day. $15 tax to Italian restruant area. Too many good restruants to chose from. USS Constitution, north Church. Harvard, Cheers are on bus stop tour.

title: “perfect location”
text: Very friendly and helpful staff. Clean, comfortable rooms. Great Location. Walking distance to everything from a grocery store, convince store, pharmacy, public transportation (all within one block) and most of all...Fisherman's Wharf. My only complaint is the room was a little small. But then really didn't spend much time there.

title: “Great vibe. Great style.”
text: Love this hotel and will try to always stay here when in NYC. It has a darkly lit and very populated lobby with a dj and a cool bar. You enter and you feel transported to another planet. Room rates range depending how big and comfortable you want it. But all look modern and stylish. You literally feel energized at this hotel.

title: “Great room with Great Price”
text: Every year we take a cruise. Our bus leaves from Jacksonville. This hotel goes above and beyond to assist us in anyways possible to make us comfortable. Rooms are extra clean. Staff is super courteous. It's like a home away from home.

title: “Great location - Good breakfast”
text:
This place is in an excellent location, you can walk to everything. We are a family of 5 and had the larger suite, it suited us well. We arrived early about 10 .30 am - no problems our room was ready & speedy check in. Breakfast had a good & plentiful selection.
We had a ground floor room, which was convenient. We did not have a car - you could walk or use public transport easily.We hired bicycles just around the corner.
It was a little more than we expected to pay,but was good value for a family of 5 compared to others we had researched.

title: “Wonderful!!!”
text: This hotel is wonderful! From the start, the doorman/valet was extremely helpful. Although the room was not ready (I was a couple of hours early), the front desk clerk was very friendly and helpful and pointed us to a fantastic restaurant. The nightly happy hour was great--unlimited drinks! and the breakfast was the BEST I've had at any restaurant. The room was great, the bed was comfortable and it was centrally located to a lot of museums and within walking distance to many, many sights. This was my second stay here and I will always try to book this hotel!!

title: “Very nice Hotel, the quality expected from Hilton.”
text:
Extremely convenient location from the Charlotte ring road, (i77). 
Easy parking available, nice reception, helpful check in staff who covered all I would need to know including the invitation to the Managers wine reception that evening.
Booked an executive room on the 7th floor, which I think is well worth the extra cost.
The room was very impressive, well equipped and clean, everything I expected of the Hilton name.
The executive lounge was convenient with the usual complimentary snacks, aperatives and drinks, and the lounge staff were very pleasant. 
I did not eat at the restaurant as I was going out with friends for dinner, however the menu at Davinci's looked really good, (maybe next time). I was recommended the breakfast buffet but had all I needed available in the executive lounge, (complimentary).
There is a small pool and sun deck at the back of the Hotel, the bar area is small and open plan, all in all a really nice Hotel in really convenient location, I would certainly recommend it for anyone needing a room in this area or just passing through Charlotte.

title: “Good Option”
text:
Good option to choose!
Nice place, near of union square.
Could be cheaper but is good.
Quiet room and clean room!

title: “I am made to feel special when I'm here.”
text: Great staff, good food and excelent service. Everyone is very friendly with an upbeat attitude.

title: “Tripadvisor is right, Hotwire is wrong”
text:
I booked this hotel on Hotwire: a 3.5 star hotel near the airport for$75, and a "customer favorite". 
It is near the airport.
It is a multi-building hotel, rather like those 1980s two-floor all-wood condos. I didn't hear any other-guest noise like the other reviewers, but I may have been just lucky. 
There is no elevator, not a big deal, but annoying. The room was OK -- usual Holiday Inn, always something broken, but not bad -- and the bed was very nice. The TV was in a hole in the wall way off to the side of the bed. OK, I know that's a whine, but it's really hard to see. Another whine from me is the parking lot: it is a strange labyrinth, with arrows pointing in weird ways and, I think, some blind alleys with no "legal" means of exit.
I guess $75 is not too bad. But it is a 2.5 star hotel. I've reviewed it for Hotwire, and I hope their "customer favorite" gets erased.

title: “Very good for the price but...”
text: Stayed at the Rodeway Convention Center for a week in February. Chose it because it looked to be very close to the LA Convention Center, clean, and affordable - was on a very tight budget. The room was very clean and as it appeared in the photos online. The staff were pleasant and helpful and overall the room was good value for the rate. I wouldn't stay there again though - the area the hotel is situated in is rather depressing, not dangerous (I live in another big city) but very run down. I also had to take a bus to get to the Convention Center everyday as it is too far to walk, so not that convenient. Anywhere in LA without a car is a nightmare, so that's not the hotel's fault, but the name is misleading, it really isn't that close to the Convention Center. One more thing - the breakfast was terrible, a choice of filter coffee, toast and one kind of fruit self-served in a really grim little room. If you're on a budget, a cheap, clean place to stay but if you can at all afford to stay somewhere nicer, do.

title: “A great stay in the city!”
text:
I can't say anything bad about the Monaco. 
Lots of good things to say:
Friendly and accommodating staff.
Nice touches like the morning coffee service and flavored ice water in the lobby. 
Good quality wifi. 
Comfortable bed. 
Aveda bath products!
Centrally located, close to Union Square and transit. 
VERY dog friendly!
I wouldn't hesitate to stay here again.

title: “Mark Hopkin$ mi$$e$ the mark”
text: We stayed at the Mark Hopkins last Friday night after attending Roger Waters' The Wall at AT&T park. The hotel is nice, and we had a great city view from the 14th floor, but it lacked that something special we were looking for. We stayed at the Fairmont about a month ago and found that to be a much more enjoyable experience over all. We did get up to the Top of the Mark for a martini before the show, which, while pricey ($50 for two martinis, chips and salsa) the view was outstanding! Don't bother with eating there though. We made the mistake of going there for breakfast on Saturday and spent $70 on two buffet breakfasts that were not very good. Everything was kept warm in chafers, including waffles and pancakes which were soft and spongy, The frittata was down right gross. The only thing that looked good and tasted good was the fruit selection and yogurt parfait. We wound up down at the Ferry Building a little while later and are kicking ourselves for not dining there (Roli Roti porcheta sandwich and Blue Bottle Coffee, anyone????), not to mention the lovely and bustling farmers market scene.

title: “beat generation and art deco boutique hotel in heart of north beach”
text:
i'll preface this by chiming in with the articulate details of other posts....north beach is small. the rooms are not large. if you want a palace, go spend a million bucks at south of market or on union square.
this hotel was perfect for us = we booked 3 rooms (fiancee and me, maid of honor, and mother of the bride) a few months back for our oct 21st wedding in san francisco and we stayed two nights. the location is unbeatable: right on columbus avenue nestled between faboo italian restaurants, bakeries, and some of the best damned espresso you'll ever encounter. the hotel itself is so eclectic, so charming in its design...total throwback decor art deco style with amazing photographs of the beat city crowd of the 50s. the lampshades in the hallways are covered in old newspaper, very artsy, historical, and warm. no, there isn't a fridge or a mini bar. who needs one with stella bakery literally 2 steps out the front door and all the restaurants north beach and san francisco have to offer. the bed is comfortable (though i always without fail find hotel pillows too soft for my liking so i just bring my own firm ones from home!...yes, we drove to san francisco, didn't fly....), the bathrooms are totally art deco sexy (no tub but again, we didn't care...) and the 6p sherry was a particularly groovy touch.
the best part of hotel boheme is the old school service. gary and stan took care of us throughout our stay, keeping up with the congrats and good moods for our nuptials, and were so friendly and positive, we really felt appreciated. best of all, an hour before the wedding ceremony when my fiancee realized he left his suit slacks at home, gary? or was it stan? called a cab service for us, and when no one picked up on the line, he ran outside and hailed my fiancee and maid of honor a cab and shot them down to a men's dress store, even going so far as to dial us in with someone he knew there. between these two guys, they saved the day.
also worth noting: they did not charge our cards until we checked out...this was great for us being a couple saving up hard and long for the big wedding day and being able to secure 3 reservations without a big advance payment. we really appreciate this, so thanks again hotel boheme!
sure, there are plenty of old hotels in san francisco that provide great customer service, but many times i feel the strain of someone really having to try hard at not hating their jobs. but between the vibe and decor, the price for the location, the cleanliness and service all combined, hotel boheme cannot be beat. totally authentic. we will always come back to hotel boheme and hopefully next time, get to share some sherry with the fine gentlemen running the place!

title: “An experience for the young ones and young at heart”
text: I am rather late in posting this review. I stayed for one week with my 77 yr old mother(!) in Sep 03. Ok it was dark, but our room was large (2 very comfortable double beds) and on the same floor as the rooftop terrace. Staff throughout hotel and especially the bars made us feel very welcome although you can imagine we weren't their ideal type of customer. But even they realise that money is money whoever is spending! Concierge was first class. We returned to NY again in Sep 04 and we stayed at Morgans but in hindsight preferred the Hudson. Why am I writing this now ? Well I'm looking for a hotel to take my 21yr old daughter in Feb and - yes, I'm going to book Hudson because she'll just love the bars and the whole ambience and the quirky decor. Bye the way, my mother is quite deaf and hardly noticed the noise!

title: “You get what you pay for - THE BEST STAY IN LOS ANGELES (SO FAR)”
text:
Paid a lot for the room- got exactly what we paid for, impeccable service, great room, attention to detail.
Now, I probably am a little biased since I live in a Four Seasons residence full time elsewhere, but I found the service to be great and undisappointing.
Will most likely stay here every time I am in Los Angeles.

title: “A terrific weekend get-away”
text: An excellent Hilton with a beautiful view of the water. Great service, super clean, right near the entrance to the Gas lamp District where you can find any kind of restaurants and bars to sit and people watch downtown. The room rates and valet parking were too high though and really should be adjusted down some. No mini bar or refrigerator in the room which would have been nice to have. Overall, a great place to stay - especially as we did - for a weekend get-away.

title: “Quiet respite in University City area”
text: The Inn at Penn is a Hilton property located literally across the street from the main University of Pennsylvania campus. With that location comes a variety of nearby eateries, shops, and cultural venues. I actually stayed the night "Super Storm Sandy" hit the area. There must be super soundproof windows as I heard nothing..no wind, no rain, no storm noise. I realized a full hurricane storm was raging only if I looked out the window. The employees are cordial, efficient and the room was comfortable with modern furnishings, including an in room iPad to use to keep up with email and other internet business. Like many newer hotels I only wish the window could have opened just a bit as I always miss fresh air in many sealed hotel rooms. I would recommend this hotel and stay there again as its location and ambience was quite a find in the middle of a large urban area.

title: “New Hyatt in New York”
text:
We stayed at the Hyatt 48 Lex the weekend before Christmas and found to to be excellent. Even before we checked in, I got a foreshadowing of the great service in store for us when I called the concierge concerning tickets to Phantom of the Opera. The were most helpful and were able to obtain the tickets which I collected on my arrival. 
The check-in area is tiny, but they were very efficient and we were in our room within minutes. The rooms were average in size but had excellent amenities including a small sink and refridgerator. The bathroom was very modern in design, with a large shower. The noise level was low overall, but I could hear the elevator at night.
The only drawback might be the two small elevators. The wait for them could be long at times. Also, there are only two rooms in the hotel with double beds. All the rest have kings, so plan accordingly. The beds themselves were comfortable.
We had a drink at the bar in the restaurant and enjoyed the friendly staff. We also had breakfast and found the service sluggish, but the food good.
The location was fine, with most everything within walking distance or a short cab or subway ride.

title: “Very Fari....much better in Chicago than this....”
text: Stayed there this past weekend for 3 nights. We got a good deal on a suite from Quikbook but this is an old condo building converted into a hotel. The elevator situation sucks as you can't even fit in the elevator with your bags. There were 4 of us and 2 small kids. As a result you wind up waiting for elevators every single time you want to leave. The front desk is rude and doesn't get customer service and they barely speak english or understand how to deal with people. The room was big but that was about it. It was dark, dingy and was a half hearted attempt at a conversion with thermostats half hanging off the wall, no lights, etc. My daughter is allergice to feather pillows so called down to ask for FOAM and they send up feather pillows. I call down to complian and they finally send up the right ones but on one could have cared. Maybe they would have if I sued them after an allergic reaction. We travel all the time and am from Chicago and decided to try this place. Never again as there are far better in Chicago as there is little service and they could care less about trying to make it nice there. Place sucks and you can do far better. This is the first time I have ever posted and felt the need as besides a big room there was no other redeeming quality of the hotel.

title: “Very Nice”
text: I was here for only one night while in Phoenix on business. My flight arrived early and I was able to check in early. The room was very clean and comfortable. The staff was extremely friendly and helpful; they even offered to have the free shuttle bus take me to and from dinner so I didn't have to drive there in the dark. Breakfast wasn't the best I've ever had at a Hampton, but it wan't bad. All in all, I'd definitely stay here again.

title: “Nice Hotel In December for the price”
text: We stayed here from Christmas 12/25/05 to New Year's Day 1/1/06. I'm in my late 30's and my husband is in his 40's. We are both professionals and love to travel. Just so you know who's writing the review. I searched for quite some time for hotels and the prices weren't cheap for this time of year. But I was able to find a package on Travelocity that included the air and hotel (based on what we would have paid for the air separately, the hotel price was about $200/nt including all taxes, etc.) The lobby is small, but who needs a big lobby anyway. The rooms were a decent size, big bathroom, comfy beds. The staff was mostly friendly except for a cranky concierge named Myra. The restaurant was VERY expensive. Went down one morning just for a cup of coffee. With tax and tip it was $8.00! Also we went for the New Year's Day Brunch. It was painfully disorganized. Not all the food promised was out and it was mediocre at best ($45 each). Skip that! But the front desk staff was very nice and even helped up print some emails. The first day we got there one of the handles on our dresser was broken and they quickly fixed it. They were very attentive and we appreciated it. The hotel is in a nice location. Away from the constant chaos of Times Square but close enough to walk. Grand Central Station is a short walk away. There is a very nice wine shop just around the corner (Sussex) and a little further up is Dunkin Donuts (for a cup of coffee under $2). A cab was always easy to catch just outside the front door. Overall, for the price, this hotel is really a good find. We did find some lovely restaurants in the city while we were there and would recommend Chez Jaqueline up by Washington Park - small, quaint, romantic and excellent french food at a VERY reasonable prices ($100 for dinner for two with a nice bottle of wine, two appetizers and tip) and the River Cafe, which costs about 3 times as much as Chez Jaqueline, BUT is one of the most amazing restaurants I've ever been to - first class all the way, it is on the water in Brooklyn across the Brooklyn Bridge (actually just under it) and has the most spectacular views of the Manhattan Skyline at night. The food was incredible - one of the desserts was the Brooklyn Bridge made out of chocolate! I know it's a lot of money, but it's as much as you'd pay for two tickets to a Broadway show and to me, it was more memorable. We did the dinner cruise for New Year's Eve and had a great time - better than crowding in with thousands in Times Square! Of the museums we saw, our favorite was the Guggenheim. Ellis Island and the Empire State Bldg are touristy but both worth the trip. Greenwich Village and Little Italy/Chinatown were the best places to just walk around. Nice pastry shop in Little Italy called La Bella Ferraro where the owner even sang old italian songs for us! Also the Christmas show at Radio City Music Hall really is a excellent show.

title: “We had a good time.....”
text: I was secptical at 1st,after all most hotels in this price range leave alot 2 b desired,however my significant other and myself were pleasently surprised when we entered a newly remodled room with up 2 date decore and most the modern perks that u would expect from a aspiring hotel. Personally when staying @ hotels i expect at the least a CLEAN room,bedding,and a helpfull and 'on time' staff,we were not disapointed. Its clear that the hotel is going thru a major reinavation an look forward to the final product,for the $ u cant go wrong....

title: “You will love it here!”
text: We stayed at the Dolphin during the week of Thanksgiving. We had such a wonderful stay; the rooms were small but so clean and fresh. The breakfast included juice, sweet muffins, bananas and yogurt. We think it would be a nice addition to have some type of bread that's not so sweet as the muffins! And also herbal tea, for the non-caffeine visitors. The staff was very helpful for all of our needs at all hours of the day and night! The Dolfin is right across from the pier and it is such a fun place to venture. The neighborhood is safe and the bus stop (for those public transportation types) is right on the corner. The owners are also very kind and concerned that their guest have a great stay. You just don't find that these days. We have stayed at more expensive places in San Diego, but you can't beat the Dolphin's prices and service! If you enjoy simple and clean, stay here!

title: “Not as good second time around”
text: We have stayed here before and thought we would on our recent visit to NYC. However, the hotel seemd to have gone down hill a little bit. Not in an obvious way, but more subtely. The room was not vacuumed once while were there (5 days) and neither were the sheets changed. Service was given if asked for but only if you tipped the staff. It just seemed to care a little less about the customer and more about how much money it could make than the last time we visited. We will not be staying for a thrid time at this hotel

title: “Wonderful Experience”
text: We stayed at the Vintage Park Hotel from December 28th through January 2nd 2005. What a wonderful romantic experience. The rooms are beautifully designed and tastefully decorated. The service was outstanding. The conceriege was the most helpful conceriege we have encountered. She gave us wonderful advice on local restaurants, bars, tours, etc. The hotel has a wine theme and hosted wine tasting in the cozy lobby each day from 5 to 6. It was a great chance to taste local wines. Tulio's restaurant and bar are in the hotel and the food and service there are outstanding also. I highly recommend this hotel for any type of visit to Seattle.

title: “Rancho Bernardo Inn, what a great resort in San Diego”
text:
I recently traveled to San Diego and experienced a great service, excellent food and accomodations. Our room in Rancho Bernardo Inn was very large with separate shower and bath tub overlooking at the golf course. The beds were very comfortable and wooden shutters made the room very private. 
I was able to catch up with my work with the wireless and high speed internet connection while I was listening my Ipod thru the hotel's stereo system which includes DVD, Ipod connection with a powered stereo system.
Dinner in El Bizcocho was incredible. We were glad to have a room after we ordered their tasting menu which includes a wine with each course.
Golf course was in a great shape and it was nice to have a seperate pool for the adults.

title: “Different - but really good”
text:
Bright and clean
Friendly and helpful staff
Innovative (Yobot, electric bed)
Good position, not far from Times Square and the subway
I'd stay there again

title: “Really Dog friendly”
text: Seriously they are VERY dog friendly, I stayed here before on the 2nd floor, I like the interior corridors. This last time I came with 2 other co-workers. Granted the front desk warned me I might not want to stay due to animal allergies, but since I had made the reservation and the other 2 people were okay with staying I figured I could just take an allergy pill. The room I stayed in (#125) smelled like there had been 5 sweating/drooling saint bernards in it.

title: “Will stay again!”
text: The hotel itself is cute, very compact, perfect for a night in the city. It's very clean, which is a super plus. Also the staff is amazing, super helpful, and very friendly. For this reason alone I would stay here again!

title: “Great Stay, We'll Return”
text:
Very convenient location for touring Philadelphia. Staff was friendly, helpful. Room was spacious, clean and well appointed. Beds were very comfortable. Luxurious, all marble bath was complete with our requested extra linens. Joining Wyndham By Request before your visit provides many benefits. For example, you won't wait in the long line to check in or out. You will have personalized refreshments awaiting you on your arrival. Members receive offers of great rate specials. 
We were nervous about booking this hotel after reading the bad reviews, but our stay was most enjoyable. The only negative for us was that the indoor pool enclosure was an unbearable 100+ degrees. The family was disappointed that we did not use the pool. Parking in the hotel garage is min. $20/day. We parked in the 12 story city garage across the street for $5 a day on weekends. All considered, a great value. We look forward to returning.

title: “Terrible........!! Terrible....!! Terrible.......!!!”
text:
Hi All,
I made an online Reservation through Hotels.com for day stay in Hollywood Inn Express North and i got the confirmation through hotels.com. when i showed my confirmation in Help desk in Hollywood Express Inn North, they informed me no rooms available and all sold out. When i inquired, they informed all rooms sold out and manager of Hollywood Express Inn North was Terrible and RUDE. Even after confirming the reservation he desperately told us to get out from their hotel. 
Is this the Way they treat their customer.......!!
VERY RUDE AND TERRIBLE SERVICE.......!!

title: “Starwood Fan”
text: I am a huge fan of Starwood properties being that I used to work for them and the properties are always great. I was kinda unsure of this property being that it was a category 2. I arrived at the hotel very late and the staff was very welcoming considering the time of night. I wish I had more time to enjoy everything the hotel offered but I was basically only there to sleep and head on my way. The bar/lounge area looked very nice. My room was very clean. I didn't exactly care for the decoration but that did not impact my stay at all. The heavenly bed was great & I fell asleep almost as soon as I hit the pillow. The friendliness of the staff was exceptional. I even texted my former manager and said, "Oh the service of Starwood's staff. How I've missed it." Everything was great and I definitely recommend this place.

title: “Good location”
text:
Clean rooms with cooking facilities but hardly any have a double bed where both parties have a bedside cabinet. This is strange as the room is big enough but not designed for two. We moved to a smaller room just to get a bed where one person doesn't have to climb over the other to get out. Good location though and frendly, efficient valets if you are driving. Breakfast was OK for one of thes types of places and they don't mind you taking out food.
Good value option if you need to be near the rich folks.

title: “Location, location, location”
text:
After many trips to SF, we decided to try this hotel. We requested rooms (two couples) on a high floor and received them and they had been recently renovated as well. Super comfortable beds, spotlessly clean and sleek but small bathrooms. Room was plenty large enough.
We loved the location. Easy to drop off the rental car across the street as well as pick up the shuttle to SFO outside the parking garage. We walked everywhere - to restaurants (try Fino Ristorante - excellent), Chinatown, Gumps. Despite other reviewers concerns about security we never felt uneasy walking around day or night.
One note: we had free breakfast passes (Hilton Diamond) but our friends did not and breakfast was a surprising $35.00 pp.

title: “Has Class but also Flaws”
text:
Arriving at the Biltmore and entering the lobby is impressive indeed. It is spacious and rather grand. A long hallway runs behind the lobby and contains restaurants, shops and convention room. The hotel has a good business location and is near the Dorothy Chandler Pavillion. 
When I went to check in, I had to wait for about 10 minutes because the entire computer system had crashed. However, after, that there way no wait and I was on my way to my room. It was unacceptable.
First, the room looked like something out of the 1950s -- an older looking, low-level queen bed complete with a 1950s/1960s style cream bedspread and dust ruffle that didn't match, didn't fit, and was torn. There's good retro and bad retro; this was bad.
The carpet was stained. The room was very, very small and very dark. The view was of a wall. The bathroom was tiny and poorly remodeled. There was one wing-back chair that looked incredibly uncomfortable. Also, the room was so small that you couldn't possibly sit in the chair and watch TV. TV was on the dresser. There was a desk with a desk chair. However, the desk was the only table in the room. There was no nightstand -- some weird heavy box-like object (like an overturned computer box) was lying on the floor right next to the bed with various wires attached to it. Not sure what it was or what it was for. But no bed light, no place to put anything if you lay in bed. I didn't see a clock. The only phone was on the desk -- not reachable from the bed.
The worst part, however, was that there were huge stains on the cream-colored bedspread. At that point, I demanded a new room.
I was upgraded to a "junior suite." Very large with separate sitting room, but the furniture was still somewhat dated and I couldn't fairly describe the suite as attractive or luxurious. The carpet was stained. Tiles were missing from the dressing area counter. The TVs (there were 2) were only 19" at best. The bathroom was ok but small and also a bit dated. 
Also, no mini-bar and no bottled water, coffee or tea. Not sure if there were vending machines but, other than tap water, nothing in the room to drink. 
Service was unremarkable -- neither great nor bad. Concierge was helpful. Checkout was slow -- there were 7 people in line and only one person to provide assistance. 
Room service (breakfast) was fine -- prompt and tasty. Had dinner in the Japanese restaurant; it was good as was the service there. Didn't make use of other hotel facilities.
I get the impression that what room you end up with could mean the difference between a decent stay and an unsatisfactory one but am not sure what room or type of room you need to request. There is a club level -- didn't stay there but maybe it's better.
Overall, my experience was merely okay (once I was in the second room). I've stayed in many nicer hotels for the same price and thus will probably look elsewhere when I return.

title: “Clean & Nice breakfast!!!”
text: I stayed on a Saturday night for minty-nine dollars. Nice size rooms. Clean, neat, and spacious. Inside pool but not extravagant.

title: “Clean but underwhelming”
text: Small and poorly designed room with NO storage. Bed too short for normal size adults, no closet in bedroom, no hooks or towel racks in bathroom, no place to store even a carry on bag. Small would be ok if design were better able to accommodate basic needs or even minimal unpacking.Front desk staff disengaged to the point of rudeness. On the plus side it's very clean and well located.

title: “Great Place!”
text: This is a great place to stay! The whole place is clean and well decorated. The breakfast food is great! A wide variety to choose from. The staff we encountered were wonderful and helpful! We asked for some resturaunt locations and they gave us some great recommendations. It is a short trip to downtown. After we had checked out and were headed home (about 15 minutes away), we realized that our sons stuffed animals had been left behind. I immediately called the hotel. They took my name and number and said they would have someone check and call me back. They found them! When we arrived back at the hotel the lady who had retrieved them from the room was at lunch, but she still brought them down to the from desk immediately. Thanks for a great stay!

title: “Simply the best”
text: This is so late, we stayed over 4th of July for 3 nites. WHAT a WONDERFUL PLACE!! The last nite I thought I was at home the bed was sooooo comfortable, the walls a little thin for noice, I can't wait to go back. Keep up the good work. The breakfast place behind the hotel is to die for , fresh tangerine, orange, mango juice and the best BREAKFAST ANYWHERE. 2 TA LU

title: “Perfect stay”
text: We had read mixed reviews about this hotel and were a little scared upon arrival. We loved it! My husband and I took off for a few days and never regretted our stay at the Sutton Place. Clean room, nice bathrooms, great location and walking distance to Magnificent Mile. The one thing we did not like was there was only one outlet in the room and it was behind the curtain so we did not find it until the last day. The beds were extremely comfortable as well. Concierge was great, they gave us "priority seating" for Gino's east pizzeria we also got free breadsticks for using it. O'hare airport is about 20 minutes away with a taxi and will cost roughly $35. Original house of pancakes was right across the street but I recommend eating at Tempo Cafe two blocks down. Pancake house kicked us out for bringing in a star bucks cup. We will definitely stay here again on our next trip to Chicago.

title: “great reservation experience...can't wait to go there”
text: I found out about this hotel from friends who had stayed there in May and highly recommended it. So I decided to call them as I am celebrating my 25th anniversay in August and wanted something special. Special it is......the reservation person at this hotel has gone above and beyond with thier service...arranged a limo to pick us up from the airport, organized a nice romantic city tour, a nice dinner at the Architects café and has given me some great insights into the city........I am looking forward to this experience

title: “Wonderfull place, great staff”
text: What a treat. We booked two rooms while visiting Charlotte for my sons birthday. What a nice place. The location was great and the staff was fantastic. I wish I had noted the name of the gentelman at the front desk, as he was very kind and really made us feel at home (Look for his black & white eyeglasses). If you valet park you will be greated by an outstanding group of people. We self parked but they went out of there way to make us feel welcome. The rooms were very well appointed and very clean. The beds were very comfortable and loaded with pillows. The bathroom was sparkeling clean and my favorite feature most people may not notice. There was an air return in the bathroom that constantly and quietly drew the steamey air & oders out of the bathroom. The A/C was perfect and quiet.

title: “Awesome Value, Friendly Staff”
text: I love Beach Haven! This was my 2nd time here and I loved it. No, it is not the Hilton, but yes, it is a great bargain. The staff was wonderful, the other people staying there are always sooo nice, and the room was perfect for 6 girls! Right across from the popular Garnet Street and a block away from PB. We were up all night and never had any problems! And trust me, we were loud!!! Continental breakfast is only muffins and pastries, but when you're partying like us, the last thing you want in the morning is breakfast.

title: “Wonderful consideration of our needs”
text: My daughter and I were on a rail tour of the northeast visiting potential colleges. We arrived in Penn Station at 11:30 AM and made our way easily to Affinia. Despite our early arriveal the staff allowed us to check in hours early, allowing us to freshen up and head out to visit NYU, tour 5th Ave/Rockefeller for the Christmas displays and have dinner with relatives. Upon returning to the hotel at midnight we retired for a great night's sleep so that we could bounce out to catch our next train ready to go. This gracious consideration of our needs on top of the large, clean room and kitchenette and the very comfortable beds have endeared us forever.

title: “Neat, Clean, Comfortable with friendly accomodating staff!”
text: Stayed at Pear Tree Inn SA-Airport twice on the front and back end of a weekend to the TX Hill Country. Both times we were welcomed by friendly staff, received prompt courteous service, and a clean, comfortable room. The pool was sparkling clean and the water comfortably warm. We enjoyed the complimentary breakfast and the evening happy hour also. Close to restaurants and shopping and airport. We will definatley stay here again.

title: “Great stay! Great location!”
text:
My 8 year old son and I just returned from a four night stay at On the Ave. This was my son's first vacation and I wanted to make it so special. I poured over hotel reviews for weeks - changing my mind several times. I finally just went for it and am so glad I did!
We arrived around 3 PM on Friday. The doorman had opened the cab door before I even realized we had stopped in front of the hotel (cab ride from La Guardia was about $40 including tip). Our room was not ready but the hotel stored our bags and told us it would be an hour. We took off for a while and returned to room 1403. While the room was lovely and a nice size with a great balcony, the pillows were on the floor, without cases and it was not the 450 square feet promised as a "Penthouse Loft". I went to the desk to share my concern and was quickly and graciously moved to a new room (1506). This room was as lovely as the first with more space, a dresser, and two chairs. 
The bathroom was perfectly functional with an excellent shower. The wall mounted tv was great with plenty of channels (though several local channels did not come in clearly). The balcony was fabulous and offered great views of Broadway and the Hudson River. The bed was comfy. Our rate included nightly turn down service - on nights we were there, the chambermaid kindly asked if we needed anything when she turned down the bed and gave my son his nightly chocolate.
All of the employees were helpful and very friendly!
The neighborhood is fabulous! We walked to Central Park and the American History Museum easily. There are great restaurants all around - Manhattan Diner, pizza spots, breakfast places (New Wave Cafe is great and Shake Shack for burgers - yum!)...there is a market across the street for snacks, drinks, etc. The 79th & Broadway stop is two blocks up Broadway.
I would definitely stay at On the Ave again and I would recommend it to friends and family. I felt very welcome with my son and we both appreciated the peacefulness of the spot after crazy days in the city!

title: “Sleep well and spoil yourself”
text:
We spent our final two nights in Manhattan at The Westin. We decided to treat ourselves and it was worth it! We stayed in a corner unit which had beautiful views. The hotel is located across from the Port Authority station and right next to Times Square! 
The hotel has a business center that allows you to print out your airline tickets free! We also ran into an issue late one night while trying to print concert tickets ($8.50/15 mins of internet); a plugin would not load and therefore we were not able to buy the tickets at that time. I spoke to the front desk who immediately offered to remove the charge. We printed our tickets first thing the next morning when a business center employee was available.
Pros:
The Bed...it was indeed heavenly!
The Shower...Loved it! 
Great Views
A coffee maker that brewed Starbucks packets. Tasted better than what you get from Starbucks and saved me a trip to the local coffee shop.
Security at the entrance during the later hours of the night
Cons:
Wireless internet for a cost.
I would definetly stay here again should my budget allow it.

title: “Very good location”
text: The hotel is your typical Hampton Inn. The rooms are pretty standard and what is expected from a Hampton Inn. The location is very good as it is very close to the Space Needle and EMP. The staff was very helpful and friendly. The breakfast area gets very crowded in the mornings. There are not enough tables for the number of guests that stays here.

title: “Good value”
text: This hotel is a 10 minute walk from the Riverwalk and Alamo and is slightly off the beaten track, but it was actually nice to get away from the busier areas at the end of the day. It is very clean and the area it is in feels safe. Parking is free, which is not the case for many of the hotels in this area. The free breakfast was fine, with some impressive Texas shaped waffles. The only negatives for us were noisy air con and the beds were not very comfortable. I like a firm mattress but the one we had was very firm. The sofa bed was also not very comfortable (but they rarely are in my experience). This is a good value hotel. If you want to be right on the River walk, book somewhere else but you will pay a much higher price.

title: “Ok for two nights, but won't go back”
text:
Booked one of the apartment suites as it looked like a good alternative to a regular hotel room for two people sharing. This was actually a small one bedroom apartment that they made into a suite by putting a second bed in the living room. It had a kitchenette as advertised which came in handy. 
The place looked as in the photos, but the white walls and doors were scuffed from luggage and were dirty around door handles. But other than that it was clean and bedding was changed daily.
Overall I liked the room, but that we had two continuing problems:
1) The heat was centrally controlled and the bedroom was to hot at night--had to open the window and live with the street noise.
2) The door was very hard to lock from the outside. The locks should be replaced.
Not a bad experience, but not good either, especially considering these are their most expensive rooms

title: “House keeping staff was excellent!”
text: I would like to commend the Housekeeping staff for the excellent care they take of their guests. I am a flight attendent and was on a layover at the Gateway. I left my ring in the room. I called the hotel and left a message regarding my lost ring. In just a short time ,I received a call back from Juana Pailla at Housekeeping. She was so professional and courteous. My ring had been found! I was so happy! I would like to write a special thank you to Gloria Cardena who found my ring and turned it in. She is a special lady. I appreciate so much her honesty and integrity. I would also like to thank Cesar Gonzales, who arranged the shipping of my ring. We in the airline business travel so much and hotels become ,at times, our homes away from home. The Housekeeping staff of the Sheraton Gateway made my stay as comfortable, safe and secure as if in my own home. Job well done!

title: “Great mid-loop location, fun hotel style and pleasant staff service, poor soundproofing...”
text:
Entered the hotel with a friendly and smiling welcome. Received a free spring gift - a plush goldfish. Able to get early check-in about 30 minutes before standard 3p check-in.
The 9th floor room was away from elevator and had foam pillows (both as requested). The room was spotless and the warm color palette was inviting. I absolutely loved the padded window seats and cozied up there both nights of my stay - with the bolster pillow, the beautiful and soft throw, a book, and my camera.
I had wished the room had an in-room coffee maker. Although the hotel provided a free coffee and tea service from 6a-9a, I didn't want to have to get dressed just to get a cup of coffee from the lobby. 
The walls and door to the room may as well have been made of cardboard, as hallway voices were as clear as if the door was open. And I awoke at 230a the first night and early the second morning to folks in an adjacent room gettin' busy... loudly. Folks can do whatever they wish in their rooms, I just don't want to hear them clearly. Turning on the tv and radio helped to mask their sounds...

title: “Beautiful Friendly Hotel”
text: This Hotel is beautifully located in an almost park like setting. The Lobby and common areas are richly appointed but still comfortable and inviting. Our room was beautifully furnished and comfortable. The Staff was polite and attentive. I can highly recommend this hotel.

title: “location,location,location”
text:
stayed in holiday inn weekend of the 11/112 Nov,very friendly 
helpful staff at front desk, check in was quick even though they were busy.
very pleased with the room, nice quiet, and very clean. the location of this hotel is excellent whithin walking to everything
center city. parking right beside the hotel

title: “Studio Suite”
text: This was our second stay at the Westin Riverwalk. It is a beautiful hotel in a great location - right on the river, but still quiet. The hotel has La Merienda, an afternoon tea, Monday through Friday, with live music. We ate at the hotel's Zocca restaurant. It was very good!

title: “Impressed from the moment we stepped out of the taxi....”
text: We've been to NYC many times, and we both agree the Doubletree Metropolitan was a very pleasant surprise! We stayed there from February 5th to the 8th. Our room was on the ninth floor, and was surprisingly quiet, even without double-glazed windows (which we were told are being installed). It makes us wonder how other reviewers could have had such apparently bad experiences........it appears that hotel managment has taken steps to address concerns, and has done a fine job correcting things. We got a super rate on the Doubletree website, and we got excellent value for the price. Our room was newly refurbished with very attractive furnishings, a very nicely fitted bathroom (with a great shower-head), and above all - it was a decent-sized room for a NYC hotel! We found all of the staff to be attentive, pleasant, and helpful - we were greeted at the front door by the duty manager, and looked after all the way from there. Like most (all) hotels, the prices for meals and drinks in the bar were on the high side, but if you can manage to walk the length of yourself, you can find wonderful options closeby (including a very nice deli right beside the hotel). The location of the hotel is super - close to everything you want to see, and right on a subway line and bus routes. This is truly a wonderful find from our perspective, and we've been in many hotels all over the world. Next time we visit New York City, it's the Doubletree Metropolitan for us!

title: “Nice Place to Stay for business trips.”
text: I came in to town on a business trip. When I arrived I was able to get a room quickly and with out any trouble and the front desk clerk Dean was very helpful. I asked Dean for suggestions of some good restaurants and he was able to provide some as well as give me directions. Everyone was very helpful and friendly and the rooms were nice and very clean.

title: “Customer Service issue resolved”
text: Stayed at this property for 1 night at the end of my anniversary celebration. Upon arrival the essentially manditory valet service for our vehicle, at $34 per night was a suprise, (although there is an AAA discount on this).
