The room and amenities lived up to those promised on the Kimpton website and the rooftop pool/fire pit area was lovely. Our real challenge was in the morning, when the room service we ordered the night before did not come. As we had a 7:45am business meeting, we ended up checking-out without food, and expressed our unhappiness with this at the front desk. Although the initial response of the desk staff was minimal, I received a phone call the following day, in which it was explained that the situation had been researched, staff miscommunication had been idenified, and as recompense, a portion of the charges from our dinner bill during our stay was being cancelled.

title: “FABULOUS!!!!!!! EVEN DURING A SAD TIME!””
text: My sister and I had to travel to Chicago on 01-12-2012, due to the death of her 41 year old daughter. We stayed at "THE WHITEHALL HOTEL." The stay was really nice and so were the staff. In the end we were almost sorry to leave. Upon arriving we found ourselves in a valley of smiles from the very first person we met, the Valet, the bellman: Ramone, & especially the Guest Services Manager: Derrick Beverly!!! He was very polite & intelligent, along with being very compassionate to our present situation. He explained everything I had available and put me in the most beautiful Junior Suite that I've ever stayed in, in my life!!! Entering the room, the first thing I noticed was the King-sized bed. Everything was clean and quiet (couldn't hear a noise). The bathroom is also very clean & spacious. I truly adored the marble. The shower was very refreshing & quaint! But, the bed was one thing that if I could I would have taken home with me. My sister & her god-daughter were on the top floor with 2 beautiful queen beds. We felt like we were having a heavenly experience, like floating on a cloud! We didn't want to get out of the beds. It hugged me in all the right places! LOL! These are the things that made us truly enjoy our stay at this hotel! But, my warmest congratulations are to the hotel for their choice of personnel. They know how to really make you feel at home, and if you need anything it is like asking a family member. Congratulations from the heart, you all were fantastic!!!

title: “An Oasis of Calm”
text:
We were fortunate enough to fly to NY from Scotland via Heathrow on the day after the chaos of Thursday 10 August. 
This was our third trip to NY in the past two years for my wife and I, and the Kitano was the best yet. From check in to check out six days later, we were well impressed by all aspects of the hotel, especially the ambiance of calm relaxation after a hard day shopping and sightseeing!
The hotel is located in a quiet area of Park Ave and 5th Ave and all the midtown sites and shops are easily within a short walk. Also, there are several restaurants and bars (especially Irish) close by.
The staff in the hotel were exceptional - friendly, helpful, and always willing to share a smile.
All in all, a most enjoyable experience and one I woul have no hesitation in recommending and booking again.
NB - these are by far the largest hotel bedrooms we have enjoyed in NY, more like good sized European hotel bedrooms.

title: “Very good location. Nice views from room. They nickle and dime you for everything”
text: Rooms were nice. Location is excellent. Parking $42.00 per day, they charge you for wifi. Our room first day they had cups for coffee bur only decaf coffee. Next day they had coffee but no coffee cups. Third day they had coffee and cups but no creamer or sugar. I don't understand why these big hotels cannot afford to provide free wifi in the room or complementary coffee in the lobby after charging hundreds of dollars a night whereas hotels like Days Inn or Ramada inn can provide all that and much more including continental breakfast while charging far less. If you want to use a computer in their business center they charge you per hour. No microwave in the room.

title: “It was all okay until the 4am false fire alarm.”
text: I chose this hotel after hearing from a family member about what a great place it was. I had mixed feelings. When I pulled into the parking lot I was happy to see a lot of parking spaces, and what seemed to look like a nice building. Once inside it looked great. But appearances can be wrong. Our room had big stains on the floor, and was supposedly "Recently renovated." The AC had no power, and so only one side of the room was cold, and the other extremely hot, the exhaust fan in the bathroom did not work making it absolutely miserable trying to take a shower or use the bathroom period. For one night, I didn't think it was too terrible and I could survive. That was until I was awoken at 4am on a Sunday morning to a fire alarm. As we evacuated the building no one seemed to know what was going on or where to find the stairwells (They are not clearly marked). As we all arrived in the parking lot for further instruction not 1 staff member was there explaining anything or giving us any direction. People weren't sure if they should get out of the premises, or if it was a false alarm. 15 minutes later (YES 15 MINUTES!) the San Jose Fire Dept showed up, walked in with an ax, and still said nothing. I was absolutely disappointed in the way Arena Hotel handled what could have been an emergency situation. The next day, as we rushed to get out by check-out time, i called to find out what had happend and they told me, "We can offer you a late check-out." "Well, what could is that going to do me now?" I thought. I will not be returning to the Arena Hotel (Or using the 25% off coupon they're sending me as an apology), this place was a joke. After we were allowed back in to our rooms, we could only go as high as the 2nd floor (I was on the 3rd), because the fire walls had dropped blocking all walkways and those hidden stairwells. We were all lucky that night that it wasn't an actual emergency, the lack of professionalism was astounding.

title: “Hotel Indigo is top notch!”
text: The friendliest hotel I've ever stayed at! Hotel Indigo's staff were all so incredibly nice and accommodating. As a first time tourist to NYC, they offered handy tips and made our stay a complete joy!

title: “Pleasant Surprise for a Best Western Hotel”
text: Spent 6 nights here with my wife and two kids. Stay started off in a Jr. Suite becasue Shell Vacation Club screwed up my reservation. The room was very spacious and was in the newer part of the hotel. The front desk was very helpful in getting us to a Queen Suite after Shell go us upgraded. The new room was in the older part of the hotel but the inside of the room did not reflect the outside and we had a full kitchen which was great for us due to our two year old. The bedroom was separate from the living area and kitchen. Ther was only one bathroom which would be tricky if we had up to 6 people in the room. The service was great, everyone was friendly and greeted you when ever you crossed their path. We even got a call in our room 10min. after we got in to make sure everything was okay and if we needed anything. The location is the best, it's not in the very busy or loud area of San Diego but on the water and minutes away from all the area attractions. The only negative about the location is the frequent sounds of Helicopters and Jet Fighters from the Navel Base accross the bay. Howvever, they only seems to run excersizes on certain days and on specific times of the day. When returning to SD I will most surely try booking this location again.

title: “Very fine, but the incidentals added up.”
text:
The Adolphus delivers the full experience of a revered big city hotel. 
We were initially put off by the bustle of preparations going on for a big wedding, but our room was a spacious and beautiful haven. The room service dinner was terrific and delivered with aplomb. Casual breakfast in the bistro was equally fine. It's worth noting, however, that those meals plus valet parking added rather noticeably to the bill. No complaints, though.

title: “Walk to everything”
text: A really great hotel with fantastic views, fast elevators, nice gym and indoor pool, great restaurants and great service. Best bed ever. Immaculately clean.

title: “Wonderful Hotel with a great location”
text: We stayed at The London in early Oct. on a trip to NCY with our friends. The suite was everything we needed and more-with a comfortable living area to allow us two couples to visit in between sightseeing! The location of this hotel was perfect with it being within walking distance to most areas of interest for us. The hotel doorman was just wonderful and so nice to help us in any way possible from advice to good restaurants and offering us complimentary car service to different locations. The cars and drivers were classy all the way and we were sure to tip well since this was so much better than catching a taxi! Loved this feature of the service at The London! All in all-very prompt and polite service with a smile from everyone and this made our first trip to NYC a completely wonderful trip for four 50ish travelers from Alabama!

title: “River Walk”
text: I had a great stay at the Four Points. Checkin was a breeze, my room was clean and surprisingly large (essentially a living room and a bedroom in one), and I had a fantastic stay. The hotel is only 2 blocks from the Riverwalk, which is a great way to enjoy the city without having to compete with cars on the street.

title: “Royalton upgraded service but STILL read this!”
text:
I stayed at the Royalton again 3 nights last week. During my stays there I have seen 5 rooms. Ours and friends. NONE of them looked anything like the professional pictures. I've attached realistic photos again. This time I was able to procure a KING size bed!! The first time I asked if they had any in the hotel I was told "No" however, he managed to make one appear somehow!?? Maybe he thought I meant Available Kings?? IDK, I hear there are very few. We were in room 1112 the first night and bumped into each other all night. The next day they moved us to 1119 with a King bed. It was a bigger room and bathroom too. Same price. I forgot to ask for a top sheet on the bed my first night but asked housekeeping the next day. It was hard to make her understand that I needed another sheet to cover up with since the comforter is so heavy and hot. Why is this so foreign? The front desk was far more helpful and cordial this visit, however, they are STILL using children (Very young adults) to run the front desk. Can be frustrating when they mumble and talk fast. NO, I'm not THAT old!! The bar area can be very loud and crowded on certain nights. Thursday must have a special happy hour or some kind of draw for locals.?? If you go to the bar, look CAREFULLY at your bar tab. Their menu said scotch was $18. When the bill came it said $23. We had a group drinking so at $5 extra dollars a glass it got really expensive! They did the same with several of our drinks, even beer! We had to take it to the bar manager and put up a fight before he would change it to the original prices on the menu!!! Needless to say, we don't drink there anymore. And the last visit keeps us from eating there. With that said this hotel has a GREAT location!!! It's on 44th between 5th & 6th. I was steps away from luxury shopping on 5th Ave, Park Ave. and Madison Ave and if you go the other way I can get to Bryant Park in 2 blocks, 42nd st, Times Square, Rockefeller Plaza... Seriously PRIME real estate! This hotel is SO convenient to everything I love in NYC that I will likely stay here again. 
The showers are still wonderful with great water pressure but the beds and pillows are awful. Neck and Back aches for sure. OH!! The wireless internet was FREE this time!! The Bellman that brought up our luggage gave us the code and it was free and worked great the whole time! Also, they have iPads in each room for your use during your visit. It has your name on the screen when you turn it on and that's where you can find all of the hotel information such as menus and amenities... By the way, this is NOT a good hotel for children. I don't know that, during our visits, I ever saw a child.

title: “Great place to stay”
text:
We stayed at the Skyline Hotel March 1-3, 2006. We would absolutely stay here again because of its location and value. 
Skyline is easily accessible for those who drive to NYC; close to the Lincoln Tunnel. Rooms are very large, compared to other city hotels. We were given a complimentary upgrade to a king-sized room, which was very clean with a nice, newly-remodeled bathroom. 
A couple of very mild criticisms: the website advertises parking at $8 a day, is actually $10 a day; still cheap for NYC. Television service in room was poor but hey, how much TV would one watch in NYC?
The restaurant lacked good service but the breakfast buffet was affordable, with good food.
Overall, this is a fine hotel for a couple searching for an inexpensive getaway or a family wanting a good experience. Take some time and explore the gentrifying Hell's Kitchen neighborhood. Eclectic restaurants and shops are nearby. Skyline is also well-located, an easy walk to the subway and some touristy offerings, such as Times Square.

title: “Very dangerous shower and no counter in the bathroom to put anything”
text:
We stayed here for 3 nights and expected much more after reading other reviews. I did expect the VERY SMALL room but I did not expect the bathroom situation. There was absolutely no counter in the bathroom and the toilet had a sloped lid so nothing even stayed on top of that. We had to carry toiletries back & forth while trying to balance them on the sink. Also the walk in shower did not drain away from the floor and the floor was very wet after each shower and I slipped and almost fell untill I finally got enough towels to put all over the floor. Up to that point it was 2 towel, 2 washcloths, 2 hand towels - no extras. 
Also on the first day I was pleased to receive the newspaper as usual but we were off to an early start so I left it unopened on the dresser expecting to read it upon our return only to find it gone. When I complained at the front desk I was told they would get me one - never happened. For the next 2 days I never received a newspaper and after requesting one from the front desk was told they would get me one from the store - never happened. I asked 3 times and when I saw one on the counter was told it was for another customer! 
My biggest surprise was when I looked at my bill only to find out I had been overcharged from what I was quoted on my reservation. After I emailed them a copy of my reservation showing the lower price they sent a new bill and only time will tell if my credit card is charged the correct amount. 
This motel is clean and very close to everything and we were able to walk or take a short taxi ride where we wanted to go. The front desk people need to do a better job of assisting customers.

title: “Comfortable and Handily Situated”
text:
Booked CQ,blind after checking websites,reviews and City attractions. Have to say we were not disappointed. Transfer for wife and self (mature couple) was 15minute taxi ($30 inc.tip) from airport.Easy to find on Chestnut Street. The stand alone clock outside the entrance is a good marker. Lobby is on first floor accessed by lift (elevator) from street foyer. Smooth and straightforward check in,with issue of door card after scanning credit card into the system. You do need your door card to operate elevator (two of these) to rooms.
Rooms are small by US standards but for any Europeans,pretty standard size and perfectly adequate.Double bed was one of the best we've slept in-very comfortable with good bedding. You get a chair at the desk
(more a workstation really), TV, smallish clothes closet,decent size bathroom with big shower instead of bath.Soft,thick towels-nice! All clean and in decent decorative order. Everything worked.
Just off the lobby area is a smartish Italian restaurant. Didn't use it during our 3 night stay but would have had we stayed longer. There are three free PC/Internet stations in the lobby area (as well as free wireless access throughout hotel if you're on business).Also in the lobby are free warm drinks, a larger flat screen TV, a selection of free daily newspapers, comfortable soft furnishings and a few shelves of readable books.
Staff were unfailingly friendly,courteous and knew what they were doing.
On the street outside,we were at first slightly disconcerted by a group of boisterous youngsters a few yards along-till we realised that they were students at the next door Art Institute taking a smoking break-absolutely not a problem.
Directly across the street is a large new mall,work,apartment development called Liberty Plaza. This was handy for eating,drinking and shopping. Club Quarters is a 5 minute stroll from Maceys and City Hall. It's about 25 minutes walk to the Independence Buildings and exhibitions and about 15 minutes walk to the Convention Centre. Philly is easy to walk.
When we left for New York, I was wishing I'd booked Club Quarters in NYC as we found the formula to be pleasant, comfortable and sensibly priced-especially for city type breaks when you're generally on the hoof and you need comfort and functionallity from your hotel. Acid test-would you stay again?-Yes.

title: “Great Property Great Location”
text: Stayed here a few days after 4th of July. Great location just 1 block from all the action at Union Square. I had a funky problem with an opening behind the sink area. Called "at your service" and an engineer was up there within 5 minutes to get my iitems and then the area was repaired while we were out touring the city during the day. Had the priviledge to have concierge lounge access and the breakfast and evening desserts were great. I never took part in any evening hospitality. The room was spacious and uber clean. Valet worked well. Valet charges are higher than some other properties in the city and although I didn't have to pay it, I still find the 12.95 fee for wifi just ridiculous. I never used the lounge or restaurant finding too many more desirable options just steps outside the door.

title: “Great Location”
text:
The Park Central good points:
1. good transport links (easy ride on E line from JFK airport) 
2. location (just a few blocks from Times Square and Central Park and ridiculously close to MOMA)
3. surrounded by cheap and cheerful eateries (Lindy's, Carnegie deli etc.)
4. reasonably clean and comfortable
thing to be aware of:
1. it's a typical conference hotel, slightly shabby and in need of a refurb/refit - particularly noticeable when waiting for the bizarre lifts or on the floors where the actual rooms are.
2. No free WIFI
3. generally a little soulless
4. sheets in beds not tucked in properly which gives a sloppy impression.

title: “R/C Platinum Member and done with this property!”
text:
My letter to the General Manager:
I have been a regular and frequent guest of the Ritz-Carlton, Philadelphia for several years and have decided that I will no longer utilize your property for overnight stays. My recent stay from July 5th to July 8 was consistently poor in several areas and my attempts to rectify the problems were met with only more problems. I can understand why your property is now #32 out of 85 hotels in Philadelphia on Tripadvisor. 
 My first difficulty was at the front desk upon check-in. The staff member checking me in, Oliver, made several loud remarks that I had “pre-paid my reservation with Travelocity” in a clearly condescending manner. In fact, I had used some American Express points to book the Club-level room. My understanding is that AmEx uses Travelocity as it’s booking agent. I also presented my Ritz Carlton Platinum card, which should have indicated my room preferences. I was then placed on the 14th floor in a room that overlooks the HVAC units across the street and has a noticeable low frequency hum. I went back to the front desk and asked to be placed in another room without the hum. I was then moved lower to the 9th floor, with the accompanying street noise. My clear preference for a high floor was ignored. 
 The second problem was on Friday night when I placed the “do-not-disturb’ sign on the door prior to going to bed early. I was then woken up by a member of the housekeeping staff with a phone call asking me if I wanted turndown service. Clearly, the answer was no, hence the sign on the door.
 In addition, the rug in the room has a noticeable bump near the window by the desk. I found this defect when I tripped on it and almost hit my head on the desk. 
 I filled out the comment sheet upon checkout and was called back by the Manager On Duty but was unable to pick-up the call as I was driving in heavy traffic on Interstate 95 South. I called the hotel operator back to speak to the Manager On Duty three times, but she (Kristen/Christine?) was either on the phone, out of the office, or in a meeting. I think that calling back three times is more than sufficient. 
 Finally, I received my folio by email later in the day and it includes Internet access charges. As a Platinum member, I believe this should be removed and have asked via email back to the front desk.
 Overall, I found this visit clearly sub-standard and have many other options for my stays in Philadelphia. I have already cancelled my stay at your property for this weekend and will stay at one of your competitors both next weekend and in the future.
 One final note, I would like to direct your attention to Pennsylvania Code Chapter 11, State Board of Accountancy, section 9 regarding “Use of the designation “certified public accountant” and the abbreviation “CPA” solely as a mark of achievement by individual without current license.” I saw it on your checkout letter and did a review of your educational background in Canada. As it is unlikely you are licensed as a CPA in the State of Pennsylvania being educated outside of the US and without a graduate degree, I recommend you review the pertinent state code and remove the designation from future correspondence if that is the case. I have also sent a copy of the hotel check out letter to the State of Pennsylvania State Board of Accountancy.
Although I cannot succinctly correlate a drop in customer service at the Ritz-Carlton, Philadelphia with your arrival about a year ago, I do have my suspicions having stayed at the property numerous times both before your arrival and after. And I find your use of the CPA designation disturbing and possibly in violation of State of Pennsylvania code. 
The hotel has many great departments, but several members of the front desk, housekeeping and maintenance staff and possibly yourself, need to undergo close scrutiny to get better.

title: “Going out of their way”
text:
I recently booked a stay with Monaco. It was the first time I went to this Kimpton hotel - I've been to all the other Kimpton hotels in Chicago at least once and I like staying at them because of the great services they provide.
Recently, I was on a business trip coming up from Dallas to Chicago and I got a call from Kimpton - they oversold, felt really bad (my flight was late, really late, so I was the one of the few to get the boot), but they already booked me a stay at the Wit and I wouldn't have to pay for that night. A bit bummed, but I heard good things about the Wit and I wasn't paying for it, so sure! I thanked them for thinking about me, taking care of things already so that I wasn't blindsided when I got to the hotel.
This isn't a review of the Wit, but when I arrived, I found the room was gorgeous, it just didn't have a bed. It was a "parlor" room, where I had to fold out the couch and sleep on a thin mattress. No pillows. Had to make the bed myself. It was 2:30 am local time, and I was exhausted, so I just slept as best as I could.
In the morning, I visited the Monaco, thinking, how could they have snubbed me? They probably got the cheapest room available. Nope - it was the last room Wit had, they were told, and they spent $680 for it. They weren't told that there wasn't going to be a bed. Monaco staff were shocked at what happened, and were very apologetic. They put me up in the best suite in the hotel, not charging me extra for it, and got the room ready early. I was up there for an hour - a quick call asking if everything was ok and if there was anything else I can do.
My luck didn't continue - I left my bag at the hotel on the way to the airport, but they were ready to ship it when necessary. I opted to keep the bag there until I returned next week on business.
To me that story tells me so much about Monaco and the Kimpton hotels in general. They really care about making people feel comfortable, and if something went wrong, they go out of their way to make sure they make the situation as best as possible. Not a single hotel I've been to has demonstrated this level of service. The rooms at places that I've stayed when a Kimpton isn't available lack character, don't have an honor bar (which comes in handy many times - there's food, snacks, and even medicine, etc. in there), and aren't as stylish but usable too. How many times have you been to a hotel where the sync is large, beautiful, but shallow and leaves no counter space for your things? I've yet to experience that in a Kimpton hotel.
Not to mention with their InTouch membership (free), you get free Wifi, and a credit towards a couple of things in the honor bar. How awesome is that? Many times I go to a hotel and have to pay 10-15 dollars a night for Wifi.
All in all, I will always find myself going out of my way to stay at a Kimpton wherever I am. I've never felt more comfortable away from home.

title: “GOOD LOCATION, AVERAGE ROOMS, AVERAGE SERVICE.”
text:
We went on a 2 week vacation to Boston and wanted to stay at a central location since we were going to visit all the local attractions.This Sheraton hotel in Boston is located perfectly because you can walk to Fenway Park; you have access to a mall from the 2nd floor of the hotel; you can walk to take boat tours; etc., etc. Everything is easily accessible from this hotel. But, we found out that there are several other similar hotels located in the same area, and some of them might be a little less expensive.... so we might stay somewhere else next time.
Our room was average/comfortable, but the bathroom was really small! We were on the 12th floor. We did get the WORST view we have ever gotten from any hotel! It was this brown structure, we found out it was the back wall of the mall. For an expensive hotel we were surprised that the coffee maker had one creamer and one sugar and there was no mini bar! Not the best Sheraton we have stayed at. This hotel is REALLY busy all the time. Because of this, there are people in the lobby and in the entrance at all times! Several times the doorman was not able to get us a taxi because he would be overwhelmed with other guests. Luckily there are always taxis parked a block away, so we could just walk and flag them down ourselves.
They have good room service and the concierge is very helpful. Their bar is well stocked and they have good service.
Overall, it was a very good experience and we would stay at this hotel again.
**********************************************************************************************

title: “Satisfied Stay”
text: I booked this hotel due to its location and trendy environment for my sister-in-law's bachelorette celebration. A day before our check-in, I woke up to an email about my reservation cancellation due to an invalid credit card. Once I got in touch with them and explained I had paid in full earlier in the year, they were very accomodating. When I checked in, I learned I had been upgraded to a higher floor and provided complimentary champagne. Even more, they decorated our hotel room in honor of my sister-in-law's bachelorette weekend. They made us feel very welcome and special, and the staff was very attentive of our many needs/demands.

title: “Great Hotel........”
text:
Metro Hotel is in an excellent position. Right next to Empire State Building, 5th Avenue, and round the corner from Macys, Times Square. Ideal and central. Hotel reception friendly as are all staff. Free wi-fi too! 
Their breakfasts are continental and more than enough for everyone, with the staff ensuring supplies are there of pastries, cheese, yoghurts, tea / coffee etc. At the end of the day you are there to have a quick bite to eat and out you go to tour and walk your feet off!
We did go to Tick Tock nr 8th Ave for a typical American breakfast one monring, but mostly we brought coffees to our rooms whilst getting ready.
The rooms were adequate, clean, maid excellent. I have no complaints, would definitely recommend to anyone and would go back!

title: “Great location - Great View - Great Service”
text: We had a wonderful weekend celebrating our anniversary and as always enjoyed the excellent service from the Westin-Michigan Ave. I look forward to visiting this hotel again soon!

title: “Great bargain”
text: Great price (about $110) for a clean, funky place right in downtown SF. Staff was very pleasant.

title: “Rude, much??”
text: First off I paid $105 bucks for one night. It's in ghettoville which by the reviews I figured it wasnt... Our rooms air did not work and the lady at the desk argued with us it did. The air ran for 2hrs and we sat in there and sweat the whole time. Finally moved us but had to yell at us and tell us we were stupid that the air works fine. Our new rooms air worked great and it was so cold we had to turn it off for a few mins!! If I'm paying 105 I better get decent survive. They offer crap!

title: “great room, great lobby bar, gym so so”
text: The rooms are great. The building is a cylinder, so rooms are like a shaped like a piece of pie, with a desk centred on a huge window overlooking the city, incredible view. The lobby bar has Guinness for $4 a pint and free internet. My room was clean, with great bedding. The gym is an after thought. It's ok, gets the job done, but not an experience. Pool the same. I was at the Empress in Victoria prior to the Westin an it's pool was fantastic. Both hotels are four star. Overall good value .. it's very close to the westlake metro station, and thus free transportation within the city during the day.

title: “You get what you pay for!”
text: Being in a really tight budget, we decided to go ahead and book this hotel, despite the many bad reviews. So we where not expecting much, with that being said we arrived and no kidding this hotel is right smack in the middle of times square, with the city at your doorstep, you hardly notice the peeling wallpaper in the hallway or the stained carpets. Our room was in the 12th floor, (we foun out the last day that the slow renovation progress had just reached the 10th floor..D'oh!) The room was clean, and most important bedbug free! Please note, the water in the shower was warm at best, so if you love your hot showers be warned! We had a baby stroller with us, and to reach the lobby is a couple if stairs (no ramp) so that was an inconvenience. Overall, for the price and location you get what you pay for, you can't beat the price and location!

title: “Top notch location and service”
text:
We stayed here for our 40th anniversary during the Thanksgiving holiday. We made a superb choice. The staff, especially Linda, bent over backwards to make our stay enjoyable (thank you for the hand written card and the goodies!). 
We especially enjoyed the wine/beer reception each night where we casually met people from all over the world. It was a half block walk to the Macy's parade and the same to Times Square yet the hotel was very quiet. They supplied a refrigerator and coffee maker on request which made the 5 days that much more enjoyable. All the little touches like individually wrapped cotton balls and plenty of light and outlets just showed how they go out of their way to make your stay enjoyable. Couldn't be happier.

title: “Not a Business Hotel”
text:
Good points:
 - very clean and well furnished
 - friendly staff
 - nice beds
Problematic for Business Travelers
1) No speaker phone in room. Very annoying if
 your business is global and requires extensive
 late night conference calls. Inexcusable for 
 such an expensive Hilton property.
2) Mobbed Breakfast Area. This property clearly
 markets aggressively to get huge families on
 vacation from Latin America. Makes the breakfast
 area hopelessly unusable. 30 minute waits for
 everything. Even worse, there is no nearby substitute
 restaurant (a solution I have used at other Embassy Suites)
3) No hot water circulation system. Not a business
 travel problem, but inexcusable for such a premium
 property. Have to wait 5-10 min for the hot water to warm
 up all the pipes between the basement and the top
 floor before you can take a shower. Premium properties
 worldwide usually have a system that constantly 
 circulates hot water on each floor to avoid this lag.
4) Inept laundry service. Was 2 hours late. But they also
 forgot to charge me for it.
5) Expensive and clumsy parking system. Garage is 
 reasonably nice, but they want $17/day for it and
 they have to fumble around with your room number
 every time you drive in and out. And they also have
 trouble keeping track of your charges which requires
 multiple visits to the front desk to correct their
 cooridination problems.
6) Slow room cleaning. Rooms still not serviced at 4PM
 on some days.
7) Sealed Windows. Again, not a business travel problem,
 but I hate hotels that won't let you get fresh outside
 air into the room... particularly frustrating when you
 are near the ocean and can't enjoy the offshore ocean
 breeze in your room.

title: “NOSIEY”
text: I liked the way the Hotel looks on the outside but on the inside it was filthy and noisey at night. We could hear every sound from outside. The beds were uncomfortable and I even found a big yellow stain on my sheet. But the staff was decently helpful.

title: “Great View of Timesquare”
text: This was our 3rd time at Novotel in Times Square as we love the location. We chose a room with a view of Times Square which was spectacular although a bit noisy in the early hours of the morning as the room not totally sound proofed of the goings on on the busy broadway street.Our stay was lovely as always my only wish would be that a coffee / tea machine be added to the room.

title: “Nice price, not horrible.”
text: My 2 kids & I stayed here for 5 days on vacation. The room was clean and suited us well. Customer service was great and I do appreciate good customer service! It was a bit noisy in the back, but I have stayed in worse. Hot water never seemed to run out which is a bonus when there are 3 people in a room. Dennys was right across the street, and the freeway on ramps were very close. Alot of places to eat in the area including an In n Out, Chili's, Red Lobster, and Phil's B-B-Q, old town is close and a neat place to visit, Seaworld is right around the corner too. People criticize the strip clubs being close but you'd never know it by the activity around the place, we never saw anyone around it. I just wonder why it smelled like marijuana smoke in the stairwell and near the other rooms.....

title: “A wonderful hotel in a great location!!!”
text: We searched high and low for a hotel for our first family vacation in 9 years. Let me tell you, the hotel webstie does not do justice to this great hotel. The rooms (1 BR suite) were large and comfortable, the kitchen was small but very usable (saved a ton on breakfasts), the master bedroom had a king size bed with what felt just like our tempur-pedic mattress, and the kids said that the pull out queen bed was comfy. The neighborhood was awesome and safe (with a great market just around the corner and a great place to eat called Nicks that delivers), the hotel staff was super friendly and helpful. When we go back next year, there is not another place that we will even consider. Subway 3 blks away, central park 2 blocks away. STAY HERE, YOU WON'T REGRET IT!!!!

title: “Elegant lobby; nice rooms; comfy beds”
text:
This was our second experience at a Holiday Inn Express and it didn't disappoint. 
The hotel is a newly renovated historic bank building which gives it a unique feel of a 3 or 4-star hotel. The odd thing is that the immediate surrounding neighborhood that is not that great. Holiday Inn has taken a chance putting the hotel here and so far it seems to have worked. 
We did walk over to Inner Harbor and little Italy which was no more than a 10-minute walk. There is a Whole Foods in the Inner Harbor area where you can get some tasty items to take back to the hotel. By the way, the rooms also feature a fridge and microwave. 
This hotel features a free and quite decent continental breakfast, with one or two hot items as well. I had cinnamon rolls, eggs and cereal. 
The staff was polite and courteous throughout my stay. 
There's not much bad I can say about this place. My only complaint was that they wanted an additional $12 to park in what appears to be an unguarded lot in back. You can save the parking fee by parking at a meter across the street after 6pm until 8am. If you are staying during the day, all-day parking at the meter is $8.

title: “Great stay, great room, great staff”
text: Thank you for a perfect stay during a crazy st. Patrick's Day weekend !

title: “How is this hotel #80??”
text: I recently (as in I just got off the plane) stayed at the St. Regis and rushed to write this review. Let's just start with this: Don't even think about another property in NYC, because this is the closest to heaven on earth in hotel form. From beginning to end, the stay was well worth every penny spent on site. Ok, ok- the room service is pricey- but you're not at a HoJo, and you get what you pay for. I spent this weekend at the St Regis celebrating a momentous occasion and happened to mention it as I reserved my room. Not only did I receive a welcome note and chocolate strawberries from the GM, but it seemed as if all of the hotel staff knew of the celebration too. This examples the overall feeling of my stay: Every detail wasn't too small to be overlooked. The concierge, Peter, was more than helpful securing dinner reservations, exhibit tickets, spontaneous nail appointments and the like and we were grateful for his help. Going to NYC is in itself a stressful task due to the overwhelming amount to see/do and the desk guided us perfectly. We sent some items to be pressed and was pleased that they came back only a few short hours after sending them down. The rooms are beautiful and ample though it was a little difficult to find an available plug in that wasn't in the entry way, bathroom or behind the bed. I resolved that this is due to the age of the hotel itself, which also explains the smaller than expected bathroom size. This is the only negative I could possibly point out, and attributes the 4/5 on the room evaluation. Make sure to go to the King Cole Bar, if only to marvel at the King Cole painting, but I would recommend trying the Bloody Mary. Tea service was pricey but also worth a try and the spa was satisfactory. I can't wait to go back.

title: “Beautiful hotel in great location”
text:
We unfortunately arrived right at check-in (3 p.m.) and it was very very slow. The staff was friendly, though, and I think the issue was because a few people had problems with their rooms (room type they wanted not available, etc.).
Our room was on the 8th floor and had no view. It was stylishly decorated and spacious, especially by NYC standards. There were motion-sensor lights under the bedside tables, which became rather annoying pretty quickly. One didn't seem to be working properly and never turned off so we just unplugged it. This feature is much more convenient in the bathroom. I loved the full-length mirror inside the closet; wish more hotels had these. 
The rate for our room itself was pretty reasonable, but parking is outrageous at $65/day. There are plenty of much cheaper garages within walking distance. There was also a $15/day fee for wi-fi access which is a bit steep... and room service prices were ridiculous. Again, there are plenty of nice restaurants in the area with much more reasonable prices.

title: “Good Stay”
text: On way back from Minneapolis to Columbus, Ohio. Had stayed at a Sleep Inn in Madison on way to Minneapolis, and was pleased with the experience. This hotel did not change my opinion. Good comfortable room, pleasant and professional staff.

title: “Just O.K. - It's Style over Substance”
text:
I decided to stay here because it was "new". The Hotel is just o.k. It is a renovated Amerisuites. I would have muched rather stayed at a Hampton Inn or Holiday Inn Express for what I received for the $98 price.
The only "free hot breakfast” they have is toast & bagels. Everything else hot you have to pay for & yes it's at hotel prices. For $98 I could have gone to Hampton or Holiday and got a full free hot breakfast. I was very disappointed with this. 
The noise levels of the AC and doors were horrendous. I am talking about all day/night the heavy doors would just hit and shake the walls of the room. The doors do not have springs were they close quietly. The AC in the rooms are old wall AC's that are DIRECTLY ON the bed. It is very loud and VERY noisy. 
Pros: 
Bed is great
Large Flat screen
Nice Decor
Cons:
Breakfast not as nice as cheaper hotels (just because you have real plates does not make your product any better).
Heavy doors hitting & shaking the walls
Loud AC unit
Thin walls
Room layout is not that great (think old school motel sinks on the outside directly in front of the bed). 
I probably will not stay here again unless the price is a steal. The cold plain breakfast alone was a major turn off. If your into style over substance than this is cool place.

title: “Nicer, older hotel”
text: Stayed over early September for a family funeral. The hotel is very large and the grounds are beautiful! Upon check-in, I was greeted by a very friendly associate, immediately handed 4 warm cookies for my family and I, and recognized for my HHonors status. Check-in was a breeze. Our room entrance overlooked the inner courtyard, pool, and spa. Sadly, we came back too late from the visitation to enjoy the pool, and had to leave early in the morning for the procession. The room itself was nice. The hotel appears dated (older elevators, building itself, stone walls in the rooms), but these things did not detract from our experience. It is obvious that the staff do an excellent job keeping and older building filled with newer renovations. The only downside my family could find was the room entrance itself. The door and front wall are made of glass with a privacy curtain. As we were expecting to be gone most of the evening, it was a little difficult drawing the curtains behind us as we left so nobody could see into our room, and the same process with removing the curtains when we returned. Had I been traveling alone, this would not be a problem, as I trust the hotel with my security. My family, however, does not travel as much as I. We ate in the restaurant then next morning. The buffet was nice and fully stocked when we arrived. I did realize at that time, however, that I did not receive my breakfast vouchers at check in. Since it was early and we were in a rush to leave, I didn't think much of it. It wasn't that big of a deal. It was a very nice experience, and I had a good nights sleep, which is all that mattered on this trip

title: “Lovely”
text: This hotel was very nice. The room was very clean and comfortable; the bathroom was beautiful. The location was great as well. The staff was helpful and friendly. I highly recommend this hotel and would definitely stay here again.

title: “better than expected”
text: We bid on priceline for a 4* room downtown and got University Place. THEN we read the reviews. We were just going to "donate" our $ to Priceline after reading them and stay at the new JW Marriott downtown. We finally decided that even if we stay one night at the University Place and leave the room empty for our 2nd night and go to JW Marriott than we are still saving money. So... we got there, my husband checked in. He messaged me that there were 3 people in front of me - so I thought, here we go... it is going to be 15-20 minutes to check-in. But he was back in 5 and he said there was one person at the desk.. he said the lobby looked nice. OK, so far so good and I kept thinking how gross the room will be BUT we got into our room and it was very nice and very clean. I was very impressed. Bed was fine, shower was fine. Breakfast was good but it did take a bit longer than normal to receive and it was fairly expensive. We continued to debate our move to the JW and finally decided that there really wasn't anything bad except the location, which was NOT downtown. But during our 2nd evening, we did experience some loud neighbors who had the tv on and were yelling while they were getting ready to go out at midnight. Anyway, all was pretty good except location. Everyone was very nice. We even got cookies and bottled water in the evening. Very pleased. Maybe we were lucky with a nice room (they did upgrade us to a Junior Suite). healthclub was decent... pool was a few blocks away

title: “Clean new hotel, friendly staff”
text: We stayed here from 3/14 - 3/17. The hotel is easy to get to off highway 101. Highland Blvd. is a very busy street so turning left out of the hotel parking lot is almost impossible, you have to go another way if you need to go north on Highland, like if you are going to Universal Studios which is not far up 101. The hotel is very new and is therefore very clean. The staff was always friendly and always greeted us warmly with a smile - the front desk staff, the parking attendant, the maids and the breakfast buffet custodian, everybody. The lobby is tiny and only consists of the front desk. Everything else is on the 4th floor, which is good for security purposes. There is a convenience store and a few food places across HIghland, but I felt a bit uncomfortable going there because there are bums that hang out in the parking lot. However they did not bother us for handouts or harass us in any way, it's just a little disconcerting that they are around. The location of the hotel is very convenient to Hollywood Blvd, practically around the corner from the famous Graumann's Theater. Be aware that it is an uphill walk back to the hotel from there, but it is only about 2 - 3 blocks. You can find lots of places to eat there too - we went to the Disney Soda Fountain for an ice cream treat right at the corner of Highland and Hollywood, yum! Our room was an executive queen suite, which was a very large room for a family of four and probably fit 6 comfortably. It was offered to us at the same price as the standard two queen room so it was a good deal at the time. There is no separate living room, just an arched wall separating the beds from the sofabed. The sofabed, being new, was in good shape and not lumpy or uneven. When opened there was still plenty enough space to maneuver around. The queen beds were wonderful and I liked that they provided lots of pillows on the beds. I added photos of the room so you can see how it looks. We were on the 4th floor which was THE BEST, get a room there if you can because all the amenities are there - business center, pool and FREE breakfast buffet. Our room was in a corner of the building and was a few steps from all the amenities and I felt safe letting my 12 and 9 year old daughters run out to breakfast alone to grab a bite in the morning while I finished getting ready. Even though our room was right along Highland Blvd, we never heard traffic noises, and like I said it's a very busy street. I wasn't expecting much from the breakfast buffet because it was free but I was pleasantly surprised. Every morning, there were eggs, bacon or sausage, an array of bready items (bagels, bread, muffins, pastries, cereal), juices, milk and coffee/tea. A very decent start to our day. We really enjoyed our stay here and would definitely recommend this hotel. I would stay here again if I'm ever in Los Angeles.

title: “Served our needs well”
text: My stay was pleasant, the staff was helpful, the selection of foods for breakfast was adequate (missed eggs).

title: “Bed bugs-read what to look for and check EVERY bed you sleep in”
text: I stayed in this hotel as a result of volunteering to give up my seat on United Airlines. Oh, boy. What a mistake. The shuttle ride took about 45 minutes as traffic was horrible. I had just missed the previous shuttle so stood outside approx. 1 hour waiting. I got to the hotel and checked in. I took my stuff to the room and threw my stuff on the bed. Ugh. I then went downstairs to eat with my $20 food voucher. I had a shrimp appetizer and a hot tea. It was good but the service took forever and it was freezing in the restaurant. I went back to the room and it looked very nice and inviting. I climbed into bed about 11PM. I had to be back at the airport for a 6AM flight. So, I was only actually in the bed about 4 hours. It was so comfy and felt really clean. I travel every weekend. honestly, for some reason I have never even thought about bed bugs. What a terrible misconception. When I arrived in Philadelphia later that day I noticed 2 huge bumps on my face. I had no idea what it was. Then later on I started having horrible itching on my back. I stopped at a roadside rest as I was in agony to have a look. I was covered in huge bumps. Coincidently, I Googled bed bugs and low and bhold I knew that this was what I had. I called the hotel manager who insisted that they have never had an incident and pretty much brushed me off. he also stated that they would investigate. However, he said there were more guests in there and it would have to wait until they checked out. So, now more people with the critters. He said they would call after doing the check. I then felt like nothing would actually be done so I called the Denver Health Dept. I was covered in bites. I probably contaminated more people as I stayed in another hotel, and traveled home on a plane. I researched this extensively. I had my husband meet me at the airport with clean clothes. I bagged and threw away what I had on. He also brought trash bags and we triple bagged my luggage and put it in the back of a truck. It is still sitting in my garage. I never heard back from the hotel so I called them again. The manager did return my call and leave a message that they had found 1 bed bug in the room. I had 45 bites in 4 hours. These bites burn and itch and hurt. I still have red marks 6 weeks later. I am totally freaked out and feel like I constantly have things crawling on me. I have spent a fortune buying bed bug detectors in case I brought any home. I also had to buy a lot of new clothes as I don't want to open the plastic bags. I did find a company that will disinfect my luggage and purse for $125 each. The hotel offered me absolutely nothing to compensate me for my expenditures. The place I contacted in Las Vegas that does the disinfecting says the hotels should pay for this service. United said they had no responsibility. Even though they sent me there. The Denver Health dept also confirmed that there were bed bugs in my room. I do not know what is going to stop this epidemic unless the hotels take responsibilty and help with the cost of cleaning up the mess caused by a stay in an infested room. I am going to post my experience everywhere I can.

title: “Great location, great value”
text: A fantastic location, just a couple of blocks from the Empire State Building. Both the hotel and the street are quiet. Subway station on the corner. Rooms were small but clean. Shared bathrooms were small but clean. The rooms also have a sink. I would definitely stay here again and recommend it to anyone looking for a budget hotel.

title: “Excellent Stay !”
text: We spent 3 nights at this hotel over the weekend of 9th January - which happened to be the coldest temperatures that Boston has had for about 20years!! The fantastic location of this hotel helped us a lot given that the sky walks meant we did not actually have to venture out into the cold weather if we did not want to. The Palm restaurant, the hotel bar, the staff, the rooms and most of all the location were excellent and we would not hesitate to stay there again. Boston is fab and I would love to go back in the summer !

title: “Noisy, musty and need of a good cleaning”
text: The location is great and the price was right but the room smelled musty. Plus our room was too close to the firehouse across the street and the screaming sirens woke us up all night long. If you do come, ask for a room away from Arch St and the noise.

title: “Wonderful”
text: This hotel was great, very clean, great customer service. The only downfall was they have a dress code for the lobby after 6:00pm (thats difficult for tourists walking around all day sweating) and no free internet in your room. With the price they charge I believe the internet should be free for guests not for anyone that just walks in the lobby.

title: “Beresford”
text: The Beresford on Sutter St. was a bargain buy. The room was REAL small. It was clean and the room service was good. But the view was horrific, I had a fantasic vantage point for seeing the trash in the alley outside.The room didn't have Air Conditioning. The valet parking was quick. The location is right across the street from the new "Who's your daddy hotel" No kidding!! That is the name of the place.It was fairly modest lodging. I would recommend it for the no frills traveler.

title: “Creepy bohemian chic”
text: Nobody stays at the Chelsea for the rooms or the dreary midtown location - it's the history that attracts. Dylan Thomas went out from here to drink himself to death, Andy Warhol filmed The Chelsea Girls and Sid Vicious murdered his girlfriend Nancy Spungen in room 100. Our room at the rear was plain, small and shabby. By all accounts the rooms at the front are the most desirable and difficult to get. There are many long term residents and there appeared to be a small religious cult in residence on our floor. The corridors are wide, gloomy and mysterious and reception is full of "art" contributed by residents. Staff were friendly and helpful. The building itself is a beautiful piece of architecture and there was an excellent spanish seafood restaurant next door.

title: “Great location!”
text: Beautiful hotel in a perfect spot. It is just steps from Times Square and many shops. We took advantage of the stack parking across the street for $25/night then walked and rode the subway around the city. Do not touch any drinks or snacks in the room though unless you want extra charges. Overall it was very clean and made for a great NY experience!

title: “Nice downtown hotel”
text: I just stayed at this hotel, and enjoyed the stay. The staff is friendly and welcoming, rooms are typically decent Residence Inn studio, and was roomy and well furnished. The location downtown can't be beat. I'd stay here or the adjoining Courtyard in a heartbeat.

title: “Great Place To Stay”
text: The room had two double beds and was pretty clean. The bathroom was nice too. We had a great view in our room with a patio. the pool was just steps away from our room, and it had a huge hot tub. Our room also included a free breakfest buffet that was wonderful. You could eat outside or inside. They also had a pool that had two Sea Lions which was a nice touch. There was certain feeding times where you could watch them feed the Sea Lions. Nice bar on site too.

title: “Wonderful Stay”
text: We decided to spend Christmas away from home and family this year - a difficult decision! We were thrilled with our accomodations at the Hyatt. We had an early flight Christmas Eve and the hotel had NO problem letting us check in early (1pm) so we could try to enjoy the afternoon. Just a block from the 16th Street Mall the hotel made access to food, shopping and entertainment a breeze. The staff at the hotel were top notch - very professional and courteous. When we returned to our room Christmas Eve we were greeted with a plate of scrumptious, hand-made cookies - for Santa we presume! The breakfast buffet at the hotel restaurant was out of this world, with a wait staff catering to all our needs. We rented a car on our second day in the city - the Enterprise desk is in the lobby of the hotel and they pull the car to the front door. When we returned that evening the valet just took the car and the keys and that was it - no hassles with parking! In the end we thoroughly enjoyed our trip and would definitely stay at the Hyatt on another visit to Denver. Clean rooms, superbly comfy beds, awesome views (we were on the 16th floor with a view of the city AND the mountains) and great people - what more can you ask for?

title: “fab hotel”
text: just returned from the Affinia Dumont. Before I booked the hotel I had read several hotel reviews and didnt see a single negative review about the Affinia and I wasnt disappointed. Staff were all polite and courteous, room very clean and the kitchenette was an added bonus. I was travelling in a party of 4 and the room was very spacious for us all. The hotel is ideally situated being within walking distance of many attractions. Cant wait to visit New York again and I'll certainly stay at this hotel

title: “Very nice”
text: My brother and I stayed here for one night while we were in town and the room was so nice. The breakfast was really tasty. They had the basic bagels and danishes as well as pancakes, eggs, and biscuits and gravy. At the front desk they also had the most delicious coffee i have ever had! They were renovating the dining area while we were there but they provided trays so you could take your food back up to your room, which I actually really liked! My only complaint was that they charge $34 for valet parking but when you pull up no one is out there to open your door, greet you, etc. We had to walk inside to the front desk and check in and just hand our keys to the front desk girl. Not the valet treatment I expect for $34 added on each night.

title: “Good airport hotel with a few notes”
text:
I have been here a few times before. This time, hotwire assigned me and my family to this place. Probably at the low end of typical Westin hotels: I should not complain since I payed only $120 per night, although this is a big increase from last year when I payed $80 for a room at Hilton which is across the street with a similar quality.
I had no trouble with the stay. My kids loved the little swimming pool and the jacuzzi. Free wi-fi was available at the lobby.
Some complaints were 
- when we requested little items missing in the room such as plastic bag for ice and additional hygienic items, they did not eventually get them to us. 
- Although weak, we could smell urine through A/C. Long time ago, when I visited this property, I had a big trouble with this smell.
- Touching anything in the fridge seems to turn on a bill. 
- Parking may be expensive, but we did not have a car.

title: “Poor Staff”
text: My main complaint is the customer service is poor. I like this hotel facilities and location. However in general the staff are badly trained and management is awful. Occasionally you get some really nice people who are willing to help but they are undermined by the way the hotel is run. At least I received a discounted rate through Resorts Plus International.

title: “Nice Home Base for Sleeping”
text:
Had my parents stay here for two nights while they were visiting. I believe this is their third stay at the hotel, and I'd definitely have them stay at the Holiday Inn again. It's a great home base for resting and sleeping, as they don't need anything fancy beyond a comfortable bed and friendly staff and Chinatown restaurants less than two blocks away. The Mondrian is right around the corner, but the Holiday Inn feels more homey. 
Pros
* Very friendly staff. The bellman Abhi (sp?) was especially helpful and super friendly. Liked the complimentary iced tea in lobby.
* Great location, especially for walking tours of SoHo, Chinatown, Little Italy. 
* Comfortable, but small room. The bed was very comfortable and the furniture seemed pretty new. The bathroom was a little dated, but clean. 
* Free wifi, but service was spotty at times. 
* Tiny gym, new equipment. 
Cons
* Tough to catch a taxi outside hotel. The bellman will help you, but it may take awhile. Use Uber or car service if you're on a tight schedule. 
* Small room. The sleeping room is dominated by the king bed, with just enough room to walk around the bed. 
* Window A/C unit a little loud. No central air. 
* A little bit noisy. Can hear conversations outside and occasionally ice being dispensed from ice maker.

title: “Great location for a charming hotel”
text: Really nice room, with character, but like real character - as in rooms were quaint and pretty, and not character as in grimy. Location was awesome, right on Union Square, close to everything, including those trams that would take you everywhere. Windows were soundproof enough that noise from outside wasn't a problem at night. Front desk was very courteous and helpful, housekeeping was prompt. The pillow options were a great touch, so were the free local phone calls. All in all very good place for it's price. I paid around USD$100 per room per night.

title: “Ahoy captain”
text: Yes, everyone talks about the size of the rooms. Imagine a captains cabin on a navy destroyer and you are just about there. The rooms are very clean and the bunk beds are quaint and everything is new - reminds me of motel 1 in Berlin both in size and atmosphere. If you are looking for a place to crash on a budget and don't want funky old beds/furnishings or rasty neighborhood then the pod is the ticket. Staff is a bit cluessless at times about how to run a hotel but they are trying. Nice Thai restaurant around the corner.

title: “Can't beat the price!”
text: We didn't know a lot about that hotel before making our reservation but were really pleased. We loved the "historic" look of it and the room looked really nice clean and the King bed was confortable. We had free wifi but it wouldn't work well in our room. We asked a room that was not on the street side (too noisy) but on the parking side and with the AC on it was perfect. There is not elevator but that wasn't a problem for us. Can't beat the price of 49$. Try to visit the Paramount Studios since it's the next door!! (make you reservation in advance)

title: “Great room with jacuzzi for 2! Excellent location!”
text:
We picked this hotel because I was serching for a hotel room with something a little special. The room we had is considered a King jacuzzi suite. It was a two area suite. When you walk in it had a living room with a TV, sofa sleeper and a full bar with fridge, then the bedroom had a King bed and another TV. The furniture was beautiful. 
The view was looking down onto the famous 6th street from the 11th floor of this hotel. The best though....was the bathroom...it had a huge jacuzzi tub that easily fit 2 people, it also had a seperate shower stall and two vanities and 2 toliets! There was door that could seperate the 2 room bathroom area if necessary. This could be a great set up for a family or a great setup for a romantic night! The price rate great too at $192.00 for the night with the AAA discount. The valet parking was mandatory at $15.00 additional. This was nice for a special treat! The location is walking distance to the restaurants on 6th street.

title: “Very good hotel in the Heart of Chicago”
text: I've stayed at this hotel several times, and have taken a liking to it. It is centrally located on Michigan Ave., has a very nice dining room that is underutilized at dinner, and a good bar with excellent service. A very nice, up-to-date gym. The rooms are very good, the larger rooms with a separate bath tub. Unfortunately the hotel is situated close enough to the buildings around it that in some rooms it picks up the local HVAC noise. And the highest rooms, on the 17th and 18th floor pick up the hotel's HVAC buzz. But lower floors are fine. The lobby needs a new lay-out, there is a lot of wasted space. Still, this hotel feels like a boutique, and trumps the chains around it. It is not like the Conrad Hong Kong, but is darn nice. Good service.

title: “Wonderful Romantic Getaway”
text:
I had originally planned on staying in another hotel - but with the declining dollar and the financial crisis, the Gild Hall slipped into my (Eurobased)budget. I stayed there with my wife a few days before Christmas for her Birthday.
We were warmly received on the evening of our arrival and after a speedy check-in shown into our large and nice room (the guest pictures shown here well-reflect what the rooms look like).
The cake I had ordered via e-mail was duly delivered on the birthday next morning together with a nice breakfast. Because we couldn't eat the whole cake it was stored for us and taken out on our request (we were even served a complimentary hot chocolate one afternoon) - the cake was too huge to be eaten up completely - and delicious. Except on this one occasion, we never had breakfast here as we were always up and rushed early in the morning for siteseeing. 
The place appears to fill up as a bar in the evenings although we never made it - always being to exhausted from a day out.
The location is absolutely no problem - it does get quiet in the evenings (which is great for light sleepers like myself), but access to nearly everywhere is excellent with well-connected subway stations within a few minutes.
The hotel also offers a gym (not seen or tested) and a small internet room with free and fast internet terminals.
The the last day there was a pipe burst which put one of the elevators out of service and flooded the 2nd floor bar and lobby - put it was professionally handled and elevators were back in service fairly quickly - it was an exciting little "adventure" while staying there.
All in all service is excellent, friendly and very personal and for under 200USD a night, the value for money was great.
Thanks to the Gild Hall team for making our stay, my wife's first to New York, so pleasant.

title: “very disappointing”
text: i was very disappointed in my stay at this hotel. I had a guaranteed reservation, but they were oversold the night I arrived. They put me up in a terrible room--not a hotel room but a conference room with a very uncomfortable pull down trundle bed. To make things worse they insisted on charging me full price for this room. They were very condescending when I suggested that it was inappropriate to charge full price for such horrible accomodations, especially when they fail to meet a guaranteed reservation.

title: “New,quiet .comfortable,but needs attention”
text: We stayed at this motel for 3 nights ,made reservation with call center but no good direction given to get there ,No exit #.. had a hard time finding. Nice & new opened in Jan,quiet & comfortable,reasonable rates but..needs attention from staff.No listing of TV channels & there are many,said that cards are not made up yet.I said why can't you make a list of the channels & make copies for all the rooms.Phone at the desk didn't work so, no internet They did have a room with 2 computers that you could use..No directory of motel services.Only a few items put out at a time for breakfast.Whole wheat bread was dry.No kleenex holder in bathroom & toilet paper holder in awkward position.Drain poor in tub & water ran from tub & shower at the same time,couldn;t control.Micro & Frig in cabinet in corner could be better at angle.They will probably get all this sorted out in due time.

title: “Near Macy's”
text: The hotel is well located in Midtown Manhattan on the 35th, near Macy's and the subway station (34th). We have asked for a wheelchair accessible room and we got it. The room was at the 2nd floor, near the hotel's office and with the opened place at the entrance of the hotel we can easily ear all the noise coming from the main entrance. 2nd floor is also the way to go to the fitness center. So this was continuously crowd and noisy. Room was very well equipped but you understand that at the second floor there is no view at all on the city. The prize for the room was fair if we consider the location of the hotel which is very good. I can easily recommend the hotel for limited budget avoiding to go to stay in New Jersey just for a cheaper prize... but avoid the second floor.

title: “Great hotel. The prepaid price was really good for the experience. Service was very good, the pool and gym were great.”
text: We checked in early and because it was Christmas week, the hotel was not heavily occupied. The staff was friendly and greeted us by name. We prepaid for a suite and the room was ready for us with a gift for both of my young kids, along with a personal welcome message for both the children in the room. The staff provided extra robes for the children. The pool was well appointed and so was the gym. I reserved a spa appointment online which they didn't have upon arriving, but the staff provided a new spa appointment for the next day which was acceptable. Overall, a very nice experience.

title: “Everything a family could want....we had a BLAST!”
text: We are a family of 5 and this was perfect for us. After a full day of walking around DC...the evening reception was just what we needed! Then soaking in the hot tub while the kiddies swam was the perfect way to end the day. The room was plenty big enough for us and the breakfast in the morning is THE BOMB! WE WILL BE BACK!

title: “Good location, acceptable but could be better”
text: Great location, just south of Central Park and close to subway station. The room is good size for NY city. The room is showing its age and housekeeping can do a better job, but all in all not too bad. The bed is too soft for my liking. The heater didn't work so it's a good thing it wasn't too cold when my husband and I stayed. If you can afford a more expensive hotel, you should. Otherwise this is not a bad place to stay if you're not too picky.

title: “Not the best, Not the worst...”
text:
Stayed 4 nights here as we were on a budget.
Cons:
Funny smell as you walked in-definitely needs a make over.
No fitted sheet or underlay which was REALLY annoying.
Noisy street outside due to the muni train but we got used to that.
NO Tea and coffee facilities or anything usefull 
Parking was a first in first serve so we made sure we were in early.
Pros:
HEAPS of tv channels which i loved
Room was big and away from bathroom which was a nice change from all the other places we had stayed in recently...
Had a fridge and microwave
Should be a little cheaper for what it was but not as bad as some we have stayed in.

title: “Great practical hotel”
text:
Great practical hotel: clean, bright, wonderful location and amazingly nice staff.
The room is clean and comfortable. They provide free bottled water, nice supply of towels, and supplies. The staff is amazingly nice and friendly.

title: “Perfect Hotel Perfect Location”
text: Excellent hotel. All the reviews say the same, excellent. If you find fault with this hotel for any reason, other than the cable stations which are limited, you should be staying at the Waldorf. In New York City this price usually gets you many many things, mostly bugs. This hotel is clean, clean, clean. Thanks guys.

title: “very cool place, great location”
text:
This is a very unique hotel, right at the edge of Chinatown. The staff is very helpful, with great restaurant recommendations, quickly providing any extras we needed. The daily happy hour is nice, they went out of their way to get something for my kids.
Just a warning, it is small. The room (we had a double-double) was tight, with a sink in the room outside the bathroom. The lobby is also pretty small, but there is plenty of space to hang out (I stayed down there in front of the fire after the kids went to bed). However we had no problems with the size of the room, unless you are entertaining it is fine for sleeping and dressing.
If you do have kids, we heard there was a dog in the lobby. In reality he belongs to one bellman, who is not there all the time. After three days we saw the dog once, which disappointed our kids a little.
Overall it is in a very convenient location, we could get to public transportation to just about anywhere in a few blocks. Definitely would recommend it for a family if you want a cheaper alternative to the pricier high end hotels.

title: “Better than expected.”
text: Great hotel, great price. Customer service was superb. Would stay again, and recommend.

title: “Top Notch Hotel with Great Staff”
text:
My wife and I stayed here from January 5 to 10, and the hotel and staff exceeded all expectations. I have been a Hilton Hhonors member for years and generally speaking the hotels are nice, clean and comfotable. The Hilton Garden Inn Times Square is, however, above and beyond in all categories. The room was large, spotless and quiet. The maid service kept it spotless throughout. I had told the guest relations staff that we were celebrating an event, and we found a bottle of champagne waiting on check-in.
 Everyone on the staff was professional, friendly and thoughtful.
 The location is hard to beat: Times Square and Rockefeller Center are only a short walk away and a subway station right across the street can take you south to the World Trade Center site or north to Central Park attractions like the Museum of Natural History without any change of train required. Many theaters are also close at hand.
 This is the first review I've written for Trip Advisor, as I was waiting for something worth writing about. This hotel is that.

title: “Good Location, Tiny Room”
text:
Hotel 373 is located right next to Empire State Building--you can see it out of the window. The room was the size of a walk-in closet, I had never stayed in anything that small. For the price ($370 mid-week) it felt like a rip-off, even by NYC standards. The building is old and even though it's been renovated, there is no central AC with big noisy AC box buit into the window. The room didn't have much light, the bathroom door wouldn't shut completely. 
As for the positives, the location is great, the room was clean and the bathroom was relatively nice. It was fine for overnight stay.

title: “Absolutely Blown Away-Bravo!”
text: What an absolutely amazing experience at the new Omni Dallas! The check-in process went very smoothly and the hotel room accommodations were superb! What a beautiful view of downtown Dallas and the TV in the bathroom mirror was a very nice touch. We had a great time at the Owner's box and were even waited on by the general manager himself, Mr. Josh French, with whom we were very impressed. The gym at the hotel is gorgeous and looks out onto the city as well. There are a ton of cardio and weight machines as well as a whole free weight area. The breakfast buffet was a little pricey ($17/person) but the money was well spent. The buffet had everything from fresh fruit & berries, granola, yogurt, pastries, frittas, scrambled eggs, bacon as well as a station where you could order your own omlettes and waffles. Many thanks to Alan at the omlette station for a wonderful breakfast. After breakfast, we headed to the pool which like everything else was just amazing. Our waitress Helen was extremely accommodating and hospitable. Great drinks-the bartender at the pool even created a special drink for us which was fabulous. All and all, if you are staying downtown, you can't go wrong with the Omni. The price ($145/night) in my mind is a great value and I couldn't have been happier with my experience!

title: “Overpriced for what's on offer”
text:
I had high expectations when I arrived at this hotel, I had been told when I booked my stay that it was one of the best hotels in San Francisco and we decided to spend 3 days of our honeymoon at this hotel expecting the best. The check in area was very impressive and spacious, although I did notice straight away that people not staying at the hotel seemed to use it as a shortcut through to get to Union Square. It took quite a while to get checked in, they seemed to only have 3 staff and it was a busy monday night. When we finally got checked in there was a long queue for the two lifts that go to all floors and they are definitely not big enough to service such a large and busy hotel.
It took quite a while to find our room as the hotel seems to consist of lots of corridors that all pretty much looked the same on our floor. When we finally found our room I was dissapointed, it was right at the end of a corridor next to some sort of staff room and fire escape. The room was a lot smaller than I expected, it was no bigger than a normal double bedroom back home although it was nicely decorated and had a large flatscreen TV. The bed was extremely comfy though which was probably the best thing about the room. The bathroom was small but again it was very well decorated. There was quite a bit of noise at night and we could hear people walking up and down the corridors at all hours.
One of the biggest dissapointments was that I had been told the rooms had views of the city...my room had a view of a wall and window of another part of the hotel. The best thing about the hotel is the restaurant, we had a fantastic meal there on out last night, the food was fantastic and the service was brilliant. It was beautifully decorated and surprisingly quiet which we loved. The hotel is in a good location and is in walking distance of some great shops and the underground. 
We expected a lot more from the amount of money we paid to stay for 3 nights and when we looked into it, we could have stayed at the Hilton for a lot less money for a bigger room and more facilities. If I go back to San Francisco I would not stay here again...but I would go for a meal at the restaurant!!

title: “Location, location, location”
text: Stayed here for our 30 anniversary. Loved it! Very clean and roomy. Had a little deck facing Columbus St. 1 1/2 blocks from cable car turnaround, and kiosk for muni passes $18.00 for a three day one, Get one! it is worth it as a single cable car ride is $5 one way. Free parking was a bonus, as the car did not move the four days we were there, as FW, and most other sightseeing things are not far away. Recommend the Alcatraz Tour. Excellent rate $79 a nite. Would defineately stay here again.

title: “QUICK decline of a hotel”
text:
I've stayed at the Hudson in the past, and therefore when the opportunity to return to NYC surfaced, I did not hesitate recommending this hotel for my colleagues' and my 6 night stay. It looks like that in 2 years, things have started to decline, and the overall experience was pretty poor.
Before even returning, I had read the many poor reviews, and thought that people were exagerating - but it looks like people's issues have come to full fruition.
Issues:
1. Television did not work the 1st evening. Had to go to front desk to have it serviced. 
2. It took more than 60 minutes for my luggage to be delivered to my room upon arrival. 
3. There was no hot water during the 1st day and therefore had to take a luke warm shower at 7:00 am. As you can imagine, not the most pleasant experience. Again informed front desk, and was resolved
4. The phones were erratic. The message indicator light was going on and off for no reason.
