5. LAST morning, I took a bitterly cold shower at 4:30 in the morning!!! Not a sign of heat!!!!
6. Upon comparing notes, it sounds like my colleague's rooms did not have hot water as well!
7. Safe was missing in my colleague's room!?!
To be frank with you, for the price point of this hotel, the amount was unjustifiable. Basic services such as hot water should not be optional. I actually accepted the small size of the room, but when it comes to basic ammenities, that's when I'm a bit perplexed.
I am returning to NYC in December, and at this point I have no incentive to return to your hotel. I would live to hear the reasons behind my inconveniences. To be frank with you, I have read the poor reviews of the Hudson on tripadvisor. But unfortunately, if looks like your hotel is beginning to live up to its poor reputation. 
Sabrina from Customer Service contacted me, and informed me that there are a myriad of upgrades beginning in January. I have plans to return to NYC in December, and am very skeptical of the idea of returning to this hotel. For the price that you're paying, it might be better to really consider spending a bit more and bringing your business else where.
V.

title: “Beautiful hotel, amazing service!!!”
text:
I stayed at Le Meridien for a night with friends in September and enjoyed every moment of it. From the moment we arrived we were treated so well! With a wonderful greeting by the valet then a fast and friendly check-in (we also enjoyed picking out our own custom room key!). The room was very large with 2 extremely comfortable double beds, flat screen tv, and a lounge area with a large couch. Also, the close proximity to the Galleria is great, we enjoyed the mall quite a bit.
2 comments about the service- after a night out in Downtown Dallas my friends and I were craving some late night snacks and the room service menu didn't have much that appealed to us at the time. Since we had been drinking we were sort of stuck were we were!! We called the front desk and they suggested that we have the valet drive us to wherever we wanted to get food and then bring it back, which he happily did! I have never heard of such a thing but it was incredibly thoughtful and convenient!
Also, the next morning I went downstairs to the lobby in hopes of getting some coffee and breakfast with my friend. Unfortunately the bar area had stopped serving food but we asked a man in the area and he said he would have whatever we wanted brought out to us. So, my friend and I sat in the lobby (in those great whimsical chairs) and had a leisurely morning filled with conversation, coffee, and wonderful service.
I would not hesitate to go back when I return to Dallas!

title: “Best hotel stay ever - really shacked!”
text:
I had an interesting experience at Hotel Rogue, which is known for being an "all red" boutique-inspired hotel. I don't really like the color red at all, but after researching all of the other hotels in DC I decided this was my best bet. I like unique places, and didn't want to stay at a Four Seasons or Ritz. 
I called Hotel Rogue to inquire about my pending stay, and ran into a few problems. After I brought it to their attention Hotel Rogue went above and beyond to ensure that I had the best stay possible. 
First the reservationist called me to make sure that everything was ready for my arrival. The manager also called to make sure I did not need anything else. The check-in girls were friendly and efficient upon arrival. 
The best part, came, however, when I walked into my room. I was on a very high floor in a huge room. At my request, the hotel provided me with Frette linens, a goldfish they named "Bob Marley" and six of their special red velvet cupcakes. Everyone should order the cupcakes, they were amazing.
They also left a handwritten note for me that was really sweet. I went downstairs to meet a friend, and found out they had free wine and truffle bruschetta during happy hour. They also have a free hot chocolate bar in the afternoon. 
That night I slept like a baby. The next day the staff changed over but were equally as professional and friendly. They actually really helped me out because there was snowstorm in NY, and my flight home was canceled. So I got to stay in my room for an extra nine hours while I was trying to sort out my travel plans. 
All in all, I would highly recommend the Hotel Rogue if you are in DC. The decor is very funky - which is important to me as I'm taking interior design classes and really like to be surrounded by unique decor. The food at the bar is actually really good - much better than you would ever think. There are a lot of free perks, and it's a fun place to come back to at the end of a long day. The best part is that the room was also extremely affordable, and the customer service is bar none.
I was so impressed I actually wrote them a thank you note when I got home - which, trust me, is rare for me to do.

title: “Warwick Denver”
text: Great location, good restaurant on premises and 2 blocks away. My room was luxurious and my bed slept so well. All the staff were helpful and friendly. I got a great deal on my room and recommend this hotel highly. I was a single woman traveling alone and felt safe in the neighborhood. Looking forward to a return visit.

title: “A missed opportunity for good customer service”
text: We booked one night in the Hotel Reserve in order to attend the baptism of a friend's child. Unfortunately our flight had mechanical difficulties, was canceled, and there was no way we could get to New York. Our reservation at Hotel Reserve was an advance purchase and required a 24 hour cancellation. The manager, Daisy, though very kind said there was no way she could reverse the charge. Things happen, we understand the policy, but feel this was a missed opportunity for good customer service.

title: “Pleasant but nothing fantastic”
text:
We stayed here in a two queen bed room for three nights towards the end of June. The room was claustrophobic and heavy and made staying in it depressing. Quite a low ceiling, heavy furniture and a very old clanky air conditioning system that was large and took up a large part of the area by the window didn't help. We did have a front facing view which was very nice of the surrounding area and Downtown LA in the distance. The bathroom was very, very small, but clean. There is a large fridge, a microwave and coffee maker.
The bar serves a starbucks coffee and there is a Coffee Bean outlet around the corner and a Ralph's supermarket. Also a car hire company directly opposite. Outside the hotel is a bus stop that will take you to Santa Monica, The Grove, Rodeo Drive etc. It's a nice quiet area away from the masses of Hollywood Boulevard having stayed in that area before, it can get too much. 
If driving it's easy to get to the nearby highways, Venice, Santa Monica and beyond.
The check in and out was quick and easy.
Our overall stay was quite pleasant I can't either say that it was anything great either. The rooms mainly could do with modernizing.

title: “10th Floor is the way to go!!!”
text: We stayed here from 8/27/11 to 8/29/11. We ended up staying the extra night due to Hurricane Irene. This hotel is one of the best. We stayed on the 10th Floor which is the top floor and has the executive lounge. The staff from valet (Ben), to the front desk, to everyone in the executive lounge especially Mr. Lewis and the bartender Kirk!! Mr. Lewis really made our stay special. I wish I could remember another staff member working the desk outside he was the best!! I would totally recommend this hotel as well as staying here again. What a way to ride out the hurricane. The only way we knew there was a hurricane was on tv or looking out the window. We could not hear a thing.

title: “Great Stay!”
text: I'm in NYC every month but I decided to take the girlfriend with me. Excellent staff, very helpful. Rooms were clean and spottless. Location was perfect, walking distance to Times square. Ill be back for sure.

title: “Cool but had some problems”
text:
We stayed here one night for the location in Seattle and because we thought it would be so "technologically" impressive. We were disappointed by a few problems. 
The Good:
The decor was nice, the room was mostly clean, and it was very quiet. The view was very nice.
The Bad:
Arrived to check it at 4pm... their check-in time and had to wait about 30 minutes with many other very unhappy travelers.
When we got to our room, about 5 minutes later, a maid walked in without much notice (probably a result of them trying to hurry and get us our room).
The tv remote had a broken button, their "engineer" had to come up to give us a new one.
The technology was far less than expected or advertised.
The Ugly:
We bought a bottle of wine from a local store and went to use the complimentary glasses only to find lots of dust and mouth prints. They were quick to bring us new ones.
Took a bath in the soaking tub (best bath ever btw) but when I pushed the button to open/close the automatic privacy shade, the thing completely fell down from the ceiling... mounting brackets and all! That was the worst... and then the only thing they did was to give us half off our parking which amounted to about a $15 discount. 
Over-all the atmosphere was a little hectic, like it is a newer hotel that hasn't ironed out its problems. The "technology" was not all that it was advertised to be, and the rooms were falling apart. We will probably stay in another hotel next time. For the same price we could find an equally, more established hotel that will not have so many problems.

title: “Another terrific stay”
text: We stayed here last year and I was a bit wary becuase of some of the recent reviews. Luckily we encountered no real problems during our stay. Location is a bit weird to get to but the value makes it worth the effort. Front desk is fairly knowledgable. Several restaurants and a movie theatre less than a mile west of here.

title: “Right in the Heart of Things”
text:
This was our first night of our trip and the Hotel was in a great place for food and night life.
The room was comfortable and quite and the staff friendly.
Breakfast was excellent!
A great start to the trip

title: “Great for people on a budget!”
text: The Dolphin Motel is a quaint little motel right on the harbor across from where fishing boats come in, therefore a great location for fishermen. It is old, but probably the cleanest place we have ever stayed. Rooms are tiny, but when you are in beautiful San Diego who is going to spend too much time inside any way. The cleaning staff does a great job and the guys behind the front desk are very friendly and helpful. If you stay here you will get to meet the owners, a father/son team who are very personable. It was ranked #6 I think in all of San Diego and definitely deserves that loftly ranking when considering room rate(very low by the way)/cleanliness/location/and staffing. We will definitely stay there again if we are ever fortunate enough to venture to San Diego. This place is not for everyone, especially if you are used to some of the more expensive places, but it suited us perfectly.

title: “Beautiful and Outstanding”
text:
I have stayed at the Parc 55 twice in the last year. You can not ask any more of the staff. They are outstanding! Forgot my razor, three delivered to my room within 10 minutes (at 5:30am!) The Concierge Lounge has phenomenal views of the city and the staff are incredible.
In regards to everyone's comments about the homeless - LOOK AROUND! 
They are everywhere in San Fran!! Heck, the city pays them a monthly allowance.
Every city has it's "bad side" of town. The Parc is located in Union Square and I've never felt unsafe walking to shops or dining at night. 
The Parc keeps the streets around their facility immaculate. I highly recommend the Parc 55 to everyone.
Regards - John

title: “The park and sail program was very convenient for us.”
text: Clean rooms. Friendly staff and gave helpful imformation regarding restaurants and other area information. It worked out well and made us more rested to start our cruise the next day. The transportation and parking was great too!!!

title: “Gem”
text:
Cant add anymore than everyone else has said...
Hotel is an absolute gem.
Position excellent.
Immaculately clean.
Food good.
But overall whats makes this hotel so good is the staff . From the cleaners to the concierge, from the minute you arrive they cant do enough for you.
If you are looking for a hotel in Boston look no further.
I am a Travel Agent and very rarely can find no fault with a hotel, but this one has made it through with no faults.

title: “Amazing Stay”
text:
We stayed at this hotel for 4 night during the first week of October. The lobby and elevator are very small but it wasn't that big of a deal. The room is gorgeous and the rate was amazing. We were steps away from everything! 
The beds were so comfortable and the temperature was perfect. The bathroom was huge and had a seperate area for makeup, hair etc which was wonderful since we had 3 girls in the room. The only issue with the bathroom was the shower door not closing all the way. 
I would like to stay here each and everytime I come to Chicago. I only hope the next time I can meet Jermaine the manager. I looked for him but was never able to catch him

title: “Friendly, modern and great location”
text: I met my sister here for a weekend get away and was impressed with the modern, elegant and spacious rooms, the friendly staff and convenient location. Be sure to request the complimentary "Walking Tour" experience kit chocked filled with the best maps, guidebooks and flash card walking tours of Chicago. The kit even includes an ipod with pre-loaded walking tour. Since the hotel is close to Millenium Park and Lake Shore Drive there are lots of great walks. We walked along Lake Shore Drive, through the Gold Coast and Old Town to the Lincoln Park Neighborhood filled with great boutiques, cafes and other shops. I highly recommend the Affinia. Their "pillow menu" allows you to request a special pillow of your choice. Nice touch! Also the C-View restuarant is excellent. While it hasn't made any of the restaurant picks in Chicago, we had dinner their one night and it was one of the best meals we had in Chicago. I liked it better than the Spiaggia Cafe. Prices are better as well.

title: “Lovely Arizona resort”
text: Very swanky resort with all resort amenities. Great spa, wonderful staff, great food. Fifteen miles north of most Phoenix attractions, but with AWESOME pools, why leave?

title: “Fun New Renovations! Believe me, it's changed!”
text:
We stayed at The Milford Plaza in late June and it was a pleasant suprise. Having seen the Milford in it's previous state, it has had an amazing transformation from old run-down rooms, to fully renovated 'chic' style rooms. The rooms are cheesy and fun, however even if it's not your style, it is great to have a hotel in such an amazing location right on Times Square be so clean and modern! 
If you are after a base right in the middle of everything, The Milford Plaza will not dissapoint. The only thing I guess is that the rooms are small, but hey, it's NYC.
If you love NYC, you will be back to the Milford Plaza ;)

title: “Luxury”
text: We stayed at this location for a vacation. From the beginning the staff treated us like we were their only guests. The amenities were exceptional and the concierge's recommendations were excellent. We chose to stay on the Club level and it was worth the extra cost. The lounge was well appointed and relaxing. My only complaint, if you can call it one, was that there were entirely too many kids on the club level. I wish there was something they could do to limit that distraction.

title: “pretty good”
text: We stayed at Helix in July to celebrate our anniversary. It was a clean and cute hotel with a modern feel. The modern feel felt a little bit fake and overdone in the halls but the room was nice, big and clean. We requested a pet-free room and found no trace of any pet, which I was happy about. We enjoyed the complimentary beer and wine in the lobby at happy hour everyday. The staff surprised us with a bottle of champagne and a note in our room on the night of our anniversary. We thought that was a nice surprise. There is a cute outdoor patio area good for having drinks. The breakfast buffet was sparse and there were flies on the food. We ended up grabbing coffee there and getting food elsewhere. The hotel is a good 15-20 minute walk to attractions, which isn't bad, but when you are walking the entire day, it gets a little tiresome.

title: “No fancy frills but nice hotel and good restaurant”
text: The room was was and while could use an update it was clean and roomy for a NYC hotel. I've been in much smaller rooms that cost a lot more and we had room to move around. The staff was extremely friendly helping us navigate the subway and buses. I had breakfast in the restaurant and while prices were high (as all hotel restaurants prices are high) the food and service was great.

title: “Great location and Service in Chicago”
text: Great hotel with great service, food and views of Chicago. The front Office Manager James Bristow was great and called me when a room opened up! The entire front office staff was great including Jonathan Burba, Victoria and many others were helpful. Service express was friendly, Annie Holmes and many others were kind and helpful throughout my short stay. I highly recommend this location.

title: “Fabulous hotel at an affordable rate!”
text:
I stayed at the Best Western Hotel-Dallas while traveling for business and I must say that this is by far the best hotel I have stayed at in a long times that even gives the Hilton & Holiday Inn hotels a run for their money.
Their beds were so comfortable that I have slept better in this hotel than any other, & I travel quite a bit throughout the year. After talking a very friendly front desk clerk, they informed me of the new carpet & bedding that had been added as well as a refrigerator & micorwave in all rooms for the guests convenience. The complimentary wireless & high speed internet were very convienient as well. I also helped myself to a complimentary breakfast buffet the next morning which was delicious! There was fresh fruit, muffins, french toast, eggs & cereal just to name a few of the tasty items. I will definitely be returning to this hotel every time I travel to the Dallas area.

title: “My all time favorite”
text: This is an exceptional place especially for the price. The staff make you feel like you are royalty. Anything you need, they will help. They are always friendly....you will never get attitude. They made me feel comfortable. The rooms are impeccable and have a nice feel. No dirty or stained carpets !Nothing like sitting out on the balcony and watching the ocean. Awesome view! The location is perfect. You can park your car and walk to restuarants, bars and shopping. Once I was surprised with an upgrade to a beautiful suit. This place understands good business and how to keep customers coming back. I have told other hotels that they should take some lessons from Pacific Terrace, see how a good hotel is run and go back and train their staff. I can't wait until my next visit. Look forward to sitting out by the pool and trying out the hot tub!

title: “Not as nice as it used to be”
text: We have stayed at this hotel four times in the past four years. It has become run down. We had a small room facing the street (even numbered) with lots of street noise. The hallway carpets were filthy. They were never vacuumed all weekend. We were charged 30$ per nite for an extremely uncomfortable cot for our 11 year old. It barely fit in the room. The bathroom was tiny and the towels were like motel6. The only good things I can say were that the parking was free-although hard to navigate with a minivan-and the location was great as we were visiting penn. next time we will switch to the inn at penn or the new home wood suites.

title: “Clean hotel, Great staff!!!!!”
text: Really great hotel stayed for four nights in September 2011 with my boyfriend (aged 22-23). Rooms are very clean and unique. The hotel is a lively hotel and has a very clean pool area. The pool area hosts a lot of pool parties, 3 during my stay. Which play loud music and a lot of people attend that are not staying in the hotel so you get to meet and talk to a lot of local people. The parties do start mid day and last almost all day with crowds of people staying all night in the hotel lounge and hotel bar drinking and dancing. The noise could be heard through out the night lasting until the early hours even though are room was on the top floor. The staff at the hotel were so helpful and kind giving advice about car rental and day trips, the staff couldn't do enough for you they printed maps and directions for us. The location of the hotel is about a 20 minute journey on the bus, and the bus is very cheap. Over all stay was great and I would stay here again, however I do think the hotel is more suited to younger people as it is lively and noise levels can be high. The hotel also offers a free ride from LAX airport which is great just give them a ring when you get to the airport, The driver gives you free bottled water and snacks.

title: “Good location and service”
text:
Stayed for 5 nights while attending a conference. The hotel is well located for the Magnificent Mile, just around the corner from the Millenium Knickerbocker, Westin and Drake hotels.
The hotel is clean, the lobby is spacious with free WiFi. The pool is up on the higher floors with a view of the Lake.
The room was good, though not amazing. The bedding and linen, though, was fantastic. The suites are spacious, and you can split the room into two, and use the sofa bed as an alternative bed i sharing with non-spouse (we were in a two doubles room). The bathroom is reasonable, with a good amount of towels. There is a small sink and coffee machine in the lounge area, which is helpful. WiFi and wired internet in the rooms costs money.
Staff were excellent, and very helpful.
Note that the Magnificent Mile is good for some things, but it's not quite the busy night bustle of downtown, so you might find that you trek down there every day. Food specifically was a concern, with mainly high-end restaurants near the hotel. It was a good walk to the nearest cheap food joint.
Overall, happy with the stay.

title: “Family visit”
text: The only problem we encountered was that the TV from the next room was on all night and we could hear it since it was loud; not a quiet night, otherwise all was good. We enjoyed the room, staff and the fact that they were very pleasant although my flight had been delayed and i checked in very late. Good area and would stay there again. Thank you.

title: “Great Hotel!”
text: My wife and I stopped in Boston for one night on the way to a week's vacation in Maine. We stayed at the Lenox on a Friday night and could not have been more pleased. The staff was very helpful. The accomodations were great and the location was the best. Great proximity to the T, to Fenway, and to all of the shops and restaurants on Newbury. This was our first time to Boston. Boston is a great city and the Lenox is a great place to stay to experience it. We will definitely be back to Boston, and will definitely stay at the Lenox.

title: “Don't worry -- there are no room inspections”
text:
I recently spent three nights in the Constitution Inn and found it to be excellent value. There is free use of extensive fitness facilities in the building, there is use of the Massachusetts General Hospital canteen facilities next door and also use of their free bus shuttle to the nearest rail/underground station. The YMCA is in the heart of the former naval dockyard with restaurants, a 24h shop the US Constitution and a regular ferry shuttle service to the city. Bunkers Hill is a stone throw away and the staff of the YMCA are extremely friendly and helpful. I can 
recommend a stay there.

title: “Rooms too small!!”
text: I loved the location. Even though you check in yourself there was somebody to help if you needed it and it was fast. The rooms however are too small and my sheets had stains on them. The bed was def not comfortable. The bathroom needs too be a little more private you can here everything. Overall probably wouldn't stay here again.

title: “A very nice hotel, despite being stuck in Denver”
text: Flight was cancelled multiple times so I stayed this hotel as a distressed passenger. Hotel was very clean, and the staff was very nice and welcoming. Included breakfast was also very good. Pillows and bed mattresses were a little soft for my liking, but otherwise the rooms were clean, spacious, and modern. Fitness machines were adequate, but there were no weights/resistance machines.

title: “Ok hotel but overpriced”
text: Stayed at the Hilton for 5 nights between Xmas and New Year. Arrived early at check in 2.30pm, after a 7 hour flight (and a 5 hour time difference) and were told our room wouldn't be ready until 3.30pm by a very rude employee. We waited in the very impressive lobby until our room was ready and heard numerous people complaining about things in the hotel to staff. When our room was ready we were pleased to find that we had one of the renovated rooms (which we did book) on the 16th floor, the room itself was spacious and clean, bathroom was great with a fantastic shower. Room was cleaned daily and beds made up. Breakfast was not provided so we went to the New York Marketplace within the hotel one morning, which is buffet style I would stay away from it, there are much better places to eat outside the hotel we paid over $60 dollars for the two of us for a couple of pancakes and a cooked breakfast. We ordered room service the first night of our arrival which was way overpriced also. The location of the Hilton is great with Times Square, Fifth Avenue, Central Park only five minutes away. Overall the hotel was clean and comfortable and probably would stay there again.

title: “Great location”
text: Nice to be close to everything without being in the middle of all the tourists and commerce. Lovely boutique hotel with all that one would want or need. Very European. My room is/was small, but I did not come to NYC to stay in the room. Some people just like to complain if spaces are too small. Be grateful for what you have......

title: “Ottima scelta per Denver vicino all'Aeroporto Internazionale”
text:
Magnificent Hotels near Denver International Airport, the rooms are great suites with kitchen and living room, the bedroom is the bed comfortable and quite large, even if only king, the bathroom very wide and with a large shower with double size .
The well-equipped gym and swimming pool with jacuzzi convenient, complete the excellent hotel facilities.
Convenience key to shuttle to and from the airport free of charge and can be recovered once delivered to the rental car at the airport.
A wonderful choice with very good prices if booked in advance.

title: “A good, comfortable place to stay”
text:
This Residence Inn is better than the average Residence Inn, which is usually very, very good. The comfort of a suite (we had a one bedroom suite) gives you room to move around if you're staying for more than a day or two. They have recently remodeled, which even improves the comfort level. They offer an excellent complementary breakfast buffet to select from, and even offer some evening mini-meals. In addition, the staff is very helpful and cooperative.
The property layout has some unique characteristics which, while not overly negative, take some getting used to. The parking lot access from the hotel varies, depending on where you have parked. Sometimes you exit from the 2nd floor and sometimes midway between the first and second floor. Access to the lobby and breakfast area is not an indoor walk through the hotel- you exit to the outdoor pool area (which is surrounded by the hotel rooms) via the first floor interior doors, and then walk back into the hotel at the breakfast area. So, when you leave your room, you have to consider where you need to go in order to decide which floor to go to. But this is only a minor quibble- the hotel is definitely worth a stay.
Another point worth making- this hotel, on Hotel Circle, requires a car. You are not too far from anything if you're driving, but you would be lost without having a car available. There is a daily parking fee, but it's a lot less than if you were staying downtown in the Gaslamp Quarter. The daily room cost is also a lot less than downtown, plus you have that very excellent complementary breakfast.
Overall, definitely worth booking a room here, wherever you intend to go in San Diego.

title: “Snobby, noisy, and rude”
text:
Normally I love Starwood Hotels, and the W is beautifully designed, there's no two ways around it. However, the service at the W Hollywood is among the worst I have ever experienced. Our bed was layered with: flat sheet - dirty duvet with no cover - and another flat sheet on top of that. Nothing else. We called down to see if it could be remade properly, someone came up and dropped a stack of flat sheets at our door and scurried away. Not that we were able to sleep anyway...
The noise of the club downstairs echo'ed into our room (bass drum sounds all night) well past 2am on weeknights, and we woke up at 7am to incessant hammering. When we finally called the front desk at 7:30am to complain about the noise, the front desk person audibly snickered. She actually laughed out loud at my complaint. When I asked her why she thought it was funny, she said "oh, ummm sorry, it's not funny, we can hear it too and it's really loud" -- OK, then thanks for doing something about the racket. Isn't it your job to attend to these things before people complain? Or to offer any kind of solution? She then put me on hold for 10 minutes listening to music that ensured I wouldn't be able to fall asleep even if the hammering stopped. And then, of course, the hammering never stopped, and the front desk person was unapologetic, and didn't offer earplugs OR COMPASSION. This is the kind of place where earplugs should be dropped in your hand along with the room key when you check in. We slept less than 3 hours that night due to all the noise at night and in the morning. Rude and absurd, uncourteous and unclassy.
We ordered breakfast in the room and my $20 waffle had three pathetic strawberries on it and tasted & looked like a stale Eggo. We got a slab of bacon heaped on top of my husband's meal -- Thanks, DUMMIES, we're vegetarians! Final total for inedible crap: $53.
Our wake up calls never came through. Our toiletries were never replenished. Our final bill was incorrect. A friend who came to pick us up was told that he wasn't allowed to pull into the stadium-sized driveway to wait TWO MINUTES for us to descend in the elevator, told that he would have to circle the block and call us to have us meet him on the street. We didn't feel we were treated kindly or with respect as guests at any point.
This hotel is loud and obnoxious and snobby, and is perfect for guests who are loud and obnoxious and snobby.
- - - - -
Weird sidenote: don't share a room unless you're totally comfortable seeing your roommate naked. There's a full length frosted window from the shower into the suite, thus defeating any sort of potential for privacy.

title: “Good Location & Value”
text: The hotel is in a great location! My wife and I stayed there for 2 days in the beginning of September and were happy with the proximity to the shopping and sites. The rooms were very clean and comfortable. The breakfast was very good and had a lot of variety. The gym is very small but fits the needs for a short stay. The hotel staff was really helpful and friendly. The elevators are small and there can be a decent wait time during breakfast.

title: “Would not stay here again”
text:
I booked 3 suites here for my family and our friends, a month in advance, but our rooms were no where close to each other. We each had a 2 bedroom suite. All of the suites were clean, and that is the best thing I can say about our stay.
Unfortunately there are many negative things about the property.
1. There is no privacy in the bedroom. They have vertical blinds with no curtains. You can see right into the bedrooms from outside.
2. There are not enough towels. Each of us booked a suite that accomodates 6 but were only given 4 towels. When we called to request more, we were told they were completely out.
3. The supplies in the bathroom are inadequate. There was no extra roll of toilet paper in the bathroom and no box of tissue. No hair dryer in the master bath.
4. The shower in the master bath is TINY. You WILL hit your elbows, while washing your hair. 
5. The "fully equipped kitchen", was not so equipped. There was a small coffee maker and no mugs. Sparse silverware, a spatula and a spoon. A 4-inch skillet and a small sauce pan. A cheap hand turned can opener - that was broken. 4 plates, 4 bowls. There is a refrigerator, oven, microwave, dishwasher and disposal. No dishwashing liquid or dishwasher detergent. No hot pad.
6. The breakfast room has only 4 tables, with 4 chairs each and 2 counters with 5 chairs each. There was not enough room to eat and the food was not good. Basic at best.
7. The complex is very run down. The lawn was overgrown and full of weeds. 
8. The thermostats in the rooms do not work. We had it set at 80 and were freezing. The a/c units in the room make a loud rattling sound.
9. There were no blankets on the beds. We made requests for 3 blankets which were never delivered. We finally vistited the front desk and received the last 2 blankets they had.
There is a large sign in the lobby stating this is the newest Hawthorn Suites. It is a very poor representation of the Hawthorn name. It appears that an old apartment complex was purchased and is in the middle of conversion into a hotel, but they have a LONG way to go.

title: “good”
text: This hotel was nice. The front staffs are very kind and room was comfortable. Also the breakfast was enough rich for our stay.

title: “Beware the room size”
text:
The Hudson is a stylish hotel situated very close to Central Park on 58th St. Extremely handy for Columbus Circle subway it is very easy to travel to most parts of the city from there. 
The hotel does not announce itself. The building's exteroir is very bland and does not even have it's name on the front. All the public areas in the Hudson are beautifully furnished and decorated. Having said that, I might be wrong as the reception areas were hardly lit in a 'trendy' way.
Our stay was spoiled by the size of the room. It was minute with a postage stamped size bathroom to match. Barely big enough for one person let alone two, There was very little hanging space and no shelves or drawers. As a consequence, for our 3 night stay we had to leave our clothes in suitcases on the floor which restricted space even more. The air conditioning was the noisiest I have ever heard, and although we were on the 11th floor the noise from the street was constant. 
On the plus side the room's decor (similar to the public areas) was very nicely done in dark wood. 
When we tried to change our room all we were offered was a very expensive upgrade. 
If you do go to this hotel, ensure that you get a larger room.

title: “smell like a cigar”
text: This hotel smell like a cigar in reception, in livingrooms, and of corse in the rooms. I dont recommend it.

title: “Don't bother staying here at all”
text: I made reservations a month in advance for the 4th of July Fireworks Package. This includes free parking pass, round trip on the water taxi for 2, 2 drinks at the bar, continental breakfast for 2 (eggs, bacon etc.) I called the day before to confirm the reservations and that it was indeed still the Fireworks Package. Reservations agreed saying it had not changed at all. The next day we checked in. I wasn't handed anything different other than the room key. I asked why and was told I did not have the Fireworks Package. I was confused immediately. Everything went wrong from there. The front desk girl Tabatha..I think said regardless, they ran out of the water taxi coupons 4 days ago, however she would give me the coupons for the breakfast. I found out why the next morning. Apparently, continental breakfast to Wyndham meant fruit, coffee, and bagels. Me and my husband just opted out of that one, only getting coffee, although we were offered grits and oatmeal too. The morning of check out, my husband took a shower and complained about the water pressure saying he could get a better shower from a water hose. The pictures on their website are completely different than what we saw. We might as well have stayed in a cheap seedy hotel because I felt like there was no difference. The hotel needs to try a little harder. The staff was helpful but the upper management was not.

title: “Class act in the Financial Center”
text: I found this hotel via Hotwire.com. It was discounted as a 4-Star and if anything, it was a five star. It was impossible to find any dirt...ANYWHERE and I looked. The rooms were perfect, the staff helpful and to be so close to the financial center, B O A Building, Transamerica Building and so many great restaurants not to mention the nearby cable cars...well, try it. Remember, San Franciscans try to ignore the fare collector on the cable cars-locals believe tourists should pay. Sometimes they get away with it but it is fun to watch them hide from the cable car operator.

title: “Great location.”
text: Stayed here in December for 4 nights with friends. Could not fault this hotel. Great location and attached to the Prudential Center. We had the buffet breakfast which was lovely. Not a lot of seats/tables in the breakfast room but we always managed to get a table. Staff very friendly and would definitley stay here again.

title: “Good rooms, very poor customer service”
text:
Stayed for 5 nights. Made the reservation through the hotel's website (not expedia, hotels.com or orbitz). They have a very good and modern website that lets you choose different amenities for your stay. Unfortunately, the staff at the hotel doesn't even know that those options in the website exist, so don't expect to find what you asked for when you arrive. 
We called the front desk to ask for what we requested (and was willing to pay for) at reservation but not only they had no idea about it, but they were rude and then didn't return the calls. They didn't even try to solve the issue but kept pretending that I was making things up. Then, on top of that, one of the nights we returned to the hotel at 11pm and found that they forgot to clean up the room. I went to complain to the front desk and the manager on duty only reduced my rate by a total of $20 out of $1,500. Ridiculous, but didn't have more energy to discuss. I was on vacations...
The rooms are big and nicely decorated. Very good king mattress. TIP: If it is cold, ask for an additional blanket as soon as you get in because they run out of them quickly.
The best thing in this hotel is their executive office manager Marybel. She was the only one that stepped up and personally solved the main issue that we faced with our reservation and showed real interest in making our stay better. Unfortunately, the people at the front desk and at the phone don't even care. I feel sorry for Marybel as she was really great, but this review is about the general experience with the hotel.
Net, I spent $1,500 and even though the rooms are nice and big, the poor service ended up making my stay unpleasant. Will not stay there again. I will choose a Marriott, Hyatt or one of the other major brands with more professional staff.

title: “Excellent Location!”
text: The location is fantastic for seeing the city. It is in walking distance from just about every part of town. The staff is friendly and accommodating. I would highly recommend this hotel.

title: “Great location!!”
text: I booked this hotel after much research for a birthday weekend trip with my sister. It lived up to expectations. The location was great - within walking distance of all Broadway theatres, Times Square and subway. Check in was quick and easy. The art deco decor was lovely. Our room was great size for price and location. It was one of few places with two beds for reasonable price I could find. We loved the mini kitchen in our room. It allowed us to have breakfast in room every morning and save money. The main elevators are small and slow, so we generally used the service elevator at end of hall. Only complaint was our room had connecting door to next room which allowed noise to draft easily to our room in morning.

title: “Better than expected”
text:
My sister and I stayed at this hotel the 2nd to the 6th November 06 and although we read some 'iffy' things about it found it to be very clean and comfortable. We were not sure if breakfast was included in the price, it was not, but you could buy a buffet breakfast for $15 approx, we went out and ate in local cafes and restaurants for a lot less than that.
The staff were friendly and approachable, although the only time we asked for directions they were not very good at telling us where to go.
The room although not really large was adequate for the two of us for 4 nights, and we had the room made up and clean towels every day. Initially the towels were not very big but on our last night we had large, fluffy towels left. 
The hotel is the wrong end of Michigan Avenue and is a fair walk from the shops and restaurants, but there are lots of buses and taxis, but if you are able it is well worth the walk.
I would stay at the Best Western Grant Park again and would recommend it, but take comfortable walking shoes!!

title: “Am I easy to please?”
text: It's true that the rooms are very small. Ours had just enough room to slide between the end of the queen bed and the small TV and clothing drawers /built-in cabinet. Also the closet was tiny. However on the plus side are friendly, helpful staff, a cappucino machine in a lounge off the lobby that works 24/7 and the complimentary computer/internet (w/ 2 computers available). Also the maid service was prompt and efficient and the room (on the fifth floor with a view onto a drab brick wall) was quiet. There was only a shower, but it was good sized. (One of the shower walls was a full length mirror -- a definite work-out/diet incentive!) We got a decent rate on Hotwire. Considering that almost any three star hotel is $200 or over, the comparative value was okay. If I were to obtain a comparable rate next time I'm in New York City, I'd stay there again.

title: “Very pleasant”
text: We moved from a different hotel and were very pleasantly surprised at how well we were treated at this hotel. The staff was accommodating and the room was very nice at a very reasonable price. The restaurant that was attached to it had a great breakfast and very nice people working there. All in all my wife and I were very please. We certainly would stay there again.

title: “nice location for air traveler”
text: We stayed in the Bay Club Hotel on the recommendation of a friend who lives in San Diego. We only had an overnight between flights. There are hotels closer to the airport but we got a great rate (less than $100) with free shuttle to and from hotel. Our room was clean and comfortable. We had a nice, reasonably priced dinner in the hotel restaurant. The front desk, shuttle and restaurant staff were friendly and helpful. We had to leave too early in the morning to take advantage of the complimentary breakfast. The hotel is located right at a marina.

title: “Great 10th Anniversary”
text:
My husband and I planned a trip to New York for our 10th Anniversary.
We booked the hotel on priceline.com and got it for $175 a night.
As many reviewers have stated it is not a new hotel but is a typical New York hotel. The room was not large but then again we did not spend much time in the room. 
I can be a bit anxious about staying in hotels and I can say that this room was very clean. The room was cleaned each day and I was very grateful. We did not have any trouble with elevators.
The location is wondeful, so close to Times Square and also Rockefeller Centre. The Cosi's accross the street is great for a bagel and coffee each morning. The Grey lines tour was a great way to get your bearing and then go back to the sites that you wish to visit.

title: “Excellent for families with a couple of caveats”
text:
Our room was very comfortable - larger than we expected, with cushions on the couch that could be moved to the floor for sitting and playing. Comfortable sleeping - except for pillows, which were very soft. We asked for hard pillows, and there were none, so we actually bought a couple of cheap hard foam pillows at the nearby bed, bath, and beyond and were reinbursed by the hotel! The pool is very small and was closed for part of our stay for a clean-up of some unspecified disaster. My biggest A++ was that the room was quiet. If that's an issue for you, request a room facing the back. The morning scene is convivial, with lots of travelers loading up on breakfast foods. Absolutely fine for kids - waffles, sausage, breakfast cereals, fresh fruit, donuts, etc. The staff is trying very hard to be friendly and helpful. We walked everywhere - to the Capitol, museums, etc. I wouldn't feel 100% comfortable walking past the little park across the street from the hotel at night, or by the corner two blocks away, of 6th and H, so you might just want to keep a head's up on that. You can walk downtown on 7th or 9th.
Valet parking is expensive, worth it for one night, but if you plan not to use your car, as we did, there's a parking lot one block further up on 6th ST. that charges $20 a night. For your last night, you might want to use the valet, as you have to be out of the $20. lot by 7 AM, and you can stay at the hotel lot til 3, with your bags stowed.

title: “Okay, not great”
text: Booked this hotel on Priceline, which guarantees two people in a room but not bed types. Since it was my brother and I, I called over a week in advance to request two beds in the room. The person told me such rooms were all booked but she would make a note to have a rollaway in the room. However, when we arrived, no rollaways were available, and we did not receive one until the next night. I understand I used Priceline so the hotel probably is not giving us its best service, but why tell me a week beforehand we could have one if they couldn't provide it? Also, the hotel is trying to be chic, with a sliding semi-transparent door to the bathroom, but it didn't even close all the way and you could see (and hear) into the bathroom from a certain angle. On top of that, the shower door is clear. Not the best for privacy. Finally, rooms are not very soundproof and we could hear all of the action in the hallways, doors slamming, etc.

title: “Great location, but overpriced”
text:
The Stockyard Hotel is in a great location in the middle of all the action. It is a neat old property with lots of character, but not really worth the price in my opinion. The restaurant is also overpriced for mediocre food in my opinion.
We stayed in the "back forty" room and one of the ceiling tiles fell during our stay. The hotel did discount the room $50 for the inconvenience. 
All of the staff was very helpful and friendly. Parking is valet only. I probably would not stay here again, but overall we had a good time.

title: “my stay at days inn”
text:
I thought the accomodations of the room itself was very nice. I liked the fact that it had coffee, a fridge, microwave and continental breakfast. However, I felt it was Overpriced for the area and because it was only a Motel (rather than a Hotel.) I did not like the fact that I had to Pay for Parking also. Although the Rooms were cosemetically nice, the Motel's Corridors needed a Facelift. I felt they were in Need of New Paint and Carpeting. It had a very "Dingy" Look and deterred tremendously from other Motels I have stayed at. That had a lot to do with me only rating it "Average" 
Thank You for your concern about my Opinion and I hope this will be useful to you in improving the qualify of this Motel.

title: “A pleasant surprise!”
text:
Stayed at the Salisbury this past weekend for one night. Booked by calling the hotel directly, last minute, and on a long weekend. After calling many hotels and endless online attempts, Salisbury offered the best rated. Found staff to be professional and very helpful.
Arrived at the hotel before 10 am and was able to check in right away. Had a room on the 18th floor with a small kitchenette, fridge, microwave, and coffee maker. The room and the bathroom spotless and very spacious. Had a flat screen TV although experienced some problems with the remote (didn't report it). As a previous reviewer mentioned, request a room at the back of the hotel, you'll sleep so soundly that you'll forget that you're in NYC!
Didn't try the breakfast as there're several nice diners in the immediate vicinity and a ton of cafes. Tip: try Angelo's restaurant two doors down. They serve the BEST pizza I've ever tasted! And I've sampled pizza everywhere including Italy. Check out the ricotta/garlic topings, you won't be disappointed!
Loved the Salisbury and would go back in a heartbeat!

title: “Absoutly fantastic!”
text: I loved this hotel! The room was huge! We got a superior queen with two beds. We had two bathrooms which was extremely helpful since we also had out two kids. The pool on the roof was great! The bar has happy hour 5-7. The margarita's wernt that good, buy for $3 you can't complain. I will be staying in this hotel again.

title: “Great Place To Stay”
text: Made the trip to San Diego to see my son graduate from Marine Basic Training. The hotel was only a mile from the Depot and the room was very clean. Traffic is not an issue and it was only a 10 minute drive to downtown and the marina area. Shopping is very close as well. Great value for the price. Don't look past this place when planning your visit.

title: “Lovely hotel. Great location. AND they made my wedding magical!”
text:
If you are looking for a wonderful, romantic place for a wedding/wedding reception (or frankly ANY kind of reception), this is THE PLACE!!! It is two blocks from the Capitol (yes, the "Capitol Capitol"), an easy walk from the Union Station Metro, and Tracy and her staff of chefs and coordinators are simply sent from heaven. She made our reception classy, with great food (when was the last time you heard guests rave about hotel food?), and this allowed us to actually ENJOY our guests and our time at the reception. 
I read all the magazines (yes - EVERY magazine), and checked out the websites for at least 6 months, and determined that I wanted something more original than the standard cookie-cutter, interchangeable chain hotel. I also needed a hotel to accomodate out-of-town guests for a reasonable group rate, and give them options for things to do (tours, restaurants, sightseeing within walking distance, etc) during the non-wedding down time.
I saw the Phoenix Park mentioned in a blog, and gave them a call. Tracy (aka "event planner extraordinaire") was never too busy to talk and answer questions. She provided a series of menu options and was happy to point out the pros and cons of the different options.
For a late-morning (11:30am) reception - I ended up with an hour long open bar cocktail reception upstairs in the Powerscourt Room with a gorgeously laid out fruit and cheese tables and waiter-passed hors-d's. People are still talking about the lamb chops and no they weren't extra! We had a choice of other tasty things like mini crab cakes and duck in phyllo pockets that we got to try during a lovely tasting that Tracy coordinated. The waitstaff were all extremely accomodating; our guests said that they only had to look like they needed something and someone was there to make sure they were okay.
And the food! Everytime I've gone to a wedding reception, the food has been cold/mediocre/forgettable. But this food was GOOD! I gave guests a choice of the salmon, a basic chicken, and a pork chop, and everyone kept commenting about how the food was tasty and served HOT. I can attest that the salmon was very good and perfectly prepared (not overcooked like many restaurants do).
Tracy was there on the day of the reception from sunup (to confirm a question about the seating) to late afternoon, when she had to prepare for another reception! Honestly, I don't know how she does it, but she was on top of everything, which gave me and my new hubby a chance to actually enjoy our party.
Other bonuses - the gorgeous honeymoon suite with a gorgeous view) is included as part of the reception price (the night of the event). You get the "pretty chairs" and china and votives as part of the package. The Dubliner Restaurant (a hangout for the local politicos) is open early for breakfast and late for bites and cocktails. The hotel is pretty and charming and CLEAN, and the staff is unbelievably nice and accomodating.
Seriously, whether you're traveling to DC and looking for the perfect location for sightseeing, or you're looking for the perfect place to hold a wonderful wedding reception - or any kind of reception, this is THE PLACE.

title: “Best hotel in the area”
text:
This is a large, elegant hotel with great ammenities. I particularly liked the down comforters and comfortable beds. The pool was great, as were the exercise facilities. 
The rooms were bright and cheery and had been recently renovated. They were always very clean, although one time I saw a cockroach in my bathroom -- I'll chalk that up to a freak occurance, since everything was very clean and well maintained.
I have stayed at a couple of other hotels in the area (Courtyard, Fourpoints), and this one is my preference by far. 
I found that the prices seemed to fluctuate quite a bit (forcing me to use other hotels in the weeks when it went up) -- not sure what that was about.

title: “Don't judge a book by its cover.”
text:
If the hotel was rated simply on its lobby, it would receive 6 out of 5 stars. However, there is more to a hotel than its lobby. The lobby is an art deco masterpiece. Soaring painted ceilings, stunning light fixtures, fantastic ambiance. I could spend all day soaking in the beauty and elegance of the lobby. Which is what I should have done. The rooms are old, yes. But that gives them their own charm. You can picture what it must have been like to stay in the hotel in the 1thes. That wasn't the problem with our room. Apparently, no one had stayed in our room in months because there was a visible layer of dust on everything. Even our bed linens and pillows had to be fluffed to remove the dust. That was disappointing and a little gross.
The service was not an issue because we didn't receive any. We checked in in the evening and then out again the next late morning so we didn't have any interraction with anyone aside from the front desk.
My suggestion, go for a drink or just sit and read a book in the lobby but find somewhere else to sleep for the night.

title: “HOME AWAY FROM HOME”
text: our children live a block away and since we are from out of town we sped 3-4 days each month at this hotel .THIS HOTEL IS LIKE A HOME AWAY FROM HOME FOR US the staff is friendly and cooperative.. and makes you feel welcome from the moment you arrive until you check out the staff is friendly and cooperative. making your reservations is a pleasurable process and they always try to give you the best possible rate ROOMS ARE BIG AND CLEAN AND THE BEDS ARE SO COMFORTABLE.anything you need the staff is there to assist you with in a quick and efficent way ..IT IS A PLEASURE STAYING HERE AND I RECOMMEND THIS HOTEL TO ANYONE LOOKING FOR A CLASSY BOUTIQUE HOTEL WELL PRICED IN NEW YORK CITY

title: “Concert stay”
text: Excellent location. Friendly staff. Breakfast was not up to par compared with other la quintals we have stayed. Room was spacious, a little outdated but clean...had a smell though. Always love that la quinta's are pet friendly.

title: “What a wonderful surpirse!!”
text: I almost didn't stay here because the reviews were not as good as I would like and I was worried about the freeway noise. I was staying on points so I needed to stay at a Hilton so I said, "Ok, so it won't be perfect." But what a surprise. The location of course is great. I asked for an inside room, I got a huge suite with a deck and full kitchen and balcony overlooking an inside courtyard. Must have just been remodeled. Granite counter tops, seven pillows on my bed, fireplace, flat screen TV in the living room, very modern. The weather was perfect in Seattle but the room so nice I just wanted to hang out in the room. I didn't - but almost wished for a rainy day. Plus, this was the only hotel in the world that I have stayed that the valet parking actually worked well.

title: “Stevevaca”
text: Excellent---gracious staff, attentive. Rooms fabulous. Would def go back!

title: “clean and ok for the price, but VERY NOISY!”
text:
We stayed here last night, actually, April 3, 2007, a Tuesday night. I had booked thru AAA and failed to specifically request a non-smoking room. That was my fault. The reservation was actually for a city view, but we got a harbor view instead (not complaining) and that kinda made up for being on the smoking floor. We were also just staying for one night before we went to the airport, so smelling the smoke from room next door was tolerable.
Pros - 
1. The harbor view really is very nice, and the Star of India (about three blocks away, I think) is not blocked at all by other buildings. We arrived just before sunset and it was beautiful setting over the harbor. 
2. It is less than a 5 minute drive to the airport.
3. It is walking distance to the harbor area and Little Italy. 
4. The parking was 7.00/night. From what I've read, this is fairly reasonable for downtown. And it's right next door.
5. I thought the breakfast at the Bayside Grill next door was just fine, with the vouchers. Coffee was only listed with our option of cereal/milk and toast, but when we asked for juice for our daughter, he brought us all a juice at no charge (in addition to our coffee.) Also - the coffee was very good, and my husband and I are really picky about our coffee. We always bring our won for the room coffeemaker. 
6. AAA rate for our room was 129/night. Not bad for a harbor view and breakfast.
HOWEVER - 
Cons-
1. NOISY!!! OMG, even with the windows closed, it was sooo noisy. My 9 yr. old, who normally doesn't even notice urban noise, complained about it. The trolley runs by CONSTANTLY. The Amtrak ran by twice within the first 2 hrs we were there in the evening. A plane flew overhead - really close. The pool was right below our room at ground level - and although we were on the 9th floor, we still heard kids in the pool at 8pm. In the morning, we heard the cruise ships blowing their horns. This was with the windows closed. 
2. The TV reception on the 9th floor was awful. ALL OF THE CHANNELS were fuzzy. Not one station was clear. Not one, out of thirty-something channels. 
3. Our room was cramped and small, and our bed was uncomfortable - sagged in the middle. 
 The first two, for me, far outweighed the pros, and I don't think I'd be happy staying at this place for a week, or even a few days. Maybe if I was really on a budget, but I would not want to be in the room for long, even if it was non-smoking. 
I would assume that a lot of hotels downtown and by the harbor would be noisy, but I haven't stayed at those, just this one, and, even with the view, I wasn't that impressed.

title: “Ok”
text: I don't know that I would stay here again. it was nice - but I've stayed at places I prefer. I planned a work meeting here. It was nice to receive complimentary wine. It wasn't nice to have to ask for receipts or for credit to my Starwood Preferred account. i think that Marriott Rewards offer more.

title: “It's the people”
text:
In my experience, this is the best of the LAX hotels. Everything works. The building, which looks non-descript from the outside, is elegant within, with a handsome marble and art-filled lobby, speedy elevators, and recently renovated (though relatively small) rooms. The lounge is an inviting place to eat and drink a glass of excellent wine; it's large enough to afford privacy, if that's what you wish, but also arranged to make it easy to watch sports on the big-screen TV. My AAA rate provided a club-level room, plus free valet parking, and was actually cheaper than the regular rate at some of the other airport hotels. The club level here is a real pleasure, with good complimentary food at breakfast and in the evening. 
What really makes this hotel special, however, is its people. Absolutely everyone -- at the door, the front desk, in the lounge, the club room, and at the concierge's desk -- was welcoming, helpful, and very competent. It's a real pleasure to deal with such positive people. I'd return for this reason above all.
This is not a luxury hotel, the art work notwithstanding, and the view from the rooms is primarily one of airport parking lots. So I would not recommend the hotel to someone principally interested in vacationing. But whenever I need to stay near the airport in LA, this is my choice.

title: “Very nice, good for an extended stay.”
text:
This hotel is nice, and our room was just as pictured online. Pool was small, but well kept. Breakfast was not great, but decent, which is typical of "free" breakfast hotels. 
We only stayed 3 nights, but it would be a great hotel for an extended stay as the rooms have great little kitchenettes, fully equipped with dishes, microwave, stove, and refrigerator.
The location of this hotel was decent for the price. We paid $85 a night and had to drive about 20 to get to downtown Austin. The cheapest hotel that wasn't a dump downtown was pretty much double that, so we thought the drive was fine. There are plenty of stores, and restaurants around the hotel, but mostly chain stuff, so if you want to experience local food and shopping you'll have to venture out. However, "Baby Acupulco's" is a great restaurant around the corner with live music a great food.
We would stay here again.....

title: “A unique and pleasant LA Hotel”
text: I had stayed in the Kyoto Grand Hotel one other time about 2-3 years ago (when it was called New Otani). The hotel has clearly improved. I didn't have any significant problems with it before, but it's clear that the rooms and the lobby have been renovated, and they have stayed faithful to the Japanese decor that makes the hotel and the area so unique. Don't be afraid to walk outside the hotel and around Little Tokyo. It's a nice little area with some good Japanese restaurants. In the room, the view was nice, and the Japanese sliding screens on the windows were a nice touch. Also, it's nice to have the mini-fridge. The bathroom was very clean, but still needs some updating. The tile around the bath tub is a gaudy pink color, and although I liked the handheld shower head, it wouldn't stay in the right position when I put it on the hook. The faucet at the sink was difficult to operate and get a good temperature. I will also insert my usual complaint about extra fees, including $24 for self-parking. However, overall, the hotel was a great place to stay, and another great deal ($80 winning bid on Priceline).

title: “Excellent”
text:
We so enjoyed our stay in the Palomar. The staff were helpful and friendly - esp. desk staff- went out of their way when my husband had to contact a Doctor. Always a smile when entering and leaving the hotel. Having travelled all over the world this hotel stands out from the rest. We appreciated the Free drinks on offer in the downstairs lounge at 5pm - 6pm after a tiring day out in the city. The piece -de -resistance ..THE Sable Restaurant where we had The Tapas dining experience ! ! Excellent ! ! Can't praise this enough. If all Kimpton Hotels are like this - would definitely book 
Elizabeth Eccleston.

title: “Great Service”
text: I had arrived at another hotel I'd originally booked online and was told I didn't have a room. I drove from that hotel to the Comfort Inn in Ft Worth and was met at the desk by the night attendant and manager. They were able to get me in a much larger room than I had originally booked for only $50 per night more. They bent over backwards to accommodate me, which made my trip a tremendous success.

title: “It was ok...”
text:
This hotel is very old and from my experience could use a little updating. My room was on the 24th floor and was actually not that bad we had a corner room with one king ad had a view of the museum and the Avenue of the Americas. 
But then i went to my familys room and they had a view of a brick wall and had random spaces in their walls but it is an old hotel.
If your looking to stay in this hotel it is great location but not luxury... Maybe try the premier rooms??

title: “Wonderful small hotel”
text: Our family enjoyed staying in this charming hotel for one evening on a quick trip to Seattle. It is in a great location, near fabulous stores and in walking distance of the Pike Place Market. My husband, having some work to finish, used the 'Business Center" in the hotel, which was very adequate and everything worked perfectly. The lobby is very inviting,with coffee in the morning, and just a great place to sit and relax or read. We would stay there again in a minute!

title: “A Denver best value”
text: The best lodging value near downtown Denver. Located in an industrial neighborhood 2.5 miles from downtown with frequent public transportation a few steps away. A little worn around the edges, but good sized rooms and comfortable mattresses. Complimentary coffee only. Rooms away from streets are quiet

title: “Would Stay Here Again”
text:
I recently stayed here with friends and we had a great experience. We redeemed a Groupon with no issue and had a wonderful time!
The hotel itself is very nice. We arrived around 10:30 on the day we were to check in, and although check-in is not until 3:00 they allowed us to park our car and check in. The room was nice and spacious enough (I saw that some people have indicated that the rooms are small; perhaps compared to other hotels, but I felt it offered more than enough room). It was nicely decorated, and had a modern feeling. There was free WiFi, and the staff were also kind and helpful. 
Dupont Circle is located only about two miles from the Mall and monuments, and so we were in walking distance to the sights, which was great! Of course there is also a Metro nearby. The bar downstairs seemed to be pretty popular the Saturday evening was there, but no noise reached our room, despite the fact that we were only a floor up. I would definitely recommend staying here, and would chose to stay here again!

title: “Nice room but not user friendly”
text:
The hotel is unusual and it seemed like converted office space with high ceilings and windows. Although we had a spacious, nicely decorated corner room the light was not good and the unusual layout left no space for the bedside table lamp to be of use. The bathroom fan was attached to the bathroom light and it was incredibly noisy to the point where it was preferable to try to use the bathroom in the dark. Although we were on the fifth (top) floor, we were woken in the early hours of a Friday morning by a street fight which made me think that the hotel location is 1-2 blocks out of the best area. (I noticed the Marriot was closer to the metro stop). The hotel receptionist spent at least an hour talking on the phone while we enjoyed the complimentary wine and cheese (which was a nice way to meet other guests)and she was not the slightest bit interested in the guests although she did manage to lodge a wake-up call while in the middle of her other business.
 On the plus side, it was easy to take the metro from the big 30th street station (just two stops) and then walk about five short blocks to the hotel. This metro stop is also only one block from the Reading Terminal Market where we enjoyed some great food. Most of the historic sites are within walking distance and we loved visiting the private homes of Dolly Madison and the Bishop which can be booked (no charge) at the visitor centre.

title: “Beautiful hotel, under renovation”
text: We stayed at the Palmer House Hilton in June for a girls' weekend. Our room was lovely and looked recently redecorated. It was also very large and we comfortably set up a cot with room to spare. However, some parts of the hotel were under renovation at the time and the second bathroom in our room was completely closed. The bathtub in our room plugged up and we had to wait over an hour for them to come fix it, and only after we made a second phone call. When the renovations are done I'm sure it will be a lovely hotel, but we were a little disappointed in the service we received. On the bright side it's in an excellent location, within walking distance to many Chicago attractions.

title: “Beautifully renovated, huge rooms!”
text:
I couldn't believe how nice this hotel was. Ok, the exterior looks like something out of the late 70's, but the inside has been beautifully renovated. 
Staff went above and beyond, going so far as to lend me their phone charger when I forgot mine. 
Being within walking distance to the Galleria is nice as well, though finding the path takes a little work. 
All in all, a solid choice!

title: “Nice but...”
text: Stayed here for almost 2 weeks on a business trip. I had stayed in this hotel in the past about 3 or 4 years ago but it was nicer then. Staff was okay but had a problem with a guy at the front desk but the name of Sam who for whatever reason, did not want to give me access to concierge although I am gold status with Marriott. I had to call Marriott and pass him my cell phone. Marriott Rewards straightened him out for me. The rooms were clean but the hotel is slightly run down now and so there were a few problems with the air conditioning/heating, and the overall fascia of the room but nothing major. One problem is, the door of my room was not flush against the jamb when it's closed so whenever someone in a nearby rooms closed their door, my door shook noisily. There was also some rooms being remodeled on my floor, adjacent to my room as well as above me so the noises from construction was a bit annoying and especially first thing in the morning. There was a huge convention in the hotel and several producers from major television networks were in the hotel during my stay. This became a bit annoying because upon arriving back at the hotel after work, security would not allow you access without showing identification and your room card. The concierge lounge was always extremely packed with producers from shows like Hell's Kitchen, and CSI and so going to have breakfast in sweats or workout attire was a little embarrassing because everyone else would be dressed in business suits, congregating for a meeting in the CONCIERGE LOUNGE which was a bit unfair to other patrons. Overall, and after the TV network people checked out, the stay was quite nice.

title: “Very nice hotel, but get a car!”
text:
I stayed at the Universal City Hilton from Oct 1- 5 for a conference and was pleased overall with the hotel itself. I didn't eat at the hotel but the food (especially the seafood buffet) looked absolutely delicious! We had some issues in our room with the phone and the air conditioning but other than that, our view was fantastic and the room VERY spacious. The staff was EXCELLENT. All were extremely helpful and friendly except one lady at the front desk who was not very interested in our complaints concerning the phone/air. Too bad I can't remember her name. Anyway, Billy the bartender was the absolute best! It still ticks me off when I stay in hotels of this caliber but still have to pay for wireless internet. It's either $9.95 per day in room, or $3.00 a minute in the business center.
The walk to the metro is close by although down a steep hill so if you have knee problems or are disabled, this will be a little difficult. We took a L.A. tour that picked us up and dropped us off at the hotel. That was convenient. Other than CitiWalk/Universal Studios, there isn't anything else within walking distance of the hotel, unfortunately. You would definitely need to rent a car or use the Metro because the cabs are really expensive due to the never ending L.A. traffic!
Overall, I thoroughly enjoyed my stay, however, the next time I am in L.A., I prefer to stay in a hotel that is downtown.

title: “Top hotel with top staff!”
text:
This really hurts me to say this because if i say what i am about to say then eveyone will book this hotel and i might not get a reservation when i want.Oh well ,here goes...The guys at marcel are the friendliest people i know in Manhatten,i know its their job but they genuinely are great and will help you out to such great lengths.The hotel was recently refurbished and now boasts an upmarket cool,chic look but not an upmarket price.It has a terrace on the 10 th floor with free coffee and internet access all day(great for printing boarding passes).
This will be the 4th time myself and my wife have stayed here and quite frankly we wouldn't go anywhere else.
 We were upgraded to a king suite from a queen because of the duration of our stay and they also let us keep the smae room when i had to arrange for another night but the king wasn't available but they said it was ok,so i paid for a std queen but got deluxe king.
 Special shout outs to Mark who without his credit card we wouldn't have got to Boston , top man! Also Michael,Zack and Lyndsey were superb as were everyone.
Now remember,shhhhh mums the word, we don't want everyone going there.

title: “A Change of Pace”
text: I recommend this hotel for those wanting to stay close to Wrigley Field. I was in Chicago for the Paul McCartney concert and wanted a hotel within walking distance to Wrigley. This hotel is a change of pace from Magnificent Mile properties. The Broadway area is very walkable, diverse, and eclectic. Plenty of shopping and dining. I liked Ann Sather for breakfast and Stella's Diner. This hotel is not your usual Best Western. It has a small courtyard, boutique feel, with continental breakfast, microwave, and refrigerator. The staff was very helpful. Downtown is only a cab away and the staff will find one. I will stay here again if I want to be near Wrigley. Plenty of Starbucks handy,too.

title: “Great place to stay”
text: Our stay at the hotel was GREAT! Friendly staff and quick check in. The room was beautiful and very comfortable. The elevator were a bit small but no big deal. Great location just around the corner from Good Morning America and Starbuck! I enjoyed my stayed and will return in November for some pre-christmas shopping. Cookie & Jorge

title: “Dollar store item pretending to be something it most definintely is not”
text: I had read several reviews regarding the rudeness of the hotel employees, but decided to chance it anyways. Everything began smoothly.... however through the course of my stay I discovered that the the towel hook in the bathroom was NOT actually attached to the wall, the bed was uneven and I kept falling into the center, and the amoire door was broken enough to where when I opened it, it fell off the hinges. When I complained to hotel staff, they promptly acccused me of breaking everything and alerted me that anything I complained of would be fixed- at my expense! Not only was I another victim of the hotel's rudeness, but I now also get to outfit the hotel with new fixtures and furniture. Yea me! My advice is to avoid this hotel- unless you enjoy being ripped off of course.

title: “Great two night stay”
text: My husband and I stayed at Vagabond Inn for two nights while visiting San Diego. We stayed in the jacuzzi suite. The room was very clean, the bed was comfortable, the TV was large, and I appreciated having a refrigerator and microwave for our food. Although I enjoyed the bedroom area, the highlight was the jacuzzi and the bathroom features. I appreciated all the amenities that were in the bathroom from the robes and slippers to the sit down vanity and jetted tub. There weren't any flaws that I could find in the room. We were able to grab some waffles and coffee in the front lobby for the complimentary breakfast. I only wish they had a larger space to set out tables and seating in the lobby to be able to eat breakfast instead of having to bring the food back to the room.

title: “Perfect choice.”
text: The Chandler was a dream. Though the lobby is under renovation, the staff was beyond accommodating and gracious, offering upgrades and friendly service. I was traveling with my elderly, disabled mother, whom they treated with care and respect. The rooms were immaculate, large (by NY standards), and extremely comfortable. The Hotel Chandler is a great place to stay.

title: “Loved it”
text: we stayed here for 2 nights & LOVED the entire experience! the hotel itself is extremely welcoming with it's vibrant colors & neat look. The staff was cool & laid back, made us feel right at home. The bar was fun & drinks were tasty! The location is totally convenient...I highly recommend that everyone stay on a high floor because the view is awesome!! I will definitely be returning to this hotel!!

title: “Construction is finished & hotel is great!”
text: We have stayed at the Denver Warwick several times before and have loved it. We read the prior reviews on the construction going on and hoped it was completed...and it was. There was over a $20 million dollar remodel and it shows. The pool was open and very clean. We had a quiet room with a balcony. The employees were all very friendly and the rooms very very clean. Checkout was quick on the TV.

title: “Good location”
text:
We stayed for 3 nights during the marathon weekend in Oct. My company had a good corporate rate so I was very happy with the price/location. The hotel was very close to all the shopping and there were tons of good restaurants only a few blocks away. It was about a mile from Grant Park and it was an easy metro ride from Midway airport (although the metro stop was about 5-6 blocks away). The breakfast hours were great (6-10am) and they were very good at refilling - even right up to 10am. There was a nice selection of waffles, cereal, bagels, muffins, patries, juice, yogart, etc. The room was very clean but there was only shampoo and soap so make sure you bring everything that you need. The sign in the room said $299 / night....which is way more than I would pay for any hotel. This was a nice hotel but definitely not $299 nice although the location was really good. However, there were tons of other hotels within a couple of blocks so I would recommend looking around for a good deal when planning your trip. 
I would definitely stay here again!
Suggestions......Timothy O'Tooles for a good sports bar, good lunch at PJ Clarkes (next to Embassy Suites).

title: “Excellent value and location”
text: Fantastic value hotel in good location. Booked through Opodo just 2 weeks in advance and travelled with Lastminute.com on Virgin from Heathrow 15 to 24 Jan 08. Virgin were good as usual. Hotel staff, Alex and Doris, very friendly and helpful.
