Booked 2 Junior Suites but was offered 2-bedroomed suite on arrival - we'd tried to book this in advance but wasn't available and when I contacted the hotel directly (always worth a try - have had some good deals this way) they wanted to charge us $200 extra per night on top of Opodo price, which we refused. So, very surprised to be offered this free of charge on checking in. Very spacious, clean and neat accomodation - completely the opposite to reviews we'd read! 2-bedroomed (plus lounge/sofabed) ideal for up to 6 or family, consisted of one room twin beds and the other a double so decided that as we were two couples this wasn't fair to one of us we reverted back to Junior Suites. They gave us two next door to each other - good value, clean and neat and very big with lounge area for entertaining and small kitchen with everything you'd need to cook a full meal! Only things missing from room were kettle and dressing gowns (but had coffee percolator, microwave, full cooker, fridge/freezer, toaster) - well equipped. Plenty of deli's/cafes for breakfast and bars. Best restaurant in area is Docks (good value), our favourite for many years. But plenty of others within very short walk (10 mins to around 30 restaurants). Lebanese nearby also good. Go to Central Cafe, E42nd opposite Grand Central for good breakfast. Try the 4 loops bus tour for $79 with Grayline or Citysights to use over 48 hours including Empire State or Top of Rock ticket and short Cruise - good value and good way to see NY for first of second visit. Try Gallaghers Steakhouse on W52nd for greats steaks and atmosphere (expensive), Mars 2112 on Broadway for fun lunch, Macy's Cellar Bar/Grill for burger lunch, Nuovo Latino at South Street Sea Port for Cuban style food at good price. Great shopping and bargains everywhere but do allow a full day for Macy's and Bloomingdales and get your 11% discount voucher from the visitor center. In smaller shops don't be afraid to ask for the best price they can do. Been 7 times in three years and looking forward to next visit already.....

title: “Great Hotel if you can stay in Santa Monica”
text:
Had the pleasure of staying at the Luxe recently. Staff was great and courteous. When checking in, there were suites available and they quickly upgraded me without a question. The suite was wonderful - big (probably 1,000 square feet) and the bathroom was outstanding - marble stone all the way through and separate shower and tub. Room was definitely A+.
Hotel itself is pretty hip and may not be so great for kids - but I did hear a family next store so I could be wrong. I didn't get to check out the pool and fitness but heard it was very nice. I ordered room service and it actually got delivered in 15 minutes rather than the 45 and normal hotels.
Would definitely recommend staying here if you are in Santa Monica. Only drawback - there isn't anything in walking distance from the hotel. You want something to eat or a cup of coffee and don't want to stay at the hotel - you'll need your car. Its a short drive either direction on Sunset to find something but you can't walk.

title: “Let's not get too carried away”
text:
Look,Tthe Blakely does have a great location and the rooms are spacious by New York standards but if you are expecting service here, you won't get it. I'm not talking forelock-tugging obsequiousness, just a smile and a willingness to accommodate. 
Having stayed at the Shelborne Murray Hill and the Waldorf on previous visits to NYC we were looking for something in between and The Blakely fits the bill. However, our stay was marred by a lack of friendliness in the staff. Most of them seemed very young and I suppose this is their "other" job. There is definitely a difference in hospitality staff who make it their career. The guys on the door are fine. The desk staff are the problem. Gee smile now and again okay. 
Our main complaint, however, was that we requested a late checkout (ie, an hour later than their late checkout of 3pm) as we were flying back to Australia and would have liked to freshen up beforehand. Also, such long flights require you to be at the airport 3 hours before takeoff and we didn't want to be there any longer than necessary. The hotel manual in the room reads as if this is not a problem. We were informed by a man at the desk (wearing a beige uniform) that it would probably not be possible but that if we paid half the daily room rate ($200 plus for an hour extra) it would be possible. Mmmm Nice. 
I wasn't seeking any compensation for the fact that the construction work next door going on during all hours of the night kept me awake or that the light in the bathroom was inadequate, or that the hairdryer in our room needed replacing. How far do you think I would have gotten it I did. It wasn't the fact that they couldn't accommodate us for the extra hour that left me with a bad taste, it was the fact that they could for a fee. A large one.
 Oh and when our final bill (including $60 a day in taxes) was given to us we were charged for 1 beer and a Jack Daniels from the mini-bar at $25.00. We didn't use the mini-bar once and when we said it wasn't ours we were met with very unbelieving looks. 
Having had almost universal praise on Tripadvisor (that's why I booked the Blakely) I feel like I am swimming against the tide here but if its room size and location you are after then the Blakely is still a great option. And maybe it is used mostly by business travellers who aren't interested in the hospitality end of the hotel stay but, if you are staying for pleasure then you might like a bit of friendliness too and and not a everything-for-a-price mentality.

title: “Great Location, good hotel”
text: We started our East Coast trip in Boston at The Lenox. I knew I wanted to stay in Back Bay and that was definitely key to the trip. You can walk everywhere, even to Fenway. The hotel was cute but old. They did have coffee available in the morning and lemonade and cookies in the afternoon which is a nice touch. I was a little disappointed when I got in the elevator and the woman told me she was paying $65 a night to stay there and I was paying $250 each for 3 rooms. She also was in an upgraded room for $65 and I had requested an upgraded room (with which I was going to have to pay) but didn't get it, so I am not sure about how that works. Otherwise it was a nice stay in a great location.

title: “Excellent location!”
text: We went to see an Orioles game and this is the place to stay! The bar was packed before the game, and the location gives you walking access to any place in the Inner Harbor. We have stayed here before and will again.

title: “help”
text: the general manager help me with the issue with hotwire!!!! thanks Ken Patel The hotel have a great rooms, good location, and exelent service . people like me we need wi-fi and this place have a good signal for work!!

title: “Oh Dear”
text:
Myself and two colleagues stayed in hotel rooms in the Flatotel on business last week and were disappointed to say the least.
On the plus side, it was very convenient for our office and the midtown area, I like hard beds so found then very comfortable, there was Molton Brown stuff in the bathroom and the wake up call system seemed to work ok.
On the minus side though, the rooms smelt funny and musty, and for a non-smoking room, smoky. The bathrooms had not been cleaned and the (unnecessary) jacuzzi was grimy. The room design was odd with the closet in a difficult position, and the connecting doors weren't sound-proofed. The Fitness Suite was really not up to scratch with possibly the most terrifying spiral staircase in NY leading from the 46th to the 47th floor, right by the full-height windows, and the fitness equipment was old and had no instructions. Staff were surly, phone calls were laughably over-priced and overall it seemed far too expensive for what it was, even on a corporate rate.
Overall I wouldn't stay here again unless the only other option was a hostel, and even then I would have to think very carefully.

title: “Great Hotel!!!!!!!!”
text: We stayed at the Woodfield Inn for 3 nights and we had a great time. The king suite was large and roomy, and most importantly clean. We arrived at 6:00PM and checked in immediately. Our room was on the first floor and it was quiet. The staff were professional and helpful. The breakfast were great, especially the waffles. An easy location to get in and out around San Antonio, ample parking and close to the Riverwalk, Alamo and Market Square. I had my car so we did not use the Trolley, and driving around San Antonio was very easy and parking was not a problem for me. I will stay in the future at the Woodfield Suite.

title: “Excellent hospitality and very helpful!”
text: Very comfortable and secure hotel in downtown Dallas. I would love to stay here if I travel back to Dallas for business again. Close to shopping (Nieman Marcus) and other areas as well as restaurants. Shuttle service provided by hotel was extremely helpful and courteous staff.

title: “Disgusting Hotel”
text:
This is one of the worst accomodation experiences in years, including countries like Senegal or Cambodia.
The place is absoultely ready for tear down and re-buid. Cracked paint everwhere, old furniture, dirty, bad-smelling "kitchenette", rotten smell everywhere. Let alone the carpet in the hallway - probably 30 years old. You don´t want to know, what creatures live there - probably at the brink of intelligent life.
DO NOT GO!
Good was the WiFi access and (my) bed. Other trevellers of the group however had different experiences with their beds. 
Aircondition, only in some rooms and inacceptably loud.
Windows are thin, in fact you are sleeping on the street in respect to the sound level.
Different members of our group were charged different rates (although all booked at the same time through the same online portal) - between 74 and 101 USD.

title: “great hotel, very convenient location”
text:
This was my second stay within the year, both for conferences. The hotel is conveniently located to the Navy Pier, Magnificent Mile and many great restaurants. It sits on the river and offers great views of the city. The beds are amazingly comfortable, the rooms are clean, the staff was always freindly and helpful and facilities are well maintained. The gym is small, but had a nice variety of equipment and was frequently used by many guests during my stay.
The conference facilities were very nice and seemed well organized. The front desk for check-in and check-out got quite crowded and they could have used another staff member or two to help. I was surprised to find that the Chicago Burger restaurant inside the hotel is considered seasonal and was closed. We did enjoy the Lizzie McNeill's pub next door (along the river) for quick bites and a more leisurely beer than sitting in the crowded hotel bar.
High praise to the concierge staff...they always had great recommendations and even provided written walking directions to many nearby places.

title: “Good location.....errrmmmm....pretty much it!”
text: The price you pay for the location of this hotel isn't too bad (about $150 per night, and there's a tram stop near the entrance), but the desk service was woeful, as different staff members gave contradictory information regarding car parking and travelling locations. There's a price to use Wi-Fi in your room and the business centre computers cost about .50 cents per minute. That's a great system........for 1998. The rest of the hotel was average otherwise. If you're desperate to get accommodation near the centre of Memphis city, you could consider this place, otherwise look elsewhere.

title: “This is an illegal hotel room in a residential building!!!”
text: This is a residential building. The "hotel rooms" are ILLEGAL. I felt like a squatter. No services. Just awful.

title: “Actually, we had a quite pleasant stay at the Carter!”
text: After having read all those cheerful reviews, I thought that the Carter would be Hell on Earth. Fortunately, it turned out not to be so bad after all! I organised a trip for 28 Dutch students, ages varied between 15 and 19, and 4 teachers for a week in May during our break. I already told the students not to have too high expectations of the accommodation, and that it was low budget! However, when we entered the building, things seemed okay, not the Ritz, the staff was nice (okay, maybe they wouldn't pass a general English test), ask for Elaine, the rooms were sufficient (obviously not decorated by that hunky Nate Berkus, often seen on Oprah, or any other modern hip designer), the beds were big (!), the sheets we had were clean, and when they forgot to remake the beds, they did it the day after, and so on. The same for the towels, when you didn't get fresh ones, you just asked for them and they would be given to you, no problems there! Some windows could be stuck! Also the elevators, I read here that some had to wait 15 minutes or langer: BS! The elevator worked just fine! Problems with an unlikely guest, just tell one of the clerks, probably the big black guy, or the PC term African-American, and he will throw him/her out on the spot (only happened once, the poor guy). Some of our students stayed on the 8th floor, and no, there were no ghosts (actually, we stayed at the 6th floor as well, room 624 pretty clean). Yes, you couldn't close the bathroom doors in most cases/rooms, but, hey, if you have a nice bottom, why don't share it (or use the curtain!)! The shower worked well, hot water on the spot! Flush the toilet twice though! And if you need privacy for nr. 2, just go down into the lobby, they had a 'private' toilet down there! The location is great, no worries there, we loved having breakfast at the Europa Cafe, quite tasty! Thus, my opinion is that you could do a whole lot worse! This isn't a 5 star hotel, it's low budget, so what do people expect. None of our students complained, and they are Dutch, so rather picky, like me, and so did none of the teachers! So, if you just want to have a big comfortable bed to sleep in, and a hot shower 24/7, this is a sufficient option! I'll book it again next year when I will return with school! Enjoy..... and who is going to stay in his/her room all day long, to e.g. watch telly (yes, just 2 channels, and they were bad!).....? C'mon people, this is New York, try the outdoors! Happy hi! (BTW, this doesn't mean that I cannot appreciate the Plaza or anything else for that matter!).

title: “really great accomodation!”
text:
Great position, close to Union square and public means of transport.
Room was pretty big and really clean.
The breakfast is free, but you can have it just between 7:00 9:30 and it's a bit poor I must admit
The only thing I would improve is the internet wi fi which was not for free.....
On top of all:Lovely staff, really kind, careful and smiling.

title: “Great location, great value for money”
text: The hotel is in a fabulous location - a very short walk to Union Square and right on the tram line to go to fishermans wharf. Chinatown, little Italy all only a short walk away. We didn't have any expectations so were quite impressed actually. There is a convenience shop across the road and a full mini bar and fridge and a coffee machine in every room. The rooms are a little quirky (odd!) but very comfortable and clean. The staff are very helpful. I would definitely recommend this hotel. It is great value for money.

title: “Great atrium/central meeting space, bedroom suite is 2 separate rooms”
text:
Earlier reviews mentioned cleanliness so I was leery! But overall the hotel was quite good and I will stay here again. 
* We appreciated the huge central atrium, with many tables and chairs around. As a working group, we were able to easily meet and work together for hours. 
* Manager's reception - there were chair massages on Tuesday, wow! After going to the bar for our first free glass of wine, a server came around pouring more through the evening. Nice touch!
* The bathroom was not the sanitary level of clean that is REQUIRED in a decent hotel. I did a quick clean with "wipes" and it wasn't too dirty, but not the sparkling clean it should have been. I think the management is paying attention, improvement still needed.
* Free breakfast - nice! Eggs, hash and sausages ready to go, or omlettes made to order. Good fresh fruit, decent (light) coffee, cereal, etc.
* Exercise room - good, 2-3 treadmills, elliptical, free weights, medicine balls.

title: “Don't waste your money- mediocre hotel here!”
text: The Curtis is overpriced and underwhelming. The front desk team knew nothing about Denver and had trouble recommending restaurants and things to do. The hotel hints at fun with its themed floors, but the themes are totally underdone. For a boutique hotel, this was surprisingly like a Holiday Inn experience---which would be fine if we had paid Holiday Inn prices.

title: “What I needed”
text: Overall, the room was perfect for my needs. The bed was amazing and the desk was there as well as wifi. If I were wanting to do more that just sleep in a bed, it would be a disappointment. The room is not very big, the TV was old, the bathroom was very small, there was no safe to put valuables in, the maid did not give me a new towel, it had a radiator heater that never shut off, and the a/c was pointing into the heavy drapes so the room never got cool enough. However, I just needed some place to sleep after my meeting and the room did provide a nice, very comfortable bed, so I left with a happy experience.

title: “Very disappointed”
text:
Myself and my husband from Ireland stayed in On the Ave. Hotel for 4 nights in May 2005 as a stop over on our way to Florida.
The hotel was very average but it was sufficient for our needs.
We check out on Saturday morning and arrived in Florida that afternoon.
When I began to unpack I discovered I had left several items of new clothing in a bag on top of the wardrobe.
We rang immediately and was told the staff were off but it would be checked out next day. All information of room number, exact clothing etc. were given. Got no phone call until we contacted them on Monday and were told they had got no message about this. Took all details again and said they would get back to us as soon as possible. Wednesday afternoon they rang to say no clothing were found. I was most disappointed at the 'could not care less attitude' and obviously no attempt was made to find these clothes as I could have got them collected.
Thank you
Kathleen Phelan, Co. Leitrim, Ireland

title: “Business Trip”
text:
Very nice Hotel with a great location. Located in the Financial District of SF but about a $7 cab ride to North Beach for the Italian section and also Chinatown. The Hotels rooms are on the small side but well appointed and the beds are very comfortable. I usually having troubble sleeping when away on business but not hear. Very quiet rooms with thick walls and have not heard any noise from next door. 
Now this is a business trip with about 400 ppl so the food has been mass produced but it has been pretty good as well.
 I would recommend staying hear no problem, comfortable and close to everything.

title: “If you have NO other options”
text: Very very disappointed. Staff didn't hesitate to continue their personal conversation while checking us in. Rooms were damp and musty smelling. When we had to check out a day early, clerk realized we had a pre-paid package. The "oh well, nothing I can do" attitude was the straw that did it for me. I wasn't asking for anything, but maybe a little recognition that I was checking out vs. him checking out the girls walking through the lobby. Terrible value for the price. You can pay the same amount, and be closer to activities.

title: “Excellent Hotel”
text: Our hotel stay after our cruise was just absolutely wonderful. Homewood Suites staff made us feel extremely welcome and referred us to a couple of places while waiting to check in. Will definitely stay here again when we are back in Seattle.

title: “Not impressed...won't be returning!”
text:
The only good thing about this hotel ws the friendly staff. The worst thing about the hotel were the bathroom doors. They had sliding doors which don't shut all the way so others in the room can easily see into the toilet/shower area of the bathroom. So if you like your privacy...stay away from this hotel.
The t.v in my room would turn on by itself at 6:30AM every morning...we mentioned this to the front desk and the "engineer" said he would take a look at it but it was never resolved. Woke us up every morning and no one could explain why.
My mom and sisters stayed at the suite and complained about the uncomfortable sofa bed because they could feel the springs. 
We stayed there for 5 nights and every single day we dreaded going back to our hotel. 
Like I said, the staff was nice but I would NEVER return to this hotel!

title: “Great Location”
text: Old Hotel but well kept and staff is friendly. Location to airport is great and good dining in area

title: “very nice boutique hotel in Rittenhouse Square”
text: The hotel lobby is very nice, with a great fireplace and comfy sofas. There is a dining-room- like set up where you can have complimentary wine from 5-6 and mingle. Our original room was on the dark side (interior) but we were able to upgrade to a higher floor with a city view for free! The staff is very professional and extremely friendly - and it didn't seem forced or phony. There was a security guard checking room keys on New Year's Eve, which made us feel very secure (I was there with my husband and 81 year old mother.) We had breakfast at Square 1628, which is attached to the hotel - again, very nice staff and a very good breakfast (not included with our room.) I would definitely stay at this hotel again.

title: “Beautiful View”
text: We love Hiltons. This one was as luxurious and quiet, despite the other reviews about the construction. We would have liked the pool to be open (huge disappointment) and it appears our room had not yet been renovated as the older style cabinet fridge was inaccessible. We got a good rate and stayed busy in the city so we were willing to overlook these details. The location is excellent, a block from the cable cars, a couple blocks from China town, just minutes from the Bart Station which we took from SFO. Why rent a car when it will be parked the whole time anyway? For a weekend packed with sightseeing, it was nice and convenient and luxurious (at least to our mid-class family). Would definitely stay here again, especially with the future improvements!

title: “Damp”
text: We have stayed at this hotel before in the summer and loved the location and layout. This time it was raining and damp and the hotel room had a distinct mildew smell and damp carpet. When another room was offered to us, it had the same problem. When we walked in to our original room, the bathroom window was open in an attempt to air out the room. We stayed one night and changed hotels for the rest of our stay. Very nice and helpful staff and a great location!

title: “We'll be back for sure!”
text:
A really good hotel for the low price we paid. The hotel has a great location near Central Park and one block away from the subway that take you downtown. You have Columbus Ave. just around the corner with Deli's, restaurants and shops. It's a nice and quiet neighbourhood. 
The room was cleaned every day with new towels. 
The breakfast was for free with coffee/tea/chocolate, juices, yoghurt, cereal, instand oatmeal, toast, bagels, waffles, pastry, boild eggs, peanutbutter and jelly/marmelade. Be sure to get up early so you get a table and don't have to wait for one. 
The only thing that we got a bit tierd of was that you share elevator with the staff so somtimes we had to wait for quite som time at the elevator, and since we stayed on the 9th floor it was to many stairs to walk. But that was a small thing.. 
We're absolutly going to stay here next time we come to New York!!

title: “Great for a family vacation!”
text:
Stayed at the Homewood Suites San Diego-Del Mar over Spring Break with my husband and two young daughters - 5 & 3. The one-bedroom suite was great for the four of us. The suite had a two queen beds in the bedroom which were very comfortable. The bedroom and the living area were separated by a door - great for putting the kids to bed early. The kitchen area was slightly cramped and the table only had two chairs - which was a little inconvenient for the four of us but we worked around it. There was a full refrigerator in the kitchen along with a stove and sink. There was also a full tub in the bathroom - great for the kids. The bathroom was separated with the shower & toilet closed off and the vanity open to the bedroom area. This was slightly inconvenient if you needed to use the vanity sink after the kids were already asleep.
The location of the hotel was good. It was north of the city and very convenient to I-5. Only about 20 minutes from the airport. It was slightly tucked away in a residential area but once we figured out how to get there, it worked out fine. And parking was free - bonus!
The free breakfast in the morning was wonderful. Lots of choices - waffles, eggs, bagels, cereal, fresh fruit, etc. We tried the free dinner one night and it was good as well - simple with a very specific meal served each night. Worked well for the kids after a long day out & about.
The pool was small but adequate - although unfortunately it wasn't warm enough to swim for very long while we were there. The hot tub was very nice.
Overall, I would highly recommend this hotel for families needing a home base for an active vacation who aren't planning on just hanging out at the hotel.

title: “Unforgetable”
text: We went for our honeymoon and felt like kings and queens. You must stay here atleast once and I'm sure you'll want to go back just like we do. I can't wait to stay here again. PS duck dive has the best ribeye sandwich I've ever had in my life!!! We had it 33 times.

title: “Tired, Dirty, & Poor”
text:
Generally speaking, Extended Stay America properties are usually pretty good for the money, unfortunately, their Castleton, IN property is quite a dissapointment. It's by no means terrible, but there were a few things that made me really annoyed during my brief, one-night, stay.
For one, the AC unit in the room leaked all over the carpet. it leaked so much that the carpet surrounding one side of the bed actually "squished" when you walked on it. Not pleasent. The furniture was old, worn out, and pretty disgusting. My travelling partner wouldn't even sit on the desk chair. The bathroom was the same way.
I stay in all types of motels/hotels when I travel, and it takes a lot for me to mention the cleanliness of a property. Read my other reviews if you don't believe me. But this place, really was quite tired, dirty, and poor.

title: “great staff”
text: finding this hotel was a bit of a challenge. we made several calls to the desk and the staff member actually came out and crossed the street waving his arms to help us find the place! it was a tight room - not a lot of space to walk around so we had to place our luggage strategically. very neat. nice staff. too bad there was no pool.

title: “Great Property”
text:
Beautiful property with helpful staff. Very good food in the outlets. Ric's is the free standing restaurant in front of the hotel and the food the is very good. 
Pool/lazy river can get crowded, but I guess that's to be expected at such a cool property. Close to great shopping in Scottsdale.

title: “Nice, but pricey”
text: Came to see two Yankee games at Camden Yards. Nice hotel with continental breakfast included that would be much nicer if they had more than three tables in which to sit and eat. Had to take food and drink back to room. A complimentary bottle of wine at check-in is a nice touch. Everything about the room is top notch. Very close to bars and restaurants of Fell's Point. Would stay again if I could get a better rate.

title: “Great Location; Small Average Room”
text: Gorgeous lobby and friendly staff. No complaints on service. Room very small. Got a good deal on the gov't rate but room was downsized (I hope!). Very small average "holiday inn traditional" decor. Nice bathroom marble counter(toiletries stink as well) but small shower and bathtub average. Expected much better for price. In no way in league with a loews or ritz hotel, but the location cannot be beat...near white house, mall area and museums!! There is a great small bakery across the street, a barnes and nobles and the landmark, "Old Ebbitt"--don't miss this one! Ask for the courtyard and enjoy! One small warning: DO NOT take anything out of bar to view or put in your drinks. it is sensored and will charge you for everything you lift up. We did not read the fine print and were charged for everything we removed to put our water in and then some. They removed it but it took some haggling. one surprise..their #20 Breakfast brunch at willard was very good with all fresh fruit, pasteries, eggs, bacon, etc!

title: “Recommended……we had a great stay”
text:
Recommended……we had a really great stay at the Intercontinental with no problems, our room/suite was fantastic. Staff were helpful and friendly with the exception of the concierge who looked at us with disdain and brushed us aside when we enquired if he could call a cab, obviously this was beneath his station in the chain of command…get a life !!
I can’t comment on the Restaurant as we decided to eat out every night and sample what SF had to offer, why bother eating in an overpriced Hotel Restaurant (which was empty throughout our 7 night stay). Bar was very expensive and appeared to be mostly used by people on business and expense accounts.....
As for location, again no complaints ..... only a few minutes walk to all the hustle and bustle of Market Street. I find it strange to read comments about poor location and ‘very long’ walks to Chinatown? Location was perfect for us - only 10 minutes to Chinatown/ 5-10 minutes walk to Union Square and we’re in our late 40’s .. ..Not the greatest of surroundings but if your not planning on spending your whole trip walking around Howard/5th St I don’t see the problem…… Would I recommend this Hotel to a friend – already have. Would I stay again – definitely without question.

title: “If ya gotta stay in Times Square”
text:
I had a friend coming in from Australia and he wanted to stay in Times Square so we grabbed a fairly nice rate in the Casablanca ($299). There is basically no lobby on the first floor, but who wants one on Times Square? The rooms are variable in size, and all have ceiling fans and Morrocan style furnishings. I like the ease of the window air conditioners and enjoyed a quiet room on the airshaft with windows I could open with no issues. "Rick's" is the breakfast and drinks room on the second floor and it is comfortable and friendly with flat screen TV's and free wine and beer each afternoon. The best thing about the place is the staff. They are always available, helpful, and pleasant. They all speak English and seem to enjoy their jobs. The guys at the desk helped us get limos and got us a room for part of day so we could check out in the evening.
There is a Disney-esque feel to the place, but the staff and quirky rooms make it feel authentic. It is literally steps from Times Square but an oasis of calm.

title: “Cool spot in hot desert”
text:
Lots of families enjoying the pool scene during a 110 degree summer. There are several swimming pools, which makes it nice for children of any age. I traveled with my 8 and 3 year olds, and they felt safe throughout the property.
We hired a Town Car to and from the airport ($30 each way), then rented a nice Toyota for a couple of days from the on-site Beverly Hills Rental Car (competitive rates - no need to wait in line at the airport). 
Food prices and food were OK - one child eats free with adult entree purchase, and you can expect resort prices. There is a grocery store and pharmacy about half a mile from the resort - stock up on goods there.
Free shuttle service to the other Pointe Hilton resort. That one had tremendous views of the city, but the famed Different Point of View restaurant was closed when we went.
Downsides? Only a small mini-bar fridge in the room. We didn't see a concierge until the day we left. The building itself was not really all that impressive.
Overall - great value.

title: “Nice building in Downtown Chicago”
text: I believe it is an old building, its really good located, it is some blocks from the rivers and 6 blocks from the harbor, shops and nice restaurants around, if you want party there are blues bars few blocks in the windy city.

title: “A shopper's delight.”
text:
I arrived at the Westin Galleria Dallas on a rather scorching day, but came to find out that was completely normal for Dallas. I was greeted by friendly staff who expedited me through the check-in process. The hotel lobby was very modernly decorated and clean. My room was large, smartly decorated (very modern) and clean. The bathroom was large and clean as well. One complain however. While taking a shower, it kept getting cold despite my efforts to the contrary. I discovered that the shower handle had a slight design defect. In order to have the perfect water temperature, one would have to place the rather heavy handle in the horizontal position. Well, the handle had not been tightened down when it was installed, thus it kept sliding down. As it would slide down, it would change the water temperature from perfect to polar ice cold. I pulled a MacGyver and fashioned a knot with a towel around the handle to keep it in place. I immediately called the front desk and notified them regarding the issue. Well, it was never resolved. I would have given this hotel a 5 star rating, if it weren't for that. 
For those who are shopaholics, you'll be in heaven. The hotel is attached to the Galleria Dallas which makes it very convenient for those diehard mallies. Most stores and restaurants are upscale, but you'll enjoy the scenery regardless of your financial status. I patronized the hotel restaurant once, but was pleasantly surprised by the quality of the food. I'd definitely stay at the Westin Galleria Dallas again and again.....

title: “Fantastic Place to stay”
text:
My wife and I stayed for a total of six days at the Hotel Frank, we were greeted upon arrival by Jackie who turned out to be a real gem of information and helpfulness, she guded us to a couple of very nices places to dine at, and was more than helpful at other times, other staff were also very helpful when help was needed.
Our room was not over big, but turned out to be more than adequate for our stay, it was clean and very tidy when we arrived and the bathroom was well stocked with all the usual towels and soap etc. The only fault we could find was we were on the side of the hotel so had no real view but this was no problem. The hotel was only a very short walk to Union Sq, and the cable cars that are famous in San Francisco, it was also a short walk to the main ferry terminal building when we went to Sausilito, and of course you could walk to Fishermans Wharf if you wanted, so overall a really great location.
We both liked the hotel for all the right reasons, location, staff, and the area, it was also very close to the hop-on hop-off buses.

title: “Cramped, hot, noisy, dark”
text:
Stayed here for a week, myself and my girlfriend.. Location is nice, right next to the park. We arrived very late (past midnight) and had let them know this would happen, and had no problems at all checking in. Staff are helpful and friendly. Price is good for Manhattan.
Our room was on the ground floor with a single small window facing a small dark grubby courtyard. Almost no light was able to get to the window. The AC unit in the window was extremely loud (it seemed to be rattling itself to pieces) and wasn't able to cool the room much below about 85F (it was over 100 outside) making it a pretty unpleasant place to be. At night we had the choice between being kept awake by the AC or drenching the sheets in sweat. Mmm, Nice.
Anyway, if you're visiting sometime when there isn't a killer heatwave and you don't plan to be in the room much, it's fine.

title: “Need Improvements,”
text: I have stayed at this Embassy Suites two times in the last 4 months and this hotel needs several improvements. The room bedding needs to be more modernized. The carpet has several spots and needs to be washed or replaced. The staff was friendly. This hotel from the outside looks beautiful. A few improvements to the rooms would make this an ideal place to stay for all business travelers. The breakfast has plenty of choices.

title: “Hidden Treasure”
text:
Hotel Andra is a hidden treasure in Seattle. Located in an older but classy building, once you walk in the door, it's modern yet warm charm envelopes you. The staff is friendly and very helpful yet not obtrusive.
Our room this trip, a suite, was large, very nicely furnished and comfortable.
For the value, this place is a hidden treasure. Excellent restaurants nearby, valet parking and close to Pike Place and downtown, Hotel Andra hits a home run.

title: “Excellent service at the Phi bar”
text: Received excellent and friendly service at the Phi Bar in the Hotel Indigo. Specifically, Devon went our of her way to call each patron by name and remember their drink order. This type of detail gives hotel guests a sense of community when they are potentially far away from home.

title: “Walk in closet”
text: The smallest room I ever stayed in. So small the tv was placed on a stripper pole at the base of the bed. The bathroom was a joke. I had to step outside the bathroom to put my close on. My car had more room in the garage than we did and was much cheaper than our room.

title: “Convenient location, but falls short of typical Hyatt brand”
text:
I arrived late from the West Coast after flight delays and checked in about midnight. The hallways were dirty, with many wall bruises and worn carpet. The room was ready, comfortable and mostly clean (bathroom floors were spotted). There was also a lot of metal fixtures and other rubbish stacked up in the hallways right outside my room. 
Since my meeting didn't start until close to noon, I wanted to sleep in a bit for the jet-lag, but the housekeeping crew would not let me. I placed a DND tag on my door, but by 8AM the housekeeping crew was in the halls making more noise than a middle-school recess. They were banging on doors, clanging metal objects and carrying on with loud conversations right outside my door. This was the loudest housekeeping crew I've ever heard. 
When I finally checked out, I could see that there was also a construction crew working in the same hallway, moving furniture, and apparently prepping for some sort of remodeling job. 
Overall the location was very convenient, but the housekeeping crew needs some training and room assignments at check-in should be better coordinated with construction demands.

title: “Return Trip didn't disappoint!”
text: My sister and I love the Affinia Dumont - so spacious for NYC and great location. We stayed in a twin bed junior suite which has a very decent sized lounge area, a work desk and a small but excellent kitchen runs off it. The Fridge is big, you have a microwave a stove, a coffee maker and a deli a few doors down for supplies. The bedroom is seperate, so if one person is tried they can go to bed and the other can read, etcetera in the lounge. Makes things so much easier when travelling with another person. You even get a bath. The decor is creams and browns in the junior suites and is fine, not glamourous but everything else about this place is top notch. Our lovely cleaner did a great job every day and Karen Medina the front desk manager and Crystal, who also works on the front desk were very helpful, courteous and professional when an issue cropped up at checkout (our issue, not theirs) which they remedied with the minimum of fuss. The beds are amazing and the only problem I had with our stay was that it didn't go on longer. If space, comfort, cleanliness, location and excellent customer service are your thing, stay at the Affinia Dumont!

title: “Ruined my vacation”
text:
Please believe what some others have said- this is a terrible hotel. I chose to go here mostly because of reputation, so I ignored other people's bad experience. There is no way this place is even close to a 5-star property!! Let's start at the beginning-
1- I spent extra money to book a room with a mountain or garden view, & was to be credited $50/day towards food/booze. I was really looking forward to eating at Wright's, and relaxing at the swim-up bar
2- We checked in, and were told valet parking is $21/day, or we can self-park for $7. We chose self-parking, and I wouldn't have minded paying the $7 if the parking was right near my room- it was not. It was a few blocks away, which is a good hike in this heat.
3- We checked in around 7:30 pm, and the first room they gave us had no windows, no view, no patio and the A/C didn't work.
They moved us to a similar room that at least had a sliding glass door and working A/C, but still no "garden" or mountain view- I had a view of the back of some shrubs. (By the way, we stayed in the "cottages"- my husband said it felt more like a cave).
4- The carpet was stained, some of the tiles in the bathroom were broken and cracked. The bed was obviously too hard because they put a pillow-top on it, which kept sliding off the side of the bed, with me on it. I had a terrible night's sleep, and the TV doesn't even have HBO! 
5- The pools- this was probably the worst part of our stay. The pools were filthy- I mean, really nasty. The water was green and cloudy and greasy-looking. It was so hot I went in anyway. As I was swimming I pulled my hand out of the water, and there were long black hairs wrapped around it (NOT MINE!!)
6- The service at the pool bar was rude. My husband ordered a Michelob Ultra, and the girl who took his order disappeared for about 4-5 minutes, then came back and said" Umm, we are out of a lot of things. They have Michelob Ultra at the bar inside. I suppose I could go get one for you if you really want me to." What kind of 5-star service is this??? For the $6 they charge for a beer, did she want ME to go get it myself??
7- Went to make reservations for dinner at Wright's and found out it was closed for renovations. Of course, this is not posted on their website, and I was not informed of this when I checked in.
I could go on and on, and I will tell everyone I know to NEVER stay here. What a waste of money and time. I could've stayed at the Phoenician or the Four Seasons or any true luxury resort for the money I wasted here.

title: “Location is the clue for this hotel”
text: The fact that this hotel lies just a few steps from Beale street, makes it the best place to stay if you would like buzzel of Beale street, jet also want peace and quiet in an business hotel. The Westin is not the cheapest hotel in town. And it show signs of wear. If you pay this amount one should think that you get some basic services included. But you have to pay for both Internet, both wired and wireless, and breakfast. We tried breakfast as room-service and it cost a fortune, about the same or more than we payed for dinner all the nigthts in Memphis. The breakfast was ordinary and nothing special. If you are into guitars there are Gibsons to be taken up to your room, witch is nice treat. The Gibsons branch office is just across the street. They also got this snackbar witch is weight based, if you remove one item for more than 30 seconds, you get charged. After my opinion this is totally idiotic.They should leave this to wending machines. There is also a free shuttle-bus to Graceland and Sun Studios leaving from the opposite side of the street. A good hotel if you get a good deal.

title: “Loved the hotel and the neighborhood”
text: I almost hesitate to write a good review about this place. I don't want it to become so popular that I won't be able to get reservations next time. We stayed at the BW University Tower for 4 days. The hotel and staff were great. The continental breakfast was very good. Tully's coffee is right next door with an ajacent door. There's a nicer restaurant in the basement. Free internet access. The decor is definitely not what one would expect of a Best Western. It's a block from University Ave. There are allot of inexpensive eateries around, a grocery store, and a laundry mat. It was a 15 to 20 minute ride to downtown. There are bus lines to downtown nearby if you don't have a car. We just loved this place. Even though it was right in the middle of a college are the hotel itself was not noisey and there were allot of businese people staying here. We'd stay here again...if we can get a reservation.

title: “Just OK!!”
text: I booked this hotels after reading a lot of good reviews about it, but as my surprise it was not what I was thinking, My room was hot and smelled funky, the air unit took a long time to start working propertly, We thought for a moment to go and stay at another place, but we decided to stay because we booked just for one night, also the rate that was giving online was not the right one, when I got to the front desk they informed me that I have to pay more for the room they made a mistake a gave me goverment employee rate at the time of booking, it was just ok!!, maybe I wasn't lucky enough to get a excellent service that make me recomend this hotel, I definally wont booked it again to average for the money I payed!!!...:(

title: “This is not your average airport hotel.”
text: I stayed here with my niece as she was on an overnight,9 hour layover. I wasn't sure what to pick because I have heard nightmare stories about some of the hotels near SeaTac airport. Everything from the reservation process to the fresh baked cookies at check-in to room service and shuttle service was handled spectacularly. The room was decorated well, the bed and the linens were top notch, and the room and bathroom were spotless. They clearly are customer driven and make sure that every need is met. I only stayed for the night but would have been happy to spend a week there. They are a little higher in price than the others in the area, but it is worth spending an extra 25 or 30 bucks to sleep in a place that is comfortable with people there waiting to handle all your needs.

title: “affordable, fun”
text: I stayed in one of the "cabana suites" last october 2002. I lwas on the second floor and overlooked the nice pool/spa. I was solo and it was my first time in LA. i felt comlpetely safe in that neighborhood and had a great time. 12 dollars to valet the car overnight in the back lot was a deal. the cabana rooms were decorated art deco, and were fun to relax in. good shopping was nearby for those of us not at all interested in rodeo. i happen to love tacky tourist shops, which there was an abundance of. staff was excellent. i was satisfied for the price I paid. the loby was under construction, wish i could see the results

title: “Cheap, Clean, Nice, Quiet.”
text: Close to just about everything. Are isn't the nicest but it's safe. Hotel was clean as if it were a 5 star Hotel in Vegas. I would highly recommend it.

title: “If for the bed alone..”
text: My new husband and I stayed here for the last two days of our exotic honeymoon. After traveling in the South Pacific, we were just looking for something nice to finish off our trip. I must say that while we truly enjoy luxury hotels, Sheraton is quickly becoming a favorite of ours if for it's 'heavenly bed' alone. These beds are AMAZING!! The hotel is nice, but the rooms are quite comfortable, the beds as I already said are amazing, and the concierge at this hotel in particular is truly par none!! He knew us by name from the first day and always had things 'just so' for us. Truly exceptional! Not only that, but I must say that the management of this particular hotel is very professional! We selected this hotel on priceline and yet when they knew we were staying there as part of our honeymoon, they quickly upgraded us to a Junior Suite at no charge. This was a very pleasant surprise and we were quite impressed. Overall I would say very nice hotel, very convenient to the airport, and very professional!

title: “Great hotel on St. John River”
text: Recently stayed at hotel for a getaway weekend with husband. From check-in to check-out staff were friendly and helpful. Suite was very clean and comfortable and view from balconies of river was beautiful, especially at night.

title: “I love the hotel, the restaurant attached and the location near blues and jazz”
text:
The hotel is great. Not one complaint.Really comfortable. I love Hampton Inns always. This one Has a Ruth's Chris Steakhouse which is simply sublime. The bar is wonderful. The Pool in the hotel is Ok and best of all, it is in walking distance of 2 of the greatest blues and jazz clubs in chicago., I does't get better.
I will be back.

title: “Nice rooms, quiet, close to Convention Center”
text: I was here for business and the rooms were a good size and clean. We didn't have a view so that would probably have been nicer but being there for a convention we weren't in the room much anyway. We did the breakfast buffet once and it was pricey (as are most breakfast buffets) but it was very good. Can't beat the location by the convention center & the Gas Lamp area both 5 minutes walk from the room. I would stay here again for business.

title: “Made an excellent choice and we'ii definitely be back!!”
text: We chose to stay in Detroit for my birthday/our anniversary this year and we're glad we did. Corktown Inn was a great find located just on the age of downtown. We stayed in the (2 room) King Jacuzzi Suite (price-unbeatable). The rooms were nice and clean, the staff was very polite (both night and day) and we were able to watch our cars( in the secure parking lot) on the TV in our room. Yes we even saw homeless people across the street in the park and hookers down the street, but tell me what city doesn't have them!! Our stay was Excellent and we'll definitely be going back soon!!!

title: “Awesome Place! Make this your first choice!”
text:
Great location and the service was perfect! We had a junior suite which was huge- 2 king beds plus hug bath and sitting area... ask for this room! Christopher, the conceige, was so helpful and friendly;.. he called me by name everytime we came into the lobby. Such a special feeling in this place... they also have a lovely bar on the rooftop. It's small, and just beautiful. Danielle was a server the evening we were there and she made us feel right at home. 
I have nothing but great things to say about this place. Parking is expensive at 48 / day, but you could self park and walk down to hotel about 3 blocks away. for about half the price.. We opted to stay in hotel parking as it was easier.

title: “Great location but not the greatest Sheraton”
text: On the plus side, the hotel is almost brand new and in a great location right between Soho and Tribeca. On the other hand, the 'deluxe' room was very small, with no storage / wardrobe to speak of, no mini bar, expensive wifi, the smallest bathroom with strange folding doors and an extremely noisy ventilator (we're talking hurricane strength), in top of the imcredible noise from the street (despite the higher floor). Staff efficiency and friendliness was mixed, the room wasn't made one day until we enquired. I know New York isn't famous for its warm hospitality but given you always seem to spend a small fortune in hotels (once the 6 different sales, room and local taxes have been added), this left room for improvement.

title: “Nice hotel”
text:
We had 2 rooms here the week before Easter. They couldn't get us next to each other but did manage to get us on the same floor. Having to take 2 elevators to get out to the street is a pain, but the location is great and the employees (though they're could have had more of them) were very nice and helpful. The hotel was sold out so the morning breakfast was very busy, so we never waited in the long line to get eggs cooked to order. The scrambled eggs that were already made left a great deal to be desired. The bacon and sauages were good as were the rest of the offerings. The coffee was not good. I made coffee in out room, and that was good. I don't know what they did to it in the lobby, but it was terrible. I paid $199 + tax per night and I would stay here again for that price. I just checked it for next month, and it is much more. I will call my travel agent to see if she can get it at the same rate again.
I didn't like

title: “Great Value for NYC”
text:
Okay, so let me just say that some people don't understand lodging in NYC. They expect a hotel that is $200 a night to be the same as a hotel for $200 a night in Columbia, SC. You cannot compare apples to oranges folks. For NYC, this is a real bargain. We dug around for several weeks until we hit a deal for less than $170 a night at this hotel. My parents stayed here the year before. Booking is a breeze online. We arrived via taxi and checked in within five minutes. The location is phenomenal. 51st and Lex with a subway station in front. The 6 train will get you most places with only 1 transfer. There are still rennovations in the lobby area where they appear to be replacing the bar. Whatever it was, it was demolished when we got there. The elevators were very fast and we rarely waited more than a few minutes.
The room was small, but not by NYC standards. We had a queen bed which was perfect. The bathrooms had some small cracks in the sheetrock, but it appeared to be minor. My only complaint is that the heat was BLAZING throughout the hotel so we kept our window cracked all the time, even though it was 40 degrees outside.
We never ate in the restaurant, but that was fine because there are several cafes within a block. Our favorite was the Cafe Oxford. Convenient, quick, and good. The coffee was bad, but neither here nor there.
Overall, I would stay here over and over, especially for the rate we got. If you want luxury, pay out the nose and get it. If you want a clean, convenient place to crash, this is the place for you.

title: “BED BUGS!!!!!”
text:
Beware of the bed bugs in this hotel! I had read about many hotels in this area having bed bug problems before visiting, so when I arrived the first thing I did was pull back the sheets and look for any evidence. I didn't see anything, but on our 3rd night I saw a bed bug running across our sheet as we were laying in bed! We immediately packed up our things (hoping to not see any more bugs in our luggage) and went down to the front office. We wanted a refund for that night and they refused until we showed them the bug. Luckily we had been able to catch and kill it, because otherwise we wouldn't have been able to get our money back. The guy didn't even look surprised and just said "We monitor for these things...".
To top it all off, I had reserved the room 2 weeks before our trip and was given the total price. When we arrived we were charged $4 more than my confirmation page said (even though I had printed it out and brought it with me). I didn't make a big deal about that at the time since it was such a small amount. However, when we complained about the bed bugs, the man at the front desk gave us our 1 night refund, however said he wouldn't give us the tax back that we had paid that night, claiming he couldn't since it had already been filed. I plan on calling the Better Business Bureau after calling Super 8 Corporate. I have a feeling keeping that tax is illegal. I've never bought merchandise at a store and returned it to have them tell me they can't give me the tax back...
The location was convenient for the Marina (we were staying there for the Fleet Week air show). However you would need a taxi or car for Fisherman's Wharf. Parking is extremely limited. The wifi barely works, "breakfast" is a tiny (about 2 servings) dispenser of stale old cereal in their 10 square foot lobby. There's no elevator, 3 floors. The room itself seemed clean (minus the bed bugs of course!) however had a bad smell to it from the start. There were 2 beds in the room and 1 was literally about 9 inches in front of the bathroom door, very hard to walk around. 
Do yourself a favor, although this hotel may be less expensive than some others in the area, save up a little more and stay somewhere that doesn't have bed bugs! I found a website, called www.bedbugregistry.com that people can list a hotel they've stayed in with bed bugs. Too bad I found this after my experience as I found this Super 8 already on the list!

title: “Good blend of location, cost and value”
text: I have stayed here several times. This hotel's proximity to Gas Lamp, it's comfortable modern rooms and great roof top bar make this an ideal choice for a stay in downtown San Diego. Though this hotel is part of the the IHG group of hotels it feels like a boutique hotel. Parking is a little pricy and the hotel only offers valet but parking is expensive anywhere downtown when you stay. You can walk to the local baseball stadium, Seaport Village and attractions along the bay.

title: “Great Service”
text: This isn't one of your newer hotels in Dallas but it makes up for it in the wonderful service. At first I just thought I was getting special treatment and then realized everyone was treated that way. From the restaurant with all the happy wait staff, to Betty and Juan at the front desk and just the others that I passed in the hall that always spoke to me, they were all so nice and helpful. I heard someone else saying they had never stayed anywhere where everyone was so nice. So you want good service, this is a good place to stay and it is so easy to get on and off the freeways. I also heard 600 count sheets are coming soon. Love that. I will stay here again.

title: “Design shabby chic!”
text:
Designer hotel and near the Park. The check in staff were superb and very
professional. I checked in first thing, so my room wasn't ready. Which was
not problem. I returned early evening and entered what I thought was the
little room from 'Alice and Wonderland'!!
I was disappointed especially given the rate. However, post hurricane Sandy
anybody would be grateful for a warm, dry, clean room. Only the room stank of mildew.
The wonderful reception team switched rooms immediately.
Room - same size as the first only with a baby tub that did not smell of
mildew. Phew had a great nights sleep.
Shame is that I couldn't wait to check out and duly cancelled the rest of
my stay. Fortunately found a better rate at a lovely hotel in a better part
of town.
Nothing against the Hudson its a slick operation and very cool, with great
staff. However, wish I was warned about the size of the rooms. Especially
the bathroom - put it this way my dog couldn't fit into that bathroom!!
Love to hit the bar but sadly not the rooms.

title: “Great Home Base for Exploring the City”
text: My girlfriend and I spent July 4th weekend here and got a SniqueAway rate (the hotel seems to be aggressively marketing flash sales recently). The Queen Deluxe room we had was small (220 sf) but comfortable, though the bathroom layout was not totally functional. The concierge staff, especially Joey, were always helpful in securing dinner reservations and helping me try to get tickets to the the Cubs-White Sox at Wrigley Field. There was no one in ground-floor bar/restaurant on Saturday night, and it seemed to be pretty sparsely populated the entire weekend. The hotel is well-located and close to a lot of great bars and restaurants. We ended up walking 10-15 minutes to a bunch of places but it's also an easy inexpensive cab ride to most places in the city and a couple blocks from the train.

title: “New York at it's best!”
text: My husband and I were in NYC for a weekend to attend a Reunion.One of the reasons we chose this hotel was the location and proximity to everything that we wanted to do.The hotel is located in a great location that is close to the theatre, restaraunts, entertainment, transportation, museums, galleries, shopping, transportation,etc.The hotel has a smoke free policy The check-in was efficient, our room was ready upon our arrival. We were on a high floor with a good view of the city. The room was well appointed and very clean.You can have a choice of king or queen double beds, some rooms offers sofabeds. There was no evidence of any little critters around. The bed was very comfortable for a restful night after fun filled days, The staff was available to assist with any questiions or concerns. The amenities are great as well. There is a business center, internet access, state of the art fitness center, pool, concierge lounge restaraunts including a Starbucks. The View restaurant that has revolving rooftop is a must do. It is the ony in NYC. If you just want to sit in the lobby and people watch, you will not get bored.There are so many interesting people that stay at this hotel from all over the world. Each morning you will receive a USA newspaper to read while drinking your favorite morning beverage whether it be a cup of coffee or a bloody mary. It was very convenient when shopping at the very many stores in the area. You must wear very comfortable shoes for walking. There is restaurant row on west 46 th street between 8 th and 9 th avenues. The restaurants offer 3 course meals at reasonable prices that would suit any taste buds. I can't wait to get back to NYC in the very near future. There is no place that can duplicate it.

title: “Location Location”
text:
This was my first visit to San Francisco and my husbands 2nd. We were recommended this Hotel by the Travel Company Trailfinders. We found the location for few days/stopover to be perfect for the top sightseeing musts. There were plenty of restaurants/shops/bars in the vicinity and close by to tram/bus stops for adventures further into San Fran. 
Slight confusement upon check in as we couldn't find our Hotel Voucher (Our fault, tired from the long flight!!!), but found it as soon as we got to our room which was a standard room (small by American standards) which overlooked the inner courtyard. We were on our first leg of our Honeymoon and even though Trailfinders requested 'Honeymoon' nothing happened. Oh well, would have been nice....
Room was adequate but may be a little crtamped for more than a few days.
Found the staff friendly like the other reviews.
All in all a nice little hotel in a good location in Fishermans Wharf.

title: “Convenient and friendly”
text: Room was clean and tasteful. All staff were friendly and professional. Continental breakfast was plentiful with fresh fruit. Conveniently located with 5 min drive to Old Town and 10 minute drives to Zoo and Seaworld.

title: “Great Hotel”
text: I've stayed here before and had another great stay. They were full when i checked in and i had to wait, but they got me room type i requested and gave me an extra cookie for my wait. Good location near logan circle with lots of shops restaurants and its a log walk, but can walk to the Mall. Room was great, clean and comfortable. Would definitely stay again and also recommend.

title: “Absolute Jewel in the Middle of the City”
text:
I was only able to spend one nite at the XV and tried to extend to a second nite to no avail. My one nite was very impressive, and look forward to coming back again in the future.
This isn't your 'cookie-cutter' Starwood or Marriott property, the XV is a boutique hotel with alot of character and fantastic customer service. I stayed in one of the 'classic'/regular rooms and was very satisfied with the layout of the room. 
It was an excellent find and highly recommend to anyone looking for a nice place to stay centrally located in downtown Boston. If you're expecting a Starwood or Marriott - don't come, it isn't a cardboard cutout room.

title: “Eastgate - Thumbs Up!”
text:
My wife and I recently spent 5 nights at the Eastgate Tower Hotel (March 1-6) and thoroughly enjoyed our stay. We booked a Junior Suite and it felt like we had our own 1-bedroom apartment (kitchenette, spacious sofa area and dining table) - and, above all, at an affordable rate. Important to add that the room was impeccably clean.
We were checked in within minutes and given a key to a safety deposit box (upon request). Hotel staff was courteous and efficient.
The walk to the the Times Square area is about 15 minutes. We liked being several blocks east of 5th ave. - a noticeable difference in the level of traffic noise at night.
Upon our return, we received an e-mail from the hotel inquiring about our stay. A first class operation all the way for budget-minded travellers.

title: “Fairmont Olympic Worth a little More”
text: The great benefit is having the hotel's sedan to drop one off and then the ability to call for a pick one up and instead of relying on the nasty taxi! With a taxi, you never know how clean or dirty they will be and if one is well dressed you have no worries with the sedan. My wife & I were headed over to an event at the Rainier Club and were pleased to use this free service.

title: “Nice for the price...”
text: Rooms were small but nice. Great location for walking around New York City.

title: “Excellent hotel, excellent location”
text:
My wife and I were going to a play at the Looking Glass theater and decided to take advantage of a Groupon at the historic Whitehall Hotel in downtown Chicago. The Whitehall is famous for the Beatles and Mick Jaeger staying there. I can understand why. The rooms are well appointed and the service is excellent. When we arrived at our room, the manager called and explained that grey needed our room. We were upgraded to a junior suite. The room was large and very comfortable. We enjoyed a breakfast at there dining room and it was very good.
We'd stay ther again, but look for a good rate.

title: “Greath location, spacious rooms”
text: We stayed at the Tuscany for 2 nights, we loved the location. We found the hotel to be clean and quiet. The rooms are spacious and confortable. We drove and found the hotel to be easy to acces from the tunnel, valet parking will cost you $ 50.00 plus tax, we figured it was fine for New York. We had a very good stay at the Tuscany!

title: “Theft at the Bristol”
text:
I stayed at the Bristol since my brother was having his wedding reception there, so did a lot of my family and family of the bride.
The next day my wife and I went and spent the day at the beach and sight seeing in downtown. We got back to the hotel went to bed, the next day we got up and started packing and realized my cufflinks that were a gift from my brother for being his best man were not in the box i had put them in. I specifically remember putting them away the night of the wedding. After tearing the room apart looking for them a family member came to the room to tell me he was also missing something. He then began to tell me an uncle had his Ipod taken from his breifcase.
We contacted the guest manager and told her what had happened. She had us fill out a form. And said she would conact us in a couple of days, which she didn't, I contacted her only to be treated like it was my fault that i left it in the room. She also said they had checked the computer to see who had used their keys to enter the room. Supposedly we never left the room, which is a lie. Everybody else has recieved the wonderful Bristol treatment that i know of. To much to write! Stay there if you want, just dont take any of your belongings with you on your stay if you want them when you leave.

title: “Our favorite place to stay when we're in the D”
text: We travel to Detroit often to attend baseball & hockey games as well as visit the restuarants and the casinos. The Westin Book Cadilac is our favorite place to stay when visiting. We have stayed here several times and love the spacious rooms and large bathroom area. Service has always been professional and attended to promptly. Location is great as it is convieniently located down the block from the people mover and is walking distance to several venues. The hotel itself is beautifully decorated although the pool seems to be in an odd out of the way location (we have yet to use it though). The only downside is the cost of the valet parking (this seems to be a norm with many Westin hotels) and I don't believe there is a self parking garage at or right near the location (but I could be wrong). It would also be nice if they offered shuttle service to many of the venues like many of the surrounding hotels do. Would definitely recommend & look forward to staying again soon!

title: “Great for what I needed”
text:
I stayed in the New Yorker for one night on my way to NJ for a business trip. I just wanted one night in the city to connect with friends and to explore the city. I've stayed in NYC a couple times before and this is definitely the best bang for the buck. As many others have said, the location is great. It's not the most ideal for sight seeing as I would prefer being between Central Park and Times Square, but being that I had an early morning train ride out of Penn Station, it was great for this trip. 
The room was surprisingly large with a great view of the Empire State Building and Chrysler building. The room came equipped with a large HD TV, good workspace, and a comfortable bed. The bathroom is bit small, but the shower has excellent water pressure and space. I could see how some women may be concerned with the size of the bathroom, but that's about the only negative I could find. Also, the restaurant nearby are okay, but you can find better places to eat just a few blocks away. 
Overall, this hotel exceeded expectations. It is old, but offers a lot of charm and character. The staff is friendly and helpful.

title: “Great Location”
text: We just returned from 2 nights at the Marriott on Pennsylvania Ave. and loved it. We found the hotel beautiful, a great location, and the staff was very friendly. We were lucky to get a full view of the Washington Monument from our room. The rooms were about the size you would expect from a downtown big city hotel; not very big but fine. The elevator is not too "techy." It was simple to figure out and very convenient. The pool was nice, but it's the location that would get us back. Great stay.

title: “Staying here is like playing Russian Roulette”
text: My boyfriend and I had to queue at the reception desk for AGES when we first arrived. There was always lots of people in the lobby at whatever time of day we went through there, but I suppose that was due to it being mid December and a busy period. LOTS of irate guests around! We had booked a 'superior' room rather than a standard. The woman on reception gave us our room key and we went up to find it, when we opened the door we could not believe what we saw! DISGUSTING! constantly running tap in the bathroom, filthy carpets, TINY bed, and it STUNK of smoke. Well we went straight back down to reception and started to queue again. But a porter spotted us and said 'oh, you two complaining about your room? Come straight to the front of the queue - you don't have to queue twice.' So we saw the woman again and complained that the room was disgusting and demanded a better room. (on the way down in the lift we talked with another English couple who were on their way to say the same thing! Apparently its pretty common practice for them to put you in a crappy room first and wait to see if you complain.) So anyway, woman on reception said 'booking a superior room doesn't guarantee you one. There are none available, sorry.' So my boyfriend got very angry at this - at which point she glanced at the computer and an available superior room MIRACULOUSLY appeared to become available. She gave us these new keys and THAT room was a world apart. Huge queen size bed, big TV, clean. It was like a different hotel. The lesson to be learned from this experience - complain until they give you a satisfactory room! They give the nicest rooms to the ones willing to fight for them, and believe me, you do NOT want to see the horrendous state of their worst rooms. Be prepared for a lot of running up and down between rooms and reception desk - NOT the most relaxing start to your holiday after a long flight. Also I remember a school trip of girls staying in our corridoor running up and down and screaming all night long, and leaving toilet roll scattered around outside. Having said all that, the breakfast was yummy, and it was handy for the subway - but not in my opinion a 'fantastic location.' VERY touristy area. There were other English people everywhere! The hotel is next to a real rip-off Sbarro! Quite difficult to find places to eat round here. Next time I'm staying in a hotel in Central Park West which gives more of a taste of the real New York, away from tourist central.

title: “Best Embassy Suites Out There!”
text:
Can't say enough great things about this hotel. The rooms are new and exceptionally clean and the service is incredible. This is the first hotel I have stayed at in a long time where I can say all members of the staff are " 5 star".
The manager's reception and breakfast area is large and there are plenty of places to sit. Room service was good. 
Loved the "upscale - 4/5 star "feel" of this Embassy Suites! Would not hesitate to stay here for business or leisure. Rates are weekends are a steal!

title: “Superb staff; Great room”
text: Four of us shared a room here between arrival on a late flight and departure on one early the next morning. Since we didn't get in until midnight we were really tired. We called for the shuttle, it was very prompt and we dragged ourselves in the door. As soon as we were greeted by Terry we were energized! He was so welcoming, professional and gregarious that we couldn't stop smiling. Our room with two queen beds was perfect for two couples with two separate bathrooms and plenty of space. We wouldn't hesitate to stay here again and highly recommend it if you're looking for lodging near the airport. It exceeded all our expectations.

title: “Not spectacular but nice little perks”
text:
First of all I think the renovations are complete so I did not have the problem of renovating noises. 
Even though the hotel is "all suites" I found it is no big deal as they are small suites. I can see how some people would find this not so attractive as each of the rooms are not that big ... they are not tiny but nothing spectacular.
The rooms are nice decorated with Flat screen TV's on the wall and I did not have the problems that previous people complained about (the bed was great, nothing wrong with the curtains and windows, etc.). Again, the rooms are nice but nothing spectacular.
The other thing that I find annoying is the 2 sets of elevators. You need to take a set of elevators up to lobby level and then change elevators to get up to the room. I found that bothersome, I know some of my friends find it "secure".
One thing I was very impressed about is their Omni Select program. I have never seen so many perks with a program - I would recommend joining it even if you are only going to stay there once. The best perks of that program are:
- Late checkout up to 5pm
- 2 free beverages of your choice (in a glass) in the morning
You also get free newspaper with that and exercise equipment in your room if you want but I don't see those as big deals ... 
Location-wise, Omni is great considering that it is just off Michigan Ave near all the shops. The Cielo resturant does have decent food and if you sit at the window you do get a spectacular view of Michigan Ave ... 
All in all, I had a very pleasant stay but I can get better hotels at lower prices ...

title: “The Giraffe has animal magnetism.”
text:
The Hotel Giraffe is a well-groomed boutique hotel in the less touristy, more real New York, Park Avenue South neighborhood. The lobby comprises the entire ground floor and is one of those “active” lobbies where people come to meet each other and enjoy the hotel’s fairly liberal guest policy for their free continental breakfast and wine and cheese hour. 
The rooms are reasonable in size, though not recommended for those who require spaciousness. They are well appointed, as is the bath. Each room has a floor to ceiling set of French doors that opens on to a tiny balcony. The views from most rooms are typical NY views of adjacent buildings. 
There are lots of nice touches throughout the hotel, ranging from your choice of free wired or wireless high speed Internet access, free bottled water in the room, and large flat screen TVs. There are also lots of electrical outlets in convenient places for those of us who travel with lots of electronic gear. The halls are very dark, intentionally so I suspect, as this seems to be something that “cool” hotels must do these days. I would urge management to turn up the lumens in the halls.
I stayed there one night on a business trip and everything went perfectly. This is a great hotel when being a bit off the beaten path of midtown is acceptable.

title: “Great business hotel”
text: Stayed here for 4 days for a conference. Hotel is beautiful, service is great in the restaurants and bar. The front desk staff was pleasant, efficient, and professional. The rooms are well appointed and modern. There were no toiletries in the bathroom when I arrived, however, a quick call to the front desk remedied the situation. The bed is plush and comfortable as are the towels. The only complaint is that the wall may be a bit thin. My neighbor's alarm clock went off several times during the night and woke me up each time.

title: “Great Experience”
text:
We stayed here for one night in November and were very pleased with our experience. The room was nicely decorated and very clean. With high ceilings, nice decor and very large windows, the room lived up to our expectations of the Palace Hotel.
We went for a swim in the indoor pool and a dip in the spa. The pool area was rather crowded, but there's nothing you can do about that, so we made the best of it and appreciated being able to swim in a huge indoor pool in the middle of San Francisco. It was a treat.
We live in the Bay Area, but had been wanting to try this hotel and we were not disappointed.

title: “Beyond helpful staff. Great hotel. Wonderful location.”
text:
We booked our room through Hotels.com, but unfortunately, our reservation was non-refundable and we had to change our dates. At first, it was nearly impossible to change, but the Hotels.com representative spoke to the Hilton hotel manager and was able to change our reservation dates with the Hilton's approval. Thankfully, the Hilton didn't charge us more since the rate had gone up by $100 since we booked our room. Also, when we checked in, without us asking, they had upgraded us to a better room for free. Nice.
The rooms were a little smaller than expected, but very comfy. The decor was nice and modern. The free internet was a nice touch from the hotel. There's also a coffee maker and tea available to you.
Overall, I enjoyed my stay here. Most of the tourist spots are within walking distance. Union Square is less than a mile away. Also, Chinatown and North Beach (aka Little Italy) are pratically right outside the hotel. I would highly recommend walking to North Beach for Italian food. My recommendation would be Franchino's, which is nice moderately priced family-owned Italian restaurant (about a 10 min walk).
