My only complaint would be that no matter how high your room is, you can still here traffic and other noises. We were up on the 23rd floor, and we could here children playing in the playground across the street. Also, parking is really expensive here. Valet is $53 a day and self-park is $30 per 24 hrs. I would advise you to drive around the neighborhood because you can find parking structures with cheaper prices.

title: “Not my cup of tea”
text: Hip & trendy = trashy. Upon arrival no bell captains to bring your luggage up to the room. Just drag it up yourself! Modern room decor with bar lighting. I'm all for "Streetcar named Desire ambiance, but It was hard to see! Bouncers at the front door asking for your room key for proof you are staying at the hotel & not just one of the DC bar goers. Went outside and no one available to flag down a taxi. This hotel is not cheap but is more like a Motel 6 then a 4 star DC hotel. I will not stay here ever again. For the same price one could stay at DC hotels where he or she is treated like royalty.

title: “Pretty nice hotel, but seedy location.”
text: I stayed at the Hyatt over Valentines weekend. It was your typical Hyatt hotel but the location was kind of shotty. The surrounding blocks are unattractive and gloomy. I booked a room at a discounted rate so I was happy with my stay. When I go back to Boston however, I will probably look to book at another hotel only because of the surrounding area aound the Hyatt as well as the design of the building and it's awkward entrance. Other then that, I was happy with the other aspects of the hotel (ie - room, staff, decor, etc...).

title: “Very Friendly Staff”
text: Great hotel! Staff was very nice and helpful. We used Priceline. Rooms were small (European small). Little walk to Michigan for shopping about 5 blocks, nice walk tho. Would stay again.

title: “Happy enough with the Hotel”
text:
Paid about 88 dollars for a room on a Friday eve. 
Check in was quick and easy - there is free parking at the hotel 
Room was fairly small but clean and in good shape. Microwave and refridgerator and a the room had a safe which was handy. Bathroom is small but fittings decent. Beds and Bedding clean and comfortable.
Our room was on the second floor - didnt notice too much noise from other guests or the road outside which is fairly close.
Didnt have the breakfast as we werent up early enough.

title: “Great Hotel For Business Travelers”
text:
We stay in Charlotte twice a year for business but we turn it into fun and stay the night each time. Normally we stay at the Hilton City Center but decided to give this hotel a try. I think that the difference in cost is around $40.00 a night, and parking is $10 here and probably $20 at the Hilton. The two hotels are pretty much steps away from one another.
This hotel is in a wonderful location - after you park your car you can walk everywhere. Great restaurants all around, cafes, bars, etc. Charlotte has so much to offer and is such a fun town to visit just for fun, by the way! 
This is the good hotel for business travelers, or for those who are just trying to stick to a budget. Nothing fancy and not a high end property but it is very comfortable, seems to be newly renovated. Comfortable beds for sure. There is not "central" air conditioning in the rooms, it is a "unit" in the wall under the window. There is one sink that is outside of the bathroom which has a traditional bathtub with a shower curtain. The toilet is in the same room as the shower. 
Parking was a problem trying to leave, as you have to use a key to exit and we sat in line while others were not able to get out, us included. We were refunded for parking, however. 
I have to admit that we really do like the Hilton better and will stay there again next time, most likely, but there is not a thing wrong with this hotel and it is in an awesome location.

title: “Melbourne, Australia”
text: Great value. Great location. The staff was very friendly, helpful and always on hand. Stayed in New Orleans (Ambassador), Austin (Hilton) and then the Ramada Canoga Park and this was the best of the three. The rooms was clean and the bed great. Great restaurants nearby, only a 10 minute walk to the Metrol Express Bus and another 5 minutes to Westfield. Will stay here on our next visit to the US. Keep up the good work.

title: “Awful. Coffee machine in room broken. Tub dirty. Bed mites. Charged me 91.00 but quoted 70.00 when I signed in.”
text: This is one of the worst places you can stay. Bed bugs, broken coffee pot in room. Breakfast put away downstairs by 8:30 though they advertized 9:00. Staff unresponsive. Tub filthy with oily slime. Thinnnnn walls.I called and spoke with the lady manager who said "go ahead and complain, thats alright". Definately would not stay at any other Days Inn.

title: “Sheraton Hotel and Towers in Chicago did not disappoint!”
text: This was our first trip to the City of Chicago and to the Sheraton Hotel and Towers. The location was perfect and our accommodations overlooked the river as it meandered below the flower clad streets and bridges providing a landscape of varied architectural styled buildings and skyscrapers-beautiful views- day and night! From check-in to check-out, our stay was comfortable and easy. Well appointed rooms and wonderful beds, attentive staff, and concierge staff that acted on every request made in a timely fashion.

title: “Total Bliss”
text: This hotel is one of the finest places to stay on the face of the earth. The staff goes above and beyond the call of duty. If there were 10 STARRSS I would give all 10 just based on my wonderful experience with the sleep number beds - I went right out and bought one for every bedroom in my house. The friendly folks there will always be remembered by me and my husband. Thanks Lord Bltimore.

title: “loved the room and hotel”
text: we were there for a wedding and found this hotel clean, modern, well appointed and in a great area...try it! the tv and channel options were great, the balcony wonderful, the quiet option lovely...we would go back.

title: “Excellent hotel for the price range”
text:
My wife book this hotel for 5 days on 4th of July weekend. When I arrived to this hotel; I was not impressed by ambience. I was thinking, we might have booked some other hotel. 
I went to front desk; the staff was very friendly. They initially gave me pool view third floor room but they changed on our request to second floor. Rooms were excellent. My kids loved the swimming pool and jacuzzi. They were very clean had lot of fun in Spa. Free WIFI and awesome breakfast in the morning. What more you need.... It is located at very convenient location. 15-25 minutes drive to Zoo, Seaworld, Safari, Legoland.
And the most important --> lots of restaurant on walking distance. You have lots of choices for dining out.
We liked this place very much. My first impression was completely wrong. I will highly recommend this.

title: “an excellent stay!”
text: We stayed at the hotel for four nights. We had a deluxe room, the room was very convenient to our needs, even though we were three. The hotel is located in walking distance to Broadway, Central Park, 5th. Avenue, Times Square. A starting point for bus guides is situated round the corner. The breakfest buffet in the hotel (17 $) can be recommended. By and large for us an excellent stay.

title: “For the right price, a nice hotel ...”
text:
For the most part, the location is very good, close to four major freeway intersections (10, 60, 105, & I-5). That said, I wouldn't want to walk the streets around the hotel after dark. 
This is an older hotel and it's starting to show. The room AC / Heat is still a central service type, so trying to achieve you ideal temperature is a bit of a challenge, no thermometer, just a small sliding lever. The rooms, hallways and lobby was clean and maintained. The room walls are a bit thin, I could hear my neighbor talking, but overall I was comfortable and did sleep well.
The staff was friendly and helpful. 
Given that I got a great deal, I give Sheraton three bullets. Then I gave them one extra bullet because of the free self-service in/out parking pass. In general, downtown hotels charge for parking (up to $40 a night) and then you end up giving a tip every time they get your car.
The downside ... like most downtown hotels, Sheraton nickel & dimes you on things like the Internet ($10 per day), Mini-Frig ($25 during your stay), 16 oz Bottle Water ($5), etc.

title: “Great Location, Great Staff, Great Value”
text:
Spent five nights here on our recent holiday to the USA. First time in New York, used this hotel on recommendation of someone else and it lived up to all expectations. The staff were great, very helpful and approachable. The room was extremely comfortable (great bed) and plenty big enough for the two of us to relax in. The location is fantastic for getting around New York, 1 block away from a subway station, and in mid town the rest of Manhattan is at your disposal. Would definitely stay here again.
Oh, and I thought the rates were exceptional for such an hotel in such a city. Thanks

title: “Great 2 weeks”
text: Our family recently spent 2 weeks at this hotel and it was a wonderful stay. We tried 2 other hotels nearby this one and wasn't satisfied. The breakfast was exceptional, the pool clean and refreshing and the staff couldn't be any better. (Especially Alex at the front desk.) He really went out of his way to make us feel at home. We'd definately stay again!!!

title: “Best in Houston”
text: Did a 3 day group meeting for 45 people. Meeting facilities, food, and staff top notch. Hotel near shopping. Sleeping rooms great. Nice pool.

title: “A Very Hollywood Experience”
text:
We just returned from Hollywood . It was the first time since my wife and I were kids (30+ years) that we had been in that area of Los Angeles. The whole time they were gearing up for the Academy Awards. By the time we left , they had closed off the street in front of the Kodak and Grauman's Chinese Theatres. 
Overall , we had a good experience at the hotel. It's a classic , old architecture jewel to be sure and situated in the middle of the Hollywood experience . There's lots of funky activity going on with the street performers and urchins. It's life in the big city after all. 
With a few exceptions, the service at the hotel was quite good. The guys at the door were extremely helpful and the service and food in the restaurants (steakhouse and hamburger joint) was fine, we thought. 
The rooms were of adequate size and the maid service was prompt and noninvasive. 
It does strike you that the hotel is quite dimly lit. We saw no ghosts, but the way. I guess that adds to the charm. One night we accidentally stumbled onto a crossdressing , gay party held downstairs....ooops . No problem.
Here are the exceptions:
They have to work on some of the help at the front desk. Our receptionist acted like she owned the place, or maybe she was just nominated for best supporting actress? You know the type. No pleasantries at all. We were interrupting her day. 
Service at the pool was lousy. We couldn't get anyone to come over and take our order, so I stepped up to the bar and was told to go sit back down as the waitress would come over. She never did. We waited . We left. 
Our shower had this half glass door . No kidding. It doesn't close off the shower stall . It would leak all over the floor whenever we tried to take a shower.... it was like living with a puppy dog....
There was some loud party going on our floor. It woke us up at midnight. It sounded like it was right next door. I tried to call the front desk, but could only get a busy signal. Kept trying , but no luck, until we heard someone knocking loudly on their door, could have been security....only happneed one night. 
You will have fun at the Roosevelt , especially if you're there to take in all of the funkiness and history of the Hollywood scene.

title: “Not so good...”
text: Room was damp and smelled weird. Icemachine didn't work. Lots of bugs in swimmingpool. No clean towels in pool area for days. Breakfast was pretty bad, juice was watered-down. Clean rooms though and good location.

title: “Everyone was right!”
text: We stayed in the Sofitel between 15th-18th November and cannot recommend it enough. As everyone else says the location is excellent, the beds are very comfy and the room was spotlessly clean. Particular mention to the staff who were very friendly and extremely helpful. Cannot comment on the food but can recommend the Red Flame Diner a few doors down. Would definitely stay there again.

title: “Great weekend!”
text: My husband and I stayed at this Hampton Inn this past weekend while attending a Clinton Anderson Downunder Horsemanship event at the Agriculture Center on Germantown Road. Special rates were given to those attending the event, which we appreciated. The location was great, rooms were clean and quiet, staff was friendly and helpful and breakfast was great. Would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone visiting E. Memphis area.

title: “Good choice for the price but”
text:
Let's face it, NYC hotels are a fortune! We moved here from one of the more expensive hotels in the city and I would say we got a better night sleep and for considerably less $$.
Not much going on in Herald Square aside from Macy's but a good location if you have an event at Madison Sq Garden. The subway is right outside the door so heading north or south is easy enough.
The staff was friendly, helpful and accommodating. The room was immaculate and the bed was quite comfortable. Our only complaint is that almost every room is within vicinity of the elevator. 10 rooms on each floor virtually surround them. They did as good of a job as you can insulating the walls but we were able to hear it in our adjacent room all night long. 
On a busy weekend the elevators take forever and are very crowded. The breakfast included is fine for the caliber of hotel. It compares well with many of the Hilton Garden Inn's around the country, a mid range chain.
This new HGI is a great economical choice NYC but not exactly a sexy, trendy one.

title: “very nice historic hotel perfect for freedom trail sightseeing”
text: My husband and I were delighted to come up from the subway station and look right across the street to see the Omni Parker House Hotel. It is literally steps away from the beginning of the freedom trail route next to the State House and Boston Commons. The history of the hotel is so interesting-make sure you read it and have a piece of their famous Boston Creme Pie! SOOOO worth the $8! The hotel is convienent to shopping, subway, dining, sightseeing and has all you need! The rooms were very clean and quiet and the beds really soft and comfortable. We did only have a double bed and the room was a little small compared to newer hotels but if you look at the convenience, price, and history of this hotel--it is not a negative! I wanted to sleep close to my hubby anyway so it wouldn't have mattered if we had a king! I will stay here again when we return to Boston! Oh and the staff was wonderful! helpful, friendly and even let us check in early! Thanks OPH!!!!

title: “Teeny tiny rooms”
text:
Do not stay in room #234 at this hotel... the room faced the street and the window a/c unit allowed all the street noise into the room.
the room is half the size of a dorm room...very tiny.
On the plus side...the room was very clean. the bathroom was large...very nice shower...good maid service...
be careful on hallway staircase.....I tripped every time I climbed those steps.....
Would have liked to keep the bathroom window opened for ventilation..but there are residences directly across form the hotel and the shower curtain was clear plastic!!!!
very difficult to sleep because of the city noise....If the a/c had been in the room and the window could have been closed that may have helped....Very good location for broadway shows and 
restaurants.... try Rays pizza
The Art Cafe on Broadway and 50th is a good breakfast spot....reasonable prices and the meal was served less than 5 minutes after ordering.
This hotel is way overpriced for their rooms...

title: “Not anymore”
text:
I also got stuck with this hotel using Priceline. This place is nowhere near the star ratings I've seen it at. The place was dingy, dirty. When we checked out, we heard someone telling that there were ants in its bedroom...
I would never stay here again and would most certainly not recommend it to anyone else!!!!!

title: “Good location.”
text: Rooms are nice, service is good, restaurant was tasty.

title: “Beautiful hotel and very convienent to sights around D.C.”
text: Not only is this a beautiful hotel but it is so convienent to the sights around D.C. You can easily walk to many things or you have the direct access to the Metro without even leaving the hotel (and on one of those horrificly hot days in D.C. this is a plus). The rooms are a good size and well appointed, and the beds are very comfortable. The breafast buffet at the hotel is great. And we've had other meals here through room service that were very tasty as well. You even have a Starbucks right in the lobby. And there are also many restaurants within walking distance. And I also felt safe here walking around the immediate nieghborhood even at night. And best yet the staff is great...friendly and very helpful. Yes they do get a lot of conventions and businesss people here but the staff never seems overwhelmed and the hotel doesn't feel crowded. Everything seems to run smoothly.

title: “Look no Further, Stay Here! Great Hotel and Staff”
text: Hotel Palomar has everything. We thoroughly enjoyed our stay. The hotel is in a great location (close to metro and very lively at night though not noisy), has the most wonderful staff, is very modern and has a lot of really nice extras such as complimentary wine in the lobby from 5pm-6pm everyday. After I booked the hotel I notice you could send requests to the concierge prior to your arrival so I sent them a note letting them know that we would be celebrating our daughter’s seven birthday while there. Well everyone and I mean everyone at the hotel went out of their way to make our daughter feel special. My daughter still can’t stop talking about it. After reading other reviews on trip advisor I had high expectations for our stay and I’m happy to say that the staff and the hotel far exceeded our expectations. This was one of (if not the best) hotel experience we ever had. I highly recommend this hotel and wouldn’t considering staying anywhere else if our travels once again take us to Washington D.C.

title: “Great Girlfriend Getaway.”
text:
In September, three best friends travelled to Boston for our 50th Birthdays. My neice had recommended Nine Zero and everything she said was true. From the moment we arrived until we left- the amazing staff helping us celebrate our birthdays. The room was spotless, the beds comfortable and the wine hours, was something we looked forward to. The staff was extremely helpful at all times and always offered great suggestions. The service from all the staff there was spectacular.
We would love to return again and would not hesitate to encourage others to give Nine Zero a try. As a side note- Boston is a great city to shop in!

title: “convenience at a good price”
text: This was our second stay at the Belvedere. We arrived at noon and were given a room right away, even though check-in was at 4:00pm. Room was clean, 2 queen beds, coffee maker, microwave & fridge. Staff were helpful especially the doormen. We were amazed at how close we were to the theatres and restaurant row! Only negative comment was that parking rates were not made clear to us upon arrival - Next time, I'll ask first!!

title: “Could be so much better”
text:
Don't be misled by the "Marquis" branding - this is a very ordinary hotel, but in an excellent location. The only Marquis dimension is the pricing!
The rooms are bog-standard chain rooms, decent bed, average size room, ok bathroom and flat screen TV - though in my room this was sittingt on the cradenza unit so to one side of the bed - bit awkward.
But one night, they hadn't replaced the glass tumblers, so waking up thirsty meant cracking open the water bottle provided on top of the mini-bar - $6.40 ker ching!
Breakfast buffet - all I wanted was some fruit and scrambled egs on toast with a coffee - minimum charge $29.13!
Now I am on expenses and understand the costs involved for hotels, but at these rates even I am not willing to be gouged to that extent, so walked out for breakfast the other days and double checked the glass count before going to bed!
We had an inclusive deal on the internet, but that would have been $14.95 a day
The public areas are very basic, with no areas just to sit other than in the wine bar or a few aiport style benches in front of the concierge. There are escalators up and down to a central court under the atrium that is just crying out to be a busy social gathering space - instead it's like an empty bus station with a scattering of chairs and benches some odd screens and zero atmosphere. This should be the heart of the hotel - instead its a dead zone.
The bar on top of the hotel has great views - if the cloud hasn't rolled in, but was so noisy that you wouldn't want to meet anyone there or sit and enjoy the view over a cocktail.
Location is great for shopping, hopping on the cable cars and union square etc.
So, it does a job, but really leaves you feeling it could be so much better... and/or cheaper!

title: “Not the Hilton You Expect”
text:
We had some extra time, so decided to spend the Thanksgiving holiday in NYC (and catch the Macy's parade). We wanted a brand hotel and not a boutique place. We also wanted to be downtown. The hotel itself is in an absolutely fantastic location. Access to pretty much all of the subway lines - they are all within a few blocks and 2 of them are right there. Century 21 is right next door so you can't beat that. 
Our room was mid floor and looked down on the WTC site. We had heard comments about the noise of construction, but we never heard a thing. It must have been the height. The rooms themselves are in need of updating. While the bed and other furniture are newer, the infrastructure is definitely in need of work. The air handler was either on full blast or not at all. The thermostat worked when it wanted to - which meant either the room was too hot or too cold. This made it a little tough to sleep. When asked, the front desk almost acknowledged there might be issues with some older equipment. Housekeeping made the bed and provide new toiletries, but seemed to lack the ability to clean other parts of the room. It appeared the spaces behind the desk, around the air handler, within 6 inches or so of any piece of furniture was off limits to cleaning as was any flat surface like the desk, armoire, nightstands, table or countertop. 
For the most part the staff was helpful, albeit not engaging. The exception was the concierge desk. They were extremely helpful and knowledgeable. Not only were their directions precise, but they gave landmarks as well "you will see ..... when you get there". 
The final piece of this trip was the bar area. It seems as though housekeeping doesn't even cover this area, and neither does any other staff. The chairs were stained, the tables dirty and there were food bits all over the floor. We decided one night to have a Manhattan (since we were IN Manhattan). This is, by far, the worst cocktail I have ever charged for. Part of the issue was the lack of service. After waiting 15 minutes for a server - which we had seen when we sat down, but had disappeared within seconds, we grew tired of waiting and approached the bar and placed our order. The standard garnish for the cocktail is a cherry, so we were surprised when they were made without. When questioned, the bartender (and we are assuming that is what he was since I had to interrupt his daydreaming to ask for a cocktail) shrugged his shoulders and said that's how he makes them. We sat back down and the mystery server came back. I asked about the garnish and was informed that they did not use cherries. When she saw the questioning look, she explained this was a corporate decision. Hilton did not serve cherries. (When we got home I called Hilton and asked and was told that is specific to that location). When we were almost done with our whiskey - I can't call it a cocktail, the server came over to take the order of a table that had just sat down. She provided them with bar munchies. This may be trivial, but we really felt like we had not been treated with the same level of service as the other folks. We went to our room, packed and got ready to leave as our flight out was the next morning. Needless to say, we will not be returning to this location. 
When we returned home, I contacted Hilton and provided these comments, which were then relayed to the hotel. The hotel management had no concern for any of these issues and had the general attitude of that's how it was. 
The hotel rates 3 stars mainly because of its location.

title: “In dire need of some TLC!!”
text:
We arrived by the side enterance, our first impression was 'Oh my god' the place stank of cooking and was full of smoke from the takeaway on one side and the restraunt on the other, the place looked awful, we proceeded to the front desk in the Lobby where our impression changed to one of relief,the lobby looked lovely with all the christmas lights, the staff at the desk were very helpfull (Sheila) was the lady who booked us in and out and on both occassions couldn'y do enough for us.
W then proceeded to our room on the 16th floor and had to laugh at the absolute state of the place, peeling paint on the walls, carpets were old and dirty, the green door to our room looked like it was armour plated, the corridors looked like something out of the film 'The Shining' we half expected to see a young lad riding his bike, REDRUM!!!
The rooms were just as bad, dirty, old, and in need of refurbishment, the shower was powerfull, but the bathroom itself must of been installed when the hotel was built, the cleaners changed the towels daily and our bed was changed the first two days but not for the further three days?
A word of advice, if its somewhere to get your head down for the night then its ok, otherwise look elsewhere, the place is a mess!!

title: “I can't decide”
text:
I liked the Carlton--there was nothing wrong with it. --a bit loud but old thin walls. Staff was great. It was clean and larger than some reviewers seem to find it. I also didn't find the neighborhood sketchy--but I wasn't out late at night. 
On the other hand --it wasn't that close to anything. (and probably why they charged only $77 a night) They do this complimentary wine thing from 5:30-6:00--a mix and mingle --nice touch, but if you are on the Coit tower and want to go to North Beach for dinner you would have to go all the way back to the bottom of nob hill/top tenderloin for it.--it's 30 mins each way . And it's not a neighborhood where you really want to go walking.It's sort of where regular people live. 
All in all -if I didn't have expectations that this was going to be a great place -I'd have thought it was a great place. But I did have expectations and since I spent less than $80 a night I wasn't really disappointed. If you don't go in with a lot of expecations hopefully you won't be either.

title: “Amazing Hotel, Great Views!”
text: Stayed here for one night. It was a perfect location for our engagements in the city: Orpheum Theater and AT&T park. We were able to walk to both. It was a bit of a walk to the stadium, so I wouldn't recommend it for a night game. The bellman also offered to hold our luggage during the game since we'd already checked out. The rooms on the upper floors are spacious and have gorgeous views whichever side you are on -- floor to ceiling windows! The shower is devine. Beware the mini-bar; it is EXPENSIVE! The room service continental breakfast is great and reasonably priced. Would highly recommend staying here!

title: “Good value, great service”
text: The location is great, there is free pick up from the cruise ship terminal. Although we weren't particularly happy with the noise of the train. What impressed us, however, was the service. On the last day our rental car's alarm was accidentally triggered, and we have no clue how to disable it. Several staff came out to help, including the shuttle bus driver, and the front desk staff. When we still couldn't silence the alarm, one front desk staff took the trouble of calling the rental car company for us (since we don't have a phone), and after a couple more attempts, the problem was resolved. We were very grateful for the staff's help as we have never driven newer models of cars and are not familiar with how things work.

title: “The most impolite people ever”
text: The hotel is nice and teh location is cool, but the people working there at the reception are by far the most impolite and rude i have ever seen. Problems finding our room, upset because we got an internet deal for less than they usually do (is that my fault??) and the next day they used some excuse to charge 15$ more per room... what a nightmare. On top of that these folks have been consistently rude in dealing with us. I would not recommend this hotel!

title: “Good room, great staff”
text: This was my first stay. I'm pleased and I will be back. The staff was uniformly courteous, competent, and helpful. The room was small but not so small as to be a problem, with a huge closet and a comfortable bed. Everything looked very nice. There were no noise problems from within the hotel, though anything overlooking Union Square will have street noise. On the whole, finding this place was a big win.

title: “Good and bad...”
text:
Every hotel has good and bad reviews, so I wasn't too concerned with the bad reviews on this hotel, until I arrived....
Yes, the location is fantastic (5 mins to Times Square) with an absolute quality Irish pub across the road, and the hotel does look really nice on the outside, but....the rooms are a tad small (so that puts it on a par with the rest of New York) and it is dark and dingy once you get past reception
The important thing to remember is the bad points in previous reviews. Yes, I got the room on the 3rd floor looking out to the sidestreet with a view of another building, and yes, the Air-Con unit for the whole block was outside my window and it was really noisy, and, remembering previous reviews, my window would not lock.
So, I decided to complain about the windows, and here's the clever bit, I complained out of hours so only a skeleton staff was working. They couldn't fix it, and I refused to stay in a room without a lockable window with the fire escape outside the window. In the end, they upgraded me from a bog-standard room to a suite, and an impressive suite at that.
Awesome (upgraded) room, 5 minutes from Times Square, for absolute peanuts. Result.
So.....if you get lumbered with the dodgy room with the window that doesn't lock and the Air-Con unit outside......COMPLAIN!!! It really does work.

title: “More than I expected”
text:
Just came back from 5 days with my wife, son (16) and daughter (12). We were very impressed with the resort with it being rated as a 3 star resort. I am sure in its earlier days (before the Phoenician's and Boulders came to be) this was the place to go. We were somewhat hesitant to book a 3 star resort but came away very pleased and would stay here again.
We paid $161/night with AAA and found that to be a good price for the room/resort. We had a two, queen bed casita with a pullout out couch in the common area. We spent sometime in the on-site waterpark (the waterslide was not open and we should have been told about this upfront) and had a nice time there with the kids. Coming from Mass. the weather was great (mid 60's) and certainly pool weather for us!
Ate two meals (one dinner and one breakfast) at the Off the Wall restaurant on the property and found the food was ok and very pricey. Would suggest you eat off the property. By the way...there was rattesnake listed as an appetizer on the menu at Hole in the Wall. The waiter brought out a frozen rattlesnake from the kitchen. The kids loved that!
There was renovation going on at the fitness center and they had temporary quarters (no charge to use) and had plenty of equipment. The new facility looks fabulous (I wish it was done for us..oh well). Other than that we saw very little renovating happening. My sense is that our casita had been renovated sometime in the past year. It smell very fresh and was very clean.
The staff was great and friendly, particluarly the concierge.
Tip of the trip: Make a dinner resrvation at Sam's Cafe. One of the best meals we have ever had.

title: “Loved Our Stay”
text: On our first trip to San Francisco, we stayed at the Serrano for 3 days April 6th-8th, 2007. The lobby is charming and we loved the nightly hospitality hours with free wine and organic beer. In the mornings complimentary organic coffee and a variety of teas are available free to get you started for your daily adventures. The staff was very friendly and helpful, the rooms were nicely decorated, bed very comfortable, and we loved the robes provided. The room was spotless with a well stocked mini-bar/snacks and in room safe. Through our friend the travel agent, the room rate was great. The location was very close to Union Square and 2 blocks from the cable car. We loved our stay and would definately consider the Serrano again!

title: “Full-Service in One Stop”
text: Travelled to NYC for the first time with my girlfriend who has been there before. A friend suggested this hotel because of their known reputation on great service. We were impressed that the Guest Relations agent was able to answer all our questions and take care of our requests/reservations all in one visit to her desk. Usually chain hotels send you to 3 different places with 3 different lines. Very professional and knowledgable staff who value their guests' time and business. Great stay and great visit. We will return to the Barclay.

title: “Overnight Trip!”
text:
The Palmer House is gorgeous throughout the main lobby/hall. It was my boyfriend and I's birthdays that weekend so we did a little overnight getaway basically. When calling to make my reservation, I requested a higher floor. Upon check-in the front desk asked if I still wanted it. We were up on the 21st floor, and we had a great view from our window. 
I do my reviews by categories:
The Room- very clean. We stayed in a King-sized bed room. However, the TV was still an old tube TV...and the bathroom was outdated. I understand this hotel is supposed have an old look/feel to it, which i like, but for example, the faucet was an older 1990's style and shower looked worn. You can get newly-made vintage-style bathroom decor to match the feel of the hotel to keep the charm....which they probably should look into. Also, the bathroom was very small. The room itself was a very nice size and the bed was comfortable. We weren't even near the "L" and i could hear it running every 5 minutes early in the morning...also our A/C unit started rattling in the middle of the night. I tried to sleep through it but it got to the point where i had to get up and shut it off myself.
Location- decent! Right by Michigan avenue, and close to Chicago attractions such as the art museum. I didn't even bother to check the prices of food at the hotel itself because i read prior reviews explaining single bananas costing $4... We ate at Miller's Pub (great bar & grill food) located on the east side of the hotel. There was also a Corner Bakery, and various restaurants on Michigan Ave. Also a Starbucks at the ground level.
Staff- Very nice! Everyone was friendly from the front desk, to the maids, to the employees passing by in the hall.
Would I stay here again? Yes. With some minor room renovations, this place would be close to me rating it a 5 overall rating.

title: “Good value hotel”
text:
Recently spent a week in this hotel in one of their triple rooms.
Good points:-
- Good value by NYC standards - I couldn't find any other en-suite triple rooms in central Manhattan for $200
- Location - just a few minutes from Penn Station, and several subway lines, v.easy to get anywhere in NYC from here. Also walking distance to a number of sights - Empire State, 5th Av, Macy's etc.
- Room was big, clean and also really quiet....certainly wasn't disturbed by banging doors in the middle of the night like other reviews suggest.
Bad points:-
- No major faults with this hotel, but a few minor downsides..
- Antique heating made a lot of noise one night, but was swiftly fixed
- Rooms are a bit dingy and old fashioned...but it was made in 1904, so what do you expect...!
- Hotel is located in a slightly soulless business district - not much in the way of eating / drinking options on your doorstep - but it's so easy to get about it doesn't really matter
- Puny muffin provided for breakfast was a bit stingy - however there is a place called Brooklyn Bagel Cafe round the corner which is great value for breakfast.
Overall, would definately recomend this hotel as a good value base to explore New York.

title: “Clean and Fresh with World Class Service”
text: Have stayed at the Ritz Chicago several times a year for the past few years and each time it has been exceptional. Was last there 8/23-8/26 and found the room to be clean and fresh as always with world class service from the front desk to the person who picked up my clothes for dry cleaning. No matter how often I return, I am impressed how the carpets always look fresh and stain free...and the bathroom is spotless, as if it was just built that day. Walking distance to some of the best restaurants in town and easy access to all to see in Chicago!

title: “Great Stay”
text:
The hotel was even nicer than I remembered it from my last visit two years ago. It has either been renovated recently or it has been very well maintained. The rooms were nice, quiet, and clean.
We stayed on a club floor though at first I couldn't find the club room (it was on the floor below). The breakfast in the club room was more than the typical continental breakfast and the staff was extremely nice. One downside is that the hours seemed a bit limited.
The location is also very good. Although it's not right on Inner Harbor, it's only a block away and within easy walking distance to all of the attractions on the harbor. It's also easy walking distance to Camden Yards in the other direction. Parking struck me as a bit expensive for a small city at $25, but it was convenient self-parking in a garage (this garage apparently is also used for people attending Orioles and Ravens games, so I don't know if it may fill up during events).
One of my main reasons for visiting Baltimore was to go to the National Aquarium. I made a big mistake and didn't buy tickets for the Aquarium ahead of time so by the time I went to book them online, all of the morning times were sold out. Because of my schedule I thought I might have to miss seeing the Aquarium, but when I called the hotel front desk, they said they had tickets that were members tickets which allowed you to go in anytime--and they turned out to be cheaper than buying them directly from the Aquarium!
I would definitely stay again the next time I visit Baltimore.

title: “Overpriced Internet”
text: Bayside room is nice and clean. Big resort pools small. $15 per day for slow Internet connection and $25 to park is a friggn joke. These people over charge for things that should cost 1/2 the price. Don't bother with this dump. Stay at the Del and you will be better off

title: “Fantastic apartment hotel for families”
text:
Our extended family spent two nights at the hotel and thoroughly enjoyed our stay. We had two rooms - a one bedroom suite and a studio suite. The one bedroom suite was very spacious with an excellent separate lounge/dining area and kitchen. There were plenty of pillows and towels as well as bathrobes. We enjoyed the complimentary breakfast, especially the hot waffles. 
The staff on the desk were very helpful. The complimentary internet access in the lobby was much appreciated and allowed us to print our boarding passes for our next flight.
The location in Hillcrest is excellent and is in easy walking distance to the zoo and Balboa Park. There is a supermarket only a block away to help stock up the kitchen. There are numerous restaurants nearby. We found it easy to catch the bus into the city. Being next to the hospital caused no problem and we didn't notice any extra noise. We also found parking in the hotel garage to be trouble free.
If our trip had allowed more time, we would have liked to have stayed longer. This hotel was one of the highlights of our brief trip to the USA.

title: “Baymont”
text: Great place if you want to stay on the north side of Austin. Quiet and out of the way.

title: “Central, comfortable, friendly”
text: Always treat me well when I visit. Great location, steps from the shopping of Newbury Street or the mall. Try Trader Joes nearby for groceries, or Shaws if you are going cheaply. Ask for a north-facing room to see the river, MIT, BU, Harvard, Fenway Park, etc.

title: “Very Pleased”
text:
The 6 other women and I were pleased by the cleanliness of this hotel. Front desk staff was helpful and pleasant. The consierrge was no help at all.
Rooms were decent size for the amount of time we sent in them. We had 3 rooms booked. Our room was the only one that did have a very bad musty smell coming from the bathroom, but it did appear quite clean.
Great location for walking to everyithing in area. The complimentary breakfast was good and was clean and food items were promptly replaced when depleted.
It has it's own little bar on premises.
Except for the musty smell in my room, it was a very nice place to stay

title: “Business Travelers delight”
text: I have stayed at this hotel over 30 nights this year and the one thing that keeps bringing me back is the comfort and hospitality that is shown by this hotel. The room is very clean and comfortable. I have yet to complain about any of the beds that I have slept in at this hotel. You can expect a good nights sleep in these beds. The hotel is attached to a wonderful workout gym so there should be no excuse not getting your 30 minutes of workout time per day in. The breakfast is wonderful and the wait staff are extremely professional. If I am doing any type of business in the DC area this is my first choice for hotels.

title: “maid service horrible..but overall very nice...”
text: i liked the overall stay at the edison...the room was small but cozy...the beds were nice...its nothing i would spent the amount of money i did on it though...my only complant was the maid service she was really rude to me and my friend...we were getting nagged and nagged to get out of our room...even though check out time wasnt till 3...and it was 9 am...we also had a do not disturb sign on which clearly she couldnt read cuz each time she just opened the door till she go very snotty wit my friend and asked us are we leaving yet..,

title: “Funky, Roomy, Close to Transportation, a little noisy”
text:
We stayed at Hotel Helix from May 4-7. Here's the pros and cons:
PROS:
1) We checked into our room early. We had a red eye and got to the hotel at 8:30am hoping to just check in our bags. Thankfully they let us check into our room early! 
2) Check in was fast and easy. 
3) Funky decor is not bad. We are a relatively conservative couple when it comes to decor and were a little hesitant when booking this hotel from looking at the website photos...however the decor is not that overbearing at all. Kinda fun..
4) very close to transportation. Close to the 52/53/54 bus lines (just 1/2 block away) which go to many of the main attractions.
5) Close to places to eat and walk around. We spent a few hours just walking around the area- a lot of cute areas to eat at and neighborhood homes to see.
6) Aveda bathroom amenities! I loved the rosemary mint shampoo and conditioners....a nice change from the other hotel bathroom soaps/hair supplies that leave my hair dry and in knots!
7) Roomy! We had a king size bed that had a sheer curtain separating the bed from the living area- this was kinda fun. The living area was very large- we didn't use the futon bed-- but even if we did, there'd be plenty of room still.
8) Plush robes. Each room gest two plush robes (animal print!) that were nice to lounge in and jump out of the shower into!
9) Dogs were okay. We were a little weary about staying in a hotel that was pet friendly, but we didn't seem to have any problems. There was a dog in the room across from us, but we only knew this because as we walked by, the dog would bark. Otherwise, we couldn't smell or hear the dog.
10) Cheap Happy Hour every night! Happy Hour is from 5-7pm nightly in the lounge. You can get half price cheeseburgers (comes out to be $5.50) which is nicely charbroiled with all the fixings and yummy french fries. They even let us take it "to go" up to our room and fixed it up like room service vs just in a doggy bag.
11) free wifi- a definite plus to look up things to do, places to eat..
CONS
1) Noisy at night. Our room was on the 3rd floor above the patio lounge area. The bar/restaurant is open until 2am and if the weather is good, there's a lot of people hanging out outside....and you can also hear the music from the lounge too. We were so tired from the red eye flight and days' activities that we managed to sleep okay.
2) Noisy in the morning! The lounge is undergoing renovation- luckily right beneath us. They didn't start construction until 9am, however it was very loud.
3) No microwave. We could've used one.
4) Small bathroom. The bathroom was very small.

title: “Top Hotel in Fort Worth”
text: This was our third stay at the Omni. Although our first stay had a few problems, subsequent stays were great. The hotel and guest rooms are upscale, beautifully decorated and well maintained. In general the hotel staff was very courteous and helpful especially reception. A few issues though. While we enjoyed the food and service at the Cast Iron Restaurant, the hostess seemed bewildered. Also, I had asked to have my shoes shined and delivered to my room the next morning. Instead of leaving them oustide, the valet woke us up by attempting to open our door while we were asleep! Crazy and annoying!

title: “Good location rooms are a bit out dated”
text: Stayed here for a few days for work. The location is great on Ohio between michigan and st Clair, right off mag mile. There is no room service, and the elevators are inconsistent as they lights and indicators don't always work. The bathrooms are a little older and the window ac units are a little loud. However the rooms are clean and the service was very nice and friendly.

title: “Nothing Special...”
text: We just got back from Chicago and I wanted to write this while everything was still fresh in my mind. We stayed two nights, with extended family. My husband, sister, and brother-in-law, and I stayed in one room, while my mother, stepfather, and brother stayed in another. We made reservations over a month ago, for the historic tower, only to find when we arrived they did not have rooms avaliable so we were moved to the other tower, we did receive a much cheaper rate, so we were ok with that. The girl who checked us in was very slow and it took forever, we probably stood in the lobby for over 20 minutes. We went up to our rooms, and they were ok, but nothing special. To me they actually seemed a bit small. The beds were hard as a rock, not comfy at all. The bathroom was ok as well, but again nothing special. My husband had a drink at the bar which cost $9 (which is a bit much, for me) and then he said it was so strong he couldn't even drink it. We went to check out the pool and fitness center, and both were very nice, then as we were leaving we found out that you have to pay to use the fitness center! I would think as much as you pay for a room in this hotel the fitness center should be free. The location was very good, close to many good restaurants, and tons of shopping, but if I ever come to Chicago again I probably would not stay at this hotel again. We saw several other hotels in the area that would probably be a much better value for your money.

title: “Great stay!”
text:
This was the first stop in our four week road trip and looking back it was one of the best places we stayed at. The owners were very friendly and were always happy to point us in the right direction for the next part of our trip. They insisted we would visit the Cabrillo Monument before leaving San Diego and it was worth it, so thanks again for the tip ;-)
Our rooms were clean and comfortable and it was nice to enjoy the breakfast muffins on the balcony in front of the rooms while enjoying the view. I'm convinced you won't find a better place to stay in San Diego for this price.

title: “Clean but dated Decor”
text: We picked this hotel for its proximity to LA Live. For the price we paid we were disappointed at how dated the rooms were. The room had a faint smell of old water although the room appeared clean. The beds, dresser and TV were the only furnishings that seemed to be updated in the last decade. The closet had old mirrored doors, the bathroom had a sink faucet from 1980 and overall had a time warp feel. The light switches were dated along with the lamps, phone and alarm clock. This hotel's only saving grace was its modern lobby which includes a restaurant, Starbucks, internet area and a small TV 'living room'. Also, another positive was the free parking across the street at a meter on a Sat night to Sunday.

title: “NO that great”
text: The Drake was an okay hotel..very old..I expected mote from this hotel , they need to renovate their rooms...service was great at the hotel..employees are very helpful though I would not stay here again..very disapponted with the rooms..we were given 2 full beds!!!!!!

title: “What was needed!!”
text: Perfect location and appropriate price. Discovered a great French restaurant over the road, pascolos (spelling wring!). Reception and concierge very helpful! A/C is very noisy so in hotter months that could be a problem choosing whether or not to run it overnight.

title: “Good location, small room”
text:
Stayed here for 2 nights with husaband.
This hotel is getting older but has it´s charm.
The room we stayed in was very small but cosy.
Location is excellent.

title: “Great Newer Hotel Near Plenty of Downtown Attractions”
text:
On a recent visit to San Antonio for a business, I opted to extend my stay by 1 night and experience the La Quinta Inn & Suites for the first time. I was very impressed! The hotel, opened around 2005, is a new construction hotel built near the former site of the very first La Quinta Motor Inn (opened in 1968 for the HemisFair). You can read all about the brand history through a mural of collected artifacts of the last 40 plus years on display at this hotel. It was really a pleasant surprise.
Upon arrival, I was checked in by a friendly but busy front desk staff. My room was ready early, so I had time to settle in and enjoy the expansive pool area and hot tub. It was mid afternoon on a bright sunny Friday, but only a handful of people enjoying the pool. The area was fresh and clean, and the water sparkling! My room was on the 14th floor (of 15), but with plenty of fast moving elevators, there was rarely a wait. The suite was spacious, clean and cool. The bed was extremely comfortable and everything was in working order. The TV service features a really nice bonus – several channels of “ambient choices”! A great way to relax. The room included a work desk, free Wi-Fi (although slow), and a coffee maker, fridge and microwave. Bathroom amenities were basic, as expected for a limited service hotel. The hotel features a rare option for La Quinta – a lounge area with light menu. I enjoyed a glass of wine before retiring, but opted for dinner at one of the many restaurants within a few blocks of the hotel.
Although I knew it would be chaotic on a Saturday morning, I decided to experience the free breakfast. It was indeed ridiculously busy, a reason why free breakfast has little value to me, a single traveler in this case. I imagine it would have been far more pleasant during the business week. The dining area and lobby however were very inviting. Not flying out until later, the hotel happily held my bags for me while I explored the city once more before leaving. Check-out was slow because the front desk is always busy, and often multitasking by also taking reservations. The hotel is directly across the street from the RiverCenter Mall, and about a block from the River Walk itself. You’re less than a ½ mile from the Alamo, Convention Center and Zoo – in other words, a great location and good value in downtown San Antonio! Upon departure, the Bell Staff quickly and politely gathered my bags and called a cab. Overall, a great first experience with La Quinta, and I would definitely recommend the Convention Center location for midweek business travel, families, and easy access to many of the Downtown offerings.

title: “Best hotel ever!”
text: If I could give them 6 stars it would be more appropriate. The place was just renovated and is gorgeous and the service is unmatched . We stayed 2 nights because we split our trip bw San Fran and Napa. That was a mistake. We should have just stayed there for our entire trip. The first night we had the most delicious chocolate covered strawberries waiting for us in our room. The second night that we checked in they upgraded us to the Club level. OMG! So amazing! All because they knew we were there to celebrate my husbands 40th. The staff is so well trained and customer focused we felt like royalty. I will only stay at the Ritz from now on. Best money we spent our entire trip! They even drove us to the Pier in the hotels Lexus so we wouldn't miss our ferry for an excursion that they booked for us!

title: “Really Nice and Great Value”
text:
I was really pleased with this hotel after my husband found it on Trip Advisor. The hotel was in a really central location and we spent our mornings walking to the wharf (a long, hilly, but really great walk) which is definately something that can be done (I was pregnant). We would take a cable car or street car back to Union Square later and do some late afternoon shopping. 
Very nice staff, very clean rooms and bathrooms. The hotel is a block away from Chinatown and a few blocks from a great little street (Belden) with some fantastic restaurants.

title: “Ok, not brilliant”
text: Unfortunatley NYC is expensive so if you are on a tight budget and dont want a hostel your options are limited. The rooms are clean and the beds are comfortable.. They are also very tiny. I have stayed in tiny rooms before and have managed fine, but the layout of the room is bad so you will trip over your bags. The bathroom is old and in dire need of an exhaust fan - you had to shower with the door open and not bring anything in as the steam would get everything wet - I had to make sure I didnt have a hot shower like I normally like, something you shouldnt have to do. The housekeeping staff hassled us on a few occasions to clean our room - I generally only need my room done every 2 - 3 days and them hassling me to clean my room to get their tips was annoying. I understand The Pennsylvania is a not as great hotel, but has bigger rooms and if I was to go to New York again would stay there or Clarion near Times Square. Location was pretty good - had a good meal at Coopers Tavern downstairs. Staff at Tick Tock diner need to improve their customer service skills.

title: “Good choice for early morning flights”
text:
We wanted a place that was close to the car rental return, which is some distance from the airport. This hotel fit the bill. The staff, knowing proximity is a consideration, hands out printed directions. Furthermore, there's a not-overpriced gas station on the way.
The hotel is up to HIlton standards: clean and comfortable, good but not luxurious. One complaint: Their Internet connections aren't wireless.

title: “Much better then anticipated !”
text: I can honestly say that this was a first for me at a Holiday Inn. Although not by choice as it was a business meeting, it will now be for the next time as I was very impressed ! My thoughts were completely different - great place to stay on all counts. Would have stayed a week without any regrets. I just hope that everyone else will feel the same so long as the service, value and cleanliness remains the same. If your looking to eat - "Seven Bridges " - great steaks !

title: “Great stay”
text: Liked the way room was set up, there customer service was excellent, we enjoyed how close it was to train station and other attractions we saw, breakfast was great. everyone there was lively and friendly, we enjoyed our stay .

title: “A Step Above the Rest!!!!”
text: We stayed at the Homewood Suites from April 5th-14 and were very pleased with this hotel. We stayed in the 2 bedroom suite, which accommodated our family of five quite well. The rooms were very spacious and the beds were comfortable. We were also a little concerned with the hotel being so close to the airport, but we weren't bothered at all by any noise. The hotel backed onto a wonderful walk way and park, which we used almost every day. Our kids also took advantage of the heated pool and hot tub. This hotel also had a huge patio BBQ for guest use. It was very clean and well maintained. The breakfast and dinner receptions were plentiful and the wine and beer was a nice touch. The staff taking care of the meal area were polite and very friendly. We let them know that they were appreciated. The front desk and housekeeping staff were very attentive of our needs and respectful of our property. I was very impressed when Stella knew me by name whenever I needed something from front desk. Thank you Homewood Suites for making our stay in San Diego so enjoyable. I look forward to our next stay.

title: “Great find!! Glad we finally stayed here!”
text:
We currently live in California but my husband is a native New Yorker. We usually take a trip to NYC about once a year and have stayed in different hotels everytime. I had heard about the Hotel Newton a few years ago but never ended staying there. This trip we were taking some especially budget-minded family members for a little reunion of sorts. I remembered the Hotel Newton, checked it out some more, and decided this sounded like a good location and a good deal as well. 
My husband and I reserved a Superior Queen as did his older sister and her partner. The younger sister and her husband and two teenaged daughters went with the Deluxe Double. When we arrived those of us who had reserved the Superior Queen rooms were upgraded (at no extra cost) to Deluxe Queen rooms. We were on the 8th floor but I can't remember the room number. 
The Deluxe Queen rooms were very roomy by NYC standard with plenty of room. We had a nice flat screen television and a good sized closet. Rooms were very clean. The bathroom was a bit small and the only thing I found weird is that there was a window in the shower itself that wasn't privacy glass. As our room faced the street with other buildings across the street I felt a little uncomfortable as the window would show everything from about the waist up. Maybe it was one way glass?
Our family members traveling with teenagers ended up on another floor and their room was considerable smaller than ours, especially with two teenaged girls and all their stuff. They had a problem with their air conditioner not working but when they complained it was promptly replaced with a brand new one. 
Yes, the elevator is slow and there is only one but as we were never in a hurry that wasn't a big deal.
Front desk staff was great!
Location is good in a nice family neighborhood. When walking on a back residential street we even came upon a little girl and her dad with a lemonade stand. We also spotted actor Matt Dillon one night! Depending on which subway lines you are taking the station is either very close or a bit of a walk. There was a deli (can't remember the name) a couple of doors south of the hotel that served great breakfast items at really good prices. We got our breakfast there everyday. 
I would highly recommend the Hotel Newton to anyone looking to stay at a comfortable, clean, reasonably priced hotel in NYC.

title: “intensely appealing!”
text:
Immaculately clean - beautiful! 
I stayed here with my husband for a wedding weekend in Dallas - I would totally recommend it. They even handed out happy hour vouchers/drink tickets when we checked in. Classy hotel. Loved the decor - and the room was staged very nicely. Felt like a creative room, not just a box hotel. 
We would definitely go back.

title: “Great resort - wonderful service - super employees”
text: Stayed at this resort for a one day conference - but was overly impressed by the cleaniness, service, facitilites and overal appearance. I especailly enjoyed being served by Angelica Stephens - the best waitress in the world!!!!

title: “Excellent stay- no issues”
text: The location can not be beat- directly across from Alamo Plaza. From the airport, you can take city bus (VIA) route 5 McCullough and land within about 3 blocks walking from the hotel. I had prepaid through a third party for 5 nights and noticed after the first night that I was being billed again when I reviewed my account on the television. I promptly inquired at the front desk, they apologized profusely. Einstein Bagels is in the lobby and were open 24 hrs for 5 says a week. Amazing!

title: “Pleasantly Surprised”
text:
While my mother was visiting me from the midwest, I decided to surprise her with a trip to NYC (she'd never been). I ended up at the Park Central through Priceline with a winning bid of $120 per night. After reading various reviews on TripAdvisor, I must admit that I was a little nervous about this hotel. I was very pleasantly surprised by my stay there. We were there for two nights (8/8-8/10). I found the staff to be friendly, efficient, and helpful. Other reviews complained about long lines for check-in/check-out and the elevators. I experienced neither. The one quirky thing that happened was that there were no towels in the room upon arrival. I called and was told towels would be sent immediately-they never arrived. Fortunately, while filling the ice bucket, I found the linen closet and helped myself to towels. 
We got to the hotel around 12:30 p.m. and were told that our room wouldn't be ready until 3/3:30. They have a baggage room available, but there is a $3 charge per bag. We left our bags and immediately began to explore the city. Our room was comfortable, clean, and nicely sized. 
This hotel is in a great location (W. 56th and 7th Ave.) with plently of inexpensive restaurants nearby. The hotel was a couple of blocks from Central Park and Times Square. Who could ask for better?

title: “Yes, with quibbles”
text:
They are right about the beds -- very comfortable, and nice cotton sheets. Temperature control in the rooms actually works. Computer terminals and online access available free -- a rarity these days.
They're stingy with the coffee. You only get two coffee pads, and those are stale. I suppose they want you to use the Starbucks in the lobby, which I did. I have to admit it was good. Other quibble: you can still hear noise from the next room, though it's pretty muffled. And what is this trend toward loud music in the lobby? Adds to the stress of traveling.
Wonderful location, half a block from Boylston Street, around the corner from the Hynes Convention Center.

title: “Great location. Great Value”
text:
(sorry I'm a little late for this)
We had a little trouble at check in, getting the room we booked, but I believe it was mainly because the guy was new. We had to go back down, to get moved to the proper room, but the manager stepped in and fixed us up right away.
We had a corner suite room for $169/nt+tax (Sun&Mon). It was Humongous! An incdredibly large room (see pics), with an outstanding view of the street cars. It's and older hotel, but we found it had lots of charm. The street car noise did not bother us at all. We thought it was pretty cool, hearing the street car bells ringing. Again, you can't beat the price for that kind of a location!
Plus, there is a very, very, very large shoe store just across the street! (I like spoiling my girl! I think she got 4 or 5 pairs this trip..... not shown in the picture :) 
This boutique hotel is part of "Personality Hotels" which owns 4 other chic hotels around union Square. They all looked pretty cool.
See em at: ---

title: “Awesome service nice view and great price for San Diego”
text: Stayed there on 4/1/2011 to 4/3/2011 wonderful stay the room was spotless they gave us a somewhat secluded room facing the marina with a nice patio . It was the end of our honeymoon trip and this was the best place . We had one small issue with our breakfast but they corrected it right away and then comped us the breakfast . They we always asking us if there was anything they could do to make our stay better all employees were very attentive we were so empressed we will definately book our next stay there . They made our last two days of our honeymoon very memorable .

title: “Glamorous and comfortable”
text:
My husband and I really enjoyed the Palace Hotel. It is conveniently located, the door to the hotel being right next to the exit for the Montgomery BART stop. It's walking distance to Union Square, the shopping centers, and Chinatown.
The inside of the hotel is very grand, with a lot of gold gilding and embroidered fabric. Our room was on the small side but elegant and very clean, with a big comfy bed, flat screen TV and good quality furniture. The shower was hot with good water pressure, which I appreciate! 
Their pool is very nice. It's indoors with a glass roof, and there is a big exercise room. We didn't use either though, we just walked through.
We had afternoon tea in their Garden Court, which has an astonishingly grand glass roof, lots of chandeliers and marble pillars. The tea was very expensive ($40), so I would say, eat there for the experience and the surroundings, but not for the food. You can have afternoon tea elsewhere for cheaper.
We ordered room service for breakfast, and the food came promptly and was excellent.
We found a good rate for the hotel as it was Labor Day Weekend. When we decided to stay another night they not only honored the special rate but actually discounted it even more.
I highly recommend this hotel. We felt very pampered. I'd look online and ask carefully for discounts, as we found they are available, especially on weekends.

title: “A little hard to get to from Ben White but worth the trip”
text: Hilton Austin Airport was just what I've come to expect from Hilton Hotels worldwide. Excellent customer service, the right price and amenities to make your short stay during airline travel as comfortable as possible. The bed was absolutely heavenly. If you are looking to enjoy Austin in all its glory, I'd recommend a Hilton facility downtown but this Hilton location is superb for early morning travel.

title: “Great location, comfortable beds”
text: This boutique hotel has a great location, 2 blocks from the Dupont Circle metro stop. Great restaurants and shops are walking distance from the hotel. There is no lobby to speak of, and no swimming pool, so I would not stay here during the summer. The decor is different - black, brown, taupe, modern looking decor. The beds are quite comfortable with triple sheeted beds and duvets. We had a deluxe room, very spacious. The toilet/tub shower are in a very, very tiny room. The sink and dressing area is more spacious with a lot of closet space. Great restaurant in the building - the Firefly. It's very crowded, make a reservation. Avoid the overpriced continental breakfast, go to Cosi's by the metro stop instead. We got a great rate for the quality of the hotel, I think we got it from an online special at the hotel website.

title: “Excellent Location, Good Value Hotel”
text:
We really enjoyed our stay here over the Easter weekend. The meatpacking district is a great base with good transport links and excellent restaurants nearby.
The rooms are a little small, but average for NY. The decor is very tasteful, the bed was very comfy and the view (11th floor Grand Deluxe room) looking north was brilliant.
The hotel has a well equipped gym (with TV and headphones). The pool looked like it would be nice in summer, but whilst we were there it had a temporary winter cover that intensified the chlorine smell and made it less appealing.
The desk and concierge staff are efficient and helpful.

title: “Great place to stay...”
text: We found this Hampton Inn a great place to stay, with a friendly staff that went out of their way to help us with our travel plans and excursions.

title: “Not the Hyatt Hill Country”
text:
My husband and I and our 2 kids(ages 2 and 5) came for 4 days a Wednesday thru Sunday. When we made reservations we were encouraged by the agent to purchase the breakfast buffet ahead of time for $30/day. We did and had to wait 30 minutes for a table and another 30 minutes in line for the food. They had 1 man making omelettes and we had to ask for staff to replenish foods that were gone. This was on Thursday morning and the waitress told us to expect a longer wait on the weekend. We called the manager to ask for a refund for the buffet for the remainder of our stay and they gave us a $50 credit. 
When we wanted to use the pool our family had to share 1 chair between the four of us because they are lacking seating. We had a hard time finding tubes for the slides and lazy river because people would hoard them because they do not have enough of them. We hung out by the small kiddy pool where there was only 1 waiter for the whole area. The first day they allowed parents to go down the small slides with their toddlers but the next day they abruptly changed the rule to toddlers only. How do you explain this to a 2 year old. All of the decking around the pools is extremely hot. The outdoor bathrooms have only 1 changing station so there was a long line just to change a diaper. At night they played movies for the kids outside but once again there was not enough seating. When we valeted our car it took 10-20 minutes for the staff to retrieve our car. 
Everything was stressful from the lines to lack of seating and tubes. We visit San Antonio every summer we usually stay at the Hyatt Hill Country and we will go back there next year!

title: “Pleasant for tourists; not sure if great for business trip”
text:
I had a couple of free nights to use before the offer expired, so my wife and I went across the Bay from Oakland to SF to spend a pleasant weekend at the Mark Hopkins. On balance, we liked it quite a lot. Here are some pros and cons (along with a couple of tips), with the cons being more the downside of the hotel's beautiful location atop Nob Hill, rather than (with one exception) any deficiencies of the hotel itself.
Pros:
1. Overall the service was good, efficient and very friendly.
2. The Deluxe room was nice, though not all that large (350 square feet?). Certainly comfortable and suitable for our purposes.
3. Good view from the room on the 14th floor.
4. Smallish but fine fitness center: about a half dozen aerobic machines and about the same number of weight machines, plus some free weights.
5. As noted, beautiful location atop Nob Hill.
6. Wonderful views from the bar/restaurant Top of the Mark, at I guess what would be the 19th floor of the hotel. We were lucky enough to get the prime corner table looking over the Bay for a late afternoon drink, but there are many nice views. At night (at least on weekends), there's a band playing some good dance music. Wasn't quite what we were in the mood for, but other folks might find it fun.
Cons:
1. That wonderful location could be a bit of a hassle for folks, especially on business, rushing to get to or from the hotel. We like to walk, and spent a good part of the weekend strolling around various parts of town. But it's definitely a steep hike to the hotel, and the couple of times we tried to grab cabs to get there we had to wait quite a while. It was in the evening both times, so maybe (Oakland hick that I am!) I'm overestimating the difficulty of getting taxis other times of day. And of course there's public transportation. But someone there on a business trip might want to read other reviews or do a bit of other research to see whether I'm making a mountain out of a molehill here.
2. As a more minor downside of the location, a cool and breezy day in SF is even cooler and breezier at the top of the hill.
3. The one downside of the hotel that was more than minor was a rather pushy approach by the desk clerk when I checked in, trying to get my to buy into some special service package. He emphasized that without mentioning that as someone with Intercontinental Ambassador status I was entitled to free internet and a few other perks anyway.
4. A couple of very minor glitches by housekeeping.
Not really a negative but...The place seems mainly a tourist hotel, which is of course fine--we were tourists, too, after all!--but again does seem more catered to them than someone there on business.
A couple of tips:
1. Though there are nice views from all rooms on the upper floors, I'd suggest asking for a room with a Bay view.
2. Looking for a place on the hill and in the neighborhood for dinner Friday night, we booked and had modest expectations for an Italian restaurant called Venticello a few blocks from the hotel. But it was great! I had a great, crisp, light Caesar salad and my wife a radicchio salad to start. Then she had a shrimp/scallop risotto and I a fantastic peppered tuna sauteed with some great greens on top of what I believe was a mashed potato/gorgonzola concoction. Neither of the mains was a very light dish, but we loved them both as well as the salads.

title: “amazing time in new york”
text: my husband and i visited new york city at the begining of may ,we stayed at the wellington hotel which is in midtown manhattan the hotel is about a fifteen minute walk from time square and one block away from central park ,the hotel itself was comfortable and clean we had booked for a standard room but when arriving at the hotel found that they had upgraded us to a suite room which had more space and a little area with a fridge, sink,,and microwave but no plates cups etc the room was situated at the back of the hotel very quiet until the work started on the buildings next to the hotel ,which never bothered us as we were normally awake by then .the only issue we had was with the lifts very slow at getting to the floor on which we were on and on the last day the lift was out of order ,we were not told that there were other lifts and therefore waited about fifteen minutes for someone to take our cases and for us to take the other lift the staff were friendly and polite loads to do in new york we walked everywhere even though there are plenty of cabs we didnt want to miss a thing in the time we were there cant wait for our next trip

title: “Great hotel, very expensive”
text:
Booked through Starwood which was probably a mistake. They were unclear as to the final price of the stay. They only quoted one night's price and stated that that price was for the entire stay.
Hotel itself is very nice. The rooms are elegant, well laid out and had plenty of light. All the controls were fully automated and were accessible via a remote by the bed. The bathroom was spacious and the shower featured a rainfall shower head and a seating area in the shower along with a separate bath area. 
The concierge was helpful along with the front desk. Everyone was very courteous and service was excellent. Only blemish would be the lady who came by to fluff our bed. She ignored our do not disturb light and walked right in. I suppose that getting a bed fluffed might be important to some people but it was rather a nuisance to have someone just barge in. 
The restaurant below, Ame, is _ok_ but not as good as some reviews would have it. The staff there was also excellent and helpful although our waiter disappeared for long periods of time to talk ot 2 (single?) females eating together. He seemed to enjoy talking to them quite a bit which deterred from the otherwise great service.
The elevators are quick and we only had to share it once with one other couple. They are well timed and calibrated so you barely notice the acceleration and deceleration of the elevator.
The indoor pool, outdoor lounge area, indoor lounge area and the fitness center are top notch although the indoor pool can be a bit tricky to find. That may have been the reason why it was empty when we went which was a boon for us.
Parking is valet only and internet is not free. There is supposedly a business center but we never could find it.
But for all this there is a price to be paid. At the original price of $800 / night for our room, it would be very hard to justify staying there. I'm sure you can get cheaper rates than that as the price may have been inflated due to the All Star game. Still very hard to justify when other great hotels are in the general location at 1/3 the price.

title: “Nice room, poor customer service”
text: The rooms were nice- clean, spacious, and a good value. However, that is the only nice thing I can say about the place. All four of the people I dealt with were either incompetent or just unhelpful. They didn't reserve the type of rooms that we wanted. As a result, we had small children in the room above us running around at 2am making enough racket to wake up my parents. After the first night, we tried to switch rooms but couldn't. They also locked us out of our rooms after the first night because they had our rooms reserved for only one night instead of two we had actually made the reservation for. When my father spoke with the people at the front desk, they were unhelpful and wouldn't take any responsibility. The manager was out of the weekend and so we couldn't speak with him because we were checking out on Sunday. We were offered no discount or compensation for the inconveniences they had caused.

title: “Great views from the higher floors”
text:
Revere Hotel is an excellent choice if you want to stay in the center of Boston. Everything is within a walking distance. Try to get a room from the higher floors as the views are really spectacular and there are balconies.
We stayed three days and found the service being impeccable - from the nice ladies of the check in to the waitresses of the breakfast room.
The only negative thing was the shower: even though it looked very stylish its adjusting to the right temperature was very difficult and rather frustrating.

title: “Nice hotel, great location, poor technology”
text:
Stayed with buddy over weekend. Nice hotel, GREAT location. Reasonably big rooms, huge bed, clean bathroom.
But couple disappointments:
no free internet!!!! You have to pay like $7 per day for REGULAR, or $14 for premium access!!!
Here is the solution: right beside hotel there is Starbucks. They give you voucher for Westin network!!!!!!!!!
